title: “It was OK, but I was not thrilled.”
text:
The hotel was ok, but nothing more.
The pros:
- very good location
- helpful staff
- boarding pass printing station in the lobby
- illy café in the building
- free wifi in the lobby
The cons:
- loud music in the reception area
- breakfast selection is dull
- crammed rooms, no ergonomics, you always bump into some oddly placed furniture
- no free wifi in the rooms (although occasionally you can hook on the lobby one from the rooms, too, but it is patchy)
- no sign of my Marriott Rewards two weeks after my stay

title: “Indigo does not leave you 'blue'”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Indigo last weekend and had a fantastic stay! The checkin staff was marvelous and helpful with directions and ideas where to go eat and hear music. The room was lovely and quiet. The big flat screen tv was nice as well as the Kuerig coffee maker in the room. The shower was roomy. We had a corner unit on the 11th floor and it had an okay view (remember, this hotel is in a residential area so we saw lots of other buildings!). I loved the fact that they had Aveda products (Shampoo, conditioner, lotion and soaps). We had a king bed and it was comfy with lots of pillows (yep, i am a girl that loves pillows). 
One downside is that they dont have parking onsite so you have to use the ramp next door. They charge $41 per 24 hour period - but the hotel will give you a $2 discount if you give them your parking ticket. 
Lake Michigan was 3 blocks away - easy walk! Nice to walk along the lake (you can get to the sand or just use the walking/bike paths too) We walked all the way to Navy Pier (about 1.3 miles)
The L train was 2 blocks away with easy access to the Red Line so we parked the car the whole time and walked or took the L. And there were tons of bars and restaurants nearby (even the famed "Mothers" from St Elmos Fire)
No pool, no hot tub. They do have a spa and fitness room (we did not partake in either)

title: “Comfortable location, fair price. At the end of its lifecycle”
text:
The hotel is becomming outdated. Our room however was fine and non of the complaints others had occured during our stay. Only discomfort was a missing light bulb and a broken one. The airco is a "classic" and makes a lot of noise.
The pickup at the airport was OK. We had to wait for 15 minutes and it brought us to the hotel free of charge. During our stay we used th T tot go to town. For 2 dollar one way very cheap and only a 5 minute walk from the hotel.
Complementary breakfast is very limited but OK. Free wireless internet in the lobby. Once you have logged in it became free in the room as well (magic!)
The shuttle back to the airport runs on the hour. It was not on a sign so we had to wait unfortunately. Very nice driver who dropped us at the rental car location instead of the airport.
If you don't expect too much this is a comfortable and afordable option to stay in Boston. Sunny beaches nearby!

title: “Superb”
text: Got stuck during the winter weather hitting the east coast, Wyndham gave me a short notice room and short notice extensions as I needed. Nice place to stay!

title: “Deceptive reservation!!! Certainly not a suite!”
text: We booked our room and it was supposed to be a suite. What we received was a room that was intended to be an extra bedroom for an adjoining room. It had it's own hallway for the room next door. It was not only loud because it was not a room in itself, it only had a bed and a desk. We did't even have a BATHTUB!!! The bathroom had a handicapped shower instead. I brought this to the attention of the manager and asked for some sort of a discount because of this deceptive reservation. After waiting five days for the response, the manager explained they were sold out and that was the only room available. Do you think they could have told us that when we made a reservation for a SUITE! If your in Detroit don't stay here!!! Motor City Casino, Caesar's Windsor, and MGM have great rooms!!!

title: “Great location, great value, and comfortable clean rooms”
text: We had a four night stay and were quite satisfied. The location is great; we walk when we travel, and we walked all over San Francisco from this hotel. It is only a 6 block walk from the BART stop for easy access to/from SFO. The pillows were a tad on the large/hard side, but other than that our stay was perfect. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “No better than average”
text:
Stayed here while watching the Thurs, Fri & Sat US Open matches. While this is a "nice" hotel, I found it no better than average. There were some real plusses, however, those were:
Gravity - the fitness center. One of the best available to hotel guests I've ever experienced! Bring your headphones for the elipitcal, treadmill, etc...and they have Cybex equipment.
Close to Central Park for walks
Close to Madison Ave/Fifth Ave shops
In my opinion, the big draw for this hotel is location (you don't vacation to workout, although that was a big plus). 
Drawbacks:
Concierge - not as informed as they should have been. My first time to US Open, and had read on line and the tennis mags, knew that I would have to transfer on the subway to get to Flushing Meadows - the concerige was rude acting as if I should know where to go. Give me a break, guys! My first time in New York, I know I COULD have made it there without you, but did you have to be so snotty about it? They also had absolutely no suggestions for restaurats - a first for me. Never, ever been to a hotel, anywhere, that the concierge had no opinion on dining - or preferred times for guests!
elevators - they suck. slow, and at least one was down the entire time.
housekeeping - first two nights, no new glasses!!!! Hey, we'd been out in the heat all day, needed water!!!! had to call for them
last night - they took our blankets with none returned!
Norma's - breakfast is okay, but nothing spectacular. Yes, it's good, but I would much rather go down 57th street to the bagel place and get a #2 breakfast for $4.95 and fresh oj for $2.95 than pay $30.00 for eggs and $7.00 for oj. I will say the service was spectacular. 
The side cafe, Seppi's or something like that, had very attentive waiters. We only had drinks and appetizers there, but was very cozy
Will I stay there again? Depends. I won't pay over $300 per night. If a rate under $300 is available, I'd probably do it.

title: “Good for an overnight close to the airport.”
text: Convenient to the airport for an early morning flight. Good value. Room was clean and they have a 24 hour restaurant. Outdoor pool and spa. Staff was friendly and helpful. I would stay here again.

title: “Great Hospitality - Outstanding Value”
text: I stayed at this hotel for a business trade show Oct 4th and 5th - originally planning to spend just one night. The staff was extremely accomodating - the door man was exceptionally pleasant & the place was clean and well maintained. The building itself is old, the rooms are nothing fancy, but the service was great and there was a full breakfast buffet included in the price. A great location & a great value.

title: “What's with all the NOISE!?”
text:
Just thought I'd give a summary of the recent stay my wife and I had in the Midtown Hotel, Boston.
Initial impressions of the place were good. Ron at the reception desk was very friendly, and our check-in was handled in a matter of seconds. An equally affable porter offered to take our bags to the room, which was number 172.
The room was huge; two double beds, a desk, small table and seating area, plus a good sized bathroom with bath and shower. The facilities were good too - nice TV with plenty of channels, and a funky little cafetiere for making fresh coffee. Everything was very clean, though the decor was slightly dated, and the bathroom suite showed some signs of age. I'm not one to pick at such things, however, so all in all we were happy.
Being somewhat jet-lagged, we decided a short nap was in order. Sadly, I didn't get a wink of sleep. No sooner had we settled down, we were subjected to an ongoing cacophony of slamming, shouting, and what sounded like the practising of an inexperienced drummer. The noise irritated me somewhat, but given that this was still only late afternoon, I wasn’t too bothered.
Our siesta having been abandoned, we decided to explore a little. The location of the hotel was very good. The immense Prudential shopping centre was just a couple minutes walk away, and had a subway stop to get wherever we should want. Massachusetts Avenue, with its assorted shops and restaurants, was only a few minutes walk in the opposite direction.
So, having been fed and watered, we returned to the hotel for a well-deserved (and by then long overdue) night’s sleep. Unfortunately, once again I found sleep hard to come by. It seems that the noise of the Midtown hotel persists at all hours of day and night. Doors slamming, voices shouting, and a variety of crashes, bangs and wallops - all conspired to rob me of a restful slumber. After two such disturbed nights, we did complain to reception, who said they could only help us if we were able to tell them which rooms, specifically, the noises were coming from. Not wanting to wander around the hotel in our pyjamas in search of the parties responsible, we decided just to grin and bear it. In time, we got used to the constant racket, but felt annoyed that we’d ever had to.
In summary, I was a bit disappointed by the Midtown. The room was large, comfortable, and reasonably well-equipped, while the location was very good. However, the ongoing noise of the place – and the staff’s apparent unwillingness to help – put me off, and means that if I do ever return to Boston, it is unlikely I will rest my head at the Midtown.

title: “Nice if your deaf & suicidal”
text:
The Angeleno is right next to the 405, and that alone being bad enough, the A/C is simply mounted in a hole in the wall. So, 405 noise isn´t only relayed through cheap-ass windows, but also vented in as soon as the A/C starts working - the noise from the freeway actually gets closer as soon as the fan starts to spin. So if you plan on getting any amount of sleep, you better be deaf. My stay there was only for a week or so, lacking alternatives in the proximity. One of the nicer amenities to compensate for the lack of sleep overnight is the free shuttle service - which I relied upon for two consecutive mornings, only to get involved in an accident in the hotel shuttle on a 2-mile-journey from the hotel to UCLA. I have driven all my life and never had an accident, and three times a 2 mile drive should hardly be accident prone - unfortunately for me, it was. Luckily no one was hurt, but both cars were severly damaged. I relied upon my own car from then. 
What was odd was also that even after the accident, the hotel declined to offer any kind of compensation, and they actually wanted to raise my room rate because they were getting "booked". I moved out that same day - its a pity the rooms are decorated so nicely, they should move the furniture to some other hotel that really matches decoration with service.

title: “Feels really good to stay here!”
text: I was in Houston at another hotel which was so bad I needed to find another hotel quickly. I searched online and found rooms in this hotel. Although it was a little bit cheaper than my first hotel, I have to say: This hotel is really great. From the service, to the rooms, to the pool (very clean and nice), the wifi (works flawlessly), etc. My room has a fridge and a microwave oven. Really, I'm happy to be here. Also, the neighborhood seems very nice.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: Great room. Excellent food. Very nice service. I had breakfast in my room, lunch in the restaurant, and cocktails and dinner in the bar. A really enjoyable experience.

title: “Lovely hotel, excellent staff”
text:
I stayed in this hotel for four nights in September 2012. The hotel is lovely, beautifully decorated and spotlessly clean. The staff are wonderful, especially the concierges, who helped us tremendously during our stay. Nothing was too much trouble. 
We were there to celebrate a special birthday. When we checked in, the receptionist asked the reason for our stay. We thought nothing of it, However, 10 minutes after we were shown up to our room, the bellboy knocked on the door and delivered a gift basket full of snacks, treats and a soft toy lion with a Lenox ribbon around his neck. The note on the basket wished me a very happy birthday from the staff of the Lenox. It was a lovely surprise and certainly made me feel special. 
I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

title: “WORKS FOR ME!”
text:
I stayed in this hotel for 2 nights i really like it.
the rooms are really great , clean and nice.
the location is perfect 1 and a half block from the subway.
so i went everywhere by subway , i did not need take taxis.
the neighborhood, is full of places to eat burger king, pizza place. italian food, sturbucks, subway and a pharmacy store also,
from the National Reagan airport is 25.00 usd dollar cab, or u can take the subway!.
i would stay again in this hotel!!!.

title: “The Wit is nice hotel”
text:
Enjoyed this hotel. Rooms were well above par compared to your standard Doubletree.
Nice mini bar. :)
Great central downtown Chicago location!

title: “Nice getaway for a long weekend”
text: We booked a king suite for labor day weekend. Our room was in the South Point tower which is central and close to the River Ranch. Overall, the room has a nice layout, but even though they said it is renovated, it is starting to show wear and tear. What we didn't realize is that the hotel sells rooms to the locals at a substantially lower rate than what I found online and the place was at 100% capacity for the holiday weekend. We found this out from talking to a couple of locals. Needless to say, the River Ranch was packed and parking was at a premium. We enjoyed the hotel and the pools, but what we didn't like was that the River Ranch closed at 10:30pm and that they did not offer anything special,e.g. entertainment, food, movies(except for friday), at night for the holiday weekend. The bar by the south tower pool was closed at night every night we went. We stayed an extra night after the labor day holiday and the River Ranch closed at 8:00pm. A bit early for a resort. Overall, I would say it's a nice place to stay, especially if you have kids. You won't be able to get them out of the River Ranch.

title: “Lives up to expectations and exceeds”
text:
When reviewing a Four Seasons hotel you start out at a very high level of expectations. The Chicago Four Seasons meets those lofty expectations. The hotel is located in a nice area close to Lake Michigan and near the John Hancock tower. Starting at the 8th floor of the tower in which it resides, views are stunning in every direction. Rooms are impeccably furnished and clean. The shower is fountain of relaxation and the bathroom stocked with L'Occitane products. The gym and dressing rooms were spotless and the hotel's pool, while not ideal for lap swimming, was beautiful and still did the job. If you do use the gym or pool, bring the clothes down with you as lockers and even a bathing suit drying machine are available.
The staff is courteous and the whole environment is lush and refined.

title: “Dana the best in mission bay”
text: Wonderful, beautiful view of the Marina, nice areas, very clean, excelent service, nice room (we also received an upgrade), everything perfect!!

title: “Very nice downtown property”
text: Very nice hotel in downtown Houston in a convenient location besides the Convention Center - Restaurants were top shelf with fair prices - The guest rooms were very nice with one of the best mattresses I have ever had at a Hilton property. All in all very nice Hilton property.

title: “Great Location and better than some reviews suggest”
text:
Had two rooms for 4 nights in April - good rate from Hotwire but parking balanced it out - $35 a day but cheap compared to safe parking in London - and these guys valet parked and collected for you.
Has seen a lot of service but still OK - beds clean, comfortable - staff very helpful - free coffee or iced teas till noon if you join their reward program ahead of time.
Pool area great - very social - fire pits, cabana's and bar etc. Free wifi.
Busy business hotel but friendly with it. Didn't feel too uncomfortable in shorts and T's!
Nice place.

title: “Consistently Superb”
text:
The only place I will stay when in San Antonio. The staff is nothing short of first class in service and friendliness. My wife and I have stayed in many Comfort Suites, but this hotel is our favorite. The rooms are spacious and relaxing. The gathering room is warm and comfortable, with the Thursday night wine and cheese social becoming the highlight of a busy week.
The Riverwalk may be a little further away, but the hotel makes up for this small inconvenience with excellent service and accomodations. I highly recommend the Comfort Suites in downtown San Antonio.

title: “Great Choice, Again”
text:
We booked two rooms at this hotel. It is very close to SAN so it is convenient picking up guests flying in to visit. Our family was very happy with the hotel, also.
Our rooms were in the Marina Tower. The rooms are very clean and spacious. The balcony was big enough for 2 chairs and a table with extra room to boot. The beds were wonderful. All four of our group raved about the sleep we got after playing tourist all day. 
Check-In was a breeze. The lady made sure we had rooms across the hall so we got to see both views from our respective balconies. Also, the concierge recommended three restaurants. He made reservations for us and we were not disappointed. All staff that we came in contact with were friendly, courteous and helpful when needed. The grounds are beautiful and very well kept.
The only drawback that we had was the parking. Since we self-parked, it was a long walk to the gravel parking lot. Also, should we really have to pay $22 per night to park our car in a gravel lot?

title: “Good Hotel”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights in June. Hotel was perfect for our trip. It was in a good location, friendly staff, clean and comfortable, so comfortable we didnt wake up till midday! Hotel is close to the subway. Nathaniel Square (great place for restaurants/bars/shops) is only about 2 stops away and Harvard about 4/5 stops away. If you're in Boston make sure you explore the side streets as there are some lovely boutiques around. Overall a very pretty place to visit.

title: “Continues to shine”
text: Come on--review the Palace?? Everything was perfect--from the room to the food. The only complaint would be one night of 4 we did not get complete turn-down service.

title: “Great Location and Value”
text:
Having stayed in San Francisco a few times I was specifically looking for a hotel in this area.
It's location by Union Square and China Town is ideal for getting out and seeing the city and its attractions.
Parking is available at a discounted rate across the street from the hotel which was useful as we picked our car up from the airport (although its worth noting that several hire companies are located within this area).
Checking in was fast and the reception staff friendly. We were upgraded to a bigger room which gave a great view of the street below, there was some noise from cleaning trucks in the early morning but wasn't too much of a problem.
The room was sparse but clean and larger than most I've stayed in SF.
The Quality of the hotel is very good for the price especially when you compare to other hotels on the same block.
I'll definitely stay here when I next visit SF.

title: “Great budget hotel, but they probably have bugs”
text: I found this hotel a couple of months ago and booked it right away. the price and location were just what I was looking for. After paying in full I started reading reviews. Had I done this first I would not have chosen this hotel. All the reviews about bedbugs scared me but I'm too cheap to change my reservation and I knew I wouldn't find a hotel on the upper west side for the same price, so I decided to risk getting bedbugs. Before my trip I spent many hours reading about bedbugs and I got really scared of bringing them home with me. When I got to the Belnord our room was on the fifth floor(no elevator) but that didn't bother me considering the price. Our room wasn't too small and It was fairly clean. I immediately looked behind headboards and in drawers for signs of bed bugs and all I found was a few black spots that could have been bed bug droppings (They looked exactly like pictures I've seen on the internet.) We slept with the lights on and kept our hard plastic suitcase (which is almost air tight) closed at all times. The first night as I was trying to sleep I noticed a blood stain on the wall right next to my bed which was the same size and shape as the stains I'd been warned about on the internet. During our one week stay we got a couple of bites that probably were from bed bugs but that's it. Bugs that aren't very hungry won't come out if it's light, or so I've read. I don't think we brought any bugs home with us and overall the hotel was great. But I felt worried about bed bugs for months so I'm still not sure if it was worth it. If you are deciding wheather or not to book this hotel read reviews on this site for a couple hours first. Then read about bed bugs. If you're not scared of bed bugs, this hotel is perfect for the budget traveller.

title: “Very pleased with this hotel; a well-run establishment”
text:
Stayed 4 nights in Sep 2003; found the staff to be permanently pleasant and helpful, the rooms were kept clean and well housekept, and the location of the hotel is ideal for the Hollywood Bowl, and other attractions. The high standard of the hotel set against their keen pricing makes this place an absolute bargain, in my view.
Will certainly be paying them a return visit in future.

title: “Best Customer Service I have ever experienced”
text: Hotel is a decent 4 star standard and good value for money. Customer service at this hotel was the best I have ever experienced, and I am a high-maintenance hotel guest! If you have a car and don't feel the need to be walking distance to restaurants etc, this hotel is a great option. Thanks to all the staff who served us during our stay - the great service made such a difference

title: “Average motel, great value for downtown San Jose”
text:
This is an old, decently remodeled property in the "motor-court" style as another reviewer pointed out. It's a couple blocks from the convention center, and several blocks from the university. Plenty of restaurants nearby. We really liked Original Joe's Italian restaurant which is just a short walk.
The check-in people are very friendly and helpful. Parking was ample while I was there. This is a 3-story, outside-corridor motel with an elevator. I found it to be very quiet. Just to be sure, you might request a room near the center, since there are a lot of clubs along 1st street. I did not feel unsafe walking in a 3-block radius of the motel, from the convention center to the university.
The room was nice in appearance, and very clean. The bedding was nice, but the bed itself was of indifferent quality. It'll seem a little flat and hard if you're used to the pillow-top mattresses in a lot of even mid-range hotels these days.The bath is well appointed but the fixtures are fairly archaic, as is the plumbing - the shower went warm/cool/warm/cool repeatedly every morning during a 3 night stay. Not scalding/freezing, but still annoying. The shower smelt somewhat mildewy. The wall unit A/C looks cheap but worked well and was quiet. Wireless internet was good but you have to hunt/crawl to plug in your laptop. The TV had few channels. Housekeeping was excellent.
Overall, the Ramada was a decent place to stay, especially when you consider the price is half or less compared to the convention center hotels a couple blocks away -- and unlike those places, the Ramada has free in-room Internet and free parking. It's definitely not the Ritz but it's a clean, decent place and a good value.

title: “pretty good hotel, good location”
text:
The pros: The hotel's location is good--far enough from powell street crowds, and yet close enough to get to almost anywhere on foot. The room was clean, the bed was comfortable, and we got it for a really good deal ($99). The staff was great.
The cons: The room had a musty smell which either went away (or we probably just got used to it), so it was no big deal. The room, I forget which one, didn't have a view--only of the brick bldg next door--again no big deal since we hit the streets the minute we got there. We also found an empty plastic bag tucked in the top fold of the outermost blanket. To be quite honest, we didn't know if it was ours or if it was there from the get go, but either way, it didn't disturb us (too much).
In the end, we would definitely stay here again.

title: “We fell in love with the Inn and the Chelsea boys!!”
text:
Chelsea Pines Inn is the only place I'll stay in NYC. First of this was my 1st NYC trip and it was awesome thanks to Jay,Al, and all the staff. We really depended on them to navigate us through the city and they happily helped. They reccomended the best restaurants. The inn is perfectly located. The subway is practically right outside the door. The rooms are super clean and the perfect size. The business center is so convienant if you need to print something up on your way out. The breakfast was perfect. Coffee all day a huge bonus!
 I would totally reccomend staying here. It's ........ Delightful.

title: “Ripoff! Do not stay here!”
text: I am a Kimpton member with 50 nights that I stayed in Kimpton hotels in the USA this year. This is by far the biggest ripoff hotel in the USA. The rooms are the size of a closet. Old and dingy. One queen size bed only in each room. Wtf? $62.50 for parking everytime you retrieve your car from the valet. So if you stay one night and use your car once in the middle of the day they charge you $125. Scammers. I am contacting corporate tomorrow. F the Kimpton NYC!!!!!

title: “Excellent location but had a number of problems”
text:
First, the hotel is well decorated, the rooms are spacious, and the proximity to the Capitol and Union Station is very convenient. The bar and recreational area are nice, although I wouldn’t suggest the restaurant unless you are willing to pay a lot for mediocre food. 
That being said, we had a number of problems with the customer service and reliability of the hotel's promises. We arrived later in the day due to plane delays and upon checking in, we were told that there were no rooms left with double beds. Although we reserved a room with two beds online, the staff impatiently told us that what we 'reserve' is not guaranteed. They did offer to upgrade us to a suite; however, there was only a king bed in that room as well, and one of the three in our party would have been sleeping on a pull out couch for four nights. Finally they found a smoking room with double beds which he had no choice but to take (by the way if you want a view, make sure to 'request' an view of the Capitol...our family friends were also staying in the hotel and had a beautiful view at night while we had ugly rooftops and a view right into the office building across the courtyard). 
On our second night there, I pulled back the sheets and there was dried blood on the top sheet. I called housekeeping, and I must admit, angry as I was, that the woman was very apologetic and professional and changed the sheets right away.
Finally, when we were preparing to leave, we received the bill and were surprised to find that they had significantly raised the price that we were quoted from the internet. We went downstairs and showed them that we reserved the room for a certain amount, and the bill was now some two hundred dollars higher. They then told us that because they had full occupancy for the last two nights, they reserved the right to charge us an extra fee (for reasons beyond any understanding). We had a few choice words with the manager, who was polite and we were able to pay the original price. 
Overall, the hotel was ok, but we personally had a number of bad experiences and the staff's friendliness and willingness to handle problems varied greatly. Frankly if you're looking for a little more reliability, I would suggest the Hyatt or Holiday Inn across the street.
On a side note, for an excellent view of the city, try the Old Town Trolley Tour. It stops right at the Hyatt on New Jersey and has something like 19 stops. For 25 dollars a day, you can see all of D.C. and have your own personalized tour! The Holiday Inn on New Jersey also has an excellent restaurant if you just want good old American food.

title: “nothing worked”
text: Shuttle advertised but didnt run till 9am her plane was at 8am The safe didnt work and the guy at the desk didnt know how to make it work the internet wouldnt work because of improper ip address desk guy couldnt fix that either room was clean but it was a smoking room for three people and generously provided with one ashtray I hate their coffee cups personal preference but still cardboard ? three pillows filled with What they disappeared when you layed on them, at that rate there should have been 3 to a person.

title: “A bit scary”
text: I recently stayed at this hotel, and chose it because the photos posted on the hotels website were amazing, and the prices seemed quite reasonable for the area. Let me just say that the photos are not a good representation of what the actual hotel looks like. When my friend and I were driving up the hill to the place, and finally figured out how to get there, I was very disappointed. The buildings were originally apartments, and the outside has not been kept up at all. The place kind of reminded me of a place you would see on an episode of cops!! For us, two women traveling alone, we were freaked out. The inside of the room was nice, very spacious, and great view of the city from the balcony. Had we stayed in this room, I probably would have enjoyed my stay more, but we didn't, because after the first night we discovered that the heat did not work. The staff at the magic castle (who owns the HHH), was very accomodating in changing our room, but 2 minutes after stepping foot in the new room we decided to check out, that room was not at all like the first, was dirty and smelled like stale cigarettes! We packed or stuff, and went down to the magic castle to check out...the staff asked us if there was a reason for leaving and I told her that we were not at all happy with the conditions at the HHH and they knocked $100 off of our stay for the night before, and offered for us a suite at the magic castle hotel for a discounted rate. We did take the suite, and found the Magic castle wonderful. I have to say thank you to the staff here they are amazing...especially Gretchen (I believe that was her name). I think that if you get the right room at the HHH, you could be satisfied with your stay, but if you are traveling alone, or a group of women...the place might seem a bit seedy...but the Magic castle is a great alternative.

title: “superb location”
text:
We stayed for 2 nights and found the location was perfect. Easy to walk to Grand Central station where we caught the subway to go to the US Tennis at Flushing Meadows. Also right between 5th Avenue and Madison Avenue. The room was perfect ,spotlessly clean with lovely quality bedding. It was quite pricey but worth it. 
We ate at a restaurant 2 blocks away called Papillon and had breakfast at Frescos to go It was fabulous value. All bread baked fresh and choice was fantastic. Cost for 2 about $18

title: “Close to Universal Studios”
text:
The main advantage of this hotel has to be that it is right next to Universal Studios. You just walk outside the hotel, follow the arrows and you are right at the front of Universal Stuidos. 
The check-in process was fast and the front desk was very nice. Lobby was very nice looking. I had reserved a 1 king bed room and was given 2 double beds which I was very disappointed with. Called the front desk but they couldn't help me and I did not want to wait around trying to switch rooms later.
The room itself seemed larger than normal, it seemed to be stretched out long. It also had a great view, I could see the front of Universal Studios from our window. Which is great at night because the lights from the city walk looked nice. 
Did try out the room service, great food and it came up fairly fast.
Check out was super easy, they slipped a bill under our door sometime while we were sleeping, if the bill looked fine we just leave and that amount would get charged to us. Very simple and saved a lot of time.
Besides visiting Universal Studios, there isn't much else to do around this area though.

title: “Excellent all round”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights while in NYC. It ticked all the boxes. Very friendly staff, rooms were cool and the location was perfect. Bryant park opposite the hotel was a also a nice outlook with a garden cafe and bar. The hotel bar downstairs had a slightly weird dungeon theme but out of way. Would stay here again without question.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
We stayed two nights at the University Hotel and recommend it to other travellers. The rooms are contemporary design and comfortable and clean. Above all the staff are very friendly and helpful - giving directions, recommending restaurants,arranging for the shuttle van. The hotel is located near the U of Washington campus and offers complimentary shuttle service to the downtown core. It was great to be able to park the car for a couple of days! In the evenings we walked 2-3 blocks to nearby restaurants in the university district.
Our room looked out over a courtyard pool in the back which was undoubtedly quieter because of less traffic noise - so you may want to book your room with that in mind. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Amazing stay!!!”
text: The Dana Hotel is just an amazing place to stay and I am always happy to come back here. The bellmen, TJ and Christopher are always friendly, welcoming and remember me each time. I had a corner king suite and everything from the comfortable beds to the awesome showers made my business trip that much more enjoyable. The room service staff were always prompt and so friendly...even at 6AM!!! I only had breakfast in the restaurant one morning but the wait staff were so GREAT! The food was excellent and the service even better!! I decided to treat myself to a spa treatment and Geraldine was fantastic! She sat me down and really listened to what I wanted in my facial---the result was unbelievably awesome! I looked refreshed and relaxed. I absolutely love the Dana Hotel and always recommend it to clients and friends!

title: “Very comfortable high quality hotel”
text: Comfortable, high quality 4 star hotel with very helpful staff Breakfast was outstanding but very expensive ($50 for two of us) with no local alternative. In terms of dinner there are only sports bars locally. You have to pay for WiFi but could use a computer in the bar area. Within easy public transport of the town centre and the airport.

title: “disgusting”
text: We stayed there as an overnight stay before catching our morning flight, rooms were not clean and very outdated through out the hotel, did not have the rooms available that we booked and was offered an alternative on the smoking floor, which was unacceptable when you have children but did nothing to rectify their booking error. would not use or recommend this hotel to anyone. very disappointed.

title: “Wonderful Rooms”
text: I recently stayed at this location while on a business trip to Jacksonville. The staff was very courteous, helpful and very nice overall. The room was great. I would definately stay at this location again.

title: “Overwhelming service”
text:
All members of staff were accommodating, pleasant and helpful. The shuttle service was excellent; the designated pick-up and drop-off points were conveniently located, and the drivers were always available.
The manager actually went out of his way to deliver several items that I had forgotten in the safe before I left the city.
I highly recommend this hotel, and will certainly stay there during my next visit to Seattle.

title: “Aptly named”
text:
I traveled here recently for a meeting of about 50 people. I was a bit leery upon checking in to see so many families. I was afraid that the stay would end up being noisy and crowded. I was flat wrong. The conference center is lovely and set apart from the hotel. It is a short walk depending upon which building you are staying in (the property is enormous but does not feel that way). There are numerous staff that will drive you over in a golf cart if you prefer. 
There is an impressive looking water park and an attractive golf course on the property. I did not have a chance to sample either. The food was excellent both at the conference center and at Rustler's Roost. The room was clean and spacious. The property was surprisingly quiet and I slept very well. I would wholeheartedly recommend this property for business or leisure travel. Enjoy your stay

title: “Loved this place!”
text: This hotel has amazing staff! We got help with anything we asked about. This was our first trip to NY, so we had a lot of questions! This hotel's location was perfect. Close to the subway, restaurants, and attractions. There is free bottled water on every floor, and this hotel is environmentally friendly. They give you the choice of new towels and sheets during the stay. We also felt safe because you have to activate the elevator with your room key, so not just anyone could get on the elevator and have access to the building.

title: “Outstanding”
text: A very pleasant hotel in a good location. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The wine served at 5.30 pm was a novelty and a wonderful idea.Room was spacious and comfortable I would definately stay again

title: “Hole in the Wall”
text:
This is an awesome place to stay - if you can find it! Located along Wabash between Madison and Monroe the doorway is easy to miss when walking down the sidewalk and the 'walkway' to the elevator is not impressive, but when the elevator door opens on the second floor your eyes will 'bug out' at the sight of the expansive lobby complete with complimentary fruit water and grand piano. The rooms are all redone with beautiful oak accents, comfy beds, unusual window treatments and bathrooms you'd be proud to take home! 
The location is great for theatres, dining and only a few blocks from the train stations and Millenium / Grant parks. We spent the weekend without taking a cab!

title: “priceline rooms”
text: We checked in at ~4pm. A few weeks prior, we applied the Hilton Honors Card and requested a king size bed. At the check-in counter, a lady employee quickly gave us a room #1355 and only mentioned us prepaying the room (asked whether we wanted to charge the $2/night for some fees). I was curious to see the room # ended in -55. Remembered from another forum that it may be a priceline room (rooms ending with 1&2, 45&46, 53&54, 55&56). So I told her (politely, of course) that we requested for a king size bed. She said there isn't any, and that's why she's giving us a queen size bed. Although my alarm bells are buzzing in my head, I thought, why not go up and take a look at it. It may all just be hyped up. So, we went up and looked at the room. It's the room next to the elevator shaft, and yes, every 30 seconds or so, we can hear the elevator moving up and down (sounded like an airplane flying above our heads) next to the wall. By the way, the room was tiny. We ended going back to the check-in counter and met with another employee, and told him that we couldn't possibly sleep in that room (with the noise). He was kind enough to give us another room with a king size bed. What bothered us most was that the first employee lied about the availability of a king size bed room. However, overall, the trip was very good because we were allowed a late check-out (3pm, instead of 12noon). Oh, our rates for 3 nights were $105/night plus total tax ($54.14).

title: “So Far So Great”
text:
I'm in the middle of a month (to 2 month) stay at this hotel. Since I've checked in I've received nothing but consistently stellar service.
I had to relocate to a hotel after a sewage spill in my house. Needless to say it hasn't been easy trying to navigate what's happening at my house while moving temporarily into a hotel. Gratefully, I chose this hotel and they have been more than accommodating with everything. They've even welcomed my dog with open arms!
My room (a studio) has a great layout with a view of the city and bay. It's got everything I need to feel "at home".
One of the aspects that really makes this hotel so great is the way you are greeted upon arrival. I don't think I've ever met a better run valet service or a nicer group of guys running it. I'm in and out a lot at the hotel and they never miss a beat. These kinds of things are helping make this stay so enjoyable.
I've also gotten to know the front desk team and their positive attitudes and willing to do whatever is needed reminds me of a staff I would find at a 5 star hotel. 
I'm a local San Diegan (actually live about a mile from the hotel) and I will be recommending this hotel to friends and family.

title: “BED BUGSS!!!!!!!!!!”
text: Stayed in this hotel for two nights. First night at about 4 am woke up to find a SEA of BEDBUGS. Requested a change of room. Next night same thing happened. Highly suggest not to stay at this hotel. Frontdesk is rude, rude rude. The manager is incompetent and full of himself. And needless to say... BEDBUGS!!!!!!

title: “Wonderful,wonderful”
text: Spent one night 2/24/12 and have a new homebase when I'm in the Jacksonville area. Check in was a breeze. The clerk,(I'm terrible with names) was very pleasant and helpful. The loby was well lit , coffee and lemon water available. Room clean with a nice comfortable chair and ottoman. Desk chair was too big for the space and blocked the path to bathroom. The hot tub was first rate, clean and hot. I'm not sure but I think the pool had cubes in it. It was so cold. Great small fitness room, as with everything else clean and well enough equipped to get a basic workout in. I didn't have time for the sauna but it was a nice touch. The dinner buffet at $10.95 was first rate. Waitstaff was attentive and friendly. Southern style vegatables were really good. I am already planning to stay here on my next trip to the area.

title: “Sleepless in Seattle 2: Avoid room 233!”
text:
The positives:
Most of the front desk staff were incredibly nice and helpful. 
Free breakfast with waffles, muffins, breads, danish, bagels, fruit, yogurt, oatmeal, assorted cereals, and juices. 
Great coffee in the lobby and at the restaurant.
Aveda toiletries
The negatives:
I had a room that directly overlooked the alley between the hotel and IHOP next door. This alley housed the dumpsters which were emptied at 3am and 5am. I was on the 2nd floor (room 233) directly over where the trucks were parked so got the sounds of breaking glass loud and clear. No sleep at all after having arrived from the east coast well after midnight.
After the 5am garbage truck wake-up call, I gave up on sleep, took a shower, and went downstairs to speak to the front desk clerks. They were sympathetic but said "oh yes, the garbage trucks." I asked to be moved, but the hotel was booked. They said I could come back around at 10 or 11am to check but they were booked solid again that night. Meanwhile I had to go to business meetings in Bellevue on no sleep.
I called my corporate travel agency and asked to be moved to a sister hotel in Bellevue. The agent arranged it but told me that the front desk manager (Tammy) was upset that I had not given the hotel a chance to rectify the situation!!!! Apparently she had not been notified of my 6am conversation with her staff. Tammy then told the agent that she would refund my remaining 2 night prepaid stay if I got there by 2pm; it was 1:20pm at this point so I had to rush to Seattle from Bellevue, and surprise! there was heavy traffic in Seattle. Anyway I made it there and happily checked out.
My stay at the Silver Cloud Eastgate was far more pleasant and restful. The Silver Cloud Broadway needs to reconsider subjecting guests to the ridiculous racket that seems to be a regular occurrence given the nonchalance of the staff to my complaint. Otherwise guests beware of the 2nd floor alley rooms.

title: “Not Bad for the Price”
text:
I booked through priceline and got a room for 2 nights. For the base rate, it's not a bad hotel. But I would have been very dissapointed if I had paid more than what I did.
PROS
1, Nice staff - we showed up at 1.30pm and were promptly assigned a room per my phone request - a queen bed on the 1st floor (have a baby so did not want to lug his stuff upstairs). They were very polite and answered all our questions and even held our luggage for a few hours after we checked out the last day.
2. Great Location - Within walking distance of the major attractions in Seattle. Plus they have a free shuttle to take you to other attractions that are not within walking distance.
3. Decent bathroom amenities.
4. Okayish Breakfast. Bagels, Breads, Pastries, Juice, Coffee and Tea. Not bad for the price we paid (65 bucks per night). The coffee and tea were available all day, and the coffee was rather good.
5. Walk-in closet was helpful in storing all our stuff. Since we had a corner room, there was a window in the closet, in the kitchen and in the room which made it very pleasant even when the a was not being used.
CONS
1. Rooms do need updating. Decor was non-existent in the room though they do seem to have put some effort in the bathroom.
2. Kitchen was almost ghetto like. Ages old fridge and stove and microwave do not make a kitchen to me even though all functioned as they were supposed to. 
3. The room backed out into a parking lot where strange people loitered at night. And noise from garbage trucks woke up my baby in the morning.
BUT overall, a nice stay. The staff made up for the physical shortcomings of the hotel, as did the decent location. For 65 bucks a night we got an okay room in a great location with decent breakfast and a free shuttle to the major attractions. Not a bad deal.

title: “Motel, but not really a motel”
text:
We stayed at this hotel/motel for 1 night. I booked it as I thought that it would be a proper motel, as I have never stayed in one. It turned out to be a plain and simple budget hotel. Saying that it was clean, but very basic.
My partner described the lobby, corridors and room itself as clinical and hospital like. It was ok for one night, but would probably choose something a bit more elegant and inviting for a longer stay. 
The location is ok, although there are quite a few homeless people in the surrounding area.

title: “Would have been five stars except for the food”
text:
I picked it because it was close to Johns Hopkins. The staff from curb to room were top notch. I had a lovely and CLEAN room, very quiet. I did not meet one rude person on staff during a four day stay. They were anxious to help me and meet any special needs I had. It's a beautiful hotel, formerly the Baltimore & Ohio Railroad headquarters. I saw Tiffany windows and the most beautiful hand plastered ceilings from the turn of the last century in the lobby. It is the middle of the bustling downtown area, very vibrant and I actually felt safe in the hotel and on the streets outside. (I'm from a small down and don't always feel safe in large downtown areas.) This was an incredibly nice place to stay. I will definitely stay there again.
Room service on the other hand....NOT SO GOOD! Twice they did not bring us what we ordered, but the hotel made a generous adjustment to the charges. The restaurant has great friend staff, but it's gourmet weird. Best breakfast we had was across the street at David & Dad's Cafe across the street.

title: “Ideal for a quick trip”
text: Well located, very helpfull staff, comfortable room (air con a bit noisy), slightly faded boutique hotel. We flew in for a three night break from the UK and would go back.

title: “Enjoyed the stay except for one thing”
text: The beds were awful. This was a family re-union and every single one hated the mattresses, we could adjust the firmness of the mattress by a hand-held controller, yet the mattresses were VERY uncomforable, I will still DIFINITELEY reccommend this hotel.

title: “Not worth the headaches”
text:
Okay people follow our cue. We had someone's dirty underwear under our bed for a whole week. Told them at the desk on the first day and after that and no one came to get them. Thank god it wasn't a dead body. We wanted to have a glass of wine but all they supplied were plastic bagged cups. Come on. The elevator were so slow. Ice buckets are made of waxed covered material and leaked all over the table and floor. Thank god we didn't have the iPad or camera on the table of anything of import ace like passports. No tooth brush holder and only body wash and conditioner which wasn't very good. Cheap stuff. No storage in bathroom for the wife to put her stuff. All had to go into desk drawers. No coffee maker in the 
room. Had to go each morning downstairs to get to morning cup and over priced coffee at that. No safety deposit box in the room but if you wanted to go and put stuff in the lobby and should you miss place the key it would cost you $150.00. Tons of room to put a box in each suite. Had to show my room to some guy each time I came in even if I went across the street to get something to eat or drink. Not a big deal unless you are loaded down with parcels or bags. Lobby sitting area you couldn't even take a coffee and sit. No drinks allowed. If you like to watch some T.V. forget about it. Something like 8 channels. One of those was about the hotel.

title: “Very enjoyable stay”
text: Our stay at the Hotel Abri was pleasant in every way. We were greeted by a very friendly desk clerk upon our arrival which was during the night. He advised us that the room left for us was nice but small and it was the best he could do as the hotel was sold out for the night. He offered to move us to a bigger room the next day when there was more availability and left directions for the day staff accordingly. In the morning they called and asked if that was still our wish. Agreeing, they asked us to pack our things so that the bellman could move them when a room was cleaned and ready. The room they moved us to was on the inside of the hotel overlooking the courtyard and was spacious, quiet, and comfortable. The staff was very friendly offering help and suggestions with sightseeing, restaurants, bus accommodations, etc. There is an Italian restaurant right off the lobby and open to the street which seemed to be a very popular spot. We did not have opportunity to eat there but did check the menu which was inviting. The hotel is nicely decorated having undergone a renovation in recent years.

title: “Good base to explore downtown San Francisco”
text:
I stayed here four nights and used it as a base to explore San Francisco.
This hotel is located a few blocks from the main road that leads to downtown, with the main tourist sights and shopping area. Though convenient during daytime, the area tends to get a little seedy at night, though I did not experience any problems myself. The hotel has a distinct style but only from the outside. Inside there is nothing special about it though.
My room was spacious and clean, with everything in working order. I guess I was lucky, as my room faced the courtyard so I did not hear any street noise. Breakfast, served in the nearby Cafe Moda (with a voucher provided by the hotel), was good and you could add items at your own wish, paying a surplus. Hotel staff was helpful and guests can use an internet PC in the lobby for free.
I'd say that overall the price/quality ratio was fair and it's a good base to explore downtown San Francisco.
Just one thing: I found out by chance that the hotel (or the staff?) has a big commission on any tour it books for its guests. So you can either request a discount or book yourself directly at the tour operator or via the internet.

title: “Great 4 days”
text: We just stayed at this hotel for 4 days and really enjoyed it. It was clean, comfortable, good views, etc. A little pricey, but you’re downtown. The location is across the street from the Convention Center, a 30 second walk. There’s a little convenience store on the sidewalk at the Convention Center. Pike's Market is 6 blocks west on Pike St (the hotel is 6th and Pike). The Seattle busses are good and cheap. Download the free iPhone app “onebusaway”. It shows all the routes, etc. You can get many busses 3 blocks away on 3rd Ave where they converge, or in the bus tunnel which can be accessed between 3rd and 4th Ave one block north of Pike, which I think is Pine. The only criticism is the top sheet on the beds feels like it is plasticized, so it crunches when you roll over. Oh, and free wi-fi is only in the lobby.

title: “Should be the Low End Studios”
text: They should rename this place to the Low End Studios. The room we stayed in was creepy to say the least. The double bed had a hollow in the middle and bed springs were about to poke through. The carpet was actually about 10 different pieces that were mashed one on top of the other and the sink was dirty and had caulking stuck all over it. It looks like they hire a trained chimp to do any of the repairs, even the doornob was painted over. The person at the front desk was about as helpful as a rock and didn't even acknowledge us standing there waiting to check in, he was more interested the person phone call he was on. The website caption says the rooms are decorated in pastels...my daughter and I found out they were way past hell !!! Forget this one...

title: “Great Location and Comfort”
text: This facility is primarily a timeshare. It is spacious with a dining area, sitting area, sink and fridge, bed and bath. The bed was the most comfortable I had slept in at a Marriott. Do not expect to cook in your unit. There is a convenience store and deli just across the street to stock up on snacks, soda and water. The breakfast room was disappointing and limited. You could get that first morning coffee to go down there, however.The views of the waterfront and Quincy Market and Boston, in general are beautiful and even better from the observation deck. Virtually everything is within walking distance including Fanuel Hall/Quincy Market, Aquarium, Children's Museum, Copley Square, the Prudential Center, shopping at Downtown Crossing or Newbury Street, the theater district, Freedom Trail, Boston Common, the North End etc. Plenty of restaurants and to do nearby.

title: “Location, location, location!”
text:
You can't beat this location: only two blocks from the subway and within comfortable walking distance of many NYC attractions, including Rockefeller Plaza, St. Patrick's Cathedral, Grand Central Station, and the UN. Our room was quiet, comfortable and classy (bathroom a little on the small side), with many amenities available. The staff was friendly and helpful, especially the concierge. Elegant lobby, too.
We're young single professionals just starting out, and probably couldn't afford the Barclay's regular rates; but we were lucky enough to find an amazing deal online, and it was worth every penny!

title: “Great hotel, great location, outstanding staff”
text: This was my first time at this hotel, even though I've been to Philadelphia tons of times. I will definitely stay at the Sofitel again - super clean, incredibly outgoing and friendly staff, great breakfast, quiet, and just a really nice place all around.

title: “Great Experience”
text:
Stayed 2 nights over Labor Day weekend for Baltimore Grand Prix. I have averaged 75 nights/year in hotels for over 30 years and this staff has to be one of the best in all my travels.
From the front desk people, the breakfast staff, the guys parking the cars and the folks cleaning the rooms, they all were the most friendly group of hotel employees I have experienced.
Hotel was very clean and close to many good places to eat. Nice to know you don't have to spend $300 and up per night to have a nice visit.

title: “Good for west end business”
text: I was in Houston for business and stayed at this hotel. It was good value for the money and was comfortable and clean. I liked the bed and the pool was nice and warm. i would stay again.

title: “Felt like a guest at a mansion”
text:
I loved this hotel and did not want to leave. I really did feel like a guest at a mansion. Our room was beautiful and spotless. I had fun just exploring the hotel, peaking in the bars and ballrooms. It is beautiful.
My family loved the pool. My kids and I played in the pool upon our arrival and I swam laps the next morning. Not the best for laps because it is difficult to see how far the wall is (without lane markers), but as a pool to relax in, it is perfect.
The breakfast had so many delicious options - an oatmeal bar, a yogurt bar, an egg/omelet station, pancakes, sausage, bacon, french toast, fresh fruit bar. My only complaint about breakfast is that the waiter was slow to refill the coffee. Half of the reason I go to breakfast is to get my coffee fix for the day and I am grumpy until I do!
If you are going to bed early, you may want to find out about noise upon check-in. We had a room above the outdoor bar, which as a couple we would have loved. But since we were with our kids we went to bed around 8:30 pm. The band at the bar played until about 9:45 pm, which is really not that late (unless you are a little kid). 
Overall I loved the hotel and would definately return.

title: “Birthday Getaway”
text: Every time we stay at the US Grant it reminds us why we love it there so much and it brings back memories of past trips. It is so centrally located to everything San Diego has to offer. It just so happened that we were there during Comic Con. That was a blast to watch. If I could change anything it would be to add in-room internet free.

title: “Nice City Hotel”
text:
Worth the money. The whole Kimpton group hotels offer a lot for the money. Rooms in general are larger than in other hotels, there is always complimentary coffee available in the morning and there is a wine happy hour in the evening in the lobby. 
The interior is very stylish, their restaurants offer a small, but very nice selection of food.
Hint: sign to the loyality programme and you will get WIFI for free as well as a voucher of USD 15 to raid the mini bar. In addition, continental breakfast is often for free as well.
Pool area could be nicer, pool in the Kimpton Palomar LA is very small, located in in the backyard surrounded by walls to protect outside view and felt very narrow.

title: “Nice hotel, nice price”
text:
We got to this hotel and had a good deal on the internet. 150$ a night on Expedia. Best part of the stay: we get there and they give us 2 rooms for that price! My friend and I wew were not looking forward to sleeping in the same bed and without asking anything...they gave each of us a room. Thank you to the really nice people at the check in counter. Nice, professionnal, super griendly. We checked our room for bed bugs...nothing everything was super clean! 
Everyone was nice at this hotel as soon as you walk in the door all the way to the check out.. Try to go for a walk around the back of the hotel to the historical street....beautiful little bars and cafe...nice restaurant. All in all a great hotel in NYC. We will sure check in the next time we are in town.

title: “Great staff”
text:
The good: the staff and the location. The ok: room amenitites and decor. The not so good: this is an old hotel that's been renovated. The rooms are evidence of this. The bathroom was tiny, the light switches barely worked, stuff was just a bit rundown. The restaurant was really expensive ($14 for oatmeal, juice and coffee?!) and $7 a day for Internet. 
But, this really is an ideal location for visiting Universal Studios and City Walk.

title: “Clean hotel. Perfect for a girls weekend!”
text:
Just stayed at this location with three of my girlfriends. The two bedroom suite that we had only had queen size beds as an option. This location would've been outstanding had we had the option to sleep in king size beds, which all of us are used to.
The room itself was lovely. Kitchen was great to have. Would have been nice to have more silverware and dishes beyond what the hotel had provided. 
The breakfast offered in the mornings was okay. It was enough to tie you over, but nothing spectacular.

title: “ABSOLUTELY AMAZING IN EVERY ASPECT!”
text:
My parnter and I recently got married and chose New York for our honeymoon destination. We spent 5 days and 4 nights and had the most fabulous, amazing time! We booked to stay at the Waldorf Astoria and when we arrived mentioned that it was our honeymoon to then be upgraded to the Towers! 
From the moment we arrived we were in heaven. The Hotel was incredible, the staff were so attentive and polite and just couldnt do enough for us and to make our stay as enjoyable as possible.
I had read other reviews about the hotel and was prepared for areas to be a little 'tired' and not quite 5* but I cant say I saw any of that. the hotel was wonderful. A few minor details showed its age, but its just that, its the most iconic hotel in New York so if you want cutting edge comtemporary then you wouldnt stay here anyway!!!
Faultless faultless faultless......except.....
We didnt seem to be able to get cold water out of our taps, always warm or even hotel, which was interesting for the toilet! However, if this is all I have to complain about then I am happy! We were offered complementary mineral water from the spa for drinking water so wasnt a problem.
Would definately stay again and was worth every penny. Although on that note I also have to say that we paid an amazing price through BA for our flight/hotel package and I can only imagine it was because they had work being carried out on exterior of hotel which meant surrounded by scaffolding?!?!? If this meant I got to be able to afford to stay in such an iconic hotel then who cares!!!!!
Bed - amazing, best nights sleep ever!
Pillows - Never had anything like them
Noise - So quiet, was prepared for noise from other reviews but we found where we were very quiet (looking out onto the Chrysler building)
All the tours pass the hotel as it features on the tour, which was handy as we just hopped off at this point of the tour and used it like a bus!
Thank you for making our honeymoon so special and memorable!

title: “get your modern day Mad Men kicks at the Pearl SD!”
text:
I came down to the Pearl this past weekend and it was an amazing hotel + experience!! I must admit I am a Mid-Century aficionado and so when I was booking my hotel, I wanted something swank, and vintage. When I discovered this place I was absolutely pulled in by it's nostalgia, it's modern, and it's location! I had planned a nice dinner at the Bali Hai, which was about oh, a 2 min. cab ride, and that made it all the better!
I stayed in the Gem, and it was a tad smaller than I expected however, the lavish amenities like the stand alone shower, the comfy bed, and ..ahem, mirrored ceilings, made the room all the better.
The pool was gorgeous, the bar was well stocked, apparently the food is delish, and the whole staff was very nice to us. I booked my room with a employee named Erika who made my stay 10 times better than expected!
I highly suggest coming to the Pearl for a nice hidden get away with someone special.

title: “Stay, Park & Fly a great value.”
text: We did the Stay, Park & Fly at the Days Inn on a recent trip to Maui. The room was clean and fine for our one night stay. We left our car for a week and the car was just as we left it when we returned. Staying and parking at the hotel was a great value and very stress free. The shuttle took us right to the airport door and picked us up after our trip.

title: “Awesome hotel, great price, great location, HUGE room”
text: We had 6 in our party including 2 teens and 2 small children -- and the room was HUGE and fantastic. Great location one block from Central Park, easy walk to Times Square, across from Russian Tea Room. The attractive staff was friendly and courteous. Great service, great price, great room, will definitely recommend AND plan to stay here again.

title: “Nice but too much noise from road.”
text:
We chose this hotel because we thought it was very central but were disappointed by it's location. Our room overlooked the freeway & was extremely noisy. When we checked in we'd asked for a quiet room, so if this was the quiet room I'd hate to stay in what they consider a noisy one! Also we didn't like the location because the walk to everything took longer than we thought.
Our room was clean except for two old coffee wrappers under the bed. In the wardrobe we found a pair of ladie's boots, obviously no-one had checked the room properly. This was the only hotel where we didn't have a 'hotel folder' explaining all the services on offer. I searched the desk etc but it was nowhere to be found.
On the plus side, the beds were lovely & comfortable with good quality crisp, white sheets. The TV was difficult to access channels but a good size.
The coffee/creamers etc were not replenished & we had to find the maid in the corridor for more supplies.
All in all I wouldn't choose to stay here again due to the noise & location. The hotel is in great condition & the rooms comfortable but you can't escape the contant drone of the freeway.

title: “Poorly run hotel”
text: I stayed here with my son and husband while we visited USC. The location is wonderful: right across the street from USC. Unfortunately, The front desk was generally unhelpful and the attitude was less than positive. There is no wifi, and when I used the Ethernet cable and attempted to download a movie on my computer, it took approximately 16 hours. There were no movies, or movie channels and the television was of poor quality. When I returned to the room in the late afternoon the privacy sign I had slid under the door when I left at 11:30 am was on the outside doorknob. At first I assumed the housekeeper had put it there after cleaning the room. However, when I entered the room there was a note from the housekeeper slid under the door which said the room was not cleaned because the privacy sign was on the doorknob. However, the privacy sign I had slid under the door upon my departure was nowhere to be found. The Housekeeping Manager was cooperative, however, the beds were comfortable and the rooms clean.

title: “Nice renovation, but lacking in details”
text:
The property has undergone a big renovation and it's a nicely updated hotel. It's a fairly small hotel adjacent to the SJ Convention Center, good value, good rooms, good location.
There were some blips, however, but nothing that cannot be easily improved.
First, our bellman brought up the wrong rack of luggage. This is why it's a good reason to always keep your personal items (such as laptop bags, etc.) on your person!! I have always thought my husband to be over-protective of his work gear, but now I see why! Our bellman was so nice and obviously kicking himself for the mix up, it's not a very big deal at all, but with the travel industry being what it is, the hotel should be aware that not everyone will see past these kinds of errors.
At 5pm, the very small pool (which is really only good for a brief cool off) was out of towels. Dirty towels were strewn everywhere with no one in sight. Now this is a common occurrence at mid-range hotels after the peak rush on the pool, however, it's a pet peeve of mine. If the pool doesn't close until 10 pm, there should always be someone tending the area until closing time. Guests should not have to call for clean towels. No excuse! 
As for the room, the coffee maker was stocked with only decaff coffee and there was no in-room dining children's menu. When I called the restaurant to ask, the person on the other line rattled off a couple things that they could make, when I called back later and asked the same question again, another person rattled off another list of items, this time including options the first person had apparently forgotten. This is simple, print up some children's menus, stock up on plastic cups with lids and have them available for guests! Lots of hotels do this and we parents really appreciate it. 
There was a definite lack of kid-friendly channels, Disney shows were considered paid viewing which I have never seen done before! I've never stayed at a hotel where the Disney and Nickelodeon channels have not been accessible. Augh.
There was a hair on the bathroom counter, which was kinda gross, but not a big deal. It happens. The lack of other things (towels, menus, etc.) were more annoying. Hairs happen, it's a hotel room, not an operating room. However, it's a hotel and the amenities have to be here to make it like a home away from home! 
Hopefully these things will be improved. I can't say I'd be staying here again, though. At first I thought it'd be a nice place to stay during December when SJ has its Christmas in the Park, but I might rethink this plan.
But let's end on a positive note:
Location is nice, no airport noise although it's fun to see the planes pass by. Updated rooms are nice, room is spacious, really like the tiled entry. Starbucks is nice to have! Like the toiletries from Crabtree & Evelyn and the desk work space. Nice fitness area. Comfy bed with plenty of pillows!

title: “Worth returning: Comfortable and great location”
text:
We had booked our reservations online. We had gotten a pretty good rate, but when we arrived there, we were told the rate we had was a computer error and instead of $139, they had to charge us $199.
We weren't happy paying more for the same room, so management offered us a better room: newly renovated, on the top floor with a fabulous view. We were surprised to see we had a living room separate from the bedroom. The furnishings were really nice and all in Art Deco style. 
The bed was really comfortable and to me, having a white duvet on the bed just reassures me that it IS clean. There were too many pillows on the bed to sleep in, but really useful for reading in bed.
I really enjoyed my stay, I'll be back!

title: “Very Nice ~ Easy Access to The Rose Bowl”
text:
We recently stayed at the Hilton in Woodland Hills and we were very pleased. We drove in from Fresno to attend the Rose Bowl, Oregon vs. Ohio State. It was easy to find and we chose it for its easy 20 mile straight shot to Pasadena. Very nice accommodations, we had a great king room on the corner with a nice view of the hills and the price per night was really reasonable for the New Year/Rose Bowl time frame. Woodland Hills is a sweet little area just NW of Hollywood and Universal Studios is very close. The Hilton location in Woodland Hills offered great places to eat nearby and a huge shopping center within walking distance. Woodland Hills is clean and feels safe. 
We will definitely come back here.

title: “OK due to few hotels for college graduation”
text:
This is an average hotel for the person going to Boston who is not using the nearby medical facilities. Yes, the reception staff were friendly. The rate at over $300/night before taxes for a large room with basic kitchen facilities (but oddly lack of full set for four of utensils, glassware, and plates) was really too much except for the fact it was college graduation season. We had two other rooms with two beds at about $250 per night. We booked these rooms over 11 months in advance due to lack of Boston availability. 
The attached mall is really minimal. The hotel is close the the public transportation. The restaurant is OK for basic food (e.g. salads, burgers, soups and breakfast).
The hallways are really dreary and a bit dark. 
The hotel served its purpose as a basic sleep option, but I would not return. It was an expensive hotel three night stay for just average or a bit below accommodations. It was really not a Best Western Plus experience.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
I am writing to thank everyone at the Charlotte Executive Park Marriott for a great stay. I have traveled with Marriott since '83. All personnel here are excellent in every regard. Chad & Tracy in the rooms management department arranged our reservation & did a super job. My wife & I are celebrating our 45th wedding anniversary & Chad & Tracy went beyond the call of duty to make it special. 
Housekeeping kept our room super clean, the workout facilities were maintained beautifully, the am & pm conscierge personnel were super, the restaurant personnel were great, the valet people were super--everyone here cares about their guests.
Thank you Charlotte Executive Park Marriott!
John F. Sanders
000-796-730

title: “Convenience and Cookies”
text: We booked a queen room with a pullout sofa online for our family consisting of mother, father and a tall teen son. When we checked in the pullout sofa ended up being a pullout chair. We called the front desk and they sent someone up immediately. She took one look at our son and said that the pullout chair was unacceptable for someone his size and she wanted him to be comfortable and walked us to a queen/queen room at no additional cost, We were so greatful and impressed with their promptness and accomodation to our needs. The hotel is compact, but clean, modern, well appointed and well staffed. It is conveniently located in the flower district and between two subway lines (7th Ave and Broadway) making it very easy to get to anywhere in the city. Walking down the street and seeing and smelling the flowers was amazing. The breakfast was pretty typical but the ambiance of being in an atrium type of atmosphere was nice and made you feel a little New Yorkish. And at the end of a long day of walking in the city who doesn't want to come back to their hotel to a batch of cookies waiting for them?

title: “Thanks Trip Advisor”
text:
We love New York. I was disappointed when we could not get reservations at the Super 8 on 46th Street for Veterans Day weekend and had to look for another location. The Boston Globe had an advertisement for Riverside Hotel and Suites, but after reading the reviews on Trip Advisor, we decided to keep looking. Based on the reviews in this forum, we chose the Hotel Grand Union for our seventh visit to New York this year. (we only live three hours away by car)
From check in to check out, everything was great. Since we are a family of four, the quad was the way to go. My daughters were quite happy they did not have to share a bed. We were able to check in @ 11:30 am and left the car in a parking garage on the next block for $ 20.00 per night. The room was recently updated with a marble bath and nice comforters. It even had a small refrigerator!
For meals in the neighborhood, we ate at the Barking Dog, Notaro, Captains Cafe, the Murray Hill Diner and New York Kom Tang. We were pleased with all of these establishments and would like to thank everyone who made recommendations. 
In the past we have stayed at the Marriott Marquis, the Sheraton Midtown Manhattan and the Super 8. Since so little time is spent in the room, I prefer the less expensive options. I really enjoyed the Murray Hill area neighborhood and will certainly go back again.

title: “the service is great: timely, thoughtful and truly hospitable”
text: The Warwick is tucked a block behind the once grand San Francis. This was our second stay there--and the Warwick will certainly be our first choice next time we are in SFO! The rooms are compact but very well laid out and comfortable. I cannot think of a better value for the location and the service--which is unfailingly offered with a smile!

title: “Great View!”
text: The hotel itself is grand. It has an interesting history. The rooms are a bit on the small side and no microwave, but the comfort was great and the room was very clean. The pool is like a step back in time. I took pictures but didn't swim in it. The location of this hotel can/t be beat! It is right in the heart of shopping and eating. It is walking distance to Navy pier. It is a short trolley ride to the museums. The view was outstanding and can't be beat. I watched the sunrise over Lake Michigan every morning. Incredible. Mostly I am easy to please, but the inability to reheat leftovers was annoying. We had to eat out EVERY MEAL. The fridge was stocked and overpriced(like 4 dollars for a bag of M n Ms and 6,95 for bottled water). So we couldnt use the fridge either. My bedroom at home might be bigger than the room was. The tv was large and flat screen and awesome for watching tv but we didnt watch a lot of it. Too busy seeing the sights. Overall it was neat but I have stayed at other places that were even better and DIDN'T cost an arm and a leg per night.

title: “Perfect for our Family”
text: This hotel was picked for several reasons that were important for our family. Location (close to Gershwin theatre with Wicked) and subway stations, free Breakfast (hot with plenty of choices), free 24 hr coffee/tea/hot chocolate and apples for snacking, Queen beds instead of double beds. Our family has 2 teens so breakfast saved us a bundle each day. Coming back to the hotel after our busy sightseeing days, the free hot drinks and apples were a welcoming touch. We also appreciated the queen beds instead of doubles which with teens sharing a bed is a must for keeping the peace. Next door to the hotel are plenty of food choices and a drug store for things forgotten. Laundry mat down the street was helpful when drenched with tennis shoes at Statue of Liberty (45 minutes later and 6 quarters problem was solved). Hotel was even able to accomodate a late check out after they checked their schedule when we asked them. We were able to leave directly from hotel to airport which was a nice way to end our stay since we were exhausted. No complaints.

title: “Not Bad”
text:
My girlfriend and I wanted to stay at a hotel 
that was more personal then the large chain ones. We found Harborside Inn on the internet. The room was not at all like what was on their web site. The web has pictures of hardwood floors and brick wall in the room we slelected. Upon arrival we found out the Inn was still under construction and the room was not at all what we see on line. The location of the Inn is perfect. The employees were very nice and helpful. The room was very clean but had very poor lighting. The price was fair. 
We would stay there again but this time we will have a more detailed talk the the front desk.

title: “Hip & Happy Hotel”
text:
I had my reservations about staying in a "rock" hotel. They didn't last long. The central courtyard was an ideal place to hang out as we were traveling with friends. I loved all the art features and the ambient night lighting. The local area is certainly "colourful" and I was more comfortable taking taxis at night. The staff were extremely helpful and friendly. Breakfast at first glance looks average. But when I sat and enjoyed mine by the pool - the coffee was excellent, and there was a regularly replenished selection of great pastries. My one request/ suggestion would be a greater selections of juices.
