All in all - I would go back for sure.

title: “Highly Recommended”
text:
I spent 11 nights at the Hotel Rouge and it was one of the best experiences that I have had. Being a botique hotel I expected a very small room, and was quite surprised at the size of the room. At first I thought that because I was staying there for almost 2 weeks that had upgraded my room - but I peaked in a few other rooms (while the were being cleaned) and most of them were as large or larger.
The room was well appointed with King Size Bed, dressing area, modern ammenities and Aveda products. And the hotel staff keeps the rooms very impecably cleaned. The hotel offers free high-speed internet access. This was very helpful in checking e-mails and purchasing tickets for sporting events, attractions or theater.
The only disadvantage, was the view - I was on the back side of the hotel - so while this is the more quite area - it did overlook the employee parking area.
Every afternoon they do offer a happy hour serving various Red Wines, RedStar Beer and other "Red" themed drinks. Most of the time I was out touring the city and therefore did not have the opportunity to endulge in this ammenity
The staff was very helpfull and were able to recommend several excellent restuarants within a 7-8 block walking area. In addition, they work with a spa and can arrange in room massages or other treatments.
The hotel is located off of Scott Circle. And unfortunately, you will need to walk a good 10-15 minutes to reach a Metro station.

title: “Union League Club of Chicago (ULC) - Great Rooms too! + Library”
text:
I have also posted a review about the greatness of the ULC but this time I have had also a room. The rates are great and the comfort, size, and coziness of the room outstanding. if you want to be in the city and have great access to the financial district, sights, restaurants - all in walking distance - chose this hotel. Again their valet is great and everyone is so nice. The food at the club is also well done - and it is a great conference, large meeting club. There are rules, which need to be followed but nobody would ever be rude about it - ever.
The library service is very nice. You can book a room to do your phone calls, just sit a round and read and enjoy!
I love this place and now that I know about their great room rates for Chicago for a clean comfortable room - I am even happier about it!
Job well done ULC!

title: “Nice downtown hotel”
text: Very nice hotel, close to pike place and all the other fun downtown stuff. Beds are super comfy, room is clean and nicely appointed. Easy walk to monorail and lots of great downtown shopping. Check in was super fast and the gentleman at the desk was very friendly. You are right on pine street, which is a busy urban street, so some street noise is to be expected on the lower floors. We will stay here again.

title: “Nice resort with so-so staff”
text: Stayed here 3 days with coworkers for a conference, and I must say that the hotel and grounds are beautiful. Catering was excellent too! We did not have time to for any of the outdoor activities, but I would like to return to experience the pool and lazy river. For me, the only negative was that mixed quality of service received from employees - particularly at the front desk. A few people were helpful, but others acted like they would rather be anywhere else.

title: “Definately a business hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed at Club Quarters several times over a six month period in 2007-2008. We finally decided to look for other accomodations, so I though I'd write the pros and cons to help others decide if it is right for them.
It is definitely a great place to stay for a few nights if you are a single business traveler and have business in the Financial District. The price is much lower than other hotels in the area. But the rooms are also small and rather unremarkable. The decor is various shades of dark blue, so the rooms are not what I would call "cheerful". Staying for a week or two at a time, it actually became depressing.
Also, for a long stay, there are not many restaurant choices. The main meal in the financial district is lunch, so if you want breakfast or dinner, your choices are limited without going for at least a 20 minute walk in any direction.
Pluses are that the hotel is safe and very clean and staff is very friendly. They arranged for me to use one of their conference rooms at no change when I needed to hold a business meeting and then have amenities helpful to a business traveler like being able to print documents from your laptop.
But I wouldn't recommend it for a vacation or honeymoon.

title: “Nice location for a conference”
text: Convenient, professional and dependable. Building is a bit worn, hallways are dingy BUT once you reach your room it is quiet and warm. Staff were helpful and responsive to the minor issues that came up. Restaurant although a bit pricey is excellent (try the crab bisque it is outstanding). Love this hotel for conferences b/c the facilities are convenient and food service is brilliant.

title: “great hotel”
text: I went with my wife and family for a week on the 10 feb 2006 for our silver wedding anniversary. The hotel was excellent,rooms very good,staff very friendly and helpful,especially "felix" who was on the front desk.Great location to see everything you want to see and do.Lots of places to eat.I would reccomend this hotel to anyone.We were there in time for the snow blizzard,we went to central park to make a snowman because my daughter had never seen such so much snow before.Would tell people this place is worth a visit.Would like to come back sometime.

title: “Great staff with a beautiful roof top view”
text: the stay was excellent the staff was very helpful when we needed anything the was no long waut the staff made sure we were comfortable and at ease the refreshments were excellent for a before bed snack and the morning breakfast was deliscious too. the gym and pool area was excellent the Hotel was clean and well decorated.

title: “Excellent throughout, modern, clean, great location!”
text: Fantastic place to stay! Brand new hotel means clean room, functional, equipped with IPAD in each one of them, light etc. We loved our stay there. Brilliant location - very central. Great service. Comfortable beds. We also got great service from the concierge who advised us and arranged most of our visits. Couldn't recommend this hotel enough!

title: “Brilliant location, very helpful and friendly staff”
text:
I spoke to reservations at the hotel and they advised me to become a "Grand guest" as I would get a discount when booking online. I was concerned about the noise from the bar after reading other reviews and so requested a high floor room. We were given early check in and I was really pleased to see we had a 6th floor room (there are 8 floors). Each floor has a coffee machine, which also provides hot chocolate and hot water - which was brilliant for tea-making after a hard days shopping! There's also an ice machine. The room was quite spacious (we upgraded) and had a good view over Avenue of the Americas. The only noisy night was a Thursday when a DJ played in the bar for a party. But once the door is shut we couldn't hear anything. The white noise machine sound like teh air-con but it wasn't needed. I thing noise may be more of an issue if you are on lower floor.
The hotel is ideally situated if you want to shop downtown in the SoHo area, but it is also 5 minutes walk away from Canal Street which has loads of different subway lines to all parts of the city. Getting a cab is very easy too as the hotel is at the intersection of 2 main roads. The hotel staff were incredibly friendly and helpful. We asked the concierge to recommend bars, restaurants, diners which were really good. Ask for the shopping map as it has all the shops in the SoHo, NoHo area as well as uptown.
This is a great hotel to stay in if you want to be able to access all parts of the city easily but want the feeling of a local neighbourhood. Great shops and bars in easy walking distance and they are friendly and helpful in the hotel.

title: “Exceptional Staff!”
text: This was my second stay at this hotel and I was once again pleasantly surprised! The hotel staff, from the concierge to the front desk staff, were very helpful and friendly. Everyone always had a smile on their face and went out of their way to make the trip enjoyable! Room service was a little pricey for a basic sandwich, but the quality of the food was good. There is also a little coffee shop in the lobby that has excellent hot chocolate and wonderful service!

title: “Great Hotel!!”
text:
The hotel's location is great, close to everything! 5-10 minutes walk from broadway, 3 minutes walk to the fifth avenue and 2 mintes walk to the central park, with a subway station right next to the hotel!
the rooms where pretty and very clean, just like living in New York.. we went to a close supermarket and bought food, and in the morning we ate in our room, since we had a nice small kitchen in our room and a small dining place..
every room is decorated differently since it's a boutique hotel.. 
the view was great, and the staff were very nice!
next to the hotel there is a nice deli and in a short walk you can enjoy an amazing italian restaurant with the best pizza in the world!!

title: “Great stay, Great location, Great staff”
text:
I booked with the hotel website after comparing expedia, hotels.com, and orbitz...it was twenty dollars cheaper per night. The hotel is chic and tiny. I would much rather have good service and clean/trendy atmosphere than a crappy mega/anonymous chain.
When we went to our room it reeked of cigarettes, though we were on a non-smoking floor. I called and they immediately sent a maid with an ionizer and deoderizer...since I was still not satisfied, I asked for a manager who brought us keys to our new room in five minutes flat.
Everyone was friendly, gave good directions, and the bell hop stood in the middle of the street to get us a cab. As a same-sex couple we were treated very well by all staff (which means a lot to us).
Would stay again as it is close to time square, subways, and walking distance to trendy part of 5th ave.

title: “Great Hotel, great location”
text:
I travel frequently to DC for business, but this trip was for sight-seeing and pleasure. The Homewood is a terrific hotel in a very good location. The staff was always cordial, the hotel was always clean, and while the morning breakfast was not as good as most Embassy Suites (where I normally stay), it was still pretty good. At night, there was also food and free drinks on Monday through Thursdays; all in all a very good deal.
As far as location, it is at Thomas Circle on the NW side, about 3 to 4 blocks to a couple different Metro lines (Red or Blue/Orange) while the Green/Yellow lines are a little farther. Of course, it is very simple to switch lines at the stations which cross. You can catch the Blue line at National Airport and get out 4 blocks from the Homewood in 22 minutes for about 3 1/2 bucks. The National Mall is about a 20 minute walk if you want some exercise.
Many good restaurants/grills/ taverns close by, also a Whole Foods 4 blocks away. Check the "ThaiTanic" on 14th street; corny name, outstanding Thai food reasonably priced for DC. 
If you are looking for a place with a suite and a small kitchen, this is it.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: I have stayed at this hotel 4 times. We stay here mainly for nights out in Broadripple. It is about a $15 cab ride from Broadripple, and the front desk will call the cab for you! The cab is always there within 10-15 minutes even on busy nights such as Halloween and New Years. Last time we got a coupon from the front desk for the cab company and got 15% off our ride! :) The staff is always very friendly, and the check in and check out process is easy. The rooms are clean! I have stayed in the studio rooms (1 bed, a pull out sofa, and a kitchen) and the double rooms (2 beds in seperate rooms with doors that shut and lock, a pull out sofa, and a kitchen) and they were both great, and worth the money! I love the kitchens. We have brought food to cook, you can bring drinks and they stay cold, or you can heat up leftovers after a night out! The hotel has always been quiet when we stayed here as well. The breakfast in the morning is pretty good. It isn't the most spectacular, and the lobby is small, but its decent. They have frozen waflles, bagles, muffins, danishes, fruit, cereal, and oatmeal. They also have a little snack bar that is there all the time that you can buy things from! The ONLY problem I have with this hotel is their pet policy, and even that isn't that bad. The last time we stayed here, we brought our dog with us because we didn't have anyone to watch him overnight. I was glad that the hotel accepted pets. I think that is great! However, it is a $50 non-refundable charge regardless of how long your pet will be staying. That is a GREAT deal if you're going to be there a week or longer. However, for just one night it is a little pricey. I know I could have probably boarded him for less, but we like to take him with us so we paid it. I just wish there was a better deal for 1 night. Maybe you could get your money back, or half of it if the dog didn't tear anything up. Or maybe it could just be a little cheaper? Other than that, no problems at all! Stay here if you're looking for a nice hotel that is close to everything, but feels tucked away and quiet!

title: “Amazing! Unbelievable! Stay here!!”
text: The Conrad hotel is beautiful. The staff are curteous and helpful. The rooms are spacious and comfortable. The bathroom was twice the size of my bathroom at home! The location is perfect - right near Michigan Ave. I couldn't find anything wrong with this hotel. It was a great stay!

title: “Pros & Cons of downtown Memphis Crowne Plaza”
text: Only 1 table lamp = dark , lots of mirrors but not enough light to see well. Sink s l o w to drain, not enough towels & slow to get them. It was clean and the beds were comfortable. Staff was very pleasant. Especially, Terrence the van driver. Free van service to close areas. There was NOTHING close by to do or to walk to for eating, etc. It was right by the interstate.

title: “The location is very good the service not so much.”
text: The mega room is the way to go here as it is the size of an average room you would get outside of the city. The staff are nice enough and well meaning but there is no attention to detail so if you are looking for a room close to Time Square and don't need anything from the staff this would be fine. If you are the type of person that likes room service, concierge services or pretty much anything else that the staff would provide this is not the hotel for you.

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: Stayed for 7 nights in mid march, perfect place to use as a base while staying in Phoenix, Clean room, good food, and great staff. The maid service was outstanding. We asked at the front desk for extra coffee for our room and by the time we got to our room there was someone waiting with with it at our door. I dont understand some of the complaints about this property because we never had any issues whatsoever

title: “Staff that makes you feel like your home”
text:
I have been traveling to Chicago for three years and this hotel has been the most welcoming and responsive to my needs over this three year span. It is also a good value but the real reason I stay there is the staff.
The rooms are spacious for a downtown location. They are also clean and attractively furnished even if they are a little "stiff". The cleaning staff is very efficent and have managed to find things that I left long after my check out!
The complimentary breakfast does leave something to be desired but it is never a reason I would chose any hotel.

title: “Great location and pleasant, helpful staff”
text: A great downtown location and an upbeat, helpful staff are the highlights of this hotel. We were attending a trade show at the convention center and this hotel was only four blocks away. In addition, we were steps away from "restaurant row" on 13th street (which intersects Walnut Street) where numerous, trendy restaurants were at our disposal. For those of you who like to shop, Walnut Street is lined with fashionable stores (exit the hotel and go right). The staff was very hospitable, especially Gwen who quickly checked us in, two hours early! The only negatives were the poor lighting in the bathroom (a problem when applying makeup) and a noisy air-conditioning unit that struggled to get the humidity out of the room.

title: “Enjoyed the Old Town Inn”
text: My husband and I stayed 3 nights at the Old Town Inn the first week of January 2012. I was pleasantly surprised. The property was well kept, included an extended breakfast and was very close to Old Town. There was a small pool but we did not use it. You could park in front of your room which I liked. If we did not stay here we probably never would have known Old Town existed.

title: “Not Impressed”
text: For our first time in Beverly Hills, I was dissapointed. This hotel certainly is beautiful but the bar and so-called restaurant is tiny, (with a disengaged and inattentive staff). We were with my in laws who have health restrictions and our rooms were up several flights of stairs-the bellman are required to even carry luggage up and down these many levels! It does make it private with lots of little sitting areas and abundant landscaping but it should be stressed that most (if not all) rooms require outdoor access and limited elevator access. The guests must be impressed with themselves because most were rude and pretentious, one little boy even blocket my way through a hallway and stood in front of the ATM while I tried to use it while the front desk clerks and his mother all looked on-I was mortified! Also-this hotel is not convenient to walk to any restaurants we wanted to try. I will definitley stay at one of the many alternatives on my next visit.

title: “Loved esp. hotel-restaurant”
text:
The hotel room was OK, but what impressed me most was the kind reception in the hotel restaurant. Very friendly staff, going out of their way to please.
Breakfast executive style 10 dollar good value for the money
The concierge very helpful to organize shuttle service to int.airport. Taxi would cost 50 dollars, shuttle at 15 dollars pp. 
I can recommend PRIME TIME SHUTTLE , red vans.
(733 8267)
In L.A. I found a visit to Hollywood and there a round trip Open deck bus most enjoyable, starts at Chinese Theatre ( hop on - hop off)

title: “Extremely Pleasant Experience”
text: I booked a room at the InterContinental without knowing what to expect of the hotel itself and their staff. I usually book whatever is available during the conventions I attend, so I have no expectations. However, I was immediately welcomed by the fantastic hotel attendants the moment I stepped in. The entire weekend I was met with enthusiastic, friendly staff members and consistently excellent service. The rooms themselves were absolutely gorgeous and spacious. I had even managed to get a room upgrade at no extra charge thanks to the incredibly sweet front desk associate. I am so pleased with this experience that I fully expect to return the next year for the next convention. I highly recommend this hotel and you will definitely not be disappointed by your stay.

title: “bad experience with this homewood”
text: We stay this last weekend room 517, the room was not very clean the bath was very nasty in the outside, the front of the sink had soap splash all over, the floor was nos clean and the kitchen had some rice from previous customers. the cleaning people were horrible when I asked for some spoons one of them hand me a dirty one and told me to wash it, and the last thing when we sleep I notice some smell in the bed so I marked the sheets and pillow cases just to bee sure, and no wonder they did nos change them. We love Homewood and were very shock to see how bad this particular one is.

title: “Clean, comfortable, good price”
text: We stayed here in March while in town for a concert at Highline Ballroom. Room is small-ish, but to be expected in NYC. We had a king and had enough room, so no problems, just a little smaller than you might expect with other Hampton Inns. Valet parking was easy, they will take your car from the front door and bring it back when you want. Hotel did have some construction while we were there bu I am sure it is completed now. It did not bother us. I would certainly stay here again in NYC unless we really needed to be further uptown.

title: “need to stay a night near the airport? this is it.”
text: We stayed here for one night. We found the rooms to be spacious. No bathtub basin, only a shower stall in the room we were in. The pool is indoor, but it's small. The hot tub is lukewarm at best. There are three (3) computers set up for internet access, which is very convenient. Compared with other free continental breakfasts provided by other Best Western hotels, in my opinion, this breakfast was above average. This hotel would meet your needs if your staying one night and then off the night morning, and you'd like to be near the airport. Location is absolutely NOT within walking distance to any of the Seattle attractions. Overall, this place fit our needs and was adaquate.

title: “Not so grand.”
text: The hotel was nice enough. The room was spacious and the bathroom was very nice.The only thing is it wasn't a very big hotel as the name might lead you to believe.The lobby was very small and the outdoor entrance was even smaller. They had started to remodel the entrance a couple of days before we left on July 8th, 2010. They had nice fresh fruit and nice cold water for the guests which was a welcome after a day of sightseeing. No concierge in sight. I like hotels on a grander scale.

title: “Grand, old, and worn”
text:
Stayed here three nights for a conference at the same hotel. 
The "poor" rating comes from a simple fact: the air conditioning in my room was (per the "engineer" who arrived after a call) was not adjustable. The fan was on high and the temperature was 62 degrees. The temperature setting is only adjustable for heat in the winter... for the summer the only way to get this room warmer than 62 degrees was to turn everything off (which at least quieted the a/c fan) and let the temp gradually rise. 
Rather not quite suitable for a hotel that uses the "luxury" word on its website. And nobody I talked to seemed especially concerned about any of this. "It is what it is" attitude seems to prevail. If you want something different like actual temperature controls, go someplace else.
Phone system was erratic as well... each time I pushed a marked button some other function answered the phone and then switched me to the right location.
Bathroom had been refurbished and there was a flat screen TV. The chair in the room and the desk were covered with scratches and gouges. And don't expect to charge many electrics at once. The desk had a single outlet in the lamp base. The next place to charge anything was in the bathroom. Way behind modern standards. 
I was in the "Towers" area on the 15th or top floor. The hall ways themselves are clean and wide. Probably very fine in the 1920s.
Conference meeting rooms... again also not up to usual modern standards, especially acoustics.

title: “AN EXCELLENT CITY HOTEL”
text:
We stayed at the Commonweaalth for 4 nights during our first visit to Boston. We could not be more impressed. Our welcome at the door when we arrived, the friendliness and efficiency of the staff at the front desk and our large and beautifully appointed room all exceeded our expectations.
Add to this the excellent restaurants, the metro station next door and the easy access to the hop on hop off tourist bus and to Newbury street and other attractions then you have the perfect base for explorating this wonderful city.

title: “Feels like home to me”
text: I stay at this hotel whenever I can. I come to Seattle for work about 5-10 times a year and am always so bummed when it's sold out for a conference. It's like coming home. It's usually cheaper or the same price as the Westin Seattle, but it's so much better! It was completely redone a few years ago and you can tell. The lobby is beautiful, the rooms are very nice, and the work-out center is top-notch - it's on the top floor and overlooks the whole city. There is also an indoor pool and hot-tub up there as well. The people are so friendly who work the front desk and there is a restaurant and a small cafe to pick up lattes and bagels in the morning. it's also in a great location walkable to Nordstrom and the shopping mall as well as tons of great restaurants.

title: “Great Service”
text: Front desk staff were excellent, actively looked for ways to be of assistance, remembered our names, went the extra mile. Clean and quiet. Would stay there again.

title: “Small, miniscule rooms....”
text:
I booked the Hudson due to a market show we were attending for business. Special rate of $149 seemed very reasonable offered through the show. I believe the saying, "You get what you pay for," applies here.
The positive - staff were very helpful. The interior architecture and design for the restaurants and reception area are very interesting (albeit dark) and the outdoor dining spaces are lovely.
The negative - Rooms took small to a whole new level. This was the smallest, and most oddly designed room, we've ever stayed in - including all our travels in the US and Europe. Total square footage is 160 sq. feet for their standard rooms - same size as those teeny-tiny rooms on most cruise ships - however lacking all the cruise ship's clever storage areas. 
The bathroom was so small, all 5'3" of me could hardly move - and I'm described as petite! My poor 6'0" husband just laughed when he saw it. The miniscule tub had very poor drainage and the shower flow was poor. Things didn't look to me to be as clean as I would have liked it.
I was told the hotel had been a dorm or women's hostel at some point prior to being converted to The Hudson. The rooms still have that feel although they've added funky lighting.
Our joint advice - save your money to dine here and stay elsewhere - unless of course you prefer small, closed spaces.

title: “Very disappointing”
text: The most positive point about this hotel is that the rooms are spacious and reasonably well equipped. On the other hand the hotel itself is isolated. There is practically nothing to do in the immediate neighborhood except perhaps walking to the southern end of China town which apparently is neither very attractive nor very safe. The restaurant and deli shop attached to the hotel are of very low quality. The (not so cheap) breakfast is lamentable. The staff is indifferent.

title: “Priceliners alert!”
text:
I travel frequently on business, always staying at five diamond properties. Personal travel is another story -- I look for the best deals out there. I booked a weekend trip to San Francisco on Priceline, and "won" a four star hotel room. Turned out to be the St. Francis.
Good
Location can't be beat. The property is located in the heart of Union Square.
Check-in took no more than 2 minutes. The front desk was impressive, faster than I ever experienced in my life.
The room was available 2 hours early.
Room Service was polite and prompt.
Valet parking ($40, typical of car-hating San Francisco) was slow, but friendly and satisfactory.
Bed and linens were quite good; this is Westin's come-on.
Shower had great pressure, with two Speakman shower heads. Toiletries were of high quality.
Bad
Room was tiny, almost cell-like, similar to older "manor" hotels like the NY Plaza. The extra tall ceilings helped alleviate claustrophobia.
It was obviously a smoking room as the stench of cigars lingered throughout my stay -- I smoke, but even one star hotels do a better job of airing their rooms.
Walls were paper thin -- bring ear plugs if you want a good night's sleep.
The furniture looked like they were bought at a garage sale.
The bathroom had outdated tile, moldy grout and a vanity made of plywood that looked like a coal bin -- difficult to describe.
Room faced an alley.
I had to request room cleaning. I was told it was it was their policy to clean only upon request. OUTRAGEOUS.
I paid $80 a night. I developed a mantra: What do you want for 80 bucks? Helped me enjoy my weekend, and turn a blind eye to the darker side of the Westin St. Francis. The room definitely was worth every penny I paid. But not a penny more.

title: “Find a Better Deal”
text:
Great deal at $149/night (not including exorbitant room tax and mandatory resort fee). 
But, because of this rate I have to first share a little about the guests...this place was horrible and attracts an element of people and families that are classless. During our stay we had the "luck" to be neighbors to about 100 teenage girls who were in town for a basketball tournament. Yikes! The girls were rude and loud well into the night. Three calls per night to security were made to quiet the girls down. Wouldn't you know it, security never showed up. The girls were also never taught that trash goes into trash cans.
On to the hotel review. Property is huge getting in the right room is tricky because if you don't you will end up walking miles in desert heat. Waterpark is nothing like they market it. It's a real shame because it has potential. Room itself needs updating. TV's definitely need to be replaced. Staff was okay. Bell staff for the most part were good, courteous and friendly. Housekeeping staff was horrible. We didn't get soap in our room until day 2 out of 4. Furnishings and carpets were rarely cleaned. In fact, during my checkout sweep to make sure we didn't leave anything behind I found a moldy bag of opened cheetos under the bed. How sick is that?
The only nice thing I have to say about the property is this...restaurants were good. Aunty Chilada's, Rustler's Rooste, and the lobby restaurant were good. Staff was excellent and prices were decent.
To reiterate, find another place to stay. The Hilton's and Marriot's all have waterpark type pools without touting them to be more than they really are AND their rooms are much better and cleaner.

title: “Lovely rooms, great service, all in the heart of downtown.”
text: Modern room design, except for the kitchenette in our suite. Looked like an 80's apartment. But the rest of the suite was designed well and elegant. The staff is always pleasant, and the cookies and milk treat each night is a bonus.

title: “It's got a free wine bar, what more do you want?”
text:
I'm generally ambivalent towards Best Western hotels. They're my go to hotel chain when I can't seem to find a funky, interesting hotel where I am. So when I saw that a Best Western was number one in Houston hotels, I was quite surprised. Since I was going to be in Houston for a week and they had a weekly rate, I decided to give it a try. I must say that I was really impressed.
The first thing I noticed was the staff. The guy at the desk was more than a standard clerk. He was extremely friendly, made great chit chat and was able to give me outstanding advice regarding the local area. He even offered to get my bags for me but I declined so he could help another guest. He remembered my name throughout my stay and always seemed to be interested in my day. This guy has no business being a hotel front desk clerk, he should be doing something way better.
As a mini suite, the rooms have a small refrigerator, a microwave and a coffee maker. There is no stove or cooking equipment. This was fine with me as I can't make breakfast cereal without setting something on fire. The rooms were very clean and extremely well maintained with a couch and coffee table as well as a desk. The wifi worked fine but wasn't quite fast enough to download a youtube video. The beds were not quite soft but not quite firm, somewhere in between. It was quite comfy and I slept quite nicely.
The pool was clean and maintained. The gym was a little small with only a single multigym, a treadmill and a cross trainer. It was enough but a little crowded if more than one person was using the gym. Breakfast was the standard Best Western breakfast, if you've ever stayed at a Best Western you've had this breakfast. What wasn't standard was the wine bar that was served from 4pm to 7pm, all free. It was something I've never encountered in a hotel before, even the five stars.
One thing to be aware of is that the hotel is not in the best of neighborhoods. Be cautious if walking out by yourself at night. I would recommend everyone staying at this hotel have a car.
Final thought: If coming to west Houston, it's hard to beat the Best Western.

title: “Great location, nice suites and happy hour”
text: Terriific location in central Seattle, close to Conv center, hospitals and short walk to Pike St Market.

title: “Fabulous!”
text: The Galleria Park Hotel is in a great location in San Francisco, but what will make me return in the graciousness of the staff, the beautifully appointed rooms, and the "family" feel of events such as the free wine happy hour in the lobby each evening. I also know that the management is a local "good citizen" in that they support local non-profit organizations by donating gift certificates for raffles and other fundraising efforts. Kudos all around to the Galleria Park!

title: “Great at Special On Line Price”
text: Arrived when hotel not full and given upgrade from basic smaller room booked at bargain on line rate to very nice queen in quiet location by exceptionally nice staff. Very comfortable bed, nice linens and toiletries, good temperature control in very tastefully decorated room. Murray Hill location has many advantages and for those willing to take subway stop on useful North South Line for many sites of interest only a block away on Park Avenue.

title: “For the price it was ok.”
text: I have stayed in a few Westin hotels in my time, and this one was a little less modern than the others I have stayed in. The lobby and restaurant were great and so was the service. No complaints there. The room was a little dated. Bathroom was older, but not bad. My room overlooked the roof with old tennis courts with ac units sitting on top of them. I would stay there again, but not at the price of a newer Westin.

title: “Very cool place to stay”
text: Room was very nice, bed was comfortable. Very clean and stylish. A/C was cold and had a very nice stay. Lots of places to eat within walking distance.

title: “Great New Hotel!”
text:
I stayed at the new JW Marriott for 4 nights for a recent conference and was very impressed. The rooms are very nice with all of the new technology. Laptops can even be connected to the big screen TVs! I stayed in one of the rooms on the upper floors so I had access to the Executive Suite which was also very nice to use as a break from my room. Complimentary beverages and snacks as well as big screen TVs and computers are available in the suite. An exercise room is also available, however I didn't have a chance to use it.
The hotel is located within walking distance of most everything downtown, restaurants, clubs, shopping ... even Conseco Fieldhouse and Lucas Oil Field.The views are great - some of the rooms overlook the ampitheater, the river and the park. The staff was exceptionally friendly and very helpful. The food was good, too. I believe there is a Starbucks that will be opening on the 2nd floor in the next couple of months. If there were any downsides, I would say the self-parking fee was a bit high ($28/day) and the daily fee for internet dial-up was $12.95, but I believe there is free wireless in the lounge.
Overall, it was a very pleasurable experience and I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Trapped in NY”
text:
Hotel at check in was the last pleasant part of the stay. Checked and found no bed bugs was reassuring. The room was cramped. The bathroom dated, cramped and the shower controls were broken with little to no hot water. 
The worst part was the checkout and the doorman who was trying to move patrons to taxis and ignored anyone with car service.

title: “Nice hotel, good service-- problem with Private events”
text: As per previous reviews, we also encountered closure of the outdoor bar for a private event. We only stayed at the hotel for 2 nights and primarily chose this hotel because of this amenity. The rates are not cheap, and it is quite disappointing to be turned away to go sit in a downstairs restaurant bar instead. The rooms are nice, clean--beds are a bit firm for my taste. Enjoyed the complimentary wine in the evening. Breakfast was good when we used the facility. the location can't be beat...close to bars and restaurants, and the bay walk. Valet parking is $40 a day...pretty high. would recommend hotel once they get the private event closures under control..

title: “Peaceful hotel in the heart of Manhattan”
text: This review is based on three days spent at the Library Hotel at the end of our honeymoon (thanks for the complimentary bottle of bubbly!). In short, I would recommend the Library Hotel to anyone (except Hen do's and Stag do's, I think it's a bit peaceful for them!) We thoroughly enjoyed it there as a couple, there were other people staying of all ages. Although the hotel was full, it was not too busy so there were always free tables in the breakfast room and at the rooftop bar (which was very nice indeed - tables both indoor and outdoor and a perfect place for a beer or cocktail before heading out for the evening). Our room was perfectly fine - small, but no smaller than expected by Manhattan standards. It was clean, everything worked as it should. We were on the 12th floor, one below the bar area, and were pleased that no noise filtered down at all. Decor throughout the hotel is modern and clean. Staff were EXTREMELY helpful, and full of good advice. At various points we were helped by Arman, John, Billy and AJ and all were as courteous as could be, and gave us tips on transport, and things to see and do. The other staff we saw all seemed friendly too. we didn't take advantage of the early evening complimentary cheese and wine, but we saw other residents doing so, and it looked REALLY good, not a taken effort, but a proper large plate of various cheeses! The hotel is well located in midtown on Madison Avenue - it's a pleasant peaceful respite from the Manhattan crowds, yet pretty much in the heart of things. Overall, we were very happy with our stay and would highly recommend the Library Hotel.

title: “Landmark hotel but incredibly expensive!”
text: I was here for work in January, and though it's probably one of the most beautiful hotels I've ever stayed in everything was so expensive including internet ($14/day), bottled water ($7) and the restaurant was overpriced too (croque monsieur was also incredibly salty). Luckily, I was able to get a government rate so it wasn't as expensive, but probably wouldn't have stayed here otherwise. Lots of history in this hotel hotel though and everyone has stayed here from Prince Charles to James Brown--I would definitely recommend taking a stroll down their Hallway of History.

title: “Service some of the best I've had...anywhere”
text:
Having already stayed at a couple ofl other New York properties and eaten at various high quality restaurants, I assumed that nonchalent service was just something you'd have to put up with in New York. 
However, at the Soho Grand I was greeted warmly, provided an excellent room with a view of the New York skyline and spoken to in a friendly courteous manner by every member of staff I encountered. A few drinks in the hotel bar were an enjoyable way to end the evening. Having stayed at 5 star hotels in other cities around the world, I can honestly say that this is up there service-wise with the others. Something I would not have anticipated after my other New York hotel experiences. And the rooms are pretty good too.
By the way, I later stayed at the Westin Times Square. I would have stayed an additional night at Soho Grand, but the deadline for cancelling my Westin reservation was up. Although the Westin is a nice hotel facilities wise, the service was not. The check in guy couldn't find my reservation, then condecendingly asked me if I had the right hotel. I quoted my Starpoints number and it came up - no apology. No help with my bags, and when waiting for an elevator to my room with my bags, a porter with a trolley full of other bags moved quickly to make sure he got in the elevator before me (thereby filling it up) so I had to wait for the next car. Similar lack of service quality was experienced at check out and attempts to get a taxi. The only exception being the male concierge who was very helpful in advice on airport transport (hire cars etc).

title: “Wonderful hotel in the heart of a great city”
text: The Huntington Hotel is a real gem. I found myself planning my next visit as I was walking out the door to my taxi. Located in the beautiful Nobb Hill district the hotel is a short walk from Union Square, Chinatown, and within easy reach of all SF's greatest sights. The spa was absolutely wonderful and the rooms were romantic and beautifully adorned. I can't wait to return!

title: “Fantastic First Trip to New York”
text: The Library Hotel's quality started when we first arrived. We were first greeted by AJ (or Ajay?) who checked us in, ported our bags, helped with parking and described our rooms. After three nights we were on a first name basis with the front desk staff. Each floor has a literary theme, each room has a specific topic and there are books in the room about that topic. Very clever. We stayed in 1) Law and 2) Money. Read the books, but leave them there. Our rooms shared a vestibule and an outer door. That's how they connected. There was no door between. This really worked out well. We could be together with our kids (11 and 13), but still private. One room had a sitting area that poked out from the exterior of the building. The view was awesome. The NYC Library is just down the street. Rockefeller Center and Times Square are walking distance. Breakfast is very ample and well served. The best part of our stay was the staff.

title: “Great Location!”
text: This was a great place to stay for a quick three day trip with my mom. We loved how it was two blocks from the subway right in midtown. The lobby is modern and stylish with ipads on the walls you could use whenever and a really helpful, kind concierge. The bathrooms were surprisingly nice with marble showers, rain head showers and fun music playing at all hours! We booked a double room with bunk beds which was small but perfect for us because we were almost never there. There were little tv's in front of each bed, which was a nice treat. We had our own sink and we used it every night and morning before going to bed. That makes a big difference when you are sharing a bathroom. There was a perfectly large window in our room to bring in light and make it feel larger! The only downside was I thought the carpet smelled a little, which made the hallway smell a bit.

title: “Comfortable hotel in convenient location, with excellent breakfast and evening reception”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for one night as part of a cross-country road trip.
Pros - great location near Galleria, free breakfast and evening reception with wine, beer, and snacks, parking garage with entry at each floor, we booked it for an excellent price on hotwire.com
Cons - loud AC unit, rooms are showing signs of age
Overall, I think this hotel would be an excellent place to stay for a business traveler while still having everything a family would need.

title: “A good experience”
text:
Stayed 3 night in late November at the rate of £100 per night (~$165) booked through hotels.com. Chose the hotel as it was the convention hotel.
It was a good experience. It's in a good location. It's a nice decent hotel. There is plenty of local (expensive) parking. I didn't really use hotel facilities other than the gym which was fine with some decent equipment (2 x-trainers, couple of joggers, and couple of bikes in one room and free weights and space in an adjacent room). Internet was $12.95 +tax per night - didn't use it as I now have mobile broadband.
Would be happy to return and probably will!

title: “Not worth the price”
text: My spouse and I and my daughters family stayed one night in two suites and were not very happy with the rooms nor the service. Upon arrival we had leave our auto enter the hotel to seek a bellman to help with our luggage .Once that was done, entering the beautiful hotel lobby, one would believe that you were in for a fine stay, don't be fooled. Late that evening when we returned to our room we found a broken lamp in the livingroom and the bedroom ,a non working television in the bedroom, no blankets on the beds only a sheet and comforter, no shades nor draperies on the windows just blinds which allowed the light from the floodlit hallway across the court to illuminate the room making almost impossible to sleep. When we were detailing this to the desk clerk the next morning we got a arguement from a maintanance worker who was nereby making us feel as it was our fault for not calling the desk at midnight to have our room changed. You can do better at many of the fine hotels in town for a similar price or lower.

title: “Great”
text:
Super helpful and friendly staff. They were very compassionate and helpful in assisting me as our cabbie made off with my tote bag ( always get a receipt so you can track yellow cabs!)
Very clean rooms and wonderfully comfortable beds..amazing water pressure in shower. We were close to elevator but was quiet. Rooms a little on the small side but nothing like Europe and really it's NYC don't expect to be camping out in your room. Great locale to subways..not too many dinner restaurants walking distance but great breakky options close by. Will stay again :)

title: “It was ok”
text: We stayed at the Quincy for one night. The pictures on the website made it seem it was very new but in reality when we got to the room, it seemed rundown (the couch was sagging and the minifridge looked like it was from 1980). Our room was super hot so we had a window open all night, which was fine except for all the noise we heard from outside ( I read this in other reviews and its true). I was walking around with socks on and I stepped on a screw on the floor and I could see dust piled up on the carpet in the corners. We parked our car in the adjacent garage, which I thought was $$ but because we had a lot of things with us and were constantly going in and out it was convenient that it was right next door. The front desk staff was very friendly.

title: “Tiny, but reasonable, pleasant place to stay”
text: Good Hotel, clean, good service, great free internet. Rooms are tiny basically just a bed - but a few different lounge areas you can utilise in teh hotel. Great value for San Fran where everything else seems so expensive. A little noisey, especially at night lots of sirens etc...

title: “Customer service beyond compare”
text: I stayed at this hotel with two girlfriends this summer after snagging a great summer rate online. We could not have been more pleased. The staff at this hotel is obviously well-schooled in good customer relations and it shows. Everyone -- front desk staff, waitstaff, concierge, bellhops -- were courteous, friendly and helpful. I am very picky about customer service and find it sadly lacking in many places these days. The Drake is a welcome exception to the rule.

title: “Loved Marriott Canyon Villas”
text: We traded through II into this property. We stayed from April 26th to May 3rd. The weather was perfect - high 80s to high 90s during the day and at night you needed a light sweater. We didn't see one cloud the entire week. The villas are only 20 minutes from the airport - very easy access to the highways. We checked in around 5 pm and the staff were very friendly. We were in unit 2959 (the third floor). The units are very nice and comfortable. The bed was great. We had a walk in shower and jacuzzi tub. The balcony was small .. had a table and 4 chairs, but it was a squeeze. The resort offered a few activities as well as activities at the JW Marriott, where you would walk to or take a shuttle. The shuttle also went to the Desert Ridge Marketplace - plenty of shopping and restaurants as well as an 18 screen movie theatre and a supermarket. They are building a new shopping area (right next to the Marketplace) called City Place that will open in the next few years. It will be a more upscale shopping center with Nordstrom and Bloomingdales. I've been told it will be similar to Kierland Commons (near the Westin Resort). We ate dinner at Kierland Commons twice .. once an italian restaurant called North and at a french bistro called Zinc. Zinc had a nice courtyard room where the roof retracts in nice weather. Both had very good food. We went to the Chart House for dinner one night and had a great meal. Their chocolate soufle was wonderful! We also had dinner at Roys over at the Marriott Hotel - very nice. We had dinner on the patio - it was lit with Tiki Torches and they have a firepit. If you dine there on Friday and Saturday nights, you can hear the music from the band that plays outside on the Marriott patio. The pool areas at both the resort and villas was very nice and kept very clean. My husband golfed every day. He loved that he could get out very early in the morning - just after 6 am. We bought the par n'pamper pass for $500 which entitled us to 5 rounds of golf, 5 spa treatments or a combination of the two. Good deal - especially in the high season months! The spa was the nicest I have seen. It had it's own pool with a jacuzzi and very plush lounge chairs. The spa has it's own restaurant and the two services I received were WONDERFUL! I can't wait to go back. Feel free to email me with any questions.

title: “Phenomenal on every level.”
text: Other luxury hotels need to take lessons from the staff of the Hay-Adams.

title: “Excellent hotel next to Times Square”
text:
Very good hotel on 5 mins walk from Times Square. Next time I wouldn't choose this location again (a bit too touristy) but the hotel is worth it. The rooms are clean and cleverly arranged, not very big though.
The tv didn't work but the staff was quick to give us breakfast for two for the st of our stay (which was seven days) for free to make up for that.
The breakfast is really good, very well presented continental breakfast with bagels, croissants, yoghurt and different types of cereal. Also fresh fruit available.
The hotel has a sauna, gym (small room with some equipment), a sauna, steam room and a swimming pool.
In comparison to most other NYC hotels the price is very reasonable, especially considering the quality of the hotel.

title: “Terrible service!”
text:
This hotel does not understand the meaning of service. When calling to leave a message for a colleague who was (unfortunate enough to be) staying there, I was told "our computers are down, please call back in 15 minutes". I asked if I could leave a manual message, and the desk man said "Actually, it's pretty hectic here; you'd have a better chance if you call back in 10-15 minutes." I agreed to call back. When I called back, I was told the computers were down for at least an hour and I should call back then. I explained that this was an important message and could someone please write it down; my colleague would check the front desk. I was told this was simply not possible. I spoke with the manager who said "we can't take manual messages", and that I could "fax a message". (I have no idea why they could handle the paper from a fax, but not one from their own hand.)
When I expressed my frustration and suggested that this would be bad publicity, the manager said "all publicity is good publicity". Well, to those of you who are considering La Quinta - you know what you are getting into. Just don't expect to receive any messages.
RM

title: “Two one night stays”
text: As a part of a two week coach holiday we stayed the first and last nights at this hotel. We had a good room and enjoyed some of the facilities. Friendly staff. Great location for Times Square and Broadway. 10 minutes walk but watch out for all the red hands at the crossings of Avenues and Streets. Recommended for a reasonable priced stay for easy access to the major sites of New York.

title: “Nice hotel, miserable customer service”
text:
The good things about the hotel: The staff at lower levels (everyone providing basic service) were terrific. In fact, I received some of the best service from individuals I have seen in awhile. The room was lovely and clean. 
The management, however, is apparently fixated on milking as much money out of you as possible and without warning. I was charged for business services despite not being informed by the business office that there was a charge (I called in advance.) there was an error in my reservation - it had me arriving a day early - and I was told it would be "no problem." I was then charged for the night - WITHOUT INFORMING ME THAT I WOULD BE CHARGED. They ran my credit card and didn't tell me. I was told (when I asked if it could be removed) that they hotel was busy and my reservation kept them from booking the room. Had rust not run out of my sink when I arrived, I might have bought that. 
The bar is incredibly understaffed. One poor server covered the entire bar, and the service and food delivery time were as slow as you would expect. I don't blame the server - she never stopped moving. It must be another part of the management's attempt to make every possible dime they can.
If the review were based solely on the room and the service staff, I would have given it a 4 (minus one point because it took 5 minutes to get hot water to my room at 6 am.) Due to the management, it is a 2. Don't go here without deep pockets and unless you like surprises.

title: “dated but good location”
text: This hotel fit the bill for what we needed-- a last minute hotel in NYC for 1 night. Som pros are the locations--East side and walkable to lots of things--price & bar on the top of the hotel. Drinks were definately pricey, but the view is great and the perfect place to get a drink before heading back to our room. The room itself was mediocare & very dated. The tv was old, which I can deal with, but very limited cable access (you couldn't even get channels like ESPN). It suited our needs for one night, but I doubt I will be back again.

title: “Family Gathering”
text: The services was good and the rooms was very presentable. The location was in a good area. I like the fact that the rooms have a microwave and refrigerator in them , but could have used an flat screen TV.

title: “Wonderful stay - don't be put off by homeless comments”
text:
Having spent a fabulous 4 days with my girlfriend recently in San Francisco staying in the Metropolis, we can only echo the positive comments people have previously written. The staff were all kind, welcoming and very helpful in answering any of our questions. The décor, fittings and bathroom in the room (9th floor) were all clean and modern and the bed was very comfortable. Complimentary fresh coffee was well received in the morning, as was the free use of the business centre (including free printing facilities) and the public PC / internet access (very useful for two travelling Brits who didn’t have a laptop with them). 
Don’t be put off by comments relating to homeless people etc. Yes, the first time you pass them heading for Union Square it is a little intimidating, but we weren’t bothered by them, and besides, there seemed to be homeless people on every corner in San Francisco!
Oh, and the icing on the cake would have to be that the rates for this hotel are extremely cheap!
Recommendations:
- Farmer Browns is a bar/restaurant adjoining the hotel. It’s an excellent venue for a drink by the bar or a meal (I would advise booking if visiting on the weekend). The food was excellent as was the atmosphere, especially when the live jazz band played. I believe they also offer a weekend brunch for $15 which is no doubt also very nice (although we didn’t try it).
- Hana Zen Japanese/Sushi – within 5 minutes walk of the hotel. Very nice food.
- Puccini & Pinetti - Italian restaurant, 129 Ellis Street within 5 minutes walk of the hotel. Typical Italian menu but very nice food (at a great price), excellent service and a great atmosphere (even on a Monday night).

title: “Good location, not good on service”
text: The room is not the quality that we expected from Wyndham. The room is old, mold in badroom, wall paper peeling. We were never provided the number of towels needed for the people staying in the room. One day there was only one towel for 5 people. Asking for towels at the desk became a hassel. Sometimes we would get the towels and some time they would say housekeeping would bring the towells. Houskeeping did not bring the towels. The airconditioner face was loose. We could see to the outside through the crack. It was difficult to cool down the room.

title: “Better Than Expected!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel with my female friend on 15Nov for just a night. As there aren't many value hotels with free breakfast and free high speed Internet to choose from, we looked this hotel up through trip advisor. The homeless shelter next to the hotel made us worried before we got there, but things turned out better than we expected. 
First thing, location. This hotel is right next to the Philadelphia Convention Center and just a block from Reading Terminal Market. It was so easy to find! We just used the city map provided by the information desk at 30th street station and things worked out great. This hotel is also close to other landmarks like the Liberty Bell and Chinatown, all within walking distance. Right next to the hotel, there is a small convenience store that sells snacks and other amenities. This hotel is not far from the SEPTA station and it took us just 5 mins to get to 30th Street station. Really conveninent!
Price and service come next. Staying at main hotel brands doesn't fit into our budget, this hotel provided a nice, comfortable place for us to spend the night in the city. Though the room was a little dark when all lights were on, we did not care much since we spent most of our time outside anyway. The bed was comfortable and the restroom and shower were clean. The signals of the wifi were really strong that my friend and I were able to upload photos to our blogs instantly. There are not many varieities for breakfast items though, they only had bagels, muffins, yogurt, and cereals. But the toaster made my bagels alright. One thing I have to pick about the free breakfast is, their coffee is tasteless. If you are a coffee lover, I recommend that you go pick up a starbucks instead. Check out was quick and the staff was friendly. My friend and I were not even paying attention to that homeless shelter at all, the people did not bother us and our trip ended up great.

title: “Great Stay - Perfect Location”
text: My fiance and I stayed at the Hyatt April 7th-11th. We went to San Francisco to see the sights and were not in our room except to sleep. For that purpose the Hyatt was wonderful. The location could not have been better, the BART, cable car, and the Street Cars are literally right outside the front door. The Ferry Building on the Embarcadaro was right across the street. You had transportation to where ever you wanted to go. We got our room from Priceline for $90/night and was well worth it. We did not eat or drink at any of the restaurants because we wanted to experience San Francisco and that was easy to do because of the location.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Moorpark Hotel last summer to sightsee and visit relatives. What a beautiful hotel! We were all thrilled to see the lovely lobby. There were always apples available in the lobby for our hungry teenager. 
Our room looked out onto the parking lot, but we didn't find it noisy. The other side of the hotel faces the pool. This would be a lovely view, but there is a highway on the other side of the hedge and it might be noisy. The beds were very comfortable and the room was spacious. The bathrooms were luxurious. The kids loved the bathrobes.
Our kids, aged 10 and 13, loved the pool and hot tub. It is surrounded by greenery and roofed tents to protect you from the sun. There was internet poolside that was complimentary. The hot tub was large and we all enjoyed it immensely.
The hotel, pool, and rooms were kept very clean.
Just outside the hotel, across the parking lot, were family style restaurants.
The staff were very friendly. We had no problems with check in or out.
I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Excellent stay for a trip with official delegation to the capital of the USA”
text: I have stayed in this hotel at least 5 times over the last decade during my trips to the D.C. For me it is perfect hotel while I am with official delegation visiting the US because of the number of reasons. Staff is trying hard to make your stay comfortable the moment you arrive there. Excellent and rich breakfast, quality buffets, happy-hour, gym, pool... Lots of space in the room - which is convenient if you are too tired in the evening and do not want to go elsewhere. If you do want, then it is pretty close to Georgetown and number of interesting clubs/bars to visit.

title: “A bit run down”
text:
We had been wanting to stay at this hotel for a while and had heard great things about it. The location is wonderful - within walking distance to many great restaurants and shops, plus the park is right there. The service was wonderful at the hotel, but the rooms and hotel in general were very run down and need of some serious updating. Especially for the prices they are charging! The stereo in our room was from the 1970's and didn't even work. The bedside controls for the fireplace and stereo didn't work. The carpeting was not flat in areas, the vase was dusty when we first walked in. 
Also, had heard such great things about the rooftop and when we got up there it was such a dissapointment.
The hot tub sounded too good to be true and they were nice enough to heat it up for us for when we got home that night, but when we went to check it out, it was slimy and dirty...
I hope they do some updating and serious cleaning. The updated restaurant was also great.

title: “Great location, outstanding service, good value”
text: This hotel by Hilton is within about 4 blocks of the space needle and Duck tours. The lobby is fairly quiet and unassuming. They have friendly and helpful front desk staff, a hot complimentary breakfast (more than just fattening pastries and sugary cereal), and the complimentary manager's reception dinner Mon-Thurs was better than I expected. You can take care of your laundry, and the workout room is open 24/7 w/room key. The suites themselves were perfectly nice and my room was quiet although close to the elevator. I walked to/from the convention center every day for my conference to get a nice tour of the city, Pike's Place Market, and some of the local shops.

title: “Great location but too many compromises including ONE WHOPPER”
text:
The Good:
-Location
-Nice laid-back manager
-Jacuzzi in the bathroom though we ended up not using it
-Cheap
-Parking
The bad:
-Very small room. Barely enough room to get around with 2 people in there. This is the least important negative to me and I don't actually care too much, but I wanted to let other know.
-Included breakfast is a joke: packaged danishes (think little debbie's) and make your own coffee. Again, don't really care.
-There are only about 6 parking spots available. If they're full, you have to go park a block or 2 away (still free). No biggie there.
The ugly:
-No insulation between rooms and hallways. When someone's in the hall, you know it. We got woken up every morning at 6am by other people just walking around and chatting.
-No security. Venice beach is not the best neighborhood at night (though it has gotten better) so this made us a little uncomfortable. There's no one at the front desk, the main doors are locked with a code you're given, but they're windowed doors so not exactly Fort Knox.
-Also the rooms are locked with combination locks (which beep quite loudly, see insulation note). Not a big deal, but Greg, the manager, is quite cavalier about giving you your code, announcing it loudly. Not sure how often the codes are rotated either.
-The bathroom door is windowed, so anyone sitting on the bed can see into the whole bathroom. Not a big deal except when I'm doing my "business" where I'd rather be private.
-the bathroom had a weird smell to it... I dismissed it as bleach, but it lingered
-Greg, though a nice guy, is not always on site and he seems to be the only employee other than the maid.
-We had to pay in full at check-in
The unacceptable:
Cockroaches! Yes, I found 2 cockroaches on 2 different days in the bathroom. They were small, but still cockroaches! If it weren't for this, I could probably recommend this hotel to others with a few caveats since the location and price are great. But nothing can excuse this. It made us very uncomfortable even to sleep there, but it was too much hassle to leave and we had already paid. I would have said something to Greg, but he was rarely around including when I left. I've meant to contact him to let him know about this, but I was too busy immediately after my trip, and now I'm tired.

title: “Average hotel”
text: Just your average business hotel. More modern than the Westin Gaslamp, which is only 4 blocks away. Internet in the room costs $, parking costs $, but the bar offers free WiFi and, coincidentally, has a pretty good happy hour. Walls in the room are thin.... could clearly hear the guy in the next room talking on his cell phone and he was not yelling or anything.

title: “Hampton Inn-Convention Center- nice but-”
text: The hotel would be a nice one if there wasnt construction next door. The stafff was very friendly and very helpful.my girlfriends and i usually stay at the hampton hotels because of the free breakfasts that they have every morning. The hotel was easy to get to but it would have been easier to get to if there wasnt constuction going on Race Street.

title: “Treated Right,Good Value”
text: Stayed here last Sat night and went to a Red Sox game.Hotel was nice ,clean and staff was friendly and helpful.Rubber duck is a nice touch.Convienent location to alot of things within walking distance.The staff told me to check out their website for the best rate next time I come back. I will try this for the next game I go to.

title: “Excellent hotel, staff and location!”
text:
We just returned from a 4 day stay in Boston, staying at the Back Bay Hotel. I had emailed with a few questions, mentioning that we would have an early arrival. Not only was our room ready by 0900 we were upgraded to a lovely room on the 6th floor. Quiet, luxurious with the most attentive staff, always there to answer any questions. Heated towels, seperate shower, a tassimo in the room, turn down service. It was lovely to be spoiled. 
This hotel is in a perfect location to the T, but we actually walked everywhere. For those of you from out of town, a Frommers was a great guide. As were the many Bostonians who stopped to ask if they could help. A perfect "holiday" in Boston.

title: “Great place to stay....”
text: We just came back from New York and stayed at the Candlewood. The location is great; so close to everything. The room was plenty big enough, staff was helpful and friendly, and those yummy cookies were the best. Couple things though, our room had a very noisy fridge, wish there was more counter space in the bathroom, maid service only if you stay a week or more which we did but you only get the service once during that week and the coffee pot was broken but replaced the next day. There were 2 great breakfast places close by that were recommended to us by the staff; Tick Tock and I think it was called West Way - both had great food. I would stay there again based on the price and location.

title: “Service with a View”
text:
Arrived on Friday, April 8th at the Hyatt Chicago to celebrate my daughter's 20th birthday. We were greeted warmly by Isabella at the check in desk. We were given as requested a double and Isabella made sure it had the perfect view of the Chicago River. She was wonderful to us. The hotel is perfectly situated to enjoy all Chicago has to offer within walking distance. We did awake to protesters but once you saw what they were protesting about you wanted to join. It had nothing to do with the Hyatt but issues facing all American's and were joining as one and that was the slogan, "We are One". 
We shopped, we dined, we had big fun all over Chicago from the hotel to Greektown and much more. We checked out with the friendly Cassandra and stored our bags for one last tour of the city. Millennium Park was right outside their door and more. We went on to our second hotel to finish our stay but can not wait to return to the Hyatt. Two conventions were happening but it was still quiet and the bar will blow your soxs off as well as their in house restaurants.

title: “Enjoyed every moment of SF!”
text: My wife and I celebrated our 25th anniversary in San Francisco this past March and loved every minute of it! The weather was perfect (which doesn't happen very often in SF) and our hotel turned out to be a pleasant surprise! the Broadway manor Inn is relatively economical (why we chose it) but the rooms are in great shape - spotless, microwave/fridges, irons etc. Perfect - plus you can't beat the location! there are tons of restaurants and bars all around - everything is clean and touristy in the neighborhood - walked to all the major sites (crookedest street is a must-see by the way - beautiful i nthe summer time when all the plants are blooming). Great trip that did not break the bank!

title: “Great little kitchenette suite - returned our lost clothing :)”
text: My wife and I stayed here in August of 2012, it was 110 degrees F outside, however, our room was always cool and comfortable. The "thru the wall AC" unit ran most of the time. We booked a kitchenette and it came fully equiped with a dishwasher, full fridge and freezer, sink, micorwave, and countertop hot plate. Also all of the dishes and such were included. Laundry was available on site and they also provided a cafetiria type area with snacks and drinks you could purchase on the "honor basis" and fill out a card and drop it into the box. Great location for us adjacent to the Black Canyon Highway, road noise was not to bad at all. Overall, the room was perfectly adequate, clean, and fairly spacious. We did not use the swimming pool or hot tub. We accidentally left some clothing behind in our room, the staff saved it for us, bagged it, tagged it and entered it into the log book. We returned to PHX two(2) weeks later and retrieved our clothes. Thank-you to all the staff there, they were fantastic and we would stay there again. Please remember, that your expectations, may be different than ours, this hotel is older, and does show it's age a bit, however, our stay was great.

title: “Amazing view with walking distance to restuarant and shopping centers.”
text: First I just wanted to let everyone know that this is an amazing hotel. Our room was very clean. We were next to the Seaport Village, Convention Center, and all the nice restuarants on the fifth ave. The view from our room at night was spectacular. The people in the front desk were very helpful.

title: “Get'em In, Get'em Out”
text:
This is a great hotel is you are looking for an attractive room and a nice bed to grab a few hours of sleep on an airport layover. The beds are very comfortable. However, this is NOT the hotel to consider if you need anything more than sleep.
This was my third stay at this hotel and unfortunately, my arrival at Logan, was after midnight. I was informed the shuttle bus would arrive in 15-20 minutes which was reasonable. But after three hours of traveling I was hungry and thirsty and eager to get to this hotel.
The ride in the shuttle bus was just short of terrifying. It seemed as though the driver was late in leaving for the night and weaved in and out of the maze of roads at Logan to reach this hotel. This hotel lives up to the old New England adage, you cannot get there from here! How the luggage did not fly from its storage area amazed me when the driver appeared to take the corners on just two wheels!
It appears "full service" airlines and hotels is now defined as getting you from point A to B with no services in between. As frequent travelers know, the food service on a multi-hour flight is now limited to a one ounce package of pretzels, the thought of a late night meal once getting to the hotel was not to be. 
What I really wanted was a cold beer which was not possible, in spite of the fact there were two bartenders behind the bar at 12:30 AM. When I approached the bar and requested a beer, the bartender simply gestured by waving his hand across his neck signifying the bar was "cut off". Not a word was uttered or a simply apology saying the bar was closed. I had to settle with a bottle of soda from the closet gift shop off the front desk. I guess all that “service” forced the price of soda to $2.50! I wonder why they could not have offered a cold beer in this little closet? Surely they would have made at least $10 for a beer if a soda costs that much.
One would think this hotel might think about having some sort of late night snack available for late arriving guests. I have had more considerate service from a Residence Inn. But Hyatt, a supposedly high-end hotel that caters to business travelers? At least they might have suggested a late night pizza place that offered delivery service.
I am sorry but this hotel has totally lost sight of who their guests are and what there needs might be. Especially if you arrive at midnight and leave by 7 am.
Sadly, service is not something to expect from this hotel or its staff.

title: “Hip Hotel in Lower East Side”
text:
Got a great deal using the Hotel Tonight app. Really enjoyed the property - definitely is an ultra-modern hip hotel. If you only stay at Marriotts or Starwood hotels, you will likely not "get" this place. Likely a bit of a lifestyle shock.
Else, I highly recommend as the customer service was excellent and enjoyed the great location to walk to SoHo in minutes.
Definitely will be back my next time in the Big Apple.

title: “Great hotel in Denver”
text:
Great area, service , food, and bar is excellent.
Can't beat the proximity to walking to stores, restaurants, etc.
Safe area! The staff are couteous and helpful from valet to front desk to housekeepers to 
Restaurant and bar staff? Spa, antoine du chez is excellentbalso-angela is a great masseuse

title: “Convenient to LAX & free shuttle”
text:
Great location for convenience to LAX w/ free shuttle, but no free parking (both valet & self-park are $$) and the self-park is actually a separate LAX parking lot behind the hotel for $10/day. Rooms are clean and good size. Easy to work in with a good sized desk & certain rates include free wireless internet. Couldn't get the wired connection in the room to work. Bathrooms are tired, with dirty grout lines in the shower and along the countertop. Bathtub drain was slow. Smallest shampoo/conditioner/soap sizes I have ever seen.
Bar stays open late w/ full menu for late night dinners.
Very quiet considering the close proximity to the airport.

title: “Location : great; Hotel: not so great”
text: There are two good things about this hotel: the location and the free parking. Otherwise, it is just not worth it to stay here to save a few bucks. The hallways smell. Our room was very small and dark. The mattresses were not very thick and the sheets kept coming off of them during the night. The place just seems very run-down. There was some peeling paint in the room and in the pool area. The place just seemed to give the impression that the owners don't really care about making it look nice for the guests. We really regretted staying here and wished we'd spent a little extra money to stay somewhere nicer.

title: “---- in the form of a hotel!”
text:
This was the first night of our trip which was booked as part of a tour. We arrived quite late having flown from Chicago, so wanted to get checked in - easier said than done! They had no idea which group we were joining - so kept sending us of to different people who had no idea what we were talking about. When we finally got a room we wanted to cry as it was just horrible! The first thing you noticed as you got out of the lift was the smell, smoke filled the corridors. We managed to find our room even though there were no signs, as the room smelt like an ash-tray, we called down to reception to ask for a non-smoking room we were then informed it was a non-smoking room! They did send a maid up to spray air freshner - but nearly chocked on the sheer amount. There were some facilities eg. microwave, fridge and 2 mugs that you would never dream of drinking anything out of! as for the bathroom it was filthy, you would have to have another shower after using the towels! No-one in there right mind would of taken there shoes off either unless you wanted to stick to the carpet!! we thought that we would just go to bed as we had to get up early in the morning .. easier said than done .. every time you moved the smell of smoke came out of the bedding! 
We were suposed to return to this same hotel on the last night of our tour, so went to reception to see if we could pay more to be upgraded to another room, they were rude and unhelpful, and not prepared to do a thing. 
Lucky we managed to get booked into the Essex House hotel round the corner, as we could not have faced another night in this ---- hole. 
Totally disgusting, if anyone is thinking of going there please do not waste your money on this hotel when you can get something a lot better for not much more.

title: “Great Time, Great Service, Great Rooms, Central Locale”
text:
Just returned from a wonderful 3 day weekend in early Feburary, 2006, in Philadelphia where we stayed at the Windsor Hotel.
We rented two rooms, one for our adult offspring and the other for ourselves.
We think the hotel is wonderful. Our room, had a wonderful view of Logan Circle and the museums as well as a balcony. The room had a nicely equipped kitchen if one were so inclined, two double beds and was very spacious accomodations. The beds were a tad soft but comfortable. Both room were very large and included a wardrobe area containing a dresser as well as dishwasher, microwave, oven and plates. Around the corner is a Dunkin Donut and "Wha Wha's" where you can pick up groceries if you wish (it's similar to a 711) and breakfast ingredients.
Everything about the hotel was great - the staff uncommonly helpful, polite and accomodating - we asked if we could check out at 2 PM rather than 12 noon as it made flying back from the airport more convenient and the hotel management readily agreed.
