It is true if you are looking for the latest in modern furniture and super plush carpeting, the hotel would be somewhat lacking, but if you want comfortable , clean rooms in a hotel with a very personable and friendly staff and centrally located, then, this is the place. There is a small "gym" in the lower lobby with treadmills and weights. 
Parking was in an adjacent parking lot which costs $24 per day for infinite come and go privileges. If you just want to leave your car, you might do a tad better with some local parking lots, but just a tad - the convenience of being adjacent to the hotel is worth the difference.
In the lobby is a WONDERFUL restaurant, "ASIA ON THE PARKWAY" with very fine cuisine and service and prices moderate.

title: “great value, friendly staff, would stay again”
text: very clean rooms, all staff nice and friendly, gas station convenience store within walking distance, fridge and microwave in all rooms. Booked through priceline 60 dollars a night.

title: “Perfect Service and Location”
text: Having read the great reviews, we chose the Casablanca for a short stay following a transatlantic cruise and we did not regret it. What stands out at this hotel is the friendliness of the staff. Any time you run into a member of the staff...whether in the lounge, elevator, or lobby, they introduce themselves and express genuine interest in your experience at the hotel. For those visiting New York for the first time or for a theater break, the location simply cannot be beat. In less than a minute you can walk from the calm comfort of the lounge to exciting bustle of Times Square. The mini suite was very comfortable and romance package included a rose on the bed, chilled champagne, and rose petals in a heart shape surrounding the lone rose. Rose petals were also strategically placed in other locations in the suite to make for a truly romantic atmosphere.

title: “COCKROACHES”
text:
This hotel is awful. The website is totally misleading. The carpets and furniture are old and dirty, the windows don't fit properly and it is noisy.
We found a large (and alive) cockroach in our kitchenette. we left it for the staff to see and received no comment or explanation from them
We booked suites and the staff tried to palm us off with a normal room advising us not to use Expedia which , they said, lies about the hotel.
We also paid over $300 a night based on the website.
The only saving grace is the fitness room which is good.
Please don't stay at this hotel, there are so many others which offer much better value for money and quality.

title: “Good hotel, clean, comfortable and convenient”
text: We came back for a second stay this Christmas, so that says something. The first room we were shown to (third floor room one) was pretty smelly and only had a view of a wall when I thought I had booked a full view. We asked to be changed and were upgraded to a 17th floor room which was a huge improvement and free wifi - which can be a very annoying hidden extra. Clean, comfortable room with good views. The staff are helpful and the location is good. We only ate in the restaurant once. The food is good, but breakfast quite expensive so we tend to go round the corner to Think for coffee or Peels (excellent new place) for breakfast. Would recommend, though not cheap. But what is in NYC.

title: “New Years Adventure!”
text: We were running behind on booking our room for the New Year’s celebration at the Wortham Theater. Luckily, we found availability at C.Q. We were actually pleasantly surprised at the cleanliness & friendly staff. It is so conveniently located! If you need a place to stay in the theater district or downtown for a night of clubbing this is a great spot. Note- there is ONLY valet parking. Not too terribly expensive. I think less than $20.

title: “Charming”
text: We spent just one night is the historic part of the hotel, room 640. We thought it was very charming. It is small but, very clean, and had everything you would need. Very comfortable king bed, large flat screen T.V., small refrigerator, coffeemaker, ironing board, safe and decorated beautifully. The location is perfect, close to union square.

title: “Great location, better than other reviewers have said”
text: I was worried about this place as soon as I saw it was the hotel I had booked on Hotwire. All the reviews are terrible, and I was expecting something bad. I've traveled plenty in my 25 years, and mostly stayed in mid-priced chains like Holiday Inn. This place was nicer than almost all of those. The only imperfections I could see are a little bit of scraped paint on the walls. It has nice upscale decor in the rooms (including the obligatory blues/Memphis stuff, nice, new looking carpet (within the last three or four years I'd say, and the bedding was clean and soft. The location was great- not on Beale street, so we avoided some extra noise at night I'm sure, but it was a four or five block walk there, so we meandered down there at about 10 p.m. and back when we were done. I'd reccommend the nearby Rum Boogie Cafe for a free (at least on Thurs. night when we were here) show. The check-in took about five minutes, the woman helping us was pleasant, and the free cookies you get when you check in are amazing. We didn't park in the ramp, because I had read it was $20 (which isn't terrible) but we got one of two parking spots that were open (again, Thurs. night) on the street running along side the hotel. The small outdoor pool was closed when we were here, but that wasn't an issue for us, have not yet eaten at the TGI Fridays in the hotel, but will for breakfast today. This is listed as a three-star hotel, I'd give it 3 and 1/2.

title: “Impressive”
text:
Stayed at the Peabody for one night on our drive to Chicago from New Orleans. The hotel is an impressive sight from the street and that continues once you go inside.
Check in was quick and easy as was the check out. The rooms were luxurious and the beds were amazing!
Absolutely loved the lobby and the piano player.
Parking was easy and not too expensive - plenty of space and large bays.
Would have loved to have stayed longer!!
Definatley recommend this hotel!

title: “Loved It .....”
text: I stayed at this Hotel last week for 5 days and the service was excellent. They are about 2 miles from alot the sites, but if you ask they will provid shuttle service. They served good hot breakfast in the morning, (their coffee was the best hotel coffee i have ever had) and dinner every night from 5:30- 7(which was a first for me). The customer service was very professional, welcoming, and excellent. Even though I was on the 9th floor next to the swimming pool, I never heard anyone outside of my room. I would suggest anyone stay at this hotel. I know for sure that it will not be my last visit.

title: “Loved Topaz”
text: Spend a long weekend at Topaz last month. Large, well appointed rooms. great downtown location, near Dupont Circle and subway. Pretty block too. Very attentive staff who looked after our needs. Including walking our dog during day when we were out sightseeing. Our first visit to this hotel but not our last.

title: “The best by far”
text:
I stayed here about a year ago and the experience was just amazing. You wouldn't be able to tell at first glance but this subtle hotel really does have the most to offer. 
The best thing about this hotel is the service, just astounding. The staff are always attentive and there for your needs. And if they do mess up they are more then ready to make up for their mistakes, no questions asked. Everyone is very obliged to help you.
The rooms however are average, nothing spectacular. You do however get a mini walkout balcony even in the lowest end rooms which is very nice. Complimentary Fiji water is also very nice. 
Amazing house car service! Less then 10min wait times and they even offer a Rolls Royce, although it is first come first serve. 
Overall this subtle hotel is stellar. Do not overlook this hotel by its sheer style or looks, the service alone is the sole reason I will come back again and again.

title: “Absolutely Fabulous!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text:
We booked a 1-night stay at the MGM Detroit as our first night away from our 2-year-old son. Prior to parenting, we were avid travelers to luxury resorts and have stayed in 5-star hotels throughout Mexico and beaches in the Caribbean. Our goal for this 1-night stay was to cram a week-long pampering and relaxing vacation into 1 night, and at the MGM, it CAN be done! 
The previous reviews do a nice job of summarizing some of the basics of the property. Customer service and professionalism were superb. We were treated like royalty by every single staff member we encountered. They have truly gone above and beyond in creating an environment of catering to the guest.
The property was flawless with upscale, modern decor, water fountains, fireplace lounge for hotel guests only, easily accessible elevators, concierge readily available for assitance, and key-entry accessibility (meaning no casino riff-raff) for all of this plus the spa, pool, fitness center, and rooms. 
The rooms were goregous. We had a luxury king (the "basic" model), and it was aout 500 square feet and very well appointed with a large comfy bed, well stocked mini-bar, plasma tv, outlets everywhere. The bathrrom was very well done - marble countertops, super large walk in shower with two shower heads, separate toilet, great towels.
The fitness center was large and had everything you can imagine. The pool is something out of a Zen-magazine, absolutely beautiful, with gradual depth, rocks/hard wood as decor, comfy canopy chairs. Just beautiful.
We totally indulged at the Spa, and enjoyed manicure/pedicure, hot stone massage, and sports massage. The spa has a very calming atmosphere, and again customer service was superb. We were assigned a host who walked us from each of our services to the next - totally unnecessary, but completely indulgent. The locker rooms are decorated in the same eastern Asian theme, with a large steam room and hot tub (mens, womens separate). The services at the Spa were well above average and exceed the quality at some of the other well known spas in the Detroit area. We were very , very pleased with our Spa time.
We had appetizers at Wolfgang Puck and dinner at the steakhouse. Wow. Wow. Wow. The food at both was outstanding. Incredibly delicious and beautiful and over-the-top. Yes, expensive, but wow, was it worth it. Again, decor was grand and service was exceptional. 
We walked through the casino, and yes there was some smoke, but it was not outrageous. The bars and tables were busy (even on a Monday night). 
I wish we could have stayed a 2nd night and tried out the other restaurant and indulged in more spa services. 
This is a beautiful property, with exceptional customer service. The food options are many, and are very, very good. Entertainment is aplenty with the casinos and numerous nightclubs. The Spa is heavenly. I really can't say enough good things about the MGM Detroit!!! We will definitely be going back, and sans child. It really is not a place for children.

title: “Nice Hotel in central location”
text:
The Hilton San Francisco Financial Dristrict was perfect for my boyfriend and I. Although its probably better described to a taxi driver as the one near china town, as we told them the one in the financial district (we didn't have the exact address as i mis-placed it) and the driver took us to the wrong one telling us there was no other in the financial district. It is within walking distance to Union Square (shopping) 15mins and about 20mins to Fishermans wharf and ferries to Alcatraz. The walk to fishermans wharf is good for anyone who wants to have a look around china town or to have something to eat in little italy, right across the road from china town.
The standard rooms are reasonable size with also reasonable sized bathrooms. Very comfortable. We were also really happy with the service. the staff were nice and informative. the overall look of the hotel was modern but still comfortable. Good views aswell.

title: “Great "Visit NYC" hotel!”
text: We booked longtime ahead and that gave us a great price/quality relation in always expensive NY: this hotel offered us clean, quiet and comfortable rooms (be it a bit small, but this is NY) with a beautiful view over the city. Personnel is very friendly and helpful. We appreciated the tasty croissants at breakfast as a change to all the sweet cakes generally offered. Location is excellent in between Central Park and Downtown Manhattan in a quiet and apparently safe neighborhood with restaurants and shops nearby.

title: “Great downtown location by ground zero. Amazing views if you get a high floor”
text:
Some of the rooms are a bit tired and small, but if you can get one on the high floors (50-55) then they are newer and you get a fantastic view. Ask for a corner room (see my photo). 
Only problem I had was that there was a very loud resonating humm in my room (5001). It sounded like it was coming from a beam in the roof. The hotel was happy to move me to another room on the second night and that was much much better.
The hotel has a pool, which many in NY don't, which is a bonus for me.

title: “Small Rooms but very artsy and convenient”
text: We stayed here when I took my husband to a piano bar for his birthday, and the hotel is in a great location in the middle of downtown. The room was a little tight, but the hotel is decorated in a cool, modern style and the staff were very friendly. It was also very quiet and clean, Great price, we would stay again if needing a place to stay overnight downtown. Also, redfin sushi is downstairs and they are amazing!

title: “Enjoyed our New Years Stay”
text: Place was affordable, parking is on premises and $25 a night. Internet is free and there is a computer in each room. Starbucks coffee in the rooms and there is a Starbucks a minute from the hotel. The blue line is about a 5 minute walk from the hotel. There are a few cool little spots a block down from the hotel, I can't think of the exact name but is something like the dog cafe. Also there is a little convenience store across the street.

title: “Modern, clean, and just that little something different that I loved!”
text: I was looking for a hotel to host my 40th birthday party and also be convienent to LAX because my birthday dinner was booked at the Encounter restaurant at LAX (you know, that spaceship looking building in the middle of the airport). My birthday theme was cosmos and cocktails - a futuristic feel (based on the restaurant) and I wanted to find a hotel that could match that theme...and I did with the Custom Hotel! I love the modern decor in the lobby, the poolside, and in the 2 bedroom suite that I chose for my birthday night! Absolutely PERFECT for my party and for my taste in general. It is NOT a stuffy hotel with egomanics....it is the exact opposite! Nice people at the front counter, the valet service, everyone was so nice and easy going! The valet service really helped me out for my birthday party experience to transfer us to the restaurant safely and the whole experience went smoothly because of this hotel. I LOVE the Custom Hotel and would stay there again for sure! and the L.E.D. lights had me sold from the first minute I saw the hotel at night!!

title: “Couldn't have been better”
text: I am a corporate client of this hotel, and place numerous guests throughout the year, so I decided I needed to try it. It could not have been any better. The rooms were beautiful, spacious and yes, trendy, which The W Hotel is know for. The Staff were great, accomodating, and the whatever/whenever way of life at The W is probably what really pushes them above the other hotels in the area. I have traveled to numerous locations around the world, and have stayed at numerous 4 and 5 star hotels, but this has got to be one of the best. Their sand bar is beautiful and a lot of fun, their restaurant is tasty and the bar is a great place to go and unwind. If you are looking to party though, don't go to the lobby bar, it isn't that kind of place. Being an ex-hotelier myself, I am a bit of a hotel snob, but all in all, this hotel is top notch, the service is top notch and the food is even more top notch. I could not find one bad thing to say about this hotel, and highly recommend it.

title: “Magnificent? Only by name”
text:
I went to Chicago to run the Half Marathon and as Marriott Reward Member I was very excited to find a Magnificent Marriott very close by where I needed to be. What a mistake!
The hotel is nothing similar to magnificent. The service is very bad, the first day my room was never made! I arrived back to my room around 4pm and it was still undone, I called housekeeping and they said they will send someone, that person arrived 2 hours later.. by 6pm I didnt want to have ANYONE in my room. 
My minibar was empty, and i do not remember getting asked if that was my choice. 
Given that I was going to run the marathon I asked them if they were going to have a special breakfast for the runners, and the answer was no. I asked the if I could then have an early breakfast, around 4am... the answer was also negative. 
The hotel is old, terrible service and I didnt feel they cared about anything. And it has a lack of details, such as a ramp in case you enter the hotel from the magnificent mile... you have to carry your bag down the stairs with no help ofcourse. 
The hotel is perfectly located, but i think a travelodge service would be better! So look for something else.

title: “Chicago”
text: Parking was good, it was under the hotel, food, breakfast was all very good, the service was excellent and they were able to give us suggestions where to go for dinners.

title: “great location, good hotel”
text:
This hotel is in a great location making it easy to get to times square etc ........,
We travelled with our two children aged 10 and 12 and found the room to be of good size for all of us. The rooms were clean and looked ok. We didn't eat at the hotel as it was really expensive - especially the room service. Overall a good hotel in a great location.

title: “A resort without valet parking... this first impression set the stage for the stay.”
text: The resort is extremely disorganized and looks more like a patched work amusement park where each year they add on new rides (i.e., buildings). It was surprising that a resort could function without a decent valet service as you find yourself walking a lot to navigate the oddly laid out facilities. An additional charge for the fitness center was not appreciated and parking seemed higher than what was normal for the area. Rooms were in need of a major overhaul and the creepy children paintings in the room were disturbing (e.g., think haunted house). Except for the Trellises Restaurant, the other dining venues were seriously sub-par. Don our waiter at Trellises was probably the best part of our stay as he was friendly and accommodating. Unfortunately I cannot recommend Town & Country as a place to stay.

title: “Great Hotel, good location”
text:
Jury's exceeded our expectations from the time of our arrival to our final farewells. We arrived in Boston at 9:00 am and fully expected to check into the hotel but have to wait until noon or later to actually get into our room. Not so at Jury's! The receptionist had a room ready for occupancy and called for the bellhop. Within a matter of minutes, we were handed our door cards and led to the elevator for the beginning of our weekend. 
Once we entered our room, we were once again pleasantly surprised by the relaxing contemporary decor, absurdly plush bed (which I will get to in a moment), and huge bathroom with a full size walk-in shower! The shower has double shower heads for those hard to reach places. 
Shortly after, the bellhop delivered our luggage, gave us a tour of the room and all of the amenities in it. Explained the layout of the hotel and suggested that if we needed any further service to call the front desk and ask for Keith. I know that this is probably more of the routine learned at the initial training but his demeanor and pleasant smile made me feel like this was going to be a wonderful weekend.
Once we were situated in the room, I took a minute to relax and test out the 'absurdly plush bed' I spoke of earlier. Let me give you a brief description of what that means. The bed was a standard king, long in width and short in length. The bed was covered with 2 decorative pillows, 4 rather large feather down pillows, an overstuffed comforter and underneath that was a feather down blanket. The mattress was pillow top and very, very thick. All in all, the assembled bed reminded me more of a colorful cloud than an actual bed. Needless to say, I had the best rest in a very long time in that bed.
The only drawback is that the room was a little small. But you should expect that if you are going to stay in a hotel that was renovated from a very old police station. In the end, it really doesn't matter that much. Who goes on a trip to relax in a room?
Lastly, after exiting the hotel, we come to location. With all of the outstanding things listed above about Jury's, there is the issue of location that keeps me from rating it a 5. The location isn't bad at all, in fact it is in the charming South End. You are only minutes from Copley Square and Newbury Street (SHOPPING!) or Boston Common for a relaxing day in the park. Unfortunately, it is located a good 20 minute or more walk from the famed Faneuil Hall and Hanover Street in the North End. You will probably use some type of vehicular transportation for the more famous sites like Fenway Park, Harvard, and Boston Harbor. Although that could be said for about any hotel in the central area. Depending on where you stay determines where you can walk to and where you will have to ride to.
One last note more for Jury's than anything. You should change the 3-D holographic design in your elevators. It's so big and so out of place with the rest of the European design.

title: “Filthy hotel - be warned”
text:
We arrived early on the day of our stay, and they offered to put our bags in their locker room whilst they sorted out the room. We got back at midnight and the room was ready, but awful.
- There were blood stains on the comforter
- There were body-hairs within the bed
- The toilet was covered in pubic-hairs (i.e. unflushed)
- There was a hole in the wall next to the air-vent.
I have added photos for you to see.
The first two were unacceptable, but they did come and give us new sheets and a comforter at midnight. The latter we only realised in the morning after a freezing night's sleep (we had ensured all the windows were closed and couldn't find the hole in the dark).
Also the internet didn't work and their reason was "the connection isn't that good in the corner rooms" the first time, the second time we complained they said it was "because lots of people are on-line" - at 0200 in the morning on a weekday in New York - really!
After complaining they changed our room for the last three nights and the manager guaranteed the room would be clean. The room was cleaner (not hard), however there were still hairs on the bedsheets, so we had to get them (again) to bring up some clean ones.
Apart from the state of the room:
- Breakfast: nice selection of hot and cold items, however the 
- Internet: regardless of the room, it was slow and prone to cutting out.
- Location: a block from Central Park, and the subway, so great.
- Staff: nice, always willing to help with all our problems, and polite too. There was issues with the cleaning and room-staff however based on the cleanliness of the rooms.
Overall, I wouldn't recommend staying here unless you are willing to risk a filthy room

title: “Spacious & Appley”
text: While at first it may not look as extravagent as the other hotels in that area of New York, the Best Western is first in the terms of location. Another good factor is the size of the rooms and the kitchenette in the room meant you could be as flexible as you wanted. Enjoyed my cheap stay :)

title: “Good place to stay with kids”
text:
If you are looking to stay in Time Square with teens or kids, consider this hotel. Our room was a standard hotel size, not the tiny size you hear of in NYC. If you request a room with 2 beds, you will get queen size, not full. It is extremely quiet. I could not hear Time Square noise at all. I booked a standard AAA rate and requested a high floor. I was given a room on the 30th floor and could see the Empire State Building. All in all, I have no complaints. 
I would recommend this hotel for business travelers as well.

title: “Great hotel.”
text: Nice clean hotel... both the halls and our room. Our suite for 6 was nice, it wasn't huge, but it was roomy. They are doing construction in the lobby right now, but they should be finished soon. The staff was excellent! Very friendly and helpful. They gladly stored our bags both the day of check-in because we arrived in the city at about 10am... and the day we checked-out until about 8pm when we were ready to leave the city.

title: “Average hotel, friendly staff”
text:
I stayed here for only one night on a business trips right after Thanksgiving. I was assured rooms would be available for my early arrival (I was at the hotel at 2 p.m.) but still had to wait while the rooms were checked if they were cleaned. This was only one hour before their normal check-in time and was somewhat surprising. 
It's an extended stay so amenities are spares, as was expected. I did not get a remolded room and had the pleasure of listening to the light rail go past my first-floor window through the night and early morning. Also, the doors slam VERY loudly.
I appreciated the easy, quick breakfast with fresh fruit and the ample parking.

title: “A fine resort”
text: This is a fine resort (really a motel on steroids), that has beautiful grounds, a good restaurant, and is right across from the marina on one side and a beach (although not one of San Diego's best) on the other. A great place if you like to bicycle (I believe the hotel will lend you one). Great for kids. The only negative is that there is not too much nearby, especially in the way of restaurants, or interesting shops, but that isn't why people stay here. The rates are reasonable except perhaps when there is a concert. This resort is a great spot for intimate concerts and attracts many well known performers. You should check the schedule. When there is not a concert the resort is great for families and couples wanting some rest or leisure at a reasonable rate. If there is a performer on the schedule you like, there hardly could be a better place to stay and watch them.

title: “lovely”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at the Langham this past weekend for 3 nights (memorial day weekend). Overall we loved the Hotel. We loved the location especially close to everything you would want to see in boston historical area. We loved the decor of the hotel and the room they were perfect and very clean. The room we had was a classic king I believe, wasn't to big but perfect for us bed was amazing! we loved the ipod soundock in the room. We got to enjoy the indoor pool and gym which was very nice. Wish the pool was outdoors but think its a great idea for winter months in Boston!. We didn't get to enjoy any of the restaurants since they were very expensive!! We got a great deal from expedia and would definitely stay again. We parked across the hotel in the lot for $10 a day holiday special which was sweet. On out last day the Fire Alarm went off at about 9:30am which was strange but all was taken care of in a matter of minutes with not worries. As we were checking out at the time it didn't really bother us. Checking in and checking out was very smooth.
Boston is a great city!

title: “Great hotel for many reasons...”
text:
Stayed here for a weekend and loved it. The Chandler is a small boutique hotel on 31st between Madison and 5th. It is 3 blocks from Penn Station, 2 blocks from the Empire State Building and a $5-$8 cab ride to any of the main attractions in Midtown - or you can walk it. Times Sq is 9 blocks.
The hotel is very clean, the rooms are smallish but well appointed. Ours came with awesome bath robes, full size ironing board/iron, hairdryer, three phones and even an an umbrella. There is a turn down service which is a nice touch. The bathrooms are very modern with an awesome shower. Our room had a nice 32" LCD TV on the wall. 
There is free WiFi and free coffee. There is a restaurant but we did not use it. The 1231 bar was nice for a couple of beers before going out on the town.
The staff made us feel welcome and they were all friendly. Some trivia: Simon, the husband of 'Real Housewife' Alex McCord was the GM there for several years until quite recently.
I would definitely stay there again. Neither myself nor my wife had any complaints at all.

title: “Excellent Service”
text: Excellent service, clean rooms, and the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in! The renovations are coming along nicely and are nearly complete, certainly unobtrusive. I would definitely return.

title: “Not as bad as everybody says!”
text:
The Hollywood In Express South is not a five-star hotel but it not as bad as many of the reviews say, either.
We stayed there for two weeks (two adults, one child) and found most of the the staff members quite friendly. The pool is small but nice, the rooms are not luxurious but spacious and well-equipped. The beds and the bathroom were perfectly clean. After a while one gets a little sick of donuts for breakfast but again, for that price one can't expect a big breakfast buffet. For a change one can try the great Brooklyn Bagel Bakery just around the corner, and there are a few fast food places within walking distance. 
The rates are certainly good, the location is convenient and we would definitely consider coming back!

title: “Very Very Nice”
text: Got a good deal, got upgraded to a suite. Was really large with ample space for everything. Free Wi-Fi was very nice, free business center with printer was also a huge plus. The front desk was very helpful. Wasn't the most comfortable bed in the entire world, but it wasn't bad either. Location was great if you are going to Boston Medical Center or the Brigham and Women's Administrative Center, but really not much around in the terms of food or other things. Still highly recommended.

title: “Abuse of the elderly”
text:
Comfort suites 7111 Rancho Mission Drive Houston TX 77083
An elderly 83 year old woman, who was a guest at this hotel, was having breakfast in the morning. She had dry-mouth due to the medication she was taking. She asked for a bottle of water with her meal. She was told to go drink from the fountain. When she repeated her request for a bottled water, she was told the case of bottled water was locked in the manager's office.
When the manager arrived, the manager called the police: she said she did not want this elderly woman on the premise. The senior citizen want to get her things from the room and the police said if she did not leave immediately, she will be arrested. The elderly woman left the premise. Some other guests had to go to her room to collect her things. This happened before the checkout time which is a violation of the written contract her had with Comfort Suites at check in.
I used to think that Comfort suties was a good hotel but it appears their public relations need a lot of work.
This elderly woman should have been given a bottle of water as she requested even if they had to charge it to her room.

title: “Good Airport Access”
text: Very comfortable hotel with an adequate breakfast buffet. Proximity to the airport is good, but shuttle service was not predictable nor reliable. Front desk staff were very polite. There is a Ruby Tuesdays restaurant right next door that you can visit or get room service from. They obviously try to keep their hotel very clean.

title: “Bad customer service”
text:
We stayed two nights at the Farmer's Daughter in January 2006. This is the second time we have stayed here in two years. The actual hotel is fine. It has clean rooms and is in a good location. It is directly across the street from the Farmer's Market which has excellent and afforable food (try Loteria taqueria for great breakfasts, lunches and dinners and Mexican coffee). 
The customer service, however, is sorely lacking. The hotel now has mandatory valet parking which apparently was included in the price of our room. We did not know this when we pulled up and the young valet boy could not articulate this, nor was he assertive enough to do his job. This hotel, really a motel, does not need valet parking, by the way. It is too small, and if your room is in the annex building, you end up having to walk very far with your bags, with no offer of a bell hop service. Anyway, we ended up parking our own car and were rudely chased down by who I assume to be a manager, although, he never introduced himself. He shouted at us that we could not park our car ourselves. We explained that we were not aware of the mandatory valet service and that we asked two of his staff members who could never answer us. He never apologized, and acted poorly overall. We did not feel like guests, but intruders. 
BTW, this motel uses the term parking to mean valet. 
We will not stay here again.

title: “Absolutely amazing location!”
text:
If you want to be right in the middle of everything happening in Times Square, the Doubletree Guest Suites is the hotel for you! We absolutely loved the location. It was so convenient for everything we wanted to do on our 3 day, 2 night trip. We had purchased tickets for one of the bus tours of the City, and one of their stops was right outside the hotel, making it incredibly easy to get on and off. It's also near the theaters if that's what you're in New York for, as well as many stores. 
The least convenient part of this hotel is just getting into it. From the street enterance, you take an elevator up to the 3rd floor, where the lobby is located. From there, you get on a separate set of elevators to go up to your room. I understand that this is most likely due to space issues-better to be tall than wide in NYC!-as well as security, and really, it wasn't a problem at all. Just one of those things. The only other negative that I can mention is that, being right in Times Square, the lights are ALWAYS going, and there's no end to the honking and noise from people. The rooms do a pretty good job of keeping those distractions out, but if you're a light sleeper you may have problems.
We walked here quite easily from the Port Authority bus terminal with our luggage. There's a McDonalds right next door for cheap eats, and obviously endless other options of restaurants close by. We did order room service one night, just some soup and a dessert, and it was very good. Really, though, if you're in NYC, make the most of it and try some food while you're out and about. 
We had our 9 year old along with us, and having the 2 room suite was wonderful. He was able to sleep on the fold out couch and have his "own" TV, while we had a separate TV in the bedroom. Having each room have an enterance to the bathroom was wonderful. The convenience of a mini fridge and microwave was wonderful. 
I highly recommend this hotel for your trip to NYC!

title: “Great mid-range hotel”
text:
We really enjoyed staying at this hotel. For us, it was perfect. It was clean, charming, and had great service and a convenient location.
The hotel staff were friendly, helpful, and efficient. No matter how late in the day we left the room, when we came back, the room was cleaned and we had fresh towels. 
The location can't be beat: right across from Lincoln Park. It is a nice, safe neighborhood. There is a bus stop just across the street. Just a couple of blocks away is Old Town. 
It *is* an older hotel that has been remodeled in a cool retro style, so if you like new and sleek, this isn't your place. The rooms *are* pretty small, so if you like to hang out in a big room instead of getting out into the city, this isn't for you. (We found that hanging up our clothes and putting the rest in the three chest of drawers worked for us and left us plenty of room.)
The room had the good kind of air conditioner, that you could turn on "fan only" for white noise, so the street noise never bothered us.
But if you like a charming, retro, clean, affordable, and convenient, this is the perfect place. When we come back, this is the place we'll stay!

title: “Excellent Business & Lesiure Accomodations”
text: I recently stayed at the Hard Rock Chicago for a Business Trip. The Room was very comfortable. The Business Center was extremly accomodating in helping me to print documents that I had forgotten. The Location was perfect located right on Michigan Ave, I was able to walk to Millenium Park prior to my meeting on Monday Morning and wish I would have had more time to do some shopping as they were not far either. I would highly reccomend this for anyone traveling on either business or for fun.

title: “Very Nice Stay”
text: We stayed at the Seattle Marriott Waterfront the week of August 16th and enjoyed our stay very much. The hotel is not large, but is well maintained and in a great location. It is true that a train runs behind the hotel, but we did not hear any train noise inside the hotel during our stay. 5 minute walk to Pikes Place Market and 10 minute walk to downtown. We experienced superb customer service through out our stay. Concierge lounge was small, but nice. Only drawback was $25 valet parking, but there really wasn't another viable option and we knew this going in, so not a big deal. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Worth it in Fort Worth”
text:
On a weekend trip to Ft Worth, we stayed 2 nights at the Omni. This hotel is very clean and has great cowboy/western decor which really made us feel like we were in Texas. The hotel is on the trolley shuttle which will take you downtown Ft Worth to Sundance Square. Very unique area with shops, restaurants, etc. 
The hotel is within walking distance to the TRE (train that takes you to Dallas). And, although we weren't there for a conference, it seemed like the place to stay if attending a conference since the Convention Center was right across the street.
We told them it was our anniversary so they upgraded us to a corner room with a king size bed, walk in shower. Very nice! They also sent up a complimentary bottle of red wine. If ever in Ft Worth again, we'll be back to the Omni!

title: “Is overrated”
text:
We stayed there for four nights and were somewhat disappointed: Refrigerator was out of service, glasses were not washed and two days later disappeared without being replaced; not very sound proof (banging of doors in the morning and loud radio/TV in the evening). Bathroom was very small and the sink had cracks. In addition the internet was expensive (14$/day) and also the price for parking was stiff (50$/day+tax). (Parking fee can be halved if you park your car in the public garage across the street). Check out was very slow (10 minutes to take care of one person) Positive: Room was clean.
In view of all this we would give to this hotel one star less than advertised.

title: “A great stay in a classy boutique hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Whitehall for 5 nights at the end of September. We found our stay extremely comfortable, loved the amenities and the staff most helpful. We will be back!

title: “Nice addition to Denver!”
text:
My husband and I live in Denver, and had the opportunity for 24 hours on our own while family members watched our kids, so we decided to try out the Ritz. Generally speaking, we try to stay at Four Seasons when looking for a luxury experience, but of course that's not an option in Denver.
This Ritz actually surprised us - it's much more Four Seasons-like than the other Ritzes I have been to. Very contemporary and more understated than the typical Ritz.
Valet was friendly and prompt, no problems there. Valet was $25 overnight, but it's a Ritz and it's downtown, what do you expect? (As a side note, if you go there to use the spa, valet parking is free.) We were offered bell services but didn't need any assistance since we had one tiny suitcase between the two of us.
Front desk staff were very professional and friendly, very easy check-in process.
The rooms are huge with unique and beautiful hardwood entry. Beds were comfortable with very nice linens. Flat screen HDTV I think was 32". There was an espresso maker in the room - we didn't use it but what a nice touch! The view was of another building - the location of the hotel isn't great for mountain views and I was told that the only rooms with mountain views are the suites. I see the mountains every day so I didn't care much, but it's too bad that out of town visitors won't get a nice Colorado view.
Bathroom was very nice, separate shower and large tub, double sinks and separate water closet. Shaving mirror in the shower was nice for my husband, and water pressure was fine. Frette towels were terrific and the toiletries smelled great. I loved that they had a full sized Ionic hairdryer in the room. 
I have to admit I am a bit perplexed by the location. The hotel used to be an Embassy Suites so I can see the appeal of renovating an existing building, but I can't say I'd expect to see a Ritz directly across the street from the Greyhound station. While the location is pretty good in terms of being a short walk to many attractions, restaurants, etc., you're still stepping over a lot of homeless people and the bus station and immediate area is a bit sketchy, particularly at night.
We ate both dinner and breakfast at Elway's - the only restaurant on site. (Though there are many others close by.) We weren't terribly impressed with the dinner. The food all seemed to be overseasoned and the tuna appetizer we ordered was just OK - lacking in imagination. Our steaks were both overcooked. The manager came over (we didn't really complain, just asked that our steaks be redone) to apologize and comped our entire meal other than drinks. It wasn't awful - I'd give it another try if Denver didn't have so many other choices for a steak dinner - Morton's, Sullivan's and Capital Grille are all superior choices and all reasonably close. We had dessert via room service - a warm brownie with ice cream, and it was delicious. The breakfast, though expensive, was quite good.
We both booked appointments at the spa. I have been waiting for a luxury hotel with spa to open in Denver because the day spas, though plentiful and many upscale, don't give the same relaxation, in my opinion. The Ritz spa has a beautiful locker room and two relaxation rooms - one where the therapist comes to get you for the appointment, and the other where you won't be bothered at all. (Different rooms for men and women.) The locker room has several showers with dual shower heads, a steam room, whirlpool, and plenty of space and products to get showered and dressed. Towels and bathrobes were soft and fluffy as you'd expect. Relaxation room had cozy chaise lounge chairs, magazines of course, fruit water, tea, nuts and fruit. I discovered a few minor problems and all were taken care of immediately by the attentive staff. My massage was wonderful, and I'd highly recommend the lime blossom scalp treatment - smells amazing.
We did not use the gym, though it is a gym that my husband used to belong to before it was renovated and linked to the Ritz. We did take a walk through it. It's a full-service gym, you won't be waiting in line for anything or find that it's lacking in equipment.
Overall, I loved it and would recommend the Ritz Denver to anyone. We were also astonished at the price - $199 a night! The hotel was booked solid when we were there, so I'd be surprised if that price sticks around long. If we have the chance to stay again we definitely will, even if the price does go up.

title: “Girls Weekend”
text:
Stayed here to visit with my long time friend & do lots of shopping. The hotel was nice, but could of been in a better part of town. I liked it for the airport shuttle, I had to leave at 4am to get my flight and they paid for a private limo to take me to the airport, NICE!!! The morning breakfast is good and the cook is awesome, remembering so many orders. The evening reception is nice and they are generous with drinks. Pool area nice also.
The only problem we had was someone pounding on our door in the middle of the night. We called the front desk and they sent security up right away. Also people partying in the parking lot.

title: “awesome stay in Indy”
text:
Our stay at The Canterbury was nothing short of EXCEPTIONAL! 
Upon arrival we were greeted by a very nice bellman who assisted us with your luggage and valet parked our car. We reserved a standard king room which we were able to upgrade to a suite upon arrival which was a few dollars more, but well worth it!
The room was perfect! It offered a huge sitting area with a four poster bed where we slept better than we do at home. We enjoyed room service on Saturday morning, I highly recommend the French Toast, it was absolutely the best I have ever tasted. The service and attention to detail by all the staff was refreshing and appreciated!
We enjoy finding special quaint hotels like this when we travel, they extend a warmth and charm you do not find with the larger chain hotels. We will recommend this hotel to all our family and friends as well as we plan on returning soon for another wonderful experience.

title: “Icing on the cake”
text:
I thoroughly enjoyed my time in New York and to just top things off the hotel was a) clean b) spacious and c) offered great customer service. Reading some of the reviews i was aprehensive coming to the hotel as i had booked it before checking on any recommendation websites. This was my 2nd time in New York but my girlfriends first and she was celebrating a birthday while we were there. On our check in they had it noted on my reservation that it was her birthday and gave us a complimentary upgrade to a queen delux room which was a great start to the holiday. I hear the space in rooms in NYC is not much however this had all the room we needed and at no extra cost. The staff were friendly and the rooms were cleaned every day and we were not disturbed while this was done. The bed was fantastic with different settings for comfort and the tv was large and HD. The bathroom was clean and th hot and cold water working fine. The only issue i had with this room was that the heating didn't really work but at the time it wasn't an issue. We stopped on floor 26 (out of 27) and had no trouble sleeping so i would recommend a higher floor. 
Overall i would definitely recommend this hotel and do not judge until you have experienced it, otherwise on the back of some of these reviews i would have staye somewhere else. I'm glad i stayed here, the staff were fantiastic and it really capped our break!!

title: “I expected a lot better!”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Westin from 4th to the 8th December, 2004. Perhaps I`m being very niave, but it was our 25th Wedding Anniversary on the day we booked in, and although I mentioned this when booking a few months earlier, there was not as much as a free newspaper in our room when we arrived. The check-in clerk knew about our anniversary from notes on the screen, but still tried to sell me an upgrade without a trace of personal service. A 5 dollar bunch of cheap flowers would have meant the world to us!
Anyway, much more important to would-be patrons of the hotel are the facts, facts, facts. The room was a decent size with an average, but not spectacular view. It was clean and had up-to-date decor but not well lit. The bathroom however was not nearly as clean as I would have expected for a modern hotel. Corner areas were positively filthy and in general it was small, dark and claustrophobic. Most worrying and disturbing was the fact that you could hear a pin drop in the hallway outside, and when we had noisey neighbours for a night in a room opposite, we heard every shout, scream and swearword! Noise from the room adjoining ours was also easily heard. For this reason alone, I would very much doubt ever using the hotel again. I need my sleep!
Shulahs Restaurant onsite served excellent food,but I found to be very expensive, and if you like to sit 40 foot apart from your partner at the end of a long narrow table,but 2 inches from the stanger next to you, you won`t be dissappointed! I`m sure that given the teeming metropolis of NY, there must be hotels offering better value-for-money.

title: “Awful place”
text:
I travel quite frequently and stay in many hotels around the world.
Without a doubt, this is the worst place I have stayed.
I can't comment on the staff as I didn't really have any interaction with them, but my complaint is with the actual hotel itself.
You will love this place if your idea of fun is spending the weekend in prison. It is dark, smelly, dirty and oppressive.
Black walls and ceilings, really? I can appreciate that decor is subjective, but, were not talking faux dive here - that's really grime on the bathroom walls and stains on the curtains.
Would never stay here again.

title: “mostly fine”
text:
The hotel was mostly good. The room is quite spacious and clean. I had a room on a high floor facing the river, so I really enjoyed the view.
The stay would have been perfect, except for the house-keeping -- she kept using her key to come into my room even though I had the privacy sign (or "peace and quiet" sign as they call it) out on the door knob. I was still sleeping, and she woke me up 3 times by coming in. I told her to go away, but then only 20 minutes later, she called me and woke me up again.

title: “Need to clean the rooms”
text: I travel alot and it is important to me to have a nice Hotel with clean rooms.The hotel itself is beautiful the staff exellent but the room was horrible. When we checked in the room had mold in the bathroom, black dirt in the shower head,rusted bathtub and a huge stain in the rug by the television, we called down to the front desk and asked if we could be moved, they changed our room same floor larger room cleaner but not great, bathroom was dirty,mold, floor was filthy, did not want to move again so we cleaned it ourselves and stayed. The ice machine was broken on that floor so everytime we needed ice we had to go up or down one floor.I was afraid I was going to come home with bedbugs.I loved this hotel but would not stay again. Cleanliness is important to me but apparently not important to the hotel, hopefully they willl fix this problem so other people can enjoy their stay. I spoke to Ramon about the problem and he told me he would get back to me, havent heard from him yet. For 360.00 a night I thought that I could at least have a clean room.I took photos of the room unfortunately I dont know how to post them.

title: “Nice find in china town”
text: Clean, quiet, friendly staff. Parking a pain....checked inch gave me the penthouse. About the size of a small bedroom. Comp. breakfast 2 doors down where new yolks finest were also dining.

title: “Modern hotel, helpful staff, and perfect location”
text: Our first stay at The Pearl Hotel, and it was a very very pleasant one - we had requested a room with two double beds, and were offered an upgrade to the executive king suite on the 11th floor upon check-in, and were happy that we accepted it. Very clean, modern, efficient, warm and spacious - we were happy to find six spacious bureau drawers to unpack into, and one of the best shower/bath combinations we've seen in a long time. We took advantage of the complimentary wine and cheese reception upon checking in, and one complimentary continental breakfast - every other morning we enjoyed the luxury of sleeping in until 10 am. We asked for recommendations from the concierge for a Saturday evening restaurant prior to a show at Lincoln Center, and Shannon graciously accommodated us, leaving both a voice mail in our room and a reservation slip at the front desk for us to pick up later. Our room was VERY quiet, with great ventilation and easily controlled by us for our comfort. Our entire experience here was seamless - a job well done by the entire staff! A bonus tip - the hotel is directly across the street from The Book of Mormon - we avoided long lines for the restrooms at intermission by dashing across the street to use the hotel lobby restrooms - accessible with our room keys

title: “Good location, friendly and personal service”
text: We live locally so don't often stay in Boston hotels but had a birthday to celebrate and had a good offer to stay at this hotel. We booked two rooms, one for us, one for the kids, and had a really nice stay. There are glitzier hotels in Boston, for sure, but the Lenox is in a very convenient location on Boylston Street (in Back Bay - excellent for Newbury Street, Hynes Convention Center, Prudential Center, Fenway Park, most of the local colleges - not on the waterfront or in the financial district) . The rooms were nice, comfortable, and we had a great stay. It's a smaller, more compact hotel - you won't feel like you're crossing a huge lobby or fighting the crowds. The room size is decent though, I've seem much smaller ones in far more expensive Boston hotels. What made it special was how nice all the staff were, even sending a cake up for my son's birthday and really making him feel important. I have definitely recommended this to friends and would return myself.

title: “All about guest service, not about hours...”
text: Great price for the value and guest service exceptional... even for one day. Upon arrival, greeted courteously, free cookies at desk, given great room as a goldpoints member (highly recommend you join, it's free)... slept great... upon checkout, we were extremely delighted that despite the hours saying 7am continental breakfast, we found it was all ready at 5:30am since we were not the only ones having to leave early... which gave us a chance to eat before running... best quick breakfast I've had and we travel a lot...omelets, sausage, fresh waffles, etc. They also have breakfast bags to go for those who can't stay. A great service treat! Thanks!

title: “Very pleased with the hotel, location, and the room.”
text: The hotel is quite pleasant. The rooms are clean and well appointed. Will definitely stay there again.

title: “The hotel has it all: great location, service, and facilities”
text: When I booked our stay at the Omni, I did so because of its location and trip advisor reviews. It may have been the best hotel decision I have ever made. The price was very competitive with the same class hotels in the Union Square area. The location was perfect-an easy walk to Union Square shopping, the Ferry Building, Embarcadero, public transportation, great restaurants, etc. Despite an abundance of homeless people in San Francisco's downtown area, the area by the hotel did not seem to have that problem. The hotel lobby and the room were exquisite. Our room was on the 15th floor and had a partial view of the city. The bed was very comfortable. The room had a desk and a chair with an ottoman. The closet was fairly large and included a safe and bathrobes. Everything was very clean. The staff was great. They brought in cookies and milk every afternoon for my son. We requested a cot for my son because there was only 1 king size bed in the room (my mistake when booking). The cot was almost like a rolling twin size bed so my son slept very comfortably. On a Sunday night, when we asked the front desk staff for dining suggestion, instead of steering us to the hotel restaurant, they recommended a nearby tavern that was great (Wayfare Tavern, owned by Tyler Florence). I suppose that, had I rented a car, I would have complained about the parking fees. However, it is like that everywhere in downtown San Francisco. You really do not need a car there. The public transportation can take you pretty much anywhere.

title: “A very well located clean hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel Metro for six nights on business. Whilst I was slightly reticent at the prospect of staying in Midtown - which is hardly the nicest part of Manhatten - I was actually pleasantly surprised all 'round.
Location wise, you are a very short walk indeed from either 34 Herald (N,Q,R,W trains if you're going downtown to Wall Street/Battery Park and Liberty Island and the B,D,F and V trains if you're off to Queens or the Lower East Side, both of which are worth a visit) and only another block again to Penn Station. You're two blocks from Time Square and two again to the Empire State Building and only from Macys. It's only a ten to fifteen minute walk up to the top of Fifth Avenue if you want to take in the sights as well.
But, the best part is that despite being in such a great location, you're not slap bang in the middle of the tourist horror traps of Time Square. You don't step out of the hotel into the latest wave of back-packing students, or hoardes of tour groups that insist on standing the full width of the pavement.
The hotel itself is modest, but was spotless, as was my room. I have stayed in more expensive hotels that have not provided a room as immaculate as the one I stayed in.
One tip, though - if you can, ask for a room at the back of the hotel. The rooms on the front can be noisy on account of passing traffic (it's not a busy road, but New Yorkers tend to use their horns at every possible opportunity). It didn't help that next door but one to the hotel is a construction site that was operating 24 hours a day. 
The bed was very comfortable, the pillows a generous size and the housekeeping staff attentive and civil. Whilst the hotel may be looking a little dated, it's not horrific and was very clean throughout.
The fitness studio was very good indeed. Sorry to labour the point, but there are more expensive hotels out there that provide nothing more than a few mismatching dumbells and a third-hand treadmill. The fitness equipment was very new, offered a good range of choice and the area was air-conditioned and served by two huge flat screens. On the roof of the hotel is a very unusual and pleasant terrace which offers some nice views and must be very nice in the summer months.
My room had a new iron and ironing board in the room, a decent safe, decent size TV and a speaker system that will fit your iPod, so you can even take your favourite tunes with you.
If you want a magnificant, opulent hotel that will rip you off on the room rate and cost of breakfast - rather then the very ample and free breakfast consisting of a big range of different bagels, breads, fresh juice, coffee, breakfast cereals, yoghurts etc served at the Metro - then this isn't for you.
Considering the price, the great location and standards of the rooms, it's certainly worth giving serious thought to staying here. 
I was a satisfied guest of the Metro and would stay there again. 
This hotel is particuarly suitable for tourists who want the convenience of being Midtown but who don't want to be right on top of Times Square and the associated noise and problems that brings. In addition, if you're on business, you're very well placed to take a short walk uptown or hop on the Metro to go to Wall Street.

title: “Great, eco-friendly hotel!”
text: My coworkers and I stayed at Hyatt at Olive 8 for 2 nights during 4th of July weekend. We went on a road trip from California. This was their first time in Seattle so I wanted to make sure we stayed downtown, where we can have the best access to restaurants, shops, bars, and so forth. The location is ideal, as we were able to walk to a lot of places. The room was very neat and was organized neatly and efficiently. It also had great downtown views. We enjoyed the indoor pool, which was very nice and clean. We ordered room service one night and the food tasted delicious. Overall, the ambiance and customer service exceeded our expectations. My coworkers will definitely remember their first trip to Seattle thanks to this amazing hotel.

title: “Okay' but only just okay.”
text: Nice Hotel but needs redecoration. The beds were a bit too soft and the furniture was a little old and broken in places. The bathroom was small and also needed redecoration. The front desk staff were fine. Although the night shift clerk was not very friendly when we checked in. I hope this perhaps has changed maybe he had a bad night?? The surroundings were clean and efficient. This hotel is okay for a night or two and the freeway is easily accessible from hotel.

title: “Not bad, would stay again but on the other side of the building”
text: The hotel is clean, well kept but is too close to the elevated highway and the rooms may be too noisy at times. The lobby is pretty impressive, the staff at the front desk are very nice and helpful. The Inner Harbor and Fells Point are 1 and 1.5 miles away respectively and make for a nice walk. I will definitely stay here again but will request a room on the opposite side of the building.

title: “A bit of chic in the Lower East Side”
text: Both my friends and trusted website metrotwin.com raved about the Hotel on Rivington, so I decided to stay there during a recent trip. If you like Lower East Side cool fused with a bit of pampering, then you're going to love the Rivington. We stayed on the 12th floor and was amazed at how quiet the rooms were, despite the busy streets below. And the view from my room was just stunning. The rooms themselves are spacious and generous - our bed was gigantic and the tub in the bathroom could have filled an army. To my surprise, I would recommend this as a romantic get-away, as much as a destination for single travelers wanting to get up to no good in the local area - you couldn't be better placed, the bars between ludlow and stanton all have a cool rock vibe going on, making this a great place to stay.

title: “perfect”
text:
So you have to take a lift to the reception and walk 30 yards to check in - HELP !!
Perfect location , perfect service , perfect rooms , nothing to complain about , quite the opposite , it will be hard to find a better hotel in Chicago , or elsewhere for that matter.

title: “My 6th stay at Clift Hotel... still love it!!!”
text:
The Clift Hotel is fantastic; great service, nice/big/comfortable rooms, excellent bar (The Red Wood Room).
I'll definitely stay there again next time I visit SF

title: “Fantastic!”
text:
Fantastic place - the warm welcome from the doorman the moment you arrive, the incredible lobby , friendly reception staff (nothing is too much trouble). Brilliant bell boys who take your luggage from the car directly to your rooms - and show you where to find everything. Friendly houskeeping staff - Nothing is too much trouble. It would appear to be the kind of place where people actually enjoy working at. 
The room was huge with the most comfortable bed ever and was super clean and well appointed with loads of room for all your shopping!
This is the most amazing place I have ever stayed, in - well worth the extra money to stay here. It really is a luxury hotel and well deserving of its 5 star rating - unlike other we have stayed in. It is well located for shopping and restaurants and everthing here is catered towards your needs as a guest - either for business or pleasure.
I really can't rave enough about the place - I'm looking forward to our repeat visit!

title: “My favorite boutique hotel in NYC”
text: I almost don't want to give away the secret! I love this little place so much. The rooms are small (some tiny), very European. However, the charm outweighs the cons for me. Absolutely lovely sitting room off the lobby - great place to meet friends, and the wine and cheese in the evenings is a great touch. I would recommend this place to anyone visiting the upper east side.

title: “Great hotel”
text: We spent two nice nights here and found the location of this hotel to be absolutely perfect. We walked everwhere, including Faneuil Hall, Quincy Market, Cheers bar (both locations), Boston Commons, etc. You'd be hard pressed to find lodging in a better location within Boston. The Freedom Trail runs right in front of the main entrance.The hotel is beautiful and well maintained and we found the staff friendly and helpful. The food was very good though the Boston Creme Pie was disappointing considering it was invented in this hotel.Our room was very nice but quite small and cramped and we had a problem with the AC unit, though it was fixed promptly once we reported it. However, we didn't spend much time in the room because it was so easy to get everywhere. Overall I'd say it was a great choice of hotels if you're visiting Boston and want to be close to everything. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Clean and comfortable with character!”
text: I just dropped my daughter off to begin college at SFSU! We're from San Diego, not at all familiar with the Bay Area, so were a bit overwhelmed at the prospect of figuring where to stay, getting her moved in using public transportation and and still seeing some sights. For the spring SFSU "Sneak Preview" we stayed at the Grant Plaza in Chinatown (after fleeing the terribly located Alpine Inn in Daly City)and loved it, but realized we needed to be closer to the school this time. The Ocean Park Motel was perfect. We got the two-bedroom, three-queen bedroom suite for about $175 per night. Specific instructions are left in the rooms regarding where to eat, how to get there, as well as recommended tours and how to get there all via Muni transport. Muni/bus stops are steps from the motel so not only did we get quickly to and fro from SFSU, but were also easily able to get to the city and up the coast. The room was very clean and comfortable. When the toilet wouldn't stop running, Mark was up to our room immediately and had the problem fixed in minutes. I loved the history of this little place, too, and would definitely recommend it if for whatever reason you want to be out of the bustle of the city. And as far as proximity to SFSU, I'm certain it's the best choice. While the Days Inn is also nearby, it (alas) has no character like this little gem.

title: “Great hotel. Great location”
text: Excellent hotel. Wonderful staff. Everyone was very helpful. Your best bet if you are going to the convention center. The only complaint is the elevators were very slow! Ask for a low floor and walk up when you can

title: “I guess you get what you pay for with some surprises”
text: My sister and I arrived Sat June 9th-June 12th. First night extremely tired so went to sleep. Waking in the morning I noticed dried blood stains on both of my pillow cases and my sisters. In looking at the rest of the linens there was dried blood on my bedspread as well. My sister went down to the office where the manager was working at the front desk to get the linens changed quickly. His response to my sister was "that is interesting". I have worked in health care and the thought of the blood borne pathogens was freaking me out. He didn't even apologize or anything which made me rather uncomfortable.with the whole situation.

title: “not terrible”
text: The traditional rooms really need some help--very rough around the edges. The bed wasn't bad, but wasn't nearly as nice as the beds in other Westins I've visited. I'd give it a 2.5, but since that's not an option, had to go with a two.

title: “Wont Be Returning”
text: My fiance and I booked a room through Priceline.com months in advance. I was excited until the first morning of my visit. House keeping knocks on your door between 8 and 9 am in the morning. They did this everyday I was there waking me up. The room and establishment was clean, but my restroom sink was clogged. The pool was dirty throughout the weekend. And to top it off,THEY REBILLED MY CREDIT CARD, EVEN THOUGH I PAID IN ADVANCE. That really soured me. I would return only if I had a choice between Wingate and a hotel in an unattractive area.

title: “Convenient and quiet”
text:
Stayed at this property on a business trip for five nights, and was pleasantly surprised. The location is great - while the street that the hotel is quiet, the hotel is in a great midtown location. You can walk (25 minutes) up to Times Square or (25 minutes) down to the NYU area. The hotel is also close to several subway stations, making the whole city easily accessible.
The rooms are incredibly small (not much room to move around), but if you're in NYC to sightsee and visit, the room size shouldn't be too much of an issue. The beds were extremely comfortable, and the size of the hotel (rather small, with only a few rooms on each floor) made for quiet evenings and restful sleep. 
The amenities of the hotel are so-so, and nothing worth noting. The staff at the front desk vary - some are extremely helpful, and others seem like they wish they were anywhere else - carrying on personal conversations, not providing many details or information about the hotel and surrounding area. My only complaint about the hotel would be the poor attitudes of some of the staff, but other than that, a solid place to stay while visiting NYC.

title: “Excellent business hotel”
text: The Renaissance Harborplace Hotel in Baltimore has a number of strong points to recommend staying there when on business in Baltimore. First, it is right in the middle of all the Inner Harbor venues: the convention center, multiple restaurant sites, all other downtown major hotels, Camden Yards Ballpark, Fells Point, Little Italy, Federal Hill, and the harbor edge. Everything is within walking distance or a short cab ride away. Second, the hotel is upscale business in decor and maintenance with responsive, well-trained staff who deliver. The rooms are large, have all the expected accoutrements, and are not in need of renovation. Third, it is immediately adjacent and attached to a major indoor shopping mall, allowing shopping and multiple meals choices without ever having to go outdoors, a big plus with any bad weather. Although not a destination resort hotel, for business trips it is decidedly reliable and consistent, with excellent rooms and facilities. There are better venues for young families or romantic couples, but for business travel or convention attendance in downtown Baltimore it can't be beat.

title: “Good location, good hotel, friendly service”
text:
-Check-in was quick and efficient. Hotel staff was friendly. I arrived before 3 p.m. so my room wasn't ready yet. They asked if I preferred to be bumped to a queen room or to be placed on the waiting list for the king I had originally booked. Since I was eager to get to my room to get organized, I appreciated the consideration and chose the ready queen.
-The room was tiny but functional. The bed was comfortable and the room was quiet. I slept well (something I rarely do in hotel rooms).
-The bathroom was nice - Aveda products and a nice size. The water pressure on the shower was seriously lacking. It took me a long time to rinse my hair because the pressure stream was so weak. 
-I worked out at the fitness center in the morning - it was pretty nice. Plenty of machines - no wait (and I was there at 6:30 a.m., so prime time). Each of the treadmills has its own TV screen, and the hotel provides free earbuds for anyone who wants to watch. The weight room was not particularly well stocked, though. Still, there was no add-on charge for use of the fitness center as there is at some hotels, so I was not unhappy with the quality of the center.
-I had breakfast in the hotel restaurant the next morning. It was as pricey as I would expect in a city of this size, but it was really good. Good service and good food. 
Overall, my Mayflower experienc was good. I would stay here again, although I might try to score a larger room next time I do.

title: “Good price, Good enough for family”
text:
I booked for less than $70/night for a family of 5 during the Thanksgiving Holidays, So I am pleased with the deal. Because I have a family with small children, I am very picky when it comes to cleanliness and the Double tree was clean. We got a room on the 5th floor. The elevator was clean and roomy. The bed sheets, carpet and bathroom were clean. The bathroom was equipped with a hair dryer. The only thing I didn't like about the bathroom was that the door slides shut without a lock. Apparently it was constructed that way to avoid collision with the main room door but it was not very private. One of the 2 double beds had huge gaps in the padding of mattress itself. It was at the foot end of the bed, but noticeable when you sat on the bed. The tv had regular cable. Not a lot to watch but we were not there to watch tv. Kids watched cartoon network before bed.
The swimming pool is not very big, but we were the only ones using it. Hot tub is stuck to the wall between a door labeled "restroom" which kitchen crew were continuously coming in and out of with kitchen equipment and a small corridor that lead to meeting rooms. There was a nice outdoor sitting area between the hot tub and pool that could use some TLC and would be perfect to have a meal in. The only thing I was disappointing about was that there were no sauna/steam rooms. 
There was a courtesy shuttle that will take you to and from nearby attractions in the downtown area, namely the River Walk and The Mexican Market area. The driver, Mike, was doing the best he could during the busy holiday time to maintain the time schedule, which was impossible with the traffic. In spite of the conditions, I felt he handled the circumstances very well.
The hotel is in a great location. Minutes away from the river walk, Market area, the Alamo, and a short 10 minute drive to the zoo and Japanese tea garden. 
Customer service was good except for the night of the light parade which was the busiest night when the phone for the front desk was continuously busy. They were understaffed. The cleaning staff left a note in my room explaining that there were no towels a the time they cleaned my room and an extension to call for towels when I arrived. A staff member with a set of warm, fresh towels knocked on my door seconds after I called, to my surprise. I did witness a costumer complain that his room was not clean and the staff at the front desk quickly, with no questions asked changed his room. 
Cookies were not offered to me, but when I asked I was given free warm and yummy gourmet Chocolate chip cookies with bits of walnut in them. My children loved those.
This was my first time in San Antonio and after seeing some of the other nearby hotels that I was looking into cooking, I was thankful for choosing the Doubletree. It was clean and in a safe, convenient location. Not Luxurious, but not will not consume half the cost of your vacation either.

title: “better shop around”
text: Great location if you want to be near Georgetown. If we would have stayed an extra night it would have been $359. Got the business rate but that was still $259. Others found rooms for around $100 such as the Grand Hyatte. Only problem we had was the sink in the bathroom backed up twice and this black stuff came up thru the pliumbing . Maid acted like it happened all the time. Otherwise room was clean and the bed was wonderful.

title: “Fantastic for the Price”
text: Our family of four drove up to NYC from Florida in Summer of 2005. We chose this hotel due to reviews like the one I am writing now. NYC can be a very expensive trip but Travel Inn made it far more affordable than we could have expected. The FREE PARKING is definately a major plus for this hotel. We pulled into Manhatten at 10 pm, the garage door was open and there was a parking spot right there in front by the side entrance door. We parked and never drove again using the city transportation and walking the whole trip. Our vehicle was right there and we were able to see it every day as we went in and out. The staff was very nice and the room was clean and basic. Nothing special, but we only slept in it and as long as it was clean and roomy enough, it met our needs. The location was very convenient and within walking distance to Times Square and the Hudson where we took one of the night time cruises (just BEAUTIFUL). When we go back to NYC Travel Inn will be home away from home.

title: “Great hotel for scenic San Diego stay”
text: My partner and I chose the Bay Club Hotel and Marina largely for its scenic location on Shelter Island. We were not disappointed. Our second floor marina-view room was great--beautiful view and ample space. It is an excellent choice if you prefer to avoid the mega hotels in San Diego, which are full of the convention crowds. Hot buffet breakfast is included each morning, far better than any similar hotel breakfast I've had. The decor is a bit simple and slightly dated, but overall quite acceptable. Free wireless internet is provided. The staff at reception and dining room were exceptionally friendly and helpful. We did experience some noise in the room and public areas, due to a rather boistrous large group staying there, but after their departure, it was quieter. We walked to dinner at nearby Bali Hai restaurant one evening, which we highly recommend too. This is a hotel gem which will showcase beautiful San Diego for your visit!

title: “Central location and great room.”
text: We stayed here for two nights and what a delight. We were upgraded to a corner suite, without asking, and found the room so welcoming and the king size bed so comfortable that we did sleep very well. Wi-Fi in rooms has to be paid for...at a very high price..but free Wi-Fi is available in the lobby. The lobby bar provided some great icy cold beer, after a long day of sight seeing it was appreciated, and the staff were very attentive. So close to the main attractions of Washington and easy walking distance to some great eateries.

title: “OK stay”
text: Nice clean room. Right off the freeway with easy acess. Bed was comfortable. Breakfast was very bad. Nothing stocked, no one monitoring ended up going elsewhere.

title: “Quite a disappointment”
text: In sore need of renovation: furniture in the room was dented and damaged; blackout drapes falling off the hardware; shower drain slow; finial missing on lamp and replaced with a bolt that didn't fit so shade was crooked; stains in toilet. A very busy, noisy convention hotel conveniently located with trolley service to other areas. We are lifetime platinum elite Rewards members and this location was about the shabbiest we've stayed in (a total waste of points!). Nice concierge lounge.

title: “Excellent Hotel and Excellent Location”
text: We just returned from a four night stay in Philadelphia. We reserved a room at the Omni for a very reasonable price and were delighted with the staff, the accomodations, and the location of the Hotel. Note: all rooms ending in the number #11 are corner rooms and are larger and have more windows than the others. After we reserved our room, we called a few days before we arrived and asked the staff for a #11 room. And it was a GRAND room. Great views, walking distance to everything--Independence Hall and general environs, Reading Terminal Market, Chinatown.... This is the place to stay in Philly--and we are picky.

title: “nostalgic and quiet”
text: I traveled about 14 hours from Singapore to LA. I stayed in Hilgard house for 4 weeks during my visits to UCLA. Hilgard has its own charm that I liked.
