Majority of the staff members were warm and friendly. I particularly liked the free flow of hot drinks throughout the day. The breakfast was simple and good though not elaborative. In terms of accessibility, needless to say, was excellent. It is very near Ralph (opens 24 hrs) and many eateries and best of all a stone-throw from the medical center where I was visiting. The room condition is clean and acceptable -depends how you make it to be. Though I was referred to an alternative hotel, I chosed to remain in Hilgard house because I find serenity and safe in the environment. I will definitely stay in Hilgard again should I return one day. Thanks to the hotel crews who have made my stay a pleasant and memorable one.

title: “its not fantastic”
text:
unlike most of the reviews ... the hotel staff lobby staff barely noticed us, never had a hello and only had the door held open twice in our 6 night stay. And we only received the "complementary" water 2 of the 6 nights - and once we had to ask the lobby staff in which they had to locate the maid service to drop it off. The AC vent was positioned to where it blew on our faces all night. Plus if the AC wasn't set on 50 HIGH ALL DAY the room was stuffy. (our visit was late May) The carpeted floors in our room felt like wet towels had been left laying around. It wasn't pleasant to walk around without shoes on. We had NO internet reception in our hotel room on the 7th floor. 
Noise was not a problem for us.
the bathroom was big, 
the room size was small but doable 
bed and linens were comfortable -- huge thick pillows (not my taste)
the breakfast is CRAZY EXPENSIVE!

title: “Pleasant stay, but the rooms need updating”
text:
I was thrilled when I booked this hotel at a bargain rate to attend a conference at the Wyndham Washington, about 8 blocks (10 minute walk) away. (The Wyndham Washington's rate was more than double than at the City Center, even with the reduced rate conference attendees received). Checking in and out were seamless processes, but I didn't have much contact with staff otherwise. The lobby is very attractive with dark, hardwood floors and a large, comfortable seating area. The room I was assigned was a corner room and was extremely spacious (judging from the emergency exit map on my door, the corner rooms are the largest rooms). The bed was, as Wyndham always promises, extremely comfortable, and the bathroom included nice amenities from the Golder Door Spa. The room also had a coffee/tee maker, iron and ironing board, and cable TV, but no mini-bar (although they do set out 2 bottles of water for guests which cost $3.50 each). My room overlooked the rear of the building over some rooftops, a small area with trees, and into some office buildings--very quiet except for noisy vents on the roof. The hotel has a great location next to the Ritz, 4 blocks from DuPont Circle and the Metro there, and 10 blocks from Georgetown. 
The only reason I can't give this experience a higher rating is because of the serious state of disrepair in the room. The walls and ceiling had major cracks that had been painted over in a non-matching color (it looked like maybe there had been water damage from the room above). The carpet, although vaccuumed, was so stained and icky looking that I didn't want even my socked feet to touch it. This was a smoking room, and there were multiple cigarette burns in the bedspread, curtains, and couch. Although the shower pressure was fine, the bathroom tiles were stained and cracked, and the wallpaper was peeling. Judging from another review, it sounds like the hotel is being rennovated; I would definitely ask for a newer room if staying here again as the older ones are in truly sad shape (although they may only give the old rooms to people who book bargain prices on-line). 
My only other complaint was that housekeeping doesn't seem to have much respect for "Do Not Disturb" signs. They banged on my door twice when I had the sign hanging out. 
Overall, I was glad to stay here and not at the Wyndham Washington, which has so many conferences and events that their admittedly lovely lobby is like a zoo. Although there was a conference being held at the Wydham City Center while I was there, too, the hotel is much smaller, quieter, and more intimate, and I barely even noticed the conference-goers. I would stay here again, but I would certainly ask in advance for a rennovated room. I would also suggest anyone staying at Wyndham hotels sign up for their free WyndhamByRequest program, which gets you a complimentary bottle of water, drink of your choice, and snack of your choice waiting in your room upon arrival, free local and long-distance calling (!), and 2pm check-out.

title: “Worth your money and Great location...!”
text:
My wife and I are occasional travelers, but we certainly appreciate
clean accomodations and friendly attendance any time !
Stayed at the Sohotel for 10 days and never felt more comfortable
and welcome. We decided to write this, not only to thank the staff
but also to reccomend the place ! The unique blend of the past
architectural features and the modern renovations, gives to you
a different sensation among other hotels choices; anywhere in
Manhattan ! Once we get home, we'll share the experience with
our friends in Italy and thank them again for sending us there....!
Ciao, ...until December....

title: “Great Staff, Excellent Value”
text:
I took my girlfriend to New York for her birthday and booked us at this hotel. The hotel itself is very impressive asthetically. The rooms are clean, tastefully decorated, with comfortable furnishings.
The one thing that stood out particularly was the service, which was excellent. I informed them prior to our arrival it was my girlfriend's birthday and they arranged a bottle of champagne in our room. I saw the manager and thanked him - he got my name right and was very courteous.
For the value and location (five mins walk from Strawberry Fields in Central Park), this place can't be beat.

title: “Overall a nice stay”
text: We stayed at the Edgewater for 2 nights and overall had a good experience. We booked a city view but upgraded to the Jr. suite water view when we arrived. The view was beautiful for both evenings, but the 2nd morning we woke up to a huge cruise ship right outside our window I felt like I needed to keep the curtains closed they were so close. The room was very nice and other then the cruise ship the only complaint would be the bed/pillows, not sure what exactly but my husband and I both slept poorly and woke up stiff and aching in the morning. There are a lot of attractions to walk to nearby and the complementary shuttle was excellent for going farther. Be prepared to walk uphill just about anywhere you go, as the hotel is on the water everything else in the city is up.

title: “The Drury is not Dreary”
text: Our room overlooked the famous River Walk, and was simply delightful. We sat on the balcony in the evenings with a glass of wine, watching the people walking the river, and the riverboats passing by. At night it's all lit up with tree lights, along with the lights from the many businesses and restaurants. We were within walking distance of the Market Square and the Alamo. The room was clean and well cared for. The only downside was that the carpets in the halls were not well vacuumed. Some debris was there for the three days we stayed. Oh, and the breakfast and evening snacks were well intentioned, but definitely institution food. Great to get the two free drinks per night though.

title: “Gem Of Downtown”
text: The Brown Palace is a must stay! The staff is extremely knowledgeable, friendly and professional. When traveling, my boyfriend and I always try to stay in smaller boutique style hotels. This is one not to be missed. It has a beautiful atrium ceiling that is absolutely gorgeous. So even if you don't stay here you should go check it out. The hotel is one of the oldest hotels in Denver and it shows it well. There is a lot of history and tradition in this place. Take time to wander through the hotel as well(it is encouraged)! One thing I really enjoyed seeing was the afternoon tea time. It was nice to see people taking a moment out of their hectic lives to set back and relax.The rooms are clean and comfortable and the linens are as soft as clouds. Take time also to get a cocktail and enjoy the Ship Tavern. We sat down just to enjoy a glass of wine and stayed for much longer due to the fact of their live entertainment. It was a piano player who was playing show tunes. People from the audience were able to participate. It was pretty amazing! We saw a few gems that night! All in all I highly recommend staying here. Its pleasant, well located, and simply beautiful.

title: “It's New York baby, location location location, you are going to be so busy....”
text:
Well New York is Expensive with a capital E, we won this trip from Australia but paid for 6 nights extra Accommodation, lucky we got the Sony Music corporate rate! We just wanted something comfortable and clean, we went out site-seeing that big old city for 9 days and nights straight, getting home very late and out very early in the morning. There is so much to see you don't won't be in your room much at all. Rooms are small (it's New York deal with it), clean, neat, staff were great to us and we were especially treated well by the doormen who did not want us to tip them. The Time was perfect for us to come and go, it's a boutique Hotel so all the rooms are done up in blues, yellows and reds - RED is my fave colour and we got the RED room, it was perfect for what we needed. We played pool in the trendy bar on some late nights and we had booked action packed tours - New York is not a place to go to relax! Highly recommend you grab the 48 hour hop on hop off Double Decker and get yourself orientated, we then went on a Liberty Helicopter tour over Manhattan and started our 3 Day New York Pass which I also highly recommend, this had us running all over that fabulous city seeing everything you could see, it was wonderful to have express entry into everything, have individual maps and details in our little booklet/pass. Make sure you organise yourself in areas, so do all the downtown stuff in one day, then uptown, etc. We took a beautiful Winter horse and carriage ride thru' Central Park, it was so romantic. As I said we won this trip to see Kings Of Leon at Madison Square Garden in Jan 09 and won 3 nights acccommodation, Airfare & tickets as part of the prize, and knew you just can't do New York in 3 days. The food is fabulous, you need to search it out, there is some great street food, google before you go and you will find where the locals hidden gems are. Highly recommend Carmines in Times Square - my husband Romeo is Italian and this was recommended to us by Italian's we know, the service was impeccable and the prices were low and great quality food - ask for Ralph from Brooklyn to be your waiter ha ha, he was a tripper!
The Time is all about location location location, it was perfect for us, everything was close by, the Subway, the Port Authority (we went on a brilliant shopping tour), entertainment, food, shopping - get your little souvenirs downtown, much cheaper!
So much to say about New York! See the photos for the best coffee in New York!

title: “Really Surprised”
text: Went out to see my parents in Phoenix and stopped in San Antonio on the way out and back .I have stayed at the Hilton many times and frankly it was dated .We checked in today and was I really surprised !! lots of Porters and Valets...Lobby redecorated and guess what ?? all the rooms and elevators are too..These rooms are BOSS and I mean it !! I wanted to stay longer when I saw them but they were booked ..I don't want to leave ..This Hotel has done a 180 and you will ,be surprised ..Trust me ..the Desk Attendent, Brian Moreno treated me like a king .They must have a great manager to turn this place around ..

title: “Fab location - hotel not so great”
text:
I was here for 9 nights as part of a business trip to the US. When I checked on I was given room 759 which was tiny, very dark and cramped and looked out onto a brick wall. It was also very noisy. I asked if I could move and was given room 1028 which was almost twice the size, bright and airy with a view towards the harbour and much quieter.
The room itself was fine but the public areas of the hotel are dark and dowdy. I know the hotel is old but it just feels lacklustre.
There are coffee makers in the rooms and if you sign up to the loyalty programme you get free wifi and a choice of drinks delivered to your room each day with a newspaper. For a few extra dollars you can have a bagel, muffin or croissant which is a nice touch.
I found the food in the restaurant to be bland and expensive. There are some amazing restaurants nearby which are much better.
The location of the hotel is brilliant. 5 minutes walk from Quincy Market, 10 minutes from the Harbour and 2 minutes from Boston Common and the Park Street T stop - brilliant! There are other hotels nearby and I would probably choose one of those in future.

title: “Poor Customer Service”
text:
We were there with a Groupon offer. While the reservation process was smooth, once checked in. we asked for a room with a bigger bed. Front desk said that it was our deal to have that room and no changes were available. No free internet. If you want Wi-Fi you have to pay. In our package were included two museum's tickets. I picked the Met, and I was told, during reservation, no problem. Once we got there, they gave me two tickets for the Guggenheim instead. I didn't realize until I got back home. Then I had to travel so I called back the hotel after three weeks, asking if they could kindly change my tickets for the Met, which was my original request. I was told no. They wouldn't do it, even if it was their mistake. 
Location is not that great if you want to catch a subway. There is a pretty long walk to the nearest subway station. Bottom line, I would never go back there, despite the fact that I am a frequent NYC traveler.

title: “awesome beds ,monica and ayleena ..stars”
text: Fantastic location right next to Empire State Building,easy access to whole of manhattan,1st room was a lil dissapointing ,lil tired looking but the bed was amazing ,spent 4 days here then 6 with family and last two days back at hotell,2nd room was fantastic totally refurbished ,amazing bed again,wonderful decor ,lovely towells,the two staff i dealt with were wonderful ,Monica and Ayleena ,try to get these girls if you can ,friendly ,accomadating and professional.all in all I would use this hotel again but I would make sure I book the new room which was awesome,slight noise from air con and outside but nothing to moan about,no view to speak of but hey I was in NY...hoping to be back next june /july ,thanks Herald Square for a lovely visit ..kisses J ,xxxx

title: “Great Staff and Location!”
text: The group at Pier 5 made our first visit to the Inner Harbor a memorable one. The professional and knowledgeable staff made our visit even better with recommendations for food and drinks. A big shout out to Josh and Terence. Both guys are great to deal with and have a vast knowledge of the area. Josh was great with our kids during Crabby Hour. We had a great Harbor view and a very short walk to the National Aquarium. The room was very clean and had great decorations. Thanks again from all four of us.

title: “Outstanding service in potentially difficult circumstances.”
text: I rarely complement anybody on anything, but I feel obliged to relate my recent experience in this hotel. I have been a tour manager (sometimes called tour escort) for the past 16 years. I recently stayed in this hotel which was part of an itinerary I was running for a British tour company. Shortly before arriving, we were involved in a tour bus accident which took place on Interstate 5 close to Tacoma. Two of my 30 British passengers were injured. I contacted the hotel and made them aware of a late arrival. There reaction was AMAZING! They were greater by the front desk manager Paul Hvidsten. They were offered a private meeting room at no extra cost. He personally came as they were being served drinks, oriented them and made sure all would feel appeased and comfortable. Paul double-checked personally that all would go well, and assisted me in every task I had to conduct, liaising with the office manager. But this was just the beginning: from front desk staff and management (Val, Celine, Dylan etc.) to porters to waiters, NOONE worked hard enough to make our guests feel at home and get personal attention, in spite of the fact that this is a very busy hotel and that they had a lot of other people to attend to. Great staff, great rooms, great location, great food, great service. All thirty members of my group made the same remark. We can't thank you enough Paul and on behalf of everyone we will certainly recommend this hotel as you knew how to treat us not only as clients but as human beings and valued guests. Top notch international level of service!

title: “HVS - Elk River - Franchise Training week.”
text: Rooms were nice, elevators were a little slow. The high light was in the A.M. Best "breakfast included" I have ever seen in a Hotel. Lassandra was so fast, so skilled, so pleasant, so efficient, she truly was exceptional. (Good service & Good Personality!) (She'll never have to worry about losing her job!) I asked her "What did you put on that pancake?" She said, "Melted Butter". The butter was grilled in! Wow! Lassandra was my "Mom" reincarnated! Thanks! Great Experience!

title: “Grand historical hotel that misses the mark on service.”
text: I have never been to Memphis and just came from Nashville where we had stayed at the service focused hotel The Hermitage. Check in was unorganized, with long lines. The room was tasteful but dated. Hated the bedding. General lack of of customer first attitude. Bellman would come into elevators with the luggage carts when it was already occupied by hotel guests. I will say that the staff in the gift shop were very nice. The duck walk is a good draw but at twice a day and the fact that there are more non-guest and kids running around really detracts from the elegance of the hotel. Too many add on charges that bring no value.

title: “valuable stay”
text: The hotel is excellent compared to the price. I think travelleres can't get such an affordable and valuable hotel in downtown Philadelphia, so strongly recomand everybody to get it.

title: “Fantastic value in the heart of Manhattan”
text:
We stayed in the Eastgate for 7 nights in August. As others have said before the rooms are enormous ( I think larger than the two bedroomed wimpey house that was our first home ). I travelled with my husband and two teenaged sons and we had a two bedroom suite. This meant that anyone suffering from Jetlag could go and sit in the sitting room whilst others slept. 
It was cool ( in a very hot and humid NY ), very clean, and quiet. The rooms could be a bit smarter, but the carpet in ours looked brand new ( certainly less than a month old ), and the bathrooms were well cleaned each day, and the sheets changed every other day.
We used the laundry room in the basement that has 6 washing machines and four dryers – so we could leave with all our clothes clean.
The location in mid town is great, just in the area that tourists think of when they think of New York. We had 7 day passes for the subway/buses and we became expert at catching the uptown/downtown busses at each end of the block. The buses are clean, and air conditioned, and the stops have the schedules, and the buses are on time.
We asked a question of reception the first day, and they gave us bogus advice ( recommending a taxi to go to somewhere 3 blocks away ) – so we used tripadvisor from then on. Apart from that , the Eastgate was perfect. We got a $200 a night deal which included internet, and the value we got for that price could not be beaten.
Also check out the Mexican restaurant Singuel on 3rd avenue and 40th – the best meal we had in 16 nights in the US. We went on the last night – and wished we could have gone again.

title: “Perfect Location!”
text: Although the room was a bit pricey, the location was excellent. It was very close to all of the main attractions in the Fisherman's Wharf area. Our room was clean and the bathroom was big and bright. The beds were decent, and the pillows were awesome. The decor was nice and modern and the employees were helpful. They even allowed us to check in 2 hours early!

title: “great location, pretty good hotel”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights in Oct 2006. Paid extra for a queen room.
A great location on w 11th street near Was Sq, NYU and the subway. Lovely quiet leafy street. Pleasant staff. Breakfast uninspired. Room looked out onto street, leafy view, plenty of storage space.
Bathrooms pretty basic but never crowded.
A good "budget" stay in NYC. Tip--get the nice room--we saw into a single room and it was cell-like.

title: “Decent hotel for low cost.”
text: Good location. Close to many attractions. Small average rooms but good deal for cost.

title: “Great stay!”
text: While I was in Dallas for a wedding, I really enjoyed my stay at the Sheraton Dallas. Every staff member I came in contact with was exceptionally friendly and worked hard to make my stay enjoyable, from check in to all the times I needed cabs. I used the fitness center twice while I was there (I know, impressive!) It was larger than I expected, very clean, and had lots of equipment. I'm not sure how to explain this and I wouldn't expect it to happen again, but somehow I never had to wait on an elevator...didn't matter if I was on the 1st, 4th, or 27th floor, when I pushed the button, the elevator was just there?!

title: “One of the Best”
text:
This is a hotel that sets the standards for others. First of all the hotel has been beautifully finished with lots of attention to detail. Originally three row houses, the hotel is a beautiful example of how to take something old and revamp it into something wonderful. The staff at Rittenhouse 1715 is outstanding. the continental breakfast is delicious and there is now an option for freshly squeezed juices, omelets and waffles with all the trimmings for a reasonable fee.
 I particularly want to mention the front desk staff who go out of their way to be helpful. As my family and I have stayed at this hotel numerous times, together and as individuals, it is nice to be remembered by name and asked how the rest of the family is as well. It is also nice to see that there is very little turnover in staff, always a sign that people are being treated well. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Excellent Choice - Suprisingly Reasonable”
text:
Stayed with wife for two nights after cruise. Booked room through Priceline at a very reasonable rate. Priceline rates this as a four star hotel and I would agree.
We were checked in early with no problems, and asked for a quiet room on a high floor. Our room on the 29th floor of the north tower was very large, with two queen beds, a sizable work table, and two easy chairs, as well as a large screen TV. The room had a lovely view, partly obstructed, of Elliott Bay, and was very quiet. The room was clean, the beds very comfortable, and the bathroom facilities quite excellent, especially the shower with dual heads. Hot water was plentiful and water pressure quite adequate.
The service at the hotel, although we did not require much, was excellent. The lobby is efficient but lacks charm or character. The lobby seems to be fitted with wi-fi, although I don't know if it is free. The room itself also had a high speed internet connection, but I believe you must pay for it.
The hotel is well situated for most tourist and business needs, and the concierge staff was friendly and helpful.

title: “Great stay - would recommend”
text: My husband and I stayed here for 4 nights (as a party of 4), the hotel is in a great location the staff were always very pleasant and helpful, our room was clean and kingsize bed very comfortable, bathroom was clean with over bath shower. We did not eat in the hotel, so couldn't comment but we can recommend Joanies (Happy Days Diner) just across the road. We have stayed twice in S.F last time we stayed off Union Square but if returning would definately stay at this hotel again - found Fishermans Wharf more relaxed. Recommend Wine Tour and cycling over Golden Gate Bridge.

title: “Awesome spa room, great price, great location”
text:
I used the King Spa room as part of an engagement proposal for my now fiance. The plot went down without a hitch and the staff went so far as to change the name on my reservation at the front desk to help me pull it off in secret. So kudos to them.
The room itself was quite large - especially for being in DC right near Dupont and as cheap as it was. It had an amazing bathroom, too, with a large shower and 2-person jacuzzi tub. This thing was as good as any hot tub I've sat in and really could hold 3 people if that's your thing. haha. Overall, a great experience!

title: “Perfect Business Convention/Meeting Location”
text: This hotel has it all and more. The meeting planner, Janie was most gracious and well organized....she left no detail out of the planning. The support staff, including Veronica, Pedro, Ernest, Maggie, and many others were on the mark. Ok, and not to mention the food...fabulous...great job Eugene and Okan! Planners of any event that is to be held in San Antonio should consider the Westin Riverwalk as the hotel of choice.

title: “Not what I was expecting”
text:
This was the second time staying, the first was very nice. I work in travel and am often given a nice room for the word of mouth, however this trip the room was tiny compared to the first, it was clean but a little shabby. I was told my parking would be covered by a person in sales and when I came the final day to get the car, I was informed that they no longer did that and I would have to pay. I was not prepared for that but did pay. When I went to the hotel they were no help and basically said I could call when she was in on Monday to see what she could do. I was reimbursed however it was a hassle I was not expecting and no help was offered.
It is a good location though.

title: “Great, inexpensive, close to the city!”
text:
The Edwardian is a great hotel for a single person looking for value for money whilst in San Fransiscio.
I stayed there for two nights and was very happy with my room - with a double bed, adequate bathroom and tv. It was quiet both in terms of street noise and other guests in the hotel. There are no closets in the room (so if you have a suit, bring a hanger and hang it in the bathroom).
The Edwardian is very close to the city and the Mission with a bus stop litterally outside the door. There are also a number of amazing places to eat right down stairs.

title: “Will return again”
text:
I've now stayed at this hotel on 2 occassions. On the 1st occassion I was put in a Tower room which I did not care for. Zafar handled the situation immediately and put me in the Main Plaza where I was very comfortable. When I booked this property for the 2nd time, I emailed ahead of time and let Mike Ehmann know my preferences of rooms and he accommodated my request. I travel 80% of the time for work and the simple things like great customer service and attention to detail mean a lot to me. I will definitely stay here again highly recommend this hotel.
Brandi

title: “Consistently good hotel”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel a few times and keep coming back. The rooms are comfortable, the shower heads are at a height that works for a 6'5" guy and it is walking distance to a number of great restaurants. 
During my last stay, I found a billing error after I checked out. I contacted the hotel and they put it right immediately.

title: “A nice, cheap hotel”
text: The hotel was a great place to stay. It is close to many attractions. The staff was helpful in referring us to nearby restaurants. My only complaint would be that the toilet paper is too far away from the toilet. You almost have to get off of the seat in order to reach it. The housekeeping staff was great in locating my clothing that I had inadvertently left behind. They are in the process of shipping it to me. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “New, Fun, Amusing and Clean.”
text:
Small but super efficient rooms. First I found a room where the design and functionality has been optimized to his best.
I have to go back this summer to enjoy the Terrasse.

title: “Excellent!”
text:
We were first time visitors to new york and I had spent ages researching hotels. We got this hotel at a pretty cheap internet rate and that was the main reason we chose it. We thought it was a good base to explore nyc, VERY clean, really modern decor and we liked the Rare burgers! We thought the receptionists were just ok, but we did seem to arrive at a very busy time.
Just one minor complaint, we didn't like our hot our room got, we phoned the front desk because we thought the aircon was broken but they informed us because it was cold outside the aircon was running at neutral, however, we didn't think it was that cold outside and our room was definately at an above average temperature.

title: “One Night Stay”
text: My son and I stayed one night in July when out west for Summer AAU basketball. Upon arrival, I was greeted with a glass of Champagne and a quick check in. The hotel is amazing and is connected to the JW Marriott right across from the Staples Center. The staff was very helpful directing us to the area. The Movie Theatre accross the street is perfect. We enjoyed walking around LA live and had dinner at one of the restaurants. The room was Ritz at its best!! And the turndown service is just what you expect from the Ritz. They even put our slippers they provide right next to our bed! The best part of the hotel is the pool on the 24th floor (I think that is the correct floor). Swimming at night was really awesome. You look up at the residence condos. I used the pool area in the morning also.!!! I highly recommend the RITZ at LA Live.

title: “This hotel is a great value.”
text: I needed a hotel near downtown denver with quick access to Boulder. It was a little difficult to find but well worth the effort. It has clean rooms and and a nice breakfast buffet included. The hotel was just remodeled and looks more expensive than it is. I will definitely return when I need to stay in the area.

title: “Great Location!”
text:
I stayed here Memorial weekend with my husband and 2 kids (ages 11 and 7). We wanted to sightsee, and this hotel was within walking distance to all of the colonial landmarks. Our room faced the Benjamin Franklin Bridge with gorgeous views of the Delaware River. We even saw a bolt of lightning knock out the power on the bridge briefly during a fantastic thunderstorm. My kids were impressed! 
The room was clean, offered a robe and slippers, and it was quiet, despite the fact there was the Jam on the River festival a block away, and weddings and proms going on downstairs. The restaurant was never crowded and the food was delicious. The concierge was helpful with sightseeing tips and the hotel staff was quite friendly.
We really enjoyed this hotel and wished we could have stayed longer!

title: “I love the Sheraton Hotels”
text: The hotel was recently remodeled I believe. The room was small but had all the amenities needed. The Sheraton beds are the best!! The staff was quite helpful & friendly. The food in the restaurant was also wonderful. The one negative is that the shower head is placed too high. Standing on my tipee toes I still had difficulty moving it. I am 5'4".

title: “Front Desk Staff Rude”
text: On a recent trip to Denver to research hotels for my wedding guests to stay at, My Mom and I were excited to check out the Hotel Monaco as we had read many great reviews about it. Upon entering we were greeted by a Hotel Manager that welcomed us to the Hotel & offered us a free glass of wine, which we thought was very nice. So immediately, our impression was very positive. After we spoke to the man at the front desk though, we were pretty turned off from staying there. We asked him about the rooms, and what they were like for what price etc. so that we could get an idea for our out of town guests. He was not very friendly, and very rudely told us that "he could not quote exact prices" and that we would just have to contact his "Marketing Manager" for further information. I told him that I was just trying to compare & contrast the different ammenities that they offer in comparison to other nearby hotels & he was just overall rude & was not willing to really explain anything or try to "sell" the hotel in any way. I then asked him if it would be a huge inconveniece to actuallly look at a regular room & a suite just to get an idea of what they were like. He actually rolled his eyes & said "let me see what I could do". After much hestitation , he finally offered us a key to a room to check out. He was just overall very rude & we decided on that first encounter to not stay or put our guests at that hotel ever. First impressions can really make a huge difference!

title: “Great experience with the hotel staff”
text: We stayed at the hotel for one night. The hotel is located close to the Capital, so it took us 10 minutes to walk there in the morning. The staff of the hotel is very nice and helpful. In particular, Dave Loiseau, is a very nice guy, great attitude and great help. He really cared to make our stay at the hotel as enjoyable as possible

title: “Pleasant stay and great breakfast buffet”
text: Right in the middle of New York's Time Square, this Double Tree by Hilton property provides all the amenities to make your stay in NYC very pleasant. Staff was friendly and accommodated all the needs of our family. Rooms a bit small to be consider "Suites" yet, comfortable enough for a family of three. The food quality and service in the Breakfast buffet was superb. Also, recently stayed in the Waldorf Astoria using same amount of Hilton Honors points and after this experience I will rather stay in this property. Parking was $35 (quite a deal for Midtown). Welcome cookies were not freshly baked as advertised, yet a nice welcome treat after arriving from a long trip.

title: “historic hotel with value”
text: I enjoyed the stay from the checkin to the checkout. Great service and I felt right at home. Thank you.

title: “Tiny room but convenient”
text: Far and away the least expensive room in midtown manhattan and clean, convenient and friendly. Front desk was accomodating free breakfast uncluded But the room is dorm sized and amenities minimal. Would stay here again.

title: “What a DUMP!”
text: First time to San Antonio so looking online for something reasonbly priced and close to the airport...my bad! Took forever to find and when I got in the room I was highly upset. The carpet was stained, window seat cushions stained, shower ran constantly, toilet seat was loose, and felt like something was crawling on me constantly! Guess I'll be going to get checked for bed bugs!!! Did I mention that the room smelled liked mildew...what a dump!

title: “The bed did me in...lol”
text: Checked in from long trip and the bed was amazing it was soft and I was a goner...My room was on the side of the freeway but didn't hear a thing very quiet location.

title: “very little rooms but super trendy place”
text: the reception is very classy and original, the design of the entire place is top, its very cool at night, they have a club disco bar, and the brakfist is fantastic

title: “great staff”
text: I travel frequently, I have find the concierge staff specially Ms Anya Orlanska as well as Ms Sarah to be exceptionally knowledgeable and helpful. Thank you all very much.

title: “A nice hotel. I will stay again”
text: I stay at the verona hote on april 2006. they have renovated put new carpets, beds and have painted the rooms. I think that this hotel is in a good condition no matter what other people say. I can say that front desk clerk is friendly and can help you with everything you need. the neighborgood is not that bad. I can say that it is a good hotel. I will saty again no matter what other people say.just because other people say is bad I thought that is better to see it for my self than believing other people.

title: “Good location, clean design”
text:
I booked the hotel based on location, price, and design. 
The location, close to subways, was prime. Since we traveled all over the city. Good breakfast options, though not great evening dining around the hotel. But thats not a negative for me. 
The queen room we had was large, the accessible room, we later learned. No view, but we pretty much only sleep in the room so not a factor.
It was located very close to the elevator. And we think thats what you get if you order the larger rooms. It was somewhat noisy but we weren't really bothered. Slow elevators. The design of the room was not really as good functionally as the look of it. But nothing really irksome. 
Good value - in very pricey new york. I would stay here again.

title: “A double booking hotel - truly dreadful”
text:
Arrived after a 24 hour journey for our first time in New York - 13:30 in the morning to witness an arguement between lobby staff and a group of American tourists who were told at 3pm their rooms weren't yet ready but when they returned after an evening out were told they had been double booked.
 The same happened to us - we had to wander to the Flathotel to in -13c temperatures where they had booked us in for the night to find they had room for 4 although our party was 5. Some of us then had to wander back to ask them to fund another room as Novotel did not answer their phone. We spent the night in a hotel we had not booked and had to wait to check in on the first morning of our short city break. The hotel and also the hotel manager promised that they would refund the first night of our trip but never did.
 When questioned the person at the desk advised that they did this as people cancelled and this happened regularly. It was a shame that they did not respond to my e-mail asking them to confirm that everything was ok the week previously - so they should have known that there was no need double book us.

title: “looks can deceive”
text: The entrance to this hotel can be easily missed and the tiny lobby area will give you the feeling that you have made a terrible mistake when you first check in.But do not despair as the actual rooms are quite large and are vrey clean. I admit that I might have been lucky with my room(1203) but I had a great view of the empire state building that was lit up all in green on St Patricks night.I found the staff most helpful at all times and was asked if I had any problems even if I found myself travelling in the elevator with a member of staff. The area leaves alot to be desired,especialy at night but I never felt threatened and the subway was only a few yards away on the next corner. I was never bothered by the daytime stall holders and in fact it gave the feeling that i was seeing part of the real new york. The only thing to fear from this hotel is the pounds you will put on,eating those wonderful doughnuts at breakfast. One more foot note,let the hotel book you a car when you return to the airport($45+toll+tip). It will save you a lot of money by not being stuck in a traffic jam on the freeway with the meter running in a taxi. You might even get a Cadilac like we did.

title: “Good hotel - has room to grow and will be great”
text:
I stayed at the Conrad hotel for five days on a recent business trip. The hotel is in a great location located near the Hudson river and only a few blocks away from the 9/11 memorial. There are several decent and not overly expensive restaurants nearby including a Whole Foods in case you feel like just grabbing a few grocery items. 
Pros - brand new suites with a lot of amenities, nice gym with nice assortment of equipment and refrigerated bottled water, friendly staff, and location near the Hudson River and walking distance to quite a number of sights. 
Cons - need more power outlets by the desk (had to share outlet with coffee maker) 
In all, this is a good hotel and I have no doubt it will be one of the best in the near future. It has plenty of space to add more hotel conveniences. 
For me - a business traveler - I liked the little things - free bottled water in my room stocked daily, newspaper by 6am at my door (key when you have to be out for an early meeting by 7), location making it easy to walk to the office, and lots of nearby restaurants to select from. Check out the Shake Shack if you get a chance. 
I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Service Staff”
text: I have never been more impressed with any other catering servers. Mentionably Estela Estrada. She was so kind, attentive and curtious. I was so surprised to find this kind of service at a sheraton.

title: “Nice room, great location”
text:
This Travelodge has absolutely the best location if you need to be close to someone who is in one of the three hospitals that are within walking distance. We stayed there for four days and had a clean room room with a comfortable bed. We had no problems with the neighborhood, although we were not walking around late at night. 
The front desk people were courteous and efficient. They were very helpful when we had to change our reservation. I would go back to this hotel again and would definitely recommend it to others.

title: “Great location, loved the historic atmosphere”
text:
The style and atmosphere in the Riverwalk Vista made for a great home base while visiting San Antonio. I loved the restored building which has a classic old-world feel, with wood floors, high ceilings, antique decoration, but modern conveniences too (the bathroom was totally new - our room had a great walk-in shower but no tub). The location was perfect to explore the Riverwalk area of San Antonio, across the street from steps to the middle of the Riverwalk and within easy walking distance of the Alamo and the Tower of the Americas. Breakfast was fresh and varied each day, with choices to suit a variety of appetites and preferences. 
I would caution other travelers that there are some things unique to this small hotel that not everyone might like. It is an older building in the very busy tourist area and San Antonio is a big, active city, so there is street noise. It didn't bother me or my travel companion, but might be more than a light sleeper would tolerate. This is a small hotel, with a small staff. The service is friendly and attentive, but there is not a front desk or a large specialized staff. The best parking is about a block away (no on-site parking available), figure about $12 - 15 daily. The parking deck is safe and well-lit and attended around the clock, but doesn't have in-and-out privileges (you will pay every time you leave, but you may find you mostly walk to your destinations anyhow). If these things matter to you, you probably should save yourself some unhappiness and stay somewhere else. If you are fairly easygoing and looking for a hotel with great character and an excellent location, I would expect you will be very pleased with a stay here.
Also worth noting is that there is wi-fi but it is about as slow as dial-up service. And, the available fitness center is a long, long walk away. (I checked out the distance and decided not to bother, so I can't evaluate the fitness center itself.)
In my opinion, the Riverwalk Vista is a great hotel, with atmosphere not to be missed. I would happily stay there again if ever again in San Antonio.

title: “Feels Like a 2nd Home”
text: I've been staying at this place for years. I am a Platinum Premier Marriott rewards member and can honestly say you can't expect to get much more than what they provide. The breakfast is more than what you get at a typcial Residence Inn and the social hour during the week can't be touched by other hotels. Believe me, I've had the "nacho's" (tortilla chips and cheese whiz) that most RI's say is their evening fare and they can't compete....this place provides full meals most days. The staff is fantastic and treat you like a friend and not just another face coming into the hotel! If you have a problem, they will go out of their way to fix it. The renovations look great and provide a fresh new look to the hotel along with nice upgrade to the TV's in each room.

title: “Very fun night”
text: Was staying here for a company party stayed overnight had a very pleasent eperience. Staff was more than accomidating to us. will stay here again for sure.

title: “Good enough”
text: No complaints. Staff was friendly and accommodating. Room was clean and adequately sized. We were on the 36th floor and had a nice view of the skyline. It's within a couple of blocks of Grand Central. There are lot's of cool restaurants in the area.

title: “BUENA UBICACION”
text: DESAFORTUNADAMENRE EL HOTEL NECESITA UNA REMODELACION URGENTE, LA HABITACION HUELE A CIGARRILLO, AUNQUE YO PEDI DE NO FUMADORES, LA ALFOMBRA JAMAS LA HAN ASPIRADO NI LAVADO, EL BAÑO ES BIEN ANTIGUO, EL PAPEL HIGINIECO ES DEL MAS BARATO, EL JABON Y TODOS LOS IMPLEMENTOS DE ASEO SON FATALES. EL PRECIO DE LA HABITACION ES MUY ALTO PARA TENER TAN MALA SU INFRAESTRUCTURA

title: “Good value”
text: Very clean, very decent free breakfast. Room had a refrigerator and microwave, very nice for the price. My only complaint is the parking. We chose this hotel because the parking was free (apparently a rare commodity in Seattle) but I have a minivan and the parking garage and parking spaces are extremely tiny and I had a great deal of difficulty using the garage.

title: “Extremely positive ending to overseas vacation.”
text:
My husband and I stayed 2 nights at this hotel after our vacation in Europe. The front desk were decent and the room was fine.
We then proceeded to the 'Managers Reception' which was disappointing because free drinks meant poorly made drinks.,although the bartender was sweet.
We asked a young waitress in the courtyard for a pepperoni pizza,an hour went by and no pizza,so we approached the waitress again (who had to pulled away from her cellphone)..only to be told we HAD NOT placed any such order with her.
The Bartender placed the order and made a gin martini for my husband that was warm and had far too much vermouth,and if she had bothered to ask,my husband has a fondest for bombay sapphire gin....we decided to take the pizza to go....
we then lose our bartender to a 20 minute "crude" spanish conversation with 2 other employees and a cook...we are caucasians who understand spanish! ...this was unpleasant.
I had ordered a chocolate martini ..it never came.
The next day after a long day sight seeing and waiting for friends to arrive from LAX...We decided to call room service and no one answered...so we are forced to venture back into the restaurant.
The phone is ringing of the hook...2 employees stand by the entrance telling us to sit anywhere....a new bartender is swamped with customers and asks for someone to answer the phone...she is frustrated and tells us she will be right back...
the gentleman beside me, informs us he is a regular and this bartenders drinks are worth the wait..and although we waited a while ...we couldnt help but feel for this poor girl...who was run off her feet.. while others stood around...her 'wish i was an octopuss comment had us all laughing'...
when we asked for a chocolate martini ...she offered me 4 different kinds..but insisted I try her ultimate chocolate martini..Which was so delicious I had 2!!..
My husbands gin martini was perfect..it was shaken so well it had shreds of ice forming on the top..and made with bombay sapphire.
Our party arrives and we proceed to a table where a wonderful waiter called Jack took great care of us and helped us forget the evening before.
The Rainbow trout was so good and our friends enjoyed the pasta dishes...the mahi mahi wasnt so enjoyable and the food took too long.
Also the bickering amongst the staff and lack of teamwork really lets this restaurant down.
Not ONCE did I ever see a manager and it seems that job is also left for the poor bartender to do.
Around 10pm that evening my husband informs me he has lost his wallet, full of credit card and cash as we had just cashed a travellers note that day..
we search the restaurant...then the room...we called the restaurant and the woman on the other end tells us to call a manager tomorrow.
By 11pm we are frantic...we call the restaurant one last time and the Bartender answers..she tells us she will look for it and call us back...
11.20 pm there is a knock on the door..it is the bartender holding our wallet. .we are amazed to find that not a dime is missing...
we are so moved by her honesty that my husband tries to give her 100 dollars...she thanks us ..but refuses to except the money,
I dont remember her name..shes a New Zealand girl and I wanted to share this experience with the hotel and other people like ourselves you value this kind of service .
and the best chocolate martini you will ever taste..
Thank you ...we will be back.,

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text: Our family had a wonderful time at the T & C. The service and accommodations are first class. The grounds are beautiful and vey clean. My wife is thankful for the short walk to the shopping center.

title: “Nice Hotel, Small Rooms”
text: Wonderful experience and amazing staff, only problem was the small rooms and limited amount of space to move around. Hotel itself was up kept and clean.

title: “Luxury, Courtesy and Friendliness in New York City”
text:
Having just returned from our recent stay (Jan.14-16), I want to thank everyone for the wonderful hospitality. It is always such a pleasure to be at the Intercontinental Barclay in New york. The Staff goes that extra yard to be friendly and accommodating. The Check-In
procedure which has always been very efficient, has improved even more. Moving the Ambassador Desk back to the Lobby is so much better. Ms. Annmara Gayle was terrific in expediting check-in and should be commended for her pleasantness, efficiency, and Friendliness. Ms. Mimi Dagot. is always effective in making guests feel welcome. All of the staff try to remember our name, which always makes a guest feel special.

title: “Sleek, modern hotel with lots of extras”
text: We stayed just one night at Cedarbrook Lodge and found it to be stylish and spacious. The common area in our block was an unexpected bonus with chocolates, water, ice-cream, potato chips and hot drinks complimentaty to all. The complimentary breakfast was also of a good standard. Service in the bar was a little slow, but overall would reccommend.

title: “Perfect Comfort”
text: I just checked out from the Mondrian Soho after an extended stay so I had a chance to really get a feel for this hotel. Realy great location tucked into a quiet street in Soho. Super, super staff - genuinely friendly, very professional, really helpful and nice. There was zero attitude at the Mondrian. They were there for you if you needed something - but not too over the top. Perfect balance. I had a great room over looking the city with a backdrop of the Hudson - very clean. The gym is compact and offers everything for a full workout. The restaurant has a beautiful atrium - and on Saturday afternoons offers live music. Great Saturday lunch spot. Love the breakfast and lunch menu. I completely would recommend the Mondrian Soho to friends and business associates coming to NYC. I travel extensively around the States and OUS - I now would look for a Mondrian property first. Thanks for a super stay.

title: “Happy holidays with the family”
text: Stayed here with our kids as well as my brother and sister and their kids: 14 people and 4 rooms overall. Our visit was on the weekend before Christmas. The purpose was simply to have a family get together and get some shopping done on the magnificent mile. There is probably no location better in Chicago for access to the M.M. Nordstroms and the rest of the downtown mall is right across the street. That and the layout of the lobby, with it's large open bar and other common seating areas distinguished the downtown Marriott from most other large city hotels we've stayed at. It made socializing in large groups easier and the older kids could come and go as they pleased while the adults relaxed with a beverage. There were several large screen TV's and although this wasn't a sports bar it made it easy to watch the NFL game that captured the attention of many of the patrons. The rooms were small and non-descript. While the pool area was fairly large and accomadating, the pool itself was small. There was a good-sized workout room with lockers and showers available as well. We also received a rate of 129.00 which was a terrific value compared to their normal rates. All in all it was a great experience made better with the large, welcoming lobby, bar and access to all the best Chicago has to offer.

title: “Great Location”
text: This property was clean, friendly, convenient. The staff was polite and helpful. The only problem I had was there were no filters for the coffee pot. The nearby restaurant (Tin Tin) was recommended by the office and it was amazing, so many choices for a good price. This was the first time I stayed at a Suburban Extended Stay and it will not be the last, great value for the money.

title: “Old Style Charm, but Too Old”
text: What a great place and location, but the rooms are too dated to be considered a good deal for the price. There are better options. Sad for the Drake once held the premier place, but now it is just a storied hotel below the others in the area. The attitude of the front end staff was far below 5 star standards. The porters and bell men were excellent and funny.

title: “Excellent for overnight business”
text: Centrally located, very reasonably priced (by my standards at least), and well kept, this was ideal for an overnight business trip. Friendly staff. Good in-house restaurant (tad pricey for breakfast). Have recommended it to friends. Would stay again. Nice views from upper floors.

title: “WOW is all I can say about this Red Roof Inn”
text: This was one of the nicest PROPERTIES I have satyed in. Not as a Red Roof Inn, but ever! If this property were set in another location, it could be a Marriott. Fantastic rooms, very spacious (I was there for a month) and never felt closed in. Convenient to everything (abundance of restaurants within walking distance) and no need to spend cash on breakfast with an AMPLE continental breakfast and 24hr coffee. JJ and the rest of the staff were always there to lend a hand with directions, etc. An all arounf great location for a great cost. Why stay across the street for $100 more per night?

title: “Great family stay at Fairmont”
text: We got a very special price for this hotel, which is why we ended up staying there. We would simply not be looking for a + 500 USD/night for a family vacation. What a pleasant surprise. We absolutely enjoyed every bit of it. The professionalism of the front desk was fantastic and all the staff was exceedingly friendly. The location was great for touring around DC - we have a 7 and 9 year old and went everywhere with the Metro, which as only a few blocks away. Everything was very clean, the fitness facilities and pool were perfect for our family, and the overall surroundings and atmosphere were sophisticated (but not overly so).

title: “Great hotel and perfect for MICA visit”
text:
Was very impressed with this hotel. The 9th floor room we had overlooked the square which was beautifully lit for Christmas. The room was very large with two comfortable double beds. Furnishings were very nice and tasteful - beautiful wood headboards, an antique nightstand, armoire for the TV and a desk. Did not feel like a hotel room - more like you were a guest in very nice house. There were nice architectural features - tall baseboards, large crown mouldings and very deep window sills. Beautiful bathroom with marble tiles on floor and full walls, heated towel rack, wall-mounted extension mirror, and jetted tub. The "dresser" consisted of built-in drawers behind closet doors with a very large mirror and light above - very nice. Another "closet" had a mini-fridge, etc. And a third "closet" was an actual closet. A very pleasant room.
If I were to be picky, I would say housekeeping was not meticulous. While the bathroom was very, very clean and the main surfaces in the room were clean, the tops of the headboards and baseboards could have used a dusting, and the vacuuming of the carpet missed the edges near the baseboards. But this certainly wasn't an issue for our one night stay.
Also, parking could be difficult. There is very limited space to pull up and use their valet service - just an area where the sidewalk cuts in that can maybe hold 2 cars. When we arrived after 11pm on a Saturday night, that space was full and more cars were parked next to them in the street. We were able to park in the Walters Art Museum lot just a few buildings away since the museum was closed and we left early the next morning before it opened. So it turned out to be a lucky break that we couldn't get to use the (expensive) valet parking service.
The restaurant was beautiful and the waitress very pleasant. Not impressed with the breakfast food.
Location is great for a visit to MICA and the hotel has special rates for MICA visitors.

title: “Gloomy common areas, but good rooms”
text: I am surprised to see so many rave reviews here because although service is good and the rooms are high quality, the hotel lacks any character or flare and during a 12 day stay that was something I really noticed. The lobby is gloomy, the business centre is in a room as big as a cupboard. The bar is out of the way and uninviting. The lobby is also full of ovepowering piped music although this does seem to be acceptable to most. On the upside, the rooms are modern and comfortable and well equiped - ipod dock for example. The service is exemplary. If you're looking for an efficient, could be anywhere on the planet, business hotel then this is fine. I'm less surprised that the people at head office in Seattle say no-one plumps for the Hyatt on their second visit - but they head off for something with more character

title: “Nice business hotel”
text:
in at 4 PM and was given an upgrade to a king room on one of the towers/executive floors. The lobby is very small and in my opinion, uninviting. There are no areas to chat. There is just bascially the front desk and concierge stand. Front desk staff and bellman were very curteous and helpful. parked my car in the adjoining ramp ... self-parking is $16/day and valet is $20/day. The concierge greated me with a big smile when I arrived in the lobby and asked if I needed any help. The service at the front desk seemed somewhat dry and uninterested. If you stay on one of the towers floors, you get a choice of beverage delivered to your room in the AM along with your choice of newspaper.
I was very happy to find that I was given a corner room. I'm glad I got this room because even for a corner room, I felt the room was small. I can only imagine what the other rooms are like. Ask for rooms that end in XX12 as these are the largest rooms on the floor according to the floor layout on the door. The bed was very comfortable and contained Hilton's new Serta bedding package. There was a robe and upgraded products in the bathroom. Wired and wireless high-speed internet are available in the room .. it is complimetary if you are staying on one of the exec floors. In order to use the wireless net, you need to call down to the front desk and receive an access code. I found the wireless net to be very slow and drop numerous connections. For best reception, you need to use your computer towards the center of the room. I also tried using the wired high-speed net, however the connection was not working. Since I didn't need to use the net an extensive amount, I decided not to call the front desk.
I felt the exec lounge was ok. Evening hou'douvers (served from 5-8) consisted of teriyaki steak strips and various cheeses and crackers. There are also plenty of complimentary soft-drinks to select from. When I was there on a weekend, the bar was manged by the concierge. Alcoholic drinks are charged to the room. There is a few nice leather couches and some tables, but overall the lounge is not big by any means. There is also a good selection of magazines and CDs (the exec rooms have the Hilton alarm clocks with CD players). The late night offerings (8-11) consisted of fruits and cookies. I checked out early the next day, and did not have a chance to go to the lounge for breakfast. I must agree with a previous poster who stated that this lounge seemed lackluster compared to other lounges.
I ordered room service that night and found the food to be very excellent. 24 hour room service is available. I also heard the sunday brunch in the restaurant is one of the top brunches in the Charlotte area.
The hotel is connected to small plaza which contains small shops and a gift shop. I did not have time to explore this area, so I'm not sure exactly what types of stores were there.
A few other words of advice .. when checking in, I was not asked if I parked my own car, so I needed to go down to the desk later that night and receive a parking permit. My room did have a mini-bar, however I was not given the key and needed to stop at the front desk for this as well. I was told that the hotel is removing the mini-bars from all the rooms due to discrepencies in billing. Only a few rooms still had them. They are probably not necessary if you have access to the lounge. Also, turndown service is available on the exec floors. However, you need to call the front desk and request this service. I was not told this upon checking in. I didn't realize this until it was too late in the evening.
Would I stay here again .. probably. The weekend rates are great (I payed $89 dollars for my upgraded room). However, I felt the service and quality of the rooms were must better at the HGI and for what you get for what you pay for during the week, you'd probably be getting a better deal at the HGI.

title: “Christmas Escape”
text: My partner and I traveled to Dallas with 2 small dogs and were joined by two other friends for a Christmas escape at the Mansion. Accommodations, service, food and beverage could not have been better. When traveling with pets, request a "patio room" on the first floor. The guest room opens onto a private walled and landscaped patio with a bistro table and 2 chairs. The hotel staff is without peer.

title: “Fabulous!”
text: Beautiful, spotless, roomy! This hotel is 1/2 block from Times Square. Close to the subway. Some reviews I read complained about the noise from a construction elevator outside. It never woke me or my son up. There were earplugs in the room just in case. Everything about this hotel exceeded my expectations!

title: “Excellent Facility Outweighed by Substandard Staff & Services”
text: I have stayed in this facility at least twice over the past six years; once for three days and once for five. As a native Washingtonian, it is always pleasant to go back home. And the physical plant is quite welcoming. Each time I have arrived the check-in has seemingly gone very smoothly with a keycard in my hand within five minutes. On one trip I was traveling for a tax-exempt governmental subdivision. I explained that they were paying for the room, that they could put my personal expenses on my personal credit card, and be sure not to charge my employer any tax. When I went on the in-house computer system the next morning there were the inappropriate taxes. My home office had to call to straighten them out as they would not listen to me. And then there was the room service. A meal which added up to $22 on the room service menu ended up costing me $55. The same two-for-one charge was true of my other meal as well. The housekeeping, room service and door staff were excellent which facilitated one trip after suffering a shattered kneecap. Uncharacteristically, it was the front office and accounting staff which made my trips a chore rather than a deligtht.

title: “Great location in downtown Houston”
text: Went to the DoubleTree for an overnight stay for dinner and a play rather than making the drive back to the suburbs. The location is great and the room was nice. We stayed in a corner king on the 14th floor facing Dallas street and it was worth the extra cost to upgrade to the corner room. We visited the bar after the play and enjoyed that as well. I would also suggest the breakfast buffet in the hotel restaurant. The staff is very friendly and everyone has customer service in mind. The bed was comfy. The only downside is that the decor is a little dated. We will definitely stay there again.

title: “Overpriced, everything is extra..Go somewhere else.”
text:
In a nutshell, stay somewhere else. 
For $130 a night, does NOT include:
Parking: $15 extra
Internet: $10 extra
No breakfast: Continental Breakfast cost $18.95 plus tax
No vending machines in the building. If you want a 12 oz coke can, prepare to pay $3.25
No Hair dryers in rooms.
Awful, staticey TV's, no HD barley a signal. 
Rooms are well decorated, but for the money you can get something better for a lot less. I will not be staying at an Omni again. It is obvious they are here to gouge their customers and not concerned with providing the best customer experience.

title: “Very nice with a couple of "buts"”
text: Super convenient location for Central Park, major shopping, the subway, eating out and Broadway. Nice attentive staff and beautifully styled inside. The couple of "buts" are that our room was smaller than we had imagined and as shown in most photos we had found, just enough room to move around the bed, and that the bath itself was very small. We suspect this is because we had a cheaper room as we booked through Expedia and got a great price. The bed was lovely and was, as advertised, a "Heavenly Bed" and the shower was good. But the rest was OK, not fantastic but certainly not poor. We had Christmas Lunch in the hotel's Cafe Botanica and. although pricey, it was excellent. So overall I would recommend the Essex House on location alone but pay the extra for a bigger room if you really want something special rather than average.

title: “Good value”
text: We stayed at the hotel on Wednesday and Thursday nights last week. We arrived before noon and were able to check in early. The staff was helpful and courteous throughout our visit. Heater noise could be a major issue during middle of winter. Door sound proofing could be better. Room size and amenities were very good. Location is great, particularly if you know your way around the city. Good value--we'll stay there again.

title: “Hilton Westchase - in desperate need of a refit”
text:
It looks good from the outside only. The entire hotel internals are looking dated and faded. The entire décor is old , the carpets and fittings are worn , the lifts are barely working. On the seventh floor the buttons are wired backwards. Down for up, up for down. The only part that was really half decent was the Rio Rancho , and this is also looking a bit second hand. Security was an issue with anyone able to walk in the back entrance and go to any floor. I had a homeless person dosing down in my corridor. 
The staff were good and attentive and the cleaners did their best with what they have . Come on Hilton , invest some money and bring this Hotels infrastructure back up to a reasonable standard.

title: “Excellent Hotel, Service and Location”
text:
I have traveled all over the world and I keep coming back to this Hilton Garden Inn (HGI). This property understands customer service and provides exceptional customer service in all areas of the hotel. I have been coming to Washington and specifically returning to this property because of the experience that I have had each and every visit. The staff bend over backwards to provide for any of your needs. The frontdesk staff are courteous, helpful and very personable. The restaurant provides excellent food and drink in a relaxing atmosphere. The rooms are very clean and very comfortable and the hotel, despite its size and location is quiet. The metro in just across the street.
Recently, I was unable to book this property for an upcoming trip. The General Manager personally arranged for me to get a reservation at this wonderful hotel. There are many options for accomodations in Washington, DC but I will continue to select this property for my business and leisure travel. I highly recomment this hotel for outstanding customer service.

title: “great value, spacious room”
text:
Moving to Asia from Missouri with our two small children. We broke up the trip with an overnight in LA before embarking on the long flight. I was glad we stayed here, as this met all our needs. With AAA booking directly on their site is a great value.
Had a room with two queen beds. Clean. The room was bigger than many we've stayed in - even had a couch, which was perfect for last minute Skype calls and re-arranging luggage. Internet worked really well and was free. 
Breakfast was standard Super 8, basic cereals and muffins with beverages. Seating area was open all the time as it's part of the check-in area. This was great for us, as I have food sensitivities. This allowed me to fix my own dinner/lunch with the microwave. The rest of the family ordered food from a restaurant that delivered, which was very convenient. 
We made use of their coin laundry. We enjoyed the courtyard/parking lot area which felt very safe and allowed our kids to run off some steam. 
At the airport, the station where you are supposed to be able to call the hotels for shuttle service was out of order (this is not the hotel's fault). We had Super 8's phone number, so we called with our cell phone. It should be noted that a phone call needs to be placed in order to get the shuttle service. We waited about 15 minutes after placing our call, and the shuttle had plenty of room for our massive amount of luggage. Returned to airport the next day by shuttle that left on the hour. The drivers were very helpful and friendly and helped us with all the bags. Shuttles are free + tip for driver's help with luggage.
Only potential drawback is that if you are a sensitive sleeper, the planes are pretty loud. We were exhausted so it didn't bother us a bit. We couldn't hear anything from the neighboring rooms or outside, other than the planes. Perhaps ear plugs would do the trick. :) Also, at one time hot water ran out fairly quickly. About one hour later it was back in full force.

title: “Wouldn't recommend it to anyone”
text:
I thought this hotel was awful. On the evening my colleage and I checked in, a gentleman at the desk was reporting that the room he had been assigned to already had someone in it. Red flag #1. 
After checking into our own rooms, I found that the heat in my room didn't work and there was someone else's hair in the tub. I ordered room service only to find that there was a hair on the tray and no spoon for me to eat my soup with. There was also a hair on one of the washcloths and I don't want to get into what kind of hair it was. 
My colleage found that her room contained a half eaten box of Oreos, 4 diet cokes, several bottles of water that were of varying brands. One of the bottles of water was half empty. When she showered the next morning, she found that one of the towels had been hung up wet. We're still not sure whether someone was just showering in her room before she arrived or whether they never let the towels dry after being washed. 
We reported these problems to the front desk. I'm not sure if it was because we were "nice" about complaining or what, but there were no offers to give us a free night or anything else. As a matter of fact, there wasn't really an apology. I believe the front desk supervisor just said, "Oh, that's the not way its supposed to be." 
Needless to say, I'm disappointed. I was also rather disgusted. If those are the things we could see, what kinds of things were not visible? Anyway, we switched to another hotel after the second night of madness (i.e. the hair was never taken out of the tub and the heating was fixed, but cranked to 85 so my room felt like a sauna). Never again.

title: “Cookie Cutter Service at Personalized Prices”
text: Checked in the night of the Chinese New Year Parade and we couldn't use the front enterance or the garage. Needed to park a few blocks away. Spoke theh the front desk personnel about having to drive around for an hour in traffic and he totally blew me off. As a Platinum member he should have been at least a little understanding. Since they send me a form letter two days prior to arrival, they should have included notice that there would be issues related to the parade. They also did not post anything on their website. I wrote to management on Tuesday and received another form letter on Wednesday letting me know that trusted my stay went well. I forwarded this to management and still have not heard anything from them a 5 days later. If they want to view themselves as a high end hotel, they need to have more customized service, especially to Platinum members. As far as the hotel, it is nice but old. Doors sqweek, elevators are small, etc.

title: “Will be 5 stars once construction next door is finished!”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay at The Muse, except for the construction noise next door. We were awakened every morning at 7:00 am by the loudest sounds you can imagine! One of the days we were there if sounded like they were hurling rocks at our windows! I thought our windows were open, it was that loud! The Muse does offer earplugs and they do help. We were there in March of 2012. A Hyatt is being built behind The Muse, so check to see if it is completed when you make your decision, unless you can stand wearing earplugs to bed or are an early riser.
The staff was very friendly and extremely helpful in offering directions or suggestions. This hotel is about a half block away from Times Square, so we didn't have massive crowds or noise to contend with from that craziness! Our room was very clean and the size of a normal hotel room you would find in any other city. Bathroom was larger than normal and offered lots of counter space. Beds and pillows were very comfortable and clean.
Wifi is free if you sign up to be a Kimpton member, which is also free and offers a few perks; including $15.00 worth of free snacks from the room's snack area. We didn't realize that until we checked out. Would have gotten into those M&M's had we known they were free!! :) We did partake in the free coffee in the lobby each morning. They offered a coffeepot in our room if we wanted it.

title: “Great location”
text:
A typical business hotel that works both for pleasure and business. Staff were friendly and helpful, but we did not notice them except at check in and check out. We were upgraded to a suite which had views of the Bay Bridge. The room was equipped with a king-size bed, an office and a living room and a large bathroom.
The hotel offers easy access around the city, we soon discovered that it was very close to everything and that's why the hotel gets four points. If you want a more luxurious hotel and more attentive service, you should stay elsewhere. That said, the location is very good, close to Chinatown, close to cafes with free wifi, close to the Ferry Building and Fisherman's Wharf, Telegraph Hill and the train around the corner takes you easily around town.

title: “discriminatory and snobby”
text: Our stay was awful. Just because we were a young, non white couple the workers there were giving us dirty looks and treating us as though we did not deserve to be in the "establishment". I know that is what it was, because there was another young couple who did not look like us and they were treated with the utmost respect. it was our first wedding anniversary, and we wasted time and money here. My husband tried out the wine hour and everyone there was gawking at him as though it was a bad joke. We got facials and massages and though our actual facialist was great, everyone else had the worst attitude ever! When we checked out, they RAN to get our keys as though they couldn't wait for us to leave, and still had us waiting for our car. The front desk was rude and unaccomodating. We had a suite, and though our room was great, this hotel can still go straight to hell! If you aren't what "normally" would patronize a "high class" hotel, don't go here! We definitely will not ever again!

title: “Better than adequate”
text:
The Holiday Inn Express New York City 5th AVE was perfect for our purposes... which did not include frills. The location is great, room was clean (although small like any other Manhattan room), and continental breakfast, free local calls, and in-room water bottles and snacks came in much handy.
My only complaint is that I requested an early check-in knowing I'd be there at 8am and they had no record of it. Even after getting there at 8am it didn't seem as though any accomodations were made for me, and I didn't actually check-in until 4... which was a pain.

title: “Great Location, Bad Service”
text: Recently stayed at this hotel for a few days during a business trip. This hotel was in an excellent location and very convenient to the convention center. The room was very comfortable and had a great view of the pool. I am not one to complain at a hotel however the toilet in my room leaked around the bottom (not too bad but enough that i needed to keep a towel around it). When the maintenance staff came up to look at it they determined it would need to be replaced and they may need to change my room. The desk called and said they could either change my room or i could stay there and they'd give me a $50 credit and they would schedule a time to fix it. They were supposed to fix it the first day I would be out of the room (I was staying for 4 days). They did not come to fix it at all during my entire stay! Then when I checked out I had to ask that my $50 credit be applied to my room. There was also a lot of loud banging in the walls during the morning hours that was quite loud. And when I asked about complaining the woman at the desk did not have a manager to direct me to she just said "I don't know what to tell you." Next trip to Denver I'll hopefully stay somewhere else!

title: “Wonderful Funky Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the W in San Francisco for one night during a business trip and really enjoyed the hotel. This was my first stay at a W property and it definitely had a younger and hipper feel than other Starwood hotels. The hotel staff was very friendly and the hotel and room seemed very clean overall.
My room was stylishly, yet comfortably decorated. It had a nice king size bed, large desk area, flat screen tv, closet, and window seat with bridge view. The room was a nice size, but not huge. They made the most of the room size by adding a built in desk with tv hanging over top. The room's window seat was a unique touch. The room, like the hotel overall, had funky and hip decor touches like a glowing color changing Buddha lamp, kaleidoscope, alarm clock radio with ipod dock.
