The bathroom was clean and a good size and had some trendy decor as well. However, the bathroom door was made of a frosted glass which was slightly see-through and didn't have a lock. This was fine for me since I was traveling alone, but may be inconvenient to people traveling with friends or kids .
I liked this hotel much better than the Westin St. Francis (another Starwood property in San Francisco). The St. Francis caters to a much older crowd than the W. Overall, I really enjoyed the W hotel and liked the funky decor. I would recommend this hotel to business, couples, and younger (or young at heart) travelers.

title: “AAMC conference”
text: I have nothing to add - it was a great stay/value for the price I paid - only frustration was that internet kept logging me out.

title: “It was possibly the best stay I've ever had!”
text: This hotel was comfortable, staff was incredibly accommodating and friendly!! The staff held doors, cleaning staff made the room look like it did when we first checked in. There was always someone to greet you when you come in the door. They always have the "can-do" attitude in making sure that each customer felt comfortable and at home. The concierge service was polite and always ready to assist with transportation. Rooms were spacious and comfortable. The bathrooms were very spacious as well. The front desk clerks were pleasant and had a wealth of information as to the local places to eat, local stores, and sight-seeing opportunities. While I was on a business trip, I felt comfortable and cared for and never had to complain about any amenities, services, etc., the entire stay. I give this hotel 5 stars!!

title: “Loved it and will be back!”
text: Great hotel in great location. I loved the arty ambience of the lobby, with art works and installations peppering the space. The room with it's modern, clean decor was spacious and pleasant. The restaurant, David Burke's Primehouse, was another wonderful experience with innovative and interesting dishes that we have tried at the lobby bar and for breakfast.

title: “Excellent location - clean and tidy”
text:
This was our first visit to San Francisco and our stay at the Chancellor was arranged via Trailfinders as part of a driving tour. Things did not start well. Arriving in San Francisco at 5pm is not a good idea, especially for someone unfamiliar with the area. Having done several tours of the block trying to find somewhere to park and unload, eventually one of our party went into the hotel for ‘guidance’ as our tour of the blocks continued. Should have done that sooner! The Bell Captain came out and sorted us out, showing us where we could park and unload and helping us to unload.
Check-in was efficient, if somewhat ‘sterile’ and a smile or two would not have gone amiss, perhaps it had been a long day, especially as the hotel seemed very busy with the Oracle conference being in town. They explained the options for car parking as, like most city hotels, they have no attached car park. We chose the $22/day self parking option, which was a multi-storey a couple of blocks away, we just drove there and the attendants did the rest. As it turned out, this was a good option as ‘public’ car parking was more expensive and this allows as many in and outs as you like, although the public transport is so good and cheap, we just left the car in the ‘lot’ during our stay.
The hotel itself is a (relatively) old building, built in the early 1900s so is classed as ‘historical’ and the decoration and style reflect this. Our room was on the 9th floor, not much of a view but then we don’t expect that in any city hotel. By US standards the room was small, but very clean and tidy and well decorated. We were a bit concerned about there being no air conditioning as it was a warm day and opening the window allowed in all the San Francisco noise – however it turned out to be part of the charm listening to the ‘ting ting’ of the street cars, the general hub hub of city life and of course the wailing sirens of police cars in the distance ! There was a ceiling fan which we couldn’t get to work – at the end of the day this was down to ‘user error’ by me. You are even offered a ‘pillow menu’ here to choose from a range of pillow types but the ones supplied as ‘standard’ were more than adequate to complement the large, comfortable bed. Despite the local noise (with the window being open) we had no problem sleeping and it was lovely to wake up to the sound of the street cars going by. Although no coffee/tea making facilities were in the room, coffee was available in the lobby and again it would seem that most city hotels do not provide these room facilities.
The strong point of this hotel is its location. Plenty of shops, diners and restaurants in the immediate locality and a two minute walk to the cable car stop – which you just have to do ! We chose to eat out and had breakfast at Lori’s Diner a couple of blocks away – highly recommended, we even had the two ‘cops’ on the next table enjoying their pancakes – just like TV! We had an evening meal at a nearby baseball themed ‘carvery’ which was excellent value for money. As we already had a trip to Alcatraz booked (a not to be missed trip!) and with only one full day available, we tried to cram as much in as possible so we spoke to Susan the hotel concierge who was very helpful. She sorted us out with day passes for the public transport and booked us a three hour bus sightseeing trip of the city. We chose to use the streetcar down to Pier 39 area and benefited from a commentary by the very friendly ‘brakeman’ at the back of the car, pointing out local sites and interests. Both the Alcatraz and bus trip were very good, certainly whetting the appetite for a return visit and a longer stay at the Chancellor.
So all in all, a very pleasant stay at the Chancellor and we would have no hesitation in staying there again. As a footnote, I left my glasses in the hotel room, only realising later as we were on our way to Yosemite. After contacting the hotel on my return, Wes (the manager) posted these back to me at the hotel’s cost – now that’s service !

title: “Very nice Art Deco hotel..”
text: We arrived here after a long trip around the US and to be honest I would have rather been on the plane going home... However, once I walked through the doors of this hotel, I was perked up. The decor and the ambiance hark back to a time prohibition and and Al Capone, the bell hops looked as if they had been taken off the set of Some Like It Hot and somewhere behind the reception desk lurked Marilyn Monroe... It was bang on. The rooms are small, even for New York standards, the walls are paper thin, so expect to hear your neighbors (and we heard some interesting conversations) and facilities in the rooms are basic, windows open slightly, the air conditioning needs some work... Yet, it all works... (at least for me). We didn't stay in the room much, we were out an about shopping for much of our week long stay on this occasion, so the location is PERFECT! Close to Time Square and Grand Central station and the shops on Madison. Its a real gem if you want a little piece of history and want to be close to all the major attractions at a very reasonable price. I would deffinitley stay there again as a couple... perhaps not as a family.

title: “I give the staff 5 stars”
text: I arrived there and was greated by a very wonderful lady who happened to be the manager, Josephine. She was very helpful with everything. My room was nice and clean and there were alot of great places to eat close by. I will definately be back when Im in town again.

title: “AWFUL - NOT recommended”
text: Completely overpriced ! Hotel was overbooked when we arrived ! Receptionist was extremly unfriendly and no one apologised for the mistake. We got given a Smoking room whereas we specially requested a non smoking. The smell in the room was horrible !!! Room was dark and not that spacious ! Nothing like this would be expected for a $500/night hotel.

title: “Pretty Bad”
text:
Once again I went with an American Express "Fine Hotel" - and once again dissapointed.
Firstly, I believe I read their website, and about how they're all about the linens and beds... I don't know if I've slept on such a horrible, hard, uncomfortable bed! I don't have exceptionally high standards when it comes to beds, but this was just rock hard.
The room was OK, stained carpet, torn furniture, etc. It was clean, and it had everything you needed, so if you don't mind those little things, then no big deal.
We were on the 37th floor, and the traffic was still quite loud. If it bothers you, I'd request a higher floor. The 37th Floor was not quite high enough to avoid the flashy billboards (er, video screens) from Times Sq.
As to Location, fantastic. You're right there, in the middle of it all, and I'd recommend it for young couples/singles, but I wouldn't recommend it for families.
Check-in/reception is actually on Level 7 - You take the elevators up to Level 7 (every time), and from there you take your designated elevator to your floor.
Food was good, but certainly not worth the expense, and well, you're in NYC - get out there and hit one of the many, MANY fabulous restaurants.
I would recommend any of my single friends to stay, but I've actually stayed at The Time, a couple of years ago, and I would recommend that first. It's also in the mix (just off Times Sq), and is quiet, well appointed, and friendly.
Speaking with Concierge, and Reception is extremely difficult as afternoon turns to evening. They're right in-front of the bar, in an wide-open hard-walled area. I found it rather unpleasant coming back from a full day in the city, and having all that noise to deal with in the 'lobby' of my hotel.
My final thoughts - too expensive for what you get, unless you have money to burn, I'm sure there are better options (including The Time).

title: “Excellent Service, Great Location, Good Rates, Free Breakfast...”
text: We stayed for 3 nights. The rooms were clean and spacious, nice beds and bedding. Customer service was top notch! Included free hot breakfast. Location is perfect for the downtown loop, with-in walking distance of many venues. Centrally located near blue line and redline subway for easy access. Con - No pool...

title: “Laughably Pathetic”
text:
This place would be better off calling itself the "WTF?" instead of the "W".
First off, I've never spent so much money to be treated as horribly as I was this week. The thing that stuck in my mind through most of the trip here was the fact that I never felt welcome, at all. 
When my vacation here began, the lady who checked me in was Marisol. She was reliable and smart and I enjoyed when she helped me. 
The deposit, was 500 dollars which is way more than any other hotel I've been to in LA. 
Wheels, is HORRIBLE! Do not park here at the W, if you can help it. LAZ parking owns wheels, and all of their employees are disrespectful and unwashed. They will leave your car smelling like a hollywood hippie. Charge you for leaving your car overnight, even if you never parked it there overnight. Seriously, a truly unprofessional company, that is not owned by the W, and why they would have such riff raff, trash the nice people's personal property is beyond me.
They act like they have a monopoly, becasue they basically do. I was overcharged, again and again by these ridiculous fools. Definitely put a sour taste in my mouth for the whole trip. No one in the Hotel takes any responsibility, they will only tell you, "our valet service, isn't part of our company"
When we checked out, they actually made us wait over an hour to have someone go and "inspect" our room?
Seriously?
Places infinitely better, don't act this ridiculous. 
So aside from being a complete waste of money, I was also called a very nasty derogatory comment, by one of the Wheels employees who thought that he could argue my rationality by telling me something so rude, that it caused me to basically start shouting uncontrollably. 
I was over charged over 150 dollars, and I never parked my car there for more than a few hours. 
I think if Marisol, had been around, I would gotten all of my charges reversed. But I unfortunately had the ill-pleasure of Maureen, being my receptionist. This front desk personal, is another winner. It seems that they have the absolute most terrible employees, working during checkout. Maureen, not only took from 12:30 to past 1:30 just to check us out. She didn't help us reverse any overcharged the hotel made... like charging us for a phone call to the hotels reservation desk. (another 2 bucks) Easy stuff like that was beyond here reach. 
I swear it looks like they take all of the unemployed morons in hollywood, that can't seem to competently make it in the entertainment industry and turn them loose on the "more successful" entertainers for the horror of their own benefit. 
When you get a room here, you are not guaranteed any sort of passes for entrance into Drai's.
Drai's isn't more than just a pool, during the day. 
They were remodeling, and the place was a mess. The pool was open, but there was a film on top of the water from the construction. Nothing I like more than having my nephews swim in a swirl of muck. 
I love staying in hotels in Hollywood. But this is the easily the worst experience I've ever had staying in this part of California. Stay away from here and keep yourself very happy by staying somewhere you can get your money's worth, which for sure... isnt here.

title: “great hotel”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel twice previously. Check in was quick and easy. We had a double double room on the 11th floor. Our room was front facing and was quite a bit louder than the rooms ive had previously which were both backwards facing. The school opposite the hotel created quite a bit of noise, however not unbearable noise.
This room was definately dated, the safe was broken and i could only open it by sticking my little finger into a small hole and dragging the door open. The radiator leaked and made the carpet a little damp. These were both bearable problems and didnt bother me, but did bother my partner slightly. 
On our second morning the toilet blocked so we went down to the reception to make them aware of the problems, the lady was very helpful and explained she didnt have a double double available until that evening so we could pack out stuff and put it in storage and then check into the new room later that day. When we explained we didnt need a double double and had only booked one as it had been cheaper on the internet than a king size, she gave us a king room on the 14th floor straight away. 
We promptly went and threw our belongings in our suitcases and moved rooms. The second room was excellent, the best bed i have ever slept in (i looked forward to going to bed just so i could lay in it) the room was still the same size and was backwards facing so the noise was reduced. We had no further problems and really enjoyed the central location of this hotel.
The staff were all friendly and helpful, conceige booked us a town car for our return to the airport. We were very pleased and would not hesitate staying here again.

title: “A quiet spot in Times Square does exist - check in here!”
text:
This Marriott Courtyard pleasntly surprised me. I have stayed there twice now and wish I had stayed there more often when visiting NYC. My office is located in the heart of Times Square so there are several hotel choices for me but most are very expensive. The rooms are updated, clean, and although small, they don't feel too cramped. The bed was comfortable and I could not hear any street noise even when I stayed on a lower floor. This hotel is tucked quietly away on a side street (40th Avenue) just steps from the hustle and bustle of Times Square, and is clean, service-oriented and a great expeience overall. As a solo female business traveler, I also feel safe here when returning later in the evening. 
When staying in/near Times Square, make sure to check out this hotel for a convenient, yet quieter experience. You will not be disappointed.

title: “Great hotel in an awesome neighborhood”
text:
When my friend and I were researching hotels for our 4 night stay in NYC, price and location were key. Not only is this hotel reasonably priced, it was in a great location close to many cafes and restaurants. It was also very close to the subway stops.
Although the bathroom was tiny, the rooms were very clean and the beds very firm and comfortable. The temps outside were frigid cold, so our first night there we were freezing. The baseboard heaters weren't working properly so we called downstairs and within a few minutes they brought us up an electric heater. The staff were very friendly and helpful....even when we had drunken neighbors with loud music on at 6am. One call downstairs and within 10 minutes they were quiet as a mouse.
We definitely recommend this hotel and would stay again.

title: “Weekend stay at Biltmore”
text: Wonderful hotel with courteous staff. Place is full of history and you enjoy amazing archtechture and history, this place is for you. The food was great, the grounds and pool were spectacular as well. Also, they have a limo service that is very reasonable to/from the airport. In fact, I left my laptop in the limo and hours later was able to retrieve it. Don't think that would have happened if I took a taxi.

title: “Decent Stay”
text:
We chose this hotel because of the location and the size of the rooms (being a family of 4 plus a friend, this fit the bill when we booked). It is convenient to get to all the major attractions, Sea World, the Zoo, etc. When we first checked in, we didn't realize the 2 bedroom suite was going to be so small - plus, the bathroom was in the main bedroom which was not a good thing for us. The 2nd bedroom also only had bunk beds. I wish they would have let us know that the bathroom is in the master bedroom as I would not have booked that room to begin with. Upon calling the front desk, they moved us to another 2 bedroom suite, with 2 bathrooms this time - of course for an extra fee per night. Being that the bathroom in the bedroom was not what we wanted, we changed rooms. While the staff seemed really nice and helpful for the most part, when we went to get the key to change rooms, they didn't seem to be too happy. When we asked if the room was near the other room and could we use the same entrance, we were simply told yes - meanwhile, when looking at the map, the room was on the opposite side of the hotel, definitely not using the same entrance. The layout if a little weird, can be confusing, but once you figure it out it is simple enough.
They do have a great breakfast every morning. We were there around Memorial Day Weekend so it was pretty busy - a few mornings we actually decided to avoid the breakfast there since it was so packed, but the food is good though and the staff is great with making sure they keep it stocked up. They do also offer free dinner as well as beer and wine Mondays thru Thursdays but we can't speak to this as we never made it back in time to have dinner there. 
While we were there they were doing some sort of work in the parking lot which was a bit of a pain. Oh, and they do charge you every night for parking - why not just build this into the cost of the room? Also, the nights that it was hard to find parking because of the work being done (and they also had one of two gates closed for periods of time) it would have been nice if they would have had some courtesy and waived the parking fee. Not sure if anyone else thinks so, but the parking spots seem to be a bit tight. We had a minivan, but it just seemed that the spots were a little on the small side. 
Overall, we had a good stay - just not sure we'd come back again.

title: “good place to stay”
text: Have stayed at this Holiday Inn Express on two other occasions when in San Jose for fun and appreciate its basic and clean environment and helpful, friendly staff. They provide a complimentary breakfast which is much better than most places, with both cold and hot foods. Yum on the biscuits and gravy. One thing I would recommend to the hotel is the option of not having new towels every day, since I felt that it was unnecessary and waste of resources to change the towels every day.

title: “Great first Kimpton experience”
text: My stay at the Hotel George was my first at a Kimpton property, and it lived up to my (admittedly high) expectations. The room was spacious and much larger than I expected, and the hotel staff was outstanding. They were helpful during check-in and check-out and in between and went above and beyond to make sure that my requests and previously indicated preferences were met; Jazmin was particularly wonderful. My impression that customer service is Kimpton's primary concern was definitely confirmed during this stay! The hotel location is incredibly convenient, less than a 5 minute walk from Union Station and the Capitol Building. I had meetings throughout the city and was able to walk or take public transportation to all of them. My room faced north and overlooked a handful of office buildings; while it wasn't a spectacular view, it was perfectly adequate, and I appreciated the quiet. There were one to two things that weren't up to the standard of the rest of the hotel (i.e. a shower door that would not close completely), but overall I found that the property, location, and, most particularly, the staff met or exceeded the expectations that I had for the hotel.

title: “Good Value”
text: Hotel is located in a great location and close to everything. Staff are very friendly and helpful. Price is hit and miss as sometimes I find they have great deals on and sometimes they are more pricey. Rooms are clean and well designed. Will return when price is reasonable.

title: “Ridiculously small rooms!”
text: The negative reviews are right -- the rooms are small, the bathrooms are the size of closets (no, really), and in-room climate control is very noisy. Fine for solo business travelers (good midtown location) but rooms are a tight squeeze for 2. This is an *old* hotel building that has been redecorated with dark paint & furniture to look tragically hip. No idea why this hotel rates 4 stars -- the hallways are narrow and dark, rooms are compact and gloomy. Lots of better choices in NYC.

title: “Great hotel, modern trendy and outstanding location”
text: This hotel was chosen for location and because I was redeeming my Starwood points. The hotel is clean, modern, good facilities such as the gym/spa and espresso bar. It's a shame there is no free wifi in the hotel rooms, and sometimes we had to wait a while for the elevators, but the rooms and service were excellent! Staff were friendly and helpful and couldn't do enough for us! Would definitely recommend!! Many thanks - definitely "Parker perfect"!

title: “Great hotel”
text: This was our third time staying here. We booked a Times Square view and we were given a great room on the front corner of the building. The rooms are spacious, clean, the beds are very comfortable and there is a nice sized flat screen tv to watch. The only thing missing would be a fridge which would be nice. The hotel is very close to Duffy Square where TKts on the Square is, plus the "red stairs" . The restaurant 1605 has a nice buffet breakfast and a good selection of pre theatre dinners for around 30 dollars. A total recommend enjoy. Rhoda at the front desk was very helpful - a great employee

title: “So-so”
text:
We stayed at the Marriott Canyon Villas for a week as part of a group of several families with young children. Our experience was mixed.
Pros:
- Very spacious, attractive, well-appointed suites at reasonable rates. We were able to host a dinner for 8 adults and 6 kids in our suite by using all of the tables and chairs provided.
- For kids, there is a small playground, a shallow splash pool, and a large 3.5-foot-deep pool at the resort.
- Access to the JW Marriott next door (long walk or short drive) with its "lazy river" pool, Roy's restaurant, and very attractive grounds.
- Big shopping center across the street has a supermarket, Target, and many other shops and restaurants.
- Half an hour drive away from downtown Phoenix and the airport, museums, zoo, Desert Botanical Garden, etc.
Cons: 
- The buildings are very densely packed on the property. The 3300 building, where we stayed, is very close to a busy four-lane road. Most of the time we couldn't hear the noise inside our suite, but when we stepped outside it was very noticeable. As I walked from one building to another or to the pools, I was very aware of the housing development just a few dozen yards away, and of the fairly massive resort buildings packed fairly close together. The net result for me was that it was missing that "away from it all" feeling that I typically get in a high-end resort.
- I could not get the climate control to work correctly. I like to keep the fan on to keep the air circulating. In both of our rooms, if the fan was on, so was the AC, and the room kept getting colder. In other words, there was no way to run the fan without also cooling the room. Eventually it would get too cold (much colder than the thermostat was set for, and the only solution was to switch the unit off.
- There were bright spots (engineering was super prompt and helpful when we had some minor issues with the rooms), but overall service was mediocre. As one example, two days in a row the supply of towels at the main pool ran out. I can see this happening once, but twice in a row indicates someone's not trained or not doing their job.
- The playground and splash pool are far from the main pool. So if you have toddlers on the playground or in the splash pool, and other kids or adults in the main pool, the groups are not going to be interacting.

title: “One of the best hotel experiences I've ever had”
text:
My husband my best friend and I spent 10/2-10/4 here -- I am a junkie for TripAdvisor and use it as my guide to all things travel -- the reviews did not disappoint - the hotel is literally a 5 minute walk to the White House and just a couple more minutes to the Mall. The staff is amazing - Eddie at the front desk kept me in stitches the entire time we were there -- he even ridiculed me jokingly about my obsession for maps -- Mark the Valet was such a nice guy - the entire staff was wonderful, helpful and accommodating but these 2 gentlemen really stood out. My friend stayed behind on Saturday because she wasn't feeling all that well and when we came downstairs, Mark asked where she was and how she was doing because he hadn't seen her all day -- I can't remember how many floors there were but the fact that they remembered who we were was really a nice personal touch - and we aren't high brow society types -- we don't get to vacation often ad certainly don't have scads of money so they were definitely not trying to suck up -- just being nice and friendly.
The room was great -- nice and big and airy with a HUGE bathroom - microwave and mini fridge which really came in handy -- also loved the free wifi - we brought our laptop with us and it really helped with restaurant reviews, tickets, etc. Neutrogena products in the bathroom and Henry Miller ergonomic chairs -- if you don't this guy, his products run around $1,000 ea!! Free cookies and coffee at night -- we didn't eat in the restaurant but I did go down one night to get some tonic water (for those g&ts in our room :)) and the bartender was really nice.
We didn't use the metro across the street -- Eddie suggested we go to the metro station a couple of blocks away so we wouldn't have to change trains - but it was nice to have a train so close by -- and incredibly easy to navigate around the city
I'm sure the hotel is more expensive during the holidays, cherry blossom, etc. but we paid $150/night and it was the best hotel money we've ever spent - an excellent time and will definitely stay there again when we go back.

title: “Average hotel.”
text: Average describes this hotel well. We were in town for the NCAA tournament and wanted to stay near the airport and be walking distance from the lightrail train to get to the games at HP Pavilion downtown. We were only able to go to one game so we were litterally getting into town, going to the game, going to the hotel to sleep late at night and getting up early to fly back home. So all we wanted was somewhere to get a decent sleep. And we did. Beds were comfortable. The rooms decorating was horribly out of date. But it was clean. The building overall could use some remodeling. But we got a good deal on the price, so we certainly weren't expecting anything amazing. The people at the checkin desk were very helpful and courtious. And the free shuttle to and from airport is nice. I would recommend this hotel if you are only staying a night or two like we were. But if you are on an extended stay, then this probably isn't the place for you.

title: “goog bargin”
text:
I sayed here at the end of may with my boyfriend for five days.
I knew the hotel was basic and was pleasntly surprised. The hotel is in a fansatic location and only a few minutes walk from the subway. The hotel was clean and most importanly so were the shared bathrooms.
The hotel was only half full during our stay and as a result had the bathroom to ourself.
The bathrooms are cleaned throughout the day and we never had any complaints.
The only down side was we had no view from the window in our room with very little day light as a result ,but not all rooms have this problem.
Over all it was a goof hotel worth every penny.

title: “Gorgeous and cool”
text: Loved this place!! Great location and the most beautiful bar/lounge ever!

title: “Dependable, Upscale, Secluded”
text:
We have stayed at the Hilton Dallas Park Cities on numerous weekend jaunts to Dallas. The location (Preston Center near the NW Highway and Dallas Tollway intersection), is a major plus. It is well centered to access all parts of Dallas. The staff is friendly, the hotel is pet friendly, and the rooms are comfortable and quiet. Since the hotel is located on a small, secluded street, there is NO street noise. Over the last couple of years, the hotel has been completely renovated. Recently, I was upgraded to an executive floor room that had high ceilings, a comfortable bed, plentiful workspace, and all the amenities one would expect. I had the opportunity to dine in the newly renovated restaurant - bar. The bartenders were terrific and the southwestern flavored small dishes were actually better than I expected.
Since we travel to Dallas frequently, the Hilton Park Cities is always one of the two or three "top of the list" lodgings for us. We highly recommend it!

title: “Wonderful hotel!”
text: We loved our stay at the Sofitel Water Tower Chicago. My husband and I wanted to stay somewhere near downtown and walking distance to different sights. The hotel was located just a couple of blocks from the John Hancock building and close to Michigan Avenue and shopping. The hotel and rooms were very clean and never saw any of the cleaning staff in the hallways while we were there. There was always a complimentary bottle of water next to the bed each night. Very nice touch. Also we read a comment about the candles being lit in the lobby everyday and how nice it smelled, well it was the same while we were there too. We would stay here again and recommend it to others.

title: “Great place to stay with toddler!”
text:
Recently stayed at Balboa Park Inn for 5 nights with our just-turned 2 year-old VERY active son. Room (Mayfair Suite) was PERFECT for the toddler. Full kitchen, separate bedroom, etc. All this for less than the single room we were supposed to stay in for my partner's conference (granted, not cheap, but worth it!). 
Walking distance to zoo and (slightly further walk, but a beautiful one!) to a great kid's playground. Very nice and free breakfast every morning - which came in handy as we were all still on New York time!

title: “Great location in mid-town Manhattan”
text: We recently stayed in the Alex hotel for 3 nights. It is an easy walk to Grand Central Station and Times Square. Room (1003) was modern and basic but nicely appointed. We did not eat at the restaurant connected to this hotel simply because we looked at the prices - e.g. pancakes - $18. I would suggest walking a block or two down Third Ave. and eating at Cosi for a decent inexpensive breakfast. On the negative side you had to pay for an internet connection and wifi is not free. Also the shower flow was rather light and the bath to shower mechanism was not the easiest to operate. Room had two double beds which were comfortable and made up daily (leave the bedside info cards on top of the bed so the room cleaner does not replace the bedding unnecessarily). Very friendly staff. Overall I would recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

title: “Is there better?”
text:
I don't think so! My wife and I spent nine nights in Boston at this hotel and found it faultless. There was absolutely nothing about which to complain. We received a complimentary upgrade to a suite and absolutely loved it! My wife managed to blow a fuse in the room, we reported it to the desk staff and by the time we'd finished breakfast it had been sorted! Beat that!
The hotel is spotless, the meals are first class and the staff!!! There are no words to compliment the staff here! Every single one was pleasant, helpful, and efficient. The old adage of 'Staff being the biggest asset' is absolutely spot on here. Polite, friendly and well able to handle Scottish sense of humour! Magic!:O)
We can't recommend this hotel highly enough! If the hotel inspectors wan't to be picky about not having a pool and a small fitness room then let them. This hotel should be lauded to the heavens!
Without denigrating anyone else, we found Nina at the Concierge desk, and absolute treasure.
It is handily placed for the T, Copley Square being the closest, and is easy to use. The Prudential Mall is almost next door and the ladies will LOVE it! :O) There are not enough superlatives to do this hotel justice.
Thank you to every single person at the Lenox for making our holiday extra special. Hope you enjoyed the chocs!:O)

title: “Best Hotel Ever!”
text:
Following the advice and recommendations of many here we booked a room at the Sofitel to stay over on July 4th. The hotel is in easy walking distance to the mall, Smithsonian, etc. Everything worked out perfectly, from the time the valet parking took our van to holding our luggage early before checking so we could see the 4th parade. Everyone there was super friendly and helpful. The room was awesome, and we loved the bed - my wife said it was the best sleep she's ever had.
If the hotel was just good, we wouldn't have bothered to write a review, however our stay there lived up to every expectation we had and more. Next year we are coming back for the 4th festivities in DC and staying here again.

title: “Something great from LaQuinta that I did not know”
text: LaQuinta hotels have always been known for their great services, etc. I find out another great service they offer at my last stay. We stayed at the one across from the San Antonio, TX airport. We knew they offered free shuttle to the airport, which is great. But, they also let us leave our vehicle in their parking lot while we went on vacation. We did not have to worry about finding a parking spot at the airport or some where else. This great service cost us only $20.00 and you can leave your vehicle for up to 14 days. Other hotels might do the same, but I have never asked up until now. Just remember to let them know you are picking up your vehicle when leaving, they might report it stolen, etc.

title: “Chicago on the way”
text: Everything was excellent except we always only select Hotels with free Internet access, so it was actually a misunderstanding. The confirmation said "High Speed Internet" was included, but it appeared that it referred to 3 PC's on second floor (which were occupied when we checked) or on 3rd, but we need to use our own. So we had breakfast and did our (free) internet business all 3 mornings of the stay on Starbucks next door (there were 4 Starbucks within a blocks distance, maybe that's why?). Next time we'll find and Accor Hotel with Internet included, or a Starwood, or Marriott, if possible?

title: “Good hotel, good location”
text: Stayed here multiple times in 2009, for 30+ nights. Nice clean hotel, good layout. Staff was always very friendly and helpful. Occasionally had noisy guests over the weekend (one weekend in particular was very bad) but for normal business travel it was great. Very close to a Super Target for inexpensive groceries, and close to a lot of restaurants, not to mention the museums. Adjacent to trinity park, good for a nice long walk. Would definitely stay here again. Occasionally would hear a train but never disrupted my sleep.

title: “Good Experience”
text: I found the room to comfortable and well furnished. The staff was attentive. If you are arriving via the subway from the airport you will need to take a cab from the nearest station (Grand) to the hotel if you have bags. I don't care for the fact that they charge for internet access--a nickle and dime affair.

title: “nothing good but the location”
text: I'm astounded by all of the positive reviews. This hotel is pretty awful. Small pretentious lobby, unfriendly staff, tiny clinical room, no bar, no room service, no coffee. The ONLY good thing about it is the location.

title: “Great Hotel / Great Service”
text: I typically don't write reviews, but when I checked into the Hilton, it was my fifth hotel over four cities and 12 days on the road, so I was feeling a bit road weary when Stuart greeted me at check-in with a "welcome back" before he even looked up my reservation--and I hadn't been at the hotel in over five years. We made small talk which included that my stay was going to be days 12-14 and then home, and Stuart surprised me with an upgrade to a magnificent room saying he wanted this to be the best hotel experience of my trip. The whole hotel is great... it has the amenities of a vacation place with the conveniences for business, but what a treat. Stuart then went the extra mile by calling my room shortly after I got there to make sure it was okay, plus the hotel delivered a lovely fruit plate as turn-down service my first night. I would definitely return to the hotel for leisure or business, and I hope management recognizes Stuart for the great brand ambassador that he is.

title: “Great hotel, great location, great staff!”
text:
Booked the Serrano Hotel for a week stay in San Francisco.
The hotel is smack bang in the middle of the Union Square region, and is diagonally opposite the Hilton, and various other large chains. Being 2 blocks from Macy's and Union Square, the hotel is located in the perfect location for avid shopping fans.
Those wanting to get around SF, the Muni system is accessible via buses, cable cars and trains all located at easy walking distance from the hotel.
The staff have always been very attentive, assisting us on our queries, and the free coffee/tea in the mornings and free beers and wine in the evenings is a bonus.
The leopard print bathrobes are a hilarious contemporary addition to the room, which comes with Aveda products in the bathroom, and free WIFI access which has most definitely been a handy extra.
The only downside is that there are a number of homeless people surrounding the area, but that most likely comes with the territory of being located in the city centre.

title: “Nothing special, but what we needed”
text: Stayed here for 5 night during Thanksgiving. Reviews are very mixed, but I would say it's above average. The rooms where clean and comfortable, though a little warm. Opening the window solved this problem. The staff was very attentive and responded quickly to our requests. It is a little out of the way. I wish it where a few block west, toward Grand Central. About what we expected, considering what we paid. Relatively good value for NYC.

title: “Noisy but handy”
text: This hotel was close to the likes of Union Square, Bart, Trams etc. My wife and I stayed in this hotel for three nights at the start of March. Our room was on the second floor, and for the the time of our stay, we could not sleep with the noise coming from the hotel night club, which finished around 2am. The room itself was on the small side, but clean. The staff we found to be helpful, but the breakfast was a bit of a disappointment as choice was limited and you had to carry the food back to your room. if our room was higher up away from the noise, we might have enjoyed our stay better, however if you get a room at the bottom of the hotel, expect a long night.

title: “Don't let the lobby fool you - it's gross.”
text: This place looked promising: relatively modern exterior, nice lobby with a FedEx Kinko's and Starbucks. The room, however, was disgusting: the sheets were worn and had pilling that felt like crumbs or worse. The air conditioner barely worked. The faucet fixture was scratched and the bathroom is a very unattractive white. The remove control is ancient and vaguely sticky, and the television was a large tube-screen that just looked sad. The hotel staff is horrid: inattentive, rude, and they don't honor your requests for a particular newspaper or a high/low floor. The place is just depressing; you can just feel the conventioneers' spirits floating all over the place, their body soil in the carpets. Also, they tried to charge me for two days' use of high-speed internet that I never signed-up for; luckily I challeneged the charge. Horrid place - certainly not up to Marriott's usual standards.

title: “Mmmmmm~”
text: The location is good for the price... it is a quick walk to time square. Lots of neat deli's to eat at in the same block...and there is a Starbucks right when you walk out the door! BUT.... ours first room smelt HORRIBLE....and the view faced a brick wall. We went back down and they gave us another room, this one smelt better but I never walked barefooted anywhere in the room....and wish I had some shower shoes for the shower. The lobby is beautiful and staff friendly, but the rooms are very out dated and could use some clorox....not pine-o-pine! The bar in the hotel was great....grabed a quick cosmo before we headed out the first night and was the best I had ever had! The David Letterman show is one street behind the hotel and one block down. Keeping in mind we were only in the room to sleep.... I may stay there again. Nahhhh....probably not!

title: “Staff is the best!”
text:
I have traveled globbably on business, and not experienced a team more intent on pleasing its customers. The service orientation was extensive from the maintenance man in the basement garage to the manager on duty.
Priced right, as advertised, and pleasing staff.

title: “Great Hotel in Downtown Detroit”
text:
We stayed at the Holiday Inn Express the weekend of August 4th for the Tigers/Cleveland Indians series. The rooms were very nice with everything in working order and good TV. The hotel was very busy the weekend several large groups but the hotel staff did a very nice job handling the large groups and always had a can do attitude. We were appreciative in recieving the room upon our noon arrival as we had an early flight into Detroit Metro that morning.
Look forward to staying here again in January for the auto show.

title: “Loved the Renoir, not the taxi driver”
text: Last week we stayed at the Renoir hotel in downtown San Francisco. Our experience with this hotel was totally satisfactory, considering the excellent rate we paid and the excellent service we got for our money ( a big credit to the helpful young bellman). Our room (on the fifth floor, McAllister Street side which i recommend for being quieter) was large, clean and had everything we needed: a comfortable king size bed, bathroom, cable TV, phone and internet acces (although it was a relatively expensive dial-up connection). We were told they were in the process of upgrading all rooms to Wireless - great! We live in Santa Ana and fly to San Francisco quite frequently, especially on weekends. The homeless population that is visible allover downtown doesn't scare us, and last week it was very cold, so they were less visible than usual. Also, the city seems to be more aware that they have to take care of all these poor people and that they can't continue letting them hang out in front of hotels and restaurants wherever you go. We had one unpleasant experience though: the taxi driver who took us into the city tried to "divert" us from the Renoir, telling us that this was the worst neighborhood of the city and that he knew much better places for "people like us" (!), for the same price. Knowing exactly what to expect from our chosen hotel (which we had prepaid anyway), we declined to be brought to a different place (I won't give you the name), but he really insisted a lot. We both got the impression that he was somehow "interested" ($$?) in convincing hotel guests to follow him to a property where he potentially could receive a commission for his referral. So if you come to San Francisco, don't believe everything your taxi driver tells you, he might have his "special" reasons for giving you such advice.

title: “Just OK. Could be better.”
text: I stay at the Warwick for 4 days on a business trip. First, the plusses. Location is great in Downtown Denver. The view of downtown at night was very nice (ask for rooms looking towards downtown). The staff was very helpful, very nice. The lobby, nice. Now let that be my segway to the not soo good. The rooms are old and outdated. the bes was ok, but I felt like I was visiting my grandnother, old chairs and furniture, dark bathroom, tired carpet with stains, the roof top pool was sad, but the worst was the white light bulbs in all the lamps. Don;t get me wrong. I am all for the enviroment and for being green, but this is 2012 and soft white bulbs are available everywhere. Why not to buy some? I felt like I was in the morgue. The artwork didn't match, photography in one wall, gradma picture of a goose in the other. The balcony was great, but rusted and moldy. Guys, come on, you have a great location close to a somewhat trendy neighborhood with cool restaurants. It seems like the whole neighbourhood is having a rebirth and the Warwick is dying in the morgue with white lights. Give therooms some love would you?

title: “A good night's slepp”
text:
Stayed here for two nights in August 2011.
The hotel is very convenient for the stadiums and the arena, although that makes it a little remote for visiting the city (which we did). It is also well located in respect to the airport, and they offer a free shuttle to the airport.
I was working at the Arena, so the location was perfect. I also visited the city using the subway system and was only a 15 minute commute (3 dollar round trip).
The room, whilst dated was renovated and very spacious. The room was also very clean, and to be honest I have no complaints.
There were two queen sized beds with varying pillows (pillows had tags telling if they were soft, hard etc). There was a desk, a tv, a microwave, a coffee machine and a fridge in the room. I was lucky to have a beautiful view of the city skyline, but my colleague was equally lucky having a view of the stadiums. Overall rooms were great. Shower was clean, and like a sandblaster (lots of pressure). I did end up with a slightly cold shower on the second morning. Wifi was free, but not exactly hi-speed....
I ate at the restaurant and bar and found the food to be good and the prices were also good. My main complaint would be with the coffee...nasty stuff. Wish there would have been a Starbucks or something like that either in the hotel or close.
Overall the hotel was good for my needs. I am not sure of the value, as Io never saw the bill.

title: “Great Spot on Michigan Ave”
text: The service is extraordinary and everyone is very polite. I like any hotel attached to a Nordstrom. It was easy to get in and out of, great access to Michigan Ave, etc. The first room they put us in smelled like cigarettes. Surprising! It's no smoking there. However, we called down to the desk and within 3 minutes had another hotel room and were moved up 10 floors to a room with a view for our "inconvenience." They were great. The gym was really nice too. If anything, I can say that the rooms aren't very big (big enough) and, I presume because my room was close to an elevator, you could hear doors slam every once in a while. That's it though - I would stay here again (2nd time staying actually) and highly recommend it.

title: “Times Square”
text: The best thing about this hotel is it's location, however that does make it noisy from the street outside at all hours of the day. The room we had 421 was small. There is no bath - just a shower. The towels are all small - not really bath towels. The Wi-fi did not work at all whilst we were there - and when we asked we were told it was being fixed next month !!! save yourself money and go to the Olympic Diner for breakfast -turn left out of the hotel and then right - it's on the other side of the road - half the price of breakfast elsewhere -also convenient for the metro station if you are heading that way.

title: “Great luxury hotel in Chicago”
text: We have stayed here three times and plan to return. Although relatively pricy, the location and service are great. Rooms are clean and fairly roomy. You can shop in the Water Tower without going outside which is a plus during winter. And best of all they allow pets without an additional fee and provide bowls and Evian water!

title: “Good Hotel and Service”
text:
We stayed at the Omni Shoreham on the first night of our honeymoon and were impressed with standards and service during the four days we were there.
A really nice touch was a complimentary bottle of bubbly and strawberries to mark our special occassion.
The hotel is less than a 5 min walk from Woodley Grove metro station. We found the metro a cheap and convienent way of getting around the city.
It is set in really nice gardens where there were lots of places to sit and enjoy the sunshine. The pool also looked really good (and clean) although we did not use it during our stay.
Did not have breakfast in the hotel, but instead went to a small cafe/bar which was just opposite and was really good.
We had one meal in the hotel on the last night of our stay, which I cannot fault. It was delicious.

title: “Very Poor Quality Hotel”
text: Stayed at this hotel for business. The elevators (at least a vast majroity of them) did not work, causing at least a 5-7 minute wait to get one to come up to the ninth floor. Next, I asked for a no-smoking room, and clearly, the floor was marked as no-smoking, but the room smelled an awful lot like smoke. I opened the balcony doors to air out the room. The next day, much to my surprise, there was a ciggarette butt on the balcony. Perhaps the maid, or perhaps it landed there from a floor above, either way, I don't smoke, but clearly, someone at the hotel does...Next, bugs. I saw 4 roaches during my stay, 2 in my room's sink, on the last morning. Awful. I can only imagine if I saw 4, how many there really are. Finally, as with any hotel, the lobby bar drinks are way overpriced, and the whole place is out dated. There are no refridgerators or safes in the rooms, and the TV is an old school unit, about 3 feet deep. If I ever get back to Houston, I certainly won't stay at the Post Oak.

title: “nice when finnished!!!”
text: We arrived at the hotel,(which is in a great location)to the lobby still under construction.After the reception eventually decided where our room was as we were staying a week and this seemed to complicate matters(we had been booked in 3mouths before).We were put in room 215.We were aware when we booked it was the atrium room but being on the first floor with very little light coming down from the 8th floor it felt very "coffin like"! Our room had just been decorated which was nice,although our bathroom door never closed over,and a bit of a shabby job decorating the bathroom.3 curtain hooks in the shower curtain although but the next day it was fixed We awake on our first morning at 7.15am to the sound of drill and hammers turns out the rest of the floor/rooms were still under a re-fit.We waited till the next day and the same so we asked to be moved rooms,which the did to a bigger,brighter atrium on the 8th floor.The hotel will be nice when its finished! If you book an atrium make sure its near the top unless you work in mines and are use to lack of sunlight and air.

title: “Great location - Don't expect too much and you won't be disappointed”
text: I've stayed here in the past and although it's not "dirty", it's not very well kept up either. The only complaint we had was that one of the beds had a horrible, sticky-textured feel to it and the pillows weren't very comfortable so you may want to bring your own. The rooms were decent in size (2 double beds), the a/c was ok, TV in working condition, pool was out of service "indefinitely" and the restaurant below was pretty good - Asian food and they were open pretty late. You can't beat the location if you're coming in for a Red Sox game at Fenway, which is why we chose it and would probably choose it again unless someone opens up a nicer hotel in walking distance.

title: “Funky but flawed”
text: The Hotel Erwin is a great place to stay. It is just a little let down by it's surroundings. I do admit our visit was 'out of season' April, but side streets, and general area, were a little run down. We didn't feel comfortable venturing out at night, but the Erwin has a great alternative - the roof top bar 'High'. It is very cool, and has amazing views (especially at night) across LA. The room's were good, and we had a free upgrade for one of them (for a Facebook 'like!) to a suite, really nice to have dinning table, settee, and kitchenette, in a good size room. Our breakfast in 'Eat', was ok, but was served warm, not hot. Service at the desk was great, in addition to the response's from my 'online' questions, prior to our visit. I would recommend a stay at the Erwin (for great access to Venice Beach), they do know how to look after you.

title: “Outstanding Facility”
text:
Great location to airport!
Facilities well kept and attractive!
Personnel (front desk, shuttle driver and hostess) always went above and beyond to make our stay comfortable.
Will stay again when we are back in the area!

title: “My Stay at the Westin Copley Place”
text:
My husband and I recently stayed at the Westin Copley Place and we had a wonderful experience. We were only there for one night, but we wish we could have stayed so much longer. Our room had such a breath taking view of the city, that we never even closed our curtains. 
The furniture, the size of the room, the bedding, the decor, everything was amazing! 
We also did room service for breakfast and it was delicious! 
We will definitely stay there again!

title: “great location”
text: I made the reservation by hotwire without knowing the name and when i began to read the reviews here, i was very worried because i read some with the words: BED BUGS. But when i arrived i checked the whole room and it was fine, none of them :-) the best of that hotel is the location, close of muni, cable car and lots of stores. The room was clean but i think it was small for 2 double beds, but i was alone' so i didn't have that problem.

title: “Rush concert with my son.”
text: This was a nice clean hotel in a good area and I would recommend it and stay there again. The room was comfortable. I was very happy that there was a workout room which I did use daily. I found it a convenient location for everywhere that I needed to get to.

title: “Beware the front desk. Once you clear that you are in good shape”
text: My experince with this hotel started when I pulled over in my suv and was told that they can't park my vehicle in their parking garage because it is too high. I was directed to park it at the Mariott hotel 2 blocks away. When I walked back to the hotel. I saw them park an suv just like mine for a guest because he is staying two nights. Second was the front desk, the manager gives every guest the meanest look his name is(BABA)Last is check in. Check in is at 4pm I get there at 3pm and was told to wait until 4pm. I when to see the Museam and got back at 6:45 I was told that the room is still not ready. The hotel is great for the price but the service is a big zero.

title: “Late for airport”
text: The shuttle was reseved for 8:20am. Apparently it came by ... Early. I got to the lobby at 8:19am. and the shuttle already left. Had to wait for a cab and missed my flight. I had called the front desk to schedule the shuttle earlier that morning. The rest of the day was effected on account of missing my flight. The blame was placed on me for not being there on time...but the clock in the front lobby...the big dial clock...was a little hard to refute. I don't know if I will ever stay at another of your hotels or affiliates. Will wait for a response before I place my complaint on face book. Thank you for your time.

title: “Great hotel, Great Area, Affordable stay!”
text: When we told everyone we were staying in Harlem we got plenty of warnings about danger and many people telling us to change locations! This hotel is right across from the police station and there was police presence everywhere! Not to mention the hotel security at night!. Great hotel with very large rooms and very comfortable beds! They have a lovely WXYZ lounge with a pool table, computers and printer for use, and of course a bar and appetizers for order. There is no restuarunt but they do have appetizers for order at the bar as well as a convenance shop with drinks and sandwhiches for purchase. The staff was super friendly and helpful, they gave us directions and were happy to answer any of our questions. They also have a great incentive program for everyday you opt out of maid service they give you a $5 voucher to use in the hotel store or WXYZ lounge. The area has great food places, mcdonalds, the Apollo theatre and just a short walk to the subway or the bus stop for public transit! Highly recommend this for anyone wanting to visit New York. Just 2 stops from Times Square on the A or D express trains.!!! Also, being very paranoid about the bed bug problem in NY, I throughly checked the rom for bed bugs and found no signs of any or even of any treatments for them!!! came home bed bug free! =) A++++

title: “Two-star experience-four star price”
text: Front desk staff were indifferent as to our existence. Bathroom grouting in the tub was brown and missing. Valet parking is on 41st not 42nd! Be CAREFUL! I got a $115.00 ticket. convenient location, but not really the four-star experience I paid for.

title: “Great hotel, not ideal for business”
text:
Staying at The Stoneleigh was a great experience from start to finish, and I have only very minor complaints. The hotel is in a great location and my room was clean and spacious (though I was upgraded from a standard to a deluxe king room when I arrived).
My only complaints: there's no coffee maker in the room (is this a new trend? why?), so if you're a business traveler, that means ordering it via room service or going without coffee before your morning meeting. It's annoying, but not fatal. Also, I ended up ordering breakfast in my room both days (it was pretty good) because I was afraid that the sit-down breakfast service would take too long. 
My only other complaint is that the equipment in the fitness center was pretty inadequate and outdated. It certainly wasn't up to the standards of the rest of the hotel.
Overall, this hotel was a great value (I think I paid a $199/night rack rate) for its price class.

title: “Wish we were here longer! You'll love the shuttle service!!”
text:
The Silver Cloud's staff was very friendly and helpful. We loved the location. Free parking, free internet and free breakfast were a great combination! The rooms were spacious and clean. Wish we were in the room long enough to enjoy it more. Lots of trendy restaurants and bars within walking distance. It was nice having coffee and tea in the lobby at all hours. The best feature about Silver Cloud though is its free shuttle service! They had 3 destinations: Pike's Market, Pioneer Square and the Space Needle. All you had to do was call the hotel to let them know you wanted to be picked up or dropped off. It was wonderful since all the reviews I read said parking was ridiculous in Seattle. Thank you Silver Cloud for making our stay in Seattle more enjoyable than expected. We had a party of 10 and we all agreed we'd love to stay here again! 
Only downside: garage parking is great especially when it's free but you won't be able to fit a minivan with a cargo compartment on its roof. The other family we travelled with had to pay for parking on an outdoor lot next to the hotel. The free shuttle service more than made up for the inconvenience.

title: “Shaky Start But Excellent Service”
text:
The Omni San Antonio is a wonderful property located just 10 minutes from downtown. 
Upon our arrival in San Antonio, we called the hotel for directions - which was not very helpful at all. The normal ten minute drive from downtown lasted approximately 3 hours by following the hotel directions. When we arrived at the Omni San Antonio, I requested to speak with the manager about this problem and she promptly called my room and made sure that our stay was pleasant. For the trouble that we had, we were upgraded to a king suite compliments of the hotel. That's a value that can't be beaten. 
As an Omni Select Guest, we received prompt morning beverage service along with our newspaper. This was a very nice gesture and excellent service. 
All of the amenities of the hotel were well thought out. There are two swimming pools - one indoors and one outdoors. The indoor pool is a regular rectangle, while the outdoor pool is a little more fun as it has a lap section, volleyball section, basketball section, and plenty of floaties. Both pools are accompanied by hot tubs - which is a real treat... as most hotels may have one hot tub. The inroom ammenities are excellent - they included Institute Swiss items, luxury robes, etc.
I highly recommend the Omni San Antonio for business, pleasure, etc. It is a wonderful hotel that houses so many attractions such as live entertainment in the lobby bar on Friday and Saturday nights, dual swimming pools, fitness center with refreshments, pool side cabanas, suana, and much more. 
Would I stay there again? Yes, I will. :-)

title: “Great time”
text: Loved the city of Indy.. had a great time when visiting out there. I would recommend this hotel to others.. a little high on the price however.. could be lower

title: “Icky and Overpriced”
text: We were booked into this hotel by Hotels.com; what a rip off! We had to cut our vacation short due to a death in the family and had made arragements to fly out the next morning so we needed a place close to the airport. The entire hotel is dirty. The heater/air conditioner made so much noise we had to turn it off. There was mold in the shower. The free continental breakfast was so bad we didn't even take anything; no fruit, juice, or anything edible. The price was high $80 + tax. The front desk person could not answer any questions about anything. If we could have gotten our money back we would have gone elsewhere. Do not stay here! There are many other hotels in the area.

title: “Great location”
text: I stayed here on a Friday night after enjoying a night out with friends. I probably should have researched parking a bit as valet is $31. Come to find out the parking garage a block away is $5 a day on weekends. I little ticked at the valet service I confronted them and they gladly gave my truck back with no charge and I parked at the garage. All the the staff had this same helpful attitude. Very pleased with my stay.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for four nights for the Marathon weekend, got a great deal because I booked early however, Marriot allow you to cancel at short notice without charge so there is zero risk.
The rooms were extremely large and clean for a City Hotel and that was what attracted me the most.
The position is 15 minutes walking to Broadway but there is a subway on the corner just outside as an alternative.
Staff are polite and helpful and plenty of options locally for pharmacies, book stores and restaurants/deli's etc.
Would not hesitate staying in this hotel as it is far better value than staying on broadway.
Would suit families as well due to the larger rooms.

title: “Charming and great location..”
text:
Frankly, I am surprised by some of the negative reviews of this charming and unique property in San Francisco.. It is a "boutique" hotel with great prices, beautiful furnishings, and fine service. Check in was simple and friendly.....and yes, parking is $35, but that is a bargain for San Francisco. Front desk clearly recommended allowing 30 minutes when retrieving your car (so plan accordingly, people....try driving around the block in SF in traffic and commuter hours w/ walkers, cyclists, and clowns, and you can understand why you need to allow 30 minutes)...
The Nob Hill Hotel is in a great location, with easy access to bus routes and cable cars...and decent connection to BART. It is a safe and clean neighborhood with plenty of dining options. The front desk was quick to offer ideas for dining and things to do in SF.
The room was beautiful..Victorian furnishings, comfy bed and pillows, and sparkly clean. Sure there was some street noise...but you should expect that in SF in the older hotels. Lighting was fine... with Tiffany style lamps and a chandelier (quite pretty). New flatscreen TV, plenty of channels, and an armoire (wardrobe) for hanging clothing. 
The bathroom was newly remodeled and beautiful...great lighting, fixtures, and a larged jetted tub/shower combo.
I rather enjoyed the "older style" elevator...reminded me of the old elevators formerly found in department stores (usually tended by an ancient man or woman). There are stairs, for those who care to take the speedy route to their rooms.
Breakfast was a typical "continental breakfast". Cereal, toast, etc. Certainly not fancy, but enough to get you started on your day before heading out for the really amazing food of San Francisco. 
I found the service to be extremely pleasant from start to finish..and thoroughly enjoyed my stay..I certainly plan on returning to this hotel in the future!

title: “not quite up to Westin standards”
text: not too familiar with Westin properties, but thought they were on the higher end of the Starwood properties. The staff was extremely friendly & helpful, but the property definitely could use some upgrades. Beds were VERY nice. Conference facilities were good, but food was marginal at best. Great fitness center & nice to have Starbucks in the lobby.

title: “This Hotel is AMAZING”
text: We are Seattle fans and have traveled often from Florida over the past 10 years. This hotel by far is our new home away from home. From Virginia at the front desk to John behind the bar at Lola, this is a true Seattle Home experience. The staff is well trained, and they respond to any issue with professionalism and a sincere demeanor that just makes you feel good about spending money to sleep. We started a two week trip at Hotel Andra and then changed the end of the trip to stay with them longer. Great location, great rooms, great service, and great food but most of all great smiles. STAY AT THIS HOTEL.

title: “Good Accomodations for the Business Traveler”
text:
I stayed for one night on June 4. I'm a big fan of the Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificient Mile but the rates were very high - must have been a large convention in town. I had not stayed at the Courtyard Chicago Downtown before but the location seemed good. Overall I was pleased with my stay.
PROS (mainly for the business traveler)
- Free highspeed internet 
- "Business Center" open 24 hours on the basement level - not fancy but there are two computers and a printer. This was perfect for printing a boarding pass and printing a document I neeeded for a meeting the next morning
- Clean rooms
CONS
- The bed was one of the worst I've had at a Marriott. No cushy matress cover. Very uninviting.
- Because I had very little time in the morning and because the Starbucks downstairs had been closed the day before "due to problems with air conditioning," I decided to order room service for breakfast. I decided the healthy choice of yogurt, granola and fruit would be good. I would have felt like I got more for my money if I had chosen something else. I literally received a small yogurt (from a multi pack), a 1/4 cup of granola and a small plate of fruit. I know room service is a rip-off but this was very disappointing for $21 (this did include a small pot of coffee).
Overall the stay was good but next time I will return to Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificient Mile if I can find better rates.

title: “Until this visit, we found Westin to be constant”
text: Our stays at a Westin in Costa Mesa and other locations were always comfortable. The Chicago Michigan Ave. was in a good location, but that's about it.

title: “No mini fridge”
text: There is no mini fridge in the room which we missed. Not for the overpriced food and drink that hotels usually put in them but for when we brought small qualities of our own stuff. For example you couldn't even have milk on hand for breakfast cereal or your own orange juice or store stuff left over in a take home pack from dinner. The rest was ok but because of this lack of mini fridge I wouldn't stay there again.

title: “Bland, charmless, overpriced, uncomfortable”
text: The best that can be said of this Starwood property is that the lobby's nice and the staff helpful. After that -- once one exits the elevator into the institutional-beige guest floors and the drab institutional-beige rooms -- it's Motel 6 territory, for $200/night more. The overall design of the rooms is atrocious. the mind-numbling dull color scheme, the peculiar arrangement of the lights, the shabby grout and tile. Luckily I was only here three nights -- any longer and I've had joined the bums in camping along the embarcadero.

title: “Nice place in good neighborhood”
text:
This is a very nice hotel in a good part of town. Centrally located at California and Powell. You are directly on two cable car lines if you want to get places, but keep in mind the cable cars, while practical, are expensive (6/ ride) to actually get around on due to their tourist popularity. 
This hotel is on the top of Nob Hill. So if you coming back to the hotel on foot you WILL go up hill. Leaving is down hill though!
The hotel itself if very nice, but rather pricy. I paid for the "deluxe" room and found it very spacious and nice. For the $200/night rate you couldn't do much better considering the area. I did notice some of the smaller rooms (via peeking inside) and they looked very much smaller than my deluxe room. If the rates are similar you will be better off getting the deluxe room.
Our room had a view from the 5th floor, but keep in mind that you WILL hear the cable cards when they go by during the day. The non-deluxe rooms may not have a view, but they are probably slightly quieter. With the fan on I could not hear any street noise. 
We also arrived before noon ( checkin is a 3 ) and they were able to get us a room!
In all I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Outstanding service”
text:
I stayed at the Hyatt because I was there for a really large convention that pretty much took over downtown Denver. I absolutely must comment the Hyatt's entire staff; never a misstep, and with this high end crowd, they surely had a lot to deal with. 
The front desk staff, the concierge, the wait staff, everyone was a pleasure to deal with. The location is good, an easy stroll to Larimer Square, and steps to the Convention Centre. I always felt safe walking around the hotel area (and believe me, I walked a lot!)
Rooms were spacious and well kept, decent amenities.

title: “This place is a total dump - Website looks are deceiving!”
text: What you see on the website is not what you get. The lobby is pretty. But past the elevators, this place is horrible. We're a young, hip family from Dallas and we were completely disgusted. My pregnant wife was completely grossed out. For what they charge, you'd be better off at a Motel 6. *Booked the room via Kayak = BIG mistake. Room had vomit stains and plastic bags over the pillows for head lice. Nasty. We refused to stay there and the hotel made no effort to help us. We got stiffed paying for 2 nights and the hotel lied to Kayak by insisting we stayed there when we didn't!! Very shady. Where we DID stay was heavenly = Le Parc Hotel on Knoll. What a GEM. Le Parc is A+. Wilshire hotel should be destroyed.

title: “What happen to customer service???”
text: Fort Rapids is by far the worst place that I have had the experience of staying. When approaching the building I was a little concerned because there was a very tall fence which sent up a red flag for me, I thought the place must have security issues. We went to the went to the water park while waiting on our room (the room was suppose to be available at 4pm and we did have reservations) we did not get our room until after 5pm and when entering our room the floors had not been vacumed, the tables were not clean, dead bug in front of the microwave, and to top it off when I inspected the sheets there were blood stains on them. Management was immediately informed two members of management inspected the room and said that they would move us. We waited and waited I called the manager and he said that he had four people ahead of me and that he would call me back, I gave him half an hour and informed him that I would be requesting a refund after that and would leave the hotel. Finally the manager talked in person to me and gave us another room at approximately 7pm. My family was hungry and my daughters wanted to have fun in the water park with their parents but their parents had to address problems with the room which took time away from family time in the water park. Later when we went back to the room we found that the television did not work so we called the front desk and they said that they would send someone up to fix it. Waiting, still waiting, 45 min. later I called again, and waited but no one came. In the morning I called again and we finally got someone and waited some more and we eventually got the television 30 min. before checkout. Totally unacceptable service. Just a thought, if the sheets, the floor, and the tables are dirty then how is the water park being maintained?????? Or are they???? Scary! In the water park the hot top had some occupants that were doing everything but having sex in front of others including the life guard and the kiddy pool is located by the hot tub. The water in the kiddy pool was so cold that the toddlers lips were turning blue. There were no clean towels available to dry off and the locker room and hallway to the locker room were dirty. Some of the members of our group took home bed bugs and cock roaches, and others had toilet flushing issues and had to go out in the middle of the night to use someone elses toilet, and to top it off there was a break in, a master key was used to enter a room and there were multiple teenagers in the room thank God what would have happened if there was one of the teenage girls in the room. The 2 african american males that entered the room were not staff of the hotel. Again scary. We work hard for our money and I just feel that Fort Rapids is a waste of good money. Very disappointed that management did not make much of an effort to make compensations to the degree of our bad experiences.

title: “Elegant Lobby, clean room, great location”
text: After reading mixed reviews, we were pleasantly surprised by friendly staff. Room was clean, although on the small side. Enjoyed hanging out in the lobby and bar. Location was excellent, with walking distance to Broadway, Times Square, Grand Central Station, Rockefeller Square. Internet charge is a rip-off, but we didn't use it. Breakfast way too expensive, but plenty of alternatives a block or two away.

title: “Unbelievably bad”
text:
Booked two rooms - got a VM on the way in from the airport that only one room available - a "maintenance issue". Coincidence that Pres Obama was in town and the city was booked to the gills? Rollaway bed and King bed to house me and my elderly parents - less than 6" between rollaway and bed....fire code violation? No apology offered until I responded to hotel survey.
Wouldn't recommend to anyone

title: “very comfortable and clean”
text:
Stayed here for 5 nights and then went on to Las Vegas for 5 nights.
The Omni Hotel is wonderful, its clean and the staff are very friendly and helpful.
There is everything you need in your room, nothing is forgotten.
Its lovely to eat there and just pass the time. You can book trips to the famous zoo or other sight seeing tours by going to the conceirges desk at the far end of the reception. 
Taxi's are just outside the door to take you anywhere you want to go.
The Gaslamp district is right on the doorstep, plenty of places to eat and drink and have a good time.
The trains run just around the corner from the hotel so this place is very convenient for everything.
I cannot fault it whatsoever.

title: “Excellent ubication and good service”
text:
We were in New York in a medical related trip and were very glad to be at this hotel.
Its location is excellent, not only near university hospitals and doctors offices, but close to Central Park, good restaurants and shopping areas.
Beds are VERY comfortable and service was very good, in particular that of Mr. Pedro Hilario, Front Desk Manager.

title: “Enjoyed our stay...But...”
text: We enjoyed our visit to Boston very much. The Best Western Roundhouse Suites were suitable as we were able to use their shuttle service which took us every place that we requested - very friendly & informative drivers. The rooms were clean - with a sink, microwave, coffeepot, fridge & small cupboard in the livingroom - this room also had a sofa bed that has seen better days, writing desk, large TV inside an armour. The king-size bed was very comfortable and there was also another large TV inside an armour. The continental breakfast was good - all sorts of cold breakfast foods, plus freshly cooked waffles, available in a very crowded lobby area. The use of the internet, computer and printer was appreciated. I would not walk around in this area during the day, never mind at night. The staff was very helpful & friendly, but if it wasn't for the shuttle bus we would not have spent more than one night.

title: “If this is a 3 star, I'm a super model.”
text:
Avoid this place. It's a dump, it's dirty, and it's dated plus it's in the middle of nowhere. Got the room on a Priceline bid of $75, about twice what this place is worth.
STAY AWAY and beware the three star Priceline bid.

title: “Unbeatable location”
text: You're in the heart of Times Square and the Theater District. Lots to see and do nearby or a short subway ride away. The rooms are small but comfortable.
