When we checked in, the air conditioning in our room didn't work. However, the staff quickly and politely moved us to another room. The ice machine on two floors was out of order. But overall, I would have no problem staying there again.

title: “Poor hotel & terrible customer service”
text: My partner and I stayed in this hotel as we know New York well and thought the location and reviews of the hotel were decent enough given the price point. What we experienced was awful service, we were given 2 inadequate rooms, ie after we complained we were transferred to an even shabbier, smaller room. Both were dirty, had broken drawers, hangers etc, were incredibly noisy. We have stayed in NYC many times and know what you can get for your money, we did not expect luxurious huge rooms with amazing views, we wanted a well located crash pad that was clean and had the basic things covered. We were paying for the location & the price was not unreasonable comparatively but there are better places to stay for the same price point or even less. When we complained to the manager - very politely - he could not care less and patronised us by saying we shouldn't expect anything more than this for the price we were paying - he practically laughed at us for even bringing it up with him. Go elsewhere this place doesn't deserve your custom.

title: “"Staying here made life easy"”
text: We had every thing we needed right here!! Room service was great! and The Staff was Friendly

title: “Great Location”
text:
Right in the middle of the city. From the entrance, if you point to the right (facing the main entrance) you can walk to the White House in less than five minutes. If you point to the left, you can walk to China Town in less than five minutes. If you point straight, on the next block you have a two floor "Forever 21 store," which my daughter loved. Feel like seeing some wax characters that look so real that it is just creepy? Well, that's across Forever 21. Other places of interest within five minutes: Hard Rock Cafe, Verizon Center (I hear tickets for the Wizzards are a bargain now that they are 0/8), Ford's Theator, the National Archives, and much more.
The hotel itself is impressive. Althought they are undergoing a $23 million renovation, we couldn't see any construction going on. I was dissapointed that I had reserved a room with two double beds and they didn't have one for us. The front office clerk (in training) told me that this was not guaranteed (which is news to me). Any way, they gave us a cot, comped wireless service and put us in a high floor, which my kids wanted. Problem solved.
The main living quarters of the room were clean and the room was large. The bathroom I will easily forget. The shower had a couple of hairs left over from the previous traveler. The grout needed bleaching and worst of all, the toilet had this industrial flushing mechanism that you see in bar urinals. It didn't make sense, such a nice lobby, proffesional staff, nice room and then this! No biggie, it certainly didn't ruin my stay.
One of my favorite parts was the bell hop. Professional and courtious. We asked twice for directions and he almost walked us there. Nice guy. Front office clerks were just as professional and courtious. 
And finally, I got a room for a Saturday night for $99 plus tax.

title: “Loved the Beekman - Old School Class”
text:
The Beekman was amazing. We stayed in a 1 bedroom suite with a great view. We got the room for only $112 a night last minute!
It is not located in the centre of tourist Manhatten but I found this refreshing. After staying near Times Square and participating in the tourist life it was nice to come across to what felt like a more residential area. The restaurants nearby were quaint and we felt it was a very safe area. An enjoyable stay and a great end to a NY holiday.

title: “SPG Platinum worst stay in Manhattan”
text: As an SPG Platinum member I receive generally good service across the board, and there are many SPG properties from which to choose in Manhattan. Do not waste any time or points on this property. It is only affiliated with Starwood - these franchise owners have not a clue about how to support SPG Platinum guests. My room had dirty carpeting, a hole in the wall. It was not an "upgrade." After the front desk refused to listen, I spent an hour on the phone with SPG Platinum concierge to move across the street to the Sheraton Towers - at first they refused since I had already checked in. I told them I would be taking pictures of the room condition and sending them to SPG Platinum, for a full refund of the night's points, unless they facilitated the move. Finally they did and I was in an acceptable business room at the Sheraton Towers. The Manhattan was like something out of a 70s horror film. Avoid at all costs.

title: “Hipster hotel that's actually a pretty good value”
text:
I prefer arty boutique hotels in big cities. The Ace is about as youthfully trendy as I usually go, but I was happy to see the trendiness came without attitude or problems (e.g. noise, discomfort, poor quality). It was very comfortable and a good value in Manhattan. 
Here are some specifics: 
LOCATION: Very good - neighborhood is grungy, but it's centrally located for lower and central Manhattan spots. 
RECEPTION: Almost too hip, but the front desk girl was friendly and helpful. I also found out that she gave us a better room than one of our super trendy friends, so I was impressed with that. 
ROOM: We were on the 3rd floor, which was incredibly quiet. Our room faced a central building shaft, but they did a surprisingly good job of making it as nice as the rooms with views (i.e. more windows and tons of lamps). Our "medium king" room was roomy by Manhattan standards and very comfortable. Only CON: the room smelled musty. 
BED: Fantastic, clean and soft bed with no bed bugs (I checked). 
MINIBAR: It's actually more like a maxi-buffet... we had a full-size vintage fridge in our room with tons of good snacks and drinks. We caved and ate the $6.50 cashews, which I'm happy to report were almost worth it. Nice, high-quality products. 
ENTERTAINMENT: Flatscreen TV with loads of movies, record player w/ records & stereo. 
OTHER AMENITIES: The usual basics (hairdryer, iron, ironing board), and some creative extras like sweatshirt robes.
BATHROOM: Very nice - rain shower head with bathtub; fair, clean towels, and nice bath products. One note: bath products were in large dispensers in shower rather than individual bottles. I actually like that (less waste; you never run out of conditioner), but some people might not like it. 
RESTAURANT: Dark and retro with a small, high-quality menu that features a LOT of meat (few veggie options). Go early or be prepared for a wait, and bring a lot of money. 
STUMPTOWN ROASTERS (coffee): Cappuccino was the best I've had outside of Sant' Eustachio in Rome (if you've been there, you know that's the highest praise). Very trendy (but friendly); long wait. at rush hour.

title: “The best place to hang out in a fun and relaxed trip”
text: The W Chicago Lakeshore made my trip one of the most memorable ever. The rooms have a beautiful interior decor making it ideal for couples to hangout. The lake facing rooms provide a scenic view to Lake Michigan. Being in the heart of downtown, it is close to shopping and recreation area. Its pub on the top floor is the most amazing part of it and makes for a perfect place to end the day in fun and frolic.

title: “Loved the amenities!”
text: On a recent business trip to Autin, I had my choice of staying at another local Hotel or at the Hampton Inn-Arboretum. When I called the other Hotel they were going to charge me the "week-end" although I wasn't showing up at the Hotel on Sunday until later in the evening. When I called the Hampton Inn, They quoted me the "week-day" rate even on a Sunday. My decision was made to stay at the Hampton Inn-Arboretum. When I arrived, the lobby was very clean, well put together and inviting. They had a coffee "buffet" that looked very appetizing. I dont drink coffee but it was so impressive, I did my entire stay! The staff was very friendly and accomodating. My room was very clean and comfortable. I did arrive hungry and to my surprise they do not offer room service however, the staff alerted me to a nice restaurant and fast food location within walking distance of the Hotel. I found the work-out facility to be amazing. Everything I needed to complete my routine as if I was at the gym! I was going to be staying a few days so I alerted the house cleaning crew and informed them they did not have to make my bed or give me new towels. However, every day my bed was made and I had fresh towels. Upon leaving I was asked if I wanted to enroll in the HHonors rewards program. THis would entitle me to gain points to stay at another like Hotel in the future at a discount. I did and have been receiving e-mails regarding points, PIN#'s and everything I need to sign up. I am going to be going to Columbus GA in December and plan on redeeming my points and staying at the Hampton Inn near the airport. Thank-you for a wonderful experience! Oh and by-the-way....the complimentary breakfast was amazing. Very well put together. I'm all about presentation. And the food was good too!!!!

title: “Comfortable, but restaurant undergoing renovations”
text: We stayed at the crowne plaza for 2 nights prior to a cruise. The hotel is attractive and the rooms are comfortable. Location is about 1 mile from the airport, but not in an area where you can walk to other things (near intersection of two busy highways). the restaurant was undergoing renovations, so the menu was limited, but food was ok. this lack of a more significant menu prevents me from rating the hotel higher. I believe the restaurant renovations will be done in May. all in all, a reasonable choice for an overnight stay in Jacksonville with a flight or cruise the next day.

title: “Location is Great!”
text: We arrived at the Lindberg airport, took a taxi to hotel. Taxi cost about $12-$15 depending on taxi. Supper Shuttle is $8.00. Hotel is about 10 to15 minutes from airport. Hilton Gaslamp is located at the entrance to the Historical Gaslamp District. Check in went smooth, staff friendly. Hotel is like a boutique hotel with 12 floors. Rooms have been re done, (bed comfortable) as the Hilton Gaslamp was built in 2000.There is Spa attached to the hotel called Artisan, hotel has a small swimming pool, fitness room. An upscale restaurant is right next to the Hotel. There is a nice outdoor sitting area across from the entrance to the hotel. Free internet in the rooms, buffet breakfast or traditional breakfast served in the New Leaf Restaurant. There is also a happy hour with free snacks and I think half price drinks. Hotel does not have an Executive Floor, but you get free breakfast coupons to compensate. Hotel is located within walking distant to many restaurants and bars. Close to Petco Park, and across the street from the convention center. You can purchase Trolley City tour tickets from the concierge for $34.00 at trolley station for $30.00 Trolley (tour is very enjoyable). Hop on and hop off. Yes the train tracks do run across from the hotel, but sound of the train did not bother us. I want to say a special thanks to Melody and Tiffany for their wonderful “Hilton Hospitality”. Yes! I would stay here again! P. S. I have also stayed at the Hilton Bayfront and can compare. I like the Hilton Gaslamp because the people are warmer and willing to help. Hotel is cozy. Hilton Bayfront is a high rise Convention Hotel. Staff does not exhibit a warm hospitality. There are charges for every little thing. While it is a newer hotel (maybe 2 or3 years old), to me it was not constructed with the average tourist in mind. It is clearly for business and convention goers with expense accounts who do not mind the extra charges.

title: “Okay... Great location for convention center”
text:
I would stay here only if I have another convention in the convention center. Otherwise the Marriott in Union Square is nicer. 
Pros: 
- 2 blocks from convention center.
- close to some great restaurants.
- comfortable beds and linins
- Starbucks in the lobby
Cons:
-Dark bathrooms
- Over price breakfast, $20 for the breakfast buffet. Even if you only get a yogurt and fruit.

title: “Nice and cozy, good Location”
text: If you are have a trade show at the convention center accross the street, then this is the place to stay. Nice Boutique hotel. Small rooms but cozy and clean. The bathroom are big and I would stay there again. Nice little bar too.

title: “Swanky!”
text:
Sixty is in a great location in Soho - near a number of great shopping, bars, and restaurants. It also has a few restaurants/bars of its own. However, you must use your room key to access different floors with rooms so it is very safe despite a number of people trekking in and out.
The front desk staff in the lobby is unpleasant, bu the gentlemen downstairs at the door are extremely kind and welcoming. Housekeeping is also great and leave "treats" around like brownies. The hotel also uses Keihl's bathroom products, which if your a beauty product snob you'll appreciate ;)
The boutique hotel's decor is "swanky", trendy, romantic, but dark. Beds are very comfortable - had a great nights sleep. The walls are a bit thin so you can hear the smallest of noises which may be a concern if you are staying here on the weekends when the bars are happening. I would stay here again for its reasonable price given the area.

title: “Wall to Wall Elvis”
text: I have just returned from Heartbreak Hotel. My son and I thoroughly enjoyed our stay. It was just what we wanted, very close to Graceland, and just 'wall to wall Elvis' O.K. it isn't a 5star rating, but everything was clean and just as you would expect for the sixties, which it depicts. The staff were very friendly and helpful. If someone picked up my CD that i bought at Sun city studios of the 4 entertainers I hope you enjoy it or send it back.

title: “always very good and i'll be back”
text:
I have been staying at the Comfort Inn North once every week or two for the past eight months when attending classes at Ohio State University. My stays here have been consistently very good. There are many other hotels in the area in a similar price range. I have stayed at a few of them, but i have been most satisfied at this hotel.
The rooms here are clean, comfortable and problem free.
The staff is excellent. They are always helpful, friendly and courteous. They do their work efficiently which is evidenced by comfortable experience of my many stays.
The work-out room and indoor pool never crowded. I use the pool regularly to unwind after my drive.
There are dozens of restaurants and stores where I can find anything that I need very close by.
The location is very convenient for me. The hotel is located immediately off of I-71 on the north side of Columbus. The free breakfast is consistently good and very convenient. I typically need to get moving quickly in the morning. Check-out takes only seconds and in about 15 to 20 minutes I am sitting in my class at Ohio State.
Like I mentioned above, I have tried other hotels in the area and I have found the Comfort Inn North to be the best for the price. I plan to keep coming back.

title: “Excellent!”
text: The room was great, everything was up to our standards, we would definately stay here again. Only thing I'd change would be the breakfast it needed more of a fruit variety. Other than that everything was excellent!

title: “For an elegant and stylish stay, try the Magnolia!”
text: From the greetings at the reception desk, to the gentlemen dealing with the coordination of taxis,the hotel staff of the Magnolia Hotel in Dallas were professional and friendly. Go see the Dallas Art Museum and new opera house. The hotel is terrifically situated for easy urban adventures.

title: “Great beds”
text:
This is an older Hilton and it shows in places but the beds are very comfortable and the rooms are quiet. Don't miss out on the restaurant. I was positively surprised about the food quality. Basically everything is good on the menu.
The hotel has a free business center with computers and printers that actually work.
On the downside my toilet seat fell off on the second day. The hotel bar has only 4 bar stools and the whole bar area is poorly designed. The free breakfast at the Executive Lounge was a joke. Any Hampton Inn offers a better variety. 
If you can get a good deal I would recommend this hotel for the excellent sleep comfort and the restaurant food.

title: “Great hotel in downtown Detroit”
text: Great hotel in downtown Detroit. Rooms are very clean and what you would expect from the Marriott. Layout is very odd and confusing in my opinion; views were great since I was facing the river and Canada! If you get some time, take a look at the GM cars on the first level. It is quite fun and free!

title: “Tk - Completely handled our needs”
text:
My husband and I stayed at W for our 20th anniversary. The lobby and main areas are beautiful. The hotel is very clean but we were surprised by the small size of the rooms. Also, the current train schedule is a bit noisy. 
That being said, we were treated like we were important and even received a celebratory bottle of Champaign to celebrate our anniversary. There were also gluten free snack options available in our room when we checked in to accommodate our dietary needs. 
Overall, we had a wonderful stay and will definitely be repeat guests.

title: “My 7 Days in NoMad Hotel”
text: during my stay the the hotel, stuff ware amazing, location right in central manhattan, subway ride takes around 5 min to times square, very close to madison square, rooms are little small, but it contains every thing you need, very clean, little expansive to dine or to drink

title: “Excellent”
text: First time at a fairfield inn.What a great hotel. I have stayed in 5 star world class luxury hotels all over the world and the service at this fairfield inn was equal to or superior to those! Perfect location in the flower district close to union square and the village area. The rooms are small but then again so are most NYC rooms. Rooms are very clean front staff could not have been more accommodating. My only "complaint" would be a softer bed. I would highly recommend.

title: “10-15 minutes walking distance from all major sites!”
text:
I needed to stay over in Seattle for a short conference in Downtown Seattle. Via the internet I found a great deal for a king size bedded suite for $99/night. The livingroom was spacious with nice chairs, a nice queen size sofa-bed, a kitchenette with dish-washer, toaster etc! Free coffee and tea were available 24/7! Bedroom was ok.
The check-in was ok, I arrived 4 hours early travelling from the Netherlands, but they arranged the room within no-time!!! Rooms were cleaned every day! 
Breakfast was okay (eg eggs, fruit, juices, milk, coffee, tea, bagels, cakes, wafels, cheese, jam). If you compare it to the Grand Hyat in Seattle it was far better in La Quinta!
The hotel is a 10 minute walk from Pine St, 10 minutes from the Space needle and 15 minutes to the Pikes Market. Public transport to/from Seatac is a 5 minute walk (direct bus 174) or a 10 minute walk (direct bus 194). You can transfer buses to get closer to the hotel (nearest busstop is 30 yards from the entrance). 
La Quinta has a small work-out room, and spa! All together I enjoyed my stay at La Quinta!

title: “Not so much...”
text: This hotel is in a wonderful location, but so are many others surrounding it. And, yes, it's very stylish and sleek, however, the service does not match the price. At $47 a day for parking, we were shocked to have to wait more than 20 minutes for our car three times. Also, while the rooms were clean, they are very small, and they didn't include a top sheet, which I found strange. There's no in-room coffee maker (there's too chic for such conviences, I suppose, but I'm not). They also charge for wi-fi, which I don't expect to pay extra for at a 4-star hotel. Also, the staff is hit and miss. Sometimes a doorperson was there to greet you, mostly not. Some were friendly and helpful, some were not. All and all, I would spend my money, time and vacation at another hotel. A

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Stay one night on your way to Sedona. The hotel was convenient to the airport. It was clean and had a good breakfast. The staff was friendly.

title: “Brentwood Inn is a pleasant place to stay in LA”
text: This inn is fabulous. A Brazilian architect updated the inn, which is a classic, and I like the charm of it. The staff is friendly and helpful. The rooms are immaculately clean and comfortably furnished. The bed was comfortable. For those who prefer more room to cozy, try the deluxe room which is larger and has it's own private patio; they even lit a candle for us when we stayed there. We were fine in the regular rooms, and perhaps others will find the bathroom too tight. I have to admit I am partial to the deluxe room. Some reviewers did not prefer the feather pillows--I honestly didn't notice since I use my Bucky pillow. The location is convenient for walking to Brentwood Village (10 minutes) or St. Vicente Boulevard (15 minutes) for a variety of cafes and restaurants. The neighborhood is pretty and feels safe. The staff will help you with reservations and detailed directions if you ask. For a reasonable drive you can go to Santa Monica, Venice Beach, the Getty, Getty Villa, Mullholland Drive, and West Hollywood. The breakfast is a light, continental style breakfast. The terrace, just outside reception, is pleasant and you can eat there or in the lobby. Available for breakfast are: juices, coffee, tea, oatmeal, fruit, danish, muffins, and whole fruit. WIFI is free. Parking is free. We usually don't have a car.They can arrange transport to and from the airport. There is a laptop in the reception area if you didn't bring one and want to Google the LA scene. I recommend this inn.

title: “Interesting but tired”
text:
My office set me up at the Congress. It is in a great location near the lakefront but the once grand old lady is tired. My room was quite large with two double beds. The entire room was very clean. The furnishings and decor were dated and needs updating. The air conditioner was very old and could not keep up with the high heat of the week. A ceiling fan would have helped.
One thing I didn't care for was that I was paying $189 a night and the hotel wanted to charge me $9 for 24 hours of internet service. That was unacceptable.

title: “Good value for your money”
text:
Moderately priced hotel room right in the downtown area. Across the street from the Main Public Library which is an architectural gem and within walking distance of Pike Place Market and a lot of other attractions. 
Nice thing about the hotel is that it is not an anonymous chain. On the down side, the rooms are somewhat smaller and it lacks the amenities of the larger hotels - minibar, etc - but there is a nice cozy feeling about the place.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: My wife and I were going to the Yankee game on Sunday night, driving down from Ma. so I decided to find a hotel in the city for a 2 night stay (Sat. & Sun.). After viewing many locations on the computer I called the Westin at Times Square and inquired about a Government rate. I'm a Sheriff's Deputy and often inquire about a reduced rate in our travels. They indeed had that rate at $214 a night (vs. $279) so I chose the Westin having not been there before, but wanting a central location in the city. We couldn't have been more pleased! The staff was friendly, answered our questions, and upgraded our room to a corner over-looking Times Square. ( a smile and being polite has always worked for me). This location between 42nd & 43rd St's was ideal. We taxi'd to Little Italy for dinner on Sat. night, ($15 w/tip) but rode the Subway all day Sunday, even to the big ball yard in the Bronx on Sunday night. The hotel was clean, roomy, and quiet overall, with the occasional fire truck siren in the distance. I was impressed with the security, as when you enter the hotel from 43rd street, your met by a number of bell captains who ask for your room I.D. before they allow you to access the escalator to the lobby( after 11pm). Times Square (1/2 block walk) and everything else the city has to offer is a short cab or train ride away. I recommend this hotel highly.

title: “Always will incorrectly charge you for something after check-out”
text:
W Hotel Seattle - This is the 5th time I've stayed with you, and this is the 5th time you've tried to bill me for something never used in-room after checkout. I understand the occasional snafu in being charged for something every now and then, but this hotel has done it every single stay. It is clear to me now that the hotel is scrounging for money and will try to pass off false bills to your customers hoping they don't catch it on their credit card statements. Shame on you, and shame on me for staying with the W Seattle for a 5th time.
Get your accounting up to shape with the rest of the world... until then, you will not see me or anyone else I speak with as a guest.

title: “We had a great weekend!!”
text: We just spent three great days in NYC and I am so glad that we picked the Holiday Inn Express Madison Square Garden. The location was perfect. We walked to Times Square, Rockefeller Center, Central Park and the Winter Garden theatre to see Mama Mia . The staff was very friendly and helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel to my family and friends. I am sure I will be back in the future.

title: “Great Location”
text:
I booked this room using Hyatt Passport reward points so to be perfectly honest I expected a standard room. I was pleased to be given a deluxe King on the 29th floor of the West Tower with an absolutely stunning view of the river and the lake. 
The room-size is what one would expect for an urban hotel, but I must admit the designers were quite clever in making this room "workable". The headboard served as a low room divider with a nice desk area behind it near the window. I very much enjoyed sitting at this desk and watching the traffic along the river. There is a small table on coasters that slides beneath the desk allowing for additional work space. I also wheeled this table around and near the bed to hold room service while watching television.
There is a nice comfortable easy chair with ottoman, an additional table, and two very small extensions of the headboard that serve as bedside "tables". The small round table by the easy chair held a living bamboo plant. 
The in-room safe had problems and I complained to the front desk who connected me to security. A young man came up immediately and worked for a long time to fix the problem, without success. He told me that someone would be up the next day and asked me for a convenient time. When no one had arrived a half hour after the desginated time I called again and someone immediately responded who worked a long while before calling for his supervisor. It was determinied that a new faceplate was needed. The repair was made and both gentlemen were extremely apologetic. I was able to store items in the safe. It is a bit small for storing an average-size laptop, however.
I had two breakfast meals and one late night dinner via room service. Each time the meals were delivered within the time promised (20 minutes, 35 minutes and 40 minutes were times given, but two meals arrived in 20 minutes and one 35). The meals were all very good. I also used the express take out coffee and pastry place and found the food fresh and convenient there.
As another author has mentioned, there are a lot of choices for food near the hotel. In-room dining is always expensive with the added fees that come with it, but there are times when the convenience is worth the cost. The in-room coffee maker would have allowed me to avoid the cost of the large pot of coffee I ordered with breakfast had I chosen to do that, but I agree with the others who complained about the mini-bar. 
I appreciated the fact that the front desk notified me that the mini-bar was weight sensitive. Knowing that, I did not even open the door. Normally, I really enjoy having the bar and often do purchase items. Having had a weight sensitive fridge charge me for items I did not use which resulted in my having to argue with the front desk at another property--I avoided the bar. I think Hyatt would be better served replacing the mini-bars than dealing with the ill will of so many. There are likely others like me who would welcome the bar and use it if they were not concerned about touching something and causing unwanted charges to be added to their bill.
And speaking of charges....I was charged a fee of $5 plus for receiving a fax at the hotel. It was listed as "Business Services". i was told it was there upon check-in and that I should go four flights down to pick it up. Before I got around to doing that it was slipped under my door so I don't know if the charge was for delivery or for receiving the fax, but I did not attempt to argue over it upon check-out. I have stayed at other urban hotels where I have not been charged for receiving faxes or packages and where free internet has been available. At the Hyatt, one can purchase a Business Plan, but the plan packages Internet service and a continental breakfast and newspaper as part of the plan. I did not purchase the plan but the newspaper arrived daily anyway and as far as I can tell I was not charged for it. I wish they would remove the breakfast from this plan. Actually, what i wish is that they would provide free wi-fi. I find myself frequenting coffee shops and other places that do provide this service and avoiding those who do not. It is increasingly difficult to find free internet connectivity at large hotels and is becoming much more easy to find it at budget properties. I woud rather buy my morning newspaper (as I do at budget hotels) and have free wi-fi. Perhaps we can all collectively say this loudly and eventually be heard.
I was at the hotel for four nights and there were at least two different large convention groups at the hotel during my stay. The hotel is large, but that fact did not interfere with my having a very pleasant stay at the hotel. The fact that this hotel is a convention destination really did not impact me at all.
The employees were all friendly and I found the location to be excellent. I have traveled to Chicago many times in the past both for work and pleasure. I often stay at the Marriott on Michigan and it has long been my favorite property in Chicago. This visit to the Hyatt is making me re-think that, though. The view from my room was just so wonderful--the Navy Pier lights and fireworks at night--the river and lake blues and greens of the day--that view really made this room stand out.
There was a robe in the room, typical Hyatt amenities--Portico soaps, etc.
I guess my only complaints would be the lack of drawer space and plumbing noise. There were a lot of hangers in the closet and there was a shallow and a deep drawer in the closet, as well as the one by the bed--but, I could have used another drawer. I was traveling lightly, but I still would have liked one more drawer. Also the toilet flushed nosily and whenever the person in the room above flushed the toilet or used the shower the noise could he heard in my room. I heard noise in the hallway several times.
If you can get a reservation at the North Pond, a restaurant located in Lincoln Park, I highly recommend that while you are in Chicago. Lots of wonderful places to eat, but North Pond is among the best.

title: “Horrible”
text:
I called for the van at 10:50pm. It didn't show up until 11:35. And then, it was a Holiday Inn van with nothing on it that indicated it was the Days Inn shuttle. Would have been good information to have if one of the two people I spoke with on the phone would have told me what to look for. Took over an hour from the time I called to get to the hotel that is only 10 minutes away.
The room was just ok, and for the money, not worth it. I won't be back.

title: “The worst room location I have had”
text: I have stayed at this hotel many times. This visit was the worst located room I have had. 3rd floor...No view. End of hall #301. I also had to ask for drink vouchers normally given. They told me they forgot...

title: “Good location for shoppers”
text: I frequently travel to SF on business. I'm not sure how people do there rating, but compared to other hotels I have been to this is at best a 3 star. Definitely not the most modern hotel. I liked that there was a fridge in the room and the staff was great. There is a lot of shopping nearI suggest using the stairs, the elevator is old and slow. I had one meal at the restaurant which was expensive and not that good. I ordered a hamburger with french fries. The fries were WAY too salty and the bun was hard. The bathroom had a shower and the sink was outside of the bathroom in the front hall in a way too small area (ok for me, but if I were there with my GF not even close to enough room). Ive stayed in worse and Ive stayed in nicer in SF, but this was a good deal for what i payed.

title: “Great Location, Good Service and Clean”
text:
The Holiday Inn has the location going for it, thats for sure. Very close to everything Fishermans Wharf has to offer. The hotel was quite, clean and comfortable. The rooms while small were well appointed and room service excellent. Front desk staff EXCELLENT. The breakfast buffet was the low part of the stay but it will make do. The parking is $40 per night which I thought was just crazy but after sight seeing and noticing other parking fees the $40 per night was pretty much in line with everything else in area. Parking is a premium in the area for obvious reasons.
If you want to be close to the action at Fishermans Wharf, this is a hotel I would recommend you check out. Price wise, its a great value for others around area with similar locations and offerings.

title: “Didn't sleep a wink at the Westin Detroit Airport”
text:
Actually, my initial impression of this hotel was that it would end up being one of the best hotels - ever. Decor is extremely tasteful and modern, while the staff members definitely know a few things when it comes to professionalism, and putting the customer at ease. Upon being escorted to my room I was told, among other things "we have over 400 soundproof rooms". I can tell you that I didn't sleep a wink. My room was anything but soundproof, located right across from an elevator. All night long, every time the elevator arrived at my floor, a stiking "F" ( I am a musician with so-called "perfect pitch") could be heard loud and clear.
 So - there it is - I can not recommend a hotel that claims to be soundproof, when it is anything but. If I don't sleep, the hotels star rating becomes irrelevant. The allure of decor and amenities can quickly fade in such a scenario.

title: “Great location, great hotel!”
text:
Located right in the heart of Denver, the Embassy Suites is a great spot to relax in comfort, and enjoy subtle luxuries in the hotel. Right from the awesome rooms, super comfy beds, shower accessories, to the amazing cooked to order breakfast, you cannot go wrong by choosing this hotel for your stay. Do it, and you will not be disappointed. 
The staff at the hotel were really great. They gave us good reviews for restaurants to check out, things to do, and places to see. 
I will be sure to come back to this hotel when I am in Denver next.

title: “Just okay”
text: Nothing to write home about. Seemed clean enough. Definitely no frills. Staff weren't overly friendly when I requested a forgotten toiletry, nor were they helpful explaining how to connect to the wireless Internet. Probably wouldn't return; just stayed here on business.

title: “Not a quality night of sleep”
text: The hotel is beautiful, has a great location and the staff is super friendly, but I didn't sleep well at all during my one night stay. The walls are paper thin enough that you can hear nornal conversations going on, even understanding the conversation if they are close enough to the wall. The outdated AC was set for a cool temp but the output was so weak we were hot the whole night. My biggest complaint though was the window. I love my room dark and cold, but they don't have curtains in the rooms, instead they have a pull down screen that allows a lot of light from the sides and impossible to sleep if you're on the window side of the bed.

title: “Simply excellent..the New New York Hotel”
text:
A wonderful gem of a hotel in a gray location. Easy access to my meetings uptown and lunch in Soho. The property is fresh, upscale, warm and inviting. The entire staff from housekeeping to the front was exceptional and acccomodating. They went head over heals to help in every way. My room was exquisite and spacious (no small feat in NY. It was both contemporary and inviting. Because the food choices in NY are overwhelming, I never dine on property. In this case, I chose to and invited guests. I am truly glad I did.
I have all intention of bringing my family to the Eventi for a vacation getaway. A perfect business or pleasure hotel!

title: “very convinient”
text: Hotel is located close to Logan Airport. Just take the shuttle bus outside the airrval terminal . Hotel staff is friendly and responsive.

title: “Julie”
text: We have just come home from US and stayed here for 4 nights. Beautiful place, but don't make a phone call! They know how to charge. Needed to ring my bank and was on phone for approx. 7 mins. When it came to paying for bill on leaving, they wanted to charge me $138 dollars. When I questioned it, the bill was halved!!!!! Still need to contact manager to complain further. Apart from that, the service and staff were great.

title: “Small rooms, dark corridors, not 4 star”
text: The Hudson rooms are, as other people have mentioned, absolutely tiny and those on the lower floors are ridiculously noisy. The corridors are always dark and anyone with claustrophobia of any kind should avoid this hotel entirely. The bars are lively though and the public spaces are attractive but for the money I'd definitely recommend staying in a more traditional hotel with larger rooms.

title: “Very Good”
text:
5 of us spent 6 days here at the start of Xmas holiday period, it was fabulous. Hotel check-in staff very polite, check in was not busy at all and as we had three rooms the receptionist went to the trouble of getting us all rooms close together, the only person in a room by themselves got allocated the largest room much to their delight. Found staff extremely helpful, obviously if you have attitude with them you are going to get attitude back. You get more with honey than vinegar!! 
If you are planning a short trip would suggest you get the first flight from London to NYC, it will get you into NYC around 2:30pm, more time for sightseeing. Loved NYC as usual but would point out a couple of thing. If anyone is thinking of going to Tavern on the Green (Central Park) for lunch - DON'T!! We went for brunch, spent nearly $500 for 5 people and ended up with food poisoning. Not good, they have a "just pack em in and throw em out" attitude, not what I would expect but at least the decorations were nice. If you are sightseeing you get a great view of the Empire State from Rockafeller Plaza observation desk, personally preferred it to the view from ES. 
Allow plenty of time for the return journey to the airport, especially if travelling back from JFK can take anything up to 2 hours from downtown to airport in traffic.

title: “A Gem of a Hotel where Peace & Serenity Reside"”
text:
Situated in the Financial District of the city the Vitale is placed right on the waterfront across from the Ferry Building on the Embarcadero. It is a very unassuming building that sits in the shadows of the larger financial towers to the South. It has an unobstructed view of the Bay Bridge and the Ferry Building. Street car lines were easy to find right on your doorstep as well as double-decker bus tours with pick-ups just a 30 second walk away on Stuart Street. There is also a 5th Floor terrace that is a nice place to sit after dinner and watch the night life below.
The greeting from the desk staff was warm, friendly and sincere and we were in our suite at the earliest chance. Now I should say this hotel has some wonderful rooms that are out of our price range and these rooms were on the higher levels were views were unobstructed. Our room which was by no means inferior in quality and did have a pretty good view of the Ferry Building as well as the street but did leave the view a little lacking. The room itself was very tastefully done in a modern Feng Shui in colours of Pale Blue & Beige. The bathroom was tastefully done in similar soothing pallets. Dimmed lighting added a nice touch when a soothing quiet bath was needed. House-keeping was excellent and we always returned to a clean and fresh room. The mini bar was well stocked but as usual over-priced. We didn't eat at the Hotel due to special dietary needs, so for breakfast we ambled over to the market where we found a Gluten Free vendor that met our "breakfast & lunch on the go" needs. Peets Coffee was the place for a wicked cup of Joe to kick start your day, in our case we people watched while drinking our coffee. The smells that wafted through the market place every morning were intoxicating, from the fresh breads, cheeses, fish and every type of produce possible.
In closing I have to say we did spend minimal time in the hotel because we were off sight seeing and doing the tourist thing but when we came back from a long busy day the staff were always smiling, the room was always clean and the beds were the most comforting and luxurious we have ever slept in. At no time did we hear other guests whilst in our room. 
If you like cool, relaxing and peaceful places with the city fun just a stride away then the Vitale is for you.

title: “Very nice but could be better...”
text:
I just came back from a three night stay at the Hyatt Regency for a conference. The newly remodeled room was lovely and the location of the hotel is perfect. 
That said, there were a number of areas where the hotel could make improvements. I had long waits both on check-in and check-out -- each time only one attendent was at the front desk and it was very frustrating. I was late getting to the airport upon checkout because of the long wait. Also, I went to the Business Center to check my email and found that I would have to pay $10 just to use a computer! I have never had to do that at any other hotel before. And, for some reason a small percentage of guests had newspapers outside their doors in the morning but the rest of us did not. The walls are very thin and I kept hearing slamming doors (I think because of their weight).
I would still give this hotel a high rating because it is beautiful and in such a lovely location. We also enjoyed the restaurant, Pisces, though it was very expensive.

title: “At the heart of Times Square”
text: I booked through Hotwire and was pleasantly surprised to get a suite for three nights at this hotel. The suite did not disappoint as it had a bedroom and living room overlooking Times Square. This would be the perfect place to stay for the NYE countdown as the location is excellent being at the centre of New York and it was safely crowded. The hotel was always busy so it's not a place to stay for peace and quiet. The staff was generally friendly although my check-in process didn't go smoothly as they initially cancelled my booking as I didn't turn up on the first night. After arguing, the hotel manager came and educated his staff that since my booking was fully prepaid for the whole stay, they couldn't cancel it. They then offered me a cookie to apologise.

title: “Parker House- a warm oasis on a cold, snowy day”
text:
Booked an overnight at the Omni Parker to celebrate a friend's birthday. Ofcourse it was snowing on Saturday and instead of leaving early we left leominster around noon.
due to the condition of the roads it took us three hours to get to the hotel instead of the usual hour.
Slipping up Park Street with snow swirling, slush on the sidewalks and the wind blowing once I entered the lobby it was majical. Beautiful deep colors and a warm ambiance welcomed us. the front desk was friendly and got us in the room quickly. 
Small room but very comfortable beds, a nice view of the King James Church in lights helped us to relax and get out into the city for food and drinks.
Good breakfast the next day, park house rolls, bacon, eggs and all the morning foods plus excellent coffee.

title: “Great Rooms, Great Service, Great Location, Great Value!”
text:
I stayed at the Doubletree Times Square for three days in August 2006 and I cannot complain. The hotel is large and we had a great view of Times Square from our room on the 25th floor. The service was excellent, the staff was very friendly and helpful (especially the bellhops) and our room was ample and comfortable. I've listed some information about the hotel below: 
1. Great Location: Right near the heart of Times Square (on 47th St.) and the future TKTS location is right across the street. There are also plenty of taxis driving by the hotel so unless they are taken it's easy to catch one as you leave the hotel. 
2. Great Rooms: We booked a double deluxe suite (there was 5 people all together) and it was very comfortable. The beds were soft, the television worked fine and we used the sofabed and it was so easy to use. 
3. Great View: If you really care about a great view when you look for a hotel in New York City, then definetley choose the Doubletree. You'll get a good view of Times Square on the higher floors, though, so remember to mention that when you are booking your room. 
4. Great Staff/Service: The hotel's staff anmd their services were so helpful and great. The bellhops stored our luggage in a safe place while we went out to shop before check-in. The housekeeping service was very nice and the staff was very friendly. And on weekdays a copy of the USA Today is delivered to your door in the morning. You can cancel that service for $.75 credit (but we didn't). 
5. Cons: Since I rated the hotel five stars, there is only one con about the hotel which wasn't too bad. There was only one clock in the entire suite, for those of you who don't have a watch on hand. 
Overall, I would definetley choose this hotel again on my next trip to New York City because of the amazing features. It can be a little bit pricey, even for two nights, but it is absolutley worth it.

title: “great location, but be careful when leaving valuables in your room”
text:
This new hotel has received many positive reviews, and upon returning from our recent trip to NYC, we were ready to write a nice review as well. However, one unfortunate incident has made it difficult for us to trust returning to this hotel in the future. But first, the positives: the best thing about this hotel is the location. We loved that it's not in the middle of something uber-touristy, like Times Square, etc. It's close enough to walk to some excellent restaurants and shops. The room itself was fine -- we were expecting something a bit bigger, but it is NYC after all, and space is hard to come by. We liked the quirky modern wallpaper and other modern amenities (such as the huge tv), but the bathroom was just average (e.g. avg shower, no counterspace & no shower gel). During our stay, the front desk staff was helpful, if not a bit harried and rushed from the high volume of activity . In our book, all of that would merit 4 stars and a recommendation to friends to try out this hotel. 
However, the day after we returned home, I received a fraud notice from my credit card company that someone in NYC had tried to charge nearly $650 in theatre tickets from an online NYC-based theatre company. This was on a card that I hardly ever use and hadn't used in six months. I stupidly left that card as well as a few other materials from my purse in the hotel room (under a pile of clothes and in a drawer) while we attended a wedding so I could downsize my bag. We put the "do not disturb" sign on the door, and rushed out the door because we were running late. Many of the staff at the hotel knew that we would be away for quite a while as we had asked them for help coordinating our transportation, and indeed, they were quite helpful with that. So we made no secret of the fact that we'd be gone. (Again, I'm the first to admit that leaving my card in the room was a dumb move. ) 
After receiving the fraud notification, we notified the hotel of the incident, and they helpfully said they would do an investigation. According to the management, the investigation was comprised of reviewing elevator videos, the official key card access log, and some interviews with staff. The management concluded that no unauthorized entry had occurred: only our keycards were used on the door. On our end, we did a lot of investigation and research of our own, and concluded that there is no other reasonable explanation of how someone was able to get ahold of that credit card number. Although we cannot prove it, it's too coincidental - I never use the card, it was the only credit card left in the room, and someone in NYC tried to purchase broadway tickets from a NYC company online using the credit card number (the card itself was not stolen) the day after we returned from NYC. Unfortunately, we can't trust that official keycard entry is the only way of gaining access to a hotel room: a bad apple who is going to steal from a room would likely know how to jimmy a locked door as well -- particularly our room at the end of the hallway when we were away for close to 12 hours. Thus, we are not satisfied with the hotel's investigation and conclusion. Still, we admit that it is possible that we could be wrong. 
We're posting this review not to be vindictive or malicious towards this hotel. Indeed, before this occured we were largely positive about our stay here. It's just we feel that our privacy has been violated; and in our personal opinion, the only reasonable conclusion seems to be that someone broke into our room while we were away. We realize that all it takes is one bad apple, and we realize that this happens in many a hotel. Still, it is never pleasant to have it happen to you, and we've spent the week cleaning up the mess of other potential misuse of other materials we left in the room. Part of the reason we are posting here is to check to see if this has happened to anyone else staying here--please post and let us know. We also wanted to forewarn future guests to be more careful than we were with belongings left in the room, even in this hotel which is trying to be and markets itself as an upscale establishment.

title: “Definitely not 3 stars!”
text: I selected this hotel through priceline (unnamed) since it was listed as 3 stars for $69. There is no way this hotel should have been listed as 3 stars. Two stars - maybe. As soon as we walked in the room I could see it was in serious need of a remodel. The closet handle was completely broken off, furniture was dated and beat up. The TV was not a flat screen (amazing how this signifies the level of hotel quality these days), an d there was grime and spots on the walls. I've stayed in the newer Wingates and was actually happy when I first saw on priceline that I had ended up at a Wingate. What a dissapointment!

title: “Great hotel, great location!”
text: The staff is friendly and helpful and it offers access to all the great places Denver has to offer.

title: “Quality makes the price worth it, but 2 surprising problems for a Hampton Inn”
text:
We stayed here due to its proximity to south Philadelphia for a hospital stay, not because of the airport. We were willing to pay a little more than other hotels in the area due to our past good experience with the Hampton Inn chain and the free wifi. This hotel is mostly up to Hampton Inn standards: clean, modern, quiet (no airport noise), good breakfast buffet and friendly front desk, buffet and housekeeping staff. There is a Ruby Tuesday restaurant right next door adjoining the hotel parking lot, so it's a convenient very short walk to a good dinner and salad bar. For air travelers, Philadelphia airport is a short hotel shuttle ride away. The hotel also throws in wifi and 2 bottles of water for free, a nice touch these days. Housekeeping requests were promptly addressed.
We had 2 problems you would not expect from a Hampton Inn. We did not get a requested wake up call, which can be a big deal if you're catching a flight. It turns out the phone message light would blink when a call arrived instead of the ringer sounding. Also, given the importance of hotel security, the deadbolt on our door did not work. A staff member checked it promptly in the evening, but said maintenance would have to fix it in the morning. Also surprising for a Hampton Inn. We invoked the 100% satisfaction guarantee as a result of these problems and to their credit, the hotel did not quibble with a one-night refund.
So my advice is stay here if the cost and value are worth it to you, but check the room phone and your door lock before you accept the room.

title: “Good room, convenient to Smithsonian, GREAT breakfast”
text: Very close to the Smithsonian museums, though not good for night life. I can see it being very good for business travel. We slept well and the beds were comfy. Free wireless was great too.

title: “Stay With Pleasure”
text:
OVERVIEW: as with all of my reviews, I rate the property to similar area facilities not class of hotel in one area vs. same class in another area.
Located equidistant from Love or DFW airport the hotel is along a freeway with minimal facilities around the property. Cab ride from Love was $30.00. Single building, public areas are semi Roman in design. Small Gym and outdoor pool. There is a shuttle service available about $15.00
THE GOOD: Rooms were spacious with soft contemporary furnishings. Large 42” plasma t.v. Work desk with plugs for high speed and additional electric outlets at desk. Very nice bath with some granite. Bellman at door on arrival. Check in flawless. Sound proofing excellent. Never heard freeway noise (room on freeway) or neighbor. Great bedding. Breakfast buffet in the restaurant outstanding and a great value. Excellent cookies provided during breaks. Mini Bar service, daily paper.
THE BAD: The food service provider for banquets should not be considered as a provider of a palatable source of food. 
THE UGLY: As there was a large (for this hotel) convention. The single in hotel restaurant was closed for a private party. Forced those without cars to eat snack food at the bar. No support facilities were noted nearby so if you arrive without a car….
BOTTOM LINE: This is a great business hotel. If I was passing through Dallas and needed an overnight, this hotel is an excellent value. The hotel seemed to perform flawlessly for the convention (except for the food) and is a very nice upscale, quiet facility.

title: “Friendly staff, hotel is stuffy, small.”
text: We stayed at the hotel from Sept. 1 - 6th. We ended up changing rooms three times. The first time was upon request because the view was of a brick wall and garbage. The staff gladly moved us to a new room. It was soooo small my wife and I could touch fingers from corner to corner. No room to even set out suit cases down. The city was very warm when we arrived (95 degrees). That night the air conditioning quit. It got up to 86 in our room. (Tough Night). Patrick at the front desk felt bad and switched us to a bigger room which was better but, had no air either. Eventually the air problem got fixed and all was good. A couple of other items that were negative was that they have no ice machines so you have to requst it everytime. The breakfast they offer is not bad although the restaurant seats the Casa people in a certain spot and you take a big time back seat to the regular customers, almost rude to a point. The lobby, restaurant, and elevators are not finished. Overall it's not a bad hotel the staff does try hard. They have a long way to go. I think next time we will stay elsewhere.

title: “NO AIRCON”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights prior to our cruise. We were told on arrival that we had been upgraded. When we got to our room it looked exactly the same as the photos and was the same as the description of the room so could not understand what we were upgraded to. We had booked the same hotel for our return from the cruise for 1 night prior to flying back home to Australia. When we checked in to our room we found that it was very hot and could not find the aircon switch. We phoned the front desk and were told that there was only 1 floor that had aircon (their deluxe rooms) and we were not on it (we now understood where the upgrade was for our first stay). The room was so hot that we asked to be put into an airconditioned room so that we could at least get a good nights sleep prior to our long flight home. They readily obliged....for an additional $40.
We are on our last leg of a 6 week tour through the USA (covering 10 cities) and this is the first hotel we have been in that does not have aircon. It is also the only hotel where we have had to pay for wi fi. 
I would not consider this hotel to be cheap either. We stayed in New York Times Square and paid not much more for a room, but included in the price was air con, wi fi, full hot and continental breakfast buffett and wine with hot snacks every evening.

title: “Great location and good hotel”
text:
The Grand Hyatt was an excellent hotel to stay at during our two day business trip. Everything was clean, the staff was nice, and the gym (additional $10 charge) was just as nice as my local gym. Valet took approximately 30 minutes to get our car during a non busy time which wasn't a great way to leave. The Breakfast Buffet was one of the best buffets I have ever seen and highly recommend it. 
Overall it was a nice place to stay with a wonderful breakfast. At Four Seasons pricing I didn't feel we received nearly as good of service however. If you find this place at a deal definitely take it but look elsewhere if you are looking for a top notch hotel.

title: “Loved this Hotel”
text:
I stayed here for three nights last month with my wife and adult daughter. We had selected it carefully following research on TA and were not disappointed. The staff were very helpful and friendly and the room was extremely comfortable. I liked having one of the 3 Cable Car routes right outside the front door but be sure to get a MUNI Visitors Pass ($20 for 3 days) as they are expensive.
I joined the 'Select Guest' scheme with OMNI hotels so got free internet and the early morning beverage which was excellent. 
All in all a great experience.

title: “Very clean, comfortable beds, great location”
text: We were impressed with our room (6th floor, 2 twin beds, air conditioning, in-room sink, toiletries and towels provided, daily service) and with the cleanliness of the shared bathrooms. The staff were all very friendly and helpful and the lobby area was very nice and very clean. We did not have any issues with noise, either from other visitors or from street level. The location is very convenient to subways and is safe; also very close to various restaurants, cafes, and grocery stores. We would definitely stay again as for the price and location, it was worth every penny. I only docked a star because there was little hot water on our floor. Having traveled through several countries I've never had to deal with a shortage of hot water at a hostel! But otherwise all was well. Free street parking but make sure you observe the signs (you need to move your car on certain days) - we were simply told parking was free and got a $45 ticket!

title: “Was quiet and restful”
text:
Husband is in the hospital in Denver so have been staying here on weekends. Front desk has always been helpful. It has been quiet at night. The Marine Ball and the Black & White Ball was there last weekend. Alot of people and it was still quiet. 
The young lady at the restuarant in the evening is one of the most polite young ladies I have ever met. With all the traffic in and out throughtout the week, she remember me when I was back for another visit with my husband.

title: “Not terrible, but still disappointing for such a hotel”
text: We stayed for 3 nights with our 20mth old daughter. The location was good, just a few mins walk from Inner Harbour and shopping, restaurants, Aquarium etc. The interior of the hotel and our room looked impressive and stylish, yet one evening, despite us having to ask a number of times, our room was not cleaned until after 5:30pm. Otherwise, the reception staff were generally helpful. The valets outside the hotel will park your car in a car garage around the block for a daily charge several dollars more expensive than parking it yourself in one of the several garages also located within a block or 2 of the hotel. We found checking in difficult because of this, as there was nowhere immediately outside of the hotel where we could park eaily to unpack the car and get to our room. Breakfast was included in the room price and breakfast tables are arranged around the far side of the hotel lobby, so there is no "breakfast room" as such. The food was simple but tasty (cereals, make-your-own waffles, breads, muffins, hot drinks, juices) and enough to start the day off. Our room was modern, had 2 big beds, built-in wardrobe, bar fridge, large bathroom, TV and airconditioning. The room was adequate, but not especially large. In the block behind the hotel was a bar that hosted music bands playing outdoors. We had a lot of trouble sleeping one night as it was very loud, even above the airconditioning. One very big complaint was about the cleanliness of the indoor pool. There was clearly a coating of green mould around the lights, which when brought to the attention of reception staff, was unfortunately not taken care of (at least within the 3 days we stayed there), therefore deterring any potential swimmers. Overall the quality of this hotel, and certainly for the price we paid, was not to the standard I would have expected.

title: “What a surprise”
text: A lot of the reviews I had read were not favorable. Wrong! The hotel is in a great location, there was plenty of free self- parking with in-and-out capability. The room was large - not elegant but large and clean. Service is a little sloppy but the front desk crew was fine and friendly. Breakfast was fair - ok if you eat pre-made stuff like cereal and yogurt. Hot food was not so good. Two minor complaints - I never heard of a hotel that ran out of tissues - no box available for the bathroom. The kitchen ran out of orange and they were out for two breakfasts. If you can't get the fountain oj, go to the supermarket and buy a few half gallons to get you through. I bought two nights with parking and breakfast through Living Social. Really a bargain. I would go back - and bring my own tissues!!

title: “Friendly, clean, brilliant location - would stay again”
text:
We stayed here for four nights on a trip to New York and loved our stay. On arrival we were greeted by the friendliest staff who checked us in quickly (it was late & we have 4 year old twins) and efficently and were help to our room by the loveliest man. We had been upgraded to a harbour view room which is just amazing. The rooms comes with a telescope too, so we had a great look at the statue of Liberty.
The room was large, clean and extremely comfortable. The bathroom was huge with a separate shower and stocked with toiletries. The hotel knew it was my husbands birthday the day we arrived and had left us chocolate dipped strwberries and a tower of chocolate with birthday wishes. They had also left us milk & cookies for the boys.
The location was perect for us. We didn't want to be staying in the (fantastic) mayhem of the city, so chose this area as it would be quieter but allow us to get anywhere is NY with a degree of ease and as the hotel is 3 mins from the subway station this was possible.
Yes, room service is expensive, but that didn't matter at all. Starbucks is moments away and as we were only staying for such a short time we were up & out early each day.
The hotel and staff are fantastic with the children. If you have kids, don't worry about it being stuffy or up it's own backside, because it really isn't.
We loved this hotel and would have no problem is reccomending.

title: “Convenient place to stay”
text:
This is the location to stay at in downtown Detroit, although the Rencen is still very difficult to maneuver and you will get lost several times while you are there it is still the place to be. There is a people mover stop so it is easy to get around town once you find your way to the stop, but there are lots of people willing to show you the way. 
The hotel is a nice property, the beds were very comfortable, the huge decorator pillows were a bit annoying, great flat screen TV with hi-def channels to watch, no “free” internet which is annoying, but the big Marriott’s seem to like to nickel and dime you when they can. Nice maid service we never left our room before 1 or 2 and our room was all nice and clean when we came back.

title: “Very Small room”
text:
Almost exactly 7 years ago I stayed at the Serrano Hotel and at that time I found it to be an excellent hotel which is why I chose to return on my recent visit to San Francisco. It is also a part of the Kimpton brand which is a hotel chain I respect. However I found my recent visit somewhat disappointing.
Firstly we booked into the queen room, which I mistakenly thought was the same type of room we had stayed in last time. This was not the case as the room was tiny with barely enough room to walk round the bed (and clearly nowhere to put our two cases). While disappointed by this (and I feel the room was too small to be offered by a prestigious hotel) this would have been far less of a problem if the room was well designed and maintained. The tiny room had large pieces of furniture in it making it even smaller, the large drawer unit containing the mini bar and that the TV stood on was so large that the wardrobe door did not open fully. The door to the room opened straight at the head of the bed (meaning it was noisy and light from under the door was visible when you were in bed) and did not open fully because it hit the night stand. 
Even more annoying was the hotels use of 'nighlight' style light switches in the bedroom. There were two of these located in the main part of the room at mid level directly visible when lying in bed. After trying to sleep with these surprisingly bright lights in my eyes for half a night I got up and used whatever I could (towels and toilet paper) to block the light as best as I could and then I could finally get some rest. It was also extremely frustrating in a world of powered gadgets that there was not a single power socket available in the bedroom (they were all occupied and behind furniture) so my husband and I had to resort to leaving our phones and other electronic equipment to charge in the tiny bathroom, being very careful not to get them wet.
The bathroom was small but again could have been fine if well designed but this was not the case. In particular the toilet was next to the door and but the Toilet paper holder had been placed on the wall on the other side of the room. Whilst the room was small this was just beyond the reach of someone with normal arm length without getting up from the toilet.
I find the decor of the Kimpton hotels general pleasing and cute in a slightly traditional kind of way. However our room had been very badly 'touched up' (I avoid saying renovated). For instance the wood trim was obviously tired and in need of a repaint, instead of sanding back old paint, filling dents and carefully repainting it was clear paint had just been slapped on resulting in paint all over the edge of the wallpaper.
I also felt that the cleanliness of the room was not up to the standard we expected. I found items generally dusty, particularly in the bathroom and dirty wine glasses taken from the wine tasting in the lobby were not cleared from our room.
The lobby of the hotel is however lovely and the check in staff very efficient but I found the wines offered at the wine tasting generally of a poor quality. 
In the morning they offer complimentary tea and coffee but when we were there the only tea on offer was earl grey. When I asked a member of staff if they had green tea he was very helpful and went to check but only came back with English breakfast. I decided to have the English breakfast tea (I needed the caffine after not sleeping) but then there was only half and half or soy milk to put in it. I asked again but was sent to the restaurant next door to ask them for some normal milk. The staff were again very helpful but it made the whole process of making a cup of tea very frustrating and time consuming.

title: “Cheap, clean and good breakfast!”
text:
We were 4 friends in one room. It was clean, and nice peolpe working there.
Nice beakfast with youghurt, bread eggs and cupcakes.
Just 5 minutes to walk to time square. Just next door too the bussterminal.
I want to go to NY again and I will look for this hotell again!

title: “great stay!”
text: This hotel was a great find. We were going usto the baseball game and we wanted a hotel nearby, we actually walked! The hotel was clean and comfortable. The staff was helpful especially the young gentleman at the front desk. The breakfast was one of the best we ever had! They had shuttle service both to the harbor and to the ballpark. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great surprise on the upper West Side”
text: This hotel has some of the biggest rooms in Manhattan. And its light and clean and under-priced for what you get. Great neighborhood. If they have space, this is where I want to stay in the city.

title: “Wonderful Stay!”
text:
We stayed at the Eventi Hotel from January 6-9 and had a wonderful time. We got to the hotel at 11am and was fully prepare to just leave our luggage there but they were able to check us in no questions asked. Our room was on the 16th floor with an amazing city view (and the Empire State Building). The bathroom was really spacious with a nice rain shower. The bed was super comfortable like others have mentioned. 
Service was excellent- twice we asked housekeeping to bring something up for us and both times they were fast and super friendly. Wine hour was a plus too. They made sure that your wine glass nothing goes empty. 
Location- It was really close to Penn Station and a couple of subway lines. I mean you're not paying for prime real estate in NYC - it's not trendy or lined with restaurants but it's definitely convenient. 
Overall, great hotel and I would hesitate to recommend it. The hotel contributed to my amazing trip in NYC.

title: “Great location”
text: The location is great, you are right in the heart of New York, you can pretty much walk to wherever you need to go. Rooms are clean and cosy.

title: “Loved this hotel”
text: Traveling to Myrtle Beach, Stopped here for a visit. This hotel was a real pleasure...wonderful reception, delightful staff, and very clean....refreshing charm throughout the hotel.....convenient location...loved our stay!!! Best value in uptown Charlotte!!!

title: “nice hotel!”
text:
we went on a school trip to new york and stayed at the edison hotel for 4nights, and it was great! we were on the fourth floor. 4 of us shared a room, there wasnt loads of space but it was big enough AND 2 of them were messy!! last 2 nights there was 6 of us sharing the room,(yes 6) and there was still room!
wonderful location, right in the middle of times square, and not to far from our main attractions.
the bathroom was really small and could do with abit of bleach as there was dirt round the taps, but the shower was powerful and there was hot and cold water!
the deli downstairs was really inexpensive and served us really quickly so i recommend that! also the little shop next door had everything you needed.
i didnt come across the bell boys or staff at the front desk so we cant commment on that!
we would stay there again and recommend it! all in all it was great!

title: “Cheers Boston Hilton”
text:
I spent a week in Boston during September 2011, with wife and my elderly mother, for a break and to visit distant relatives. Easy access by taxi from airport, although room not ready, it was before check-in time, staff at reception very helpful, using their advice, we went for a walk around general area, to get our bearings.
We were given a large, quiet suite, clean and although decor could be described as 'tired' no problems or need to seek a move. Hotel location was ideal, convenient to the shops and many bars/restaurants, with Quincy Market and quay area (where most of the tram tours are located) a short walk away, likewise with Boston Common. 
Staff at hotel were extremely helpful, especially the concierge team, with advice, especially on locations and how best to visit, decided to hire a car, all sorted virtually over the phone and delivered to the hotel.
Overall service was good; easy check-in and check-out, recommend if staying over in Boston.

title: “Nice place if you get a deal”
text: For the price I was not really super impressed. Our room was was an ok size, something I would think of as really great in Europe, but a little small in the US, even in a big city. Check out was sort of a nightmare. It took nearly 40 minutes to get our car out of valet.The food in the restaurant was pretty good and the staff in the restaurant was great when you could get them. We were at our table for over 20 minutes before we even got water. And another 20 minutes between the waiter describing the menu and until we could order. The location was really good for Michigan Ave. shopping.

title: “Great experience, Priorityclub members treated well”
text: We enjoyed our two day stay at the Crowne Plaza near Sugar Land. The rooms were spacious and the beds were very comfortable. The breakfast buffet was well stocked and tasty and the waitstaff were always there to help. Our checkin experience was prompt and accurate. They also provided parking right out the front door for Priorityclub members along with a little gift bag at checkin. We will be back.

title: “If you like traditional hotels, then you will love this one!”
text:
We have just returned from our first trip to New York and we stayed at this hotel for 3 nights. It is more expensive than other hotels but it well worth it!
We got a special romantic package deal, which cost $500 per night, which included continental breakfast in the restaurant and a horse & carriage ride in Central Park. We also got expensive chocolates and fresh flowers in our room!
The room was fantastic - loads of space, lovely furniture including a huge comfy bed. The bathroom was also lovely and the toiletries supplied were the best I have ever come across in a hotel! 
The staff were very friendly and helpful at all times - there is always someone close by to help with luggage, doors, directions etc. 
The hotel restuarant was quite expensive, hence expensive room service food. However, the food is fantastic and the service from the staff is excellent. 
I liked the additional items which were available on room service - such as painkillers, antihistamine etc, as well as snacks and other essentials useful if you are caught short.
The location is fantastic - right across the road from Central Park - although we felt that there was not much to do in the evenings in this area of the city.
The only bad points were the view from the room (we were on the 5th floor at the back of the hotel - I think this is the cheap rooms!), and the noisy air conditioning!!

title: “perfect for us”
text: we stayed at the dolphin for five days. It was ten minutes from sunset cliff beach. it was very close to everything we wanted to see. The owner even drove us down to get a rental car. The night clerk suggested pizza nova the lamb shanks were to die for. Point Loma seafood was very good and just across the street. It is a very quiet location. We took the ferry to corondo island and ate at tartine the mussels were fantastic also homemade passion fruit sorbet,so good we went back for breakfast.on Shelter island drive is a deli at the marina great cheap breakfast and lunch. Many surfers at sunset cliffs also can jump off cliffs. great people clean small room maybe not great for big family. We were very happy with our choice.

title: “Nice rooms, great views, location good for tourists”
text:
Stayed for 5 nights as attended a conference at the hotel. Rooms are modern and spacious. I was on the preferred guest floor and given that these were on the higher floors had great views of the hudson river. Nice flat screen Tv.
Location is good for access to the port authority bus station and visit to woodbury common. 
There is also access to a cinema on the lobby floor.
Given that its on 8th Avenue, its one block to Times Square/Broadway. Towards 9th Avenue, you are at Hell's Kitchen area and the restaurants there...however that area seems a bit more seedy in general especially at night.
Slightly long walk to 5th Avenue stores and Macy's at Herald Square.
Was a bit hard to get cab for meetings downtown and to the airport given that the hotel is on a rather quiet street.
One warning is that they charge you for your stay when you check in and they also take a deposit for potential damages which they credit back at check out. I got a shock as I got a call from my credit card co for charges of over US$3K when my stay would have cost more like $2K. Thought my credit card details had been stolen. Front desk said it was policy although later manager came to apologize.

title: “I never rate anything a "5"”
text:
Though I did not chose this resort, I will definitely return. From the checkin to the restaurants, to the conference facilities to the staff, from the conference setting to the comfort of the rooms...this was a 5. The staff was remarkable. One genuinely felt welcome and appreciated...by every single one of them. I was speaking at a conference where the podium set up, the food, the quiet way assistance was rendered, the acoustics were all good. My husband joined me for our 45th Wedding Anniversary. We were treated by everyone as though they had always known us and couldn't do enough. I've traveled for many years and have never felt so appreciated as a guest.
I

title: “Great Location, very trendy”
text:
This is not your typical hotel. It is very trendy and most of the customers seemed to be in their 20's and 30's. During the time I was there one night the lobby was closed because David Arquette was having a party and the next night the pool was closed because of a wrap party for a movie. Many of the locals come to the pool on Thursday nights to hang out yet during the weekend the staff made sure that I was staying at the hotel before letting me enter the pool. 
The location is great, right across the street from the Grauman's Chinese Theater and the staff were very friendly especially Kelly the concierge. Valet parking was $30 a night and internet was $10 a day although there were computers that you could stand at in the lobby for free.
