The only negative was that the people in the room next to me on the Saturday night were extremely loud at around 2 in the morning and it sounded like they were in the room with me. I did complain and eventually the noise did die down. Overall I had a good time and would recommend this hotel to others although not for families.

title: “From booking to checking out there was nothing but hassles”
text:
it started when i tried to book the hotel, i had a question so i called...and called...and called... no one picked up, just ringing. finally when the woman answered the phone she was uninformed and put me on hold for over 5 minutes. 
when i went to check in they had no record of my reservation and i had to stand in the lobby for 30 minutes while he called around. Finally i got my room key. Since the location of this hotel is horrible (ghetto pretty much) my friend was forced to use valet parking for his hummer. they charged $38 for one night and the man that picked it up couldnt figure out how much change from $40 and sped off in it.
finally we (all 4 of us) head up to the room. we get into the elevator which fits one comfortably and try to find our way through the narrow and stuffy halls. i open the door to the room and it just smells...reeks really. something between wet dog and mold. the beds were disgusting and you could barely get into the porta-potty sized bathroom because the toilet was in the way of the door. the vents were connected so we could hear our neighbors puking all night.
we woke up to protesters at 8 am across the street (not their fault) but since the windows were so thin you could hear everything they said. check out went smoothly untill it came time to get our car back. 30 minutes we waited in the lobby, finally it showed up. 
i just checked my bank account and they charged me $100 ontop of the $99 from Travelocity, it really been nothing but hassles. i wouldnt recommend this hotel to my enemies.

title: “Great family choice in innter harbor”
text:
We stayed one night between Christmas and New Year's just to enjoy the Aquarium and Science Museum with our kids. The hotel is in an excellent location for all the Inner Harbor activities, and it's very family-friendly. We had a queen suite with a foldout and were able to get a rollaway bed as well since our kids didn't want to share. (Rollaway was $20, well worth it to get everyone a good night's sleep.) 
The suite is not huge and would have seemed a bit cramped if we'd been spending a lot of time in the room, but it was comfortable for sleeping and had everything we needed. The evening reception and the breakfast excellent and added a lot of value for us. 
The staff members were very friendly and accommodating. They helped us get Aquarium tickets in advance so we could avoid the long lines. They gave us great advice on everything.

title: “Excellent location, modern hotel”
text: I actually stayed in Dec 2010 but I'm only getting round to writing a review. I got married in New York and stayed here with my husband. I loved the hotel, so close to Empire State building and Fifth Avenue shopping. The selection for breakfast is excellent and tea/coffee/hot chocolate is available free all day. The room wasn't overly big, but it's New York after all, and the room was clean and bed comfortable. We are going to New York again in Dec and I wanted to book this hotel, but I couldn't get anywhere near the rate I got with Expedia two years ago. Highly recommended though.

title: “Great location, terrible service.”
text: Our recent stay at The River Hotel started off wonderfully due mostly to the very central location of the hotel between Michigan Ave and Wabash along the river. However we quickly realized that our air conditioning wasn't working. I called the desk three times to report this. They did send up an engineer who confirmed that our unit wasn't working and then disappeared without fixing anything and we never saw him again. It made for a very uncomfortable stay, as our room was 80 degrees with no fresh air the entire time. Upon checkout the lady took off one night's charge for valet in order to try to mitigate my disappointment. I would have rather paid the second night of valet and been more comfortable for the weekend. The service was all very friendly but not terribly helpful. We checked in with many bags and were not offered help from the valets or the front desk with carrying the bags or offering a trolly to push them to our room. The price and location were outstanding, but next time I will pay more and stay somewhere more accomodating.

title: “Fawning service soothes the soul”
text: If you enjoy being greeted every time you get off the elevator, like having not one but two people on hand to open the front door as you leave or arrive, and expect not only a chocolate mint but the remote to be placed close to hand when you're ready for bed then you will feel right at home at the Hay-Adams. To maintain the sense that you are a pampered guest and not a walking expense account, avoid looking at the myriad notices in your room reminding you that if you take the robe, the umbrella, or the hangers they'll be charged to your room, that ice is available from room service at a price which does not include 10% DC sales tax and a mandatory 28% gratuity, that anything removed from the minibar will be deemed sold,etc. Just enjoy the tasteful luxury of your room and the fawning attention of the staff. You deserve it.

title: “OMG! Though not a 5* hotel officially this one offers amazing service”
text:
When I was booked in this hotel I was told "this is a very small hotel, very simple, and not so great but it should do because it is close to your meeting place".
Well, sorry guys but I don't agree. Though it is no Plaza on the 5th avenue in NY, this hotel offered such a great level of service and such a quiet room with comfy mattress that it compares very well with the 5* hotels I have been to!
Checkin with Robert went through very quickly and with a big smile. I needed to check a few emails and print a contract? No problem, free wifi everywhere, printer in the office.
I needed to fax a contract? No problem Robert was here to do it and for FREE.
Gym? check! clean, well equipped, large TV screens.
Room? Very quiet, bathroom just finished with all the amenities. Mattress and quilts amazingly comfy and QUIET!!!!!!!! I slept like a baby.
24/7 there is a tea/coffee area with a great choice of varieties + lemonade for the kids.
Breakfast is not your usual FREE breakfast: it has fresh fruits, fruit salad, waffles, muffins, scrambled eggs, etc.....
Frankly, this is the best hotel on the block!
Two thumbs up!

title: “Service is great , some flaws you need to know though”
text:
First , I want to say that I do recommend the Hotel. It is an older building but it has a lot of charm. The check-in was very nice and Miguel was very professional. I stayed in the Towers (15 th floor).
The good: 
Train station is very close ( from Hotel to Airport , it took me 30 minutes)
Location is amazing, you can walk everywhere
Very good restaurants next to the Hotel
They have an express elevator for the 15th floor only
Check-in
bed was very comfortable
professional employees and polite
2 bottles of water complimentary
small refrigerator ( i did only find it the last day though)
Bathrobe and slippers
Nice bath products supplied
The complimentary breakfast on the 15th floor was amazing
Big and wide hallways
The bad:
small rooms
tiny bathroom ( the smallest I have ever seen) 
You can ONLY be in the bathroom with the door closed or you cant access the towels, toilet, etc.
thin walls ( i did hear my neighbours on both sides )
have to pay for internet
So at the end , since I didnt spend that much time in my room , I have to say that it felt good to come back at The Boston Park Plaza. Everything is expensive in Boston but at least it was close to everything and the service was impeccable.

title: “Very nice, cozy hotel in Greenwich Village”
text:
I spent five days in NYC recently and made a good choice when selecting the Washington Square Hotel! It is perfectly situated half a block from Washington Square, and less than a block to the subway. The rooms are not large but are well appointed with European-style beds (double means two twins, squished together) and a VERY large bathroom with a shower big enough for a family! The front desk staff are courteous and helpful. The restaurant is excellent--friendly service, and reasonably priced for NYC. I opted for the full service breakfast every day, and wasn't disappointed. 
I was somewhat concerned about noise simply because it was NYC, but the room was completely silent! There were guests on both sides of me but I didn't hear a peep from the other rooms, or from the outside. 
In short, this hotel exceeded my expectations, and when I return to New York, I plan to stay here again!

title: “Great location and fine place”
text:
I was here with my girlfriend about 2.5 years ago and second time in this March. Already in the first time we fall in love with this place and it didn´t let us down this time either. The hotel is very convenient and nice but the coffee shop is the best. When we were ther in this March we talked there with Kevin Spacey and he gave us his autograph and best wishes to our holiday. It was really nice!
This hotel is really clean and renowated recently. Rooms are quite big and really nice. We haven´t try the pool yet but it seems to be very nice. We will be in this hotel in our next L.A. visit also!
Sorry my bad english. I hope you understood my point at least..

title: “GREAT PLACE!!”
text: I came to stay here for a couple of nights and was surprised at how nice and clean the place was. The staff was very friendly and helpful, the room was very clean, the beds were REAL KING SIZE beds. The entire hotel is smoke free. It was a great experience over all. I definately recommend it to everyone.

title: “Substance over Style - the Place to Stay.”
text:
Whatever wear-n-tear in the decor was more than made up for by the first-class attention from staff members. Everyone we came in contact with treated us as if we were their only guests. In fact, the graciousness seemed so unusual, I thought they might have confused us with home-office executives doing a surprise inspection. If we had been, they would have passed the performance review and received an A for cleanliness. 
The person in charge of maintenance made himself visible and available. The concierge was an ace in multi-tasking. Desk personnel were always out front and ready with answers and assistance. Even the dining room managers made their presence known at all meal times. Housekeeping never invaded our privacy or took over the halls in the morning. 
While the design of the hotel is a little different than most Embassy Suites, it appears it was necessary to soundproof the rooms from the airport noise. It didn't take anything away from the experience, which was a week's stay in easy comfort, with shuttles running continuously to transportation centers and the weeknight bartender sharing his wealth of Boston knowledge. 
These were our "hosts", from the first greeting and early accommodation at the desk to the efficient checkout and extended luggage storage, not to mention the shuttle driver's help with our bags at the airport. This is definitely an "extra mile" hotel.

title: “Nice place”
text: I like the place, I knew what i was getting when I called and booked the room. 1 thing and 1thing only, Bed bugs, I came back so bit you could play connect the dots. Stay away from room 301. I am glad I only stayed for only 2 nights.

title: “Do not stay in a room on the City Side if you want to sleep”
text: Hotel is nice overall; however, if you want to sleep do not let them put you in a room on the "City Side." There is construction and street noise that continues from late in the night and starts up again a 5:30 am, and continues all day (at least during weekdays).

title: “Great Location, Nice Rooms and Helpful Service”
text: We stayed for two nights at the Philadelphia Downtown Marriott. It was a very busy weekend with a baseball game and a marathon so many of the local hotels were at capacity. The lady checking us in was as friendly as could be. We were getting two rooms so she searched until she found us exactly the types of rooms we were requesting on the same floor. Because we had several Marriott Rewards Cards the check in took some time. The whole time she was apologizing for taking so long even though it wasn't her fault. She really seemed to care and made us feel wanted (rare these days). The hotel bar staff, room attendant, and concierge picked right up where she left off, everyone seemed glad to have us even though the hotel was at capacity. The only downside was the cost of the valet parking ($45 per day) but we rectified that by finding an off-site parking garage about a block away on 12th Street just before Chesnut for $17 per day. Overall the stay was most enjoyable and the locations was great for seeing the downtown sites.

title: “Free drinks in New York? Yes!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Andaz 5th Avenue for three nights in Spring 2011, and it was absolutely our best stay in NY. The hotel is located across the street of the Library, and they were nice enough to give us a room with a library view upon request. 
We had breakfast in the restaurant every morning, and the preparations are very simple but delicious -- and extremely unpretentious. We also loved the free in-room snacks and non-alcoholic drinks (part of the Andaz brand) as well as the free drinks (coffee, espresso, water, and wine) in the lobby! :) Would definitely go back!

title: “Gorgeous hotel, wonderful city. We didn't want to leave.”
text:
We have just returned from a wonderful five night stay at this hotel and quite frankly didn't want to leave. Upon checking in we decided to see if there were any upgrades available as we'd had a few unpleasant surprises in various hotels in Canada over the two weeks prior to arriving in Boston. We had originally booked into a Junior Suite but decided maybe something with a full harbour view would be better. The Concierge was extremely helpful and we ended up in Room 4140 which was exquisite. 
We had a full harbour view and spent many happy hours watching all the sailing out on our private terrace area. The Room/Suite was so lovely that we actually stayed in and had Room Service on two nights just so we could enjoy it more. Room Service was prompt and delicious - make sure you try the lobster on brioche!!
The bedroom was spacious and the bathroom a lovely size with a shower to die for. I can't thank the Concierge enough for sorting this room out for us at short notice, we had a fantastic time at this hotel and it made a really great end to out Canadian/American adventure. Highly recommend it to anyone.

title: “Great Location, Average-ish Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the ULC for a business conference also held in the hotel, so it was obviously very convenient. If I hadn't been attending the conference, however, I'm not sure anything made this hotel particularly stand out from others in the Chicago Loop.
The Pros:
- Location in the "Loop," next door to Intelligentsia coffee shop and easy walking distance to all kinds of restaurants, shops, and Millennium Park.
- Overall nice decor, tasteful, and "old world" Chicago
- Great shower! Marble walk-in with fantastic water pressure.
- Amenities like free wifi, hairdryer, nice bath products
The Cons:
- The "luxury" aspect of the hotel is a bit overstated. The room looks nice on the surface but is not very well taken care of (ratty towels, stained/torn upholstery, etc).
- Maid service is terrible, at least on the 16th floor. Things like tissues and toilet paper not replaced.
- If you face W. Jackson Street there are no views. on account to the office building across the (narrow) street.
In short, if you're attending an event at the ULC the hotel is definitely worth a stay due to the convenience and overall amenities, but if you're simply looking for a nice hotel in the Loop I'd recommend going elsewhere.

title: “Nice stay”
text: It was a great stay, nice hotel, and great check out time

title: “I was extremely pleased with this hotel.”
text: This is an all-suite hotel, so all of the units have a kitchen, which is nice because you don't have to spend so much eating out. The hotel looks new and it is very well kept. First we stayed in a small suite (it may be called studio or efficiency). It had a queen-size beed, an armchair, small desk/table, and full kitchen. Since my husband and I are used to sleeping in a king-size bed, we decided to move to a one-bedroom suite. It was very, very nice, because it had a separate bedroom with TV, chest of drawers, nightstand, table, and closet (and one queen bed). Then there was a living room with another TV, armchair and a queen-size sofa bed. There was a full kitchen and a large desk/table. Also another closet. The bathroom in both types of units was roomy and nice. I liked the laminate floors in the kitchen and also the color scheme. They have a shuttle that runs Monday thru Friday and it takes you to the Medical Center and also to other places within 3 miles. The staff is very friendly and helpful. They make you feel welcome and at home. If I could change something, it would be to have some units with king beds. Otherwise it is perfect. It is not a fancy hotel, but it has everything you need.

title: “Lovely hotel”
text: Great hotel. We has some issues with the checkin and the location was a little further out than we had hoped. This said, staff were friendly and the metro is very close. The hotel was beautiful and has superb leisure facilities inc outdoor pool. All round great place to stay.

title: “Disappointing service”
text: Great location and comfortable beds, but our recent stay was unfortunately marred by several service problems. Front desk staff didn't seem to really care about special requests (ours and others on our behalf). They provided an amenity package that took three calls and two days to get delivered to our room. A friend sent us a bottle of wine, but the hotel lost the card that was supposed to go with it so we weren't really sure who it was from. And on the weekends, there's no daily paper available (only the weekend editions of US Today and WSJ) and no NY Times on any day. The maid didn't leave hand towels, so another call for service was required. The only staff member who came through was the concierge, Meg. These were all rather minor things, but added up we didn't think the staff delievered first class service.

title: “A-MAZ-ING!”
text:
I was referred to this hotel by SniqueAway.com (pronounced Sneak Away) and was immediately struck by the beautiful pictures. I carefully read all the TripAdvisor reviews to be fully informed. Let me say that this hotel is beautiful! I planned this weekend as a date night/ getaway with my husband and all weekend all he could say is 'Wow!'.
Upon checkin, you're offered a companion goldfish to name and care for. Pets are welcome as well and the hotel provides pet toys and food to welcome your critter. The decor is incredible -- the ceilings in the guest rooms must be about 12-14 feet high and the bathroom is well appointed with Aveda products. Basically, you can trust the pictures - the hotel is really just as beautiful as it seems.
We didn't dine at the hotel restaurant (B&O) but we did go by to see it. It had a funny smell, kinda like cleaning supplies maybe. We chose to accept another TripAdvisor recommendation and eat at Vaccaro's up the road - another excellent choice.

title: “Great place for the money!”
text: I stayed here for 2 nights when I went to San Antonio to see my boyfriend who had just got back from bootcamp. I was only able to see him in the evenings, so I spent alot of time during the day in my hotel. I had the standard suite, which felt bigger than some of the the 3 star hotels i've stayed in. I loved the layout, it really never felt like I was in a hotel at all. They were very busy the weekend I stayed, but check in was very quick and curtious even with the phones ringing off the hook. It was spring break weekend, and I wish I had booked the room for the 3rd night ahead of time because they ended up being booked by the time I decided I was staying an extra day, I ended up paying the same price but staying at what was just above a motel. This is a little further from the riverwalk and Ft Sam Houston, but it is well worth the extra drive. Some of the neighborhoods closer to the attractions do not feel safe especially at night, but this place was great for a female traveling alone.

title: “A real find in New York”
text: I spent two nights here in late December 2006. This is a very reasonably priced hotel for Manhattan. I booked a single and the room with double bed and TV was small but sufficient and with a spacious and clean private bathroom. Free buffet continental breakfast was excellent with fruit (oranges, apples, bananas), orange and apple juice, yogurt, bagels, donuts, pancakes, cream cheese, peanut butter, jam, cereal (muesli and corn flakes), coffee, tea, cappucino.

title: “Centerpiece of a great vacation!”
text:
My family of four stayed here for six nights at the end of August 2011. We paid about $160 per night average from Expedia and were very pleased with the value we received from this terrific hotel in an awesome location in downtown Chicago.
Suite was clean and large and the private bedroom was great for Mom and Dad while the kiddos slept on the large sleeper sofa. Fridge and microwave were basic but allowed us to store & reheat dinner leftovers, keep cold drinks, and cook dinner in the room on several nights (purchased from the very convenient grocery store across the street and also the Trader Joe's one block away!)
We have had many free hotel breakfasts over the years, but this was sincerely the best we have ever experienced, both in terms of quality and quantity of food.
The location was so nice! One block from the Red Line which connects you to everything! Public transit in Chicago is top notch. How awesome to get the Orange train at Midway, make an easy transfer to Red and end up only a block from the hotel, all for just $2.25 per person. You do NOT need to rent a car in Chicago.
Evening manager's reception provided drinks and fun munchies. Small pool and hot tub, but perfect for the kids to fill time here and there. Pool area was clean with plentiful towels and did not reek from being over-chlorinated like so many enclosed hotel pool areas. Computers (with printer) in business center allowed us to research area attractions.
I would add some negative comments but there really wasn't anything wrong, except that our bedroom door didn't really close all the way (the frame seemed to be warped). We had a great time in Chicago and this hotel contributed to a good vacation by providing everything we needed, and more.

title: “Beautiful hotel, but a little noisy”
text: The hotel is beautiful and new; very well decorated. We had a room overlooking the pool with a huge balcony which was very nicely furnished. The Pool area was also beautiful. The staff was wonderful and the shuttle service was a great feature. The only drawback is you can hear EVERYTHING being said in the hallway. The walls are quite thin. Other than that, we really enjoyed our stay.

title: “Good, but not great.”
text:
The Drury has many positives: The hotel was clean, the halls and lobby quiet, a friendly staff (front desk clerk recommended a local place to eat that was delicious), and the hotel is in a part of town near many amenities. Though I didn't take advantage of the 5:30 Kickback, it is nice that they offered guests several complimentary alcoholic beverages. That's the first time I ever encountered that. 
The negatives are: While I think their evening drink service (5:30 Kickback) could be improved by having more than one beer selection and perhaps having some spirits available, my biggest problem though, was the bed. I need a mattress with some support and the mattress in my room offered none. It was simply too soft. I managed some sleep, but woke several times due to a sore back.

title: “Great Experience”
text:
I was very pleased with our experience at this hotel. 
When checking in, there were two people in front of me.....the first was extremely rude, demanding his car immediately be brought up and the second was simply checking in~~ but strangley rude. Never saying thank you or anything just grabbed her keys and stormed off. Despite all this, the lady that checked us in was extremely pleasant. I found all staff extremely pleasant and accomodating. 
We enjoyed the chilled cucumber water and hot coffee in the lobby
We arrived at around 9:00 and our room was not yet ready. (most understandably). We did the paperwork and we ventured out for the day. They indicated they would call us when our room was ready ~~ but we never heard from anyone. When we returned our room was ready.
I booked a grand suite and found it to be exacty that. Livingroom with TV, pullout sofa and wetbar with fridge and micro. Bedroom had the most amazing bed and pillows, tv, vanity area, bathroom had huge shower, but somewhat small room. (expected in older hotels). We didn't find it at all inconvenient. Great bath products.
Can't say enough about amazing staff. I ran into a "repair man" and told him of a small problem in room and he was there within minutes to fix it. Bell staff was also always pleasant and helpful.
Enjoyed rooftop patio.
There was a small market across the street from the hotel. (cross the street and walk down steps) They have everything you may want for snacks, wine, rum, vodka, milk, juice etc.....but although they were very pleasant...they were also very overpriced. Around the corrner was a market called Potash.....not spelled correctly ...had a much bigger selection & much better prices. (they had beer, wine, rum, vodka, ect..along with grocery items) It is a walkable distance.....if you don't buy too much)
We were also withing walking distance to the trolley. Great tour guides would highly reccommend. Tour guide Lance was the best and Rosetta was fun also.
We walked to Ruth Chris, Mike Ditkas, Harry Carry, Billy Goat Tavern and Geno's East Pizza...tons more restaurants withing walking distance ~ those are just the ones we visited.
I was concerned about some off the negative reviews ~~ but we have only great things to say, We have stayed in 4, 5 and 6 star hotels ......we were very pleased (especially for what we paid for stay) 
The business center allowed you to print free boarding passes.

title: “It was a perfect trip”
text: It was our ten year wedding anniversary and the accomadations at this hotel where wonderful.All of the staff was very accomadating and the room was fabulous.The restuarant inside the hotel had great food.The hotel was also centrally located to all the attractions we wanted to see during our stay.Our entire family enjoyed the stay so much we wanted to stay another night but the hotel was booked.I would reccomend this hotel to everyone and we will stay at this hotel on every trip we make to Baltimore.

title: “Fabulous location!”
text: This hotel never fails to please. We have stayed here before for the location right on Pacific Beach, plus great dining close by. The manager went over and above to make our extended stay so enjoyable!

title: “We stay here several times a year .... love it !”
text:
My husband and I discovered the Constitution Inn several years ago and do not stay any where else when we go to Boston - which is usually several times a year . This past August we stayed there with 6 other family members and as always the Constitution Inn did not disappoint . The people that work there are always pleasant and assisted us with taxi's , places to go and places to stay away from :) The rates are so reasonable and if you are a member of the military or retired , you get even better rates !!!! 
The rooms are clean & the ones we had had a kitchenette area - plenty of room . Remember to bring some cooking utensils - the hotel doesnt supply those .We take the water shuttle to Long Wharf and from there , you can go anywhere in the city. The shuttle even though is provided by Mass General is great-what a valuable resource to the community . We took it to North Station and again , from there the city is at your fingertips . I can't say enough good about the Constitution Inn and the staff that work there . Whenever we return , the staff remember us and you really couldn't ask for a better place, location and staff ! In fact , we are going for a birthday weekend for my husband at the end of March and we cant wait ! 
There have been some comments that the elevators are slow and there is no place to eat but we never had an issue waiting and there are some many great places to eat in and around Boston . Places near the hotel are Tavern on The Water - great views of the harbor and some wonderful margueritas ! Finagle Bagel will get you a quick fast bite and the shuttle picks you right across the street . There is also a conveinence store ( called 24/7 I think) that you can pick up supplies or get a hot buffet type quick meal and go back to the hotel . Parking is down the street and is discounted for hotel guests .
Enjoy Boston !!

title: “Amazing Time”
text: We stayed at Time for a bachelorette party and from start to finish we had an amazing time. The staff was friendly and extremely helpful, the hotel room was nicely furnished and the amenities were great. I will definitely stay in this hotel again and would recommend it to anyone looking for a chic hotel in the heart of NYC.

title: “Nice Property”
text: This is a former private club that was has kept its historic charm, but is now a modern hotel in downtown Seattle. Convenient to light rail to the airport, sports venues and commercial district. Property is clean and well maintained. The problem is a lack of attention to detail. The gym equipment is limited and had the same maintenance issues as they did the last time I stayed here months ago. So, don't expect a fully equipped fitness center, but they will give you a pass to a nearby gym if you want to go out in the typical Seattle weather. Bill was incorrect (and another guest was complaining about the same issue), and the room's internet connection was improperly installed and apparently had been that way for quite some time. If management raises its game this could be an outstanding property, but unitil then it's a very good choice, but not up to Hilton's standards.

title: “Free Wine at the Rex”
text: The Rex is centrally situated near Union Square and easy to find. The bedroom was well appointed and spacious but could have done with air-conditioning. We had breakfast in the adjoining restaurant once, but as it was a little pretentious with a limited menu we preferred to go to Lori's Diner a few doors along the street. The staff were all very friendly, especially the barman who was both knowledgeable and interesting to talk to. There was a free glass of wine each evening in the bar, which also provided some musical entertainment some nights. The lounge bar was a very pleasant place to sit and go over the day's events.

title: “Average Motel. Got a good price with coupon from book you get at Welcome Centers.”
text:
Right on I 35, so very congested especially in the morning rush hour. I though we only had that up North!
Staff was very polite and professional.
Room was average. Shower didn't work as well as it should (The shower set know was broken). We could only get a little better than a mist. We were on the first floor facing the rear (the pool) and was very quiet. I parked in the rear so I could see my car from the room.
They allow pets, and I could hear 2 dogs barking loudly as I walked by that room (2 doors from ours) But, we never heard them in the room.
We stopped here because of the coupon.
We were headed South to San Antonio and this room was on the North side of Austin, so we crawled through morning rush hour until we were south of center city Austin. 
If we had been thinking, we would have got a room south of Austin to avoid the traffic.

title: “Perfectly medicore”
text:
Staff fantasticly friendly. Room just like any of 1000s of other chain hotels and motels. Clean. Breakfast was not good. Greasy bacon and sausage and runny cold scrambled eggs. Only fruit was bananas. Watery juice. 
Big problem: only one working elevator. Sign on the other one was out of service and someone kept changing the numbers of days it's been down. It was up to seven when we arrived and still counting (14 now). 
Great location near the wharf. 
If you just want a regular room to sleep and shower no problem. Nothing special though.

title: “Very Pleased! Convenient, friendly staff, nice little gym.”
text: Great overall stay. Great value. Comfortable Bed. Perfect Location. Awesome Staff. Even better bar. The only 2 things I would change, would be having a larger toilet (just small in size), and the outside noise, which clearly they can't control. Very pleased though, will definitely stay again on my next trip.

title: “Restored our sanity”
text: We arrived after a horror flight from Australia - delayed 12 hours in LAX and also lost our only suitase en-route. The Sheraton was a great place to restore our sanity - very comfortable room, good location (attached to the Prudential centre and close to everything), and last but not least, free internet terminals in the lobby!

title: “Nice Place to Stay”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights. It was very clean and hotel staff was very friendly. They did take a long time to bring extra pillows. After waiting for about an hour I called and then again called about another 1 1/2 later. Other then that it was very nice to get away for a couple nights.

title: “Great service, lovely views, really comfy bed and brilliant location.”
text: Myself and my husband have just returned from a weeks stay at the Trump Soho, we booked the hotel totally based on the reviews from trip advisor and yet again we were pleased with the results. The view from our room was amazing, and the cleanliness was second to none. The bathroom was an excellent size with a large shower and separate bath. The bed was one of the most comfortable that I have slept in (second only to the langham in London). The bars, spa and gym were all what you would expect in a hotel of the class and the staff were extremely attentive and pleasant. If I had any negatives it would be the $74 dollar charge for wifi for the week and the exorbitant price of the snacks and drinks in the room. I don't mind paying slightly over the odds for having these items in your room but $65 for a half bottle of wine or $5 for a kit kat is rubbing it in a bit. Also if you are staying for a while, I recommend Amelia's diner one block south on Varick street for breakfast, you will get 2 full breakfasts for the price of one in the hotel. All in all we had a great weeks stay in the hotel and will definitely be back.

title: “Best Stay You Can have in this Great City”
text:
This is a great place to spend time with your loved one. The staff is very friendly and helpful, and if you rent a car they have a under ground garage. The hotel is located in the hub of Seattle's Queen Ann area with easy access to down town using the mono-rail system and the must visit Pike's Place market. Within easy walking distance of the Space Needle and some great eateries like Thai food located on Mercer and 1st Ave rated as one of the top fifty in the United States, and Peco's a short one block from the hotel. Order the Dungeness crab omelet and a 'El Diablo Mary at Peco's. Enjoy your stay, and by the way this is the first time I have taken the time to write a review.
Frank and Debra Gallant

title: “Friendly atmosphere, trendy, modern feel”
text:
The staff I met were friendly and well-trained. My room was large and well-equipped, overall I felt it was good value for money and ended up staying an extra night. 
Onsite dining options are limited but there are fun ethnic restaurants within a five minute walk.

title: “SF to LA”
text: Our trip was from San Francisco to LA, driving by the Pacific Coast Highway, so the Hotels were basically for sleeping only. We started in SF, at the Days Inn Civic Center Area, the main reason Free Parking... All in all clean, the room was good in size, 4 friends slept in 1 room (I´m 6'4" tall) bed was comfortable. The only bad aspect is the Front Desk, staff NOT very helpulf nor friendly.

title: “Absolutely perfect!!!”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Giraffe recently, and it was the most amazing experience we've had in quite sometime! Yes, you get what you pay for- most especially in any big city- and the Hotel Giraffe is quiet, very clean, has a super friendly & accomodating staff, and is in a perfect location. We had a suite with a Juliette balcony on the 5th floor that was just so lovely. The staff welcomed us like we were VIP's, and the complimentary cheese & prosecco in the lobby, as well as breakfast, is the perfect touch!
We had the best sleep we've had in a while, as the beds are delicious- I need to know what thread count the sheets were because they were fabulous! Ask for Ashley- she took care of our every whim and helped make this such an enjoyable vacation. The 1PM check out is so civilized, and that's why we prefer boutique hotels over the mega chains, and Hotel Giraffe exceeded all our expectations. Thank you for making our weekend so enjoyable and memorable.

title: “Didn't clean the room completely”
text: Great location. Attentive front desk. But the room was only slightly larger than the double bed. And the trash and stale coffee from the last guest were still in the room. As I arrived late in the evening, it's not like they were in a rush to prep the room.

title: “Fabulous hotel at a great location and a great price”
text: We just got back from staying at Sheraton downtown Seattle. It is on 6th Ave and Pike, so it is extremely convenient to everywhere. You can walk down to Pike within 10 minutes. The rooms were spacious. Hotel staff was very friendly. To our pleasant surprise, they not only comp internet charges at the rooms, they also have a business center where you can access the internet AND use their printers for free. We were very impressed with that. They had a summer special and we were able to get the weekend rates for $145 a night. That's a good deal for this hotel. We'll definitely go back.

title: “Great Place”
text: My husb & I were on business...The service was excellent , courteous, at the door, the desk, and everywhere. Great location by the Metro. Beds were comfy. Rooms clean.Food in rest. very good. There was renovations & noise until 5PM. But everything else was fine. We would go again.

title: “Wonderful Staff”
text: Our son had been promised VIP treatment when he checked in (due to Hurricane Sandy, he had to leave his apartment), and the room was not at a VIP level. I phoned the manager, Blake Augustus, who was extremely gracious and understanding, and she agreed to give him a 50% reduction on his one-night stay, as well as a discount on a future visit. I felt valued as a customer, and Blake treated me with kindness and respect. She and her staff have made me a loyal fan.

title: “What a surprise!!”
text: While this property may have a bit of a "vintage" look on the outside, the rooms where generous, and updated as were the lobby and pool area. But the most important feature was the balcony that had a view of the entire San Diego Harbor and bay. It was spectacular!! This trip was with my sisters and 87 year old Father. Needless to say we weren't walking as much as we usually do.....no problem, the hotel had a free shuttle that took us to the zoo, the trolly stop was across the street, and we took a fabulous boat tour of the San Diego Bay that departed across the street as well. Did I mention the complimentary shuttle to and from the airport? It was well priced and a great value!

title: “Good breakfast variety and pleasant, helpful staff”
text:
We stayed on a Fri. and Sat. night, May 11-13th with our 9yo. Front desk was very pleasant and helpful. I was disappointed that the hotel didn't have an indoor pool, but this was my fault for not verifying ahead of time. BUT, we were very happy that the front desk arranged for us to walk over to the Hilton Garden Inn right next door (it is a very short walk through the front parking lot) and use their indoor pool (with hot tub). That pool is small, but fine for kids not doing laps. My daughter didn't like that there was a lifeguard watching her constantly -- she felt like she was being stalked. I explained that it's his job to watch, but she still felt self-conscious and only swam for 15 minutes. If you are an adult swimmer, the Hampton has a deal with Bally's next door and you can swim and workout over there. Unfortunately the Bally's doesn't allow young swimmers (don't know the age cut-off). I believe she said the Hampton outdoor pool opens at the end of May thru end of August, but I would double-check on the dates.
Our room was clean. The reason why I didn't give it a 5 is due to inadequate space if you have kids. We had a king and my daughter had the sleeper sofa. With the couch pulled out it is cramped floor space. The bathroom countertop space was sparse as well. So you make due keeping everything in your bag/luggage and lining them up against the wall along the hallway.
Breakfast had excellent variety. Hot eggs with meat or potatoes, do-it-yourself waffles, bagels, muffins, croissants, oatmeal, variety of juices, apples, oranges, bananas, yogurt, variety of cereals, and coffee station with four types of brews. I was particularly happy with the fresh (not canned) cut up grapefruit and oranges on Sunday morning.
Lots of restaurants and shopping nearby. We went to the TGI Fridays and had a nice meal. Recommend this hotel unless you are counting on an indoor pool for your kids in the middle of winter (they would be cold walking across the parking lot.)

title: “fantastic staff with excellent service”
text: My wife and I stayed here on a business trip from the lsat part of May thru the first week of June. The manager, Rocky Mountain was nothing less than fantastic. Anything we needed he was the first to accomidate us. The hotel's shuttle van driver, Jose was the friendliest person you could ever meet. This stay was great and I would recomend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Great location”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Shoreham between Christmas and New Year's, and we were pleased at such a nice hotel for a decent price. The rooms were small but were really clean and decorated in "hip" fabrics and decor. I really liked the Bose radio and the modern touches. One especially nice feature was the hot beverage bar downstairs with complimentary drinks. We never left without a drink in our hands. The location is great; it's situated between 5th and 6th, only a few minutes walk from Central Park or Rockefeller Center. We never ate in the restaurant since there was a cute French restaurant across the street and Klein's grocery just around the corner on 6th Avenue. There are bigger, fancier hotels if you want to pay the extra money, but I'd definitely stay here again.

title: “You get what you pay for.”
text:
I didn't think the hotel was so bad - we got what we paid for - but my husband hated it. 
A few things to be aware of if you will be checking in late at night: The cancellation policy says that if you cancel your reservation within 24 hours, you'll be charged for the first night. If you don't arrive until after 9-10pm on the first day of your reservation (or, say, 1am that night, like we did), you will automatically be charged for the first night (on the card you reserved the room with, regardless of what you pay with). Upon your (late night) arrival, you will also pay for the full hotel stay (including the first night again). The fee that was charged to your account for failing to arrive before 9pm will then be refunded, but (depending on your bank) it might not make it back into your account immediately, so if you were counting on that money being in your account, it's something to take into consideration. Also, that late, the parking lot fills up quickly and good luck getting anything larger than a compact into the carport areas. 
The pros: The landscaping is extremely pretty. Flowers and benches and walkways everywhere. The pool was clean, lighted, and warm. We didn't test out the hot tub, but there were several people in it. There is a microwave, stovetop, and mini-fridge (that was very cold) in the room, as well as two closets (one large and one small), an iron and ironing board, and several shelves in the large closet. We didn't hear any noise at night, but our room was near the stairs (of which there are several; no elevator that I saw), and people were extremely noisy starting around 7:30am. The girl at the night desk was very friendly and efficient, and the woman at check-out was the same.
The cons: The hotel room is tiny. We are a family of five and while I expected it to be small, the room was exceedingly cramped. We brought a pot to boil water and it took over half an hour for the water to get up to a boil. That was somewhat annoying. The second night we found that if we started out with hot water, it took about half the time. The air conditioning was pretty ineffectual unless you let it run all day while you were gone, and our first night was unbearable as the room was too hot to sleep and didn't cool down until it was time to get up. The pillows were awful - bring your own (unless you enjoy lumpy bits of disjointed stuffing thrown into a pillow case!). There's no fan in the bathroom (there is a window), so it gets extremely hot and wet in the room while showering. The shower has amazing water pressure - it's really strong - but it nearly takes your face off and there's no way to change that (I listed this as a con because while my husband loved it, it wasn't great for washing the kids). The carpet was disgusting; prepare to wear shoes at all times while in the room or leave gross, black footprints on the bath mat when you go in to take a shower (ew!). And $6.95/night or $19.95/week for wired internet ("wireless internet coming soon!") - not a huge fan.
Neutral: As stated in several other reviews (which I read before going), there are long term residents living in the hotel, but other than encountering a few doing their laundry on the way to the pool, we didn't really notice them. There is a continental breakfast that I didn't bother to wake up for. Husband says it was fruit, coffee, toast, and mini-muffins. He brought me back a banana. Other than the carpet, the room was clean but worn; the counters, closets, and bathroom were clean. The bedspread was a bit stained when I pulled it down, so we just took them off completely and used the blankets underneath. The bed was bouncy and not the most comfortable, but not awful (husband hated it, too). You're only given three towels (again, family of five; that was fun), but we didn't try to ask for more, so maybe that would've worked. The tv is tiny, but we were on vacation and didn't spend much time in the room, so that wasn't terribly important to us. There is a locked gate you have to go through to get to the rooms (you're given a key to the room and a key to the gate/pool). The back parking lot is locked until 5am and there appeared to be a security guard patrolling the grounds when we arrived the first night.
Overall: I probably would not stay here again. The convenience of having a stovetop and fridge in the room was excellent, but it wasn't worth the headache of cramming so many people into such a small, confined space with inadequate air conditioning and no ventilation. If you need a quick, overnight stop, it's not bad, but I wouldn't try staying with more than two people for an extended period of time.

title: “Worst W Hotel ever... Don't stay here”
text:
This is the most disappointing W Hotel that I have ever stayed in (and I have stayed in many W’s). The lobby looks cool but the building is extremely old and the walls are very thin; so thin that I heard the guy next door on his cell for most of the night. The service was really disappointing, too. I checked-in with my current Platinum card in hand; however the front desk staff didn’t bother to honor it. They didn't even give me a Platinum sleeve for my room key. The bathtub was clogged and the bathroom had no towels. When I called to request some towels, they asked me if the room was cleaned (which was a bit scary as I just checked-in). The only cool element of the room was the bed; everything else sucks. I finally broke down and called the hotel manager; he didn't bother to call me back. 
I'm beginning to wonder if it's worth maintaining my status with Starwood when their staff treats you so badly. This hotel does not live up to the W Brand.

title: “Better than I expected”
text:
Just spent 4 nights there. I wasn't expecting alot from the Salisbury because it's in a city and usually you pay more for less in cities, however this hotel was really clean, great location and the continental breakfast was included in our deal but would only cost you 3 dollars anyway. 
We were allowed check in at 12 even though check in is 2 o clock.
Our room was cleaned every day. Go out the door of the hotel, walk less than a 100 yards and you were at the subway that took you straight to Times Square, 34th Street or Ground Zero. A couple of doors down is an Italian restaurant called Angelo's. Reasonably priced and nice food. It was perfect for our first night. Little Italy has a fantastic selection of Italian restaurants for lunch or dinner. You just get on subway until you get to Canal Street. Overall very happy with the Salisbury. I would go back there again. We paid €664 for 4 nights for the two of us.

title: “Great business hotel”
text:
So very pleased with the hotel. 
Service: Terrific service for the most part (except the bar which was universally bad). This is a "service inclusive" property, so you pay one fee and you don't have to tip anyone ever. I kind of like that, personally. Hotel staff was terrific. The event staff for our tradeshow was less than impressive, but adequate I suppose. 
Location: Good. Right across the water from the airport (although a $15 not-short cab ride), close to downtown. Not a lot in the immediate vicinity, so not a great option if you are a tourist. For business, it's great. 
Rooms: Big and spacious. Great beds and pillows. Only complaint there was hearing all the room doors in the hallway open and close all night - could use some sound insulation under the doors I think. 
Value: Room prices were VERY reasonable. Food and drinks, however, were really expensive. Free wi-fi, which is huge for me. 
Amenities: I did not get a chance to check out the pool or exercise room, but the photos looked really nice. They have an AWESOME business center. For example, you can print files from you room to a printer in the lobby. Just enter a code, and voila! And I think it was totally free. Other printing options too. 
Overall, this was an outstanding choice for the price. I would absolutely stay again.

title: “Wonderful stay”
text:
A fantastic hotel in a lovely location in Memphis. The hotel is located in an upscale neighbourhood 5 minutes north of downtown Memphis on the banks of the Mississippi. Ample parking is available on street outside the hotel. A short cab ride gets you to Beale Street and restaurants downtown.
The hotel is a boutique style Inn and is personal and intimate. The decor is first class as are the rooms. The beds and the bed linens are amoung the finest we have experienced in any hotel. Staff were courtious, friendly and efficient.
We opted to have dinner at the hotel restaurant, Currents. Incredible food and again the service and staff were second to none. Breakfast was equally as good.
A great place to stay if visiting Memphis.

title: “Great for Families”
text: Very positive experience. Our party consisted of five adults and two teens. We stayed in 2, two bedroom (queen beds) suites and both were clean and well maintained. Enjoyed the morning breakfast and appreciated the staff that made sure things were well stocked and cleaned. Check-in went smooth. For families, this hotel is a great on the budget.

title: “My review of extended stay north park”
text: I really like it here it is the best I have been, nice people to accommodations I need. Its very clean quiet and the management is superb. I want to say the best person I like here is Michelle she does an excellent job with customer service she goes out her way and I thank you sooo much.

title: “Over Rated”
text:
This hotel is just not ready for prime time. After booking and confirming a "large king" sized room, I was nonetheless, placed in a tiny tiny room with a twin bed. I had to call downstairs to complain before being quickly placed in the proper "paid for" larger size room. The excuse I got was that Hotels had forwarded them the reservation as a "standard" room. This was obviously a not true, as Hotels had sent me multiple emails to various places all listing the room as a "large king". In New York, you need to speak up to get what you've paid for, but when you spend $300 a night you should not have too. Had I been passive, I would have spent the night in a tiny box.
The hallways are way too dark, narrow and hot. Was I in a nightclub or a hotel hallway? The smallest hallways I have ever seen. No air conditioning could be felt on the floors, other than the lobby. The air conditioning unit in my room was on occasion, so loud, that it kept my wife awake. 
Plasma TV's are cool, but with only a handful of channels, no premium channels and no in-room movie purchases available, the Plasma wasn't a big deal. Like a Mercedes without wheels. 
No coffee makers in the room. 
Room service was inadequate. My wife ordered a large pot of coffee, and they only sent up one cup. Then the muffins came without any butter, jams or jellies. No one asked "For how many" room service was being ordered.
The bathroom showed no style, in fact, bland is the first word that comes to mind.
For the price paid, you can better at other hotels in New York.

title: “Excellent.”
text:
Drove to New York for a 3 day getaway with, thanks to my better half, a list of 34 stores to visit (!!) (yes, once in a while, you do have to make your better half happy and endure a new york shopping marathon), most of them being confined in NoHo, Nolita, TriBeCa. 
First note: front end/ back end staff are great, period. Whether its answering pre/post booking questions, on site helping helping you out with any request (e.g. do you have a Zaggats lying around? can we get a reservation at xxx?) they have managed to staff their hotel with qualified, friendly staff and that extends to the bell boys, buss boys, cleaning staff etc. Not much if you think about it but definitely a cornerstone to feeling good where you are staying.
Rooms: sorry Im low on cash and I just booked the regular rooms, which was very fine considering my better half was planning to book the NY typical dorm-room-toilets-at-the-end-of-the-hall kinda place. In fact rooms are gorgeous albeit not that big. you wont notice. bed is excellent, pillows are to die for, rain shower had the most freaggin insane pressure (which I love!!). View is superb, gorgeous 30's something french vibe, floor to ceiling window, facing eastwards and I didnt get a chance to ask the staff who the hell was owning that piece of garden in the back, ridiculous by NYC standards.
Location: if you are, like me, a tourist, the place is very well located, 5 mins away from the better parts of broadway, bond street etc. even walking to Chelsea/Greenwich is relatively done easily if you have the time. East of the hotel, 2nd, 3rd, 4th street, 2nd and 3rd avenues give you plenty of restaurants and nightlife, albeit definitely a student-ish area (NYU is just two blocks away)
Hotel Amenities: Gym: no time, sorry. Restaurant: very good basic italian dishes, the Maitre D' is weird as hell to my Quebecois standards, prices are reasonable for NY (about $100 plus two glasses of wine for a very good meal) and the place seems to be becoming a hip place with models etc... Hotel bar: hum, well, there's where i do have a few comments. Terrasse is nicely secluded, staff is friendly, cocktails are good. However, the place is a pre-night hangout for locals and the Maitre D' for the bar is picky (snobish according to my better half but then again this is a common NY complaint from foreigners) as to who gets a seat in the inside area or terrasse, even asks you to sit with others (which is fine, made some very interesting encounters) but has no issue having his acquaintances by-pass everyone looking for a spot and from what Ive seen get free drinks on the house. maybe they were celebrities, I dont know, I dont watch TV often. In any case, when settling to such a gorgeous hotel it is a shame that the bar's objective is more to cater to the hip crowd for $20 cocktails rather than the ''tourists'' who just laid close to a grand for spending the weekend in New York. Sad, the ''vibe'' in the lounge/bar area i quite nice and the terrasse is lovely. Also, would suggest they configure the seating on terrasse for 4 folks rather than the 8 plus they have.
Other than that, hotel is gorgeous, well located depending on your plans and staff goes above and beyond to make your trip just awesome. Oh and they have an umbrella in your room in case it rains likes in the hold testament which was the case when we were there.
Final piece, if money is no object, the valet park is about $45 a day if I recall properly. Else suggest you troll 2nd and 3rd avenues to the east for some ''don't park on tuesdays thursdays 10 to 12'' local parking. Worth the 30 min driving around and we ended up not even 40 meters away from the hotel. ha! 
All in all I will go back there in a heartbeat but will anticipate a couple of hundreds more for the bathtub and the view that comes with it :-)
ps: on the 12th floor free wifi was enough to read news but way too slow for streaming, ethernet jack please!!

title: “Friendly staff at check-in. Good hotel”
text: Helpful check-in. For us, a good location - only one block from Central Park. Clean, well appointed room but without a view. Most of the staff we encountered were very helpful. We booked and paid on Priceline but found hotel charged our credit card as well. Check-out person said he would take care of removing it from our credit card and would send an email. This did not happen. After making several phone calls, we eventually received an email, saying the charge would be removed.

title: “Paid less then expected for quality of room & service”
text: Great Value. I would have paid much more for night stay at this Best Western for quality of room and service provided. I think the rates are higher for their busy season but still Great value.

title: “We'd stay here again”
text:
We stayed here on a Saturday night in mid-April and thought it was a really nice hotel. Our AAA rate of $188 was kinda high, but this is a fairly new hotel right off Beale Street, so we splurged.
The rooms are big. The bathroom is wonderful....a "heavenly shower", separate tub, tall sinks, soft towels (BIG), lots of good bath products. 
There's an iPod docking station on the clock radio. The ice room in the hallway even has a door on it. The bed is super comfortable and we loved everything about our stay except the DRUNK idiots who came back to their rooms at 4am and screamed at each other in the hallway for 20 minutes. A call to Security finally shut them up. 
The conciege desk was staffed by two really helpful people...Joan & Rocky. There's an endless supply of things to do in Memphis!
Valet parking was $21, and we didn't eat in the restaurant. Instead, we took the conciege's advice and walked to The Arcade Restaurant. Our breakfast was just average (the french toast is weird), but it was cool to walk down Main Street. After breakfast, we walked to the Peabody Hotel to see the ducks walk into the fountain. Pretty cool.

title: “Acceptable”
text:
Not bad. 
Needed a hotel room for a 10 hour stayover at LAX and we choosed this one since it had a free shuttle to/from LAX. 
Frontdesk lady was not really a smily person, but she did the job. 
Room was old and tired but clean. 
It had a AC sounding like an Airbus under takeoff. But after a long flight we did not care. We just wanted to sleep, and we did. 
Bathroom was old and not nice but it did the job. 
Price paid was just ok for what we got. 
For a one night stay between two flights this is good enough.

title: “Don't Expect Fancy”
text: If you expect a fancy hotel with a snobby work force, this place is not it! It is a nice clean hotel with a great staff that made our visits to Texas Children Hospital less stressfull. We even had a van driver lifting our souls by singing to us! Maria in cafe was a delight always a cheeful welcome. Wonderful maid who never complained when our sick child had an accident and always cleaned our room early so our baby could sleep after hospital visits. When we checked in it was a pleasure to have someone make eye contact with us when we asked silly questions , that i'm sure they had to answer a million times before. We are still on our journey with a very ill child and will always return to stay here not because it's fancy, but just because it's now home!

title: “Below Average Experience”
text:
Stayed last week for one night. The main issue was that it was the middle of the winter and the heat did not work! I find this unacceptable. If it's uncomfortable to sleep at the hotel why did you put out hundreds of dollars? 
Additionally, it's not the hotel's fault but the pictures on tripadvisor lead you to believe this is a typical Embassy Suites with an open atrium with the usual greenery atmosphere. It's the first ES I've visited where that is not the case, which kind of makes it just like any other run of the mill hotel.
I will be staying at a different hotel on my next trip to DC.

title: “Nice for overnight!”
text:
We dropped into this airport late Saturday night for a Sunday morning flight on the way out of Austin. While a little awkward to get to (cargo terminal exit from the highway, but there was a sign!), but this was a cool, recently renovated gem. Lobby was beautiful and the hotel is "in the round", with the center area enclosed and a cool bar and seating area.
The room was large and the bed was extremely comfortable. 
I think the airport location was a long way from the 'Austin Attractions', but for us on the way out of town this was ideal. Very quick drive for rental car return, or they'll take guests to the airport in a free shuttle!

title: “Great Stay”
text: I booked this hotel through Priceline (again) and got a good deal on this. We usually are at the bottom of the totem pole when we book through Priceline, but these guys treated us really, really well. We were offered a free upgrade upon check in, the staff was very nice and professional. The location is okay, it's not located downtown (around 1 mile away from the center of the 16th street mall) but they offer a free shuttle which operates within a 3 mile radius. We used the shuttle to travel all around the city and didn't have to wait more than 15 minutes. The room was spacious and clean and pretty up to date excepting the kitchen. Add to it they have free parking too. I would definitely recommend Burnsley and it would definitely stay there again if I visit Denver.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: My work is using this hotel for a few employees for 7 weeks. I have noticed people stay for a long time, which is good and the fact they are gone all day too. They have done a lot of remodeling and everything is new. The TV is great! The hotel is quiet and very clean. The staff are all very helpful and professional. Great location and not too far from downtown. I highly recommend Homestead.

title: “Could have been a 5 Star Stay”
text:
The Copley Hotel is a wonderful place to stay and could very well have been a SOLID 5 Star stay were it not for the flat broken down pillows that provided no support for you head and neck. My wife and I awoke each morning wishing we would have stopped by one of the many shops and purchased pillows.
The Hotel is clean and comfortable with a Asian flare to it. Our room was a King Suite (511) and despite the pillows provided us the ability to relax after a long day walking the Freedom Trail or shopping one of the thousand nearby shops. 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a comfortable place to stay that is located just three blocks from Newberry Street and all the shopping one could ever want.

title: “My family and I had a wonderful short stay!”
text: Close to DIA, wonderful rooms, restaurants close, clean pool & hot tub.... We will return! Only negative, my 9 year old found it too easy to purchase pay per view without us knowing! The hotel gladly subtracted the charges.

title: “My new favorite hotel in NYC!!!”
text:
I had one of the nicest stays in nyc in my entire life at the recently restored Plaza hotel. In fact, it changed the way I used to feel about the older hotel. I in fact never stayed in the older one before, but remember going through the place. I noticed how they kept the main venues that were historic, such as the palm court and entry lobby, but they went to totally 5 stars with it. They use the fanciest materials wherever possible to do so. The extrodinary ceiling in the lobby is so impressive as is the hot new rose club. In the rose club, I couldn't find anyone over 40! This place seems to be attractive to the younger generation. The check in process was a breeze. Suzzane I believe it was, was so nice and kind, she went out of her way by being so considerate and did not remind me of the old, stuffy serivce that is very typical of hotels of this caliber. 
Then we got to the rooms, which were so beautiful. The hallways are also unique. You have to see the molding in the hallways, and the cool carpet. They are quite "hip." My bellman, Eddie was awesome, he told us how he's been here so long. Our butler, Oliver showed us how to use the high tech remote control, and the functions of the room and his services. He was again, like suzzane, who adds a lot of fresh energy to this historic place. I'd requst him in the future. The bed was ultra comfry as was all the other amenities. I have to say, although almost all the rooms don't face the park, the room makes up for it big time. The courtyard is so nice because of the soothing sound it makes. We kept the windows open just for this reason alone! And even then, it has the best location of all! 
I'd return in a heartbeat, altough I really wish the spa and whole shopping area and the oak bar was complete. This place also needs to work on improving the service in the champagne bar with being more like the st. regis's bar when it comes to service. I'm sure this will take place given that this place is recently re-opening. 
All in all, were be back before you know it! Thank god I don't live very far from the place!

title: “GOOD VALUE IN EXPENSIVE CITY”
text:
I chose this place because of location, proximity to public transport, value, and because I had never stayed in North Beach. It was a great choice! Google maps failed me (I came into SF via the GG Bridge) but since I lived in SF 30 years ago I thought I could find the motel anyway - which I did. 
Room was spacious with huge bed, wide- screen TV, and a small balcony with pigeons and pigeon poop (I asked for the 3rd floor) that looked up and down Columbusand had a great view of Coit Tower. The room was very clean and quiet - the only noise was once during the night when firetrucks went roaring down the street. Other than that, not a peep. The hotel clerk on duty was neither helpful nor unhelpful - he didn't volunteer anything, just chcked me in. But I am not looking for hotel staff to be my best friend, so I don't really care one way or the other.
I left my car in the (really teeny) free parking garage and took public transportation or walked. 
I loved that pretty much anything a tourist could want was within very easy walking distance. Convenient to Beach Blanket Babylon, Fisherman's Wharf, Aquatic Park, etc.
This is a place I will be staying at again.

title: “Great value for money”
text: We spent 4 nights there and loved it. The rooms were spacious and clean and the staff were friendly and accommodating. I would highly recommend this place...

title: “Very nice!”
text:
Lovely stay at the Kyoto Grand. The room was quiet, the views were fabulous and the amenities great. Very clean, no smelly smells, nice TV and comfortable bed. The water pressure in the shower was a bit weak and the tub a little small but I still give it 5 stars for a quiet room at night for a good night's sleep. I would definitely come back here to stay. The location was great, walking distance to the Geffen, MOCA and JANM as well as plenty of places to eat nearby. Free wifi at Starbucks downstairs. Lots of cops around since it is just a half block from LAPD HQ. Parking next door under Weller Place is cheaper than the hotel valet. We paid $26. for two nights in the garage next door. Everyone at the hotel was very friendly and accommodating. When the in house wifi (paid) didn't work very well, they refunded my money. I like the quietness....not near major freeways...we were on the 17th floor. It looks like they are remodeling some areas so construction during the day.
We will be back next time we are in LA.

title: “excellent experience in SF ... friendly staff, comfortable rooms”
text:
We really enjoyed the Monaco. Staff, especially James and Benjie were excellent. welcoming and very efficient. Rooms were recently decorated and while a little busy, LOTS of spots and stripes, the essentials were good, great bathrooms, well ventilated and with enough safety features to assist the slightly physically impaired. Excellent beds and, apart from the occasional street noise, very quiet. 
We had drinks and snacks in the bar, very friendly, and one meal in the restaurant which was also excellent. The other great aspect of the hotel is its proximity to Union Square and the huge range of breakfast places nearby. We really enjoyed Davids as we had not tried Kosher food before, and also one we called Bleary O'Learys, but that isn't it's right name. Lots of major stores nearby close to transport and theatres, also some excellent small galeries. A very pleasant experience, we'd stay there again, despite the costs of valet parking. Car retrieval was prompt and efficient.

title: “Fabulous hotel and perfect location”
text:
I recently stayed at the Hudson Hotel with my best friend. We were in New York for 5 days of shopping and sight seeing. We were a little bit concerned about the hotel because we had read in reviews that the rooms were tiny and it was very dark everywhere.
When we arrived the staff were very friendly and our room was lovely...yes it was small but believe me for the amount of time you spend in it it was perfect. 
The location was amazing with a subway station at the end of the street and Times Square only a few blocks or a short subway ride away. 
It was dark inside but it was all part of the ambience of the hotel.
We didn't eat in the restaurant because there are so many other places to eat but we did use the bar. On Saturday night it turns into a nightclub with a great atmoshere and people even come in from the street to have a drink and party because it's so nice. 
Overall I would highly recommend the Hudson hotel for a city break.

title: “Not as bad as some reviews suggest...BUT.,..”
text: First of all, my daughter booked 2 rooms on Priceline and cost was around $100/night. My room had nice view of pool area with the bay beyond; my daughter's room had a marina view. One tip: we visited during a cold front, and to get your room to be 70 degrees, you have to set the thermostat at 85. When I first set the thermostat at 75 and left the room for a couple hours, I returned and the temperature was a toasty, er frigid 65 degrees. I called the front desk, and maintenance made no big deal about my complaint -- the guy set the themostat at 85, and acted like that's what every intelligent person would do who wanted a room to be about 70 degrees. The cafe (Blue something) was nice but expensive, as was room service. The soups both night tasted homemade and were great to warm me up in the room with the weird thermostat. Room was clean, bathroom fine except for the crack in the bottom of the plastic tub -- walls and floor were newly tiled and sink had new granite. Room was big and bed was comfortable, though I'd have liked a real blanket, not a thin flannel rag between two top sheets (weird -- yes there was also a bottom sheet), covered with an old bedspread that felt greasy -- maybe that's the purpose of the extra top sheet, to buffer your face from the germy bedspread. And the TV had "snowy" reception on the pay-for-view movie channels as well as the lower-numbered stations. Lobby is dark and depressing, and you have to walk outdoors (and it was raw, windy, and cold out there) to get to the elevator in the tower. There is no way in hell this room was worth anything more than the $100 or so a night I paid; it's more like a $75 room with a nice view. And hang on to your soap; you don't get fresh soap the second night.

title: “OVERRATED!!”
text:
This can't possibly be the best/highest ranking hotel in Chicago based on our experience! Sure, it has all the usual 5 star facilities to be expected. But to be ranked 1st it needs to offer something special and outstanding - qualities which lacked at this hotel. 
From the moment one enters the lobby, there is not a sense of warmth. It feels cold and fake - with it's wide expanse of marble, rectangular room, indifferent art work and 'just put there' sitting chairs. Staff are very courteous and helpful. This was the hotel's most outstanding feature, but was not enough to make up for the lack of comfort and luxury it was trying to convey.
Breakfast was expensive - $50 for a couple of pastries, fruit and coffee!
We had been looking forward to staying in this hotel for many months and it was such an incredible letdown. 
If you are happy with an average 5 star hotel then the Waldorf is an acceptable property. But if you want an exceptional 5 star hotel, then this is not the place for you.

title: “AWESOME!”
text: We stayed here for a family reunion. EVERYONE, from doormen, front dest, housekeeping and club level staff was great. I wish now I remembered more names. Rene in Club was super.

title: “Times Square Hotel”
text: Everything was great with this hotel. The rooms were small but comfortable. The price was not outrageous. The breakfast offering was adequate. The location was great. We were close to a subway stop and lots of stores!

title: “WORST EXPIRENCE EVER!!!!”
text: Do not stay here. We got kicked out for making too much noise, but we weren't even there. We checked in after 5, changed and left, we didn't get back til 3:30 am and they claimed we had been making noise all day. they would not compromise with us. They didn't really know where the noise came from so our neighbors were also kicked out. 3 or 4 rooms in our hall got kicked out. They gave us 15 min to leave. I think they should have investigated a little further. Also We have tried complaining but have not received a return call. DO NOT STAY AT THIS PLACE!!!!!!!!

title: “Excellent Hotel with lots of little extras”
text:
We booked this hotel for our 25th wedding anniversary and it did not disappoint. First, our room was ready ahead of time. Second, they upgraded us to a beautiful suite. Third, we ordered the celebration add on and it had the most delicious treats we ever had. The macaroons melted in your mouth and the chocolate covered strawberries were to die for...
Good location where you can walk anywhere. Comfortable beds. TIP.. join their free VIP membership for small, but well appreciated, perks such as free internet, morning paper, bottled water.. The robes in your room will wrap you in comfort after your long day in NYC.

title: “Great historic hotel, but rooms are way too small. I felt claustrophobic.”
text: I used to stay here all the time years ago and loved it. I started staying at the Drake because it seemed more up to date and was in a better location for after business hours activities. I decided to try the Palmer House gain because of its recent magnificent renovation. I was glad to see how nice the James were, but can't tell you how frustrated I am with the room I was assigned. It is do small that you have only two feet to walk around the front of the bed to the closet sized bathroom. When I had status I used to be upgraded to huge rooms with two bathrooms, so I guess I never had a chance to experience the shoebox. Anyway, I wot bother staying here again until I get to an Honors level where I can be guaranteed a bigger room. Not happy. Also, my free water never happened because the tokens they have me were of no value in a machine that seems to be perpetually empty. Tokens? How tacky.

title: “All around excellent”
text: Even for a Four Seasons, this hotel stands our for service, food and facility. Everyone on the staff was attentive, happy, helpful. Restaurant was excellent and the rooms and view were as good as any I've stayed in.

title: “Metro Hotel New York”
text:
Went to New York mid Feb 09, Had fantastic time.
Stayed at Hotel Metro West 35th Street. The hotel staff were excellent even though our travel agent had messed up our booking and hotel had no record of rooms booked for us they gave us a room for the 1st night untill we could contact our travel agents for them to provide confirmation that we were staying 3 nights. The hotel is very clean, rooms are nicely furnished, contental breakfast is provided. TV and shower in rooms, clean towels every day & shampoo shower gel etc provided could not ask for more. This is the second time we have stayed there and would stay again next time in New York. Also Macey's department store is at end of street, 5th ave at other end, Empire state building in next street and Times Square only few blocks away good location for visiting lots of places

title: “Clean, Comfortable Accomodations”
text: easy access to johns hopkins, inner harbor, restaurants and freeway. nice view from 8th floor. comfortable beds, pillows and pleasant staff. the free breakfast was a nice plus which included eggs, sausage, cereals, juice, breads, etc., more than your normal continental breakfast. we didn't use the shuttle bus but if you are going to johns hopkins, it would definitely save you on the parking fees.

title: “Beautiful hotel, great staff, wonderful location”
text: I stayed at the Mansion for a long Memorial Day weekend. The staff was wonderful, the hotel was immaculate and well cared for. The only suggestion I would have for the hotel is that for a 5 star hotel they really should have updated televisions. Even basic Hilton's have flat screens in them! Other than that the stay was perfect!

title: “Great Hotel & Excellent Service”
text:
We were here for one night only in January and were a bit concerned because of the mixed reviews, but we found out for ourselves that it is indeed a great hotel.
