The hotel lobby is really beautiful, and we got valet for our car very quickly and efficiently. The check-in process was great, and the person helping us was very friendly (which is not what New Yorkers' are known for ). 
We staid in a beautiful 1 bedroom suite - there was no view at all, but we preferred the peace and quiet over the room with the view of the street/city.
We come to NYC about 4 times per year, and have staid at many different hotels including Hilton, Westin, W, etc. and this is definitely right up there with them.

title: “Spacious and comfortable”
text: This was our first trip to NYC and we stayed at the Setai for 11 nights so we were very grateful to have such a spacious room with a large wardrobe where we could completely unpack and make ourselves at home. The hotel does not have any designated "check in or out" times which is great because they will work around whatever suits the guest. All staff were extremely helpful, attentive and friendly. The rooms were HUGE, clean and comfortable. We loved the addition of the Nespresso machine and small sweet treats that were delivered to the room each night - it's the small details that make this a special hotel. Great location, close to shopping and Times Square. Highly recommended! Oh and do try the wonderful restaurant on the 2nd floor - Ai Fiori - you must book in advance, but it's worth it !!

title: “Gay Pride 2008”
text:
Stayed at the Washington Plaza for DC Gay Pride 2008 and they offered a special "gay" rate of $119 per night for the weekend. 
Having previously stayed at the Plaza in 2004, they have added new carpet to the rooms and that's about it. 
Horrible 1970's decor with a creepy Andy Warhol style George Washington picture hanging on the wall was uncomforting. 
Room service prices were not listed correctly on their "room service menu", in fact at check out I was told I was suppose to double the menu price. No where on the Menu does it say this. 
For $119 per night in DC on a sumer weekend, I can't really complain. 
I wouldn't pay more than $119 to ever stay here again though. 
Christy at check in was great. 
Overnight valet spoke zero english and appeared to be confrontational when returning my car for the night. I don't speak spanish too well but I didn't appreciate him yelling at me. 
The front desk gladly comped my parking for his rude behavior.

title: “avoid room 624”
text:
My husband and I decided to stay at this hotel although most of the time in Boston, we like to be at Fairmont. Should have done it as usual. The room after upgrading was 624. This is one of the connecting room, and we were able to hear EVERY THING the next room women were talking about. The voice simply came through the connecting door. They were not loud at all, just to make things straight. It was as if there was NO WALL between 2 rooms. We were shocked. 
When I was in the shower, I heard someone banging on the door. I thought it was an emergency or something.. like the hotel on fire?? It turns out that people above our room were walking around. I could not believe the poor condition of the hotel.
It didn't help when we checked in, NO ONE came to help us with our luggage. The room was average with poor amenity. Some of the lights were not working.
I want to think that room 624 had some major issue and that we were unlucky. I want to think that they were too busy carrying guest's bags. However, I do not want to go back and risk another annoying night at this hotel.

title: “Great Base Hotel near the Action of Times Sq.”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights in December last year. This was our 1st trip to NYC and we loved it.
The hotel was nice and clean and the beds made for us every day. The reception staff had reasonable local knowledge and we ate at the Theatre Row Diner every morning for Breakfast which is just across the road. 
My boyfriend and I walked almost everywhere from this hotel, it took us about 10 minutes to get to the heart of times sqaure, 15 minutes to get to the Minskoff Theatre (where the Lion King was showing), 30 minutes to 5th Avenue and 25 minutes to Macy's. (we do walk quite fast however!).
We also ate at a little Chinese take away which is down the side of the hotel and serves good food at reasonable prices. Also there is a great CVS Pharmacy right across the road that seemed to be open at all hours and has everything from drink, food, make-up, magaznes and medical supplies.
I would definately stay in this hotel again.

title: “Clean, spacious, economical (for NYC) value.”
text: We rented 2 rooms for 4 adults for 5 nights. We chose this hotel for the location & the $ & it did not disappoint. Close to Grand Central, Times Sq, Rockefeller & subway. The rooms were spacious & very clean with good beds. The bathrooms were nice & the shower was great. Overall, the hotel personnel were helpful if not particularly friendly (seemed to be a NY attitude rather than anything else). The hotel needs to upgrade the sheets & the concierge needs to be better trained. And both of our room doors squealed terribly - invest in some WD40! If you want a dark room, stay away from the 3rd floor front. Skip the continental breakfast & go to the Dunhill on 45th & 6th or the deli on 6th around the corner for a geat price. Overall, we found it to be a good deal for the price we paid. We'll definately stay here again.

title: “Good with adjustments”
text:
Thanks to reading everyone reviews prior to my visit, my stay at the Hyatt Islandia was very nice. The first room was musty smelling and small. However, I did refuse the first room and was able to get moved to the Towers. This room was great. This is an older Hyatt so there are some signs of age. However, the staff was above average and the food was great. It is also a very convenient location for sight-seeing. LaJolla is minutes away and Old Town San Diego is too.
The pool and grounds were very nice.

title: “Nice hotel, near great mall and complimentary breakfast.”
text: I enjoyed my stay at the Silver Cloud Inn. The location was great in the University area and right next to University Village where you can do lots of shopping. Nice, friendly staff and clean rooms. I enjoyed the complimentary breakfast, especially making my own waffles. They also provide shuttle service in the area which is a plus if you don't have a rental car.

title: “Slowest internet - lousy tv no channels”
text: Slowest internet in the world whether in your room or at the guest computers. Lousy tv's as in poor picture quality and no channels to watch (no E, no comedy central, no shopping, no amc, no tcm.)

title: “fantastic colourful motel!”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights at the end of July at the start of our trip accross the Western US. We had a great stay. We parked easily in the car park just outside the hotel and the car stayed there for the duration of our stay in San Francisco. The room was large, colourful and comfortable - we were sharing with our two teenagers and the one room was fine. Breakfast was quite impressive, the reception seems tiny but they manage to put on a pretty good spread of toast, yoghurts, bagels, muffins etc It was pretty cold eating outside, even in July and wouldn't have ventured anywhere near the pool. SanFrancisco in July certainly made the UK in summer feel warm!
We walked easily from the hotel only using one of the scenic trams for the experience rather than anything else! 
We would certainly recommend the hotel.

title: “Great location, clean, friendly and a calming atmosphere.”
text: Great hotel. Currently here with a group of 45. All our rooms were ready upon arrival and the staff was friendly. The restaurant and coffee bar are great and very convenient. The location is perfect for getting to and from anywhere in the LA Area.

title: “A Japanese Experience in the Heart of San Francisco”
text: We enjoyed a wonderful stay at the Hotel Kabuki. The service was friendly and warm when we arrived to the hotel. We felt as if we stepped into a hotel in Japan. There was a beautiful japanese garden in the lobby and the rooms had rice paper screens and a japanese bath tub. The hotel is located next to Japantown which provided us good restaurants and shopping.

title: “Loved the Magnolia in Houston”
text: We were very pleased with everything about the Magnolia, except the $20 a night charge to park our car. The room was beautiful and spacious; the service was excellent. We received a coupon for two free drinks at the bar that evening, plus a really superb free continental breakfast - hot oatmeal, many other cereal selections, yogurt, various sweet bakery items, three kinds of juices, bagels, coffee, hot tea, etc. We highly recommend the hotel.

title: “Good location and amenities”
text: The location was great and within walking distance of my meeting. The rooms were clean and comfortable. Breakfast is included and was a good variety. I would definitely stay here again when in Baltimore.

title: “Beware the hidden extras”
text:
Stayed here in October 04 for 3 nights.
The room was spacious and spotlessly clean. The Hilton had the most comfortable bed against 3 Canadian cities. Large bathroom but with an odd shower set-up, that understanadably invites criticism about water pressure (management take note, invest in some decent power showers!)
The Breakfast Buffet was good value and offered plenty of choice although my wife felt that the quality was average.
Location was good... a two minute walk from the nearest subway stop and the hotel is well served by an airport shuttle bus(twelve dollars) although this is poorly advertised when you land at Logan and we were forced to trek across town via the subway with cases (look out for the brown mini vans when you land, although I have no idea which stand that they collect from.)
Location was good... close to the restaurants and shops of Newbury Street and the Prudential Centre. (Recommeded: Legal Sea Foods at the Prudential Centre. Not recomended: Ciao Bella) Boston is a very 'walkable' city so the Hilton & the Back Bay are ideally placed.
Service at the Hilton was on a par with every other major hotel / city.
Like every other hotel of our journey around Canada & the U.S we found ourselves having to pay tax on our room. Unlike Canada where you can claim back your GST, we were forced to pay Massachusetts Sales Tax, Boston City Tax, and Convention Center Finance Tax amounting to almost 30 dollars a night. When we queried the convention centre tax (something we had neither used or visited) we received the explanation that it was because it was nearby... just as well that the Big Dig wasn't as we might have been expected to pay for that as well!!!
This is a decent hotel and 'bounce back' represents good value until you get stung by the hidden extras. Buyer beware.

title: “ultra hip, trendy and chic”
text: great staff, incredible view, great service, modern building, modern rooms -- made us feel like movie stars!

title: “Great Base of Operations for San Diego”
text: Easy access to everything, including a moonlight walk along the bay. All the ammenities with a big plus for us being a wonderful, hopping, lounge. We truly enjoyed ending our touristy days with a drink and dance at the lounge. They had live bands, blues bands, every night we were there, and each gave energy and life to the place. The hotel is great, but the lounge will bring us back.

title: “It was stunning”
text: From the lobby when we walked in I was overwhelmed by the beauty of this hotel. Stunning, jaw dropping beautiful. we had an executive level room. 2 bed & 2 bath with everything we could ask for. the beds were full, fluffy like a pillow bed should be. Slept great! the sound of the train was low and actually worked as a white noise, enough to let my 7yr old sleep all night & morning. The food was amazing, the staff accommidating, & pleasant, The pool was warm, the hot tub even hotter. We rarely left the large room except for walks around this grand hotel. Breakfast & hor d"ourves for us every day for free. The negatives: Our view was lacking, next time I'll request the corner room. Our only disappointment was housekeeping. Hard to catch them & took 2 days to turn our sheets, had to ask for towels, & they forgot to clean the 2nd bathroom. Otherwise, I'll never go anywhere else. Wish you had a book so I could just look at the pictures and remember my wonderful time. Thank you

title: “awesome hotel for families!”
text: I found this hotel on TripAdvisor several months ago. Having stayed in the Riverwalk area several times in the past, I knew what it was about and wanted a nice place at a reasonable price with a great kid pool to stay with a few other families. This hotel popped to the top of the list on TripAdvisor and it was correct.. A very nice large free breakfast, free internet, rooftop pool and instant Riverwalk access made it a perfect fit..oh I forgot, the free happy hour everyday was the cheapest way to get a margarita on the Riverwalk. In the end I was very impressed with Drury. I'm a Hilton Diamond member who travels alot and who has seen alot. I'm not into fancy hotels with bellman, doormen and concierges but I do require clean, safe properties with a helpful friendly staff. This was perfect.

title: “Perfect”
text:
If you want a great hotel in downtown LA then this is it. A great place to stay, rooms are fab, beds great, service good. We stayed in club and it was one of the best we have been to. A massive room well fitted out with leather chairs etc, great food and drink.
Would recommend

title: “Comfortable, versatile, great location!”
text: We had a wonderful stay. Our room was exceptionally neat and comfortable and also spacious and quiet. We loved the convenience of the bars and restaurants and had so much fun just exploring this magnificant space. The location is next to the Art Institute and Crown Fountain. It is not a budget hotel, but you get so much for what you pay for--a total package.

title: “Great Hotel with Bad Beds”
text: This hotel has a great location downtown. Very easy access to and from I5, if you're driving. The hotel is very clean and our room (single King) was very spacious. Staff was helpful in every instance. The only problem was that the bed was too soft. I have a bad back so soft beds are a problem. We were at the Sheraton for four nights and I had very little unbroken sleep. My wife, who has no health problems, also found the beds uncomfortable. If you don't mind a softer bed, I would highly recommend this hotel. If you are driving, be prepared for expensive valet parking ($43 per night in November of 2011).

title: “A bit of Dublin in Manhattan!”
text: I almost hesitate to write this review, because I want to keep the Fitzpatrick a secret! This is one of the most delightful hotels I have stayed in. The rooms are small, but perfectly appointed. It is an easy walk to Bloomingdales and other shopping, the subway, theaters, restaurants, and much more. But, the best part is the service. Everyone was delightful. (And, I have to admit, I enjoyed hearing the Irish accents!)

title: “Simply great”
text: A wonderful Hotel with a great staff in a perfect location. Great rooms with reasonable prices. Nice restaurant and Bar. Walking distance to most downtown day & night hot spots. Easy access to all public transportation systems.

title: “Great location, nice hotel”
text: Stayed here on a recent trip to New York. If you're wanting somewhere close to Times Square but just slightly off the beaten track and therefore near restaurants etc which aren't too expensive then this is the place to stay. Rooms are comfortable and staff are friendly. Subway stations aren't too far away to get you to the rest of the city or you can just walk everywhere as we did. If I'm going back to New York then I know where to stay......!

title: “fabulous”
text: Excellent place to stay-no complaints whatsoever!

title: “1 night stay, nice place - great for plane buffs”
text:
As a silver member I had a top floor room with a great view of terminal 2 comings and goings. The room was big with a relaxer chair and large HD TV - one of their new media rooms. 
Hd tv is great for the stations you have but sure makes the normal channels look like a snowstorm on every channel. 
Room and bed ideal- bathroom cramped and couldn't fully open the door past the toilet 
breakfast a rip off, and the bar area is nice but not the cosiest -food quality OK but not exceptional

title: “Great Hotel and Value for money”
text: I have stayed here now 5 times and just love the location and this hotel, yes there was construction going on this visit but I was advised ahead of time, they compensated with continential breakfast and wine and cheese a very nice touch, yes rooms are small but they have everything you need, compared to what you are paying it is a great price and the room has everything you need. The staff are very helpful but need to be on agreement on their prices, 1 person quoted us $50 a day for parking in actual fact it was only $40

title: “Oustanding Location, Great Staff”
text: Stayed there the week of July 18 and had an excellent experience. From the prompt, professional greeting at the Valet (yes it is expensive to valet but offsite parking is not cheap either and is not in any major US city), to check in. Stayed on the 11th floor and had a very clean, very well-maintained room. Used room service and was pleased with the amount of healthy-choice breakfast options. The location is great if you plan on going to a Rockies Game... about a 10 minute walk and the area itself felt very safe to walk at night. If you go to the game, try Breckenridge Brewery...it's right across the street from the ballpark and have some really good brews and food! Good for business or family stays.

title: “Rude Staff, Dripping Sinks, & Dirty Sheets, OH MY!”
text: We pulled into the hotel &I go inside to check in, & it's two young kids working the counter. Nothing wrong with that, I am only twenty myself. I check in, they take my DL to photocopy it, & then h& me the one room key. I asked for a second one, but they made it very clear that they only give out one (even though the person in front of me requested a second one & they gave him one). We walked around the building twice, & could not find this room. Walked up & down but the room just did not exist! Not having a cell phone, we then walked all the way back to the front & asked them where the room was. She then said (& I quote) "OOPS! Forgot to mention, we have a second building. You will have to drive back out to the street & go behind the restaurant." Now, frustrated that we now have to put everything back up & drive to another building, we just want to sleep. We eventually found the room. I always bring our bedding from. The sheets had cigarette burns, all the way through to the very springy/squeaky mattress. It just looked like such a perfect burn, that the sheets were not even touched after whoever did that checked out. The comforter smelt stale, as did the room, so we ripped off their bedding & put down our own. The A/C was not on, so the room was very hot. Not only hot, but very humid. The window was left open! We cranked on the AC. The toilet SEAT had spots all over it. The shower faucet leaked all night long along with the highway noises & loud shaking AC. Next day: A girl is pounding on our door at 10 in the morning (on the Saturday) screaming for housekeeping. We opened the door & told her no thank you, & she told us that check out was now & we had to go. I again told her no, our check out was tomorrow & politely asked her to go away! When we got in that evening, our room key card had been deactivated! We now have to walk across the way to the other building to get it sorted out. The girl working the counter were in there. I was so livid, that I could not deal with it. My boyfriend had to deal with it. After about 10 minutes of complaining, & reasoning with the girl that we made the reservation until the next morning, she finally agreed to look at our confirmation again & THEN went on to say "Oh" (giggles) "My Bad!" & reactivates our room key.

title: “Nice place! Location depends on what you plan to do while you're there.”
text: My husband & I were in LA for 4 nights and stayed here our 1st night in LA. The valet parking is $24 with in/out priviledges, self park is $19 -- we did the valet, which was nice after hours of travel to get there. Very nice hotel. We stayed on the top floor and had clubroom priviledges which was very nice -- complimentary drinks 5-8pm, and free breakfast -- the view up top is really nice. We took the Metro to Hollywood Blvd -- to save time and headache with the car -- glad we did. The Metro station is a short walk (2 blocks) -- be sure to have singles for it. The area of the Pershing Metro is not in the safest area when it's dark, so I'd recommend only using it if you're back before dark. The entire staff was very nice, and helpful. I would stay again, but only if we were doing more activites that were located in the downtown area.

title: “As expected - and a great location”
text:
I've stayed at quite a few Hiltons around the world, and this was neither better nor worse than others. The rooms were maybe a bit smaller than usual, but then again: all NYC hotels have smaller rooms, or at least the ones we've tried.
The lobby is really not very charming, seemingly inspired by Grand Central - not really a place you want to be, but rather just a place to pass through.
Staff was friendly enough, though not overly so. We bought tickets for a bus trip round Manhattan and they gave us tickets to "Big Yellow Taxi", not Gray Line. The price was about the same, but there wasn't nearly as many busses available for "hop on, hop off", which wasn't really good.
For some reason Hilton has not moved into the 21st century, and therefore still charges for internet access (around $15/day). If you need a computer as well, you can use one in the business center (2. floor). To use this and get online is only $10/10 minutes!!!!! This is of course ridiculous. Go across the street and have a nice coffee at starbucks. Comes with free WiFi :-)
Nice touch: There were check-in kiosks in the lobby which seemed to have most airlines. You could therefore check in on-line without being charged the outrageous fees for internet access. Worked like a charm.
The location of the hotel was perfect. Close to most uptown sights and shopping, and also only a couple of blocks from the subway.

title: “the worst”
text: Awful, rude service - small uncomfortable rooms - this nonsense about "modern open design" just means your bed is in your bathroom! The location seems great - but the Gaslamp district is unbelievably noisy all night - with loud garbage trucks in the wee hours - every morning. Also more expensive than a luxury hotel in New York! Unreal prices! If you're into torture and punishment - if you're into being fleeced - then this is the place for you - otherwise, steer clear. The worst clip joint I have ever seen, and I have traveled all over the world!!

title: “Comfortable and Clean Hotel in Northwest Austin/Cedar Park”
text:
Stayed at the Hampton Inn for one night. The hotel is relatively new so the furnishings are very modern. Our room was spotless with a comfortable king size bed. The bathroom had an oversized shower and a large vanity area with granite countertops. Complimentary wireless internet was fast and easy to setup (password given upon check in). Complimentary continental breakfast had waffles, bagels, and scrambled eggs and turkey sausage. The coffee was pretty decent.
The area is near Lakeline Mall but on a quiet side street so I had no trouble with noise (though the walls were a little thin and I could often hear talking in the hallway). Overall a pleasant stay at a business oriented hotel.

title: “Perfect location!!!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here for one of 2 nights we spent in the city during our stay in SF. We thought the hotel itself was very cool, the room was clean and nicely done out. The best thing about this place was the location, it's a stones throw from forever 21, the cable cars at Powell and also westfield shopping centre! We booked the hotel through hot-wire so got a really good deal.
We spent the evening in the bar drinking a few beers while we watched the giants win game 1 of the world series! Had some garlic fries from the bar too which were amazing!
Staff were really nice and I would definitely stay here again!! A must have for people looking to have a good shop while staying in SF!!!

title: “Great Customer Service”
text:
When yoiu need help, Sheila the operator, makes it happen. The HVAC unit in my room was not working, my internet connection would not go through, and the toilet seat was loose. Sheila came to my rescue and all were fixed in record time. The unit was replaced and Sheila helped me get on the internet.
Kudos to the Sheraton's great teamwork!

title: “Unpretentious yet sophisticated, great room and impeccable service.”
text:
We booked a double room (two double beds) for a week's holiday with two adults and two children aged 8 and 10. The room was a good size; bigger than your typical 4 star double room and therefore huge by Manhattan hotel standards.
Service at the hotel was absolutely great. We were checked in within minutes despite arriving at 10:00pm on a Saturday night. The lobby was a geniunely nice place to spend time, with free snacks and drinks and comfortable seating. The kids felt at home and relaxed and were treated courteously by the hotel staff.
Free wi-fi throughout the hotel worked like a charm, unlike other establishments where you have to pay for wi-fi and spend 20 minutes on the phone trying to get it working. Even minor issues were dealt with well, e.g. the first night there were only two sets of towels in the room, and I was expecting to have to call down and ask for more, but when we returned to the room the next day extra towels had been left without even having to ask.
We really liked the stylish but understated decor including black tiled bathroom, dark wood floor with a rug around the bed area. The Andaz has a 'boutique hotel' designer feel minus the 'look at us we're crazy' vibe you get in other hotels that are just trying too hard to be different.
The beds were firm yet comfortable, and the motorized blackout blind meant we were able to sleep well in to rush-hour (8:30am most days) without being disturbed. The bathroom was great - fantastic rainfall shower and none of the water leaking problems reported by other reviewers.
The room is generally very well thought out with simple 'scene setting' lighting controls for "work', "relaxaton" and "nightlight" plus plenty of spare power sockets - no crawling under tables to unplug lamps so you can charge your laptop/moble phone/Nintendo, etc. A huge flat screen TV and iPod dock rounded things off perfectly.
The only minor issue was a lack of storage space for clothing and luggage. It was more than adequate for an individual making a short business trip but not for a family of four staying for a week - perhaps unsurprising given the Wall Street location and the main demographic of the guests, although we did see a number of other families in the lobby during our stay.
The Wall Street location proved to be the ideal base with very little traffic noise making for good night's sleep. There is a wide selection of places to eat nearby, everything from delis through mid-priced family-friendly restaurants to upmarket venues.
With several subway lines are just around the corner from the hotel, we were able to get to the more conventional mid-town tourist locations quickly. You can be in the heart of Times Square in less than 20 minutes, and we often made a mid-afternoon trip back to the hotel for a break before heading out again.
Wall Street is close to many attractions; walking distance to the Statue of Liberty Ferry, Staten Island Ferry, South Street Seaport (with shoppiing, restaurants, old ships and views of Brooklyn and the bridget) plus several smaller museums. You could easily spend a couple of days in the local area doing tourist things without getting in a taxi or taking the subway.
All in all I wouldn't hesitate to recommend the Andaz as a great place to stay for business or leisure, and we'll certainly be back the next time we visit New York. The kids rated it 10 out of 10.

title: “GHOST TOWN?”
text: Hotel new super clean rooms are a little small but well equipped.The bed was a little hard for me.Staff is friendly & efficient.During my stay I only saw 1 other person hmm.Easy access to shops,eating places.Hotel also has a restaurant in hotel but I never saw any one there.Kinda creepy as I felt we were the only ones staying here.

title: “It is okay for a night”
text: We went there during a trip so the kids could play at the water park. When we got there we realized it has that kind of run down feeling. My wife couldn't open our door, I had to basically kick it to open it every time we came back to the room. The room was nice sized but a little dingy feeling. The coffee maker did not work in our room and neither did the ice maker closest to our room. The kids did have a lot of fun at the water park, but it seemed to be majorly understaffed and the people working were not doing too much except talking with others. The whirlpool was drained.Overall, it was fun for the kids, which is why we stayed there but the hotel is definitely in need of a remodeling.

title: “Major Infestation of Bedbug Parasites”
text:
I suffered 51 bites from parasite bedbugs in my hotel room (Room 311). Some of the bugs in my room had been smooshed on the ceiling by previous guests and had blood stains next to them. The pain and suffering was unbearable. It was a nightmare. The hotel staff denied they have bedbugs twice to my face. Then they came to my hotel room and I showed them the evidence and asked how it would be possible for them not to know about the problem when other guests had smooshed them on the wall and there were blood stains. They then admitted they originally had lied to me. 
This is clear neglect and has continued to result in significant pain and suffering for me. I researched the problem and this has been going on at the motel since 2007. Someone needs to do something about this so that motel guests no longer suffer.

title: “First Day of WInter”
text: Overall good experience clean rooms decent surroundings----quite peaceful--light traffic---very nice staff front desk very welcoming and warm----Laura specifically----moring juice and coffee was an added extra complmentary--very nice---yes i would ahd have been here often--will book here again and excellent budget worthy hotel

title: “Nice, just not my style.”
text:
We visited Chicago courtesy of our in-laws, who surprised us by springing for a suite. The room was HUGE. Like, too huge. It would have been nice were there not so much wasted space. Our suite was on a corner, which may have made some of the difference, and it was quite oddly shapen. There was a large sitting area and large closet and wet bar. Additionally, there were two pulldown beds that sprung from the wall. It was a bit odd and it wasted a lot of space, as we did not need the extra beds. The bathroom, though well appointed, was quite small and that extra space would have helped there. The bed and furnishings were nice and well taken care of. Super comfy bedding with a nice duvet. Unfortunately, the armoire that contained the tv was in a location such that you could not see the tv from the bed, which is rather inconvenient. 
Our room had a view directly into the Louis Vuitton store, and you cannot beat the location. Immediately adjacent to the hotel is a large mall containing a Bloomingdale’s and several other high end boutique shops. The staff was incredibly friendly and professional. The hotel is older, but it is maintained well. The Crabtree and Evelyn toiletries are nice.
One thing I did find rather annoying- you have to pay $10 to use the gym facilities. That is absolutely ridiculous. The gym is nice and new, but that should be included in the price of stay. 
We had brunch at the Sofitel Water Tower, which was wonderful. That hotel is a bit more modern and I think if we return to Chicago we will be staying there, but there is nothing wrong with the Drake. Just not my taste.

title: “VERY GOOD HOTEL, QUIET LOCATION”
text: We just spent four days at this hotel. It is a very good hotel, nice lobby, nice bar and good restaurant. Although our room was comfortable, we did not have an outside view. The location proved excellent to us and to the things we intended to do in the city. Park Avenue is mostly deprived of the sirens and horn blowing common in other parts of the city - and what a relief that is !! Excellent restaurants within one block from the hotel - David Burke and Serafina! We only had breakfasts at the hotel. Nice hotel. Will probably stay there next time ! It is not a luxurious hotel but suited us very well in a city where you are mostly out all day and only come back to sleep ! Recommended.

title: “Got it on Priceline, didn't really like it.”
text: We got this room through the bidding process on Priceline. We got a good price, and it is centrally located in downtown Denver, but we wouldn't choose it again. The hotel charges $18/day for parking (not listed on their website), which virtually eliminated our name-your-price savings. The rooms are fairly small compared to other hotels, though they are nice. The pool was closed two of the three nights of our stay for private parties. Guests were offered the option to pay $10/person to swim at a nearby health club instead. We couldn't fully close the drapes to our room, which made me uncomfortable, too. The worst part, though, had to be the trash left in our hallway by housekeeping. We know because it was by our door, probably from our room (pizza box and other things). It was there when we returned to our room one night, and still there the next afternoon. Overall, not a great experience.

title: “Our new home away from home!”
text:
I recently took my family to Austin for a week-long conference and needed a family-friendly hotel. Orangewood was more than I could have hoped for. The service was excellent and the value was incredible. The staff bent over backwards to accommodate our every need. Moreover, they took time to get to know us; we felt like we were staying with family. The hot breakfast was a great way to start the day.
The location was perfect. It took me less than 15 minutes to get to the Convention Center each day. Also, there is a bus stop near the property and a metro rail station 1 mile away.
For me, the best part of the stay was the set-up. We stayed in one of the 2 bedroom, 2 bath lofts. To be able to retreat upstairs at night, to not have to try to get me, my wife, and our children in and out of the same bathroom, was unbelievable. The full kitchen allowed my wife to shop and actually lowered the trip costs for food.
The bottom line is this: my wife and kids absolutely loved this hotel. The staff took great care of us, and it was a great deal. We will definitely be staying at Orangewood the next time we're in Austin!

title: “A comfortable hotel in a great location”
text: We stayed two nights at the Hotel Indigo. The location is excellent, with the 7th Avenue Subway (#1 train) on the next corner and Penn Station just a few blocks away. The flower market (lots of flower and plant shops) is on this block, which makes for great strolling. Our room was clean and comfortable, if on the small side. It's true that you have to be careful with the shower--there is only a glass half-partition, so you have to make sure the showerhead is angled toward the wall or you get the bathroom floor soaked. In general, the Hotel Indigo was a pleasant place to stay and service was courteous. One drawback was really poor elevator service. There are only two elevators and they are awfully slow. One was sometimes out of service, and stairs were not easily accessible.

title: “Great location, not so great hotel.”
text:
Advantages: Excellent location.
Disadvantages:
Smelt of Chinese food.
Peeling wallpaper.
If you have a back room you are woken every other day at 2am with the garbage bins emptied.
You have to pay for the Wifi and then it doesn't work!!
For three days during our stay the elevator was out of order - not great if you're on the 7th floor!!
One member of the desk staff permanently has is earphones on and is no help what se ever.
Oh and a guy was shot and killed a block down during our stay but I guess I can't blame that on the hotel.

title: “Almost fully renovated and still working on it”
text:
We just checked out today after three nights in a newly renovated room on the 20th floor. The room was quite comfortable and well thought out. It was equipped with a mini refrigerator and had a view overlooking Union Square. Floor to ceiling blackout shades are very helpful during the afternoon to block out the direct sun. 
Because the hotel is in the process of renovation (the last phase will be the relocation of the signature restaurant on the 36th floor and its conversion into function rooms) the staff and management are especially helpful and apologetic and concerned about keeping guest informed as to what is happening.
The location is very convenient to the Muni and other public transportation as well as shopping and other tourist oriented activities.

title: “Horrible, Horrible, Horrible”
text: Undoubtedly the most overrated hotel I've ever stayed at. 5 star prices, 1 star bathrooms and public spaces, 0 star service. Tiny rooms, tiny bathrooms, tired and dirty all in one location. If you are thinking about staying here, don't. If you have a reservation, cancel it. Service was incompetent, negligent and downright hostile. Management was too inept to accomodate for that. Not sure where the "Soho attitude" comes from, they work at a toilet.

title: “you get what u pay for”
text: Not a great place. Small rooms kept fair. Not a lot of room to move around in. Great location to clubs, but just up the road much better accomodations for a few more dollars. Don't expect 4 people to fit in comfortably.

title: “Anniversary in NYC was fabulous!”
text: We were so excited to celebrate our first anniversary in NYC and our stay at the Cassa was outstanding! The location couldn't be better - close to theatre, subway, buses and lots of food! The rooms were clean and well appointed. But ALL the staff were fantastic! Always very friendly and welcoming and so helpful. They always took the time to answer our endless questions, helped us arrange tickets and made wonderful recommendations for sights, subways and adventures. The card and wine for our anniversary was such a very special surprise. Thank you for a memorable celebration in NYC!

title: “Fun Overnighter!”
text: My 16 year old daughter and I stayed at Yotel during our stay in NYC. It was close enough for us to walk to the theater, Times Square and the bus station. Our room was spotless and very comfortable. We loved the sleek designs of everything. We had a great time.

title: “Mediocre to Average”
text:
On the surface, the Hyatt Regency appears to be a great hotel - close to the Capitol, nice lobby with attractive furnishings, and it is in the "city." However, dig a little deeper and the hotel is not what it appears:
- Location: yes, it is close to the capitol, but the nearest Metro stop is 3 blocks away at Union Station. Nothing of interest nearby. Fifteen minute (minimum) walk to the museums.
- Lobby/hallways - nice furnishings, but the hallways are very dark and "cavelike." The lobby is nice.
- Rooms - again, nice furnishings, but the old tube-style television is a negative. HVAC unit did not keep the room at the desired temperature. Biggest complaint: I could hear EVERY noise in the rooms next to me and up and down the hallway. Who exactly decided to furnish metal ice buckets? It sounded like a mortar round anytime someone used the ice machine. Also, the door closers did not serve any apparent function as every room door would slam LOUDLY.
I see the appeal of this hotel for those who are lobbying and attending events at the capitol. For others, there are plenty of better choices.

title: “Great show!”
text: Have stayed at many Hampton hotels and are most impressed with the new one at Bartram Park in Jacksonville, FL. New hotel, great front desk service and welcome amenities. Rooms are top-notch and can't wait to try the breakfast. Great show!

title: “Comfortable, friendly and clean”
text:
We were in NYC for the second time , now with the kids.
Belleclaire is a perfect choice for family . We booked the suite and it is ideal for a couple with 2 sons ! Price is absolutely reasonable considering mean fares in Manhattan. Walk distance from Underground, good restaurants, nice shops.
Only remark : I miss the coffee-heater in room. Why it wasn't there?
Anyway : a must choice in NYC !
Maurizio (Italy)

title: “Great location and beautiful lobby!”
text: I stayed here for 2 nights in September. The rooms were nice but a little small. I loved the fog free mirrors in the bathroom! Hotel supplies were great too! I also loved the fact that I could take a water taxi right to the hotel. It was great for someone who hasn't been to Boston in 30 years! It was a beautiful day and it was great to see the city that way. It was a very nice bar as well. I liked the windows. It was very comforable.

title: “Yotel Yeah!!”
text: Excellent price and service. Rooms are small but comfortable, staff is excellent and facility is excellent also. only gripe would be no room service but thats all!

title: “Absolutely loved the hotel!”
text: Stayed here with my daughters. Rooms were very clean and spacious. Staff was friendly - service and location excellent. The only problem was the renovation that was taking place. No noise at night, but one elevator was reserved for the workers, so we usually had to wait for the remaining one. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Highly recommended”
text:
The hotel's location is excellent. It's close to all sort's of public transport which makes travelling around San Francisco a breeze.
Could do with more counters at the reception desk. Checked in the day before the Zazzle Bay to Breakers Run and the queue at the reception desk was long. However there was a supervisor on site to talk to guests which sort of negated the frustrated feelings one would get when a queue does not move.
Room was cosy, The room service excellent (the chocolate coins is a nice touch). The WiFi however I felt was a bit of a letdown considering I paid good money for it with the slow connection being my main gripe. 
The breakfast service at the Exclusive Club Lounge was so-so. Could do with a larger selection of food. 
Despite my gripes I still think this hotel deserves a Very Good rating as the location, the cosiness of the rooms and the friendliness of the staff makes my stay an enjoyable one.

title: “The place to stay for city-lovers who want to experience San Antonio at its Metropolitan best.”
text: This is the place for a fun-packed stay in SA. Picture-perfect location (nestled tightly between the Alamo to the east and the Riverwalk to the west), nice accommodations, and a hopping urban atmosphere around the clock make this a great destination for a weekend getaway or short vacay. Special recognition to the in-house restaurant, Q, which offers top-notch grub and a great selection of beverages, and in particular to our server, Brandi H, who's swift, attentive service and charming sense of humor were spot on. Kudos to everyone at the Regency. You certainly left me wanting to return.

title: “Donatello, great for honeymooners!”
text: Picked this hotel based on positive TripAdvisor reviews. Location & size of the room vs. price couldn't be beat -paid $150 per night incl valet parking. I mentioned that we were honeymooners and would like a quiet room off the street, which was granted. Champagne and chocolates were waiting for us in our very large and nicely appointed room. All the staff were wonderful, polite and helpful with directions, advice, etc. Try the Pinecrest Diner for a great breakfast, Max's for a casual dinner...both great and right by the hotel. Our plane arrived late our first evening, we were tired and just wanted a nice dinner within walking distance of the hotel. The front desk suggested Luna on Castro St, 2 block walk. Small Italian restaurant with outdoor seating. Friendly staff and the best Carbonara I've ever had (and I've had a lot!) Would stay at the Donatello again in a heartbeat!

title: “So pleased I stayed here”
text:
I stayed here for 3 nights in March & booked this hotel after reading the positive reports on Trip. I was travelling alone & had friends staying in a nearby hotel.
I have asked permission of those named below to include them by name.
I arrived after 7pm & was warmly welcomed by Richard. Thank you. 
I was on the 2nd floor in the 'Troy Donahue' room which was facing the street. The room was clean & quirky with huge posters. I had chosen a room with sink & shower but without toilet. The loo was just along the corridor & I never saw anyone else go in or out. It suited me fine.
The bed was very large & very comfy. The only slight drawback was that as the bed was so large it was near the far end wall & I had to siddle past. Having said that it was great to have a big bed.
The shower was efficient & towels replaced daily as needed. The complimentary toiletries were most welcome.
The breakfasts were good & set me up for the day. There was a choice of orange juice, coffee, various teas, 2 types of cereal, fruit, muffins, doughnuts, bagels & cookies. The plates were fab. All themed around filmstars & movies. I'm a saddo & I took photos of my plates each day having chosen different ones each morning.
My friend arrived to collect me on the first morning & I had asked Richard the night before if it would be ok if my friend had a coffee & cookie with me, I would happily pay if he would added it to my bill. He said there was no need & my friend would be welcome. What a warm gesture & much appreciated.
Each evening when I returned to the hotel Richard was on duty & we had great chats. He was really helpful over all sorts of info I wanted to know. Thank you again.
The other guests were quiet but we passed the time of day.
On the last morning I went to reception to ask if I could check in for my flight. Ric (not Richard) was on duty, I hadn't met him before. Another total sweetie. He happily helped me to check in using his computer & then printed off the confirmation sheet for me at no cost.
I also met Jay, the owner, on my last morning, again another really warm helpful guy. When I was ready to leave, he helped me with my bags & hailed a cab for me. Thank you.
I really appreciated the warmth shown to me by Richard, Ric & Jay. They made a good stay GREAT!
I would return. The location was excellent with the subway at the end of the street, a minute walk away. All the cab drivers knew of the location which is a bonus.
If you like a good location & quirkiness then stay here. There was redecoration going on but every establishment has to maintain a property. It didn't interfer with my stay at all.

title: “Great staff and location right on beach in heart of Venice Beach”
text: reasonably priced and great location. An older hotel and not the swankiest place, this hotel offers a homey feel and has a wonderful and accommodating staff. Right in the heart of Venice Beach it offers fabulous views, many great restaurants and interesting neighborhoods within walking distance, Bus service is also easy and convenient to beaches both north and south. The street life amazing and interesting. Not yet gentrified and boring, the world outside this hotel truly represents the freedom of expression that makes the USA so great.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We recently stayed at the Hyatt in Phili and had a wonderful time. The room had a beautiful view looking over the river and it was also a really nice size! The staff were very friendly and the location was perfect. It's a shame they don't offer a discount for parking;however, over all it was a really nice place to stay and I would love to stay there again.

title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text:
I stayed hee for just under a month and found it a very pleasant stay.
The staff were all friendly and willing to help.
The rooms were a nice size, but the cooker wasnt the greatest as it randomly stopped working.
The laundry room was also a big bonus for me.
Location was great.
I would definately recommend this place.
Only downside was it was pricey, esp for a 1 month period...ouch!

title: “Great place, great people, great hotel!”
text: My wife & I booked a room last minute and got a steal of a deal for the area: everything else was either a motel, or double the nightly rate. The amenities are plush, the rooms cozy and modern, and the staff extremely helpful. We liked the swanky bathroom shower, and the King bed was very power nap-worthy. The rooftop lounge/pool/bar looks like a great summer hangout. Additionally, I left some personal belongings there and they FedEx-ed it to my home address. One caveat: the hotel is brand new, so there is some construction noise, and our fridge didn't work. Other than that, I can't wait to visit again!

title: “What has happened??”
text:
If you are attending an event at the Boston Convention and Expo Center and are looking for the convenience being able to walk to the Convention center without going outside--then this is the place to stay. But beyond that convenience, this hotel has really deteriorated since its opening just 5 short years ago. I have to attend a conference each year at the BCEC and enjoy the convenience of the Westin but this will most likely be the last year I stay here. The once stellar service has become lackluster and un-attentive (I had to break up a game of grab butt at the front desk when trying to check out and was treated like I was a major interruption), the quality of the food is horrible (how do you screw up fried eggs??) and the condition of the hotel is on par with a Red Roof Inn. Dirty walls in the dining room, torn and broken chairs in the Birch Bar and dented and scratched walls and furnishings abound.
I travel extensively for my business and usually stay at my 'favorite' spots year after year. I have to say that I have never seen a hotel deteriorate so fast and so dramatically as this Westin. I will not be back.

title: “I was really pleased with my stay there.”
text: My small room was cozy, reasonably priced, and appointed with everything I needed. Everything was clean and up-to-date. Continental breakfast was well stocked and pleasant. And the location is truly convenient, near Empire State Building, near Macy's, near Penn station and near 3 subway lines. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Mostly Happy With This One”
text: No breakfast included and the wireless is really expensive; however, the shuttle service was great. They picked us up at the airport and also at the downtown Doubletree and brought us back at night outside of the normal scheduled hours, just call the hotel and they radio the driver, if he is around, he will come and get you. Make sure you sign up in advance to use the shuttle. The Upperdeck Trolley company comes to the hotel every morning and picks you up if you are interested in their city tour, which I recommend. The room was nice although the walls are too thin. This wasn't a problem until our last night and we heard everything in the next room. For the price I paid with AAA discount, this was worth the money. Although we didn't use, it is close to the T station although you have to cross a busy street which is torn up right now with construction.

title: “Great location, not-so-great room”
text:
Stayed in NY while attending the US Open tennis tournament. We arrived at the hotel very early in the morning but the woman at registration was willing to get us into our room immediately. She told us it was one of their deluxe rooms and was on the floor just below where they were doing renovations. At first we balked but was assured the work was done only between 8-5, so we took it. Room looked great when we entered. After figuring out the lighting system we got unpacked and comfortable. Nice flat screen TV. Bathroom was a little to be desired - frosted glass doors for privacy for toilet and bathroom, double vanity but little storage space, very low-flow shower head, water took some time to get hot. Then we discovered a water leak behind the toilet. Once we reported it to housekeeping, the leak miraculously stopped.
Overall, the size of the room was great. And you can't beat the location of this place - Grand Central Station. If they could improve the bathrooms the rooms would be great. I probably wouldn't recommend staying given the rates they charge.

title: “OK for the price”
text: This is an OK hotel if you're on a budget. It's very near Fisherman's Wharf which is great. The rooms are extremely basic and the staff are surly at best so the less time you spend in the hotel the better! If you're looking for a cheap place to rest your head I guess you could do worse.

title: “The official hotel of pimps & bugs”
text:
What do you say about a hotel whose area dining options are a Subway restaurant and a Mc Donald's that isn't even open after 1 am? The area is teeming with check cashing places, used car lots, hourly rate hotels, and "adult" entertainment stores plus lots of Korean marquee shops that seem to be shuttered after dark. The friendly taxi driver even asked me if I really wanted to stay there & told me not to explore the neighbourhood after dark... I am starting to think my company's travel agent really has a sick sense of humour booking me here.
First impressions of the hotel: the desk clerk is busy arranging the cash drawer which has about $50 in singles for 10 minutes before checking me in at 1 am in the morning (thanks to LAX making my plane loop the airport for an hour). Two dudes that could only be politely described as ripe smelling, low rent pimps were checking in after me causing the desk clerk to quicken his pace luckily. Finally after getting my room keys for my third floor room, I take the elevator up only to be greeted with that unmistakable aroma of "bug bomb" in the hallway.
My room description. After inspecting the closet in which I had to put the closet doors back in their tracks, I notice two rather large horse flies that have infiltrated my room through the air-con vents. I handily kill them with the phone book on the desk (did I mention that the prominent ad on the cover was for bail bonds?). I leave a light on after seeing other reports on line of roaches at this "hotel". The sink situated outside of the bathroom proper is clean. The bathroom proper consists of a clean toilet, stocked toiletries, and a tub with shower so small and narrow that they had to install one of those curved shower curtains in order to preserve the illusion of a "normal" size tub basin.
The beds are spartan hard, the bedding looks like it has seen some high mileage and its better days are far behind them. The TV gets only about 10 channels. The microwave and refrigerator I do not dare use because only God knows what they were used for by the last occupant. The furniture has the light wear of Sanford & Son merchandise.The "free wireless internet" does not even need a hotel provided password, so actually burning the furniture and sending smoke signals to the outside world would be a faster way to communicate as probably half the neighbourhood is probably using this "hotel's" wi-fi as judged by its one bar signal strength and burning fast 30 Kb/s connect rate. Avoid this hotel at all costs. For what this room cost my company, I could have stayed at a much better hotel in a safer area.

title: “shorty walk, good for the money”
text: We stayed at the red roof inn. the End of Feb,08 Was some what concerned because of a couple of reviews I read. But I should have known You can't please all the people all the time. We Stayed on the first floor and have no complaint at first when we arrived I was a bit concerned we had a smoking room but after we turned on the air conditioner the faint smell went away, The room was warm also I should add from being unoccupied. It is a short 2-3 block walk to the Alamo and from there theriverwalk is very accesable if you don't feal like walking catch the yellow trolley. All in all a very pleasnt stay, I would stay there again with out hesitation.

title: “Brilliant stay”
text: My husband and I stayed for 3 nights at the Chelsea Pines Inn. From the moment we checked in, staff went above and beyond for us. We arrived very early after checking out the other hotel during our stay so we were able to leave our bags there. Jay was so nice and went through a map of the area so we knew what to do near to the inn. Our room was huge and the breakfast was tasty. We also loved the fact that we could get tea/coffee during the day. Shower pressure was good. There was a newsletter left under the door every morning with some information on it which was a lovely touch. Free wifi was brilliant. Wine/cheese night was brilliant before we left for the airport. The best part, as well as the location, is the staff. Each and every person was so helpful and friendly and we will definitely stay here again. It made for a very relaxing break.

title: “Excellent location & value; loved the free internet PC in the room!”
text:
The Sheraton University City exceeded my expectations when I stayed here for one weeknight in mid-May 2009.
Well-maintained, somewhat older business hotel, clearly making every effort to stay current. The lobby is nice, with seating, though the fake-wood floor looked a bit too fake. My two-double-bed room was clean and modern, with a flat-screen TV and -- get this -- not just free Wifi in the room, but an actual PC with free internet, as well as an excellent hub for USB or other devices. I had the sense that this may be a new convenience Sheraton is rolling out. Bathroom was tidy and in good repair, though not recently redecorated, based on the old-style square tiles.
My (negotiated-contract) rate included breakfast. The appealing menu yielded a much larger and better than average omelet. I believe all the breakfast items were in the $10-12 range if you were paying cash; I've had much worse breakfasts for much more money at many Hiltons, Sheratons, Marriotts, etc, so this was a definite plus.
Location: Excellent -- a major plus. 6 to 8 blocks from the 30th Street Station (main Amtrak station in Philadelphia). You could walk it, though they aren't short blocks; I took a cab ($8 including tip). Directly adjacent to the Penn campus, three or so blocks from the Locust Walk main drag. Also very near the Drexel campus, and a few blocks from the major hospitals (Penn and Children's Hospital of Philadelphia). Starbucks down the block, multiple restaurants in the area, and a Wawa convenience store across the street.

title: “First class service with a smile”
text: This hotel is in a class of its own. Nothing is too much trouble, right down to offering umbrellas on loan when it rains. The room we had was big and the beds extremely comfortable. The bathroom was a bit on the small side, but perfectly adequate for what you do in a bathroom. We didn't eat at the hotel - the prices were slightly above our budget. We managed to book this hotel at a bargain rate, cheaper than lesser hotels that are nearer downtown. However, we actually liked the fact that the location is further away from the hustle and bustle. We walked into town and back - good exercise, but maybe not for the physically challenged after a day's sightseeing. The Omni Shoreham does kind of capitalise on its historic hotel status and association with presidents and mega stars, which it really doesn't need to do. It's up there among the best on merit, and I would recommend it to all.

title: “Beautiful Hotel by the White House”
text:
The Willard Hotel is a very historical and classic hotel. The exterior and lobby are very ornate and opulent. The location is very close to the White House and a few blocks away from the National Mall.
Check in was quick and efficient. The front desk staff, and all the staff in the hotel, were very helpful. It was a bit difficult to find restaurants and bars in the hotel because of all the nooks and crannies, but they were very helpful. We had the breakfast buffet at Cafe du Parc, and it was really good.
We received a complimentary upgrade, and the room was huge. We stayed in Room 741, which was near the back elevator that was more convenient than the main elevators on the other side of the hotel. The beds were very comfortable, and every night there was chocolate on our pillows. The restroom was fairly large, but the toilet wasn't working that well by the time we checked out. Overall, the room was in good condition.
We checked out eh gym, which is part of the Red Door Spa, and there is a lot of gym equipment there. You also have access to the sauna and steam room.
The only issue we had was with the parking. Parking is $42 for an overnight stay, and there is no self-park. The attendant downstairs was very surly and not helpful at all.

title: “Very comfortable stay!”
text:
Myself, my husband and 2 of our friends stayed overnight on May 27th at the Silver Cloud on Broadway the night before our cruise ship sailed. We stayed on June 4th for an extra day in Seattle on the back end of the cruise too.
The staff was very helpful and let us put all our luggage out in the back after checking out on May 28th so we could do some sightseeing in the morning before boarding our ship. Then on Sunday the 4th, we disembarked pretty early from our ship but were able to check right in as they had a room available. 
The beds were VERY comfortable and linens were soft and smooth. We took advantage of the shuttle to various downtown areas to do some sightseeing both times. The staff was very helpful with recommendations and calling various transportation to get us to the port.
We really enjoyed the fire that was lit in the fireplace as it was a bit cool outside. 
The glass slider doors could use some weather sealing or something in both the rooms we used, since there were significant air leaks. The door came right off the track when trying to open it in one room! 
I'd still stay there again though as it was very clean and the breakfast was great! They even had a protein choice - lots of hard boiled eggs! Not to mention Tully's coffee. VERY good!

title: “real good value”
text: room clean. tv excellent. only negative - noisy extractor fan in bathroom - but not much! staff were very friendly and helpful

title: “One of the best”
text:
I travel a lot. This hotel was fabulous. The Kimptons generally are a step above in terms of service and this hotel is no exception. In addition to service the room was truly beautiful and I was stuck in it working most of day. The set up was excellent for getting things done. I did feel pampered even though working. Great location. Staff was beyond attentive. 
Ellen Musinsky

title: “Impeccible service, great amenities, and all the comforts of home”
text: We stayed in a suite at the Houston Marriott Medical Center while attending a friend's wedding. We were pleasantly surprised by all the welcoming touches the hotel had to offer. Staff were extremely courteous, polite, and prompt. The decor was warm and cozy, with vibrant color. The bed was really comfortable, and the bathrooms were very clean. The suite was stocked with anything a traveler would need (including great iron and ironing board!). We were really impressed with our stay and would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to anyone. The location is great for anyone needing to have services in the medical center, visit family, etc.

title: “Quite Disappointed”
text:
On the positive side, the location is excellent and the room spacious. However, we were appalled to find a matted clump of hair on top of the shower drain. This was not A stray hair (from the cleaning staff or passerby), we're talking a mass of tangled hair. Unsat.
After check-out, I reviewed my credit card statement and was charged approximately $20 for minibar items which we did not consume. I declined the key to the minibar when it was offered at check-in, so practically speaking, I couldn't have accessed the minibar. To be fair, when I contacted the hotel about this matter, they agreed to correct the error and were pleasant/apologetic. Still waiting on the correction/refund. Not the biggest deal in the world, but annoying and indicative of a lack of attention to detail (i.e. if I didn't have the minibar key, how could I have had minibar items).
Finally, for those interested in the property as a "pet-friendly" choice, I would recommend that you look elsewhere. First, there is a $300 pet-deposit. I was not apprised of this deposit at the time of my reservation. While I certainly understanding the concept of a deposit, I think $300 is excessive. I've traveled extensively with my dog (including to a few 5-star properties in Rome and Lucerne) and I've never paid such a heavy deposit. Again, to be fair, the deposit was promptly refunded, but still I found it high. More troubling to me was the lack of "friendliness". While the dog is allowed in the guests room he/she is not allowed in any common spaces for any length of time. Without getting into a long discussion of my experience and/or my dog's merits (she's a Canine Good Citizen and pursing her Therapy Certification), it suffices to say, I was very disappointed with the limited, common-area pet-friendly options available.
I fully appreciate hygiene concerns (kitchen, pool, etc.) and also the preferences and comfort of other guests (e.g. fear, allergies, etc. Even as a dog-enthusiast, I certainly don't like to listen to barking/whining/howling, be jumped on, or otherwise subjected to unruly behavior). However, if the hotel is going to tout itself as "pet-friendly" then I think there needs to be a bit more flexibility on where pets may stay. As I explained, I'm not talking about unruly/out of control animals, obviously their owners should immediately and appropriately address such situations (frankly, I don't know why one would travel with such a pet-- not fun for the owner, not fun for the pet). Rather, I'm thinking of the vast majority of pet owners who spend the time and expense to travel with their pet and have well-behaved, properly socialized animals that are capable of behaving appropriately in public.
To the extent that Sofitel is interested in constructive comments, I would suggest offering a sitting area in/off the lobby that is 'pet-friendly'.

title: “Not Friendly”
text: Our first room had a major water problem, the second room blew a fuse when using the hotel blow dryer. The 3rd room I was moved to had to have a refrigerator delivered to an hour after I requested it. Do not think you are getting a special deal with complimentary continental breakfast & Orderves. There is not enough seats for people, it's like a mob scene to get a muffin & you might find yourself standing while your trying to juggle your coffee (When the machine isn't broken) & muffin. By the way, the room is too small and it is a challenge not to drop your breakfast while your trying to eat moving for people. Forget the convenience, don't get the package, spend the money & go out to eat.

title: “Completely awesome!”
text:
Completely awesome! We'd go back in a heartbeat.
The hotel is brand new and the staff is terrific.

title: “Excellent location with friendly knowledgeable staff”
text: Picked Chicago Comfort Suites for location, room size and value. The front desk staff were very helpful and knowledgable about anything we asked. We had 2 queen suite with window overlooking Michgan Ave which was fun to see in the mornings to see how people were dressed for the weather. Room size with bath down the hall away from sleeping area and kitchen was a big plus--we had full kitchen with washer/dryer which we did not use. We used the frig but were gone all day until evening. A negative was the small bath area--a very crowded separate room for tub/shower and stool --had to close door to get into--with large walkin closet (never used because 2 other closets) adjacent to this wonder why bath not expanded. Small sink area with one sink--needed lots more towel bars. Very slow WiFi and not very usable. Liked the hot breakfast to start the day. The location was ideal as we were walking distance away from Museums, Millennium Park, Magnificant Mile, Chicago river and and other landmarks. There is a Starbucks, Walgreen's and Seven 11 close by. We purchased a 3 day pass on Chicago Trolley and Double Decker Bus which hotel staff booked for us as well as the Architectural River Tour. The Trolley was a great way to get around and visit the places we wanted to go. We were pleasantly surprised and greatly appreciated the friendly and helpful staff. They made up for the room deficiencies.

title: “Love, love, love this hotel”
text:
This was our third time staying here and we love it. The staff is so friendly and helpful, the manager bussed our bags to our room! The beds are so comfy and the room is immaculate.
Can't wait to go back

title: “Just ok....”
text:
I was not real impressed with the hotel, despite its pretty good reviews. I arrived to find that while the common areas were well appointed, my room was worn and small. The heater/ac was very loud, a large gap under the door, where the light shown through all night, and an extremely small bathroom with dirty grout, a couple pubic hairs or two, and cheap, crooked towel bars that looked like they had been knocked off the walls several times, probably considering the very limited space. I requested another room for the rest of my visit, to wit this room was even smaller, but cleaner and quieter. Received a little bit of attitude front the front desk due to the request to move. Oh well, I'm paying for the room, right?
I didn't feel the price and size of the room was a good value, considering how many choices there are in the Magnificent Mile area. No coffee maker, useful refrigerator, or any economical breakfast choices rounded out my disappointment. The topper was a $15/day minimum fee to use wifi--are they kidding in today's day and age?
Look elsewhere for a better deal.

title: “Perfect for us!”
text: I took my parents for a break in May and stayed here. We had a lovely room with 2 double beds, looking out to Alcatraz. Location could not be better, everything is within walking distance- Pier 39, restaurants, shops, cable cars, street cars, bus tour pick up points ect. The staff at the hotel were really helpful, the breakfast is fine, yes it was difficult to get a table at the weekend- so I would get up early if this is important, but worst case you can always take it back to your room on the trays provided. The room was really spacious and kept very clean. I would definately stay here agin when I return to San Francisco. We did did several of the hop on/ off bus tours which were really good, Alcatraz was unmissable and we also went to Yosemite for the day- it was a really long journey, but it is just spectacular.

title: “Be Very Careful...”
text:
We booked two rooms here (for a variety of logistic reasons). I paid almost 2X what my partner paid on the same trip and got a room that was a complete dump. The bathtub was disgusting (photos attached). Thankfully I could bath my kids in the other room. My room also had a terrible odor (the room service person my first night even acknowledged that it smelled bad), and the “deluxe garden view” was two small trees right on top of the patio with the pool fence behind. 
I think this place is VERY over-rated. While the staff is nice, service and attention to detail is completely absent. Interestingly, I was never asked at check-out if everything was “OK.” I was ready with tub photos and a list of issues to present. My opinion – there are a lot of hotels in close proximity. I would expect you could get a lot more value for the money elsewhere, without the extra cost for the stench and filthy bathtub.

title: “Nothing Special Here”
text:
I stayed at the Hilton Squaw Peak for a conference. As an earlier reviewer said, the bed is extremely comfortable; however, the property itself is a little rundown...missing roof tiles, tired carpet, that kind of thing. My room was on the fourth floor of one of the main buildings, and to get there you ride one elevator--by that I mean there is no service elevator, so half the time you're trying to negotiate around giagantic serivce carts or other maintenance equipment. Very strange. The part of the hotel I stayed in is very reminiscent of a Super 8, or other cheap motels with outdoor walkways--nothing special and certainly not resort-y. I do not know what the conference planners where thinking when they booked this spot; it's clearly a place for families with little kids, and it's minutes from...nowhere. Not my thing. 
I asked that the toilet in my room be fixed: it ran all the time. It was fixed so that it dripped all the time. Both were equally annoying and sleep-depriving. My room was very small--European small--and was dark, dark, dark. The trash cans are inadequate, and there is not one at the desk--although again this is not a hotel for business travelers. The conference planners must have been having an off day.

title: “Stay somewhere else”
text: The hotel messed our reservations and when asked to fix it they became defensive saying that I was the one who screwed up. The nieghborhood is horrible with kids off the street asking you for money when you pull in to park. The security is bad because the same kids were running around in the halls wich make it very uncomfortable. LOCK YOUR DOORS. Management needs to takes some courses on people skills.

title: “Room with a view of Alcatraz”
text: This is a great hotel for the price and location. I was surprized by the view of Alcatraz from my window. The parking is outrageous but there is no alternative. At least the valet was always quick. Quick walk to the wharf and shops.

title: “Clean & Comfy-Comfortable beds, awesome shower, very clean, great free breakfast. Loved it, will stay again for sure!”
text: I live in Colorado but had a concert to go to this night. By staying here, I only spent about $50 more than I would have if I had taken a cab from my house! Well worth it! It was extremely clean, the view from our room was amazing, even for a Colorado Native! The free breakfast was definately more than I had expected but you may have a hard time finding a place to sit. There isn't a lot of seating room during the breakfast. The beds are extremely comfortable and the water pressure in the shower is quite impressive. lol I would definately recommend staying here to anyone. As for those traveling here, you won't find a better location for the price. This hotel is right in the middle of downtown Denver. One block from shopping, restaurants, movie theater, etc.

title: “Good place to stay”
text: We stayed for a week - a work/pleasure combo trip. We had a few long work days and then attempted to see as much of the city as we could so it was important to us to get a good nights sleep and we did. We were on the 12th floor and couldn't hear any noise from our neighbors and not much from the street below. The room we were in was small but accommodated our luggage and equipment - a bit of a do it yourself place in terms of luggage. The location is good with a terrific little breakfast place two doors south. Subways a couple blocks away. Everyone was very nice, but especially Harry who saw to it that we could check out late and arranged for a car to the airport. Good price for a good place. Will stay again.

title: “Good hotel, expect to pay for it”
text:
Recently I spent two nights at the Hilton. Total cost was about $900, not including any meals. 
The location is great. Rockefeller Center is right nearby, with lots of things in walking distance. They only keep the 6th Avenue entrance open (6th Ave is also called Avenue of The Americas). All of the side doors are locked. So you could be at the hotel, but still have a full block to walk around the corner.
Check in was quick. The room was average sized and very clean. The bed was very comfortable. I also liked the night lighting that gets activated along the floor as you walk by. The TV is a 26-inch LCD. Down pillows are standard. I called the front desk for firmer pillows.
To my surprise, the shower pressure was good. Space is limited. When using the toilet, your legs will be brushing against the bath towels on the rack. Toiletries were Crabtree & Evelyn.
On my first night there were some kids two doors down. All I could hear was constant shrieking and laughing. At 11 PM I called the front desk. I was ready to pound on their door but decided to let the hotel handle it, which they did. Just remember that you can still have noise even at the nicer hotels.

title: “Great location!”
text:
This hotel was great for us! We are a young couple, no kids. This is not the best hotel for families. It's adjacent to the Gas Lamp District, financial district, House of Blues, walking distance to Little Italy, and a small trek to Coronado Ferry. 
The hotel & the rooms are very modern & swanky. The door to the restroom is pretty much see through. The beds are ultra soft with nice linens. There are animal print robes in the closet. And a nicely stocked bar. Wood floors were also a nice touch.
The pool lounge is very cool. Good music, good drinks, heated pool...what more could you ask for!
Service was also great. The conciere always helped us where we needed to go. The cocktail hour was appreciated as well!
The only CON I can think of is the parking situation. The hotel does not have it's own parking. But I guess that comes with the territory when you stay at a downtown hotel. I think we paid $38.00 a night. I think that's kind of steep. Otherwise it was a great stay!

title: “Great Value”
text:
This place is affordable and very clean. I felt right at home immediately. There is a great staff with attentive customer service willing to go the extra mile to make your stay an enjoyable one!
They have a great free breakfast, high speed internet, a fitness center and pool. I was able to get a good night's sleep, which is rare for me since I tend to not sleep well in different environments.
The hotel is in a super convenient location downtown and not too far from the Galleria for some great shopping and good restaurants. My friends and I enjoyed our stay while in town for a wedding.

title: “Great place - with a few caveats”
text: My sister and I have just spent three nights at the NGH, in separate rooms, the one larger than the other. On the whole we would agree with the favorable reviews, though we found the service a little blasé and the WIFI definitely spotty. The manager acknowledged the problem with the WIFI and said they were talking about upgrading the entire system; however, the company that owns the NGH is dragging its heels and it could be quite a while before the problem is resolved. Meanwhile, the TVs are anchored on the wall, and therefore audible in the adjacent room. When, at 1:30AM, my sister called the front desk to complain about the TV in the room next to hers, the front desk simply called my room - nowhere near hers - and woke me up. Not the end of the world, but it seemed to be typical of a certain attitude.
