Coincidentally, another guest complained that he'd been kept up much of the night by his neighbor as well, suggesting the rooms are not well insulated. Given the number of rooms in what was once a house, occasional annoyances may be inevitable, but management might take them a little more seriously.

title: “Best value hotel EVER!”
text: Me and some friends went down there for NBA All-Star Weekend and I have to admit I was scared after reading some of the reviews on here. I think they must get this hotel confused with the Days Inn on H-Wood Blvd because this one was perfect. Small but quaint room, everything VERY clean, nice pool, great underground parking, breakfast was kinda mediocre but who really cares about breakfast when you're on vacay in LA? It's close to TONS of Shopping/Tourist Sites/Restaurants/Niteclubs, you name it it's in walking vicinity to the hotelOverall great stay, VERY PLEASED and will stay again next time I'm in LA!

title: “Great customer service at 2:30 AM and a great room too!”
text: We were in Washington DC last Saturday and had booked through a 3rd party company yes one that is through trip advisor only to arrive at our hotel in Georgetown to find no room at the inn. I had stayed at the Grand Hyatt in Washington before they also had no rooms but told me to call back after 2 in the morning if I had not found something. Needless to say nothing had been found I called Steven and he told me that yes he could give me room. He did not gouge me and gave me a good price. The service was excellent, the moetro is so easy from here you do not have to go outside. Although, this was a quick trip their customer service is always great. We watched the Euro 2012 at their bar and also had great customer service. This is our home away from home when In the DC area!

title: “acceptable”
text: I choose this hotel because of its proximity to my meeting and the reviews on tripadvisor. The room although spacious is dated, the breakfast and shuttle service were very good. Deanna Sgro

title: “Great location, small rooms”
text:
This hotel is good. Great location only 2 blocks from Union Square, nice modern decor and friendly staff. The hair products they provide are Rusk - good stuff. The mini-bar is stocked with great items including energy drinks and they are decently priced. Parking was my only concern - $35 a night. Unfortunately, that is the cheapest you will find unless you walk miles. So be sure to include the extra $35 ($40 with tax) when you are budgeting for your trip. 
Overall, the hotel was great. Small rooms

title: “Dirty diapers and bugs....oh my!”
text:
My daughter is a UT student and I have been to Austin so many times. I normally stay further out but wanted to see if there was a hotel closer to her house that could meet my needs. This was not it!
My first room was remodeled and looked good UNTIL I was ready to get in the shower and found the bath mat soaked - with the soap neatly displayed on top of it. Either the maid had not cleaned it or the room had been used after. I tossed the mat out and prepared to use a towel on the floor as my mat. I opened the soap and tossed the wrapper into the trash to find that the trash was NOT empty - it had DIRTY DIAPERS in it. That was it for me! Oh - did I mention that this hotel is a maze and I was as far from the elevator as I could possibly be? I actually had to get a floor map from the desk when I couldn't find my first room.
The clerk was very apologetic and moved me to a different room. This one had not been remodeled. It needs it. However, it was comfortable so I showered and went to sleep. I woke to a bathroom full of bugs! Gnats. The desk clerk seemed unconcerned - they seem to be everywhere and the hotel is having a hard time getting a handle on it. Oh my. 
I was unable to change or alter my reservation in any way as I had used hotels.com and the Doubletree has a policy to not allow changes without a forfeit of a rooms fee. Well, I had to tough it up and stay one more night. They did give me free breakfast that I didn't use since I had plans with my daughter. My normal hotel has a nice hot breakfast FREE and FREE parking - this one didn't. 
I left something behind and I have contacted housekeeping - I am still waiting for them to call me back..Still waiting. 
I will stay where I normally stay. I won't use this place again. There are some fine hotels in Austin. This is not it.

title: “Good downtown location, good service”
text: Pleasantly old-fashioned decor. Friendly and competent service. Room was large and quiet.

title: “Great place to stay! Loved it!”
text:
I love Kimpton!
On my trip to Seattle, we found the Hotel Monaco by searching for hotels online. What I loved about Hotel was that it was nice and clean. And very trendy!
An added bonus was that they gave us our own pet fish to take care of in our room. we didn't have to feed it though, the hotel staff took care of that!
Also, what I liked was that they gave us free breakfast at their restaurant! And the breakfast there was really good! They even served alcoholic breakfast drinks early in the morning. HELLO! B-52!
The rooms were nice and clean, and I enjoyed my stay here. I will definitely be booking at the Hotel Monaco again the next time I'm in Seattle!

title: “Friendly and helpful”
text: I just returned from a trip to Memphis with a group of older adults from my church and stayed at the Hampton Inn-Beale Street. We had a wonderful time and the management and staff of the hotel were extrememly friendly and helpful. The rooms were very nice and clean. There was a little noise from Beale Street in the distance, but nothing too disruptive. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Never again - cold rooms and poor service”
text:
I've never stayed at a hotel where the room was cold! We had to blast the heating device which still didn't heat the bathroom. The in-window heater/AC unit (think Motel 6) was so loud we couldn't get a good night sleep even on a king size bed. 
Staff kindly moved us to another room the following night with a newer heater/AC, but it was still noisy. To top it off the bathtub had mould on the walls, but at least we had a bathtub, the first room didn't. 
Asking for something from the front desk was a comedy of errors and staff were rarely there to open the front door. This is one of the reasons not to book non-refundable rooms as we were there for three sleepless nights.

title: “Great business hotel with ample amenities.”
text:
The service is fair. Location is great! Room condition ample for business travel. Check-in and Check-out were ultra efficient.
Great access to restaurants near by and cabs are not too hard to find in the area.
The service, however, have room to improve : such as sending plug adapter to the room took more than 15 min; and there were no one to help me with my luggage when i stepped off the taxi). 
Bottle waters in the room would be great, there were none.
I would give it 3.5 stars instead of a 3 if i can...

title: “My impression”
text:
Was a little worried when I first arrived at this hotel... Directly across from a train station - but this seemed to go quiet afyer 9pm - and a few quirky things with hotel itself - I had a disney world hotel phone as my room phone and you needed quarters to get ice (which were provided) but, hotel turned out to be just fine with friendly and helpful service, cleaning was pretty good though thier looked their were lipstick marks on my bath mat... wi-fi was free and seemed to work fine and bed was comfatable fridge was alos in room McDonalds and a few other take aways about 3 min walk away.
Would stay again

title: “Well, it's ok - but nothing special”
text: The Fairfield Inn & Suites Columbus OSU is located close to the Ohio State University campus. As other hotels were all unavailable for my travel dates I chose this one and it was an absolutely ok'ish stay. Nothing really to complain about - also nothing to be especially happy about. The breakfast buffet was very crowded, food quality was on the lower end of acceptable. The rooms were pretty large and comfortable, but noise from the hallway and the elevators was always auditable.

title: “We loved it and it was the best sleep ever!!”
text:
We stayed here during our engagement trip and were so pleasantly surprised at how beautiful the hotel was and how friendly the staff was. They were very helpful and made our trip so easy. 
The bedding was the best that I have ever slept on and can't wait to order it online! It was wonderful! Even our smoke detector went off falsely in the morning and the cleaning lady was able to rush in and call the engineer to come up immediately to fix it. So helpful!
I cannot wait to get back there to the views, the excitement and classiness of this hotel!!

title: “Above expectations”
text:
I recently stayed at this hotel for 8 nights while taking a course a couple of blocks away. The staff were mostly very friendly (especially Melissa who brought up room service and served me in the restaurant), the room was clean, and the bed comfortable. The pool area was great, and the wine servings generous :) 
I liked that the Light Rail was a block away. The restaurant food is quite good, especially the breakfast buffet.
There were two negative things about my experience. First, I ended up adding a couple of nights to my original booking that had been done through my administrative assistant. The website showed those nights as $30 cheaper than what I was paying throughout the week; however, the employee handling my checkout insisted that the price was what had been agreed upon. I wasn't happy about that - I felt I should have been giving the going rate for the extra nights I ended up staying. Unfortunately, I was hurrying to catch a flight, and did not have time to speak with a manager. Whether or not the manager would have given me the going rate, I don't know. Perhaps!
The second negative -and this is the one thing that would stop me from ever staying in this hotel again - is that the internet connection was lousy. I tried both wireless and not - web pages took ages to load, if they ever actually did. This made it impossible to work from my hotel in the evenings, and on the weekends, when I wanted to price car rentals and see what Phoenix had to offer, I just couldn't access pages I needed to access. Simple email was ok, however.
If the internet connection were improved, I would certainly stay at this hotel again.

title: “A beautiful Chicago hotel.”
text: In my experience Chicago hotel rooms are often a bit of a let down, but not the room at the Park Hyatt. The staff were friendly and helpful. Honestly the only disappointment is that breakfast was supposed to have been included in the rate I booked, but the hotel would not honor it, saying that the rate was currently unavailable even though I had already booked it. A relatively minor thing, except it turned out the only other option for breakfast in the hotel was an omelette at NoMI that cost $40 with tip. That being said, it was a delicious and pleasant meal, and service was excellent. I look forward to returning for dinner. Getting back to what's important, though, the room was very large, modern and clean. The climate control worked well. Nice touches that were appreciated included electric window blinds; wifi (I still can't believe any reputable hotel would charge for it, and the Park Hyatt did not); a very large, clean and comfortable marble bathroom; a large bathtub and separate enclosed shower with two nozzles. The seventh floor fitness facility was excellent. It offered a surprisingly nice selection of good equipment and supplies like clean towels and fresh ice water with fruit and mint infusions. The locker room was also a very appropriate space. There was an overall clean, modern and luxurious feeling to the entire hotel. I wish I'd had more time to spend and hope I'll have the opportunity to visit again soon; next time for pleasure.

title: “Don't Come with High Expectations”
text:
Booked this room through an RCI (timeshare program) special. The photos of the rooms were lovely and looked extremely spacious (then again when do they not). I was a little skeptical and had to call the hotel to make sure that it was enough for my family of four. The front desk assured me that a STUDIO (in NY?! ridiculous) was enough to fit my family, so I went with it. 
The price was fairly reasonable for New York ($300 for the night, which at NY is reasonable) and I love New York to bits. I was so excited as I arrived in Manhattan and began looking for the hotel out of the car. The lobby was mediocre at best and having lived in the Waldorf and the Hilton, the lobby did not even compare with those fine hotels. 
The first red flag was that the room was not ready at 2pm and later at 3pm. A lady in front of us in the line complained that she had been waiting for her room since 7am in the morning. The bellhops were no better. There was one tiny skinny man and a bigger one. The bigger one left the skinny little one to do most of the work (mind you, we had seven pieces of luggage) and gave us attitude when it came time for the tipping. Obviously we gave the smaller one a substantially larger tip, at the expense of us having to quarrel with an obnoxious bellhop that felt his tip was too little. 
The room was a lot smaller than what I had imagined and smelled strongly of cigarette smoke, even though it claimed to be a no smoking room. I was furious that the front desk felt that the size of the room would be suitable for a family of four with two teenage boys. After some reasoning with the front desk, they gave us a slightly larger room but was still way to small for my family.
Now it wasn't all bad, even though it seems like it is. I found the bathroom to be of a generous size, especially for New York. There was also free wifi which surprised me a lot! The location is also impeccable. 
Overall, I would not book this hotel ever again, especially for its selling price of around USD $500. It really dampened my experience in New York.

title: “New York Trip”
text: Lovely Art Deco Style Hotel. Stayed for 11 nights Very good service. Hotel room was dated but comfortable and clean. Fantastic location right in the middle of Times Square. Walking distance to Macy's. Fifth Avenue, The Met etc... Definetely recommend.

title: “Good stay, good value”
text:
I stayed here one night for business. This hotel was very easy to get, and I thought the price was very good for the area. My room was a little dim and dark, and the bath area was small and evener darker, but probably not any dimmer than your average hotel room. Everything was clean and smelled good. The bed and pillows were comfy. Good price for the hotel. 
The breakfast was good and the staff recommended a few great restaurants for my group. 
Only issue was the desk clerk couldn't find my reservation at first and encouraged me to look up my confirmation on the business computer in the lobby. I found my confirmation (after worrying that I had booked the wrong hotel) and he checked me in without a problem. This happened to another member of my group, so maybe he just wasn't listening well?

title: “This hotel is noisy!”
text: A nice renovation spoiled by the failure to double glaze the windows. Every car, truck, and motorcycle that passes the hotel is clearly audible in the guest rooms. In addition, the hotel is on one of the approaches to Love Field, so plane noise is a problem until that facility closes around 11 PM. But, worst of all is the presence of a late night club accross the street that features a patio open until 2 AM. Loud music and revelling are very audible in the rooms facing Maple St. This hotel is far too expensive for these problems. I recommend the Hotel Za Za nearby which is similarly priced and has similar amenities.

title: “Fabulous hotel and Location!!!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the St. Giles for 2 nights in December, 2010-the week before christmas and the crazy snow! We had an amazing time and this hotel is simply beautiful. It is about 2 blocks away from Grand Central, so it made it super easy to jump on the subway and get to wherever we needed to go, and also just as easy to come back and relax in our room. There are lots of good restaurants nearby as well, and lots of shopping is just over 2 streets away. 
Our room was impressive, we stayed up high and had a beautiful view of the empire state bldg. It was GORGEOUS. Room was way bigger then I expected, and so was the bathroom. In fact, the space in the bathroom was almost excessive (no complaints though!) Great ammenities and the staff was accomodating and friendly, even after we checked out. They held our bags for us even we we got there early to check in, and even after we checked out but were waiting to go to the airport. I would recommend this hotel to anyone for the location and the quality. We got an excellent rate online as well, very good considering it was the week pre-christmas. All in all- GO AND STAY AT THE ST. GILES COURT!!!

title: “Your credit info will be stolen”
text: Sent my son here for a stress free weekend only to have his credit info stolen. The view may be great but when the front desk clerk tells you this happens all the time something is wrong. No response back from security or the CEO - guess they don't care. Is the view worth you losing your identity?

title: “Good solution”
text: We stayed at the Club Quarters for one night stop while going from DC to NY. Reservation were made through Expedia the day before with a rate of $118. The hotel is in a good position, our room was big and very cleaned but had very dark colors and for that reason was not very lightful. Check in and check out are made by yourself at the online machine at the lobby but the staff is available for help. The stay was ok, probabily they could add a continental breakfast in the rate.

title: “Extraordinary service at the Talbott, a home away from home in Chicago.”
text:
We were in Chicago for a long weekend to celebrate a 20th Wedding Anniversary.
The Talbott was the perfect choice to meet all of our needs. We stayed in King Suite and were impressed with the size of the room with a separate bedroom, living room area and extra large bathroom with soaking tub, shower and two vanities. Loved all of the windows and natural light that came into the room, we felt like we were at a home away from home. Hotel was very quiet and floors don't have as many rooms as a large chain hotel. Location was excellent for sightseeing and visiting shops along Michigan Ave. Hotel staff was extraordinary and all from valet, bellman, front desk and concierge staff were very nice and made us feel welcome at all times. Equinox fitness center was very nice, even if it is not in the hotel. We were able to use the healthclub to get a good workout. Also need to mention free WIFi internet access. Book online with hotel and recieve complimentary continental breakfast. Only drawback was the hotel has two small elevators for 16 floors but we never had to wait long. The hotel next door was under construction during our visit but we did not hear any noise as we were on the 10th floor of the hotel. Good proximity to Rush Street, Michigan Ave. We would return to the Talbott for our next visit to Chicago.

title: “There is no other choice!”
text:
We just returned from a week in San Diego and our stay at this Residence Inn was simply wonderful and a great value.
With the AAA discount, we had a one bedroom suite with a full kitchen for only about $139 a night. Keep in mind that it INCLUDES a large breakfast buffet every day, plus a dinner buffet Mondays thru Thursdays, including wine and beer. The coffee is always on in the lobby. Add in free internet computers in the business center, including a printer, and a little shop for snacks and drinks. Plus, a gym and a game room for the kids.
And then there is the staff. They must have all come from Disney! EVERYONE always had a smile and a nice word for you. They ALL bend over backwards to help in any way possible. Even the young man in the breakfast room who had to keep teaching people how to use a commercial waffle iron kept his composure. We were missing a trash can and the alarm clock in our room (why would anyone steal a $6 clock?) and they were replaced in minutes.
The grounds are beautiful, with a tennis court, a dog walking area complete with pickup bags, a beautiful pool with a hot tub, a large gas grill where you can cook your own steak, and gorgeous flowers an trees.
And then there is the location. Mission Valley seems to be close to everything. Jump on I-8 or I-5, and you can go anywhere. Old Town is literally 4 minutes away, with great history, shops and restaurants.
The bad news is the noise from other rooms. The walls are thin, but most kids sleep well there so after 9 pm it was quiet enough. My suggestion to management is that they may want to try and group guests without children in the same area, or on the top floor. If you start on one end of the hotel with couples and on the other end with families, the noise won't be so obvious. THIS IS NOT A DEAL BREAKER! When we travel to SD again, THIS is where we will stay.
Thank you, Residence Inn Mission Valley!

title: “Very nice but cramped”
text: The hotel is new and clean, modern decor. The room was extremely small, there wasn't even room for a chest of drawers for our clothes. There was a small closet to hang clothes in with 1 small drawer in the bottom and a shelf on the top. We pretty much lived out of our suitcases. The maid never had our room cleaned before 4:30 pm. There was no concierge, and the front desk was not helpful in that regard. They also tried to push their own taxi service back to the airport which would have cost $62.00 plus toll plus tip. They also told us that the yellow cab fee to JFK was a metered fare which I knew was false. Taxis to and from JFK to midtown Manhatten are by law $45.00 plus tip. Decent breakfast but the breakfast room was too small to handle all the people that tried to eat around the same time. The hotel is very convenient to subways and shopping.

title: “great for romence and business”
text: very elegant romantic historical hotel. nob hill location is less when travelling with kids like i did.

title: “Good not great hotel, good size rooms.”
text: The whole place needs a vacuum and good cleaning, but if yoy can get past that it was a nice place. Seems modern and fairly new, just needs a deep,cleaning.

title: “Comfortable like a known pair of jeans”
text: I was a recent convention attendee at this Austin, TX property. Really no complaints. The staff was friendly and attentive and when I had a couple of minor room issues (clogged drain and a dead hairdryer) they were on both within minutes. Room furnishing were "comfortably worn," but not so much to be a turn-off. Incidentally, my room size was perhaps 100' square feet larger than the typical hotel room. I never had to wait for more than about 30 seconds on an elevator and although my room faced the open atrium, I never hear outside noise with my room door closed. Convention food was perhaps a tad better than most and after eating & drinking too much the downstairs fitness center was a pleasant break with an indoor pool and (for a hotel) a better than normal outfitted gym. At the end of the day, would I stay here again? Yes.

title: “Perfect location”
text:
Perfect location, especially for families. Try for a view of Times Square. Everything is just steps from your hotel--theatres, subway, restaurants, etc. 
The View Restaurant buffet is perfect for kids, and they love the novelty of the revolving restaurant with great views. 
Comfortable rooms with great beds.

title: “BIG disappointment”
text: The Mayflower is not even a 5 star wannabe. It offers very little to compete with other DC hotels (such as the Fairmont, Four Seasons, etc). The deluxe room faced an air shaft/other buildings. The room was big, the amenities were lovely, the bed and bedding were fabulous but the towels felt like sandpaper, the tv was old and antiquated(I don't mean historical as the hotel likes to pass itself off as, justifiying the lousy views and small rooms). However, there were no safes in the room . Their customer service is lacking for a 5 or 4 star hotel. I was treated as though I booked on priceline when in fact I booked using points (since I "was" a frequent Marriott guest and I was down for an upgrade). I came to the conclusion that the "deluxe" room I booked was the worst room in the hotel (due to the darkness of its lack of any view)

title: “Excellent Service- Extremely Kid Friendly”
text: I had a terrific experience with this hotel. What I want to say most in this review is that the hotel is very child-friendly. I have a six year old and a two year old. The girls were each given an activity bag at the front desk at check in and the hotel sent up complimentary milk and cookies later that evening. Also, kids eat free in the restaurant. Our standard room held all four of us very easily- we had a Queen bed, pull out sofa and lots of sq footage. We had stayed a couple of times at the Parker House in Boston (another Omni property) and liked it so much, we signed up for the "select guest" program. This is a free loyalty program, and immediately upon signing up we were given two really good discount coupons- one half price, and one free upgrade. We used the half price coupon for our room at the Phila Omni- it cost us $80 for the night as opposed to $160. The fitness center was under renovation while we were there, but they still had a fine workout room with an elliptical and a couple of treadmills. The new fitness center opening this Spring looks like it'll be pretty elaborate. Hotel staff were very responsive, professional and helpful. The room was nice- good view of Independence mall, and again very large, there was a nice bathroom and good room amenities. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “All together average”
text: The hotel is in an excellent location. It has the airs and graces of a luxury city hotel but turns out to be decidedly average. The shower was old, there was no minibar and therefore no fridge to keep our drinks cold, and the room key failed to work. The latter was most annoying as we had to return to the front desk each time to get someone to come open the door. But the location is great and the hotel does the job and it seemed to be undergoing renovations so it could be about to improve.

title: “Best Kept Secret in SF!”
text:
Stayed here three nights last weekend. While this great a deal could be suspect for a big-city hotel ... I believed the ever-trustworthy TripAdvisor reviewers and am SO glad I did! 
Room was clean, big, nice flat-screen TV, table with chairs, sliding doors and a little balcony, even! The decor, furnishings and fixtures were nice and perfectly adequate. Coffee pot with coffee included; ice machine a few steps down the hall. You can even rent a small fridge for $5 a day.
Covered, lighted parking is FREE! Wi-fi is FREE! 
Our room was on the street side, but other than sirens (which friends in the "inside" rooms heard as well), there was no annoying noise.
Columbus Street is Little Italy! Just walk up the street and there are gobs of delightful restaurants, breakfast places, espresso cafes... gelato, truffles, yum :)
You're three blocks from Ghirardelli Square, Fisherman's Wharf, one block from Starbucks and Trader Joe's, a few blocks from Pier 39, the Alcatraz pier (33), and Chinatown. 
Pat's Cafe on the next street is great for a hot, traditional breakfast.
You can't beat this hotel for a visit to San Francisco!

title: “Couldn't get a better location”
text:
Just back this morning from a 5 day trip with my daughter to the Paramount Hotel. I did weeks of research through the net and trip advisor to find the best hotel/location/reviews/price and settled for the Paramount and was delighted with my choice. Following a hair raising transfer from Newark by Super Shuttle (I'm not the best car traveller in the world and the driver was weaving in and out of the busy traffic in the heat thought I was going to pass out !!) we arrived at the hotel. The hotel is a couple of minutes to Time Square next door to one theatre and across the street from another. The reception is cool ,calm and dark on arrival we were given an upgraded room this was on the 9th floor the window looked into the back of the hotel with no real view and was quite dark but was a large room and very quiet. Sheets and towels were changed every day and room had it's own air conditioning. During our stay we had breakfast at the Dean & Deluca coffee shop attached to the hotel that sold bagels, croissants, cakes etc. The only negative comment I have about the hotel is their bar charges we only had one drink in the hotel and after receiving the bill it was the last too! For a vodka and diet coke and a malibu and coke it was a whopping $27!!!!! That's over £9 a drink which I think is excessive I had a $20 out the shock must have been written over my face as the bar tender told me this included a service charge.
New York is a fantastic vibrant city I would definitely recommend the Top of The Rock tour which we did on our first day which gives you a fantastic view of the city and lets you get your bearings. We also bought a Gray Line three day hop on hop off ticket from an agent in Times Square. Tours were informative and the ticket we bought covered the night tour as well buses were frequent tour guides did mention tips but weren't over pushy some guides were great and New Yorkers we had another one who was African! and therefore a bit difficult to understand. Definitely do the night tour they start at 6.30 stop at 9 and are over 2 1/2 hours long best time to go is around 8 8.30 as it's just beginning to get dark we had a great guide on our last night who came complete with CD player and played Frank Sinatra New York as we were driving through the city. During our visit it was very warm and humid. The upstairs of the bus was great to get a lovely breeze even though it was a warm one!
If you wish to go to see the Statue of Liberty can't really recommend best time to go we went in the afternoon and had to queue for tickets and were told that there was an hour wait after you had purchased your ticket so were standing out in the sun for that length of time - then you have to go through airport style security. I just wanted to see the statue up close so we never got off at Liberty Island or Ellis Island and just got the boat back and was glad too when I saw the queues of people waiting to get back.
To sum up had a great time I felt very safe and there is a highly visible police presence. The Paramount is a lovely hotel and I would definitely stay there again and recommend it to friends and family. 
 Never saw the famous Brian mentioned in all the reviews. :0(

title: “Thank goodness - no multiple night minimum stay”
text:
On a recent trip to San Diego, we had to book our last night at a different hotel from the rest of the visit due to a wedding party that had booked our entire hotel. We had a very hard time finding a desirable hotel that would allow us to book only one night (a Saturday). Most other hotels that we tried insisted on a 2 or 3 night minimum (on a weekend).
So we ended up at the Marriott Gaslamp Quarter. A nice hotel, right next to Petco Park. We were assigned to a high floor and the view was decent, facing east. The room itself was nothing fantastic, but suitable for our last night in San Diego. The location gave us an opportunity to check out the Gaslamp Quarter and the waterfront between the convention center and the USS Midway museum. So as far as location is concerned, not bad at all.
We arranged a breakfast special which included a buffet breakfast as part of the room charge, which was perfect for us. The hotel has a well known roof-top outdoor bar, but we didn't have time to check it out. The business center was available for airline web check-in, so we were able to book our seats and print our boarding passes. Wireless internet was not included in the room price, which for me is a huge disappointment. You'll know from any other of my hotel reviews that as far as I'm concerned, with hotel prices being what they are, I don't see why they can't just include Wi-Fi for free.
The beds were comfortable. I noticed that because of the location, it is possible you will hear the sounds of druken revellers in the streets below in the wee hours of the morning. But although I did hear some commotion (we opened our window), it wasn't so bad that we were unable to sleep. Your mileage may vary.
Overall, not a bad hotel, in a great location. We still like the Pacific Beach neighbourhood better, but if you have to stay downtown, this isn't a bad place to be.

title: “Lots of freeway noise”
text:
The hotel is yards from the freeway, so even though I asked to change room there was no escaping the noise. It does not get quieter at night - the freeway is very busy 24/7 24 hours a day. Although the valet parking is expensive, this is the same everywhere you go in LA. I eat out twice and had to pay $6 each time for parking ($4.50 charge plus tip). I also had to pay $20 for parking in the underground car park of the offices I was visiting. 
With no buffet at breakfast, I found the service slow which is frustrating when you are pushed for time.
I tried to check in early, and was told that there were no quieter rooms available until 3pm, only to be given at 3pm the room which must have been the closest to the freeway. I asked to change rooms, which they did. The door handle on the new room you had to push up rather than pull down.
However the bill I received on checking out was $18 per day higher for the first 2 nights, and $38 for the third night. When I raised this I was told that I had been moved to an upgraded room (I could see no difference to the first room I had), but reception said nothing about extra charges when I moved room. To their credit they agreed to amend the bill to the agreed rate. However it took two receptionists twenty minutes to make the change. Luckily I was not in a hurry.
I would recommend it if you are not in a hurry and don't mind traffic noise.
I sat by the pool for an hour to get some sun. It is very small with very little seating and the sun disappeared at about 6pm.
On the positive side they did not charge for internet access, which you only seem to get at cheaper hotels (I do not understand why).
Personally I would rather have stayed in the Luxe across the road, but they had no vacancies the nights I was there.

title: “Don't accept room 1-870”
text: We have stayed at the Hilton Union Square at least 3 times before and always been very pleased with our accomodations. For some reason, this time we were stuck in a gruesome room. I wasn't too upset when we stepped off the elevator and our room was the first one down the hall. Surely Hilton would make sure there was adequate soundproofing in the wall to hide the elevator noise at night. WRONG!!! We could clearly hear the hydraulics of the elevator all night long - only way to mask it was to turn on the furnace fan. Secondly, they shouldn't even bother to put in windows when you are looking at the wall of a parking structure about 10 feet away, separated by the tarpaper on the roof supporting central air/heat units. After getting settled, I entered the bathroom to find the porcelain lid of our toilet sitting slightly askew and visibly cracked. Seriously, we're paying $200/night and the toilet is broken. VERY DISAPPOINTING. Hopefully it is only room 870 in Tower 1. Travelers - do not accept this room if you think you'd like a good night's sleep in a nice room.

title: “Good once we upgraded the room”
text: The discounted wotif.com room was tiny and looked into a noisy construction site which got very noisy from 6.30am on Sat morning. The hotel did kindly move us to a nicer room for the remainder of our stay but it's bad luck if you end up with one of the rooms facing the demolition next door. Breakfast food was good, service very slow. All the staff are very keen to please however and friendly.

title: “Excellent service - highly reccomended”
text: We spent a weekend at the Inn at Penn (at a very good Expedia.com rate) and were very impressed with the service. The staff could not have been nicer or more helpful. The hotel is nice and clean and well-run . It's in the heart of the University area. Highly reccomended.

title: “this hotel is old, dusty and overrated but typically American”
text:
I visited this place for business, so a had to stay for a full week to attend a conference. The rooms are small, the breakfast was amazingly expensive and so was the internet access in my room.
I also had to pay for the gym in the hotel.
They charged 6 US dolars for one bottle of drinking water and the coffee maker was placed in ...the bathroom..in Europe that's not even allowed.
The only positive item of this hotel were the doormen.

title: “Awesome location and friendly staff!”
text:
We stayed last night in 2 rooms in the Pier 5 Hotel.
The location of this hotel deserves 10 stars if I could.
The room itself I would give 2 or 3.
We needed two rooms since we were travelling with our 5 kids. We had requested adjoining rooms, but all of those were sold out. The best they could do was 2 rooms 10 doors away. I begged for 2 closer rooms and we were then given 2 rooms side by side. 
The room with a king bed and a pullout sofa was very large and spacious. The mattress on the pullout sofa had many stains and was VERY uncomfortable. My son who slept there did not enjoy it. The king mattress was great and this room had 2 tvs, NICE!
The other room we had was 2 queens and those were both nice. Watch the heavy wooden headboards if you have little kids. We had a few headbumps on those.
The decor is very nice.
Our view out the window and sliding door was really sad. Considering the harbor is there, all we could see were 20 air conditioning units. Really bad.
The best part of the trip was the Crabby Hour. It is free everyday from 5:30-6:30. We learned how they make crepes with a very cool crepe maker and each of us got to make our own. The kids loved the plain ones, the adults loved the artichoke/spinach stuffing. Free local Ravens beer and wine made it a perfect evening.
The King suite had a nice thermostat on the wall that worked very well. The 2 queen bed room had a very noisy poorly working wall unit.
One really strange thing, the counter in the bathroom seemed really short. I am average height and I was bending down to use it. My over 6 foot son looked ridiculous trying to brush his teeth and bending waaaay down to reach the water.
Valet parking worked very well but we only parked and took the car out one time.
Breakfast was one downfall. The food was not all setup when we came down. There were no plates, no knives, small problems. But all the baked goods, bagels, muffins, danish, toast, tasted like they were first served a week ago. Yes, they really tasted that stale. The one highlight was the fresh fruit. Really nicely cut and displayed and super sweet! Oatmeal, juices, a few yogurts, cold cereals and cottage cheese rounded out the rest of the buffet. The toaster worked great but took about 6 minutes to toast each thing. I can only imagine how crazy that is when a lot of people are all eating breakfast at the same time.
There are many amazing wedding rooms in the hotel. What a great location for a wedding or event.
All the staff members we interacted with were lovely and very helpful. A+

title: “Pleasant Space, Great Location”
text:
I have stayed at the Lucerne Hotel numerous times over the last few years. The rooms and beds are comfortable, clean, and nicely furnished. The service is always very good the front desk staff and concierge are pleasant and efficient (can't speak to how good the concierge is. I don't know.) The bell service and doormen are a particular bright note time after time. They are quick, friendly, and on the ball to assist at the door, which is good because there are a handful of steps at the main entrance.
 The "superior" rooms are small but this is NYC. The "deluxe" rooms are more spacious. Two minor annoyances: the windows have recently been made non-opening and the bathrooms are seriously lacking in counter space.
 The hotel is in a perfect location on the Upper West Side; full of restaurants, shopping, and "You've Got Mail" scenery. It is one block to Broadway and the 1 train to get anywhere else in town. The Museum of Natural History, Central Park, and plenty of other sights are only a couple blocks away. You can be in the heart of the theater district in only a few minutes by taxi or subway without paying Times Square prices for a soulless, postage stamp room.

title: “Good location, good price”
text: Hotel Circle has like 30 different motels/hotels. This place is fine, nice pool and spa, clean rooms, great location and 2 restaurants onsite so that's convienent.

title: “The quintessential Japantown hotel!”
text:
This is really the perfect stay in SF Japantown. Lovely and modern Japanese-style rooms. Very clean. Friendly and helpful staff. Great location near restaurants, Japanese mall, and movie theater.
My only issue, and it is minor, was that the pricey breakfast buffet was only so-so (and not Japanese!). Although I should note the room service had some delicious-looking Japanese selections.

title: “SUPER SMASHING GREAT!!!”
text:
After opening late last year, this relatively new hotel exceeding all our expectations! 
Situated just 5 mins walk from TIMES SQ, YES FIVE mins and 10 and 15 mins from Grand Central Station/Chrysler Bld and Empire State Bld respectively. 
The location is just perfect as we were within 5 mins from local attractions and from TIMES SQ 42nd st Subway which we used to travel Downtown, to Greenwich Village, Chelsea, Soho, Little Italy, Wall St etc and the 1 Line to the Statue of Liberty. 
It was near to the Rockefella centre to where if you visit 'the Top of the Rock' you get the most incredible view of the Manhattan skyline. 
For shopping you are with a few mins from the shops on 5th and Madison Aves. Macys, Tiffany and Bloomingdales are all within a short subway/20 min walk away. 
The staff were SO helpful and courteous - but not pushy, making you feel very welcome. We were greeted on arrival with a beaming smile and told that we'd recieved a free upgrade from studio to deluxe room. The room was spacious, clean, pretty chic and very comfortable. Great TV and trendy bathroom. By the way the carpets were cool - the colour not to everyones taste but what IDIOT gives a hotel a bad review because of this? Clutching a straws you miserable people! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED
JUST BOOK A ROOM AT THE CASSA - FOR THE LOCATION, STAFF AND PRICE, YOU WILL FEEL LIKE YOU'VE WON THE LOTTERY....

title: “STAY IN HIGHER FLOORS, DON´T BE LATE FOR BREAKFAST”
text: Small room no refrigerator no wifi in room while we were there(but if you see the site...) small breakfast area long wait 10th floor for the elevator smal lobby and weekend nights we have to share with the people goingo to the roof bar - we arriving wiht family pós dinner and "hot" girls sitting by the fireplace...Door safe damaged took 1 day to fix...Room not made 4 pm...Transfer SUV to JFK flat rate but the driver with angry face when I paid the amount guy on the lobby told me to. Noisy door 1007 when closes.

title: “So So”
text: Very central location. Room was clean but worn. Hotel need to be updated.

title: “Nice place”
text: Great hotel, convenient to everything. Rates are very reasonable. Service is good too, they do all they can to help. Right behind Quincy Market & Faneuil Hall.

title: “Perfect Inner City Get a way!”
text: This hotel is a cross between a traditional hotel and a beautiful home. It is an oasis in downtown DC, peaceful and beautiful. When I sat on the front porch I felt at ease. The hotel is surrounded by beautiful gardens and trees - like a house. I got to look out on busy DC and yet feel sheltered from downtown DC at the same time. The beds were extremely comfortable. The room was charming. The staff were very friendly. I would go back and stay in a heart beat. The only thing I would change is the lobby and stairway carpeting needs a good cleaning or replacement - it was getting dingy. It was clean but it was looking worn and dingy. Also, there was a small amount of dry rot on the balcony connected to my room. This is to be expected in a building of this age. It didn't affect the safty of the balcony, it just cryed out for attention. This is a fantastic hotel!

title: “Great Service”
text:
My company booked about 50 rooms for a trade show in town and held meetings in the hotel. I stayed there five nights and enjoyed my stay very much. The hotel is large and luxuriously comfortable. The bed is as good or better than Westin's. The pool and hot tub was great. The staff was eager to please, the bell captains and bell hops were prompt and courteous, the wait-staff in the Terrace and La Esquina restaurants were very good. The service and set up in the 27th Floor Honeysuckle and Rambling Rose rooms was awesome with a very nice custom-made ice sculpture and buffet service (great shrimp!).
When I set up for a presentation in the Emerald Room, the hotel technical support team went above and beyond the call of duty in helping me set up my projector with their screen and their sound system.
The only mishap of the week was on check-in when the desk wrote the wrong room number on my key slip, which caused delays in delivery of my luggage and presentation materials to my room. Fortunately, the bell captain took care of my things and all was well.
The only improvement I could suggest would be that they hire a few more bell hops. If you are in a hurry, plan ahead or expect to wait a while for luggage pickup.

title: “Disappointing”
text: We got Hotel 140 through the Expedia "Unpublished Rate Hotels" feature and, when we checked the hotel website pictures thought this was going to be good. I have to say we were very disappointed. The room was nothing like what was shown on the website. In fact, the first room was so small that, with 2 suitcases in the room, if the person sleeping on the inside of the double bed against the wall wanted to get up, the other person would have had to get up first to make room for them to get across the bed to the floor. When we arrived in that room there was a loud vibrating sound. I went down to the desk and said that we couldn’t stay in that room with that noise. The first woman at the desk said there was nothing she could do as the hotel was booked solid. I said sleep would not be possible in that room. Luckily the woman who was going to be working overnight overheard the conversation and said to let her see what she could do. Ultimately she changed the room to one with 2 double beds in it. It was larger and was alright. We were very very grateful for her! This is indeed a former YWCA albeit refurbished. There was no restaurant or breakfast room on site. It was very conveniently located next to mass transit (train, local metro and buses). There was good security in that you used your room keycard to operate the elevator. We were very disappointed with what we received for the money spent. This was the third most expensive hotel we stayed at on our 3-week east coast road trip (including New York City, Washington and Savannah) and the least satisfactory.

title: “This hotel exceeded expectations”
text: My wife and I were in Denver for the International Shrine Convention. This hotel could not have been more friendly and service oriented. Every need was taken care of with a smile. The rooms were gigantic, the special breakfast was good every day, the open bar at 5:30 warmed a lot of Shriners Hearts. Heartily recommend!

title: “Worst hotel I have ever stayed in... AVOID!”
text:
We had originally booked to stay the Penn Hotel for 4 nights but had to leave after the 1st night. The room was tiny, out-dated and filthy. Bed was barely made. Staff were rude, slow and not very helpful. Although they did waive the $50 early check-out fee.
The location was good, but it definitely didn't out-weigh all the negatives.

title: “Great breakfast, nice pool area”
text:
I did like this hotel even though I thought they had a little bit "dark" rooms and it felt a little bit dated. But everything was clean, the rooms were big, the pool area was good and the breakfast great!!
But I didn't think this was a nice location in San Diego - you really have to take the car if you want to go anywhere... the surronding neighbourhoods felt a little bit rough, nothing dangerous but I didn't want to walk too far. I stayed at another hotel in San Diego before this, and that hotel was placed near the city and I preferred that location, it felt like you were in the middle of nowhere living here !

title: “Absolutely Wonderful”
text: Traveled across the bay for an anniversary celebration. The room was beautiful and the service wonderful. The rose petals on the bed for our turn down service was a nice touch. Will be back same time next year.

title: “Another great stay at Sofitel”
text: I stay at Sofitel often when visiting NYC on business and have always liked this hotel. But this latest trip in August was different. I finally went to NY for pleasure and had to pay for accomodations myself and not through my corporate account. So I was looking for a good location and value. Sofitel had this amazing deal where if you stayed for 3 nights or more you received a complementary upgrade to a suite. We got a huge, 2 room suite, really large by New York standards. I have to say that their regular rooms are also large, spotless and very well appointed. Our whole stay was great. Service is always top notch, locations is perfect - right in the middle of Midtown and next to the theatre district. Finally, they have really nice room service food. You have to try their breakfast which always comes with a basket of french pastries!

title: “Horrible”
text: Located in the middle of a highway. very scary area, and was hoping nit to be shot when we came in and out. Mold on the wallpaper and bathroom falling apart. Parking lot not lit, and was scared to leave the car there. Room door would not lock. No restauraunts around. Smelled horrible

title: “Pleasant stay”
text:
Spent two nights here with spouse during weekend visit. Short walk from Market East SEPTA stop from Airport.
Check in was quick and easy. Received room on 8th floor looking west towards downtown.
Room nicely furnished. Bed comfy and linens very nice.
Quiet area. Starbucks 1 block east on Arch. Easy walk to Independence sites, Constituition Center and much more.
Would stay here again.

title: “Not worth the $$”
text: We stayed in a 2 bed suite last weekend to attend a wedding reception in Pheonix. My experience began poorly when I called from the car to get directions the day of my arrival. They advised me that my confirmation number was not valid and that they didn't have a reservation for me. I gave them the name of the person who I talked to and he said, "That's me." To make a long story short, I had to make a new reservation and they gave me a new confirmation #, which was very similar the one I had originally. (I will be checking my credit card statement to see if I was charged for two rooms) I knew they had lost my first reservation. Not a good start. We arrived, checked in, made our way up the (dirty) elevator to our room on the 4th floor. The pool looked nice but over crowded with screaming people. Our 2 bed suite was clean and spacious, and included a kitchenette and living room with big TV. We had no problems with the room itself. The next morning we went to the "complimentary breakfast" area that we knew ended at 10:30 (we weren't hungry, just looking for some coffee.) I walked through the (open) door at 10:31 and a man quickly snapped, "We're closed!" I softly asked where I could get a cup of coffee and he again snapped, "We're closed!" He was so rude and the way he raised his voice at us, I found to be totally unnecessary. All in all, I would say the hotel room itself was pretty nice for the $110 we paid, but the rest of the experience was just too unpleasant for us to return there. I've had many good stays at Embassy Suites, but this one just doesn't hold up to their reputation. They need to fire their current staff and start over from scratch. Maybe then I'd return.

title: “Great location at reasonable prices”
text: Cow Hollow Motor Inn offers spacious, attractive rooms in a great location for a reasonable price. It's only a few blocks from the Embarcadero. There are many interesting restaurants and shops in walking distance and you can catch a bus which will take you to China Town or Fisherman's Wharf right around the corner.

title: “Good location and price but getting a bit tired”
text: We chose the Milford Plaza based on two considerations: location near Times Square and price. On both accounts, we did well. 3 minute walk to Times Square and a price well below what we have paid at other hotels nearby. Be prepared, however, for a hotel that is getting old and needs some TLC. If you are okay with a couple of things in your room maybe not working and decor that is pretty worn, this hotel will be okay for a day or two. Just know this is definitely not more than a 3 star property, and do try to get a room on a higher floor up away from the busy street noise.

title: “take a pass on the sheraton FW”
text: This was an old hilton property that was remodeled to a sheraton a couple of years ago. The finish of the rooms are marginal and you can hear the guest in adjacent rooms like you were sitting in the room with them. The AC is the window style you expect at a fairfield inn that are very loud. The small flat screen attached to the well is not movable ( restricts viewing angle unless you in the bed). The upside is as a platinum member you get access to the lounge which is actually finished very nice and large enough to spread out with your group. Don't waste your time or you money on the "Dan Mario" steakhouse, the food is sub-par and the service is worst. There are several high quality places to eat near by -- Del Friscos/Ruth's Chris and numerous places at sundance square. If you get a good deal ($100) then not a horrible choice otherwise keep looking.

title: “great property, but traffic into and out of town was a problem”
text: Hotel is clean, beautiful with swans in lobby area, nice rooms, excellent breakfasts, and good manager's reception at "happy hour" time. However, we found the traffic very frustrating. Google or MapQuest would say that something was 14 or 15 minutes away (should have been a quick drive along one of the expressways), but night after night, traffic was horrendous between the hotel and the areas we wanted to visit, which were ALL in the same direction from the hotel: downtown venues, S. Congress St., and Zilker Park area. Because of the traffic, if I were visiting the area again and wanted to stay in this hotel again, I would plan an itinerary that did not involve going back to the hotel at the end of the day before going out at night. In other words, i would stay off the roads between 4 and 7 p.m. We had a GPS and could take side roads instead of the expressways, but they were also packed and slow-moving. Loved Austin, though.

title: “I will never go back!”
text:
I am disapponted with this hotel. I will not spend my money with them again. After making reservations for a particular room and calling the day of the check in to cofirm the room, I didn't get what I made reservations for. The 2nd item of displeasure is, I reserved the room with my business credit card and paid for it with my personal debit card upon checking out. Of course the charges went through right away on my debit card but the card that was used to reserve the room are still there and I was treated uncaring at very best by the person in accounting.
There has to be a number of hotels in Chicago that understand customer service.

title: “A wonderful place”
text:
Sept. 04, 2007
We are just returning from our San Franciso trip. During planning this trip we did not know where we were going to stay. We had four hotels to chose from and had never stayed at a boutique hotel. We are so glad we did and it being the Villa Florence. This is a wonderful hotel in an awesome location. The hotel accommodated our every needs. We requested a quit room and got it, which you may want due to the busy, nosey and excited streets. The concierge was wonderful, he attended to all our tour needs with no hassles. The hotel wine tasting between 5-6pm is a wonderful touch along with the attached restaurant Kuleto's, (great food). You are literally right at Union Square and in walking distance to public transportation to get all over S.F., no car is needed if you only want to see S.F., parking is expensive. Don't worry about the small rooms, you're only sleeping in them for a short period of time, but the beds were very comfortable. We will definitely make this our first chose upon our return to S.F. Great job Villa Florence, 
Signed: T. & D. C.

title: “Great Room, Nice People, Sucky Wireless”
text:
We stayed here Friday, June 15, 2012, Room 119. Compared to the experience we had at the BW Cypress on Katella, we were apprehensive as we drove in, kind of run-down looking on Topanga Blvd. However, the gentleman who checked us in was great. We arrived at the room and opened the door and WOW, clean, bright white sheets, bright white towels, great beds! 
We did have an issue with the wireless internet. We had three computers and only one would connect and that was only at dial up speed. 
The grounds are nicely landscaped and the pool was clean though we did not use it.
There is a Sushi place immediately next door and actually shares the same parking lot. I have to say we were up till after nine and people were lined up out the door waiting to get in. AND, they took some of the hotel parking so it was tuff finding a place when we came back from our outback experience.
All in all, we would stay here again because the value is there, we just did not like we could not get internet as we depend on it when we travel.
We did not take breakfast however I will tell you it is two cereals, plain corn flakes and frosted, plain little bagels with cream cheese, some pastery and two juices.

title: “Very classy, high-service property”
text:
I stayed 2 nights here in January. The rooms are very well appointed and comfortable. I had a small problem on the first night and they front desk had me moved for the second night - no problem.
I had dinner one night in the steakhouse restaurant. It was pretty good except - no baked potato (in a steakhouse)! Not the end of the world.

title: “Worst Hotel Experience Ever!”
text:
I booked a two night stay here and ended up only staying one night. My room was a non smoking room, but smelled terribly of cigarettes. My room was also next to a crying baby all night that literally sounded like it was next to me in bed. The walls were paper thin - I could not only hear the baby crying, but I could hear conversations of the people in the next room over. Horrible. 
When I checked out, I called reservations. They said I would not be charged for my second night. When I got to the front desk to check out, I was told that I would be charged. I asked why and was told that they did not have any more housekeeping staff on duty to clean my room. I explained that I had not been in my room since it got cleaned and that I only needed to grab my already packed suitcase. She said I would have to speak with the manager, who would call me later that day or the next day.
As I was walking back to my room to get my suitcase, I passed several rooms that were open, being cleaned by housekeeping staff... so - apparently the front desk person was not aware that there were still housekeepers on duty? When I checked out, I was also not offered a receipt. I left my name/number with the front desk person and expected a call back to resolve my second night charge. This was over two weeks ago and I have yet to get a phone call. I've emailed several times and have not gotten one single reply.
As of today, I have a charge for two nights on my credit card that I am going to end up having to dispute. It is a shame that they don't take the time to contact their customers - especially when they have a poor experience.

title: “Exceptional Property”
text:
My wife, dog and I recently stayed here for a long weekend. We had a fountain-view room on the sixth floor. The view rivals anything in Europe whether it be Paris, Rome or Geneva. The staff is very personable, while maintaining a strong sense of professionalism. The room was very clean and had a comfy bed. We used room service the entire weekend because we did not want to leave our elderly dog alone. The food was perfect and always delivered within 30 minutes. The room service menu is extensive enough please anyone's taste.
If Philadelphia is in your travel plans do yourself a favor and stay here. You will not be disappointed!

title: “Great Hotel - but be cautious of ongoing construction noise”
text: The hotel was lovely. Our room was nice and we especially enjoyed the bathroom - there was a large soaking tub and a separate shower with a rain showerhead (which we love!). There was also a tv in the bathroom, which was nice when relaxing in the tub. Also, high end fixtures, granite counter, tile flooring, etc. The bed was quite comfortable with nice linens. Also, the small refrigerator hidden in the armoire was helpful for drinks, etc. The complimentary Escalade was wonderful and helped out tremendously when we went out on Saturday night. We explored several downtown and LoDo places on Sat night, and when we needed a ride, we simply called the hotel, and within 10 minutes we were picked up. They even picked us up from the Bronco game on Sunday. The staff was professional and helpful - from the concierge to the valet to the bellman - everyone was great! We ordered room service on Sunday night, and the service was excellent but the food was a bit disappointing, especially in light of the price. Only major complaint would be the construction going on across the street - as we discovered they began work EARLY even on Sat and Sun morning - so it did not work well for 'sleeping in' - but overall the hotel was able to make up for this.

title: “Great Location, Fair Rate”
text:
Convenience: Within walking Distance of many major attractions like the UN, Times Square, Central Park, St. PAtricks Cathedral, Rockefeller Center etc. and many Restaurants.
Clean Room, friendly staff, a little delay in getting room after arrival. 
Because it is NY, we did not stay in the hotel, except to sleep, and it was quiet considering people were reving up for New Years Celebrations.
Famly had a good time. ( 3 night stay)

title: “Finally, I experienced the Waldorf .....”
text:
I stayed 3 nights at the Waldorf Towers in a Lux Suite & my experience during my stay was truly memorable. Had a huge corner suite with views along Park Ave and 50th and although some may say that the rooms are not as luxurious as some other 5 star hotels around the world, the beds, linen, service, character, friendliness and "couldn't do more you" attitude more than made up for it! Just take a walk down many of the exquisite corridors and you will see who else has been "in residence" previously - JFK & Ralph Lauren to name just a couple .....
You also must try the Bull & Bear Manhattans in the bar - very generous measures but be prepared for the cheque ! Think we paid $30 for just 2 !

title: “Wow! GREAT location and value!”
text: My husband and I stayed here prior to attending a convention in the downtown area of San Diego. Our first night (of 4) was in a mini-suite facing the marina in the Casa Del Mar building. This room was not one of the remodeled ones and had several problems (A/C not working - looked like someone had kicked it, phone didn't work, old - and small - TV, TV cabinet had to be propped open with the ironing board since the doors kept closing). When we mentioned it to the front desk the next morning, they immediately arranged to move us. I told them that I was somewhat disappointed in our room since Trip Advisor had spoken so highly of the newly remodeled rooms in Casa Del Mar building. Those were the magic words! We were moved to a beautiful, corner suite on the ground floor for the remainder of our stay (room 410). We faced the marina - although a bay view would've been fine as well since the entire area is so scenic. Free parking and high-speed internet (unlike our convention hotel downtown). Can't say enough about this place! Even had coin laundry on site (we were in San Diego for a total of 10 days - so this amenity came in handy). Ate dinner at the on-site restaurant "Blue Wave". Very good - and had breakfast delivered to the room one morning. (This is Best Western?!) Will we return? Yes! Yes! Yes! Would love to go back and catch an outdoor concert at Humpheysby the Bay - which is right next door!

title: “Great price and location”
text:
I was pleasantly surprised by this hotel. My room was spacious and clean. The hotel was within walking distance to several big attractions and some really great neighborhood restaurants. The only downfall was I heard the hum of traffic at night. However, for the price I got on the hotel, I would gladly bring along earplugs to drown out the noise.
Also they don't have wireless internet so if you are planning on using the internet you should bring your own cable or you can lease one from the front desk.

title: “Great boutique hotel, well located, with personal touch”
text: I love this hotel. Close to Grand Central and the NY Public Library so brilliantly located, very friendly and with a personal touch. I have stayed there twice, most recently with my 12 year old nephew. He loved the big flatscreen telly and I liked the wine reception at 5pm! The hotel clocked that it was a special auntie/nephew trip and put cookies and soft drinks in our room with a card from the manager - very nice personal touch which we appreciated. Fantastic base for a stay in NYC and I will definitely be back! Thank you to all the staff, manager and the various concierges for looking after us so well.

title: “Suite!”
text: Last minute trip to Chi-town for daughter's bday. Lucked into a suite at the Omni. Central location to all of the places she wanted to see -- American Girl, Museums and the Lakefront. The concierge was great to help us organize our agenda and maximize our time in the city. Rooms were perfect for a family trip, living room and separate bedroom. Allowed kids to crash after a long day and gave us time relax.

title: “Very resonable”
text: Checked reviews prior to staying at this hotel. Wanted something in city that was resonable. Called hotel when I got into city and got a room for $59.00 plus tax. Very basic room but very clean. 15 minute walk to Fishermans Wharf. Nice neighborhood, felt safe. Lots of restaurants and coffee shops nearby. Had lunch at local restaurant around corner of Hotel called Nicks Taco, Very good lunch! Someone local had recommeded it. Man at desk was helpful and pointed out places to go and areas to stay out of on map. Would definitly come back and stay here

title: “WOW...Our new hotel for EVERY Chicago trip!”
text:
Our love of this hotel started prior to even arriving! My husband is from Chicago, so we spend A LOT of time there visiting family. We booked our vacation in March 2010, only to find out in May 2010 that our dates needed to change.......when we called a young man named Brendon was so accommodating that I actually posted a compliment on the hotel's Facebook page about him! 
When we arrived to the hotel with 2 kids (newborn included) we honestly joked that we were treated like we were at a 5 star hotel...everyone from the doorman, parking assistants, front door staff and attached restaurant were fantastic! (BTW, the deep dish is to die for...better than Gino's East, Seriously!)
Our room was gigantic, clean, and modern...the pool and patio were awesome and kept clean (we called for towels a few times, and they arrived within minutes). 
Truthfully I could go on and on about the ease, modernness, amenities, parking, wi-fi, pool, location, staff, deep dish at restaurant......haha! 
We will be back SOON!

title: “Big D hospitality.”
text: My girls and I stayed a couple of nights at the Sheraton in Dallas over the July 4th holiday and we were enthralled with the comfort and hospitality provided by the conveniently located hotel. Ver good quality and nice sit down buffet style hot breakfast with dishes & glasses, tired of paper plates & donuts at other hotels. Nice out door swimming pool however it was a little close to the highway. I really liked the exercise room. It had treadmills, etc., but there were several weight machines that I was able to use. Extra clean. The rooms weren't large but comfortable. I will use this hotel again.

title: “OK for a budget hotel”
text: This hotel was inexpensive ($200 for 3 nights). Breakfast was included (cereal, bagels, fruit and waffle maker) Drinks were served in DIXIE cups, which was a little strange. It was close to the airport but about at $15 cab ride to downtown. I tried using the light rail and bus system in the city but it was somewhat confusing. When I went to check out the girl at the desk was clearly on a personal phone call. When I walked through the door to check out she said to the person on the phone, "Oh hang on a second I have a customer." She continued to talk to this person as I checked out and when I asked how I get to the airport shuttle, she walked me outside (while still on the phone with her friend) and said, "I am sorry I work and go to school.. (to the person on the phone)" and opened this door and said, "Have a nice day." That ended my stay...It was great having the shuttle to and from the airport but the pictures online defiantly made the place look waaaayyyyy nicer then it was. When I was heading downtown the cab driver told me that it was the, "rough part of town," Which totally made me feel better that I was staying there...The rooms themselves were OK. Comfortable beds, older TV's, Carpets had an odd smell. They did have a computer in the lobby that guests could use to print out boarding passes, etc. They charged $0.15 a piece of paper to print.

title: “Bad News”
text:
Pros:
-Location
-Price ($50 on Priceline)
Cons:
-Dirty rooms
-Poor customer service
You be the judge. I'd stay here only if you get a good deal on Priceline; otherwise, don't waste your money. Rooms were filthy and staff couldn't care less.

title: “This hotel is a must stay in Chicago!”
text: I have stayed here severeal times before and on this occasion was the best! The receptionist on checking was excpetional so warm, polite and friendly. I was allocated a superb room. Was truly exceptional. Had the opportunity to use the Executive Lounge as a Hilton Honors Gold member. This was wonderful. The staff were always so polite and attentive, with one exception. The man behind the bar on Thursday and Friday, was rude and lacking any charm whatsoever, a complete contrast to his colleagues. This is a hotel I will certainly return.

title: “Clean, comfortable, secure - will stay again!”
text:
The location was very easy to get to, and within a few miles of just about everything I was planning to do. The neighborhood is fine. Didn't feel unsafe for a moment. The hotel has very good security, with an underground parking garage,
The glass partition between the staff and guests in the lobby was closed for the first 2 days of my stay (mid-late September). On the 3rd day it was open. I asked about this and they said the lock on it was broken and they just got it repaired.
Standard breakfast that you find most places these days - bagels, waffles, cereal, juice, milk. All kept very nice and clean with things that needed to be kept cold in a fridge as opposed to a bucket of ice that many places will use.
Room was comfortable and clean. Walls seemed a little thin - either that or the guy next to me had his television up really loud. A quick call to the lobby solved the problem.
All in all, the place was very well located, clean, and secure. Staff was friendly too.
Oh, coffee and orange juice available 24 hours a day - a nice little bonus!

title: “average stay”
text:
Good : 
Close to downtown with free shuttle service. Close to DART train. 
Awesome atrium, Awesome view from Reunion Tower; Dome lounge even gave us a free gift (for drinking too much, I guess)
Very comfortable beds.
Staff were friendly & helpful.
BAD: 
NOISE: the rooms facing downtown (with the better view) was noisy- with the train station right beneath us. kept waking us upseveral times in the middle of the night. they did change us to a higher room the next day, but noise still there, though less.
Small POOL: the most miserable I have ever seen in a hotel of this class!!
Poor ventilation, couldn't open windows.
EXPENSIVE prices both room service & at restaurant, added a 'delivery' charge to room service in addition to the hefty tax! $4 for bottle water! give me a break!
Internet useres: pay >$10/day!!! 
Parking >$18/day!! suggest one of the nearby lots @ $2-8 and walk!
Closese place to eat/shop/party West end/DeepEllum.
Downtown Dallas is 'dead' in weekend & evenings (a shock for us from NY city!)

title: “A great quick one night stay coming into Austin.”
text:
Stayed here for 1 night, booked the room through Priceline for $59 a night. 
We arrived late at night from the airport and left early the next morning, so it was just a quick stay to save some money on hotels for the weekend trip. The hotel was very clean, quiet, and welcoming. The size of the rooms were spacious and no odd smells in the air. 
There was a free shuttle service from the airport so that was nice. The staff was nice and friendly. One minus was that they charged for a basic continental breakfast that most places would offer for free. But it might have been because we booked through Priceline. 
The location is a little bit away from the airport with some other airport hotels. Not much else around. 
Overall, a great airport hotel. Would stay again.

title: “perfect in every way...”
text: My sister and I stayed there for her b.day. We were treated better than family; surprise treats, cards, constant laughter. The windows open so we could hear the street sounds, cool robes, crazy fun colors, textures and located close to everything plus they allow dogs which is always a delight. Coffee is delivered to hotel by local roasters on bicycles; people there are gems. Kinda pricey but if you have to spend $, spend it there.

title: “consistently great”
text: Service is excellent. Food is great. Rooms are clean. 6th time at this hotel with our children, always a pleasure.

title: “Pay for internet?”
text: Currently at this hotel for a meeting. Hotel is part of a convention center so can get a little confusing in the lobby. You can not beat this location, on the river. Bathroom small but adequate. Expected to pay for internet which is disappointing...We were put on the 3rd floor without a view

title: “Excellent Hotel, Location and Staff”
text:
We stayed at the Wellington Hotel from the 27th December until the 1st January. We were allocated a room on the 26th floor (2644), it had a fantasic view towards Central Park. The room was small but I was not expecting a large suite. The room was clean and I think this floor had been recently decorated and was just lovely. The only thing was the Air Con/Heating did make some weird noise sometimes but for a couple of seconds. The rooms were always warm, and if it was a little warm we would just open the window. The location is first class as everyone else has mentioned, you really cannot go wrong for the price. We also found the staff VERY polite and could not do enough for you. Comments on the lifts by some reviews I found harsh we were there at peak season and we did not have a problem, we did have to que on New Year's Eve when everyone came back from Time Square, So what! 
I would recommend Mickey Mantle's Resturant which is five minute walk and it is the best place for food we found. The food in Time Square is expensive anyway. 
If you are looking to buy diamond at a fraction of the price go to China town it is fantasic. My husband bought me a 1 carat Diamond ring I was so lucky.
New York is a busy place so take your comfy shoes. The best part of our trip was going to Woodbury Common it is fantasic and with the exchange ratethe way it is, you get mega bargins from all the Top Designers. 
New York is a fantasic city, we did all the tourist things the Gray Line Tours were well worth the money to see a little of a big place. If you are thinking about going do, and give the Wellington a chance I think some comments have been a little harsh.

title: “YOU CAN FIND BETTER”
text:
5 night stay that started out ok and went downhill from there, after travel into town and worn out sleep was all that mattered, but a noisy inside air unit defeated that possibilty.
Rooms operate off of a "Green" policy that requires your key to be in a holder on the wall for lights/ HVAC to operate, so room was hot and stuffy upon arrival. First day out we were gone 2 hours 8a-10a and upon return none of our keys would open our rooms, back to the desk for reprogram, but wait, you have to have the key for the power as well as the key for the door reporgrammed together. left out again about 12n and returned @ 5p, maid had cleaned the room, taking the shampoo and soap I had just opened from the shower and not replacing it (which I didn't see until 6a the next day. She also removed the card in the power slot which I had to get replaced along with another door key. Day 2 finds us again locked out of our rooms when we return. After a short nap I go downstairs to the workout room to find a treadmill and a bike along with a clock on the wall still showing DST and a flat screen TV mounted on the wall with no control for it, which didn't hinder me since I was iPoding it anyway. About 20 min into my run I look around to see no water anywhere in the area and had to stop my routine to go out to the lobby area to get some water. After 2 sleepless nights I downloaded an app of white noise to my iPod and was able to play it through the room radio thru a Mp3/Aux cable that fed the radio for a better night of sleep. Between battling for constant room/power key replacements and lack of other things you would be better served somewhere else for the money.

title: “Great Service, Mostly Great Location...”
text:
I had the pleasure of spending 3 and a half months at the Residence Inn Alamo Plaza in downtown San Antonio. As far as service is concerned, I've stayed at 5 star hotels and been on expensive cruises where the service didn't come close. All the staff consistently go out of their way to make sure you're enjoying you're stay and that you have everything you need. The few times I decided to forego maid service they almost seemed upset they wouldn't get to clean my room that day. Don't get me wrong it's still a chain hotel and nothing very lux but I was overall very impressed with the staff. 
Breakfast every day is nice although my job here has me showing up at 6AM most days before the breakfast starts, but it's a pretty standard hot continental type deal.
