Mon-Wed there is a social dinner deal with anything from Make your own nachos to chicken tenders to chicken sandwiches and usually some salad. Beer and Franzia are also available at no charge.
As my stay is relatively long, the small gym (2 nice treadmills, 1 not so nice eliptical, 1 bike and some random dumbbells) wasn't making do so I asked if I could use the gym at the big marriot rivercenter hotel a 3 minute walk from the residence inn. I headed over and the manager hooked me up with a card to use the gym and pool area my entire stay here, very nice! They have a much bigger selection of nautilus equip and more cardio stuff, plus the indoor pool + whirlpool and sauna is a nice bonus. 
Lastly, the location. At first glance and still overall: Awesome. Downtown San Antonio is a lot of fun, you're a block and a half from the mall, a block from the alamo, and a 4 minute walk to the riverwalk. There's tons to do, and besides the higher prices levied on this tourist-rich area it's really great. The only downside (small) is that you're on what I would consider the Edge of downtown and the border of the not so nice part of San Antonio. I keep my car in the hotel garage every night and one night had to have it valeted due to the lot being full and sure enough the car was broken into and my gps stolen. The hotel/valet company took care of everything (beyond my expectations) but sure enough a month later a friend parks across the street and we go have a few beers and he's suffered the same consequence of parking his car outside and had a bag full of important files (to him and no one else) stolen.
That being said. If you're in San Antonio for more than a couple days I would highly reccomend the Residence Inn Alamo Plaza. I've stayed at 4 or 5 other hotels downtown and this is my favorite. Just be sure to park in the nice gated hotel garage if you have a car!

title: “Not a place we will ever stay at again...”
text:
I was looking online to see what kind of policies Super 8 has because the room that we were in is by far the worst room we have ever stayed in. I started to read the rants and reviews and after reading the very 1st one and by looking at the pictures that were posted, I realized that it was about the very same room. 
 The beds were very uncomfortable and probably have been there since the place was built, Tried to call the office but the phone still has no dial tone no nothing and the dead bugs that they complained about in the pictures under the glass were still there. Not to count the 2 lights that are mounted on the wall between the beds did not work and the lamp in the corner had no light bulb (which we noticed when we 1st got there and the lady from the office took care of it). There was also no smoke detector, dirt between the sheets and blankets, a bug in the tub and the toilet still ran.
 Couldn’t call the office because of the phone and of course our room was the farthest room from the office and it was on the 3rd floor.
The gentleman running the front desk said he was sorry and that it shouldn’t have been like that but also that he was not able to do any refunds. The manager was not in so I left him a detailed note and asked him to call him. It has been 3 days and I still have not been able to get a hold of him and no return call either.. 
 What bothers me the most is that they were aware of these problems a month ago and did nothing about it and they still put us in it. The manager is supposed to be in no later than 3 today and if he doesn’t contact me or I can’t get a hold of him then I will be going to the owner. Here are some pics…..

title: “Close to the airport, and they know it!”
text: Stayed 1 very short night in October 2011 to catch an early morning flight out of Denver. This hotel is incredibly overpriced for what you get (you're essentially paying for its location). Will definitely stay a few miles further away next time in hopes of less noise, cheaper rates, and better service at the front desk.

title: “Overall good experience”
text: We just got back from 5 days in this lovely hotel. It's well located and the staff is extraordinarily friendly and helpful. The room was comfortable, clean and had a good view of the fireworks of Sea World every night. However, the pool area was congested and you had to fight for a place to sit on some days. There are lots of kids, too so if you want a quiet swim in the pool, this is not the place for you. The food was excellent in all the restaurants, but overall everything was overpriced, including the fee for parking. I am not sure I'd stay here again simply because of the pool situation (someone needs to monitor large groups that grab chairs and then don't use them) and the kids in the spas that they just take over. Overall, I thought the place was lovely, but overpriced. I have to commend the staff, though, they were all great. My ONLY bad experience was that we reported on several days that our shower head was broken and that someone had taken the fire alarm off the wall, but no one ever came to fix either problem. With just a little extra effort by the room maintenance folks and and some attention by staff at the pool would make this place a five star experience. I don't want to pay the prices at this hotel if I can't sit at the pool.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
This is a great property in Midtown. We two different rooms different rooms during our stay. The first room was in the North tower, which was quite inconvenient. You have to go through the conference area to get to the north elevators. 
The second room was the Andaz Suite. It was nicely appointed room, but the best part about it was the bathroom. From the foot soaking bowl to the bath products, everything about the bathroom was awesome!
Lemon poppy-seed pancakes are must haves at the restaurant. One of the best pancakes ever.

title: “Not up to standard”
text: so disapointed with this hotel have used sofitels for many years in europe and have been very happy with them.standards here are far below what i have been used to. first when going to bed found the duvet covers soiled and stained! restaurant not open in evening nor the next evening although a booking was taken. breakfast was adequate but not lavish. and staff were very offhand and impersonal.did not feel in any way a valued or welcome client

title: “Disappointing”
text:
If you are looking for exceptional service from a purported high-end hotel, look elsewhere. If you are happy with a Holiday Inn pretending to be the Ritz, then this hotel will be satisfying. Even though we are Lowe's First members, we will not stay here again.
There were no bellmen in site even though the parking attendant informed us we were required by hotel policy to wait for one. Ridiculous. If he's not ready to work, then I can take my luggage myself. Finally he showed up running and apologizing: not for his tardiness, but for hotel policy requiring him to handle our luggage. He asked us which floor we were on the directed us to the wrong elevators. 
We reserved a king bed, but when checking in we were told no king’s were available. The desk clerk assured us the bed available was a true queen and not a double in queen sheets. Oddly enough, when we reached the room this queen size bed mysteriously transformed into a double with twin sized flat sheets. To make matters worse, the room was dirty and the carpet terribly stained. 
The bathroom was nice, although the usual robes were missing. There was no mini-bar, the fridge didn’t work and the ice bucket was an astounding 4”! We had to ask for extra blankets and a second wastebasket. There was only one wastebasket in the entire room.

title: “Very Pleasant Stay”
text: I stayed here for my birthday week and was very surprised in a good way. The previous review scared me but I had no problems whatsoever. The location is great and the hotel has recently been redone. I stayed here for one whole week and it was all good. The maid service was very good, the hotel was quiet and I was able to walk to starbuck's and ralph's supermarket. The following week I stayed at another property with a friend which was rated better but I should have stayed here as this was the better property. I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Perfect location”
text: The location was perfect for us - close to Michigan Avenue, the transit system and Millennium Park, as well as being so close to the legendary Buddy Guy's bar. The rooms are small but we didn't spend very much time there as there is so much to do and see in Chicago. The staff were very helpful and friendly.

title: “Nice hotel in a great location”
text: I found this amazing hotel, the Inn at El Gaucho on ILoveinns. The hotel is intimate, comfortable and the staff is lovely and helpful. The location is fantastic, we were able to walk everywhere we wanted to go; Pike Place Market, the Aquarium, The Space Needle, Shopping, Dining and more. They have extra touches that make it really nice, delicious chocolate chip cookies in the room on arrival, cozy bathrobes, Starbucks coffee (and tea) in the morning, room service from the restaurant at El Gaucho and the food is amazing! I highly recommend it.

title: “Smelly and dirty”
text: My wife, baby and i ordered 4 nights in this hotel, but we left after 1 night only. The floor was so dirty, and the bath too. We asked 3 times for baby crib, and finally i had to go to the hotel desk and bring it by myself. The girl at the desk didn't seem to care of anything but her piercing. And about the parking - parking in the street is limited to 2 hours during daytime, and there is no other place to park nearby, so be prepare to move your car every 2 hours.

title: “The Best Location When Visiting SF!”
text:
Ok, I'm not really from way too far, in fact I live in the East Bay of the SF Bay Area. But being from the suburbs, my family and I sometimes like to play tourists in the city. When my young son had to do a report on the Chinese New Year for school, we decided to make a weekend getaway of it and spend a night in the city to watch the Chinese New Year parade.
We checked in at the Galleria Park Hotel and was amazed with the location, the chic lobby and the friendly front desk staff. But let's go back to the location. Upon stepping out, you step into shopping paradise. You can feel the spirit of SF surround you. In addition to that, the charming Ferry building, Chinatown, Union Square and the cable cars are all within reach. 
When we got to the room, we loved the corner suite which was perfect for us and our three young children. More importantly, we didn't have to view the parade in the rain on the bleachers like many. We had a wonderful view from our 3rd floor suite cornering Sutter and Kearny -all warm, comfy and happy. My son was tickled pink to have a great view of the parade as we, his parents took photos of the parade for our personal collection as well as for his report. 
All in all, we were all very pleased with our stay. The location, the friendliness and the comfy accommodations made Galleria Park Hotel a home away from home.

title: “Watch out for the $3 service charge added to your bill”
text:
We booked this hotel along with my cousin and her husband through ParkSleepFly.com. The package included parking and shuttle service to the airport and back, as well as one night's stay at the hotel. The hotel touts its free shuttle service, free internet, and free breakfast on its website and in hotel materials in your room. 
When we checked in we were asked to initial a statement saying we'd be charged $3/night for "services" including the airport shuttle, the warranty for contents of the safe, and two other items. When I questioned the charge, I was told we would be charged whether we initialed the statement or not. 
When I spoke with management about this the next morning, I was told the charge covered local phone calls, the supposedly free internet, and the supposedly free breakfast. I asked the manager how she would react if her supermarket tried to charge her $3 for use of a shopping cart when she checked out with her groceries, and she shook her head "no." The charge was subsequently removed from my bill.
This kind of "bait and switch" tactic has got to be challenged by travelers. When a hotel quotes you a rate, there should be no fixed service charge added to it, especially when the staff attempts to justify it by saying it covers items that are advertised as "free" on the hotel's website and in the services guide that's in every room.
Lastly, I asked that the hotel manager call me at home to discuss the wisdom of sticking customers with a charge they hadn't been told about when they booked their room, was told that he would call, and, of course, he hasn't.

title: “Not excellent, not horrible”
text: Stayed there for two nights, just got back a week ago. The location is great for the daytime-close to almost everything. The location is not so great for the nighttime. Very noisy-it's downtown. You'll hear garbage trucks at 4:00am, people outside at all hours. It's an old building, definitely needs work, but when you pull up, you see it's an older hotel so you can say it has character. Restaurants downstairs are decent. There are plenty of restaurants surrounding it, ask at front desk for the restaurant binder. Besides the half-eaten apple under one of the beds, the room was nice enough-air conditioning worked. Shower had very low water pressure, though. Probably wouldn't stay there again, but it wasn't awful.

title: “I am giving it 5 stars and haven't even stayed yet!!”
text: If the help I have been getting from concierge team is any indication of my upcoming stay - 5 stars to the St. Regis! I have been inquiring about dining, tours,etc. via email for my trip and they are the most helpful staff I've even encountered so far! If this is any indication of the service while at the hotel, I am surely going to be spoiled

title: “Perfectly acceptable”
text: The Midtown Hotel's best feature was its location. It was walking distance to downtown Boston, and just a few blocks from the New England Conservatory of Music and the Museum of Fine Arts. The hotel was clean and the staff was friendly and helpful. While it was not the most up-to-date building, it was in good condition. The only downsides were that the drain in our shower did not work, and the rooms seemed to be separated by just wallpaper; it was rather noisy. However, we would return to this hotel. Our overall experience was very good.

title: “This hotel is VERY outdated. Had to change hotels after the first night . Only one positive thing is the location.”
text: My advice is not to stay here. Even having been upgraded to one of the best rooms, tThis is one of the worst Hiltons I have stayed in, having stayed in many around the UK and America. The decor is extremely outdated, the bathroom was old and more like a Travel lodge standard. The food was bad. Unclean and generally a very bad experience. We changed hotel by the next night.

title: “Just... Wow”
text:
I had to travel to San Francisco for business on short notice. All hotels were sold out due to a citywide event. I usually stay at the Fairmont San Francisco, so thought I would try their new property. 
The hotel did not have any single rooms available due to the event. My two colleagues and I decided to book a three bedroom apartment. Since we are all pretty private, we were hesitant to do so. We should not have worried. This apartment was absolutey stunning. Each guestroom was humungous and featured a king bed and bathroom. The living room and kitchen were sleek and modern and perfect for entertaining. The best part of the apartment was the balcony - it had the most amazing view, overlooking Alcatraz. There was also a fire pit. Absolutely wonderful.
The service was great as well. I arrived really late in the evening due to a flight delay and was exhausted. I told the front desk this and they refrained from giving me a brief overview of their services, delivering me and my bags to my room quickly and offering an overview in the morning. 
Additional perks - there is a free continental breakfast AND the business center is free. What a rarity in a luxury hotel! Other hotels should take notice. Your guests are willing to pay a good rate for a good hotel, but they would rather not feel as if they're being "nickled and dimed". 
Although I usually prefer to stay in a more central location (this hotel was located in Fisherman's Wharf), I would certainly return given the chance.

title: “Great location- big clean room - great service”
text: I was booked at the Westin for a conference in Boston and expected a small poorly maintained convention hotel. The Westin was modern, clean and bright. The room was huge and the employees were attentive and polite. The bathroom had a cool double shower head and plenty of counter space. The hotel was connected to the Boston Conference Center via a mezzanine bridge, which was very convenient. It was also just a very short walk to the harbor where there were a lot of great restaurants. I would recommend this hotel and I would stay there again.

title: “Pros and Cons, but mostly pros in my book.”
text:
We booked 4 nights at Yotel to celebrate our 5 year wedding anniversary. At first I wanted a fancy upscale hotel (Waldorf-Astoria, etc.) but during my search I came across the Yotel $149 deal. I couldn't resist. I ended up getting an extra bit of money off by using a promo code for the Orbitz website, and it just made sense. Why spend so much money on a room when there are so many other more exciting and memorable things in New York to spend your money on? So it was a go. I've kept my eye on the reviews here and was prepared for some of the 'challenges' but all in all it was a good experience. In order to keep things organized, I will organize my review into Pros and Cons:
PROS:
*new establishment -- feels 'fresh'
*great location -- I don't understand how people can complain about being 2 blocks from Times Square (albeit 2 long blocks) is a bad 'location' - the walk was not unbearable. It felt nice to be a bit 'removed' but be in the thick of it within 15 minutes. Besides, that's part of the whole New York experience!
*staff was excellent. Addressed anything we needed (iron, etc.). Front greeters are genuine and friendly and helpful.
*24 Hour CVS across the street was a godsend -- was like a security blanket. We ended up buying cereal and milk there our last 2 days (my husband has an addiction to cereal, but I digress)...we also bought water and any other toiletries we needed. 
*The fridge on the floor to store said milk -- unfortunately the coffee machines were broken
*rain shower was nice
*I liked the smell of the soap! It boasts that it's organic and smells as such! A fixable problem!
*Views were nice from the room
*Outdoor patio was beautiful!
*Storage of luggage at appropriate times
*Liked being able to play iPhone through television -- nice touch!
*Mood lighting in room was nice too!
*niches and smart storage solutions in room
*if you are feeling frisky, the glass shower is visible from the bed if you choose it to be --- use your imagination ;)
*I found the map left in the room for us easy to read
*can't beat free WiFi! A Godsend when you need some info on a destination!
*use of computer on Floor 4
CONS:
*bed WAS firm as outlined in reviews -- we bought a memory foam with us. Personally after sitting on the bed I told my husband that it was 'fine' but he thought it was too hard. (I know it sounds excessive to bring a memory foam with us but we already had it and the cost for an extra piece of luggage still didnt't amount to what a room like that would NORMALLY cost)
*the bathroom situation with just the curtain could get ...awkward. We just turned the volume up on the TV LOL!
*coffee machine was always broken
*drinks are overpriced
I can't speak for the food as I never ordered anything at the restaurants, and we woke up too late for the continental breakfast.
I can't say enough about the staff through -- they seem genuinely interested in helping you and helped us with everything from our bags, to flagging down cabs, etc. 
I would recommend this hotel to young couples (or the young at heart!) those who want a nice lounge at the end of the night (it was nice to hang out on the terrace when you weren't ready for bed, but still wanted to feel like you were 'doing' something cool) and the single 20 - 30 something year olds with an open mind. 
However, as much as I enjoyed myself, I do think it was a wonderful experience, for the money we paid...but I'll be honest, if the price went up considerably (and I believe it has) I would have to do some more shopping and comparing before booking again. I'm not saying it's not worth paying more, but I would have to see what else is out there. 
All in all, a great experience that we enjoyed! We had fun with it -- hope you do too!

title: “Quiet, Clean, Amazing Staff, Great Location, Good Nights Sleep!”
text:
Hubby and I stayed at The Orchard last year and upon checking out made a promise to the staff to return again this year and when we walked in on Sunday, 9/5 we were greeted so warmly and I was even reminded of my promise to return by the staff and we did!
We spent 6 wonderful days in San Francisco and The Orchard had a lot to do with it. We didn't encounter any problems during our stay this year or last. We always had plenty hot water, the room and bathroom was kept clean, the staff was friendly and always greeted us with a smile upon leaving and returning and was always helpful with suggestions and we didn't have any problems at all with the free internet. I just plugged in my laptop and logged on, no problems at all.
Everyone has different experiences, but if you are looking for a place to stay that is clean, quiet, helpful staff and a great location, then The Orchard Hotel is what you are looking for!
If you are looking for a place with a big fitness center and evening wine get togethers then this isn't the place. But if you do stay here you will get in some good exercise walking up and down the hill! Hubby and I enjoyed the walks and looked forward to the hill everyday!
The location is great, 2 blocks down the hill to Union Square and the Westfield Centre, 2 blocks down to Chinatown, the cable car stops on the corner that will take you to Fisherman's Wharf, many other shopping stores, restaurants, jazz clubs and coffee shops located so close together!
We enjoyed our nightly walks around the city and only 2 people asked us for money and neither one looked homeless.
We will definitely stay at The Orchard Hotel again and have no problem recommending it to family and friends.

title: “Not all perfect”
text: I brought my sister and family to New York for her first time and for her 60th birthday. We stayed 5 nights, received great room upgrades, and the front desk staff and the concierge were wonderful. On our last night, we got back to the hotel in a pouring rain and wanted a farewell night cap. The bar was closed because its ceiling had just collapsed so the front desk suggested a beer in the very downscale on-site hamburger joint. The staff there was very disorganized and rude. We tried to stand in line at the order window to get some beer and were told to sit down and wait for table service. We no one came to the table, we tried to get the attention of a waiter and were told we had to go back in stand in line at the order window. We ended up never getting served, and got no satisfaction when complaining to Food and Beverage Manager Aiske who was also unpleasant and ineffectual. The only choice left to us was a mini-bar drink in the room which was hardly a fitting birthday party. On top of that, only 2 of the 3 elevators serving the hotel's upper floors are in working condition, leaving us with 10 to 20 minute waits every time we wanted to go up or down. Upon checkout, the front desk person asked about my stay and said that considering our experience at the hamburger place the night before, he'd try to waive a $10 workout fee. He checked with the Front Desk Manager who denied the request. No attempt for remedy and quite unusually weak management for the Le Meridien standard!!l

title: “Perfect Location!!!!”
text: Stayed here with my 4 boys and we loved the location. First we stayed in the double suite and it was perfect...two double beds and another sitting room with a pull out couch. Then we were moved to the Family suite which was the same room except three beds which was ok. I like the double suite better because there is a sitting area but we needed to move because I had two separate reservations..long story. The employees were unbelievable. The bell hop which held our bags so we could go sight seeing Tony was so careful and nice. He really made us feel like our stuff would be fine. Then the girl Norma at the front desk couldn't be more helpful. She took her time answering any questions we had and she was also very helpful with other areas. The parking is expensive that is why we parked on the corner behind the hotel across the street. It's an outdoor parking area but it cost $25.00 dollars instead of $40.00. We would walk by the van just to make sure it was ok and there were no problems at all. The pool in the hotel was excellent. Clean and comfortable. The fitness room was great. All my boys really enjoyed it. Right off the pool was an outdoor garden with nice views. The lifeguards were very nice and watchful. The best part of this hotel is the location. Right across the street from Grant Park and in walking distance to Millennium Park and Michigan Mile. We also were able to walk to Al's Beef famous restaurant and Giordano's was a little bit of a walk but not too bad. We also took transit to Wrigley and also to the Museum of Science and Industry with no problem. The only negatives at this hotel was the bathrooms. Extremely small. Outdoor sink right outside of the bathroom area was tiny. You couldn't really pass a person brushing his teeth so we just took turns so no one would get frustrated. Overall would stay here if we ever came to Chicago again.

title: “Disappointment”
text:
Saw reviews and was very excited to go to the Drake.
Positives: Good Location, Quick check in, easy check out.
Negative: 
* Very Expensive (paid $700 for 2 nights), 
*Thin walls - You can hear other people's showers, people in their bathrooms, 
*Our room was next to the storage room - so we constantly heard a door open and shut, 
*our room was very small- I have had a bigger room at a Best Western or a Marriott
*Misleading information on their website- Their website says they have the internet but when you log on you find out that they charge $11 to your room (who charges for the internet).
*Can only use the gym for a fee- again who charges for a gym
*None of the hotel staff spoke to us

title: “Service was poor.”
text: Price about right for DC. Room was big, but bathroom was tiny. Also not enough electrical outlets. Common areas were also nice. Ate lunch and breakfast there, ok food and service, but pricey. We were there for a conference, at the icebreaker, at exactly 9 pm, they turned the lights off and on to chase us out, so they could set up for the next day. Hey close the bar, ect, but flash the lights in a room with 400 people in...tacky.

title: “False advertising”
text: The advertising for this Travelodge was misleading. The rooms are small and dark compared to the website pictures, and they are also more expensive. The wi-fi rarely worked, and there were loud fights.

title: “Beck's was great!”
text: My partner and I stayed at Beck's over the Gay Pride weekend, and we had absolutely no problems what so ever. Beck's is a good hotel in a GREAT location. The Castro is only a few blocks away, which makes it ideal. Granted Beck's is not the Hilton, but for the value and the location, it gets an A in my book.

title: “Some good, some not so good”
text:
I've stayed at this Residence Inn several times over the last year and a half. 
First, the good. This is a standard Residence Inn. All R.I. locations are pretty much decorated the same; I've even seen some of the same framed pictures at other locations. The rooms and bedding are comfortable. The kitchenettes in the rooms are well stocked with pots and pans. As other reviewers have said, the breakfasts are great. Lots of choices, and plentiful amounts. The staff are courteous. When you book a Residence Inn, you know what you're going to get. Generally speaking, 
And this is where the "not so good" comes in. There are a few differences at this R.I. from others where I've stayed. 
The wi fi only works about half the time. The staff is always apologetic, with copious promises that "it is being fixed", but I've been told that for over a year now. There is a computer in the lobby's "business center" which usually works, but that is even down sometimes. So if you depend on internet access, request a room that is hard wired... they have 16 hard wired rooms in the hotel. 
Also, they don't always do a good job of restocking necessities. I've had to consistently ask for things that should be provided.... toilet paper, kitchen towels, toiletries, cups in the gym, dishwasher soap, etc. Also, on linen changing days (twice a week), they don't always change your linens. They just make the bed so that it looks changed. 
The Monday through Thursday evening "meals" are usually not much of a meal. They have a Tuned In night, which is just cookies, pretzels, and chips. Other nights are just a salad, or other simple things. And the food quality is not very good. Wednesday nights are usually the best, with The BBQ of hotdogs or hamburgers. The El Paso area has lots of great restaurants though (my favorites are Cattleman's near Fabens for an unforgetable steak, or Little Diner in Canutillo for homemade gorditas).
There is a brand new Homewood Suites by Hilton being built right across the freeway from this R.I..... which I think is going to give this R.I. some serious competition.

title: “My new favoriye place in NYC!”
text: This hotel was excellent in all respects. I called ahead to get some ideas for my trip and the person on the phone was so helpful. When my six year old and I checked in, they upgraded us to a beautiful room just because they said I was so nice! It was a busy weekend. The servers all remembered my name at breakfast, room service was great, and I got all the help I needed. I will be back at the Warwick on my next trip. It is a real gem!

title: “Cant wait to go back”
text:
This is the first time we had stayed at a Hilton, we were expecting high standards and we were not dissapointed . We had an "executive room" on the 34th floor, it was a very good size and the beds were REALLY COMFORTABLE, the same could be
said for the pillows, way above average. We had our breakfast - included in the room rate - in the 44th floor lounge, its a pretty standard continental breakfast, wont set the world on fire but filling and plenty of it. One tip here though is GET THERE EARLY we used to be there by about 7 and when we left there was always a long queue to get in as the capacity of the room is 99 persons and any more is illegal as the sign clearly points out!!!.
There is also free internet access in the lounge, you can either use your own laptop or the provided pc. Although it is shared with a lot of guests it works well as you just book a 15 minute slot, we never had any problems using it. The loung also provides free tea and coffe throughout the day upto 2245 and hors d'oevres at 5 pm, again the secret here is get there early.
I had read several rather negative reports on trip advisor about this hotel and I was a little apprehensive especially as it was part of a birthday treat for wife and daughter, but everything was fine To give an example one evening the bathwater was very slow to run away, i rang the reception and they were going to send up a plumber straight away !!! now that is what I call service.
There are two nearby subway stations, one by the Sheraton and one by the Radio City music hall, which is the one we used mainlhy as more lines go through it, both of them are less than a couple of hundred yards from the entrance.
One thing though which shouldnt happen is the Hilton's policy of charging 3 dollars 50 cents per bag if you leave it at the hotel after you have checked out and before you actually leave for the airport. In all the hotels I have ever stayed in no one has ever charged for this. I did object to the charge, pointing out I had paid a lot of money to stay in their hotel and didnt expect to pay for something which should be provided free. the charge was waived, so do query it and tell them how unacceptable it is. The lady in front of us collecting her bags was charged 21 dollars which does seem a rip off. 
This is a good hotel, in a great location in a truly world class destination, as they say NewYork NewYork its a wonderful town, and we were really really sorry to have to leave, 
Certtainly stay here again

title: “Awesome Hospitality and smiles”
text: I stayed at the Homestead in Tigard Oregon for 18 months for buisness and moved down to San Diego on buisness . I have been here now for almost 2 months and the Management and staff has made this a wonderfull experience in making myself and my team memeber feel like part of the family Emeil and Cheyne are always on the property talking to the guest and getting our opinions and concerns which we dont have any very well run property , The front desk staff is alwyas cherrfull and the housekeeping staff Violetta makes my weekly cleaning remarkable like I just moved in. Attention to detail will keep me coming back and this is one of the best properties I have ever stayed at. Great Job all !!!!!

title: “very lovely”
text: had a very nice room on the 27th floor. 2 fullsize dbl beds - great for friends sharing and nice seperat closet for coats and shopping to be stowed away in. Bathroom not so big, but all very nice and clean. extremely pleasant in all aspects

title: “Love this place!”
text: I've stayed here for business multiple times, and will continue to return. The location can't be beat (esp. for a Red Sox game) and the staff is extremely helpful and friendly. I recommend the Junior Suite - luxurious and spacious at a reasonable price.

title: “Excellent Location for Patriots Game”
text:
My fiance and I went down to Boston for the MNF game featuring the Patriots and Chiefs. We stayed at the Seaport because of its proximity to South Station. This hotel was extremely clean, well kept, and in a safe location. The staff was extremely helpful when asked questions about the area, and there were always cabs waiting outside. We did not pay for the harbour view room, but still had a harbour view, so don't waste the extra money. The beds were also extremely comfortable, and there is a fridge and safe in the room. 
This hotel is only a ten minute walk from South Station, where you can catch the Patriots Train on gameday. I strongly recommend this train as a way of getting to the stadium. There is a 7-11 convenience store and Dunkin Donuts right next to the hotel, and just down the street there is a pub called the Whiskey Priest (excellent food) and a Sports Bar called the Atlantic Beer Garden (tons of high-def tvs, and cheap beer). The Barking Crab (best seafood in Boston) is also a short walk from this hotel.
Overall, I strongly recommend this hotel because of its convenience to South Station, excellent service, cleanliness, and the amenities around it. If you are going to catch a Pats game, or are just visiting Boston, this hotel is an excellent choice.

title: “Great base for exploring SF”
text:
I stayed at the Pickwick for 4 nights at the end of August 2006 - sorry for not getting round to writing this review sooner! Overall it was a great experience - you can't beat the location, especially as a single traveler just coming in from the airport, so close to public transport, all amenities and attractions. 
The room was more than adequate - true, the mock French furniture are a little bit OTT, the TV/fridge console blocks off an entire corner of an already not exactly large room, and there is some wear and tear, but come on, for $70/night (Hotwire) I felt like I got an excellent deal. After all, this is San Francisco - so I spent all my time exploring this fantastic city rather than surveying my room through a magnifiying glass... I did like the view from my 4th floor window, too - right across from the MInt (and the San Francisco Chronicle, which I loved, being a journalist myself!)
I never used the restaurant or other hotel services, so can't comment on them. House-keeping was sketchy, and I did feel lucky to have the room all to myself - it would have decidedly felt cramped with 2 people in it - but on the whole, it was a great, clean base for exploring this fantastic city.

title: “not for families with small kids”
text:
We stayed in Bryant Park Hotel with our 2 small kids. We chose this hotel because of the location. Initially we booked the room for a week but after staying for 2 days we had to go to a better hotel. As we came to NY from Japan with 2 small kids we were having terrible jetlag. so it was normal to wake up in the middle of the night for all of us and making noise. Of course we were trying to keep children quiet as much as possible but it's not that easy to do so in a small room. So as the isolation wasn't good, we couldn't relax because of fear that we were disturbing our neighbors.
the terrible thing about the room was curtains without blinds and that thin, plastic roll curtain didn't fit the windows and the flashing light was making even harder to control children's sleep cycle.
The service was OK, food too. Just ones we tried to have breakfast early in the morning
but the restraunt was closed eventhough it was their opening time.
So,the location is good but I think for the same price it's better to stay in Intercontinental Hotel in Times Square, where everything is much better.

title: “Well-placed comfortable hotel”
text: We spent a week in this hotel while sightseeing in New York - we very much got the impression on arrival that this was an unusual length of stay, as I suppose it was given New York hotel prices, and this hotel is not cheap, but this was a special trip for us. In position the hotel was excellent - walking distance from Central Park, the Rockefeller Centre and Carnegie Hall, had it been the season for concerts - and with two useful subway stations nearby. The room was a good size, very comfortable, and the mini kitchen a useful feature. If I have not given it an excellent rating that is only because of the "complimentary breakfast". Breakfast on site is a definite plus in any hotel deal but the quality was poor and the staff offhand. A slip was provided to obtain a tip, minimum suggested 2 dollars per person,so that is what they got. Breakfast was served in the attached restaurant and it really put us off trying the restaurant for a meal. So a great choice of hotel in most ways but they need to improve the breakfast.

title: “Mark Twain - GREAT CHOICE!”
text:
My sister, dad & I just stayed at the Mark Twain hotel in October 2011 for 3 nights. 
If you're looking for a nice hotel that is reasonably priced, has friendly staff and is in a good location then this is your place,.
I spent HOURS reading reviews for everywhere I stayed all over the states & promised I'd post honest reviews when I got back so this is one of them.
If you're an impatient person that nit picks everything & is never happy & expects gold when you only wanna pay silver then you may not like that SOMETIMES the lift takes about 1 min, or that the lift isnt MASSIVE.
Location is great, 2 shirt blocks to Powell st where the cable car line is, one block from Macy's & other awesome shops.. A nice restaurant downstairs, cafe next door that does a cheap breakfast.. Oh and free water & lemonade out of a dispenser type thing right next to lifts which is handy when you don't have any on you & dont necessarily want a whole bottle - haven't seen this at other hotels. 
Taxi from airport was about $65-$70 but the hotel organized a car for us on way back to airport which was a really nice, big car (for all our luggage!) which was only $45.. So enquire about that first.
The rooms were cleaned really well - as in you could smell the cleaning product which was fine by me.
The room we had wasn't massive - no room to spread all your stuff out but had a decent sized walk i pn cuoboard & we werent there to chill in the hotel room! 
Flat screen TV with lots of channels.
Noise was fine, didn't bother me - can't even remember hearing much noise... If noise is something that bothers you perhaps request top floor but wasn't an issue for me at all.
All in all, good hotel - I'd stay there again & definitely recommend it.

title: “It was horrible!”
text: My wife and I (a young couple from Iceland) find it very hard to even give this horrible hostel a single point, maybe a half point would be appropriate for the hostel's just being there. Our experience was utterly terrible, but here we will only mention the absolutely "worst-of" West End Studios. It should be noted that before arriving we had no expectations whatsoever. After all, we had booked a "cheap" hostel in NYC. First, we booked a double bed room, but when we arrived we got a disgusting prison-like fall-apart bunk-bed room with an unclosable window (in NYC!) and a dirty unflushable toilet almost at the head of the bed with no door and a urine-stained floor. We're not even speaking of the bed, just to avoid the thought of it. There was no help whatsoever to get from the main staff (not all of which seemed to understand very simple english). We were given another room the day after, almost equally horrible and disgusting, with see-through holes around the door, broken furniture, a lot of stains on the walls and almost no lighting (to keep you from seeing the filth, I imagine). We'll have to stop here, before breaking into tears, but in short, there was absolutely NOTHIING OK about this hostel, except for the location (to be fair).

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text:
A grand old hotel located in City Center and within close proximity to fine shopping, dining, sightseeing this hotel has been upgraded and remodeled to fit today's travelers needs. The room features a large flat-screen television, wired internet access, and a large king-sized bed. The room was very well appointed. 
 We found the service at the hotel to be above par from the doorman through the concierge and housekeeping staff. In general, it was an excellent choice for a weekend in Philadelphia.
 On the down-side, our room... located on the 6th floor... featured a view of the back side of the parking garage wall. We found keeping the drapes closed helped immensely. Also we were booked on a package that included a museum exhibit and a continental breakfast. We wandered aimlessly for awhile trying to find that breakfast when I finally decided to ask directions. The concierge explained that there really wasn't any but if I went to the Tavern 17 and ordered a juice, coffee, and a Danish that the charge would be removed from my bill. Not exactly the same thing and in fact when we went to the Tavern 17 they had no Danish anyway and we ended up ordering a breakfast.
 We would definitely return to the Warwick should our travels bring us back to Philadelphia again.

title: “Near perfect stay near public transportation”
text: This hotel has it all. Clean, quiet, friendly staff, nice furnishings, great climate control. Local shuttle and easy access to light rail. Nice restaurant, lovely lobby. Can't name anything that didn't exceed expectations

title: “It was average.”
text: Firstly the location is great. We had a view of Lake Michigan and Navy Pier. Only 2 blocks from Michigan Ave. The lobby was nice and modern. Rooms were old. Rooms looked like a motel with a few modern pieces like a flat screen tv. The bath tub had scuffs in it. For $350 a night, I expected luxury, but it was average. They need to make it "cool" like the W in New York and not an immitation. Oh yeah, spa pool was nice but gym needed upgraded. Overall- location was perfect but hotel was not up to my W Hotel standards.

title: “Awesome”
text: This was the second time staying at the Resort. I would recommend it to everyone. My vist was on mothers day so it was not very busy at the water park. On the previous visit the water park was a lot busier. I think it was the middle of the summer.

title: “Excellent historic property, Halloween everyday!”
text: Really wonderfully restored historic hotel with many authentic restorative touches. However, guests do experience a true halloween type experience every now and then, i certainly did! The reception area is quaint ans special. The bar selection quite extensive. Great rooms, comfortable beds. The bathrooms are interesting with a window in them. Good turn down service.

title: “Nice Room”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights here in a Queen-Queen Room on the top floor. Had stayed here once before back in 2004 and I remembered the hotel being clean but the rooms being very small, so I was prepared for a small room....not so! THe queen-queen room was really big. Room had a fridge, microwave, dresser with 6 big drawers. Bathroom had a hair dryer. Closet had about 10 hangers in it plus an iron and ironing board. The room was clean and even though our room faced Broadway, it wasn't too loud. The only time we heard our neighbors was early in the morning (7am-ish) when they were all moving about but you could hear what they were saying - just general noise of door opening/closing. THe shower was clean and didn't show any signs of mold. The beds and pillows were really firm which I found to really help after walking around all day long.
Check-in and Check-out went pretty smoothly. Subway stop less than 2 blocks away and plenty of places to eat and drink nearby.
The downsides: one very slow elevator, the room was too hot. We slept with the window open and it was still warm. There was no way to control the heat setting in your room. 
I would definitely stay here again based on my most recent experience.

title: “Enjoyed our stay at the Tuscan Inn”
text: This is the first time we stayed at the Tuscan Inn, our room was very nicely furnished and the bathroom was neat and shiny. The location was great for sight seeing and visiting the many restaurants close by. The social hour between 5 and 6 p.m. was a nice touch. We met a very nice couple from Vancouver (even though the U.S. Olympic Hockey team got beat by Canada the Sunday we were there). The restaurant serves a very nice breakfast.

title: “Faded Grandeur”
text: This hotel is in a great position on S Michigan Avenue, opposite Grant Park and close to Van Buren metra station. A room at the back of the hotel gives you a view of the El and the Sears Tower and you can almost imagine the gangsters doing drive bys. The lobby and reception is just pure Americana. However when you try to find your room be prepared. If you are not an expert in orienteering you will probably be found in a blind corridor months later dead of starvation. I took the stairs down one day. Big mistake. Led me to a service area which hadn't be used since 1972 according to the faded yellow copy of the Chicago Tibune I found on a hatch way door. I opened a door hoping it was my way out but it just led to a brick wall. I found my way back to the elevator and went upstairs and started again. On the first night there was no hot water but there was the next morning. The room was huge but has not been refurbished since probably prohibition. I am sure the Palmer House has things that work whilst keeping to that original 1930s ambiance. But then the Palmer House is 4 times the price. Youse pays yer money youse gets yer choice.

title: “Absolutely lovely!”
text: The Riverwalk Vista has all the charm of a bed and breakfast - without the tackiness. It has the cleaniliness, decor, and amenities of a luxury hotel - without the high price. The staff was lovely and not at all intrusive. The breakfast and welcome cookies were delicious. Some reviewers speak of street noise, but this was not at all a problem for us. (White noise machines were in the room if a problem had arisen.) Parking was a bit of a hassle (you have to park in a deck a half-block away), but with the wonderful location of the hotel, you can't expect to park onsite. My husband and I adored this place and will definitely stay here again if we ever are again in San Antonio.

title: “What a hotel?!”
text: I have never stayed at a hotel like Yotel. The concept is really fantastic. I strongly recommend this new, hip, extremely well located hotel - and it wasn't even expensive!

title: “Not a good hotel for women.”
text: I have spent 25 years visiting New York..and would not recommend this hotel to women. The hotel is clean and seems nicely run, small rooms, no good dresser space...but lovely bathroom. Unfortunately I was awoken late at night with someone trying to enter my room and saying they were sent to pick up dry cleaning...I had the impression after reporting the incident that this was NOT an unusually occurance. They seem to customers who drink to much regularly! Also, if they had a full time doorman they were not present at all times, I don't believe I ever say one in the evening. Did not feel safe.

title: “nice room”
text:
Nice room, hotel good, spacious.
Rooms with wifi
with LCD TV, safety box
Bed very comfortable and large
with elevator

title: “It was a great stay!!!”
text: Almost everything about this stay was great!!!! The only thing I would suggest is having breakfast stay open a little later...... We turned in late on Saturday so we missed breakfast by 15 minutes..... overall a great stay !!! Cant wait to be there again......

title: “An excellent experience”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at Hotel Griffon on the 5th of July. After spending a week with family in the bay area we were looking forward to a stay in the hotel. Majorie was working at the front desk. She was kind and extremely welcoming. She went out of her way to give us directions and tips in the area. Our room was nicely appointed with a great view of the bridge. It was spectacular to look at night when the bridge was lit up. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Big, Crowded, and Average”
text:
This hotel is a classic example of being too big. The lobby feels like Union Station in D.C. There are constantly throngs of people always running throughout. It can get very loud.
The biggest advantage of the hotel is its great location, right on Michigan in the heart of the shopping districe. Another nice advantage is that there is a Starbucks right in the lobby of the hotel. The staff is friendly and helpful.
Some key negatives (in addition to the size/noise) include:
-Elevators. They are always crowded and take a long time to get to you (clearly way too many rooms/guests for the number of elevators they have).
-No wireless internet in the rooms. This is a HUGE negative for me. I can't believe that small little Marriott Courtyards all have wireless in the rooms and the big daddy downtown Marriott can't. What an embarrassment.
This basically is a hotel constantly at a frenetic place. There are far better choices in the nearby area that will make your vacation more pleasant.

title: “Worth the splurge”
text: The Fairmont is a beautiful hotel with top-notch service. We had a lovely dinner outside in the courtyard while live music played. Gym is beautiful, well appointed, immaculate. All the employees we interacted with were excellent. Location is halfway between foggy bottom and Georgetown--walk to either in 5 minutes. No metro very close by, but otherwise good location.

title: “Great location and friendly staff”
text: This hotel was a great find for a recent business trip. I love the Embassy Row location for two reasons: first, the street itself is fairly quiet - not a lot of street noise to wake you - and second, it's a block and a half from the Dupont Circle Metro Station for when you feel like exploring the city (and hearing all the noise). My room was large and comfortable, and the only issue I ran into was my in-room coffee service not being refilled most days. (A call down to the front desk always had that remedied, but it was still a bit annoying.) The hotel gym was one of the best I've ever seen with plenty of equipment and amenities. Most importantly, perhaps, I'd like to point out the staff, all of whom were exceptionally friendly and who constantly provided excellent recommendations for food, shopping, and entertainment at night. It is hard to get a rate here that is within our company's hotel limit, but when I can, I book here as soon as I know I'm going to be in town.

title: “Quiet”
text: If you are looking for a place to get away from the family and relax I would recommend this hotel. However, if you are relaxing to get away and stay in the room to watch tv, this is NOT the hotel. The TV was the worst for me. My whole purpose was to stay in the room and watch TV. You could barely read the guide on the TV to see whats on. Overall, it was nice and clean but being that this is mainly for business people, I see the TV is their least concern. I went twice two weekends in a row and still overall liked it.. MINUS my main purpose was the TV.

title: “Pretty hotel, but had some issues.”
text:
The Intercontinental Addison is a pretty hotel in a great location - hard to beat the dining selections available within a mile of the hotel...perhaps hundreds. But we had a number of issues, most especially the temperature. The ballroom hovered around 65 degrees for our two days of meetings, fine for some but cold for others. The exhibit hall never got below 80, which made for uncomfortable days. In both cases, the hotel management told us they would "work on it, but this is usually what it is like in the summer." Look, your hotel is in Texas. Texas gets hot in the summer. If you are going to host conventions and meetings, wouldn't you figure out how to make areas comfortable?
The problems weren't limited to the common areas. Of my group's fourteen rooms, only four or five were cool enough for comfort. The A/C kept cranking, but never got really cold air out. That's a problem.
That said, the in-hotel Starbucks is a nice touch, and the hotel bar is reasonably comfortable, though lacking a wide selection of finer liquor options. Free parking is also a huge plus. A note on this, too: the free spaces filled up by 9 a.m., leaving only the $10 garage. By 5 p.m., there were plenty of spaces. If free parking is full, consider springing for the $18 valet because the garage isn't come-and-go. If you leave even one time during the day, the valet option just paid for itself. Plus the garage is a bit of a walk, whereas the valet is at the front entrance.
I'd stay there again, but not during summer months.

title: “Excellent Service”
text: Valerie and Erica helped me through a difficult time in my life. The personal service i recieved made my whole trip to El Paso better. I was here for my mothers funeral and they helped me through it. Kudos to them. Thank you!!!!

title: “the most wonderful dc hotel”
text:
my girlfriend and i spent last weekend at the hotel which was wonderful, its got a great atmosphere ,the japanese food restaurant is amazing and the roof bar fun. but it was the staff who made it and especially Jeanine and Mark at the front desk who were so helpful and went out of their way to advise and help and make our stay so wonderful their service was outstanding
because of them we will now only stay at the Hotel and are making plans to return .
chris chappel

title: “Wonderful Service”
text: Just returned from a weekend stay at the Ritz-Carlton Battery-Park. The hotel has a good location, the rooms are very nice, and the harbor view is spectacular. However, the aspect of this hotel that is obvious early and often is SERVICE. I have stayed in many good hotels around the world, but I must say that each and every employee we met here is extra friendly and helpful, making it obvious that it is a prime management goal. We stayed on the Club level (which is well worth the extra charge), and the concierges there (Cullen and Angelica) absolutely bent over backwards to help us (e.g. excellent restaurant reservations, times & directions for attractions, a casual mention of our wedding anniversary resulted in many favors, etc.). We'll definitely be back....

title: “A very nice, roomy apartment within walking distance to Central Park. Lots of drawer space and pleasant staff.”
text:
We got the metro ticket for 29 Dollars and used it every day to get around. However,
we were happy to walk to very nice restaurants and were always impressed by the lovely tea and coffee facilities when we came back from anywhere. The coffee was great!

title: “Your basic Hyatt”
text:
This hotel definitely lived up to the Hyatt reputation- clean rooms, professional service, great pool, large grounds, etc.
My only complaint was that they charge for the business centre usage and for wireless. You'd think if you're paying a premium to stay at the Hyatt that they'd let you use the computer for free.
Also, being in my early 30s, I would probably stay in the Gaslamp district (about a 10 minute walk) next time I visited San Diego... More nightlife, action, etc... We took cabs into the area every night.
On the other hand, the bay area where the hotel is located is nice and quaint, if that's what you're looking for.

title: “best cost-effective hotel in the LAX area with great beds and great beer”
text: The Four Points Sheraton LAX is my favorite place to stay in the greater Los Angeles area, whether for business or pleasure. The park-and-fly deals and room rates are great and the beds are exceedingly comfortable. The property's proximity to freeway, airport, beaches, and local businesses make it a perfect selection for sleep, and the lobby bar with 100-plus beers also makes it a perfect place to host a business meeting or networking event.

title: “What's up with you Trip Advisor Reviewers who have made this hotel the Number 1 TA pick in Denver (Really?)”
text:
I chose this hotel based on it being the number 1 hotel in Denver on TA at the time I booked our hotel. I thought it would be conveniently located to the Airport as it had a free shuttle. 
I called the shuttle service once we arrived at the airport and were waiting for our bags. They told me to call back once we got our bags. So I called back in 10 min. once we had our bags and they said the shuttle would be there in 30 min. I asked why they didn't just send it when I called 10 min. ago and they said that was not their policy. We waited outside in 40 mile an hour winds for 40 min. for the shuttle. From the Airport it was a 20 min. drive to the hotel. 
We got all our bags out of the shuttle and went to check in (the desk staff was not very friendly or helpful). I had, as always requested a high floor room away from the elevator. Our first room was beds (head side) up against the elevator wall. After being in the room for five minutes we heard the (ding) of the elevator passing right where our heads would be that night (not to mention that it sounded like a roller coaster going by). They did switch our room but didn't seem very happy to do it. Although we were the ones inconvenienced by having to bring all our bags down to get the key and back up to a different room.
Our second room had pubic hairs all over the tub and a few hairs in the bed I slept in. I found the hotel room small and dirty. The swamp cooler was extremely loud and the hotel walls were thin.
The fitness room should be labeled a cardio room as it only had a few low quality cardio machines (no free weights or Nautilus equipment).
The best thing about this hotel was that is was next door to an Uno Pizza restaurant which we ate at for dinner that night.
We signed up in advance to take the shuttle back to the airport the next morning and all went smoothly (a little less than 20 min. to the airport early in the morning). That and the fact that I did feel safe at this hotel was the only reasons I gave this hotel a star at all.
I would never stay at this hotel again and I would question whether or not to stay at a Country Inn & Suites as this was my first experience and a terrible one at that.
Downtown Denver is about the same drive time from the airport as this hotel. After tipping the shuttle driver both ways and the inconvenience of the shuttle I suggest renting a car for $20 and driving yourself to a hotel in the downtown area. We also stayed at the Downtown Denver Hilton Garden Inn which I highly recommend and it was not that much more expensive than this hotel.

title: “AMAZING, AMAZING, AMAZING Pacific Terrace Hotel”
text:
We booked the Pacific Terrace Hotel mainly from the positive reviews on Tripadvisor.com, and true to the word of most people that stayed there, it was excellent.
From the moment we arrived at the hotel, Joe and Dan assisted us with our bags, parking the hire car, and all information required for our room and amenities.
The room was large and had two king size looking beds, plus enough room for a travel cot/crib. There was also a 40" TV, plus a DVD player, safe, ironing facilities, coffee machine, fridge and fully loaded mini-bar.
The room led direct to the swimming pool and jacuzzi.......as well as amazing views of the beach. 
Breakfast were "all you can eat" style, and there were plenty of choices for all the family. 
The hotel had a "relaxed" style, with all staff willing to chat as well as being extremely helpful and friendly. Enrico, Angela(s), Dylan, Mcgarity plus all the other staff were always so happy to help.
We loved the atmosphere at the hotel, it was always relaxed and easy going. All the staff always wishing you a "good morning/afternoon/evening" whenever they saw you.
The hotel itself is in a great location....overlooking Pacific Beach. You can people watch all day if you want to. You are only 15 minutes drive away from the City, but there is still so much to do and see that is walking distance from the hotel. Defiantly hire a bike and cycle down the broad-walk to Mission Beach.
There is no dinner service at the hotel but they do have a "charge back" option with a few local restaurants. They can also help with ordering a take-away if needed.
The concierge desk were also very helpful, getting our tickets for tours of the island and the zoo, helping with directions, as well as making my birthday extra special :)
There is 24hr access to their gym, which is small, but loaded with all the main machines required. There is also a laundry room, a conference suit and a spa room as well. 
One negative point about the room was that it wasn't that well lit, and the AC was a tad noisy.....but that is nothing when looking at the big picture.
Places eat at locally: Konos (go there for a big breakfast....but get there early), Naraya (great Thai food), Duck Dive (American grub with a fresh twist), JRDN (fine cuisine with great views), PB Ale House (get a table on the roof if possible), FireHouse (Try the wings!)
All-in-all San Diego was an amazing holiday for me and my young family, but it was made extra special thanks to all the great staff and the Pacific Terrace Hotel. Thank you guys. We will hopefully be back one day :)

title: “Good Stay”
text: The hotel is located to many good restaurants, bars and tourist things. The staff all were very helpful and nice. The bar at hotel is very up scale with nice service. The security is tight around the hotel which I liked.

title: “Decent Room, Thin Walls!”
text:
Pros: Location, Friendly concierge, comfortable room.
Cons: parking cost. thin walls and poor security.
I was down in San Diego for the weekend and booked the Hilton Gaslamp through Hotwire. Decent price and the room was ok. I understand this is a party atmosphere part of town, but the hotel party in the room adjacent to ours, kept my girlfriend and I up all night. Sercurity came once and broke it up, yet the party continued. I called security personally at 2:30am, security came again, and the party continued. Again, I know its a party atmosphere around this hotel, which is fun, but i shouldn't have to hear house music through the thin wall til 4:00am...
Whats worst of all is I wrote a letter to the hotel manager about the issue and he didn't have the time of day to even email me back. The W was so much nicer on our previous stay, and for just a few bucks more i'll stay there next time.

title: “Ok, could be better”
text: The service from the employees varies widely. The front desk was a mix bag. They were either extremely helpful or absolutely rude and unhelpful. The man at the concierge desk was too busy checking sports scores on ESPN.com which was in plain view than he was in helping a guest. The bell/valets were also a mix bag. The rooms are very nice though. Housekeeping did a good job and the location is nice. Whatever you do plan in advance when it comes to parking. HORRIBLE! Some went far beyond the call of duty; other s didn’t seem to want to do anything. I expected a lot more from a Grand Hyatt. Plan where you are going to park in advance.

title: “Amazing views, great location, really nice staff.”
text: This hotel was located a walk away from the venue where I got married. The views from the top floor of the Comfort Inn are amazing - panoramic views of the Bay area, including the Golden Gate Bridge. It's a short drive to get to Crissy Field which is a great beach and is where we had a catered BBQ the day before our wedding. They are a relatively short walk away from vibrant Fisherman's Wharf. The rooms were comfortable, on the modest side, and were very clean. The staff was very friendly and accommodating.

title: “Great stay above the High Line”
text:
My husband and I live in NYC and enjoy taking weekends "away" and staying at new or boutique hotels in the City. The Standard is in a fantastic location -- above the new High Line and steps from all the great restaurants in the Meatpacking District -- and is incredibly affordable. 
Although the rooms are a little small, even for New York standards, that hotel does the most it can with the space. The rooms have a nautical theme and floor to ceiling windows with spectacular views. The room was clean, there were good products, and nice sheets. Our room had a view of the High Line and the Hudson that was truly memorable. 
We think the Meatpacking District is one of the best areas in New York and so we were happy to have so many great restaurants steps away -- Pastis and Spice Market are two of our favorite.
If you are coming to New York City and want a hip hotel in a great location and at a discount, this is the place to be. You won't be disappointed!

title: “Filthy and owned by a RUDE family”
text:
We were promised a Fridge & Microwave and got neither. We asked about it, he said it got smashed and nothing could be done. Both of the Indian owners were COMPLETELY RUDE about it, no idea about customer service. Made it out like it was our fault, keep saying just check out, check out if you dont want to stay here. San Fran was all booked so we couldn't until the sunday. We also tried to use the hair dryer, broken, Phone, BROKEN! I asked about getting another phone, no way! Wifi was as good as dial up, we gave up. The place smelt, no elevator, limited parked. 
Im not sure anything is good about this place. We have been traveling for a month now, and this is the worst hotel i have stayed. 
DO NOT STAY HERE

title: “The worst customer service EVER!”
text:
My husband and I chose to stay here after seeing that the hotel was only minutes away from Balboa Park (San Diego Zoo), was recently remodeled, offered infant cribs, and had bunk beds (added bonus since our daughter has always wanted to sleep in a bunk bed). The pictures of the room sold us....but I should have known better. 
The room we booked online was the family suite, and it appeared quite spacious. In reality, it was the size of a regular room that had a wall put up to create 2 smaller rooms, hence turning it into a "suite". Whoever took the pictures worked some magic to make it look much bigger than it seemed.
When we walked in the door opened up about 3 feet away from the bed. The room also came with 2 TV's, one in each room. Unfortunately the TV's were located about 4 feet from one another which defeated the purpose of having them since you could hear one over the other even with the sliding door shut. The shower floor was old and stained and the tile floor appeared unfinished. 
Our biggest complaint however is the unbelievably bad customer services. Because we were traveling with an infant, we booked a hotel that provided infant cribs. Prior to our arrival I called as we were driving down there from Orange County (about a 90 minute drive) to ensure that the crib would be in our room when we arrived. The woman who answered the phone said she would have the crib delivered so it would be in the room when we arrived. Once we got to the hotel to check-in I asked if the crib had been delivered and her response was, "You asked for a crib?" I then followed to explain that I had called about an hour ago asking about the crib and showed her the printed reservation which showed the crib request. She proceeded to say they would send one up immeadiately. Thirty minutes after getting to the room, still no crib so I called down to the front desk and no one ever answered. This was after calling 3 times and letting the phone ring about 2 minutes each time. My husband then went down to ask where the crib was and again the person he asked stared at him like a deer in the headlights like she had no idea what we was talking about. Now there were only 2 females working that night and both were present when I asked about the crib 30 minutes before. Again they said they would send one and about 15 minutes later it was received with the attendant hanging around waiting for a tip. He didn't get one. 
The service was absurd and a far cry from what I expected having stayed at other Choice Hotels before. I will never stay here again and will choose to spend the extra $30 to stay at the Doubletree down the freeway or the Hilton next door.

title: “Great location, very clean and comfortable”
text: The reviews on this site were right on as usual! Stayed here for about a week while I attended a conference. The hotel's location was perfect, with a very short walk to the convention center and an easy stroll down to the Pike Place market area. Plenty of restaurants within a 10-15 minute walk, and the hotel's restaurant and room service were also quite good. All of the staff members were very nice and everything in the guest room was new, comfortable, and scrupulously clean. Highest recommendation.

title: “Nice except for the construction noise at 7am”
text:
I stayed at this hotel down by Hobby airport in March 2012 for business. I can't remember the room number - but I do remember that it was located right next to another room being renovated (sticky plastic on carpet outside door adjacent to mine). At 7am the next morning (which was fortunately 15 minutes after I woke up), I began to hear loud construction noises from the room next to mine (electric drills, hammering, etc.). 
Aside from that annoyance, the hotel is actually quite nice. The lobby is renovated into the new Courtyard style - which includes a bar / coffee station. This was nice since I was travelling with two co-workers as well and we were able to go relax in the lobby late at night and enjoy a drink while watching a basketball game.

title: “Indeed a hidden gem”
text: First class hotel in an unexpected neighborhood, excellent service levels, comfortable and accommodating. Nice common areas on lobby level, good fitness equipment and coffee available around the clock.

title: “The best in DC”
text: I recently stayed at this hotel with my family, which consisited of 3 adults, one child and one infant. The front desk staff was there to help all of us with anything that we needed whenever we needed it. Once we got to the hotel, we were greeted by the valet and then the doormen. When we got inside the hotel we were greeted by a lobby attendant and the front desk. Check in was a breeze. This is by far the best hotel to stay at when in DC. One of the best features of this hotel is its proximity to the national mall.

title: “Great Vacation Made Better By Drury!”
text:
Short review for those of you who don’t want to read the long review: it’s a great hotel and I highly recommend it!
 For those of you interested in details, here is the long review:
 This is the first vacation my wife and I have taken with our four year-old son. When he was younger we would vacation without him because he did not travel well (don’t worry, we left him with responsible grandparents). 
 This year we felt he was old enough to try to travel with him so we went somewhere close. We live in Las Vegas and decided to go to Phoenix. We thought about staying at an expensive resort like when we travel without him, but thought it would be wasted on him. Thus, we decided to spend a week at Wet-N-Wild and looked for a hotel close to the water park. Tripadvisor led us to Drury, which turned out to be a great choice.
 With all the great amenities and the low price of the rooms, I wonder how this hotel chain stays in business. We stayed for five nights (July 5-9, 2010). On the first day we got to the hotel about 45 minutes before the 3:00 p.m. check-in time. Rick at the front desk was more than helpful and got us the room we had reserved, the oversized one bedroom suite (see pictures). We went to Wet-N-Wild after we checked in until it closed at about 6:00 p.m. After changing into dry clothes we went to the evening light snack which is included for free with the price of your room. 
 However, this is way more than a light snack. My wife, who is a picky eater, thought the food was great (I’ll eat anything). They were serving hot dogs, Chinese vegetable egg rolls, buffalo wings, Idaho baked potatoes and assorted chips and salad. While it may not taste very good if you are a gourmand, it tasted great to my family and me. Even my son, who is also a picky eater, ate enough to fill him up. 
 Oh, did I mention that the evening food comes with free alcohol? Three free drinks per adult staying in the room. The hotel not only had beer and wine but also mixed drinks.
 As stated above, we booked the oversized one bedroom suite. It’s more than big enough for our family. The only drawback is the one bathroom in the suite can only be accessed through the bedroom. Thus, if you have someone sleeping on the fold-out couch in the living room portion of the suite and they have to use the bathroom, they have to go through the bedroom. The kitchen area is huge, probably too large to be using the space effectively. I’m not an architect, but I wonder if they could’ve made the kitchen smaller and somehow provided access to the bathroom through both the bedroom and living area or kitchen.
 I tried to find faults with this hotel but had trouble doing so; free internet, free breakfast and a large, clean hotel room. If I have to find any fault on the first day of our stay, it’s that the Cajun trail mix served at the nightly snack was stale. That’s a pretty small problem, however.
 This is how friendly the staff is: the nightly snack and breakfast is a self-serve set-up. After you eat, you throw your paper plates and such away. However, the staff working the food area, if they were not doing anything else, would ask how everything was and clean up anything you had finished. The service was better than some four and five star hotels at which I’ve stayed.
 The only real fault (Cajun trail mix aside lol) I can find with the hotel is the workout facility, which is small. It has five cardio machines to use but nothing else. The cardio machines are in good shape (three treadmills, one bike and one cross-trainer). Working out may not be important to all travelers, but I’m a workout addict and had limited ability to work out during my vacation. As a recommendation (if anybody from the hotel reads this), perhaps they could make an arrangement with a nearby gym (if one exists) to allow hotel guests to work out.
 Breakfast is just as good as the evening snack. Waffles, French toast, donuts, sausage eggs, biscuits and gravy, bagels, muffins, cereal, fruit coffee, tea, hot chocolate and juice. There is something for everyone. My son was very disappointed that there were no donuts the second morning of our stay (they ran out). However, they were back the third morning and for the rest of our stay.
 We spent each day at Wet ‘N Wild and our room was always clean upon our return. Even though we did not use all of the hotel supplied shampoo and soap, housekeeping left new soap and shampoo so there was always at least one sealed item in addition to the one being used. 
 The evening snack (okay, from now on I’m just calling it dinner) on the second day had the baked potatoes and hot dogs again but also meatballs (which were a little dry) and chicken strips (which were fantastic). I didn’t really want the Cajun trail mix again but wanted to taste some of it to see if it was still stale. Apparently, they opened a new bag because it was no longer stale. These items were rotated every other night with the first night food items, with baked potatoes and hot dogs provided every night.
 In summary, this is one of the best hotels I’ve ever stayed at. The staff was extremely friendly and the facilities (except for the workout room) are the best. Rick at the front desk told me they are opening up another Phoenix location closer to downtown in Tempe. 
 The only other recommendation I can think of for this hotel, and this is really being greedy, is to have desert (ice cream, cookies or whatever) with the evening food. Being on vacation and forgetting our diets, we went out for sweets every night after eating at the hotel. Regardless of whether the hotel adds desert to its menu, I’m still planning on going back, as it’s a great value.
 Side Trip Recommendation 1: Go to Sweet Republic in Scottsdale for ice cream after dinner. It’s a place I read about on the internet before our vacation that has fresh made ice cream and sorbet. It’s quite a drive from the hotel, about 20-25 miles, but it was well worth it. It’s some of the freshest ice cream I’ve ever had…and my wife also loved the oatmeal chocolate chip cookie they had.
 Side Trip Recommendation 2: The last night we were at the hotel we went to dinner with some friends that live in Phoenix. Go to Paradise Bakery, which is just about 1 mile north of the hotel in the Dick’s Sporting Goods shopping center and movie theater. My wife and I always go to this chain restaurant when we are in Phoenix, as they aren’t yet in Las Vegas. The food is great and their cookies are to die for!
 Side Trip Recommendation 3: This is the perfect hotel to stay at if you are going to Wet N’ Wild. If you go to the water park just twice, it is cheaper to buy a season pass. This is what we did. In fact, we had so much fun, we are planning to go back (and stay at the Drury Hotel again) in August.

title: “Very kind Staff”
text: I only searched for a cheap hotel in New York, because i only went there for christmas shopping. I searched around Timesquare (over the Internet) and found there the small hotel 41 and booked there a special christmas arrangement. The booking process over the internet was very easy and i received all informations i needed.
