The day i checked in, the reception staff was very kind and the room i got was really big and very lovely. The bathroom was a bit small, but more than the NY-Standard for that priceclass. During the stay, there was a room-service that worked as fast and exact as possible and a broken TV-Remote was changed just in minutes. So all together: I'll be back there, when i visit NY the next time.

title: “Great Bang for your Buck during Soft Opening”
text: This hotel was excellent for the price I paid ($235 plust tax), I stayed at the Gansevoort subsequently for $465 plus tax, and Rivington was just as good if not better. The room was large, funky with two big flat screen TVs (one in sitting room and one in bathroom), and had nice products in the bathroom and great views of Lower East Side. The service could definately be improved upon, the staff were friendly but over-worked and could have been more helpful but just didn't want to go out of their way (they wanted me to walk 10 blocks to buy and international adapter something I would expect to be standard and one of my TVs did not work on the first night).

title: “Great time”
text:
My wife and I stayed while attending the Republic of Texas motorcycle rally. The hotel is located downtown about a block away from 6th street. It is also within walking distance of the state Capitol. 
The staff was great. I was contacted about a week before my stay and asked if I any requests. I had several things in mind and the staff was very helpful with suggestions. 
When we arrived, check-in was quick. Everything I requested was honored. I always ask for an upper floor room. 
The room was not large but it was comfortable. The restroom was large with a walk-in shower. 
The pool is on the roof. It is small but the view is great. 
The staff was very informative about the restaurants within the immediate area and made several suggestions which were great suggestions. 
We are looking forward to next year motorcycle rally and will stay here again.

title: “Great location for parts of DC, but challenges for families”
text:
I stayed at the Liaison with my wife and son for 4 nights, in a room with 2 queen beds. It was extremely convenient to Union Station (we arrived by train), and an easy walk to the Metro at Union Station, Capitol Hill, and the Smithsonian museums at the east end of the Mall. 
However, by the end of the week the small size of the room (particularly the bathroom) left us feeling claustrophobic. In particular, the shower and sink were all in the same room, without an outlet to plug in appliances such as a hair dryer. In fact, we had to move items off the furniture, to have room, and then got charged for drinking the in room bottled water (which was simply stored in the cabinet) - the charge was immediately removed when we pointed it out. Also, the perks - the tour kit, special pillows, and exercise kit - were not really worth the effort; the iPod tour was unexceptional, and the exercise kit needed a DVD player which the hotel had run out of. Finally, the beds were elevated quite high, which I have frequently seen on business trips, but which was uncomfortable for family members.
Also, there wasn't any lounge or lobby area for a quiet place to read or relax. The lobby (with WiFi access) is adjacent to the restaurant and bar, which get quite loud. The pool on the roof was not as bad, and had a lifeguard.
The staff tried to be helpful, and generally succeeded; the concierge Michelle even reached out to us before we arrived in response to a question I had sent about a tour. (We drank a lot of the excellent punch by the front door.) These constructive suggestions did not detract from having a great DC vacation, but from the hotel's reputation, and the praise from a work colleague who had attended a wedding there, we had hoped for a better experience. (We avoided the restaurant because of its prices, in favor of nearby Subway sandwich shops, and our "splurge" meals at the Capitol and the Smithsonian.)

title: “Great stay!”
text:
All of the wonderful reviews of this hotel were accurate. The location is fantastic, literally on the trolley line and just a couple of easy blocks to Beale Street, Mud Island, the Peabody, etc. 
We had a "larger studio" which was just that - plenty of room to stretch out, with a slightly lofted bedroom area - great renovation of a historic space. Clean and comfortable. I was worried about soundproofing in an older building but we never had any problems. The rooftop has beautiful views of the river and the city - too bad we weren't there during the week to enjoy any barbecue! 
The art deco lobby is quite nice. The entire staff was very friendly and welcoming - a particular "thank you" to Tracey Henninger, who made sure my wife and I were treated well for our anniversary!
Our one and only complaint was the bed, which offered virtually no support - I'm not sure if we got an older mattress, because Residence Inn's beds are usually very comfortable ... but our aching backs agreed that this bed was terrible.
That anomaly aside, we had a terrific stay and will definitely return. Highly recommended.

title: “You may think this is a bad review...but it's not! Keep Reading...”
text: I found this hotel after doing tons of research. It was the best deal I could find (at least for a place that I felt comfortable staying in!). For $240.00 per night it was still pretty steep - but compared to the other hotels in the times square area for the dates I was traveling, this was was nice a bargain. When we got to the hotel, we had had TERRIBLE service from SuperShuttle, so I was not in a particularly good mood checking in. The desk clerk (who I am sure hear me yelling at the shuttle driver) was not super welcoming but she also wasn't unpleasant to deal with either. Then they told me I had to pay up-front; which is not the typical operation of a hotel. So my vacation did not get off to a good start. It was hot (our vacation happened to coincide with the 3 hottest days of the summer...over 100 every day!) and I was cranky and irratable after the flight and the horrible experience getting there. Then...we get to the room and holy smallville batman! there wasn't even room to walk around the bed - it was weged from wall to wall. But I had found in my travel research that hotel rooms in NYC were small. So okay - we will tolerate it. and Viola...finally a good vacation ensues! We headed downstairs to engulf ourselves in the wonders of NYC and find the nearest restraunt because we were starving. We stopped in the lobby to ask what they recommended nearby and the bellman was kind and most helpful. We were greeted when we returned by the nice bellman and a different desk clerk - and she was wearing a smile! Morning came and ...out we went into the great wide city. Passing thru the lobby we asked for extra towels for the rest of the week, and a wonderfully nice desk agent assured we would have them. We were also greeted by the kind bellman again, and there was a very nice continental breakfast to be had. Well...we got our extra towels. We got the extra blanket we asked for. There was fresh water bottles left for us every day, fresh soaps in the bathroom, and fresh linens. Every day we were joyfully greeted by the desk clerk and the bellman; and we had a splendid time! The service was good. The room was small but functional. The in-room safe didn't work and we were told the batteries needed to be changed; and I don't know if they changed them when we were out of the room; but we were never able to get it to work. It could have been the safe...it could have been us not being clever enough how to figure it out. All in all this was a good place; good price comparitively; and I would stay again in a New York minute!

title: “Heavenly Pillows”
text:
Overall, we had a very nice stay at the Sheraton. We were on a Globus tour (Hi to Al and
Niles). Our room was large and the beds and pillows were delightful. However, when we
arrived there was no soap to wash and we had to call down to the desk. They sent some 
up in a timely fashion. Also, the toilet kept on running, and the desk sent someone up
immediately to fix it. However, the repair did not last long and again we had to call down
to the desk to get this fixed. This time the repair lasted. We found some of the folks at
the front desk very pleasant and some others very unpleasant. We ate breakfast in the 
lounge and found it very good, especially the oatmeal. The hotel was only at 50% capacity
at the time and some folks who arrived later in the morning had to wait to be seated. Remember this if you have limited time. We found all of the breakfast staff to be very
helpful and efficient, especially Dustin and Chennelle. We also had a snack in the lounge
in the afternoon and found the food very good. There is free internet in the loung and quite 
a few computers available.. The Sheraton is very convenient to a lot of attractions. I am 
not an art museum person, but the Denver Art Museum was outstanding. The mall is right
outside the door and there is a free shuttle. However, whenever we sat down on one of the
benches in the mall to rest, we were approached by the homeless asking for money. We found the television easy to use and the air conditioning was fine for us. Overall, a pleasant stay.

title: “Great modern hotel in a great location”
text:
I made a one day trip to Los Angeles with my 20 year old daughter for an appointment at Cedars Sinai. We chose the Sofitel for it's proximity to both Cedars and the Beverly Center. I loved the hotel. It was clean and modern and gave us great service. I used Expedia to book and the check in was quick, they had all of the correct information which isn't always the case when using online booking sites. The staff was so friendly and helpful and great at anticipating your needs. 
 Gym was up to date and very clean and well stocked. Pool area is lovely, though loud as you might expect on a very busy street but so pretty. My only complaint is that the platform bed was a little hard.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
This is a great hotel for anyone wanting to stay in the heart of New York as it is situated a couple of minutes walk from Time Square.
Because the hotel is quite small, the staff were really friendly and the service better than most 5 star hotels I have stayed in.
The rooms looked like they had been recently refurbished and were clean and well maintained and continental breakfast was included in the rate. This really is a great base to explore New York for a few days.

title: “The place to stay pre and post cruise vacation!!!!!”
text: I stayed at the Quality after a cruise for 3 days and I enjoyed every minute of it. The service provided by the management and employees was very professional, accommodating and friendly! Would definitely stay at this property again because of hotel, staff, free breakfast, and location to cruise & airport shuttle. The rooms were very clean, bed and pillow comfortable. ! upgraded to the whirlpool tub suite for a few bucks more.The internet was very fast. I do wish they have more channels on TV. Breakfast had hot eggs and waffle very nice. The hotel is less than 10 minute walk to the needle, park and duck tour. The hotel shuttled us to local restaurants and Pike’s market place. i like the mercedes van very big and easy to get in.The front desks even help put together a tour to Boeing museum. The hotel was behind a large Walgreens. A Must see! I will definitely return to this property when in Seattle. I'm looking forward to coming back very soon!

title: “Great Inn”
text: This was a nice quiet inn right across the street from the riverwalk. The rooms were very nice and clean, the bathrooms were large and beautiful. I much prefer to stay in a small inn like this one, than a large hotel. The breakfast had a nice selection of fresh fruit, some sweet bread, sausage in a bread shell, boiled eggs. There were several things that made the stay not as nice as it could have been. First, as other reviewers have said, the arrival and unloading of the car was not the greatest. I was prepared for this, I thought. There were no spaces available in the unloading area for the restaurant next door, where you were supposed to stop and unload. Another couple were traveling with us, so one of the men got out and helped us get the bags out of the car and onto the sidewalk. Then while my husband and friend went across the street to find where we were supposed to park, my friend and I lugged the luggage up the flight of stairs, to the landing, in the summer heat to get them off the sidewalk. Not a nice way to start your stay. When we got up to the floor to check in, the innkeeper invited us to have lemonade and cookies. There were 4 of us, 2 glasses for the lemonade and 3 cookies. She didn't seem to notice the shortfall. Anything we asked about, she wasn't a big help. I asked about a map for the trolley and she said that was their most popular map and they were out. You would think if it was the most popular, they would keep a supply. I would stay here again, the service just wasn't what I expected. We did have one riverwalk view room and it was quiet, no problem with road noise. This was a weeknight, so maybe that helped.

title: “Great Location!”
text: This is a nice hotel, no doubt- just be aware when booking through any other site other than the hotel itself (I booked through a third party whom I think is best to remain nameless for this posting)- if you want to change your room from the "Traditional" room (which has one queen bed that felt like a double), it will cost you extra. We were initially told we could have a room with 2 double beds (or 2 queen's can't remember) and it wouldn't cost us extra. The next day we inquired about this and we were told that it would cost $50 extra- this is because we didn't book through the hotel directly. We decided not to opt for this, but were disappointed that a hotel of this standard and caliber wouldn't give us a room with 2 double beds (I personally do not call this an upgrade- 1 or 2 beds in a room are standard at most hotels). If the Omni Parker House believes third party booked customers not worthy of the same treatment as other guests, then why even use a third party at all? It could be our luck and others may say this has not happened before at this hotel, but it was a little disappointing to me and my friend. Other than that, the hotel itself is very nice and located right on the freedom trail close to the Boston Common, Faneuil Hall and Quincy Market and the waterfront. A tip- valet parking is $42 a night, so we parked at Center Plaza and from Sunday to Tuesday it only cost $60. Go to the Central Parking website and print off a coupon to save on parking! Besides the small rooms and slight disappointment with the information provided by the front desk, the hotel was great and and the staff are super friendly. The Boston Cream pie originated in this hotel and it's really good! I would consider staying here again if I came back to Boston.

title: “Home away from home.”
text: For me it starts with a hotel company that cares about it's guests. I have stayed at several Kimptons in the US and this is always the case. Eventi is perfectly located 2 blocks from Penn Station which is the easiest way to go to and from JFK. The rooms are larger than most NYC rooms and very well appointed. I wish I could spend more time in them. I always try to book Kimpton first.

title: “Great hotel - great location”
text:
Although the rooms are a bit small they are perfect for a long weekend stay. The location was excellent (a few steps to Starbucks and Union Square and a block from Macy's). BART was 2 or 3 blocks away so a taxi from the airport (SFO) was not required. The staff were excellent - friendly and efficient. All questions that I had (emailed) were answered quickly (within an hour or so). Coffee, tea, cold water and cookies in the lobby were a wonderful addition. I would definitely recommend the hotel for a stay in the Union Square area.
Did not notice air conditioning (may be an issue if it is hot) but had a great ceiling fan.

title: “very nice hotel”
text:
Stayed at the Magnolia 6/12-6/15. The room was very nice. ..looks new....a great size, good working space in room (desk with built-in electric plugs, lamp, wired broadband, comfortable chair). Bed was very comfortable, A/C worked great ....very nice bathroom .. no complaints.
Rate included Continental Breakfast (very good food), NY Times delivered to room every morning, happy hour (great deal) in bar 5-7 each night and cookies and milk every night for free in the lounge.
Location is very convenient for Downtown offices ---walking distance to most. Neighborhood looks iffy but there are several places outside the hotel on Main St if you've had enough of the food (good quality but a little expensive) in the hotel.
All in all, a very nice place to stay

title: “Appartment in NY / Perfect location”
text:
We stayed at the Affinia Dumont for 6 nights (2 adults and 2 teenagers). Our room was a one-bedroom-suite on 22nd floor with a perfect view to the Chrysler Building. The rooms were spacious and clean, kitchen and bathroom in good shape and the service perfect. The location was perfect as well. A lot of good restaurants and Delis around and only a 5-10 minute walk to Fifth Avenue. Nothing to complain about. We recommend this hotel, especially
when you are looking for larger rooms because of your children. We will be back !

title: “Average at best”
text: This is a large, rather impersonal hotel in a decent location [close to 6th street]. We stayed on the executive floor hoping for more peace and quiet, but it's hard to get away from all the partying at night. The food was only so-so, and it really peeved me that you have to pay to use the fitness center. Given the price and experience, we'll stay elsewhere next time.

title: “Excellent location and value”
text: An older hotel kept clean by a friendly staff. The location is downtown, close to Pike Market. Easy to/from airport by Light Rail for $2.50. Perfect place to explore downtown Seattle by foot. The rooms are more quaint than spacious, but cute in their old style way. Yes, you get sounds from the city, the hum of the elevator, and can hear your neighbors come and go, but this is a delightful hotel.

title: “Nice property, good service”
text:
This is a great hotel if you're visiting Six Flags Magic Mountain! You might even get a room where you can see one of the roller coasters, like we did.
Service people here care about guests. Just make sure you book your hotel shuttle rides to and from the park in advance. They get very busy during park opening/closing hours and they only have one van (7 passenger).
There are a few restaurants nearby, but you really want a car to get around if you're going to eat out. Valencia has lots of great places to eat.

title: “We can't wait to stay again!”
text:
My fiance and I stayed here for 2 days and three nights along with my mother, father and sister. We loved every minute of it! The hotel was so warm and inviting it made it hard to leave everyday. The hotel staff was very friendly and accomodating. The General Manager of the hotel, John Duponce, was at the front desk when we were checking in and came around to shake our hands and welcome us personally to his hotel. The rooms were exceptionally clean and comfortable. We loved the bathrooms! The restaurant, Bvd. 16, was absolutely beautiful. We expected the food to be average since we were dining in the hotel, but to our surprise it was amazing! The chef did an excellent job creating the menu. 
What we liked to take away from this hotel experience was the overall FEEL you get when it's all over. Sometimes its hard to pinpoint WHY we (people in general) feel a certain way. All we know is that it was good or bad. In this case, we felt at home, comfortable and taken care of. We felt good and Hotel Palomar made it happen. We will definately stay here again when we return to LA.

title: “For the price and location - excellent!”
text: Just returned from 6 nights spent in DC at the Embassy Suites. The hotel lived up to its billing and the reviews on this site. We were pleasantly surprised at the size of the suite. The staff was excellent - particularly the staff that mans the breakfast and the manager's reception. The breakfast is nothing to write home about - I like my eggs out of a carton and cracked, not out of a carton pre-mixed, but that's my prejudice. Here's where you get what you pay for. I was totally astonished however to find that the pints and cocktails at the manager's reception were complimentary. You can't even get this on a domestic flight anymore! If you're looking for cheap eats, try Chipotle on M street in Georgetown. One burrito and you're set for the day. I would also recommend Pan Asian near Dupont Circle. Very inexpensive Pan Asian food that's fresh and toothsome. Toronto has some of the best asian food in North America and I would count this place as a good facsimile. One street north of M, off Wisconsin, and you'll find a local hangout called, I think, Boogeymanger. The sandwiches here were terrific. It also seemed to be the only place open late (Georgetown late) for something to eat. As a sidenote, each time we went there we were privy to some student drama, or another. Kind of like dinner theatre by proxy. Bypass however Zed on M street. Though passerbys and diners had told us it was great, it's not. I should have given the $90 spent for dinner to a deserving charity. My best advice for eating in DC is eat near your hotel. If you're looking for food anywhere near the mall, you'll either pay heartily for substandard fare, or have a difficult time finding something decent (during the weekend many shops near Pennsylvannia Ave or Downtown were shut). Finally, the Embassy Suites did have in/out parking privileges. This proved to be a blessing for worn out feet. At night we made several trips to Georgetown for dinner and to the monuments. I've driven many places in the world and I must say DC at night was pretty easy. All the traffic seems to be in the 'burbs. A great trip at a solid hotel in a great city.

title: “Wonderful and fun”
text: My husband, brother and I stayed in one of the double queen rooms. How wonderful to enjoy a brand new hotel, decorated in a whimsical, colorful, modern style. Staff were excellent, the amenities fabulous, loved the walk-in shower (so big there's no need for a door) and the big flat screen TV with DVD player. Most comfortable beds of our entire trip. The prices were quite low for rooms of this quality. The free parking in attached garage, with elevator into the hotel, was a big plus. (Most hotels in downtown Seattle seem to be valet parking with 20 per night at minimum.) Location was great - easy walking to monorail, Space Needle, Experience Music Project, various theatres. I plan to stay here whenever I come to Seattle, and have already recommended it to many friends at work.

title: “Anniversary Trip”
text: Nice, clean, historic hotel. Friendly staff. Did not have a chance to try the LandMark restaurant for dinner but the breakfast was very good. Since it was our first time to Dallas, we chose to take a taxi to the Opera (Music Hall) and a Dallas Cowboys game. It was the best decision since traffic was quite heavy during the weekend. Hotel is walking distance to several shops and restaurants. If you are sensitive to noises, choose a room away from the street "Cedar Springs". The street is home to a local fire department station.

title: “Happy at the Chancellor Hotel”
text:
Our stay at the Chancellor Hotel was May 5 - 9, 2007. We were in room 1003 which faces east on to Powell Street with a view of Union Square to the right if you are close to the large window. The room was clean and fresh, linens crisp and bathroom spotless upon our arrival. The bed was extremely comfortable. Although this hotel gives a extensive menu of pillow options for its guests to select, the "standard" pillows worked great for us.There's plenty of room for 2 guests in this room. In addition to the bed, there were 2 nightstands, a desk area, chair & table, dresser and TV. The walk in closet was spacious and has a safe for storage of valuables. The water pressure in the shower was awesome. 1003 is a corner room and we did not hear any hotel noise or other guests during our stay. We do like the fresh air and the sounds of the city, so we opted to keep our window (and bathroom window) open during our time there. Seemed to us that unwanted noise would not have been a problem no matter what room we had been in. The few questions we did have about getting to our various destinations within the city were answered by the staff in a prompt, accurate and courteous manner. The staff has a very positive and helpful attitude.
For us, the convenient location,comfortable & clean rooms, value and attentiveness of the staff make this the ONLY place to stay in San Francisco. Looking forward to returning again!

title: “Boston, May 2012”
text: Third trip to Boston in less than two years. Booked the Commonwealth the first time account great reviews by other Red Sox Nation members. Despite its proximity to Fenway Park, the hotel is very quiet, both during and after games. The staff is friendly and helpful and more than willing to answer nearly any question sent their way. Complementary Champagne at check in was a welcome surprise after traveling 3/4 of the way across the country to get there.

title: “Excellent location”
text: We just got back from our first visit to NYC. We stayed at this location four nights. The location was great. It's only a few blocks to EVERYTHING. It's almost exactly across the street from the Grayline Tour center. Everything in times center is within walking distance. The staff were friendly, professional and courteous. The room was very clean and included wi fi at no extra charge, a 32" LCD TV with premium channels and all the current movies for purchase. We also had a fridge and microwave. There is a small pantry store open 24 hours a day with snacks, etc and a large grocery store right next door. The only thing we were not impressed with was their on-site resturaunt. The tables are so close together that other guest had to get up to let us in and out and the tables were so small you can't even open your menu. The staff were rude and the service was slow. The food was not great either and over priced. There is a little diner across the street that had a much better and reasonable breakfast menu.

title: “Nice hotel, right next to the Convention Center”
text:
Stayed for a convention. The hotel rooms were modern, clean and well maintained. The service was excellent. There is a very nice bar on the 27th floor. The regency club was a good place for light breakfast or to have 1:1 meetings. Exercise facility was also excellent with good mixture of equipment. There were many very good restaurants within walking distance. 
When walking to the convention center - need to be mindful of their light rail system. Easy to walk on the tracks without really noticing.

title: “Excellent hotel for the price, with extra good customer service”
text:
Stayed here for one week on a business trip to San Francisco.
At a corporate rate of $150/night including tax I think this is the best value hotel stay I have had in downtown SF, having paid more than $200 for much less nice service in the past.
The room was small but quiet and very comfortable, and the front desk staff were extremely warm and considerate. There are also multiple nice touches like l'Occitane toiletries and an ipod dock stereo which make the stay feel luxurious despite the cheap price for the area.

title: “Nice, but not my first choice for DC hotels”
text: I stayed at the Washington Hilton for a meeting held across the street; we had a steeply discounted rate. I generally dislike large conference-oriented hotels, and this was no exception, although it is a step above other similar hotels. The room was comfortable if bland. They charge an arm and a leg for internet access (as is typical for conference hotels-- one reason for my disdain). You are likely to have to walk a 1/4 mile from the elevator to your room. The restaurant has decent, if expensive, American food; presentation was nice, but I did not feel it was good value. Room service breakfast was good, abundant (2 types of meat with eggs and toast) and in line with what other hotels charge (which is to say expensive), but not a bad value. There are several bars in the hotel, which is nice for meeting up with colleagues after work. The fitness center was outstanding-- it is actually a club you can join even if not staying at the hotel. Overall, the experience is comfortable yet bland, sterile, and impersonal. The neighborhood is nice, but there are more appealing boutique hotels nearby.

title: “Doable for one night”
text: Stayed there for one night due to having to extend my trip and no availability in my current hotel. Cookie was nasty (must have been in that warmer a while). They overbooked and had to put me in two-bed room instead of king room. Very frustrating to me as I am a Diamond and at the least they should have given me a suite (which they did have available), she just didn't feel like giving me. Room was clean and quiet, though. I did not venture outside, but the area didn't look the best.

title: “Urgh. I could smell the pillow”
text:
I stayed at this hotel because I left it too late to book anything and had to sleep somewhere.
The room was a good size, but I could hear the karaoke (or that's what I think it was) from the Mexican club next door. Biggest dissapointment was being able to smell the odour of the pillow. Yeuch!
Breakfast was included, but selection was very limited - there are only 4 tables in the lobby where breakfast is served.

title: “Fantastic”
text:
Hey, if you're looking for a quality room in a reasonable quite neighborhood, try this Tribeca goody. Just steps away from the subway, excellent staff and comfortable beds. So they didn't have a breakfast buffet...you're in the city..have it delivered.
However, I do recommend that you tell cabbies to take you to the Tribeca Park because some don't know where the little side street York is located. We left the cab and got the Fire Dept guys to direct us. Cool!

title: “Really nice!”
text: This was our spot to stay for attending a Saturday wedding in Philadelphia. The staff, room, location and breakfast were all fine, and the historic building and restored decor were lovely. They even keep some snacks available throughout the day, and were very good with recommendations for sights and restaurants.

title: “Bizarre 70s hotel”
text:
I wouldn't have stayed here if I hadn't been attending an event here but I was perfectly satisfied with my stay apart from the room rate (I had to share with a colleague in what are quite small rooms) and the layout. The hotel is organised around four towers with its facilities and meeting rooms scattered across the five common levels with minimal signage. (One panel I planned to attend was cancelled because nobody could find the room!) Be comfortable with your body if you plan to use the gym because it has see through walls and extra exercise equipment located outside on the bridgeways... we could watch the gym users exercising as we walked between meeting rooms on the third floor!
Services seem much higher priced than average - many of my colleagues were complaining about printing costs and the paid wi fi connections are one per computer not one per room (the other person in my room had to buy a separate subscription). Compared to some other US hotels that host conventions the good point is lots of cheap or casual snack/lunch options rather than just having an overpriced hotel restaurant (though it has one too) - that said 6-10 outlets seem to have recently closed, although the microbrewery is still going strong. 
Beds in the rooms were extremely comfortable with the usual US overabundance of pillows; bathroom was pleasant and very clean although one couldn't actually sit down in the shower bathtub.
If you're scared of heights you'll want to avoid this hotel as all rooms are accessed by lifts that run up the outside of the building (and plunge into a feature pool on their way down to the lobby). 
As the last word on the hotel layout I was told by someone else at this event that the Bonaventure has been used as an example in a famous book on postmodernism in the arts... Or if you know London, picture four AA batteries standing on top of the Barbican Centre and there you have it.

title: “Great location in Union Square”
text: So many reviews had mentioned the picketers, but we didn't see any when we were there on a Tuesday and Wednesday. The room was decorated with fun and funky lamps and faux croc headboard. The room was small, but still managed to be big enough for 4 women with all of our stuff to have room to move around.

title: “5 Star Four Seasons”
text:
The Boston Four Seasons is the only AAA 5 Diamond, Mobile 5 Star Hotel in all of New England as well as being very highly rated by T&L magazine and several other publications. Now that we have the opinions of the experts I'll have a go at it.
 My wife and I decided to visit Boston for 3 nights over the 4th of July. We selected the FS based on location, reviews and reputation. 
 Our room was a Deluxe Garden view room on the 5th floor overlooking the Public Garden. The room was well appointed and seemed to be recently renovated. I was told that the hotel recenty completed renovation of all their guest rooms. Some earlier reviews on this forum expressing concerns about the need of an update can now be put to rest.
 We found the Bristol Restraunt and Lounge to be excellent. Everything was well prepared and served. Request a table by the windows for a great view of the Public Garden across the Boylston Street.
 The complimentary Downtown car service is great and the driver was very helpful with local information.
 The Concierge Desk was well staffed with knowlegable and helpful people who seemed to take the busy holiday crowd in stride.
 The 2 young men in the pool/fitness area went beyond the call of duty keeping the area open late for guests to watch the Fireworks from the glassed in 8th floor vantage point. they even had a radio playing the Boston Pops performance that went with the fireworks.
Lemonade, cookies and brownies were also provided.
 We had a great stay and would happily visit this hotel again. Their are a number of fine hotels in Boston but I believe the experts are correct and this one is just a bit above the rest. And I am a great fan of the Ritz Carlton chain.
 The housekeeping staff is very professional and keeps the hotel in imaculate condition 
The maintinance staff must be exceptional becuase everything works perfectly, not so much as a dead light bulb and we never saw a single maintinance person during our entire stay. How do they do that?

title: “Worst experince ever”
text: This is not a place you want to stay! Hotel staff has no control over the property. There is No security. Crowds gather in parking lot as early as 9pm with the music so loud it rattled the windows. Called office starting at 11pm, called 3 times. Then at 2am I made a appearance at the office. Still nothing was done about the crowds, loud music, gun shots and false fire alarm. At one point I looked out to see the the security gaurd posing for pictures with some in the crowd. I WOULD NOT STAY HERE IF IT WAS FREE. After talking to the so called general manager nothing was offered but a upgrade on our next visit. Next visit, you got to be kidding. Now about not charging me for the 3 rooms I stayed in. Costing me $400.00. Not a chance

title: “Awesome hotel -Definitely not your average Courtyard!!”
text: This hotel is not what you think of when you think of Marriott Courtyard hotels- instead it is in a beautifully restored 1920's historical buillding renovated in the 90's - - this hotel exceeded our expectations in every way-from service, cleanliness, room size, ammenities- (free wi-fi in every room, fitness club, small pool perfect for young kids, etc),- especially it's fantastic location. We walked to the Museum of Art and the Rodin sculpture garden and then took the $2 Phlash bus back -The hotel is located right by city hall and has a gorgeous lobby with free cookies and fruit flavored water and a comfy waiting area - it also has a modern bar/restaurant on ground level- we were so surprised at how nice this hotel was and how reasonable the room rates were - definitely would stay there again and have already recommended it to friends-

title: “Worst breakfast we encountered”
text:
After five weeks on the east coast of USA,we had stayed in many Holiday Inns, Hampton Inns, Embasssy Inns etc. 
Without doubt this hotel had the worst buffet breakfast. Even allowing for the disgraceful use of disposable cutlery, crockery etc that we encountered everywhere in the USA, I cannot believe that so many reviews accept chocolate iced donuts, cardboard muffins, fruitloops, the sweetest orange juice ever , white bread for toast , overripe bananas, and flowery apples as a "great breakfast".
Travel to Australia, Italy and New Zealand and find out what a good breakfast means! Avoid the breakfast and go just a block away on the corner of Taylor and Lombardo to a really great, cheap cafe for smoked salmon bagels,really good coffee etc, so good for around $10 a head that it covered lunch as well.

title: “promises unkept”
text:
We stayed at the Chicago Blake for 4 nights at the end of May 2010, and we left with mixed feelings.
While the location is great if you want/need to be near the Loop (CTA close by, Blue Line perfect for airport transfer) and Grant Park (Buckingham Fountain), and the personnel we met was welcoming and friendly, the Hotel appears to “over-promote” its virtues.
Our reservation confirmation clearly states “floor-to-ceiling windows”, which our room had not. And while it might be true that some rooms offer “spectacular views of Chicago”, ours faced the windowless side wall of the neighboring at&t building. The “Savvy Shopper's Hotel Blake Guide to Chicago shopping complete with directions, shopping tips and an assortment of exclusive discount vouchers“ we were promised in the confirmation never materialized. The “Continental Breakfast” on the other hand was there, but we still wonder what continent they refer to. It was mediocre coffee, poor pastries and some fruit, put at disposal in the lobby, more or less in front of the counter. Complimentary minus the compliment.
We will return to Chicago, but we won’t stay at the Blake again. When returning from our tour around Lake Michigan in early June we had another 4 night in Chicago, this time at the Belden-Stratford opposite Lincoln Park. Not as convenient a location, but a much nicer place that -in stark contrast to the Blake- keeps more promises than it makes (including a decent breakfast) for a lower rate! Chicago 2011 for us will be no Blake, more Belden-Stratford.

title: “Great comfortable room in a stylish hotel”
text: We booked two deluxe double doubles and the rooms were spacious. The beds were comfortable. The room was very hot despite turning off the heat and turning on the A/C. The second room had some plumbing issues. The staff was really friendly and helpful and displayed none of the superior attitude that you often encounter in upscale hotels.

title: “Meets Expectations”
text: Ideally located in San Francisco, this small luxury hotel offers nice accomodation and interesting packages. Rooms can be pricey if you don't book in advance or don't get the best deal, though. We had two successive bookings for two different room types and, as I would have expected, we have been upgraded to be kept in the same room. That in itself justifies the maximum rating given. Service was efficient and friendly throughout, with the right balance of attention and discretion. Nice room layout, fittings still in their prime (or feeling so) and a respectable size bathroom with separate shower and bathtub, and Molton Brown amenities. LAN and wireless, and laptop-zise safe. Room service is efficient and food above average. Excellent breakfast if at a price (but certain packages include discount on breakfast and one free item of dry cleaning). The only hiccup was that one full internet charge is applied per device connecting to the wireless, and these days it is common to have one iPad and one PC. However, at checkout, the front desk staff agreed to waive one of the wireless charges. It would have been harsh indeed not to give the Taj the maximum rating.

title: “Figueroa - happily go back”
text: Surreal, you expect to find a privtae dectyetive in a long trench coat to come out from behind the wardrobe. The wind whistles through the gaps in teh windows and the ploice sirens wail away all evening, but this is LA.We stayed here as part of a longer coach tour. Situation is execellent, near to Macey's, the Staples convention centre etc. The atmosphere is something else, a mix of Moroccan/Indian/Mexican and all the rooms are tastefully decorated. OK, its' dark, and if you look closely the decor needs attention, but it's an experience. Has a great little cafe (a bit Cuban?).The only gripe was the price of the beers!

title: “Very nice, posh hotel”
text:
I really enjoyed staying in this hotel. The room was huge, bathroom exquisite and was just a block away from the George Brown Convention center. Staff was very nice, helpful and maid service was twice a day.
Just a couple of things that I would make note of is that there was no coffee maker in the room ( although it had slippers, robes, etc). The other thing was that my room was next to what I assume was the laundry room as heard the dryer running throughout the day. Ear plugs worked great for an afternoon nap.

title: “We crossed the us and this is , hands down, the best choice!”
text: Since the second we walked in we were in such good hands. I've never seen people so polite and kind and making such a big effort to make us feel home. Excellent motel.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
The good:
1. The property was well maintained and had a modern feel to it
2. The morning front desk associate was extremely helpful during check-out.
The bad:
1. Valet service did not care much for my car, spilled water in my back seat and carpet and did not tell me. There was an ice chest in the back seat and by the time that I got my car back, all the water have already spilled in the back seat and the floor. My backseat and carpet were wet overnight. My wife and I have just driven from the Carmel/Big Sur Area without the ice chest tipping over so I know that they were driving my car recklessly. Also it is impossible that they did not know about this as I heard the ice moving around through out our drive. They would definitely hear it tip over. For $45 valet service, I expected so much better. (This alone will prevent me from coming back to this hotel)
2. Poor movie quality - After the drive my wife and I just wanted to relax in room and watch a movie. For $15.95 I expected much better quality. I have been through multiple hotels in San Francisco and outside the country, and the image quality in Hotel Nikko is undoubtedly the worst. I have no issues paying $15.95 for a movie, but for the quality that I got, I was pretty disappointed
3. The evening front desk associate was efficient but very cold.

title: “Going back, again and again :o)”
text:
I stayed at this hotel in August 2009 for the first times - spending a few days in NY on my own after going to the West Coast, and was conquered at once! 
In March, I went back to New York for a week with two friends, and after a lot of search, I booked a room there again as there was no reason to book anywhere else!
We are now going back for New Year's eve, and the hotel has been booked since May - no doubt about where we're staying anymore! :o)
The Quality/Price comparison is really good, free breakfast is definately a plus and the room was always spotless when we came back after a day out and about! 
The location is just perfect, close to Times Square but not in the midst of it all, which allows you to sleep (when there is some noise, earplugs are more than enough to sleep like a dream), especially because the matresses are very comfy!
If you are still doubting about where to stay, don't! This is the right place to be in New York City!

title: “A very average fairmont”
text:
More a convention property than an upscale Fairmont property.
Well located near the Art Institute and Millennium Park, this is a good property that delivers little of the personal services you expect at a quality Fairmont property.

title: “Good location”
text: Great place to stay if you have an event at the American Airlines Arena Center. I loved the pool area. My husband and I enjoyed just sitting around the pool. The staff was very friendly and easy to work with. We would stay there again without hesitation.

title: “Beautifully Renovated and Close to Everything!”
text:
This hotel had a complete renovation a couple of months ago and it really shows. The rooms were modern yet inviting (not austere at all). The service was top-notch and the rates are great. Although this hotel is not in center city, it's close to downtown and also close the suburbs that I had to visit.
The Front Desk was super efficient, fast and friendly. They are very well trained and are clearly there to help you with whatever you need. Bell desk was the same, very friendly and efficient. Unfortunately, I didn't get a chance to speak with the Concierge since they weren't there past about 9PM.
The renovated rooms are modern, large, and comfy (Room 655). The finishes are stylish and it shows that no cost was cut. My favorite part of the renovation was the bathroom. Everything was super clean, sleek, and gorgeous. There was no tub in the bathroom which may be bad for some, but it was ideal for me. They also have the European electricity management system where you need to use your room key to turn on the power in the room. GREAT IDEA! I'm so glad they took the initiative to be a greener property (the entrance lights work without the key in there so you don't have to find where to put it in the dark).
Room service was super fast and friendly, but the quality of the food was just average and they got my breakfast order wrong one morning. They offered to send up the correct order, but I didn't have time to wait. Prices were standard for hotel room service. Internet was $12.95 for every 24 hours, so I decided just to use my smartphone.
The one absolutely TERRIBLE thing at this hotel is parking. You're required to valet @ $35 per night. I'm sorry to say the valet employees are AWFUL. They have no sense of customer service and you can tell they hate their job. The lot was full for non-guests one night and they just came up to my car and told me I couldn't park there. I was confused of course since I had been parking (and paying) for two days at that point and this same guy had parked my car for me. I asked him where guests were to supposed to park, when he realized that I was a guest, he said I could in fact park there. No apology of course. This was pretty much the level of service I received from them the entire stay (what a waste of tip money). I later found out the valet is NOT run by Hilton, (thank goodness) but a third party company, and it shows. Unfortunately there is no substitute in the area besides a garage two blocks away for only $3 less.
Lastly I want to talk about the living room. There's this gorgeous library/living space on the lobby floor that is so warm and inviting. Very comfortable seating and warm fireplaces on a cold night. Don't miss out on this great amenity!
All things considered this place was stupendous and one of the best hotels I've stayed at. Parking in any city is just about always a hassle and this is no exception. The guest rooms are comfortable and beautiful. Service is top notch. I'll definitely be back!

title: “A gem of a hotel located in the heart of the performing arts district of San Francisco”
text: The front desk staff went above and beyond the call of duty to assist me.

title: “Exceptional Hotel and Staff”
text: I called into the hotel before my daughters and her fiancee's stay at the hotel and spoke with a staff member named J.J.. I explained it was my daughters wedding that upcoming weekend and needed certain accomodations for their stay. He said he would get with a supervisor and call me back. He did call back in a timely manner and was able to go above and beyond his call of duty and more than accomodate our needs. It was so nice to feel comfortable with the person on the other end of the phone and get our needs taken care of. Hats off to J.J. and Westin Hotel. Thanks for making my daughter's and her fiancee's wedding weekend a memorable one.

title: “Thanks for the enjoyable stay”
text:
My wife and I stayed at this hotel from 11/24 - 30 and could not have been happier. We checked-in late afternoon on Thanksgiving day the and the clerk at the fron deask could not have been more plesant. Check in was very smooth and she informed us about the free breakfast and weeknight social hours. 
We had a nice 1 bedroom suite with a very nice kitchen. The sofa and chairs were very comforatble as was the bed. Morning breakfast vaired by day but they always had eggs potatoes and meat... along with juices, coffee, muffins, bagels and bread for toast. They also had fresh fruit, oatmeal and cereal. There was always plenty to eat. One day the attendent brought us out some bacon and appoligized that he had put out sausage 2 days in a row. He recognized us from the day before and that showed the attention to customer service the hotel has. 
The whole stay was a pleasue and will return the next time we are in Austin
There were only 2 small things that I noted.
1. We were in building 1 on the secind floor street side and there is a bit of road noise... it do not prevent me from sleeping but may cause some lite sleepers issues.
2. The electrical plug under the window was "worn" out so plugs would not stay in. The power cord from my laptop would just fall out. It was not a huge deal and I just plugged in my computer elsewhere.
I hva no doubts that if I would have alreted the hotel about the plug they would have sent a maintenance man to fix it... that is just how good they were

title: “Met our needs for short DC trip”
text: After reading the reviews for 4 Points, I was a little nervous! Turned out nothing to worry about. A basic hotel, clean room, comfortable bed,convenient location, early check in not a problem and nice front desk staff. Noise was not an issue since we were at the end of the hall on the 9th floor. Booked package-hotel and air thru Orbitz . I never do that, but the price came up unbelievably cheap (less than $100 per night including tax). No other comparable hotels came close to this rate. All in all, was very pleased!

title: “Big Disappointment”
text: I was anticipating my stay at what has been described as a world class resort and could not have been more disappointed. We asked for a non-smoking room but there were ashtrays in our room and the room smelled terrible. The hallway smelled worse. The air conditioning is old and noisy, we ended up having to turn it off to get some sleep. You have to call if you want turn down service - something I have never heard of at all of the hotels I have stayed at around the world. We called one night and they never even showed up. There were no wash cloths in the bathroom, there was mold in the bathtub grout and the light next to the bed did not work. The jets in the hot tub near the spa didn't work and all of the pools and hot tubs had unsightly cosmetic problems. Service at the pool bar is terrible. Service from the rest of the staff is almost non existant. I would imagine this resort will not continue to get the ratings it has enjoyed in the past.

title: “Clean, quiet, beautiful!”
text: This was an overnight stay that was in a convenient location for us. The room was very clean, quiet and beautiful. I ended up with a king suite because I booked at the last minute and that was all that was left. It was reasonably priced and worth it. I would definitely stay there again. Great breakfast also!

title: “Good service, nice stay”
text: Stayed here a week while visiting Denver on business. I was originally given a double room but the front desk gave me a king room after I requested the change. The rooms were clean and the breakfast was good. The location was also close to several good restaurants.

title: “Blood on the sheets!...yuk!”
text:
I must say that the staff was very friendly. I commend the young lady working at the front desk. She was very accommodating to our requests. Now for the bad parts... The dead bolt locks on my door and the door of my travel partner didn't work. My travel companion moved to another room which was better and the door lock worked.
It was a bit noisy as the hotel sits between an exit and entrance ramp to interstate 405. The neighborhood is very run down. There is a closed gas station across the street with fencing around it and multiple homeless people hangout at the subway restaurant next to the gas station. Most of the shops near the hotel have bars on the windows. We did NOT feel safe enough to walk one block to a restaurant near the hotel. This hotel realizes the danger as there are multiple security guards on duty at night. These guys are huge! While it was nice to have security, it is evident that there is a need for the security. These guys looked like they should be playing Pro football! My biggest concern was that after I slept in the bed, I found dried blood on the sheets on the opposite side when I awoke in the morning. Thank goodness I slept on the other side of the bed. This is an open air hotel. It is not enclosed! The hall way floors are all cement for weather.
I travel extensively for my job so I am accustomed to staying in various levels of hotels. This was the first time I ever had doubts as to whether or not I would be alive in the morning. I actually barricaded my door since the dead bolt lock didn’t work. I didn’t get a lot of sleep and we left as soon as possible in the morning.

title: “great hotel”
text: We booked as a package with flight. They upgraded us. Nice clean modern decor. Great location at Grand Central Station. Near everything and just a short subway ride to Time Sq etc.

title: “Great Location”
text:
We stayed here May 27th - June 2nd. Perfect location, clean, tidy, great maid service, breakfast at $4 a head more than enough.
Staff informative and helpful when required. Best meal of the week was a pizza at Angelos next door. A beauty. We had a room on the 10th floor, a double double. Bathroom fine, shower worked perfectly all week. Air con in room was great, noisy but show me a unit that runs quietly. We did sleep with window open one evening, dont bother its like being next to M25. Take the aircon unit anytime.
As for Manhattan we felt safer here than we do in central Bristol. Didnt here any bad language or witness any violence all week. Would certainly return to Manhattan and definately this hotel.

title: “Uhhhhh...Not So Great”
text: Just of bit of background...we are a family of five and Hilton's Homewood Suites is our brand of preference. Still, my six-year-old daughter and I decided to take an impromptu trip to Chicago and wanted to stay at a different hotel. We picked Doubletree because of the location and based on some of the reviews. We arrived at O'Hare and decided to take the subway in order to get a true feel of the city. The subway ride was entirely long and the train stop (Grand - Red Line) was quite a distance from the hotel. When we arrived, the lobby looked rather contemporary and new. The front desk staff were reasonably hospitable. My disappointment is with the room itself and the amount of noise you can hear in the hotel. Every morning and evening we would hear the other guests coming and going through our room door. It was so loud that one night my daughter and I jumped thinking someone was trying to get into our room. Then one guest must have been checking out at 5:30 in the morning so we were unfortunately awakened then as well. I so wanted to get some rest on my vacation since the whole purpose was to releax and have fun. We simply weren't able to do so at this hotel. We could also hear through the relatively thin walls. The noise reason alone will be the reason I will never return to this hotel. The beds were indeed comfy and as one reviewer already noted, the pillows weren't so great. There was a lot of settled dust around the nightstand (on the clock, the lamps, etc). The problem with that is it indicates the areas were not cleaned prior to our use. The bathrooms were just okay. We stayed in room 2507 and the cabinets in the bathroom were damaged and the door had visible dirt. The shower curtains were extremely fresh and had just been laundered. The towels were clean and so was the sink, toilet and tub. The shower head had an extremely soft flow and there was definite temperature restrictions on how hot you could make the water. I do feel we would have better enjoyed our trip at the Hilton Homewoood Suites. Not only was it much closer to the Magnificent Mile, it was much closer to the Subway. Also, I'm sure it was quieter since I didn't see guests complaining otherwise. I will also say that the Concierge (with the exception of a lady that was working Saturday, Sept. 19 in the evening) and the staff in the restaurant were extremely friendly. Also, the hotel is reasonably close to Navy Pier. Chicago is definitely a great city to visit! I will definitely be back but just not necessarily at the Doubletree.

title: “Swissotel - A Great place to stay.”
text: After reading alot of hotel reviews on Tripsaver, my wife and I liked what most people had to say about the Swissotel. So we booked a three night stay for the first week in Sept. We were not disappointed. From the beautiful lobby, to the freindly staff, to the spacious room, we were impressed. The view from our room was spectacular. It overlooked the river, the lake and Navy Pier. We were in walking distance of most everything we wanted to see. Millenium park [loved the bean], Mag mile, Rush and State streets, and Navy Pier [you have to have lunch at Bubba Gumps]. We also had dinner one night at the Palms in the Swissotel. The food was excellent. We plan on coming back to Chicago during the Christmas season to do some shopping and see all the decorations, and yes, we will stay at the Swissotel. What a GREAT city!!!!!!

title: “Funky Hotel, Good Location”
text:
Cool hotel, nice big room and comfortable bed. Great coffee in the lobby in the morning and accomodating staff that were fairly helpful if they knew the answers. Tough finding out about local transit except for the Metro which is a bit of a walk.
Odd little bar/cafe in the hotel - emphasis on funkiness instead of comfort, went there a couple of times but found better quality and value down on P street.
A few technical glitches during the 4 days but nothing drastic. Hotel could use an upgrade to things like wallpaper and furnishings, but hope they don't lose the chic stylings.

title: “Nice but business hostile”
text:
This is not the place to stay if you have business in NYC. We took 2 rooms for a convention at Javits Center. The location is fairly good for that. What I literally found offensive was the 12.95 day per device wireless charge. I needed to print boarding passes. The "business center" had three printers with 2 drawers each for paper. On the sixth I found some. The floor was covered with wasted receipt sheets. When I put paper in the printer for the computer I was paying .50 minute for, it spit out over twenty such receipts going back three days, so obviously the printer was empty for three days. It cost me $20.00 to print two boarding passes by the time I was finished.
Also, housekeeping. They never replaced face cloths, but they did take them. Second day I had to use a hand towel. Toilet paper was so thin it was like using none at all. My bill was over $5,000 for the two rooms for the five days. This is my third stay at this hotel and will be my last. It may be my last at a Doubletree as it seems they are now taking on the greedy policies that often keep me away from Hiltons.

title: “Old, dirty, musty, nasty, etc.....”
text: This hotel is in a great location and is surrounded by some very nice hotels. Unfortunately, this hotel is very dated and looks like it has never been updated. The wallpaper was pealing from the wall. The very small tub/shower had rust stains all over it. The bathroom was small. The carpet was extremely dirty. There was some type of humidifier/air cleaner in the room that ran constantly and created unnecessary noise. The view from our room was horrible. The breakfast was not good either. Basically just bread products and cereal, and the bread products weren't appetizing. I had a danish and the filling was still semi-frozen. The only thing positive I can say is that the price was good - around $60. Otherwise - avoid this place.

title: “Lots of Style, but Misses the Basics”
text:
Great location in Midtown Manhattan. Staff was friendly. We were wowed by the lobby ambiance. 
The experience was not so good once we made it to our room. Our Superior Double was beautiful (expected), small (somewhat expected), and completely impractical (not expected). 
There were no drawers for clothes. The bathroom lighting was dark enough that my daughter and wife had a hard time doing their hair and makeup. The finish on the tub was coming off, and the bathtub drain did not work properly. The beds were set back into walled niches which looked cool, but were a giant pain. I whacked my knee on that wall a couple of times each night. The only (3) power outlets in the room were hard to get to, and hard to find. 
I'm a frequent business traveler, who is accustomed to a focus on comfort and practicality. Perhaps I'm not cut out for the boutique, all style and no substance approach?

title: “What service! And a lovely room, too.”
text: What service! I was staying at Hotel George when Hurricane Irene was about to hit the city and decided to leave a day early. I hadn’t checked out that morning, but the guys at the desk simply would not allow me to pay for the night. Let me add that when I checked in, I was flustered (the earthquake had hit that day) and left my wallet at the reception desk -- before I even knew it was gone, a staff member came upstairs to return it. Perhaps needless the say, everyone is really friendly and helpful. Hotel George is elegant and comfortable. I had a spacious room (interior view, and therefore quiet), with a comfortable bed, lovely bath, writing desk, and easy chair. The lobby was welcoming, and is clearly a gathering spot. The hotel is less than a 10-minute walk from Union Station.

title: “Loved this Hotel”
text: Bid on Hotwire and received this property. Excellent hotel in the heart of San Francisco especially for the price that I paid. Was totally surprised that my room had partial views of the bay - just knew I would be placed in the Hotwire Basement. BART and MUNI about a 12 minute walk but I ended up walking to most of the sights as there is just so much to see in this area (I was here during the week so the area was fairly active could be different on the weekend). Room was elegant, spacious, and relaxing. The bed was truly out of this world. Limited interaction with staff but help desk was efficient, friendly, and professional during my check-in.

title: “Top location,value for money”
text: Hotel st james was excellent value.large rooms,well serviced every day.Great location,close to subway and the major bus depot.walking distance to all 5th avenue shops and macy's.ALso central to all the broadway theatres.Front desk staff friendly and helpful.Thouroughly reccomend hotel st james.

title: “Great stay!”
text:
My friends and I loved this place. The room was so nicely decorated that we posed for pictures when we arrived. 
We had a 2 bedroom suite at an unbelievable price. A night's stay in the suite (with kitchen and 2 baths) was the price of a night's stay in a standard room in Sedona. 
The pool area and outdoor eating/seating areas reminded me of an HGTV redesign. They were lovely and very Southwestern. The free breakfast was very good and the staff was friendly. What more can you ask?
There's a little mini-market setup for snacks and things you've forgotten. We didn't spend a lot of time in Phoenix so I can't say whether it's centrally located or not but it was close to the JW Marriott and the concert we were attending. And close to the express, Target, AMC movie theater and restaurants.
Pay attention when you drive there. Our GPS told us it was on the opposite side of the street. The hotel is right next to the Mayo Clinic. They share a little road.
I was very pleased with my visit.

title: “A waste of time and money”
text: After booking this hotel from the pictures off the internet for a weekend stay to see a Mavericks game, we quickly realized this was a huge mistake. What they don’t tell you is that on the weekends the "pool" turns into a "spring break-1989 Ft. Lauderdale nightmare". Evidently the Joule would rather cater to the 18 year olds drinking scene than to the people and couples spending d$400 a night to stay at their hotel. We not only couldn't enjoy the pool, but our room. If you try enjoying anything about the hotel between Friday night at 3 pm til Monday at noon, you are screwed unless you are 18 and know the gay bartender or you can afford to pay the door man $500 to get all your 18 year old friends into the pool bar. Don’t worry, the 5x5 pool area is nicely greased with oil, trash, and floating cups for your enjoyment. If you don’t like wearing massive jewelry, bikinis and Speedos; you will need to stay somewhere else! I would recommend the motel 6 over this place any day of the week!

title: “Much Nicer than the pictures! Wish it was closer to the 405”
text:
Hey Everyone,
I usually stay in Sherman Oaks Best Western but they actually wanted 170/night at that property which is nice but not THAT nice...Maybe they are trying to loose the questionable element north of Burbank but they also priced out my business..
Sooo I just stayed at the this hotel and I was VERY PLESANTLY SURPRISED..First of all the room look edmuch more modern then the photos above..The bedding is a crisp clean white duvet, not the usual horrid floral. I stayed in an executive room which was nice and large on a higher floor (worth the extra ten bucks but the fridge is small). Great soaps and water pressure and also they made a robe avaliable. Good Pay per view movies avail( including indies).Solid Internet Service unlike the Comfort Inn down the street
Funnily water bottles have seemed an issue in other reviews but when I checked in they offered me a FREE ICE COLD WATER right away since it was hot out.. to clear up this issue mentioned the previous bad reviews..Rooms come with 2 Holiday Inn Water Bottles (you can always get more for free at the front desk) and they also have 2 FIJI Bottles which are 3.00 dollars each which is says in the bottles! So I hope that puts the issue to rest...
Critques: I had to change rooms on the second day because the pay movies were not working on my tv the night before and I didn't want a room switch at 11pm, The Fridge is a half mini-fridge which is small...Encino is close but not that close once you drive down Ventura a couple times in bad traffic...

title: “Great location.....Great place”
text:
Our family of six stayed here for the Gator Bowl. The staff was friendly, efficient, and helpful.
The hotel was clean, parking was great, and it was convenient. We had a corner room and it was roomy, clean, and comfortable beds. The only downfall was that you had to pay for wifi in the rooms. If you walked down to the lobby, it was free.

title: “Good Location, good room, good service”
text:
Everything was good. Nothing was exceptional.
 I like the location a lot. Some cheap clothing wholesalersnare onnthe direct block, but 2 blocks away is Madison Square park with fantastic food vendors, Eataly, Hill Country fried chicken (best pies around) and the shopping of 5th ave thatbpeople come to NYC for. 
The room was a good size. We stayed in a slightly better room with a claw foot tub. The drain on the tub didn't work, huge downer. The toilet was in a separate room from everything else (shower and tub included). That was nice, but it was in a weird dark closer room and the door to getbin would stick. Comfortable bed, Argon shower/bath products, nice view.
The staff was very pleasant.

title: “great hotel.ideal location,”
text: great location helpful staff. basic but everything you need here would recommend for location alone,its certainly not the ritz but as hotels go in new york its ideal the price was great to,which included breakfast rooms were ideal as your only there to put your head down clean towels and maid everyday. would return .

title: “Nice, well-located hotel but amenities could be better”
text: We spent one night at the Holiday Inn Fisherman's Wharf in order for the family to be within walking distance of the Wharf. The location is great- just a block away, the rooms were newly remodeled and very comfortable. A downside for a large group (we had 9 people in four rooms) is that breakfast was not included and was only available in the hotel for $24.99 per adult. Another was that parking was $24 per car (we had three). We later found a parking garage a block away for $19, so it is unclear why the hotel charges more than the market rate. When the additional costs are factored in, the hotel is not necessarily less expensive than more upscale hotels that do include breakfast and parking but in general we were satisfied. Staff were helpful.

title: “Huge, classic, big-city hotel close to a variety of attractions - but bring a fat wallet”
text: Stayed here 8 nights in June/July 2011. Lots going on close by at that time like Taste of Chicago, concerts, fireworks, etc. This hotel dates back to the grand era of urban hotels with its cavernous ballrooms, ornate fixtures, and long list of VIPs who've stayed here over the years. With 2 adults and 2 kids (13,10) we had a room with 2 double beds and 2 bathrooms. The 2-bathroom rooms are a HUGE plus when 4 people are trying to get ready in the morning! The room itself was a roughly 350 sq ft room and a bathroom was on each side of the main room. Beds were very comfortable, climate control was great for cooling, LCD tv had lots of channels, water pressure even at the 18th floor was very good. Getting extra towels each day was no problem. Concierge was good (but personally I thought could have given better deals - i.e. baseball tix with a 50% to 75% mark up???!!!). Check in/out was fast and staff were very knowledgeable. Called ahead a few days to reserve a refrigerator for the room - DO THIS if you can and go to a local food store (we used CVS a few blocks away) and stock your room with cereal, fruit, milk, juice, crackers, etc.- especially for when you're looking for a snack or quick breakfast. Fridge is $40 for length of your stay but we saved some serious $$ eating a quick breakfast in the room each morning as their buffet breakfast is over $20/person. Indoor pool is nice, sundeck is nice, lots of seating and even more towels available. Exercise equipment is not free unless you are a silver or higher HHonors member. Biggest gripe is the wireless internet charge of $40 for 5 days or $18 for 1 day. The Motel 5 at any truck stop provides free internet so being charged so much for wireless after paying nightly room rates of $250+ is pretty greedy in my opinion. But I must admit the wireless speed was fast and reliable. This location is across the street from Grant Park which was a great place to walk and relax - my son and I took our baseball gloves and had some catches relatively close to the hotel when we had some down time. The aquarium, Field museum, and planetarium are a 20 min or so walk from the hotel. Navy pier is a cab/bus ride. The CTA red line is 1 block west and 1 block north - that will take you to wrigley and US Cellular fields among lots of other places. Overall a nice hotel if you're in Chicago for a week or so.

title: “They know how to define “Luxury Collection””
text:
The San Francisco Palace Hotel was a wonderful retreat on a fun SF weekend. The staff, location and rooms were all perfect with a special nod to the staff. The staff took great care of my wife and I, the other friends we were traveling with and were always pleasant, friendly and helpful in any situation we had (like directions, ideas etc.) They know how to define “Luxury Collection” in every way, shape and form!
All I have to say is that the next time I’m in San Francisco, I will stay at the Palace!!!

title: “Home away from Home”
text: The Library is fantastic. All of the other positive reviews are correct, I've been here several times and each time, leave thinking I won't stay anywhere else. I've had larger rooms and smaller rooms, each time perfectly appointed, spotlessly clean. The amenities offered here really suit me. Wine, cheese, breakfast, it's all just perfect. The staff is gracious, the location is wonderful, beds are comfortable. Just a wonderful experience. I've traveled on business, leisure, family trips, and in each case, The Library treats us like family.

title: “We LOVE the London!!!”
text: We always stay at the London when we come to NYC. They have spacious rooms by NYC standards and a great central location that is far enough away from the times square noise. During this last trip we experienced a couple issues which were not usual for the London, but the Manager for the front desk was extremely helpful. I think her name was Heather. She even called to check back with us and remembered our names when we would pass in the lobby. This is the personal touch every hotel in NYC should have. Even though the city is so fast, you feel like you matter when you are there.

title: “No worries. Great relaxing stay!”
text:
Travel was for a business trip. 
BLUF: As a business traveler, this hotel offers all the amenities you are looking for.
I would stay here again.
Check out time - 12 Noon.
Cheers:
------- 
Kitchen – just like home only smaller. D/W, frig (w/ ice maker), microwave.
My room had two separate living areas. Bedroom and a kitchen/living room. 
I had 2 TVs – one in the BR and one in the Living room. 
The room was nicely decorated with 9 foot high ceilings with modern furnishings and a nice neutral paint color.
Nice bed and sofa.
Free breakfast.
Free dinner on Mon – Th. 
Nice quite AC unit.
The room was nice and cool when I arrived.
Internet service w/o logging on.
2 phones – 1 by the bed and 1 on the desk.
A nice work area with power outlets above the desk.
Pool. 
There is also a small on-site convenience store to get soda, chips, water, snacks, etc… 
The room darkening shades did a good job on keeping out the light if you need to rest during the day.
Free paper. 
Jeers:
------
OK water pressure.
Slow Internet 
Local area info:
------------- 
There is a BP right next door so you can gas up the rental car before you return it to the airport. There is also a Subway within the BP.
There is also a FedEx Kinko’s and Jersey Mike’s subs close by.

title: “Better as expected, but...”
text: the breakfast needs getting used to - at least for me as a European. Dishes etc. were all plastic, food was rather fast food style. Besides that, housekeeping forgot to clean the shower one day. Our room had modern furniture, the bed was above standard. Hotel is in good shape since it is newly opened (Spring 2008).

title: “IT WORKED...”
text: You get what you see and pay for, nothing wrong with this place great location and if you are only in your room to sleep then why pay more? The staff was friendly and the room was clean. Perfect!

title: “Accomodations for medical treatments”
text:
La Quinta on Buffalo Speedway in Houston Texas is especially convenient to patients receiving care at MD Anderson or other hospitals in the area. 
The staff is most kind and accomodating during the stressful time, and work with you on scheduling transportation to the hospital This and the breakfast and the privacy/quietness of the hotel is very comforting.

title: “Large impersonal convention hotel”
text: Rooms are adequate but not quite what I had expected. As a Starwoods preferred gold member I am usually upgraded at their properties. Room was not ready on arrival although the hotel did not seem very busy. We were supposed to be called when it was ready--never happened! We will try to avoid this hotel on our next trip to Boston this month.

title: “Great hotel, great location!”
text:
We stayed in Chicago for a short break end Nov/Dec 08.
Hotel was great. Lovely rooms with little luxuries. Friendly atmosphere, attentive staff. 
Most amazing breakfasts in the French restaurant. Room service prompt and delicious though expensive. We didn't eat in the hotel restaurant for lunch or dinner.
Situated on a quiet street just off Michigan Ave. Fantastic location for shopping and sightseeing. Main sights (John Hancock Tower, lake, pier, river, shops) within walking distance. Chicago is a fantastic city with lots to see and do - we wanted to move there after we had visited!!
Knowledgable concierge, arranged an architectural river cruise for us which was fantastic. 
Would recommend this hotel, and Chiacgo for a fantastic break. Would stay there again should we return to Chicago (hope to soon).

title: “Great Location and peaceful surrounds”
text:
We only spent the night but this is not what you think of when you think about Best Western Hotels. It is actually 3 properties that are sort of interconnected and have a lovely marina on one side and a view of the bay on the other. 
Our room was in Casa Marina and was VERY impressive. When we were first assigned a room that was on the bay side, so I asked if we could be moved to a Marina view. The gal at the front desk gladly obliged. Moved us immediately to the other end of the floor. This turned out to be the perfect location. The beds are adjustable and very comfortable.
 I would highly recommend staying at Island Palms if you want a nice hotel but do not want to be in the heart of the craziness (Gas Lamp Quarter) yet only a few minutes away. Free Parking was also a big plus vs. $25-$30 in the downtown hotels.

title: “Excellent hotel & location..would definitely stay here again”
text: We booked two nights at this hotel for a visit to Washington DC. The hotel is under renovation but we barely noticed it and the work that has been done is impressive. The lobby, breakfast room and our rooms were very clean and attractive. The desk staff helped us with directions and restaurants nearby, which I will also do reviews on and were very good. The neighborhood was the type where we walked and felt safe, better than even downtown where the panhandlers were. We enjoyed our stay, saw things we never saw before and I was glad to stay here. Thanks to hotel staff people, Noemi and Kyle. The internet was fast and free and the room had a large new flat screen tv.

title: “Good price, location, and service, but very basic amenities.”
text:
The best thing about the Buckminster Hotel is its convenience.
