The hotel is located within spitting distance of Boston University, Fenway Park, House of Blues and the Kenmore Square T, and it's a decent, very pretty walk to Newbury Street, the Hynes Convention Center and the Prudential Tower. We visited Boston in late September, when the walking weather is at it's best, and it was a cinch getting around town. 
The service is top-notch, too - very friendly staff, attentive housekeeping, and when we had an issue with our room, someone was there within 10 minutes. 
On the flip side, do not expect too much of the room itself. You'll get what you need: a bed, a desk, a chair, a bathroom, and there was a microwave and minifridge in the room, as well. However, there was no coffee maker, a tiny 13-inch TV, and an extremely spotty internet connection. The hotel offers one hour of free internet per day at very slow speeds (one day we couldn't even load email) - any more time or speed, and you'll have to buy it. There are a number of free networks floating around - if you can catch one, I recommend using that instead. If all else fails, and you need to connect, there's a Barnes and Noble across the street. We can't complain too much - the price was outstanding for the convenience. I just wish we could have left the window open at night (the room overlooked the Turnpike as it feeds into Back Bay).
The free breakfast is your typical continental - coffee, bananas, bagels and danish. I'd recommend heading over to Trident Books and Cafe on Newbury Street for breakfast, instead. It's packed on weekends, but quiet during the week, and their menu is awesome. I'm sure there are reviews here - check them out.
All-in-all, if you're looking for a place to rest your head at night after a day of touristing, shopping, watching the Sox, or dropping your kid off at BU, the Buckminster is a pretty good choice. If you're looking for a romantic getaway or a place to get some work done, you're better off looking elsewhere.

title: “Well priced Boutique Hotel”
text:
My boyfriend booked us a trip to NY without my knowledge - until we got to Gatwick I thought we were going to Newcastle, UK, to visit relatives! 
We were impressed with Hotel 41, very clean, tidy and up to date in all public areas and the room itself. Although the room is small - door barely opens fully without bumping the end of the bed - it was fine for what we wanted as didn't spend a lot of time in room except for sleeping! However, one small gripe, which has been mentioned in previous reviews, is the lack of temperature control at night. The air con unit didn't seem to maintain the desired temperature and so you had to keep getting up and switching it on / off when you woke either sweating or freezing! 
Aveda toiletries, the robes and the complimentary breakfasts are all nice touches, and all staff very courteous and happy to oblige any requests. The bar is obviously popular with non residents especially during "happy hour", so do not be alarmed to see it overflowing into the lobby during these times.
All in all a great place to stay, especially for a weekend trip such as ours. Would definitely go back!

title: “Busy area, great beds”
text: Just returned from the Grand Hyatt San Francisco, Aug. 13. First impression...not great as the lobby is small and underwhelming. Not much room to sit if waiting to meet ppl. Loved the fact that Hyatt guarantees connecting rooms with their "family plan" and a discount on the 2nd room to boot!! Rooms were small, but nicely done. Beds oh-so-comfortable! Actually that was the best thing about the hotel. Had brunch upstairs 4 out of the 7 days there with my family. Ok...nothing great. Wait staff very friendly along with the concierges and doormen. Starbucks everywhere as the location was great for shopping and coffee! We did not rent a car instead choose to walk, cab it or take some form of public transportation. Overall a very good hotel.

title: “Ideal Location”
text: This hotel was ideally located, close to Grand Central Station where we had to take the train to the US Open. We felt safe walking around the neighborhood at night. The room was spacious, the staff helpful. We'd left a jacket in the closet and had asked the hotel's Lost and Found to assist us in finding it. The staff made sure to call us back to confirm they'd found it and that they would send it out. Within two days, we got the jacket delivered to the house.

title: “Nice location”
text: The Dana is a clean hotel with Wi-Fi, Pay per View, a Pool, and Jaquzzi. The grounds are nice with two restaurants on site. The surrounding area is beautiful looking right out on a marina. You are within a 10 minute walk to the ocean. Also, there is a large park within walking distance. This area is only an 8 minute drive to Balboa Park and the San Diego Zoo which is why we chose it in the first place. I was not that impressed with the hotel itself but I loved the location. If you are not going to spend a lot of time in your room, I would recommend this for travelors and I would stay there again.

title: “Used to be great..now very disappointed”
text:
Have stayed at this hotel many times and always loved the small boutique quality of it. Lots wrong this time. Very soft beds, rooms with strong smelling air freshener, bad for allergies.
Furniture chipped and need of repair. No "on demand" movies. Worst beds I have ever had in a hotel. Lots of quality lost. Would not stay here again.

title: “good option for concert goers”
text: Other reviewers have commented that this hotel is in a rough neighborhood. Yes, it is an urban area, and Colfax is busy and noisy, but the trade-off is that that hotel is also located in the middle of a bunch of desirable concert venues and restaurants, not too far from the capitol, and close to city parks (although there were a lot of liquor stores on the block as well). We found the hotel to be a good option if you want an affordable downtown hotel. The room was reasonably appointed and sized for the price. We were on the second floor and didn't hear a peep from other hotel guests the whole time we were there (though, again, there was noise from the street). Another feature of the hotel that surprised me was that a series of businesses (H&R block, nail salon, barber shop, etc) had doors that opened up onto the first floor of the hotel, directly across from the rooms. We opted not to eat at the hotel, as the breakfast seemed pricey and there were lots of other restaurants in the area.

title: “Nice hotel but nothing special”
text:
Our room was nice as they were able to give us a view room even though the hotel was very full that night. They are in the midst of remodeling their entry so you do have to go through the garage and then back up to the third floor.
I was surprised at how cold the hotel was in most areas. It is October and cold outside. The fitness locker room for the women was FREEZING. And for some reason, they must have TVs everywhere, even in their nicer dining room!
But we found the staff to be wonderful. We were always greeted with a smile by everyone and wished a nice day/evening. 
It is a bit dated, but not that bad. As far as the price of the room - you will not find anything cheaper in downtown Boston. That's just the way it is.

title: “Nice hotel, good location”
text: My daughter and I spent four nights in this hotel in August. Location is great, right across from Central Park, 5 min from Times Square. Rooms were s,mall but clean and fairly well appointed. The negatives were that we were put on the non park side of the hotel and he construction across the street started at 6 am every morning. Also, why do four star hotels persist in charging for Internet which is free at a Hampton Inn, and the big glaring deficiency was an in room coffee maker. Room service was the most expensive I have ever seen ( and I'm comparing to London, Paris, Tokyo) so the Starbucks down the way was getting lots of business. Not sure I would stay there again.

title: “Great location, tired hotel”
text: Fantastic location just of Times Square central for everything. Rooms were basic but clean needed refreshed. Staff weren't to friendly could have been nicer. However location more than makes up for any issues. Would use again

title: “Good Value”
text:
Hotel provides a free airport and cruise terminal shuttle throughout the day. Rooms a spacious and well maintained - a faulty tv was replaced promptly after it was reported to front desk.
Front desk staff are very helpful and friendly. Location is about 10 mins walk to shopping mall and restaurants and about same to waterfront. Very quiet area.
Breakfast very limited selection and could be improved.

title: “Saturday night ringside fights, iffy elevators and urine smelling stairs.”
text: We stayed for a Friday and Saturday night. The staff was friendly but somewhat confusing to understand. Self parking more costly than valet parking not withstanding tips to valet upon parking and retrieval of the automobile. The elevators worked if they felt like doing so. A repair person was there twice during our stay. Another guest was trapped in the elevator until the desk clerk ran to the basement and made a button call from there. My wife and I waited 10 minutes for an elevator to come to the 5th floor so I took the stairs telling my wife to wait. The stairs smelled like transients used them for a urinal. Beer cans were scattered about on the landings. When I got to the lobby one elevator was on the lobby floor and the other at the top, 8th floor, neither moving. I told the desk clerk my wife was waiting on five and had been for some time. He hit the button for the elevator on the lobby level, the doors opened, he hit five and it went all the way to eight stopping at every floor and back down stopping at every floor however with no passengers and not opening the doors when it returned to the lobby. Five minutes later my wife came out of the stairs saying she saw the elevator lights do the same thing I observed frm the lobby but never stopping with open doors to let her on. Saturday night from 2:15 a.m.-3:00 a.m. there were three people, 1 F, 2 M having a HUGE FIGHT in a room and three times in the hall with F this and F that continually. One M telling the F to get her stuff get out of his room and come back where you belong...she said she had too much stuff he told her to grab what she could carry and get out of that room. He lost out she spent the rest of the night with her boyfriend as the husband loudly objected from the hall banging on the door and cussing. I was truly afraid to stick my head out my door to tell them to hold it down as it sounded as if the husband was so irritated gunplay could earnestly be involved. What a place...Not one for "Executives". I had to drive 300 miles the following day with 4 hours sleep. Upon check in I found a dirty used baby bottle on the floor from a previos guest. I seriously doubt if I will ever stay in the Exeutive Pacific again.

title: “Great value for its location”
text: My wife and I stayed at Hotel Mela three nights for our anniversary. We couldn't be more pleased with this hotel. Its location is ideal between Time Square and 5th Ave, and you can easily walk just about anywhere in Manhattan if you are fit. My wife and I went north through Central Park, and south through SoHo. We didn't use room service or any of the optional amenities, so I can't comment on those. But the room was clean, contemporary, and I think plenty large considering the average hotel room in Manhattan is very small. The one negative, which I'm not sure is even something easily fixed, is the outside road noise, which came loud and clear into our room on the 11th floor. Seemed louder than when we stayed at a Marriott right in times square. Perhaps the outside wall/window insulation could be improved. Bottom line though is this has our full thumbs up recommendation.

title: “They were overbooked and tried to put me in another hotel!!!”
text:
Stayed here for 2 nights in January 2007 for a conference. When I tried to check in they stated they were over booked and tried to put me in other hotels in the city for the first night!! I didn;t want to travel to a new hotel, so I had to stay in my colleague's room that first night. They were apologetic and willing to pay for the first night and transportation costs, etc. But VERY unprofessional. 
The room and decor was nice. It was relatively quiet, although I was on the 3rd floor and could hear street traffic at times. The hotel is pretty close to many DC tourist sites, but not the best for walking. You usually need to take public transportation (there is a Metro station near by). The hotel restaurant and bar are good, but expensive and not really worth it. 
 The biggest down sides = 1) They didn't have a room for me, 2) They charge $14 for access to the gym, 3) They charge $10 per day for internet, 4) The hotel is located in the capital/business district, so it is not a "fun" or "hip" area at all. In fact, on the weekends it is completely DEAD. There are very few restaurants or cafes nearby and no cute shops or neighborhoods to walk around. You really have to travel to Georgetown or Dupont Circle for any type of people-watching, shopping, "cool factor" or nightlife. Not worth the money

title: “Who needs the Ritz with service like this???”
text:
After my third stay at the Palomar last week, I felt compelled to write a reivew. I can check all the basics that are needed for an enjoyable hotel stay -- great location, restaurant quaility room service, clean and well apportioned rooms, great outdoor pool and deck individual attention, etc.
 However, I CANNOT SAY ENOUGH ABOUT THE STAFF'S ATTENTION TO DETAIL AND COMPLETE DEDICATION TO SERVICE. 
Some examples -- I lamented out loud that I forgot to put lotion in my purse while taking the elevator downstairs to cocktail hour. Five minutes later a staff member tapped me on the shoulder and discreetly handed me a small package containing 2 tubes of Aveda lotion; I asked about the hours of the outdoor pool/lounge as my neices were joining me for an afternoon while I was in town on business. Not only was the lifeguard standing by with armfulls of toys for them to play with, the front desk sent up complimentary cookies and milk for them to enjoy once we returned to the room.
Although, as weary travelers, we would like hotels to get 100% of things right 100% of the time, some things fall through the cracks. I was a bit frustrated to find the front doors locked with no one in sight upon arrival to the hotel after significant airline delays. The 3 minutes I waited for the door to be opened felt like three hours due to my west-coast jet lag. I grumpily mentioned my frustration while checking in and trudged off to my room. I was further annoyed by a knock at my door 10 minutes later, but changed my attitude when I was told that the staff member was there to usher me to my upgraded room for my inconveniece where a decadent dessert and wine arrived shortly thereafter.
So, I must endorse the Palomar, the botique hotel I originally stumbled upon because the Ritz was sold out ( I love the sports club). But the Palomar gets it all right (or kills themselves trying) with a staff committed to exceeding your expectations (thank you Rhonda!) and a management team that obviously empowers their employees to do so. I encouraged a colleague to stay here this time and she thanked me for uncovering such a find. I've also done the Mandrin, Hay-Adams, Willard and 2 other Ritz properties during other trips. The Palomar visits, have been my most enjoyable stays by far. Give this gem a try.

title: “Enjoyed our stay at Summerfield”
text:
My husband and I were recently in San Jose for business and stayed at the Summerfield Suites in San Jose. We had a very pleasant stay at the hotel and they offered a delicious variety of breakfast every morning. 
The rooms were very spacious, clean and comfortable. The only problem we encountered was that our room was on the ground floor and we heard kids running up and down the stairs and in their rooms during the night. However, once call to the front desk took care of the problem immediately. Although we spent the majority of our time in San Francisco, the drive back to the hotel was worth it.

title: “Great Hotel in Good Location”
text:
Easy arrival dealt with by polite and very helpful staff. Nice high floors so the view was great of the city and the rooms were clean and modern.
We got back from a night out and a bottle of bubbly was on the counter from the management wishing me happy birthday - lovely surprise and very appreciated by us all.
The bedrooms had a great bathroom and the bed linen was an excellent quality, the foyer was comfortable and the bar looked seductive at night. Apple computers for customers use, 20 minutes free use daily for guests.
Location wise was great - a short walk from Union Square so all the entertainment and transport needs are at hand. We booked through Virgin Holidays so the Alamo Rental Car location is also very close on O'Farrell.
We spoke to a receptionist about a restaurant we had read about which had a blue door which I believed was near. She knew exactly which one we meant and it was called Dotties and it was around the corner ! She also knew it was closed on a Tuesday and as we were leaving on Wednesday she suggested we should go on Monday morning - good skills ( I was once a Office Manager in a 4 star hotel - she knew all the tricks to impress) Talking of Dotties - long long queue even at 8am - worth every cent.
Only funny thing that happened was at around 11.30pm to Midnight there was a loud bang - like a gun shot - forgot to ask what it was and it happened both nights ? If anyone knows what it is let me know.
Overall loved the hotel and was very impessed - particularly the staff.

title: “Great Boutique Hotel!!!”
text:
I have stayed at The Churchill on 3 separate occasions over the past year, with my last stay being just last Friday (Dec 3). Each time I have received great service, a lovely room, good food (if not a little pricey), all in a great DC neighborhood with access to everything. I don't think you can even come close to getting a better hotel for the rates they charge. As I said, the only issue I can take with the hotel after 3 stays is the cost of some of the food. But then again, it's certainly not any more expensive than what you would find at a comparable hotel. I make a number of trips to DC throughout the year and will definitely continue to stay at The Churchill. I would certainly encourage anyone who prefers quiet little boutique style hotels to the large busy/noisy ones, to stay at The Churchill.
MWilson

title: “Well positioned and excellent value”
text:
The Good
• Very well positioned
• Pleasant staff 
• Access to local restaurants
• The bedding is very comfortable after 33 hours of travel 
The Not so Good
• Easy access to power points, I needed to move furniture as the desk lap’s external plug was faulty
• I did not receive a booked wakeup call and consequently missed a flight

title: “A Real Palace”
text:
The New York Palace is stunning in every way. The rooms are wonderful, really clean, spacious, and very comfortable, I can't fault them in any way. The staff are polite, helpful and although sometimes not overly friendly at first meeting, I found a smile from me went a long way towards making them smile more too! The location is fantastic, how near Sak's can you be? Central Park is a fifteen minute stroll away, Times square about ten minutes, and Rockefeller Centre literally across the road!
Okay, it's expensive, but in this world you get what you pay for, and the Palace is definitely worth the cost!

title: “Affordable hotel in good location”
text:
We stayed here Thanksgiving week and were pleasantly surprised by the quality of the hotel and the convenience of the location. It is in the Chinatown/Little Italy area and therefore off the well beaten tourist path which was exactly what we were looking for. The hotel is within walking distance of several subway lines and also within easy walking distance of Soho and the East Village. 
The hotel staff was excellent. Everyone we encountered from check in to check out was friendly, professional and willing to assist. Our room was large by NYC standards and very comfortable. The bathroom was large but had no tub, just an open shower (just a cloth shower curtain) which required some pre-thought before turning on the water to assure nothing important got wet. The beds were comfortable and the rooms were very well kept. There were four of us in the room but only bath accessories for two. This was quickly remedied by the front desk staff.
Breakfast was okay. Lots of carb-heavy offerings, oatmeal, apples, bananas, two waffle making machines. Would have liked a bit more variety, perhaps yogurt or fruit salad. The immediate neighborhood had restaurants and bakeries galore so there are other options for breakfast. Judging by the conversations around us at breakfast this hotel is popular with visitors to the US. 
The hotel offers free wifi which was a little slow. There are also computers available for use in the lounge area. One thing to note: The hotel is non-smoking and you sign a document stating you will be charged $300 if you smoke in the room. Not a problem for us but something to be aware of if you travel with smokers. Overall, we were very pleased with our stay here and would stay again.

title: “My favorite hotel in Downtown DC”
text: Every time I go to Washington, DC, I like to stay close to everything because I go only for a few days and want to do a lot of things, including work. The location of this hotel is very convenient, if you come to Reagan National Airport, the metro blue line leaves you in front of the hotel in just 15 minutes and the red line with its many junctions is only a couple blocks away. It's always easy to take a taxi if you are in a hurry. The rooms have all the necessary for the business traveler, the bed is big enough if you have company and plenty of pillows for a good rest after a busy day. The personal is very attentive and always handy. Plenty of eating options around, recommended Tuscana West just around the corner. The corporate rate at over $200 compares well to other surrounding and similar hotels.

title: “If you like the movie "The Shining", you'll love this place!”
text:
Me and my friend were traveling on a tight budget but did not want to stay at a hostel, so Hotel Penn was the best for our price range. The best thing about this place is the location, it's at the heart of everything! The subway was easily accessible and Penn Station was just next door. It's within walking distances to the Empire State building, great shopping, and delicious food at Korea Town. If you don't mind walking it's also about a 20 minute walk to Time Square. 
As my title suggested it was one of the first thing that popped into my mind when I went there. The hotel itself is very old, and even though they tried to renovate the lobby to be a bit more modern, there was no hiding the cracks in the wall and musky carpet. The decor is very dark and there isn't enough lighting in the halls or in the room. The room itself was small but manageable, and even though the bathroom was renovated, the bathtub had cracks and pipes were exposed. We didn't feel comfortable taking our shoes off and checked the bed thoroughly before sleeping on it.
The most helpful thing the Hotel provided was probably the map they give up with your key card. The staff was not helpful at all with the exception of the pleasant storage boy in the basement, which by the way looks like another horror movie set. In fact, I think I got more help and smiles from the other patrons of the hotel than from the staff. They were also very slow and there are long check-in lines every day we went by the lobby. 
Overall, since NYC has so much to offer in terms of activities we didn't stay much in the hotel room, so it was fine, but if you are traveling with a family or like to stay in a comfortable room, I would find another hotel.

title: “loved every minute”
text:
before we went on this trip we read lots of reviews on this location & this hotel, so we were a bit worried about going. well i just had to write my own review so that anyone else like us who would like to stay here can be put at ease, here goes
the hotel is just what you expect it to be, elvis everywhere. we had a room on the first floor, yes you could here people talking outside your door but that is if you sat in the sitting room & it is an hotel.we had breakfast every morning at the hard rock cafe, the staff there are really friendly, as are anyone we spoke to in memphis.we had a free shuttle from the hotel to beals street, we
had drinks in the rum cafe & also went to BB kings, the service at both places were outstanding. we also went to sun studios where again the hotel provided a free shuttle, & not forgetting the free pink cadalac which takes you to marlows the best fatest ribs in town. we also went to graceland which was in walking distance of our hotel but a shuttle takes you across which is again free, we went on the V.I.P. tour which i would highly recommend.all in all a fantastic seven days & i would recommend anyone who goes,to stay at the heartbreak hotel we had the best holiday ever.

title: “This a fantastic deal in NYC!”
text: We stayed in Sept 22-26 2007. Read all the reviews and checked out their website. We were thrilled that they were all accurate! The Wingate on 35th in NYC is an amazing deal in a city that charges hundreds of dollars for a worn out looking room. The hotel is EXACTLY like it's pictures and claims: big room, up to date furnishings, free bottle water, refrigerator, microwave, breakfasts, a business center, a real closet and helpful staff. The only downside is the location on 35th street...not the prettiest street in the city. However, it's conviently located so you can easily walk to many of the sights, loads of restaurants, etc. Would definitely stay here again!

title: “All a hotel should be...”
text: This was our first Kimpton experience and we will definitely use these hotels again. The Palomar has an excellent staff: from the doorman, to the front desk staff to the wait staff at the bar. Staff was very accommodating and helpful. You could tell their goal was to enhance your stay. Daily cocktail hour in the lobby was lovely feature. Refreshments provided all day e.g.- coffee, water, iced coffee, juice boxes for any kids. Stayed in the King Spa Premier Room. Very comfortable and spacious with a modern and inviting decor. We left relaxed and re-freshed after our stay. Hotel has great access to all Chicago has to offer.

title: “Gorgeous Hotel and Great Staff!”
text: The hotel was quite attractive and had wonderful personal service. As a handicap patron, all of my needs were easily met. The rooms, although small, are quaint and serve the purpose for sleeping or relaxing with the t.v. or Internet. However, Internet services are not free. We slept great. The location is phenomenal! We plan on staying there again our next stay in NY.

title: “fathers day”
text: This was the second time at this hotel and was great just like the first time. This hotel is not a hotel for kids. The hotel is great for adults looking for a clean hotel 4 star place to go. The location is prime gaslamp and hotel is top notch. We will stay here again.

title: “Good price. Good location.”
text:
We couldn't find a better price, and we tried Priceline (several months later my friend went to Seattle through Priceline for about $70 and stayed an equally good location at nicer hotel).
The hotel is not what I am used to, but I think it was perfectly fine. Nothing bothered me. The entrance is more like a side door on the street (not prominent) and the front desk appears somewhat more informal than I usually find. All in all it was a fine experience. The staff was helpful and very polite. The parking was not bad at all. But in general you certainly don't get the feeling that you are spoiling yourself. 
The location was definitely very good. Easy to walk to everything, but not much around for the first 5 minutes in any direction - which is not a big deal, but things are not right outside your door (except the library which I hear is very nice - we didn't go).

title: “Beautiful, but...Pillows Were Like Sacks of Cement”
text:
The wife and I did an overnighter here attending a family function off-site. The room was beautiful, relatively new and scratch-free. A relative stayed here at the same time and except for a king vs. twin beds, the rooms were identical. Everything worked. I liked the well-organized hutch containing the coffee brewer. micro and fridge. The king-sized bed, albeit a set-your-own-firmness mattress came with a multitude of smaller, square-shaped pillows, each one less comfortable than the last one. I refer to them as "cement sacks."
Neither of us got a good night's sleep account of the pillows.
The next morning a bunch of us ate breakfast together in their grill. There was a choice of the buffet or order from the menu. I checked out the buffet and saw several items were out or low and I advised the cook staff who's body language told me my advice was not appreciated. They did replenish those items quickly to their credit. The food was just OK, not bad but nothing special. I enjoy biscuits and gravy when traveling and was slightly disappointed in the gravy that was pretty bland tasting.
Our waitress to her credit was very obliging and informative.
I would stay there again in the future and call housekeeping for softer pillows if necessary.

title: “Right in the middle of the city”
text:
Right in the Middle of the City. We were able to walk everywhere.
The breakfast was filling, and the helpful staff were cleaning and filling up the trays at a fast pace.
The hotel staff were friendly and helpful.
Rooms large and clean.
I would stay here again ,paid 115.oo through AAA.
3 star resturants a couple of blocks away. 
Theater and Music venues within blocks.
Shops just on the other side of Broad Street
Easy to hail a cab, or take the public transportation.

title: “BAY VIEW SUITE GOOD”
text: We spent 400 on two nights ...We were happy with the place real clean and close to sea world and Beach..we would definitely come back....location looks a a little outdated inside but for the price it is a nice location and very safe and clean

title: “Elegant stay”
text:
I stayed here for one night in May so my experience was somewhat limited.
As others have noted, the hotel is elegant with a large, beautiful lobby. The room was very nice but nothing particularly memorable- a large desk to work at, comfortable bed, nice bath.
All the interactions with the staff were great- especially very early in the morning as they helped me flag down a car to get to the airport.
I would recommend the hotel to anyone that likes a more classic styling/luxury property.

title: “Very happy to recommend to others”
text: Don't understand the negative comments- we've just returned after 8 night stay, and were very happy with the hotel. It's not a luxury hotel- it's great value. Rooms, halls etc do look tired- area isn't the best- all this is true, but irrelevant to a great holiday. Too many people expect too much. Beds fantastic- pillows absolutely terrific. Very handy location for Times Square, ESB, subways etc- found staff very good, excellent transportation service on last day. Our second stay in NY- would return to hotel. One point of criticism - had the worst meal at Coopers- three meals, all awful, esp pizza, which was terrible(cold lumps of mozarella garnishing a dry biscuit), burger was quantity over quality. All meals returned with very little eaten- staff couldn't have given a monkeys. Apart from that- all good. Recommend people try restaurant row on West 46th Street- only found a couple of nights before we left - classy selection of quality restaurants- we went to Lattanzi - number 361- absolutely outstanding italian, with a Maitre D that my wife thought 'a very nice boy'

title: “Biggest let down ever”
text: Waldorf Astoria - great location for business and pleasure; beautiful common areas. Staff was very friendly and helpful. However, when I checked in they said that there was some remodeling going on and I may hear some odd noises here and there, but that it would not go past 5 pm. The noise was so loud you could not even make a phone call. And it went past 5 pm, at least until almost 6 pm. Started up promptly at 9 am again. I went to relax on the star light roof top with a business partner, which the whole floor was a construction area. No notice that it was closed or to not go there. Then that night I received a voice mail after returning late to the hotel that there would be no water available from midnight until the next morning. "Sorry for the inconvenience." On top of it all, I ordered breakfast for the next morning. Somehow a $27 combo of 2 eggs, toast and coffee added up to $49 (I knew the delivery charges, gratuity, taxes, etc would definitely add up though). But the eggs were stone cold, and the toast was burnt. Just overall experience that I would expect at a 2 star or less hotel, not the Waldorf. The Waldorf has its location and its romantic brand image going for it; but from what I saw, that's it. Huge let down.

title: “Okay Hotel for the Price”
text:
We just got back from 2 nights at the New Yorker (Jan 1st to 3rd). The hotel was extremely crowded for the holidays (to be expected) and there were long lines to check-in and out. Since we were checking in on New Year's our room, we were told that our room would not be ready until late in the afternoon. After asking for the manager, he promised to do his best to get us checked-in as early as possible (ended up being about 2:30pm- check-in time is supposed to be 1:00pm). We appreciated that the manager was willing to help us, but we found the other front desk staff to be rude. 
The room itself was pretty standard- clean, but tiny and with no view. The heat wasn't working very well, it would either blow really hot or cold air and we found the same happened with the shower. 
Overall, I think we got what we paid for. We paid a little less than $150 a night. In the future, I'd probably spend a little more and stay someplace nicer.

title: “Exceptional value!!! A wonderful choice!!!”
text: We chose this hotel based on a recommendation and it did not disappoint! Our room had two comfy queen beds, and a pull-out couch - very spacious and comfortable! Was also exceptionally clean and well made-up daily. Staff were excellent - always pleasant and helpful. Location is great - 10 minute walk to 5th avenue, 15 to Times Square. Would definitely stay here again - with family or friends.

title: “It was Ok..but you can't beat the location”
text: Right on the Riverwalk you cannot beat this location! the hotel is an older one but the lobby was nice and room was nice. the bed was comfortable though i came home with two mysterious bites on my big toe ...which was scary. the pool is very small and only one hot tub. also..if you rent a car watch out for the price for parking because it is very high! you are better off going down the block to a parking lot and paying that price! but again, you cannot beat the location it is right in the middle of everything!

title: “Refund”
text:
I just wanted to Thank Boston Waterfront Westin for allowing a refund on a business trip that was cancelled by a customer. I had done a prepaid trip for two nights non refundable. When I contacted Starwood guest services they said it was up to the Hotel to refund the visa charge, and that it was very unlikely as I had agreed to non cancelllation. I am so happy to say they did honor my request for full refund. Although I have never stayed at this Hotel I cant wait until I can! I would recommend this Hotel just on the basis of the kindness they showed to me, it was a large amount of money and they certainly were under no obligation to do so. Thank you, Thank you!! Thank you also to Starwood guest services for supporting your members.!
Nancy Dewar

title: “I love the place!”
text:
It was a wonderful experience. Yes, it is 2.5-star hotel but Mount Vernon is one of the best in its category! Friendly staff, clean room, big TV with decent channels, GREAT hot breakfast (why did someone complain about this? ), free wireless Internet. 
This location could not be better!! Light rail from and to BWI airport for $1.6! Bus line 11 and 3 are around the corner which takes you downtown with 20 minutes. Talking about the corners, there are Walters Museum, library, Basilica of the Assumption, 7-11 convenient store, best Chinese restaurant in town (I'm Chinese so this is the best for me:-)), and the whole Mt. Vernon cultural area! you get to all those places mentioned above within 5 minutes on foot. I took a cultural walk in that area up to the Baltimore Museum of Art (bus 3) in spring blossom. I had to say this is one of my best experiences in many years! You can also walk for 40 minutes along Charles street to inner harbor to see all those attractions there. anyway, this is a wonderful affordable place for museum/art/architecture/history lovers like myself. I will definitely stay there again next year.

title: “It's Grand in size with good service in good location!”
text: I had a chance to stay one night on business with a co worker before we moved on to Park Hyatt in Washington D.C. The main reason I chose to stay here was great pricing and good reviews I read in Tripadvisor. As we drove up to the hotel we were wowed by the size of the hotel and lobby was huge. Our check in was very smooth and we were upgraded to Premium View at no charge. Our room was decent size with very comfortable beds. I guess best part about staying at thie hotel was the view of San Diego harbor and our room had a view of aircraft carrier. Our internet was complimentary but we did not try any of the hotel establishment due to our busy schedule. Overall I can not say anything nice but this hotel and will most likely stay here again if I am ever in san Diego again. I loved the location and view of San Diego harbor.

title: “Rude staff”
text: The staff at the front desk and the employees in housekeeping were VERY rude, I would never stay here again!

title: “I had a great stay at the hotel. It was clean new roomy & modestly priced.”
text: I really enjoyed my stay at the hotel. I was a great place to stay. The hotel and room was clean, roomy, and very stylish. I look forward to going back soon and taking family too.

title: “Austin Four Seasons”
text: terrific hotel, great location, get a massage with Janet!

title: “Terrific place to stay while visiting NYC”
text: Wonderful hotel with large, clean, nicely appointed modern rooms. Comfortable lobby with interactive information screens and customer service-focused staff; smooth check-in/check-out and helpful info from concierge. Conveniently located to Rockefeller Center, Times Square, 5th Ave. shopping, restaurants and multiple subway stops. Would definitely stay here again when visiting NYC.

title: “Great Hotel close to finest Gallery”
text: Excellent hotel, close to the Michali Fine Art Gallery. I came to buy art and found it walking distance to the gallery..made and excellent investment and had a delightful stay.

title: “Great hotel in a great location”
text:
Stayed at this hotel between 14-20 March 2006. After reading other reviews I purposely requested a room on a high floor to reduce the noise of the road below, and was really pleased when we were given a room on the 25th floor. You could still hear some traffic noises below, and the occasional fire engine, but even as a light sleeper it didnt stop me from getting a good nights sleep. There was some building work one block away that started at approx 6am, but you kind of have to expect a certain amount of noise being in the centre of New York. 
The rooms and beds are huge and the bed was really comfy, with a pillow menu to choose from. There was also a kitchen in our room which had a fridge/freezer/microwaver/cooker and a great view of the empire state building when I was washing up! 
The only disappointment in the room was the bathroom which was the smallest I had ever seen (even smaller than the walk in clothes cupboard). It would have been nice to have a bath to soothe aching legs and feet after all the walking, but will say that the shower was hot and powerful so not all bad! 
In relation to everything else, the staff were really friendly and helpful (especially the concierge desk who I rang daily - I found it easier to ring them from the room instead of going down to the desk and queuing for 10 mins to speak with them), rooms were cleaned/serviced daily, the lifts were quick and best of all the hotel is in a great location - 2 mins from Macy's and Madison Sq Garden and Penn Station subway, 10 mins from Times Square and Broadway, 10/15 mins to the empire state building. Even as a 3 star hotel, it met all my usual high expectations (and I am a fuss arse) and thoroughly deserves its high ranking in the list - would definately recommend it.

title: “Not What I Expected”
text:
First, let me say that choosing a hotel in Philadelphia was not easy. After reading lots of reviews, from several sources, I decided on this hotel. Being a Hilton Honors member, helped me make my decision. I've stayed in several Hampton Inn's over the past few years. The hotel is located nicely, so that it is possible to walk to almost every important attraction. Unfortunately, the neighborhood in which the Hampton is in, is NOT good. It is on the edge of Chinatown, within a very seedy neighborhood. Homeless people and unsavory characters. Walking to dinner, to a restaurant recommended by the staff (a good choice), was uncomfortable, to say the least. 
Having said that, we arrived, after bypassing the hotel once, to fairly friendly staff. We did NOT get a cookie or any goody bag, as some other reviewers eluded to. What we did get, was the wrong room. We had booked a king suite, as this was seemingly the only room available when I booked the room, but instead got a room with two double beds. We only found this out, when we went up to the room. The front desk never told us of the downgrade. When we immediately came down to the front desk, to tell them of the mistake, they informed us that we were downgraded because nothing else was available, and we should be comforted by the fact that we were only paying for the lower graded room. After explaining, that as a married couple, we would not sleep in separate beds, they found two rooms with king beds. They did apologize and nicely send us on our way. The room was okay. Nothing special. Clean enough and the housekeeping staff was very friendly. The front desk staff was okay. Nothing special. The free breakfast was good. Very busy, but nicely stocked with food, coffee and tea. I love the waffle maker. No complaints here. The parking is either valet at $35.00 or off site parking for $25.00, per day, across the street. I realize that this hotel cannot be compared to the Rittenhouse, but because of the immediate neighborhood and the downgrade in rooms and the so-so front desk staff, I don't think I would choose this hotel again. Sorry.

title: “Worth a short visit”
text:
The staff were all friendly from the front door, house keeping, security, and the restaurant staff. 
My wife and I were there on business and pleasure, but we also brought our newborn. There were a few drawbacks as you might expect with children and casinos. The only restaurant you can take them is Wolfgang Puck, because it's not inside the casino floor. This rule is understandable and acceptable, as many adults go there to get away from kids. Fortunately, we had great service all three days we ate there, and the food was great. It's expensive, but less than the other restaurants on property from what we were told. 
The only problem we had was scheduling our room to be cleaned. We requested twice for it to be cleaned in advance, but it took over three hours later for them to show up after walking down to the front desk and have them call house keeping. 
The casino was surprisingly smokier than we anticipated, but most people drink and smoke while they gamble. It's much better than Greektown, but not as good as most Vegas casinos. 
The rooms were nicer than we expected. The bathroom is unique and spacious. It even has a mirror with a TV behind it. The room was well appointed and comfortable.

title: “Everything was great... until the bedbugs”
text: My husband & I stayed for 2 days. Got a good price, the room seemed really clean, came with lots of tv channels, free parking, microwave & fridge. 1st night was fine, but on the 2nd night we started itching. I turned on the lights and found a bunch of huge bed bugs. We left immediately without bothering to stop & check out.

title: “Best Hotel on Earth”
text:
This is the best hotel on Earth. The staff is extremly friendly, helpful. They made the stay great. The hotel is nestled in a safe community, with beautiful greenery. I highly recommend to stay there. If I am in LA next time, will difinetly go there.
The rooms are recently renovated with a modern look.

title: “Good Stay”
text: This was our second time staying at this hotel & both times have been very satisfactory. The first time we had our dog & the hotel is very pet friendlyThis time we were not traveling with any animals & the hotel was very accomadating by giving us a late check-out(1pm) as my husband had a 1:45 appointment just a few minuites away. We would use this hotel again.

title: “An Oasis of calm”
text:
We arrived at the Omni after a long transatlantic flight and tiresome airport transfer to be warmly greeted by the staff ,the check in was handled efficently and with a smile.Indeed the quality of the service from the staff throughout the hotel was impeccable!
The Omni is ideally located for getting to and from all the tourist sights as well as Union Square.
We stayed for four nights as part of a west coast tour and could not have chosen a better hotel to kick off our trip.
First class in every detail !

title: “Very nice hotel, great pet policy!”
text:
We were looking for a quick getaway over the fourth of July weekend, and the prospect of a Kimpton Hotel for reasonable price (~$150) THAT ALLOWED DOGS sealed the deal for us. We weren't disappointed. The hotel was in a beautiful restored building (former home of the B&O Railway). The location was not quite central (it was in what felt like a business district, which at night and on the weekend felt a little deserted). However, the hotel itself was very nice and we enjoyed our stay. It was an easy walk to the harbor.
Rooms were large - we had a double room, which worked out fine for four people (2 adults, a 13 and 16 year old). I had noted on my reservation that we would be bringing our dog (no extra charge), and when we arrived, there was even a small dog bed and dog dish of food/water for our pet! Staff was friendly. Room was very clean and comfortable. Only complaint was that we were awakened in the night by loud talkers next door - so maybe the soundproofing isn't as great as one would expect in an old building. But other than that, we had a great stay.
One note: parking at the hotel is $36. However, after 5 or so on the weekend, street parking is free, and seemed abundant (check the parking ticket machines on the street - it seems different parts of town have different regulations and hours). So for our Saturday overnight stay, we just parked on the street right down the block from the hotel.

title: “So-So Hotel for the money”
text: My husband & I stayed here on Dec 3rd. Everything about the room and bathroom seemed very old although the room was larger than most NYC hotel rooms. It was an okay stay but for $300+ I think we could have done a little bit better.

title: “Good choice for seeing Manhattan”
text: Stayed at The Edison from May27 - June 3 2004, on the recommendation of a friend. It was all he said - ideally located for a first-time visitor - just off Times Square - clean & comfortable. Good size, air-conditioned, smoke-free room with 2 large, comfortable beds. Surprisingly quiet, too, considering the location. Small but adequate bathroom with very powerful shower & plentiful supply of fresh towels. Hotel staff were helpful & courteous at all times. Hairdryer, iron & ironing-board provided within minutes of request. Hotel is just 2 minutes from the Times Square tickets-booth, open-top bus-stops & subway & in easy walking distance of the Broadway theatres, Central Park & other tourist sights. Not very impressed with the attached cafe & didn't try the restaurant. The Deli 2 doors away offers a wide choice of foods for breakfast.

title: “Too much neon and overpriced”
text: This is a tourist hotel. Do not go here if you are there on business. You will be annoyed after a minute on the 4th floor. The elevators are packed and stop on every floor. It's excessively neon. I'm still fuming at the price. Microscopic rooms. Grr. Don't go.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text:
We booked into The Bentley for 5 days to celebrate our honeymoon. The journey from JFK wasnt too bad (approx half hr during rush hour) and our initial impressions were very good. The lobby was very attractive and the staff were very helpful. We stayed in a room on the 11th floor which was lovely and had 2 very large beds! We had a very good nights sleep the whole time we were there. 
The view was exactly how we imagined New York to be with a view of tall buildings one side and the river and Roosevelt Island on the other- very nice. 
We were able to walk to eveywhere which was quite handy. Bloomingdales and Central Park only a few blocks away. There were plenty of places to eat and drink within the vicinity. 
The only negative we had was that because the hotel is next to the FDR there was a lot of traffic noise, but then thats probably the same wherever you stay in NYC. Once we'd got used to it it was fine. 
The rooftop bar and restaurant on the 21st floor is stunning. We went up one night and had cocktails on the veranda which was quite romantic. Stunning views! 
Although the hotel charges for Wi-fi we roamed and managed to find access to someone elses which wasnt password protected and was on all the time! Definitely recommend trying to get away with that one!
We would quite likely stay here again if we ever get the chance to go back to New York.

title: “Beautiful roof top bar!”
text: We love the Kimpton Hotel chain and have stayed at 4 different hotels, 3 of which were in NYC - we booked at the 4th Manhattan hotel for our stay May 11-13, 2012. We were not surprised to find a warm welcome as always. The hotel is located a little out the way 49th and 11th but a block from the Hudson River. They always have a wine hour from 5-6pm in the lobby. This hotel had a roof top bar that we went to check out for a drink before going to dinner - what a view! It was so beautiful to see the setting sun on the river and the downtown core from the other angle. Drink can be expensive but I guess that kind of view has a price. Would stay there again in a minute.

title: “Exceeded expectations for airport hotel”
text: My family of four stayed one night at this hotel before flying out of the Indianapolis hotel in the morning. The hotel exceeded my expectations in every way. The room was big and clean - and the staff was very helpful. I will stay there again when traveling from the Indianapolis airport.

title: “Great stay, perfect location”
text:
I stayed at the New Yorker with my husband for 7 days mid May, we both had a wonderful time, we were out most of the day so mainly used the room as a place to crash or have a mid afternoon rest before venturing out again. The location is fantastic, within walking distance to all major sites and very close to subways and buses.
The room was very clean and modern, we stayed on the 23rd floor (room 2333) and had a great view of the Empire State building out of our window!! :o) Didn't have any issues with street noise as we were so high up. Ok, the rooms are on the small side especially compared to European standards, but space is at a premimum in New York and I have heard that most NYC hotels have tiny rooms so was kind of expecting this. However, we were given two double beds for no extra charge which was handy as it meant that our room was bigger than average. The bathroom was a little dated but served its purpose and had lots of toiletries and towels (wish they had proper bath towels rather than lots of small hand towels, but that's me being picky) never had any issues with hot water as some other guests mentioned. All the staff we came to contact with were very pleasant and friendly and check in and check out was fast. There are a number of lifts in the lobby which service this massive hotel, they were very efficient and you rarely had to wait long to catch one.
Breakfast was not included, but with so many restaurants and cafes around, this was not a problem- loved Jumba juice bar- gorgeous smoothies and they do a tasty egg and spinich toasted tortilla wrap - yum!! We tried out the Tic Toc Diner for breakfast one time (diner attached to the hotel) after hearing so many good reviews. Once was enough, it was ok, but very average. There are much better places out there for a better price. We tried out Ellen's Stardust Diner for the experience one lunch time, it was very cheesy, but had a great fun factor with wannabe theatical performers singing tracks from popular Broadway shows whilst you eat, worth going and try the milkshakes- 1000's of calories but VERY nice. (on 1650 Broadway). For a nice dinner try Ruby Tuesdays- on 7th Ave (between 41st/42nd St) we had the most delicious steak which cut through like butter, great staff and they even gave us free starter as we waited 'long' (only 15 mins!). 'Vergils' steak house on the otherhand not so good, humongeous portions (one starter and main shared -main only half eaten) huge but not great quality, we found the meat to be overly salty and fatty.
Top of the Rock (Rockerfeller Center) very worth seeing and is better than Empire State building, look up 'High line' park on top of a dis-used railway track about 6 meters above ground level, very unique. BB's jazz club worth popping into.
Had a great time and did loads of shopping as well as sightseeing, if I were staying in New York, would definitely consider New Yorker again.

title: “Top birch!!!!”
text: Excellent location, love the happy hour and service. Great terrace on the 14th floor.

title: “Luxurious Hotel in heart of Downtown”
text:
This is one of the most luxurious hotels I have stayed in. It is designed to give the ambience of a boutique hotel and from the mintute you step inside you don't want to leave.
Everything from pet goldfishes to Aveda toiletries make this a worthwhile visit. The staff were friendly and helpful and the complimentary evening wine tasting makes you forget about those tired feet. The rooms don't have a great view but youl'l be too taken in with the decor to notice.

title: “Holiday Getwaya”
text:
My wife and I had the pleasure of spending three nights at this hotel. The overall experience was good. The bed was great but the pillows were horribly soft.
My only compliant revolves around the fact that we were given a handicap room after I told the check-in agent that only one of two rooms were to be for the disabled. 
Forget the expensive hotel parking and park in the covered garage around the corner.

title: “Top Floors Suites Comparison”
text: Our family spent Thanksgiving in both the Penthouse Suite on the 22nd top floor, and the Presidential Suite on the floor below. Perks of the Penthouse suite included 2 full baths, full size fridge, wine fridge, microwave, two leather couches and a surround sound system. We preferred the Presidential even though it had 1 1/2 baths. The full bath had a jacuzzi with TV and picture window. The spacious living area featured marble floors (vs. carpeted upstairs), more decor, dining table and 8 chairs, 3 stools at the bar, office area, 2 small fridges and a microwave in the kitchen. Three TVs. The corner bedroom has windows on both sides and a chaise lounge. Although both suites had picture windows facing the water, the 21st floor has a door out to a balcony. Lots of room to spread out. Valet parking or self park garage. Walking distance to our Thanksgiving dinner on South Street!

title: “Best Hotel - Seattle”
text: We stayed for 2 nights at this property and fell in love w/it. Location, location, location -- near to Pike Place Mkt, fabulous restaurants and shopping w/in walking distance. Staff was very attentive as well as friendly -- one had the feeling that they enjoyed their jobs. Rooms have alot of charm and very comfortable. We could not have been happier and will stay here in the future

title: “Excellent service”
text: We were in town for a vacation the staff welcomed us and treated us with the best service. The pool and jacuzzi were wonderful .

title: “Great Stay”
text: It was a fantastic view. The room was very cheap considering what the other hotels were charging. Plus they gave us a free upgrade to an ocean view. Excellent

title: “"stay somewhere else" the worst stay”
text: this hotel is the worst ive ever stayed at.....the rooms oare about 8 by 8 feet . You can hear everthing in the hallway and stairwells..No ice or ice machines Cant access your car while u "Stay" if i could i would have stayed anywhere else in times square.... tried to order roomservice only to have to phone answered by someone who didnt nKnow anything about the menu and also had to wait 20 minutes on hold for just the order.Then i asked to speak to the manager and never even got a call back..my advice stay anywhere else dont befooled by photos the lobby,s as small as the rooms some pathetic fish and cubicle seating...a weak attempt to be "hip" more like ...custied out..

title: “incredible service”
text: Stayed here for a long weekend for a wedding at this hotel. Had a blast. The room was a typical hotel room. Clean and very comfortable. My request for a quiet room was filled. Average size room and bathroom. The hotel is all about the service. Every staff member was friendly and accommodating. I couldn't walk down a hallway without a smile from a staff member. The grounds are very attractive as is the entry area. We had a special wedding rate which made the hotel more affordable. I don't think I would want to pay the rack rate on their website for this hotel though. The pool was fairly crowded. Took a tour through the exercise facility and it is impressive. Our group loved the gazebo by the pool for drinks and snacks. The hotel bar also was great to hang out with family after the rehearsal dinner and wedding. Restaurant was good, pricey but with great service.

title: “Perfect hotel”
text: Great hotel!! Very affordable, very clean and spacious rooms. A perfect location. Very friendly staff. Free breakfast, a great deal!!

title: “Stayed 3 times this summer...will continue to stay there!”
text:
My husband and I had to be in Jacksonville 4 times this summer (2-3 nights). The only reason we didn't stay in this hotel all three times was because this hotel was sold out.
The staff and management are professional, personable and met our every need. 
The rooms are excellent, newly furnished and kept very clean. The TV lineup is great (many channels) and there are a lot of outlets which is a big plus with cellphones, laptops, etc.
The buffet is delicious and the bar area is very comfy. Can you tell I really like this hotel!

title: “Great place and location, some minor issues”
text:
This is a great and stylish hotel which I would recommend at any time. Stayed in a standard room with hardly any view (courtyard) and in a suite on the 11th floor facing Stout Street which was very nice. Housekeeping is impeccable and breakfast very nice (although it is only served until 9 AM - 10 AM weekends - which is not long enough when on holiday).
Also great: Free Newspaper, perfect downtown location (nearby drugstore open until midnight, many coffee shops and restaurants, 16th Street Mall just a few steps away). Very nice bathrooms.
Why just 4 stars? There were some minor minus points, but they add up to "above average" instead of "excellent".
Staff was gerenally very friendly - there was just one arrogant dissapointing exception at checkin. Aditionally, there was a loud noise from a water tube everytime the neighbour flushed the toilet; it woke me up almost everytime. No noise related issues besides that.
Wireless Internet is free, the provider's IP address, however, is blacklisted so most of my outgoing mails got caught by spam filters and never arrived. Also, the connection is very unstable or jammed (sometimes no access for several minutes, mostly slow access) - for me working online a lot this was very annoying.
The TV remote control probably got some orange juice stains, some buttons glued in when pressed down, so I asked for a replacement but the new remote had exactly the same problem.
In the suite, no information about how to turn up / down / off the fireplace was available. The hairdryer in the suite did not work.
Parking is the big problem here: Staff has many creative ideas how to prevent high fees in the adjacent garage, but they all consist of cheating ("tell them you lost your ticket") which is not for everyone. It probably would have been the thing to do anyway - since the system is very unfair and not logical: Arrive friday at 6:05 PM and stay until monday at 5:55 AM - because no attendant is there during that period, just insert the credit card and pay the weekend rate of 8 bucks. When you leave, however, monday at 10 AM when the attendant is present, you pay the whole weekend plus for hours of friday and monday, up to almost 40$! The hotel should make sure FAST they get a special rate here since valet is 24$ per day.
Anyway: Much more plus than minus, I'd stay there again.

title: “Pretty Good place”
text: The customer service and staff was some of the best I've experienced. The bed was uncomfortable. Okay value for the money. Quiet neighborhoond. Starbucks nearby. Proximity (next door) to a good supermarket (Harris Teeter) that serves buffet meals a plus. Really easy to reach from the Metro line (NoMa station). The weekend rates were very reasonable. Don't know if I'd pay that amount for weekdays.

title: “A Nice Hotel, but Flawed”
text:
In general the staff was friendly and professional and the hotel was clean. However, there were a few things we didn't care for. The room was quite cramped; there was only a foot or less of clearance to walk around the corner of one bed to enter the room. Electrical outlets were positioned in locations that required considerable contortions to access. The wooden blinds let too much light into the rooms if you want to sleep late. The bathroom didn't give you much privacy; there was just a partial door to the toilet and the sounds of every bodily function that occured there were shared with anyone in the room. We made our reservation through an on-line promotion which said we would receive a free bottle of wine with our stay, but they said they knew nothing about the free wine when we checked in. I suppose if we had put up a big stink they might have given us the wine, but we were tired from travelling and were in not mood to fight for it. They keep the lobby air conditioning set to what felt like 60°, perhaps because their staff wore what looked like wool uniforms; such a waste of energy. We had an early train to catch and our 5 a.m. wake up call came at 5:20, so we had to hustle to Union Station on time.
We enjoyed our breakfast at the Café Dupont and appreciated the free wi-fi.

title: “I love Holiday Inn Express”
text: Somehow they just hit-the-spot with me. Everything I need (breakfast, wifi, iron and ironing board, comfortable bed and pillows, plenty of TV choice) plus what I like (helpful staff) with nothing extra. No muss no fuss, just comfortable and affordable place to stay when I like. The only complaint I have is the noisy heating/cooling system (well, the rooms in New York at least are pretty cramped, too).

title: “Very well pleased”
text: We are here for 5 days celbrating our 50th Wed. Anv. Extramly pleased with the folks who work here, esp Ricky Shah who has been most helpful and friendly. Would clearly stay here again if we were to return to Memphis!. We intially came for one day, extended to four, and then added another day.

title: “OK but Expected a little more”
text: For the price they charge and being rated a Four star hotel, you would expect more perks such as free wi fi, but nothing is for free in this hotel. Not even a business center with internet access, which I think is rediculous. The best feature was the comfortable beds. The AC thermostat appears to be a "fake" meaning they give you the impression you can set the temp, but we could not get the Temp in the room below 72, no matter how low we put the AC set to and for how lung. I would go for a gas lamp location next time near 5th avenue. Parking can be a pain if you don't want to pay $30.

title: “Took a second stay, but this time one word for it "Perfection"”
text: We had stayed in the Lenox last year during the Christmas break but there were small nagging issues that prevented me from giving this hotel anything but 3 stars. We decided to give this hotel yet another try during the Thanksgiving weekend and this time around, our stay could not have been better. Right from the old world charm of this hotel, the service, the location, their rooms (we stayed in one of their PURE guest rooms), the dining, the heavenly bed (I slept more peacefully there then I had in a number of months) - everything was amazing. Even when we stayed there the last time, the service was exemplary and we were happy to see the same standards a year later. All the nagging issues we had last time - there was nothing to spoil our experience this time around. The location (right next to Prudential and Copley and a block from Newbury) was perfect for shopping and taking the T. The close proximity to some of the best Boston restaurants (L'espalier and Mistral) does not hurt either. The breakfast in the dining room was also a perfect start to the day and the drinks at the City Bar in the evening were great (one of the best Mai Tais I have ever had). All in all, we thoroughly enjoyed our weekend at the Lenox. Big thumbs up!

title: “I would stay here again”
text: I attended a convention that was held at an adjacent hotel that was under construction. I had never been to this Sheraton before but my experience was very good. The suite was clean and had a great view of Downtown Dallas. They offer a free shuttle within 5 miles, which was great. The staff person took me to a nearby supermarket so I could do some grocery shopping - as the room had a fridge and microwave, which was a real cost saver! The air conditioning works so well that you should plan to bring a light jacket with you. I can't say enough about the friendly staff -- especially the folks at the front desk. Great job!

title: “Very nice hotel”
text: Very nice hotel. Everyone was pleasant. Took my wife for our anniversary. Rooms very spacious. All that one would expect from a upscale hotel. Only complaint is that the beds are a little hard. (You hear other guests complain about it in the elevator). Other than that, great hotel and staff to run the place.

title: “Tries to be a 4-star hotel, acts like a 2 1/2 or 3-star”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel about once or twice a year over the past several years. The property has gone downhill each time I stay there and I actually checked out early on this last trip.
Upon driving up, there were no parking valets, no bellmen, nada. I unloaded my own bags after waiting 5-10 minutes onto a cart and brought them up to the front desk with me. Finally, someone spotted me with a cart and offered some assistance.
The hotel is comparable to the nearby Marriott, Hilton or Courtyard, but they are all cheaper.
After several days of waiting for the car in the morning, or waiting for a parking attendant, I checked out a day early. Calling for luggage assistance, I waited 15 minutes, and again, no help. I carried my own bags downstairs and left. 
I am a Starwoods Gold Member and I'll never stay at this hotel again. Discussing the problem with the front desk staff, all I got was the shoulder shrug.
Lots of other places to stay in the area, for less, with better service.

title: “Good Hotel - no complaints”
text:
Stayed here while in San Francisco for 5 days. 
Hotel was very good. We were placed on the 22nd floor which offered a great view.
The location is excellent. You can easily travel to parts of SF with Bus stops right outside the hotel and a Cable car stop on California Street (which is next to the hotel). Buy a Muni Pass and travel the buses and cable cars as single trips on a cable car are $6 one way, but a 7 day pass is only $27. You can buy these from the Hotel's gift shop.
Breakfast was good. Offering Continental as well as hot (though 5 days of Scarmbled eggs got boring). 
There is a pool on the 6th floor, but we never used it.
Rooms were well sized and clean. Beds were comfortable.

title: “The Affinia was a perfect match for us!”
text: Took my 15 yr old son to Chicago for Spring Break. At check in, I explained the reason for our trip and since my son had never been to Chicago before, we were hoping for a room up high with a good view. The front desk person; Jeff told us that he did not have a dble room available with a good view but he would upgrade us to a better room with a great view at no additional charge. The room was perfect and definately had a great view! It was the beginning of a 4 day stay where great service was always demonstrated! The amenities and location were unbeatable. The suggestions for dinner by the concierge were great. I will definitely go back and suggest the Affinia to all my friends and family!

title: “Airport Life”
text: I loved the convenience of this hotel to the airport. The heated pool made a long day seem to fade away. The restaurant had marginal grill food but you can't beat the convenience. The room was beautifully decorated and had the feel of upscale amenities. As a picky consumer I found this hotel to be one of my favorites for a close nights stay for an early departure.

title: “Great Location, Friendly Staff, Kids loved it!!”
text: I stayed 3 nights at the Pac Terrace with my wife and 2 small children (8,6) and we had a blast! This wonderful hotel is situated right on the boardwalk overlooking the beach and Pacific Ocean... literally steps to the sand. Our sunset view from room 220 was spectacular! The location is perfect for a business or leisure trip to the area. We loved the heated pool and hot tub, both were very clean and well maintained. The kids could have spent hours in there! The staff was so friendly and approachable. There was nothing they wouldn't do for us during our stay. The hotel supplied us each with cruiser bikes to take up and down the boardwalk.... certainly the highlight on sunny day in SD. We'll be back for sure!!

title: “Early morning flight, convenient, terrible restaurant”
text: We picked this hotel to assist with catching a 6 am flight. Quiet and convenient. Pricey overall for what we got. Access to a pool and hot tub was a pleasant pus for an airport location. The low point was our meal at the only dining option. Terrible value, long wait and really lackluster fare.

title: “Average hotel, excellent location”
text:
There were some extremely negative reviews of this hotel on here prior to my visit, so I went expecting the worst, however I was not as aghast as I thought I may be. 
We chose this hotel because we were travelling into NYC by train to Penn station, & we wanted to be able to get to our hotel quickly- well, I couldn't have asked for better, as I could see the entrance of the hotel before I'd even stepped out of Penn station. 
Times square is about a 10 minute walk away, & the Empire state building was a 5 minute walk away, infact we even had a view of the Empire state from our room. 
We waited for around half an hour in a queue to get checked in, the staff behind the desk seemed in no rush! However they were courteous. Our room was clean, the water was hot, & the towels were replenished every day. In terms of value for money, it couldn't be beaten. You get what you pay for in New York, & this hotel was cheaper to stay in that a crummy rat infested B&B in my local town. It's not the Ritz, but come on, this is NEW YORK! Who needs the Ritz when you've got that to explore!

title: “Fabulous!”
text: Just arrived back in Scotland having stayed 5 nights in this glorious hotel. Myself and 15 of my friends were in NYC celebrating some of my friends 50th birthdays. I emailed ahead to Jessie to request adjoining/higher level rooms and when we arrived we received rooms on the 41st floor, free wifi AND champagne and chocolates in each room. 4 of our party were upgraded to a junior suite which became our meeting point! A small tip ($3) each day ensured we had enough glorious Starbucks coffee on hand and a short walk round the corner to the deli provided an adequate breakfast to start the day. The beds were indeed "heavenly" and the double headed shower was a god send after a hard day shopping and sight-seeing. The rooms was spacious with an absolutely fantastic view and immaculate. The bell boy, reception staff and doormen couldn't be more helpful. The hotel is situated just far enough away from the centre of Times Square but as it's near 7th Ave, very convenient for everything. Loads of restaurants, shops and deli's nearby. On our last day (Tuesday) the hotel was celebrating it's 10th Anniversary and before we left, we were treated to a glass of champagne and cake in the foyer and the bell boy took our luggage from our rooms and stored it until we were ready to leave. Can't thank Jessie and the rest of the staff enough for the best time ever. Will definitely stay in this hotel again. Miss it already!!!

title: “Give me a break...its not that bad!”
text: My husband and I have stayed at the Grant Plaza twice and I will say that the first time was great, we had a small room, but it had a window overlooking Grant Street and we could jump on the cable car in an instant or walk anywhere. The second time we were stuck in a former closet (I think) that looked out into the A/C unit. We simply went down and told them we didn't want to stay in that room and they put us in the room we had stayed in before without question. This place is a few steps up from a hostel... it is not fancy. On the other hand, they are nice and will see to it you are happy if you ask. We'll stay there again without worry!

title: “Perrrrrfect!”
text: The location is awesome. Literally a walk to great food, shopping and the river. It has a neighborhoody feel in the middle of NYC. Walking distance to Ground Zero, West Village, Greenwich etc. The hotel is beautiful. The staff is great, service was attentive and authentic. And....they give you free bottle water! I hate hotels that charge $5 for a bottle of water. It was great, I will definitely stay there again.

title: “Nice stay”
text: Very centrally located hotel with exceptional service. Rooms are modernized and clean. Only downside is that parking is a little expensive.

title: “Couldn't Be Happier”
text: I just got back from staying three nights at this Hilton, and I couldn't be happier. I took my parents and my daughter to NYC for a short Easter vacation, and we stayed from Sunday (Easter) until Wednesday. When we arrived, late afternoon, there was a short wait to check-in, but I was able to get two rooms on the 31st floor, my parents got a king bed, and my daughter and I had two doubles. The rooms were spacious and well decorated. There was plenty of storage for clothing and closet space. The bathroom was clean, and somewhat small, but it served its purpose. The location was excellent, as I prefer to stay somewhat clear of the times square crowds, but close enough for an easy walk. We also spent time at the American Girl Doll store, and were very close to this location. Best of all, we got the rooms through priceline for $115 per night, and were not treated like anything other than proper guests of the hotel. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Average hotel but nice location”
text: I like the hotel location but the rooms are average. The bar attached is nice and also having the mall right there is nice. The elevators are slower than what you would expect. The staff was nice and the meeting room facilities were good.

title: “Not the greatest”
text: Stayed at Super 8 for a couple of days; some of the rooms smelled like cat litter and others were very small. Not much room to move around with all the furniture they try to put into some of the rooms. Our room had an unwanted pest (cock roach) in it, one night and also heard another member of our party had the same thing. Hotel was re-done but still has more work to do. Hard to also park in the parking lot with a staircase, on both sides of the building protruding out into the parking lot. Other hotels next store, look way better (like Great Western). Would not suggest this hotel with the type of people that come there. Had a derelict next to us; had door and window always open. Was drunk and bedding was totally stripped and didn't care.

title: “Good location for Old Town”
text: My husband and I stayed here to attend a concert at the Sports Arena. It was the perfect location. We had a 5 minute can ride to Old Town and the same to the Arena. They have a managers reception for a couple of hours in the evening, they had small appetizers and beer. We didn't use this service but saw a sign that offers guests a shuttle to pro games if they stay there. We would DEFINATELY stay for that added service. Hotel was clean, reception area had an attached game room, pool table. We would stay there again.

title: “Its really a motel”
text: Great location, very large and very busy. This hotel operates more like a motel, very old building in need of many repairs, long lines for check in and out, quality of service dependent on which floor your room is located, rules such as pet policy changes with whoever is in change. If staying just to briefly rest and primarily to tour NYC, then it will suffice.

title: “Some Issues but a Beautiful Facility”
text: I have been staying at The Drake for right at 20 years and always rated it well. The hotel is just an elegant gem that continues to hold its' own after all of the years. Even though it is not convenient to the business area I continue to stay here. Two issues: The internet is simply awful. For a business hotel charging $13 a night for slower than dial-up internet it is a crime. I gave up trying to download business documents. Second issue...they lost my FedEx package. I was not notified of the arrival and 6 hour later I went down looking for it. It took them almost an hour to find the package. The day manager was polite and professional but she needs to whip her front desk and receiving staff in line. One sad note. The wonderful Cape Cod Restaurant (where i first ate nearly 50 years ago) was just empty. It is clearly struggling in this economy. The food was great but in the two hours I was in the restaurant during prime dinner time they served just two tables.

title: “What happened to service?”
text:
