The hotel, unlike a lot of Courtyard properties, needs some help. The service is well below what I would expect from Marriott hotels and the amenities are being cut back to the point of making it unpleasant to stay.
Our room overlooked the Houston Metro Rail. Normally not an issue except that the windows are single pane and allow the noise of the tram to filter in all night! Difficult to sleep when you hear a bell ringing every few minutes. Otherwise, the room was ok. The office chair is so low (at it's highest level) that you end up with sore shoulders from reaching up to the desk to work.
My biggest beef is that every other Marriott property I visit offers free coffee throughout the day. Not this one. When I asked, the answer was "Nobody drinks coffee at this time of day." News flash, I do! The recommendation is to visit the Starbucks on the corner. Thank you, but no. 
Everytime we left the hotel to look for a restaurant, go to work etc. we were accosted by one or two "gentlemen" demanding spare change. I realize that homelessness and panhandling are not the hotels issue but, encouraging these folks to move along and not bother the guests would be very much appreciated.
I visit Houston regularly and will now make an effort to visit other hotels, even other Marriotts rather than stay here.

title: “Crowded room, poor customer service”
text: The Hampton Inn has been our first choice when traveling for many years. We had our first bad experience at this hotel with the room being way overcrowded with excess furniture making it very uncomfortable and difficult to get around. The desk clerk was very rude and did not help us find a cart to transport our luggage to our room. His comment when asked where all the carts were was "Probably the Concourse Hotel has ours". Being Senior Citizens these where two big negatives in our stay. The desk clerk in the morning was the complete opposite and very helpful., breakfast was great and shuttle service was top notch. They were great in letting us keep our car there for 9 days at a reasonable fee.

title: “Fantastic New York”
text: Stayed for 4 nights. Staff more than helpful and polite, made full use of concierge desk who were able to answer every question we asked. Had two studio rooms between 5 adults. First rooms offered quite small and dark, on 12/13th floor. Asked to be moved higher and got bigger better rooms on 22/27th floors, very clean, bathrooms however very small. View breathtaking. Restaurant served good thanksgiving dinner, reasonably priced. Street noise didnt bother us although Fire Dept only seemed to go out at night. But hey it wouldnt be New York without noise. Within walking distance to Macy's and Broadway and Empire State. First visit to New York but will not be last. Would certainly recommend Affinia to others.

title: “Terrible!”
text: The room at the Pennsylvania Hotel was one of the worst I've ever stayed in (and that includes some really bad fishing camps). The bathroom was filthy! Cables exposed in several locations with holes in the walls. Shower head sprayed water all over the bathroom. When we arrived the room smelled like a bottle of bleach! The ads for this hotel appear to be inaccurate - the room we stayed in had not been remodeled in 50 years! It was a terrible selection - we wouldn't recommend to anyone!

title: “Room Quality was "Gross"”
text:
My wife , 12month old, and I checked into our "villa" bay view room on 12/30 for some relaxation and change of pace. We've stayed here before for a wedding, circa 2009 and we loved it. So, when we saw the awesome deal on Expedia we jumped. Well, here is our story:
We checked in around 4:30pm, I was tired from driving 3hrs, so I settled in for a quick 30 min. cat nap. Fast forward 1 hr. and I wake up to my arm being literally "glued" to the comforter and the duvet style blanket. I was disgusted, my wife jetted down the hall to get ice as a means to get the gum off my fairly expensive shirt. Fifteen minutes past, and the final outcome was a RL shirt with remnants of pink bubble gum still stuck on the shoulder. My wife called the front desk, then was transferred to housekeeping. I spoke to housekeeping, and they said they would send someone up. Thirty minutes go by, nothing. Forty minutes... and then I called to remind them to pick up the items. A gentlemen finally did come, and he said he will redeliver the items with fresh ones. I understand things happen, so I tried to cut some slack to the housekeeping "oversight". The family went out to dinner, we returned at 9:45pm still nothing.I called and they said it was still be cleaned, what? no extras at a 300+ room hotel. My wife said she wasn't that cold, so we gave up and went to sleep with just the sheets. In the morning I spoke to the guy at the front desk, and all he said was "sorry about that". It was disingenuous at best. 
Pros:
The pool was beautiful and it had a 1 ft pool for the kids
The bay view was super nice.
No charge for cabanas usage.
Beautiful grounds
Running and biking area within 100 feet of bay rooms
Cons:
Gross housekeeping in our room (hopefully an isolated event)
Peeling wallpaper in the bathroom
$30 for parking
Lackadaisical staff

title: “Nice Hotel - Easy Access to Zoo”
text: We stayed here one night over the Labor Day weekend. We chose this hotel for it's location near Adams Morgan, Mt.Pleasant and the National Zoo. It's a short walk to Dupont Circle, and in a safe part of town. Rooms were small, but clean and the hotel was quiet considering it was busy. Would stay here again - and continue to use the Room + Parking Package offered on their website. (Parking in this part of town is very difficult and can be even more expensive than what the hotel charges.)

title: “Amazing!!”
text: This place was incredible! We booked a room with Travel Planners and told them jokingly to give us a great room because we had never been to Chicago and we were in shock when we were taken to our room! Following the bellhop past all of the single doors on the 14th floor to the end of the hall, we came to a set of double doors. When he opened the doors to this massive suite, we thought there had to be a HUGE mistake as we were only paying $150 per night! It had a huge living and dining room, a bar, 1 huge half bath, and 1 unbelievably huge full bath with a shower large enough for 4, and a giant tub with a tv built in the wall! The bedroom was incredible with 2 oversized chairs and an ottaman, an armoire with web tv, nintendo, and a large tv. There were windows down each side of the room, lots of them, that overlooked downtown! The maids put jelly belly's on your pillow at turndown and there's a big vase full of jelly belly's. It's decorated with what looks like way cool pier 1 furnishings. Just unreal! We were there for 8 days and I long to go back but I am sure that suite is well over $1000 per night. It was the best and such a fun, unique place!

title: “Okay service, dirty rooms, internet hackers in the business cetner”
text:
I stayed at this hotel with some colleagues for a business trip. I booked three single rooms with king sized beds, when I got to my room, there were two beds. But when I went downstairs to complain, the man at the front desk said since I booked through Expedia, they don't guarantee rooms.
The room was okay, I was somewhat annoyed because there was what looked to be a food stain on the duster of the bed. A little gross.
The breakfast was okay, the table dirty and the service was slow.
When I checked out, I asked for a receipt, they couldn't give me one saying that since I booked through Expedia, they don't know how much I paid. This would have been fine but the woman at the front desk was outright RUDE.
Lastly, when I got home, I noticed some weird things going on with my credit card. Turns out someone hacked my account and added themselves as an authorized user. The only way I can think this happened is someone either was watching or hacked my account when I was in the business center. There were some shady characters there, and I know not to look up financial information at hotels.
Overall, no major issues but enough minor ones to make the stay unpleasant.

title: “Rooms not what was reserved”
text:
Traveling with children, we had email confirmation that rooms would be adjoining. Did not happen. Kids were down the hall.
Also room reservation clearly states king room with sleep number beds. Once again no such luck. I am thinking that breakfast tomorrow morning will not have coffee

title: “Great location and very clean”
text: I have traveled here with my family in the past week. The staff at check-in were extremely friendly. The location was key. Only three blocks from Grand Central. The rooms, even though they had not been updated, were very, very clean and large.

title: “A Brilliant 5 star hotel with the best Breakfast area in America overlooking Times Square”
text: The rooms were large, clean, spiffy and all had an area for a lounge suite and lounge chair.The location was amazing and the staff great.For groups, try to get out of the $3 surcharge per person per night...we did! its tipping in disguise of a charge.

title: “Beauty and Basics”
text:
My husband and I came here for the weekend of May 16th and 17th. The room rate was great for downtown San Francisco. I am not a big city person and was awed by the location. I work in the hospitality industry, so I'm a harsh critic when I stay anywhere. I was very surprised by the look and feel of the hotel. It was very modern, and beautifully taken care of. Most of the time when I've gone down the halls of hotels there is a bit of a sterile feel, but the decor and over all feel was very earthy and homey, while maintaining the chicness throughout. The person who checked us in was very nice and courteous. The halls were a bit of a maze, but that's design not the hotel's fault. 
The room while small, was just fine for me and my husband. We don't need a large room. I'm a stickler for checking cleanliness of the bed and any signs of pests, the matress and linens were crisp and clean and beautiful. The bathroom was nice and quaint, it was clean and the basics were there.
A downside was the parking, call me unknowledgable of the area, but there was no parking for hotel guests. So the parking that we were directed to and I quote " is about three blocks down, you can't miss it" We apparently couldn't find it, because when we came back for the day at ten that night, the only lot that was available was about 6 blocks down. I don't mind the walk, just wished there was a bit more specific direction to the parking. 
One of the downsides I had was in the restaurant for breakfast. I had pancakes and as I was eating them there was a hair in the pancake, not the most pleasant of gifts. I had gotten through most of the meal already so I just set it aside and let the waitress know. She was apologetic and courteous. 
We ate there again in the evening, mostly because I love the Elephant and Castle restaurant that I had eaten at in Seattle. The food that evening, while busy for St. Patrick's Day was wonderful and the atmosphere was great. The food was amazaing and I highly suggest the cheesecake. It is to die for!

title: “Top Class Location”
text:
Stayed here over easter with my wife to be. The location is excellent. You can walk to times square without taking a breath!! Hotel is also quiet for its location. Rooms are very small, but in fairness i was aware of this before booking as it stated the exact size of the room in square feet on their website!Rooms nice-bed extremely comfortable-nice plasma TV in the room. Would i stay here again?-Yes i would. Highlight had to be meeting Jenifer Anniston outside the front door as they were filimg 'The Basting'.
Staff very helpful. Hotel lobby very classy...
Down side of the hotel- I paid extra to have Breakfast (Continental) included. This consisted of muffins, Orange Juice & Tea. Not even toast or cereal or fruit. Not worth paying extra for. The bar/club in the hotel charge a fortune for drings. One beer and a G&T cost me $20.
Overall - 
-Staff very nice.
-Complimentary internet a nice touch.
-Rooms very comfortable.
-Location excellent.
-Food & drink way overpriced. 
-Will be back

title: “Convenient for conference”
text: I had a one-day workshop in this hotel, and I found the experience quite comfortable. The room was spacious, and it had an interesting view of planes taking off and landing. In spite of being part of the airport, however, there was little to no noise from the airplanes. In fact the only noise was in the hall when someone opened a door. The bed was very comfortable, and the service was outstanding.

title: “Greatly Improved”
text:
Spent a couple of nights here and thought this hotel was very good. It is well placed in El Paso and in a nice part of town and had everything we expected it to have based on the previous reviews on this site, they don't do it justice. We got a good rate which made it great value for money and the hotel is in good condition so everything feels nice.
This is the perfect place if you are in town for a short number of nights, as everywhere is pretty close.

title: “A little noisy but lots of character”
text: We spent two nights at the Peabody in October. I booked a corner room, which apparently does not mean necessarily the corner of the hotel. My assigned room was not ready when I checked in after the check-in time but after some delay I received another room. It was great: high-ceilinged, spacious, withgreat windows overlooking Union Street . It had a king bed with deluxe linens and a separate seating area with a comfortable sofa and chair positioned for easy reading and television viewing. The bathroom was older but well appointed, and I loved having a large bar of soap. The only downside was, as other reviewers have noted, some noise issues. The street noise carried into the room. On one night we were awakened around 4:30 a.m. by a drunk profanely yelling in the hall; he seemed to be inches away from the sound (security was called and removed him -- or at least the noise). Parking in the self-parking lot is convenient if you intend to be going in and out but otherwise, for the $5 difference, I'd pick the valet. I'd go back in a second.

title: “Nice Hotel, Good Value, Good Location”
text: Had a very nice stay here in August, 2011. My wife and I were visiting someone who lives in Eastern Market, and we also wanted to see some of the monuments and museums. The location was perfect for both purposes, at the foot of Capitol Hill and just a few blocks from Eastern Market. The rooms are large, price is reasonable, staff are friendly and efficient. The free breakfast was a nice feature. To do better, I think you would have to pay luxury prices, which we are not willing to do. A nice choice if you like the area.

title: “An excellent apartment, like home from home”
text: The Marmara is a great place to stay. We had a one bedroom suite, which was ideal as we have a teenage daughter. She was able to sleep on the sofa bed in a separate room. A very high level of cleanliness and a super comfy bed! I guess the sheets and pillowcases are luxury egyptian cotton as it was like sleeping on a cloud. Having a kitchen was great too, especially for breakfast and hot drinks, and also chilling wine! Approx. 10 mins to the nearest subway and around 10-15 minutes ride to Central Station (an awesome building). I would recommend to anyone. A tip for bargains in clothes, shoes, jewellery etc is a department store called Century 21, located in the Financial District. Spent hours there!!

title: “Fine Rooms, Friendly Staff”
text:
Stayed here for two nights on business. My colleague and I each had king suites. Our rooms were city views, which was fine. I could see the riverwalk from my room. The accomodations are pretty standard. Bed was comfortable and room was fairly quiet. Did like that it was a true suite with separate bedroom. Tries to be on par with a trendy boutique type hotels with the exposed brick wall in the lounge area of the room.
The property is only two years old so the ammenities are newer. However, the hairdryer looked like it had been through the wringer - some of the coating on the handle was chipped and falling off. Also the bathroom is nothing too spectacular. The tub is deep but you have to step up to get into shower/tub combo. The shower head is a little low and I'm only 5'9". I almost tripped getting out of the shower since it is a big step down.
Some of the furniture in the great room/lounge area of the suite looked a little worn but it was alright. Did appreciate the full length mirror in that area.
The other cons:
Wireless internet is available, as is ethernet, but it is $9.95 a day to access the hotel's wireless network. Cannot pickup the free AT&T metro wi-fi in a guest room. 
If you want a true LCD/HD flat panel screen TV - this it isn't. Just a standard flat front TV. 
Expensive valet - $25 a day.
Pros:
The staff was very helpful in answering any questions and giving directions and recommendations. 
Property is on the River Walk - on the quieter side - which was nice. 
Centrally located.
Able to get a great mid-week rate online. 
Does have a spa. 
Decent roof top pool & workout room.
Conference area.
Bar, restaurant & gift shop.

title: “Wonderful position”
text: Have just returned from a stay in Boston and the location of this hotel is so good that I wanted to share it with others. It is linked to the two main shopping malls in the city by walkways, there is a Starbucks in the lobby, and it is a short walk to the Newbury Street shops and Back Bay area. The Duck Tours and trolleybuses stop right outside and there is a huge supermarket across the street. The hotel is absolutely ideal if you want to stay right in the centre of things but still have a quiet refuge in the heart of the city. The bathrooms are small but that's the only possible complaint I could have. I would not hesitate to recommend it you cannot go wrong here.

title: “Best Hotel Ever for a Great Price!”
text: The hotel was beautiful. The staff was very kind and helpful. The food was delicious. The parking is good. There was not one reason for us to complain.

title: “Staff goes to limit to help”
text:
The hotel was about like any other downtown hotel, but the staff is over the top. they had no problem solving problems and being kind and thoughtful to everyone. Ask a question and you might get 2 answers not just one.
The hotel is located near the Green Link which takes one on a downtown route for free from 6:30 Am to 6:30 PM, Monday through Friday.

title: “Totally disappointed”
text: My friends and I were beginning a trip from LA to Seattle with San Francisco being the 2nd night. We chose the Parc 55 through Priceline and were excited to get a pretty good deal with naming our own price. We normally stay in 2 or 3 star hotels, and were excited to try a beautiful 4 star hotel! After our flight was delayed, we arrived at the hotel late and checked in, only to walk in to a room that was already occupied, with the occupants in bed! After returning to the front desk, we got a new room but no sincere apology for the mistake and were disappointed once we were settled in. The rooms with two beds are very cramped, the windows were broken and we had to keep the shades drawn the next day because of window washing. The bathrooms have horrible lighting and almost no ventilation. I believe the fee for internet access was around $15, and although they did offer two large bottles of lukewarm Aquafina in the room for $4.50 each, there was no mini-bar or refridgerator. The beds were comfortable, but it was a little gross to find long blond hairs on the bedspread in the morning, considering that everyone in our party is a brunette. Also the fee for parking with tax is $50/night which we thought was pretty steep. All in all, we were disappointed with our stay. The location is OK, but definitely not the reason to stay at this hotel...... as far as the rest of the trip, we stayed at Ramadas and other common hotels where the rooms were clean and spacious, with amenities like free internet, parking and fridges. We ended our stay at the Westin in Seattle for two nights, and I highly recommend it. Try the Westin in San Francisco.....you'll be happy you did!

title: “One of the worst! Avoid!”
text:
As stated above, it's one of the worst hotels. Bed bugs were very true. I don't mind if it's a tiny room but it's dirty! The lift was a bit of a disaster too. One small lift and if the cleaners were cleaning the rooms, you will only have one option which is to use the staircase.
On the other hand, breakfast was good. Not a good night sleep though. Service was average. Free WiFi.

title: “great hotel, not cheap tho”
text:
Me and my missus stayed here for 3 nights in October this year
Here are my comments:
great service, friendly staff
clean hotel, well polished
very comfy beds
quite expensive at over £300 per night
good location right next to a tram stop and chinatown just up the hill
nice gym
shame it has no pool
the breakfast is good but should be at $30 per person
I would definately go back

title: “Good location, close to the beach”
text:
We stayed at Ocean Beach Cottages during September 2008, the cottages are located in a quiet area of Ocean Beach and are about a 4 minute walk to the beach. The cottages themselves are a little bit dated but are clean and have everything you need. It felt like your home away from home.
We had a fantastic time, they have 2 bikes and a BBQ which we took full advantage of. Restaurants, bars are only an 8 minute walk away and the area felt really safe and we were happy to walk around at night.
There are a couple of other bad reviews, I just want to note that these date back to 2005, we didn't experience the same problems.
I would definitely recommend staying at this place and the price it can't be beaten! Go to their website for more info - http://www.theoceanbeachcottages.com/

title: “Super Romantic Hotel”
text:
I recently took my husband to stay for his birthday weekend. We just needed a relaxing place to be together and not worry about anything. Hotel Granduca delivered!! The staff is so attentive and helpful. Its hard to find quality service like this! Anyting we needed was taken care of immediately. Our room was amazing and worth every penny. I can never sleep in a hotel but this was a exception. The beds were so comfortable, everything was spotless and clean. They just do so many things that make this a special place. 
 We got dressed up and had dinner at the hotel. As we walked into the hotel entrance there was live music softly playing. The food was delicious and everything I had hoped for to make his day special. We left rested and more relaxed then we have been in a while. 
 We did not get to go to the pool to relax due to rain. But we will upon our next visit, the cabanas look wonderful as did the food and drinks that were served there.

title: “Satisfied staying”
text: Room is awesome and very clean. Staffs are helpful. Parking is about 28 wiz taxs per day. I recommend if you can, park on street which is free from 6am to 9am. By the way, bus stop is very close to the hotel.

title: “The great Manhattan robbery”
text:
The bedbugs which you find in the meantime in many NYC hotels were the friendliest part of my trip. Never ever have I been cheated like in that hotel. I checked in at 11:30pm and immediately connected to the internet until 1:00am. In this hotel I had to pay for 2 days (always until midnight) after I complained at check-out they removed one day internet only to cheat even harder afterwards. At check-out my room-rate was $282. When I received my credit card account I realized that they changed the room rate to $309. Now they refuse to discuss this with me and I have already instructed a lawyer to act on this.
STAY AWAY FROM THIS HOTEL!!!!!

title: “Girl at front desk..”
text:
As I was checking in thru the kiosk in the ground floor I approach a young lady by the name of Nardory because I was having a difficult time checking in. She was not very friendly and seems that she did not want to be bother with me. I felt that she was very rude and unprofessional and had an attitude problem.
I am a buisness traveller and has stay in this hotel on many occasions. I asked her if she knew what she was doing an she stated that she was in training. I then ask to speak with someone with more knowledge that can assist me, she stated that I would have to wait for a manager.
I was trying to get eye contact with her because i needed help with my reservations and she was ignoring me. If i am going to get this kind of treatment from this young lady i would rather stay some where else.

title: “Large rooms”
text:
So far, we've stayed at the Fairmont, the M Street, the Westin, and this trip, the Melrose. All are four star hotels, all deservedly so. These hotels are located within a block of each other in what priceline calls northwest DC. We like this area as it's close to Georgetown and the mall. There's also plenty of parking on the street at night, if you don't mind running out at 7am to put money in the meter.
 The rooms are large, modern, and comfortable. The wet bar is well stocked and reasonably priced. I can't think of any negatives, or any reason not to stay here. Especially at priceline prices.

title: “Nice hotel; improvements possible”
text: The Curtis has a great atmosphere with friendly staff. I'll list 4 things both good and bad I experienced. 1. Good - Ice machine was on our floor (10); Bad- It made noise when it was making ice, and our room was located near it; if it were enclosed I don't think the noise would be an issue. 2. Good- towels smelled clean, nice selection of soaps and shampoo's in the bathrooms, linens smelled fresh, flat screen tv was nice; Bad- I could hear the people taking a shower in the next room and I could hear people talking and walking past our room late at night, some cheap sealing around the door and blocking of air vents in the bathrooms would solve this. 3. Good- The breakfast was a buffet, good selection, freshly made; Bad- We didn't get any because we purchased our rooms through priceline ($60). 4.Good- Decor was nice, weight room looked good and was accessible 24hrs; Bad- I called twice to get more towels; waited 1/2 hour, finally went in person to the front desk to ask for more; they were delivered within 5 minutes afterward.

title: “THE place to stay.....look no more.”
text: We stayed at this hotel 03/04/12 thru 03/07/12. We actually loved the location. Right down the street from Times Square. We went out to Times Square every night. The staff went above and beyond to make us feel at home. There was hot apple cider waiting every day when we got back from our outings. The room was larger then expected for NY and extremely clean. The only thing was there was not a mini fridge in the room unless requested. I really don’t see any reason to look any further for a room. We plan to return to NY in a year or so and plan to stay at this very hotel when we do. One very important thing was that they held our luggage the day we were to leave so we could site see without lugging around our stuff because our flight time was late departure. Now that is service if you ask me.

title: “Great Location - Nice Hotel”
text: The hotel is super convenient to any kind of shopping and restaurants that you could want. It's also close to the main expressways. The rooms are typical HGI. The first room smelled like dirty socks and even after they sprayed, I couldn't stay there. They moved me with no problem. I did have a problem with the refrigerator temperature, but maintenance responded immediately. The HVAC was quiet, which isn't typical for many hotels, but the room got stuffy when it was off. The staff was friendly and helpful. An indoor pool opens at 5AM. The fitness center is open 24 hours. The 2 treadmills have built in TVs in addition to a wall mounted TV. An eliptical, free weights, a weight machine and kettle balls are available, along with a balance ball and doctors scales. Headsets are available at the front desk. Room service is available 5-9 PM. The USA Today is available in the lobby, but not delivered to the room, even for Hilton Honors members. I would stay again.

title: “Residence Inn disappoints”
text:
Let me preface this review by saying that I am a loyal Marriott patron, having stayed in Marriott properties throughout the US. I have stayed in several Marriott properties in the Charlotte area, but because this hotel was conveniently located to the workshop I was attending I decided to stay at the Residence Inn rather than a full service property. I must say that my stay here was quite disappointing for a number of reasons. Upon check in the desk clerk was no where to be seen. Granted it was late, around 8 pm, it it seemed he was more interested in watching the news on tv rather than being attentive to greeting arriving guests. The room itself was slightly smaller than the typical Residence Inn suite and had a rather "worn" feel to it. It had the typical appointments one would expect to find in a Residence Inn suite. One couch, lounge chair, a very small coffee table, desk, chair, and in the bedroom queen size bed and two side tables. There were two flat screen tv's, one in the sitting area and one in the bedroom.The kitchen 
was also typical; however, a dishwasher was not secured in place (bolted down) and moved 
every time I tried to open it. The rug was stained in several places and there were crumbs left from a previous guest on the carpeting. The most disgusting thing was mildew growing in the bathtub grout. Although I reported this on the first day, it was not addressed by the management or housekeeping. I returned from my appointment late in the evening to find it untouched. I called to the front desk to complain, and housekeeping (without advising me) arrived about twenty minutes later to spray down the mildew with clorox. By this time I was trying to eat dinner and did not want to deal with the fumes as I wanted to relax and not be bothered. Perhaps this problem will be addressed after I check out, but as for my stay I showered in a tub that was not up to the standards of cleanliness that are typical of a Marriott. For what I paid for the room it should have been sparkling. I was offered no consideration for this problem. So to sum up, cleanliness of this particular property is not up to Marriott standards, rooms are beginning to have a worn look and need updating, service at check in could be improved, and rooms are overpriced for what you get. Will I stay here again? Nope. There are other properties in the Charlotte area that are less expensive, cleaner, and better managed.

title: “We'll be back!”
text: This was a wonderful home base for exploring the city, with a very convenient location to Times Square, upper east side, Chelsea, and 4 blocks from Grand Central and the subway. Three of us shared a room with a queen bed and a hide-a-bed couch. The room was dated, but very clean and comfortable. It was large and had a great little kitchen. There is a grocery store 2 blocks away, an all night drug store 1 block, and lots of good restaurants close by. Quite a bargain, we prepaid.

title: “Great place! Construction noise wasn't bad”
text:
I stayed here on August 21-23rd 2010. My wife had to fly out of JFK and I was not trying to drive back & forth to MA in such a short timeframe.
I read reviews & people complain about the noise from WTC construction, but honestly: find another hotel or at least look at maps so you know that you WILL be right across the street from it all.
I was on the 19th floor and could barely hear anything. Just the noise from the TV or AC made it disappear. Now I bet that the 2nd floor would probably suck, but call the hotel 1st to see what floor you might get. It was extremely clean, nice 42" tv in the wall and super comfy king size bed with lots of down pillows. It was worth my $172 per night on Hotwire.

title: “Great Value and Hotel”
text: We stayed here when we were in town to play a golf tournament at Brickyard Crossing. We got a great rate. The hotel is new and modern. The rooms are large with flat screen TVs. Excellent breakfast which is included in the price of the room. Plus a wonderful staff. It was also super quick to drive up to the Brickyard.

title: “Nice,cute hotel”
text:
We stayed at The Hotel Carlton for 6days. It's a little out of the way (about 6 blocks to main downtown), but we enjoyed our stay. The staff are very friendly and accomodating. The first thing they did at our greeting was open a san francisco map and go over the 'good' and 'bad' areas nearby. They were always willing to suggest sites to see or restaurants to dine at. The hotel has afternoon wine tastings in the lobby every day. We went a couple times and really had a good time. You definitely have to check it out.
 The rooms are clean and on the small side. We had a standard queen room. The walls are very thin, which we noticed one night after our neighbors kept us up speaking loudly. Otherwise, we liked the room. Overall, I would recommend this hotel. The price was great and location was pretty good.

title: “US Open 2012”
text:
This was a very special trip for us to the USA OPEN GOLF tournamentJune 10th-17th 2012.The hotel was a good location, excellent service from all staff, concierge were very helpfull assisting us with travel advice to and from the Opympic club .Rooms comfortable, breakfast very good. I would highly recommend this hotel to family and friends.Thank you all.
Michael, Mgt furlong, Kilkenny, Ireland.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text: Just got back from a girls long weekend in NYC. This hotel was great. The rooms are huge by NYC standards. We had a suite (2 Queens and a pullout sofa) with 2 bathrooms! Perfect when sharing with two others. The staff was wonderful, and the attached resturant/bar was fun. Location is great. It is in a quiet neighborhood and a short 4-5 blocks from the subway/grand central. Would highly recommed this hotel.

title: “Front desk staff unacceptable, hotel stay made up for it”
text: My husband and I arrived to the hotel at 730pm to find out our reservation had been cancelled. They cancelled stating I had an invalid credit card, which in fact the situation was the card expired and had been reactivated with the new expiration. This was after I called the hotel the week of our stay to assure confirmation was made. The front desk starff was extremely rude, did not apologize, stated they had tried to call me to notify me but said they had gotten an invalid phone number which was my phone number. Noone had tried to call. The man continued to help other customers, did not call his manager when we asked, and offered us a rate that was 70 dollars higher then was quoted originally. Completely unprofessional staff. The cleaning staff, breakfast, room, and location were all ideal!

title: “A brief stay before a flight”
text: The front desk man started our enjoyable stay with efficiency and humor. The rooms were spacious and immaculate and the shuttle service to and from the airport was excellent. All in all this was a great way to stay and fly!

title: “Great service”
text: A special thanks to Kurt for responding to concerns of my wife. Great hotel, personel, service and location.

title: “Great Price--Free Parking!”
text: Stayed here Dec 29 - 31 on a spur of the moment trip to Chicago and had a wonderful time. Saw a deal on TravelZoo for $99 per night with free parking and in/out privileges ($40 a day) and I highly recommend staying here. The deal continues through the end of Feb. Read other reviews about the construction and lobby and all of that but we were not bothered by it one bit. The staff were friendly and the bottled water and snacks in the lobby were a nice touch. I would highly recommend this hotel, especially to take advantage of the $99 deal.

title: “Awesome Hotel, I Loved It”
text: This was a great hotel. I went there with a couple of my friends and it was great. The staff were nice and there was great beds. The restaraunt was awesome, the rooms were clean and the room service was great. I recamend this hotel to all travelers who stop in Memphis and I hope you enjoy your trip!

title: “Seriously?????”
text:
I made a booking more than two months in advance for a single room with a queen sized bed and I end up in a double room for handicaps with a dirty wall with closed windows and no view? I have been a very loyal customer of W hotel and I am devastated with this reception. I'm writing this review from the hotel room at this moment and I am furious about this!
Never again!

title: “Three STARS my Big Fat Aunt Fanny!”
text: Please do NOT be fooled by this hotels claim to 3 stars. For less than half the price of a stay in this hotel you can stay ANYWHERE else and get better value. DO NOT BE FOOLED BY THE PICTURES ON THEIR WEBSITE!!! The hotel "claims" to be newly renovated.....WHERE! My family had a HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE! We took our own pictures. Our reservation was WRONG even after TWO phone calls and an email to verify. Our first room was hot and the smell of mildew ws over powering. The second room was FREEZING! Two double (hard) beds (mobile home size) the pillows were stuffed with hard cotton. The wallpaper was peeling, the ceiling crumbling in spots. The carpet was stained and coming up. The bathroom drains were VERY SLOW. The decor sparse and drab. Towels were thin and scratchy. The elevators were scarey and dirty. The hotel in general stunk of garlic and mildew. The cold water was hot and the hot water SCALDING! Doors slammed all night and you could hear every sound in the adjoining rooms. Phone calls from other guests at ALL HOURS. Loud staff in the hallways (who did not speak English) Our linen was stained (yellow spots). The hotel was overrun with drunks. We had dirty glassware. I never saw a doorman or concierge. Internet service was an ADDITIONAL $10.99 in your room or if you felt like standing in line for hours, FREE IN THE LOBBY. The restaurant was only open for "breakfast" from 6:30 to 9:30 am. No refrigerator or microwave in the room. There was a coffee maker for your DECAF coffee. Parking is $10 for EACH TIME YOU EXIT. Self serve snack bar offers convenience store sandwiches at $7.00 each and bottled soda for $2.00 each. Canned sodas are $1.00 each but only available on the 10th and 14th floor as is the ice maker. The outdor pool was over crowded and undersized. The view from our window was of a littered roof complete with a large garbage can. The ONLY UPSIDE to our stay was the parking attendent, Lisa, who went out of her way to be friendly and helpful. I retired from the military after 30+ years and am currently a minister. In my 63 years I have NEVER HAD A WORSE HOTEL EXPERIENCE. There should be a minus sign in front of their 3 star rating. After all of this, they had the nerve to offer a "promotion" allowing a LATE CHECKOUT of 5 HOURS for an ADDITIONAL $50.00! They should be ASHAMED of themselves! Check out OUR PICTURES!

title: “Great room, breakfast, and service”
text: Had a great stay with very comfortable accomedations. We had a conference which was hosted by the Marriott and the LaQuinta offered a more economic choice. My wife and I enjoyed our stay. The staff seemed to go out of their way to make the breakfast excellent, well stocked and lots of selection. In fact, my parents stayed in another room, my brother and his wife stayed in another room and my sister and her husband and daughter stayed in another room. We all enjoyed our stays immensely.

title: “Truly a dive, and I don't mean the pool area”
text: The neighborhood wasn't very good, and didn't seem real safe. It is literally on the corner of a street also known as a highway, and traffic noise was loud. Our room had a sliding door in it out to the balcony (we were on the 3rd floor). The balcony was only about 2-3 feet wide, and overlooked the traffic and the roof below. This sliding door was broken and I couldn't lock it. We didn't want to leave any doors unlocked in that neighborhood. It must have been broken for awhile, because there was a wooden dowel in the slider to keep it closed. I expect more than a 39 cent wooden stick to secure the place for what I paid for that room. It was over $100 for that night even after they made an adjustment for the broken door and noise inconvenience. The roof below is open at night so people can go out there and smoke/party/whatever. Some girls were giggling and screaming most of the night. The elevator was broken and out of order. The room was depressing looking, as was the whole place. The breakfast in the morning was boring and tasteless. I could have gotten a better one at the local 7-11. On the bright side, at least now I know where NOT to stay when I go back.

title: “One of my favorite places to stay...”
text: Couldn't have been a better visit. The staff - especially John S. and Katie - were friendly and courteous. Looking forward to coming back with my family.

title: “Great for sports teams coming into town”
text: I am so pleased we chose this location. the staff from the planning phase all the way through our stay was some of the best I have ever incountered. I traveled with my son's baseball team and the hotel was nice enough to print directions and key information about the tournament for all the parents. They also gave our group free breakfast and a discounted rate for booking as a group. During our time, the staff was efficient, so kind and did whaterver it took to exceed our expectations. Top notch location. They even gave us a free van ride to Easton towne center

title: “Above Expectations”
text: We just spent a long weekend in San Antonio and stayed at the Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk. At the time we booked this getaway, we didn't think of San Antonio as a spring break destination. We were surprised to see how many families vacationed here at this time of year. The hotel was hopping, and I can understand why a family would choose this hotel. The complimentary breakfast and afternoon "kick back" small meal and happy hour are real value added benefits. Our room was in the new tour; it was spacious and well appointed. Staff was pleasant and helpful. We certainly would go back and recommend it to family and friends. Also, the location was central to many downtown tourist areas and easily accessed by freeway.

title: “Lovely Stay”
text:
I have to admit I was a bit nervous booking this hotel after reading some of the reviews.
We had a queen suite in the same building as the check in. We were able to check in and be up to our room that was facing the pool in about 10 minutes.
The room was more than I expected. Everything was very clean and the air conditioning worked perfectly which was great because I think it was around 103 degrees F. The beds were very comfortable with lots of big pillows.
We ate at all the restaurants on site and enjoyed all of them. We really liked the ambiance at the Hole in the Wall it was quite fun and the food was quite good. We really enjoyed Rico's though, we ate at the restaurant one night and ordered room service from them one night and both dinners were very good.
The staff is very helpful and extremely cordial. The concierge was exceptional and very knowledgeable both times we used them.
Out only complaint and it is minor was the hours of the lazy river. It was only open from 10-6pm which we didn't fee; was long enough. We also felt that the drink service at the lazy river was quite slow.
I did go to the spa and have a treatment and it was very good. The staff really accomodated me to fit me in at the last minute which was wonderful.
We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and would absolutely stay there again with no hesitations.

title: “Strictly Business”
text: My business meeting was downtown and the location was perfect. This is a very large facility, the parking is very expensive and not so sure about anything other than the room was comfortable, clean and updated.

title: “Neat boutique hotel, great service, would return again”
text:
I stayed here for 3 night in October 2010. I almost changed my reservation to the Elan, which has one of the highest TA ratings I've ever seen for a 3 star hotel, but decided to stick with my first choice. 
Nice quiet room with a comfortable bed, great location close to restaurants. Walking distance to the Grove.
The bathroom was spotless, and I loved that the hotel provided Bulgari soaps and moisturizers. Plush, quality towels, too.
I opted for the breakfast included package. While the breakfast is limited, with just 4 hot options and a few cold, continental items on the buffet, the spinach, zucchini, cherry tomato and mushroom frittata was delicious, and l liked the banana bread. The servers in the restaurant were outgoing, and made this single traveller feel welcome each morning. If I return to the Orlando, I would probably get the regular room rate in the future, and order breakfast separately. 
The front desk was very helpful. No complaints.
The atmosphere is low-key, and geared more towards travellers than tourists. No grand lobby, but there is small lobby/library near the elevators with a tv, and internet terminal. This isn't a place for someone who is looking to be pampered or coddled. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.

title: “More from the Moorpark”
text: We had a wonderful experience at the Moorpark. Service was great, the room was quiet and clean, breakfast was yummy and the pool area was nice. Very conveniently located, not only to the freeway and restaurants, but also to the Mountain Winery which we were going to for a concert. The highlight of our experience: on the way through the lobby the front desk gal heard my husband whistling the tune that was on the sound system. She said, "Do you like this song too?" My husband said, "Yeah, do you know who it is?" She didn't, but promised to find out for us by our return. When we returned back to the room later that day, there was a gift bag with the whole CD inside and a note thanking us for staying! We are no VIP quests, so this was a big surprise. Would definately stay again.

title: “Clean and Okay location but very cramped and noisy”
text: The GEM was clean and a 10 minute walk from Times Square - but the room I had (104) was very cramped (had a hard time even sitting in the desk), and it was located next to both the front desk and the stairs, I could hear customers, phones ringing and the heavy door to the stairs slamming throughout the stay. It was cheap, and clean but I'd rather stay somewhere else next time I'm in Manhattan

title: “Nothing to brag about”
text: This hotel is less than average. The hotel room furniture is outdated. The main draw back is the wifi. It does not work. In this day in age, that is a must for travelers. Two nights was more than enough

title: “Best price in Boston for a 3-star”
text:
I stayed on a Friday in June with a hotel full of other Red Sox fans; fun! Note, however, that the hotel is NOT within walking distance to Fenway Park unless you're up for a two-mile walk; cabs are plentiful, or the subway is very convenient to both the hotel and the ballpark. There are other hotels much more convenient to Fenway, but the price is insane, $300 a night and up. Book on the Holiday Inn website for good prices, detailed description of the options, and Priority Club points. When I checked in, I got a surprise upgrade to the executive floor as a Priority Club member! Very nice room. Spacious and very clean.
This hotel was safe, clean, and quiet; as noted, most guests this date were families in town for a Red Sox game. (Looks like it's mostly a business hotel during the week; Mass Gen Hospital is right next door.) Jimmy at the front desk is great. The hotel is in a city neighborhood, but not a bad neighborhood. Plenty of amenities within a block; Starbucks of course, CVS (drugstore), Whole Foods Market, White Hen Pantry (like a 7-11) I went to Pizzetta Pizzeria right across the street that had great pizza and calzones for a post-game snack. It was full of locals, always a good sign. The sign said it was open until 3 a.m. on weekends! Hotel does have an outdoor pool, which I didn't check out but looked good through the window.
Great location convenient to most of what Boston has to offer, clean and well-run, and cheaper than the comparable chains. Only warning: stay away from the hotel restaurant. Breakfast from the buffet was so cold that it was inedible.

title: “Great service and room!”
text: We arrived at the Westin st. Francis on August 1st mid afternoon and it took us 2 minutes to check in. We had a traditional room overlooking Union Square. The room was very large and clean and the view was great! The service was fantastic and we recieved complimentary champagne and strawberries from a guy at the front desk (Ray) on the night of our wedding. Would definately recommend this hotel!

title: “Wonderful hotel”
text: My sister and I stayed at this hotel the first week of August 2010. It was wonderful!! The staff really takes customer service to the highest level. Everyone greeted us with warmth and made us feel welcome. We had a room with 2 beds with a HUGE walk in closet! Our room faced out onto Powell St which is noisy, but didn't bother us as we were so exhausted at night that we could have slept through anything. And that's what ear plugs are for!!! All in all we couldn't have asked for a better place to stay and would stay again in the future.

title: “"Tiny Room"”
text: Thought this was going to be so luxurious for close to $200 a room; but the room was the size of a shoe box and the bathroom the size of a cracker jack box! Only one set of towels,no bathrobes(luckily I always bring my own). Went to look out the window at the non view we had and the windows were absolutely filthy,And parking was $55! Wow no bang for my buck there.

title: “Very Convenient”
text:
We were in Chelsea Lodge last january 2005 and we had a great experience. We would definitely book again but we will try to chose a second or third floor room, with views to the street.
 Good points: convenient and cute location (next to everything, lovely street), atmosphere (helpful receptionists, quiet, lovely decoration, cosy, very clean). I do agree with all the positive reviews. But...
 Not so good points: small-tiny rooms (not suitable for long stays or large baggage), not so good restoration (although the building has been restored, your bed might be affected by some the floors which are not horizontal, its just a detail, but very annoying one. We tried two rooms and both had the same situation), very noisy heating (ONLY in lowfloor room, but we were changed into another one), no elevator (but if you stay in bottomfloor room you might get the noise from the people comming up and down the stairs).

title: “Will be returning here”
text: Great Value. I have stayed at 3 & 4 star hotels that weren't as good as this one. I was impressed. Fresh fruit on breakfast line is a added plus.

title: “Above the Crowd”
text:
A second blizzard in two weeks having Denver squarely in its sights, and not wanting to miss more work, I started searching for a downtown hotel to hunker down in. I live in Boulder, but work in downtown Denver. I was NOT going to be stuck at home 2 weeks in a row. So I started surfing the web for downtown hotels.
There were more "tony” (and expensive) hotels closer to my office, but the reviews of the Hyatt at the Convention Center on Trip Advisor-- and the more reasonable rates -- sold me; sight unseen.
Now that I have seen and experienced the Hyatt, I am pleased to recommend this as a great hotel. Let's define "great": if you want a boutique hotel, a micro hotel, or if you believe there IS status in overpaying, skip the Hyatt; it's not for you. But if you want a clean, modern, comfortable and efficient hotel that really knows how to take care of its business guests for a reasonable price, this hotel is for you.
The Hyatt is huge. Located one block off the 16th Street Mall and adjacent to the Colorado Convention Center, to literally towers over the competition. The view towards LoDo from the 27th floor bar, with the blizzard swirling outside brought back memories of the long gone (and much shorter) Top of the Rockies restaurant in the now razed Security Life Building.
The Hyatt towers above its competition in every other way for a business traveler, too. It has a 24/7 health club with lots of top equipment and weights in great condition, all maintained by a friendly and helpful staff. The view from the striders and treadmills is of the convention center. The Denver light rail, operating through the snow, and the giant snow-covered blue bear peeping in the convention center, made it look like someone had laid out a train set and a large scale model village model under someone's Christmas tree. This is hotel that understands its customers want to work out in a nice club and that the basement is not the place to put it.
The rooms are designed for business travelers. Attractive and functional. Not Spartan, but not overwrought. WiFi, flat screen TVs, a wheel-out work table AND a working counter-desk, ergonomic chairs, ample and well-positioned electrical outlets for chargers. I'm going to enjoy recommending this Hyatt to my out of town clients.
In addition to the friendly bars, the restaurant breakfast brunch is good, filling and very reasonably priced.
And location? Don't be fooled by the name. This Hyatt is not just for convention goers. As I sipped fine top-shelf beverages from the 27th floor bar enjoying the Denver lights below, I could see the Denver Center for Performing Arts 2 blocks away. All of downtown Denver is accessible from the free 16th Mall shuttles 1 block away. Denver Pavilions, a shopping and entertainment complex with a 16-plex movie theatre is one block away.
But a hotel is only as good as its staff. The Hyatt’s is friendly and helpful. When I called down to see if I could book an extra night, they had it done in less time than it took to type one-half of this sentence; so fast I went down to make sure I understood them correctly! And when the blizzard moved out and sun came out and I wanted to go home, they waived the cancellation fee without hesitation. And when the room was not made up because their cleaning staff was stranded at home, they "comped" breakfast and apologized profusely (and unnecessarily). The Hyatt couldn't help being short-handed in a blizzard, but knew how to treat it's guest. That's what sealed the deal for me.
Denver has lots of very nice (and very expensive) boutique hotels. But don't confuse "large" with "institutional" at the Hyatt. These folks run a tight ship with a great crew. For the business traveler, you will not be disappointed.

title: “loved it. Definitely will go back”
text: Close to everything, and actually can walk out to the riverside walk.

title: “They make you feel at home!”
text:
I've stayed at the Hotel Blake for three weeks. The staff, from the Bellman to housekeeping are always friendly and helpful. Once, I thought I left an item and called the front desk. Ian was very attentive and after checking all sources could not find the item. I felt like a fool when I found the item at home and called Ian to thank him. 
The location of the Hotel is walking distance to everything downtown. I HIGHLY recommend this hotel as the room is very clean and neat, but the service is TREMENDOUS!

title: “close to universal studios”
text:
The main thing that left me disappointed with my stay here was the unfriendly staff at the front desk. Most of them barely even looked at us when we would enter the lobby, and it always seemed like we were inconveniencing them by asking a question. On the positives, the girl at the gift shop was extremely helpful. The free shuttle bus to the metro and universal studios was convenient and ran frequently, however needs to be bigger in size for the return trips at the end of the day as it always seemed overloaded with people standing or being told to wait for the next bus (the drivers were friendly). Although this hotel is situated further out, the metro was an easy ride and with the free shuttle to/from the station this was an ideal mode of transport for us without a car.
We also enjoyed use of the heated pool and spa in a lovely well-maintained area. We ate breakfast at Tula's cafe which is convenient and reasonable priced. There is decent internet access for those without their own, with 2 computers which we found readily available. The room was quiet, beds were big and comfy and bathroom clean.

title: “What a deal”
text: This hotel is perfectly situated and is the bargain of the century. For about $100 you stay on 46th St close to Times Square, free contintental breakfast and a clean room with pleasant staff. What more could you ask for? If you're looking for luxury this is not the place. If you want comfortable accomodations at a reasonable price it is the place for you.

title: “I have been to a Waldorf Collection Hotel, and you, Mr. Arizona Biltmore, are no Waldorf Collection Hotel...”
text: I stayed on a Monday for 1-night and was excited to stay in the newly renovated Ocatilla Wing of the Arizona Biltmore. Over-rated!.....Over-rated! I paid over $300 a night and the only room they had left for poor, little old me was a handicap accessible, room with two queen sized. No problem, I guess. Am I one of the 47%ers? I got into the room just before kickoff of the Monday Night Football game and the TV didn't work. No problem, I had 10 minutes before kickoff...that should be plenty of time for Engineering to get to the room and fix the TV. 60 minutes and 3 phone calls to the Instant Service desk later...they arrived. They were both very nice and fixed it in a jiffy...but the point is that there is a gap between the brand expectation of a Waldorf Collection Hotel and what the Arizona Biltmore now represents. It feels more like an old Sheraton at a Luxury price point. Beware AMEX Fine Hotels of the World agents, your clients won't like this dinosaur.

title: “Very comfortable hotel and location”
text: We recently stayed at the Churchill Hotel for our first trip to DC in years. The hotel was very clean, acomodating, and in a great location. We got a great deal on the internet for a weekend stay. Walking distance to great restaurants, Georgetown, and metro. Valet parking at reasonable rate. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great location, needs updating”
text: I was in Denver for a conference and loved the location of this hotel. There are two sides to the Sheraton, the towers (old side) and the new side. My room was in the towers and had a great view of the capital but smelled of mold. When checking in the new side is nice but when you get to the older side you smell that moldy smell in the hallways, the conference rooms, and my room. I was on the 19th floor and it was apparent in the hallway to my room. Room 1933 has a great view of the capital. During my stay I wanted to go back to my room to lay down at 4:00 in the afternoon but the maid hadn't been there yet and I could not lay down knowing that she would be there shortly. This hotel sits right on Market Street which is about 8 blocks of stores restaurants and bars. Free buses run up and down the street but it was great walking around. I love the location.

title: “Good location”
text:
Sheraton is great as it is right on 16th Street Mall and the trolley stops in front. Connected to Peet's and Yardhouse & Starbucks across the street lets you get that morning and evening fix. Hop the trolley to transfer to bus/public transportation to connect to most tourist sights throughout Denver.
Rooms are spacious. Housekeeping is nice as they do a good job and not intrusive about coming early in the morning.
Pool is located on 5th floor so it can get a bit windy and chilly up there. Internet is alright - requires log-on every time you power up the computer as compared to other hotels.

title: “great location - threadbare rooms - grand dame is ready for an overahaul”
text: The Waldorf is ideally located - easy access to everything. The staff is incredibly helpful (great concierge!) - but the room we had was pitiful, way overdue for an update. Paper thin walls - with a neighbor who slammed the door at least a dozen times a night between midnight and 2am - the lingering smell of smoke (nasty!) - no glazing on the windows so even on the 19th floor you felt like you were in the midst of mid-town traffic. All the more annoying since I had called the hotel and specifically requested a renovated room (to avoid all of the above). Management was not particularly helpful when I pointed out on my confirmation that I had made the request, their answer was to give my daughter a stuffed bear. A lovely gesture - but a quieter room without the acrid smell of smoke would have been better. My husband is a fan of the Peninsula - I fully understand why. If you want a reasonably priced room and are willing to take your chances with a room which may (or may not!!) be renovated then the Waldorf is just fine. But in a city with so many great hotels - I'd try elsewhere the next time.

title: “Cute hotel. Great location.”
text: Staff was great. Molly was very friendly and helpful in particular. The hotel is close to many good restaurants and attractions in Union Square. It's also close to the muni and BART lines, making a car a non-necessity. Although it didn't bother me, the rooms are rather small and lack much of a view, but they are cozy, clean, and nicely decorated.

title: “Visiting The Historic City”
text: The hotel is a great location to all the historic sites the city has to ofter. Great location!!

title: “Best anniversary at the Mandarin Oriental”
text: From the moment we got there we were welcomed and treated to exceptional service. Everyone knew we were celebrating our anniversary. From the front desk (they upgraded our room to a suite), the spa (we were served a happy anniversary treat after our relaxing massage), to room service, and the restaurant staff at Asana. Everyone wished us a happy anniversary and provided exceptional service. Just to give one small example, when I asked for a late check out the night before they were only able to commit to an additional hour which was about all I hoped for (busy time for them). Next morning after we had breakfast delivered to our room, the same front desk staff called to let me know they extended our late check out to 3pm. All without me asking. It is not only the big things but the little things that make your stay at a luxury hotel well worth the money. We will definitely return again.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: My husband and I recently stayed at this Holiday Inn Express for 7 nights. We loved it. We do not have anything negative to say. The staff was very helpful and friendly. My room was very clean. The bed was comfortable. The free internet is a plus!! The buffet style breakfast is good. I could eat the cinnamon rolls every day! They are great. If you are looking for a good place to stay while in NYC, in my opinion, this is it!

title: “get the right room!”
text: The rooms here were ok comfortable enough but nothing special! the bathroom was small and needed a revamp, but the worst thing was that our room was on the ground floor and over looked the bus station the noise was awful!! ask for a quiet room on a high floor. We would rather have stayed up towards Union square as we felt the wharf area was a bit tacky.the city is fantastic and we will return but would not stay at the sheraton.

title: “Best weekend ever”
text: I had been to Philly only two times before. Once while in middle school and again to take my kids to the X games. This past weekend I stayed in town from Friday till Monday. It was the best weekend I have ever had. The locals were extremely friendly. From the parking lot attendant to the ladies at the frontdesk to bumpy the bartender. Friday I had my nails done at "Colors" near market and 2nd. sorry i don't remember exact location. Saturday, Bumpy sent me to Ralph's for dinner. It was amazing. Brian the shuttle driver was wonderful. My room had a beautiful view of the bridge and across the river I could see fireworks on friday evening. I would recommend this hotel to anyone! It is close to everything and is one of the only hotels in the area that has a free shuttle.

title: “Calfornia Adventure”
text: Depending on your reason to visit LA the Sofitel is a great location. Beverley Centre with Macy's right across the road. Hop on Hop bus stop also across the road - good value as you get to stop and wander at various tourist spots. Great cafes next block in 3rd Street. Check out desserts at Magnolia Bakery in 3rd Street and also Joan's on 3rd for a hearty breakfast etc with the LA set. The Grove and Farmers Market easy stroll from hotel.Service was freindly and mostly helpful but bar service needs a shake up. Although a little pricey would definately recommend and would consider staying there again on next visit to LA.

title: “Best Deal! Great breakfast! Friendly Staff!”
text: Stumbled across this diamond while searching online for great deals. Huge rooms, lots of cool amenities. All the things I need in a hotel - microwave, fridge, free internet, free breakfast, pool & fitness center. I would love to stay here again when I'm back in San Jose!

title: “Great Stay”
text: Quick Check-in & Check-out; nice workout room; ample breakfast; USA TODAY free; free high speed internet; clean room; good bed; friendly service people; all-in-all - very good place to stay!

title: “This was the worst and most expensive hotel stay in memory.”
text: San Diego in July. Crowded, crowded, foggy and cold. We booked a room for our last night in town as we had a 6:30 a.m. flight. We asked for an early check-in. Got there at 12:15 and were not allowed in our room until 4:20 p.m. The front desk staff was rude. The room was incredibly expensive and our card was charged $50 more than we were quoted over the phone. All in all, our stay there cost $400 (after I complained and got the $50 taken off our bill) for 16 hours of time, only 12 hours of which were in the room. Oh yeah and they flunked wake up call too. Fortunately we woke ourselves up and made the plane. Total rip off!!!

title: “good hotel”
text: a good old fashioned hotel, very close to central park and the theatre district, the only down side is that there is not tea/coffee making facilities. the room was small but clean and a daily cleaning service, soap, shampoo etc is provided, the soap is changed every day.

title: “overnight stay”
text:
From the moment I called for reservations, I was greeted by the friendly voice of
Toni at the reservation desk. Unpon arriving, I was greeted again, by Toni.
The room was one of the most cleanest " I have seen in awhile.
The entire staff was helpful and friendly, breakfast was wondeful.
KUDOS TO YOU AND THE STAFF. WE WILL SEE YOU IN OCTOBER.
 Roberta and George Van Pelt

title: “I've had better ive had worse.”
text:
Few things. With what we paid for a "suite" I would expect a mini fridge or a microwave. 
Our air conditioning was broken. Our tub had no way to stop the water so you could take a bath. The operator sent up maintenance and honestly that sweet man is responsible for most of the stars on the review. I hope they appreciate what an awesome find they have. I can't remember his name but he only has sons and was very sweet to our little girls. The issues were fixed fast and we were able to enjoy our stay. The lady in the gift shop was also a sweetheart 
I wish the pull out sofa had more blankets and our room ran out of tp. Service was excellent overall. Would have preferred more food choices.

title: “Superb location and staff; moldy rooms”
text: I enjoyed everything about this hotel except that the room reeked of mold. I would have thought it was an isolated incident until I read that many guests have experienced the same thing. That tells me the hotel knows of the problem and isn't fixing it. They stick unknowing guests in these rooms and hope they don't complain.

title: “Not Sure I would Go Back.........”
text: Just returned from a three night stay and I am on the fence about returning. We arrived at a busy time in the evening and my car was handled efficently and quickly with a nice greeting form the doorman. Check in went well and front desk clerk was nice and accomodating. The bellman that took us up to the room was more like a character from the Flatbush, with a put on accent from New York that I think he thought my 19 year old daughter was impressed with. He stared at her to the point of making us both uncomfortable. He did not offer up to much information about the room, just that the ice was down the hall. I handed him $5.00 for two bags and he seemed disappointed. We went up to the club floor and it was ok, not great just ok. Our room smelled like the people before us had been in there for a week without opening the door. There is no window to open, so it was smelly. The bathroom was nice and remodeled with granite and wood. Here is the STICKLER. The sheets were terrible and the mattress pad was stained with blood. The sheets were so thin, it was revolting to look at. The sheets also did not fit the beds?? What is that all about! I called and specifically asked for the sheets and matress pads to be changed, it never happened. Our one and only club chair in the room was stained and dirty, I put a towel over it when I sat down in my pajamas. We were on a club floor and for the price, around $360.00 per night, I would have to say it is overpriced and needs some help with the decor. The lobby is nice, but the hallways have huge floral print rugs and yellow walls. Maybe they are not finished? Anyway it's overpriced and the club lounge should offer computer access, at least to print off boarding passes. The attendant in the lounge seemed over worked and a bit harried. we had brunch in the restaurant downstairs and our waitress was pleasant and informative. Tthere were only two parties in the restaurant, but it still smelled like last nights tequilla shots. The lobby has a sitting area off to the side with a big screen TV and is well decorated. Overall the hotel is OK, just seemed overpriced for what it was. They seemed to be trying to hard to be groovy and hip, but seemed to miss some of the key things........

title: “Ok Ritz Carlton - but beware the external central a/C vent”
text: Pretty mundane hotel with too informal front lobby staff, laughing and joking around. Got no sleep as my room looked out over a grassed terrace which had air con ducts pointing sky wards. No need to stay anywhere other than Boston Harbor Hotel in this city.

title: “Most amazing day's of my life!”
text:
My husband and I had our reception and wedding partying staying at the Carlyle. We were welcomed with open arms and hearts. We had the most amazing wedding and reception!
We can not express our thanks to everyone! Thank you Joanne Sipe and the whole team at Carlyle Suites.
We would definitely suggest anyone couple gay or straight to stay at this beautiful setting nestled in the heart of Washington, D.C.

title: “30 In Manhatten”
text:
Booked the Room Mate Grace hotel for my 30th Birthday for one week having looked on trip adviser for the hotel i was really please when i finally arrived with my husband.
The flights was with British Airways and were comfortable and onece at the other end we paid 12 dollas each to get on the bus which takes you to your nearest point near your hotel, ours was about a ten minute walk away from the hotel which was fine.
We managed to find Room mate Grace down a side turning which was a ten minute walk from time square which was amazing.
Such a fantastic city alot like London and easy to find places due to the block system.
Arrived at the hotel and as soon as you walk in the staff are friendly and welcoming and were so helpful.
The hotel was very clean and looked very smart considering it was a threee star i have stayed in five stars that were not up to this standards.
once in our room i was surprised that i could not hear that much noise as we were facing the front of the road. the bed was so comfortable one of the best i have ever slept in and lovely fluffy pillow which is what you want when you do a walking tour.
The bedroom was small but there was enough space for me and my husband and it was cosy and very clean. the shower was always hot and very smart.
We had a petite room which over looked the main road at the front and even though we were next to a pub we herd the music once but nothing that ear plugs didnt keep out.
we had booked to have breakfast in the hotel and it was a continental breakfast which was all fresh and plenty of food , the seating area was comfortable and clean and again the staff in the restaurant were so friendly and helpful, never had to wait to get a seat and it over looked the pool area which was amazing and a plus for a NYC hotel.
I really cant recommend this hotel enough it was for me an amazing holiday in NYC and enjoyed and loved every part of it.
The room had an ipod dock which was also an alarm which came in handy in your room, the hotel also had internet acess in the lobby.
I visited many attractions while here and managed to do a list of things while in the Big Apple. i would highly recommend would be NYC tours it was one of the most amazing trips i had ever done on any holiday i have been on.
This included a private tour guide who was amazing and had fantastic knowledge on the city i managed to take the sub way the bus and go to Harlem and see the real New York, we walked to many parts of NYC and foun this amazing and made it easy for us to find our way around the city throughout our holiday.
We had dumplings in china town and got a real insight of how New yorker live!, this was amazing this tour was about £350.00 but was truly worth the whole experience our tour guide was Lawrence who lived in Queens and we literally walked from 10 am till 6.30 pm that night it was amazing we saw the whole of the city and was more than we could have ever have dreamed of.
WE also went on the staten island ferry didnt go up to the statue of liberty but was not really fussed about doing so, u can see it really close on the ferry and go quiet near it to.
We also went to the Rockerfella centre and done top of the rock and went up to the empire state building the views were amazing.
i can not wait to revist the city as its a place where i could visit time and time again, i was quiet disapointed with the shopping especially woodbury common i did manange to get some DKNY jeans for six pound each which was amazing but the clothing was very american . Also found that the designer shoes were cheaper in london than here even though the uggs were alot cheaper here than in london.
I would highly recommend this hotel and the tours this was an amazing experience, we ate in an italian called Bella Vita which was just off of times square it was cheap huge portions friendly staff and always got you a table was something out of good fellas the best pizza and italian i have had ate here every day pratically for dinner it was so lovely.
The hotel had a resident dj playing melow house music which was amazing and had old black and white films on the screen while you were swimming , it also had a steam room and a sauna.

title: “Great base for exploring NY”
text:
We stayed at Park 79 for 4 nights in January and would reccomend it to anyone looking for a base in NY. We were very happy staying there as it was close to 2 underground stations, restaurants, shops and Centra Park however If you are looking to spend much time in the hotel you could be dissapointed.
The hotel is quite basic and has no bar/restaurant etc however our small room was nicey furnished and was quiet and clean. The bathroom was modern and had a nice powerful and hot shower. The view from our window was a brick wall but for the price we paid we didn't expect great views of the city plus who wants to be sat looking out of the window when there is the whole of New York to explore?
The staff we not overly friendly but for the small contact we needed with them it really didn't matter.

title: “New York noise & hard beds”
text: We were assigned a room on the second floor of the Chelsea Savoy Hotel...right above an all night bar and a very busy street., This, and the fact the bed was very hard, made my friend and I regret our choice of hotel. The next morning we complained to the front desk and were immediately offered a 2 bed room on the 5th floor in the back - away from street noise. For this change we were grateful. It made the hard beds a bit more tolerable to have noise eliminated. If you do not have bad back issues, I suppose the beds are ok. My friend and I both do have back problems, so would not select this hotel in the future.

title: “A few kinks to work out...”
text: We stayed here because my nephew's wedding was being held at the hotel. Overall it was a pleasant experience, but there were a few less than perfect moments. It started when we were checking in and had to wait for our luggage to be brought up because there were no bellman's carts available. Normally I would have just schlepped my own bags, but we had lots of extra stuff for the wedding. We had upgraded to suites, which are HUGE! Apparently they do a lot of extended stays and this was the nicest place for that I have seen. The rooms are nicely decorated...very contemporary...and the bed was very comfortable. Excellent room darkening shades, but one of the venetian blinds in our room had a knot in the cord all the way at the top so we couldn't adjust the slats. The toilet ran continuously after flushing until we figured out to pull up on the handle. Also, there was no luggage rack in the room, so our suitcase started on the bed and ended up on the floor. I would have called to request one if we had been staying longer or had I not been so busy with wedding activities. Also, the on-site wedding coordinator was not readily available. When the florist arrived with the flowers, it took her 30 minutes to find out where we were waiting for her. The complementary breakfast was tasty, but several of the food items were cold. As I said, overall a pleasant stay.

title: “Would have been nice.....if the A/C worked....and they didn't lie about it....”
text: My husband and I chose this hotel because of the location and the fact that it was a smaller, boutique hotel. It looked really cute online. Also, it had a fitness center. Being an avid runner but not used to heat and humidity I was looking forward to being able to keep up my mileage while on vacation. The hotel is right next door to the John Hancock building and 2 blocks from the water. We arrived on July 21st, right in the middle of a nasty heatwave. The temperature was over 90 degrees and had been for several days. We walked into the lobby and immediately noticed how warm it was. The employee that checked us in told us that the A/C had been down since Monday and it was just fixed that morning and the hotel would be cooled down in a few hours. Annoyed but trying to keep positive, we get into our room and the A/C was on full blast, set to 50 degrees but the air coming out wasn't cold, wasn't even cool. We went out for about 4 hours and returned expecting coolness but Surprise! no change whatsoever. I talked to the same employee that checked us in and got a somewhat rude response.
