She said "like I told you earlier, its going to take a few hours to cool down." At this point it had been about 12 hours since the A/C was "fixed". After a sweat-soaked night of tossing and turning, we went to the front desk and inquired again. Now we were told that the A/C has a new problem and should be fixed that day. This was Friday morning. Needless to say, we checked out on Monday and the A/C never worked the entire time we were there. I understand that things like this happen, but what boiled my blood was the fact that they lied to us every single day, telling us the A/C was going to be fixed that day. Also their indifference was annoying. They never apologized once and acted like it was no big deal. When it's 95 degrees with 90% humidity, it is a big deal! We asked to be compensated in some way for our inconvenience. We were told that since we booked and paid through Expedia, we had to worked with Expedia to get money back. So I called Expedia that night, they put me on hold and tried to call the hotel. The hotel hung up on them twice and then put them (and me) on hold for 45 minutes before I gave up. So we got nothing. If this hadn't happened, I would have given this hotel 2 thumbs up. But since they screwed us over so bad, I am not even going to tell you what was nice about this place. At this point, I wonder if they even have A/C at all!! Beware of this place!!!!

title: “Exactly What You Want in a FS”
text: Everything about my four nights at this hotel was a pleasure. An easy and personable check-in at 2 pm. A generously sized room overlooking the fountain in Logan Circle. A reasonable package rate inclusive of breakfast (reasonable by comparison to hotels such as the Sheraton, Omni, etc. for which rates seemed out of whack during the time I was there -- the rate at FS was much better than the rate at the Ritz ). So here are the details: the room had two double beds, desk, dresser, good sized closet (with mini-fridge for keeping dinner leftovers). Missing from the room was a comfortable chair (other than the desk chair), for which there was ample room. Super clean. No chipped or worn furniture or furnishings. The sheets were the usual high quality one finds at a FS. The bathroom was well appointed with plenty of towels, very nice robes and L'Occitane toiletries, which were plentifully replaced. Good strong Speakman shower. Room temperature controls worked nicely (windows could be opened too). Housekeeping twice a day (at evening, the ice bucket was filled). No extra charge for basic and adequate wi-fi (you can upgrade for a charge). Breakfast off the menu was terrific, and the hostess remembered my name and preferred table each morning after the first. While the Fountain Restaurant was closed for dinner while we were there, the Swan Lounge was a very nice place for a relaxed light dinner, and while menu prices are the ususal sky high, portions were good and shareable. The pool and fitness room were nice, with good amenities in the locker room. Sauna, steam, geat shower, etc. Food can be ordered at the pool, and the cheese tray and drinks we ordered came down in short order. While the hotel is formally decorated, it is so in a contemporary way, so there is no feeling of stuffiness. One is not uncomfortable in shorts and a collared pullover in the public spaces, except perhaps on Saturday night when there were folks milling about in formalware for a function. This contrasted nicely with the FS in NY, which had rather cold and formal feeling public spaces, beautiful though it was. The FS Philadelphia is well located just a few blocks from City Hall, and a few more blocks after that to Independence Mall, Broad Street, and the rest of Center City. The hotel is just a long block from the Barnes (highly recommended), a beautiful public library and the Philadelphia Art Museum. If you deign to ride the double decker tour bus (which I recommend if you are visiting for the first time), you will be pleased that there is a stop right around the corner from the hotel entrance. My weekend at the FS was exactly what I had hoped for . . . nothing dissapointed.

title: “Stayed there for my best friend's daughter's wedding and the service and location was perfect for the event.”
text: Staff were very nice and accommodating. Great event at a great location.

title: “Stolen laptops at the hotel!!!”
text:
We got our laptops and a digital camera stolen the 2nd night we stayed there.....The general manager never contacted us we never got any reports from them concerning the issue. All they offer was a free breakfast which is a joke since a night in this hotel is close to $200 a night!! I can buy my own breakfast any day!!!!! 
PS. The staff and even the hotel President were indifferent and unprofessional regarding this issue!!! WORSE EXPERIENCE EVER!!!!

title: “Good for an inexpensive place to stay”
text:
I was in Seattle for a weekend and knew that I wouldn't be spending much time in the room, so booked a room at the University Travelodge since it was one of the less-expensive hotels in the area. I don't understand why a lot of the travelers had such negative experiences.
The staff during check in and check out were very kind and considerate. The room was definitely on the more worn side, but clean
and comfortable. It's within easy walking distance to the UW campus, and there is a great shopping area across the street.
If I am in the Seattle area, I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Stopped for the night”
text: Busy little hotel - lots of young adults and truckers. Not too noisy and decent room. Laundry room was close and in working order. We just stopped for the night along the way (unplanned) which was decent enough but we probably would not seek the hotel out if that was our destination. Staff was courteous.

title: “Great place to stay in NYC”
text:
We stayed at the Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan the weekend of the (cancelled) NYC Marathon, so it was completely booked with marathoners and those without electricity due to Hurricane Sandy. We arrived early Friday morning on the red eye and they held our luggage (for a fee) until a room was ready. The front desk staff were friendly and professional, and I really appreciated their effort to find us a room before the official check in time as I was unable to sleep on the plane and nearly delirious by noon. 
I'm over the trendy boutique hotels where rooms are the size of a shoe box. I want comfort and the room we had (a king) was clean and a good size, especially for NYC. The bed was really comfortable and I appreciated the outlets located on the nightstand so I could continue to use my ipad while charging. We had some problems adjusting the thermostat, but I think that was more due to user incompetence. My primary complaint about the room would be about the size of the bathroom. The sink was located separately outside of the bathroom, so it was just the shower and the toilet in there - and the bathroom was just big enough to fit those two. 
The hotel location is great. You can easily walk to so many places nearby - Central Park, shopping, restaurants, and the subway stop. There's also a Duane Reade across the street if you want to buy snacks/drinks for the hotel room. I would stay here again.

title: “Dissappointing - Wanted to love the stay, but so many wrongs!”
text:
I was so excited from the first moment I saw the hotel. Very cool place with great ambiance. Excellent location.
Housekeeping was the worst I've had in a while. Left trash in (and around) rooms & wouldn't take dirty glassware we set out for removal. Robes and towels were left strewn about, and fixtures like makeup mirrors and soap dishes were falling off the walls. A call to fix was met with a jury-rigging that left it only partially hanging off the wall. Calls for extra towels were met with responses of "we're out of that those now."
We had no cold water for one day, and part of the next evening.
We were told that the hotel had a house car that could take us to an event, but when I tried to arrange for it with the front desk, I was told I should "just go down and ask and maybe they'll be able to take you. You'll just need to wait and see."
On the bright side, the valet service was awesome and extremely helpful. 
I'd have to really think hard before I went back. I'd only recommend it with a "buyer beware."

title: “JUST AS GOOD AS THE PICS!”
text:
I came to Jacksonville for the first time to cruise. Not cruising for the first time, just cruising out of Jacksonville for the first time. The hotel is GREAT!!! I viewed the website so many times hoping it was not falsely advertised. I even booked this one over the hotels closer to the cruise port because it was so adorable online!
I arrived in Jacksonville late (after 2am) from Ohio, when I'd planned on arriving by 7pm. I was super tired and cranky and just wanted to crawl into bed. I'd called around 3 to say I wouldn't arrive by check in time. I spoke to a very helpful young lady who said don't worry 
she'd check me in at 4. (I was under the Friends & Family program. Not sure if that made a difference.) I was pleasantly surprised to find that the hotel is located right off of the freeway so no getting lost. I walked in expecting to have hassle. To my surprise, she'd not only kept her word but alerted the 3rd shift person and left my keys ready at the desk! Less than 5 minutes and I was all set.
I was able to park right outside the door. The parking lot is bit and well lit. They even have a small parking garage attached to the hotel in case you prefer it! 
I walked into my room and was once again pleasantly surprisd to find that I was assigned to a handicap suite. It was as spacious as a 1 bedroom apartmenr! I may be paranoid, but since it's Florida I had my hubby check everywhere for lizards, snakes, or scorpions. Happy to say there were none! I can even confirm the room is well dusted!
There are so many little touches that makes it feel better than home. I wanted to crawl into bed, but the bathroom was so large and inviting that I just had to take a shower. The mini fridge has a little freezer in it so I was happy to refreeze my ice packs. The free wifi was fast and reliable. I had one king size bed, a sleeper sofa, and a love seat! In addition to a desk with a super comfy enorgamic chair, 27 in flat screen tv and plenty of lamps and lighting. I loved it so much I could have stayed 2 days!
I will DEFINITELY make sure I book here whenever I stay in Jacksonville!
I haven't had the FREE breakfast yet, but I'm sure it'll be excellent also. Even if it isn't, no biggie. I still have lots of leftover fruit from the road and I'm going on a cruise where I'll spend a week to my heart's content!
If I remember, I'll take pics tomorrow and post them. With this same title if not entire post.

title: “Regularly stay at this hotel once a month”
text: I've stayed at the hotel about 3 or 4 times due to the location being between two offices I visit while in San Antonio. Its near shopping and restaurants I like also. Its normally extremely clean, but this visit the hotel is very busy with summer and lots of children and families. Its not as clean as normal and the room hasn't been as clean as I prefer. I used to stay at the other location near Medical Center and found it old and too noisy. I will give them another chance here. Service is good here,

title: “Not a Four Star Hotel”
text: Okay.. The Lobby is beautiful. You drive up.. Valet parking you think wow elegant... Valet attendant comes to open the door, even handed me my seat belt when we got ready to leave a few hours later..... If that alone would make it a Four Star then hands down they got it........BUTTTTTT.... They Nickle and dime you to death... Valet $20.00 a night... and they ONLY have Valet; Incidentals $50.00 a night...yes a night... I have never stayed at a hotel where they charge incidentals per night... $30.00 to have a fridge, $30.00 to have a microwave... $19.00 breakfast buffet.....Really.... Of Course this was a priceline deal... I usually stay at the Sheraton Suites but looking for a cheaper deal.... I will say the rooms overall were nice however the wooden sliding bathroom door would not slide all the way closed... and there was back up in the sink and tub.. the drain system was not great... soooo overall... nice place to lay your head but Four Star... NOT...

title: “Gem of a hotel”
text: Great experience from booking to departing. Beautiful spacious room on penthouse overlooking the bay. Loved being so close to Pike's Market. Great food recommendation for Lowell's in the market. Charming hotel.

title: “Older and everything "skimpy"”
text: Central location is convenient. My wife and I stayed one night when I had business in Philadelphia. Hotel is just "functional." Pleasant enough staff in lobby. No place in the hotel to just get coffee on the go in the morning and no convenient near-by safe place to walk to. Everything seems old and fairly tired. The most annoying issue is that things are just skimpy: the bathroom supplies seemed like a Motel 6 -- one tiny bar of soap for both sink and shower and 2 old threadbare towels . Very limited cable TV channels and then half of them did not work. While it's not supposed to be the Ritz, it was not inexpensive -- but it certainly felt cheap.

title: “fantastic staff, great location”
text: Its taken so long to write this but i thought the hotel deserved the review. The staff were friendly, the room clean and the hotel great. The breakfast of croissants and pastries was very handy, it meant we could have a leisurely breakfast whilst deciding where to go. The best thing was the location, it could not have been better. Would definautely go ago.

title: “Excellent home base for a visit to San Antonio”
text:
Attended a three day business meeting at this hotel, and extended my trip by a day to do some additional site seeing.
First off the location is just about perfect for those wishing to enjoy downtown San Antonio and the Riverwalk. The Alamo was a 2-3 minute walk right out the front doors of the hotel, and the Riverwalk is right out the back doors. 
The staff was very friendly and courteous. All of my interactions from the front desk staff, concierge, wait staff and bartenders to the maids and maintenance staff were very pleasant. It seemed like what ever my question or request, they were happy to talk to me and help. 
I ate breakfast and lunch at the hotel everyday, and dinner one evening. They were all very good, and at no time did it seem like 'regular" buffet type meals. Breakfast offered eggs, meat, potatoes and very good picante sauce. A generous section of fresh fruit and pastries, and lots of very good coffee.
Lunch was free range chicken and a very tasty fish, a southwest style cold salad and some wonderful deserts. Another lunch was cold cuts and cheese tray, along with ships and salsa.
Dinner was a petite filet and it was cooked exactly to my liking. Interestingly the steak at the hotel was FAR superior to the one I had at Landry's later that week.
My room was clean and spacious, and while I had an "interior" view, it did look out over the beautiful atrium lobby and River-walk.
Took advantage of the rooftop pool one evening, and it was a nice experience as well.
There is plenty to see and do within walking distance of the hotel. Shops, museums, historic sites, and more restaurants and bars than I had time to explore. I also took a bit of a hike and walked down to three of the five historic missions on the mission trail. The Alamo was originally Mission Valero and from there Mission Concepcion was a 4 mile walk, some of which was on city streets and other parts on the Riverwalk trail. Sadly not all of it is open, but the parts I was able to get to were very nice. 
The National Park Service main visitor center is at Mission San Jose, and it is the largest and most complete of the four. Mission San Juan required a bus ride and a 4 mile round trip walk, despite what the park rangers tell you, the 42 bus line doesn't take you very close. I did also get to visit the Espada Dam and aquaduct, an ingenious irrigation system used to help farm around the Missions. The last Mission Espada was an even longer walk, and with no bus service I was getting hot and tired so I returned to the hotel to cool off on the Riverwalk.
Most of the chains have places on the Riverwalk such as Rainforest Cafe, The Hard Rock Cafe, Dicks Crab Shack, Coyote Ugly, Howl at the Moon, Landry's and others. I enjoyed meals and drinks at The County Line, La Paloma, Mad Dog's Pub, and several others.
All in all I had a wonderful visit, and plan to return with my family to show them a beautiful southwestern city.

title: “Great Personnel”
text: We arrived early Sunday morning after a long flight from Singapore. Jesus at the front desk was awesome in assisting us with an early check in so we could clean up and go to our granddaughter's 20th birthday party. 3rd time we've stayed here and will certainy do so again.

title: “Beware if you drive...”
text:
When we walked in they were renovating - oh i thought to myself, that's why i got the room for $100 per night. Everything was under construction in the lobby and restaurant - no problem since our room was on par with similar doubletrees ive stayed at. 
My issue is with the valet parking... I knew there was a $28 charge for parking - no problem im in DC - What i didn't know when they took my car was that it would take them more than 40 min. to retreive it! Even after calling down before check out and the front desk letting me know they would bring it out for us. We came down 15 min. later and then waited 40 more min.
What really killed me was as we and other guests lined up at the bellstand - there was only one guy strolling to retreive cars - the manager came over and found the other bellman literally HINDING out in the bell closet on his mobile!!!! To bad the managers reaction wasn't as intense as my own internal disgust. You're in the service industry people! 
In the end we got our car, paid only the $31 not $28 dollars for valet service. The guy in the closet had the nerve to look at me for a tip... he didn't even offer to put my luggage in the trunk like most bellman do.
If i were you i would walk two blocks around the corner, pay $15 for overnight parking and have access to my car whenever we need without the wait. It's worth it especially if you can get your sweetie to drop you and your stuff off at the door.
On a positive note - LOVED the recycling bins in the room, hope it actually gets recycled... didn't notice the staff separating the two.

title: “Great service”
text: My husband and I just stayed for a week at the Sorrento Hotel in Seattle. We stayed in the Sorrento Suite (call direct for great rates, better than Orbitz or Expedia). The service at the hotel is top notch - we lost our luggage the first day and the concierge was very accommodating with items that we requested. Room service was quick and the food from the Hunt Club was excellent. The only negative about the hotel is that the suites are small with VERY small bathrooms. The beds are heavenly - there is quite a bit of street noise, but the beds are so comfortable you will sleep right through it. If you are looking for a quiet, old hotel with lots of charm and great service we definitely recommend the Sorrento Hotel. Stay away from the cafe right across the street - worse breakfast I have ever had in my life!

title: “Nice, but WATCH OUT!”
text:
I stayed here 2 nights at the end of August. It's a nice hotel with a great Upper West Side location. And by booking through Priceline, I got a good rate for NYC. I wish I didn't have to say this, because I liked the hotel, but.... WATCH OUT! At 2 different times they added a charge for use of the minibar in my room. I know about these minibars and did not even touch any of the items in it. At check out, there was a minibar charge which they removed when I told them I didn't use it. They explained it is very sensitive, so that must have been what happened. They removed the charge. The woman checking out next to me had a minibar charge for $35 for whiskey - she said neither she nor her husband drinks. The following day I was reviewing my credit card charges and saw another charge from the hotel for a different amount! When I called, they told me it was for use of the minibar. I told them I didn't use or touch the minibar and they began to give me the same story about it being very sensitive. They removed that charge, but you have to wonder how many people get taken.
My advise - the hotel is nice, but their billing practices are shady. If you stay here, scrutinize your bill.

title: “Wouldn't even get out of the car!!!!”
text:
We pulled up out the front & the hotel
was surrounded by so many homeless/drug looking people that we didn't even feel safe enough to get out of the car with our kids! 
We drove away & found a hotel at Fishermans Wharf & did not care about loosing the money we'd spent on the Renoir.
 The pictures of the hotel on the website are certainly out of date. I now wish I had read previous reviews on here before booking!

title: “I resent paying for Wifi”
text:
when i can get it free in a bar around the corner.
I am a hyatt member and have used many of their hotels - moscow, paris, milan.
Grand Hyatt NY is OK. I had heard of big refurb but wasn't too impressed by it. The entrance looks grand, the bar is a little shabby already. Rooms ok size for NY as was bathroom
Service was very good however and any problems rectified quickly.

title: “Eh.”
text:
When we booked Travelodge, we were only looking for a place to sleep for one night in Philadelphia. Naturally, we weren't expecting something luxurious, but let it be known that you get what you pay for here. 
I thought the hotel itself was in a nice location - there's a nice convenience store next door, and Jake's Pizza down the street is great. Some people complained of the hotels' proximity to a homeless shelter - I honestly had no problem with it at all. You wouldn't have even known it was there. 
The interior of the hotel was quite old/dirty, for example, there was mildew on the shower curtain, and the ventilator in the bathroom leaked. The room itself was incredibly tiny, with a window looking out only to the hallway. Our sink also was not located in the bathroom, which was a bit of an inconvenience. 
Just to sum it up...
Pros: Price, Location, Staff
Cons: Price, Cleanliness, Parking (2 blocks away, extra fee)

title: “bed bugs”
text: We stayed in Room 412 and found a dead bed bug in the sink area. We told the receptionist who was extremely apologetic but claimed that she had never heard this complaint. Upon reading a December 2009 review we now know that we were not the only unfortunate souls to experience this horrible occurance also in room 412. The receptionist called the manager who was off site and did not believe us so we brought the bed bug in a plastic bag as evidence with the intention of having him followup on this by fumigating. They gave us $15 for drycleaning however we will never stay there again. Too bad as the location is great. We should have been given an entire refund. We asked to be contacted with their followup plan to address the bed bug problem but that never happened.

title: “Noisy!”
text: The Andrews Hotel was not as advertised, but I guess you get what you pay for. Parking was a problem and not because there is only a valet service. There are parking zones in front of the hotel that shares the block with two other hotels and a laundromat. At times there were a number of patrons in the street using the few parking spots. Inside the hotel itself the walls are rather thin making it quite noisy later in the evening and early in the morning. The hotel staff seemed aloof and the management was sparcely available. I highly recommend spending $30 eleswhere in Union Square that has parking and cleaner rooms.

title: “Good stay in San Fran”
text:
I just visited The Opal and was a little nervous since it was my first time in San Francisco and reviews were mixed. But overall my stay was very pleasant. I was there for 4 days and the staff was actually very helpful and nice. They gave my fiance and I great advice on places to visit and where to eat and how to get around. The hotel itself I would say is pretty centrally located. You can get around easily in San Francisco so its really not far from anything. We took the BART train from the airport and got off at Civic center. We were having issues getting a cab and didn't know the bus system, so I pulled out my Iphone and used my GPS to walk to the property which was only about a 7-10 minute walk. 
 The rooms were ok...I stayed in room 210. I think they were pretty nice for the price. Clean rooms, comfortable bed, clean bathroom...not bad at all. The hotel has been around for awhile so you can tell its an older building but its well renovated and that oldness brings charm. There is free breakfast in the morning but its pretty scarce...just bagels, toast, and coffee but there is a restaurant attached to the hotel and the next block up is a 24 hour pastry /breakfast place that is pretty affordable. You do have to pay $28-30 for parking but we didn't bring a car. 
 So overall great place to stay in San Fran...when we go back to San Francisco we will definitely stay there again because its affordable, centrally located, and clean. Hope this helps:-)

title: “GREAT location, nice hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed in this hotel for 5 nights last week. We loved it. From what I saw, it is the nicest hotel within a couple of blocks of Fisherman's Wharf - a short 2 block walk, and you're at the Wharf and the tons of things to do there. TONS of restaurants nearby. There is also a cable car turn-around across the street from the hotel. The hotel staff was one of the friendliest I've ever seen. In our 6 days there, not one time did a hotel employee walk by us without saying hello or asking if they could help. The rooms were nice, roomy, quiet, the bed was comfortable, the air conditioning worked very well, and the TV was modern and large. The only odd thing about the room was that there are no doors on the shower - only a partial glass wall.....made for a bit of a chilly shower....but the bathroom was large with a lot of counter space. The room did not have a fridge, and that would have been nice- that's really my only complaint. Starbucks served in the lobby, and there's a Starbucks across the street. Walgreens within 2 blocks, which was convenient to pick up things we needed. The pool and hot tub area were nice also. Overall excellent stay, in a GREAT, GREAT, GREAT location!!

title: “Good location, but depends on the room you get.”
text:
I tavel to this location a great deal and stayed at this hotel twice. One trip was just for a few days and another for a few weeks.
Overall, the location is great especially if you like shopping. The restaurants are high end but reasonably priced.
The hotel looks good and always kept clean. The staff are pleasant.
The first time I stayed there I had a room on the 4th floor away from everyone. This was great except if you took the elevator, you have a long walk to the room because of how the building was constructed. If you took the stairs, humid stairways up and down 4 flights.
The second time was for a longer visit. This is what pulled the score way down for me. I don't know if they were trying to save on the electricity bill or if the hadmechanical problems, but the main areas of the hotel and elevators did not have a/c. So it was hot, humid, and smelled musky. The first room the put me in was on the 1st floor. DO NOT recommend this floor. Noisey from above and outside. Asked for a room change, but couldn't the first few days due to a large group stay. Once they did move me, I was on the 3rd floor, it was quieter, but the room smelled horrible. No chance of changing rooms cause it was fully booked. I had to buy several room fresheners. Yes i had the rooms cleaned, but would not get rid of the musky smell...think it was the plumbing lines. Speaking of getting the rooms cleaned, I normally only like to have the room cleaned 2-3 times a week. I had to ask the front desk to inform the cleaning staff to clean my room several times beause they didnt pay attention to the door magnets.
Teammate had a worse experience. Someone brought a dog inside and the next day her room was infested with fleas. The front desk called someone and they exterminated the room...with her personal belongings not protectected. She had to speak with management because od how they exterminated while she was pregnant. Then when they wer done, dead fleas remained until she asked the front desk to clean everything. She also didnt have pots or pans to cook.
For the location, you expect top motch. Recommend elsewhere for the money unless you like fire alarms being tested Saturday mornings.

title: “Great Hotel! heplfull and close to Times Square”
text:
Sup guys! 
We had been in Las vegas nov 2010, Florida March/April 2011, Florida July/August 2011 and Here NYC October 2011 and This hotel is GREAT!!!!
We passed a good vacations there, the staff was great and very helpfull
the standard room was pretty and enough for 2 personnes this is why I said under that Don't be demanding if you choose this room because if you guys are still outside so you don't need to get a big room...only if you're rich or with your familly, clean room to the bed till the bathroom 
I recommend this hotel because the staff is very great all day they are still smiling 
We'll come back
Salut tout le monde!
Nous avions ete a Las vegas nov 2010, Floride Mars/Avril 2011, Floride Julliet/Aout 2011 and Here NYC Octobre 2011 est cette hotel est Super!!!
Nous avons passés des excellents vacances, le personnel ete super gentil et tres serviable
La chambre standard est très belle et assez pour 2 personnes et c'est pourquoi en dessous j'ai dit ne soyez pas exigeants! si vous choisissez cette chambre parce vous allez toujours etre dehors donc c'est pas la peine de prendre une grande chambre sauf si vous etes riches ou en famille...chambre propre du lit jusqu’à la salle de bain
Je recommande cette hotel parce que le personnel est tres sympa toute la journee et tres souriant 
Nous reviendrons

title: “Adequate but certainly not nice”
text: I stayed here one night while travelling for work. The hotel is fine. The staff was friendly & helpful. Room was clean & decent but by no means was this a nice hotel. One thing that was great was the water pressure in the shower....this was very important to me after a long day. The hotel is only a few blocks from the subway and Times Square so that was helpful. I would recommend you stay here is money is a concern and you are truly only using this place to sleep & shower.

title: “A Pleasure”
text: The service people were terrific...the room was comfortable,clean,with magnificent paintings of DC...the bar is comforting,room service is right on the food was great...the location can't be beat...and the price was right....

title: “Highly recommended!”
text:
Gorgeous room, Gorgeous bathtub - the room was big and immaculate!!!
Good location too.. just a few blocks walk to the centre and shops.
The view wasn't anything to shout about but who needs a view when you're in a luxury bedroom??? 
We found the staff very helpful and friendly - nothing was too much fro them!

title: “Preferred Property in NYC”
text:
Whenever possible, I stay at the Hilton Garden Inn on 35th Street for the following reasons:
1) Conveniently located - just a few feet from the subway, a block from Macy's and an easy walk from Penn Station. 2) Great staff - always courteous at the front desk and they will go out of their way to be helpful; I left a theater ticket with the front desk for a colleague who was staying at the 48th Street HGI this week - no hassles at all; 3) Breakfast cooked to order. The rooms are pleasant and I always appreciate having a refrigerator - one of the best perks in a Hilton Garden Inn.

title: “Trendy and affordable.”
text: Hotel Max is in a great location in downtown Seattle. The rates are affordable, the staff is professional and pleasant. This is a perfect place for young folks hip on the art scene-- as the decor and atmosphere is right up that alley. However, I am a square, middle-aged nurse and found the place to suit my needs and I was very comfortable there. The concierge gentlemen were very helpful and accommodating. If you stay at Hotel Max, you will have an easy walk to the typical Seattle attractions like Pike Place Market and the Space Needle. The hotel is spotless. Checkout time was noon-- a treat!! No matter where you go in Seattle, be prepared to pay a lot of parking. Seattle still hasn't figured out decent parking options yet, but she's getting there. Easy walk from the light rail station if you happen to take the light rail from the airport.

title: “Over priced and not very helpful”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at The Lennox for two nights during a trip to Boston and Cape Cod. 
Our trip started in Washington DC and we had just stayed at the Palomar Hotel (a Kimpton Boutique) and been very spoiled.
We checked into the Lennox at $100 per night more than the Palomar and expected old fashioned luxury. Instead, we found a small, pokey room, unfriendly staff and a disappointing stay.
There was only enough room at the end of the bed for one of us to walk by, the bed wasn't very comfortable and on a couple of occasions, the desk staff weren't very helpful.
They even asked the car hire company to move the car they were delivering to us and we were in the lobby waiting to step outside!
At $260 per night I expect a lot more!

title: “Colonnade”
text:
We spent 2 nights at the Colonnade in September.
The location was excellent for shopping, eating out and for transport as there is a T subway station right outside the hotel.
The room was a reasonable size for a city hotel and the quality of the bed linen, mattress and pillows was excellent. The bathroom was small but well appointed.
The room was clean but the bathroom needed some attention to detail, very dusty ledges, mirror lights, back of door, top of phone etc..
Reception staff, concierge and doorman were very helpful.
Disappointed that the roof top pool had closed as this was one of our main reasons for choosing this hotel.
Brasserie Jo the only eating option, some coffee in the lobby would have been nice.
Would certainly consider staying at the Colonnade again.

title: “My new favourite in Washington DC”
text: I used to always stay at the same hotel in Washington DC and recently had to search for an alternative location. I found the St Regis Washington DC Hotel. Since I have stayed at the hotel on my last 3 trips to DC. The location is perfect, the rooms are luxurious and the bar is second to none, in particular Khaleed, truly a barman par excelence. The reception staff, particularly Kristin, are truly a delight and the most helpful I have encountered. This is my my new DC home.

title: “Loved the Mayflower Park Hotel!”
text:
We stayed at the Mayflower Park Hotel in late April 2007. We used to live in the area, so knew the location was prime. The hotel has a great reputation, so we decided to book our stay here and see for ourselves. We were not disappointed!
We had a room on the 3rd floor. Our room was quite large, and very comfortable. As we walked in the door, there was a large wet bar with a small refrigerator. Upon entering the main part of the room, there was a sofa and several chairs with ottomans as well as a large coffee table. A very useable seating area, which is not always the case in hotels. We had a king bed, and near the bed area was the large walk in closet (with bathrobes for our use) and the bathroom. The bathroom was a tad small, but not cramped. Everything was nicely appointed and extremely well maintained. 
Our room looked out to the street towards the old Bon store (now Macy's), so at the holidays it would be a very nice view.
Our room was very quiet. We never heard noise from other rooms or from the street. 
We did not have any meals at the hotel restaurant, but we did have drinks in the bar, Oliver's, several times. This place gets busy, so the wait for drinks can be a bit, but it was never very long.
We used the valet several times and they were always very quick. 
Our visit was so enjoyable that while we were checking out, I booked another stay there for this fall for a girls week in the area. The room was beautiful and the location cannot be beat.

title: “Fantastic value and great location!”
text: In our first trip to CA, staying two blocks from Union Sq was very convenient for transportation and dining options. The hotel has a nice, spacious lobby decorated with lovely and discrete japanese theme. We had a priceline US80 booking for 5 nights and asked for a complimentary upgrade for partner's birthday, which was not given to us, but instead, our demand for a high floor with a view, was provided for us. Fair enough! The room is not huge, but definitely not as small as I feared from some other reviews on TA. In fact, the room and the whole hotel experience was really comfortable for us.

title: “Got Great Rate!”
text: Went on Priceline and got a great rate for this hotel. I even knew the name of it before we booked it! Got free breakfast which was awesome! ($22.50 usually!!!) Rooms were nice, location was great..Only drawback was .no pool and internet was way to high priced for "us little people" w/out a business expense account! All in all, glad we stayed there!

title: “Location Location Location”
text:
We stayed here for three nights over Memorial Day weekend. Pros: The location is great and we were close enough to walk many places. There is a drug store right across the street for anything that you forgot. Warm cookies at the front desk in the afternoon! Rooms are big enough and beds are comfortable. Staff was extremely friendly and the housekeeping staff always had a good morning!, for us and did a great job cleaning the room.
Cons: We asked for a city view but we were facing a large building. The pool is small and one family of 15 took up the all of the chairs and the hot tub, squeezing us out. Our tub drain was slow and filled up with water when you showered. The restaurant attached-Weber Grille, was horrible. The hostess was rude, 2 hour wait for sub-standard food. Ribs were tough and the meatloaf full of salt. I would never return to the Weber Grille. Not sure if the hotel is involved with it or not but should be if not. 
Overall hotel was a good deal but find another restaurant!

title: “At the bottom end of fine”
text: I know that staying in Seattle in the summer is expensive, but pay a little more and stay somewhere else. The place is very old and smells like smoke in most rooms. I suppose it is clean enough, so that is one good thing. The gym is really a joke, not worth going to at all, and I would not dare stick my foot in that hot tub. The breakfast place was very drab and unwelcoming. I have had much better breakfasts at other Best Westerns. Not awful, but really not very great.

title: “This Embassy Suites and its true Ambassadors of Great Customer Service”
text: My family and I stayed at this Great Hotel for three nights two weeks ago. The suites were very nicely decorated, and has just enough ammenities to please us all, nice breakfast, but mainly excellent staff who really know the real meaning of good customer service!., This was our first time in Philly, and if we come back, we will definetly stay there again, we would in fact recommend this hotel for its convenient location, close to everything interesting to see and do in the area, and their nice facilities and great customer service from the front desk staff, to their entire perssonel involved in the hotel's smooth ways of pleasing their guess.

title: “Big hotel , no fuss hotel but perfect location.”
text: Very crowded this hotel atleast on the ground floor , 8 th floor ( lobby ) actually this floor reminds me more of a small airport and sometimes the elevators even if there are many. Restaurants and bars in this hotel are not atractive and menus are poor . Rooms remind me of the late 70s beside the very nice flatscreen tv. Rooms are clean and do have all the essentials for a tourist or business traveler. Gym is very nice . This hotel is in urgent need of modernisation wich is happening i believe on certain floors . Location is more then perfect but choice of hotels is large in this are of new york so if i can receive this special deal again ( 1268 usd for 4 nights excl tax ) i will be back but usually this hotel is more expensive and then i prefer to look for alternatives in the area.

title: “Great hotel in a great location friendly helpful staff”
text:
A really lovely hotel in a most convenient location to visit all tourist attractions in New York. Lovely spacious room and beds extremely comfortable. Lovely patio restaurant at the back of the bar which could easily be missed if you weren't the inquisitive type to roam around !
Greg the concierge helped to make our trip a great success with his New York sense of humour which I love !
I'll be back !

title: “Great location but severe construction noise”
text:
We are Kimpton InTouch members and prefer the brand because we like the decor (hip but comfy) and free wireless, and usually they give us an apple or water (not here). The Muse basically does not perform like the other Kimptons we've stayed at. The guest room was below standard: couch you couldn't sit on, no coffee table, non-working heater, bad plumbing. We were also hammered with extreme construction noise at 7:30 every weekday morning (mid-December-2011). Kinda gets you out of bed early. It's on the back (north) side of the hotel. Our package included "full American breakfast", but what that meant was we got the continental breakfast (hard little pastries or toast + bowl of cut fresh fruit) and were able to add either an egg, or pancakes, or oatmeal. It's probably better to skip the package and eat at one of the nearby restaurants.
On the upside, the location is excellent (easy walk to everything), the hotel restaurant was excellent, and there is a terrific Cuban restaurant a few doors away. Actually, we decided all the food in NY is great. Anyhow, you need to check out the cool restrooms next to the lobby.

title: “All as expected”
text: Good value for what was expected. Two bedrooms, enough room for all four family members (mom, dad, 2 adult kids), although bathroom is small. Clean. The management very effectively and unhesitatingly addressed a concern I had and left me feeling very positive about their commitment to customer service. Right on Time Square and close to all amenities, including Hop On-Hop Off bus. Complimentary breakfast was included in our rate and filled us up for the day ahead.

title: “Good weekend get-away”
text: We stayed at The Westin Oaks while in town for the weekend. The Westin Oaks was a nice oasis amid Houston traffic & the rush of the city. Our room was clean but there was a coffee stain on the bed linens. When we brought this to the attention of the staff it was quickly remedied. The bed was comfy, fridge was convenient, bathroom & bedroom were nice sizes & the view was very pretty with the lights from the city. Convenient location to the Galleria Mall which made it easy to park the car & then have choices of restaurants & things to do closeby. As previously mentioned in other reviews, the elevators are REALLY slow which is frustrating & inconvenient. Overall, a nice hotel & we'd choose it again.

title: “The a/c didn't work!”
text: Nice size rooms, clean, very friendly staff, HOWEVER ... two of the four nights we were there, the A/C didn't work. When I reported it to the front desk, they just said "Yes, we knew it was out". Ummm, what? They said it would be fixed the next night, but the next night was just as hot. When we checked out and again reported the problem, she said "Did you alert the front desk" to which we said yes. And that was it, no mention of a discount, no apologies! I am disappointed because I really wanted to love this place, but unfortunately, even despite the great location, I will not be staying here again. No one likes to sweat while they sleep!

title: “Great Location - Mixed Service”
text: My family and I stayed at the Marriott for 3 nights to start our Northwest vacation and our review is mixed. Although I made one reservation for two rooms they put the rooms on separate floors. We had to wait past 5pm for two rooms on the same floor. Then the air conditioned in the second room would only blow hot air. They did correct the problem by giving us an awesome corner room (very spacious with nice views of Pugent Sound). In the end it was a great location. The cafe had excellent food selection and prompt service. The restaurant was the complete opposite. We have terrible service; our waiter finally admitted to giving our food to another table when we asked him why our meals were taking exceeding long (we waited over 30 minutes for french toast and an omelet). In the end the food was mediocre at best. So, I would recommend staying here for the location but just don't eat in the restaurant.

title: “Darned nice”
text:
We would definitely stay at this hotel again.
The location is excellent, adjacent to the airport, yet not so close to the airport as to be congested traffic-wise or overly noisy from jet traffic.
The circular design is quite interesting, and lends itself to rooms a bit larger than what you would ordinarily expect. The staff was friendly and excellent, particularly the servers in the restaurant, which featured better-than-expected fare at dinner. 
Easy, clean, large, interesting, and friendly staff. What’s not to like?

title: “Nice Surprise”
text: After reading some of the reviews concerning the Hudson, we were a bit worried. However, a double bed room proves to be roomy enough for three individuals. The staff was friendly and prompt. Overall, I would gladly stay here again.

title: “Good central location”
text:
I'm from Philadelphia, so don't have much occasion to stay at hotels in the city. For Christmas my wife gave us a "night on the town" in Philly based around an excellent price at the Doubletree for one night (my value rating largely reflects an overnight price of one-hundred dollars). First of all, the location is great. That's definitely the biggest selling point. Philadelphia is a great walking city, and the Doubletree puts you in the middle of everything. The historic area is nine blocks or so, the Avenue of the Arts is right outside your front door, a plethora of good restaurants surround the hotel, etc. There's even easy access to the SEPTA subway right outside. 
What we liked:
> Location
> Room furnishings were high quality, and bedding was very comfortable
> Room was very clean
> Great view from the 22nd floor
> Convenient attached parking garage, while not cheap (~$25 overnight) was comparably priced to others in the area... beware, though, the garage is very tight to navigate if you have a larger vehicle
Could improve:
> No huge issues on this visit, but some "could be improved" things...
> Front desk staff was unaware of a special offer that we had been e-mailed as part of our reservation for an as-available upgrade to a executive room with breakfast. Unfortunately, we didn't bring a printout of the e-mail, so we didn't push it (even though we saw we were right when we got home)
> Even though we were on the 22nd floor, we still got the occasional "city noise" wafting up to us through the single-glazed windows that could be more soundproof. If we were on a lower floor I'm sure it would have been much louder.
> A fair amount of noise from the hallway; why can't hotels make their hallway doors more soundproof? I don't get it.
As others have noted, for some reason elevator noise can be high in this hotel. Even though we were well down from the elevator, I could still hear it "whirring" in the middle of the night. I can't imagine how loud it would be if you were right there. There is actually a hotel room on each floor right in the elevator lobby between the elevator banks (I think it's #xx10). Avoid that at all costs! 
Overall: A decent hotel, good location, and generally pleasant staff. I wasn't wowed by it, though. But, of course I liked my cookie upon check-in!
Some hints: if you don't want to spring big $$ for the hotel breakfast, there's an IHOP very close by, as well as Starbucks and other food purveyors.

title: “Very poor hotel”
text:
This hotel was the poorest room and hotel ammenities I've stayed in in the past 5 years 
Lounge and restaurant never open.

title: “Average business hotel but great location”
text:
I've stayed twice here, both times because of its great location downtown. The rooms are good and clean but not exceptional in any way. The hotel does not have any catering or room service which is a shame, and frankly unacceptable. But across the street are some great restaurants, so as long as your hunger coincides with their opening timings, you are ok. Otherwise there is a vending machine in the reception :-)
I was upgraded to a suite, but I could not find a minibar - not even a bottle of water. Going down to the reception to get one after having changed into my PJs seemed too much effort.
Breakfast quality is poor. Horrible tea, none of the tea flavours taste like what they are supposed to. If you like a decent cup of tea, just take your own tea bags. Food itself is a hit and miss affair, since they only prepare a limited variety of things (scrambled eggs/bacon etc) and all else is bought packaged.

title: “Lovely hotel but eat elsewhere”
text:
I recently stayed at the Taj Hotel and although I absolutely loved our room with the fireplace, I was disappointmented with the food. I ordered the crabcake which was supposed to be served over a bed of greens. The crab was fishy and it was served with a side of finely julienne cut veggies...hardly a salad. I had also tried the soup of the day, which was a tomato bisque. It was flavorless. For the exhorbitant prices, the food should be much, much better. I would recommend eating elsewhere.
Everything else about the hotel was lovely. The location is very convenient, the bar room was one of my favorite places to have a drink...very very cozy, and the staff was pleasant.
We were not able to get the club access as it was full, but I am certain that makes the stay exceptional.
I would recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

title: “Cool, friendly, convenient”
text: I have stayed at the W several times now as it is so convenient to many Midtown locations. I love the cool feel it has about it, especially in the lounge / lobby area - doesnt make you feel like you are a business traveler. Rooms can be VERY small - I will admit that - but then who spends a lot of time in their room when they are in NYC! This time I was lucky and got an upgrade to a slightly more spacious room. It has all that you need. Biggest drawbacks are what most NYC hotels suffer from - quite a lot of noise (I never travel without earplugs) and expensive extras (from internet access to minibar and room service - luckily there are lots of cafes and restaurants nearby).

title: “Service combined with location have made this hotel my favorite in Indianapolis.”
text:
First, the front desk staff go out of their way to make an extended stay like being at home away from home. Cherie, Annette, John and Connie greet you personally to make you feel welcome and go out of their way to assure your comfort during your stay. A simple task such as giving extended stay guests a laundry basket ( cost less than $5 ) instead of those unwieldy plastic bags to carry one's dirty clothes to the laundry room make the stay enjoyable. Second, the hotel is on a canal. Joggers, walkers, bikers etc can be seen every day and in better weather you will see paddle wheel boats, kayaks and an occasional gondola on the water. 2 seater and 4 seater bikes are available in season for rent. A trip around the canal is approx. 3 miles. There are several museums, condos and
 a college campus for Indiana U and Purdue U on the canal. You are within walking distance of Lucas Oil Stadium, Conseco Fieldhouse, Indiana Repertory Theater and downtown Indy including Circle Center Mall . Free Breakfast is served daily at the hotel and free meals are served several evenings for those too tired to venture out to numerous restaurants also within walking distance.Swimming pool, hot tub and exercise room are also on the premises. I just completed my fourth stay at the hotel and hope to return in the future.

title: “Good hotel even when things go wrong”
text:
We checked in to the Clift for three nights - our first time in SF. Very pleasant room, nicely furnished, very comfortable bed. The restaurant and bar are excellent - very cool places (all dark wood with quirky pieces of art). The Clift is only two blocks from Union Square, so the location is great too.
On the third night we returned from the bar to our room about midnight. We could hear the party next door - extremely loud music and shouting. (Walls are paper thin). We went to the front desk and the young man on duty immediately dispatched two security guys to tell the partygoers to knock it off. Very impressive result - and much more effective than the front desk ringing them to ask if they would lower the volume. 
So what could have been an unfortunate end to our stay was resolved satisfactorily. 
Overall a good choice if you're staying in San Francisco.

title: “Fun Resort; Older Rooms”
text: I stayed here with a friend in Summer 2003 because she had a free room voucher. This is an older resort. The rooms are older and very average, but the water features are GREAT. Kids and adults alike will love it! There is a Lazy River where you can float around a "water course" on an innertube (provided by the resort). There's waterfalls; several pools; water volleyball; fantastic drink specials; and a western themed restaurant. For dining out, please go elsewhere! Phoenix boasts many great restaurants, but none of them are at this resort! The resort is tucked away from most of the city, but you can reach restaurants etc within a 15-20 minute drive.

title: “Perfect location & price”
text:
I have stayed at The Stratford Hotel on 4 separate occasions. It is the perfect San Francisco hotel, priced right with an ideal location. I do not like paying for all the frills, as I not a frills person so this hotel is exactly what I like. The staff are friendly & helpful.
If your room faces the street, it maybe noisy at night, so now I request a room that doesn't overlook the street. Although the street facing rooms allow you to look out at the hustle of the city from the comfort of your room.

title: “Ocean Fix”
text:
Can't be much closer to the ocean, listening to the waves as you sleep. Price is right, clean rooms with great parking. Only real flaw, new carpeting is needed. When booking request the quiet side or next time we would preferably book the rooms right on the boardwalk, worth the extra money. Great location for a lot less cost. 
Patrick was very friendly when we checked in. Went the extra for making our stay as great as possible.

title: “Good price, no real complaints and smoking rooms!”
text:
Just got back, stayed from 27/03/08 for 3 nights- two 60+ couples, first visit to N.Y.
Booked via Hotel web-site. by pre-paying we got two 2 double beds rooms for £136 pn each. Rooms were very spacious and clean, we were on the 2nd and 3rd floor and heard little noise except on one night when there was a do on and it was loud but a quick call downstairs and reception assured us it would finish at midnight, which it did.
Drinks in bar expensive $8 for a small glassof wine. $22 for a bottle- go round the corner and you could get 11/2 litres for $11, and you can buy a corkscrew from the local liquor store (open until midnight )
 Breakfast was good , $53 for Juice ,tea/coffee, bowl of fruit (to share) ,eggs,bacon ,fried potatoes and toast, for four including taxes.
 No problem getting about, walking to Times Sq enabled us to come across districts we might have missed , 46th St 8th Av-Jazz club plus 3 course meal $25. We also got the 48 hour Grayline pass, which included a free night time tour.
 Staff?! Fella on the Tours and info desk was really friendly and helpful. 
Plenty of bell boys ( yes they still call them this) but no offers to show us our room or carry our bags- and we had a tip ready.
 Bags were stored for no charge on last day , even though the notice said there was a charge of $1 per bag,
When we went to pick up the bags ,we were asked if we would like them to order a taxi to JFK For $60- we pointed out that the flat rate was $45 but the odious fella said we would have to pay tolls and tips and may have to wait a while if we tried to get one ourselves- this worried beloved so we agreed. I followed him out and he just hailed a cab and got one within a minute- deffo a scam and left an unpleasant taste after a good stay.
No problem with lifts ,always available and it was nice getting a smoking room withuot feeling like a social outcast

title: “Hipster hotel”
text: The Ace is what i call a "loud lobby" hotel - and it was insanely loud, happening and packed everytime i was through there, and dark. The rooms and hallways above though didn't hear anything. I got upgraded to an insanely large room with a bedroom so I can't judge the regular rooms, but of course I had no issues with the room which I could have thrown a party for 50 in. Vintage furnishings but clean - books, guitar, vintage fridge. the room was pretty dark and i couldn't figure out how to turn the lights on in the bedroom so i crawled around in there. Lots of nice touches but comes with a price tag. I appreciated the nice note saying how glad they were to have me, with a bottle of water, but noticed that if i actually drank the water it would cost $7. The minibar and other supplies were usual hotel premium. Didn't spend a lot of time in my large room, but I would come back here. Nice vintage vibe.

title: “Location, location, location..”
text: Me and my wife really enjoyed our stay in this hotel. It has just perfect location to explore New York on foot, or by using the Subway network. Our room was quite small, but it was very cousy and clean, and obviously very recently refurbished. Hotel was peaceful, and the daily vine reception was very nice.. We can easily recommend this hotelli to anybody visiting New York.

title: “Beautiful Hotel, Great location, mediocre service”
text: We stayed here with the kids for a long weekend in April. This was our second stay at this resort. The hotel property is beautiful and it is in a great location, close to shopping, great restaurants, Fiesta Texas. We at at Francescas and didn't care for it. The meal lasted 3 hours - we enjoy leisurely service but frankly this was ridiculous for 2 people. My room key quit working one day while we were down at the swimming pool so I had to walk through the lobby in my wet swimsuit and wait in line for a front desk clerk before I could get a replacement. (She did ask me for ID however I didn't have one with me.) The Saturday we were there we came back to our room at 3 or so and it had not been made up and cleaned. We decided to go to the pool and when we came back my son's ipod was missing. I don't know if it accidently got put in with the sheets or stolen. The hotel has been very uncooperative in dealing with this issue. Moral of the story: use the in-room safes!

title: “A pleasant surprise!”
text:
We stayed at the Residence Inn, Chicago Downtown, River North, while my husband attended a conference. The hotel is very conveniently located to all public transportation and there are many restaurants within walking distance. The room was spacious, immaculate, with all amenities. All rooms are suites, with a large sleeper couch, arm chair, full kitchen. The full kitchen was a surprise. It had full-sized refrigerator, 2 burner countertop stove, microwave, all utensils. A full, hot breakfast is served daily as well a dinner Monday-Thursday. We expected a few hors d'oeuvres but one night had lasagna, salad, bread, wine or beer, dessert. The next night was chicken Caesar salad with all the other mentioned items. Having both breakfast and dinner would certainly save a family a lot of money!
 The hotel has an exercise room and indoor pool on the top floor, free access to internet in the lounge/dining area, a very comfortable lobby and helpful staff. It shares an entranceway with Springhill Suites, another Marriott property. I don't think the guests at Springhill have the manager's dinner included in their stay.
 I would definitely stay at the Residence Inn again.

title: “Very pleasent stay - fantastic service - cool building”
text:
The Omni hotel is an amazing building. With its huge open space inside it is really a great experiance. The rooms were clean and good serviced. 
For free internet access one had to become an Omni member. It would be nice if it was included. The pool and jacuzzi at the rooftop with a fantastic view over Austin skyline is breathtaking. Disappointing that the jacuzzi was broken during my stay.
Omni's close location to Austin's 6th street makes it a perfect place to stay and hang out for the night. Even though it is downtown it was not noisy inside.
Overall this is one of my favorite hotels in Austin.

title: “One great night then two awful nights”
text:
Stayed at the W on business and it was like staying at two different hotels. Wednesday night had probably the best nights sleep at a hotel, the bed is huge, very comfortable, the blinds/curtains create a completely blackened out room, only with a small night light by the bed for a little light = perfect for sleeping on a business trip. Staff at the desk were so polite, Philip the guy from Germany was so helpful.
Thursday return to room after breakfast and room had been cleaned, well barely, sink still full of the green slime from the hand soap they provide. Thursday night was kept up by people in the neighboring room but didn't complain to reception as they went quiet around 2 am.
Friday returned from the business meeting and toilet was blocked so had to phone reception to get that sorted out, not sure what the maid had put down there but it took the guy about 5 minutes to fix it. Friday night was like a nightmare, came back to the room after enjoying the DJ on the roof top with friend. Music was being played really loud from the room next door. Called security and they quietened down. About 1 hour later the people were talking really loud still, having a small party in my room. After 5 calls to reception they got me a different room, but the guy who came up acted like I was an inconvenience to him. 
Overall had one amazing night but two terrible nights. Wouldn't recommend this place if you need to be up early for business meetings! However the desk staff were so friendly and helpful especially Philip. One more thing, they charge per computer you connect to the internet $15 each for an iPhone and a laptop gets expensive! The breakfast though expensive at the hotel is excellent.

title: “Ideal for stopover”
text:
My husband and I unexpectedly had to change our direct flight to LAX, to an in-direct via ORD. I'm really quite pleased we did!
After being checked in by a very pleasant and helpful member of check-in, we left our belongings in our room and took the train into the city from station at ORD, which happens to be directly under the hotel. Extremely convenient. 
Having spent the evening in downtown we didn't use many of the hotel's facilties, but wouldn't hesitate in staying at this hotel again. The rooms was clean, well equiped and the location was absolutely perfect for our early morning departure the next day.
Thank you Hilton :-)

title: “September 2012”
text: Checked in on Saturday September 15. Easy and friendly check .and then it was off to our room. Room was facing Petco Park. No train noise at all . All staff we encountered were very friendly and command center or whatever they call front desk was very quick responding to any needs extra towels etc. Room service, bellmen and maids top notch. Crowd was pretty wild on Saturday night but great people watching and no issues in hotel or hallways. Impressed with security measures at hotel. Love the location just cannot be beat for a hotel in the Gaslamp quarter. Waitress at pool bar on Monday Sept 17 was super friendly and made us feel like Rock Stars. Great stay !

title: “Good location”
text:
Good location midtown hotel. Less than a block to times square, yet I heard little noise despite having a room facing the street.
I stayed here as a last minute booking following being stranded in NYC following hurricane Sandy, but the hotel staff were a little unsympathetic, and unable to accommodate my request for a room with a bathtub, which I was desperate for after not having showered for 3 days.
Rooms are on the small side but that's to be expected for the location.

title: “Nice hotel and Location”
text:
We stayed for one night prior to taking an Alaskan cruise. Nice hotel although you would never know there was a hotel at this location as you see the restaurant first, then a small sign for the hotel entrance. Everyone is right about the stairs. No elevator for guests. There is a bell-person to take your bags, which was very worthwhile. 
The room is very nicely appointed. New furniture. Flat screen TV was a plus. Nice leather furniture in sitting area. But was disappointed in bathroom. Our bathroom was fairly worn. Marks on the walls and chips taken out of floor. It just didn't seem to fit with the rest of the room. Not impressed.
Location was great. You can walk a few blocks down the street and run into many restaurants. Belltown seems to be getting fixed up. Lots happening and renovations going on to a number of buildings. Easy to get to any Seattle attraction. And a $5 cab ride to the cruise ship terminal.
I probably would not stay there again.

title: “I really want to give this hotel a good review, but...”
text: Just spent 5 days in DC with hubby and kiddos (9 and 6) for spring break and to see the sights. I travel a ton for work and stay in all manner of hotels, so I have a pretty high bar, that said, if a hotel is clean, comfortable and well managed, that's pretty much all I need. I doesn't need to be fancy. So, I had high hopes for this hotel, the reviews here seemed to bode well, but it's just a little off. The good: great location, 3 block walk to subway (McPherson sq. on the blue or orange line), 5 blocks to Dupont Circle, 6 blocks to White House north lawn. Great neighborhood, very safe and comfortable walking around, tons of delicious local restaurants and 1 block to a huge Whole Foods and Starbuck's, which helped to defray the ridiculously high costs of eating on the mall (we packed a lunch almost every day). They upgraded us to a suite when we checked in. There was a fridge, microwave and coffee maker in the room, they all worked well. The bathrooms seemed new and were pretty nice. There is a bar on site that had some nice wines and wasn't too expensive. Cons: Our room was very musty and I think my daughter and I were both allergic to it. They upgraded us to a suite.. nice of them, but with 4 people (even though 2 of them are smallish) we needed 2 beds, and this room had 1 King. It did have a pull out couch, but really, when you've booked 2 queens, sleeping on a pull out couch doesn't really cut it. The whole place seemed a little run down and beat up and the attention to detail was just a little off. For instance, wiping down all the surfaces in the room. There were a lot of smudgy, grubby spots on the coffee table and bedside tables, around the fridge, etc. I ended up walking around the room with a wet washcloth and scrubbing most of the surfaces. The room heater in the wall was VERY loud and had left a pall of dusty grub on the ceiling where it blew out it's air. There was a balcony on our room, but the door and windows really didn't close very well, so I didn't feel all that secure leaving our things in the room and it got quite cold at night from the draftiness. The bed, for some odd reason, was a total pretzel maker. The pull out couch turned out to be more comfortable! Closet was just an indent in the wall with a bar on it, leaving you with a feeling of having all your clothes hanging in the middle of the room. When we were leaving, the bellman pointed my husband in the direction of the ramp to wheel the cart full of luggage out to our car instead of HELPING him (he was just standing there.) All in all.....if I was going to DC again and wanted to use points, I might stay here again, but I would sure look around at my other options. This would not be my first choice. However, it is really conveniently located and I've stayed in far worse hotels. Middle of the road to slightly shabby would be my rating.

title: “Loved, loved, loved it!!”
text: We stayed at the Pacific Terrace in early February and wish we could visit it every day! We absolutely loved the place and can not say enough great things about it. From the fantastic staff, to the spacious room to the outstanding view...I can't think of a single negative thing about it!!

title: “Delightful Stay in Boston”
text:
Our stay at the Courtyard Boston Copley Square was very enjoyable from the moment we arrived. We received a friendly greeting from the valet who parked our car, were welcomed at check-in by a courteous and efficient front desk agent, and enjoyed the comfort of a clean, spacious, and nicely designed guestroom. The hotel is convenient to shopping, restaurants, and late night entertainment and is within easy walking distance to Fenway Park.
We appreciated the friendliness of the staff and their genuine desire to provide helpful information and services that made our stay in Boston all the more pleasant and hassle-free. I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for clean, comfortable, convenient accommodations in the Copley Square area of Boston with a staff that aims to please.

title: “My worst Novotel stay ever”
text:
Staff hospitality 3/10
Room cleanliness 6/10
Room condition 5/5
Location 8/10
Business lounge 8/10
Hotel cleanliness 6/10
The worst part is the service and hospitality of the staff, which unfortunately to me are the most vital parts of a hotel.

title: “Noisy noisy noisy”
text: Impossible to sleep/rest in the morning. Every 5 minutes doors are banging, every 5 minutes you hear knocking on doors close to your room and screaming "Housekeeping, housekeeping". Walls are so thin that you hear the shower and toilet flush from your neighbours. Rooms are not very nice, outdated. Location not good, outside the hotel you get immediately aproached by beggars.

title: “Great Staff”
text: This is one of the best hotels I have stayed at because of the staff. I have never met nicer, more helpful people, and I travel a lot! Recommend it just because of them!

title: “Excellent choice”
text: This place is a triumph of design and efficient use of space. Everything in my small room was designed for ease of use and thoughtful attention to what a traveler needs. Yes, the sink is small but completely adequate; new soap is provided every day. There is a hair dryer hanging underneath. . . Bed is very comfortable, desk and chair very useable. The wall safe is big enough to store your laptop as well as anything else you want out of sight. There are large drawers built into the base of the bed, a place to hang clothes, a luggage holder, a surface to put lots of things on, out-of-the-way places on the floor for a backpack and shoes. Lighting is excellent, TV is flatscreen built into the wall, A/C cool. Only thing missing is a small refrigerator, which would be nice. Location puts you within two blocks of the Lexington subway line and two blocks another direction to the E train that takes you to Times Square and the theater district. . . There are four bathrooms on my floor, and a red signal lights up over the door inside your room to mark which ones are occupied before you leave your room. Bathrooms are also well-designed, with modern fixtures, the showers furnished with excellent shampoo and shower gel. . . Other guests ran the gamut of age, nationality, sexual orientation, couples, singles. . . The people at the front desk, the bellhop's desk, the concierge--all offered excellent service, with accurate answers to questions. . . My only complaint is--what's with the truly awful music (or any music at all) piped into the bathrooms? and the lobby (where it is louder)? Why?

title: “Prime Location-Comfort!”
text: I travel here for business very frequently. Great stay and courteous staff. Complimentary breakfast is great! Never had an issue that wasn't resolved quickly.

title: “Location Location”
text: We stayed at Hotel St James for 8 nights at the end of May and if Times Square is a priority for you this is a great location with a great price. The room was very basic, no frills, but clean. Reception not big on personality but like the room, got the job done. Noisy air con and rickerty lift but the price more than outways any negatives. At less than a block from Times Square and a great 24 hour delis either side, you can't ask for more.

title: “Good value hotel”
text:
Our room was lovely, loved the feel of it and and it was cleaned and bed made daily. Only grumble would be the loud music and subsequent late night revellers coming from the bar across the street until very late into the night. 
Staff were friendly, glad to help with advice on where to eat etc, plus we used some of the fact sheets provided at reception for finding out more about SF.
I'd agree with others about the location - while nothing bad happened to us, the huge amount of people begging and pestering you on every street corner around the hotel did make me feel a bit uneasy (but this would be the case for many hotels on this street and around Union Square). However the hotel is really conveniently located and we walked all over the city and were close to trams and buses.
Unfortunately the breakfast was not very good quality, and for the price you may as well go elsewhere - the legendary Dottie's is just around the corner and is highly recommended - just get there early!!
Overall we really enjoyed our stay - despite the few negative points, I would recommend it for a few nights, ideal for exploring the city.

title: “Attention to the detail”
text: I stay in the hotel for a long weekend and i really enjoy my stay and the service experience. In many ways the hotel service is giving attention to the detail with a relaxing and friendly manner which is my favourite. Very organized and clean rooms and friendly staff. The location is perfect with easy access on foot to many NY attractions.

title: “High Price and Low Service”
text:
We booked a Double Queen bed room in Gild Hall hotel, and we were 3 people. The service was not satisfactory because they even did not provide us with enough Shampoos, Soap. Every we were about to asked them to put these items for us. Also, the size of the room was to small in comparison to the standard of other hotels. However, the place was too convenient to all downtown areas. The breakfast was not included and the price of breakfast, lunch, and dinner was too expensive. 
The most awful thing was the speed of internet, and you have to pay 10$ per night for the internet. Seriously the speed was awful and comparable to disconnection.

title: “Luxury hotel in the middle of everything happening in DT SD!”
text:
I've stayed here before, and had a great experience. This time I can say the same thing! A beautiful hotel, close to everything, and courteous/helpful staff - you cannot go wrong. Check out their lounge on the 40th floor, you will not be disappointed!!!
Their rooms show their age a bit, but nothing that would be too bothersome; they are super clean, comfy beds, and amazing views! I would recommend they get more options for vending type needs.
If planning a trip to SD - stay here! You will not regret it.

title: “Nice Stay”
text: Excellent service and a warm and helpful staff more than make up for the lackluster rooms. The hotel staff was some the best I've encountered, the breakfast buffet was very good. Booked the corner room which had a nice city view. I would repeat.

title: “Want to return!”
text: Loved our stay (May 17 to May 19)! Check-in was easy. Got street parking in front of the hotel (lucky) which saved us $38 per night. Stayed in the superior suite which was huge (living room area and a separate bedroom). Very clean. Comfy bed. 2 tv's. Little recycling can in room for paper, glass, cans. Comfy robes to use. Hairdryer, iron in room as well as nice shampoo, conditioner, lotion. Excellent fitness center on 2nd floor. Very nice wine reception 5-6pm which was well attended. Coffee/tea/paper in am until ?9 am. Parents stayed in "motion room" which had an elliptical machine and a 2 person deep tub with jets. Staff very nice. Great location...2 blocks from Dupont Circle which has Metro. Plenty of restaurants in walking distance. FYI...great little crepe place across street for breakfast, lunch, or snack! Ate there twice! Also, there is a little convenience store across the street. Very safe area and can just stroll up and down the streets in the residential or business areas. Embassies nearby. Only complaints are that front desk did not review upgraded room rates when we checked in, and tv reception could be better. Would definitely stay there again, and in fact, will look for Kimptom hotels when we travel to other cities.

title: “Chicago At its BEST”
text: In the heart of down town chicago! Shopping, parks,public transit and great restaurants(Atwood cafe was superb)at your door steep or should say at the hotels door step. Staff was excellent and super clean hotel. No matter if Im in Chicago for visit or business i will defiantly come back to hotel Burnham.

title: “Respectfully disagree”
text: My husband, a friend and I were here earlier this month. Granted it was just for one night, but we certainly had a much different experience than the one described by Hancho. All staff, from reception to housekeeping to shuttle driver, were professional, helpful and seemed to be enjoying their jobs(!). The facility, especially considering the amount of wear and tear it must endure as an airport hotel, was well maintained. And yes, the carpets were being cleaned, a fact that was communicated to all guests. It didn't inconvenience us at all. Our two bedroom, two bathroom suite was well designed (bedrooms separated by the living space) and nicely appointed. Was it a bit pricey? Yes. Was it worth it for our group? Yes, definitely.

title: “Disorganised”
text:
The general feel of the hotel is 'fun and hip' with a lot of colour and dark lighting to create a night-club feel to it. The quality is typical of higher end Starwood hotels.
The rooms were very good and included an iPod music system which I always appreciate. The shower is one of those impractical designs where the water ends up all over the bathroom floor; it looks trendy but what a dumb idea.
The restaurant is excellent and there is a night-club in the building which had very classy clientele and appeared to be very popular.
I arrived at the check-in area which shares space with a bar with very loud music (on a Friday night). The check-in took about 40 minutes.
