The staff seemed to take an enormous amount of time with each guest as they chatted away while other people were standing in line. Rooms were not ready even at 6pm. There were a few disgruntled travelers waiting for a room and becoming short with the staff. The loud music also made it very difficult to communicate with the reception staff.
It was very important that I had 4pm late-checkout the next day and I was told it was no problem because there were plenty of rooms. However, the next day, I was disturbed no less than 5 times via door knocks and phone calls as to why I hadn't checked out.
Check-out took about 20 minutes because the receptionist could not work out how to add a mini-bar charge to the bill. Eventually she disappeared into the back-office and 10 minutes later another appeared and I had to start all over again; the first one decided it was simply too hard and gave up! The second receptionist apologised and said #1 should never have been at the front-desk because she was not trained.
The hotel has a 'hip' and 'anything is ok' attitude but they really should just hide their beads and get the job done rather than trying to live up to a 'fun' brand. Even the 'concierge' couldn't seem to arrange a taxi, and instead stood on the corner trying to wave one over. I ended up doing it myself.
If you are after a fun, laid back style of premium hotel and have time to spare, it's a good choice. If you are looking for a slick, efficient hotel, there are better choices.

title: “"Great facility and amenities"”
text: This hotel's facilities reflected their renovation, and were very pleasant. The morning breakfast, and evening supper were above average for this level of hotel, and I appreciated them very much. My room, which included a 2nd bedroom with bunkbeds, was very clean and comfortable. The wireless internet worked perfectly. The daily room servicing was detailed and made my return each evening feel like checking into a fresh room each evening. Though my schedule didn't allow for it, a larger pool and two hot tubs were a plus. The hotel even had a dedicated video game room off the pool atrium. I have stayed in numerous Residence Inns, and this one offered the best amenities with great facilities.

title: “real nice stay”
text: Had an excellent stay at our hotel. location was very convienient, only half a block fron union square and all public transportation was close. Took the BART from San Francisco airport to powell street station ($8/person one way) and walked the 4-5 blocks to the hotel. Staff was very friendly and courteous. Housekeeping staff did a great job.Concierges were very helpful on suggestions for tours to take sights to see or car rentals in the area.We strongly urge visitors to take a sightseeing tour right away just to see were everything is to plan your activities.We stayed in a deluxe double double which the room was a little tight spacewise but the bed was very comfortable. Only 1 minor problem was the ceilng fan knocked after a few minutes of use, slept with window open a few of the nights since there was no a.c.but the area around the hotel was surprisingly quiet so noise wasn't an issue. if your looking for something other than the large chain owned hotels this is a great option!

title: “Special Secret Retreat”
text: Recently returned from a trip for daughter's wedding to newly graduated Marine. Wasn't sure what to expect, but was very impressed with this quaint little inn. We stayed in the Las Palomas suite with great private balcony that overlooks Park Blvd and Balboa Park. It was very comfortable and we really enjoyed sitting on the balcony for the complimentary continental breakfast and our after dinner coffee. Staff provided us with solid recommendations for restaurants in area that were very reasonable (for San Diego). We would recommend this place to anyone who wants something different and doesn't need a luxury hotel where all the rooms look the same.

title: “Great property”
text:
Two night business visit at the start of a trip to the US
Good Points.
1. Staff are extremely friendly.and service is excellent
2. Restaurant is beautiful - I only had breakfast as a part of a package - but the food was excellent
3. Room was extremely well appointed - I was upgraded to a suite and it was very comfortable
Bad Points
1. Corridors are in need of a refurbishment
2. Spa was closed and therefore I did not get to experience the swimming pool
Wilst the restaurant on site has a bar - there is no bar scene and the hotel is more reminiscent of a very smart apartment block - where you can make best use of neighbourhood bars and restaurants
I would return sine it was very comfortable - but not my favourite

title: “A great getaway!”
text: Stayed at the W San Diego in May. The weather was still a bit chilly but it didn't effect our weekend at all! The W had fantastic service, a cool atmosphere and gorgeous rooms. We loved the rooftop beach bar and at night enjoyed drinks and a dj under the stars. We also enjoyed a dj inside with salsa dancing. During the day, we used the Acura service to go to the ocean and had some great food, drinks and shopping. I'd highly recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a fun getaway at a trendy fun hotel. Seems like the kind of place that even if you never left the hotel, you'd still have great food and fun. I'd definitely stay again.

title: “Good hotel in San Francisco”
text: My daughter and I had a long weekend here the last week of August. We paid about $160 per night before taxes for a king room. Our room was on the 9th floor and had a decent view. The bed was very comfortable and there was a good selection of channels on the tv. The shower had good water pressure and temperature and the bathroom was large. The sink is located outside of the bathroom, which makes it convenient for one person to shower while the other is person is putting on makeup and drying hair. We used the hot tub and indoor pool, located on the 2nd floor, one night and it was very enjoyable. The fitness center looked nice but we didn't use it. There is a Starbuck's inside the hotel, as well as a bar which we didn't go to. The hotel is located about 1 mile from the Ferry Building and a few blocks away from the Westfield Center and other shopping opportunities. The Bart station is about a 10 minute walk and you can take it directly to SFO airport for a little less than $8.50 per person. There is also a wonderful pizza place called Napoli's that will deliver to the hotel - get the phone number from the front desk. Our only complaint was that one day housekeeping did not replenish the hand towels or wash clothes but other than that, everything was great.

title: “Good place to stay.”
text: Stayed three days, two nights at the Hyatt Place on the Riverwalk. As others have said, the room is large with add'l sofa bed and 42" flat screen tv, microwave and small refrigerator - all good amenities. The bathroom was small and the exhaust fan was loud, but not enough to make me want to move to another room. The a/c was somewhat loud, but not enough to keep me awake at night. The walk to the restaurants and bars on the riverwalk was, in my opinion, pretty far when considering walking in the 100+ degree heat. However, the free parking provided offsets that con for me. The continental breakfast offered was my speed as I'm not a big breakfast eater, but they had good variety just the same. Overall, a good stay. Will be back in two weeks.

title: “just not great”
text:
The views were tremendous, the location was excellent but I was disappointed with the hotel in general. We were told at check in that our credit card would be charged an additional $200 a night in case of any damage that may happen during our stay. I've never had this before and thought that this was a touch pretentious. When I got up to the room, I was generally underwhelmed. Considering that we had just been charged an additional $400 for the 2 night stay, I was disappointed to see that the furnishings were scrappy, all bashed up and marked. The dresser that held the minibar looked so tired and out of place. The wet room was awful, as it didn't drain properly, which meant that following your shower, 20 minutes later when you brush your teeth you're lucky not to break your neck on the slippery floor.
I proposed earlier in the day to my girlfriend and so wanted to head up to the rooftop bar for a few cocktails to celebrate. Took the lift to the top to be told that we had to leave the hotel, and re-enter via the side entrance, where we had to present ID then have our hands stamped. A little excessive - we went elsewhere.
Overall expensive considering the small room size, and not as polished as i would have hoped for such a new hotel.

title: “The people watching was so much fun!”
text: We started our Thanksgiving in Granbury at the Nutt Hotel then drove on to the Stockyards Hotel. Being a holiday, there were people there from all over the world and what fun to meet land talk to people in the lobby. There was a large group checking in from Germany when we walked in. This is a perfect place to hang your hat then go to the rodeo and on to Billy Bob's. Now, get ready for noise from local bars and the hotel is OLD but it is worth it all. Be sure and eat breakfast next door... Super place.

title: “Internet, Pool & Location Big Draws”
text:
The Sheraton Boston was a pleasant surprise. I'd felt a bit hoodwinked by priceline when I bid on a 4 star and received the Sheraton, whose own front desk manager told me was only a 3 star property. However, my stay was delightful, and the location within the Prudential Center complex was fantastic.
The room itself was large and bright with a great view of Boston Harbor, and the king-sized bed was of average comfort. The bathroom had a great vanity counter, but the towels were a bit on the rough side. Sundries provided were basic, and the shower had moderate to weak water pressure. 
The fitness center charges a daily or stay rate, and the pool alone is free. There are sparsely scheduled pay as you go classes across the street in a gym somewhere in yoga and step, but none were offered during my down time. 
The lobby has both free internet kiosks for guests, as well as WiFi for those with their own laptops. Boarding passes can be printed at a special kiosk, but any other printing or business needs are available at a business center upstairs in the conference center. 
This property is huge and geared towards conventions, but the staff was friendly and helpful. Cabs within in Boston are cheap! It was $5 including tip to go to the theater across town! 
The subway, the "T", is located in the Prudential Center, and the ride to and from the airport took about 25-30 minutes terminal to hotel. A bus at the terminal takes you to the "T" and drops you back at any of the terminals at Logan. This is probably the quickest, and cheapest, way to get in and out of Boston. Parking is exorbitant in the city, so if you're flying, take the "T" and walk. 
Newbury Street shops and restaurants are conveniently located to the Sheraton, and the Prudential Center Mall has just about anything imaginable all under one roof.

title: “5 Star hotel, only 3 star service”
text:
As others have said the lobby is beautiful and does get full around the duck parades, which is a bit of a shame for the paying guests, but that's the way it goes I suppose.
We had tried to book direct with the hotel but found that they never responded to e-mails sent to them unless you had someone's direct e-mail address, if you wish to contact them best to do it by phone.
Our stay didn't get off to the best start as when we arrived at reception we were told that they had no record of our booking! Given that we'd flown all the way to Memphis to get married this was not what we wanted to hear! The hotel staff blamed our tour operator for all faults with our booking, however as some of my family had booked with other tour operators to us and also had issues this excuse looks a little weak, the common denominator was the hotel. After about 30 minutes of heated exchange (including with the duty manager) the staff did eventually come good and check us in with a free room upgrade, so well done for rescuing the situation. For the reception staff, Desirae was excellent, the others we found to be quite offhand and even rude (not a good check out!) and quite frankly we expected better from a "5 star" establishment. 
The Concierges were friendly however their information could be a little out of date (was given directions to a cafe that had closed down) but this is a trifling thing and is forgivable.
Some of our family and friends did say that the noise from the streets did disturb them on some nights (particularly the weekend) but we didn't really find this to be a problem.
Bar staff were on the whole very courteous but service did get slow when the bar fills up a bit.
The lifts were a bit of a problem, fine at the start of our stay but by the end only 2 out of the 4 were working which meant looooooong waits for everybody. As we were staying up on the 10th floor, the stairs weren't really an option. This problem was exacerbated on the Thursday night which as others have pointed out is party night up on the roof. If this were limited to hotel guests only it might not be so bad but the hotel floods with visitors heading up and down in the lifts so be prepared for disruption. (Also we found the bands down on Beale Street to be more to our liking but this I accept is just down to personal taste).
I should point out that none of the above ruined our stay, however I can't help but feel that the hotel is a bit over-priced and as a result would probably look elsewhere if visiting again (there is a Holiday Inn directly across the street, thereby sharing the great location)

title: “Good enough.”
text:
We stayed at The Lenox for one night. We arrived late at night and left early, we really only needed a bed for the night. The room we got was very good value for the price. The neighbourhood is good, with many shops and restaurants nearby. We had dinner in the old part of Boston and it's too far to walk. 
The room was nice. The window pointed to the next wall, but that didn't worry us. The bathroom was very small, though. That's the only real drawback and annoyed us a little. Otherwise a nice stay.

title: “A great oasis in New York”
text: It is not fancy but still comfortable and clean. The staff is amazing. They solved all our problems with efficiency and politeness. It was scorching hot in NY and returning to the hotel was a relief. We enjoyed staying in the "salon" to cool off with all the other guests . A great hotel!

title: “Too many problems for a one night stay...”
text:
I'm here at the Skyline for one night only, for an expo at Javits on a week night. I stay in NYC all the time and this hotel needs help.
Concierge is rude, check-in clerk barely spoke engligh (kind of a problem for a hotel check-in clerk!), floor in room smells horrible - like dirty feet, girls stuck in elevator, shower barely gets hot enough, A/C is very cranky.
I dont recommend this place. There are much better hotels for a better value. Really, don't bother.
The location, however, is great.

title: “JW Marriott LA Live”
text:
Located adjacent to the Staple Center and Nokia Theater, the JW Marriott and Ritz-Carlton hotels are the perfect place to stay if your travels take you to Downtown Los Angeles. Within the LA Live complex are a number of restaurants that will meet your needs. Fleming's Steak House is always fantastic, excellent happy hour there as well, reservations for dinner a must (use Open Table). The Palm Steakhouse is about two blocks away, as well. Wolfgang Puck has an excellent Italian restaurant all in all, about 8 great eateries. If you are not a local, or even if you are, you must eat at The Original Pantry, been open at the original location 24/7 since 1921. GREAT breakfast, ham&cheese omelet is to die for, mountain of fried potatoes and sourdough bread/toast. Comfort food all day/night. Located one block away. Large multi-pled movie theater next door to complex.
The JW Marriott has an excellent restaurant located right next to two of their full service bar and wine bars. Great drinks and excellent bar bites. A very lively scene, but comfortable. The rooms are all contemporary design and furnishing. Large showers and comfy beds. The Concierge Level lounge is excellent, one of the best I have visited at a Marriott. The only downside is the outrageous fee for underground parking, about $40 bucks a night, so keep that in mind if you intend in driving there. Within the same building is the Ritz-Carlton hotel. I have not stayed, but if you do, all of the above is available. Within the Ritz-Carlton is a new Wolfgang Puck Asian restaurant and bar, located on the 32nd floor or so. Killer view of Los Angeles. Even if you don't dine, it is a must for cocktails in the evening. This complex is fantastic if you travel to the downtown area for a concert, Laker/Clipper basketball game or other event. Probably the best hotel complex in all of downtown Los Angeles.

title: “Nice location, small hotel, average but fine”
text:
The hotel is easy to find if you go in and out of Grand Central. Leave through the 42nd St. exit, turn left, go three blocks, cross the street, and check in. Too close for a cab. One problem was getting cabs from there without luggage... they prefer to go down the street and maybe get a Grand Central person going to the airports. 
My room was small, but not terribly small. I had a desk and a chair and a flat screen TV. Clean enough and overlooked an airshaft in which people were doing renovations, so I never opened the shades. Dark. The bathroom was nothing luxurious, but the free internet for Honors guests is always appreciated. I also received a continental breakfast coupon for the morning, which was ample and a nice touch.
There are two banks of elevators and each services a side of the building. Not many rooms per floor per elevator so it was small and mostly quiet. I was shocked, however, that my room was adjacent to the most active linen and supply room in the world. It was entered and used all night, and each time the door was banged shut with little thought to the person paying three hundred plus dollars a night for a small dark place to sleep a foot away. That was disappointing.
I'd stay again if I were pressed for lack of other locations, but this is not my first choice Hilton in NY...

title: “Superb!”
text: If you choose Drake in Chicago, you will do the right thing. It comfort, luxuries, and in ideal position in the City, as for exploring by foot or to do a business. It is in a hart of town, near all landmarks and it provide superb service.

title: “Fantastic hotel, fantastic location”
text:
Just came back from a fantastic 4 night stay at this hotel. The room was very clean and spacious, with 2 double beds. Plenty of drawer and cupboard space, iron and ironing board, wall safe and hairdryer. Shower and bath were great with plenty of hot water always available. Our room faced 8th Ave, but it was still nice and quiet. The hotel also has free wi-fi available in the room, if you have an iphone or laptop with you.
Location is excellent. Only a 5-10 minute walk from Times Square and right next to a subway station. Just a block away from some great restaurants on 9th Ave and a few minutes from many of the great theatres.
Free breakfast was excellent, although get there quite early to avoid the long queues. Plenty of choice available - 6 different types of cereal, fresh fruit (both as fruit salad and whole fruit), juices, breads and pastries and one hot choice (bagel topped with cheese and ham, omelette, turkey sausage, to name a few). There are also free "breakfast on the go" bags consisting of water, fruit, muffin and a cereal bar. Free tea and coffee is always available in the lobby, as is more fresh fruit.
There is a little shop in the lobby for souvenirs, soft drinks and sweets. There are also 2 free internet machines. Apparantly there is also a small gym in the hotel, but I didn't use this. (I was on holiday!!)
All the staff were very friendly and helpful and can't be faulted.
All-in-all, an excellent hotel that I would highly recommend.

title: “Very Satisfied (for second time)”
text: My wife and I have just returned from our second stay at this hotel. Each visit has been for a full week. Our first stay was in April 2002; our second stay in late September/early October 2004 cost almost exactly double--an encouraging sign, I suppose, that New York tourism is prospering once again. We feel that the Quality Hotel is worth every penny even at the higher rate. Rooms small but clean and comfortable. Had small frig both times. Bathrooms shiny and new but be careful on those darn tile floors. 94th Street sounds remote but in practice not a problem at all. There are bus stops and an express subway stop almost at the door--you can be anywhere in no time--we made it one day to the Staten Island ferry in just 25 minutes. There is a real neighbourhood feel to the area that is a refreshing change after a day in the more boisterous tourist-clogged areas. Safe walking area even at night, people sitting out on the boulevard benches at midnight. Good, reasonably-priced restaurants abound in this area. Key West Diner on ground floor of hotel open all hours and has intriguing Manhattan staff and clientele, excellent, cheap breakfasts, though other meals more variable. Also a Tex-Mex place right in hotel but we didn't try it. People often complain, in particular, of two things at New York budget hotels--lousy elevators and lousy windows/views. Here this place shines: there are four elevators (we have never had to wait more than a minute) and both our rooms have had big windows overlooking not a neighbouring wall or air shaft but a sunfilled street view and a beaut of a view, too, Broadway at its Upper West side widest, with a boulevard full of trees and flowers. Staff seemed reasonably courteous and efficient: wakeup calls made as requested, early morning cab call made as requested, and a plugged toilet fixed one morning between time we left for breakfast and our return.

title: “Nicely Renovated!”
text: I found the staff to be extremely attentive and helpful. The in room service was excellent, along with breakfast buffet. The hotel is located close to the airport; which the hotel provides complimentary shuttle service to the airport. I would definitely stay here again. The bed was extremely comfortable with nice linens. Lovely 37in. LCD TV was a nice touch. Overall a good hotel. However, the room appeared to be dated.

title: “stay away”
text: I got a room here for the NYC marathon. I was not expecting a lot, but I thought some basic things like hot water would be included. I had to take a cold shower because the hot water was out on the 6th floor. When I went to complain the hotel would not move me to a different room or give me a discount. The rooms looked horrible, the carpet was so old I was afraid to walk on it with out shoes. Stay far away from this hotel, you would be better off sleeping in a tent in central park.

title: “great value and location”
text: reasonable rate for family of four (approx. $149) in a great location. Room was very comfortable and clean. In room internet was a little slow, but this was not our priority. Several convenient stores located near hotel for family snacks and quick meals ( CVS, subway, bread/bagel store). One week day there was a farmers market a few blocks from the hotel (maybe it was Thursday?) Great location, easy to walk to most sights.

title: “Excellent excellent hotel”
text: Cannot recommend this hotel highly enough. We had no problems whatsoever. This was our second stay in this particular hotel and once again it did not dissapoint. Fantastic location, the hotel is situated between 5th Avenue and Times Square about two minutes from 5th, yet the street is completely quiet. I would describe the rooms as 5 star business class, they are immaculate and very very comfortable. There are no words to describe how great the beds are! They put a duvet under the sheet as well as over. Room service was lovely but I wouldn't recommend the restaurant, purely because its a bit quiet and there are so many great restaurants within minutes of the hotel (highly recommend http://www.osteria-doge.com/ if you want super romantic mid price italian) . Hotel also has handy business centre with internet and printer just off the lobby which was useful. The lobby is quite small, not the kind you'd hang out in or have a drink in but you dont really go to New York to hang out in the hotel, do you? Really recommend the end of November as a good time to visit as prices are cheap after the Thanksgiving rush and you get to see all the Christmas lights being turned on (and great sales!)

title: “Good Location”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights on first leg of our USA holiday. Excellent location. Short stroll to Fishermans Wharf. Friendly reception. Did not have our correct room available on first night (though did arrive at 1am) but moved us the next day to an excellent room with a great view of the Wharf and Alcatraz. Would def stay here again. Denny's restaurant integral to the building and open 24 hours also very convenient for breakfast etc.

title: “Great family hotel”
text: I´ve spent 5 days with my family at this hotel, the staff was very friendly they even received a package I had delivered to the hotel and kept it for me, the rooms are very functional with a full kitchen inside great for a little saving. The complementary breakfast was good but the better parts is that they are flexible with the schedule, they even had some snacks on the evening. Pool and Gym are very nice small but nice, and also there's a barbecue area you can use. I would really recommended is a great deal.

title: “Best 30th birthday ever!!”
text: My Boyfriend and I have just arrived back from a 5 day holiday in NYC. This was a present for my 30th Birthday and we spent a while checking reviews for good hotels. We eventually decided on the Hotel Metro from the good reviews it received. My boyfriend was a bit dissapointed when he looked at the photos people had added, but when we arrived he could not have been more surpised, the hotel was lovely, very clean, amazing location (2 minutes walk to Macys, 10 mins to time square, roof top view of empire state) Our room was perfect just the right size (the tv had a dodgy reception but who watches tv when they are in the city that never sleeps) the bathroom did not have a bath but the shower was perfect and the complimentary goodies in the bathroom were great ! the rooms were cleaned daily and the staff were very helpful and friendly (they even put a little card in my room and some choccies wishing me a happy birthday) The Complimentary breakfast is really nice and great to fill you up for a days sightseeing. One thing to remember this hotel is located very centrally and gets very noisy at night, bring your earplugs if you can't sleep through noise (my fella got woken at 4:50am by road diggers !!!) All in all though we couldnt have made a better choice and will recommend this hotel to anyone !

title: “Fool me once........”
text: Tried back again after getting a discount for problems during the last try. Called ahead to get an early check-in, was told no problem the suite would be ready. Got the key, went upstairs to find the room was still not made. Back down to the front. Had to wait 30-60 mins. for everything to get done. Room smelled like cigarette smoke, even though it is a no-smoking room. Still very noisey at night. The breakfast was nothing to write home about, and there were no local papers. Fool me once..................... .

title: “Excellent location and price”
text: The rooms are a little old and they have no free WIFI. The price to get WIFI was very expensive and you could only connect one computer. The front desk was helpful and nice. The location is excellent and the kitchen clean, complete and useful.

title: “Not Renaissance Quality or Value - Never Coming Back”
text:
I travel weekly and depend on Marriott to provide a quality stay - Renaissance is usually a step above the traditional Marriott properties. This hotel is an embarassment to the family of hotels! The service was terrible - room service trays were left in the hall for days, the bathroom was worn and the wood on the door was chipped, and there was no working clock in my room. Hot water was non existent and the room service food was a disappointment.
At more than $250 per night for a conference, this was a big disappointment. It may have history, but if it is not comfortable and providing good service and value, I won't be coming back.

title: “Less than Impressed”
text:
Not at all impressed. We booked this place as friends coming to Chicago for the first time. Its location is excellent, but that is all I will give it. We had booked a room with two beds and got here and were told they had none of them left and we would have to share a bed. I like my friend, but not that much! when we told the guy at the front desk we had booked two beds and we also had it on our email confirmation he said "oh those confirmations can be misleading." Um, how so? If I book and pay for something then that is what I am expecting to get. The rooms are TINY and the bathroom is as well. There was hair on the bathroom floor when we got there as well as a massive one in the bathtub and the walls and doors desperately need a paint job. There is nowhere to store anything in the bathrooms. Our bed was VERY soft -so much so that our backs hurt in the morning. The biggest issue we had was the sheet on the bed. It did not fit! I only went to the end of the mattress but did not go over the end. We accepted this for night one and then night two complained. The manager was very nice and had it fixed for us for night two. Night three it was back to the short sheet (they dont use fitted sheets!) and the top sheet had dried blood on it and so for night four I complained again and got it fixed by a woman with no teeth who was shouting at me in spanish!
The elevator is TINY so you often have to wait for a few runs to get on one. Especially in the morning as we waited almost 20 minutes for one with our luggage. There are no fridges in the room which I was annoyed about but I guess there is nowhere to put one! The in room iron left a mark on my friends new shirt. They are VERY skimpy on supplies. For two females staying there, they gave us one bar of soap (which we used for the handsink) as well as two small bath towels and a foot towel. This is what I would expect for one person staying, not two.
Outside of that, the location is excellent. It is within walking distance of everything you would want to see and do in downtown Chicago. You have to pay for internet in your room but you can use it for free in the lobby. I never had any issues with the speed as it always worked fine for us. the front desk staff in the day were helpful and polite but the evening ones we found to be extremely rude and unhelpful.
Overall, if I were to come to Chicago again, I would not stay here as I would want somewhere of a better quality.

title: “Avoid Pacific Beach”
text: We are a family of four who stayed at the Pacific Terrace for 3 nights. I cannot believe that other posts do not list the overriding fact that the area of Pacific Beach is a complete dump and not family friendly. It is a mix of collge nightclubs, run down motels, surf dives, and delapidated shops. The crowd is college party drinkers, homeless, and way-way out of towners (foreign/Michigan). Our guest's car was broken into the second night and the hotel would net help offset the costs of fixing the smashed window, they did not even check on us for the rest of our stay. The room was late in being ready at check-in, the concierge was completely wrong about availability of road bikes at their rental outlets, the hotel restaurant recommendations are the ones that are closest, and the whole thing has the feel of a motel with an expensive facelift. The price ($350/night) for a premium view room makes it seem as if the area, facilities, services will be high-end--this is not at all the case. BTW, the beach is across from the hotel but you have to go down a 30-foot bluff to get there--just don't get hit by a bike or trip over a homeless guy to get there.

title: “June 6-9 2004 excellent location”
text: Stayed at Doubletree Suites for 3 nights in NYC. The location is excellent and the security is great would stay at doubletree again. (but stay out of the mini bar a can of diet coke is $3.50 )

title: “Absolutely Fabulous!”
text: My partner and I stayed at the Royalton in November, from the moment we arrived to the time we checked out we had an absolutely wonderful time. The hotel is stylish yet comfortable, the staff were helpful and welcoming and you couldn’t ask for a better location – a short walk away from so many of New York’s major attractions. We loved New York and this fantastic hotel was just the icing on the cake! 

title: “Comfortable, very convenient to transit, quiet”
text: Good value, rooms are small and comfortable/functional. Not the most memorable neighborhood in New York, the commercial heart of mid-town, but hop on to the subway and find yourself anywhere in a flash.

title: “Highly recommended”
text:
Although our stay was a freebie using points, everyone treated us like paying guests. Omar greeted us at the desk, had our Priority Club check-in ready to go, and provided concise tips on restaurants and attractions within walking distance. The pay valet (one price all day with in-and-out privileges) was superb; quick and courteous, and the valet even recognized us later that day as we approached his stand. He pulled our keys and retrieved our car quickly.
The room was spacious, clean, and everything was in perfect order. The only caveat is to try to avoid rooms overlooking the street. Highland is busy ALL THE TIME and some street noise does make it through closed windows.
The included breakfast had good variety and was well-maintained. Housekeeping was thorough with no missing actions during our 3 night stay.

title: “The Finest Hotel Experience - Ever”
text: My partner and I have traveled to many countries around the world and I must say we have never experienced such a welcoming and accomodating team as yours at The Donatello. We were made to feel completely at home. Special Kudos go to Jesus at the Front Desk. He became our friend and exceeded our expectations EVERY time. He is truly a superb representative of your organization. You entire team is very well crossed-trained, as they constantly filled in for each other if their colleagues were busy at the time. An example was the night security guard registering our car while the parking attendant wasserving another customer. Or the bellman showing us several rooms from which to choose. The Donatello is our favorate place on earth!! - Tony & Arthur

title: “Great service, nice room”
text: I stayed at Hotel Allegro Chicago this past weekend to attend a friend's son's wedding. I was among 80 guests from Boston. Prior to arriving I joined the members program, which I find helps in getting the type of room and amenities I request. I requested a room on a high floor & indeed ended up in a room w/King bed on the 18th fl (hotel has 19 fls). It was away from the elevators & vending machines as requested. The room was not overly large yet suffice for 1 person or a couple. It was clean. Bathroom somewhat small w/small sink. What made the difference in this hotel was the wonderful service from all the staff--from the doormen, to desk, to concierge, waitstaff--everyone gave a smile, accommodated my requests & took exceptionally good care of all of us--as individuals and part of this group. We were delighted. The coffee in the lobby in the am & wine hour in the afternoon are very nice touches this hotel offers to their guests. Just as we were getting on the bus to take us to the wedding venue, the skies opened up with pouring rain, thunder & lightening. The hotel was able to provide us with umbrellas so we wouldn't get soaked in our beautiful dresses & sandals. They did take our room numbers to ensure they would be returned,but hey--we were grateful since we there was no indication of a storm coming & it helped keep us dry. I think this was a great hotel & having never been to Chicago before can't wait to return to this great city & this nice hotel. Finally, they offered a late checkout at 5 pm at an additional low cost that is worth it if you are staying for most of the day.

title: “Good location!”
text: My family stayed here for the weekend and nothing spectacular but great location to everything. Cost was a bit high but it is SF so I understand, rooms were nicely kept up and we enjoyed our short visit.

title: “Nice Room and great location!”
text: Room was very clean and pristine, bathrooms clean and pristine. Placed order night before for breakfast room service and time to be delivered. My grandson eats as soon as he wakes up and food delivered at exactly time I requested to be delivered. Good tasty food. My suggestion is to request to stay at the back of hotel, rooms at front have alot of street noise. The location is great close to Union Square, taxis available,Walgreens across the street, and Starbucks close by.Staff was helpful and friendly, when my reservation was booked incorrectly, but resolved quickly.

title: “RAFINO”
text: While I understand the "ambiance" of a 100 year old hotel, I don't think one should have to suffer because of it. My spouse required the use of a wheel chair but there is only one exit point which entials walking almost a block to an exit. Someone forget to clean our room one day and left only one bath towel the day before. While the staff was genuinely interested in our well being, they unfortunately have a 100 year old hotel that crys to be renovated.

title: “Absolute luxury”
text:
Stayed at the hotel over the Easter weekend with 2 friends as a treat for my birthday. The hotel is fantastic. Really luxurious. The staff are very friendly and always helpful whether they are recommending places to visit or simply calling a taxi for you. The hotel rooms are lovely, huge tv, loads of room, very nice toiletries left every day in the bathroom, enormous fluffy white towels and the most comfortable hotel beds I've ever slept in. We were left chocolates every night and the night before Easter Sunday we were each left a Lindt Chocolate Bunny. Such a nice touch. 
The location is excellent on Madison Avenue between 50th and 51st and right opposite St Patricks Cathedral.
I would love to go back again.!!!!

title: “Quaint is the word”
text:
Wonderful old world decor and ambience.
Tea in the afternoon in front of the fireplace.
Chess parlor.
Rooms are beautiful, but dilapidated (in just the right way)
Breakfast was perfect...great fruit, yogurt, breads.. ( no preformed microwaved sausage thank you)
Management is completely unobtusive.
Short walk to Union Street, have a scotch or three at the Bus Stop.
A great place.

title: “Highly recommended!! Great staff !! Great service!!”
text: We took our children for a getaway for their summer vacation. This is the third Embassy we've visited. We have had a great experience at each Embassy but this location was the best. The staff was so nice! From the time we arrived to the time we left they were so professional and friendly. Whenever we passed a staff member in the hall or interacted with them in any way, they were alway pleasant and smiling. That really counts for something nowadays because good customer service is hard to find. The rooms were very neat and well decorated. The view was so beautiful and relaxing...it made you want to sit and kick back and not worry about a thing. The indoor pool was really nice with an all around view of the outdoors, it was like the best of both worlds. The Manager's Reception offered more than we expected. There were complimentary drinks for the adults and children, not to mention the greatly prepared hot finger foods, fresh fruit and other nicely prepared snacks. Oh and that breakfast! Unbelievable! By far the best breakfast we've had at any hotel. I have paid for food at nice restaurants that wasn't a good as what we we're served. I had an omlete made to order that was so huge I could barely finish it...and it was soooo good. It's hard to say what I liked most about the experience because everything was so great! I guess I can say that the staff and the services they provided made everything exceptional. This is by far the best money I've ever spent on a hotel.

title: “Fantastic location...”
text: I read a lot of these reviews before we went to Chicago, and they only succeeded in making me nervous about what we were getting into. I was traveling with my family - which includes a six and a nine year old, and all the negative reviews gave me some concern...however, once we arrived nearly all of those concerns went out the window. People have to keep in mind that this hotel is over 100 years old...is it a bit run down? Sure. But it was clean and the location is perfect for a downtown visit. We walked nearly everywhere on our brief visit to Chicago.,.the museum campus is close, and we walked to the Shedd aquarium and Field museum (by the way you MUST take advantage of buying tickets online for the Shedd - we walked right past the line that others waited over two hours in), we walked to Millennium Park, the Magnificent Mile shopping, and even Navy Pier (a little too far for the kids - but a ten dollar cab ride back). Buddy Guy's Legends is less than two blocks away and a must visit for blues fans (I saw Buddy himself perform there the night I went). Bottom line is you are paying for the fantastic location in downtown Chicago. Be aware that the building is old and temper your expectations...we only stayed in the hotel to sleep anyway. The staff was helpful and cheerful, and our only issue was that our coffee pot in our room clogged up, which was easily fixed. Remember that most people who take the time to write a review are probably upset and venting a complaint...ignore the nitpickers and the ridiculous ghost stories and stay here for the great location.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
This was our first visit to Dallas, and whilst is was not the easiest hotel to find, it turned out to be quite convenient. Just a short drive to downtown. The hotel and room were new and well appointed, the room was large with a comfortable king size bed, large writing desk and lounger. All were very clean and tastefully decorated. 
The breakfast was typical of similar grades of hotel, but nothing special. My only complaint was that the staff, whilst being very courteous and enthusiastic, could benefit from a little more training on the local area and on the business side of things. Even the manager could not send an international fax. Only other point I would raise, is that there are no restaurants close by the hotel.

title: “Excellent hotel and great staff”
text:
We stayed at the Sofitel for 4 nights and our experience was great from start to finish. The staff at check-in were very helpful and the room was very modern and clean and exceeded expectations. A few small thoughtful touches like delivering chilled water in the evening to your room make all the difference. The pool area is nice if small but we managed to get seats (not lounger) even at weekend and is well staffed to cater if you need drinks or snacks.
The location of the hotel is good as it's opposite the Beverly Centre and only 10 mins in a taxi to The Grove and Farmers market. There is a hop on/off bus stop opposite the hotel so if you don't want to hire a car (as we didn't) then you can utilise the one day or two day pass to get around L.A., Santa Monica etc.

title: “nice independent in downtown boston”
text: I'm developing a love affair with independent hotels. This is a small, independent property in the Back Bay area only a block away from the convention center hotels charging a heck of a lot more. We arrived way early but they had a room available and checked us in at 11:00 AM! Rooms are smallish but this is a big city, so what else is new? They must use a hiring profile that emphasizes youth and enthusiasm because everyone we encountered from check in to check out was young, positive, competent and engaged.

title: “What a lovely hotel!”
text: I was lucky enough to spend one night here and wish it could have been more. The front desk staff couldn't have been more helpful and wanted to make sure that if I had any questions, they were answered. Beautiful lobby area. The room on the top floor was furnished in understated elegance with every possible amenity. It was a sweltering 100 degree day in New York and the a/c worked like a charm. Immaculate room, corridors and lobby. They even had a bottle of water and fresh fruit waiting for me in my room. I'd stay again in a second.

title: “Great location”
text: Hotel is lovely rooms are a bit dated however location is great 2 min walk to fifth ave 5 min walk to time square everything you need is around this hotel . You can buy your breakfast from the lobby bar where they serve Starbucks coffee and fresh fruits and pastry cereal smoothies etc overall cannot wait to go back .

title: “Very comfortable and great location”
text: We stayed at this hotel for four nights on the ground floor overlooking the marina in early October. Our experience echoes the many other very positive reviews. While the property is getting a little dated, it proved to be excellent value and the location cannot be beaten. It was quiet, with great views and so close to all of the main attractions and downtown. Breakfast was typical buffet and we would a have liked to see some yogourt occasionally (may be there but we never found it). We parked across the street which was very convenient. This avoided the hotel's very narrow spaces on the ground level or manoeuvring into the underground as well as saving the $5 daily charge. Excellent restaurants in the immediate area that we tried included Pomodor Ristorante (2833 Avenida De Portugal), Hunphreys dining room and Solare. We would definitely return when back in SD..

title: “Comfortable rooms, loud lobby”
text: Three of us stayed at the W hotel on Lexington Ave in July. I booked on Priceline.com. We were three and needed two beds, When I called the W they said the Priceline rooms were single bed rooms. They agreed to give us a room with two beds but there was an extra charge. When we arrived the front desk told us there would be no extra charge for the room. The room was not ready, and we were given vouchers for the bar to wait while they prepared the room. Every staff member we encountered was friendly, helpful and polite. The average rating is because of the lobby. There wasn't any place to sit, relax and talk. In the evening there was a DJ who cranked up the music to hurtful levels. In the morning there was music piped in that, at least, in my opinion was unnecessary. Along with the usually background noise of people checking in and out it was unfortunately not a place you could sit down after a busy day of sightseeing. The W is a good place to stay only on block from the subway and on the Lex Ave bus line. In an already noisy city it would have been nice to walk into a lobby that offered a toned down atmosphere.

title: “Great stay”
text: Nice location, worthy of rating on trip advisor. Homely feel to rooms and hotel. Staff very helpful and add little touches to your stay that makes this place great. I would like to visit again and stay for longer in New York and I wouldn't hesitate in booking at the casablanca again.

title: “Great Experience--No Complaints”
text:
We stayed at the Hampton Inn Times Square North for three nights. I found a great rate through the hotel's own website (under $120/night) for a king room. The hotel is non-smoking and they include free breakfast and internet in their rate.
The breakfast selections were very good and plentiful. They included a couple of hot items like waffles and sausage and other continental items such as breads, fresh fruit, cereal, yogurt, pastries, juice, milk, coffee, tea, and hot chocolate. Not gourmet, but it gets you on your way and saves you a bit of money and time. The workers overseeing breakfast replenshined everything over and over again.
The room was very large, especially by big-city standards; the bathroom had enough counter space for two people; there was an in-room safe; the wireless Internet was very good the whole time; we didn't notice a lot of noise from outside or the hotel itself; t he bed was comfy; and maid service was timely.
The location is very good for getting around Manhattan; there are subway stops within a one-block walk; and a drug store is also a block away; there were also some good restaurants nearby.
Overall, we enjoyed our stay and would gladly return.

title: “Nice option...downtown.”
text:
I've stayed in this neighborhood a few times, so I took a chance on the Fairfield Inn for one night. As a platinum elite, I would have expected a nicer/larger room or possibly a suite, but I was stuck in a corner room that seemed "small" to me. The room layout was enteryway, straight ahead to small sink (with very little counter space) - then a small bathroom; to the left was the drawers and bed/bedroom. Even though the room was small and hard to manuever around, everything was functioning and there was minimal street noise. The neighborhood was nice, tons of mid-level food offerings are steps away. 
The free breakfast in the morning was adequate, but there were quite a few people, so seating was limited. I ate quickly and departed. Service was good. The staff is very friendly. 
Overall, I'd give this an average, just because I expect a little more space in a room and I was not "wowed".

title: “Stay at your own risk!”
text: My family and I stayed at Town & Country Resort this past weekend for the Cal State games. Terrible experience!! The reservation staff gave wrong information regarding using a debit card. We asked for extra towels and never received them. Had to call multiple times so my kids could have towels to use when getting out of the shower. Kids running all through the halls! When we called to complain, we were told sorry we couldnt find them when in fact the security guard specifically spoke to them. The noise continued and I asked to be moved to a different floor, to no avail. We were told we would receive complimentary continental breakfast which was completely FALSE! Wrong information all the way around. Terrible place to stay and the staff is not helpful at all with the exception of Janet in the Lost & Found. Stay at your own risk!!!

title: “BW Hollywood”
text: We chose this hotel for its proximity to the Greek Theatre. We found it reasonably clean and comfortable; we were given a large 2dbl room with kitchen for $129; unfortunately it overlooked the 101 freeway. If staying here again I would ask for one of the (possibly smaller) rooms in the second building that surround the pool. Free underground parking and great coffee shop with Hollywood hours: 7AM - 3AM!

title: “Somewhat overrated”
text: I don't know if it is because we moved here after three nights at the impeccable Westin Jersey City Newport, but this hotel was somewhat of a letdown and we couldn't wait to get back to the Westin for our last two nights. We spent four nights at the Affinia Gardens and were offered a king with a bedsofa as opposed to the double queen we had booked as our room was not ready when we arrived. That was after I had politely declined the offer of paying USD40/night for upgrade to a junior suite. Not a problem because if the queen beds were as uncomfortable as the king bed, then we were grateful to have the bedsofa! If all four of us could have fitted in the double bedsofa, we would all have slept there to avoid waking with stiff necks and backs! The bathroom was a very pleasant surprise because, although compact, it was very well designed with half of one wall filled with a mirror and a ledge in front with plenty of room to lay out your toiletries. The white tiling looked quite fresh together with the good lighting. The kitchen was just as expected but we found we only prepared a lighter breakfast there as it was so expensive at the supermarkets a la Food Emporium in the area, that it was not much more expensive to dine out. The room itself was large by any standards and we were on the 6th floor overlooking the hospital and it was quiet at all times. The room was very clean and fortunately we did not experience any evidence of blood stains such as another recent reviewer wrote but we did witness a number of patients being wheeled in and looking the worse for wear (I thought it was only an eye, ear and throat hospital across the road, some of them looked like their were bandaged from head to toe?). The cleaning of the room was without fault, except that our towels were changed every day even though we had hung everything up (with advertising suggesting we do this, but they don't follow through on their environmental thinking since they continually replaced them). The entire establishment, from the lobby to the lifts and shabby carpet, looks tired, but in fairness, it is only a three star establishment. The location is excellent and just ten minutes' walk from Central Park. But what put me off this place is the below par service we received on arrival. We had booked on the internet on a special prepaid rate that actually included HSIA (which would otherwise cost USD15 per day). When I asked them to confirm this when we checked in (since I have read horror stories of guests being charged incorrectly for HSIA at other places), they asked me instead if I had something on paper to prove it. I was also advised in a non-professional manner that we were paying about 70% less than their rack rate, interpreted meaning that we should be lucky to even get a bed for that price, let alone having HSIA included. And the doorman who was standing there quipped in that if everyone paid that rate, soon they would be giving rooms away. Well, firstly, he had no idea what rate we paid but for the record, it cost USD169 per night plus tax and, if the Affinia Gardens does not like selling their rooms at that price, then they shouldn't make such deals available as it was booked directly on their own website via Travelzoo for access to the promo code. So I didn't dare to use the HSIA until I checked again the next day (with the same guy who checked us in) and he could then confirm it was included (but that it would be debited to our account then credited at checkout). The MyAffinia thing didn't work, but this may have been my fault as I did it only a few days prior to arrival and it couldn't match it up with my booking. So it might work next time I stay at an Affinia establishment (which will be never as I love Westin). So there was no pillow menu for us, although they did manage to provide us with the two I asked for at checkin (but again, told us we were really only entitled to one - why then is there a drag and drop action which allows the choosing of up to two pillows?). The BYOB kit was not available nor any of the others due to them being booked by other houseguests so the whole concept of tranquillity and ambience was lost as far as we were concerned. And, although the peppermint tea in the lobby was lovely, we didn't feel welcome enough to sit there and enjoy it after the very lukewarm welcome we received at checkin so we took it up to our room to enjoy and to avoid any possible comments from the staff (like perhaps they would complain that they were offering us a free cup of tea!). Had I known that we could get from WTC to Lex and 59th via Lexington Express train which takes less than 15 minutes, we would have stayed the entire time at the Westin and commuted over to Manhattan, even for getting to Central Park and visiting friends on the Upper East Side.

title: “Poor Location”
text:
My boyfriend & I booked this hotel for 2 nights when we stayed in Seattle for the Supercross. 
Overall, I have no complaints about the hotel itself. The rooms where clean, the beds were fairly comfortable, but it is very, very old and outdated. Thin comforters, dim lights, stark white bathrooms and old green carpet. 
I agree wth another review that said to bring earplugs - the room next to ours had a party going on and people walking in and out, slamming doors. We finally had to call down to the front desk and complain. 
As far as location goes, in our opinion, it wasn't very good. It was on the outskirts of downtown and there was nothing really close by to walk to to grab a quick bite, aside from McDonalds, and a sketchy looking place across the street.
Overall the hotel was what we expected for the money, but I think next time we'll spend the extra cash and get something closer to town.

title: “Incredible service and quality of room”
text:
You definitely pay for what you get but this was an incredible experience. the staff continuously went above and beyond. I had given in my suit for pressing and left $150 USD in the pocket without realizing. That night, an envelop was on my table with a note say this was left behind and all the money returned.
Amazing. highly recommend.

title: “Great Staff - Unlucky Timing”
text:
We recently spent 4 nights at this hotel. It's incredibly well located, the staff couldn't be nicer and more helpful and we were upgraded to a wonderful room. 
Unfortunately, the air conditioning in our room was not working properly - it was quite warm. Not bad enough to move to another room which the hotel offered, but definitely not comfortable. Each day we asked them to fix it and they said they would. We went three days like this and finally, on Day 3 it was fixed. If it could be fixed on Day 3, it could have been fixed on Day 1.
Also, we stayed at this hotel specifically so my wife could swim. They have a modest sized pool that met her needs. Unfortunately it closed of maintenance half way through our stay. So, just unfortunate timing for us.
On the other hand, the staff was incredibly helpful when I discovered I had left one of our suitcases on the baggage carousel at LGA, in making restaurant reservations at some of the top restaurants in the city, directions, etc.
While we chalked this up to back luck, the bottom line is that we will stay elsewhere next trip.

title: “Fantastic for Sports Nuts”
text: This hotel is fabulous!!! The fact that it is really close proximity to the TD Banknorth, makes it fantastic for us hockey-nuts!!! The T is right around the corner and everything is within walking distance - you don't have a view from the windows, but really, who the heck is busy staring out a window in Boston?!!! :) This was the 2nd time I've stayed at this hotel and will continue to stay there - the hotel staff is down to earth and the atmosphere is homey...which is exactly what I want.

title: “I really like this Hampton Inn.”
text: I really like this Hampton Inn. I just wish the neighbor hood was a little better. I must say I have stayed here four or five times with no issues. The nice things is there are four of five places to eat that are close by so you do not need to wounder that far. This last time I was there I saw a Papa's I will have to try it next time. This Hampton Inn is very well taken care of from your rooms to the lobby to the grounds. It is very clean! The location works great for me being right off the freeway.

title: “Can't Wait to Return!!”
text: My partner and I spent my birthday weekend in my favorite city!! I researched hotels and am very picky about staying in dumpy places however I don't want to spend $500.00 for one night!! I was quite leary when I saw the price...never thought it would be as nice as it sounded. How nice to be surprised!! It did have great reviews on Trip Advisor so that was my deciding factor! Everything was clean and spotless...the room was newly decorated, bathroom was immaculate, and Peter Roth bath amenities to top it all off! The bed was incredibly comfortable and plenty of room for a NYC hotel room...people were complaining about the "pain in the neck" system of the elevators! I thought it was great....felt very secure! Not easy to get up to the floors if you didnt have a room key. Oh yeah, and location, location, location!! Definitely will be back!

title: “Good hotel for San Francisco weekend”
text: Great hotel for a weekend stay, especially if you plan on bringing a vehicle and can find a deal involving free parking (ordinarily $54/night). The Financial District area around the hotel is much quieter on the weekends and the hotel is within easy walking distance to the Embarcadero BART station and the Ferry Building. Enjoyed a comfortable classic room. Note to those who have to share a room with co-workers, the bathroom door is a sliding door that doesn't completely cover the opening to the bathroom which could lead to some issues. Would also be nice to have complimentary Wi-Fi and high def channels on the TV.

title: “My first stay at a Hilton!”
text: I was VERY impressed with the whole expirience we had this weekend. The people who checked us in and out were very nice, and all smiles. Our room was AMAZING, it was a standard double queen (traveling with friends) and the size was impressive, the beds were SUPER comfortable, the pillows were the best pillows I had ever had in a hotel. We did book our room through Priceline, so our rate was fantastic. Not sure how much their standard rate is though, but I am willing to bet it is worth the money! The location was great, we could walk to Jones Hall, and to all of the food places around downtown Houston.

title: “It'll do but the club crowd can be noisy”
text:
My husband and I stayed overnight on a weekend so we could enjoy the nearby Ohio State Fair. The hotel is approximately ten minutes from the fairgrounds and Ohio Expo Center. It's easy to see off the highway, but due to cement barricades that prevent you from turning into the parking lot directly from Dublin Granville Road, you must drive past the hotel and turn around to access the side road which takes you directly to the hotel. Be very aware of the No U-Turn signs in the vicinity.
 Upon arrival, we noticed the nightclub in the front of the hotel property, and the parking lot is next to a very worn looking miniature golf course. We chose to park in the back after checking in. The front desk clerk was friendly and very kind with our questions.
 The rooms do not open directly to the outside, so you must use the corridors to access your room. You can access these corridors from the lobby, or from the locked entrances located at opposite ends of the complex. You will need to use your keycard to enter the building if you enter from the locked doors.
 Our room had two very soft double beds and a refrigerator that barely kept anything cold. This particular room was also lacking an alarm clock. The TV worked nicely, the table and two chairs was a nice addition, and the shower head had massage setting which actually worked. The tiny coffee maker in our room only makes one cup of coffee. 
 After midnight, the corridors became loud with some guests partying the night away. We resorted to leaving our TV on so as to mask some of the noise.
 The next morning, we were happy to find a nice selection of cereals, danish, bagels and juices for our complimentary breakfast. The bagel toaster was a nice added touch.
 Overall, the hotel was clean, our air conditioner worked well, and we did manage to get a night's sleep without having to complain for it.

title: “No Complaints about Skyline”
text:
I stayed in the Skyline Hotel January 5th through 9th 2004 and have no complaints about my visit. The room was spacious and clean, the staff members were friendly, and the concierge was extremely helpful. The location was ideal for getting to Times Square, Rockefeller Plaza, and the subway-- only a few minutes walk. Several diners and restaurants lined the street near the hotel, and most delivered directly to the hotel, which was convenient for late-night dinners. The view from the pool area on the top floor was beautiful. Even if you don't use the pool, go up there anyway (especially at night), and bring your camera. 
It's worth it.

title: “Great location”
text:
May 7 2007 - The Taj Boston Mass.
Having read a few negative reports about this hotel (formerly the Ritz -Carton) I was pleasantly surprised.
The accomodations of a standard room king bed where very large - definitly over 360 ' sq. The bed needed a step stool to get into it, and although my room was without a view of the Boston Commons it was very comfrotable. 
The service at the hotel was impeccable with very friendly accomodating staff. The location is amazing as you step out onto Newbury Street, he swan lake in the Boston Commons, a subway stop a block away, fantastic restaurants, pubs, shopping.
I would reccomend that if you stay, you make sure that a refurbished room is available. The new managemanet is beginning its update of the hotel which is a little tired looking at the moment. I found the price of 326 a night on par for a major convention city. 
The negatives - the lack of seating in the lobby....you cannot sit and read a paper. The bar is very lovely and tends toward an older trendy crowd. The business center has only two computers - rather small. This is a great hotel for older travelers, business travelers. A little stuffy for singles and families.

title: “Great location close to Universal Studios and Hollywood”
text: We just returned from spring break in California and stayed 3 nights at this hotel. Nice location within a mile from Universal and they provide a free shuttle that runs every hour in the morning and every 15 minutes in the evening. The staff was very helpful and the room was clean. I would recommend a room on the pool side however if you want to avoid traffic noise from the freeway. We ate breakfast every morning at Tula's, which was good and kids 12 and under eat free. We also had a couple dinners there, which were also tasty with great service. Only complaint is the parking fee, which is $15 per night. We did receive $3 off of that because we are Holiday Inn Priority Club members; however, still don't like the fact we had to pay for parking. Overall, its a nice hotel in a great location to be able to do Universal Studios or any other studio tour, as well as Hollywood Blvd.

title: “Not Fun!!”
text:
We stayed at the Omni South Park for our visit to see “Thomas The Train”. Two miserable days, the light in the bathroom went out the first morning, so when had to shower and dress in the dark. We were never able to dial out of our room and no one from room service or maintenance ever picked up.
When we left a staff member seeing two women and children together assumed we were lesbian and started that conversation, when we quickly informed him we were sisters we just walked away, not even an apology……not my idea of a comfortable get away!!!

title: “AMAZING hotel”
text:
I stayed here for a conference, and got a free room upgrade to a Splendito Suite. It was beyond "splendito." The suite, was more like an apartment (bigger than mine at home!) and was just gorgeous. Within minutes of arriving, I received some snacks delivered to my room, and a bottle of wine. I believe this was compliments of being a "zzip member" - their Loyalty Program.... (SIgn up for this!)
I slept like a baby and didn't want to leave. 
The conference meeting/eating rooms were great and comfortable. The best part of the hotel was filled with fantastic photography. 
I would definitely go back to stay at this hotel.

title: “Rooms ok......landscaping beautiful”
text: I am not too happy with the room, but the area around the resort is beautiful. Bathrooms need serious upgrades!

title: “Very nice and east access”
text: This hotel is very nice. It was close to all of my interests which makes it nice really handy. The personal we encountered were all very well trained and friendly. We did not eat there but the restaurant looked inviting. I would recommend staying there.

title: “Modern Hotel in a Rockin' Location”
text:
If you want to exeperience Beale Street, this is the place to stay. The hotel is right at Beale Street so the music, food and nighlife are outside your hotel room door. When we arrived, we coulud immediatley hear the music from Beale Street which instantly put us in a Memphis mindset! 
The rooms are modern and have all of the conveniences you would want, including comfy duvets. We stayed in a 1 bedroom suite with a sofa bed in the living room and a kitchen. I would recommend the layout of this room to travelers who need 2 beds in separate rooms or require additional space. It was nice having a fridge to put snacks and beverages in too. There is a door that separates the living area from the bedroom, so guests sleeping in the living room can also have some privacy. And there are two televisions in these rooms, one in the living room and one in the bedroom. The only bad thing is that the sofa bed wasn't that comfortable. I would suggest that the hotel secure additional bedding or mattress toppers for the sofa beds and provide them to guests upon check in. We requested such items at the front desk, but they don't have these items.
The parking is convenient and located in a parking structure connected to the hotel so there are no inconveniences. It is true that the music from Beale Street can be loud and heard slightly in the rooms into the evening, but it was faint and not a problem. So don't worry about it!

title: “I love this place”
text: This is the first hotel I have been to where water, robes, slippers, chocolates and true service is complementary. The rates are a little high, but their rooms are huge. I had a room with two queen beds, and there was still space for a rollaway for my third friend. I will definitely return, thank you for taking care of us.

title: “Will be nice when construction is done”
text:
We stayed at this Hampton Inn while on a trip to Seattle. The room was nice and spacious with a recently updated bathroom. The bathroom had a large vanity with a granite top and instead of a tub there was a large shower stall. 
The hotel itself was nice but under construction when we were there. The 4th floor was being renovated so during the day it was hard to get an elevator because they were being used by the workers. The lobby is incredibly small and the breakfast is in one of the conference rooms and is modified from the normal Hampton Inn breakfast. The downfall of the hotel other than the construction (which I assume will soon be gone) is that it is a bit confusing. If you are the 6th floor you can't ride the elevator from the parking garage to your room, you have to walk halfway across the hotel to the other elevator. Also, the business center and workout room are on the other side of the hotel from where the lobby is located, so in other words not the normal Hampton Inn layout that you may be familiar with. 
The location is very convenient to the Space Needle, not too far of a walk to the Public Market (15 mins), and there is a QFC (grocery store) close by if you need anything.

title: “Making Business Fun”
text:
The hotel looked like it had undergone some renovations. It was clean, bright and located near the interstate in a business district. The room looked great and the sleep number beds were just what I was looking for. Plus, the room had FREE wireless internet and more cable channels besides Fox News and CNN (I get enough of that everywhere else). Best of all it was directly across the street from Dave and Busters so I could leave the car keys in my room and walk to D&B for a stress free night of dinner and fun.
I also tried the hotel restaurant. The bartender was fantastic but the menu left much to be desired. You basically have a steak option, salad option, chicken option. One of everything but not a lot of "jazz" in any of them.
I would stay here again because it's within minutes of downtown, shopping etc, safe walking distance to restaurant, and the comfortable rooms.

title: “Required Disclosures”
text:
We travel a lot, here and abroad. This property is not yet ready for admission to the top tier. Other reviews can give you more details but a three night stay this week produced the following observations: The hotel is understaffed (as of this writing). When you attempt to deal with the front desk, there apparently is no hotel operator. So, while you are attempting to resolve an issue or gain information or just get service, the front desk attendant is constantly answering the phone. Be advised: the telephone takes precedence, not the guest being served. The front desk uniforms have been cleaned and pressed to the point where they are visibly shiny, annoyingly shiny, waaaay past the point they should have been replaced. The system used in the hotel cannot split a folio, cannot edit a folio and produces a very difficult situation if you are trying to deal with getting two bills during a stay, one business and one personal. There is no true "concierge" in the hotel. There are people to respond to requests but whether the request will be fulfilled is another matter. While it is clear that the staff is trying, the training and being open six months has not yet produced top-tier service and procedures. There is no visible evidence of supervisory management out and about. 
The parking is expensive and there are no-self park options. The hotel does not adequately inform a guest in advance that the $18 additional parking charge is not optional if you bring a car. Every time you want to drop by the hotel it's in-and-out with valets, the accompanying delays and the requisite tip, every single time. The entrance drive is exceedingly cramped and very poorly marked as you enter the property. It is just as likely you will go the wrong way to pull up under the portico as it is you will go the right way. Exiting the hotel to go any direction except east-bound requires a diversion east-bound and then attempts to make a U-turn in frequently heavy oncoming traffic. They cannot do anything about that but for some guests it might be disconcerting. 
The rooms are stylish, nicely decorated and have good amenities such as the Frette sheets and the very nice bathroom vanity and sink. The door to the rooms does not fit tightly and noises out of the room easily come in, and vice-versa. Beware if you are expecting privacy. A huge plus is that the in-room internet is wireless and free. Many plaudits for that. 
Room service was 50-50. One order worked nicely and was delicious. The other was a three-trip disaster with significant delays. First, cold coffee. Second, no milk for the cereal, third some other annoyance that has been repressed. The solitary, small croissant was sample-sized. The person taking the order on the telephone could not understand what a croissant was. Entirely unsatisfactory. Newspapers are delivered each morning in a bag hung on the door. 
Physically it's a good makeover of a tired old Hampton Inn. The service and management standards have not yet caught up with the designer and the construction contractor. If you can get it at a good rate, and aren't too picky about service and "just thrilled to be here" then you will have a good time.

title: “Nice Stay”
text:
My friend booked this trip so I had no input what so ever. This was my first time in Philadelphia and didn't know what to expect. The hotel has a good location everything is a few blocks away (please bring comfortable walking shoes). 
Sidenote: Two negative things; upon checking in they didn't have any KING beds available so we had to settle for double beds. 
One evening while away from our room upon returning we realized our take out food from the previous day was not in our room. (Housekeeping threw it away and we had it NO WHERE NEAR A TRASHCAN) I was heated because I was hungry and wanted to nibble on that food. I called the front desk and they offered me a meal voucher for breakfast. The breakfast buffet had everything you could imagine. All was forgiven!

title: “Friendly and Helpful!”
text: Stayed here in August 2011 and returned for 3-day special in October! Very clean; basic, but comfortable rooms. Hotel staff knowledgeable, welcoming and friendly! Attractive retro lounge area with adequate, basic continental breakfast and newspapers. Great cafe next door! Safe area near the university, with lots of cafes and restaurants within walking distance. We especially valued the FREE shuttle to shopping and downtown, (goes to other locations as well) and free, safe parking! In August we greatly enjoyed the attractive, clean, well-maintained and attractive seasonal outdoor pool (lots of towels and some seating) and only wished it had still been available in October! We have family in Seattle and when staying with them isn't possible, we plan to return to this bright, decent, colourful, arty good-value hotel!

title: “A Great Hotel - Thanks to TripAdvisor”
text:
"Thanks to TripAdvisor" - We did not have much time to plan for our trip to New York & fortunately we came across this fantastic website. The Carlton Hotel was everything we wanted & were thrilled with our twin bedded room on the 10th floor overlooking 29th street, with a view of the Empire State Building. The bed linen was lovely, crisp white duvet covers & sheets changed daily, with great pillows on the beds which smelt fresh!! We were apprehensive about large city noises, but had a great sleep each night (6) & heard no disturbance at all. Our room was directly opposite the lift, which had a marble floor on exiting the lift, once again we heard nothing!! 
We were in New York in the middle of June, the weather was hot, each evening the temperature in our room was fantastic, thanks to the A/C!!
The bathroom was great, just enough room with a good size handbasin & marble top vanity. Ample good white towels changed daily.
We found great restaurants nearby for evening meals & had our tasty breakfast each morning @ Cafe 28 just around the corner.
We would recommend this hotel & would definately return. The management were proud of the refurbishment which the hotel had gone through although the new reception area & restaurant were not completed it will be very smart when it is completed!!

title: “Best room ever”
text: I only stayed in this area of Chicago because I was attending a theater event nearby and planned to go to Wrigley. I say that because it is a very openly gay area and I was quite uncomfortable with the hand-holding, etc., on the streets. However, the hotel was excellent. Had a double room/suite on the fourth floor (Room 421, I think). It had beautiful hardwood floors, a dividing wall for my traveling companion to have privacy, a walk-in tiled shower with glass door that was such a treat (I hate stepping into tubs) and was high enough above street level to sleep with the windows open and enjoy the fresh air. We both absolutely loved it. Most of the reviews I read in advance were right on the money. It was a quick walk to Wrigley and the red line. It was convenient to a lot of good places to eat. You do have to do the separate entrance thing but that was no big deal. They held our luggage until check-in time so we could enjoy the day. We did not eat breakfast there so I don't know how that compares but it did seem like a pretty small meal area so I'm guessing it was basic continental.
