In the past, I have stayed at the downtown Hilton and it was quite the opposite in terms of size. But this place gets my vote in terms of everything else. Oh, and the bed was fabulous, too.

title: “great location, nice room”
text: The hotel is very close to the San Diego convention centre. The room has a nice flat screen TV and a superb sound system. No coffee maker, but has a nice selection of drinks. It was slightly expensive compared to other places and you will have to pay for the internet (but have a good offer of $17 resort fee which includes domestic calls and entry to fitness centre). I won't recommend it to family but great place for party animals. I would like to go back for holiday for sure.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
was really excited t the prospect of staying here..looked fab on the website... what a disappointment the room was tiny (even for new york), tatty , extremely noisy...the whole hotel was dark and dingy and felt in need of an update.. and as for some of the staff-it is supposed to be a service industry-so rude.
Would not recommend this hotel..have stayed in much better in NYC at a much lower cost.

title: “Spiffy in every way!”
text: We've stayed at all the usual suspects in S.F. but now we're committed to the Monaco exclusively. Got a great rate including parking directly from the hotel website. The staff here is sublimely professional and gracious in every way. What a revelation! It's a very pretty hotel. My only complaint was that the room was really tiny, although they did try very hard to upgrade us when I complained. Next time I'll book a larger room, and there absolutely will be a next time!

title: “Exactly what we needed - quiet, restful, and convenient”
text: I stayed in this hotel after arriving at IND near midnight after a 20-hour trip, with plans to travel on the next day. I needed a dark, quiet room, good A/C, hot shower, comfortable bed, and crib for my toddler, close to the airport so we didn't have to drive far after the long trip. The Crowne Plaza met the bill. We checked in quickly despite the late arrival, and our room was dark, quiet and cool. Buffet breakfast in the hotel restaurant was fine, checkout was quick. Despite what one earlier review says (which had me worried) this hotel is in fact next to the NEW Indianapolis airport (which is actually at least 5 years old now, maybe closer to ten) but it is a good 5-minute drive on the airport access road. I wouldn't book this for my vacation, but it's perfect for what it is - an airport hotel intended for travelers.

title: “Bugs and cold water showers”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights last week for a business conference, and were not impressed. 
The 'street map' the front desk provided was totally inaccurate and not-to-scale, and we drove around in circles trying to find our room, which was in a building that resembled a cement bunker. We were forever getting lost in the maze, and found it very inconvenient to get anywhere on the 'campus'. It was inconvenient for a conference b/c it was a 5 minute walk to get anywhere with poor signage along the way.
There were mini ant-like bugs crawling around the room, on the sink, on our tooth brushes, over the desk and the coffee table. I remarked to my husband the first morning that I had probably eaten a few in my sleep! 
The daily charges of $20 for parking and $15 for the fitness center were ridiculous!! 
The first morning we both commented on the great water-pressure in the shower, but the next day the water was luke-warm, and was cold on the last morning. The only good thing about this was that when we complained about the cold water they took the $60 parking charge off our bill! $60 to park in the deserted lot 100 feet from our room.
We were also disappointed that there was no wireless internet available. We took turns plugging into the one ethernet cable in the room (remarkably they did not charge for using the ethernet cable; perhaps they overlooked that). The room did have a great big walk-in closet, but only 8 hangers, so it did not do us much good.
The decor was rustic country, which surprised me for a Southern California hotel. There was a couch and coffee table, and 2 uncomfortable wicker chairs. The doors of the large hutch containing the fridge and tv could not be opened all the way b/c they hit the footboard on the bed.
I did enjoy the view out to the patio at the back of our room, which was very private and nicely planted. Unfortunately it was only 60 degrees out so we could not sit out there.

title: “Great Find - Great Staff”
text: A wonderful find with a great location just off Michigan Ave. Small lobby, no wasted space. The rooms are spotless and spacious with all the ammenities you need. We had lunch in the restaurant and a room service breakfast. Both were great. As nice as the hotel is, the real stars are the hotel staff, always pleasant, helpful and ready with great suggestions. Peter at the front desk was especially helpful.

title: “A convenient location but it's a little tired inside”
text:
The location is convenient for walking to Chinatown, Union Square and Russian Hill. 
The price is reasonable, but with the best will in the world, beyond sleeping there, I didn't feel that I wanted to spend any time at the hotel. I've got nothing against functional and minimalist hotels but this one did seem just a little bit too tired on the inside. 
The staff were helpful and the tv is very big with in the room. 
Be advised that there are no temperature controls in the room and I found it a little warm at night even with my window open (and this was during the winter).

title: “Not all that!”
text:
The hotel lobby is nice....presentation great but there are no real good choices as far as rooms go.
We wanted a non-smoking room as away from the freeway as possible, and a balcony. turns out that we had to choose between having a balcony and being away from the freeway, or having a balcony and taking a smoking room!
The acoustics are terrible. One can hear people talk and walk along the corridors, or people walking around inthe next room.
All in all, okay stay, but would not recommend the hotel to friends unless it were really cheap!

title: “Great hotel rooms, great location, staff a bit rude.”
text:
Enjoyed staying at this hotel.
Positives:
- good modern rooms
- comfy bed
- room service v.quick
Negatives:
- communal areas very busy, no place for meetings, foyer coffee shop always packed
- staff in general areas (not including checkin) rude and unfriendly.

title: “Mostly Positive”
text:
Stayed here when we needed an emergency overnight stay in the city. We got a standard room on a lower floor. Agreed, the room is very spacious and comfortable. I wished for another chair (there was a large space next to the bed that would perfectly fit more seating) and brighter lighting, but the dimness I suppose is part of the "modernity." 
Good stuff: the flat-screen TVs (inclu. in bath), DVD and CD players were an excellent amenity. The bed is the most comfortable ever. Ordered room service which arrived promptly and with friendly service. Overall, the staff is very responsive, which lead me into the:
Not-so-good-stuff: this particular standard room's Achilles heel was most definitely the bath. First, the shower apparatus (European-style coil) had to be replaced entirely when we realized it wasn't working. As noted the staff took care of this immediately. 
However, the actual shower creates a huge flood in the bathroom, as the shower area is basically only separated by a small metal divider on the floor (it's not sunken and has no doors, etc). The shower is so powerful that the water pools and goes out into the rest of the bathroom. The mat was sopping wet. This was evidently not the first time either as we could see water damage on the tiled floor, a "water line", exactly where the flood usually extends to each time the shower is used. 
Our stay also coincided with the first very hot day in NYC (mid 90s with equal humidity) and I was surprised to find that the hallway (4th floor) was not air conditioned. The AC in general is not very powerful in the room either. 
Also, we could tell someone had been smoking in the room previously but as the hotel was fully booked we could not change our room. Also the staff's reaction was, "well, we have all non-smoking rooms." Well, judging by the amount of cigarette butts outside the windowsill, someone's been puffing away. It is possible to open the window so the previous occupant(s) felt free to smoke in the room and it definitely left an odor. Not pleasant if you are non-smokers as we are. 
For business travelers, note the Alex does not have express check-out. I'd be very careful (as always) to check the bill, too--we were erroneously charged for a movie we did not order and had to correct the bill. We also noted that because the hotel is on a (thankfully) quiet side street off Third Avenue, it was a long wait for cabs on a Thursday morning around 10am. 
It's too bad these things marred the experience, because otherwise this hotel has potential.

title: “Nice big hotel”
text:
The location is a bit off as it sits bordering convention center exclusive area with dirty Chinatown. Plus the entrance is under sort of a bridge between buildings. 
In terms of area amenities it is great. Near to chinese restaurant (me being asian), of course the convention center, shopping areas, walking distance to the historic district, subway stations and greyhound terminal. 
The standard room is roomy and clean. The beds (2 double) are so comfortable with too much pillows. We thought of taking the bolster home ;). There are two big LCD tvs in the room, one in front of the beds and another at the sofa area. They also have functional microwave, tea making facilities and fridge. I only wonder if they have a safe box coz I couldn't find one, but I did not ask.
Overall the stay was wonderful. The staff are quite helpful but could be better. Somehow, they couldn't find a box delivered to me when they have already arrived. Anyway, they found it within the hour to my relief.

title: “"PerFeCT LoCaTioN, GReaT VaLue and SuPeR STaFF"”
text: Back in December 2010, My husband and I stayed at your hotel for two nights. The hotel staff welcomed our arrival with a cheerful and friendly smile. During our stay we have the opportunity to talk with the staff Alex, Justin, George and Tess all of them gave us the impression of being like a family. They are extremely helpful and they personalized service to a new level, a true asset to the hotel. Our room was very nice, bed are comfortable and everything else was spotless clean and organized. We are more than pleased with our experience! My husband and I loved this place and we'll definitely come back in the near future and would highly recommend your hotel to friends and relatives.

title: “Portrait of a Dump”
text: We booked four nights at the Amsterdam Court Hotel on Hotel[-], arriving on a Thursday and leaving on a Monday. Although I called to confirm the reservation and was assured a king or queen, when we arrived about 11:30 PM on Thursday the only room left had two double beds. That would have been OK, except the window air conditioner made as much noise as a gas lawnmower and the beds were worn out and soft. Given it was hot and humid in NY we had to use the airconditioner, but slept very little. We were not able to move the second night because the clerk did not give us the correct instructions for changing rooms, although we requested to be moved Thursday night. The third night we we moved to a room with a king, but again the window airconditioner was loud and this time so loud and grinding that it was not at all useable. So they moved us to a room with two soft worn out double beds and another loud airconditioner. In this room, the circuit breaker blew in the evening before we returned to our room, turning off the airconditioner and lights. We waited for some time to get it back on. Electrical overload can cause fires. On the fourth night they moved us to a "luxury" suite, not usually given to Hotel[-] customers. This room was OK, however the bathroom had not been cleaned well leaving dark hairs on the shower walls and in the tub. The capucinno machine worked one day out of four. The staff person said, "It's always broken." There are no coffee machines in the rooms, and the coffee available downstairs was burned and not drinkable. Absolutely no security was visible. Well, atl least there were no rats in the stairway. The staff kept apologizing, but nothing changed. One of the elevators was out of service off and on. The computer did not work when we wanted to check out and we had to wait. Take my advice, go somewhere else.

title: “Excellent Hotel at a great price!”
text:
4 adult ladies stayed here from May 17th to May 21st. We checked in at 12:30pm and our room was ready even though check in wasn't until 3pm. We used valet parking at the adjacent lot and it cost $40/24 hrs for my SUV. Very convenient with all our luggage. I wouldn't do it any other way. 
The room was spacious by NYC standards, very clean and had 2 queen beds. The lobby was spacious and offered a concierge (which we never used), hot chocolate, coffee, tea and apples all day long/night. The buffet breakfast was good and plentiful and we didn't have an issue getting a table at all. The staff came around and offered us mints and asked if our stay was pleasant and if we had any concerns or complaints to please let them know so they could make it right. We paid $201.75USD/night plus NYC state taxes. The beds were comfortable, lofty white duvets, clean sheets every day. We met a couple from Dubai that were staying at Milford Plaza and they were very envious of our awesome hotel experience as theirs was terrible! 
I will definitely return to NYC and I will definitely stay at this hotel again. It's very close to Times Square, Empire State, TOTR, Macy's, Central Park and is in the heart of restaurant row. 
When you book at this Hampton Inn, you're getting a great hotel with great value.

title: “Hotel still not Fairmont Level”
text: We booked last minute and the hotel was very booked. We came a day early and had two separate reservations for some reason. This hotel has all the potential to be a Fairmont but it's not there yet. We are frequent travelers and insist on a certain level of details when it comes to our leisure stays. Fresh squeezed oj means... Orange juice squeezed from an orange. Not what it says on a box. Just 1 small detail for example. Staff is very polite, not their fault that management still needs to go back to training. Elevators are ridiculous. Why isn't there express? There are plenty of elevators but if your on an upper floor it could take you all day to go to and from your room. We had a suite in the south tower, beautifully furnished, great views, but the smallest bathroom I've ever seen! I found out our last day there was a pool. Nowhere in the I do that was in our room was there anything talking about the pool! Would have liked to have known that upon checkin. I love Fairmont. Plaza, Savoy... But not sure I'd choose Dallas Fairmont. Too many details not noticed.

title: “Nice location”
text: As expected location is assume opposite a shopping mall right in Beverly hills. However the buffet breakfast oops sorry a five star hotel with no buffet breakfast but a la carte. Since I was traveling with my family and kids I asked for hot water in the room they charged me usd 5 for water as service charges it felt like a little crazed not for the money. Overall the place is good

title: “Expensive...but mainly worth it!”
text:
There seems to be some really varied reviews about the Soho House and I would like to share my total experience...
I would have to agree with the previous review, the rooms are quite noisy. This is because the Soho House is in the trendy Meat Packing district of New York and from 11pm the cab drivers descend upon the area to pick up the revellers.
I would also have to agree that the roof area is smaller than I expected, but understand it is about to undergo some work, so it may improve, but it really isn't that bad.
The bedrooms are absolutely fabulous - huge beds and a fantastic bath at the end of the bed. The shower has an in-built steam-room facility - pure luxury. The TV in our room was fine, as was the quality of the sound.
I expressed my concern over the outside noise to the staff after the first night. They could not have been more helpful. They also did everything they could to recommend and get us into some of the best restaurants. We decided very late on Saturday that we wanted to eat at the very popular Blue Water Grill. The staff really went out of their way for us and got us a table at a fully booked restaurant. The room service staff were extremely curtious and possibly some of the politest I have ever come across. The door staff would always flag a cab for us without us even asking.
A tip for future travellers - this is a private members club and as such many people come through the small front desk - many people no doubt trying to 'blag' their way in. The staff seem to change quite regularly, so show the staff your room key when you walk through the front door - then they know who you are (it's a shame they don't tell you this themselves...). 
If you don't mind a bit of noise and want to stay in a fabulous room at a 'hotel' in a very trendy area of NY that has a pool on the roof and you don't mind spending some serious cash - you will enjoy the Soho House!

title: “Something rotten in the big apple.”
text:
The good:
++ Helpful desk
++ Great location
The bad:
-- Smelly rooms
-- Some rooms (such as ours) had a view of a brick wall with no natural light
-- Very noisy light fittings when switched on
-- Very small rooms compared to other hotels we stayed in on our tour of the east coast within the same class
-- Shabby interior of hallways, etc
-- Lobby on a number of occasions was far too crowded with customers waiting to depart with their luggage blocking exits, internet stations, etc.
-- poor reception on television
Overall, wouldnt stay here again.

title: “good choice”
text: this hotel was recommended by my sister. it is in a great location and the room is nice. comfortable bed- quiet- staff very helpful with recommendations as to restaurants. pike's market a 4 block walk. would stay there again.

title: “Always reliable”
text: The Lowes in Denver is very clean and quiet. The rooms are nicely appointed. If you become a member of their Loews club when you make a reservation you have a choice of your welcome package.... newspaper or wine and cheese/fruit and of course at night there is the turn down service with the chocolate on the pillow.The Lowes is the nicest hotel located to The University of Denver Campus, and they have parent rates. It is great!

title: “Great stay”
text: We were very impressed with the size of the room, the breakfast, and cleanliness!! Would definitely stay again.

title: “A wonderful first visit to Philly”
text: This hotel was selected for us under the Name Your Own Price feature of Priceline. It was a four-star hotel that we scored for $95 the friday night before Independence Day. This hotel was formerly the Ritz, and it is absolutely stunning.. Upon arrival, we weren't merely tossed in the least attractive room for booking through a discount travel website. We were allowed to select a high/low floor, double or single bed, and our proximity to the elevator. The staff working at the front desk even offered recommendations for dining and attractions during our stay. I would recommend this hotel to friends and family and gladly stay there again.

title: “Tlc”
text: We had a horrific flight experience and were worried about our hotel reservations. We called into the hotel and received remarkable individualized service from Crystal at the desk who called me personally on my cell phone to let me know our arrangements were in order and at no extra cost to us. The hotel was extremely accommodating and comfortable.

title: “Another Perfect Stay”
text: We always use The New York Palace when visiting The City. Our preferred rooms are The Towers, under the direction of their excellent manager, guests can be assured of first class treatment. Our room was on the 48th floor overlooking St Patrick's Cathedral. The room was large with traditional furniture, as always it was extremely clean and comfortable. Housekeeping do a fantastic job. As part of our package we also had access to The Towers Club on the 39th floor. This offers a variety of food servings throughout the day with beverages as needed. There is a complimentary bar in the evening. For us there is no other choice of Hotel/

title: “Just Okay”
text: Stayed at the River Inn for a long weekend recently. While the hotel appears to have been renovated in recent years, it seemed tired to me and was not as clean as I would have hoped. The bathroom, in particular, was disgusting - mold in the shower and on the shower curtain and the bathroom didn't appear to be renovated. This hotel just wasn't up to par with other hotels I've stayed at recently. As far as location - it's great if you need to be near Georgetown and it's a short walk to the Metro, but if you want to be near major DC sites like the Mall, Washington Monument, etc. I would suggest staying closer to the center of DC.

title: “What a hotel!”
text: This is an unbelievable hotel! Location is right across the street from the World Trade area and there are plenty of local restaurants and pizza shops within walking distance. I was upgraded to a two room suite due to my Diamond Status. The view from the 54th floor was awesome and the walls of windows was awe inspiring. Breakfast was great and included with my Diamond status. Staff were great and always offered assistance and directions. Great pool area as well.

title: “Great Location”
text:
Great location. Nice modern & spacious rooms. 
close to Tram terminal & Pier 33.

title: “We loved the Hotel and we we,ll be back”
text: We best location for us. Staff members are very friendly and courteous.

title: “So comfortable”
text: The bed was heavenly and the room quiet. We felt like we were coming home after a long day pounding the pavement. The first day they brought a variety of fruit to the room, stale but some of it was good. It was my birthday - left a nice card and a pc. of cheescake, decorated on a plate with my name in chocolate on it. Bathroom is small but rearranged the glass table to go beside the vanity and it worked. Walk in closet. Great TV. View was fantastic- 38th floor over the park! Very friendly, helpful. The bar had great drink menu and bar food- yum! Noisy at times but very comfortable, classy spot. The location can't be beat by anything off 5th Ave. A gracious place without the attitude.

title: “A Heavenly Stay!”
text:
This was the first time and I was so glad I did. Everyone was so nice and friendly! The room was so clean and the bed slept so, so good. I'm going to return for another stay! Again, all I can say is Yeah!!! great price, exellent customer service etc.....I hope that everyone will stay here so that you can experience what I did!
Terry

title: “Great location, but a second rank”
text:
You can walk to Newbury street from this hotel. It's in the convenient location. The service staff is friendly, the room is not bad but something tells me that this hotel is not the first rank. 
Their shower situation is so poor. For me, a good hotel should have a good shower but this hotel only has a shower nozzle that is attached to a wall and what you can get is just a drizzle. It is like those hotels in Paris.
We had a breakfast in the hotel restaurant. Again the service staff is very friendly but we had to wait for more than 20 minutes to get our food. 
So this hotel is not bad. Certainly better than a chain restaurant but I think they have many rooms to improve.

title: “Amazing Stay!!!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at Hotel Lincoln the other night for a one night getaway. The hotel is very nice and the staff is friendly and personable. The rooms are smaller but still newly renovated and nice. This is a great location, close to old town, shopping, bars, the beach, zoo, etc. every thing is within walking distance. The roof top bar (just opened 2 weeks ago) was amazing, one of the best I've been to in the city. I definitely will stay there again and recommend staying there!

title: “wonderful!!!”
text: A great location, staff and room!

title: “Convenient , busy, but not perfect”
text: Not impressed To be told on arrival at 11pm at night that the room you had booked 9 months in advance was not available after a 14 hour journey from the uk! Although somewhat expected after various recent reviews.We had booked a standard room with 2 double beds to accommodate myself , wife and teenage child. We were offered an upgrade which seemed acceptable, however it was the same size room with a king size bed and a roll out bed, which didn't exist! We had a quiet chat with another receptionist, went for a walk till midnight to return to a room With a newly delivered bed with a poor mattress and no bedding! Another trip to reception and this was resolved along with vouchers for complimentary breakfast( value apprx 80 usd). Following morning I informed yet another receptionist that we expected our bags to be moved to the room that we had booked upon our return that evening. The error was resolved and the room we booked and expected was supplied, along with a further complimentary breakfast. Apart from early mishap, great stay, great location, good sized room, views over chrysler building and no noise from other rooms/corridors.everything clean and in order, breakfast staff excellent, doormen will magic you a taxi in seconds! Hotel is as busy as grand central station, continual functions/ conferences in reception areas, don't expect to be recognised after a few days as way too many people.

title: “Will not stay here again!”
text: The ceilings were so low, it made the rooms (which were already small) and hallways feel very closed in and cramped. The service and food in the restaurant were poor; and the prices were high. In the hotel lounge, they added a 30% "sin" tax to the drinks, making the drinks very expensive.

title: “Some great - some not so great”
text: Just returned from a 5 night stay at this hotel. When we arrived they didn't have our reservation, and since the Sox were playing in town there was no room in the Inn! They were ready to send us out into the street when I went into my EMail and came up with a reservation number WITH the correct date. Still no room, but they set us up with a room at the Colonade just down the street at the price we were quoted for the Marriott Copley Place. (when we checked out of the Colonade the next AM, they tried to charge us a MUCH higher price! - got that worked out, though.) They gave us a really big corner room when we checked in the next day - likely to make up for the fuss. Like some other reviewers, we did notice that the sheets weren't changed every day, but ours were clean with creases the first day. The foam mattresses and down bedding is lovely, and the room smelled like they had just cleaned the carpets and drapes. The bath was spotless, plenty of towels - just as I'd expect for the price. The conceriege was quite wrong not once but twice when he gave us directions to places that weren't right around the hotel. Ask the workers at the "T" station if you really need to know how to get someplace. The breakfast at the restaurant was good, but I was expensing it, otherwise we wouldn't have eaten there.

title: “Top notch service at an exquisite hotel!”
text: We stayed at the Lenox for a long weekend, celebrating our anniversary in July. Every detail was incredible, and the service was outstanding. I have experienced many exquisite hotels in my travels, but the Lenox went above and beyond in delivering care and attention to detail in every aspect of our stay, making it a delightful and memorable trip. The rooms were beautiful, with a fantastic amenity and thoughtful touches (loved the cookies and turndown service!). We dines at Azure for breakfast and dinner, and had cocktails at City Bar and the food was delicious and the service exceeded our expectations. We will definitely be staying at the Lenox every time we visit Boston! Highly recommended!

title: “Excellent value Comfortable Hotel”
text:
This hotel far exceeds all the rotten reviews it gets. I found the staff to be over the top helpful and friendly. The rooms were averaged size which made them plenty roomy enough. The beds were extremely comfortable. There was plenty of hot water. The room was extremely clean and well taken care of. There is a free continental breakfast that exceeded my expectations as it allowed you to toast bread or bagels. It had muffins, juice, cereal along with coffee and tea. For $5 more you could get pancakes and scrambled eggs. 
The hotel is located nearby so many things that were convenient like restaurants, Walgreen's was next door, the post office was just down the road, the bus/trolley station is less than a mile walking distance away with bus stops even closer. 
As for the shuttle, they have 350 rooms and most were full the whole time I was there. Why anyone would think that a hotel could cater to you and shuttle you around when there is so much public transportation nearby blows my mind. For 5.00 a day (less if you get a multiday pass) you can ride the bus/trolleys all day. I did not expect the hotel to shuttle me around. I did find that you should book your return shuttle to the airport a day or two before to make sure you are able to get a time slot you want. I saw the staff take a lot of abuse from people and not once did they lose their cool and they tried their best to be helpful. The demands that some people have are just crazy. They do have a computer in the lobby that you can use but it is old and slow. I found it useful to check emails and facebook for messages though. I would definitely stay here again and I think any reasonable person would agree that this is a good hotel especially for the money.

title: “Pretty good...except”
text:
I tried this hotel again after my last experience and I have to say unfortunately not much has changed...
There's no 'do not disturb' signs in the rooms, you have to ask the front desk....I had to tell the cleaning staff to go away every 15-20 minutes at least, which was rather annoying.
Still crappy TV's...only 20 channels, no hookups for anything...
The wifi was pretty bad. I hooked both my Playstation 3 and my laptop up to it and had major problems.
The sleeping at night was alright...quiet and cheap. No bed bugs, hotel staff in general is very responsive and helpful.
Other than that, it was good.
Suggestion to hotel: Keep 'do not disturb' signs in all the rooms! I forgot about this and had to pay the price with very disturbing knocks on my door every half an hour at least.

title: “Flawless Service”
text: This hotel is located in west Philly (Drexel, Penn) with easy on/off access to the Schuylkill Expressway considering it is a city hotel. Only parking available through the hotel is valet ($39/day)(park on your own in a nearby garage for $25/day). Service was impeccable. Valet parking and bellhop staff were very friendly and helpful; front desk staff was very professional. Hotel, including rooms, is beautiful. Room had hardwood floor foyer; very modern and beautiful bathroom; firm/comfortable bed; IPAD in every room; plenty of lighting/seating for business travelers; and lots of Philadelphia periodicals in the room for tourists. The most noteworthy thing about the hotel is the quiet; you would never know you were in a city (with college students filling the sidewalks in this area). If you watch Food Network, some of the food trucks featured on that network are parked at 36th and Market.

title: “So so”
text:
No heater in room. 
Toilet just been renovated.
Lift is very old n slow.
Hotel is walking distance to Union square n cable car station.

title: “DO NOT STAY HERE”
text:
Pros: Continental breakfast was alright 
One of the staff was amazing and I loved her to death 
Had a washer/dryer on site 
Location was 15 min from everything we needed 
Cons: Toilet seat broke 
Towel rack broke 
Room cleaning sucked! Our rooms were not cleaned on two of four of our days even though the do not disturb signs were in the room on the desk.
Smoke detector kept going off 
Doors don’t lock 
Dirty walls and floors 
Cracked sink 
No bathroom fans 
Horrible smell 
Dirty towels and soap were left from the previous person that stayed 
Nothing is replaced like Kleenex and toilet paper 
Stains on the carpets 
Unsafe neighborhood 
Back stairwell doors do not lock 
Patrons are allowed to smoke out by the pool area 
DIRTY FACILITY ALL AROUND

title: “Great Service”
text:
Spent two nights and have never had such service. On sunday morning there were no newspapers available for us to read about our beloved UT Longhorns. They always have a few complimentary papers but they had been taken. The desk would not hear of us not having a paper, so they sent someone out to buy some, and delivered one to our room. I have never had such service, even at the highest priced hotels.
We'll be staying with them again this weekend for more excellent service. ps: the breakfast, although not free, was exactly what we wanted and at such a low price.

title: “Poor Service, Small Rooms”
text:
The Boston Park Plaza is a large hotel with very small rooms. The air conditioner was loud and did little. Service was the largest disappointment as the hotel seems to be understaffed.
Its time to get over their aging reputation as one of the leading hotels in Boston and start making changes.
Try one of the many hotel alternatives in the area.

title: “Great central location; new renovation”
text:
We stayed here for two nights before working in the Manhattan area. I hadn't been to NY for a while and wanted a location I could get to the midtown/upper sights easily. The hotel is newly renovated which is nice. It is however, that a bit impersonal and chaotic. We arrived at the upper entrance and had to make our way down to the lobby without assistance (lots of baby gear in tow). 
The room was new and had no view but wasn't expecting much for the price. Service requests were dealt with promptly. Wifi is costly. 
Overall, the issue with hotels in New York tends to be price/quality. I have had bigger disappoints than this hotel in this price range probably given it was newly renovated and we were fairly low maintenance.

title: “Our stay was quiet and tranquil.”
text: I would highly recommend this hotel and is an A+ in my book. Check-in was quick and easy and the staff was helpful. Our room was on the first floor and poolsidev absolutly beautiful and very clean. My husband and I sat out on the porch after dinner and enjoyed some adult beverages listening to the tranquil sounds of the night.

title: “Great location, wonderful customer service”
text: We were on our honeymoon for three weeks touring around America. Sarah at the check in desk asked us what we were doing in Denver and we told her ~ later she sent a card and champagne up to our fab room ~ such personal service for such a large hotel. The rooms are lovely. The hotel is easy to find, great location ~ only one block from 16th Street Mall. You won't be disappointed if you book this hotel!

title: “Hilton LAX Life Saver”
text:
While planning our trip to Oahu this August we decided to take the stress out of the first leg of our trip by spending the night by LAX instead of the madness of the 2 hour drive prior to departure. We could not have been more pleased.
The Hilton was reasonably priced and the hotel is very nice and made us feel as though our vacation had begun in style. The front desk staff were warm and helpful, parking was great ( we used it for our long term parking which was very convienient), and the room was extremely comfortable.
In the morning we went down for breakfast, which was a bit pricey for the restraunt side, great on the Starbucks side, but delicious in spite of it all. We were able to pop up stairs and easily make our way down to the courtesy shuttle and we were at the airport in 5 mins, through security and ready to fly.
This will be the way we handle all of our trips from here forward. It was totally worth it, great location, great hotel and staff and great long term parking prices! Plus the Hilton Honors Points!

title: “Nice hotel.”
text: The hotel was pretty nice, better than your average Holiday Inn. The room was average to a little on the small side, but was comfortable and tastefully decorated. It is centrally located to lots of food and entertainment. The only real draw-back for us was the high price of parking... I suppose had we paid full rate I might have been harder on the hotel (we booked through Hotwire for $75).

title: “Nice Hilton stay in the middle of mid-twon near Time Square”
text: I use my accumulated Hhonors points from travelling with work to stay in this hotel with my wife so I am not aware of the actual cost but the place was very nice. Hotel in New York is always a difficult choice, location/price but clean make it always a difficult place to stay for less than $200... This hotel was conveniently located (we left through Pen St to get to Newark airport and went to the Madison Square Garden for some Knicks action!) and the room were very decent. The complimentary Internet and free business center (including printing) was a plus, it's not always the case... The biggest problem for me was the noise... Our room was right above 7th Av... and it was definitely not quiet even with the double glazed windows and my ear plugs... If you are a light sleeper like me ask for rear faced room :)

title: “Room smells very musty”
text: Staying here for a wedding, room damp and musty. The hotel lobby, public areas very nice, but our room smells horrible, cannot sleep due to dampness and smell. Would ask for another room, but hotel full due to various events. Would not stay again or recommend. Must be an old hotel

title: “Great staff and Service, Excellent Value”
text: My fiancee and I were celebrating our 5 year anniversary and decided to book a hotel room in the city and the Crowne Palaza looked like a good choice. Upon checking in we were greeted by the Lobby Manager Leo and he asked what brought us to the hotel that day. We explained that it was our 5 year anniversary and we wanted to just relax and enjoy our evening. He congratulated us and sent up a bottle of champaign to our room - this made our night! The room was beautiful and the view was terrific! I would absolutely go back!

title: “Great Location!”
text:
Location: The property is not far from the Bowdoin T Station, which is closed on the weekends. We walked from Government Center, which was a fairly easy walk. 
There are many places nearby - a Whole Foods is next door, Dunkin Donuts and Starbucks are across the street. TD Garden, Boston Common, the North End, and many other places are within easy reach on foot.
I've read complaints about noise from the hospital across the street, but we had no issue. 
Check In: Check in was pretty painless. The receptionist thanked me for my Plat PC status and provided us with room keys. 
Platinum Benefits: I have yet to be upgraded as a Plat at any US property (most of my stays are in Europe). They did give us vouchers for the continental breakfast - we could have added the hot bar for about $4-5, but chose not to as the cold bar was sufficient.
Room: The room was spacious, but definitely dated. Beds and linens were comfortable and the bathroom amenities were good.
Facilities: This property has many conference rooms, a gym (did not use this trip), and a restaurant. We only visited the restaurant for breakfast.
The hotel had wifi, which worked fine for both my sister and I.
Overall, my experience here was fine. The location is good and would motivate me to use this property again.

title: “Amazing trip”
text:
We stayed at the Novotel at the end of August for 7 nights. Location of the hotel was perfect for us - Empire State, Central Park, Rockefellar Centre, subway all within easy walking distance. 
Our room was located on the 10th floor and overlooked Times Square which we were really happy with. Room itself was really quiet - couldn't hear any traffic. The only real noise I would mention was the pipes during the night!
Didn't eat in the hotel as we always ate out but we had a couple of drinks on the rooftop bar which I would recommend - great view of Times Square. Also nice to relax on the loungers for an hour or so after a long days sightseeing.
Although the room had no tea/coffee facilities I used to pop to the Cosmic Diner which was just across the street (corner of 52nd and 9th) where a tea and coffee cost $3 which was a great way to start the day.
I'd recommend the Circle Line bus tours. For $54 we got a 48 hour pass which included downtown tour, uptown tour, Brooklyn tour, night tour, boat tour, $10 off a meal at Planet Hollywood and a free pass to the Museum of American History - the downtown tour was our first real view of Manhatten and it was nice to see the sights and learn a bit of the history off the tour guide.
We did both the Empire State and Rockefellar although we preferred the Rockefellar as the views are better - but you can't go to New York and not go up the Empire State Buiding!
All in all a fantastic trip.

title: “Excellent and old world”
text:
We drove in and had a sat nav which confused it with the Hilton around the corner. Just pull up and valet park, less confusing. Now this is swish, bell hops, doors opened, just how the other half lives... What are you wearing tomorrow night dharlink??
Rooms very spacious & clean.
You do pay for everything though so be careful, the $9 room order coffee ends up being $20 with tip!!!!
Internet $13/ day.
I found the pillow slip had a tear and only a small amount of toilet paper, with no replacement readily available!
Like I said overall established but be careful of the costs. Even the bar attendant tried to skim, giving us the wrong account, would have forgiven him but another guest offered to pay (and had paid for) our drinks!!!!
Hope this helps.

title: “Central location”
text:
We stayed in the hotel from 12/12/11 to 16/12/11 and on arrival were initially surprised as it was quite dark and dingy in reception but over a few days that opinion changed to quirky. The room on the 3rd floor was also very small and we were initially disappointed as the bathroom had old fittings and a stainless steel sink and looked tired but again the room turned out to be very comfortable and clean but very small and sparsely furnished, dingy corridors though.Very central location made up for the defects!!
Reception staff were very helpful and wi-fi in reception was great with access to IPads. Beware though if booking a car to Newark - don't try to pay by credit card as I got a CC rate from the hotel but arrived at Newark and had to run around like a headless chicken looking for a cash machine.
Also if you buy an international dialling card for 10 dollars it will cost you 1.25 dollars per call to use it, a 52 dollar charge which reception cut to 26 dollars(1st hotel in NY we have been charged in). Also 2 dollars per bag to store our bags is a new way of charging customers and also a 1st.
Carve around the corner was a real find bacon and egg bap with a deliciouscoffee for 3dollars 75(same as a coffee in the coffee shop attached to the hotel). Great trip all round, don't miss Jersey boys and Sister act and visit Woodbury Common to shop.

title: “Hang out in Austin at the Embassy Suites”
text: Stayed here for a week in November. Nice hotel, clean and spacious rooms. Free breakfast and happy hour. Free internet in the business center, but $10/day in the room. Short walk to 6th street, nice trails around Town Lake. Good location on South Congress with "public" transportation to UT. Austin is not that big so walking is popular, as are bikes. ES is near a Hyatt, a Raddison, and a Hampton Inn, all on Town Lake. At least 3 places to eat near the hotel and more within walking distance. Lots of clubs close by if that's your thing. I got free parking in the garage, but its a walk and an elevator ride away.

title: “Nice hotel, but a musty room.”
text: We spent one night at this hotel on our way to Southern Florida. The staff was friendly and the room was nicely appointed. The only down side was the mustiness in the room. After being in the room for a while, the mustiness was not as noticeable but did cause some breathing difficulties for my wife. In all fairness to the hotel, we did not report our issue to the staff and just went with what we had. The breakfast buffet was nice and what one would expect at a Fairfield Inn. If back in the area, I would not hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Did not RESERVE the rooms I made a RESERVATION for”
text: I made my reservation well in advance (6 months), for Two connecting rooms with double beds. I was told at check in that they didn't have any of these available. What is the point of making a RESERVATION if you aren't going to RESERVE the rooms? So they had us switch rooms for the second night which was very inconvenient. Still not in the connecting rooms we reserved, but at least for the second night we had the correct amount of beds. I realized shortly after moving to the second room that I had left something very expensive in the first room. I knew EXACTLY where I had left it. The front desk could not be more useless. They said house keeping didn't have it. And that was that. S.O.L. Let me remind you, if I didn't have to switch rooms in the first place, I would not have lost this item.

title: “Roosevelt Hotel NYC”
text: I recently stayed at the Roosevelt Hotel (29Mar 3nights) with my husband and 8 year old son. The location is great, very convenient and a great spot. The main hotel areas seem well maintained but this is where it ends. There are 12 floors and mostly only 4 elevators work so a 15 minute wait for one is the norm. There is no atmosphere to this hotel whatsoever so if you are looking for a great American experience don't stay here. It is completely soulless with money 'tip grabbing' staff particularly the bell men. I overheard one of them say we store luggage for free but it is expected that you pay me to take your bags to the store room! Very handy when I also saw guests carry their own bags to the store room and then watched the bell man count out his stash of money in front of me!!!! The rooms are so small I couldn't believe it with two very small doubles and no room to move - the only way it worked in our room was when two people remained in bed whilst the third moved and squeezed their way around the room. I'm disgusted that British Airways are recommending this hotel and I would never ever stay here again or recommend it to anyone - do not stay here, it is the most horrendous hotel I've stayed in during the last ten years. I would rather pay double the price to at least get friendly and sincere staff and a room that you can fit more than one person in. Seriously there are better places to stay and whilst I get the 'you are only there to sleep' concept it was a major issue during this hotel.

title: “Tremont Plaza, very comfortable, great location”
text: My husband, daughter and I stayed at the Tremont for almost a month in August, 2011. I had a major surgery and it was our home base during my surgery and recovery. The rooms are comfortable and clean...beds are very very comfortable which was so important for me. It is directly accross the street from Mercy Medical Center and close to the inner Harbor. A very clean and safe part of Baltimore. Many restaurants close by. The hotel has a store which serves sandwiches and a few grocery items. The ballroom is absolutely beautiful for special events. There is a small exercize facility and pool. The room had a small kitchenette with fridge, microwave and sink which helped my husband during our extended stay. They were very accommodating when we needed a lift to the inner harbor or a restaurant, since we did not have a car and we didn't even need it. Their driver picked us up from the airport and returned us and was friendly and courteous. I highly recommend this hotel for your stay in Baltimore.

title: “Great stay, again...”
text:
Another enjoyable stay at the Affinia 50. We had a Junior Suite with 2 double beds, sofa bed and kitchenette. Good value and loads of space for the family. The hotel is well located in mid-town with easy access to the subway, 5th Ave etc. Loads of restaurants nearby. Staff are helpful and friendly.
They showed a movie in the lounge on Sunday evening which was fun for the kids (free popcorn). They also have coin-operated washing machines/dryers in the basement which is really handy when travelling.
Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Excellent location and FREE parking”
text: After reading some of the reviews I was quite worried about the Channel Inn Hotel - but there was no need to worry. The location is brilliant - especially if you have a channel side room with a balcony. Beautiful views over the marina and the most stunning sunsets. The Mall is 15-20 mins walk away. The hotel is situated in a very quiet and seemingly safe area. A complete bonus is the free parking - fantastic. Just a couple of grumbles - no fridge or coffee maker and the bathroom, although clean, could do with updating. Otherwise I would thoroughly recommend this reasonably priced hotel.

title: “Better than I expected”
text: This is a very well located and reasonably priced hotel. The rooms are clean and the staff nice. It is located in a quite noisy street so if you can book a room not facing the street, that would be best. It is not a stilish hotel and the sheets are a little rough, but overall this is a decent hotel. I would certainly go back.

title: “Small room, good location”
text: Between rockerfeller center and broadway/times sq. Very convenient to subway. Crowded area. Clean rooms and friendly staff. Internet is in the lobby only. A bonus during our stay is the complimentary loaner umbrellas

title: “Worth it if you get a price deal”
text:
Very good location. Very good service. I was not able to see what separated the Sofitel from the Westin which was down the street other than the price. (They even valet your vehicle in the same garage) I was really excited to stay here because of the glowing reviews but I felt a little let down when I arrived. I think I have come to expect good customer service from a hotel in the 4 star range and just was not blown away by anything here. 
I would definitely return here if there was a good pricing deal, otherwise I would probably pick one of the neighboring hotels at a lower price point.

title: “Great stay!!!!!!!!”
text: i stayed at the homestead hotel on salisbury rd and it was the best stay ever. The staff was very friendly and caring. I came because i was attending the mayo clinic. The shuttle service was a great help since i did not have my own transportation. I found out htey just recently changed their breakfast and i got up every morning to enjoy all their items. THey said it was continental but I can assure you it was way more than just continental breakfast. The manager was so nice, I believe her name was nicky. All staff at the desk was their to help out. I felt I became part of their homestead family for the time I was their. I will always keep them in mind for hte next time I have to stay somewhere. Thank you thank you thank you for all your care and friendliness... I'll be back.

title: “Deserving, Yet Just Short of Perfection.”
text: The Trump International is well deserving of its award winning status! Being able to walk out of your hotel doors and be directly across the street from Central Park is like nothing else. I stayed in the Executive City View Suite. The suite is exactly how it is described on the website, but for views of both Broadway and Central Park be sure to request a corner suite. The personalized service exceeds expectations! However, I did have an unpleasant experience with the service at the spa, but management offered compensation that was beyond reasonable. I would also note that there is no true lounge at the hotel, and that the bathroom's layout and design are not as impressive as the rest of the suite.

title: “Outdated and Dirty... Wish we'd stayed elsewhere”
text:
My husband, son and I went to Phoenix for a business trip/vacation. Our first impressions of the hotel were good -- nice entrance, pretty lobby, well kept courtyard. We were surprised by the motel layout as that's not what we expect from an Embassy Suites.
The room was less than desirable. We expected a well appointed, clean room. We got a dark, dingy, outdated and moldy room. The furnishings were old and worn out. There was visible mold and mildew in the shower which is awful for my husband's allergies.
My husband complained to the management and since he is HHonors Gold they moved us to their "executive" suite, promising that they'd have Housekeeping check it before we moved rooms. This room was bigger but not any better. There was tons more mildew in the shower. When we got to the room, it had 3 inches of standing water in the jacuzzi tub. It strangely had two AC Units and only one worked. The faucet fixture in the tub was so caked in minerals it was clear that no one had been cleaning it.
As for other parts of the hotel, the restaurant had tears and crumbs on the bench seating. The staff couldn't keep up with the demand for pool towels (with less than 25 guests in the pool area) and the poolside drinks were overpriced. The front desk staff had very little to offer for dining suggestions. The elevator was old, dirty and scary.
We will not stay here on future trips. It was very obvious that the management doesn't hold housekeeping to any standards. It was hard for me to understand how in an arid area like Phoenix a bathroom could have so much mold and mildew.

title: “Employee steals and still is allowed to stay employeed.......”
text: This has been by far the worst hotel that I have ever stayed in. We were out of the room with the do not disturb sign on the door. The maid entered our room with a security card and stole money and went through all of our possessions looking for more. When we returned to the room and found it in the condition that it was in we called the front desk and the security officer was sent up to our room to talk with us about it. After the talk it was decided that the hotel manager would give us a phone call the next day that they were in the office and we would receive a night paid for by the hotel. After thinking about what had happened I was not happy with the outcome I called by to the front desk and told them I wanted to speak with the police over it. The local police officer was sent back up to our room and took our information. When the officer returned with the house keeping manager we found out that the maid in question was still at work. She had admitted to taking the money but said that it was a accident. I found it hard to understand how someone could pick up a full cup of change that was quite heavy and not know that there was something in it and the sifting through our possessions I am not sure how she explained that (maybe she was dusting off the inside of the drawers? After talking to the officer and the house keeping manager it was decided that the maid would loose her job and the room would be free for one night. I was told that the paperwork would be put in and taken care of and I would receive a call from someone at the hotel at a later date. I just contacted the booking site that we used to get the room no paperwork has been put in and I still have never even got the phone call. It is now the 11th and this happened on the 4th. To me this is dropping the ball big time, I just want to share me experience with the next person when they are selecting a hotel to stay at. When it comes to this hotel my advice to the traveler would be go to wal-mart and get a tent and stay at the lake or something at least that way you will be aware of the dangers that you face and not expect any level of professionalism because I found none when it came to this hotel.

title: “Fine, if you know what you're getting”
text:
I bid on a 4* hotel on Priceline and received this hotel. Like other reviewers on Tripadvisor, I agree that it is a 3*. 
We had a room in the East Tower on the 10th floor. The view of the harbor was very nice. The hotel is full service, with several restaurants and a very nice pool. The location is ok. You can't walk to anything, but it's a short drive to many of the attractions in San Diego.
However, the room was definitely 3* quality. It was very basic. The toilet seat was peeling, and there were stains on the carpet in the hallway.
We were given a club level room with access to the club lounge, which was very nice and elegant with great views. It is located on the top floor and offered breakfast and evening hors d'oevres to club level guests. However, even there, the fabric on some of the chairs was peeling.
If you come here expecting a 4* hotel, you will be disappointed. However, if you expect a 3*, it's not so bad.

title: “Nice room and pretty grounds.”
text:
Stayed at the Ocatilla Club. Rooms are nice. Ocatilla club offers continental breakfast but ends too early ...9:30am on weekdays and 10:00am on weekends. When I'm on vacation I don't want to rush in the mornings. Plus the food selection is a bit sparse. This is why I have rated breakfast as poor. I didn't have breakfast at the other restaurants except for brunch at 'Wright's.'
Beautiful landscaping. Grounds and hotel are well maintained.

title: “The best hotel I've ever stayed in”
text: Admittedly this is the first time I've stayed in a 5* hotel but I was very impressed. Customer service was outstanding and the refurbishment means the whole hotel is immaculate. Gym with complimentary water, valet parking (a bit pricey but totally worth it), very friendly staff- faultless stay!!

title: “Careful: Chronic Noise Prob at Morgans”
text:
We booked in for 7 nights in June. We normally stay at the Chandler down the street but thought we’d give Morgans a go given the positive reviews. What a massive disappointment. 
Each morning at around 5.30 am – 6.00 am we were awoken with constant door slamming on our floor which would go on for hours. And note: when I say LOUD door slamming I mean LOUD. 
The problem is two fold:
1) We checked out the rest of the hotel and it was pretty much the same. Each of the small floors in Morgans has a service door that house keeping and the like use constantly, going in and out like flies and slamming the door each time;
2) The doors of all the hotel rooms themselves slam loudly like there is no tomorrow too, so you get the double effect from guests going in and out of their rooms as well. 
Appears none of the doors in Morgans have a slow release or pressure release on them and certainly no door sweepers or sealing around the door frames. Its like a gunshot going off every time one closes. 
To put this into perspective, after a late first night at the Hotel, my girlfriend and I got woken up at 5.30 am or so. After putting up with it for 2 hours we got up and went for a walk around the city. I came back at 11 am to try and get a couple of hours sleep, but in the first hour I counted 38 times (!) the door loudly slamming from the service room down the hallway on our floor. And that’s not including any slamming from guest doors. 
Look, the hotel is nice enough, save for the doors the rooms are ok too, staff pretty good (although there was no offer to rectify things when I raised it with front desk staff after our second night of woe), the breakfast is good and it’s a great location. But be warned, if you are looking for a decent night’s sleep, you might not get it at Morgans if our “door slamming” experience is anything to go by. 
One final point: I live on a highway, with a lot of traffic noise and in a building that has a lot of late night parties. Been there for 4 years so I am not pretentious or anything when it comes to a restful night. But the problem of doors slamming loudly every couple of minutes for hour after hour was just way too much to bear at Morgans. We moved out after our first two nights, and headed back to the Chandler – a welcome friend where we could get a full night’s sleep.

title: “Clean and comfortable”
text: The least attractive part of this hotel is the street on which it is located. The interior is an oasis--clean, attractive, modern. The breakfast was basic but free. Room busy but not unmanageable. Staff friendly and efficient. Excellent location for restaurants and attractions.

title: “Roof Top Bar”
text: Press is without the best Rooftop Bar with the Best View in New York City

title: “Don't eat the breakfast!!!”
text:
The rooms were renovated and pretty nice... however our air conditioning kept making some obnoxious noise that made it hard to fall asleep. I took it apart and couldn't fix it.
My girlfriend and I woke up in the morning to get breakfast. We walked downstairs and saw a small buffet with orange juice, milk, small boxes of cereal, some bread and a toaster, and some bacon. All of this food was sitting out in the open not being warmed. They had a few other things I don't specifically recall. The things you would typically expect from a free continental breakfast.
We ate our food and after 5-10 minutes a woman came out and asked us if we were okay. We finished eating and to my astonishment she came and handed us a bill for $30. I about had an aneursym. The food wasn't even worth $10.
This is basically a scam. Any reasonable person would assume a hotel charging $160 a night offering crappy breakfast options is offering it for free. There were no signs anywhere advertising the cost of breakfast. I would have rather paid $30 for a Mcdonalds breakfast.
They also try to rip people off with $10 parking too. If I'm spending $160 for a hotel then don't try and nickel and dime me. If you're going to charge $30 a two person breakfast then can I at least get some freakin pancakes or some cooked food? Is that too much to ask for? 
I won't be staying at any Crowne Plaza hotels again... and I hope others won't either.

title: “When I stay in san diego, I always stay here”
text: I love this hotel, small, charming, clean, cute, great view, peacefull courtyard. When I stay here i usually bring a friend and they love it. Its right across from the beach, and super close to tons of restaurants and shops. You cant go wrong.

title: “Good but wouldn't pay full price”
text:
I got the hotel through priceline at what is a relative steal, given that their rooms generally range from $250 - $350 and I didn't even pay half that.
The first room we were put in was right by some HUGE air handlers right outside the window and it was insanely noisy, so I asked for a change and was moved to the 10th floor, 2 rooms down from the presidential suite. This room was much more quiet but still had some noise in the bathroom, kind of like the fan was always on. I didn't complain since this noise was easily muted by keeping the bathroom door closed. The ait conditioner being inside the room is also quite noisy but you get used to it. I still think the best solution is central air like at the Omni @ Cnn Center.
The beverage and newspaper service in the morning is nice, but unlike the Omni, you can only select from Coffee or Tea, not juices and the like.
There were two really bright spots. I struck up a conversation with a security officer for the hotel and he was really nice and even gave me a guided tour.
The other bright spot was the Sunday BRUNCH!!! It is $50/person but the champagne is flowing from the moment you sit down. They have assorted shrimp and a seafood salad, along with some sushi and raw oysters. There are soups, bread, smoked salmon, and cheeses...all as appetizers. You then order your main course, I had a marvelous crab cake, but you can select from eggs, steaks, or seafood (the menu is quite limited, however . . . maybe 12 items to pick from). Then comes dessert which you have to see to believe. They are almost too pretty to eat. Throughout the meal they had a flautist and guitarist playing really pleasant music.

title: “Definitely not a four star”
text:
We booked through Hotwire for a 4 star hotel in the empire state building area, and this is the hotel we got. The location was convenient for what we needed, and since we stayed only one night (sat) we had free street parking right outside the hotel which was really nice. We arrived around 7pm and there was a lot of parking available. 
Aside from the location, I did not like this hotel. The service was fine, but the room was pretty bad. I would definitely say this hotel is a 3 star - 3.5 star at best. The room was actually pretty big for a New York hotel and at first glance it seems ok, but upon further inspection the blanket was dirty, the ipod player didn't work, there's a sketchy looking couch, the shower didn't drain at all. The hotel just felt dirty. 
I would say I'm definitely picky when it comes to hotels, and I usually stay at 4-5 star hotels. Its an ok hotel, just not 4 star for sure.

title: “pleasantly surprised”
text:
to be honest I wasn't expecting much for $175 in Manhattan bt i picked it based on the proximity (across the street) from Penn Station.
However the room was large, with a nice sofa and a desk, in attractive, contemporary design (they must be upgrading the rooms- some reviews talk about run-down rooms but mine was fresh and beautiful).
Nice touches were the iPod docking station and the windows that open for some fresh air (and NYC noise). The gym was adequate. I wouldn't hesitate to stay again, even if I don;t have to be at Penn.

title: “First Courtyard in San Antonio”
text: Frequent visitor to San Antonio but first at this hotel. Above average hotel ( but not 4 dots) in a location that is nice for a short walk to Market Square and a longer but reasonable walk to the Riverwalk. Convenient to I-35 exit and parking is no problem, unlike the maze of streets downtown and expensive valet parking, This hotel is great for those commuting South to work outside of downtown. Rooms are just ho-hum - nothing special (for a Marriott). I had a handicap room that had a wheelchair accessible shower and built-in seat. One problem with a shower you can roll in a wheelchair, is no real lip to keep water in. The floor was puddled until I learned to better manage the shower stream. The new lobby design is good with a limited food and beverage selection. Overall a good hotel for business trip. This is the 7th hotel I have stayed in San Antonio and this ranks mid-pack at 4th. The courtyard in the center of the hotel seems inviting with nice outdoor areas, but did not spend time there.

title: “Should let guests know about conferences”
text: We stayed at the hotel during a Furry convention. There were hundreds of people running around in animal costumes. The nature of the conference didn't bother us; however, the convention guests seemed to completely overrun the hotel, were oblivious that others were staying there and the hotel staff did not do anything about it. For example, there were several organized meetings held in the lobby - if you were in the hotel bar, it was very distracting. In addition, the costumed characters were very aggressive in how they approached guests - coming up and trying to give people hugs. Several times we had to actively avoid being approached. It was very disconcerting and had we known about the event, we would have stayed elsewhere.

title: “Perfect location to see washington”
text:
We stayed at the Omni Shoreham hotel for 5 nights at the end of July 2008. This is a beautiful hotel. It was very easy to get to from the airport by shuttle bus. The room we had was very comfortable with a huge double bed and I had my very own walk in wardrobe which was great. The bathroom was very stylish. The only down side was we didnt have a very nice view from our window as it looked directly out onto lots of air conditioning things, so couldnt really see anything, but that was okay we were not there to look out the window as we had planned lots to see in Washington and would only be using the hotel as our base.
The location couldnt have been better there was a subway just across the road it took us a few minutes to get a train into the centre of washington. We used it a lot as it was so convienant and really cheep to get around. One of the open top bus tours also stops outside the hotel too so you can use that to hop on and off for 2 days if you want to. There is a really nice restaurant type dinner across the road if you do not want to eat in the hotel. The location for us was most important this ticked all our boxes it was quiet, friendly and the rooms were very comfortable after a hard day sight seeing. I would definatly go back again

title: “Excellent experience in NYC”
text: We had a great experience at the hotel from the front door till our check out.......No complaints..met every expectations......

title: “Nice for the Price”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Wellington for two weeks while in NY on business. We used to live a block away, so we know and love the neighborhood. We stayed in a 1 bedroom suite, which was very spacious and perfect for a long trip. The hotel could definitely use some renovations. The carpet in the hallways are worn and the elevators are slow. There was some rust in the bathroom, but everything else was clean. The lobby is always crowded, and it seems to be a hotel with a lot of group bookings. If you want a good hotel for the price, though, it was a nice stay.

title: “Don't even THINK of staying here...”
text: My adult son and I stayed here one night. The rooms were filthy, including hallways, carpet, bedding, and walls, but the price was too good to pass up. Well, we should have passed. On returning to our room late at night, we discovered our electronic door lock no longer worked. After about 40 min. of running back and forth from the lobby to our rooms to prove to the clerk that our door lock did not work, the clerk gave us another room for the night. We slept in our day-old clothes with all our luggage in the original room: no toiletries and had to forgo vital nighttime medications. Harry, the morning clerk, refused to comp our room, stating that he comped the first room (well duh, we couldn't get in), but we would be charged for the alternate room, regardless of our not having our possessions with us. I called Motel 6's guest relations while standing in front of him, filed a complaint, and made it clear I would be requesting a chargeback from my CC company. Harry stood his ground. As we left, another guest who was checking out told us that he had run into similar problems with the (family owned?) management: "They don't budge an inch."

title: “BRILLIANT LITTLE GEM”
text:
just returned from a great 4 nights at the Library. Could ramble on for ever but suffice it to say that we would recommend this hotel for anyone wanting a quiet retreat in the midst of mayhem. Staff could not have been more helpful, breakfast superb, and wine every evening most welcome. If there is a downside...and there aways must be somewhere I suppose..the rooms are small but really not a problem and, of course slightly noisy at night (no surprise in NYC!)
but this is the place to stay

title: “Location Location Location”
text: We visit San Diego several times a year and always stay at Diamond Head Inn. We love having a kitchenette plus being so close to the boardwalk. The rooms are large and convenient to places in the area. Walking the board walk is a must both for exercise and experiencing the "culture". GThere are great restaurants along the way plus great coffee places. The continental breakfast isn't much but at least something to start the day.

title: “Nice staff, grand old hotel but needs a better breakfast”
text: Enjoyed the Adolphus over all and found the staff friendly and helpful. The room wasn't as updated as others (TV was old and pointed away from the bed), but held the charm of an older property. Only complaint is that the breakfast buffet was one step above a two-star chain. The hotel deserves a grand buffet in the European tradition to match its elegance.

title: “Poor customer service for families”
text:
I was given a handicapped bathroom when the front desk knew I had 2 kids.
It is so slippery and dangerous cause there is no eat to stop the water from flowing all inside the bathroom and into the small room itself
If you have a family don't bother coming there go to Marriott they treat you better and understand how dangerous it is .
If my daughter fell and hurt herself I would have sued them for putting me in this room and telling me there is no other room . We are full.

title: “We Were Not Disappointed!”
text: Often staying downtown means an older hotel building with smaller room. Not the case at the Joule. You will have the convenience of staying downtown but the luxury of a modern, spacious and beautiful room. I think the room would be best described as SEXY! Although the Joule is in the heart of downtown, the room was extremely quiet and great block out blinds. We slept sooo well. The fitness facility is one of the best I have seen in a boutique hotel and open 24hours. I loved the pool area...felt like I was in West Hollywood. Only suggestion to the hotel is turn the heat up on the pool a few more degrees. We will definitely be staying at the Joule the next time we are in Dallas!

title: “Still my favorite SL hotel but management seriously needs to pay attention”
text:
My wife and I have been comming to this hotel for her birthday in July for years. I have stayed in hotels all over the city and this is one of my favorites. The rooms are spacious with an ocean view to die for. You could not pick a better central location to shop and tour from with the Bart and trolly car line terminating at the front door. 
Our most recent trip was marred by serious management lapses that I have never experienced before. A few years ago the hotel turned it's famous revolving roof restaurant into a private club for executive level guest. It is a fabulous treat to have breakfast and cocktails there while enjoying great veiws. Unfortuantely the hotel did not exercising any control over the club and it was over run by large families with out of control children who made the club their only vacation destination. What has always been a pleasant retreat became a zoo. A number of couples complained to the manager but nothing was done to correct the problem. I will certainly give the Hyatt staff another chance but they lose a star this year.

title: “Great location and room if you go at the right time of year”
text:
I own several timeshares and rented a one-bedroom suite with two bathrooms from an owner at Manhattan Club. RCI is the timeshare company for all suites except the penthouse suites, which is affiliated with Interval International timeshare management.
This is a great property on West 56th and 7th Ave.-near Carnegie Hall, across from Redeye Grill. Easy walk to small grocery and Duane Reed pharmacy/sundry stores. 
I stayed here before in a studio suite, which is okay for a couple but crowded if you bring a grandchild. The one bedroom suite with 2 baths is large for NYC with nice kitchenette, dining table with 4 chairs. Plenty of dresser drawers and two closets. Best king sized bed I have ever had in a hotel,too. The sheets had several large tears in them but were soft.
Only problems were:
1. The elevators are very slow and crowded. Take your chance at the lobby elevator or the service elevator and hope for the best.When we were there, one of the lobby elevators was out of service for "improvements". A staff member told us the improvements would make the elevator nicer but would have no affect on speed - too bad!
2. Climate control can be a problem depending on time of year.
We stayed in April and the rooms were VERY hot. You can open the windows but we had a room facing another building and ventilation was not great even when we had all four windows open. The temperature outside was between 48 and 62 F. We requested a fan but were told all of the fans were loaned out already for each day of our 3 night stay. We requested a fan twice a day for 3 days with no luck, although everyone was very polite. Why not put two fans in each room? It would have made our stay so much more comfortable. Management and the bell man told us they were not required to turn the air condioner on until late May. They said since this is a very old building there are only two pipes instead of four, which means they could turn on heat for the cooler months and A/C for the warmer months but never a choice of heat or A/C at all times. Everyone in the building was complaining of being too hot. We were considering purchasing a timeshare here, but the lack of individual climate control changed our minds. I would stay here only in December through March (good bet for the heater to be on) or June-August (good bet for the a/c to be on). 
The housekeeping was excellent, bathrooms were clean and of adequate size. Only complaint in bathroom is that there is a pedestal sink and absolutely no cabinet or stand to put toiletries. No hook on back of bathroom door to hold a hanging toiletry case either. Two nice terry robes were provided but only one hook in the small bath on the wall to hang one robe. The kitchenette had microwave,coffeemaker,small refrigerator, dishwasher, sink and small supply of dishes,bowls,plates and utencils.Maid service was provided daily (unusual for a timeshare) and soundproofing is good between rooms. If you close the windows, you hear minimal Manhattan street noise like horns and sirens. We ended up leaving all windows open to keep the room cooler. We were awakened by construction noise which we assumed were related to sandblasting since sand started coming through the opened windows on two mornings of our 3 night stay. We had to close the windows and leave until later in the day. There is a nice exercise room and business center, along with an owner's lounge on the 26th floor. Wireless internet was free and worked well in our suite.
The "Penthouse suites" have access to owners or their guests by a key in the elevator on the 26th floor. I don't know if there are similar climate control problems but there are two terraces (north and south) with lovely views. Only problem is the very loud air handlers on the roof near both terraces that make conversation difficult due to noise. 
I would stay again but only during months when heat or A/C would be on.

title: “Great value for a short stay”
text:
This is the perfect budget hotel for a short stay but if you are staying longer than 4 days then you may want to look for a place with a few more facilities.
Friendly staff and the room was exactly what we expected. Basic but clean and tidy. We stayed for 3 nights (4 days) and found by the end that we missed having more room facilities and a bar/lounge to collapse in at the end of the day after sightseeing before heading our for the evening.
For the price this has a great location and does exactly what you would expect - a place to sleep at the end of a busy day. The local bars & restaurants are also excellent value for money.

title: “The best airport hotel I have ever stayed at”
