text: This place is great. When traveling, it is so refreshing to have an experience such as this hotel. Every staff member we encountered was enthusiastic, helpful and pleasant. The location in proximity to the airport is good and the shuttle drivers pleasant and helpful. Our room was spacious, clean and comfortable. We actually stayed here traveling to and from our destination and both visits were equally pleasant.

title: “Renovated, what year was that?”
text: True: location is great. Otherwise, very tired and not too clean...

title: “Great location, nice big rooms”
text: We spent 3 nights at the Hilton Club in NYC earlier this week and just loved it. They have a super easy check-in on the 37th floor along with a great continental breakfast and evening appetizer buffet along with wine and beer. Soft drinks, coffee, tea and water are available 24 hours a day. The elevator bank was easy as it just went to 10 of the floors. We were able to walk to every destination except the 911 Memorial. The guest rooms were quite large, with a great flat screen TV, Bose radio, and well equipped bathroom. I would definitely stay again.

title: “Superb in every way...location, staff and surprise upgrade”
text:
In a real neighborhood, the hotel is one block to the subway and a short walk to Central Park.
Booked a superior king and opened door to a suite...nice
The staff couldn't have been nicer...yes, it's a bit old, but it has old school NY charm

title: “The secret is out!!!!!!!!!”
text: Last year when I visited, the hotel was not full. Over this past weekend and last Tuesday night it was really full. Clean cozy atmosphere. A well ventilated comfortable room, an amazingly comfortable bed I(as comfy as mine at home!) A decent free contintental breakfast, including 3 different juices, toast, hot and cold cereal, bagels, muffins. Nice shampoo, conditioner, and 2 soaps. I am happy that I stayed. No pressure to check out a bit after 11:00 and check this out... The clerk at the front desk remembered my name!!! Boy was I impressed. Oh did I mention free parking while away and free airport shuttle. One happy camper, that's me.

title: “Mostly Positive Experience”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for four weeks during a business trip.
Positives: The staff, including front desk, cleaning personnel, and valet attendants were very friendly and helpful with directions, restaurant recommendations, and other needs.
There is a CVS right next door with some frozen/refrigerated foods, canned/bottled beverages, and boxed (cereals, etc.) foods available. It was very convenient. Also, there are several restaurants within walking distance from the hotel.
The hotel also has two computers and a printer available with free Internet access in the "business center" on the 2nd floor. There was also an Internet connection in the room; I think it was free, but I'm not sure. The hotel also had laundry facilities on two floors, making it extra convenient for extended stay travelers. The free breakfast seemed to have basically the same items every day including eggs, biscuits, sausage, cereals, waffles, and an assortment of breads. The hotel offers hospitality nights two days a week including a free dinner.
The TV in my room didn't receive a couple of the channels listed as available. I notified the front desk one morning on my way out and by that afternoon when I returned the problem was fixed. Also, my garbage disposal didn't work but was fixed the same day I reported it. Both times, I received a phone message from staff members letting me know that the problem had been fixed and to call them directly if I had anymore trouble. The only other complaint about the room was that the closet doors often slid out of the tracks. One morning I tried to fix it but didn't have time - when I returned it was back on track. I assume the cleaning lady saw it and took care of it.
Negatives: A couple of mornings I was awakened between 4 -5 by a loud noise outside my window. I was on the alley side of the hotel and I assume it was some sort of garbage truck.

title: “Good Value”
text: The price was reasonable for DC standard. The hotel is fairly close to everything that you might want to see....the Mall for example...It was relatively cheaper than others. The room was comfortable and the staff was friendly. There is nothing particularly special really. You will get a good night of sleep. I would stay here again when I am in DC.

title: “Good Value, Clean and Comfortable”
text:
We enjoyed our 2010 stay at Comfort Suites so much that we booked 3 nights for our return to Indianapolis. The value for the price paid was excellent. The hotel is holding up well, and I encourage the staff to keep it well maintained. We will certainly return again.
My earlier assessment is still valid regarding the comfortable night's sleep, pleasant sitting area in the room, clean bathroom, and complimentary breakfast; I won't waste time and text writing the same except to say that all aspects were good.
The hotel is not downtown, but the few miles is easily manageable for visits to the Indiana state capitol, the President Benjamin Harrison home, Crown Hill Cemetery, the downtown canal and parks.

title: “Outstanding! Great view, great location, great value.”
text: We wanted a clean, comfortable room on the San Diego beach. We found it. Everything was perfect on our 3 night stay. Great shops and restaurants right on the boardwalk next to the hotel. You don't even need shoes to go to the beach. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “Hotel and Staff are great”
text: I cannot say enough good things about this hotel. It is a gem in the city of Chicago. Stay here if you can the service is great, the location is great, the rates are fair and a parking ramp is a couple of blocks away with a quick shop a half a block away. If possible get one of the corner rooms. EK

title: “Good Hotel, Good Value, Great Location”
text:
The hotel is clean, reasonably priced for mid-town. Rooms aren't huge, but as I was there to see the city, it was only really for sleeping. Service was great. 
The best part is the great location. You are very close to 5th ave, Empire State, Macy's, and Penn Station. Sort walking distance to Grand Central, NY Public Library, and Time Square. Subway station right at the end of the street which can take you to Central Park, or down to the village. 
Definitely recommend. Great value for money.

title: “You Get What You Pay For”
text:
I decided to take a long weekend trip for my birthday to San Francisco since I had never been there before. I found a great deal for this hotel and read from other reviews that it was a nice clean hotel and great for the price. That was not the case. This place was extremely filthy, noisy and not so safe of an area. When I first walked into my room, I was greeted a roach! 
The only good thing that I can say is that the front desk staff were amazing. They tried to help as best as they could by giving me a different room, the only problem was that the room faced a parking garage and a dumpster that had to be emptied every other day at about 5 am! 
Next time I go I will spend the extra money to guarantee that I'm staying someplace that I know I'm going to be comfortable.

title: “No one does it better than the Ritz-an oasis away from home!”
text:
My husband and I were attending a convention in Boston and had originally booked a room at the Mandarin Oriental (see MO review entitled, "Dirty and Disappointing"). As you may surmise from the title, the Mandarin Oriental was awful. Indeed, it was one of the worst hotel experiences I have ever had and for the first and only time in my life, I actually left a hotel.
Angry, exhausted, and frustrated, the first alternative hotel I thought of was the Ritz Carlton. The Ritz has never disappointed me...and this time was no exception. I stepped into the lobby, took a deep breath of that fabulous "Ritz smell" and said, " I should never have strayed!" I was immediately invited to sit down and the front desk agent leaned toward me and said with genuine concern, "We were expecting you...AMEX just called to say you were on your way...what happened?" As I spilled the horror story that was my Mandarin Oriental experience, the concierge came up behind me with a glass of champagne with a perfect berry floating delicately and said, "I thought you may enjoy this." THIS IS HOW TO MAKE A GUEST FEEL LOVED! I literally felt like I had come home! The whole hotel is soothing...to the eye, the nose, and the soul! In short, no one does guest service like the Ritz....it is its specialty, its brand, and its pleasure.

title: “Dream hotel down town”
text: My boyfriend and I has stayed here for a weekend in August. We were just amazed with the hotel experience overall. One of the best weekends we've had this summer. The rooms were literally like being in a cloud. The dream hotel was not only SUPER CLEAN but very comfortable. The showers were so modern and up to date. The service was excellent. Gina and Andy who were at the front desk were very professional and super friendly. They welcomed us as soon as we arrived and made us feel like royalty. We ended up going to the pool party that they had on Monday which was a great time. Highly reccomend and we will be staying there again.

title: “Perfect Spot”
text: Loved everything about the stay - there for the Nike Woman's Marathon - Lovely location would go again - very nice -

title: “Beautiful hotel, excellent customer service”
text:
Gorgeous accommodations. Pleasant and professional staff. Huge fitness center with a plethora of machines & free weights. Only 2 blocks away from Phoenicia--the most incredible specialty food store (www.phoeniciafoods.com). Very quiet and comfortable beds.
Areas for improvement: 
$14.95/day for internet access is steep, and it was sometimes intermittent
Can't change the time on the alarm clock (and it was wrong)

title: “Much nicer than I expected”
text: We stayed two nights since we were in town for a wedding. The price was very good considering how expensive the hotels are in NYC. I liked being in the heart of the financial district - it was easy taxi ride to both the lower east side and Brooklyn where we needed to be for the wedding and rehearsal dinner. I liked strolling down to the Sea Port where we could chill out, have brunch and people watch on Saturday before the wedding. The desk clerks were great. We were sorry the hotel restaurant was closed for renovations. The room was clean, attractive and comfortable. Noise could be heard from the hallway, but not thru the walls. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Why we keep coming back.”
text:
I've stayed here multiple times and always find a reason to return. I do suggest the Ocean Front Rooms on the 2nd and 3rd floor. A never ending story plays out in front of you on the boardwalk. Seems to be a great mix of families, surfers, couples, youth, life guards, and others. Centrally located, plenty of restaurants, grocery store, shopping etc. The sound of the ocean is incredible at night.
The front desk staff have always been fantastic to work with. They are always willing to help with any situation. The parking garage is well worth the daily rate.
It is not the quietest, quaintest location. There is lots of action in the area, so if you are looking for quiet, solitude, this may not be the best location for you.

title: “Always a pleasure and a class act”
text:
I've stayed many times at the Westin Riverwalk in San Antonio and will do so again. I can always count on a pleasurable experience -- from the service of staff members like Monica Castillo in the convention services department to the front desk staff to the concierge to the wait staff in their wonderful Zocca restaurant. (By the way, this is one of the nicest Italian restaurants in the city, and their weekend brunch is a real treat as well. Casual, classy ambience.)
On this last trip, Wendy at the front desk was friendly and helpful, pointing out that I could sign up for the hotel's rewards program. 
Service and a relaxing first-class experience set the Westin apart. You won't have to worry about noisy, raucous guests in the poor or the bar or lobby. And, of course, it's right on the Riverwalk. On that point, one more thing, you're right on the Riverwalk with a gorgeous restaurant bar and patio right on the river's edge. But you far from the hullabaloo of the River Walk further east and north and its clubs and restaurants. Not that there's anything wrong with that party scene. And if you want to partake in it, it's just a short, delightful stroll away.

title: “Bed Bugs! Insulting management!”
text:
I stayed here last week. I woke up on Tuesday morning and found blood spots on the sheets. I knew that this was a sure sign of bed bugs, so I kept watch and slept rather poorly on Tuesday night. I woke up a bit past mid night and found the actual bug on my leg.
While the front desk did move me to another room, I was told that a manager would be contacting me. When I hadn't heard from them on Thursday evening, I called them. The manager of the hotel only kept saying "what do you want me to do?". I told him that I should be compensated by the hassle of drying, washing, and laundering everything to an extreme before I walked into my house so as not to bring the bed bugs into my own home... not to mention the WORRY of bringing these things with me. The manager questioned the validity of my claim and offered drink coupons... (!!!) This was extremely insulting. I informed the management that the sheets still have the blood spots on them, even if the "maintenance crew" didn't see the actual bugs. The manager even suggested that "it would not have been a bad idea" to carry the bed bug with me as proof!
The other reviews here are also true. It is basically a motel. They have taken pictures of the only nice spots of their hotel (lobby and roof top dining area). The courtyard where the rooms are is a giant parking lot. The rooms are cramped and you have that dirty sense when you walk into them.
This is the very first time I have ever written a review or complaint. It's not my way to complain or be indignant. I have stayed in many hotels both for business and pleasure. But I felt compelled to come here after my experience. 
In the end, I was given nothing but a room change and an insulting experience.

title: “Quite a nice place to stay in Dupont Circle / Kalorama”
text:
I was part of an interview committee which met candidates in D.C., and the search firm suggested this hotel. Very comfortable, downright luxurious! I had a bedroom and a little office area off the bedroom -- with a view of Connecticut Street.
I would definitely stay here again if the neighborhood were convenient for a goal I had in D.C.
The front desk was very helpful.
I'm always annoyed that places this nice charge separately for wifi. Roll it in, people! 
The only other negative comment to make is that the restaurant is currently closed for renovation -- but they still advertise the space (and it's complimentary wifi!) in the elevators.

title: “Perfection”
text:
Came in town when the temperatures soared close to 100...but that didn't stop us because we were just a short walk from the beach, half a block from the train just a little further to buses that make the sight seeing painless and the staff was always there with helpful ideas and directions!
Could not have been happier with the room...which we returned to often to cool off and relax before heading out for more shopping and great restaurants just steps away from our front dorr! Can't wait to return and get in everything we weren't able to squeeze in this time!

title: “basic room”
text:
close to everything
room is small
don't like that they didn't 2 beds, I have to share my bed with sister
friendly employees
love the refill water bottle
My room was clean. 
Lobby have a computer area
complimentary breakfast

title: “Rough but Fair”
text:
Nobody is perfect, and when you are booking a $100 per night hotel in San Diego you get what you pay for.
The service isn't sterling, but it's not outwardly rude either. The Keepers are simply functional in their job duties so if you keep your expectations level you won't be dissapointed. 
The room was probably a bit below average. I'd measure it at about 10X15 and was very average in it's appointments. The bed was large and fairly comfortable, there was no microwave or coffee maker, but they did give me an iron and board for my entire 5 day stay. Basically the room was cramped but not uncomfortable.
The location has it's ups and downs as well. Planes land less than a mile away and the train runs about 100 yards in the other direction. Pacific Blvd is never quiet and the neighborhood isn't upscale. That said - I never felt as though my sleep was interrupted or that I was in a particularly seedy part of town.
The bottom line here is that if you book this place you have no business expecting top tier appointments and service. It's a $100 motel in San Diego. I enjoyed my stay knowing that the extra C-note per night was spent on enjoying my time in one of America's best cities.

title: “Nice, not great”
text:
Because of its location and its ability to accommodate business conferences, this Marriott can command high rates. Many attractions of the Inner Harbor are within easy walking distance.
On the positive side: our room was very nice, and the bed was comfortable. Staff members (front desk, concierge, bell station, housekeeping, bar, food service) were without exception pleasant, knowledgeable, and professional. 
A few disappointments: most notably, the swimming pool is very small and unappealing. Minor disappointments: lumpy pillows, and no video checkout.
One peeve: Wifi is available, but at a charge of $12.95 a day -- and the day runs from noon to noon. Nowadays, when free wifi is the norm at moderate and even low-cost hotel chains, charging for wifi is a rip-off.

title: “Well appointed and located hotel”
text:
This is a decent hotel which, though not one possessing any out-of-the-ordinary character, would make for a good base for tourists or business-people visiting downtown Washington DC. 
The location is good: within easy reach of the excellent metro and reasonable walking distance to most DC tourist sites and business areas. The only real downside is that at weekends the surrounding area is dead, with many of the shops, cafes and restaurants closing when the city's employees disappear. That, though, is a problem which I imagine is common to many or most of downtown DC's hotels. 
Despite an unprepossessing concrete exterior, the lobby has an appealing swankiness, mainly because of the armies of government officials and conference goers strutting self-importantly around the place. The bar - if you can stomach the predictably prohibitive prices - makes a decent spot for a short bout of people-spotting.
My standard king-size room was spacious, well-appointed, clean and comfortable. 
All in all, a good hotel, and certainly worth the $87 per night I paid on Priceline.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text: The staff could not have been nicer or more accommodating. The hotel was been recently renovated...it is very contemporary, but still very comfortable with a cozy ambiance. We had a wonderful and relaxing stay. It is in a great location close to the Boston Common. The parking garage is attached and was included in our package. We will surely visit this hotel again in the future.

title: “Great visit to Big Apple”
text:
Stayed at the Westin Times Square 11-19 Sept 2005. I had seen some very mixed revues and was a little aprehensive. I need not have been. The hotel was great, in an excellent location in the centre of the city.
The bed - well it really was heavenly as described. We asked for a fridge for the room and one was supplied (not wanting to open the drinks unit). Excellently located for the sites and the underground. Great visit had previously booked for Chicago (Excellent show) and at the last minute on our final Saturday thought we would like to see Mama Mia (didnt think we stood a chance) but we asked and we got great seats (at a price 150 dollars each) but it was worth it. Thanks Westin, we will come again

title: “Great location”
text: We booked a marina view room at The Dana in early June. After an early morning drive from the Phoenix area, we arrived in San Diego to a traffic nightmare. A marathon was occuring right in the area of the hotel! After 1.5 hours on the freeway wihin 500 yards of our exit we made it to the beutiful grounds of The Dana. We were hoping they had a room available for early check-in and the girl at the counter did'nt dissapoint. We were given a secong floor marina view room in the original section of the hotel. The rooms are very small when configured with two beds like ours was. But we knew we would be out playing in the great San Diego weather and did'nt let it bother us. The room was clean, well kept, updated and cozy. The beds were very comfortable .This hotel property is one of the best locations in all of San Diego. The Dana is directly across the street from Sea World, and easily walkable with kids. You are also right near freeway interchanges which makes getting to other areas incredibly easy. Mission beach is located right down the street, and their are plenty of good places to eat nearby. Our experience here was great and we would definately stay here again.

title: “Old, unsafe area”
text: I checked in late and the front desk was very accomodating, offering me a shuttle to the local restaraunt area. That is where it ended. The room was older, worn looking. The tub had huge black hairs on the curtains. Parking was poor. There was no room in the tiny lot so I had to park in the alley near the hotel. I was going to walk the 4 blocks back from the restaraunt, but felt unsafe, so took a 4 block cab ride, since shuttle service ended at 9:30. The hotel was ok, the staff was ok, but the area is TERRIBLE.

title: “Nice place to stay.”
text: We went for a night out on the town. It was very centrally located for drinks, dinner, our show and night life. There is lots of places to go within a short walk. Great place to stay.

title: “Comfortable and Convenient”
text:
This is a centrally located hotel convenient to major NYC activities. Check in was very friendly and efficient. My room with a king-sized bed was clean, comfortable and bigger than many New York hotel rooms. Considering how busy the area is, the room was surprisingly quiet. Having a complimentary breakfast provided every morning is a bonus even though there were some problems: line-ups no matter what time I arrived and the food was not hot. I never had a problem finding a seat. 
Because I was in NYC with extended family whom I don't see often, this hotel had limitations because there is no comfortable area in the hotel to sit and chat, have a snack or drink and relax. The lobby is small and not set up for people having long conversations. We found ourselves sitting in one of our guestrooms which did not have enough chairs for this kind of visiting. However, people who spend their time going to shows, sightseeing, etc. will find the hotel an excellent choice.

title: “Confortable place to spend the night before our cruise”
text: We used this hotel as a stop over to board our cruise. We found our room to be very clean and confortable. We had a room overlooking LAX landing strip. I really enjoyed watching the planes land. There was a little bit of extra noise, but after a while we didn't really notice it.

title: “Was NOT impressed with the service I received.”
text:
We requested a room with two beds as we were two friends travelling together..... This room was booked months ago, so plenty of time for them to try and sort out this 'request' (Also the only hotel on how whole trip that wasn't able to fill this 'request') We checked in early so we understood our room wasn't ready.... we left our bags and went for something to eat. Came back 1/2 hr after check in time...... room still not ready....We get to the room cleaner is still there cleaning and they've given us the wrong room!!! Although 3-4 people standing behind the front desk, we still have to wait up to 20 mins before someone even says hello. 
I was NOT impressed with this hotel; it was the most expensive hotel I've staying in in NYC in the last 4 months!! Way better hotels out there, don't waste your money.

title: “Highly Recommended”
text:
I stayed at the Belvedere from 7th to 12th May with my elderly Mother. I was a little concerned about reviews I had read regarding the lifts etc however we were both delighted with the accommodation and staff and had no problems with the lifts. They are quite small and slow at busy times but then they would be in any hotel. 
The rooms are a little shabby but were clean and comfortable. Bedding and towels were changed daily and the room was also cleaned daily. Apparently some rooms have been refurbished so may be worth asking about them.
The breakfast in the hotel cafe was excellent value offering two options, cold buffet or hot buffet. 
Location was excellent, very near 'restaraunt row' and theatreland. Easy walking to Times Square and within a short taxi ride to many 'must see' locations.
I would have no hesitation in recommending this hotel, very good value for money.

title: “Chris & Phil Wallsend UK”
text: Stopped at the Back Bay Hotel to celebrate our 30th wedding anniversary, great location. On checking in, which was a breeze and to our surprise a bottle of wine and chocolates were in our room on the Sunday, thanks so much Evan . Big thanks to Nikki concierge who was brilliant and funny and helped us a great deal with booking tours. Another big thank you to all the staff, bar tenders, bell hops & cleaning staff nothing was too much trouble, fantatstic staff you should all be proud of yourselves, would recommend this hotel

title: “OK but isolated”
text: The main drawback of Denver Tech Center is its remoteness from downtown Denver and anything picturesque. The hotel is, like everything else at DTC, modern and efficient and is physically located near the Hyatt and Marriott. If you are going there solely for business you won't be disappointed. High speed internet access was a little flakey and just a tad pricey. The in-house restaurant is also somewhat over-priced for what it offers, perhaps because of the absence of much local competition. But Financial Plaza, ten minutes's walk away has a reasonable range of local eateries.

title: “Great location, safe and good service”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights while on vacation. Used Priceline to get the room and got it for less than half price. 
The hotel is 2 blocks from the water, with nice breakfast and lunch places all around. We had a rental car so used the basement parking garage, $40 per night, but worth it for the convenience and safety. It was raining so we didn't have to get wet going to the car. I was impressed that a doorman was outside all night. We came in after 2 am and at 1 am and found him there. This is not a bad area but it is nice to know someone is out there, keeping an eye on things.
We didn't use the restaurant because it was pricey, $18 for breakfast. There is a great breakfast place just across the street, 
They upgraded us to the business level floor and our room had a view of the water. Service was great. Everyone was friendly and considering it is a busy hotel with large tour groups (buses) there all the time, that is unusual.
We've been to SFO several times and normally stay downtown. I am glad we didn't since this area is much safer to walk around at night and more convenient to park and not have to deal with traffic. It was easy to get to the bridge and up to Napa or go south to the coast and Monterey.

title: “New Property with Questionable Service at the Front Desk”
text:
This property is very new. From the moment you enter the lobby, it is apparent that the hotel is new, well designed with excellent attention to detail regarding its physical plant.
Situated in downtown San Antonio, the hotel is located right on the river walk with the associated bars, restaurants and attractions. For the tourist, it is central located to many sites of interest and for the business traveler, it is a central hub for meeting with clients not only in the city, but the outlying communities as well.
The rooms are standard fare for Embassy Suites...a living room/sitting area and a second bedroom. While smaller than most Embassy Suites rooms, the room is very clean, with above average furniture and appointments. I did have an issue with the air conditioning that required service from the hotel engineer. He was prompt, professional and fixed the problem completely within 30 minutes of the call for service.
While the hotel is new, it is apparent that many of the staff are new as well. Upon check in, not once did the front desk associate look me in the eye or address me by name, even as HHonors Gold Member. When I asked her if she could make recommendations for late night dining, she rolled her eyes at me and said, "Don't think it is a bit late to be eating?". After a long flight, it was not appreciated.
Valet parking runs $27 a day. While many people find this expensive, it is actully quite average or below average for mid/large market hotels. The valet kids hustle and provide quick service.
Overall, this is a good property with inconsistent service. This is a solid choice for the business traveler or those traveling a family. While certainly not an upscale hotel, it is new, very clean and provides excellent value.

title: “Honesty Still Abounds”
text:
We had a cruise planned and this is the perfect stop for one night before getting on the ship. The rooms are not very fancy, but are very clean and it did contain a flat screen TV. I had thought I had lost forever a very valuable and one of a kind diamond and ruby ring. I informed the desk upon leaving for the ship, heartbroken, that I had lost my ring and could not find it. Upon our return after the cruise, after a week, imagine my surprise when the manager told me they had found my ring. I was and still am elated to know that honest people still exist and can be found at the Vagabond Inn in San Pedro, CA.
Clarine Merritt

title: “Please DO NOT STAY ON this So called HOTEL & Suites!!!!”
text: Very bad all around, rooms very dirty, no a/c working. I reserved double beds and they didn't have them available so I had to settle with KING size bed. Then room that was offered, someone was already staying there. They didn't even know which room was available, so I finally got one and it was very dirty! No towels, toilet was ok, tables were not wiped and many things I don't want to spend time writing... PLEASE RECONSIDER DO NOT STAY in this PLACE NEVERRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR!!!!!!NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!!!

title: “If we're back in SF and need a place to stay, we'll look at the Argonaut Hotel.”
text:
Fisherman's Wharf might be a cheesy and touristy spot, but the Argonaut Hotel is in a great location adjacent to Ghiradelli Square and the Powell-Hyde cable car line. I was out in SF for a one day meeting at the hotel and brought my family along and extended my stay. Major SF Muni bus lines are near by and getting around town was fairly painless. Hotel staff was friendly and helpful - in particular, they were great with my kids. The hotel has an afternoon happy hour (drinks for adults and treats for kids) which offered a nice segue to dinner and other evening plans. There was also a Wii in the hotel lobby for the kids. Our room was spacious and the internet is free if you sign up for the Kimpton loyalty program.
We only had breakfast at the hotel restaurant, the Blue Mermaid, and it was good comparatively speaking.
All things considered, if you can get a "decent" rate, the Argonaut is a solid bet.

title: “Decent Hotel, Awesome location”
text: We spent 2 nights at the Marriott Downtown. The hotel is quite good. A bit aged and in need of a facelift, but it was clean and comfortable. The hot tub was broken and pool is quite small, good for kids, not adults. We had to swtich rooms as the thermostat was not working right in our room, but the staff were extremely helpful and courteous. Common areas of the hotel were nice. Perfect for a place to sleep in the heart of the action. And that is the main thing. The location is awesome. Right on the mile, Rush & Michigan. Central so you can walk to all of the shopping, to the pier/lakeshore, restos, bars, etc. Fantastic. If you are looking for a decent price, decent (but a bit aged) hotel and fantastic location, this is it.

title: “15th Anniversary Getaway”
text: We searched for months to find a nice hotel to spend a extended weekend at for our 15th Anniversary. I am so glad we found and selected this hotel. The hotel was in a perfect beautiful area. The area was growing and it was gorgeous there. The rooms were beautiful and most comfortable. The staff was friendly. The rooms were extremely quiet you did not hear your neighbors like most hotel rooms. Stayed at a 4 star hotel during the weekend and enjoyed this one better. I only paid $71.00 per night for a lake view!! My only suggestions would be to get fridge and microwaves in all the rooms, and a fan in the bathroom. Great there, will return when ever I am in the area.

title: “The Drury needs to change their slogan "The Extras aren't Extra" to "We'll get you with parking".”
text: When I found out that I will be charged almost $15 a day to park at a hotel I am already paying to stay at, it left a bad taste in my mouth. I have never been charged extra to park at a hotel before when I am paying for a room. That is tacky, I feel like I'm being fined for parking legally.

title: “This hotel exceeded our expectations.”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Abri for our 36th anniversary. From the first greeting at the front desk the friendly staff gave us exceptional services. We asked for a quiet room, and got one. The manager upgraded us to a suite without our asking and sent us a bottle of wine for our anniversary, with personal greetings!
The room itself was very comfortable, and had every amenity we could have asked for. We enjoyed the very comfortable bed as well as the two wide screen TV's. The location was perfect. We would definitely stay here again. Even though we don't live too far away, we really felt "on vacation" here at the Abri.

title: “disgusting”
text: The hotel's location is terrible. It claims to be in a super, convenient location, but the various blocks around the hotel are practically desolate or if inhabited, by no one you would like to be approached by. We booked this hotel on expedia. It cost almost 200 dollars, so you would assume it's got to be decent. we drove to the driveway of the hotel, got in and immediately we wanted to leave. The lobby was ugly (startling for a $200 a day stay). The surrounding area filled with riff raff, no place for a vacation. But we were going to put up with it. After all, it's a pain to have to move to a different hotel. But the interaction with the front desk clerk did it!!! I considered it a stroke of good luck that the clerk was so disgustingly rude. Obviously he doesn't realize he's in the service industry. He provided no service, no hospitality, only an attitude of "don't you dare bother me." His hair was oily, greasy. He was checking me in, in the midst of it, then interrupted it with another transaction and left me standing there. WHen i complained, he snapped. so we called expedia and immediately booked ourselves a different hotel. His rudeness was a stroke of luck in disguise. Believe me, the location alone will make you weep with depression. You can spend your two hundred dollars a night on a better place. we even payed the penalty just to get out of that hell hole.

title: “Comfortable place next to the River”
text: We stayed here twice during our tour of New England - at the beginning and at the end of the trip. This is a great place to stay in Boston. It is right on the Charles River so you can watch the crews rowing in the morning. It is in walking distance of MIT, Boston University and even Fenway (yes, we like to walk!). The hotel has a free shuttle that will get you to Harvard or to downtown Boston. This service is great so you don't need a hotel right in downtown Boston. The staff at the front desk is very helpful and room service is very responsive. The on-premise restaurant is a great place for breakfast. They have a continental breakfast buffet or a full breakfast buffet. While you can order off the menu, the buffets are the way to go. A good value for a great breakfast. I'd stay here the next time in Boston.

title: “Very comfy bed and room!”
text: We spent 3 nights at Cassa in June and we had a lovely experience. Everyone at the hotel was very nice from the front desk to the housekeeping to the engineer! The location was great for being near the theater district and times square. We were also very close to multiple subway lines. I was traveling with my son, husband, parents, and brother. The hotel was accommodating to all ages. The room was great. Everything was spotless including the bathroom. The shower seemed brand new with a rain shower head and sparkling glass doors (no icky shower curtains here.) We did think the towels could have been thicker and fluffier. The bed was super comfy and we slept great. We were on both the 24 and 15th floor and no issues with street noise. Our only issue was our AC. We were in NY during a heat wave and our AC broke twice. Frank the engineer came to our room immediately to work on it. It was fixed before we went to sleep and it was nice and cool, but when we woke up it was 82 degrees. We switched rooms that afternoon. We would definitely return to Cassa in the future.

title: “I loved my Suite! Beautiful and great chocolates and fruit!”
text:
I stayed at the InterContinental Chicago this past weekend. It was awesome location just steps to Michigan Avenue Deluxe Shopping, The Water Tours, The Marilyn in front of Chicago Tribune, and River Walk. 
The room was beautiful and the staff very helpful and friendly. 
I recommend this property highly.

title: “Save Your Money!!! Not Worth It!!!”
text: I stayed at the Four Seasons in New York for 2 nights, and all I can say is....Don't ever stay here. I thought it was the worst Four Seasons and Worst hotel I had ever stayed in. My room was spacious, but dirty, the wood lamp in the room was peeling and cracked, there was a paste substance that I did not know where it came from were in the cracks of the sofa. The management was not any help. They offered a small discount, but for the price I paid, which was $900 a night, was not at the least worth it. The staff were not helpful. All they did was merely apologize and that was it. The lobby was nice and clean and the food was decent, but don't judge a book by it's cover on this hotel.

title: “Our Third Stay: Love This Place”
text: We have stayed here twice before and were delighted to be upgraded to a fancy suite in the second building for our 5-day stay. If you're expecting the 5-star Ritz, this place is not for you, but we know that the hotel is clean, the service is the best, and the price (when Congress isn't in session) is right. We were doing research in the Library of Congress (across the street), so this was perfect. Will stay here again.

title: “Sofitel Stay”
text: Everything was great: room, breakfast, location, service. The package we got that included breakfast and parking was a fantastic deal, especially for a hotel like the Sofitel...hope it is offered again; I will definitely take advantage.

title: “Be aware of extra costs”
text:
I had to move room two times over 6 days because of not having the facilities I needed and had ordered. Fortunately the front desk staff were very helpful, especially Tabitha who made up for the problems. The location is the best thing about the hotel and buffet breakfast is great. Be aware that it's $10 per day extra for parking and $10 for fridge or microwave (each) if you want those in the room. I had ordered a fridge and it had insects in it as they are not always turned on and are brought to the room on request.
So I had to move on the second day. The next room I was in didn't have internet running and front desk kept saying there was something wrong with my computer - when I knew there wasn't. So next day I moved again. If it wasn't for Tabitha this place would have got a big fat zero.

title: “Worth the wait!”
text:
This hotel has been on my list to try for a number of years, but I just couldn't get a good rate. When I finally caught a deal, I booked it! Very much worth the wait! 
Room was not big, but well laid out, never felt cramped. Bathroom was very large by comparison, large sink top with room for all your "stuff", good lighting, swing out make-up mirror, shelf below for more storage, marble shower, and BIG towels! oh, and did I mention wonderful Molton Brown products? a (minor) word of warning - 4 of my 5 nights there, I thought I was hearing a faint coo coo clock and it was driving me crazy! On my last night, I finally traced it to the sound therapy machine set to a very low "rainforest"! 
The staff was wonderful! Housekeeping, front desk, bell and doormen, they all introduced themselves and asked my name and when I was planning to come back – everyone was genuinely very nice and made me feel welcome. For a hotel known for catering to the hip, fashionista crowd, this was a nice surprise!

title: “Friendly staff, nicely luxurious for the price and great location”
text:
I stayed over Thanksgiving and the hotel is in a prime location for the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade. On check-in my room wasn't quite ready (I was early) but they stow luggage and text when the room is available. I had a large King size bed room which was very clean and very comfortable (bathroom only had a shower for those who like a bath). The hotel has a large restaurant for breakfast with a buffet (not a lot of Manhattan hotels do)and my room rate included breakfast (unusual for NYC). All the staff were friendly and helpful and it was a lovely stay.
The hotel has a fitness centre and spa which I didn't use.
It is possible to book a shuttle to both JFK and Laguardia.

title: “Tight, but fun”
text:
My wife and I traveled to New York for an extra long weekend, and we stayed at The Pod Hotel based on the good rating it had and the good deal that we found. It is by no means a luxury stay (the room we got, with bathroom, was almost the only upgrade you can get), but we enjoyed it. It was almost like being in a train sleeper car, without the rumbling and squeaking. Nice little semi-public garden across the street, where we relaxed and ate once. Several restaurants on the block, and a supermarket on the corner. It was nice to be in more of a neighborhood that the last time we visited, when we were closer to Times Square. It was close to the subway, and we never took a taxi the entire time (even to & from the airport).
Nice rooftop place to look off into the neighborhood.
Overall a nice, modern, hip place to stay.

title: “Unfriendly and Far From Downtown”
text: This is a nice, if slightly dated facility. The front desk service was slow (10 minutes for check in) and unfriendly. There is a significant construction going on between the atrium and the tower which is a bit of an annoyance, but there's likely no way around it during renovations. The only other downside of the hotel is that there is nothing within walking distance. The best upside was the 102" flat screen TV in the bar.

title: “Cool and convenient”
text:
Stayed here one night before an early morning flight back to the East Coast. Decor is hip and comfortable. Bed was luxurious as was the bathroom. We didn't have a chance to eat at the hotel restaurant but it looked pretty swanky. Being in the heart of San Jose, there were quite a few options in terms of restaurants, shops, and clubs. The light rail stops right in front of the hotel which makes it convenient to get around without fighting the infamous Silicon Valley traffic.
We took our chances and booked through Hotwire. Paid $149 for a Sunday night. All in all, I would stay here again.
Loved the fact that they had a Mac and a PC in their business center - no charge for either. They also had free internet service in the rooms.

title: “Heavenly!”
text:
My husband and I have been staying in the palomar for the past week, we are very sad to be checking out to go home today. We got a lovely room on the 14th floor. I got a great deal on hotels.com as a treat to celebrate my husbands 40th birthday. When we got to our room we found a nice treat and happy birthday note, it was a lovely gesture. The rooms are beautiful and very comfortable. They have been designed well with power points next to the bed, lots of mirror space, and fab bathrooms. The beds are really comfy. The staff are lovely, in particular the lovely doorman Jean Luc who took super great care of us. He's a genuinely nice person. The daily wine reception is lovely and also the free coffee in the morning is great. There is no coffee machine in the room though, so beware all coffee addicts! Luckily for me my husband got up to go down and get the coffee each morning!! The Sable bar and kitchen is a nice spot for food and drinks, the food in particular is really exceptional though the drinks are a bit overpriced. Definitely visit the Rock Bottom brewpub across the street for excellent beer and cocktails, at a more reasonable price. The food is also really good. 
This wasn't our first stay in a kimpton hotel and certainly won't be our last. We had a wonderful time.
A tip, make sure to register for rewards on the kimpton website as you'll get free wifi!

title: “Completely Satisfied - Amazing Value”
text: We were very happy with our week long stay at The Donatello. From the moment we arrived, to the moment we left, the staff made us feel very welcome. The service was exceptional and it never faltered, even the wake up calls were pleasant. The location was great, whether we walked right down to the MUNI or needed a cab in a moment's notice. We only had one meal in the restaurant, but it was one of the best we'd had all week. The size of the room was great and the bed was extremely comfortable. Free wifi was a nice plus too. I wasn't a big fan of the shower head or rough water pressure, but this wasn't that big of a deal. I felt very safe and secure in our location, with no worries about our stay. The housekeeping staff was also very courteous and helpful! For the price, this was an amazing value and I would highly recommend it for couples or groups of friends - maybe not families with small children, if you want more to keep them occupied.

title: “Great Staycation!”
text: We live in San Diego but wanted to find a good weekend Beach Getaway! The OB Hotel was a perfect choice! It has an amazing and friendly staff! Brad, Jill & Sam were all very helpful and accommodating! The rooms are clean and cozy! I really like the fact each room has its own Fridge. It's in prime location - only steps away from the beach, shops, restaurants, and bars! Has a very cute courtyard! I LOVED laying on my bed to see the ocean and beautiful sunset! We will defininately go back this summer!

title: “Clean and quiet and a free ride to the airport via shuttle”
text:
Only stayed for a one night layover, but would recommend it. Its clean and efficient and not noisy. The beds and pillows are very comfortable and the free coffee is a nice touch. The shower is great with lots of water pressure and they were generous with the amenities.
 The bar was hopping and the hotel was decorated in chic fashion for the holidays. 
The check-in was hassle free and check out was ready under the door before leaving.
The only bummer was that the "free wifi" asks for 10.95 to be charged to the room. Lame!

title: “Second time here, still love it”
text: The experience was great. The lazy river is one of the best at the hotel chains. My favorite part of this hotel is the people. All your interactions are top notch.

title: “Very centrally located and nice staff”
text: Check-in was a breeze and the manager who checked us in was very attentive. Hotel was very convienient to Septa Transportation and had a great view of the city. Since it was soooo hot, the hotel was providing cold bottled water to everyone. The only thing that I didn't like was the small elevators and very few. I was on the 21st floor and it took forever for the elevator to pick me up.

title: “Expensive but Still Worth It”
text: It was the commencement week for all colleges in Boston Area. Expected to be expensive. Especially with its location. Starbucks is right downstairs, however, there was a long queue like every minute even in the evening. Cleaning lady was kind and cheerful. Didn't mind to come back later in the afternoon as our younger children slept in till noon. The hotel was fully booked, so at this time of the year, couldn't expect extremely helpful staff at concierge, lobby, valet parking or anywhere.

title: “Nice hotel at a great location”
text:
Dupont Circle is one of DC's trendy neighborhoods and the Dupont Circle Hotel sits right in the middle of it. We stayed one night. Our room was clean, modern decor and the bed very comfortable. The bathroom had a unique feature, a switch for heated floors. Complimentary bottled water is offered.
There were some problems though. The bathroom sink is shallow so running water tends to splash on my shirt. The shower has no curtain, but has a glass panel which does not contain all of the water that falls on the floor. The complimentary wireless internet did not connect or was excruciatingly slow. 
Still, it is a nice hotel in a fun neighborhood and worth staying at.

title: “Good Enough”
text:
We don't really have any bad complaints to speak of. The elevators impressed us--we never had to wait for them. It is two blocks from the White House and not far from food or shops or a metro station. The air quality in the room was iffy. On our second day we noticed how moist the room was. When you touched clothes that were laying out or a piece of paper you could feel how damp everything was.
If you don't want to be kept awake on a weekend night don't stay in a room directly above the street. A lot of talking and noise down below on our Saturday night stay-- it kept me up late into the early morning even on the eighth floor. And yes I expect noise in the city but I am just giving you a heads up because other rooms are available. 
Our price was $80 a night on Priceline. But, don't expect a fair change in bedding arrangements being a Priceline customer. We asked for a king bed instead of 2 doubles which was arranged ahead of time and confirmed at the check in desk. But when we got to the room it was a big room with just 1 small double bed. The front desk informed us since we were Priceline customers we got whatever was not in demand at the time.

title: “This is a complete dump! Avoid it!”
text:
I took my wife to NYC for a week to see a few shows and have a nice vacation. We were prepared for a lot of things in the city, but we were not prepared for the absolutely horrible "3 star" (in reality a -1000 star) hotel, called the Park Central. We arrived at 1:30 PM and they had no rooms to check us into. The desk agent didn't offer to keep our luggage while we could get a bite to eat, we had to sit in the lobby until 2:40 with our bags until they found us a room on the 17th floor. 
The main reason we booked this hotel is because it is close to Broadway, the park and accross from the Carnegie Center and their web site indicated the property has just been renovated at the expense of over $50 million. The room was awful. A dingy blue chair in the corner with stains on it I don't want to guess about, a desk with a broken leg, none of the lamps worked, the towels in the bathroom were all on the floor, obviously used, the bed was not made up. The bellman, who was as rude as can be, looked at the $5 tip at the door, and when I turned around to ask him what the joke was he pulled the door shut and left. I immediately went to the desk and demanded an appology and a different room. We were told, the best they can do is clean the room for us, they can not move us. I asked for a manager. The manager sent word out that he is "BUSY?!?!". At 5:30 PM they finally gave us another room. The room was equally as dirty, even "clean". The bathroom was disgusting. Since my wife and I both work for a very large property managment company, I called the desk and asked for the manager to come up right away. The carpet, despite being in a non-smoking room, was burned in 29 places. Yes, I counted it. The wallpaper in the bathrooms was peeling all around the ceiling and the bathtup had rust in it! The sink looked like it was wiped out with a dirty rag, obviously not cleaned properly. The curtains were yellow?!?! - they were supposed to be white... The comforter on the bed was burned with cigarettes in 7 places, 3 where the inside of the comforter was poking out! I asked for a new comforter, and after I took it off the bed I discovered the sheets were burned as well. I called the desk again, asked for sheets. 
Not unreasonable at 6:00 PM, right? At 7:45 we went to dinner and got back around 10:30. The comforter and sheets nowhere to be found. I called the desk again and asked for the manager. The desk told me the manager had already left for the day. (they have only one - !?!) When I was about to ask if they only had one manager the agent hung up on me. 
The sheets and the comforter arrived at 11:23 PM!! Since we had prepaid for the room through the NYC city travel group, I could not get my money back to go to a different hotel. The entire staff, with the exception of the bartenders, needs to be fired immediately, starting with the managers!! The cleaning crew is for crap. I purchased cleaning supplies the next day and we cleaned the room ourselves. The day after we came back from having lunch we discovered the maid took our cleaning supplies! I asked the desk to give them back, they said sorry, already threw them away...
I wrote 14 letters since then to the managers of this dump "hotel", no response yet. If you read this, and you are wanting to stay at this awful hotel, just donate your money to a charity. At least you won't be ticked at the horrible service you receive on top of possibly having to stay at the dirtiest hotel in the world. The Best Western accross the street has nicer rooms and much better staff, and they are much cheaper. The Park Central is a complete disgrace.

title: “FIRST CLASS”
text:
WOW
 i was so apprehensive as to whether or not to stay in this hotel, after all the awful reviews i had read!
it looks amazing on the hotels website, so i rang the manager and he assured me i would get a great room, as they were renovating the hotel, he explained why some of the reviews i had read may have been of a distasteful nature!!
OMG i think we got the best room available, very spacious, maids v. pleasant and the place was spotless when we arrived back each evening!the desk staff were more than helpful and v friendly!
And to top it all off My Fiance proposed to me in central park!
I am DEF goin back next year for my anniversary!
GREAT HOTEL!!!!

title: “Great Location, Friendly Staff, Good Hotel”
text: This hotel is located 1 block from Times Square. Many places to eat around here. Efficient staff, nice, clean, quiet rooms. Safe and secure. Not much to not like!

title: “Nice Stay”
text: Great location. Room was comfortable and clean. Staff was pleasant and helpful. Will stay again!

title: “Great location, great rooms. Great hotel overall”
text:
I am very happy I found this hotel. Stayed for 3 nights and would have liked to stay more. Great location. Right across lots of restaurants, bars and shopping.
Rooms are really big and very comfortable, with great king bed in the bedroom, a very good sofa-bed in the living room and a table with chairs. I stayed there with my wife and 3 daughters (2 teenagers and a 4 y-o) and we were very comfortable 
The gym is great and there is also a playroom and laundry. Great views of the city from the top of the tower.
The only issue with the hotel, as many others have mentioned, is the noise from the bar across the street during weekends and also the noice from the cars, ambulances, etc... The first night we were at the 2nd floor and could not sleep at all. Then we moved to the 15th floor and it was a toatally different experience.
Complimentary internet and you can also use the swimming pool at another Marriott that is very close.
I highly recommend this hotel (unless you stay in a low floor on the wrong side of the building...)

title: “Not bad but...”
text: A quiet, clean, well-ventilated and temperature-controlled room with a bed that supports a good night’s sleep is what every hotel should deliver to its customers. Anything beyond that is luxury. The Hotel Majestic in San Francisco only partially delivers this. Street noise can at times be a major disturbance as there are no sound-proofed windows. And there are only king and queen beds but no twin beds. If you want to sleep separately, you will have to use the pull-out sofa bed which is so bad that you are better off just sleeping on the floor. The building is charming though, and the service effective, friendly and personal. The hotel is located in an attractive area with lots of shops and restaurants around. If you wish to spend a romantic night in SF which involves sharing a bed, then this is an acceptable choice at a competitive price.

title: “Brilliant introduction to New York”
text: We spent 9 days at the Hotel Giraffe over Christmas 2011. Our room was lovely with sophisticated decor and enough space for us to settle comfortably during our long stay. The bathroom had a good shower. The hotel has a friendly atmosphere helped by the use of the lobby for continental breakfasts, wine and cheese and all day coffee. The location was really good, a couple of blocks away from Madison Square Park, a block away from 28th Street subway station. We ate at Bread and Tulips , a restaurant affiliated to the hotel in the cellar of the building, on our first night and the food and service were good. There were also several excellent restaurants nearby such as A Voce (Madison) and Tamarind.

title: “Great service; old building.”
text: The staff was very nice, and gave us a night of free parking, but we probably won't stay here again... the building is very old with all the rooms looking into the cavernous center where every conversation echos. It reminded me of a prison. It needs to be torn down and re-built.

title: “Decent downtown option with great views”
text:
Stayed here to attend a meeting at the adjacent conference center. The decor is hip and up to date. So up to date, that repeated clients were mystified by the elevators - you have to tap your number in and then pay attention to the displays to assure you get on the elevator actually going to your floor. The lobby was relatively small, but certainly adequate, with a small bar. 
I was given a room on the 26th floor overlooking the lake and Navy Pier. Really an amazing view during the day or at night. It has all the amenities for a business traveler, with docking stations, a large desk, coffee maker in the room, and safe large enough to hold a laptop. The bathroom had double sinks, was large and well lit, with a decent shower. It was quiet at all times. I would agree with another reviewer, pillows too big and rather hard.
I didn't have time for the fitness center or pool. However, the hotel's location allowed us to walk to dinner more than once, and I'd guess you could walk to the waterfront in no more than 15."
Although I didn't take the L in from the airport, there's a station within 2 blocks of the hotel, which I was told by a fellow conference attendee was painless and likely quicker than my taxi ride.
I did not need the assistance of a concierge, but agree the staff were not exactly warm/fuzzy or especially welcoming. 
The pluses of the hotel were location, clean, modern, decent desk, and great views; a bit pricey though.

title: “Overpriced. Poor service.”
text: Very disappointed. Poor service across the board. Multiple requests were not fulfilled. It was so bad that when I requested a newspaper, I fully intended for it not to be delivered. So overpriced and not as billed that I feel like I was robbed. If this is a top 75 US hotel, then our hotel industry is in trouble. It was clean, which can be said for many lesser priced hotels. The only advantage is that it has a great central location downtown. I would NOT stay here again, but others may only if in a bind for a place to stay downtown.

title: “Quiet Retreat that is a Treat”
text:
Can't say enough good things about the level of service and the people who operate this lovely mid-century revitalized resort complex that is close to San Diego but yet far enough away to make you feel like you are in the countryside. The fellow who is the General Manager obviously has done a good job of hiring young, helpful staff noticeable from the minute you arrive. Not just staff trying to be pleasant but really nice folks who made our stay memorable and who really cared about us - not just their paycheque.
Food is excellent in both the more casual Terrace Restaurant which overlooks the golf course to the formal dining room which we heard was going through a make-over shortly...but as long as the quality of the food from Chef Nic remains the same - with an emphasis on locally grown items - we can see why locals and visitors alike flock to this place for special events, meetings and a weekend getaway.
Ask for a room overlooking the golf course...quiet and close to the main building with a lovely bar area and again, outstanding service. The Spa is lovely, the golf course is a bit of an older style, resort course but playable for all levels which makes it fun because you are not constantly being punished for a bad shot. If you want a real challenge go 7-minutes up the road to Maderas Golf Course where 'target golf' abounds but green fees are pricey. 
Rancho Bernardo Inn is truly a place to relax and we spent four lovely nights at the place. If you want nightlife close by then this is not the place to book, go to downtown San Diego...but if you want a great guest experience, good value for your dollar spent, comfortable surroundings and a chance to leave your car in the parking lot and just unwind, then try this resort complex and you will not be disappointed.

title: “Newly Renovated and pet-friendly”
text: When I went the rooms had just been renovated and every detail was immaculate. The location was perfet. Central to all my needs. We ate at the Farollon restauant twice. The food was good and not too expensive for a hotel in the heart of San Francisco. I loved that it was pet-friendly. Being able to take my dog anywhere makes my life easier. The staff was so loving toward my dog too. I loved the architechture. Combining old world charm with the comforts of technology. The bed and bedding were pristine and soo comfortable.

title: “Omni is always a nice place to stay in SFO”
text: We stayed at the omni for 4 nites in October 2011. We find the service at the hotel to be very good. Also they have the most comfortable beds anywhere.

title: “Loved everything about this place!”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Mayflower for 3 nights.... we loved it. The staff was fun and friendly and always helpful and available. The breakfast was more than enough... it was yummy. We loved the look and feel of the hotel... it was so perfect for San Francisco. It was perfectly located... we walked to China Town and Nob Hill and even down to The Wharf..... and we saw lots of things on the way. It was clean and we absolutely loved the old elevators. The price was great and they even have a small parking garage that we were able to use without any extra cost. We loved it!! I will always stay here when in San Francisco. We didn't want to leave.

title: “A little oasis!”
text: A great stay at this beautiful historic hotel situated in the heart of the historic district. All the reception staff on duty were incredibly helpful and gave good advice. The room was very comfortable and stylish overlooking the courtyard. Very quiet too, considering the central location. Continental breakfast was available in two lovely rooms - the only drawback being that sometimes you had to go into the next room to find milk etc. There is also a restaurant on site. We visited once and the food was quite good in quality but relatively small portions.

title: “Awesome Hotel”
text: The Pearl Hotel is a perfect hotel for couples, families or if you're traveling solo. I found the hotel to be a fun happening place to enjoy & enhance your stay in San Diego. I had room 19 right across the movie screen, I didn't even have to leave my room to watch. My roommate was a red Betta Fish named Ginger. The food was excellent. The staff was very pleasant. Shout out to Jessy. If you plan on staying try to be there for Tuesdays Burger & Beer night, Wednesday Movie night and Sunday Brunch. I loved my room, (thanks for the H2O products I will be purchasing them). The bed was so comfortable. The decor from the lobby lounge to the pool, bar and a quaint outdoor room right off the lobby was just what I love, a mixture of Zen & Retro. Loved everything about this hotel and I will make it a point to come back.

title: “great hotel and perfect location”
text: Stayed at this hotel for 2 nights. It is a very nice hotel and in a really good location. Walking to Pike Place Market was convienent and the monorail really is just 2 blocks away, which is handy to go visit the Space Needle. I stayed here for vacation, and I can see business travelers like this hotel as there were a lot of them around the lobby and business center. It is a good location for business or vacation. The convention center is nearby as well, walking distance to the hotel. This hotel actually takes up the whole block, and there are 2 towers. If you want easier access to the pool and fitness room, you would want the tower they are in, which is all the way on the 35th floor, instead of the other tower, where getting to that pool area is further and didn't seem to convienent. The view up there was nice though. The room itself was clean and beds were comfortable. Staff was friendly and knowledgeable about getting around the area. There is a quick snack/grille near the lobby, which is convienent for a snack or water. Street noise was quiet, didnt notice much at all. Overall i would absolutely stay here again and recommend for anyone, vacation or personal. I had a good promo rate, so the rate is a factor as all hotels in the area seem to be high.

title: “Fabulous downtown hotel!”
text: We were very satisfied with our experience. The staff is friendly, helpful, and courteous. Our room was clean, comfortable, and was supplied with little extras you don't find at many other hotels. We had no issues with noise - we slept very well. We will return. Location is a plus too!

title: “Best Customer Service at the Front Desk in years!”
text:
I was in Austin on business. I had a particularly trying day. The microwave in my room had not been fixed as promised. The front desk attendant came up to my room, picked up my frozen dinner and took it to the kitchen and cooked it for me. She delivered it back to my room with a glass of complimentary wine. Her compassion about my trying day was real and she went above and beyond anything I had expected. Not only did she provide excellent customer service, every single front desk person was personable, friendly, helpful and a pleasure to deal with. I highly recommend this Residence Inn if you are in the Austin area. The hotel manager also greeted me at check out and was just as personable and friendly as the hotel staff. Thank you Residence Inn Austin Northwest/Arboretum for a truly remarkable stay!!
Pamela

title: “Camino Real makes El Paso worth it”
text: We had never been to El Paso so we checked the web. We were amazed by the Camino Real hotel webpage, but who believes these pictures? However, the actual hotel surpassed our expectations. It is an historic hotel in a plaza with other cultural buildings (a performing arts center and a museum). The hotel is beautifully and tastefully decorated - wood, marble and a huge stained glass dome encompassing the bar. This elegant atmosphere made our margharitas taste so much better. Near the bar was a 4 diamond restaurant that was a bit too pricey for our present vacation which was to visit Big Bend and other national parks. Our rooms were spacious and decorated with furnishings unlikely to be found in an American hotel chain. Each floor was nicely decorated (we checked!). The lobby showcased artwork with huge paintings of horses, native Americans etc. done by local artists. The hotel staff was helpful and suggested restaurants even though there were two in the hotel. This stay set a nice tone for the trip. We were there for only two days and I wouldn't look any further were we to find a reason to be in the El Paso area again.

title: “The Magnolia is a lovely hotel.”
text: I was in Dallas for business and chose the Magnolia because it was close to my destination. I was pleasantly surprised to find a delightful historic building with great amenities and a charming staff. I liked that the room had a mini fridge to keep my snacks cold, free wifi for working in the evenings and a good breakfast buffet. The bathroom was nicely appointed, the bed was comfortable and the staff was very helpful. I have only two suggestions to improve my next stay: while the room was restful, it was a bit dark, due to the dark brown walls, and the minimal amount of lighting fixtures. I would prefer a little lighter wall color and more lamps. Additionally, I had room service two evenings, and while my choices were delicious, I didn't have a large selection from which to chose. I would have liked a turkey club, or another lighter sandwich or dinner size salad. That said, I definitely will stay here again!

title: “Great experience!!!”
text: The location can't be topped, and the staff was most accommodating. We arranged for about 20 rooms for family and friends attending a wedding reception downtown. The staff was quick to grant any wish. I had a brunch for 70 people in my suite (coming and going), and they didn't bat an eye. They supplied us with extra tables and chairs and tons of ice. During a blackout they barbecued by flashlight so all the guests could be fed. Overall we had a terrific experience, and all of our family and friends agreed.

title: “Love this place”
text:
This was our 2nd visit to this hotel and once again it was amazing.
The year before we had gotten engaged whilst in New York and loved every second of our stay.
When we decided to go back to New York we had no hesitation in staying here again, making this the 1st time either of us had decided to stay in a hotel for a second time.
we stayed in a junior suite. These rooms are amazing. Large bed, lovely bathroom, a really nice little kitchenette, a nice sitting area as well as desk but it also has amazing views.
The location is great as it's really central, the staff are really nice and I can't recomend this hotel enough. Both our stays here were brilliant

title: “Aging reasonably gracefully, recent renovations”
text: Stayed 2 nights recently to attend a meeting at the hotel. This is a very large (1840 rooms) older hotel (formerly the Adams Mark) built in 1959 and last renovated in 2009 I believe. For the most part, they've done a nice job with the renovations, although the hotel shows its age in some areas. Amenities are generally nice, and the rooms are well appointed. They have a terrific fitness facility (12 treadmills, 10 ellipticals, and a large strength training area with machines and free weights, all very modern) as well as a comfortable outdoor pool (no spa). The hotel's primary role is for business meetings and it excels in this way. The conference facilities are easily accessed from any of the 3 towers. The hotel is connected by skybridge to the Marriott City Center and the Plaza of the Americas (small ice skating rink, food court with fast and sit down food during the day). DART (light rail) is immediately adjacent to the North tower of the hotel, which offers great views of the art district, but at the expense of train noise. The train does make for easy access around the area. Like most business oriented hotels, they have most everything available, and charge full service hotel rates for most everything. All in all, it's a good place. If traveling for business, it's great. If for pleasure, it's ok, but the extras add up.

title: “NY Palace Great!”
text: This is a wonderful hotel. We enjoyed everything about it. The rooms are very spacious, clean, and comfortable. The hotel staff treats the guests wonderfully. The view of St. Pat's is amazing. The hotel is also located around many attractions and easy to get around. I would recommend staying here to anyone.

title: “Huge Cockroach in bedroom; unfortunate shame for the great staff :(”
text: In booking this trip, I passed on a swanky, cheaper 4 star hotel to have more space where my kids would have a great first time hotel experience. I knew there would be some compromises but for almost $50 more a night, I never expected it would be in the form of a huge roach in our bedroom behind my bed when my husband removed one of the sheets!!! YUCK! It was like Wild Kingdom searching for it to kill it in order for us to sleep comfortably the rest of the night. Needless to say, we did not catch it and we had to put towels under the door to the bedroom area while we all huddled in the living room to sleep the rest of the night. Thankfully, it was our last night but I'm disgusted to know I slept in a bed with my child and a roach in tow. Not good! On the upside, the ladies at the front desk were wonderful, friendly, courteous, and helpful.

title: “Wonderful Hotel - Absolutely Recommend and Will Return!!”
text:
I am so pleased with the service at this hotel. From the front desk staff offering travel advice, to the car valets, to the cleaning staff - wonderful! 
The room (1101) was terrific. Fresh duvet covet with really comfortable bed (may have been new?) with fluffy towels, and plenty of space. A relatively small kitchen, but their breakfast on the second floor certainly was what we used every day. A bit busy at 9:30am for finding a table, but the food and cleanliness was 100%.
The pool is pretty good. Bring down the larger towels as the small ones are not the best. The spa was pretty hot, which some people may not find suitable. I enjoyed it. As for the person who gave a negative review because they allow kids in the spa, that person needs to learn how to travel and not sweat the small stuff. 
The parking is somewhat costly at $42, but that is the same price as every hotel. There is a lot down the street for $30. Attendants are friendly. It takes about 10 minutes to get your car. No issues.
The location is perfect. Close to too many restaurants to mention, and about a mile walk to Michigan Avenue or $6 cab. 
The only negative: It is near a firestation as many other hotels in the area. So there were sirens on occasion. It did not bother us on the 11th floor. You may want to bring ear plugs. But that applies to the whole city with people honking horns. Just plan for it.
But all in all, this hotel scores a 5/5 without a doubt. I will definitely return.
The staff and management are outstanding to say the least.

title: “Very nice hotel...”
text:
We stayed at the DFW Hyatt Regency, which is located on the DFW airport property, the night before a 6:30a flight. This is an older property that has been completely renovated top to bottom (including bathrooms) and is quite lovely. The room was very clean with flat screen TV. The bath had a walk-in shower type arrangement that you find in the newer hotels. The vanity area was separate with a granite countertop, which was nice. For the ladies, there was a magnifying makeup mirror - always appreciated. No shower caps though. They do provide toothpaste, soap, shampoo, conditioner and lotion (I believe it was). There was a large full length mirror in the room and two smaller long mirrors on the closet doors in the vanity area. In our room, there were two electrical outlets on one side of the bed, but none on the other. However there were additional outlets in the desk area, which proved ample. The room was amazingly quiet for being at an airport. We did not hear any plane noise during the night. There was a complimentary shuttle to all of the airport terminals that ran 24 hours a day on the 20's (top of the hour, 20 minutes after and 40 minutes after). Also, free airport parking for nights stayed at the hotel. Just remember to get your parking validated.
We had dinner at Jacob's Spring Grille and it was quite good with lovely presentation. May I suggest the crabcakes...excellent!
My only two complaints are these: 
1. There were two bottles of water in the room (about 16 oz size), for which a charge of $4 per bottle was levied if consumed. 
2. There was a $15 per device/per day access fee for computers, i-pads, etc. 
This is not the place to stay if you are in the DFW area as a tourist, but would highly recommend if you have an overnight layover, an early morning flight, or circumstances that require you to be at the airport.

title: “Almost perfect..”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights early July. The hotel is in a really nice part of Philly. Walnut street (for shopping) is right round the corner, and there are loads of bars and restaurants nearby to choose from (Highly recommend Monks and the black sheep). 
The reason I gave the Sofitel 4 and not 5 stars ? There was a used bar of soap from the previous guest sitting in the bottom of the shower stall, and the toilet (flusher) was broken. We called down to reception, and they said they'd send someone straight up. But we were calling back again 30 minutes later to find out where they'd got to. When they did get there, the toilet was fixed really quickly, but I expected the service to be a little better than what we received. 
Apart from the hiccup in the beginning, the rest of the stay was great. The room itself was lovely and clean, with super comfy beds, a great tv, modern decor, a nice long, deep bath and a very helpful concierge. The housekeeping for the rest of the stay was also perfect. There's a nice little farmers market on a saturday morning in Rittenhouse square - with great banana bread !
Loved Philly. Pretty city with a great vibe.

title: “Echoes of Old San Antonio”
text: I have loved this building since I was a child and walked the river with my parents in the days before it become "The Riverwalk". Now when I am fortunate enough to return to San Antonio, this is the hotel I come to and I am taken back to old San Antonio. If you love history and glimpses of the way life used to be, this is the place for you. I love the quirky layout and never know what I will find when I round the corner of a hallway. The staff has always been on the top of their game, allowing me to drop my luggage when I appear early in the morning and head across the river to the Mokara (will always be the Watermark to me) Spa for the most luxurious spa experience in the world.
