This is a bit of a splurge but think of it as a first-class trip to the wonderful and exotic - without having to show your passport or enduring the intimacy of the TSA body gropers.

title: “Location and Comfort couldn't be better”
text: The location in Times Square couldn't be better...right in the heart of the city with easy access to all points North, South, East and West! The staff was friendly and helpful. Can't wait to go back!

title: “Grand Stay at the Grand Hyatt”
text:
I have to say that our recent stay at athe Grand Hyatt was amazing. We understood before we arrived that the lobby was under renovation so we were prepared for that...and besides, who comes to NYC to spend time in the lobby!??
We arrived very early in the day, around 10:30 a.m. We were using one of our free nights that we got from gettng a Hyatt Mastercard. We did not expect our room to be ready, but thought we would give it a try. We were met by Claudine, who was training a young man by the name of Chris. Claudine made a few phone calls and said our room would be ready shortly. To make up for "any inconvenience" she gave us two coupons for free breakfast the next morning (which isn't cheap, by any means!). They then gave us some coupons for free coffee/water/tea at the little market in the hotel. We got to talking and mentioned that we were in the City for our anniversary. Claudine made us feel like we were her best friend. Chris took time to talk to us and was so very friendly. I cannot imagine anyone complaining that the hotel staff here is impersonal! There was not one employee, from the housekeepers to the maintenance men, to men in suits and ties, to the restaurant staff, that didn't say hello to us and talk to us.
Our room was a "deluxe king" which meant it had a little extra space. It was new and clean. It even smelled great. The bed was amazing. The linens were perfect. I have no complaints about the room. Yes, the bathroom is very tiny. There is no bathtub, but it was adequate for our needs. I will say that the toilet paper is a little hard to reach!
There is something that looks like a clock on the nightstand. It may be an Ipod docker, or clock radio. We couldn't figure it out! We couldn't find the time anywhere. The alarm went off in the middle of the night (to some very, very loud music). We must have it the snooze button because it went off again. Finally, I had to unplug it. It would be nice if there some instructions in the room as to how to use the thing!
When we arried back to our room later in the evening, there was a tray with crackers, cheese and some other goodies. There was no note, but Claudine must have picked up on the fact that it was our anniversary.
It was pouring rain the day we were there and it's great to be able to access the hotel through Grand Central Station without having to go outside in the rain.
This was one of the best stays in the City that we have ever had and look forward to returning to the Grand Hyatt the next time we are in town.

title: “What a Great Find in New York!”
text: We recently had a fantastic stay at the Library Hotel - what a great find! It is cosy, quiet, welcoming and in the most fantastic location. The staff were friendly and helpful in every way. The rooftop terrace bar is the perfect place for a pre-dinner cocktail and the reading/breakfast room, which is also open for coffee/tea throughout the day and for pre-dinner drinks and snacks, has just the right mix of homeliness and luxury. In a city oozing with hotels this one should not be bypassed.

title: “Charming but update needed.”
text: Charming though a bit outdated as far as quality of bedding, pillows, towels and decor. Had a spacious room on the street side, queen bed was soft and a bit saggy. The hotel is ready for new furnishings and a good cleaning and spot painting, particularly in the bathroom. Walls smudged and grungy and a good cleaning or painting would make a world of difference. Upon arrival, desk staff was stuffy and not overly accomodating however warmed up once we continued with the paperwork. Evening Sherry, Tea and cookies were not present when scheduled. For the rate we paid, I think we could have done better but was a busy weekend in SFO. I would recommend it only if others in the same class and category (Victorian) were not available.

title: “Great Location - Free Parking”
text: I came for an overnight stay with my elderly mother for the 4th of July. Very accomodating staff. Love the free parking and the location was great. We walked to Times Square to purchase theatre tickets, walked to the show, walked to dinner. Nice restaurants all along the way. Rooms are not plush, but nice. I gave the room a rating of 4, because they are a bit dark. It was difficult to read. Other than that, we had no noise and slept comfortably. A note for purchases through Expedia: The booking will not provide two double beds. If the hotel has them available, they will do their best to accomodate. In my case, the hotel was booked for the 4th and a double bed room was not available. The hotel did offer to waive the fee for a rollaway. I would stay again.

title: “Classic charm, a dying breed in New York”
text: I was on a business trip in New York which I combined with a family vacation, travelling with my wife, 3 kids and a nanny. The hotel is situated a block away from Central Park and along the shops of Madison Avenue. Our stay was great, the hotel staff really tried to look after us and surprised the kids with a special treat for Halloween, decorating the rooms with spider webs, pumpkins and the like. Best of all, when you're staying at the Carlyle, you have a porter in each elevator (which can be a bit slow when it's a busy time of the day), the Bemelman Bar had Paul McCartney show up when we were there, the Carlyle Cafe features Woody Allen performance every Monday. Rooms are good size for NY, although bathrooms only have one sink! I loved the hotel and will be back, very child friendly too!

title: “Excellent Contemporary Hotel - Great Stay”
text: From the moment we arrived until the time we departed, the staff was very friendly and courteous. Check-in and out were handled efficiently. We were upgraded to an "edge room" allowing a view on all sides of the hotel. The room was clean and comfortable, with a great flat screen TV. Located right in the heart of Back Bay, within walking distance to the Prudential Center, Newbury Street and numerous bars and restaurants. The hotel assisted us in securing tickets to the Theater. Although no full service restaurant, there is a bar located in the same building that served great drinks, and in the morning we were treated to a complimentary continental breakfast.

title: “Past its prime”
text: I travelled to DC for business and thought I would try something different than the usual suspect Hilton brand hotels. I had stayed at the Hay Adams in the past and was expecting a hotel that would be comparable. Boy I was wrong. The hotel is well past its prime and in dire need of a thorough refurbishment. My room was decorated in this tacky quasi old american style, was small, dingy and stunk of cigarette smoke. There was no bath and had the ambiance of an upmarket Fairfield Suites. I have to say that the staff kept up to the usual high St Regis standards though - they didn't put a foot wrong the entire stay. Food and beverage was also above average, particularly the standard of room service. For the price point though, the hotel was a real disappointment. I will definitely be going back to the Hay Adams for my next stay in DC.

title: “Wonderful time at CIAA Week”
text: The hotel staff really make the stay worth while...Carolyn Jackson(front desk), thank you for all that you do to make our stay such a wonderful experience. We could not have done it without you! The location, service, food and additional amenities are excellent. Management has gone beyond what's required to make their guest "welcome"...they provided additional areas for entertainment and longer hours for food availability...exceptional service. Thanks again..see you all next year!

title: “Modern, clean and convenient”
text: Were we not getting such a great military discount, I would have asked for a different room. It was one of the smallest I've ever stayed in! That being said, the room was very nice, the bed awesome, and the staff accommodated our request to be adjacent to the couple with which we were traveling. AND, as they knew this was a celebratory trip, a bottle of sparkling wine and fruit plate was in both our rooms upon arrival. The guys at the door -David in particular-are awesome. Helpful and congenial, they went out of their way to help at every opportunity. The lobby is a bit small and lacks seating that invites lingering. The bar is the same. The wine reception is a nice idea, but the wine is terrible. A real mix of guests, which is always interesting, one easy block off Times Square and most theaters. I would stay here again....in a larger room.

title: “Kimpton Hotel in Downtown Denver”
text: Lobby is fun, staff very helpful, morning tea in the lobby is wonderful--try the Vanilla Bean with or without milk! Of course there is coffee too. The 5-6 pm wine tasting is fun. Lots of folks gather and chat. The room is normal size with a very comfortable bed, robe, lots of pillows. Join the Kimpton membership for free so wi fi is free. The hotel restaurant is upscale and tasty. I sat at the bar by the chefs--entertaining way to eat alone. The bar does a busy business with food and drinks, outdoor seating too. The door staff reserved a car service for me that was very good.

title: “5 star!”
text:
This hotel has only been open for a few weeks, but I can say it's done a good deal to repair my impression of the Hilton brand. (See my other reviews for my impressions.) My wife and I stayed for 5 nights in April. We were upgraded for being a HHonors Gold, and then again due to our first room having an electrical issue. As a result, we stayed in a corner suite, which was incredible!
Pros:
* Very safe, excellent location. Good for seeing the Hudson, and going to financial district, if that's your thing.
* Rooms are stylish and comfortable, beds are very nice as well. (See attached photos.)
* Staff is very friendly, helpful and courteous. I would imagine that opening a hotel is a stressful affair. While we could tell there were a few staffing shortages, everyone working here is doing a great job.
* High-tech amenities are nice. The room control is linked to physical controls, and also the television system.
Difficult to categorize:
* You won't want to leave your room in the morning. New York is a great city, but I was really thinking about spending more time in the hotel than seeing the city. (I felt like a bad tourist. :)
Cons:
* If you are looking for a hotel right next to a subway, this place isn't it. It's a 3-4 block walk. That didn't bother us, but it might matter for some people.
* As I mentioned above, it feels like they're still ramping up on staffing. Sometimes you'd call the front desk or the restaurant and it'd take them a long while to pick up. But otherwise they did a great job.

title: “Great choice for Park and Fly”
text: We stayed here the night of Sept 6. Nice clean room, and good bathroom. Breakfast bags were convienent, and the hot breakfast (ready 30 minutes earlier than advertised) looked really good too! Shuttle service to and from the airport was convienent, and the driver was very helpful. They even invited us to stop back at the hotel when we returned from our trip for some coffee before we got on the road home!

title: “New Courtyard Hotel”
text:
We were given a large and lovely corner room in this new and beautiful hotel after expressing dissatisfaction with the room we were assigned at a sister property.
It would have been a perfect stay if our room had been cleaned on the first day of our stay. When we returned to the hotel at five, after having been out all day, we had to call three times before somebody showed up to clean our room.

title: “Beautiful hotel, but poor service”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for our wedding anniversary. We made reservations a week in advance, and they said we could have an early check-in (2pm). We got to the hotel at 2pm, and the front desk was very rude. Saying they never give out times, and demanded to know who told us. They also told us that many other customers had said the same thing. 
They told we could check in at the normal time, which is 4pm. So we wandered around the Riverwalk until 4. At 4 my husband called back. They said we couldn't check in until 5-5:30 because they had a large group filling half of the hotel. So, to make a long story short, we finally were able to check-in at 5. They comped us drinks at the bar, and a free breakfast but that's not the point. You should honor what you say. It's a beautiful hotel, though. Very romantic. I don't know if we'll be staying here again, though.

title: “Another fabulous visit to the Hilton”
text: This is the fifth or sixth time (maybe more) that I have stayed at this hotel. I have never been disappointed. The location is excellent - just on the side of the financial district and Chinatown with a short walk or bus ride to the Embarcadero or wharf. The views from the upper floors facing the bay are uniformly superb. Each time I have arrived, I have received excellent service, typically with someone welcoming me "back". While I recognize that is good software, it is still a nice touch! The beds are terrific, the rooms are well equipped and although there is a bit of street noise outside (big city), I found earplugs in the room which almost totally blocked it out. If you are on exec floor or are a premier Hilton member, there is a terrific continental breakfast which includes a great variety of fruits, cereals, pastries, etc. No need for anything more to start your day. The bar is pleasant for a cocktail and parking is not too difficult on the streets in the evening. Also the Portsmouth Square garage across the street is a slightly less expensive option to valeting at the hotel. There are other hotels in SF that I also like, but the fabulous views and lovely staff here make me choose it most of the time.

title: “unimpressive and would not recommend for a 2+ night stay.”
text:
First of all, let me say that the staff were helpful and friendly. 
Unfortunately for the most part of our 8 night stay it was problematic and lackluster. The first room that we had had a truck engine for an air conditioner it was horrible and we didnt get any sleep. I think i could outreach my arms and basically touch every wall in the room, that's how small they are..and the beds, well they should provide two as only one person can comfortably fit in them! Smaller then other hotel rooms that i've seen and stayed in, in New York. 
The staff thankfully agreed to move us to another room but only after i asked to speak to the manager. the room they moved us to was lovely, it was a disabled room which meant that it had to be bigger and that served us pretty well for the remainder of the trip.
The lifts!!! S L O W, its quicker to walk down the stairs on crutches and a bung knee then wait for them. 
Great location right next to time square and mid Manhattan - without the noise (or maybe that was just the air conditioner blocking it out). 
In terms of food, the restaurant downstairs, the Aspen does a great steak. Evergreen the diner next door is also fantastic, we had breakfast there most mornings. The staff are friendly the food is cheap yet delicious and fresh.
They were a bit sneaky, there is only free wifi in the lobby, in the rooms you need to pay for it. Also they don't tell you but you will be charged a $50 per night incidental charge that will be held until your departure. Silly me gave over my debit card so it held back our holiday funds....make sure you give a plain credit card so that it doesn't actually affect you directly. 
With the hassle we had with the room, the small beds, unbelievably noisy air con and 'tight' rooms i wouldn't recommend this to anyone that plans on staying for a reasonable amount of time.

title: “I would highly recommend this hotel”
text:
We spent 10 nights at this hotel and thought it was a great location so long as you don't mind walking up a few hills!!. The trolley stop is right outside if you don't do the walking thing!! Remember to buy a municipal pass to use on the cable cars and other transport as its better value.
There is a spa downstairs where you can use the pool and jacuzzi for free. Or you could just sit by the log fire in the spa in your robe and read a magazine.
The staff were very friendly and helpful from the hotel reception to the cocktail mixers in the comfortable bar.
You could even join in the locals who tai chi in the park across the road if you are an early riser.

title: “Nice Location”
text: Very easy access to many of New York's must see places.

title: “Awful excuse for a boutique hotel”
text:
I was appalled when I walked into my room thinking that the Mosser was a boutique hotel. It's essentially an over-styled dorm with mediocre service but a great location. 
The room is the size of a refridgerator -- you can barely walk the perimeter of the bed without knocking your knees into the walls or the other furniture. We couldn't even open the door fully when we put our little suitcase on the suitcase rack in the only place it would fit. The sink is also in the middle of the room. 
The bed was uncomfortable, I have never heard so many trash trucks in one night, and the room isn't dark at night -- there is a window above the door that lets a superb amount of light in from the hall all night long. 
The linens were NOT clean - there was still make up on our bath towels, and the comforter looked so questionable that we threw it on the floor. 
The elevator is slow and awful - you also get to ride it up and down with their cleaning staff.. meaning the slow ride up is spent with dirty linens. 
Beware also - we went in the spring and the room was stuffy and hot -- there is NO A/C, just a ceiling fan -- so if you go in the summer and have to prop the window open, you get all the joyful sounds from the street.

title: “Still good but could be great”
text:
We have just returned from a 5 night stay at this hotel. I had previously stayed there with my mum in Feb 06 and was keen to see if the place had changed at all. First, the location of this hotel cannot be beaten if you are looking to be within walking distance of shops, good restaurants and many of the sights. The subway on Lex and 51st will get you to places further afield.
Second, all of the staff that we interacted with were very helpful, courteous and friendly - particularly the lady who manned the safety deposit boxes. 
Third, this is a lovely traditional grand hotel with a jaw-dropping lobby and reception to die for (even the ladies toilets are grand!). Plus, the rooms are large!
We would return to the Waldorf and may well do so on our next trip to NY. It's a good hotel, but a few tweaks would make it a great hotel. Some minor grumbles below.
When we arrived, it was very busy (rush hour too, it took about 2 hours to get from JFK in the cab). Owing to the traffic, the cab driver dropped us at the front entrance rather than entering through the designated entrance for cars and cabs. Fortunately as we only had 1 case between us, this wasn't a problem, but if we had been travelling with more luggage, we would have struggled to get it through the revolving doors and then up the stairs and into the lobby. Of course, this wasn't the fault of the hotel, but I fail to see why they cannot have somebody on hand to alert the bellhops if guests do enter via the main doors...surely they might require assistance with luggage too?!
Check-in was very speedy, which we appreciated, since we just wanted to get to our room, freshen up and get out and about. There certainly seemed to be a more hurried feel to the entire experience this time around as compared to 2006, although to give the hotel the benefit of the doubt, this could be because we stayed there in the very busy period running up to Thanksgiving. On top of that, there were all manner of private events being hosted there, in addition to a wedding in the lobby area of the hotel on the Saturday. This didn't cause us any problem at all, although the letter posted under our door would have been better received the night before rather than at some point during the late morning on the day of the event! We had already left the hotel before the letter was placed under our door and knew that a wedding was probably going to take place in the lobby as there was a team of florists setting up an enormous archway made entirely of pink and white roses, right over the steps to the lobby! The location of the wedding meant that hotel guests could not access the main lobby from the Park Ave entrance, but rather had to walk through the hotel, take a lift or the stairs to lobby level from the Lex Ave side, then through reception back towards the Park Ave lifts. Again, a minor inconvenience, but if you are planning to stay at this hotel, be aware that these private functions are quite regular. Which is why I would have thought that the letters or notices could have been posted a lot earlier.
On both occasions I have stayed here, the rooms have been of a very good size. The sheets are nice and clean and the feather mattress toppers make you feel nice and cosy. The bathroom sizes vary; on the latest occasion, I would say that the bathroom was about double the size of that of the previous room. This time around we also had a separate secluded entrance to our room, which was rather nice. 
The rooms are cleaned to a good standard every day. I would rate cleanliness at 4 and a half stars only because on this occasion, I noticed quite a bit of dust built up on the bedside table during our stay. That said, the rest of the room was spotless and there was no dust there when we arrived. 
The Waldorf claims to provide all guests with a nightly turndown service, but this seemed a little sporadic. Each night I stayed in 2006, upon return to my room at approximately 8pm, the bed had been turned down, music was playing (!) and the bedside light was on. On this occasion, on some nights the bed was not turned down at all (although the room had been cleaned and the bed made etc), while on one of the 5 nights we stayed, we indeed experienced the full turndown service. No criticism of the staff - the maids seemed to be there morning, noon and night. However, I feel that the service should either be provided fully or not at all. Personally, I don't require a turndown service but others might be disappointed if the service is sporadic.
As other reviewers have noted, not all rooms at the Waldorf have a safe, so do ask upon check-in. Again, this was a minor inconvenience and in fact the lady who generally manned the safety deposit boxes was lovely and friendly, always greeting us with a smile first thing in the morning.
Dining in the hotel can be pricey, so be prepared. We didn't eat in the hotel on this occasion (too busy sampling the meatballs at The Meatball Shop (84 Stanton Street - GO THERE!!) for that. However, I have previously eaten here and the food was good, though expensive. As other reviewers have said, there is a Starbucks in the entrance of the hotel (would have thought not the image that the Waldorf would want to portray, but no matter). Don't bother buying from there unless you are desperate, do yourself a favour and if it must be Starbucks, visit the one on the corner of 51st and Lex. It's about half the price and right around the corner from the hotel.
We have both stayed in other hotels in New York but we like the Waldorf for the size of its rooms, the staff and the location. This is not a hip and trendy hotel by any means, but it doesn't need to be. Frankly, if those minor niggles could be resolved, it would be a great hotel and we wouldn't even consider looking at other places to stay when we visit NY. Fingers crossed that they work it out!

title: “I Love this place”
text: I stayed here with my sister for her 50th birthday. The staff were wonderful, the room was beautiful, although we had no view, and the location was just perfect. There was no restaurant when we were there, although they did have room service. Everyone from the doorman to the bartender were outstanding, friendly and ridiculously helpful. I would make this my "staying in New York" hotel if it wasn't just quite so expensive.

title: “Great view”
text: This place has one of the best views of the Boston harbor ! It's a short ride to the many neighborhoods Boston is famous for. Spend the extra $ for a harbor view! The service was good and everything we ate was wonderful.

title: “Very happy with this hotel!”
text:
I recently returned from a stay at the hilton new york. It was for a bachelorette party and i did not book it myself. but was very happy with staying here. The hotel is VERY big - it looks outdated from the outside but they have put alot of money into updating the interior. Our rooms were upgraded to a "updated room" so our rooms were very nice (i don't know how they "older" rooms would be). It was really unfortunate we could not get rooms closer to each other (we had 3 rooms booked) luckily we were on the same floor but was a little disapointing. 
The room had 2 double beds in it. So it is tight if sharing with more than 2 people. the beds i thought were very comfortable and have very nice features in the room -a very large tv. a great ipod dock that you can play music from! the bathrooms were lovely. everything was very clean and the room sizes were actually very spacious. 
On the main floor they have a little cafe and take-away with a starbucks cafe! (i did not eat here but it seemed a lot of people were). The hotel is easily accessible by subway and the bell boys at the front of the hotel can get you a taxi in a matter of minutes. 
overall this hotel was a good choice.

title: “Great hotel and staff”
text: I am an avid traveler and was very impressed with the services and staff. The location is great. The Foggy Bottom Metro was a block away and I used it a lot for meetings in DC. The room was clean and large for a urban hotel. The front desk staff was friendly and very helpful. I called down to see where the closes drug store was and the front desk person offered to pick up the medicine for me...very nice. The only thing that I would mention is that the room is a little dated.

title: “Awesome boutique hotel - Hotel Manager Jason was top notch!”
text: This hotel exceeded my expectations. Well situated in Koreatown in mid-town Los Angeles. My room was quiet, spacious, trendy and clean with a nice sized, flat-screen satellite tv (and a remote control that worked!). Cleaning staff were polite, courteous and attentive. Hotel Manager Jason was absolutely excellent in all manner of hotel operations, customer service and attention to detail in making guests feel valued and welcome. He spent more than a few minutes answering my questions and providing a wealth of information on restaurant options, the LA music scene and how to get various points of interest in the City . His professionalism and kindness made my already excerllent stay that much better.

title: “Excellent Stay!!”
text: We’ve stayed at many hotels in the past and Hawthorn Suites by Wyndham Columbus-North was by far the most nice if not the nicest hotels we’ve ever stayed at in the states. We lived in Columbus for 12yrs and frequently visit; however, this was our first time staying at this hotel. The suite itself is like an apartment. The room is very large, clean, has all amenities such as: a full size kitchen with a refrigerator, a dishwasher, a full size stove, a stink and garbage disposer, all utensils and dishware, a bar, a living room with a TV, a couch that pulls out into a bed, we had a queen size bed, a bathroom that can accommodate a family of four, a full size closet, a balcony and an amazing view. The hotel also had a workout room, computer room, basketball court, tennis court, outdoor pool, excellent room service, a home cooked breakfast included for free and the staff was exceptionally cordial. The price was very acceptable it was roughly $66 dollars; however, if we would have booked in advance we would have gotten an extra 10% off for my husband’s military service. We actually just got a studio but I personally think it was as nice as what a penthouse would be. With that being said, this is our new place to stay when we visit Columbus. Thank you very much to the excellent staff at Hawthorn Suites Columbus-North for an extraordinary staff!! Much appreciated!!

title: “Very Nice Stay.”
text:
Went purely based on the favorable reviews on this web site and I was not disappointed. Although the hotel is oddly situated right in the middle of a rather shady looking neighborhood, you forget all that once you walk through the two sliding doors into the modern-appearing, warm lobby.
1. friendly staff
2. Small but nicely docorated, modern-appearing, clean rooms.
3. King sized bed was very, very comfortable with lots of pillows and very nice sheets.
4. Thoughtfulness everywhere, best exemplified by the complimentary bottle of water every day.
Down sides are 
1. shady neighborhood kind of away from major stuff 
2. rooms are very small
3. no central A/C or heating, wall unit worked very well but was also quite loud, had to turn it off at night to sleep, but then got really cold in the morning
Otherwise, a very nice stay.

title: “Low key hospitality”
text: I stayed here for 4 nights over Thanksgiving and it was a calm respite from the shopping crowds at the Magnificent Mile. Appreciated the self service pantry at the lobby area. Staff were friendly and efficient. The rooms are large with a very comfortable bed. There's free bottled water everyday but no coffee facilities in-room. However, you can get woken up by noisy guests in the corridor and door slams. Ask for a room with a view.

title: “This was ok for the price...”
text: We stayed only one night and found it hard to get to. We had a GPS that helped us get round. We found the front desk people very friendly and our room was clean and neat. We get the senior rate, and it suited us just fine.

title: “Very convenient, comfortable -- pool small, food mediocre”
text: We stayed in this hotel several days with two small children, and it worked great for a family. The suite, though not large, was very comfortable and clean and was made up promptly every day. The hotel staff will go grocery shopping for you -- at no extra charge -- this way you can really use the little kitchen. And the hotel was extremely convenient for sight-seeing in downtown Philly -- easy walk to Independence Hall, Chinatown, Reading Terminal Market, etc., and easy to get the "Phlash" trolley (right in front of the hotel) that takes you around to tourist sights. Main drawbacks were: TINY pool (nice and warm, though), and very mediocre food, especially at the afternoon "receptions." No alcohol served at those, and the food was very unappealing (meatballs, iceberg lettuce, etc). Breakfasts were better, but not great. Limited offerings of fruit, chewy Belgian waffles. If food were improved, I'd have given this five stars. Still, a great value for central Philly.

title: “Fantastic Boutique Style Hotel”
text: Awesome hotel -- service is exceptional, they make you feel very at home, staff always goes above and beyond, lots of little things are included like the gym (which is fantastic), internet, drinks and snacks in the room, wine in the evening, etc. The look and feel of the entire hotel is wonderful. And the hotel feels twice as expensive as it is.

title: “Not terrible - but bring your own plunger!”
text: We checked in early Friday morning to a most accommodating front desk person. We were shown our room which was basically what we expected for the price. All seemed well until the second night when the toilet began to overflow. My boyfriend went down to the front desk to make them aware of the situation, but the front desk did not seem to care. He asked for another room and was told there was none available. He then asked for a plunger and was told "I'm sorry, I can't leave the front desk to find you one." He didn't know what to do; how do you stay in a place with no washroom facilities and the night clerk was of absolutely no help and of really bad attitude. My boyfriend then went to another hotel down the street to ask if they had a plunger, but no they could not provide him with one. He asked if they knew where he could get one, they told him at the Duane Reade drug store in Times Square. So at 3:30 a.m., because of the refusal on the part of the hotel staff to do anything, he walked over to Duane Reade to buy a plunger. We asked for a discount on the room but they only agreed to reimburse the $4.42 he had paid for the plunger, saying we had made the reservation through Hotel Conexions and that we would have to take it up with them.

title: “No frills cheap fare”
text: Small hotel, perfectly placed on Manhattan's upper West side, close to subway, central park etc. Rooms are extremely small, so do not expect any comfort, but who does for such a cheap price? The bathrooms are the smallest ever and the shower doors are completely misplaced, making for a good Mr. Bean moment when trying to move around in there. The radiators make a lot of noise if you go in winter, so be prepared to wear ear-plugs. The staff is kind enough to joke about it in a sardonic way, meaning self-critical. Cleaning service is very good. This hotel is for people who don't have any expectations on high room comfort and who want to feel like they have made a good deal, but still want nice personal and respectful service from the staff. On this low-middle level the hotel is highly recommendable.

title: “Spacious in Seattle”
text:
This hotel exceeded our expectations. My husband, parents, two children (5 & 1) and I stayed here for nine days in early April. We had a two-bedroom, two bath suite with a balcony. The bedrooms and living room areas were spacious and inviting. The kitchen was a bit smaller than other suites, but absolutely functional since we cooked dinner there on several occasions. The bathroom (toilet & shower/tub) was a bit on the smaller side, but since the sink was separated from that area it did provide enough room. Each morning the hotel serves a “continental” breakfast. Let me just say, that there is nothing “continental” about the type of breakfast they serve since items such as Belgian waffles, scrambled eggs, sausage, etc. surprised us each morning.
The hotel staff was very friendly and extremely helpful. They even had an extra umbrella stroller for us to borrow during our stay. While we were there, the hotel held an Easter party (complete with the Easter Bunny) for all of the children staying at the hotel. The indoor heated pool is a nice size with an attached 3 foot area for our 5 year old and offered us a reprieve every evening with our kids. I found the laundry room (right next to the pool) to be extremely helpful since the hotel staff would actually bring change for you up to the room. My husband frequently visited the business center that had two computers with complimentary internet access.
We initially had some concerns about the hotels proximity to downtown Seattle, but it was only a short cab ride to any downtown location and it was adjacent to beautiful Lake Union. Plenty of restaurants and walking areas are across the street by the docks and there even was a children’s play area nearby. For us, the amenities of the hotel outweighed the downtown location, but the Lake Union area was a thoroughly relaxing site.
We kept saying throughout our stay that we made the right choice in hotels and would highly recommend it for either families, guests with dogs, or anyone looking for a bit more space with close proximity to downtown.

title: “Oh My God!!!!!!”
text: I can't even begin to describe how shabby and run down the accommodations were. We checked out. Save yourself look elsewhere! It is clear that no money is put back into this operation......

title: “Clean room; good location”
text: Room was clean and adequate in size. Stayed in the area to be close to some friends who were staying in a nearby hotel. Overall, I was fine with my stay at this hotel.

title: “The best!”
text: This is the absolute best place to stay in Chicago. Extremely affordable. The hotel staff was extremely friendly. The room was very clean and had a great view from our room. The hotel is located just a couple of blocks from a jewel osco and near some great restaurants. And the parking. Free parking!!! We even asked to keep our car there a few hours after check out and they said it was more than ok. Metro stops (bus and rail) are also very close by. We will definitely be back to stay at this hotel!!!

title: “Business trip San Fancisco”
text:
I stayed at the Executive Vintage Court for 6 nights in order to attend a full week of seminars at the Moscone Convention Center.
The hotel is very well located, less than 5 minutes from Chinatown and also very close to major shopping areas like Macy's. Also within walking distance is the access to the BART and other public transport services. The Moscone center is about 10 minutes in walking distance. Fisherman's warf about 20 minutes.
There is no restaurant or food services at the hotel. There is a restaurant attached to the hotel, but it is not related to the hotel itself and is very very expensive ($100-$200 per person).
The room a bit aged, like an old victorian house, but it was clean and comfortable. It was basically a square room not much bigger than the bed itself, a little bit like the rooms you would get in Paris, but a bit bigger. The room had a working desk and a furniture piece with 3 drawers....a little bit light on the storage capacity. The bed was comfortable.
Adjacent to the bedroom, separated by the door frame without a door, was a small powder room with a big mirror and a small cube that serves as a bench. The bathroom, with sink, bathtub and shower (in the bathtub) was adjacent to the powder room. There was a dryer attached to the wall in the bathroom, and it was working propoerly, so no need to bring your own.
There was also an iron and and ironing board in the room that I used every day and it worked well, generating enough steam to do a good job. The room was also equipped with a good LCD TV. 
I was on 5th floor and it was very quiet inside the hotel. We could hear when people were talking in the corridor while walking by our room, but there was very little traffic in the hotel, especially at night. We could also hear noises outside the hotel through the windows, but it didn'Mt prevent us to sleep well. This is a small hotel, I would say maybe about 100 rooms distributed on 8 floors. I would avoid the lower levels of the hotel because of the poor isolation to the noise.
The lobby of the hotel is small, but somehow nice. The hotel lobby has free cofee in the morning, cold water during the day, and free wine tasting from 5pm to 6pm every day...wine was good quality. The staff in the lobby was very helpful each time we needed help or anything. We called the front desk for checkout and asked them for a cab. when we got downstairs 15-20 minuyes later my bill was ready and my cab was waiting for me.
I would say that the 2 strongest features of this hotel are the location itself and the relative low price compared to other hotels in the area. 
If you are looking to spend time downtown, shop, eat and visit Chinatown and are ok with a simple basic room and little services, then you will probably like this hotel. If on the other hand you want a hotel with full service, require luxury, and are planning to spend a lot of time in your room or at he hotel itself, then maybe you should pay more and look for something else.
As for myself, I liked my experience at this hotel and would go back.

title: “Go somewhere else!”
text: We stayef here because of the value. I wish we would have stayed somewhere else! The hotel has seen better days. They now rent out some of the rooms as apartments. The exercise room has all broken equipment and the complimentary breakfast is just some cereal and danishes. The rooms leave a lot to be desired. The bathrooms are outdated, have mildew and hair snakes in the tub. The carpet and couch looks like someone died. If you have the money do not stay here. The only thing that really works is the air conditioner!

title: “Excellent stay”
text:
Very pleasant hotel staff, nice rooms. I had a king size room in a corner at it was plenty big for one and also for two. Room 316 was wvwn bigger and had really nice windows and light.
Everything is very red so if you do not like that colour then stay away.
Its in walking disance from everything (if you lije to walk like a Scandinavian ;-) 1 km to the White House so perfect for the morning run.
Can only recommend this place. My only two regrets, they didnt reflll the body loting tubes and the breakfast was not included in the rate.

title: “Dirty, Dirty, Dirty”
text: I felt like the place was rolling in dirt. Walls everywhere in the hotel were dirty. The floors were slippery and wet and I almost wiped out. The only thing was the bed was comfortable which was good but I will not stay here again...EVER!!!!

title: “Cozi Stay”
text: For the money this Best Western gets the job done. The area isn't very nice but the hotel and rooms themselves are good. I stay at this location about 8 nights a months and I am satisfied so far. I have stayed there about 35 nights this year so that says something!

title: “Above Average”
text: It was a great experience staying in Palomar. Excellent location, friendly staff and a great spa tub in the room (we stayed at the deluxe suite). Valet parking was a little expensive.

title: “Great location, lovely room”
text: The hotel is literally right on the Riverwalk so it is very convenient. The hotel decor is nice, and our room was (in typical Westin style) large and equipped with a comfortable bed and excellent bathroom and Heavenly shower. Very clean and has tea and coffee facilities. We enjoyed our stay at the Westin, and would recommend it to anyone headed to San Antonio.

title: “Worst Hotel Experience EVER!”
text:
Be careful of this so called swanky hotel.. It was apparent to me after visiting Hotel Zaza Houston that they are not what they claim to be. They charged my credit card $3,450.00 in room damages because they said I dirtied their couch with a glass of water. They charged me $1900 in cleaning fees for a few towels and some bed linens and the worst part is they don't respond to any of my calls or emails. It was the worst experience ever including this. We purchased a Splendido Suite which was not ready by our 3:00PM check in so they made us wait in the lounge for 2 hours with no free drinks. Once we arrived at our room, we come to find out that our mini bar is completely empty. No one ever came up in 2 days to refill the mini bar from the last person who stayed.
Service was horrific. Our bathroom over looked another condominium building and the shower had a huge window where everyone can see into the shower from the opposing building. When we asked for a room change, they stated there were no rooms available. Come to find out when I asked the service technician to fix our air conditioner that the hotel is only half full. They lie, and play games and we will never go back to this hotel ever.

title: “Good for the value”
text: This hotel is in the perfect location. Close to everything in Boston you would want to walk to or take the train to. The rooms are huge and very modern. Currently the lobby area is under renovation, but the staff goes out of its way to be accommodating. I would happily stay there again.

title: “Disappointed :(”
text: The pull out sofa was filthy under the cushions. The amenities were very sub-par compared to other comparitive hotels I have stayed at. As a few examples I had to ask for lotion and the lotion that was provided was very poor quality. I might as well have rubbed water into my skin. Other items that are nice to have without asking are q-tips and cotton balls. The continental breakfast was very skimpy. Any items other than basic cereal toast and unripened fruit were not complimentary. I ordered breakfast from the kiosk and paid for it with my credit card only to be told that my selection was not available. The waffles I was offered as a substitue were disgusting and tasted like baking soda. The food service worker's attitude was non-apologetic. The bed in our room was uncomfortable. The A/C unit was very loud each time it would come on, making it difficult to get a good night's rest. Overall, I was disappointed with our stay here. I have stayed at much nicer places for the same price or less. The pool was average, but there was no hot tub, which I thought was odd. Just one more amenity that you would think would be there, but are disappointed.

title: “Not a good experience”
text: Booked a room because we found Hotel Vitale on tablethotels.com which is one of my favorite sites. When we arrived, we liked the aesthetic -- very hip hotel, good location and the bar on the lobby floor was really happening. However, the experience quickly did not meet my expectations. When we checked in they only had a king room available even though I had booked 2 queen beds. Only after 10 minutes discussing the issue did they agree to find a room with 2 beds -- which took more than an hour. Then when we got to the room, we found 2 full beds. When I called to ask why we weren't in a room with queen beds, the employee said, "Those are our queen beds." But they were *not* queen size. Later in the evening my friends and I had difficulty getting a cab back to the hotel from a local bar. After trying unsuccessfully to reach a cab company through the internet, I called the hotel and asked them to send a car. They said they didn't have a car to send and couldn't help me get a cab and then hung up on me. This is not the level of service I've come to expect from hotels on tablethotels.com. Overall I was very disappointed and wished I had booked a room somewhere else.

title: “Stayed for 10 days and got a good representation of the hotel”
text: Service was amazing... Jeff and Marcus were great! Rooftop bar - best view in town! Rooms comfortable but their smallest rooms (with equal size bath) are not my preference. Many of the less $ rooms have no view. ATT cell phones have little or no service in hotel/area. Bathroom had limited privacy - ok for couples not for others. Loved the "living room" for coffee or cocktails and free wifi. Restaurants all good. Spa was booked while we were there and Acura car wasn't available. Whatever/Whenever service helpful. From what I can tell, W is very competitive with area hotels. You give up space and amenities when you stay downtown, Alexandria, etc had more options. We wanted to be close to everything this trip so it was the right choice.

title: “Not up to Radisson Standards”
text:
I have stayed at many Radisson's - in faact our company uses Radisson's in Toronto to house clients - as the standard is excellent - and has always been so - until I stayed at the LAX Radisson.
The room was smelly, the TV had 8 TV channels, the matresses were lumpy (all the Radisson's I have stayed at have duvets with fantastic matresses - one of the reasons for choosing Radisson).
Spend the $20 per night more and stay elsewhere.

title: “Get a room at the back”
text:
I stayed here on two occasions two and a half weeks apart in order to break up the long trip between Canada and Australia. 
On the first occasion, I was given a room near the front of the building. Though clean and comfortable, it had a spartan feel to it, and was poorly insulated from outside noise, which included vehicles, jet engines and some people shouting and laughing as they passed on the street at about 3 a.m.
On the second occasion, I had the pleasure of staying in one of their more spacious and well decorated rooms at the back for the same $67/night rate. It was much quieter, making it an ideal place for someone who is merely stopping over at LAX after a long overseas flight and looking for a place to shower, shave, sleep and eat. (For the latter purpose, the adjacent Denny's restaurant and the free breakfast come in handy.)
For those who need or want to be near LAX, the Travelodge offers basic, affordable overnight accommodation; but make sure that you request a room at the back.

title: “Great hotel, outstanding location.”
text: Let me start buy saying the customer service was top notch. The rooms were accomidating and very clean. I was very impressed by the professionalism, and the view from my room on the 37th floor was outstanding. I would highly recommend this hotel and stay again. Oh the room service was really good too. Great job New York Palace!

title: “Very good except for dirty toilet seat”
text: Everything a you'd want in a NYC hotel: good sized and clean room, excellent location, no bedbugs, quiet floor, free Sunday brunch, fast check-in and check-out. But the dirty toilet seat was unacceptable, not to mention a health hazard.

title: “Glorious ballroom!”
text:
I attended a conference held here, so didn't have a choice where to stay, but I normally stay in Hilton properties - often Hampton Inns. The first room I had was a Jr King Suite on the 8th floor. Had a nice view of the lake, but the room and furniture smelled very musty. In speaking with co-workers, I learned that there was a renovated floor. The hotel was gracious in changing me to a room on a renovated floor. With they had done that when I first got there, but at least they did have room to change me for the remainder of my stay. 
Since I was there for a conference, I didn't get to try the restaurants. The hotel did provide all our meals though, so I got to sample a lot of the items. The food was better than most conference foods, so I was pleased with that. 
The Ballroom is stunning!!! You must take a peak inside if your stay doesn't call for meetings in that room. They just don't build hotels anymore with the glorious features that are in this Grand Ballroom!
Staff was kind and very accomodating, would return - but only if can get on renovated floor.

title: “Disappointed”
text: I spent 4 days at the L'Enfant Hotel ( Jan, 19-23 of this yr. ( 2012). Was fairly disappointed. The lobby was five star and very comfortable. But the room I was in was disappointing. It was spacious and had a good view, but the cold air came right in through the windows . I always felt cold ! Thankfully, there was a thermostat , so I kept turning up the heat. The room was old and very worn. The carpet looked dirty, as did the ceiling air vent and the bathtub ( though the bathroom itself was a good size). The daily buffet breakfast was great ! There are 2-3 restaurants on the main floor, but I found them a bit expensive .Don't count on the restaurants and shops underneath the hotel to be of much help. Everything (except McDonalds) closes down at 6:00 p.m. ! That caught me by surprise ! And, unless you have a car, there are no other restaurants nearby to compensate for this.

title: “Excellent value and convenient location.”
text: I've stayed at this motel many times. The staff is efficient. The rooms are clean, and it's very conveniently located near to I-695. The rates are quite reasonable. It's a good value for the money. ...

title: “AMAZING!! AWESOME!!”
text:
Can not think of one negative thing to say about this outstanding hotel! From the door men to the reception it is a FABULOUS experience. 
Room service is top notch...the food is unbelievable. 
It's the little touches that really matter and this establishment has covered all the bases!

title: “curate's egg”
text:
Accepting that centrally located elderly hotels in San Francisco are going to have to operate within space constraints, this hotel had one huge problem. It has only one small elevator so that, if it is not actually already being used by room service or the maids, you may have to share a ride with well virtually anything that needs to go up or come down in a hotel.
The location also means that daylight is at a premium in the hotel and the general lack of direct light was amplified by some very earthy coloured decor (presumably because of the style being sought). This is particularly pronounced on the stairs. There is no natural light and the artificial light is not overly bright, yet they have laid brown striped carpet which makes it very difficult to see the edge of the stair tread. With the elevator problem making recourse to the stairs for descent (even at four floors up) a more frequent then usual occurrence, particular care had to be taken.
The room, whilst generously proportioned and quiet, also lacked daylight and was not brightly lit artificially. It was a bit depressing. The bathroom/ shower was good for such an old building. The lack of coffee/ tea making facilities was not helpful particularly since the bar served dreadful coffee (we didn't dare ask about tea).
Staff were helpful, although some seemed overly commission motivated, and there was no one to help with cases. The location is very good.

title: “Excellent hotel, way better than expected”
text:
I have just returned from a 5 nights stay at the Andaz Wallstreet. From the moment one enters the hotel, you feel that you are well taken care of. We arrived early but nonetheless there was a room available immediately.
A large and clean room, nice ammenities ( loved the shower gel and shampoo) , the free non-alcoholic mini-bar and the complimentary wifi ( fast and reliable) were all top-notch. A two minutes walk to the Wallstreet subway station and good connections towards mid- and uptown made it possible to avoid taxis and use public transport often. I have stayed in New York more than 30 times before and do frequent 5-star hotels around the world for at least 100 nights per year. The Andaz Hotel Wallstreet is a very good choice and I can highly recommend it.

title: “Good hotel in top location”
text:
I stayed here with my family for four nights as part of a tour of the US. After a somewhat belated access to our room, at the 24th floor, we could enjoy the view of the Eastern part of downtown SF and the bay - just like we had requested.
The room had an ok size, good beds - and a television from the last century... We did not watch anything else than a couple of weather forecasts, but a flat screen could save some space!
The service of the hotel was, apart from the check-in, was excellent. However, in this class and price range, one could expect services as WiFi to be free. The $10 ålus charge per day seems both 'cheap' and out of date.
The location at the NE corner of Union Sq is absolutely fantastic.
The next time we go to SF, and we will!, our hotel research will have to come up with an absolute stunner to top this one.

title: “o.k. stay..”
text: Booked this hotel through Priceline. Flight into San Diego to move daughter from one apartment to another. So the purpose of my trip was not conducive to this type of hotel and stay. Parking was outrageous at $30.00 a day plus $8.00 a day for coffee and water. Asked the parking valet if I had any other options to park and they said no. I ended up parking 7 blocks away at 7th and Broadway for $10.00 a day for those willing to walk. I was uncomfortable in the bed (just too hard) and didn't sleep well during my stay. If a person is just interested in visiting the Gas Lamp this would be a good choice. Very quaint.

title: “A well deserved 3 star Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Edison for 4 nights, middle Feb 2012 and it was a decent hotel. It is very dated and nothing modern in sight, but it is very clean and comfortable. We upgraded to a deluxe room which i think is just a double room with a sofa in and maybe a bit bigger but hey, it was only a small fee to upgrade. The location is superb, smack bang in the middle of times square, literally 30 seconds walk round the block and you are where all the lights are! Overall the hotel is more than good enough for a short break to new york and to be honest you don't spend that much time in your hotel. The staff were more than friendly enough but most American people are. We had no issues while we were there, we would definitely recommend it.

title: “Great service and great food”
text: The gold buidling had limited views of the harbour but the sevice was among the best I have ever received. All of the food was great and they served breakfast, evening appies and dessert in the lounge. The ravioli at the main restaurant was better than the restaurants on Salem or Hanover. Great location; it was walking distance to most of the main attractions, but it was about a 15 minute walk from the T.

title: “On the Ave - what a find!”
text: Thanks to other tripadvisor reviews, I booked 3 nights at On the Ave. First of all the location can't be beat! It's on 77th Street at Broadway, smack in the heart of the Upper West Side or as I like to call it, food heaven. Zabar's and H&H bagels are 3 blocks away. Right across Broadway is the Westside Market which has single serve portions of just about anything 24 hours a day! The 1 train is at 79th street and the express 2/3 is at 72nd. It is also close to the A/C train. I stayed in room 726 for the first 2 nights - it was standard room that was very small but comfortable and with a great view of Broadway. The only downside was the shower stall - it was very difficult to shave my legs! Unfortunately on my second night my neighbors decided to party all night - I think there were at least 20 people in that tiny room! Security was very responsive but in the end I didn't get much sleep that night. To make up for it the manager upgraded me to the penthouse suite, room 1409, for the last night of my stay! What an amazing room! Living room, huge bedroom, 2 private terraces, big bathroom with giant shower, plush towels...the works! They even left me a note with some brownies. If you can't stay in a room with a balcony, there is a common balcony on the 16th floor with adirondack chairs that has stunning views. I paid around $300 a night for the first 2 nights and paid $200 for the third. Parking was easy - valet for $50/24 hour period.

title: “Nice for airport hotel”
text: We stayed here for 6 nights while attending a conference at the hotel. The rooms were very nice and very clean. The furniture was pleasant and the bed was comfortable. The bathroom was typical for a hotel of this type. Internet access was $12.95/day including local phone calls. It worked well. There was a flat panel tv with a decent selection of channels. The pool was nice, but needed heating. There is a nice fitness center and also a hot tub. Check-in was easy and most employees were polite. The restaurant was very slow.

title: “Nice hotel”
text:
Comfort Inn Manhattan Bridge is a nice and friendly hotel. It's located in Chinatown, with Little Italy just around the corner. The tube is only 100 meters from the hotel.
Breakfast is great and the personnel is very hospitable. 
Only, the room could be a bit bigger, but hey, it's New York.

title: “Great stay, wonderful breakfast”
text:
My husband, son, and I stayed at this hotel during a college tour visit. We were in Philadelphia to look at Drexel University and decided to stay across the street on the U of Penn campus.
The hotel is in a downtown location. Parking was $39 for the night. When we checked in, the front desk clerk acknowledged my husband's previous stay. Our room included two free breakfasts but since we had our son with us, she gave us an extra coupon for breakfast so the 3 of us could eat. This was very much appreciated.
The room had two double beds which served our purpose. The room was recently re-done and looked great. A robe and some chocolates were on one of the beds which had been turned down. The bathroom was large and was stocked with supplies. 
The nicest part of the room was the iPad on the desk which had our name welcoming us on the home page. I was able to check in for our flight home the next day without having to go to the business center. If needed, room service could be ordered or anything else done on the iPad. It really was a nice touch.
Breakfast was wonderful. An omelet chef made items to order. Not only did the buffet have the usual breads, fruit, breakfast meats, etc... but there was a tray of smoked salmon and nice cheeses. The service was excellent. It was a great way to start our day.

title: “Pleasant experience”
text: My friend and I stayed at The Inn at Union Square in late February 2006. Our stay was a very pleasant experience. Regarding the hotels location, you would not want to be staying anywhere else. Transport, shopping, restaurants, nightlife were only a block or two away. The rooms were quaint and adequate with old style decorating, which added to its ambience. Rooms were not overly big, but comfortable. No views out of the window, but no big deal. The afternoon wine and cheese sessions were a really good idea. It gave you an opportunity to mix with other guests if that is what you want. The staff were helpful. The boutique style of the hotel added to our overall excellent opinion of San Francisco and would certainly stay there again.

title: “Amazing hotel”
text:
It doesn't look like much form the outside, but on the inside this hotel is quite nice. Staff was very helpful and friendly. The touroperator through which I booked the hotel only booked my room for 2 nights instead of 6, but the receptionist never made me feel like there was a problem and sure enough, after a few minutes it was all taken care off. He also pointed me to the back-exit through which you're at the Wharf in no time. When I dislocated my knee someone from reception was called by my neighbour and she stayed with me, called the doctor for me and had someone go to Wallgreens to fetch me a bandage. Concierges are very knowledgeable, nice and helpful overall, except for one lady, but I guess you can't have it all.
My room (booked for one person) had a lovely queensize bed (I didn't understand the sleepnumber-thing, but then again, the bed was right as it was) and my room had a view of the Wharf and Alcatraz. Plenty of channels to choose from on the tv.
For breakfast and dinner I tried Johnny Rocket's, Ihop, a local diner and Boudin's Bakery. My favourite was Johnny's, I love the whole Grease / 50's diner feel, the staff was very friendly and actually recognised me the second day, plus it's so easy to get to: you leave the hotel through the rear-exit, cross the little place by the pool and enter Johnny's from their back-entrance. Boudin's was kind of a letdown: I found out I don't like sourdough bread when my french toast actually tasted sour, no matter how much syrup I used. But again, this is very easy to reach, leave the hotel through the rear-exit, cross the pool, walk throught the little passage and enter the Wharf. Then you cross the street and there's Boudin's.
Apart from the Wharf, you're at Pier 39 within 10 minutes, and I found the cutest little beacht about 15 minutes on foot from which you have a lovely few of the Golden Gate Bridge. Cruises and bus tours all leave from the Wharf or the Pier.
I would certainly choose this hotel again for any future stay in San Francisco as it is so convenient with good rooms and friendly staff.

title: “Superb Service”
text:
Had never stayed at the Bryant Park...my client made the reservations. While at first, it was a bit stark and modern for my taste, I quickly fell in love with the service. Now I'm hooked. Ahmed Omar, the front office manager...in fact, the whole staff...could not do enough to make my stay as perfect as possible. Whatever I wanted or needed, it was always 'no problem!' 
I travel often to NY, and I've been looking for a hotel to call 'home'...I'm happy to say, my search is over. The location was great...right across from the charming park it was named after, and walking distance to all the shopping I tried to squeeze in. Great restaurant, Koi, and very attractive bar on premises. 
 I highly recommend the Bryant Park.

title: “Good hotel, great rooms.”
text:
We stayed at the Beacon hotel from Feb. 20th till 23rd and would recommend it to anyone who likes to visit New York and not pay too much for designer hotels, rooftop pools etc. We liked having a kitchenette in our room to make coffee and toast in the morning and to keep some cold drinks for our evening rituals before going out at night. The room was larger than expected, the bathroom was rather tiny though. 
Very important (for me as a Dutch shopper), within walking distance you will find Victoria's secret, Sephora, Pottery Barn, Urban Outfitters and Barnes & Noble and at Columbus mall: J Crew etc....for all the stuff you won't find in Europe.

title: “comfy, good value”
text:
Our large king room was away from the street on the 10th floor. It had one wall that was nearly all glass, and two of the window panels opened for nice ventilation without too much noise. The room was remarkably quiet and comfy, we slept well, and I appreciated having a microwave, dishes and usable fridge. The room was very clean; for example, we were in our room when housekeeping wanted to dust the ceiling corners. The location is terrific, just off Union Square. We left our car with the valet and walked everywhere for 3 days. I have stayed in downtown San Francisco many times over the years, and this is my new favorite hotel in downtown.
In-room connectivity was intermittent, apparently depending on how many others were using their devices and how close you were to a router. Near the window, I could not get mobile phone signal from AT&T and the free wireless Internet signal was weak. However, I could usually get an excellent phone signal near the door. As for the wireless Internet, I got an excellent connection near the door during the day.

title: “I was there today.”
text:
I have stayed at the Four Seasons chain for several years now. I usually go to the one in Nayarit, Mexico. It's a resort rather than a hotel and they never cease to amaze me. I had to be in Houston for a few days and I decided to stay at the Four Seasons. As soon as I stepped out of my car and was greeted by the valet I was greeted: "Welcome to the Four Seasons, Sir" and I knew I could expect top-notch service as I would in any 5 star hotel. 
The doors were opened for us everywhere we went. Our bags were taken up and our car was valet. Standard for this hotel. The lobby looked great, but not the common "Grand" entrance in comparison to other Four Seasons hotels I've stayed at. I was processed really quick to get my room key. The lady walked me to the elevator explaining all the hotel's amenities such as the out-door pool (which unfortunately I did not get to try out due to the rainy weather), gym, and the italian restaurant. Very courteous. I went up the elevator and got to my floor, which as many have commented looks rather old. Not in a classy-old, but rather in a way that you can tell they have put off hotel maintenance, restoration, and remodeling. I stayed at a Hilton in post oak blvd in houston with nicer hallways/decor. 
The room was nice, as I would expect. Very neat and great bedding. Including all the ammenities you would expect from a Four Season such as the sandals (his/her), the bathrobes, news paper, shampoo, conditioner, lotions, etc. By now we had our bags delivered by the bag service gentleman. The decor of the room was nice, but like I said, I have stayed at nicer hiltons. The Four Season should be in the same "playing field" as a St. Regis or a Ritz but the rooms are not even close. I don't complaint so much being that I paid about $170 for the night and $30 valet parking per day in comparison to $700 a day in the Four Seasons in Mexico.
The concierge was great they are very helpful in getting anything from reservations to exotic car rentals to pretty much anything you want. The food was great. I highly recommend the lobster pannini they have to share. It was great! Overall, the service was great, food was great, value was great. I would go there again but this hotel shouldn't really be called a "four seasons" until they heavily remodel. End of story. Still, I'd visit again.

title: “Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk/San Antonio* Fabulous Trip!”
text:
We just got back two weeks ago from San Antonio. What a wonderful city! The senior volunteers at the information desk @ airport welcomed us and gave us pamphlets and tips. The people at Drury Plaza were nothing but nice. Desiree, Jonathan, etc. were all very friendly and courteous through our whole visit. All the restaurant workers on the Riverwalk were extra nice as well. 
 The Christmas Riverwalk was gorgeous and beautiful. Yes, it is a tourist attraction, but you can also venture out to the Alamo, the art museum, the market center, etc. The river which is very small is very, very long. 
The hotel has an excellent view of the city at the top of the roof. Take advantage of swimming pool and hot tub. The view is incredible in the dark.
The breakfast buffet was fabulous (hot links, eggs, pancakes or waffles, cereals, oatmeal, snails (breakfast rolls), and drinks were complimentary. In the evening at 5:30, they had pasta, hot dogs, tossed greens for quick evening pick ups. Plus, free mixed drinks, coffee, tea and soda pop. All were served on real dishes and not paper plate. 
This hotel has a wonderful art deco ambiance. It used to be an old bank. Our room was on the 20th floor and we had a great view of the city and partial river walk. I think we were in the old section. 
Check out the bottom level. You will see the old vault and walk out to the Riverwalk.
We made our reservations in July for the December trip. 
The other Drury (Inns and Suites)was not as fancy as this one. They are more casual and paper plates with plastic silverwares there. This one is on S. St. Mary's Street and it had real plates and silverware.
There are security police all over the Riverwalk. It is so secure when we were there that people were walking and filling out the Riverwalk at 8 p.m. If you plan to ride boats, it's $8.25. It's worth it to ride during twilight. Make sure you get Juan. He's a comedian and will make the ride worth it. We ate out at Casa Mia and United Republic of Texas (average but great desserts). 
Check out Mi Terra at the Market Center for great sopapillas. The Mexican ambiance is overwhelming and the bakery is the largest panderia I have seen on the west coast.

title: “I had a hard time getting back to reality!”
text: This is a beautiful hotel and the best location for anyone attending events at the convention center. I was given a huge parlor room on an upper floor at the convention price, although I received an email a few days before my arrival suggesting room upgrades at a higher price. The bath towels are fluffy and huge - a sure sign of a luxury hotel! Don't neglect to eat dinner thinking that you might grab a late snack from the vending machines, because the Hilton does not have vending machines! The hotel food was really good. I had lunch at the Liberty Tavern and dinner at the Loft Bar, as well as a banquet lunch as part of my conference. Everything was delicious and well-presented. I was by myself so I decided not to seek entertainment on 6th Street, which is a short walk from the hotel. I recommend walking or biking the hiking and biking trail around Lady Bird Lake. A must-experience is to watch for the bats taking flight from underneath the Congress Street bridge. Hundreds of people line the bridge and lake to watch for this each night. The bats didn't fly the two nights I was there, but it was a beautiful sunset and gave local flavor to my time there. I had a couple of hours to kill before heading back to the airport for the trip home, so I rode the light rail from the station outside the hotel out to the end of the line and back. This adventure would not be for everyone, but I enjoyed seeing the transition from urban commercial or surburban to rural landscape on the trip. In-room internet service is outrageously priced at $13+ a day but I somehow scored in-room internet at no cost. I had a great stay and I would go back.

title: “Stayed 1 night due to cancelled flight”
text: We were supposed to head to Jamaica with friends for our anniversary. We checked in at the airport, bags and all, and just as our flight was to board, they cancelled our flight. No others available until 5:45 the next morning. So, A A said they would put us up in a hotel. When we arrived, I admit, I was cranky, but what can you do, but deal with it. I was impressed, the hotel is clean and elegent. Check in was a breeze, and the front desk staff were very friendly. We were given a harbor view room, which also overlooked a runway (I got to watch OTHER people take off for their vacations!), but the view was very nice, as was the room, clean, neat and large enough. The beds were very comfortable as were the pillows, and we heard no noise. The bathroom was very nice, and the shower was great, plenty of hot water. The amenities were great too, even toothpaste, so we didn't have to unpack everything. We just opened our carry ons. There is complimentary coffee, but the bottle of water that is left for you to use, will cost you $5.00! Speaking of crazy expensive, don't even consider using the restaurant. We were given 20.00 per couple vouchers from the airline, nice touch huh? Except we were charged a $30.00 sitting fee for lunch! A sitting fee? We paid for lunch, tax and tip, plus the "sitting fee". Total cost for 6 people...over $200.00 for LUNCH. We got club sandwiches, burgers and soda, no deserts. Anyway, the gym was nice, and clean, as was the pool and hot tub. There is a ferry that will take you to Faneuil Hall Market place, but we had left our coats in the car at the airport so we didn't take the ferry. We went back to the lounge in the evening for a drink and appetizer, the staff was great, we even met sisters that work there that had been to Jamaica and they gave us some travel tips. The shuttle arrived on time, all six of us could not get on the same flight to Miami, so we left first and there was only 1 other couple on the shuttle. It brought us right to our gate, nice touch. If I ever have another flight cancelled, I would stay here again, I would just eat elsewhere. I can't imagine staying here for an extended period of time, as I believe this hotel is over priced.

title: “Excellent place to stay”
text: The staff is incredibly helpful and friendly. Honored all my extra requests with a smile. Very clean rooms and comfortable beds. Complimentary breakfast was the best I have seen with a great selection to fit all diets. Overall, it was a great experience and I would not hesitate to stay there again the next time we are in the area.

title: “This place is one of the WORST in NYC - Do not understand the good reviews”
text: I have stayed in a lot of business hotels around the work, and hotels in NYC. I was horrified at the terrible lack of professional customer service, the overall shabbiness (for what they charge) and how they never, ever pick up the room service trays. I had one sit outside the room for about 26 hours, until I finally called. Disgusting. We saw room service trays in the floor constantly. There are many great hotels in NYC, and you should not waste your time on this shabby one.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: Stayed with 28 people in this fantastic hotel. Very nice staff, super location and very nice rooms. Recommend for everyone!

title: “Loved it”
text: We stayed here for my sister's wedding. Lobby area is beautiful. Have to agree with gentleman about the long walk to the rooms from the lobby, however, you can park by the back entrances for closer access. Elevators just inside the door. Beds and bedding most comfortable. Room was clean and the staff couldn't do enough for us. Every employee from the maids up to the managers greeted you and asked if we needed anything. You are pretty much stuck eating at the hotel restaurant unless you like the Waffle House or fast food. Easton mall is a short drive north on I-270. Lots of good eating places there. You can also take US 62 east to Gahanna for several nice restaurants. We went to a place called Max and Erma's. Excellent.

title: “Wonderful stay!”
text: Stayed one night here for shopping @ Polaris Mall. Easy access to mall & many restaurants. Hotel was very clean & comfortable. Loved everything about our room. Comfy bed, clean bathroom with big shower. No complaints @ all!

title: “very noisy if room faces powell street”
text: i enjoyed the hotel, small rooms in need of some modernisation, but is clean and quirky. It fulfilled our requirements. step outside hotel and you can catch the cable cars. very close to shops and links to alcatraz etc. very lively place for october and if your room faces union square it is very loud. But it added the buzz to the location.

title: “Nice, Beautiful and Close to Everything”
text: I am glad to say I had the pleasure to stay at this hotel. This is a very clean, nice, and beautiful place to spend time at a place where is close to everything, location, location, location!! The staff is extremely nice and helpful. Two thumbs up for The Westin Seattle :) Would I recommend this hotel to my friends?? Absolutely yes!!

title: “Great new property. Thin walls =lots of noise and with scratchy sheets, mean terrible sleep. Ho-Hum staff service”
text:
This is a great new facility, and is located right by the airport. The shuttle service is prompt and convenient, even though they have a church van type shuttle (meaning a high step up) that has bench seats rather than the normal airport shuttle bus type vehicle. 
The actual property is very nice and new, even though you can see signs of wear in places, and some of the rooms etc. One of the rooms had cigarette burns on the pull down window drapes. The walls are VERY thin, and some of the rooms have the shared doors between rooms, which means that you can hear EVERYTHING your neighbor is doing, from his evening ritual, to his paid mature movie selections and his morning toilet routine. I was not happy. The breakfast ordered from room service was up very quickly, but looked like it was made by a 7th grade home economics class. Even though the breakfast was supposed to come with bacon, the person answering the phone kept saying it wasn't "time" for bacon, and then delivered the breakfast sans bacon. He told me to go downstairs in about 15 minutes and I could get bacon. Huh? The point of room service is that it is ROOM service. I asked him to bring the bacon when ready, and gave him a generous tip to ensure follow up. He never showed up. The staff at the front desk is young and can't be bothered, and don't care as they are just going through the motions. Such a shame as the location is great, and the property is for the most part very nice.
Rooms: Nice modern rooms, but no easily accessible power outlets by the bed. When will hotel designers learn that you don't want to have to crawl under and re-arrange furniture to get to a power outlet, and that a lot of people use their laptops while in bed? This along with the question about why they bother to put up signs telling you not to hang anything on the fire system sprinkler, but then don't actually offer you enough hooks in the room.
