But I digress - this is a property to consider if you have a short stay and just need a room for night (and may or may not care about actually sleeping), and also REALLY want to get those starwood points. That won't be me - don't think I will return.

title: “Business trip”
text: Clean, breakfast was good, overall good value. Would stay there again. A little difficult to get to from the Parkway.

title: “Perfect Hotel for NYU families and those who enjoy SOHO and the village”
text: I have stayed in this hotel on several occasions. So long as the prices stay reasonable (below $300 nite) it is a perfect hotel for a couple of days in the City. It is easy walking distance to all the SOHO shops, the meatpacking district, the village (west and east) and right near the subway line. The hotel is clean and the rooms are typical Sheraton comfortable (great bed). The front desk is a bit hit or miss, some of the people are excellent (friendly and helpful) and others, well, it seems like they are always annoyed. There are always taxis out front on what is normally a quiet side street (which makes for quiet evenings/nights). There is a gym, though I have never used it and a bar/restaurant. The only odd thing is that they only give you paper cups in the room. When I asked for wine glasses to drink the bottle of wine I had bought, they told me I could only have a glass if I bought wine in the bar (apparently they are separate, though they are connected in the lobby)...would be nice to have wine glasses in the room Te business center are two ancient computers in a hallway -- neither had the right software to print my ticket, but the woman at the front test was more than helpful and handled it for me on her computer. Other than that, great little hotel.

title: “My Home A Way From Home”
text: Great location, Near shopping centers such as Neiman Marcus, near the Dallas convention Center, near restaurants and a pharmacy. Friendly staff, A breakfast buffet that will start your day on the good foot! The Valet staff will bend over backwards for you and will go above and beyond the call of duty for you. You are greeted with warmth and made to feel at home. The rooms are clean. The beds are comfortable. The price is affordable. All that and then some. I highly recommend the Magnolia!

title: “Enjoyable stay”
text: Check in can be painful as such a busy hotel. Location is brilliant right next door to Penn Station and down the road from Macys and the Empire State building. Rooms are small but it is the centre of Manhattan, make sure you get a room from floor 25 and above and book a room with a view of the Hudson River or the city.

title: “Slipshod Service Consistently Poor in a Stately Historic Ambience”
text:
This hotel has a stately look and feel with glorious wood and elegant chandeliers-very elegant for a Wyndham property.
However, the beauty ended there. Our room was moved the first night after they could not get our in room movie system to work and the 2nd engineer claimed it was due to their dated telecommunications infrastructure that needs replacement.
The business center computers were repeatedly "under repair".
The hotel charged me for internet access despite this being free to Wyndham Rewards members.
The basic room is woefully small albeit the suite they relocated me to was well sized.
The Housekeeping service is very poor. We had to call 3 times on the fiirst day to get the room cleaned. Furthermore, they never really cleaned the sinks or showers during our stay.
The concierge was never at their desk and had to be chased down for not returning our calls to attempt to place restaurant reservations.
I can go on and on with the service deficiencies. 
There are some nice staff here but overall the service is quite poor.

title: “Fantastic location, great view, good service”
text: We stayed at the Copley in adjoining rooms with our four teens - we had a wedding to go to and they were not invited, but we felt comfortable with them shopping and dining at the attached mall while we were out. The rooms were nice and the view was fantastic. The kids got ice cream from room service and the service was prompt and the portions were huge. We had a great time at the indoor pool, too. We're going back in June.

title: “Location is Great”
text:
We picked the New Yorker because of reviews & recommendation. It did not get of to a very good start with the Front of House member of staff having an attidude of I don't care .
 My husband was due to come on the 6 day trip with my Daughter & her friend but was taken ill so unable to travel . I emailed the hotel as soon as I found out 5 days before, asking for two rooms together. This was confirmed by them, as done . Upon checking in not only were they not next to each other, they were on different flloors !!! I asked to see a Manager as this was unacceptable. After an hour I finally got two rooms on the same floor. When checking my room was smaller than booked . I went down again to Duty Manager try to change, would or could not change !!! These two people were the worse FOH staff I have encounted on my 5 previous visits to NYC. This was brought to the attention of the General Manager a day later & since has offered something for my next visit, nice but would have better to have been dealt with on this stay .. Very clean hotel. all the other staff from Room to Security were great.. The TICK TOCK Diner attached is excellent for breakfast. Price is good , portions huge, staff smiling.The location is excellent , as we are great Macys fans. So not far to carry bags !!!!Near Penn Sation
The car service in the recption area NEW YORK RIDES are the best I have ever used in NYC . Our flight was 1 hour early , we thought we would have to hang around. No the driver was sent early as they checked arrivals.

title: “Great for Traveling with Teens”
text:
We stayed one night while attending a fundraising event at the hotel. President-Elect Obama was holding his first press conference here at the same time we were to check in - so I was expecting chaos - Instead, the hotel was running quite efficiently in spite of the extra congestion - they appear to be well-equipped for dealing with large crowds.
We stayed in an Executive Level room. This level has it's own check in staff and a lounge. We did have to switch rooms initially since the first had a bathroom that smelled strongly of cigarette smoke. 
Our room had two bathrooms and two full beds with a nice view to the south. The two bathrooms were an excellent feature since we had 3 teens that needed to shower and primp. 
The location of this hotel provides convenient access to Grant Park and the museums.

title: “Fantastic location, basic and clean room.”
text:
Excellent location in downtown, on walking distance from the typical Chicago pizza places (Uno + the others) and the metro red line. Ideal to visit the city for a weekend deal.
Good price for american standards (still more expensive than in Europe), but very good deal.
We got some noise from La Salle av. the first night but surprisingly calm in the second and third night for being in the middle of the city.

title: “Great Hotel to celebrate 20th wedding anniversary”
text: This hotel takes you back in time. I must admit that when my husband first told me that this is where we were celebrating our 20th wedding anniversary I was thinking "Oh, I wonder what kind of hotel this is." Well, was I pleasantly surprised. First of all, this hotel is a beautiful old historic building which I consider a hidden gem in midtown. The location could not be better. Quiet at night after a busy day in the city but so easy to walk to the hustle and bustle of midtown. Everyone we encountered at this hotel was beyond pleasant. We had a beautiful suite overlooking 6th Avenue. What an incredible view. For NY standards this room (we had the Warwick Suite) was very generous in size. The room was spacious, and the living room was a wonderful size. We could sit and relax in a nice couch. Bathroom was small but very modern. The heating system I felt was not working well. We had to open up a window because it got very warm in the room but otherwise, it was great. We had champagne delivered to the room and we had personalized champagne flutes that we brought along with us. The following morning housekeeping took away our personalized glasses and left the regular flutes that they had brought up. I called immediately and within 20 minutes they brought back the flutes. Service was phenomenal! The restaurant was great for breakfast. They have a very nice selection. We went to the bar after dinner for an after dinner drink....which was pleasant enough. All in all, I would recommend this hotel and would return. Oh and I forgot the BED was SO COMFORTABLE as were all the pillows. Thank you to the Warwick staff for making our 20th anniversary a celebration to remember!

title: “THE FINEST LITTLE JEWEL HOTEL IN NEW YORK”
text: Very well situated, in the heart of Manhattan, small and personal, with the finest attemntion to the clients........We have been several times and will continue to return........

title: “Decent Hotel for the Price”
text:
Pros: Obviously the biggest draw to this hotel is the price. It really is a pretty good deal for the neighborhood. The hotel is close to a lot of attractions and amenities such as the Empire State Building, Times Square, Broadway theatres, subways, decent restaurants, shopping, etc. You can even go to the rooftop for some great views of the Empire State Building. 
The staff is friendly and helpful.
Cons: The rooms are small and cramped and really outdated. I picked up a copy of the hotel's brochure in the lobby and it claims be be newly renovated but I guess that must have been printed back in the 1980's. The wallpaper in our room (#603) was really gross and had a mysterious white stain running down it. The rooms and hallways are very dark and bleak. The shared bathrooms were always fairly clean but the fixtures are extremely outdated and at one point when I was showering the cold water stopped working and wasn't fixed for a couple of days. 
Overall, I would recommend this room for a short stay. We stayed here 7 nights which was just too long. Our room was overflowing with our purchases and we kept tripping over each other and our belongings.

title: “Wonderful stay”
text: My daughter and I stayed here for three nights. What a wonderful stay! The Staff was super friendly and the room was awesome. We had a small suite and the furnishings were all modern and very comfortable. The only downside is the shower wasn't scrubbed well, however, I have discovered that most hotel/motel showers aren't. I would recommend this Hotel to anyone and plan to stay here again.

title: “Awsome Great Location Great Staff”
text: Room was very nice, and clean, Beds very comfortable, empolyees every curtious, always said Hi and asked is there anything we can do for you. They were great in giving direction on things to see in and around Denver. Resturant was very nice we only had breakfast, food was good and nicely presented. Location couldn't have been better one block from 16th street, for resturants and shoping. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Abysmal!”
text:
It baffles me as to how this hotel could possibly be regarded as a four star. I had booked a room on Expedia, stating explicitly that I wanted a quiet room, on a high floor, with two beds. What did we find when we arrived? A room on the fifth floor, overlooking a busy main road, with a small double bed!! When I complained to reception they stated nonchalantly that all rooms were fully booked and they gave us what they had left - which was the worst room in the hotel! My wife was so upset she cried, and I was utterly furious! I then rang a number of NY hotels, finding them all fully booked until by a miracle I managed to find a room at the decent Novotel hotel (see my review of that one). We left the Excelsior as soon as we could but still had to pay one night to them - they did at least refund the other five nights.
Avoid this place like the plague!!

title: “Lots of extras for the price! Great location too!”
text: Hotel must have been apartments renovated to hotel rooms - suites are really just like a one bedroom apartment - a nice one though! We really enjoyed the free cocktail hour (which was extended because we were steered in the wrong direction) - very nice! We missed the milk and cookies as we were at dinner - but have heard people love this. Morning hot breakfast was also super, many choices - all delicious. Bathroom had a huge tub - nice extra as well. Would definitely stay again - oh and can't beat the location - right in the heart of everything downtown!

title: “Great Location”
text: The hotel was located in the middle of many of the sites of San Diego. Rooms were very clean and nice. They need an extra waffle iron on the weekends for the breakfast area, There are also several restaurants nearby. We enjoyed our stay and will return to this hotel the next time we are in San Diego!

title: “Fantastic!!!”
text: Wow! What a great experience staying at the Suites at Fisherman's Wharf during the week of July 20 - 27, 2012. You can't beat the location, as it is close to Fisherman's Wharf. The trolley and bus stops are literally steps from the hotel. The one bedroom suite was a like having a home away from home. There was plenty of space for 3 adults (my mother was traveling with us). The suite was clean, beautiful and comfortable. We were on the 3rd floor and had quick access to the roof top deck. The view is amazing! All of the staff were so wonderful. They catered to all of our needs. The staff were very knowledgeable regarding the area, they were friendly, and offered great suggestions for dining and navigating around San Francisco. We stayed at the Suites at Fisherman's Wharf for a week while attending a conference. The commute via bus to downtown was a breeze as it was only a 20 min. commute. Words really cannot express how truly amazing our stay was. I would definitely stay again!

title: “Great location!”
text:
This was my second stay at the Chancellor, first time in 2006. Choose this hotel again, for its location and comfort of the room.Appreciated the coffee and cookies in the lobby.
Was great to be able to buy a Muni pass from the gift shop in the hotel.

title: “Nice place - not great - but nice”
text:
Stayed here in mid August 2008 in the North tower - fifth floor.
Had none of the problems previously mentioned - it was a good stay. The staff was, as previously mentioned, excellent.
Room was clean and housekeeping arrived at around 2 pm every day. The lobby area is nice and the on-site restaurants are quite good.
The one problem is the street people that frequent the area and occasionally manage to infiltrate the hotel lobby itself. They are quite aggressive about begging for money. They approach with an extended hand, which if one accepts, apparently gives the beggar license to expound some ridiculous story that involves either the bus station or a local hospital and the need for $14. 
After one such encounter I blew the subsequent players off - and in one such instance he became violent and abusive. 
I noticed that the bell staff is fairly alert and that they move them along with a simple harsh glance.
Other than that (which is not the fault of the hotel) I enjoyed my four night stay.

title: “Good hotel. Great location.”
text: In this price range, it's the best hotel I found so far in NY. It's a good value! Great location, 1 block from Empire State Building. Lobby really small for the amount of people there. The front desk guy was rude but the rest of the staff was nice and friendly. Nice, clean and big room with a separate living area (with "sofa bed"). Small bathroom but this was not a problem. Elevator small and slow. Overall I good stay.

title: “Amazing hotel!”
text: Fantastic hotel, very modern and you can't beat the location right downtown within walking distance to everything. A bit pricey but cheaper than some of the other downtown hotels and I feel this is a better hotel overall. We will definitely stay here again to see Louis CK, who will be performing just down the street.

title: “Rooftop Clubbing”
text: The club in the Andaz hotel is great. Junior got me in the guest list and I was allowed access into the rooftop. It is amazing being on top of a hotel overlooking the beautiful city of San Diego. The staff are very professional, helpful and polite. The music is good and so are the women. I hold no regrets for visiting the Andaz hotel and club Ivy.

title: “Location and the Staff -- "The Best!"”
text: Yes the rooms are on the smaller side but clean, and the parking is across the street but the location and the price can't be beat. As for the staff, I could not remember a time when I was treated with such care. I know that this is there job and get paid to do this but I feel that they went above and beyond to help. If there was a answered need they were there to help. There was a manager named Scott that helped me and I don't think that there was a question that he did not know how to answer. He was the best. Need less to say if he is any guideline to how Club Quarters is run then I will be staying at Club Quarters for all my future trips.

title: “Quiet, huge room in the middle of it all”
text: We stayed in a Jr. Suite, and the room was huge! The bathroom was huge! It was well-appointed but very simple and modern. Linens were great. Quiet even though our room faced the street. Also quiet even though we were close to the elevator--didn't hear it at all. Didn't hear much noise from other guests either. During the day, the room was light and very nice. We looked down into the park, and watched people ice skate. The staff was so helpful and welcoming, I didn't expect it because this hotel seemed hip, but there was no attitude. During the day, there is tons to do walking distance from the hotel, and a subway stop right down the block. Super convenient.

title: “Service Shined”
text: This hotel lived up to all my expectations. The hotel was very clean & the rooms comfortable. The fitness room had more equipment than I had previously experienced. My midnight arrival was no problem

title: “Best Choice Near LAX”
text: I've stayed at a number of the three and four star hotels near LAX and the Westin seems to be the best choice in the area. Room was quiet and clean, bed was comfortable, lobby and amenities were good as well. If you need to overnight near LAX this is a solid choice for an airport property.

title: “Dirty and Old>>>>”
text: Beware.. this is place is so old and dirty..when you walk on the carpet your socks will be black from the dirt..The rooms are in very bad shape and the mildew smell is overwhelming....

title: “"Great Location, Great Hotel"”
text:
My wife,myself and our friends stayed at The Edison during the first week of March. We couldn't believe how close to Times Square it was. Less than a minutes walk and we were right in the center. Fabulous location! 
The hotel itself was pretty good too. We opted to stay in a twin-double room. So whilst it was a little small, it was by no means cramped. It was clean, tidy but in need of updating. But this shouldn't put you off.
The bathroom facilities were fine. REALLY hot shower every time, and the towels etc etc were changed often.The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful and the hotel bar was warm and welcoming, helped by friendly bartenders. 
Overall, a great location for a crazy city........

title: “Very nice but overrated”
text: The hotel lobby is extremely well decorated and impressive as are the rooms however the duck show is so lame and staying in the hotel isn't worth the price tag. Location is great and if you have the money to spend then by all means stay but if you dont you arent missing much.

title: “Nice hotel - Good Price - Large Rooms”
text:
I normally stay at other hotels when I am in NY, but this was a conference and this facility was recommended.
The rooms are quite large for New York City. I had a King Room that was similar to a Hampton Inn anywhere - but way larger than your average NY City Hotel - especially at Hampton Prices.
Nice Lobby. Large Breakfast facility (never large enough for the peak rush - but much better than most city hotels with free breakfasts).

title: “The NYC Experience!”
text: The Sheraton, built years ago as the Americana, is an ultralarge, convention dominated, excellent hotel. I've stayed here often and despite its size the staff do a great job of maintaining the rooms and public spaces. The location is fabulous if you are visiting from out of town and want to do the Times square and theatre district activities. The subway is a few blocks away and good food is steps from the front door of the hotel. I stayed here right after Hurricane Sandy and during the following Nor'easter and frankly none of this seem to have an impact on the hotels operation. The rooms themselves are a decent size and generally well appointed. The bathrooms are small but functional. The elevators split the hotel in two--1-28 and 29-50+...this works well, few waits etc. I particularly like the fitness club with its excellent equipment and spaciousness. This is a busy hotel with no sense of intimacy--but it works well.

title: “alcatraz is more liveable”
text: As soon as we arrived we were greeted by the friendly staff!!..clearly that is a sarcastic statement, once we had to spend more money at reception to get the rooms sorted, even though the travel agent had confirmed it all, we ventured up to our rooms, where we found a desolate room with disgusting layout, they say you "get what you paid for" well when we payed a decent amount for our stay, we got served second fiddle! You know a hotel is bad when it doesn't have the typical "bible" in the top draw. There was no alarm clock, desk light, tv remote, and dont get me started on the bathroom. In closing, I cannot wait for my stay to end and will be happy to depart, bed bugs and all!

title: “Worst Marriott Ever”
text: Any prior review commending the staff at this hotel must be outdated. Having stayed in many, many Marriotts, and having stayed in many of the best D.C. hotels (Willard, St. Regis, Hay Adams, etc.), this is by far the worst Marriott I've ever stayed at and the worst D.C. hotel. Elevators did not work. Called for shaving cream...never came. Called 45 minutes later...never came. Room temperature was completely messed up. Fan would never turn off, no matter the temperature setting. Beds and pillows were very uncomfortable. There are too many better hotels in D.C. (and in this area of D.C.) to justify staying at this Marriott -- especially at its price points.

title: “Fantastic staff!”
text: We couldn't fault the staff, especially those on reception. I want to mention "Cathy" and say a very big thank you to her for all of her help and for being so kind. Will definitely be staying at the Paramount on our next visit to New York.

title: “Not as good as I would have expected”
text: My husband (SPG Gold member) and I stayed here the second weekend it was open. The valet staff were great and very friendly but the front desk staff was just average. We asked for a room on a high floor away from noise and we got a 5th floor room that looked out over the atrium of the living room. When we checked in we didn't think it was that big of a deal but when we tried to sleep at 11:30pm the music from downstairs echo'd through the U shape building like a wind tunnel. Also we had a drink outside and it took about 20 minutes before a waitress came over to us, we even had to ask a bus boy to send our waitress over. In the morning we at at delphines and it took forever to get a waitress to come take our order. All in all, I think the service is lacking. The best part of the stay was the fitness room and going to the irish pub Dillon's across the street. They actually had waitresses who were nice and very prompt.

title: “Not what I've come to expect of Marriott”
text: Disappointed by my stay at this property. First of all, outside signage is non-existent. I drove completely around the building twice (there is a small, attached convention center) before asking two guests sitting on a bench if they were by the entrance door. They directed me back to registration on the opposite side. I unloaded my luggage from my car and went to reception where I was told that I needed to re-load my luggage and drive back to where I had seen the two people on the bench as my room was in the furthest reaches of the hotel. I said that having already unloaded it, I was not up to loading and unloading it again. There was no offer to help me get the bags to my room, so I struggled on. When I got to my room, I found that there was no bathtub - only a shower! I called down and asked if I could be moved to a room with a tub and was told to return to the front desk (presumably toting my bags) and they would give me a new key. I was too tired to do this, so settled for second best. In hotels that have rooms without bathtubs, this needs to be clearly stated in their web site or on the phone, and a preference should be asked. I had room service each of three nights and the food choices were extensive, but you wouldn't know this unless you called. The menu had just a handful of items. On one night, I ordered a burger. When it arrived, the deliverer said that she forgot the mustard, catsup and mayonnaise and would have to go back to the kitchen to get them. She must have been traipsing through the convention center, too, as when she returned about 15 minutes later, she said that they would remake the meal since it probably was cold. I said that was OK, as they were busy and the poor thing looked run off her feet. Unfortunately, when I uncovered the burger, it was missing the pickles, lettuce, onion and tomato, so I called down. The operator had an edge in her voice but the server returned with them. Unfortunately, but now, it was cold (about 30 minutes since delivered), but I gave up, unable to deal with it any more. Would not return.

title: “business trip”
text: This particular Wyndham was fine; however, the week prior in Wisconsin the Wyndham was deplorable. I would definitely check before going the next time and inquire if the rooms have been updated in the past few years.

title: “Pool was closed...we even asked about it at rsvp”
text:
Front desk staff and manage were rude and didn't care that we expected a heated pool. It was closed for renovation. 
We carried our down luggage cart. 
Buffet buffer items were not refilled in a timely manner. Waited 20 min for more pancakes. 
Overall disappointed!

title: “Over priced and over crowded”
text:
O.K. It is the cherry Blossom season and DC is over crowded. But there is no excuse for the lack of minimum service in this hotel. We paid about $380/night for this place. The room cleaning staff ONLY change towels. The pool is as dirty as one can imagine filled with Chlorine and kids who jump and dive in the pool ignoring the signs. The hotel staff also ignores their own signs. The breakfast items run out by 9:00 am while the breakfast is served until 9:30am. 
I have been to Embassy Suites in Tahoe. That is an upscale hotel compared to this. Don't you even think of coming here. I have heard the other ES in DC is nicer.

title: “Great place to go”
text:
We stayed 2 nights for my daughters 14th birthday trip to NYC. They even gave us birthday cupcakes.
The staff was the best ever! The room was enormous for a NYC room. We will be back to the Affinia 50! The only problem was i placed an order for the health and beauty aids that were offered, asked again at the desk, but never got them. Good thing there are duannes all over.

title: “Fabulous Property”
text:
I stayed at this hotel on a recent business trip to San Antonio. Having never been to San Antonio before, and tight on time, I was glad of the hotel's convenient location to the Riverwalk and other downtown attractions such as the Alamo.
The hotel itself is easy to find, but the porte cochere is a bit difficult to find. Valet parking, at $25 seemed a bit pricey for a small city like San Antonio, but not completely out of the scope of reason. After speaking with the valet attendant, I was informed that the lower priced parking across the street did not allow in/out privileges (I did not verify this with the garage operators).
I was allowed a much-appreciated early check-in and proceeded to my room which had a beautiful view of the Riverwalk. While the view was fantastic, I would not recommend paying much extra for this as the hotel is so convenient to the river, you'll be seeing it all day anyway.
The room was clean, quite comfortable and well laid out. The design fuses modern comfort and convenience with classic Texan colors and style.
I only dined at the morning breakfast buffet while staying at the Westin as I was more interested in the dining options lining the Riverwalk. Breakfast was very good and reasonable at about $16. Yes, a bit pricey for breakfast, but this IS a very nice hotel.
The staff was friendly and kept their cool well during a very busy Sweet 16 weekend. The valet and bell attendants were extremely helpful with directions, luggage and very quick in retrieving my vehicle from valet.
I highly recommend this property...for the business or leisure traveler.

title: “good location, nice stay”
text:
my husband and I stayed fro 3 night in March 2012 and we enjoyed our stay.
Location: The hotel is ideally locted in walking distance of main attarctions of Manhattan.
You don't need to take a taxi at all, time sqr is 10 min walk, broad way Ave, fashion district, Empire state bldg... are all at max 15 min walking distance.
ROOM and STAFF:Our room was clean not very spacious but enough for our loggage !!( we had 8 loggage in total !!!!). bed was comfortable, the breakfast was very good. BUT one of the issues is the lift, the hotel has two lifts which is used by guests as well as the house keping staff so in specially in morning time you should expect longer waiting time.
The front desk staff (all shifts) and concierge, bellman,... were all friendly and ready to assist you at all tiem.
MUST do: take a hop on hop off tour to go around manhattan and central park , BUT the tour that was available in hotel concierge was not good, the waiting time in each stop exceeds 1 hr in that breezy weather and wasted our time alot while the other tour was always on time and frequent , therefore I informed the lady at concierge and told her it would be more convenient for hotel guests if they can work with the other tour.
A HINT: you may expect some noise if your room is located close to ice maker machine.

title: “Poor customer service, and hotel manager ruined it for us”
text:
I stayed at this hotel with my twin sons during the last week of October. We flew from California to visit local relatives my children had never met, and to see the capital. This was my sons' first trip anywhere, and a 10th birthday treat. I chose the hotel for its suite arrangement with kitchen facilities, and for its continental breakfast, which I figured we would need at least the first morning, before we had a chance to shop for food.
Our flight was delayed and we arrived at the hotel at 11:30 p.m. The person at the front desk saw me struggling to get our luggage up the steps just inside the front door but made no offer to help--in fact, he disappeared into a back room until I'd assembled everything in front of the desk. I checked in, then hauled everything to our room, where there was no sign of the rollaway I'd ordered and no linens for the stained and rickety sofabed, even though it was obvious at least one of us would have to sleep on it. (There was only one bed in the bedroom area.) I called downstairs for some linens and was told to come down and get them myself! When I got down there at midnight I was handed a threadbare blanket and some sheets, but no pillow, as they couldn't find one.
The next morning I dragged myself out of bed at 9 a.m. (6 a.m. California time) to go down to the breakfast area and get some food. I took one of my sons with me but reluctantly left the other one in bed, as he still wasn't feeling well after first complaining of feeling sick on the plane. I took along a small plastic bag so we could bring some bagels or toast back and still carry a couple of drinks.
When I got to the basement breakfast area I saw a sign posted in the doorway that breakfast would end at 9:30 and that food was to be consumed in the breakfast area. But with a sick child upstairs, the clock ticking, and not knowing about this rule before, I went ahead and gathered four pieces of (very stale) toast and two hard-boiled eggs, and started pouring some juice into two cups for my helper son and me to transport upstairs. Immediately a man appeared from a back room and asked me if I planned to take the food out of the breakfast area. I said yes and explained that I had a sick child I couldn't leave alone upstairs and no food, as I had checked in very late. Apparently not believing me, he folded his arms in a very aggressive posture and loudly and obnoxiously said he was "sick and tired of people like you coming in here with bags to take my food. You just want to save it for snacks later. My policy is no food is to be removed from here, and I'm not letting you out of here with that food." 
I was truly stunned by this. (For one thing I wondered why anyone would want to steal stale bread and warm milk.) I told him he could inspect the food I was taking to see if it was an appropriate amount for three people, but this seemed to enrage him further and he refused, and just moved toward me menacingly. I then told him that the only other option was for me to go upstairs and bring my sick child to the dining area, where he could spread germs around to others. He said nothing and just continued to stand there. So I went upstairs, coaxed the sick one out of bed, and tried to console my helper son, who wanted to know why the hotel thought we were thieves.
That was our introduction to Washington D.C. and the Georgetown Hotel.
The rest of the stay was uneventful, though cold (the windows didn't close all the way and the heater thermostat didn't work) and noisy (the room overlooked an apartment building with patios where residents had loud social gatherings until late at night.) I never went to the breakfast room again, so the hotel certainly saved some money on our week-long stay. Whenever we crossed paths with this manager he avoided eye contact, and seemed uncomfortable when other staffers chatted with my quiet and well-behaved twins.
What a disappointment. The only reason I even give this hotel two stars is for the location (near Metro and Trader Joe's), and the spacious and pretty clean room.

title: “Nice location on the bay”
text: I booked this hotel while I was in town for a conference - I stayed there for three days, two nights (Mon, Tue, left wed), I did get an excellent price for the room, but they stuck me at the end of the furtherest room, next to marina parking lot and maintenance. The hotel was pretty much open, being it was in November and the weekday...I wish they would have put me a lil close to something other than the noise but with that being said, the room was nice, it looked like it was upgraded. The room had two beds, not very comfortable to me. The room also had a microwave, a nice coffee maker & frig. While I had a lil off time from the conference, I was able to check out the grounds. It's very tropical & well kept up. It had two pools and two jacuzzi's.

title: “Motel stay”
text: We stayed one night at the Travellodge at the Space Needle in Seattle. The only reason we stayed there is because it was close to the Key Arena for a concert. It is an expensive motel plus we had to pay $15.00 a day plus tax to park our car in their parking lot!! I don't really think they monitor the parking lot because we saw other cars parked in there that did not have a dasboard pass. We didn't want to take the chance of our car being towed so we paid that in addition to the motel room. We did not get much sleep because there was a water softener or something connected to the bottom of the sink in the bathroom and it would knock intermittently all night long and of course, it would knock whenever you fell back asleep!! We wanted to unplug the unit but it had a label on the outlet to not unplug. We did not report it to the staff because it was close to midnight when we got back to our room and we knew that the maintenance worker would not be availabe at that time of night.

title: “OK but overpriced”
text: The hotel was OK, we stayed in the "new" tower which is a renoation of the old tower. Bath rooms are small. Service is extremely slow. Breakfast is very poor.

title: “Can't go wrong with this one...”
text:
Was attending a convention for one day in San Fran and then planned to take a few more days to relax and see the sights. We were booked into the Argonaut for 5 days and must say that the location is perfect.
Early morning walks on the Piers overlooking the Golden Gate, to late night taxis home from restaurants and bars, everything was enjoyable.
We were in a room on the 3rd floor facing the street behind the hotel. Not bad, but could have been less exciting as a few rooms face an internal courtyard where nothing much is going on. The marine theme is consistent throughout the hotel, a bit unusual at first, but you quickly get used to it. The rooms are very clean and comfortable.
There is a wine bar next to the front entrance, which is a good place to have a local bottle before heading out.
Need a taxi? It can be a bit hit or miss, but the bellmen/concierge are glad to help with enthusiasm!

title: “Great historic hotel!”
text: The Blackstone once hosted the likes if Al Capone. It is very historic and is amazingly updated inside since Marriott bought it. About a mile from the heart of Chicago. The hotel has a FANTASTIC Spanish restaurant. Don't miss it!

title: “Clean, Cheap, Confortable.”
text: If you plan to stay in San Diego this hotel is cheap and clean! The staff is very helpfull. If you plan to rent a car, you have an AVIS in front of (Hotel Circle North). You can take the Bus or you have near the Trolley. Very good option.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Trump Soho for the 4th time and each time the experience has been great. The experienced staff directed us to great restaurants and made reservations at top hard to get places for us and friends. Even our NYC friends were surprised that we got in. The one bedroom suite was beautiful, spacious, and extremely well maintained. If you want a top notch NYC experience, I would recommend the TRUMP SOHO.

title: “All Around Very Nice”
text:
As others have written previously, the Omni Chicago is a great hotel. We stayed about a week. I was tagging along on a business trip my boyfriend had. He checked in the night before I arrived. He left my name at the desk and I had no problem obtaining a key. 
The room is very comfortable and having the two rooms makes it nice when one person is a nightowl or gets up early to go to work. TVs in both rooms. DVD player in the living area (and a Blockbuster is about a block away). Bed was super comfy with high quality linens. We had a corner room (1717) and looked north and west. Not a great view but good light. 
We did have the mini bar key and used that refrig to store small things in. (There's a Trader Joe's three blocks away.)
The entire staff was pleasant, efficient and professional. The concierge gave us some great ideas for dining and made reservations for us. 
The location is great, just off Michigan Ave. across from the Apple Store. The red line train is 3 blocks away at State and Chicago. 
We got a good rate: $159 during the week and $171 over the weekend nights. Good value for the quality. 
Sign up for their loyalty program and get free wifi and delivered coffee and juice in the morning. But skip their restaurant. It's nothing special and there's lots in the area. Also the business center charged $6.95 per 15 minutes to use the internet (although you could print airline boarding passes for free). I just waited until BF got back with his laptop. 
Finally, sign up for a Chicago Greeter. I had a great 4 hour walkabout and saw things and explored neighborhoods I'd never been to before.

title: “An Great Find”
text:
The Library was recommended by a friend. Even though I was there for only 1 night, I found it a very nice place. Staff were exceptionally friendly and room was well appointed and large enough (by NYC standards).
I would return to The Library Hotel for sure.
Lindsay

title: “Park Central Hotel needs to be cleaned throughly and updated”
text: I spent 3 days at this hotel over a long weekend. The location (just 2 blocks from Central Park) was ideal for us. The staff was somewhat helpful if not uninterested in assisting people. If your room is not ready (tried to check in 15 minutes early), you must check your bags for $3.50 each. There is no free wifi available, and the lady at check-in suggested the nearby Starbucks. Our first room was so filthy that we asked to change rooms. The second room they gave us was slightly better, but still way below what we are used to in terms of upkeep and quality. Some other reviewers found this hotel to be a good value, however at around $300 a night with tax; there are many better options nearby. I will be sticking to a chain next time.

title: “Great service!”
text:
My brief stay in Austin was great, and I have the Hilton on Research Blvd to thank.
From the moment my co-worker and I walked in - we were greeted in a friendly manor. And even thought we did not check in until quite late in the evening, the gentleman at the front desk was able to suggest a delicious all night pancake house where we could grab a quick bite.
The rooms are clean and spacious, are setup perfectly for persons needed to do a little work while away, and have conformable beds where you can adjust the softness/hardness. (very sweet!)
My room also came with a fridge, microwave, coffee maker and iron. Everything you could need while on the road. The breakfast buffet available was also very convenient and yummy!
There are a lot of great restaurants around Research Blvd, including Chuys and Rudy's (you MUST visit Rudy's, best BBQ I ever had).

title: “Almost Perfect!”
text:
I know most reviews are saying this hotel is old and outdated, and it is! It didn't bother me though. My family was there for spring break 2012 during the busy cherry blossom season. We JUST missed the blossoms as the winter was so warm they came early. Let me tell you, there is NO OTHER hotel in a better location that this one! You are RIGHT THERE! The trees are all around you! The bands and activities are right outside your door! Our room faced the channel and we awoke every morning to the marina and fell asleep seeing the sunset over the Jefferson Memorial! WOW!!
This hotel is within a 15 minute walk to the National Mall. There is a circulator bus that stops right across the street and takes you right thru downtown! $1 per person!!! The metro is also about 10 minute walk away. We went to Arlington Cemetery on Easter Sunday and we were there in a few minutes. It's right across the bridge a few blocks from the hotel!! 
The restaurant in the hotel is marvelous! A bit high priced but the view of the water is wonderful and the food was great!! The hotel also has a small breakfast cafe where you can get basically anything you want for breakfast. PS...kind $$ of high if you are getting anything but your basic breakfast. They really get you on the sides but the food is really good!!! 
I have heard tell of a grumpy front desk manager. I have to say I talked with 4 different desk people and they were all more than helpful! The gentleman I believe everyone is referring to was a bit gruff but very nice and helpful. Even the maids were GREAT!!
The only reason I didn't give this hotel 5 stars is that it definitely is old and ragged. It was clean though!!! and the bed was lumpy!!
PS...DO NOT USE THE PIZZA DELIVERY that the hotel recommends. They STICK!! The pizza was aweful and it was VERY overpriced! The delivery kid actually made avery loud remark because we only gave him $2.70 for a tip on a 2 pizza delivery!!! AND he was 30 minutes late!!! Geez!!!

title: “The Best Staff Ever”
text: i stayed at the memphis airport courtyard for a week and i had the time of my life the staff was so triendly and so helpful. the worker that was working that night james helped me every night that i spent there i stay there for a week and every day he ask me have i eatten or was i hungry or did i need to go any where he made me feel like i was at home and that if i need anything he would go above and beyond th do it. and he told me that his general manager told them to never tell the guest no. now thats service

title: “San Diego Adventure”
text: The Hyatt Regency Mission Bay is a well maintained and great looking resort. The service was faultless throughout our stay the only downside was that due to the location there was very little retail / food available within walking distance therefore expect to pay resort prices for your food and drink on site. The resort has a great feel to it and always something going on to keep the kids amused. Public transport is easily accessible with a metro bus stop only a very short walk from the resort. It is also very close to Seaworld therefore the added bonus of a free fireworks display most nights.

title: “Good stay”
text:
Value for money. Airo a bit noisy, as usual in motels. Location on a busy street, but near I59.
Clean, proper facilities.

title: “This hotel overbooked my room last year”
text:
WARNING, DO NOT STAY OR BOOK THIS HOTEL: 
I am finding hotel where I want to stay next week in Boston. Last year's things remind me why we should not make a reservation in The Boston Backbay hotel. 
This hotel overbooked my room even if I fully pre-paid my stay and then attempted to waive its responsability. In some jurisdictions, selling the same thing (the right to occupy the room) twice, is considered fraud. 
In my many (over 20) years of travelling, many of which have been for business travel around all continents and staying at hotels of all levels, from small family owned hostels to high-end Asian ultra-luxury palaces, I had never experienced such an unethical and illegal behaviour as the BackBay Hotel. 
This hotel does not honor its basic contractual obligations, even when stays ave been pre-paid. Leaves no option but to sue in court. 
Do not run the risk, stay elsewhere. There are plenty other ethical options in Boston.
I cann't not forget this kind of experience in The BackBay Hotel in rest of my life.

title: “Nice boutique hotel”
text:
Positives - friendly staff, good breakfast, free soft drinks and snacks all day, wine reception, quite close to all central amenities. 
Negatives - very small room, very very noisy (creaking floorboards and noise all night long so don't expect a good nights sleep). Overall, expensive for the room but the extras do make up for up somewhat.

title: “Decent hotel, doesn't seem like a 4 star”
text: Good hotel, good price but parking is expensive $32/day

title: “Good property, great location”
text: I had stayed at the Latham several years ago, and took advantage of their special pricing during renovation to see the Van Gogh exhibit at the Art Museum. The boutique hotel has a great location just off Rittenhouse Square. The room was larger than you would expect from an older property, and very comfortable. The staff was friendly and helpful.

title: “Great location; pool not the best for beginning swimmers”
text:
Very nice hotel in a GREAT location -- we enjoyed our 1 night stay. We booked through Hotwire[--] for $182/night on a weekend when both the Tall Ships and LollaPalooza (sp?) were in town and rooms everywhere were expensive. We're more used to Holiday Inn/Comfort Inn type accomodations but even the downtown locations for those chains were more expensive, at least for the night we were staying.
The valet staff courteously explained the parking/luggage process (something we are used to doing ourselves), and the front desk staff were efficient if not overly friendly. However, housekeeping ignored our Do Not Disturb sign and rang our doorbell promptly at 9 AM to see if they could make up our room. Also, the light bulb was burned out in the small entry hallway in our room, making it hard to see in the hallway closet. The bellhop that brought up our luggage said he would contact maintenance to get it fixed, but nothing ever happened. Another word of caution: parking is $41, not the $10 to $25 estimate listed on the Hotwire website. However, we were allowed to drop off the car 2 hours before check-in time (our room was ready that early also), and leave it in the garage 5 hours after check-out. We walked or took free trolleys everywhere (Navy Pier, Millenium Park, American Girl Store, Rainforest Cafe), saving us parking fees at other places. 
The pool area is gorgeous, if you like historical decor, which we do. The pool itself is huge (75 feet long). However the shallow end is 4 feet deep, so if you have young children be sure to bring their flotation devices. Our daughter ended up using the kickboards that are available at the fitness center desk (one of the few things that were free). We were a little surprised that there was a substantial daily fee ($17?) to use the fitness center. 
Our room was in the Historical Tower, and faced Michigan Ave. As another reviewer mentioned, we heard sirens all night, even though our windows were closed. We just figured that was part of the Chicago experience! Our room had 2 double beds, but one of them was about 6" from the wall. It was fine for the three of us, but a fourth person would have had a hard time getting out of bed. Obviously hard for the maid to vacuum also, as there was a row of dust bunnies along that baseboard. Otherwise the room and bathroom were very clean and comfortable.

title: “Good location and good price”
text: Booked the Holiday Inn through Hotwire for $75 a night - when we rang in advance and asked for a twin room they said they could not promise anything because we booked through a third party. When we arrived we did get a twin room - double beds - rooms are small, bathroom very small, but clean and great showers. Location is very good, 10 minute walk from Quincy Market and Boston Common and a few minutes away from the nearest red line stop which takes you to Harvard in 10 minutes. Staff are very friendly and helpful. There is also a great bar called Sevens just round the corner. All in all, you get more than what you pay for - it's not fancy but it's absolutely fine and I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Best hotel in new York!”
text: The hotel was perfect, the service and the staff were so nice and warm, they took care of everything we asked and did it with alot of caring. The location was perfect. The hotel have a nice pool on the last floor. We really enjoy every minute of the the staying. Highly recommended !!!

title: “Great place to stay in Dallas Texas”
text: What is there to say? I stayed there at the end of November 2012. The hotel is very clean and the staff very attentive to your every need. Valet parking is nice. The wireless network does need some improvement depending on which floor you are located. The location is not the best but is easily accessible by car. Overall a very nice and safe place to stay.

title: “A good base for an amazing experience!”
text:
Staff helpful, friendly & attentive. With the exception of the waiter in the bar who's name sadly escapes me. Horrible little thing!
Sadly as with any hotel in New York on a tourist trip like we had, you spend little time in the hotel and most of your time seeing the sights and taking in the amazing atmosphere of the Big Apple so although we did choose this hotel on it's merit on TripAdvisor we really did only sleep here, exhausted after a busy busy day to be honest, we took little notice of the hotel itself. The beds as most people comment are truely amazing, the rooms, well decorated, comfortable, the shower is lovely. I have no complaints about this hotel, i would re-visit. However, if you are looking for a special/romantic/once in a lifetime hotel, there are other hotels that we looked at that were superior with the extra attention to detail. Enjoy

title: “Small Beds for a spacious room”
text:
I stayed for the President's day weekend in a double bed "suite", which is really nothing more than a large room. Not even a room divider. It came with a mini fridge and microwave. It had a small couch and two double beds. New 32" flat panel HDTV, but only a very limited selection of HD channels.
The room was certainly large enough to accommodate two queen beds, but they only put in doubles. 
It does have an indoor pool, hot tub and work out room which are adequate, but nothing spectacular.
The self serve free breakfast was okay and included waffle maker, sausage patties, hot eggs, cereal, breads, but the coffee was awful.
Other than a business office park not much else around in the immediate area besides a gas station and fast food joints.

title: “It was a great moment..”
text: We spent short but a great time in Chicago.It was really a " windy city "..Museums, pizzas, streets, skyscrapers all were fantastic.I miss there and wish to see the ciyt soon...

title: “Week Long Stay with No Problems”
text: We needed a place to stay during a move and settled on this hotel because of the reviews here on Trip Advisor. We stayed on the first floor near the lobby, which I figured would be loud, but it actually has not been a problem at all. There was a loud dog (the hotel is pet friendly) one night, but other than that, it has been very quiet and pleasant. The rooms are good-sized, but not huge. They have really high ceilings which give a feeling of openness that is very nice. I'm often wrangling my kids in the morning and need later housekeeping services and they have been very accommodating. Everyone in the family has been happy with the breakfast selections, which are substantial and include things from cereal to eggs and bacon or sausage, waffles you can make for yourself, and more. My kids are fans of the cookies they have in the lobby in the evening. The hotel is very clean and well maintained, staff is friendly and helpful. The hotel is located in a safe area and is well lit and convenient to lots of shopping and dining. Lakeline Mall is a few minutes away, and if you go south on 183 from the hotel area, there are tons of restaurants and shops as you go into Austin. North 183 goes to Cedar Park, and 620, which is not far, goes out to Round Rock. One thing worth noting if you are planning to work in the "business center" - it's very small and located in the middle of the lobby. The rooms have Wi-fi, though, so that helps a great deal. We would definitely stay here again and I would recommend it to my friends and family.

title: “Felt like home!”
text: My family of five ( including 3 teens) stayed at this hotel for 4 nights and had a great time! The rooms are spacious with plenty of storage areas.The beds were very comfortable! The hotel and grounds where very clean and well kept. There is a nice pool and game court (basketball, tennis,etc-equipment at the front desk) along with a patio area and grilling area. there is an library area with two computers and some board games and books. Breakfast was really good and not too crowded. The front desk was very helpful as was everyone else I spoke with. Close by there is a Target, Sam's Club and Spouts. also just a 5 mintue drive from the hotel is a beautiful shopping area/mall called "The Domain" and a yummy burger place, "Mighty Fine". One more plus was that our dog was able to stay with us! My only complaint was that the hallways were kinda hot....of course we are in Texas in July.

title: “a great Resort!! The Best!!”
text: Had a great time, everyone was very nice just wanted to say every single employee there is very friendly and they treated us very well, Their Fitness room is great and very big. Meet alot of people, had 2 employees that were trimming a tree, they stopped what they were doing and helped my husband to unload our luggage and assisted him with my son and his wheelchair, cant forget their names (Carlos and Gabriel) The Breakfast was delicious and room service was great also!!!!!! looking forward to go back soon to enjoy their ammenities especially their waterpark!!! I really recommend everyone to visit!

title: “Perfectly adequate with great staff”
text:
I stayed here as part of a week long stay in LA where I also spent nights in the W Hollywood and the SLS Beverly hills. The SLS is a beautiful hotel, but for my final 2 nights I was mainly going to be working, and I didn't see the point of spending $600 a night on a suite when all was going to be doing was sitting behind the desk. So I decamped to the much cheaper Sheraton Downtown.
And what can I say? I really was very happy there. It's a mid tier Sheraton, not the newest but not the oldest either, and the area of downtown is actually pretty OK with Macys, Starbucks, Walgreens all very close. Everything you need. I also really liked Octopus (sushi restaurant opposite) which served pretty decent sushi that was also, like the hotel, great value.
Top marks go the staff who were superbly friendly both on the front desk and around the hotel, exceptionally so in fact - it was them that made me decide to write this review.
One negative is that the hotel does not have it's own gym - instead you sign into the Bally gym in the shopping arcade. The distance is not a problem but the gym is fairly horrible, a fairly old 1980s style place. So if you do like a nice private hotel gym, you'll miss that here.
So in summary, it's not somewhere I'd bring a date to impress and won't be on my top 10 list of hotels, but for a solid Sheraton to kill a few days working in LA in, it did a great job.

title: “Kimpton is always pleasant”
text:
Enjoyed my 3 nights at the Palomar recently. Room overlooked the courtyard/Old Navy store below. Goldfish to stare at, cool old dog guarding the lobby. Everything functioned as it should in a hotel, though I felt my room was a little dated compared to other Palomar and Kimpton rooms I've seen. Like maybe this was an "early" Palomar and 10-12 years old, in need of a refresh. Good location if you're doing the Moscone convention scene (2-3 blocks), and right on Market (seedy but cross it and you're at Union Sq in 5 minutes.) SF is a great walking city, and this place is in the heart of it all. 
I'd like it if they had a coffee maker in-room, but there's free coffee at the 5th-floor restaurant in the morning so you'll get your drip on, either way. Wine reception in the afternoon is nice, though I didn't partake. They've got town cars for the airport ride which cost a couple bucks more than the (already overpriced) taxis but are more pleasant.
No lobby to speak of but they'll always greet you at the door and as you breeze past the front desk (6 steps to the elevator, but who's counting.)
Fully-stocked mini-bar in the room, with a little space to spare for the odd beverage you might want to add.

title: “It just needs a little attention to it.”
text:
Stayed two nights this week on business, upgraded on arrival i was told to the SPG members floor - however I am an SPG member so should have been on that floor anyway - my two colleagues were not but got the upgrade to that floor - so good for them, but i felt like my membership wasnt that valued.
No Minibar in room (think this is now a hotel chain policy) but none of the vending machines on five floors i tried worked or had any product in them so i was a little thirsy in the night.
Bed comfortable, room a good standard, but bathroom needs a refit - it just looked tired and old. Bar area in main reception was good, couldnt at all fathom the parking entry / exit thing despite been given a validated ticket for my two day stay by reception, i couldnt get into the car park with it on day two so took another ticket (which i then binned as i had my single validated one) then on my final exit from the car park at 10am after check out (ticket validated to 4pm) it said it was not a valid ticket which was annoying, with more cars behind me and no barrier preventing my exit i had to just drive out - if i subsequently get a huge charge for seemingly driving out without a valid ticket i will be complaining - as yet though i am good.
The folks on reception and at the bar - very good - a saving grace for this tired hotel :)

title: “service/ambience/location - A+++”
text:
Less than a block from the Public Market, this is a primo location. More importantly, you will feel so welcomed, beginning with the valet and bell service and then the front desk. We splurged on the water view room which didn't disappoint - sat for hours (early a.m, daytime and evening) watching activities on the Bay. Concierge and Front Desk extremely helpful with recommendations and directions. I truly felt pampered and would return in a heartbeat!
The rooftop terrace is quite large with many chairs, tables and lounges....bring your wine and some cheese and watch the sun go down. The flower bouquets at the Market will blow your mind - they're only $5 so buy one and the hotel will provide a vase!

title: “Much more than we expected!!”
text: This Country Inn & Suites used to be a "step up" as a Cambria Suites. It's a bit offputting from the outside - very plain and modern and looks like it might be an office building but once inside it's quite lovely. The furnishings in the lobby as well as the suites is very modern and sleek. The suites are large, nicely furnished with a TV room and a separate bedroom. The beds are really really comfy! The complimentary breakfast is adequate, waffles, breads, fruit and each day a different hot entree like breakfast burritos or sausage and biscuit sandwiches. Coffee both in the room and in the dining room is good. We stayed Christmas Eve and Christmas Day and although there were signs stating that rooms would only be cleaned on Christmas Day by request our room was cleaned anyway - which we thought was nice but had not requested such. We were quite satisfied and stay in San Antonio quite a lot since we have family there and we will definitely stay here again! Kudos to the staff for a very pleasant stay!

title: “worst breakfast ever”
text: This morning we went down to the breakfast area and it was poorly stocked to say the least. We stood in a long line only to find that the hot items were completely gone. What was left was merely some stale muffins and cheap danishes. Not to mention that there was no staff member there to replenish the items that were in short supply. The hotel is close to the harbor and that is the only selling factor. Definitely overpriced and not worth the money.

title: “Nice - but showing wear.”
text: We stayed one night. Had been there twice in the last few years. Staff and view very nice. Hotel is starting to show some wear. A couple of chips in bathroom tile. Several stains on carpet in room. Older model TV. I am not very picky - but for price - feel like should be kept up. Pay $25 if want valet parking. Restaurant - some items good, others fair. Overall - pricey. I was a litle bit disappointed - but had a nice experience overall.

title: “Elan Hotel deserves its high rating”
text: This boxy hotel on a busy street nonetheless feels innovative and personal. It is adapted for 21st century travelers, skipping the unused add-ons (in house restaurant, glam lobby) but providing all of the details I look for in a room -- reliable free internet, big enough closet with lots of hangers (11); coffee maker; alarm clock with big display of the time, iron, toiletries, decent pillows, and windows that open. The free breakfast buffet, which provided healthy choices, and smiling desk staff made the hotel a convenient bargain as well. The turn down service turned the clock radio on to the local NPR classical mustc station, which clinched my five star rating. Only price complaint is cost of parking, but given the outsourced valet model, it worked pretty well. There are lots of options and lots of neighborhoods in LA, but the Elan fit my needs very well.

title: “Wonderful, Wonderful, Wonderful”
text:
We stayed at the Vitale in early October - it was our first trip to San Francisco and also our honeymoon.
We have read many reviews of the Vitale which comment upon the great location, the excellent standard of the rooms and the coolness of the interior and exterior spaces - and we agree with them all.
We would like to comment upon the 'experience' of staying at the Vitale at the beginning of October 2005.
At check in we were greeted extremely warmly and courteously - the staff appeared to have a genuine interest in us and our trip. When Reception discovered we were on our honeymoon they immediately offered us a complimentary bottle of Champagne. As if this was not enough, they also asked my wife if she preferred chocolates or flowers!
Somehow, by the time we got up to our room a chilled bottle of Champage and a box of liqueur chocolates were waiting for us - which made us feel very special indeed.
Throughout our stay other staff members (particularly the barman and a wonderful waitress in Americano)made us feel particularly welcome and at home in the hotel. I would go so far as to say that the Vitale had by far the friendliest and most helpful staff of any hotel I have ever stayed in.
We went on a trip around California for the second week of our holiday, but returned to San Francisoco for our final two days. We loved the Vitale so much that we booked in for the final nights before we returned home. When we returned to the Hotel we were given a great room on the 4th floor, which was of the same standard as we had stayed in on our first stay. The only drawback was that it had a view of the inner courtyard (as opposed to the Bay bridge etc). When I asked the manager about the possibility of a change of room he could not have been more helpful and understanding.
He explained that the hotel was fully booked for that night, but promised that he would provide us with a room with a view for our final night. True to his word - and typical of the lengths Vitale staff went to during our stay - we were upgraded (at no extra cost) to one of the oval suites with panoramic plate glass windows, sunken bath,walk in shower, and 180 degree views of the Bay. 
This gesture was the perfect end to a fantastic holiday - and something that will live long in our memory. It just goes to show that the hotel industry still has the capacity to turn a 'stay' into an 'experience'- it is just unfortunate that there are not more hotels that try as hard as the Vitale.
Thank you Hotel Vitale - you are wonderful!

title: “The place to stay in New York!”
text: Travelled with my husband and two adult sons, our first visit to New York and to the USA. We were made so welcome by Jay and his excellent team, they are all genuine, warm people who go the extra mile to make sure all their guests are well looked after and any request for help is met with an honest desire to assist and please. However, they are not at all intrusive, it is like being a house guest but with more freedom, they have the balance just right. All has been said before about the superbly clean, well equipped rooms, they are small but cosy and comfortable to return to after a busy day enjoying the sights. Great not having to rush out for breakfast, thoroughly enjoyed our leisurely breakfast in the garden, a good choice of bagels, muffins, fruit, yoghurt etc, couldn't have asked for more. Thank you to the young man who went shopping to get me English breakfast tea when they had run out! Chelsea market is a must for local produce and a treat of lobster and cup cakes! Jay gives you a great map, shopping guide, restaurant guide and theatre tips, we saw James Corden in ' One man two governors', a must if like us you appreciate splitting your sides laughing, Jay will tell you how to get reduced price tickets. Hotel location perfect for the subway, we bought a week pass which was terrific value, also enjoyed the museum of natural history, biking in central park and a different day out to the zoo at the Bronx ! Thank you to all for making our stay so special, we would not hesitate to return or recommend.

title: “Definitely not recommended”
text:
Horrible, just horrible, I don't know where to begin:
- plumbing in my bathroom was never fixed. The shower ran from hot to scalding. And it would randomly fluctuate during your shower from those two temperatures. I have an infant daughter and was deathly afraid of giving her 3rd degree burns during her bath.
- Breakfast was OK as long as you showed up before 8 AM. After that it's pretty slim pickings as the food does NOT get replenished. The lady who looks after it from Mon to Thurs is very nice but the other two who do the weekend shift spent most of their time hiding from guests.
- the hot tub was out-of-order during the entire week I was there. The pool had a LOT of sand in the bottom of it. Neither were fixed nor cleaned. 
- anytime you asked the front counter staff for anything (shuttle bus, detergent for the 4th floor laundromat) they didn't know the answer, the bus just left, we just ran out of soap, the plumber just fixed it, etc... It was like listening to people describing UFO sightings.
- front counter staff did NOT know the neighbourhood at all. When we asked him where the closest grocer was he had us walk 20 min down to the bad part of Washington Ave. How bad? I was in line between a drug addict and a drunk. We found a grocery store later that day just 4 blocks away.
In my case this was one of the last hotels available (I was going to the ESRI conference June 2007) and I will never allow myself nor any of my coworkers to stay here at future conferences. San Diego is a beautiful place to visit. Just don't stay at the Sommerset Suites.

title: “great location”
text: If you are going to Times Square area this is the best place to stay. Right in the middle of it all. We were able to walk all the way to Central Park. Not that far. Rooms were big. Had 2 adults and 2 kids ages 17 and 12 plenty of room. Prices are high in resturant food ok. Eat at Juniors across the street. Good food and they give you alot. Great Cheesecake. Saw Mary Poppins show it was wonderful. Would see it again. No problems with the elevators. Very fast. Stayed from June 30th to July 4th. People everywhere. Would stay here again. No noise from the street. Were on the 42nd floor. Staff was very helpful and very nice.

title: “AMAZING”
text:
This was a splendid hotel and it provided all the necessary amenities. For instance, free WIFI in lobby is huge and the link @ sheraton experience was phonomenal. Very close to a metro station which makes it very easy to commute and in the heart of downtown right by all the necessities wallgreens, etc. I managed to snag this on priceline so I got a terrific rate and also early check in. Room was cozy a tad cold but did what I would expect for what I paid. No complaints, very very happy.
I've discovered a secret to a decent room.... Say.. I am very sensitive to noise so would I be able to get a hotel room higher up? This eliminates all noise issues.. I love it.

title: “Great place for business travel & awesome bar”
text: I had the pleasure of staying here for a week while on business to Charlotte. This place was great with nice spacious rooms, big lobby with bar and a great outside patio. It was the off season but was right new to the Panthers stadium and would think this would be a great place to stay for a game. Their staff was great for my entire stay and made it feel like home. It is within walking distance of lots of great resturants and things to do. I highly reccommend this hotel.

title: “Try to avoid the hotel at all cost despite its low rate”
text:
Being this our first visit in NY, we wanted to make sure that we stay in the best location possible. Well, our wish was granted - Park Central Hotel's only advantage is its location; everything else is just enough to ruin even the LOCATION advantage.
We got to the hotel after a 13 hour flight and were given a key to a room on a 19th floor - two out of the four elevators didn't work so we waited about ten minutes for the elevator. Made it to the room, which was located next to the ICE MACHINE, which was making an enormous amount of noise! Got inside the room to find a cockroach on the ceiling welcoming its guests. Disgusting!
Went into the bathroom to find wet towels and when I finally opened the curtains, I was petrified with a feeling that I am in a prison cell - the tiny window that's looking directly to someone else's room and just a bit of glimpse onto the street.
Well, that was the last draw - I was hating New York already and I haven't even been anywhere. I asked for another room and having the big plus of wearing high heels and a tight top that day, I was given a better room on a higher floor, which only meant we needed to wait even longer for the elevator to come up. Wouldn't recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Great Rooms and Service”
text: This is a very nice hotel, very rustic and warm and inviting. They have a great staff and they are very, very, very friendly. Great value.

title: “Family stay at the Parker NYC”
text: We had a nice stay at the Meridien. Our second time there with kids in tow. We took advantage of the family special and got a spacious and comfortably outfitted room. The rooms are looking a little tired, but they are a good size by NYC standards. The kids loved swimming in the pool and the proximity to the park and kid friendly attractions in NYC was a boon. The staff was not as attentive, or friendly as they were during our previous stay and at times seemed downright out of it. When we went down to pay for the sitter we had booked well in advance through the concierge desk, as instructed, we were told there was no sitter booked and that we couldn't put the charges to our room as we'd been told previously. After much confusion and back and forth between the concierge and the reception the whole thing was sorted out and we did indeed get our babysitter and the method of payment was accepted. Only exception would be the bellman, who especially made the kids feel welcome from the moment we arrived. We were hoping to eat at the burger joint but the lines were too long. We will return to the Parker again, we hope it'll be less busy (we were there during the Tennis Grand Slam) and we'll have better service.

title: “Clean, tidy and good value”
text: We stayed the day of our arrival in Denver and the night before our departure. They have an airport shuttle that works really well. It was a very clean room and hotel, enough area for all our bags and a comfortable bed. This is an extremely great value. It's located in a newer developed area with lots of other hotels and a few restaurants, there's a Ruby Tuesdays within walking distance.

title: “A Tourist's Best Pick”
text: Hey, all these good reviews can't be wrong. The Bostonian really is the best location for tourists visiting Boston. I've stayed at the Prudential Center, too, and like this spot better. Good access to the T, easy walking to the National Parks Visitors Center, North End restaurants very close, and that Quincy Marketplace right across the street for eats and shopping -- it's all right here.

title: “Best Customer Service Ever!”
text:
I spent a weekend at the Westin Hotel on Beale Street and I had the most courteous, attentive staff I have ever met! Before I arrived a friend wanted to surprise me with flowers and wine - the concierge "became his best friend" to put it in his words! I arrived early, my room was ready and waiting; the staff was very proactive - kniew what I needed before I did!
I will defiinitely stay there again!

title: “One of the Great NYC Hotels”
text: Great staff. Excellent location. Phenomenal room service. WOODY ALLEN WAS PERFORMING JAZZ IN THE LOUNGE!! One of the coolest experiences On my life.

title: “I Loved it!”
text: This hotel is like nothing I've stayed at before. Be sure to get the cool corner room for $70 more. Much more space than the regular rooms. Well worth it. Oh yeah, be sure not to get the minibar, they slap on a bar charge that's as much as the room. I live in San Diego and staying here was like a vacation away from home. Would I stay here again? Most definately! Don't forget to grab your CD on your way out.

title: “Delivered as promised”
text: Enjoyed our stay. The positive reviews on Trip Advisor were accurate and helpful. The hotel is well-appointed (albeit the rooms are small) and the staff are friendly and helpful. Only criticisms (and they are minor) are 1. no room service after 11:00 pm and 2. door staff recommended we catch a cab on Fashion Ave. rather than hailing one for us. Overall, would definitely recommend the hotel.

title: “One of my new favorite hotels”
text: I stayed at the Admiral's Fell Inn for a week and the service was amazing. Dorian, one of the employees at the front desk provided extraordinary customer service and great dinner recommendations. This hotel believes in customer service and ensuring you truly enjoy the fell's point area. I cannot wait to travel back to Baltimore and stay at Admiral Fell's Inn and hear the wonderful ghost stories.

title: “What a lovely find for a place to stay!”
text:
What a wonderful hotel right near to Times Square.
It has the most friendly staff I think I have ever come across who couldn't do enough to make sure that my stay was pleasant.
The pool with 'swim up bar' was awesome and good fun although I would say they could do with turning up the temperature on the water as sitting around tends to be more chilly - not a moan though but a suggestion instead.
The room, although small, was lovely and had everything I needed for a pleasant night.
Best of all, whilst there is no restaurant on site, there are plenty of local take out places and you can eat them in the hotel without any complaints and in comfort. Much better than being stuffed up in your room!
Finally, the breakfast was excellent although rather busy. Plenty of bits to choose from and fruit to take away.
All in all an excellent experience and certainly a place to try out.

title: “Never Again”
text: Ugh!stay away from "The Landing".In & Out was better.Truly horrible service and food.Needs a lot of work.

title: “We thought the Felix was great”
text: Everyone there was extremely nice and helpful. Yes the rooms were a bit small but I wasn't going to live there.The best thing is how clean everything is.We would stay again and also recommend The Felix to anyone staying dowtown.

title: “Great Place”
text: Me, my wife and 2 kids stayed here from 8/31 - 9/2 to attend a beautiful wedding. The only bad thing I have to say about this hotel is that our room smelled like it was a prior smoking room. I didn't complain as the smell wasn't overpowering but was noticeable when you entered the room. Otherwise I would have given The Fairmont a 5. The service was excellent, the food was exceptional, the valet was very prompt and the gym was great for a hotel. The pool isn't too big but the kids did enjoying swimming for a few hours.

title: “decent place in the heart of the city”
text:
