We found a good deal on this place for MLK weekend, probably because their employees are conducting a strike/protest and therefore waking guests up early with their megaphones and literally shaming them as they walk in the hotel. I actually really do want to be supportive of their employees who are dissatisfied with the new management's failure to recognize the hotel workers labor union, but their approach didn't make me feel real supportive. 
Anyway, we had a King Executive Suite, quite a large room for this area. The room was clean, the bathroom was nice, and bed was comfy... can't ask for much more. The location is good; even if you don't want to spend a ton of time in Union Square, it's a central location for exploring the other areas of the city. 
It's nothing crazy fancy and you won't be treated like royalty or anything, but I'm a picky traveler and it worked for me.

title: “Still a good central location”
text: Marriott Courtyard Times Sq is better than the last visit (2006??). The check-in is the usual chaos because it is too small. The hotel has no bar or restaurant but that is not a problem at this location. The bedrooms are large for NYC with comfortable beds. The concierge is excellent.

title: “Great staff great place”
text: I really enjoyed the hotel the staff was amazing Going on a Wednesday is the best time the managers repctipn was amazing free food and drinks and thu give you a chance to win free points which I did !!

title: “Rates are cheap, but may not honor reservations in the busy season!”
text: I am writing this past midnight. I made a reservation a week ago. However, i arrived a few hours ago to be told they didn't have a room and would i be ok if they called around and tried to find me a room elsewhere. They discover all they have are smoking rooms, so they send me to one without telling me (my reservation, they agreed, was for a non-smoking room), hoping perhaps that if you get travelers late enough in the evening maybe they'll just accept it. I say No way! Can I speak to the manager? He's not here and he's not answering his calls. Can you try him tomorrow? And so on. And its gets even better -- if you cancel a reservation the day of, apparently they dock you for a day's charge ("as we held the room for you!"), so you can't bail on them, but they can bail on you! And they offered me $10 as cab fare to an alternate hotel. These guys are something else. The rates are cheap, but I guess this is the lesson -- it's a shoestring operation, so they can't actually track rooms against reservations made, so it is hit or miss in the busy season and quite "informal".

title: “Fall visit to New York City”
text: We stayed in this elegant hotel for 4 nights, and enjoyed the stay very much. The hotel is in Nomad, near Midtown and there are subway lines within easy walking distance. Madison Square Park is only a few blocks away, as is the Flat Iron Building- a good landmark. The Empire State Building is just above the hotel- another easy landmark. The lobby is very elegant at sub-street level and there is an attractive bar right off the lobby. A 24 hour business center is right off the lobby as well. My husband used the workout room, which he said was adequate, although I did not see it. The restaurant has a French bistro style which overlooks the lobby. We had breakfast in the hotel each morning. A buffet was available only for special Marriott members, although some room rates may have included breakfast. Our rate did not. There are coffee shops in easy walking distance if you prefer not to have breakfast at the hotel. The staff was very nice and welcoming and arranged for a hotel car to take us to the airport at about the same fee as a taxi ride. Our superior room had an elegant modern feel, and while small, was adequate for NYC. The bathroom was quite small. Our room had no view as we looked into other windows and looked down on rooftops, but we were not in the room too much, so that was not a problem. The A/C kept the room very cool. We will definitely stay here again if we want to stay in this area of Manhattan.

title: “Good value”
text: The other reviews are right on. The location is pretty good, especially for the price, although not right in Times Square. The high floors can be noisy from the club, but not bad for the city. We stayed in rooms on both sides and both high floor views are good. Rooms are nicely decorated and feel new but they are tiny. My only complaint was that my (platinum member) boyfriend asked for a late checkout Sunday afternoon and was told that the hotel was sold out and so it was impossible. Later that afternoon when our flight was cancelled, we called to see if we could have a room for that night and, guess what, rooms were available. We stayed there anyhow, despite the lie, and we'd probably go back.

title: “Great long weekend vacation stay - would recommend!”
text:
Pros: great location, excellent value for NYC, friendly staff, overall nice property, well maintained, clean, and quiet - we didn't hear any neighbors.
Cons: not anything significant. Bed is fairly hard...could be upgraded, and need at least one accessible outlet that isn't in the bathroom.
Overall great room, we would go back for sure.

title: “Love the location...perfect!!”
text:
We stayed at the Omni when in town visiting family and to do some sight seeing. The lobby is just beautiful and the scent that is in the air is amazing! The room left a bit to be desired with several small but noticable issues. The water pressure was so high that when you washed your hands, your shirt and the entire countertop got pretty wet. Room definately needs to be updated. 
The location though is the best part. You are in the middle of the historic district and can walk to so many attractions. The choice of restaurants is amazing all within a few blocks and there is a little market right around the corner on 4th between Chestnut and Market where you can get hoagies, tastycakes, fresh fruit and soft pretzels..yummy!
Parking is scarce and the choices at the hotel are self park or valet. Valet is steep at $35 a night and self parking is $10 less but then you don't get in and outs free. 
The front desk staff is very friendly and I will most likely stay here on my next trip back to Philly!

title: “It may be on Union Square, but pass it up!”
text: We stayed here for 5 nights during a professional meeting, and we have stayed here in the past. This recent visit was a real disappointment. This hotel is on the skids and doesn't deserve past deluxe status if once had. We stayed in the Tower. There is are essentially undecoration--I have seen better in motel chains. The halls were actually cold. Our room, 1682, was reasonably large, but the tub leaked badly and the stopper was inoperative so you could not take a bath. We found the maid service erratic from day to day. One associate said that her marble shower wall (in the old wing) had a thick layer of dirt indicating that it had not been cleaned for some time. She complained to the manager. And another friend said that the shower water was only luke warm, never hot. A third associate had no lights, and they still were not working when they returned from dinner. The elevators to the Tower are a disaster. They have six elevators to the tower of which only three operate from the ground floor (according to a manager) so the lines for elevators are long, especially on the weekends. Others in our group were stuck in the elevator--it just didn't move until a higher floor was pressed, and in a number of cases the elevator just didn't stop at the requested floor. All of these issues indicate that there are real maintenance problems at the the St. Francis, and we can not recommend this hotel. It has a established name at a prime location, but given our recent experience it has serious service issues. This is not the deluxe hotel it would like to portray. There are other hotels in the immediate area, such as the Grand Hyatt or Fairmont San Francisco, where we have also stayed, and with no complaints. We recommend trying one of those first. Forget location and go with service.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: We really enjoyed the hotel. tt was small enough to get some great service. The location was close to North Beach, which was close to the things that we wanted to do. We would stay here again!

title: “Outstanding in every way!”
text: We just returned from 2 nights at the Surrey Hotel in NYC. We chose it based on Trip Advisor reviews and it was Perfect from beginning to end.When booking ,we checked a preference for room on a higher floor ,and that we were celebrating an anniversary.Every staff member we encountered was friendly and helpful,especially the front desk.!We were upgraded to a suite because there was no upper level room availability.It was the most beautiful space with sumptious bath,and a very very comfortable bed.Attention to detail is neverending and we enjoyed our stay immensely.A chilled bottle of champagne was sent to our room in honor of our anniversary. I could go on and on but just will say that it is the best place...its convienient to Museum Mile,Central Park fine restaurants and shopping.Cafe Boulard on the premise is a fine dining experience, and the Rooftop Garden puts the Surrey as a number 1 NYC getaway.

title: “I'm being generous with 1 Star!”
text:
I will say first and foremost I did not book this hotel a friend did. I probably would of done a little more research before booking. 
Upon arrival we were told our room wasn't ready but we could wait in the lobby as it wouldn't be long. We were not upset because we were there about 20 minutes before the scheduled check in time. While sitting in the lobby we first noticed the lack of upkeep on the property and how everything looked quite outdated. While patiently waiting we noticed the clientele coming and going and if you told me they rented rooms by the hour I would not be surprised. 
After checking in and waiting forever for the very slow moving elevator we went to our room. What a joke. The bedspreads were from the 1980's and probably not washed since first put on the bed 3 decades ago. The walls were nasty dirty and could of used a good hard scrub. The carpet was gross and we all made a pact not to walk barefoot across the floor as we weren't too sure what kind of bugs and or parasites were possibly living within the nasty stained floor. The bathroom was dirty and the towels seemed cleaned but were probably bought the same time the bedspread was and were worn quite thin. I felt like I was in Mexico and was afraid to use the water to brush my teeth. The best part of our room was the puke on the back of our door. Yep nasty puke all over the back of the door! 
I will say the only thing that was half way decent was the front desk staff and that was probably because they probably felt bad for you.
They also advertise that they are close to the sports complexes but are not! Cabs are very hard to come by and we had to call a couple of cab companies to finally secure a ride. The only thing positive I can say about the location is that there is a great dinner right across the street.
DON'T STAY HERE if you value your life. Pay the extra money and save your health!

title: “What a bargain!”
text: I visit Chicago frequently and, being on a budget, I try to find good hotels that are reasonably priced. They are not easy to find. My sister stayed at the Essex last year and recommended it to me. I finally found what I was looking for! This hotel has a great location on Michigan Avenue, clean , comfortable rooms, a fabulous indoor swimming pool and an excellent exercise room. The staff was friendly and very helpful, and there are many good restaurants, bars and clubs in the area. I really liked the free shuttle they have that takes you to Navy Pier and the North Michigan Avenue shopping district. The room rates were very, very reasonable compared to other hotels. The Essex is an incredible bargain. I am recommending it to all my friends, particularly those with families.

title: “The place to come back to!”
text:
We recently stayed at the Conrad with some friends
Rooms were spotless and quiet. Beds were very comfortable. Plasma TVs were a great touch. Prime location!
Even with the huge crowd in town, I felt the staff were very pleasant, helpful and accomodating. Any of our needs were addressed immediately.
We didn't use the exercise facilities but will definitely do so next year when we return. Likewise for the restaurants.
Would whole heartedly recommend to anyone who likes to spoil themselves.!!!

title: “So comfortable and accomodating in a lovely part of NY!”
text: We enjoyed a lovely weekend at the Hotel Giraffe. It's convenient to many nice places to eat, the room was very comfortable, the staff so accomodating and the amenities in the lobby and the terrace were wonderful. We will definitely return.

title: “price VS quality very good”
text:
I stayed here for 3 nights and it was a good choice.
The hotel is situated right next to the Interstate so when beeing outside it was very noisy but beeing inside the room it didn't bother me. They also have a nice pool but I didn't use it. Your car can be parked underneath the rooms so it stays cool when it's very hot in Austin sometimes. Room was clean, smelled fresh, wifi worked fine and felt safe. Good location, right in the middle of downtown Austin and the north with all the shopping malls.
No breakfast in the morning but they had coffee and some fruit to take. So if you're looking for a good price, good location and a clean basic place to sleep this is the one !

title: “Awesome best hotel around”
text:
I'll be the first to admit. I'm a bit of a freak when it comes to hotels on cleaning. This place is awesome get room 812. It was better than the suite I got in Hawaii Hilton on wiki beach rainbow tower. 
The corner room with wrap around balcony is awesome vie of state buildings & capital. Prime spot. Away from the drunks. Perfect data research person nailed it here!
Just can't get over the nice art everywhere & afordable! 
Get room 812

title: “Great city experience”
text:
My husband and I stayed over Thanksgiving and chose this hotel in order to be centrally located. What a great spot! The staff was efficient and polite. Our room was small, as most are in NY, but with a fabulous view of the Empire State Building. Very romantic and very New York. The room was stocked with everything you would need. There was a great bar/lounge on the roof with sweeping views and balconies. The subways were located a block away and tons of restaurants and bars in walking distance.
I have stayed at the Weston and the W, this is equally as nice and a better location. I loved the fashion flair and boutique personality. If you want a hip, comfortable environment this is it.

title: “Sufficient but not stellar”
text:
The room was much more well-maintained that I expected, but as a woman traveling alone, the outside entrance to the room was very off-putting. 
I checked in late at night and was told that my room was on the back of the building...the dark, deserted back of the building. Needless to say, I was fairly uncomfortable with the situation and hardly slept and all, and I'm not typically scared to be alone. 
I would have appreciated some sort of escort, or an offer to be in a less isolated room. 
But the room was clean and well-appointed.

title: “Felt like home”
text: location was a little far, but the place is exrtremely nice and quite, very difficult to find a cab from the place although, the breakfast felt like eating at home, cozy place, but the hotel has no restaurant (neighbouring one has although)

title: “Excellent Location and Wonderful Staff”
text: My room was clean, comfortable, and quiet. The room is very similar to those at the Hotel Indigo but in my opinion, the location is better. My king room was large but it was more than adequate for my long weekend. The comfort control system and the wireless internet were great. The staff really did a great job. When I got to the airport, I realized that I had removed everything from the hotel safe except my house/car keys. I called the hotel and they took care of everything. While I was writing this, the keys arrived. Great service. My wife and I have booked another trip to this location during the Christmas Season. It is within a few blocks of 2 great subway stops (Penn Station and Herald Square). Korea Town is just up the block with many unique dining options.

title: “Elegant Hotel for price”
text:
We stayed 2 night at this Hilton which is across the street from legends where we went to see buddy guy,
Its a elegant hotel which was used in the movie the fugitive and the building in ww11 was used for the Army before it had been a Hotel,
Nice staff, clean rooms the beds and were very comfortable, just wished they had bottled water in rooms !

title: “Bad Advertising: The King George is not a Boutique Hotel”
text: The King George is a very European hotel - nice bar and small lobby. The rooms, however, vary in size - and the one we had for the first two days of our stay was so tiny that my husband and I couldn't turn around at the same time and the bathroom mirror was divided at the room side so that one could only see a couple of inches in front of one! (Made it hard to put on makeup:)We were moved for the last two nights (they claimed they were full and could not move us earlier) to a slightly larger room. Nice, international group of people both staying and working at the King George - but I've stayed at better small "boutique" hotels in the Union Square area than this.

title: “Great hotel, unbelievable service.”
text:
Whoever hired the staff at this hotel should get a raise. It wasn't just that everyone went out of their way to be helpful, friendly and fun, though they did. The best thing is that they were also thoughtful. 
We had been booked at another hotel in Times Square but when an ad came for the Eventi I asked my colleagues if they wanted to try it. I was a little nervous going to a brand new hotel, especially since I had suggested it. I needn’t have worried. Every one of my colleagues has thanked me for finding such a great spot. 
The rooms were lovely, the hotel itself had the usual Kimpton funky vibe. They had a great patio on the 5th floor (I can't imagine why they didn't put the restaurant there). Only a couple of complaints about the place: 1. they need more practice in the restaurant, and they were a little obsequious. Yes, I can push my own elevator button! 2. The air system in the room was loud. I had to turn it off to sleep and then it was too hot. 3. Some of my co-workers' keys kept having to be reset. 
But please don't let any of these little negatives scare you off. The bed was comfy, the atmosphere was elegant, comfortable and funky all at the same time, and we were very, very well taken care of, from receiving large packages before getting there to having any little need taken care of when we were there. But the best part was just the attitude of the staff. Highly recommended.

title: “Very clean and nice”
text: We had a wonderful stay here. We took our daughter, but would've been able to enjoy the spa without her. Not so child friendly, there is no pool but for a couple or adult, it's got it all. Breakfast was really good as well. Will go back.

title: “A pleasant surprise”
text:
I had to have an emergency medical outpatient procedure performed early in the morning and wanted to stay in a hotel near New York Hospital the night before the procedure. All the good hotels nearby were booked. I found 254 East Vacation on hotel .com. The price for Manhattan was very cheap and I expected to be sleeping in a flea bag hotel. I was pleasantly surprised at the old but very clean apartment with a backyard garden, kitchenette, comfortable bed , 2 TV's and quiet sleeping conditions. I felt like I was sleeping in my grandmother's house in the 1940s.
Don't expect luxurious furniture, plush towels, a concierge or even a check in desk. But Danny met me outside carried in the luggage and upgraded my room at no additional charge when I told him I preferred not to have to walk upstairs. He was most pleasant and helpful.
The hot water pressure was very good. There were adequate towels, a good hair blow dryer and a short walk to the hospital. The neighborhood is a lovely safe area with restaurants and perfect for a family or couple. You can't beat the price.

title: “Classy, Convenient, Comfortable”
text:
I stayed here for three days with clients. The service and location were great - the restaurant was excellent but a bit pricey - across the street from a fabulous mall - other shops and restaurants (the Ivy, etc) within walking distance - only complaint is having to pay for internet! The staff went above and beyond to accomodate my requests for a last minute group meeting. (The restaurant has a private room in the back that can accomodate about 12 people)
The room layout was one of my favorites - very comfortable bed, large desk, flat screen tv, big sink with plenty of counter space, huge walk in shower with a window so you can see the tv (and hear the audio) while showering under a fabulous large rain showerhead with great water pressure. Also had a large walk in closet with many hangers.

title: “Great room and convenient.”
text: Good sized King room for NYC. Rooms on each floor that end in 01 are end rooms and much larger. No views in these rooms. Great 2 night visit, couldn't be happier.

title: “Very Nice!”
text: We had a wonderful stay at the Omni. Our suite was well arranged, clean and attractive. We took advantage of the hang tag for room service delivery of breakfast every morning, which was very nice and reasonably priced. The location was perfect, right in the heart of downtown. The staff was friendly and helpful. The only down side was the price. But since this trip was an anniversary celebration, we felt like the Omni was a great choice!

title: “Very modern Hotel”
text: We were looking to stay in new york with our family. This hotel is only 1 year old and very very modern. We were a little worried about bringing kids, but everything went well. The pool is very cool, on the roof overlooking the city. We walked to all of the local area places with ease. Would suggest this one if you are staying in NYC.

title: “Thought this Hotel was great!”
text:
Recently had a 3 Night stay at this Hotel. Enjoyed every minute. Conveniently located to the Universal City Board-Walk- With a free Shuttle- Bus (Place to go on an evening & really safe!).
Room good, Food good & service good... No complaints at all.

title: “Great hotel close to Hollywood Blvd”
text:
Great hotel,friendly helpful staff.
Organized a shuttle to Disneyland for us.
Nice sized rooms and free internet.
Breakfast was a bit average but it was free so I ate it anyway and the coffee was lousy but good coffee was hard to find the entire trip so it wasn't exclusive to this hotel

title: “Nightmare Hotel”
text:
The directions to the hotel were wrong. When we did arrive there the hotel looked nice. We were on the 5th floor. The hallway stunk like mildew. We got to our room which looked nice at first. There was a hole in our wall, and the down filled matress cover, (which will doubles as your only comforter/blanket,) had body fluid stains all over. I can not express how badly it needed cleaned, and obviously, it isn't cleaned often. The seriously dissappointing part was for two mornings in a row we were not able to shower. On the first morning, my birthday, the front desk informed us they were experiencing boiler issues . They told us we would have to wait at least 2 hours for hot water. We made the best of the circumstances and went to the Sears tower unbathed. The hot water worked that afternoon. The next morning we had no hot water again. At that time, we were told to wait a half an hour until the water heated up. We did, and still had no hot water. We got tired of waiting and left for home with no shower again. If you expect no morning shower or appoligies from the front desk, go to Hotel Blake. If not, choose somewhere else!! We never recieved any compensation for the hassel, not even the phone call we were promised from the "boss" who handles complaints. Convieniently, that "boss" doesn't work weekends, so all weekend complaints are not dealt with until Monday.
As for the restaurant, we spent $40.00 on two cheese omelets, two cups of coffee, and two orders of whole wheat toast. Very fancy, and not so very good. Not reccommending the breakfast.

title: “NICE ROOMS”
text:
POSITIVES: Rooms were huge we were in a king size non smoking up stairs the room was very clean it came with a fridge and couch the bath tub had jets and there was a desk and free WiFi! Breakfast was decent your typical cereal and waffles... Our bath tub didn't drain so well so when we asked to get it fixed it was fixed the same day and working great housekeeping came each and everyday and we didn't even ask they made our bed and stocked our towels and vacuumed or floors great house keeping staff!!!!
NEGATIVE: Front desk staff not so helpful.... while he was helping me front desk staff was talking on his cell phone and upon check out no one was at the front desk I rang the bell serial times and no one came to the front desk so no recite :(
But for the most part very good hotel!!!!

title: “Enjoyed it so much I am going back in two weeks”
text: All I want to say is after having spent five wonderfuly days at the NYP hotel last year I am going back in two weeks time fo celebrate my birthday with friends. Its certainly worth having a deluxe room with views over St. Patricks cathedral I found the staff extremely helpful and personally thoughts the security there was excellent. We go every year if I could.

title: “OK rooms, staff was rude”
text: Stayed here the last week of July. The rooms were OK and the executive lounge has an OK but not great continental breakfast. The hotel has installed thermostat controls, meaning that the rooms don't get very cool. I had a couple of opportunities to speak with the front desk staff and they were not helpful, to the point of being rude. I would not recommend this hotel.

title: “Location and Value”
text: We were attending a convention at the Cobo Centre, about a 10-minute walk away. Our room was on the 21st floor and was probably the largest hotel room, short of a suite, that we have ever stayed in. The bathroom was also very spacious, though, oddly, there was no towel rack except for 1 in the tub enclosure. The service was fine and it seemed that a supervisor checked up on how well the room was cleaned every day - we stayed there for 5 nights. This was our first time in Detroit and we felt comfortable in this area, though we did notice a lot of security people everywhere, even in outdoor parks. My wife preferred not walk around during the day when she was on her own and chose instead to drive to nearby towns to shop. At night, security was clearly on the job with exterior doors locked and a guard at the elevator to check that you had a key. The People Mover is easily reached from the hotel and is very convenient for getting around. Friends stayed across the street in the BIG Marriott and were not happy, mostly because of the confusing layout. The restaurant breakfast was great,and not unreasonably priced but in the evening, there were too few servers for the crowd so things did not go smoothly.

title: “Flawless!”
text: Stayed there for 3 nights last month and will never contemplate staying elsewhere again in New York. Everything was top notch, from the super-friendly staff to the impeccable room. Location is great - quiet in the evening but busy during the day, and a short walk to the nearest subway station. Highly recommended!

title: “Very Clean!”
text: Stayed there with my husband! Interior coridors, great continental breakfast and clean room. It's all I want from hotel and I found it in this hotel. You cant beat it for the price.

title: “Terrible rooms, dangerous area, rip-off”
text:
Pros: Nice lobby, quick elevator, good shower pressure and warm water
Cons: It is very telling that there are more photos of san fran sites than of the hotel. The room we got (two double) was incredibly small, with the beds almost touching each other and spanning from wall to wall. There was one thin window (more like a slit) which was mostly blocked by the shade of the building itself. Everything in the hotel looked like it was from the 1950s, and hadn't been updated in as long. The floors creaked. The complimentary toiletries were a small pouch of shampoo and conditioner so that once you open it, it can't really be used again. Housekeeping almost broke our door down to clean the room the morning ON THE DAY WE WERE CHECKING OUT, whereas every other hotel in the world crosschecks so as to not needlessly clean a room that will be vacated in a couple hours. The staff downstairs was terrible, unhelpful and often rude with snarky comments about how we're lucky to even have a room at all, even though we had had a reservation. The hotel isn't really close to anything and is a good 15-20 minute walk to the nearest train station (civic center). The diner right by is ridiculously overpriced and fantastically slow. There are two waitresses for the whole place, and they have cashier duties too. It takes forever to order, receive, and pay for even a simple meal. The area is not nice, lots of homeless people and beggars, especially at night. STAY FAR FAR AWAY!!

title: “Ideal low-cost hotel”
text:
Friendly staff, safe neighbourhood, quiet area, nice restaurant, near to clubs and bars, small rooms but CHEAP and CLEAN!
Perfect if you prefer to be out exploring rather than in your hotel room :)
Shared bathrooms were no problem, never had to wait for a shower or toilet.
Room comes with towels, small dressing gown, a safe, TV, and storage space.
Will definitely stay here every time I come back to NYC :)
Only down point is thin walls so you can hear more than you would probably like.. unless you're into voyeurism or something then it would be perfect.

title: “It was perfect in every way!”
text: My husband and I and our two friends stayed at the Talbott Hotel in Chicago to celebrate a special birthday!! None of us had been to Chicago before so we really didn't have a clue what part of the city would be best to stay in etc. Luckily someone from my office recommended this one to us and we are so glad. The hotel is in the nicest part of town. It is cozy, quaint and charming. The staff is exceptional. The concierge Jean Murray was right-on, when it came to sending us to restaurants and to a really cool blues club. Everything about our stay was perfect and we would go back to this hotel again when we re-visit Chicago.

title: “Nice property, great location”
text:
stayed here one night while waiting to board a cruise to Alaska. the hotel staff was very friendly, and the shuttle to seatac was easy to obtain.
The Hotel is surrounded by a large number of eateries, and the Southcenter Mall, all within a few minutes walk.
The room was clean and spacious.
The only down side was that the hotel was hosting a large number of teens that were attending a sporting event, and they were very loud and disrupting into the later hours of the night. The rooms face inward toward an open attrium that seems to allow voices and other sounds to travel and echo. Not the best set up.

title: “Excellent value - great location”
text: We have just arrived back from a great weekend at the Washington Court Hotel where we stayed for 2 nights on a Groupon deal. I was a little nervous on arrival as i'm never quite sure what to expect on a cheap deal (and it was cheap, $89 per night for a room for 2 adults and 3 kids) but I was extremely pleased regarding all aspects of the hotel. On checking in we were told that we'd been upgraded to a King Room and it was huge! There was a desk/work area, a table and four chairs, a large bed settee and a huge bed! This is one of the few hotels that i've stayed in where, even with the bed settee made up and the roll-away bed up for the kids, there was still plenty of space to move around. The bathroom was spotlessly clean and the bed linen was great. My only complaint would be that the pillows were a little firm, for my taste, but the housekeeping staff changed them as soon as we asked. We didn't have breakfast in the hotel, but did eat dinner in the bar area on the night we arrived. The menu was very good and the staff were really helpful and offered to make the kids any kind of pizza that they wanted, as the choices on the menu were a little grown up for my smallest. The food and service was excellent. The hotel is located a 5 minute walk from Union Station and from there we were able to catch the hop-on hop-off trolley bus tour, which was a great way to get around. I really couldn't recommend this hotel enough.

title: “Perfect stay and great staff!”
text: I stayed for 4 nights at this lovely hotel. Stayed at the hotel with my starwood miles I had accumulated. Drove in from the airport and it was very easy to find, located a few minutes from Union Square. I am glad I booked this hotel and not the Union Square Westin as this hotel was much newer and sophisticated. Originally my car was parked in the basement hotel parking but I discovered a cheaper parking garage just opposite the hotel. In my original email to the hotel I asked for a king size room on a high floor and away from the lifts. This had been granted on check in and I was very happy. Check in was smooth, quick and efficient. And the staff were lovely throughout my stay. I was very happy with the staff right across the board, from the valet staff to the housekeeping. The concierge were very helpful throughout my stay and gave me tips and suggestions on restaurants, road routes and general tourist things to do in San Fran. They made bookings for me on all accounts and their recommendations were always spot on. My room was clean and spacious with lovely amenities one always receives in Westin hotels. My stay in this hotel was just superb and I would recommend it to anyone and everyone!

title: “Location....Location....Location”
text: Definately a place to stay if looking to be near the hot spots. This hotel is conveniently located near 16th Street and a nice walk to the Coors Field. The hotel was very clean and modern. The only drawback is the parking. I hate paying to park my car. However, you are in downtown so it is to be expected. We took advantage and parked across the street for a reasonable rate. Not much to comment on the breakfast....your average donuts, muffin, cereal, etc. They do serve a "hot" breakfast which when we were there was an egg omelet but it didn't taste all that great. Looked and tasted like it was cooked somewhere else and put in the microwave to warm up. So, we decided to eat out the remainder of our stay.

title: “Nice people, Horrible hotel”
text: The first night i got there i was suprised at how small our room was; there was hardly room to move in the room. The sheets had stains on them, and the bed was suppose to be for two but barely fit one. The staff was nice enough to "upgrade" us to a bigger room. this room was definetly nicer, and presented us with more room. The only problem was the mattresses were as hard as a board. Sleeping was practically impossible. The next time i stay in new york i will look for a little longer and probably choose a chain hotel, so i know it has creditiblity.

title: “We will never go back to Sportsmen's lodge Hotel and never recommend it!”
text:
We arrived at the hotel an hour early to maybe enjoy the pool like we do when we go away. There is nothing like being on vacation and sitting by the pool with a nice cold drink. We were looking forward to relaxing for the weekend. Unfortunately, that was not the case at the Sportsmen's Lodge. We were never informed that the pool was a public pool! It was hard to find a chair to sit in and the pool was crowded, nothing relaxing about that. The service was awful, the waitress was not only slow but couldn't understand our food or drink order. It took her 20 minutes to understand what we wanted then another 10 minutes to put it in the computer only to put it in wrong and another 20 minutes to fix the problem. Not only could she not back -up the bartender, there was only one bartender who was great but constantly leaving the bar to deliver food to the pool area. We waited two hours for our food then another hour for our check. When we went up just for drinks we waited an hour so we would each order two drinks only to have them get hot in the sun otherwise it would be another two hours before we got another one! That was only Saturday! 
 On Sunday morning we decided we would eat in the cafe, food was ok but again 2 hours to get food and there were only two other tables in our area. We started our day early, by 10am the pool was filled with what we named "the bracelet people" again no place to sit and no towels. We were there for a wedding so we all together had about 15 rooms. We were also told the hotel was sold out, so why would you have public swimming at your pool when your hotel is sold out and no where for your paying guests to relax or swim. We had one table and two lounge chairs between 20 of us because there was no other place to sit, we had to alternate who sat and who stood. We even had a person come sit in the middle of our group! I had two rooms in the hotel and that is not what I paid for! In all my years of traveling (34 yrs) I have never seen anything like this! 
On Monday morning we checkout early and ate breakfast elsewhere.
 Your hotel is poorly managed! I would have put a sign up a month before that the pool would not be open to the public that weekend because the hotel was full. I think if it was not for the convenience of the banquet hall next door you would not have the amount of guests staying in your hotel. I know that when I come out again and it is for a wedding there, I will not stay at your hotel. I will drive the extra time it takes to stay elsewhere. 
When we checked out we were asked how was the wedding, we said "great". And then we were asked how was our stay and we said "Not so great", we were never asked why it was not great and what was wrong with our stay. Again poor management!
I did learn one thing and that is from now on I have to ask a hotel if they have public swimming so that I do not book there.
I hope you can now understand why we will not be staying there the next time we are in town

title: “Personalized Care”
text: My experience at the Triton, since I started staying there in the late '90's, is that they really care about making your experience, fun, pleasant and comfortable. Once when I was with girlfriends in a party mood, the bellman jumped in a cab with us and delivered us tourists to the Tonga Room in the basement of the Farimont. It was hilarious and unforgettable. Most recently, when my brother was able to break away for an evening from his home in Mountain View to join me in the city, the staff made accommodations for him last-minute. Really great follow-up from the staff, too. And location can't be beat.

title: “Hospitable Staff...Great Hotel & Location”
text: This was my 4th stay at the Phoenix Park Hotel. I have an annual business trip in December at a nearby hotel. The value vs. amenities are excellent. The location to Union Station, and other DC attractions is superb. If you are a walker, many sites are in walking distance. On my recent trip I needed my check in time adjusted by several hours. The front desk was very accommodating, and allowed me to check in early. I then loss my cell phone for several hours in a taxi. Local calls are $1/call, but once again a front desk staffer let me use their personal cell phone to make several calls. If you're wondering where good customer service went, well I found it at the Phoenix Park Hotel.

title: “Great Location”
text: The best thing Mariott's Rivercenter has going for it is its location, right in RiverCenter Mall and adjacent to the River Walk. You can catch the river taxi and cruise right there; there are some excellent restaurants in the mall, and you are within walking distance of The Alamo, San Fernando Cathedral, and the Spanish Governor's Palace. Standard Marriott hotel and amenities, although the hotel restaurant was diappointing for anything other than breakfast. Very limited menu. Then, again, who needs a hotel restaurant, when all of the great River Walk restaurants are a short stroll away.

title: “Appalling and Unethical Billing”
text: I recently took a weekend trip to Chicago with a couple of my girlfriends from grad school. Loved the city, other than the wind. Absolutely disgusted with the Hilton Suites we stayed in. A couple of weeks after returning home, I happened to check my credit card balance to find a extra $100 charge from the hotel. Assuming it was some kind of mistake, I called to let the hotel know. They proceded to tell me that they did not know what the charge was at that time, but that they would call me back. I gave my phone number, email and name. They proceeded to call one of the other girls who stayed in the room and to tell her the charge was for "trashing" the room! I can assure you, we left the room in perfect condition with all of our "trash" by the door. We barely spent any time in the room as it is. The manager told me they had a report and pictures of the damage to the room, but when I requested they send copies to me with an explanation of the $100 charge, he insisted he was not allowed to do that. Can you imagine, it is their word against mine, and they don't have to provide any type of receipt or evidence, but can charge me this ridiculous charge! Something in this scenario does not add up. I'm disputing the charge through my credit card company, but feel this is completely unbelievable, not to mention unethical. I am over the $100, but not the principle. I will never stay in a Hilton, and am passing this information on to spare others this experience.

title: “Great Location + Great Hotl= Great time in NYC”
text: Just stayed at the Solita Soho and loved it. The location could not have been better for us right in Little Italy and walking distance to China town, Greenwich Village. The only complaint that I would have is that the rooms were small like other reviews said, it was tight for all four of us to fit but it worked just fine. Are room was on the 11th floor and we could not hear the nightclub that is right next door(which I was worried we would hear). Other then that the place was awesome definitely worth checking out next time your in NYC, and if you do stay here check out Petit Abeille for breakfast on 134 west broadway only a 14 minute walk from the hotel.

title: “On the River”
text: Very nice hotel, very comfortable beds, river view rooms, close to Magnificient Mile, short walk to Navy Pier. Friendly staff. Walk out to River Walk. Hop on/off bus has a stop at this location. I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Charge for everything”
text: Grounds are 4 star, rooms are 2.5 star. Bathrooms are in serious need of an upgrade, You can hear the TV next door plain as day. The only thing included is the Pool, everything else is extra. Fitness center $12, Parking $25 per day, Internet $10, Mini golf $10 per person, bike rental $10 per hour, you get the picture. They have mastered the art of extracting money. On the upside the grounds are wonderful and the location is excellent,

title: “Great Location, friendly staff, spacious room.”
text:
We normally stay in the Manhattan area whenever we are in New York. We have stayed in the Old Drake Hotel years ago because of the location. The Omni is also very well located, near most any place one might want to be. Theaters, museums, eating places, shops and more shops!
The doormen were funny! Warm smile to greet you every morning. The concierge was helpful. I needed my luggage mini lock opened, and engineering was dispatched to solve my problem, pronto! We were booked in a nice, suite at the top floor. Coffee and juice arrived at the time requested. I need my coffee first thing in the morning, and that was a good amenity.
Will I be staying with Omni Hotel anytime soon! Yes, we are still here in Bershire, but by Monday, we will fly to Chicago, to another Omni Hotel at Michigan Avenue or about 20 or so days.
Happy camper!
T. Meneses

title: “More than impressed”
text:
Having read the reviews earlier in the year when I originally made the booking I was a little concerned that the later reviews gave me cause for some concern.
We are a family of 2 adults and 3 teenagers. We booked a suite and a superior room. We arrived very late at night and were swiftly processed and taken to our rooms. I can understand the comments posted on a few points, yes in places it is wearing but I found it immaculately clean and comfortable. The staff were excellent and very obliging.
The evening drinks and snacks were great and apart from the greediness of some of the other guests, particularly hogging the free internet access, we thoroughly enjoyed it.
We would definitely return.

title: “You might as well be invisible”
text: I stayed in about a dozen hotels over a two month period in the DC area due to business commitments. I limited my stays to 3 and 4 star hotels. Out of the dozen I would put this one at about 8 (with 1 being the best). The best part of this hotel is its size (if you like large hotels and large rooms) with an amazing lobby that displays its long history and a great location. The worst part is the service and the indifference of most of the staff. It was my experience that a customer literally has to argue and be rude before they will get even a reasonable level of service. It was also my experience that most of the staff have the attitude that they don't care if anyone stays at the hotel or not so everyone might as well get lost. I believe that if it weren't for their history, this hotel would never survive based on the large number of rooms they need to fill together with their poor service. Also, the air conditioner was very very loud during my stay. I beieve this is because it is very old. The only remedy I could think of was ear plugs or freezing the room until bedtime, then shutting off the air conditioner before attempting to sleep. When I brought this to the attention of the front desk I was told "all the rooms are like that". Therefore either the hotel needs a newer central air system or the front desk lies because its easier then giving a customer a different room (see indifference above).

title: “Decent food service would give it 5 stars”
text:
I've used this very helpful site so many times that I've decided it's only fair to begin to contribute to it. This hotel has a lot going for it. First, a great staff, the equal to the best hotels we've ever stayed in, very friendly and helpful. Second, terrific rooms, or at least our room was. We had a very nice one bedroom suite on the club level with incredible panaromic views of the sound, the peninsula and but for an unfortunately located building next door, Mt. Ranier. The clunky tv in the armoire was a bit of a surprise in this context; the room cries out for a plasma on the wall--not that we would have turned it on with the views! 
However, the restaurant and lounge situation keeps this hotel from the 5 star level. First, if you think Ritz Carlton when you hear club level, forget it. You pay for what you might order from the extremely limited and basic drink menu, even for a diet coke, and the hor d'oeurve service is,well, unimpressive. There is only one restaurant and lounge in the hotel, the Ruth's Chris Steakhouse located next door (with an entrance from the hotel lobby). If you want a quiet drink, it is noisy and crowded and filled with people who perhaps have been there too long. If you want breakfast, you get a limp one page xerox of your egg choices. If you want dinner, you get steak. This is just lazy and cheap, and really a shame given the staff, the location and the physical plant of this otherwise fine hotel.

title: “Great Time!”
text:
My mom, 2 sisters and I stayed at this hotel week of April 14th. We had the best time. I was nervous about the service after reading some of the reviews but the staff could not have been nicer. We got one of the rennovated rooms which was very nice, clean and the beds were comfortable. Yes, the hotel is crowded and you have to wait a little bit for the elevator. But seriously, this is New York! You're not in the middle of the countryside; there are people everywhere! I also wouldn't eat here. The prices are outrageous and there are so many other dining options in the city anyway. Heck, there's a Starbucks across the street where you can get a pastry and a coffee for less than half of what you'd spend at the hotel. 
All in all it was a great stay. You can't beat the location and the accomodations are very nice.

title: “Great Hotel for the Bachelorette Party!”
text:
I stayed at Hotel Vitale for a bachelorette weekend and it was wonderful. The service, decor and beds were awesome. The staff was at our beckon call and we loved sleeping in the beds!! 
The hotel was kind enough to give us a bottle of champagne and a tray of gourmet cupcakes for the group which was super sweet. We loved the rooftop terrace (what a view!) and overall the hotel was great. 
Overnight parking was $$ at $40/night but that was my only complaint....we went to the bar in the hotel and had a lot of fun there as well. 
Next time I go to this hotel, I am going to do a more romantic trip as the hotel is good for both scenarios...great stay overall. 
Thanks Hotel Vitale! (more specifically Nicole Muller)

title: “Okay”
text: This review is neither good nor bad. I am not sure what to say really. Was booked for 3 nights but decided to cut trip short by a day. Got a deal on Expedia and because of the deal could not find out much about hotel or what type of room we would be getting. It ended up being kind of small for a teen boy and myself ( his mom). I don't know many teen boys that want to share a bed with their mother. Maybe if it had been at least a queen sized bed but it was a full. I decided to sleep on the floor but needed more padding. I asked a couple of times about my options because they don't have cots due to them being a fire hazard. I was given an extra pillow and blanket but was told twice that an extra comforter would be brought to the room as well and it was not. Oh well. It wasn't horrible but could have been better also. Breakfast was okay. Most of the employees don't speak a whole lot of english , some were very , very nice but some of them seemed very stressed and didn't want to share elevators with us ( like they were told not to). I am a hard working individual myself who doesn't have a ton of dough, work on my feet all day, very physically and mentally demanding job and can really relate to people who work physically demanding jobs also and I felt badly that they kept insisting on giving the elevator up for us even if they were waiting there first. I'm not quite sure what to think of that. It makes me wonder what life for some of the people working in South Boston is like in terms of living. I guess this review is partially about the hotel and partially about the South Boston area. Hope the info helps! : ) Oh , the cafe in the arcade was a bit " different" but the Tavern restaurant that we had dinner at was great! Great waitress too!!

title: “Hospitality should be taught to front staff...”
text: If all your looking for is location, then this hotel may suit you. We arrived a bit early for check in and approached the not so friendly, did not make eye contact, nor did he have a smile hotel check in gentleman. We all have bad days, but when you pick a hospitality profession unfortunately, those days should not exist. He did not crack a smile, when asked will there be rooms available at 2 pm, like he said they would...he responds, "I really don't know we will see at 2!" When we returned we decided to use another person at the counter. Well, to our delight this gentleman had the same instructions as the other. Don't smile, don't make eye contact and speak mono-syllabic. Went up to the room...The room had two temperatures, cool or inferno. I had one of the super dated rooms on the 16th floor, (which by the way look very little like the pictures you see online). Anyway, the higher the floor the better noise reduction from Times Square. Strolled back down to pick up a map from the concierge person. I thought it not possible, she was trained along with the other not so friendly, please stop bothering me personality fellows. I never write reviews but read some of the ones for this hotel and thought I needed to share my experience. I have stayed at many hotels and really can live with a lot of crap except unfriendly staff! I will never stay here again, for what I paid and the service I received.

title: “Very nice, but......”
text:
My husband and I stayed at XV Beacon on a Saturday night to celebrate our wedding anniversary. I booked and paid for in full the room via Snique Away and I paid for the higher priced corner studio room. This stay was a surprise gift from me to my husband and I was very excited about staying at XV Beacon based on the description & reviews here on Trip Advisor.
Upon checking in, we were told that the corner studio we had PAID IN FULL for was not available and they had put us in a smaller room that was "just a bit lower in quality" than our booked corner studio. I said "what do you mean a bit lower in quality"? He said that it was almost but not quite as good. What is that supposed to mean?? Well...you can imagine my reaction. He then said that they were comping us $100 to use in the restaurant. That was all well & good but it was 2PM, they were no longer serving lunch, and we were not planning on eating dinner there. Also, neither one of us had brought proper dress for that type of restaurant and the man told us that it was "upscale casual" which did NOT mean shorts & sandals. We were in town to have a nice casual night out on the town (North End festival & Quincy market) and then our overnight in the room. So, we checked in as I had no choice, and went to our room. Because I have never stayed there before and I do not know what the rooms look like except for photos on their website, I did not know what to expect. The room was nice. It was fairly large and had a nice bathroom. It had the amenties one would expect from a hotel of this caliber. Our room was quiet and very clean. We had no view except of office buildings. Certainly not a corner room. After getting settled we went down to the bar for drinks and whatever food they would be able to serve us. There is a VERY limited menu and we both had salads. No bread was offered or served with the salad. The service was good but the salads were small ($16 a piece!). The bartender was very friendly.
Because we still had $50+ to spend in the restaurant, we ate breakfast there in the morning. Again, it was nice but certainly not $50+ for 2 people. My husband had a small omelet that they did not even serve toast with. I had french toast which came with a small amount of syrup but no butter. Between the 2 meals we were able to spend down the $100.
I would have given XV Beacon a 4 or possibly a 5 if our room had not been sold out from under us. That did not sit well with me even with the $100 food comp. We only stayed one night but our stay was nice and the employees friendly. I don't know if I would stay there again because of the room switch. If we did, we would not eat in the expensive restaurant unless we were being comped. We know Boston well and already have our favorite places to eat at.

title: “Thumping music on a Wednesday night at 12:30 am”
text:
I am a big fan of all Starwood properties and have stayed in some nice Sheraton, Westins, St. Regis and Four Point Hotels, but have never had the music thumping so loud that I couldn't sleep. It may be just my room on the 31st floor, but it is truly making my stay here unbearable.
Everything else like the bed, furnishings and bathroom.....all nice. But what good is a nice bed if you can't fall asleep in it?
Won't be staying here again. There are nicer and quieter places elsewhere in the city.

title: “Nice place to stay and great location”
text: Have stayed here on numerous occasions. The rooms are stylish, clean, reasonably new, a good size, with comfortable beds. I slept well. The check in and out was efficient and friendly. I recommend this hotel if the ptice is competitive at the time of booking.

title: “Superb Location; Great Value.”
text: We enjoyed our stay very much. The hotel is clean, modern, and well maintained. We couldn't ask for a better location in midtown; steps from Times Square, theatres, public transit, restaurants, and numerous other attractions. Included breakfast was very good.

title: “Fantastic location and service!!!”
text:
We stayed for two nights on our honeymoon, and from the moment we walked in to the moment we left, we felt that we were the only guests there!!
The continental breakfast was basic, but free, and still good quality, and could have tea or coffee at anytime.
The cheese and wine in the afternoon was a welcome treat, and again was very nice.
The rooms were a reasonable size for NYC and were very clean with well specced bathroom.
The location was awesome, out of the door and a few steps to the corner to times square! Yes it could be a little noisy at times, but it's the centre of times square and it was never bothersome, it's just New York!
Would love to stay here again!!!

title: “New favorite hotel in boston...”
text: While the lobby is a bit of a scene, once you wade past all the party-goers, behind lurks a great hotel. Interesting history and architecture, a great vie of the city, convenient location, stylish but not uber-trendy furnishings, and I will never forget that water pressure blew... Nearly blew me out of the shower - love it!

title: “An oasis of calm amidst the hubub of Los Angeles!”
text:
Stayed two nights at the Elan Hotel and couldn't have been more pleased. Have stayed at several other nearby places (Beverly Laurel and Farmer's Daughter) and the Elan was so much nicer! The lobby is warm and inviting. The staff was friendly, helpful and a pleasure to talk to. After checking in, we were greeted by name every time we returned to the hotel after an evening out or a daytime excursion. Very "personal" service!
Although there is not a restaurant on site, the complimentary evening wine and cheese (5pm to 7pm) was a delight, with an abundance of cheese, fruit, and lovely wines. Likewise, the "continental breakfast" (which is included in the room cost) was replete with breads, fruit, yogurt, cereal, coffee, tea, juice and even hard boiled eggs! Displayed nicely in an alcove off the lobby, it was a lovely way to start the morning.
The hotel also has a "room service" agreement with a neaby restaurant that will deliver food to your room until midnight (!!!!) and without the standard delivery fee. In addition, "Jan's" (a fine, well-known coffee shop) is just across the street, and there are several other restaurants on the block. Plus the Beverly Center is only about 100 yards away.
The room was large and furnishings were up to date and comfortable. Plenty of outlets for charging the cell phones, GPS, and oh yes, the FREE wireless internet connection was a bonus. I am soooo tired of hotels charging $175+ a night for a room PLUS $10 or more per day for internet service -- such a ripoff! The FREE wireless connection here was reliable and if you didn't bring your laptop, there were three computers downstairs in the lobby, available 24 hours a day, for guest use. Guests also have access to the nearby health club for that morning workout!
Parking is valet-only with in-and-out privileges. The car was safely ensconced in the underground parking area (not out on the street) and easily accessible for retrieving a pair of sunglasses and then later, a jacket we had left in the back seat.
I travel to the area often and will definatley make the Elan Hotel my new home away from home. It was a pleasure to stay there.

title: “2.5 stars...expected better of a Hilton”
text:
My wife and I stayed here when I ran the marathon last weekend and honestly expected better. Upon arrival at 3:30, we, and many others in the lobby, were told our room wasn't ready and they were still cleaning them. We went out for a while and came back at 5 and the room still wasn't ready. At that point it was unacceptable and it took a nasty comment from me for a manager to come out and re-arrange our room. The room was roomy and clean so no complaint there. The next day, after running the marathon and coming back our room keys did not work and we had to go to the lobby where we were told we couldn't go back to our room because of renovations. We would have to move rooms, however none of the rooms were ready because they were being cleaned. After some more nasty comments from us and the fact our luggage was still in the room, they "allowed" us to stay in the room until another was ready. Of course then our keys stopped working again and we had to go back down to the lobby... We ended up moving and to their credit, we were offered help to move the bags and also were given our second night for free with no prompting. 
So other than the staff seeming to not have their act together, the hotel was in a great location close to liberty bell, convention center, museums etc. The rooms were clean,comfortable and no issues with noise. As an aside, the 10th Floor Grill was not available either day of our stay for some unknown reason no one seemed to know so I have no comment other than I guess the Hilton family like losing money. Additionally, the elevators were very scary and probably need some maintenance.

title: “Wonderful stay!”
text: The hotel is interesting, to say the least but the staff is friendly, check in and check out is so easy, and the rooms are luxuriously comfortable. I casually mentioned it was my birthday and we came back to the room after a walk around boston (the hotel is perfectly located) to find a cupcake and balloons in the room!

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: Spent 5 nights at this beautiful, clean, comfortable hotel on Nob Hill. Room is not huge, so might be snug for more than 2 people . My husband and I decided to eat in the restaurant about 9:00 at night. The food took a little longer than usual. We didn't care, but the manager apologized for the delay and that we would not be charged. That is the way to do business!

title: “Why would you stay anywhere else?”
text:
We loved the Millennium Hilton! I booked this room through Orbitz and got 3% Fatwallet cashback, combined with Entertainment Book coupon codes, we saved a bundle! I called directly to the Hilton before our trip and talked with the front desk clerk a little and he volunteered to bump us up to a higher floor room from what Orbitz gave us. I would definitely recommend staying on floor 31 or higher, the views are spectacular and there's almost no noise from the 'round the clock WTC construction site that's directly across the street. 
 We arrived at the hotel at 9:30 in the morning and when I went to the concierge to ask about keeping our bags until check-in, they said "Why not check in now?" Really? At 9:30 in the morning? No extra charge? OK! The Bellhop grabbed our luggage and off we went. 
 We were very impressed with the room. The Hilton hasn't let us down yet. We opened the door to a clean, fresh smelling, and spacious room. I was worried if the Standard room would be nice enough for our romantic getaway, Absolutely. From the plush King bed to the trimmed out, wall mounted flat screen, even the sofa chair and executive desk, it's all there. 
 The little interaction we had with the staff during our 4 day stay was all pleasant and cheerful, they always seemed eager to help. Housekeeping was great!
 Security was never in question. The lobby and front entrances are well lit and there was always a doorman, even after midnight. The financial district is mostly quiet on the weekends, but even so, NYPD had officers posted at the hotel on Friday and Saturday mornings during the week of 9/11. 
 There are just a few things you need to know about the location of the Millennium. It's directly across the street from Century 21 discount clothing store (You could spend hours in here shopping, they have a separate 3 story annex for shoes). There is a Starbucks within walking distance in either direction and also a Dunkin' stand. The Fulton St Subway Station is just a few steps from the side door of the hotel, that gets you right uptown. It's just minutes from Chelsea Harbor Market with plenty of shopping and the Bodies Exhibition (See this! It's worth every penny!). There are 2 for 1 coupons in the NY Entertainment book that you can buy online for $10 bucks before you go. It's worth that for the Bodies coupon alone. 
 Our trip was fantastic thanks to the Millennium Hilton. I'll be posting a trip report soon! Thanks for reading!

title: “Things could only get better after check-in....”
text: The family was in town for a soccer tournament and we decided on a double suite to allow us some down-time from the daughter plus allow her some space with her soccer teammates. Unfortunately, when we checked in, I was told we were in a King Suite with a hideaway. As I stated I was confirmed with a two-bedroom suite,but I was told-repeatedly-by the front desk personnel, that Homewood didn't confirm the room, only the soccer tournament confirmed the two-bedroom suite. As can be expected, there were no other rooms available at this hotel or any hotel in the area due to this soccer tournament-the hotel knew it had me, I knew they had me. The King Suite was fine except for: Huge spot on the bed's comforter-not a huge deal since I pull it off-but still gross, and the very sticky floors in the kitchen and the bathroom, the child lost a flip-flop while walking through-but even though the start of the trip was horrendous, Management at the hotel did call me later in the week and offered their apologies plus comp'd the room but that didn't make up for all the angst at check-in. It is a fine hotel but I would not come back again due to the problems-life is too short to patronize such establishments for creating strife during a family trip.

title: “Too clean and spacey!”
text:
I stayed in Sutton Court for 1 week. It was really clean and spacey (especially for NY standards).
I fully recomend it.

title: “Very nice, quiet, good location”
text: This was our 1st trip to Phoenix and we chose the Best Western I-17 MetroCenter because of the location, price and also the fact that we could get a pillow-top bed. We stayed only 1 night but were very comfortable; the room was on the 2nd floor and very quiet. The hotel is located on the I-17 highway in West Phoenix, very easy to find and amenable to other venues. The room was very clean. There is a Marie Callender's 1 block away. We would stay again.

title: “Great Stay!”
text: Stayed here for the weekend and was surprised to see the negative reviews on this website! We had enjoyed drinks on the 35th floor of the revolving lounge many times over the years, but this was our first time as guests. From what Im' reading we stayed in a renovated room (no complaints except the configuration of the room is a little strange because it is a half moon) on the 20th floor of the Triangle tower. The shower was great, the bed was one of the best I've slept in - overall the whole room experience was incredible. And you can't beat a 20th floor view in Los Angeles. We had drinks at the lounge- and the girl was so attentive to us - I've not had my drinks served that quickly. I highly recommend this property and it is one of the most unique and centrally located landmarks you can pick. Two warnings: If you like hotels that are close by to food and entertainment /malls, etc - this is not your hotel. It is downtown and pretty much lonely on the weekends - which is fun for walking over all the downtown sky bridges too. Second, parking here (like any downtown) is astronomical at $32 a night. Just be prepared to pay or find some of the parking that can be found within a few blocks if you try hard enough....

title: “Fantastic staff...perfect place to stay in NYC”
text:
From the minute we stepped into the lobby of the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square we knew that our stay in New York City was going to be a special one. We were warmly greeted by Charles whose wonderful personality made our entire stay so memorable. Jared and Marcel were also very friendly and helpful.
The front desk staff was kind and accommodating, especially since we had taken an early morning flight and arrived at the hotel before 9AM which was much earlier than the normal check-in time. Throughout our stay, regardless of the shift, the staff on duty helped us with any questions or issues we had. 
The personnel at this hotel is fantastic. We stayed here for ten days and had the opportunity to interact with many of them on a daily basis. They took the time to smile, laugh and be friendly, yet were very professional as well......Yes, it can be done and this staff proved it.
The General Manager, Kaizad Charna and the Director of Guest Experience, Laura Maldonado, deserve to be commended in creating an atmosphere which encourages excellent customer service.
Our room was on the 5th Floor and we found it to be clean and comfortable. Our housekeeper, Xiomara, did an excellent job and was such a fun and friendly woman whose bubbly personality was such a treat. As far as street or subway noise, it really wasn't a factor in our case. We managed to sleep soundly every night. 
The location of this hotel makes it the perfect place to stay especially if you enjoy walking. It is close to Times Square, the Theater District, restaurants, etc. etc. This was our first stay in the city and we loved how close and convenient everything was. It made exploring New York City so much fun. We will definitely stay at the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square again and highly recommend it if you appreciate terrific customer service.

title: “Rooms in the back very noisy!”
text:
When I made my reservations a month in advance I requested a quiet room away from the "L" tracks just west of the hotel. When I checked in and arrived in my room I realized that I was in one of the rooms closest to the "L" about a block away. I stayed in the room for a few minutes to see if I could make it work. After several trains passed by I realized there was no way! I went down to the front desk and they informed me that the hotel was full and they had no other rooms available. So, I was able to sleep about 2 hours that first night, which made my business meetings the next day very difficult. They did move me to a different room the next day, which solved the problem. 
As is said in many of the reviews, this is an old hotel in a great location. The rooms themselves are not too bad, but the entryway is terrible - just a horrible first impression. The glass doors are always dirty and look like they're 50 years old. There was a dirty rag lying just outside the main entrance that was lying there for several days of my 4 day stay. And as stated in other reviews, the wireless internet connection hardly works. The connection kept fading in and out during my stay. 
In summary, this hotel will work in a pinch, but just barely.

title: “A Good Value with Great Location”
text: For what we would pay for a regular room in a more "upscale" chain, we had a king suite, with lots of room. It would easily and comfortably accomodate a couple with one or two kids. The location was perfect; lots to do. The hotel is well done, with lots of attention to the decor and furnishings. We ate one breakfast in the hotel restaurant and the food was very good. We noted that some people complained about noise from next door rooms but we heard nothing at all (and the hotel was busy). We had a room on the main street and also did not think it was noisy (the windows provide good sound proofing). Not just a good value but a good hotel.

title: “The Best Deal In Town”
text:
My wife and I stayed at this hotel for two days (8/19 - 8/21) and after scouting out the other hotels we were going to book with, we are convinced we got the best deal. We had wanted to stay at three other hotels and actually canceled on one after reading the reviews for this hotel. We were not disappointed. Our room seems brand new. The fixtures, toilet, sink, tub, countertop were all premium quality and spotless (no mildew even under scrutiny). The bed was extrremely comfy. The sheets / bedspread were spotless and premium in feel. We also had a fridge and microwave! Wow.
We really appreciated the fact that so many things were included in the price at no extra charge: internet access, business center access, bottled water, luggage hold (because we arrived too early), and free hot breakfast (unheard of!).
Finally, the staff was extremely helpful. They gave us great suggestions for food and directions.
Our only complaint is that the air-conditioning fan is fairly loud. But man, does it do the job. It cools down the room in five minutes flat.
There is no question we'd come back to this hotel again.

title: “Baseball Buddies”
text: Last fall, I was in charge of booking rooms for several college buddies getting together to see some Astros games. I found the reservation process easy, the rates wonderful, and the help confirming arrangements close to the check-in date was particularly helpful. Dimples and her staff took care of our every need. I found the rooms clean and comfortable. The bar was a great place for us all to catch up with each other. Should I have the opportunity to visit Houston again with a group, the Crown Plaza would be a top choice.

title: “Still honest people in the world”
text:
My wife and I spent 5 days at the Best Western Cabrillo Garden Inn while I attended a conference at the convention centre. Hotel is convenient to Gaslamp area for eating and shopping and easy highway access for travelling around San Diego.
Hotel was good value for money. Rooms were clean and reasonably furnished. Stay was enjoyable and staff were always helpful.
But the reason that I am writing my 1st review was a pleasant surprise on our return to Canada. I had been walking to the convention centre and listenting to my Ipod on my daily trip. However after we had left the hotel, I discovered that my Ipod was missing. A phone call from the airport resulted in a promise from the front desk to have the staff check for it. The next week my Ipod arrived healthy and sound with no charge for shipping.
Thank you staff at the Cabrillo Garden Inn for confirming my faith in people!

title: “Good Hotel, But stayed in Better”
text: Ive have stayed here a few times over the years, its a typical upscale Marriott hotel. No wi-fi in the rooms (as of May 2011) which is a big downfall, must go into the lobby to get a signal. Rooms are nice and clean, but don't have the modern feel other hotels i have stayed at in SF have for the price it cost per nice.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
As other people have mentioned great location for soho etc but if you want to spend a lot of time in the times square/ central park area it's not the right area for you . 
There's a direct train to jfk from centre st which is very close (assuming you don't get lost on arrival!) and loads of places to eat/drink/shop
service discreet and helpful; rooms clean, quiet and well equipped.

title: “DO NOT STAY HERE!!! DUMP!”
text: We pulled up to front of hotel prostitute approached our vehicle...witnessed a drug deal right on steps of entrance...and watched a man with an exposed knife walking towards our vehicle...all during 2 minutes in broad afternoon daylight!!!!!! Needless to say we had no choice but to stay elsewhere. Was booked through booking.com (another horrible decision) and alerted them immediately of the situation. 6 days later they said they can't help get a refund and closed the case. On top of that we were double charged for the room we never chked into, almost $400 later...no resolution with management being a bunch of crooks! If you value your life and money do yourself a favor and book elsewhere. Travelocity puts their customers FIRST!!!!!!

title: “Perfect”
text:
I have nothing but good things to say about this hotel and its people. All staff was very friendly: cleaners, receptionists, concierges, doormen, etc.
My room was big and very bright. Didn't get a great view but still decent exposure to some of the gardens and a skyline of some parts of the city.
I enjoyed the harder mattress although my husband said he would have preferred a softer one.
Elevators are pretty fast and readily available so I never had to wait more than a few seconds (if any at all!)
The pool wasn't open yet so I cannot comment on that, but the gardens were magnificent.
Locations is also great. Just steps from the Metro and one stop from Dupont station. Also close to the zoo, although I didn't visit it. 
We rented a car the last day. Parking was $35 for self park or $39 for valet parking. But they also told us that there is free parking during the night and all Sunday on the street.
Overall excellent experience which contributed to enjoy Washington DC.

title: “Pleasant last-minute surprise”
text:
We arrived in Seattle late on a Thursday afternoon with no idea of where we'd be staying until our flight out on Saturday.
We pulled off of I-5 and logged on with a laptop to see what was available.
Based on other Trip Advisor reviews, we chose the Silver Cloud on Lake Union-- which happened to be less than a mile away from our offramp.
We were delighted when we arrived. The fax of our reservation got there a minute or two before we did. We were given an upper floor room with a view of the lake and the weather was spectacular.
The rooms are large and clean. The free continental breakfast is served in a nice location which also has a view of the lake. Restaurants are about a half-mile away, but you can also ride the new Seattle streetcar (South Lake Union Trolley-- SLUT!) which takes you to the center of downtown shopping, monorail, etc.
Pool, spa, free coffee at all hours. Great place.

title: “Worth it for the location”
text:
Just stayed here and must say I enjoyed my stay. The rooms were recently remodeled and were very nice. The beds were comfortable, but seemed to be on the smallish side. They were more like full size beds rather than queens. My only complaint about this hotel was the plumbing. Even though the rooms were recently remodeled, neither the sink nor the bathtub drained properly. 
As indicated in the title, the location is excellent if you are going to Philly for historic sight seeing. It is adjacent the the cemetary were Ben Franklin is buried, is right across the street from a historic quaker building, and is within 2 blocks of several other historic sites.

title: “Great place but watch for hidden costs”
text: Attended a wedding in the San Diego area, and stayed here . Like most Embassy Suites, this is a great property for families/friends traveling together. The rooms were very spacious, with a pullout bed in the couch for extra room. Enjoyed having a door that could separate the bedroom area from the living area, so could hang out in the room witht disturbing those sleeping in.
