The breakfast was excellent (cook to order eggs, omelettes, etc), and a great value-add for a start to the morning without having to go to a restuarant. The lines were not bad when we were there The staff was extremely friendly, and quickly responded to questions we had. Parking is in a garage adjacent to and easily accessible to get in and out, although some of the stalls were pretty narrow. The cost to park there was $20 a day even if you used the hotel parking lot. Plus extra taxes by the city ,town, municipality etc which added to the bill.This was not mentioned in the web site or on the phone.The hotel in the immediate area includes a PF Chang's, and an outdoor shopping mall across the street.The quest reception every night was a welcomed relief after site seeing .

title: “Best place to stay in Downtown Denver!”
text: Great staff. Great room. Ideal location for us since we were going to the Denver Center for Performing Arts. If you don't take advantage of the pool and spa facilities included with your room, you're missing out!

title: “Nice, quiet & well located with comfy basic rooms.”
text:
Chancellor provides good service and excellent location with a modest price. Breakfast was a bit pricey but otherwise excellent order-from-menu type cafe. In Feb time quiet and nice although very near to Market Street and Union Square shops & restaurants.
O.K. Finland

title: “One star is too generous for this dump......”
text:
I was adamant that I was going to write to Best Western upon return to the UK about this terrible hotel. I have never felt like this after a hotel stay before (and there have been many)
In short, I can't be bothered so i'll just share my pics here!!
It wasn't very cheap, it's dated, dirty, the staff are morose,it smells horrible,The air con sounded like a not so distant tsunami,Internet constantly dropped out,The tv didn't work properly, The window didn't even latch shut in my room & I worried for my possesions throughout my whole visit. 
Hell, they couldn't even through in a breakfast to counter the bad points somewhat!
How a multi-national like Best Western continue to have this hell hole in their portfolio beggars belief!!!

title: “stay here !”
text: stayed in one of the recent renovated rooms, looks more like a motel but clean well outfitted nice personal nice area walking distance to the convention centre (+/- 20 min), airport gaslamp etc. and most of all quiet rooms in the evening and night. Great stay

title: “WARNING: SHOULD BE CALLED CRACKCOMEBER SHORES”
text:
My girl found their ad on Craigslist. I knew the rate for the week in the middle of summer just blocks from the beach had to be too good to be true!
I should of been paid to stay there!
-Rooms horribly decorated
-Bed hard with springs poking out
-No air condition
-Janky windows
-Dirty Carpet
-Stained comforter
-People openly doing drugs!
-Children running around
-Roach infested
-Management is rude, unprofessional, I'm not sure what half way house they found them in
-NO PARKING
-We didn't even have drawers to put my clothes in
Those are only the things I can think of off the top of my head. The place was swarming with shady looking characters. My girlfriend wouldn't stay in the room alone!
This place shouldn't even be allowed to rent rooms! 
The only way I'd stay here is if I didn't have a car to sleep in.
YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED

title: “Comfortable stay”
text:
I was recently on a whirlwind trip to the USA for the love of the NBA.
We decided to watch a few games at the staples center, It was about a 20 min walk from there.
LA being such a big city it is probably advisable having a car to see all the attractions.
However as far as downtown is concerned it is pretty central.
50 dollar cab ride from the airport.
Friendly staff, clean hotel, it has a lot of history and character.
The concierge was only to helpful for any of our silly questions.

title: “Fantastic Hotel!”
text:
This is a beautiful hotel in a perfect location for visiting Baltimore. During a trip down the East coast with stops along the way, we stayed for a couple days in Baltimore. We loved everything about the hotel!
The best thing is the location. Across the street from Camden Yards and only a few blocks from Inner Harbor, you have easy access to everything. 
The hotel itself is perfect. We had no complaints about our stay. Check-in was easy, staff was very nice, the room was wonderful, and check-out is simple with their zip check-out. Definitely, definitely get room service or eat at their restaurant for breakfast. We had food delivered to the room for only slightly more than it would have cost to eat at the restaurant, and it was one of the best breakfasts we've ever had!
Minor issue was the housekeeping knocking on the door several times starting at 9am the day of checkout, but just as much our fault for not putting out the 'do not disturb' sign. 
Other than that, we would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting the area.

title: “Couldn't be happier”
text:
We were here three nights (March 27th-30th) using rewards points. We had a great room on the 36th floor with Times Square view, no problem with the lights or sounds. The room was a very clean two double beds. Room service was excellent and fast considering the size of this hotel which happened to be full. We had no problem at all with the elevators system, though when we arrived it was a bit crowded, with people trying to reach the 8th floor for check in. We used the Elite line, so we did not have to wait. The staff was great, and the location was even better, right in the middle of everything. We walked to ""Wicked and "A View from the Bridge" theatres. We even walked to Central Park. 
On our way back to EWR we took a cab to Penn Station and then the train to the airport (total time from hotel to EWR less than an hour) Consider this option, because if you use shuttle services they will need you to be ready 4 hours in advance to get you from the hotel to the airport, and you can rather be at the City for those three additional hours. The cab to Penn station was about six dollars, and the train $15 per person. We would have probably walked to the station (is not really that far) but it was raining a lot. You can also use the same option from the airport, but in that case consider walking from the station if you do not have a lot of bags, because most cab drivers will not take you to the hotel trying to avoid Times Square traffic.
We had the greatest time and our teenagers we fascinated to be right in the middle of it all.

title: “Nickeled and dimed to death”
text:
A very pleasant hotel, but sheesh, the prices! 
$48 a day to park!!!
$5 a day to use the room safe.
$13.61 a day to use the internet. 
$25 a day to use the mini-fridge (which I needed to keep meds cold)
Exorbitant room service prices.
And so on, and so on.

title: “good value for money”
text: I stayed in this hotel for 2 nights, it was just i wanted, room very espacious and clean, the recepcion was not very knowledgebale about the area and other services but tried to be helpfull tho.. it was good enough for what we pay. the area was safe and central.

title: “Avoid this Motel and neighbourhood!”
text:
I've made a mistake not checking the property on TripAdvisor. Now I must agree with previous comments! For a first glance the building, corridors, pool and room looks dirty, worn out and creepy. Room was dirty, had stains on walls, broken lamps and ALL TOWELS were DIRTY and obviously not changed. Bed linen looked worn as well. We got terrible sleep while bunch of "Afro-Americans" were making so much noise all night long. 
Creepy people are staying there!!! Outside motel we have been warned several times about dangerous neighbourhood with risk of being robbed or assaulted after sunset. Staff rude and unhelpful.
DON'T stay there making same mistake as we have done!

title: “Great experience”
text:
Westin is my preferred hotel chain and this one does not disappoint. This was my first stay in this particular property as I usually stay at the nearby Westin Gaslamp (Horton Plaza). When I couldn't get a room at the Gaslamp property, I reluctantly took the room here. I should not have been worried. Of the two hotels, the staff at this hotel was the better of the two. From the valet to the bell person and everyone in between, the staff was exceptional. 
We were down in San Diego for my son's first birthday (zoo trip!) so we had a lot of "gear" for him. The bell staff was extremely helpful in getting everything out of the car, bringing it up to the room and helping us get things like ice to keep his food cold. The valet staff also was very gracious in retreiving toys from the car that this dumb dad forgot. We didn't take advantage of a lot of other services since it was a short trip, but I will definitely consider going there again. 
If you go, try to get a water view. We were on a Preferred Guest floor and the views of water were amazing, especially at sunset and daybreak. 
There are only two slight drawbacks which prevent me from giving it 5 stars. First, the room, while an acceptable Westin room, was not as updated as other properties I have been in. To whit, there was no minifridge. There was a space in furniture for one. Second, it is slightly on the outskirts of downtown. Granted it is not a far walk (or a cheap taxi) to the Gaslamp district, it is farther out than the other Westin at Horton Plaza.
If you don't walk to walk far, Karl Strauss brewpub is a short stroll up the street from this hotel. A great option for either a business traveler or a family guy. It is within walking distance of Santa Fe station if you arrive in San Diego via Amtrak.

title: “Good Gaslamp Location”
text:
I title the review "Good Gaslamp Location" because it is close enough to walk to the Gaslamp District but far enough way to not hear any of the noise from the revelers.
We stayed three nights at the beginning of February and enjoyed the hotel stay. The staff always had a hello or welcome back for you and always asked if they could help us out with direction or restaurant suggestions. Usually the suggestion was followed with a discount card for a drink or appetizer at the particular restaurant.
We went out for our breakfasts most days as we wanted to try something different each day but the one day we had breakfast in the hotel we felt that the food was good and the value was also good. 
There is a nice outdoor patio on the ninth floor that you can get a drink at while enjoying the city view.
Only problem we had was the coffee machine in the room would not work. Mentioned it to the desk and they said it would be changed. Next morning machine still did not work. Don't know what happened there. We mentioned it again at our check out so hopefully the next guest will be able to make a coffee on their first morning.
Would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: “not worth the money!”
text:
We stayed 3 nights in september 2011 in this hotel.
we were on a 2,5 week holiday on the westcoast, and this hotel was not the best we stayed in.
and yes breakfast is okay and location is good.
but carpet in the room is dirty and bathroom is not good!
Hotel needs an urgent renovation!
more than USD 200,00 for a room is very overpriced.
Adrian from the netherlands

title: “Room and amenities not as advertised”
text: We were there for a convention and were placed in the Tower portion of the hotel. Room was not what you would call spacious and bathroom was very small. If you used the desk someone else would have to crawl over the bed to get to the chair. King size bed took up most of the room. The bottle of water in the room was $4.00 and sodas in the machine on our floor were $2.50 but if you went to the other floors were cheaper. Desk staff were not customer service oriented if you had a problem. No water in the pool and exercise room was not as advertised and was told it was the artisit rendition of what it would look like when done.

title: “Great, centrally located hotel.”
text:
My husband and a colleage were heading to San Fran for a business trip, so I decided to tag along. We booked through priceline and got a rate of $120 a night for four nights. 
We arrived super late on Tuesday night/Wed morning and upon coming from Oakland airport, we went to the wrong Hyatt. There are two in San Fran, that are both very close to each other. Turns out we were staying at the Grand Hyatt, which is on Stockton Street, about half a block away from Union Square.
Check-in was easy, and our room was on the 5th floor. The rooms are very nice, and have a iHome alarm clock where you can dock your ipod. I was dissappointed the first morning to see that although they had a coffee maker in the bathroom, the coffee to make it was in the mini-bar and cost $4! So I went to the mezzanine the first morning to get a small coffee and a bottle of water and it cost $5.50. Fine for business travelers who are expensing it, but I recommend going to Startbucks across the street, or getting bottles of water at Walgreens down the street (that is what I did).
Otherwise, we did not eat at the hotel, but did go for drinks on Friday night at the Grandviews Lounge on the 36th floor, great views. I also used the fitness center, which was very well-equipped. 
Check out was very crowded, but we used the automatic check-out machines and took advantage of using the computer in the lobby that is there for you to print your boarding passes. Service at this hotel was also very good and you cannot beat the location.

title: “nice visit”
text:
Huge room. Great service. Very expensive price. Worth the price. Nice location.
Restaurant probably not worth price but rooms and service are good.
Staff is superbly trained and responsive.

title: “You get what you pay for”
text: All i'm going to say is that you have options. There's lots of hotels in the downtown area...Unfriendly/not helpful front office staff.......asked for a restaurant that delivered and the answer i got was, ( we have the flyers at the front desk) asked for a cab company's phone number , and the clerk gave me what I thought was a cab drivers number. When i went down stairs it wasn't a cab driver at all, she had given me the number to a family member..I was totally freaking out, however I didn't want to miss my flight. Just remember, you have options.

title: “Great Location. Do not book through Hotwire.”
text:
We stayed at this hotel July 13-18. After reading the reviews I was a bit concerned as we booked our hotel through Hotwire.com. We were told we were going to be given the standard full size room (90 square feet-small even by NYC standards).
After arguing with hotwire for hours, we finally spoke with the hotel directly and they gave us a complimentary upgrade to a queen room. This room was still on the small, very small side, but adequate. We had to put our luggage on the window sill, but, we made it work, and thoroughly enjoyed it. After all, we only slept there.
A note about booking through hotwire, if it shows a 3.5 or even a 4 star hotel, avoid using hotwire.com at any price, and go to any times square hotel website and the price will be the same or less, AND you can select the larger room. Once you book through hotwire.com, any hotel property will treat you like a third class citizen. The room we originally booked via hotwire was not even listed on Stay hotels website as an option. 
A note about NYC hotel rooms: We have stayed at many NYC hotels, and if you book a boutique hotel (ie: stay, paramount, the mansfield, W) the rooms are going to be extremely, EXTREMELY small if you are used to staying at a chain hotel in other cityies (ie: Hilton, Marriott). The lobbys and furnishings will be fantastic, but you will sacrifice room size. Just depends on your travel needs. The largest standard rooms we have found were at the millenium broadway.
Location: Fantastic. Steps from times square, subway stations and times square.
So, I digress. The lobby at Stay was sleek and modern. The Aspen Social club was nice to pop in for cocktails after/during running around all day. Our room was on the SECOND floor, but over the front desk, not over the club, Tuesday through Friday we did not hear a thing. We had an early flight on Sunday, so we had to leave at 4:00 am and . the club on Saturday night was in fact the loudest music I have ever heard except at a concert. Unbelievably loud as we were leaving. Patrons were having a great time though.

title: “Great Hotel for night before cruising out of Port of LA in San Pedro, CA”
text:
Booked this hotel for an overnight stay for a cruise out of the Port of LA in San Pedro, and it was absolutely perfect. They offer a free shuttle to the pier, and it only takes about 5 minutes time. The staff was very courteous, and even provided us with free toothbrushes, toothpaste, and combs when our luggage was lost for a few hours at LAX. Room was very clean, and beds were quite comfortable. If you need an overnight hotel before or after a cruise out of San Pedro, you simply can not go wrong with the Crowne Plaza. The best thing to do in San Pedro is the Cabrillo Marine Aquarium. The Crowne Plaza offers a free shuttle to and from the aquarium (or anywhere else within a 5 mile radius of the hotel). The aquarium describes itself as an "educational" aquarium -- which means that its not overly fancy (no dolphin shows, etc), but it does offer some outstanding exhibits of local Southern California fish and marine life. They only ask for an optional $5 donation for adults, and $1 for children, and it is completely worth it. After the aquarium, you can walk across the parking lot to Cabrillo Beach as well. 
We ate dinner and the next morning's breakfast at the Grinder restaurant which is about 1 block from the Crowne Plaza -- it's basically like a Denny's or a Perkins. The food was very reasonably priced, very tasty, and the service was extremely friendly as well. 
Take advantage of the free shuttle service at the hotel -- they ran the shuttles with a sign-up sheet system, and were always very prompt picking us back up after we called them from our location.

title: “Three star at mostu”
text: Good location, service, and nice grounds. Too dark at night. Uncomfortable bed. Room not clean. Room service and bar food terrible. Chocolate cake was dry muffin split in half with fake whipped cream. Maids took no trash including empty cans and room service tray. Rooms are cinderblock and clammy. Wouldnt complain if not touted as upscale resort.

title: “It was a like a dream.”
text: Hotel was so comfortable! Beds-perfect. Rooms-big and beautiful. Lobby-luxurious. Location- really? SO MUCH FUN.

title: “Nice hotel, parking and internet cost you extra.”
text: The hotel was nice, the room clean, the staff friendly. No complaints on that. To bad in the city you always have to pay extra for parking and Wifi while the price is already higher then a nice countryside motel. Location is very good, close to the freeway and close to Warner Bros, Universal, Hollywood. Far from the airport though.

title: “Surprisingly Awesome!”
text: To be perfectly honest, we chose this hotel for the price and its proximity to the Riverwalk. We were so surprised by the cleanliness of the facility and the great staff, especially the ladies who prepare breakfast (which is really good, but the way)! And the rooms are not tiny, little boxes. We took the trip to SA for my daugther's birthday and spent one of the days at Fiesta Texas - it was only a 15 minute drive away. After an exhausting day at Fiesta, it was great to relax in the hot tub! Needless to say, we will definitely be staying there again on our return trips to the Alamo city!

title: “Wonderful lake views, clean, classic hotel”
text: The hotel was a 5-10 minute walk from the Magnificent Mile and offered superb lake views. We stayed in a standard room which was clean and well-stocked. The concierge was very helpful and directed us to all the tourist sites we wanted to visit. We were able to get a good deal on the hotel so it was worth the money but if we had to pay full price, we would have wanted to stay somewhere closer to the Magnificent Mile as Chicago winters can be bitterly cold as we witnessed firsthand!

title: “Try somewhere else”
text:
I travel a lot and stay at a lot of hotels. I recently stayed at the Westin in Melbourne, Australia, and was so impressed that when I had a choice of hotels in New York I naturally choose the Westin. I believe there are two primary aspects that define a hotel experience. The first is the comfort of the room and the second, the service.
This hotel has only just re-opened and so the rooms are nice and fresh, tastefully decorated and quite cosy. The bed is comfortable, the curtains block-out, the aircon works well and the bathroom is a reasonable size. I never like showers over the bath and I like them even less when the drainage does not work effectively. I mean seriously in a newly renovated hotel I do not expect to end my shower standing in 2 inches of water. Other than the shower, which was a big disappointment, the room is comfortable.
The service however was the most disappoint aspect of this hotel. There are lot's of staff but they all seem to be busy with something other than their customers. There was more than one occasion I sought out assistance only to be handed off to someone else that was even less interested. I will come to New York again in another month, I will not stay at this hotel.

title: “We Would Definitely Stay Here Again!”
text: We are the type that like to see the property first before booking. This could be a problem (especially as the Buick Invitational was going on at the time in nearby La Jolla) and as we had been staying at nearby Surfer Beach Hotel and left for a 3-day side trip to Sedona, AZ without making reservations for our return trip to San Diego, we were dismayed to learn that the Surfer Beach Hotel was completely booked! We drove around and viewed numerous rooms in the area to no avail. We saw this one and asked to see a room without much hope. The front desk staff was so nice and helpful and let us view several. We chose Room 67, a second floor room with cathedral ceiling. It was absolutely HUGE! It had recently been remodeled and reminded us of a way higher priced room what with the glass shower wall, contemporary fixtures, decor, etc. We wished we had found this place sooner, but unfortunately, we could only stay the last 3 nights of our trip as we had to fly home. We stayed there on January 25 through January 28. Half a block from the ocean, great location! Free parking was great, too! It was too chilly to use the pool, but it looked great, very clean.

title: “Loved Chicago”
text:
Chicago is a clean, exciting, trendy city...but most of all I felt like I was safe too!!
Lots to do from lots of museums to discover to shops to spend your money in or keep it cheap and check out the parks and have a picnic by a fountain...what ever your budget gooo gooo gooo!

title: “Horrible Experience and Rude Staff”
text: I stayed at this hotel, due to good reviews I had read. However, my experience was horrible. The room was musty and dirty, including bloodstains on the carpet. Some members of the staff were rude. You know it is bad, when you ask for something and the front desk tells you that they will have to find an employee of theirs that is not rude. Not the kind of customer service I want to pay for.

title: “A nice place, at a nice price, in a great location”
text:
My wife and I stayed there for a week while I was in Chicago for a conference. The service was excellent; the concierge and doorman were particularly helpful. The room was the standard size for a business hotel, and the internet was free in the lobby. The location was quite convenient in terms of shopping and entertainment, and it was helpful to have a 24 hr Duncan Donuts and 7/11 literally across the street.
If you are the kind of person that needs to be pampered and tends to try to order things that are not on the menu in every restaurant you go to, this quaint, comfortable, nicely-located spot may not be for you. On the other hand, if you regard yourself as a regular sort, then I highly recommend this hotel to you.

title: “Super location, friendly staff, cramped basic room.”
text: I found this hotel pretty easily even though Downtown is a little tricky to drive in with all those one way streets. It didnt look like your typical Motel 6, it was a nice 4 story building with palm trees with a spanish type theme. I was impressed with the looks of the lobby and outside. When I got to my room it had a nice view of a freeway off ramp so we were easily moved to a quieter inside location. The rooms were very small, I would say the smallest hotel room I have ever stayed in. But it was clean and quiet. No extra anything, very bare bones but it was half the price of most other hotels in the area so it worked for us. Location was awesome. We were just a few blocks from little Italy and the Maritime Museum. Since we dont really live in our hotel room like some people do, so location was much more desireable. I would stay here again but I also have to say the Howard Johnson we stayed in later in our trip was a 2 star hotel and man what a difference. Not a great location but so much better accomidations for the same price a night. I am glad we did both but it would have been hard if we went from the 2 star to the 1 star.

title: “No heater...very cold!!!”
text: Although the price was reasonable, the room was too small. The bathroom seemed to be larger than the bedroom area. There was mold in the bathroom walls and ceiling. The room was very cold when we arrived (3:00 PM) and we soon found out that the tiny radiator heater found in the room was controlled by the hotel management. They turned on the heater for a short period of time during the evening (5:00 PM) just long enough to make it somewhat comfortable. Upon our return from dinner and a walk around the city, there was no one at the front desk. Our room once again was very cold but this time the heater was never turned on. Needless to say it was a very very cold and uncomfortable night. The sheets and blankets were old and not thick enough to keep us warm. The turned on once again the following morning at around 8:00 AM. By then, we were more than ready to check out. The room is definitely not properly equipped for the summer days either. Please don't waste your time and money in this hotel, you will regret it as much as I do now.

title: “great stay”
text:
What an incredible hotel, staff and location! 
The hotel room was fantastic along with their breakfast buffet both mornings was terrific!
This is definitely the place to stay in Chicago!, The hotel staff were so friendly and helpful, with any questions about what top things to see and do while there.

title: “Not up to par”
text: We took the kids ages 2 and 7 for 3 nights. We booked a bayside suite which was right on the beach with a lovely view. the hotel has fun activities for families~ mini golf, bikes, ping pong, pools. Room service is pretty sad though. The food was mediocre. The grounds coulld be kept up a little better. We checked in at 4pm and rooms were not ready when we got there. There were many families with wild kids (mine included) running loose in the lobby while we waited for rooms to be released. If check in is at 4, the rooms should be ready. We don't plan to stay there again.

title: “My Best Stay Yet........”
text: I loved this Hotel! The staff was very friendly. I went during the Thanksgiving holiday, so you know it was very busy. However, I felt that the staff catered to our every needs. When I made my reservation, I had one king bed for my mom and I. That was not going to work! When I checked in, I asked if we could have two double beds, and they said yes. At the same rate we were paying for the king bed. The location was great, one block from Michigan Ave., and steps from the Grand Luxe Cafe. Overall, I have nothing bad to say about this hotel or my experience there.

title: “Gorgeous hotel, gorgeous people”
text: The Hudson Hotel has beautiful common spaces-the lobby, the bars and restaurants, even escalator. The rooms were beautiful too. What was not beautiful was our broken air conditioner that we complained about for 2 days before we insisted on moving rooms, and the outrageous waits for the elevators.

title: “Very good, but..”
text: I really want to give this hotel 4 stars. In terms of the service and initial impression it is. However, I found the room to be a bit worn down - the surface of the bathtub was peeling, the drains were slow, the carpet had several stains on it, and there were some other little issues around the room. Especially because the carpet was stained, I felt uncomfortable sitting on the couch and bedspread, wondering if those were dirty as well. On the other hand, the room was very spacious, had nice decoration, and the marble in the bathroom was nice. If they refurbish the hotel a bit, I would rate it 4 or 5 stars. I also had room service several times, which was pretty expensive ($4 delivery charge + 20% tip) but very good.

title: “I Recommend Four Points”
text: The staff was great help and friendly. Rooms were clean and made you feel comfortable. Quite place to rest. Big open space to work. WiFi area was nice. The bar area has everything you are looking for. Five Stars!!

title: “Location great, tv not so good....”
text: The service was pretty good, they let us check in early and any requests we had for extra towels and blankets were handled quickly. The tv in the room lost signal a lot and the tv was hard to change channels.

title: “Clean, slightly above expectations.”
text:
Stayed here for one night with family. Property was fully booked with two weddings and a conference at the nearby hospital.
Rooms were exceptionally clean for what appeared to be an older property. Beds were comfortable, but there was some ambient noise that drifted from the wedding's DJ (by ambient, I mean a strong bass-line that was inevitably going to permeate the premises) Toilet would not flush but engineering was quick to respond, given the busy nature of the place.
As in most Hilton-propers, no free WiFi unless you're a HHDiamond. Pool was nice and clean, along with ample parking. H

title: “olde world charm”
text:
This is one i've stayed in off and on for years, great location, staff friendly, a character of a doorman, and the ambience all make a great impression on entering off the street. 
The beds and pillows are very comfortable and the rooms clean, and usually for the price this is value for money.
Right outside a Bart station so getting too and from the airport is a breeze for $8.25
Located in civic but close to SOMA walking distance to powell street and the city and a short tram ride either way up or down Market street
Unfortunately the street people seem to congregate nearby and can be a distraction but actually are always polite and are not too in your face.
A few down falls are, the doors seem to slam and you hear them all down the corridor. the lifts tend to be a little slow but they get there.
and some of the features in the rooms need a bit of updating like toilet seats etc.
but still a charming stay,

title: “Paradise Resort”
text: Paradise Resort is definitely what is says. Paradise!! You feel like you are in Hawaii. Very clean, friendly and helpful people, four pools and hot tubs, rental equipment. Food was good and the prices reasonable. Away from the crowds. Would stay again if we are in the San Diego area.

title: “Snow storm blew us in.”
text: We drove into Denver on Saturday to avoid snowy and icy roads in the middle of the night to catch a flight. I found the front desk to be very nice and helpful. I found the hotel was not really very sound proof and you could hear people coming and going all night. It is an older building, not as clean as I want in my hotel stays. For myself, I will pay more to stay somewhere else next time as I don't enjoy being able to hear people in the halls and rooms above and next to me. It is priced lower so that is a good value and located close to the airport.

title: “Excellent place. Great for a show or visit to Intrepid”
text: The place was great. We plan to come back some time with our 4 sons and stay there. We would take in a show as well as taking them to the Intrepid Museum. Everything was clean, the staff was friendly and helpful, the room was beautiful. My only problem was that it was loud outside on the street--considerable noise came through the window. This is probably something that you cannot control. Otherwise, we were happy with the stay and will be back. Thanks.

title: “Holiday Inn express has better service?”
text: I have to travel frequently to Houston for work, and have stayed at a the Holiday Inn express a few times. Have also used a couple of other similar chains in the same NW Houston area. We decided to pay a little extra and stay at regular Holiday Inn rather than an express. One the Hotel is feeling a little aged, they label the pillows as though there was some difference in them (not) I have to say the express had a better trained and friendlier staff, every time we were heading out for the day they would acknowledge you, and offer you a bottle of, much appreciated water, considering the heat in Houston. Got back to the hotel last night and realized we hadn't stopped for water, so husband heads down to the lobby to inquire where we could get some. The restaurants closed and we're all out you can go to the machine. Ok where is the machine near the elevator okey dokey checked the 1st floor 2nd floor 3rd floor,nope. OK back to the lobby, oh I think they moved them hang on because this other employee apparently is in a hurry and I must take care of him first, than he did come and help to find the wandering water machine which 1st one was out second one didn't work OK third one right, nope doesn't work either, really. Just to check today asked any change in the water department? Nope.

title: “misinformed”
text: We telephoned from the East Coast, but were not informed (a) that the Magic Castle Club has a dress code or (b) no children are allowed. So, our stay was very disappointing for our two teenageers. For one of them, the Magic Castle was to be the birthday surprise. The hotel should inform potential guests.

title: “Better hotel in this area”
text: I have stayed with Hilton and this one in this area. This hotel is better than Hilton. Like the indoor/outdoor swimming pool and the gym. We can alway get a quiet room we like. The only thing bothered me might be the changing color lights high up, but I did not see them in the room with the curtain closed.

title: “Highly Recommended”
text: I'm staying at the hotel right this minute and it is a God-send. Only vacancy I could find near Union Square and not only is the price really great ($89 a night), but it is nice. Most pleasant, beautiful lobby, marbeled elevator, what looks to be a newly renovated room. The staff couldn't be nicer or more helpful. The area is good, since the Hilton is just a block away. Nicely stocked minibar at the most reasonable prices I have ever seen. Rooms are very clean, and mine is quiet and peaceful. I highly recommend it, and I'll probably stay here every time I have to visit SF from now on. Valet parking is $20 a night, about average for SF, and they sure make it easy to leave your car -- it's quick. If this is a budget hotel, then they should all be this nice. The room has more room than I was expecting from other reviews. There is a seating area as well as all of the basics. The bed is really comfortable.

title: “Peabody Memphis”
text:
I have made reservations at the Peabody in Memphis, TN. I have read the reviews and looking forward to a pleasant stay. The major concern I have will be making reservations through the Reservation desk in Orlando, FL. The issue being card charges...holding charges(double the amount), charging the card when advising customer service rep we will be paying cash, etc.
More to follow on our stay!

title: “Well, its cheap...”
text: Well I stayed there in January of 2003. It really wasn't that bad. It was not nice at all, however I wasn't expecting much. There was no control for the heat - my room was just hot. But I could open the window some and even it out. Never saw bugs and they cleaned the bathrooms (you have to share) several times a day. Its just a place to sleep, or at least thats all I used it for. My door locked fine and I never had any problems.

title: “WE LOVED!!!!”
text:
When I read some reviews of the hotel my expectations were low and I'm afraid. But I have a very nice surprise!!!
Great location. The room was very clean and comfy and not so small, the staff was extremely friendly and helpful! 
The subway was 2 safe blocks walk and bus stop was a pleasant and safe 1 block walk. 
The only complaint I would have is the cable issue. If you are looking to watch a lot of TV on your vacation, I wouldn't recommend this hotel, but if you are looking for a GREAT deal on a great room in a great location, this place should serve you as good as it did us!!!
We paid $119 per night for a room (hotelconxions) we thought excellent value.

title: “No Problems Here”
text: Well this is a Travelodge, not the Ritz. But it's very clean and comfortable and a block from the Red Line Harrison station. For the price, I doubt it can be beat. Yes the building is old and somewhat shabby but the rooms are renovated and the bathrooms are new and spotless. Had everything I needed including a coffee maker, in-room safe, lots of towels and toiletries, new heat/AC unit, just about everything. Bed was comfortable and everything was in order. Staff varies from very friendly to very indifferent but that's normal for this type of hotel. The snack bar off the lobby is handy for an inexpensive but good meal or snack. If you're looking for a safe, clean and inexpensive place to stay in the Loop, try the Travelodge.

title: “Good with Kids”
text:
I am torn about my review for this hotel. My husband and I stayed here with two kids, (11 and 13) for four nights at the beginning of August. We received a rate through the hotel website for 429.00 per night, which included breakfast for four at the hotel restaurant. For a two bedroom suite in New York, this was a great value, but the hotel itself was just okay. We received a corner room on the 29th floor that had a great view of Times Square, but the room itself was smaller than the rest of the rooms. There was a small fridge, microwave, in-room safe, and sink. We were able to buy drinks and snacks from a nearby Duane-Reade, which helped save some money since room service and in-room snack center were very expensive. The lobby and front desk staff were friendly, and we never encountered any long lines. 
 We ate lunch at the hotel restaurant our first day, and it was not very good. Like the rest of New York, it was pricey. The breakfast buffet, which was included in our rate, was very good. In addition to hot and cold buffet items, they had a cook-to-order station with eggs, waffles, pancakes, and french toast. The hot and cold buffets had a great variety of fresh fruit, oatmeal with a wide variety of mix-ins, and numerous other items. 
 The reason I am torn about my review is that, while I was not impressed with the hotel overall, I still felt that it was a good value for New York. Here were the problems: The bathroom was not completely clean upon check in. I called and no one ever made it up to finish cleaning. The iron in the room was broken, and when we tried to use it, water poured out all over the clothes. Again, I called about this and it was never replaced. The room itself was just okay, very plain and a little run down. The hotel has no rollaway beds available. 
 We did not have any problems with the internet--the hotel website states that there is a per day charge for access; however, we received the Hilton signal and it did not require a password or code. It was not terribly slow. The workout facility was decent-elliptical and treadmills with televisions, free weights and machines. It is open 24 hours, which is convenient. 
 Overall, it was a good value for the amount of space(although get a rate quote INCLUDING taxes, as they are very high in NYC--our 429.00 rate was much higher once taxes were added).

title: “Hampton---- but really still a Howard Johnson's”
text: First time in NYC and we picked a Name brand hotel HAMPTON INN service is great but the rooms and the halls need to be redone it still looks like a Howard Johnson The staff were some what friendly but the location is great Needs to improve on the rooms

title: “Very handy to IND”
text:
Had a 6am flight so spent the night here the night before the flight. The room was newly remodelled. Clean. No complaints. Nice TV. $2 for chips in the vending machine seemed high. Shuttle right on time at 430am on a Sunday morning. 
Closest hotel to the airport. Recommended.

title: “Impressed!”
text: Stayed one night in an Executive Suite. Exceptionally clean; great amenities. Very large hotel with excellent service in the dining rom, at registration and valet check-out. Had breakfast and dinner in the hotel restaurant and it far exceeded our expectations. No complaints!

title: “Used to be a good hotel”
text:
We were in NYC on business, for a weekend of events to attend; we're not tourists, and we've stayed here before, years ago, before Barclay was added to Intercontinental. We parked 5 or 6 blocks east, for cheaper parking, and walked to 48th St. and Lexington. We arrived very wet from a torrential rainstorm, and were looking forward to a hot cup of tea, seated comfortably in our room while we dried off. Alas, not to be.
The lobby is large, formal and busy. There are lots of people sitting around using laptops because they charge extra for internet in one's room. The check-in went smoothly enough.
When we arrived at our room, we were a bit surprised at how tiny it was. There was only room for one chair, at the desk. The bed was too tall for me to sit on. Then we found that the coffee machine was broken. We called "Instant Service", and were told an Engineer would come to look. Forty minutes or so later, he came, pronounced it broken, and went off to find a replacement. 
While waiting for him, I went into the bathroom and found a wet used bath towel on the towel rack, draped over the unused towels. Yuck. Also noticed a few long dark hairs on floor and sink. So we called "Instant service" again, and were told to not touch the offending towel, and wait for Housekeeping with fresh towels. A man with a stack of towels came 15 minutes later but refused to touch the dirty one ("not my job") so I put it on the vestibule floor, then washed my hands. The Engineer then came back with a non-broken coffeemaker, tried it out, and left, stepping over the towel on the floor. I asked the desk about tea but was informed that they do not have teabags, I would have to call Room Service, at $12 a go. By now we were almost late for our event, anyway, so we went out.
Next morning, I was grossed out by a very mildewy shower curtain (photos), and that there was now no coffee (nor tea, of course.) Husband went down to the desk to get a packet, and was told to order room service if he wanted any coffee ($12, as I mentioned.) No one ever did come to pick up the dirty towel on the floor, inherited from the last guest. We just kept stepping over it.
Now these are not disastrous things, but irritating, especially at $279 per night (AAA rate). Upon checkout, we complained to the clerk. The front desk supervisor came, and told us that at that "reduced rate", he could not grant us any price reduction, but offered 2 complimentary breakfasts at their buffet ($37 each). We noticed the long line, and opted out in order to make our event on time. 
The management did not go too hard out of its way to correct what I saw as real lapses in service. This hotel bills itself as luxury, and charges a lot for it. I'd be a lot more understanding if it was a Comfort Inn, and indeed I've had better treatment at Comfort Inn. There are lots of hotels in NYC, and we'll find a better one next time.

title: “Staff outshines facility”
text:
The facility is rather run-down for a Sheraton. The hallways need to be vacuumed, the pool is too murky for me to even stick my feet in, and the overall condition of the hotel is TIRED.
That said, every associate that I encountered went out of the way to be friendly and helpful. Kudos for that!

title: “Enjoyed my stay at the Four Seasons”
text: Came here on a business trip with a group. Had not been to Austin iin 30 years or so. This is a nice hotel. They try hard and there are little details like robes and slippers (which I did not nor would I ever use so not sure who does). They offer free coffee in the morning, and the staff seems motivated to help. Beds are a little soft for my tastes but at least they give you plenty of pillows, which I appreciate. They have real wood hangers in the closets and you don't have to wrestle with the "theft proof" type. Nice toiletries in the bathroom,and a really good shower which is always welcome. I liked it. I had a nice view and it's near walking and running paths. I would certainly recommend it.

title: “One Night Getaway”
text: We actually live in San Diego and just wanted a place to stay downtown. As Starwood members we got an excellent rate that included breakfast. We had a nice room with an excellent view. The staff was awesome and we enjoyed our stay.

title: “Never again!!”
text: Well maybe it is a different hotel.. but for me it was a terrible choise, room full of skulls all kind, so scary... no closet, tv updated, very noisy.. al night were the dumpers picking the garbage downstairs, elevator sucks.. un friendly.. everything was a disaster.. it was like a nightmare.. I hope that never happen again.

title: “Palomar was a pleasure to stay in.”
text: I enjoyed my stay at the Palomar. I wasn't familar with the Kimpton hotels, and found most of the little luxury touches very sweet. The coffee in the lobby in the morning and the happy hour were well attended, and the choice of newspapers delivered to the room in the morning was great. I found the location to be very convenient to the metro. bus, and a variety of restaurants. My only complaint was that the door to the hallway did not seem to screen out all the noise from families going to the rooms farther down the corridor.

title: “Amazing staff, service and little extras....”
text: My new husband and I stayed at this hotel 7th November for 4nights. I booked this hotel (direct) based on the very reasonable room rate for NYC and excellent reviews on TripAdvisor. We arrived by yellow cab and were greeted by such lovely and welcoming staff. I had advised upon booking (almost a year before departing) that it would be our honey moon. They had very kindly upgraded us from a lower floor queen room to a superior on the highest floor possible (32). A view of the Empire State Building to the left and a view of the Hudson to the right. Perfect. Reception also sent up a couple of cupcakes to our room with a note they had written offering their congratulations. What is lovely about this hotel is that there are only 5 rooms per floor and only those rooms can access your floor in the lift by swiping the door key in the lift. So there isn't a constant flow of people coming and going to their rooms or being noisy etc etc. Our room was nicely decorated and we had enough room. The bathroom was very modern and we had a lovely shower. The hotel isn't down the nicest of New York roads, but lets face it, you walk from your hotel to explore the city and back down the road, to the hotel for a nights sleep. It's not enough to worry about. Just a couple of seedy shops. Reception had free coffee in the mornings and warm apple in the afternoon. This was an added extra because you could just grab a takeaway coffee/apple and head to your destination. The hotel was apporx 6/7 mins from Times Square. Not far at all. I really loved the feeling of this boutique style hotel and loved the fact that it is a bit of an undiscovered gem. I will always recommend this hotel for NYC.

title: “Beautiful hotel, small rooms, excellent service”
text:
The hotel is very fancy shmancy, at least, compared to my typical digs. Beautiful lobby and great service. Before I came, I was worried about a thunderstorm that was going to break while we were in town and asked if we should bring an umbrella or if we could borrow one of theirs. Their concierge emailed back right away and let me know that there would be one waiting in the room for our use. I had also asked about what to bring in terms of clothes because being from California, I only know casual beachy attire and she gave me a lot of suggestions and advice. I wish I could say that it was accurate, but she tried and I appreciate that a lot. We were greeted at the door every time we left and every time we came back. Very friendly and helpful staff!
Upon arrival, we were upgraded from a standard room to a deluxe just because it was available. That was nice! But on entering the room, it still felt extremely small, especially for an upgraded room. It was still very nice and gave us enough room to dance around in, but wow, we are so glad we were upgraded to deluxe instead of the standard room! The bed was very comfortable, the tub/shower was a bit small, but all in all, a beautiful room. The Wi-Fi had pretty good signal, but the TV was much worse for reception than I would expect. Oh well, we weren't sitting in the room watching TV all day, so it wasn't that bad.
The area is quiet, in that there aren't a lot of restaurants, bars, or clubs nearby, but still kind of noisy compared to my neighborhood back home. We could hear people arguing and sirens going off until around 2AM sometimes, but got used to it eventually. This is even from 8 floors up. The hotel can't control what goes on outside, but something to keep in mind if you're a light sleeper.

title: “Great folks, nice, clean, comfy hotel.”
text: This is a nice "little" hotel. They have complimentary wine tasting most nights. The rooms are comfortable and clean. Having to subscribe to get free internet is a slight pain, but not a big deal (nbd). The little work out room is kind of a joke, but it is a clean and well appointed joke...the TV (w/headphones) on the exercise machines is nice. The hotel is kind of at one end of the part of town if you're walking around, but, again, nbd. The bartender of the restaurant was great.

title: “Comfortable and closeby to a lot of POI”
text:
We were very pleased with our 3 night stay here. The room was spacious for a mid-city hotel, we had all the comfort we wanted, such as: flatscreen TV, Wifi, hotel lobby seating area, free cooled water dispenser on our floor and a Starbucks next door. Parking for the car is located in a public parking 1 block away and is not cheap, but you get a discounted price when the hotel staff validates your ticket. Parking is always expensive in the big cities.
The hotel is just a few blocks away from the Willis/Sears Tower and the Millenium & Grant Park areas. The magnificent mile is a 20min walk or you can take a Water Taxi next to the Willis/Sears Tower to take you to the start of the Magnificent Mile. The Water Taxi is a fun way to travel. The neighborhood felt very safe to us, even late in the evening. 
Walls between rooms are a bit thin, our neighbors woke us up on the 1st night by arriving loudly around 4 AM.

title: “Warm Cookies and nice pool”
text:
I pricelined this hotel for an awesome deal and I was beyond happy. In fact, I preferred it over the other hotel I pricelined on the coast. The parking was $22, but there was a lot and metered parking right across the street in addition to various lots all over the city that were cheaper. Download the best parking app for android or iphone and you can locate various cheaper option all over. If you have a large or wide truck you will need it the parking lot is very narrow.
The lobby is really nice and there was a cute bar right by the check-in area. The pool is on the roof and there is also a hot tub. The hotel is within walking distance of the gaslamp district and the marina area. The beds were comfortable and clean. 
As other mentioned the warm cookies at check in was a nice touch, and the cookies were very good!

title: “It did the job”
text:
I should note that the date of the reservation and subsequent stay was in December, so some of the details may be a bit blurry, but much of the memory is still there.
We arrived a bit before checkin, but the early check in was not a problem for the desk clerk. She quickly found the reservation and sent us up to our room, which was on the 22nd floor as I recall. When I called in the reservation, I remember talking with an operator who tried to talk me out of getting the room with a view; she said that just about all of the rooms have a wonderful view and that it probably wouldn't be necessary to pay extra for that feature. Somehow, though, I read "room with a view" to be "corner room". Needless to say, I was sorely disappointed it was not. Don't get me wrong, the view was still great (see the photo with this review), but I don't think it was anything for which I needed to pay extra. 
The room was clean and seemed a bit roomier than most hotel rooms in which I am accustomed to staying. Housekeeping did a great job every day. Everything looked great. It is a standard hotel room; I mean it's clean, had a great view, and you're in Chicago, so how much time will you actually be spending in your room?
Pool seemed a bit cool, as others have noted. It also was a bit too crowded for my liking, so I didn't get to enjoy it too much. Again, as others noted, the food prices looked quite a bit too high to justify eating in the hotel, but again, you're going to be in Chicago. Get outside of the hotel. Do go to the bar at least once during your stay; the view is absolutely magnificent. I could justify drink prices that were a bit higher for that view--right at the fork of the Chicago River.
The open air courtyard was nice. It was relaxing and the open feel was nice to see when leaving the room. I was quite tempted to get some of those little plastic soldiers with parachutes and drop a bunch of them to see them fall down to the courtyard, but thankfully, was talked out of it.
The hotel is accessible via enclosed walkways all the way from the brown line station (Merchandise Mart). Some previous reviews I read noted that the walkway wasn't open on the weekends. I didn't find that to be the case, but it seemed as though there was a special event going on that weekend, so I'm not sure if that was a fluke or a new rule.
Finally, I gave 5/5 for value. Since the stay I'm reviewing in Dec. 2008, it appears as though the hotel has raised it rates and substantially. If I'd paid the current amount for the room, I'd probably give it a 4/5 for value. The location is right near the heart of Chicago, yet far enough away that you're not awakened by sirens and/or traffic and/or trains. You'd be hard pressed to find a better location in Chicago.

title: “Tired, Tired, Tired”
text: We stayed at this hotel for three nights. It was a convention hotel pick. The room was very tired...spots on the carpet, burned out light bulbs, TV remote in need of a battery. The bed, in an attempt to make it a heavenly bed, lacked the proper sized sheets. The bedding ended up off the bed in the middle of the night and was just "too much" to make it acceptable. The location is scary....we were warned not to walk around after dark in this section of town. In our opinion, it just stays in business because of its location close to the convention center. If you are not at the convention center, don't waste your money and time here.

title: “Ritz Feeling the Pinch?”
text:
What a disappointment - I have stayed at this hotel before, but you can really 'see' and 'feel' the cutbacks and this is not the only Ritz Carlton I can say this about in the past 3 months.
The amenities in the room have really been scaled back - had to call to the front desk to have a shaving kit and other things sent to my room. There was a Govenor's Meeting or something going on the next few days, you would have thought they staffed the hotel up but didn't seem to be so. In speaking to some employees, they told me that they weren't hiring anyone because they had to cut back hours on current staff due to business cancellations.
I've stayed at two other Ritz Carlton's in the past 3 months and I've seen the same type of cut backs in the rooms, the club level, and in the staffing of the hotels.
I pay the rate because I expect the service level to remain the same, regardless of the economic climate.

title: “Great Service”
text: Excellent service at this Hotel. They went out of their way to get us a “special request” conference room without any notice. Excellent place and I would highly recommend. The check in process was quick and convenient. The lobby area and all rooms were clean and neat. The entire staff seemed as if they really was glad to have me as a guest in their hotel.

title: “Great,classy, friendly, easy place to stay.”
text: Hotel Rouge is one of the friendliest, easiest, most efficient, cleverly decorated, funky and classy at the same time hotels. I found it last year when I need a hotel in this area--and will stay there anytime I return to D.C on business. The staff are lovely--service is old-fashioned wonderful, Its super clean, very comfortable, even the street facing rooms are insulated enough to support a good rest, and the environment is safe and friendly. I love that its pet friendly---and the wine hour encourages getting to know other guests, which is unusual in this day and age. Its a super hotel.

title: “Nice hotel, would stay again”
text: Hotel was nice and the room was clean. Only problem was the pool. The pool filtration was not working and the pool had debris floating on top that looked disgusting. Otherwise the breakfast buffet was good and I would stay again . . . .

title: “unexpected pleasure”
text: After issues in my planned hotel, I checked in at midnight to the Westin, Time Square. A Warm party-like reception, with a polite and educated lady on reception; I was checked in swiftly, provided an immaculate and well thought through room. Hard to believe I was in the middle of one of the busiest spots in NY. The staff could not have done more, and the facilities could not have been better...

title: “Friendliest hotel staff in the world, best location in Manhattan, favourite hotel experience ever.”
text: My husband and I stayed here recently and had a blast. Each and every staff member is friendly, helpful and charming. Nothing is too much trouble. We had problems with our television and so they came, took it away and gave us a brand new one! Room is spacious, the bed is amazingly comfortable (we wanted to take it home with us!) shower is a rainfall style one in a lovely roomy glass shower area. Towels are big and fluffy. Had breakfast only once but it was great. Hotel is so close to Hells Kitchen, you are literally 5 minutes from hundreds of restaurants/diners etc for all budgets and tastes. Subway right next door connects you to rest of Manhattan. Walking from the hotel leads you to all the major sites of NY. So, you cannot beat the location, the room, or the staff. A hotel that is worth every cent- now that really is something!

title: “Outdated Rooms, Awful Service”
text: For US Business Travelers: Please stay away from this hotel. The rooms may be spacious, but the hotel is filthy. The bathrooms have mildew in between the tiles. The carpet is old and worn out. The furniture is from the 70's. There is dust and cobwebs on lamp shades. The televisions are flat screens, but the signal is very blurry. Also THIS IS NO LONGER A STARWOOD OWNED HOTEL. You may get the points, but this hotel is owned under a private company now. The service is terrible, the internet connection is unreliable. They gym has nice equipment, but stay out of the bathroom by the fitness center. Don't say you weren't warned.

title: “Pwrfect”
text: Great hotel in a great location. We could only stay for one night, but will definitely be coming back! Great coffee at the kiosk in the lobby too.

title: “Great experience, good price and nice staff!!!”
text:
When we got to the hotel it was approximately 1 p.m. but our check-in time wasn't until 3 p.m. Though we were early the front desk clerk got us an early check-in so we didn't have to wonder around for 2 hours. The room was very clean compared to other hotels we stayed at in the area plus the breakfast was delicious....waffles, eggs, bacon, WOOOW! Kept me from going to I-hop plus save me $8. 
Thanks Super 8 University...I'll definitely be back!!!!

title: “Wonderful hotel and staff”
text: We used this hotel for our daughters wedding to put our bridesmaids, groomsmen and out of town guests in. From the moment we got out of the car everything was in order. The service was great, everything we asked for was delivered promptly, even a humidifier at midnight. We had an after party for 60 plus people, the food was delicious, and every detail was handled from our first meeting, as it was with the room reservations also. Our vehicles were promptly valet parked and delivered , service was superior. IN planning this, all emails were answered quickly and efficiently. The rooms were clean and spacious. The proximity of this hotel in Cherry Creek is perfect for people visiting, because you don't need a car for restaurants, shopping, movies or night life.

title: “Good value for your money”
text:
It was not bad accomandation for the money, but with few little problems.
There were ants. On the bathroom there wasnt curtain and even not curtain rod. Everybody can see you on the window when you are showing from the street! WTF???
Internet was OK. Free parking was OK, the staff was helpful with us.

title: “excellent location for the price”
text:
We have just returned from spending five nights at this hotel & would definately stay there again & recommend it to anyone who wants a reasonable hotel in a great location.
While the hotel itself is a little grubby round the edges l felt that the overall standard of cleanliness was high. We booked two rooms which were clean and ready for us when we arrived and then cleaned every day that we were there. They could perhaps do with a fresh coat of paint in areas but overall we were delighted with it. The rooms were a reasonable size as well which we were relieved about.
Our rooms were on the fifth floor but the staff member on duty was more than happy to help with our bags both on arrival and leaving.
The best thing about this hotel has got to be the location - it's just off lexington which has some great bars and diners and about three minutes walk from the empire state building. Pretty much everything is walkable from here & it is this that would have me going back should l ever return to new york. If the hotel was further out l would still say it was ok but would be tempted to see what else was available for the price. The hotel was average but the location excellant. 
The staff were ok, didnt go out of the way to offer help/ conversation but if you asked them for anyhing they were great and happy to help - just not forthcoming. I had no concerns about my safety of the safety of my stuff while we were there & we came and went at all hours.

title: “Perfect Time Out”
text:
Very nice hotel, I could tell it has recently been upgraded. The rooms were quite spacious, the hotel staff was genuinely courteous. Loved the free shuttle.
I and my family thoroughly enjoyed the complimentary hot breakfast they provide, let us evade the lunch altogether.
The fleet of shuttles are also being upgraded so had the new car smell. Very nice! will definitely come again!

title: “Hurricane Stay”
text: Stayed during hurricane Sandy. My organization had a meeting. The hotel staff did a phenomenal job. They were organized and very helpful. They went out of their way to ensure that all of our needs were met. Rooms were clean and comfortable. We have been coming to this hotel twice every year and this was our best experience.

title: “My new 'home' in downtown Chicago”
text:
This was my fourth stay at the Hotel Palomar Chicago and I will definitely return. The rooms are clean, quiet and feature contemporary, comfortable design. The service is excellent. Everyone says hello, addresses you by name and makes you feel at home. 
Everything about this hotel is lovely. The towels are large and fluffy, the robes are animal print, the bathroom amenities are high-end.
The manager hosts a wine reception each afternoon. Be sure to try the on-site restaurant, Sable. We shared several 'small bites' plates and everything was delicious.
Hint: if you join the Kimpton loyalty program, you receive complimentary in-room internet, an honor bar credit and room upgrades when available. Also, if you arrive before check-in time, you can park your car, check your bags and go explore Chicago. The front desk will let you know when your room is ready. All you have to do when you return is pick up your room keys and your bags will be waiting for you in the room.

title: “Nice Value....but a little out of the way”
text:
My girlfriend and I traveled there for a getaway weekend and stayed 2 nights. I found the room to be reasonably clean and they had Aveda complimentary shampoo (nice touch). The common areas around the lobby appeared to be clean and well kept. 
My girlfriend had stayed at Silver Cloud hotels and she loved the breakfast waffles they serve. The breakfast was reasonable and the waffles were great.
I must add that one night we had gotten a bit lost late at night. I called for the shuttle. Although we were not in an area where the shuttle normally picks up, the hotel manager made an exception and had the shuttle pick us up. File that under "good customer service". I travel for business about 100 nights a year and I found this hotel to be a nice value.

title: “Best Hotel Bed Ever!”
text:
If you are new to NYC then this hotel is in the perfect location. It is right on the south side of Central Park and you walk out the front doors and see it every day. Plus all the taxi drivers seemed to know it, no mean feat considering the number of hotels in the city.
Apart from the location the only other thing that set this hotel apart, in my opinion, was the fantastic bed (and pillows). It was unlike any bed I have ever slept in. To say that I felt like I was floating on a cloud is no exaggeration! We almost asked the concierge if we could take it with us.
Not that I am a fussy sleeper but usually, as many people will experience, the first night in a strange city/bed/etc. is usually not that restful. During my long, hectic w/e however, I always looked forward to falling into that wonderful cocoon every night (can't believe how tragic this sounds but it has to be said).
The ensuite was a little peculiar, I'm sure the toilet seats were heated but the bf said it was my imagination. However, it was a nice touch in the cold spring weather. Only gripe was the shower seemed to have two settings: scalding hot or 3rd degree burn.
The breakfast was quite dear, but a worthwhile luxury if you can afford it. Staff helpful and of course the service was with a smile.
Would not hesitate to recommend it.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text: We loved the hotel. It was in a great location, 2 blocks from the inner harbor! The room must have just been redone. It was updated and almost brand new. Great to have a full service kitchen in the room as well. We had a studio suite. Breakfast was good. Lots of choices and hot food. Yum! We would return to the hotel again. Great value and great room. Oh yea, could not get the public computers to print our pending cruise docs, so the hotel desk clerk went out of her way to help me, and ended up printing my documents for me, at no cost I might add! Thats going the extra mile for a guest!

title: “Delightful Dallas Stay”
text: Hotel is simply the best. I highly recommend the club level as the chief hostess, Miss Jackie, makes it her business to make a weary traveler welcome and at home. Overall the staff was very attentive, efficient and courteous. The rooms are spacious and well maintained and I enjoyed a great view of Dallas. The in-house restaurants were above average. The location of the property is superb. On a scale of 1-10, I rate this hotel at a 10+. You can do no better when visiting Dallas

title: “Good Old Arizona elegance in the heart of the camelback district”
text:
The Biltmore is quite possibly the Queen of Arizona hotels. It is elegant and beautiful and classy..... with a price of course, but you find yourself not caring what it costs because it's that good. We've stayed here when the kids were little and they accomodated them beautifully and as teenagers it's every bit as good. The pools are great in the summer, on campus restaurants are fine if a bit overpriced, and nearby restaurants are the best in casual dinning. Shopping nearby Biltmore is quite good... and Scottsdale fashion square with Nordstroms rounds out anything you might want. Memorable getaway especially with Kids, young adults and pets. Elegant grounds and recreation abounds... Great gym and tennis complex as well as full length golf course rumored to be very good (I've not played it) You can self park but wear comfortable shoes... it's a hike.
The Biltmore should not be missed though... it's worth all the added on fees etc.... SUPER NICE surrounds. Flower gardens and surrounds and fun things to do.

title: “WSH great value and location.”
text: Stayed for 5 days in August 2011. Room was good, I hear they can be hit n miss. But the location, value and service were faultless, would stay again.

title: “Poor service, poor communication”
text: For the price, was very disappointed in upkeep, front desk service and room quality. Had a problem with the free internet service, and manager never called back (even a week after the stay, after filling out a comment card and providing a phone number). They even tried to charge me for the phone call to their outsourced tech support.

title: “Great Spot”
text:
If you need a vacation spot or a quick stop over, the Hampton Inn Sea World in San Diego is the place. The staff is super friendly, breakfast is whatever you want and the rooms are clean and easy to access. 
I stay here every month for several days at a time for business and I keep coming back.

title: “Never again”
text:
Air conditioning was out for the two days I stayed in this hellhole. WIFI also was not available either night with numerous excuses given. Could't sleep because of the heat amd couldn't work with no WIFI.
Manager never returned call one.

title: “Absolutely fantastic”
text: Great service, great location, highly recommended! Would definitely come back again.

title: “In the mix and plenty to see”
text: I recently stayed at the Westin in Philly. I was close enough to walk to all the historic locations I wanted to see. I also walked to Pat's and Geno's to eat a Cheesesteak. The service at the hotel was top notch, friendly, very elegant and clean lobby. I would definately recommend staying there. There is plenty of shopping also, some of it in an indoor mall hooked on to the hotel. I have no complaints.

title: “Good value”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nites ,good location 2 blocks to union square
Staff where very helpful
On our first night room was small and we asked to be moved, of which they did
breakfast a little disapointing it is served on your floor, first in best dressed,however for the rate we paid, overall this is a great hotel

title: “Awesome service, Stinky room”
text:
Just returned from a 3 day trip and if you are looking for convenience, this is the place to stay. The location is outstanding and the service/staff are exceptional. The only real "turn-off" was the odor in our room. It smelled of urine in the bedroom and bathroom and hit you in the face the moment you entered the room. I cannot believe the housekeeping staff didn't notice it immediately or they had no sense of smell. 
Housekeeping was called immediately and supposedly the room was re-cleaned while we were out to dinner. Upon return, the smell was still as pungent as ever. However, we were so exhausted from a red eye flight we just tolerated it and slept with the windows open. We were out all day and most of the evening the following day so we didn't insist on being relocated. Under different circumstances, especially a vacation, I would insist on another room as this odor was extreme. This hotel is very nice hotel and staff treats people well.

title: “Sometimes being cool isn't cool enough!”
text: The relaxed and informal easy-going attitude of the reception staff has gone a bit further. Firstly, they chat with each other in a loud voice behind the reception curtain and leave guests stranded and eagerly waiting for their conversation to end to get assistance. Then, they show up, preauthorize an extra USD 500 on the credit card without notifying the guest; who given an aggressive answer "every hotel has its own policy" . The over-doing act of having to present a photo ID for every transaction or even when accessing the room is very annoying.

title: “Fantastic service and comfortable rooms.”
text: I stayed in the hotel with around 40 students from my high school, as part of a media studies trip. We spent 4 nights in the hotel, and the prices were reasonable. I wasn't expecting wonders, and was pleasantly surprised by everything upon arrival. The room was clean and a good size, the beds were large and extremely comfortable. The shower worked well and the TV was good enough. We had a balcony, however it was over-looking the car park; not amazing but still got a pretty good view of the surrounding landscape. The food was brilliant, both in the restaurant and the room service. Prices were also quite reasonable. The hotel staff were all kind and helpful, especially the waiters and restaurant staff. The jacuzzi and pool were both warm and clean, so not much more you could ask for. The wifi worked very well and all in all, it was an amazing experience.

title: “Happy with stay”
text: Staff was friendly and courteous. Room was clean and nicely furnished. They really hype the adjustable bed aspect however I was unimpressed. I like a medium soft bed and even with the settings turned all the way down I still considered it fairly hard but it was supportive. Other than that I was happy with my 5 day stay. Very nice having the business center avaiable to get online and the ability to print plane boarding passes there. They also have a small workout room and pool although I tried niether during my stay. If you are a light sleeper you can hear planes take off from the airport but running the fan in the room completely muffled any airport noise so it was not an issue for me.

title: “Good Choice”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights in January and glad I chose this hotel. Spacious room and tv, mini bar, safe etc. Good location, about 5-10 minutes walk from Macys. Friendly staff and very informative and helpful, particularly the Concierge. Breakfast ok but choose from the menu rather than the buffet. 
Boston appears to be safe and I walked everywhere or took the subway.
If you like shopping, I would recommend a visit to the Wrentham mall, about 45 mins away, this can be booked at the hotel.
Would return to this hotel in the future.

title: “Did not have the room I booked and were totally unprofessional.”
text: I was very excited to stay at the Mondrian Soho with my sons last evening. I had stayed once before and have had breakfast meetings many times at the restaurant. I booked a suite for the 3 of us which said it had a king bed and a sleep sofa. When I checked in late yesterday afternoon I confirmed with the check in person that the room indeed had a sofa bed. She said the rooms on the lower floors do but on the higher floors we can put in an air mattress on the floor. I was not interested in having my son sleep on the floor on an air mattress and couldn't understand why she was so concerned with the floor I was in and not providing me with the room I reserved.. She then said we have a suite with a sofabed on the 3rd floor. I said that would be fine as I never requested a certain floor. When I got up to th room there was a queen bed.. I called the front desk and explained that I needed a king bed as indicated when I booked the suite and indicated on the hotel website under the suite description. She had me on hold for awhile and then said she would call me back. She called me back 10 minutes later and said the only rooms she had with a sofabed have a queen bed. I explained to her that wouldn't work. She transferred me to a manager named Ricardo and he was extremely patronizing. He got,on the phone and said can I help you and I said aren't. You aware of the situation and he said yes. I explained the situation to him and that a room with a queen Ned would not work. He told me to hold on and he would get a room that would accommodate us. He then got back on the phone and said you have a room with a queen bed and a sofabed and I said yes you know that. He said at was all he had. He didn't seem to care and he offered no upgrade or help. I was shocked... I stay in NYC all the time for business and leisure. I had checked out of The Surrey to,stay downtown with my sons. What a shock to me how I was treated,.l. I spent over an hour dealing with this unprofessional and patronizing manager, I had to then look for another hotel. My evening plans had to be cancelled because of this. I would never ever stay at The Mondrian.

title: “Great hotel with awesome staff”
text: Well after reading some reviews we were apprehensive at first,but after arriving we found this hotel to be very well maintained and the staff very accomodating. We were in town for a wedding ,travelling with family and had reserved 4 rooms. Upon check in Angela made sure that all our rooms were ready. We had planned a large (around 25-30 people) family reunion w/ my niece. Her hotel however wanted to charge an additional $200.00 for use of a small meeting room, we spoke to Angela and she graciously accomodated us that evening in the hotels breakfast area free of charge. Simply outstanding!! Our rooms had king size beds & pull out sofa beds, the bathrooms were very nice w/ marble sinks, floor to ceiling marble shower enclosures,large mirrors and hair(blow) dryers. There were full length mirrored folding doors on the closets,ironing boards & irons inside. The rooms each had a refrigerator and microwave. The housekeeping staff did a wonderful job each day of our stay. The morning breakfast,was good w/ a selection of cerels,fruits,eggs,bacon, juice, coffee ,etc. making for a good way to start the day. Although the hotel sits back from the main road, it is centrally located to all of the areas attractions. They do have a pool / jacuzzi, which although small is perfect for familys with children as it was not too deep (3.5-4.5ft). The only things that were a problem were the parking (which if you have a larger car can be tight) , the breakfast area which can be very crowded at peak times and there are some dead spots in the hotels wi-fi system. But that being said, it was not so much of a problem that it would have affected our stay. All in all we had a great stay and I would recommend this hotel to others, especially those travelling with children.
