title: “Quiet, comfortable and centrally located”
text: I stayed at this hotel for a wedding in August, 2012. The room was quiet and comfortable and clean. I was supposed to get a wedding gift bag upon arrival but never received it until I inquired. The roof top pool was a nice surprise as was the Starbucks in the lobby. The hotel is near all the 6th Street activity if that is your thing. The building is attached to an office complex, so it feels a bit corporate. There was a minor mix up with my bill which the manager quickly fixed. The concierge was friendly and helpful. All in all, a very good stay. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Excellent value and convenience.”
text:
Stayed here for 8 nights during the Professional Disc Golf Association World Championships in Charlotte in July. Have stayed in Microtel properties elsewhere so had a good idea of what to expect (and not to expect) from the rooms and facilities -- clean, comfortable room with fridge and microwave, without a lot of frills or extras. Given the outstanding rate we got (using the PDGA discount), it's hard to imagine a better value. The staff was consistently friendly and helpful (and being there for 8 nights we got to see everyone). The common areas were generally clean and comfortable, albeit a bit cramped. Some of the other guests were disappointed in the early closing time for the outdoor pool, but given the location of the pool immediately outside some of the first floor guest rooms, this seems like the right approach to avoid having issues with noise from the pool preventing guests in those rooms from sleeping. 
Breakfast was acceptable, but nothing special -- a handful of cereal choices, packaged bagels, donuts, pastries, etc., hard-boiled eggs, a cook-your-own waffle station, etc. Fruit options were limited to oranges and bananas, and if you were looking for a way to do a low-carb breakfast your options were pretty much limited to the hard-boiled eggs and a banana or orange. With the fridge and microwave in the room, however, it's easy enough to work around that. 
There were a couple of minor quirks and issues -- no shampoo or soap stocked in the bathroom our first night, which we didn't realize until we were undressed and not really motivated to go back down to the desk. We also wanted to sleep in a bit after a long day our first night, and so had the do-not-disturb sign on the door until we were up and about. We got back to the room that night and found that it had not been cleaned/restocked (except that the used towels had been removed, leaving none at all in the bathroom). When I checked with the front desk, they explained that they don't come back to service the room if the do-not-disturb sign is out when they are servicing the other rooms. I've spent several thousand (literally) nights in hotels on business and leisure travel over the last couple of decades, and never encountered that before, but it wasn't a big enough issue to worry too much over -- we just made sure we were up and out of the room before they came around for the rest of our stay.
The surrounding area wasn't the best in Charlotte, and the proximity to I-77 no doubt increases the risk somewhat, but I didn't feel at all unsafe at the hotel (though I did worry a bit about the car being broken into) or the restaurants nearby. I had a pretty good idea of what to expect coming in, though, so I wasn't surprised. And being so close to I-77 and I-85 made it extremely easy to get to the courses and to tournament headquarters at the Blake Hotel downtown. The Northlake Mall area just north of the hotel on I-77 is a relatively new, safe, comfortable area with all of the usual suspects for chain restaurants and retail. It's also a relatively short run up I-85 to the Concord area with all of the racing-related attractions there.
All in all, the hotel worked extremely well for us -- given the length of our stay, we needed something with a relatively low nightly rate, convenient to a wide range of locations in the Charlotte area, with a fridge and microwave, with comfortable and clean rooms. We got all of that plus friendly and helpful staff. It's hard to imagine how we could have gotten a better value. If I were going to be visiting a particular attraction in Charlotte, I might opt to stay somewhere else closer to my destination, but under the same circumstances I'd have no hesitation booking here again.

title: “Classic charm in great location”
text: I love historic hotels, and this one epitomizes their charms...windows that open, thick soundproof walls, lovely lobby. This place has been wonderfully renovated, so the bathrooms have all modern fixtures and there is a plethora of outlets for all the gear we carry today. The location introduces one to a peacefully new York neighborhood, near the East River.

title: “I'll be back!”
text: We love Chicago and visit there at least once a year. I booked this hotel through a deal on travelzoo, so it was well worth what I paid. We only stayed one night, and were very happy. Check-out was at noon, but they kept our bags as long as we needed them to, while we walked around the city. We were on the 10th floor, and going downstairs to the nice lobby to use the free wi-fi was no problem. The lobby was nice and comfy. The staff was very helpful, when I called them to find out how to get there from Midway airport. They told me the airport shuttle was $19 per person, and a taxi would be about $30. I asked about the train and they told me the nearest station was only 2 blocks away. Everything is within walking distance, and the room was comfortable, though the bathroom was small. It was exactly what I expected in a boutique style hotel.

title: “many shortcomings”
text:
1- Air conditioner in room was so loud it kept waking us up. Can't do without it though, the room was quite hot.
2-Wireless internet in the room is nice...when it works properly. Never had such a hard time opening emails. Tried all their available connections at different times of day, to no avail, slow and splotchy. receptionist was no help, shrugged problem off.
3- bathroom is nondescript, so is the room decor but clean. Room only had decaf tea, and the coffee maker was missing a part, rendering it unusable. No sheets ready or stored in the room for sleeper sofa for my child. 
4- lobby, breakfast area ok, forgetable.
5- overall, not worth the price.

title: “Loved the Aloft!”
text: I decided to stay here the night before flying out of PHL airport and I was glad I did. Not only was the room amazing, I had such a great night's sleep, courtesy of a wonderful bed. Between the Bliss toiletries and ultra-mod amenitites, I was very pleased indeed. I kept my car at the hotel while I was away - the $7 per-day fee was less than any of the nearby off-site airport parking. If I hadn't been so intimidated by the fact that the pool was in almost full view of the lobby, I'd have gone swimming too!!

title: “Watch your car!”
text: While my stay was satisfactory, my car was severely vandalized (about $1500 damage) while parked in the motel lot overnight. The management was not at all interested in helping me find the jerk who keyed the whole drivers side of my car. An exact quote "Get over it". Won't stay there again.

title: “Sorted Ski Stop-over”
text:
We stayed at the Denver Doubletree the night we flew into Colorado on our way to ski, and the night we went home. We've stayed there before, and it was easiest to settle for somewhere familiar.
I think the experience at this hotel varies hugely depending what events are on, as the other reviews show. We were lucky, whatever was going on wasn't noisy. However, our first night was in a room with a connecting door, next to incredibly loud people who argued and made way too much noise. Luckily we had earplugs! We probably should have complained but way too tired from the flight to attempt it. I'd make sure to ask about the connecting door another time. The second night was absolutely fine.
The staff have always been incredibly helpful, the decor is plush, our rooms had everything we needed. The restaurant and bar food is fine, a little pricier than outside, definitely don't come here if you are likely to use room service as the prices are mad with loads of strange add-ons. The airport shuttle worked well for us. The hotel is not particularly handy for the city centre, if that's what you are looking for.
The thing I like best is the view - waking up on a morning when you're off to the mountains and seeing them in the distance - woo hoo!

title: “OK if you get a good room rate”
text: We stayed here for 5 nights beause we got an excellent room rate. The room looked beautiful even though it had a view of the building air conditioner, but then things went downhill. There was a lot of noise from adjoining rooms and the corridor (but, surprisingly, not from the building air conditioner)... even if people were holding normal conversations. On the weekend it got downright rowdy. Housekeeping is with a contract company with a language barrier so we kept having to ask for soap and cups (we actually ran out of both and no replacements were left in the room) and towels. We had asked that our bed linens be changed and for the next 3 days we were left clean sheets folded on the foot of our beds. The bathroom is too narrow for two people to be in there simultaneously unless one is in the shower...but the shower head was one of the best ever! Lots of news and sports channels on the TV but only HBO for movies - I guess they want you to do pay-per-view. Parking is $16 per day - that seems to be the going rate for this area, though some places have free parking. The Bistro is a quick convenient place to grab a breakfast, sandwich, or snack, and the yogurt/granola parfait and oatmeal were good. However, the breakfast sandwich on ciabatta bread was tasteless - really awful. We only ate breakfast there a couple of days and then found Denny's - there are two in Mission Valley. I had no problem with the internet connection on my iPAD and the lobby computers had one set up to print out boarding passes - very convenient - and free printing on the other computers (which were slow but adequate). A real plus is that there were lots of accessible electrical receptables in the room for plugging in electronics, etc. However, this is by far the noisiest place I've stayed in San Diego and do not plan to stay here again.

title: “Fantastic place to stay!!”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights on our honeymoon in June 2012. It was fantastic!! We had booked the hotel using the TA reviews and we couldnt have been more pleased. Everything everyone has said about the hotel was spot on. 
1. Hotel is not on the nicest of streets with the Port Authority building accross the street - but was totally not of an issue as its still very safe and is only a few blocks from Times Square and all the attractions. One of the best things was the subway on the corner of the street which took you anywhere - would definately recommend to use the subway. 
2. Hotel staff are superb - Staff couldnt have been anymore helpful. We were offered an upgrade on our arrival as it was our honeymoon and were placed on the 30th floor. The staff also left us a congratulations card on our wedding and a couple of complementary cheescakes it was so nice. They were also helpful with regards how to get places and where to go. 
3. Rooms were great. - We had views to both the Hudson River and also to the Empire State building - it couldnt have been better. The beds were lovely and comfy and the maid came everyday to make the bed and also changed your towels every day or two. Being on the 30th floor also meant that we had no noise at all. There are only 5 or so rooms on each floor so you dont here a thing. 
Overall we had the best time and I would not want to stay anywhere else on my return to New York - my only concern is they will put the prices up as its so good.

title: “Fabulous”
text: There aren't many places to stay in downtown LA, (especially near the Fashion District where we needed to be) so one would expect the rates to be high because of that, but it was surprisingly affordable. It's a very nice boutique hotel that looks and feels high end. The beds are fabulously comfortable. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “Average”
text:
I actually stayed at this hotel in Nov/Dec 2003 but I could not go any further back on the date of stay option and wanted to write a review.
The hotel was okay but nothing special, I was actually a bit disappointed and was hoping it would be nicer. It was mum's 50th and we had arrived in San Francisco, stayed about three nights before hiring a car and heading to the Napa Valley. We then headed back down route 1 all the way to San Diego, stopping at Cambria, Carmel, LA and other locations en-route.
Fisherman's Wharf is the poorer part of town and going out the hotel at night was not so nice but I felt safe enough, just perhaps more alert to possible danger.
The hotel was a touch dull and had no thrills but it was clean enough and we still had fun. We had a few nice meals out at nearby restaurants at Fisherman's Wharf such as Bubba Gumps but next time I return to San Francisco, I will stay in Union Square.

title: “W Austin Rocks!”
text:
Let me start by saying I haven't stayed in a W hotel that I didn't love. The W Austin was no exception. I LOVE, LOVE, LOVED it. I live in Austin, so a W stay less than 10 minutes from home was a bit of a splurge. I used my SPG points to justify my extravagance and booked the room to celebrate an old friends 40th birthday. 
I received an e-mail offer from the GM a few days before our stay extending an offer to "just ask" and I did. I mentioned the birthday celebration and submitted a wish list that included a balcony upgrade overlooking the pool and a signature W hat for my collection. Haley, the Executive Assistant, granted all of my wishes and added a few W touches to make our visit truly memorable.
From smiling faces to birthday wishes, the W staff made us feel like VIP's during our stay. We were suprised with chilled champagne, chocolate cake with berries, and gifts that included the W hat I had previously inquired about. Our room was beautiful, understated, and relaxing. Our balcony overlooking the "Splash Pad" was awesome. That's code for the pool. I now know why new hotels limit the number of rooms they build with balconies. No one would ever want to leave. I was bummed when my friend wanted room service instead of going downstairs to TRACE for dinner, but thankfully the food was very good. We never made it into TRACE, but I do hear it is outstanding. 
For the record, I've written this review reluctantly. I'd like to keep the W Austin a secret. The W Austin is my idea of the perfect place stay downtown when I have tickets to hear music at ACL Moody Theater or want to hit the 2nd Street District or 5th & 6th Street and don't want to drive home.

title: “2 star in a 4 star location”
text:
1) check in was good. Staff was helpful and efficient. Check out staff was efficient and just over it all it seemed.
2) unlike others Hilton's, an inclusive breakfast let's you choose from bread, fruit and cereals. Hot food etc for an extra payment of about 17usd. Then you have to tip as well.
3) room is very average. No bottled eater, no coffee making facilities, the sheets are lint filled so don't think about sitting on the bed with black pants, you'll regret it.
4) bare minimum toiletries in the room: soap, shampoo, conditioner. That's it. No toothbrush, razor, shower caps, vanity packs, bath salts etc.
5) the view we had wasn't onto the avenue, it was a side street and not interesting
6) lifts were not working at night, nor was the gym open due to maintenance and there was no compensation of any sort for inconvenience. Oh, there was a letter to inform us of it.
7) and the most frustrating of all: the internet was absolutely unreliable and kept falling out. Shocking. You can't even think about doing any work here, you'll feel like shooting yourself in the face with how many times the internet falls out. In the space of 45 minutes, I had to connect 22 times. 
Good things: 
Beds were queen size and comfortable.
Location is great. Very convenient and walking distance from saks, time square etc.
Always lots of taxi's
Advise: 
For the same price, I should have booked the W. In fact the W was priced below the Hilton at the time, but we needed a twin bed set up which they didn't offer.

title: “Reasonable for Chicago Marathon runners”
text:
We book it through the Marathon travel link and it was a good value with in a reasonable walking distance to the Start line.
We checked in at 10am on Saturday morning and the staff was very nice and gave us a room already available...even though it was quite early for check in time! 
The distance to the start line is fine, it has been a good warm up to me!
The parking at the hotel is kind of expensive (39$ per day) but being Chicago a big city you can find a lot of cheaper solutions within walking distance, we parked on a covered self parking garage on Frankling ave, we booked it on line before and we paid 9$ per day! 
The hotel restaurant is nice, we did not taste the food but they were nice enough to warm up my pasta!
The pool is nice and big.
The only complain I have is that the AC/Heater fan in the room is kind of noise.

title: “NYC Birthday Trip”
text: This had to be one of the worst places to stay that I have ever experienced. The staff was kind of friendly but the place is in poor condition. The elevator is very noisy and one of our party did get stuck. The carpets were filthy. There were no "Do Not Disturb" cards to insert after they were requested. The place was loud and the parking was atrocious. We were told there were 16 spaces for 90 rooms. The beds were passable. There were not enough towels and no shampoo. The ice machine was on the first floor which is difficult considering the condition of the elevators. Enough said, go else where if possible.

title: “2 years and still love this place”
text:
I stay at this hotel 1-3 days per week, 2-3 weeks per month. I've been doing this for 2 years now. Note that I am a platinum level so I do get faster check-in and always a nice room. However, the service, amenities and overall quality have only gotten better during this time. I recommend this hotel to any traveler, business person or vacationer. Be careful of some reviewers who complain about their one time here - or for that matter at any hotel. Better to trust the reviewers who have stayed many times. 
You won't go wrong here. Modern, close to airport and reasonable.

title: “Ok, could be much better with few small improvements”
text:
We had a nice stay at the HIlton Garden Inn, and it was good value for money but were disappointed about a few things. 
First the pros:
-Good and friendly service
-Great location
-Decent size room and bathroom (actually bigger than I had expected for NYC)
-Free wifi
Cons;
-No safe deposit box in room which was very annoying, however there was a microwave and empty fridge....pretty useless. Don't know anybody who would eat in a hotel room in Manhattan...???
-Very noisy A/C unit, which when on made the room very cold and when off it got warm quickly, no happy middle
-Very squeaky elevator which we heard from our room (we complained to the reception and they were going to look into it but we never heard back)
-Elevator wait in the morning was always between 1-5 minutes!
-Came back one afternoon at 4pm and our room had not been cleaned yet

title: “70s timewarp, but great location”
text: What is it with the Starwood Group and its brown, dated, 70s-era hotels? This one had a particularly ugly lobby, with the worst artwork I've ever seen. What saves the Westin is its location (just opposite the Hancock Tower and the Cheesecake Factory) on Michigan Avenue. That, and the wonderful views if, like me, you get to stay on the 27th floor (of 27 floors). The room itself was spacious and comfortable, but the soundproofing between rooms could be better. The staff were absolutely wonderful (especially when I thought I'd lost I'd lost my phone, and they couldn't have been more helpful in trying to assist me). The restaurant looked cold and gloomy, so I didn't eat there, but there is a nice little coffee stand in the lobby, as well as a shop. This is a great place for business people and visitors alike, if a central location is important, and worth it for the views alone. Just close your eyes as you walk through the lobby.

title: “Excellant Staff, Clean Well Kept Hotel!”
text:
We had a gourp of 17 including kids and babies, so we had (4) rooms total. The hotel was well kept, clean and comfortable. The rooms were very nice and everything was in good working order. The real difference was the staff! Everyone was VERY friendly and helpful! Erica printed out several directions for me to various attractions and restaurants!They all went out of their way to make sure we had a good stay. I was very impressed as I have never seen this kind of service at any other hotel! I would definately recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Austin, it is just a few minutes from downtown and everything is easy to get to. 
I had never stayed at Hyatt pevious to this as I have a Marriott card and always leaned towards them. I found a great deal on this through COSTCO, so I thought I would give Hyatt a try! I have to say that in the future I will definately stay at anoter Hyatt and hopefully have an experience as good as this one!

title: “Loved it!”
text: We stayed here because of the price, location and other reviews we read. It exceeded our expectations. Short walk to The Alamo and Riverwalk. Large, comfortable room. VERY comfortable bed. I have trouble sleeping generally when I travel, but here I slept great. We did wonder about the parking when we first arrived, but the lot that's reserved for the hotel is just a short distance away. My husband who worries about security was actually comfortable leaving our rental car in this lot.

title: “Our Honeymoon Night”
text: My Husband and I had a Horrific Time getting married (including a mugging and a robbery), this hotel was WONDERFUL! Their prices are extremely reasonable (esp. for the quality of the hotel). The rooms were great. The staff was professional....I couldn't recommend them more!

title: “Wonderful San Francisco Experience”
text: Very nicely located near Fisherman's Wharf. Clean, recently updated. Courteous staff. Start the day with quiet and calm experience of the wharf and end the day with its full of life activities. Will stay here again.

title: “Overbooked and I would never stay here agian”
text: I am an HHonors Diamond member and I would never stay here agian. The sevice and staff were rude and overworked given the capacity over this weekend. I was over billed and I had to find the error as they could not. I was very disappointed in the entire stay. I would really vaod this place on the weekends.

title: “Clean! Quiet!”
text: We got in late on a Thursday night and unfortunately found our room right next to the elevator. However, we never heard it once nor did we have a problem with airplane noise. The best part was that it was a very clean room! No surprises! We used the Park & Fly and the transportation to the airport was efficient and on time. I would absolutely book this motel again when flying out of DTW.

title: “Chicago Business Conference - Great stay!”
text: The Sheraton Chicago Hotel & Towers was fantastic. The front desk staff was super nice and helpful. They changed my room reservation to a nice room, no questions asked, no charge. Delivered a mini fridge, no charge and quickly. The hotel was clean, comfortable and with all the accomodations you would want on a trip - free wifi throughout, great fitness center, GREAT location near N. Michigan Ave. I would definitely stay here again the next time I'm in Chicago for either business or pleasure.

title: “Conrad was elegant”
text: We enjoyed staying at the Conrad and the room was lovely. I did find the lobby to be much more simple than I expected. It bordered on austere and had no warmth to it. But the staff and location made it a good stay.

title: “Our new place to stay”
text: We travel to Dallas quite a bit and we have stayed at a lot of hotels and I have to say by far this is one has been our favorites. For the location and brand of hotel I was expecting to pay more but I only paid $59.00 for a night. The hotel is close to a lot of malls and shopping centers. Check in went great and I wish I could have gotten the gentleman's name when we checked in. He was very helpful and courteous. A true asset to the Marriott team. Our room had a comfortable king bed, 42" or 46" LCD TV, Free Wifi, coffee maker, iron and ironing board and a nice view. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “Enjoyable Place to Stay”
text:
We stayed at the Eastgate tower for 7 nights and it was a very good expierance. 
Location: It is about 5 minutes walk from the UN Embassy, 10 minutes from Grand Central Station and about 20-25 minutes walk from Time Square. We found that most of the places we needed to go to started from Time Square so if you don't want to walk there each day you can take a taxi for around $8 (includes tip) or take one of the many buses that drive buy, which costs a $2 a ride. 
Room: The furnishings were basic but everything was clean and tidy. We didn't really use the kitchen to cook due to as the New Yorkers say "Why cook when you have 36,000 restaurants" also it worked out similar in price to eat in as it did to eat out. If you are a light sleeper like me then be warned that in the summer the air con is loud and even if it is switched off you can still hear everyone elses (pair of ear plugs sorted the problem for me).
Staff: Really friendly and helpful.
Overall I would say to anyone who has the money to get a hotel closer to Time Square, however if you cannot then this is a really good alternative.

title: “Perfect Place in Downtown”
text: We were very pleased with our stay at this hotel. We were attending a concert in the 6th St. area and were primarily concerned with paying a reasonable price for a quality hotel within walking distance of the concert venue. This property met our needs perfectly and we’d definitely stay there again. The fact that it’s two blocks south of 6th St. meant we close enough to the all the action but far enough away to avoid any noise when we were in our room. It appears very shiny and new, with all that entails, including spotless rooms and comfortable beds. Our rate included a full breakfast buffet with eggs cooked to order. The only “flaw” I would offer is the room has a generic business chain feel, but that’s what we expected when booking a Courtyard.

title: “A home away from home”
text: This upmarket hotel is located in Pacific Heights, a gentrified suburb of San Francisco. Quiet and safe streets, filled with huge old mansions make, make the location great. We stayed at the hotel for 3 nights. The room (306B) had great views over the city and we could see the sunrise over San Francisco from our bed. The decor was classically elegant. There is no air-conditioning in the room, but, being high up, we could open the windows during the day to get the air in. The outside temperature was warm (25ºC/77ºF), but we never had any problem with the heat. (You probably would have to close them at night if you are a light sleeper and don't want to be woken up by the occasional noise). We had read the reviews about the hotel being too far from downtown, but this wasn't a problem for us because we had a car (plenty of street parking). At night we were going out to dinner in nearby Filmore St (full of nice little restaurants) - a 15min walk through this very nice area. Breakfast is held in a room downstair which feels like you are in your own dining room. Same feeling for the living room were you have drinks, biscuits and newspaper available all day. You can sit in the available sofas and chairs and really feel like you're home. On the downside: one night we thought we'd attend the daily cheese/wine offered by the hotel. But on that day there was noone else in the room and no drinks/cheese were served (we assumed that one probably had to ask for them,and we didn't dare).

title: “AC doesn't work and we've moved to 3 different rooms”
text: The AC is horrible in this hotel. We've moved 3 times in our 3 nights here and we don't even use AC at home. It's July in D.C. and it's hot and muggy. The hotel is in an awesome location, but it's hardly worth it if you are sleep deprived and cannot enjoy D.C. I'm contacting my company's travel department tomorrow to request that they move me to a different hotel.

title: “Shining Star”
text: I stayed here last Friday night. The online reservation was easy to make, the front desk staff was efficient and friendly, but the room was very clean and so welcoming. It was comfortable and homey. Is that a real word? The breakfast buffet the next morning had eggs, sausage, oatmeal, waffles, and a variety of breads and pastries. Of course, there was lots of hot coffee, juices and other drinks.

title: “Great location, above average hotel”
text:
I was luck enough to book this hotel through my company & got a rate of $99. So when I say the price for this hotel cant be beat, I mean my corporate price... not the full price. 
Check in was a breeze. After driving 2.5 hrs from Houston, floating the river in new braunfels all day then driving to ATX, the desk help saw that we were exhausted. She offered us both the Platinum points and a bottle of water, as we...."looked thirsty." A random act of kindness that was greatly appreciated.
Our room was a great size, full kitchen, over sized bath, etc. We were on the 10th floor and had a nice view.
Parking wise, its much easier to self park. The lot is underneath the building, and the elevator takes you right into the lobby between the RI & CY.
My only complaint with this hotel was housekeeping. We stayed for two nights... after the first night, we left for the day around 1pm and took the do not disturb sign off. Around 7pm when we came back, our room still wasnt cleaned. I called down as I only wanted clean towels, and even that process took two calls and 20+ minutes. 
The next day, I asked for a late check out as we were going to lunch and wanted to come back and relax in our room before we drove back to Hou. We packed up our stuff, went to lunch and came back around 1:15 to find the housekeeper just finishing up our room, even though we asked for - and got - a 2pm check out! Ugh... 
With housekeeping being an exception, this is a great hotel! I wish they still had a rooftop bar still. It looked like a nice place! oh well

title: “South Lake Union Location- Great Rate”
text:
We had a family wedding event in the downtown Seattle "Sodo" area the weekend of September 29th. My brother-in-law negotiated a rate of $109 a night for a Friday and Saturday night stay. This was a very busy weekend with a college football game the same Saturday night as our wedding function. To get this great rate was remarkable given other similar hotels wanted at least $250 a night and some had a two night minimum stay.
A bit of a warning there. For those not from Seattle South Lake Union is not "downtown" per say. It's a mile north of the heart of the city and not on the waterfront (there is a Marriot there as well).
So, if you need to get to a game at Safeco Field for the Mariners, or Century LInk for football it's about a $20 cab ride with tip. However, u can take the south lake union trolly and and then transfer to the light rail for much cheaper. It's doable. And, u can get to Nordstrom, Macy's etc via the So Lk Union Trolly was well.
Also lots of Tom Douglas restaurants close by.
My room was spotless and the staff was great. Fitness Center on site. Parking is $20 a night. All in all a positive experience. Cheers.

title: “For the Price...Stay Elsewhere”
text: I booked this hotel through priceline and next time I will wait for a Sniqueaway or Jetsetter deal to pop up (they only offer deals to "true 4-star and 5-star hotels). We arrived at the hotel to great and speedy valet service, but a 30 minute wait to check-in. The hotel lobby is very small so it almost felt like we were waiting in line to ride a ride at an amusement park! When we got to our room (via elevator which I think has been there since 1920), it reeked of cigarette smoke and was generally musty. We called the front desk to change rooms- they were very friendly but made me go downstairs to the front desk to switch rooms. after another 15 minute wait, I got a key to our new room. When we opened the door, the same cigarette/musty smell greeted us. We didn't ask to switch rooms because we figured the whole hotel must smell like this. Needless to say, we did not spend a lot of time in our room. Overall, the hotel location is great, but there are numerous hotels close by and I would advise you to stay there instead.

title: “Great stay, good value”
text:
My wife and I recently stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn in Downtown Denver and can report a very favorable visit. 
The staff was friendly and efficient. The location was great, but since we are from Colorado and know Denver well it worked to our advantage knowing where to stay for the event we were attending, the convention center is right next door. The rooms were clean and the beds quiet comfortable.
We paid $119 for a Saturday night through the Hilton website.
We did not eat at the resturant, so no help there. 
The only minor complaint was the $25 valet fee to park your car, you really don't have any other choice, seemed high.
Overall, we had a very pleasant experience.
That's my opinion, I could be wrong.
Skippy in Colorado

title: “A bad place to stay”
text:
my boyfriend and I had a road trip in California and decided to stay here for 1 night.it was one of our terrible experience comparing to the other hotels, because of:
noisy room,
Room was too small for two people.
AC was not working properly and it was very noisy.
you could hear your neighbors easily.
I don't recommend this hotel at all.

title: “yeah it was very good and well priced”
text:
Excellent hotel, stayed there one night, the only hitch was they checked me into a smoking room and I then had to attend the reception again to change rooms. Received a starwood guest room on the top floor.
The room was excellent very nice and clean, services was very good.
I got a full breakfast for the price of the room included $85, the breakfast was excellent and the waiter was one of the best I have encountered in the USA.
I would stay at this hotel again, and even if I was visiting LA I think I would base myself at this hotel for a few days. For the price this hotel is excellent and would rate it 4.5stars
Bed was a Westin Sweet sleeper bed, very nice.

title: “Are we talking about the same hotel? This place is depressing!”
text:
Here are the good points about this Hampton Inn:
- The staff really, sincerely try to keep the rooms clean.
- Free wi-fi internet in the rooms (didn't try it out)and free high-speed internet hook-ups in the lobby. 
- Next door to a really good Chili's restaurant, where the manager was nice enough to give me my entire dinner *free* because they didn't have one item I ordered.
Now here is what makes this one of the worse Hampton Inns I've stayed at, and why I wouldn't go back:
- I stayed on the first floor, and as I walked down the hall to my room, the ceiling was so low that I felt claustrophobic - and I'm only 5'4"!
- The hallway carpet was old and dingy, and had giant, 4 foot wide stains every couple of feet.
- The room had furniture that must have been nice once. Now it was old and scratched. Very dim - you can open the curtains for more light but then the whole parking lot can see in. The carpet was old and stained - I kept my shoes on the whole time. 
- Loud ac/heater - I turned it off or it would have woke me up at night (it kept cycling on every five minutes). 
- The room smelled funny - not exactly like smoke, but not pleasant. 
- Older TV with bad picture (but there was a nice selection of cable channels)
- You can definitely hear traffic noise like ambulance sirens going by, but I did sleep though the night despite that.
- The outdoor pool was tiny, didn't try it. Worked out in their workout room and the exercise bike didn't work. Caught the tail end of breakfast: rubbery eggs and dry biscuits. Yogurt was good though.
If you find yourself stuck here and need groceries, there's a place called Randall's (I think) that's pretty good. Come out of the Chili's parking lot heading east on the 183 access road. Make a right on Cameron Road. Drive about 2 miles, make a left on the 290 access road (after you pass beneath 290). You'll see a supermarket in a strip mall immediately in front of you - skip it! After 1/2 mile you'll see the Randall's store on your right, at the corner of Berkman.

title: “Overestimated hotel?”
text: Location is exellent, near Times Square/ theaters, good restaurants nearby (9th avenue). Our room had a magnificent panorama view over Manhattan, good size, clean, great beds, barthroom ok. But..everything is very expensive: rooms, minibar, restaurant, above all the breakfast, no buffet available, just a la carte. The breakfast was not included, but that`s, I heard, is usual in NY. We had dinner at the hotel restaurant once, and it was nothing special, except the price! Our room had a pc, but we didn`t use it. Television was ok, but the remote control didn`t work from the bed, you had to be about 1 m distance. The lobby staff was courteus and helpful. Good design in the hotel, but maybe they are trying to be too contemporary. If I come again, I will propably choose an other hotel.

title: “Good location”
text: Our initial impressions from the outside were good but less impressive once inside. The hotel is showing signs of age and would benefit from upgrading - perhaps starting with new carpets. Our room was small and our daughter had a fold out bed but we had some warning of this when booking and we did book at short notice. The outdoor garden, prominent in photos of the hotel, could also be improved by some investment - better paving and more seating for starters. Good points were the continental breakfast and the free shuttle. The location is also good - a short monorail journey from downtown Seattle.

title: “Nice hotel, great location”
text: Can't complain as long as you get a reasonable price. Clean and much less hectic than neighboring hotels. Room was bigger than average.

title: “Beautiful boutique hotel in San Francisco!”
text: I absolutely love Hotel Boheme, everything about it was perfect, the decor, aesthetic, Jerry Stoll prints adorning the walls, the colors, the friendly/helpful staff. We came here on our honeymoon and stayed in Big Sur and L.A. as well, but Hotel Boheme captured our hearts. I loved our corner view out to Columbus Ave where you could hear the hustle of the city (the noise was never a bother, it gets really quiet during the week at night). If you want something unique, romantic, perfectly located, clean, friendly and with the feel that you're staying in your own place in SF, not some faceless hotel chain, stay at Hotel Boheme, you will not be disappointed!

title: “Staff bend over backwards to assist you”
text: Clean well appointed rooms. Exceptional staff. They keep their comittmetns

title: “Bedbugs”
text: Stayed at London NYC hotel in August 2012 and brought home bedbugs as a souvenir. $1,000 and much anguish to rid my house of the problem. Outrageous. Do not stay here! The room seemed nice. The hotel seemed clean. But, it was not.

title: “Tiny...but charming”
text:
Here's one hotel that doesn't look or feel quite like any other in Manhattan. From the outside, it appears just like any other building on this quiet, unassuming Chelsea block -- which of course, is part of the fun. If you've ever fantasized about having a cute apartment on the perfect NYC street, give this a try. You get a key to the front door, and for the moment anyway, it feels like you live here.
I arrived at the hotel after an overnight flight. They not only let me drop off my bag at 8am, they also allowed me to check in at noon! I found the staff here very businesslike, but friendly and ready to help. Both my second floor room and the (shared) bathrooms were small, but squeaky clean.
Just off 8th Ave, it's a short walk to Greenwich Village and just a few blocks to the train (NYC Subway) which, after a little practice, will take you anywhere in Manhattan and beyond.
Some basic cable channels might help, but other than that, this is a terrific low cost choice for a few nights in the big city.

title: “NYC Hula Girl in SF”
text: Great value, great location, highly recommended! On arrival, I needed to change reservations from a king to double beds, high floor, QUIET room away from the street activity. Amelie at the front desk was very helpful with the room and informative about our other travel needs. The room (329) was a fair size for two people, TV, DSL internet, full bath, clean. There is also a small fitness room with four machines: elliptical, tread mill, stair master, bicycle. Coffee is self-serve all day in the lobby. The Opal Inn is four blocks from the California/Van Ness Cable Car, near all buses and streetcars, above Mel's Drive In for great American Diner food and next to the AMC movie theater. Many choices for food nearby. I recommend Swan's Oyster Depot, Post Street/ California Street: fresh seafood, friendly local restaurant, delicious. Enjoy San Francisco and get a good nights' sleep at the comfortable Opal Inn.

title: “Just an "Okay" Stay”
text:
Our room was booked over a month in advance, as the online prices are better if you pay in advance. This is the 3rd year we have stayed the Hotel Indigo for a weekend, when visiting San Diego. In years past I would have rated it a 5, but things have changed and now I would rate it a 3. Reasons for lowering the rating:
1. The Hotel has started a Friday Night DJ, not enjoyable if you are trying to get to sleep and it runs till a little after midnight. When the front desk was phoned, they said that they had moved people from another room already, but there was nothing available which would be quiet. Also, since the room was paid for in advance the Hotel would not refund any portion of the money paid for the room.
2. Breakfast menu is not near as nice a it used to be previously. We ate there one morning, but the rest of the days we went to restaurants outside the Hotel.
3. The valet parking has increased to $35/day.
Time to find a new hotel to stay when visiting San Diego.

title: “SWEET HOTEL!!!!”
text:
Stayed at the Bryant Park Hotel for one night on the 6th of August, to say this hotel is a delight to stay at is an understatement.
Easily the most professional staff I've ever dealt with, particularly the front desk staff.! Hotel and location could not be better. 
Our room was on the 14th floor, even though it was facing on to Bryant Park, we had the most amazing nights sleep, no disturbances at all, absolutely beautiful views from the room onto the park and Library (NYC public library) The room itself was completely decked out in all modern amenities. We thought the Wi-Fi was a free option, turns out its paid service, which is no big deal, might be an issue for some business users. Bathroom was superb, free Molten Brown supplies and a service to buy more if needed.( im sure the hotel would provide some free samplers if needed) 
Dinner in the restaurant was pricey but delicious, can't really fault it at all. You pay for quality everywhere. 
Overall I can't recommend the Bryant highly enough, fantastic service, location and staff.
Stay here, you wont regret it.!!!!

title: “BEWARE: Don't order breakfast!!”
text:
I'm very disappointed on this hotel. I knew that this hotel wasn't a cheap hotel so I accepted to pay what it was needed to get the best value on service and stay on the very special Valentine’s weekend, but in returned I got stab on the back by the account department of this hotel.
First of all, the king bedroom with river view that I asked for wasn't what I expected:
- The decoration of the room wasn’t even close to the ones shown on the gallery, what scam!
- The bathroom needed a retouch because the paintings and the bathroom itself was old enough for anyone to notice.
- The room didn’t smell good like you have on other even cheaper hotels.
- The hotel itself lacks on style and decorations not even valentines made it nicer.
My girlfriend and I order an expensive breakfast that had a real bad coffee and the eggs weren't cooked enough. Having a bad coffee in the morning really gets you mad especially when you are paying like if it was wine in a cup. But everything was still ok even after the big bill. The problem came 3 days after when I noticed THAT THE ACCOUNT DEPARTMENT CHARGED ME TWICE FOR THE AWFUL EXPENSIVE BREAKFAST!!!
I'm currently in the process of disputing the extra charge, but these definitely made my opinion of the high class Hyatt go down to the high kaka Hyatt. 
I would never ever put a foot on any hyatt and I don’t recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Heart of Columbus”
text:
I stayed here for concert when I was in Columbus. It's right off I-71 N/S and easy to get back on the interstate if you're going anywhere really, airport, etc.
Maybe 5 blocks or so to High Street. High Street is the main drag in Columbus. North and South. South to OSU campus. Tons of places, to shop eat, and hang out.
True, the neighborhood isn't the greatest but the hotel was really nice, super clean, helpful staff. I'm not sure why some people had trouble finding a place to eat, there's a Wendy's right next door. 
I would stay there again.

title: “Associate made it so easy”
text: I wanted to spend some alone time with my partner after I we were forced to be apart, due to work, on their birthday. I shared this with the Sheraton Associate, Cynthia when I called in to make my reservations. I cannot say enough about how special my visit was and the excellent customer service I received. Thank you Cynthia for helping me to make this time special; you are a lifesaver.

title: “Nice hotel..great staff”
text:
I just returned from a 4 night stay and was very pleased by the facility, soon to be updated but fine for me. The modest lobby was easy to navigate (my last stay was at the Venetian in Vegas) with all services easily accessed. Great amenities (warm pool, clean spa, workout options, store w/ helpful staff, nice open bar). I read complaints about room size and if you are in SD to spend your time in your room, a Phoenix Inn might be a better option. This was adequate for my daughter and I. We walked to the football game and back and were easily able to either jump on the trolley or call Flex Trans to get where we need to go.
The entire staff at the hotel were fantastic in all respects. What a nice, friendly and helpful crew. This is obviously a well managed property and I would suggest giving it a try. A weekend at La Avenida on Coronado prior to heading to the Marriott, made for a great trip.

title: “Great location, great hotel”
text: This hotel is perfect for an LA trip. It is within walking distance (1 block) of the Kodak theatre, Walk of Fame, and the Metro. I definitely recommend this hotel and would not hesitate to stay here again. The hosts were friendly, courteous and very helpful with restaurant suggestions and directions. Parking beneath the hotel seemed a bit pricey but after we realized how limited parking is in this area, we were thankful our rental was safe and secure with the 24 hour attendant. We had friends visit us in the hotel and they allowed them to park there briefly at no charge. I believe there is a visitor rate as well. Morning breakfast was fine and well attended. The hostess was friendly and kept the area clean. The hotel is located across the street from a Starbucks, a liquor store, and a convenience store which proved handy.

title: “Great staff! Perfect location!Value for money!”
text:
Coming back fro a great trip..I had ro point out this hotel because:
1. Location! 
I was able to reach everything by feet (location near to Times square, subway/ train station/ bus station only few blocks away)!!!
2. Staff 
 Allways very friendly and helpfull! The biggest plus of this Hotel. I hope the bosses of them are recogniziing this!! 
3. Value for money 
With the overprized Hotels in New York in my mind. I thought that this Hotel (for the price of doubleroom = 150 Dollar but breakfast included) would be a lower service Hotel. But it was not like that! Ennough space, very good equiped (the bed was just great) and very clean rooms! 
The only negative aspect was the really small breakfast room and the poor breakfast on its own. But at least it was included and I am not a breakfast fan ...just need coffee and a snack in the morning!

title: “Great Location”
text:
Great Hotel. Very centric, Is located in the heart of downtown. As a member of SPG, we accumulate points. The bed Is Very comfortable, it has toiletry that Is not the generic soaps on the rest of hotels. The train station Is just one block away. If you rent a car beware! The parking Is 32$ per day! There Is no cheaper option to Park around . We used the train transportation since Is quite reliable on time schedules. The Rooms are spacious, once you reserve they will ask you to upgrade for a Bay view, I knew better and did not upgraded, but yet still got the bay view. The Orange line Is just two stop far from seaport village, where there are few selection of restaurants and shops, this Is a must see. The blue line goes to old town, another place to see, which has a big selection of mexican restaurants. 
Overall Is a great service, no complaints. Rooms are very clean with a fresh smell, yet the best Is that is smoke free hotel. For the smokers would not be their First choice.

title: “Amazing trip to D.C.”
text: We would highly recommend the Sofitel for its very convenient location. It is within walking distance to the White House, Renwick museum and many other attractions plus has a metro stop with in 2 blocks. The staff was very courteous and always helpful. Our coneirge, Mrs. Van Zant, even printed a metro schedule for us as we had heard there might be major delays with repair work (we had no problems). The rooms are very comfortable, clean and large by DC standards - the food was excellent, somewhat pricey but very large portions. Recommend splitted if not big eatters. Would stay there again if ever back to DC!

title: “Not sure about this hotel.”
text:
I agree with the other reviewers: decent for business because of downtown location, but not for vacation. There is presently construction taking place inside the hotel and across the street. Also, it has a quirky entrance.
The best thing about the hotel is its employees. Everyone was extremely nice, from the doormen, to the concierges, to the front desk people, to the room cleaners. I am coming to believe that the Hyatt does a really good job of employing and training its people.
I would advise staying here for business but not for vacation because most of the major attractions are not within walking distance.

title: “Great room for the price”
text: Friendly staff and beautiful clean suite and hotel. Since the suite was on the 2nd floor above the lobby area, it was noisy during the day. Not a problem at night. I also heard a little freeway noise. Had to keep getting the room keys re programmed after the second day.

title: “Excellent location, price and service”
text: We chose to stay at the Congress Plaza in Chicago after a trip from California on the California Zephyr. The positives for us were the price and location. The many negative comments gave us pause, but after reading other comments concerning the picket line and that many of the negative reviews might be bogus, we went ahead and stayed two nights. We had an excellent stay. We would stay there again and highly recommend the Congress Plaza. It is very convenient to Union Station-an $8 cab ride took us to the door. There was a picket line at the main door but there was never an issue or confrontation. If not crossing a picket line is important to you choose another hotel. This is an older hotel and it looks it, but it is clean and well kept. It has a beautiful large lobby with plenty of places to sit. There are many other “nooks and crannies” with comfortable chairs. The room itself was large and clean. We paid a bit extra for a “lake view” and were glad we did. The Congress Plaza is well located to most of the major attractions. We walked to the Art Institute and could see most of the other major museums from our room. Based on our experience I believe that many of the negative reviews are not from people who actually stayed here, but are a result of the labor action. The Congress Plaza is inexpensive and well located. We had a great stay.

title: “Great experience”
text: I found the Hampton Inn Austin to be very comfortable starting with making reservations. I was planning a trip for 6 ladies/3 rooms. Marilyn was so friendly and worked to get our rooms together. The comfort of the beds, the friendly service at the desk and dinning room, the cleanliness of the entire hotel made our stay a great experience. Thank you Hampton Inn. I would definately stay there again. Also close to a great mall.

title: “Does what it does quite well!”
text:
We stayed for three nights over New Years in the Back Bay Hotel and really enjoyed it. If you're looking for a comfortable, modern home base for your visit to Boston with a touch of character, this is a great choice!
Pros: Wonderful bed, very clean, flat screen TV with good channel selection (typical these days, but worth noting), in-room fridge, free bottled water, free wi-fi, shower, towel warmers, modern & stylish decor, friendly yet unobtrusive staff, location allows for short walks to the financial district, heart of Back Bay, Boston Common, and Beacon Hill
Cons: "Superior" room is just a tad too small... I'd rather have a larger room and smaller bathroom than vice versa, While the location is ultimately convenient, it would have been nicer to be more in the center of Back Bay activity (hotel is on a sleepy block 2-3 blocks away from the "action").
We didn't dine in the hotel, but the restaurant menu was enticing. We didn't use the workout room either, but it looked surprisingly large.
It's not a luxury hotel, nor a truly full-service hotel, but it's a great alternative to the over-priced options right on Copley Square.

title: “Don't be afraid - Downtown L.A Rocks!”
text:
Ok...I came to L.A by myself for the first time, *just* because I wanted to go, from England. I booked myself into a more expensive hotel nearer LAX for my first night because I didn't want to travel far from the Airport in the dark and now know where I was. 
I found an amazing deal on expedia offering the Cecil hotel at £25 per night which I thought was incredible! So, after reading a few positive and negative reviews, I booked 6 nights there. 
The lobby is just amazing, faux marble or not, and the staff (especially security) are incredible and SO friendly. There are also some real characters living in the Cecil Hotel who I really got on with. 
My room was pretty much average, if a little too hot at times. My only complaint would be the really high phone bill, although that was most likely my own fault for not understanding how much it costs to call england from the USA (I spent $200 on the phone bill!). The bathroom was clean, as were the sheets, and there was plenty of room to store my things, as well as lots of choice for channels on the Cable T.V. 
Despite being alone and thousands of miles away from home, I never once felt scared, and everyone I met at the Cecil and around the area made me feel so at home I never wanted to leave. I was never without help if I needed it, and there was always somebody about to tell me what there was to do in the area. 
All in all, I had the holiday of a lifetime, by myself, for less than £500 to Los Angeles in the Summer. You don't get much better than that!
:)

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: I really enjoyed our stay at this hotel during Memorial Dat weekend. We got a deal on Travel Zoo which included free valet parking. Room was great. Staff was really helpful. Location was perfect too. Close to everything. Enjoyed the little restaurants around the hotel too for late night dinners and morning breakfast. There's also a little shopping center across the street. Starbucks too. Stayed for 4 nights and not one complaint.

title: “Super Location”
text: If you want an exceptional location in NYC, this is the place. The hotel is very clean, although the rooms are small. If you are a traveler, who needs a huge room? The price I paid was great for that area in NYC. It is in a very safe location with lots of businesses around and is about two blocks from Times Square. Many people have commented on the rude staff, but when I asked questions (and my needs are few), I was given directions in a courteous manner. I require very little as a traveler and would stay at this place again and again.

title: “San Diego Business Trip”
text: I recently stayed at Town & Country Resort in San Diego, CA on business and found the hotel and it's staf were great. The resort itself felt like you were back in time when leisure and fun were top on the agenda. I enjoyed all the lovely flowers, the pool and dining options while staying on property. I especially wanted to make a note that while dining in Trellises Restaurant both my server Pati Mukzivicz and the Assistant Banquet Chef Steven Lee were wonderful! Pati was very sweet and professional and Steven made it a point to come out and introduce himself and make sure we were enjoying our meal. It made my dining experience very pleasant!

title: “Great Location!”
text: I had a chance to stay at the SAX hotel from March 2-4 for my boyfriend's birthday. The service was excellent and hotel staff were very helpful. We had a delayed flight from California and so we checked later than expected. We not only were greeted we were also upgraded to a higher floor. So, thank you for that. The hotel's decor was very trendy and the room was clean. My only con was that our bed was not as comfortable as we hoped, and the pillows were really small for a KING size bed, but other than that you can't beat it!

title: “Perfect. Exceeded all expectations!!”
text: I am joining Trip Advisor to review the two hotels my family and I visited last weekend. Until now I have used this site compulsively, refusing to stay somewhere if the general reviews were unfavorable. I have always gotten good recommendations, and have appreciated the site so much. I am writing my first review because my experience was so good, I have to share it. I traveled with 4 teenagers: 2 of mine, 2 of their friends. My 18 year old daughter is disabled and uses a wheelchair. Before we arrived, I called to request one of the offered ammenities: a kid's see the city backpack. (I was unable to get their automated website to accept my request.) I was told they normally need a little notice, but she would try to get it for us before our weekend was over. My daughter loves bags, and was so excited to find that when we arrived 4 hours later, it was ready, in our room! We had also web-accepted a $9 upgrade offered to us if they did not fill the junior suite. (we'd booked a stuio suite) When we arrived, we were told we did get the upgrade, but I needed 2 beds for my daughter and I, and they had given me 1. The front desk receptionist (I am sorry I do not remember her name!) immediately changed our room to a junior suite with 2 beds and asked, "Would Sam like a room with a view?" (my daughter) Of course, Sam did, and we were put on the 35 floor. Upon entering the suite, we could see, out the giant windows, the empire state building...seeming to be right next door. I lived in NYC for a few years...would not have thought a view could make me gasp. This one did. What else! Well, a tiny, clean, full kitchen, with a full sized refridge, stove/oven, microwave, dishwasher!, dishes, glassware, silver, etc....amazing! Then a huge living room, with a couch that could have turned into a bed, a club chair, an entertainment center with tv and stereo, and an entire desk setup with fax that a business traveller would adore. Then a separate bedroom (with a door), two immaculate beds, extremely comfortable, and another tv. The bathroom was a very good size, and clean as well. There was also a sort of a closet/dresser area between the bath and bedroom. I have honestly stayed in a lot of hotels, in a lot of cities. This was the biggest suite or room I have ever seen, and it was spotless and tastefully done!! We stayed the weekend; I could have stayed forever. My kid's godmother lives on the Upper East Side. This suite was twice the size of her apartment!! I didn't want to let her visit us, lest she feel depressed! The location was good for Sam and I...near the dress shops we wanted to go to for a prom gown. It was very easy to get to Times Square, 5 minutes, which was great, as that is where I had my other teens stay. (Want to compare? I am writing a review for the Night Hotel also) Downstairs, next door, was Dunkin Donuts, and next to that, a 24 hour Deli/grocery with all the essentials you could need. My final comment is on the staff. Every single one of them were extremely friendly and helpful. My daughter could not stop commenting to me how nice everyone was! And, I have to say, due to the obvious disability she has, I felt like they killed themselves to make sure she was comfortable and happy. My only regret?? That I had my son and his friends stay in another hotel! I could just kick myself!! I believe because of the month of the year, we got an excellent deal on the room price, and I am not sure we could afford it each time we go if the rates go up as it gets warmer. But the Affinia will always be my first choice in Manhattan if I can go there! I would add that if you are a business traveler, and have to have an extended stay in Manhattan, stay here!! It is like a little home away from home!! The same goes for families!!

title: “Perfect for a trip to Chicago”
text:
We were meant to arrive at the Essex Inn on a Tuesday evening, but travel complications meant we arrived early on Wednesday instead. We phoned the hotel to let them know we would be there the following morning, so they checked us in on the Tuesday so that we could go straight into our room when we arrived.
The hotel provided great information about the city and even had a free shuttle bus to take guests to the main attractions e.g. the mag mile, navy pier and museums! The room was clean, spacious and had everything we needed.
As it was so hot when we visited we took advantage of the rooftop terrace and inside pool! The sun loungers were lovely! We had breakfast in the new Tribute restaurant which was very nice too! All in all this hotel is fantastic if you're working with a smaller budget!

title: “Top of the Line Service!”
text: From the moment you arrive to the moment you leave, the service in this hotel is top notch! I have never had a better hotel experience. The front desk staff makes you feel like a VIP the minute you walk up to the desk. They go out of their way to assist you with your every need. I so appreciate their willingness to give me an end room every time I request it. The rooms are modern, clean and inviting. The bed is the best feature, however; it's like sleeping on a cloud. I stay at this Sheraton on a regular basis, and I've never had a bad experience in over two years. It is my hotel of choice when in Phoenix!

title: “Average Business Hotel”
text: I stayed here for one night on a business trip. Great location if you have business that the PA Convention Center. Close to Reading Terminal. I stayed in a suite - bathroom was a bit outdated. Ovearll, room was fine. Nothing extremely special, just a nice average business hotel.

title: “You have to confirm your reservation!”
text: I chose the Francisco Bay because it locates near the Fisherman warf with free parking space, and affordable price. I have made reservation through hotels.com and already paid for the whole cost with email confirming my reservation. At the time I checked in, the fron desks said "we don't have your reservation and there is no room available!!" They said this problem can normally happen and just sent us to the other hotel with the same owner but was much more far away (quite not responsible). They said I shouldn't have any problem with the distance since San Fran is a very small city, you can take the bus around. I think that is not their business to judge! I have read from the review that there was this kind of problem before but didn't think this should happen oftenly. I think they might intentionally give my room to the other with higher rates. So if you make a reservation through internet, you have to call them and confirm it!

title: “Great Place to Stay!”
text: Just back from an incredible week in Washington, D.C. My husband and I had not taken a vacation in years, and we wanted this trip to be something special. We needed a room that was going to be close to the Smithsonian, along with a variety of attractions, such as the various memorials. We were very happy with this hotel, its location and the services it provided. It was only a couple of long blocks to the Smithsonian, the Metro entrance was located below the hotel's underground garage levels, and underneath the hotel was a shopping area (although it was pretty pricey). Our room was a "standard," but it really turned out to be a mini-suite. King-size bed, couch, chairs, coffee table, desk, etc. There were even live plants in the room which provided a nice touch. Our room was on the 12th floor (pool level), and the pool even had a lifeguard on duty. The staff was extremely helpful and friendly and the food was great (all of the meals we took at the hotel could have graced a fine restaurant for presentation and deliciousness). Special thanks to Michael in the Lobby Lounge, and Andi in the American Grill - they treated us like royalty. The concierge was very knowledgeable about the area, and answered all our questions thoroughly. I would HIGHLY recommend this hotel.

title: “Beautiful Resort!”
text: Visited Steinheimers for the day and the customer service at La Cantera Resort was wonderful. We were first greeted by Victor, who was professional, at the front drive. He took care of our cars and then directed us to Steinheimers. The bartender, Dennis, was friendly and conversable. Our drinks and food were delicious and arrived promptly. We enjoyed our stay at La Cantera Resort and we will return very soon!

title: “The Majestic--Great Place to Stay!”
text:
We arrived on Nov 20th, to warm and friendly greetings. Staff was very helpful in getting our luggage to the room (the Sunroom Suite). The room was quite large, the "sunroom" sitting area had a nice view, and the tiny kitchen was sufficient for our needs for four nights. The continental breakfast was adequate, the coffee quite good. It was also a nice treat to have coffee, tea and cookies in the afternoon.
As others have stated, this hotel has the charm of an old, European hotel.
The heating system took a little bit to get used to, but was not a big deal. The bed was comfortable, the rooms quiet. The assistant manager was extremely kind and helpful.
All in all, it was a great experience, and we plan on staying here again.

title: “Good value in a happening part of town.”
text: Comfortable and accommodating. The Ace Seattle was a good place to call home for two nights. A location slightly off the main circuit - but close to many places to experience: Pike Place Market and Space Needle, for sure. But don't miss Olympic Sculpture Park and Chihuly Garden and Glass and a walk along the water's edge. Found the room comfortable and efficiently arranged. Solo traveler so it didn't feel to small or tight. Happy to have a desk and free wifi along with sink in the room. Shared bathrooms were clean and never crowded, so it made that aspect of the Ace very easy. Breakfast is similar to many with granola, yogurt, fresh fruit and make-it-yourself waffles along with Stumptown coffee. Liked the space a great deal - a converted building with high ceilings and good feel.

title: “Shame no kettle!”
text: Previous reviewers seem to have been lucky enough to have a microwave, fridge and kettle in their rooms. Unfortunately we had none of these and the absence of any tea/coffee making facilities proved to be a real pain! We asked at reception if it would be possible to provide us with something but the response was only certain rooms had these facilities and as ours wasn't one of them it would not be possible to provide us with anything. For this reason alone we would not stay in this hotel again as a cuppa in the morning or after a tiring day of sightseeing was important to us. The local cafe and Starbucks did very well out of us! Apart form this, the hotel is in a good location, breakfast is good value and the breakfast staff very cheery. The room was kept very clean by housekeeping.

title: “Excellent place to stay!”
text: This may be the best Hampton Inn I have ever stayed in. The lobby is inviting, staff was great and they had cookies for you at your arrival. The room and entire property was clean and well kept. The breakfast was excellent and there was plenty of room to get around, get your meal and sit down to eat it. There was staff there to assist and even came to each table to offer mints! The hotel is a little off the main drag but within a mile of a lot of shopping and restaurant locations. You won't go hungry if you stay here. They also have a 24 hour "sweets" shop to get soda, water, snacks and some personal items. The hotel has an area to wash clothes if you need to. Take a serious look at this property if this location is convenient.

title: “Great Downtown Indy Hotel Choice”
text: This hotel is great. The building was transformed from a warehouse in 2006 to a very nice hotel with spacious rooms that include full size frig and stove top. The interior brick is original to the old warehouse building. Conseco Field House is 1 1/2 blocks, as well as many restaurants and shopping. Indianapolis has a great downtown. The only downside was the street people that seemed to be on most corners.

title: “Nice Rooms, great location”
text:
Stayed here Sept 2008 during a holiday touring California. Stayed 3 nights here. This hotel is ideally located for seeing San Francisco.
Positives:-
- Great location
- clean modern rooms
- reasonably priced for San Francisco
Negatives:-
- Valet parking expensive, but no different than any other hotel in San Fran.
While in San Francisco we did the following trips:-
- Boat trip to Alcratraz and Golden Gate bridge
- Trolley tour of city - defiantly worth while for seeing the different sites
- Hire car to Napa Valley. Visited Sonoma, petrified forest, Ye Old Faithful geyser and wineries. Defiantly worth doing.
- visit China town, pier 39, Coit tower
- great meal in North Beach at Calzone's on Columbus

title: “Priceline got me a good deal here.”
text: Excellent in everyway. The bell boys were calling me by name after day one of three days. Always there to help, they were the best I've seen. This place had more pilots in gym than anyplace I've ever been. The food prices were abit above most.

title: “Just okay”
text: We stayed three nights after Hurricane Sandy. The front desk had kind of a long wait, but the representative was pleasant and helpful regarding what subways were operating, etc. The first day, our room was not cleaned despite our being out from 8am-5pm. I guess they may have been short-staffed because of the storm. When we called for clean towels and fresh coffee and shampoo, they brought a lot, but no one offered an explanation or apology. We called the next morning to make sure that the room would be cleaned that day. Overall room was clean and average size for a centrally-located hotel (about the same as the Hilton and larger than Club Quarters) in New York City. We were two adults and two young children, and didn't feel too cramped, although we didn't spend a lot of time in the room. Space was well utilized and bed comfort was average.

title: “Come back to the 80's”
text:
I was stuck here for a meeting and thought the location was good and brought the family along. I called to see if they had a pack & play or cribs the person at the front desk could not answer the question? The doorman was friendly and that is where the good service stopped. The hotel was sold out for the night but it should still take less than 30 minutes to check in. The key was not welcome I like a key card myself.
We go to the room it smells like a smoker’s room and looks dingy. The bathroom was worn and tub was peeling. The bellmen had his hand out before the bags all in the room. The meeting rooms on the 4th floor are not accessible from the elevators to the rooms. You have to go down to the first floor find the other set of elevators and go up to the 4th floor. It was raining and the umbrella they gave us was cheaper than what the street vendors were selling. I had them bring up my car to get my umbrella. The meeting rooms were nice but poorly ventilated. The bathrooms in the hotel were constantly dirty. I kept telling my kids not to touch anything in the public restrooms. We also cleaned the tub with bleach wipes before we bathed my 2 year old and told the older boys to wear flip flops to take a shower. No pool was disappointing. 
The location was great.
parking was super expensive even for NYC
The rooms were a good size two double beds and a pack and play fit in the room.
Bottom line at $500 plus a night you pay for location not for amenities. I would call it a classic style Hampton Inn.

title: “Great choice!”
text: Great Location, in the charming Marina District. Good sized room, clean and well maintained. Helpful reception desk staff - we asked and got a quiet room. Plenty of good restaurants around and the Marina is only 10 minutes walk away. Would definitely return.

title: “Comfortable stay in a Great Location”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights and really enjoyed it. We had a deluxe room in the new tower building on the 10th floor. We arrived at 1pm (2 hours before the official check in time). I had booked a room with 2 twin beds and this was not ready yet which we were not surprised about. We were offered a king bed room which was ready immediately but we decided to wait for the room with 2 beds which we were told would be ready in half a hour. I had returned the car to the rental company and a good job as it costs $57 a night to park at the hotel. 
We were in the room soon after and a great room it was. The tower building is a little walk from the lobby but for the view from the room it was worth it - fab city views. A big bathroom with huge shower and bath though the safe is not big enough to fit a laptop. I had joined the presidents club prior to arrival (free to join from the Fairmont website) and this gave us free internet access.
We headed straight out and found the cable car stop right outside. This was one of the best things about the hotel - a fab location. Not in the hustle and bustle of fishermans wharf or union square but within easy reach as all 3 cable car lines stop at the hotel.
Very comfortable beds and good maid service. The hotel dry cleaned a sweater for me while we were there, done very quickly over the Easter weekend. Also very quick to come and collect our bags when we were checking out.
We had swopped our disney vacation club points for the stay so no cost to us but the location alone would have been worth paying although it is not a very personal experience as the hotel is so big.

title: “Wonderful Mission Beach”
text: My husband and I stayed here: 11/2/11, 11/9/11. The weather was not so hot but that didn't stop us. The best thing about this hotel was the location. On the beach and walkable just about anywhere for shopping, restaurants and Ralph's for groceries. The hotel is a little older but very clean and they were painting on the outside when we left. Service was good and the maids are thoughtful to your needs. There is pool and hot tub in front view of the ocean. Only draw back is that parking is not included: Cost is $16.00 a night and if you have a car, trying to find a parking space on the street is impossible. We had a second floor room 212 with view of the pool and partial view of the ocean. Bus service is a block away and we were able to take the bus into Old Town and the city, $1.25 one way for seniors and (weekly bus passes are reasonable). We would stay there again. Hope this helps.

title: “Beware of this hotel!! - Do not use your credit card to reserve!!”
text: Made a reservation for the Whitcomb for a New Years vacation. Mad reservation in Sept but looked again for better hotel rates in Dec and found a great deal at The Triton so called to cancel the Whitcomb. Got the cancellation emailed back no problem. Come March I find that my card was charged over $100 for not showing up. I have been in touch with the Whitcomb several times to remedy this and they did refund my $, but nobody really seems to care and nobody apologized. These guys suck. Their attitude about this has been incredibly poor like it is my fault I got screwed because I did not come to stay at their overpriced worn out dump of a hotel when I got a better deal somewhere else. They promised me a letter to give to the FRAUD DEPARTMENT at my bank and it has taken over ten days so far and no letter. If you really have your heart set on staying here I would recommend just burning a hundred dollar bill, stay at home, and avoid the future hassle.

title: “Convenient”
text: We selected this hotel because it is across the street from the Wang Theater. We were attending the Pixies concert there Friday night. We arrived on Thanksgiving and were approached by valet parking attendants in plain clothes....(not to worry our car was returned to us on Saturday) I read a lot of complaints on other websites about this hotel having small rooms. I took the advice given and asked to have a larger room at the front desk upon check in. We were given a HUGE room and it was facing the W. The view sucked, but it was quiet with the exception of some sirens. We were able to walk to New England Aquarium from the hotel through Chinatown. There are a lot of great restaurants surrounding the hotel as well.

title: “The price and location were decent.”
text:
It could of just been my room. The price and location were decent but there was an odor and cigarette burns in the carpet and bedspread. They could not move my room because they were sold out. There is an Extended stay sign outside as well but there is only the 1 hotel. 
 Go about a block and a half S. to the Extended Stay (5200 S. Quebec St. Greenwood Village, CO) it was about the same price, newly remodeled, very clean and the staff is very accommodating.

title: “hotel warwick and more”
