text: the hotel warwick was an excellent base for our first trip to new york. the hotel was very good value for money clean comfortable and efficient.the bell boys were particularly helpful with directions and infomation. just around the cornerthere is a fabulous little french bistro called le bon soupe great value great food and service.we found all people friendly andpolite. we would definately return to new york and use the warwick as our base again.

title: “Far above any other Holiday Inn or Holiday Inn Express”
text: I regularly stay at HI Express when I travel and most of them are similar to each other, varying a little in style and offerings. This time, however, we were really surprised and delighted. It is fairly new and the owners have taken full advantage of that. The decor throughout the hotel was exceptional with colors, designs and art work far above that of any other. The room was fully equipped and spacious - it had ample room for the twin king sized beds! And they were available at the regular rate. The staff was pleasant and accommodating and even had a cold drink ready for us when we checked in. We will go out of our way to stay at this hotel in the future.

title: “Warning Warning Warning Warning Warning Warning”
text: BE VERY CAREFUL, this place is managed by con artists, they charge your card without permission so please cover yourself, they do nothing to assist you and leave you high and dry when you need help most.. I was moved to this place from their even worse property TEMPO and put in a place where the lock on the door would not let me open it, the internet did not work, the toilet was blocked all the time, and most of all in the middle of winter it HAD NO HEATING, they did nothing except make my time in NEW YORK a misery. They moved me from over four apartments and were like terrorists in the way they did business, The staff were just plan unhelpful always telling you to write to anna well anna hardly replies.... One night i came back from the theatre and was locked out again at 2am i had to get a locksmith to open the door, i only now after two months have got that money credited. They still owe me for my deposit and refuse to offer any compensation for my stay. It is disgusting and be very very careful unless you want your holiday or business trip totally stuffed up. I ended up sick after no heating and had a terrible time in my time in new york thanks to them. Another good one is I was to move from Tempo on Chirstmas Day and they made a mistake so I had packed up and then had to wait at TEMPO to work out where i was to go, they then lied about the rooms there being available saying mine was booked then for a twenty dollars extra suddenly it was available again by them FULL ON. Happy Christmas, then the next day they send me to Third Avenue House, no one there knewq about me no keys nothing and i had to wait for three hours outside on boxing day for a cleaner to be sent from TEMPO to open my room without heat and no intercom, no phone, no tv, no internet NOTHING. THEN TO MAKE IT WORSE NO ONE BOTHERED TO TELL ME OF THE CODE TO GET IN AND OUT OF THE BUILDING SO WHEN I LEFT IN THE MIDDLE OF THE SNOWY NIGHT TO GO TO DRUG STORE I CAME BACK TO FIND I WAS LOCKED OUT IN THE SNOW ON THE STREET WAITING FOR SOMEONE TO COME HOME TO HOPEFULLY HELP ME IN, I WAITED FOR TWO HOURS.... BE VERY CAREFUL, WE ARE NOW GOING TO MOUNT A CASE AGAINST THEM TO PROTECT OTHERS AS THEY STILL REFUSE TO COMPENSATE ME EXCEPT FOR 20% OFF MY NEXT STAY.... YOU HAVE TO BE KIDDING AS IF ONE WOULD STAY AGAIN

title: “"Chic"”
text: Sheer elegance every step of the way! This is one of the best hotels I've stayed in. They even brought a fish in a bowl to our room for my toddler! Beautiful views from the rooftop with a nice heated pool to relax in. Excellent service!

title: “dissatisfied”
text: normally in the past my stay there was good,but this time it wasn't what I would call a good experience. We had to move our room because the tv didn't work and the maintenance staff had prior knowledg of this before we got into the room. After moving to the new room on the second floor I was awakened by the sound of plates and silverware clanging together it sounded like I was the kitchen itself, I couldn't go back to sleep. Then our bath tub wouldn't drain the water while taking a shower. And last the waite staff at the restaurant were not very helpful, we were told to wait to be seated,but there were about 7 open tables and seating at the bar available. The hostess disappeared and after 10 mins of waiting us and another hotel guest decided to just seat ourselves. The one bright spot was the gentleman that checked us out he did his best to make up for the short comings of others at the hotel.

title: “Convenient to Theater District”
text: Coming to NYC for shows, then this Marriott might be your choice. We were on the 30th floor in a comfortably sized room. All double bed rooms were taken in the hotel due to the Model UN Conference being held, so we had a king size bed + sofabed. Worked for our family of 4 staying with Marriott points. Recommend taking advantage of the concierge lounge for breakfast and appetizers, water, and sodas. (Glass of wine = $13!) Plenty of food making it unnecessary to eat out for every meal. Since we were in town to see shows, we never actually ate out for dinner. Appetizers before were fine and allowing us to have dessert out. Due to the conference there were extremely inconvenient waits to use the (open view) elevators. Although they have been updated since our last visit, their elevator system is still an annoyance. The hotel ran out of extra blankets as well! Seriously? We utilized the gym while we were there. It took 2 attempts to get the attendee to replace the empty water jug for free use. Couldn't help but wonder if the intent was to have me purchase the bottled water or sports drinks that were over priced and directly next to the free water. I did forget my personal headphones and they had some there for use. Although convenient and overall pleasant, I prefer closed in elevators so I would opt next time to go back to the Renaissance Times Square.

title: “Nice place when attending a convention onsite”
text:
Really good room, Starbucks coffee with liquid creamer, very clean and great service. Didn't get charged for the bottled water I drank. Bed great and the furnishings were quite nice. Internet was pay except in lobby-very bad form for women traveling -boo! 
Had a really nice stay here. Area has great breakfast options-cafe at the hotel I heard was very expensive. "Yokes" was good and so was a market called Fox and Obel. Walk into the market and head all the way to the back-there is a food bar-great oatmeal etc.
Short walk to the Navy Pier-very nice and comprehensive stain glass exhibit in doors. Right on the water which was lovely on a beautiful fall morning. Very clean area, with pleasant parks and pathway. Walked to the observatory from hotel-2.25 miles-mostly exhibits for kids.

title: “Good location”
text: Being just slightly away from Times Square was good - we had friends staying right in Times Square that found it too busy! Salisbury is also really close to Central Park which was great and only a short walk to Times Square. We stayed here for 5 nights and then changed hotels to one down in Tribeca (for no other reason than to get a different perspective of NYC). The Salisbury was clean and the $6 breakfast offer was good too, especially if you don't want a hot breakfast from a cafe every morning. The only problem we encountered was the lift broke down for most of one day - luckily it wasn't on the day we checked in/out as I wouldn't want to have to get my luggage down 15 flights of stairs. Just note that internet access is not free here. The hotel could use a bit of an upgrade but overall we were happy with our stay here.

title: “Good Choice for an overnight”
text: The room was a standard issue hotel room - a little on the small side for our family of our. However we weren't in the room much so it was not a problem. Staff was exceptional provided us with good suggestions for dining and getting SUP boards for our teens - parking reasonable - and the hotel breakfast of made to order breakfast tacos was great. Starbucks in the lobby for those jonesing for coffee. Pool is outdoors but was warm enough to swim in. RIght by the Congress Bridge, so poised for the bats nightly flight. Walking distance to the Capital and music scene and a short trip over the bridge to South Congress and Amy's ice cream! Bus ride up to the UT campus. All in all a reasonable and convenient place for a short visit to Austin.

title: “Many extras, fine service”
text:
My wife and I spent an enjoyable weekend at the Affinia 50, one of the better New York hotels we've found in its price range ($159). Our initial room in the hotel was average size for New York hotels -- smaller than rooms in most cities, but then no one goes to New York to sit in a hotel room. Unfortunately, it also had a heater that could not be turned down, but the staff promptly upgraded us to one of their massive suites (which included a small kitchen and large sitting area). This is more room than we needed.
Since most visitors probably won't have this sort of luck, it's worth mentioning that, even with a smaller room, this would have been a very pleasant place to stay. The location is excellent: close to the east side shops and restaurants, but only a (brisk) 20 minute walk over to the Broadway theaters. It has a well-equipped fitness center (2 eliptical machines, 2 treadmills, a stairmaster, some bikes, and various weight machines) that is open 24 hours a day. There is no lobby on the first floor, but the second floor has two large sitting rooms, with books, big screen TVs, books, and a gas fireplace -- a very nice place to sit and read the newspaper before setting out. There's also a small room with computers (though the price for internet access is a bit steep).
My wife tried the buckwheat pillow and liked it quite a bit. 
The staff was quite helpful. In addition to the upgrade, the manager bailed us out when we somehow managed to enter a combination into the closet safe that neither of us could remember (I'd always wondered what would happen if you did this), and a broken bed lamp was repaired, without our mentioning it, by housekeeping. The hotel also makes various packets of maps and guidebooks available for those interested in shopping or in museums, while runners can get packet which includes a pedometer along with the maps. Internet connections are available in the rooms and, helpfully enough, there was an ethernet cable in the desk drawer.
I had only one very minor complaint: though there are coffee makers in the rooms (always a welcome feature) and while there is a pod coffeemachine available on the second floor except when breakfast was served, the only way to get coffee during breakfast (which will set you back $15 -- we opted for a coffeeshop down the street) is to pay $3.50 a mug. But with Starbucks infesting the neighborhood, this wasn't a major problem.
We'd certainly stay here again.

title: “Will Be Back!”
text: My husband and I booked this hotel off of orbitz and got a great deal. 99.00 plus tax. When checking in we were allowed to check in early, the agent was extremely nice. She had asked if we have been there before and we told her no, we recieved 2 $10 freeplays as well as breakfast for 2. Such a great deal that was 40.00 there since the breakfast was 11.99 per person. The room was very clean and nice. Flat screen tvs, comfortable beds, quiet rooms and spacious. We will be returning here for our next day. An added bonus we attended the tigers game and it was such a quick walk to and from the ballpark!

title: “Unforgettable, romantic stay”
text:
Edgewater is built out onto a pier, so it really is over the water. The rooms are lodge decor, with a cozy fireplace. If you upgrade to the nicest rooms, be aware that the higher room numbers are out farther, are completely unobstructed. And you should upgrade because the views are amazing. Plus the soaking tub was lovely, as was the newly decorated bathroom. The room decor could use some upgrading--the bedspreads are in need of a change. 
Absolutely do eat at the restaurant--great food, beautiful decor, right on the water. And we enjoyed the nightclub afterward, which had good live entertainment. Breakfast was great too.
The one negative? No free internet which drives my husband nuts.

title: “Never again”
text: First when look at the rooms online they make them look better than what they are. The lobby is nice and cozy but as soon as you go up to your room the halls are like a ghost town. When we opened the door to our room I was disgusted, the room was so depressing with one small window. I regret not taking pictures of this place. The walls were dirty, the ceiling in the bathroom was cracked and the bathtub was rusted. EWE, let me tell you, i got 6 bedbug bites on my right leg from this place. We stayed in the room for about an hour, i literally almost began crying from how depressing and dirty this room was. I got on my phone and googled other hotels and found Park Central for $30 cheaper. We checked out of the hotel and spent an additional $480 for the new hotel. We didnt care about the extra money we had to spend, we were on vacation and i refused to stay in a dirty room. FYI the staff offered to change our room but I refused to stay there. Im not the type of person to bash a place but I had no choice to write up a review, i just dont want others to be fooled about this place.

title: “Charming Romantic Unbelievable Service!”
text: We stayed only one night at this beautiful hotel and can't wait to go back. We bought the "chart your course to romance" package and talk about romantic! From the very minute we arrived in valet parking, we were treated like royalty. Fast check in service, bell service, concierge service, what ever our hearts desired! They even upgraded our room, which, by the way, was already a star! I would recommend this hotel to the president! Absolutely beautiful in all ways, service, cleanliness, beauty, room service, everything was fabulous! Thank you so much for making what we thought was going to be a special time, into one of the most wonderful we have had at any hotel we have stayed. Everything was perfect!

title: “What a fantastic hotel!”
text:
We had such a fantastic stay at this hotel. It was clean and nicely decorated. The hotel has a restaurant and a small market to purchase snacks. Located in the Century City/Beverly Hills area, it is in a safe location that was a great starting point for virtually anywhere in the city. 
What pleased me most about this hotel was the wonderful valet. Valet parking here was only $15 dollars a day, much cheaper than many other hotels, and the valet gentlemen could not have been nicer. They kindly and courteously spent time going over maps with us to help us find the best routes for travel. They quickly brought our vehicle to us and courteously opened doors. When we would leave the hotel, they knew us by name also. What a pleasure it was for us to get such a helpful team of people from a hotel that only cost us $200 a night. The service there rivaled much more expensive accommodations we have experienced elsewhere. We have nothing but high praise for this hotel. We would definitely stay here again, and feel that we had great location, excellent service and fair price all rolled into one at this hotel.

title: “Location Location Location!”
text: Stayed at the JW Marriott over Easter Weekend and it was terrific. Three is really nothing special about the hotel - it's clean & comfortable as you'd expect. A pool - as any parent will attest - is a must when you are traveling kids and the JW pool does not disappoint - It was the perfect way to wind down after a long day of sightseeing. The best thing about the JW - it's right beside the White House and the Mall and pretty much everything you came to DC to see. My only complaint is the cost of parking - $50 to park overnight!!!! I know I know it's DC - but still... wow! There is cheaper parking in the neighborhood - There's a PMI parking garage around the corner that costs about $25 for 24hrs so do your research!

title: “BED BUGS!!!!!! DO NOT STAY HERE!”
text: So we came here on a school trip with 25 high school kids. The first night one of the rooms had be bugs and they had to change rooms at 3 in the morning. A day later they tested the room and it came back positive for bugs. That same next day a girl in our group in the next room had bites and rashes all over her. They were already in a tiny room. They then got moved into a room that couldn't even fit 2 suitcases. We only had 1 towel and we called down. We didn't get them. After calling 5 times and 3 hours later we got towels. This is honestly the grossest hotel. DO NOT COME HERE!!!!!!!!

title: “Hated it”
text: We Stayed at this hotel on two occassions ,water damage to ceiling and ceiling paint/stucco was falling off,room smelled awful,room was filthy.2nd stay was for pool for our kids but water smelled horrible , requested better room than 1st one , but this one was crawling with spiders and roaches, bed linen was burned with cigerettes,bed was old and torn and actually had spiders crawling out of materiel, I could not sleep at all as I was up killing bugs so they wouldnt be crawling on kids and hubby while they slept. internet didnt work for crap , next day we went to pool and had 3 couples consuming beer in the pool area , people in the pool who were not guest or hotel occupants , one man and women there were drunk but in the pool told me they were living in a tent behind the hotel, scary and disgusting that the pool was probably their bath time. We wont be staying there again.

title: “A nice weekend stay”
text:
checked in last weekend ...nice location, room and bed were great. Air conditioning was impossible to control ... either froze or burned up all night...Bathroom tad bit small. Love Paulette's...disappointed that roof top bar closes at 9 on Friday night and they (all the bars and restaurants had never heard of St. Germain ??)
Breakfast included but only in restaurant ...champagne at check was quite in nice, and port at turn down...but Lindt truffles for $270 a night in Memphis ?
Loved the 24 access to the well equipped and spacious gym ...
friendly service.

title: “Quiet Please!”
text: Went for business with a little fun too. This hotel is directly on the Riverwalk, which is worth the boat ride. The hotel is also attached to a mall with a Macy's and a ton of restaurants. There is a Starbucks in the lobby -- all the amenities a traveler could ask for. However sleeping was not the easy part. Even though I was assigned to a "sleep zone" area they gave other rooms in the same area to families, the one across the hall from me had 5 people in their room and the door banging as they went in and out of their rooms went on all night. My air condioner kept shutting off (which could have helped block out the hall noise) and never reached anything less than 75 degrees. A very nice engineer checked it and promised it would not shut off again, but it did. Three nights of a hot room in a city where the temperatures outside was over 100 degrees.

title: “Very well located”
text: This was our first visit to NYC, we arrived full of expectations about the thrill and liveliness of the city and we were not disappointed. The hotel was clean, comfortable and very airey. It is well equiped with a drinks cabinet and snacks. It also has a safe for your valuables but the best thing was the location virtually a stone's throw away from Time's Square which is always buzzing with tourists and street entertainers and brightly lit up in neon lights. Noise is no problem as the windows are very well sealed so you are guaranteed a good night's sleep and I assure you in New York City you will need a good night's sleep because you'll be constantly on the go. Checking in and out of the hotel was no problem as the staff were very friendly and cordial and the concierge desk very helpful when inquiring about tours, restaurants and tickets for the theatre. Such is the location of the hotel that we were lucky enough to see a concert by Taylor Swift and her interview by ABC from our room window. All in all when we next visit New York in the not so distant furture we would not hesitate in staying at this hotel agin

title: “No room service on Sundays!”
text: The hotel room was very clean. A little small since I expected a bigger room since I reserved an Executive King. I guess I'm comparing to the room that I had at another hotel on West 51st between 6th/7th Aves that I stayed at 2 weeks before. I don't think the thermostat in my room was working. I had to turn it down so I will not suffocate or have a heat stroke! It's too hot! It's strange to have the alarm clock situated across the bed next to the flat panel TV. Totally weird! When I called the Front Desk to have it moved next to my bed, she offered to give me a wake-up call instead which is unacceptable because I like snoozing my alarm. So I insisted on having someone move it (wires were all tangled behind the cabinet). My flight arrived at around 8pm on a Sunday night. Checked-in & called for room service to find out that they don't have room service on Sunday evenings. I could pay for a service but I decided to brave the cold, windy night & walk to nearby DB Bistro Moderne to have a decent meal. All these are minor but after a long flight, these things become an irritant & inconveniece. Things settled down the next 2 days. The Front Desk staff needs some improvement. Sometimes it feels like they just want to answer 1 question. The Front Desk staff at the West 51st St hotel knew my name on my 2nd day. Those are nice little touches. I must say that the bed was comfortable & the bathroom amenities were excellent. I'm glad that I paid what is considered an average rate for NY standard when I booked this hotel. For the price that I paid, I can recommend this hotel to friends. But nothing more. Thanks hotel.com!

title: “Convenient and Comfortable”
text: While not on the ocean, this Marriott is still very convenient to the water as well as downtown, Qualcomm stadium, San Diego State University and is conveneitnet to all the major highways. The hotel itself is very quiet and comfortable. The concierge lounge is a lilttle small but the staff are very accomodating. The rooms are spacious and the room staff are very efficient. The pool is very nice and there are private cabanas. Another nice touch is workout equipment outside the exercise room in the fresh air. Front desk staff is very friendly and efficient. There are a number of places to sit outdoor both in and out of the sun. The rooms are very quiet. Overall a very realxing and comfortable property.

title: “Excellant Value”
text: This hotel was excellent in all details. The rooms were clean and a large size. The buffet was adequate to start the day. The staff were efficient and very helpful especially Nick Dorsey the manager on duty. We stayed for 3 nights and the hotel is in a very nice area and all the major sites are easily accessible.

title: “Third year we have returned!”
text: My husband and I have stayed at this resort the last 3 years in a row for one of our annual staycations. The reason we return year after year is due to the friendly, helpful customer service, fantastic views, comfortable and clean suite style rooms and tropical pool area. Highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Okay Hotel - Comfy Stay”
text:
I read all the posts before booking this hotel with my ccard points. I found them to be very accurate. I agree the lobby is very small like a foyer with a desk. Also, agree the workers were all friendly. Fairly close to Metro stop and DuPont circle area. Rooms were comfy.
This was a quickly planned vacation and I was trying to keep expenses down.
So, I was disappointed that when I called to ask if I could get the breakfast of $1 promotion it was not available since I booked with points. While I understand, I love breakfast and would have so enjoyed it before a full day of sight seeing. However, I was given a coffee pot for my room and the lobby coffee was really top quality. Next trip to DC, I think I will look for hotel with breakfast included.......I missed it. I usually book hotels that include it.

title: “An oasis of civility!”
text:
After a grueling day of moving (what other kind is there?) and not wanting to sleep among stacks of boxes at our new home, my wife and I chose to reward ourselves with room service and a night at the nearby Cedarbrook Lodge.
We’d eaten at the Copperleaf Restaurant in the Lodge several times and had been impressed, both with the food and service in the restaurant and by the beautiful property itself, so we decided to look into the cost of a room. 
We were pleasantly surprised that the Cedarbrook Lodge is very competitively priced. And because a day lifting boxes full of our prized possessions had left us tired and sore, the over-sized soaking tub clinched it for us. 
This beautiful property was built in 2002 as Washington Mutual’s conference center. It became a hotel following WaMu’s acquisition by JPMorganChase. A desk clerk told us the Chase folks, being East Coast types, had no interest in keeping such a property so far away, so it was reincarnated as a hotel as September 2009.
And I’m ecstatic!
Our guest room, a Deluxe Queen, was not particularly large at 276 square feet, but was very well laid out. Ten-foot ceilings made the room feel more spacious. In addition to the usual retinue of amenities, rooms have very large desks that provide plenty of space for working (if you’re so inclined). The queen bed in our room was flanked by a chair and ottoman that made for more comfortable TV watching than sitting up in bed.
Bathrooms all have over-sized soaking tubs that were so exquisite my wife is already talking about adding one to our new home. (Despite the favorable room rate, our stay may have turned out to be quite expensive after all!) Amenities are by Green from Natüra, a line of soaps and shampoos I first encountered at the Hotel Avalon in Portland. They’re designed to minimize the impact on the environment, including the inevitable waste caused by the short-term, single-use nature of hotel soaps.
Because we were too tired to change into nicer clothes and trundle to the restaurant, we had room service bring dinner to us. We shared a Market Greens salad, Alaskan Black Cod fish & chips, and fromage blanc for dessert, along with some well-deserved Pinot Gris. All items were well prepared and delivered quickly.
Those who are inclined to wander from their rooms have a variety of options. The bar is equipped with a pool table, there is a fitness center, and the grounds themselves have numerous walking paths. Even if the weather isn’t the best for leaving the building, the hotel has generous common areas called “Living Rooms.” All offer light snacks 24/7. Many include fireplaces and are wonderful for sitting and talking, reading a book or surfing the ‘net, or just drinking in the mountain lodge atmosphere.
A continental breakfast is included each morning. Smoked Pacific Northwest salmon augmented offerings of the typical continental breakfast items. What an unexpected delight!
Staff was uniformly wonderful: professional, courteous, engaging, making us feel like welcome guests instead of “paying customers.”
As a bonus, it’s close to SeaTac airport. Businesspeople who tire of the typical airport hotel (and who doesn’t?) would be doing themselves a favor to look into this oasis of civility.

title: “Excellent hotel!!”
text:
Spacious room, very, very comfortable bed, attentive service and a hotel staff who would do everything they can to help.
I could not recomend this hotel highly enough!!

title: “Old world elegance in NYC”
text:
The Pierre is classic old world elegance. From white gloved elevator operators, impeccable staff, and excellent service. The hotel underwent an extensive renovation a few years ago. Like all older hotels, there is only so much room you have to work with. That said the rooms are small and so are the bath rooms (at least in the standard size room that we had). Of course this is NYC and most rooms are on the smaller side. Not spending a lot of time in the room, this is no big deal to me.
From the moment I entered the hotel, I felt like I was stepping back in time. In todays world, what you pay generally does not equate to good service, here it does. I don't require much, but I do expect friendly staff, quick response to room service and house keeping requests, and overall professionalism. They hit the mark on all of these.
The accommodations were comfortable, good lighting, and it was clean. The location is excellent, across from Central Park and by some of the best shopping in the world.
I tend to lean towards hotels that are a little more contemporary, but I would definately recommend staying here and would stay here again.

title: “very basic make sure you get price before you go in writing”
text: this hotel was basic. we never stayed in the room long and glad we didn,t . we had luckily enough our laptop with us wich had the email confirming the price we agreed and the number of people staying if we didn,t we would have to pay more. the wee woman that everyone says is so nice wasn,t so nice when we had the evidence in front of us. the room was very basic , not iron and no laundry facillity . we found a wee beasty in the bed and the carpet was black didn,t trust the coffee maker to make coffee. yes the donuts were great thats all

title: “Security concern”
text:
First the bad:
My room was on the 20th floor facing the back, so I had a view. The first thing I noticed was a balcony, so I checked it out. The door to the balcony didn't have a lock on it. Just push and it opens. The bad thing is that the balcony isn't private. Other rooms have doors to the same balcony. I reported it right away and the desk clerk said he would have maintenance check it out, but I stayed two nights and a lock never got installed.
The clerk wrote my room number on the key card with a permanent marker and the key card had the name of the hotel on it. So if I lost my key, someone could have gotten into my room.
There were no towels or soap in the room. I dialed "0" expecting to get the front desk, but no one answered the phone, so I went downstairs. They gave be bath towels but they didn't have hand towels or wash cloths. I don't know if the clerk even knew what I was asking for. (I know some countries don't use these items but I would expect them in NY.)
There was a small desk that I wanted to use, but the only chair was a big old "easy" chair that actually blocked the desk. I had to move it to use the desk, but the seat was so low I had to use the comforter and a pillow so I could sit high enough to work at the desk.
Now the good:
I arrived at 12:30 p.m. and the clerk checked me in early. He was very nice.
The room was supposedly one of the "renovated" rooms. It had fresh paint and bathroom tile. However, the carpet was old and there were no fixtures in the bathroom (except handicap rails). The toilet paper roll was propped up on the handicap bar and I had to put my soap and shampoo on the floor of the shower.
The bed and the bedding were very nice.

title: “Great option”
text:
We stayed at the Edison Hotel in January, a kind staff( yes at the elevators if you don't show them your room key and just pass by, they ask for it in a not so cute way, but its for your safety), clean, nice lobby, and we got a recently upgraded room (very nice room for the price- no bedbugs, no mold, no night noise) They were remodeling some rooms on our floor but we didn't had any problem with noise or whatsoever (although we were away from the hotel all day ) Location= superb (20 meters away from Times Square) Price= excellent. Would definitely book Edison's at our next trip to NYC.
(note for the internet people..WIFI is 9.99 for 24 hours, you can get free wifi on a starbucks right across the street)

title: “Pleasant Stay”
text: We were happy with our stay in the Marriott. We received our stay as a gift from friends and I feel the regular cost of $300/night may be a bit high for the quality. There was nothing wrong with the hotel, but it wasn't overly wonderful. We loved the atrium view but found the elevators to be slow and the system a bit difficult to use. They told us when we checked in there were problems. The view from our window was magnificent looking directly onto the center of Times Square. Yes, you heard the police cars and ambulances day and night, but you are in the middle of NYC and it added to the excitement. While we didn't eat in a restaurant there, we did buy some drinks and ended up paying $10 for 3 drinks...get them before you head into the hotel! There is no breakfast (we knew this, but in case you are wondering...) We had a problem with the safe which was immediately taken care of and the housekeeping were friendly when we were still in the room. The furnishings were high class, tho the cleanliness was not. I was sorry to find empty water bottles, candy wrappers, etc under the beds. I hope they cleaned after our visit. Overall, a satisfactory experience.

title: “Great big city hotel”
text:
This is a great hotel with a great location and extremely helpful staff.
Rate was high at $869.50 for two nights and was upgraded to 41st floor facing Times Square.
Elevators are very different but I'm sure they have researched it and this is the fastest method to get elevators to all the floors.
Gym is the BEST hotel gym I have ever seen. Treadmills have fans on them, hooked into cable television, they even have partner stats if you are running with someone on the next treadmill.
Problems would be that its a huge hotel and takes time to get around (walk to room, elevator system, etc.). 
Bell desk was fantastic since I had boxes incoming and outgoing and cases and laptops, etc., etc., etc. They were great and very quick in getting items to room and retrieving items I shipped out. 
Room service quick but as you would expect very expensive. 
Highly recommended if you are on a business expense account.

title: “Excellet Hotel and great shopping close by”
text:
Stayed at the World Center Hotel for 5 night. Nice large rooms and great location in Low End. If you don't stay in Low End you might miss out on some great places like Battery Park, southern bay area and Department store 21th Century Outlet... EXCELLENT!!!
If you don't want to spend a whole lot (NY prices) on a nice hotel this is the place to stay.

title: “Great location”
text: Rooms are large clean, and comfortable with upgraded linens and furniture. Quiet and excellent service from staff .Location is excellent for walking to "Mall" areas. Plenty of food and shopping in area. Valet parking worked great for me, they took my car and I picked it up 3 days later when I left!

title: “Would not stay anywhere else but here”
text:
We stayed here our first night in SF and I regret not staying here for the remainder of our trip. 
Service is unparalleled and the location is perfect. Although they say it's in SOMA, it's just a 2 minute walk from Union Square's BART transportation and the Westfield Mall. 
The lobby, bar, and hotel restaurant are upscale chic. The 6th floor has a club concierge lounge that I highly recommend upgrading to. The lounge provides complimentary drinks, mighty leaf tea, cappuccinos, and appetizers. Not your typical mozzarella sticks, but items such as beef wellington and spanakopita. Look for Luis in the lounge. He's the friendliest person ever and really makes you feel at home. 
Also for such a nice hotel, the price is more than affordable. 
I would definitely stay here the next time I'm in town!

title: “Not worth the money”
text: My boss sent us to New York for our Christmas present. Great boss huh!!!!!! Because he booked it so late there were not that many nice hotels available for that particular weekend so he thought because he was paying so much it would be really nice. It was ok. The room was very nice and the bathroom was clean. But for the money I was expecting something GREAT. It was an ok location if you are visiting for the first time or doing all the touristy things because you are close to grand central station.

title: “I'll take my history at a museum, please.”
text:
Traveled to Chicago for two nights on business, and arrived at the Palmer House around 10pm. HHonors Desk was closed, but was checked in quickly nonetheless. 
This hotel boasts that it is the oldest continuously operating hotel in the country. The first room I was checked into must have been the oldest continuously operating room in the hotel! It looked like it hadn't been renovated in about 20 years (the green tile in the bathroom was quite charming... really.) and had a lovely view of an A/C compressor that was bigger than my room! Went back to the reception desk, and asked if an HH Gold upgrade to the exec floor upgrade was available. Was upgraded to exec floor, to a room with one double bed. Room was nicer than the last one, but you couldn't have parked a Yugo in there with enough room to open the doors! 
Stay was pleasant enough afterwards. A bit noisy during the night. Lobby is undergoing renovations. Exec lounge was fine. Not bad for a business trip, but next time I'll be staying somewhere that has a bit less "history" in my room!

title: “Great Spot”
text: Located in a nice neighbourhood with alot of things within walking distance. The room was a good size and nicely laid out. The walk in shower was comfortable and everything was clean. Staff was friendly. The free parking was a perk as I'm used to paying $30+ for parking at hotels in Seattle. They were just about to open a restaurant when we where there and this would definitely be a plus as it is nice not to have to go to far for breakfast. However, if you do go out for breakfast make it Toulouse Petit! I would stay again. Good value for the money.

title: “Clean comfortable and very good value for union square location”
text: Stayed 3 nights on basis of TA reviews May 11, very happy with this hotel. Had upgraded 'queen' room which worth it, very good value for central SFO, where alternative is to pay nearly double for modern hotel soulless room. Didnt see standard rooms but our facilities were as per hotel web site, quiet comfortable room where we were able to fully recover from jetlag. View of city not very scenic but much better than a ventilation shaft/light well which has been our experience elsewhere. Room had ceiling fan, cant remember if there is any aircon, but opening windows are a bonus in our view. Hotel and rooms are well used but interesting (murals on walls), pretty basic furnishings but all spotless. Staff very helpful but sometimes busy, unsurprising in a small hotel

title: “Old world elegance, contemporary service.”
text: In today's world of budget cuts and penny pinching, it is refreshing to see a hotel that maintains its integrity of service. A superbly well rounded upscale product, complimented by sincere good service. My hat is off to this oasis of elegance in this dessert of corporate, executive properties.

title: “Great hotel at a great location”
text:
Very nice hotel and a perfect location. Free internet! The internet is through an ethernet cable, but who cares if you can't carry your laptop around your room. I didn't try the complimentary breakfast, but you are in Chicago. Get out of the hotel and try some of the best food in the world.
Footsteps away from the CTA red line. When you walk out of the hotel the stairs to the red line train are directly to the right. If you are familiar with riding the train in Chicago, it is perfect. If you are there to see a Cubs game, you get on the northbound red line train, and get off at the Addison stop which drops you off at the stadium.
The hotel's entrance has an unloading area on Grand that is convenient for pulling into for unloading your group and luggage. An attendant will ask if you will be valet parking. Valet is $40 per day with in and out privileges. Self-parking is $26 per day after you have the parking ticket validated at the front desk. The regular price on the sign in the garage is $35 per day. The self-parking garage is connected to the hotel with entrances on both Grand and Ohio. If you are planning on parking your car and leaving it during your stay, this is the way to go. If you do self-parking, ask for the front desk to validate your ticket before you leave. When it is time to depart, you'll then insert your card into an automatic payment machine just outside the lobby to the right that you can pay with a credit card or cash.
When I go back to Chicago, I am definitely going to be staying at the Hilton Garden Inn - Downtown.

title: “Spectacular!”
text: This hotel had one of the friendliest front desk employees that I have ever encountered. I wish I noted her name but we checked in about 8:00 on Mother's Day, May 13,2012. She was genuinely a sweetheart! The hotel is immaculate, the beds comfy, the suites spacious and a wonderful breakfast!

title: “Classy New York”
text: We recently stayed at Algonquin for 1 night and loved the hotel. The location could not be better and the staff was very attentive, especially as we were travelling with an infant. We were upgraded to a king-size bed room- the room was indeed very small, but impecably clean and functional. The lobby and the bar area are gorgeous- easy to travel back in time and imagine how New York must have been...

title: “Love this Hotel!!”
text: We have stayed at this hotel twice in the last year. We were staying at this hotel last summer when the black out hit. The staff was incredible!! Our elevators worked because the hotel has a generator for emergencies. You can not beat the location right in the heart of Times Square. The rooms are large and comfortable. I highly recommend this hotel!!

title: “Great stay Oct 11th thru 14th”
text:
We stayed at this hotel Thursday to Sunday. I was a little apprehensive as some of the reviews were not very favorable. We had such a good experience that I couldn't believe some of the reviews!! I had read previous reviews and saw that Mary Mastrobuoni the Concierge and Shawn (sorry don't remember his last name) at the Club Lounge were exceptional employees. Well.... I totally agree and in fact would go as far to say they make the stay at this hotel!!! They are very lucky to have such good employees that truly enjoy their job and because of this I would definitely stay there again and would recommend it to others. When I first arrived there, since I had read previous reviews, I went up to Mary and told her I had read very good reviews regarding her help to customers. She was very gracious and asked my name also. The next day I went to go and ask questions about a tour and she remembered my name. Wow, I was impressed!! Also, I had seen some terrible reviews about the Club Lounge and it not having very much to offer. Well, I disagree as the breakfast was great and Shawn was as far as getting anything we needed and went out of his way!! In fact, we had said something about needing a frig for medication and he ordered one for us. He then promptly called us a little later to make sure we had received the frig. I told him not yet so he said he would check on it. Not 10 minutes later he was at our door with a frig. Now that is service!!! 
Our check in was very prompt and good also (sorry can't remember the employees name). 
All in all I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “FAB-UL-LOUS!!!”
text: Fantastic 5 day break in the Big Apple.... My husband and I loved every minute, the location is literally off Times Square, bedrooms were about the right size, the beds were v comfortable and clean, hotel itself is v elegant & has a vintage feel about it - beautiful establishment, staff v helpful, concierge most knowledgeable. Plenty of excellent places to go for a meal & also smack bang in the middle of the theatre district. Awesome!! Thank you so much for an amazing holiday. I cannot wait to return

title: “Lovely property and respectful of many religions”
text:
For many years, my husband and two children have vacationed around the US during the holiday season. Canyon Villas is THE FIRST to offer the lighting of Hanukaah candles, for those of us who don't celebrate Christmas. We are so appreciative of this! Thanks, Marriott Canyon Villas, for helping us celebrate our holiday traditions away from home. 
We also greatly enjoyed the beauty of the grounds, proximity to JW Marriott, lovely units and view, and quiet and peaceful atmosphere. We've had a great week!

title: “Just downright excellent”
text:
I'm just piling on here, but the service was impeccable.
Danny at the front desk, and especially Joel, the bellman, were as helpful as it gets. Joel went out of his way to find out if the LBJ Library, which is under renovation, would be closed for my visit, and then he set up an appointment for me with a researcher for a project I was working on. 
Rooms are comfortable, clean, well-appointed. Lobby is luxurious. It's everything you'd want a hotel to be. My only fault would be with the unpredictable wifi connection which seemed to cut out on me frequently. 
Downtown Austin and 6th Street, on the other hand, is a little seedy for my taste. There are restaurants nearby and I'd hit one of them before traipsing up to 6th Street again looking for food.

title: “Great marriott!”
text: I stayed here labor day weekend and this hotel was packed! A game was going on and so was a local convention, but still all the hotel staff were very friendly. I lost my work badge and one of the employee's came running up to hand it back to me. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “My favorite DC hotel when on business”
text: Within walking distance from Union Station and the Capitol, it is the perfect spot for those conducting business on the Hill. The rooms are efficient but chic. Their in-room cash bar set up is one of the best. If you are not in the mood for a full course meal, head to the bar and let the bartender recommend fantastic wine and cheese pairings.

title: “Nightmare”
text: Where to begin...... no a/c in the lobby or breakfast area (temps outside were in the 90s)... spoiled fruit and stale doughnuts for breakfast..... two lights in bathroom, only one worked... bathroom was not thoroughly clean (hair in sink).... not enough hot water for one shower (there were two of us in the room).... curtain rod was propped on window ledge, so when the curtains were closed the rod fell down.... extremely noisy, as I could hear conversations in hallways and adjoining room... .. maids left bags of garbage on and near the tables in the hallways..... odor in hallways was unpleasant.... it was a nightmare... I booked thinking it was a Hampton Inn.. would not have booked otherwise... am happy to know it is not a Hampton Inn.... oh, and did I mention that there was a tennis ball sized hole in the twin-sized (bed was double-sized!) comforter?

title: “Way over priced”
text: The rates are way overpriced. Equivalent to New York 4 star hotels. The cable has maybe 20 channels, rooms are old and small. Location is just the southern end of Chinatown. It is close to the subways, so you can go visit places you would rather stay. The in-room air conditioners sound like your sleeping in a wind tunnel. Wireless internet is spotty at best. Could get work done at night in the room.

title: “Simply the Best!”
text: Overall, we had a wonderful experience at this hotel! It cannot easily be seen from the road, but is easy to access right off of I-10. We stumbled upon this location a couple of years ago and have come back time after time. The clean rooms, affordable price and outstanding service make this choice an easy one. On this recent visit we rented the small conference room for a family gathering and the staff was great! Free coffee and water service and free room set-up/clean-up all for a really great rate when you also book rooms at this location. We had an enjoyable time and will rent the conference room for future small gatherings. All of our expectations were exceeded during this weekend stay and the staff was exceptionally attentive and personable. This location will be our choice for accommodations for all trips to San Antonio!

title: “Room with a view in a great hotel!”
text: Hotel 31 was fabulous!! I had a nightmare beforehand trying to find somewhere cheap, in a good location and where the reviews were good (it appears there are some awful hotels in NYC). This was the only one i found and we were not disappointed. The decor is a little random but that's the only negative thing i could possibly think to say. The room was great, the staff really friendly and helpful, beds made and new towels given everyday. Bathrooms were really clean! Plus, i had an amazing view of the Empire State Building from my window! I'd recommend this to anyone looking for cheap but nice accomodation in the heart of Manhattan. Oh and go to the Cafe at the top of the road for breakfast - awesome food at minimal expense! When can i return?!? :)

title: “Stay there if you get a good rate!”
text:
This hotel is very good overall. I have never had any problems there. The location is great and the rooms are clean and spacious by New York standards. I stayed there a few times and paid around 200/night. If you can get this rate, then stay here!!!
Otherwise, there are better hotels in New York!

title: “Could have been great”
text:
This hotel is one of those grey ladies that you see in cities like Boston. Those buildings that for, whatever, reason, never got purchased by a chain and have languished through half hearted refreshes. It appears this hotel sustains itself on Fenway Park, and unless you're going for a game there, or want something slightly better than a hostel, then this hotel is for you. 
Check-in: The staff was courteous, I asked for a room on the highest floor available, away from the elevator. They got half the request right, by putting me on the 5th floor, but very close to the elevator. 
Room: European is right. These rooms are small with old tv's ancient phones and very small bathrooms and tubs. The bed had a traditional headboard on a small queen bed that had that characteristic squeak every time I did so much as blink. 
On night 2 a family with small children moved in. I could not only hear them through the wall, but also make out what they were saying. By 2am I had enough and decided to call downstairs for another room. I was told that while other rooms were available they didn't allow customers to move rooms because they'd have to "clean two of them" and that I should know that in old hotels like this you can hear everything. 
Night 3: The fire alarm went off at 3:15 am and we had to evacuate. You can imagine what this did to the kids next door. 
Check out: The rate I requested had wifi included. They tried to charge me, I showed them the rate, they said that was a Priceline thing. After a stand-off they finally agreed to honor the rate.
My biggest problem with this hotel is that any request is met with indignation are argument. For a business traveler like me it is unacceptable. The value does not support the treatment.

title: “Excellent location, clean, and friendly stuff”
text: A great hotel, I had been there for 4 nights, and we enjoy to be there, is nearly all los angeles attraction, room are clean and spacious, front desk stuff is friendly and help us at anytime, If we come back to LA for sure I will stay there!!!!!

title: “Convenient and Attractive Downtown Hotel”
text:
We arrived for a four night stay during the fourth of July holiday week in 2007. We were quite pleased with the attractiveness and cleanliness of the hotel. The front desk and bell staff were very friendly and attentive to our needs. We were a little disappointed with the concierge staff, never received a smile or greeting when he was seated alone at his desk as we passed by. 
The room was very nice and had a very comfortable king bed with 6 comfy pillows. The bathroom had great soap/shampoo amenities and look forward to buying them for my home. 
The restaurant was the most disappointing experience. During happy hour we ordered a couple drinks, and was served a cosmopolitan in a chipped, leaking glass. The server didn't notice it and quickly left as he set the drinks down. We had to go search for him to let him know about the broken glass. The service was very slow and there was no reason for it either. Nobody was dining in the restaurant and there were 3 waiters who were handling about 8 tables. On our second adventure to the restaurant/bar, we were acnowledged when entering but were completely ignored when we were seated. After 5 minutes, we got up and left and went outside the hotel for our dinner.
Housekeeping did a good job for the most part. However, we didn't receive any service on our last night and I had to contact the front desk. They sent somebody who did a haphazard job of restocking the towels and soap amenities, but didn't clean the room in the same style that we had experienced the previous three nights. 
Hotel has a convenient location in downtown Seattle and is just steps away from world class shopping and dining.

title: “a cozy retreat in a busy city”
text:
We stayed here in May 2011 for two nights. We got a great rate on the room,which was
spotless. This is a old hotel with alot of charm.The Main lobby is great! The staff is above
average. I will definitly stay here again.

title: “Ok Hotel in Excellent Location”
text:
Stayed 3 nights in small, double bed room on 25th floor. Great river view, but building curves, so even better views in the lower digit room numbers per floor ( 2507 vs 2541). Went with 2 other families and were able to get rooms all on the same floor, which was a bonus. Did I mention small rooms? A bit cramped with table, chair floor lamp,desk/console & 2 very comfortable DOUBLE beds, not queen. Rooms were in ok condition, decent carpet and wallcoverings, a little boring but ok. REALLY tiny bathroom, shows wear and tear but ok. Hotwire rated this 4 stars but 3.5 is more accurate. Pool, location, and price were the reasons we went for this (BLIND Hotwire) hotel: I would not have paid rack rate.
Pool was small, but great for the kids. Parking was listed at $49/nt so found a lower level lot a block away for $28/nt. Never had a problem in the past parking there but this time with lots of rain, dripping from above caused a "glazed donut"looking mineral deposit on the roof and back window of our car. I didn't notice right away so didn't speak to lot attendant about it. Read online that vinegar would remove it and thankfully it stubbornly rubbed off. Easy access to Navy Pier, Michigan Av and water taxis. Took the #146 bus on Mich Av, south to Field Museum and Adler Planatarium---fast and fun. 
Fun lunch at Dick's Last Resort, overlooking river and great pizza at Giordano's. Terrific breakfasts at West Egg.

title: “Fantastic entrance and satisfactory service. Rooms tend to be disappointing/”
text: Firstly, the hotel is really quite good, it provides something in which you get what you pay for. The entrance is really quite grand and exotic and i was hoping the rest of the hotel would follow suit. However, I was shortly let down as the lifts were just so slow and very unreliable when using them. The croaky set of stairs soon provided a slow and painful walk up. The rooms were not too bad, reasonably cramped but with good facilities. A reliable alarm and air conditioning provided not the worst ever night sleep. The beds weren't too bad. The next point is the location, although the hotel itself does not serve breakfast, there are planty of other bakeries and take-aways nearby. It also within walking distance of the "T" (American Subway) and the main street of Broadway. However, don't be expecting fancy granite worktops and chocolates on pillows because that won't happen but for the value it's not bad.

title: “Not a Place to Stay”
text: The area around the hotel has fallen to deperation and is not very safe. My wife was accosted just outside the resteraunt entrance of the hotel.

title: “Initially Disappointed...But Hotel Turned Things Around”
text:
I was attending a conference at this hotel and initially had some serious problems with some shipments I had made to the hotel, but the staff was more than helpful in their attempts to resolve the problems.
Aside from the shipping issues, the hotel rooms were well appointed and relatively clean. I say this because when I checked into my room there was a used candy wrapper on the floor and a dirty towel hanging on the back of the bathroom door. Other than that, the sheets, tub and toilet were clean (at least they appeared to be). Also, as I walked barefoot across the floor and did not end up with dirty feet, I can attest that the floors were also clean. 
Because I was attending a conference, I took many of my meals in this hotel. The food was excellent. The staff (from the events coordinator, maids, front desk, security, business center and banquet set up) were all helpful and friendly. 
Phone calls, internet service and printing services at this hotel were very expensive, but given the location it was expected. 
The hotel is located within walking distance to a good many attractions and several restaurants of varying quality.

title: “Clean but has some issues”
text:
Good news first: the room was clean, relatively large for Boston, and the bed was comfortable. This may be enough for many visitors.
The most serious problem for me was that windows on ground-floor rooms open right onto the sidewalk in the middle of the city. No bars or other security devices between you and a prowler. And plenty of loud traffic noise. And when I was there, the air conditioning was not working, so without the windows open it was uncomfortably stuffy. 
The front desk said to me when I mentioned this on checkout: "Yeah, a lot of people complained it was too cold, so we turned the A/C off. Now everyone's complaining it's hot." Apparently not the most modern of heating systems!
Also: no accessible electrical outlets for recharging your phone or iPod. Terrible, small, old TV. Embarrassingly cheapo furniture, other than the bed. Towels were fair but soap and shampoo were meager and motel-ish. Much higher rates on the weekend than on weeknights, so their trade is mostly tourists rather than business. I stayed there for a convention because the Sheraton was sold out. I'll keep looking next time.

title: “If you want to stay in the heart of DC, the Beacon Hotel is the place to stay.”
text: Because of it's location, we did not need a car to see the sights. The Metro was only two blocks away. The staff is courteous and helpful. Junhee Kang, the front office supervisor, went out if his way to make our stay memorable. When we had a problem with our A/C, he immediately resolved the issue and placed us in a better room. When we go to Washington again, we will definitely stay at the Beacon. We felt safe and cared for there.

title: “Nice hotel in Downtown Baltimore”
text: Depending on why you are in Baltimore and how much walking you are happy doing, this can be a great choice. My experience is that of a weekend traveler so I figure I got a special rate. It is about a 15 minute walk down to the beginning of the inner harbor, where many tourists like to go. But the inner harbor hotels were charging at least $60 and some $150 more per night than the Tremont Suites. Personally, I like walking, so, for me, it was a no brainer, but people who don't want the trek might be unhappy. On the other hand location wise, the hotel is very close to the N. Charles Street set of restaurants. The hotel itself gave me a very nice suite, 2 t.v.'s, big refrigerator, microwave, Re-done but acceptable bathroom. Only negatives I had were that the maid did knock on the doors at 9 am on the weekend and no, I did not have the Do Not Disturb sign out, but I did have it double locked, so I thought they should be able to tell that, but maybe they can't. Also, the doorman gave me a warning that I should not have left my car in the front apron without telling one of them and that they would tow such vehicles. While I appreciated the warning, I told him nobody was around when I pulled up to check in and the desk knew that I had checked in and asked what I could do with the car. -- No communication. But it's a good hotel; I would stay again.

title: “Fading Glory”
text:
Back in the day, The Whitehall was a classy and elegant boutique hotel. Having just stayed there for four days, I regret to say that it is not what it used to be. It's still elegant, but frayed around the edges. It is rated 3 and 1/2 star but some of the furniture has seen better days, and the service was inadequate and is not what one might expect in a hotel of the three and 1/2 star category. We ordered ice sent to the room (no ice machine, no minibar) and waited 45 minutes, although we called three times to check on it.
Two days out of four we had no washcloths, only towels delivered. However, the location is just ideal and the value wasn't bad; the best in the area. The ambience of the lobby is cozy and lovely, and the front desk very accommodating. But if you are looking for first class service and deluxe rooms, this would not be your place.

title: “Deceiving”
text:
I'm just looking at Trip Advisor for other hotels and remembered my stay at this Hilton Garden Inn back in January of '06. According to the website, it had just opened in November of 2005, and claimed that it was a new hotel. Wrong! It was actually a former Days Inn, which to me is not comparable to an HGI. The drawing on the website looks nothing like the actual hotel. 
The hotel is very old. While the lobby is bright and open, the upper floors are extremely dark. The walls and doors (which are as tall as the ceiling and very heavy) are all covered in chipped paint that is many shades of shades of gray. 
The rooms were extremely small. The hotel was rather noisy overall, allowing us to hear a couple "getting intimate" for most of the night. 
The staff was rather rude, especially in the gift shop, when the cashier accidentally pushed my dad into a $20 knick-knack, breaking it, but forcing us to pay for it.
The breakfast was also not standard HGI. The hotel was attached to a separate restauarant which (if I remember right) costs extra.
Overall, I am a fan of the Hilton brand and almost all of their hotels - but not this one! Mr. Hilton bought a decrepit Days Inn and slapped a few new signs on it, attempting to deceive hotel guests by passing it off as a real HGI. There are so many better choices in New York, stay away from this one!
(If anything has changed in the past 3 years, please let me know and I will write a retraction or try to delete my comment.)

title: “Building work very close to the Hotel.”
text: We were recommended this Hotel. The location and the Hotel itself were good, but what we didn't realise was that there was massive building work going on right next to the Hotel. It was extremely noisy from early on in the morning until about 8 at night. When you sat at the pool to sunbathe or swim everything was covered in a fine dust from the work going on. I have been in touch with Expedia USA to inform them of the situation but as yet have not had a reply except to acknowledge my e-mail. I have taken photos and have enclosed them to let you see for yourself.

title: “Not worth it !”
text:
We took this hotel because we went to a concert at the HP Pavillion.
The location was good, because we walked there, but except that, everything was pretty bad for the whole 75 dollars we paid.
The room was way too crowded, even for 2 people, the sink outside of the bathroom and the worst part - The sheets wern't clean. Looked like someone steped on the Pillows.
We stayed near the stairs so we had lots of noise in the morning (6AM...).
All and all, i'm glad we stayed there for only one night. You can find better in this price and this area.

title: “Paper thin walls and an idling bus daily outside the window”
text:
Walls are so thin you can hear people in the bathroom next door as well as snoring.
There is some type of large bus parked outside the right side of the hotel from 5:30am-ish to 7:15am with its engines idling which causes a vibratory noise in the room. Its awful. 
All the lighting is bright flourescent. Energy efficient...I get it but don't they have subdued energy efficient lights these days? Service was so-so. I mentioned the bus and they rolled thier eyes.
The HVAC system is loud and terrible.

title: “Fantastic!”
text:
We stayed here for three nights in February after snapping up a fantastic rate of £85 a night for a king deluxe room.
On our arrival we were upgraded to a 1 bedroom corner suite on the 11th floor.
The room was very clean having recently been renovated and was very well furnished with lovely bedding (the most comfortable bed), good sized bathroom and plenty of free toiletries to use.
Location was great with Fanueil Hall very close by for shopping, and was an easy walk into downtown.
Transport to other areas of Boston was very easy with the train station very close, the airport only a 15 minute taxi trip away and an easy to use underground.
Loved Boston and the hotel and would definately stay here again!

title: “Basically a renovated motel trying *really* hard to be a boutique hotel...”
text:
...and for the most part, they are getting it right. But, unfortunately, there is only so much you can do with a building shell that was obviously a former motel. 
To provide a bit more background about my travel style, and therefore expectations: I am a TA devotee. When I travel, I always consult TA first and then make my travel plans accordingly. Everyone who knows me knows of my faith in the TA community and our honest, helpful reviews. When my mom and I were planning this short trip to LA, I told her that I would plan the hotel and assured her that she was in good hands. She is more of a hotel brand name follower and I'm sure would have preferred that we booked with Four Seasons or Ritz Carlton, since those brand names give her comfort - and for good reason, since they invariably deliver on their promise of luxury, often at a price.
Back to the Elan - when we arrived at the hotel and pulled up alongside where the valet station was located, I could feel my stomach drop. The website, while only providing limited pictures and none of the exterior of the entire building, certainly did not prepare me for what I was seeing. As I mentioned above, the exterior showed a two-story building that was most likely a former motel or travel lodge. The lobby was small, but nicely decorated, as were the rooms themselves. It is obvious that considerable renovations were done to this property, as the furniture in the room had little extra touches, such as wood trim and a flat screen TV. Also, the shower head and water pressure in the bathroom were superb. But unfortunately, the room itself was extremely small, as were the "balcony" and bathroom. I was also disappointed with the quality of the linens. Most distressing was the room's heating mechanism, or more accurately, lack there of - the instructions on the unit were extremely confusing and even when we figured them out and did as instructed, we were still left shivering in a very chilly room! Given the attentiveness of the staff, I feel comfortable that someone would have come to lend a hand if we had called, but we were so tired from being out all day during both days of our short stay, we were simply too tired to hassle with it and just bundled up for bed.
Some high points - the breakfast buffet provided a lovely array of baked goods. Also, the location was right down the road from the Beverly Center and close to freeway access. Unfortunately, the road on which the hotel is located (Beverly) is rather busy and the traffic was a bit noisy at night. The free high speed internet really was free and really did work, which was a nice surprise. 
Overall, this wasn't a bad property - but honestly I was expecting so much more given that it is rated as #1 in all of Los Angeles! This is the first time that I have ever felt let down by TA reviews, and unfortunately I now fear that it has made a skeptic out of my mother.
I would not return to this property because I feel that with the great number of hotels within the greater Los Angeles area, there is probably somewhere that I would enjoy more. But I do give kudos to the owners and management of this property for making the most of what they have to work with.

title: “Kimpton Does it Again”
text: This was not my first Kimpton experience but it was my first time at the Burnham in Chicago. The location was excellent - we walked everywhere - Navy Pier, Millenium Park, Shopping on Michigan Avenue, restaurants on Hubbard but that was just the icing on the cake. Every person we encountered while staying at the Burnham from the Doorman to the Housekeeping staff were supremely friendly. The front desk was always helpful and I love being a member so I get my "Raid the Mini Bar" coupon. The room was comfortable, modern and very clean. It is an older building but that only added to the decor. The restaurant/bar was lovely and we ate there almost every morning. Room service was excellent too and we found it actually had more choices than the restaurant. Kimpton goes above and beyond to make their guests feel welcome and that is why I always look for a Kimpton property wherever I travel. I would stay here again and again - great job Kimpton!

title: “Suite with a great view”
text:
I recently stayed at the Hyatt Grand and found the suite very nice. The view of the water and the city was amazing. The staff was very friendly and helpful. 
 I would definately recommend this hotel to friends and family.

title: “Great Budget Hollywood Hotel”
text:
This is a great hotel.
We stayed for 5 nights in October 2009. For the price we were not expecting much but we were pleasantly suprised.
Rooms are nice and clean, and they are serviced daily. We arrived early (8AM) and they serviced our room straight away to get us in.
The breakfast is basic but still ok. You get coffee, orange juice, a few cereals and croissants. 
The owners were friendly and provided us with all the directions and information we needed. The subway is really close as well as shopping centres and fast food restaurants.
The room had a fridge for us to use which was great, but no microwave.
For the price this place was great. Most the other hotels in Hollywood cost around $200, so this place is a bargain.

title: “Not A Way To Treat Hyatt Gold Passport Members”
text: To begin with, we had a long flight and just wanted to get to our room. When we arrived at the front desk - no eye contact - just last name please? Not a professional start - even for GRAND HYATT standards. It was late around 9:30pm. I gave my name and the agent quickly excused herself and disappeared stating that she would be right back. 5 minutes elapsed when she returned. I was using 72,000 Gold passport points and paying for the remaining three nights. I was then told by the agent that I did not have enough points to accomplish this - huh? Hyatt already deducted the points to secure the reservation. Then the manager came out and blankly told me that - yes, there were not enough points. For this treatment I cancelled my reservation at the Hyatt Regency - Capitol Hill??? I suggested Gold Passport's stringent guide for bonus points usage as well as the fact that I called the day before and they confirmed 72,000 points and the awards were sent to the hotel. Finally, I offered to show the confirmation via E-mail on my Blackberry. No, not good enough. I then suggested that as the front desk manager, to call Hyatt and confirm herself. This entire process was now nearing 30 minutes at 10:00pm, after a long flight, etc. The manager confirmed that the points were found, and something about an E-mail that never made it to them that prevented them from checking us in. I suggested that a thorough re-training be quickly put in place by the hotel's Director of Rooms. The manager to her credit did apologize, but the idea of calling Hyatt first before saying "NO" seemed too much to handle.

title: “Very, very average -- except for the size of the tiny bathrooms”
text:
Stayed here for a conference of about 200 people. The public areas were nice and clean, and they accommodated our needs well. However, the rooms could use a refurb and the bathrooms -- the size of closets, you have to shut the door to sit on the toilet -- were grungy at best. 
The service at the hotel was baffling. I booked a concierge level room, and upon check in I was given a room on the 8th floor, not concierge level. After looking at another so-called concierge room (in the fifth floor of the older building) I went back to the 8th floor room, which had none of the concierge level amenities -- in fact, none of the staff could tell me exactly what those amenities were, other than a bathrobe, which was not in either room I looked at. The Concierge lounge is a nice space, but the offerings in the morning are no better than a Hampton Inn continental breakfast. It is NOT worth $30 extra a night. 
Internet outrageously priced at 12.95 plus a 1.00 tax for something, although there was free wifi in the public areas. The main restaurant was closed, so the only choices were the bar with a very limited menu and a Starbucks with only one barista for so many people. 
Its location in the Tech Center is isolated with few restaurants or shops around. It is close to the Bellview light rail station, if you want to escape to downtown (as you should). 
I would not go back to this hotel for any reason -- work or pleasure. My colleagues had similar reactions, so think twice before booking this hotel for any reason other than you must be there as the location for a conference.

title: “San Francisco Stay - Orchard Hotel”
text: Excellent hotel. Well located near Union Square. Hotel is spacious, well appointed and staff is friendly and knowledgeable.

title: “Book late pay lots”
text: because i booked only 3 days in advance i paid $271 inc tax for one night. not good value. no no-smoking room. apart for the convenience for the airport i wouldn't stay here.

title: “i think the nicest airport hotel i stay at”
text: we came from poland to travel a bit in US and in Columbus i was meeting my friend so airport hotel was the best option. we figured that four points would be the best option there and we werent wrong! we loved it. we loved the staff - always smile on their faces. it was funky somehow - i mean the interior - different but liked it. we loved the pool, gym was nice too. anyway furniture and design is def. your subjective opinion but when it comes to staff it was just the best of all sheraton properties i ever stay in.. and believe me i travel a lot.

title: “Wonderful stay for a night out wiht my husband!”
text: My husband and I planned a last minute night on the town and decided to stay at the Magnolia for one night. We could walk to everything we wanted to do and the free breakfast was great!! The view from our 21st floor room was quite amazing. I enjoyed our stay and will stay here again in a heartbeat when we plan on going downtown!!

title: “Improving More Each Year”
text: This is my third stay at the Crowne Plaza Times Square and the hotel keeps getting better. The location is great, the rooms are large with very good bathrooms and the staff, this time around, was very pleasant and helpful. A very good stay.

title: “Oasis built into Lookout Mountain”
text: Seven pools, great golf, suite rooms where you can sleep while breathing Sonoran desert air, and a not too pricey resort . Comfortable in every way. You can get your calf muscles in shape if you choose to explore the hidden parts of the resort.

title: “Charming Hotel in a good location”
text: My husband and I loved this hotel. The staff were very friendly and eager to help. Cookies and fruit were supplied daily in the lobby. We were on the 14th flour up above any possible traffic noise. With our window open every night we were serenaded with a saxaphone which only added to the atmosphere. The room was big enough for two with a fridge and a great walk-in closet. The Chancellor even has a pillow menu, which I was happy to try out. We would highly recomend this hotel for anyone to stay in San Francisco.

title: “Smelly hotel”
text:
The reviewers that gave this hotel a rating of "excellent" must not be accustomed to staying in very nice hotels. The Renaissance Chicago Hotel is old and dated, with a distinctly old and used aire from the lobby to the guest rooms. The lobby is cheap and hideous looking with ugly floral carpet and couches and used, warn furniture. Also, there are gold fish bowls on top of the coffee tables in the lobby, a very bizzare touch.
The worst thing about the hotel was that our room smelled really, really bad. I don't want to be vulgar, but it smelled like a dirty, sweaty butt. The entire floor was permeated by this stinch and also by the smell of burning hair that appeared to be coming from one of the rooms. Also, the "clean" towels and sheets smelled very, very dirty. I only gave this hotel an "okay" rating instead of terrible because the staff was very helpful. Our reservation was lost, and the front desk staff took the time to call our travel agent and take care of the process for us. Very helpful, too bad the hotel smells so bad.

title: “Excellent Value”
text:
Stayed with family at the Inn (not Suites) in December 08. Ideal place for us, who (A) had a car (free parking) , (B) did not want or need to stay in Union Square or other more traditional tourist areas and (C) wanted something economical.
Highs:
* Great location in the Marina, near restaurants and a number of shops one block away on Chestnut St.
* Very reasonable prices (we paid less than $100/nt) and as mentioned, free parking (refrigerator is another $5)
* Free wifi
* Spacious room, with bathtub
Lows:
* Perhaps it was a bad couple of days but the people working the desk that we dealt with seemed very unhappy (or just tired?) -- not unprofessional at all, just seemed very down.
* Strong smell of marijuana smoke in one of the hallways -- thankfully not near our room -- for most of the time we were there.

title: “Fantastic location”
text:
We stayed three nights in the Mayfair suite, with two adults and one 17 year old. The suite was more like a scrupulously clean apartment with a separate tv for the 17 year old. Although the hotel did not offer internet, we piggy-backed on a neighbor's unsecured wi-fi, which worked out well.
The breakfast was tasty and served within minutes of asking.
The patio (including rooftop) was quite nice, although we made little use of it, spending our time away from the hotel except the evenings.
The location is super. We loved Balboa Park and the neighborhood. If you are used to standard hotels, be ready, this is furnished more like a bed and breakfast, but everything was comfortable, suitable, and clean.
We would definitely stay again.

title: “Early morning flight - convenient stay”
