text: Had a 7am flight and got stuck overnight in Chicago. This was clean, tidy, safe and convenient. Very handy and if the need arises I would stay again. Nothing fancy but for a quick stay this works. There is a handy late night cafe if you need something healthy to eat or a coffee.

title: “Huge Rooms”
text:
My husband and I stayed in Affinia 50 with our two toddlers for 3 nights, and I must say that this is now our hotel of choice when visiting New York. Location is great; within walking distance of Rockefeller Center. Staff was very friendly, rooms were clean and a mix of retro modern furnishings. But what most impressed us is the size of the rooms...huge by NY standards. The first 2 nights we stayed in a Studio Suite, and the last night in a Junior Suite. Both were very spacious for a family of 4, but the Junior Suite was like a mini apartment...with a couch, coffee table, and plenty of room for the kids to race around in. Another thing that impressed us was the sound-proofing of the room...we never heard our "neighbors"...almost felt like we had the whole floor to ourselves (which i'm sure was not the case).
We will definitely be staying there again...and again.

title: “Great Location”
text: Stayed here for 3 nights on the third leg of our multi-centre city holiday from the UK. The hotel did not disappoint, it is in a great location. The staff were friendly, extremely helpful, and efficient. The room was very clean and comfortable, with all mod cons and toiletries you could need. We liked the automatic nightlight as you entered the bathroom a nice touch, in this smart boutique hotel. The bar Cuffs had a great atmosphere, nothing was too much trouble. Magnificient breakfast selection, and all day bar menu. The concierge was excellent gave us some great advice. Also got us a table at the Atlantic Fish Restaurant in Boylton Street, that is hard to get into. Had a stunning meal there. We will certainly be staying at this hotel the next time we are in Boston.

title: “Clean”
text: This hotel is an unexpected Gem... Very convenient, clean, updated, quiet. Short walk to Denny's for dinner. Free breakfast including waffles in the shape of Texas! Breakfast could have been better managed. Eggs and hash brown containers were either empty or cold. I booked using booking.com and got a good rate. On return trip I called directly to see if they would honor previous rate and they did. Friendly, helpful staff. will pick up and deliver to airport. HOWEVER, you will need to take the hotel's phone number as it isn't listed on the phone bank for pick up calls...

title: “Wife's Birthday in NYC”
text: This was a great hotel! The location was ideal, the rooms were well appointed and comfortable, the bed was soft and the bathtub was huge. The staff was very friendly and made our stay very memorable. If you can, or are willing to, afford a hotel room at $240 a night, this is a great place to stay.

title: “Minging”
text:
Hi,
 Rather a late review as we stayed at the Wolcott in April 2004 but having browsed other reviews this evening, I felt compelled to join in. We were on a school trip so stayed there for budget reasons but I have to say that it was MINGING!!!! Musty, dirty rooms (I would love to know how other reviews describe it as clean). I was afraid to take anything out of the case incase it got contaminated with the mustiness. Felt I needed a shower when I'd walked barefooted on the carpet (wish I'd taken slippers). I wasn't expecting anything grand but this is the first holiday abroad in 30 years where I've actually been glad to check out of the hotel. I wouldn't stay there again if you payed me!!!

title: “Great little hotel!”
text:
What a little SF gem!
I am a Trip Advisor fanatic, so when I was in the planning stages of a long weekend getaway in San Francisco to surprise my husband for his birthday, I spent weeks reading hotel reviews for the downtown SF area. My criteria: affordable and close to BART as we would be relying on public transportation to get around the city. I narrowed my search down to Hotel Fusion but was still a bit nervous about some of the negative reviews I had read on TA regarding thin walls, street noise, etc. and I am very sensitive to unwanted noise. We left the Hotel Fusion thrilled to death.
The location of the hotel is ideal. It is one block from the BART station which was unbelievably convenient. It's also very close to the Powell Street cable car station if you're into that. A hint: the lines for the cable cars at the Powell Street station are ridiculous. If you want to ride and don't want to wait, walk up Powell Street 5 or so blocks to the next cable car stop and there is no waiting. 
When I contacted the hotel to book the room, I asked for a king room, and I'm pretty sure that all of these rooms are located on the top (5th) floor. 
The room was small, but nice and perfect for our needs. We could have spent 2 or 3 times the amount we spent on our room for a luxury room, but we really just needed a home base and didn't plan on spending much time in the room so size wasn't really an issue. For the record, I really think two double beds would have made the room feel tiny and claustrophobic but this wasn't the case with the king room. The bathroom was TINY but fine.
Some of the negative reviewers have complained about the lack of A/C in the rooms which really wasn't an issue for us. During the day, we opened up the windows to get some fresh air in the room while we were out and about in the city, and the hotel provides a great little fan that helped keep the air circulating. In the evenings we closed the windows and that, combined with the fan noise, completely drowned out most street noise, aside from the random ambulance so street noise was no problem. This may have also been less of an issue for us due to being five floors above the street - who knows? But street noise didn't adversely affect our stay a bit.
As for the thin walls...we really didn't experience this at all either. I don't know if we didn't have anyone next to us or not, but we didn't hear anyone in adjoining rooms at all. Not once. 
The front desk staff was excellent. I had requested an early check in and was told they couldn't guarantee it, but would ry. When we arrived at our hotel at 1:00, we were able to check right in, with no problem, so this definitely scored points with us.
I guess if pressed, the only somewhat negative thing I could comment on was the water pressure was a little goofy at times - I showered in the room 3 times and each time the water pressure dropped down to next to nothing for a few seconds, but honestly? No big deal.
We had such an amazing time and hope to make this trip an annual event. We will definitely return to Hotel Fusion.

title: “Wonderful hill country experience”
text: My husband and I celebrated our anniversary here. I was a little nervous after reading reviews on all the kids running around if this would be romantic enough. But it was a wonderful time! We arrived Thursday evening and upgraded to a wonderful hyatt regency king room with 2 bathrooms. We were given a coupon for a free dessert at the cafe. We went out to the adult pool around 10pm and no one was out there. The pools are open to midnight. The next day we spent at the adult pool and at its maximum there were 10 adults. The sounds of the waterfalls drowned out any other distractions. The inter tubes in the pool were wonderful to float on. We ordered poolside service for lunch which was nice. The rest of our meals we ate at the Regency club which was good. The Saturday breakfast was european style and delicious with smoked salmon! The grounds were amazing and we thoroughly enjoyed the nature walk. One of my favorite activities was sitting in the hammocks in the cool evening breeze. The bikes you can check out were rickety and poor-probably my only negative comment. We got a day pass to the spa on Saturday which was so wonderful and relaxing and uncrowded! We will be back. They had a great family special going on for golf-4 for $99 in the afternoon!

title: “I'd stay here again!”
text:
I did not chose the hotel, nor did I have to pay for my stay; In Boston for a meeting, I was chagrined by the negative reviews, but I found the Hyatt to be quite nice.
The beds are comfortable, bathrooms adequate, they just upgraded the tv sets to LCD flat screens, the windows open a bit, the rooms are a decent size. The only noise I was ever aware of was water noise when someone took a shower. The hallways are bright and cheerful, and there is a 4 floor triangullar open space outside the elevator lobbies that really opens the space up.
Yes, you have to go down 4-5 steps from the street, but the doormen are more than willing to help you with your luggage down those few steps (and no, they do not expect a tip). Check-in was efficient and friendly (thank you, Julia). Abdell, a young man from Morocco, is a great asset to this hotel at the front door. 
I found the staff to be uniformly pleasant and helpful. The location is really great - its a 15 minute walk to Copley Square, a 15 minute walk to the North End, and a 2 minute walk to Boston Common and the Public Gardens. Keep in mind that there is a ton of stuff to see during your 15 minutes of walking.
I ate in the restaurant on 2 occasions, once having a steak and cheese sandwich which was one of the best I've ever eaten, and one having the clam chowder, which was delicious. The food was pricey, but very, very good.
I'd stay here again.

title: “Outstanding Hotel”
text: The hotel is always a wonderful place to stay. The staff is amazing. The hotel is 18 months old and it still looks like new. Candlewood is the only hotel I will stay at in Fort Worth.

title: “Great hotel”
text: I stayed at this property August 14 - 16th as I had business at the ConocoPhillips office on Dairy Ashford so this property is super close. Check in was quick and the room was great. There was a king-sized bed, desk with chair, couch and a decent sized t.v. There were nice toiletries in the bathroom and a coffee maker as well. I just went to the lobby to get creamer instead of using the powdered stuff. The room was quiet, temperature in the room was easy to control and although I noticed late the first night my phone wasn't working, I didn't do anything about it till the next morning but they had it fixed immediately. You do get newspapers at your door during the week and they have a wonderful breakfast/brunch available at a reasonable price. I never got an opportunity to go into the pool area, but it was clean and open for long hours. I would definitely recommend this hotel and will stay there again.

title: “Great location and great price”
text: We booked this hotel almost solely on the recommendations from this site and were really glad that we did. The location is great (about 25 minutes walk to the White House) and the price is too. The rooms were clean and very spacious, the staff were helpful and polite. Having the living area on the inside of the atrium meant that we weren’t disturbed by the noise of the waterfalls, but if that space was used for sleeping it could be a little noisy. The all-inclusive breakfast was varied and plentiful. It was fine for food to be taken back to rooms. We went down around 8am each day, but noticed that even at 9.30am there still seemed to be plenty of everything. The Manager’s Reception was a great plus. The quality of drinks and snacks wasn’t amazing, but then it is free and we could go back for a second round. The on-site restaurant was fine, but not very exciting. The shop is handy and open until late. The hotel is very family friendly, which might put some people off but we weren’t there to sit around in the hotel so weren’t bothered by the number of children. The pool was pretty small and occupied by lots of children, which was a shame but to be expected. There is a charge for internet access in rooms, but there is a small business centre (3 PCs) and also two PC’s near the elevators, which was fine for the occasional checking of email. We had a really great stay here and would thoroughly recommend it to others.

title: “Amy Clapp did an awesome job of waiting on our group”
text:
First off this Sheraton is very nice, the work out room is one of the best i have ever used in a hotel. 
Second I wanted to give Amy Clapp some recognition as she was just a very nice person, did a great job of taking care of our group while we were in the hotel lobby lounge.

title: “It is a very nice hotel”
text: Loved the hotel and Service. What I did not like was that I reserved a King Size bed inadvance 3 weeks out. Only to show up and find there were no King Size Bedrooms available. That is just wrong. The second night there a drunk man in the room next to mine was talking loud, cursing and Smoking. There is a door that separates our rooms. Yes, I could Smell the smoke. I complained and was allowed to move to King Room on third day. The clerks were very nice and helpful except when I checked in and got a double full room.

title: “Prices good, location great, room -an important correction to description”
text:
After checking prices on other hotels on the Riverwalk, I decided on the Drury Plaza. We definitely feel that we got our money's worth. The price was a little more than we usually pay for a hotel, but this time we wanted to be on the river so the Drury was our best choice. The parking fee of $18.00 a day sounds high until you compare it to other hotel's charges. The valet service was very quick and always helpful with directions. 
The location was great; it was not in the busy area (yeah), but yet just around the bend from it so it was easy to access. 
****As for the room, we had the oversized 2 room suite with 2 Q. beds. The description of the room states that there is a sofa (not a sofabed) in the living area. This is wrong!!! This is my only complaint!!! Having 2 teenage boys that can't sleep together, I was counting on them alternating nights on the sofa. It was a short loveseat that would not accomodate anyone more than 4'. Luckily, the seat cushions removed and we made a palate on the floor.**** Otherwise , the room was nice.
Every employee of the hotel was pleasant and helpful.
We ate breakfast at the hotel every morning and it was plentiful with a good variety of items. We only ate at the 5:30 kickback once; the food left much to be desired, so we chose to use this opportunity to eat out. The free drink tickets were a nice perk.
A Little known secret - there is a second pool that hardly anyone knows about on the 9th floor of the small tower. It is quite nice. To get to the main pool on the 22nd floor, you must first walk through an area of stench which is quite offensive and the pool and hot tub are always crowded. Find the one on the 9th - it is well worth it.
The exercise room was fine and the laundry next door made it easy to accomplish both at the same time.
At checkout there was a correction to my bill and they did not hesitate to do so; the only thing I didn't like is that my credit card had already been billed. I have never encountered a hotel with this policy. We paid cash, but the charges had already been processed and must wait a week for the credit.

title: “Wonderful Stay!”
text: My husband, our three daughters (aged 8, 10 and 15) and I just returned from a three-night stay at this hotel. I booked our room after reading some good reviews on here, and all I can say is that the reviews were spot on! The front desk personnel were professional yet very kind and accomodating. On our first night there, I went downstairs to see if I could get some shampoo as I forgot to pack it. The desk clerk gave me two handfuls of shampoo and conditioner. Every time we came into the hotel or left, the desk person and the door man greeted us with a friendly smile and a "How are you today?" The room was very nice, with nice furnishings and soft, comfortable bedding. It was very clean. The maid did a good job everyday we were there. My only complaint about the room was that the bed were only full size...queen size would have been much nicer. We ate breakfast and dinner in the hotel every day and the food and service was top-notch. Especially Carlota, our morning server. She remembered the drinks we liked and what we had ordered the day before...and gave us wonderful service! The location was about 5 blocks to The White House and several blocks from The Mall...but this didn't matter to us. I had an injured knee so we took a taxi when we went out. An added plus? Two different 'hop on-hop off' tours picked up right in front of the hotel. Overall, we had a wonderful experience here and will DEFINITELY stay there again on our next trip to DC.

title: “Good Hotel, Great Loaction !”
text:
The Doubletree Metropolitan is a good hotel in a great location. I have stayed at this hotel on and off for over 5 years. I used to live in Manhattan and always stay at the Metropolitan when my husband and I go back to visit. We always get a AAA rate thru the hotel website. Well worth it ! We stayed right before Christmas for only $220 a night including taxes ! You can't beat it.
The rooms are less than average size but you don't go to NYC to spend time in your room. The rooms are always clean, the bedding is very comfortable, and the staff has always been very friendly and helpful. 
The location is what is key. Only a 10-15 minute walk from Times Square. But the hotel is also located right on the subway line for the E,V, and 6 lines. Perfect for heading to Little Italy, Chinatown, Soho, or the Village. 
I have never eaten at the hotel restaurant or the coffee shop attached. I do think the restaurant is overpriced. For anyone staying here do yourself a favor and either walk over to 3rd or 2nd Ave. There are other more reasonable deli's, coffee shops, pubs, and restaurants. 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone. Its a great deal for Manhattan !

title: “Thoroughly recommended!”
text: I stayed at the Shoreham with my mum at the end of March, and it exceeded all expectations. We were originally booked in a smallish room (but with a kingsize bed) with a shower - we asked for one with a bath and were immediately moved to a large one with a tub and with an electronic massage chair thrown in - bliss! We found all the staff to be incredibly helpful, especially Daphne on the main desk. The beds are as comfortable as everyone says, and the rooms are serviced every day with new bed linen and towels, and were always spotlessly clean. The breakfast is very good if a bit pricey. The free drinks machine comes is great, as is the gym and the internet access. Whole hotel is very trendy and modern and has a really great feel to it, and the location can't be beaten. If you're looking for a hip, urban, boutique hotel experience in the heart of the city, the Shoreham really is the place to go.

title: “You Must Book This Hotel!!!!!”
text:
The St. Gregory Hotel is a great place to stay!!!! The hotel is secured, safe and quiet. There is a restaurant located in the hotel. The service and the food is wonderful. The hotel staff is very helpful and willing to make you as comfortable as possible. My wife and I stayed there for 5 nights in August 2009. We plan to stay there again when we are in the D.C. area. There are a variety of nice restaurants and social events nearby. Georgetown was only 8 blocks away. We walked to most of the attractions and took the train. The train station was only a few blocks away. We took the train from the airport , then walked to the hotel.
YOU MUST BOOK THIS HOTEL!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Great location, very friendly staff”
text:
We've spent 6 nights at this inn, and had a very good time in NYC. Main reason was the excellent location of the hotel. Al subwaystations were within a 2 block distance, and Times Square is just one block away. Hells Kitchen, where we discovered some nice - not expensive - restaurants, is also just one block away. 5th avenue/central park is like a 20 min walk from the Inn. All and all: a superb location!
The front office staff was very friendly upon arival and very helpfull as well. They really helped out arranging things for us. Breakfast was simple but more than ok.
The room was small, but clean(ed every day). For NYC standards it was just what you can expact for the price.

title: “It is what it is....”
text: Spent a long week there for business. The room was spacious with a full kitchen and sitting room It was clean and the bed was soft but comfortable. The work space provided was very small and the lighting was poor. I felt like I was checking my email in the dark most afternoons. It feels like an older apartment inside. The staff was nice and helpfull with several requests I made. One downside, one of the elevators broke and the on that was left was very slow. I walked down 12 floors to go out to dinner...happy that I wasn't on the 30th or having to walkup. It was fixed that night so it must have just been something small.

title: “148th hotel in nyc is about right”
text: better than marriott downtown but stay at the omni for same price is my recommendation. windows are not double glazed so loads of road noise. wont stay at this hotel again.

title: “Fabulous Family Vacation”
text: The resort was excellent. Beautiful surroundings,beautiful pool, staff was very friendly and went out of their way to make your stay comfortable. Food was great as well at the restaurants. We celebrated our sons 5 birthday and he had a blast. Resort is right on Mission bay with sandy beaches and fire pits . We took the new water taxi on the resort to Sea World my son thought it was the coolest thing, no waiting in any lines. Would definitely make a return visit.

title: “Almost five stars”
text:
This hotel exemplifies Marriott service at its best: from check-in to check-out they get everything right. 
The plus side:
1. Great location if you need access to one of the several hospitals on Fannin and Main street. We never used it, but Marriott is across the street from the high-speed bus line. 
2. Good gym: hotel photos do not exaggerate size; everything works and there are plenty of towels, water, and apples. Gym has access to indoor pool and outdoor seating.
3. Rooms are small, but these are typical rooms one finds in big city hotels. 
4. Marriott had extra towels and microwave in room on my arrival.
5. Room service is quick, good, and no more expensive than half the hotels in Houston. Daughter, who attends school there, loves to crash and order their quesadillas with pulled pork and seared tuna. Dinner for two with two appetizers and two entrees was $65. 
6. Starbucks in lobby has erratic hours -- they're usually not open on weekends and sometimes close in mid-afternoon on weekdays -- but there is another full service *$ half a block south. Go right out the front door, cross the street (you'll see a Chipotle on the corner) and *$s is a couple doors down. It is open early on weekends and carries the NYT. 
7. Marriott is across the street from Rice University. Three mile running track; great in the daytime but daughter advises not to use at night. 
8. Again, the service: upon check-in, the front desk informed me that I would get free Internet and free breakfast. When they mistakenly charged me for one breakfast it came off my bill immediately. 
9. Driscoll’s restaurant: Great breakfast; brunch was under $15. Service is A+++.
10. Overnight self-service parking is $9.
11. Free shuttle service to local stores. 
The not so great:
1. If air conditioning had been available in the Middle Ages, it would have operated like the a/c at this Marriott. In order to get air at all, you have to turn it 24/7 to 62 degrees, which eventually makes the room a tolerable 72-74 degrees. The real downside is that it is noisy -- very noisy. Marriott needs to gut this a/c and start over. Houston is hot, but so are a lot of other cities with hotels that know how to deal with this. 
2. Internet should be free regardless of whether one is Silver, Gold, Platinum elite. The cheaper Marriotts -- Marriott Courtyard, Marriott Residence -- offer free Internet, why not this brand?
3. Nothing to do with hotel, but this location, while great for hospitals and Rice University, is just far enough from Rice Village, where the shops and restaurants are located, to require a car, especially when it's 100 degrees in the shade. Public transportation is a joke, so don't count on it. 
Tips:
1. Ask for high floor room facing Rice University.
2. Check out the Salento café in the Brochstein center at Rice for a beer or a glass or wine. They have a wonderful selection and free Internet access. I hang out here while waiting for daughter to get out of class; it's airy, bright and music level is tolerable. Monday-Friday 8-7 and Sat. 9-6. Closed Sunday (http://dining.rice.edu/RetailContent.aspx?id=138)
3. Black Walnut Café, Rice Village. High end self-service restaurant set among shops, with outdoor seating. Loved it. Great steak salad. (http://www.blackwalnutcafe.com/rice.html).

title: “Beautiful hotel, Great location”
text: Stayed here in January 2011 for a conference at the Moscone Center. I was very impressed with the quality of the finishes used here. The staff was very accommodating. I arrived 2 hours before checkin but was given a room immediately. The health club along with pool access was $10 extra per night but was well worth it. Location was perfect. 10min walk to Moscone Center, 10min to Chinatown. I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

title: “Best hotel for the price, location and services”
text: Very nice and clean hotel. Restaurant inside is OK, a blessing for us who arrived about 8:00PM and the free breakfast buffett is top notch. Most attractions and Georgetown are walkable unless you are lame as we both are over 60 and walked all over. We will stayy here again in a heart beat unless we win the lottery then we will stay at the Willard.

title: “Great location...Times Square”
text: Stayed one night and found the location to be perfect if your looking to be close to the action. The hotel is modern and the rooms are clean and comfortable. The staff was absolutely fabulous, ready to be of assistance and friendly. Be patient with the elevator as it is small and only fits a few people at a time, but, who cares, you're in New York! I would stay there again.

title: “Outdated and overpriced.”
text:
Small rooms and dated layout contributed to the poor quality of my 12 days here. 
The laundry service lost one of my socks and the management response was to inform me socks were available for sale in the gift shop.

title: “It's still a La Quinta, but it's noisy . . .”
text:
I stayed here in the pet rooms on a weekday night. The pet rooms are across an alley from an auto-body repair shop. The noise was unbearable, and I asked to move. Unfortunately, with two dogs those rooms were the only ones available to me. Combined with the noise from the busy I-8 freeway, the din was unbearable. I had an enormous amount of work to do that required concentration, and I could not concentrate at all.
La Quinta is a wonderful chain, though, and as soon as I complained to the desk (and said I wished I would have stayed in the quieter Chula Vista location), the desk manager offered to move my reservation over there. I was staying in the room on points (I'm a dedicated La Quinta Returns member), but he got me on the phone with the Returns reservation people, who promptly gave me back my points and moved them to a reservation at the other place. The whole process took about a half hour, and everyone was friendly and helpful all the way through. Not bad for what's really a budget business hotel. I'm not sure the Sheraton would manage things that well.
If you need to stay at this La Quinta because the location suits you better, it's not bad. The rooms are a little small (at least the pet rooms were), but they're clean. If you're traveling with pets, though, and have to be in the room before 6 or 7 p.m., I wouldn't recommend it. I often stay in La Quintas when I need to work, and the desk and chair here was inadequate for that.
But I do thank La Quinta people for helping me out. Everything turned out great. The room at Chula Vista was fantastic -- complete with proper work desk and super-comfortable chair.

title: “Awesome desk staff, its home away from home”
text:
I spend 5 weeks out of 6 in this hotel. The staff here has allowed this hotel to become my home away from home. The review asked for a specific date but I'd like to comment on a year in broad terms.
The front desk personnel are always the very best. Jason has been the main man I depend on for exceeding expectations on every stay. There are always one or two superstars working in a hotel, here it has been Jason.
All the typical metrics of a hotel, room clenliness, location, comfort of bed, and room ammenities are excellent for the value and the professionalism of the team here is outstanding. These are all pluses to the value of the stay. 
There is a frightening pattern here though; managements inability to pay the folks a reasonable wage to make a living after they have exceeded expactations to the customers. Every individual that has excelled at this position has left, including Jason. 
With every change in front desk help, my stay deminishes. I am not recoginized and I do not get "welcomed home". It is a travisty of the management team to let such talented people leave for a minimal increase in pay. You are losing the true reason why I return over and over; its the desk team. They are the window to the customer and the only ones who make the first impression. With every tenured departure, each new replacement leaves much to be desired; usually a poor first impression to someone who returns often.
I do enjoy my stays. HI is a leader in the industry, no question. But its not only the room - that is EXPECTED; it is the staff you get to represent your company that makes the only true difference to people who stay with you again and again.
It is very sad that yet another great employee is gone. I have little faith that the management here will change this policy; its must be a corporate issue.
So here are some things that will help with all customes in the future:
Bring back the washers and dryers. Very poor decision to make a regular go to another hotel to do the laundry on a weekend.
Update your channel lineup list!
Please, please work with the room service crew to actually answer the phone if a room service order is placed.
Take the hand written notes off the menu for room service; its been more than half a year.

title: “Memorable stay”
text:
We just visited Dallas for leisure. My overall stay was very satisfactory. Hotel doesn't have any problem upgrading my room to two double bed, even though hotwire booked king bed for stay with kids. I enjoyed the ambiance and stay. 
I would have rated 5 if they waived my upgrade fee.

title: “Suite perfect for staying with an infant”
text: My wife and I found the Tremont hotel to be a very good stay for our 2 nights in Baltimore. The staff was very accommodating, courteous and helpful and the suite was perfect for both my wife and I to both get a good night's rest in separate rooms. Our experience was very positive and we would stay there again on our next trip.

title: “Awesome Customer Service”
text: This hotel has been recently renovated and is beautiful. But Beauty without a great attitude is nothing. Everyone here, from the people working in the Bistro to the front desk was outstanding. It was like they were a family taking care of their extended family. Everytime I asked them for something, once they served me, they would say, is there anything else and they sounded like they meant it. I would go back tomorrow. In fact, the next time I'm in Austin that's the only place I'll stay!

title: “Fabulous little gem convenient to the center of the city”
text: Warm service, great location, and the most comfortable bed.

title: “Wonderful experience at the Omni”
text: We just returned from a two night weekend stay at the Omni. We stayed there based upon TripAdvisor reviews and couldn't have been happier. Everything was as expected and more. From the attentive, friendly service of the staff to the comfortable, clean room, it was all perfect. We signed up for the Select Guest program when we arrived and had free coffee and newspaper delivered to our room at the time we requested. This was a really nice extra touch. The hotel is in a great location to walk to most of the main attractions in downtown San Francisco. We will definitely stay at the Omni again when we return to San Francisco.

title: “Good for Elvis Fans”
text: Went to heartbreak hotel for 3 nights on 5th April, great location across from Graceland - but not near any other attractions. Great complimentary airport bus and bus's to Beale Street ( make sure you are 15mins earlier than they tell you for pick as they do not wait and the buses get crowded) Breakfast was great ( and for free) . The Hotel room we had was very nice - the only thing was there were no decent restuarants near by, but we did enjoy out stay!

title: “Perfect Place”
text: Stayed overnight at LAX and this hotel is great. Clean rooms with plenty of space. Very nice clean beds. Bathrooms were very clean and neat. Hall ways were clean, well lit, and quiet. Room service was quick and fantastic and did not "stick it to you" with the prices. The lobby bar is amazing! The staff was friendly and happy to make any kind of drink you may order. You can also eat at the bar. Service there is fast too. Shuttle to and from the airport is free and runs 24/7. All and all this was a great hotel. The only negative thing I can even think of is that you hear the planes taking off and landing all the time......but you ARE at the airport after all !!

title: “Mixed feelings”
text:
Above all, a good hotel, if very traditional. We booked a Central Park suite for New Year's Eve specifically for the view of the fireworks and on that front it did not disappoint. The room was a good size, with two bathrooms. My friends occupied the bed, which they said was fine, although they'd slept in better in a hotel. I slept on the pullout couch in the living room. It was awful. I felt like I'd been stabbed in the back and I was reasonably well lubricated by the time I went to bed so I should have been able to sleep comfortably on a rock covered in broken glass. That couch should go and the hotel, if it's reading this, shouldn't be finding out about it on TripAdvisor. The rates were jacked for NYE, and that's to be expected, but if I'd paid regular rate even for that disgraceful sofa bed I'd be very disappointed. However, not something I will remember on my deathbed. 
I know hotels are in business to make money, but the $25 pot of coffee for three through room service seemed steep, though not fit inducing. However, I thought the $35 dollar fee for delivery of an ice bucket and three champagne glasses was just outright highway robbery and a disgrace. 
Additionally, the suite offer came with various trinkets, including a $250 credit at Barney's. Here's the thing... it expired at midnight on Dec. 31st, 2009, which they didn't note on the website. To the hotel's credit, they knocked $250 off the room rate, so I thought that was really good of them, but realistically, it is kind of souring to haggle over it at the front desk at check out. 
I will say they were exceptional at pre check in email correspondence (initiated by them, not me.) Never had a hotel fall all over me in advance like that. 
Overall a good hotel, but every time I stay in a hotel for the first time it has a shot at being my default regular. I can't say I automatically rule the Essex House in, though the experience was good enough. I still think that ice bucket cost was ruthless even for a hotel. So I say yes, I would recommend it to a friend, but with the proviso to consider all options carefully.

title: “I wish I could say it was fabulous, but”
text:
Well, let me start off with the best things about this hotel. The location was perfect for our needs, the beds were very comfortable, and the staff very friendly and helpful. But ..... I wish this hotel would spend a little money and upgrade their windows. The street noise was intolerable even with ear plugs. We later discovered a fire station was located a block or two away, and since it was the Saturday before Halloween, the engines were busy that night. The following night was the night the Giants won the World Series, and the street noise was unbelievable. So, we probably got maybe 4 hours of sleep per night. My other complaint was the mold on the window in the shower area. It looks like they painted over old mold which is now coming up along with the new mold. Another correction that could be made with new windows. 
I understand that this is an older building, but just a little help could make this hotel more enjoyable.

title: “Good Value and Service”
text: We stayed here the night before our flight out of Midway airport. The front desk service was very efficient and professional. The hotel allowed an early check-in and offered a free crib for the baby. We had a clean modern room and expected amenities. We took advantage of the free shuttle to both the El and the airport, as well as the included continental breakfast. The shuttle is shared with the Holiday Inn Select and the Hamptons Inn, which are all next door to each other. I had considered the Holiday Inn Select but am glad to have chosen this less expensive hotel.

title: “A flawed but oddly charming boutique hotel”
text:
The Clarendon is Phoenix's effort at a boutique hotel with a pool scene, similar to, say, Ace Palm Springs or Rumor Las Vegas. Physically, the property is a remodel of a much less reputable hotel, and the Clarendon is a big step up in style and substance from its predecessor. However, the legacy of the old hotel shows up in the awkward layout of rooms and the overall maintenance and condition of the property.
There are a lot of things to like about the Clarendon. The staff are friendly and helpful. The service fee charged per room pays off late at night, when the front desk will cheerfully give you snacks (pepsi, cheetos, etc) after the restaurant closes. The bartenders make good drinks, and the bar and lounge areas, while modern and minimal in style, are welcoming and relaxing rather than pretentious or achingly hip.
The best thing about the Clarendon, by far, is the rooftop lounge area. The Clarendon's location offers a great view in every direction, so you can sip your drink, hang out under the umbrellas, and chill out under the desert sky. After a hot day, few things are better than grabbing a cocktail from the bar downstairs and relaxing on the Clarendon rooftop with friends.
But what could be one of the best things about the Clarendon is actually the best illustration of why Clarendon is, at best, a flawed but oddly charming property. The Clarendon would like you to think that it is built around a pool scene, and indeed you can see a pool or two there in the courtyard, with colorful umbrellas and a reasonable attempt to look like a boutique hotel in Palm Springs. But the wide variety of clientele results in a confusing pool scene mixing kids, older parents, vacationers, would-be hipsters, local partiers, and alcoholics, none of whom is quite sure that the others are really supposed to be there. Time of day doesn't seem to matter, either, and this strange pool scene bleeds into the rooftop scene the longer the night goes on. It's not unusual to hear kids stomping up the stairs to the rooftop, then see them running around shouting and punching each other while their drunk parents grope and fumble through a slow dance while barely avoiding the cactus. Ah, romance.
The least attractive feature of the Clarendon is the relentless noise. Part of this is due to the general condition of the hotel. In our suite, for instance, the windows rattled incessantly, prompting a quick fix of wedging paper into the window frame just so we could hear each other talk. Likewise, as a legacy of its earlier incarnation as a much cheaper sort of hotel, the walls are very thin, both between rooms and between the rooms and common areas. But part of the noise is also due to the wide range of noise-making clientele. All of the noise from kids screaming and stomping, pool music blaring, drunk people shout-talking, and outside traffic zooming and honking, is transmitted directly into your ears with minimal interference. Even having a suite, with a (mostly pointless) sitting room situated between the front door and the sleeping area, didn't make much of a difference.
The key to boutique hotels is having a unique vision and identity that carries through the entire property. While the Clarendon has obviously done a lot of work to upgrade the appearance of the property, much less thought has gone into what kind of hotel it is really supposed to be. The result is more like a budget motel with nice decor and attached bar/restaurant than it is a boutique hotel. I can't recommend it for long stays. But if you're in town for a night, you might check it out, if only to sip your cocktail on the rooftop and enjoy the desert breeze.

title: “Very helpful staff member got us through Boston traffic”
text: We were totally lost in Boston driving there because the streets are crazy! We called the hotel and the front desk employee stayed on the phone with us and told us street by street where to turn to get there. That was way beyond his call of duty! It was a great location and I will definitely stay there again when I go back to Boston.

title: “Good location....old hotel”
text: The Sheraton is in a great location, very easy walk to the waterfront, attractions, and good seafood. But the hotel is old and needs to be updated, the rooms were pretty clean (nothing noticeable) but all the linens, towels, carpet, iron, etc were very old. If you don't plan on spending time at the hotel or in your room, then the location would make this hotel ideal. But if your expecting to relax in a nice hotel, then I would go else where. San Francisco is a great city and we will be coming back....but not at the Sheraton.

title: “Wonderful location only a few issues”
text:
I recently stayed at the Embassy suites since I had a training there. The hotel is an interesting layout inside. Every time I got off an elevator I was completely confused as to where I was. The elevators were sort of slow, but you had to plan. The room itself was a great size, it had a living room, dining area, separate bedroom, bath and kitchenette with microwave. Perfect for extended stays in the area. Beds were comfy and plenty of room to spread out and not feel confined. 
I was trying to connect to my work through VPN and had a difficult time with the hotel internet. There are free areas in the hotel on the 1st and second floor, but If you are trying to do something in the morning or later in the evening you have to pay $9.95. I didn't find it to be worth the money. I was disconnected a number of times. I guess after traveling, I will never understand how these hotels can charge $250 a night and also charge for an internet service. At this point, I feel it should be a perk. The connection I had for the $9.95 was not worth it, so I say for that I would next time travel to the lower floors. 
In room menu was decent - it was a TGI Friday's menu. No issues there with the varity. It is close to so many places for meals there really isn't a need to eat in. The Comcast building has a great eatery. 4 Seasons is right across the street and I believe the Pub house is near by, plus you are a short walk to Rittenhouse square. 
For attractions, this location is great for some many different things. I would suggest the hotel, not their internet.

title: “sea world trip”
text: the rooms were clean but very out dated. the shower head was a little short. the location was good we were right off the freeway and there was local shopping just a few blocks down the street. and there was also a few good restaurants to choose from as well. we were only about 10 min from sea world. next year me and my husband are most likely going to find a different place to stay. this hotel was ok for the price.

title: “Can't beat the price or location”
text: My 12-year old niece and I stayed here right after Christmas. Having read some very mixed reviews, I was a little nervous, but everything was great. Yes, a little run down, but who goes to New York to sit in a hotel room? Plenty of room for 2 - we each had our own room and TV, with a shared bathroom in between the rooms. Each room had a closet and basin, and one room also had a table, chairs, fridge and microwave. Yes, maybe a little dusty in the corners, but the shower and toilet were clean. Beds were very comfortable. Great, quiet neighborhood, easy walk to subway, very helpful staff. I would not hesitate to stay here again - in fact I've already booked a stay in May for a girls' road trip!

title: “Our anniversary get away.”
text:
This trip was a gift from our children and spouses for our 40th Wedding Anniversary. Don't let our age bracket influence you in a negative way. We saw all different ages that stayed here and everyone seemed to be smiling. The room was large and very clean. No complaints at all. The Sheraton is about one mile from the airport and consists of two separate buildings, a five minute walk between them. We were told upon arrival by a cab driver that the Marina building was for the younger crowd and the Bay Tower building was a little more relaxed. The only complaint we had was the Starbucks was in the "other" building. We didn't rent a car the first two days. By the third day, we rented a car as the cab rides were getting expensive. There's a lot to keep you occupied: Old 
Town, Balboa Park, Coronado Island, USS Midway, San Diego Zoo, Littly Italy for dinner, Boat rides, Seaport Village to people watch and coastal drives. Oh, and Tijuana. Keep an open mind and enjoy the vitality there.

title: “Perfect place to spend Christmas”
text: Ideal location, we walked to dinner in the North End on Christmas Eve, had lunch accross the street at a great seafood restaurant and Christmas Dinner in the hotel restaurant. Staff were friendly and helpfull and both times we rang for ice it came within five minutes. A very pleasant and relaxing Christmas.

title: “Great escape”
text: I was here for business and decided to stay a few extra days for a mini vacation. From start to finish, it was a wonderful experience. I stay at a lot of hotels throughout the year and many do the bare minimum for their guests. This was not the case. The staff is very warm and the grounds are BEAUTIFUL! We had a suite and couldn't be more comfortable. It was a little oasis in itself after a long day at work. The property is built into a mountain, so of course it is hilly - I chose to use it as a great way to get a different kind of work out. They have so many pools on the property, that if one gets too full or loud, you can find another one that will probably be less crowded. I definitely will come back again

title: “Would like to live here!”
text: Stayed at the Vintage Park on a recent business trip to Seattle. Not only is it in a great downtown location near the convention center, shopping and Pike's Place, it is also a very, very cozy and comfortable. A quiet refuge from a busy day. Has a fantastic restaurant (Tulio's - better for dinner than breakfast, though) and a great, spice-infused bourbon and cider alternative during the nightly wine hour. I will certainly stay here again.

title: “I Loved This Hotel!”
text:
I really loved our stay at the Edison. Its not the most glamourous looking place but I've really seen worse! We got a really good deal for our room - 2 queen size beds and had a really good stay. The bathroom isn't massive but its fine. Was surprised that the small hair dryer in the bathroom was so powerful - not having to take your own hair dryer really saves space!
The free safety deposits here are a life saver. Very courtous and speedy service when we checked in and out too. Loved the information service - helped us find great places to eat - Ariba Ariba the Mexican, YUM. The hotel is close to Trattoria Trecalori - try it, again YUM. For breafast we ate at the hotel - fast service and very good prices. Loved the pancakes! We loved the food in New York, we spent most of our time eating. Luckily that you do so much walking in New York to burn off all the extra calories! Wear comfy shoes!
The location is amazing - at the heart of Times Square. Right opposite the TKTS booth if you want to go catch a Broadway show. We went to see Grease which was just down from the hotel too.
I'm going back to New York. It was amazing. And when I go back I will go back to The Edison.

title: “Lives up to expectations”
text: We spent three nights here over the weekend in Fort Worth for a wedding. We selected this motel from its Trip Advisor reviews, and it lived up to its high ratings. The room was good sized, with a king bed and a sofa area that made it almost seem like a suite. The lavatory is outside the bath area which makes for more efficient getting ready to go out for two people. Everything was clean and in good condition. The only negative is that on the side by the freeway there is quite a bit of road noise, but we were able to drown it out by keeping the heating fan running, so it didn't interfere with sleep. The location is 12 miles from the downtown area, but we were able to drive there quickly on the freeways. This motel is an outstanding value compared to the ones closer to downtown.

title: “Unforgettable experience.”
text: Prior to arriving in NYC, I didn't have high hopes for this hotel, and expected not to want to spend much time in our room. However I was very pleasantly surprised to find that what was quite a small room was so cleverly designed and appointed that it didn't feel small at all, and I was very happy to spend as much time in it as I could. Another delightful surprise was the friendliness and helpfulness of all the staff. They couldn't do enough for us. Daniel, Ben, Klauson, DJ and Amanda, you are fantastic people. Thank you all so much for making our stay so pleasurable for the short time we were there. Can't wait to stay in another Yotel again!

title: “Excellent Location, great value, a few disappointments”
text:
Pros: if you are lookin for a location with great access to broadway and central park, this is perfect. Room was quiet and bed was comfortable. Large bathroom with a big soaker jacuzzi tub (if you're a tub person). Lots of plush towels. Good air conditioning. Complimentary continental breakfast for the pasty/ carb lover. 
Cons: crappy shower head that you'd find in a high school gym, poor lighting with only two head board lights and one corner lamp. No light by the desk. Very slow elevators and quite drab looking hallways. Expensive in room wifi - $12.95 per night AND for each device which is a rip off.

title: “Good hotel; beware the 'El' noise”
text:
I was happy with my stay:
1. Excellent location
2. Comfortable bed
3. Spacious room
4. Nice breakfast restaurant
5. Well appointed lobby
My only complaint is that my room faced the elevated subway (the "El") and the noise from it was loud enough to awaken me several times throughout the night. Next time I will request a room on the other side of the hotel.

title: “Pleasant & convenient”
text:
- got a good rate for the room
- good size room with TV, wifi 24 hrs, useful kitchenette, modern bathroom
- in house laundry is very convenient
- 5 min walk to shopping plaza that has Walmart Supercenter, Pizza outlet, KFC etc
- 8 min walk to Bank of America, Indian restaurants, AT&T store
- may other food, dine in, take out establishments within 10 min walk
- 3 miles to TIAA CREF location
- 1 mile to Hwy #85 (direct to airport)
- garbage disposal on every floor
- plenty of parking

title: “Adequate Sleep Inn, but not the best in the chain.”
text:
Checkin was fast with a very helpful young man. My third floor room was spacious and nice. The internet worked great. But then I kept finding little things wrong. The TV only has about a 19 channels with the main networks and ESPN. There was no chain lock on the door. Breakfast was very limited with toast, fruit and cereal, no waffles. The AC in the rooms worked great, but the hallways were very hot. The beds were good and I slept well, so that was nice. The bathroom is typical Sleep in configuration with a sink and very small counter area and seperate shower/toilet. The hotel is next to a Sam’s and several other hotels, with eating establishments nearby. Easy access to the interestate, but motel was still quiet.
They have a park N Fly program, but a separate parking lot for them which frees up the spots right in front of the hotel for guests, which is really great. (Great idea!)
I paid $50 + 17% tax, and the tax is outrageous for a city the size of Indianapolis. I am not sure I would stay here again. In general, when visiting Indianapolis, I try to stay outside the city due to the high taxes.

title: “Nice hotel wiht great service”
text: We recently stayed at the Four Seasons DC. We stayed in an renovated Junior Suite which overlooked Georgetown. While it's not the most glamorous of Four Seasons hotels, it is very comfortable (great beds, quiet, two flat screens tvs, two bathrooms) and the staff takes great efforts to make your stay pleasant and memorable. Everyone we came in contact with, from housekeeping, to the people at the front desk, to the concierge, was helpful and friendly. All in all, a nice experience.

title: “Great Conference Hotel”
text: I recently attended a conference at the beautiful Renaissance Austin Hotel and spent three nights there. The rooms were clean, in well working order, and appropriately furnished; they are, however, starting to show some wear. The common areas are excellent for conferences, the conference rooms are well equipped, and the staff are extremely helpful, efficient, and friendly. Every member of the staff with whom I came into contact was very professional and expressed a genuine concern for my comfort as a guest. The coffee packs in the room traditionally have one regular and one decaf; when I asked for additional regular packs they readily gave them to me without charge. Parking is free unless you use valet parking, which I recommend during inclement weather. WiFi is not free. I would be inclined to return to this hotel the next time I am in Austin.

title: “Great spot to hang your hat!”
text:
I just returned from a 3 day jaunt to DC with my wife and 2 kids, ages 9 and 6. Simply put, this is a great place to stay. You feel welcomed the minute you arrive. Typical city hotels make you feel rushed to clear your car away and hurry inside, but not here. They took care of everything the minute we walked in. Refreshments were in had for all of us, and before I knew what happened, my kids were picking out stuffed animals for their arrival. 
The hotel is located about 2 blocks from Dupont Circle. It's a great area to stay as it is far enough from the hustle and bustle of the tourist attractions, yet full of great restaurants, bars, cafe's, etc. I would definitely recommend staying in that area. 
The rooms are very spacious, beds are comfortable, televisions channels are abundant. The wine hour is always a huge hit, and the food in Urbana was top notch. 
I knew it was a winner when my 6 year old said to me, "Dad, you picked a great hotel". 
Well done Kimpton!

title: “Great Location”
text: Ideally situated in the center of the city, this hotel offered easy walking acces to Millenium Park, the Art Museum and great restaurants within the Loop. Rooms were spotless and beds were comfy.

title: “Modern beauty that looks like it's always been there”
text:
The Bowery is an exceptional hotel that I had the pleasure of experiencing twice. This small, boutique feeling hotel new but the attention to detail makes it look as if it's always been there. And it belongs! The staff is very attentive and happy to help with any request.
On my first stay I was in a corner king room with stunning views to the North and West. The room was a good size for NYC and with floor to ceiling windows, it feels much larger. The bath was big with a large tub and rain fall shower head. The view from the bath is to the North and breathtaking. 
During my second stay, I was in a corner King with views to the South and East. Both the room and bath were slightly smaller but the views just as good. It looks over a beautiful courtyard and down onto the private decks of the suites. 
The decor in both rooms was simple, elegant yet modern. The beds were extremely comfortable and the clock/alarm provided an iPod dock for my music pleasure. Robes and slippers were laid out each night with turn down service. Being new construction, there is no street of adjoining room noise. 
Although the upper deck bar gets packed, the lobby bar is secluded and dark with some privacy from the rest of the world. It's truly a place to see and be seen. With fabulous rooms, amazing views and a great neighborhood for dinning, drinking and shops, The Bowery is a must for both business and pleasure.

title: “Immediately Comfortable”
text: We had a really large room for SF. We used BART to arrive and it is only 11/2 blocks from Powell station. Everyone was very friendly and the place was very clean. Did not go to the restaurant as we desired Japanese and found a reasonable place that was very good less than a block away. We will however try the restaurant the next visit. It was beautiful and very busy. My wife is fussier than I and she did not want to leave. Close to all plays.

title: “Busy but nice”
text: Walk past the convention and discover HUGE rooms with great views... is that not what a hotel is all about? Food available very late so no worries about late arrivals or flight delays. Despite the size of the hotel the staff knows your name and remembers you when you return. Always a good choice if you dont need a downtown hotel

title: “Huge room, plush bed, excellent stay”
text:
My husband and I booked the Renaissance for the last night of our honeymoon, as our flight from Jamaica came in too late to book a connecting flight back to Seattle. For $99, our expectations were definitely exceeded, and we would recommend this hotel to anyone!
We arrived after 11 p.m., exhausted, and were pleasantly surprised to find out we'd been upgraded to a suite. The suite was huge and shaped like a rectangle. The separate sitting area, desk and old school TV were on one end, but that area was the farther from the window so rather dark. The restroom was in the middle of the suite, along with an empty fridge (no minibar but the sign said they could stock it for you) and a big mirror, good for getting ready while the husband was in the shower the next day. The king size bed was luxurious, and we appreciated the huge flat screen TV in that area of the room. We had a view of the airport and Burger King from our 6th floor room. One odd thing, the room had one bathrobe and one bottle of water, as if it was set up for one traveller even though we'd noted there were two of us on the reservation...but no big deal.
The only slight drawback was speed of service in the lounge. We went down at 11:20 p.m. for a quick bite as we hadn't eaten since 4 p.m., and it took our food (an average club sandwich) 45 minutes to come. There were maybe eight people in the lounge so I'm not sure what the problem was, but the server apologized.
Overall, for the incredible value we would definitely stay here again if we have to fly in/out of LAX. One nice perk, we are Marriott Silver Elite members and they recognized us with a coupon for a free latte in the morning. This was definitely one of the nicer Marriott brand hotels we've stayed in.

title: “GREAT HOTEL ENJOYED OUR STAY”
text: Probably one of the best hotels we have stayed at clean, close to alot of attractions Lucas oil stadium, Indianapolis ZOO, shopping etc... The breakfast was great and staff friendly. We were definitely pleased and would stay here again no questions. Great value.

title: “Just as all the reviews say - it's really good”
text:
great location, and it really is an osis on Time Square. The 2nd floor being given up to be a residents lounge is a great idea and serving free wine and sparkling wine (plus nibbles) from 5-8 every night is just a treat.
Rooms are clean and tidy and a good size. The quality of all fixtures is excellent and the service is both attnetive and subtle.
As a further treat this hotel is attached to Tony di Napoli's restaurant (via a connecting door) and this place is amazingly good (we ate there 3 nights out of 5!). Check this out on tripadvisor too.

title: “"Very Disturbing-Bedbugs"”
text: Booked from the road for 2 nights, 7/21 and 7/22/2012. Had stayed at 2 other Holiday Inn's during our 10 State road trip and found both to be very nice. Due to a very crowded event in Indianapolis, a minor emergency at home and the hotel being filled with teenagers and young people participating in a softball tournament, we decided to leave after one night. Next morning (Sunday, 7/22), I was sitting on the couch talking with my wife when I felt a pinch and saw an insect crawling on my knee, swatting it off I saw blood on my knee and realized I'd been bitten by a bedbug. I researched the internet with my phone and identified it as a bedbug. It wasn't in the bed as we had slept all night and had no issues plus I had showered earlier so it had to have come from the couch. I brought it to the attention of the desk clerk, Dora, (another clerk, Jake, was also present) and actually showed them the bug. She put it in a plastic bag and said she would tell maintenance. To the hotels credit (and after two visits to the front desk), Dora reversed the charges and I was not charged for the night, she seemed as disturbed by the incident as I was. The room, #508, was actually a very nice room with a small kitchenette, a clean bath and bed room and although facing I70, relatively quiet. I know these things happen and the hotel (I guess) handled it as well as can be expected but it was still very disturbing. Needless to say, I am finished with that Holiday Inn and probably all Holiday Inn's.

title: “Fair enough”
text:
Considering the crazy hotel rates in DC, well, probably shouldn't expect much more. Rooms are basic, old furniture, old TV sets, old carpets with particular smell. DO NOT GET A ROOM in the first floor!! 
Apart of that, well, the location is privileged, beautiful neighborhood and proximity to Metro Zoo and Du Pont Circle. Lots of nice restaurants, gyms, drug stores and book shops around. If you are going to DC for an embassy paperwork, this is your hotel.
Staff is frendly and cooperative. Breakfast is basic. They have a vending machine, ice, and a couple of computers to check mails if you didn't bring your laptop. The wireless network is fairly good.

title: “Absolutely the best decision I've made in choosing a hotel...ever.”
text: After an 8 hour drive from Louisiana, evacuating from Hurricane Isaac, my fiancée and I were exhausted mentally and physically. We found Extended Stay America -Westchase online and decided to give it a go. It was conveniently located near the parkway, very easy to find. The front desk staff's customer service skills were second to none! They were friendly, courteous, extremely helpful, and always available. The place was quiet, homely, super clean, and secure. It was the best rest I've had in a long while. I've recommended to all my relatives and associates to check in here if they ever come this way. This is how a hotel stay is supposed to be.

title: “Unparallelled service”
text: I booked a free night I had been given at the hotel as a celebration for my Mother's 85th birthday. We were both treated like royalty by the impeccable staff who not only remembered our names and the occasion, but went out of their way to make my Mother feel as if she was their only guest. The executive suite was gorgeous - albeit without much of a view on our side of the hotel. The no-tipping policy was disconcerting because this is a staff that deserves to be tipped. However, we were assured that they are well taken care of by management. The staff was genuinely nice and not artificial in their kindness and helpfulness. The food at the bistro was quite good, again with impeccable service. I look forward to another stay at this wonderful hotel.

title: “Comfortable rooms, Poor food, Not really on Riverwalk.”
text: The weather was bad so we ate most meals at the hotel. The food was nothing to brag about and the hotel is not near the Riverwalk stores and restaurants so we were stuck there attending a convention.

title: “Perfect for that 1 night stopover....but bring your breakfast with you....”
text:
For a one night stay this was fine and great value for money. Friendly staff, large and clean room.
There is a coffee machine downstairs but no means of getting any breakfast. Only option is to go to the gas station next door. 
Its a cheap motel but friends stayed in a best western that offered complimentary breakfast and the price was only $5 more.....

title: “OK, But not for extended business travel!”
text:
Dupont Hotel is a decent hotel, but it is not my style at all. Very chic and trendy. Looks over functionality. Location is excellent, however. Metro, bus stops, and tons of restuarants are in the area. 
The hotel restuarants and room service were extremely overpriced, so I refused to dine there. Housekeeping was excellent though. Conceirge desk was unfriendly. Business center has two computers which were always taken. Had to wait alot. 
Elevators were broke for most of my 10 day stay. At one point, only one elevator worked!! Needless to say, I climbed the stairs to the 5th floor too many times. Also, hotel was still under construction, with workers everywhere. I didn't hear much noise though. 
No laundry facilities in the hotel.
Room--bed is very comfortable. Radio/clock has an ipod docking station, which was the biggest plus for me. Storage is a problem. There's no furniture in the room with drawers and the closet is very small with only 8 hangers! The closet had shelves everywhere, so when I hung my pants and dress they hit the bottom of the shelf and got wrinkled on the bottom--very annoying. My room did not have an iron and ironing board so I had to request it when I needed it. By the way, it took them 45 minutes to bring it when I needed it. Free internet access was great however!
The windows have plantation shutters instead of curtains. No blackout drapes either. This was bad in the morning because they did nothing to block the early light. Plan on getting up early everyday. 
Bathrooms--No privacy. Extremely small! Entrance has a swinging, frosted glass door. Those outside the bathroom can hear your every move, if you get what I'm saying. The shower is separated from toilet and sink by a small frosted glass partition. I basically flooded the bathroom floor every morning. There is nowhere in the bathroom to put your toiletries as the sink is a pedestal with a two inch lip all the way around. Nowhere inside the shower, to put your toiletries either except the window sill. Yup, that's right there're windows in the shower! A little weird for me being a woman traveler. The heated floors were nice, but they took forever to get warm. I just left them on all the time. 
The toilet was crammed next to the wall, so everytime I used it, I had to sit on it sideways. Just a little uncomfortable. Toilet paper hung under the sink due to a lack of wall space. 
Anyhow, this hotel is good if you're only staying 1 or 2 nights by yourself or with your spouse. Bathroom offers no privacy if you have children.

title: “A great time in the City”
text: We stayed at this location on the 75th Birthday of the Golden Gate Bridge. The hotel was located near Union Square and it was a surprise how nice it was. The beds were comfy, the staff was so nice. The parking guys were even nice and efficient. Will definatley stay again.

title: “Comfort, chic, contemporary, classy...”
text: This was my first stay here and I have to say it was wonderful. Everyone I dealt with at the hotel were very friendly and helpful. The valet parking was top notch and my vehicle was always ready to go by the time I made my phone call and got down to the parking garage. Mike at the concierge desk was very helpful and friendly and assisted me happily. I stayed in 1905 and had a wonderful view of the city skyline. The shower was AMAZING and the bed was extremely comfortable. There are some restaurants within walking distance and inside the hotel. I didn't eat at any, I traveled out of the downtown area for that. I would highly recommend the hotel, it did feel a bit too "LA" at times--but that is too be expected. The fitness center was great and I did not want for anything there. The facililty was great. I did not use the salt water pool, but was told it is fantastic. Overall, I would highly recommend the hotel. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay.

title: “On The Avenue-Great Experience”
text: My daughter and I stayed at this property over the weekend. We were upgraded to a nice room, ample space for a NYC hotel. The staff were attentive and this hotel is well-located. There is construction across the street, but the noise did not bother us at all.

title: “Nice but Expensive Internet and Bad Views”
text: This place is clean and has nice size rooms. Unfortunately, my room overlooked an indoor atrium with views into other people's rooms. I felt like I had no privacy when I opened my drapes, and if it weren't for the roomy size of the room, I would have felt claustrophobic and as if I were in a cave. I enjoy sunlight and didn't get any staying here. The restaurant was nice, but the lounge left a little to be desired. Very tiny bar area. And, $11 for 16 minutes of Internet was highway robbery! There is absolutely no excuse for that pricey of a service. The staff was very helpful and their service was excellent.

title: “Okay for a night.”
text: Hotel is a little out of the way, but close enough to the airport that they have a shuttle. The rooms are pretty nice. You can tell the hotel is older by the lobby of each floor and elevators. The TVs have a limited number of DirecTV channels. Room service for a medium pizza was average cost and small looking pizza. Otherwise, good stay.

title: “Really nice people”
text: We stayed in the Rodeway inn for a couple of nights in July. The staff were really friendly, one member of staff in particular was very kind and he piked us up for free from the airport. Overall, it was a very nice place to stay.

title: “Loved it!”
text: Room was large and had everything I needed including a refrigerator, in-room safe big enough for my laptop, a 32" flat screen TV, and a balcony. The room was nicely furnished, clean, and quiet. I would highly recommend this hotel. However, it is about 2.5 miles from the Smithsonian museums, but a pleasant walk. Taxi will only cost about $8 each way. There are several restaurants nearby including a Greek Deli called Port of Piraeus that had excellent sandwiches and Jack's for a quick inexpensive breakfast. The hotel bar and restaurant are excellent as well.

title: “Very mixed experience”
text:
The hotel is located near the Capitol, Union Station and not very far from the National Gallery. Otherwise, the vicinity consists of office buildings and parkings. The hotel underwent a renovation and it has a relatively new look. Some rooms come with a bathtub and some only with a shower; in both cases the bathrooms are sufficiently spacious with a good selection of amenities. They lack magnifying mirrors. The bathrooms are appointed in a pseudo-minimalistic style without sufficient shelves in the shower stall; they only have one small towel bar so towels cannot be well spread. This is especially important as the default hotel policy is to change the towels only every third day. The same policy, posted on a small board, applies to bedding. However, the standard daily change can be requested and is promptly fulfilled. 
The minimalistic decor applies also to standard rooms that are moderately spacious, however space for more than two suitcases would be difficult to find. The room has a nice, quite large desk and an ergonomic office-style chair quite comfortable to sit on while working. There is plenty of electrical outlets, some conveniently built into the desk. WiFi service is available at $9.95/24 hr (and free as a part of an upgrade “Business Plan” at extra $50/night). The pay-as-you-go policy (or nickel-and-diming) applies also to access to a fitness center ($15/night), a pretty ridiculous proposition in the hotel that pretends to be upscale.
There is no fridge or minibar but the rooms are equipped with a coffee maker with a selection of complimentary teas, coffees and cocoa. Drinking water bottles are also provided but at a steep charge of $3 per small bottle. A/C system is very quiet (a big plus for me). However, the rooms facing the hotel front (New Jersey Ave) and especially those over the entrance atrium should be avoided because they are very noisy even with closed windows. The noise seems to come from the exhaust fans or other very loud equipment. In the other parts of the hotel, the noise level is not too bad although better windows could cut the sound of police sirens.
While the hotel facilities are pleasant, although definitely not luxurious, the staff attitude is quite variable. We arrived to the hotel very late, at 3 am due to a significant airplane delay. While I made the reservations, I asked for a non-smoking, quiet room on a high floor. Knowing that my plane may be late, two days before arrival, I called the hotel directly and asked for a quiet non-smoking room to be held for us as this was very important for us. The attitude of the front desk clerk to whom I talked on the phone was that of a confusion but he promised to make a special note with my request. When we arrived, we were given a room reeking with smoke odor, on low level and directly over the noisy fans. We were further told only other rooms available were only on the smoking floor. We spent a few very uncomfortable few hours trying to get some sleep. At 7:30 of the same morning, when a front desk manager came, I complained about our treatment and immediately were offered a much quieter room (that was ready) on the top non-smoking floor that somehow appeared between 3 am and 7:30 am. We were also offered complimentary breakfast during our stay. 
This uneven staff attitude seems to be a pattern. For example, the so-called concierge could not find brochures about city bus tours but another front desk clerk extended our checkout time for three hours without any problem. The restaurant staff was also very attentive. The buffet breakfast (complimentary for us) costs $20, a steep price given the limited variety of food (standard overcooked scrambled eggs, bacon, potatoes, pastries, some fruits, cereals). We did not tried a la carte items. A similar selection of pastries, coffee, juices, etc. can be also had for takeout in a bakery/coffee shop at a much more reasonable price.

title: “great hotel if you get the right room”
text:
My mom and I stayed here for 3 nights in Oct 09.
I was a little hesitant based on several negative reviews posted here but I wanted a new hotel and paid a very reasonable $132 per night, about $100 less than the Sofitel or other higher-end hotel, and it was the same distance to the sights.
THE GOOD: the hotel is a converted office building, built 1910, as such the rooms are quirky in size. It is clean, new, very friendly and efficient staff - we met a lot of them - from the front desk, housekeepers, even the Gen. Mgr. came up to check our lock when the key card wouldn't work. Everyone was exceptional. We were in the very spacious Room 910 (903 is the same size, I would guess that those rooms ending in 10 or 03 are the same on each floor), a corner room with 4 big windows and probably 12-ft ceilings. A nice spacious entryway leads to the room. I did see other rooms and yes, they are really tiny - get the corner rooms you'll be fine. Bathroom also a good size and it was clean - (I'm so picky about clean bathrooms that I bring supplies and clean them myself). Towels were nice and white and fluffy and plentiful. I even liked the soap and shampoo. We ate in the restaurant once for brkst. and it was fine. Lots of desk/workspace but the "closet' is just a free-standing armoire without a lot of hangers. Others complain about the location but for us it was a positive - yes the area is in "transition", but it's a 2 min. walk to the subway and a 3 min. walk to the Reading Market with every possible kind of fresh food - it was great. No real complaints about the area but it is not very picturesque but I did feel safe walking back from the subway, alone, at midnight. We heard nothing from other rooms and get a room on a high floor to avoid street noise.
3 computers are available in the lobby and I never had to wait. I can't comment on the parking as we didn't have a car - but, there is no sign so prepare ahead with your directions.
THE BAD: toilet is a low-flow and needs a "rest" or it will plug. No safe in the room. Bedlinens are of a low quality and are already "pilling" (pillows and the bed are good though). Old-style blankets - that don't get washed every time- are used instead of comforters that do get washed every time (like they use at Hamton Inns).
Overall, it's new, clean, I saved a ton of money staying here, very pleasant and efficient staff, I'd definitely stay here again. A great city with tons of stuff to see.

title: “AVOID THIS RAT TRAP !”
text: This classic hotel is horribly neglected; staff have been on strike since 2003 - longest labour dispute in US history yet no warnings on hotel website - picket lines every day - disgraceful wages and employee conditions; low functioning air conditioner just recycles stale, humid air resulting in very damp room; air conditioner vent clogged with dirt; entire hotel needs maintenance before this historic gem is lost - neglectful owners; avoid the "Gazebo" restaurant - grossly over priced and worst breakfast I've ever eaten; noise; low pressure in faucets; no WiFi in rooms; no outside phone lines; uncomfortable beds; dirty carpets; needs a major overhaul with a heritage architect; will never stay at this hell hole again !!!

title: “Don't buy into the negative hype!”
text: Do your due diligence before coming and you won't be shocked. I knew what to expect by doing some research. Last time my wife and I came to NYC, I spent 3 ½ times more for our hotel, and found it very basic. So expecting the worst but ready to save some money, I brought cleaning material and our own sets of sheets based off of reviews, but really didn't need any of them. When we checked in to the room, I was concerned when I found that the room door was left open. Luckily, there were no homeless people or dead hookers under the beds! I was pleasantly surprised with the condition of everything. There were some items on the floor which showed that vacuuming was lacking, but everything else was pretty clean. We were in one of the renovated rooms which helped. For the positives; This is New York City and the location couldn't be any better. Its real close to Times Square and next to multiple Subway lines.
