Its within walking distance to many attractions. The shower had ample hot water and pressure for us. But the biggest perk is the price. With the money we saved by staying here, I was able to take my kids to a Jets game, 2 Broadway shows as well as ice skating at the Rockefeller Center under the tree! Now, to the negatives; room service is every other day and completely lacks in detail. They won't really do anything but restock some basics and change your sheets. They didn't even change my pillow cases. They don't give you much in the way of toiletries either; but really people, what are you doing with all of those little bottles of shampoo? Bring them with and save a ton of money! I found some chewed sunflower seeds in the table drawer. The phone didn't work and the bathroom door wouldn't close without doing a door dance beforehand. If this hotel was in any other city, I'd give it 1 star. But being that this is NYC and its located less than a block from Times Square, that has to be taken into account. Also, the “stripclub” next door, isn't really next door, and you can't hear their music. Its midway between Carter and the Westin hotel. There is a little shop/deli attached to the hotel that's open 24 hours and offers some decent food at a decent price. Don't buy into the crazy negative hype of this hotel, its not that bad. If you want to save a ton of money and don't expect 5 star accommodations, I'd highly recommend this hotel.So bottom line, bring some toiletries keep expectations at a reasonable level buy some tickets to some shows with the money that you're saving and enjoy New York City!!

title: “Nice Stay at the Sheraton Tribeca”
text:
I reently completed a nice weekend stay at the Sheraton Tribeca.
The hotel is new and clean. It is located in a busy spot on Canal Street and borders the SOHO
and Tribeca neighborhoods, whch are filled with boutiques, art galleries and restaurants. The hotel is also about a mile walk from the World Trade Center / financial district. 
As Lifetime SPG Platinum, I was well treated and provided with a Junior Suite on the Club Floor.
Room size was adequate and everything was clean. The 21st floor Club Lounge is quite nice and has a great outdoor patio with panoramic views of mid-town and the Hudson River / NJ. 
The valet parking worked out fine. However, you need to provide 30 minutes notice for the hotel to retreive your vehicle from a neighboring garage as the hotel does not have its own underground garage. 
Overall, a nice hotel in a prime location for covering the trendy neighborhoods in lower Manhattan.

title: “Perfect for exploring Manhatten!”
text:
This August my husband and I visited New York with my parents and my sister and her partner. We had a lovely family stay. The hotel is perfectly located to visit Manhatten, yet sleep peacefully at night. The subway is just a few steps away and there are nice places to have breakfast nearby, aswell as plenty of small shops to buy water, snacks etc.
The hotel itself is kept very clean, towels are refreshed daily, the staff is friendly, but don't expect anything too fancy. The styling, furniture, equipment and fittings are not exactly new, but it's all in good working order (like for example the vintage lift that has to be operated for you by the staff ;-)
The only flaw was that our reservations hadn't been registered correctly. As a result one of our rooms initially turned out to be the wrong type: a small room with two small double beds to sleep four persons, instead of the two bedroom junior suite we booked. This was however put to right immediately and without any problems - after we showed the printed copy of the confirmation of our reservation. Make mental notes all: always carry those with you!
Thanks for a nice stay, staff of Deauville!

title: “Nice hotel!”
text: I stayed at the Loews Hotel in June with friends after a concert in Philadelphia. The hotel itself is not very obvious or flashy on the outside, but very up to date and sophisticated on the inside. The rooms are beautiful and modern and offer all the amenities you want in a hotel. We only stayed overnight and left early in the morning so we didn't do much other than sleep but I would certainly stay here again while visiting the city.

title: “Not bad but should be much better”
text:
The hotel is in the Times Square area, but not Times Square. The rooms are small, calling it a suite is a bit of a misnomer, but the rooms are liveable. I have never seen a shower enclosure that small - really.
Breakfast is a zoo. The breakfast area is far too small to accomodate al the guests, we gave up and went out. also we expereinced terrible elevator problems, there are only two with a third in occasional service, fully inadequate for the numer of guests and the number of floors. We had to take the stair from the 14th floor a few times after waiting ver 10 minutes for elevators.
Its a busy bustling place.

title: “Retro value for money”
text: This 50s motel is utterly charming, clean and well run - and great value for money. It's close to the Farmers' Market in West Hollywood - brilliant place to eat - and accessible for the beach, city and hills. My only criticism of this place would be that there were no coffee making facilities in the room, but since there's a great coffee shop /retro burger joint downstairs that seems to open all the time you might, quite reasonable, think this isn't a problem. Parking free.

title: “Filthy room and Smelly hallway”
text: The room was really disgusting. There were food finger prints all over everything. I mean I figured it would be kinda dirty since it was cheap but I was so sceeved out by the human filth all over everything. I was glad we brought our own blanket and pillows atleast. PACK YOUR OWN SHEETS, CLOROXX WIPES, ROOM SPRAY, AND SHOWER CURTIN. or just plain stay somewhere else. The was were so thin I could here the room next door watching porn and a drunk woman across the hall yelling.

title: “Very nice, well run, family owned hotel.”
text: Landscaping was very pretty. Rooms were comfortable & clean. It was very quiet even though it was close to Hobby airport. The owners have a binder in the lobby with directions to many local attractions, which was very helpful. Hot breakfast every morning.

title: “Great Value”
text:
We stayed over christmas 07 in the waldorf and found the hotel to be excellant value for money
Was locateded centrally to all the main attractions
Stayed in standard room and found this to be quiet large and very comfortable
Staff were very plesant and always helpfull
When i return to new york i will definetely stay in this hotel again

title: “Good hotel with very nice location....”
text:
Took a taxi from Penn Station to the hotel for just a little $6. Very easy for the driver to find the hotel's location. Check was quick and the front desk was friendly and efficient. I lucked out and was able to check-in before the suggested time of 3pm. Sweet.
The room was more or less what I expected, small with a window a/c installed in the window. Luckily, my room was right next to the shared bathroom, which made it convenient. 
Cable TV and Wifi Internet were a big plus. 
Didn't take advantage of the continental breakfast which was included.
Check-out was equally fast and friendly. 
Pros
Location
A/C
Price
Cons
Shared bathroom
Small room
Slight stench whenever entering the room attribute it to the carpet, rather then the cleaning staff!

title: “We had the best of times”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Edison for the first time last May. It was my very first flight and in a moment of madness decided to visit New York: the place of my dreams.
We had reviewed many hotels on the net and had viewed Times Square through the live-earth cam. 
Because we had no experience of staying at hotels outside the UK, we chose the Edison because it looked and sounded ideal for our holiday; proximity to Times Square and Broadway.
The arrangements were made through Expedia and we flew with Continental Airlines: I will not go into the personal fear and anxiety that the flight cost me. 
We actually met the pilot while we were waiting to board at Edinburgh. I was silently weeping into my husband’s shoulder at the time. The pilot assured me that he would deliver us safely to New York.
Jim and I have nothing but the highest praise for the Edison Hotel and all the staff that we came into contact with on our first and this past stay. 
I could run out of superlatives; kindness, courtesy, good humour and nothing was too much trouble. 
The concierge, reception and the security men were so helpful and attentive. Jim and I enjoyed our little chats by the elevator bank when we returned from our latest adventure.
Especially on the occasion of having been kissed by Robin Williams after watching his magnificent performance.
The trip this year was my retirement present to myself and to my hero, husband and navigator, Jim. We chose the Edison again because we knew that we would be welcomed as valued guests. 
We are now back home in Scotland but we are still buzzing with the romance and thrill of it all. Everything about the holiday, every minute of every day, was an exciting revelation to us.
We had managed to extend our holiday by one more day than last year, but it all went by so quickly. 
However, we did manage to pack in four plays (you can maybe imagine how it felt when we saw and actually spoke to such amazing actors from T/V and the movies) Stomp and two films, as well as many landmark locations. 
I could carry on indefinitely as New York has captured our imagination and our hearts. I would just like to say how much I admired the plumbing . One quick flush and no noisy tank filling up. 
Just one little thing to mention, which is not a criticism: this year we did not have a chest of drawers in our room and we had to keep most of our clothes in the cases. 
Looking on the bright side, it did keep them nice and flat: we also loved the wide screen television and the high level of housekeeping.
Yours sincerely
Barbara Watson

title: “No avoiding the smoke”
text:
Having arrived tired after 2 flights from England, I was confronted by the desk clerk asking me whether I wanted to pay an extra 39 dollars per night for an upgraded room plus breakfast, hors d’oeuvres and nibbles and no limit on non-alcoholic drinks. Unfortunately I missed the vital word continental and was non -plussed to find the next day I was not enjoying a cooked breakfast. 
Anyway my wife said overall it was good value-not completely convinced. The other initial problem was I was allocated an upgraded smoking room. When I got to the room I discovered that despite the assurances of the desk clerk that no smoking had occurred, the room stunk of it. The solution-one of the domestic staff with a few blasts of an air freshener! Well you can image how effective that was. We changed rooms the next day only to find that smoke from the next room was seeping into one of our bathrooms. Wedding attracted a young couple with a baby next door and the thin walls meant we could hear the screaming infant quite clearly. Not the kid’s fault but the walls were a bit thin.
Apart from the extra charges and smoke the hotel was quite impressive with an old world charm.
New room was large with 2 bathrooms. Main Bar was a bit impersonal with a transient population. Beer prices changed on the weekend- you guessed it they went up-not come across this sort of thing before.
Surrounding area was a bit dodgy at night with homeless people constantly harassing you. Overall I was a little disappointed considering the favourable reviews I had read.

title: “Great location”
text: Typical for a Marriott Marquis, but... The location is great. A short walking distance to just about everything. There's even a target right across the street. I do not recommend eating at the hotel. Food was mediocre.

title: “Business Travel”
text:
Attended a three day conference that was held on the property. Conference room was centrally located and serviced multiple times throughout the day. (Water/Soda/Bagels/Cookies etc.) Breakaway rooms were available for any splinter group meeting requirements.
Hotel room itself was very comfortable with above average quality linens/towels/bath products. Breakfast and Manager's receptions just serve as the icing on the cake. Really no reason to stay at any other venue when Emabassy is available.

title: “great location!”
text: went to Valley Vista Casino for a concert and hotel was walking distance. Staff was nice and helped with all questions and provided transportation. Only bummer was no fridge and bed was a little hard.

title: “Amazing Place for Our Long-term Stay”
text:
We had a family member who was having long-term medical treatment in Houston’s medical center, so we spent many nights over several months at the Crowne Plaza River Oaks. As you may know, long-term medical treatment can be extremely wearing especially when the health problem is life-threatening, and for us the Crowne Plaze was our refuge from the storm providing us a place of peace and tranquility during our many stressful days.
The people who help me at a hotel are usually what make the difference for me between a good stay and a great stay, and this was our experience at the Crowne Plaza. The staff in general were outstanding and two of them were especially exceptional from beginning to end - They are Debbie Hollier, the Director of Sales and Marketing, and Mandy Bates, the Concierge. They took such wonderful care of us, addressing our every need, and were always there to brighten our days with a smile and kind voice. There were many others that I should also mention as they are all part of the finely-tuned orchestra that helped us on a daily basis – Freida Bell; and at the front desk were Roxanne, Shaila, Tara, Jackie, Chris, Marcella, and Anna Maria; and the operator, Sammy.
The hotel itself is also quite impressive. The lobby is well-decorated. The rooms are very clean and comfortable, and the suites are spacious with a 2-room layout. They have a cocktail lounge and restaurant serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner. And they have a parking garage providing cover from the rain, and shade from the sometimes intense Houston sun. They truly have everything you need.
I strongly recommend the Crowne Plaza River Oaks for any length of stay, and I would especially recommend them for a long-term stay.

title: “Grand Old Hotel”
text:
Wife and I spent four nights there last month. It's an old historical hotel that has held up well through the years. Great location. Easy walking distance to China Town, the museums, the ballpark and the Ferry Building. Hotel staff was very courteous and polite. We had a king suite that was roomy and up to date. Rooms were fairly quiet. We could hear outside traffic noise even though we were on the 5th floor but there was little noise from the interior of the hotel. 
I would give the hotel 5 stars if not for their reservation system. One reason we choose the hotel was because their website offered a stay 3 nights and get your 4th night free. Although the original confirmation said nothing about the free night we just assumed it would be reflected in our final bill. I even questioned the desk clerk on check-in about the offer and was told they had nothing to do with the reservation system but it would probably be reflected on our final bill. Of course when we got our final bill we were charged for all 4 nights. The desk clerk put me in touch with their reservation staff and I was told the particular nights we stayed did not qualify for their offer. (They did not bother to tell me which nights did). 
Despite the reservation snafu we had a good stay. Even if you choose to stay elsewhere, at the very least come have breakfast or lunch in the beautiful Garden Court and be sure to stop by the Pied Piper and view the Maxfield Parrish mural behind the bar.

title: “Best NYC Experience Ever!”
text:
I booked this hotel online knowing nothing about it -and ended up pleasantly surprised! The location is fabulous - right at Rockefeller Centre and you are within walking distance of all the famous NYC tourist attractions.The neighbourhood is safe and clean. 
The rooms were gorgeous - really tastefully decorated, and on the large side. Didn't have a great view from my window on the 3rd floor, but that's my only complaint - and a minor one at that. Rooms were very clean, many "green" options were offered, and very quiet - I couldn't hear other guests in the hallways, elevator, etc. Worth noting that they offer FREE water to all guests - very cool when most hotels charge $4 and up for a bottle!
Staff was great - super friendly and very helpful. I found myself asking them all sorts of questions and they could answer with ease. We took their advice on visiting a few local attractions/restaurants and they did not disappoint. My friend and I really appreciated being greeted and welcomed in a friendly manner every time we came back to the hotel. Special kudos go to Meredith Ann & the guy that worked at night (forget his name)..they were GREAT!!!
I would definitely stay here again - it would be my first choice for my next trip back!

title: “Goo Goo G'joob”
text:
Stayed here three nights in June. Lobby is gorgeous and the Polar Bar is a nice spot to have a cocktail (they have absinthe service). Rooms are on the smallish side but nicely furnished. Wife thought bathrooms were cute as heck. Had a room facing the rear and the HVAC system, which had a low murmur that was not disturbing but not pleasing to look at. Would request a street facing room, which may come with its own bus murmur. Loved the building, former Arctic Explorers Club with walrus tusk medallions adorning the exterior.
Easy walking to Pioneer Square, which is a lively area with great histroic buildings and far from the skeezy district guidebooks make it out to be, to Pike Place Market, a tourist haven that lacks local flavor (except for the flying fish I suppose), and to Chinatown if your ideal breakfast is dim sum (Jade Garden) or pho (Pho Bac).
Overall, a very good affordable stay (pre-booked the non-refundable rate online), though complimentary coffee in the morning would have been nice (restuarant downstairs does open at 6am as do a couple of nearby coffee places and a piroshky joint).

title: “Polite, central location, not bad at all”
text: I was almost disappointed to hear on my arrival that the hotel was overbooked for my selected and prepaid room during my recent trip, but before I could frown they were letting me know they would make it up to me, and did they. The hotel is clean and in order with one of the best outdoor patio/ pool areas you'll find in this price range. The large parking lot has a dining option or movie for everyone and not to bad of a drive to the beach or hop to the mall. Our one issue did come with hair on the towels and in the intake for the whirlpool tub (which I'm not one to use anyways). This can be a quick and large issue for some, but don't lose touch people it happens. And we all know something like a towel will hold to hair and a jet will suck them in and release later, plus they could have blown through the air. So as long as its not a large clump I can turn my head and get it with a tissue. Overall my best stay in Jax.

title: “Fabulous servcie and staff! Marvelous bathrooms.”
text: This hotel was absolutely fabulous. The staff was charming and extremely helpful. The hotel is lovely and is a great location near shopping and Pike Place Market. The rooms were comfortable and the bathrooms were extraordinary! Meeting rooms were well equipped, with a comfortable temperature and reasonable seating. Even the conference food was good! Not your usual rubber chicken!

title: “Pre Cruise Hotel Stay”
text: The location of this hotel can't be beat. Walked to Westlake to catch the Monorail and also to Pike's Market Place. Hotel is only average, nothing stellar about it. Rooms with the garage view really should be discounted ALOT. Breakfast in the restaurant was ok - food was good but the service was extremely slow. Place was barely occupied, but I was on my third cup of coffee before my breakfast arrived.

title: “Quick getaway to Seattle”
text:
We booked this hotel through Expedia.ca. Received an awesome rate of CDN$129. Rates for our room would usually go for over $200 a night. We think it was because we booked the room just for one night (Saturday) and just two days before we were in Seattle. They may have just been trying to fill the rooms.
Upon our arrival, check-in was excellent. The front desk was extremely helpful, we used the valet service and it was $15 for 24 hours with unlimited in-out privileges. Considering that the hotel was on 4th Avenue. It was an awesome deal.
When we got to our room, it was on the 11th floor (the hotel only has 12 floors), the front desk had booked us into a quiet corner suite and the room was immaculate. Others mention that it was smaller but for a married couple, it was just fine. The bed was comfortable, the sitting area with the TV and the desk with the mirror was helpful for putting on makeup since the bathroom didn't have much counterspace. The bathroom was small but had all the essentials. A good flowing shower, plenty of towels, complimentary products and bathrobes. We only stayed for one night so we didn't even use all the products but it was definitely great. Keep in mind, this hotel was built back in the 20's (i think) and it has been renovated a few times but the essence of the old-school style wasn't lost but it didn't feel dated or grungy at all, in fact, we felt like it was a great little getaway hotel that was close to the main downtown Seattle area.
The lobby lounge, Oliver's, has really good martinies, they have won competitions for it. It was really nice also with the big windows and the high ceilings because you could watch people walking by and enjoy a tasty drink at the same time. A great before-dinner option.
The concierge was extremely helpful, he gave us some options for how to spend the night and we gave him ideas of what we wanted to do and he gave us suggestions that fit it perfectly.
The restaurant Andaluca's, we didn't go to but supposedly they have the best mediterranean, we will definitely check it out next time we visit.
Overall, our stay at Mayflower was excellent. We would highly recommend. Even though it is rated 3.5 stars, it could be 4 stars for sure but since it is rated 3.5 i guess you are even more pleasantly surprised. And since it hasn't been taken over by any of the big hotel franchises, you can go away feeling like you have really supported the local businesses.
Me and my husband can't wait to go back to Mayflower Park!!!

title: “Go somewhere else!!”
text:
Staff is rude!!! Concierge and restaurant staff seem to think it is not part of their job to be of assistance to their guests. When asking for a glass of water at the bar we were yelled at because it was 30 minutes before "opening" and then they just turned up the music to an exceedingly loud level and ignored us. This was not one person but 3 staff members. We ate thanksgiving dinner here - BIG MISTAKE. Not only was the food overpriced and not good, it was cold. We waited an hour and a half to even get the food - no wonder it was cold. The staff was uninterested in us which is actually understandable given that the TIP is AUTOMATICALLY included in your bill - therefore service seems to be an afterthought. I'm pretty sure the waiter was drunk as he spilled the bottled mineral water we paid for all over the table, didn't bother to wipe it up, and then charged us for it.
As I was staying with my international in-laws I was embarrassed by the service we received at this hotel. I was upset by the ATTITUDE of the staff - even if this is NYC - and not having manners may be the stereotype of a New Yorker - they definitely lived up to it. The rooms are terribly small. The only plus to this hotel is the location in Times Square if that's were you want to be.
Spend your money somewhere else!!!

title: “Great location, great hotel”
text:
We stayed 6 nights in July 2010. Immediately we felt a great service. Without requesting it the agent at the check-in made sure we would get a better room than we had booked. This level of service was the standard for the entire stay.
Room was nice for the price. No minibar but a gigantic fridge/freezer (which is actually much better than a minibar). Everything was nice and clean. There is the noice one has to expect when living at the centre of a city that never sleeps.
Location was excellent. Opposite Penn Station (very central) and walking distance to Central Park, Empire State Building etc. It couldn't be better.
A steal for the price - a warm recommendation.

title: “Overpriced and terrible”
text:
For $187 a night, I expected to at least to have a warm room (no heating), running water (water trickled and then stopped during shower), warm water (November is not summery). When I told the front desk staff, she responded with "I'll send someone to have the heating turned up" Upon returning to the hotel room a few hours later, it was still cold. When I rang from my room to let them know that I had NO water, she said "I'll change your room for you" but I had to go down stairs with wet hair and demand that something be done. I then had to move my things myself to the new room.
The "continental" breakfast required a very long stretch of the meaning "continental", though the tray of Dunkin Donuts fits in very well with the "hotel" overall. 
The "high speed" internet was non existent. I spent most of the time with "connection time out" or waiting for over ten minutes for pages to load. I was in PA for a conference, so I had a lot of work to do after each day at the conference which requires the internet. I've had better internet service on the NYC subway. Do not make claims on services that do not exist. 
The room change was no better. There were towels already used on the towel hooks behind the bathroom door. No TV remote, no decent running water for a shower. 
The Rodeway Inn is not a "hotel", it is an overpriced and really terrible hovel. You do NOT get what you are paying for. As someone who travels frequently and appreciates the basics of a clean, well priced, and well run hotel, The Rodeway Inn is a joke.

title: “Superb!”
text: Our decision to try the Salisbury was based primarily on its comparatively reasonable price and ideal location (across from Carnegie Hall and the Russian Tea Room, 2 blocks from Central Park, a few short blocks to Times Square/theatres). Upon checking in, I noticed that the reservation print-out specified two beds, instead of the king bed I'd reserved. When I pointed it out to the front desk agent and presented my Frequent Stay card (for which I signed up when I booked the reservation), he immediately checked for available upgrades and gave us a lovely, quiet, king suite with two flat screen TV's and three closets. Frankly, it was larger than some NY apartments! After reading some of the reviews, I was prepared for a lengthy elevator wait time, but with a couple exceptions, they usually came almost immediately. As they're relatively small, it's probably helpful to be on a higher floor to catch them before they're filled on the way down. To top off a perfect stay, I was informed at check-out that we'd already stayed enough nights and earned enough points to get one night free. The hotel is by no means grand, but the accommodations were lovely, the location is ideal, and our stay could not have been better.

title: “Overnight Stay”
text:
Nice rooms with nice decor. Surprised to find the WiFi wasnt complimentary as standard. Gym small and dated and swimming pool very cold. Staff were friendly and helpful. The food was nice.
I wouldnt say the hotel was luxurious by european standards but it was comfortable. I also found some of the Decor old fashioned and slightly out of date. Good location.

title: “Market Center Hotel”
text: Stay here every time I go to or pass through Dallas! Great Location and GREAT hotel

title: “Conference”
text: Nice hotel in a fabulous location. Special thanks to "Ericka" at the front desk who was courteous, polite and professional. Housekeeping staff and porters were all very pleasant. Restaurant is average but not a problem as the location offers superb dining in close proximity.

title: “A hidden gem”
text: I had the pleasure of staying at the Conwell Inn last month and found it to be a rare gem hidden away on Temple's campus. The staff was courteous and very helpful in making my stay there a pleasureable one. I mean it is on a college campus and you do hear the normal activities of college students on the weekends, but having the campus police right next store makes your stay safe. Highly recommended!!!

title: “Convenient option with a few issues”
text: Stayed two nights last weekend. Rooms are good size (relative to NY), beds are comfortable, fitness center is fantastic (lots of aerobic equipment, heavy boxing bag, weights, warm towels, etc), elevators are pretty quick for such a large place. Room service was very fast and the Market in the lobby is a convenient pantry service that's accessible 24 hours, beer, beverages, light sandwich and snack options. Can't beat the connection to Grand Central Station. Drawbacks - restaurant and bar service was a little slow and I thought the food options in the restaurant were limited. In the room, the HVAC system was erratic, blowing (literally) hot and cold - too hard to regulate. And in the bathroom, there's a shelf right above the sink that makes it impossible to bend down to wash your face or rinse from shaving. Annoying. Overall, the location and room size would probably bring me back but my first choice in the city is the Hilton Times Square.

title: “In the middle of San Francisco”
text:
This hotel was a great find, and it's not surprising it receives such great reviews on tripadvisor. 
Hotel is located near Powell Street and Union Square. Best place to take photos on the cable cars, with the hanging out pose is at the end of the line!
Since this location is near a busy road, noise can be heard from the bedrooms. The windows are only single glazed. We had a double room, and it was fine, but nowhere near ample in size. The rooms are dark inside, as limited windows fir light to come in. The website for this hotel dies a great job showing bright airy rooms or we were just unlucky not to have been allocated a bright room.
Location is definitely a plus point if this hotel. It's close to everything.
Hotel has free wi-fi, which is a bonus. The staff at reception were always friendly and helpful.

title: “A very enjoyable trip!”
text: Booked Ames for St Patty's day weekend! When we arrived, the hotel was a little hard to find, you just have to look for the arched windows half way up the building. The staff was very professional and helpful. We were upgraded to a king room, which was very clean and comfortable with a nice view. Hotel location was fantastic, right in the middle of everything you want to see! Street noise level was pretty loud but that didn't bother us, especially for being in our 20s on St Patty's Day weekend! My only complaint was the the shower stall, which had glass walls and was large enough for a romantic time for two, only had a half wall on one side. Water kept spilling onto the bathroom floor, so make sure you put enough towels on the floor near the entrance of the shower stall. Other than that, the hotel was perfect!

title: “A Little out of the way but overall a very nice stay”
text:
I am sitting in the lobby drinking the complimentary mineral water some high end brand and am reflecting on our stay. The lobby is really nice an the rooms are nice
The bed sat on the floor which may be a problem for older people.
The staff was great, there was some work being done in room above me and they in trad accommodated my late check out
Good place

title: “A Real Find”
text: My wife and I stayed here for four nights. The 1 BR suite was bigger than most Manhattan apartments and was very comfortably furnished. The furnishings were not new, but everything was perfectly functional and very clean. The room was very quiet and the mattress was excellent compared to most hotels. For the price you won't find anything that even comes close to this. We ate one night at the Tower restaurant and the food, service and view were all excellent. The surrounding neighborhood is very safe with lots of restaurants, pubs and grocery stores to choose from. Everything in Manhattan is easily accessible via foot, bus or subway, so the location of this hotel wasn't a drawback at all. In fact, it is right next to an FDR drive exit which made getting there, and back out of the city, a snap. The staff were all great too. We are looking forward to our next trip to NYC in part because we plan to stay here again.

title: “If you're claustrophobic, FUGHETTABOTIT”
text: This property maintains a great location (you can see Central Park from the entrance of the hotel). However, there was one elevator for at least a minimum of 10 stories and was no larger than an average-sized pantry. If you had one regular-sized piece of luggage, there would only be room for two additional people. When I got to the room, the door opened up and was 4 inches from the bed (I had to step inside, then drag my suitcase in and slide it to the right in order to close the door (this room was the size of a large walk-in closet. The chair they provided you (similar to an old dining-room chair) had to be slid over to the closet area in order to walk in front of your bed to the bathroom. There was literally 9 inches between bed and dresser. They did provide a very nice flat-screen television and the bathroom had recently been remodeled; however, for over $250 a night (average in NY), it would've been nice to have secured one of the spacious rooms they offer when you're viewing their property online.

title: “OK hotel - I've stayed in better”
text:
We had friends riding in the Seattle to Portland (STP) bike ride, so we stayed in this hotel on Friday July 13th. They picked it because they thought it was close to the starting point of the ride at the University of Washington, but it was about 3 miles or so to the starting point. The room was a pretty basic two bed room, although I think Marriott referred to it as a "suite". It did have a refridgerator.
The room was not well insulated, so there was quite a bit of noise. We had some pretty noisy neighbors, and we could clearly hear people talking in the hallway. We were on the lake-side of the hotel, so we had a view of the lake that was nice. It also meant we had traffic, and we could hear every car that went by. I woke up a lot during the night, and I think it was the random traffic. I always fall back to sleep, but my boyfriend and another friend said they didn't get any sleep because of the noise.
I rarely have a problem with beds, but two of the four people in our group complained that the beds were not comfortable. I didn't notice.
The people at the front desk were helpful and very nice.

title: “Nice hotel!”
text: I was glad to find this hotel...it clearly is a converted apartment building from the 70s. I had no idea I would be getting something so large. The rate for the price is great. The restaurant downstairs for dinner was exceptionally good. Close walking distance to Dupont Circle and other DC areas.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text:
We just spent five nights at this hotel in May 2007. Fabulous. It was extremely busy the whole time we were there but that didn't stop the staff going out of their way to make us welcome and remember us whenever they saw us in the lobby. Sean on the front desk, Lance and Lincoln were just the nicest people and went out of their way for us. 
Its very well located - right across the road from a large mall and fairly close to Santa Monica and Beverly Hills. Quite central to most things although this being LA you would need a car. 
After spending a month travelling through the US it was a lovely end to our time overseas and I would definetely stay there again.
Note to people like me curious about the mini bar - if you lift something out of the fridge....you will be charged...be warned!

title: “Lovely Stay”
text:
I cannot recomend this hotel highly enough. This was my 4th trip to New York but my 1st stay in this hotel. The whole experience was lovely from the hotel itself, to the staff, the restaurant I could go on and on. We stayed the week before christmas and also got engaged whilst over there. Given the time of year and how close to christmas the main tourist and shopping areas were really hectic it was great to come back out of the "madness" and be able to relax. The front desk staff especially Oneca were great and looked after requests which had been made by my fiance prior to our arrival. We ate in the restaurant twice and the food was delicious. We are already considering returning for a few nights during our honeymoon:)
Thank you all at Affinia Shelburne for making a special time for me and my fiance a very memorable experience. Hope to be back in 2013!

title: “Nice Room great location”
text: I got a fantastic rate on this hotel and wasn't sure what to expect. It was very well kept and currently undergoing renovations so everything is brand new. This is the quietest hotel I've stayed at in DC, we even left the window open at night and weren't disturbed. The location was very close to the Dupont restaurants and shops. The staff was very helpful.

title: “ABSOLUTE WORST!!!!!”
text: I have stayed at W hotels before, I have stayed at "no-tell" motels before. I cannot decide which is worse. This was BY FAR not a 4 star hotel. Our room was an absolute utter disgace. It was approximately 80 square feet. BEWARE if you are over 5'9" and need to sit on the toilet. My husband injured his knees when they hit the wall (I'm not kidding) as he was sitting down. We requested to be moved, but the hotel was at full capacity (were all of the other guests complaining I wonder?) and we could not be moved. To boot, they double-charged our bar tab to the room. All I can say is thank G-d we only stayed for 1 night. We had an entire day planned the day of our departure that we opted to cancel because we needed to check out of this hellhole at 7am on a Sunday. I have never felt so claustrophobic in my entire life. There are soooo many other great hotels in this city. DO NOT stay here.

title: “Quick Stop over in LA”
text:
We stayed at the Beverley Hills Crowne Plaza as part of a quick stop over in LA on our way to a wedding. We wanted to go to Universal etc so our agent recommended this as a reasonable location with child friendly facilities. 
When we arrived I was a little taken aback by the location and the outside - it does not really seem close to anywhere and is in a residential area with not many things around. The building itself is a tired 70s style faceless block. We wandered about on the first morning but quickly concurred that we probably needed to get cabs to Santa Monica, Universal etc and the tourist attractions as there did not seem to be much to visit around us. 
The rooms were okay - quite decent sized beds (we had two doubles) and clean and well laid out if a bit tired. The communal areas are similarly a bit past their best. We were tired after travelling and opted for the in house restaurant which was large but virtually empty. The decor is a bit jaded like the rest of the hotel but the food and service were good and the meals reasonably priced. There is an in house Starbucks so reasonable coffee and the breakfasts are also served there - buffet style, plentiful and varied. 
I ordered the in house car service to take us to Universal next day as we had a 10am meeting point for a VIP tour so I did not want to leave it to chance with a taxi. This was a bit of a disaster as they seem to have overbooked the service and so our 9.00am car never appeared and eventually at 9.30am we were asked to join another couple in a minibus! The driver drove like mad to get us to our appointed time of 10am for the VIP tour, but we were still late in getting to the gate etc which was a pain having sorted everything out the night before. The driver also charged us more than we were advised because he was not coming back for us. Perhaps we were just unlucky, but the organisation of the driver service seemed a bit haphazard with lots of people waiting for pre ordered cars whilst taxis were pulling up regularly!
There is a nice outdoor pool which is a welcome respite at the end of a busy day and is a nice extra. 
When I looked at our reservation afterwards, this hotel is at the cheaper end of the others we stayed in whilst in the US and I would say this is reflected in their offer. If you are after a basic 2/3 star hotel for a quick stop off this would probably work for you but I would happily have paid for something a bit more modern and upgraded.

title: “Great holiday”
text: New York is a great city and the hotel Ameritania was the right choice: strategically located near Times Square. The guys at the hotel were all extremely courteous and willing to help, especially Jalal

title: “perfect birthday weekend!”
text: Hotel Palomar in San Fran was the perfect location and experience for my birthday celebration! Josh was extremely helpful throughout our stay and made us feel welcome. His recommendations were spot on and only enhanced our stay. Thank you Josh and the Palomar staff :)

title: “Amazing river view and great service for a romantic night”
text:
This hotel is simply fabulous! I highly recommend selecting a room with a river view. The city view is also nice but the best view of downtown Detroit is from Windsor, across the river. I stayed on the 64th floor so the view was stunning. I selected a suite and explained to the hotel staff that it was for a romantic evening, so they helped make me in almost every way possible. They put a chilled bottle of Champagne and strawberries and chocolates just prior to my arrival. I had placed candles in the room and asked them to light them but they said that the fire marshal does not allow this. The only other tiny problem was receiving a call from the front desk early in the morning, alerting me that my car may have been stolen. It turned out to be a misunderstanding. LOL.
The suite was much larger than I had expected. We could have easily played football in the main room without touching the dining table.
The revolving restaurant at the top is spectacular and serves amazing food. Definitely do not miss this restaurant or hotel.

title: “Great Find”
text: Stayed here mid week and was pleased that this hotel still has the staff that "goes the extra mile" to provide GREAT customer service. The room was excellent and we loved the view of the waterfront. We will be back for sure!

title: “Nice hotel, location and smooth ripoff”
text: Right on Logan square, with a beautiful view if you can get those rooms. 10-15 minutes walk to shopping and theater district. The usual Four Seasons polish though nothing particularly special at his location. Now, $49 daily parking fee? That's out there. It's so high it should be advertised when you reserve really. A smooth scam if you ask me.

title: “Mediocre Visit to the Conrad Chicago”
text:
My spouse and I recently stayed at the Conrad Chicago for 4 nights. We were in Chicago for a short vacation, and wanted to ensure that our accomodations would be top notch and were willing to pay for that. The hotel location is very good, but so is the Marriot next door, Hyatt down the street, and Intercontinental across the street. However, on arrival the entire lobby / street entrance was undergoing construction, and you have to walk through a less than appealing maze to get to the actual reception, of course there was no mention of this prior to arrival. 
A very bright note of the stay was the concierge service throughout. Nothing less than excellent. 
The room itself was unfinished, with receptacle wall plates missing where contractors must have assumed that the curtain was going to hide them. The rooms have large Flat Screen TVs and Bose sound systems as advertised, but to go to all of the trouble, to put the flat screen, etc., in the room, then leave all of the cables, plug in, wires for same in plain view, makes appearance cheap and look "thrown together." 
Housekeeping could use improvements - the bathroom was not vacuumed or swept during stay, when the bed is turned down perhaps there is a better place for the bedspread and pillow besides next to the bed on the floor. Maybe closet shelf? No fresh soap in the bathroom - used same small little bar throughout, and bare essentials - shampoo, conditioner, nothing more - definitely not indicative of a high end hotel chain. At night there was one bottle of water placed by the bed when two of us were staying there - cheap? 
Check out - receptionist was alone, with a long line up and wait, I asked him if he was understaffed due to the length of wait and check out line up, and no apology, just a flippant response that no he was not understaffed, one person was showing someone a room, and someone was at lunch. I would think staff lunches would be scheduled a little later than noon considering that is checkout time. Definitely did not feel welcome at check out, was not asked how stay was or safe journey or anything. I have been doing extensive travel all over the Middle East, Mediterranean the last year, and wanted a very special experience for my spouse and I now that we are reunited, and this was anything but. I have stayed in many 4 and 5 star hotels, and Conrad Chicago is mediocre at best, and considering the room rate poor value for money.

title: “Visit but NOT on a Weekend!”
text:
Loved it! 
But will surely go on a weekday-NEVER again on a Friday or Sat. The courtyard by evening became crowded and the crowds were VERY loud until after 12 am and a reception was going also on so the music vibrated my room and I actually called front desk...and that let out at 12 am.
And it also seemed like some or if not more people who were gathering there came to enjoy the evening and not necessarily were all hotel guests or for the reception. Oh, and note you will have to park in a parking garage-the hotel doesn't have a parking lot-the hotel is right along connected to the stores.
I reserved a room on a Sat-through the offical website for $169. It had a balcony. It is a great hotel-very cozy and unique. I went there because it was fairly new...and that means clean-trust me I look for nice and clean. It has a lovely courtyard, outdoor pool on the 5th floor, and nice views from balcony-open for all guests, and plently of cozy sofas to relax on.
Driving into Santa Row you will SURELY feel as though you just walked into another city...I live in San Jose so it threw me off, me and my friend were like where'd this come from...where'd these people come from-nice people :) And you would never think driving by how nice it is-drove by it several times and never imagined.
This is unique and not like no other. And the room style is unique also. It's perfect for a romantic evening or just to relax. I'm very picky and rarely ever give my opinion but I really like it-and if you're skeptical just go and check out the 3rd floor which has the courtyard and bar-or the website, photos on the webiste look very nice and in person it looks even nicer and better. It was worth the price.
I would surely recommend this hotel...just when it's not on weekends or holidays! Avoid the crowds! :)

title: “Great location, nice hotel, awesome breakfast”
text:
I stayed here over labor day weekend with my husband and two kids (12 & 7). Yes, the hotel is undergoing renovations, no it did not affect our stay. The hotel is very nice, there was no noise, the entrance was clearly marked and easy to get to. The location can not be beat - on the wharf, across the street from Quincy Market and a short walk to the North end. A few tips; upgrade your room to include the breakfast package. A few dollars more gets you two adult breakfasts and kids are free. It is a breakfast buffet with everything you could ask for (omelet station, waffles, pancakes, bacon, sausage, potatoes, fruit, oatmeal, yogurt, pastries, etc.) I even got a latte to go! Don't miss the pool and outdoor deck overlooking the harbor. It was a great spot to eat a snack or even dinner. The staff was very pleasant and helpful. The only negative we could find was the charge for internet. Just doesn't seem possible for Marriott to be able to get away with that in these times.
But we would stay here again in a heartbeat! Can't wait to go back!

title: “Old tired hotel”
text:
This hotel is old and tired. The rooms are small like a New York hotel. The bathroom is extremely old. The shower water temp goes up and down and you can barely move in the bathroom. The furnishings are old and the bed wasnt very good. There was a small window with no view and there was no climate control in the room. You can hear every word clearly in the hallways which will wake you up in the middle of the night. There is no on site parking and you have to walk 2 blocks to park.
Positives:
It was only $40 on priceline. The staff was very nice. It is only about a 10 minute walk to the basketball arena and a 15 minute walk to the baseball park.

title: “Fantastic value”
text: If you know the city well and are looking for a different part of town base your stay in than you could do a lot worse than the River Inn. Neighborhood is nice and quiet and I was able to find street parking without a problem. For the price the quality of the rooms can't be beat.

title: “Very Convenient for SMU Visit”
text: Hotel Lumen was very welcoming. The staff were all very friendly and helpful. We spent the day on campus and were allowed to keep our car parked in the garage. Our room was spacious (especially the bathroom) and comfortable, with free wifi, two flat screens, and a kitchenette (refrigerator, microwave, and full kitchen sink) but no dishes, silverware, etc.. The style is more minimal (which we appreciate) but may not be for everyone. Our room also had a balcony, which provided a pretty view of the campus and surrounding neighborhood. The late night room service menu was limited (soup, sandwiches) and of average quality. Continental breakfast (included in our room) was good - coffee was great (in the lobby). They are building a new wing and pool.

title: “Highly recommend”
text: Front desk staff very friendly & accomodating. Concierge lounge offered wonderful brkfst items--eggs, bacon, smoked salmon & cereal toast etc. Great to visit in the evening as well. Very clean & quiet hotel--wonderful beds & pillows. Perfect location & plenty of restaurants and attractions nearby. Appreciated the 6 elevators & quickness of them!

title: “3-star hotel with a 5-star service!!!”
text:
PROS
We recently stayed at this hotel for our anniversary and it was great! The service was impecable. The amenities is 5-star worthy especailly with FREE Wi-Fi (virtually unheard of in a Manhattan hotel) and newly installed in-room safe that can store my 15.6" laptop (max). AMAZING! Jenny the maid was very sweet. We loved her and she did an awesome job. The front desk staff bright and cheery and were ready to help even before we reached the counter. We stayed in room 3003 and we had an unbstructed view of The Empire State Building. The bed was very comfortable and comes with adjustable firmess dials on either side of the matress so you can select your prefered setting for you comfort. It's a small thing but having the ability to store our water bottles in the fridge to keept it cold meant a lot to us. Some hotels don't even give you a fridge.
There's no denying that this hotel has a 3-star look and feel to it, but with all the amenities, friendly staff and location, it makes it feel like your staying at a 5-star hotel in mid-town Manhattan for a 3-star price. Most of the time we were out visiting NYC so we didn't want to spend a lot of $$ on our hotel since we were only there to sleep anyway. It's no wonder that at the time we booked it, it was rated #25 out of 450+ hotels in NYC listed on Tripadvisor.
CONS
Our room (3003) had a slight mildew smell coming from the carpets and requires steam cleaning. I can imagine how bad it would smell during the summer months. We kept the A/C on and it seemed to help a lot.

title: “GIRL WEEKEND”
text:
We had a girl weekend and had a blast. The room was clean, large and the beds were so comfortable. We ordered room service and everything was hot and very good.
Karen B.

title: “Beautiful hotel located in a perfect area”
text: Had the pleasure of booking this hotel directly through the Starwood web page, which linked me to this hotel. I was quoted 199.00 per night, and thought that this was a very reasonable deal. After reading some comments, I took some with a grain of salt. I have stayed at the Palace in Madrid Spain, and thought if this was anywhere near that ,I would be happy. Location is about 40 minutes to SFO. I hired a cab take myself and my date, the cost one way is 45.00. Upon leaving the hotel after our 2 night stay, I was offered by the doorman a black Town car to return to SFO for about $50, plus I tipped 10. They staff was very friendly and served you with smiles. The concierge was a life saver. They ordered a strech limo for me and my guest to go out for dinner and club hopping. Cost was billed to the room for $210 including tip. The moment you walk in , it will take you a while to absorb the architecture of this building. It was very ornate, simular what you might find in Venice or Rome. All avenues were spotless. Rooms were small, but had marble, shower,tubs, all necessities one would need, including free bottleds water. The only down side is that there is a refrid. in the room, but no mini bar.Wonderfully done bed, and very comfortable. I had scheduled a romantic lunch at The Gardens. Very opulant and grand. Lunch was around $100. They even sprinkleed our table with rose pedals,something I had not asked for, but made me look like a hero...Thanks!!!!! Went to the sushi rest. adjoining the hotel. Had wonder dinner, sushi etc for about $150. Mornings, I went to a Starbucks no more than 150 feet from hotel. I would absolutly stay here again. There was some signs of age, but I would rate this hotel a 4 out of 5. The Wharf is a 11 dollar taxi ride. Enjoy...I did.

title: “Excellent staff and overall great place to stay!”
text:
Yes, i have to agree with most of the comments here. I stayed for 3 nights from 24 - 27 April.
I cannot see any fault with the lifts as one just have to time oneself. But generally, the excellent customer service more than makes up for it, notably the red haired guy from Niagara Falls called Daniel. Everyone was so helpful, polite and cheerful and that helps make your stay that much more enjoyable. there is nothing to fault the hotel on.
I am glad i chose Staybridge suites and feel the same as the rest who has contributed very positively in this review forum.

title: “Outstanding hotel: great fitness center and pool and great value!”
text: This is a great hotel. I found it on Expedia and it is conveniently located to the freeway and many amenities. It was clean, comfortable, large room and great value. I will definitely stay again.

title: “Great Stay”
text: Hats off to this wonderful boutique hotel. We felt right at home the minute we walked in. From the Reception Desk to the Dining room to the Lounge the staff was incredible. No "hotel" food here the Chef is a marvel as is his staff. Our rooms were very comfortable, spacious, well kept AND from our window we could see the Washington Monument, an unexpected plus for a first time Washington visitor. Being able to stroll the neighborhood added to our pleasure. I would recommend the Savoy Suites to both business travelers and my friends. My next visit to DC will include a stay with the Savoy Suites.

title: “March, 2009 Stay at Inn at the Opera”
text: My wife and I just returned from a week's stay at the Inn at the Opera. A nice and charming hotel in a very well kept older building. Very clean. Agree with others that it is located a bit away from many of the attractions but the municipal transit system is pretty easy to figure out with bus and trolley stops within a few blocks. At first the room seemed small but we quickly got used to it and enjoyed it. We used the coffee maker a couple of times and kept bottled water and wine in the fridge. The continental breakfast was nice - bagels, English muffins, danish, cereal, fruit (bananas, watermelon, cantaloupe, honey dew melon), yogurt, coffee, tea, juice. It is served buffet style but the staff will fill your coffee cup. The hotel also puts out a bowl of fresh apples in the lobby every morning. They were really good. In general, the hotel staff was very accommodating, professional, and customer oriented. The only lapse we experienced occurred one evening around 10:00PM when some newly arrived guests opened our door. The front desk had mistakenly assigned them our room. A good reason to always use the chain lock when you are in the room. Judging from how well everything else was done during our stay this was obviously just one of those flukey things that happens now and then. We would definitely return to this charming hotel.

title: “Excellent airport hotel”
text:
We stayed one night in the Courtyard hotel between long distance flights. The hotel was excellent for this purpose: it was easy to get to the hotel and back to the airport with the free shuttle bus (duration of the journey around 10-15 minutes), the rooms were large, silent, very comfortable & in great condition, and the breakfast was good.
Tips: The shuttle bus picks customers at each terminal under the red sign. There are also plenty of other shuttles stopping at the same stop, and it's good to know that the name of the hotel is in this context "Courtyard" (there is another hotel called Marriott LAX). The same bus also serves two other nearby hotels, and the hotel names are shown in front of the bus.
The buffet breakfast costed 10-13 dollars, and was very nice. We also visited Disneyland between the flights which was quite easy to reach with first shuttle bus to airport and then with another shuttle bus to Disneyland (19 dollars and 40 minutes) from the airport green sign stop.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
We had a wonderful time in this hotel.The rooms are spacious, quite minimalistic, but nice.
The breakfast was delicious, best eggs benedict ever!!!!
The location was amazing. We wanted to do some shopping...we were a couple blocks from a wonderful mall and many great stores. it's not so close to the touristic area though.

title: “Wonderful”
text: This was our second visit to the Giraffe, and we thorougly enjoyed our stay. In fact, I had booked family as well, and everyone loved their experience. I am well traveled, and find the Giraffe very accommodating in every way. Yes, our room wasn't ready prior to 3, but keep in mind on the other end, checkout is at 1 pm. One great advantage is the comfortable lobby where you can have complimentary breakfast in the morning, cappuccino & cookies throughout the day, and at 5 pm, cheese, crackers and wine. The lobby in very condusive to talking and meeting friends in the city. The rooms are very comfortable and have many ammenities. The only drawback, is there is noise from the street, which you find in most NYC hotels. The doorman and lobby staff were wonderful, and when it was pouring rain, they were sure to flag a cab for us. Try the Giraffe, you won't be disappointed.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
My 2 boys (ages 6 & 8 yrs) joined my husband in SF while he was there for business. While this is primarily a "business" hotel, we were able to enjoy the hotel as well. Not s super "family friendly" hotel...but the staff is extrememly helpful, bringing a refrigerator, microwave, & rollaway bed upon request. Could not have asked for better service!
The room was a little small for the four of us, but updated, modern, and very nice.
The lobby was undergoing major renovation, but we were not affected by noise or dust. Just a little bit of an "eye sore." 
The location was great, easy walking distance to Union Square, restaurants, and the cable car.
I would stay here again.

title: “Real People, Real Deal”
text: The Dolphin is clean, quaint, inexpensive and pleasant. Yes there are mirrors on the walls, but that really helps the somewhat small rooms feel larger. But the truly great thing about the Dolphin is the owner, Holly. He's been at the helm for nearly 30 years, as has his head housekeeper. He greeted us first-timers like we were family, and personally did everything he could to make our trip work, even having his staff keep an eye on our truck parked in the street during our 10-day fishing trip. And the free morning coffee and local doughnuts weren't bad either. Now, you could stay at one of the chain motels on either side of the Dolphin...you'd pay more, and you'd get a larger room with the all character of white bread, and both you and the motel's employees would be nameless, faceless folks just passing through. Or you could be a real person, staying in a real place, with a real owner shaking your hand when you walk in the door. I know what my choice will always be when I go to San Diego.

title: “Excellent Hotel & Location”
text:
The New Yorker Offers an excellent location near to most of the major sites (Empire state building Times Squares & Broadway and also the subway and penn st station)
The hotel was clean and the staff efficient and friendly.
 Our room was very stylish with a fantastic view of the Empire state building and also the hotel provide free wi-fi to guests.
We had a great time in New York and this hotel added to our enjoyment.

title: “Great time”
text: First time in san antonio river taxi to all bars and food clean rooms great staff. Will be back

title: “Great Nights Sleep before Thanksgiving Day Parade”
text: This hotel has been revampt with bigger rooms!!! The 3 of us had a large room with 2 queen beds and 2 tv's. Even had a small refridgerater to keep items cool. The bathroom was large and had nice towels. Few drawbacks, my other half got stuck in the elevator one morning when he was out for coffee! Unfortunately the complimentary coffee isnt available until 11am! I was ready for lunch by then! But overall it was a nice 3 night stay, and the staff was friendly as well. We would return because we also loved the midtown location!

title: “Great stay!!”
text:
I just got back from the Hyatt Regency. I stayed for 3 nights on a family trip... so we had 4 rooms in total. We got a great rate on Expedia. My boyfriend and I were in a room on the 29th floor overlooking the river. We had a great view of the city and the John Hancock building. The other three rooms for the rest of the family were located high up with decent views. Our room was nice and very clean and housekeeping came each day to pick up our mess! I was impressed. Oh and the beds were suuuper comfy. The ironing board was dirty so if you plan on ironing, check the board first. 
I "liked" the facebook page prior to leaving and wrote a note about our upcoming trip. Every one of our rooms had a nice surprise!!
The elevators were a bit slow during check-out time but fine any other time... 
Oh and there's a "Ped Way" that gets you to Michigan Ave without going outside... we didn't find out about it until the last day but it's a great way to avoid some cold weather for a bit longer! The hotel is also very big and there are a lot of dining options and shops available without going outside. 
The location is great! It's just south of the river, one block from Michigan Ave. The Magnificent Mile starts just on the other side of the river on Michigan Ave. It's a short walk to the "L" and there's a bus stop to catch most buses on the corner of Michigan and E Wacker. Millennium Park and the Bean/Cloudgate are within walking distance, as is the lake.

title: “This was the best hotel/experience we have ever had!”
text:
We travel a lot and in our opinion this was our favorite place to stay of all time. We got a parlor suite, at around $600 a night, however you get what you pay for!! The rooms are a great size, master bath very nice. The bed, sheets, pillows first class all the way...best night sleep in a hotel ever. Will probably start using the Ritz for our hotel rooms now, because of this experience
Thank you

title: “Refreshing”
text: The staff is always amazing at the Fairmont. This last stay was even better. From the valet to to the housekeeper everyone was top notch. The room was immaculate and the garden outside provided a tranquil setting for breakfast.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: The place was absolutely fantastic. The decor was charming, the staff was extremely courteous and helpful, and the rooms were very comfortable. I loved having my own DirectTV in my room, and the location is absolutely magnificent. The place was huge!! With Hotel prices triple the price, it really was a steal.

title: “Great value and location”
text: We left our luggage and went out for lunch when we arrived, then had to wait another hour for our room to be ready at 2pm. Nice waiting area in lobby with CNN. Great location one block off Connecticut between Dupont Circle and Farragut metro stations; lots of restaurants and shopping. Our room at the end of the top floor had a view of the other buildings and Scott Circle, so much light that we had to close drapes at night. Nice bathroom, but only a tiny ledge for toiletries. Good shower, but NOTHING to hold on to getting in and out, and slippery enough that I had to put a towel on the tub floor for traction. No mini-fridge in a regular room. Staff was efficient and friendly and helpful on a busy weekend.

title: “Will only stay at the London now when in NYC!”
text:
Every room here is a suite, so you have a separate sitting area and plenty of space. Honestly, I had my sister and her boyfriend up to the room and they were joking about how it was bigger than her boyfriend's Manhattan apartment. 
The bathroom is beautiful, white tile, an amazing shower, so clean, so immaculate. The service was great too, everyone did an excellent job at helping and when I tried to get a cab one morning to a work thing they escorted me in the hotel's Range Rover instead. 
There are also dual electric shades/drapes on the windows so you can block out all the light. I loved the location as well, walking distance to Times Square, Central Park, the Met, MOMA, 5th Avenue....Loved this hotel!

title: “Love her for what she is”
text: The Peabody calls to mind a doddering, old grand aunt whose flowered hat is pinned on crooked. There's a certain charm to the old bird. Pun intended. The duck schtick, exuberantly embraced, is more hype than substance, but the silliness is, well, refreshing. The people seemed genuinely eager to please and old-south friendly. Booking for a busy weekend at the last minute, we were forced to a suite at an extortionist's rate. The two rooms were matchbox small but clean, tidy, and appropriately furnished. The bed/linens (though a queen) was comfortable. The bathroom was miniscule though (marginally) serviceable. That said, I'd hate to see them update it all and lose its quirks in the process. Our anniversary was acknowledged with a bottle of champagne and chocolate covered strawberries.

title: “Good Service, Great Location”
text: After seeing some of the reviews I was a little nervous... but we were pleasently surprised by the great service and quality of the room.

title: “Clean, great location, with wonderful service”
text: We enjoyed every facet of our stay at this hotel. The service was in the above average to exceptional range from everyone to the valet, room service and restaurant staff. We loved the rooms decor and how clean everything was. We are planning a future trip with the kids in early 2011.

title: “beautiful charm”
text:
this hotel is so gorgeous. i wish i can take a chunk of it home!! the checkin desk is slow but they get their things done so no complaints there. its just a shame this place is lacking a swimming pool !! when we stopped here it was mega hot !! prob as hot as florida!!
i love marble standing showers. the hotel will tell you that only the mediterannean suites have that. theyre wrong!! if you are looking for a king bed, ask for room 1228 with standing marble shower. if you want a tub only then ask for 1229!
valet is super pricey (they literally either leave your car on the block where theres a spot or theypark in the underground garage a block away). my advice is to search online for an overnight deal for garage parking... that way you will save loads of money!! i got a corporate rate on this hotel so it made everything so much sweeter. my corporate rate also got me and my guests free breakfast at the restaurant in the hotel! it was a great breakfast!! i went during a busy weekend for baltimiore. it wasn't deserted/dead til night time came. during the daytime, plenty of people out and about. yes, the area a block backwards is questionable with shops boarded up and whatnot but if you are ina small group, i'd recommend sharing a cab everyhwere. 
also sign up for kimpton intouch program! they give you $10 to raid the mini bar, whcih at checkout you can tell them what you spent it on so they dont charge your room. i believe u also get free wifi when you become a member so thats also a plus!
definitely ask for a companion goldfish! why not???!! this hotel has so much charm!! such a shame that the location is not by the water! the hotel is definitely walking distance to the water.. if you tend to speed walk, i'm sure you can make it to the waterfront by 10mins. otherwise i'd say 20mins is a good estimate of the distance.
also don't forgo their snack hours! they have morning coffee/tea available in the living room til 10am. cookie hour is 3pm(i missed that !! darn)... and then at 5pm wine reception. free alcohol and there was 1 hors duerve being served. i think smoked salmon crostini! delish!!! ive also heard there is free wii games at night for the kids but didn't get to check that out.
baltimore is a city that you can prob stay 1-2 days and be satisfied with some nice activities. its a very low key place and more relaxed.

title: “Hotel in a Seedy Area”
text: If you do not mind being on a seedy side street but in a decent hotel at a fair price then this is the place for you. The rooms were clean, beds comfortable, with double windows so very quiet. The bathrooms were adequate although hot water took about 5 minutes sometimes. People at the desk were very pleasant for New York.

title: “Luxury Is In the Details”
text: What many Americans think of today as "luxury" is really just excess or show. The management and staff of The Library Hotel understand that luxury is scrupulous attention to detail and an unfailing desire to help their guests in any way possible. My son and I stayed at The Library Hotel for four days, and the hotel itself became an important and positive part of our visit to NYC. From the continental breakfast in the "reading room" (lined with books and a baby grand piano) to the elegant and comfortable rooms, to the wide variety of interesting books (and a DVD library), the facilities are top-notch. The service is of equal quality. All of our interactions with staff were very positive - from housekeeping to bellman to front desk, staff were friendly and professional across the board. (We made extensive use of the front desk for advice on getting to our various destinations, and they were able to guide us, right down to the exact spot to stand to catch a particular bus.) The restaurant attached to the hotel, Madison and Vine, is also worth a try - good bistro food and wine with the atmosphere of a Parisian sidewalk cafe. I travel extensively, both for business and pleasure, and have already started to think of The Library as "my" hotel in New York.

title: “Great for families”
text: We stayed two nights with two children over the weekend. The rooms were clean and quiet. I would recommend requesting a room away from elevators. The breakfast area does get busy during the weekends. Parking can be a challenge as well. The location was centralized for us due to the quick access to I-10 or 410. Overall, great stay and will be back.

title: “One of the worst La Quintas I've stayed at”
text: Rooms very old and dirty. Stained carpet and old bathroom.

title: “Convenient and Affordable”
text:
This is a decent, convenient hotel with no frills. The standard room was very large for a NYC hotel, and everything was clean and comfortable. It looks a little worn around the edges, but that's typical for an older property. 
The staff was very nice and helpful and the $3.00 continental breakfast is a great deal.
The location is excellent, with subway stops at each end of the block, and Central Park a couple of blocks north and the theatre district a few blocks south. I wouldn't pay more than $100 or so to stay there, but it's a great deal for that money.
I stayed an additional night at the Warwick a few blocks away and for $20 more a night it was definitely a step up.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: This hotel is reasonably priced and well worth the money. The rooms are average, but they are very clean. Parking is nearby and you can feel safe leaving your car there. It is also very close to the trolleys and Market Square. The best part about the hotel are the owners. They are very helpful. They recommended places to eat and visit. They even made us a reservation with a table overlooking the water. Very nice couple and great customer service. I would highly recommend staying here.

title: “Great Location and Hotel”
text: It is hard to ever go wrong with a Marriott! This Marriot is great! The location is nice and close to a BART station as well as close to Union Square. I have stayed here about 5 times and never been disappointed. The staff is very friendly. The concierge is very helpful. It is a short cab ride from AT&T Park, about a $13 fare. The rooms are always clean and quite. I did stay once and we were put off in this weird part and it was like walking through a maze to get through the room, but it wasn’t too bad for us youngsters. For older folks, they were EASILY get lost...so that was kinda annoying. But I think that was just a fluke thing and all my other stays have been superb! I hate that the bar/restaurant closes sooo early, but most Marriott’s are all the same in that regard! There is a great diner down the street that the concierge recommended when we tried to eat after the restaurant was closed! The Marriott has a nice little Starbucks located right inside so you dont have to even leave for that morning cup of joe!

title: “I love this hotel and its staff”
text:
I have just returned home from a fantastic holiday in USA.San Francisco then Los Angeles finally Las Vegas.We stayed in the Sofitel it was wonderful.Although renovations are in place it is still a great place to stay.The staff were friendly polite and could not do enough for us.They do not know the meaning of the word NO.
Beautiful bathroom with plenty towels and accessories which are continually replenished turn down service if required and chocolates what more do you want?
The bed was the best bed I have ever slept in.As for expensive for breakfast I totally disagree.Breakfast is served at a lovely table on beautiful plates with lovely cutlery orange juice flows and coffee never ends.OK nearby you can go to a deli which we tried its ok.But for a couple bucks more you are served a bit special. Worth it I can assure you.
Shopping is easy with the Beverly Centre across the road with every shop you need.
I will be back in LA sometime for a holiday and I can tell you The Sofitel will be my first choice of where to stay they sold it to me on my recent visit.
Ohhhhhhhhh how I wish we got that service over here.
Linz

title: “could have been worse”
text:
I just stayed at this hotel and I think they must have done a little remodeling because the other reviews are from 2005. It was not the best place to stay but I did not want to spend twice that amount just for a place to hang my head for two days.
I did not see any bugs and the bathroom was clean enough. The tap water did not seem to work in the room but the refrigerator was nice to put take out food in. The bed was clean and the room itself had no stains and no holes. The door lock was good.
I took the elevator and it was always reliable. There is a winding corridor but you get used to going in the right direction. Because it is an old building, there is a mildew smell when you get on the elevator but I did not notice a smell in my room. The air conditioner was pretty good. If you want cheap and you don't want to stay too long, you could stay here. There is everything you need in walking distance and even at night I did not have to worry about being mugged etc.

title: “safe, reliable but isolated”
text:
I wanted to stay with hilton property and wanted to stay in the smu / northpark area so i tried this hotel and it was ok. nothing special but no problems. didn't get the requests I indicated but when i asked again at check in they made a change. the hotel was clean except for the stained bedspread, limited tv channels, it's an old hotel that was partially renovated a few years ago. 
parking was free and easy, getting in and out of the hotel is a bit tricky and you have to drive anywhere.
business center computers were slow.
front desk staff - nothing exceptional, just answered standard manner. recommended an hour anywhere i asked to drive to - even though it was only 15 minutes away.

title: “Will not return”
text: The breakfast is very good and if you don't mind crowds, the drinks before dinner were also a plus. But we had so many problems, we'd never go back. We heard there were lots of families and kids and, of course, they are often noisy. But we didn't think there would be drunk teenagers/college students wrestling in the elevators or screaming and running up and down the halls all night long. The room was like the other ES hotels...a little small but nice to have the two rooms. However, the air conditioner in our room rattled and made the strangest noises at all hours of the day. The telephone couldn't receive outside calls; when we ordered wakeup calls on two days, the calls began 90 minutes before our scheduled time (imagine getting woken up every TEN minutes, beginning at 6:15 AM). The desk people kept telling us it was getting fixed but we had to disconnect the phones and use our cells. The alarm clock, by the way, was also broken; the time was accurate but it read AM when it was PM and the alarm function couldn't be programmed (wasted lots of time trying). The TV in the bedroom looked about ten years old; there was a small flat screen in the front room but the aspect ratio on the picture was stretched out which made the TV unwatchable. Room service food was poor;. The service people were friendly but we had a Ceasar salad which was simply lettuce and some cheese and a watery dressing. The burgers were flat and a step below McDonalds; the fries were just tasteless. Finally, we travelled with another couple and checked out together.
