Both of us had signed on for the internet service so we could do emails (many hotels offer wireless connections for free but not this one) but when our friends got their bill, they realized that instead of $9.95 a day, they had been double and tripled charged (one day, they were charged $9.95 three times!). They were also charged for a movie they didn't watch ($13.95). The front desk guy said that they had probably clicked on one of the sign-on buttons too many times (sounds like really primitive software which doesn't catch mistakes like this) and implied that it was actually THEIR fault. When we got our bill, we were stunned to see that we also had been double and triple charged. The front desk guy acted like we had some kind of conspiracy going on or were just plain stupid rednecks (actually, we're all from NYC). He removed the charges but was quite displeased; he didn't make eye contact, didn't apologize and when he printed out the corrected bill, he handed us the paper, mumbled a thank you and then walked away to chat with another desk person and totally ignored us.

title: “Enjoyed my stay at Empire”
text:
At The Empire now on my 5th and final night in NYC. I don't wanna speak too soon but so far all I have is love for this hotel. I was nervous after a few reviews but I'm starting to think some people are just professional complainers. The staff was friendly. I don't know how helpful they were because I never needed them for anything other than an ironing board and towels. But it doesn't take much to please me. As long as the place is clean and the Empire is definitely clean. I only used the hotel for sleep. Pros
*early checkin (1230)
*near the 1 train, 2 stops from TSQ
*3 min walk to subway
*restaurants, shops, snack shops downstairs
*Location is directly across the street from Met. I watched from only 10 ft away as Sarah Jessica Parker, Valentino, Anne Hathaway, and Anna Wintour walked the Red carpet at the Met for Valentino's fall gala!!!
*comfortable beds
Cons
* Not a lot of fast food in The area. If ur looking for a quick, cheap, meal you will have to jump on the subway. Also, the restaurants in The area are really expensive. 
*The elevator didn't sound very reliable
*Still don't get the one door on the shower
*no place to store luggage.
I got the hotel through Priceline for $230/ngt. I Thgt that was expensive but its NY. However, I wld hve never paid $500 to stay here. But overall I can't wait to book the Empire for my next trip to NY.

title: “A Dirty Bathroom, Fuzzy Televisions, and Rotten Fruit--How awesome...”
text:
My stay at this Hyatt was a nightmare.
I stayed there this past week. I got in relatively late from a night of work, checked in, and entered my room. I always look at the bathroom first, and I was completely disturbed to find that my toilet contained debris and my shower was visibily dirty. I called the front desk, and they told me they'd have someone clean it up. There was no apology. I stepped out to grab something to eat.
When I returned, it appeared that there were some cursory cleaning, but there was still debris in the toilet. I was tired, so I went to my bed and turned on the television. The television was extremely blurry. I was like--for real? This room is costing a fortune, and all I got was a dirty bathroom and blurry television. I call the front desk again, and they tell me they'll send an engineer. I wait for almost an hour, and the engineer arrives. The engineer told me that that's the way the television is. Again, no apology.
So, the next day, my assistant calls the Hyatt and tells them of my miserable experience. They send up some fruit and a bottle of wine as an amenity and leave a nice phone message. I go to bed.
When I get up after my second night, I was planning to eat some of the fruit for breakfast. When I picked up the plum, the plum was spoiled, so the juice from the plum ran into their other fruit, thus making the other fruit inedible. 
So, in short, this place is a disaster and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. I spent my third night at the Setai, which was both cheaper and way more lovely.

title: “The Peninsula Does Not Disappoint”
text: Our stay at the Peninsula met all my expectations. The room was spacious, clean and was cleaned well daily. The restaurant in the lobby had nice selections for breakfast and lunch with live orchestral music during lunch. The fitness center was well outfitted and well kept equipment. Location was in the Magnificent Mile specifically across the street from Saks and quarter block from Neiman.

title: “amazing value for money”
text:
loved it
Clean, great location , perect for sightseeing around LA
dont waste your money in 5 star -this has everything u could need
staff amazing and best of all we ran into the playboy bunnies!!!!
20mins to santa monica, 10 mins to rodeo drive

title: “Great location”
text:
This hotel is in a great location ,right on Grant Park. The reception/foyer area is small but tidy. The staff helpful enough. The room was small but clean, in fact the designer of the room is to congratulated. How he got a shower with bath, toilet and sink in such a small are is amazing!!!!!
The hotel does however need a complete refurb as it is very tired BUT it would not be as well priced then.
The bar has a good atmosphere and the restaurant is OK but there are better and cheaper within a 20 minute walk. The waiting staff in the evening were fine but I think they scoured Chicago to find the Rudest, Most Miserable, Most unhelpful people in the city to set you up fo the day on the morning shift.
Overall it is good value but if the hotel itself is important to you look elsewher.
If you fly out of terminal 5 at O'Hare airport you need to be aware that there is NO food available once you have gone through security.

title: “Excellent Central Location”
text:
Excellent Place to hold a meeting. We used thier conference facility. Great Central location.
Modern / Artistic rooms were attractive...may not be right for everyone.

title: “EXCELLENCE!!!”
text:
Every time that I stay at the Drury Plaza I am more and more amazed at the reception that I receive from the time that I pull in at the valet parking to the registration to the staff that you run into during your stay. There are so many things that are great about the hotel and the staff but one thing that stands out to me is the greeting that you receive from literally every single staff member that you come in contact with. Everyone, and I mean everyone greets you and they are so eager to help you with anything that you need. I always feel very welcomed and I have the feeling of home. The Drury Plaza team is definitely the best hotel staff I have come across in all of the traveling that I do.
Sincerely,
Julie
Houston, Texas

title: “Keep coming back”
text: Great place to stay. Close to everything. I absolutely loved the decor, the service and the luxury rooms. Will recommend.

title: “"Simple rooms, close to Airport, average place to stay"”
text: This Hotel is close to airport and that was the reason for selecting it. Rates are ok. Free Shuttle connects this hotel with airport. You can walk to bus stand which is near the hotel for travelling to various places at Los Angeles, specially to visit beaches Santa Monica & Venice beaches. The rooms are average & we had taken room facing airport and could see planes landing. But inspite of room facing airport there was no noise/disturbance which was good. The Hotel lobby has nice open restaurant for having breakfast. I would recommend this hotel only if you have come to see/explore Los Angeles & need place to spend night/keep luggage or you are in transit & need accomodation close to airport. Staff at reception & travel desk were nice & helpful. All tourist buses which you may have booked for seeing Los Angeles comes to hotel for pickup.

title: “Nice Hotel, But the Omni Spoiled Us”
text: We've been lucky enough to have snagged a great deal at the Omni San Diego for the past few years during the holidays, but unfortunately this year, the Omni didn't offer very good rates. So, I checked out the Hilton Gaslamp on-line and saw that it was in the same area so I thought we'd give it a try. First off, the location is great! It's within walking distance to everything, and our room overlooked the San Diego Convention Center and a dog park below. The hotel sits at the entrance to the Gaslamp district, but is very quiet. However, when we checked into our room on Christmas night, we did not have a comforter or blanket on our bed: just a sheet. There was no honor bar either. And, when we realized we forgot to pack a hairbrush, we found out that the hotel does not have a gift shop for essentials, so we were sent across the street to a mini-mart where we did not find a hairbrush. Parking 2 blocks away was less expensive than the $30 a night fee at the hotel, (we were charged $15 at the garage) but parking in the lot adjacent to the Omni was far cheaper. Overall, I'd say this was an okay hotel, but we still like the Omni better!

title: “Great Sleeping Experience”
text:
For some reason the air conditioner ran nonstop so I slept great! 
The bathrooms are a little tired but the rooms are current. 
I thought the location on the 16th street mall was great.

title: “Enjoyed It”
text: We went to Philadelphia with some friends on our way to see the sights on the way to NYC. We chose Hampton Inn because of its indoor pool...we were there with 4 kids and thought evening entertainment would be good. Our rooms were clean and nice sized. It was a $25.00 cab ride from the airport. The staff was very friendly, helpful, and even funny. It was a very laid back atmosphere (not slacking, but just a happy, unpretentious, and comfortable). We walked to a great pizza place for dinner (there is also a diner that delivers right across the street), and then we hung at the pool and hot tub at night. The sights were about a 15 -20 minute stroll away, a couple minute cab ride. There were warm cookies at night and a very nice continental breakfast in the morning, with both hot and cold foods, hot tea, coffee, juices and milk. The rooms were clean, nice sized. I would stay there again.

title: “This is a Hyatt?!?! Could have been much, much better”
text:
First the positive.
Reservation mixup. 
Made reservation on booking.com on 12/31/11 while in Austin, TX. Erroneously made the reservation for Feb 3, 2012 and not Jan 3, 2012. Amanda Burroughs at the Hyatt changed the reservation while we were in Baltimore, MD with a $10 increase in price. This was great and I appreciate it. This is great and they really didn't have to accomodate us especially since the reservation was "non-refundable." So, thanks.
The service. 
The staff was helpful. The valet service was great. They helped us with our two sleeping kids. Helped us with a luggage and whisked our car away. The front desk staff helped us up to the room and gave us a hand getting us settled in. 
The room. 
The room was large and clean with two enormous beds. Since we were travelling with two small kids the bed space and spacious room was more than enough for us. We were in a Queen Queen Room.
The location.
The location of this hotel is just incredible. We were right in the middle of the city and went by foot to where we had to be on Jan. 3rd.
The negative.
While I Paid $189.00 + $28.73 in tax + $37 for valet parking, which represents a 34% savings off their regular price and that is great, but was it still worth the price? My response is a resounding, "NO!" Why? The room, the internet, the breakfast, the noise.
The room.
I know that they are updating the rooms, but these rooms are really, really, really in bad shape. The faucet handles fell off. The carpet was stained. Shower didn't work properly. Toilet made a horrible noise. Etc., Etc., Etc., Luxurious? No. 
The internet.
Not free. Not included in the hotel room. I just don't understand this at all. This is a Hyatt. Internet should be included.
The breakfast.
What breakfast? We were on our own. I know we saved 34% off the regular price. Thanks. But no breakfast? Come on.
The noise.
They warn you about the construction noise because they are refurbishing the hotel rooms, but what they don't warn you about is the noise from the corridor. I'm not sure what those doors are made of, but they are NOT sound proof. My hope is that with the refurbishing of the hotel rooms, a large room like ours will have a small foyer before entering the hotel room in order to reduce noise. Rooms that have 15 foot+ ceilings need foyers to cancel noise from the corridor. Without this small addition, noise just amplifies within the room and even mouse peeps sound like elephant stomps.

title: “Great location, service, amenities, and quiet rooms”
text: Loved, loved, loved this hotel - the location couldn't be more perfect, the rooms are nicely appointed, and did I mention location? Service was great - few hotels in New York do you walk into and feel warmth and sincerity from their staff, but the staff at the Mansfield were all extremely friendly and down-to-earth. I will definitely stay again.

title: “A haven in Manhattan”
text:
Arrived the day after Sandy for scheduled business trip. Wasn't sure what to expect given the chaos and difficulty of getting into NYC. The moment I walked into the Library I felt calm and comfortable. The staff members were polite, friendly and efficient. My room - Journalism - was lovely and comfortable. The Reading Room was delightful - you could make a light evening meal from the wine and cheese buffet and the atmosphere was very restful. Breakfast the next morning was a well-stocked Continental. I ventured up to the top floor bar - it was packed and very lively. The Madison and Vine restuarant provided a very nice evening meal the next night. Of course, the location is excellent - you can walk to anywhere in MidTown easily. And..I got a good night's sleep, a rare thing in a hotel so central.
I will definitely return.

title: “Nicest little hotel in New York City!”
text: Hotel Giraffe is the "nicest little hotel in New York City!" The service is impeccable as everyone from the doorman to the front desk people bend over backwards to be helpful. My standard room was more than generous in size and the accommodations were more than comfortable. It is centrally located between Gramercy Park and Midtown which makes those areas, Broadway and the lower east side a comfortable walk. The best thing about the "Giraffe" is the amenities which included a buffet breakfast (cereals, hard boiled eggs, croissants, fruit, yogurt ,coffee and cappuccino) with newspaper. 24/7 complementary coffee and cappuccino. Also they include at no charge, a wine and cheese bar between 5 and 7 pm. They also include a free bottle at bedside. The only below par amenity was the shampoo and conditioner. It needs to be upgraded. They do not have a restaurant, however, they have an agreement with the two restaurants next door that provide room service. I will definitely stay here again!

title: “Excellent Location and Staff!”
text: Both by husband and I thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The hotel has several restaurants on-site and Durty Nelly's Irish Pub was the best. Both Jesse and Michael A. deserve special recognition for providing excellent customer service and remembering guests when the return to the hotel. The rooms are extremely clean and provide a great view of downtown. The location is right on the riverwalk so its convenient to shopping and restaurants. We would definitely recommend this hotel and stay again!

title: “An Anniversary Stay to Remember”
text:
My wife and I chose the Affinia Dumont for our 20th wedding anniversary based on traveler reviews from Tripadvisor. We knew the minute we arrived in the elegantly styled, softly fragrant lobby that we were in for a wonderful and memorable stay. From the friendliness of the doormen and bellmen, to the care and concern of the front desk receptionist, to some unique personalized treatment by the staff, nothing could have made our stay at the Dumont more memorable. 
The Junior Suite was larger than we expected with a warm, comtemporary decor. The bed was very comfortable and draped with a lush down comforter; the kitchen was clean and spacious; the spa downstairs was welcoming and had all the expected amenties along with a courteous and knowledgeable staff. If that's not enough, the view out of our corner window was spectacular: the classic New York skyline, Chrysler building included! 
We found the Dumont's location convenient, just a short cab or subway ride to all the important destinations. The Barking Dog restaurant adjoining the Dumont offered an interesting, reasonably priced menu and the Martinis were terrific. We were sorry we didn't discover the Barking Dog sooner! Not a day's gone by since we've been home that we haven't enjoyed remembering our visit to Manhattan. Our next trip is in the planning and the Affinia Dumont is the ONLY place we'll consider staying.

title: “Best Wedding Ever!”
text:
I had my wedding reception at the Warwick Melrose. The staff there are the most hard working, attentive, and happy people you will ever encounter at a hotel. The true star at the Warwick Melrose is Bethany B., the wedding coordinator. Because of her careful planning and wise counsel, I had countless guests tell me that our wedding was one of the most beautiful and most fun they'd ever been to. Thank you, Bethany and all the staff at the Warwick Melrose!
P.S. The food was incredible too!

title: “Unique and very comfortable”
text: We stayed here 3 nights in March 2003 and really loved it. We had walked by these cottages on previous trips to Pacific Beach, and always wondered what it would be like to stay here, since we both love sounds of the ocean and the beach ambience. We don't normally spend this much on a hotel, but it was worth it. Cottages are clean, comfortable, and kitchens have everything you need. The decks are great too; but next time I'd go a little later in the year to take best advantage of them because it rained and was a little chilly to spend much time outside. I'm sure we'll be back to the Crystal Pier!

title: “Older hotel that use a makeover buy was still nice.”
text:
I stayed here on May 20th for one night on my way to San Antonio. The hotel was easy to find and had plenty of parking. Check in was quick and the staff very nice. Our room was dated yet very clean. Our bed was awesome and the linens white and crisp. Overall it was a good value for what I paid. I booked on name your own price on priceline and won $59.00 plus fees and taxes
We looked at the food menu and it seemed pricy so we opted for one of many places to eat within walking distance. 
I can't com

title: “Substandard Hotel Room”
text:
My husband and I, together with our baby stayed in River Hotel a week ago. We booked a superior room with kitchenette for a 4 nights stay and had requested for a crib and kettle upon making the reservation as we would be bringing our baby along and needed all those stuffs. That was the reason why we had booked the room with kitchenette too. We were being advised that our requests had been being taken care of. 
When we arrived at our hotel room 903, no crib was prepared for us (which was fine as we could call recept and ask for it). But to our horror, the so called 'kitchenette' was just a corner with a squeaking microwave and coffee maker! There was no bath tub and the sink was outside the toilet which was noisy when we need to cleanup and the baby was sleeping. We had paid extra actually to upgrade to a room with kitchenette and we had specifically mentioned that we have a baby and would need the room to be baby friendly! We were not told that the kitchenette was substandard and without a kettle. When we called the reception and explained that we do need a kettle to boil water for the baby, and we need at least a plate for the microwave,we were being told to go and buy those stuffs ourselves as the hotel does not provide! We should be advised that the kitchenette is not a normal kitchenette in the first place and we would not have booked this hotel since we cannot compromise with a baby in tow. 
The aircon was really noisy and the microwave squeaked loudly. The room feels like a motel room. I should have paid $20 more for a room in Sheraton where we have special rates. The only reason we booked River Hotel was because of the kitchenette it promised.
The frontdesk staffs were friendly which was the only consolation...

title: “Perfect Spot for Washington Tourism”
text: We stayed here 3 nights. Perfect spot for touring Washington. Close to the White House and the Mall. Plenty of restaurants nearby. There is room service via a neighboring pub and plenty of take out options too. We ordered in Chinese one night. Reservations, check in, welcome and maid service were great. Check out was also fast and efficient. Staff very helpful. Room was large and had a kitchenette with stove, fridge, microwave, sink etc. You could cook your own meals if you wanted to. No breakfast, but there are breakfast cafes close by and you can always get a few things from the 7/11 around the corner. Coffee machine in the room that was replenished daily and there was coffee in the lobby too. Bathroom was spacious. Absolutely nothing to complain about, except perhaps a lack of towel rail space in the bathroom. Good value for money too if you book early via the hotel website.

title: “Okay room for one night or more”
text: This was not the best La Quinta we have stayed at , but the room was clean and seemed to have been remodeled within a few years. There wasn't much to their continental breakfast other then the make your own waffles. You are located in an industrial area of San Antonio and about 15 minutes from downtown.

title: “The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly”
text:
First the good:
The location is excellent! Park Central is central to some of New York City's most famous locations. It is just a few blocks from Times Square, Central Park, Rockefeller Center, Ed Sullivan Theatre, Broadway theatres, and Carnegie Hall. In addition, the double-decker sight seeing busses have a pick-up location right outside of the hotel. There is also a subway stop just outside of one of the doors. The area is nice and my husband and I felt completely comfortable walking late at night. The lobby is nice, as are the rooms. The rooms are good sized, by New York City standards, and are tastefully decorated. The bathrooms are plenty big enough. 
The bad: 
The elevators are PAINFULLY slow. It seems to be more of a problem when going down than when going up. I have no idea why, but that was our assessment of the situation. HOWEVER, they are supposedly upgrading their elevators and we did see a crew doing what appeared to be some signficant construction. So maybe this situation will rectify itself soon. We were only on the 6th floor, so we often took the stairs down, which really wasn't a big deal. If you plan to use the Internet, plan again. It is expensive, and like the elevators, painfully slow. 
The ugly, and I mean ugly:
When we arrived to the hotel on Saturday, we checked into our room and turned on the air conditoning. When we returned late that night, the room was defintely cooler, but not the frigid cold that you often get when in hotel rooms that are cooled with individual units. We noticed this, but proceeded to bed. When we woke up Sunday, the room felt somewhat cool, but the unit didn't seem to be pumping out cold air. When we returned that night, it was obvious that the air was not working. We called the front desk, who told us that indeed the air was not working and that they were hoping to have the situation resolved soon and asked for our patience. My husband and I understood and dealt with the situation. Needless to say, the next morning, the room was VERY hot, as during our stay New York City was having record heat. We got ready for the day and were confident that all would be resolved when we returned that afternoon in order to freshen up for dinner. No such luck. It was still hot and now humidity was starting to settle in. Again, we inquired and again were told that it was broken, being repaired, but they believed that it would be on when we returned for the evening. We we returned from dinner, still no air. By Tuesday morning when we had only gotten about 2 hours of sleep because of the heat, I demanded that something be done. I talked to a manager named Denis who became loud during our conversation and attracted the attention of others checking in. He told me to call Orbitz and that something would be worked out, but he was pretty rude about it, even though I felt that I was being pretty courteous and polite. We did call Orbitz and they managed to get us $422 refunded, which apparently is the equivalent of 50% off of three nights of our stay. 
Many people have complained about the staff being rude; however, with the exception of Denis, my husband and I never found this to be the case. We always made it a point to great them by name and ask how they were before starting into our conversation. 
All in all, because of the location, I would consider staying here again, particulary if I knew that the temperature would be controlled.

title: “you get what you pay for...never again!!!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Sky Hotel for one night. We could hear everything going on in the next room ( and they weren't loud) therefore, did not gt muchsleep and the smell from the new plastic on the head board of the bed make us feel sick. The rooms have only one small window that looked out into the closed courtyard and everyone walks by your window. This hotel should be advertised as motel.
Management would not refund us for the the following nights that we were supposed to stay, actually the general manager was rude. 
Don't be fooled by the pictures on the internet or dragged in by their promotiona rates.... and just a response to the hotel saying these bad reviews are not true... this is true! 
Never again !

title: “Great Location”
text:
I was pleased to find that the previous reviews of this hotel were pretty much accurate. The small and somewhat crowded lobby, lack of ironing board or iron in the room, and the need for a room key swipe to use the elevator fully prepared me for my experience. These wre mere observations and small details when it came to the nice clean and up to date rooms and the unbelieveable convenience of being in the best location imaginable for NYC. I am always happy to see internet access included too. Kudos to this hotel for tech! I would absolutely stay here again. 
I booked our two night stay on Hotels.com and payed about 220 per night. What a great deal for such a nice room. The price to value ratio is perfect for a city visit. This place is pefect for tourists or business travelers. 
Only criticism is the shower setup. The baths are built "cruiseship style" with the entire bathroom floor as the shower stall. the floors were not pitched to the drain resulting in a very cold puddle of water (in spite of a pile of towels used as a dam) until the poor maid came in and mopped each day. This should be addressed by the hotel ASAP but I am sure that it will be a costly repair in order to correct it. In the meantime the hotel needs to provide foam type squeegees for in room use. Not a deal breaker however. I give this hotel a thumbs up!

title: “Signs would help.”
text:
I’m from Charlotte but have not lived there in years so when my friend decided to have his 30th birthday party there I decided to go. I also decided to try out the new vibrant UPTown area. I looked around and noticed that the W brand of hotel had opened an aLoft right downtown. I love the W and I love the Starwood points so I decided to go there. I purchased the hotel off of expedia, my first mistake as SPG doesn’t give you any credit if you buy off of a site other than theirs. I learned this the hard way.
 After having fun getting our car from Avis from the airport we get to 210 Trade street and cannot find the hotel for the life us up. We end up calling them and finding out the entrance is on a completely different street. We do the Charlotte one-way street shuffle and finally get to something that looks like it might be the entrance to the aLoft but you can’t really tell. We are also supposed to use the valet parking because of coming and going privileges that you didn’t get in the car park. That was an extra $20 a day, plus tips when leaving. 
We park in what looks like the valet area and wait, and wait and wait. It’s 9pm at this point so they should have enough staff and we have a dinner to make at 9:30pm. I leave the car with my travel partner and attempt to find the entrance to the aLoft. I know we’re in the right place because I can see the building with the big neon light’s saying aLoft. There are some elevators in a little entrance that has an aLoft sign on the wall that only says aLoft. Nothing else. I stand at the elevators for about ten minutes before getting frustrated. Seems the elevators are for the whole complex and not just the aloft so EVERYONE was using them. During this time I had to ask someone where check-in was and was told on the 5th floor.
There was no indication of this what so ever in that little lobby. Really, all they needed to do was put a sign there saying check-in is on the 5th floor.
I then go and find stars that I might be able to actually make it to the lobby and check in. The stars at the street level where locked so I couldn’t use them. I went into the middle of the epicenter and went up as far as I could only to make it back to the elevators I had been at but on the 4th floor now. So I had to use them, there was no way around it. So I waited and waited and finally got to the lobby. 
Ughhhh.
Once there though the hotel was fine. We got a nice corner room on the 11th floor. Modern and somewhat funky, which I like. The room was a bit small with very little storage and almost no place to put a towel to hang up if there is more than one of you. I find this funny because they are a “green hotel” so they only replace your towels if you put them on the floor. So I got new towels very day.
After the check-in ordeal everything was fine. Would I stay there again. Probably not, the hassle of parking and waiting for the elevator outweigh the funky cool feeling you get.

title: “One word: Amazing”
text:
Outstanding service, incredible amenities, and great views. Anytime you can stay at a Four Seasons, definitely do.
The one in downtown Seattle is close to attractions, shopping, and outstanding restaurants.
An experience that I will always hold as the baseline for hotels I stay at in the future.

title: “A convenient place to stay in New York”
text: This hotel is in a very convenient place indeed. It is almost opposite the Empire State Building and a straight walk down from Central Park. Be careful of the extra charges that stopping inside the city entails. We were surprised to see that we were charged an extra £100 per person per night for the privilege of stopping within the city walls, so to speak! A lot of money for four people on an 11 night stay! Very clean and friendly place.

title: “Classy - Great bath robes”
text:
The Hotel is on a quiet street, right near the Fleet Center, the location is good and everything is well within walking distance.
The Hotel has well decorated modern, sleek, stylish rooms with very helpfull staff. The FREE breakfast in the mornings went down well, the bagels are a must!
There are a great selection of in room movies, games, video jukebox and a class touch screen alarm clock.
There is a bar next door called Porters, excellent friendly irish/bostonian bar, which serves ICE COLD beers at a reasonable price, the 1st time we walked in they even asked if we'd like to start a tab.
Definately would stay there again. An EXCELLENT hotel choice for people who like modern, chic boutique style hotels.

title: “Great location”
text: This hotel is wonderful. Service is doting and personalized without being obsequious. Room service dinner had the quality of a superior 5-star restaurant. Good for families or the corporate traveller.

title: “Down and up”
text:
Visited Seattle recently for a meeting held in the W.
When I called to let them know I'd be arriving late (around 10:30 PM), they said no problem, and that parking shouldn't be an issue. However, arriving that late, I was stuck with one of the rooms facing the garage. While the interior of the room was nice, facing the fencing and parking lot made it feel like we were in prison. Also, the bathtub drain was slow/clogged. Very depressing and gloomy. Also, they had run out of parking for the night, so we needed to park in the big garage next door ourselves, which was a hassle that late at night when you just want to check in and go to sleep.
It took my asking for a different room after 2 nights (they didn't voluntarily let me know rooms opened up), I got a room now facing the street. Much better. But the early experience with the garage-facing room had already soured me on the place. Really, it would have been better without a window, and just a big picture simulating an outdoor scene or something.

title: “great place to stay”
text: This was a great place to stay. The location was great. The staff was very helpful with directions and recommendations. I have been to New York before but this was by far the best place I stayed. I would strongly recommend it to anyone. The buffet breakfast was great also.

title: “Good hotel in a good location”
text:
We booked two rooms at the Millennium Un Plaza through Expedia. The hotel is located on 44th Street and 1st Avenue so not quite in the heart of Manhattan but still in a very good location. 10 mins walk to Grand Central, probably about 20 to Bloomingdales and 25 to Abercrombies/Tiffany/Central Park etc.
We were greeted by the doorman who helped us inside with our bags. Reception was efficient rather than friendly but all the bell boys were very helpful and friendly.
Our rooms were on the top 38th floor so we had good views facing the Empire State building. The hotel has two towers and our rooms faced partially onto the other tower. However all windows have reflective glass so you have complete privacy. 
The rooms were good sized with plenty of space. One room had a king bed and the other twins (as requested). Although the rooms were booked on seperate bookings, the hotel had put us close to each other. I'd emailed them to request this.
The bedroom was lovely - very comfortable and clean. The TV had a range of TV and pay movies. A desk and chair were provided as well as a sofa. The only negative point about the room furnishings was the lack of a mirror. Two mirrors were provided in the bathroom but this meant that one of us was held up getting ready while the other used the mirrors for make-up and hair.
The bathroom was not as nice as the bedroom. Nothing wrong with it other than it needed decorated - rust around the door hinges and cracked ceiling plaster. Minor points and otherwise the bathroom was clean and tidy. Again a good size room with a good shower. Toiletries provided (by Gilchrist & Soames).
My one gripe is about the air-conditioning. It's good but noisy. I don't sleep well in noisy rooms and the first night I struggled to sleep. After that it was fine but I don't know whether this just affected our room or was generally the case throughout the hotel.
The hotel was busy with tourists from all over the world and airline crews use it as well. It has a tennis court on the 37th floor and a spa and pool on the 28th.
Checking out was smooth and both the bell boy and door man went out of their way to make sure we got a SUV taxi back to JFK. They were both really friendly and gave the impression that nothing was too much trouble. The doorman even remembered that we'd been there 6 nights and were from Scotland. We hadn't spoken to him since our arrival!
We didn't try any of the hotel dining facilities. I'd recommend John's deli on 44th and 2nd and Bully's on 44th and Lexington. Both excellent for breakfast.

title: “Good place and nice room with blankets”
text: The room was very nice and blankets were very nice. There was a spare blanket in the room cool. Also shuttle schedule with Nelson Shuttle Service at [--] was excellent. I used the spare blanket very clean for a Best Western 5 stars on clean rooms. Also a very good cleaning staff in are room. One suggest is wish they would put two spare Blankets in the rooms someday. Since the room had two queen beds. The indoor pool was great with Hot tub. Also staff is very friendly and helpful. Also, had to verify with celebrity what pier for Nelson Shuttle service since Best Western wrote down the wrong pier information from pier 91 to Pier 66. I am glad i change this information since Best Western wrote down the wrong pier information for the driver. Other than that a good place to stay from the Airport Seattle. I would stay there again. Nice food near by too.

title: “A Perfect Choice for us!!”
text:
We chose to spend 2 nights at the Hilton after viewing this site and couldn't be happier with our choice! We knew it would be close to Universal and Hollywood so the location was just right. 
When I originally called (just last week--3 days prior to our trip) the only room available was an "accessibility" room at a rate of $169. Our family of 4 didn't mind having this room, but at check in, we mentioned that we didn't need an accessibiliy room so if something else was available, that would be fine as well.
The woman checking us in couldn't have been more helpful in checking other options. Sure enough, she offered to upgrade us to a jr. suite--for no additional charge!!
Our 2 sons were THRILLED to be on the 16th floor overlooking Universal. What a view!!
Our room was extremely clean, the beds were heavenly and we found a lovely fruit and water basket waiting for us after our CityWalk evening visit.
We easily walked to the park and even walked down the hill to take advantage of a metro ride to Hollywood Blvd.(El Capitan theater, Kodak, Grahmans, etc.)--just one stop away. So simple and convenient!!
Loved the pool and the spa as well--clean and relaxing. We brought coffee and muffins (from the gift shop) there for breakfast. 
I only wonder why this hotel doesn't offer a coffee bar and quick/easy snack buffet for those families wanting to zip to the park. Their buffet options look beautiful, but are pricey and would take too much time for families on the go.

title: “Good value and premiere location.”
text: Connected to the Rivercenter Mall and right on the Riverwalk, this hotel is also just a short walk from the Alamo. The location alone makes the property very attractive. The staff was very friendly and the rooms were fairly spacious and clean. On the downside, on-site parking was pricey (not surprising for this area) and hot water seemed almost nonexistent in the evenings. We were on the 25th floor. Overall, this is our first choice accomadation on the Riverwalk.

title: “Ups and downs”
text:
Today we returned form a 5 day trip to NYC. We picked the Skyline hotel because it had rooms for 4 (we travelled with our 2 young kids).
Ups: more than enough space in the room (suite), concierge staff and bell boys were friendly and effective. Front desk staff were not too bad. Also the guys at the bar were fine. Maids performed well, the room was kept very clean.
Downs: restaurant staff were terrible during breakfast. One lady calling herself "Her Royal Highness" at the bill (.. served by....) didn't give any attention to customers and never had a smile on her face. Only contact was her throwing (yes... with a bang) the bill on the table, while we just started eating. One other woman (being referred to as Mrs. BMW) tried to make up for this behaviour a bit.
Don't expect much from the pool, the water quality is poor and during most of the day you cannot swim because it is used as a local swimming school. We also missed a coffee maker in the room, no coffee available in the lobby either. Like another reviewer we had also problems with our TV and the safe. Luckily our room had two TV's, so at least one was working. The safe worked again after I gave it a reset by turning it off and on again.

title: “Elegance And Comfort”
text:
This establishment offers stunning Back Bay views, and is in a very convenient area... just steps away from one of the Old Town Trolley stops. The rooms are modern, yet comfortable, and the staff is always friendly and willing to point you in the right direction.
Hotel 140 - 1-866-451-1440 - www.hotel140.com

title: “A weekend at Grandmas apartment”
text: This place is OK, and its' location is excellent being next to the park and easy to find in the Hilltop area. Rooms are in need of a facelift, but Shell, the new owners are promising that. Miss not having a gym or a pool, or a hot tub. Our room was a King sudio, nice size for a hotel room, and it had a kichenette with minimal cookware (forget about hotpads, dish cloths, or even paper towels). The microwave was low-tech, and we had to cart it to another room to plug it it, as it had a polarized plug, and they are not many so-equiped recepticles. Most of the eletrical stuff is pretty beat up, and the door lock is a little flimsy. For being a littl worn, the room was really clean with one exception, the ceiling fan is caked with dirt. I would have appreciated a little heat but the boiler was not on, and none of the windows closed tight. Still the place has some charm, and the resturant food and breakfast buffet are really good. Hopefully Shell will do there usual fine job of restoration in 2012.

title: “Not Bad - A Few Pros and Cons”
text: I stayed one night at this hotel recently. Received a very large corner room, however it was sparsely furnished and as a result it gave the appearance of being "underfurnished" if there is such a thing. Carpet and furniture were also a little run down; however, the bed was very comfortable and bathroom was fine. The lobby/common facilities were modern, well appointed and immaculately clean. Service was outstanding all the way from the front door through the front desk. I forgot a razor and they had a complimentary one at my door in less than 5 minutes. I did not eat at the hotel so can't opine on food service. Overall average as outstanding service somewhat offset by quality of room and furnishings. I would not have a problem staying here again.

title: “Incredible Value”
text:
Definitely not your typical La Quinta. We sometimes stay at La Quinta's for quick overnights and locations with easy highway access. However, this La Quinta is something else entirely. It is a new property and has several of the amenities of more upscale hotels. The rooms are large, the beds are new and comfy, and everything is spotless. The breakfasts (included in the price) are good. There's even a bistro offering a lunch menu, which was very reasonably priced and really tasty. The fitness center is small, but very well equipped. 
I intend to stay here anytime we are traveling in the Dallas area.

title: “Not a Pleasant Stay”
text:
We traveled around the U.S from Australia staying at 4 star hotels booked using a mixture of Priceline, Hotwire and hotel chain corporate websites. All but this one were fantastic. This one was a disappointment.
We arrived from New York on Dec 29 after a delayed flight and were so tired that we did not check the room(869).
As I tried to get to sleep I kept hearing a noise that I put down to the cable cars outside on Powell Street. At 2am I realised that the noise was not the cable car but the elevator and our room was directly behind the elevator shaft!! On thinking back to the checkin I remembered the woman behind the desk grimacing when she saw what room she was giving us and a slight look of panic as she handed us the room keys.
At 6am, after getting no sleep I rang down to the front lobby to get a change of room as we were staying 4 nights and the room was too noisy. The clerk on the front desk asked what room I was in. I told him and he said he understood perfectly. He told me we could go to 874 and I should come down to reception to get the keys. After packing our bags and moving them to outside 874 (at the other end of the hotel) I went down to the lobby to drop off the old keys and pick up the new ones.
I asked the clerk if 874 was next to an ice machine, stairs, elevator etc and he said "I wouldn't do that to you, brother. I'll just make sure".
He opened a drawer and consulted a sheet of paper which I guess contained all the Priceline rooms. It took him 15 minutes of consulting the computer and the sheet of paper before giving me the keys to room 867 (two rooms from the first room, 869). So I went back up to the 8th floor, told my partner that we had to move the bags back to the other end of the hotel. I wondered what was wrong with 874.
So, after carrying our bags all the way back to the other end of the hotel, I opened the door to 867 to find the new room was a lot smaller than the first one and we had been downgraded from a king-size bed to a queen. I rang the front desk again and was told that I was given a standard room with a queen bed and the only standard rooms with a king size bed were next to the elevator shaft.
I am 6'6" tall and am used to sleeping in a king sized bed but having had no sleep that night I resigned ourselves to this room. The room did not appear that clean- it looked like it had not been vacuumed in quite a while (there was visible dust and the bath looked like it had not been cleaned with a creme cleanser in a while). Little did I know this was just the start of our hygiene problems.
On New Years Eve, the 8th floor rooms started filling up with what appeared to be frat aged guests. The hotel was hosting a New Years party and the atmosphere became quite lively which I enjoyed.
In the early morning we stepped out of our room to go on a tour to find a pool of vomit just outside our neighbor's door. A few more yards along another pool of vomit and then another one just outside the elevator. I thought I should mention this to the front desk as it would be hours before the housemaids would be coming around. With the smell still in my nostrils I mentioned this to the woman behind the front desk. She did not look surprised and asked if we would like another room. I said no as I had already been moved and I was just mentioning this as it should be cleaned up as soon as possible. I told her where the vomit was.
She consulted her computer. After a few seconds she said "Priceline" to herself out loud without looking at me and opened a drawer. She removed a couple of complementary coffee coupons from the drawer and asked if could she offer me them in apology. I said no thank you but felt quite insulted by her manner. First of all, a coffee costs 20c to produce and secondly, she categorized me by the fact I was a Priceline customer.
When we returned to the room that evening the "solid" bits of the vomit had been cleaned up but the smell and stains were still there. I rang the "Express Service" number and mentioned it to them. Two hours later, after no action, I asked one of the housemaids cleaning a room next door (late checkout) to address it. The stain outside my room was shampoo'ed but not the others. Is "Express Service" an oxymoron at Westin??
In our travels around the U.S we used a mix of Priceline, Hotwire and hotel chain websites to get good value rates. In comparison to to other hotel chains where I received excellent service and value for money I don't think I can recommend Westin either for this hotel or their approach to service.
On the plus side, the hotel is the oldest hotel in San Francisco and oozes history. Have a look in the ballrooms get get a feel of the old San Francisco. The location is perfect in Union Square. You can walk from the Market Street BART station (3 blocks slightly uphill) straight from the airport. Only $4.35 each.
P.S I lodged the above comments via their website and got a response email offering me 5.000 (sic) points Starwood Guest Points. In the response they called me by another surname 3 times and my surname is the 15th most common surname in the English language. Is this indictive of the customer service?

title: “Great Service and Location”
text: I just checked out of this hotel -had two rooms for two nights- and I can't say enough about how nicely we were treated. Malia checked us in and was so accomodating on room types and making sure we had everything we needed. We were tired and ordered room service. The order came up to our room and it was perfect! The next morning, I met Sharby in the dining room for breakfast. She was great! The made to order omelet station and fresh fruit on the buffet is very good. The second night we slept fantastic and were happy that the room had great a/c since it was hot outside. This is wonderful location for shopping, close to I-25 and everything that you might need.

title: “loved the location”
text:
Hard Rock was a fantastic location for all that we planned to do. After checking lower prices with travelocity and finding rates at 30% off, I called the hotel directly and they gave us 4 nights at the 30% off price. (Originally we were going to stay north of the downtown area and take the train back and forth - we were glad to stay downtown in close proximity to all we planned to do.) Other reviews were correct in stating that the rooms are somewhat dark.... I kept wanting to turn the lights "up" a notch and they weren't the kind that did that! Room was typical for a hotel. I guess we paid for the location. Oh yeah... the bedding and mattress was heavenly.... we were out walking a lot every day and when we came back we crashed and had very good night's sleep! Concierge was stuffy, but still answered our questions and gave advice about misc. When I made the reservation I asked about a refrigerator and it arrived in our room within minutes of checking in! We had a great view towards the river! We did eat in the Hard Rock China Grill before going to see Wicked and it was VERY high priced. My daughter and I ate conservatively and the bill was about $80. Service was fabulous and it was great food!
(We saved quite a bit of money by parking under Millennium Park in the Monroe Garage - about half the cost of using the Hard Rock valet service!) 
- will be posting our travel log with our 5 days of packed sightseeing and events (for first timers in Chicago we did great!) What a city! What a trip!

title: “What would you like to do?”
text:
A question we were asked in abundance when we stayed at the James, and no hotel since has been able to match their immaculate customer care.
Staff members always at hand to arrange cars, reserve tables, book shows, you name it, they achieved it. Bending over backwards must be a way of life for the employees as the answer was always "yes sir".
Relatively speaking, this standard of meeting customer needs and attention to detail is more than worth the money it costs to enjoy this hotel. 
As a city break hotel the James comes well equipped. The rooms are contemporary, maintained to a high standard and well proportioned. Prime Steakhouse is delicious, easily one of the finest steakhouses chicago has to offer. The location is superb, seconds from all Chicago's highlights. Very well appointed fitness and spa facilities.
All accounted for the James ticked all the boxes as a high standard hotel should. But the unrivaled guest service during our stay ensured it was beyond our expectations.

title: “The Radisson Fishermans Wharf”
text:
The hotel was comfortable, quiet, clean, free wi-fi, helpful concierge, very near the F line trolley which takes you all the way thru the central area & ends up in the castro.
Could not say anything negative about this hotel. The Radisson in Europe tend to be very modern, new & minimalist. This hotel was not up to the European standard for the chain however, was still a good standard of decor, cleanliness with a very comfy bed.

title: “Excellent Hotel for the price”
text: Me and my girlfriend stayed there for 2 nights for Red Sox vs Yankees game. We usually stay at a Kenmore Square hotel but we decided to try somewhere different and were pleasantly surprised with the hotel and how convenient it was to both Fenway park and Quincy market. The check in went very smooth and quickly. We were upgraded to a Charles river view and what a great view of the city. The room was very clean and the bed was very comfortable. We will definately stay there again in the future.

title: “Great location friendly staff”
text:
Mainly very good hotel so here are the positives and the not so positives............
- great location between 5th & 6th avenue and near the subway
- friendly, helpful staff nothing is too much trouble, bell/door man really great
- iPad in room with hotel amenities and room service details etc available
- lively and welcoming hotel lobby with fantastic feature flame fire and bars ( noted previous comment saying if you like the quiet of the Sofitel you will hate this - I am inclined to agree). If you like loud music and a lively bar then this is great!
- rooms (standard) a little bland and not much light but bathroom contemporary good size and everything you need. Beds and pillows really comfortable. Bathrobes provided. Nice toiletries too!
- no tea or coffee making facilities which isn't good considering room service charges $13 for either beverage. I appreciate there's plenty of cafes etc nearby but it's nice to have this facility for when you first get up. Selection of snacks and emergency supplies available at a cost. Fridge/minibar
- again appreciate this is New York and the city that never sleeps but I was awoken every morning in between 3.30 and 4.30 for over an hour with loud noise like lorry deliveries, bin emptying etc I have been to New York several times and not experienced this before
- I would stay again but would recommend upgrading room type for more room and light

title: “Excellent service and a nice property”
text: This is a very good choice for families with young kids (and others as well) as it includes almost everything, including light dinner (granted, not all the choices will be to your liking, but still...) Nice, quiet room with full kitchen amenities. It's not very close to anything that a tourist would need - still, it's only a 10 minute drive to whatever you do need, and the surrounding area is nice with office buildings and condos. Very helpful front desk and a general manager who actually mingled with the guests. Since San Diego is so large, with attractions all over the place, this property works well if you want to take advantage of stuff all over the metro area - just note that it's not very close to downtown. Solid choice overall.

title: “worst Marriott we've ever stayed in.”
text: This hotel was filthy. Finger print and sticky stuff on every switch plate. No mattress pad on bed. Hallways dirty. The elevator stuck and the manager later told us that never happened. Never again..

title: “Q: How many bar staff does it take to serve a drink?”
text:
At the Hotel on Rivington the answer is more than five.
There are lots of bad things about this hotel.
The bar staff don't seem to have been told that they are there to serve customers. 
Having been ignored for some minutes at the bar by five staff, when one of them left the bar and walked passed me I asked him for some drinks. He told me to wait at the bar. I told him I'd been doing that and suggested he go back and get the drinks. He didn't seem to find this a reasonable suggestion and so did so with bad grace. 
The doormen display the same attitude.
The room service staff are a bit better, although they are let down by the food they deliver. 
It would seem reasonable that if you order some food that is what will arrive. Something else probably will. Something that isn't even on the menu on one occasion. And if the food should be hot, don't expect that it will be.
And if you don't order a wake up call in the early hours, don't assume you you won't receive one. On realising the caller has called the wrong room, don't expect an apology either. Expect him to laugh instead.
Don't expect the furniture to be clean either.
It's in an interesting part of town but the hotel's a triumph of slightly dated style over substance.
On the plus side, if you have a room on a high floor, the views are great but that, along with it's location and good beds are about it. I had some meetings with some contemporary art dealers at the front of the bar. They are a discerning bunch who viewed the place with a cross between amusement and mild horror.
I often thought complain but there were so many things wrong I'd have been doing so constantly and the staff really couldn't care less so I wonder what the point would be. I just won't stay again.

title: “Temperature of the room ruined my stay”
text: We stayed at the hotel for 2 nights. The rooms were very clean and nice, and the bed was quite confortable. I loved that the pillows were soft, and clean, and there were plenty of them. The location was great, and I liked the self park option. We don't get to travel much, but love coming to Chicago at least once a year. The room temp was way too hot, which made my in-hotel experience very disappointing. I like it at 68 degrees, less for sleeping, but the room felt like 80. We asked for the temp to be lowered, but in the end, the temp stayed the same, even with the windows open all night. I should note the outside temp was about 15-25 degrees. Unless I bring a large fan with, I won't stay again because of this. Sorry.

title: “Simple and comfortable, no frills, great location!”
text:
The Tremont hotel is a prime location to tour on foot around downtown- Steps away from shopping on michigan ave, restaurants on state st, a short cab ride (or a long walk) to millennium park, or the beach area. 
Upon arrival, we were greeted promptly by a friendly concierge who escorted us and our loads of luggage to our room. My encounters with the staff were all positive. They always held open the doors and had warm words of greeting or departure. 
The building is old, the elevator creaks, and the rooms are small. I personally like the old charm of chicago hotels, but don't expect any frills at the Tremont. The rooms are clean and fairly modern - cushy beds and flat screen tv. The bathrooms however need some updating. I like to take a hot bath and was deterred by the condition of the tub and tiles. 
If you can get a room at a decent price, then this hotel is good for a comfortable 1-3 night stay.

title: “Great Hotel & Great Price”
text: This is our 2nd visit to New York during Christmas and both times I have gone by the reviews on this website and it has been great so far. We arrived at The Roosevelt on 12/9/04 and everything the staff did was with a smile. This was a great hotel especially for the price.

title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text: We had a wonderful time at the Hotel Indigo! Not only did my boyfriend and I enjoy ourselves, but our dog Dozer did too! You see, this is a pet friendly hotel and they give the same special treatment to your pet like they would to you. For example at the outside front of the hotel is a water bowl and doggie treats. How cool is that!....The staff made us feel very welcome. They were friendly and willing to hep us with anything! We stayed at the hotel for one night and the next day had our launch party there at the roof top bar. If you are considering having a special event or party, the roof top bar on the 9th floor is the place to have it. The view from up there is awesome and the ambiance is great! There are certain staff members we would like to give a special thanks to.....Vince from the valet service, Brian the bellman, Clare, Monica, and Thaddeus at the front desk, Joseph also from the front desk who wasn't there during our stay, but provided me with customer service over the phone, Brandon the bartender at the roof top bar, Kenney the server who helped us with tables, Marcello the Food and Beverage Director and Caryn and Milena from the Sales and Catering Department. These individuals went above and beyond customer service and really made our stay an enjoyable one! As we were leaving to go home, our dog Dozer put on his brakes at the front entrance, because he didn't want to go. I assured him that we are definitely coming back again and he was happy. We highly recommend this stylish and comfortable hotel to everyone! Thanks Hotel Indigo for all you do!

title: “Great place to say in New York”
text: The Belvedere was a bit rich for my blood, but it was money well spent. Be advised that the earlier you can book your hotel, the better chance you have of finding a lower rate. I was very close to Times Square, yet in a quiet location, and I always felt safe walking "home" at night with my daughter. The accommodations were clean and classy. With a microwave and fridge in the room, I was able to bring home "doggy bags" and heat them up later. There are no dishes, however, aside from glasses and cups. There was a coffee maker and coffee supplied each day. The in-room safe was a nice touch. Everything I read in the official hotel "blurb" was accurate. I found nothing to complain about and was happy staying at the Belvedere.

title: “Luxury, Comfort, Peace”
text: My daughter and I stayed at the Hotel Commonwealth when in town for a college visit. The location of the hotel is wonderfully convenient, the staff is extremely helpful, the rooms are beautiful and comfortable, the appointments thoughtful. I would certainly recommend the hotel to anyone traveling to Boston who was looking for a very special experience,

title: “Good standard of hotel. Excellent location!”
text: I stayed at the Millennium Broadway from 14th-19th of Feb 2009 and was very happy with hotel. It's location is excellent to Times Square, literally a 10 second walk. The room was spacious with a queen size bed and widescreen tv with the usual accessories; desk, hairdryer etc. Previous posts note that the bed was hard but I didn't find this to be the case at all and slept comfortably. The sheets are slightly light so it was a bit cold but I left a note for the Housekeeping asking for an extra sheet and when I returned to my room in the evening I found an extra sheet had been left as well as the heating turned up! The only 'moan' I have is that I checked into the hotel about 1 hour before my room was ready so left my luggage with the porter and returned within the hour, by which time there was a huge queue for the reception/check-in desk. As I'd already checked-in I approached a member of staff to explain that all I needed was to pick up my keys. He wasn't pleasant at all and told me to join the queue. After a few minutes of explaining that I'd already checked in and didn't see why I needed to queue for at least another 1/2 hour the manager was called and I was given the room with no problem. Other than this incident I found the staff very friendly and helpful (calling taxis when required, making conversation etc). This hotel is brilliant for a short stay; rooms are clean, spacious, staff were generally happy to help and it's in a fantastic location to Times Sq. I would definitely stay here again and would recommend others to try it also.

title: “Clean, Charming, Practical "Location Location Location" Spot”
text:
Loved our first trip to New York and stayed at this very lovely hotel. 
At first when we arrived I was a little concerned as the cabbie turned up 40th Street and dropped us in front of the narrow hotel front. As soon as we stepped inside I was warmly greeted by the front desk staff and liked the ambiance of the lobby waterfall.
The room on the was well appointed and the king bed was great. I loved the full size fridge and little kitchenette although we didn't cook at all in the room.
We felt at home here very quickly and the concierge was very helpful for dining recommendations and directions.
The buffet breakfast ws appreciated as it saved us time and money.
NY Recommendations: 
- Take comfortable shoes for LOTS of walking
- $1 pizza - at the end of 40th street
- Deals on Show tickets - booth under stairs middle of Times Square 
- Blue Man Group; Chicago, Pricilla - all great shows
- Onboard Tours - 5 hour tour was great
- Nizza Bar & Vin Italien - 630th Ninth Ave (44&45) walk from hotel

title: “Very Good Hotel”
text: We stayed for 3 nights in week prior to Christmas and were very pleased. We arrived prior to check in time and our room was available. The check in procedure was extremely efficient and courteous. A parking space was available in front of the hotel and we were able to leave our car there while we checked in. We opted to park at a nearby lot rather than the hotels valet parking. Our room was acceptable in size for a New York City hotel. The room and bathroom were very clean, with a very efficient layout and excellent lighting. As noted in other reviews, the room was a bit warmer than we preferred and we were unable to lower the temperature. Housekeeping did an excellent job each day of cleaning the room and bathroom. The bed and linens were first class and extremely comfortable. The neighborhood was very quiet with very few first class restaurants in the immediate vicinity. The hotel restaurant was bustling and active every evening with good burgers, wings, etc. Nearest subway at Grand Central is 5 or 6 blocks away. Overall we were very happy with accommodations and service and would stay here again.

title: “good stay, but a few quirks”
text:
I got a good rate from Quikbook and decided to risk staying at a new hotel. I was unaware that this was a much hyped hotel until reading some web postings. If I could afford a bigger room, I'd consider coming back there to stay in that area again
Positive
* room was clean
* everything worked well -- front desk had my reservation, room key worked first try. All components worked fine -- lights, sink, toilet, shower, TV, etc. 
* ipod charger was a nice touch 
* good location -- but entrance is actually on 58th street
Negative
* room was tiny -- about 12 ft x 12 ft -- no desk, no chair -- no stand to place the suitcase -- I had to leave it on the floor and ended up tripping on it several times
* design elements were lost on me -- fur in the lobby and elevator was described by one employee as "pony fur".
* photo over the bed didn't do much for me -- a photograph showing feet wearing high heel shoes sticking up in a car, with an airplane flying overhead
* phone rang in the middle of the night -- no one was there
* window faced airshaft

title: “Great location and wonderful rooftop bar!”
text:
Just stayed 5 nights at 60 Thompson in Soho, NY. What a great location! I fell in love with the area and the hotel is walking distance to all amenities eg subway, cafes, shopping.
I stayed with 3 girlfriends, we had a double deluxe room (2x queen beds) the room was a great size for NY and the bathroom was spacious, especially for 4 girls! 
The rooftop bar is memorable and the bar staff both downstairs and roof were very friendly. 
We did not spend a great deal of time at the hotel but the bell boys out front looked after us well. My only complaint was the staff at front desk we felt they did not offer us much support. We had to ask for a map and other information (tourist) info was very slow coming. We were traveling from Australia, extremely long flight and for the price of this hotel I would have liked a friendlier check intros did not dampen my experience, I found info else where and overall my time at this hotel served me well.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: Our son and daughter-in-law gave us a gift certificate for the Inn. It was our 2nd stay here and we hope to return in the fall. It is a convenient location and the accomodations are excellent. While we didn't use the kitchenette for actual meals, it is handy to have all the amentities of a small apartment and much more relaxing than the standard hotel room. The keyless entry is handy, but the staff is readily available if you need them.

title: “Fantastic!”
text: Wow. I'm from Singapore and I was absolutely impressed with the place! There's free breakfast with muffins and bread which were pretty delicious coupled with the orange juice. Parking wasn't a problem, plenty of space. Close proximity to the Colt Tower and Fisherman's Wharf which makes it even more attractive. I recommend staying in this inn if you have a car and if you have a budget. =)

title: “Not the best idea”
text: I happen to live on the same block as the Sheffield House. Two positive things about this place: It's cheap ($30) and it is ideally located for the Wrigleyville neighborhood (right on the north end of Wrigleyville.) The bad: This place is sleazy with drunks staggering around and frequent police visits. It used to be called The Carlos Hotel and was targeted at transient (live-in) guests. It did clean up a lot when the name changed, but I'd still avoid it if possible.

title: “Rip off $10.95 undisclosed 'fee' charged to every guest”
text:
The hotel staff does a great job but at checkin you will be informed of a completely inexcusable $10.95 'hotel services fee'. No exceptions. When I asked what it was for, I was told it was for all the 'hotel services', like shoe shine (didn't use it), and free morning coffee (where was it?). I had just flown cross country for a conference or I would have left immediately. Their rates were certainly no bargain and the $10.95 'fee' was just the frosting on the cake.
Unbelievable!

title: “Riverwalk Value”
text: This is a good hotel in a location with easy access to Riverwalk & Alamodome! Good service & comfortable rooms completes this package!

title: “Lovely experience.”
text: Booked a one night getaway with friends and was very pleased. The Lowes is a beautiful art deco style hotel! The room was a deluxe with double beds, spacious, very clean, great decor, bathroom was modern and spotless! Arrived early (10:30 am) and was able to check-in right away. Had an appointment for pedicures at noon, but construction emergency caused the spa to be closed. The hotel provided a free cab ride to their sister spa in the Ritz Carlton a few blocks away, where we had complimentary champagne with our pedicures - very nice! Had room service meal - excellent service and food. Breakfast at Sole Food next morning - again delicious. Service at every turn was professional, prompt, helpful and friendly. Would stay again and would certainly recommend to friends and family.

title: “Friendly staff makes you forget that you're in a big convention hotel”
text:
The location, in the heart of the Magnificent Mile, is excellent. The lobby is cheerfully decorated in bright colors and was a lively and vibrant space all hours of the day.
The room was average, with a more "urban" decor--darker colors and more contemporary furnishings--than many Marriott properties. The bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was on the smallish side, probably because the building dates from the 1970s and the size was typical of the era.
Even though this is a big convention hotel, every member of the staff went out of their way to be friendly and welcoming. From the woman who was helping coordinate the (not too long) check-in line, to the front desk clerk, the bellman walking past me in the lobby, and even the housekeeping staff--all offered smiles and greetings that one finds in smaller, boutique hotels.

title: “decent hotel for a sweet price!”
text: Not too bad! Rooms were clean staffing was super nice, price was awesome. The only thing that was kind of a bummer was the location on the highway feeder. A little hard to get around when you keep having to make U turns. Breakfast was typical continental with eggs, pastries, do it yourself waffles. Definitely worth staying here if you're ok with the basics!

title: “Good location, but rooms were old”
text:
Great great location, Hollywood Orchid Suites is strategically located behind the Kodak Theatre. With just a 3 min walk away, you can access the Kodak Theatre mall where there are lots of shops and food outlets. Very convenient. Universal Studios is also a short drive away.
This was more of an apartment than a hotel. The rooms came with an attached kitchen area, a living room, and a bedroom. There is also a laundry room at the basement of the hotel. The interior of the rooms were rather old and dusty, we had 3 people staying in a room and the sofa which doubled up as a queen sized sofa bed had a very thin and uncomfortable mattress. Other furnishings also looked rather old and dated. There is free parking and breakfast and a small swimming pool which I did not have the time to use.
I guess the major plus point for this place is the location!

title: “Amazing Hotel, Outstanding Manager and Staff”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Silver Cloud Hotel Stadium prior to going on an Alaskan Cruise. We were celebrating our 10th anniversary. This hotel far exceeded our expectations. The room was fantastic, the location was great, and the shuttle that took you to various downtown locations was superb! The security was phenominal, you had to use your room's key card to operate the elevator, something more hotels should do. One of the best parts of this hotel is the manager, Bill Weise, he is by far the best in the business! If we ever go to Seattle again, you can bet we will be staying here and I have already been telling everyone I can about it. Thank you, Bill, for everything!!!

title: “A great stop-over in El Paso”
text: The La Quinta Cielo Vista is located right off I-10, on the north side of the freeway, and is a great place for travellers going through town. It shares a parking lot with a grocery store, so you can stock up on all your travel needs. The parking lots are well-lit and patrolled at night by security. The rooms are standard, for a chain hotel, but clean, quiet and well-kept with a small fridge, microwave, and coffee maker. The breakfast offered in the morning is the standard continental fare (cereals, coffee, tea, muffins, fruit, etc) but adequate to meet a day's activities. The hotel's proximity to restaurants, shops, and a major mall (the eponymous Cielo Vista) are additional pluses.

title: “Enjoyable night in a great location”
text: Very enjoyable and comfortable night's sleep. Evening flight and a late dinner had us spend a night in SF before driving up to Napa for a few days and really liked the hotel. As Marriott Gold, was upgraded on arrival to an 8th floor room with a very nice view of the bay and city landmarks. Room is an odd shape due to the old-world architecture of the hotel, and we found that a plus as well. Room was in good shape, newer technology throughout, great nights sleep for us both. Nob Hill location is excellent, several parking lots within 2 blocks if you want to skimp a bit on the hotel's valet charge. Have stayed in many SF hotels and would definately return to this one.

title: “Cheap Price, Cheap Hotel”
text: My teens and I have just come back from New York where we stayed at the Astor on the Park from March 5 to March 8, 2008. I was so concerned about the negative reviews of this hotel that I tried to change my reservation but it was too late. Overall, the hotel is rated 2 stars and it worths 2 stars. Rooms and bathrooms are very clean (although the carpets need to be changed). We first had a room with a view at the back of the hotel (awful), I asked to change the room and it was done with a bigger room on the 8th floor. I recommend that hotel only if you don't want to spend much on your stay, otherwise, maybe pay a little more to have a better hotel. Astor is located near the 106th Street, Broadway is on 42nd Street.

title: “Perfect for our needs.”
text: Two friends and I were doing a Sprint Triathlon at Genesee Park on Lake Washington. We wanted a clean, close by, reasonably priced place to spend the night before the race, and the Georgetown Inn was all that. It was only a few miles from the park, so we were able to sleep a bit longer that morning without having to worry about fighting traffic. The room was kind of small, but nice and clean and the bed was comfortable. Additionally, the hotel was remarkably quiet. They had a small but adequate continental breakfast, which included fresh fruit, assorted Costco muffins (waaayyy better than those little prepackaged ones which were baked who knows how long ago), cereals (including hot), english muffins, and coffee/tea. Just right for us, and definitely better than what some of the major chain hotels offer. The Georgetown Inn is located near Boeing Field in an older neighborhood, but easy enough to find with a Garmin or other navigation system. We got settled in early and got a good night's sleep; which was what we wanted anyway. It's not fancy, but it's clean, comfortable, and the staff were very nice. I recommend the Georgetown Inn to anyone who wants a clean, simple, affordable place to sleep.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
I have stayed for three weeks at the W and I have somehow mixed feelings about it. Some things were quite disappointing for a hotel in this category. Upon arrival, late at night, my husband and I were asked if we preferred a king size bed or two separate beds. We opted for the king size, of course, only to find out the following morning that the room faced a very narrow shaft and was so dark that you couldn't tell if it was day or night. In the morning you couldn't see anything without turning the lights on. You couldn't even see the sky, as the window doesn't really open and is frosted. Also the layout of the room is odd, because the bathroom is huge, and yet there's no bathtub, and the actual bedroom is pretty small. We resisted a couple of days and then asked to change room, so we moved to a room with double beds that had a nice big window and a view of the Treasury. I would have appreciated if the staff at check-in had explained to us the difference between the King-bed room (basically no-window) and the double room, especially considering that we would stay for three weeks, whereas I clearly had the impression that she tried to get rid of the super dark room first and see how it went. 
Another disappointment was that, at least four times during my stay, I came back in the afternoon to my room and it hadn't been cleaned yet. (And I have heard other guests in the elevator complaining about the same thing) Other hotels in that category have a way of finding out when a guest leaves her room so housekeeping goes right away and services the room.
As for the staff, my experience was that the staff at the front door and concierge was nice but the waitress I had at the Rooftop bar was really unfriendly and snooty. Since I have read other reviewers complaining about the same thing, this is clearly an issue that the hotel should face. 
Finally, on our last day, we asked if we could check out late, as our flight was at 11.30 pm. We were told it was not possible, because the hotel was at full capacity and the room had to be prepared for the new guest. Fair enough, until another staff jumps in and says that if we agree to pay half of the daily rate, we can stay until 5pm. Uhm, so what happens to the new guests? Do they wait until 7 pm for the room to be ready? Again, I had the impression they were lying. 
Dining: we had breakfast one day at the J&G Steakhouse and I am sorry to say that the continental buffet is simply ridiculous. It consists of one basket of pastries, one of granola, plus yogurt.
