Honestly, while the muffin I had was really good, the variety of offerings is shocking for a continental buffet in such a restaurant. Again, it can't stand up to the competition. 
Among the things I liked: 1) the beds are really comfortable and linens are of excellent quality; 2) Bliss toiletries are great; 3) I had problems with my internet connection (which, by the way, is 14.95$ per day) and the external support team was nice and helpful

title: “Great hotel. Horrible location.”
text:
We were to spend five days here, but left after only two. The room was spacious, the bed comfy, the bathroom clean. We were literally driven nuts by the room air conditioner. There was no wall thermometer, so we were either shivering, or uncomfortably hot. There was no comfort there.
The hotel itself is located in a very, busy, very congested area, near the 5 freeway. The traffic was unrelenting no matter the time of day. Every time we left the hotel it was pure madness. The streets were always packed with a line of cars. Very unpleasant indeed.
We saw some unsavory characters strolling through the parking lot, walking around our car and other cars. That was disturbing. Further, there appeared to be several encampments of grizzly homeless people about the outside of the hotel. We just didn't feel safe there.
We checked out the hot tub. When we came back some ten hours later, the same group of rowdy drunk people were still where they were when we left. However, some 40 or 50 of their beer cans were carelessly strewn about. Nice that they had their own private hot tub with greenish yellow water! That was very poor of management not to keep an eye on the public areas.
Jasmine and Susan were very kind, very sweet people. We enjoyed them immensely. Susan took a liking to our little dog and gave him lots of attention and treats. He liked her too.
This hotel was recently renovated. They did a fine job. But, they can't change the location of the property. And that was the reason we chose to leave. 
The owner should promote Jasmine. She is one of the precious few people who truly understand hospitality. An amazing young lady.

title: “Great stay at the Amalfi Hotel!”
text: I definitely recommend staying at this hotel in Chicago. The customer service was terrific and we enjoyed the complimentary breakfast and cocktail reception. The location was perfect for all attractions and activities. The room was clean and comfortable. You won't be disappointed with this hotel!!

title: “Perfect location”
text:
You can't do better than this if you want to be central - steps away from the start of the Freedom Trail. The hotel is as you'd expect from Kimpton, quite buzzy and stylish but still friendly. We were there during Hurricane Sandy and they organised movies and an extended wine hour whilst we were stuck in watching the rain go past - I thought this was a great touch. Breakfasts and room service meals were good quality and the service was always friendly.
Yes, it's expensive. But you get what you pay for!

title: “Wonderful service”
text: We stayed overnight at the Marriott when we came in from Auckland and were waiting for our flight the next day to Dallas. Service was excellent - the luggage porter went above and beyond to help us and talked to us in a friendly manner - he even got us extra bottled water and a newspaper after he'd dropped off our luggage. He came the next day when we were checking out and was polite once again. The room looked great as well - very posh to us - the 18th floor w/ a big flatscreen tv - very nice :) We ordered room service and it was great - the desserts were lovely and the pool was wonderful as well. They brought us a crib for our 3mth old twins and it was pretty secure and not that old so I felt safe putting them in it. Overall this was a wonderful night we had in LA at the Marriott.

title: “Lovely Place”
text:
My husband and I stayed here las month and we're welcomed by a very friendly reception staff and enjoyed every minute of our stay. The hotel is charming (right on the water) and has great harbor views. The rooms are spacious and very clean. Overall a great place to stay and a great location to explore the Inner Harbor area of Baltimore.
Dana & Rob (Short Hills, NJ)

title: “Great Stay!”
text: This was a good hotel at a reasonable price. The location was super, the room was comfortable and it was very clean ! We requested a coffee maker and one was brought up to the room quickly. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Nothing special :(”
text:
We stayed for 2 nights before going back to Peru .
We had stayed a few days before at the Faitmont San Francisco and loved it but as we were coming back from Santa Monica we couldn't find a room at the Fairmont and thought a JW Marriot is always good but we were very surprised to find out that there was nothing special about this hotel , well maybe location is good but everything else was very poor for us.
I like Marrriot hotels but this is one of the worst hotels I ever stayed at .
Front desk staff was very rude and even if we said we didn't like the view and smell of the room they did very little to help us feel comfortable.
I would not recomend this hotel at all.

title: “2 Nights at Gild Hall Hotel”
text:
Much prefer the rooms in this hotel than Soho Grand. Very impressive, a great deal of thought has obviously been made in the design of this hotel. Shame about the 15$ charge for internet. But then it is for 24 hrs.
Amazingly, they had the same fan as Soho Grand and the same engineer. Pic attached.

title: “Seen better than this...”
text: Room was comfortable and reasonably silent being next to the airport. Personnel was friendly. The room and the common parts of the building look as they haven't been renewed for a couple of decades, which is a bit of a disappointment for a hotel of this category.

title: “Beautiful room”
text: I stayed at the Sheraton Downtown Denver recently for a weekend conference. The room was very beautiful and spacious (located on the Plaza side). I think I had the largest hotel bathroom I've ever encountered. And equally important - the bed was extremely comfortable and the hotel floor was quiet. The meeting space was comfortable & accessible, and the restaurants & bars were great with fine service. There is a mall next door with a movie theater and restaurants. It's a terrific location.

title: “Well located for Ballet, Zinzanni, etc.”
text: Went to Teatro Zinzanni to celebrate our anniversary and stayed downtown so we could drink more wine and walk to bed. Zinzanni had a discount arrangement with the hotel and it's right around the corner so it was super-convenient, especially since the parking was free! Would be a great place to stay after a night at the ballet (think Nutcracker?), the Seattle Rep, anything that's down in that area. Rooms were clean, shower was great, the lounge area looked cozy although we just walked by it.

title: “Good, but not as good as last time.”
text:
I last visited the Pan Pacific in January 2010, and as I had such a glowing review last time, I was expecting much of the same this time.
The service is still top notch, however the rooms seemed old to me, more worn and slightly musky this time
I cannot complain about the room nor the bathroom as I knew what to expect, however there was something missing on this visit.
As per usual the bed was awesome and I slept well, which is always a bonus for me...
The other guys that I was with tought that the hotel was great, so as mentioned, it may just be me with high expectations.

title: “Typical Holiday Inn - No Surprises”
text:
The 3-star rating is appropriate.
Positives:
good overnight stopover location, handy to I-95
in-room fridge & microwave 
in-room wifi, decent speed
business center is good for printing
Negatives:
none for this star level

title: “Vintage but lacks customer service”
text: I had made my reservations through Priceline, which of course doesnt give you an option to upgrade your room so I had to call the hotel directly. I called 2 weeks prior to my trip and mentioned that I needed two beds, they said they'd make notes on my reservation and it was way in advance so I was sure to get the room with double beds; to my surprise they didn't and the only thing offered was a rollaway bed. the room is very small, room service had to take a side table and lamp out of the room to fit the roll away which made the room smaller and hard to walk around....the TVs are old and not very many channels, the restroom is super small, the tub was backed up, the toilet needed to be flushed several times....I realize this is a 1900's building but come on..... the bed was very comfortable, the A/C was noisy...nice area since its closed to everything but I wouldn't stay there again.

title: “Lived up to a Ritz Experience!”
text:
First off, if you are looking for the most updated room, this would not be your first choice. However, I suspect the reason people choose to stay at Ritz-Carltons (including us) is for the service and amenities. This is where this hotel and most importantly, the staff, does not disappoint. Despite the age, the hotel is well-maintained and clean. It is very much a business hotel, but we were there on vacation and felt very comfortable. The location is central and across the street from Biltmore Mall and a movie theatre.
When we stay at Ritz-Carltons, we choose to stay on the Club Level, as the continuous food presentations and beverage options throughout the day certainly complete the whole experience and add to the value. Here, it is on the 11th floor and the design of it is a bit different in that when you exit off the elevator, you walk straight into the Club Lounge. Typically from staying at other Ritz properties, the Club Lounge is in a separate room. Jean, the concierge on staff at the Club Lounge is excellent. She certainly embodies the level of service that you would expect of the Ritz-Carlton. She is kind and inquisitive, without ever being intrusive. What you later realize, she knows just the questions to ask just so she can then ask how can she help. After mentioning one morning that the A/C unit wasn't cooling in our room, she almost seemed perplexed that we hadn't mentioned it during the night; reminding us that they have engineers on staff 24/7. An engineer had the issue resolved within 30 minutes of mentioning it to her. 
As mentioned in some of the other reviews, the pool is rather small, so certainly not the size you would see at their resort properties. There are only a few lounge chairs, although they have a larger cabana area that would be perfect to add some more chaises, but while we were there, they chose to keep it empty. On a Friday afternoon with the pool area so full that we ended up sitting in two chairs from the dining area, there was only one pool attendant on duty. Not the typical level of service you normally see at a Ritz, but this was the only noticeable delinquency I observed during our stay.
All in all, a very nice stay.

title: “A cheap hotel at a cheap price”
text:
For "recently renovated", The Executive Pacific Plaza is amazingly shabby and outdated. It appears to have been constructed in the early 1900's, with few upgrades since. They still use radiators for heat, and have no AC. There are pipes running across the hallway ceilings, and the lights in common areas are depressingly dim. The headboards, however, appear to be circa 1975, since they are mustard-color vinyl with brass tack edging. 
The rooms are laughably small -- only about 3 feet on any given side of the queen size bed. The bathroom sink is so small (appx 10" in diameter) that I could not even get the iron under the faucet to put water in. 
We were unfortunate enough to be there during a 4-day stretch of 85+ degree days. With only a ceiling fan and small tabletop fan to cool the room, the heat made sleeping very difficult. There is also noisy construction going on across the street, and the small window in my room overlooked a noisy parking deck.

title: “Like Living in a large NYC Apartment!”
text: Wonderful hotel. Lots of international visitors here. As noted, location is unbelievable central to times square, central park, transportation, broadway , bars etc! I got a deal for $99 per night through their website and was worth every penny!

title: “Great Location with Beautiful Views”
text: My wife and I spent 3 nights at the Hyatt Regency after booking on Hotwire. We were given a room that overlooked the Chicago River & Navy Pier. Very nice room, very clean, and the service was great. Just a couple blocks away from shopping & entertainment. Only tip I have is to park at the lot across the street instead of paying to park at the hotel. $15 cheaper per day.

title: “Stylish, Historic and a Great Location in Chicago”
text: The Intercontinental Chicago is a beautiful, unique hotel originally built in the 20's as an exclusive club, it now serves as a Stylish hotel. Our stay over a recent holiday provided us with a nicely appointed room overlooking Michigan Avenue that included a marble bathroom. Michael Jordan's steakhouse recently added off the Lobby was a great place for a drink or a meal. If you have a moment take a short tour of the hotel and you'll see some fantastic architectural features. Service was excellent.

title: “Great stay, thanks reviewers!”
text:
After reading the reviews here, I went ahead and booked 2 nights in a 2bdrm suite. We were traveling up and down the CA coast visiting family and we wanted to end on a tourist-y note. Can't beat the location or the service. The area felt safe enough that I let my two teen-age sons walk to and from Hollywood Blvd un-escorted, even during the evening. Big kudos to Gretchen. I called to confirm our arrival and she asked me what she could to do meet our needs. Just being asked was nice. She had books, tour guides all ready for us when we arrived. The rooms do have a slightly run-down feel but I think it adds character. The bedding was very comfortable, the accommodations more than roomy enough for 3 teens, me and my 70 year-old mother. Everyone was pleased which is no small accomplishment. I agree with what past reviews said about the pool, the b-fast etc. If I ever visit Hollywood again I would definitely stay again. Better yet, move the whole place, staff included, to Encinitas. I know I'll be visiting there more than Hollywood. 
ps if you stay be sure so stop by the pool to chat with Danny. He's a long-time resident and a good guy with great stories.

title: “Great location and staff”
text: Just visited for 4 nights. I must brag a little on this hotel. Great location, great staff, and great perks. 9 out of 10 staff members were excellent and really tried to make you feel like you were at a top notch hotel. (we won't talk about the 10th since no hotel can be perfect.) The hotel is in the perfect location to walk to Mag mile, restaurants, all of the theaters, and Navy Pier. The breakfast was just enough to carry us over until lunch. The only tiny and I do mean tiny thing that I will mention (which is no reflection on the hotel) the alley directly behind the hotel is filled with dumpsters (30-I counted) and for some reason they choose 5:30am to dump them so you will wake up early if you are a light sleeper but I would stay here again in a heartbeat. Well done!

title: “After forty years staying at the Hotel Edison, I still love it...!”
text: I found the Hotel Edison forty years ago and I try to stay there every time I travel to New York. I work in the Theatre and I love the location and the wonderful charm this hotel has. The staff is always friendly and accommodating and the nostalgia is captivating. Another one of my favorite features is the piano bar with Karen Brown...! I just love the Hotel Edison and hope to stay there for many years to come...!

title: “The Peabody, Memphis (Home tp the famous Peabody Ducks!)”
text:
We were unable to stay here during our stay in Memphis but couldn't miss visiting to experience the famous Peabody Ducks! 
We had afternoon tea in this beautiful hotel and waited for the Ducks to perform their march at 5pm as predicted. a very enjoyable and entertaining experience, which I would recommend if you get a chance to see it. This is also in short walking distance to the famous Beale Street, which is a must for anybody visiting Memphis.

title: “get a room Not Facing Taylor Street!”
text:
The hotel Mark Twain is a boutique hotel situated behind the Hilton Hotel. However, in SF, a block away does make a difference. 
The room was clean, there is a restaurant on the bottom floor of the hotel, and there is a fitness center off of the lobby. That's the plus side of the Mark Twain.
The negative comment? WHATEVER YOU DO, GET A ROOM THAT FACES AWAY FROM TAYLOR STREET! People are yelling outside the hotel until one thirty in the morning. The Hilton deliveries are carried out in front of the Mark Twain, so you hear the garbage truck (and other trucks) roar up at all hours. Also, Greyhound buses are picking up and dropping off passengers on Taylor Street beginning at 5 am. One evening, there seemed to be a drag race taking place out on Taylor Street at about 4 a.m. 
I am used to some noise. I live near a freeway in Honolulu, so I am no stranger to the sound of traffic. However, I left the Mark Twain exhausted due to lack of sleep. 
Also, always turn left as you leave the lobby on to the street. After you hit Taylor Street, take your first right onto O'Farrell Street. Otherwise, you will find yourself in a fairly spooky part of town. 
There are other boutique hotels nearby that are quieter, feel safer and don't cost much more. This is a second choice, rather than a first.

title: “A surprisingly nice stay..”
text: We checked in on Saturday 4/16 at 3 PM. I am used to staying at larger, more upscale hotels so I was a little concerned when we got onto the tiny elevator and up to the narrow hallways. Definitely not what I am used to - it seemed more like a NYC walk up. We had an actual KEY to open our room door and we were told we would need to leave it at the front desk when coming and going - that was a first! And again, left me a bit unnerved because not what I'm used to. The room had very old architecture, same as the building. Windows with wood moldings and frames and they ACTUALLY OPEN!!! BUT, the hotel lobby was inviting, the staff pleasant, and the Room was CLEAN and smelled fine, actually, there was no smell at all. The bedding was a little old - but clean, and I checked all the way down to the mattress. The room was very cool and there was a bit of a draft coming in through the AC in the window but by the time we went to bed it was very comfortable. The room had everything we needed but nothing more which was fine because all we did was sleep and we did sleep! (It was a little noisy at times, but New York is noisy and it is NOT a huge hotel chain with sound proof windows etc.) They offer a flat screen tv and free wifi and there is computer access in the lobby. One of the best features were the lockers they offer in the lobby. We checked in on Saturday late afternoon, went to Madame Toussads(got discounted tickets from the conceirge and was able to skip the very long line with VIP pass), then came back to bed. Next morning we went for breakfast then checked out, BUT we still had plans for Sunday - the Museum of Natural History in the morning and Mary Poppins at 3. We took a locker and loaded our gear and were able to spend all of Sunday and part of Sunday night in the city without lugging around our gear. We all had a great time and felt very comfortable. I would recommend this hotel, but inform of the very authentic New York experience - you feel like your staying in a friends guest bedroom, not a modern hotel.

title: “Excellent location”
text: Friendly staff,great location,lobby in need of a reno.,room was ok,nothing special,probably a three star hotel

title: “Business trip made easy in San Antonio”
text: I enjoyed my stay at Hotel Contessa. Easy access to Riverwalk and Convention Center. My room was great. Food was good. ALL the staff were very friendly and helpful, especially Eddie Gomel. Hope he stays around. I used public self parking across the street instead of valet - cheaper and the car wasn't going to be moved anyway until time to leave for home. I would recommend Hotel Contessa and I would stay there again when I visit San Antonio.

title: “Beautiful hotel in a central location”
text:
My husband and I stayed in this hotel for 3 nights. It's a beautiful hotel and the staff is excellent. We had a very warm welcome at the reception, the (standard) room was spacious and clean and so was the bathroom. The hotel has beautiful public areas. Only disappointment was the pool: we wanted to have a swim after a warm day, but the pool is for children, not swimming depht so we looked a little bit stupid.
Hotelconcierge did her utmost to help us to hire a car, and gave us many options for going out and dining.
Overall: very, very good. But don't forget: it's mostly a business hotel, so weekdays are busy with congress etc.

title: “Lots to like.”
text:
Yes, it's older, but there's a lot to like about this Embassy Suites property. We like the self-catering possibilities, with a microwave oven and fridge in the room and a gas barbecue available, dining in is easy (housekeeping provides dishes). The pool is well laid out for sun and shade. Custom-cooked breakfast and "happy hour" are included in the price. 
Ask for a room on the side without a parking lot for the quietest night.
While there isn't much to walk to in the neighbourhood, there's a handy grocery store a block west and a decent Italian restaurant a few blocks east. Beer and wine are readily available at a market a block east.

title: “300 $ just for accomodation??”
text: stayed at the Hilton on Times Square Sep 05 for 1 night. Though staff was somehow friendly by NY standards I cannot agree in what other travellers commented. Due to a cruise we started from NY we had some suitcases to be carried and helped with. There are two different bellman depts in charge of your luggage. 1st from street level to 21st floor,2 nd. from reception up to your room which means tipping twice for one service and, yes, the bellmen of each division fight with each other regarding the tipps. Very unpleasant situation fot the guest!! rooms are average, bathrooms small and not very welcoming equipped. beds far to soft to be comfortable. Due to late arrival we did not leave the hotel for any food or drinks but decided to take a glass in the bar. bar/restaurant/reception all located in kind of a station hall without any optical or accustical dividing. Sound level just to high to have a conversation. but price level even higher.... Decided to go up to the room and order something to eat from 24 hr. roomservice. Were informed that roomservice ends by 10.30 pm due to new procedures. Well, what makes a hotel worth the money, how defines a hotel its nightly price? With lacking services???? We do not agree and will definitly avoid this hotel in future. A management dividing the hotel into cost structures and canceling services the moment they are not profitable is not what we expect from a hospitality place

title: “Couldn´t expect more for NY!”
text:
The rooms were spacious, clean and nice! The front desk really helped us when we needed an early check-in and the location is very good! Close to Central Park and Columbus Circle.
Holiday Inn really reached my expectations! I couldn´t expect more from them!

title: “Excellent hotel, fitness center and business center”
text:
Off course, it is a bit special to stay in a marine memorial hotel.
However, it was a very good experience :
- staff and concierge are helpfull
- rooms are clean
- breakfast is excellent, great choice and very good view on the city
- fitness center is unique : a lot of appliance, plus a real swimming pool : 25 yards !
- good business center.
The hotel decoration is old fashioned, then does not expect a design hotel, this is the only weak point in my opinion.
Location is very convenient, close to Union Square a few minutes walk.

title: “Great Place, Great Location!”
text:
I highly recommend this hotel if you are staying in Seattle and want to be in a great location.
Major attractions are just a few blocks away such as the Space Needle and museums. I also loved that bus transportation was just outside the door and made it so convenient to go down to Pike's Market, Pioneer Square and shopping dowtown. The room was comfortable and had extras like a refrigerator and microwave. Starbucks in also connected to the hotel so goodies were available. The staff at the front desk was so nice and helpful. Thank you for a wonderful stay while in Seattle.

title: “Esther Williams Pool”
text:
My sisters and I spend two nights over a weekend in August. We stayed in the historical tower. We swam in the beautiful pool where once Esther Williams swam. Our room was clean and the view fabulous. We could see the Chicago river and were close to shopping etc. 
This is the 5th time we have stayed there in the last 8 years. We wouldn't think of staying at another place.
However, we did miss the cozy lounge where there was jazz playing in the evening. And during the afternoon after shopping we would sit and have a snack and drinks and watch the shoppers go by. We used to entertain visitors there. 
But all in all it was 5 stars for us.

title: “Heavenly bed!”
text: We arrived late at night after a horrific 3 hour wait at immigration at JFK so to be greeted by an incredibly friendly young guy on reception who speedily checked us in was refreshing. We got a room on the 21st floor and had a view all the way down to the river. It had the added bonus of being quieter as further away from the street noise. The room was huge for New York standards (just a standard room) and the bed was divine. Incredibly comfortable and hard to get out of in the morning! You cannot beat the location of this hotel. Not even two minutes from Times Square and less than a fifteen minute walk from 5th Avenue.

title: “Not worth it...”
text:
We stayed at The Four Seasons for two nights (9/28-9/29) and while generally the hotel was fine, we didn't really experience the great service that the other reviews raved about. We arrived 15 minutes before check-in time to find that our room was not ready, but we were told it would be ready within 15--45 minutes and that we would be "upgraded." (We had originally requested non-smoking room with a king bed.) When we were shown to our room one hour later, we were given a SMOKING room (complete with several ashtrays) that was extremely small. (If this was an upgrade, I can't even imagine what our original room would have been--A utility closet?) The room was clean and comfortable, but it reeked of cigarette smoke, much like a Las Vegas hotel room. Because we had waited so long to get the room and we were only staying two nights, we decided to stick it out rather than requesting a switch.
That evening while we were waiting for a cab in front of the hotel, we were pleasantly surprised when an employee ushered us to the back of the hotel to be driven to our restaurant in the hotel's town car. Unfortunately, once we made it to the area where we were supposed to enter the car, another employee apologized for the mix up, explaining that the car couldn't take us because our restaurant was outside the hotel's one-mile radius and that we would need to head back out front to try for a cab again. This was irritating, to say the least.
The next day after we returned from the day's activities, we discovered that our room had not been cleaned and our breakfast dishes were still there. We called housekeeping and waited, but 30 minutes later we called again. After the second call, housekeeping arrived promptly.
We did have good luck with turn down service and room service and all the staff we encountered were extremely polite.
I think it was a fine place to stay in that it was clean and had a nice location, however the service was spotty and the room was small and not luxurious--For that much money I expect great service, not just average. We will not be staying there again.

title: “I love this hotel”
text: I will stay here whenever I come to San Francisco. The staff was great, the view was wonderful and the room was perfect. Beautiful!

title: “Long weekend in New York”
text:
Just got back from our stay at the Intercontinental Barclay. Right across the road from the Waldorf Astoria,so we were impressed with the area. Last time we were in New York we stayed on the west side. Definitely prefer midtown east.Everyone was very helpful at the hotel. They will store your luggage if you arrive early or check out late. A few tips for your time in New York.
Go in Spring or Fall. Summer is TOO hot,TOO many people and TOO many line ups.
Don't bother with the hop on hop off bus tours, better to walk around or take the subway.
Go for brunch or dessert at the Loeb Boathouse Restaurant in Central Park (72nd & 5th Ave),
lunch or dinner a little more expensive.
Walk the Brooklyn Bridge. Rent bikes to ride through Central Park.

title: “Lovely!”
text:
The Galleria Park Hotel was great - we finished our honeymoon there, and had a ton of wine from our earlier days in Sonoma, and they helped us ship it off from the liquor store next door. It was a huge weight off our shoulders.
The rooms were nice as well - I enjoyed what we got for fairly low prices. My only grip is the location, which is pretty touristy/financial district. But that's my own fault for not researching the area thoroughly enough! It's right near the BART, which is a major plus.

title: “What a relief!”
text:
While in New York recently on a business trip, I stayed at one of the big expensive downtown hotels, compliments of my company. Once the meetings were over, I stayed in town for a few days on vacation. To save money, I needed to find a more affordable hotel. As I had never been to NYC, I was nervous about finding a decent place in my price range. After reading the reviews at TripAdvisor for the On the Ave Hotel, I decided to stay there. I wasn't disappointed.
The rooms were small, of course. This is, after all, NYC. But, the hotel was lovely, and the bed was the most comfortable I've ever found away from home. I loved the big fluffy pillows and soft down comforter. 
The lobby was ultra chic, and the halls and rooms were clean and well cared for. In comparison, the big expensive hotel had been shabby and quite ugly.
The hotel also has a large beautiful balcony that can be accessed by all guests. It's a lovely place to sit and enjoy the view of the skyline and the Hudson River. In general, the location of the hotel is excellent. Two blocks away from the subway station, and right across the street from the Manhattan Diner. This is a fabulous restaurant with very reasonable prices. As the hotel itself has no kitchen, all room service orders are actually delivered from the Diner. That was fine with me, as the meal I had delivered to my room was one of the best I'd ever had in a hotel. The prices were outrageously reasonable, too. An enormous cheeseburger was only $6.95!
The On the Ave Hotel is definitely a great value, and I will certainly stay there EVERY time I return to NYC. One bit of caution though...the rooms are not sound-proofed very well so they can be quite noisy if you have boisterous neighbors. The heating units are also pretty load when they kick in, to the point of being startling until you get used to them. To be fair, I've never really found a very quiet hotel in my travels, so I don't think this is much of a deterent for On the Ave. 
Cheers, and happy traveling!

title: “Great hotel”
text: Clean comfortable beds - nice staff. Would highly recommend

title: “Loud! Great place to stay if you like feeling like you are sleeping on the street!”
text:
Granted, I was there the Thursday night before St Patrick's Day through the day after but still, with single-paned floor-to-celing, windows, I heard every whistle, horn beeping and voice. And the light blocking shades still let a fair amount of light in
Got a great group rate of 129/night or so, staff was friendly and attentive and the restaurant was really good, but I was there for a multi-day nonprofit board meeting and was thoroughly exhausted from not being able to sleep.

title: “Coming back next time I'm in town”
text:
We stayed at the Towne Place suites for 2 weeks with a newborn. We will definitely return the next time we're in town.
Pros:
The standard hotel room was a big enough size for all of us. Unlike some of the other hotels in the area, Towne Place did not charge for a travel crib in the room. And, having the kitchenette was very convenient for making those bottles in the middle of the night. 
We enjoyed the hot buffet breakfast, which was typically an egg dish, potatoes, a waffle maker, canned fruit, cereal selection, and muffins. Although, after 2 weeks it did get kind of boring! 
On weekday evenings they have a Manager's Special dinner with a different option (spaghetti and meatballs, etc.) each night. 
Also, it is a fairly quiet hotel. Based upon the guests I saw, it looks like the hotel is also pet friendly.
Cons: 
The air/heater was loud. 
The shower temperature was warm, but not as hot as I typically like.

title: “Spectacular place!”
text:
The Mansion is incredible. I had no idea how great it would be for kids. I took my now 8 year-old daughter for tea for her birthday and she was THRILLED! We were treated wonderfully, even being presented with a special Fascinator to wear! We were fed well, in her words "More desserts than you could even eat!" And entertained for hours, we spent an incredible amount of time exploring the Mansion and we both loved every nook and cranny! Thanks for a perfect celebration day. 
-Carrie

title: “Handy Location”
text: My wife and I stayed here for 4 nights. Our travel agen had stayed here and he recomended it as well priced and central. We had flown from Las Vegas that day and found the BART system easy to follow. With just one train to catch right at the airport it delivered us to the Civic Station which is just accross the road from this hotel. The hotel staff were especially helpful with transport options. The room was reasonably spacious and very clean and well maintained. It also had free WiFi in the rooms. Trams are also just accross the road and a short walk will take you to some big name shops. Would definatly recomend this hotel to family and friends.

title: “Swissotel was Awesome!”
text: Beautiful Hotel right on the water. The late night walks cant be beat. Very close to everything. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful. Will be going back and staying here.

title: “Consistantly Excellent Property”
text: I always stay at Fairfields because of their uniformally comfortable rooms, good breakfast, and immediate service if any problems arise. The Fairfield at Fossil Creek is a tribute to Marriott. It is conveniently located on 820 so it is easy to reach Ft Worth or Dallas. Construction on 820 is a temporary bother but it will eventually be finished. Rooms are comfortable and large. Bathrooms are large and designed for safety. Swimming pool is inside, beds are comfortable like all Marriotts, and restaurants are conveniently located nearby. The management team is always helpful. This is a great base for a visit to Ft Worth or Dallas. Dallas can be reached easily by the TRE train that is about 15 Minutes from the motel at Richland Hills Station.

title: “Times Square view from our room!!”
text:
We had reservations at the Times Square Marriott Marquis for four nights and requested a Times Square view room. We were not disappointed!!! They put us on the 44th floor with wonderful views of Times Square!!! We could look right down on the GMA studio and watch people lining up for the show, then watch the same thing on the TV! The lights at night are incrediable and we could even see the Statue of Liberty!!
The lobby on the 8th floor is very nice and the elevator systemis very high-tech. We did not try the restaurant. That area looked a little uninviting and did not have a warmth about it. 
The 8th floor bar area does overlook Times Square and that is a nice view also.
The staff was friendly and professional. Another huge advantage of the hotel is location...location...You can walk most everywhere you need to go and if you can't walk there are taxis right at the hotel and the subway is close by.
A very nice hotel in the middle of the Big Apple!!!!

title: “Great place to stay!”
text:
We stayed here from July 19-21 (3 nights). This hotel offers so much...and it is in a fun area where you can walk to many things! Great breakfast, great lake view, great front desk, great shuttle, etc.
Undesirable details are NOT the fault of the hotel. For instance: This is a non-smoking hotel. We opened our 5th floor French doors and smoke blew in from the folks on the 4th floor. We wanted to sit out on the balcony to eat our breakfast, but smokers were out on the balcony in the eating area. Many, many children....which is NOT great if you have already raised yours! Also, if e-mail is important to you, bring your own computer. They have fast internet access available in the room, but the public computer in the lobby is usually tied up.

title: “Dean R”
text: We have stayed at OB Hotel many times. Great service and great rooms. We especially love the apartment with a full kitchen. Great balcony to view all the people and restaurants and antique shops to walk to. Will stay again.

title: “My Kind of Place”
text: We celebrated our 38th wedding anniversary in Chicago and stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn. It was so much better than I expected. The room was wonderful, a corner view, Room 2170, and clean and bright. I would recommend the hotel to anyone traveling to chicago. I was really having a hard time deciding but price was finally the deciding factor. I was pleasantly surprised to have everything, including location, be so wonderful. the hotel delivered a bottle of champagne and complimentary breakfast passes because it was our anniversary. The staff was pleasant, friendly and very helpful with all of our questions.

title: “Great hotel for the money”
text: Family of 6, 3 rooms. My family has taken a holiday trip to NYC every year for the last 20 years and we always enjoy the Waldorf. Rooms are recently refurbished with comfortable beds and elegant appointments. If you stay overnight Saturday, you must experience the Brunch at Peacock Alley on Sundays. Exquisite dining awaits at a reasonable $75 per person.

title: “Great stay!”
text: We stayed in the Pod Hotel for 8 days. There was always someone at the front desk and all the staff were all very nice and approachable. Our room was small but it was a good size to just sleep in, as most of the day was spent exploring the city. We had our own bathroom and it was cleaned everyday! There was a TV in the room that had a lot of channels and an alarm clock. Overall, it was good value and I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Had we stayed on the 2nd floor, we would have given it a 5...”
text:
My husband and I, along with our 10 year old twin boys, spent 4 nights at the Magic Castle. We debated on our rating because we loved the hotel, except for one major drawback.
First the positives. The hotel is a converted apartment complex (think Melrose Place) and it is a refreshing change from the cookie cutter "hotel in a box" that so many chains have become. The staff is friendly and helpful. The amenities are great - especially with kids - free snacks, sodas and movies. Anything we asked for was promptly delivered. In the afternoon, they offered cookies and cider (wonderful smell upon entering the hotel...) Of an evening, they lit candles on the tables in the courtyard surrounding the pool.
The location is one block off Hollywood Blvd, right near the Kodak Theater. We'd venture out and about during the day, then park the car in the free hotel garage and wander out for dinner.
All of that is wonderful, but then there is the one big negative we experienced. Our room was a 1 bdm suite on the 1st floor. It was large and clean and right next to the courtyard pool. The problem was the noise from upstairs. Anytime the guests in the room above moved, it sounded like a creaky herd of thundering elephants. When they took a shower, it sounded like a foghorn. Now, our neighbors were not overly loud - they were just moving about their room. To the hotel's credit, when I complained after the 1st night, they offered to move us, but they don't allow roll away beds on the 2nd floor, so we decided to tough it out. Earplugs were a must for sleeping.
If we find ourselves in Hollywood, we would definitely stay at the Magic Castle again - our boys absolutely loved it. And we will recommend it to friends...however, we will insist on staying on the 2nd floor.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
My best friend and I went to NY to celebrate her 30th birthday. We chose to stay at the Empire Hotel because we thought it looked really cute online. It was an added bonus that after we booked the hotel, we heard that the Kardashians stayed there, too! 
We booked a standard room with 1 king sized bed because it was almost half the price as a room with 2 queen beds. We arrived before check-in so we asked if it would be possible to check in early. The woman at the front desk said we could check in early if we upgraded our room, which we weren't interested in doing at that time. She said she would call us if our room was available early. 
We left to walk around and eat lunch, but after a few hours, no one ever called. We came back to the hotel to ask if our room was available - it was (even though no one ever called to notify us). 
We went up to our room which was TINY... there was no dresser or space to store clothes, and the bathroom resembled something you'd find in a camper or airplane. For this reason, we decided to ask about upgrading to a suite. 
We called the front desk and the woman said we could upgrade to a suite, but we couldn't see the suite first. This made no sense so we walked down to the front desk. After explaining that this made no sense, we were told that we could in fact look at a suite before deciding whether or not we wanted to upgrade. The upgraded suite was still only equal in size to some of the other rooms we've stayed in in NY, but we decided to pay the fee to upgrade anyway because the standard room seemed unbearable. 
It takes a lot for us to complain or even submit a review, but ultimately the service is what has caused us to do so. 
Other complaints:
- The hotel doesn't have an ice machine so you have to call Room Service for ice. Be prepared to wait an hour or more, even if you call more than once. 
- The suite didn't have a dresser or space for clothes, either, so I lived out of my suitcase the entire time.
- There was no iron or ironing board but they were available upon request. It wasn't uncommon to see irons and ironing boards just sitting out in the hallway.
- Our dirty drinking glasses sat for DAYS on the floor outside of the door to our room. 
- It's impossible to shower without getting water all over the bathroom floor. 
- The lamp turned on and off by itself; we couldn't even get it to stay on.
- We never even ended up using the rooftop pool or hanging out up there because it really wasn't impressive at all. 
On our last day, our flight was cancelled so we needed to book another night at a hotel. We ended up staying at the Tribeca Grand and were instantly impressed by how much better the service and the quality of the hotel were.

title: “My New "Go To" Hotel in Manhattan”
text:
Initial impressions are even better than previous visits (which weren't bad)... good experience at check-in as, after a brief wait, the clerk seemed to go the extra mile to find me a quiet room as requested (away from the St. Paddy's Day madness). He did well... I got a very good night's sleep. 
Room service for dinner was quite good - both the quality of the food and the hospitality of the order taker. When I asked if there was an ice machine on my floor, he said "don't worry about it, we'll send a bucket up with dinner" - and they did - both nights. That was an unexpected and pleasant surprise. 
One downside to the room - it's nicely furnished, with a big flat screened TV, but the TV is on top of the chest of drawers (I guess for lack of anywhere else to put it). Unfortunately it's a bit of a neck strainer since you have to look up to a level of 6 feet and higher to watch TV. Also, there's no view from this particular room, even though it's on the 39th floor (3945), thanks to a larger building across the street. 
I like having a hotel cab stand, a couple of Starbucks in the hotel, a BankAmerica with ATMs right beside the hotel, and Broadway right next door. Based on this latest experience, this may have become my "go to" hotel in Manhattan.

title: “Great Local...”
text: Chose this hotel based on reviews.. I was taking my daughter to school(freshman year) and decided this would be the right place based on it's location. the room was small but clean the bed was comfy too.. Hilton does need to stop charging for every little thing such as the high priced internet(20 bucks) and the extremely high self parking I paid more for parking than the full sized rental I had (38 bucks a day) and on top of that the Starbucks in the hotel that normally offers free wi-fi didnt have it either.. the food was costly but thats ok We went to the cafe bakery on the corner and ate breakfast... (get the blueberry muffins but go early)And there are plenty of great restaurants to eat in, other than the hotel.... Otherwise the hotel is close to everything... good shopping on State and of couse Michigan Ave... lively people watching on Wabash... Close to public transportation because if I did not have to have a car to move my daughters stuff... I would definitely take public transportation.... the traffic in Chicago is RIDICULOUS!!! worst than D.C and NYC!! I love Chicago!!! Would I stay again? possibly (By the way the customer service was really accomodating) but I want to try a different hotel every time I come back to Chi town...

title: “Although undergoing construction, the staff were extremely friendly & helpful, room was clean and bed comfortable.”
text: In addition, the location was excellent for fast entrance and exit to San Francisco, but not within walking distance of much of interest. I was very impressed with the friendliness and helpfulness of the staff.

title: “Wonderful stay”
text:
What a wonderful weekend I spent at the Westin in Charlotte! The valet was helpful and polite, he even offered to give us information about local eateries which I took him up on the next day. Check in was immediate even though the hotel was very crowded on that weekend. My room was very clean, the beds are 'heavenly'! I even had a great view.
My favorite part was the bar and lounge area. After spending the day at the convention center (right next door), it was a great spot to unwind. There were a couple of large plasma tvs to watch the games on and nice comfortable couches as well as tables and chairs. Our waitress, Ruby, was attentive, friendly and prompt, even though she had a big group of us to attend to.
I would love to have this exact hotel in every city I travel to!

title: “Good quality big-box hotel, no surprises”
text:
This is a big hotel, central, and civilized - prime convention territory!
But no surprises. Big, comfortable rooms, nice bed (with a futon between the bottom sheet and the mattress - novel - but comfortable), well appointed bathrooms, the food's good, staff are well-trained-polite, if a little try-too-hard friendly (when I told the check-out clerk I was flying to Boston, she said "oh, send me a postcard!". Yes, of course, what was I thinking...). 
But this hotel is just what you'd expect from a big Hyatt in a big city, and there's nothing wrong with it. I paid about $300 which was a bit expensive for what I got, but not by much. My Hyatt status gets me free internet, tho' I'd guess it 's probably not cheap otherwise, and it worked generally ok. Tea/coffee and ipod player in the room gets plus marks, as does a big bathtub.
The negatives weren't life-threatening. The hotel's been well renovated, but it's nevertheless an old big-box hotel, "mutton dressed up as lamb". The one major niggle wouldn't be a problem for most travellers. I checked before I booked that there was a pool, and what the opening hours were (from 5am). I checked again when I got to the hotel, with the front desk. And I checked once more in the hotel services booklet. Jetlag, an early flight, and a training programme, meant I was at the door of the pool at 5:00 sharp in the morning. Locked door. 5:05 still locked. I called reception, who said they'd get someone from security to come, which they did... at 5:30. So my long workout turned into a short workout and I could have stayed in bed another half an hour. And neither the receptionist nor the security guard attempted an apology.
So any other lunatic early morning athletes beware. The rest of you... ignore that whinge! 
But more of you might be unimpressed with the "business centre" that consisted of a room of machines, all self-service with a credit card. No staff in sight and you can't charge faxes, etc, to your room - credit card swipe only. Now THAT's pissy.

title: “Great value.”
text: I was on a very tight budget and this hotel was a good fit for location and price. It was clean and the staff were personable and professional. Motel 6 is across the street, but I would not hesitate to recommend this place as a much better value. Be aware that the kitchenette has nothing but the cupboards and appliances; you will have to supply your own silverware, can opener, etc. It worked for us - Mom and 14 yr old daughter on Spring Break.

title: “Good hotel in a good location”
text: Stayed here day before new years. Was nice. Looks like good hotel if I was working in downtown boston rooms are quaint. Probably not a family hotel. More for couples

title: “Good Stay”
text: we just got back from our stay. We went for our sons Marine graduation. Location was perfect. This hotel, airport, and MCRD all very very close. We never had to stray far. A short walk to Old Town, a historic area of San Diego. We ate 3 times at a great Mexican rest called the Coyote Cafe and it was awesome. Try the Chicken Quesadilla. Its money. Also very close to a lot of other eating places within a very short drive. The staff was great at Western Inn. They helped me several times. Bed comfort wasnt the greatest but ok. I would stay there again, no problem.

title: “Nice Location”
text: We stayed there in late July for 3 nights. We were for the first time in San Francisco and the surprise was how cold is the summer there, but luckily, the room had heating. And yes, we kept it working constantly. The hotel is located across from China Town, which is great. We were close to almost everything we wanted to see in San Francisco, by car or on foot. Very comfortable hotel, clean, with friendly staff. The room we stayed in was located at the end of the hallway and it was quiet at night. I'm not sure if I would like to go back to San Francisco, but if I do, I wouldn’t mind staying again at this hotel.

title: “What a Fab place to stay”
text: Just got back from a 4 night stay at the Edison ,was a bit worried by some previous reviews, but found it an excellent place to stay.Yes some rooms are a bit dated but ours was very clean with fresh towels each day , a superb hot shower and working hairdryer.The bed was very comfy and not a bug in sight, as we were on the 12th floor we had no noise from outside and the staff were very helpful and polite.We didnt spend much time in the rooms as we had loads to fit in, we did the Empire State building, The Statue of Liberty,Ground Zero,Brooklyn Bridge,watched the New York Rangers play the New Jersey Devils at ice hockey in Madison Square Gardens,did a World Yacht dinner cruise,The natural history museum,ice skated on Central Park and saw Lion King,as well as fitting in lots and lots of shopping,no wonder we were shattered when we got home!We had the best time ever I cant wait to go again.

title: “Great few nights in New York”
text:
I recently stayed here for 4 nights with my husband on our honeymoon before we flew to Mexico. 
The hotel is great, perfect location two blocks from Times Square and right beside the Port Authority bus station which was so handy to get to and from Newark and JFK (private car from hotel to newark cost 95 dollors so we got the bus back to hotel from airport 18 dollars) 
The hotel doesnt have a very inviting lobby as its so small, but that didnt bother us as we were never there. Free internet, tea and coffee in the lobby which was great. 
For our first three nights we stayed on the 29th floor with a few of the Empire State building. The bed was extreamly comfy and the bathroom big with a great shower. However the room was tiny and we could barely open two suitcases. But when your not in the room for any length of time it didnt really matter. On our last night we were on the 4th floor. This room was much bigger but was beside the port authority bus station so there was alot of noise - bring some ear plugs. Breakfast was not included, however we did eat here and found it very good and the same price as anywhere else in the area. Theres also plenty of places to eat at the bottom of the street with plenty of choice here. 
Ive never stayed in New York before so I cant compare it to other hotels but i would definitly stay here again and would recommend it to others.

title: “Wonderful quirky boutique hotel”
text: Great club room for breakfast and dinner hour snacks. Nice rooms with everything working - which isn't always the case for NYC hotels. Would be nice to have more than one elevator on occasion - being on a low floor allows for a quick trip up the steps (but you can't descend the stairs below the third floor). Having the Monkey Bar and Restaurant on site is a nice plus.

title: “Classical Feeling Hotel”
text: We traveled just after Christmas and just before the New Year. The hotel was beautifully decorated in a very classic style. The public space was very nice. The rooms were very nice, but the bathroom could have used a little bit of updating, but it matched the classic, almost vintage quality of the hotel. The service was great - whether in person or on the phone. They also did a nice job of having apple and hot cider available in the lobby for guests.

title: “You have not experiences New York if you have not stayed at the Waldorf Astoria!”
text:
I Would most deffinately recommend this hotel to anyone who wants the ultimate New York experience. It's location is fantastic for first time visitors and experienced travellers. Nestled perfectly on Park Avenue you are a stones throw away from Grand Central Station which is not only a must see, but makes it easy for you to get around, and impossible to get lost. You are also within EASY walking distance from central park, rocker fella centre and many more attractions. Just tap the address into google maps and see for yourself!!!
Within the hotel you are greeted by the most helpful staff who are a credit to the hotel. Everywhere is spotless. The rooms are huge and come with all the facilities from irons, hair dryers to satelite television offering a decent range of programmes. Although I found that the power output from electircal appliances such as hair dryers and straighteners was weaker than I am used to, so ladies you may have to get up a little earlier for perfect hair!!!
The food is amazing with varieties to suit all tastes. Although not the cheapest, it is not necessarily expensive when you consider the expertise of the chef that is cooking for you!!! Not every day can you say an award winning chef has prepared your lunch...well you can when staying at the Waldorf.
You do not get the impression that the Waldorf attracts a "type" of traveller, there is always a range of people wandering in awe around the lobby from business associates to families, to couples. The hotel caters for the needs of all it's guests on an individual basis, which makes you feel invited to part of the hotel family (not a fish out of water)
My partner and I would never contemplate staying anywhere else and will be back as soon as possible!!!!

title: “Great choice for Vacation stay”
text: The hotel was easy to find. Staff was super friendly and welcoming. Room was clean and very spacious, lots of storage space and loved being able to cook some meals in the kitchen to save some money. Room was the quietess I have ever stayed in. My only issue was that I did have a reservation in advance that clearly stated 3 people and the bathroom was only stocked with towels and washcloths for 2 people and the sofa bed did not have a pillow or blanket; only a fitted sheet and flat sheet that I found in the closet. Staff was quick about supplying the proper items though. The Candlewood Cupboard left something to be desired, very few items availble so I would suggest bringing your own food and snacks. With that said, I would definately stay again.

title: “Beautiful hotel, perfect location...”
text: Stayed for a two night birthday celebration for my 8 year old daughter who wanted to go to the American Girl store. Honestly could not beat the location. Check in was smooth and my kids loved the elevator bank. We were out and about all day but since the hotel was so close to everything we just kept returning to drop off our things. Saw The Lion King right next door and absolutely loved it (really worth the expense!!) The hotel food was pricey and we did eat our meals outside of the hotel. Junior's on 46th was fabulous for breakfast. Would definitely recommend to anyone traveling with kids--the 2 queen beds and a pullout couch was spacious We didn't hear another person the whole time we were in our room on the 37th floor--soundproofing was amazing.

title: “Terrace cafe”
text: Stayed in this resort this weekend and found the grounds to be beautiful, the concierge desk very helpful and the rooms fit our needs. The only down fall was the Terrace Cafe, found their breakfast buffet to be pricey especially for your average food selection as convenient as it was to eat there would not do it again.

title: “A great stay”
text:
A colleague and I stayed for 4 nights at the Westin River North for a meeting at the convention center. For comparison, I stayed at the Hyatt McCormick Place last year for a similar convention and promised myself that I wouldn't do that again--the convention center is in the middle of nowhere in Chicago. The Westin River North is very conveniently located by the river--less than 20 minutes by shuttle to the convention center and a 5 minute walk to the Magnificent Mile. Had a nice partial view of the river. If you're in Chicago primarily for shopping, though, it's probably a better idea to stay on or right off the Magnificent Mile.
Pros: Heavenly Bed and Bath. Wow. Even if the hotel room were in an alley, I would happily stay there. Smoke-free hotel is nice. Wireless internet free in the lobby.
Cons: Use of the fitness center requires an extra fee. If the price is almost $400 a night, this should be included. Also, no free internet in the rooms. Also--the toiletries were average. The W has Bliss products and the nearby Hotel James offered Kiehl's products
Overall: based on the location, cleanliness and the Heavenly Bed and Bath, I would definitely stay here again while in Chicago.

title: “The Magic Castle Hotel is Magical!”
text:
My wife and I recently went to L.A. for a wedding and to visit our daughter. With all the rave reviews of the Magic Castle Hotel, how could we not try it? We arrived there in the evening with high expectations, but we were quickly disappointed. The carpeting in our room had numerous holes like cigarette burns (it turned out that these were dark spots). The next morning we debated about complaining to the management. After some hesitancy, we decided that management should know that our experience was not consistent with the reviews that we had read. After all, we were going to be there for three more nights. We started wondering whether the reviews were written by real guests of the hotel.
We addressed the carpet problem with the person at the front desk. She was very understanding and offered to place us in another comparable room. However, this room was near the street, and we did not want to risk the possible noise. So we decided to stay put and thought that was the end of it.
As we were enjoying our breakfast at poolside, we were approached by the general manager. He apologized and offered us further assistance. He indicated that another room was opening up that morning. A little later that morning he gave us the key for this newly vacated room. Were we surprised! The room was enormous with a full kitchen, dining area, living room, etc. Besides this free upgrade, he advised us that the first night would be deducted from our bill.
With large smiles upon our faces, we promptly moved over our luggage to our new luxury suite. We then went back to the pool for swimming and sunbathing. Upon our return to the suite, we found a beautiful bouquet of flowers from a florest with a note apologizing for the inconvenience from the general manager. This was astonishing! Where do you get such service from a hotel?
The remainder of our stay there could not have been better. The location is 2 blocks from Grauman's Theater and other tourist sites, as well as the subway that we took to Olvera St. The pool was refreshing with staff members bringing out popsicles and cool towels. The staff members were incredible - from helping with directions to caring for our every needs. The general manager was awesome and went over the top in making sure that we were satisfied. Would we stay there again? In a heartbeat. For us, the Magical Hotel was magical!

title: “love LOVE love this hotel... BUT, DON'T EVER go to their restaurant...!”
text: From the time we walked into the hotel until checking out, everyone EXCEPT the restaurant was great! The doorman, bellman, front desk receptionist... Outstanding! Came for our daughters 6th birthday and our first time in NY. We got the I love chocolate package. This is where I knew we would never eat here. No one greeted us so after standing for about 10 mins we go back up to the front desk and are told we seat ourselves. Maybe the waiter and hostess that walked by 3 or 4 times past us could have told us that. We finally seat ourselves and tell the hostess that we had the package, so she and the waiters assume thats all we wanted? No water, menu...nothing offered. My husband finally went to the bar to order... And that's when some waiter came by to offer help? I wanted them to at least brink a candle out to put in the mini cake but that would mean someone would come around to check on us. It must have been too busy with the 2 other guests seated at tables? Then to top it off, they actually tried to charge me? Then checking out, oh gosh, over 45 mins to wait for a bellman to help with our luggage? After calling down 3 times my husband decided to go find a cart himself. That was a little aggravating. Other than those 2 minor disappointments (well, the restaurant being a huge one because when we have stayed at other hotels, they have always acknowledged our daughters birthday and taken some part to participate in it).... We are staying here again for the Macy's Day Parade... I cannot wait! Hopefully the service at the restaurant will be better next time we are there, not for us, we refuse to eat there, but the other people who decided to go. The delay in baggage upon checkout, loved the location and the treatment of the hotel staff soooooo much, can overlook minor issues like that...!

title: “Pretty good hotel with Free Breakfast!”
text: We chose this hotel because of its proximity to Times Square and a free breakfast (we paid ~$300 including taxes). The breakfast was great every day. The room was pretty good, you can tell that it was updated and they did a good job, it's just not the nicest hotel I've stayed in, which I didn't expect going in. We stayed at the Westin in Times Square for about $500 a night and this hotel was much better for value and a FREE BREAKFAST. The hotel was also very close to the metro. If you want to stay near Times Square, stay here.

title: “Horrible...I should file a lawsuit!!”
text: I was extremely disappointed with my hotel room. The lobby and location were good. The hotel has 2 on-site restaurants. One of the restaurants is a sushi bar (if you like sushi). I love sushi. The food was good but the service was poor. The front desk host talked to me like I was there to clean the floors. I was dressed down and maybe I just looked simple minded. I finally had to end the conversation before he dumbed it down any further. That was the beginning of a horrible stay. A rude experience with the front desk can ruin any trip. In this case, that's what happened. I also wasn't impressed with my room. Let me preface these comments by saying that I'm a member of this hotel's frequent quest program. I stay at their sister properties all the time. However, this property was just not up to par. The hotel itself (being clean, spacious, excellent location, concierge etc) are all there. However, I called the front desk and asked if long distance calls were free. I was told they were $1/min. I later discovered that I'd been given the wrong info regarding the long distance rates. The rude service and misinformation given by the front desk absolutely made me hate this place. I was glad to leave and will not return. I should have left a complaint with the manager. I should invest in a PR campaign to embarass them and bring attention to their crass attitudes!! I may post a video on youtube that re-creates my bad experience with them. If you're a minority, you may not enjoy this "good 'ol boy" establishment.

title: “This grand old New York hotel is as luxurious and wonderful as ever!”
text: I can't say enough about what a great experience we had at The Waldorf. We were celebrating our 39th anniversary and the hotel and its staff could not have been more wonderful. The lobby is a grand step back in time and our room was simply fabulous. The staff from Agnes at check-in to Graham at the concierge desk were amazingly helpful and gracious. Whoever said New Yorkers were brusque and rude has never stayed at the Waldorf Astoria. And the location was an added benefit - easy to walk to the theater but out of the hub-bub of Broadway and Times Square. Wonderful restaurants in the neighborhood and the breakfast buffet at the Waldorf was simply magnificent.

title: “Great location and felt spoilt!”
text:
I went to New York for the weekend on my own as a break from three kids under five, so anything was great for me! However the Trump SOHO was more than fabulous - mostly because of the room and in-room service. The hotel was in a great spot - about 20 metres to a subway station and not much further to great cafes and restaurants. 
The bathroom was fabulous, with a big bath, which I sunk into after walking for 7 hours - and even better, a TV in the bathroom so I could watch TV while soaking. 
I went out to a show and came back and my room had been readied for bed - pillows fluffed, bottle of water, chocolate and slippers by my bed! 
I will stay there again - and have booked my husband in for his weekend away as well.

title: “Very nice stay”
text: We spent 3 nights in San Antonio at Comfort Suites Alamo at $110.49 per night. The room was very clean and nicely furnished. The breakfast bar was very good with a large variety and a hot breakfast provided. We were there Tues thru Thurs and each afternoon from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. a Manager's Meet & Greet was held. Snacks were provided and beer or wine was also available at no charge to guests. The attendant, Gloria Rios, made sure you were greeted and got plenty of food and drink. She did a great job and was a really pleasant hostess. The hotel is a few blocks from the Riverwalk, however, they run a free shuttle every hour to various locations on the Riverwalk. We just called to be picked up. All and all it was a very nice place to stay.

title: “Great Clean Hotel in Great Location”
text: This hotel is right across the street from Penn Station and for us this was great bc we were coming in and leaving via train. We originally had one of the smaller rooms but the staff was nice enough to upgrade us to the next larger size which meant we had a kitchenette as well. That was great bc we had two little ones with us. I like this hotel bc I feel that it is centrally located to all that Manhattan had to offer. Mostly we walked everywhere from here except when we were trying to catch Staten Island Ferry- then we took taxi. It did rain while we were there and so had to take taxi's bc of that but otherwise, woudl highly recommend this hotel. There are plenty of restaurants and shopping nearby as well.

title: “Friendly staff and exellent location!”
text:
Went for a short 3 day trip to New York with my wife and my in-laws and we could not have asked for a better hotel for our stay. The hotel staff was friendly and very accommodating, they even let us have breakfast when we arrived at 9:00am even though check in is only at 3pm. They also have a service to hold your bags which was great because we came in way before check in when we arrived and left long after check out when we left. It was great to leave our bags there while we got a jump on exploring the city. 
Hotel could not of been in a better location either, just a short walk to Times Square, Central Park and Madison Square Gardens. The only time we really needed to cab was to get to the financial district to visit the 911 memorial and battery park. We will definitely stay here again on our next visit to New York.

title: “I want to live in The Michelangelo!”
text: This hotel is fantastic!! We loved the great location, beautiful room/suite and could not believe how friendly and polite each and every staff person was. The turn-down service, complete with chocolates, at night was a wonderful bonus after a long day of sightseeing. The concierge, James, is a gem! Our only suggestions would be to offer free wi-fi in the rooms, have a coffee maker in the room, and offer fruit or juice along with the pastries/coffee continental breakfast. We highly recommend staying at the Michelangelo!!

title: “What a beautiful hotel to experience...just work on the service.”
text:
I stayed at the Fairmont a year ago with a youth group. We were in town for a youth convention - so there were A LOT of kids at this hotel. 
The good: The hotel is just lovely. Our room was massive, the bathroom massive (I was in a room with 5 young ladies so this was greatly appreciated), there was a vanity area, good closet, and very large hallway. And all of the space was beautifully appointed. The beds were soft and the bedding was delicious and I couldn't have loved the space more. (Until the five young ladies made every corner of the room an out of control mess.) The hotel lobby and lounge is gorgeous and a lot of fun! The hotel is in a great location, easy walk to the convention center, easy walk to lots of fun places to eat and the train. It's across the street from a great park and fountain. It's just a very cool area.
The bad: Now these are just picky, but they still bothered me for the level of place we were staying in. Our rooms were not ready on time. After traveling a long distance and being extremely exhausted, it was an excruciating wait. Also, there were five people in our room. They knew this, they provided the air mattress and we paid for that extra person. But I had to call housekeeping every single day to have one or two more towels delivered. This is really a nuisance after about the third day. Our bathrobe disappeared after the second day never to be replaced. Our air conditioning didn't seem to work very well. (They did get an engineer up to our room ASAP and got it mostly working.) But the one that really got me is that we worked with the concierge to find a nice place to have dinner with these 12 kids. The concierge was very nice although she didn't seem to quite understand what we were going for. (She kept wanting to send us to chain restaurants when we were looking for something unique to San Jose.) We finally picked out a restaurant, she said she would call and make the reservation and call us if there were any problems. When we showed up at the establishment , they didn't have our reservation. They were a place that didn't accept reservations. Well, that was embarrasing and aggravating. I know we were a group with a bunch of kids, but we were paying customers and I would have expected to be treated with the same level of care as other customers. It may have just been that particular concierge. The others seemed more professional - she is just who happened to be on duty when we walked up. All in all, these are fairly minor.
We did love this hotel and the location. I would not only stay here again, but I would definitely look forward to staying in a Fairmont in other locations as well.

title: “Ok but they charged tax that wasn't on web site”
text: We stayed June 22 for 2 nights and found the hotel condition to be about average 3 star mainly because it was old but functional. We booked through its hotel web site which showed total amount including taxes but this is incorrect. They added additional $1.84/night "San Diego Marketing Tourism Assessment". I will complain to BBB about this improper business practice. They don't tell you taxes til you checkout. Pluses that you normally don't find include refrigerator, microwave, and wi-fi internet from your room. Parking was crowded and small spaces.

title: “Perfect (almost).”
text: My granddaughter and I moved from a truly horrendous hotel for an early check-in and the next 24 hours were my 12-year-old's favorite New York experience--except for Lion King of course. The room was spacious, the bathroom even more so, and the service was brilliant. Of course it is in a price range I wouldn't normally be experiencing but as an anecdote to the previous night's disappointment. I must say we were not overwhelmed by the food..it wasn't bad exactly, just seemed quite ordinary considering how great everything else was...

title: “I would stay here again and again!”
text:
I was in NYC last week for business, and wasn't sure exactly where I wanted to stay. I had looked up many room reviews on trip advisor, and was turned off by reviews of dirt, mice and unhelpful people, so I wasn't sure where I would stay.
I'm a bit of a picky hotel traveler- must be clean, safe, and up to date. I usually have good experiences at Hiltons, so I decided to try this Hilton.
I arrived very early, prior to check in, so the woman behind the check in desk offered to call me when my room was ready. The bellman held my bags while I was out all day long. It was a no brainer. They were very friendly and accomodating. When I returned back at the end of my day, my key was already waiting and I was ready to go.
In regards to the room- It was very clean (from what I could tell) and updated. The room was quiet and actually larger than I have seen in NYC. The bed was nice and Comfy, and the towels were nice and big :)
The location was great- right around the corner from Times Square. If you're looking for fun, I decided last minute to go see Mary Poppins, which is a few doors down. Great show, and if you're travelling by yourself like I did, it's easy to find a seat. The only thing I wish I would have done was go to TKTS in Times Square and find a half price ticket, but since I was alone, I didn't feel like wandering out once it was dark.
I did, however find this area safe and easy to navigate.
I will definitely come back to this hotel again. I'm sort of a hotel snob, so if you are like me, you will probably find this to be a good place to stay while in NYC.

title: “Totally Enjoyable Experience”
text:
Our stay comprised a three day event with the highlight being a wedding performed in the Morris House courtyard. The Hotel Staff were very gracious, kind and helpful to meeting all of our needs for the wedding ceremony and reception dinner.
This Hotel is highly recommended for a casual, family wedding of about 100 guests.

title: “It was better than I expected and I expected a lot!!!”
text: The room, the restaurant, the bar I loved them all.

title: “Best Hotel in Chicago”
text: The Hotel Monaco is my favorite hotel in Chicago (and anywhere else)! It is so comfortable and the staff and service are the best in the business. I always feel like I'm at home when I stay there. If you want a beautiful room that feels like your bedroom at home and people that make you feel like you're family, stay at the Monaco!

title: “Very good hotel”
text:
Very nice stylish hotel with beautiful quiet and clean rooms. 
The only complains are the beds were a little bit hard and we had to ask twice for a babycot. But overall a good hotel with very friendly staff and an excellent location.

title: “Excellent location and amenity, average front desk staff”
text:
Hotel Vitale has one of the best locations in town with bay bridge view. It is located right across the Ferry building and proximate to many top restaurants. Very easy and safe for those who like to run by the water (from Ferry building to bottom of GG bridge and back is 10 miles). The room is spacious and is consistently maintained so it feels fresh and clean. The decor is modern. Waterfront view is a plus.
The hotel seems to cater towards vacationers and pay less attention to frequent business visitors. If I compare Vitale to other hotels I stayed when vacationing, then I would say Hotel Vitale met high marks. However, it's attention towards frequent travelers still has a lot of room for improvement. For example, the joy program advertises upgrade based on availability, but of course it never offered to me without asking sadly the answer was always no. The front desk staff can be more friendly and helpful. May be it is too much for them to remember names and preference (even it is on the profile!), but they just seems to go through the motion to check guests in and out. In contrast, all other staff in the hotel was amazing! The valet/bell team has super memory (names, time needed a car, etc.) and are always so ready to help. Last time the valet staff set the cab driver straight when he refused to take me to a nearby location (he was expecting airport). I very much appreciated the help.

title: “great location and good value for being in manhattan!”
text:
Stayed in the hotel for about 10 days before flying back to the UK and thoroughly enjoyed my stay!
First up, the hotel is in a great location, right next to times square, broadway and penn station.
Rooms are small, but thats expected in the type of hotel it is! They are very comfy rooms though and clean! Free Wifi is also available!
Staff were friendly enough but only really spoke to them at check in/out.
Only problem we had was the breakfasts... which were very nice but it was always so busy that there would be nothing left! And I don't know whether it is because I'm British and enjoy a good queue but it was more or less a free for all and people would fight to get the food!
