But apart from that the hotel is great value and definitely a good place to stay especially for young couples!

title: “A relaxing summer getaway/staycation”
text: My girlfriends and I had a fantastic time at Arizona Grand Resort. One of my friends and I live in Phoenix, but we had another friend fly in from NY (where it is much, much cooler). Being out at the pool and the amazing water park, you totally forget just how hot it is. I felt like a teenager again going down the 12-story slides! All the staff we came into contact with were really nice. And, the rooms are awesome. Every room is a suite, so you really can't go wrong. They are so roomy, and there was a nice sitting area away from the bedroom where we could sit, talk, play games, etc. We will definitely be back!

title: “Accomodating and Convenient”
text: The hotel is conveniently located on the magnificant mile.and the doormen Willie and Stan are very friendly and helpful in giving you directions to all the various sites in Chicago.I live part -time in Chicago, next door to the hotel,and the front desk manager ,Simon has been very gracious in getting very favorable rates and upgrades when my family comes to town.If I were a tourist I would always stay at the Intercontinental Chicago.

title: “Morgans in New York”
text:
We stayed at Morgans for three night and we can really recommend it. If you like shopping it's a walking distance to great stores. The included breakfast is a big plus of course.
The minus is that they don't offer free WI-FI and be careful using their cab service. They tried to charge us 90 USD for taking us to New Ark airport (taking a yellow cab is about 65 USD on a flat rate).

title: “Great location, incredible views, reasonable price considering the location.”
text: What else can I say. If you go, insist on an upper level floor with a poolside balcony. The views to the city are incredible at night. Yes, the airport is right next door and I suppose if you are a light sleeper you could have some issues. But with the sliding balcony door closed, I had no problem at all. Relatively new hotel with restaurant and bar, a little more expensive but nice. You have to try Oggi's Pizza which is on the backside of the parking lot. Overall, a great experience.

title: “Oasis with great location”
text: We stayed in petite room for 9 nights. The room was small but nice and it had everything we needed. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We especially enjoyed the 2nd floor. It was like an oasis for tired travellers.

title: “Away from home”
text: I travel a lot for work I have been at this hotel thru the mon-fri for 4 weeks. Having to travel for work is hard enough and these folks go the extra mile to ensure your comfortable and that's usually not the way other places operate, they don't give you lip service here. I like this hotel.

title: “Excellent hotel for family”
text: It is located on 6th ave, just next to Seneca street. What does it mean? It is just minutes walk down to Pike or Pine street where all things happening there. Just keep in mind SUUPP so you won't be lost. S for Seneca, U for university, and Union, next is Pike, and last P is for Pine. Seattle is a very tourist friendly, and so is Crowne Plaza. Very convenient to get there, don't spend too much money on shuttle, you can just book a Downtown Airporter from SeaTac that cost you about $13 per person, and being a Crowne guest you'll be benefited to get dropped off first before anyone else, as that is the first stop from the airport. While you can stroll around during the day, you can ultimately enjoy your rest as the hotel is in a very quiet neighborhood. If you need small bite, subway is just down, next building. Get some groceries at the store just cross the street at 6th and Seneca st junction down the parking garage. Overall it's worth for money, considering the family friendly and the great location.

title: “Great location - Not-so-great hotel”
text: One main reason we chose this hotel was that it is very convenient to everything - and it certainly is - and there is free parking. However, this hotel states it was renovated in February 2011; but when we arrived in July 2011, the renovation was still taking place. We went without cable for a night and half a day while it was being upgraded without being advised beforehand. Our room, one double bed, was very tiny for two people but it was clean. The parking was filled very quickly, and one night we had to park in the next-door hotel's lot. The breakfast bar didn't have a microwave, so I couldn't get oatmeal (I could have made it in my room as there was a microwave there; but I didn't bring any with me). There was no hotel book in the room for reference, and the people at the front desk seemed very disinterested. We paid for our stay with Priority Club reward points; and I believe 25,000 per night was too many points for what we received.

title: “5 STAR SERVICE in a 3 STAR SETTING”
text:
The staff is among the friendliest i've ever encountered. All extremely helpful. From Vinnie and Jenny at the front desk. Jay in Valet, Gary the bellman, and especially Ally the new intern who has a bright future in Hospitality.
The downside was the condition of the carpeting in the halls. Worn and stained. I stayed in their largest suite called the EXTREME WOW. A two room suite and living room. It was somewhat large but yet confining. The furniture was very uncomfortable. The decor was all over the place. The room had 9 vases in it. What do you do with that many vases?? The TV channel guide was lacking channels. We had large stains on our carpet as well. Bring plenty of cash for room service though you might want to bring in take out because the quality was average at best
The gym was small. Mostly cardio machines,a few dumb bells, and one universal cable set up.
I could watch Sunday football in my room but in the gym i couldnt watch any game because the gym TV was on a different channel guide according to staff member.
Great location for food, shops, etc, but for the money spent it should have been better dressed

title: “Definitely coming back to Hotel 41 At Times Square!!”
text:
We stayed 6 nights at Hotel 41 and I have to say that it was 110% positive experience. Extremely friendly and helpful staff. Originally our reservation was for 7 nights but we missed our connection in Paris so I had to cancel the first night of our reservation.They changed our reservation for 6 nights, no penalty fees, no questions asked. Our room (superior) was super clean and bed was very comfy. Air conditioning was bit loud, but hey; it was 105 'F outside!! Bathroom was very nice and clean. Complimentary WI-FI, breakfast and cappuccino .
Location was the best, subway(s), Port Authority, Times Square...just few steps away. 
We'll come back for sure!!

title: “Good Place to Stay”
text: Stayed for 3 nights in July. Family of four with two teenage daughters. Selected this hotel because of location and free (included) breakfast. Hotel is a short walk from the Gershwin Theater, home of "Wicked". Did the behind the scenes tour (highly recommended, daughters loved it) and the Saturday show. Could walk back and forth from hotel. First room smelled musty, so asked for different room. No problem...second room fine. Was personally taken to the room by Silvio to make sure was all ok. He checked in with us each evening to see how we were enjoying our stay. Didn't really expect this type of hospitality in NYC. Four stars for Silvio...they should keep him there. Rooms are typical Hampton (nice), although maybe a bit more worn (because of the high amount of use I suppose). They are re-doing some wallpaper etc to spruce up. Maid did a very nice job cleaning the room each day and should be commended. I'm pretty pickey about things, and I'm not beyond asking for changes or a discount if things are not right. Not the fanciest NY hotel, but still good. Breakfast was very good but room could get crowded. On Saturday there was a long line out the door to get in...but thankfully we had eaten early and had a much smaller crowd to contend with. Other days were ok. We enjoyed our visit and would stay here again if we return. We all commented to each other on how well everthing worked out so well staying at this Hampton Inn.

title: “AWFUL MANAGER ON SITE!!!!!!!!!!”
text: First of all I would like to say that I have stayed at this hotel many times in the past years and it was a pleasure because of the price and location... Upon on trying to get to this hotel I took a wrong turn somewhere and got lost so I called the hotel and spoke with a young woman named Kristen who tried to assist me she even went so far as to get a made out and try and help me..I did what she said got turned around and was still lost so I called back. Then the trouble started got someone on the phone by the name of Almead (found out he was the manager there on his off day). He asked where was I, I told him I was on a street called Schretz and 35.He kept asking where is that. I tried describing what I say.He kept saying tell me again where u r I told him again he said look calm down i'm trying to help you I'm not in the car with you so I dont know where you are so tell me again at that time I ask to speak to someone else. wanted to say more but no room..plz contact me..

title: “Beautiful historic hotel”
text: The Palace is a large, historic hotel located on Market Street near the Financial District. It has the charm and character of a "grand dame" historic hotel -- high ceilings, beautiful woodwork, and other architectural touches you don't see in newer hotels. The Garden Cafe restaurant is one of the prettiest hotel dining rooms I have ever seen -- soaring glass ceilings in a beaux arts style. The hotel is adjacent to public transportation (a BART station is in front of the hotel, and the electric trolleys run along Market in front of the hotel). It is an easy walk to the Union Square and Chinatown areas, with all of the restaurants and shopping there. The downsides are relatively small rooms and bathrooms (at least in the "superior" rooms), somewhat worn and dirty carpet, and significant noise from adjoining rooms and from the street outside. Bottom line is that this is a classy historic hotel that is a nice break from the usual business hotels, so long as you can tolerate the nicks and dings that are inevitable with a 100+ year old property.

title: “Better Places to be Found in Chicago...So NOT Four Star”
text:
I stayed at the Avenue for one night for a business trip. I went with a colleague to check in around 2p. Unfortunately, we were told that rooms would not be available until 3p (the check in time). We got back around 4p. I got upstairs to my room and it had an odd smell: moldy almost like someone had smoked in the room. I called to the front desk to change my room. The only room available was the kid’s room (colorful room with plastic toys). It was odd that management or someone from the front desk never came up to smell the room. My colleague came down and smelled the room. She too had a room with a similar scent, but not as bad. As best I can describe – the smell was like an antique cellar. I passed on the kid’s room and stayed put. 
Later in the night when I returned from a work event around 11p, I turned up my heat. By 1a it was still chilly in the room and I turned the heater up to 85 degrees….but it just got colder. By 130a I called the front desk and within 10 minutes an engineer was in my room. Now, I am happy he came so quickly and only took 20 minutes to take apart my heater and clean the filter. By 4a I had to be up for a 6a flight – only having 2 hours of decent sleep. No one at the hotel ever called to apologize or offer anything—this was customer service at its worst. For a $300/night room rate - I expected more. 
Basically, this is an outdated hotel desperately in need of upgrades. The reason the heater was spitting out cold air was b/c of build up on the filter – you would think a four star hotel would be constantly monitoring for this. 
Pluses on this was that the person that checked me in was really helpful in looking up restaurant recommendations and addresses. In general, the staff was responsive, but never went above and beyond. Location is great, but there are so many other hotels with great location. Bed was comfortable and bathroom spacious (but again outdated). I also had a nice partial view of Magnificient Mile.

title: “Basically Fine”
text: The key to this hotel is BASICS. You have a basic bed, room and TV. That's it. On Riverside and W. 80th it's one of NYC's finest locations, 2 blocks from the legendary food emporium Zabar's, across the street from Riverside Park, its great boardwalk and cafe, overlooking the Hudson River, 2 blocks from the 79th St. subway. The room I had was twice the size of a single - but very comfortable - bed. The TV got 7 basic channels. It was clean, staff was nice, hotel was quiet, neighborhood is terrific. Hotel has a nice sitting room, usually empty. Rooms have no ambience, no color, no extras of any kind except refrigerator and microwave. No reading light! No designer soaps, no plush towels, no internet. If you need a safe place to sleep that's near NYC's great aged-like-cheese-and wine West 70's, this is it. Probably the best hotel bargain in Manhattan.

title: “Skip this one”
text: We must have hit a low point for this hotel when we visited this summer! Upon arrival, our room wasn't ready although it was after check-in time. The person at the front desk told us she'd call my cell immediately when it was ready. She never called. We checked in after waiting a couple of hours. Upon getting ready for bed, we found the sheets dirty, with stains on them you don't want to know about. It was very disturbing! Their response to this was short of frustrating as we had to wait longer than we should have for clean sheets to be delivered to our room. The accommodations were average at best and I would not recommend this hotel. Too many better choices out there.

title: “Great Place - Great Price”
text:
Great hotel, elegant, modern room, perfect location. Stayed at the Conrad with 3 other girls. We got two adjoining rooms. The bathrooms were huge with large soaking tubs, granite showers, double sink vanity with granite tops. Large flat screen tvs, white, fluffy duvets. And then to be located just above the Nordstrom!?!? What else can a girl ask for? We enjoyed a couple of breakfasts and a late night snack via room service which tasted good and was prompt. Service from all employees was courteous and efficient. Can you tell we enjoyed the place? We only paid $185 per room per night which seemed like a bargain to me. 
FYI.... Made the reservations through central reservations. They said that they could not guarantee the adjoining rooms but would add it as a request. I called the front desk the day before arrival to see if there was any way to ensure the adjoining rooms. Stephanie said no problem, she would take care of making sure we had them and we did.

title: “Fabulous getaway!”
text:
Just returned from a very mini vacation in the city. The hotel was fabulous - they upgraded our room upon hearing it was our anniversary! What a lovely gift. The room overlooked Times Square! 
The location is great - right in the middle of the Theatre district! We had dessert and drinks in The View - pricey but fun!
The room rates are high but worth it!!

title: “Pretty bad”
text: This Hotel is bizarre. Here on business. Yes - the water park is good if you're into that kind of thing - the beds are comfortable - There are one or two good restaurants in the property - but the neighborhood is crappy, the general layout is really lousy - no central eating-drinking spots - golf front nine is terrible-back nine much nicer. Just stay away-go elsewhere unless you have lots of kids that like a water park and you don't care about your own well-being.

title: “1st Time in Seattle”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 4 nights in Feb this year. The checking area was nice and the service was prompt and efficient. The parking is very expensive and there are a few lots near by but the price difference is very minimal. There is street parking available across the freeway and is considerably cheaper for over night parking. The bar on the street level is nice and has decent food menu. I would avoid sitting near the windows because every time someone comes in you get a major draft hitting you. I would advise sitting in front of the bar or to the right of it to be sheltered. The rooms are very nice, and the beds are comfortable. The only issue I had was that the bathrooms had no extractor (air vent) so If you take a hot shower the mirror gets totally fogged up. Nothing major but just something that would have been nice to have. You can walk to the water front if you'd like, great workout coming back since it's all up hill. I would recommend this hotel for anyone looking to be near downtown yet have the east of easy on and off the freeway.

title: “Very Pleasant”
text:
It was a very pleasant stay, we got a great deal by booking 2 months in advance. The hotel or the room weren't a clean or well maintained as they could have been but it was satisfactory for us. 
Bathroom was functional again needed to be updated. 
Amazing entrance foyer with a very impressive flower display- always felt nice to return to in the evening

title: “Adequate”
text: I stayed here for three nights while attending a conference at the convention center. The lobby of the hotel was very impressive but my "premium view" room was merely adequate. I believe I was in the older of the two towers. My view was quite nice but the room was underwhelming - old style CRT TV, small bathroom, typical hotel furniture. The service was good and the location is convinient to downtown and the waterfront. I would probably stay here again but insist on staying in the newer tower which I assume is nicer.

title: “THOROUGHLY DISGUSTED BY LACK OF ACCOUNTABILITY FOR STOLEN PROPERTY”
text:
My family and I visited Chicago in early November for a weekend of Chicago shopping and sightseeing...We found the Conrad-Chicago to be a typically appointed Conrad Hotel similar to several others we have had the pleasure of staying at not only for Business, but leisure travel....what we found shockingly disturbing, and quite frankly, appalling was the Conrad's (and Hilton's Corporate Executive Offices) complete lack of accountability or willingness to compensate us for the loss of STOLEN property from 1 of our 2 adjoining rooms....I am hopeful that reviewing my experience below at the Conrad Chicago will save others from countless hours of follow-up and property loss ..... One of our daughters decided to bring her $1800 Dell Lap-top computers along with her for the trip to complete her homework/projects....This computer was in one of her small tote bags that also contained shoes....A front desk attendant indicated a security tape of the lobby confirmed the bag was definately carried in by her at check in Friday Night, and I know it was definately in one of the rooms as late as Saturday afternoon... When we went to pack up on Sunday Morning, the bag with shoes and laptop was found to be missing...so after thoroughly checking every inch of both rooms, we reported the missing items and black bag to the front desk personal and they pleasanty said an investigation would take place...we were very appreciative and left to tour the SHed Aquarium...upon returning to the Hotel for a late check out I went back to the rooms to check one more time for the bag with no luck.....Unfortuntely we left the hotel with no laptop or bag with shoes but the Hotel front desk assured us that a investigation would be completed....
After returning to our home, my wife waited until Tuesday, and after no response from the Conrad Chicago, called to inquire about the investigation for the lost black bag with shoes and a laptop...Intitally the staff she spoke with were unaware of any such investigation, not giving up and getting increasingly frustrated my wife eventually was put on the line with the Hotel GM who repeatedly talked over her and essentially called her a liar by stating that there was no evidence that a black bag with shoes and a laptop was brought into or checked in to our room, AND HE THEN HUNG UP ON HER......UNBELIEVABLE !! At this point I became involved and wrote numerous emails to Conrad Staff who eventually FINALLY said they would complete a thorough investigation.....a few days later, "INCREDIBLY" after interviewing staff members and searching the Hotel, it was indicated to us that black bag with shoes (BUT NO LAPTOP) had been found under one of the beds in one of our rooms, and it was returned to us promptly...COME ON CONRAD -WHO ARE YOU TRYING TO KID HERE, it is OBVIOUS and does not take a genious to see the FACTS do not lie - there is some type of cover up going on by Hotel staff including the Hotel GM for a laptop that was stolen from us in our room at the Conrad.... ALMOST 3 MONTHS later we have yet to be compensated a single dime for theft of a $1800 Laptop computer that meant even more to our daughter as it had all of her school projects in progress on it ....and we spent over $2,000 at the Hotel for our 2 day stay....REAL NICE CUSTOMER TREATMENT...if you want that I suggest TRUMP Chicago up the street, my wife and I stayed there last month and had a truely 5 star experience!!
I have resisted sharing my experience here as I typically like to take the high road and expected that a Hotel such as the Conrad would make this bad experience right promptly ....BUT THEY HAVE NOT, IN FACT THEY HAVE CONTINUED TO DRAG THIS SITUATION ON TERRIBLY, NOT TAKE ANY ACCOUNTABILTY OR ACCEPTANCE OF BLAME FOR OUR LOSS, AND MOST INFURIATING, they have INSULTED MY WIFE AND I ALONG THE WAY....

title: “Satisfactory hotel near Amtrak”
text: We stayed in this hotel two nights before we boarded a train for home. It was adequate. We had some trouble with the shower. After they fixed it , it was much worse. But they did credit us with one night stay when we complained. We were a little further from town that we thought. But it is on a direct busline right into town. It was very easy. My husband is disabled and he could drive the scooter we rented right onto any of the buses very easily.

title: “Excellent Stay”
text:
We were very pleased with our experience at the Hyatt Fisherman's Wharf. We stayed four nights in a top floor interior Business room. The room was quiet (very important to us), spacious and comfortable. Service was excellent, uniformly. Staff members were well trained, courteous, and responsive. They were quite knowledgeable about their hotel and about their city. 
We did not eat in the restaurant.
The hotel is well located, near Fisherman's Wharf, cable cars, and Ghirardelli Square. For strong walkers, most of the tourist sights are accessible on foot; we walk to Union Square, the Embarcadero, even the South of Market area. However, most visitors will want to take public transportation to those areas.
Hotel parking is quite expensive, but the hotel staff were happy to recommend alternative parking sites. Look for packages that include breakfast or free valet parking. Top floor interior rooms are quietest, but pool noise can be distracting during the day.

title: “10/10 very happy with stay”
text:
Stayed here for 10 days for a first trip to New York from Australia. Staff were very attentive, happy to help, always smiling. Good sized room, had everything we needed. Unfortunately the lift was not working for most of our stay but we overlooked this due to the friendliness of the staff. 
Less than a 10 minute walk to Times Square, the location couldn't be better for the price! This hotel is not 5 star and would not be suited to everyone however it was clean, comfy and did the job. Will be returning to this hotel with my mum and brother for our second trip to NY later in the year.

title: “Wonderful experience”
text: My daughter and I stayed here on our way to Chicago. The hotel was very clean, the staff was friendly, the beds super comfortable, and the breakfast was awesome. When we first drove up and saw the gated parking lot, we were a little concerned. Once we got inside and met the staff and saw our room we just felt more secure. Not only were we safe and sound but so was our car. I definately would return if I ever make it to Memphis again.

title: “All bases covered”
text:
Does everything all around well.
Great location in the Gaslamp district, close to convention center etc.
Front Staff very helpful.
Breakfast is great. 
Room is well appointed and hotel is easy to navigate.
I would say that the pool and the exercise room are on the small side.

title: “Great location”
text: Right in the center of town and very handy to the train station etc. Yes it has the worlds slowest lift but got fit using the stairs. Very tidy room and hotel. Free Breakfast was basic but was a good start for the day. Would recommend that you try not to get a room facing the street as the trams are very noisy. We were on the top floor at the back and it was very quiet. A tip for the trams: get on/off outside the hotel (you will have to push) rather than wait in the big lines at the end of the stops.

title: “Beautiful!”
text: Classy and beautiful. The room and service were second to none. I will definitely return. From valet to the front desk I felt welcomed. It is a beautiful hotel! I loved the corner room and enjoyed the view from the balcony.

title: “First Class”
text:
I stayed at the hotel for 7 nights two of which were during Hurricane Irene. From the minute I arrived, the service was first Class. The Doorman were so friendly , helpful and no advice was spared when asked for ..thankyou Angel...yes that was his name.
Check in and out was efficient, I stayed on the 12th floor room 1269 which was spotless and very comfortable.
During the hurricane the hotel provided up to date information at what for them must have been a very trying time.
food wise I never ate at the hotel because there are plenty of good diners in the area offering a good breakfast at a great price. Would recommend staying here. free wifi is available in the lobby, but why not offer it free in the rooms. ( starbucks next door have it free for all customers)

title: “keep your cancellation number”
text:
I made a reservation to stay here in August 2007 and just got charged for the night I canceled.
So I would recommend that if you reserve a room here and cancel SAVE YOUR CANCELATION NUMBER!

title: “Very loud & run down (right next to RR tracks!)”
text:
I was in Memphis for a conference and my coworkers and I selected this hotel based on the good reputation of the Marriott chain. BIG mistake. This is a bad hotel in a NOISY location. I actually checked out after the first night and spent the second night at the Staybridge Suites- which was just down the road (less than 1 mile away) and a thousand times nicer. 
The Residence Inn is literally 100 feet (at most) from a busy train track and not too far from a street where the trains cross and blow their whistles. Trains came on a regular basis all day and all night long with a hour at most between trains. It was EXTREMELY loud and I got more or less no sleep. I am a 20-something that lived in dorms/apartments not too long ago, and currently live in an urban area, close to a fire station--so am used to noise and am certainly not what would be considered a "light sleeper". I do not see how anyone can sleep through the freight trains going by this hotel!! My room was on the back of the hotel facing the train tracks - however, my coworker stayed in a room on the front of the hotel and he said he could hear the trains loud and clear from his room as well. My room was so close to the tracks it actually shook as the freight trains went roaring by all night long.
My room (in the main building) was also dingy and run down. The coffee machine had not been cleaned and had mold growing inside. The closet door and towel bar were broken - closet door actually fell off when I tried to open. Room was missing an iron. The light in the bathroom had burned out. The room could have been cleaned better too (hair on bathroom floor, etc. etc.). 
On the positive side, the staff was very friendly, kind and most apologetic about the train situation. There is really no fault to be place on the staff for the awful location of this hotel and my bad experience staying here. Also, positively speaking, were the warm chocolate chip cookies served at check-in and the free breakfast (which I thought had a good selection). 
If you absolutely must stay at this hotel, I would suggest you be REALLY tired when you arrive, to the point where nothing would wake you - or bring a pair of earplugs. The Marriott chain should seriously consider removing their affiliation from this particular property. I cannot imagine there are any repeat customers. I will never stay here again.

title: “Great hotel and service. Will be back for sure!”
text: I was very pleased with every aspect of our stay with the Pan Pacific. One of my biggest surprises was the complimentary WIFI service. This is rare at a nicer hotel. We visited the Seattle Aquarium, Woodland Park Zoo, Pikes Place Market, and of course shopping downtown Seattle. The hotel was right in the middel of it all.

title: “There on business”
text: My wife and I attended the annual Powersports Dealer Expo at the Convention Center. We stayed in a (spa/king room) room with a king size bed and a spa. The spa is still the best ones we have ever been in. Very comfortable for 2 people and it was located in the bedroom which was a great touch (could watch TV from it). Most hotels that offer a spa or whirlpool are located in the bathroom and too small for 2 people. We also enjoyed dinner at Carrabas Italian Resteraunt (great food) and the Texas Roadhouse which are both adjacent to the hotel (2 minutes walking distance). All in all I had no complaints of our stay and booked the same room again this year. I'm keeping my fingers crossed that we have another great experience.

title: “Great value”
text: A friend and I stayed two nights there for a 3-day class near Airport Blvd and Century Blvd. We were able to walk to and from the class, have dinner at Denny's next door (we were too tired to go anywhere else). Continental breakfast is quite adequate, fruits, cereals, milk, Danishes, bagels, bread, coffee, and juices. The room was basic but clean. We paid $81/night, very good value.

title: “rooms are terrible”
text: worst stay ever in a hotel especially for a wyndham!..check in service was great (Terence) we got to our 1st room #309 it stunk of mould!!! the room itself was in very poor quality. The paint job was a joke paint all in ceiling the bathroom also had a bad odor and the bed sunk in the middle as soon as i lay on it. So i called Terence and he changed our room very quickly to room 229. It was a bit better as far as smell but the room itself felt damp and when i went to the small bathroom a roach was crawling out of the a/c vent. Very unhappy 1st and last time i would stay at a wyndham

title: “All about the location”
text:
Stayed here for a quick weekend trip to NYC. You can't beat the location. Not even half a block to Broadway, breezeways to MOMA, restaurants like Le Bernardin and Bar Americain, etc...
Staff is friendly and helpful, especially the door men and housekeeping. No complaints there.
My biggest complaint is the room itself. Apparently I had one of the rooms that had only been partially updated if that. Needs further updating. Hole in the wall in the kitchenette. Many scuffs in the paint, especially around the closet. Outdated VCR and TV. Toilet looked like something circa 1980s out the TV Show Dynasty. I will give them one thing though: it was very spacious by NYC standards.
Continental breakfast was pathetic even if it was free.
Rate versus location versus overall cleanliness is the winner here.

title: “Perfect view of Union Square!”
text: My stay here was nothing short of perfect. I was here for a business trip, and the company sprang for a corner room on one of the upper floors, giving me a gorgeous view of Union Square and the rest of San Francisco. The bed was the perfect blend of firm mattress and soft sheets, the bathroom was huge, and I got a copy of the San Francisco Chronicle every morning. The staff here is amazing...everyone always has a smile on, and there's always at least five people waiting to help you with your bags, opening the door, or getting you transportation. This place even has a gym, so I didn't have to hike to the nearest 24-hour Fitness on Montgomery. Only thing was that the internet was $10 a day, but I found that having to pay for internet is the norm among SF hotels. If I could afford this place, I'd definitely stay here when I'm in town for fun.

title: “Awesome Hotel”
text:
We LOVE this hotel. It is small, very clean and the staff are very nice and helpful. We really enjoy the huge rooms and the silence in the hotel. 
we will definitely recommend this place to all of our friends and relatives. It is close to everything and the place is fabulous!

title: “YOUR REVIEWS HELPED ALOT-Sud at the desk was great too!”
text:
I have booked a room, have not seen it yet, but after 3 hours of looking, calling fussing about how expensive the area is....we called...talked to Sud...he was awesome. He gave us all the information we needed. I am hopeful that the area and photos are accurate. 
If so I will give raving reviews...stay tuned for our opinion on this hotel. So far the reviews and the great customer service have me pretty happy.

title: “Surpassed expectations”
text:
As a female who travels a lot ifor both business and pleasure I have high expectations, particularly for bed quality, in room amenities and for the general ambience and security you feel when travelling solo. From the minute I was helped from my cab on arrival to departure next lunchtime I felt pampered, cared for and cossetted in a way I rarely feel. Service was truly faultless ( I think this is genuinely the first time I can recall saying this) and I especially liked the feeling when initially opening the door to my room that a bedside light had been left on and the BOSE radio was quietly playing Chicago smooth radio. I didn't feel alone which you can often do on opening the door and everything about the room was immaculate, stylish and comfortable. I pay much attention to my bed at home - the right quality and positioning of pillows to the thread count of the bed linen and the weight of the duvet and this bed was bliss - felt like home which takes a lot of doing for any hotel and I slept wonderfully. The bathroom was well designed and I loved the separate bath and the ample generoasly sized towels plus the great illuminated mirrors which are a godsend if you wear contact lenses and are fairly short sighted without. Morning tea was fabulous ( v small point - a couple of small home baked cookies would have been a nice addition here) and breakfast was excellent throughout - a wonderful fresh smoothie as an 'amuse bouche' to granola better than I bake myself, to a generous cafeteria of coffee and granary toast kept warm with butter at room tempertaure, a newspaper to linger over and as a sole guest a table where I could admire the external view.
However it was the sevice which was the best thing about the hotel - everyone I spoke to addressed me by name, and seemed to pre-empt my wishes with quiet, unobtrusive professionalism. That balance is difficult to get right - this hotel did and if and when I return for a longer trip to Chicago this has set the standard for my return, I will come back certainly!

title: “Spacious room, friendly staff”
text: We stayed here before an early flight abroad. Check in was fast and the staff was very pleasant. Our room was really large, clean, and with a huge deck (which would have been nice in the summer), and a big bath with lots of high-end bath products. We took the shuttle to the nearby Hilton (associated) for dinner. (That was an experience that needs its own review, the food and service were so fabulous). The shuttle driver was polite and the van was clean and warm. There was a bit of a walk to the elevator to get to our room, but we didn't need to go outside at all, which was nice considering the weather in Seattle. The room had a nice living room/TV area, so it would have been OK for a family. The bed was comfortable and we got our 3 AM wake-up call as requested. They had a nice Keurig-type coffee maker, so it wasn't the typical crappy hotel in-room coffee. This was nice since there was no coffee in the lobby in the morning. THe shuttle that dropped us at the airport was warm and the driver was pretty cordial, considering the hour. Overall, would highly recommend this hotel. Not sure how it would be in the summer but I think it had a pool, so the kids would be happy. It looked like it had some nice, smaller restaurant options and a coffee bar, but it wasn't open at 4 AM.

title: “GREAT HOTEL”
text: This hotel was very good, clean rooms and friendly service. Plus a substantial free breakfast in the morning! The pool was clean and very warm with nice fluffy towels on the sun beds.

title: “Amazing Service”
text:
The hotel was really nice but the Service is what they should be really proud of. Everyone from the valet to the front desk was amazingly nice. 
This place is truly pet friendly and it was great to be there with the dog. One quick piece of paperwork and after that it was just lots of love for the dog. 
We got a room right off of the elevator on the 6th floor and I was worried about noise being an issue but it wasn't. We heard one of our neighbors once and my wife had mentioned multiple times, how quite the room really was. 
The bed was comfy and they supplied a great selection of pillows so everyone could find one they liked. 
If you wanted to walk to Pikes Place market with the family, this could be a little tough depending on your kids but I will say the walk home will be a lot of up-hill

title: “Great location, room & breakfast buffet”
text: The hotel was conveniently located for walking and views. I had a corner room with floor to ceiling windows - room was small but very nice and I really enjoyed the view. Arrived after a long day of travel so I went to the restaurant and had a very good salad - service was very speedy which I appreciated. The breakfast buffet was very nice - huge selection of food, not at all typical of a hotel buffet. The breakfast buffet had a nice selection of hot and continental items, but really enjoyed the fresh items - berries, fruit, salmon.

title: “Great Service”
text:
The hotel is ideally placed. The rooms were very nice, but sometimes an individual employee can make a very good hotel a great one.
The Concierge, Kat Bride, was without doubt the most efficient and helpful hotel member of staff I have ever met.
I would recommend this hotel as the ideal place to stay on a New York visit

title: “Delightful Experience!!!”
text: My husband and I went on a cross-country tour of the southern states this past week. The final leg of our journey brought us to San Diego, CA which I have to say is one of the best cities in the USA. One of the things that made the trip worthwhile was our accommodations at The Westin San Diego (do not confuse with the one in the Gaslamp Quarter). This hotel by far is one of the best 4 star hotels I have ever stayed in. The hotel associate, Thi Nguyen, went out of her way to make us feel welcomed and pampered. She helped us get a room with a view of the bay which was on a higher floor. The room was spotless, the bed was truly "heavenly," and the showers (there were 2 heads) were reviving and relaxing. Simply put, I did not want to leave. Also, the hotel was in the downtown area so every tourist attraction was close by. We can even see the USS Missouri and the ferry dock to Coronado from our window. If you stay here, you will be able to maximize your vacation as it will save you on travel time.

title: “Like Sleeping in a Train Yard”
text:
Enjoyed a fabulous view of downtown San Diego from my room on the 25th floor. But, was awakened several times each night by the trains blasting their horns as they crawled through downtown. They almost seemed to be doing it on purpose.
The room was clean and comfortable, I won't be staying here again. I suggest staying in Mission Valley or La Jolla and taking the trolley to visit downtown.

title: “5-Star treatment - even for children”
text:
Instead of going to the shore for a week, my family decided on a mid-week trip to Boston. My husband and I usually stay at The Lenox or The Elliott, at the other end of Newbury Street. But this was our daughter's first trip to Boston, and I wanted to be by the Common. What an exceptional choice the Four Seasons turned out to be. We had a lovely, immaculately clean suite, and my daughter slept on the sleeper sofa that the staff came and pulled out and made up each night, then made up to a couch again each morning. While checking in, a wagon of stuffed animals was pulled out and my daughter was told she could choose one. When we got to our room, a special kit of toiletries was brought for her - paraben and petroleum free - and a cute welcome snack kit, as well as a robe and slippers that fit her perfectly. It is my husband's birthday week and a little while after arriving, a lovely "Happy Birthday" dessert tray was brought to our room.
On top of all those lovely touches, everyone addresses you by your last name as though you are a permanent resident, and addressed my daughter by her first name. Evan the concierge was helpful in suggesting child-friendly activities and restaurants and booked us the use of the hotel's Mercedes sedan to drop us off at our destinations.
All staff (Deborah at Concierge, Tony and Ian at the front desk, Po from housekeeping, Abdelilah our bellman, etc, etc.) were unfailingly polite, accommodating, and better yet, cheerful. If anyone on staff was having a bad day, we most certainly never knew.
There were other small touches that separate Four Seasons from other hotels - if your glasses are out, a chamois cloth is put beneath them. Take off your rings? A small jewelry dish is put out for you. A bookmark in your book, a water and glass on a coaster by your bed. 
The location in itself is truly perfect. Across from the Public Garden (the oldest public garden in the US) there are lovely views - especially from the indoor pool on the 8th floor - of the Garden, with it's beautiful pond and Swan Boats gliding across. Boston Common is to the right of the Garden, and Newbury Street is to the left of the Garden. With Charles Street and Beacon Hill at the other end of the Garden, no matter where we went, we had the most beautiful walk back to the hotel and spent our few spare moments just relaxing and enjoying the sunshine before walking across the street back to our rooms. Not to mention, it is the end of August and we had the most fantastic weather - no humidity, low temps, sun all day.
We used every amenity offered to us - pool, steam room, the hotel shop, the restaurant, car service, etc. and not one thing fell short of expectation. My daughter has fallen in love with the city of Boston, and we have fallen in love with the Four Seasons. Can't wait to return.

title: “Loved Jurys ”
text: We went for St. Patrick's Day and loved it - great hotel, great food, Irish Heritage is wonderful and the bar is wonderful! The rooms are nice and modern and elegant. All of the employees were overly helpful and the service was great! Will definitely go again.

title: “Great location, great price, friendly folks”
text:
The place was kitchy and oh-so-cool (because, thankfully the air conditioner was kicking as it was in the 90s temp-wise). The price is what draws you, but the cool hip-factor is what keeps you.
The rooms were clean, shower water pressure was fine, and even had a small fridge. Coffee was available free in the lobby, but Jo's coffeebar is also right next door.
The location is convenient and we got along fine without a car, although the hotel does have some parking if you've got wheels - I think you have to arrange in advance with them for that.
Next time I'm in Austin, I'll go when it's cooler and stay here again.

title: “It's great.will definitely stay in residence inns again!”
text: We travelled with our 2 year old who still needs his nap so we spent a lot of time in the room. We got a suite which is best for our needs. The staff were great, it's very clean, it's nice.breakfast was nice but the light dinner wasn't so great but hey, it's free so no complaints there. Had a really pleasurable experience and holiday.!

title: “It was the Perfect Wedding!”
text:
We found the Maple Manor on the internet when trying to find a central location for our wedding. I particularly wanted a garden ceremony with a reception indoors all in one location. We took one look at this place and knew this was it. The garden is just beautiful with the fountains and greenery. No matter what time of the year, you cannot go wrong. I thought rain would force the ceremony indoors but it stopped a few hours before the ceremony and the staff worked hard to sweep the remaining water out of the garden and set up the chairs. It was perfect. The food from the Old Warsaw was excellent. Monique was great. She made the wedding planning stress free. And her recommendation on the vendor for the cake was the best. Guests are still commenting on the beautiful house, food and cake.
We really could not ask for a better ceremony or reception. If I had to find one thing that needed improvement it was at the end of the reception. The staff hurried my family out while they were trying to gather up the decor, etc. and then locked them out before they had a chance to finish loading their cars.
But I would not have that hold you back from experiencing the beauty and elegance of this hotel.

title: “Very enjoyable”
text: While the room was very small, it was very comfortable. The whole hotel was clean and nicely decorated. I walked from there to the art museum and to the Navy Pier. The staff was helpful and friendly. I ate dinner at the bar area, the food was amazing! The bar tender was very funny and everyone in the bar area was having a good time.

title: “Comfort Inn & Suites”
text: I enjoyed my stay at this hotel. Im visiting Parker College which is in walking distance from the hotel making it very convenient for travel. The guy at the front desk was very nice and professional. The room was reallly nice and clean. Breakfast area was very clean and organized. There were numorous resturants located around the hotel which made dinning easy. I would definitely come back to this hotel again.

title: “Excellent for the price”
text: This is a gem of a hotel right on Union Square. We have been staying there for more than a decade. The staff is very friendly and helpful. On our last visit, we registered a complaint with the front desk regarding our shower head. It was putting out only a dribble of water. The problem was fixed immediately. We look forward to eating breakfast in the hotel's cozy dining room. The staff there is welcoming and very efficient. My husband particularly enjoys the Breakfast Skillet--eggs, fabulous hash brown potatoes, chicken sausage and other vegetables served in a piping hot cast iron skillet. The hotel also offers free coffee and tea in the morning in the lobby. We always request a room in the rear, because of the clamor of Powell Street, but have in the past had to stay on the front a few times. The hotel is well soundproofed, so it wasn't really a problem. The rooms are clean, and usually have two arm chairs, a side table, a desk and a clothes chest, plus a closet. The carpet is clean, but a little tired. The hotel has in the past few years updated its bed linens so now they are crisp white shams and a fluffy duvet. The bathrooms are small--definitely one person at a time, but well appointed with shampoo, conditioner, body lotion, shower caps, hair dryer and good soap. The bathtub/shower is an older version that is very deep, so you need to be careful getting in and out. There is a grab bar on the wall to hold on to. And possibly the most wonderful thing about The Chancellor are the free, home made cookies available in the lobby all day long. I noticed on this trip they now offer apples, too, but they can't compare to the oatmeal raisin cookies.

title: “can't find any better”
text: the muse is an excellent hotel in which to spend any time in nyc. you can look but you won't find better. the staff is friendly and the facility is first class.

title: “Fabulous”
text: We journeyed from Canada and arrived at Cedarbrook in the evening, for a one-night stay prior to an early flight from Sea-Tac. The place was so wonderful we wished we had a longer stay ! A little jewel, in its own pleasant grounds, quiet although 5 mins from airport. Lovely little touches like high-quality toiletries, and lounge with free water, yoghurt, snacks including ice-cream. Dinner in restaurant very good. Staff universally helpful and friendly. Highly recommended.

title: “Great location, good hotel”
text: Austin confuses me. For such a hip, 'weird' city, there is a distinct lack of distinctive properties. This is the third hotel I have tried in Austin, and while nice, it really was nothing special and did nothing to enhance my stay in Austin. This hotel could have been in Pittsburgh for as much Texas style as it offered. Other than the $400/night Driskill, this seems to be the case with most hotels in the area, it's like they aren't aware there is an exciting entertainment district one block over. Anyway. The rooms were nice, big, comfortable and clean. The service in the restaurant was pretty abyssmal for the two meals I ate there, but the food was decent. Wonderful front desk staff, bell staff and door staff - any personality the hotel has comes directly from these great guys. Can't say I would stay here again, for the price, the InterContinental is probably a little more interesting.

title: “Good Location - Good Hotel for NYC low standards”
text:
If you want to be really midtown Manhattan, this hotel is perfect. Just 8 min from Times Sq., 3 min from Fifth and Bryant, very close to some main subway stations.
The hotel itself is quite good for Manhattan generally low standards. It's not the newest hotel in town, it shows its age, but it is well tended. We booked on their website a standard double queen room and got a very good deal because we booked a 4 nights offer. At check-in we asked for a higher floor room and we were given a thirtieth one facing the main street (42nd). The room was ok, it seemed clean and comfy but even if smoking is forbidden, it smelled terribly of cigarettes and so we complained about that. They were really sorry and upset about it and immediately upgraded us to a little suite. Nice customer care. Internet is not free in the rooms but in the lobby they have a free PC workstation dedicated to flights check-in and boarding pass printing. I'd recommend.

title: “Well located modern hotel ideal for tourist”
text:
Very well managed hotel. Clean rooms, Vera good beds. Breakfast had to be taken in a separated building (only 4 doors away).
Close to China Town en Little Italy.
Subway only 3 minute walk away.
Try to have a room @ the frontside of the building. Those at the backside are sometimes a little bit noisy due to ventilation systems at the outside'

title: “excellent hotel and location in nyc with veiws to die for of nyc!!!!”
text:
stayed here feb 2010 with my family. on arrival staff were excellent and pleasant and we got upgraded free of charge to a deluxe room on the 42cnd floor.
the room was brill!
the luggage guy took our bags up so quick he was there before us!
he even stayed for a good five minutes and explained to us where things were and the excellent veiw we had from our window.
one of the best nioghts sleep we have ever had with these so comfy beds, its what you need after being out al day.
overall would definately recommend this hotel to anyone , but do go for a higher room as its really quiet and veiws to die for.

title: “incredible place to stay”
text: My mom and I took a trip to Victoria, BC and were only in Seattle one night on our way back home. We booked the Doubletree only because we got a fantastic price for our one night; otherwise this hotel is out of our price range. I wish we could have stayed here longer. The room, the service, the facility - all were wonderful. We happen to drive up at the exact moment a bride and groom arrived for their honeymoon stay, and that was a cute moment. We had a problem with a light switch and they helped us quickly and efficiently. The beds were comfy and beautifully made up. Food from room service was good and delivered quickly. Every staff member we interacted with was helpful, pleasant, and friendly.

title: “Terrible Experiense”
text:
with the exception of the location the hotel experience was terrible, it is very noisy. Planes are fying just above and the side street leads to the freeway, in adition we had a very noisy group of people in the adjacent room drinking and talking loudly. 
I stayed two nights and could not sleap at all. I had to move to another hotel.
I will NEVER GO BACK HERE.

title: “I highly recommend the Waldorf=Astoria”
text: I have never been so well look after in a hotel before, I highly recomend this hotel. This is one of the most famous hotels in the world, yes you can find cheaper hotels in New York but it is well placed for many attractions as well as the subway and sometimes it really is worth spoiling yourself.

title: “Lots of VIP touches”
text: I recently stayed for 3 nights and found the hotel to be top-notch. From check in to room service, all employees were wonderfully helpful and accommodating. Room was spotless, extremely comfy bed. Room had lots of nice extras, Bose music/tv system, plush robe, slippers, even a toothbrush kit. Hotel even has outdoor rooftop movie nights! Centrally located (no need to rent a car, everything is within walking distance) A great hotel with lots of extra touches, I plan to return.

title: “My relatives always stay here when they come to visit”
text:
I live in San Francisco and I always advise my visiting friends and famiy to stay here and they are always happy they did. As other reviewers have said the location is the best on the wharf. 
The bayview rooms are wonderful but at $300+ are not neccessary, who spends time in the room except to sleep? I think they are the only hotel who have bayview rooms and in my years of making reservations for family are usually all sold out of view rooms unless reserved in advance. Also, because they sell out of those rooms means they have no rooms left to upgrade guests to. I guess you get what you pay for, but the normal rooms are just fine.
The staff has always been easy to deal with, especially the maids. The rooms are clean, but somewhat dated. My mom visited recently and she got to try out one of their Sleep comfort beds with the remotes, she got a kick out of it and said it was comfortable.
Anyway, this hotel is clean comfortable and wonderfully located. It's my choice of hotels on the wharf.

title: “Happy Hour”
text: This hotel is not only well situated, right across the street from the Convention Center, but they have a fully stocked bar that opens in the late afternoon with great deals on drinks during Happy Hour. It is a little tough to find a place around there for a cocktail.

title: “Ladies Weekend Away in New York”
text: 6 girls met in New York for a wonderful few days away over the Memorial Day weekend. Friendly staff, clean rooms, and the air conditioning kicked in just in time for the heat that added to our trip. Great restaurant next door - short walk to Time Square, very safe neighbourhood - located across the street from a cop shop. Very informed staff - extremely friendly. I would definitely recommend this to anyone, but not for a romantic get-away. Family oriented, not too noisy, very comfortable beds. Only problem - pillows not fluffy enough.

title: “Hilton- Sell off this property.”
text:
Being a Hilton Honors Gold member, and needing to find a hotel near the Phoenix Airport, I picked the 24th street location thinking the website pictures on the Hilton web accurately portrayed reality. I knew there was a problem when I saw the property. I don't care if this was the "first Embassy Suites". I characterize this property as a 3 story motel 6. I don't consider any rate higher than $100.00 acceptable. My restless night included hearing my neighbor's laughter and TV all night long through the paperthin walls. (Other Embassy Suites with atriums are built well)
While it may appear I am knocking this property, well, under the Hilton banner/Embassy Suites it doesn't do the Brand justice. As my title states- Hilton- Sell off this property. (or lower the rates and come clean on your websites)

title: “friendly”
text:
Just want to say ,what a very clean and friendly hotel ,the staff are probably the most helpful and friendliest out of all the hotels we have stayed at-particulary with 2 young boisterous children running riot ! . Particular mention must go to the restaurant/bar staff who were very good (and patient).We thoroughly enjoyed our visit to houston and would
definetely recommend this hotel to any visitors to houston.

title: “Great Location; Price”
text: Let me say I was a little nervous about booking due to the reviews I read. However, I'm glad I made the choice to stay here. LOCATION was perfect. After the first night's sleep was interrupted by noise emanating from pipes in the wall, we were upgraded to a brilliant, larger room with a ‘sleep number’ mattress. We were given vouchers for a full American breakfast for which the restaurant charge was $20.00 It was a nice benefit. (The breakfast buffet was excellent. Later we had tea and cake at the restaurant late one night and there was an excellent jazz group playing until 11 PM) You walk out your door and New York is before you. Want to see a play? You can walk to the TKTS booth. (PS The Seagull is a perfect production!) The subway line is conveniently located 15 steps from the lobby! The staff upon leaving kept our bags safe so that we could tour the city one last time and arranged a ride to Newark Airport. I recommend this hotel.

title: “What a GREAT place!”
text:
Me and three of my friends went on a hockey trip to New York City and what a great hotel we had. We got a one bedroom suite and stayed there for 8 nights and it was great! There's a large living room with a flat screen TV and a sofa bed, a sitting area and a fridge, a small microwave and a coffee machine. The bedroom has two queen size beds which was a little hard compared to my own bed but everybody slept good anyways and there's a flat screen TV as well. The hotel is a bit old and the bathroom pluming makes a bit noise if you turn on the water just a little but we didn't find that to be a problem at all. 
We were on the 12th floor so the noise from the 57th St. didn't bother us at all and we had our bedroom on the backside, so it was quiet at night.
We had breakfast on the 3rd. floor every morning and it costs $4/person. They have coffee, tea, different kinds of bread, cornflakes, donuts, orange and apple juice. We thought it was OK for $4. It's not a big room so you may have to wait to get a table but the staff works very fast as soon as a table is free.
There's two elevators and they work fine. We got one in 1-2 minutes when we needed one except in the second last day when one of them broke down but you can't blame the hotel for that.
The cleaning crew was great. They made the beds every day, took out our garbage (mostly empty beer and water bottles), and kept everything very clean.
The hotel is located very nicely on the 57th St. There's subway stations in both ends of the street about 80 meters from the hotel. If you want to go and have a late night drink or a beer there's bars 300-400 meters from the hotel so that's not a problem.
We booked our hotel at Hotels.com and got it for a very good price compared to other hotels located at midtown. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to stay close to the center of town, with big rooms and to a low cost.
I hope to go back to New York someday and this is where I will stay every time!

title: “Reasonable stay at the Marriott Copley Place”
text: Stayed with a colleague in a standard room at this Marriott while attending a conference. The room was clean and roomy enough for two persons. The bed was soft and comfortable, absolutely no problem falling into sleep. There was no complimentary water though there was a small coffee machine that can boil one cup of water each time. Luckily the supermarket was just across the road so we bought a gallon of water. Later we found water coolers on the second floor. There was no complimentary shower cap and no hook in the bathroom to hang our clothes in the bathroom. Free Internet access is only available in the lobby and the second floor. It also took sometime waiting for the lift when the hotel was crowded. We had a decent 5-7 minutes conversation with a hotel guest while waiting for the lift on the 18th floor on a Sunday. Besides all these, the stay at the Marriott Copley Place was overall comfortable.

title: “Excellent service and accomodations”
text:
I recently booked numerous rooms at the Inn of Penn, and used it as a base for a major event. Our rooms were exceptional, and the board meeting I scheduled there, the members said the food, service and the meeting room were excellent. 
I also had a well known celebrity staying at the hotel and she and her entourage were also very pleased with all the accomodations and service. Bessie from the Concierge department was absolutely exceptional, especially dealing with the needs of our international singing star.
Everything went perfect and I would recommend this hotel to anyone!

title: “Not four stars!”
text:
We stayed at The Alex for two
nights over St Patricks wk end. Based on the Priceline deal of $150 that we got, the hotel was ok. However it is not four stars, and I wouldn't pay rack room prices. The room was very basic. Not luxurious or comfortable. The tv was just ok. The phone didn't work at all even after tellIing the desk person. So no room service for us. The airconditioner blew Luke warm air. Fortunately we could crack the window for air. The shower was difficult to use, and the tub was always full of 6'' of water when we showered. Also, the shower doors were difficult to close. All the handles were on the outside? To top things off, we went to
the little bar downstairs to have a martini. After being served our drinks, I was relaxing with my feet on an ottoman, and sitting at a booth near the bar when one of the hotel staff walked past and said "Get your feet off there, people sit there!". I was so embarrassed that I didn't want to finish my drink. Every time I walked in and out of this hotel, the bar was dead. I wonder why? Had I not been insulted, I would have stayed for another drink... I would not recommend this establishment to anyone.

title: “Modern and upscale hotel with excellent service”
text:
I was looking for a hotel with a good location, but didn't want to spend $350+ a night. I booked last minute and found a room at this hotel.
Very contemporary, with just enough lighting in lobby and bar areas, and with a good flow. The building is old, but the rooms are very refreshing with comforting earth tones and very quiet as well. I never heard noise from other rooms while I was there, and hall noise was at a minimum.
The bathrooms are really the only thing that are not as updated, with a small and low to the ground toilet, although little touches like a small dimmable lamp and seperate "his and hers" shower heads are great. The $60 oxygen bottle, an option like a water bottle "to revitalize you" is purely ridiculous, as is the extra small Voss water by the bed.
So, like W, it is modern, hip, and a great location, and can be had at a reasonable price. But W hotels are understaffed with jaded 20 year olds, all the halls are unforgivingly dark, and the Voss water is $10 (but it comes in the glass bottle.) So there the comparison ends. Hotel Andra is what W Hotels should be. Period.
So what was bad? The valet lot must be a city away as it routinely took 10 - 15 minutes to get the car. $35 a night for that honor didn't help. The restaurant (Lola) was very hip and very Greek; I wish there had been a couple more Americanized appetizers for when I just wanted a snack. But thats just my taste. The crowd in the restaurant was mostly walk ins, so they are doing something right.
Overall an excellent, excellent choice in this price range. I felt like I was coming back to a cool apartment, and not a hotel room. And that was a great feeling.

title: “An awesome hotel in the Back Bay”
text: We stayed at the Lenox last year and thought that was really nice - but the Back Bay Hotel was even better! All the staff was really friendly and helpful, the room was immaculate and a bit bigger than expected. It was nice to return to our room at the end of the day and have our ice bucket filled during the turn-down service. It's the little touches that make a huge difference!

title: “Truly a delight”
text:
I am a big fan of Kimpton hotels and have stayed in over a dozen, including The Muse and 70 Park in NYC. Eventi is my new favorite (sorry Muse!). The entry to our queen suite was a long, elegant hall that nicely hid the roomy closets with the requisite animal print robes. The living area was reasonably sized for Manhattan standards, with chic urban comfort featuring sweeping views of Midtown, including the Empire State Building. The bed -- well, I have insomnia, and I was asleep within minutes. But oh, the bathroom, which seemed nearly as large as the bedroom. Glorious marble and Italian tile, featuring a double vanity, separate commode, a soaking tub, and fabulous rainforest shower. The sliding door was a clever and stylish spacesaver, and we had no problem with "sound privacy" that concerned an earlier reviewer. 
We spent more time in the common areas than usual during a hotel stay. The 5th floor features a glorious and expansive veranda that encircles the building and provides both large and private seating areas for socializing or quiet discussion. The exercise facility was more than adequate, with a significant number of elliptical and other cardio machines, and another wonderful view of the city to watch as you work out. The spa was intimate but luxurious. We didn't eat at the restaurant, but peeked in and saw that the ambience matched the rest of the hotel.
The staff was charming, eager to please, and apologetic for even the slightest mishap. The standard Kimpton wine hour was hosted by two charming women who poured generously. :-) Though I didn't take advantage of Kimpton's fabulous pet policy this time, I saw several other guests with happy dogs and, as usual, was never disturbed by barking or other misconduct. 
Negatives? There is currently some street construction that lasts into the evening, so I recommend a higher floor. We were on the 11th floor and were not disturbed by noise. The restaurant and room service are still being completed, so room service offerings are limited. Overnight valet parking was a bit steep even for NYC; my SUV was considered an "oversized vehicle" and I paid $65 for one night. Next time I will take Metro North in if I'm staying only a night. The Chelsea location is not as convenient to Midtown locations as the other Kimpton hotels and there were few restaurants and shops of interest in the immediate area. Upon the recommendation of the desk clerk, we had lunch at the Antique Cafe on 26th just off Ave of the Americas, and their homemade puff pastries (eaten al fresco) were delicious.
Without hesitation, I will gladly stay there again and am already a devotee. Enjoy and safe travels.

title: “Good location pity about the rest...”
text:
So whatever happened to Pride of Super 8 as a guide to their standards? Maybe after visiting this place they reckoned there was no hope. This is a run of the mill motel that doesnt deserve the Super 8 branding. 
It wasnt amazingly cheap so it scores low. The place feels unclean and it lacks a customer focus - but this isnt the place to go if you want customer focus. So if you just want a room and dont care for the rest then go here. the location was really ace.

title: “Great hotel in a great location”
text:
Stayed 2 nights at the Warwick the first week of October with my wife and daughter. We did not get a room with a view (we were overlooking the parking garage from the 6th floor) so I did not get to experience the Space Needle view that others have talked about, but I had paid for my room with airline miles, so I wasn't going to complain. 
Our room was perfectly adequate for our stay. The beds in 2 bed rooms are doubles, so it's a bit tight for couples, but I knew this going in. I don't believe our room had seen recent renovations, but it was still clean and was exactly what we needed. 
The two contacts I had with hotel employees were pleasant. The person that checked us in was very helpful and efficient. 
I also received a call the evening before we checked out to see how our experience had been and to inquire if we needed anything.
The only minor complaint I had (more of a personal preference) is that the thermostat in our room is not one that allows you to select heat or cool. You simply set a temperature and it adjusts the room to that temp (with heat or A/C). In October it's not really necessary to use the A/C, but the room did get stuffy when closed up even though the thermostat showed a temperature of 66 degrees. 66 is as low as the thermostat goes, so it was not possible to run the A/C to clear the room air. Opening the outside door did the trick, although that can be noisy. Overall, not a big deal, I am just used to manual control of the temperature in a hotel room.
I did not use the restaurant or other facilities besides taking my daughter to the pool. It's in the basement so it's rather industrial, but is in perfect working order and clean. The water was comfortable and my daughter enjoyed herself. 
Overall it was a great experience. I would love to stay on a higher floor in a north facing room, but maybe next time.

title: “Great Hotel, but small rooms for 2 singles”
text: Love the location but be prepared for the small size rooms. Great Front Desk staff. The room was pleasant and the decor very nice. The bathroom products (shampoo, lotions etc) are super. Large soft bath towels. It's just a little cramped for 2 singles, but other than the size of our room, we really enjoyed our stay there. We would stay there again.

title: “3.5 - 4 star”
text:
Booked the Crown Plaza late through Priceline and was decently happy with the results.
Parking situation was a little unexpected. You pull into their garage yourself, which is shared with monthly parking users. Must take an elevator to the lobby. 
Once their, check in was simple. They charge parking to your room credit card and activate your room card to let you out. Going up to the room requires using your room card in the elevator to access the upper floors. 
Rooms are somewhat how you'd expect a 3.5-4 star hotel to be. Flat screen tvs. desk, comfortable bed. 
Great location on the southern part of the 16th street mall (actually 1.5 blocks off the mall)

title: “Excellent boutique hotel!”
text:
We booked 4 nights at the Pearl through Expedia. Though we were a bit unsure about all the ravishing reviews, we now concur that they are all very well deserved! Location, cleanliness, comfort, quietness in spite of the busy location, extremely helpful staff, starting from the solicitous doormen, to the desk personnel, to the concierge, always eager to help with highly useful tips. 
We had wanted to see "The Book of Mormon" right across the street, but the show was booked till September.... So, we contented ourselves to hang around after the show to see the performers emerge from the service door to be surrounded by admirers and autograph seekers. On Sunday we saw them on the big screen in Times Square in connection with the Tony Awards. For our part we are giving a Tony Award also to the Pearl Hotel! We have already recommended it to three other couples planning to visit NYC. It's fun to share a good find (when you get to find one, a rarer and rarer occasion nowadays...)

title: “Really pleasant stay”
text: I stayed for one night after flying from the UK to San Diego. Great service and pleasant clean rooms. I looking for a room later on next week and I'm hoping to return here.

title: “Did not get what I paid for”
text:
I was really excited when I booked my room at a seemingly good discount for New Years Eve. When My friend and I arrived we were totally psyched to see our room because the lobby was so gorgeous. Check in went smoothly and we were allowed to check in a few hours early. When we walked to the elevators there were security guys asking to see everyones key card, I'm still not exactly sure what the deal was( they were gone when we got back from the club we went to at about 2 am.). They elevators were a bit small but whatever. When we got out on our floor (18) it was absolutely freezing. We found our room and finally got in after having some difficulty with our key cards. We were so disappointed when we saw how small the room was . We actually thought there was something in bouth the beds at first because the covers were so lumpy. We dropped our stuff and headed out for some pre-party shopping without really checking things out. When we got back a bit later we started exploring. We found the mini bar inside the dresser/tv stand. It was disgusting. I would never have eaten anything that had been in that thing. Then we discovered that once you opened the doors on the dresser, they wouldn't stay shut unless slammed. My friend decided she wanted to take a nice long bath and went into the bathroom. And immediately walked back out. When I went to see what the problem was I saw a filthy tub that had some thing yellow and crusty on the edge. There was hair all over one of the towels and so much mildew gathered in the corners I refused to walk in there barefoot. When it was my turn to shower, I looked up and saw a pube hanging out next to the one and only light in the bathroom( it provided very little actual light. The towels were like sand paper too.
The next morning we waited 15 minutes to get an elevator going down that wasn't over crowded. We finally had to take one that was going up (as did several other people). It then took us 15 minutes to get to the lobby. I could feel the floor flexing everytime someone shifted their wait.
There were a few other things that bothered me as well but this review (complaint?) is already too long.
The beds were really comfy though.

title: “Charming hotel, excellent service”
text:
We were very pleased with the Omni La Mansion del Rio. I really liked the Spanish colonial feel to the property. Service at the front desk, the valet staff, & and at the concierge desk was very friendly, professional, & helpful. The rooms were very nice & I loved the dark wood French doors that opened to the balcony. Our room did not face the Riverwalk but I think that worked out better to avoid the noise level from patrons along the Riverwalk esp on a Friday or Saturday night when the Riverwalk is packed with people. The building we were in was very quiet. 
It's in a great location on the Riverwalk. Close to many restaurants. Paseo's is an excellent Italian restaurant. There are many tex Mex restaurants in walking distance as well as a CVS & other shop to buy water or snacks (mini bar in room is ridiculously overpriced). If you need to purchase tickets for the Riverwalk boat ride, it's a short walk over the bridge to the Aztec theater to buy tickets & the boat stop is right outside the theater. 
The valet parking is steep at $32 per night. However it did prove to be very convenient esp if you will be in & out throughout the day. There is a garage across the street for $8 a day but it does not have in & out privileges so if you have to leave periodically throughout the day, you will be charged. If you'll be parked your entire stay, then the garage across the street is more price advantageous.

title: “If you want the total Pike Market experience”
text: WOW, What a great location and view for a vacation to Seattle, The service is top notch and the location to everything Seattle is great. The market is in your backyard, easy walk to downtown, the pier or Seattle center. I wanted one more day to just sit on the rooftop deck and take in the views of the bay, the market and the mountains.

title: “Comfortable room for a relaxing weekend”
text: For my first extended trip to a big city (I'm from a small Midwestern town), the Crowne Plaza was excellent. I chose to stay here because I wanted to stay somewhere different than the hotels around my hometown. I was not disappointed. From the moment I stepped out of the taxi, the experience was great. The staff was great and knowledgeable. The hotel is very warm and inviting. The lobby is huge and beautifully decorated. The room (King suite 1531), was beyond what I had imagined. It had a seperate living room, with a TV, desk, chair, and sofa (which pulled out to a bed). Beyond that was the bathroom and bedroom. For seclusion, if there was anyone staying on the sofa bed, you could have privacy in the bedroom by closing the door. The bedroom also had a TV, and the most comfortable bed I have ever laid in. The balcony had a stunning view of the Greek Town (Greek Walgreen's right across the street), and to the left, the Sears Tower. The bathroom was equally stunning. I loved the rainfall shower head; it was very relaxing. The lighting in the entire room was able to be dimmed, which was great. I can't wait to go back.

title: “Highly recommend for families with young children”
text: We have been to San Diego/Sea World every summer for the past 5 years. I had been happy with our choice of the past 2 years, a property about 20 minutes from SeaWorld. This yeard, I didn't want to drive the extra distance daily to and from Sea World. After lots of review on this site, I decided on the Residence Inn. This was a great choice for our family, with a teenager and two 6 year olds. The room was comfortable, with my little ones sharing the kids room. Instead of bunkbeds, the hotel gave me the option of 2 twins which worked out well. The breakfast bar has plenty of good food and will save lots of money on breakfast. The lobby has cookies, fruit and punch/lemonade available all day. There is a small game room for the kids and larger game room with 2 pool tables, foosball, air hockey and pinball. This gave my teenager something to do. There is a large laundry room with several washers and dryers available. The hotel provides laundry soap and dryer sheets. Thank you!The stafff was very friendly and helpful. We took full advantage of the kitchen, but there was no stove. Grocery store was only 1.5 miles away. We also used the business center and wireless internet in the lobby. Parking and hotel seemed very secure, as you need your room key to enter the parking lot and get in/out of the hotel through the side doors. Oh, and the best part...only a 5 minute drive to Sea World!
