title: “Pricey -- and in need of renovation”
text:
I'm a loyal Hyatt Diamond member, and I had high expectations as set by prior Hyatt experiences elsewhere. I was disappointed by this hotel. While it is "fine," the room was in desparate need of renovation for the price point we paid (stained carpet; stained couch; ceiling above sink in bathroom with drywall exposed). 
On the positive side, it is a great location, and XIX is a very nice place for breakfast. 
They claimed that renovations are starting this month -- but since the General Manager has stated for three months on TripAdvisor that renovations are "starting now" I'm a bit skeptical.
Net-net, a fine place for $100-150 per night . If you are paying over $250 (as I was), you are better off at the Four Seasons or the Ritz.

title: “LOVE IT!”
text:
Just great as usual! We've just been there for the second time and we just love this place. Nice furniture, amazing view on the Empire State building, excellent situation in Manhattan, very nice and helpful people at the front desk, lively Hall. I you wanna "feel" NY stay there!
I would however not recommend this place for "elderly" people who might neither feel so "comfy" nor at ease there.

title: “a "10" in our books”
text:
Decided on a last minute get-away to D.C. Reviews were positive so I went to their website and got a great "no frills" package. For $119/night we got a king jr. suite, not large but perfect for us. It also had a full kitchenette area w/microwave, stove, and full refrigerator. The marble bathroom was roomy and nice w/ an oversized pedastal sink.
Parking was $13.50/ and we arrived in the morning on Saturday and left Sunday at 3:30. They allowed us to keep our car in their garage even after check-out w/no additional fees. We also received an excellent continental breakfast w/our room which included, a croissant, another baked goody, yogurt, fresh fruit, and granola. The restaurant lounge area was lofty and attractive. 
The hotel is just south of Dupont Circle, but it was an easy walk to some local restaurants. The staff was wonderful, accommodating, and friendly. The room was impeccably clean, nicely appointed, and comfortable. For that price, you just can't get any better.

title: “Good Value for Money”
text: I was a little worried after reading the reviews, but went with it as I am budget-minded. True, the hallway smelled funky, but I noticed the same smell emanating from other older hotels as I walked by. (Hotel Beresford was built in 1911). The hall windows were opened & closed each morning by the staff to help. No air con, but there was an unusual cold snap & A/C wasn't needed. The heat was supplied by what looked to be the original steam radiators-quite an interesting sight for this Floridian. The room was a bit small. Bathroom was shower (no tub). The window looked out at the building next door, but I don't book a room based on view. One computer with free access for all-other guests were quite reasonable and shared so it was not a problem checking e mail a couple of times. And the White Horse Tavern has a meat loaf that we talked about for 2 days-it's different but delicious! The front desk & all other staff were pleasant and accommodating. Had to transfer to another (more expensive) hotel for business and within 24 hours was wishing for the unpretentious atmosphere of this place. I would stay here again.

title: “Hip and cool”
text: The Clarendon Hotel is the best. Funky, cool, hip, edgy & fun. Great food, better beer, cool staff.

title: “Pretty old hotel in a great location”
text: I stayed here for two nights on a business trip. San Fran hotels can be quite expensive for what you get but this was a surprise. I've stayed at Hotel Union Square and Powell Hotel before and these were cheaper and the rooms were nicer. There wasn't anything hugely wrong apart from it's an old hotel and the room was very ordinary, outdated and uninspiring. Might be a bit of an unfair comparison but I'd just spent a week at Loews in Philly so probably was expecting more for the price, considering it was a large saving off normal rates based on the special price on Expedia. And I'd enjoyed Hotel Union Square before so was figuring this would be on par. Well, luckily it was only for sleeping but the location is certainly brilliant. Close to much of where it's happening so that's what you're paying for I guess.

title: “Bed Bugs!!!!!”
text: I stayed one night in this hotel and it was the worst hotel experience I have ever had. I noticed that the lobby and corridors were not very clean and the carpet in the room was really nasty, but otherwise the room looked clean enough. The next morning I woke up to itching ankles and discovered that my feet, legs and waist were covered in bites. OMG! I have heard of it, but never seen it before. I told the housekeeping Mgr. and she did not seem very alarmed. She said she would make a report. Also, we left something in the room and came right back to get it. The housekeeper was in the room when we got there and our personal item was missing. She denied ever seeing it. Hmmm! very strange. I know exactly where it was laying on the desk and she had already cleaned off the desk. Very Bad experience.

title: “Great Location, Very Affordable”
text:
My sister and I spent two days in Seattle and stayed at the Executive Pacific Plaza Hotel. We chose this hotel because it was affordable and in a prime location. For travelers who are only going to be using thier hotel room to sleep and shower, this is a great choice. It is not a luxury hotel, but a practical choice for active tavelers. 
Here's what we thought of the hotel:
PROS:
-Location, location, location. The hotel is across the street from the stunning Seattle Library, and within walking distance of Pike Place Market, Pioneer Square, and the waterfront.
-Affordable. Of all the downtown hotels we looked at this was the least expensive.
-Friendly staff. The front desk attendants helped us make the most of our stay by recommending restaurants and calling taxis. Also, they offer complimentary maps, and will loan you an umbrella to use for the day.
-Newly renovated. The hotel is certainly old, but they have made an effort to update the look with new modern furnishings. The down comforters on the bed were wonderful!
-Clean. Although there was a faint smell of old smoke in the hall, our room and bath was neat and clean. I saw no signs of mold or dirt.
CONS:
-It's Small. The lobby, the rooms, the bathrooms--they're all small. My sister and I were able walk around comfortably, but there's certainly no extra space. I think it would feel cramped if there were more than two guests in a room.
-It's a Buget Hotel. Travelers who are used to the luxury of larger resort hotels will be dissapointed. However, as I've said before, if you're only using the hotel room to sleep and shower, it's more than adequate.
-It's Old. While they have made an effort to revamp the hotel, there's no hiding the fact that the building itself is old. There was a faint smell of old smoke in the halls and the doors have obviously been painted many times. Carpet, furniture, and bathroom fixtures, however, are new.
-Street noise. While street noise will be a problem in any downtown hotel, this hotel doesn't have the thicker windows that many of the newer hotels are installing. The noise wasn't enough to keep us from sleeping.
Overall, a great pick if you're looking for a clean, affordable place to crash before hitting the town again. If you're looking for something luxurious or romantic, this probably isn't the place for you.
Hope this helps! Enjoy Seattle!

title: “Absolutely Wonderful”
text: This hotel was awesome. My wife and I spent the first night of our honeymoon there and loved it. The staff was friendly and very helpful. Since the hotel is located in terminal D of DFW the bellman took our baggage to check in for us and saved us the trouble. From Terminal D you can check in and then board the sky link to your terminal. I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

title: “Can't rave enough about this place!”
text:
If you go to Hollywood, you have to stay here! We were travelling with our 2 kids 5 and 8. The rooms are huge, though not brand new or anything flash, this place was our kids and our favourite place to stay during our entire 6 week trip to the states!
We were all made to feel so special by the staff! The kids loved them and my daughter ever drew a picture to give to the lovely lady on reception when we left. They loved the free drinks and snacks at reception and we loved the 'local' knowledge from the staff on everything from transport to family friendly restaurants etc. Amazing, amazing, this is what I call customer service....you love the vibe so much, the breakfast, that you overlook the flaws in the accommodation rooms (not that we could pick anything!)
They have an onsite laundry which is handy and walk over to Hollywood Boulevard. We would definately come back and stay here again. Thank you everyone there it was the perfect end to the time in your country!

title: “Wonderful boutique hotel in a great area”
text: My wife and I spent February 9th - 12th at the Nolitan Hotel. I had lived in NYC in the late 80's and didn't return to visit again until 1999. I have never been one for large chain hotels and have searched most of NYC for these little hidden gems. Some of the reviews where not good but I took a chance and booked a corner king room. When we arrived there was discounted parking across the street. Upon checking in we where we'll greeted by a young man "Ben" from Liverpool UK. He was wonderful. Telling us about the hotel and the surrounding neighborhood. Upon entering our room I was pleasantly surprised to find it very Euro chic. Bathroom was amazing even though it was completely open to the room. Amenities where also great. We encountered one problem. On the 2nd night the drain on the tub broke. The next morning we stopped at the front desk and told them about it. It was fixed by the time we returned that afternoon. Some of the other reviews have said the staff where not very kind or attentive. I'm going to beg to differ. They were all wonderful! If you want the Ritz or 4 Seasons treatment then damn well stay there. I'll be enjoying myself at the Nolitan and surrounding neighborhood.

title: “Perfect”
text: Our family of 3 stayed at the Omni on a Friday and Saturday night. What a great week end deal! We paid 159.00 a night with free valet parking and breakfast for two each morning (we didn't need 3 vouchers because I'm not into breakfast). The guys selected breakfast items from a wonderful buffet. The rooms were quiet and comfortable. I loved the floral scent every time I entered the lobby. The hotel is in walking distance to the Disney Concert Hall, Our Lady of the Angels Cathedral and The Dorothy Chandler Pavilion. The Omni deserves the high Trip Advisor ranking it receives. We highly recommend it for a week end visit.

title: “Excellent stay”
text: We as a family have stayed at the Beacon twice now and both occasions our stay has been very good. The hotel is located on Broadway but far enough away from the hustle and bustle. The 1 bedroom suite we had was large enough for our family of two teenage sons.The view from our room on the 24th floor was magnificent. There is no restaurant or swimming pool but being New York we didn't need these facilities. The hotel reception staff are very friendly and well informative.

title: “top notch!!!!”
text: Not a better hotel in San Antonio! while different and contemporary, the service is simply friendly and outstanding. Can't say enough about their restaurant--their tenderloin is no less than perfect.

title: “Remember the Alamo”
text: I spent 6 nights at the hotel and when I arrived, my room was ready. the hotel was accessible by public transit. The room was clean and the first few nights the bed was turned down. The bathroom was small and clean. Wireless internet is provided for a fee. My room was on the 4th floor and I had a nice view. the hotel is opposite a highway, but the noise was not distracting. Towels were neatly placed. the first couple of days, the room was cleaned. I returned back to room on the fourth night and found a plastic bag of towels on my door. It seems as though my room had not been cleaned for the day. This happened again. I was so busy going to conference workshops, that I did not report to the management of the hotel. the bed had not been made up, nor the trash dumped. Maybe they thought I did not need these services. that was the only negative. The hotel had a continental breakfast each morning. this was a variety of muffins, fruit, coffee, tea, hot chocolate and orange juice. the hotel is within a long walking distance of the Alamo and the downtown, but you can catch a convenient trolley that comes by every 15 minutes. Overall I would stay at this hotel again. the staff was helpful and in spite of the one negative with the housekeeping, I would recommend this hotel as a bargain for the money.

title: “Excellent”
text:
Everybody was good to us , keep up the good work.
The hotel staff was very nice, the housekeeper was nice and friendly. Tony was very helpful , he told us how to get to the football game. The room was very nice and I liked it very much. The lady that put out the food and drinks was very nice and friendly too.

title: “Very Noisy, worn around edges”
text:
I stayed here in October 2006 before catching a morning flight out of Indianapolis. I booked this hotel because of the good reviews here on trip advisor. I have to say that I think that this time the reviews here steered me the wrong way.
The front desk was very helpful, but I felt that many other hotels near the airport provide the same services (free parking, airport shuttle, high-speed internet, and breakfast) without the major negative of being very noisy. The reason to spend the night near the airport before a morning flight is to get a good night's sleep and to be closer to the airport. I didn't sleep at all because our room faced the interstate and we heard noise all night long. Also, the rooms weren't exactly dirty, but they didn't exactly feel clean either. After our trip, when we called for the shuttle to pick us up at the airport, we waited about 15-20 minutes (and the first time the driver drove right past us so we had to call back) which seems long given that the hotel was only 5 minutes from the airport.
I would say this was an "okay" place to stay, but other airport hotels probably provide the same services in a newer, cleaner facility, so I will stay someplace else next time I have an early flight. If you stay here, request a room on the parking lot side of the building.

title: “Great place to stay at the right price”
text: .I would definitely stay here again. Inn is in the right place and at the right cost. Since there is no check in or check out it makes staying there easy. Marked 4 for service, but really there are no services. I never saw on staff person but that is what the inn is all about

title: “Everything you want out of a hotel room in NYC.”
text: I have stayed in NY on business a number of times and I have to say that this was my most enjoyable stay in a hotel there. No small dark cramped rooms that look out on a brick wall or where the street noise keeps you up all night. This modern hotel is convientely located in the heart of Times Sq, with great service, a decent bar / lounge area with friendly staff. The rooms are large, bright, airy, modern and clean. The bed was massive and very comfortable and the view overlooking the Hudson was a delight. I am glad I read the previous reviews on tripadvisor as it swayed my choice to stay here and now I know that on my next visit I don't need to look any further than the Crowne Plaza at Times Square.

title: “Quaint, convenient and overall a nice little gem of a hotel!”
text:
The location was perfect, the staff outstanding and the modern decor refreshing. Yes this space is shared with residents, but that's half the fun. Seeing folks come and go walking their dogs, or stopping to chat with the doorman - it adds to the charm of this mod Chicago boutique hotel. It was a perfect location for us, within blocks of shops, restaurants and major landmarks along Michigan Ave. 
The rooms were spacious, the bathrooms not so much - but the suite we had was a great space. We stepped down from the entry into the living room, and the bedroom was set off to the left. Huge windows offered downtown views and sounds - which our 6 year old found facinating. 
We will be back for sure during warmer weather when we can explore the city more.

title: “Wow, can service make a difference”
text:
We stayed here for the better part of a week and left feeling really just shocked at the indifferent service. Not just indifferent. It was as if even being in the hotel was a bother for those who worked there. The doormen did not hold the door open, say hello, or offer to flag down cabs (except in one circumstance - there is actually one doorman who was very nice). When asked to hold our bags for the afternoon that we checked out, the elderly bag check man let out a very audible sigh. And we're tippers! When checking out, the receptionist told us we were done, but never offered a receipt until we said we wanted to check it. And then didn't ask us how our stay was or to have a good day or any of the normal courtesy comments one might expect... We asked the concierge how best to get to the airport and he all but told us to figure it out - he offered no suggestions whatsoever. 
We were not given toiletries for 4 days in a row. I finally called and after waiting an hour, we had to leave for dinner. I asked at the front desk if they could have it handled and, upon our return, we found 4 rolls of toilet paper on our bench --- not toiletries. The cleaning service came in our room twice notwithstanding our do not disturb signs. And did not clean our room once even though we had the "freshen up" sign up. It was odd.
We were upgraded to a king deluxe or something like that - had a living room off of it - which was nice to have space in NYC, but the bathroom was TINY! There was not a functional plug in the bathroom. Otherwise, the room was comfortable, including the bed. Actually, the bed was a bonus. It was too close to the ground, however, so the construction noise was a bit bothersome (though we had no expectation of "quiet" in NYC, so we got over that).
The location was OK for getting to other areas of NYC - walkable in large part - but not a neighborhood feel.
All in all, we felt that our room for under $200/nt was probably worth the value, but we would NEVER return because of the most curiously bad service. There is absolutely no way this was a 4star. Just no possible way.

title: “A Grand Hotel in a Surprisingly Good Location”
text: When we first arrived here we were slightly concerned at how far from the centre of DC we were, however on walking to the Metro (2mins) it only took a few stops to find ourselves in the centre. The hotel and room were very spacious and comfortable with a great dining room. The additional use of the pool was also nice, considering the heat in DC in August.

title: “Disappointing experience, smoky smell in my room.”
text: My daughter and I checked into a beautiful suite only to find it smelled strongly of smoke. A black air purifying machine sat on the floor, inoperative. We were moved to a smaller room only to have 2 strange men enter our new room with a key. Wifi kept going out and we had to keep logging in. Restaurant food was good, hotel experience disappointing.

title: “Surprised by negative reviews”
text: I came to Austin with my daughter who was attending a conference, so I spent a lot of time at the hotel. The negative reviews this hotel is getting must be coming from people who are used to a Hilton or better. One very positive comment I have is the pool area. I spent four mornings and one entire day at the pool. It was by far one of the nicest chain hotel pools I have ever seen. It was very large, enough to swim laps in, it had a 2 foot deep baby section and also a hot tub, although the water was not heated at the time we were there, but when the temperature outside is 105 who wants hot water in the hot tube. The pool water was very pleasant and the landscaping all around the pool was very nice. It even has a small fountain with a stone waterfall. There were plenty of lounge chairs, and tables with umbrellas. Our room was a king and it was plenty big for us with a work desk and a small sofa, microwave and refrigerator.It overlooked I-35 but the noise from that didn't bother either of us at night. The air conditioner worked great, but was a bit musty smelling when it kicked on as if they hadn't changed filters for a while. We had a comfortable bed which did have a top sheet! Not sure why the lady who said her bed didn't have one just didn't ask for one. Very easy to get to Congress and downtown from here. I would drop my daughter off at UT every morning and it only took about 10 minutes to get her there. Sorry this place has so many bad reviews I really don't know why. Our room was very clean and so was the lobby area.

title: “This hotel is a jewel!”
text: Don't let the first impression of the surrounding neighborhood dissuade you - you'll be fine! We were so happy w/this hotel. It's just a mile from Union Station. We 3 women walked it 2 or 3 times. We would not do it after dark however. The free shuttle to Union Station was great! The rooms were nice & very quiet. Sheets, pillows, towels were of a very high quality. Coffee pot & coffee in room. Coffee was a gourmet brand. We booked on line & continental b'fast was free. Staff was very helpful & friendly. Shampoo, soaps, lotion in bathrm. were very nice quality. Everything in our room seemed to be recently upgraded & very pretty. There were 2 computers in lobby to use for free. Campus was quiet & pretty.

title: “Terrible - with Roaches and awful customer service - STAY AWAY!”
text:
Upon opening our room door the stench hit us, we walked in, debating whether we wanted to stay & promptly spotted 1, 2, ... 3 roaches. Running out of the room to the front desk, they refused to refund our money (fortunately Citibank saved us from the charge).
I would NEVER recommend that ANYONE stay here. There are too many decent hotels within this price range and within this area - no one should pay to spend even an hour in such squalor. STAY AWAY FROM THIS PLACE.

title: “Outstanding Hotel, Great Value for Money, Very Clean”
text:
I read some negative reviews about this hotel and was actually considering cancelling my hoiday. Just before going, I discovered I was pregnant so wasn't sure if I should really stay in a "Budget " Hotel, I was worried about cleanliness and hygiene. However, I was pleasantly surprised when we arrived. We had a double room, renovated, en-suite. 
The bed was nice and firm, just how I like it and the linens were impeccably clean. The room was given a clean every day and unlike a lot of New York , this was a bedbug-free zone. 
The room was quite spacious, with a wardrobe, writing desk and bedside table. There was both heating and air-conditioning. We used both as it was a week of very changeable weather when we stayed. We also had cable TV and a radio/alarm clock. 
The hotel offers free Wi-Fi in all rooms, an extremely useful service if you have an iphone or Ipod. If you don't have these, there are two computers in the communal room for internet access. 
The staff were very pleasant and accommodating. We had a problem with the toilet one morning and it was sorted out within five minutes. 
The location was good, in a relatively quiet area, but with some nice European-style cafes and even a couple of American diners nearby. 
The Subway was a 2 minute walk and brings you to the heart of downtown within 10 minutes. 
Just one thing to note, if you don't book an en-suite, you will have a shared bathroom (I think it was one per corridor). I had thought this would be like in a hostel with a few different stalls but actually it was just enough for one person. Although, I never saw a queue outside.
What I liked best about this hotel: Great value for money, very clean
What I liked least about this hotel: Having to leave! 
I would definitely stay here again and would strongly recommend it.

title: “Good Budget Hotel”
text: A nice budget hotel which made a welcome stop after an 11 hour flight. The only thing which put me off was finding a cockroach in the bathroom very soon after we arrived. Otherwise, the staff were extremely friendly & helpful. Breakfast was basic but adequate.

title: “The ultimate in the "San Francisco Story"”
text: Hotel Rex has been my personal choice and recommendation over the years (8) for business, and pleasure visits to the city. The quaint accommodations, personal attention to detail by staff, perfect location for activities, and fabulous dining always leaves me feeling like I wouldn't choose any other location. It is "my San Francisco home".

title: “Good Hotel, Value??, Parking??”
text: I usually stay at the Hilton by Grant Park. This hotel is more expensive, north of the river, a few blocks off of Michigan Avenue. Plenty of eating options in the area. I usually pay $40 less to stay at the Hilton, and the parking is $40 at either place. Rooms are clean and quiet. Free breakfeast is a plus.

title: “no problem parc 55”
text:
From the time you leave San Francisco Airport, It was a breeze getting there . Taking the Bart made it to simple, coming out of the station walking maybe 20 feet stood the Parc 55. Expect
to see the homeless as you enter or leave the station. Parc 55 
is accessible to all modes of transportation, union sq, mall, etc
We picked up a 3 day passport , 18 $, to be used on , muni, cable cars , trolly cars for unlimited rides..good bargin.
We stayed there 3 nights , no problems what so ever, staff was friendly, instead of the concerierge , ask the BellMen for directions, info, etc.. they were very accommodating .
The so call sports bar on premises , wasn't lively, low key,
unless super bowl or world series was being played you may get sound on the tv's...they had 6 flat screens in a small place .
 go somewhere else if you're looking for a sports bar.
Other wise check out the Pac 55 .

title: “great location, beautiful foyer”
text: stayed for 1 night in august. very convenient to old part of town. good value for money and clean room. negatives- was offered an upgrade for room at a price and whilst room was on a higher floor, the view was not worth the money, older style rooms and sleep number bed, not very comfortable. However if in town for short time, would recommend.

title: “Amazing Hotel Close to Wrigley and Everything!!”
text:
I came in from Boston with my brother for the Red Sox/Cubs series at Wrigley. The City Suites hotel is walking distance to the park, a million restaurants nearby, and is right at the Red Line/Brown Line L stop, so you can go anywhere in Chicago extremely easily! 
The L is literally outside, but I never heard it once in my room, which I thought was crazy. 
Also, the breakfast is a MAJOR perk here! The guy who runs the breakfast is on top of everything and you have some eggs, oatmeal, cereal...in other words, way beyond the bunk continental breakfast that lowballs you at many other hotel chains! (thanks for that crossant and coffee..NOT!)
Rooms are very clean and maid service is second to none....there is also random bar across the street that I made friends at every night with a cool bartender to boot. 
This will be my 'go to' hotel when travel back to Chicago...

title: “Customer service needs improvement”
text: The location was great and I quite liked the room, however I was overcharged about $75 on top of hotel price+taxes for my stay (still don't know why). The staff weren't the best I've come across and I felt like I was talking to a brick wall when I asked them questions regarding their charges. It is a fairly no-fuss hotel (express check-in and go) which I liked but even so their customer service was lacking. I'll definitely remember this hotel, but not in a good way.

title: “4 Star Grounds, 1-3 Star Service”
text:
Arriving at the Arizona Biltmore gives you a sense of what a "5-star" resort must have been like for movie stars and millionaires during the early part of the last century.
You can tell that the place definitely had its moments of elite history, and while it may have truly been one of the most glamourous hotels back then, it shows its age in both good and bad ways.
It's as if, as another reviewer noted, that management can't decide if it wants to embrace its past or evolve into some vision of a Las Vegas resort future. The lobby area is truly lovely, cozy and inviting, if a little schizo. There's clearly Asian influences, southwestern influences and, oddly enough, a sense of pacific northwest lodges here. That's the interior... the outside is a different story. The "iconic element" of this resort are the building tiles that cover everything (and I mean everything) all rendered in glorious greenish concrete. 
The property loves to drop Frank Lloyd Wright's name, and I can see the influence. That is, if FLW designed a hospital. It's very institutional and the buildings just look a bit like a very well maintained "sanitarium" from the 1920's.
Luckily, the interior of my room was a different story. Very, very spacious and well-appointed. A few small gripes:
- The desk chairs are not well padded. Sitting on them for more than 10 minutes will cause you some pain.
- Their attempt at copying the "dream beds" of other hotels is merely a very large mattress topper placed on a cheap mattress and covered with very nice linens, which another reviewer noticed as well
- The in-room safe uses a key. Get with it... time for an update.
As for the grounds, if you can get past the concrete you'll notice how well maintained they are. Truly beautiful. I saw no notice of the mosquitos, cloudy pools and trash that other reviews make notice of. Simply put, they were immaculate.
The service varied widely. Check-in and check out were efficient and everything they should be. However, once I got to my room a staff member was in the room making what appeared to be personal phone calls. She politely excused herself when I seemed to startle her upon pushing open the door.
The bakery/cafe staff was indifferent and seemed "bothered" by having to serve patrons. The laundry service caused me some grief. I called very early and informed them I had some laundry to send out for same day return (promised back by 6pm). Come 6pm, no laundry. At 6:30, a call to housekeeping/laundry was met with a typical "we'll check on it" response. At 7:15 still no laundry, and a 2nd call got the the same "we'll check on it" and call you back response. At 8pm, a call to the manager on duty had my laundry to me within 10 minutes, delivered by a staff member who was clearly annoyed that I wasn't about to offer up a tip after waiting 2 hours for overdue laundry.
Housekeeping also came very late-- in my case after 4pm.
Dinner at Wright's was amazing. Our server, Wesley, gave nothing short of perfect service and made sure we had everything we needed without asking for it. His, and the somalier's, recommendations made for a truly esquisite experience. Highly recommended.
One more note for the staff in charge of assigning meeting space: you really should have better sense than to book a rousing political rally next to a roomful of folks trying to concentrate on research presentations. Oil and water.

title: “Great Stay!--Don't Beleive the Negative Reviews!”
text: Don't believe any of the negative reviews on here for the Hotel! We had a great visit starting in the lobby, the hotel is clean, the staff was friendly and it is priced right! The Lobby has 2 computers for use which came in handy when printing out airline tickets. The Gift shop was stocked with a lot of Elvis Stuff and the lady was really friendly! We had dinner at the Jungle Room Lounge in the Hotel which was good! They show Elvis Movies every night in the Jungle Room Lounge. They also have 3 channels on the TV's in the room that have Elvis 24/7. We ate the Free breakfast each morning, it was very filling. If you go to Marlowes Restaurant ask the front desk for the 10% off coupon. If you go you will not regreat it! I can't wait to go again!!!!

title: “Wonderful Hotel, Wonderful Staff, Wonderful Breakfast!!”
text:
Chose this hotel on the suggestions of many NYC travelers. Showed up and was welcomed by a friendly staff that took care of the weary travelers. Our room service was good. Breakfast the next morning was even better. Lots of fresh fruit, fresh pastries and made to order breakfast! My husband is a Diamond member of Hilton, so our breakfast was gratis, but it would be well worth the price to fuel up for a full day of walking and sightseeing.
The room was clean and comfortable. The air conditioning worked very well! Only problem we had was in the middle of the night the air conditioning would click off. We did not know if there was a motion sensor or something. The elevator was a problem, but not enough to keep us from staying here again.
I also wanted to mention that this hotel is two doors down from the subway and one block away from Broadway and Macy's. 
I would stay here again!

title: “Decent and Functional”
text: Good Service - Rooms were clean and functional, its NY city who stays in the room anyways!!! - awesome little bar in the lobby area - the hotel staff was very helpful with our questions. If you are looking for upscale modern rooms stay at the Hilton but if you are looking for a clean place to lay your head- this is the place. The location is awesome by the way !!!!

title: “Location, Service & Free Parking”
text: Spent President's Day weekend at the Savoy Suites while visiting family. The location was perfect for us-- walking distance to family's apartment and all the shops in Georgetown, including the Whole Foods store. I booked an on-line no refund rate of $83/ night with no cost for parking. The hotel has a nice small bar area and an excellent breakfast buffet for $11.95 each-- pastries, breads, eggs, bacon, waffles, omelets made to order. The rooms provide the basics- comfortable bed, updated bath (great shower), and free wi-fi. The staff was very helpful and courteous at the front desk, the bar and the restaurant. This was the perfect spot to fit our needs-- will be back when in DC.

title: “Nice”
text: Nice hotel, good location. Very friendly staff, storing luggage, etc. Great restaurants nearby.

title: “Nice but Noisy”
text: Rooms are small but adequate for a busy weekend. Main drawback: our room's walls must be made of paper and thin paper at that. We could hear EVERY word from the room next door and they weren't shouting. Our sleep took a beating with their noise including their door slamming at 4:00 AM. I don't blame the guests, the walls are just not insulated to keep out the noise.

title: “Great dc hotel, almost perfect for tourists”
text: 140 a night incl. tax thru priceline negotiator. We went during a heat wave with temps in the 100's and night lows in mid eighties. We didn't get to see as much of DC as we wanted but the hotel was great. block from white house. Robes but not enough towls. Great suction from bathroom vent for tokers. Sealed windows. We had a dinner in their restaraunt, ICI, very good, huge lamb shanks. We had lunch in their bar, bread on sandwhich was a little hard but fries and wife's combo were good. Room service for dinner, we had them add a baby octopus salad from the bar. it was great. Personal pizzas, very good.

title: “Good accommodation for short stay.”
text: We drove down from LA to visit SeaWorld and San Diego Zoo, so this hotel was chosen out of a number available on Mission Valley. It was good value and ideal for a short stay. We stayed a couple of days although I personally wouldn't stay longer, for a week or more unless you are on a budget. Pool area was relaxing and clean.

title: “Hookers Actively Working the Lobby - Need I Say More?”
text:
There is not too much to say. I checked in for a 3 day stay and left after the first night. When I returned to the hotel the first night, there were two younger prostitutes actively and openly working the lobby. I did not notice when one followed me to the elevator and got one. She accosted me on the elevator offering her services.
When I got to my room, I immediately called the front desk. Both security and the "manager" were quite rude for some reason. I wondered if they were getting a cut of the hooker's fees as they both separately seemed irritated that I called to complain. Neither seemed surprised by my call as a normal hotel would be. No apologies, no excuses. Nothing but irritation at me. 
I made a reservation at the Doubletree Metropolitan (wonderful hotel BTW that I have stayed at several times) that night and left early the next morning. In 20 years of making regular leisure trips to NYC, I had never seen anything like this before. I thought I was past being shocked in my life, but this truly shocked me.
I usually stay at the major chains and this confirms why. The room was a bit dumpy and rundown on top of all this.

title: “Everything You Could Want”
text: I recently spent a week at this location for business. As I traveled around Chicago during the week, and visited friends at other hotels, I confirmed again and again that the Hilton Garden Inn is the best kept secret in Chicago. Being in the River North area is perfection. The train is steps away from the front door, there is a grocery across the street (with a surprisingly good natural food section on two aisles...don't be put off by all the processed junk you see as you enter the crowded space), a Trader Joe's two blocks away, Nordstrom across the street in a mall that fronts Michigan Ave for easy bus access, and restaurants everywhere you looked. My husband was thrilled that the Chicago Jazz Mart was a block away as well as an exceptional used bookstore. Spend too much and need to mail things home? There is a post office across the street from the grocery store. It just doesn't get better than this for location. Regarding the room, it was spacious, perfectly appointed, had a great city view, and was spotless day after day. My only small complaint was the bathtub was tiny and not the kind you can lean back in...too concave....so I relaxed in the hot tub near the pool each day. I also loved the business center with three computers, printers, fax machine and copy machine. Wonderful! Regarding noise, the whole city is noisy. That's Chicago. The hotel restaurant, Weber Grill, attracts a lot of lively traffic, but so does every other restaurant in the area. The weekend crowd was noticeably rowdier than the weekday crowd. This is not a sedate hotel for retirees, if you know what I mean. Ask for a room on the upper floors and don't hesitate to call the staff if you need assistance. They were great.

title: “Best Jazz Fest Package”
text:
The Hyatt was the "official" hotel of the 2011 Jazz Festival and they made it a great experience. The weekend package they put together for the price was terrific. We had a room with 2 queen beds, buffett breakfast Sat & Sun, 2 drink tickets on Fri and Sat and free self parking, all for $149 per night - within walking distance of ALL three of the Jazz Fest stages. Could not beat it and this is a gorgeous hotel, it is nicely appointed and the rooms are lovely. We did not have a real "view" but we were there for the festival so it did not matter. 
Only complaint and not against the Hyatt but all hotels, one I have mentioned before and will repeat until the end of time, if a hotel can supply coffee and toiletries replenished each day why not bottled water - not the giant size but 2 regular size bottles of water each day, why charge your guests, I just don't get it.
But the Hyatt - you get high marks from me and I can't wait until next year's Jazz Festival!

title: “Very Nice Hotel Great Location”
text: This was our first stay, but it seems to be a great hotel for the weekend with a wonderful location for downtown area Dallas event.

title: “Evening concierge room”
text: Rosie is such a friendly and comforting person who is always happy to assist in any of your food and beverage needs. It is nice to see someone who genuinely care about you when out of town and away from home. Hilton has a great asset in Rosie.

title: “High Quality Hotel with very reasonable rates”
text:
My partnetr and I recently stayed at the Comfort Inn Times Square to celebrate our 4 years together. The location is so close to everything. We walked out the front entrance and the next street over is right where the ball drops in Times Square. The hotel was very clean and looked like it had just been remodeled. The room was a good size for NYC and the bathroom was very roomy. There was also a free breakfast every morning, fitness room, business center and tons of brochures. 
We went to 4 shows while in NYC and also did the City Sights All Around Town tour. We were so close to everything, it was amazing. The last we stayed we stayed in NJ and went back and forth via NJ Transit. While that option worked out great and helped save some money, the chance to go back to the hotel for a few hours this time to rest was a great benefit. With the rate I got through Choice Privileges we only paid about $20 more a night then when we stayed in NJ. Overall the location, cleanliness and amenities in the hotel made out weekend amazing and allowed us to enjoy every minute to its fullest. 
I would highly recommend this hotel to everyone.

title: “You make the call. You can ask the room next door, they'll hear you...”
text:
This was one of four stops on our California tour. Like many, I booked this location because of reviews here and that Reseda was a family stop over before our next stop, (Yosemite). The jury is out on this one. Unlike other reviews, you judge for yourself.
We had a late check-in, (like 3 am) because of flight delays’. Even though I called five hours earlier to notify them of my status, they no longer held my credit card reserved NON-smoking 2Q room. Instead my family received a 2Q “must have just had smokers” room. It’s amazing how easy you can tell the different between a non-smoking and a smoking room. There’s just nothing that’s going to take the smell out. Lucky, this was just a two night stay.
Quiet place; so quiet that when my family checked-in at 3am and just started to settle down a 3 and 6 year old on jetlag, it was enough to spawn a call from the front desk within 5 minutes of us being in our room for making to much noise. I think it was the toilet flushing that did us in. I have never been call on before for noise. So assume very thin walls. Continue and you'll see.
Room had up to date furnishings including a HDTV. Channel selection is all over the spectrum. Some channels worked and others didn't. (Not sure to blame hotel or Cable company).
The location has a courtyard style pool / lounge area. Small but nice design since it keeps the views of the surrounding auto body shops out of range.
Location has wireless except it was not accessible from our room. Probably out of range or the signal was overwhelmed by all the other local auto body shop businesses wireless connections.
Location: Reseda is big, so all locations in Reseda are NOT the same. We witness that coming down Reseda Blvd. from the 405, (approx 2mi). Went from a upper class nice looking shops to a blue-collar mix class, mechanist industry location. Your parking and entrance ways are both gated by access cards. 
The jury here comes back deadlocked. If the reservation was kept as a non-smoking room and it didn’t warrant a call from the front desk, (who obviously knew we just checked in), I would better rate the place. However, things like this just don’t go well, especially after a long travel day. Also, consider the location if your traveling with families. Not much within the surrounding area. Not a great night life.
Now about the thin walls. Our second night we were awaken around 2 am by a couple who obviously was having a much better start to their vacation then ours.... :)
Next review stop: Best Western, Sonora, CA

title: “Nice Hotel March 2004”
text: Reception was professional and allowed us to check in hours ahead of time. Room did not have view, but was clean, nicely decorated and quiet. The restaurant & staff were excellent along with the food. The pool area was nice. The bar, however, was disappointing....very tacky compared to the rest of the amenities. Free parking & shuttles to and from the airport were appreciated. After other disasters over the internet this turned out to be a pleasant surprise. Would stay here again.

title: “Amazing! Amazing! Amazing!”
text:
Me and three friends stayed at ths hotel for our stay in NYC. It is in a perfect location for shopping and sight seeing, and the service provided by ALL members of staff was fabulous. 
The rooms were cleaned daily (towels changed daily too), we were given the use of a safe for FREE, the internet (and printing) was FREE (both Wi fi and the use of the hotels computers), late check out was FREE and breakfast was FREE!!!!! 
There was a great selection for breakfast, e.g. fresh pancakes, fresh fruit, cereal, toast, bagels, muffins, crossiants, omlettes, sausage, bacon, fruit juices and tea/coffee (tea and coffee was available for free 24 hours a day!). 
Breakfast time can get busy, and there is limited seating so make sure you go down early and you wont have any problem however, hotel staff are very relaxed and allow you to take your breakfast to your room if you prefer (mmm....breakfast in bed- what more can you ask for). 
As I mentioned previously all members of staff are exceptionally helpful but I just wanted to mention Walter- he arranged our transfer back to the airport and looked after our luggage for us until the taxi arrived- Walter was very proactive and reliable : ) 
I would recommend this hotel to friends and family, and if I go back to NYC I would definately go back to this hotel. The rooms are small but this was not an issue- who spends lots of time in their hotel room when in NYC?!?!?!
Thank you to all the staff at the Holiday Inn Express, Times Square, NYC : )

title: “Best Courtyard I've ever stayed at!”
text:
I was so impressed with this Courtyard - I can't say enough good things about it! I'll be honest, I didn't make the reservations and have no idea how much we paid, so I am not evaluating this for 'value for the money' but it's a Courtyard - I can't imagine it was much more than any other one. The little Starbucks bistro served a great breakfast, and even the evening drinks were fantastic. I loved the layout of the lounge and the lobby. It was quick, efficient, friendly, and inviting. It was certainly hipper than any Courtyard I've ever seen. The rooms were spacious and well laid-out, and the bathroom was perfect. The only issues I had during my stay was that the gym was full between 6 and 7:30, so I had to wait for equipment (longest wait was only 10 mins) and there was quite a bit of sand in the tap water - so much that when I arrived there was sand in the bathtub, and the next day, after I brushed my teeth, there was a ring of sand in the sink. So don't drink the tap water. (Sand in the water is new to me, yucky tap water at a hotel is pretty normal.)
All-in-all, I say this is a fantastic hotel! I was really impressed!

title: “Perfect for short breaks”
text: My friend treated me to a trip to New York to celebrate Paddy's Day for my 50th birthday. The Pod Hotel was perfect for 1st timers to New York, nice friendly staff, couldn't do enough for us. Room was fine, (I wasn't there to sit in my room).Toilets and shower room spotless. Location was 1st class as you can walk to Time Square or 5th Avenue in minutes. Really good experience.

title: “Nice Place, Small Room”
text: First time stay at the Hudson. The hotel was very comtemporary and quite welcoming, even though it was very dimly lit. Part of the charm, I guess. The room was extremely small, but comfortable. Didn't spend much time in there anyway. The bar on the main floor, called The Library, was very nice and had a good crowd until closing. The nightclub adjacent to the lobby was incredible and rocked until about 3 AM. Staff was very friendly, and there are plenty of elevators, which I never really thought about until I stayed at a hotel with only one. The hotel is located 1 block west of Central Park, so there is not as much foot traffic as the area closer to Times Square. Not as much early morning noise, either. Also, there are not as many bars and restaurants as the Times Square area, but that's only 2 subway stops away, so no big deal. I would stay here again.

title: “Nice and charming little boutique hotel!”
text: We were there last week and it was our 1st time in Philadelphia. We were offered a glass of wine and cheese and we were informed of different tours of the city. The room was well decorated, a little small but with high ceiling so it was ok. The location was incredible. We walked the city and loved the Reading terminal market where i had the best cheesesteak! We took the subway to the Eagles game and it was very convenient!

title: “Amina is the Greatest Concierge”
text: Amina Blacksher, the Concierge, really made the our stay memorable.

title: “OK, but dicey”
text:
This place almost has it going on, but not quite.
The good:
- It has been recently renovated so the rooms are in good order. Pretty clean, nice suite amenities.
- The internet access speeds are good.
- The workout room is ok..not great.
- The free breakfast and coffee are good quality.
The dicey:
- The front desk is not staffed with the top-notch fresh-faced friendly people you see at the better hotels. You know what I mean. The ones who smile at you and greet you when you check in like you're a long lost friend. Not the vibe here. Purely business. Texting behind the desk. It seems like there's some place they'd rather be.
- It's not in a good area of town and you have plenty of 'Swiss Family Robinson' going on. I walked into the breakfast nook one morning and was bowled over by the smell of people who had not showered before coming to breakfast. Argh..talk about the way to start the day. Needless to say, you don't have this at the better business traveler hotels.
- The house-keeping people are constantly talking loudly in the halls amongst themselves. It's quite a put off.
Bottom-line: It's a pretty cheap place to stay and it has a lot of potential. The problem is that it needs to be managed much better. Everyone in the place needs to be trained on customer service basics: How to greet customers, how to smile, how to make guests feel like you are glad to see them, when to be quiet.

title: “Not as bad as I had feared”
text:
After reading some of the other reviews, I was a little bit concerned about my stay. However, I was attending a conference at the Westin and decided not staying at the host hotel would be more inconvenience than it was worth.
I arrived around 11pm after flight delays and a few wrong turns from the airport. Check in was smooth and the room was fine. The heavenly bed was as heavenly as in other Westins and the bathroom was acceptable - a few hairs from an incomplete cleaning, but nothing that scared me too much. Westin standards? Perhaps not, but nothing to warrant changing rooms.
The location right inside the Galleria was great for shopping and breakfast at Starbucks (considerably less expensive than the hotel restaurant) and convenient to the businesses in/around the area.
One minor frustration was the coffee pot in the room -- it appeared to be one of the "pod" type pots; all of the coffee packages were regular sized. I asked at the front desk a few times for the correct coffee, but never received it. I finally realized that what was in the room would work, but was never told as much by the front desk. If I had to find something to gripe about, that and the somewhat limited free parking would be it.

title: “perfect location, perfect view”
text:
What a beautiful Hotel, we loved our stay at the hotel with our 3 children. The Hotel is near all tourist attractions and people that work there are glad to help you in any way they can. They are super child friendly, the boys loved to explore the treasure chest and a big thumbs up for Steve! Steve is the best and most friendly guy that works there, the boys adored him!
The Hotel is very clean, we had a fantastic view from the room and we can recommend the burgers they serve :)
hope you will enjoy the time there too...

title: “we loved it”
text: If you want to really enjoy the hotel be aware of not receivieng a room with courtyard view. It"s noisy and it:s only a wall. The location is the best

title: “Cool place to stay”
text:
We just got back from a quick four night stay at the Hotel Triton in San Francisco. It was our first time to the city, so I wasn't sure how the location would be, but it was great. The hotel is right across the street from the Chinatown gate, and within walking distance to all kinds of bus stops.
As soon as I walked into the lobby, I was pretty certain I'd made a good choice. The decorations are bright and fun, but not tacky. The lobby is large and has a nice seating area and TV (which they played the World Cup games on, which was nice). We checked in at about 11pm, and the young man at the front desk was very nice and upbeat. In fact, every time we walked by the front desk, whoever was there would always say hello or welcome back, and seemed quite genuine. We also ordered a cab the night before we checked out, and the young man who did that for us was also very helpful and friendly. Check out was a breeze and only took about 30 seconds.
When I made my reservation, I signed up to be a Kimpton In Touch member (free), which gave us free internet access and a $10 gift card for the mini-bar that came with a note from the manager. Nice touch. We booked directly through the hotel website and got the "Stay 3 and save" deal, which saves you 30% if you stay 3 nights or more. This put us at $135 a night. I thought this was a good deal.
We were in room 721, a Deluxe Room with a queen bed. The mattress was soft, the blanket was dreamy and the pillows were feather (can be foam on request). I almost always have trouble sleeping, even at home, and I slept great in that bed. The room had two closets, a desk, a nice looking flat screen TV, dresser and mini-bar. The bathroom had a shower/tub combo and nice Aveda soaps. Another nice touch is the artwork by local artists in the room.
I really liked the atmosphere and design of this hotel.
I would definitely stay here again. The only real reason I gave a 4 instead of a 5 is that they don't have breakfast. I would have given 4.5 if I could. There is a café next door that we went to twice that you can also order room service from (more expensive than physically going into the restaurant, so we just went in), and there are tons of places in the area. They do offer coffee and juice in the morning, and I grabbed an apple from a bowl of them once or twice for the road. There is also a wine hour daily at 5pm, but we were never around for it.

title: “A Pleasant Discovery”
text:
Because our first choice of hotels was booked, and finding a comparable hotel was becoming a problem, we reserved rooms at Park South Hotel. It advertised a high rating with a reasonable price. We were pleased with our visit. On weekend evenings, jazz ensembles performed in the restaurant/bar. The music was excellent, the seating was intimate, and the performance was free. No ordered drinks were required, although those served were delicious. The musicians were approachable and personable. Instead of venturing back out after a day in the city, it was a delightful treat to sit back and relax in a room that opened up to the street. Unlike many hotels that remove their continental breakfast by 9:00 or 10:00, Park South offered a complimentary breakfast until 11:00. The food was fine, and we especially enjoyed sitting at one of the tables on the small patio outside to watch the people passing by. A small balcony, which extended over the lobby, provided an interesting assortment of hardback books to borrow or peruse. The desk staff was remarkably helpful, friendly, and witty. They recommended restaurants within walking distance of the hotel; they provided requested information about other nearby places as well. 
Our room, however, was elongated and cramped, with poor lighting that cast shadows even in daylight. A room without a view, tall brick walls outside the window blocked the sun. The closet was too small to accommodate a suitcase, and no luggage stand was available. No television listing was provided. But those were our only complaints. 
We would definitely stay at Park South Hotel again.

title: “Careful of the rate!”
text: Stayed here in late October. Rooms were pretty nice, common areas not bad either. Room was booked for a conference rate of $199 plus tax ($48). At check out the rate charged was $349 plus tax! Desk clerk was very helpful attempting to resolve, but ultimately had to contact the manager on duty with the statement "please come down to the front desk, we have another one". The manager attempted to convince us the rate was correct even though another couple we traveled with during the exact dates had the correct amount charged to their bill. He had difficulty getting his story straight regarding the timing of the reservation (he had nothing to say after we demonstrated that our reservation was made 3 days earlier than our traveling companions, after he had stated the other couple had received a better rate for an earlier reservation). Ultimately he refused to honor the rate and became exceeding rude until we decided to leave. Plenty of nice hotels in S.F. We'll stay somewhere else the next time we're in town!

title: “GREAT”
text:
Absolutly perfekt
The room was large and clean, the view amazing and the stuff very, very nice.
We started the days with a good breakfast, which is included.
We´ll come again

title: “The worst Hilton we've ever stayed at”
text:
My husband and I just got back from a two week trip including Sedona, the Hopi Reservation, Durango, Co, and Phoenix. We are HiltonRewards members and used out points to stay at the Hilton in Sedona (fabulous), the DoubleTree in Durango, (wonderful), and the Point Hilton Squaw Peak Resort in Phoenix...not so much.
First of all, the air didn't work - it was 112 when we got there. Nothing was ever done. Second, we had ANTS...everywhere. The blinds didn't work and the housekeeper kept moving our things around to where she wanted them. The resort itself seemed run down. The pictures made it look much larger than it is. A "professional" miniature golf course winds around the lazy river at River ranch and inner tubes covered the whole golf course. We, along with several other people couldn't even follow where the holes were. One minute you were on top of a hill, and the next minute you had to cross over a hole someone else was playing to get to your next hole. While we were there, they also had an adolescent basketball conference. Banging of doors, yelling, running up and down the stairs, and yes, one night some kids tried to break into our room. Unfortunately, I was in it! I chased them down the corridor and made sure they understood I didn't find their attempts funny. All, in all, not the most relaxing time. I must say, however, that the HIlton in Sedona was absolutely fantastic, as was the DoubleTree in Durango, Co. My husband and I have stayed at Hiltons for years and the Squaw Peak resort was the worst Hilton we've ever stayed at.

title: “Decent Hotel…Until You Open the Door to Your Room”
text:
Marriott Courtyard – Decent Hotel…Until You Open the Door to Your Room
We got this hotel stay free as a gift and were excited to be back in Philadelphia. When I checked in, I walked up the front desk and only waited in line a short time. There were a ton of children around, like 5 or 6 up at the desk. This is a family hotel, and they do have programs that cater to children. Unlike the Palomar that we stayed in 2 weeks ago, this hotel wasn’t sexy of chic, but more family / child friendly. My check in went off without a hitch. Looking around, I liked the high ceilings and old charm of the building. The entrance has a quiet elegance about it that is appealing.
When you get in from a flight, one thing I always appreciate is when hotels have a light snack station to buy sodas, snacks, fruit and yogurt within the hotel at your convenience. I was able to buy a large fresh fruit cup that looked great as well as a yogurt to get me energized after the hassles of the airport. Perfect!
Everything was great, until I checked into my room. Ugh. There was a HUGE nasty dark stain on the wall that looked like someone had once been killed in the room. (Room 830.) I just wanted to unpack and settle in. I reasoned that this wasn’t worth the confrontation at the front desk for a new room and I just wanted to get on with my stay. I do feel strongly, however, that under no circumstances should a room be rendered to a customer in such disrepair. The next day after housekeeping had come through…UGH…another nasty stain on the blanket on the bed that I hadn’t noticed the day before. I rubbed my hand over it to make sure it wasn’t just how the fabric was laying, but…nope. It was a dark stain. SO GROSS. I don’t think I have ever stayed in a dirty room before and certainly not at any Marriott. I felt like I was sleeping in filth.
The room is very basic and lacking in any upscale amenities. The toiltries are fine and just standard. (The Palomar had top shelf toiletries.) The room décor itself is dated as other reviews on this site indicate. You do have a flat screen TV and you have a little fridge in there if you want to store leftovers, or fresh items. The bedding is awful and a very low thred count. Also, even if you just slightly turn to the left or the right in bed, the bedding all comes apart off the bed. (Aren’t all hotels known for having suction cup sheets that never come undone?) I read about this in one of the reviews and thought the reviewer was just being dramatic about the sheets coming apart, but no. They really do. The actual comforter that lays over you is paper thin and isn’t comfortable. It's more like sand paper. As far as TV channels…forget it. This hotel is pretty much geared toward conventioneers and businessmen. (Think, a ton of sports channels and CNN / FOX News) They didn’t have any “fun” channels like we found at the Palomar, so laying in bed and channel flipping was kind of out. We watched shows on my lap top instead.
You do have an Ipod player in room, which we used and liked. There is no makeup mirror for ladies to use and a very small vanity area. The lighting in the room is good and you have plenty of natural light coming into your room, or at least ours did.
Checkout was seamless and we were billed exactly as we should have been. I was able to store my luggage with no problem before my flight.
What you will like about the Marriott Courtyard is:
-The location. You are right by Maggianos, The Reading Terminal Market (don’t miss that!) and Chilis. We ate at all three places because they were close and easy to get to. 
-Spacious hotel with high ceilings and room to spread out. Lots of nooks and crannies to slip into to do work, take calls or read throughout the hotel.
-Big spacious rooms to work. The restaurant turns into a lounge when not in use for people to use the tables to work from their laptops; it’s nice.
-Old world, historic charm. It is elegant, and you will feel a sense of history.
-Amazing staff. Every single interaction I had with the staff from the time I checked in to the time I hailed a cab was perfect and impressive.
What you won’t like about the Marriott Courtyard is:
-Kids and families that can be loud or in the way
-Wet elevators constantly from the pool, and kiddie feet
-REALLY ugly outdated rooms that aren’t clean, lacking romance and comfort
-Hearing every tap on the walls from other guests
-No frills, and nothing really additional to make you feel special or welcome. There is little attention to detail here.
-No shopping around the hotel, like there is around the Palomar
-A lot of bums and beggers around the hotel constantly asking you for money or baggering you. I felt 100% safe at the Palomar and the surrounding areas, but did not feel nearly as safe around this hotel. I would not have left at night alone, but felt very comfortable at the other location at the Palomar.
I Wish This Hotel Had:
-Better bedding and sheets.
-Free unlimited internet instead of the 1 day free, slow internet. They make you pay more if you want a faster speed. I didn’t have trouble for basic surfing, but did have trouble with streaming.
-Nicer room amenities / updated décor.
This Hotel is Perfect For:
-Families
-Older folks
-No frills, basic needs clientele
-Business meetings and conventions
This hotel is not recommended for:
-Young couples
-Hip / trendy crowds
-Girls weekends
-Romantic weekends
Points of Interest:
-They don’t have room service here, but rather a Chili’s to go menu that you can order and have brought up to you. Chili’s is literally steps from your door, so save yourself the 18% gratuity and just pick up the to go order yourself.
-Don’t leave Philly without doing the double decker bus tour just outside your door at the Marriott. It is really great, cheap (only $27) and is 90 minutes in length to sit through. I loved this, especially on a nice day on the upper deck. You get a full guided tour to listen to and you get to see everything before you commit to getting out at any one location. It was really cool.
-Make sure you go to Mikimoto before you leave Philly. One the best restaurant experiences we have ever had for Japanese. See my review on tripadvisor.com
-We loved Alma de Cuba for Latin food.
Overall:
-You can do better than this hotel. Because the hotel pricing is so competitive in Philadelphia, I would book a 4 start hotel on HotWire.com and try your luck with that. 
-I would also recommend the Palomar for a more upscale, trendy experience. (See my review on tripadvisor.com) The Marriott Courtyard hotel is basic, no frills, and nothing special, but if those are your needs, then it might be perfect for you.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text: I stayed here recently for my nephew's wedding in the area. The hotel was very nice, staff very friendly and complimentary breakfast had a nice variety of delicious food and beverages. The room was nice and I really enjoyed the sitting room area where our family could hang out and visit. There were a couple of good restaurants adjacent to the hotel that we enjoyed.

title: “Very spacious,clean but noisy”
text: We stayed at the Best Western Hospitality House New York last week. We found this accommodation quite appealing as it is very hard to find a two bedroom, roomy apartment for New York that isn't extremely expensive. It also had a fully equipped kitchen that meant we could cook or eat any meal I the room if we cared to do so. First impressions were average however because the 'lobby' or more entrance was extremely small and not that welcoming- it can't be too hard to make it a more pleasant area. The service/reception was good nothing excellent but they were happy to answer questions we had. The apartment was very clean and quite spacious although it wasn't anything ultra modern. We quickly found out how noisy it can be in NYC at night as we struggled to get to sleep some night because of loud garbage trucks and city hall workers maintaining the streets in the middle of the night. We were on the 2nd floor facing the street so that may have effected the noise factor a bit. Good ear plugs helped a lot in those situations though. The television had a large number of free channels which was good. Overall our stay was very pleasant and comfortable and we would recommend it to others.

title: “Excellent value & location”
text: Could not have been happier with our recent stay. Everyone we had contact with exceeded our expatiations. The front desk staff were very efficient and helpful. The rooms, while not what you could call large, were very adequate and clean. Best of all was the location. Just 1/2 block from Times Square. It does not get any better. The next time we visit NYC, this is where we will stay.

title: “Stayed here for the NFL Draft...money well spent!”
text: Great location, great staff, very friendly. We just wanted a nice clean place to stay that was in a great location and this was it. The room was actually a lot larger than other NYC hotels we've stayed in, in the past. 2 blocks from Times Square and 6 blocks from Radio City Music Hall...will be staying here again for sure!

title: “Great family hotel”
text: My family of 4 (two boys ages 4 and 7) just returned from spring break. We split our time between the pacific terrace and torrey pines lodge. We tend to like to stay in very nice places and were hesitant about Pacific Terrace - but it was terrific - perfect location, great pool, nice rooms and very clean hotel. We stayed on 3rd floor in an ocean view room. We could see dolphins swimming from our balcony. Tons of great restaurants within walking distance. My boys absolutely loved pacific beach and the vibe. As mentioned over and over the staff at PT is super friendly. They add nice touches such as bikes available to borrow and sand toys. We were very pleased with our stay and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

title: “Poor Service in a Rundown Property”
text: We arrived late evening were greeted promptly, and assigned a room. Upon inspection the safe was locked shut. Went back to the front desk and kudos to Sam he was the only one to attempt to get it open. Reported it again in the AM and was blown off several times. The whole property was in a state of disrepair and the repairs that were made seemed to be the most inexpensive way to get them done, such as the magnetic closet door holder being reattached by a large glob of caulking. (But at least they tried) The drawers of the dresser/TV stand were all broken and caved in and not operational. Choice Hotels should inspect this property and seriously think about removing their name from it.

title: “The Entrepreneur’s Perspective”
text: As an alumnus of one of Chicago’s most renowned colleges, I have had my share of hotel stays; from five stars on the Magnificent Mile to what some may call a “rink dink” in the heart of the “hood”! As a young music entrepreneur, I travel to Chicago relatively often; and I always need a safe, clean environment to lodge. At times, lodging creates a traveler coin toss for me though – Should I spend x amount of dollars on what could be my shopping adventure, on a hotel over standing the lake? Or should I stay in some cheap motel across the street from a hustler’s house, and still have money to splurge at Macy’s? When vacationing in large metropolitan cities like Chicago, these typical scenarios play a huge role in the success of a traveler’s venture. The Amber Inn is the ideal example of “the perfect medium”. Located minutes from Downtown, the hotel’s ambiance is cozy, friendly, and forthcoming. The staff goes above and beyond to make you feel like you are right at home! My last visit left such a savoring taste in my mouth; I can’t even begin to put it in words-yet I must. The staff actually allowed me to extend my check out time 3HOURS in order to accommodate my transportation time. While waiting the staff, offered and shared food with me, and even gave me great networking advice. I feel like my stay at the Amber Inn contributed to my vacation as a whole in Chicago! I was in a safe, clean and friendly environment, at a discounted price-IT GETS NO BETTER!

title: “A wonderfully unexpected magical experience - we didnt want to leave.”
text:
We stayed here during a month trip to States travelling with teenage boy and girl. We had booked on the internet and some of the reviews were a bit mixed so we weren't expecting too much. BUT - it was just wonderful! They sent a driver to pick us up at the airport - cost less than a taxi fare and much more fun. A really attentive and helpful welcome on arrival. Our room was absolutely spotless and lovely touches like the had set the bed side radios to be playing gentle classy music when you went in, and we also had a chocolate cake because we'd let them know it was my birthday trip. Staff were the most helpful I have ever come across - everyone from the porter, the reception staff, the maids were falling over themselves to help. Complementary breakfast which you could eat by the nice sunny pool, or take back to your room - great choice of fresh baked pastries, cereals and fruit. An added bonus was the guest laundry - really cheap $3 I think - and so necessary when travelllng with kids. The location was great too - only 5 minutes from the madness of Hollywood Boulevard - but 5 minutes from Runyon Canyon where you could hike or jog. Also just short walk to the subway that takes you straight to Universal Studios.
There is free wireless in the rooms, and free soft drinks and snacks at reception, as well as videos. All great to keep teenagers happy.
We would definately go back - a real unexpected gem.

title: “Hotel Stay”
text: Great location, clean rooms, really good breakfast area, very helpful staff. Our only problem was that the safes in both our rooms didn't work. One had no front panel and the other one you couldn't set a code.

title: “Marriott does it again! Fantastic!”
text: The Marriott Residence Inn in the Piper Glen area of Charlotte NC is not to be missed. Every room is a suite and a very large suite at that! I think my room is as big as my first apartment. Each comes with full size fridge, microwave, dishes, dining area, 2 tv's, seperated rooms, central heating and air....the list goes on and on. The cleanliness of the rooms was impecible and met with my strict standards.The outdoor pool is lovely, but the workout room is a bit small. It only had 2 treadmills, a bike and a stepper. The best thing is the breakfast! Full service, complimentary breakfast with eggs, sausage, waffles, cereal, yogurt, bagels etc. Very good, and it changed daily. Also, each day had a happy hour with complimentary food in the evening. If you're looking for a great place to stay, the Residence Inn has it all.

title: “nice hotel”
text:
Great hotel, with wonderful friendly staff who were always so helpful from the minute we arrived until we left. Nice bright & clean room with the most comfortable bed ever in a super location, a quiet spot at the top of the hill but close enough to walk to Union Square, China Town in a few minutes or even Fishermans Wharf for the energetic and ride home on the trolley bus that stops outside the hotel.
The gym was brilliant and also enjoyed an hour or so in the lounge & bar in the evenings. We took a few meals in the hotel all of which were excellent especially the breakfast
Would definitely stay here again

title: “you don't get what you paid for”
text:
Booked a three night stay at the Omni through Expedia.Paid an extra $25 a night for a premium room with two double beds, a balcony, view of the bay and downtown skyline. First room no balcony and a view of a roof top. Second room no balcony and a sliding bathroom door that's a half inch shorter than the opening. I was told the hotel only offers a balcony with a king size bed and they were not responsible for what was listed on the Expedia website. A king size bed was unacceptable since my 23yr old daughter was staying with us. Expedia said the hotel maintains all the information on the website. The hotel offered to comp the vallet parking to make up for the discrepancy with the room since they couldn't change the rate. I didn't use the valet parking the first night because you can park 
across the street for $11 per day .They also claim I was the first to complain about the bathroom door. I said maybe they do things different in calif. but when I use the facility I like total privacy. In addition construction was going on across the street. Who needs a wakeup call when you can 
hear a bulldozer at 8am. I would not stay here again, at this price there are better hotels to select.

title: “great”
text: Went with 3 girlfriends who are all picky and we were happy with this hotel. The rooms were a good size, more towels provided when asked, water presure good, room service good and friendly staff. I like staying on the east side but the prices were too high and I got a great deal at the holiday inn. I am planning another trip and looks like im staying here again. I would upgrade if I could but prices are again too high and I had no problems with this hotel except the bar closed at midnight so we had to continue our evening with a bottle to go up to the room. If you can't afford rockstar prices this is the best place for you.

title: “Good Experience for the Price”
text:
We stayed at the Red Roof Inn when we were in town for a wedding. I wasn't expecting much and was pleasently surprised. The rooms are clean and the beds are comfortable. The location is fantastic. 
The room was smaller than I expected - even for a city hotel. If you are traveling as a couple alone I would suggest requesting a room with one king sized bed. Our room had 2 double beds and it was difficult to navigate. We had trouble finding places to put our suitcases!
Overall it was a good experience.

title: “Town and Country, Same as it ever was.”
text: What can you say about this property? It's old and it has pretty gardens. I prefer to stay in newer more modern hotels but this wasn't bad. When we checked in our A/C unit was leaking. Since it was well past midnight we waited until morning to report it. They had a guy up there within 5 minutes. Yes, the decor is at least 20 years old, but everything was immaculate. The staff was friendly and helpful. The price was fair for the room and location. Excellent cable (at least 35 channels.) We had a room in the tower but peeked into the bungalows and they are all pretty much the same. Our room was quiet and clean. I recommend getting a car so that you can go to all the shops and restaurants in the area. The mall behind the hotel has PF Changs, California Pizza Kitchen, Cheesecake Factory. About 3 miles away there is Kings Fish Market, Chevy's and drive thru. Motel Circle is a bit of a nightmare to navigate and not friendly to pedestrians. The hotel is enormous, there are over 3000 rooms. All in all it was fine.

title: “Location & service”
text:
This was our sixth visit to this hotel. As always the service was right on. One small problem. The hair dryer went on the fritz. Within 5 mins. the maintenance dept. was up to fix it. Within another 5 mins. we had a new dryed installed. Now I dont care about a hair dryer, but my wife does. For me a bad hair day means I still have some. Check in and out was flawless. We check out early because of taking Amtrak. Desk clerk called a cab for us. This may seem a small thing. However the cabs in San Francisco are a lot like cats. You can call them but they dont always come. I know the hotel has a little more pull, so I ask the desk clerk to make the call. The staff were all great and very helpful. Price was right .
