The room and the bathroom were clean and fresh. I always check the bathroom frist. No problems. Bed was king size and an air mattess. Very nice. Ask for a room away from traffic no problem.
A lot of people dont like the tourist area of Fishermans Wharf. We love the action there. The location is great. The Cable Cars are about 4 blocks away. The F line street cars stop about 1/2 block away. There is a passage way from the courtyard to the Wharf. I Hop next door. 
Fire pit is nice for relaxing and making new friends, All in all a great hotel.

title: “Exceptional Customer Service”
text:
Exceptional service at reception/arrival by hotel associates Mr. Francisco Sanchez and Mr. Matt Arnell. We are frequent guests at the Barclay Intercontinental and the service is always great. However, Francisco and Matt did a terrific job of welcoming our party and making us feel right at home. It is coworkers like this that establish the level of excellence and an expectation you always manage to exceed here at the property. 
Managing Executive Sean Olmstead provides the leadership and quality management that communicates the professional attitude and courtesies extended by Francisco and Matt. It is truly appreciated and makes the stay that much more enjoyable. Please acknowledge their great service, attitude and professionalism. Staying at the Barclay--from the greeting by the doormen to the final sign off is like being at home with a gracious and courteous staff

title: “Friendly staff and clean, modern facility”
text: Stayed 3 nights at the Madison Hotel. The facility is an old bank, and gym's walls are made of thick exposed steel and the vault is still present...pretty cool. The lobby is absolutely beautiful. Staff were friendly and everyone makes it a point to greet you when they pass you in the hall or on the elevator. A few minor flaws. When we arrived, we told the bellhop that all of the luggage from the car would be coming into the hotel. He told us to go ahead and he would bring it to the room. But he only brought a few things and still left some pieces of luggage in the car. So we had to go back out and get it ourselves. Also, we were told at check-in that the continental breakfast would be served on the mezzanine...but arrived to find it empty the next morning. After asking at the front desk, we were informed to go to the restaurant. The only issue with this is, it was sit-down service only. We particularly chose a hotel with continental breakfast buffet so we could grab a few things and go back to the room or head out around town. Also, only 3 small draws in the room. Had to leave most things in the suitcase. Small room, but very nice, spaceous bathroom. And the bed was very comfortable! Overall, a good experience. Close enough to walk to Beale Street.

title: “Do Not under any circumstance stay here Ever.”
text: When reservations were made, rooms were quoted at $ 120 per night due to the Beale Street Music Festival..when we arrived $145..then with 3 of us in a room, we only had 2 towels..they charged us $10 per extra towel..Rooms were filthy, very run down place...worst part: The cleaning lady told us to lock all of our things in our car when we left, because, the owner always went through the rooms when guests were out!!!!!!!!..Our other friends, also staying there were greeted with a recent hatch of cockroaches...This was the absolutely worst lodging available...I would have preferred joining the homeless on the street corner...!!!!!!!!!!!! I will be researching to find out whom to report this hotel to, something needs done..Do Not Stay Here!!! There is not enough alcohol in Memphis to make this place acceptable.

title: “Girl's Weekend”
text:
One of my younger sisters and I decided to have a girl's weekend away from our kids and husbands. We wanted something that was a little posh, in a good location with lots of shopping and dining options. The Westin was PERFECT. To begin with, I called the Westin directly to see if there were any specials currently going on. This was after pricing it on various internet sites and also through a few other travel options that I have. The gentleman that I spoke with, extremely helpful, polite, humorous, and he was able to reserve a room for us at a great deal. I received a couple of emails from them prior to our trip, which was also nice.
Location: Was exactly what we were looking for. There were numerous shops and places to dine at all within easy walking distance. As in across the street. The Westin in on the end of the Domain shopping area, before what looked to be condo/apts began. This was nice because that meant you weren't in the middle of all the shopping where noise and traffic might be a concern. The variety of shops and restaurants was also nice.
Hotel: The inside feels very urban to me. Not sure if that is the correct style, but modern, straight lines, clean, earthy tones. Everything looked very nice. When you walk in, there is a lounge area to the right and the bar with more lounge space is to the left. Check-in was straight ahead.
Room: Again, a very city urban feel. I will admit, that I hated the color of the carpet, but my sister loved it. Also the closet door looks weird. Reminded me of those tall filing cabinets from school. But loved everything else. The beds....wow. Comfortable! With nice plush covers and pillows. No complaints :) Water pressure was also very good, especially given that we were on the 7th floor. Our room was in the front of the hotel, so our view looked out over the entrance and over to the shopping areas. Again, no complaints.
Staff: A room is a room is a room. But staff can really make or break a place. That and a lousy bed :) Everyone there was wonderful. No, better than wonderful. I'm not really sure I can think of a word to describe how incredible they were. My sister and I had arrived late and were interested in food, but it was almost 10pm. Both of the girls at the front desk were extremely helpful in helping us decide where we wanted to go and eat. Then when we wanted to go shopping, they had some great suggestions as well. The waitstaff in the Urban grill was extremely friendly as well. The bartenders were more than willing to let my sister sample the various beers that were on tap before choosing one. When we needed a taxi, they not only called one for us, but found us in the bar area to let us know that it had arrived.
Overall: Next time I need a place to stay while in Austin, this is it. I couldn't ask for more. And when I travel in the future, I will definitely see if there is a Westin hotel near!

title: “Holiday Inn SoHo”
text: Stayed in So Ho for a long weekend. The rooms were small, but we weren't in them enough to care. I think most of them are in New York. Rooms were clean, bed was comfortable. A little street noise but not too much. Location was good. I would stay there again. Price was reasonable.

title: “Historic Elegance”
text: We recently stayed at the Fairmont in San Francisco. the Nobb Hill setting is incredible with views to both the bay bridge and golden gate bridge. We stayed in a one bedroom tower suite that had almost a 360 view of the city downtown area. The room was old school elegant with a really comfortable bed and incredible views. They even equip the room with a telescope! The rate for the room was fairly expensive but worth it. TIP: If you want to pay for a suite...make sure you request a room above the 8th floor or higher.

title: “Cosmopolitan Hotel”
text: The Cosmopolitan Hotel is a great deal for budget minded travelers. They even have a room for 5 people-2 queen beds and a sofa bed-while small-it was super clean and quiet. Great location in Tribeca with the subway right outside the door. No restaurant but Starbucks downstairs and lots of inexpensive restaurants and delis around the corner plus upscale restaurants on West Broadway. Staff was friendly.

title: “we loved it”
text:
My wife booked a room at the Chelsea Hotel for a one night visit a few weeks ago. I read the reviews on this website the night before we flew to NYC with our two college-age daughters. I was appalled by some of the comments. We wanted to back out - but of course it was too late. So we decided to tough it out instead. We're happy we did. 
Our 7th floor room was fantastic - beautiful hardwood floors and tiled fireplace, french doors between our bedroom and an internal foyer and bathroom, and two large windows opening onto a wrought iron balcony, where we spent some time the next morning looking out on the city as it headed to work. Our biggest concern before we arrived - cleanliness - was unwarranted; our room was as clean as any of the four star hotels we've stayed at in NYC and elsewhere. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful. 
The Chelsea Hotel is old and it shows. If you're looking for an uber-fashionable but sterile environment designed to make hotel guests feel elite, the Chelsea is not your place. But if you think you might enjoy a stay in a hotel rich in history that attracts a diverse clientele with authentic stories to tell (including those told by some of the outstanding artwork on the walls), I don't think you could make a better choice.

title: “OK hotel, good location, angry protestors and uncaring staff”
text: I wish I had read these reviews about the protestors prior to booking or at least traveling. We stayed for 2 nights at the end of September for a work trip with my husband's partners, and I booked the hotel. You can't beat the location. The rooms are ok...cute decor but not expensive looking. There were plastic covers under the sheets and the automatic bathroom light was annoying at night/early morning. We also used tried to use the hotel computer to try and print off boarding passes and the computer was not only ancient, but the also ancient printer was broken. How about a sign on there or get it fixed? I could overlook these minor details if it weren't for the loud, angry, harrassing protesters outside each day, and the management/staff's complete lack of care about the situation. We had no warning upon check-in of the situation which happens DAILY. We had people yelling in our ears as we entered and left the hotel...screaming at us "SHAME ON YOU...blah blah blah." It wasn't until my husband ASKED the mgmt about a seperate entrance away from the protestors, that they told us about the entrance by the restaurant. Why wouldn't they just tell us in the first place? I was embarrassed, having been the one to book this hotel for a corporate event. There are so many cute boutique hotels in the area that I would rather give future business to. It's unfortunate.

title: “Great location with reasonable price”
text: We stayed here over the Martin Luther King weekend and found it very reasonably priced for DC. It was in a superb location near Dupont Circle and close to Embassy Row. The rooms were nice and we had a lovely view toward the Washington Monument etc. The service was quite good and everything as expected for a Courtyard.

title: “New Hotel * Great Experience”
text:
My husband and I recently had the opportunity to stay at one of Chicago's newest hotels in downtown Chicago, Hotel Blake. We took the rapid transit in from O'Hare Arport and was surprised to see that the hotel is located right on the Blue Line stop. We walked just a block and were right at the hotel's doorstep. The hotel is also walking distance to the Art Institute, Buckingham Fountain and many other sights in the area.
The hotel rooms are quite large and very nicely decorated with fluffy down comforters on the beds and the rich colors of the decor are absolutely beautiful.
The hotel staff was most polite and accommodating to our every request. We found the hotel to be comfortable and to our liking in every way.
I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a great stay while in Chicago.

title: “Wedding trip to Austin”
text: We were greeted by a professional and caring staff. The property is centrally located in the north western Austin area. We enjoyed shopping and eating in the nearby Arboretum. Our room was very clean and appeared to be updated recently. Our room package included a cooked to order breakfast that is also very good. Our children enjoyed the indoor pool and hot tub.

title: “great place, good value”
text: we stayed for 3 nights at the beginning of feb. would recommend this hotel. staff could not be more helpful, the room was great and the location was perfect for all the sights. would definately stay there again.

title: “expedia price couldn't be beat”
text:
We got an amazing rate at Le Meridien -- about $160 per night, which is unbelievable for San Francisco. When I checked in with two teenagers, the kind woman at the front desk said, "I bet they'd like a view..." and promptly put us in a room with a bay view on the 24th floor. Everything was perfectly clean, the view was amazing. The concierge was friendly, knowledgable and helpful. 
I would call this a great business hotel. I'm not sure I'd agree that it's a five-star hotel, as some ads claim, but it's a solid four-star stay in a great location.

title: “we loved it and we'll be back”
text:
we were a group of 12 persons, teens and adults( between 18 and 45 yo) and we stayed 5 nights. the hotel is very nice, the staff was very helpful,, the location is excellent, and decoration awsome
i particularly would like to praise one of the concierg and john the doorman that was fantastic in helping us
i would advise this hotel to everybody

title: “great location”
text: We chose this hotel because of the location and it included breakfast. We were on a parking package also. Hotel is located only 3 blocks from Navy pier and one black from Michigan Avenue. You are in the heart of the city here. The staff was very friendly and helpfu. We would stay here again

title: “When can we go back!”
text: We enjoyed our stay at the Catamaran very much. Place is well kept, the staff was very helpful with everything that we needed, including rental car and coupons for nearby restaurants. We can't wait to go back! We didn't take the kids, but it is a family friendly hotel as well. I would highly recommend.

title: “Old and worn out”
text: We stayed here before flying out on vacation. As we used points, they charged us $10 per day for parking. Used the shuttle to get to airport - close to on time but confusing upon return as there are 4 different Holiday Inn shuttles that pick up at O'Hare. The 2 elevators at the hotel did not work in the morning, so all guests had to use the freight elevator which caused a long wait and very frustrated guests. Carpet was dusty behind the easy chair and hadn't been vacuumed in months there. Toilet was wobbly, and sink drained poorly. The carpet on the stairs to the parking was threadbare and the stairway poorly lit. The bar off the lobby was noisy, and looked popular with young business travelers anxious to meet others. The whole facility must be about 50 years old and is just worn out.

title: “A San Francisco Gem”
text:
I thoroughly enjoyed a recent stay at this boutique property located near Union Square. The hotel staff is genuinely friendly and strives to make your stay as pleasant as possible. The rooms are oversized according to SF hotel room standards with attractive furnishings and bonus amenities like CD/DVD players with free DVD rentals, free Internet access, Aveda toiletries, and soft linens. Housekeeping does a stellar job with gleaming bathrooms and extra touches such as turn down service that does not have to be requested (which is definitely a rarity in most hotels at present). Each morning a complementary continental breakfast in the hotel's attractive restaurant is provided, which is much better than the usual packaged and processed foods that are found at low-end properties.
Having stayed at numerous SF hotels, I was impressed with the excellent service and fashionable accommodations of the Orchard Hotel which come at a very reasonable price. This property is a fine example of what astute management can bring to the benefit of the customer. I have highly recommended this property to colleagues and plan to make it my preferred choice of lodging in SF.

title: “Nice time in the Gaslamp Quarter..”
text: This was our first time staying in the Gaslamp Quarter. My in-laws always stay at The US Grant and they were joining us on this trip so we stayed there too. The hotel is very nice! The staff were very attentive and pleasant. The rooms are small but comfortable. They even offer free bottled water in your room! And they will give you as much as you want. I loved that! The only complaint I have about the room is that it wasn't dark enough. If you like to sleep in a bit, I suggest you bring a sleep mask. Also, there is not a coffee maker in the room so you have to either go to the gift shop to buy a cup of coffee or walk across the street to Starbucks. There are all kinds of bars and restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. We would stay here again for sure!

title: “Priceline and University Place - good luck”
text:
We booked three rooms on Priceline and ended up with University Place. Strike one: I seriously question the "downtown" rating that Priceline gives it as you cannot walk to anything "downtown" from this location. It's a cab or car ride to any sporting event, shopping or downtown restaurant. If you are needing to be near the IUPUI campus or medical centers, it's perfect. 
Strike two: We checked in at 5:00 PM and were told all 3 of our rooms were not ready. Since we had dinner reservations at 5:30 PM and tickets for an event at Lucas Oil, we were told by the front desk they would store our luggage until we returned and checked in, which we said would be around 10:00 PM. Strike three: We arrived around 10:00 PM to find that the hotel was overbooked and they only had two of our three rooms (which we already paid for). In addition, our confirmation for double beds for three staying in each room wasn't available and those were now king beds. Rollaways were ordered and they would credit the $14.00 parking fee for the inconvenience (that was an amusing offer). As for the third room, we were given the standard "walk letter" for a room at the Columbia Club and I packed up my 7 and 12 year olds and we went out into the cold night via a cab to the Columbia Club and finally got checked into a room around 11:15 PM and two plus miles away from other members of our party and the vehicles we all came in. Connecting for breakfast and the return home was an additional inconvenience. When I asked why they didn't tell us at 5:00 PM there was a problem and they, in fact, didn't have three rooms available, no one could answer me. Upon checking into the Columbia Club, I was told by the desk attendant that they see this a lot and the University Place/Priceline team is great at overbookings. 
Bottomline, if you use Priceline for a "downtown" hotel be careful. If you end up with University Place, good luck.

title: “THE BEST HOTEL IN CHICAGO!”
text:
What can I say? Each time I stay at the Omni Chicago, I think to myself, "WOW, it can't get any better than this." And it DOES! We celebrated our 31st wedding anniversary at the Hotel. When the staff found out, they sent up some very, very nice surprises for us. We were just spoiled rotten the whole time we were there. We were treated like royalty.
We stayed in one of the Governor's Suites. It was very spacious, very clean, and tastefully decorated. All rooms are suites with a TV in the living room, and one in the bedroom. The Omni is right on Michigan Avenue where you are just steps away from shopping and restaurants. 
As a Select Guest Member, my husband and I received a pot of coffee, juice and newspaper each morning, at the time chosen by us. If you choose to stay at the Omni, you might want to consider joining their Select Guest Program. It is free and there are so many amenities included. You get your choice of high floor/low floor, near the elevator/away from the elevator, and so much more.When I joined I received a 50% off coupon for a weekend stay. I also received another coupon for an upgrade. And, of course you receive the coffee, juice and newspaper delivered to your door in the morning at no charge. 
I want to thank the whole staff at the Omni Chicago for making our stay so perfect! You're the best!

title: “Intimate Luxury”
text: My husband and I stayed at the XV Beacon for our anniversary. We stayed in a studio - very spacious with beautiful furnishings, linens, great sound system. The bath room was a bit small for a hotel in this price range, but all appointments were luxurious. The best part of this hotel is the service - it is impeccable. The staff are courteous, friendly, not fussy, and very responsive. The restaurant (Federalist) has absolutely fantastic food - and the service, as in the rest of the hotel is wonderful. This is a VERY pricey hotel, but worth the money if you want someplace intimate, with wonderful personalized attention. It is what all top hotels should be.

title: “From now on, this will be my only hotel when I go to NYC”
text: I researched many hotels online, which is how I found out that *the* question to ask is: "Does each room have a private bathroom?" The nyma reviews were mostly positive regarding value, cleanliness, and accessibility--and it was within walking distance of the Mid-Manhattan Library where I was speaking. The front desk staff and the lady whi assists with sightseeing were pleasant and helpful. (I had Google maps to three places I needed to go, but she gave me better directions.) The room was slightly larger than I expected. The room, the bed, and the bathroom were all spotless. The free continental breakfast had the usual choices: bagels, toast, doughnuts, yogurt, cereal, apples and bananas, juice, coffee, and tea. Everything was available in abundance and the breakfast room was also clean and inviting. When I was looking for my scheduled ride amid the trucks and cleaning crews on the street, the dooman came out and offered to hail me a cab. Every member of the housekeeping staff I encountered were also friendly and polite. The hotel is on a street packed with Korean restaurants, and is also within walking distance to Broadway, 5th Ave., the Empire State Building, and dozens of stores and restaurants. Highly recommended.

title: “Wonderful hotel”
text:
This is a wonderful little pearl in the middle of Washington DC just in front of the white house. Ok it's expensive. But you get what you pay for. Perfect location, personal service from the staff and wonderful rooms. 
During our stay the hotel was undergoing refurbishment. We were not informed of this and one day it was very noisy and the entire hallway carpet was wrapped in plastic. Since we were travelling with a little child who needed a few hours sleep during the day we had to change room. We were fist offered a smaller room but when we refused this they gave us the same size on another floor away from the construction site. We received four breakfast coupons for the inconvenience. The breakfast was great - but expensive.
The staff was very friendly.

title: “Not worth the money...”
text:
My overall impression of this hotel is that it quite simply is not worth the $1200/night price tag. 
- The rooms are comfortable, but basic and the decor is unimaginative and lacks the luxurious touches expected of a hotel of this sort (there were no cushions on the sofa, no complimentary fruit and water in the room).
- The check in was disastrous. One of our rooms was not ready yet, we were taken by a member of the reception staff to have a drink in the lounge. We were left standing at the entrance for 5 mins whilst the receptionist ensued in lengthy debate with the girl at the desk in the bar that we couldn't sit down for a drink as they were busy (they weren't); this situation could have been handled much better had someone taken charge. We were then taken all the way to the back bar where we were charged for our drinks (any other 5 star hotel would have given these to the client complimentary).
- I asked the concierge for an adapter (as did the other half of our party in a different room), it took 2 phone calls and an hour to get this adapter to us).
- Our room was not turned down on the second evening of our stay.
- The first morning we booked breakfast with the concierge half an hour in advance, went down for breakfast and the restaurant told us they didn't have our booking.
However, on the other hand:
- The rooms are large with great views.
- The lobby is fantastic and I don't think I have ever seen one to rival it.
- The location for shopping is unparalelled.
- The breakfast was fantastic.
- If you can overlook the inefficient service, you realise it is warm and friendly.

title: “Wonderful stay at Nine”
text: This is an excellent boutique hotel. The beds are comfortable and so soft. They even except dogs but you don't see them. I only heard one dog bark a little bit and that's it. The location is excellent. You are in walking distance to everything and close to subway train. I enjoyed my stay very much and it's a great place to stay.

title: “Wonderful hotel!”
text:
After reading the reviews, I felt I needed to put my two cents in. The Sofia Hotel was a great place to stay! The staff was very accomodating and the room was very nicely appointed and spacious. (queen bed plus queen sofa bed). There's nice reading lamps, a modern sink, a comfortable bed and nice amenities (soap, shampoo, etc.) The Currant restaurant below had great food and drinks. The location is great, too. Easy to get to from the 5 freeway. Valets were great. A bit pricey per night at $28, but parking is so scarce in downtown SD, so believe it or not, it's still a good deal.
I didnt' have time to check out the spa, but next time, I'll stay longer.
Thank you Sofia Hotel, for one of the best stays in San Diego.

title: “Very pleasant”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay at the Courtyard. Check in was fast, friendly and efficient. Nichole at the front desk was perky and pleasant. Overall the staff were much friendlier than I have experienced at other hotels - surprising for a Courtyard, which is not a full service hotel but more of a business hotel. They often asked how we were doing when walking through the lobby. 
Location can't be beat. It is a 5-8 minutes walk from the blue line train that goes to Ohare airport and Orange line that goes to Midway airport, and a 1 minute walk from the red line train that goes to Wrigley Field. There are tons of restaurants, bars, and convenience stores in the area. It felt very safe even late night. 
Room was very clean, typical Courtyard everything. Our rate was pretty high due to a convention in town, but so was every other hotel. 
Free high speed internet in room (wired ethernet, no wireless). It was a fast connection though - unlike some other hotels I have stayed in. We never heard any of our neighbors talking or noise in the halls. Newspaper delivered to our door every day. Nice TV in room, great picture - similar to a Sony WEGA TV which is still a tube but a flat tube with bright picture. Parking was $36/day but we did not have a car and you get robbed for parking anywhere downtown. Skip the car and ride the train or take a cab. 
I was very pleased with every aspect of our stay.

title: “Great location!!”
text: I've stayed at many hotels throughout the us for business and pleasure. The staff at the Hilton garden was very accommodating. Will definitely stay there again.

title: “An almost perfect stay”
text:
We stayed at the Library hotel in the last week of October 2008 as part of our honeymoon around the US. 
The positives - the hotel is in a fantastic location right near the public library and within easy walking distance to Times Square and many other NY landmarks. The rooms are relatively small, but if you are spending all your time in your room in NYC then you are there for the wrong reason. The continental breakfast provided has excellent variety and the wine and cheese receptions in the evening were a pleasure to comeback to. Igor (Chief Concierge) was funny and extremely helpful - even providing exact details to a small concert hall out in New Jersey with maps and directions. 
The negatives - Firstly, as mentioned by other reviewers, the hotel will not take payment at the time of booking. Given we booked our accommodation when the Aus dollar was at 98c to the US dollar it was disappointing that payment would only be taken at checkout when the dollar had dropped to 59c. This meant our stay cost and extra 1500AUD than it would have when we booked. Secondly, we had huge issues after we had checked out with our credit card. We were advised when we checked in that the cost of the accommodation plus $100US per day for incidentals would be placed on hold. This was fine. Unfortunately when we departed (and our account had been finalised) the amount on hold was not released resulting in the hotel ‘double dipping’ so to speak. When we contacted the hotel to ask them to release our funds (given we had paid our account in full) we received a very unfriendly response from a front desker named Lennard who informed us that it was not the hotel and that banks are quick to blame hotels for their own mistakes. After a few (VERY EXPENSIVE) phone calls to my own bank in Australia I was able to confirm that it was indeed the Library that still had the funds on hold (a total of 2800USD). After another unpleasant conversation with Lennard, we were forced to call our bank in Aus back and ask for them to call the Library hotel. Luckily our bank had more luck when they spoke with Lennard and were able to resolve the situation immediately. But it really did spoil what was a fantastic stay. 
OVERALL - Would we stay there again? Absolutely - the rooms are clean, well serviced, the food was great and the location is excellent. Would we do anything differently? Yes, we wouldnt provide a credit card as security to avoid the unfortunate situation we found ourselves in.

title: “Great location if you want to be in Times Square or Theatre District”
text: I brought my 7 year old to NYC for our first "just us" getaway. It was a last minute trip and as such hotels (in NYC at Christmastime) were exorbitantly priced. Cheapest 4 star was 519! Well, I gave price line bidding a chance and we won the room for 275. I asked for a room near the elevator, and my little cutie asked "can we be super high in the sky??" so, rightfully charmed, they honored her request. From other reviews I gather that bidder price stays are put in the less favorable rooms but we had a perfect adequate space. It was clean, with amazing views, and exactly as pictured. Updating WOULD be wise, as the accommodations were 3- 3/12 star and NOT 4 star, but I have no complaints.

title: “Not as bad as people have reviewed”
text:
Stayed here for two nights on 12/13 September 2012.We found that there are very few middle of the ground hotel/motels in san francisco - everywhere is either too expenisve or looks crap and dirty (and expensive) Buena Vista I think was right for us. we had both a king suite and a double queen room as a party of 5. Get the bad points out of the way first - it is a little dirty in places but I'm only talking about general use as in scuff marks on wall and the odd bit of dirt on carpet and floors. That's about that. 
The location is really good 10/15 minute walk down to Fisherman's Wharf. Or 10/15min walk up hill to the twisty part of Lombard street.at night if you dont want to eat down at the wharf there are nice reatsaunts up two blocks to Union street . We ate in the italian on first night and it was excellent. the breakfast is fine- tea and coffee bananas and apples and various pastries(fine as all included in the price and saves you some money at the start of the day). Car parking is free and off the street.(it is tight but you will find a space).
Overall this hotel is a good place to stay for a few nights in San Francisco.it is reasonably priced for a stay in the city and we had no issues.
I would happily recommend Buena Vista to anyone that doesn't have unrealistic expectations for a hotel located where this is and the price you will pay.

title: “Cute, Cozy, & Cosmic”
text:
I've been eye-ing Yotel since I first heard about it's opening in NY and was thrilled when I got a great deal through Travelzoo. I've worked in the hotel industry in both customer service and sales. I thought it was a cool concept - the design and the integration of technology. Using the kiosk to check in was a breeze, in fact the employee that was there to assist actually ended up making it a little more difficult for me. The elevators were kind of a hassle, but the room made up for it. It was cute, cozy, and cosmic! The bathroom was a little awkward since the door to the toilet/shower was far from soundproof. Make sure you're travelling with someone that you're comfortable with and don't mind if they catch a peek!
My only complaint was the restaurant. We went down to grab a bite at 4:45pm on a Saturday. The hostess explained that dinner wouldnt be available until 5, but we were fine with the lite fare options anyway (despite the steep cost) We chose to sit outside and the hostess explained that we could sit where ever we liked and a server would take care of us. Well after sitting there for 10 minutes with no greeting whatsoever from the only server we saw who walked by eyes multiple times (avoiding any eye contact), we decided it was not worth the wait. 
Note: If you have trouble getting service at the restaurant too, go to the corner of 43rd and 10th, Mr. Biggs! Great service, nice outdoor seating, get the Mexi Curly Fries!!!
All in all I will be staying here again for sure and will recommend it to everyone. But Yotel Management really needs to step up staff training. Just because the design is minimalistic doesnt mean the service should be too.

title: “Elegance and Bliss”
text: I love this hotel. It is classy, gorgeous, and truly 5*. The rooms are beautifully appointed and the toiletries and bathrooms elegant. My only minor complaint is on the size of the room, which was not substantial, but given that it was just me in the room, this was fine. All of the personnel are attentive and anxious to help. I wanted a ticket one night for a Shakespearean performance and the concierge managed to score one with no additional service charges tacked on and no "hotel fee" for booking it for me. This is a rarity. One afternoon I noted one of the personnel taking a beautiful display of Belgian chocolates on a plate to a room. I commented casually, "I wouldn't mind one of those in my room!" He asked for my room number and within minutes a complimentary chocolate platter decorated with lilies appeared. The hotel's cafe served spectacular breakfasts and its signature restaurant, "Kevin Taylor," is amazing. Every dish was perfection. We ordered a bottle of red wine that I still dream of. A warning: this place is not cheap. It is a classic example of getting what you pay for, so if you are up for a splurge, this is most definitely the place.

title: “Misleading hotel details”
text: My sister and I stayed at this hotel so we were near the airport for a early morning flight. The shuttle was only available on the hour and it was a van, so fortunately only 7 of us showed up for the shuttle at 6am - otherwise others would have been turned away. The details of the hotel indicate there is a coffee maker in the room, we did not have one and the room reeked of cigarette smoke even though I requested a non smoking room. The hotel details also indicate a business center which looked like one computer in the lobby, and when I asked about a printer to print our boarding passes, they didn't have one. There were so many other choices nearby, I would not stay here again. Granted, I could have gone back out to the desk and said I wanted a coffee maker and a different room, but was so tired I just wanted to go to bed, and I think when these items are clearly requested or shown as amenities, they should be provided. Period.

title: “Good location but quite noisy and feels a bit tired”
text:
I really couldn't fault the staff at this hotel - they were incredibly helpful and polite but not too 'in your face'.
The rooms are really big by NY standard and location is great for Broadway and the LES. I didn't go in the pool but that's a big bonus for summer.
I personally had a room with an adjoining door to another room and I could hear everything from the next room which I found a bit annoying. Everything from their shower to what they were talking about.
The rooms feel a bit dark and the space could be better laid out I think. Everything felt a bit dated compared to the other Thompson hotels I've stayed in.
Overall really good but not amazing! The staff made up for what the room lacked.

title: “Clean enjoyable but definately room for improvement.”
text: Stayed a few nights at Hotel Fusion. Great location, clean and does the job for a tourist who will be out for most of the day. A little bit of a funky smell, but goes away after a while. One thing is that the walls are paper thin, expect to hear many noises during your stay. But after all is said and done, the Hotel was a nice base for our trip, definately no Hilton or Marriott, but a decent boutique hotel.

title: “Brilliant Value for money, excellent location!”
text:
If you are looking for a down to earth, basic, friendly and clean hotel which is ideally located for everything you could possibly need/want then this is the one for you. 
The Comfort Inn provides a clean, comfy bed, nice shower and bath (although the warmth of the water dropped occasionally) lovely breakfast, helpful and friendly staff and tea and coffee by the entrance of the hotel (clever idea to prevent the need for drink facilities in the rooms). 
To be honest the rooms were dark and could possibly do with a refub but they were full of character and we really felt it didnt matter as we were there to get up at the crack of dawn and sightsee not spend the day in the hotel. All that mattered to us was a good night sleep and a breakfast to set us up for the day. 
All in all the hotel was exactly what we were personally looking for from a stay in New York. If you are wanting something other than a clean basic room then I would suggest to look elsewhere. :-)

title: “NYC 2011”
text:
We went to NYC specifically to see a broadway show (On a clear day you can see forever-Harry Connick Jr.-AMAZING).
I foolishly booked the tickets in July not realizing it was Thanksgiving (we're Canadian!) and also, black Friday (who knew?!?). We were pretty worried about cost and flights were already completely outrageous so we were suggested this hotel by a friend who lives in NYC but had never stayed there.
It was perfect-again, we don't care much about room size as we are barely in them but it was clean, had coffee for the morning and the staff were extremely accomodating for all things-luggage storage-directions-ideas-VERY friendly.
We ate at the restaurant as well which was a nice steak house with great service, and friendly staff as well. There's also a rooftop cocktail bar which was a nice option when we were tired. The cost was reasonable through hotels.com and I imagine it would be more so--on another weekend. We would stay there again for sure-it's located close to many things (we walked to Times Square and Central Park-which were pretty far but it is also close to 5th ave and other major landmarks). We took the subway as well which was cheap and quick. Try it, it's a nice little spot.

title: “A luxurious hotel with personality”
text:
My brother and I hadn't researched this hotel at all as it was a pick from priceline but we were really lucky.
Beds are super comfortable, the bathrobes were nicer than the ones you get from 5 star hotels, the internet is really fast, our room was really large and clean. We loved it. 
The staff were very nice and I think we were upgraded to a larger room.
We also thought the hotel's theming (prints on the wall, fabric of curtains and furnishings) had a classic American feel. As we are from Australia, the decor made the Madison stand out from the other hotels we stayed at during our holiday.

title: “Perfection Location, Fabulous Staff, Beautiful Hotel”
text: What can I say other than this hotel exceeded my expectations. The location of the hotel is great. I was a bit nervous due to the outside noise, but once I was in the hotel and also in my room I couldn't ear any of it. The staff was very friendly at check in and throughout my stay. Gave excellent restaurant referrals and was more than willing to secure us a reservations or transporation. The hotel was beautiful decorated. After staying at this intimate boutique hotel I now have a fondess for boutique hotels and will continue to stay at boutique hotels over large chain style hotels. I look forward to my next SF trip and will stay at the Galleria Park Hotel every time.

title: “PROTESTER ALERT!!!”
text: This hotel is very nice, but if you plan on sleeping in, don't stay here. A union, protesting the renovations, starts at 7:30AM and stops around 10:30AM. They scream, chant, and blow whistles in between those times and make the visit rather unpleasant. Unless you like seeing 2 giant inflatable rats in front of your hotel and all the noise, avoid at all costs.

author.location: New York, New York, United States

title: “Excellent, will stay again !!!”
text:
We stayed at the Grand Union at the end of March 2005 for 5 nights. Our first trip to New York, we picked the hotel after reading the reviews on TA. 
The hotel is in a excellent location and really good value for money. 
 We had to make 2 reservations (one for 2 nights & one for 3 nights) through two different companies as we couldn't get 5 nights in total with the same company. I called the hotel about a week before we due to arrive to double check they had a reservation for us (after reading one review on TA about someone having problems) and to advise them that we had booked via two companies and that we would prefer the same room if possible for the duration of our stay. The polite guy on reception located the reservations straight away so I didn't need to worry about the previous review. He said he would make a request on our reservations but wouldn't be able to guarantee the same room. 
 On arrival at the Grand Union reception told us we would need to check with them after our 2nd night if we could have the same room again for the further 3 nights. Unfortunately we couldn't keep the same room but this wasn't a problem for us. We left our luggage in the secure left luggage room until our room was ready later in the day. We were told we were 
moving to nicer (recently decorated) room for the remainder of our stay. 
Couldn't fault the staff, they were always polite & cheerful. 
ROOMS - Very clean and comfortable. 
All en-suite - no need to share a bathroom
The 1st room didn't have a lot of spare floor space, enough room at the end of the bed for 1 suitcase on the rack but our other suitcase we had by the side of the bed and one of us had to step over it. But the plus point was the bathroom was bigger than the second room. The bathroom in the first room had a bath with a shower overhead. 
The 2nd room had loads of floor space (by this time we had 3 large suitcases after all that shopping) and there was plenty of room and no need to step over any of them. But we found the bathroom a lot smaller with a shower cubicle only no bath. The shower cubicle is however on the small side, I was ok as I'm very small. This room was also located at the front of the hotel, 9th floor and we never found the street to be noisey at night.
I will attach photos in a couple of days
Hotel has free safety deposit boxes which are in the office behind reception. 
The hotel is in a excellent location with one of the 33rd street subway entrances a few yards away. The Empire State building was only a few minutes walk away, en-route there is a good bagel shop to get breakfast or lunch. 
Hope you enjoy your stay as much as we did. We will return to the Grand Union.

title: “Newer Property”
text:
We have stayed in some rough Holiday Inns lately. So it was much to our delight to find a newer property (3 -4 years old). The lobby has a huge mosaic waterfall wall. The rooms were updated nicely. Ours had a dead fly here and there and dead lady beetles, but at least they were dead. The bed was clean and comfortable. They used to give Holiday In Priority members a discounted breakfast, but that has gone by the wayside these days.
After the Red Roof Inn at this exit disgusted us with their filthy rooms, we were glad to find clean and updated accommodations. 
Their business center looked nice, but they had the access locked and no way to get online.

title: “we love this place.”
text: We are here every year and we love it. So close to the ocean and not overprized. We will recommend this hotel for people who love the beach but dont want to pay 300 dollars a night . Also great pool and nice people.

title: “You should occupy Wall Street”
text:
We arrived at 6 PM on A Sunday night, in time for the wine and snacks which are free. They had Walnuts, olives and cookies in addition to water and ice tea. The cookies made no sense with the rest of the spread, where some cheese would have made it much more harmonious;
I would have much preferred no snacks in the room, in exchange. That is the only thing that was less than stellar in this review. We booked the lowest priced King room, and were amazingly pleased. The room was plenty large, the shower and bath were huge, the lighting, window shade and night light all controlled from the wall next to the bed. Non alchoholic drinks were free in the fridge, and the aforementioned snack of chips, and healthy bars were in the room too. On the 10th floor we were very quiet, heard a few garbage trucks as day light neared, but no big deal. The location was right next to the subway, close to Fulton Market, and the Brooklyn Bridge which we biked across. TIP: Around the corner was Stone Street, which was a 5 minute walk. The street is closed to traffic (until Nov 30) and there were numerous pubs, pizza and Mexican restaurants. We ate family style on one of the many picnic tables set up outside, lots of fun, on a warm October night. Service was laid back but very pleasant very and accommodating. Parking next door was $44 for our minivan for 24 hours with the voucher supplied by Andaz. When I picked up the car, I saw the price listed on the parking fee sign, said $46 for up to 24 hours, so I am not sure why I was told by the hotel and Imperial Parking that the cost would have been $64 without the voucher. The protesters were blocks away and never a factor in any way, don't let them sway you from going Andaz. All in all this way was 9.5 out of 10, and compared to another hotel I previously rated on Madison Ave ( which I liked) this was a step above, and a better value even though a continental breakfast was fee there, but not here,

title: “Not worth it..”
text: I agree with the review before me. This is not a 4-star hotel. Don't get me wrong, there was not much wrong with it. However, nothing really "wowed" us. The rooms were average, customer service, average. Pretty much the only thing that made me upset was that you actually had to PAY to use the business center. It deffinately wasn't worth what I paid for at this hotel.

title: “Staggeringly good!”
text:
This is an absolutely incredible hotel. Very modern and really eye catching.
We had an offer to upgrade to junior suites - brilliant rooms with a (distant ) view of the Hollywood sign. The bathroom was excellent and the shower superb. Spotelssly clean everywhere.
The hotel had a very very cool feel to it. Very modern decor. It is opposite the Beverly Centre and lots of local food nearby. If you stay here - check out the Concierge desk - wow!!
Excellent and huge gym. Didn't eat here - so cant comment on food. Free iMacs to use in the Lobby! Staff and service very impressive. Parking a bit expensive but valet system worked really well.
One of the best hotels ever - just really good fun. Heartily recommend and a definite for a return trip. Would not consider anything else.

title: “It was about average....”
text: Just returned from 3 days at the Bayside; was there for conference, so decided to stay for convenience. Room was on 3rd floor above conference floors; it was very clean and comfortable, altho the entryway and bathroom areas were abit cramped. Restaurant on premises was abit pricey, but because there is nothing very close by, you are a 'captive audience'. Food was pretty good; as part of Holiday Inn's "Rewards"-type program, I received a $20 off breakfast (per day) coupon, which came in very handy! Pizza Nova across the street was tasty; try their lunch special (pizza or pasta and a salad). Otherwise, can be abit pricey, but beautiful view of the marina. Further up a block, is Point Loma Seafood. The most beautiful fresh fish I have ever seen! They have a 'sushi bar' which will make some selections for you to enjoy on the patio, plus they have seafood to order to takeout. Nothing fancy, but it was packed at lunch! They have fish, clams, shrimp, crab, calamari, etc., of which you can have in a sandwich, on a platter, in a salad, or in a taco, with sides of fried, onion rings, cole slaw, etc. Had the Boston chowder in a breadbowl for lunch, then walked back for a calamari plate dinner. Fresh, tender calamari strips were delicious! And, for less than $9.00, a great deal! Had I known this was so close, I would have come the previous day and tried more on the menu. They also have smoked fish that you can have on a sandwich or buy to take with you. We heard the line is out the parking lot at lunchtime and I believe it! Well worth the trip tho, IMO. Propertywise, the Bayside is finishing up some upgrades; i didn't see/use the pool or putting green. Staff is very friendly and helpful. Pluses? Free shuttle to airport, $20 off breakfast (Rewards club perk), great staff. Minuses? Pricey coffee shop on premises, rooms abit small. Would I return? Yes, but I would checkout their sister property nearby at Humphrey's.

title: “Simply the best place to stay while in Seattle!”
text: This was my second stay at this hotel. I enjoyed it as much as the first time. The service is excellent. They have the finest staff, everyone is professional, friendly, and made us feel very welcome. The rooms are large, comfortable, and spotlessly clean, clean, clean. Our full breakfast was fantastic - great for my teenage boys. I was able to keep up on my business with the wireless internet in my room, while I still enjoyed a relaxing get away with some sightseeing also. The location was perfect to enjoy Seattle - everything was close and easy to get to. I will be back.

title: “great location, great value,clean.”
text:
Stayed here September 2012 for sight seeing in the city. Ideal location less than 5mins from Union square. Rooms a good size, great big comfy bed. Bath, shower ok, It is basic but ideal as a base to see the city.
Free coffee in the lounge with dougnuts in the morning. 
Come out entrance and turn left and walk down to Lauries diner for breakfast. American retro diner, food amazing. A two minute walk!
Would stay here again, had a great time in a great city.

title: “friendly, classy & convienent”
text: The staff was very friendly and the rooms were very clean comfortable & cool, with a fresh woodsy smell when we came in from outside. Nice!!

title: “Great stay, excellent value!”
text: If you're not looking for anything fancy, this really is a great hotel at a great price. My 13-year old daughter and I stayed for 3 nights, and I'd highly recommend it. The location couldn't be better - close to everything. We always felt safe, even though it was just the two of us, even while walking back to the hotel at night from a nearby Broadway show one night and from Top of the Rock another. The staff was exceptionally friendly and helpful. The free breakfast was really good, and two of the three mornings we stayed, there was someone in the lobby standing by to make sure everything was stocked and that guests had everything they needed. Sure, the place is small, but so are most NYC hotels, and how much are you in the room other than when you're sleeping? The room was very clean, with ample space for the two of us and our luggage. A computer with internet access and printer was available in the lobby for a small fee, which was helpful since we were able to print our boarding passes for our return flight. The only negatives I can think of are that it's a bit noisy (lots of sirens since there's a nearby fire station), but hey, it's New York, right? Also, the elevator is old and not the fastest thing around, but was perfectly functional. Overall, a real value. We definitely would stay again

title: “Wonderful stay”
text:
We stayed here 3 nights from 27th July to 30th July. Our flight was delayed due to the stormy weather but what great customer service from the minute our taxi pulled up the hotel. The staffs were polite at all levels. Location was convenient.
At our request, the room was quiet on a higher level. We used the bar for late evening snack and the food was good. Location was convenient.
Improvements: I would like to have a coffeemaker in the room. An offer of "to go" coffee was a nice gesture in the morning but I would like to have the convenience of making my own hot drink beside coffee. In the evening when they came to turn down the bed, they provided us with a small (12 fl oz) bottle of Evian water for my husband & I to share. Can they not afford a bottle of water for each guest?

title: “Omni at Independence Park”
text: We visited this location at the beginnning of August 2012. Due to the shortness of our stay I did not get to experience all the hotel had to offer and as such have held my rating only to very good. But, as to those amenities we made use of, I can say this grand older hotel still has all the luxury you would expect of such a fine establishment.The customer service and amenities at the hotel speak for themselves. Further, the hotel was within easy walking distance to restraunts, exhibits and national parks. I would warn there is little to no parking in the area so plan on going the valet parking route. Otherwise, go, stay and enjoy.

title: “Very pleased with service!”
text: The rooms are clean, staff friendly and helpful, breakfast was good, convenient to trains, Michigan ave, restaurants. Will definitely stay again.

title: “Small but tastefull and friendly”
text: Spent five nights and were very happy with top to bottom service, cleaniness and decor including in the breakfast area. For a small hotel, everything is nicely laid out and fresh cookies in the lobby every afternoon was a great touch.

title: “A real find! Service like the Ritz but a fraction of the price!”
text: My 12 yr old son and I came into town for his first Bears game and i noted from other reviewers to request something special to commemorate this first. Right after we arrived a jr Bears football and a #1 fan glove appeared at our door. Needless to say this was the start of a great stay - any question, the staff handled as if you were a friend staying in theri house... 'i would like to locate a blackberry charger"... the front desk specialist - here, borrow mine - I"m here until 11". We really felt taken care of in a new large city. The accomodations are first rate, value is terrific and i ditto the other reviewers on the breakfast - nice surprise - again, feeling like you are staying at someone's home. Stay and enjoy. The view and location are not special - but you are right in the middle of things which overrides the immediate surroundings.

title: “Great hotel!”
text:
The location is excellent, within walking distance of lots of stuff, and several subway stations. If you look real close, you _might_ be able to tell that this building is old. Indeed, they have done a really nice job at making everything look both nice and modern. The rooms are definitely well maintained and well designed. If you get above the 30th floor or so, the views, especially of the Park, are really nice. There is a rooftop pool (which I didn't discover until the final day) which might be really good for some vacation exercise. The elevators were slightly rickety, but not so much as to feel unsafe, and they had monitors that were constantly playing Tom and Jerry; someone told us that this was to get people to look up into the security camera. The downstairs restaurant was quite good, and the breakfasts were especially yummy. The bar was small, but with a nice, dark ambiance. In general, the service was great. There was one of the employees at the concierge desk who was rude, in that she spoke to us like we were back-woods yokels. Otherwise, the concierge service was great; they even got us a reservation at Nobu on 57th.
Overall, an excellent experience.

title: “Nice Hotel, But Lots of Extra Charges”
text:
We had a renovated room which was spacious, nicely decorated, and very clean. Beds were extremely comfortable, bath was small but clean with tile bath and granite counter top. As noted elsewhere, the location is terrific. Only complaint was all the extra charges, we definitely felt like we were being nickeled and dimed at every turn. Almost $50 for parking per day, $50 to use the gym (!), $3.50 per bag to check your bags - and coats/jackets each count as a bag. We did encounter some delays for elevator, but not nearly as long as other people have noted here - perhaps hotel was not full when we visited. Make sure you mention that you're Hilton Honors when making a reservation and ask for a renovated room.
 We found the lobby to be odd, with almost no seating except for a couple of circular seating areas around the busy registration area. For such a huge hotel, there was no comfortable area to sit, and no areas that were laid out for people wanting to have a conversation, or to read or wait to meet others. Almost like lobby was planned to force people to use lounge area if they want to sit or meet people, and feel compelled to purchase drinks.
 Would still recommend this hotel if you could reserve a renovated room. Just be aware that some perks that are offered for free at other hotels will cost you here.

title: “Superb Location and a really laid back atmosphere”
text:
Firstly, to echo other reviews, this place is an upscale motel, and not a true B&B or hotel. If you go stay here expecting the full American B&B treatment, then you will be disappointed. 
We paid $99 dollars a night for the Aruba room for two nights, and for San Diego that's cheap even by motel standards. Considering what we paid, we thought this place was fantastic! 
Location wise, this place is just a few minutes stroll from the entrance to San Diego Zoo (best zoo in the world in my opinion), and a short drive from Hillcrest and other sites...it's also close enough to the freeway to get to Seaworld easily.
The room itself was small but came with a huge bathroom with a great jetted tub, and an outside table to enjoy the motel's enclosed and secluded courtyard. Breakfast was simple, but served to our door each morning at the time we specified. We thought the 'aquatic' theme in the room (cuddly toy fishes dangling on strings from the ceiling!?), and the colourful courtyard were both really fun! And most importantly, everything was totally clean.
Okay, so some of the flowers in the courtyard are plastic, and the room themes are a little over the top...but we thought this just added to the fun of the place...it doesn't take itself too seriously, which makes for a great place to just relax. The owners have obviously gone to a lot of effort...it's just that it might not be to everyone's taste.
I'd definitely recommend this as a great place to stay, provided that over-the-top room themes make you laugh rather than cringe. And one final thing...we were recommended a local diner by the lady at the front desk, and I had possibly the best burger ever there...it's called Brian's and it's just a few blocks from the Inn.

title: “Awesome location, friendly staff, loved it”
text: This is a GREAT central location, right around the corner from the Copley T stop, great Back Bay location close to wide variety of shops, restaurants from cheap eats to super chic, and easy subway access to everything else. Cannot say enough about the wonderful staff at this location. Breakfast was good, too, if you get it included. Rooms also had a refrigerator, which was great for saving a little $$ on meals.

title: “Nice but not nice enough”
text: Was disappointed to find out they only use a comforter on the beds and no flat sheets however we were able to request a flat sheet. There was a room service tray with left over food in the hallway left all day and still there on the morning we checked out.The halls smelled like adhesive during the day from the work they were doing in the rooms. The bathrooms were large and clean but poor water pressure in the shower. The navigator/ concierge service was helpful. It was nice to be able to access wifi at no charge from the starbucks in the lobby. Is very close to an excellent restaurant Tamarind and to bus stops.

title: “Pleasant hotel”
text: Friendly staff, spacious an dclean rooms. Breakfast was a bit disappointing. Location is good for exploring Chicago.

title: “Nice Location”
text: We stayed 4 nights and overall found the hotel comfortable, clean and the staff accomodating. We arrived about 1/2 hour prior to 3pm check in and took the chance to see if our room was ready. It wasn't. So we figured we'd wait in the lobby/walk around until the room was ready. Instead, front desk suggested we pre-register, go to the mall across the freeway and they'd call when our room was ready. The front desk staff seemed a little surprised that we asked to have our luggage held until our room was ready. Front desk called after 4pm. I was surprised and a little disappointed that for checking in on a Tuesday they weren't ready on time. But more surprised that they didn't apologize for the delay or have an explanation. They did forget our request to be on the non-freeway side, but quickly re-assigned us when I confirmed our room location. The view from the back side of the property is a lush hillside filled with trees, bushes, and flowers. It was pleasant to look at. The "heavenly beds" they advertise have great pillows and a comfy duvet, though I wouldn't describe the mattress as heavenly in comfort...just average. The room was nicely furnished and clean. I did like the solid bench to put the suitcases on rather than those rickety strappy stands many hotels have. Housekeeping did a great job. My daughter enjoyed finding her stuffed animals creatively arranged on the bed everyday. I agree with the reviewer about the carpets. A shampooing wouldn't hurt. There were plenty of hangers, an ironing board and iron in the closet. I thought all Sheraton's had robes, but this one did not. I also was surprised there was no in-room safe as the reservationist had confirmed. The water pressure was great, but a taller shower head would have been nice. Why do hotels think guests are 5 feet tall? We had one maintenance issue that was promptly addressed and resolved. The tub took 20 mins to drain. When making the reservation, I asked if the hotel was kid-friendly or more "business" based and told it was kid-friendly. Based on our time there, we saw only one other family with a child. While we weren't shunned, the suit crowd was more the norm. We liked the restaraunt. The food was good and the service prompt. It was disappointing that there was no kid's menu. The server was very understanding and accomodating in getting us a kid friendly cheese crisp and some fruit for our pre-schooler. He indicated they are working on developing a kid menu. We enjoyed the pool and spa. There were plenty of towels and lounge chairs. There is a little shop on property for sundries. The woman staffing it was very friendly. There were many family friendly restaurants nearby and the location of the hotel made it very easy to get to/from the airport, Sea World, Legoland, and the Zoo. We also appreciated having the Target store across the freeway to stock up on bottled water and snacks to take to the attractions. Overall, the hotel was nice and all but one or two people were extremely good to us. We were told that they have only been a Sheraton for 2 months, so maybe they are still working on the Sheraton level of service in a few areas?

title: “Guess we got lucky”
text: I read all the reviews after I booked the hotel and I kept thinking my husband and I were gong to be staying at a real dump. Not the case at all. Our king, non-smoking room on the 8th floor was clean and spacious. Yes, the room and fixtures could have used some updating, but this is an older hotel in Philadelphia. The room was clean, we had no problems with plumbing, and did have a room right around the corner from the elevators and were not bothered by them in the least. We went to Philly for the weekend to explore the city and had a fabulous time. The girls at the front desk were friendly and polite, as was the bell-hop. We did not use his services but spoke to him and he was great. We had no problem whatsoever with this hotel. The only unpleasant experiences we had were at the restaurants throughout the city. The waitresses are always in such a rush to get your order. We had just walked into Campos deli and were barked at to order before we had a chance to look at a menu. (there was nobody else waiting) Also, at Downeys, the waitress there did not seem to understand English very well and was in a rush for us to order a dinner after we ordered drinks and an appetizer. She made us feel so uncomfortable we opted not to stay for the bargain $16.95 2 lb. lobsters. Our best dining experience was at Dinardo's Famous Crabs. The jumbo hard-shell crabs my husband ordered were to die for and I ordered the sauteed soft-shell crab special which was fantastic. The waitress here was top-notch also. The others could use a lesson from her. Overall, we had a great time in Philadelphia, the Holiday Inn was just fine.

title: “Nice ....Getaway”
text: lots of hotels to choose from in the area..but liked this one...valet on top of their game, front desk..early check in..no problem..all the staff speak when passing..in the elevator etc..room was clean, and comfortable ..the included am coffee and pm wine ( lobby)are crowd pleasers ...out the door there is plenty in walking distance..cafes, shops ( new and consigments, sephora, southmoon under..etc...drug store..and if you really dont mind you can walk a little further and catch macys, city hall, liberty bell etc..just depends on you... i went for the musuems and am very pleased that i narrowed down to this hotel..even short trips are heavily influenced by where you temporarily lay your head and the Palomar..is a nice home away from home..ill be back

title: “Excellent Location”
text: The rooms in the hotel are a little tired, however the location is fab. 10 mins to Times Squre and 15 to Empire State. Great as a base for families or couples during a short stay in NY. If you want to do as much as you can during your stay get the New York pass, you can buy this from Planet Hollywood in Times Square, good value for money if you want to do lots and queue jumping so great in high season.

title: “Great value for the location”
text:
We chose to stay here after reading the previous reviews. It was a great location right down by the wharf and to get that with free parking...awesome! It's definitely not fancy but is clean, provided our basic needs and we felt safe. There is no blowdryer in the room but you can request one from the front desk which I did. There is free coffee/tea/hot chocolate at the front desk. Any staff we came into contact with were pleasant and helpful. 
We were able to leave our car and walk to Pier 39 (lots of shops) and if you have AAA/CAA, stop into the Welcome Center and ask for your coupon book. Pier 33 is where the Alcatraz tours leave from and that is also within walking distance. There are lots of restaurants around and we enjoyed eating at the Boudin Bakery which is a very short walk from the hotel. You can also watch them making the bread. Something else we came upon by chance while walking along Pier 45 by the WWll submarine and WWll Liberty Ship is a musuem of mechanical machines that has free admission. Check that out if you have time...we had loads of fun in there. You do have to pay a quarter or so for each machine you want to use.

title: “Vine & Melrose”
text:
I spent 4 days there and liked the area of Melrose and Rossmore, just across from Hancock Park, Larchmont Village and next door to the Pavillions market. There were good inexpensive restaurants around the corner on Melrose and the location was convenient for driving, not far from Wilshire Museums and the Grove and walkable to Hollywood and Highland via Cole which runs parallel to Vine. Paramount Studios is walkable east on Melrose past Larchmont.
The room had been refurbished and for the price it was a good deal when traveling alone on a budget.

title: “Trendy Hotel with lots of restaurants and shops within walking distance”
text: My husband and I stayed in a Jr. Suite for our anniversary. The hotel sent up a bottle of champagne on the house. The room was very clean and had a great view. We were on the 9th floor but could still hear the live band in the bar on the main floor. When we checked out the front desk suggested that we ask for a quiet room next time. That was our only issue. The continental breakfast that was included was terrific - fresh pastries and a wide assortment of fresh fruits and berries, plus juices, coffees and teas. I would highly recommend this hotel. Also had free wifi in room and throughout the hotel plus a 24 hour business center with free computers and printer.

title: “Nicest people in DC”
text: The Helix is my home away from home when I'm in Washington. I've had the opportunity to stay there many times over the past five years and have always been comfortable and enjoyed my visit. The staff couldn't be more friendly and helpful, and make me feel like each visit is my first and needs to be made special. I like the free wine bar. The location is very convenient to all of downtown DC. The rooms are clean, comfortable, and quiet.

title: “The Name says it all:Standard is right on the money, but very trendy/cool if your 20 something”
text:
My husband & I booked this hotel in conjunction with spending the day at the LA Film Fest which was very close by. First of all we could not find this hotel easily since its in an office building that looks like just that-an old, bland office building. After finally finding it, we were told they were farther away from the Staples Center than we thought. Valet is $30.00, plus we would have to take a cab or drive & pay for parking as well unless you take a shuttle, which we never saw. That is downtown LA: Parking costs are HIGH.
After spending the day at the Film Fest we went back to The Standard, looked around & then went to our room. We found a ping pong table in the lobby next to the elevators & a lobby that is truly (not made to look it) from the 60-70''s & obviously is in an office building that was never updated. A fuze ball table + firepit are in the frontage area/parking lot. Bright pink modern furnishings light up a nearly totally dark lobby & an empty, but cool looking bar finishes it off. There was some cool stuff there & I had hopes for a nice room to match. There is an escalator that leads up from there, but we never checked it out since young people were sort of running around the area on top. The rooftop pool area sounds like its a happening p,lace, but we were very tired from the Fest. So, we ordered very late night room service which was good & not crazy expensive. One BIG gripe I have is after my husband asked for ice with our meal, so we could have ice water, the person taking orders told him its down the hall & in essence to get it himself with the ice bucket from our room. Before calling him back myself we looked for an ice bucket. Finding none & being outraged that Room Service, at any hotel, would basicly say "get it yourself" I called to give the kitchen a piece of my mind. I got a nervous response after saying "do you mean to tell me you don't have ice in your big kitchen down there??" that they do but "do not have ice buckets to bring it in." I told him to bring 2 glasses full of ice & hung up. Thats all we wanted & what he should have asked about when it was requested. I guess 20 somethings are willing to put up with allot of BS from hotel staff, but trust me when I say that 40 somethings spending their $$$$ do not & know paying to get food delivered to you whenever, getting a comfortable, clean & hopefully plush feeling & clean feeling atmosphere in which to spend their 24 short hours (its acutually less when you add up the hours you pay for) is what we are paying for and expect. without any excuses. If there are issues in the hotel...take it up with the boss, otherwise I don't want to hear excuses. When you check in, the face that checks you in & welcomes you should reflect joy that you picked his or her employers hotel for your expensive night away from home. We didn't get that & when we don't get that we don't go back & we spread the word...period. What happend to high standards in the U.S.??
The rooms: are sort of Star Trekky. Walls are bright white with a mod vibe. The bed is on a platform & the blanket smelled very, very strongly of smoke. Without it I would have been cold or I would have removed it abonded it to the furthest point away from us. In fact, the whole hotel smells of smoke & after complaining about it the next day were told their clientele is mainly European & they have only partially non-smoking floors, which to me is sort of point less since smoke travels. So, this place is no good for those who want smoke free environments in which to breath in:( No msoking laws don't apply to hotel rooms...I learned something new. There is a 70's feel here, especially in the breakfast room that is BRIGHT yellow & screams WAKE-Up! I expected Doris Day to be sitting around the corner. 
We were curious about this place because we saw "Get Him To The Greek" & it was near our key location. My curiousity is over & I we were happy to leave. In fact, I entertained the idea of leaving & not sleeping there at all, even if we were charged for the night. The smoke smell is gross, the cleaning solution the maids use is really strong & really bad-like oven cleaner that you smell when walking down the halls. They are definaltey not using eco-friendly products here, which I sincerely wish they would change. The street noise of buses goes on all night. I didn't even shower (a first for me) before leaving this hotel in the AM, since the bathroom seem like the rest of the hotel...which is don't look too closely, you may not like what you find.

title: “Huge Rooms”
text:
My husband and our 2 teenage boys stayed at the Windsor Suites this past weekend. The location is very convenient on Benjamin Franklin PWY and 18th street. It was a quick walk to the Science Museum a bit of a hike to the Art Museum and easy access to Reading Terminal. Cabs were quick and easy. Not more than $7 anywhere we went. We had no reason to move the car. The only down side to the location is the very busy street. It is a little loud at night.
The suite is HUGE. I am not sure why there is so much closet space, but everyone can have their own private dressing room (or recording studio, which my husband set up). Our room was in sad need of new furniture. The living room furniture was ratty. Falling apart with cushion you had trouble get out of. The sleep sofa was pretty uncomfortable, but we also got a cot and doubled up on the matresses. My son also found a half eaten Reeses cup in the bed. I understand they are slowly rennovating, so request a rennovated room. We had a patio which was fun to stand out on. The AC worked great which was a great relief given the 93 degree temp outside at night. The shower had very little water pressure.
There is a full kitchen which was very clean. Only one pot, but plenty of dishes. 
The people at the desk were very nice. I had spoken to the manager after I say a "manager's special" on the website and got an even cheaper rate inculding parking, so it is worth a call.
The space worked out great for us and we would definitely recommend it for a family.

title: “Good location and value”
text: Stayed here on Dec 2, 2008. Very nice property in downtown. Room was a little tight, but it was just me. If I was travelling with spouse or kids the room would have been small. They also offer a free dinner and breakfast. I skipped the dinner and hit the Cheesecake factory a few blocks away. Hotel is right next to the convention center. Fitness center is very nice. Very clean and newer equipment.

title: “Disaster”
text:
The staff was not helpful. The offer complimentary Keurig coffee. It was broken when we got there - no big deal - but it was still out of order in the morning. We asked the staff - and nothing happened. The right thing to do would have been to remove the coffee service. In this case, they raised our expectations and never followed through. A quality hotel would have provided coffee from their bar or kitchen. Instead, we had to go out. The irons in the room blew the circuit and we had to call maintenance. The floor AC units are not hooked to a hose so they shut off overnight since the water bucket filled up. There is a night club across the street and it is very noisy. 
We had a self-inflicted problem with the original reservation and they did not help us at all.
Overall, miserable end to a TERRIFIC vacation......
Th

title: “great location”
text: great location and very helpfull staff clean rooms and close to six flags, about 20 minutes from downtown highly recommended

title: “I LOVE SOHO GRAND HOTEL!!! ;)”
text:
Hello there,
I stayed at Soho Grand one time but it was a fantastic experience. The room was very noisy the first day so I asked to change the room and they gave me one at the 15th floor with great views. All staff was very nice and helpful so I left good tips ;) I am going back in January and have booked it again there.
Relation quality - price: Excellent.

title: “Central property, great value for money”
text:
Great customer service. Extremely friendly from the minute we walked in, to offering us some bottled water for our long drive ahead on exit.
Big rooms, yes they're not the swankiest but remember, this is the Embassy Suites. Staff quickly put together our sofabed and crib for my kids. This means a lot when you have tired, jetlagged children.
Decent buffet breakfast with a large area to sit. There is also a good cafe at the front of the hotel. 
Valet parking is expensive. On Sunday you can park opposite for free and round the corner is a cheaper carpark for overnight.
If you want a suite in the heart of downtown Fort Worth, I highly recommend staying here.

title: “Loved this place!!”
text: Great location and great views :) The kids really loved the slide at the pool! I also liked how they had a special kid menu for room service! I liked how the hotel had an Einsteins Bagel company attached

title: “Very nice”
