text: As a business traveler, I am tired of the 4 walls of hotel rooms. This hotel has a very nice buffet/TV/Social area to feel a little more at home and talk to other people that are non customers. The breakfasts were great and evening socials were an unexpected surprise. Light meal with beer and wine. Very nice. Staff friendly and accommodating. Nice little store area for snacks, ice cream, and microwave meals if you need it. Computers in lobby for boarding pass printing.

title: “Nice get away...worth the cost”
text: Our experience was wonderful. The staff was very attentive. The view from our room was amazing; it was a nice treat for a special occasion. Some things were "overpriced," but it is NYC! Room was very comfortable and clean.

title: “Best location, Value, Service in Chicago”
text:
You never know when you are booking a hotel from online if it will be as good as you hope, near what you need, in good condition, etc. I traveled to Chicago with my daughters (ages 7 & 8) and my mom for a special birthday weekend for my daughters to American Girl. When I travel to Chicago in the future, I will ALWAYS stay at this hotel. 
It was very easy to get to from the interstate (just exit the interstate and one left turn, then you are there). This is definitely what you like when traveling to such a busy city as Chicago. From the moment we arrived, we were treated like we were the Embassy Suite's most VIP guest. Just to have parking was fabulous. A bellhop came down to the parking garage for us to unload the vehicle (no small feat when traveling with little girls who feel the need to bring everything they can think of), he patiently waited for us to check in, then took us to our room and unloaded everything. Check in went very smoothly. We were slightly earlier than the beginning of check-in (about 2pm) so we had no lines. The rooms were typical of what you expect with an Embassy Suites...very clean with the living and bedroom area separate. Plenty of room for the kids to spread out and play. We were particularly pleased to be set off on the end room of a hallway. 
Service, Service, Service. Our first night we had dinner reservations at American Girl Place and needed a cab. The hotel usually has cabs sitting out front waiting, but this night they were gone. The wonderful night door man worked very hard to get us a cab. He walked down the block and across the street to hail the cab, then rode with the cab to stop in front where we were waiting to ensure we got it (because while he had been trying to hail a cab, several other people came out to wait for cabs). In my opinion, he went above and beyond! This is the type of service we received throughout our stay. The concierge was extremely helpful with directions and dinner reservations. I liked how he called and worked out reservations to get us exactly what we needed plus gave us a card with all of the restaurant information, location, number, and the name of the person who confirmed the reservation.
The location...couldn't be better. We could walk anywhere and had lots of choices for restaurants. If we didn't want to walk, the cab ride for wherever we want was only $5. On the corner of the hotel block, there was a Starbucks. Every morning I would get coffee for my mom and I. Loved the convenience. There is a coffee maker in the room, but it only makes 2 cups of coffee. Not a problem since Starbucks was right there.
The main reasons I selected this hotel before staying there were the location, the price, the breakfast in the morning, the room size, and the fact it had a pool for the kids to use. After staying here, the number one top reason why I would stay is Service. You can't go wrong with this hotel regardless of if you are traveling for a family trip, business trip, or for a romantic get a way.

title: “Fabulous”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel in Jan with my sister in law. I can not fault the hotel or its staff. Our room was fantastic (junior suite) so there was plenty of room for 2 girls to get ready. Everything about the hotel was fabulous and the word of the weekend was 'opulent'
The staff were always very helpful from check in staff to doormen, only down side was lots of tipping. Can highly recommend the Champagne Afternoon Tea in the Cocktail Terrace Bar to really soak up the New York atmosphere.

title: “Awesome Hotel and Location”
text:
I stayed here the 1st weekend in March and enjoyed a unsually warm SF weekend. The hotel is extremely clean and in a great location. It is within walking distance to the new shopping mall, Union Square, Moscone, SOMA district, museums and Chinatown.
There is a small indoor pool, nice courtyard on the lower level, along with a restaurant and Starbucks. Everyone working at the hotel was very nice. Valet parking is $40 per day, in a covered garage. Worth the fee since parking is difficult to find in the area. 
I would stay here again next time I visit SF, especially since the price is so reasonable!

title: “Nice hotel close to the Gas Lamps area”
text: Nice renovation of an old building, The furnishing and decor were contemporary with a nice comfortable bed. The location is close to the Gas Lamps area but without the nighttime noise that some of my colleagues experienced in other hotels. Internet access worked much better than at most hotels I stay at. My one criticism is the lack of breakfast, as the restaurant did not open until lunch time.

title: “Great Location, Quiet and Comfortable”
text: My husband and I decided to do a quick get away in NYC. We chose this location because they had the best nightly rate for the weekend. We like the HIlton brand, and also really love the cookies that Doubletree provides. The room was large for a NYC room, bed comfortable. The hotel is in the midst of a renovation, so I suspect furniture in our room was on the newer side. If there was one downfall,it would have been the size of the bathroom. it was a bit tight. It took a long time for the steam to leave, and after a shower, the ceiling dripped with condensation. However, the staff was super nice and accomodating, and I would defintely stay there again. Also, it is very close to the subway, and makes it easy to get anywhere in the city.

title: “Pleasant Surprise”
text:
I had not previously stayed at the brand but was very pleasantly surprised. The facility as well as the rooms were very clean, modern and comfortable. The roomm was roomy with many amenetes.
The staff was very pleasant and helpful

title: “Better than expected...there is room for improvement”
text: The staff was extremely nice. An inviting lobby and unbeatable location. The room was of a decent size for New York and nicely appointed with a brand new LCD, complimentary high speed internet, comfortable "sleep number" bed, good linens and work chair. The bathroom was tiny but.. we are in NYC... Direct access to a diner type place called Raffles which has excelent service for breakfast. Also direct access to a walk through Starbucks.. It beat my expectations but apparently not every room is so new. Make sure you get a renovated room.

title: “Bonjour. High end hotel.”
text:
Nice rooms great service at a price. At this price point somewhat irritating was: no in room coffee facilities, nice gym but in windowless location, 
Strange to be greeted in french by mostly non french people. Somewhat conceited methinks! Vive la France.
Unless youre a sofitel fan suggested 11th in Chicago at time of writing is exaggerated.
D

title: “not too bad”
text: I recently stayed here for 1 night to take an medical board exam in Seattle. The location is not bad--it's in an area full of other budget hotels and self-park lots--a bit sketchy at night. But it's walkable to the main downtown area including the waterfront, convention center and the Space Needle. The front desk was friendly, and the room itself is what you expect for a budget hotel. The room was pretty quiet, although my room facing Seventh Avenue heard some ambulances, loud cars, etc at night. The water pressure is good in the shower. The bed was fine. The room was adequately cleaned with plenty of towels. Overall, not bad for the price--Downtown Seattle is full of more expensive options. If I was traveling on a budget in Seattle, I would probably stay here again.

title: “Outstanding hotel with an exceptional restaurant”
text:
I usually enjoy staying at a Sofitel but this one is great. the beds are terrific and they have a great selection of pillows. The building is modern and looks great and the area is surrounded by restaurants and bars so there is plenty to do.
The great part here is the restaurant for dinner. I usually never bother with hotel restaurants for dinner but viewing the menu made me think twice. The food was outstanding and the service in the restaurant was also outstanding. Highly recommended.

title: “Loved the Comfort Inn”
text:
We were very happy with our stay at the Comfort Inn. The people were very friendly. The room was small but very clean and comfortable. The hotel is located close to the theater district. A great location. 
I would highly recommend this hotel for anyone that is coming to NYC. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “So disappointed”
text: Where to begin..Arrived to this "pet friendly" hotel to be questioned about having my yorkie in tow..?? Staff member said, 'ok she can go ahead and stay'..?? Got to 1st room- AC not working, trash on floor, used rag in bathroom, soap open, blood on towel..!!! Complained to very friendly staff, moved our family- child and baby included, to another room.. Which had empty beer cans on balcony and dirty night stands and sticky floors:/ oh, the hallway floors were stained with black residue and hotel reaked of smoke:///

title: “HIghs and Lows - Service is Everything in My Book”
text:
The Lows: I stayed at this hotel with my family from 12/3/09 through 12/7/09. We arrived @ 3:00 a.m. (about 3 hrs late) because of a flight delay ...which led to delays at every other step along the way. We were greeted immediately by someone from valet parking. He asked if we wanted valet parking and my husband said, "I am not sure...give me a second to think." Needless to say, we were functioning at less than top speed at this point. At this response, he promptly disappeared....back into his valet office/room & away from the cold. He did not ask if we wanted a bellman....which we definitely did. I went inside to check in while my husband unloaded the car...expecting a bellman to appear at any minute. By the time we were checked in, my husband had brought all of our bags inside so we began looking for a cart. We found one and loaded our bags on it...right in front of the valet window. My husband went to park the car while I took the bags and two children upstairs. When I came back down to return the cart, I decided to ask Mr. Valet Parking whether they even had a bellman on duty. He told me they did and he was on break, but he would be happy to help. This offer seemed a bit disingenuous since it came after he had watched us load our bags on the cart and watched me and my two children struggle to move it past his valet window. I told him I had taken care of it and he promptly went back to looking at his computer screen.
Highs: On Friday we decided to order room service for dinner, but didn't have a menu in our room. After waiting for one to be delivered for half an hour, I finally walked downstairs to the restaurant to get a menu. Mr. Magdy Rizkalla did not have a menu, however, he kindly offered to let me order room service at the restaurant rather than continuing to wait for a menu to be delivered. Our order was delivered in about 30 minutes and, surprisingly, it was complimentary. This was completely unnecessary, but very much appreciated and demonstrative of the fact that Mr. Rizkalla definitely understands the importance of service. On Saturday night we had dinner in the bar while we watched football games and had excellent service by a woman in her 40's with long wavy blonde hair...don't know her name, but she was terrific. 
Another Low: Our room service menu took slightly over an hour to arrive. We got it about 4 minutes before our food was delivered.
Another high: The room was clean and quite spacious...bedding was very comfortable. We were attending a dance competition at the hotel so we were in and out of our room all day. The hotel was at maximum capacity and yet our room was serviced in a timely manner...and completely without our knowledge. How did they do that?
Because of Mr. Rikalla, service in the sports bar, and housekeeping, I would recommend this hotel. Service means everything in my book.

title: “BED BUGS”
text:
Whilst I know that every hotel is susceptible to bed bugs, yes, even ones owned by Hilton, I feel that it is a fair warning to any traveller that may be looking to stay at this hotel. 
And it's not one or two bites. I had at least nineteen bites on my face alone (largely thanks to the fact that I was wearing long-sleeved and long pants to bed, thus leaving my face unprotected). The made a trail from my right temple all the way to my left jawline and a thick cluster under my chin. Yes, I am being descriptive because I'd rather anyone else not experience this. It isn't pleasant. The pictures aren't pleasant. 
It was so bad that all my friends that saw it cringed in disgust and had immediately urged me to go to a doctor and to complain to the hotel management. I had more down my neck (two very distinct trails), and a few along chest, arms, hips, stomach (concentrate largely the area where the top of my pyjamas separate from my bottoms. Basically anywhere they could reach) and legs.
As for the rest of the stay, it had adequate amenities, as per its star ranking. I suppose my only other complaint would be that the air conditioning wasn't as cold as I'd like it to be (despite turning it to the lowest setting). The bed and pillows were very soft and nice and if they weren't infested with bed bugs I would have loved them, really. The breakfast isn't as impressive as some I've had but it's not too shabby either. Nice flat screen. The room was modestly sized. Not too small that it becomes a tight squeeze but not large enough that it becomes something to shout out about. The premise is clean and kept.

title: “Be careful when booking car services to airports”
text:
when we were leaving, we let the hotel front desk and bell boy that we had already called a car that will take us to Newark Airport. We had already payed the fee with credit card. 
The bell boy tells us that our car is ready and get us in another company, that we didn't know (west end cars and limousines). 10 min later our company calls asking for us and then we found out that the Hilton (or somebody there) has a deal with this car service and gets a comission for each traveler! We got charged double cause the driver wouldn't let us get our bags at the airport! A mess!

title: “would not recommend.”
text:
First off, I was never told by either [--] (who I used to book the room) nor by the Pod, that I would get a 'shared bath' room. And, there were 2 bathrooms for the entire floor, and they were a long walk from my room. I'm female and felt unsafe and it was unsanitary. And, I paid $150 before taxes, which is not cheap.
The room itself was tiny, about the size of a large closet.
But, I was stuck there for one night. I've vowed never to stay there again and never to use hotels.com.

title: “Nice experience”
text:
I was in Seattle for a long weekend for pleasure.
The hotel is in a very central part of town. Practically everything is walking distance. This is very nice. Although this is mostly a business hotel, I did not feel overwhelmed from the business type of atmosphere. The staff is helpful. The rooms are comfortable, and above average for a typical room at other large hotel chains even if the bathrooms are a bit dated. Ask to be on a higher floor so you can enjoy the lovely Seattle views. I do not have any negatives to say about this hotel. You get what you pay for. 
Overall, a nice experience. The big plus is location. Being able to walk throughout downtown is very convenient. And after a long day of sightseeing, coming back to a comfortable room with a nice comfy bed is exactly what you will get.

title: “Need more stars”
text:
I sent four family members on a single-night (2-room) getaway, and the reports back were glowing. The property staff went out of their way to accomodate all their needs and wants, making a perfect stay.
Kudos, 6 stars.

title: “Superb Service - Loved the Bathroom Mirror Defroster”
text: We loved the hotel from check-in to check-out. It's an beautiful building, the staff are dressed to please, and they are attentive to the little details that make the stay grand. We loved the turn down service, complete with a small bottle of water and a chocolate and slippers. We spent alot of time walking in Boston and the slippers were a nice touch to pad our feet at the end of a long day. The concierge was helpful in arranging a nice restaurant for our first wedding anniversary - Mare. The bell hop arranged a taxi for us as needed. We were a short walk from the subway station and on the weekends, the financial district was quiet. We were able to sleep soundly - my husband was grateful for this. Access to free wireless internet would make the value for my dollar even higher. A lovely hotel.

title: “great place”
text: we stayed at the monticello sep 03. its got a lovely reception area, with free tea/coffee available pretty much all day, with a free wine reception one night a week too. our room was a good size, with a massive bed and the bathroom was pretty massive too, with a full size window which opened out onto a view of downtown (bit weird to sit in the bathroom looking out the window, i know, but it was actually quite fun sitting on the windowsill watching people go by). the hotel has a good location, only 5mins from the cable car terminus and union sq. so yes, it can be a little noisy at night as the cable car goes by, but hey you're in the city, what do you expect? all in all, good hotel right in the centre for a reasonable price!

title: “I'm a convert to Kimpton.”
text: Our stay was wonderful! Eric at the front desk took excellent care of us, the room was comfortable and beautiful, the view was stunning, and the overall style of the hotel was perfect for us. Even our teenagers loved it. I would certainly stay here again!

title: “Good Hotel”
text:
Overall: A nice hotel. Decorated well, great location, very friendly and accommodating staff.
Pros: Location, 10minute walk to 5th Ave and the shopping areas.
Cons: Small rooms. Hollow walls, you can hear other guests and plumbing sounds.

title: “Nice hotel with Great Staff”
text: I recently booked this hotel for a great rate and we had a very nice stay. Overall the hotel itself met all our needs for a one night stay. Very convenient downtown location with a very accessible shuttle service. Each employee we encountered was very friendly and helpful from the front desk staff, the shuttle drivers, and bartender. Even the General Manager (Bill) was making rounds to greet guests and making sure we were having a positive stay. This hotel definitely exceeded my customer service expectations.

title: “good location but terrible attitude and service”
text:
the location of the property is excellent if you want to get around to doing the usual touristy stuff in LA. But for some reason the people at the front desk have a serious bad attitude problem. Forget about a smile they are close to being rude. We had stayed at the super 8, la mesa at san diego just a night before and the Indian owner at the desk was delightful and knowledgble. walking into culver city was just the other way round. The check in clerk was ignorant and rude. The breakfast was below par. They had exactly 2 things of which also the bread ran out and on being asked was given an answer by the lady that just do without it! Disinterested owners. 
The good part was that the location was fabulous and the rooms superbly sized and good.

title: “Great Location - Nice Old Fashioned Hospitality”
text:
My Husband and I stayed here for 6 nights at the Casablanca during our Honeymoon in October 2011 based on great reviews we had read on Trip Advisor and it was certainly the right decision.
Upon arrival we had a bottle of wine and a congratulations card which was unexpected as the previous two hotels we had stayed at did not do this.
There really are no negatives to mention - The room was on the small side but I have been informed that this is a trait of NYC hotels. It was not tiny but a little tight.
Positives include fantastic location right in the heart of time square, great service on the front desk, willingness to help you and always smiling, clean rooms, clean bathroom, heater is set to a timer so it never felt cold and breakfast was lovely in the eating area. 
I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to NYC. Cant wait to return!

title: “Apparently Best Hotel in San Jose - Probably True”
text:
I had 2 spend 2 weeks in San Jose for business and this hotel was recommended as an absolute mucst by my colleagues. I stayed for just under a week in Sept 2010. From the way my colleagues went on about this hotel I was expecting something absolutely AMAZING. I was disappointed. The hotel is very nice with a large lounge and trendy bar. the rooms were nice but unremarkable - I had a view over the car park and in the VERY early morning the delivery lorries would park below leaving engines/refrigeration units on causing an unbelievable amount of noise.
Breakfast is included in the price and is pretty good though very samey with a selection of hot eggs meats and breads etc.
I have stayed in much nicer but also much worse hotels. Location-wise it is better to stay here than in the heart of Silicon Valley as there is a mall and a few restaurants about but if this is the best San Jose has to offer, I'm not impressed. Going again in March 2011 for business.

title: “Good Value and location”
text: We stayed here for a family vacation. We found the Inn on TA and decided to give it a try. We stayed in a Studio Suite and an Economy room on separate visits. Rooms were clean and fresh. The breakfast was simple (Waffles, pastries, bagels, cereals, coffee, juice) to get your morning started. There's a small pool, self service coin op laundry facilities, internet access in the lobby. The staff we encountered were friendly. Location wise ~ OT Inn is good since your centrally located and within a few minutes drive to San Diego's attractions. We would stay here again.

title: “Good hotel for business travelers”
text: I stayed at the Holiday Inn Mart Plaza last week. All in all, it was a great value and found the hotel to be pretty decent and clean (along with my room). The room looked to have been recently renovated along with a very nice view of the Chicago River from the 20th fl. I will most likely stay there again on my next visit to Chicago for business.

title: “Location and cleanness”
text: 30 sec and you're in the Barnes & Noble on 5th Ave, 5 mins to the public library, 8 mins to the Crate&Barrel, by 10 mins you're searching toys in FAO Schwarz and Mac shop. Love jog to the Central Park in the morning for the fresh air. Lots of great place to eat nearby, 5 mins drive to Anthony Bourdain's Les Halles for its notorious onion soup and steak + fries, or 5 mins walk to Oyster Bar in Grand Central Station. Decent room, very clean and big room size by New York standard. Bear in mind that the rental charge of international adaptor is USD18 per day, but the Best Price shop around the corner is USD14. Thank you so much to the hotel for UPS back the jackets I left in the wardrobe to Hong Kong.

title: “get a room at the back ;)”
text:
Good value for the location - a few steps away from the hubbub of Times Sq. First room I go was 2nd floor at the front. Newbie error I am sure. Room was tiny and smelled of cigarettes. But when I called the next morning and asked to swap the guy couldnt have been nicer and gave me 2 rooms to choose between. One at the back - 7th floor was fab. No view at ALL, but twice the size.
Rooms were clean but sparse. Air con woke me up a few times doing som clanking. I had a bath which made me very happy - but hot water seemed a bit unreliable in the bath and the plug didnt work - so you got out quick before it seeped away ;) No inroom amenities beyond bed and TV really, but the deli next door was great for morning coffee, juice etc. And I certainly had more channels than I've had in other hotels which was welcome
A bit scruffy around the edges, but if you want to be in the centre, with a quiet room for good value then its definitely possible at St James. 
As for the staff - it varied HUGELY - had a couple of guys who were wonderful, really great and helpful, then sometimes I got a couple of guys who just were totally stand offish. Happily the nicer guys seemed to work the most :)

title: “Hotel Monaco...a perfect stay, as usual!”
text:
We have stayed at the Monaco several times...and it is our favorite hotel on the planet! However, it has been a while since we shared our feelings and experiences with fellow travelers, so we decided it was time to write another review.
Practically speaking, the Hotel Monaco is ideally located. It's near the corner of Wabash and Wacker, just steps away from public transportation, across the street from a 7-Eleven and one of our other favorite haunts in Chicago--The Emerald Loop. The hotel restaurant, South Water Kitchen, is just wonderful! Throw in the afternoon wine reception, and we are always tempted to just hang out in the 200-block of North Wabash and never leave...everything we really need is right there!
The staff--every desk clerk, bell-hop, housekeeper--is tremendously friendly and helpful. Case in point: We forgot to bring the power cable for our laptop, and the front desk staff tried and tried to locate one for us. Even better case in point: Leftovers from our meal at the aforementioned Emerald Loop were re-warmed for us at 3:00 am when we returned from a night on the town and decided we were hungry. But, unlike at home, these leftovers weren't just nuked...the staff plated it up beautifully and served it as if it had come from their own restaurant! Way above and beyond!
Finally, to put it simply, it is just beautiful at the Monaco. The decor...the artwork...the color scheme...I always start to feel relaxed as soon as we walk into the lobby. Then we walk into our room, and I can almost hear my tension cracking away.
Visit their website...take a virtual tour...sign up to be a Kimpton In-Touch member (a free service)...and go to the Monaco!

title: “Beautiful Hotel A+”
text: The hotel is beautiful and the location could not be more perfect! However it is the staff at the Omni that makes this hotel above the rest. Upon our arrival the front desk assisted my daughter and myself to plan tours, directions and transportation for our stay. Joey "suggested" not pushed on several choices based on our interests. As we were in the first few minutes of unpacking in our room, Joey sent complimentary refreshments via roomservice. The extra attention the entire staff including the housekeeping service was beyond our expectations. Rooms are nice, clean and comfortable. Chinatown and Union Square are within walking distance. Other transportation we purchased the 3 day muni pass and rode the trolley and cable cars to every destination on our list. The suggested tours of Muir Woods and Napa Wine Country were awesome. Tower Tours picked us up from the hotel front door, they were well worth every cent. The tour guide named Will was outstanding. It is recommended 100%. We will certainly return to the Omni for our next visit to this fantastic city and would not even consider another hotel. Although we did not dine at Bob's, I regret not having done so. It will be on the list the next visit!

title: “A great place to stay for Universal Studios”
text:
We stayed at the Hilton for 4 nights and were very pleased with it. The lobby and restaurants are bright and cheerful. Our room was good size and comfortable. It could definitely fit a cot, but we were told they didn't allow them. We had a room on the 20th floor with a great view of the mountains. We enjoyed the pool and hot tub area and found them not busy late in the day. The continental breakfast was in a separate room from the large buffet which was a nice change. The main reason to stay here is it's vacinity to Universal Studios and Citywalk. We ate most of our dinners at Citywalk. There is a great variety of restaurants to choose from (Hard Rock Cafe, Buca di Beppa, Wolfgang Puck bistro, sushi). You can take a short walk to Universal/City Walk for take the shuttle from the hotel. The shuttles run very frequently, but my only criticism is that they stop at 8:00 p.m. If you eat at CityWalk or walk around at night you have to walk back to the hotel. That is when you need the shuttle the most. 
The hotel is very convenient to the different highways and I would highly recommend it.

title: “Average at best”
text:
Crowne Plaza Times square... stayed there last week 8th April, 2012. 
We had requested a Times Square view room, and wow what a view. As I recall the room was 3011 and right opposite the lifts which we thought would be noisy. But not the case.
The food around Times Square was ordinary and expensive. The hotel was nice enough. the bar was on level 2 with virtually no view, the Manhattan cocktail was soo strong.
The hotel had no safe, well a safe you had to swipe with your credit card... no will not do that, what if you lost your card or it was stolen... Had to have my passport with me all the time, was a pain.
No fridge, no safe, was a water heater thingie, but no cups. So did not bother.
The shower was the standard bathtub with shower overhead. The bed King size was comfy and clean and I checked for bed bugs, all seemed ok and after sleeping was ok, no itching.
I had trouble sleeping 30 floors up, my body kept feeling it was falling, but did it for three nights, and glad to come home.
The breakfast was underwhelming and the hotel in general was underwhelming - but expensive. 
One of our backpacks had been opened during the day, so not sure about the security, but all our electronic equipment was locked in a suitcase while we were out of the room because of the no safe issue.
Next time in New York I would love to find an apartment and stay for longer and really look around, perhaps a month and visit other places. NYC is interesting and multi layered place, but a like it a lot

title: “Very good, consistent.”
text:
No surprise at all. Marriott standards are fully respected.
Very attentive staff and suites at the corner are spacious for a reasonable price.
This hotel remains among my favorites in Charlotte.

title: “Bad neighborhood - noisy”
text:
Large room - but strange smelling
Travel guides do not recomment to walk this neighborhood after dark.
We had a corner room - wifi didn't work well, very noisy, you hear screaming, sirens and othe noises the whole night
Lady at front desk vey nice
Parking lot in front was nice

title: “Nice property with great Georgetown location”
text: After reading other reviews I had to check that we stayed at the same hotel – our experience was a positive one! We stayed here during a recent meeting in DC. All of the staff we encountered were friendly and helpful. While the property has a small exterior it has large spacious rooms and lobby areas. Hotel bar and restaurant appeared to be fine (we ate out) and the lobby renovations seemed complete when we visited. Room rate included wifi and we happily didn’t have any trouble with the hotel's quirky electronic key system.

title: “stay here regularly for business and like it”
text: as with my previous review, this is a nice hotel for staying in s.j. the rooms are spacious and some of them have nice extras like a balcony or a glass enclosed sitting area (7th floor room) for watching the courtyard and the skyline beyond. they also provide some nice extras upon arrival as a vvip club member which is very much appreciated. the staff at check-in and check out are also very courteous and professional. the rooms are quiet early on in the week but you can get a bit of street noise later in the week (although this thursday it is pretty quiet). the main drawbacks here is that it can sometimes be difficult to book a room on a tuesday even when you try a month in advance. this is unfortunate as i much prefer the hotel and it's service and proximity to decent restaurants compared to my other options (pruneyard plaza or, gasp, larkspur landing). the breakfast buffet is also quite good here with fresh fruit and (for me) a selection of ham and italian cold cuts. i do agree with one earlier reviewer that the rooms are not conducive to having a comfortable place to work. the long desk area, while stylish, is uncomfortable for actually doing productive work. all in all, however, i do look forward to my stays here for business. note: i give it an excellent rating on value because i get a discounted corporate rate. the rooms are quite pricey otherwise i believe.

title: “We love this place!”
text:
My boyfriend and I had a fantastic week long visit at the W San Diego and this location definitely holds up to the other "W" standards. Customer service was top notch, they really know how to make you feel special, the hotel amenities are excellent and the second floor "beach" is a fun touch. Our room was on the eighteenth floor and had a fabulous view that we could enjoy from our window seat. I loved the Bliss products in the room as well as the chalkboard! 
The W is very conveniently located, we are looking forward to returning!

title: “Great Location even better Staff”
text:
I traveled over from Scotland for the ACL festival this past September. Yes the rooms were a little old but as you can see from other reviews the hotel is being updated. The Suite was a great size 2 bedrooms and 2 baths . The maids were amazing and really looked after us. The rooms were clean !
The location is just perfect for both the festival and walking to the capitol or hanging out on 6th street etc. Its also 2 mins from the Bat Bridge .
The Breakfast staff were ace too the only downfall this hotel has is the breakfast times seems odd and finish early plus the lines for the food can be a bit off putting but the food was really good.
The Happy hour was alos amazing please tip the satff guys !!
The driver of courtesy shuttle was one of the nicest people I met on my trip and told us a lot about Austin. Would I stay again yes ...I am looking forward to seeing how they have updated the hotel :)

title: “Stellar Service.”
text: Stellar service. Warm and ultra-professional staff made us (2 adults, 2 kids) feel happy to be there the minute we drove up. Great "Flatiron" location near countless resturants and bars. One block away from the subway. Delicious breakfast in lobby. Tasty wine & cheese hour (with a piano player who looked as if he had just stepped off a movie set). Yummy cappuccino/hot chocolate/tea available all day. Elegant, understated and homey at once. Exceptional housekeeping staff--they incorporated my daughter's stuffed animals into their evening turndown service. We were all sad to leave our comfortable Park Avenue suite. I would highly recommend this boutique hotel as a home-away-from- home to business & pleasure travelers alike.

title: “Great location in LODO”
text:
Reviewed May 8, 2012 NEW 
1
person found this review helpful
We really enjoyed staying here for a conference. Great locationnear the 16th St. Mall. We did some shopping and enjoyed dinner at Marlow's. Spacious room well appointed very attentive service. Wifi extra but free in lobby beware of extra charges for internet in meeting rooms. Only quibble was the garage is very cramped and the hotel key cards are hit and miss when it comes to access. Great location at a great price -- we really do love this area!

title: “Great value, location and friendly staff”
text: Brian is NYC best doorman! Chris is a lively bartender, that pours a good drink.

title: “Good five nights stay”
text:
We booked this hotel and after reading reviews on here thought we had made a mistake. However, our 5 nights stay was a good one, really good location, close to Fishermans Wharf, Cable cars and 15 minutes walk to the Alcatraz ferries
The bedrooms were a typical Holiday inn, you could be anywhere in the world and it will be the same sort of décor and lay out. Room was in the main block over looking the pool so no problem with noise Visited in March and the nights were a bit chilly but the room heating worked really well and a quick trip to the coffee bar for their hot chocolate was a winner.
Being spring break we did have a group of young kids running around quite late one night but not sure this is the hotels fault? Still I am sure we woke them up early the next day!
We only ate at the hotel once. Compared with UK portions a starter would be enough for most people, the mini burgers and fry’s was like a main.
Only annoying thing was being a Priority Club member, the reception told me I got a % off the bill by showing the restaurant my member’s card when I go to pay. I did this and was told sorry you need a card from the reception so I cannot give you a discount. Did not even offer to walk 1 minute to go and get one for me.
Did not have breakfast at the hotel but used Denney’s Diner which is just around the corner. If you are using Virgin then you can get a meal deal from the Virgin rep. Make sure you get there before 9am as it gets VERY busy.
If I was in the same room then I would you this hotel again (can’t comment on the other rooms)

title: “For the money, they should be ashamed”
text:
I chose the Waldorf Astoria because of the history that surrounds it. The amount of esteem that it "commands" and the fact that it is supposed to be a high class, amazing hotel that is world renowned. I was wrong... For almost $500 a night, the closet door was broke, the tub would not drain (so you are standing in a pool of water as you shower), and a couple electrical outlets would not work. I complained to management but nothing had been done about it by the time that I left. I had wanted to stay at this hotel for years, but was seriously let down. The next trip to NY, we stayed at the Crown Plaza in Times Square and was very pleased. It was close to everything that we wanted to do and the bar served good drinks with pleasant service. We have also stayed at the Doubletree on Lexington which was a great experience as well. 
In summary... avoid the Waldorf Astoria (unless they get their act together). The Doubletree and Crown Plaza were better, and cheaper.

title: “Pick Another Airport Hotel...This One Was a NO Go”
text:
We arrived from Istanbul into LAX. Our home is Las Vegas so we overnighted. We used the one night free certificate from the Marriott Rewards Credit Card as payment.
They have a shuttle from/to the airport free of charge. It runs about every 15-20 minutes. Shuttle to hotel was full.
Arrived at hotel. They have a separate check-in desk for Elite members from 3-11 pm. Well, at 6:00pm NO ONE was there. Anyway, went over to the reg. registration desk. No one acknowledged us as gold members as they always do. Clerk was indiffernet and was more concerned asking if we parked a car so they could charge us the parking fee.
Went to the room. Have not seen a room this TINY at a Marriott Hotel in ages. The bathroom was a freakin joke. REALLY...even for free...this room was overpriced.
We were dead from our long flight so we went to bed. Slept awhile and then...OMG...the itching began. It was about 1:00am. This itching has happened at a few other Marriotts we have stayed at. It is either something they put into the wash/dry cycle of the linens/towels. OR, something they spray onto the mattress to resist/kill bedbugs. It only is at Marriott does this itching sometime occur. Literally, we were up till about 6am...itching, talking about it, more itching. Sleep was slim this night.
Had a flight out around noon so we went down to have breakfast around 8am. The prices for breakfast...you know, eggs, waffles, coffee, tea, etc. were again a joke. The buffet was $21.00 and the continental buffet was around $17.00. REALLY?
Well, the food was tasteless and the "service" was even worse. Used plates/glasses were sitting on our table the entire time. I had to ask for every tea refill. Then, the bill came and it was wrong. Go figure.
But, the real killer was on the one side of the bill portifolio was a notice to the "International Guests" staying/eating at the hotel. It says that it is customary to leave a 15% - 20% tip for service. REALLY? Almost embarrasing for a US citizen to read this crap. A tip should be just that...a voluntary tip for GOOD service. Not because the hotel/restaurant does not pay the employee an adequate salary. Or, because they want the diner to feel obligated to leave money to keep the employee. The "service" we had here was crap. Why would we, or anyone want to award this person for this??
Marriott really crossed the line on this one in our minds. 
We would never stay at this place again and could not recommend that you do either. There has to be better than this.

title: “A wonderful stay in New York City”
text:
We were in NY to celebrate my daughter's 21st birthday. The hotel gave an upgrade and free internet for the duration of our stay - a lovely perk. 
The room was very clean and neat and nicely appointed. The beds were amazingly comfortable and the bathrooms, though not very large, were large enough, and the shower head was strong and good.
The staff was all very pleasant, and they stored our bags for us for free - a nice extra for NY these days.
We booked it on Priceline and got a very reasonable last minute price - enough so that I would not hesitate to go back. 
Any use of the fridge would cost something, so we did not open it at all during our stay. The staff "warned" us of that. 
Wonderful location as well - walking distance to theater and restaurants, as well as easy access to public transportation.

title: “Great view, poor service, noisy”
text:
Rooms are fine, if a bit worn.
Beds are great -- nice, clean sheets and comforter.
Room service good.
Ice machines on every floor are UNBELIEVABLY NOISY. The front desk declined to turn them off. I piled all of the bedding from the other bed against the door to try to muffle the noise, but it still sounded like there was a '67 Camaro revving its engine in the hall.
I even changed rooms the second night, but even a room a few doors further away from that floor's ice machine was noisy. The bedding muffler worked this time, but then I discovered that there was a persistent grating sound coming from somewhere behind the wall or ceiling. Ventilation? I asked the front desk about it, but they put me on hold and never got back on.
I've never considered myself a light sleeper or sensitive to noises, but after 2 nights at the Rennaissance I feel like Felix Unger.

title: “Vast Resort Complex with plenty of Activities for the Family”
text:
Went with my 2 teenage kids and wife for 4 nights during Spring Break. I've used Trip Advisor in the past and want to give back so I hope you find this review helpful.
This course is pretty tough - bring a lot of balls if you're anything more than a 20 handicap. The greens were ridiculously slow and really took away from our enjoyment of the course. I paid $200 for my 13 year old and myself which is steep. The course offers good variety and blends between links and desert style. It's also very close to the freeway on a few holes which is a bit distracting and noisy. We started our round and did not see a single beverage cart until the 17th hole which was a real bummer. Go figure!
Prices are standard for Resorts where you are pretty captive. You really need a car to get to anything off resort unless you want to dare the 6 lane higways and massive intersections to get to 'Claim Jumper' or 'Joes Crab Shack' down Baseline.
The service was very spotty. Most servers were fairly content just doing what they were told and nothing more. 
The rooms were very clean and spacious with balconies. One drawback for us was proximity to construction of the new lobby which is 'supposed' to be complete on 4/9/2009. We never tried to change rooms because it wasn't really a distraction except when going to the main lobby through some of the construction area which was a bit of a hassle and not something you want to endure on vacation at a resort. The construction workers were exceptionally cordial as you passed by which made the inconvenience less unpleasant.
The gym was outstanding - probably the best part was the many classes offered throughout the day. There's also a great lap pool at the gym. Each complex also has its own pool and jacuzzi which gives you the chance to really get away if you want some quiet.
The Oasis Water Park was great and offers all sorts of activities from the lazy river to basketball/volleyball to dive in movies during the evening. 'The biggest drawback here was the service (it was just about impossible to get anyone to help us and worked best to just get it yourself) and most of the 'lifeguards' who are predominantly Asian transplants and exceptionally subdued. 
At one point, I went down one of the waterslides and lost my magnetic bracelet (a personal item). I asked the lifeguard if he saw a bracelet come down - he said 'there's nothing check the front desk'. It was bizarre to say the least. When I tried to engage him, it was clear he had little grasp of english and even less interest in helping me so I gave up. The lifeguards appear to be on duty to police the activity in the lazy river making sure everyone has an inner tube as required by lazy river law. This seemed to be their mission and they were quite dour with a few exceptions. Blech!
I would say the service at the Oasis water park was the worst part of the trip but the water park itself was exceptional!
We stayed 4 nights. Per night we paid $239 + $30 taxes + $30 'Resort Fee' which is for the wi-fi cloud hanging over the resort (very very slow and sometimes hard to use), the USA Today paper, the water park and minor amenities. 
Late breaking news...
We requested late check-out due to a late flight and were refused. Very tacky!

title: “Excellent value. Room was spacious, clean and very comfortable. Hotel staff went above and beyond (read inside).”
text:
There is a little bit of a story associated with my stay here in late August 2011. We were SUPPOSE to be staying for one night, before heading to the SFO airport for a flight back to the East Coast. Well, Hurricane Irene changed all of that. We were stranded when the East Coast was heavily impacted by Hurricane Irene. The Hotel Staff was able to accommodate us and extend our stay until we got a flight home several days later, even though the particular room type we had was already booked solid. 
I give an A+ to all of the staff for helping us out and making us comfortable.
Okay, now for a review of the hotel. We stayed in a 2 bedroom, 2 bath suite which also had a smaller full kitchen. The hotel is located among a number of corporate campuses, so there isn't anything to do in the immediate area, but attractions in San Jose, Santa Clara, etc.. are short driving trips. If you chose not to eat from the included daily breakfast, or the manager's dinner (Monday thru Thursday only), you can walk across the parking lot and pick from a number of places to eat. There's a greek place, vietnamese, cheesesteak place, Subway's, etc.. All of those restaurants were packed during lunch, filled with employees from the local corporations.
Hotel amenities included: Free daily breakfast, free manager's dinner (Monday thru Thursday only), free WIFI or direct-in room connection, in-room fireplace (in my suite at least), pool, small workout room, coin-op laundry room, free parking. The lobby also has a small library of DVDs you can borrow for free and basketballs for loan, but some not-so-nice guests who either stole the balls or kept them for the duration of their stay (we never were able to borrow one).
In summary, very nice appointed suite.. spacious and clean. If you can take advantage of the breakfast or one of the dinners instead of eating out, you can save some money. 
I wish every hotel we visited worked out this well.

title: “Wow Wow WOW!”
text:
I LOVED this place! I was lucky enough to get upgraded to their WOW suite and boy did it deliver! It was huge, comfy and very nicely decorated. It had 2 window seats with what seemed like a twin sized mattress in them with some comfy pillows. Perfect for taking a nap and relaxing in. I had friends up to the room and even w/ 6 guys and 2 ladies everyone fit comfortably on the couch or in the closest window seat. 
Service was wonderful, but I've come to expect that at a W. The room service was good and fast, also available 24 hours a day. We had drinks at Drai's one night and the drinks were great and the atmosphere was fun, perfect way to kick off a conference. 
All in all I really didn't want to check out when it came time to leave! Loved this place and would be back again.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text: We stayed here on an overnight before flying home, in a two bedroom suite. The room was very clean and staff was helpful to direct us to local restaurants. The hotel pool was great for the kids and breakfast had a wonderful variety of hot and cold food. Easy access to the airport the next morning.

title: “Stay away!!!!”
text:
We were looking forward to discovering this nice looking (on the web site) hotel...But it was SOOOOOO disappointing!
The room had not been cleaned at all (we thought we had entered someone else's room!!!!) and the hotel (well the corridor and swimming pool mostly) really needed some upkeeping as it looked old and abandonned. The view was certainly great but everything apart from that was a nightmare...especially considering the price!
We finally stayed at the magic castle and enjoyed our stay there (friendly staff by the way!).

title: “Comfortable”
text: We stayed here to celebrate our 19th wedding anniversary on 8/20/10 following some partying in Austin and because it's a new Westin and a very quite area. Parking spaces are very small; good quick check in; room was a king as requested with direct view of the Domain shops. Would have liked a suite since we were celebrating our wedding anniversary. Very clean room with good a/c, bed is excellent (it is a new hotel) but water will leak out of the all glass shower, (they need to fix that. feel sorry for the maids) the shower is really good size and good water pressure. no extra pillows and only one shower robe. We did not smell any odors as other reviewers have stated. Breakfast next morning was included in the rate plan an it was good. The Urban has a la carte and buffet for bfast. We opted for the buffet and it was quite good especially liked the OJ and the Coffee. Buffet consist of eggs, fruit, cereal, sausage, bacon oatmeal, etc. Very nice stay and would very much would consider returning.

title: “Overall experience good but had to fight for it”
text: The desk clerk explained the towel card policy ($25 deposit per pool towel) by letting us know that everyone steals the towels. Seemed hostile. We originally had a "Bayview" room, it was more like a no tell motel than a Hyatt. No balcony on the motel side. I went to see about changing rooms to the tower and had to wait behind two other groups trying to change their rooms to the tower. I did switch but it was a king bed for our family of four ( extra 30 bucks for the upgrade, extra 20 bucks for the rollaway), luckily our kids are small and were happy with the couch buffered with ottomans. This was a much better room, well worth switching. Yeah, what is it about all the wind at the pool? The pool is great though, on a hot summer day it would be fantastic. The clerk forgot to give us towel cards though so we had to beg for them at the pool. It is way more convinient to self-park here, the bell hop made the suggestion to us, "You know, with your room here it would be closer to self-park, save yourself X " Well, no room is nearer the lobby than the parking lot, does everyone get this routine? and then we all tip the bell hop extra and have to tip the valets to retrive our cars. The kayak rentals and Einstein's bagels right outside our room were great.

title: “Very cute”
text: Very cute boutique style hotel in downtown. The location is convenient to Navy Pier and other common attractions. The staff was kind and professional. The drawbacks were that the front desk was slightly overwhelmed and may have needed extra help, the sheets were quite itchy, and the room itself and the bed were a bit small.

title: “Disgustingly dirty. DONT STAY HERE”
text: Took 3 and half hrs to book in.They told us we were not booked in even though we had proof. Absolute idiots work here. All staff incredibly rude - shockingly so. Eventually got to room via nice reception and ok lifts - to the REAL hotel. God awful corridors and terrible doors to rooms- very depressing and dark and full of dust, dirty linen and bits of plaster from Walls and electric sockets covered in black soot. The rooms are even more depressing, very old and tired, plaster naming off Walls, cracks everywhere, all furniture is very old and every item was broken in some way, very old grey linen with one small pillow each (asked 3 times for.more but after 3 days still waiting), the lamps did not work, the phone did not work and the hairdryer did not work !! The bedroom was disgustingly dusty. And bits of dirt that I planted in a very obvious place on the carpet was never hoovered up. The maids quite obviously only come inane empty bins and make bed. The bathroom - enter at your own risk. I have never in all my years of travelling stayed in such a filthy bathroom. Ihad to clean the huge amount of dust from ALL and I mean ALL fixtures and fittings. The only good thing about this hotel is the location. Please don't waste your money pay extra and get a clean place.

title: “Great location!”
text: Spent three nights here last months and it is perfectly located on the Magnificent Mile! Everyone working there was very helpful. Super friendly and accomodating housekeeping. Nice lobby bar for meeting people.

title: “Rooms much better”
text:
This hotel has improved a lot. We previously stayed about 4 years ago and it was terrible. The renovated rooms although small are modern and clean and that is all you really need in NYC.
The staff seemed much friendlier then before and more professional. We checked in at 1am so no surprise our room did not have the best view, so they told us to change rooms in the morning to a city view room and having a nice view made such a difference to how the room feels.
Elevators were no problem at all, I actually like how you enter your floor before you get in.
can't beat the location. Will stay again for sure.

title: “Excellent NYC hotel!”
text: We stayed 22-24 July and had a king room at the back of the hotel which was extremely quiet. The included breakfast and the free wi fi makes the room rate quite reasonable when comparing to other hotels which charge for those items. A much appreciated exceptional treatment was the opening of the Club room at 4:30 am for this insomniac still on European time to work on the computer without distrubing his wife! The breakfast is the best continental breakfast I have seen and the beds were extremely comfortable. A great location tops it off and we will be return visitors for sure. Gary

title: “Excellent hotel Experience for Conference”
text:
I stayed a week (March 15-22, 2012) in the Crowne Plaza San Antonio for a conference. Even though renovation of the restaurant was underway, this did not detract from the meals as the staff worked around the construction. 
All staff was excellent. Especially I want to express my appreciation for Lazaro, the bellman in the lobby. He took care of my every need and answered all my questions about where to go. He also helped me receive packages for me. And always with a friendly smile! Thanks to Lazaro for making my stay go smoothly!
Paul Learned

title: “Horrible Customer Service”
text: Tried to book a room, got hung up on 5 times, placed on hold for 20 min only to be told sorry we are sold out!

title: “Very nice!”
text:
Had an unplanned overnight in Detroit, wound up here at the Double Tree.
Very neat building conversion, I really liked the mix of modern and retro decor. Front desk staff were friendly and helpful, rooms were BIG, bed was comfy. Used the gym which was in good shape too. And, the breakfast buffet was good value.
I wouldn't hesitate staying here again.

title: “A Nice Addition To San Antonio”
text: Just got back from a short 4th of July vacation break at the Wild Oak. This is one of the newer Hyatt resorts and I have to say we were very impressed with the facilities. The property is beautifully maintained and was a lot less crowded that the much larger Hyatt Resort & Spa across the road. A tip to note is that you can visit the Resort & Spa and charge to your room at Wild Oak. This way we were able to marry the best of both facilities. I would always choose the Wild Oak to stay due to it being, as said earlier, much quieter. Both locations have a lazy river for tubing for example but the one at the Wild Oak looked cleaner and was exceedingly less crowded. My kids loved also loved the two large water slides - the largest must be 75/100 ft tall. Contrary to a couple of reviews here, I found the staff very friendly, helpful and professional. The barmen at JB's, Larry from Boston & Paul from Michigan were two of the best. JB's itself however, does have a limited menu - I tried the pizza which was pretty good but the brisket was quite poor so for dining I'd normally go offsite unless I was "snacking". You are close to a few restaurants 3 to 4 minutes down the road where 151 & the 410 loop intersect. If you want to eat in San Antonio proper on the Riverwalk it is quite a hike – around a 20 minute drive. The Wild Oak is close to Seaworld but when you are within the property grounds you feel very secluded. You will likely see a fair bit of wild life onsite such as rabbits, raccoons & lizards. Apparently, there even are a few rattlesnakes in the bushes as we were told a young girl had been nipped on the ankle last month. However, living in Texas we know this is possible but very, very rare so don’t let it put you off at all. The property currently has 3 or 4 "blocks" but will be expanding to at least 8 so it will get “unfortunately” busier. The rooms themselves are very well appointed in a rustic style which was very tastefully done - the living room has a 42 inch plasma as well. The only negative is that you do have to pay $10 a day for in-room cable internet. Considering the cost of the resort, the Hyatt could at least throw this in for free. There is also pay for use wireless in a couple of spots. All in all we had a great time and I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again.

title: “cheap, clean, comfortable, convenient, friendly”
text:
This is a simple and cheap hotel. Decoration is basic. It is clean, room is spacious enough, bath/shower/WC/wash basin, good bed. Table for two for simple breakfast which can be collected free in the morning at the reception, bureau to work on with lap top. Good conventional large television with plenty of programs. Staff is very friendly and helpful. Free internet. Swimming pool. Parking.
Safe area to walk. Near (5 min. walk) Town&Country Convention Centre. Bus stop in front and about 2 min. walk with access to all destinations. Public transport is $5 a day for unlimited travel in the San Diego area.
Perfect place to stay if you can do without full breakfast and jack knifing attendants.
I will definitely go there again.
Not 5 star but a very comfortable 2-3 star. Very good value for your $$.
One draw back: No decent restaurants in the direct vicinity, so you have to go Down Town for that

title: “Still a lovely hotel”
text:
We stayed here because our preferred hotel, the Royal Palm, was fully booked. We tend to avoid these large hotels because they attract the conference crowds (I've been a conference crowd so I'm not trying to be a snob) which means that there are often crowds at places you'd like to go, the pool, the gym, the restaurants. They have done some major renovation, so the hotel does not feel as tired as it did the last time I was there. One caveat, we had made a reservation for tea with my in-laws. Because they are older, at the last minute, they did not feel well enough to join us, so we called to cancel (about 2 hours before the reservation). We were told there would be a $15 charge per person. This cancellation charge had not been disclosed when I made the reservation. I did later call the front desk to explain the situation, and they waived the charge. But, they should not have had such a charge in the first place. A no show charge is certainly understandable, but we make reservations for fine restaurants everywhere in the world, and noone has charged us for cancelling a reservation.
Otherwise our stay was great. The room was comfortable and large. The breakfasts are great. The spa is top notch.
It's still a big hotel, however, so keep that in mind.

title: “quick one-nighter”
text: I had to make a quick trip to Memphis to visit LeBonheur and was only in the hotel room for about 10 hours. Long enough to sleep and shower basically. The beds were very comfortable and the sheets were clean and without stains or holes. Plenty of comfy pillows in the room. The fridge was COLD, the Internet was fast and the TV had plenty of cartoon channels to entertain both of my two year olds. Hotel is not in the best location, but is definitely not in the worst either. Our room was right beside the stairs, so it was loud on and off throughout the night with people screaming at each other as they were coming and going on the stairwell. The noise woke me up several times, but my kids stayed asleep, so I didn't worry too much about it, and it quieted down rather quickly once everyone was off the stairs. The bathroom was not exactly dirty, but it didn't look very clean either. Towels and washcloths were clean, as was the bathtub, but stray hairs and a dead bug on the floor when we arrived. Didn't report this to the manager, as I was exhausted and only wanted some sleep. I was just glad the bug was dead and not alive. The exterior of the hotel looks a bit run down, but the inside wasn't bad. Breakfast looked good, and coffee was hot. Front desk clerk was very nice and polite. Overall, an okay experience. Would consider staying here again as long as I didn't have a room next to the stairs.

title: “Are you kidding me? NEVER AGAIN!!!!!!!!”
text:
I booked this hotel because the price was right ... but you get what you pay for. I didn't know the area, wish I did. Wish I had taken the bad reviews seriously. 
Husband and I checked in mid afternoon ... while checking in, a guy comes in with an obviously dressed prostitute asking to rent a room for an hour ... REALLY? Of course the desk guy did ... and the man renting the room stated that he did this last week (to the clerk). Should've been first clue. 
We got our room, it wasn't great ... bathroom window would not close, mold around the bathtub and windows. A/C did not cool down. 
We went out to dinner ... came back, room STILL HOT. So husband went down and they did give us another room ... a few doors down. So we move down, settle in ... still mold but the a/c works. Then the noise starts, it was more like a feaking apartment complex than a hotel, parties in the parking lot, loud noisy guests ... I will say the bed was pretty comfy. 
The next day we decided to head to Banning ... note: we paid for 3 nights, we had that room reserved for 3 nights. 
Decided to stay in Banning overnight ... went back at almost midnight on Sunday (again our room was paid for until Monday) our room key would not work. We tried for 10 minutes ... nothing. Good thing we took our suitcases with us. 
Husband went and rang the night bell non stop for 10 minutes and NOBODY answered. It was drizzly and we were tired, so we went next door to Best Western Lamplighter Inn & Suites ... got a room. Had no choice. 
Next morning hubs went to check us out of HoJo's and they did credit us for that Sunday night but they were adamant that they WERE there ... 2 of them ... well then why the heck didn't you answer? 
So we ended up paying 87.00 for a few hours sleep at Best Western (which, by the way was wonderful). 
I would never stay there again ... never. Have written to corporate but not sure what they will do.

title: “Great location, helpful staff, Nice accommodations”
text: Met my friend in San Francisco for our Nov birthday celebration. Enjoyed the accommodations at this Marriott and the location was good. The concierge was most helpful in booking dinner reservations and info on getting around in the city. My friend had used the spa/pool on other visits and said it was good and free. Friendly, professional staff including housekeeping. Had breakfast at Mel's Drive In a block away and it kept me going till dinner!

title: “okay downtown hotel -- you can do better elsewhere”
text:
I was on business in downtown Los Angeles. The Hilton Checkers is nothing special -- I recommend you stay elsewhere.
The Hilton Checkers is at the bottom of a relatively steep hill known as "Bunker Hill." At the top of the hill are a cluster of office buildings, the Disney concert hall and performing arts center, and other destinations. Across the street from the Hilton Checkers is the Biltmore hotel. At the top of the hill is the Omni.
Hilton Checkers is 1920s vintage building that has been significantly renovated. Rooms are up to date -- flat screen TV, relatively new bathroom fixtures. Desk and desk chair are adequate for work, but mediocre ergonomically -- typical of this class of hotel, nothing unusual. In room wireless access for a fee.
Fitness center was small. 3 treadmills, 1 elliptical, a modest assortment of dumbbells. Machines are jammed together. At 6 am all machines were in use and people waited. Pool is tiny and outdoors. Fitness center is on roof, with nice views, but the machines face the wall and have no view.
Concierge and bell desk was helpful and busy.
Breakfast service in the hotel was slow both days I ate there.
I recommend staying at a different hotel in downtown LA. I have not yet stayed at the Omni, but hear that it is recommended by business travelers. I liked the Biltmore for charm and fitness center, although HVAC is better at the Checkers.

title: “Small Rooms but central location and nice staff”
text: The rooms where nice, with more conservative decor, but definitely on the small side. Rooms are quiet except for right next to the elevator. Reasonable price for the location and quality of the room, expect to pay extra for parking and breakfast. No pool or exercise room but that's not what we looked for on this trip. It was nice to be able to walk out the door and be right there in the middle of hustle and bustle and there are nice breakfast options like coffe houses nearby. I'd recommend the Italian cafe on Union Square for morning coffee as their cappuchinos are excellent. The free computer and internet use by the lobby was a nice plus!

title: “Unbelievable Stay!”
text:
My wife and I were celebrating our anniversary with a trip to Chicago this past Sunday-Tuesday. You just knew from the second you walked into the hotel that this wasn't your standard hotel. Everything from the warm greeting from the valet attendants on the street, to the smiling and attentive guest attendants (more importantly the line of guests checking out were all smiling!), and amazing interior, our stay was handled with the greatest display of professionalism and customer service we have ever experienced! We arrived early Sunday morning and Glenn checked our bags (check-in is 3pm). He was amazing! (My wife said she wanted to put him in her pocket!) Since it was our anniversary, he offered to upgrade us to an available lake view room overlooking Lincoln Park Zoo for just $10 extra a night (usually $40) and we bit. After running about the city that morning/afternoon, we returned after 3pm to check-in. Our room was located on the 11th floor between 2 elevators and the ice machine. Needless to say, we weren’t initially feeling it. However, it never was an issue during our stay (note: we passed out during our stay vs. fell asleep, so your experience may vary!). Views overlooking the lake were great and room (queen bed) is adequate for 2. About 10-15 minutes after arriving to our room, we were greeted with a bottle of Chardonnay on the house with a personally hand-written card from Glenn. Seriously, who does that anymore? Unbelievable! From this point forward, if we got a little attitude or insincerity, we could probably live with it (sad, expectations of customer service have sunken that low, isn’t it?), but we never did. From the food/beverage manager who most likely took a risk in letting us up to the J. Parker rooftop bar/restaurant 10 minutes prior to opening (ok, it was so early they were holding a staff meeting and a landscaper was removing dead leaves from pots). This was a perfect opportunity for the hostess or servers to give a dirty or unwelcoming glare from afar, but it never happened. In fact, we were welcome openly by both the hostess and front-of-house manager that let us in to the rooftop area and said they would be with us
shortly to take our drink order, and they were. Exceptionally world-class hotel with a friendly, competent, and willing staff that clearly exceeds expectations! One of the first 
things they teach you in customer service/sales, etc., is to smile, because it’s difficult to 
fake a smile, but most importantly the smile is contagious and it is passed right on to the guests! Thanks guys/gals for a great stay, we will be back!

title: “Very beautiful hotel”
text: The rooms and hotel are beautiful. The room was spacious. There was a little sitting area and a big desk. The kitchenette was small but adequate. Breakfast was better than just a basic continental breakfast which was awesome. Valet was the only option and was $23 per night!!!! The staff were very nice and helpful!

title: “Not what I have expected”
text:
The good -
It is located near Whole Foods. 
It is walking distance to most areas (we walked from this hotel everyday to 59th).
The rest -
Expect mid-20s crowd.
Expect check-in not friendly (men are better than women).
Expect room to be dark (dark brown wall and carpet) with small size windows, also dark brown/black titles in the bathroom.
Expect individual air condition unit rather than central air (noisy).
Expect room to be very small, measure before you go. It is about
210 sq ft for the entire room. Yes small is expected for NY, but this size room isn't suitable for international passenger with large luggage, ok for overnight guest with boston bag. Remember the room has either king or two double beds.
Expect shower basin to be light brown (used to be creamy white when it's new). The hotel is only four years old. I bought cleaner but couldn't remove anything.

title: “grumpy staff”
text: As a Hilton Honors member, this has got to be the least friendly Hilton Hotel in existence. Checking in was OK (nothing special), checking out was a nightmare. Paid for their Park and Fly package. On exit, we were 20 minutes late for our 7 days parking package. The clerk tried to charge us for a whole days of parking instead of an additional 30 minutes. Being at midnight, there was no one else I could talk to according to this clerk. His response was if you don't pay, you don't get out. Finally had to "educate" the guy that its 20 minutes late and not 24 and 1/2 hours late. He finally recognized his mistake but was too arrogant to even offer an apology. I would have been satisfied with an apology. Ended up paying for an hour of parking (spent a total of another 20 minutes arguing with him) so he made me pay for the entire hour instead of 30 minutes. Could you believe such attitude.

title: “great site for a meeting”
text: enjoyed the city view from our balcony, the staff was very friendly and helpful. I loved the pool and spa area, the firepits were charming and so comfortable for chating and relaxing

title: “Truly a "home away from home" experience”
text: I recently stayed at this hotel and had a fantastic experience. I had an allergy attack just prior to my flight to Chicago. I called the hotel from the Airport and told the front desk clerk that I couldn't have any feathers in the hotel room when I arrived in a few hours. When I checked in, I was greeted as if I was coming home. (I stayed there once before over 10 years ago.) They assured me that the room had been attended to and all feather products removed. They did as they promised and I slept well (and didn't sneeze) for 3 nights. The service is outstanding, the hotel is well kept, the restaurant is excellent and the location is great. I can't wait to stay there again.

title: “Location location but the concierge level disappointing”
text: Great sized rooms and great location if u want action until early hours. But the access was not upto the standard of Marriott. Concierge level crowded and well before breakfast time over they ran out of croissants .... Not befitting a Marriott marquis ! They need to increase the size to allow for the size of the hotel so that people are not waiting like a food court for a table. Be sure to arrive a little earlier than closing time if you don't want to wait 15 min to get to the buffet. The bell captains are fab and warm e en with our huge load of luggage.

title: “Lice”
text:
My brother and I planned to stay here one evening, only to be welcomed by a cigarette burnt blanket and lice. Upon discovering the lice within the shower, we immediately packed up and headed downstairs. When we demanded a refund we were verbally assaulted by the owner and two facility workers. Thankfully after waiting on-hold for over an hour with hotels.com we were able to secure our refund.
I would never come back. Hopefully it is torn down by the time I return to Philly.

title: “Very pleasant”
text:
We stayed at the Westin San Diego for three days to attend the San Diego film festival. The location was great and we could easily walk to all the venues. The train depot is nearby and the highway entrance/exit is less than a mile away so it makes getting around the San Diego area very simple. The hotel itself was very clean, felt freshly decorated and comfortable. The room was spacious and everything worked properly. The bed is enormous and we slept very well. There were two 'comfy chairs" of different styles. We got some noise from the train depot and the ships coming into the harbor, but nothing to inhibit rest. The staff anticipated us running out of shampoo, etc, and left more when they saw we were running low. On my birthday, I came back to the room to find they had set my birthday card from my husband( --which I had just opened that morning )on the bed and surrounded it with chocolates! We attended parties for the festival at different venues and met up with groups staying at the nearby W hotel, and both my husband and I agreed we preferred the Westin for comfort and serenity . Our room overlooked the bay and we could watch the sailboats and cruise ships come in. It is well worth a little extra to us to get that sort of water view. All the employees from the front desk to the valets, housekeeping and restaurant staff, were friendly and helpful. Every single one. They gave us directions and answered questions. No attitude or rush. What a refreshing change after a recent stay at a factory-feeling hotel in Vegas!
 The breakfast buffet at the restaurant is a little expensive ($18--for me who usually stumbles around at home in the morning with tea and toast) but has a great selection of fruits, yogurts, breads and hot dishes. You can also order a la carte off the menu and there is a coffee shop in the lobby so you can just grab a quick bite.
My only caveat would be that despite the convenience of the location, some people might not enjoy the area as there are many homeless who may approach--and did ---even just inside the hotel doors one evening. There is a Greyhound bus station a couple of blocks away and the people you meet on your walks can seem a bit dodgey. I'm from LA and used to that, but I know my family from Wisconsin would be uncomfortable. Area parking is also expensive but worth it to keep one's car safely indoors under guard. Again, coming from LA I find it is a false economy not to pay for parking in a downtown area. 
We had a lovely time at the Westin and could easily recommend it to friends.

title: “great!”
text:
Stayed here on a New Year's Eve with my husband. Though we weren't in the room for long, it was great! Nice comfy bed, great decor, great location.
GOOD coffee and breakfast the next morning....we needed it! ;-)

title: “Now called - Double Tree Hilton”
text: If like us you are one of the people who booked this hotel last year, you may not know that the hotel is currently in a state of transition. In short it has changed ownership from the previous owners when it was known as 'Wyndham Gardens', to interim name of 'Hotel 36', and then finally to relaunch as 'Hilton Double Tree'. We stayed at the hotel over the last six nights and during that short time we stayed in their best room '2608'. This is on the top '26th' floor and the views were truly spectacular. When sitting on the king size bed we had clear views of the empire state building close by, the illuminated New Yorker hotel, and then the freedom tower in the distance. At night the view over the city was stunning, plus sunset again staggering. Get this room and you won't regret it. During our six night stay the staff have worked day and night without disturbing guests to transorm the hotel into the Hilton brand. Well done to them and the especially the front of house guys who were very helpful. Some have complained about the room sizes which aren't huge, but rather compact. We stiil had plenty room. As for breakfast, this was provided free as continental style. Again no problem with this. Also the hotel gave free wifi access which together with the breakfast, saved a few dollars. Location wise this hotel is bang on the money for all that Times Sqqaure has to offer and if your a sports fan Madison Square Garden is 2 blocks away. Whilst there check out 'Nick & Steffs' steak house for arguably the best food and service we've ever had from a restaurant (do try the steak cut chips!!). Anyhow, back to the hotel. The lifts are fast but during busy times you can be waiting a few minutes for the next one. Apart from this we have no complaints at all, and if your a traveller on a budget who wants to be in the middle of the action - choose this one - but remember to get a room on the front and close to the top if you want to enjoy the city view. Room 2608 is the best!!

title: “Luxurious”
text: Whenever we travel to Philadelphia, a stay at the Sofitel is a MUST for us! The staff is truly accomodating, the crepes are wonderful for breakfast, and the rooms are quite luxurious! The location of the hotel is right in the heart of the city, also--perfect!

title: “It's ok!”
