text: First of all, if you are booking this hotel and expecting 4-5 star luxury, then book the Sheraton, Hilton or whatever other hotel. It is NOT even close! If you are looking for a inexpensive place to sleep that is comfortable enough, then this is the place for you. The bed was comfortable, the room clean enough, bathroom space was adequate. Subway within walking distance. Plenty of places to grab a bite. Duane Reed right downstairs. Would I recommend it to someone, sure but I would warn that this is a no frills hotel that does the job of a nights sleep. Would I stay there again, no, only because I would rather stay in Times Square!

title: “Non Smoking? I don't think so!!!”
text:
We requested a non-smoking room and honestly the smell of the room and the entire floor was simply nauseating. Unfortunately we had to stay for two nights since we were booked into this hotel for business travel. The first night we went to a nearby Target to get air fresheners that are supposed to reduce the smell of smoke. Between the air fresheners and us utilizing the air conditioner/fan in the room, we were finally able to reduce the smell in the room to less than the odor in the hallway.
After leaving this facility and traveling to Kentucky I looked forward to sleeping in a truly non-smoking room that smelled fresh. Much to my chagrin, my PJs still smelled of smoke from the stinky linens at the Comfort Inn.
I love Columbus and the Polaris area -- but if I can not locate another room in the area I will drive several miles rather than stay in this facility again!

title: “Loved our stay”
text: We booked the hotel on Hotwire and got a good value. There is a tunnel at the end of Erie St to get to Lake Michigan. Try the West Egg for breakfast which is next to the hotel. The swimming pool is great.

title: “Don't even think about staying here.”
text:
Absolute worst hotel I have ever had dis-pleasure of staying at. They advertise free continental breakfast and when asked on first morning I was told then did not have it. On second morning when someone else asked, clerk brought milk, bread OJ and a big tub of margarine (half-empty) out for breakfast. I would not eat breakfast after I saw everyone digging in margarine with their own knife. Not very healthy in my opinion.
Asked for coffee and was told there was a pack of coffee in my room. Told her I drank it and she suggested I go next door to restaurant. She said "there was no water in lobby to make coffee"
No 'wi-fi" as advertised. They did have internet access in lobby, but had a wireless keyboard and batteries were dead and no batteries available.
Run from this place. Run fast and don't look back.

title: “Great Hotel for the price”
text: The room was clean, with a microwave and frig. The staff was wonderful. The free breakfast was modest, but was just enough for me. Hot and cold cereal, bagels and cream cheese fit my appetite. The bonus of staying here is the fantastic restaurant, Al's Seafood, right out front. The crab cakes are authentic Maryland style. I appreciated that the unseemly stations on the tv were blocked for family viewing. I don't quite understand the previous rating. I'm coming back again next time in Baltimore.

title: “Yuck...Not so good!”
text:
Hi all,
 Just wanted to comment on our stay at the Powell. We booked early and got a reasonable rate. $135 with parking. This is the second time to SanFran . We stayed previously at the Larkspur Hotel on Geary and really liked it!
 The Powell Hotel was indeed very different!!!
 To be fair, the Powell does have a great location to the BART and Cable Cars. The room we stayed in was ample and had 12 ft high ceilings and newer looking bed and amenities. BUT....heres where it ends!
 The "business center" consisted of one computer right next to the reception desk with "5 minutes of internet per guest" actual sign says "over 5 minutes... 5 dollars charge per minute" What!?!???!!
 Like other posts the room and bed smelled... well kinda stank a little like "poo" according to my travel partner. There is no other word for it. Much like the smell of musty dank B.O. and well...excrement. But ,they had our credit card # and we were stuck. We had no other options so after a quick "poo search" (just in case the cleaning person missed something) and subsequent excessive perfume dispersal- it then smelled like Lilac and "poo".
 The room and elevator were ample for two to four people with modest luggage. Our room was on the sixth floor. Windows were huge! Lots of light! 
 BUT... Here's the fun part... Windows are 6 ft tall and 36" wide, there is a single broken latch, the window opens, and there it is... a sleepwalker's doom! A gaping 36" x36" hole in the wall right next to the bed 18 inches off the floor and- 6 floors up!! No screen, no grate, NOTHING to prevent anyone big or little from accidentally falling out to their death 6 floors below whilst looking for the potty at night, or sitting back accidentally in the "lounge chair" Beware of this if you have little kids! 
 Also, the room faced the side alleyway of the hotel. Nice seemingly private- not so! At 3am every night- the trash man cometh'. Dumps a steel bin full of glass recycling into his truck. This could be a great marketable feature for the Powell website "...excellent early pre-dawn wake-up service for those prone to sleeping through an alarm clock or loud explosions.... Suddenly, spring to life in the pre-dawn hours of morning to get a jump on all of the SanFrancisco tourist sites with the sounds of breaking bottles and skreetching steel containers". Ahh...just like heaven! Actually, this really sucked!
 The concierge was also less than helpful... staff took 45 minutes to fetch our rental form a nearby garage. Creepy hotel staff janitor-type-dude lurking around the lobby wearing blue rubber gloves was also a nice touch. What has he touched and why does everything her now smell funny?
 Nice lobby, but they were having the boiler serviced at 10 am and the sounds of someone drilling concrete was like a subway station in the lobby while we waited for our rental car.
 If you are honest hard workin' folks like us looking for a good quality hotel- this is not it. STAY AWAY!!!
Should you be misfortunate enough to stay the night at the Powell Hotel, be sure to bring earplugs, a good OSHA approved respirator, some disinfectant, and a parachute or bungee rope for a soft late night landing on the alley way below. 
Happy Trails!

title: “good hotel”
text: very good customer service and Amet is very very nice. will be staying here alot more. very clean room and bathroom. good location

title: “Great Location in San Francisco”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for a conference. It has a great location near the cable cars and Union Square.
The rooms were very nice, quiet and very clean. Service outstanding.

title: “Great Location, Hotel Needs Some Tweaking”
text:
We stayed at the Doubletree for four nights over the Christmas holiday. The front desk staff were excellent, very professional and pleasant. Our first room was a corner room in the older portion of the hotel. It was very spacious and nice, except the heat was not operating. We called down to the front desk and a repair person was sent immediately, but he was unable to fix the problem. We were moved to the room next door, which was very convenient to move to, except the room was much smaller and there was an odd sound of water dripping constantly that we were never able to figure out what it was. Also, the heat in this room did work but it was extremely loud. It actually startled me when it shut itself off with a loud thumping sound at one point when I was in the bathroom. 
Of the four-night stay, we received housekeeping services two nights. The second time, we walked into the room, noticed that a few things had been moved, remote control removed off of the bed, pillows thrown to the middle of the bed, some towels removed from the bathroom, (we assume by housekeeping staff) but the room wasn't cleaned. We called the front desk and informed them and they sent up clean towels, but were unable to explain what had happened. 
We had breakfast included in our rate, which was provided by the TGI-Friday restaurant within the hotel. We could choose from all but one menu choice. The breakfast was average. My english muffin was burned one morning and the hash browns in particular were of the same caliber as you would receive from McDonald's, which was disappointing. How hard is it to cut up a few fresh potatoes and cook them? 
All in all, the location was great and the front desk staff were some of the nicest and courteous we've ever experienced. I would stay at this hotel again, but would probably skip the breakfast and would request a more recently renovated room.

title: “Very relaxing environment”
text: Service was great staff always asked if we needed any assistance. Room was very clean king bed comfortable. Flat screen TV was nice but reception for picture quality was poor. A/c worked fine shower was oversized which was nice. Free shuttle to and from airport

title: “Very nice hotel and excellent service”
text:
This is a great place to stay in San Jose. The service was wonderful, the staff at the restaurant during breakfast were very cheerful and glad to see us.
The rooms were comfortable.

title: “Just what I wanted”
text:
I was in Los Angeles for a family reunion and taking some time to also see old friends. This location was central for me, with a quick access to the Harbor freeway for my trips downtown. Patel at the desk very helpful with explanations for the card keys and the wireless access.
The room was small, but as a single person, it was more than adequate. The location was on the 2nd floor down a small passageway (the only one in the motel), with the window facing the cinderblock wall of the next building. Because of this, the noise from busy PCH was minimized, especially with the fan on (it was a very hot week). 
The price was excellentl, so I didn't expect much in the way of amenities, but the room had a very comfortable bed, nice sized bath, full mirrors on the closet, decent towels and basic toiletries, as well as a built in hair dryer. There was a refrigerator, a microwave, and a large flat screen with HBO. The wifi was decently fast for a hotel, and not hard to connect to at all. It was free; something that my relatives paid $10 a day for at their hotel.
Only coffee was available in the lounge, but with so many restaurants, fast food places, and Starbucks nearby, it wasn't an issue. I did have their coffee one morning and it was pretty decent.
I would definitely choose to book here again. Especially if I could get room 203.

title: “Great service”
text: I stayed in the Dallas Fairmont for three nights on business, and I found the staff to be quite friendly and helpful. The curbside service was excellent when we arrived even though there were several guest arriving. The check in staff was extremely helpful. I left my laptop powercord in a conference room and the conference personel (not hotel staff) contacted the hotel staff and when I returned to my room I had a message from Austin following up to help locate it. They were prompt and professional. The nicest bellman was there to take my luggage down, his name was Tony Bennet and he hand me this card and asked me if I was please with my stay, which I was. Today 6 days after my return home I found this card with Tonys name on it and wanted to thank him for being so friendly and kind.

title: “No serious complaints”
text: I stayed here for 5 days and 6 nights for a course that took place in the hotel. I can't say much with regards to whether it's worth the price because it was all paid for, as was breakfast, but the rooms were clean, the beds extremely comfortable, and the cleaning staff was excellent. It's convenient for sightseeing and is attached to a shopping center which was great for me during my breaks, though perhaps not for my credit card. I do believe that large hotels should offer free wifi nowadays, which they don't, but otherwise I don't have any complaints about my stay.

title: “Confortable”
text:
The hotel is new, very confortable and good service.
If you are tall, be aware that some rooms have short showers!
Good location.

title: “Anywhere but here!”
text: My friend from out of state came to see my and his best friend. He was going to his next stop be for shipping out for overseas, AKA: WAR. I pulled in the the drop off zone to and was going to just let him get his room on his own. He had 3 bags; over seas bag, a very big duffle, and his army backpack. We had to care all his stuff, the bellman did not even ask if we need a cart and did not ask me if i needed help! I am 5'2! his sea bag is as big as I am! We got to the checkin and he was tolled he would be paying 300$ on top of what he had payed for his room. This was for stuff he my use or get during his stay. And I came to find out he would not get the cash back in less he asked for it when he left! The room was old and rundown! He may as well of stayed at my place, it dose not smell!

title: “Great Hotel”
text: From the moment we checked in the service was great! I felt like I was being welcomed into somebody's home. The rooms we very clean and the beds are very very comfortable!

title: “Disappointing”
text:
Stayed at hotel form July 30-31, 2010. I booked the hotel's "romance package" for our wedding anniversay which was to include champagne upon arrival and daily in room breakfast. Called the hotel in advance to notify them that we would be late arriving. Obtaining information at check-in concerning the package that we had reserved was difficult. 
 The rooms are "small" but comfortable. The bathrooms are large, however, they lack fans so taking a hot shower results in a rather steamy mess. A request for an additional bath robe was ignored. We went out to dinner and returned 3 hours later and no champagne. Two phone calls and it finally arrived. 
 Ordering breakfast was easy and room service staff were pleasant. However, the "All American Breakfast" left a lot to be desired. Their fatty tasteless "applewood smoked bacon" would even have Oscar Meyer laughing. We decided against breakfast on the day of check-out. 
 At check-out we were charged for the breakfast and a reminder to the desk agent that the breakfast was included resulted in this snooty retort: "The kitchen is required to add this to the bill." Rather than to say we are sorry for the mistake and just remove it. I get that for a response from a hotel that bills itself as "Luxury." 
 The hotel has a very good location for walking/public transportation and restaurants. Two bright spots, "Chris" the bell man and the Concierge Staff. However, this Sofitel does not measure up to Chicago or New York.

title: “Great location and great staff; rooms need thorough cleaning/updating”
text: My family and I have stayed at the Magic Castle approximately 5 times in the last 3 years - most recently in November, 2009. Many of the hotel staff have been there for years; they take their jobs seriously and absolutely go out of their way to make you feel comfortable. The breakfast is really very good and there are snacks available throughout the day. Parking is easy - although a bit tight (don't bring your Escalade). If you are in LA as a tourist, the location is fabulous - many famous Hollywood sights are within walking distance. What is sad is that over the past 3 years, we have seen the cleanliness and overall quality of the rooms diminish. The property would do well to spend some money to refurbish the rooms - everything looks tired and dirty. We are in LA again and have chosen not to stay at the Magic Castle - which makes us kind-of sad.

title: “Nice place to go to each night after work”
text: Easy to get to from the airport. Convenient to the Oakland A's Muni Stadium where I was working. Not a ton of restaurants around only a few fast food places about a mile or two north up 44th. The breakfast at the hotel served a nice buffet, nothing fancy but enough to get you full and on your way out the door. Wish it was included in the price of the room rate, but the front desk young lady who checked me in gave me a 1 day complimentary breakfast buffet, which was very nice. I would stay here again.

title: “Location - but that's about it”
text: If you want a real "pot luck" experience in San Francisco, book into the King George. The major selling point is its location: just a block from Union Square and surrounded by diners and bars - though the streets of San Francisco in this area have a very high concentration of people rattling a cup under your nose for some spare change. Nevertheless, it's cheap compared to other hotels in the area - but be aware that your experience is likely to reflect the relatively low price. Because the hotel is narrow and stretches back from the street, the views are mostly to the sides. If you're lucky enough to get a high room on the north side you'll get a view up the hill; but you're more likely to end up on the other side with a terrible view or no view at all. In my case, the first room I was given had a tiny window which looked directly on to a wall. Since I was there for nearly a week I asked for something better and was given another room on the 3rd floor with a view on to the back alley. Since at least it was quiet (well, apart from one night when a drunk guy sat and hollered late into the night), I settled on that room. A family member who joined me the next day was given a room on the same floor in which the window actually had FROSTED GLASS to hide how ugly the view was outside: it looked directly on to the building next door's rooftop, complete with all the machinery you find on top of commercial premises. Next, infrastructure. The King George might look charming, and to be fair, the decor has been renovated; but it fell short in a number of ways. One was the elevator: just one and incredibly slow. Secondly, no air conditioning: fine in early June but I wonder about July and August. Thirdly, the internet - admittedly free - was most definitely not high speed: it was almost impossible to log on and incredibly slow once I finally got a connection. And most strikingly for me, the hot water system was totally inadequate. The first morning I ran the shower for more than five minutes waiting for the cold water to turn warm. Eventually I called reception and asked if there was a problem. I was told I had to "run both faucets until I got hot water then turn off the one I didn't want". After 3-4 more minutes finally the shower ran hot and I adjusted the mixer tap - but within a few minutes it was cold again! For six mornings I endured the same thing: waves of hot and cold water as I showered, almost always ending with me rinsing my hair in cold. And it wasn't the mixer tap: the same was true in the sink as I tried to shave: one stroke warm, the next cold. All things considered, I wouldn't go back to the King George and wouldn't recommend it to other people. If price and location are all that matter, go ahead: but go knowing that the old adage applies: you get what you pay for.

title: “Thanks Palmer House for ruining my 40th birthday!”
text: I would like to start off with the positive, the doorman & staff were beyond exceptional. Top Notch. The Lobby is truly beautiful. A Chicago Landmark. I live in Chicago & was excited to stay at the Palmer House for my birthday & I love Hilton Hotels. I booked a King from AA vacations with my miles stating that I only wanted a King or Queen. At check in we were told our room was a double. 2 people in a double..Ouch. Well, I'm pretty easy going, gladly took my key & went to my room. So sad, the bed was so tiny and the room was the size of a closet size coffin with the bleak view of a inner courtyard. I have stayed in Hiltons across the world & really love the touches they add to their rooms. However, this was not the case at the Palmer House. Honestly, I would say you could do better at the Holiday Inn. Not only was the room tiny, we could hear our neighbors discussion about how their dresses didn't fit & people in the hall casually walking by. It felt like the walls were paper thin & we were sleeping in the hallway. Besides that the heating system was as loud as a small helicopter. I'm all for vintage charm( my house is over 100 yrs old) & truly not a high maintenance person but this was really crappy. We went to an art exhibit down the street, hoping when we got back, somehow are room would grow on us. It didn't, it was throughly depressing. We checked out, after 2 hours. The front desk was surprised and offered us another room with 2 Double beds. We declined. It was a nice suggestion but really, the idea of sleeping ala Lucy & Desi was not appealing. Let it be known..2 People really don't fit on a double bed..2 double beds really doesn't solve the problem for a couple. We left & chalked this up to a bad weekend. Went home, had pizza & slept in our own queen size bed. The bad part about all this is A) I will never have another 40th bday. B) Iost about 11,000 miles on a room I didn't want or stay in. C) No apology from management or staff. That's downright crappy. Thanks Potter Palmer.

title: “Best nights sleep”
text: Usually when i stay at a hotel, the first night I toss and turn and the next night I sleep just from exhaustion. The beds at Comfort Inn were SO comfortable I fell right to sleep and slept all night. Awesome pillows, good sheets too. Nobody likes to sleep in hard, scratchy sheets. Peter at the front desk was so helpful. I will definitely recommend this place to anyone who wants to stay in a nice, friendly, clean hotel.

title: “Beautiful Hotel/Resort”
text: Only had a once night stay here, I wish it had been longer:) Hotel was beautiful in every regard. Outstanding views, spacious lobby, plenty to places to eat or have a drink. Staff were friendly and helpful. I am Hilton Honors Gold, we were upgraded to corner suite and view of Downtown SD and another window with a view of Coronado Bay. Room was very clean and luxurious. Loved everything about this place. Pity about the 25.00 parking fee, but this is normal in this area of SD. The hotel more than maked up for it:)

title: “Absolutely Faboulous!!!!!”
text:
My frien And me stayed in the Omni for a long weekend and we had the time of our lives. The staff and managers couldn't be more helpfull . One of the managers even show us the
hotel . The room was spotless and the maids were always taking care off anything we needed. 
I highly recomend this hotel to anyone. And I'm sure I will be back there soon.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: This was my first stay at this hotel, but it definitely won't be the last: I've already booked 2 return trips. Things that I REALLY like: coffee available all the time, great breakfast choices (way more than a continental breakfast), really nice sheets and towels, and incredibly helpful staff. Enough said!

title: “My entire stay at the Bahia was flawless!”
text: Every staff member is an asset to the Bahia, friendly, efficient, helpful, courteous. They take care of the resort as if it is their own home and treat you as a welcomed guest. The grounds are beautiful, the dining delicious, the bar a quiet yet fun spot, it is just a short walk to the ocean, the rooms very comfortable. I give the Bahia a top rating.

title: “Not worth it's money and the hotel had "better" times.”
text:
For the money we paid we did not get the service which should have been appropiate.
Room: Even though the room was spacious it was not clean. We found several insects in corners of the room and the dust layer in some places was just incredible. Some rooms have a walk-in wardrobe which is great ... just that there is no light in them! Even though there is a plug for a bulb they have decided to not put one in! When we asked why there is no bulb they just said that they do not put one no more...
Bathroom: Bathroom size is average. You only get a shower and it all looks a bit old.
Service: I was very unhappy wiht the service I received. In the lobby were huge queues! Even if you just wanted to ask somethin you had to wait in line with people who wanted to check in! The 3 times I went I was treated unfriendly 2. Also the room service was highly disapointing. Every day its a surprise. Sometimes you get showergel but no shampoo and vice verca. In the restaurant everyone but one gentleman were unfriendly and the breakfast was not very tasty and consisted every day of the same.
Internet also is not free and if you do not want to pay 14 dollars a day you bhave to go to starbucks which is luckily next door.
The only good thing of this hotel is its location. Its right by a subway station and very close to central park and times square.
This hotel seems to have once been a great hotel but it isnt what it used to be. It does not deserve 4 stars! Not recommendable to go.

title: “Nice retreat from busy streets”
text: The Hilton Garden Inn Times Square is a nice retreat from the busy streets of the Theatre District. The rooms are nicely decorated (with beautiful black and white photos of NYC) and comfortable. Most importantly, they are well-sized and soundproofed. The hotel offers a fitness center and a business center. The latter is particular useful, though small: four computer stations with a fax and printer are available for free 24 hours/day for hotel guests. The staff were all friendly and responsive. Although I didn't order room service, the restaurant was always busy (leaving me to believe the food is good). The location is excellent-- walking distance to the theaters (so no fighting for taxis) plus easy access to the busses and subway lines. I'd definitely choose this hotel again.

title: “Riverwalk Convenience_DvB”
text: I was attending a conference for school officials with late notice. The hotel at which the conference was being held was full. I do not usually pick Four Point hotels but thought this price was very reasonable. Excitingly, this property is conveniently located to allow walking to great restaurants, bars, and the Riverwalk itself. The staff was very welcoming and even provided a nice welcome gift. The rooms are spacious and clean, and I had no trouble with any aspect of the hotel.

title: “Very convenient for shopping”
text: This is the second time i have stayed here and its great! its very close to the southcenter mall and there were many resturaunts in the area. The staff was very friendly and told me how to get where. The lobby computers were convenient to find more info about the area. the room was very clean and spacious. They would've given more towels, but i called the front desk and they sent them right up. i think this was a great hotel for the price. i reccomend it to anyone!

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
Marriotts are always a wise choice. The Lax location did not disappoint. The lobby sets the atmosphere. The staff are friendly and helpful. The rooms are spacious and clean. Comfortable beds are a plus. Convenient for business travelers as airport shuttle is provided.
Would highly recommend this property!

title: “Lovely hotel”
text: Close to Union Station so convenient for Amtrak travellers, Hotel George is a gem. Staff were attentive and knowledgeable, afternoon iced beverage in the lobby was a nice touch, and our well-appointed room included a walk-in shower. Perfect.

title: “Small but served its purpose”
text:
This hotel is clean and nice, however at first glance you can easily miss it. It almost has a "hole in the wall" feel to it. The lobby is quite small and when it gets busy, its really difficult to manouver in it. There there is no comp breakfast, the hotel has a restaurant that offers it (we did not eat there however).
There is comp wi-fi and a coffee maker in the room, but the room is the smallest I HolidayInn room I have ever stayed at. As you open the front door, you are met with the bed and the dresser. The bathroom is quite tiny as well.
It is within walking distance of Ground Zero, Ellis Island/Statue of Liberty, Southstreet Seaport, and Financial District. 
Not a bad stay overall

title: “Super Service”
text: I stayed at this hotel per my boss's recommendation with 8 other colleagues from Tokyo. We arrived very early in the morning from the airport and was not sure if we could check in much before the official check-in time. The front staff was so kind that everyone could check in and take good rests after the long flight from Tokyo. It was Easter Sunday and most restaurants were closed for lunch and dinner. Again the front staff called several restaurants, gave me a couple of choices, and finally booked a very good one for us all. The hotel staff was very responsive in any matter and did everything they could do to make our stay comfortable. I would definitely come back to this hotel and recommend my friends and colleagues to do so.

title: “Two granddaughters loved every minute”
text: I took my two granddaughters ages 9 and 11 to New York for three days as a birthday present and we stayed at the Marquis. They were properly impressed and loved the location. Everyone at the hotel treated us just as we had hoped that they would. The most unique thing is how the elevators operate. It was a little pricey but not to far out of line for a New York hotel. The room was much larger than other hotels in New York and the ammenities were well above others.

title: “Certainly not a 4 star, Hotwire price was not worth it.”
text:
The location is great for tourists hitting New York for a first or second time - particularly if you want to see some shows and Time Square. The room was relatively clean (expected better from a 4 star though) and the bed was large with elegant bedding. Our room was on the corner of the hotel with an incredible view (which was blocked out by thick curtains when we wanted which was necessary given the BRIGHT lights from the billboards).
However, there were many minor to middling issues:
The room was cleaned but there were stains on the bathroom wall, on the shower curtain, and on the wall just past he entry. I joked that they could be blood but my wife suggested red wine.
The headboard to the bed was nice, but three of the buttons (little black square tiles sewn into the matting) were loose on their threads, two of them hanging sadly down.
There were quite a bit of dust gathered around the bed legs where the vacuum clearly didn't reach ... clean enough to walk around on because my feet weren't going to touch their if the vacuum couldn't, but not exactly fresh. There were two pillows on each side of the bed, but the orange pillows were so hard as to be useless!
The bathroom was the biggest disappointment. If it was a 2-3 star hotel it would have met me expectations: not terribly small but clean towels and bottles of soap, shampoo, and conditioner. However, the floor and toilet bowl had some caulking stuck to them that could've been removed with some elbow grease or a razor. The lighting grate over the sink was quite dusty and misaligned (I pushed it into place for them).
Internet for $12.99/day? That's simply unreasonable these days, there were free wifi access points nearby but not accessible by all rooms.
Rather than extending our stay there by a third night, we moved closer to Downtown at the Ace Hotel on 29th st. It was INCREDIBLE by contrast - hip and super clean, simply a night and day difference. While we would not recommend the Millennium Broadway for anything over $100/night, the Ace Hotel was fantastic and we got a very reasonable price for a room at the last minute. Also, the gym at the Ace was MUCH better equipped.

title: “BEST BAR VIEW INDEED!!”
text:
We went to the lounge area after a very exciting evening in New York City and it was a perfect location. Comfortable and relaxing, we were sitting at full length windows of Times Square view just there! Ideal!
We were served well and everyone was very friendly!
We closed the place down and servers stayed friendly to the end!
I did not stay here however I would like to someday because it is a perfect location!!
At least, go to this lounge. Keep walking to the back to where you get to the big windows and the Times Square view! It is breathtaking!!

title: “Noisy and loud people in hotel which downgrades the hotel !”
text:
Booked this hotel for 3 nights end of april 2009. At arrival it was pretty bussy. The attendants were all very nervous with ed. There is only valet-parking and it is to busy.
The hotel looked beautiful but the average gast is a motel 6 -person. As classy as the hotel looks, as not classy are the average gasts. Loud and noisy ! 
The room we had was not clean at all. Carpeting was not vacumed for weeks and even coins lay on the ground and also some food ! We complained and got another room, but that was not cleaner. The location is good, on the riverwalk. But you have seen the riverwalk within a hour. Very very very loud and lots of people. Lot's of "MTV" Mexican youth with their pants 4 sizes too big and an attitude. Lots of bumbs outside of the riverwalk. We only stayd 1 night and cancelled the other 2 nights because of the not cleaned rooms, the noisy hotel with lines in front of the elevators and the loud people.

title: “NYC 2009”
text: This hotel was perfect! Great place to relax after walking endlessly!! Excellent location with plenty to offer. Just steps away from Times Square and very close to the 7th Ave subway and Times Square subway.

title: “Outstanding Boutique Hotel”
text: Great location, quiet hotel. Have stayed here twice and the hotel is wonderful. Very reasonably priced. I have been upgraded both times, one times into a huge suite with a piano. Made a reservation online at spg.com just 15 mins before I arrived and they had upgraded room all ready.

title: “Good value, great spot”
text:
We were only able to stay one night, so we paid extra to book a room overlooking the Riverwalk. This hotel is at one end of the Riverwalk, so it's not overlooking the noisier, busier parts of the area and is super convenient. You can watch the iconic river barges and river taxis float past, and easy to walk to everything: the Alamo, the restaurants, etc. Their in-house restaurant was a good value, too. 
Staff: friendy and helpful. The valet parking worked out well for us (though it's $25 per night). Typical of big tourist metro areas.
Someone else posted a compaint about a view of the gross rooftop across the river, but the view is BELOW - the Riverwalk is the draw here. The old building across is abandoned and lends a bit of character to an area that used to be really seedy and has been developed into Texas' biggest attraction. We liked it.

title: “Not perfect, but excellent value”
text:
We stayed at the San Antonio Drury Plaza in late July. We arrived late afternoon to find. The hotel staff at a near-meltdown. Apparently the hotel had a turnover of over a thousand guests, and housekeeping was having trouble getting the rooms ready quickly enough. Rosanna at the front desk invited us to the second floor for refreshments or the use of the rooftop pool while the rooms were completed. Her professionalism went a long way in keeping us happy. We decided to partake of some complimentary soft drinks and popcorn for the kids, and also enjoyed their 5:30-7pm "Kickback" which included light cocktails, soft drinks, chicken tenders, nachos, baked potatoes, salad, hot dogs, macaroni & cheese, etc. When we finally checked in at nearly 7pm, Rosanna comped our valet parking. Wow. 
The hotel room was very comfortable. We had a king suite which included a separate bedroom, a queen foldout couch, bath, refrigerator and microwave. This is the most comfortable bed I have stayed on.
The rooftop pool was very nice, although it could use the services of a good pool man. Water should not be green - my guess is that it was over chlorinated at some point and needs some conditioner to bring back the blue. In any case, the view of the Alamo City at night from the pool is absolutely dazzling.
There is easy access to the Riverwalk from the bottom floor, and the hotel is right in the middle of downtown. You are five to ten minutes from any destination on the River Walk.
Breakfast was nice - scrambled eggs, hotcakes, sausage, biscuits & gravy, pastries, cereal and fruit were all available, as are juices, coffee and tea. A very nice spread in this buffet, served on real dishes - not plastic or foam plates.
This hotel offers a big bang for the buck. This is a great property and is well run by a professional staff. While it's not perfect, I have yet to stay in a hotel that is. It is a lovely OLD building that has been converted to a hotel. Elevators are slow at peak times, and in some places it clearly shows its age. However the quality of the staff and the quality of the "extras" make this a place I will return to on business and for family holidays.

title: “FANTASTIC Stay!!”
text:
The hotel it beautiful! A 5-star all the way. I got there early and was able to get in a room. I asked for a fridge for medication and was given it with no charge very quickly. The room was perfect! Small, but very clean and the bath products wre great! They even have turn down service! The hotel is right next to the San Diego Civic Center where I was attending RENT. Great trip all around! Very close to the airport. $10 cab ride.
OH, and the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in!!!

title: “A pair of shoes stolen”
text:
I booked a room in this hotel for 4 nights (May 19-23, 2012) with my sister and brother-in-law to attend the funeral services of a relative. The location of this shotel is ideal due to accessibility from the freeway and proximity to the church where the wakes and services were held. We checked in late 7PM on the first day/night of May 19th and nothing happened. It was on the second day/night (May 20) that theft happened when a pair of shoes were stolen from our room. The room wasn't cleaned that day and privacy sign was up so no one was supposed to be in the room. Also we told the cleaner we met in the hallway not to clean our room that morning. We came back to our room late afternoon to change and left again after 5PM for the wake service and never came back until around 11PM that night. It was the next morning we discovered that the shoes were missing. The missing pair were not brand new slightly used. There were other newer pairs of shoes next to it but the thief took a particular liking to that pair of shoes. She or he must have been eyeing them earlier. We reported this theft to the front desk at 2 separate times. On the first time, the lady wrote it down in their logbook. On the second time we reported, we were already checking out from the hotel the morning of May 23rd. The front desk lady promised to report to their Management somewhere. I would like to warn future guests of this hotel to watch out not just their valuables but also their shoes. I wonder if there were other similar incidents in the past in that hotel that we never knew or warned. Thanks for reading.
NNB

title: “Another Great Kimpton Property”
text: I stayed at the Topaz Hotel for three nights while on business in D.C. From the Aveda products to the fabulous bathrobes and nice welcoming touches in the room, I will definitely return the next time I'm in D.C. The room was spacious and clean. The staff, without exception, was friendly and outgoing. The location was excellent with great restaurants and shopping nearby. The metro is a short distance and taxis were always available in the front of the hotel. The restaurant seemed like they were still trying to figure out who they are, but no problems as the dining in the area is superb. The only semi-odd thing, which I'd read a review about and forgot until I heard barking, is that they allow pets. Overall, it was an excellent place to hole up for three nights.

title: “Great Location, Staff for Us”
text:
This was our first trip to NYC and the Hilton Garden Inn proved to be the perfect hotel for us. The location on 8th Ave between 48th & 49th was absolutely perfect for everything we were doing. Times Square is about a block away along with many theaters being very close by. The staff was very helpful and friendly. The adjacent restaurant & bar was nice to have breakfast or a drink in the evening. Our room was a very nice size for the two of us and was very clean.
We enjoyed restaurants near our hotel as well as on 46th (restaurant row). We were pleasantly surprised at the cost of our meals in this area. We had been told everything would be very expensive. We did not find this to be the case. While not cheap, our meals were not much more than they would be at a nice restaurant at home.
We would highly recommend the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square to our family and friends. We did stop in many of the high-end hotels and while they are beautiful, we felt more comfortable at the Hilton Garden Inn. It suits us perfectly.

title: “A brilliant location”
text: This is a 'predictable' motor inn. Good sized rooms with clean and helpful staff. It is in a very good location and close to some good eateries, coffee shops (try Noah's bagels around the corner for breakfast) and good spots for evening drinks.Tourist Buses run nearby.

title: “Great Family place”
text: Great hotel, walking distance( good walk) to the Mall. We stayed with our teenage son at this hotel for 3 nights. Overall this is a great hotel. It's clean and well kept.Has a small pool, The staff is very helpful. We arrived early at 11:00 am, our room was not ready yet, but we parked the car and within 2 hours we could check in. At check out we kept our car 2 more hours at the parking with no add. cost. The free breakfast was awesome! The room (studio) was very spacious. The sofa turns into a bed. The bathroom was clean and nice. Also, this hotel is located in a great area --- it's a 5 minute walk to the metro. If you're looking for a place to stay in the DC area, this is it! No restaurants in the area but pizza place & Mc Donald's very close, also deli store, but it's closed early.Stay on the upper floor facing the street, (no noise from the train)

title: “Great Location/Friendly staff”
text: We stayed at the Casablanca from 17-20 December. The staff on reception/door men were extremely friendly and offered us advice where to eat / how to find certain stores etc. The hotel was small - safe enough for our twins (age 10) to go and get themselves a drink or biscuit from Rick's cafe. The rooms were very clean (my only gripe - we didn't really need the towels changed every day - would have been nice to have a sign saying only change when requested). As in other reviews, no view from the room but we were out all day anyway. We enjoyed a rest before seeing a show on Broadway (Mary Poppins - a must see) in the cafe - having wine and bread/cheese/crudites (between 5-8pm). Complimentary breakfast (pastries/fruit salad) was also a nice touch. Location - a few metres from Times Sq - very handy to walk everywhere (although taxis are very cheap compared to England). Overall, we would certainly recommend it. ps. Beds comfy too!!

title: “good location, decent facilities, pricey parking”
text:
This hotel is located a short drive from the airport. It overlooks the north island naval base so your kids will see ships and aircraft coming and going. The $19/night parking is ridiculous...
The restaurant provides a good breakfast, which is a little pricey starting at $13

title: “Suites are Perfect for Traveling with Children”
text: We recently stayed at the Hotel Contessa while we vacationed in San Antonio. The 1 bedroom suite was perfect for traveling with our children. The living room area had a pull out sofa and one t.v. while the bedroom had another t.v. The rooms were nicely furnished and very clean. The hotel is located in a quiet area of the Riverwalk and was very convenient for walking to everything. We loved the hotel restaurant brunch which we ate outside by the Riverwalk; it was also reasonably priced. Although the hotel pool was being renovated during our visit, the hotel had made arrangements for guests to use the Westin pool next door which was fine with our kids.

title: “Very convient to everything!”
text: Loved the location. Everyone was very helpful, and friendly. Can't wait to go back next year!

title: “Wonderful Hotel, Close-In, Charm & Character”
text: Just returned from Easter weekend stay at Willard in DC. Stayed in Exec Suite on 8th floor (Room 800) which had great view of Pennsylvania Avenue. Having been to the area before, stopped by Cafe Du Parc for their wonderful steamed mussels. If you like mussels, these are some of the best we've ever had. Sweet, tender, plump. Easter brunch at Occidental next to the hotel also very good. Accolades to the front desk check in who personally escorted us to a couple of rooms for our selection--what great personal service. Lobby of hotel has real charm with the Peacock alley tea service and the Round Robin bar. Only blocks area from White House or Mall...an excellent choice for a DC weekend.

title: “Good location And Package Deal”
text:
We got a room with a view of the Washington Monument that included free breakfast for two adults, free valet parking and Metro passes. The location was excellent, a short walk from the mall and perfect for the sightseeing itinerary that we had planned. The parking attendant was welcoming, the bell staff rather pushy, and the front desk staff hospitable. After hours, with no concierge on duty, the young lad at the front desk was very helpful with restaurant recommendations and called for a reservation on our behalf.
The room was on the small side, with two smallish queen beds to sleep two adults and two children but there was no better option to sleep four of us. We spent so little time in the room that the beds were the only thing that mattered.
I should say that it was extremely difficult finding the hotel entrance. We circled the plaza area and parking garages several times, even upon returning after dinner and the next day, before we could figure out where to turn in for the hotel.
The breakfast buffet was excellent, and the restaurant service was very obliging.

title: “Outstanding Customer Service”
text: This is my hotel when in Austin. Management is great, providing outstanding customer service. Jennifer is wonderful, she is friendly and has a great warm smile. I love staying here. When I have a problem they take care of it right away

title: “Fabulous!!!”
text: I LOVED my stay at the Omni Severin. I had an amazing Phenomenal Friday rate which they promptly upgraded to a Plaza Suite after I joined their Select Guest program. I walked into the most beautiful suite I'd ever seen. I had a huge bed, beautiful living area, 2 tv's, a fluffy robe, fabulous balcony. I had a wonderful stay and was met with nothing but exemplary service. I'm from NYC so the street noise made me feel right at home. I will definitely stay at the Omni again if I'm ever in Indianapolis and look forward to staying at other Omni properties.

title: “GREAT FACILITIES FOR A CONFERENCE”
text:
The facilities of this hotel is great!
Be sure that the hotel does not overbook itself for your conference. Also- hotel does not understand what the word BLOCK of rooms means. They will split up your party amoung towers and floors unless you harrass the front desk personnel. This was frustrating with minors.

title: “Nice Place, on the Riverwalk!”
text: Great place to stay on a get away weekend! Staff was very nice and friendly. The breakfast was way more then you would get free, in any other hotel, and to top that off, they have free drinks in the early evening hours. It is about a 5 min. walk to the main part of the river but, a very nice walk.

title: “Love this place!!”
text: A group of 10 of us stayed over the Memorial Day wknd May 2011. We also stayed Memorial Day wknd May 2010. We love this getaway with friends! It's a bit pricey but well worth it! They have the best poolside service, restaurant service, etc. The rooms are nice, clean and quiet. The hotel is BEAUTIFUL and has georgeous views!

title: “Wonderful stay”
text: The staff are always friendly; the location is convenient to shopping and museums, located close to bus and subway lines. Breakfast and afternoon tea is delightful.

title: “Chinatown, NOT Soho”
text: I booked this hotel based on its description as the Holiday Inn/Downtown Manhattan/Soho. Imagine my shock, then, when the cab stopped in CHINATOWN. If you don't believe me, check out the photo - the hotel's name is written in English and in Chinese, just like everything else in the area. Apparently Soho borders Chinatown, and the hotel is on the Chinatown end of the border but technically has a Soho address, thus the misleading description. The only time I felt unsafe during my visit to NYC was one night when we climbed out of the subway onto the street a block from the hotel. Every window, it seemed, was barred and the streets were deserted except for one screaming drunk/crazy person, who of course was directly in our path to the hotel. This hotel also looks nothing like the glowing photo featured on the Holiday Inn Web site and on this page. In fact, we could barely find it, as the only thing marking it on the street as the Holiday Inn were a few nondescript, tiny flags. On the plus side, the hotel was clean and the staff friendly and helpful, and it is only a short walk to the subway. I just didn't appreciate being misled by the supposed trendy Soho location.

title: “A Short Walk to Affordability in NYC”
text: This has been our hotel of choice the last three visits to NYC. It's a bit off the beaten path, but it's an enjoyable walk and only a long block from the subway. The small size of the room is a fun switch from the full-size rooms we're used to. And the best part of this hotel is the shared bathrooms, believe it or not. They're clean and have great rainfall shower heads and soothing music piped into the room. There's also a rooftop complete with picnic tables and it's open in nice weather offering views of the city. They have an outdoor cafe that's a nice way to start the morning with coffee. Of course, it's not open during the cold winter months. The price makes this hotel an affordable option to the higher priced, more centrally located big chain hotels. I flew into LaGuardia on a Saturday morning and arrived here exactly 20 minutes after walking off of the plane. It was an easy taxi ride.

title: “great location”
text: It's in a great area, a really short walk to the capital and lots of places to eat. The rooms are on the small side and don't touch the snack bar! $8 for a handful of cashews, but it's what you would expect from a JW. Also the parking was pretty pricey so if you drive in be prepared.

title: “Dream is a nightmare”
text: I stayed here on October 18, 2004, and the place really was a nightmare. It was still under construction and shouldn't have been receiving guests. My first room had exposed wiring and a lock that didn't work. They moved me. The second room also had a lock that didn't work and required a number of instrusive visits from hotel staff. A closet filled with garbage - yes garbage - was directly across from my room. Most of the time, the closet door was open. Although the decor purports to be hip, it's like sleeping in a meat locker. A clossal disappointment, especially for the price.

title: “Maybe I'm just not as picky as some of the others ...”
text: I thought the Westin was fine. The complaint about a long wait to check in was certainly true. That was a bit of a pain. The room was sizeable, slept great. Enjoyed the 11th floor view of downtown each morning. Rate was 179 a night. Only thing I can figure is people forked out a lot of dough for this place and had high expectations -- certainly can understand that. But again, it's a classy place, and it is within walking distance of a lot of downtown.

title: “Fit for a king... but you had to be one!”
text: Myself and my wife honeymooned in NYC in November 2002 and we thought we woud splash out on this fine hotel. Entering the hotel, the foyer and reception area met our expectations and affluence...checkin was swift and friendly...but thats where it ended. I forget what floor we were on but we were allocated a broom-closet of a room...the smallest room we have ever stayed in. I contacted reception and made mention of this and played the "honeymoon" card but the hotel was full and there was nothing to be done...extremely disappointing given the cost and our level of anticipation.While we were there, the King of a lesser middle eastern country was visiting NYC and staying at the hotel. So for two days before and during his stay, the hotel was full of agents of one kind or another - making lounging around the hotel a little uneasy.I bet the King didnt have to close his closet to watch his TV!!!In summary, the hotel is overrated, slightly the worse for wear and lack of repair and needs to take care of its customers better (I filled out a comment card with negative comments hoping for a followup call/email which never materialised)

title: “Personal Touch makes all the difference”
text: We had a phenomenal stay. Best Location, Best Value, Best Staff, Best Lobby. The staff went above and beyond our expectations to ensure our stay was fantastic. The beds were sooo comfortable. I visited all the other hotels we considered staying at-- We hit the JackPopt with Villa Florence. Highly recommend this upscale boutique hotel with 2 great restaurants included. Eduardo was extremely helpful and knowledgeable, when we were considering booking. The Valet Staff was also great. The 2 reasons we chose Villa Florence were,1, Edardo responded to the trip advisors comments ( shows he cares) 2. Frommers recommendation...One of the best vacations we ever had. Thanks Villa Florence!

title: “Alright, but a few issues”
text:
Overall, the room was nice and the service was good enough. The hotel is in what could be a good location, but it seems that virtually everything closes early. I couldn't find a place to eat outside of the hotel that was open after 8pm within walking distance of the hotel. This may be a function of Columbus as much as this hotel, but I picked a central, downtown hotel because I could walk to things. I just didn't expect everything to be closed.
When checkin in I was given a coupon for a discount for food which was nice. I tried to use it for breakfast since I had to leave early for work in the area. There were two couples already eating when I came down, but I couldn't find any employees in the restaurant. I waited for a bit at the "please wait to be seated" sign, and then just wandered the fairly small restaurant to see if I could find someone. Nope. No one. After a few more minutes I gave up and ate on the road. This reduced the value of the coupons fairly substantially in my mind and, sadly, my overall experience with them.

title: “Gencon Trip”
text:
We stayed at the Sheraton for our Gen Con convention due to its location. 
The room was nice and clean, the bed was fine. We paid the extra money to be able to go to the club room. It had snacks, breakfast items, and most evenings wine and cheese. We stopped at the club room most afternoons to relax and play a game or two at the tables. They had yummy brownies and cookies in the evening for us to enjoy. My only complaint was the $25 dollar a day charge for parking. It was an added expense I was not expecting. When I asked the front desk person about the charge she was very snippy about it, and said all the hotels charged for parking. I have traveled to Indianapolis for business trips frequently, and I can say that not every hotel charged me for parking. The pool also was looking a little dated, it needed a face lift. Overall a good experience, the club room had yummy food, and a nice person working there, and the room was clean and comfortable. The staff at check in could have been nicer, and I was surprised by the $25 dollar daily fee.

title: “Worthy of the high ranking”
text:
A cousin's wedding brought me to San Francisco a few weeks ago. The wedding party reserviced blocks of 20 rooms at the Donatello and a local motor inn. The price for the Donatello wasn't that much higher. And it was far lower than nearby hotels with less favorable reviews. 
Location, location, location. The hotel is right in Union Square. The BART (metro) station is a couple of blocks downhill. You couldn't ask for a better location.
Aside from the location, the staff were great. All were helpful, especially with getting me a taxi during a big Oracle Convention. Ellisson and company litterally take over San Francisco. All of the taxis seem to follow. My preference for tranpsort is the bus. The cable cars aren't very fast and it was impossible to get on one. There was a huge line for them at Fisherman's Wharf.
I called the hotel in advance to reqest a room facing away from the street. The desk staff assigned a room for me on the 6th floor, overlooking a roof or parking garage. I heard very little street noise. 
The bed was on the firm side but still comfortable. The room had plenty of space including a small couch and coffee table. Wifi was free. My room key had a small piece of paper with the password next to it.
The bathroom was good, pretty typical of a good hotel. I liked that the shower has an inner and outer curtain liner. My only gripe was getting the shower temperature just right. Very small adjustments would change the temp too much. Toiletries included shampoo, bars of soap and body lotion. No shower gel, no big deal.
Next door to the hotel is a company that rents bicycles. I'm in good shape but I was not quite prepared for the hills (and I'm not talking about Lombard Street). The ride to Golden Gate park is scenic and fairly easy.

title: “Excellent service but limited smoking room availability”
text:
I forgot an entire drawer full of my belongings in my room. Realizing this only after I unpacked on returning home to Atlanta, I contacted the hotel housekeeping and was delighted with the service provided by the Housekeeping Manager, Angelo Blakely. He personally searched for my belongings by checking with his staff and had them shipped UPS the next day. Everything missing was in the package and Angelo went above and beyond in providing excellent customer service!! 
My only discomfort was that I'm a Hilton Gold VIP member so was disappointed when I had to switch rooms in the middle of my stay because this hotel didn't have enough smoking rooms available for the entire duration of my stay and I moved to a non-smoking room. Even though I'd booked my room weeks in advance of my arrival.

title: “Yes, yes yes”
text: Great hotel, great staff, and my goodness, great view. I promised I would write a good review if my requests were met -- pretty simple requests really. Early check in and a great view of the Empire State Building. Well, we were allowed to check in 3 hours early...and the Empire State Building practically jumped into our room. The rooftop bar is a hidden gem too. You'll pay up, but you'll also be having a cocktail, staring at the NYC skyline. Yes, yes, yes...stay here.

title: “Great location”
text:
This hotel is located right next to Faneuil Hill and the Quincy Market. You also have the harbor at a few steps, the freedom trail and best of all, a subway station right on the left which is just two stations from the airport so the location is worth the price.
The hotel is clean and nice, staff is friendly and the hotel rooms are nice, not really small. I had some problems connecting to the Wi-Fi but nothing that a quick call to the provider's customer service couldn't solve. Too bad the lobby was being remodeled so there was a little noisy there. Overall, this is a very nice hotel with a great location.

title: “Excellent Location. V. friendly staff”
text: Stayed here at the end of last year. Staff were amazingly friendly and helpful. Location was great. Easy walking distance to everything. Spot on.

title: “An excellent experience”
text: Certainly its age remains apparent despite the restoration, but if you enjoy staying somewhere with character rather than sterile or ostentatious, this is a great stay. It's more like a bed and breakfast without the obligatory group breakfast. The staff were all as attentive and helpful as we have seen anywhere. The building has such character. It's not on the Riverwalk, but just a very brief walk there--one complaint I read about being far from everything likely emanated from the fact you do have the feeling that you are away from it all even though you aren't. Hemisfair Park is right across the street and that end of the R'walk is a pleasant walk thru the park of less than a mile, while the restaurant end is even closer in the other direction. If you want character, service, and a little distance btwn you and the R'walk, watch for a discount offering on this place.

title: “I loved it and will be back!”
text: I love San Francisco. Best city in the West. My stay there made the trip even more pleasant. Stayed at the Clift Hotel in Theatre District. Excellent location just a short distance from BART that brought us from the airport. It was central to everything. Cleanest hotel I have visited in quite a while. Close to many eateries. The decor on the lobby floor was a bit unusual -- there is a massive chair sitting in a curtained alcove that reminded me of the Horror House at Disney but it was not bad. I loved the hotel and would definately recommend this to anyone who is a bit flinicky about their surroundings.

title: “Would not stay at again”
text: Decided to stay at the Orchard based on location and online hype. Good location, the rest is hype. Our reservation for 2 double rooms was not kept, instead we were given 1 double and 1 king. Beds are ROCK hard. Rude front desk, had to argue at great length to get room situation corrected for 2nd and 3rd night of our stay. Breakfast was ok, just hard boiled eggs, fruit, cereal and toast. (Go instead to Mama's on Washington Sq.) Nothing special...except the exceptionally rude staff during breakfast. On the other hand, the rooms were clean and nicely decortated, but we sure could not get past those AWFUL beds. Will not bother to stay there again. One very bright note...FANTASTIC doormen that always had GREAT suggestions and huge smiles on their faces...especially Cornelius.

title: “Where to stay in NYC and why”
text: From the moment we stepped into the hotel our five senses came alive. It is beautiful to look at, the furnishing are comfortable and inviting, sounds of travelers from all over who a were cheery and personnel was happy to assist, the bartender's special drinks, and the incredible fragrance that permeates the lobby (which we asked if they knew the name of the scent so we could purchase it). This hotel is exactly what a person/s needs when traveling, it was a fabulous perk to our unforgettable visit to NYC.

title: “Very nice stay”
text: Came down for the football game..... Our room (3rd floor city view) was very large ; loved having a fireplace to come back to after wandering in the rain. No noise issues to report - everything worked well. Wonderful beer selection in the bar (microbrews as opposed to commercial sludge) I wish Seattle had more waterfront access - but a good time was had by all

title: “Pretty good place”
text: This is a great hotel. Probably needs a little money put into it but overall great value. Everyone has to have one complaint though, right...one thing I dislike are miniature ironing boards. If you have an upgraded/larger room can't you at least have a full size ironing board? Fast and easy checkin check out which is great after 3 hotels in 6 days.

title: “Great location, clean, friendly service”
text: Just returned from 3 nights in this hotel with my sisters. We went for an Oprah taping, which was a 10 minute taxi ride from the hotel. The hotel is in an excellent location, with lots of restaurants in walking distance (Harry Caray's Steakhouse is across the street). The room was very clean and comfortable. Stainless appliances in the well-stocked kitchen. Breakfast was included and was one of the best ones I've had - waffles (which Isme, the friendly server made for us), eggs, sausage, potatoes alond with muffins, cereal, fruit and yogurt. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Simply the Best”
text:
This hotel is second to none, my wife and I spent 3 days last week and it was the best 3 days we have spent in any hotel across the world. From the front door, greeting person and front desk through to the amazing club level everyone of my wishes were answered.
Great job and we will be back.

title: “Excellent SD Hotel”
text:
We stayed one night at Humphrey's. I was a bit concerned since there were some not so great reviews and this isn't your normal chain place, but I couldn't disagree with them more.
The layout of the place was great. We were in a bottom floor room, I believe 6 or so buildings down from the lobby, that had a sliding patio door out to a patio area. Yes that patio faced the parking lot, but the plants & fence around it that made it a good place to just sit outside and chill. The pool area seemed really nice, we didn't use it but it seemed like those that did were really enjoying it. There is a picture on here of a larger building that looks like it has multiple rooms in that building. The room we were in was in a building that had 4 rooms on the bottom floor, 4 above it, the stairs to the upstairs rooms connected that floor to the neighboring building's upper floor. The ice & vending were right outside of our room but we never heard anything from that or the parking lot.
This hotel was a great location for everything we were doing in North SD County, Coronado, and downtown. It was even a close drive to the airport. It seemed like a pretty close drive to places like Sea World and Balboa Park too.
Our room was really nice, none of the "half remodeled" stuff that others have referred to. I am actually really picky about cleanliness & rooms falling apart, this place seemed right on the ball.
There was some sort of Veteran's Day 5K or something that closed the street the hotel is on. I was really glad they let us know. We just walked up the block that morning and by the time we were ready to check out, the participants were getting into their cars & walking around, but the road had re-opened & we were fine to leave.
All together I would love to stay at this location the next time we're in San Diego. The whole area was just a cute quaint little waterfront area. It was just great!

title: “Third trip and not dissapointed!”
text:
This was our third trip to the Hard Rock Chicago, and we were not disappointed. We typically travel as a couple, but this spring on a whim decided to take our toddlers into the city. We weren't sure if the Hard Rock, known for its music, bar, and rock star atmosphere would be good for kids. We were welcomed with smiles though, and felt right at home, even with our kids. The Vallet was very accomadating, opening doors every time we came in/out of the hotel with the stroller, giving us the best directions to Shedd Aquarium by subway so our kids could ride the train, and helping us load/unload all of our gear. 
They had a roll away bed available for us, which was nice. 
Never disappointed with the service here. Great location, just across the street from Giordano's pizza and around the corner from The Corner Bakery and shopping. We will keep coming back! I just hope they get a rewards system for repeat customers. It would be nice to get perks for staying so often! ;)

title: “Overpriced and Paper Thin Walls !”
text: I stayed at the Hilton for 4 nights and have to change room several times.One night I was woken up by noise from, a male and female in the room next door around 1 30am (there was an interconnecting door that allowed noise to travel easily).At the same time the people on the other side of my room had their clock radio (beside the bed in every room so watch out for this !) switched on and were playing music - the walls are so thin everything couldf be heard - even with my own headphones switched on - I could hear every word from both rooms! This was the case when guests turned on their TVs etc on other nights.The 14th floor which was refurbished was better decor (my first floor 12 was very shabby and poorly decorated).The bathrooms were badly designed so you had to close the door everytime you wanted to go to the bathroom otherwise you couldnt sit in the bathroom comfortably ! at $ 300 a night I ve had far better value at much more upscale chains like Ritz Carlton = the staff were friendly but this is a huge hotel that trades on business/conference/vacation short stops ! I urge you to try somewhere else if you want a peaceful nights sleep ! Having to pay $ 15 to use the gym at this rate is unaceptable especially with no breakfast.Doors slammed loudly on the corridors with guests leaving and arriving at their rooms at diffrent times.You could also hear the drapes being opened and closed by guests in adjoinig rooms ! sleep well I hope if you stay there !

title: “Great Airort Hotel”
text: I never stay at airport hotels but I will certainly stay at the Hyatt again. This new property is top notch. Great rooms with flat screens and even better bath rooms. Nice bar area, ok-ish restaurant and a great health club...there is even a roof top pool to catch some Texas rays.

title: “Other than check-in, was nice”
text:
We did arrive at the Argonaut at 2:30pm, instead of the 3pm check-in time. I felt like I was being reprimanded for arriving 30 minutes early. The front desk clerk remided me of the check in time and I was told to take a seat in the lobby and they would let me know when my room was ready. As we were sitting there, I noticed other guests arriving and immediately being handed their room keys and going to their rooms. No one ever came to let us know our room was ready until I walked up to the counter just after 3pm and stood behind others checking in and asked why others were getting keys and we were still waiting. They simply forgot about us. 
The room we booked was a standard room, decorated nicely, and overlooked a courtyard with restaurants and shops (I guess it is called the cannery). There are brick walls and huge wooden beams in the room and the hallways left over from the cannery the hotel was made from. It was unique and looked nice. There were several selections of wine served in the lobby in the afternoon. 
We were given a great recommendation for dinner from the concierge. It is called Albona Ristorante Istriano; Albona for short. What a wonderful dinner experience. It is located on Francisco St. It is a small, intimate place, and is warm and cozy. Because of its size, make reservations. The owner Bruno will come over to your table and welcome you with open arms, talk to you about his restaurant, and the evening's specialties. Later he will stop by to see how you liked your dinner. Don't miss it!

title: “Great location, Comfortable Beds!”
text:
I love the feeling I had as I entered the hotel - it's bright with interesting art and a really friendly staff. We were there for 3 nights. The room had 2 double beds and I loved having 4 plush pillows all to myself! You are able to hear your neighbors, as the walls are thin - and there was one day when housekeeping never cleaned our room, so when we arrived back after touring downtown I had to call and request someone come up. 
Outside of that, this was a good location with helpful staff. Our room was relaxing and comfortable and the stroll down the riverwalk to downtown was gorgeous. I would stay in this hotel again.

title: “When In Chicago Stay at the Hyatt at McCormick Place”
text:
I stayed at the Hyatt McCormick Place and was very impressed. The suite was beautiful, the views we outstanding. We were able to view a fireworks display at the Navy pier form our room on Saturday night - I wondered if Liz, the Guest Experience Manager, ordered that display for our party. Service was excellent, the suite was excellent and very roomy. The view of downtown Chicago and the lake were awesome. 
The staff was great and helped us out by providing extra trash cans in the room. We had a get together at my suite after the graduation, 30 people and tons of food fit easily. The staff helped us transport the supplies and food in and out of the hotel.
It was an excellent location as I was attending an event at UoC. Access to downtown was very easy. I would very much like to stay here again. As a matter of fact, it was very hard to leave the room to head back home. LCD tv, great walk-in closet, nice living room area and very highly recommended!
I want to thank Liz and the staff for making my stay a memorable and enjoyable stay.

title: “Hotel Commonwealth”
text: This hotel deserves it's superlative reputation. The staff are so friendly and helpful to make sure that your stay is perfect. Before we arrived at the hotel, we informed them of our impending 25th wedding anniversary during our stay and were absolutely delighted to find out that we had been upgraded to a junior suite room. The hotel itself is in an excellent location, just on top of Kenmore T station which is so convenient for travelling downtown. It is also just opposite some small takeaway restaurants for coffee and bagels etc. Dining at the Eastern Standard Restaurant was a highpoint of our stay as it was brimming with atmosphere, with a very friendly, efficient waiter service. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone coming to Boston.

title: “First time in New york”
text: My husband,myself, and our 3 children stayed here during spring break. We found the staff to be very friendly and helpful. The breakfast was okay, after all, it is a continental breakfast. The elevators were an issue, so we took the stairs, luckily we were only on the sixth floor. The location was great! The price was the best we could find. I did notice that some of the other people staying there were not so nice to the staff, and in return they were not going out of their way to help them. The room was clean, but the halls are in need of repair. We would stay again.

title: “Quality!”
text: Not a 5 Star full service hotel, but in many ways it is better. Very clean, price is competitive and the extras make this place a must stay.

title: “Worst Hotel Experience”
text:
We just came out of our worst experience of Hotel Stay in US. It not only spoilt our much awaited vacation but has shaken our faith on Choice hotels.
Me and my fried made 2 reservations and both of us had to undergo same nuisance for 3 days.
As we have small kids , While booking the hotel we requested a Microwave in our room.We were committed for the microwave but while reaching the hotel we found that not only Microwave but even Coffee maker was missing from the room. Person at reception had no idea how to deal with it. He promised to arrange for one in next few hrs but could not do so for next 3 days. He kept saying that his maintenance staff is not cooperating with him.
During the first night itself ,Air Conditioner did not work for whole night and Worked intermittent for next 2 nights. Once again no one came to fix the issue but we were told that there might be some issue with wiring or power load issue as hotel was fully booked.
Air Conditioner was coming out of window fixture and highly unsafe to stay with children. One can easily look into the room from outside due to gaps in the AC and window.
Our Room's Door magnetic Card worked intermittently and every evening we had to go to reception to get it fixed. As usual , they don’t have any reason for it.
There was huge queues during Breakfast time and single lady in the Kitchen was unable to handle the rush. Queue in the counter were bigger than queues in Disney
Manager during checkout was rude and kept smiling when we mentioned about our exp. Staff seemed to be least bothered to listen to the customer (not even pretending). We mentioned that we will be lodging a complaint but there was hardly any response to that and person handed over our receipt to us and turned back to his work.
With the kind of experience we had, I don’t think we are going to choose or recommend any of the Choice Hotels to anyone.

title: “Jerks”
text:
My husband and I always try to get away on the anniversary of our only child's death, March 31st. I had read about the Tuscan Inn and booked it well in advance for our arrival. It sounded like a great place to be for the occasion.
We took a train from Santa Barbara, and I knew we were going to arrive quite late. I was looking forward to the assurance of our lovely room awaiting us. As it turned out, we arrived at around 3:00 A. M. totally exhausted. We were supposed to have arrived around 10 P.M.
But I had guaranteed with my credit card, so I knew we could just get there and go to sleep.
Well we arrived and THEY HAD SOLD OUR ROOM! I was totally shocked.
The snide, sadistic clerk at the desk was completely unapologetic and sarcastic. QUINN. He said he found us another room that was like the one we'd reserved non-smoking King. We also always look for free wi-fi. We were taken to another hotel where the room was totally reeking of cigarettes, because it was a smoking room, and 2 twin beds. By then it was almost 4:00 A.M. Internet access was not free.
I was so upset and angry, and that desk clerk is nothing but a black hole for Best Western's public relations. There was no" MISTAKE"-there was no "MISUNDERSTANDING"But there was an abundance of ill will and greed.
If a late arrival guarantee has NO meaning, and is not honored by the hotel, than how can I trust their hospitality code? I have NEVER had such a crappy experience at a hotel. I really feel that he sized us up and decided to try to wield power, because there was nothing we could do.
I will tell all my friends about this, and we are not, despite Quinn's assessment of our social status, a bunch of unsophisticated hillbillies.
This was way below terrible.

title: “Not a three star”
text: I got an excellent price on this hotel from Priceline but it has some problems. Priceline has it listed as a three star - it may be a three star in Mexico or China but not in Texas! It appears that they started redecorating but stopped. Although the furniture is new and modern the carpets were VERY badly worn and dirty. The cleaning seems to be sub-par also as my bathtub had hair in it and the desk lamp was covered with small stains (it looked as though someone had sneezed near it). But, as I said, I got a good price. If Priceline let me exclude hotels, I would exclude this one.

title: “Never again”
text: I have never experience such bad service as I did in this hotel. First when we arrived the room was not ready, then they gave me the wrong room,when we finally got the room as I enter that room I notice the carpet being really dirty, the linen on the bed was dirty, as I enter the restroom the mirror had water stains everywhere, there were hair on the floor, the shower curtain was dirty and I can go on and on but the thing is that I mention this to the housekeeper crystal when she came to check the room after it has been clean, she said that she would make sure the room was clean next time, but the next day the room was dirty again. Then when I inform front desk nothing was done. The noise that come from the hall every time someone is getting ice. Never the less my experience in the hotel was awful.

title: “Looks nothing like the glamorous website pictures, spend your money elsewhere”
text:
