My fiancé and I chose this hotel based on a great Travelzoo deal we got, and changed from another hotel reservation we had on Harbor Island. The hotel does not look as pretty and “spa” like as pictured on their website. It overlooks a blah lagoon, and the scenery is average. Our bell boy looked literally like a bum, dirty shirt tucked out, pants hung low, and in dire need of sleep. That was not a good start. The garden view room is okay – clean and dated, nothing spectacular. If you have kids and are going to SeaWorld, this is probably the place for you as the location is convenient. Romantic it is not – we could hear kids running and screaming around at night before their “bed time”. 
Don’t let the pictures deceive you, and only stay here if you are going to be nearby. I wish we would have stayed at Harbor Island, our original location, as we were in San Diego to go sailing, and not to go to SeaWorld.
Not to mention, they charge you $20/night for parking. I can understand for hotels downtown, but in Mission Bay? Not reasonable at all.

title: “Very nice hotel - well located”
text:
Stayed at the James for 5 nights in August. Check in was a breeze and our luggage was waiting for us in our room. Very helpful and friendly staff all round.
The room itself is nice and modern, the bathroom was large which made a change! However the only thing with the bathroom was the sink, it was pleasing to look at but was too big and flat and as a result it didnt drain properly.
Beds were large and comfortable and the room we stayed in had a little nook with a couch and table where you could set up your laptop/write postcards etc....
Very well located, just a block from Michigan Ave and close to bus and train stops.
It was a blessing in disguise that we didnt receive free breakfast as E'leaven across the street serves the most fantastic breakfasts (try the french toast!)
All in all a very enjoyable stay and would def recoomend.

title: “Cool Looking Hotel but Beware”
text: Great location, hip looking hotel, but...VERY noisy so bring earplugs (you hear outside noise the people above you, below you etc...) Also, the windows are not well sealed so the wind comes in and you just can't seem to get warm. We ordered room service that was to take 15-20 minutes and showed up 45 minutes later. When my daughter was blowdrying her hair the electriciy went out in the room. The best was the people on our floor smoking the Mary Jane. Really?? Just not the best family hotel. With all the options, you can do much better !

title: “Nice place to stay in San Francisco”
text: Superb hotel!! Comfortable beds, large bathroom, very friendly staff. This was my second visit to the Taj Campton Place in 6 weeks and each time I thoroughly enjoyed my stay. You can't beat the location in Union Square and the staff make you feel at home!! Hats off to Remy who went out of his way to find us umbrellas on a very rainy day when they ran out by the front door. It's the little things like this that make the Campton Place a great place to stay. Can't wait to go back.

title: “Amazing!”
text: The room was exceptionally large for a hotel room in NYC, and the location was super convenient, right next to the ACE train. The rooms were clean and I loved the size of the bathrooms and shower. Customer service was very good, and made me feel very welcome

title: “Great Location”
text:
After having read some of the previous review I did not have great expectations for this hotel. We chose it because we are Marriott Gold members and an event we were attending was being held at the hotel. 
We were pleasantly surprised. We were upgraded to an Executive King, which was in the corner, so we had a larger than average room and a beautiful view of the park across the street and the street below; we could even see the Washington Monument. Yes, the bathroom is smaller than the one I had in my first apartment, but it seemed to have been updated and was adequate. The Concierge Lobby was excellent; plenty of good food; if you were seriously on a budget you could realistically eat all your meals there, and the view is spectacular. Staff is professional, polite, and friendly, although I was disappointed with the Concierge service. The person I spoke to seemed to know very little about the city. Overall, I would recommend it and would return.

title: “Charming well located boutique hotel”
text:
We enjoyed our stay at 414 Hotel. 
This is the best alternative tho the skyscraper-type of hotels in the area.
Only two blocks away from Times Square, yet in a very pleasant neighborhood,
where the hight of the buildings is limited and there are trees along the street.
There are plenty of restaurants nearby. 
The room was clean, facing the little charming terrace on the back, hence no street noise. Breakfast was included, we sat at a rather small table with other guests.
Sweats, doughnuts, coffee, tea, fruit juice, etc. 
No complains, this hotel was perfectly in line with what we paid for.

title: “I know it's New Years but come on”
text: The hotel was very nice, the guy at the bar was great also. I would know because I spent a lot of time at the bar because it took almost 3 hours to get my room. I know its new years and things are hectic but you have to remember to make sure to call guests when their rooms ready. Especially if they are a gold member.

title: “Terrible Terrible Terrible”
text:
Nice lobby and bars...and rich heritage of Oscars - which they will proudly tell you about...
But the rooms are awful! 
The worst hotel visit you might have in America.

title: “ExcelGreat place to stay”
text: Was concerned based upon reviews. Found this place great! Love the AVEDA products!

title: “Formerly grand, now not being maintained”
text: We have stayed in the Hilton Anatole at least once a year for the last 20 years, going through independent ownership, a tour as a Wyndham hotel, and now a Hilton. Over those years, it retained a solid position as a very good hotel Despite the changes. When we were there last year, the new ownership was obviously struggling, with the lobby torn up and inadequate dining opportunities available. Getting a car took half an hour or more. This year, those things are fixed, but it is clear that the hotel is being neglected in favor of profits. The loveliness stops at the lobby. The carpet in our room was horribly stained. Elevator lights just did not work. One or more elevators was out of service much of the time. The staff was very friendly, but not necessarily competent (I had to show the check-in person what she was doing wrong in swiping my card). Car valet was now very fast and friendly. This is still an adequate hotel, but for the price there are better options. It is conveniently located on the freeway and just a block from Oak Lawn AVe. which gets you to many restaurant and other areas.

title: “Great location, good rooms, friendly staff”
text:
I spent 2 nights here in May on a romantic break with my wife. This hotel is well run and does what it says on the tin.
Strengths :
- Location is superb. You can walk to Times Square, Penn Station, Rockefeller Center, 5th Avenue shopping and there are subway stations pretty much at either end of the street for going further afield.
- Our room was good - we booked Deluxe and got an upgrade to Executive, which was quite large with a sofa. Furnishings contemporary, good bed. Good bathroom, but NB shower only no bath, fine for us though. Free wifi was easy to use. Not much of a view, but weren't really expecting that.
- Breakfast : Surprisingly good - continental was more generous than just pastries, it included cold meats, cheese, some filled rolls, cakes, cereals
- Rooftop bar : Good views as advertised, we went once, it was nice
- Reception : Well-appointed and had friendly and helpful staff
Weaknesses : Only a few - if you're here on romance these may take the gilt off the gingerbread a little :
- Location : As in other big cities, no street is perfect and this one has a few unsalubrious features - some porn shops and discount type stores. Busy and safe at all times though, no shifty types hanging around - walk up and down on Google Streetview if you want to be clear before you go
- Breakfast : This one I think they should do something about - the drinks at breakfast time come in paper cups (although the plates are china), which gives a tacky impression, a shame when the quality is good and the room is pleasant.

title: “MLK Memorial Dedication week”
text: The Willard is a lovely property. Proximity is even more lovely! The staff was very helpful and knowledgeable. The GM was very comforting during the hurricane Irene scare and had vast experience in natural disaster situations.

title: “Great experience and location”
text:
This hotel is charming: it is perfectly located in Union Square on Powell Street (with the cable just in front). Rooms are very nice (European like, so a little bit small compared other hotels but quite sufficient), cleanness perfect, very friendly staff. You have free wifi access. Breakfast was delicious !
You have everything located close to the hotel: shopping, book stores, restaurant, and with the cable in the same street it is very convenient to go everywhere.
The parking is located 1 block from the hotel ($22 per day), you can have your car whenever you want, it is very convenient given the mess to park in SF....
Definitively recommend it.

title: “Great Stay / Excellent Value”
text: Elevators are a challenge getting to and from your hotel room. Service was great and the location is right off Michigan Avenue!

title: “Great Service; clean rooms”
text:
Stayed at the hotel for 5 nights with the family. Front desk and room attendants were all very welcoming and did their jobs exceptionally well.
Rooms were clean and the amenities were excellent; especially the frequent shuttle service to Inner Harbour and John Hopkins Hospital.
Breakfast buffet was good and ala carte service in the evening was very good.
A nice touch would have been concierge service.

title: “Half Hotel, Half YWCA”
text: The good part is the room was clean and right at Copley. This building also houses the YMCA. VERY small room. Bed, One Wooden School Chair, a TV Stand and not room for anything else. Looked like a place to "dry out" or come off something. This would probably be OK if you were on a High School trip to Boston or a college exchange student spending one night. No Restaurant, No Bar, No Nothing.....I did wonder if there was a Pool where you had to swim naked with a Locker Key around your ankle.....Just like the old Boys Club.....

title: “Just ok”
text:
We stayed here for one night and the place was OK. We were looking for something really close to LAX but we didn't want to spend much since we were only going to sleep there and leave early in the morning. The place is marketed as a retro-type hotel and it definitely looks old. Our room was clean and the bed was comfortable. Breakfast was good and the place was clean as well. My number 1 complain is that our flight got in just before 1 AM and we had to wait a good 45 minutes for the hotel shuttle to pick us up. A nice police officer called for us asking how often the shuttle ran by LAX and they said every half and hour. We waited for the 1 AM and by 1:40 we called again and they said we should have let them know we wanted the shuttle to be there... Don't believe it's going to be there every half an hour. Call requesting it specifically or you're in for a loooong wait. The driver got there within 5 minutes and he was super nice. 
The hotel has seen better days. It looks a little run down and I don't think I would choose it again, but it was what we needed at the moment.

title: “Wonderful stay!”
text:
We couldn't get one hotel for the four nights of our stay so changed from a charming but quirkier hotel to the W Austin for the last two nights. Great to have two very different experiences and we loved both.
The staff at the W was wonderful - very friendly and accomodating. Concierge gave us a great restaurant suggestion. The pool was a bit different - sort of a cross between a big lap pool and huge hot tub - but fun. Quite a scene on our wkend night - very "meet and greet" - fun to watch. Wait staff at the pool was wonderful. Room was immaculate - very dramatic, a la W style. My only issue was the fee for in - room internet - so done with that in the 21st century. Parking was expensive but we found street parking and a $6 lot - made it work pretty easily.We'd certainly come back again.

title: “Clean room before an early flight.”
text:
Needed to come up from Columbus to catch a 6:00 am flight. The hotel is right by the airport, has an efficient shuttle (was there in five minutes). The room was basic but clean.
Breakfast was served too late, and the promised "take away" bag did not materialize, but I was happy with the property.

title: “Nice and quite”
text: A very nice hotel in the hearth of New York. Really close to Times Square. The atmosphere is very nice and the room has all the comforts a person need. The toilet inside he room is special and nice!

title: “TOO DATED TO RETURN”
text: We stayed at the Double Tree Hotel at Southcenter on 5 Jan 2012 and found the hotel not very pleasant. We stayed on the 7th floor and the hot water was a long time coming. The bathroom is very small and not what I expected from a suite room. The sink is out in the bedroom which is ackward if you need to get a drink of water in the middle of the night. The room, although clean, was quite dated and showed signs of too much wear. The lobby atrium open to the roof allowed noise to travel up from the bar on the main floor to our 7th floor room. The breakfast was quite pleasant in the morning and we appreciated the fine service. The hotel needs a complete make over before we will consider this hotel in the future.

title: “Amazing!”
text:
My travel agent suggested this hotel and at first I was conearned due to the reviews on this page. I went for it anyways as the price was great.
This hotel was GREAT! I cannot complain about anything! The staff was great and extremely helpful! We booked our broadway tickets with our hotel and the concierge helped us out with where to go in the evening. He even called ahead for us and got us on the list so we would be guaranteed entrance. The location is also great!
My sister and I walked to MACY'S which was about 20 minutes and times square was not even a 10 min walk straight up the street! No turns or nothing.We even walked to one of our Broadway shows which was located super close as well.
We ordered room service and although the food was not the greatest it was exceptionally fast and was cleaned up when we called as well!
The rooms were small compared to North American rooms but who goes to NYC and stays in their room? The bathroom was also small but we did not care! Everything was clean and pressed and that is what we appreciated!
Our luggage was taken care of extremely well and everything I felt was very organized! 
I COMPLETELY recomend this place to anyone who wants a good location from Times Square!

title: “Sleepless in San Diego--Wild Party next door to our room”
text:
Nice hotel, but we had the misfortune of a wild party with about ten people in nearby room that kept us up most of the night. Called front desk at 2 a.m., 2:15, 2:30, 2:45 and 3, but they chose not to deal with it. The easy way: knock on the room door, ask to see the registered guest, and then demand that the rest of the crowd leave. That didn't happen. In fact, the party was still going on the next morning--with cigarette smokers in the room and on the balcony--in this non-smoking area. The hotel was well aware of what was going on, and for whatever reason, decided not to handle it. The hotel has since offered us two free nights to return--what we haven't heard is a change in policy. What happens the next time there's a post-midnight party in the next door room? 
The good: great location, beautiful views, terrific pool, Hawaii like layout. 
The bad: $9.99 a night for wireless Internet and above issue with partyers.

title: “the hilton resort offered the right combination of luxury and comfort.”
text:
i recently stayed at the hilton resort for a week to host a business function. the resort staff was extremely accommodating prior to my arrival and throughout the week. they did everything in their power to ensure our meetings occurred smoothly and never hesitated to assist at any given moment.
the resort grounds were lovely and the the views of the water in the background were very nice. the aqua and olive restaurants served delicious meals. 
i hope to return and enjoy the resort when i'm not there on business.

title: “Bed Bugs”
text:
I stayed there in November and although I wasn't expecting much, I was disgusted by the room I was given. It was small, shabby, dirty. The window wouldn't close all the way. The towels had stains on them. There was a wet towel on the floor of the shower stall when I checked in. 
There were holes, dents, scuff marks on the walls. And to top if all off, I left the place with bed bug bites on my arm. I would never stay there again.

title: “Very happy with the Holiday Inn Golden Gateway”
text:
After reading some of the reviews concerning this hotel my husband and I were not sure what to expect. We figured even if the place was a dive it wouldn't matter as we would be gone most of the time sightseeing. We were pleasantly surprised. Check in was smooth (of course, it was 2:30 in the morning but that is another story). The room was smallish but well appointed. No, this isn't the Ritz but we thought the decorations were soothing and pleasant. Bathroom again was a little on the small side but clean and the fixtures were all new looking. We were on the 17th floor and the view was spectacular. Better than when we stayed at the Renaissance Park 55 Hotel in Union Square. As far as location, we again were happy. The California line for the cable cars ends/begins right there and it is always easy to get on unlike the Powell/Hyde line. If you want to go to Fisherman's Wharf take the California Line all the way down to the end which is Embarcadero Street. Then take one of the refurbished electric trolleys to Fisherman's Wharf. You can hop off the California Line when it crosses the Powell/Hyde line and take your chances on finding room on a cable car. It all depends on the day and the time whether you will get on or not.
We would definately stay here again. You can get this hotel on Priceline for around $70 and for that price it is a good deal.

title: “Amazing service, beautiful rooms, friendly staff, convenient location”
text: My stay at the W New York on Lexington was perfect. The rooms were nice, the hotel staff was friendly and welcoming and the service was amazing. Jolene Koepp was hands down the move fabulous person to work with on a room reservation.

title: “Excellent visit!”
text: Was in NYC for Toy Fair. Hotel was close to event and Madison Square Garden. Staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Breakfast was very good with good variety each morning. It is great that it is a pet friendly hotel. I only wish there was a soda machine available. Overall though, a great place to stay.

title: “Very enjoyable stay”
text: We enjoyed our stay. The Hotel was in excellent condition with several new upgrades. We booked a suite at $189 a night and thought it was well worth the money. Restaurant was a bit pricey but we were expecting that. Service was excellent from all aspects of our stay including, valet, bell captain, reg desk and room service.

title: “Half Moon Half Rate”
text:
Terrible room service—was actually served food that we saw fallen on the ground outside and was not even dusted off—even plate chips in the food!
No accountability. We are SD natives and have used Half Moon for years even kept our boat there for 5 years. 
Great location, great concerts but, the Hotel and staff has gotten tired. 
There are better choices in this area.

title: “Great for the money!”
text: This was a great hotel for a stopover. The rooms were comfortable (though a bit on the small side) and ours included a pull out sofa, which was great for our kids. The staff was very courteous, and aside from the hotel being a bit difficult to find at first, it was great! Lots of local restaurants deliver food, so dinner was really easy too!

title: “Huge Disapointment! Not a luxury hotel.”
text: This was the biggest hotel disapointment that I have ever had! My wife and I scheduled a long weekend in Phoenix and wanted to try the Biltmore for something different than our usual stays at the Phoenecian or Royal Palms. There is no comparison....the Biltmore is very dated, has horrible service in the restaurants, and is somewhat depressing inside. Even in a suite, you almost feel as though you are in a dungeon. We joked that it was somewhat similar to the "tower of terror" ride at Disneyland. The worst part about it is that we were woken up early 2 out of the 3 mornings by the groundscrew and their leaf blowers outside of our room. We ended up checking out early and spending out last night at the Royal Palms...and were happy we did!

title: “Had High Expectations...but not quite met”
text:
Stayed here a couple of days ago.
As a recent convert to the Starwood program I would have expected a little bit more from this hotel. I travel to SF almost every week and have stayed in almost all the 4 & 5 star hotels. 
Pros:
- Rooms are modern, clean and nice
- Bed, comforter and pillows were comfortable and I enjoyed my sleep
Cons:
- Quite a dry welcome, not asking for any preferences in hotel room type
- No coffee maker in room. When I asked for one, it was brought up but in this massive tray and the coffee maker itself looked like it was from the 90s
- Biggest con. I happened to forget my kit at the security checkpoint and asked for shaving foam and toothpaste. I was told it would be $7.50. Now having stayed in hotels for the last 5 years almost every week, I have never come across an instance where a hotel charged for this anymore. Especially to loyalty members. The Ritz, Fairmont and Ghirardelli Square and even the Hyatts and Hiltons in the city have never charged me or any of my colleagues for such a request. Quite a letdown given the room rate. 
I would recommend this hotel for the rooms, proximity to financial district and if you have your kit in your bag ;)

title: “Never come back”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel on Dec. 15. We were taking the morning flight to Las Vegas. 
I have to say this is the worst experience with Best Western we have ever had. First of all, the heater was broken at late night so that we were too cold to sleep any longer. The hotel did not provide any quilt but a very thin blanket. We were almost frozen. Secondly, the breakfast was not good at all, few choices, no bacon or sauge or ham, and the hot water was not hot enough for oatmeal. In comparison, the Best Western in Redding is too good to be true.

title: “Don't believe the reviews”
text: We picked this hotel for a one night stay before flying out early Monday morning. It was near the airport and the car rental return and had good reviews, but I think the other people must have stayed at another hotel. The place was old, worn out and dismal. Our window looked out into an alley and the bathroom was filled with cracked tiles, moldy corners, and looked dirty. The carpet was old and worn. The heater produced damp, clammy air. The deck clerk was rude when we checked in - I stood beside the only person checking in and the clerk snapped at me to "get in line" like there were dozens of people waiting. I would strongly suggest that you spend a few dollars more and go somewhere that was more welcoming. It was not a deal for what we paid, even in San Diego.

title: “Annoyingly Trendy”
text: I don't have any real problems with this hotel, in fact we slept great here. We asked for a 4 star hotel through a low bid on priceline. So it wasn't necessarily a hotel we would have normally booked.Based upon other reviews, we asked the receptionist for an inside room away from the "L" tracks. The room was spacious. I say this place was annoyingly trendy because it just seemed that the dark blue lights in the elevator, the dim lights in the hallways and the music in the lobby were strange. Anyway, I would give this place 5 stars for comfort and 3 stars for annoying. But that is just me.

title: “Calming retreat - No worries here! They take care of you.”
text: My husband and I recently visited Seattle together with our young adult daughter, to visit our son at Ft. Lewis. Traveling takes so much out of us any more. The Four Seasons Seattle is like an oasis: it's right in the midst of busy downtown Seattle, but it is calm inside and everyone seems to be there just to make life easier for you. This is a great place to stay. The main reason I don't give it all excellent scores is that I am a picky person, so it takes perfection to get an excellent score from me. A good rating from me is, well, pretty close to perfect. Specific to this visit's ratings: 1) as to value, well, it is priced appropriately for what you get, but it isn't over the top; 2) as to sleep quality, we have our issues independent of the hotel and it doesn't ever reach perfection any more; and 3) in re to cleanliness, although throughout our stay I would rate it excellent, there was a very minor bloop noticed when we first entered the room. Staff is outstanding, and more than make up for these very minor issues. I definitely recommend Four Seasons Hotel Seattle for a fine hotel experience!

title: “If I Could Live at this Hotel TRUST ME I WOULD, THE FOUR SEASONS IS BEYOND THE BEST”
text:
I recently stayed at the Four Seasons LA at Beverly Hills, and trust me it was one of the best hotels I have ever stayed at. Everything from the check-in, the room, the pool, the service, food, restaurants everything was excellent. I had lunch and breakfast at the Cabana Cafe and the food there was excellent as well the food at Culina was excellent to. 
If I could live at this hotel I would check in and never leave. This is by far the best hotel in the Los Angeles / Beverly Hills area. The hotel provides transporation to and from Rodeo should you like (in a Rollys Royce) or it is easy walking distance about 10 minutes and a nice walk to.

title: “I want to go back”
text: I saw some complaints on here about the size of the rooms so I was expecting something tiny and cramped. But honestly, the size of the room was perfectly fine and everything was really clean and in good shape. I loved being there. You can walk downtown to Union Square, or up to midtown in a reasonable period of time. Staff was so nice. And the Italian restaurant downstairs had a great menu and very pleasant service. I will definitely stay there again and feel lucky to have found the place.

title: “Nice hotel for the price. Conveniently situtated within walking distance of good places.”
text:
My husband and I stayed for 3 nights while he was attending some training here in Beverly Hills. The hotel is nice and clean. The housekeeping staff does a good job of keeping the rooms clean. The rooms are rather small and the bathroom is even smaller and is situated strange in the room but everything worked well. 
The hotel staff did not seem very knowledgeable about the surrounding area. I asked for assistance using the public transportation and they had no idea. I also found the cost of a cab to the airport to be rather high ($40 one way) but this is out of their control. I just wish there had been some kind of shuttle service. 
The hallways were loud and you can hear everyone as they talk and can also hear the doors slamming. If you want to sleep in, don't stay here. The housekeeping staff going in and out of the rooms as they clean gets rather loud.
We had drinks at the bar each night and found it to be nice with very friendly staff but the drinks were pricey. All in all, this hotel was adequate for the price we paid in the area it is in.

title: “A Good Stay with Extra Pointers”
text: I just came back from a three night stay where we stayed in the 2-bedroom suite. This was the very last unit (or first depending on where you start) on Roy Street. Because of road construction or trash collection, we were jarred up early with their banging and beeping when the trucks were moving in reverse. This was during the week days so if you're staying over the weekend you may not encounter this. Parking is ridiculously tight... and I agree with the other reviews in regards to this. I found parking in their garage (you use your hotel keycard to get in) was easier as most guests seemed to park outside. Everytime we parked in the garage we were able to find two spaces together that were unoccupied which made parking easier. There is a market, Quality Food Center, across the street (corner of Mercer and 5th) that was is quite nice.

title: “A Magical Experience”
text: Having read "Hotel on the Corner of Bitter and Sweet" by Jamie Ford, our Whidbey Island Reading Group of five age 65+ "girls" headed to Seattle for the real experience. What a treat. Jan Johnson's Panama Hotel is truly of that era...BUT...the rooms are spotlessly clean, the decor of each room is lovely, the beds old but incredibly soft with crisp linens and lots of pillows and a down comforter. Do know that you will use a shared bathroom down the hall, but each room does have a sink. The downstairs coffe/tea room is cozy and comfortable with delicious brews and local pastries. Jan herself is very pleasant and more than willing to share stories of this historic hotel. We had a fabulous time staying at this hotel and visiting the Asian shops in the area.

title: “Nice but some noise”
text: Nice hotel--other comments are fairly accurate. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Everything very functional. We would have enjoyed having AC. Rooms are noisy at night--just not much they can do about noise from room to room and within facility. Great location.

title: “Why stay anywhere else”
text: This hotel never ceases to amaze me.. The service starts when you stop at the front door and the valet is there to meet/greet you and look after your vehicle and luggage. This is when your vacation actually starts. The staff is always professional, courteous and helpful. This trip we had made a snafu with our park and fly package (my mistake) which could have cost us lots of money, but thanks to a wonderful young lady named Jessica, she corrected everything. In all my years of travelling, I have never met a nicer,more helpful person at the front desk of any hotel that I have stayed at. She WAS that nice!!. All the staff that we dealt with (esp. Donelle Hudson) helped to get our group vacation off to an amazing start. Whatever the manager does at this hotel, he must be doing something right as this place is run like a "well oiled machine" I cant wait until the next stay!!!

title: “Safe location, good breakfast, wish they had queen sized beds”
text:
No problems at all except the bed size. We were traveling with teenagers and had to double up on beds. The king beds with the rollaway didn't sound very appealing, so we took the two doubles. Other than that, the place was a very good example of what a Comfort Inn establishment could be.
Breakfast was as expected. It was a pleasant surprise to find out that they had enough dining area to handle their breakfast crowd.

title: “Great staff, good location, pity about the facilities”
text:
The staff in the Back Bay were very helpful and it is in a great part of Boston. However, compared to other 4 star hotels in the US, the facilities are a bit lacking. First, the concierge desk was essentialy doubled up by staff from the desk. Also there was no display of attraction leaflets, like most hotels have. Second, the bed was fantastic but apart from that the room was no great: no minibar, no coffee making facilities etc. Third, to go to the fitness room, you had to walk through part of the bar! Fourth, the AC was very noisy.
One plus point for me i suppose was that being Irish, the hotel did feel genuinely Iish- right down to the lack of facilities!

title: “Great Stay”
text: We had an enjoyable two days at this hotel. The staff was friendly and very helpful with any needs we had . The room was not as we had reserved and they were quick to find us even better rooms. The restaurants had excellent service and food and were child friendly. Beds were comfortable and rooms quite. Except for one limo driver we had a perfect weekend .

title: “Horrible Service!”
text: I called to try and make a reservation, horrible customer service, the man that answered the phone would not speak up, his tone was very disengaging, if you're in reservations your voice should sound upbeat, this man was horrible!! DO NOT BOOK!

title: “Enjoyable stay during recent convention”
text:
Spent five night here during a basketball convention and had an enjoyable experience.
My room was spacious and the bed very comfortable. The bathroom was clean and roomy.
My only complaint about the room was that the cooler, which looked like a fridge, didn't really keep my soda/food cold. I ended up sticking things in my ice bucket.
There was plenty of staff available and they were all very pleasant. Check in and check out were a breeze.
Ate at the restaurant off the lobby - very good - and the sports bar (Champions) - okay.
Had to pay for wi-fi in the room but it was free in the lobby. Folks were complaining that if they had two laptops in their room, they would have to pay for the wi-fi twice since it was by computer not room. That seemed to be a bit unreasonable to me - especially when so many hotels give you wi-fi for free.
Hotel is located close to the Circle Center and lots of restaurants. Noticed that many places were closed on Sundays and Mondays even though the Women's Final Four was in town and there were twenty thousand people milling about.

title: “Good choice”
text:
Just got back from a 5 night stay at the Fairfield Inn. The location was great as there was a subway station at the end of the block and another 2.5 blocks in the other direction. Our room was not large but was clean & modern. More importantly it was quiet and the bed was comfortable. Our room was in the back and faced a yoga studio. However we were only there to shower, sleep & change so it was not a big deal as we just kept the shade drawn.
The breakfast was adequate with fruit, coffee, muffins, cereal, & yogurt. My only complaint with our stay is that when we came back to the hotel in the late afternoon (3-3:30) our room had not been made up yet. The maid came while we were there but did agree to come back after we'd left. It was not a super big deal but I did find it a minor annoyance. Other than that I would given it 5 stars for my stay and I would still stay here again (though I would discuss the maid deal first). FYI the lamb gyro from the cart by the red subway entrance was really good.

title: “good stay”
text: This is a nice hotel, close to universal, not a far drive from Hollywood Blvd, right at a freeway exit/entrance. Starbucks is right across street, 2 fast food places down street but nothing else good is close at least that I saw. The breakfast was horrible, the room was not vacuumed well, and there were ants in the bathroom. I paid over $200 a night for a suite and did not feel it was worth that much money. I read the other posts about the window break in. I asked the desk about it and she said it never happened. My window was on the ground floor in the back facing the alley but there is a fence around the back. It looks like a good fence but like anything- if someone wanted to scale it they could- but the fence made me feel better. Though honestly I felt insecure here. I felt like at any time someone could just walk in off the street or in from the window. As we were leaving we noticed that one of our windows was broken and did not close and lock.. I probably would not stay here again. Though the free parking was great and the location was close to sightseeing. I think tours pickup here too.

title: “Great place to stay in the heart of Wall Street Area”
text: I've stayed here a few times over the past year for business multiple nights each time. Rooms are clean and updated. Staff is very pleasant at front desk and Breakfast room. Decent breakfast buffet included for free and includes eggs meat (sausage or bacon) and cereals and full selection of breads, sweet rolls and coffee. Rooms are small but thats average for "express type hotels". Like I said great location to Wall St, easy walk to south st seaport and a quick walk to World trade center location. Usually the best priced hotel in the area.

title: “Great hotel and awesome employee's”
text: I have enjoyed staying at the Residence Inn Mission Valley, very nice rooms with lots of space and always clean. I really like the involvement of the staf,f hosting game night and being able to meet the people that keep the hotel a place you will always want to come back to. The only down side would have to be is the amount of families that stay with very loud children. But overall a great place, with a great sales team! I will stay again nexdt time i visit the area.

title: “How do we love thee?”
text:
My boyfriend and I travel to Philadelphia for work and for leisure. We've stayed at this hotel 4-5 times in the last two years, each stay surpassing the previous as we get to know they staff and they us. The new restaurant at the hotel is superb!
We love this hotel because it feels like an upper west side apartment with enough kitchen to allow you to prepare purchases from the Farmer's market @ Rittenhouse Square on Saturdays; we love this hotel because the staff is courteous, friendly, helpful and knowledgable about the area; we love this hotel because of its central location near great restaurants (shout out to The Marathon -- again!), shopping, museums and the park along the Schuykill River where I go running in the morning. 
What you won't find here are kids running in the halls, bored tourists in a soul-less lobby, obligatory bad breakfasts -- and that's fine with us!

title: “Right off the highway and very clean”
text: We stayed here for a wedding we had to attend and it was a nice location and very clean rooms. They were acoomidating to all of our needs. We were not there too much becuase of the wedding but it was a nice place to sleep and get ready. I would recommend this hotel to others.

title: “Good Hotel, Good Location”
text: Good hotel with pricey food. Hotel Pool excellent. Room 0915 faced the Pool and had a partial view of aircraft arrivals at LAX. Staff attentive and efficient. Free Shuttle bus to Airport. I have one gripe however and that is the cost of valet parking at $25.00 per vehicle when you have no choice in the matter. Also the car was parked no further than 200 feet from the hotel entrance. I also notice that they would only accept liability for lose of keys and not for any damage they may have done to the vehicle.

title: “Great Location at a Great Price”
text:
We recently spent 6 nights at this hotel. The location was top notch. We could walk to the theater, Central Park, Times Square, the Lincoln Center and 5th Avenue comfortably. There are several good places to eat nearby. 
The hotel itself is a bit dated but the room was good size by normal standards and huge by NYC standards. The layout of the bathroom and dressing area was a bit cramped and could have been laid out better. The only real negative were the elevators. They are extremely small and if you over fill them, they will get stuck between floors. We found ourselves stuck on more than one occassion when, despite our warning, people crammed into the elevator. 
The value was tremendous- most of our nights were in the $150-$170 range. I have already recommended this hotel to several friends.

title: “The Cadillac Hotel is Wonderful!”
text:
I spent the evening with my two Sons, to have a great family night, and to enjoy the beautiful sunset and being within walking distance of all that Venice has to offer.
The Cadillac Hotel is a gem! Jeff and his team do a great job of making a home away from home.
You are stepping into history when you stay at the Cadillac Hotel. Charlie Chaplin himself used to spend weeks at a time here at the Cadillac, and one look out the window at sunset tells you why... There is nothing like a sunset at the Cadillac. They have brought great modern amenities to each of the rooms... There is a great gathering area to the left of the lobby to sit and chat, great Starbucks coffee in the morning and so close to so many great restaurants.
Enjoy your stay at the Cadillac... Great folks and a great place to stay!

title: “Great historic hotel. Fantastic restaurant. Great beds.”
text: Ask for a courtyard or 3rd Ave view. 4th Ave is noisy and has a view of dilapidated buildings.

title: “Poor value for price”
text:
Typical chain--somewhat tired in decor and amenities. I would say the service wasn't very good except that no service existed. Food trays left in halls for 24 hours. Inattentive front desk staff but pleasant enough once you got their attention.
Positives--1. good location for meetings at convention center. 2. nice quick breakfast cafe and outstanding breakfast buffet in restaurant. 3. very comfortable beds.
Negatives--1. walk from elevator to room of approximately two city blocks. 2. Inadequate room lighting--including dark shower area. 4. late or missed wake up calls. 5. annoying journey from turning on tv to actually getting a live station. 5. mistakes on bill 6. overall just average at way above average prices. 7. Terrible ac system.

title: “Hospital Visti”
text: We have stayed with you for 5 years when we have appts at Dana Farber. This time we had someone above us who screamed for hours. Security finally quieted then down about 4 am. Otherwise a great stay.

title: “The customer service was excellent and very helpfully at at times”
text: The employees were very friendly, and helpfully at all times of the day. The only bad thing out of the trip was the shuttle service to the begging of the marathon race, other than that inconvenience everything was excellent!!!

title: “Nice Location & Generally Great Prices”
text: I prefer to stay in Kimpton properties but when prices are too high or the city is full - On the Ave is a great alternative. The hotel is clean, staff is friendly and they have very comfy beds. The neighborhood feels safe when you are out and about. There are a couple of nice restaurants in the area - not high end but pleasant enough for a bite eat. Again a nice hotel with reasonable rates and all amenities.

title: “Great Location, Reasonable Hotel”
text:
Like pretty much everyone, the location is excellent for downtown Chicago - within easy distance of buses and the metro. Initially we were given a large room on the 39th floor (fantastic views) but... it was next to the aircon for the hotel. When this kicked in, even the furniture vibrated, to say nothing of the noise. The first offer was to change for a "smaller" room as there was nothing else available - when I saw the room it was a bad joke - small was an understatement. After refusing the substitute of the smaller room, a large room on the 28th floor was found to be available(!) and we moved there and it was fine and comfortable. The front desk staff were really helpful.
The downstairs bar is good for lunch / dinner - but avoid it for breakfast as service is slow and less than friendly.
A big plus is the business centre where there is the possibility to check-in and print out boarding cards for free, to make the hassle of O'Hare a bit less.

title: “Unfortunately, location is only thing going for it”
text:
If you want to be in the heart of NYC, right on Time Square and an easy walk to the theaters, then you still might wish to consider this hotel. If service means anything to you, go elsewhere.
In short, there was NO customer service here. Period. 
Just one of many examples: I requested a feather pillow twice the first day, and three times the second, plus left a note with housekeeping. Nothing. My husband went down to speak with someone at the front desk on the third day and was told the hotel did not have feather pillows. (Not true; our friends next door had them. Also, if they did not have them, why not just tell us the first five times we asked?) So I called housekeeping, asked for a manager, and took a name, and then explained the numerous requests with no response. I was told there must be a "shortage" at the hotel and they were checking each day after a room checked out to see if they had a feather pillow. I see. (Interestingly enough, half an hour later, a feather pillow was delivered. It only took a total of 8 requests). Other things- No wake-up call for my husband's conference as requested. He spoke to them at the front desk - and half an hour later, security came banging on the door, "Wake up call! Security!" (Uh, the person who had requested the wake-up call was already up and complaining to you! CYA move?) 
Sheets had holes in them and were not long enough for the bed. Shampoo, conditioner, etc were not replaced when empty until pointed out to housekeeping. Comforters were dirty and obviously not cleaned or replaced between guests. I could go on, but you get the idea...

title: “Fantastic location”
text: We stayed at the Novotel for 10 days during September, it was our first trip to NY and the location was perfect for the many things we chose to see and do while we were there. It is close to subway, bars, restaurants and theatres. Staff were always pleasant and helpful. Our room had a view of Times Square, and had a huge bed which was a bonus after spending all day out and about.Housekeeping did a great job and the room was spotless during our stay. We did not eat in the restaurant during the length of our stay but with so many choices close by that didn't matter. Coffee making facilities in the room would have been a bonus but with Duane Reade (also great for fruit & yoghurt) and Starbucks within a block this didn't really matter either. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay in NY and Novotel and if you are looking for somewhere to stay in a great Midtown location you would be hard pressed to beat this. The outside bar & observation deck is a great way to chill out after a busy day.

title: “Fantastic stay”
text: My husband and I went to Philadelphia for the weekend for our anniversary. We stayed at the Windsor Suites with the Sleepover package. The hotel was great. We were upgraded to a suite on the 16th floor with a great view (we didn't even tell them that it was our anniversary). The staff were very helpful and the location was great. We were within walking distance of the art museum as well as plenty of restaurants. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Ok hotel but bad parking”
text:
We just returned from a 2 night stay at this hotel. I chose this hotel for it's location and parking. We, two sisters, were attending a concert both nights and would be returning late in the evening. In all the ads for the hotel it says on site parking. When we arrived we were able to park in the underground lot, no problem. But, upon our return that evening the parking lot was blocked. I had to double park, run inside and ask what was up, they said the on site parking was very small so you had to go to another lot 2 blocks away! And I must add, the desk clerk was very rude about the whole thing. We did not appreciate having to walk through unfamiliar territory at 11 pm at night! It was not a comfortable situation. They have very lax security. 
My complaints fell upon deaf ears, they did not care. I will not stay at this hotel again. The hotel itself was just okay, we did not like the decor, felt like you were in a child’s room with silly drawings on the wall and painted furniture. Bedding was okay, room was pretty clean. They did have computers in the lobby and wifi which I couldn’t get to work in the rooms, probably my fault. TV didn’t have many channels, just basics. Toilet didn’t want to work right, needed a light touch. Shower was okay. Had breakfast the last day in the restaurant and it was fine, nothing special. If you didn't care about the parking it would be an okay place.

title: “Functional and central”
text:
The best about this hotel is that it has a reasonable price for a very good location. The hotel is surely above average, but also not one of the best hotels I can remember. It is modern, clean and functional. The staff is correct, the breakfast ok, the rooms are large enough and clean.
The best thing about the hotel is that it is located at walking distance to the Magnificent mile, Lake Michigan and the harbor, Grant Park and the loop...
It is a hotel surely worth considering when staying in Chicago.

title: “Perfect West Side Boutique Hotel”
text: My girlfriend and I stayed at On The Ave for 6 nights and had a fantastic time. The hotel is small and the staff was very helpful. Our A/C died on evening and the staff REPLACED the unit for us at 11:00PM! Wow. The next day the manager on duty brought us a gift an apologized for the inconvenience. Double wow. OtA is located 3 blocks from Central Park and 5 blocks from the 72nd Street train and Gray's Papaya (and NYC landmark). Easy to get everywhere. Restaurants, shops, and grocery stores all close. Will definitely stay here again!

title: “Exellent downtown hotel!”
text:
I had a very good stay at the JW Marriott while I was in town for the LA Half Marathon in late October. The hotel is modern and clean, and my room was big, quiet, and comfortable. The bed was just right - not too soft and not too firm. I noticed a hum from the air conditioner, but I just turned it off at night since it the weather was so mild.
Everywhere in the hotel, I found the staff to be helpful and very courteous. They made for a pleasant stay.
The shower head seemed to be of the water-saving variety, but there was adequate water pressure for a good, hot shower. I noticed LED lighting in the hall outside the elevator on my floor, and presume the hotel was built to modern energy-saving standards.
The rooftop pool looked very really inviting, but I didn't have time to use it. At 5pm on a warm Saturday it was surprisingly empty.
I had been skeptical that the convenient LA Live location would be noisy and crowded, but it was fine. Driving to and from the hotel was no worse than the rest of downtown LA, and I felt very comfortable walking around the neighborhood.
The parking valet person told me I'd get a discount on parking because I drove a hybrid car, although at checkout they missed the discount so I had to remind them. All downtown LA hotel parking is expensive, so I was thrilled to get a substantial discount. The valet pickup area was very busy, but the wait to get my car was less than 10 minutes.
While nearby hotels like the Millennium Biltmore offer great old world charm, this JW Marriott is a great contemporary hotel.

title: “Maria...”
text: I have had the good fortune of traveling to 29 countries on 4 different continents. At no point have I ever encountered such wonderful hospitality. There is a lady named Maria that works in the hotel restaurant. She is by far the kindest, most gentle soul I have ever met. My father is receiving treatment for cancer in Houston. She treats he and my mother like they were her own family. Her kindness does not go unnoticed. She is definitely a wonderful person and employee and should be treasured. Thank you Maria.

title: “Good for small family”
text:
Stayed for 2 nights with my wife and teenage son. Hotel is all suites so you can close the door for privacy at bedtime. We opted for Time Square view on the 19th floor and it turned out to be a good choice. High enough to subdue some of the noise and low enough to see the action on the street. I was surprised how quiet the room was and we had no trouble sleeping. Rooms are very small, but very clean and adequate for our purposes. We really only slept there. Minifridge is a plus so you can bring in some of your own beverages and save some $$.
If you drive in, you can just pull up in front of the hotel and they will valet park your car in the lot across the street on 47th street. To save money, pick up the car yourself when you leave. It's very easy and they will bring to car down to street level and you can load your luggage and drive right out and down 47th to 9A and out of the city.
Check-in was easy and they will store your luggage if you're early or want to leave the city after check out time which we took advantage of to give us 3 full days in the city.
The only negative we had was when they brought our luggage up to the room, one of the bags must have been handled pretty rough as we had a bottle of white wine in there that got broken. The bellhop couldn't leave the room fast enough when he delivered the bags. Luckily not much got wet and we just put the bag in the tub to dry out.
If you want to base your NYC vacation in the heart of Times Square, Doubletree is a good choice and the subway is literally just a few steps away from the front door.

title: “Nice hotel...great location”
text: The Park Central hotel was nice and in a great location. Our family of four stayed in a double room. The room size was decent for NYC standards. The bathroom was a little small. The hotel offers muffins and coffee for purchase in the lobby in the mornings. The subway is right outside the side door. The concierge were very helpful and friendly.

title: “loved this B & B”
text: The Newbury Guest House was a perfect place to stay. It is obviously right on Newbury street so it was very close to all the great shops on that street!!! It was also very close to the T and to the Prudential center (we went to the Sky Walk which is great way to see Boston and hear about the history with their audio tour). The rooms were very nice. We had the midlevel room and it was large enough for us and very clean. The breakfast was also very good. I would definitely recommend!

title: “We'll be back!”
text: Great lobby, great location. Good rates. Get a suite if you can. Great response from maintenance and housekeeping for things we needed like an extension cord and more towels. Right across the street from Grand Central. I would stay there again as long as we had a suite.

title: “Fabulous for a great price and PERFECT location”
text: we stayed here on our honeymoon on our way to Napa and it was great! we were able to save a little money with this hotel which was great...without having to give up anything! it is a couple blocks from the wharf and most major sites and the inside had been recently renovated so everything was new and modern. Would def. go back the next time I am in san fran!

title: “Loved it”
text: Excellent! The pizza we ordered through room service was good but we were not used to the Chicago style. We were thankful we were able to get a room here after a long day.

title: “Cool and probably a bit too trendy for us”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights recently. The location is great adn we loved LES generally. The room faciltiies were fine and the bed comortable. Our request for a quiet room was met in that we were on the 9th floor on the pool side so away from any noisy bar area. The pool staff were very nice but the fact that the pool areaconverts to a bar in the early evening is a bit off putting especially on hot days. It was also being used for a private event one afternoon when we wanted a swim. The food in the Japanese restaurant was nice but I had the most expensive beer I have ever had there $15 ! The gym has great equipment and was very good and great for a workout. The front of house are all beautiful and very friendly/helpful but I felt 20 years too old as lots of local young cool people frequest the bars. Would I recommend the LES ? Yes with thes provisos I mentioned. The area is great with lots of fun bars and restaurants, close to Chinatown and Little Italy.

title: “Great Location and Staff”
text: Stayed here over Memorial Day weekend. The staff was SO friendly and the location was right in the middle of everything. The rooms were very clean and beds were comfortable. We caught the water taxi right by the hotel and for $4 per person...rode it to Navy Pier for a perfect day! We will stay here next time we're in Chicago!

title: “Location location location!”
text:
The hotel is well kept and well managed a lovely break from the busy outside world. 
It's location is tremendous with Trulucks (seafood) across the street, Capital Grille in the attached building and Nobu (Fantastic Asian cuisine) in the hotel!!!
Spa is quite nice.
What a great get away from the grind!!

title: “Weekend w/ Michelangelo”
text: Breathtaking. Absolutely beautiful with astonishing service. $$$$ but worth it if you've got it.

title: “The most friendly hotel staff we have come across in a long time.”
text: We were visiting San Diego for an event on the USS Midway and this hotel was recommended to us. We asked for early check-in and our room was ready when we arrived. They had even upgraded us to a yacht harbor room. We were introduced to all the front desk staff at check-in. Our room was beautiful with a nice balcony. We were always greeted by staff every time we left or came back. Breakfast buffet was wonderful with lots of hot dishes and a waiter for your table. This is where we will be staying from now on.

title: “Great place to stay in Ft. Worth.”
text: Centrally located downtown near great restraunts, theatres, and night life. Great service and the rooms are nicely decorated and comfortable. Excellent way to relax and get some work done.

title: “Excellent Hotel - Early a.m. Departure Difficulties”
text:
I travel to Houston for business purposes and love this new hotel. The 024 lounge includes a modern waterfall with plenty of separate furniture groupings for discussions with your co-workers. The lounge staff are very friendly and willing to work with you on obtaining items off the menu even after regular kitchen closing time. The room and bed were great and the in-room safe the perfect size for multiple laptops and other electronics. 
The only issue occured when I needed to check out at 4am to catch a 6am flight out of Houston Hobby. The hotel no longer prints the check out docs and puts them under the door and I had a 15-20 min search around the lobby and the first floor to finally find a front desk attendant to process my departure and make it to the airport in time.

title: “I wish there were a James Hotel in every city”
text:
My daughters and I stayed at the James for a Spring Break trip to Chicago and I recently came back for a work trip. I have to say that I'm a forever fan and wholeheartedly recommend to anyone looking for a respite in Chicago.
The staff is the friendliest and most service oriented I've ever encountered. They're very attentive and not only take care of any needs or questions I pose, they foresee anything I need and take care of without me even knowing it was a need.
When traveling with my young daughters, everyone was incredibly sweet to them, making them feel even more special than they felt by staying at such a cool place. We all felt incredibly welcome.
One of my biggest pet peeves of business travel is paying for wireless access. Not at the James, wireless is free.
The rooms are simple yet posh. The beds are very comfortable and the rooms are quiet. The bath products are Kiehl's (a major selling point for me) and the little extras in the room made me feel like I wasn't just making another business trip in some generic hotel.
All of this at an incredible value. It really isn't too good to be true.
Thank you for making both of my trips so memorable and comfortable. I will never book another hotel in Chicago!

title: “Lovely but room NOT like shown on website !”
text:
I made a reservation based on the pictures I saw on the website, booking a grand deluxe with fireplace and patio. It looked lovely in the pictures. 
Reality however, was a TINY room, with a large enclosed patio that felt a little bare, despite the table and chair.
I was disappinted, because I would have chosen a larger room had I known - and the website square footage description was misleading as well, since it included the patio...
Bathroom was tiny as well, with a single sink and an old-fashioned shower/tub combination that had a curtain instead of a glass door.
Other than that, the service was utterly stellar. 
The grounds are lovely. 
The food was excellent, and Chef had made a special menu for us, which we thoroughly enjoyed. China and linen were exquisite.
Valet was wonderful, and remembered my name the next morning.
I would stay at the hotel again, but this time ONLY in a garden suite next time, which the concierge recommended after I complained. 
Interestingly enough, she had someone else in the lobby who also was disgruntled to find their room NOT like the pictures on the website (I could overhear their conversation).
The website is NOT accurate, and should be updated properly to reflect not only the way the room really looks, but the square footage of the room non-inclusive of the patios.

title: “Were these my friends or employees???”
text:
I recently stayed at the Hard Rock for a week of fun! The ladies at the concierge desk were great! They made us feel like they really cared that we were having a good time and enjoying ourselves. The valet's outside were excellent! The entire staff made us feel like we have known them for years! 
The bed OMG that bed and those pillows were so comfortable! The shower was amazing! Beautiful view, great location in the Gaslamp area. 
thanks everyone for making my vacation great!

title: “BEDBUGS!”
text: Bedbugs. AC barely functioning. Then the run-around where management never available to answer 4 phone calls & 2 letters.

title: “would definitely stay here again”
text: We enjoyed our stay at Petite Auberge. Great location-access to public transportation and easy walk to Chinatown. It was fun visiting with other travelers during the wine get-togethers in the early evening. Room was great, very cozy with the fireplace. Staff very friendly and helpful. We would stay here again.

title: “Ellegant”
text: Enjoyed the stay, beautifully appointed room and the service is exceptional .

title: “Nice place”
text: This location is good for NYC. We travel here every year. The negative about the location in the street is not the greatest, go a block in any direction it improves. (homeless and a like). The hotel was clean the ac worked. Only a few rooms on each floor. The breakfast was ok, but breakfast is a cheap meal in NYC. Hampton is about the only place with queen beds, most all the other Hotels have doubles. Subway close, times square a 7 minute walk. Texas BBQ close by great prices I think its on 23 rd st and 8th ave.

title: “Weekend Getaway”
text:
Planned a trip to the Big Apple as a weekend getaway and planned to do a little sightseeing as well as visit a friend who lives in Brooklyn. Wasn't sure what to expect because the rate was extremely reasonable for a Manhattan property (although the cost at the same place for other weekends was more in line with the typical $200+ rates) -- but such is, as I am quickly learning, the nature of NYC hotel rates. See a price you like ... book it ... because it won't be there the next time you look.
Anyhow, we arrived via train to Penn Station, took a taxi the two blocks (could have easily walked) to the hotel which is right on 35th St just down from Macy's. Room wasn't quite ready (we arrived early) so they stored our bags while we went out and toured the city. Subway stop for the Broadway line and 6th Ave lines is literally right outside the door -- extremely convenient for a trip up to Times Square, Natural History Museum, Rock Center, Wall St (including the WTC Memorial -- take the R to Cortlandt). We road the N over to Brooklyn to Jay St and visited the TKTS booth to pick up some show tickets for the evening (much less crowded than the Times Square one and it's literally right outside the subway exit).
Anyhow, after a day of sightseeing, we returned and checked in. Everyone was very friendly and efficient. Had a little issue getting into the room (card key read was malfunctioning, but after returning to the front desk, they sent someone from maintenance along to make sure it we could get into the room and that the problem was fixed). Room was comfy corner room with plenty of space per NYC standards. Very clean. It was a City View room ... but the view was unimpressive as it was only on the 17th floor facing north. Not worth the extra couple bucks. Heating/Cooling system was a bit picky -- raise the temp on the thermostat 1 degree and it would go from too cold to too hot. Did finally get it to settle down once we let it go thru a few cycles. 
Empire State building is just one block over and Macy's is just down the street -- so very convenient for these attractions and like I said previosuly, just one stop up the Broadway line for Times Square and two up the Sixth Ave for Rock Center.
We are starting to develop a list of "go to" places we try to stay when in town - when they have a competitive price - and this one will certainly go on our list.

title: “I was surprised at how nice this stay was.”
text:
This was my third trip to New York for a vacation and I was very skeptical about New York and the hotels therein. However, I thought that the Doubletree Times Square was very well manged, clean and secure. I would definatley stay there again. I stayed with my wife and 7 yr old daughter and the room allowed my wife and I privacy while allowing our daughter to wake up early and busy herself in the other room.
The one exceptional high point in the trip was bellman John Barnes who proved to be a valuable resource on where to eat and where to go in the area. I orignially went by the official consierge to ask where my family and I could eat something "New Yorky". Of the few times I went by I was treated like I was inconviencing these folks, they were generally unfriendly and upon my request to eat somewhere "New Yorky" I got the eye-roll. In my opinion, bypass these worthless ladies and find John Barnes. He directed us to subway locations, pizza, deli's and breakfasts that I thought were well worth his advice. I would have rated service higher if John had not been the only jewel in their service department.
On Sunday through Thursday is a happy hour down in the lounge and the selection while slim is good. I wish they extended it to all days as we would have started our evenings in the lounge rather than giving money to the bars and resturants. 
From La Guardia it is about an hour drive and about $40 by taxi. It is directly on the square so expect crazy crowds especially when shows let out.
There is free internet only in the lounge which is always a bummer when you are paying these downtown rates. However, it is fast and easy to connect to. 
The rooms are clean but lack some storage areas. The bed was very comfortable and my daughter had no problems on the pull out sofa. 
As for security, the hotel is accessable only though a street level elevator that is manned. You must have a key to enter the hotel proper and then must go through the lobby to a second set of elevators. I was never concerned once I was in the hotel.

title: “Nice room, great view, friendly staff”
text:
I stayed at this hotel a little over a month agi while on a business trip. I read some of these negative reviews and I didn't have any of the problems they are reporting. It sounds like several of them got SUPER cheap rates or used some third party website to book them. That shouldn't make a difference but I'd venture to guess that it probably does make a difference to the hotels.
I booked directly on the hotel's website and I also am a member of their frequent stay program which may or may not have made a difference. 
I stayed 3 nights and my rate was about u$s 200 per night but I had a King room on a higher floor. My room was very spacious and it had a very comfortable bed, a work desk and a spacious bathroom. It also had a great view of the Canal. 
The hotel does stay very crowded and there were always tons of people in the lobby. The location is such that you need a taxi for many locations. The nice thing is they have plenty of employees working in the front to flag down taxis. I never waited more than 5 minutes for a taxi. 
The internet was u$s 10 per day and worked very well and was glitch free. The refrigerator was fully stocked. I did find it funny that they had a sticker on the refrigerator warning if you took anything out and put in your own drinks they would charge you for it. That's the first time I've seen a sticker like that and I've stayed in a LOT of hotels. 
I ordered room service a few times and it was always fast and the food was pretty good for hotel food. The check-out was fast and easy as they had self check-out so I checked ou within 5 minutes even though there was a long-line at the front desk. They had at least 5 of these check out terminals. 
All in all a good trip. Definitely if you can snag these cheapo rates whtat some of these people are talking about do it. I'm not sure what kind of room they were getting but mine was very spacious and very comfortable with no noise.

title: “Great location and rooms, bit noisy”
text: Rooms very spacious and clean, beds comfy and good quality furnishing. Great to have so much space in such a central location. Breakfast was DIY but that suited us especially making own waffles! Only downside was the outside noise at night so a room on a higher floor might be better.

title: “Loved our room, Roy's and the lazy river”
text: and a great time was had by all, we recently spent 5 days at the desert ridge prior to a trip to the Grand Canyon, it was perfect after the hustle and bustle of LA. we thoroughly enjoyed our rooms, huge marble bathrooms, cocktails nightly, a special dinner at Roy's and the pool and lazy river was for sure a highlight for the kids, they ate at the taco bar for lunch every day. I almost didn't want to leave, could easily have stayed a few more days.

title: “Sophisticated and Quiet”
text: Loved this hotel-the neighborhood is amazing, with the grand houses of Pacific Heights all around you, great for walking. We booked a suite and it was very spacious and comfortable with a great sofa bed for the kids and pocket doors to separate the bedroom. The hotel is quietly elegant with a nice small reception area off the lobby with wine and snacks. I would highly recommend this hotel. You do have to self park, no valet but we had no trouble finding street parking for our Chevy Tahoe so this was actually a plus because most SF hotels charge $40 or more for parking. Breakfast was included too and was quite good. We will be back!

title: “Very Nice, Great Price”
text:
Pros: Front desk personnel very helpful, room very clean, bathroom clean, clean linens and towels. Very good price and location.
Cons: Room small, and over heated. NO VIEW of anything from most rooms. Breakfast room too small and overheated. Too much Styrofoam used for breakfast items.

title: “Great Historic Hotel Experience”
text:
Great location within walking distance of a number of restaurants. Much larger rooms than would be expected. Excellent overall experience.
We booked a weekend online with advance pay which made it a great value. 
The only problem was the bed in the room was so broken down it was a roll to the middle experience. We did get another room that was certainly not as nice as the first because the first room's view was the best.
Lightening fast room service and except for the bed a great overall experience.

title: “Great Hotel for the Price”
text:
I’ll be honest. I was a little concerned about this hotel after reading some of the reviews. It was clear that this was a love it or hate it kind of place based on the fact that only part of the hotel is renovated. I booked the 4 day/3 night package via Priceline which included airfare from Florida to LA for just under $600 total. So considering that airfare by itself would have been about that had I booked separately, I basically got the hotel portion of the package for next to nothing. I was still a bit nervous so I sent a message to one of the more positive reviewers and asked if they would mind telling me the room number that they stayed in, which they kindly provided. I then called the hotel and requested that specific room for my reservation. 
I arrived at the hotel around 1pm after traveling since 5am. The check in was quick and painless with the exception of the room I requested not being available due to the current guest occupying that particular room extending their stay. I was given an identical room on the 11th floor, the only difference being that it was a street facing room as opposed to a rear facing room. The room was great for what I needed it for. The bed, while the comforter seemed a bit outdated, was very comfortable and the sheets were soft. Some people have posted issues with street noise, but I did not have a problem with this the 3 nights I was there. Perhaps because I was on one of the upper floors. The bathroom was small, but clean and included a blow dryer. Some reviewers have mentioned a problem with the hot water running out, but I did not experience this issue. Also, some reviewers have mentioned problems with the room being too hot. Perhaps it’s because I’m from Florida and have a higher tolerance for warm temps, but I found the room’s temperature to be quite pleasant and only messed with the thermostat once and that was when I first got there. The internet, while free was VERY slow. I was in town to cover the Premiere of the movie Inception for an entertainment blog, so being able to upload pictures was a big deal and I had A LOT of trouble with this. The TV worked fine and had plenty of channels to choose from. 
I did not rent a car for this trip as the idea of driving in LA freaks me out, so the fact that the Metro was directly across the street was very convenient. It got me into the heart of Hollywood in 20 minutes. There seemed to be plenty of fast food and dining choices around the hotel, but I ended up eating a lot of room service. It was a little inconvenient that they stopped serving at 10pm. Also, the menu in the room is not current. One time I called down to room service and the phone just rang and rang and rang. When I called the front desk to ask if they were open, they said yes, but they were probably just really busy. The lady attempted to transfer me back to room service, but accidently hung up on me. I finally got through after 30 minutes of trying. 
There is a $30 dollar per day hold that is placed on your card, which may not be a big deal if you’re using a credit card but could create some issues if you’re using a debit card. And charges made to room service aren’t deducted from that hold – it is charged separately, which added additional unforeseen charges. Just a heads up for those traveling on a budget. There is a small gift store downstairs that serves a limited selection of snacks and soft drinks and various sundry items, but it is quite expensive, so I would recommend making the 10 minute walk down Wilshire to the CVS and picking up any snack items you might need. 
Overall, it was a great stay. As long as you know what you’re getting ahead of time and are not expecting more than what you’re paying for you should have no problems. Also, I am a female who stayed there alone and felt safe the entire time which counts for a lot in my book. I am returning next month and will definitely stay there again. 
A quick note about the airport shuttles. DO NOT use Shuttle Express. This is the most unprofessional outfit I have EVER dealt with and they attempted to get me to pay twice. The driver was unbelievably rude and insulting after I presented my proof of payment and refused to pay again. This was AFTER I had given him a generous tip. However, I used Prime Shuttle for my return to the airport and they were fantastic and only cost $22.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We had a wonderful experience at this property. The room was clean, large, with contemporary decorated styling. The beds were extremely comfortable and provided a refreshing sleep. The pool and hot tub were relaxing. Breakfast was delicious with a variety of choices. Don at the front desk was very friendly and professional.

title: “Best bed ever, great location for UCLA...”
text:
Loved it, got in really late and had to go to an 8am meeting at UCLA - gutted at getting out of the lovely lovely comfy bed :-)
Breakfast a total disappointment, a heap of donuts / muffins in a cardboard box in the corner of the lobby...
Wish I could have stayed longer, great hotel, love LA!!!

title: “Great location”
text: If you are coming from the airport(SFO)by train then this is the hotel for you! ,it is so close to the train station and tram stop which is fantastic.the staff are very nice and helpful,the rooms are very clean and large.the only thing that may put people off is the amount of homeless people around the area but I did NOT have any problems while staying in the area.the shower is good but they need brighter lights in the bathroom....very dull/dark.the beds are very firm which I loved but the pillows are too soft for me.there is a burger king,post office,wallgreens and subway ALL ONE BLOCK from the hotel......FANTASTIC!!!!!

title: “Very Nice Resort For Family Get-Away”
text:
We purchased the Family Fling & Swing Package which includes: $50 Resort Credit daily, Free Golf (certain time restrictions apply; see website), Free internet, Free kids meals 12 and under( at Blue Sage for breakfast/lunch/dinner, and dinner at Tuscany's as long as adult meals are ordered), Free appetizer or dessert, Free self parking, Free Resort Fee, 10% off retail purchases.
We stayed two nights, Friday & Saturday, which we thought were going to be very busy and overcrowded. But, thankfully, though it was busy, we didn't feel like we were suffocating. All hotel staff were very friendly and courteous. We were pleased with our hotel room. As mentioned in earlier reviews, the bathroom is massive and comes with a nice deep tub. The water pressure wasn't spectacular and the hot/cold shower knobs were very touchy. To get the "right temperature", we had to "play" with the knobs, so as to not get the water too hot or cold, which was tedious. The rooms give you two double or one king bed. We needed the doubles, which were somewhat comfortable, but the pillows are too small and either too soft or two hard. Next time, we will be bringing our own pillows. We enjoyed using the two comfy cozy bathrobes available to use during our stay. If you plan on using the fridge within the rooms, don't bother! There's absolutely no room! We brought our own ice chest with food for breakfast and lunch then had dinner at the resort. We enjoyed the $50 daily resort credit and used it towards dinners at Blue Sage and Tuscany Restaurants. The kids ate for free both nights, which was included in the package deal. So, for our dinner, we pretty much just paid for the tip. As far as dinner, Blue Sage wasn't very good. Service was extremely slow and not very attentive. Once our food came, we had to send a hamburger back that was cooked only to med. rare and not med well that we had ordered, then it took another 15 minutes to wait for it. With kids, you can only wait for food for so long and coloring gets old. Menu wasn't that great. The next night, dinner at Tuscany's was much better.
