We didn't have reservations, but didn't have to wait too long. Food was much better and service was more dependable.
The pool area was really nice. I am big on cleanliness, and it was exactly what we got. No "dirty ring" around the waterslide, like we saw at the Phoenix Point Hilton Squaw Peak Resort. All the pools were clean as well. Pool staff were working non-stop, keeping the pool area tidy. They also were friendly and courteous. It was such a hot weekend and there were many water stations placed throughout the pool area that had suffiicient ice water pitchers and cups available to use. We never had any trouble finding shady spots to plop our towels and belongings (we only needed 1 chair, as we were always in the water). The kids loved the Lazy river and basketball pool. Near the basketball pool there was a live band...believe it was reggae (?)...sounded very tropical island, which was nice because it really made you feel like you were on vacation. For lunch our last day, we had those tacos at the taco bar that other contributors were talking about. Mmm Mmmm!!! Only $3 per taco and you can chose from chicken or beef, plus they had fresh taco fix'ins. The taco bar also sold hotdogs as well.
The grounds are just beautiful. There are some close walking trails, which we didn't take advantage of this time, as it was too hot. But, I am sure there were some nice sights to see on the trails. Beautiful landscaping, waterfalls and flowers. Plenty of very nice outdoor furniture to relax on as well.
This was worth paying for as the saying goes "you get what you pay for". This resort was inviting, clean, comfortable, relaxing, fun. We look forward to going back.

title: “My stay at sun suites”
text: I had a wonderful stay at the sun suites. I am esther rios and d. thompson in room302. The management and faculity were wonderful service and you all have a nice facility.Thank you ..

title: “We will stay there again.”
text: We stayed at two hotels while in San Diego The Hyatt & The Doubletree. We would never go back to the Hyatt. Next time we will only stay at the Doubletree. As soon as we pulled up we liked what we saw. 1st there was FREE parking steps away from the lobby, that was a plus. Next a quick check in + warm cookies, that was a nice yummy surprise. The pool was nice and warm, and the lounge area was cozy. Overall we had a great stay.

title: “Great location if you want to be right downtown Memphis”
text: We stayed two nights and paid a little extra for a "downtown" view, which we received. There was a daily fee for parking, but it was a self-park (with unlimited in/out access). Also, getting to the parking garage was a hassle. You either had to take the service elevator (which was slow and very much in demand) or you had to take the regular elevator to either the 4th floor and walk down to either the 2nd or 3rd (depending on which level your car was on) or take it to the lobby and walk up. Not very convenient. There was complimentary coffee and donuts in the lobby in the mornings, which was nice. We did not eat at the restaurants as we generally find hotel food to be lacking (plus there is so much local food to try!). The room itself was above average. It was large and nicely appointed. The bathroom really was showing some wear and tear with lots of rust spots and cracks.

title: “Adorable Boutique Hotel”
text: I booked here to attend a conference and didn't research much ahead of time to have much in the way of expectations. Very happy to have selected the hotel. My room was small but adorable. Great products in the vanity area. Free bottled water and wifi were nice amenities. Onsite gym and yoga were great too. Comfortable walking distance to the convention center and gas lamp area. Some street noise outside but bathroom fan helps to cancel it out. I will definitely stay here again on my next trip to San Diego.

title: “Seattle vacation”
text: Overall good place to stay except the pool was outdoors.

title: “Honeymoon”
text:
We stayed at the Lombardy for our honeymoon week, and it was lovely! The room was clean, well maintained, and HUGE! We had the deluxe, and it was everything we could have hoped for. 
The location can't be beat...walking distance to all the shopping, sight seeing, restaurants, museums you could hope for. Also, if you have a room with a kitchen, there is a Whole Foods about 2 blocks from the hotel, and we stocked up with lots of fresh fruit and breakfast items. While I normally wouldn't shop at WF (seriously, that much for cantalope?!) it was very handy. 
There were a few things missing in the kitchenette, (a sharp knife, bottle opener, no coffee filters) but on the whole, everything we really needed was there. 
Thank you for being such a wonderful part of our honeymoon Lombardy! We can't wait to come back:)

title: “Pros outweigh the Con”
text:
Hotel Kabuki is not a super-luxurious property, but it has many things going for it that make it a great choice for lodging in SF. I think staying in real SF neighborhoods, such as Japan Town, North Beach, Pacific Heights, etc., as opposed to touristy areas, such as Union Square or Fisherman's Wharf, is so much more rewarding in this city. This hotel is stylish; our room was generously sized; the location is close to everything; service is friendly and helpful; wonderful views can be had from the higher floors. Being attached to the Japan Center is so convenient, not only for the many interesting shops and yummy restaurants found there, but also for the best value parking garage in all of SF! Overnight self-parking only cost us $13 because this is a city-owned lot. Some nights, it's even easy to find street parking for free.
I didn't give Hotel Kabuki 5 stars because the property is getting a bit time-worn and shabby. Some things in our room needed to be painted or spruced up. One reason we chose this hotel was for the deep Japanese soaking tub in most of the rooms; however, upon seeing it in person, we didn't want to use it. It appeared dingy and stained, not because housekeeping hadn't cleaned it, but because it simply needed to be replaced after much use. This was disappointing, and not what I expect from a joie de vivre hotel. Even the black wooden Japanese-style soap dish in our bathroom had chipping paint. Yes, it's a small item (which would be easy and cheap to replace) but it leaves you with the impression that the hotel is not that well maintained.
The slightly dilapidated state is really the only con I can say about Hotel Kabuki. The prices here are really a very good value for SF, and it's fun to stay in a hotel with a distinctly Japanese character which really reminds you that you're in San Francisco.

title: “Excellent location”
text: This hotel is in a great location for walikng to all the sights in San Fransisco. It is also close to the stops for the Hop-On and Hop-Off Bus. The hotel staff is very helpful and friendly. The rooms were very clean and the beds were VERY comfortable. Lombard St. is a little noisy so ask for a room on the side of the hotel.

title: “Amazing wedding weekend at the Four Seasons in Philadelphia”
text:
We had our wedding in Philadelphia on 9/22/12 and virtually all of our out of town guests stayed at the beautiful Four Seasons Hotel. Our guests had an absolutely wonderful experience. The rooms were beautiful, the lounge areas turned into our family hangouts and and the hotel decor was perfect.
The Four Seasons reservation team was amazing...coordinating and accommodating people from all over the world. We had guests from as far away as Singapore. The Four Seasons Philadelphia impressed them all! We couldn't have been welcomed by nicer people...from the bell men, to the greeters, the concierge and the front desk staff...all were so gracious and welcoming. 
The day of the wedding couldn't have gone any smoother...the bridal suite was the most beautiful and luxurious room a bride and groom could have asked for. Of course there were many small and meaningful touches they did for us....pastries, strawberries, notes, welcome gifts, but they even SURPRISED us with personal MONOGRAMMED pillows on our wedding night. The views of the museums and fountains were breathtaking. They also gave us a special get ready room that was perfect for all the bridesmaids.
The Sunday brunch setup and banquet team were outstanding. It was like a surprise 2nd wedding reception...made beautiful entirely by the Four Seasons. 
The hotel spa was just what we needed the day before the wedding. Relaxing massages and flexible scheduling to make sure we made it on time to all of our wedding events. Our guests enjoyed the pool very much...especially the children.
We enjoyed the Four Seasons so much we stayed an extra day after the wedding. Our family and guests were so eager to get back to the hotel between wedding events and trips around Philly! Our departure from the Four Seasons was a sad, sad time.
We love the Four Seasons in Philadelphia and would highly recommend it for your wedding weekend. It is simply the best hotel in Philadelphia.

title: “It leaves a lot to be desired!”
text: Our party reserved 5 rooms and there were quite a lot of problems. The location is fantastic, however too many problems existed to recommend this place. Upon check in, there was a used tray from room service on the floor outside one of our rooms.... and it was still on the floor the following afternoon-Yuck! The front desk couldn't tell us if our breakfasts were, or were not included in the price of the rooms. (They wanted $19 for a continental breakfast which was often bare and it took a half an hour to get an order of toast.) The rooms didn't have adequate lighting to read and the coffee included with the in-room machines were 2 measely single packs. Find a place where you can be treated like a guest, rather than an inmate.

title: “Cool and trendy hotel in great location”
text: We only stayed at this hotel for one night but would definitely stay there again. We booked a deluxe one bed suite on Priceline (excellent rate) and, having heard about NY hotel rooms, were surprised at how spacious it was. The bathroom is tiny with no separate shower. The bed is outstandingly comfortable. We enjoyed the free internet access downstairs and loved the overall design and feel of the place. Contemporary, yet friendly and welcoming. The bar area is great for a pre dinner drink, not too crowded on a Wed night but with a nice buzz. Our room was on the street (6th floor) but the noise was not a problem for us. One tip re airport transfer: leave ample time! Our taxi took over 2 hrs to get to JFK from the Shoreham and we missed our flight to London. We were advised (not by the hotel) that it would take 45mins so we left an hour and a half to be on the safe side. A combination of rush hour and a protest demonstration in Manhattan counted against us, so be warned!

title: “We feel like we were at a cheap MotelDid not have enough...”
text:
We feel like we were at a cheap Motel
Did not have enough pillows.
We were at non-smoking rooms, and people were smoking out side our door and talking until 3 am.
We call front desk and who ever answer said that the person in charge was not in front.
We did not rest. Horrible "Continental Breakfast".
Never coming back.
Never coming back.

title: “Nice hotel but a little over priced. Go to Priceline and get it for $80.”
text:
Me, my husband and 2 year old went to Indy for a buisness meeting and to go to the childrens museum. I checked the room rate online and it was 228 (wow) tooo expensive. So I went to priceline and got the room for 80 per night (better). 
 I called the hotel while on the road to find out if there was anyway that we could check in early because our 2 year old was fussy. NO PROBLEM. We were allowed to check in at 9am. GREAT. Check was a breeze and my daughter was greeted by a childs bag that included a night light, first aid kit, child socket covers and a rubber duck. Then we went to our room and the bed was very comfortable, but the bathroom was a little small. So, while my daughter took a nap I was looking at all of the hotel amentities. They brought us a small potty for my daughter that played music, a step stool so she could get on the bed without any assistance, and a extra robe for my husband. The list of extras were a mile long. Also if your children are getting a little restless before dinner you can go to lobby around 5p and they offer fruit, cheese and crackers.
 The pool was ok, it did not have stairs (just ladders). The work out room was nice but if your kids have to use the restrooms when using the pool they have to go through the workout room to get to the restroom. The floor was slippery and a little uncomfortable to have to walk through the workout room to use the restroom when you are soaking weat.
 The childrens museum is about 3 miles away. There are plenty of resturants, movie theaters, shopping and sports venues close to the hotel. Also there is a skywalk that can take you plenty of places. Hotel was difficult to find on the GPS but we found it after going around the blocks a couple of times. Parking was expensive. Breakfast was delivered on time in the morning.

title: “Excellent!”
text: We stayed during the 4th of July week. It was extremely hot and very busy weekend in downtown Detroit. There was a series of Tigers game for the 4th and we stayed over several days. The room was nice and cool when we came back after sitting in the sweltering heat (we turned the air down before we left for the games) The staff was really nice despite the huge rush of people at the front desk trying to check-in. The room was a good size. I have stayed at other hotels in the same area and for the money you spend this is the best place. They have valet parking which is nice since I don't like parking my car in one of the many "street lots" for the price you pay for valet you could easily spend 4 times that in parking on the street or in the small garages scattered around. They have a shuttle avaliable most of the time, but it is close enough you can walk to most of the places downtown.

title: “extremely nice hotel”
text:
Booked a premium deluxe room and was upgraded to a luxurious suite (I think it was a Metropolitan suite). Decor was extremely modern with some truly bizarre "objets d'arte" and yet it was elegant and inviting.. The bedroom was beautiful and cozy and plush. Automated drapes in the huge living room and br.....good idea to close them during the day because all the glass makes for a very warm suite (and wastes energy if you leave on the a.c.)
Our suite was huge and in excellent condition...the bath was luxurious, the bed was extremely comfortable and everything was the best....the linens, towels, comforters, etc. 
The pool is gorgeous...totally beautiful with magnificent lounging beds...and it was empty every time we used it.
The lobby is very chic and would appeal to very sleek, well-dressed younger people especially.
The breakfast restaurant was excellent as well. The design of the restaurant (this is their casual restaurant) is lovely. It is one of the few hotel restaurants where the food was actually hot and delicious at breakfast and all but one of the servers was gracious and efficient.
The reception staff and the front office managers were quite nice...I am a starwood platinum member and I was treated well. However, I find the attitude of the staff at the St. Regis hotels to be somewhat cold and aloof. I felt the GM at the hotel must have a stingy nature, because certain amenities which one would normally find in this calibre of luxury hotel were not provided. For example, no welcome amenity, no extra soaps, etc in the bath, a paltry amount of towels....a small matter, but curious.
Housekeeping was perfect and the room was always immaculate.
The spa is gorgeous and expensive.
I was not crazy about the location of the hotel. This is not a factor for which the hotel is responsible, obviously . The neighborhood is lively and lots to do nearby but my favorite parts of SF were not readily in reach. The concierge gives excellent suggestions and directions and we had a wonderful time.
All in all, an excellent choice with great service and a top quality product.

title: “Balcony rooms”
text: Several years ago I stayed at the Wellington because of its reasonable price and proximity to Central Park. When I checked in the room was adequate, but faced an airshaft, or "central courtyard" as the euphemism goes. After arguing with myself for ten minutes about how much the lack of view was really going to matter, I returned to check in and asked for a room with an outside view. To my absolute delight I was given one of the few single rooms with a balcony, on a very high floor. On the balcony, I looked to my right and saws the glorious entirety of Central Park. Looking straight ahead I saw the sun shining on the Hudson River. Looking to my left I saw the length of 7th Avenue and the canyon of New York buildings. The room was small and clean, nothing special. The bathroom was small and clean, nothing special. But that view made any shortcomings of the hotel irrelevant.

title: “Very Large and Clean Rooms”
text: We found this hotel very nice and spacious. Bedding was very comfortable and the suite was well equipped and spacious. The hotel provided a free shuttle from the airport (where we dropped off a rental car), to and from a nearby restaurant, and again the next morning to the airport. Contrary to another review, we found the shuttle service excellent and very quick. Breakfast, as with other Homewood Suites, was good with plenty of variety. Highly recommended for close accomodations near Sea-Tac Airport.

title: “GREAT space! GREAT value!”
text:
We stayed at Eastgate Tower for two nights. We rented a two bedroom suite which easily accommodated our party of 5 adults and a child. It was really more like an apartment than a hotel room. There was a HUGE living room with comfortable pullout sofa, large dining room, spacious bedroom with 2 double beds, FULL kitchen, another bedroom with 2 twin beds AND two full bathrooms. It was only a 5 minute walk to Grand Central so transportation was easy. The morning we left, we took a taxi to Penn Station and even with all of the traffic, it was still only $10.00. Eastgate is not the most luxurious place--it's a bit dated--BUT it was VERY clean, nice neighborhood, GREAT staff--perfect for families or groups that are looking for an affordable place to stay but don't need a lot of frills (which of course adds $$$.) I HIGHLY recommend Eastgate Tower Hotel.
My only complaint would be street noise. We stayed at a different location near Herald Square and never heard a thing. At Eastgate my husband actually got up to make sure the window was closed because it sounded like every car or siren was right next to us even though we were on the 22nd floor.

title: “Perfect for Market!”
text: This is my favorite hotel for Dallas market. The rooms are large and comfortable with a sink area in the bathroom and just outside it - perfect for two ladies getting ready. It is close enough to market to walk, or there is a regular market shuttle that runs to the hotel. Good room service and free parking. I usually stay at the Anatole, the Adolphus, the Stoneleigh, or the Hyatt during market and the Reniassance is the only one of that group that you can self park and not have to fuss with valet, which is always nice but can really slow me down and cost $30 - $35 a night at other locations between hotel charges and tips.

title: “Start spreading the news...”
text: We stayed here during the first part of our honeymoon vacation in July 2010. First impressions are that the hotel is well placed for getting around Manhatten with a subway station seconds away from the main entrance. The hotel has a decor to suit an acquired taste but doesnt offend. When we got to our room we had a complementary bottle of champagne waiting which was a nice gesture. The room was smaller than many hotels but had everything we needed. It was clean and well maintained. The gem of this hotel is the roof top bar which is very impressive. The view of the empire state building is hard to beat anywhere in Manhatten. We had breakfast twice and found it to have something for everyone and was constantly well stocked. We would recommend this to anyone looking for a good central location to explore the city.

title: “Mind the Cockroach!”
text:
Booked this hotel on the strength of other reviews here but were very dissapointed. We had a superior room which was small, dark and unclean with a huge cockroach in the bathroom. I dread to think what a standard room was like.
I have never been so pleased to checkout of a hotel!

title: “Lovely hotel- great location”
text: I was here for business, for just 1 night. The room was more than adequate and the bed comfy. View from my room was so typical of NY as i looked into 3 other buildings. I have stayed in more luxurious hotels, and more modern hotels, but this hotel has style and grace.

title: “Five Stars for Four Seasons”
text: Or, buttons, rather. Now, partly, this is what you'd expect from an upscale place like the Four Seasons. But partly, it's a superbly-run hotel, with a high attention to detail, beautiful interiors, great features. I don't always get to stay in such a posh place, but the Four Seasons Denver sets the bar for high-end hotel experience.

title: “Seriously...so good!”
text:
Staying at hotels has become a hobby of mine...I truly, truly enjoy it. And I hope to oneday work for the hotel industry and/or review hotels for a living...
This hotel is easily, easily in my top 5 --- all tied for 1st place of course! To be frank, I don't know why...and I don't even care whether this was energy efficient or not, but when I walked into my room, all the lights were on, nice & bright, the tv was on too and tuned into the hyatt welcome channel...it was great! Made me feel welcome &...special even:-)
Count it...all the amenities are there...yes folks, including toothpaste! I don't even know where to start so this review will be all over the place. The decor of the room was right...just right (see the pics). The bathroom was beautiful! The lighting was perfect. Guest services (including room service) was top-notch...the lobby bar is gorgeous...the lobby overall was great...the restaurant with the breakfast buffet was great...even their little gift shop was great...oh, and the gym was equipped with lots of new equipment! I mean...just go...it's a nice area (Capitol Hill)...a little far from National Mall...but it's still in walking distance. Right by Union Station --- which was a great spot for food options & shopping. Only 1 tiny...tiny...tiny flaw...the pool is small...and not that new...but who cares? Who goes to DC to swim anyway...
I mean...just go:-)

title: “Old World Charm in downtown Philly”
text: Apparently this is the oldest hotel in Philadelphia and it's nicely located in the heart of the downtown area and close to the Convention Center which is a short 10 minute walk. I stayed here for a convention and overall found it a pleasant hotel. The hotel staff were all very nice and accommodating. My room was large, clean and nicely decorated, in a style fitting the old world charm of the hotel's entire decor. The bathroom was spacious with lots of counter space although I think they could have done a slightly nicer job on the fixtures -- I'm obsessive about bathrooms and you can always tell when a property has skimped when you look at the fixtures and shower heads. The shower head was a cheap, basic Speakman. For a hotel of this decor and level, the should have upgraded those. My toilet had a problem the first night I was there and they had to send up an engineer to fix it which was a minor inconvenience but they did fix it quickly and everything was back in working order within 15 minutes. I didn't eat at any of the hotel restaurants nor did I use the fitness center, although the staff was kind enough to suggest a running trail for me which I did follow and was glad I had a chance to see downtown Philly and the Schuylkill River running the route they suggested. Overall I had a nice stay here and would stay here again and recommend it, given its central location, nice staff and spacious rooms.

title: “Never again!”
text: The hotel front desk was so unorganized! Asked for the manager and they said we are all managers, what? Need to go for more training! Don't leave any change laying around because it will dissappear! Told the front desk about it and he never flinched , like it happens often. If you want to leave a tip for the housekeeping staff it is not until you check out. No bathroom privacy..whatever happened to doors on bathrooms? The only thing positive was the comfy bed and the door staff.

title: “Modern, clean rooms”
text: I spent 3 nights at the Westin. It is a large hotel, beautiful lobby, confusing elevator system, but he elevator has a great view! I found the rooms to be very clean and quiet. My room included a small refrigerator. I was told that the rooms in the center tower are larger but don't have anything to compare them to. The location didn't seem to be near many sights but was near some shopping options. There are several dining options within the hotel complex. Join the loyalty program for a few extra perks. Very helpful staff.

title: “Moved out after one night of a 5night stay”
text:
My husband and I were shocked at the standard of the rooms * in the first room our bathroom window was jammed open and a bathroom towel had been used to block the freezing night air * no porter arrived to assist us in our move to a second room - we had already unpacked * in our second room there was no plug in the bath and when we requested one we were told to use a towel to plug the bath as they did not have any more plugs available * No Double Glazing in our room facing onto Broadway so we could not sleep!
* carpets in passages were filthy
* there was one redeeming feature and that was the receptionist who allowed us to check out of the hotel the following morning and thus cancel our 5night stay - we were thrilled and moved in to a fantastic midtown hotel where we could relax in a superb room and enjoy service and facilities of a very high standard for only a fraction more in price.

title: “Great property with excellent service”
text: Beautiful place, great breakfast and managers reception. Ducks in the lobby pools are a nice touch.

title: “Fantastic Stay-nice hotel, great amenities, great location, great staff”
text: It was our first trip to downtown Chicago (family of four with kids ages 8 & 10,) and we didn't know where to stay. So while I was hesitant to book a hotel based on online information and recommendations, the Four Points Sheraton really worked out great for us. I would recommend this hotel to anyone, business and family travelers alike. It had all of the amenities that were mentioned online-secure, attached parking garage, we could come and go with our car as often as we pleased (no valet.) The parking garage was well-lit and had elevators/doors directly into the hotel. We had a package deal that included parking, and I wasn't sure what to expect, and I was impressed. Our room was clean and had a fridge and microwave, which came in handy. The pool/hot tub area was clean, and our kids had a great time swimming even though the pool was only 3.5 feet deep. We didn't use the workout room, but it looked adequate and had more equipment than I would have expected. This hotel is in a great location. Michigan Avenue is only one block away. The area outside the hotel was well-lit and had heavy foot traffic. We did a lot of walking to and from Michigan Avenue and never felt unsafe. I also have to mention the staff. They were very, very helpful, nice and polite. I don't know if it was intentional, but they put our family in a room close to the pool. I really can't think of any drawbacks to this hotel. Maybe it wasn't as fancy as some hotels in the area down there, but the room wasn't drabby or outdated at all, either. Just a regular, nice hotel. We will definitely stay there the next time we visit Chicago.

title: “Avoid”
text: The only redeeming feature of this hotel is it's location. Despite our room being booked months in advance, on checking in we were told it wasn't available. When I refused to accept another room with a roll down bed for my teenage son, as if by magic our original room was available again. No coffee maker available in rooms unless by request. Sullen staff and a useless front desk didn't make this a good experience. I wondered why the pictures on the walls showed star visitors from years ago. Now I know.

title: “Lovely Hotel”
text: We stayed at this hotel at the end of November 2011 and loved it. Our room was comfortable and pleasant, had everything we needed and was maintained beautifully by housekeeping. All the staff were professional, friendly and helpful and made us feel like we were "at home". We enjoyed the bar though felt the furniture there could do with a spruce up. Unfortunately there were building renovations on 77 St which started very early in the morning and affected our ability to sleep. We understand that the hotel was doing all it could to minimize the disruption to their guests. All in all a delightful stay and the Mark will now be our first choice when in NYC.

title: “Old World Elegance and Charm”
text:
We recently stayed at The Drake, we enjoyed the executive amenities ,the room was lovely
and had a view of the lake.We enjoyed the Coq D'or and the location of the hotel was close to fabulous restaurants and great shopping. Concierge were helpful and sent us to a great restaurant within walking distance.I can't wait until my next trip to Chicago, we will be staying at The Drake.

title: “Sweet”
text: We arrived and had to park a few blocks down because valet at the hotel was $45 a night maybe because of the celtics being in the playoffs. We parked a few blocks down for $25 instead. That was not a big deal and we enjoyed the walk which let us see the restaurants to choose from. The hotel offered wine to welcome us and were quick at setting us up in our room. The room was very nice and modern looking. The bathroom was clean and bed was very comfortable. Overall a great experience and very close to the stadium which was perfect for us!

title: “At The Crossroads of the World”
text:
The newly renovated Grand Hyatt above Grand Central Station in New York City is a very exciting place to stay. The lobby is always very crowded with a huge group of hotel guests, business conference attendees, etc. Last week school children from across the globe attended a model United Nations at this hotel and the lobby was filled with diverse middle school children all dressed in suit and tie or dress and hose, beautifully behaved and very excited to be there.
The rooms are small to average, pleasingly renovated and extremely comfortable and quiet. I enjoyed my stay immensely and will surely be back because the location, right above Grand Central Station, is superb for travel and the dining choices and shopping are amazing.

title: “Loud”
text: Finally...the loud street noise outside my window was replaced with the even louder A/C kicking in. Staff is very well trained, in an American Airlines sort of way. They know the rules to the letter and won't vary, even if it is easy and will make the customer happy. Rooms were basic, standard Hilton Garden, nothing special. If you can't get a free breakfast, I Hop is across the highway and don't miss dinner at Bone Daddy's which shares the parking lot.

title: “AWESOME Resort & Great for Families”
text: This place is AWESOME. Everybody here is friendly and willing to help in every way. Three water slides, lazy river, a kiddie pool area, a huge pool and an adult pool as well. This is by far the best resort in San Antonio. We took a family of 6 here and had plenty of activities to do for them. We ran into some rain and the resort had kid board games for them to play as well while we waited for the water area to open back up. TPC course is great as well. Everyone there was just as friendly as the resort. Our room was great and bigger than we expected. We very rarely heard any noise in our room from others. Once again this is the place to stay!!

title: “Good for Location, Service, and Comfort for a Trouble Free Stay”
text: As big city hotels go, the Hyatt is more than passable though it would not necessarily "wow" you. The room we had was clean and serviced well every day which included a turn down service each evening. The size of the room was average but the bed was very comfortable. Staff at the check-in desk and the concierge were all friendly and efficient. Because we did not encounter any problems during our 3-day stay, I couldn't say how they would respond to service requests. But then, trouble-free is preferred. We found the location to be very convenient - a few minutes from "T" (subway) stops; 10-15 minute walk to Quincy Market, adjacent to lively Washington St. which then takes you to many interesting places, dining areas, and shopping; and a couple of blocks from Chinatown. Boston is a great walking city so you want to be in a hotel that provides you easy walking access to much that Boston has to offer. The only issue I had was the strange location of the fitness room. The fitness room itself was okay but getting to it required an almost labyrinthine journey. Overall, a highly recommended hotel.

title: “Feeling like you belong”
text: When you travel thousands of miles to a different culture with different systems, you could not get better than the Sheraton on Dalton Street. We arrived and were offered an upgrade for $30 per night from traditional to club. For the first 2 nights the club was unavailable, but when we did move room (which took no time) we were further upgraded to a Club Suite at no charge. The staff made us feel as if we really did belong in the Hotel, they were friendly without being pushy at all. The rooms were both very clean and the decor is precise and without clutter (we had previously spend a week at the over-rated Waldorf=Astoria in New York). You can easily afford to eat and drink at the Sheraton. So many hotels have luxurious public spaces and poor rooms. Not the Sheraton. The Club level allows you access to free drinks (cans of pop etc) throughout the day. The best breakfast is to be had down in the Apropos area as the Club is only toast, cakes, porridge etc - no scrambled eggs or bacon or sausages. Club also gives you free drinks (soft) and appetisers in the lounge area each evening 6-8pm. The portions are vast and you wont need an evening meal! Alternatively 'go green' and you collect $5 per night you decline housekeeping - fish & chips is only $15 so you can easily collect enough for a free meal. We have stayed in many hotels - all 4 or 5 star and this is the best. We actually spent our money on doing things we liked!

title: “Lower Manhattan, Millenium Hilton”
text: Stayed here from April 5 to 10th, 2009. Upgraded to a corner suite on the 51st floor with a great view of Brooklyn Bridge and Statue of Liberty. Excellent room with comfortable surroundings, friendly staff and great Concierge! 25 steps out the door to the 4,5,6 trains to Upper Manhattan and around the corner to giant discount shopping. Just an excellent stay at a great hotel. Highly recommended!

title: “Cheap and good”
text:
I was in San Francisco for just one night. Got a twin room and had no complaints really. 
For what I paid, i couldn't be happier, the room was clean and comfortable, a bit of an old musty, grandmas closet type of smell, bit that didn't last long and it didn't bother me. 
Breakfast was included but was pretty limited... Fruit cereal pastries & muffins. 
The bar on the ground floor was great, cheap beer and free hot dogs, popcorn and chips for the superbowl
Would recommend dor those on the cheap

title: “Fantastic Hotel - beautiful!!”
text: Stayed here for 5 nights. The hotel was quite expensive but well worth it. Found the twin room very spacious and full of frills! There was certainly no expense spared when this hotel was renovated. Found the staff very friendly and helpful. I thought that the coffee in the morning a great touch. Also the turn down service with Lindt sweets was great. The location of the hotel was great. A lovely area in the heart of the city! Very very central. This hotel really exceeded my expectations and the staff really went that extra mile for the customer. Will most certainly stay here again. A model hotel!!

title: “Not worth the money you think your saving”
text: I booked Hotel Bijou because they were running a 50% off deal ... it wasnt worth the money saved!!! There was NO Air Conditioning and when I asked for a fan the hotel clerk just huffed and said to open the window. The curtains looked like there had been a murder with wierd dark red substance all over them. The room was very small and not all that clean. The location is literally a block or two from the heart of it all but unfortunetley is also right next to a very sketchy area on a street called Eddy. You could hear people yelling and the smell of urine was overwhelming. One last thing ... plan on paying about $27-$35 a day for parking ....

title: “Perfect!”
text:
The room and the BED were perfect! the place is clean and heavenly located. You feel safe and pampered the minute you check in. Great Staff also! 
The prices are a bit high even if you dont get a great view but if you want to stay close to times square this is probably the best "affordable" option

title: “Great stay”
text: We stayed at this hotel on a return trip from Orlando. It is conveniently located off of I-77 in a nice quiet area. It is adjacent to several other hotels. The check in was quick. We received room 622 which was described as a penthouse. It had one full bedroom in a loft and a murphy bed downstairs (pull out from wall). There also was a sleeper sofa available. The room had a full kitchen, a 4 piece place setting of dishes as well as table and 4 chairs. Room was well kept and clean. Two full baths also. The room comfortably fit our family of five (three small kids). The room was big enough to spend several days in if necessary. The pool was well kept but lacked enough pool towels. The hours were also short as it closed at 9PM. After driving all day, a closing time of 11PM would have been better. Check out was simple as well. Front desk personnel were extremely helpful with any question I had. Complimentary breakfast was average. Nice selection but kitchen help could not keep up with the amount of people eating. Didn't stay long enough to check out the area but would stay again at this hotel if in the area.

title: “Thin thin walls”
text:
I was here for business, so I needed to get a good nights sleep at regular hours (12-7). The walls in this place are amazingly thin - I could hear everything that was happening in the room next to me. Also at night, there's quite a few noisy guests walking down the aisles - and I can hear them as well - really disrupted my sleep. 
Also, the amenities are very poor for a hotel at this price point. No free wifi. No free gym. W T F. 
The only thing that I liked was the comfortable bed. 
Will never stay here again.

title: “Great Location, helpful staff”
text: Overlooks Chicago River; leave hotel, cross street and walk along the river's path to Lake Michigan. Along the way there are bike rentals, cafe's, boat cruises, water taxis...invigorating way to exercise and see water. Shop on N State St one block away. Here's the mecca of retail discount shopping...Filene's Basement, TJMaxx, Loehmann's, Nordstrom's Rack, Sears/LandsEnd, H&M..on and on... Bargains? You bet. Upscale dining practically adjacent to hotel...Morton's, Mccormick & Schmick, Smith & Wollensky. And if you walk over the bridge and about 1/4 mile you'll find Chicago greats like the ORIGINAL Uno and close-by is Due (DOO-ay) the second one built to handle Uno's overflow. My fave restaurant is 1/2 mi from hotel called Quartino. Italian tapas that's so good, I dream about it. (see Quartino's reviews). The staff at the hotel are very friendly and helpful. We were there for 4 nights and no problems at all. Room itself is a little worn, the sheets had a few holes in them and they use only flat (no fitted sheets) sheets which kept getting untucked and made the bed look sloppy.. Housekeeper saw we were buying water and she kept leaving us free bottles...nice touch. We had a car and knew ahead of the $40/night charge so no surprise there (and it was comparable to other parking garages/hotels nearby. ) We needed a car to visit relatives but between the nearby L , walking, and taxis; the average visitor would not need a car.

title: “A gem of a Hotel; great location to Sea World, Six Flags, free shuttle!”
text:
Stayed three nights using Priority Club Points. I wasn't expecting much at 15000 points a night, but I chose it based on proximity to Sea World and Six Flags.
The staff is outstanding, the hotel is in immaculate shape, easy parking, and clean rooms. We had two kids along so the two queen size beds were great. Many hotel rooms with two beds only offer double size beds. 
They provide free shuttle to Sea World avoiding a parking fee and drop you and pick-up right at the entrance. Only a 10 minute drive to Six Flags, and 15-20 minutes to River Walk and Alamo. A truly outstanding experience and value.

title: “Amazing experience for travelers on a budget!”
text: My husband and I, both students, couldn't believe the great hotel we snagged for $65/night on Expedia! The Powell has 1920s charm - from the wide staircases to the cosy rooms - that you just can't get at a Super 8, but it's still the same price! The location is amazing - just 25 steps from the nearest BART stop, plenty of shops and restaurants, and the trolley car turnaround. We requested a room overlooking the turnaround, where only pedestrians and trolleys are allowed to cross over the cobblestone street. So charming!!! The staff are friendly and helpful. The hotel closes its doors to everyone but guests after dusk to ensure adequate security. This was definitely a major plus in our first trip to San Francisco and we hope to visit again soon!

title: “Probably the best hotel in Chicago”
text: Very impressed by this hotel. Very friendly and observant staff. Impeccable rooms, bright and modern decor with all the amenities you could want, including 42 inch flat screen and CD/MP3 music system. Location is great both close to Mag Mile and subway. Hotel has turn down service, so when you arrive back in your room after dinner, you will have dimmed light and music, and today’s biscuit on the pillow - small thing to do, but it ensures that your room is a nice and cosy place to come back to in the evening.

title: “Great customer service! Excellent choice for families desiring suites”
text:
We stayed at Residence Inn (Mission Valley) for 2 nights in May. The property has great customer service and the suites are perfect for families. We reserved the property a couple of hours before driving down from Anaheim, and were pleasantly surprised that we had been upgraded to a 2 bedroom suite considering the number of people in our party. It speaks about the attitude of the staff that someone bothered to look at our situation and offered us an upgrade that was just perfect for us and very well appreciated. 
The included buffet breakfast is an excellent value and adds to the convenience - it does end a little early, but that just encourages you to get started early in the day :)

title: “The hotel was clean, staff extemely pleasant and our room was spacious!!!”
text: We had a wonderful time, the hotel was fantastic!!

title: “Fantastic hotel, wonderful setting.”
text: We stayed here in August. It was the first destination of our first holiday in California and we were delighted with the setting, the ambiance and the amenities. We rode the free bikes, played table tennis and putting. From the poolside we were able to listen to Smokey Robinson live in concert which was an unexpected surprise. We would recommend this hotel to families in particular and we would certainly use it again.

title: “Nice place”
text: We stayed here for one night after our cruise so we could see Seattle. We arrived at 9am, so naturally our room wasn't ready, but they stored our luggage while we left to tour the city. Upon returning we went to the room and it was a nice, large room(after being in a small stateroom for a week it seemed huge!) with 2 queen beds. It also had a microwave and fridge. This would be a good place to stay before a cruise because I noticed they had shuttles to the piers in the morning. We ate in the restaurant and it was very good and the people were very friendly. I highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Good Hotel but DONT do Regency Club for Holiday (only really good for business)”
text: We stayed for 5 nights in the Regency Club level. Hotel was clean and modern with good service. Concierge were fantastic and really helpful when trying to find great places to eat - they gave great advice. Hotel food was nice, especially the lunch. The regency club rooms were smaller than expected and bathroom was a little disappointing. I would advise definately NOT to do the regency club unless you're on business as there is a smaller choice of breakfast than in the normal hotel, happy hour drinks aren't free (as they are in some hyatt regency's) and for the money you pay to upgrade it's really not worth it, but having said that the circular top floor bar area only accessible by regency club people is lovely! We found the hotel a bit "hit and miss" but only because we upgraded to regency club. Otherwise i'd reccommend it.

title: “First Time Disappointment”
text: Our first time to the area and found this little hotel on the beach in San Diego. Must say that I am very disappointed in our stay. When we arrrived we were informed that the water had been turned off for maintenance and would not be on for 5 hours. We had to go to a deli to us the facilities. We found our room to be clean but the TV did not work, broken cable, suggested we insert wire into cable input, which did not work. Next morning we went to the beach, come back for lunch and showers, no water until 4 pm. Must say that the staff working at this location were super friendly and compassionate about our situation.

title: “Good location, good people”
text: Everyone here is pleasant and really seems to appreciate your business. In the bistro area, there are booths with a TV and outlets so you can work and not have to worry about your battery. Very nice feature that is not mentioned anywhere. The room was clean and of nice size. You may be able to hear the traffic on I-% as the hotel overlooks the Interstate. Parking is available primarily underground. It is a short 2 1/2 block walk to the main drag of old town for restaurants. Took around 5 minutes r so to get there. I would use this hotel again. The air-conditioning in my room was a bit loud when ti was cooling which might affect a lite sleeper.

title: “Will stay here again.”
text:
We won our bid on priceline for 3 nights at the Doubletree in Memphis East. I was cautiously optimistic because of previous reviews, but it turns out, I had nothing to worry about. Comparable with other hotels in the area and ideal location to local business. Front desk assigned us a clean, comfortable mid-upper room at end of hall and we didn't hear a sound, inside or out during our stay. 
A promotional display blocked the handicapped access when we arrived, but was moved immediately when we alerted management. Construction in the front lobby was not obtrusive. USA Today was delivered to room at no extra charge, free wi-fi, but breakfast was not included. Lots of great places to eat nearby including Gus' Famous Fried Chicken. Pastries across the street at Muddy's Bakeshop and a few blocks away at Gibson's Donuts.
I look forward to staying here again.

title: “Worst hotel ever”
text: The hotel was small, old and dirty. I could not wait to check out

title: “Very memorable stay!”
text: Great and friendly staff. Valets were efficient and always had a smile on their face. Close to everything we wanted to do in San Diego!

title: “Simply The Best”
text:
This place is the best and the service is just great. We arrived early and they offered to hold our bags. We arrived around 10am. I was surprised to receive a call around 1pm saying we could check in and they upgraded our room. The room was incredible and the service was great. They also have a shared and private deck that look right down at Pikes Market.
Stop looking and book at this hotel. It is that good.

title: “Love this hotel!!!!!”
text: The W hotel is the only hotel I stay at in New York City. I travel a lot and from personal experience i definitely recommend the W hotel! The staff were very friendly and energetic, the rooms were always clean. And you cant beat the BLISS products they give you in the hotel rooms! They are awesome! I wont ever stay anywhere else in NYC but the W hotel! People complain about the rooms but PLEASE its NYC!!! Every hotel in NYC will have the same size rooms......

title: “Could use a little up keep to stay with the 3+ downtown hotels”
text: Stayed at the Crowne Plaza 5 yrs ago on the same floor and nothing has changed since. It is comfortable but they need to update a few things. From the parking garage (which costs $20 a day) you can swipe your room key and go directly to your floor which was nice. The pool is outdoors and is only open from May-Sept (I think it said) which was a disappointment.

title: “Unpretentious, friendly, clean, in a great area - can't beat it!”
text:
I stayed here with my 7-year-old daughter. The staff were unpretentious, friendly and courteous; they were especially nice to my daughter, which I appreciated immensely. They also warned me about the construction (even offering me a room on the opposite side of the hotel). I was pleased with that; I'd much prefer honesty than unpleasant surprises. The room was small, but very attractive and clean - very classic modern. It's located in a very convenient area, in a good neighborhood - which is always a plus...especially when traveling with a kid.
The only caveat: there were many, many young people (i.e. twentysomethings) - which I didn't mind, especially since they were well-behaved and low-key - but I guess some might. Again, the atmosphere was unpretentious, informal and not the slightest bit stuffy - which suited us just fine, and which was a very pleasant surprise. We will definitely stay here the next time we visit Manhattan!

title: “Racial profiling is not a good way to run a business”
text: I am NEVER the one to place the race card ever. I am Mixed black 25% white 50% native 25% American, I grew up with a large loving white side and black side color was never a issue. I have stayed at the Hilton garden before, my experience there was great! No issues no complaints. I stayed there a second time this past weekend with my boyfriend and his friend and his girl friend. I knew from the jump how people can be so I was going to have them come to the back when they arrived, sad that I wouldn’t even have to think this way. When I checked in I had my college sweat shirt on nice pair of jeans and shoes. His friend had a wife beater on with tattoos he is white his girlfriend black, they didn’t have a bag to place there clothes in so they used a trash bag. I knew the look of them in general they would be judged sad people are this way they are two people with amazing hearts and come from great families so they don’t have all the money in the world does this really matter? It was a weekend to get away and have a good time and I wanted to make sure to show them one. When they arrived they ended up going through the front I already had a very bad feeling about it like I stated they came up to the room and my boyfriend and I had been snacking but his friends girlfriend was pregnant and the smell was really making her sick! I lit a incent and burned it halfway just to mask the smell. We weren't smoking in the hotel so I really honestly didn’t see the problem. We only had one smoker in the group that did go outside when he needed. We left to go grab dinner and catch a movie at 7, when we came back to the room we had messages on our phone and their phone the rooms were right next to each other. The messages stated that "they received several complaints of a burnings smell coming from our rooms and to please not do that if we had any questions to contact the front desk". This just made my stomach hurt first off my room wasn’t near another rooms just who we were with and we burned Half not even a whole incent and on top of it my boyfriend and I burned incents and candles before when we stayed again with ZERO ISSUE! It’s a comfort for me something I do at home. I knew right away how this weekend would go. I didn’t bother to get back to the front desk I just stayed away from the hotel as much as possible at night we were quiet and low key again she is pregnant so we laid around and just talk and went to bed both nights at 10pm! Sunday when it was time to check out woke up at 7am made the bed placed all towels under the sink in the bathroom aired out both rooms and sprayed glade just to make it fresh made sure all trash was in the trash everything was perfectly clean and fine. I knew I just knew I was going to be charged sure enough Monday comes around I was charged 50$ for each room!!! For what reason! I am a 26 year old grown women who is working on her bachelors in social work I know more then anyone what's going on here. Ive already made the decision to never stay here again. I am a responsible respectful person with a huge heart and it hurts to know people are still this way, no worries Hilton and Garden you wont have to "deal" with us ever again!

title: “Great place to stay”
text: I've stayed in Hotel Contessa twice and had a wonderful stay both times. The location is great, rooms are HUGE with a separate living room and huge bath, and staff very friendly. Bed was very comfortable. I ate at the bar with half price tapas during happy hour. The bartender was very friendly and the caramelized brussel sprouts with pancetta delicious!

title: “Great Location!”
text: We stayed here for a girls weekend for the 4th of July holiday. The Homewood Suites is wonderful! Loved the FREE breakfast buffet; a different daily selection of hot breakfast items including potatoes, sausage, pancakes, french toast, eggs, etc. and several cold items like yogurt, fresh and cut fruit, juices, etc. Staff was friendly and helpful. FREE trolley to the Navy Pier right outside of hotel. Room was clean, ran out of towels and needed mouthwash; someone came right away with the items. Valet parking and bellhop staff wonderful, very kind! Hotel is in great location within walking distance of many restaurants, magnificient mile, grocery stores, etc. Would stay here again!

title: “Housekeeping? Pilfering....”
text: I stayed at the Doubletree the night of Oct. 2, checking out at 8 AM on Wednesday, Oct. 3. At 11:30 AM I realized I'd left my computer charger and phone charger in the room (#427). I called and informed them I'd return to pick them up within 30 minutes. Once I got there I was informed that housekeeping had not found the items - "the man who stripped the room said nothing was found." OK....I don't have them and I remember leaving them plugged in, at the desk. I hope whoever is collecting and selling things left in rooms makes some money from my loss.

title: “Historical Building with Incredible Renovations”
text: I have been staying at Kimpton hotels for at least 15 years. The Monaco can not be beaten for value, space, and service. The building was in serious disrepair when Kimpton bought it and renovated it so very carefully. The lobby is spacious and hip. The desk staff is marvelous. The rooms are spectacular, with very high ceilings, marble, and tasteful furnishings. The location is central to the Inner Harbor, the Oriole's stadium, and most of what you want to do by foot in downtown Baltimore.

title: “Loved the Pool and Food”
text: I stayed here instead of any of the lower star hotels in the area because with my little one I knew we would be using the pool and I just couldn't stand the thought of being at hotel with a pool that was stark and motely. The Pool here delivered with good ambience and it was fun for kids. Good gift shop and nice employees everywhere. Really good high end bar food next to the pool and kids can sit on the patio there. Got a 2-bed queen room even with priceline. At the end of check in they casually said they would set me up with parking and I said I didn't need it and that was that. Didn't see any valet so I assumed that was what they meant and no signs or tow away warnings for the self parking around the bldgs. Saw reviews later that said they had a weird policy that the public doesn't pay to park but overnight guests pay over $30 per night. Still don't quite understand, but I didn't pay for parking and I was not towed. Yes, this property is getting a little long in the tooth and needs updating, plus the tower, where most of the rooms are located, is a little disconnected from the hotel, but it served our purpose completely. And it was not busy while we were there, it not being not a wknd night, but I can imagine the noise level if it had been because of what we could hear thru the walls. Oh, a plus is a small empty fridge in the closet and I was able to make the AC as cold as I wanted and it worked great. We stayed on the front side of the tower and were told we would not be on the fwy side so it wouldn't be too noisy. A major fwy runs right next to this hotel and the sound and view of it on that side of the tower must suck. And that side of the tower had huge square floodlights aimed directly at the side of the bldg and into all the windows all night. I don't think anything could have blocked it out. I was so glad we were not on that side of the bldg or this might have been a different review.

title: “Meh”
text: I was underwhelmed by my experience here. The room was so, so small and was not well-maintained -- the walls were basically bare and had several damaged areas. Not what I expected for "boutique" On the bright side, the bed was amazing -- by far the highlight of my stay. For other people that booked this for under $100, its a decent value but I paid about twice that and was disappointed. I didn't use any of the amenities or service, so I can't speak to that.

title: “great service, great location”
text: We stayed at this hotel the first week in April. The staff was courteous and always willing to help us. Service was always with a smile. The Grandview restaurant was excellent with attentive service from Richard our waiter. Great location, close to shopping. Would stay at again.

title: “Good hotel near the riverwalk”
text: Stayed here during Presidents Day weekend and it was a great stay. The rooms are clean, the wifi works great and the riverwalk is about two blocks away or so. I did find the walls a little thin and we could hear people talking/laughing and a baby crying one of the nights. Overall a great place to stay at a great price.

title: “Great Staff- Hospitable Mgmt.- "A GREAT stop. . ." stayed 5/31/2011”
text:
Between Mr. Ragonese and Alexis at the front desk, we couldn't go wrong! Both went out of their way to make our stay great, even if it was for only one night. We wanted to see some baseball and took the hotel shuttle there and walked back, without any problems. Were there a lot of people out? Sure were! An occasional siren? You better believe it! This is our Nation's Capital, not Smalltown, USA. Never saw a street person or hobo there, though. 
I didn't need a shower cap, I pack my own and if they didn't have one, I sure wouldn't trash their rating for that! We had a great time at this hotel and would go back there in a heartbeat! Thank you Mr. Ragonese and Alexis! Definitely a class act!

title: “Excellent Service!”
text: Perfectly located business hotel in the heart of downtown. Rooms where very good for the price, clean and usable. Hotel staff was very efficient and helpful. Mike H. Went above and beyond when I left my iPad in the room upon checkout. I made one call and the iPad was being shipped back to me. If you are on business trip in Boston, Nine Zero is the best value and service is great. Thanks again Mike H.

title: “Tight with their muffins!”
text: Just stayed at the Bijou which was very pleasant. Good internet access, tidy rooms clean and simple. Main issue with the Bijou was the breakfast - the 'continental breakfast' was basically just toast. Apparently there were also different muffins available but every time we got there there were only blueberry left. The reception staff were helpful, and knew a lot about the area so could offer advice and tips. There were quite a few homeless people about, particularly at night, but this is by no means that bad an area to stay in. If I were returning to San Francisco I would stay here again.

title: “Great place to stay for comfort,service,and unbeatable price”
text: Excellent location for walking to shops and food places in old town and trolley. The management is exceptional for service. Have been coming here for years whenever we come to San Diego. Rooms have always been very clean and comfortable and their rates have always been great. I recommend to make reservations ahead of major events or festivals so you won't be disappointed because at Padre Inn I am sure they fill up before any other place due to their rates and outstanding place to stay.

title: “Great little hotel!”
text: We have been staying at the BW Lamplighter Inn for nearly 10 years, when we visit our kids and grandkids. The staff is attentive and helpful and the owners really keep up with the maintenance. The landscaping is lovely - lots of flowers and much nicer than you would expect for the price. The beds are comfortable and they have nice linens and even comfy feather pillows. The pool is spotless and usually heated and they are dog-friendly too. The only thing lacking for me is a jacuzzi! We are always treated like family and we just love staying at his great little hotel!

title: “Great Service, Great Location, Great Price”
text: The staff were very friendly when checking in. The decor was fresh and atmospheric. The room was large and comfortable. The location is fantastic with restaurants, shops, diners very close. If I picked fault then I would say that the sanitary fittings were a bit worn and the air con unit (which we needed) was noisy. But all in all it was great value and I would not hesitate to recommend the Rex.

title: “A Little Gem!”
text: Hotel Teatro might just be the best boutique hotel in America. Understated luxury, impeccable service, convenient downtown location, free WIFI in-room and totally reasonable pricing...what more can a traveler expect? The beds are heavenly and the bathrooms are like mini-spas. Staff are friendly, courteous and responsive. Can't wait to stay here again. PERFECT!

title: “Fees Fees Fees!!”
text:
Ok, so just as an FYI... the charge you so many fees... that might as well charge you for breathing. 
Please note, I was NOT aware of this before... they charge you $50 a night if you use a debit card to pay for your time in the hotel... please be advise... because if you didn't budget for this... it can really mess you up. Its basically a incidental charge...

title: “a great get a way”
text: early check in and parking rocks when you stay at the mosser in "THE CITY"the employees are nice and very helpful.The rooms are clean and the location is great weather your going to a ballgame or dinner.keep up the good work...patric

title: “Don't stay at Hilton's in Chicago”
text: Second stay at a Chicago Hilton this summer. Both rooms were dark with cost saver yellow lighting; looked out at other rooms, not at the street or sky; were huge but only partially furnished; and were ice cold - even with air cond off. Lobby's nice, room's not up to par with pleasant rooms at other hotels.These rooms will make you want to go home for sure.

title: “Good but not great”
text:
I have to say I was expecting more based on the star rating and other reviews. While I couldn't fault the staff in any way, it just wasn't as good as I'd expected. It may be that it's best suited to younger people (I'm 42). Our initial room had a pool view but that was accompanied by intrusive music through the day and then louder into the night. The rooms didn't seem to be well sound-proofed as we could hear entire conversations from the bloke in the next room (that I'd really rather not have heard!). The swimming pool is more of a strip of water - designed for lounging around not swimming.
Whenever we've been to San Diego before, every hotel has had a bedroom and a sitting/TV area. Solamar was just a fairly small, standard room. Although modern it was quite dull. The shower in the bathroom was rubbish and the decoration was very tired.
We moved room after a couple of nights, because of the noise from the pool/bar area. The top floor was much quieter, but the bathroom was still poor.
Also, you don't get any kind of tea/coffee making facilities in the room. It was only when I asked that one was brought to the room.
The plus side is the fabulous restaurant, where the food and staff were excellent. Local produce, cooked in inventive, delicious ways and a good range of cocktails too!
Other plus is that it's right near Petco Park which means very easy to get to the baseball games - which I loved so much we went three times.
I've previously stayed in Best Western (Pacific Beach) and Embassy Suites (near Seaport) and both, although dated from a decor viewpoint, were far better hotels in terms of space, ambience and relaxation.
If you are going to SD to party, have fun, sun bathe by the bar and drink then you will probably really like this hotel and it is in Gas Lamp, which is a vibrant area. Just down to what you are after I guess, and this didn't suit us.

title: “Good meeting place, but pricey”
text: I stayed here for meeting purposes. Rooms are very nice. The group rate we received was acceptable. But the cost for an adult beverage was crazy. Over $11 for a simple mixed drink at the bar was too much. Some of the staff seemed friendly, but overall wasn't impressed. They need to be more friendly.

title: “It is a great place”
text: The people at this hotel are wonderful. The rooms are a tad small but the beds are very comfortable, equivalent to the 4 seasons and the bathrooms have deep tubs. The staff is friendly and helpful and the rates great. True it is not the 4 seasons but the price isn't either. I love staying at this hotel because the people are nice, room adequately and really lovingly appointed including a rubber duck in the bath tub. There is parking availability. If you plan to spend all your time in your room and need/want a view and lots of space, maybe this isn't what you want but I have stayed at this hotel for several years - maybe now many years and I am not disappointed. It reminds me of a wonderful hotel I stayed in Lutz, Sweden. Great bed, bathroom, terrific feeling of attention to detail. Comfy. I have spent a lot of the day in the room working and the free internet is easy on the soul. The hotel has a relationship with Club One just around the corner wtih a pool and great workout facility. I will be staying for my birthday next month.

title: “Exceeded expectations”
text: The host hotel for my conference couldn't accommodate us for the duration of our stay so we were happy to find this hotel close by. Not only do the suites make life easier (separate bedrooom so if one of us wants to go to bed early or get up early, there's additional space to hang out), there's an extra sink outside of the bathroom, there's two TVs and lots of outlets for electronics. Best parts though were the included hot breakfast buffet (made to order omelettes, waffles, etc), but the "manager's" evening reception which was any well drink, draft beer or specialty drink they could concoct -- especially friendly staff, snacks that were different each night (veggies and rip, chips, pretzels, nachos w/jalapenos and cheese) and the opportunity to feed the koi (if so inclined). OK, yes, it's a chain and had that kind of Holiday Inn feel with the big atrium and waterfalls and generic room furniture, but the rooms were clean, fairly modern, quiet and again, the staff were especially friendly and unobtrusive. For the money and great location (close to Dupont Circle), I wouldn't trade it for something more typical DC.

title: “Marriott Gaslamp Quarter”
text: This is an Excellent Hotel. Modern, very clean, well furnished, Staff was outstanding. It is located In the middle of the Gaslamp District convenient to the trolley, 2 blocks to the waterfront boardwalk and the Convention Center. Breakfast at the restaurant was excellent.

title: “Great location, room & breakfast”
text: 16th floor room was quite. The hot breakfast was a treat compared to the average American hotel breakfast.

title: “LAURA at Drafts”
text: Laura was great! The place was packed and she made us feel very welcomed. Great customer service. She stopped out of her section to see if she could help! Off the charts. She made Dallas a great get away amd easy.

title: “Good hotel with the usual pluses and minuses.”
text: Well appointed, if small, room. Pricy internet [12.95/day for good speed; 16.95 for very hi speed] - but very stable and fast. Free wifi in the lobby, however. Very comfortable bed. Walk in shower was very nice - but dish for soap and little shampoos is inconvenient. A/c in room was amazingly efficient for the >100 degree days in DC on this trip - although halls and lobby were not quite as well chilled. Food in bar/restaurant was interesting and tasty - with good service. But the pepper bacon was (for me) inedibly spicy. Room service breakfast served on-time at the right temperatures.Attended a small conference there, and the meeting room was fine, although the chairs uncomfortable. The business center was well equipped- but they charged $1 per sheet to print stuff and too much to use their computer (I passed). Location was OK - but not so close to Dupont Circle.

title: “Tip on how to avoid going broke eating when staying at Hyatt”
text: Hotel is great. Everything you expect from Hyatt. Very safe/secure elevators, etc. Location is ideal for River Tours and Navy Pier. When I made my reservation they give you options to upgrade for fees, several things. For instance: Higher Floor. Special upgraded bed and bath. Etc. I chose non and was on a high floor with an upgraded bed and bath. Save yourself the money and chance it if you are a gambler. Ordered 2 glasses of apple juice from room service (for a diabetic who needed sugar) and it cost $16.75 plus the $2 we handed the delivery guy. Holy Cow. So, directly next to the Hyatt on Wacker is Houlihan's. WONDERFUL brunch buffet with everything you can think of for $12. EAT THERE!

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location *** dont believe the negativity***”
text:
We stayed at the building on Beach Street! Which has the Dennys in it. The check in was in the other building and was quick and the staff very friendly. After a 12 hour flight and once checked in we decided to eat at Dennys, the food and service was lovely. Got to our room and again lovely clean spacious room (this was our 2nd stay here the 1st was Nov 2002). This hotel is ideal for everything in Fishermans Wharf as you can walk to everything, you can also walk to the cable car turn and the 'beach' of San Francisco!! The sea lions, pier 39, trip to alcatraz, shops etc etc all walking distance. Perhaps not recommend walking the 'Hills' of San Francisco get the close cable car alot easier!! :) ! 
Would recommend this hotel to anyone and will stay here again on next visit!!!!
Great Hotel!

title: “Good Hotel”
text: If you are looking for a hotel just to keep your things, sleep, shower, and be in a safe location this is the hotel for you. Not much on amenities. It's in a great location 3 blocks from Central Park. Close to the Broadway and 86th subway. Perfect for a traveler. The rooms are tiny but clean. The hotel is on a quiet street. I did not hear other guests too much.

title: “continental charm & location, location,location”
text: Looking for a quiet, service-oriented place to hang your hat in LA The Wilshire Crest is your best bet. Clean, comfortable rooms with all the amenities. 24 hour front desk help. Pleasant breakfast room and large lobby to meet friends or just lounge. The Los Angeles County Museum of Art is three blocks away and the Grove and Farmers Market six blocks away. Deli's, coffee shops, and bus lines at hand. An excellent value.

title: “It was just fine”
text:
This place is really nice, and really close (walking distance) to Jones Symphony Hall, which is why we picked it. The lobby and rooms are beautiful. The pool is rooftop (albeit tiny) but has a great view of the city. The hot-tub didn't work.
The downside is the service. Upon arrival, they told me the rollaway was in my suite. It was not, and when I called, they said they would "try" to find one but couldn't guarantee it, even though I had requested it 2 weeks prior. (They found it). Their included breakfast didn't compare to the Embassy Suites. There was cereal, yogurt, donuts and pancakes. Things like eggs could be ordered for an additional charge, but there were few people to order them from, and NOBODY stopped at our table to offer us an opportunity to order. When we returned to our room it was freezing, so I called and asked for extra blankets for the rollaway. The maid arrived with more sheets.
Extras: They had a happy hour, which we didn't attend. They had a cookies and milk hour (cookies were store-bought). They had the "included" breakfast, which was mediocre.

title: “Fabulous stay!”
text: Very nice hotel. The room was clean. Air conditioning was not quite as cool as we would have liked, but not enough to complain about. The staff was extremely helpful and pleasant. The valet/driver from Spain (didn't get his name) was very friendly and personable. The evening happy hour was great, cookies and milk in the evening, and great breakfast in the morning. Very close to all downtown venues. Free shuttle service to downtown. Parking was a bit expensive $25.00 plus taxes, but at least they brought the car back with no door dings. Would definitely stay at the Magnolia Hotel again. We had a room on the 19th floor and our view was great!

title: “Perfect Location”
text: My wife and I both work long hour demanding jobs, so it is hard for us to get away sometimes for a long period of time. So for a few months we had talked about doing a trip to Washington DC for a day. We live in NJ, so from us to DC is not that bad of a ride. So I had said, why don't we go for a long weekend for our one year anniversary. She agreed and off we went. The hotel was very easy to get to, the staff was very friendly and knowledgeable. After a long day of sight seeing, we wanted to just go to a good Pub, and the bellman had directed us too one only a few blocks away. The area that the hotel is in is very clean and safe. It is within walking distance to all the major sightseeing attractions DC has to offer. The only drawback and it is not a slight against the hotel is that it cost 27 dollars a day to park my car. Now if you want to try to find a garage to save a few bucks than more power to you. The sad thing is though, with the cost of gas, tolls, and parking, it would have been cheaper to take a train from NJ to DC and take cabs everywhere, so if that is something you could do I would suggest it. Overall the hotel was spot on, the room was fantastic, the bed was like sleeping on air it was so comfortable, and the service was excellent. I would highly recommend.

title: “tourist class hotel”
text: a 3* hotel with excellent midtown location & italian flair. small and slow lifts take you to small, but well appointed rooms. Small meaning a guest is only able to fully-stretch-open a standard size Samsonite suit case on a bed. Bathrooms well maintained, with standard "NH" branded (orange-yellowish) soap amenities. Window kept slding down, allowing fresh/cold air into the room during night. If not in a package, a modest buffet breakfast costs 22 USD + tax + tip. Not worth the coast, IMO. They do serve a real cappucino/espresso/latte in a real china, though. Front desk staff and bell boy very helpfull. Barman in a hotel bar very nice and hospitable.Breakfast crew moods depends on a day. U might get lucky and run into a charming italian waiter. hotel offers a very good price/location ratio.

title: “Perfect Vacation”
text: We just returned from a week at the Resort, we loved everything about it. The location is wonderful, close to everything. The staff at the resort are first class all the way, friendly, helpful and fun. The Villa we had (3003) could not have been better. Could not say one bad thing about the Resort. We can not wait to go back and we have told everyone we know how great our trip was especially Canyon Villas.

title: “What you'd expect”
text:
I only stayed at the InterContinental in Boston for one night but you gte whjat you expoect from this great hotel chain.
No complaints about anyhting,. The staff were helpful, the room and bathroom were spacious and clean. The only small thing I've noticed is that they have stopped supplying slippers, but would definitley stay here again!

title: “An Excellent Stay at Hotel Elysee”
text:
My husband and I spent a week at the wonderful Hotel Elysee. It was my first visit to NYC, so it was great to be within walking distance of 5th Avenue, Central Park, MOMA, Rockefeller Center, and Broadway. Our room was spacious and comfortable and, thanks to the friendly housekeeping staff, it was kept spotless throughout our entire stay. Before and after my long walks around the City, the Bellmen would always greet me with a smile and pleasant conversation – they were also extremely helpful with directions. 
I surprised myself by spending quite a bit of time in the 2nd floor lounge area. The space is large with many comfortable chairs and couches. The complimentary breakfasts had a great selection of breads and pastries and the attendants were so pleasant and always willing to help/clear away plates. In the afternoons, I’d go back to the lounge for the cheeses, cookies, and other snacks. 
The Front Desk staff made a number of great dinner (and lunch) suggestions – any suggestion was always followed by the offer to make a reservation for us. I appreciated the free wifi – even though the hotel provides a computer with access to the internet for guests, it was nice to be able to sit in the lounge with my laptop in the afternoons to catch up on my email. 
I’ve stayed in many hotels around the world and this was definitely one of the best experiences I’ve had – across the board. Sometimes, a hotel will be in a great location, but so poorly-run that it just ruins the experience. That’s definitely not the case with Hotel Elysee. This hotel’s in a great spot and it’s a tightly-run ship, with fantastic staff at every level. We will definitely return!

title: “All great, except bed and water pressure...”
text:
