Very pretty little motel, and $150 for a room with a full kitchen isn't a bad deal in SF. However, the two most important things for us are a good mattress and decent water pressure. Mattress seemed both very firm, and lumpy--neither of us slept well all night. (We do a lot of hotel travel, and have rarely slept so poorly due to the mattress being uncomfortable.) And the shower pressure was extremely weak--hand-held shower, with not enough pressure to actually spray, just sort of dribbled.
Apart from these issues, it's a great-looking place, with nice folks at the front desk, and we had no problems with street noise (our room was at the back of the property, so ask for that if street noise is an issue for you). We'd have liked to return, but that bed was a deal-killer.

title: “Great hotel with super location and professional staff!”
text: My partner and I stayed here for three nights in April at the recommendation of a good friend who knows the city. We had a fabulous time in Chicago and a fabulous stay at The Sutton Place. Yummie champagne, cheese plate and chocolate covered strawberries as soon as we entered the room (pre-arranged by friends). Bed was so comfortable we were checking the mattress tag to shop beds when we got home. Super views (from room 1808). Absolutely no noise. Perfect location. Great selection of restaurants all around and a reasonable walk to tons of shopping along Magnificent Mile (if that's your thing). Also, access to the Red Line train is a five-minute walk from the hotel. We took it to Boystown as well as a nearby stop for Crate and Barrell and CB2.

title: “The best night sleep since a long time”
text:
I had the best night sleep since a long time.
The room was spaces and very nice with a nice big bathroom.
Our room was on the 9th floor, overlooking the city, the view was amazing.
Very good value for the price.

title: “Nice, quiet, convenient!”
text:
Had to be in NY last week, and went to Kayak to find something . . . The Hotel Chandler popped up. It was two blocks from where I needed to be, so I took it. Nice place, friendly staff . . . quiet.
On the plus side - 
Quiet
Nice room, decent bathroom - Killer rain showerhead
Convenient to Fifth avenue and the Fashion Accessory district
Friendly staff
On the negative side - 
AC sounded like an aircraft taking off when it came on
No real rstaurant/lounge - bartender barely spoke English - This is America, right?
I'd stay here again, walking ditstance to most of my customers.
If you can get a decent price, its a steal.

title: “Very Nice Hotel. Great Service!”
text: I ususally don't write reviews but I felt like this hotel was getting somewhat of a bad wrap. I stayed at at the Parc 55 for a family/business trip last week. I was a little scared when I bid through Priceline and got it, because I had read some not-so-flattering reviews here. But I was pleasantly surprised that, as soon as I walked through the door, a bellman was there to take my bags. They even changed my room when at first they stuck me on the fifth floor with a terrible view of the air conditioning. The views on the 21st floor were wonderful, and the location was great. Everyone was so attentive!

title: “Why Go Elsewhere”
text: Unless you must be close to Boston Commons and downtown businesses, this is a great place. It's a high rise with 400 rooms, just a block from the waterfront and the No Name Seafood Restaurant. It opened early in 2008, is sleek and modern, has a great staff, and the rooms are large and well appointed with an excellent television system. There is a subway stop two blocks away that connects you to wherever you need to go, but the hotel is not within walking distance of very many attractions and is not in a historic neighborhood. The pool and whirlpool aren't very big. The rate was barely $200 a night, a bargain for this high quality a hotel.

title: “Worst Experience, Dark and Gloomy”
text:
I had made travel arrangements thur American Express Travel for Business purpose for my company. I was recommended by the agent at American Express and we had a discounted rates for our company in Manhattan (New York). I had even looked it up and had a rating of 3 stars. With that in mine I had canceled my earlier reservation with City Club Hotel. 
The place I stayed was at: 
Club Quarters on 40th West 45th street, New York NY 10036. 
A couple of good points were free Internet, and the location was good. 
Here is the number of problems I had. 
1. The people at the front counter was not as friendly as I am used to when going to other hotels. 
2. The room size was good but I had early when making my reservation asked for a double bed. I ended up getting a single bed. I went to the front counter and ask for a double bed they told me they don't have double bed but they will send up a "cot". 
3. The room was dark and kind of gloomy. The view was to a roof top with Heating and AC units that was running all day. I know because I heard it. 
4. The bedding on the first day was kind of dirty. And, one of the pillows had blood stains on it. 
I happen to notice on the bed is that they don't change the bedding only if its requested due to a water conservation issue they have. 
5. The toilet seat never stayed up. I had to litteraly had to hold the toilet seat up each time I went to the bathroom. 
6. My reservation was from the 5th thur the 13th. I ended not being able to stay there I found another hotel. Club Quarters charged me an additional $30.00 plus tax for early cancellation since my reservation was for up until the 13th of Febuary. 
7. I was even bum that it didn't include a complimentary breakfast.
Just good luck if you plan on staying at this hotel.
Stan

title: “Great location”
text: The room was located in a quiet part of the hotel which is near everything we wanted to do in Hollywood, Magic Castle etc.

title: “Return to the Roosevelt”
text: The combination of location, consistent good service, and comfortable rooms make this hotel a good choice!! We've stayed there several times and the location makes car rental unnecessary. The people are nice.

title: “If you are a partier stay here, otherwise stay away!”
text: Do not stay in a street side room unless you are staying out till 3am, otherwise plan not to sleep. Local bars are right outside your window and soundproofing is nonexistent. Staff is medicore at best, not sure they understand what the word hospitality means. Location is the only plus , yet with so many other choices in Boston it would not gain my return. All things considered , this hotel goes into my "do not return" book!

title: “Excellent service with a smile”
text: This hotel was great for a number of reasons. One of the first things we noticed was the friendliness of the staff. Everyone was so helpful. Because we arrived early in the morning our room was not ready, however, they called us on our cell phone as soon as it was available. They were very helpful with restaurant suggestions. Great staff! Perfect location-right by Central Park; subway across the street; Starbucks and Dunkin Donuts just around the corner; 24 hour pharmacy at the corner; great breakfast spot just up the street. Shower was great and room was small, but clean. We didn't spend a lot of time there anyway so it didn't matter. Only complaint was that they didn't offer shower caps in the bathroom. Price was very reasonable compared to other N.Y. hotels.

title: “Cool hotel in a great location - can be noisy on an evening.”
text:
Spent 3 nights here with the girlfriend, the start of a 3 week West Cost USA tour. 
We picked this hotel for its location – right on Hollywood Blvd opposite Grauman’s Chinese Theatre, and its reputation as being quite a “cool” place to stay.
Finding the proper entrance is difficult as it’s not signposted. We entered through a side door (even though it was on the main road). Very dark inside, but that’s the look they go for.
Check in was fine, very helpful and friendly lady at the front desk. Our room was a corner room on a high floor. Tastefully decorated, retro print of the Rolling Stones/Bowie on the wall behind the bed, comfy bed, nice clean bathroom. The room itself was not huge, but we had only booked the basic room I think. Still, it was adequate for our needs.
Very impressive mini-bar (although not cheap) with all sorts of things including a “seduction kit” (use your imagination…).
The pool looked nice however seemed more of a nightclub through the day – i.e. packed with the 20 something LA “it” crowd drinking and dancing to loud music, meaning there was no chance of a nice relaxed afternoon by the pool. However they were all friendly and accommodating when you encounter them in the lift.
Got quite noisy a couple of nights with partying (well, more of a small gathering of people talking and having a few drinks with a bit of background music, nevertheless kept us awake) in the room next to us until 3am on a Monday night – although unlike British partying it seemed relatively chilled out and sensible, and they kept quiet once warned by security.
The area around the hotel is packed with tourists looking at the walk of fame and the hand prints outside the Chinese theatre. Lots of people trying to sell you stuff, give you “free” tickets to shows, beggars, people asking for charity donations etc. Can get annoying but that’s LA and it is a tourist area.
The hop on hop off bus tours start just over the road which is very handy. Plenty of places to eat and drink nearby (check out Mel’s Drive In round the corner), and generally a great place to experience LA at its finest.

title: “Eldon--a Diamond in the rough!”
text:
Stayed at the Eldon for one night on business. As most reviewers have noted, the Eldon is near the convention center and in an area "in transition." Take heed--the boarded-up properties are actually owned by various hotel chains--not dilapidated public safety risks! The Eldon (a former condo bldg) just set up shop there first. In the day you're fine--but definitely should look into getting a cab to the hotel in the evening.
Now on to the actual stay...
The first thing I noticed was how nice the staff was to me. Friendly and speedy check-in. I had a freedom queen room on the 5th floor. The room was amazing--definitely reminiscent of a high class condo. Spacious and modern--with an open kitchen layout and comfy sofa and flat screen in the living room. The bed was extremely comfortable. The room had a walk -in closet with plenty of space. The shower was fantastic from the creative shower head design to the water pressure! High-end toiletries were a plus. The workout room on the ninth floor was really clean but small--only a few cardio machines but no free weights or water cooler. The free breakfast was okay--just cereals, pastries, juices, and a coffee maker with various options. 
All in all a good stay. If you're going to a convention center conference or find a good deal at this hotel--it's definitely worth it.

title: “Enjoyed this Hotel”
text: Great location, OK service, room was on the Executive floor and quite good. Really can't complain about price as Boston is pretty pricey. I'd stay here again.

title: “Going downhill”
text:
Having stayed at this hotel when I come to NYC, I have to say that it has gone downhill FAST. Ok, I travel all the time for work and I’m not picking up the tab when I'm working
Having stayed here previously and loved the place, and having stayed at one of their sister hotels (in the kimpton range) in Boston called nine zero (which I loved) I have to say I’m unhappy.
List
- The room service guy kept coming back to pick up my tray/collect tip when I told him not too
- well thumbed, worn menus, travel guides etc
- Ridiculously over priced (even at corporate rates)
- $17 for a glass of wine delivered to room (they didn't get it when I asked them for a glass not a bottle but I’ll put that down to my poor humor)
- Elevator comes in and out of service
- Over $10 per night for internet
- ESPN out for entire stay (I missed Monday night football!!) - Excuse - 'it's out for the whole hotel'
- tiny bathroom (funny, I didn't notice this last time round maybe b/c all the above weren't issues)
- Minimal towels AND they aren't particularly soft
I could go on .....
Find somewhere else and use the $$$ you saved on dinner in Bryant park or somewhere else fun.

title: “Pleasant Surprise at the Denver Quality Inn”
text: I had a wonderful time while in Denver staying at the Quality Inn. It is not in the center of the downtown area, nor is it out near the airport. However, they make up for this with their shuttle service, which will take you to a lot of different destinations within about a 5 mile radius. This included the 16th St Mall, the Colorado Convention Center, stadiums, etc. They leave on the hour, and you just have to call and they will pick you up on the next run. Staff is super friendly, including the shuttle drivers, and a few that I remember fro the front desk are Patricia, Yvonne, Teresa, and a couple others that I did not get their name. Great breakfast and Betty visits your table to see if everything is OK. I would stay here again with no hesitation. Their prices are great!!

title: “Lush and opulent - great!”
text:
I loved loved LOVED this hotel!!! As you walk in the lobby, you are greeted by a magnificently lush lobby which simply takes your breath away.
The staff are extremely polite, genuine and friendly. The staff at the spa and gym went round the whole hotel trying to find someone who had 'taken' my shoes. 
One problem with the spa is the fact that men stay with men and women stay with women!!! So if you go with your partner, dont expect to be able to have a sauna/massage/chill with them - rooms are strictly separate! The gym is also good and well equipped.
I reccomend the barman Jose's cocktail making abilities, he is great!
The rooms were grand, nice sizes with a comfortable bed and great decor. The bathroom was perfect and everything was very clean and tidy.
services were brilliant - I am very impressed with this hotel and everything it has to offer, I would recommend it if you are going on a holiday in whcih you want to splash out a bit. The extra prices are definitely worth it though!!!

title: “Disappointed”
text: I generally like Hyatt hotels a lot, and there is a lot to like about this one. We had a great room, recently redone and with a comfy bed. It has all the amenities you could expect for a city hotel. My only problem was with the noise level. True to many prior complaints on this board, I can vouch for the fact that you can hear every single thing that goes on outisde your door and in the rooms next door. I am not a sensitive traveler but the noise level was incredible. Basically, I got no sleep for the 3 nights I was at this hotel. People rolled in at all hours of the night and we could hear the tv turned on next door, not to mention the ice machine which sounded like a jet engine for a good portion of the day. If you are in Chicago to party and sleep is not an issue, by all means you can't do much better for price, comfort and style at such a good location. But if you are on business or like to retire early, this is the WRONG hotel. The only other negative is that you need a cab to go practically anywhere in the city you really want to be, so that expense can add up.

title: “Excellent first time visit to Dallas”
text: This goes back a few years to my first visit to Dallas. We chose this location because I'm a Hilton employee and got a fantastic rate, but the real value was the quality of the hotel, cleanliness and service. Our housekeeper was friendly and remembered our names over our 3 night stay. Food in the restaurant was good. It was further from the stadium and downtown than we expected so spent more on cabs than we anticipated. Cowboys lost that weekend but the way we were treated is what we remember.

title: “Great place for a budget travel.”
text:
We stayed at this hotel last August. I would recommend this place to everyone who looks for a good budget hotel. It’s only couple of blocks away from that part of a Hollywood blvd. where everyone wants to go: Hollywood walk of fame, Grauman’s Chinese Theatre, Kodak theatre. Don’t get me wrong, I am not talking about luxurious hotel and it doesn’t pretend to be the one, like some others, but it’s worth every dollar spent. It has everything you need for a budget travel. You can also book sightseeing tours right from the front desk. Some of the tour operators will pick you up right from the hotel, but for some tours you will have to go to the Chinese theatre. There is one tour operator who has several routes around L.A area and one complimentary route for their clients to the Universal studios. It’s called Starline tours. You pay for one ticket and it will include three different routes and one complimentary route. They don’t have tour guides, everything is on tape, but it gives you a lot of information in real time.
If you would like to pick this tour operator, you can always pick up their brochure at the front desk. You can also book their tours at the front desk, but for this particular operator I would recommend to buy tickets at the box office buy the Chinese theatre. First of all they don’t pick you up at you hotel, because you still have to go to the Hollywood blvd. to get your bus and second, you can get some better deal at their box office, and buses are right there on the Hollywood blvd.
Overall, we enjoyed our stay at this Days Inn.

title: “Cozy, wonderful hotel with - WOW - location”
text:
Set just a few minutes walk from Bleeker street, this hotel is perfectly situated for seeing the SoHo and Village. Great shopping and eateries in the area, Chinatown not too far away, and a few subway stops in the area make this a great place to stay. Room was small, but very, very comfortable.
One negative - breakfast was over-rated and over-priced. Get out of the hotel and knosh on a bagel or egg-n-cheese sandwich from the local bodega! There are many, many food options, get out of the hotel!

title: “Fun weekend in San Francisco”
text:
We have spent many weekends in San Francisco and have always loved it, and this past weekend was no exception!! My husband and I traveled with another couple who are really good friends with us and stayed in the city for some nice Christmas shopping, a couple of fun shows and just a weekend away! We have stayed at a few different hotels in Union Square and because of the price and Tripadvisor rating, we decided to try the Hotel Rex! We were definitly NOT dissapointed and neither were our friends! it was such a cute, inviting hotel right in the middle of wonderful shopping. We walked everywhere! We took the Bart one night to Oakland to watch So You Think You Can DAnce On Tour and the second night took a $6.00 taxi cab ride to North Beach where we had some wonderful Italian food and watched Beach Blanket Babylon. 
The staff at Hotel Rex was kind enough to give us recommendations on dinner and also nice enough to hold our tons and tons of bags from shopping after we had to check out!!:) We will definitely stay here again and if there was anything to complain about it was just simply the small elevators. When arriving at Hotel Rex, all 4 of us along with our luggage could NOT all fit in there...ha ha...it was kind of a joke every time we had to go into the elevator. "Everybody suck in!" we would all say!

title: “Good location, could be better”
text:
I recently visited the Philadelphia Marriott for a conference. The rooms seems a bit dated but clean. The conference space was great. 
The lobby bar was inviting, but the service was iffy. The restaurant was good. 
I would return because I am a huge fan of Marriott and I enjoy the convenient location.

title: “Pretty good hotel”
text: Pretty amazing place with amazing staff here and nice rooms but the only thing is that whenever i stay with my family at least one person gets sick in my family for the last 4 years weve been coming and staying here either every summer or christmas and someones always gotten sick i do not know why but maybe its something thats in this hotel or something i dont know but heads up to people watch out just in case u get sick!!!!!

title: “Good location, nice hotel”
text:
The hotel is in a nice location, from the airport it is about a 50 dollar cab ride, I was greeted warmly by the front desk, and proceed to my room. 
Many reviews have said the rooms were small, but mine was very large and nice! I guess it depends on where they place you.
When I looked out my window I can see the bay in the distance ( see photo) and then I could see the trolley cars. It was very cool to hear the trolley cars at first. However, the big downside about my room with the view was the street noise from the trolley cars and the traffic. That was a BIG downside of my room. Beyond that my room was VERY nice, clean, modern, large, and comfortable.
I did eat at the restaurant , honestly GO OUT!!! Its not that great, not bad, just not great. I was just too tired to go for a walk.
The location is good, you are literally 5 minutes from China Town and 10 minutes from Union Square. Its a walk down the hill, the downside is the walk UP the hill. The hills are a killer, I took a cab back :)
My only main complaint was the concierge, was not the best. He didn't really have any good research on the city, I would encourage you to research places to eat/sights to do before you come.
The hotel is great, nice location, clean, and I would recommend it,

title: “Enjoyed the stay very much”
text:
We came to Philly to see My Fair Lady, and booked a package rate at the RC for $389 which included bfast for two and a $50 dining credit.
From the moment we drove up to the hotel to the moment we left, service was excellent, and fully met our expectations from an RC. Was the best ever customer service we got? No. But I'd be overly picky if I were to be critical. Everyone was very courteous and friendly.
The room we had was a corner room XX02, so there was lots of light. It was spacious too. The furniture was good quality. Color scheme subdued yet classy. Bathroom was large, with separate shower and bath. Toiletries first rate with Bulgari. Flat screen TV, likely 32 inch. Wired and wireless internet. Two phones, one cordless. Coffeemaker in room, and lots of (we hope) complimentary bottled water. In-room safe. Some furnishing not 100% perfect, as the photos may show, with one a/c vent loose and some wires dangling from the shades in the bathroom. But really, folks, nothing really serious. The room was very nice.
Turndown service came when we were still in the room, but the nice lady offered us chocolates. With a smile.
We had dinner at the Grill. First rate. Menu was simple. But very nicely done. Service was very good.
Breakfast also at the Grill. Can't complain.
Lobby is being renovated right now. But we knew that going in.
All in all, a very good stay.

title: “Clean, well-maintained hotel with friendly atmosphere and staff”
text: I have stayed here a few times with my family. It is a small, out of the way hotel that is comforting to go to after a day in NYC. The staff is very responsive and friendly. The accomodations are clean and comfortable and so are the beds. We actually asked what mattresses they had when ordering a new one. It's a great hotel if you want to feel like you're at home even though you're traveling.

title: “Great place close to airport”
text: Stayed here for one night before flying home. Very impressed with hotel, service and room. Big suite, clean. Staff was very helpful. Only 5 minutes away from airport so great place to stay if you have an early morning flight. Would definitely stay there again. The price was good and the cookies are always great.

title: “Bad Experience”
text: I recently had a very bad experience with this hotel. I was attending a company conference and I had to get a hotel, most hotels in the area were full. After searching through Expedia I found a hotel that looked fairly good and proceeded to book a non smoking room, Expedia required prepayment for this hotel. When I arrived at the hotel, the manager informed me that he only had a recently converted room (smoking to non smoking) and that he had left the AC on and sprayed the room, the room was musty and had a strong odor of smoke. After I expressed my dissatisfaction with the room, he sent me down the street to another hotel that was a even less desirable that Pacific Inn And Suites. I immediately contacted Expedia and demanded a refund, Expedia refused to give me a refund because they honored the hotel managers word over mine and the hotel chain already billed Expedia’s account. I even asked the have the case escalated but Expedia’s management communicated the same message, the hotel manager even boasted that I would not get my money back. Well, I paid Expedia with my Amex Corporate Card who refunded the charge with out asking any questions.

title: “OUR FIRST TIME IN DAYS INN”
text: Everything was great except, I was told {and asked} that there was going to be a microwave and minifridge provided. Since we always bring refreshments and snacks along and we were dissapointed. When we first got there we didn't even notice because we were running a little late so we just dropped everything and left. Finally, when we got back I was looking for the minifridge :( and was going to call front desk but, my husband said just to forget about it. Other than that everything was great!

title: “THE place to stay”
text: just back from my 5th trip to memphis and the heartbreak hotel and again i was not dissapointed,check in was fast and easy our room was ready on arrival and was spotless tidy and comfortable all the staff were helpful and that includes the bar,graceland is a short 5 min max walk across a car park and the hotel lays on a shuttle bus to beale street at night a 5 dollar each way fee applies and must be pre booked at reception in advance,the sun studio shuttle pick up is free at 10 to the hour every day,for a free ride in a pink caddy to marlowes simply pick up the fluffy pink phone in reception and book in advance from 4 in the afternoon.food is available to order from the bar each day from 3 and the service is very quick sadly the bar now shuts at 11 o,clock each night not very good for those from the uk lol.brian and amanda do a good job and are very helpful should you need any information,breakfast is from 06.00 till 10.00 in the bar area,the pool is on the small side but kept very clean and tidy all in all this is a good hotel and well worth staying at when in memphis:

title: “Business”
text: Beds with bad odor...night stand lamps out of order...would not leave my car park on their premises.

title: “Fun and Funky”
text: Great place. Roomy rooms. Friendlly Service. Perfect Location.

title: “Spectacular property, ideal location to Lucas, good service”
text:
I really liked this property! Decor in the property was new, modern, bright, and had a "nouveau Art Deco" look about it. From the pieces of sculpture/art in the lobby to the lighting and wallpaper, it was a comfortable public area. Hallways on floors were bright, clean, well maintained and comfortable. 
Rooms themselves were clean, comfortable, well-lit and continued with the boutique hotel feel about it. Flat-screen televisions were also nice. I had a comfortable sleep with the beds with comfy sheets and coverings. Bathroom was nicely decorated with (likely) faux granite countertops and nice sconce lighting. If you wanted additional lighting you could also turn on a overhead light in the bathroom. 
If you are going to Lucas, you literally cannot get any closer than this hotel. It is literally across the street. The rest of downtown is within about a 10 minute walk or very short drive (I would walk as opposed to keep moving a car and paying for additional parking, but that's my preference). Also, if here for Indy Indians baseball or part of the Indiana Convention Center (whenever Indianapolis decides to finish it), this will be a very convenient hotel to these also.
Breakfast was your typical HI Express breakfast, an expanded continental option with hot items, cold items, and of course the signature cinnamon rolls. You should be able to get a relatively decent breakfast.
Staff was all generally pleasant and was nice enough to let me store luggage behind the Front Desk between the time I vacated the room and time I left Indy, so I didn't have to leave luggage in the car.
While I've so far been pretty much an ad for this hotel (but believe everything I'm writing), there's a few items I didn't perfectly like. You will have some street noise from the rooms -especially if you have a street facing room. If you're a very light sleeper, it may be a problem, but I didn't personally find it that bad. Internet is free at the hotel, though only wired from what I could see. My laptop did find wi-fi signals if from nearby (such as Lucas) for a fee. Parking is not free at the hotel, though for a downtown location not terrible at $10/night.
Finally, there were a few very minor maintenance items in my room, but nothing that really took from the overall enjoyment of the room. 
Finally, more restaurants within a block or so would be handy. Right now, only a few fast food on the other side of Lucas and a small bar or two. It does appear a new place is opening next door to the hotel this fall, which will be a nice addition to the neighborhood.
Overall, I look forward to going back to this hotel next time I might be in Indianapolis.

title: “In tears...over priced...close to everything”
text: plz dont take this the wrong way the hotels was very nice,the pool had my grandson in tears his eyes burned until he feel a sleep and to make the matters worse ther was no towels in the pool area! The life guard call serveral times.. it took a guest to call front desk to get what they brought(a few). I also had trouble getting towels the next morning up until i made do and was leaveing out the door for the day..! Parking was overed priced on our last day we found much cheaper parking even thow we could walk to the lovely harbor!!Buy more linens with what you charge for parking we are you guest,would stay again

title: “Big Mistake”
text:
We booked this hotel as we were adviced that staying at The Wharf was the place to go ..for us it was a big mistake the hotel was dreary ,and the entrance from The Wharf side was seedy and 
depressing . Check in was slow staff were ok not what you expect for a Sheraton as for the parking charges that was a joke ..way expensive ...we cut our stay there short by 3 days to be honest and in my opinion The Wharf is a must see but don't stay at the hotels in that area depressing ....much better to stay up in the funkier area and travel down to The Wharf ..actually all Wharfs are the same we have taken them off all our trips ..seen one seen them all!!! ...would never go back again .....spent more on parking than on food ..just a wee bit of a rip off ..that is my view Marion Davren

title: “The Westin easily topped everything I had previously experienced!!”
text:
I recently completed an 8 Night Leisure Break [18th May – 26th May 2010 inclusive] at The Westin Beale in Memphis, Tennessee, in Double Room Accommodation with my Partner, Marion - AND - as a seasoned business traveller for many years on an international basis – plus a regular annual holidaymaker at various European and US locations – I can honestly say that The Westin easily topped everything I had previously experienced both for comfort and that ‘relaxez vous’ feeling!! 
This was not only in terms of the first class quality of the Hotel’s general accommodation, facilities and services, but also, in fact in particular, in the exceptional personal attention provided by Management, Concierge and Support Staff – from basic Room domestics to routine information services to specialist ‘local knowledge’ pointers to urgent/emergency ‘special needs’. 
Concierge Joan Robinson and Duty Manager Derek Hoffman fully deserve special praise in this regard!! 
Not only had they provided exceptional help in rearranging Westin Accommodation in the wake of the Iceland Volcanic Dust chaos, but my standout example of their ‘above the call of duty’ service was when my Laptop ‘crashed’ a few days after arrival. I was frankly ‘gutted’ at the prospect of no daily access to Email/UK News/etc, and at a loss technically on how to restore my Laptop back into full service. 
On the morning after the ‘crash’ happened I left my Laptop at the Reception Desk with a note for Joan/Derek explaining the problem – and when I returned to The Westin in late afternoon my Laptop was fully operational again – no fuss made/just part of the service!! In actual fact it was truly ‘above the call of duty’ service!! 
For a Memphis visit The Westin also proved the absolutely ideal location!!
Literally on the corner of Beale Street (but with superb soundproofing to ensure zero intrusive noise inside the Hotel) - and likewise ‘next door’ to the Pyramids Stadium and the Rock’n’Soul and Gibson Guitar Museums - The Westin is also within easy walking distance of Main Street (the Cotton Museum) and Union Avenue (the Peabody ‘Duck Parade’). 
And with no hesitation for a couple of Senior Citizens, Marion and I were also well able to stroll casually to other ‘not quite so central’ Memphis landmarks, including Sun Records, The National Civil Rights Museum, Mud Island River Park and the Riverside (perfect morning/evening stroll).
YES, FOR A MEMPHIS VISIT - BUSINESS OR LEISURE - THE WESTIN BEALE IS HIGHLY/HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!

title: “Silver Cloud Inn at Lake Union is a great place to stay while visiting Seattle.”
text: What an enjoyable stay! Silver Cloud Inn at Lake Union has an amazing staff that makes sure your stay is truly wonderful. We had a beautiful lake view room with views of the Space Needle. The hotel offers free parking in a secure garage and a convenient shuttle to Pike Place Market, Pioneer Square and the Space Needle eliminating the hassle of driving in downtown Seattle. It is also within walking distance to some very good restaurants on the lake. The rooms are spotless and the beds are very comfortable. The only thing that could be improved upon is the breakfast area. The breakfast items are adequate, but it is not clear if table cleaning is the responsibility of the guest or the staff, leaving few places to sit that are clean. I would definitely recommend staying here while in Seattle.

title: “Great weekend package”
text: We stayed here one night. It is close to all the main attractions in San Diego (La Jolla is 10 minutes west and the zoo is 10 minutes south etc). We had a view of the green hill (better than the highway view). We recommend the "Your weekend" package which was $119 in March. It included hot breakfast buffet for 2, internet, parking and one other choice (we picked breakfast for 2 more but you can pick 2 cocktails, movie etc). As a Hilton Honors member you also get to choose from a movie, 1 appetizer etc. Rooms are nice mid-range type room. There is a Wendy's 1/2 block away so that is handy for the kids or when you need a fast food meal.

title: “Too hip for its own good”
text: This is a hip, contemporary hotel in a great location. It is not terribly user friendly. The elevators are dark, and almost all guests (comedically) search for the button to their floor. The lobby/lounge is so noisy and dark (again) that you can't really hear or see. There's public internet access during the day that disappears once the bar starts going. It's a great place to hang out and people watch, though. The food is generally very good, and the bar is overpriced and the service indifferent, but you still don't mind because the crowd is so interesting. The front desk staff is very good and friendly. The wait staff feels like they're doing you a favor by waiting on you. The room I had was spacious and comfortable. My colleague was not so lucky with a cramped and musky room. Expensive, hip, attitudinal. It's a fine place to stay in Times Square, but I'd suggest other parts of the city if you want a better hotel.

title: “4 Seasons - anniversary”
text: We stayed at Four Seasons for our 5 year anniversary and loved it. It was our first time in a four seasons and we were blown away. Rooms clean, hotel was beautiful, and the staff was amazing. AA++ all around.

title: “You really CAN'T get there from here”
text:
Nice enough place but sooooo frustrating to try to get to. You can see it, but even with a map it is extremely difficult to find. It took us for our five tries (after each wrong turn, back onto expressway, down to next exit, turn around, etc.) and when I finally got there I was really frustrated.
Room okay, clean and comfortable, bathroom clean. Business center with two computers. Free coffee and USA Today. Nice pool. 
Most motels we stay in include breakfast but this one does not and restaurant on site really pricey. We paid $50 for a room via Priceline.
I would not stay there again--Austin has many better options.

title: “fantastic hotel”
text:
My wife and I had the pleasure of staying at the Skyline for a week, this was our first time in New York, we were rather apprehensive about staying in Hell's Kitchen, but all our fears were unfounded.
The hotel was very good value, the staff extremly helpful, in particular the concierge Norman lees and his wife.
The hotel was well situated and in walking distance of all the major sites in the city.
We found 9th Avenue excellent for dining out.
All in all a great holiday, and we will be back next year.
D&R Shiers, Liverpool, England.

title: “Everything has a price”
text:
This hotel was not for me. I am a budget mindful traveler. The only reason we stayed here was because my husband was on business and his work paid for the room. Everything at this hotel had a price. Internet in your room, $14. Exercise room needed a membership, $10 a day. No continental breakfast. Luckily the pool was free, which is where I spent quite a bit of time. This is a place for folks that have extra money to spend on things that are complementary at other cheaper hotels. 
I will say that the front desk staff was accommodating. When we first arrived and walked into our room on the 12th floor it smelled very smokey. We went down and explained the situation and they quickly gave us another room on a different floor. I wouldn't choose to stay here in the future.

title: “Great Stay @ the Wyndham”
text:
We stayed @ the Wyndham Denver Tech Center for 3 days at the end of July 2004. It was a wonderful room. I made the reservation and pre-paid on line. I traveled with my husband and 5 year old, so we got an oversized room with a sofa bed. The room was comfortable, the service was VERY friendly. We ate at the hotel restaurant for breakfast a couple of days and the food and service were good. The lobby provides a hub for wireless internet and it is comfortable.
I didn't like the swim lessons in the pool and thought that the water was very cloudy (so I can't recommend that. Although, my son loved this part!). Also no hot tub :(!
But other than that, I thought it was a first rate hotel at a VERY reasonable cost (only $59!), bed and room was very nice. When we go to Denver again we'll stay there.

title: “Great place, definitely coming back in an LA minute”
text: The price is right, the room is roomy and the food is darn good and best of all, the peoples treat ya like somethin' special. I've been here the last 3 visits to LA and I felt that I needed to give this independent some credit, so I thought I'd write and let the people out there know if you need a really pretty decent place to overnight, you won't go wrong here. I was here with my girlfriend and if you hapen to be here on a Friday night, there Clipper Bar is like a dance club with beautiful people having tons of fun. The good thing about it, the cover is free for the hotel guests which was a plus for us. We danced til 1am and had a blast, so for those seeking some fun, you got it here too. We checked in the jacuzzi suite they had on the site and it was pretty cool - real different and a treat. Definitely returning soon.

title: “we will be back!!!”
text:
My wife and I,went here for a romantic get away...I choose this W for my wife and to my surprise...This was a very nice and updated hotel that we both feel in love with!
We ate dinner once and breakfast once and both times and the meals are awesome!
The rooms are small but very very nice. with upgraded t.v. bed and other things makes this hotel very nice. The gym is a "3" from 1 to 10 
This hotel is close to the MONROE Train/subway station 2 blocks to be exact. So remember to take the "L" train from O'hare for 2.25$ per person get off on MONROE and walk 2 blocks and ur there:)
Over all we loved the location the people and the city........I hope you have a wonderful time as we did! Thanks

title: “Good value”
text:
The room was probably too small to swing a cat, as they say, but I didn't bring my cats, so it didn't matter. Honestly, unless you're paying a fortune, you're going to get a small room in any New York hotel! 
Bottom line: clean room, friendly staff, down the block from a subway station, one block from a cross-town bus, lots of restaurants in the area. That's all you need.
My only complaint would be that the bathtub is small.

title: “Loved this Hotel”
text: Have just returned from our holiday in NYC where we stayed at St Giles The Tuscany. The hotel was gorgeous. The rooms were HUGE,clean & the staff were brilliant. All the staff were friendly & helpful no matter what there job title was. The hotel was 10 mins walking distance from Times Square, we stayed on the 6th floor & had a wicked view of the Crysler Building a view well worth waking up to. The staff were playing a softball match on the day we left against another hotel I really hope they won & wish them good luck for the next one. This was our first visit to NYC & was a brilliant experience made even better by staying at this GREAT HOTEL. When I return to NYC I will be staying in this hotel again.....

title: “Nice place but you'll pay for it!”
text:
Great space, large living room, large nice bathroom, excellent decor. Great service! The room service was great too, nice being able to get a Gordon Ramsay restaurant meal to the room. 
A bit overpriced, have stayed at similar or better for less. No views as surrounded by other tall buildings.

title: “Superb experience”
text: I spent a year researching where to stay in Seattle for a pleasure trip there prior to a cruise to Alaska and am so glad I found the Alexis Hotel! I usually stay at Fairmont hotels and considered staying there for this trip but when I saw the hotel online and read more about Kimpton's philosophy in their hotels, I decided to try the Alexis. It was one of the best decisions I've made and was the beginning of a perfect trip to Seattle and Alaska. I always sign up for loyalty programs with hotels and did so with Kimpton's InTouch program as well. As soon as we arrived, we were treated by the front reception staff as though we were their most important guests. Surprisingly to us, because we were InTouch members, they were gracious enough to upgrade our suite that we reserved and I can honestly state that when we opened the door to our room, my partner and I looked at each other and our jaws dropped. The room was spectacular and beyond our expectations. The hotel was walking distance to everything we wanted to explore. I was very sorry that we weren't staying at the hotel longer. I don't go to Seattle often enough, but I can assure you that every time I go in the future, I will only stay at the Alexis hotel. It was superb!

title: “great location virtually walking distance to all locations”
text: just got back from the novotel,spent 4 nights there with the wife and 2 kids(18 and 11)enough room for a family of 4,only complaint from the wife was no kettle in room for that must have cup of tea.apart from that it is in a great location to walk to most places-10 mins to 5th ave and same again from central park(actually saw BRUCE WILLIS having lunch near central park)the hotel is right across the road from the MAMA MIA show which we went to on the saturday night,what a fantastic night,all in all the hotel is well situated ,clean and relatively cheap for its location,will definately go again

title: “VERY GOOD STAY WOULD GO BACK”
text: I had booked this hotel to take my Daughter for her 21st, after reading reviews I wasn't looking forward to it, BUT HOW WRONG, we walked in to a fantastic lobby, the staff were always helpful. Our room was clean and for a city a good size, the bed was very comfortable. If I had to say one thing the bathroom was clean but a bit tired. The hotel is in a great position, we walked everywhere, Times Square, Macys, Central Park, The Harbour etc. I would not hesitate to go back.

title: “Orchid Suites.....its all about location and that's it!”
text: Orchid Suites is very much like the house that you used to share with your friends in college.....habitable but nothing fancy.......the beautiful part of this hotel is the location........you are on right on Hollywood Blvd and many of the things that you want to see and do are really, really close-by

title: “Friends Birthday in the City!”
text: My college friends and I made a trip to New York to celebrate our friends birthday. We stayed the night in a gorgeous 2 bed/2 bath suite. The bedrooms were huge and the beds were SO comfortable. It had the most beautiful living room that had such an amazing view of the city. The staff couldn't have been more hospitable. We had someone personally show us up to our room and they brought us all slippers when we got there. They even knew my friends name when he asked the person at the front desk a question the next day! It couldn't have been more luxurious! Our stay at the Waldorf was something that I will NEVER forget. The elegance was like no other hotel I have ever seen. Staying at the hotel was my favorite part of my trip into New York and I didn't want to leave! I would recommend the Waldorf to anyone looking for a place to stay in the city or anyone who just wants to spend a special night in a place they won't ever forget. I can't wait till I can hopefully make it back again!

title: “Great STAY”
text:
I came to the CP at the Airport and what a suprise. The shuttle picked me up and saw I was late and called to have the restaurant stay open. The staff checked me in and brought my bags to my room, I went to the restaurant and the chef prepared me a huge cob salad and gave me the best lowfat asian dressing!
when i got to my room everything was brand new- the room looked great and the bed was so cumpfy! 
This was the best night sleep i had on the road in a while.
In the am i had STARBUCKS and off to my meeting.
Thanks CP Indy Airport!
Thomas

title: “Great budget hotel. Clean, safe and well located!”
text:
I was kinda nervous because of some of the bad reviews but my friend and I were on a tight budget, so we booked a double for the weekend of Nov. 30th. We found the Morningside to be very nice. The staff was all very helpful and courteous. I don't know what everybody is talking about, but Patrick is a very nice man, I spoke to him on the phone twice to confirm and he checked us in and gave us directions to a bunch of places. Nice guy. The room was average size, no luxuries but very clean and cozy. We had a shared bathroom but it was right next to the room and was also very clean. The only thing we would have liked was a tv in the room. There wasn't one but hey, it's NY! we were so tired from all our walking and sightseeing that when we got back we went right to bed anyway. The hotel is close to the bus and subway, as well as walking distance from many restaurants and supermarkets. It's very well located and a good place to stay if you're on a budget. I'll definitely stay there from now on when I visit NY!!
P.S. Visit the catholic church next door, it's beautiful!

title: “Great stay!!”
text: Really enjoy visiting this hotel. The airport shuttle is fast and friendly. The staff is amazing. Stella at the front desk is my favorite. The rooms are clean and you get a great view of Ladybird Johnson Lake. Good breakfast and easy access to Town Lake trails.

title: “Good hotel for business”
text:
Overall this this is probably the best hotel that I have stayed in for business
Positives:
- great location in downtown Houston meaning only a short walk to the office
- free wi-fi
- large rooms
- friendly staff
- hotel restaurant was ok (but portions a little to big)
- inclusive continental breakfast (whilst not great) was a nice touch
- happy hour (a couple of free drinks from 17.30 to 18.30) 
- complimentary cookies 
- complimentary shuttle around Downtown Houston was handy
- laundry room so no need to pay exhorbitant hotel charges to clean your clothes
Negatives:
- gym is small and gets very busy early in the morning
- shower (on my second stay only) was not very powerful
- high price for valet service and they take a while to get your car back to you
- very high minibar prices ($6 for a bottle of water!) and the fridge has weight sensors so you will be charged for taking the item out of the fridge rather than drinking or eating it

title: “Fabulous experience at the Omni Parker House”
text: I was thoroughly pleased with my stay at the Omni Parker House during my November 2006 visit. My room (#1426 @ $185/night) was a perfect size for me, beautifully appointed, and exceedingly comfortable. According to the hotel floorplan, some rooms were smaller (I probably wouldn't have enjoed that as much) and some were larger. I had a queen bed and plenty of room to move around. I joined Select Guest before my arrival, and received morning coffee, juice, and newspaper, and also evening turndown service (and chocolates!). The Select Guest suprised (eucalyptus bath salts) was lovely. I was impressed by all staff of the Omni Parker House whom I came in contact with, for their professionalism and graciousness. I will definately book future hotel rooms with Omni, and will happily recommend Omni and the Boston Omni Parker House to my colleagues.

title: “Great for business travelers”
text:
I recently attended a conference here and brought my son with me. 
Pros:
The rooms are big, especially the Executive Suite rooms. 
They have cribs instead of Pack N Play units. 
The beds are quite comfortable.
The rooms have good temperature control, and the bathrooms have dual-head showers. 
The hotel is centrally located in SOMA within walking distance to BART. 
Cons:
Like other reviewers have mentioned, since they tend to be full, they don't usually have rooms available before check-in time.
Room service menu is limited and expensive and has a 20% service fee.
Do not valet your car at the hotel unless you absolutely have to. With tax, it's over $50 a day to park at the hotel. There is a much more affordable parking garage right across the street.

title: “Meeting Concierge - Dawn Moore...absolutely awesome!”
text: The purpose of my meeting at the hotel was to conduct a training session for a client. In all of my travels I have not had a hotel execute every detail perfectly. My training required multiple technical and AV options and all were delivered perfectly. Dawne Moore the meeting concierge anticipated all of my needs and ensured that they were there before I could even ask for anything. She truly made all of the difference in my meeting experience.

title: “A Letter To Corporate”
text: I would like to bring to your attention and to ensure that corporate and all management understands the magnitude of my experience and the experiences of all that attended at the Westin At La Cantera in San Antonio, Texas on a Ladies Weekend Get-A-Way July 29th through Aug 2, 2010. My sole concern is that I might not be able to articulate to you the inexhaustible attentiveness, the attention to detail and the kinds engagement that your staff achieved during our stay. I am very proud to state even after weeks of leaving the facility of Westin At La Cantera that your employees continue to leave a reminder of how they exceeded our expectations on every level of service made available and met requests beyond what I would consider everyday amenities with a smile and an urgency to please. I want to ensure that you understand that our very experience at Westin At La Cantera has left over whelming palatable memories for all five of us who traveled from five different states to be at this weekend reunion. Below is a list of every employee that made such a grand impression on us. We hope that this letter will help “every single one” of these following employees in some way in our comparatively small effort to show our gratitude in providing us a weekend experience that could have ranged from good to great but ended up being beyond any experience we could have phantom. Thank you.

title: “Awesome family renunion”
text: I have been at the Roger Smith 6 times now and it's 15 years since I stayed there for the first time. It's taken me a while to get around to writing this review. In March, my cousins and I stayed at the hotel. I was impressed to see most of the same staff at the hotel that I had seen in a prior stay 3 years previously. It's always a good sign! The staff were super friendly. Especially the reception staff. I would recommend the rooms highly as they are some of the biggest ones in NYC

title: “Two Different Stays and Great Hotel”
text:
Stayed at the Sheraton two different times over 3 weeks and stayed in two different rooms. The first stay was for 5 days in a Traditional Room which was nicely appointed, comfortable and could generally understand the $169/night rate. The second stay was in a one bedroom suite at $149/night (Expedia). The suite was basically the Traditional room plus a separated seating room which had a bit older furniture but nice/ok sofas. The suite was regularly $305 and the room doesn't justify the price. I lucked out and was able to get it at a deep discounted rate. Overall, I liked both stays in each room. The beds were comfortable, carpets were newer and the bathroom was marbled and clean and the shower was roomy and nice. I think $129-$169 is a justifiable price for the Traditional Room and $149-$199 for the suite is a justifiable price.
On a separate matter, I called the Sheraton (as I normally book rooms through the hotel as opposed to booking through Expedia, Orbitz, etc. (less hassle if things go wrong)) to book the room at the lower rate (Sheraton wanted $189 vs. $149 Expedia). They wouldn't match the rate and asked for me to jump through their Best Guarantee form hassle in order to get the $149 rate. I was disappointed that they wouldn't match the rate online.

title: “Spent New Year's at the Embassy Suites and had a fantastic time, as expected...”
text: The Embassy Suites on NW HWY is the perfect hotel for business travelers or a relaxing vacation get away. Conveniently located, and may amenities, including cook to order breakfast and managers reception each evening. Great hotel.

title: “Most basic business hotel”
text:
Stayed here a while ago. Room is small but clean. Window faces the wall! Restaurant breakfast is so so. The only great point about the hotel is free internet.
Okay, one more great thing was on the following day when I needed to catch a cab to a business as well as later on needed another cab to go to a different hotel, they had a town car waiting for me as complimentary! Of course when I needed to go to the airport a few days later I called for the service and gave them a big tip!!

title: “not worth the money”
text:
I thought I'd written a lengthy review (complaint) about this hotel but I see it's not here.
Don't order the room service late at night and if you do (and they don't bring it....and don't really care or apologize for that), make SURE they don't charge you for the food THEY DIDN'T bring!!!
There are so many rip-offs about this motel, I can't even remember them all. It's the most overpriced place I've ever stayed and they nickel and dime you for EVERYthing.
I have to say the cleaning staff was very nice and did their job well but everything else about the place is a bunch of overpriced pomp!!!

title: “An Acceptable Room with a Nice Staff”
text: We Just Returned from 4 days, 3 nights at Hotel 41. The location is excellent. It is just a block or so off Times Square. The only bad thing I can say about the hotel is that the rooms, even the superior size which we paid extra for, is extremely small. However, this was our first visit so what did we know? It is clean, the staff is very very nice and accommodating. It is a great place to sleep after a full day of sightseeing/shopping. I would not want to spend any amount of time in the room and in NYC..WHO would want to do that????The bed was a bit uncomfortable at first but when you are dead tired, it sufficed. The morning cappacino/coffee/juice/pastries and bagels gave you a nice beginning to your busy day. They also have a nice video library to chose from. After all the hussel/bussel and all those people in NYC, It Is a quaint nice place to rest and start another day of tourism! The drawbacks-no view, kind of old, bed kind of hard and extremely small.

title: “2-5 minutes from the action!!”
text:
We stayed here for our first time in NYC for four nights and what a location! Literally 1 minute from herald sq subway which is on a main line, Macy's which is a stones throw away and 5 minute walk up broadway to times sq. Perfect! 
We previously read a few reviews on here stating the rooms were small. We may have got an upgrade without realising but our room was more than ample! A bit of wasted space to be honest! Room 1008. Very clean rooms, maids did a great job and the comfiest of beds!
We only had had breakfast at the hotel once which was nice, simple and quick. Teas, bagels etc. We eat at the Metro grill too which was great and reasonably priced.
Talk to Matthew the doorman/bellboy for resteraunt recommendations/shows etc. hats off to him!
We never got round to using the rooftop bar as we hardly stopped during our stay but we viewed it from the ESB as it is literally on top of the hotel metro, fantastic!
We will definitely stay here again on our next visit to NYC. My only gripe(and it's very small) was noise from the street below on two of the four nights due to party goers, bin men etc but then again it is a big city!! Go and experience it!!

title: “Wonderful Stay!”
text:
Stayed weekend of Dec. 16th in Rm. 2105. Gift from our son who has stayed here many times on business, so valet parking was included. Beautiful hotel, lobby inviting and warm (beautiful wood accents), helpful friendly staff and great location. Right around the corner from Market Street, short walking distance to Union Square (all lit up for Christmas, just beautiful), and the new HUGE Westfield Shopping Mall on Market. 
Nice view from our room's floor to ceiling window. Looked toward bay, and down on Mascone Center grounds, surrounding streets and to the right we could see the architectually beautiful huge Marriott Hotel. We enjoyed a very quiet and comfortable stay. Room size nice, non smoking, with King bed. Two comfortable upholstered arm chairs with ottoman, beside round table with lamp. Also, a nice size desk with chair in room with phone near window, adequate standard , regular tv and a mini bar that we we did not look in, or use. Coffee maker with pre-pkged Starbucks Coffee in bathroom/sink area. 
There is also a Starbuck's right across the street that we frequented. We did not eat at the hotel, but Jester's restaurant looked very nice. They do serve breakfast, lunch and dinner. We did notice signs stating this hotel is to become a Westin Hotel after the first of the year.

title: “Very tired”
text:
On arrival the place look very tired, reception area was chaos, staff were pleasant enough though.
The whole lobby could do with decorating, re-designing and a new carpet, it looked kind of grubby.
The hall ways are very dreary and need brightening up. The room while not a bad size, was a dull orange colour and did nothing to lift the sprits on arrival.
The room itself was clean, with a basin separate from the bath and toilet.
The lights at first seemed incredible dark as they are emergy saving and take time to 'warm up'.
The location wasn't bad, about 15 mins walk to the river and 10 mins to the Loop. 
All in all you must be able to get nicer in Chicago, but if thats all they have take it, you'll survive

title: “Brilliant place to stay”
text: Really large rooms for NYC. We where 3 adults and the 3rd adult found the sleeper couch really comfy. The bed in the main room was fantastic. Lots of space for all of us. My two year old son slept on an inflatable bed which we had brought with us and there was plenty of room for it. Was nice to have a fridge. We ate in most nights as the toddler was tired and it was great to have a seperate room for him to sleep in while we finished eating. Best part of this place was the staff who where so helpful to us and many others as we where there when Irene was coming. Our flight out of the city was cancelled and they helped get us transport to a car rental place on the Saturday. They changed what could have been a big drama into a great experience and all with a smile.

title: “Pleasant”
text: I stayed in The Comfort Inn in March 2011. it is a very comfortable Hotel,The staff were more than helpful when we asked to change rooms, we were straight out of one and into the other with no fuss at all. The breakfast was plentiful with fresh pancakes every morning plus tea and coffee was served in the reception lounge throughout the day.

title: “Friendly staff, nice room design, a bit of a ways to Times Square”
text:
Stayed here for my first time in NYC over Memorial Day weekend. Called ahead and let them know my flight was arriving in the morning and was told if my room was available I could check in early. Was able to check in around 11am which was really nice to be able to settle in and take a load off. Had a queen sized standard room. Comfy bed, nice sized flat screen and cool looking bathroom and overall furnishings. Also plenty of convenient outlets to plug in your gizmos. Even had an ihome alarm clock to dock my phone. Friendly staff and liked the vibe of the place, not at all like a cookie cutter chain hotel (even though this is part of the Wyndham franchise). 
The only big drawback for me was location. Definitely felt safe (midtown police precinct is literally next door) but this place isn't nearly as close to Times Square as I thought. It is definitely "South", like 12 blocks south. Subway station is at the end of the block so anywhere you want to go it's not hard, but must admit after a couple of late nights out on the town in the Times Square area it would have been nice to have home base a little bit closer.
Couple of other minor drawbacks:
- Hotel bar closes at midnight or earlier despite room menu that says it closes at 2. Got back around 1am my first night, was planning on getting a late night snack and drink for the room but found out that they were already closed There are not a lot of options in the immediate area (avoid Tick-Tock diner) so it would be nice to have in-hotel option but at least don't advertise that it's open later.
- No bedside lighting in the room. Didn't really need it but I think it would be nice. Just had overhead lighting and lamp bracketed to the desk side of the room.
Overall a satisfying stay, staff was great but if you're planning on spending a good amount of time in the Times Square/Broadway area just be aware of where this location actually is.

title: “Fantastic New hotel a gem in NYC!”
text:
We were very impressed with this hotel! The room was so big, clean and elegant! The bathroom was awesome with a tiled shower and sitting area inside. 
The bed was very comfortable that I did not want to get out of it every morning. The view from our window was part of NYC's skyline and also viewed the river. It was so nice to be away from the noise from Times Square! It was very quiet! We enjoyed this hotel over Valentine's Day weekend. This hotel does not have much around it since it is along River but this hotel is easy to walk to Javitz Convention Center if you are there for business and just few blocks from all the restaurants in Hell's Kitchen. It is also close enough to walk to Broadway Ave/Theater district. We usually stayed at their sister hotel in past, The Muse, which is in the Theater district but now will stay at Ink48. The staff was very accommodating to us with bringing up our boarding passes, bringing a vase to put my roses in when I did not ask them to and just being extra friendly! I LOVED THIS hotel!!! It is a top-notch boutique-ish hotel! They will soon open up their rooftop restaurant and start in-room spa services.

title: “Good Value and Good Service”
text: I often travel to NY and finding a hotel for a cheap price in can be hard. That said, Club Quarters staff are easy to work with, provide good customer service, and room rate at a good value. This is true in the US and UK just got back from London.

title: “The worst experience we have ever had....”
text:
This hotel was a let down - it had come recommended by a family member whom had stayed there last year. Not only did it not meet our expectations is was a downright disappoint - we would encourage our family and friends to NOT look at this hotel as an option.
The most significant problem began with the computer system not working and we were overcharged. I am still attempting to resolve this issue with the contact provided (fifteen emails over five weeks and still waiting). So unprofessional and disrespectful. I have had to repeatedly prove my claim with credit card receipts and confirmations - although clearly indicated.
The front desk staff were far from knowledgeable and showed little initiative or concerns or when asking for guidance.
An overall very very bad experience.

title: “We'd stay here again!”
text:
We got a great price through Travelocity, bundled in with airfare, and wound up paying about $115 a night for two people. For that price, this is a steal! It's a mid range hotel that gets bumped up a category for a few things: location, amenities and staff. 
Yes, the front desk staff (and the doormen) were gracious and helpful. We are low-key people and don't place many demands, but these folks were great. 
Next - The room was clean; the beds and pillows were good. There were two double beds, and a sofa bed. Good size room. We were there during the Olympics so did in fact use the TV every night (yup, every night). No probs with the TV / channels or reception. The air conditioning was fine. Coffee pot, microwave, fridge were all clean and functioned well. On our way in one evening, we asked for more coffee at the front desk (no decaf for us - who needs to sleep on vacation?!) and they immediately handed some over. 
Trader Joes - turn right out the front door. Go to corner and turn right again and go half-way down block. (We live near a Trader Joe's in Philadelphia so were thrilled to be near one.) Pack your own bottle opener or corkscrew - we forgot and paid 5 bucks for a corkscrew (considering how much we saved, not a biggie...) I also packed my own plastic ware and cereal bowls - stuff like that is not Trader Joe's strong point. 
Because of the great location, if you like to walk, I would not recommend buying a multi-day CTA pass. From O'Hare, we took the blue line into Clark/Lake and took a taxi (less than $10). Didn't take a taxi again! If you are walkers, this is a very walkable area - over to the river for the boat tour, down into the loop for plays; up to North Shore, over to Navy Pier.
I'd stay here again, and I'd recommend it to my friends and family. Chicago is a fabulous city to visit and this hotel definitely helped make the trip as great as it was.

title: “If you're going to Chicage as a tourist, and you like shopping, this is the place!"”
text:
We totally lucked in with the choice of Westin hotel for our first trip to Chicago! Lovely hotel, great service, gorgeous view of the water from our window on the 22nd floor, and for any serious shoppers, this is the location to be! We walked everywhere, including to get our Architectural River cruise. The hotel was clean, the lemonade and cookies were a nice touch when you check in and are parched and would like to feel a bit revived.
I would definitely return to the Westin on Michican Ave. on my next trip.

title: “First Time Visit”
text:
Took my wife to the RBI for a few days of relaxing and golf for her birthday......What a treat! Everything (and I mean everything) about the stay was beyond excellent! The staff couldn't do enough for us, the golf course was challenging but fun, the food was outstanding, our premium room overlooking the 18th hole was perfect. We had planned to go to town for some meals and things, but never left the resort! 
We plan to visit regularly in the future. Thank you RBI for making our stay wonderful!

title: “A former Legendary place that has hit the bottom....”
text: stayed here and regretted every second of it. Im all for budget traveling....but this place charges Hilton prices for flop house accomodations....paper thin walls that allowed me to be woken up to a domestic squabble next door...and not the best of characters mulling around the front of the hotel after midnight.....dont bother with this place....stick to the New Yorker on the other side of Madison Square Garden

title: “Nice downtown option”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights in early October 2012. The Tenderloin location is not charming, but it's not bad either -- and reasonably close to the BART stops on Market, the Civic Center, etc. Elegant old-fashioned lobby with strong morning coffee and a nice California wine happy hour. Room and bathroom were smallish, but comfortable and well-appointed. Decent basement gym. Friendly service. We'd come back again.

title: “Amazing Service, Very Clean, Perfect Location!”
text: The Blakely was one of the best hotels I've stayed at. The rooms and bathrooms were very modern and clean! It was like 2 or 3 blocks from times square. The service was also outstanding! I will definitely stay here again next time I go to the big apple!

title: “Comfort and high style, but pricey”
text: The Ames hotel is a treat - we had a double bedded room that was stylish and very comfortable with a great view all the way to the Fort Point channel. But the hotel is pricey; be prepared to pay plenty for parking - of course this is the same at all the Boston hotels and parking garages. Better to take a taxi, shuttle or public transport from the airport and walk around or take a taxi if necessary. The hotel also needs to improve the lighting for its magnifying mirror and add some storage for toiletries in its otherwise perfect bathroom. Don't miss the wonderful restaurant - the food is delicious and the drinks are creative and refreshing. Room service for breakfast is prompt with wonderful fresh fruit, coffee and delicious muffins as well as more substantial meals at a very good price.

title: “Night Hotel, NY”
text: We stayed at the Night Hotel a few weeks ago for 7 nights. We couldn't have picked a better hotel. The staff were very helpful and friendly and the hotel itself is unique and quite stunning. The rooms are very comfortable. We went to the bar one night to have cocktails and had a great evening. The location of the hotel is unbelievable, only a 30 second walk to Times Square. We will be recommending the hotel to all our friends!

title: “Beautiful Lobby & lounge, but not so beautiful rooms!”
text:
The hotel is a beautiful grand looking old hotel with the 1909 feel (its year of establishment). The lobby, ballrooms & lounges make you feel as if you're on the set of "Titanic" movie or somewhat to that effect. It really is gorgeous if you like that sort of character (which I appreciate). HOWEVER, upon making your way to your room, you then feel as if you've been transported from "Titanic" to "The Shining". Its hallways are dim & creepy looking. Then you open your room that has a doorbell on it & you realize the antique look is not that charming after all. There's a difference between these old hotels that are "restored" to capture their former beauty & then there is the St Anthonys where everything has been "maintained" as much as possible. 
Our room was extremely small; the bed & furniture took up the entire room. The furniture which was pretty @ one point; but all the handles on the drawers were missing or falling off. The bathroom was beyond small & very old. (I had to ask for a plug for the tub so I could take a bath). The structure reminded you of an old hospital room that was turned into an old hotel room. The food from room service was terrible. Housekeeping did Not refill the coffee/sugar or soap/shampoo when they cleaned up!! if it is something that is being used, you think it would be replenished. We had our 3 year old with us & its not what you'd call a kid friendly hotel.
Now I booked the room from Priceline for $55 a night so I guess I got what I paid for. I somehow did enjoy my stay; it wasn't a roach motel or anything; it was just old & small. I would have been upset if I had paid the normal $103-225 prices. Maybe the larger rooms were bigger & more updated. I enjoyed walking around the lobby & lounge area immensely. The hotel staff was very friendly & helpful when asked for assistance. 
The hotel is surrounded by an area where there is a lot of homeless & we got a lot of people asking for $ but it happens.

title: “3rd visit”
text:
This is my third visit to this hotel for business. It is central to where we need to be for work, has great restaurants nearby, and the staff is wonderful and suggested only wonderful places to eat dinner. Due to crazy schedules we ate breakfast and a very, very late dinner in the hotel restaurant Fire and Sage; the food and service were great. 
I will be back.

title: “Did the job”
text: Didnt expect anything but a bed and location close to hollywood blvd and it was exactly that. One thing to point out was the concierge 'Reihan' who's service and assistance was 5 star. I had an issue with a lost phone and he was more than accommodating to help me for which I was very appreciative. For a budget hotel, he set the bar for me customer service wise and I wish him all the very best.

title: “What hidden charm!”
text: Spent 3 nights at the Fairmont and it was lovely. On arrival we were taken to a side door and thought it looked just plain and dull. What a wonderful surprise when we step inside. It was beautiful. The decoration, was lovely and fresh and inviting. The staff were so welcoming and everyone had a smile and "Hello" for you. Food was good. Our suite was elegant and comfortable and quiet. No sound of people charging up and down the corridors. The only downside was the Shuckers bistro/pub. Very noisy and tables so close together you could overhear what other people were saying. Overall this was a great way to spend our time in Seattle close to all amenities linked with down town Seattle.

title: “would have be a great stay...”
text: We stayed at this location towards the end of October for two nights. We chose it based on reviews we had found here on trip advisor. We were able to take advantage of the evening reception one night and the breakfast both mornings. The stay would have been great if on the second morning we had not opened up the curtains to our room door (doors are glass windows with shears) to find a large cockroach. We complained (with said bug as evidence) and were told that a manager would contact us. We were never contacted by the manager and that experience left us unimpressed. Had there been follow through, I think I would still say this was a good hotel with a good location.

title: “Great Hotel and Great Location”
text: We stayed there for 5 nights in October last year. Very friendly staff and very comfortable beds. The service was good. The location was great with the cable car just across the road from the hotel. The Bart was just around the corner as well. The hotel has a very nice bar at the top that overlooks the city. Beautiful view at night. We look forward to staying there again on our next visit to San Francisco.

title: “A Good Time in Phoenix”
text:
I stayed at the Renaissance Phoenix Downtown for a conference. The lobby is beautiful, and the lobby bar is great. When I checked in, I was given a suite which they told me was "softly remodelled". It was HUGE ...boasting a living area with a sectional sofa, a dining room table and chairs and a bedroom area with two queen beds. However, the bathroom was not remodelled and the room appeared to have no internet/computer access, so I asked to be moved to another room. It was much smaller, but the amenities were far nicer.
Loved being in Phoenix, but couldn't believe how empty the downtown sector was, literally a ghost town.

title: “HORRID”
text: Shuttle service is horrible-that is one of the main reasons I booked this hotel. Had to walk several times to and from the hospital. Staff was unfriendly, no verbal greeting or smiles??? Ice machine was out of order on the 6th floor,(did have a sign), went to the 3rd and 4th floor, no ice and no out of order sign, finally obtained ice on the 5th floor. Room service extremely slow, attempts to even call room service or the front desk takes approximately 10-15 rings. I was given a room with a king bed when I had requested 2 double beds. They did correct the problem but had to wait in the wrong room for 30 minutes until the bellboy brought the correct keys. Also, bathroom dirty, hair in the tub. Front entrance under construction, entry is only through the garage on a side street. I will never stay in a Marriot again.

title: “After reading reviews I was terrified to stay here but a good budget hotel. However, do bring ear plugs!!”
text: After booking the hotel I was terrified to stay here. I am really affected by noise so I did bring ear plugs. When we arrived reception was nicer than expected. Also it is a 2 min walk from the train. As others have said the room was tiny and we struggled with room for our suite cases. That said they were very clean and modern. We were at the end of the corridor so only had one neighbour who was a single man so we were lucky I think. I could not hear him. I slept with ear plugs and slept well. I boyfriend said that he found it fine without earplugs but you could hear people in the corridor. Loved coffee and muffins in the morning. We had the shared bathroom which was small but again clean and fine. The hotel is far from luxury but it did the job. Not sure if I could stay again but only because I would want to stay on the waterfront. However, there are lots of restaurants and bars by the hotel. You need to be realistic when you stay. If the wrong people were on your hall it could be a nightmare

title: “A Little Off The Mark...”
text: My initial impression of the hotel was a good one when I walked by it a few days before I checked in. Although it's at the top of Mason street (lots of hills) I thought it would be well worth the trek. When I went to check in there was a long line to do so and only one person assisting with the process, which I found to be ridiculous. It's a hotel that attracts a lot of business travelers and should be better prepared to deal with a volume of people in the late afternoon/evening, when people typically arrive.
