I had reserved a king room, but was told that only a queen was available. The room was clean, but very small and the bathroom was smaller than that of my NYC apartment's bathroom. Before dinner we decided to have a drink at the Top of the Mark bar, but were told there was a half hour wait for a drink. What do you do when you're waiting to have a drink? You can't have a drink, after all. Also, there is a cover charge after 6:30, which I found completely ridiculous. I wasn't able to wait to be seated, but given the location and the view the bar speaks so highly of, I'm sure they inflate the drink prices enough. The rooms' walls are also paper thin. I could hear a lot of knocking on doors down the hall early in the morning, which I didn't appreciate. Overall this place has a good location, but I was disappointed with the service I experienced.

title: “Nice, but shop around...”
text:
We spent Labor Day weekend in NYC at the Michelangelo. The hotel location is very good, but there are plenty of others within 2 blocks. After we got back, I got a Travelzoo notice that the W was offering rooms for $199 per night on select dates through next spring. Last time we did New York we stayed at the Affinia 50, which was a much larger, better room at similar price, but is also further from "the action".
Pros: Location, comfy bed, decent sized room, clean, very quiet (we were on the back side of the hotel). Coffee, fruit and croissants for breakfast. Bathtub. Water pressure in shower. Air conditioner works well. Never had to wait for an elevator, and they're big. Internet access (not free, though).
Cons: Quiet means view of a brick wall. I don't mind that so much, but we couldn't even tell if the sun was out. Pillows not great (we asked for and got foam pillows after the first night). Can't set A/C to leave fan running, so it cycles on and off all night, which really made sleeping well very difficult (c'mon Michelangelo, fix this - it's just a new thermostat). Bathtub not jetted. 
Overall a great weekend and a good hotel, but we'll go elsewhere next time.

title: “Good location & friendly staff”
text: Second time staying at this hotel. Very convenient location to Soho, Chinatown, East Village and Katz Deli is down the street! The room is small, but this is NYC! The hotel staff very friendly and responsive. The complimentary breakfast is great and the staff very friendly. She does not rush you out right at 10 am (closing time) like other hotels. The price is right and lower than most of the other NYC hotels and will definitely stay here again.

title: “Furnishings and location were nice, service was not”
text: They screwed up our reservation. Instead of a "deluxe lakeview room" we got a view of a brick wall on the street. The front desk clerk blamed it on Expedia. I've never had any hotel complain about Expedia before. WHen I called Expedia they tried to take control of the situation, but the hotel was uncooperative, even though the hotel had faxed Expedia a signed confirmation of the room type, according to Expedia. Manager Kate was a cold fish. She said that the Blackstone did not guarantee the room type. I pointed out that I had paid $50 more to get the view. She didn't offer any solution. I said I’d take the lesser room for the usual price. She emitted heavy sighs and said she’d call Expedia. I called Expedia 30 minutes later but Kate had not called them. I decided not to ruin the day and gave up. Upon checkout, the manager (nice black guy, didn't catch his name) called Expedia and confirmed that the charges had been reduced. Other problems: a clerk took our wakeup call request, but someone called at 6:30 instead of 9:30 (on Sunday!). I never got back to sleep because of all the sirens and street noise. The shower door was clear and the bathroom door was semi opaque glass, so you might not want to share this room with someone unless you are good friends. Beds were comfy for one but not for 2 people. Decor was pretty posh but more contemporary corporate than homey. Parking was $46. The valet guys were very nice. The location was perfect for Taste of Chicago.

title: “great location, great staff, comfortable room”
text:
my fiance and I stayed at the hard rock for a long weekend in Chicago. We got a very good deal online ($140 per night... this was a lot lower than the surrounding hotels) and so I was a little nervous that it was not going to be a good stay. The staff throughout the weekend were very helpful and kind.
The location of the hotel is perfect for doing anything downtown. We had only a couple block walk to the subway and millenium park is also very close. The river is only 1 block away too. 
The rooms are very modern and comfortable.The only down side I would say is that the hotel room seemed to be somewhat dark. During the day it was not an issue with the window light but at night it was definitely not lit well if I was trying to read, etc. 
Lastly, the bar is extremely over priced. If you're looking to have a few cocktails walk a block or 2 and you'll find a better mixed drink for less money! 
I would definitely stay at the hard rock again,

title: “Good hotel for a good price”
text:
Overall, I was pretty happy with the room, the location and the price. No complaints or anything. I enjoyed my stay here and would return to the hotel. It's not super fancy but you need to ask yourself what you're looking for..
The hotel is located near the base of the L train and my first impression was that the area seemed a bit dodgey (and that was during the day) but the Hilton (Palmer House) is only a block away. Having walked around though the area a few times it seems totally fine. Also, the L train is right above the hotel and it's pretty noisy (I could hear it inside at the reception desk)
The room is pretty large but rather dark (I was facing inward to a closed off area in the hotel complex. But if my option was facing the street and listening to the train, I'd prefer the inward view (and you could hear the train from this room but very faintly). The bathroom is large, the internet is free but they have an older tube tv. The fitness room comprises of two treadmills, a step climber, an elyptical machine, a bench and a small universal type machine. 
This is located a few doors down from the E. Madison subway entrance. I took a shuttle bus to the hotel and given the ride (over an hour and a half) I would recommend taking the subway/train. The hotel is also near the "bean" and the Art Institute of Chicago. Everything seems pretty walkable (Wacker street is probably a 15 minute walk away). You're within walking distance of deep dish pizza (Pizzano, Giordano's) and a bit farther out but walkable blues music (Blue Chicago).

title: “very pleasant hotel and great location”
text: my family and i stayed here for 6 nights and had a wonderful stay. the staff was pleasant and cordial. the beds were plush and the junior suite was very roomy. it was convenient to have a laundry downstairs and great dining options in the neighborhood. i would recommend it to anyone.

title: “I had a grate time at Embassy Suites!”
text:
I stayed here for two nights. After a delayed flight and all the chaos at O'Hare, I finally arrived at a hotel. Front desk staff was friendly and helpful. I got a room on 6th floor toward state st. It was a nice, well-maintained room. I love that they have complimentary breakfast and manager's special in the evening. 
Location is also another good thing of this hotel. It's very close to Grand station redline. Jewel-Osco is across the street [you can also purchase CTA pass here.] And 2-3 blocks to N.Michigan or Magnificent mile. 
All in all, Embassy Suites downtown chicago is perfect for anyone [business traveler, tourists, solo traveler ect.]
Only complaint I would have is the Internet fee. It would be best if it's free : )

title: “They took great care of us.”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Onyx Hotel in Boston for our 25th anniversary. When they found this out they up graded us to a bigger room and sent us champagne and fruit. Then Hurricaine Irene kept us in Boston for two extra days. The Onyx did what they could to help us get a flight and gave us the Hurricaine rate on the room for the extra nights. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Wow! This Hotel & Staff are AWESOME!”
text: Having read some of the less than flattering older reviews before staying here in March I was not sure what to expect. I travel quite a bit for work and have had many occasions to stay at Doubletrees, Hiltons, Mariotts, Hyatts etc... The location near IAH was super convenient. The free shuttle was very prompt. The physical building including pool, spa, fitness center and business center were all perfect. The real shining star though is the staff. I wish I could remember everyones names. The shuttle drivers: Polite, Prompt, Professional and just plain nice. The front desk staff: Maria, Barbara and EVERY other person at the desk are simply amazing. 24/7 anything my beautiful companion or I needed or wanted: They catered to us. We had much better individual attention here than we have at resort destinations costing ten times as much. The food we ordered in the restaurant (thank you Amber) and from room service was top notch. We highly recommend the snapper. With 24 hour room service, a really nice "Hot" (not lukewarm like so many others) Tub, a big clean delightful pool, free parking, a convenience store nearby, and the best, most genuine, sincerely pleasant, helpful and nice staff, this place rates easily a 15 on a scale of 1-10. Oh yeah, the rooms are great too. Very comfy beds, very clean room & bath (she always checks), LOTS of free TV stations (including sports & movie channels), upscale interior appointments (granite, travertine...) there was really nothing that we did not like about this hotel. When visiting Houston this is the only hotel I will stay at. No I don't own the hotel or work there. Visiting from Scottsdale AZ the staff impressed me so much (superior customer service is so rare these days) that I felt compelled to write review, my first ever. They really are that good!!!

title: “Very clean hotel with large rooms.”
text: I was a little worried since I wasn't getting warm fuzzies when I had called the hotel directly asking questions prior to arrival, but once at the hotel my group was welcomed. All areas of the hotel met or exceeded my picky cleanliness requirements. The rooms had plenty of room for 4 women and all of their 'stuff''. The hotel is right off I-77, so couldn't have been easier to find. We were in Charlotte to attend a concert at the Time Warner Arena downtown and the hotel has a free shuttle to and from the Lynx light rail, so getting to the concert was a breeze. The free breakfast buffet was pretty good - with a good assortment. I'd certainly stay here again!

title: “Great service/room”
text: Room was modern, comfortable and clean. Hotel is attached to parking garage, $10.00 per day. The front desk was courteous and professional. Rooms are well maintained. Met all of my expectations. It's located in the center of the city within walking distance to many restaurants.

title: “Nice people, a bit run down in the rooms”
text: We stay at Hampton Inns often, in fact, I am typing this from another one in Kingsman, AZ, so don't expect super luxury, however, the rooms were pretty cramped, carpet a bit worn and the bathrooms were tiny. Also, no real closet, just a little cupboard type thing. On the plus side, the pool was nice, although you had to go through the lobby outside and walk down a sidewalk to get to and from it. The breakfast was the worst in my HI experience; the eggs were tasteless and a very odd consistency like little pebbles, no bacon or sausage like most HI breakfasts have. The location is really pretty and close to some nice shopping, as well as really convenient right off the interstate. The hotel staff was very friendly and helpful, but the owner needs to spend some money getting the rooms in this property up to the standard of the other 30 or so HI's we've stayed in over the last few years. I'd probably give it a B minus or C plus.

title: “wonderful stay”
text: This is a wonderful hotel on town lake in Austin. The location is perfect, close to fun shops, great resteraunts, and the fabulous town lake trails! The staff here all went out of their way to make us feel welcome. Reception was aware that this was a mini reunion for 3 of us and gave us a beautiful room on the 16th floor. We loved sitting on the balcony, We even got to see President Obamas motorcade drive by! Housekeeping brought us a fridge to keep our snacks in and extra towels. The lobby bar and patio are a great place to start out the eveing or wind down the night! The bartender makes a wonderful martini called "the frenchman" Definately reccomend the Hyatt!

title: “Great every time”
text: I love Sofitels, and this one is right up there. Great location, spacious rooms, perfect beds and decor. Can't fault it or them.

title: “Milford Plaza NYC: updated and great”
text: Stayed one Saturday night at end of August 2012. The renovations of the rooms are complete. Very quiet with a great view of Eighth Avenue. My teenaged daughter and I loved the clean, modern room, beautiful bed cover, comforter and pillows, comfy bed. The location was great for Times Square, the Shake Shack (great burgers and shakes) and the theatres. Neat elevator system, you punch in your floor and it tells you which elevator (A-H) to take. Lots of towels and nice shampoo, etc. in bathroom. Only minor complaints: no ice machine on our floor, and the hallway lighting is not bright enough. Oh, and lobby reno is not complete yet, had to lug our luggage up one set of stairs from the street level entrance to the lobby one level up. I would stay there again.

title: “Consistency at a High Level”
text: Having enjoyed our stay at this Fairmont five years earlier we were happy to finally make time to return. We were not disappointed. This continues to be a top hotel with courteous efficient service provided in a most professional way. Our king room on the sixth floor was spacious, well appointed, clean, up to date and provided all the amenities we could want. Bed was quite comfortable. Although our room was located above the front entrance it was quiet and sunlit in the morning. Flat panel tv, power center to connect every electronic device you can pack, individual coffee maker and nice little touches. While on my wife's side of the bed was the usual digital clock radio that could accommodate an iPod, my side of the bed had a tasteful analogue clock with a nice feature: although it did not glow in the dark, if you tilted it forward slightly a small light came on to illuminate it. Thoughtful. But then again at this Fairmont, thoughtful touches abound. The health club is one of the top ones in DC and the location is a short walk to Georgetown, the Metro and the scenic running trails along the Potomac for which jogging maps are provided in your room. Marble bathroom was spacious and shower worked fine. Morning paper at the door was nice. Warm, cozy lobby is conducive to relaxing with a cocktail after a day of sightseeing. Did not eat in the hotel this trip but have little doubt I would have been pleased. Join Fairmont's [free] President's Club before you arrive; the benefits are substantial. I am not waiting five years to return again!

title: “Great location and loved 9 To 5 at the Marquis Theatre”
text: I went to a book convention and brought along 2 friends. The location is great right -outside the hotel is Times Square, lots of places to eat and subways nearby both to the north and south. Also inside the hotel is the theatre for 9 To 5 the Broadway show. We had bought tickets ahead of time and were surprised the theatre was inside the hotel. The rooms are very clean and spacious and include a mini safe. The internet fees were high so I decided not to log on.

title: “Bad Service Bad Room Bad Kharma”
text: Generally i'm not a picky traveller, and i've stayed at the ace several times in the past 2 yrs but the this last visit will be the last. The Ace is a great concept, hipper than thou warholian installation a la auberge. Knowing that some rooms are better than others I reserved well in advance and requested one of the deluxe rooms in the back. When i arrived they'd given the room to someone else offering the excuse, "well, the previous guest decided to stay an extra day", and the front desk person was very rude and put out by the whole exchange. The room i ended up with was small dark and very noisy. It was impossible to sleep or enjoy staying in the room as you could hear everthing from the adjacent rooms. Nothing like listening to "Cops" blasting from the room next door at 1AM, or hearing your neighbors snoring, coughing, flushing their toilet, and wondering how much they could hear as well. Unless you're twenty something and planning on partying all night and coming home and passing out aka leading the psuedo rock star life style i suggest stearing clear. There are plenty of other places in the area to stay.

title: “Convenient location, good package”
text:
My spouse & I stayed at the Westin with a package that included passes to the King Tut exhibit at the Franklin Institute. (Passes were really worth it as they were untimed and saved us lots of time in line) 
PROS - room was neat & comfortable with modern decor. We arrived late (11pm) but had no problems at check-in. Bed was soft with 2 duvets. Location was convenient - between Franklin Institute and Independence mall sites. Restaurant at the hotel (City Grange) was good for breakfast. Was a little more expensive than we would normally pay for breakfast ($36 total), but enjoyed really good steak & eggs. Also had a buffet with cold/hot options. Shops at Liberty Place next door has a food court for fast/easy food options. 
CONS - Arriving late may have left us with a less than desirable room location (524) next to the ice machine; kind of annoying through the night, but not terrible. Thermostat for the room is located directly under the A/C vent so it kept kicking off when the whole room really hadn't cooled sufficiently. The bathroom has no towel rods; they encourage you to re-use your towels to save water, but there was nowhere to hang up our towels the first morning to show we wanted to re-use them.
Biggest frustration - We left our room on Saturday at 10:30am, returned after 4pm to relax and get showered/ready for dinner. Housekeeping had not cleaned our room for the day!! They were 2 doors down and got to us about 4:45p. I had her tend to the bathroom and skip making the bed. It was very inconvenient to have to wait for her to get to us and I left a comment card requesting that they do a better job of attending to the rooms of current guests.
All in all - We really did like the hotel, the room was comfortable with a plasma TV and nice reading chair/ottoman. Just a few minor things they could tweak in the room to make it more functional.

title: “Clean, but that's all”
text: We visited for three days following Christmas while on a road trip from Portland, OR to San Francisco.  For convenience to Bart & public transportation this is a great place to stay.  We dump the rental car and catch Muni to any place in the city using the weekly muni pass card, a real bargain.  The hotel was quiet & clean, but I've stayed in the equivalent to Best Western and had as much enjoyment.  The room was small & there was no view except the lower level roof top!  As far as I am concerned it was too pricey for it's value.

title: “Great hotel for the price!”
text: We arrived fairly late on a Thursday night. The BART stopped right in front of the hotel which was the fastest way from the airport. Check in was very speedy and the hotel lobby was awesome. The history behind the hotel is worth checking out. We had three people in our group and an extra effort was made to find a bigger room for us. The bathrooms were a little small, but you have to remember the time period when the hotel was built. Better than sharing like in some upscale European hotels. As mentioned in some other reviews, there are homeless people near the hotel, but they are pretty much everywhere in San Francisco. The f-line that takes you everywhere stops in front of the hotel too. Very handy! There is a great diner across the street too. Not fancy, but good food. Overall, we enjoyed our stay at the Whitcomb.

title: “Terrible Experience”
text: The hotel looks nice, but the service was HORRIBLE and we barely slept - the beds look nice but are uncomfortable, it was noisy, the walls must be thin, we could hear everything outside- we got very little sleep!.. The weird thing is, the elevators dont go to every floor, so we had to get off at a floor below ours, and carry our luggage up the stairs....and, I had a cold shower (I called downstairs to tell them there was no hot water, and they said "the engineer will be in at 9, he'll call you then"--- I had to be at work before then, so that didn't help), then the blow dryer didn't work, and they didn't come up with a new one for such a long time, I had to leave for work with a cold, wet head. Also, one of the employees literally yelled at me about a credit card "issue" that actually ended up not being an issue at all.

title: “Absolutely fantastic”
text:
This is a great little hotel, the rooms are small but well equipped and suited our week long stay perfectly;, the bathrooms have speakers in which is pretty cool for keeping up with whatever's on the TV whilst you, shower etc. if they were a few feet bigger this would surely be a 4-star hotel. The staff are helpful and welcoming, and the complimentary breakfast pretty decent; pastries, coffee, the usual.
Very pleased with everything.

title: “Excellent hotel experience.”
text: During a recent business trip, I had the pleasure of staying at Yotel. It is the perfect hotel if you are traveling alone. It's a bit small and the rooms lack privacy if you are with someone but if it is a solo trip. Yotel is perfect. The checkin and out are very fast and efficient, the rooms are clean and organized and the price is excellent.

title: “Great time at a classy spot”
text: From the rooftop pool to the great restraunt and lobby, this hotel is classy. I booked a jacuzzi room with a view of the sound and it was spectacular. The service was nice and loved being so close to the baseball field.

title: “No Need to Leave the Hotel”
text:
One minor issue kept this from being a five star hotel experience. The lighting was so sexy and subdued that we older folk had some issues seeing. A little more light as an option please.
Overall the experience was terrific. We were upgraded to a suite, but I think the regular rooms would have been just fine. The room was very spacious and beautifully decorated. Modern without going crazy. Blackout shades on the windows made getting out of bed an option, not a requirement. The bathroom was beautifully outfitted with a great shower and clever sink, The color selection was terrific. There was also workout equipment, plenty of closet space, great robes, etc. All in all, the in room experience except for lighting was A-1.
The hotel itself is quite stunning inside. Decoration is very hip. There are two main restaurants - Bazaar and Tres. We had eaten at Bazaar several times in the past when we lived in LA. This time we dined at Tres. Both restaurants serve excellent food and are beautiful to behold.
For visitors to LA who need to be in the Beverly Hills-West Hollywood area, this is a great choice. No need to fight the Santa Monica east of downtown west traffic.
Highly recommend the hotel. Not inexpensive but cheap by Beverly Hills standards.

title: “Recent stay”
text: We arrived early at the hotel and were not made to wait for check in time. We were quickly checked in and given our room. Everything was nice and clean. The beds were awesome and the pillows were nice and soft.

title: “Good for a budget trip to the museums”
text: When we arrived on an unusually cold Memorial Day weekend, we were told that the heat was not on, and offered an extra blanket if we wished. We keep our house pretty cool, so were warm enough sleeping but the bathroom was uncomfortably cold. Took more than two minutes of running the bath water to get any warm water at all, and then the temperature varied and water pressure was weak. The reason I chose this hotel was because of the free parking ($40+/day downtown) and free shuttle to the museums, and we were on a tightbudget. The hotel delivered as promised. The day we arrived, on a Friday, there was a note posted that the shuttle was cancelled for the day, however it ran Sat & Sun. (Buy your museum tickets ahead of time!) When we were done at the Shedd we called to request Shuttle pick-up and were told the shuttle runs on a schedule and would not be able to pick us up for 3 more hours. We took a taxi and paid about $20 incl. tip. Ended up driving to Navy Pier (no hassle) as shuttle doesn't run downtown, paid $24 to park. No complimentary breakfast. Buffet offered at restaurant next door, but it was expensive and I wasn't impressed. I'd like to rate it worse, but it was cheap and we got what we paid for. Next time I would just fork out the cash and stay downtown.

title: “better than we expected”
text: The Rex Hotel was excellent. We usually stay at another boutique or the hyatt, but when I called the hotel direct, the gentleman gave me a great rate, an excellent and quiet room, and wonderful service. When we arrived we were welcomed with smiles and wine for our anniversary. We loved everything about this place.

title: “What a wonderful hotel experience, Staff members were so outstanding”
text: and the rooms are extremley nice as well as the pool, restaurant and bar. We loved the hotels history area and outdoor patio. Service was great, rates were very good. We will definitely stop here again.

title: “Wow!!! Just Amazing”
text: We got a great deal through AAA. Hotel and free breakfast buffet for $200. As soon as we pulled up we were greeted with great service and of course a smile. Checking in was fantastic and wow the Lobby was just spectacular. We didnt have a view of the bay, but I wasnt dissapointed as the hotel room was just amazing. The king size bed with six pillows was very comfy. The best night sleep I had ever had at a hotel. The buffet breakfast was a little small, but I am not complaining when it comes to free. Only thing was the Concierge desk had us call around for Alcatraz tickets. I thought that that is what a Concierge is for. I will stay here again, and have already recommended this hotel... Four Star all the way...

title: “Stunning sea view, your own patio, perfect”
text: I took a walk along Crystal Pier just before leaving San Diego - and decided to see if I could get a room here. I had a studio room at the beginning of the pier, far cheaper than some of the hotels along the beach for a 'sea view', and this one was right on the beach. The room was clean, excellently equipped, beautiful setting and good value for the location.

title: “Fantastic Staff”
text: Recently I had the opportunity to stay at this hotel for a Special Olympics Torch Run conference. The rooms and staff were great. The bar downstairs was nice and food and drink reasonably priced. The food was outstanding. The main restaurant was priced higher than I was ready for (21.00 breakfast). I stuck with coffee.

title: “Great Location”
text: The website says it all. Great location. About half a block west of Times Square. Walking distance to shopping and many attractions. It's an older hotel, but clean and well kept. It's very busy so if you are planning on checking in early you may be out of luck. There's a great little pub just west of the hotel on 47th. called the Mean Fiddler. Reasonable prices and excellent food, friendly staff.

title: “Cheap, Reasonable, Location is fantastic”
text:
4 friends and myself travelled to NY city by a car. We booked at Hotel Habitat for 2 queen size beds, thinking we could squeeze in for the night of New Year at Time Square for 2004. Apparently, when we got there at Habitat, we were given a hostel room for a Hotel price. As they were fully booked, they only gave us a room that had 1 single bed, share communcal bathroom and toilet, no wardrobe space. Obviously we got cheated.The refused to refund our money although we booked like months earlier for a bigger room. It was disgusting! We decided to look around for another hotel with reasonable pricing and came upon Hotel Carter. It was located exactly on Times Square area next to Westin Hotel near the Ball-Drop(televised on ABC, CBS etc). We got a room for $130 with 1 king size and 1 queen- enough room for 5 people.
BAD PARTS:- 1) Bulb in room broke out of a sudden without warning. 
2) Had to change rooms because of faulty bulb 3) Bell boy told us Carter was previously an old hospital for crazy people and has been renovated into a budget hotel, told us some ghost stories before we even settled in!!! 
4) The bed leg was supported by 2 thick yellowpages book- but it did fine. 
5) This hotel is very old, creaking noises 6) Boiler for hot water spoilt the 1st night we were there- had to bath in ice cold water! (Due to NEW YEAR overload of usage) 7) The bathroom door cannot close and cannot be locked
GOOD PARTS: 1) Service is good- jst tip the bell boy with $5-10 and he'll do lots of things for you. For example he carried a modern TV from another room to our room, fixed everything in our room for us. 
2) It was huge and spacious for the price we paid! 
3) Other than the boiler problem, when it was fixed, there was plenty of hot water to go. 
4) The bed was comfortable, plenty of wardrobe space and the towels were clean. 
5) We had room service every morning, nothing was stolen! Our things were reaarranged for us in a nice, neat manner! 
6) There's a carpark below for Multiple in-out pass, for $30 a day- convenience.( Jst one guy who was nasty, the rest gave us multiple pass, jst have to argue abit and you'll get it. 
7) Grocery and burger shop below- get your water supplies 24 hours a day.
Overall, it was a pleasant stay if you're looking for budget pricing for comfortable sleep. Bear in mind though, stay in 14th floor, you will see no ghosts. Don't stay on 8th or 22nd floor- warning from bellboy, unless you're a ghost hunter.

title: “Outstanding hotel! Friendly atmosphere, great food and new friends...”
text: My wife joined me for a trip to a convention. She explored the area while I attended the meeting. We both loved the gourmet breakfast, and the afternoon wine and snacks. The chef was creative and provided lots of healthy, delicious choices. These events attract nearly all of the guests, many of whom were from out of the country while we were there. It was delightful! We made lots of new friends, and got tips about local "must see" restaurants and highlights. The staff was also extremely helpful. The rooms are charming, and the fireplaces a nice touch.

title: “Good, inexpensive choice”
text: We weren't sure what to expect with some of the negative reviews and even photos of bad areas. But all of the people who have stayed here for company business this week have been fine with the hotel. The rooms are small and dated...but all were clean. No bugs. No mold. No problems. The staff was pleasant and helpful. Breakfast was also just fine. Be careful at night when walking around the neighborhood. If you want an inexpensive hotel in the downtown LA area, and aren't picky about it being brand new, this is your hotel.

title: “Outstanding hotel with convenient Airport service”
text: We live in the mountains west of Denver and frequently need overnight lodging before or after air travel on our trips. The Holiday Inn at Stapleton is the perfect place and has become our hotel of choice. They have covered parking for our car; a shuttle to/from the airport every half hour; reasonable rates; clean, fresh, modern rooms; and a wonderful staff. Last night on our return from a trip to the east coast, our plane was delayed in Chicago for over 5 hours making our arrival in Denver 2:30 am. The hotel shuttle service ends at mid-night but they told us to use a cab and they paid the entire cab fare. It just doesn't get better than that.

title: “Good location”
text: Located over the road from Peabody hotel with it's famous ducks. Five minute walk from Beale street and the blues clubs.

title: “Lame!”
text:
I reserved a room with 2 double beds. When we checked in they gave us a room with one queen. I told them I'd reserved 2 beds and the lady was so rude - saying they didn't have any. She finally put us in a room with one King. We were early and couldn't check in yet - so we dropped our bags and when we came back later to pick up the key - they moved us back to a room with one queen. I complained again and they finally moved us to a room with a King again. I was staying with my Mom - I love her - but this was NOT ideal!
The staff was totally rude - the room had a huge stain on the carpet, a yucky shower, trash in the garbage can (that wasn't ours).
The only thing this hotel had going for it was the location.

title: “Wonderful Weekend Escape!”
text: My wife and I stayed here for a getaway from the kids and absolutely loved our experience. The room was beautifully appointed and spacious. The staff was very courteous and helpful. We enjoyed using the fitness center and the proximity to the waterfront. As the seaport district continues to grow, this hotel will become a must for visitors to Boston.

title: “beautiful room, great location, restful place”
text: I really liked staying here. My room (4B) was large, clean, and nicely decorated with a simple, meditative, clean feel. It had high ceilings, wood floors, great mouldings, super comfortable bed and sheets, candles, and a nice modern bathroom with a sauna-like option in the shower that was very relaxing, There was no TV and no phone, which is rare and a I really appreciate this decision -- it helps to break away from the stress, to focus on reading, writing, thinking, meditating (there is free wireless internet). I came on a warm summer night, and there were 4 or 5 interesting restaurants with packed outdoor seating within 2 blocks. There is a frozen kefir store right below -- delicious -- like frozen yogurt. There is a kitchen you can share on the 3rd floor, which is an unusual feature and nice if your staying for a few days. Basically, it was like staying at a friend's beautiful apartment in a great neighborhood. Publication transportation was great; a cab to North Michigan Avenue was $10 and 10 minutes, and I was able to flag one immediately in the morning.

title: “Great Respite from Tension”
text: I come from VA and need to be treated for eye cancer at Wills Eye Hospital in Phila. The Omni is the closest hotel to the hospital and they offer a discount. When we arrived, we circled up and down the one-way streets looking for parking--finally we followed the signs 6 blocks away and schlepped our bags to the hotel in a cloudburst. As soon as we came into the lobby looking helpless, a kind desk clerk ran to the fore to check us in and tell us of the parking garage right around the corner. Most cheery and welcoming! After a tiring day of travel and our cloudburst experience, my daughter and I decided to avail ourselves of the cushy provided bathrobes and order room service. What a treat! Her salad was great and my filet mignon was out of this world. Breakfast the next day was generous, too. The beds were very plush and comfortable. My only complaint was that after my medical procedure ended I wanted to take a nap, and every day at 3 pm sharp a fife and drum reenactment goes off across the street (we are in the tourist section!). I could have given the room a 5 for cleanliness, but its tiled tub/shower was old and a little stained in the grout--not active mildew, just older and stained. The soaps, however, were wonderful! Take them home with you! One other thing: I couldn't get the shower to produce anything but scalding hot water, so I gave myself a sponge bath and shampoo in the sink! Later my daughter explained that you have to crank the handle to the max, then back off to get the cooler temperature you want. I prefer showers to be a little more obvious! Nevertheless, my daughter and i had a very relaxing and lovely stay during some tense times.

title: “Best Hotel in Seattle”
text: I stay in Seattle a few times every month. I have had the opportunity to stay at several hotels on the Tripadvisor list, from cheap to boutique. For the money, the Hyatt Grand is the best deal. It has the nicest amenities and friendly staff. The hotel is excellently furbished and has a 24 hour gym.

title: “The Spa that's not worth it....”
text:
A friend and I had massages at the Spa at the Ballantyne Hotel. We were expecting a first class experience but had one that fell way short of our expectations.
The ambiance is austere - no art, no plants, dreadful lighting.
The locker room is small and cold - with no amenities and again, with horrid lighting.
The attendant that toured us around barely spoke English.
The hot tub by the indoor pool had it's jets set the wrong way, so the water simply shot up and out of the pool.
There was garbage by the whirlpool that no one had bothered to remove.
The relaxation area was poorly lit and not very relaxing - leatherette chaises without any blankets.
I had a decent masseuse, but my friend's service provider didn't know what she was doing.
For the cost of this place - it's just not a good, restful experience. Ambience counts and this was sorely lacking.
If you want to relax and be pampered, definitely look elsewhere!

title: “Grand-not so sure!”
text:
This hotel is one of the grand hotels of Chicago. Many a famous person has stayed here.
We stayed in a king deluxe room. I must say the room was laid out nicely. The fan for the
heat control ran constantly eventhough on auto setting. This made it hard to sleep because of the noise.The bathtub had mold around the
fixtures and when I closed the shower curtain closed, there was a strip of mold running down
the curtain. I think this grand old place deserves more care. I'm not sure if it was worth the money.

title: “It was ok...but expected a little better”
text: I stayed for two nights this past June (Friday and Saturday nights). My only interaction with an employee was at check-in. I was never greeted when coming back into the hotel. There was a separarte elevator for the roof deck bar. If people were heading there they were treated very nicely. The room was tiny- which was expected. I was bummed that my wireless connection did not work and I had to pay for the hotel's. Also while the bathroom was very nice and new, it had the loudest toliet flush I've ever heard. I jumped each time! Also, a lovely glass shower but no tub. I stayed here at a decent rate but if I had to pay high rates I might chose a different hotel. P.S. I did enjoy the cupcake treats at the front desk which were great!

title: “*** Stay Away FromThis Dump *****”
text:
I blame alot of how bad this place is on the New York city inspectors.Mold , Chipped paint,and broken furniture is all safety issues that should be issues for the inspectors to demand to be fixed.The hotel staff are rude.The bathroom is so small you will get the toilet paper roller stuck in your side if you weigh more them 125 pounds.I found hair and funk on the bathroom floor.The sink had missing hardware and rust,the carpet in the bedroom felt kind of damp but when I walked on it in my socks they just got dirty not wet. Valet parking cost 50.00 over night which you will have to use since there are no parking close.This was my first time in New York and I found it to be dirty and most people were friendly except for the people in the hotel..They show you the lobby which looks nice but as soon as you get off the elevator the adventure begins.
STAY AWAY FROM THIS PLACE

title: “DAV-DAVA National Convention”
text: Nice older hotel....small rooms, but 2 bathrooms....wonderful beds!

title: “Westin is my kinda hotel!”
text: A great location on the river. Close to subway and within walking distance to great restaurants and shopping! Great service. We stayed on the 17th floor in a roomy and comfortable room with free coffee breakfast, midday snacks, complimentary health club, a computer in the room with free wifi, and even a 10 min massage after my workout! The staff was friendly and helpful. They gave us a late checkout to accommodate our later flight home. This place would be perfect if it had a pool on the roof for those hot summer after shopping days!

title: “Great Little Hotel, Great Location”
text: This hotel has 81 rooms vs. the big guys at over 500. Not so crowded and quite lovely. The staff is exceptional and always there to help. The rooms with 2 queen beds quite big (room with King Bed small), but overall this is the place to stay. You are in walking distance to the main street and lots of restaurants. If you want quiet, cute and convenient, this is the place. They always had coffee and hot water in the a.m. and if you wanted to prebook breakfast, they gave a small discount if booked early. Be sure to book a trolley tour - its the best way to see the city

title: “Perfect location, beautiful hotel - cannot recommend it enough”
text:
We stayed at Hotel Vitale on the final leg of our honeymoon, having been to Vegas and Maui. The first thing that struck us was the location - it was perfect. Bang opposite the Bay Bridge and Pier 1, right in the heart of the financial district and equidistant between the centre of the city and Fisherman's Wharf.
We arrived at 6am on our flight so wanted to check in very early. When we got there we were offered an upgrade to a circular suite for $100 a night (having paid $100 a night for a deluxe room as part of our honeymoon offer) - so for just $200 (£133) we got an incredibly elegant suite with panoramic views of the harbour and bay bridge opposite, and got to check in eight hours early.
The room was beautiful, equipped with 32" LCD, auto-blinds, two i-pod docks, great bathroom facilities and adequate wardrobe space. The rest of the hotel is very modern, with superb staff always on hand to help with taxis, info and transfers. There is a very nice bar/restaurant area where we drank only briefly but the staff were kind enough to treat us to two rounds of free drinks for the final nights of our honeymoon. We also came back on the first day to find a free bottle of Champagne on ice in our room courtesy of the hotel. It is also directly opposite the superb Boulevard restaurant (seperate review).
I cannot recommend this place enough, no matter what reason you are staying in San Fran.

title: “Had a good time.”
text: A few friends decided we wanted to go to San Fran for a weekend. We have never been and I was looking for a hotel that was reasonably priced and close to union square. There was 4 of us that went. We are a younger crowd, 25-27 years old and looking for a good time. The chilled shots of Tequila at check in was a bonus! I believe the gentleman that checked us in was named Steven, want to give him big kudos! He was awesome! We spoke to him every time we passed him in the lobby. He was very friendly, always asked us about our days and nights out. He provided us great suggestions and was always smiling. He made us feel very welcomed from day 1 and through the trip. Our room was small but nice. We booked a 2 room suit, one king bed and one queen. Although the room was not huge it was fine for us. TVs in each room was nice, the painting on the ceiling and "Eagles" lyrics on the wall was nice also. The beds where super comfortable also. The area was nice also, very short walk to union square. We stayed out pretty late every night and always walked back to the hotel, we always felt safe. The Jones bar next door as a great outside area to have drinks and a bite to eat. We also enjoyed High Tide bar across the street, it was a dive bar with friendly bartenders. The hotel also had complimentary wine and cheese everyday. We enjoyed it our 2nd day there, it was a nice touch. Overall we enjoyed our stay at the hotel and would recommend it to others. Good time.

title: “OK for a night stopover”
text:
This is nothing flash, but then that's not what you are paying for. If you want somewhere that is clean, close to LAX airport with a free shuttle bus and somewhere half decent to eat nearby, then this is the place for you. If you want anything more than this, then you will be disappointed because you won't get it here.
We've stayed in a few LAX airport hotels now and this one (for the price) is the best so far. The shuttle was really easy to catch, the room was dated and a bit shabby with a really wierd shower in a hole in the bathroom wall, but it was quiet, easy to get to and from the airport and relatively clean.
The pool is deceptively deep and very clean but damned freezing! Having Denny's onsite is a real bonus but it's not the Hilton. If you have realistic expectations and want somewhere just to crash, then this is the place for you.

title: “Great location.....average hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Half Moon Inn for 4 days and coming from winter weather to San Diego was heaven! We were able to do alot of walking since we did not rent a car. We even caught the city bus very near the hotel to downtown and had no problem. The bikes were a fun addition to the hotel amenities so we took advantage and rode all along Shelter Island back and forth since the traffic was light through there. We walked to a couple different restaurants, Miguels (yummy), Red Sail Inn ( tried it twice and didn't like it much), The Living Room ( good lunch fare), Half Moon Inn Bar ( happy hour, 1/2 price drinks and off their 1st page menu). We were busy and outside most of the time, even sat by the pool and on our little lanai.
We did have to get another room right after we arrived because there were ants crawling on the coffee bar and wall plus my husband took a shower and the tub would not drain. It didn't seem to be a problem to get another room and the next room was a little more updated than the first. I could still smell kind of a musty smell upon entry to the room but it was clean, no ants, and the tub worked! Everyone seemed pleasant, especially Bill, always wanting to help. I think the hotel is just really old and even with some of the room "updates" there are moisture problems. The landscaping is beautiful, lots of mature palms, koi pond ( the biggest Koi I have ever seen), 2 parrots, very tidy grounds. It was nice to see the marinas, the bay, and to be able to walk around and not worry about safety. The airport is close by, the noise did not bother us, as the hotel filled up towards the end of our stay it got a little noisy, maybe best to get a second floor room. Hope this helps!

title: “Luxury at a price!”
text: Lovey accommodations , terrific service, good location... Cha Ching!! easy walk to the Marketplace at Pier one. No shortage of food places! try The Slanted Door for amazing Vietnamese cuisine. Right on cable car route. safe area.

title: “Nice Stay”
text: Our family of 4 stayed for 1 night. The room was clean, beds comfortable, and the breakfast was quite good. The eggs are a welcome addition to the breakfast options. The staff was professional. and treated us well.

title: “Great location!”
text: This hotel is located in a fantastic place for those people visiting Chicago for leisure purposes, and who wish to be close to tourist activities. The hotel is in a beautiful building and the inside of the hotel is quite lovely as well.

title: “Phenominal hotel”
text:
I have been staying at Embassy Suites with my parents since I was a little kid but this was my first trip as an adult. It had been a good amount of years and the only memory I had was the giant goldfish in the streams that run through the lobby. Well this trip will be one I will not soon forget.
Everyone at the hotel was extremely nice, and while it is a family hotel the manager's reception every evening is akin to a free 2 hour nightly open bar. By the end of our stay everyone who worked at the breakfast and the manager's reception knew both my name as well as my girlfriend's and our drink orders. Everyone was always nice and smiling and the concierge at the front desk was very knowledgable about the area.
It was nice to have a parking lot where we could park and forget about our car even if it was a little expensive, the free drinks and snacks as well as the free breakfast more than made up for it. Overall, not only a tremendous value but also a beautiful hotel. Even though I am in my mid 20's I partook in the goldfish feeding and had a great time. The metro was a few blocks away and a little confusing to get to the first time but the hotel was in a great location none the less. Highly recomended.

title: “We 'Love' This Place!!!”
text: My husband and I took our first NYC trip together in May 2004 to celebrate our anniversary, so expectations were high. It seemed we were playing "musical rooms" the first few days which put a damper on our plans, but were quickly accomodated by a very helpful staff. Our one bedroom suite was marvelous! Spacious, all amenities you could ask for, and a great view. The location was ideal, offering scenic walks and a quiet alternative to the more congested parts of Manhattan. One block west is Associated Supermarket which we found fulfilled our shopping needs. Can't forget the Zephyr Grill. Breakfast was fresh and delicious. Staying at the Beekman only sweetened our memorial occasion. We hope to return to New York soon and stay here once again.

title: “Labor Day Weekend Stay”
text:
The hotel is super clean and cozy. home away from home. The rooms are modern, ultra clean, and spacious. I loved the layout and the kitchen area was perfect. 
Our family really enjoyed the stay. The only problems was that we had booked two rooms but both were on two different floors. It was inconvienent since i had mentioned the request when booking the reservation. The other problem was hotel had a large group staying for a wedding who were selfish and would take up all the space during breakfast hours and would sit there chatting and making lots of noice the entire time. We had to take our breakfast up to our room the whole stay.They should have had separate eating area in one of the meeting rooms because lot of non-wedding guests were complaining. One late afternoon/evening we had the entire pool to ourselves, which was nice.

title: “Advoid at all costs!!!!”
text: Filthy room torn curtains shower faucet didn`t work no ac on 3rd floor hallways torn dirty carpeting. Mr Wright manager failed to return calls or respond to email corporate office could care less.

title: “Highly recommended”
text: I have yet to be disappointed with the Kimpton group of hotels. Check in and check out was a breeze. The room whilst a little small was clean and had wonderful views. Great food in the restaurant - we had breakfast and dinner there a couple of times. Staff were very friendly, helpful and courteous. I will definitely stay there again when I next visit LA. Heading off to a Kimpton in San Francisco - hope it is as good as the Palomar!

title: “Overall Pretty Good”
text:
The hotel had everything we were looking for a 3 night break in NY:
-Excellent location in the heart of midtown Manhattan
-Clean and comfortable room. Bed was huge and very comfortable, AC efficient and quiet. Room was bigger than expected but the bathroom was tiny.
-Staff helpful when required although did have one bad experience with a porter when collecting left luggage who was unhappy with not being tipped despite doing absolutely nothing other than unlocking a door
-Extras (eg breakfast and room service) were totally overpriced but there are coffee shops/off-license(liquor store) on the block

title: “Great Location + Great service = Happy Traveler”
text:
I based my selection on the numerous positive reviews I had read, although I tried to keep my expectations reasonable, considering some of the reviews indicating the rooms were small. 
The hotel was a very reasonable walk from the BART station close to the Ferry Building. We checked in and everyone at the hotel seemed very accommodating. We got there before noon due to our early flight, but managed to check into our room, which was great, since our feet were tired.
The evening reception was a very nice touch. I was afraid things might be too rowdy (I'm in my 30s, but still enjoy some peace and quiet on a vacation!), but the ambience was nice. 
A welcome note was provided by the housekeeping staff, which made us feel at home and added a very nice personal touch. Often times, housekeeping at big hotels can seem cold and unwanting to help and often intrude during blissful sleep. Not on this trip!
The location is great, as the Bay Bridge is right across the street and provides a great view at night. You can also take a short walk to the Ferry Building, where you can hop on the railcar to Fisherman's Wharf or the Aquarium. Or, you can even walk to Market St. and hop on the underground rail, BART, cable car or bus and practically go anywhere.
By the way, yes, the rooms are not the largest, but it worked out great for me and my girlfriend. The room was nicely decorated and I did not have any problems with the 'coziness' of the room. In fact, it's makes it easier to go from the bed to the desk, bathroom, etc.

title: “Great Location, nice historical hotel”
text:
My family and a group of friends booked The Menger as part of our weekend escape to San Antonio. Overall our experience was positive. We booked a Deluxe 2 Queen bed room with pool view (2103) and we found the room to be quite spacious, especially since we needed extra room for our baby's play-pen.
The bathrooms were a little dated and a bit small, but we didn't have any issues with it.
The location is superb, across the street from The Alamo and the River walk Mall, easy access to the main attractions in downtown San Antonio.
We used the hotel valet which was $25 (In and out privileges). There are other parking options at around $10, however, the clock starts at 4AM, so we were going to pay $20 outside. I thought the valet at the hotel was worth the extra $5.
We recommend this hotel for your visit to San Antonio, but realize this is a historical hotel, so if you enjoy modern/new construction and amenities, you may be better served elsewhere.

title: “Modern elegance. Beautiful rooms and ambiance.”
text: Two adults and three children stayed in adjoining rooms. Got $98 price on priceline for each room - great bargain! Spacious and elegant. Wonderful staff. Close to sites.

title: “fantastic experience”
text:
Outstanding service . Although the location is not in the heart of Beverly Hills the hotel provides a courtesy car within 2 miles ,so even if you don't have a car you can shop and enjoy a lot of great restaurants,because there are a lot in the area,including Rodeo Drive!!!.
The rooms are not big but are confortable .The hotel decor is absolutely beautiful.Even being a city hotel there are a lot of green areas ,beautiful flowers everywhere inside and outside. The bar and the restaurant are amazing and good choice of food.It was really a wonderful experience and the best was really the outstanding staff.

title: “You Get What You Pay For (or less)”
text: Booked for 3 nights; reluctantly stayed for 1. Nasty, dirty accommodations. Obviously houses long-term "residents". Would not be a good value even at 1/2 the price, and I would have grave concerns brining my family/small children to this place. Guests hanging over the railings smoking at all hours of the day and night. While it's true you don't come to San Antonio to stay in your hotel room, you still shouldn't dread coming back to it to rest in the evenings. Before you check in here, drive past the downtown Red Roof Inn and see what you get for about $5 a night more than this place. I was glad I moved and would recommend that anyone considering this place do the same. Good location...for drug dealers and prostitutes -- not families on vacation.

title: “Out of the way”
text: Stayed for a video game convention in the spring. It was a nice hotel with a good view however it was not that close to anything convenient. I felt like once we got back to the hotel that it was a chore to go back out for basics. We loved the warm cookies and room service was ok. The hotel had a nice view of the skyline but was very noisy from the street. One needed to understand the bus/subway system before traveling to the city!

title: “Great hotel, great location.”
text: Great hotel. Staff very friendly. Concierge, Judy, very helpful. We arrived prior to check in time so there wasn't a room ready. They blocked a great room for us on the corner of the 30th floor. Fantastic view down 6th avenue. Would definitely return to this hotel for our next NYC visit!

title: “HORRIBLE staff - STAY AT YOUR OWN RISK”
text:
This is the worst hotel in downtown Chicago. The rooms are ok (nothing great), they were remodeled and is now modern instead of classic. However, the service (staff) was ABSOLUTELY the worst. When I mean the worst, is something worst than Super 8. 
I called to the front desk because my remote control was missing and the espresso machine was broken. I got transferred to the kitchen. The lady had a really bad attitude and was even screaming at me. The coffee and remote control arrived over an hour later to my room and I even had to call twice to get them.
Fairmont? No thanks, never again. I rather stay at Hilton, Starwood hotels, or Marriott.

title: “Wonderful, accomodating & great location”
text: My church family & I stayed at this hotel July 22-25, 2010. First Ms. Gina was great & worked with us to accomodate us on everything. The rooms were nice & clean & the staff was friendly & helpful. They do not have a conference room which we were looking for to have Sunday morning service & they went above & beyond to allow us to have it in their lobby. I cannot thank them enough & if we are in San Antonio again we would definately stay at this location again. Oh & by the way....the price was GREAT as well!!!!

title: “Great conference hotel”
text: Haven't been to Dallas in many years. Was there for a 4-day business conference. Sheraton Dallas was great: great conference space and service were standouts. Room was spacious, modern, furnishings seemed new. Lots of thought put into the business traveler for internet access and electric outlets near the desk, great TV including ability to plug in to a computer. Restaurants are pretty good, and because of the bland dining choices in the area, these were welcome.

title: “very friendly -- good business hotel”
text: I stayed here based on the recommendation of one of my colleagues. Was upgraded to club level and breakfast was excellent. room was quiiet and staff very friendly. I highly recommend

title: “A lovely haven amongst the madness........”
text:
The hotel is fairly small by New York standards which appealed to us. The location is about a 5 minute walk from Times Square and about a 10 -15 minute walk to Central Park. 
The hotel itself is very smart and the room was luxurious. The bathroom had a lovely large shower and bath, it was modern and stylish. There is free Wi-fi in the room which I thought was excellent, about time Starwood caught up with this!
Check in was very efficient, not overly friendly, but efficient. They have a well equipped gym. The Concierge made us laugh as we were trying to ask him tourist type questions he really couldn't be bothered with us! Fortunately, we saw the funny side! 
I noticed a lot of corporate guests so I would say this is probably a very popular business hotel.
We felt safe here and enjoyed the peace the hotel gave us from all the fantastic New York chaos outside.
Taxi from JFK cost $55.00 plus tip.
We would stay here again.

title: “Good place to spend a night after driving”
text: Stopped here as the family was tired from driving 1200 miles in a day. Bed was comfortable, room was clean, parking was easy and plenty of spaces. Booked the room from Marriotts App on Ipad while driving, showed up 15 minutes later and had room ready and available. Check in was quick(10pm). Good nights sleep and quick exit to finish drive the next morning. Didn't use any hotel ammenities, or local estabolishments. Hotel was quiet at night for sleeping. Hotel is blocks off of I-95

title: “Loved it!”
text:
I stayed here for 4 nights when in Seattle for a wedding. After a 30+ hour trip from Australia it was heaven.
The bed was huge and comfy, the bathroom beautiful and the staff really helpful and friendly. The room was very clean, and linen and towels changed daily.
Not the mention the great location... If ever in Seattle do not hesitate to stay here or recommend it to someone else!

title: “Modern & chic in a great location!”
text: A great hotel! Clean, with modern decor and a perfect downtown location, within walking distance to the Magnificent Mile and great restaurants. The rooms were clean and comfortable, with lovely beds and amenities. The staff we dealt with were friendly and courteous; the concierge even got us dinner reservations at a top restaurant! Highly recommended, I'd definitely stay there again.

title: “Great”
text: If you are in New York you wont regret going here. great location great service and very clean. when i am back i will stay here again. Decent sized rooms for New York City. near the subway too. The bathroom was small but clean. pleasantly suprised, staff so helpful.

title: “Hotel was great we will definitely come back”
text:
It was our second time in Sofitel Beverly LA
great hotel in front of beverly center !!!
exellent service and the breakfast was great !!!
We stayed in a prestige suite,the room was large and really nice
we enjoyed this hotel and will recommend it definitely

title: “Boutique hotel with great value!”
text: I was reading the reviews because I am thinking about staying here again. I was pleasantly surprised by the Marrakech. I had a lovely corner room with nice tall windows. I agree with other readers that I slept better than I did at home. The staff is very attentive - I had a few reasons to call down for service. In addition to being prompt they also tried several ways to troubleshoot a problem with the message indicator in my hotel room. I have traveled the world on business and pleasure and have stayed in many different style lodgings from hostels to 5 star resorts. Yes, the Marrakech is in an older building and there is no lift but that did not detract from my stay. As a single woman I felt safe in the hotel.

title: “Good Hotel, But Not Great”
text: Hotel is exceptional is some ways but then lacks the finer details to earn a great review from me. First the positives: great rooms that are very clean, modern and large by NY standards; hotel is centrally located within walking distance to Central Park, Fifth Avenue, Broadway and Times Square. Downside, lack of attention to detail. When I travel with my family we normally get two connecting rooms. The London does not offer connecting rooms so we confirmed through reservations that we could have rooms that were next to each other. At check-in, they had us on the same floor but not next to each other and given that the hotel was soldout by the time we checked-in, there was nothing they could do. So much for a confrimation from reservations. Also, we normally use the AMEX fine hotel and resorts program which includes a complimentary breakfast with the room rate. The breakfast offered by the hotel is a simple, cold continental breakfast which is valued at $28 on the menu. When I tried to substitute the cold buffet for pancakes valued at $22 on the menu, they would not allow any substitutions -- hotel policy according to the waiter when I protested. To be a great hotel, the hotel needs to value each guest as an individual. In the case of the London, they don't do that.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Beautifully furnished, very clean, courteous employees, located in the Persian rug district far enough away from the crowds and craziness, and yet centrally located in Manhattan minutes from everything. Would definitely recommend!

title: “Great Rate, Comfortable Room & Central Location!”
text:
I have business meetings in Grapevine Texas so I went on Priceline to bid on a hotel room. I selected a four star hotel in the DFW area and ended up getting the Grand Hyatt DFW for just $56.00 per night! I was a bit concerned at first because I really didn't want to stay AT THE DFW AIRPORT, I was hoping to be close to the airport.
I was pleasantly surprised how convienently located this hotel is to the American Airlines terminal. You literally pull your bag off the carusel and take an escolator up to the lobby. My double queen bedded room is clean, smells fresh and feels like it was renovated in the last couple of years. Comforatble beds, spacious bathroom, 36 inch LCD TV and a large desk to work at. T-Mobile broadband internet service is $9.95 for 24 hours. Parking is free for guests of the hotel in the DFW garage.

title: “Fabulous location, trendy & fun, even better service!”
text:
I met a couple of my girlfriends for a girls weekend in NYC. We opted to stay at the Gansevoort Park after hearing about its location and great service. Everything we heard was correct!
The upscale hotel is modern with trendy decor and clean furnishings. My girlfriends and I stayed in a suite that featured an incredibly comfortable atmosphere for us to enjoy ourselves for the weekend. Suite was very spacious with a half bath, a living room/lounge, and a large bedroom with en-suite bath (that has tons of great goodies inside!). Our view of the empire state building was amazing and we also had a large balcony to enjoy some fresh air.
We ended up arriving a bit early and they were able to hold our bags while we grabbed some lunch and then called me as soon as our room was ready (which ended up being earlier than expected!). Once we settled in, we had to buzz guest services several times for random items we forgot or needed throughout the weekend and they delivered everything very timely. 
Also loved the rooftop bar/club! Great crowd and it was very nice being able to cut the line that looped around the corner outside since we were guests of the hotel. 
Overall great trip. Would recommend for a weekend get-away, business, friends, or family. Can't wait to go back for another stay!

title: “Comfortable, convenient, relaxing place in a great DC location”
text: I always stay here when I travel to DC for business, and I have had nothing but great experiences. The hotel staff are always very friendly and the rooms are in great condition. The location could not be better with Union Station a few blocks away, Chinatown down the street, and great areas to walk or run along the National Mall. This place is highly recommended!

title: “Unfortunate Restaurant Odor”
text:
I was excited to stay at the Trump SoHo for two reasons; one being the location and the other being able to experience a Trump Hotel for only $288/nt. 
The first impression was ruined by a cooking odor, which I'm assuming came from the restaurant next door. The cooking smells continued all the way up the elevator and into the corridors. Thank God it was almost non existent in the room or I would have checked out. 
The room was nice, the bed quite comfortable and I loved the large window! 
Despite the first impression, the hotel was nice. However, it definitely does not come close to the luxury brands such as The Four Seasons and The Mandarin Oriental making it far too expensive at the going rate of $600/nt and up.

title: “We loved our stay here!”
text:
This is a great hotel. It is clean, well staffed and had a pleasing atmosphere. The staff were SUPER friendly and we felt like very valued guests. The weight room and pool were nice and we made use of both during our stay. The restaurant on the 17th floor has wonderful views and offered a pleasant, upscale place to hang out for drinks at the end of the day. However, we found the menu a bit ultra modern; we like more traditional fare.
This hotel is right next to Interstate 405, but the slight noise did not bother us. The only minor drawback was that it was not within walking distance to any other restaurants or pubs, so we could not stray very far without a costly cab ride back.
We highly recommend this hotel, but suggest renting a car for easy transport to all that LA has to offer.

title: “Excellent - but......”
text: .....don't take room 702 without checking the balcony door has been repaired. We just thought it was regular New York street noise until the last morning of a 10 night visit when I realised the door didn't seal correctly, which certainly gave us a few disturbed nights. A note to Peter Velk, the General Manager has had no response, which is disappointing when he emails to solicit a positive review here. But saying that, the hotel is great, the staff are great and the location is great. We stayed at the Casablanca last year which we also enjoyed.

title: “Welcoming Place”
text: High School Graduation gift to our son was a trip to any State that he wanted to go. He chose Washington DC. After looking at their website, we selected the Hilton Garden Inn DC/Capitol. The staff at the hotel made us feel so welcomed. The rooms were clean and comortable. It was a good location in walking distance of Union Station and siteseeing bus transportation. It also had a really nice grocery store located next door.

title: “Excellent hotel!! Can't wait to go back!!!”
text: First, thank you to Mr. John Keller for referring us to such a great hotel! We arrived at this wonderful hotel on the lower east side and were greeted immediately by great staff that were very helpful. We were several hours early, and Mr. Ted Mark was great at checking us in, even though we were so early! The check in process was very quick and easy. We arrived in our room and were very impressed with the comfortable room and breathtaking views. Within a few minutes Mr. Mark called and offered us an upgrade to an amazing two bedroom, two bathroom, private terrace suite. The suite was amazing!! The views were wonderful, the accomadations were amazingly stylish and comfortable, and the excellent service continued throughout our stay. We were sad that we weren't staying longer!! The breakfast we enjoyed at the Co-Op resteraunt attached to the hotel was also perfect!! We can not wait to return!!! Thank you Mr. Mark for making our trip so memorable!

title: “Location Location Location”
text: The Hotel is very impressive and the staff are extremely helpful. I booked a 2 x double bed room for myself and two adult size kids however only two pillows were supplied. The porter said he'd have one to us immediately but it never arrived (it was our first night after a long transatlantic journey and I was too tired to go looking). I left a message next day and another pillow was there when we returned to the room. The mini bar and table top "weight" controlled tray were very well stocked, too well stocked and a great temptation but prices were ridiculous - $11.98 for a bottle of water!!! Even if you pick something up and put it back you will be charged. I felt tea and coffee making facilities would have been an advantage but it seemed not a lot was "complimentary. Also the room was small enough for three adults. Having said that the staff in the hotel were extremely nice and very helpful, nothing was too much trouble. The room was spotlessly clean and the beds were turned down each night. I did feel they were small doubles though. Would I stay here again? If I became very rich and didn't have to budget then yes.

title: “A lot to like, but...”
text:
There's a lot to like about the Washington Circle Hotel. Spacious, modern-ish, comfortable rooms (we had a one bedroom suite), great location for business or tourism, a friendly staff that tries to provide a pleasant experience, fair price for what you get. The rooms have a "functional" kitchen and we were able to prepare simple meals during our extended stay of three weeks. 
On the other hand, there is one huge negative that the hotel can't really control and that is street noise. The hospital shares Washington Circle with a major hospital with an active emergency room. It is also one block away from a fire station. Rush hour traffic backs up in the circle and Washington drivers are prolific car horn honkers. So be prepared for a lot of traffic noise and siren activity all hours of the day. If you're looking for quiet, this is not the hotel for you. No room location is really immune. 
The other major negative for this hotel is a wireless internet room set-up that makes AT&T's 3G network seem speedy. If you have any need other than email, you are going to be very, very frustrated. 
The hotel has a restaurant which is moderately expensive and living a bit on its laurels having won a Washington top 100 award in 2007. The bar however, is cozy with a fireplace and comfortable seating. 
All in all, the hotel served our needs.

title: “A Great Place to Stay”
text: We stayed at the Comfort Suites Thousand Oaks for three nights, 14-16 October 2011. The room was well maintained, and the breakfast was great. We have stayed at this motel numerous times over the years, and have never had any problems. A flat-screen tv was added since our last stay. We did not stay there during a Memphis visit last April after reading bad reviews on this website. However, this time we decided to give the motel another chance. We found the motel to be at the same high level of service and comfort that we have experienced previously. If you are looking for reasonably priced, comfortable accommodations, this is a great stay to stay.

title: “Great location for tourists”
text:
My boyfriend and I recently stayed here for 3 nights on our visit to Chicago. Upon check-in, we were told that all of the non-smoking rooms had been given away, so we received an "upgrade" to a room on the 15th floor. The view was great, facing north on Michigan Ave towards Magnificent Mile. The room was clean and modern with a comfortable bed. It was very quiet, and we never heard other guests through the walls or were bothered by the cleaning service. The cable on our TV was not working, apparently due to the stormy weather. The woman at the front desk let us pick a movie instead for free, though it abruptly turned off 3/4 of the way through. 
The location was great and within walking distance of Millennium Park, Grant Park, Art Institute of Chicago, Magnificent Mile, and much more. It was also within walking distance of 3 different pick-up stops for the Hop-On Hop-Off tour, which we used to get around all 3 days. The employees working at the concierge desk were extremely helpful and friendly! The day we checked out, we saw that we were charged $150 for the minibar because we had removed a few items to store our leftovers. The issue was easily resolved, and we were refunded the money. Overall, great location, nice rooms, friendly staff but a few too many incidents of inconvenience for the price we paid. Next time I am in Chicago, I will look for another hotel in the area.

title: “No so Grand”
text:
Let me start out by saying I am a Hyatt Platinum member and generally a big fan of Hyatt Hotels. Second, this hotel is in a GREAT location attached to Grand Central Station and close to all of Manhattan.
That is where the compliments end. This is a really old hotel that was refreshed with new furniture and beds but they did a half fast job. The walls needed to be ripped to the studs and redone from the 1980's stucco but they didn't even bother to repaint. Doors and walls were nicked and in bad need of paint. Next, the hotel bar was a cave and not a nice place to sit and order $17 drinks (although they are building a new bar. I was staying on a free promotional night so I can't totally complain but I was disappointed at free so I would ahve been annoyed to pay the $300 nightly rate for a Holiday Inn equivalent. It is really disappointing that this is the only Hyatt location in midtown. I expected better from Hyatt.

title: “Worth every penny!”
text: Having had terrible experience at Sheraton time square a couple of weeks ago, really didn't expect too much from this one which is even closer to time square. Turned out it is truly an Intercontinental. Standards are not a bit compromised because of the location (some hotels actually think their locations could make up for lousy facility and service). Stayed for three nights. Room was of good size and decor and spotlessly clean; well proportioned bathroom and nice amenities; great services throughout the stay. Most important of all, the bed was heavenly. Will definitely come again.

title: “A Little Gem”
text:
In recent years La Quinta Inns and Suites have become our default choices for accommodation, offering comfortable and affordable lodging and generally catering to all our needs.
The hotel in Mission Bay is a little gem. The staff could not have been more helpful. It is managed by a young, energetic and friendly couple who went out of their way to make our stay memorable. Restaurant and sight-seeing suggestions were spot-on and the hotel location is conducive to both.
The hotel is currently undergoing some renovation but this did not detract from our stay in the least. We would have no hesitation in recommending it to any age demographic and will certainly use it again on future trips to San Diego.

title: “Good value, great location”
text: This hotel/hostel is a great place to stay on the upper west side convenient for everything. bit of chaos at reception at all times but aint no thang. Dino Carlucci

title: “Best Hotel to Stay in San Francisco”
text: My husband and I just stayed for 2 nights in the Argonaut. This is the best hotel we have ever stayed in. The staff, decor, rooms and service were all exceptional. As for location you could not ask for better. You are right in the thick of things, with no noise disturbance. The hotel is right beside the famous tram line, 10 mins walk from Pier 39 (well worth a visit) and from where you get the boat to visit Alcatraz.. Behind the hotel you can get a trip where you ride on a restored fire enine across the Golden Gate Bridge - this was the highlight of our trip [--]. Finally if you are looking for a fabulous breakfast go to Mama's - you will probably have to queue but it is so worth the wait. Enjoy your trip.

title: “Charming”
text: My husband and I were visiting Austin to attend a performance at UT. We found the old world charm of the Double Tree Austin lovely. The furnishings in the sitting areas off the lobby are reminiscent of another time and were a great place to visit. We had a king-size room and found it to be amply large enough for the two of us. The bed was very welcoming and comfortable at the end of the day. The inner courtyard was beautiful with the 2 levels and we even witnessed the end of a wedding from the balcony. Although this hotel is located right on a busy freeway, we heard absolutely no road noise to disturb us. There are several restaurants within walking distance of the hotel (Papadeaux's, Papasito's, Fuddruckers, just to name a few) and the hotel has a restaurant as well. We only sampled the hotel restaurant for breakfast, but found the buffet to be wonderful. The check-in was friendly and fast and the cookies were wonderful.
