The parking was a bit confusing on arrival if you were not using the valet. My suggestion is to pull through past the valet stand and check-in before parking. Also, request an odd numbered room. These face the courtyard with double doors leading to the shared balcony. You can't beat the view. The extra charges are a bit much for what you are already paying for the room. Movies started at around $10, games were around $7 for 2 hours, and the internet was a bit much. Parking was a problem if anyone were to visit you since they have only the pay to park garage. These were only minor annoyances overall. I would stay there again and recommend it. If you expect to be pampered every minute and waited on hand and foot, go somewhere else. If you want a comfortable bed, pleasant service, and old world elegance, reserve a room at the Double Tree Austin!

title: “In love with NYC and the Casablanca Hotel”
text: My partner and I recently traveled to NYC to get married. We decided on this hotel for our special occasion based on tripadvisor reviews... the reviews could not have been more accurate! We are absolutely in love with this hotel and NYC. The staff at the Casablanca could not have done anything more to make us feel welcome and accommodated - they went out of their way to make our special day even more special. John, the General Manager, was especially fantastic and deserves a special mention... as do the great cheese and wine evenings : ) We are so impressed that we have already planned our return in April. We would never consider staying anywhere else......

title: “Great Location but price paid was not equal to service and quality”
text:
Stayed four nights at the W Union Square. Booked in with the Starwood free weekends promotion so only paid for two of the nights. That said, I felt the stay wasn't worth paying two nights at the 450 dollar rate, much less four. This was my first visit to New York City so I have no other hotels to compare it to but when I have stayed with the Starwood brand at St Regis for half the price I've been treated much better and the accommodations have been nicer.
Location: Union Square was a great location. Honestly, I choose to stay with Starwood on this trip because I had earned two free weekend nights and I choose this W because of the location in Union Square.
Doorman: These folks were not a very welcoming bunch. I guess I'm just not a hip enough chick for them. I finally got so fed up with the attitude, especially that of Frankie, that I spoke with the manager, if for nothing else but to make me feel better. I don't appreciate getting treated like scum of the Earth. I would ask about the house car and he'd be put out. I'd ask for a direction and he'd be put out. I'd ask if we could get a cab and he'd say sure and motion to the street. he was horrible, but the others were indifferent.
Checkin: Was the quickest ever. Just need to see id and credit card, here's your key. No nicey nice-no do you know your way around....nothing. When I was at St Regis Monarch beach last week not only did I pay half the price, even with free nights, but the staff were welcoming and a doorman led me to the room and helped me with my bags.
Room: I had called ahead and asked for a quiet room. My husband is a Gold member and we were upgraded to the third tier of rooms-not a suite, a corner room on the 18th. It was quiet the first two nights but the hotel was full on the weekend and you could hear the guests in the room next to us, people talking in the hall, etc. You could also hear tv's, hair dryers, etc. The room was a good size but it was pretty basic. There was nothing special about the bed. I even looked under the sheets and it was just a regular mattress. The sheets were better than standard. The desk and bedside table both had a sticky substance on them.
Bathroom: This was quite standard. I was very disappointed with the towels-they were like grungy old gym towels, not luxury or fluffy. There was only one robe so I had to call down and ask for one for my husband. I have a huge pet peeve when there is not soap for both the sink and the bath as was the case. I called down and requested another bar and it was left in the room. They were very stingy with the Bliss bath products. There were two of us and they only gave little bottles once a day. Now it was very hot in New York City. I'd take a shower to get ready in the morning, rinse off at mid day and then shower before bed. We never had enough product but they never replendished at night. 
WiFi-I'm so sick of WiFi charges in rooms. For the price I paid it should be free! I did go down to the lobby, or as W calls it the living room, and got on the free WiFi. 
Lobby Bar-I think this is still the part they call the living room. We did have tasty tator tots and drinks there. And the server was nice. HUGE plus!
Whenever/Whatever: Or as I like to call it, What a joke. Any time I called they acted like I was putting them out. And I didn't even ask for a bathtub of hot chocolate as the silly W ad states. I just needed simple things, like a toothbrush since I left one behind, a bar of soap for the sink, security to quiet my rowdy neighbors so I could have a decent night sleep, a wakeup call.
All in all, the location was great but I wouldn't stay at this property or probably any other W again. I don't need people reminding me that I'm not hip and cool. In fact, I'm prefectly happy that I'm not their target consumer.

title: “Excellent Location -- North Michigan Ave”
text:
This hotel is in a great location; 60 seconds to N. Michigan Ave, 120 seconds to Nordstroms. Great cafes and restaurants within one or two blocks. Lake Michigan and Navy Pier about five blocks east. 
The hotel itself. Ok, so it was built in the 1920's. The bedrooms are small and so are the bathrooms. For anyone who has stayed in a hotel in Europe, this will be very familiar. Just how big of a bathroom does anyone need? More room would have been nice but not necessary. Some rooms are bigger than others. I think we were a little fortunate to get a corner king room that had windows on two sides and great views, and was a little bigger and more comfortable. So if more room is what you need, ask for room 2025, or other corner rooms.
Condition of the room. Average, to above average but not outstanding. Certainly clean but a little worn. Nothing that a little money wont cure.
Front desk. Below standard. Friendly but not knowledgeable about their own hotel's policies and practices. Three different people gave me three different stores on the parking fees. One said that the self park was part of the room rate which I found out was wrong. The bellhops and valets were very helpful and knowledgeable. The front desk staff definately needs training.
I'd guess your opinion of the hotel would also vary depending on the prices paid for the room. In just looking at November 2007, the prices for a deluxe gueen room, will vary from $71 a night to $539. At $71 it is an absolute and amazing bargain. At $200 a night you are still doing very well. At $539 its well over priced for what you get. They are pricing for the market they are in. If you are flexible on your dates, you can get a marvelous bargain. If you get stuck with a $539 price, you will feel cheated for the value received. 
My definition of a boutique hotel is one that is special and almost perfect. This one is very good but no gold ring. However its certainly satisfactory. The room air conditioning was not all that noisy, certainly not more noise than the average hotel room. But it can use some minor freshening up, and front desk staff training. The concierge could be more friendly. 
The point is go enjoy Chicago. You will be in a wonderful and fun filled area. Use every minute.

title: “Weekend stay”
text:
Our stay was a total disappointment. I booked and paid for a king room for a 3 night stay. On arrival at 7pm I was told they only had a double room left. In addition I was told there would be a $150 charge to my credit card, $50 per day for incidentals so the clerk said we should be sure to charge any meals to our room since it would come off the $150.The desk clerk was also very apologetic and said we could try to get a king room the next day. He gave us 4 free breakfast buffet tickets (there were 2 of us) to use during out stay. 
The door frame to our room was nearly falling off. The room was freezing cold and the AC/Heating unit didn't work. The TV didn't work either. The maintenance man was very nice and did fix the TV and had to exchange the entire AC unit for a working one. The next day we had lunch at the bar. Trash and gross liquids from the buffet were brought and emptied in front of us as we ate at the bar. It was disgusting. When going for the breakfast buffet I was told I couldn't eat in the restaurant because I had a free coupon, therefore I had to eat in the banquet room which was uncomfortable especially since I was alone. I tried to call the wake up call line and it was continually busy so I called the desk and requested a 5:30 wake up call. No one ever called. When checking out the clerk told me to expect the $150 to come off my credit card in a week or so. I said the $60 we spent at the restaurant should come off that and she said it didn't work that way. I explained what we were initially told and she said that was wrong. The charge is like a deposit not an account to use. I had much higher expectations especially as a rewards member. The next time we are in Jacksonville which will be in February, we will not stay at the Wyndham.

title: “Clift is nice place thanks to redwood bar. Rooms are not good.”
text:
I like clift because many people stop there for a drink. Redwood is always crowd, service is great. But the rooms are not good for 5star. I stayed last time in normal room and this time in suite. Rooms are acceptable, bathrooms are really old.
Would not stay there for more than 2 days.

title: “pillows rated for softness...”
text:
I don't think I've ever stayed at a hotel where the pillows are rated for softness- but there was the rating, embroidered on the pillow case! A choice of soft or firm, and I could feel the difference. 
We had an emergency trip to Texas & had to overnight in San Antonio before our flight home the next morning. We found the Holiday Inn Express in a coupon book we picked up in a tourist center. The price was right, as was the proximity to the Riverwalk so we decided to stay. The hotel is located on a side street off one of the major routes through town (Commerce?) on the periphery of the Riverwalk area, near the colonial governors mansion. 
Our room was a corner room on the third floor facing the street- one of the rooms with the bars from the jail still on the window. The layout was different; we entered the room, took a dogleg right past a coffee nook and the bathroom to get to the sleeping area. The ceiling in the entry way was standard height; in the sleeping area the ceiling was about 12 foot, with the air conditioner located on the wall between the two ceilings. The room was outfitted with a king size bed, end table with clock radio, desk with hard wired internet access (wifi also available), TV with cable access, a mini-refrigerator and microwave. The decorations were simple and elegant- the sole exceptions being the mirrored closet door (which was off its hinges; we notified the front desk and it was repaired quickly) and a window valence that looked like it was hastily repaired. 
The bed was very comfortable; not as firm as mine at home, but not as soft as the pillow I chose. The linens were soft and the comforter light. It was easy to figure out how to set the alarm on the clock radio for our early wake-up (we also asked and received a wake-up call from the front desk). The wifi connection was similarly easy and fast. The air conditioner chilled the room nicely- and quietly. Our room was very quiet- no noise from the adjacent room or nearby streets. The interstate is a few blocks away, and I could not hear it. 
Clean bathrooms are important to me- and this one was spotless. It took me a moment to figure out how to adjust the showerhead, but once I did the flow was nice and powerful. 
Parking is available across the street or at the hotel. The rate for the hotel is higher. I would recommend parking across the street, as the lot at the hotel looked tricky to maneuver. The hotel also has a very small pool and jacuzzi- the size of the pool is really the size of a large jacuzzi. I did not partake, but my partner enjoyed a quick dip.
I cannot rate the breakfast; we were up and out the door before breakfast service started. 
Do take a look in the business center to see the articles on the criminals that were housed or hanged when the hotel was a prison, and ask for the flyer about the hotel's history at the front desk. 
For a budget trip to San Antonio I would definitely stay at the Holiday Inn Express again.

title: “Clean, nice area, great value.”
text: I stayed in this hotel, actually the same room, twice this past trip. It was clean and pretty quiet. It was a nice green area with nice sidewalks and areas to walk the dog. The staff was very nice and the room was clean and smelled nice. I am soo happy with Red Roof's 'No Smoking' policy. My room did not have a microwave but there is one available in the vending area if you are trying to go really cheap with meals. My only complaint, no hair dryer, otherwise I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Think twice before you book...”
text:
My Wife and I travel all over the country each month so we are far from novice travelers.
We where in LA for a convention at Convention Center which once we got there was way to far away.
Having grown up in the area was interested in seeing what Starwood/Westin had done with the hotel.
We got a late flight from LAX and checked in late about 11p very tired we where sent to a standard room that was so tight we could not fit!
Back to the lobby the FC agent told the night manager who went up to check the next room and never came down personally to say the room was fine he just called the front counter.
So up we went only to be told it was under construction (literally) dry wall dust everywhere, grout all over bathroom, shower was still taped up and oh need I mention no TV not even connected? 
We did sleep in the room only to be placed in a suite the next day but it was already to late.
Staff was ok, the layout very confusing, people where getting lost in the 4 different elevators.
Hotel is under major construction!!!
Lobby bar did have good food, staff at breakfast very rude.
Then there was a bar (private) not run by the hotel but access was in the lobby (Suede) we where dressed causal, nice dress but refused access because we didnt "fit" in.
Next day the bar manager (Big Hispanic with Minney Mouse voice) said if we didnt like it we could go to another club down the street?
Stay away from this hotel, major disappointment for a Starwood Hotel!
JW Marriott at LA Live much nicer, better area!

title: “Very understaffed, needs renovation.”
text:
I think Kimpton hotels are great but unfortunately as other reviews note, this one isn't up to par. Very, very understaffed... always had to wait a really long time to get my car brought around, always a line at the reception area, only a couple of staff who seemed to perform all duties ranging from valet to bellhop to check in desk as there was not enough staff. One evening I came back and there was no valet in site, no staff at reception and a number of unhappy families waiting to get checked in. It took 5 minutes before a sigle staff even appeared. 
Room design, an attempt at quirky (which I appreciate), is outdated and misses the mark. Need revamp.

title: “Not the best example of an aloft property”
text:
I'm a big fan of the aloft brand from SPG because for certain types of trips it gives us exactly what we want and need and no more. I appreciate there are two desks, there is free wifi, there is a fridge in the room, there are healthy, edible snacks available on a 24/7 basis (among other things, like the exercise room and the properties that have a laundromat and the free parking at most). 
This particular aloft is a little run down. The bathroom wasn't as crisp and the rooms were way too worn out for such a new property. I know it's an airport hotel and people are passing through but this is a big problem for me in many hotels in Philadelphia, not just here. The bathroom tiles in the shower had already started to settle, making it uncomfortable to stand on. The safe in our room was shut and no one noticed it. The rooms were clean enough but the public areas were not. 
The beds were very comfortable, comforters adequate, pillows soft. I am there to sleep, this is important.
I would like to praise the hotel staff for good humor and attentiveness, except for the woman who was working Saturday afternoon. She was decidedly too junior and that was clear from her interactions not just with me but with others. The hotel was booked full due to three different concerts in the area and this is not the time to try out someone new.
Keep in mind that if you are traveling to Philly and stay at this hotel, you do not need a car. The free airport shuttle will connect you to the SEPTA (regional rail) at the airport, which takes you to Center City in 15 minutes. However, there is NOTHING ELSE within walking distance of the hotel, so once you're there, you're stranded if you don't have a car. There are two other SPG properties in the same complex so you could eat at their restaurants if you had to. If you do have a car, this is an excellent option for events at Citizens Bank Park, Lincoln Financial Field, or the arena in the same complex - it's less than 10 minutes' away.

title: “A very modern Ritz Carlton”
text:
I stayed at this Ritz Carlton to visit with a few of my college buddies in Washington, DC. This Ritz's appearance is totally different than any other Ritz I've stayed in (I've stayed at Ritz Carlton all over the country). It looked like the Four Seasons and the W Hotel were combined. The hotel has an understated classic/
modern feel. In addtion, the hotel is in some type of old coal or gas
fired manufacturing plant..This history is definately reflected in the decor...very successfully I should add. The hotel fit perfectly with the trendy area of Georgetown. 
The location of the hotel was prime. A block away from the corner of "M" and Wisconsin Ave. It you want to experience Georgetown this location could not be better (It is also a block away from the legendary Blues Alley if you are a jazz fan).
The room was nicely appointed and very comfortable. The bathroom was large although the shower was cramped. My only issue with the room was the internet connection never worked correctly. It took several attempts to connect with thier host site.
The workout area was very small but had quality machines. There also wasn't a shop to get small items that one tends to forget when packing. 
I didn't eat at the hotel but did frequent the bar which again was more like a chic club in Manhattan than the usual Ritz atmosphere. 
The serive was top notch. Everyone went out of their way to assist me and the doormen always knew my name. This is the only hotel I've evered stayed at where the bellman gave me his Ritz business card in case I ever needed his services again. I thought this was a nice touch.
Overall this a great Ritz. If you are looking for a trendy five star hotel in trendy Georgetown, this is the place for you.

title: “Functional but unimpressive”
text:
I agree with the two previous reviews (Jan 2005 & Jul 2004) to a certain extent: small rooms and somewhat dark in corners but acceptable. However, the room we stayed in seemed recently renovated and very clean - especially the bathroom. We stayed three nights. The room was cleaned and sparkling upon our return from our sightseeing every evening. As for urban noise, we occasionally heard the siren of an ambulance, but I think that is expected for the location. Otherwise, the area was eerily quiet owing to the fact that nothing was going on at the convention center nearby. In fact, this quietness and the occassional graffiti and dilapidated row house in the area gave my wife some concern for her safety, but 11th and M St are well lit and we just avoided L St.
Although it is on the National Historic Register, it didn't have much charm to speak of. The complimentary breakfast was simple but well-presented in their dining room. Its just a functional 3-start hotel with a very good location with respect to the sights and fine dining.
FWIW, the sister property (Henley Park) had much better "curb appeal" and looked more spacious when we walked by it one night. Next time, we would consider that hotel, a hotel in Dupont Circle, or some place off the Orange line for the most direct Metro access to the big sights and museums.

title: “Lived up to expectations”
text: This was a great location to Times Square and the subway (one block down) and Central Park. Overall, it was what I have come to expect from a Hampton. It was actually better than my expectations based on other chain hotels I have stayed at in NYC. The only negative thing I could say would be slight peeling of the wallpaper in the bathroom (as a result of poor papering in my opinion). The staff was very helpful and we were even able to check in at noon! I was a little late checking out and they were very accommodating as well. We never heard any traffic and our room faced 8th Ave.

title: “A great property all around”
text: Great location - easy to get to via subway, and short walk to great shopping. Restaurant (had breakfasts and dinners there) was pretty good. Room was clean and spacious. Lobby was nicely done, with a convenient Starbucks-esque coffee kiosk. The gym was a bit small, but since I went at off-peak hours, it wasn't a problem - the equipment was good though. Internet service was stable and reasonable bandwidth. Wouldn't hesitate to stay there again when next in Chicago.

title: “Wellington;The central exploring station”
text: Stay as tourists seven nights.Running around all day...Not stay with a lamp to see hotel faults,just bad,breakfast and walk throu the City.Location excellent for my needs,clean,normal sized and nice rooms,little old time smell for doghunters,but for normal NY price.Booking service helpful and friendly oriented...

title: “Awful”
text: Nothing went right during my stay. Only one elevator was in service. Only one ice machine in the entire hotel, apparently, and it was out of service. I called staff about it and after an interminable wait they basically said it could not be repaired. I asked the desk clerk if there was any way I could get ice; she told me I could go to the restaurant next door. I asked her if she was categorically telling me that the hotel could not provide me, a paying guest, something as basic as ice; she said that was indeed the case. The room was small, dirty, loud, and uncomfortable. I will never return.

title: “Pass on this one!”
text: There are about a dozen cement steps up into the ornate, lovely front entrance to The Jane. There was a doorman / bellman standing on the sidewalk talking to a young man on a bike as I approached with my suitcase. He watched as I lugged the suitcase up the stairs, struggled with the heavy wooden door and tripped into the hotel. There's a reason for the training that "service personnel" are offered at "traditional" hotels! This hotel is definitely for the edgy, adventurous, bored-with-the-usual and possibly younger traveler. It is "funky" which translates to dark, battered and small. I stayed in a rather expensive "captain's room" - which had its own bath (as opposed to shared bath facilities in smaller rooms). The room lacked air conditioning - ugh! - so the opened (small) window provided some muggy circulation and lots of street noise. The room was very dark, there were slippers provided which pleased me because the dark carpet was both worn and dingy enough to be scary. The two small chairs were stiff and uncomfortable and the drain in the tub didn't work. There is an attached, very brightly lit, tile floored restaurant - not great decor but the food was very, very good. So there's a bright spot. The only one -

title: “Hotel Carlton; Great boutique hotel”
text:
I just got back from San Francisco. Stayed 3 nights at the Hotel Carlton on leisure before a week business trip booked at another hotel.
If you are looking for a cool hotel with excellent rates and excellent staff look no further than the Carlton. I had no problems with my reservation or the way I was treated while there. The doorman is excellent. The hotel staff (including Juanita the housekeeper) is friendly, helpful, and seemed to care that I was staying there.
The decor is modern with a European flair. They have a complimentary wine hour (5:30 to 6:30) and also complimentary wireless (not common at a lot of hotels in San Francisco). The rooms (although smaller by American's standard) are well appointed with nice linens, bath accessories, and clean. The only issue is that it is an older hotel so the walls are thin and you will hear your neighbor and folks in the hall. You will also hear street traffic which is not unusual for the older hotels in the city.
One point of note: The hotel, although in a fine neighborhood ,does indeed exist on the outskirts of the Tenderloin district. Do not venture into that area (you would be traveling toward Market Street , check a map) at night. I wandered through there on a couple of occasions by accident and although not as "hard" by inner city standards, there will be homeless, panhandling, and drugged out people littering the sidewalks and the streets. No reflection on the Carlton because that element doesn't exist within the blocks that it sits, but be aware of where you wander when strolling.
Nonetheless, I scored the hotel excellent because there was nothing about the hotel I didn't like. They also have a good Indian restaurant onsite and another very good restaurant next door (Brick) .

title: “Great location, Nice rooms”
text: It was a great hotel right by great shopping in Dallas. The room was very large with plenty of room. Nice service and nice breakfast as well. The parking was a little confusing but it wouldn't cause us to not stay here again. If you're headed to the Galleria - this is a nice place!

title: “In need of repair”
text: Price was very reasonable but the room, halls, elevators were in terrible shape. The carpet in the hallways is coming apart at the seams. The bathrooms walls were cracked. The shelves are all peeling. I also have a problem with $20 per night parking. I will pay a little more and get a newer, updated room next time.

title: “great”
text:
We stayed here for christmas 2007 in a suite overlooking the river and the trump building side.
The room was wonderfull, the service was great and personal, the lounge was good and the staff were always very friendly and hgelpfull, we really enjoyed this stay and will return when we go to chicago again.

title: “Great Location, No Complaints!”
text: Within walking distance to Camden Yards, Inner Harbor and Lexington Market. All common areas were clean. Had a room in the south tower, 14th floor, which had a great view. King room was clean, plenty of closet and drawer space, however the bathroom was on the small side, but for the price we got on Hotwire it could be overlooked. All the staff we encounter in the hotel were, friendly and helpful. Not sure about the other reviewers not feeling safe. Yes, being Caucasian, you are in the minority, but that should not stop you from seeing the City. We walked everywhere, up Charles St. to Maisey’s for Dinner, down to the Inner Harbor, Fells Point and over to the Lexington Market. Everyone was friendly, we never encountered any panhandlers and the Lexington Market is a most if you are a foodie. Very enjoyable stay and would not hesitate to stay again.

title: “Good value budget hotel”
text:
The Park is a basic but nice hotel right by Union Square. It's old but has been recently decorated, our room was simple but clean, quiet and comfortable. It had a fridge and TV (but only the bare minimum of channels). The staff were very friendly and helpful. The elevator is amazing and was probably installed when the hotel was first built! There are plenty of places to eat and drink nearby.
The Park is well located and good value for a budget hotel in the centre of San Francisco.

title: “Great visit with my wife on her Birthday”
text: They know how to pamper, we stayed her on Jan 3-4 2012. Concierge Stephanie went over and above providing Restaurant ideas for us and reservations. Along with that a bottle of champagne was also provided to us in our room. We had the City View over looking the Empire State Building, Room was comfy and served its purpose. Free shoe shine is a nice touch. Wine hour was also a great way to unwind after site seeing and city walking. Will stay again!!!

title: “Great location”
text: Grerat Central location, good value for money and very comfortable rooms, though rather small.

title: “Honeymoon trip”
text: brillaint hotel. We had a room with a balcony which was beautiful. The staff amazing and so helpfull. The location was second to none and will defo be staying here again. One of the best hotels ever stayed in!!

title: “We LOVED Jamie, Sunni, & Brian (and the rest of the staff too)”
text: I reserved 15 rooms at this hotel for friends and family, for our annual NYC shopping trip the weekend before Thanksgiving. In addition to the beautiful rooms and very nice breakfast, the staff were absolutely wonderful. The 3 Bellman we encountered from Friday through Sunday, Jamie, Sunni & Brian, were always smiling and very welcoming. We loved them playing guitars and serenading the guests as they returned from shows or shopping. My husband and I asked to have our room moved since there was remodeling happening on the floor we were originally put on. I made one call to Kim Cofressi, and she had the front desk change our room immediately. They were very, very, accommodating to all of our questions and needs. This is the 5th year I have been taking this trip with friends and family, and I will definetely book this hotel again next year. I certainly hope the staff remains the same. Oh, and Jamie, Sunni & Brian even sang "New York, New York," to our group before we departed. They were GREAT!

title: “Lovely hotel, friendly service”
text:
Stayed at the Hollywood Roosevelt on a pre-honeymoon layover in LA. The fountain in the lobby added a little extra touch, and smelled heavenly. Our room was upgraded for free (thanks!) and we had a perfect view of Grauman's Chinese Theater. The bed was ridiculously comfortable - bathroom was small but I like the separate tub and shower. 
We had breakfast vouchers (thanks again!) and used them for room service. The food was delicious with large portions. Even though we ate for free, the price wasn't bad for LA considering what you got. We had dinner in the burger restaurant, 25 degrees, which also had enormous portions and surprisingly good service.
Of note, we took the TMZ Hollywood Tour and the first stop was our hotel, haha - lots of historical Old Hollywood significance here! :)

title: “Comfortable but Older”
text: The Sheraton Crescent was a fine hotel but there are some things you should be aware of before deciding to book there. The hotel is MUCH older than it appears on the website. If this is an issue for you then don't stay here. I should also note that my experience with "Club Level" perks in other hotels have been far better than at the Sheraton Crescent. The alcohol is not free (about $4.50 for a domestic beer) and the evening hour'dourves were nothing to get excited about (cheese cubes, veggies, chips and salsa, etc.). Unless you like being on "Club Level" for other reasons than the lounge I would not spend the extra money here. I would also like to note that I stayed in a Jr. Suite and requested a king size bed. It was not a king size bed, it was a queen that folded out of the wall, comfortable but not what I had in mind. Finally, I called concierge for a recommendation on where to eat in Downtown Phoenix. I was then transferred to someone else that informed me that he is not from Phoenix and was not familiar with Downtown. I asked if he could find someone that was and was told he would call me back. I never heard from him. In my past experiences that is what concierge is for, they even make reservations for you. Checking in was a breeze and the rooms were clean. I would recommend this hotel for a couple of nights stay if you are looking for a reasonably priced hotel but not a luxury hotel. Again, the website can be a little deceiving when it comes to the appearance of the hotel. It wasn’t a disaster but disappointing when you get there and nothing seems to be the way it was presented to you. Hope this helps in making your decision on where to stay in Phoenix.

title: “A hip, nicely designed hotel with a great location, friendly staff and at a great price.”
text: What a great boutique hotel! Aloft is a new concept in hotels by the W. The hotel lobby is not on the ground floor, so after parking in the garage below, we took and elevator up to check-in. Upon entering the lobby, there is a nice scent throughout and hip music playing. The people at check-in couldn't have been any nicer. I grabbed a milk out of their grab-and-go styled food and drink area and they just added it to our bill. The rooms are very nicely laid out, great use of space. The design is contemporary and clean. They even use Bliss spa products! We hung out at the lobby bar that evening and had a great time. They even have an indoor pool with fantastic views. This is now my favorite hotel in Charlotte!

title: “Not to bad”
text: I had booked this hotel before seeing the reviews for it I then got worried but after being there it was not bad at all yes the plaster is falling off Walls and ceilings in some places and there was a damp smell but soon got used to it. But for what you need the room for you couldn't ask for more the only problem I had with the hotel was the doorman was very rude and it seemed like he needed a good slap. Maids came round every day and made beds. The hotel is in need of a make over I think every thing has been left since Glenn millar stayed there but apart from that I really enjoyed my stay here

title: “Cushy near Camden Yards”
text: Stayed one night during week. Hotel and room very nice and lives up to it's 4 star rating...and the lounge and amenities very nice. The view from the fitness room is amazing looking straight into Camden Yards and the indoor pool was beautiful. Location is great for Camden Yards but a couple blocks away from Inner Harbor so expect a little walk. Parking is convenient and the elevator brings you directly into the lobby so if the weather is bad this is great. Everyone I met was very helpful and kind and all common areas were kept immaculate. If I had any complaint it would be that Internet (either wireless OR wired) wasn't free unless you were a minimum Hilton Honors Gold member (I'm a member but not that high of a level). I get free internet at Starbucks for goodness sake...you'd think I could get the internet for free at a Hilton that is costing me $200 plus a night!

title: “Dissapointment”
text: We had stayed at this hotel a few months ago and had a great corner room in the historical part of the hotel, so we thought we would try again, this time getting a balcony room overlooking the river. It was a huge let down and we checked out a day early. There was a lot of noise from the balcony next door and the view was not good at all. The room itself was clean, but pretty rundown. We travel to San Antonio several times a year, but we will skip this hotel next time.

title: “The Good, The Bad, And The Ugly.”
text:
I chose The Lafayette because of its' location - only a mile or two from Balboa Park, Hillcrest, and North Park. (I lived in these areas from 1960 to 1985.) This was a nostalgia trip to cruise around on my bicycle and revisit my old "stomping grounds" and wanted a hotel near them from which to launch my outings. The location was perfect for that.
 The Good - the room and bath were clean and refurbished, and the bed was confortable. (I am an older man and I liked the old style architecture.) Parking - secure, enclosed garage beneath the hotel. I liked that. Price - reasonable. $265 total for the three nights.
 The Bad - on both Friday and Saturday, there was a lot of noise from "party people" - young people who seemed to use the hotel as a gathering place for parties - very noisy. Also, on Sat. night there was a live band somewhere near my room that blasted away until 11 PM.
 The Ugly - when I checked in on Friday afternoon, the counter person was uncommunicative - almost surly. She was not voluntarily helpful at all, almost as if she hated her job. Definitely not the demeanor that should be on the counter.
 Bottom Line - I would stay there again, but not on Friday or Saturday because of the noise.

title: “A great hotel for a city break”
text: I stayed at the Crowne Plaza for four nights. I had a room on the 21st floor and I could see the Magnificent Mile from my window. I had a very comfortable king size bed. Nice big TV and ipod dock. The only down side to the room was the dark bathroom ( not very good lighting). The pool was lovely and just the right size. Could do with a few more sun loungers. The location was great right by the shops and not far from the subway. Would recommend The Corner Bakery for any meal. I would stay at the hotel again.

title: “Clean and does the trick for business travel”
text:
Stayed here as it was just a few minutes' walk from a business meeting that I had to attend. 
Pros:
- room was better decorated than expected
- bathroom was spacious
- room was bigger than expected _for a NYC hotel room_ (for 2, it'll be a bit cramped)
- free wifi
- big Samsung flatscreen tv
- no comforter cover on the bed (which I always pull off anyway)
- good / nice smelling lotions & bath samples...but men may not like that
Could've Been Better but not outright "Cons":
- The wall adjoining the hallway must have been pretty thin as I heard the constant door slamming of other room doors throughout the night. (Thankfully I was exhausted so wasn't really frightened awake by the slamming...but the noise level did not sound muffled.)
- I, too, found it surprising that the blackout curtains didn't really move to shut the window. Heads up if you are light sensitive. 
- I didn't find one of those foldable luggage rests for my rollerbag
- The spaciousness of the bathroom could've been better used; for example, I would've added a towel rack closer to the shower and one closer to the sink so I could easily reach for towels from either of those locations
- Sink looks nice but is less practical b/c there is very little counter space for your various bathroom items. 
Tip:
- when you look to connect to the wifi, there are two "Carlton" networks. One had a bunch of warnings when I connected it and then tried to go to check my email - something about how it wasn't secure. So, I used the other network and that worked fine. Not sure if the former one was supported by the hotel or something more nefarious, but I chose to avoid it.

title: “If you want to stay in town, I would recommend this Hotel”
text: We had a excellent experience with the Washington Court. James and all the staff were very helpful to these 1st time to DC travelers, from the initial contact 2 months earlier till we departed. Thanks.

title: “Unexpected Delight!”
text:
For a last-minute business trip, I checked Hotwire for available hotels in Midtown. The Westin Times Square ended up being my selection, and I can't begin to tell you what a fantastic deal I got for this hotel!
This is a wonderful hotel in a wonderful location (one block from Times Square and three blocks from Restaurant Row on 8th and 46th). I was cordially greeted at check-in and given a room on the 10th floor in the business section. Having used Hotwire or some other low-priced search engine before, I know sometimes hotels will not treat you the same as a "full-price" paying guest. That was not the case here at all.
The room was absolutely huge (I was expecting a closet for my good-deal price), with lovely amenities - very large, flat-screen TV, Apple computer (or you could hook up your own), great bedding, bathroom, shower, etc. I really lucked out with this hotel!
Noise was not a problem at all, and I thought it might be in a 10th floor room. Not so. View was not all that great - could see a bit of 42nd street, but not much more.
I would whole-heartedly recommend staying at this hotel!

title: “A gem in the heart of center city!!”
text:
Just wrapped up a wonderful stay at the hotel Palomar in Center city Philly and it was a great stay. Many, many pros with only 1 con. This was a girls only trip for myself and my 3 college roommates. 
Since there was only 1 problem let's get that out of the way. As with any big city Parking is an adventure. It's a 40 charge per night to park at the hotel and retrieving your car takes a minimum of 30 minutes. Now that, that's out of the way. Onto the PROS
1) Location. smack dab in the middle of every thing. HIgh end shopping? Check 1 block on Walnut. More moderate shopping? check few blocks down on Market and Chestnut streets. Restuarants? check. way to many in walking distance to name. Every thing from Philly cheesesteaks to Ruth Chris steak house and every thing in between. Rittenhouse square was a few blocks down and had a lovely park in the middle. Every thing else is a short hop on the bus or very cheap cab ride away.
2) Amenities. Great. nice size fitness room on the fourth floor. room sizes were great. 2 Queens and a nice size bathrom. this comes in handy when traveling with 3 college roommates with enough luggage to supply Cleopatras barge.
Bar was a really nice place to unwind after a long afternoon. Coffe/tea and pastries complimentary between 7 and 10. then they also had a wine tasting nightly at 5. 
3)Service and decor. Top knotch. truthfully our stay went so smooth I can't say if the hotel staff is efficient, we never needed them. front desk staff was great. friendly and knowledgable of Philly.
Hotel itself is very pretty. Contemporary with a nod to the historical area. LOL since the Army/Navy game was last weekend, hotel had the bust of ben Franklin in a Go Navy and Go Army shirts. 
I plan on becoming a Kimpton rewards member and will definitely seek out their hotels whenever I travel.

title: “Mostly Great”
text:
My husband and I recently spent a week here. We chose this hotel because of the locatiom -- an easy walk to the Mall, Metro across the street, and lots of restaurants nearby. Our room was on the second level, overlooking an interior courtyard which is used for drinks and snacks from the hotel bar. Though it was often noisy in the courtyard, extra glass had been put over the windows, and we never heard a sound. However, people in the courtyard could look right into our room, so we had to keep the drapes closed when we would have preferred to have them open. Our room was spacious, clean, and nicely decorated. There was ample space in the armoire for our clothes, but next time I'd ask them to remove the robes they provide (which we did not want or use) to give us more room for hanging clothes. The bathroom was also spacious, and always sparkling clean. Housekeeping was excellent and unobtrusive, except for one day when we asked the housekeeper to return later, and she never came back. We requested service, and our room was taken care of quickly. Most hotel staff, particularly in the restaurnat, were helpful and pleasant, and often rememberd us when we saw them again. The exception were the men outside doing valet parking, but we assumed they were also there to heklp us in and out. But they ignored us, never smiled or said hello, even when we greeted them. They give a very unfriendly and unpleasant first impression
We enjoyed the lobby, finding it comfortable and welciming, and often went down for morning coffee and the evening wine tasings. Most afternoons we found fresh, warm chocolate chip cookies at the front desk when we returned from our sightseeing.
We did have a couple of maintenance problems which were not taken of the first time we reported them. Since one of them was a broken toilet handle so tht the toilet didn't flush, we were very eager to have the repair made, but when we returned to our room about five hours after requesting the repair, nothing had been done. I responded with some anger and frustration, and had a very quick response and repair, overseen by a manager. 
We ate in the Poste Restaurant once for breakfast and three times for dinner. Breakfast was disappointing -- my husband ordered his oatmeal with the broiwn sugar on the side, but the waiter said that they had mixed it in, so he was having it redone. The second time it was done correctly, but mine had obviously been sitting there meanwhile and was only lukewarm when I got it, and each bowl was $11, almost twice what we'd paid for oatmeal at a nearby restaurant (Pain Quotidian). Our dinners, on the other hand, were outstanding -- both food and service were excellent. We had filet mignin with foie gras and mushrooms, Croque Monsieur, risotto, Never-ending Summer Salad, vichysoisse, and the onion burger, which was the best hamburger I've ever had. The chocolate mousse dessert topped with Oreo crumbs and a doll[p of whipped cream was out of this workld, and the decaf coffee was excellent.
I would have given Hotel Monaco 5 stars if it hadn't been for the maintenance problems.

title: “great hotel”
text: We go to the fairmont about 6 times a year just to get away.The staff is friendly and the rooms are spacious and clean.It is located downtown you can walk to westend or to most of the museums.

title: “Great location, noisy, ok room”
text:
Having gone to college in Boston I know the city well and was happy to find a room for under $200 right in a central location for a recent trip to Boston with my husband. After reading reviews here and checking prices of other centrally located hotels we decided to book at the Chandler. We used booking.com and got a rate of $170 which turned out to be $196 after taxes. Not cheap for a hotel room, but it was Boston in the summer...The surrounding area is quite nice and we always felt safe even coming back in the dark.
Check-in went smoothly and we got into our room just after the 3pm check-in time. It was on the second floor close to the corner of Chandler and Berkeley and directly over the pub downstairs. The bathroom is basically a closet with a hand-washing sink and a decent sized shower. The room was on the small size but acceptable for a one-night stay. No closet, but place to hang things, nice tv and very modern furnishings. Overall it was decent but not exactly my taste.
I felt that the place was overpriced for what we got especially when we were woken up several times during the night due to lots of noise from the pub downstairs and when they closed people stayed out on the street for quite sometime. Perhaps rooms on a higher floor are less noisy. The complimentary coffee and tea is in the very small lobby and comes out of a generic machine, so nothing one would likely make use of. There was a cafe' around the corner on Berkeley St which looked good.

title: “Fabulous Stay in a Perfect Location in Boston”
text: The Westin Copley Place exceeded my expectations. I had stayed here once before about ten years earlier, and this time not only did they upgrade me to a suite, but the customer service was outstanding! The Heavenly beds were phenomenal, and the view out of my corner room was spectacular overlooking the Charles River and the MIT dome across the way. The location is superb with everything being walking distance - from the best shopping on Newbury to the Theatre district to the Copley T to take you to Faneuil Hall or the Waterfront if too tired to walk. A truly wonderful hotel! I will stay here every time I'm in Boston on business or for a romantic get-away!

title: “No problem at all”
text:
I can warmly recommend this hotel to low-budget travellers. But to be honest, not to anyone searching for any kind on luxury or "top place for small money". Riverside is like "last stop before a hostel" -place. Nothing more. Best properties were low price and good location.
The room was ok (tv, freezer, air conditioner, good double bed), bathrooms were comfortable and clean. Housekeeping was diligent. Location is quite good, 2 good buss-lines from downtown and several subways comes to 72st station which is just 200m away. 
After all, hotel administration should chance all the advertising information in hotels presentations:
1)"Hotel Riverside Studio is only a couple of blocks from Broadway next to Trump Towers new buildings" - NO WAY
2)"surrounded by many restaurants featuring international specialty shops, supermarkets" - NO WAY
3)"Facilities: Alarm clock, Hairdryer, Iron and ironing board, Kitchenette, Pay-per-view movies, Refrigerator" - NO WAY
4)"Landmark building with European flavor" - European, perhaps, if you travel in far-east Europe
Thanks anyway, we had a excellent week in NY! This hotel is for you dear poor people with no big exeptions. Good luck!

title: “Great midtown location and very comfortable rooms and attentive staff; excellent value for money and a touch of class.”
text: Stayed for two nights on a business trip and wish i had more time to enjoy the leisurely brekfast and the vibey Monkey Bar. Room was a kingsize deluxe and a great pity that my wife could not join me. It is possibly an even greater hotel for a holiday than for business. I will look to return!

title: “Great location and excellent, friendly staff”
text: We chose this hotel for its proximity to my family in Phoenix as well as its super close location to a major Interstate (I-17 Black Canyon Freeway) As we were traveling northbound to the Grand Canyon this location was superb to get right on the highway and go. Staff both nights (we stayed 1-night on either end of our stay) were so friendly and helpful. They really cared about their work. The rooms were basically appointed (although I'm noticing a trend among cheaper hotels - no toilet lids) with a fridge and microwave. Excellent choice for travel routes North and South in/out of Phoenix.

title: “great location and excellent service”
text: I just returned from a long weekend stay at this location. I had requested early check-in and they delivered for all three rooms we reserved. The check-in staff was courteous and was even able to provide adjoining rooms..On a side note, some people may be taken back by the valet charge ($25/day) but the fee is similar too other hotels in the area..Self park facilities are available for a lower rate but they do not offer in and out privileges and are located 2-3 blocks from the hotel...All things considered the valet provides the best value. The rooms we had were all furnished with double queen beds, LCD TV, and desk and mini fridge. While not overly large they are modern and comfortable..The swimming pool is rather small but ok for children to cool off on a hot summer day. The hotel does have an outdoor seating area to enjoy a morning coffee (starbucks on site), or an evening beverage. The hotel location on the riverwalk is excellent. Within a one to two block radius you have multiple local and chain eateries and pubs.. In addition, the historic Alamo site as well as the local market are also easily within walking distance. I was completely satisfied with my stay at this location.

title: “Fine airport hotel”
text:
This airport hotel is about ten minutes from O'Hare, just off the highway. The shuttle leaves from the airport and the hotel every half hour, 24 hours a day and both times I took it, it was right on time. I found the service to be excellent and they handled requests courteously and promptly. My room was a true suite, with a bedroom door that closes and a bathroom that had two doors--one to the bedroom and another to the living room. There was a small fridge along with a coffee maker and a room safe. Internet was around $10 a night but free for Platinum and above. There is a 24 hour pantry next to reception. I had no issues with lines at reception, thin walls, or other common problems, so maybe it was my lucky day.
The workout facilities are better than I have seen in many other airport hotels, with a good workout room, an indoor pool where you can actually swim laps, a good sized hot tub next to the pool, and a sauna in the bathroom. 
The hotel is located next to the highway and I got some traffic noise from the bedroom but not the living room, so I guess it depends on the windows in your room. The way the hotel is situated it's hard to avoid the noise but it wasn't too bad unless you're sensitive. It's a 5-10 minute walk to the train that takes you to O'Hare (two stops) or downtown Chicago (40 minutes). It would be a tough walk in bad weather but fine in pleasant weather.
I got a great rate through Expedia courtesy of Trip Advisor, much better than the hotel's own website.

title: “New - Modern - Cold - Average - Confrence Friendly”
text: Very effecient confrnece facility with expense account prices. Upgrad and get a room that does not overlook the roof of a vast confrence facility. Plan on eating elsewhere.

title: “No better place to stay in Philadelphia”
text: The Embassy Suites at Philadelphia Airport is a fantastic find! Not only are the front desk people super helpful, is the suite really a sitting room and a bedroom with two flat screens, and do they hold a daily manager's cocktail party with a live executive in attendance, the real bonus is the vicinity of Eastwick Septa rail station from which you can get every half hour in 15 minutes to Center City. The hotel's shuttle service will drop you at the station, but if the weather is nice and you feel like a mild stroll, you can walk there in 10 minutes. Breakfast is good, cooked to order.

title: “Great hotel for Moscone Center & shopping”
text:
We had a great stay here for a week whilst my husband attended a conference at the Moscone Center just down the road. The hotel's also excellently placed for local bars/microbreweries, restaurants and shopping - just around the corner from the Westfield centre.
We were in a club room on the 33rd floor; the room was spacious and had fantastic views over the bay. The bathroom had an excellent shower and Aromatherapy Associates toiletries - luxurious, but the lavender and ylang-ylang shower gel was a tad over powering for day-time use!
The room gave us access to the club lounge with free wifi, a couple of PCs and a printer and a steady supply of food and drink on tap; we subsequently discovered from some of my husband's colleagues our room actually worked out a lot cheaper than booking at the regular rate and then paying for internet access and getting breakfast in the restaurant downstairs. 
I was advised on booking that continental breakfast would be available in the club lounge and was expecting a few manky looking croissants and some coffee (obviously too used to British/European continental breakfast) but the food was amazing: a selection of cold meats and fish (including Gravadlax), fruit, loads of different breads and pastries, preserves, bacon and scrambled eggs. We missed afternoon tea every day but took advantage of the cocktails, wine, champagne,beer and (delicious) hors d'oeuvre that were available from about 5 o'clock. There was also cake, cookies and digestifs laid out after dinner.
I only had 2 criticisms of our stay; firstly, the staff could have been slightly more attentive - we basically had to work everything out for ourselves; and secondly the tomato based tasting menu at Luce, whilst delicious, was miserly to the point we had to go to the club room and fill up on cookies and was probably the only disappointing meal we ate whilst in San Francisco.
I would definitely recommend staying here if you need to be in central San Francisco, and make sure you visit Le Charm French restaurant around the corner: absolutely the best French food (especially the onion soup) I've eaten outside of France.

title: “Good Value”
text:
The hotel was well located for our Concert at Copley Hall, downtown. It also accepted our pet (dog) for an additional $20. Still the total for the night was under $100. Coffee was always available at the office as were Otis Spunkmeyer cookies. 
They offered a hot waffle and cereal for free at breakfast. 
The room was adequate with 2 queens. The shower spray was weak. Free wired or wireless internet was included. All in all a good value for San Diego.

title: “Quality is slipping!”
text: This is the second time I stayed at this hotel, and I am concerned that the cleanliness and condition is declining since last year. There was debris in the elevator when i arrived that was still there on day two. The grout in the bathroom was discolored, and the toilet did not flush properly. I had to lift the tank lid and jiggle the mechanism to get it to work. That being said, the room was very clean overall, and the bed was extremely comfortable. Beverly at the front desk greeted me with a big smile and was a most gracious and accommodating hostess. She extended to me the "distress" rate after my flight was cancelled, and I was stranded. The lobby bar has lots of comfortable seating, and the hotel's restaurant offers a decent breakfast buffet for $12.95. The hotel also has a free shuttle to and from JAX Airport -an added bonus.

title: “One of the best experiences we have ever had at a US Hotel”
text: The service, facilities and location were awesome. Beautiful guestrooms, excellent views, top quality amenities, Pricing was appropriate for the quality - something that we can rarely state.

title: “Well appointed, walking distance for most attractions”
text: The Sheraton is in a great location - but be prepared for exercise on the hills of Seattle. We arrived via train and the hotel was very accommodating for late arrivals. It is pretty easy to walk to restaurants, Pike's market, the aquarium. We did try room service and the restaurant - both good. Good view from the upper floors. PS_Actually went there in May 2011

title: “Class”
text:
This hotel is real class. I held my wedding there a few weeks ago and from my first day visiting until now, I have been treated with nothing but respect and kindness. The staff is one of the most professional I have ever experienced. True southern hospitality! They will treat you like family no matter what walk of life you are from. 
When you enter the hotel you are officially "away". You can trust this staff with your most precious moments. They will take care of you. The hotel is gorgeous and constantly being updated. My guests have not stopped raving about how well taken care of they were and how the staff couldn't do enough to help while they were there. They made the planning process easy for my wedding and took first class care of me and my family. 
We also rented the cottage that lies across the golf course from the main hotel. This home is gorgeous and was perfect for our after reception party. It was also a great place for my bridal party to get ready and relax before, during, and after the wedding. 
I highly recommend this hotel whether it is for a night away or a large event like a wedding. They will make it a memorable stay either way!

title: “Great place right off the riverwalk”
text:
We went to the RiverWalk for my neices ANSO National beauty pagent. We knew staying right on the river was going to be outrageous so we did a little hunting around and found this great hotel.. It is just a clock or two from the river walk and just across the street from Travis park. 
The bathrooms are a little dated but everything functioned fine. They probably should put a vent in them on their next remodel.
The bed was a very nice king sized 4-poster bed. We had to climb up in it because it sat so high off the floor. There was a sitting bench that was at the end of the bed left a little to be desired. I sat on it and felt like I was going to fall through. The view over looking the Travis park was very nice.
The air conditioning probably needed a little looking at it although we never mentioned it to the staff. We felt fine during the day but it felt warm in the evenings and nights when we were trying to sleep.
The pool was on the 6th floor. It was quite comfortable and not too small. I was surprised though that there only a few tables and not a lot of umbrellas.
The front entry and sitting areas were beautifula dn well taken care of.
For the price we paid for the room, it was a great place to stay and we would go back

title: “loved it!”
text: I used to live in nor cal, and now try to get to sf a couple times a year and the monaco is my fav hotel i've stayed in so far. everything about it was fantastic, rooms were decent sized, beds soo comfortable, nice bath products, great location, nice hotel staff, cool looking decor, i could go on and on. would definetly stay there again. stayed in a higher up room, 5th floor or so, just for the less street noise with 2 double beds and it was perfect. check on line at all the various places for the best deal, then call the hotel and book with them directly, they'll match the price and there's no booking fee's, can cancel if need to with out penalty 48hrs or so before hand. i stayed there over new years eve for less than 200$!!

title: “Street noise on the 12th floor? Yup!”
text:
I specifically asked for a room without street noise, having read some yelps about this place and was assured I would be ok. I can sleep through noise, especially when I'm out of town, but damn...it was a lot.
other than that, this place is pretty nice. The staff are rather oblivious to customers...I saw this many times to others and us. It could do better, especially at those rates. Oh, and $25/day parking? Welcome to San Francisco!

title: “ok, but room for improvement”
text: Stayed here for business at a corporate rate. The location was perfect for my meetings etc and very close to the metro station (subway). The cleanliness of the room could have been better - bathroom and linen were clean but there were crumbs all over the carpeting... not what you expect from such a hotel. Everything else was clean so i refrained form asking for a room change. Overall, i would stay here again for business becasue of the location but it would not be my first choice for a leisure trip.

title: “Great”
text: Staff were really helpful. Good Location with a great cafe around the corner for breakfast. Shared bathrooms were always available and clean. Would stay here again.

title: “Do not book if you are trying a CORPORATE deal!!”
text:
I booked here througha corporate deal. Thanks to my company which holds every seminar here. What i write is my personal view and should not be construed as general. But I guess the hotel needs to improve on a lot more before offering itself to corporates. I dont want to beat the statement hard but many of my colleagues shared this view
1) Internet- You are better off hooking up to the nearby greenspoint plaza as the internet is worst. The scariest part is... its unsecured and I had a virus attack (as I kept a online movie channel on) before returning from a Dinner. I would definately definately give a 2 out of 10.
2) Front Desk- The face of a hotel- I had issues with my room. I mentioned this to the front desk while leaving for a meeting in the morning. They retorted back saying, I quote" We have 500 rooms some times these things do happen. I was stunned to hear this from a MOTEL like Hilton.
3) Vino - Restaurant- A plain vanilla standard menu. I waited for 25 min before i was served. I requested for some extra peanut sauce.. and it took them the next 10 min. No exaggeration here... but I am pretty sure to the last second on the time it took them to attend.
4) Breakfast- We were served coupons. (Its funny though we had 100 employees staying here.. they stil had the coupon system).Anyway i missed out on getting the coupon one day and I mentioned as soon as i got to the restaurant.The person at the front said thats ok, but then No communication existed between her and the waiter. He bugged thrice and literally forced me to leave my breakfast and get him the PRIZEST PIECE OF POSSESSION... the coupon. I never at at the breakfast for the next 10 days.
5) I had to pay the price as the hotel complained... and well the corporates covered up. 
6) Oh yes.. the location... its not the safest neighbourhood.. dont trust try having a late evening walk.
This has left a bad impression on me. I will never ever ever go to a HILTON under a corporate deal. Had i been there on my personal expense, i would have made them dance for the pain they gave.

title: “Little gem!”
text:
A warm and welcoming hotel. It was a more personalised experience as the hotel is smaller and the staff are more inviting and helpful. 
The rooms were small but cosy and they even provided L'Occitane toiletries! The bathroom was spacious and the shower was huge. The room also had complimentary wifi.
The hotel was located near Union Square and close to major shopping department stores. (For the shoe lovers, a visit to DSW is a must!). The cable car is also close to the hotel. 
The only con: just west of the hotel is an area called the Tenderloin. We made the mistake of walking through there on the way back to our hotel one night. It's a notorious area and not one for tourists! 
Other than that, we loved it and would recommend it to everyone!

title: “Great Location, Awesome staff and services....”
text: My family recently stayed at the MMC. We loved the location. Union Square is around the block with all of the major shopping, reminiscent of TImes Square in NY. The free breakfast is wonderful and the evening cocktail hour is a huge bonus. THey even have shirley temples for the kids. The rooms are very nice as well. The bathroom isn't huge, but it has what we need. There was a mini fridge in the room and a coffee maker as well. THe views from the restaurant are amazing, overlooking the city. What better way to enjoy breakfast than looking out over the bay and downtown? Highly recommend!

title: “Oh My God!”
text: We visited NY in October 2004, when we got there the first bad thing happened - there weren't enough beds for us all to have one each! We therefore had to spend the next three nights sharing a bed with at least one other person, sometimes more. When we first got inside our room (on the very top floor) we found pubic hair in the bath (which didnt run properly), rubbish under the bed, mouldy food, and it was freezing as the windows did not fit the wall! Some of our friends found nail clippings in their bed sheets, some had blood stains. In the room next to ours a girl found a used condom in the drawer! On our second day, all the toilets blocked on our floor - so no one could go to the toilet all morning. As the bath didn't work, we couldn't wash our hair, so we had to wash it over a tiny sink, the size of a dinner plate. And to top it all off we had a policeman knock on our door to tell us to be careful of drug dealers residing in the hotel! On our last day we thought it would be over, however the shower broke in another guest's room and we had to rush our luggage through a large puddle of water to get to the lift at 7.30 in the morning! By the way, the lift had dried up sick in the corner! Not pleasant. even if you are looking for a budget hotel, with a great location - this place is not worth it. It was an experience but one we'd rather forget! Sorry about the photos - they are a bit wobbly, but it was had to concentrate with all the crap that was happening around us!

title: “At these rates, a swimming pool also”
text:
B.I. Houston Hobby was a second choice, selected in hopes of more hospitable, and intelligible, telephone communications than experienced one week earlier with another Hobby-area, Gulf Freeway hotel. Our hopes were realized!
Shuttle Service was said to be available, although we needed a rental car for travel in the Houston area between our stays, May 29-30, June 1-2.
The area of the motel was no surprise, due to I-45 South visits with relatives in Friendswood and Galveston from 1970s, and more recent Southwest Airlines flights from Houston-Hobby. The motel's setting resembled a Latin-flavored "posada" swallowed up by developments in zoning-free Houston.
Maneuvering past a Tex-Mex restaurant, then past a parked fleet of semi-trailers, we were amazed and delighted at the sight of the white stucco'd facade of Baymont Inn. 
The motel's parking area was not the unsettling scenario mentioned by some reviewers -- nothing unsettling was noted or experienced over a wide span of hours during Tues-Wed, Fri-Sat stays in late May 2007.
Previous experiences with budget motels failed to prepare us for the clean, spacious room and bath. Although Room 2xx was a Smoking Room, no hint of tobacco use was evident -- welcome for me, despite my partner's use of "little cigars".
Another reviewer's mention of microwave and small refrigerator made me envious. Was that lack in "Smoking" room 2xxm intended to balance the smoking privilege? 
The swimming pool, with its tropical setting of blooming gingers, palms and subtropical shrubs, was a delight to use. Our 8pm arrival from Chicago-Midway allowed extensive relaxation, with a morrning wake-up swim to follow.
A self-service breakfast buffet provided apple, orange, and cranberry juice. A similar range of dry cereal, bagels, muffins was provided, with half-pint 2% milk cartons. Hot cocoa mix provided reinforcement for the somewhat weak coffee. Carafes of half 'n half, whole milk, and 2% were also available for those of us not accustomed to black coffee.
The motel staff were hospitable, unlike descriptions made by some other reviewers. 
Although an AARP discount was indicated -- and provided for at check-in -- the credit card charge did not match the expected rate. It was only well away from Baymont Inn, even on the return flight, that the discrepancy of a somewhat higher charge was noticed. AARP Discount? Check and double-check!

title: “Great staff and great place to stay!”
text:
We spent the week of July 4th at the Affinia Dumont. NYC is known for it's impersonal residents. I am sure there are many in NYC but they do NOT work at the Affinia Dumont! The desk staff, the doormen, David...the concierge, the housekeeping staff and everyone we came in contact with was just wonderful. The temperament of the staff is contagious because even the guests were friendly. 
We arrived before check-in and our bags were stored until our room was ready and we were allowed to check in 2 hours early. Our flight home was in the afternoon and again the staff offered to store our bags until we were ready to leave. NO CHARGE for the service!!!
The location is great, our room was immaculate, service was outstanding and I wanted to stay longer. When I travel I am usually ready to go home within a few days but I was very comfortable at the Affinia Dumont. We met a couple checking in as we were waiting for our transportation to the airport. They lived in NYC but moved to Virginia near where we live. They have a son still living in NYC and they stay at the Affinia Dumont several times a year. We will definitely be going back!

title: “Maybe it's just me...”
text: Overall, I gave this recent hotel stay a poor rating because I felt I was mistreated and the customer service was Terrible. Booked the room through expedia and prepaid for one night. The room was nice and clean, had everything we needed, and I felt safe and comfortable. Then, when I decided to stay 2 hours longer for the "late checkout", I was informed that it would be $20 extra. That was fine by me, but of course I'm thinking that it would be added to my bill or I'd just have to pay at checkout. No big deal. Well, as I'm trying to sleep, I began getting numerous phone calls from the front desk rudely awaking myself and infant child along with constant knocks on the door and staff barging into the room. All attempting to force me to get up and pay that darn $20 immediately "or I'd be forced to vacate the premises". It was so bad I could not go back to sleep and basically spent my 2 extra hours I paid $20 dollars for being harassed. I was finally able to get up and pay the fee at the front desk in my PJs. Did not have cash or credit card on me. Luckily they had an onsite atm machine, otherwise I guess we would've been put out on the street. Took everything in me not to make a scene and I probably wouldn't go back there if they were the last hotel in Charlotte! Not trying to deter anyone from choosing this place, but this was my experience.

title: “Great Location...Just missing that 'something'...”
text:
We flew in to Newark (EWR), and got the train into New York Penn Station ($12.50 each way) which is across the road from the hotel. The location is absolutely fantastic, on the same street as empire state building, 5-10 mins from times square and theatreland, grayline office down the street, everything within walking distance, (if you dont mind walking, otherwise might be a bit far to a few sights like statue of liberty/wall street/battery park)
On entering the hotel our first thoughts were wow! The lobby is very art deco, and very inkeeping with that old new york. We were able to check in early which was a bonus, my only gripe would be that the check in staff didnt explain anything to us, hotel amenities etc.... The fact we had to hand over $220 as a deposit for incidentals was never mentioned on their website, and seeing as though we had paid in full with a credit card surely it was already on file...i think they could make this situation better..? This is a very busy hotel, with lots of people around all the time.
Our room was on the 22nd floor and was a metro queen room, it was very small, but this is New York and we were'nt expecting anything much bigger, and besides, we were only in the room to drop bags off, change and sleep, theres too much to do and see in the city the rest of the time! The room was very clean and actually quite modern with LCD TV etc, but having recently been updated you would probably expect that, however it seemed as though the bathroom had been missed out, by contrast it was at best dated, and a bit grotty in places, the towels are quite small too, but you do get toiletries.
The bed itself, was very comfortable, one of the best and was great for collapsing on at night after long days in NYC! The room was nice and quiet too, great for getting to sleep and being able to relax at night.
I thought it was good that they had security checking room cards before allowing people into the lifts, however the security deposit boxes were a bit strange in that we had to queue up at reception to gain access everytime, it just wasted a lot of time having to wait around for reception to let you in. 
The staff themselves were polite enough, but they just seemed to lack the ability to smile, and the majority of the time seemed like they just didnt want to be there.
We opted to eat at the tick tock diner one evening, and to be honest it wasnt the best food ive ever had, it was okay, nothing special and the staff again seemed like they just didnt want to be there - there are plenty of other great places to eat in new york, so i wouldnt waste your time in the tick tock and go try something authenic elsewhere!
Overall the location is great, in fact you'd struggle to beat it as its in the middle of everything you want to do, but the service leaves a little to be desired, just lacks that 'something' to make it great. I would definately stay here again for the location, but if it was service i was after i would try somewhere else.

title: “Cannot complain at the rate given”
text: The Holiday Inn is conveniently about 1 mile from MD Anderson. They offer a free shuttle, and give you free breakfast coupon for medically related stay, saves you about $12 a day in food. The breakfast buffett is good, and you can also order off the menu. The breakfast burrittos were very good! Service in restaurant and bar pretty good. We paid for an upgraded King Suite, on the top floor. Had a small fridge, but no microwave. Rooms were clean, linens and towels fine. Furniture a bit beat up, ceilings had multiple repairs and stains. Again, for the price, it is a good option for anyone wanting to be close to the medical centers,and take advantage of the free shuttle.

title: “Holiday Inn Express Close to Pennsylvania Hospital”
text: Recently I had outpatient surgery at Pennsylvania Hospital and had to stay overnight in Philadelphia. The Holiday Inn Express was convenient to the Hospital and reasonable compared to other hotels in the area. I asked for a very sterile and quiet room as I was coming straight from surgery. The accommodations couldn't have been better. The room was quiet and immaculate. If medical issues require an overnight stay in Philadelphia I will certainly stay at this hotel again.

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: Had read some less than favourable reviews so was concerned about the hotel. However, it was wonderful. I was in a corner room on the 23rd floor, great view of the river. The rooms are small but not tiny, perfectly fine for one or two people. The bed was extremely comfortable, updated bathroom, mini-fridge and microwave, heard no noise from other rooms, free wi-fi - I didn't have my laptop so I don't know what the connection was like. There are two PCs with a printer in the Lobby area that you can use for free. The staff were friendly and very helpful. On each floor is a water dispenser with bottles so you don't have to pay for overpriced bottled water from the 7-11. We ate in the hotel restaurant one night and the food and service were excellent. The location is great, right on the river, close to Michigan Ave, within walking distance of so much. We didn't realise that the city bus [$2.25] to the Science & Industry Museum stops right by the hotel, we paid for a taxi because it was raining the one day but came back on the bus.

title: “HOME AWAY FROM HOME”
text: I loved my stay at the Extended Stay. I actually stayed for 3 months, I am currently awaiting to buy a home, so saving money and waiting on a settlement check is why staying at E.S. has made my life so much easier . Staying at E.S is so convenient, that is why I would recommend anyone waiting for a house, relocating or just on vacation to stay at Extended Stay. If you're in Columbus Ohio, stay where I stayed, the freeways are right next door and the staff is impeccable!

title: “Seen better days?”
text:
Since this was a Kimpton property, I was expecting it to be just fine and then some. In reality, this place was like a theme hotel gone bad like a Vegas/ "Swingers" like hotel in DC. It was in need of a refresh. Chipped furniture, worn room, towels sub-par and so on. 
On the positive side: free wifi and good location.
I won't be back.

title: “Nothing special, just a good hotel”
text: I was there on a business trip, the hotel was nice and the staff was really helpfull and professional. The location of the hotel is good as well, close to the subway station so you're everywhere fairly quick.
