I didn't try the restaurant in the hotel since there're so many places closeby but it looked nice. The bathroom was a bit old-fashioned but the shower was good. The view from the room wasn't really good, but I guess if you pay more for a top floor room it is better. Would recommend it for business travellers, for vaction it is a bit plain, but then the rates are pretty good for that location so you might give it a try!

title: “3 star only..... Disappointing”
text:
Having just spent 3 nights at this property i can only use the word disappointing to describe the overall stay. Firstly the location is a little isolated there is not a lot around this hotel,without a car its virtually cab rides everywhere. Mission beach is about a 20 minute walk away.
The hotel is on the water and the rooms are quite nice, common areas clean and a lovely pool area. The red marlin restaurant serves nice food, fairly pricey, but the bar has the shortest happy hour in the U.S 3pm-5pm only.
If you don't like the sounds of seals in the early hours take ear plugs because they can make some noise.
Internet- I am at the stage now that if chains such as hyatt regency cannot offer free wifi at least in the lobby them i'm not using the hotel chain again. It is just poor marriott/sheraton all offer free wifi in their lobbies this hotel does not and boy do they nickel and dime you for it $6.00 for 15 minutes in the business centre.(love to know what plan that is)
There is no 24 hour room service...mind boggling if you take into consideration the location after 11pm there is no more food in the hotel.
Bottled water in the room $3 for the smallest bottle you have ever seen once again every room should get 1 complimentary bottle of water per day, as other chain do.
They have a small bakery/shop einstein bagels which only opens in the morning serving bagels. The shop is open the rest of the day charging obscene amounts for everyday items. like water $5 for 1 litre.
if your bringing the family to sea world and are hanging the pool all day this is probably not a bad option for you to stay, but for us Hyatt Mission Bay was disappointing.

title: “Quick visit to DC”
text: This hotel is located very close to all of DC's main attactions. For our group of 3 we wanted to be as close to the Smithsonian as possible and this was it. The hotel is located in a residential area, clean, safe and super close (walking) to EVERYTHING!! In the event you want to take a cab, lots around the area and very inexpensive. Hotel itself is older, but recently reno'd, clean and modern rooms with GREAT beds, nice sitting area and little coffee maker/fridge in room helps as well. Check in/out smooth and very easy, kind staff willing to ensure you have a great stay.

title: “Location, location, location!”
text: My partner and I just got back from a 5 day stay at The Galleria park hotel in San Fran. Having never been there before, I booked the hotel, scary, but I couldn't have made a better choice! It was completely central, convenient, completely affordable on my retail salary, such friendly staff and absolutely beautiful looking! The room was a street view room, which is a must - almost completely sound-proof! What a gem! Seriously, we will stay here every time we travel to San Fran - way to go, Galleria Park!

title: “Do not stay here if you want to sleep peacefully.”
text:
This is the absolute worst hotel by Starwood that I have ever seen. I travel every week and usually stay in a Hilton property. I got stuck with the Sheraton at Houston airport due to last minute booking and couldn't be more disgusted. I felt like I was dealing with a girl who wasn't capable of comprehension when I checked in. When I finally got to my room I immediately noticed the dingy, mold smell. Next thing I noticed were the dirty surfaces and stains on absolutely everything. I asked for sheets to cover the couch because it looked so terrible and old. I also borrowed cleaner to clean every surface. Sadly, this doesn't solve the stains on the bed including comforter, sheets, and bed skirt. The walls and lamp shades also have random stains all over them. The bathroom is tiny and has rusty fixtures. I'm am 100% disgusted by this establishment. My boss pricelined the hotel and I'm stuck here for 3 nights. 
I'm in hotel hell.

title: “Modern, clean and well located.”
text: Had a great stay. Good place to stay for a true sight seeing trip. Wouldn't stay here if I just wanted to hang out and relax.

title: “Historic and very good hotel in Boston”
text:
I´m a owner of Marriott vacation Club and decided to enjoy the lovely city of Boston! 
Great decision mainly for the Hotel cause the building is very interesting, an historical site in the city that´s in very good conditions, good maintenance.
Very good location with restaurants and shops( grocery right in front of the main entrance), 10 minutes walking to CVS and Washington Street where you can find some shops like Marshalls, TJMAXX Macys and HM.
The subway ( Aquarium Station) is in front the hotel too and the Boston Aquarium is two blocks walking.
The kitchen is little, just a microwave, a little refrigerator and a small sink but was enough for two.

title: “We will defintely be coming back to the Westin!”
text:
My husband comes every year to the Neocon Convention, so the location is great. he also has an early morning breakfast meeting with 25-30 people at your hotel(Woodtech).
Your service was very accomendating. I visited your workout room twice and Sam was the best. He not only helped me with my work out but encouraged, inspired and created a personal training workout just for me to take home. His passion to be heathy is contigous. I have bought my equipment and started my program.Thank You!
We look forward to next year or earlier for a vacation get away.

title: “Basic, but serves its purpose”
text:
Typically, when I go to New York, I stay just outside the city, but I was traveling with a friend who wanted to lodge in Manhattan. As one would expect, what you get in Manhattan for one price is of a lower caliber than what you get for the same price elsewhere. I'll be objective: the place is clean, and it's within a block or two of parking options and a subway stop. That's a plus. Upon checkin, they also informed us that they have free Wi-Fi, and those without Wi-Fi capabilities can connect for 10 cents per minute in their lounge area. Additionally, they offer coffee in the mornings. If you want these things, those are also a plus. The Hotel Alexander is in a safe location in a pretty laid-back part of Manhattan. We noticed a lot of bakeries and coffee shops (good for a convenient breakfast), groceries, and Mexican restaurants in the vicinity. It's an unexciting area, but it's nice.
The room: there was a dresser, a night table, a vanity (with a mirror), and a closet, which would all be good for a longer stay, if you needed to store things. The room also had a small armchair. The comforter was ripped, but the bedding was clean. There were three big windows (lots of light). If you're freezing at night, pull the blinds back and take a look at the window; they seem to leave the windows cracked, so that might be your problem.
On to the bathroom: there is a shared bathroom for every corridor on a given floor. The bathroom has the usual -- sink, shower/tub, toilet, toilet paper, towel rack, wastebasket , window, mirror -- but nothing else. There's no soap dispenser either (Bring your own soap to the bathroom.). Also, you aren't supposed to flush the paper (You dispose of it in the wastebasket by the toilet.). If you've traveled in developing countries, this isn't novel. But I've actually never seen this before in the U.S.. Just be aware that they only seem to clean the bathroom once a day, and the wastebasket in your (shared) bathroom will contain other pepole's dirty toilet paper. If you're alright with this, then that's good. If you've never seen this before, you might be disgusted. Depends on where you've been.
My friend was minorly inconvenienced by the fact that she had to ask at the front desk for towels and toilet paper (At one point, the bathroom ran out of it.), and that when she went downstairs for coffee in the morning, they were out of that as well. In a way, the staff seemed slightly unorganized; for instance, not keeping the bathrooms stocked with paper (for one), but also, on the morning we left, there was a pile of laundry on the elevator, just riding up and down the floors by itself. This isn't really a problem, but if you're a luxury traveler, you probably won't like this place. If all you want though is a clean place in a safe location, and you're looking for a cheap accomodation, the Hotel Alexander isn't bad. Just be aware that you could get a bigger, more comfortable room, in a hotel much closer to the more exciting parts of Manhattan, for the same price, by looking somewhere like Jersey City.
Would I stay here again? Probably not. But that's just because there are other options to be found in the area which offer a better "bang for your buck." If you don't mind basic accomodations and you don't feel inconvenienced by having to ask for things like towels, then there's absolutely nothing wrong with this hostel.

title: “Not very clean”
text:
Our room had an overwhelming stench of air freshener that gave us headache. The bathroom was dissapointing because it had a broken towel rack, broken soap dish,and a loose shower faucet that was sagging down the wall. And it was just all around dirty.
Beware parents:the windows open wide and have no screens.
The staff was professional and gave us a full refund.

title: “would definately go back!!”
text:
Let me first start by saying that when i comes to hotels i am very fussy...my mum and i booked this hotel for 6 nights.....it iswas spotlessly clean..beds and pillows very comfortable and an ideal location to Times Square. Port Authority bus station across the road with fab access straight to the airport for $15...don't waste your money for an expensive taxi.....The rooftop lounge has fab views of the city but you do pay for this in the cost drinks...The only thing i could moan about is ask for a room at the back or a floor up high..as we were on the 3rd floor and could here everything...and finally...the breakfast was great...lots of choice....filled hot muffins..bagels, cereals, fruit, quiche!!! i know...the americans must like this for breakfast...but it was all lovely....except for the plastic cutlery and throw away plares and bowls....
Faye and mum
from Chepstow, South Wales

title: “Great room but minor complaints”
text: We stayed in the Landmark Suite. What a great space?!! We enjoyed the room but thought it was odd that there were only two trash cans in the whole suite and they weren't in great locations. No trash can by the sink? Also, no entry closet for jackets, shoes, etc. And it was impossible to get cold water. Our sink only offered very warm and boiling hot water. Again, minor items but we can't rate this as "excellent" with these basic shortcomings.

title: “Great improvement”
text: I was really happy to see the improvements made to the hotel. The front desk staff was very friendly just like last time. My room was clean but the real bonus was that my room had a new flat screen tv instead of the old style ones. The front desk lady said they just finished all the rooms. I could tell from my last stay to this one that they are "freshening up" the hotel. Enjoyed my breakfast too! Oh, tried the lightrail since it stops in front of the hotel. Very easy!!

title: “The best location”
text:
Sleep Quality: One King bed that was very comfortable with good pillows. Room was quiet and dark.
Bathroom: Very tiny, with quite bad mould in the shower cubicle.
Food: Serve yourself to muffins, fruit, cereal, juice, hot beverages.
Location: Pure beach front – absolutely perfect. Our room was at the back of the hotel, overlooking the beach. 5 mins walk to restaurants and the tourist shops along Venice Beach.
Service: friendly staff on reception.
Value for money: Room was £100 per night including b/fast. Whilst it did represent great value and the location is brilliant, the tiny and mouldy bathroom really detracted from my stay. 
Other: More like a B&B. Cute small room on absolute beach front with kitchenette, fridge, dresser and free in room wi-fi. Small amount of parking available at the hotel. If cleanliness is your priority, this won’t be the place for you. Definitely worth considering if you want to wake up and look out across Venice Beach and can overlook a less than average bathroom.

title: “Great New York Experience”
text: This is the place to stay if you are looking for an authentic New York experience. The hotel is unlike any place I have ever stayed. The archetecture is authentic and it works to make itself a part of the neighborhood. The staff is unbelievably helpful. Paul, the night manager, was always available with anything we needed. Be sure to look at the art in the lobby. The owner painted it himself.

title: “Great location, and child friendly!”
text: We spent a memorable five nights in the Lenox with my family in June. We have three girls, and they each received a toy (stuffed dog) when we checked in. Our two year old even got some rubber duckies with her crib. The staff at the hotel was outstanding! They were friendly and helpful. They would welcome us back in a cheerful manner every-time, they lent us umbrellas when it was raining and the concierge was very helpful making recommendations from shopping destinations to activities for a rainy day. My kids loved the complimentary cookies and bananas at the front desk. The hotel offers complimentary wifi and the connection is very good at the lobby, but it was a little weak in our room which was located at the far corner in the 9th floor. The hotel location is great, it is located next to the library in Copley Square, two blocks away from Newberry street and a twenty minute walk from the Commons park. We would definitely stay at the Lenox in our next visit to Boston.

title: “Executive Floor? What a joke!”
text:
Being the first Staybridge to have an "Executive Floor" first got me excited. But after seeing what it's like makes me think twice going back. 
The only special about the top floor is the key card requirement when entering the elevator, and a "lounge"-no bigger than a master bedroom closet with a sofa, a desk -with Internet-ready computer and printer, and a small fridge with bottled water that ran out by the afternoon. The lounge does not serve breakfast. For that you have to go down to the lobby eating the same stuff everyone else is having. WiFi is basically non-exisitent during our stay. Staff blamed "increased usage" causing the breakdown and there wouldn't be anyone there to fix it until Monday, by then I was gone. This entire concept is a scam. House-keeping is a as-needed basis-another minus

title: “Glad I chose this hotel in Times Square!”
text:
Just completed a three night stay, ending mid- October, and have a great impression, overall! The front desk clerk was able to check us in to a room early, having just come off a cruise ship, and even gave us a lovely spacious corner suite, with wrap-aroud windows - bonus! Housekeeping always did a great job, as did the concierges each time we asked for advice or help.
The location can't be beat - right on Times Square so immediate access to theatres for Broadway shows, the Hop On - Hop Off tour buses and so on... A very pleasant surprise was the quality of food and service in the in-house restaurant "Brasserie 1605". They offer a very reasonably priced 3 course pre-show dinner, which we thoroughly enjoyed. So much so that we returned another evening, and each selection was well prepared and delicious. So nice to sit one level above the craziness of Times Square and enjoy a quiet meal as well.
While hotel prices in New York are very high overall, the Crowne Plaza Times Square seemed no more or less expensive than other choices. What sealed the choice for us, was being able to offset the cost by getting one night free using their Priority Club Reward Nights, a plan affiliated with the Air Miles program - therefore a huge saving.

title: “Run....there are other hotels for the same price”
text: I keep seeing people talking about how cheap it is to stay here......."so they say get over the mold!" We stayed there less than 24 hours and were charged $374.60! I don't think that's BUDGET! Yes, we checked out the next day......yes, two different rooms......horrible smell......ceiling falling down........furniture that should be put out for the trash (if it was no one would pick it up, it's not even fit to sell at a garage sale). Let me expain....no drawer handles, broken legs, the dresser tops were broken off. The sheets were so worn and rotten they were filled with holes. The pictures you see are real, the stories you hear are true! The first time I talked to the desk clerk, I was told............."These are the types of rooms hotels contracts for, if you have a problem...call them." Hotels got me a different room......same quality. Since we were there for 10 days, we found another hotel. Won't book on hotels again, cost too much!Won't EVER go back to the Pennsylvania Hotel, Central Park really is better! There might be nice rooms here, but why chance it, especially if you have your family with you? I really think the people who had nice rooms were real lucky or are employess and others who were paid to give this place a good rating! BEWARE!

title: “Nice Stay.”
text: This is a good hotel choice for the price. The grounds are kept nice and they were planting flowers while my child and I were there. Pool area is kept up nice and is large/heated. Restaurant/bar borders the pool area. I needed a one night stay because the first night of our trip was not available at my hotel of choice. Wish I had stayed here all three nights. I was reluctant to stay here because it was a drive up to your room hotel....which I do not prefer. It was fine. My child liked the pool area. Room area was clean. Staff were nice. Price was fair. No complaints.

title: “Great Time”
text: I stayed at the Carlton and I thought it was a great hotel. The space is beautiful and the neighborhood has a lot of great restaurants. Staff was wonderful to everyone in my group. For the value it was excellent.

title: “Decent place for a night's stay at a decent price”
text: The Ramada Limited Indianapolis West at W. 38th St. and I-465 exit is a decent place for one night or a weekend without breaking your budget. The rooms are small but clean. The staff was very helpful and courteous. The hotel is a bit hard to find--make sure you are in the right hand lane coming off the interstate so you can turn into the access road at the first stoplight. You have to wind your way around the access road.

title: “great location”
text: Overall this was a wonderful choice for a weekend with a family. To have a suite was ideal. It was great to be so close to Boston Common. The hotel was family friendly. There was one inconvenience. When we checked in around 4 PM our suite was not ready. We stored our luggage and were told we'd be called when we could get into the room. By 7 PM we still had not received a call. I called the hotel and was told our room was still not ready. I replied that when we returned after dinner I would be very unhappy if we still couldn't get into our room. It was ready when we got to the hotel around 8 PM.

title: “I expected more.”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Ballantyne on our wedding night as we had to catch a 6 am flight. The resort was just okay. Check-in was efficient and we were taken to our room. We had a comfy king bed, sitting area, armoir, tv, mini bar and decent bathroom. 
Our stay was fine, but for our wedding night, I just expected the property to give us wine/flowers or some type of view. A lot of people rave about staying at the Ballantyne, but it was nothing special to me. Thankfully, my husband is amazing. Check out was fine and we used the hotel car to go to the airport. No complaints.

title: “Don't worry about a thing”
text:
My friend and I and our three daughters (14,16,20) stayed in room 22G (2 bedroom suite) at The Eastgate this half term (21st to 28th October).
When we arrived we had dropped off various parties via the Shuttle bus from Newark airport. They all seemed to be staying at very glossy-fronted establishments and when we saw The Eastgate we thought "ordinary, nice-ish, passable but not glossy". However the minute we saw our suite we changed our minds. It VASTLY exceeded oue expectations! I snore, so took the smaller bedroom (big!) My girls were more than happy to share the huge lounge sofabed. My friend and her daughter took the bigger bedroom. We had loads of space-and that includes cupboards and hanging space. There were 2 little bathrooms each with a hairdryer (bath AND shower). The little kitchen was much used, and had everything we needed. The available space was fantastic. We enjoyed being together but not "confined". Location was great. Sadly my 20 year old's phone went unexplicably missing from her bedside( was using it as an alarm clock ). The verdict remains open on that one. The staff were as helpful as they could be in the circumstances. 
The view from front and back windows was excellent. The Trend Cafe is a great Deli opposite The Frontier Diner on the corner.
Cleanliness was first class -I had to mop a flood in the bathroom and the white towel used did not register one speck of dirt! It was pristine after the mopping up!
Everyone was nice and I would recommend this hotel. I had been to NY before but my hotel was not half as good- snooty beyond belief and my face didn't fit, along with crummy accommodation. This was so much better.

title: “Great location and most comfortable beds!”
text: We have stayed here twice and have had a great experience both times. The location is amazing and the hotel rooms are modern, clean and the most comfortable beds. We highly recommend the Le Parker Meridien and will stay there again.

title: “Girls Weekend”
text: My sister and I just got back from a girl weekend in LA, and we stayed at Loews Hollywood. Great hotel in the midst of hollywood. Literally a 2 minute walk from great shopping, dining and tourist attractions. Tyler at the concierge desk gave us great restaurant and nightlife advice. We tried a mexican restaurant ony Tylers advice, Loteria. Delicious, authentic mexican food for a great price and the margritas are to die for. Another great gem of a restaurant is 25 degrees in the Roosevelt hotel. Amazing Burgers! California Pizza kitchen had great food, atmosphere and price. Hotel was perfect for first time LA travelers. Only bummer....hotel breakfast very expensive...go to Mels Diner instead...and WIFI not included.

title: “Great stay. I'll be back”
text: I thoroughly enjoyed my stay. I was here on business and will be back again in a couple of months. Thank you.

title: “Value for money in great location”
text:
We had booked before checking TripAdvisor and were worried after reading some of the very negative reviews but were pleasantly surprised when we got there. All staff we met were friendly and helpful, our room was clean, so were the beds and bathroom. There were four of us in the room and there was enough space for our 3-night stay. 
We had sufficient coffee, tea, iron, hairdryer, towels, soaps, etc. The beds were very soft. It's so close to the major shops (Nordstrom, Macy's, Pacific Place) that one could shop, drop it all off back at the hotel and go back again for more. Good restaurants nearby. The breakfast in the hotel wasn't too bad either and again very friendly staff. 
I would definitely stay here again and spend my money on food and clothing/cosmetics rather than on a more expensive hotel room.

title: “Crowded, huge hotel, tiny rooms, good location”
text:
Booked a room for one night for around $170, around new year's eve. The lobby was teeming with people: waiting in line to check in, check out, just walking around, or looking for the ticket counter. Elevators are always busy. Corridors are dim-lit and not very nice.
Renovations seem to be imminent (January 2012). Heating in my room was not working, which was not very convenient for mid-winter. Called housekeeping, and after reviewing the AC unit they determined it should be changed, Nothing they could do until the next morning, so they offered to get a small portable heater. The front desk offered another room on the same floor.
Both of the rooms were minute, barely enough for 2 people. Space between the bed and the wall was extremely narrow, views out of the window were very urban, but nice. The overall feel was that pending renovations would be very welcome. I could actually hear the banging of hammers for these renovations elsewhere in the hotel - they started at 8:00 am!
Bathroom was also small, but usable. Toiletries were OK.
Next door cafeteria was convenient. Being right beside a subway station entrance is a plus - probably the only one for this hotel.

title: “Do Not Stay Here.”
text: Buyer Beware. This is the worst hotel for the price that I've ever been to. The hot water went out monday morning at 5 am, and wasn't on until noon. The next day, the air went out, and the room was hot and stale. The service is extremely unprofessional, and made us to feel like we were not even here. That is, the ones who can speak english. We will never stay here again, and will caution all of our friends visiting houston to be sure not to. A best western is higher class than this place. Also, the internet may be free, but it's incredibly slow. It took me so long to check my email, I just went and found wireless somewhere else. Oh, and don't expect if you want breakfast that you can just leave the filled out tag on your door, and it'll be there in the morning. The only thing that will be there in the morning is the tag itself, and when you call them to ask them why it wasn't picked up, they'll accuse you of leaving it after 2am, even if you put it out at 10pm. Save your business for people who care to have it. Oh, and the sink was broken, but that was the least inconvenient part of our experience.

title: “great location an fine service”
text: they know how to take care of business guests without getting in the way. walking distance to lots of nice stores - especially Kramer Books. next to the Metro to, so easy to get anywhere.

title: “A great place to stay in Philly!”
text: An old building that adds to the charm of staying close to Old Town. Great location for sightseeing, restaurants and night life within walking distance. Rooms are a little small but have high ceilings and large updated bathrooms. The front desk staff are incredibly nice and go out of their way to be helpful. They recommended great places to eat within walking distance of the hotel. With tea & cookies, and sometimes wine and cheese in the evening, as well as complimentary breakfast, it felt like we staying at a bed and breakfast, instead of a hotel! Well worth the money.

title: “Not Bad At ALL !!!”
text:
Don't complain...
We read the reviews and was terrified and wanted to change rooms before we even got there, but man it was nice compared to our expectations. 
- Our room was cleaned EVERY day
- Good aircondition
- Nice staff
But seriously what did you guys expect for 100 $ per night and across Madison Square Garden ( close to everything ) ??
We stayed their for 9 nights and enjoyed every single day.

title: “Nice Hotel!”
text: We needed a place to stay after the Giants game. AT&T was about a mile away - no problem walking. It was close to shopping and restaurants. Our room was small but had every amenity one could need. The bed was comfortable and the room was nicely furnished. Price was reasonable and the staff was very helpful. Our friends' room was a suite so it had a living room area with a couch and a lot of room to move about. Definitely would stay here again. Street noise a little bit of a problem, but we heard no one in the rooms next to us and the hotel was fully booked.

title: “Oct. 9,10 20112”
text: I have been staying with you over a period of months while undergoing treatment at Mayo as I am sure many do. This is the first time I have been disappointed in the cleanliness o fthe room. Perhaps you are rehabbing some of the rooms. This one certainly needs it. Otherwise service was as always very acceptable.

title: “Fantastic Suite Deal”
text: I thoroughly enjoyed my one night stay at this hotel. We had the two bedroom, two bath suite. One bedroom had two double beds, the other had a queen and the living room had a sleeper sofa. In addition to the great beds we had a full kitchen with utensils and serving dishes. The television got HBO and there was a DVD player attached! The only downside to this hotel is that there is only full housekeeping once a week. The rest of the time they have "light" housekeeping whereby your towels get replaced and beds made. If you don't mind this then you should definately try Staybridge.

title: “Horrible”
text: The room was not what was advertised on the website. We reserved a Deluxe Room, which we dedided on upon seeing the pictures and we were given a standard room. We had to change rooms because of a horrible smell, but the second room was no different. When we spoke to Management they told us the room was a more than actually an upgrade, which I don't know what an upgrade to what? We ended up rather loosing our money and went to a different Hotel around midnight.

title: “A very pleasureable business stay”
text:
Stayed here for 2 nights on business. After about a 10-15 minute cab ride from the airport, I had an efficient check in at the front desk. I received a King room located at the end of a hallway on the 6th floor with large windows that overlooked the city. Room was modern, clean and incredibly spacious with a chair and sofa and a desk with multiple, easy to access outlets to charge my laptop and phone. Bathroom was also a good size with a large vanity and standalone shower (no tub) and brand-name Aveda toiletries were a nice touch. The bed was so comfortable I slept like a log both nights even without any room darkening shades drawn. Also included a safe, small mini-fridge and single cup coffee brewer. Would have been nice to have more than one coffee packet though. 
Had several drinks at the downstairs bar. Wait staff was attentive and drinks were very good (and not at all watered down). Lots of restaurants within walking distance and across the street from a very small, sweet public park which I spent some quiet time meandering through. 
The only complaint I had was with the bell staff after I checked my bags for a few hours while I explored the city. There didn't seem to be enough of them working for the volume of guests at the hotel. I had to wait at least 15 minutes before I saw one and then had to practically jump him to give him my ticket even though I was standing at his desk with my ticket out and visible. 
Other than that, it was a very pleasureable stay all in all.

title: “Top location with very friendly, helpful staff.”
text:
Our stay at this hotel was excellent, room was a good size for New York, with an good air condtioning system which was needed due to New York having record hot weather during our stay. There was a microwave and fridge in the room which was a nice touch and enabled us to store much needed cold drinks.
Hotel was very clean and 100% smoke free which was very noticeable and pleasant. All staff from check in to check out where very helpful and pleasant. Donald the bellman was lovely, always cheery and happy to help with anything from bags to directions.
The location of the hotel is good a lot of the sites to visit with in easy access, either by foot, bus or subway. There very nice restaurants of varying price range within walking distance. Juniors for breakfast is a must. 
We would highly recomend the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square.

title: “Great Hotel, excellent location”
text:
We stayed at the Beverly laurel for 2 nights, on our first trip to America, on our way to Vegas.
We wanted a place that was in West Hollywood, was fun, and was reasonably priced! From menory, it was approx US$100 a night.
We read about the Beverly Laurel here on Trip Advisor, but unfortunatly, they dont have a website, so we felt like we were booking a bit blind, so we were a bit unsure about what we'd walk into!
The people there were friendly, and happy to point us in the right direction for things to see. The hotel itself is pretty basic, but its clean and comfortable; it was well serviced both days we were there. Its by a reasonably busy street, but we didnt notice any noise at all. 
We thought it was really good value for money. It was a great intro to America, and we enjoyed our stay.
There is an excellent diner downstairs called Swingers. I had the best burger that I'ver ever tasted there! I'd go back there just for the burger!
The location is great, just down the road from Farmers Market (really nice), and a $10 cab ride to either Sunset Bvld, or Hollywood Bvld.
We'd recomment it if you want a place with some spirit, and dont need luxury!

title: “great place to stay, great location”
text: Great place overall, excellent service and comfortable room. Could hear the neighbors on each side a bit, but apart from that, it was perfection. The hotel is in close proximity and walking distance to the tourist attractions and downtown.

title: “Fab Hotel Very Funky”
text:
I must say I was very worried when i read the reviews on this site but im pleased to say I had a great time at this hotel.
The rooms are small I suppose but not uncomfortable so the staff were great when i spoke to them,which i do admit was not alot I was too busy out having fun.
The location is fabulous a 5 minute walk to Central Park and a 15 minute walk to Times square with lots of things to eat and see on the way(Broadway etc).
Overall i had a great time and would go back again for sure.

title: “Absolutely loved this place”
text:
First of all, the lady at the front desk was very nice and quite helpful. The rooms are clean and very nice. They took the time to add very nice details. This hotel has a very New York City hotel vibe to it- very cool!!! I read some of the other reviews, and I really never thought of this hotel as being noisy; however, I did stay on a Sunday night. While it's not on Beale St., you are only a $6 cab ride away. 
Just a few hints for tourists- skip Rendezvous Ribs- always a huge line and very pricy. Instead, check out Central Ave. Ribs. This is where the locals go. It's not decorated really fancy, but the food is GREAT- Ribs for two with four sides for only $20. 
Also, for breakfast- check out a little mom and pop dinner called Barksdale. It's not health food, but it is the BEST southern style breakfast you can find. 
For good music, check out the Rum Boogie Cafe on Beale St. It's authentic blues music. 
Even if you skip all of this, the hotel is still worth the money.

title: “Fabulous wedding venue!!!”
text:
I'm rating this hotel based on my experience there attending a wedding over the weekend. This hotel is so beautiful! I love the old world class feel, the chandeliers, the candelabras, absolutely a WOW! The ballroom is magnificent!!! The wedding we attended was probably the most beautiful setting I've ever been. The columns in the ballroom, the candles & flowers. Gorgeous, gorgeous, gorgeous!!! The cocktail hour was delicious! I enjoyed the seafood & passed appetizers. However, we were disappointed with dinner. I guess because because it was mass produced, they aren't as fresh. The steak was overdone & the fish as well. The dessert table looked really tempting, but their dessert fell short as well. The hotel though need to upgrade their restrooms.
Overall as far experience of the venue, I think it's a grand venue if you like that Old World Regal feel.

title: “OKAY but...not worth the money spent”
text: We stayed at the Royal Palm. It's a nice place, the people are nice too but the money spent is not worth it. The facilities are old, you have to pay for internet and parking. On the lighter side, you can just walk to the mall across the street.

title: “Worst Hotel Experience In a Long Time”
text:
This hotel could have been better however the service was horrible and several things made this an awful experience.
First, I book their Alden website rate (Internet Promotion). This rate still allows you to cancel or modify the day prior to arrival by 6PM to avoid penalty. I did this as I was having surgery the day I was supposed to arrive. The front desk person I reached changed my reservation quickly and was very nice. I arrive the following day as scheduled and I am told that I was a no show the day before. I explained and showed that I had called on caller id. The desk person proceeded to tell me that I had been charged for an advance purchase and would not get a refund for being a no show. I show him the confirmation email that says I have until 6PM the day before to cancel as I did and he kept saying that I had an advance purchase. I told them I never book those and that I did not book the advance purchase. I called the manager. The manager came over and was very unprofessional. He did not greet us courteously as other managers at hotel chains would and did not try to figure out the problem. Before even looking into it or really hearing what we had to say he said you cannot get a refund. I told him that I stay at hotels every week and had never been treated like this before. He gave me his card and told me to email him and he would respond back that I could use my no show night another time. I felt railroaded into this as I did not book that rate and their confirmation tells you that you can cancel. He tried to say that the rate means something else but in other places had I booked an advance purchase the confirmation would say that and say non-refundable. He tried to say it says it on the website and not confirmation. I will come back to this in a moment.
Second thing was the elevators smelled like someone had thrown upt. Several people complained and they did not try to remedy the problem. .
Third, the air conditioner would not go off. We arrived back in our room to find it was stuck at 57 degrees. It was freezing. When you hit off, it blowed more cold air. We called maintenance and he could not fix it. So we were moved to two king rooms as a double was not available. One of the king rooms was broken as well and stayed at 60 degrees but at least would shut off. My friend stayed in my room for part of the night as the cold was unbearable. They did give us some extra uncovered down comforters and blankets. There were no apologies for the inconvenience or anything.
In the morning, we received a bill for what we were told we paid for already. Upon checkout I ask the clerk and he said their advance purchase went down two days ago. Well I booked my reservation 2 months ago and when I looked at my Amex, I had not been charged. So he explains I wasn't charged cause of the system going down 2 days ago. Well I did not book an advance purchase so that was why I wasn't charged. The clerk I changed the reservation with must have changed the reservation to say advance purchase or something. Regardless the clerk never mentioned this when changing the reservation. 
Usually places are far more professional and courteous as they want you to return. The Alden can be sure that I will never return. The manager did try to do something other hotels may have done and had a fruit plate in our room with 2 bottles of sparking water with a note. The plate was uncovered and who knows how long it sat there. It was 57 in the room so it stayed fresh. It should have been wrapped though. I shutter to think it road in the nasty elevator and then sat in our room for hours. 
Today I found my printed confirmation. I went on the site and did a little research. There is an advanced purchase rate. It is non-refundable and it says that and the wording is totally different. There is also an Alden hotel rate Internet Promotion and it is refundable as the wording outlines. So ultimately no one at the hotel knows their own policies or website. Had I been charged the entire rate I was going to dispute it with the proof they sent me in the confirmation. This was a horrible stressful trip and I was not compensated for how bad the stay was... I paid my full scheduled rate. As my mom said, I should have stayed at Marriott, Sheraton or Hilton. I know next time.

title: “Stay somewhere else”
text:
Room at check in at 415 was not ready. Was told I could have another room without a Times Square view. I booked in March so not sure why they would think I would want a different room.
Requested extra towels and a fan in the room ahead of time via phone. Never saw them the entire 3 night stay. Unfriendly staff except for bellman. I requested a birthday cake for my son to be delivered at 10AM on Monday. They said no problem. Still didn't see it at 1035. I told them I did not want it now too late as we were leaving. Had to go to front desk to get it off my bill although they told me on the phone they would take it of bil

title: “Could not be happier”
text: We stayed for ten nights and had a great stay.The rooms were clean and quiet and the kitchen was a massive bonus.We had one problem when the tap valve burst but we were upgraded to another room straight away.The staff were always very helpful and the internet come in very handy.Its close to the subway and the bus.I would stay there anytime.

title: “Hotel is okay, clean. Free parking a plus.”
text: Romms should have coffee makers...even the cheapest hotels (this one was not cheap) have coffee makers and complimentary coffe in the rooms.

title: “The Palace is still a Palace”
text:
The New York Palace is indeed one of New York´s top hotels. I stayed there last June for a few nights and from the moment we walked through the front door we were treated like rayalties. Although we walked in wearing Jeans and cardigan we were treated with dignety and rescept and one never got the feeling that that the staff look down on you whatever you were wearind, something that does happen at some grand luxury hotels. 
We stayed in a deluxe king corner room and the room was pleasing and it spacious decour made it fell lager than it´s 350 something square feet. Both the common areas of the hotel and the room combined opulence from a bygone era with modern amenities like in-room climate control and a 40 inch plasma.
We ate at the Istana restaurant twice and although there was nothing special about the food, the swift and very polite service made up for it.
The New York Palce in not generally considered to be one of New York´s top hotels. People have told me that it´s nothing compared to the likes of the Peninsula, The Plaza or Ritz-Carlton central park but I beg to differ! The location of the Palace is excellent much better in fact than the upper east siders (pierre and peninsula). The Palace manages to be a great luxury hotel without an attitude snobbery or selectiveness. Sure, it´s not as glamorous or flamboyant as the Plaza or Peninsula but with glamour comes excruciatingly tight security and the occasional snobbery so for me the New York Palce is one my top choices for New York accomodation.

title: “Fun Birthday Weekend”
text:
I can't say enough about the location of the hotel to everything in NYC. When we arrived we were told the rooms we reserved through "Priceline" weren't guaranteed, what was guaranteed was we would have two rooms. Initially, we were offered two rooms w/king size beds. We had six travelers and that would not have worked. We had to pay for an upgrade to a suite and one king room. Also, it wasn't offered to us - we had to ask if suites were available. It was disappointing we had to pay for the upgrade when we initially booked what we needed. 
The king room was nice, the suite was okay - two full size bathrooms (only one shower worked). The furnishings were a bit shabby,couche/chairs/tables had very worn areas. Pull out bed was comfortable.
Again, we did like the proximity to all attractions, the bar was nice, and staff helpful. We would stay again but only book through the hotel to make sure we got the rooms we reserved.

title: “Nice Hotel - Will Stay Again!”
text:
Stayed at the Hotel Palomar for three nights first week of December. The Hotel Palomar rates were very competitive with other hotel in Chicago. BUT, at the Hotel Palomar, there is a popular wine social nightly, Etro soap, shampoo, conditioner, lotion - great bathroom. I had beautiful corner room.
Great Service: I did not have a coffee maker in the room, asked for one, they delievered a Keurig coffee maker with a lot of K-cups. Needed cream, got it.
Location; great. Walked to everything. (Location is most important to me) 
The Sable Restaurant is attached to the Hotel (Executive Chef is a Top Chef Contestant) The Sable is known for mixology "department" - order a mixed drink! (if you're 21 and older:) The food is very tasty too. 
I look forward to my next stay - everything you want in a hotel.

title: “A scary Halloween type place.....”
text:
We booked our room online, and were obviously fooled by the photos from the website. The lobby is not a good indication of what kind of room you will be getting! Once you leave the lobby and get off the elevator at your floor you will step into a horror film. The carpets are dirty and coming apart and are taped down with duct tape in places. The walls are filthy and the doors to the rooms are the strangest things I have ever seen in a hotel....and they are all stained and crumbling. And all this is before you set foot in your room! When me and my wife set foot in our room we both almost burst out crying..it was so bad. We didn't expect any luxury for what we were paying, but what we did expect was at least a clean place to lay our heads at night. This was NOT that place. The "double" bed was tiny, delapidated and the mattress was worryingly stained. The bed linen was awful with a heavy, itchy old blanket on top. The room itself was shocking...paint was peeling everywhere...the walls, doors and carpet had stains all over them. The A/C was busted. The bathroom was actually not bad in comparison althougth I must say I tended to squint a bit when I was in there so I didn't spot anything that might have freaked me out. They were very random with the clean towels...some days we got some, some days we got none. 
It was a good job we were to spend minimal time in our room...we got up early and stayed out very late most days just so we could be away from the place...so much for a nice, relaxing, lazy weekend in New York! 
There were always long lines at the front desk and check in seemed to take forever. The staff were kind of unfriendly as if they were doing us a favour by checking us in at all. 
I'm glad we only stayed here for a weekend because I couldn't imagine being there any longer than that. Anyone that goes back to stay here after one visit much be a masochist! I would never stay here again...and would definitley advise anyone I cared about NOT to stay here. Do not be fooled by the online photos or the location, spend a bit extra money and go and stay somewhere else. This is what we will do next time. This place is daylight robbery and I'm surprised that people can get away with running such a dump of a hotel in this day and age.

title: “What a rat hole!”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights for a corporate event. The heating system was like a broken jet engine. I asked them to take a look and they told me "that's the way it is." The yshut down their WiFi service in the middle of my stay because of coverage problems. No WiFi in a Silicon Valley hotel? Avoid this hotel at all costs!

title: “Great location, great hotel”
text: My family and I (wife and girls 6 and 9) stayed here on a Friday night. The hotel was in walking distance to all the museums and the monuments. There is a metro stop 2 blocks away for those who don't want to walk and there are always taxis out front if needed. The room was clean and large and there was a Starbucks in the lobby for an early morning drink or snack. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “BEWARE OF BEDBUGS”
text: I stayed there last week-end of the 7th and 8th. On Tuesday these large red bites appeared on my body. They were from bed-bugs. My call and email weren't returned. They are once again on the bed-bug register. Inspect your romm very carefully. The bites are miserable. These things happens even in very lovely surroundings. I think it is very poor that they ignore my reports.

title: “Smoke gets in your eyes”
text: My room, labeled "non-smoking", was premeated by cigarette smoke through and through. It was as though a 4 pack per day smoker had been in the room 24-7 for months. It is inconceivable to me how a non-smoking room, on a non-smoking floor, and surrounded entirely by other non-smoking rooms could be this saturated with cigarette smoke. I have stayed in "smoking" rooms that had far less smoke odor than this one. In addition, the shower drain was plugged up so badly that over-the-ankle deep water pooled in the tub during a shower. I will definitely avoid this site in the future and will not recommend it to others.

title: “First Hamption Experience - nice place”
text:
Normally stay at full-service hotels. Had tix for a show and found a good price on the hilton.com site, we're HH members and the reviews of others on this site gave us encouragement to try their Hamption Inn hotel for a change.
It was clean, well taken care of, friendly staff and had a better then expected breakfast buffet.
Location was perfect - we felt safe walking in the area of the hotel.
Can't beat it for the price.
Will be back.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: i stayed here for one night as i visited Seattle while visitng family in Vancouver. The hotel staff we very good on check in, and the hotel was really nice. There was internet in the room which was very handy. The hotel is in a good location for wanting to see the city. I was only there for one night and it was a very comfotable stay, i would recommend this to anyone.

title: “Very convenient, friendly staff, basic amenities”
text:
I stayed at the hotel whil attending a conference. As a student, I wanted something cheap but convenient. The Union Square Plaza was perfect for that. Okay, I did not have a woderful view, but it was quiet, the room was bright and big and even though the hotel does need some renovations, still it was clean. The great shops of Union Square are 5 minutes away, the subway, the trams, the buses within 2 minutes walk. It was extremely easy just to get anywhere and the ocean about 15 minutes walk away!
There is no restaurant in the hotel but who cares? So many great places to chose from just around the hotel. The theatre accross the road is great too if you fancy a night of culture and all the galleries and antique shops are nearby.
The staff were very friendly. On my check-out day my flight was in the evening and they let me keep the room with No extra charge till I needed to leave for the report.Great, eh? Which big, chain hotel would let you do that?
I cannot wait to go to SF again and stay at the Union Sqaure Plaza!

title: “Bleh!”
text: What a disappointment! The hotel location on the web was given as Marina Del Rey, but when we actually drove there we found it was a couple of miles east of there, in a seedy looking part of Culver City. The room was clean enough, but by the time we paid the room rate (which we booked it for only because of the listed location) and the additional roll-away fee for our third child, it was $20 more than the 4-star Westin at the airport, about 10 minutes further away! If it was cheap and you understood where it was, it would be okay, but if you are expecting value near the beach, this isn't it.

title: “Previous negative reviews concerned me”
text:
We went to Baltimore and stayed at the Tremont because a block of rooms had been reserved for the out-of-town wedding guests.
I was really braced for a negative experience, based on recent reviews that I read on TripAdvisor. However, I have to tell you that it was not as bad as I was braced for.
Yes, the rooms are a bit tired, but for about $120/night, where else can you get a room with a small, but efficient kitchenette that has dishes/glassware/silverware for four? Good value for the money.
It is about a 15-minute walk to the inner harbor, so the location is great.
I also found the staff to be friendly and courteous.
The one big negative is that the TVs are ancient and small screen size.

title: “It was okay.....”
text:
We just returned from NYC and had stayed at the Affinia Shelburne. I was excited about booking it because of the amazing reviews, but I am sorry to say that I cannot share the enthusiasm. I shared a room with my 12 year old daugher; my husband shared a room with his 15 year old daughter. 
The good:
- Location, location, location
- Checkin/checkout staff - super friendly and helpful
- Concierge - very helpful when asked about food options
- My daughter loved the sound pillow from the pillow menu
- room service was very prompt and tasted great
- We ate a Rare for some burgers and fries - very good
The bad -
- Some of the elevators were not working, so there was a wait sometimes
- Traffic noise from the street was very loud
- Walls are very thin - we could hear our neighbors conversation very clearly
- I opted for a swedish memory pillow from the pillow menu, as I have neck problems. This pillow was much like a flat pancake with a bit of a bump. Awful.
- The printer in the business center would not work for me to print my boarding passes. The concierge had to print them for me, which took a while, but he was great about helping me out. 
The ugly -
- Our bathtub had a bunch of hair in it when we arrived
- The reason there was hair in the bathtub was because it did not drain correctly. I reported this to maintenance, but it was never fixed.
- We ran out of toilet paper! It is not like we were there much.....maid service just did not provide any spares.
I really, really wanted to give this hotel wonderful reviews, but I cannot. For location, I would recommend this hotel, as long as you are aware that there is a lot of room for improvement.

title: “By far the best hotel we have ever stayed at!”
text:
My husband and I have stayed at this hotel on two separate occasions now and both stays were fantastic. Our first visit was so memorable, that for our honeymoon, after deciding to vacation in California for the week, we booked this hotel immediately. As soon as we walked in the lobby, we were greated with several smiling staff members who were very polite and helpful. During check-in, the staff makes you feel very welcome. After about 5 minutes of being in our room, we had a knock at our door and there was a member of the staff there with a bottle of champagne, two glasses, and a personalized note congradulating us on our recent marriage. Later on, someone called to make sure everything with the room was satisfactory and told us to let them know if we needed anything at all. Our view from our balcony was amazing. The rooms are very comfortable and very quiet. Everything about the hotel is luxurious and elegant. There were a couple of times we called to the front desk, one time to ask about a restaurant recommendation, and they had a brochure and coupons to our room in probably 2 minutes! 
You will not be dissapointed in the slightest with this hotel. The views are spectacular, the area is safe, the rooms are clean and beautiful, and most of all, the staff is very helpful and always polite. They really go out of their way to make your stay as wonderful as possible.

title: “You could not PAY me to stay at this hotel again!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for four VERY LONG DAYS. Although the renovation was supposed to be complete by the time of our stay, it definitley was not. There were holes in the walls, some spackled over, some not. We reserved a suite, and had documents proving so, but they didn't have one "available." They were attempting to install kitchettes in the rooms, but ours had only and empty basin where the sink should be with the hoses and attachments thrown in the hole. Several times during our stay maintence (who spoke little English) would barge into the room and ask if we had a working sink, which we never did. They did knock once and then entered, no matter if we said "COME IN" or not. At least their key cards worked, which ours never did. We had to have them changed almost everytime we left the room because they wouldn't work more than once. When we arrived, there was a large wet spot in our room where it appeared the toilet had overflown from the last guests. As it was still wet, we called the front desk to have them clean it, which they never showed up to do. We just threw towels on it and walked over it all weekend. Iron did not work, ironing board had legs broken off, pool area was dirty, people were allowed to smoke while IN THE POOL which made the water dirty. Hallways smelled musty. TERRIBLE location, impossible to drive anywhere the loop was so crowded. The only good part was the breakfast in the morning. Although it was an extra charge (not comp.) it was still really good food. WHAT A DUMP!

title: “Comfortable hotel, friendly staff”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Argonaut for 4 nights on a recent business trip. We needed a comfortable place to stay, good internet service, access to nice walks and good food, and a friendly staff. The Argonaut provided it all, with complementary wine to boot. In fact, we got to the wine service 15 minutes late on our first day, but within seconds a bellman dropped what he was doing and asked us: "Red or white?" and returned in a minute with those welcoming glasses of wine. So, pleasant surprises, and no unpleasant ones.

title: “Hospitality makes the stay!”
text:
I have never stayed at a hotel where I have been treated so nicely, and where the staff is accomodating and genuinely interested in helping you and making sure that you have everything that you need. Form early checkin to directions to wherever we wanted to go, the staff was ready and able to assist. 
The hotel is very nice, clean, and located close enough to anywhere you want to go. The Chicago experience involves the train and walking through beautiful downtown, and the location of this hotel gives you a chance ot experience the city that way. 
There are an abundance of local, non-chain restaurants within walking distance so you won't go hungry! The hotel also has its own restaurant that serves a delicious breakfast.

title: “You can do better”
text:
For years I'd see the vintage brick tower of the Washington Marriott Wardman Park poking up through the trees and wonder what it would be like to stay there. I'm still wondering because, as my wife and I discovered in September '09, the tower is rarely used these days, and the rest of the Marriott Wardman Park is a sprawling, boxy, fairly non-descript facility tucked behind the tower and its park-like grounds.
Our adequately sized room was decently furnished, but had no view to speak of. And get this, mini-refrigerators are available only if you make a request beforehand. Also, the hotel has no in-room wi-fi and charges a ridiculous fee for wire internet, so we had to either cue up for one of the three computers provided in the hotel lobby or hump our laptop down to one of the nearby street cafes and tap into their network. Concerning parking: If you plan on not taking your car out of the garage during your stay (there's a Metro stop just steps from the hotel grounds), do not pay at the front desk, it will cost more. Pay the garage attendant and save a few bucks.
On the plus side, the hotel is conveniently located near The Metro, as I said, and a slew of cafes, Adams-Morgan and the zoo. It has a nice outdoor pool and they deliver USA Today to your door in the morning (too bad they don't give you The Post). 
Overall, the Washington Marriott Wardman Park was a disappointment, and for the same rate we paid, we probably could have landed a room in the much nicer Kimpton Hotel Palomar at Dupont Circle.

title: “Love the rooms, atmosphere and neighborhood”
text:
I really like the room, staff and the atmosphere. The doorman was very helpful in making recommendations of places to eat and local attractions.
I want a make up mirror like the one in my room...very cool!
What is really cool about this hotel is they offer FREE loaner bikes and all the safety equipment you need, so there is no need to use the public transportation or cabs unless you are going to the airport.
They had a wine tasting one evening when I was there and another evening they had a Philly Cheese steak tasting. They closed off the street below and had a live band and the popular Philly Cheese steak restaurants catered. The other guests were very friendly...no snob factor at all, even though this is a four star hotel!
I love the neighborhood and I will definitely start looking for other Kimpton Hotels when I travel again!

title: “Great value in NYC”
text: Our family of 4 (2 teenagers) stayed at the Lucerne for 5 nights in July and we could not have been happier. The location on the Upper West Side enabled us to get out of the hustle and bustle of midtown and stay in a quiet and charming neighborhood, yet was within a couple of blocks of two subway lines. The room (we had a corner double) was large enough and was clean, cool (important, since it got into the 90s that week), and nicely decorated. The Lucerne has the look and feel of an older European-style hotel, and we found the staff to be gracious and helpful. Best of all, the rate was extremely reasonable for New York.

title: “Beautiful”
text: We stayed at the hotel because of the location and the great rate. Everyone that we had contact was very friendly and helpful. The hotel is just a few blocks from the White House and within walking distance to the Mall and the Memorials. We walked all day and took the Metro back to the hotel. My feet we killing me there is so much to see. The Metro red line is just up the block, and the blue line was 3 blocks away. There is a fast food place called the Pot Belly with great sandwichs and salad at a reasonable price about 2 blocks away and a CVS Pharmacy. Avis is around the corner 2 blocks. Our room was small but nicely furnished. Coffee maker, comfy bed, and frig. I rated this hotel a little lower because of the noise we heard all night on Saturday. Beware! We were located on the 2nd floor along the side street. The rest of our stay was quiet. This hotel is an older hotel remodeled. Very Classy. They should have upgraded the tv's to flat screen. Otherwise we really enjoyed our stay and the excellant location. We will stay here agian.

title: “In Decline”
text: Over the past few years I have slowly witnessed the decline in Starwood properties and this property is no exception. I have been a loyal Starwood customer since '98 and a member since '00. On this stay I booked three nights in a corner club room that had supposedly remodeled recently and within 5 minutes of entering my room I knew I needed to check-out. The remodel was not a complete remodel, it was a mixture of modern (original furnishings) and English garden (fake plant) and bright greenish carpeting and chair. Everything appeared grimy and worn. I was paying over $300 per night and I could not be in this hotel for that price. I called the front desk and told them I was checking out the next day. No questions as to why, as I believe this may be common. I checked into a hotel near Columbus Circle the next day and could not have been happier with the 2 room suite and view I had for $25 more a night. Having been a loyal Starwood member I have forgotten that there are many other choices out there. For me, it's time to expand my horizons and experience true quality once again; earning points is great, but not enough to sacrifice my comfort. Upon my return home, I found pictures of my last stay in the Westin hotel, possibly same room...and the designer of the "new" space butchered these rooms with their "remodel."

title: “Comfort and good rates!”
text: Very comfortable, spacious and clean rooms. Stayed here on a very busy Saturday night with 3 other couples. Rooms were all immaculate and large with very comfortable beds. Decided to stay here due to the great rates ($109) which included a $25 Amazon gift card. Went to the Wings game and it was a quick and easy drive to park at Greektown. Excellent beds too!

title: “Great stay, great value”
text:
This was the first time we stayed at a Hyatt Place and we loved it! The hotel looked absolutely new and stylish, the rooms was perfectly clean and we had a huge sofa area with a big tv and a small kitchenette (besides a good bed and the bathroom of course). The hotel also had a coin laundry, free Wi-Fi and a basic but sufficient continental breakfast (with real china and glass ware which seems to be pretty rare nowadays in American hotels and Inns) was included (any extras like eggs could be ordered separately). There were also some tables outside so we could enjoy a breakfast in the sun.
We can really recommend this hotel - you'll enjoy a fantastic stay for a reasonably price.
The location is somewhere south of the city but easily accessable from the highway but not too close to hear the cars.

title: “Great value”
text:
My husband, son and I stayed here for three nights and really liked it. The room rate was reasonable and the location is fantastic. We were on the ground floor in a room that walked out to the pool and hot tub, which was perfect for us. The room is pretty standard - nothing terribly modern or special about the decor - but it was clean and had a refrigerator and microwave. The complimentary continental breakfast is nothing fancy, but the fresh waffles are a nice touch. 
Besides being right on the beach, there is a Starbucks and Ralphs in walking distance and an underground parking garage where we kept our rental. We were there on a Sunday through Wednesday, so it was pretty quiet. 
I would definitely stay here again!

title: “So much better than other places I've stayed in Philadelphia.”
text:
The good:
- Large expansive entry
- Conference center
- Great location
- good sized rooms
- good HVAC control
- very comfortable beds
- large flat screen tv's
The not so good:
- Check in process is always crowded with long lines
- Valet parking and Curbside arrival area is on the small side and someone is always confused as to how the process works here and ends up jamming up the roadway.
All in all, this is a very fine Marriott. I've stayed here 3 times now without andy major disappointment. 
I've stayed at the Sheraton Society Hill, Crown Plaza Downtown, and Holiday Inn Independence Hall in Philadelphia and this Marriott beats them all by a large margin.

title: “Terrible Experience”
text: I stayed in room for three nights and discovered a horrible ant infestation that covered the area above the window, stretched down to the walls around the bed. When I approached the front desk, they said no one was there to help, but that I could use a spray. I sprayed the room, and returned to find ants on the bed. I requested a new room, which was given, but when I awoke the next morning I discovered some unwelcomed guests on my person... bed bugs. The hotel employees were unhelpful and rather indifferent to the issue. When trying to get a refund, the hotel charged me, not refunded, two days and I had to talk to the manager on the phone and go back to the hotel and speak with the front desk on several different occassions (I'm still waiting for the refund). I was told I couldn't have a full refund because it was an isolated incident, but that my medical bills would be taken care of (medical bills?!). And, of course, I run the risk of carrying the pests with me as I travel back to my home state. Also, this hotel is not in Mission Valley, and is approximately 10 to 15 minutes away (by car) to said valley. There is nothing around the hotel in regards to entertainment. The staff was, as stated, indifferent to just about everything. This hotel was terrible on a volley of levels.

title: “Typical pleasant Hampton Inn experience”
text:
In my opinion the Hampton Inn chain is a "safe" choice because you know what to expect. That means, clean rooms, not a ton of extras and a nice complimentary breakfast each morning. As for price, that's predictable too, not the cheapest place to book, but not over-priced either.
This Hampton Inn was like many others we've stayed at. No complaints. In terms of location, we thought it was good. Just outside of downtown Denver and near major highways. It was just a 1 or 2 minute ride by car to get to downtown Denver. We enjoyed our visit to Denver, plenty to see and do downtown. We really enjoyed Colorado as a whole and would like to return. 
This Hampton Inn also had a small pool and hot tub which was good for our achy feet after a few days of hiking up in Boulder, CO (about 30 minutes away).
So, for a safe pick, close to downtown Denver, you can't go wrong here.

title: “An outstanding "WOW" experience!!!!”
text: What an awesome hotel - Not only is the location perfect with walking distance to Beale Street, but the hotel itself was incredible. Sparkling clean rooms, the most hospitable staff I've ever met, friendly as can be, delicious and bountiful breakfast buffet. As far as I am concerned, it is the ONLY place to stay in Memphis TN and you can bet I'll recommend it to everyone I know!

title: “Great value for the money”
text:
My son and I just got back from a two night stay on Easter weekend.
This hotel is just one block from Amtrak. Check in was immediate
and friendly despite us being earlier than check-in time. We got a 
deal online for a one bedroom suite through Travelzoo for $219 per
night. Our corner suite was on the 18th floor looking out at the Empire state room. The bedroom was great, very comfortable bed.
As previously stated by other reviews, the bathroom is a shoebox
and nothing special about the mini-kitchen but the living area is
very large and pullout sofa bed okay for two nights (could have used a new mattress). Staff was very friendly from maid service to front desk. Dunkin Donuts right next store but also free coffee in the lobby in the AM. 3 blocks to Macys and subway. We will definitely go back.

title: “Great hotel in the heart of it all!”
text: We stayed at the Marriott from Jan 2-3, 2009. This was a perfect hotel for us. It was our first visit to New York, so we wanted to stay central and near everything. This hotel was perfect for us. When we arrived, they upgraded us to a Times Square view with no extra charge! Fabulous. We had a king sized bed that was VERY comfortable. We were on the 27th floor. They wished my husband a happy birthday on check in since I mentioned it in the comments when booking. It was a nice touch. We also purchased a $40 birthday surprise. I added a picture of what this included. We loved the elevators and had absolutely no wait problems with them. All the staff was courteous and helpful to find our way around New York. The subway entrance is very close and convenient. Shopping and Broadway theatres are right outside the doors. The view lounge is perfect for people watching Times Square while keeping warm. Everything to us looked newly remodeled. When we closed our curtains, we had no problem with the lights from Times Square. We couldn't hear any noise unless a vehicle with a siren went near our hotel. I will stay here again when visiting New York! Easy to get a cab when leaving.

title: “Tranformation to a Boutique Hotel on a good way”
text:
The Hotel is located in the centre of Boston Downtown. Restaurants like Legal Seafood, Steakhousees like Smith and Wollensky, Bars etc. All nearby. Nice surroundings with a park.
Friendly Reception/Front Desk. Hotel was former a Radisson. Seems that the Transformation to a Boutique Hotel is still in progress. Unfortunately no Hotel information in the rooms, no recommendations or any other material like Postcards, envelope, Directory etc.
Plus is the inhouse Emerald Lounge. Prices are very high, as it didn't actually offers a 5 Star overall experience. Maybe next year...

title: “Very good hotel”
text:
We overnighted in Charlotte on 2 different occasions recently, and stayed both times at the Omni. The downtown location is perfect - close to the Epicenter, arena, financial district. Easy access to/from the airport - there is a "Sprinter" bus that runs every 20 to 30 minutes and drops you off directly in front of the hotel; at $1.75 per person, it can't be beat! 
Staff were very friendly and efficient. Easy check-in and out. We had a problem with our in-room safe and is was immediately corrected.
Our rooms were comfortable with everything we needed - blowdryer, bathrobes, coffee/tea maker, in-room safe, easy room temperature controls. Plenty of plug-ins right beside the bed. Very quiet rooms; our first was beside the elevators but we never heard a thing. 
HINT - join their loyalty program. Everything will be on file - check-in and check-out are instantaneous; you get free wi-fi and a free morning beverage delivered to your door.

title: “Perfect for Ohio State parents”
text:
Very nice hotel, can see why it is rated #1 in Columbus, right on the Ohio State campus, walking distance to everything on campus. Parking is either valet or you can park your car yourself in a garage next to the hotel. Nice breakfast at hotel but if you want to go off campus I recommend the North Star cafe on High Street.
As another reviewer said, there is a nice fitness center or you get a discounted rate at the huge fitness center on campus. We also played on the scarlet course at the OSU golf course - students get a discounted rate and can bring their parents as guests. It is a Jack Nicklaus redesigned course.
Don't miss photo opportunities with numerous statues of Brutus the buckeye, both on campus, near the Panera on Lane Street, and even at the golf course, dressed up in golf attire!

title: “Disappointment”
text:
My husband booked this hotel as a surprise for my 40th birthday and stressed on the booking form that it was a special occasion - this I may add made no difference whatsoever.
Although classed as a double room, the room was very small - only being able to get out of one side of the bed !!! We took this complaint to reception only to be greeted with a shrug of the shoulders and told this was the room that was allocated. We found their customer service in this regard disgraceful. Considering the room rate was over $400 per night, the attitude of staff was extremely disappointing.
Glasses we had used were not lifted by the cleaners on two occasions.
For a hotel of this standard and charging the prices they do you would expect a lot more.

title: “I never stay anyplace else in Jacksonville!”
text: This is my favorite hotel to stay in Jacksonville. Quick check in, friendly staff - always ready to accommodate any need. The beds are luxurious - a great way to end the stay - I always wake up refreshed and always have a great night's sleep! When you start for the elevator in the mornings - you can smell the bacon cooking - fantastic breakfast and I don't have to drive to get it. Coming back to the room each evening - I am greeted with freshly baked cookies - you can't beat this hotel! Close to malls, restaurants and a movie theater within walking distance!

title: “Dont waste your money”
text:
Horribly small rooms. The lobby is beautiful and fools you into thinking the rooms are very nice. Stayed in a suite for over 400$ a night. Not even coffee in the room. Old dirty couches, old bathroom tiles. 
There are beautiful hotels in the city for the same price or less. i would not recommend this to anyone...

title: “Poor service”
text: I stayed here for 4 nights over the final four weekend. Very disappointed. Twice in a row my room was not cleaned. Unpleasant to return home after a long day to an unclean room. Moreover, on calling the front desk to have the room cleaned, neither time did they apologize or show a hint of remorse. That's just basic customer service, and it just compounded the frustration when they didn't seem to care in the least.

title: “Was pretty good for New York”
text: My husband and I went there for our wedding anniversary for a weekend. We had a beautiful view of Central Park but found our room to be a little run down. Still, it was clean and the staff was very courteous and helpful. The 'Burger joint' placed was a little hyped up - the burgers were good but not 'the best ever'. The location was excellent for someone who wants to be shopping for their whole trip. We were within a 5-10 minute walk from Times square and broadway and right down the street from Bergdorf goodman. Next time we go to new york we wouldn't mind staying in this hotel again but wouldn't necessarily be loyal to it either if we found something in the same price bracket.

title: “Hotel was just OK”
text:
This hotel was in a good location and obviously right by Fisherman’s Wharf and Ghiradelli Sq. Since we like to walk, we walked the distance to China Town and Union St. We also walked along the water from near the hotel all the way to the Golden Gate bridge which is about 2 miles. On a nice day it is amazingly scenic, so I recommend taking in some sites that way. 
This hotel was pretty much purpose-only. It was nothing special to look at from the outside and inside. The room was just your basic hotel room and our view was of a wall. We had a handicap room I think because the shower had handrails and a big bench. The bench took up most of the shower so you had to stand pretty much against the wall and the water pressure was weak. Luckily the showerhead detached so you could rinse more efficiently that way. At least the mattress was really comfortable. That is a bonus while on vacation and trying to catch up on sleep. 
Unfortunately a travel agent got this room for us and I paid full price on a weekend of $230+ a night and wish I had gotten a different hotel for that price or tried Hotwire.com. Besides, Fisherman’s Wharf is a good location, but you can see that in about an hour’s time so if I could go back, I would prefer to be more in the heart of the city near Union St. 
The breakfast was a big bonus for us since we were eating all meals out for our week long trip to northern California. Since we were up early due to the time change from the east coast, we didn’t have to fight crowds for food at 7:00 am. At 9:00 when we were headed out to start the day in the city, the breakfast area was packed. But even so, you could get your coffee and something to eat pretty easily. 
The free internet in the room was a bonus since we brought our laptop. Our hotel in Monterey didn't provide breakfast or free internet in the room.
We spent two days in San Fran so we didn’t pick up our rental car until we were leaving for Monterey since the parking at the hotel is $40 and the closest garage had a sign for $30 a day. 
In the end it was a good stay, but if I could go back (because San Francisco was an amazing city!) I would stay closer in towards the heart of the city for that price and probably picked something myself rather than a travel agent who didn't get us any sort of deal.

title: “NIce stay”
