text: The desk clerk that checked me in was very helpful and friendly. The girl who checked me out however was okay but acted like it was a chore for her to leave what she was doing on the computer.

title: “Great find”
text: We stayed here for two nights the end of July. We had Red Sox tickets for two nights in a row and decided to make a weekend of it. We were pleasantly surprised by this hotel. The rate for the middle of the summer was very reasonable. The hotel is very minimalistic which for the price is very acceptable. The room is clean and comfortable. We booked an atrium room because it was less expensive. I felt a little claustrophobic, but it didn't bother my husband and we were busy being tourists in our own city so we didn't spend much time there. Location is great. Everything is within walking distance and there's a T stop right outside the door!

title: “Great hotel as I would have expected for the price.”
text:
The room I stayed in was spacious (US hotels are much more spacious than English equivalents!) and really well appointed. There was even a full Bose cinema music system which was cool. 
Great room service.
Fantastic location downtown Chicago, with amazing shopping.

title: “Nice hotel for a family of 5”
text: We are a family of five, so we are limited as far as finding a hotel that sleeps 5. We have been to this hotel a few times and I love that they have updated their rooms. Very modern and very comfortable king sized beds! The pull out sofa is a bit less comfortable so I usually bring along our aerobed for the kids. This is a family friendly hotel so you do get quite a few kids running around the halls. It could be a little noisy in the front room, but the back bedroom is very quite. The indoor pool is nice as you don't have to hope for good weather to use it. The restaurant in the hotel was good and there's a PF Chang's next door. However the service there was really bad and we waited at least an hour for our food to be served. The reason I didn't give this hotel 5 stars is because I've noticed that the people working here aren't very friendly.

title: “Location Fantastic”
text: We visited for 4 nights during April. The location is absolutely superb, particulary if you want to be close to many of the large art museums - about 50M from Central Park. The rooms were spotless and very spacious (as many New York hotel rooms are small). Good bar and friendly staff.

title: “Okay but you can do better”
text:
After having an excellent experience at the Chicago Palomar, we wanted to stay at another Kimpton hotel for our week long NYC vacation. Wanting to stay in the less touristy area, we choose ink48 in the Hell's Kitchen neighborhood. The hotel is nice but it's not near much. Sullivan Street Bakery is very close and delicious but that's only good for a quick bite. The area is surrounded by car dealerships and most cab drivers have never heard of the hotel.
Our room was nice. They're all done in a loft style. Our's had a tub literally next to the bed which at first seemed nice but after a few days we just found it useless and intrusive. Room service is good by incredibly expensive. But the worst part is there are no ice machines on the floor. You have to call room service for ice. And on the first night, they were quick. However, Saturday night took an hour and a half to get one bucket of ice. When I called down after 45 minutes, I was told by an incredibly rude woman "just relax. It'll be there". Not acceptable. I'm paying $400/night. I don't deserve to be told to "just relax". Also, after walking around Hell's Kitchen and the Meat Packing area, I saw better looking and better located hotels (ie the Standard) that I wished we had stayed at.
If you're looking for the level of service you expect from a Kimpton hotel, you won't find it at ink48.

title: “Warm and excellent.”
text: My stopover in New York was made thoroughly enjoyable by two nights in this fine hotel. The concierge service, in particlar Julieta Swanson, attnded to details and I was able to enjoy the wonderful city. The ambiance is warm and luxe. I recommend this hotel for a great New York experience because of it's culture and location.

title: “Nice small hotel room with a hiddend suprise.”
text:
Very cute. Hotel staff were nice. Location was great. I walked mostly everywhere. 
The room was very small but that seems to be the norm in Manhattan. 
The hidden suprise was at check out I was charge $21 for amenties. That's a first. I was told that since I booked with Priceline, I would have to pay for the amenties. Just seem odd to me. If you allow Priceline to offer rooms at your hotel, you should be all inclusive.

title: “So noisy we had to check out early”
text:
My husband, son and I were supposed to stay at the Sheraton for three nights, we ended up staying for only two. 
The Sheraton is in a great location close to the lovely restaurants and shops on Newbury St., walking distance to the Commons and Public Garden, attached to the Prudential Center,and near the T station. 
Unfortunately though the walls are paper thin. We had to check-out a day early because we couldn't sleep at night or have quiet time during the day. We could hear EVERYTHING the people next door were saying . And they were just speaking in normal voices, they weren't being loud. The hotel didn't care about the issue and didn't offer to put us in a different room. So I would not recommend staying here if you're at all sensitive to noise.

title: “Excellent. In every way.”
text:
1715 is my new favorite in Philadelphia. I don't know why it took me so long to stay here, but a discount rate on a travel site popped up and I took advantage of the deal. Now I know I'm perfectly happy paying the usual rates on the hotel's and other sites- it's worth it. 
The location: perfect, just a few blocks away from where I work most frequently.
The staff: engaging, cheerful, helpful.
The room: beautiful, clean, comfortable.
The breakfast: I opted to enhance the free continental breakfast with fresh-squeezed OJ and an omelet. Clearly a great choice, the chef made one of the best I've every had. Reasonably priced, it was a great way to start the day.
The atmosphere overall: positive energy is the best description.
Only two little things: first, one of the side chairs looked like an ink pen had stained the light fabric, and the tv was kinda snowy. I didn't care about watching tv, so I didn't call. There was a card explaining the operation, so maybe I didn't go through the full process to get the best picture. I'll claim operator error on this.
What I wish I'd experienced, two things: the wine reception, I had a business dinner (boo) and staying longer. I'll be back.

title: “Decent, but overpriced.”
text: Had a good stay, the staff was very nice, the location is awesome, but it's not worth the price. I would pay half and call it ok. Small rooms, no view, decor that was trendy in the eighties. The food is good, but there are so many restaurants in the area that are better and cheaper.

title: “Great Location for a family stay”
text: No complaints on this place; stayed with 2 young teens our our room with plenty of space; Starbucks, Subway and market just across the street and within a safe, 5-minute walk to the Walk of Fame area! Skip the free breakfast as you get what you pay for; instead grab a breakfast sandwich at Subway or Starbucks for a quick breakfast, or walk to Mel's Diner. You won't need a rental car as public transportation is just down the corner. And plan on a show at the Hollywood Bowl; you can walk there in 5 minutes!

title: “OTKAON 2011”
text:
I would like to personally commend Annette at the Front desk and Larry and Martin in the Security for the evening of July 31st for their help, kindness and understanding with my situation. They went above and beyond to be sure he was safe. Unfortunately the so called friends and parents of the friends had a problem and without holding a discussion with the girls and my son (all 18) to hash out the problem they called me at 10 pm at night and told me they were not going to allow my son to stay at the hotel (which her paid his part for) or take him home to Rochester the next day (7 hours travel). They basically threw him out on the streets, no hotel rooms anywhere open due to the convention, no buses, trains or flights available at this time of night and didnt care where he went. 
Annette, Larry and Martin immediately helped me over the phone to assure his safety until we could drive the 7 hours to pick him up. The secured his belongings, they stayed in contact with me and my husband, they tried to find any possible hotel rooms near by (nothing available). They allowed him to stay in the lobby till we could get there. When another friend came to offer him to stay with them, Annette called me at 4 am to get approval, put my son on the phone so I can ok the situation. 
Prior to here leaving her shift at 7 am she again called to be sure I was on my way to get him and that he was safe. Security also protected him from the parents that were kicking him out when they rudley approached my son in the lobby and told him he needed to leave the hotel --security asked them to not speak to my son and stop harrassing him.
For all their kindness and help I commend and thank them. This hotel is one I would hightly recommend due to the wonderful employees and the staff.
Thank you--DoreenT. Swan

title: “Excellent deal”
text: This hotel did not disappoint us. We booked a room for $119 per night, the week after Fiesta using Drury's own website, which promises the lowest rates. Very friendly and helpful staff. Great central location close to everything. Traveling with 2 young children, the hot breakfast saved us from having to get everyone ready and find something to eat. The free drinks in the afternoon were a real bonus, as was the free wireless internet. Rosario's is a great (but very reasonably priced) restaurant about a 10 minute walk south on St Mary's St. Across the street from there is King William BBQ, a no-frill stand, which served 2 excellent brisket sandwiches for only $4.

title: “Wonderful Downtown Denver Hotel”
text: I have stayed here many times and love this place. It is hands down one of the nicest Courtyards I have ever stayed in and it has a perfect location for downtown Denver. Two blocks from the Denver Center for the Performing Arts. Right on the 16th street mall. Very close to the Civic Center. Anything in downtown is close. The Rialto Cafe is attached and you can charge to your room. They even have a special entrance for the StarBucks! Very quick to recognize your Marriott status. Always a very friendly and helpful staff. I prefer it over the Marriott City Center and it is always less costly.

title: “The best hotel ever!”
text: This was the best Christmas surprise ever and the most charming hotel we've ever stayed in. We were there from December 24 to December 28, and from checking in to departure, the service was smooth and seamless, without being obsequious. On the first morning, we left the room for 45 minutes for breakfast, and when we returned, the maid had come and gone, leaving everything perfect. On the one day she left only decaf, we called the front desk, and THREE people arrived with regular coffee in the space of ten minutes. We had a view of the little park across I Street, and we parked our car right in front of the hotel (yes, we had to replenish the meter, but that was a minor inconvenience, and valet parking was available). The elevator reminded me of the one in the apartment house in NY where I lived in the 1940s, very quaint, manually operated with brass controls. Many restaurants and shops are within easy walking distance even in wretched weather, and there's an ATM on the corner. Everything was spotless, the linens were luxurious, there was WIRED Internet access (did that other reviewer ever hear of that?--it's far more secure!) and the place has the charming ambience only found in big cities. Both restaurants were 5-star quality, with intimate surroundings and friendly, attentive waiters. We paid more while driving there on the Interstates! We understand that we got a real bargain because it was Christmas and there were no business clients----but even at three times what we paid, it would have been a bargain.

title: “No hesitation in recommending this hotel”
text:
My husband and I and our two "twenty-something" sons stayed at the Magnolia during a recent, leisure trip to Denver. We all agreed it was a great stay and we would definitely return if Denver is our destination. We had two, double rooms on the top floor of the hotel. Our rooms were tastefully decorated, clean and adequate in size (not spacious). The hotel served as a great base for taking in a Rockies game at Coors Field and attending a concert at the Paramount as well as checking out shops and restaurants on the 16th Street Mall. Everything was easily accessed on foot (especially with the free shuttle on the Mall.) While on our trip we also visited Roxborough Park and Rocky Mountain National Park so we had a car. We found the parking garage next door to the hotel very convenient and the weekend rates were quite reasonable. (We did not take advantage of the hotel's valet parking.)
On the second night of our stay, my husband and I were concerned because a bacholerette party was based in the room next to ours. We were pleasantly surprised to find the sound was sufficiently insulated so we were not disturbed by the party.
Our sons' favorite feature of the hotel was the evening beer and wine reception. We took advantage of the hot breakfast each morning, the beer and wine reception each evening and the cookies and milk/coffee/tea one evening. With good rates to start with and these extras, we consider our stay to be one of the best deals we've ever found.
I have no hesitation in recommending the hotel to anyone visiting Denver!

title: “This was an awesome, relaxing, enjoyable, very productive trip.”
text: I strongly recommend Bahia Resort Hotel, for Vacation or, Business Trip. Business, there's meeting place there in the Hotel, awesome Service, Staff, and Location, you can't beat the awesome hospitality I received the week I spent there. This will be one of my most enjoyable Business Trips, it have already top all the trips I've taken for the year of 2008. My hat's Off to You Bahia Resort, keep up the good work.

title: “Nice rooms”
text: Nice clean rooms. I stayed here a week or so go and left my charger in the room. I called downstairs to see if anyone turned it in. I was asked the room number of the previous room. I could not remember the number. I was told they needed the date also. To make a long story short, I didn't retrieve my charger because they had to have the correct date. Not happy with that service.

title: “Great Hotel and Great Location”
text: My wife and I just spent five nights at this hotel. This was the first time I have stayed that long in a hotel without growing tired of it. The rooms are modern and very quiet. The beds are extremely comfortable. The breakfasts in the morning had a wide variety to choose from. We were met each morning in the breakfast area by a very friendly employee named Rudy who we looked forward to seeing each day. We asked one morning if we could take a plate back to the room to warm up leftovers from dinner the previous night. When we finished breakfast, Rudy brought us a tray with two plates, napkins and silverware for us to take to the room. He also made several suggestions as to where to eat if we wanted a change from the tourist restaurants. The location of the hotel is ideal. It is about a five minute or less walk to the loop of the Riverwalk that has all of the restaurants and bars so it was a lot quiter at night than many of the other hotels.

title: “Great location for good price”
text:
We were really impressed with the hotel - the room was PERFECT for us - 4 "girls" (Mum, one teenager and two 22 year olds) - roomy and clean. 
The guys on the reception were really friendly and helpful.
The diner right next door was perfect for breakfast.
The location was brilliant because it was only 2 stops on the express subway into Times Square (about 10 minutes)and the subway was right opposite the hotel.
Also the hotel was a 5 minutes walk away from Central park.
Loved it!

title: “Conveniant location and comfortable rooms.”
text: This was our first trip to San Francisco and the location is just great. We considered staying in the wharf area but I'm glad we didn't as you can actually do the walk down there yourself. The rooms are clean and comfortable and the only thing that irked me was no free wifi. They did offer free internet in the business center though, along with printers and paper at no charge. I'd certainly stay again. It is a solid 4 star hotel in a good spot.

title: “Cozy older hotel not quite near enough to Union Square”
text: I got a good discount rate via Travelocity, and was satisfied with the value, but would not have been had I paid rack rate. The hotel is in an older building, so the hallways and doors give the impression of a vintage boarding house. The rooms themselves, however, have a better feel, having been recently renovated; they are cozy and comfortable, if quite compact. The cramped bathroom was fine except for the jalacy window which provided little protection from the cold during an unusually cold and wet winter weekend. The door to the room also provided very little sound insulation, and while I was there, inconsiderate parents let their children run wild up and down the hallway. The desk staff was friendly and helpful. And while the hotel is just a few blocks from Union Square, it also borders the tenderloin, and walking down to the BART/MUNI lines on Market can take you through a couple dodgy blocks.

title: “Still the Classic Mansion Hotel”
text:
Wife, 8 year old and I were in Dallas for the Cotton Bowl,, checked in Dec 31 for 2 nights. In Room 710 (next to Presidential Suite). I havent been to the Mansion in over 4 years, but still as I remember it. TALL ceilings in rooms, spacious setting in rooms (nice desk, chairs), giant closet. My room had a French walkout balcony (no view really, just some tree tops, and the hotel courtyard),, It's just a nice way to let in fresh air. King bed very commfy. 100% tiled bathrooms have nice double sinks, deep, deep tub, and a glass in shower. Very thick and large bath towels, and lots of bath amenities (tons of soaps/shampoos) along with fresh flowers in the bathroom too. Standard amenities include 2 times a day cleaning with evening turndown.
We ordered room service, and it came up in quick fashion,, hot, and as ordered. Had drinks in --The Bar-- and breakfast in -The Restaurant-. Both places very nice and efficient, and suited to the Top Drawer fashion of the Mansion.
Wife had a massage. She also did a AM work out in the gym,, all good she said.
The room rate I paid for a -deluxe king- was 395/nt,, and since they did not have any 2 bedded/double rooms,,had to get a rollaway. The rollaway was a bit steep at 40.00/night. Thought they should eat the $40,, but I did not say anything,,just paid it.
The only room negative was the TV. It was the --old-- standard 24 inch tube TV. In my home I got rid of the tubes a year ago and I'm spoiled to the HD/flat panel LCD sets. I've been to a ton of nice hotels (Ritz/ Four S. Penninsula, etc) and they all have gone now to flat panels. These tube sets are from the dark ages and should be replaced. They had a --tv volume-- control in the bathroom, but it did
not work. Not worth the hassle for me to call and -report- it. 
The check in/out smooth and efficient as the Rosewood Staff know the game. Car valet and unload/load of baggage very efficient. Keys given and baggage in room with in minutes of arrival. Complimentary coffee and tea all day long in the reception area. All the newspapers you would ever want to read are free in the morning. 
All in all, a great stay and I would go back for a repeat visit if business/vacation takes me to Dallas.

title: “Outstanding accommodations”
text: We loved the Marriott Custom House. The rooms are suites with federal period furniture and are impeccable. The staff is so accommodating. We did not have children on this trip, but if we did we would have liked their extra kid-friendly activities. A trip to the Boston Pops Holiday Show is a must in December. We loved the location -- subways are easy and the walking is terrific. Take the Freedom Trail right from the hotel. I will be back!

title: “Clean and Courteous!”
text:
I stayed at the CP on June 25-27, 2007 while on a business trip in Seattle. I called once I arrived at the airport to see if I could check in early and the front desk was very accommodating. They put me in non-smoking, king size room on the 7th floor per my request for a lower level floor. The room and bathroom were extremely clean and comfortable and I'm a germaphobe so I inspected the room pretty carefully (especially after some of the reviews below). The furniture had a few scratches but was no where near the descriptions in some of the reviews below. My room looked as though it had been updated within the last year or so b/c the carpet was in good condition, the bed was very comfortable, and the linens (including the bed spread) were very clean. The room had a tv, desk, coffee pot, sleep kit for relaxation, a lounge chair and king size bed with night stands on either side. It also had plenty of lighting which was good for business. The hotel restaurant had decent food . . . it was moderately priced. The bar had a cheaper menu with sandwhiches and soups if you preferred. They would also prepare your food so you could take it to your room. The hotel also had room service but I needed a temporary break from the room. The hotel also had a gift shop with lots of things that you may have forgotten. The business center was ridiculously expensive to use. The free fitness room looked good - decent amount of equipment. 
The hotel is only about 5 blocks from the Westlake Center shopping and the monorail to the Space Center. You can easily walk to it. Also, if you are in the touristy area of Seattle, you can take the buses for free between 6am-7pm. Grab a Seattle Map and look for the key to the free bus area. 
The walls are very thin but I feel that is to be expected and most of the guests respected the other guest's schedules. I would definitely return on business.

title: “Great price, great location and excellent bed!”
text:
I booked a 5 night stay at the Quincy after an exhaustive search for an affordable but quality hotel for a 40th birthday vacation long weekend in DC. My partner and I could not have been happier with our stay.
After reading many reviews on tripadvisor.com, I called the night before arriving and requested a room on a higher floor, at the front of the building. We arrived 4 hours prior to check-in but only had to wait an hour for a room to be ready. Our room was on the 8th floor, facing L street. We didn't have any noise from dumpsters, but we were able to hear the street noise, particularly from the pub on Friday and Saturday night. I wouldn't have wanted to be on a floor that was any lower than where we stayed. The road noise with our window open was not the worst I've heard, but we only had to open the window for one night so it might have been more of an issue had the weather been warmer during our stay.
Our room was huge, with the most comfortable king size bed we have ever slept in, complete with 6 pillows and soft sheets. We had a large L-shaped sofa and large desk for our computers. The only small thing about the room was the bathroom. I agree with some of the other reviewers that mentioned the lack of storage in the bathroom, I had to put my things on the counter next to the microwave and fridge just outside the bathroom. The towels were divinely soft and the toiletries, including q-tips and cotton swabs were a nice touch. The water pressure was not great, but we figured it was an older building so took it with a grain of salt.
The fridge and microwave were great for breakfast, leftovers and cocktails in our room before dinner.
Our other requirement for a happy stay is free Wi-Fi with a strong signal, we got some of that. WiFi is included but our room did not have the strongest of signals. According to the front desk the signal is not consistent to every room, but we were provided with an Ethernet cable for a $20 deposit on our room bill which we worked great.
The location was ideal for our 5 day stay, walking distance to 2 Metro stations and to the Mall. Like others have said, the hotel is in the financial area of the city so there is not a lot open on after business hours and on the weekends, but you are in DC, so finding good restaurants within short walk or a Metro ride is not hard at all. We enjoyed a quick pub meal at Mackey's downstairs which was good price and was just an elevator ride away from our room.
When you look really close you can see some wear and tear on the property, peeling wallpaper here and there, but overall the quality of the furnishings and finishes in the room were very nice. Compared to other properties in the DC area, I think this one is a great deal for the price and location for anyone visiting DC for pleasure.

title: “Great Way To See La”
text: Stayed in Marriott Downtown in September 2007. Great hotel. Location is ideal for business, not so much for leisure. Staff are friendly and car hire desk on site is very handy. Would definitely stay here again as hotel is reasonably priced. Pool is great but small enough and sun is gone by about 5pm.

title: “Gorgeous”
text: Great stay for the price!!! It's clean it's nice it's decorated beautifully and the rooms are gorgeous. The pics don't do it justice.

title: “Nice place.”
text: Friendly people, nice surroundings, and great price through priceline!

title: “New and modern, but otherwise a typical 4/5-star chain hotel”
text:
I've stayed at the Intercontinental twice this year, in January and June. For both stays, I was there for only a few days.
Rooms: Since this is a new hotel, the rooms are well-appointed and large. The room had a very large flat-screen television, desk, and large king bed. The rooms have large windows (floor to ceiling), but there really isn't much to look at directly by the hotel. Perhaps a room on a higher floor would be worth seeking out if you want views of the city.
Service and Amenities: The hotel staff was friendly and polite. I didn't make much use of the staff, but my interactions with them were pleasant. One glaring annoyance is that there is not free internet in the hotel. I realize other chains often charge as well, but this hotel doesn't even offer free internet in the lobby. There is a Starbuck's around the corner you can use for WiFi.
Location: The location is fine, just a few blocks from Market and right next to Yerba Buena Gardens, and several blocks from Union Square. The neighborhood is safe considering it's San Francisco. I did walk alone at night, but not everyone would feel comfortable doing so. If I weren't familiar with the neighborhood, I would hesitate to stray too far from the hotel.
Value: Both times I booked through Hotwire, so I did not make a deliberate choice to stay here. Based on prices quoted on the web site, Expedia, etc., this hotel is overpriced. If you really want to stay in Union Square, then you will end up paying for it, but even so, there are less expensive hotels of similar quality in the area. I usually try to avoid this area of town because it is packed with shopping tourists, but for both of these trips, it was really convenient. Also, when booking on Hotwire, I try to stick with neighborhoods I know.
P.S.
Restaurant: I was very excited to try the restaurant, since the chef was recently recognized as best new chef in Esquire, but I was really disappointed. The service was the highlight. Food and wine were served promptly by informed waitstaff. The decor in the restaurant is pretty cheesy (an attempt at chic 1970s retro, perhaps?) I had the tasting menu for $34, so I didn't expect a big meal. I would expect that a seasonal tasting menu would not include things like New Zealand scallops and out-of-season strawberries (in June), especially in San Francisco. It was fine, but even for $34, it really wasn't enough food to be considered even a light lunch. It wasn't so bad that I wouldn't give it another shot, but there are just too many good restaurants in San Francisco.

title: “went to red sox game”
text: hotel was very nice ,super clean,. we have stayed here before, will stay again,

title: “Great place, great price, great location”
text:
We stayed 4 nights in this hotel and everything was awesome!! First they upgraded us to a better room for the same cost. The room was great, just like a mini apartment with all you may need to cook and have a pleasent stay.
Lots of room to store your bags and shoppings. 
For us the breakfast was perfect, they had cereal, bagels, muffins, oatmel, cream cheese, fruit, etc.
The hotel is just come steps away from Highland mall, right there on hollywood blvd and a metro station. 
It was also easy for us to arrive in the car, just by following google instructions.
I would hesitate to come back to this nice hotel!

title: “Amazing view, Romantic location!”
text:
Me and my wife have stayed to the Ritz-Carlton Battery Park for 3 nights. It was a part of our 3 weeks honeymoon to central and north America (Canada, New York and Cuba).
We decided to stay to this hotel because of its magnificent view to the Liberty Statue, the Ellis Island and the Port.
Our room was on the top floor (Club Harbour View room), clean, comfortable, many amenities, and the view was the most romantic in New York. Unfortunately, the bed wasn’t facing the Liberty Statue. The staff very friendly. If you book a club room then you have access to the club lounge (delicious and all day food presentation and drinks, friendly staff, but not a nice view).
The Battery park area is one of the most romantic, peaceful and beautiful places in New York. Day or night, morning or evening, it is magic. One of our nights there was the 4th of July and we dine at the hotel’s terrace restaurant. That night we saw the most breathtaking fireworks of our life. The restaurant was quite expensive (just only the reservation for 2 which include 2 glasses Champaign and a Liberty Statue chocolate cost more than $300).
Generally, we definitely recommend this hotel for a special romantic experience! Have fun!

title: “Good central base in NYC”
text:
My wife and I visited on our honeymoon and were fortunate enough to receive some fizzy stuff and chocolates when we arrived and an upgrade as well! 
The hotel is in a really central location close to numerous attractions. We walked to Central Park, The Met and Broadway to catch a show. Rooms are clean and spacious and decorated in a traditional style. A basic breakfast is served each day and you also get complimentary cheese and wine in the evening. The concierges were helpful and knowledgeable. 
I would recommend this hotel for anyone looking for good, simple base in NYC.

title: “Modern, clean with river views”
text: Most everything in town was booked up so we stumbled upon the Madison. Lucky for us. Our room has a view of the river and a large sitting area for less then we would have paid at the Hampton Inn and Suites. This hotel is close to everything downtown with out the noise of Beale Street. The bathroom has both a tub and a walk-in shower. The rooftop terrace is a nice bonus and we had free wifi!

title: “Fabulous Stay!”
text:
Our stay at the FS - NY was absolute perfection. Liz, the executive assistant to the regional VP of FS, came out to greet my husband and I as we checked in - we were personally escorted to our suite - which overlooks central park and many high rise buildings. 
I shopped at Chanel, Dior, and Jacob & Co...and to my delight, everyone was aware I was coming in to shop and I was greeted at Chanel with champagne and Dior with all the handbags I was looking for awaiting me... 
My hubby and I came back to the FS in the evening, and since it was his bday, they had his favorite cake and fruit awaiting us... 
The next morning...It was a late night since it was NYE and the guest manager called asking us if we would like a late checkout which was very much needed after a late night out! 
The service is spectacular and the rooms are immaculate and cozy especially for NYC. 
This hotel is def much better and more service oriented than the Beverly Wilshire. We will def be staying here again!!

title: “Very good hotel for the price!”
text:
I have stayed here 3 times and have no complaints. The room and bathroom are fairly big for NYC standard and are quite clean, no bed bugs! Breakfast each morning is decent with fresh coffee, tea and pastry. Location is great, close to the subway and Penn Station, and just south of Times Square. I like staying in Chelsea better than Time Square, it is not as hectic and the restaurant are great local eatery with good food and much cheaper!! I will definitely stay here again next time I am in NYC especially if I can get a good rate.
My only minus is the front desk people are very business-like, seems cold and not too friendly. I only talk to them during check in and out so I never had any problems.

title: “Great Value, excellent location”
text:
Stay for a couple of days, one single room in four floor, recently refurbished.
The room was clean and the service good, the down side is that the bathroom is not private.
Great choice for a business travel or a tourist on a budget. Near Central station and many places uptown.

title: “Great Beautiful Place”
text: Stayed here with a bachelorette party this June. We got a discount as one of the girls had a friend who worked there (or something) and the place was beautiful. Not only was the classy bride impressed and ecstatic, but all of the bridesmaids were pleased as well! Not always an easy task. We went out in Old City and the staff was even Pleasant after we returned from a night out. Lovely place, wish we could have stayed longer!

title: “Good but get an outside room!!”
text: The James hotel is in a great position, just off Michigan. It is pretty trendy and quirky for a large hotel.The 2pm check out time is very civilised - why don't more hotels do this?? A couple of downsides - the building is in a sort of squared off U configuration, so many of the rooms face inside. This means that if you are on the inside, the rooms opposite can see directly into yours, so basically you need to keep the blinds down whenever you are in it. Outside rooms may have the same issue from buildings across the road, but not to the same extent and are generally much lighter. Another odd one, and fairly minor at that is that there is a coffee machine in the room to make both tea and coffee - but only 1 mug (In a double room)?? Overall a good hotel, friendly staff, great position and pretty good value.

title: “Great location”
text: We had two adjoining rooms which were nice, comfortable and well maintained. The staff was friendly. It is in an ideal location, walking distance to Chinatown, MCi center and the White House. The Metro is connected, so you don't have to walk outside. At night there are lots of street people and homeless everywhere, so I wouldn't walk at night, but during the day no one bothered us. One negative, the restaurant and deli closed after lunch, so there was nowhere to get a snack in the hotel

title: “Stay away rude and awful customer service”
text: The people working in this hotel are absolutely the rudest people I have encountered. They act like they are doing you a favor by allowing you to stay in the Heartbreak Hotel. The pool is super small. There is no room service. I asked for towels and had to finally go and get them myself the NEXT day even though I was told they would be brought up that night. I had never been to Memphis before and was needing assistance on activities for the night, I was given brochures and the cold shoulder. I wasn't even instructed that I had to reserve the shuttle, if another guest had not mentioned it to me we would not have been able to go to Beale St. I was expecting a magical Elvis experience for myself and my family and left with a bitter attitude. I also left a bag with two t-shirts in it. The maid was coming into my room as I left, but guess what, no one can find the t-shirts, big shocker!

title: “What is up with all the negativity people?????”
text:
I came from Vancouver Canada and it was my first time in Los Angeles and after staying for 5 days it only made me want to come back for more. I would 100% stay again at Hollywood Hotel for the most important reason of all the location. How much close to the action can you possibly get. It is a block and a half walk, less than 5 minutes to the Red Line Metro station and that was my main mode of transportation the entire time I was there. I had ZERO problems with the location and found it to be safe either during the day or at night. 
In addition, there is a Rite Aid open until 11 pm a 2 minute walk from the hotel where I was able to get anything I needed. 
It was 4 stops to where the action was at Hollywood and Highland and perfect for all my tours I booked and just a couple more stops to Universal Studios which made my entire trip. 
As for the cleanliness, I found it to be spotless. I have stayed in 4 and 5 star hotels in Mexico that weren't as clean. The maids were always smiling, never failed to say good morning and as for the so-called rude front desk staff???? I never encountered any of that. Anyone I dealt with was more than welcoming and helpful. 
I never found any issues with the air-conditioning; there was a switch that I could control at all times and it was ideal for the hot, hot weather I encountered. 
As for my room, I found it to be perfect, especially the bathroom. Loved the shower that you could walk right into, the abundance of clean towels and again very well maintained. 
I had requested a safe and I had a room with one so I was quite happy with that. 
As for the free breakfast; again what is up with the complaints people????
I had toasted bagels with cream cheese and orange juice along with fruit each morning followed by yogurt and I was more than happy with that. In addition, there was a fresh omelette station if I so desired with pretty much any sort of filling I could dream of. 
I must comment on the mgr Jeff's assistance in making sure I was happy with the room and made sure I was promptly taken care of weeks in advance. Excellent customer service that again you don't get in the big so called "name brand hotels."
All the amenities, great staff, wonderful room all adds up to a return trip for me and like I mentioned I wouldn't stay anywhere else. I was more than pleased!!!!

title: “Fantastic location, Fantastic hotel”
text: Have just spent 5 wonderful nights at the Burnham the location is perfect , right opposite Macys, bonus, and in the middle of the theatre district The staff are so attentive to all needs the rooms though a little small were spotless, I could not fault this hotel at all cant wait to return

title: “Great location, great staff”
text:
The Sheraton was chosen as the site of the World Chess Open, the largest chess tournament in the world. Its center location and ,excellent staff made it an ideal vacation spot for my wife and me. She enjoys the shopping, the history and the easy access to places of interest. I enjoyed the spacious playing halls and way the staff was able to accommodate over a thousand chess enthusiasts 
The newly opened Banes Foundation Museum, within sight of the hotel, contains more paintings by some impressionists than all of France. Just consider nearly 50 Picassos and 150+ Renoirs. It alone is worth a trip to Philly, probably the most tourist friendly city I've ever visited.
The concierge, Mary, was especially helpful, she's a very knowledgeable, 
quick and reliable guide a pleasure to interact with.
David Worl

title: “Great Stay!”
text:
Was recommended The Liaison by a friend who has stayed on a few occasions when he has visited DC on business from Dublin. 
On arrival, I was informed by the lovely Katherine on reception that we were receiving a complimentary upgrade as I had informed the hotel we were celebrating our 10th Wedding Anniversary. The room was on the 5th floor at the end of the corridor and overlooked the back of the hotel - not the greatest view but definitely the quietest place to be! The room was large with the most comfortable bed ever! Considering the flight from the UK we both slept really well and the pillows we had (we didn't change ours) were so comfortable. 
The bathroom was large and we both thought the cut out hole to switch on the shower was a genius idea. Plenty of towels and toiletries and the added touches of cotton buds and cotton wool was well received by us.
If I was to say anything negative about the room, is that the analogue channels were very "snowy" - whilst the few HD channels were crystal clear (OK I know I'm not in DC to watch TV but when you wake up or return your room at the end of the day, it's a good form of relaxation!)
We made use of the rooftop pool on 2 days in the 94 degree heat. Great Mojiotos at the rooftop bar too! We only had drinks in Art & Soul - breakfast was taken across the street at Starbucks!
All staff we encountered were friendly and smiling and nothing was too much trouble.
The location was perfect - easily walkable to all interesting places and we did make use of the Metro from Union Station (although trains not as frequent as we're used to in London on the underground).
If we were to visit DC again, we'd definitely stay at The Liaison.

title: “Boy, did I pick the WRONG Hyatt in Chicago!”
text:
Bad customer service, mediocre food in restaurants, and loud sums it up. 
This is a huge hotel. When I checked in, rooms came and went before I could answer the questions about "upgrades". They said that I could have a complimentary upgrade to a suite. When I found it it was one floor above the street, I knew it was a problem. When I went into the room, all I could hear was the ice machine outside the door rumbling. Then someone used it and it really made noise. I asked to be moved because of the ice machine and street noise. 
I lugged my luggage back to the lobby, across the hotel to the other tower to my new upgraded room on the quiet "club" level. They left out the part that club amenities were extra (which I can understand but at least inform the customer when you are playing up the "club level" part). This upgraded room was missing a remote control for the tv, no pen on the desk, no paper. Since I heard turn-down service going from door to door I waited patiently and then realized "no turn-down service" for us upgraded people. So I had to call the desk to bring these items.
Then I heard room service pounding on someone's door at 12:30am. I have gotten room service that late myself but they are usually quiet about it as some people might be sleeping (but not in this hotel!)
About a half hour later, all hell broke loose on the "quiet club floor". When I called the desk they said they would send security. I told them it was security making all the noise yelling in the hall at 1:30 am. I never heard anyone but security and their radios turned way up making noise.
The next day the manager asked what he could do to make it up to me. I said that club level amenities would be nice and he seemed to agree. You guessed it - never got anything!
The food in the hotel restaurants was also mediocre as was the service.
I wouldn't stay there again if I were paid to do so. Several of my friends had problems as well but they can write their own posts.

title: “I am pick”
text: I like the hotel just the size we need me my husband a dog. Most importante to say is a good nite of sleep and we had good bed and very clean in second comes my dog is treet like a queen fresh bowl and water cookies is delivery at door. I like the shower and quiet place to rest a day or nite . i can not wait to be back at this hotel aahh the matress is news this for me is good deal my husband love the decor too

title: “Fabulous Hotel, Fabulous Staff”
text: This was a last minute "truly we were on the outskirts of Dallas" gem of a find. Four of us were coming into town for a weekend of shopping at Market. We like to alll stay together (so we can talk all night) sometimes it is a problem to find a room large enough without booking a suite. We booked through hotwire. One room, 2 beds :we were thrilled. When we saw the Palomar the giggles began. It is exquisitely decorated, and the staff is wonderful. The room was Huge! Location truly is everything and the Palomar was only minutes away from all the places we wanted to go to. Thanks for a wonderful and sucessful weekend of shopping with the girls.

title: “Disappointing”
text: Enjoyed staying here before but this time lots of renovation type noises at 8 pm and we chose to pay for an upgrade that would give us Internet access. The access was a bad experience and the room was too cold.

title: “Really good relly affordable.”
text: The staff was awesome, the room was clean and nice. The location was awesome. Although, when I stayed at the same hotel in Dallas, they had mini refrigerators and microwaves. But regardless my stay in live oak, tx was awesome. Will stay again and recommend anytime.

title: “Listed from the visit”
text: A small but centrally located hotel. Positive side that it has internet, breakfast and there is a refrigerator. Negatively is that there are narrow stairs and no elevator.

title: “no sleep”
text: we were booked at this hotel for two nights but left after only staying one night. the walls were so thin that we listened to the neighbors t.v. all night long. the rooms were so smoky it was unbearable. We reserved a non smoking room but when we arrived there was not one available. There was mold in the bathroom and the walls appeared dirty. We were in an executive room which was their "best" room. The breakfast was awful. The floors were dirty. The front desk manager was very unwilling to help and was not friendly at all. For $100 a night i would at least expect a clean hotel with a decent night's sleep. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Family friendly hotel with hardworking staff”
text:
We recently stayed at this property for five days while on our annual summer trip to Chicago. Due to a family of five we have found that staying in suites (namely Hilton) are the
 best value for us and afford us enough room. The front desk staff at this establishment goes out of their way to make you feel welcome. They were so attentive and interactive with our girls whenever we walked through the lobby. Our room was cleaned immaculately every day. The free breakfast offered every day was outstanding with choices changing daily. The entire staff worked very hard to make our stay wonderful. As far as the reviews mentioning the closely fire station- we had a corner suite in which only the living area faced the station. While we heard sirens ( more in Friday and Saturday night) being on the seventh floor it was not bothersome to our family.

title: “Central location, great weekend rates.”
text:
We stayed here for a long weekend trip and were very pleased. 
The Courtyard by Marriott is excellent for a quick weekend getaway in San Francisco without having to rent a car. This location is primarily intended for business travelers and has few tourist amenities. The rooms were clean comfortable and affordable. They feature large flat screen TVs and free wired Wi-Fi. In the lobby there is a Starbucks that is open during the day till 2pm. Our room was on the top floor and had some nice bridge and city views. The hotel also has a small snack bar next to the front desk. The hotel restaurant and bar looked much underused on the weekend but San Francisco has too many good food choices in any price range to consider hotel food. We did try an Indian fast food restaurant and a Chinese restaurant that were two blocks away and open weekends. Both were very good and inexpensive.
The Hotel is very centrally located in the financial district. This means on weekends, restaurant choices are limited and the streets are quiet in the evening. The hotel is walking distance to a trolley line, bus lines and the Montgomery BART station. We purchased a three day MUNI bus and trolley pass at the airport and had no problem getting to all of the sights.
If you are a tourist seeking a clean, comfortable inexpensive place this hotel fits the bill. Be sure to check out the special weekend rates.

title: “Decent value at discounted price”
text:
This is an older Holiday Inn that is good in some places, and a little lacking in others. Overall, it is a decent value if you can get it at a discounted price.
Value - through Priceline, I was able to book this hotel for a three night stay 12/1-4/2006 at $45 a night. Including taxes and fees, it came to $158.85. I think this is a good value for a decent hotel in San Diego. At the regular price listed on the Holiday Inn website of $119 a night, I would prefer a newer, nicer property.
Amenities - there is a small restaurant and bar, which I didn't try. They also have a small outdoor pool and spa which looked sparkling clean. However, I felt it was too chilly to use an outdoor pool during my stay. I'd have prefered an indoor pool in December. They also have a small fitness center. In the room, there is a coffee maker, ironing board and iron, hair dryer, two phones, plus an ethernet plug for free high-speed internet access. There were no ethernet cables in the room, but you can borrow a cable from the front desk. There is no wireless internet access in the rooms, although I was told it is available in the lobby for a fee.
Mechanicals - the older Amana HVAC unit was noisy, because the plastic grill buzzed against the housing. I fixed it by partially loosening the cover. Doing that, I noticed that the foam air filter was dirty; it should be cleaned more often. The toilet sometimes required multiple flushes, which reminded me of early low-flow toilet design. There was plenty of hot water and water pressure for the shower. It had a shower-massage head that took me three days to figure out the "normal" setting. The shower surround and faucet looked dated, but everything worked. The sink and faucet just outside the bathroom looked new, and had a granite counter.
Decor / comfort - it looked like the room had been redecorated within the last couple of years, with new furniture, carpet, bed linens, curtains and wall coverings. The bed linens and towels were nice, and each bed had four pillows.
Noise - you could definitely hear hallway noise, such as people talking and doors opening and closing. It wasn't busy during my stay, so this wasn't a big issue for me. The HVAC fan helped mask noise, but it was controlled by a thermostat and thus turned on and off. This hotel is just off a freeway; I could hear a little traffic noise if I focused on it, but it didn't bother me.
Security - the neighborhood seems safe and I didn't notice any problems during my stay. However, a relative works across the street and they have had some car thefts and break-ins in the past. That business has beefed up its security and now looks like Fort Knox. I'm no expert and don't want to go into specifics on a public website, but the security could be improved at this Holiday Inn.
Parking - the main entry driveway is narrow and winding, as another poster mentioned. If you're driving a large motorhome or towing a trailer, I'd recommend you use the second entrance, which takes you around the back of the hotel. There is a handy lower-level covered parking lot in back, with an elevator to access the rooms. Parking is also limited around the entry, but abundant in the back. I found the individual parking spaces to be smaller than what I'm used to, which seems to be typical throughout San Diego.
Staff / service - I had good interaction with the staff. The front desk staff was helpful providing driving directions, and housekeeping kept the room looking great. Every day I had fresh sheets, towels, soap and shampoo, and coffee packets.
Location - it is conveniently located off of I-15 and Aero Drive. There is a Jack-in-the-Box restaurant next door along with a small strip shopping center that contains a Kinkos and a few other restaurants. If you cross to the other side of Aero Drive, you'll find a grocery store, Wal-Mart and other stores. It didn't seem particularly close to the stadium.
View - I had to take a photo of the view out of my second-floor room, which provided a scenic vista of the HVAC units arrayed across an expanse of rooftop of the restaurant and lobby. I especially enjoyed the artfully placed, crushed aluminum beverage can, thoughtfully tossed out a window by a previous guest. I was amused and not bothered, as I wasn't there to look out the window, and it is fairly typical of older Holiday Inns. However, if I was paying full price, I'd ask for a room with a nicer view.
In conclusion - I would stay here again at this price, and recommend it to others with the cautions noted above. If any of the negatives I mentioned are really important to you, I'd recommend staying at a newer property.

title: “Outstanding service and rooms”
text: I have stayed there a few times. The beds are outstanding, clean and comfortable. The breakfast is wonderful with a cook for some fresh cooked choices. I will return.

title: “Tiny yet lovely”
text:
My fiance and I stayed at the Algonquin one weekend night in July on a lark, to see what it is like to be a tourist in our own city. We were greeted by Matilda, the resident "rag doll" cat upon our arrival and found the deluxe room tiny but charming. (In New York, one shouldn't intend to spend much time in one's room anyhow.) The halls were decorated with New Yorker cartoons and the entire hotel was full of little nooks and crannies. It reminded me of the Claridge in Buenos Aires: gracefully aged. One thing that impressed me--the rooms are entirely soundproof. We could hear nothing of the street noises below, nor of any fellow guests. 
Overall, the bed was a bit too soft for my liking and the view consisted of offices facing us across 44th street; however, the Algonquin Lobby served tasty breakfast and lunches and the overall ambiance is totally elegant.
One tip: ignore the dining advice of the concierge; instead, walk down the street to Akdeniz Turkish Cuisine on 46th between 5th and 6th, where a delicious Prix-Fixe Dinner can be had for $19.95.

title: “excellent hotel one block from convention center”
text: Stayed one night while attending meeting at the convention center. I had a conf rate so it was not outrageously expensive. Very nice room, regular hotel room. I asked for quiet room no feathers and I got no feathers. Room was across from elevator but I never heard it. There was a problem with whistling sound coming from under door (air pressure) during the first hour or so - which was fixed by placing a towel at the bottom of the door, but it was gone later that night. Hard Rock Hotel across the street can be a bit noisy at night as are the trains etc next to the conv center. This is not such a quiet area. I slept fine albeit with foam earplugs. No fault of hotel it's just the area is not quiet. Very modern guest room well appointed and with an operable window - very nice for air quality in the room. Window also seals well and is double pane so it is quiet. Valet parking at $32/day is expensive but if you want there is a public garage across the street. McCormick and Schmicks restaurant is in the hotel good for seafood. Cafe has good assortment of muffins and pastries do not have to order room service breakfast. Also good coffee. I would stay here again if I were attending a conference.

title: “Fantastic location, but hotel average at best”
text:
The accomodations at this hotel were average at best. The room my wife and I shared was clean but tired. The sofa was very worn and contained many spots and stains. Two other couples shared a room and for a suite it was very small. Also, their pullout sofa actually had no bed frame. The couch frame had been removed and a mattress had been shoved underneath the cushions. One couple actually had to sleep on the mattress on the floor. They were moved to another room the next night, but there is no reason that should have ever happened. Customer service was overall below average. Some front desk staff were helpful, but most were rude and unpleasant. 
All of that being said, we would recommend this hotel for its location. We were six-seven blocks from the National Mall and most of the monuments. George Washington University and DuPont Circle were right next door, so there were plenty of dining and entertainment options. The Foggy Bottom Metro stop was only 2 blocks away, but we walked to a lot of places because it was a clean and secure neighborhood. We are planning on coming back to DC in the future and if we don't choose this hotel, we will look for one nearby.

title: “Very good stay”
text: I had a very good stay in this hotel during my business trip. Its located in a good spot in the downtown.

title: “NYE Stay”
text: I guess if you stay New Year's Eve in a hotel you don't get a typical night. Had a great rate for the three rooms we booked through Hilton's website. The front desk was very efficient in checking in the large number of people there. We were given three rooms on the 12th floor fairly close to each other and executive lounge passes (I'm a HHonors Gold VIP). The rooms were very nice. If I stayed there again I wouldn't pay more for the Inner Harbor view, the hotel is a few blocks away and there is not much to see. The lounge on the executive floor had a great view of Camden Yards, I may come back for a weekend to see agame some day. One strange thing was the guy with his family who was walking around the executive lounge in bare feet, bathing trunks and t-shirt during breakfast. You would think the staff may have mentioned something. All in all I prefer the Renaissance which is closer to the harbor and has great harbor views from the room.

title: “Great deal on Priceline”
text:
Got this room for $70 on Priceline...My husband and I just got back from a cruise with the kids and needed a getaway just for ourselves. 
We asked the attendant at the front desk for a special room and she gave us a "hospitality suite", a two room suite with a living room and much larger accomodations. We gave her a $20 tip and we were very happy with our room! Service was always prompt and freindly. 
Our only complaints: 1) the very strong smell of cigarettes (this is a non smoking hotel) when we walked into our room. I called the front desk and let them know that we were not the smokers...I had read on TA that others had problems with this in the past and got charged for smoking...I wanted to make sure we would not be charged. I always travel with air freshener, so we sprayed the room several times, so it was not a big issue for us.
2) the pillow top mattress was basically a pad on top of the mattress that slipped and did not cover the entire bed when being used. I hate sleeping on a bare mattress and a bare hotel mattress just completely grosses me out. Yuk.
The furniture and the carpet in the room needed to be updated and the hotel looks like it is time for a makeover. Not a deal breaker by any means, just an observation.
The proximity to the Reading Terminal Market was a HOMERUN. We had many wonderful meals there and cannot wait to return. Loved DiNics, great sandwiches. Also tried Delilah's and Down Home Diner and ice cream at Bassetts. We also had a wonderful meal at Empress Chinese Restaurant in Chinatown. We live in a very asian neighborhood in Brooklyn and know chinese food...this was really really good stuff!
We found parking for $18/24 hours at the Auto Park at the Gallery Mall closeby. I came prepared with options for parking since I refused to pay $40 plus a nite.
All in all it was a good stay for the price that we paid. I would stay again.

title: “Great Cozy Stay For a Good Price!!!”
text: I went with a friend of mine in march for a nice weekend getaway. The hotel is new and very nice. The front staff was very nice and accomodating. I booked my room online a few weeks ago and was under the impression that i was getting a simple queen sized room with one bathroom. Upon entering my room i noticed that our room was signifactnly bigger and had two bathrooms and a refrigerator and other great amenites. I was in awe. I felt very comfortable in the hotel. The bathrooms are beautiful and very modern. There isnt an ice machine around but i called the front desk and they happily sent someone up with cups of ice for me. The only down fall is that they do not offer free breakfast and the breakfast it self was a little pricey for me but we just walked into the city to eat. Its located close to timesquare and lots of stores. the beds were clean and comfortable and i just cannot wait to come back. *** Sidenote*** Me and my friend were having a hard time hailing a taxi so the doorman helped us. He was very sweet and didnt even accept the tip i offered him. TRYP Hotel is GREAT! :)

title: “Nice hotel”
text: The hotel is situated close to the historic area, only a few steps away from the USS Constitution. We had a large, nice room with microwave and coffee maker. The staff was very friendly and helpful. It was easy to get to the city center even on foot. Convenient public transportation to the BOS Airport.

title: “Good Stay”
text: We recently stayed here after coming off of a late flight into Jacksonville. The hotel is very close to the airport- less than a 5 minute drive. The front desk staff was very pleasant. We were given a room on the 2nd floor (226). The room was large and nice enough for a one night stay. The bathroom appeared to have been remodeled, and the bedding also seemed new. The other furniture does not seem to have been replaced. The toilet was on its last legs, but we didn't make it an issue since we were leaving the next morning. The room served our purpose well as a quick stop after flying in. We aren't so sure how the area around the hotel is- the hotel is gated and there was a security guard in the looby. Our rate (only $89) included the breakfast buffet for four. The buffet is pretty basic, with sausage, potatoes, biscuits, cereals, pastries, yogurts, etc. but includes an omelette and egg station which is nice. Overall, we had a nice stay at the Courtyard and would return again if we were in the area.

title: “Great location, great value, family friendly”
text:
We stayed at the Pointe Squaw Peak over Easter weekend and really enjoyed our stay. We used to live in Phoenix and specifically chose this place for its location (close to great hiking and mountain biking trails, and close to freeways), and all-suite accommodations. We stayed in an Ambassador Suite, and it was huge! The room looked to have recently been remodeled, and was fresh and modern, with a very comfortable King bed in the oversized bedroom. Our little boy slept comfortably on the pull-out couch in the living room.
The only thing I didn't care for too much was how crowded the pools and water park were. There were no available lounge chairs at any pool, and what's worse, people weren't even sitting in them! They simply put their towel on the chairs and then left, perhaps to go down the lazy river or the slides. My 5 year-old enjoyed himself nonetheless, and that's what's important. This resort is a great value, and I would stay here again.

title: “Former NY'ers Loved It!”
text: We stayed in the Andaz in March and loved it. As former New Yorkers and frequent travelers, we really enjoyed our stay at the hotel. The staff was accommodating, the room was quiet with great views of the New York Public Library and we really appreciated the small touches (the free minibar, happy hour, the friendly staff, great bath products). We also got a free upgrade and a bottle of wine after the fire alarm on our floor went off early one morning. The gym is sizable with good weight machines and cardio.

title: “Nice space no big complaints”
text:
I recently stayed at the Marriott Residence Inn Downtown Houston for 4 nights. To begin with the entrance is a little odd as mentioned in previous reviews, there is not spot to pull right in to the front and unload your bags. We had a driver and he had to pull up out front on the street and pull our bags around, there is a small parking lot just past it which serves the Courtyard but it is inconvenient. The glass doors lock and you have to get someone's attention to allow the doors to open. Check in was easy. We had a 2 bdr/2bath unit which was very spacious. Each room had a queen bed, one room had a desk and the other a larger vanity area. The kitchen was spacious and nice to have. Unfortunately our window looked out on the interior dark walls of the other rooms which for 4 nights was a little dreary. Absolutely no view what so ever. The beds were comfortable enough and bathrooms nice enough. There was quite a bit of noise from the pipes next door which was irritating.
The breakfast buffet was fine. We had free Wifi which was a plus.
There is room service from a limited menu which comes from the Courtyard Hotel and some local delivery services as well. The fixtures in the rooms were nice, flat screen t.v.s in each room and updated furnishings. All in all a nice stay.

title: “What a great stay, and amazing trip!”
text:
My spouse and myself stayed here in June for our anniversary. It was located perfectly, the staff were excellent, and it was simply beautiful. We were upgraded upon our arrival, thanks to the amazing management. We stayed a week to soak up the history, site see, and enjoy lots of sea food! It couldn't have been better! We will definitely stay here again! 
Thank you Ames for such a great anniversary, and fabulous stay in Boston! :)

title: “Very Nice but Location is Everything”
text:
I m checking out of Hotel 91 today. We had a double twin for 4 nights. I am on the traiin side. Noise did not bother me since I can hear the trains at night at home as well. What bothered me is the smell walking in and out of hotel from all the Supermarkets. This was of the fish, garbage etc. I would not step in any of these because they all look incredibly filthy. And we did see a nasty rat runny wild in the street. And saw another running in the train staion where the cars would run. Thats 2 more then I have seen in my past 3 other trips.
2 blocks from the F train. This mean at least 30 minutes to any attraction. 20 miute walk to the shopping district in Chinatown. 4th time in NYC in two years first time stayed outside of Midtown. No Starbucks for a good 15 minute walk. Could not figure out what restaurants to eat in because all the signs are in Chinese. Tried one, Mings Cafe right befind the F train stop. Yummy fried noodles. I don't think I saw one place to buy a six pack or bottle of wine. Sidewalks roll up here around 9:00pm while Midtown is happening.
Room was cleaned well except, sheets were not changed. On the last day, no toiletries were given. Common areas very clean. One ice machine was not enought for all floors. There were no vending machines of any kind.
Hotel staff helpfu and very nice. The night clerk was kind enough to help me figure out the thermostat which was a little tricky.
I would not stay here again because because of proximity to Midtown. The walls were way too thin but hey, its just a little noise.
Value is wonderful. I paid$155 a night.

title: “Excellent Hotel -loved the location”
text: Loved staying at the Hard Rock, it was close to everything, we were able to walk to most attractions. Rooms were very clean and quiet, concierage service and housekeeping was wonderful.

title: “Good neighborhood, which was nice but hotel was not up to expectations.”
text: I picked this hotel for it's location, near my sisters apartment, and that it offered a small kitchenette and separate bedroom with sleeper couch in the main room. When we arrived late in the evening everything seemed okay. My husband went the next morning for the breafast. Forget the breakfast! The next night he opened the sleeper couch to find old used linen. Needless to say he slept on the couch closed up. Housekeeping said we needed to let them know ahead if we wanted the couch made up, really it is okay to leave the linen from previous guests? On the second to last night of our week stay. My husband awoke to a mouse running down tbe covers, across ths room and behind the TV. We were moved to a higher floor but we needed to insist. The staff at front desk had mouse traps put in the room but didn't seem to believe us about the mouse. There was mouse dropping under the furniture when it was moved. We received no apologies or sorry only statement like we do not have a rodent problem. Also one other problem. Only one working elevator made for long waits.This hotel could have been great. Fix the cleaning and get some friendly caring front desk staff.

title: “Could be a great hotel but...”
text:
Stayed here over labor day weekend. The hotel has a very nice appearance in the lobby. Room was clean, not overly fancy. Typical of what I expect from a Radisson. But there were some issues. The king bed was very uncomfortable. Was not a sleep number but given I don't like sleep number beds either I wasn't expecting a good nights sleep. 
But there was a real safety issue. We checked out, but were going to remain in the city until late afternoon. The valet garage took us up the cargo/car elevator to the 2nd floor, and then went back down while we loaded the car. Because we cannot operate the auto elevators, we went to the garage's staircase to get back to street level. There are 3 doors to pass through. Behind the 1st door was garbage and folded up rubber mats of some type that had to be walked over. Behind the 2nd door was a pigeon infested staircase with dead birds and dander several inches thick on the floor (this is a serious health hazard). 
I really cannot put in words how much pigeon dander there was. I'm from the city and I'm use to this. But this was over the top.
Then the final door exiting the stairwell was barricaded with furniture. This left us stuck in the stairwell with the pigeons. Our only option was to either go back and wait until another valet car came up the lift, or try forcing our way through the door. After a few minutes we made it through the door. Clearly, if this exit of the building has been left in this condition, I question if a fire marshal inspecting other parts of the property thoroughly.

title: “Beautiful Hotel in a Great Location”
text: We stayed at The Palmer House over Labor Day Weekend. We arrived on Saturday early and even though they had been sold out the night before they already had a room ready for us. Our room (as well as the whole hotel) was beautifully decorated. Our room and bathroom was small, which is understandable considering it is an older hotel. The location was perfect for us to see the sights of Chicago and was incredibly close to public transportation. It was also close to restaurants and shops (Target, CVS) which was convenient. The staff was ok, not overly helpful or friendly, but helped with what we asked.

title: “Great hotel, Great location”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Hotel Commonwealth during a trip to Boston for sightseeing and to visit our granddaughter and nephews. It was a busy time in Boston with the home opener at Fenway and the Marathon on the Monday after we left. We stayed in the "smallest" room, which was more spacious than "large" rooms at other hotels. The service was top rate. If we asked for something, it just appeared without any questions. We loved having the Kenmore T stop right below the hotel. We could easily get anywhere (using our Charlie cards). We had a dinner, a lunch and a breakfast at the Eastern Standard Restaurant; all were superb. We had a couple of cocktails and some upscale bar food at the Hawthorne bar which was also fun and very good. We can't give the Commonwealth enough praise. We're looking forward to staying again the next time we go to Boston.

title: “Parking while staying at the Whitcomb”
text: I wanted to let people know about a great parking option near the Hotel Whitcomb, since I spent a lot of time searching for an alternative to the $35 valet parking they offer and other expensive parking options in the area. The SOMA Grand Garage at 1160 Mission St. around the corner allows for overnight parking for $10 (up to 24 hours) and worked out very well for us. Be sure to check the times it's open since you can only access your car during those times (closes 6pm on Sunday but midnight all other nights, with different opening times). And while the $35 valet at the Whitcomb allows you to take your car out and put it back in during the 24 hour period, there aren't in and out privileges at the SOMA Grand Garage (you pay each time you exit) which is best used if you don't need to park your car repeatedly during the day.

title: “I love the Biltmore & downtown LA”
text:
I have stayed at the Biltmore several times over the past few years and
have always loved it. The area of downtown LA where the Biltmore is
located is NOT dangerous and is NOT near skid row, which is further east.
Yes, there is the occasional panhandler, but that is a minor nuisance.
There is a lot to see and do downtown - Museum of Contemporary Art,
Disney Hall concerts, etc. The hotel itself is beautiful; the murals in the
lounge next to the bar should not be missed. I have eaten at Sai-Sai,
the Japanese restaurant in the hotel, many times - excellent. The rooms
are charming and many have a view.

title: “the best location of hotel in Hollywood Blvd.”
text:
If you are travelling to LA this is just the place u r looking for . it is an absolute value for money. me and my wife found that whatever was worth seeing in Hollywood was at a 5 minute walk from this hotel. The staff were very helpful and arranged for a day trip of the LA downtown on just one little call. although u might find the Metro another convenient option to roam around the city , for going to the Universal city or downtown. There is an excellent grocery store right at the corner where u can find almost anything that u might need. but remember this is a motel and u are taking a room here to sleep not for anything else. Happy holidays . 
shishir

title: “4 day stay in San Diego at Old Twon Inn”
text:
My fiancee and i just left the Old Town Inn ater a 4 day stay, and we were very happy with the room. Originally we chose the cheapest "economy" room but found it too small for the both of us and all our luggage. After 20 mins in the room we decided we should upgrade to the deluxe room with the kitchenette, and we were VERY happy we did.
For the price, the hotel is great value, and if and when we are in San Diego again we will certainly be staying there. We didn't have the free breakfast, but i have read on other reviews that is it is great.
The area is industrial but it is only a short walk to Old Town, which is very quaint. One negative thing from Old Town, dring the afternoon we asked at a Cafe what time they shut, as we wanted to come back for dinner. They told us 10pm, so we got back over to the cafe at .8.50pm, only to be told "the kitchen shuts an hour early" The building shut at 10pm. Pretty pissed off about that, even the 1 hour early shutting was wrong, as we were 10 mins early.
Anyway, we drove to the local IHOp and had a fantastic dinner, so that cafe lost our money. Their loss.
Overall, if you're going to be staying in San Diego, we can strongly suggest a stay, just chuck a bit more on the budgetfor the deluxe.
Cheers :)

title: “Convenient Dallas Hotel”
text: This Dallas area hotel provides a comfortable bed, a separate living room area and complimentary parking/breakfast for Starwoods Elite Members. The hotel had a great price and the location is not too inconvenient for an overnight stay in Dallas. The staff was friendly and helpful. Be careful where you park in the lot, however, my rental car was side-swiped overnight. Overall, a very good hotel in a decent location.

title: “A mixed adventure”
text: very friendly at check in in the beginning, rooms are clean and ok, but very noisy. The wall are very thin, so you can hear when at what your nabour is doing on the toilett in the night and that wakes you up. A complain at the desk where refused, they where not able to help or give you a reduction in the price. The restaurant is ok and the service also, but not more. The spa is small but clean and ok.

title: “Wonderful Surprise”
text: My family and I just returned from our New York City vacation. All my immediate family(7), three generations stayed in a one bedroom suite at the Salisbury hotel. We were nervous at the beginning as to what condition the hotel was in. What a wonderful surprise when we arrived. The best service, very friendly and willing to help. The suite was more than we expected., huge, clean and we felt like if we were in an apartment. Plenty of space for all 7 of us. The $3.00 breakfast was excellent and affordable when you have a large group. I would love to return, now I know which hotel I would stay in. I would recommend this hotel to everyone who is undecided as to where to stay. I had no clue when I was first looking for a hotel. I pretty much went by the great reviews and we were not disappointed. I paid $727.00 for three nights, I booked the reservations through hotelagents.

title: “Very good, and great location but could be better”
text:
Very good hotel in a fabulous location. Rooms, as some have said before are small, but are very nicely decorated, and with lovely views, as well as a very comfortable bed. We were travelling with a 6 month old and had booked a cot. However there was barely enough room to get this in the room, so we ended up upgrading to a suite. This was well worth it giving us room to put the baby to bed and still have some space to ourself. However there is no bath (in any room apparently) so it is not ideal for babies. They did go out of their way however to go and buy us a baby bath which was a nice touch.
Location is fabulous. Right in the heart of Soho and near plenty or restaurants, bars and shops, but on a relatively quiet street just off Broadway.
Staff generally very helpful, especially reception / lobby area staff). Room service however not so good, and was prone to errors. 
Public areas are very nicely decorated, and the restaurant / bar area is a nice place to sit and unwind. Hotel entrance is lovely, walking through a shaded, air conditioned, perfumed walkway, into the main lobby. A lovely escape off Crosby Street having been out for a walk in the heat of New York.
Would recommend this overall, especially for a couple, but not for those with babies.

title: “Very Pleasant Hotel”
text: This Red Lion is very comfortable and understated. Room was nicely decorated and morning papers are delivered to your door 7 days a week. A last minute request for a rollaway was provided while we were out to a ball game - and at no charge. WIFI worked well enough and the downstairs restaraunt and bar was cigar friendly. Not as luxurious as the 4 star Elliott Grand Hyatt but very reasonably priced through Priceline. The staff was helpful.
