Of the several downtown Seattle hotels I have stayed in this one can claim the most accessable location to Pike Street Market, Safeco, etc.

title: “Not the greatest”
text: Hotel is in University City, not La Jolla. Free breakfast is helpful but lacks healthy choices. Also helps offset the $20 nightly parking fee. Staff is friendly. Location is accessible from I-5 and I-805. Mall right across the street. Views from rooms up to the 4th floor are of the parking garage. Disagree with MsSea about rooms looking new or renovated - it's clear that the carpeting is years old, the bathrooms haven't been updated in at least a decade and the hotel is suffering from wear and tear. A/C unit in room cycles on and off noisily all night, every three minutes, so bring ear plugs. I would go back to San Diego any time but next time will stay somewhere else.

title: “in great time of need”
text: with our grandmother just passing we found it very comforting to know they were willing to help us without stay. we were traveling with 3 kids and 2 adults we had the 2 queen bed suite ? very spacious, check in was wonderful, the staff was great, the bar area needed a little work but it had what we needed/ wanted.the hotel was clean. i have no complaints. although i no longer have a reason to come to this area again I would GREATLY recommend this for your stay.

title: “Great location but not a great value”
text: My wife and I spent two nights here for the 4th of July. We chose this hotel because it was close to the waterfront, it was pet friendly and we could use Starpoints for it. The hotel is quite large despite being only three stories. We booked a king bed and were pleased with accommodations, though we would have liked a refrigerator which are available for an extra fee. The room had small balcony overlooking the outdoor pool. As is the case with most Sheraton properties there are a wide range of services for guests including two restaurants and a concierge and car rental desk. A really neat thing they had was gas firepits with chairs set up to people watch, talk or just relax. These were located near the main entrance/guest load and unload and by the pool. We did not use go in the pool, nor did we use the exercise room. I should also note that free wi-fi was only available in the lobby. It was $14.95 per day in the rooms, though the rooms closest to the lobby may be able to get a signal. Parking was $43 per day self park or valet, no difference in price. There are several garages within walking distance that charge less but make sure they are open 24/7. The hotel location was perfect for exploring the Fisherman's Wharf area. Great access to Pier 39, shopping, food, streetcars, and ferries. Overall it was a great stay. If you are budget minded there are probably other hotels near Fisherman's Wharf that would deliver a much greater value than the Sheraton. Considering we used Starpoints, it was a good value. Had we not had our Starpoints, we most likely would have stayed someplace much less expensive.

title: “Great San Francisco Feeling”
text:
This newly renovated hotel is a great place to stay. Staff is very freindly and helpful, has new rooms and lobby...the gift shop was not yet open yet, though.....the hotel sits about halfway up Nob Hill, so if you don't mind walking up and down hills, it is very close to downtown. If you can't manage the steep hills, a cab is just $5, or you can use the house limo for a ride. The pillows were very hard foam, so I asked housekeeping to bring up some feather pillows, which they did promptly. The bar and lounge is very comfortable and a nice place to relax and have a drink and read or wait for a friend. Parking in SF hotels is quite expensive...I recommend looking on the internet for discount parking, about $20 per night and a 12 minute walk. The St. Mary's garage on California Street two blocks down the hill is just $7 per night on week-ends, $32 week-days but no in/out. Overall, I like this hotel and is one of my San Francisco favorites.
If your room is on the street, expect the sounds of The City (which I like), but the views are great. For a quieter night, request and inside room, but no view.

title: “Talk about walking to EVERYTHING!”
text:
We booked online and got a great rate for the "down under" package to stay at this hotel and go to the aquarium. The Inner Harbor is great! What a happening place. 
Our family included myself, my husband and our two sons age 15 and 10. My 15 year old took his skateboard and found many spots to board. We also got an "Oceanopoly" game that came with the package to play during our down time in the hotel.
The hotel room was spacious and clean with two TVs and a separate bedroom (always a plus with teenagers) 
Friday night we went to the Cloud Club reception that had free wine, beer and cheese and crackers. We met some nice people from all over!
But even better was the hot buffet breakfast both Saturday and Sunday morning. Eggs, sausage, bacon, pancakes, potatoes and all kinds of cereals and muffins and fruit. Delicious!
The hotel could use some updating (the carpets are rather worn) and if someone could do something about the clunking manhole cover out front it would quiet the place a bit. But you are right in the thick of inner harbor; so don't expect much quiet!

title: “Good location on the northeast side of town”
text: Hotel design is typical of the Hilton Garden Inn chain - clean, friendly, efficient. Only wish the weight room was better furnished - no exercise bikes. Close to a big mall, lots of restaurants around the area. Somewhat limited on TV channels - no History Channel!

title: “Worst Westin experience ever”
text:
1) Gym requires a 10-minute walk (in gym clothes) through a nice mall -- the directions even say "take a left at Tiffany's".
2) Dinner options are sparse, there is no real restaurant in the hotel -- mall bar only.
3) Room was shabby and needed lift (floorboards coming apart, bottom sheet was pilling and scratchy, shower curtain gross to the touch).
4) No hotel shuttle to offer a lift to offices w/i 1-mile of the hotel -- left me dragging my rollerbag along the side of a 4 lane major divided road.

title: “Very satisfied”
text: We spent two nights at The River Inn, largely based on reviews on this site, and were very satisfied. We got an excellent package deal through the hotel's website (back in March). A minor problem arose with the included attraction tickets, and the manager immediately resolved it to our satisfaction. The kitchenette is a little old, but everything else, including the location, met our expections completely.

title: “Another great visit to the Martinique”
text: We had previously stayed at the Martinique, so knew what to expect. We were not disappointed. The friendliest staff you could wish for. VERY comfortable room and good food in the restaurant, both at breakfast and in the evening. This is now our preferred mid-range hotel in New York city. Great location too.

title: “there is a lot more than river walk in San Antonio”
text:
Great views, beautiful setting, top notch service, wonderful staff, spa is spacious and many options, great meeting space, lots of options for inside or outside special event venues, while I was there, I saw a wedding. vow, the setting was amazing. 
very convenient from the airport. Shopping galore, food was AWESOME... 
I loved it.. can't wait to place a program there...

title: “Great Value”
text:
The Grant Plaza really is incredible value in such an expensive city. Its located in Chinatown, which is a pretty safe part of town to walk around in. The hotel is located within walking distance of Union Square, the Cable Cars and the BART trains. 
The rooms are smallish, but they have everything you need, bed, sink, shower, toilet etc. A reasonable selection of TV channels also. The staff were very helpful and friendly for the most part. 
The downside to the hotel for me was being stuck on the 2nd floor, with a very noisy air conditioner outside my window starting and stopping all night - and being that the rooms are no air conditioned it gets stuffy if the window is closed. Theres also a good deal of noisy traffic that passes the hotel. 
All this said i was very satisfied with the Grant Plaza and for 80-100 bucks a night it absolutely can't be beaten!

title: “Fair hotel”
text: If you have a Moscone Center conference, then this is a fair choice considering the high price of the W and the rest. It's a 15 minutes walk through one of the sliziest streetsbof San Francisco

title: “The horriblst think I ever saw”
text: we changed three times the room before we left the hotel. We couldn't believe what we saw. The rooms were so dirty. The mattresses were broken, a lot of waste, bottles, tissues, dust, mud under the bed. Dirty walls. Mold on the wall. Stickier carpet. Dead flights. No clean bathroom.

title: “Loved the Blue Moon Hotel”
text: This hotel was first class all the way. Everyone at the Blue Moon, the owner and staff, couldn't have been nicer and more pleasant. They couldn't have been more accommodating and willing to go the extra mile for their guests. The accommodations were utterly beautiful. The food was absolutely fabulous. I recommend this hotel very highly to anyone that needs a hotel on the Lower East Side.

title: “Nico hotel, good location”
text:
I leved for 4 days in this hotel. Here the pros and cons
positive:
- management was very flexible with early check in
- my room had a beautiful view of Seattle
- in the room, everything worked well, it was clean and well maintained
- extremely comfortable bed with extremely comfortable linens
- the day housekeeping lady was very friedly
- free wifi in the lounge
negative
- internet in the rooms costs 11 dollar per day, which is ok - but you cn only subscribe for 1 day and have to renew it every time. Why don't they offer a multi-day pass?
- in the first evening, there was a turn down service, but in the following three, the service was not offered anymore (why???)
- it can get noisy

title: “Good for the second timers”
text:
Excelsior is a hotel with a little bit more character than your average NYC experience. Upper West Side is a really nice part of Manhattan, slightly away from the buzz but still with plenty of nice restaurants, bars and pubs. I was fortunate enough to be experiencing the annual Columbus Avenue street market. 
Surprisingly enough, after reading some of the reviews, I didn't find staff rude or unhelpful at all.
This is not really a hotel for your first holiday in New York. Excelsior is rather far away from the action of Times Square. Being a third timer, Belvedere remains my favourite hotel but is unfortunately a lot less affordable than it used to be.
For second timers and perhaps for some more mature travellers Excelsior could be a perfect choice.

title: “Nice enough but a few major quirks”
text:
The James is a very attractive property. Aesthetically, it is well designed and the location is excellent for visiting Tribeca and SOHO. 
The hotel offers some unexpected perks such as complimentary drinks and snacks in the lobby; however, it has some quirks that are unexpected and disappointing:
- very few power outlets in the rooms. existing outlets are awkwardly placed making them very hard to use. unbelievable for new construction
- an in-room coffee maker is provided but you must place it in the bathroom sink or on the floor near the curtains in order to plug it in
- no desk / work area
- no kitchen / restaurant
I liked the James but wanted to like it more. It is fine if you get a good deal but it would be extremely disappointing if the room rates were above $300/$350 USD.

title: “Fantanstic 5* Nob Hill Property”
text: Wonderful old restored hotel (oldest property in their "chain"). Great location, extremely attentive staff. Walk into lobby even if you don't stay there.

title: “Hyatt Austin, convenient”
text: Good hotel. Very convenient. Walk to the bar/music scene on 06th but far enough away to avoid the noise and chaos. 2 mins walk to the bat bridge. 06th Ave 10-15 mins walk. Several decent restaurants nearby including the excellent Manuels for mexican. 20 mins from airport.

title: “Fabulous boutique hotel with great service!”
text: We were extremely pleased with our stay at La Pensione. The hotel has been recently renovated and looks just lovely. We were greeted by Front Desk Clerk Stephanie, who was simply a delight. Our guest room on the 4th floor overlooked the courtyard and was clean and well appointed. With the hotel next to the sign entering Little Italy, it was great to be able to walk to a cafe in the morning for coffee and to a fabulous restaurant for evening dining. We will definitely stay at this hotel again and would recommend this hotel for couples (not so much for families).

title: “Worst hotel ever”
text:
I've been travelling for more than fifteen years between three and seven days per week. This is the worst hotel I've ever stayed in. We all know mistakes happen or things don't go exactly as planned, but this hotel's response to their own problems was unbelievable. 
- Checked me into an occupied room
- Free internet does not work, they told me to stand by the door of the room to use computer
- Bed and bath linens did not look or smell clean
- I was moved between five rooms. Was there for business and got virtually no work done. 
- Walls are paper thin, could hear conversation from next door room loud and clear
- Room was very cold, heat does not work.
- They offered me room service to make up for the problems. The room service menu was out of date so everything I tried to order was not available. I recd a $38 charge for room service. 
- Staff was very rude on check in and made a big deal about me being a 'priceline' customer. 
- Was denied request to speak to manager while there. Spoke to manager after trip, she was not nice. Everytime she asked me a question, she would talk over me as I tried to explain what happened. I see where her employees get their non customer service attitude. I've requested to speak with Red Lion corp HQ four times with no response.

title: “Great Location”
text: It was the first trip to New York City for me and my 11 year old daughter. The hotel was very clean and the staff is very friendly. Excellent location!

title: “Great location, great room.”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Comfort Inn Downtown Memphis for one night on our way to Nashville. The location and the price we payed for the room was great. It's located right by the stop for the trolley that will take you down to Beale Street for $1. I know there were many other hotels to choose from that were closer to Beale Street, but I think we got the best deal with this hotel. Our room also was very large, nicely decorated and clean. The location of the hotel was also very easy to get to and then when we left, it was simple to get to the highway.

title: “If you want a place to sleep --- this is NOT the place for you”
text: If you like being woken at 2am to a the sounds of a garbage truck outside your window, stay here. The garbage truck will stay for OVER an hour picking up the garbage from a neighboring hotel. I called front desk to complain, and they said they could not move me to another room (very f***ing hard to believe that this could not be done). This was a travel nightmare. Avoid the nightmare. Avoid this hotel.

title: “Great Stay at this new Spring Hill Suites”
text: Brought my niece and her two young children to Indy to see the Zoo & Children's Museum. This was a great location for the Zoo and a short walk to the Monument Circle. Everyone was very impressed with Indy and with this hotel. The layout of the room worked out great for us--Everyone seemed to have a "private" place to change, etc. The kids spent a lot of time in the pool and it looked very cleam. Breakfast in the morning was very abundant. I appreciate the key-operated elevator and didn't find it difficult to use at all. In fact, the kids enjoyed activating it with the key. The hotel is located a little off the beaten path, but Indy's downtown is so vibrant, that we felt comfortable walking several blocks at night, as well as walking the canal. We used valet parking and found it quite convenient. We'll stay re again.

title: “Great Location and a good value”
text: This was our second stay at this Holiday Inn. We love the fact that it is next to the trolly and from there you can go anywhere. If you wish you can rent a car and take the short drive to Napa or south to Monterey. We did both. The room was spacious and clean. We booked a corner king on the 20th floor. Great view and other than the typical city noises, it was quiet. The bed was very comfortable and the pillows were good. The staff was excellent and responded to our needs quickly and with a smile. We will stay here again on our next trip to San Francisco!

title: “Good choice for a difficult city”
text: The Alexander Inn is within a somewhat longish walk to the Independence Hall area of Philadelphia. Parking is off-site - about 5 blocks (walking) but because of the one-way streets, longer driving. Our room was small, but comfortable. The neighborhood has some good restaurants, but there are some seedy bits as well. We don't like to sleep with the air conditioner running, but the street noise was too loud to sleep with open windows. Breakfast was mediocre. However, the price for a big city was about as good as you can get and the staff was very helpful.

title: “Satisfied but Frustrated”
text: I had to take cold showers 2 out of the 3 days I stayed there and this left a bad taste in my mouth. Management did however have a complimentary attitude regarding this matter. The reference towards the fact that I had a great rate as opposed to having to take cold showers didn't sit well with me. I believe that I should have been comped a night or two. That's my opinion.

title: “NEVER EVER EVER AGAIN!!”
text: Let me first start by telling you myself and a girl friend of mine went to this hotel to visit my fiance who is in the army national guard and is doing his AIT at fort sam huston. We are from Pa and this was my 2nd time to San Antonio. The first time I did not stay at hill country this time i did. we were there 3 nights and 4 days. In this time we had to change rooms 3 times. once was because the toilet over flooded and we ahd an inch of water on the floor. the second time was because we ahd about 6 four inch at least roaches or as their staff likes to call them "water bugs" in our room. The guy at the front desk handed ME a can of Raid and told me to kill them! Seriously? this is not my job! so then they moved me again. the third room i was in for one night. it was ok at best. bathroom is extremely small in all rooms, carpet is dirty, place is old feeling and smelly. at best i would give this hotel a 1 but even that is pushing it. also when i came home from this trip i was extremely sick (not blaming hotel for this) but anyway i did go to the er there they informed me i had BED BUG BITES on my legs and arms!!!n So did the other girl I was with, we had thought they were mosquito bug bites but they werent. i am in the process of trying to get my money back their GM Blaine is not helpful at all i am contacting an attorny general and the BBB this place was a mess and i will never ever ever stay here again!!!! i wouldnt recommend this hotel to my worst enemy! it was the worst i have ever stayed at

title: “Another Wonderful Stay at a Superb Hotel !!”
text: Sometimes when you have a great experience at a hotel, a repeat visit is not as memorable. However, this was not the case at Hilton Charlotte University Place. In fact, it was even better! Once again, the room was spotless and well appointed, but, this time I came back to the room to find a towel animal in my bathroom. What a pleasant surprise thanks to Oneyda from housekeeping. I was also greeted with a smile each morning by Imok in the Executive Lounge (you owe it to yourself). She kept the lounge spotless and had a nice variety of tasty goodies laid out for breakfast. I, once again, have to thank Melissa Ewert, the guest loyalty manager, for her hospitality and help with whatever I needed. The rest of the staff and management could not be more friendly and welcoming. It's worth a trip to Charlotte just to stay at this hotel !!

title: “Ok, but $$ food and poor service.”
text: Stayed here for a conference that was being held at the hotel in April 2012. Room was great. Very comfortable beds. Spacious room. Lots of storage for clothes. Nice bathroom set up (extra vanity and sink outside washroom). Pool area is nice. My major complaint is that the service was quite terrible at the hotel. The female bartender was exceptionally rude. The food was extremely overpriced and lacked variety (perhaps the steakhouse was better, but i did not go in there). We ate elsewhere as much as we could because the service was extremely slow. We left on one occassion because the waitress ignored us for at least 20 minutes while we were waiting to order our breakfast. I recommend eating elsewhere (Ladda Thai Cuisine, Zeytoun...both walking distance). There is nothing to do in the area where te hotel is located, although a new casino is being built nearby. I would recommend staying elsewhere, as this was not a cheap hotel and the service was terrible.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Hilton from December 13th through 15th, 2004. Everthing was as good if not better than anticipated. We loved the Executive Lounge and used it twice a day during our stay on th 41st floor. The elevators were fast and there was minimal waiting time. 
All the staff were extremely friendly and helpful. The room was large enough considering the average size of NYC hotel rooms and very clean.
We have stayed at other hotels in New York in the past but this will be our permanent base on future trips.

title: “Whatahotel!!”
text: What a great staff and a lovely New York hotel!!

title: “Friendly, Efficient, Comfortable and Convenient”
text:
I recently spent a week at the Holiday Inn Express Phoenix Downtown with my co- coach and our volleyball team during the Volleyball Festival June 21 - 28, 2011. Vanessa greeted us with a friendly smile and lots of energy. She had everything set up for us, so check in was nearly instant. She set the tone for the week. From that moment on, it seemed that we were the number one priority for anyone on the staff that we had the pleasure of talking with. The cook was more attentive than a waiter at a four star restaurant. Breakfast was basic, but tasty and nutritious, with scrambled eggs and meat available every day. The housekeeping staff was friendly and efficient; the rooms were clean and comfortable. The front desk staff was always on top of everything. When the night person said they would let the morning person know what we wanted, they meant it. 
The location was perfect for us. We spent the majority of our time at the convention center, just a 10 minute walk away. Five minutes will get you to the Arizona Center with a nice variety of good restaurants. The immediate area felt safe. I did not have to worry about my players' safety while walking them to and from volleyball and restaurants. The team enjoyed the swimming pool and spa once the sun went down (it reached 115 degrees one day). The property is fenced.
In all, our stay could not have been better. If you are looking for affordable lodging in the downtown Phoenix area, give Vanessa a call at the Holiday inn Express Downtown.

title: “Tiny Corner Room and SCRATCHED CAR!”
text:
After a LONG drive, we checked in at about 9 p.m., valeted the car and went to our assigned room - a TINY corner room. So much for SPG upgrades. The wait staff who brought our room service confirmed that this was one of the SMALLEST rooms in the hotel. After getting nowhere with the front desk staff on duty that night, we decided to check out the following morning and move to the St. Regis, a sister property to the Westin. 
Upon checkout, there was an awful series of deep scratches in the driver''s side door of our Grand Cherokee that were not there when we checked in - the car was flawless upon arrival. It looked as if some one had rubbed it hard with a key chain. Of course, it is then revealed that Westin doesn't park the cars and is not responsible for them - The Westin front dest manager on duty said that the separate company who handles the valet would conduct an "investigation' and determine if they were at fault. Nobody ever admitted fault or paid for the damage - it was my tough luck.
I wouldn't stay at this location again - the St. Regis or the Meridian are FAR BETTER options if you want to stay with the Starwood group of Hotels - they have better rooms with better views and FAR superior service.

title: “Reservation Not Honored. Charged full price for cot.”
text:
Beware - they won't honor your reservation, and will still charge you full price.
My fiance booked a room for a conference. She booked 2 months in advance and paid top dollar. When she showed up at 11PM, they didn't have a room for her. They put her in a cot in the hospitality suite. When she complained about paying so much and not getting to sleep in a real bed, in a real hotel room, they would only offer a free breakfast.
When you travel, you pay for reliability and trust. I trusted a loved one to the Hyatt brand and they treated her like garbage. I have lost all respect for the Hyatt brand, and hope you will avoid this hotel in protest of the way they treated my fiance. No paying customer should be treated like this.
Shame on you, Hyatt. If you get bumped from a flight, you are entitled to a credit. Apparently if you get bumped from a hotel, you get the honor of sleeping on a cot at full price, with a measly breakfast.

title: “Wonderful experience at Hyatt Regency DFW”
text: While an older but updated and renovated Hyatt, this lovely hotel is second to none in quality, class, and service. My husband and I stayed one night after his arrival home from the middle east. I booked the room via Priceline.com's name-your-pwn-price option after reading several of the reviews. From the parking valet to room check-in, from Ace's Bar and Grill to room service, the Hyatt Regency DFW is tops in making you feel as if you are their only customer! After checking in, we visited Ace's Bar and Grill in the lobby for drinks and a snack. The service was top-notch while the drinks & food were most excellent (we ordered texas steak nachos). Although some reviews stated the rooms were small, ours was of average size (as big as we needed) and furnished very comfortably. The bed is heavenly and the chair and ottoman very comfortable. The bathroom is divided - vanity/sink apart from the shower/toilet. Unlike other reviewers experience, our shower didn't leave a lot of water on the floor; in fact, the floor was dry and the bathmat was barely damp. I was only faintly aware of three or four planes landing during our stay but, hello - you are in the middle of an airport! The noise didn't disturb my husband at all. We didn't notice any noise from any other guests. Room service was prompt (less than 25 minutes from order to delivery) and the food was fresh and tasty. Everything was at it's proper temperature - the angus burger was delicious and the peach berry cobbler was simply divine! I had a side of berries (strawberries, blackberries, and raspberries) and they were fresh and sweet. The batteries were dying in the TV remote but one call to guest services and within 5 minutes, a technician was at our door to replace them. Staff (reception to room service) are very courteous, pleasant, and extremely helpful. My husband and I highly recommend the Hyatt Regency DFW and plan on staying there for all our travel needs when flying in or out of DFW.

title: “Worth staying at if you have business at McCormick Place”
text: Just returned having attended a conference at McCormick Place. The hotel itself is clean and 4 star quality. There is a skywalk on the 2nd floor that leads right into McCormick Place so it made going back and forth very convenient. As other readers have pointed out, as long as you have business at McCormick Place, it is the place to stay at for sure. The only challenge is the hotel is not near anything else (I did discover a McDonalds about a 5-10 min walk). I did make the use of the hotel shuttle into town but it only runs up to 6 pm - it dropped me off downtown and I managed to take the bus back (the #3 bus by the way). Overall, I had a very pleasant experience.

title: “THIS is our Columbus hotel!”
text: Don't be scared off by the location. This hotel is clean and the staff is very friendly/helpful. The double room was spacious, looks big enough for a roll away if needed, and very clean. The bathroom was clean, which you would not expect at this price. The hallways were swept and clean as well. I was pleasantly surprised. Glad i read the other reviews. Just DON"T be scared off by the location. We will stay here each time we are in Columbus!

title: “You will never want to leave!!!”
text: You will feel welcome from the minute you walk in the door. The staff is extremely nice and helpful and the rooms are trememdously comfortable. The rooms are spacious yet cozy and have featherbeds, robes. and a BOSE clock/radio The FREE high speed internet hook up is great and the continental breakfast with fresh pastries, berries, fruit and more is better than you will ever expect.Henderson;s Wharf will become your new bench mark for excellence in Hotels!!! You will never want to leave!!

title: “close to everything”
text: We stayed at the hotel for one night only,we had a cruise to catch the next day.The hotel itself is nice and the staff are very nice especially Reggie the doorman.The only problems we had were that the hotel had a long flight of stairs to climb with no guest elevator, and we ran into some rowdy punks while out walking to dinner,but there were a lot of other people out walking so we still felt safe.We had one more problem that has nothing to do wiyh the hotel.There were 4 of us and a lot of luggage for a 10 day cruise and we had problems getting a taxi to carry us to the port.We had to wait well over a hour to try to find a van.We only found one because he pulled up to drop someone off.I would reccommend if you have a large group to make arrangements ahead.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Just returned from a weekend break in New York. We booked the Affinia on the internet and we were delighted to see that the hotel more than matched the description we had seen. The hotel is extremely clean and has all the amenities you could require. The staff are efficient and helpful. The in-house restaurant is also extremely good. I would recommend this hotel most highly and if lucky enough to visit New York again I would stay there.

title: “No second-rate rooms for Manchester Grand Hyatt guests.”
text:
My husband and I travelled to san diego this year for the 4th of july weekend. We used a new hotel reservation service, hotwire, primarily because our travelling companions had done so and we wanted to stay in their hotel too...while we did not get into their hotel, we did get a great price on a great hotel. 
Situated at the foot of market street, in downtown san diego, this hotel has it all...and then some. We arrived a little late on Saturday, so had to take the room they assigned to us, even though it had only two full size beds and a view of the back of the elevator bank (literally, the way they arranged the furniture in the room, the bed faced toward the hotel, instead of away from it toward the downtown skyline). When I called the front desk to see about a bigger bed (you know what they say, once you've slept on a cal king you don't want to go back), they told me it was hopeless for the evening, but to call back in the afternoon and see what had opened up.
I really didn't think they would move us. We had booked our room on a discount site, were paying easily half of what the other guests were being asked to, and did nothing but complain about our dreadful room.
Not only did they move us, but they put is in the new tower, on the 26th floor where we were able to watch the 4th of july fireworks display from our room. from that vantage point we were able to see all 3 of the synchronized shows while enjoying room service and the company of our friends, instead of the drunken masses of people on the roads below us. We watched this same group of people wait for two hours to leave the area, as the traffic jam was endless.
Thank you, to the new Manchester Grand Hyatt, the bellhops and the front desk clerks who treated us right, regardless of how we came to stay at their hotel.

title: “Excellent, Relaxin time”
text: I made a road trip to San Diego with my wife and I wanted to stay on the beach. I immediately saw this hotel and knew it was the right one for this trip. The management and staff was excellent. They were courteous and made my search for a great hotel complete. For a smaller hotel with no big corporate name, I felt like an important celebrity. Even though I got an ocean view room, each room provides the great beach exprience. They are also pet friendly and provide separate balaconies for your loved pets. Thanks OBH!

title: “Great place”
text: The staff was so accomodating & helpful. The rooms were immaculate, & the beds were very comfy. Our room had a large L-shaped sofa which was nice to lounge on. The continental breakfast was very nice, & was complete with complimentary Starbuck's coffee. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Wonderful location, staff, and fun for everyone!”
text:
We have stayed at the Westin many times and have to say how friendly the staff is and how much our family enjoys and relaxes each time we visit! Our kids love the Discovery Zone with water fun and we enjoy the spa, yoga, workout facilities, and all amenities! In the winter,we love the ice rink and can't wait to see it this year. The Recreation Director even stopped and talked to us about how they are doing more with it this year. We also are able to take a shuttle to the RIM and La Cantera!
It is our choice hotel everyone we head to San Antonio.

title: “Wonderful!”
text: This hotel was beautiful, comfortable, and elegant. The room was perfect.

title: “Worst hotel experience ever”
text:
Travel extensively for business and pleasure, and the Handlery at Union Square is the worst hotel at which I've ever stayed.
First "patti" from the hotel confused our dual reservation - 1 night personal, 5 nights business so that we nearly had to pay twice for 1 night.
Second - was made aware of free wi-fi 3 days into our stay
Third - extremely loud party scheduled directly below our room on a Tuesday night
Fourth - no help with bags 
Fifth - colleagues offered complimentary coffee, papers, etc. But not offered to me until I asked forecfully
Sixth - completely uncaring staff - examples Ed (an intern) attempted to put off my complaint about lack of equal comps for our company travel until I forced the issue by standing there until something was done
I've got two night left here and don't see any improvement.

title: “The best in San Antonio”
text:
I have had to be in San Antonio 3 or 4 times over the past year or so and have stayed a couple of different places. The last 2 times [within the past 45 days or so] I have stayed at the Mokara Hotel. By far, the pick of the litter in San Antonio. 
I travel externsively for business and pleasure and what impressed me the most about the Mokara is the warm and professional staff there. Some places you stay yo get the canned lines like "my pleasure" or :have a nice day." Each of the last 2 times I have been there I felt an unusual real, sincere desire to serve from all I met; from check in to the valet.
The rooms, especially the ones on the river are large and clean. I can't speak or rate the spa or restaurants, but I highly recommend this hotel. Thanks!

title: “Great Location, Great Stay”
text: Booked The Milford Plaza for a group of 25 for 4 days for a business meeting in NYC. I was a bit nervous based on the reviews I read on Trip Advisor. We had great stay. If you're looking to compare this Hotel to the Intercontinental you will probably be disappointed but if you're for a good clean hotel in the Times Square area at a good value you will be happy. The lobby is under construction so the bar is temporary bu tthere is enough in the area if you're looking for a better bar. There is no restaurant in the hotel but again there's enough close by. Some of my group was from Europe and found an all all night deli in the area to get breakfast at 4 am.

title: “Great location, super shower and good sleeps”
text:
This hotel is not the Waldorf or the Ritz and if that's what you're looking for then this is not the place for you...firm mattresses provided great sleep...newly renovated bathrooms (with excellent showers) were terrific and while there isn't a lot of room we didn't spend much time there anyway (this is NYC after all). We had 4 rooms booked (on different floors) and everyone enjoyed the location and the cleanliness and the price and the bar fridge came in handy.
If we had any concerns it would be that the towels are small (pack a bath sheet if you need) , our room didn't have an alarm clock (we didn't have a flat screen either but most of the other rooms in our party did) , the air conditioner hadn't been installed for summer yet (which was bad on the days it was over 70 but OK because it was 52 on our last day), there are no screens on the window (which was a little odd) and there isn't a huge amount of storage space for clothing (the original closets were removed for the bathroom reno and frankly the bathroom reno is worth not having much storage space)
 Despite what some of the reviews have said we found the staff quite professional and friendly enough (but maybe that's because we're all Canadian and smiled first;-) and certainly experienced none of the problems that dogged other visitors (one of our group actually asked to be switched from a single to a double because the single was too small and they did so right away and only charged the single price).

title: “Be aware”
text: Requested an early check in as my flight arrived at 7:30 in the mornIng. Got told would be upto 1.5 hours before a room would be available. Went for a 25 min walk to the closest shops to get a bite to eat, came back to find it would be longer and finally at 2pm got a room. Called several days before arrival to make sure they had a foldout bed available in the room and early check in to find the fold out bed had not been recorded down and there was an additional charge for $30 per night. Found someone's old bandage which came out of the mattress when taking off the blanket. Had also been bitten on my legs which would indicate bed bugs. As for location, not the best unless you have a car or catch the bus. This is literally nothing close by in walking distance. Gym has very limited equipment and only suited for use for 2 people at a time.

title: “I liked this hotel, great location and awesome views”
text:
My boyfriend attended the National Home Builders convention and I went along with him to relax and take in some sites. This hotel is awesome, we got checked in easily and had a great room on the 15th floor of the north tower, it was a corner suite that overlooked both the city and the marina. (The North tower has balconies in every room and the South tower only has them on corner suites.) We arrived at a time when a lot of people were checking in for the convention but the process was seamless for us, they tried to give us a room on the third floor but another room came available, we would have waited for a higher room but we got lucky. Every one of the hotel staff that I encountered were very friendly and helpful. We used the valet a lot and they were great, offered directions etc.. Whenever we were getting ready to leave, we would call down to the valet before we left the room so they would have our car waiting when, it worked out great.
The views of downtown are incredible and the fireworks show after the Padres game was pretty cool. The train is right across the street from the hotel but I didn't find it disruptive when it came through, I found this location to be ideal for what we wanted to do.
San Diego is very impressive, if you like architecture then I would suggest renting a bike from the hotel and take off peddling, I got some great photos of the cool lofty condo's / converted warehouses in the downtown area. This hotel is also close to the downtown mall (Westfield Horton Plaza) and to Fashion Valley which you can take the train to or if you have a car, its about 10 minutes. 
Things to do: We went to the Viejas Casino one night which worked out great, I shopped at the outlet mall and my boyfriend played poker. It was a nice drive, about an hour from the hotel, we put the top down and away we went. We drove around the area and took in some sites in La Jolla, Torrey Pines golf course is great, we watched some hand gliders take off nearby.
We also drove over to Coronado and went to the Hotel Del's Sun Deck Bar & Grill watched the fighter plans take off and land (from the Naval Air Station on North Island), it was incredible!! 
I would recommend this hotel for anyone going to San Diego, I would request a high room in the North tower, we were in room 1518 and it was almost perfect, another patio chair would have been nice but overall I give this hotel 2 thumbs up.

title: “A wonderful hotel!”
text: My sister and I were greeted by 2 very friendly and helpful people at the front desk- Edgardo and Jennifer. They were able to help us with an earlier check in which made things much easier for us. The room was very attractive - lots of counter space in the bathroom for two women. The restaurant was excellent- probably the best lamb shank I ever had in my life! I don't travel to DC often, but if I ever go again, I will try to stay at the Hotel George.

title: “Best place in NYC!”
text: This hotel is my favorite place to stay while in NYC. You simply cannot beat the location, right in times square! You can walk to shows, shopping and great restaurants. The rooms are plush, clean and comfortable. Be sure to have a drink in their bar as you look out at the traffic and lights. Highly recommend a stay here.

title: “Old and Tired”
text:
I stayed here for two nights for a conference. The hotel seems as if it was recently purchased by the Blake owners. However, the management has a lot of work to do.
The room was dirty. The bed was uncomfortable. The hallway carpeting was worn in many places. Even the wall art and the choices of colors indicated that the facility is very dated. 
The hotel wireless internet was down for most of the three days that I was there.
The hotel is also slightly off the beaten bath and thus it's not easy to walk to any restaurants or bars. The room service is provided by nearby pizza shops.
All-in-all, the Blake is a tired, old facility. There are better places to stay in Charlotte.

title: “Great Hotel in San Fran”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for 4 nights while in San Fran. Overall it was great. The rooms are very small but cozy and comfortable. We had booked a King Room with Bay Views and that's what we got (although the windows were not very big). The free coffee in the mornings was appreciated as were the fresh cookies, ice cream and root beer each evening (it was quite a treat to make ice cream sandwiches and root beer floats!). The location of the hotel was fantastic. We were only 2 blocks away from the Ferry Building (with a great Farmers Market Saturday mornings), and an easy walk to Pier 39 and Fishermen's Wharf. A trolley car stop was a block away if you didn't want to walk. The staff at the front desk were helpful with suggestions when asked. Overall, a very nice stay.

title: “Good price, great location!”
text: A tree stars hotel in a great and safe location in the heart of Frisco, less than 5 minutes walk from Union Square and NobHill. Friendly people, complimentary internet access, cozy and clean room (no conditionated air, a least in our room, even if sometimes US it could be an asset!), a small but however useful fitness room. Maybe a little bit old because of the historical building it's set in, that however makes the location suggestive. Let's say: if you manage to find out a 130$ room for night consider it a good deal, considering you are in Frisco, the location you are going to sleep and the breakfast (that is often included).

title: “Great hotel”
text:
Right from the front desk to the Restaurant staff/Room keeping staff, everyone was excellent! I would highly recommend this for the business traveller. As I am not from this country, it was nice to see Ford's office right across from this hotel :D
Will stay here if I get a chance again.

title: “Only one problem”
text: This was a great location with terrific room and a great parking garage. The rooms were spacious and very clean. The front desk were pleasant and helpful. Our only problem is we went to a cocktail reception that just served appetizers and came back to the hotel still hungry. It was just turning midnight and the restaurant and bar were closed. I was shocked that a hotel in the Galleria in such a Cosmopolitan City would close their bar so early. We couldn't even get peanuts.

title: “Great Hotel For The Price You Pay”
text:
Stayed here about a week ago for a couple of days. The manager, reception and valet parking services were all incredibly friend and accomodating. Will definitely stay here again especially for the price.
Definitely get the parking package if you can or need to, valet parking is normally $30/day and self park is $25/day; with the package only paid $20/day which is a bargain by SF standards. 
Make sure to request a quiet room when checking in, the doors and walls tend to be a bit thin. Our request for a small room was met with a friendly smile, which was great. Our room was towards the back part of the hotel, away from the elevators and stairwells with no walls connected to another room so our room was very quiet. No problems with street noise either. The only thing is when people walk through the hallways near your room, you can hear the entire conversation. Not a problem if youre out and about exploring the city most of the day. 
The room itself was a little small but how much room does one need when all youre using the room for is to sleep and shower? The furnishing in both the rooms and lobby were great as is the free wine reception at the lobby everyday from 530-600pm. 
Great location as it is only a couple of blocks up from Union Square; we used public transportation to get around to everywhere else but nothing was more than a few blocks away. If youre planning on using public transportation, buy the MUNI pass. It allows unlimited access to all public transportation, plus cable cars which are $5/ride alone.

title: “Great value, friendly staff, comfortable room”
text: We had to run down to Los Angeles to take our daughter to the airport. We asked for a double Queen room and they had one. The room was pleasant, comfortable, clean and fashionably decorated. Very nice. I had free drink for being priority. Parking costs, but most places charge for parking in these areas. It was overall a nice trip. Beautiful hotel with amenities including gift shop, hair salon, lounge, restaurant, sushi bar, coffee shop, guest services, concierge, valet parking etc. Close and easy to the airport with a shuttle as well.

title: “Loved It!”
text: Hubby and I in NYC for an 10 year anniversary celebration. We both loved the Marriott. We used Marriott points for our 2 night stay. Had a great room on the 23rd floor. The room was spacious, clean, comfy bed, and a view of Times Square. We were also on the same floor as the Fitness Center which was the best in any hotel I have ever stayed and it actually tempted you to work-out, which I did this morning before checking out. The service was great - friendly and helpful staff. We loved the elevator system and if you rode up in an outer elevator, the views on your way were great. The staff that welcomed you on the 1st floor helped to guide you to the 8th floor lobby and introduce you to the elevator system. Easy as can be and no long lines to wait. After check-in and in search of dinner options, the gal who checked us in suggested Juniors which is directly behind the hotel. Great burgers and NY cheesecake. After dinner, we went to The View lounge for 'the view' and a $15.00 drink - yes pricey, but we did get a souvenir glass and we were in NYC after all. We enjoyed breakfast our first morning in the Encore Restaurant in the Marriott and had the breakfast buffet. Service and food both very good. After some sightseeing (weather was rainy, so not perfect), we had a drink in The Broadway Lounge in the Marriott before getting ready for dinner and our show - Wicked - which was FABULOUS and highly recommended! I loved the location of the Marriott, the great staff, comfortable rooms, and we will be sure to return on our next visit to New York City!

title: “Elegant and Charming”
text: I traveled to Dallas on business and this property was recommended by a colleague who works in the downtown area. From my check-in to departure, service was attentive and warm. The front desk, staff and even valets were very chatty and eager to answer any questions. I stayed in a 20th floor suite that was very large by city standards with a separate work area. The common space of the hotel is an attraction unto itself: very elegant sitting areas leading up to the French Room, with great service should you wish to have a glass of wine or some appetizers. The downstairs connects to a low-key sports bar. The property's location places you within walking distance to much of the business district, as well as several museums, the aquarium, and an art district. I prefer hotels with personality and history when I travel to other cities, and this property falls squarely in that category. It reminded me of a cross between the Seelbach and Brown Hotels in Louisville, which is a very, very good thing.

title: “Great expensive hotel!”
text:
My hubby surprised me for my birthday weekend. Rented the corner suite on the 21st floor. The view is awesome. The room is huge. The furniture is ehh, just okay and I felt there just wasnt enough furniture to fill the room. There's a sofa by the windows and a mod chair. A desk. Two chairs by the window facing the freeway, a closet and the bed. It definitely was not a plush room. Maybe it's all about the view. I dont know. The bed was very comfortable. 
We had dinner at WP24. The food can be compared to PF Changs but double the price. 
Breakfast was included in our room rate so we also had breakfast at the LA market on the first floor. I had french toast. It was very bland. My hubby had blueberry pancakes. Also very bland.
We had stayed the night to see the Michael Jackson Immortal show. The show was awesome.
I would stay at the hotel again for the convenience.

title: “This is no MGM Grand”
text:
Our new "buzz" statement whenever we entered a new place to stay after we left the MGM Grand was the title of this review. And I expect we will continue this "joke" for some time to come. The MGM Grand was hands down the most amazing place. The staff, the amenities, the room..THE ROOM..the spa, the swimming pool. It doesn't get much better. There isn't much more to say that others haven't said. I will add that the turndown service was awesome (I won't elaborate so as not to give it away and ruin the fun surprise). I live in New York (we were in town visiting friends) but I would seriously consider returning simply for a spa visit.
Dinner was great (pricey..New York pricey..but worth it). We aren't gamblers but the vibe was fun.
If you want to impress someone (or yourself) GO. This was one expensive hotel visit that was worth it. I can't recall being able to say that about any other place in recent memory-with most expensive hotels the overall experience is good but there are always some drawbacks. The MGM Grand is over the top great.

title: “Nice facility, I'd stay again.”
text:
I took 3 rooms for a weekend visit for myself and visiting in-laws. I don't have any serious complaints. The rooms were clean and well stocked. The pool area is quite cramped, but it was still a nioce diversion for an hour or so. We ate out on the river walk, so I can't comment on the restaurant. It was convenient to be able to walk right out and be on the riverwalk, although still a couple blocks from the main activities on the river (nice walk though).
Prices are a bit steep, but then so are all the rest of the downtown hotels. With the prices, I'm not sure it's also necessary to charge $20/day for parking.

title: “Great location, good quality budget hotel.”
text: The best thing about The Belvedere was that it is a two-minute walk from Times Square. As with most hotels in Manhattan, you get a double bed each (I travelled with my mother-in-law!) The only disappointment was that there was no bar, I didn't think to check before I booked because I assumed that every hotel would have one. The room wasn't as plush as the photographs, but adequate and with an amazing view of Manhattan. We didn't spend a lot of time in the hotel, but it was great for a base. There were no problems with the lifts, as in other reviews. We went to a small cafe round the corner (sorry can'r remember the name) and got a big breakfast every morning, really cheap) The bathroom was a bit on the small side. A fridge was provided, so we stocked up on fruit juice, etc. There was no kettle, just a filter coffee maker, filters were provided. Take your own tea bags! Probably wouldn't stay there again as we fancied a night-cap so would choose a hotel with a bar next time, but a good value hotel and in the heart of the action.

title: “Location is tops. Get the panoramic suite for unbelievable views.”
text: This is the third time I've stayed in the panoramic suite. It's amazing. We watched the new years eve fireworks from our windows in our warm room with champagne and in our pjs. The staff here is friendly, young and beautiful. We ate breakfast at Mijita in e Ferry Bldg and rode the trolley to the Wharf. Don't understand why people gravitate to U ion Square when they can have this! The Fresh amenities are a favorite, as well as the soaking tub with a view of the bridge and water as are the two headed shower. Very nice. This is becoming our new year tradition when we are in town.

title: “AWESOME HOTEL!!!”
text: I was quite surprised with my stay at the Comfort Suites! From the moment I walked throught the door, I was greatly by 2 very friendly staff members. We were looking to hang out that night and was given Hot Spots where we could go. The room itself was nice, cozy and very clean. The TV was a plasma and very nice. The cable sucked but we were hardly in the room. It was very quiet while we were there and 2 soccer teams were in the building. I can't forget about the free breakfast. There was any meat but it beats having to pay for breakfast. I would definitley stay here again.

title: “Kitchy & Cool”
text: We grabbed a single night paid room here prior to staying two nights at the Fairmont Olympic for our 10th Anniversary. It was nice, and had an edge to it that wasn't trying too hard. The rooms were relatively good size, but for an older property, some things are understood like smaller bathrooms, window units for AC, etc. For the money though, the location was really good, very close to the good shopping, and we liked the overall ambiance. The bar was hopping after hours as well...

title: “Beautiful Hotel, Great Stay”
text:
A beautiful hotel, friendly staff, great location. Rooms were a little small, but the bed was enormous - we nearly needed a step ladder to climb in. The food from the restaurant was excellent, and the lobby was just gorgeous.
The only "upset" that we had from the hotel was that when we arrived - after 30 hours of travelling, and we presented our travel voucher issued to us via our travel agent, we were told that our reservation had been cancelled. I'm not sure what the mix up was exactly, central reservations for the hotel had cancelled it, but our voucher had been issued 5 days after it was supposedly cancelled. The guy on reception was great though, and they honoured our voucher and put us up without too much of a fuss at all. 
All in all, we were really pleased with this hotel. It's in a great location, without being in the thick of all the action.

title: “Worst front desk staff ever”
text: The location is perfect and the hotel is cute, but the girls at the front desk were the RUDEST snots I've ever encountered. No idea what their problem was, this was a Holiday Inn EXPRESS, not the Trump Tower. There was no soap in the room to even wash my hands and horrific cob webs on the ceilings. The snobby front desk manager and her equally snobby employees should be fired. I travel often and I will never ever stay here again. I would be embarrassed to reccommend this place to any of my family or friends because the stuck up snobs were that bad.

title: “Michael Baisden Halloween Party”
text:
I really enjoyed my stay at the Blake. I had read so many bad reviews I was skeptical. The room was nice and I loved the lobby. I'm not sure about hotel service because I didn't need anything or room service. As far as the bathroom, it is a little small, but I think the half glass shower door is chic and The Baisden Party was awesome.... looking forward to next year. 
My only complaint is that the it was hot in the lobby on my floor waiting for the elevator and extremely cold in the ballroom areas leading to the parking deck. (not where the party was) Hats off to the Blake.....

title: “Democratic Convention stay”
text: Came to Charlotte in connection with the DNC. Some NBC-TV on air personnel and staff were here too, along with foreign media. Hotel suite was more than I really needed, since I don't cook. My suite and the hotel in general looked clean. Breakfast was excellent. Front desk people gave me rides to Woodlawn blue-line rail station each morning to catch train to Uptown. Staff was friendly. No complaints, other than the lack of shops and restaurants within walking distance, but this is not a fault of the hotel. Would be glad to stay here again.

title: “Worst Experience In Los Angeles Ever No Sleep Possible”
text: The W Westwood can not be compared to the other W sister hotels. The mysterious white stains on the furniture were bad enough let alone the rotten dehydrated vegeatbles left on the shelves of the bar in my room. I paid $28.00 for parking to have my car parked mysteriously off site when they were hosting one of their numerous events. I was told they would need at least a 45 minute warning to retrieve my vehicle. I was kept awake for three nights straight from the screaming, whooping, and cheering coming from the bar & lobby lounge. When I complained to the manager on duty, they asked me what they could do. Their suggestion was a pair of earplugs????? Really nice. They said that they were trying to draw the fine line of being a business hotel that hosted events and that they did not realize the event would be so large. The music from the bar continued to escalate until the wee hours. I replied that maybe they should focus on some soundproofing for the hotel. When we finally did get to sleep at 3 a.m. we were woken up again by security calling my room to ask me where the party was at in the hotel. I replied it was in the lobby and how insightful they were. I checked out early the next morning. Word of warning stay clear of this hotel. the rooms, view, food, service, amenities, are all horrible.

title: “Nice place to stay in LA”
text: We were in LA for a Bar Mitzvah and stayed at the Angeleno and really enjoyed the hotel and staff. The room was large and comfortable, the lobby was nicely appointed, the restaurant was convenient and served tasty food but Joseph at the front desk was a stand out! He was very helpful especially because we didn't know the area and his suggestions and directions were spot on! He was also very nice to my mom which can go a long way!

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: This is the best of old and new. So quaint yet fully updated. I love how it's located in the heart of downtown Indianapolis. Close to convention center and lots of restaurants. If you like the nightlife, you are in the right area. But if you are working long hours at a convention and the thing you crave most is sleep....no worries here either. Their beds are comfy and if you need anything, the staff is quick and friendly. Breakfast and dinners are good, nothing extraordinary but I'm a foodie and like more quality choices. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Lovely, if a bit noisy”
text:
We stayed one night, over a Saturday. Our room was on the 3rd floor, overlooking the pool/spa area. The room was sparkling clean, decorated nicely and had a very comfortable bed - everything appeared to be updated and quite new. We enjoyed the grounds, surrounding area and the great views from our balcony. Being over the pool/courtyard area was a bit noisy, but not unexpected. The airport noise was louder than we had anticipated, but OK. We felt very safe taking a walk in the area in the evening.
On Sunday morning, there were no seats available at the seat-yourself breakfast buffet ($10.50 ea), so we opted to eat elsewhere.
A very nice place to stay.

title: “Great location, clean hotel, helpful restaurant and theatre concierge!”
text:
I travelled to NYC and stayed at this hotel in November 2010, over Thanksgiving weekend. The room was a decent size for Manhattan hotels, the staff was great, the location was amazing, and I would definitely stay here again.
My only complaints - not enough towels in the room and it took housekeeping a while to bring extra ones up; there was also very little counter space in the bathroom.

title: “beautiful hotel”
text:
Great place to stay. The staff was excellent and the location is perfect for downtown
activities. You can't expect anything more in a fitness room then this hotel offers. The view is unbeatable. We highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Nice Boutique Hotel”
text: The Night Hotel is located in the heart of all attractions. The standard room is quite small but comfortable. Perfect for a couple that just want to have a room to sleep in. As soon as i got there i was greeted by a gentlemen by the name of Robert. He was very helpful kid. I've never been to New York so i was asking him A lot of questions and he seemed to answer all my questions with out feeling like i was boring him. he was very out going and helpful. The staff was definitely helpful. The hotel is nice and quite. I liked the area and there's plenty of shops just feet away. I definitely recommend staying. The only bad experience i had was when i called room service for an ice bucket and the lady downstairs told me she was going to bring it and it took forever so I called back 30 minutes after and Robert answered the phone and I told him that my ice bucket never came and he brought it with in 5 minutes. I live in Las vegas so i'm use to great service. besides that everything was good. the staff is definitely helpful.

title: “Hollywood. Better than expected.”
text: On our travels through California most people told us to avoid LA and especially Hollywood but we loved it. It was the same with the hotel. Great location with great rooms. We got a standard King room which was large and spacious on the top floor with views over LA and the Hollywood sign. Id like to know how the suites look. The staff were overall good and as you would expect. The breakfast was good and plenty of time to get to it. Only things to watch for is that the higher floors require you to hunt down a different elevator which is kinda annoying. Watch the valet as well. Park the car yourself. All the spots are within a few steps of the elevator. The valet will literally move your car 20yards.

title: “Great experience!”
text: Would gladly stay there again. Nice staff, good overall experience.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: This is the second time I have stayed in this hotel and I love it. The location is second to none. Restaurants, bars and shopping are all within walking distance. The hotel itself is an updated Springhill (the new style) and is very comfortable. The staff was great. I will be staying here again on my next trip to Chicago.

title: “Tiny room - poor wifi”
text:
Have stayed in several hotels in this immediate area over the last few years. This one was oikay, but OUR ROOM WAS REALLY TINY plus the wifi was a VERY poor signal. Had a lot of trouble getting connected & staying connected. Finally got them to re-boot their routers, but still VERY poor signal.
Breakfast was pretty good: Texas-shaped waffles, bagels, toast, cereal, plenty of good coffee.
Front desk staff personable and caring. Ready to fulfill requests in a prompt and courteous manner. 
Everything clean - housekeeping staff friendly.

title: “Great room with a view”
text:
We booked a sky view room for a weekend trip to NYC. I would say the room was average size for NYC, and the view from the 35th floor was great. Decoration and cleanliness were top notch. The only criticism I can think of is that there is no mirror in the room itself, only in the bathroom. I didn't really notice, but my wife and her female friends who stopped by all did.
The location was great for us. Close enough to Times Square, but not right in it, so it was quieter and less bright. Normally I don't eat at hotel restaurant's but I made an exception for Ca Va Brasserie by Todd English as I really wanted to try it. There are hundreds of excellent places to eat in New York, but I was not disappointed in the slightest that we ate here. Easily on par with the other places we dined that weekend. If we were in town longer I definitely would have gone back.

title: “Awesome Staff! More Awesome rooms!”
text:
I found this hotel on my company's travel website. They had just opened and I stay at numerous Holiday Inn Express hotels around the country. This one by far has the best rooms for a great price! The rooms are all decked out in a kind of Feng Shai style, as well as the lobby. 
The staff is excellent! I visit Dallas sporadically but I guess enough that just about everyone that has worked the front desk knows me by name. 
I had just made platinum status about a week before my last visit there and it was already updated on their computers. I was recognized as a platinum member and was given a complimentary upgrade to a suite! Cool! 
Funny thing, I visited the Holiday Inn in Buena Park California the very next week. No recognition of being platinum, no upgrade, on my check in document, they still had my PC as Gold. When I asked if that could be changed, I was told in a somewhat rude fashion, " You have to change that online." When I was walking away, the person rudely gave me a complimentary bag of a bottle of water and a granola bar. Thanks. On my profile, it states King bed. So did my reservation. When I got to the room, it was a double. That's it! Won't be staying there any longer. Too bad for them. I am a loyal customer and was staying one week per month at that hotel for close to a year! I did talk to the manager and received an upgrade but too late. 
I got off track there. Anyway, this hotel in Dallas is a very nice hotel. If you like Holiday Inn Express Hotels and are looking for one in the Dallas area, this IS your hotel.

title: “Great Property, Great Value”
text: Stayed here for one night in mid-July 2011 with my brother. This is a relatively new property. It's a bit hidden on a back street off the highway, but worth the effort to find. The lobby is modern yet warm. Check-in was a breeze, with professional, friendly staff. The room was a 2-room suite with 2 queen beds. Full kitchen. Pull-out sofa. Flat screen TV's in both rooms. Internet connection - no problem. Did not use the work-out room or pool - but took a look at both and they looked new and clean. Slept in and didn't make breakfast -- but the staffer still offered me fresh coffee w/ fixins. The room was well decorated and very clean. The bathroom area was terrific -- a separate, well-lit marble vanity with sink. Shower and toilet in separate room. Again, everything new and clean. Large, comfortable beds with a rarity for a hotel in this class -- comfortable pillows! This is a great property for business travelers and families. Highly recommend it.

title: “Not bad, had better”
text:
Having travelled all over Amercia, staying in San Fransicso, Los Angeles, Las Vegas and lastly New York. I have to say this was my least favoured hotel. Had dinner in the hotel on the first night, it was terrible and shockingly overpriced.
Room was ok, nice and clean. Good location for all there is to see and do in New York. I wouldn't recommend this hotel to a friend - it's way too pricey for what you actually get.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text:
My husband, mother and I stayed at this property for my daughter's UCLA law school graduation. We had requested an early check in and were given our rooms at an even earlier time than requested. The staff was friendly, attentive and helpful. As Starwood members we were given an upgrade on one of our rooms to a beautilful, large suite, which was perfect for our needs as we were able to have a little pre-graduation celebration.
The hotel is situated extremely close to the UCLA campus, and it made it easy to get to the ceremony. My only complaint would be that their complimentary car service, which delivered us to the campus, stopped running at 5:00 and we had to call a cab to get back to the hotel, but that was a minor inconvenience. All in all the hotel was perfect for our needs and made a memorable and exciting day even better.

title: “Great experience”
text: This one one of the most pleasant experiences I have had staying in the San Diego area... Centrally located and easy access to and from the freeways and it's only 5-10 minutes to the beach... Management and staff were very friendly and accommodating as well. I will definitely stay here again and recommend this property to my friends and family when they travel to the San Diego area.

title: “A simple yet sophisticated hotel”
text:
We stayed here for three nights in May. We stayed in a studio suite which was modern and gorgeous. Panoramic views of the park and some of the city. I read some of the reviews that stated the hotel is still not ready for guests. I completely disagree. The hotel is sleek and stylish and very,very friendly. Maybe the service is not slick, but I really appreciate and prefer warmth over perfection. 
The hotel is immaculate, and the location perfect for shopping, dining, and riding the Metro. Also the hop on and off bus stops within one block of the Hotel.
I would avoid the restaurant except for an amazing breakfast. The best eggs benedict I have ever had.
The bar is amazing, modern,sexy yet cozy all at the same time.

title: “Great Location, Bad Service”
text: The rooms were tiny, the location was GREAT. My complaint was that the service staff monopolized the 1 elevator on the property. the elevator was never available. I walked 7 flights to my room each time because the service staff and their carts were always in the elevators. My room was not refreshed on second day. Had hard time to get extra coffee packets. Bed not made, trash not emptied. Towels sparingly replenished. The TV took 5 minutes to warm up before the scrolling lines went away. The TV is HD but the programming was NOT, so the picture image on the TV was not of quality. The breakfast area was very tiny. I would suggest getting to breakfast before 9 so as to find a table to sit and enjoy breakfast. My overall impression was of being cramped into a sardine can.

title: “While I loved the 80s, I don't prefer beds from that decade.”
text:
Don't they say to always give at least 2 positives before giving criticism? Well, here are the positives: (1) great location for a 1-night airport hotel, and (2) you must try the broiled crab cake sandwich. I have satisfied the minimum number of positives, right?
The beds are a disaster. I coudln't sleep because the sheet was all discombobulated and the frame was boxy and creaky. I felt like looking for the sign that read "1 million served" on the mattress. Is there anything worse than not being able to sleep in an airport hotel? Add jet lag and loud plumbing and you get the right imagery.
Lots of better options...unless you hear that its been renovated, stay away.

title: “Excellent Value at a Venerable Private Club”
text: I used my reciprocal club arrangement to stay at the University Club prior to our trip to Napa valley. Located on Nob Hill across the street from the Fairmont Hotel, the club is nicely furnished with a beautiful library and outside balcony overlooking the bay. Although there are only about 20 rooms, it was a thrill to stay in this quiet, tastefully decorated gem - don't miss it!

title: “Always love Kimpton hotels!”
text: All experiences I've had at Kimpton hotels have been excellent, and the Palomar in LA is no exception. We recently stayed here while in town for a friend's wedding. The staff here is incredibly friendly and helpful, absolutely top-notch customer service. The rooms are stunning, clean, and comfortable, and we had a good view to boot. The wine hour was fun with friends, and we also enjoyed a brunch catered by the hotel which was delish. I would definitely stay here again, or any Kimpton hotel for that matter!

title: “A great place to stay in Chelsea New York”
text: We were looking for a boutique hotel in a convienent location and as this was our first trip to New York, helpful staff. We were travelling with my sister, daughter and her daughter and we had a truely amazing holiday. The location is close to the subway, the Chelsea Market, and the fantastic Highline Park. There are lots of great restaurants close by and the staff gave us some fabulous recommendations. The rooms are small but very clean and the movie posters add a lovely unique feel. We looked forward to the great breakfast every morning which got us started for the day. The common areas are a another great feature at the CPI. The staff are truely amazing and are SO helpful and knowlegable and nothing was too much trouble. We stayed for 8 days and when we arrived back each evening after a day of sightingseeing and exploring, we felt like we were arriving home. We will definately be back !

title: “Overnight cruise stay”
text:
Stayed at the Crowne prior to my cruise on the Princess. The staff was very helpful, the special menu pricing at their restaurant was very reasonable. Of course the free shuttle to the port was great. The rooms were quite spacious. 
A definite place to stay if you are planning a cruise out of LA.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We stayed for two nights. When checking in, we found out we were upgraded to a corner room that had an extra seating area. It was great! We were in the Tower Building. The bathroom was VERY small, but that was no big deal. We had no problem with getting from one building to the other. I had read that people found it very confusing. Not at all. Matt, brought our luggage to our room. He was very friendly and offered information about the hotel and the downtown. We also had access to the Club Lounge, which was excellent. Breakfast was very good, a choice of fresh fruit, cereals, muffins, bagels, pastries, yogurt, granola, coffee, tea and juice. There was granola bars, candies, water, soda and coffee available all day, hors d'oeuvres in the evening, and cookies at night. All with a great view from the 22nd floor. All the attendents in the lounge were great. The pool was nice. The lounge chairs could use a cleaning. The cushions were stained. The work out room was good, it had a good selection of machines. All in all we had a great experience. From valet parking, to check in and out, everyone was always friendly, said hello and had a smile!

title: “No frills but good”
text:
Location quite good, walking distance Times Square and Grand Central Station. Very small room but it was clean and really quiet with good heat or AC. Bonus that the bed was really comfortable. Staff helpful. 
We didn't have the breakfast as preferred the Westway diner round the corner for a typical US feast (come out of Hotel, turn right, turn left at junction). 
Only concern was no locking device on door at night. Only gripe was slow and inadequate lift.

title: “Very nice”
text:
The hotel seemed fairly posh. Champagne at check-in, nice pool, Bentley parked outside. They even seemed to be hosting a prom (or similar event). The rooms were nice and comfortable and it was very easy to sleep in when we got in at 4am and needed to sleep well into the morning. 
Free parking, decent fitness center, and a shuttle to take you anywhere nearby. We certainly enjoyed our stay and had no bad experiences.

title: “Great Location- Budget Hotel”
text: This hotel has an excellent location with just a 2 minute walk to Grand Central, Lovely bistros and diners within a minutes walk and at least 4 Starbucks coffee houses within 2minute walk! The hotel itself is in desperate need of renovation- which I believe they have already started- working from the top down. My parents had a room on the 10th floor and the decor and bathroom was much more pleasant than ours. We were on the 4th floor and unfortunately were not so happy with our room. There were stains on the carpet; a major draught coming in through the window (although the heating did keep the room warm enough) and the bathroom had a leak from the toilet and a funny smell. Our bathroom was also not cleaned as well as I would have hoped. However, the sheets and towels were changed everyday. There were a lot of teenagers hanging around which made the place feel almost like a youth hostel- 2 school trips were there at the time. We were also put on a smoking floor and had smoke coming under our door. If you are going to stay here, you should also be aware that the peep holes in the doors had been taken out so that people could see straight into the rooms- we had to put a sock over the door to cover it!! Having said all of this, the hotel staff were friendly enough and the hotel is very cheap so is good for budget travellers ( you get what you pay for!) The pershing Cafe opposite Grand Central do great pancakes for breakfast and the deli opposite it has a fantastic choice of fresh salads for lunch. We had a fantastic time in New York but we will definitely pay a little more for the hotel next time and make sure we get a slightly more comfortable room.

title: “Convenience”
text:
If you are visiting to see the Mall, choose this hotel for your convenience, not to mention great customer service and beautiful property.
1) Hotel was modern, updated, very clean and conveniently located. Customer service was excellent. They greet you with a smile. They even gave me a map for the mall and subway stations that I needed but wasn't expecting from them. OUTSTANDING! Saved me a lot of time from going online.
2) Hotel is literally 2 blocks away from the Mall and only around the corner from subway station entrance/exit (Federal Center). So, that means you can leave your car in the garage and start walking the mall in two minutes.
