The hotel's closest point of interest is the Smithsonian American Indian Museum (very close to the Capitol). You can work your way to the other end of the Mall and when you're done, you can hop onto the subway for $2.20 per person and end up a block away from your hotel. Also, upon check out, your car can stay in the garage until 5:00 PM with no extra charge. After that, you can move your car onto the streets for free or meter parking. That is still a lot of time and savings. Heads-up: They do charge $30 per day for parking in their garage but you probably pay more at other garages for all day parking. To me, it was worth it. 
All in all, Holiday Inn definitely did a great job with remodeling and retraining their staff. Excellent job HI people! I highly recommend this hotel and plan to stay here again next time I visit DC

title: “Absolutely Fabulous!”
text:
This is our second trip here at the hotel and they stayed true to their fine service. The hotel is so close to Union Square shopping and Macy's. The front desk staff whisked us through the HH members area efficiently and with a great upgrade. The balcony has a great view and its' nice for morning coffee. The room was very clean and the housekeeping staff were very friendly and helpful. The security staff were present and visible but not annoying, we felt very safe. I love the sense of pampering you get when you get to your room, I want that comforter!! 
The only thing we missed was the executive lounge on the top floor...please bring it back! Thanks for a great time, we'll be back!

title: “Great location but small rooms”
text: Stayed here several times this year for business. Location is great - it's within walking distance (nice leisurely 2 miles) from Federal Triangle metro stop. Or, during inclement weather only a few blocks from Foggy Bottom metro stop. Great restaurants nearby for dinner. Hotel staff is friendly and helpful but not intrusive. Concierge had wonderful suggestions for meals. Taxis easy to obtain. I enjoy the Aveda products in the bathrooms. Only problem is the size of the rooms. Unless you are located in the corner rooms, beds are small and space is tight. This would be a problem if family joined me but for business purposes it's perfect.

title: “Decent and good location.”
text: Hotel was close to Rittenhouse Square and the trolley line. Room was nice and large, and staff was efficient. Be careful when asking for recommendations on where to eat. We were sent to a "moderate restaurant" which cost an average of $25/plate. It was tasty, but more upscale than what we were looking for. The bed wasn't very comfortable, but being pregnant might have biased me. I would say your average hotel, with the only downside being that there were some really drunk college kids in the elevator, but we couldn't hear them while in our room.

title: “" Extremely relaxing"”
text: Trying to escape a busy work schedule and only a few days to do so, I decided to visit San Diego. My visit to The Dana on Mission Bay was extremely relaxing. I was greeted by Ciara C. She was friendly and very helpful. She made sure I knew excatly where my room was and were I was to catch the shuttle to Sea world. This friendlyness continued with the shuttle drivers and even the grounds people. My rooms was so comfortable , and clean. I felt relaxed and most importantly safe . I plan on returning here again, and again. One of the best Hotels I have stayed in.

title: “Good Morning. It's going to be a beautiful day. No storms.”
text: The morning of the day we arrived there were storms in Chicago. The next morning when I got off the elevator the bell man greeted me with the forecast and a cheerful Good Morning. We swam in the pool and as we were getting out the life guard got up and brought us towels before we could reach out seats. We dined at Tribute (the hotel's restaurant) starting our day off great with gourmet breakfasts. Even the toast was remarkable! I went to the desk to ask about a bus schedule as we were on a budget. There wasn't one available, but the desk person gave me walking directions. Then offered the Shuttle to the museum. "I'll get my friends." When we arrived back to the desk I was sure the shuttle would have left. The desk man was out in the garage holding the shuttle. We were very impressed. We are already planning a trip back. I think I am more excited about staying at The Essex again than seeing Chicago.

title: “So Cal Bombers Sept 14-17 2012”
text: The overall stay @ the Sheraton Crescent was amazing. Jocelin Meesenburg was an amazing planner and followed through on every detail for us. Her communication is unmatched! Jocelin's willingness to help however possible is a huge asset for your property. Nick and Meagen at the front desk are exceptional as well. Jenna in the bar/lounge is a pleasure too. The breakfast was a bit down compared to the year before, not as much to choose from and I would like to suggest breakfast be served or available until at least 10am. Traveling with 16-18 year old boys playing baseball who have late games the night before or have later games in the afternoon it's tough having to wake them up early just to go eat breakfast. I know it's a small detail but it just seemed (9am) early to be wrapping breakfast up. Service this past weekend in the breakfast area was below par compared to the rest of the staff and in no way reflects how truly great I know this property is. Front desk staff are all great! Housekeeping staff are top notch! The guys working the bell desk are very helpful and informative. For many years I worked in the service industry in a Regional Manager role for a high level customer service based company (maybe you have heard of it, Nordstrom? LOL) and make many comparisons when I travel and evaluate properties and employees. I want to thank Jocelin for her dedication and passion in making the So Cal Bombers baseball club (upperclass teams) stay an amazing experience.We will always come back. Scott Reed 714-473-8788

title: “Stay in the city as if you live in the city!”
text:
My wife and I stayed here two times in February and March for two and four nights. The Surrey is a great hotel, featuring French boutique hotel style and comfort. Since it is in the Upper East Side, you will feel like a real New Yorker and less like a tourist. The location is pretty good, but if you are really into sightseeing you may want to consider something more downtown.
Great about this hotel are the big rooms, the incredibly comfy bed, the powerful shower, the many windows and the service. The staff are very attentive! We had some drinks downstairs in the Pleiades bar which were also really good! This is an absolutely recommendable hotel and a place we will return the next time we are in the City.
The hotel does have some areas for improvement, though: the windows are outdated, meaning that they will let in noise and air freely. These should really be changed. The TV remote is extremely complicated, and while the TV offers a lot of selection, the remote is just a pain. Finally, the breakfast buffet at Boulud is really thin, offering only a minimum selection. But the quality of the food is great, which clearly makes up for the lack of offering!
All in all, an excellent choice for the European-minded traveller looking for a spacious room in a great part of NYC.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
I stayed here for two nights while in Baltimore for work. I am a fan of the Kimpton brand, so I was pleased to learn that Kimpton had a hotel in Baltimore. The hotel is located in the old rail road building, so there is a lot of history, character and charm. 
The location was right downtown. Within walking distance to Lexington market, the theatre, the waterfront and many shops and restaurants. 
The rooms were clean and well appointed. Also, they were very modern. 
The breakfast was also good. 
I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone staying in Baltimore.

title: “Very Nice Garden Inn”
text: I was very impressed. This hotel is very clean and my room was in great shape. The staff were very helpful and friendly. This hotel may not be considered a "full service" hotel, but it certainly has a "full service" attitude. I would stay here again without hesitation.

title: “Excellent Park and Fly program and great room”
text:
We took advantage of their reverse Park and Fly program to park at the hotel, take the shuttle to the airport, and then stay at the hotel when we returned to Denver after a late night flight. This program has worked very well for us in the past at other hotels. We were very pleasantly surprised by the quality of the room at the Fairfield. This was by far the best hotel we have stayed in at the Denver airport. The room was very comfortable and quiet. The bed was spacious and we had a great sleep after a long day of flying. The room had a work area, so would be ideal for a longer work-related stay. 
We would strongly recommend this place for others who need to park and then have a good place to stay either before or after a trip. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “What a letdown!”
text:
Wow, where to start? 
I originally tried to book the InterContinental for a weekend stay but was told that they were sold out on Saturday. I made a reservation for Friday night and got a reservation elsewhere for Saturday. Upon arriving (after dragging our luggage in ourselves with no one there to open the doors) I was told that the room had been booked for Friday and Saturday. Figuring I would stay at the InterContinental both nights, I called the other hotel and cancelled my reservation for Saturday night, incurring cancellation fees. I had booked a King Junior Suite but was now told that they didn't have one available. But they were sure I would like the room they had. Exhausted I took the key. The room was nice, but standard. I booked the King Junior Suite for the floor to ceiling windows which my room did not have.
When we got to the room we ordered a rollaway bed, which arrived promptly. However, the phone call at 12:15a.m. to ask us if we had received the bed was not appreciated. 
We returned to the room Saturday afternoon and were surprised to see that it had not been cleaned. We ordered room service and then the maid knocked on the door and asked us when we were going to check out. When I told her Sunday morning, she asked me to call the front desk. They told me they had no record of us staying Saturday night and by the way, they were sold out completely and we would need to check out. I explained that I had been told at check-in that the reservation was for Friday and Saturday, explained that I had cancelled my other room and had no where to go! (San Francisco marathon that weekend, hotels booked!) The manager agreed to let us stay after several phone calls, but meanwhile room service had put our order on hold! It took more calls to get our order and our refrigerator unlocked. Then as we finally sat down to eat, the phone rang yet again, the front desk was asking me to come down and give them a credit card because apparently they closed out our room tab. 
In addition to all of the above the pool and jacuzzi were closed during our stay. We were traveling with a child and chose the InterContinental because we knew she would love that pool!
I travel quite a bit and I've never seen staff confusion like this. Our stay was not enjoyable and I was very disappointed.

title: “Tower 23 is the place to stay in PB!”
text: My wife and I stayed at Tower 23 over the 4th of July and the stay was fantastic; the room, the location and staff exceeded our expectations. The rooms are modern and spacious (see photos) and the property is clearly the nicest and newest addition to Pacific Beach. We had dinner in Jordan (the hotel's only restaurant) and the food and service was enjoyable; glass partitions separating the diners from the boardwalk provided terrific, unobstructed views of the Pacific Ocean and the activity. The hotel's atmosphere is lively and relaxed, encrusted with a hip decor and eclectic clientèle. The hotel is not for those looking to save a few $$ as the rooms (+/-$400) and dining are costly, but the experience will yield a nice dividend on your investment. The noise from the boardwalk can be a little loud, but the hotel has installed large, double-paned, glass, sliding doors that filter out the noise. Overall, great place-I would highly recommend Tower 23.

title: “Average Stay...Clean rooms but really, really need upgrading:(”
text: Front Desk Staff was nice..building looks nice on exterior. Breakfast was average nothing special. The room and bathroom was clean; however, the carpet and furniture (esp the sleep sofa) looked very worn out and had a dirty appeal to it. In my opinion, the rooms in this facility really need upgrading. I have stayed in other comfort suites in Charlotte and the standard in this one compared to the others were not met and I was very disappointed. With that being said, I probably would not stay in this particular one again.

title: “Good Rooms, Good Conference Location, A/C Options Need Work”
text: I was a gues at the hotel from June 26-28, 2012. This was a work trip for a conferenc, and the hotel was extremely busy hosting 4 conferences. The entire hotel is nice and I have nothing but compliments regarding the friendliness and attitude of the staff. Room service is extremely slow when they are this busy. Each room service meal that was not pre-ordered the night before took 1 hour to deliver. Pre-ordered meals took an extra 30 minutes. The A/C is difficult to control so you are either very cold or very hot. The conference floors are large and moving from one ballroom to another requires some work. Self parking is not recommended at this hotel as it takes a long walk to get to the parking garage, and if you carry in bags you may have to carry them up a short flight of stairs. Valet parking is best. The hotel is located in a downtown area. The immediate area is nice with a few eating choices. Once you go outside the immediate area things get a little dangerous if you don't have a car. The hotel is located 25 minutes from the airport.

title: “Quirky and Fun, Good Restaurant, but Minor Concerns”
text: This is a fun property - really interesting decor, generally clean and quiet, and staff friendly and helpful. And the restuarant that serves it (forget name) is really great for reasonable prices. Couple of complaints -- hotel near Tenderloin -- I was surprised by how many homeless, wondering people there were nearby, although in all fairness, they are everywhere in San Fran, including nearby Union Square. Also, I get sense that management doesn't educate or communicate w/ employees carefully. For instance, maid tried to clean my room day I was leaving before check out -- made no sense. And front desk told me restaurant was open all day, but when I tried to get breakfast one day at 10:40 am, I was told it was closed (they gave me a $25 credit to make up for the confusion). Finally, the room I was in was small -- I was by myself, so it was ok, but I wouldn't want a couple to try and stay in the room I was in -- they'd barely fit their suitcases! I paid $287/night before tax, so who knows how much you need to spend for a larger room. One final complaint -- I went to gym to work out on Friday, and both treadmills were broken. They still hadn't been fixed by Sunday late afternoon. I know most people wouldn't see this as a big deal, and I'm sure it is hard to get service on the weekend, but those of you who are runners know that going a couple of days w/o a treadmill is really annoying, esp. given price of room.

title: “Convenient for Orioles Games”
text:
The Hilton Baltimore is very convenient if you plan on going to a game, literally walk across the street and you're at the gate. Due to a few conventions in the hotel the check in line was long (prob about 20 minutes) but it appeared they were moving as quickly as they could and a good portion of the holdup was from tired and weary travelers. 
The room we were in was impeccably clean. As others have posted they were stingy on the towels but that would not stop me from coming back. The food at the lobby bar was average but good in a pinch. If attending a game head across the street to Pickles, food and drink are good and reasonably priced. 
The facility has a great fitness center which overlooks Camden Yards, the view can't be beat. The equipment seemed to be maintained well and the room was clean.
The hotel was a short walk to the Inner Harbor, we walked there a few times during the day and late at night and felt safe at either time. 
Overall if returning to Baltimore we would stay here again if we had plans on seeing a ballgame since the location can't be beat.

title: “Perfect!”
text: We stayed here for the beginning of our 35th anniversary trip to Cape Cod and it was perfect. I dont think we ever slept better in a hotel (which is very important). The beds were so comfortable and it was so quiet. We were on the top floor which were pure rooms ( air purifiers in rooms) and we had a corner room which was very large and lovely. Kieth & Tom the concierges were so helpful. If you want an old worldEuropean feel hotel this is it!

title: “Good location, but room was like a shoe box!”
text:
We stayed at Park 79 for 4 nights to explore the city of New York. The internet photos make one believe the place is a lot swankier than it actually is. Our bedroom and bathroom were tiny. The bedroom was certainly in need of a touch of paint. 
The hotel is in a good location, extremely close to Central Park and the National History Museum. Other than location this hotel is poor value for money: the rooms are pokey, one particular member of staff was extremely rude towards us and coffee is served in cheap styrofoam cups.

title: “Elegant, Comfortable, Excellent Staff, Wonderful Stay”
text:
It is always important to do research about a hotel before you stay there. 
We (my husband, daughter and I) just spent a week at the Omni San Francisco Hotel. Having never been to SF, I wanted to stay in a nice luxury hotel with knowledgeable staff and we were not disappointed. The Hotel is located in the Financial District a short distance from the more chaotic tourist areas but easily accessible to world class shopping, eating, Fishermans Wharf , Chinatown and other scenic areas by walking, cable car, taxi, bus or rail. 
From the doorman, check in staff, bellman, concierge, housekeeping and restaurant, everyone warmly greeted us upon coming and going and always thanked us for staying with them. They went out of their way to be helpful with really good attitudes. 
We joined the select guest program for free (on their website) and this entitled us to FREE In-Room Internet Service, coffee/beverages of choice every morning, with a choice of 1 of 4 newspapers along with delivery of ice and turn down service in the evening. 
Upon making the reservation I mentioned that we were celebrating a birthday and when we arrived in our room, there was a card, birthday desert and bottle of chilled champagne waiting. We were in a regular room but I did request the top floor away from the elevator and got exactly what I asked for. 
The room was very clean - something I'm very picky about, beds were extremely comfortable and housekeeping service replaced our towels and promptly cleaned our room and bathroom every day when we left to go sightseeing. 
A concierge was usually available to make dinner reservations or tour arrangements, transportation and help with directions, areas to avoid, etc. They were always busy but always polite and willing to help. 
We ordered room service one evening and also ate in the hotel lounge. Delicious food and again great service. Bob's Chophouse, the main restaurant in the Hotel was very pricey so we chose to eat at more moderately priced meals in the different city districts. 
OTHER: Be prepared to tip. No pool. Nice fitness room. Good conference hotel. Family friendly. Parking is $48 per night, but if you have to have a car, there are a few less expensive garages nearby to park. No gift shop in the hotel but there is a little store next door you can buy drinks or get a snack, batteries, etc. Many of the little coffee shops are closed on the weekend in the financial district.

title: “A fantastic stay”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Doubletree suites Time square for our annual mother's day trip. Everything about this hotel was excellent. The service at check in was quick and easy. The cookies were to die for. The room was a two room suite. It was nicer than I had expected. The room was clean, the bed was excellent to sleep in and the shower had excellent water pressure and tempature control. The location was fantastic, right on time square. There a broadway theatre next door playing West Side Story. There loads of restraunts with in a couple of blocks and the subway entrance is right next door too. I would recommend this hotel to anyone I know who headed to NYC. My wife and I will stay there again next time we go to NYC.

title: “Historical and beautiful, but a little stuck up.”
text:
My husband and I spent time at the Fairmont, and found it to be absolutely gorgeous. The only problem I had was the walls, better yet, the adjoining doors between rooms were so thin that I could hear the phone conversations of the people next door. 
The staff was more than helpful, but they nickel and dime everything, wifi, gym, of course parking. But if you sign up for the Presidents Club membership online,(Free), then you are able to use the gym and wifi for free. Parking was $50 to park in their garage and that is with self park. You can park on the street if you are lucky enough to find a spot. BUT, the hotel is amazing and the restaurant and bar are fabulous. Overall, it was a great experience.

title: “nice stay”
text: a great place to stay if you are going to a convention which I was, very clean and wellkept rooms. The flat screen t.v. was a plus, as was the bathroom.Location was the only problem with the hotel. Costly breakfast ($23.00) we found a deli across the street which was more reasonable. Location was far away from everything but within walking distance.They have a shuttle that eill bring you to Quincy market or the North end.Very friendly female driver and front desk people.The doorman were very helpful.Would stay again for a convention.

title: “Comfy stay in San Fran”
text: Hotels in San Fran are expensive so when I saw this hotel come up at a good price I grabbed it. Location is Fantastic, a few min was to union square and shops and restaurant surrounded the area. transportation is accessible with Bart station, cable car and bus stop around the corner. There are a lot of homeless in San Fran but streets were still safe we didn't have an issue walking around the area. Te hotel itself is quite old but renovated but rooms are well maintained. Room was noisy with restaurants nearby and street noise but I don't think you can avoid that in San Fran.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
I stayed here on business last year and this was an excellent hotel. The beds were comfortable, rooms were nicely decorated and clean. Most importantly, the rooms were quite – we were originally staying at another hotel in New York that had a disco on roof that turned out to be a nightmare and coming to this hotel was a relief after that. 
I had ordered internet service for my room and it did not work properly – but when I checked out I was reimbursed for this, so they did the right thing. If I were to come to New York, I would most likely stay here again.

title: “Outstanding service”
text: The Westin provided outstanding service the staff was extremely friendly and accommodating! The bellmen Amadou and Deenny was so kind and went out of their way to assist us with transportation and help with our bags.

title: “Good place for a business conference”
text: I stayed at the Holiday Inn Chicago - Mart Plaza for a week long conference for work. The hotel conference facilities are well-apportioned and accommodated our large and dynamic group very well. The rooms were basic, but offered all of the amenities needed to keep me happy and rested throughout the week.

title: “Good hotel, too far away from everything”
text:
I booked this through Hotwire, also 4* in the West Hollywood area. Iam a solo traveller and found this hotel to be too far away from everything. I like to be in an area which is a safe walking distance to main strip for restaurants etc. Although the Orlando had a few restaurants around it (within 10 minutes walk) I didn't feel safe walking back to the hotel after dark.
I found the rooms to be very good - huge rooms with a very comfortabel bed and I thought the bathroom was fine. Yes the lifts and the hallways are extremely dated however this didn't bother me as the room was not. 
Although small, the pool was lovely and I have to say the staff were great.
Although close to the beverly centre and not too far from the outdoor shopping centre (about 10-15 minutes) I was disappointed with the location and will next time stay somewhere closer to the Strip in true West Hollywood.

title: “Lived up to expectations.”
text:
On our way to see the US Grand Prix in Austin, we stayed in The Lancaster for one night, and thoroughly enjoyed the ambiance and helpful staff. Friendly greeting at reception and our room was comfortable and well equipped. 
We dined in the restaurant and had a great meal, with excellent service. The hotel is undergoing a refurbishment and hopefully will retain its character and charm. Living in the UK we might not be back in Houston anytime soon, but we would not choose to stay anywhere else when we are.

title: “Great hotel - would stay again”
text:
We stayed in the Mulberry hotel last week and were delighted with it. Our room had a great view over Columbus Park, two comfortable beds, and a spotless bathroom. We had tea making facilities and a fridge, so we could store our own food/drinks which gave us alot of flexibility.
We weren't expecting to get breakfast which was a nice surprise - it is served at the Mama's restaurant a few shops down the road from the hotel. The only criticism of this is that the menu was limited with no healthy options, unless you purchased the food yourself. Great for fries and an omelette, but no fruit/yoghurt etc. Not really a reflection on the hotel, but worth mentioning.
With regards to the location, it's fabulous for eating in Little Italy and Chinatown and is about 4 blocks from the subway where you can easily get uptown. If you're looking to have a holiday in Manhattan and want to spend most of your time up near 42nd street in Times Square, or around Central Park, Empire State or Rockafeller Centre, you might want to consider a hotel further uptown. However, we did all those sites from Hotel Mulberry and enjoyed them - it is just a little trek to get up there on the subway.

title: “Great stay in a cool new hotel”
text:
My family and I stayed at the ALOFT hotel in downtown Dallas last weekend. The owners did a great job converting an old warehouse building into a cool new hotel. The rooms were unique, due to the configuration of the original building and surprisingly - very quiet at night ( we were on the 5th floor).
The staff/service was great and we thoroughly enjoyed our stay - I would definitely recommend this place.

title: “Stayed twice and will be back”
text:
I first stayed at the Seafarers & International House in 2010 and again in July 2012. During my most recent visit I shared a room with my brother and we stayed for four days and three nights. The management recently renovated the lobby and now it has a more modern feel to it. Although the guest house does not offer any breakfast on site, there are several coffee and tea options in the lobby.
Disadvantages:
• Wi-Fi access only in the lobby and the mezzanine
• No housekeeping while guests occupy the room
Advantages:
• The guest house is clean, quiet, and safe
• Unbeatable location
• Student discount ($86 per night)
• Rooms with 2 separate beds available (twin size bed and a comfortable camp bed)
• Two computers with printers in the mezzanine
• Luggage room available
• Onsite chapel and services
• Room revenue goes towards supporting port ministry
Note that some rooms do not have private shower and bathroom. However, there are two showers and bathrooms on each floor for the guests to share.
One of the greatest advantages is the location! The guest house is located on E 15th street which is a short walking distance from Union Square. There is a variety of stores and restaurants in the area such as Walgreens, Whole Foods, TGI Friday's, Starbucks, and many more. There is also a regal movie theater nearby with tickets costing around $13 for children and adults. In addition, the Union Square Subway station is on lines L-N-Q-R-4-5-6 and the 1-2-14D+A bus lines are in close proximity.
I loved both of my stays and will definitely be back!

title: “Clean and a good value”
text:
Very clean and well kept property.
Good choice if you're looking for a place to stay on the East side of Houston.

title: “18" of closet space?? that stunned us more than the view!”
text:
Count us in among the minority of TripAdvisors who will not be returning to this Sofitel. 
Our suite on the top floor (29th story) was indeed well-insulated against noise, had a great view, and we appreciated the fact that the windows have both sheer and black-out draperies. The large, full marble bathroom is nicely fitted out with deep tub, separate, walk-in shower, toiletries that are not heavily perfumed -- and an orchid in a vase and a candle. Large, flat screen TV's in both the living room & bedroom with a Bose clock radio in the BR. And the 2 little bottles of Evian left at evening turn-down were a nice touch, even though a bit of chocolate would be nicer :-)
Willing to overlook the couple of smallish stains on the rug and the fact that the shower handle fell off and struck my foot; these things happen. But, the furnishings/layout -- apart from the bed -- were not that comfortable (some might find the bed too soft). Most surprising, the lone closet had a rod just 24" wide and part of that was rendered unusable by the closet's caddies for ironing board and iron, leaving less than 18" -- and thus relegating us to leaving our coats draped elsewhere and being able to hang only a few garments. 
There were shelves, but several of those were taken up by the folded bathrobes (no peg for those in the bathroom), a blanket but not the synthetic pillows promised by the in-room info booklet for those allergic to down & a wicker basket with the laundry bags tucked inside. The only drawer space were the 2 narrow ones in the bedside tables. Consequently, we had to leave most of our belongings packed in our luggage, which had to sit out as there was no place to stow our couple of standard carry-on pieces. From reading other reviews here that speak glowingly of the closet space, it appears that the rooms/suites are not configured alike; if you are not traveling solo, check out what's given you & ask if another room/suite is available if you too find yourselves facing hanging rod "real estate" costing ~$30/inch. 
The beds have no top sheet, but rather are covered with simply a luxurious down-filled duvet. Even if you're not squeamish about this -- and I'll assume they change the duvet cover between guests -- it can be uncomfortably warm. So, highly recommend that you ask housekeeping to make up the bed with a sheet & ordinary blanket before you retire.
Lastly, utterly indifferent service all-around... not that I expect, or want, to be fawned over, but geez, it would be nice to feel that you're not part of the furniture. In short, an oddly bland & even irritating hotel experience we're not eager to revisit.

title: “UGH!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: We got to our hotel at 9:30 PM and after a 16 hour drive we were glad we were home(for 5 days). We get there and loaded up our luggage on a cart and went to the front desk and asked where the elevator was... she smiled and said there was NO elevator.. Not good! O.k. so we went to our room and changed our floor so we could be put on the 1 st floor...No problem. Next day had to be at our daughters parade and the dinning room was not open..Fine...Not! Next day graduation and we had to be out and about early, we did have breakfast. I feel sorry for the lady in black that was serving us, she was busting her butt with no help, you could tell she is discusted with this place ( o.k. my observation) The toilet handle was so discusting it made me sick.. told my husband to check it out.. Second room was cleaner but those mats need to be changed and bleached how discusting to be standing in someone elses stuff... The only thing that kept us being o.k. at this place was Johnny the bartender, he busted his tush off not only making sure bar patrons were o.k. but was also doing room service and dinning area... I say give him a BIG raise for his hospitality and and all around GREAT service!! Johnny come to Colorado and your service will be greatly apprecaited... Thanks for your smile and hospitality you showed Steve and I!! I am going to put you in my scrapbook and remember the good time at the Holiday Inn at Lackland!!!!!!!! Have a good life buddy, you will not be forgotten!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Great”
text:
This place is perfect if yuo are looking for a small apartment. It is clean, brand new, furnished and if you need any utilities the staff provides.
The two guys at the reception (Ali and Lucy) are great people, friendly, available, smart.. 
I stayed ther for two monts and it was a great experience.
It is expensive, as anywhere alse in San Jose. It is forbidden to smoke, as anywhere alse in the states.

title: “Great room, location and service”
text:
My wife and I just got back from staying at The Muse Hotel, NYC for 6 nights. We got married on 28th December in the UK and stayed there for our honeymoon. My only regret is that we couldn't have stayed longer. The hotel is brilliantly located about 1/2 block away from Times Square although even on New Year’s Eve we were not kept awake, even though our room was only on the fifth floor. 
During our check-in we told them it was our honeymoon and they were kind enough to send up a bottle of Cava (not quite Krug but very thoughtful nonetheless!)
Our room, even though it was one of the cheaper rooms in the hotel was very well appointed. There was loads of space, especially for a NYC hotel room. Very clean with the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in. Very comfortable mattress and pillow top and lovely feather pillows. Bathroom was immaculately clean (one minor grumble was that the towels were not as fluffy and large as you would expect from a luxury hotel - though in fairness they also provided a pair of very funky looking zebra print and tiger print bathrobes which very comfortable). 
There was a large LCD flat panel TV screen on the wall, well stocked mini-bar and everything you would expect from a luxury hotel room. A small criticism was that the a/c unit in our room was quite noisy and stopped and started a lot throughout the night. It was -7C at some points during our stay so it wasn’t an option to switch it off as we needed the heat. We should have had a grumble and maybe they would have changed our room but in fairness it only woke me up a few times.
The front desk staff were incredibly helpful and made some great suggestions for local restaurants. Spotted Pig in Greenwich, Bobo also in Greewich and Asia de Cuba were all fantastic. The bellmen were also excellent and all of them real 'can-do' guys! One of them had the loudest whistle I have ever heard and was able to hail a cab from 300+ yards! It was also very refreshing to stay in a hotel which honored your Do Not Disturb sign by not knocking at all.
A really nice touch was that they had a wine tasting evening every day in the lobby where you could have complimentary wine. It was a really nice way to start your evening and a good way to socialise with other guests. They also had warm apple cider all day for when you had just come in from the freezing NYC streets. 
We paid about £1650 for 6 nights which works out about £275/night. For Christmas/New Years I would say this was just about okay for NYC, although I was disappointed to find guests from Australia and US who had paid a lot less for better rooms. I did try shopping around beforehand to get what I thought was the best price so I guess I must have missed the best deals.
We would definitely stay at The Muse again and we are already planning our next trip for the same time this year 2010 to celebrate our first anniversary. Hopefully we will be able to score a better deal on our room this time around.

title: “Poor Service”
text:
My husband and I enjoyed the location of the hotel, but encountered poor service, which we have never encountered at other Hilton Hotels, where we have stayed at in the U.S. 
Except for one young lady, who handled our check-in, the reception desk people were impolite and unfriendly. But the worst service came from the hotel's own concierge: She was condescending and downright rude to us, when we asked her information about the city tours.
Naturally, we pledged never to return to this Hilton Hotel again.

title: “Unsatisfactory”
text: On arrival,on early morning we were told that the only room would be in different building on the second floor. This is not what we had reqested on reservation. I recently had a knee replacement and had requested that a room on the first floor. The clerk was very much "take or leave it" attitude.

title: “Charlesmark marginal”
text: Great location. Front desk service questionable. Were not very welcoming. Need better people skills. But housekeeping staff were outstanding. Friendly and room great. Front desk needs to take que from housekeeping. Stayed at the Hotel Lenox previous year and much better overall. But the price was better at the Charlesmark. BUT would pay more for the Lenox rather than stay at the Charlesmark again.

title: “great rrip”
text: Stayed at the Hotel Palomar with my husband and two boys, ages 9 & 7. We had a wonderful stay and very much enjoyed our trip. The staff was very nice and helpful and the hotel was beautiful.

title: “Best Hotel for Dogs in Denver”
text:
My husband and i and our two Shelties stayed at the Hotel Monaco Denver and we all had a fabulous time. The "girls" were welcomed with
a gift bag with a dog bone and a Mutt Mitt each, and they were permitted on the restaurant's outside seating area for breakfast. They were petted by almost every employee they came across and they enjoyed being with us for the evening wine reception (where they met a Boxer). We ordered room service the first night as it was in the mid-90s outside and the food at the Italian restaurant on site is first rate. I had the sea bass and the honey flan and my husband had the chicken piccatta and the tiramisu. Both meals were delicious. The animal print robes are cozy, and the L'Occitane bath amenities divine. I also enjoy the reading material in all Hotel Monacos and the yoga tv station. We are so glad we stayed here and we would strongly recommend it to anyone with pets.

title: “Safe and clean”
text:
As a solo female traveller, safety is important to me, and with the front desk manned 24 hours a day, and the doors closed at night, I felt safe. 
The hotel is ideally situated for shopping. There's a Walgreens close by if you want basics, and Macy's around the corner for fancier shopping. The tourist bus goes from a stop close by.
The rooms are tiny and basic, but very clean. The Internet was reasonably priced if you stay for a week or more (then you can buy the $30 monthly rate instead of the $10 a day rate) and was adequate for my needs (checking email, connecting to tourist sites, google maps etc). The breakfast was basic buffet, but fine for my needs. The beds were great.
I was at the back of the hotel, facing a brick wall, which made the room dim at all times, but I wasn't in the room much. The closet didn't allow for a full drop of skirts, dresses or pants. The one chair was a hard wooden one. It was very dorm-like, with an excellent shower in the ensuite (no bath). Could have used a fridge, but in a two star, that's not usual. 
Thought it was expensive, for what it was, but it seems that all San Francisco hotels are expensive, so not outside the norm. The people manning the desk were friendly and helpful.

title: “Nice Location but Pricy and over rated”
text: We thought being the classic Ritz we would be receiving Outstanding Accomodationns for Price paid. We found the hotel very crowded with alot of noise and staff overwhelmed by all the activity. Its not a oasis of paradise you would expect at a Luxury Priced Hotel. Recomend staying at a Hilton or Omni getting a better value and peaceful stay for a much better return on dollars spent.

title: “Very Good, will be back.”
text:
We wanted a nice place to stay for 7-10 days and be comfortable for the World Shoot. This facility worked out well. 
There was some confusion at check-in about out rate, but that was worked out. The wife suspected they were trying to get $10 more a day for the room, but we had our booking paperwork . We were also given a handicap room, but this worked out well. 
We were on a diet so the kitchen and large refrigerator was excellent. Having a two room suite with two TV's worked well and the furniture was nice and the bed comfortable. They have a different housekeeping policy and we were concerned at first but it worked out well. Staff was very friendly and helpful. 
The only real down side was the parking. It is rather limited and many of the staff take the prime spots in front. 
We did not take advantage of the Managers Reception with food and drinks on Thursdays and we did not participate in the breakfast. They both looked excellent.

title: “Best Value in Midtown!”
text:
Could not have been happier! Room was large, clean and lovely; 1920's building in excellent shape and very quaint. Highly recommend eating at the attached Plataforma (Brazilian BBQ) - outstanding!
Kitchenette was indispensible and the location is perfect. Had one issue with shower leaking (although water pressure was great); told the front desk as we left that morning and it was fixed when we returned. Most impressed with staff. Will definitely stay here again.

title: “Clean, comfortable, historic, terrific stay!”
text: What a find! The Handelry treated us like human beings! Customer service was superior to any I've found in the US. The hotel itself was clean, historic and very comfortable. Catherine at the front desk accomodated our family to perfection. What a special place. We will be back!

title: “You are only paying for location.......nothing else.”
text:
I traveled with three other girlfriends for a fun weekend in Chicago. The location of this hotel can't be beat, you are on Michigan Avenue and directly across the street from Grant Park, Millenium Park, and Buckingham Fountain. 
Now, to get to any of the fun, young parts of town we either had to walk more than a mile (which was fine) or take a cab. So, I would not recommend this to anyone who can't walk a ways or afford to take a cab.
The lobby is lovely and I checked in in mere minutes. Then I headed to my room......yikes.
First of all my room was miles away from the lobby. I had to take an elevator and then travel through 3 different long hallways. The hallways are shabby and smell. The doors to get through these hallways are beaten up and scary looking.
The room was adequate to accomodate the four of us but it was a dump. It needs a major update. There were two flat screen tvs but one of them didn't work. Someone did come and fix it luckily. The bathroom door only had a door knob on one side, I have no idea what happened to the other half. We didn't have hot water unless you ran the water for about 10 minutes and the first time I ran the shower rust came out.
I wouldn't ever stay here again unless it was dirt cheap. We payed $209 a night for a two bedroom room.
What a dump!

title: “Great for Mallrats!”
text:
Staying in a hotel attached to a mall is great, and if that mall is the Dallas Galleria, it's even better! Parking is free unless you valet then it's $25 overnight. And if you are an early bird, you can go down to the 2nd floor of the Galleria and enjoy a few eateries that open early for breakfast. The hotel itself has an open early/open late bistro/bar on the 2nd floor but it's pricey and will leave you hungry for more. My room was on the 8th floor, so I had a good view of the roof and parking lot. Extremely clean, and the free coffee/tea provided is Starbucks & Tazo! The king bed was comfy but the pillows were way too soft, so I required 3 to keep my head aligned. A fridge which looks like it used to be a mini-bar is provided. My only complaint is no free wi-fi, the charge is $10 a day! 
The hotel also bills itself as a spa, and they offer in-room massages for around $120. I didn't purchase one, but there are coupons in the room for services and some of the restaurants in the Galleria. The pool look fabulous but I didn't go in. 
All the staff were nice and attentive. Overall, great place especially for those who love to shop! If you need to go Downtown, it's only about a 12 minute drive away!

title: “outstanding customer service”
text: We often stay with La Quinta Inns for their excellent rooms, pet friendly enviornment and the customer service from management and staff. On a recent stay we had an unexpected complication that took us away from the Hotel for an extended time. Mr. Patel and his staff went way beyond what we could expect to accomadate our extended stay and help us with our dogs. Wonderful people, great location. Can't say enough.

title: “Nice upscale hotel but expensive”
text: Visited on Father's Day weekend with spouse and children (10 & 12 yrs). The location was convenient but noisy with the train passing through. The rooms were smaller than I expected but overall the hotel was well maintained. The mandatory valet parking was expensive. For the price I paid at Hotwire - I would visit again but not if I had to pay full price.

title: “Expensive New York!”
text:
We went to New York for four nights for my Birthday in May. We chose the Hotel Edison after reading many reviews on Trip advisor. We decided to go for the supreme room. When we arrived after a terrible taxi ride the staff were rather unfriendly, almost rude. 
We went up to our room on the seventh floor, which was dark and shabby. It was a large clean room with sofa, king size bed, TV etc (no coffee machine/kettle tho) but could really do with being refurbished. The best/ almost only thing going for the hotel is its location!!
From what we heard tho all of New York hotels are very expensive and normally the rooms are tiny.
If your going to New York you must try this wonderful Cuban restaurant for lunch or dinner Guantanamera 939 8th Ave it was $15 for a 3-course lunch, which was lovely. Also Mint restaurant (Indian) 150 E 50th street, between Lexington Ave & 3rd Ave.

title: “Helpless at the Hyatt”
text: Staying at the Hyatt was impersonable and problematic. Day one the AC wouldn't go below 74, the phone didn't work and sink was clogged. Called and fixed all, but later found AC only turned down 2 degrees. Finally found staff was internally controlling min limit on AC! After 3 tries finally got it to get to 70. Bar staff was rude. Room so so. All in all look elsewhere first.

title: “Definately had some issues, but staff more than apologized”
text:
I will preface this review by stating that this was our last hotel stay of a 9 night 8 hotel trek from Oklahoma to North Carolina and back. Based on reviews, I was expecting this to be one of the best experiences, however, it was the only one where we encountered any problems. I am a priority club platinum member so all stays with the exception of 1 were at IHG properties. 
 The good: Hotel lobby was nicely decorated, enjoyed viewing model of original Holiday Inn room (brought back childhood memories), location was good and the room adequate and quiet. 
 Before I start with the bad, I will add that a member of the hotel staff paid a personal visit to my room, apologized profusely and made amends to my complete satisfaction. I debated even writing a review, but upon reading the last one, I feel compelled to write.
 The bad: Very slow check in (15 minutes at least), got my key, top floor, key didn't work, had to go back down to desk, corrected, went back up to room and the room didn't have the bed choice I had booked. Three people with a teenager and one bed! Called down to desk to inform them and they said they would find a room and call me back. Now, for the reason I am writing...we had driven 8 hours, were to meet at a restaurant for dinner, however, didn't feel as though we could use or "mess up" the room that obviously wasn't going to be ours for the night. I had also mistakenly assumed we would only be there a few moments, which was not the case. Because of this we did use the restroom, and I recall wondering if, in fact, they were going to reclean this room, as others may not have been so considerate of this issue. Won't go into details of what followed, but without a room ready after 4pm we had to leave our things and go to dinner. My guess as to the other review with the shower being used, etc. is that possibly someone else was in the same position we were and had no choice but to use the facilities as they had no place else to go. 
 In conclusion, the staff did take several steps to make this up to us and for that I am grateful. However, after having 8 nights of stays with no issues at all, I would have expected it to have gone better, especially with all the glowing reviews.

title: “Absolutely fabulous staff!!”
text:
Spent two weeks at the Staybridge while in Memphis for training. The hotel was wonderful! I'll start with housekeeping: I am VERY picky and thoroughly checked my room when I arrived. Everything looked clean. I was surprised (but appreciative) when I left a glass in the sink one morning while in a rush, and when I came back it was in the dishwasher! I ran into a couple housekeeping staff in the hallways throughout my stay, and each time they greeted me with a smile and asked if I was enjoying my stay. I did not catch their names but the genuine friendliness was across the board.
The front desk staff were wonderful too! Very personable and again, always ready to greet me with a warm smile. They gave me great advice about where to go around town and always followed-up with "how did it go?"
The hotel has a shuttle that will take you anywhere within a 5 mile radius. The shuttle drivers were so friendly too! My favorite, hands-down, was Eric. He juggled a large group of us with different interests and I never waited long. I'm also a horrible backseat driver but I felt safe with Eric. He drove well, recommended places to go to, and warned us about areas we would probably want to avoid. 
Now the food. The Staybridge offers a free breakfast buffet, not just continental, everyday and happy hour Monday -Thursday. The breakfast offers a huge variety--bagels, eggs, bacon, sausage, biscuits, oatmeal, waffles and the list goes on! The happy hour offers free beer and wine and a small meal (I.e. sloppy joes, egg rolls, tacos...). The only thing better than the variety and the quality of the food is the man who makes it--Mr. LB! He is the nicest man and so accommodating. I was part of a large group who insisted on sitting together all the time. Mr. LB allowed us to move tables and chairs and never told us to turn the volume down despite the fact that we were very loud at times. He went as far as to bake cookies for our group...twice!! 
If I had to sum up the Staybridge in a few words...clean, accommodating, and welcoming. As home-sick as I was feeling, the staff really made me feel better. I hope I have the opportunity to come back soon. Thank you Staybridge staff!!

title: “Customer Service Feedback”
text:
Overall, my stay at the Affinia Manhattan Hotel was great! This was my second time staying at Affinia, and the service was excellent. In addition, what motivated me to write this review was the excellent customer service I received from Jenna. 
From the time I checked in by the front desk, Jenna greeted me in a warm and gracious manner. After checking in the computer, she informed me about the complementary upgrade to my room and internet use during my stay.
Jenna's business friendly communication style left a strong enough impression to remind me the importance of staff members consistently demonstrating quality customer service to others.
Excellent job Jenna!

title: “great location great place”
text: this place in located right on the bay, great room, underground parking garage(only $5 a day) free breakfast buffet. allaround great service, very friendly and helpful staff. i will stay here again and again. thx guys for a great weekend.

title: “Marketing genius!”
text: We booked this hotel based on trip advisor reviews and the hotel website. The owner is a marketing genius! We would admit that the pool and hot tub were very nice, but that is the only thing that makes these outdated motel style rooms bearable. The hotel has tried to put in cool artwork, flat screens and modern furniture, but it really does not make up for the outdated exterior, cinderblock walls, open air rooms which must be very hot in the summer and the need for some serious new carpets. We had a suite and our bathroom was literally too small to turn around in, the cooling system was very loud. We visited the roof top bar which was advertised as the new hip place in Phoenix, there was literally no one there at 10:00 on a Friday night. The hotel is not near anything of interest, and it is about a 20 minute drive to the airport. I have to say that the staff was very nice and helpful, but the most impressive thing about this hotel is how the owner has found a way to market such an outdated property! We live in a city and are used to city life, but my son thought the best way to describe this "boutique" hotel was "sketchy."

title: “Professional, not snotty”
text: I had been here already a few times a few years ago before the renovation of the rooms and things are going better. Room was big, hip and comfortable. Staff is professional, although things went a bit wrong at check in and check out, and although trying to act cool, not snotty whatsoever. The Thirtynine restaurant is nice, the pool area a bit small. Location is ideal if you want to be central in LA, although nothing is going on in this neighbourhood. Prices are reasonable if you look at the quality. In general: a good choice for travellers that feel young.

title: “Loved the Prescott!”
text:
We found this hotel on trip advisor as the reviews were so good. This was our first visit to San Fran had a lovely time and would def go back!
The hotel was clean, the staff friendly and the beds so very, very, comfortable!
Definitely a must!

title: “Pleasantly surprised.”
text: I was expecting it to be average at best but boy was I wrong. From the great location, to the extremely clean room to lovely LCD tv and of course the free parking! It was all good. I asked for a higher floor and facing the pool and the staff complied willingly. The room I got was a double double, room 625. I don't know if they're all the same quality though, but the one I got was just like the pictures on the website.

title: “A Wonderful Place!”
text:
My wife and I went for our third anniversary and had a wonderful time. We highly recommend the Royal Palms as your home away from home. The staff was very welcoming and super friendly. 
The Lamborghini convention held at the resort this last weekend was amazing... We liked the 1200hp Bugatti Veyron that happened to be parked out front. Check out the picture below!

title: “very comfortable, good location”
text: my room was large, very clean. comfortable bed and great location. can't ask for much more. staff was friendly. I was happy that I could walk to everything I wanted to see downtown and water-front.

title: “Great Value, Location, Convience”
text:
i stayed at the Edison for three nights with my boyfreind, just visiting new york on site seeing. I searched alot of hotels, and booked the edison. I checked with trip advisor and i read a few bad reviews and got scared. I expected the worst. 
Check in was a sinch. Less than 2 minutes, just had to sign the form and the bell hop brought everything up to the room. We had a newly rennovated room with a double bed, a night stand a desk, a chair and a good size tv. The room looked exactly like the picture because it was remodeled. The room next to ours was not remodeled and it looked like it was from the 70's. It had everything the same as ours, just older style. People complained because there was not enough plugs, it is an old hotel. There was three outlets in the room plus the bathroom. If thats not enough and you need alot bring an extension cord. I had my laptop a curling iron, a blow dryer two phone chargers and an iron. and it was completely fine for us. 
It's literally a second from times square. Very convient location, as everyone else says. Great shops and food around it.
Room service was great. I called for towels not even 2 minutes later they brought me a bunch, same with an iron. I guess the people who don't like this hotel are looking for a 5 star in a 3 star budget. The value was great, and i will definately plan a trip there again. Just make sure to ask for a newly renovated room.
They do hold the bags after you check out. It's 50 cents a bag for as long as you need. Who cares it 50 cents, everything else in NY is expensive so i don't know why another review complained it costs 2 dollars to store 4 bags? prolly the cheapest thing there. Check out was easier than checking in. Just give them the room keys and your all set.
This hotel is a deal, we visited the other hotels, near it such as the wellington which is the same money and it was gross. The bathroom in our room was small, but had a full size tub, a medicine cabinet, a toliet towel racks, and the sink. It has all the basics. Also i read a review that said there was no shampoo, etc. There was plenty it was on a shelf, they musta not looked hard enough. I recommened this hotel, but not if ur looking for a 5 star. It was perfect for my trip. Pictures are coming soon

title: “Location Location Location”
text: This hotel is in the heart of Gaslamp in San Diego. It is a quaint historical property without the hustle bustle of the large chain hotels. It has a sandwich shop open for breakfast and lunch. It has a small bar on the premises. The rooms are charmingly decorated keeping to its historical theme. It is it's location that sets this hotel apart from the others. The Gaslamp is where the action is and this hotel is in the center of it. The restaurants, bars, and music are within feet of the front door. The room rates are a little less expensive than the other hotels in the area. It's a great place to stay if your plan is to experience the Gaslamp and use the hotel as a place to sleep.

title: “Great room in a very nice hotel”
text:
We stayed from the 1st to the 5th of July and really enjoyed Hotel Deca. The staff were very friendly and helpful, even when they were working on 4th July. The cafe (Tullys) attached to hotel is very convinient and the restaraunt also attached (The District) was alao very nice and reasonably priced. Alcohol was very cheap during happy hour.
After initially declining a $15 per night room upgrade to a double queen suite, the guy at the desk bumped us up for free anyway.
It's fairly easy to get around on the bus from one street over and there's mostly young college folk on board so it's a comfy ride.
Finally, we left our camera behind in the room and only realised when we got to the Amtrak station. We called and the front desk was only too happy to collect it, wrap it in bubble wrap and send to our next stay in Vancouver, Canada.
I'd recomend this place to anyone and the renovations to building look great.

title: “Good Location...BUT”
text: We reserved a room on the advice of someone at a sister hotel....mistake! This hotel was clean and well-located, but we were disappointed to discover that despite web advertisements, it did not include breakfast. We found the staff to be pretty rude and not all that helpful when asking for restaurant reviews and other tips. The worst, though, was the pool. We were traveling with our 7 yr old daughter who was excited to take a swim. Upon check-in the woman at the desk told us to go enjoy a swim at the pool. We chose to do that right away, only to find it under construction for 2 months! Nobody mentioned this when we reserved, and obviously the desk clerk should said something. Our daughter was quite disappointed!! We also were told a different price for the garage parking by the attendant than what was charged on our bill. When my husband questioned it at check out, he was rudely asked if he had heard of tax. $8 in tax on $35 for parking??? The hotel was well located for our walking tour of the city and had nice restaurants nearby, but I would not stay there again.

title: “Excellent location but noisy at night”
text:
US grant is a very comfortable hotel located right in the downtown centre area. It is walking distance to many attractions and accessible by both the orange and blue trolley (civic centre). Bus #7 brings u to the San Diego zoo as well and bus #992 brings u to the airport.
The only negative thing is that it is rather noisy at night. A couple of bars are located nearby and the police siren is a standard "alarm" u'll hear at 1am.

title: “okay , but some minor problems”
text:
check-in was great, front desk clerk (nightshift) , offered
 friendly service . Housekeeping knocked on door for service when do not disturb sign was displayed, apparently someone took the sign down (went on for 2 days we were there).We used hotel phone to call for pizza close to hotel 75 cents local , charged $8 on bill (charged as long distance) management waived fee when confronted about error. Overall hotel appearance was nice &i would return

title: “Downtown Destination”
text: this hotel is superb! the lobby is beautiful, especially the fireplaces built into the wall as you walk though the foyer. it's a bit of a walk from your room to the parking area, which was a bit confusing to get to and from when i first got there. the food available is pretty good; only issue i had was late night dining as the nice restaurant closes around 9 or 10 depending on the night. i love that omni gave us starbucks gift card when we checked it = awesome! the rooms are very nice, and comfortable. service was good (4 out of 5, i would say.) location of the hotel is central and there's a good amount of things nearby in walking and/or cab drive distance. the "heated" (it wasn't warm enough to swim when i went; though, i went over new years) pool on the roof is beautiful and the hot tub rocks. if they had more than one hot tub - that would serve them well.

title: “Not bad!”
text:
We booked a room for 4 but seems a difficult concept for the house keeping staff. each day we had to phone reception for extra towels and coffee cups/plastic glasses. We even left notes to no avail ! 
The room we had was snug for 4 female shoppers, and the view of the Bus Terminal car park was different! Even with the window shut it was rather noisy , having stayed in New York several times this was the noisiest hotel room. However the room and hotel is very clean and fine for 4/5 nights- the reception staff where friendly and helpful.
Close to everything, found a great diner just 5 mins away - used the subway and the locals love to help lost tourist. Did not eat in hotel so can not comment on that, but overall the it was not bad for the money and time we spent there. Would I recommend it- yes.

title: “Dated Hotel Place, Free Airport Shuttle. So So Location”
text:
Hotels in Denver were hard to find last week so I picked the Renaissance. It was the nicest looking place available for the money ($219 a night).
For that price, I expect top quality service, a clean room and fast internet.
Unfortunately, the hotel slipped on several items.
1. The Internet wasn't working half the time. When I called the "help desk", the guy non-chalantly told me that they were having maintenance issues and couldn't tell me when it worked. When It did work, it was reasonably fast. The problem is it didn't work for most of my 3 night stay.
2. The Hotel had me down for 1 less night than I booked. Luckily, they quickly resolved this issue.
3. The lounge isn't open on Weekends or later in the evening on Friday. Major Thumbs Down. (It's on the 10th floor).
The location is not great. While it is off I-70, it isn't near anything worth while. It didn't feel like a safe area.
Parking is NOT free and you pay $10 a night to self park in a covered garage. 
Internet isn't free either but it didn't work half the time so I suppose that's a wash?
The inside of the hotel is quite nice but clearly dated. The interiors need a refresh badly.
On the plus side, the rooms were BIG. The bed was so so (compared to a Marriott or Hilton bed). The hotel also offers a free hotel shuttle to DIA (major plus).
If this hotel weren't $219 a night, I might be OK with what I got but it felt overpriced for such a property.
It's not bad but not great either. It'll do in a pinch.

title: “This Is A Great Place To Stay”
text:
My wife and I spent a week here on vacation, exploring Seattle and the surrounding environs.
The people in the hotel are very friendly and very knowledgeable. Public transportation is located nearby making it unnecessary to rent a car when exploring Seattle - Downtown. Many different types of restaurants are located within easy walking distance.
You get a lot of value for your money at the Maxwell and I would recommend this hotel to anyone vacationing in Seattle

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: Excellent hotel, perfect location, and wonderful staff. This hotel should be rated higher that it is on most booking sites. The price was very good and the service was excellent. The staff went out of their way to make our stay enjoyable. We were able to walk to all of the must see places in Seattle. The trip may have been business, but the stay was a pleasure at the Mediterranean Inn.

title: “Excellent value in top location”
text:
Obtained a very good rate at the Blakely, admittedly a corporate rate in February, but to snag a two room suite for $239 per night (plus taxes) one and a half blocks from the St Regis was prtetty amazing.
The Blakely is a hole-in-the-wall marked by a royal blue awningon 55th Street. The lobby is minimal in size (which means you are not paying for useless space in your room rate).. The decor is a comfortable, British library style and this carries over quite effectively into the decor and furnishings of the bedrooms and bathrooms.
There are around six rooms on each of sixteen floors. There are two small elevators that are not only slow but operate with a mind of their own. as a result, you may want to specify a lower floor so that you can use the (fire escape) stairs if in a hurry.
Our room was well furnished, comfortable bed, but only two pillows and one bath robe. The bedroom, adjoining sitting room (both with TVs) and bathroom (with walk-in shower) were all surprisingly spacious. Based on the rate we paid, this hotel has to be one of the best values in Manhattan.
A buffet breakfast is served on the first floor in an adjoining Italian restaurant. The continental is just about passable and was included in our room rate. A full breakfast menu is available, accompanied by an annoying "Tip voucher" card, inviting you to sign a form to leave a tip for the staff.

title: “Good value for families, will probably stay again.”
text:
Taking my son back to UCD downtown with my teenage daughter this was a good choice. I've stayed downtown when I didn't have a car but you get less room for the money , usually no breakfast and will have to pay extra if you do have a car. I understand they allow pets so this is also something I may want in the future. We were able to park right outside our residence , this was a plus as my son had his instruments, amps and other valuables we didn't want to leave in the car. We were on the quiet side of the complex , I wasn't disturbed by traffic or noisy neighbors though we could hear the floor sqeeking above us occassionaly.
 We've also had a suite at the Hotel across the street which we really liked and though it was higher caliber as far as decor and general provisions it was more expensve and didn't have a fully equipped and roomy kitchen , which is the best feature of the residence Inn and why I recommend it for families. Full size frig, oven, dishwasher, microwave, utensils, pots pans, real dishes , glasses mugs etc. 
It's location is very easy for us and the Hotel provides free shuttle service so we didn't need to worry about parking downtown or driving after dinner. The shuttle driver was very helpful and we also took advantage of the growing dining scene availble on this side of Denver. Fun , less expensive but charming eateries are within walking distance but no real shopping. The shuttle even returned my son to his downtown residence after move in day the final night of our stay. 
Areas that could stand improvement: We required the sofabed but not only was it not made up but we had to move it several feet to make room - quite heavy- and the bedding provided for it was inferior. We did get a nicer blanket the second night . The sofa also wasn't very comfortable and could have used some throw pillows for more support.
The TV was an older model and couldn't be veiwed from the sofa bed and queen bed at the same time and we had to fiddle with the cable to get a better picture, probably because people try to turn the TV to face the bed and have tweaked the cable, a lazy susan under the Tv would help. The WIFi worked fine.
My biggest peeve was the breakfast was only served until 8:30. We got in late the night before , ordred excellent takeout, tried to unwind from a 9 hour drive , had to make up the sofabed...but I slept poorly knowing I had to hurry to get some food to bring back to the room because we didn't bring any. When I got to breakfast it was really crowded, with a long waiting line. The attendants worked fast and furious to keep up , the food was alright though I didn't want to wait for the waffles and I didn't notice if they turned people away at 8:30. They should provide trays so people can go back to their suite more easily and relieve some of the congestion. We didn't take advantage of the breakfast the rest of our stay because of the hassle but had a few leftover muffins from the day before. I understand there's a quick take out in the lobby for people who miss the breakfast: Water, a granola bar and an apple. 
Finally, they only provide one wash cloth per person and had them out in the vanity area, none provided for the shower. I got extra towels and wash cloths only to have to get them again the second night. Little things like this can turn people away from an otherwise pleasant stay but we'll probably return if it remains a good value.

title: “Still A Classic”
text: I have stayed in this hotel many times over the last 10-15 years. We went the first weekend in December, 2012. The holiday decorations and lights are spectacular - so if you have small children they will be in heaven. The hotel itself is beautiful and service impeccable. We stayed in the main building and it is need of updating. The room was large enough with nice windows. The carpet and decor, however, are in my opinion ready for a makeover. Similarly, in this age of electronics, you still have to hunt for an electrical outlet to plug in your stuff - and the outlets are near the floor on the baseboards. So while it is still a grand dame, it may be time to for a facelift.

title: “Beautiful place to stay”
text: We really enjoyed our stay at this hotel. While my wife attended a seminar at the hotel, my son and I spent the day at the Galleria mall. The hotel was easy enough to find, but opted for valet parking because I was not too sure that our vehicle would make the clearance of the parking garage. The hotel was beautiful and was exactly what I expected from a four-star hotel. Great stay.

title: “Atmoshpere and location”
text:
Less than a block away from a cable car route, and within walking distance of many of San Francisco's attractions is the lovely, old-style hotel, Vintage Court. When we first checked in, we suspected the second floor room, which faced the street, could be noisy, but staff were happy to reallocate us a lovely quiet room on the top floor. 
Some reviewers have complained about the size of the rooms. Perhaps they have not stayed in the tiny rooms common to cities in Europe, especially Rome! We were pleased by the comforts offered by our Vintage Court room.
The wine evenings, from 5pm to 6pm in front of the fireplace of the reception area, were a great way for us Aussies to meet Americans, and share our stories. We talked with interesting people of all ages and became acquainted with some good Californian wines.
We splashed out and ate a wonderful dinner in the restaurant next door: Masa's. The degustation menu was delicious and the hand-made chocolates at the end of the meal, sheer decadence. Well worth the money!

title: “Great place to stay”
text: Great place to stay while we visited our grand daughter.... The staff were very professional.... I would recomend staying here as I will stay again....easy on and off the freeway and easy access to downtown...

title: “Good Stay”
text: This hotel is very nice as most Embassy Suites are. Rooms were very comfortable, clean and complimentary breakfast was good. Managers reception was very nice. My only drawback was the restaurant. The food was not what I expected. I ordered a hamburger and waited quite a while for it with very few customers in the restaurant. Then I ordered my favorite desert, bread pudding. What came on the plate did not resemble any bread pudding I ever ordered before. It was a very dry chunk which is hard to describe, no moisture, no sauce and it kind of looked like a dry fruitcake without the fruit. It was a complete disappointment. I may be back but will not eat in the restaurant unless they make some changes.

title: “Great San Francisco Location”
text: This is centrally located for Union Square; for the shopping, cable cars and the city. The rooms were very comfortable, there was a great flat screen TV. There is internet access. There is a newly refurbished gym and also a pool. The concierge was very informative. Its is a very busy hotel and there is the usual expensive car parking charge for being in this city. This hotel has it for the location. There is a upper level bar and you can enjoy a drink with views of the city from high!

title: “Excellent Value!”
text: Stayed in NYC for 1 night w/ 2 adult "children" (19 years old). Easy to get to, valet parking very convenient. Able to check in early w/o difficulty and leave bags next day for a nominal fee. Close to EVERYTHING. Staff courteous. Would highly recommend if you are just looking for someplace to sleep. Beds were comfortable as were the pillows. Did not check out amenities as were busy w/ shopping, shows and eating. We were on the 9th floor, and did not notice any untoward noises mentioned in earlier reviews. Our room was not one of the ones renovated, but was just fine.

title: “You get what you pay for...”
text:
Good location, if you're an Upper West Side person. 
(Personally, I prefer Greenwich Village, but the Larchmont was sold out, and the Washington Square has gone up in price.) 
So...the first room we were put in was not only claustrophobically cramped, it was also dirty. I have stayed all over the world, in some sketchy places, and I'm no princess. I have never before complained about a room's cleanliness, Sorry, but when I touch the floor of the shower and my hand gets dirty, I am not happy.
BUT...at least they were accommodating. They immediately moved us to a better room. 
The beds are comfortable. 
The woman at the desk in the morning is a doll.
The guy at the desk at night is strange.
Easy to get to from Subway.
Wonderfully close to Central Park and Zabars.
From the outside (and from the photos on the website), the place looks a lot more charming than it is. Nevertheless...
Would I stay there again, even after all my beeyotching? I would. It's NYC, and it's a good deal. But I'd be sure to request a room on one of the lower floors (the place seems to be less well-cared for on the higher floors), and I will definitely check the room carefully before unpacking my bags!

title: “A very nice hotel with great service and convenient location”
text:
I recently staying at the Sofitel in Washington DC with my wife and two young children (6 and 8). This is really a terrific place. We were there over the MLK holiday weekend, and got two rooms with breakfast included for $175/night/room. What a great deal for such a nice hotel! 
Highlights:
* The rooms were reasonably spacious, with very comfortable beds, nice bathrooms (separate tub and shower), and tasteful furniture and decor.
* Lobby bar had very cool decor, comfortable seating, and reasonably tasty food (we had a light dinner there with the kids one night, and it was great). 
* Wonderful breakfast in the restaurant. This isn't some lame hotel restaurant, but actually has an interesting french-inspired menu and quite good food.
* Very nice, very cheerful, and very helpful staff all around, from the doormen to the front desk to the concierge. You should expect this in a nice hotel, but so often they disappoint. Not so here, where it is clear that management has set high expectations for how staff treat guests. 
Downsides:
* Not much to say here, except that when we reserved the rooms we were told they were adjoining which was true in a sense but not exactly in the way you find at most hotels. There was a common keyed door off the hallway, which then led to a very small foyer with keyed doors into each bedroom. We were unable to bolt lock the door into the hallway because it is a common entry for two separate rooms. The only problem from our standpoint was that we have very young children and would have felt more comfortable bolt locking the hall door. We couldn't bolt their guest room door because then we wouldn't have been able to get in there. Not a huge deal, but something to be aware of if you have small kids with you. 
Overall, I highly recommend this hotel and would come back without hesitation.

title: “Very Nice Place to stay, not too big, not too small, just right!”
text: We stayed here in September. The rooms are wonderful and the tv is AMAZING. Add to that a friendly staff and good food. I wish they had more of these everywhere. The rooms are also very roomy with a sectional couch, refrigerator, coffee maker. Very well decorated and updated as well. Again, love that high-def tv 42" plasma. After, the hurricane, we went to stay with my parents at Hilton of Americas downtown high rise building $400.00 plus rooms. I must say they were no comparison to the Hyatt place. Hyatt Place wins hands down. Better food also.I highly recommend.

title: “Great hotel for the price- outstanding location.”
text:
