My family and I recently stayed at the King George, and we were pleasantly surprised. The rate was very fair, considering the close proximity to Union Square. This hotel is a perfect place to stay if you plan on spending most of your time exploring the city and a close, convenient hotel is needed. 
The room was ready when we arrived, clean, and totally acceptable. The lobby, rooms, elevator, and other features show the character of the building while being maintained pretty well. This hotel has not been "gutted" and reinvented, but it has been updated with new tile, sinks, etc, and retains the original San Francisco charm. One consideration is you can hear sounds through the walls. (The room next door had some kids partying and we could just about hear words specifically--Thankfully it did not wake up my kids).
Last but not least, the staff was truly friendly and helpful. They were very relaxed and approachable, ready for questions, and went above and beyond to make sure we were taken care of. We will come back.

title: “Great place with great management staff.”
text: Had a super fun time with my girlfriends in this place. It was a great hotel for some friends to share a room together, clean, nice staff.

title: “Choose The Wharf Inn”
text:
We weren't orginally booked into The Wharf Inn when we arrived in San Francisco, we booked in on short notice as the place we came from provided us with some unnerving experiences. 
We were so happy with The Wharf Inn, it was so different to what we had come from. The rooms were so beautifully set out and clean. The people at the front office were so welcoming, kind and full of interesting tourist information.
The Wharf Inn is so close to the tourist attractions and is only a block away from where most of the guided tours began, restaurants and an array of street performers.
Thankyou to The Wharf Inn for lifting our spirits about San Francisco and allowing us to enjoy our trip.

title: “I'm back because I just love this hotel.”
text: I love the hotel more now that I stayed in a newly renovated room on the 7th Floor. It has new carpet, soothing room color and the bathroom was quite a transformation from the last time I stayed. As usual, the staff are amazing and always give you a red carpet welcome.

title: “stay in moderne hotel”
text: I stayed in the Moderne hotel with my daughter for 5 days and could recommend this hotel for location, service and value. We walked out of the front door almost onto Broadway! Do not expect anything too luxurious but it was clean, quiet, comfortable and well equipped...however, I would have loved a facility to make tea or coffee when we returned to our room after a long day out walking around New York!

title: “Great hotel. Awesome staff.”
text: From the time we arrived to the time we left, the service at this hotel was outstanding. Rooms were big for NYC, clean and safe from the city sounds. Definitely will be going back.

title: “Great Breakfast! OK stay.”
text:
We chose this property because of its proximity to the airport and our need for a night's stay before heading to the mountains.
The hotel is exactly like others I've stayed at be$onging to this chain. However, I noticed a few things. The toilet paper and tissue is really cheap. Falls apart and uncomfortable. All the pillows are lumpy sof and the bed was mediocre comfortable.
But the breakfast is fabulous! They offer a great continental breakfast plus a hot, made to order standard menu. Everything was delicious, especially because of the people working in the cafe. They are funny, friendly and eager to serve.

title: “Very cool hotel”
text: This hotel is so neat! It's very historical and it almost feels like you're walking down the halls of history when you're on the way to your room. The staff was very helpful and not invasive in our space, so that was great. It also has a Starbucks attached to the lobby, so that was a great way to start out the day! We got a room with what looked like a brand new bed and it was sooo comfortable, especially after a long day walking around the city. We will definitely stay here again!

title: “Comfortable property, great location”
text: We recently spent 6 nights at this hotel. We are Diamond members and were upgraded to a corner suite which had an absolutely fantastic view of the City. Furniture is somewhat dated, however, very functional. Bed was comfortable, A/C, shower, etc. worked perfectly. Elevators are divided into banks for different floors so service was very quick. Breakfast at the hotel restaurant was good, although we did miss the old brunch buffet they had on the top floor. That was a special treat with total view of the City. I understand this area is now reserved for private parties. They no longer have an Executive Lounge at this hotel. Overall, great stay.

title: “Great Weekend Stay for Texas Game”
text:
Arrived in Austin on Friday. Check in was a little crowded and no SPG platinum line. Was upgraded to a cool corner suite. Great room. I was there for the Texas vs BYU game and was giving a greeting card in room with the BYU logo on it (team I was cheering for) and a stainless water bottle to take tailgating. Nice touch. 
Room service was prompt and food was good by RS standards. Location is great just a few blocks from 6th street and a mile from DKR stadium. 
Check out was a breeze and I will definitely being staying at the W Austin again.

title: “Great Stay !”
text:
After having our flight cancelled from the UK we arrived at the hotel four hours late after being up for nearly twenty four hours.
It was a lovely suprise to find out that we have been up graded to a Studio Suite as we were staying for four nights.
We had paid extra for two queen beds but this room had plenty of room and two armchairs.
The elephant & castle was fine for breakfast although it did have a bit of a limited menu and if you drink tea I would drink something else as it was lukewarm each time and the tea was really weak.
All the staff were really friendly and Verne on the help desk was just that very helpful.
The hotel is very close to the Magnificent Mile and the best inside mall is in Water Tower place which has more normal shops and a good Macy.
We visited the Field Museum ( Great ), the Wllis Tower ( very high ) the open top bus tour ( very cold ) and the Lincoln Park Zoo ( Long walk from hotel but got the 151 bus back ).
All in all a great visit but it seems prices in the USA has risen a lot since we were shopping last time in Minneapolis in Dec 2008.
A sign of the times.

title: “Vermin”
text: You cannot fault this hotel for location. The rooms are somewhat basic, dated and hot, however our main problem was vermin. After a couple of days, we realised that something had been in our suitcases and eaten through chocolates and cigarettes that we had packed, making an awful mess. Reception agreed to move us to a different room and sent a porter to collect our cases. The porter let slip that this is not an uncommon occurence at the hotel and is apparently because the subway station is located at the corner of the hotel. Be warned, if you are staying at the hotel don't leave any food in your room and don't think you're safe if you are on a higher floor (we were on the 21st).

title: “Pretty Nice”
text: Well located, spacious, comfortable, not cheap but still a good value for NY.

title: “Nice Hotel, Great Value”
text:
Have a great stay at the hotel for a week ... the room is clean and service is good.. 
Near to Union Square and some nice resturant near to the hotel.. 
For the the price i pay its really is value for money

title: “Great Location, Super Staff”
text:
Walking distance to all mid-town attractions (Times Square, Rockefeller Center, Central Park, Empire State Building, Broadway Theaters and more), and subway entrance one block away.
To get to the hotel from JFK we took the AirTrain to Jamaica Station then took LIRR from Jamaica station heading to New York City / Penn Station. (You can take the subway but takes over 30 minutes longer.) From Penn Station exit out the W 34th St toward 8th Ave. and walk up 8th Ave the five blocks to W 39th St. Took us about 10 minutes to walk to the hotel, all in all it was exactly one hour from when we got our bags at baggage claim to arrival at the hotel.
The Front Desk staff was excellent at check-in, and later when we asked for recommendations for a restaurant nearby they recommended the Carbone Ristorante just around the block from the hotel. This is a very good, family owned, Italian restaurant, very small, only about six tables and bar but the food was fantastic (highly recommend their pizza’s).
Room staff was also great, gave us extra coffee packages when we asked for them, and room was always clean when we got back from sightseeing.
The hotel rooms are small but clean and quiet. The Tassimo One Cup Coffee Makers in the rooms make great coffee, our room did not have a bath tub, which we would have liked, but there was nothing wrong with the shower. Our room was on the 11th floor and did not face the street; it was very quiet, with no street noise at all.
The breakfast is included in the room rate, buffet style, choice of cold cereal, scrambled eggs, sausage, oatmeal, bagels, toast, coffee, you get the idea, nothing to brag about but nothing wrong with it either.
The location and affordable price are two of the best reason to stay at this hotel, it like 6 blocks from everything!

title: “Too slow to warm up”
text:
We've gone back to visit our daughter and family a couple more times during the cold winter months and I'm afraid I need to revise my rating. In early November, we turned the heater on upon arriving at about 10pm but after about 30 minutes without noticeable change, we called the front desk. Their comment was that "it takes about an hour to warm up." We did at least notice the register getting warmer so put our coats on the bed and, by the time we woke up, the room - which was a double - was warm.
We were there again the next month - new grandbaby! - and wanted to try a King room. This time, as we were driving up at night from Oregon, when we were about an hour away we called and asked them to turn on the heat in our room. Which they did.
The register was a little warm when we got into the room but the King room was much larger to heat and had a large window along one wall. We again put coats on the bed, the room never really warmed up and my husband says he's felt cold ever since.
The rooms were still clean, the staff helpful and the rates very reasonable. HOWEVER, if you're there in the winter try staying in a smaller room and call ahead to get the heat turned on if you're arriving late.
There should at least be blankets in the rooms. And why couldn't they turn the heat on at a minimal temperature for the rooms that are rented?
This is still the only decent hotel in West Seattle, which is a great location to both the airport and downtown. Despite these experiences, we'll go back. I hope they'll continue to make improvements.

title: “Old and needs TLC, location great”
text: The location is great as the metro is downstairs. It's nice that it's easy to get back to the room. The lobby is okay, the restaurant is way overpriced but good. The room however is old, worn out looking. This hotel could be so much more if they would paint, clean, and get some new stuff. The tub shower curtain was moldy but replaced upon request. The rooms were musty. We stayed because of metro location and straight walk to Smithsonian. Next time will stay outside the city and metro in. There are not any restaurants nearby. Eat before you come back to your hotel room.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: The room was very clean, the staff was very helpful, the location of the hotel was great.

title: “Nice place if you're just passing through”
text: It was clean and comfortable. I did notice that the lotion bottle that was in the bathroom had been used by the previous visitors and not replaced with a good one. The breakfats was okay. The eggs had an artificial taste to them.

title: “In the Heart of Japan Town”
text: This well-appointed hotel is central to all business in the San Francisco area. Although the restaurants and room service are high priced, the accommodations are excellent.

title: “The Peabody is Memphis”
text: We stay at The Peabody 4 to 5 times a year. This is the premier Memphis Hotel. If you want to experience Memphis, instead of pretend you are somewhere other than the South, nothing compares. The staff is courteous and helpful, the lobby is truly one of the special hotel lobbies in America, for "doing" Memphis nightlife and then retiring to quiet there is no better location and the cookies on the executive floor are a temptation that can't be denied. We dread the day our son graduates from college and we don't have an excuse to be in Memphis at The Peabody.

title: “Central location, comfortable, clean and quiet.”
text:
My wife and I took our daughter to NYC this week for her birthday and we stayed in room 2504, a King Suite. The bedroom is pretty much filled by the King sized bed, but we didn't spend much time in the room anyway since we were there to explore the City with our daughter (her first visit to NYC), and to see "Wicked". The living room had a pull out sofa which is where our daughter slept, and that mattress really could use some added support. It was very soft and saggy, and we were fortunate each night to have tired her out walking around the City so that she was able to sleep without TOO many complaints. I even debated asking the maintenance guys for cardboard to lay between the mattress and the metal frame. The room was small, but more "cozy" than "cramped", and the three of us had no issues aside from the uncomfortable pull out sofa. There was the usual "college cube" mini-fridge (caution: it froze everything we put in it except for the OJ, and I could not find a temperature control), and in-room coffee, and everything was neat and clean. The bathroom was also tight but adequate, and had doors into both the bedroom, and living room. The shower head was very nice too.
The hotel's greatest asset is location. It's right on 7th and West 47th, right in the heart of Times Square and central to Broadway, food, bars and pubs, shopping, subways, taxis, and buses. Access is a little odd via elevators to the 3rd floor reception area, which also has the bell hop, concierge desk, and a small bar. From there, to the left of the desk, is a row of five elevators to the top floors. There's a restaurant called Ginger's on the fifth floor, but we did not dine onsite. We did sit at the bar one night after our daughter crashed, but found it a little short on variety, with the most basic of beer, and with a shallow selection of lower shelf liquor. With an ample supply of bars and restaurants nearby I would suggest looking offsite for libation. I have nothing bad to say about the hotel. The staff was friendly, and helpful. Check-in and check-out was quick and easy, and we were able to store our luggage there for four hours of exploring after we'd checked out. I've stayed across the street at the Crowne Plaza on both the 20th and 36th floors and was worried that we may hear street noise like I had before (on the 20th, not the 36th), but we heard nothing up on the 25th floor at the Doubletree. I would certainly consider staying at the Doubletree again if returning for a general tourist visit to NYC

title: “Underrated, To Say The Least.”
text:
My fiance and I stayed here while we were in Hollywood for auditions and I have to say I was pleasently surprised with this place. Check in was smooth, the room was nice and big and the property felt very safe over all. Some people on here have been saying that the area is seedy or scary- that is hardly the case. Of course sketchy characters are going to be out late at night- it is Hollywood after all, it's like the old saying goes "Nothing good happens after 10 o'clock at night". 
During the day you see the area for what it is, a working class neighborhood that is bustling and not even the slightest bit offputting to those who weren't born with a silver spoon in their mouth. The market across the street is nice with fair prices, just do yourself a favor and miss the Burger King located near by, try the excellent Subway a few blocks down the street. 
I never tried the pool but it was closed from the public and for the most part private. Breakfast was awesome and the dining area is quite nice with lots of large windows for prime people watching. 
Over all I would highly recommend this place- the only drawback to my entire stay was the firm bed- it was pretty uncomfortable but that is just me.

title: “Beautiful hotel, good price, great location”
text: One really could not ask for a better experience than what we had at the Hotel Monaco. Very friendly staff, nice wine hour, absolutely in the middle of everything in an historic old post office. Huge rooms with comfortable beds. I thought the restaurant's menu was a bit sparse and the dinner there was the least favorite part of our trip.

title: “Quiet, Convenient and a Good Value”
text: This is the 3rd time we stayed at the Crowne Plaza before going on a cruise -- and it won't be the last time. Check in was a breeze, the staff were courteous and the room was clean. We had a quiet and restful night. We booked the hotel's "park and sail" package, which included our room, complimentary buffet, shuttle to and from the cruise ship and FREE parking. All in all, another great experience at the San Pedro Crowne Plaza.

title: “Just OK”
text:
Best thing from the St Regis is its location. We stayed for a couple of days. Rooms however need a makeover. They are old and rusty. We never heard the butler service included in our suite. Impossible to get a cab. Bell boys were a total disaster.
For $1900 per night I will go somewhere else.

title: “Good location Holiday Inn at Beacon Hill”
text:
I recently spent 5 nights at the Holiday Inn Beacon Hill. The hotel is centrally located in Boston, within a block of the red line subway and at the base of historic Beacon Hill. From the airport I would use a cab or town car to reach the hotel, but it can also be accessed by public transit. The hotel is currently under renovation that is slated to continue through August 2012.
The staff was friendly and the hotel and rooms were clean but dated. During the day there seemed to be a lot of sirens from ambulances as there are many hospitals in the area, however at night it was much quieter. I would not recommend the breakfast buffet as it is $17.00. The buffet is basic and not worth the price.
On the positive side the hotel is located within easy walking distance of many fine dining and drinking establishments and excellent public transportation. There is a Whole Foods and CVS pharmacy located adjacent to the hotel. Overall I had a positive experience and would recommend this hotel and would stay there again.

title: “Our Choice Hotel!”
text: We travel to Charlotte approximately 8 to 10 weekends a year. These are 2 to 4 night getaways for my husband and I. We consistently stay at the Charlotte Marriott Center City. The staff has always been attentive to both our needs and wishes. The location is prime and centrally located to all the event sites we include in our stays. We love this town and all it has to offer. We would never choose to stay anywhere else!

title: “Very Surprised Good Hotel”
text: When in SF I usually stay at either the Marriott or Hilton. Both hotels just mentioned were booked and we ended up at the Serrano....I was prepared for the worst. Boy was I mistaken. Upon entering they have a very nicely done lobby...they were serving wine and beer free to the guest of the hotel...nice touch...also this is done daily from 5pm to 6pm. Check-in was routine and headed to my room on the 8th floor. I had a corner room. Upon entering it was clean and updated....not very big...but your in the wrong city if you plan on staying in your room too much...there is much to do in SF. The bathroom was clean and the shower head was at least 8ft up the wall.....I notice these things because I am a mid 6 footer.....and great water pressure by the way. I never ate in the hotel....too many great restaurants to go to. Be sure to eat at Dotties when in SF....it is just around the corner to your right....up 1 block on Jones street. Look at Trip Advisor comments about Dotties True Blue Cafe....its a great place to eat. When returning to SFO I will definitely keep the Serrano in mind.....very pleased with my stay.

title: “Great value and location”
text: I stayed at this hotel for three nights whild in the city for business. I've stayed at many hotels in the city and this one is solidly average. The lobby is modern and clean. The check in was easy and the staff was professional. I didnt have any problems with the elevators (any more than you will find in any NYC hotel). I thought that for the boutique size of the hotel the gym was really great. I did not have an updated room and while there were certainly things that could have been improved on and modernized, there was nothing that was particularly bothersome. While it didnt matter to me I noticed the TV was quite small compared to the standard these days. One thing to note, in my room electrical outlets were scarce which could be problematic. I was having to unplug lamps to blow dry my hair, clocks to charge my phone, etc. The only thing that I didnt like was internet could not be shared by multiple users in one room. The rate of $9.95 per day is only good for one device, even if you log off of the device and try to access from another, you have to have individualized access codes, and repay for the service for each sharing device you have. It was very easy to find a taxi and the central location was great. Would stay definitely stay again if I could find the same great rate.

title: “Best way to start a trip”
text: We stayed at Cedarbrook before a recent vacation as our plane left from SeaTac airport at 5am and staying near the airport was our best option. What a great place! They have a free airport shuttle available 24 hours a day and even have coffee waiting for you in the wee morning hours. The restaurant ond pub are terrific, the place is spotless and the free amenities are impressive. The communal living areas had everything you could need- bottled water, ice cream, yougurt, cheese etc. There are walking trails, beautiful grounds and a resort like atmosphere all at a very reasonable cost.

title: “Will never stay here again”
text: I have stayed in quite a few hotels, but this has been the worse by far. First of all, the rooms are tiny. The beds in our room seem to be sunken in the middle. The bathrooms are extremely small. A rather large individual would have a hard time trying to manuever in it. Also, the tiles in the bathroom had mold/mildew and there was a giant bug in there as well. The carpet in the hall was dirty and the walls were dirtier. The only positive thing I have to say is that it is in a good location. It is convenient to Times Square and Broadway. There is also a pizza parlor next door. I would recommend getting a slice. The food was good and the service at the pizza parlor was excellent.

title: “Close to subway lines”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel for a couple days in February 2011. We booked the hotel through Priceline.com for $90/night. Normally, the cost is over $200/night. 
The location is excellent! The hotel is within the Copley area, and is 1 block away from the Boston Public Library and the Copley T-Line. In addition, the hotel is really close to the Prudential Shopping Center.
I was able to check into the room before the check-in time. I didn't have to lug around my luggage all day.
Our room was good, but it was older looking. The bathroom had marble floors and granite countertop. The shower needed some work, especially with replacing the shower head and cleaning out the grout. The shower head was orange around the water holes. The bed and pillows were comfy. If this room was supposed to be over $200/night, I would feel ripped off since I expected higher quality.
Our room was close to the elevator, so it was a bit noisy. There was also construction either on the floor above or below us so that woke us up around 9am. During one of the early mornings (around 4am), someone must have pulled the emergency line since we woke up to a really loud intercom announcement that we may have to evaluate the building. Luckily we didn't have to evaluate in our pajamas.
BTW- No free wifi in the rooms. You can get wifi in the lobby.
I would consider staying here again due to the location. I'm sure that the hotel looks better now after the remodeling.

title: “Fantastic location and very comfotable bed.”
text: We spent tree nights in this hotel. Loved the location, literally opposite Central Park. The room was a reasonable size and the bed was very comfortable indeed with excellent pillows!

title: “Run the other way”
text:
We came for a business stay at this hotel in October of 2006. Brought along the family, and were booked into what the property called a 'family suite'. The suite was in actuality 2 small rooms with a bathroom in between. Hardwood floors (in a family suite, no less), and windows on the 4th floor that opened... with no screens. Exposed electrical plugs and lighting wired with extension cords, this was not family friendly.
The jacuzzi tub in the bathroom would have been a nice touch, if (#1) it had worked... and (#2) if it had been clean. There was hair both in the tub and a huge glob of green slimy hair in the drain, which had obviously been there a long time. When housekeeping was called to please clean the tub, they arrived and (since I had already cleaned the gob of hair out of the drain), they concentrated on cleaning the trash can that I'd thrown the hair into.
After explaining that I was more concerned with the bathtub it came out of, the person wiped the tub out with a towel. I gave up trying to explain basic housekeeping principles. The "ewww factor" was just too much.
The room was extremely noisy and not set up comfortably. For a family suite, there was no central area, just the two bedrooms. No significant table space to place food when ordering in, it was cramped and awkward.
When we booked the suite, we specifically asked about internet access at the hotel--a must have for business purposes, and we had several marketing seminars online that we were scheduled to attend, in order to make money. Internet service was one of the reasons we booked this hotel, it says it is available on the website, and both of us called the hotel at different times to confirm that it was available IN THE ROOMS throughout the hotel. We were assured that wireless internet access was available throughout the hotel and in the rooms.
It was not. We were not able to connect at all during our 3-day stay, either morning, evening or afternoon. At any place in the hotel. Several other patrons approached me as I was trying to get a connection at different places in the hotel with the same problem, they had also been promised internet access by staff and were unable to get it. Looking up old reviews on this hotel, this has been an ongoing complaint, which the staff repeatedly lies about, and when questioned about it, act clueless.
When checking out, we were told that a cart would be brought up to our room within 5-10 minutes. Two hours later, and half a dozen trips past the hotel's front desk to load our vehicle (which, by the way, was brought out by Valet Parking-- at $29/day, it was the only thing that was as promised). The cart never arrived.
If you are booked at this hotel, or considering it, run the other way. For $169/night, I expected a clean room, excellent service, and what I was promised and paid extra for. Instead, we were disappointed around every corner.

title: “Not Kimpton's best”
text: We always try to stay at Kimpton's and are always impressed by their staff and room style/cleanliness. The Serrano, although in a really good location, was a little disappointing. The staff were not particularly friendly and the room we had was looking a little tired. We were able to get a special rate when staying and it is just as well, as we would not have been happy paying the usual rate for the room quality and service received. It wasn't terrible, but just not on the usual Kimpton level.

title: “1 Star Hotel - Not worth the savings”
text: Musty, Old, rusted door frames, spots on walls (could be mold or mildew), roach ran across the BED! If that is how you keep your personal home then let me tell you....you are nasty. Do not kid yourself....This place is a dive!

title: “Anniversary”
text: This hotel is one of the nicest hotels I have ever stayed in. It was right off of Times Square. The bell men were awesome and had fun doing their jobs. It is on the pricey side but the price went down over $150 by the time I booked the room and the time we checked in. Everything you need or want is within walking distance. NY pizza is within walking distance no matter which way you go. This hotels has everything you need to have a great time in a great city. I am looking forward to going back.

title: “Nice Hotel!”
text:
I just returned from a 3 night weekend stay at the Holiday Inn Capitol. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay. The location is unbeatable. I was able to walk to the Smithsonians, Capitol and Librbay of Congress. The Metro is just a short block away. We had complimentary Starbucks every morning from the deli, a local amenity for Priority Club! Did not eat the restaurant, as we were all over the DC area, eating at ESPN Zone, the House cafeteria, Founding Famers, Clyde's and Mt. Vernon.
Rooms were very clean. Public areas clean. Elevators very speedy and uncrowded.
My only concern was with noise. Fridge in room was loud. A/C unit was very loud and kicked on often. I heard the trains very loudly as they blew whistles as they neared the station.
All in all, though, a very convenient, clean and joyful stay! I would stay here again anytime.

title: “Funky Boutique Hotel With Class Leading Service!”
text:
Everything has already been said numerous times however I can confirm that this hotel lives up to all the hype! Me & my wife celebrated her 30th birthday & the hotel staff could not have been more attentive. From the warm welcome given by John on Reception, to the free bottle of wine in the room, to the continued superb service from Sian-Pierre, absolutely first class! City View King Room definately worth the extra money & the free coffee, hot chocolate & wine were winning free touches. The only thing we could not work out was the duty & purpose of the doormen. They sometimes appeared too busy chatting up the local talent or standby around to notice people struggling with the front door with luggage etc. This was the only negative & struck us as strange as everything else was high end 
boutique so a big thank you to the 
staff & management for making our
 trip & my wife's 30th birthday such
 a memorable stay!

title: “Great Hotel for the Cotton Bowl”
text: My husband and I had a corner suite in the Tower on the 24th floor. The room was very large. We had a nice view and the suite was very clean. This is an extremely large hotel. My brother and sister-in-law stayed in the Atrium side and it was a long walk between the Atrium and the Tower. We were there for the Cotton Bowl and there were a ton of Razorback fans there. This is a good hotel for something like that. Overall, I would stay here again and hopefully will, if the Razorbacks go to the Cotton Bowl again soon. The executive lounge on the 25th floor is very nice and has complimentary continental breakfast.

title: “Not up to Westin standards”
text:
The usual challenges of a very big hotel (900 rooms). Elevator traffic, packed open spaces and lounge, a factory approach to service. 
Convenient location but doormen seemed nable an due interested in hailing cabs, much easier to do it yourself. Front desk team rude and confused. 
Room was big and clean, if a little dark. 
Paid top dollar for Westin room, got sub par Westin experience.

title: “Wonderful weekend in Boston”
text: Loved this place. My room was super clean and comfortable, with cool stuff like free wifi, ipod charger, flat screen TV and a very comfy bed. Loved the full length mirror when getting ready to go out! There's no AC in the room (well, I couldn't find it), and Boston does get humid, so plan to shower, etc. early or your room could get sauna-like. Helpful, friendly, knowledgeable staff with a sense of humor! Yummy coffee drinks in the lobby. The location is ideal, just a couple blocks from the T with many shops/eateries nearby. The Fritz, next door, has the coolest servers/bartenders and the best Bloody Mary you could ever dream of.

title: “Good location but that is about it”
text: I recently stayed at the Westin for several nights while in Chicago for business. This was my first time staying at a Westin in Chicago - I 've stayed at Westin's in other cities and have found them to be generally comfortable - not this one however. When I initially checked into my room there was a dirty wine glass on the floor outside of my room and a half consumed pepsi in the garbage can by the desk.Two out of the three days that I stayed at the hotel I had to go to the front desk and ask to have mini-bar charges removed from my bill for items that I did not consume. The bed was made up with a flat sheet on the bottom and the sheet was too short. The bottom 12 " of the bare mattress was exposed and not a very comfortable feeling when trying to sleep. The tub and toilet did not drain properly and my towel had a large rip in it.. Two of the three elevators were broken the second day of my stay. Not the best experience compared to other Starwood Hotels. I've stayed at many other hotels while in Chicago for previous business trips that seemed to take better care in guest comfort. I don't think I'll be staying at this hotel again.

title: “Wonderful Location, Amazing Staff, Pure Luxury...!”
text: This place is really something special! I do quite a bit of traveling and was definitely impressed by the spacious rooms, courteous staff and impressive amenities. Especially the gym---far and away one of the nicest fitness facilities I have seen! Whether in the area for business or to take in the sites, this hotel was so centrally located that it made getting anywhere in town such an ease. I would highly recommend this hotel and cannot wait to make a return trip!

title: “love that place”
text: I checked into hotel early on business. The desk agent was extremely nice and helpful. They were able to check me in early and took care of all of my needs. I ate dinner in the restaurant and food was fantastic! I will definitely stay here again if I am in town.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text:
After reading many negative comments about this hotel, I was nervous about going. I just want to say, my experience here was wonderful! The hotel is in a great location, wonderful staff, great complementary breakfast and internet & we never had to wait more than 2 minutes for an elevator. The room I booked was the Terrace Studio and it was very small because it was the last one available, but we were offered a bigger room, but declined because we wanted the balcony/terrace. They have the best tasting water in the lobby with grapefruit and lime!
I would definitely go back!

title: “Ratz Milner”
text: I was dismayed when we drove up--no one to help us with baggage, and we practically stepped over panhandlers to get to the entrance. Both baggage carts were dirty and falling apart--I had to fix one myself to make it usable. The suite? The bed's so close to the doorway, I was surprised it passed the fire code. Couldn't get a suitcase to roll past it into the rest of the room with lots of wasted space. Bad space planning. The bed was hard but decent, sheets and bedding seemed clean, and the DSL worked ok. We got only one threadbare washcloth, 2 older bath towels, 2 hand towels. for 1 1/4 baths. When we ordered more towels, we had to ask several times! Shower ok, no great shakes. No ice machine on 3rd floor, and no fridge in suite. The carpeting creeped me out, making me glad I had brought slippers. The "closet" wasn't enough for 2 people for 3 days--why not bigger in a suite? Everything I touched had a tackiness to it--elevator, handles, etc. My key card malfunctioned several times. Free breakfast: Had to run downstairs early to get yogurt or they'd run out; all else was cheap carbs, and the toaster didn't work. Had to eat my bagel cold after toasting it 10 minutes. IHOP's a far better choice. Hotel is close to Chase/Macy's, Staples Center, Nokia Ctr., and cheap parking garages. My advice: Stay at the Sheraton, and park in the cheap garage, and it will come out about right. This place isn't ready for prime time. We joked that maybe they misspelled the name: should be Rats Milner!

title: “Superb location, hotel staff very friendly, would fully recommend”
text:
Our first visit to NYC. Stayed during Hurricane Irene (unfortunately!). Room quiet and had view of Empire state building. (ask for room in back of hotel - front of hotel will give you view of street - not much to look at)
Well cleaned (cleaned daily) and well looked after (bathrooms could be a little more up to date but still in good condition).
Hotel staff very friendly and helpful. Would go out of way to help you.
Free wifi which was much appreciated as we were able to keep an eye on the flight situation during the hurricane.
Breakfast is continental so you know what to expect but has good choice.
Dinner in restaraunt is good value (no more expensive than eating in Times square)
Very centrally located to all attractions (1 block from Empire state (1min walk), 5mins walk to Times square & Broadway, 5~7mins walk from grand central station, library, rockefeller centre. Central park / 5th avenue approx 10~15min walk. Liberty Island/Wall street/Ground zero located in lower manhattan and is approx 1.5hrs walk (3miles). 
Felt very safe in area.
Would 100% recommend and will go back!

title: “Charming, luxurious and perfectly located”
text: Three night stay at the Chicago Intercontinental for New Years Eve. We were given a large room on a high floor. Elevators are very fast. $161/night which by city standards is very reasonable. Two buildings; the historic building which was a mens' club in the 20s and has been restored magnificently, and the newer tower. Staff attentive and helpful. Location could not be better. I had health club, and internet for free with platinum status.

title: “A Surprisingly Nice Hotel”
text: A lower priced hotel but very clean with microwave and fridge, two heated pools and hot tub and nice helpful professional staff made our trip go well since we were forced to stay overnight due to high winds along the highway home. It was also great that they allow dogs and this was a great selling point for us but the fact that it was so clean and relatively quiet was excellent.

title: “I can't believe what the previous person said!!!!”
text: I checked into this hotel on 8/12/12 and I would have to say this was by far the worst hotel experience I have ever had. While I understand that the hotel may not be able to do a lot about the age and condition, certain things are without question reasonable. My room was unbearably hot as there is no control in the room it is monitored centrally from the front desk (yes - all guest must have the same setting). Continental breakfast was TOAST, TOAST, and oh yeah TOAST. The room smelled bad, the floors sunk in and I could go on and on. I would suggest to anyone to pay a little extra and choose another hotel for your stay.

title: “overnight stay”
text: The room was clean but did have an odor when we arrived. We opened the window and it seemed to help.

title: “great time with friends at the Warwick...thank you Joanna!”
text: I was travelling with a group of 4 friends and had an excellent stay, all the more better because of Joanna at front desk. Her personnal attention to our needs and very professionnal manners were enjoyed by all. Thank you again for everything! The rooms were very nice and confortable and Joanna even accomodated us in adjacent rooms that could communicate with each other. Location of this hotel is perfect and the level of service was impeccable. Would definitely stay there again without hesitation.

title: “Great value, great location, great service, great hotel”
text: I have just returned from a US holiday travelling on my own. I spent 4 nights at this hotel. I chose this hotel as it was only a short distance from SeaWorld, the zoo, Old Town San Diego and shopping malls. I didn't have a car but the hotel had a courtesy bus to drive to me SeaWorld and the zoo and to and from the airport. The room was very clean and comfortable. Pay tv to watch at end of a long day. Free internet in the reception lounge area. The reception staff were very friendly and helpful organising day tours and giving directions to eat by car or by foot. Onsite is a reasonably priced family restaurant "Pam Pam Cafe and Grill". At end of long day, very convenient. I was given a complimentary breakfast voucher for each day of my stay. Only downside, was my room was near a stairwell, so heard a bit of foot traffic. Definitely recommend this hotel and will definitely be going back.

title: “Clean and Comfortable....Great Bargain!”
text: Having never been to NYC before, I wasn't expecting alot from this hotel for the price. I was pleasantly surprised! The location looked a little funky, but once inside, the front desk staff was courteous and friendly and the lobby was clean and cheerful. Once in our room, it was small, but clean with a comfortable bed. We felt very safe there and had a excellent experience! I would stay there again for sure!

title: “Good location, bad on cleanliness”
text: I stayed here for work recently and this Courtyard doesn't exactly match up to other Courtyard. The key machine was broken when I checked in so there was a 10 minute wait since they had to go next door to the Residence Inn. The carpet in my room was not clean and there were sunflower seed shells (obviously not vacuumed). Glasses in the room were dirty and had imprints on the rim so they were not sanitized like they claimed. Overall, I had problem with the cleanliness of the room and felt that for around $200/night, the room did not match up to the standards set by the price.

title: “Sometimes your better off going for an old fashioned hotel.”
text:
After staying at the Fairmont Copley I decided to give this new modern Fairmont a chance. I have only ever stayed at Fairmonts older properties in Canada and the States, so I thought id get a more modern version of there signature style and service. 
I was very much mistaken. Guess this proves that new does not mean better.
Yes superficially this is ultra sleek and new hotel looks promising but as soon as I made my way to check-in the bubble burst. I came in the morning and being booked into the gold floor I asked the bellman where to go, the answer the checkin desk, after queuing for 15 minutes with luggage in hand I was told that the gold floor was a separate building. Without even an offer to help transfer my bags I was told to proceed diagonally across the square to check in there. Upon arriving (still with luggage) there door would not open, and there wasn't even so much as a 'ring for assistance' button or phone. Not starting out so well. 
After finally receiving help from a very nice receptionist I finally made it to my room. 
The rest of the stay was uneventful. The building and rooms were nice with a very residential feel to them. Modern decor and amenities, especially compared to the Fairmont I know. 
Despite the young age and look to the hotel everything seemed to be well worn, wall paper scratched and paint that was chipping away covered up with paint (though not quite the same colour.)
There restaurant onsite is a real treat. Italian food meets boston american, chowder and truffle pasta on the same menu. It was very nice and service was A1, for North America. Sat at the chefs counter (bar style seating on the hotplate, so you can observe the chefs team preparing orders). There executive chef was even so nice as to show me the way (personally) to the toilets. Only slight criticism maybe is that there portions were HUGE.
Checkout had to have been the strangest I ever experienced. I presented my self downstairs and couldn't find a soul in sight. Finally when I saw what appeared to be a staff member (wearing a sweatshirt) I asked if I could check out, she said its all been sorted and told me to go across to catch a taxi, if I needed it.
From check in to check out the hotel seems to be (besides the restaurant) run by staff that have no idea what customer service is supposed to be in a 5 star hotel, certainly not what I expect from Fairmont. I think I'll stick to there older properties with staff that know how to properly treat guests.

title: “If its a great location that your looking for!”
text: Stayed at the Herald Sqaure in Jan 2003.We were slightly disappointed when we arrived.The web site was a bit generous in its description.The location was excellent to say the least.The fact that there is no comfortable reception are makes it feel a bit cold on arrival.The rooms were verging on tiny.They were clean & very warm however.Would pass on the name of hotel to friends , but would be very clear on what they can expect.Others might not have been as complacent. Location is 5 star , hotel is debatable!

title: “Sad stay!”
text:
I wish I could like this stay but I find it hard to convince myself to do so...everything from check in to room condition, air-conditioning to concierge to check out was disappointing....
I am here only because my conference is here...
PS: be careful to check your bill when you check out. The mini bar systems is cranky.

title: “Christmas Vacation”
text: My family stayed at the St. Gregory over the Christmas and New Year holidays. The hotel was very nice. The staff was very helpful and kind. We had a few issues with the people next door who had a small baby who cried all night. But that had more to do with thin walls, than the hotel or staff. The baby left after the first night and all was well. I love Washington D.C. and if I get a chance to come back I would to stay at the St. Gregory.

title: “Small, friendly and a great location”
text: I do like this hotel (I have stayed there 4 times), but the guest rooms are small. The location is perfect, just off Times Square, in the theater district, close to lots of restaurants, and near to everything Midtown. It is a short walk to the subway and the doorman will happily grab you a cab. The staff is very friendly and the connected restaurant is okay in a pinch. The only real drawback is the small rooms. Maybe I have been unlucky on 4 different stays, but I like a little more space in the City. I stayed there on business, and probably will again, as the prices are usually very competative and you can't beat the location.

title: “Not impressed, very rude front desk staff Milena”
text:
The hotel was what I expected it would be for the price and was fine for one night, knowing I was moving on to something nicer the next night. The reviews are right, you don't really want to walk around this neighborhood. Use it just for a place to lay your head. I was in room 212 and it was very spacious. There was a safe and a large vanity area for getting ready that was separate from the shower and toilet. This was convenient as we were 4 girls sharing a room.
Before booking, I called the hotel and spoke with Wes and inquired as to pricing for four people with two double beds. I also asked about pricing for a roll away cot and I was told there was no charge. I told Wes that the room was less if I booked on line so, so he said that I should do that and then call back with my reservation number to book a roll away. This is what I did. When I arrived, Milena, the front desk person told me that there was a $20 charge for the roll away and a $20 charge for each extra person over 2. When I said that this is not what I was told and I gave her the name of Wes who I had spoken to, her response was "I don't know what he told you but this is what you have to pay , I just work here." When I said that I wasn't happy about it, she suggested that perhaps I would like to find another place to go. In the end, for the price of this hotel, I would have been happy to pay a little more and have a nice place to stay. Suddenly a $70 room was $130. 
When I unrolled my roll away bed that evening, the bedding was unclean. I sent it back and shared a bed with my friend. The next morning when I checked out Milena said "I see you complained again" When I told her that the reason for my complaint was the dirty sheets, she told me that no one else had ever complained and she was still going to charge me for the bed. I asked to speak with the manager but again, as before, he was not around. I still intend to let the manager know of my disappointment but I think he might already know as Milena told me that it was the managements decision to be charging me. It was unbelievable to me that she would be so rude, her manner was condescending and I found it laughable that she had a tip jar at the front with her name on it. If you do book here, do so with a booking company that will allow you refunds. I had booked for a second night at the end of my trip and wished that I had been able to get a refund. The last night I was there I was put into a smoking room and even though there were other available rooms, the front desk person Anthony would not put me in another room because the computer had booked me into a smoking room. Anthony was friendly but he didn't know he was doing. Getting a room switched has never been a problem anywhere else, not sure why it was a problem here.

title: “Average at best”
text:
The hotel is beautiful to look at, the main enterance is truely a work of art. The service was probably the best we have ever had at any hotel. And the food was delicious. 
Now on the cons side, we had to order a coffee maker to our rooms. I have never stayed at a hotel with out a coffee maker before and I travel monthly if not more. Our bed was horrible, it was stiff and you could feel springs sticking through. The robes were one size fits all except men. The food was very much over priced even if it was amazing. The $75 breakfast we had in our room was so bad we threw 3/4 of it out and went out to find something better to eat. 
Would not recommend this hoted to anyone, consider the Westin, or Four Points or any other location. You pay to much to reveice this little. We like higher end hotels and this was the worst we have ever had at close to the most we have ever paid.

title: “One of the best hotels we have stayed in!”
text: My husband and I traveled to Scottsdale over the three day weekend in February. We chose this hotel based off the great reviews on tripadvisor. The hotel is absolutely beautiful and the staff is wonderful! We have stayed in many top hotels with the four seasons being our favorite -- The Royal Palms Resort is just as good! I got a massage at the spa and it was wonderful! The spa is gorgeous and there are so many amenities it was hard to chose where to relax. I would definitely recommend staying here. There is a $28 a day "resort fee" but since we rented a car and were in and out of the hotel it was well worth the price as you do not have to tip the staff (although they deserved extra!)

title: “We loved our stay at this Sheraton”
text:
This Sheraton is not in the main area of San Diego where the ball park or Gas Lamp is, but a short 5- 10 minute walk will get you there. The rooms are beautiful, as are the views. The hotel bar is adequate, and the business center was so easy to use to print out my boarding pass. I have no complaints about the staff. 
If you need a cab to the airport though, make sure you leave yourself a little time. I was told to call 5 minutes before I came down and they would have one waiting (which I did), but then it was about a ten minute wait with the concierge trying to flag one down in the street. Probably a miscommunication, but just bear that in mind when you have to catch a flight, because it is not in a busy area where they are going by all the time

title: “This is a solid airport hotel”
text: I stayed here one night, so I didn’t get to use a lot of the amenities, but got a good feel for the hotel, overall. The hotel is newer, so you can extrapolate what you like from that statement (I prefer new hotels). The service was very good for me, so I would rate that well. The bathroom looked good, which is important for me. I had a nice room with a lot of space, so I assume that it was a suite, because I am a Diamond VIP. But a smaller version of the room would be nice as well. The hotel is not near the city, but it is near a nice shopping area, so there are a lot of choices for food, but only a Zaxby’s (fast food chicken sandwich-type place) within walking distance. I will definitely use this hotel again when I have to fly through the Jacksonville airport.

title: “Mediocre at best”
text: Location is perfect yes. It is just across the farmers market and the Grove which is perfect for eating and entertaining. They have a restaurant which is lovely and the people are very friendly and nice. Good with the kids. I choose the hotel because my husband had a business meeting and they had a pool so the kids could enjoy it but it was no good for my 4 year old as it was too deep even where it said 3 feet and the pool was tiny. Also it was very slippery around the pool even when it wasn't wet. The double room only had double beds available which was too small and creaked everytime we moved but the beds themselves were very comfortable. Overall it was very motel like and for the price you could get better hotels although not in that location. It served well as we arrived in one car and my husband had to take it to his meeting and I could take the kids to the farmers market while he was out and he says he'll use it again for business as it is close to the studios but I would look for a different place if I had to go with him again

title: “Best hotel experience we've had in years.”
text:
Friendly. Comfortable. Quiet. Classy. Are there enough positive adjectives available to give the Hotel Monaco its due?
 Located just off the middle of the 16th Street Mall, this hotel proved to be central to everything. The selection of shops, restaurants, and entertainment -- all within easy walking distance -- was incredible. Long-time Colorado residents, my wife and I were nevertheless amazed by our downtown Denver weekend experience.
Even setting aside its terrific location, the Hotel Monaco was still the best hotel experience we've had in years. The staff was friendly, courteous, and always in good humor. We took full advantage of the complimentary wine and hors d'oeuvres offered in the hotel lobby each evening, and the dining at Panzano was delicious. The room was small, but comfortable and quiet. The rooms with queen beds may be only 300 s.f., but if this is too small for your party, a minor price upgrade to a king bed grants an additional 75 s.f. and ample room room for two. The room was attractively furnished and the bed was comfortable. Noise from the busy street below was almost nonexistent from our 5th floor room.
We couldn't have asked for a better hotel to stay in, and will be actively seeking out Kimpton hotels when making our future travel plans!

title: “We would expect more from this kind of hotel”
text:
Reception personnel was freindly and welcoming.
Rooms need an uplift but beds are comfortable.
Breakfast destroyed all our expectations. There was a hygiene issue. The meat served was cold and i got sick from it ( gastro-enteritis ). There was a tray with dried scrambled eggs that had remained open. A bag with bread inside was just lying around between the food trays. It was not clean. The waiter working that day was not friendly.
So, stay in that hotel for a sleep, but do not take breakfast there and go to another more fancy place.

title: “Baltimore with friends”
text: From the minute we pulled up to the hotel to the minute we left the staff and hotel exceeded our expectations! They were friendly and helpful with anything and everything! Our room was clean, comfortable and well taken care of, the bar was relaxing and the dining room has a GREAT buffet breakfast with eggs made to order that we thoroughly enjoyed! If you stay in Baltimore this is where you need to be..its sooo close to everything there is no need for a car and the PERFECT place to stay if you want to see an Orioles game or a Ravens game!! I'll definitely will be back to this great hotel!!

title: “Not so Impressed”
text:
We used Priceline and got a great deal on the Westin River North over a long weekend in August. For the price, I really have no complaints. But, for a Westin, I expected better. We are Starwood Members and have stayed at many of the Starwood properties and this one did not feel up to par. 
I called and requested a King size bed, river view, a fridge in our room, and a crib as we were traveling with our 2 year old. I was told no problem on any of this. When we got to the hotel we had to wait a LONG time to check in. There was a very long line and only two people working the desk, and one of them was only assisting Starwood Gold members. They gave us our room and we went upstairs. We DID get a King size bed, but there was no riverview, no fridge and no crib in the room. On our way out we stopped by the desk and asked for the crib and the fridge and we were told they would be brought right up. 
We went out to visit with friends and go back four hours later and there was still no crib in our room. At this point we had a cranky toddler who needed to sleep! I called and requested the crib AGAIN and finally they brought it to us. I don't understand why I had to request the crib three times! We did end up getting the fridge also.
Other than that, we had no other issues with the hotel except that we just didn't feel like guests at a Starwood. We are used to friendly staff and people going out of their way to make your stay more comfortable and we didn't get that impression here. It seems like there was a lot going on at the hotel that weekend- at least two weddings were happening on Saturday night- and the staff seemed preoccupied. 
For the price, we got a great deal on a nice hotel. But to be honest, I always expect more out of a Starwood property and I just didn't get that feeling at this hotel.
Also, we were VERY surprised that this property has no pool!

title: “A bit tired in places”
text:
We spent 6 nights at the Alex in a studio. Very compact but well appointed. The bathroom was a little small as the door had to be opened right back in order to negogiate the toilet. The shower was a very good rainfall shower. The towels were a little tired and threadbare in places, but they were big enough to wrap round you all the way. The prices in the restaurant and room service seemed high so we didn't eat there at all.
Everyone was very helpful although there was sometimes a long wait for the lift to the lobby first thing in the morning.
Was in a good location and would recommend a stay there.

title: “Palacio del Rio with a view”
text:
We stayed here last weekend and requested a room facing riverwalk but did not get it. We got a room on 10th floor facing the Hemisphere tower. Turned out to be a nice room and the view was good. We were not disappointed with the room, very clean and updated. Shopping at the Rivercity mall was good, but shopping at the Market Square was better. My lady enjoyed the Market square and took a few items home.
Self parking wasnt so bad and the walk was not so bad to get the vehicle, only set back was driving my truck up to the hotel to unload and load luggage. There is not enough space there to drive many vehicles up to the front to load and unload people or lugage. Recommend for anyone to just get in and out of there as fast as you can not to take up space ther waiting so long. Be prepared to get in and out and go park or where ever you are going to. I think it would be much smoother operation if people are aware and keep this in mind about driving up to the front of Hotel. Otherwise you will be fustrated trying to get in.
But over all the Hotel is nice, though we ate at different places and not at the hotel so I cannot tell you what the service is like there. We would stay there again though.

title: “What a Great Find!”
text:
I have stayed in Seattle many times, in the Lake Union Area, downtown and near the WA Convention Centre. This was my 1st experience in in UW area. I have to tell you that I have never had a better experiece and thoughtful, caring service than at the Watertown. This is a modern, clean hotel that has really remembered that customer serive is what it is about. If you have business with UW and especially the UW Medical Center, this is the place. I strongly reccomend it!
Ronn Patton
CSU East Bay

title: “Funky Boutique Hotel”
text: This hotel is in a great location near Dupont Circle, lots of restaurants & shops close by. The service at the Topaz is unbelivable, the staff are caring & they go out of there way to make your stay memorable. We were upgraded to a beautiful yoga room for our 30th Wedding Anniversary. I would definitely stay at the Topaz when visiting DC in the future.

title: “excellent hotel stay for $79 on Priceline! what a deal.....”
text:
We stayed overnight in Seattle after a spring cruise up the coast and wanted a hotel that we could walk to everything, do a little sightseeing and find some good restaurants. We like boutique type hotels, (Love Kimptons) and were looking at the nice variety of those in Seattle. Decided to do some bidding on Priceline and ended up here.
The hotel's location is wonderful. Very close to everything. Lot's of wonderful shopping around. a few blocks up from Pike's Place Market where we took the food tour from Savor Seattle which was fun. 
The Hotel is clean, the lobby spacious and well decorated, large and spacious. Big couches, fire place, big easy chairs and free wi-fi.
There is a pool and jacuzzi on the 35th floor. Indoor. The gym is also up there. Very nice.
Try priceline for a great deal!

title: “European grandeur in San Diego”
text:
I was quite impressed with the Westgate. It was like staying in a European Palace. The rooms were large with fabulous bedding and linens. The location was very convenient. I was at a conference and chose to stay at the Westgate rather than the Wyndham Emerald Plaza, due to the reviews on this site. I made a perfect choice. 
I was very surprised to see how empty the town was overall. I guess I expected a bustling typical city "scene". Not the case. The area was almost desolate at night. Horton Plaza is right across the street. I am not accustomed to the outdoor mall so I was not very impressed. It was nice to browse Nordstrom, however.
The restaurant scene in the Gaslamp area was amazing. I had gourmet Italian every night. The waterfront is about a 10 minute walk, although I did not understand the attraction. Seaport Village is a small tourist trap on the water.
The things the Westgate can do better are: more consistent water temperature in the shower, a doorman present at all times at the main entrance, the business center is weak, and the exercise room is a little depressing.
Overall, the Westgate Hotel was the highlight of my trip to San Diego. The concierge was very helpful regarding restaurants and information, and Stephan, at the front desk, was always ready to help, knowing my name from day one. He was always at the ready to help in retreiving the elevator when he saw me walk in the main door, etc. 
For a really special experience stay at the Westgate. You will not be disappointed.

title: “Suspected Bed Bugs”
text: After I checked in and noticed the area (bad) and the high security fence around the property. Not usually a good sign. Another unfortuante problem was a bus load of HS kids took over the hotel with little or no supervision from parents. They wrestled, hung out in the hallway and generally made noise past midnight. For a busienss traveler, that is a problem as I need some sleep. The next morning I had a few itchy spots that I originally attributed to mosquito bites. The strange part was that all the bites were head, arm and waist, nothing below the belt line. I had 50 in all and finally called the hotel to let them know that the bites looked more like bed bugs, from photos I picked up on-line. They called back a few days later telling me that Orkin came in and claimed there was no bed bug activity. She sent me the Orkin report and it shows that the Orkin inspector spent 10 minutes in the room. That doesn't sound like enough time to thoroughly inspect a room suspected of having bed bugs. I only had slept in my own bed the eveninges previous, so the story doesn't really hold water.

title: “Happy I did my homework- satisfied.”
text: I took plenty of time to surf the Internet for hotels in the DC area. Many hotels I searched were booked or too expensive for my budget. I ended up booking the hotel through the 1800 reservation line. The operator was rather pushy to book the room at the first rate given to me (ie 179 and 280 respectively for my 2 night stay- after about 3 different rates and offers I was finally quoted 179 promo rate for each night. Compared to other hotels rates I was satisfied and booked it. I chose for the rate, hotel pickup for Old Town Trolley, and location to the Smithsonian Air Museum- a short 2 blocks walk away. Yes it is in the business district which does shut down early and can feel a bit deserted - but I was fine with that. CVS , smaller food businesses , quiznos, McDonald's and Starbucks are all a short walk right in the same block on C Street! I was aware of limited food options so no surprises for me. Less traffic down C and 6th, less pedestrians. It was actually quite nice! Yes the rooftop pool is on the small size and only 4 1/2 feet deep. Life guard was on duty supervising each time we went. Room was clean and a convenient size for 2 doubles- roll away bed fit fine. Refrigerator cold! AC cold!bathroom had a nice long vanity counter- plenty of towels! Did my homework and requested room away from the train side and Nicole accommodated us!! Court yard downstairs was a pleasant for being in a big city. Ordered take out wings from the Bistro and they rocked!! The little Deli prices were not that high at all!!! Doughnut 1.00 muffin 1.25.... All staff I greeted especially at the front desk and housekeeping , the bistro, pool, were friendly. I did not like the fact that it appeared the in room microwave was removed from atop the refridge and when we inquired were told it was 10 dollars to get a microwave brought to the room. Also did not like missing the Old Town Trolley shuttle pickup for our nighttime monument tour - paid 11.50 for 4 for a cab to Union Station. Realized the next day by happenstance that it picks up at hotel 6 st side and not at C as I would have expected. Overall pleased with my stay- I did my homework and was happy knowing about the hotel and area before I got there. For those reviews that seem to complain about the lack of food choices , well the metro is only a couple blocks away! Thanks for reading this lengthy review!

title: “Wonderful!”
text: Walter, Walter, Walter! He greeted us wonderfully and upgraded us to a larger room because of our three kids. He took the time to give our kids paper airplanes and showed them how to throw them across floors without hitting the chandeliers. The only part of our stay that was disappointing was that valet parking lost our car keys but they found them within 45 minutes. The location was great all within walking distance. Rooms were clean and quiet. We only stay at Marriott properties and this was by far the best service imaginable!

title: “Worst I've Experienced”
text: The lobby was nice. The first room I was given was 115. It smelled terrible, the bed had a dirty bedspread and no pillow. There were no towels, no hangers, no phone and the floor was disgusting. I brought the receptionist to my room who apologized profusely, and I was moved to another room 328. It didn't smell as bad and had towels but was still awful. The floor and rug were so horrible I kept my shoes on to walk on it. The wind whistled eerily through the door all night. I couldn't bring myself to shower there. I've stayed at other Suburban Extended Stay hotels and the rooms were cheap and clean and for the most part in good repair. I think this hotel needs to be condemned, Based on other reviews it sounds like they might have some ok rooms but I would never recommend this hotel based on my experience.

title: “Good hotel, but too expensive”
text: I loved my stay in New York, the hotel is very well located, very beautiful. But it is too expensive, the room is small, it does not have breakfast, and we have to pay for the internet!! If this hotel was not that expensive i would come back there certainly!

title: “Harold’s Square, Manhattan - This is a find!!”
text: For this stay in NYC, we picked the Radisson Martinique on Broadway, which is located in Harold’s Square (about one block from Macy’s). Excellent location!! There is a Subway stop right outside the hotel. Super convenient to everything either by foot or subway. Also, Penn Station is only a couple of blocks away. We were pleasantly surprised by both the location of the hotel and the hotel itself. Hotel staff was friendly & accommodating. Room was larger than expected, super clean, and had everything we needed to keep us comfortable for our six night stay. By the end of the trip, we felt like we lived there! Free wi-fi is available in your hotel room. There is also a business center that’s easily accessible with a super fast internet connection and access to a printer. Last year, we stayed in the heart of Times Square which we enjoyed but decided to stay a few blocks away this year. Still in Midtown Manhattan. This location was just easier to get in and out of your hotel. A little less touristy. And still convenient to everything! Highly recommend this hotel and this location and would definitely stay here again! It was such a great find & we could not have been any more pleased!

title: “Great value, fabulous location”
text: Just returned from a trip to DC, would stay again at The River Inn, the room was comfortable, and staff were attentive. Sure the wallpaper was a but bumpy and the carpet a bit lumpy, but all was clean and comfy, and considering it was about half the price of surrounding Hotels and in a quiet neighborhood, we couldn't be happier. DC seems to be cheapest on Friday and Saturday nights, we paid $99. plus tax & parking, Sunday was a little more at $129. plus tax & parking, we booked online through a website. The Metro Line is close, as is the Yellow Line tour bus stops just a 1/2 block away! Georgetown shopping and restaurants just a few blocks (3), close enough to walk, but far enough to sleep away from the traffic. The rooms have fridges & microwaves, so if you have restaurant leftovers you don't have to waste them. We did not use the Hotel restaurant since we made a simple breakfast in the room and were out touring at lunch and dinner.

title: “Only there for one night, but a great airport hotel”
text: We stayed here on our way home from Alaska so that we could easily get to the airport the next morning. It's less than 5 minutes away from Sea-Tac and transportation to and from is quick and easy. We were also surprised to find that you can catch an express shuttle from the hotel to downtown, which makes it very convenient to do some quick site-seeing. Upon returning from seeing a few sites, the lobby, restaurant, and pool were bustling with activity! The pool is very large and in a beautiful atrium area. The bar and restaurant also looked nice, although we didn't eat there. We did, however, get room service and the menu was pretty extensive. Not to mention the food was good and the service was quick. The rooms are very comfortable, particularly the beds. We didn't encounter any problems at all.

title: “BRAVO!!”
text: Worth every penny...you name it..convenience, polite staff, impeccable room, prompt shuttle TO and FRO!!...Bravo Hyatt Regency DFW keep up the good work...........Thanks

title: “Austin trip”
text: The room was ok seemed like I paid a lot for what I got. We did not have reservations so it was hard to find a room. Next time I go to Austin I would make advance reservations and find a better deal.

title: “Good experience”
text: The only suggestion I have to make for improvement is training the front desk staff to activate the telephones in the room for long distance. So far I am 2 for 2 for Ramada front desk staff who have no clue hoe to activate the phones. I ended up having to make an international phone call on my cel.

title: “Great location”
text: The Omni is located right in the middle of Michigan Avenue in the middle of all the action. Rooms are great, all suites. Nice big bathrooms, good linens and products. Staff there very nice and helpful. They have a breakfast buffet and a bar but I never checked it out. Also, nice workout facility and indoor pool. You are walking distance to everything in Chicago. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “bad service”
text:
When we arrived in NY at 9:00 we checked our bags at the counter and told them we'd be back at 3:00 for check-in time. When we got back, we were told that we had been bumped. We had booked the hotel 4 months in advance and booked all theater tickets and dinner reservations based on this hotel location. They moved us 10 blocks south to another hotel that was shabby, unclean and out of the way (the Pennsylvania). By the time we got all the way down to the other hotel and waited in another line to check in, we missed our reservations for that night. The Econo Lodge staff was unhelpful, unapologetic, and uncaring. Had we been told at 9:00am that we were bumped, we could have made arrangements to find a better location and made our dinner and theatre reservations,
Don't let them do it to you.

title: “SOFITEL NEW YORK TAKES ON IRENE”
text:
I have stayed at Sofitel numerous times in the past and have written reviews about the wonderful rooms and phenomenal Staff. 
I recently visited NYC with some friends to see a show and to have a dinner at Benjamin Steakhouse on E 41st Street. All three of us were also celebrating birthdays in September so that was our excuse to go. 
Little did we know heading into the City from Ohio that we would be there to witness history with Hurricane Irene visiting at the same time. 
The entire Staff and Management were completely up to date with all of the latest news on the location of the Hurricane and all of the precautions guests needed to take. A letter from the General Manager was placed in all of the rooms detailing what would happen if Irene took a direct hit on the City and where guests could go (2nd floor ballroom area).
Coming and going from the hotel the management team, including the head of security, always had a presence in public areas to help answer guest’s questions. With the lower part of Manhattan and the mass transit closing in the afternoon on Saturday Staff members were assisting guests with how to get around town. They were also helping guests chose alternate destinations for dinners and entertainment. 
I have always found Sofitel a comfortable place to stay and have always appreciated the fact that the property is small enough for the staff to get to know you. This last trip also helps prove how concerned they are with the safety of their guests. 
Sofitel truly stepped up during what could have been a bad situation and was ready, another sign that this is THE hotel to book when going to NYC. 
The dinner at Benjamin Steakhouse was also perfect – as always.

title: “What a Delight!”
text: After a long leisurely day of exploring winding roads through the New England mountains and then sluicing the final stretch into Boston for the night with no reservations, we were dismayed at the lack of availability and costliness of accommodation as night fell. What a relief it was to find a friendly reception from the staff at The Inn @ St. Botolph - and what a delight! The accommodations were were not "just" luxurious and tasteful , but cutting edge chic apartments. This boutique hotel is a true treasure set on a residential boulevard in a red brick former manse, a stone's throw from the heart of Boston and all its attractions. It was a discovery beyond our expectations - a gem worth re-visiting.

title: “The Most Comfortable Beds Ever!”
text:
Reading other reviews always leaves me wondering which ones will reflect my expereience most accurately.
I have to say that our time at this hotel was very positive. Firstly the location is perfect, just far enough away from the busiest areas to be restful yet close enough to be able to walk to the main sites, subways shops etc. comfortably.
The hotel itself is elegantly renovated and the public areas offer a restful relaxed comfort, with cool refreshments in the reception area (great in the heat of the summer)and the rooms themselves are spacious well decorated and with the most sensationally comfortable beds and pillows.
The bathroom had a large wet room type shower and beautiful complementary toiletries which were replenished daily.
A very pleasant bolt hole away from the frantic busyness of the city.
All the reception staff, concierge, doormen and house keepers were very pleasant and very helpful whenever we had questions or requests.
The roof top bar has a spectacular view at night of the Empire State building and the Chrysler building but the price of the drinks did not allow us to use it more than once sadly. Similarly the Rare Bar ang Grill offered very good food and was very busy every night but again the cost of drinks was very high. Breakfast on the other hand was excellant and a reasonable price.
I think like many others that in todays cyber society wifi should be free or at least only a nominal cost but this is not the case here and as we were not willing to pay $13 + per day for use of the internet we were unable to access local information etc for ourselves.
That would be the only negative that I could point to.
All in all our visit was memorable and one I would like to repeat.

title: “Great place”
text: I recently stayed at the Crown Plaza and found the hotel excellent. The rooms are large and the comforter and pillows are great. I would definitely recommend this hotel. We found the concierge very helpful. After checking out, we left our luggage for the day while we did some siteseeing and upon our return we asked him to fill our six pack cooler with ice, which he did without complaint. This will be my hotel of choice when I return to Philly.

title: “Excellent location for conference center and gaslight district”
text:
This Marriott both hosts a lot of conferences and acts as a base for larger conferences that run in the San Diego conference center right beside it. As such, it's a great base if you're attending an event in either place. The rooms are reasonably large and the beds are good and offer a good work area with a comfortable chair.
