On the 7th floor I found that the wired Internet was much more reliable than the Wi-Fi connection. Everything in the bedroom seemed clean and well-maintained and my only grip was the light control in the bathroom. This appeared to be set to automatically turn itself off after a period - or maybe it had a motion detector. In either case, on several occasions I was plunged into darkness in the middle of business, which wasn't a good thing. 
On one side of the hotel you'll get a view of San Diego's skyline and the train tracks where trains pass by (noisily) pretty frequently during the night and into the evening. The other side is more peaceful and looks out over the hotel gardens and the harbor/yacht marina. The hotel is close to reasonable shopping (Horton Plaza - Macys, Footlocker, etc.) and a supermarket (Ralph's), both which can be reached in under ten minutes. It's also close to the famous gaslight district where you can find a selection of restaurants, good and bad. On the other hand, if you turn left instead of right as you leave the hotel you'll end up at the San Diego wharves and be able to visit the USS Midway (definitely worth the time) as well as eat at a selection of seafood restaurants, all of which seem to be overpriced for what they deliver - but you might be lucky and get a sea view for dinner, which takes away some of the pain.

title: “Nice but noisy”
text:
This is a very charming hotel in a great location. Our room was very large and accommodated us and our two teenage daughters very well. The bathroom however was tiny and the extractor fan did not work.
The happy hour is a great idea, we met interesting fellow guests and shared some good Napa Valley wine over a chat on several evenings.
This hotel would have rated an excellent review had it not been for the pantomime of trying to sleep. On one occasion the antiquated AC system made such a racket that we had to call the desk to complain. This resulted in someone coming to our room at 3am to open our window and place sponges on top of the unit outside - apparently the unit from upstairs was leaking on to ours and this was the method of fixing the problem, When it occurred the next night we were able to "fix" it ourselves! There was no appology for the inconvenience.
Beware also that fellow guests who get up early are clearly heard using the facilities and their footsteps overhead are very disturbing

title: “A lot of hotel for the money”
text: From the time we drove up to this impressive hotel, to the time we left, the staff could not have been more helpful. Altogether a very pleasant stay and can't wait to visit again. Very comfortable rooms, good bar service, helpful check-in and concierge service. I would highly recommend this for the price. We have paid a lot more for a lot less.

title: “great staff, great space!!”
text:
Been in NY for 10 nights and as a hotel industry profesional I need to thank and congratulate staff at this hotel for their service quality. Front desk personel is so nice and helpful! spontaneous smiles and distinctive quality service, always willing to help and exceeding expectations. I must name Alex at front desk for his unik warmth.To me that is one of the most valuable things to be found in a Hotel.
Rooms are really spacious, and though there is no doubt interior decoration and design is to be updated, they would not miss any basics and even go further. Showers are great, some of them have an interesting array of massage options! bed is very good too.
It was the less expensive hotel in our stay and for sure the best cost-effective.
Congrats to the whole staff and managers that take care of them!!!!
Free internet and an in-room safe would make an even better choice
cheers from Argentina!!!!
Ana López Furst

title: “Great location, fair accommodation”
text:
Usually when we go to NYC, we book through Priceline to get an affordable rate--during this particular week, we had an awfully hard time getting something. Eventually, we succeeded in getting the InterContinental for $200/night. We had never stayed there, but we figured we ought to be safe with a 4-star hotel.
The hotel certainly has a 4-star location. Hell, the location is 5-star, around the corner from the Waldorf Astoria. And the lobby is just splendid (especially in December, when it was beautifully decorated for the holidays). But our room was worn, with a couple of dead lightbulbs and carpet tacks just before the bathroom doorjamb. 
Service throughout our stay was indifferent. A concierge, asked to make reservations, said she'd call me to confirm--she did make the reservation, but she never confirmed.
And a personal pet peeve: one afternoon, I asked at the lobby restaurant if they served afternoon tea and got an emphatic YES! The menu described a variety of loose-leaf teas. I ordered one, and was served tea bag tea. 
I have had better experiences at other NYC hotels in the same price range--I wouldn't return to the InterContinental by choice.

title: “Trust me! Broadway Plaza Hotel is worth it!!”
text: From Kila: Broadway Plaza Hotel was a wonderful surpise to first come New York City vistors like my husband and me. We booked it online and got a great rate! I do not know how the other type of rooms are but we stayed in the Junior Suite and we just delighted! It was huge with sitting room and also eating section and mini bar & mini fridge. We live in florida & we never had a huge suite and great rate like this before! Bathroom was spacious too. The hotel is modernly renovated and they take great pride in providing excellent maid service. After a day sightseeing, it is such a relief to come back to the hotel and see made up beds & always plenty of clean towels & even their bed blankets are soft and fuzzy feeling! With the fantastic rate we got, and in a place like NYC, I never expected too much. But Broadway Plaza Hotel has exceeded our expectations and gave us peace of mind to have a clean, safe hotel and friendly staff. We took advantage of their continental breakfast and content with their location. You will experience New York City life here with the working people at Mid-downtown Manhatten. From the outside, the hotel looks like a hole in the wall..but inside you will always see a doorman there. Such helpful friendly people. So ask for the Junior Suite at Broadway Plaza Hotel and take it from me, a typical working class person, who can't afford outrageous prices at those ritzy NYC hotels, that I got an excellent deal booking online and stayed at a not too ritzy but clean, safe, immaculate and big Junior Suite at the Broadway Plaza Hotel. p.s. Don't expect Times Square atmosphere, the mom & pop shops by this hotel close down at 7:00 pm each night, trash is piled high on the streets and expect a street cleaner truck around 11:00pm...but like I said, its great to experience the Real NYC.

title: “Christmas Trip to New York at the Hilton New York”
text: This is my first ever review on any hotel and what a better one to start. For years I have read the reviews on hotels before my family and I travel. Currently I stay in Hilton brand hotels around an average 70 nights a year. So, I am very selective on where I stay. I have read the reviews on the New York Hilton prior to staying there in December 2011. I feel many people are very critical. What I can say is this, my family had the very best time while we stayed at the Hilton New York. We had a 2 double bed suite on the executive floor. We were surprised to find a Christmas tree in our room as we arrived along with ornaments and small presents for our children by the tree. We were also welcomed by fresh cookies, milk, and Dilan's Candy bar as well. We were called every day to see if we needed anything by the managers! The executive lounge was busy at Christmas, but not an issue and the food was out of this world! In closing, believe me Hilton knows how to take care of its customers. We will be back at Christmas again this winter and can only expect the same service we received in December 2011!

title: “Excepional Room in downtown location”
text:
Stayed here for two nights when visiting LA. The hotel is located near Pershing Square in downtown LA. The room we had was exceptional and the massive bed was the comfiest ever! The room also boasted a large bathroom, sitting area and big TV, with free newspapers delivered daily.
Being a visitor to the city i used the hotels valet parking facility. This service worked fine and the staff very nice, but at $30 per day + tips i felt this was unnecassarily expensive. 
If returning to LA, i think i would stay at a different hotel which is closer to the tourist features of Hollywood/Beverly Hills. The valet parking fee could be put towards getting a suite in another hotel who provide cheaper/free parking.

title: “Not good for wheelchairs”
text: After waiting an hour and a half for the room I had reserved with a roll-in shower I gave up and settled for a supposedly wheelchair accessible room. The height of the mattress was about FORTY inches. I can only hope the room designer has to use a wheelchair someday to learn the meaning of accessible.

title: “Lovely hotel - would recommend”
text:
Got a good deal on hotwire.com, so this turned out to be good value for me. 
Really nice room, great view over the water, nice little pool for a swim etc.
Would definitely recommend.

title: “Comfortable Hotel”
text: We stayed at this property before a cruise. The hotel shuttle was prompt and check in was quick. Our room was very clean and the bed was very comfortable. The rail system of Seattle known as "The Link" is right across the street from this hotel, so transportation to downtown Seattle is easy and cheap ($5.00 for all day pass). We did not sample the hotel restaurant, since this was basically an overnight stay. There are very few restaurants within walking distance. However, we did walk about two to Denny's for breakfast. I believe this hotel would be best for business travelers and for a quick overnight stays.

title: “clean hotel, perfect location”
text: my son and i stayed here for 2 nites and i think it's one of the best hotels in the world. my room is on 3 floor and i want to change to higher floor and it's ok. the staff are very helpful and friendly, we are alway feel welcome staying here. we'll back here for the next trip to US. Thanks every people here. you all are very kind.

title: “Nice, convenient hotel”
text: Stayed one night prior to embarking on a cruise. Very convenient to airport and about 25 minute bus ride to the pier. The Hotel and staff are top notch. There was a water leak under our bathroom sink, they immediately moved us to a suite and apologized for the inconvenience. We ate dinner and breakfast at Latitude 33 in the Hotel, good food and service. The breakfast buffet was very nice. Will stay here again!

title: “As far as Best Westerns go this is a plus!!”
text: I was offered a job marketing and so before I accept the position I thought I would come see and stay at the hotel. It is right off the freeway on your way to Mexico, it isn't far from downtown and the rooms are clean and nicely remodeled, and a plus in my book NO dirty BEDSPREADS, also a bit of interesting info. They not only have a trash can in the rooms but a RECYCLE bin as well in the ROOM. Free Breakfast can't beat that! oh and if you want to go across the border for lets say have some discreet surgery, they have a shuttle to an from the Clinics. Staff is friendly.

title: “Nice deal. The only downer is the distance from downtown.”
text: Hotel was perfectly clean, friendly and competent. Stylish too if that's your thing. Super convenient to highway. Places around the hotel but price is cheap because it's 15-20 minutes from downtown.

title: “OK but...”
text: nice enough...check-in dude acted like he was doing me a big favor giving me a king-size bed, as they were out of queens. Woo-hoo! If I had made my own reservation, instead of our company picking this place for us, I would have got this as a matter of course... No tub, just shower; old tube tv. Was cold close to window. One light by bed didn't work, stopper in sink wouldn't stay stopped, and shower head had a leak in back, squirting water in reverse....what left bad impression (and was the last interaction I had with staff) was when I was checking out, I wanted to tell person behind desk about these things that needed fixing, and *she did not even interrupt her conversation with her colleague or even LOOK at me while she handed me my receipt*. I -did- interrupt her to tell her.....but no "how was your stay/ how was the room/thank you and we'll see you next time". It's a shame that the art of recognizing a customer (hint: LOOK AT him/her!) does not seem to be part of the training here. The fact that I feel strongly enough to post this review should be an indicator that customers value people skills! and deplore their absence in a person employed in a service industry!

title: “Beware”
text: Had reservations to stay at the Monticello this past weekend. Called the day before to confirm and to be sure that late check-in (after 11pm) would be ok, and were assured that would be fine. When we arrived at midnight, we were told that it would take a few minutes to get the room ready, so we could bring our bags in and wait in the lobby. We unloaded the car and brought the kids in, and then the manager came down and told us that they didn't have a room for us in that building due to a maintenance issue(??), so we should pack back up and go one block over to the Georgetown Suites. Proceeded there and they didn't have a room with 2 beds available, so they sent us another block over to another Georgetown Suites building. Finally, an hour and a half later, we had a room to stay in. At each of the places, we were told that it's common practice for the hotels to "help each other out with overflow"; would have been nice if they had told us that when we called to confirm the reservation.

title: “Great Location - Walkable to the Wharf and many shopping and restaurants.”
text: This hotel is a great location to fisherman's wharf which is where you want to be when you are staying in San Francisco. It is literally 2 blocks to the water, and then it is all shopping and restaurants and great stuff to see all the way to pier 39 (which is about 5 blocks if i had to guess). The service is great, but the hotel restaurant is pricey, with many options you don't need to eat there. All in all a great stay.

title: “Worst Holiday Inn Ever”
text: This hotel smells bad, the food and the rooms both have an odor and we saw a Cockroach in the hall. The staff is not friendly at all, and they act like we should be glad they are helping us. This hotel is not recommended unless you want to be ripped off and abused.

title: “Amazing.....”
text: Beautiful hotel. Impeccably clean. Fabulous rooms and service. And look at booking this hotel directly on their site as I got a much better rate.

title: “Cancellation Policy”
text:
I have been a business traveler for many years. Travel has slowed down a little as I get older so I'm not sure if this is a new policy or not but I was amazed that this hotel has no cancellation policy, Once you make a reservation that's it. No cancellations. You lose your money. I tried cancelling my reservation a few days in advance of my reserved day and was told there would be no refund. Money lost...gone.
Well I will never reserve a room at this Hilton hotel again or any other Hilton hotel if that's what their cancellation and Refund Policy is all about.

title: “Beautiful in great locations”
text:
We stayed here for a birthday weekend. The hotel has been remodeled and is beautiful. 
I spoke directly to the reservation staff---they offered a Frosty Friday special---1st night rate was the outside temperature at 5PM ($35) and second night was at regular rate ($249) with free parking (usually $38 per day), trolley ride tickets and free hot chocolate---a great value. Hotel is in a great location also. Room was spacious, clean, bed -very comfortable. We had a great time and would stay here again.

title: “Great Beds and View”
text: This Westin is just off Market and a block from SFMOA. This location is good for the Bart (Montgomery) but not close to any of the great SF neighborhoods. The hotel is modern and clean and he beds are great, but there are few restaurants within a short walk. This is a business hotel. The lobby is busy and almost everyone is wearing a suit and tie in the lobby.

title: “Best hotel ever!!”
text: Beautiful views, friendly staff, luxury appointed rooms.. I could not fault this hotel. Sublime!

title: “Enjoyed my one-night stay”
text:
Stayed one night in September. Was able to get a good rate through Priceline.
The hotel is conveniently located less than 5-minutes walk from the Woodley Park Metro station. The lobby is spacious and impressive with lots of chairs and sofas for sitting and chatting.
The check-in and check-out were both smooth and quick. Staff was pleasant.
My room faced the pool area in the rear, with lots of trees in the surrounding area (Rock Creek Park). The room is very spacious but laid out strangely. Part of the reason is the fact that this is a very old building and the original architecture/design is still evident despite obvious renovations. That explains why the bathroom is so compact compared to the room itself. Everything worked as expected and the room was clean.
The hotel, especially the the public/lobby area, has many posters/signs/pictures decribing its heritage. Mutiple presidents, dignitaries, stars, and "VIPs" have stayed or been to the hotel. It was interesting to read about all that history.
It was about a 15-minutes walk to the zoo which I found out has free admission. However, it was near closing time, so I spent only about one hour looking at some of the exhibits. Unfortunately, the pandas were not out playing and couldn't been seen.
From the Metro, it was easy access to nearly anywhere in the greater D.C. area. By the time I got back to the hotel, it was late and to my disappointment, all the nearby restaurants/shops were closed. I ordered room service which was pricy but very prompt and tasty.
Overall, a very nice place with history and tradition and conveniently located near the Metro station.

title: “Don't blink or you'll miss it”
text:
You've seen those movies...the ones where pirates find a scroll, look left, look right, carefully unroll it, and lay it down on the table. These scrolls have dashed lines indicating a marked path, and the big "X" denotes where the treasure can be found.
My modern day scroll unfolds when I type www.tripadvisor.com on my computer. And Candlewood Suites happend to be right smack dab where the big "X" was.
I don't like to spend much money, but boy do I expect a lot. The smallest ratio of pay to satisfaction factor is what I'm aiming for, and that's what I found here. Yes it's centrally located, two blocks from Port Authority Terminal and six from Macy's . Yes, it's clean, however you mandate how clean it stays, since maid service is not scheduled daily. Yes, it's secure. And no, it's not expensive.
I'm hiding this map because I'm coming back and wanna make sure there's enough left for me.

title: “Several positives, a few annoying minuses”
text:
Positive: extremely friendly and helping staff, kind of nice location (it's korea town, but mostly nice and close to Penn station), free wireless internet, clean rooms.
Negative: breakfast is a brawl: we did not find a free seat despite waiting 5-6 minutes. The breakfast room is definitely under-sized compared to the number of guests in the hotel. Too few elevators (two): often time you wait several minutes for an elevator, only to find it completely full of people, so that you wait for the next one... there are stairs, but they look kind of emergency stairs in fact they lead you in the street without reaching the lobby, so you have to re-enter from the main entrance. Weird.

title: “Mixed stay at the Belvedere”
text: The hotel is in an ideal location for the sights of New York with Times Sq and Empire States within walking distance. The room was OK but a bit cramp for four of us and also some of the furniture was rather dated and worn. Breakfast was plentiful but we hade to pay for the kids which wasn't mentioned at the time of booking. Worse thing was the a/c in the room which was noisy and on the last night broke down which left the room hot and sticky. The lifts were also a problem as for the size of the hotel there were only two and on three seperate occasions they broke down. Would perhaps stay again but not as good as predicted by many trip advisor reviews.

title: “New room renovation is GRRReat!”
text:
My wife and I needed a night in city this past weekend and the Sir Francis Drake was a perfect getaway. Located 1/2 block from Union Square the SFD is in the middle of SF's best restaurant and shopping. Check-in was a breeze and within 5 minutes we were in the room. With limited availability the only room remaining was a deluxe queen, which normally could dissappoint, but with new bedding, plasma TV and a view of Union Square it was tough to keep the smile off our faces. The bed was excellent, room was clean and offered plenty of space. I'd recommend any travelers looking to stay in the heart of the action to stay here. We will be back.
Tip: Starlight Room is a great bar at the hotel but could be loud if you are staying on 20th floor. If staying on a weekend be sure to finish out the night dancing at the Starlight room or request a room on a lower floor if going to bed early.

title: “Great, but...”
text:
First of all, this hotel is like staying in a living beat writers museum. It's got a great central location in North Beach, and you feel like you are genuinely a part of the beat scene while staying there. The room was decent- the mattress was acceptable, but not much more than that. The bathroom was tiny but did the trick. It did have what I would refer to as a museum quality picture of the great beat writers of the day- Kerouac, Ferlinghetti, Cassady, Corso, Orlovsky... with a handwritten note about the picture from Allen Ginsberg. How freaking cool is that??? It was absolutely amazing, and it made the hotel worthwhile for me. 
That said, if you want to sleep- especially on a weekend night- DO NOT GET A ROOM FACING COLUMBUS AVE. When I tell you that it sounded like a riot was taking place outside our room, I am not exaggerating. At various times during the night (and I'd taken a sleeping pill to counteract potential street noise), my girl and I heard shouting, fighting, ambulances, police cars, sounds like bombs going off, screams, laughter, singing, more bomb sounds... I swear to you, no one could have been more surprised to look out the window the next morning and see... a street. Just a quiet, calm street. Amazing. 
Anyway, if you love character, this is the hotel for you. If you really want to be in North Beach, it's the place for you. However, if you are into pampering or quiet solitude, Boheme is probably not a fit. That said, I would go back- I'd just bring ear plugs next time.

title: “This was the worst hotel experience/service/hostiIity I have ever experienced - Frequent Traveller”
text: At 1am in the morning prior to our departure date from San Fran, we received two prank calls followed by a hostile and aggressive intrusion by the hotel's security, who demanded we settle an already pre-settled hotel bill (internal communications fault). Two security guards had been dispatched because the 0.30am calls (we thought they were prank calls) had not been answered. At first, when we heard that security was knocking on our door, we believed that the hotel had come under attack or that there was a fire alarm, but then we were treated like criminals. For someone who spends up to 6-7 months a year in hotels I have never experienced hostility and poor service at this level. I advise the travel industry, write for travel magazines, and do scenario planning for airlines, and frankly this sort of treatment is totally unacceptable. What made it worse was the manager O's response the following morning. Rather than apologise in a situation when both me and my business partner were clearly distressed, he argued that sending out security at 1am is a proportionate response (because the hotel experiences travellers who don't settle bills). I asked him if this is a hotel policy for all guests and he answered 'yes, in these circumstances'. So if you are going to stay at Parc 55, make sure that all their internal communications and accounts departments are up to speed with your Expedia bookings, otherwise you might expect a nasty wake-up at 1am. He then offered a coffee and a sandwich (which he forgot to order from the restaurant for us) as a respite. His follow up email to the situation (4 days later) invited us to a free upgrade next time we choose to stay at the hotel so 'we can better feel about our property'. This is a hotel I will never re-visit. Overall the stay was very disappointing, and the over the course of 3 days they didn't have working Wifi either. The only upside were decent beds, and a well equipped gym.

title: “Hollywood fail, forget it!”
text:
Picked this hotel for the location which undeniably is the best in town. Right on Hollywood Boulevard, across from the Chinese theatre. That was where the benefits ended. The staff were nice to look at but not overly helpful. There was an event on when we stayed and we were told by valet to park our own car around the back as the front entrance was for the 'event.' We still got charged $33 per day for valet? The room was satisfactory, though small and minimalist. Good view out the window of the star walk and the Hollywood sign. Bathroom tiny and the shower glass was obviously not sealed properly as leaked. The clincher for us was that we were waiting on a hamper from home to arrive for my friend's 30th birthday. Her birthday came and went and when we followed up whether anything had been delivered, we were told 'no'. We followed this up with the people who'd sent the package and they advised that it was delivered the day before my friend's birthday. When my friend went to the front desk to investigate the girl looked surprised and said 'oh it arrived just today, sorry." Err, no! My friend proved it was delivered two days prior but not before the front desk had made her feel like it wasn't their problem and it was just too bad. We did end up getting a $50 room credit for the inconvenience. I wonder if we hadn't of known about the hamper being delivered whether we would have got it at all?
Overall, if you want to be treated as a Z-grade celebrity on your holiday, then stay here for sure. If you can get past that, then it does have a certain tinseltown buzz about it and the location is great.

title: “Sanctuary Hotel New York”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel past weekend. It was wonderful. We have stayed in the big hotels before, but the Sanctuary is small and very intimate. We felt very comfortable the moment we stepped inside. The staff was very nice and extremely helpful. The manager suggested a wonderful little Italian restaurant that was perfect. The rooms are small but well appointed and clean. Very comfortable bed. We went up to the rooftop bar and had a good time. The hotel is in a perfect location. It is down the block from Times Square and the Theater District. We went in to see Wicked and only walked 3 blocks. We definitely will stay there again!

title: “Oversized, Cold-Feeling Hotel”
text: I can't say that I loved this hotel. It is quite large, and the first few floors have all manner of retail outlets. My room could have used updating and I didn't care for the cement interior of the lobby area. It's fine for a convention or a few days, but it wasn't my favorite.

title: “Excelent will return”
text: Food was great service was great people very friendly nex time i retun to LA with family it will be on my list of hotels to return.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
My sister and I stayed here during the week. We were in town to visit my daughter at UT. We shopped most of the day so when arrived we were tired. The valet immediately helped us with our car and luggage. We checked in promptly and the reservation was ready. The highlight of the night was our bellman. He brought the luggage up right away and was so friendly
situating everying for our convenience. The baggage next to each bed, etc. Very welcoming. Turn down service includes
roses...really a nice touch. I love this hotel. Our room was very nice and beds comfortable. Quiet even though it is 
on 6th street. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Comfortable Stay”
text:
I stayed at the Doubletree Washington from July 22-28. The front desk person that checked me in was friendly, and I was given a room on the third floor (The bedroom itself was spacious, but the bathroom was very small). I did not see any mice while there, and no one from the group that I was with ever mentioned anything about seeing mice as well. Hopefully, the mice incidents are a thing of the past.
I ate at the 15 Ria each morning, and was paying $12-$15 on average for each breakfast. I was always seated right away, but the level of service varied. The two male servers that I had were often attentive and friendly. However, the female server that I had a couple of the days would just take my order and give me the bill right after I started eating my meal. Although the food was good, I would recommend for families that you head next door to the Holiday Inn where they have a breakfast buffet for $15.95. 
Washington is a very expensive city; therefore, be prepared for high food prices (and slow service in many places). Some of the more affordable restaurants are in Union Station (off the Metro red line), along with some restaurants off M street near 17th Street. If you are coming to DC and are on a tight budget, I suggest heading to Pentagon City a couple evenings where there are plenty of affordable sit-down restaurants in the area. 
I had a great stay at the Doubletree, and would stay there again if it was for business purposes. Otherwise, I would consider staying at another hotel with a swimming pool if I was travelling for pleasure.

title: “Fabulous”
text: We stayed here for three nights eith our two kids, ages 8 and 4. We had a two-bedroom suite. The kids got to "camp" in the living room in a hotel-set-up tent. It was quiet and lovely. We had an amazing view of the lake and Navy Pier. Great location. Loved!

title: “Great Spot for your Chicago Vacation.”
text:
I too enjoy the reviews from Tripadvisor as I plan vacations to new destination. I again used this site in the planning of our trip to Chicago for the 4th of July. 
I must say, that one of the main reasons that I booked this hotel was because It was number six on the list. After visiting the hotel... Im not sure how it got such a good rating.... I would classify this hotel as a solid 3 1/2 star. The lobby was very small and unimpressive. I had reserved a room with a King bed.... but upon arrival, was forced into one with a queen bed. No big deal.
The room had A/C but it was limited in how low you could turn it down. I like it cold, so I had to removed the restrictive device. No problem...
The room was VERY large. The bed was comfy. and the bathroom was small... But all in all, it was very confortable.
The location is outstanding!!!! It is in a great spot, one block from North Michigan Ave. You can walk to many attractions, catch a quick cab or jump on the subway a few blocks away. It is a great spot for shopping or hitting the bars on Rush Street. 
I would stay here again. I think that if I was traveling with a family the extra room would be perfect.
Never intracted with staff so I have no comments....

title: “Fantiastic Dallas weekend!”
text: Our weekend staycation at W Dallas was all that we had hoped for and more. Dinner at craft was amazing, with both great food and service. (Try the braised beef shortribs!) We enjoyed probably the best massages of our lives at Bliss spa. The pool was beautiful and not overly crowded, with a nice lunch menu and great bartenders. We also took advantage of the comp. car service for dinner our second evening. The concierge was very helpful. We'll be back!

title: “Great Value in a Convenient Location”
text: If you like character and comfort, this hotel is for you. It can be a little loud, but you are in the center of Union Square. As for an interior room if you're a light sleeper. Loved the soft linens, towels and high end toiletries. Seriously, my only complaint was that there could have been a better hair dryer in the bathroom, and the windows could have been a little cleaner, but really... I loved my stay there, and we were there for 6 nights!

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Nice hotel in the Mission Valley area. Right across the highway from a large shopping area with almost every store and restaurant you could want. Suggest staying in a room on the opposite side of the freeway for a more quiet stay. Rooms seemed fine and no noise between rooms. The front desk people were first rate and very helpful. The only disappointing this is that they charged $10 a day for internet service unless you wanted to sit in their lobby. I guess I am used to free internet at most hotels I stay at and this was annoying so I didn't use my laptop.

title: “...not the best you can find but ok!”
text:
I spent 2 nights at the Pickwick in July
 Position is fantastic, just a block away from Powell cable car station, position ideal to have a good look around the city during the day and the nigts as well.
We were 3 people in the room, there were 2 queen bed but room was a bit tiny. Bathroom small, sink super small,I could harly brush my teeth in it. Shower very nice and comfortable. Hotel on the whole needs a bit of renovation, there was painting falling off the walls in some points of the room and carpet was a bit smelly.
Wifi internet is free, but unfortunately I had a corner room which wasn't reached by signal so to access the net had to turn around the corner and go to the corridor.
Parking costs 32 dollars per day. Avoid having breakfast in the adjacent cafè....expensive with rude staff. There is a cozy and very simple cafè just across the road, which sells very tasty donaughts.

title: “was great”
text: i usually go to san Francisco once a year but i guess i will have to go more this years since i found this great hotel prices are good the employees nice and the most important thing they don't bother you i have few friends coming over to see me at the hotel btw they live in san francisco and they just swing by to see me not to stay in the hotel with me but no one at the front desk who are this people or any question i like that the breakfast was very nice they have a waffle machine that make the most amazing waffles in the word the room was clean and neat but the best was great better than the one i have back home i was very surprise when i got a deal like this with free breakfast free internet and the room as great as the one they give me i will stay here every time that i go to San Francisco good people working there and overall i give to this hotel the best review it can get i usually stay at 5 star hotels never again at least in sfo was GREAT THANK YOU

title: “One of the best BW's in Houston”
text:
An excellent hotel with really only one con.
PROS: Great staff; I have stayed here many times, and they always seem to remember me when I arrive. Wine and cheese sometimes more in the evening; have to say this is a real nice touch when you have been working or driving all day. The breakfast assortment is typical of any Best Western, but it seems to always be fresh and well stocked. Great location, right off the Beltway, easy access on or off the Beltway.
Someones car hit our black rental once, leaving a large white scrape mark; the manager had someone go out and buy some stuff and buffed out the mark. Very good service. 
The exercise equipment works well, only draw back, is that there is an empty water dispenser, so bring your own water.
CONS: No elevator, plan on stairs. Albeit, there are not many and pretty easy to get up and down.
There is a reason why this hotel is rated high, I would recommend this hotel to anyone who needs to stay in Houston.

title: “Worst place I ever stayed would not recommend.”
text: This place had very poor service I imediately felt unwelcome as I entered. Very unfriendly atmosphere. Room were ages, very poor quality and floor creaked. Parking space was too narrow especially for large vehicles. Overall worst place I ever stayed at would not recommend staying there to anyone.

title: “Great Location & Price :-)”
text: We stayed here for 5 days. Hollywood Hotel is located at heart of Hollywood. The rooms were spacious and clean. We were all comfortable with our rooms. The staff are very sweet and accomodating making our stay more fun. :-)

title: “Tourist in my own town”
text: I moved from New York and found myself needed a hotel prior to going on a cruise. Spent 3 nights in New York doing the Tourist thing with my kids who have only been to New York once. They had cupcakes in the Lobby which were fantastic. Rooms clean. Great location. Walking distance to everything and the subway. Would stay there again!!!

title: “great hotel and location”
text: stayed at the warwick twice so far. great traditional 1930's hotel. got us out of trouble as for a change we had booked into the poor roosevelt but couldn't stay there for 5 days. rooms are grand and spotless. staff very good and location is excellent for everything, ie, 5th ave, times square, broadway, central park, UN...literally walk everywhere. great bar just a bit pricey but "Frank" the bar man would keep you chatting in there all night which is great until you get the tab...but thats New York! Really couldn't ask for better and wouldn't waste time stopping elsewhere

title: “Friendly, Helpful and Convenient Plus - Would Stay Again”
text:
I stayed for three nights on my own here - I had not pre booked and walked in, which I would only suggest if you hadn't already booked somewhere (they were actually pretty busy so I was lucky) - and upon arrival I was greeted by friendly young staff who may have been new but you can't really hold that against anyone - the only time you should be in a huge rush on holiday is when you're on the way to the airport! 
 The room was fresh and clean, spacious and a big relief from what I expected I may have walked into randomly on Hollywood Boulevard. A good, powerful shower with complimentary soaps, tea and coffee and a television.
 There is a pool, although I didn't use it as being I was on my own and out most of the time - probably more suitable for families staying, you may as well make the most out of it.
 The morning breakfast was quite nice; a soya option would be good but not that many places do soya funnily enough. There are several options; waffles, eggs, fruit, juice, coffees...
 This place has free wifi and generously allow guests to use their personal laptop inside the office if they need to. It is family run, which adds a nice touch to a venue, and the managers are very friendly and helpful. They know the city so ask them what's where and how if you need to. 
 Hollywood Downtowner Inn is also affiliated with a taxi service a few doors up which gives you a much better deal on cab fares than the regular Hollywood cabs, and Bechir also knows his way around. 
I travel on my own a lot and as a female this can be tricky in certain places - I've developed a pretty good intuition for picking out the good from the bad, and these are good people who are happy to help and want to see you have a good time. I've stayed in plenty of places where people really don't give a [--].

title: “What a find!”
text: Great hotel, very helpful staff especially Julian de Lacaze. We needed a room for three and were accommodated. The restaurant/bar next door was great too. This hotel is within walking distance of everything one might want to walk to in downtown Boston - and we did. Prices here made the trip affordable and the service was a plus.

title: “Great”
text: Easy checkin process. Parking price for the DC area was great. Kept our privacy sign on the door for the whole stay since its not really necessary to clean anything in our room... lets be honest, does the room really need to be vacuumed or the sheets changed when I am only there for 2 days... I don't think so. Though I asked the front desk about the post office and it was not in the direction they said... no biggie thats what googlemaps is for.

title: “My Birthday”
text: My stay at the skyline Hotel was comfortable, cozy, and convenient. My husband took me to N.Y for my birthday. He booked us here and we had a great time. Everything was walking distance and the hotel personnel made us feel at home. Highly recommend it. A good affordable hotel is hard to find in N.Y.C. We look forward to our next trip. Thank you!

title: “View of Space Needle . . . plus a Whole Foods Market”
text:
My wife and I stayed for two nights in a corner room at Pan Pacific Seattle. We found it to be a clean and friendly hotel with wide, quiet halls and an iconic view through tall windows.
Location
The hotel is located in an interesting complex with a Starbuck’s, cards/gifts shop, and a pet store. There's a nice public park, Denny Park, kitty-corner, that is great for walking, and it ensures that no buildings will block the view of the Space Needle. Best of all, downstairs (accessible by lift and escalator) is a giant Whole Foods Market. The Whole Foods Market provides all kinds of breakfast lunch and dinner foods and tables. If you select a steak, they’ll cook it for you, and you can sit down and eat it. The most interesting shops would be along Westlake Street. We walked to Pike's Place, stopping at Serious Pie on Virginia Street near 4th Avenue for a Yukon potato pizza. We had taken the Gourmet Seattle tour, and we were not impressed with any of the "gourmet" dishes except the potato pizza. 
Restaurant
We were happy to find that Seastar restaurant is accessible through the hotel. It has excellent food. The hotel provides a coupon for a free soup or salad. We especially enjoyed the crab and corn bisque and halibut with artichokes and mushrooms. There is also a pizza restaurant, Tutta Bella, next to the Seastar.
Room
Or room was quite large with a view of the Space Needle from the desk, the bed, and the bathroom sink. A coffee maker and a hair dryer are in the closet, but in order to be used, they have to be moved to a location where there is an electric plug. The refrigerator was cold but there was no freezer. There are both a phone and a temperature control in the bathroom. We received a free newspaper every day.
Quiet enjoyment
The fourth floor may be a bit low for light sleepers because trucks go up a grade on the Denny Way side of the room. The windows are double windows and we had no problem with the traffic noise. No neighbor noise, not even footsteps overhead. 
Internet
Everyone gets free Internet. A huge plus. We used only wireless because the signal was good and strong and we couldn't find a LAN cable in the desk. 
Concierge 
The doormen are special here. The concierge personnel open the door and engage guests in conversation which makes them seem especially friendly and helpful. The concierge, I think it was Mike, gave us a lift in the hotel car to the Space Needle (uphill) and we walked back to the hotel (downhill). We ate lunch at SkyCity and found the food and service to be a good value and not overpriced. 
We were enchanted with our stay at the Pan Pacific Seattle, not only for the attentiveness of the staff and a great view, but also for the proximity to downtown and (most of all) the Whole Foods Market. An unusual value.

title: “CLASSY BUT COMFORTABLE.”
text:
This hotel is awsome. It is located right on the beach, with lush tropical gardens and ponds thru out the grounds.There are areas for adults and areas for families.The hotel and grounds are meticulous and well kept, and the service impeccable. I know I sound like I work for them , but its true. This is Californias version of an " old money" hotel.Classy but comfortable!
Don Shooter
Yuma Arizona

title: “All around wonderful stay”
text: There is really nothing but good and total satisfaction for my stay. The staff at this hotel go out of their was to be friendly and helpful. This hotel is beautiful and spotless!! I think they even had some kind of wonderful fragrance being pumped into the hallways. The room is also extremely spacious with very modern updated decor. I felt like I was staying in a small apartment. The complimentry breakfast was restaurant quality and not like most of the run of the mill continental breakfasts. They offered 24 hour food if desired and even allowed you use of some kitchen facilities such as dishes, spoons, microwave, table and chairs. The amenities were also top notch. I purchased this hotel via priceline for a very reasonable price. It was actually a steal! Priceline rated this a 3 star. I feel this hotel should be nothing less than a four star at minimum. I actually booked 2 additional nights at this chain a few days later in a different location since we loved it so much. I will definitely stay here again in the future.

title: “Smooth check-in and great customer service”
text: This hotel is pretty clean and they have a decent continental breakfast. The location of the hotel is very convenient to access good dining areas, seaport village which are within walking distance & and main highways. If you have a chance to book here make sure you ask to speak with Jayson because was very helpful & attentive to us!! Thank you!!!

title: “Trendy Spot for a Weekend in NYC”
text:
Visiting NYC I would highly reccommend Marrakech Hotel for any budget
conscious traveller. The location worked really well for 4 women visiting NYC for a
 wkend of sight-seeing, shopping and nights out on the town.
We found this boutique style hotel online. Our criteria simple for 3 days: clean, spacious, 
 2 double beds, access to parking, convenient location, a place to leace our stuff, shower, change and rest on a reasonable budget. 
Marrakech was that and more. Its a brown stone building located in Uptown Mahattan near major attractions (Columbia University, Apollo in Harlem, Grants Tomb, and Central Park).
Staid in room 51 on the 3rd floor. It was big enough for 4 women, clean white bed linen, small wash room with piping hot water. Only thing missing a small safe and mini fridge. 
Loved the fact that the Metro was just steps away, a direct line to Downtown attractions, Starbucks next door, and many local restaurants.
We all agreed we'd go back to Marrakech especially because the staff were 
very hospitable and accommodating...made us feel welcomed.

title: “Keep Returning and love it:)”
text: We love going to the ocean and being able to take our 2 dogs, Ocean Beach Hotel is allways our hotel of choice when we go to SanDiego, it is allways clean has a very pretty court yard and you are just across the street from the beach. we will definately return when ever possible.

title: “Unique Experience in the Heart of It All”
text: Uniquely situated close to theaters, shopping and Times Square. Although, the rooms(cabins) are listed as small, the cabin provides a relaxing and spacious atmosphere with its design to conveniently store guests' personal belongings. Also, the moving bed allows flexibility when resting or deciding to spend a day in to cuddle. The hotel is clean and the staff are helpful and courteous. Being able to grab my in-cabin breakfast tray to get an a la carte breakfast or the 24 hour complimentary hot beverages are great! Plus the points earned with the Stash rewards program is a bonus.

title: “Terrific Hotel!!”
text: We stayed at the Langham this weekend and had an absolutely wonderful experience! From the time we drove up to the front of the hotel on Friday afternoon to when we left on Sunday, everything was perfect. Each and every member of the staff with whom we interacted was amazing, the hotel was incredible clean, and the amenities were all top notch. Whether for business or pleasure, there is no better place to stay in Boston than The Langham!

title: “A Regular "Days Inn" Experience”
text: This was just what you would expect at a Days Inn--everything was pretty standard. The hotel itself is very old and shows signs of its age due to wear and the overall construct. The lobby had coffee and tea readily available, there was a business center for use, and nice, speedy WiFi in the rooms. The staff was friendly, professional, and very accomodating. A security guard was on duty during late hours, though the area itself was very quiet in the late evening and into the night with no real "riff raff" in the area to speak of. The hotel did have free parking, and the Van Ness metro station was just two blocks away from the hotel. There were vending and ice machines, though there was no microwave or refrigerator in the room. There were clean towels and linens, though the dust cover on the bed had oily spots. The carpet was worn, but other than a few spots that appeared to have been cleaned from previous spills, I saw no earth-shattering stains that would make your skin crawl. (The carpet in the hallway appeard to be new, though.) The room did have a working phone, iron, hair dryer, and flat screen television, a safe, adequate toiletries, and coffee. If I were a traveler on a budget looking for a places with the standard amenities, I would certainly consider this hotel. If I were a traveler looking for something a bit more upscale with glitz, glamour, and all the frills, I'd keep looking.

title: “Very nice stay.”
text: Everything was very nice, they did forget to give me a tea bag one morning in my room. But overall very nice.

title: “Please replace dirty, gross carpeting”
text: First of all . . . location and price were great . . . earning the unit we were in an average rating. But . . . carpet was disgusting. Need to have sofa and curtains replaced. We saw "no smoking" signs everywhere, but the hallway (4th floor) smelled like cigarette smoke so that was a little odd?? The bathroom seemed to have been re-done which was nice and the bed was comfortable and linens were clean and comfortable. Nice flat screen TVs. I am in hopes that maybe room by room this is being updated and maybe they hadn't gotten to our room on the 4th floor yet. As mentioned before, if the carpet and sofa was replaced I would upgrade this place to an above average stay, but until then . . . yuck! Should have taken pictures to post. Maybe would opt next time to spend a little more and stay at a better hotel, just fewer nights.

title: “Perfect Place to Stay!”
text: My friend and I stayed here last weekend. What a perfect location! We were within walking distance to so many things...attractions, restaurants, theaters, subways, etc. We were on the 18th floor and had absolutey NO problem with any noise from the streets. I fully expected it to be noisy (I mean, you're in the middle of Manhattan!) but it was very quiet. Never heard other people in their rooms either. Our suite was adorable and the kitchenette was very useful! All of the staff that we interacted with were courteous and helpful. Would stay there again in a heartbeat and would recommend it to anyone!

title: “Cozy with potential .”
text: We stayed at this hotel in Jan 12 , service was good but rooms slighty smaller than average and had issue with the smelly toilet and constant sound of garbage collecting was unbearable . Apart from that great location close to central park and ballet theatre .

title: “Great stay. clean. separate parking garage. wierd neighborhood”
text: me and my guy wanted to stay somewhere nice and low cost and near his place of work. For the money we paid...like 60-70 dollars I was very impressed. nothing scary. sure u don't want to be walking around at night as there are lots of homeless ppl but just stay out their way.besides what do u expect, its skid row. but its right in downtown close to all the metro rail, historical buildings, interesting restaurants and shops. There are taxis everywhere too if you want to do more exploring which is what i did. The room was was big enough for 2 people.Nice bright white walls. tv with lots of channels. funky maze-like hallway design.We chose the room with the bathroom which costed a little bit more. The cheaper rooms have communal washrooms with other guests. I personally don't mind. They're not scary at all and I'm sure some of them are street ppl. But I doubt they're going to rob u or touch u or rape u..Dont be a fool and bring valuables to your vacation.The only thing we didn't like was the lack of parking within hotel premises. There is a separate parking garage across the street which you have to walk to is where i'm guessing where most Cecil guests leave their car. It was either that or an alley. We chose the alley which really wasn't that better. So decide for yourself. I would not recommend the Cecil for a family as it's just not that kind of place you should cram your family into but if you're looking for something nice, affordable, and charming for friends consider the cecil.

title: “This is a great hotel.”
text: We arrived at this hotel by mistake. I had made reservations at another Marriott and stupidly mapquested the wrong hotel. We were to be in town for only one night in route driving from Florida to Vermont. We had booked a night monument tour so we had a deadline and could not spend the evening trying to find a hotel. I explained my mistake to the front desk clerk who couldn't have been nicer. She cancelled my other reservation and gave me a room for a very good price. She even comped my parking and gave us breakfast for four for free. The room was very nice, and the service was excellent. The staff was very helpful. We had a wonderful breakfast with excellent service (table not buffet). The bill for breakfast would have been $50.00 but was comped. We left in the morning with ice on the roads and the valet telling us exactly how to get out of the downtown area. This was a stupid mistake which turned out to be one of the best hotel experiences we have ever had.

title: “Perfect SEATAC overnight hotel”
text: I've stayed at this hotel for years--for overnight stays between flights at SEATAC---for the following reasons: 5 minute complimentary shuttle ride to/from airport, friendly staff, large comfortable rooms and beds, very clean, very quiet, hotel has espresso, sundries, etc.

title: “Will come back again”
text:
Great rooms, great service.
Only stayed for a couple of days but I had a very good overall experience.
Booked over the phone and got a very good deal.
Parking is 30 dollars but you don't feel bad about it because the valet service is fast and very polite. I never waited more than a couple of minutes.
Wish I stayed an extra day to enjoy the spa. Menu was attractive and you can get a 60min massage for 110 dollars
If I get another good deal, I will definitely come back to this Hotel.

title: “Awsome view, location, and service.”
text: Stayed in December for my birthday...The location was perfect. The view was lovely along the riverwalk with the Christmas lights. The suite was clean and cozy. Staff was friendly and very helpful. The happy hour was nice and the complimentary beakfast was a great start for the day.

title: “Neat hotel, great location!”
text: My family and I stayed here during spring break. We were so impressed with the uniqueness of this hotel. The room was very nice and bed comfortable. Walked to everything downtown with ease. Loved the free breakfast- now that's a breakfast buffet! We will stay here again soon!

title: “Small, unique hotel”
text: Great place, great location. Staff is attentive, helpful and pleasant. Fabulous location, walking distance to all the places that matter. Have stayed at downtown hotels and this one is much nicer, newer and vibrant. Won't go wrong here.

title: “Passable budget option”
text:
My husband and I were looking for inexpensive accommodations in Chicago: we were attending a concert that evening and didn't want to drive three hours home immediately after. We chose Chinatown Hotel for its price ($80 with taxes included), cheap parking ($10 for 24 hours), and location (just a few stops on the red line from the Loop). The neighborhood is safe, and there are many truly excellent places o eat steps from the hotel.
The hotel itself was dreary and basic, but our room was perfectly fine for an overnight stay. The first room they gave us had a terrible smell (I think someone had brought their dog...), but we alerted the front desk and they immediately changed our room for us.

title: “Perfect for visit”
text: My husband and I spent Saturday and Sunday night at the Iroquois. I had stayed once there before with a friend and decided then that I could stop trying different hotels in NYC. The staff are friendly, helpful and accomodating. The room (we had a king executive this time) was large, clean and comfortable. We really don't spend much time in the hotel room, but you do have to sleep and clean up there, and the facilities were fantastic. The linens and bed are great, and the bathroom was large, spotless, well-lighted and had plenty of towels, hot water and water pressure. We were given a bottle of wine and chocolates, which were delicious, and it was nice to find a fresh bottle of Perrier when we arrived back in the evening. We had breakfast at Triomphe, and it was delicious with prompt and attentive service, and delicious food. The location can't be beat. We will definitely stay there next trip.

title: “just so easy”
text: I had such a great time in this hotel. I was there for 10 days so it became my home away from home. It was all just so easy - everything worked, no hassle, really cruisey. The only 2 negatives are no fridge - but there is an ice machine so you improvise! and the air con is really noisy - I use earplugs all the time so wasn't problem for me, but it might be a problem for some - try and get over this as the overall experience is fabulous!

title: “Class & Style”
text: We love SF, and always stay at the Fairmont hotel for business and pleasure. if you liike old sophisticated classy hotels, this is it. My wife and I always stay in Fairmont hotels around the world and we love the ambiance. The highend Suites are a little dated, but roomy and classy...if you get a chance and you are in Banff, Alberta Canada, stay in the exclusive Spa Suites they are worth every dime you pay!

title: “Nice, but don't face the parking lot”
text:
Hotel is elegant and with the right discount, a pretty good value. I stayed one night for business. Had drinks in the lobby and room service. All were very good. The lobby is beautiful. The room was adequate, but it was all I need for one night. Two double beds--not queens which seemed lame.
I had a room facing the entry where cars pull in and out. It wasn't terrible, but pretty loud both in the evening and early in the am. Just ask for a room facing the quiet courtyard.

title: “Hotel 1000 Seattle, WA”
text: Wonderful location, great staff, good value and excellent rooms! We liked the lighting and the TV was easy to operate, we especially enjoyed the "windows" at other locations on the TV! We could go to the Market, catch the ferry and was easy to check out and get to the airport from here. I would recommend this place for anyone. We played around a little with the virtual golf, but not enough to really comment. We were too busy enjoying the city and our room.

title: “Great Stay and Great Value”
text: We stayed one night at the hotel because we wanted to be near the airport and Easton Mall. I had read the reviews and was expecting a nice hotel, but was still surprised about how lovely it was. The hotel still felt new. It was very clean. The suite was a good size with a huge bathroom and a very comfortable bed. Flat screens in both rooms with a good selection of channels. I am pretty spoiled when it comes to hotels and I would have absolutely no reservation about staying at the hotel again. The service was also excellent.

title: “Great hotel on the waterfront”
text:
The hotel is very well located between the financial district and the new seaport district. The nearest subway station is only two blocks away and if your a good walker most of the Freedom's trail landmark are within walking distance.
Our room was spacious, stylish and confortable with a nice "méridienne" couch, a window facing desk, individual reading lights on each side of the bed and a nice sliding panel between the bathroom and the bedroom. The bathroom features both a shower and a bathtub. The sliding panel is very nice but might be a problem if someone has to go to the bathroom in the middle of the night as it is not lightproof.
On the "green" side, the room is fully equipped with high end LED bulbs.
The staff was available and competent.
My only concern is on the internet connection. This is not unique to this hotel but while most motels offer complementary internet I really don't understand why 4 or 5 stars hotel like this one are charging nearly $15 for an internet connection. Although I had to connect two different devices (laptop and smartphone) and when I connected the second device I didn't know wether or not I would be charged for the second device (the captive portal page is the same).

title: “Stayed one night, paid for two along with $130 in false minibar charges”
text: I was so majorly excited for the Hardrock trip to San Diego. I rushed my 51 year old mother to our room ASAP because I thought I booked us the primo Gold level Rockstar Penthouse as seen on the website. The agent over the phone explained a very impressive room with balcony and jacuzzi bathtub. The pictures online looked amazing! Little did I know that each penthouse is totally different in size and the ones pictured are the largest/nicest and most expensive for each level. We get there, and they have one agent checking guests in. We waited. We checked in. Balcony was a ledge with a railing. My mom couldnt even fit on the "balcony". When booking the room I informed the agent that I would be taking my 51 yr. old Mom here for her birthday and I wanted to stay at the Hardrock because it was the coolest looking hotel. No one over the phone or at check in informed us that all of the Rockstar penthouses were directly above the nightclub or warned us about the noise level. So we didn't sleep. Music til 1:30 AM and drunk screaming the rest of the night. The room service guy even commented on how loud the rooms are and how many guests complain that they cant sleep in the Rockstar suites. He also literally laughed at how the rooms look nothing like they do on the websute. We checked out disapointed in the whole stay. I went to pay my credit card and I was charged twice for our room. Was also charged $130 in false minibar charges. I stay in hotels weekly and I have never ever had this happen. I was even charged for a "pleasure kit"...um, NO! Lucky after making a few phone calls the charges are suppose to be removed but so far hasn't reflected my credit card. Needless to say- WHAT A BUMMER. The hotel looked so cool. I did love to art and furniture. The Aveda bath products are of course a plus. But I would have traded Aveda and cool factor over sleeping and not having to be stressed out about the huge overcharge.

title: “wonderful staff”
text: It was a great stay in this hotel ,everything was close by no problem,we did walk to Time Square ,Empire Bldg,Rockefeller,Madison Ave ,close to Bus station,We arrive early cause we took Bus Evelyn who is on that morning very compassionate & understand She check us in early,that was A plus to Management to train their staff when thing happened like this traveled 10 hours,you have space right away to rest,continental breakfast also offered to us it was great its.No problem for us with our belonging they still let us put in storage for another 5 hours after the check out,Consider this place you will have a great stay like us,your needs will be handled,I will use it again when we come back,

title: “Great Location... Average Hotel”
text: You can't ask for a better location if you're staying in downtown Chicago. It's centrally located close to great restaurants and shops along the "Magnificent Mile". I found the majority of the hotel staff to not be very friendly. The rooms were adequate size, but you could hear the folks staying next door due to the ventilation system... you could actually see the lights in the room next door when looking through the vent while standing in the bathroom. I would say this is an average hotel. You can find way nicer accomodations, but I'm sure you could equally find way worse as well.

title: “Very pleased with The Westin”
text: After reading some of the previous negative reviews on this site, I was a little apprehensive about staying at The Westin Indianapolis. However, I was attending a conference at this hotel so I went with it. The conference rate was $149. I was pleasantly surprised. I checked in around 1:00 PM. I was concerned that my room wouldn't be ready but fortunately it was. My king bed room was average size with a large window overlooking the garden area across the street. Ask for this view, otherwise you get a view of a rooftop. the carpet in my room looked brand new and was very soft to walk on. The bathroom is quite small but fine for just me. The dual showerhead was a nice amenity as well as a real hair dryer - not one of those small dryers that hang on the wall. The room also had a large TV, a chair with ottoman, a desk, two phones (one of them cordless), a locking safe, a robe for your use and a mini bar. Do not even touch or look at the mini bar or you will be hit with a $25 fee on your bill. A friend of mine in another room only placed her bottle of water in the fridge and was charged for 2 bottles of beer and some crackers! The Westin Heavenly Bed is, well, just that - heavenly! I really looked forward to going to bed each night and dreaded getting out of it in the morning - simply wonderful! The only time I heard much noise in the hallway was during the day when housekeeping was cleaning rooms. But since I was seldom in there during the day due to my meetings, it wasn't a problem. At night it was very peaceful. The Westin is connected to the RCA Dome via a skywalk which was great for me since I had a ticket to the Colts game on Sunday. Since I was traveling alone, the skywalk was a nice safe way for me to get there. This same skywalk connects to the Circle Centre Mall which is a very nice upscale mall. There's also plenty of restaurants to choose from nearby. The elevators were very fast, and the wait for one was always very short. I used room service twice and was pleased with the food and service both times. The salad I had for dinner one night was one of the best I've eaten. The front desk staff was efficient, although not overly friendly. I would definitely recommend staying here, especially if you can get a conference rate for meetings or a good deal on Priceline if you're on your own. It's very handy if you are attending any event at the RCA Dome. It will also be close to the new Lucas Oil Stadium when it is completed in 2008. I certainly enjoyed my stay here.

title: “Great location and comfortable stay”
text: The location is so convenient, close to shops and restaurants. The room is huge and the bed is comfy. I like their bathroom supplies and complimentary coffee every morning. It is a pleasant stay. The staff was nice and helpful. Will stay again. We got a great deal on Hotwire for 100 per night for 4 nights during thanksgiving weekend.

title: “Clean modern hotel, a great value for Austin.”
text:
My family all stayed at the Hyatt Place for my brother's wedding last May. We got an amazing rate and found the hotel very comfortable and clean. The rooms are HUGE with a sectional and fridge. This was great, because we had a large group staying at the hotel and it was fun to be able to host folks back in our rooms. 
The breakfast in the morning was good and offered a lot of variety. The location is a bit out of the way and you would need a car to get around. I didn't always feel the front desk staff was helpful. The morning staff was better than the evening. Those were the only downsides, but other than that I think this is a good option in Austin.

title: “Great Stay - Clean, Comfortable, Fabulous Service, A+”
text:
I went to New York for a weekend with a friend and had a lovely experience at the Affinia Gardens Hotel. The room was huge - my friend and I kept thinking - we could live here! We had 2 queen size beds that were completely comfortable, the bathroom, while smallish in size, was well appointed and they made maximum use of the space, there was a great desk and a separate area to put on your make-up, as well as tons of storage space (huge wall unit) AND a full kitchen (including a gas stove). There is a grocery store less than 2 blocks away and the area was really lovely.
The staff were great - friendly, attentive, and had wonderful suggestions. In fact - we had asked where to go to dinner the following night and they remembered and called us the next day to see if we wanted a reservation.
I've traveled a fair amount and have to say that this was one of the best experiences I ever had - it felt like personal service with a friendly staff that were genuine and kind.

title: “Beyond excellence in Customer Service”
text: I travel every single week for business. We had a problem with a reservation in Charlotte, and we had to scramble to get a last minute reservation near the airport. We are usually put up in very nice hotels, so I was a bit worried when we had to stay at this particular hotel. The room was average, but quite clean, but it is certainly dated and the TV, electronic equipment, and bathroom are in need of a serious renovation. BUT I want to clearly state that my review is completely biased based on the EXCELLENT customer service I received from Cynthia Carter, the Front Office Manager. We had some business matters to take care of, and she helped us in every single step along the way, with a huge smile. She made an average hotel stay an excellent one. It is true that the rooms need an upgrade, and I did not have anything but the coffee, so I cannot comment on the breakfast, but I cannot state enough how the excellence of an employee can change the way one feels about a hotel stay. Cynthia, thank you very much for being a rare example of excellent customer service, you made our stay wonderful.

title: “This hotel is definitely at the top of our list & surpasses the Beverly Wilshire Hotel in terms of comfort & room staff”
text: We upgraded to a superior room with view, the accomodations were very comfortable, clean and the room was tastefully decorated.

title: “Dropped the Ball On Many Accounts”
text: We transferred here from The Empire, which is superior. The décor at Best Western President Hotel is very nice, but the staff lacks true hotel professionalism and accommodating attitudes, the bedspreads left a lot to be desired w/ numerous stains on them, and the promised wireless Internet was ridiculously slow. We asked for flatter pillows -- they didn't have them (what?!). We were transferred to another room that supposedly had better Internet, and it was just all right -- not fast by any means. The toiletries were so-so (you get L'Occitane at The Empire). The only awesome thing about this hotel was the incomparable location, which is literally right upon Times Square -- amazing.

title: “Great location, but keep your shoes on in the room.”
text: Great location with friendly staff. You are there to spend time in NYC, not in your room. Fine. BUT... the rooms are so incredibly tiny that the 2ft strip of 'room' around 2/3 of your bed is so heavily trodden.. that if the cleaning is not superb.. you can quickly notice the filth. Bathroom was very well cleaned, great! That is to focus your attention away from the rest of the 'room'. Bedroom was full of hairs and stuff - floatsm and jetsom so to speak - when we arrived and despite daily 'cleaning'... gunks was always there. Toilet paper of the lowest grade, had to ask for an extra roll twice in 6 days. It's not a boutique hotel.. it's a red roof or super 8 pretending to be a boutique. If you are single and staying for a jam-packed weekend of NYC fun, great hotel. If you are a couple or staying for more than 2 or 3 nights.. I'd spend a bit more and try somewhere else.

title: “Great value, good location, comfortable stay”
text: The motor inn is walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf. The morning continental breakfast of pastries, fruit, coffee/juice was a good start to the morning. Rooms were clean and we found it quiet. Staff was friendly and helpful. Parking spaces were tight, but adequate. Great restaurants down Lombard St to the east.

title: “What a great deal!”
text:
This place is fabulous. The rooms were in excellent shape, offering an extremely quite night sleep with plenty of space and all the necessary amenities. Parking was a breeze and it made getting in and out of San Antonio extremely straightforward.
I would definitely stay here again, the pre-bundled extras made it even better. We took advantage of this for the July 4th weekend and had a perfect view of the fireworks from HemisFair park, access to RiverWalk was easy just by heading downstairs where it runs along the back of the hotel.
There were a few problems, the elevators were probably the biggest issue. While there were quite a few available it seemed that only about three ever worked. Especially for our departure, it took quite a while to get an elevator to go downstairs. In most other cases where we were waiting 15+ minutes it was just as easy to head down the stairs where you would often run in to other families lugging strollers and other large bulky items.

title: “Great location but hotel very tired looking”
text: Stayed here 4 nights in October. Staff on reception weren't very friendly and never managed a smile, the concierge lady though was lovely and very helpful. We were on the 3rd floor and the room was of a good size with 2 big comfy double beds. The air conditioning was very noisy and the room was stuffy. The television controller didn't work and the toilet didn't flush properly, the bathroom was very old and dated and needed a complete make over. It was good to have a fridge in the room too. We didn't do breakfast here, but went to the Deli over the road where we got hot drinks and fruit very cheaply. The location is good, about a ten to fifteen minute walk to Times Square. I would stay here again due to the location.

title: “Not kid friendly”
text: We stayed at this hotel to take advantage of their pools. Unfortunately, the pool rules were so strict it was hard to enjoy the pool. Even though the weather had been 95 or above for weeks the water was cold. The room was big but we found hairs and bugs in the beds and bathroom. We could hear through the walls and we kept receiving late night calls with no one on the other end. Even though its convienent to the airport I would not recommend this hotel.

title: “Sorely Lacking Hotel...”
text:
WOW! Where do I start...? I stayed at the Detroit Marriott, Renaissance Center this past weekend for a wedding and left extremely disappointed. I don't believe that the rate requested matched the product or level of service presented ($139.00). I know that $139.00 isn't much, but compared to the Detroit market and other hotel chains in the area, they are waaay over priced.
As a former industry employee and current investor, I understand the constantly evolving nature of the business. For simple request such as a steamer, robe, or late night room service, my request were constantly met with a "No" or "What is that?" I'm curious to know why such common hotel amenities aren't available to guest. 
In addition to the lack of resources, some employees didn't seem all that eager to help with small request and the ones that where didn't seem to feel empowered or have the necessary resources to meet a request. Two specific examples that come to mind involve one of the bride’s maids leaving her jacket with the bell stand when leaving to go out for the night. Upon returning from the MGM Grand (A much nicer product), the brides maid asked for her jacket from a young lady standing behind the bell stand (Deja) who wasn't motivated to assist with the request at all, giving a response of "He'll get it for you when he comes back". The second example wasn't as severe, but still annoying none the least. A few individuals who attended the wedding were interested in sending up an amenity to the newlyweds room for the night (champagne, strawberries, floral arrangement, etc...), some of which weren't available or required "the guest in the room to sign for it", even though it was supposed to be a surprise and prepaid.
I don't want to make this story any longer than what it is, so I'll just touch on a few more points. Décor was old and dated, differed from room to room. No late night room service, no mini bar, first room checked into smelled of smoke, and a few unhelpful employees. 
On a positive note, the views of the downtown Detroit and Windsor City, Canada are amazing if your room is high enough. Other than that, save yourself some time and grief and pay $20.00-$30.00 more to stay at the new Westin downtown or the MGM Grand.

title: “Emphasis on the Micro”
text: Other than a cruise ship, the smallest room we have ever stayed in. As long as you are aware that this is "bare-bones" you will be fine. $59.00 through Priceline was the tipping point. At that price, a good value. I would have been upset at paying more. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Absolutely one of the most comfortable beds we've had in a while. Breakfast was also "bare-bones"; coffee, juice, cereal, muffins, bagels, nothing resembling fruit anywhere. In other words, a fine place for before or after a flight or as we did, stay after a concert.

title: “Great location but better for business travellers”
text: I stayed here with my son for his 21st for 5 nights 5 - 10 April 2011 (no upgrade for us however!). We had a superior grade (standard) room which was fine but no walk-in rain shower as featured on the website. The location is superb as other reviewers have said but it is a very big hotel and I think better suited to business and larger party travellers. This may explain the high charge for internet usage which is hard to understand given the free wi-fi available in Times Square (although I could connect to this on my ipad in the hotel I was blocked from using it). The service is rather anonymous and in my experience slow. One whole hour after reporting a broken ice machine I got a bucket of ice delivered to the room! However the concierge service was terrific and a real bonus. I had one breakfast in the restaurant which was delicious but expensive. There are plenty of other options close by. One of the doormen arranged a private car back to the airport for us for what was clearly a discounted rate from the hotel's quoted price - worth it in my opinion. Having done the Times Square experience once for a return visit I would go elsewhere - probably The Blakely.

title: “Excellent quality and service”
text: I have to admit to being pleasantly surprised during my stay at the JW Marriott in Indianapolis.
