I've stayed at many "5-star" expensive hotels before, and have always been disappointed with both the rooms and how much they nickle and dime one to death. This hotel does not do that. The rooms are spacious and new with great views of the river. The elevators are quick. The staff is friendly and helpful. I especially appreciated the evening turn-down service with the weather for the next day. The only thing I can say that I disliked was during my last few nights a cheerleader competition was taking place and they made the halls a noisy living hell.

title: “Great hotel for the price! Very nice staff!”
text:
- great hotel for the price
- good location - 1,5 km away from the center - walking distance to the shopping area, and the Pier, seems to be a relatively safe area 
- Old rooms but very clean
- Huge bathrooms
- Very nice staff
- Flexible and accomodating - wanted to cut my trip short without any problems and storno costs
- free wireless lan

title: “Very Clean”
text: After reading reviews I was a little concerned...but I found that only one staff member was not approachable...(morning-day girl) but the other female and 2 males I dealt with were very friendly and helpful. I found our room was a good size and had a real nice bathroom. The bed was very comfortable and room was very clean. Breakfast was good also.

title: “Excellent Service. Excellent Venue!”
text:
This review was mistakenly posted on another Comfort Inn site. However, this is the REAL DEAL! 
I have stayed at this property several times and am never disappointed by the quality of the customer service and the wonderful rooms, regardless of which room we get. The beds are like sleeping on clouds. I actually regret that I can't spend more time just lounging in the bed, watching TV. It's like a home away from home, though I don't have a fireplace! I recommend this property to all of my Chicago-bound friends. The service is top rate!

title: “Nice Hotel & Good Downtown Location”
text: Stayed here while attending a trade show / convention in Febuary 2012. Typical Hilton accomodations and service, top notch andprofessional. The room was nice, good bedding, clean, comfortable. I had a great view of downtown and surrounding from my room window. It is close to all the downtown attractions, 6th street clubs and restaurants, the warehouse district, Antone's Blues Club etc. The location is i a safe secure area and has underground parking, my only negative is the parking rate of 420 per day, but that's typical of a downtown hotel. I onl;y ate at the restuarant on property once for breakfast, chose the buffet which was good. I had no problems at this hotel and I would recommend it to other staying in Austin, especially downtown since it's close everything including the convention center across the street. As for Austin in general, I LOVE Austin, was pleasantly suprized and I would surely go back.

title: “Four star hotel in Hollyhwood”
text:
This hotel is a solid 4 star hotel in the middle of Hollywood. IT has a small but nice roof top pool which closes at 5 pm to make room for the restaurant and disco. 
As for the restaurants in the hotel, they automatically charge you an additional 18% “service charge” and put it on your bill. They put this charge right over an area left blank marked “tip” in which they expect you to give a tip in addition to the already included 18% service fee. So just beware of this. 
My room was nice and had all the commensurate amenities. The valet parking was prompt. I had no complaints staying there and would do so again if I were in the area.

title: “Good location for Rose Parade”
text: We had excellent service and the rooms were adequate (carpet could use an upgrade, but the place was clean). The breakfast was a little sparse, but adequate. The location was good - easy to get to and convenient for getting to our seats for the Tournament of Roses parade and the Rose Bowl. Would stay there again.

title: “Total JERKS for management”
text: I totally disagree with previous postings. This hotel is a royal pain. I've stayed here a half dozen times because it's in a very good location for my business and sometimes can be well priced but the management and its procedures leave a lot to be desired. I am going to stop staying here. First, the hotel is indifferently maintained. Each room has its own foibles. Desks wobble, air conditioners don't work well, there are gaps in the door you can see light through...it's just not professionally managed. But the biggest problem is that the managers are real jerks when something goes wrong. TWICE, they've overbooked and sent me out once in a snowstorm and another time at midnight to find hotels on my own (they tried to send me to New York Avenue in the lousiest part of DC to take their crapola hotel there). Then they made me switch rooms because they gave me a business room and then had sold it to someone so made me switch. Each time, they just shrug. No free night. No "I'm sorry". Nothing. They are a fair weather hotel. If things go well, you're okay here. But expect to be severely inconvenienced otherwise. Jerks. You can do better elsewhere.

title: “AMAZING LOCATION AND SERVICE IN THE HEART OF NYC!”
text: My daughter and I stayed at the Ameritania Hotel this past weekend. Check-in was easy and painless. The doorman was extrememly friendly and helpful! We stayed in room 1105, a corner room with two windows, an amazing view and PLENTY of room. It was one of the largest rooms I have ever stayed in in NYC. The bed was comfortable, room was clean and bathroom was small, but very modern. The energy efficient features with the lighting, etc. took a day to get used to, but it was appreciated. The lobby is amazing and shiek, elevators and hallways just recently renovated. There is construction going on next door, but it did not interrupt our sleep and we weren't in our room during the day. The location is awesome, right around the corner from David Letterman Theater and one block from Sister Act. I highly recommend this hotel and hope you are fortunate enough to get a corner room as we did!

title: “Mixed Review - Great Location, too much construction when I was there”
text: A great hotel in a great location: steps to the shopping district. If you’re going further afield the regular bus service stops can be found within a block. The lobby and reception area of the Omni were modern and tastefully appointed, a theme which was followed through to the bar and restaurant areas. The hotel room itself was spacious, clean and fairly well appointed with nice decor, a modern flat screen LCD TV and cordless phone. The only negative point was the construction going on right next door. They are completely re-doing the area next to the hotel. So don't think about sleeping in. Apart from that, the service given by the rest of the Omni’s staff was first class. Highly recommended.

title: “Very Nice”
text: Stayed here for three nights the end of September with a group of colleagues and clients. Everyone was happy! Rooms were nicely appointed and bathroom was large and well lit. Bed was very comfortable. Hosted wine hour was nice. Wine was only fair, but it was nice to mindle with other guests. On site restuarant, Sazerac, was good but service is VERY slow.

title: “grand hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed here just a week ago and thought the Fairmont was a lovely old building very grand foyer lovely bar and restaurant and located in a very convenient location but, I was expecting a lovely room and we were upgraded to a suite but I thought it was a bit outdated and only a view of a wall which was dissapointing, there was no coffee maker and if you took anything out of the fridge you were immediatly charged for it so could not keep any drinks cold. On the good side the bed was amazing so comfortable and I liked the little card left every night on our bed to let us know the weather for next day. I would probably stay again for location but in a room with a view

title: “You could call this a Courtyard Plus”
text:
This Courtyard is a bit more than your typical Courtyard, as it has a resturant with room service, a deli, conference center, and a full bar, along with a larger pool area. It's more of an inbetween a full Marriott & a normal Courtyard, hence the Courtyard Plus I'm calling it. As mentioned in the other reviews, the rooms are very nice at this property and they keep it up amazingly well.
I had to ask how old the property was, and was amazed they said 4 years old as it looked like it was a brand new & they just finished everything a few months ago. About the only drawback to this hotel is it's location. It is in a good central location, but at the same time it's not close to anything except the airport. So expect to make a bunch of 5-10 min. drives to most items. Or go park near the Old Town trolley station & ride the trolleys. That's the best way to go downtown.
 Two items. Jim the bar manger/bartender is a master at classic cocktails as he spent 30+ years at the Del Coronado as a bar manager and is way above what you would expect to find at a business hotel. The other is the hotel will take you on the shuttle bus to any of the resturants on the Shelter Island/Harbor Island area. Highly recommend the Bali-Hi, With the restoration, the view & the high quality food it's a great Tiki Temple, and Jimmy's Famous American Tavern is basically across from the Holiday Inn about a 1/4 mi. away is a fantasic gastropub & has a nice harbor view. Very cool decor as well and great if you want a causal dinner.

title: “Very convenient but could do with a lick of paint”
text: I know that it is one of the oldest hotels in Boston so understand that it is not brand spanking sparkly. The lobby is very attractive but the bedrooms could do with a lick of paint and new carpets and sad that pipes run across ceiling. The front desk staff were all very charming and helpful so absolutely no criticism there. The complimentary breakfast was fine but the waste involved in using paper/plastic disposable plates and cutlery strikes me as very wasteful and unnecessary. For baseball lovers it must be heaven as it overlooks Fenway Park. Very conveniently located for Boston sightseeing but make sure you get off at the correct subway stop, we got off at the wrong one and had a long walk. Incidentally their public transport system is excellent.

title: “Good value for money”
text:
Good value for money for NYC. Stayed with family 3 kids so swimming pool was welcome. Sauna was broken and Gym closes at 6 pm on Saturday, a pitty.
Wifi in guestroom is very very slow and needs a serious upgrade. No problem to pay as long as it meets the speed expectation.Ideal the fact that the hotel is located just inb front of bus station that takes you mid/downtown and no need to use the crowded and warm subways.
Concierge was very helpful in arranging an airport taxi/minivan.

title: “No BMI above 30”
text:
Nice staff.
OK location- but right on 5th Avenue means lots of traffic noise.
Only one significant gripe: Small, small, small....
How small?
Don't plan on wearing a bulky coat- you won't fit in the room.

title: “Gorgeous, classy, great service!”
text: Wow. After spending 2 nights at the crappy Executive Pacific on the company's dime, I moved to the Monaco for an extra night on my own following a business trip. I had done Priceline and scored the Monaco for only $95! THIS is what a Kimpton Hotel should be (I had lost faith in the brand after my stays in DC). The lobby is AMZAZING. Really stylish and well-decorated and a great place to hang out. I actually got to take advantage of the free wine reception, and it was really nice!! Front desk staff was amazingly friendly and helpful-you can tell they are well-trained. (Alec checked me in and was very pleasant, sort of a weird gal on the overnight shift though). Doormen/valets were all really nice; got a great tip for breakfast (Bernard's on Seneca around the corner-cheap and good!) Then I get to the room. Uh, wow. It was more like a studio apartment that had been decorated by HGTV or something. Really stylish and cool, and ironically matched my own style (I would love that tripod lamp!). Super comfortable bed. Large bathroom. The entire room was IMMACULATE and it seemed that no detail had been left unattended. I'm not sure what their usual rate is since I got it off of Priceline, but I would pay up to $40 or $50 extra compared to other hotels just to stay here. I thought the parking was a little pricey at $36, but I guess that goes with the territory with a city. They had a Business Center that allowed me to print my boarding pass for free. Walkable to downtown shops, light rail and Pike Place Market. VERY pet friendly (though i didn't have pets). Really a very, very nice place. Thanks for a great stay--wish I was there longer than one night!

title: “Best $72 Hotwire Hotel Ever”
text: Got this for $72 on Hotwire and took it over the $85 4.5 star hotel (this was 4 stars) because of the Trip Advisor rating. This hotel is only 1 year old and everything is new, very clean, and hip. The rooms are very well designed and the King Bed was huge and great. Once you get the hotel on Hotwire for $72 then you sign up for their "Priority One" frequent traveler program for free and the hotel will upgrade you to a better room even on the day of your arrival like they did for me and gave me $10 free minibar coupons. Excellent value. This hotel was going for $200 a night on the Indigo website the same day I got it for $72 on Hotwire. San Diego is hurting economically and there should be plenty of great finds out there. Do not pay retail when Hotwire is around.

title: “Smelly experience”
text:
Hi, I went to the Jane in December.
The rooms are small, if you get a bunkbed cabin! You can't get dressed together cause there is no room! The beds are really hard, you can feel the wiress through the matrass. The residents that live there smell really bad and are not friendly. 
The staff at Cafe Gitane are rude, they keep asking if your done eating when clearly you are not!. And when you give them a tip, they come back for more money..
In short, if you have MORE money, don't go to the Jane!
Regards,
Caroline

title: “Great location, nice room”
text: My husband and I stayed here for 5 nights at the end of May 2011. We had booked and paid in advance for our room to get a more reasonable rate. Our room in the North Tower had a great view of the city and had been recently renovated. Quite spacious. The location of the hotel was fantastic. We had turned in our rental car and certainly didn't miss it. We took advantage of the Old Town Trolley tour that stopped right in front of hotel and also used the subway to get around. Staff at the front desk very helpful.

title: “Good place overall”
text: The location, ambiance and rooms are good. Little bit old, but goood place to stay. Room window seals had empty water bottles that had not been picked up. You need to use vallet parking or facility nearby.

title: “Love this hotel.”
text: For the 4th or 5th time, I stayed at the Colonnade Hotel in Boston for a weekend getaway. Although we couldn't use their Frosty Friday promotion (we stayed Saturday and Sunday nights), it was priced right for what was offered. We had tickets for concerts and the location was perfect for us to get to Symphony Hall and the Berklee Performance Center. It was great to be able to go to Brasserie Jo after the concerts and have drinks. The room was great, the hotel is not noise despite being on Huntington Ave. Would stay their again.

title: “Good overall stay with minor complaints”
text:
I came to Boston over the July 4th weekend and stayed at the Embassy Suites Boston Logan. The hotel was hard to find as I didn't know that you have to enter through the Airport in order to get to the hotel. Our GPS brought us right next to the hotel but the airport is gated off so we had to go back around to park. Check in was easy, and the rooms were nice. The rooms were very clean, but the room smelled too much like a cleaning product to be able to feel completely comfortable. Actually the entire hotel smelled like an overdose of cleaning products which isn't ideal for my son's allergies.
Even though this hotel is located a bit outside of the city, it is close to subway making it easy to get into the city when we didn't feel like driving. When we did drive, Valet was quick to bring our car to us and helpful with directions in this confusing area.
A free cooked breakfast for the entire family was definitely a plus, and having a pool to bring the kids too was also great.
I would definitely stay here again,

title: “Fantastic Place!!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed in the Belleclaire Hotel, queen room with a shared bathroom from April 14th for two nights. Dont listen to any bad reviews about this hotel. Its in a fantastic location, near 72nd train station which takes you everywhere around Manhattan. The area has some fantastic cafes and bars. We recommend Big Nic's on the corner of the hotel, ask the staff for details, this was a true New York diner, fantastic! The room was modern, clean and the sharen bathroom was a very good standard, it was quiet and safe and for the price you cant get much better in the city. The rooms have iron, clean towels, tv and fridge. Def would go back and stay.
Sarah and Mark, England.

title: “Nice Hotel - Good Location 12/30-1/4/08”
text:
We got a pretty decent rate on Hotwire for New Years Day on - it was pretty empty after the festivities of NYE. The location is great - you get a room up way high and you'd probably see the ball drop from your window! 
When we checked in 12/30 - our room was not finished properly (lack of toiletries, blanket for bed) but otherwise it was fine. It was on the 20th floor if I remember correctly. 
The service to the room was slow, but otherwise we had no complaints.
Keep in mind if you come specifically for NYE it's a big pain in the --- to get around that evening - requiring police escorts (everybody was standing around - but no body wanted to escort us to the hotel!) that at best is a very very slow process.
The free upgrade to the room on the 51st floor was definitely awesome. The room was prettier (as you can see on the picture) and the view was awesome.
Would definitely stay there again!

title: “Woderful ambiance”
text: The Carlton has done some fabulous renovations. The lobby is spectacular as are all the public rooms. We had a quiet room with super beds and other amenities. The location was just perfect for our nedds and the staff very helpful.

title: “What was that?!?! Oh, it was the train, again!”
text:
The overall location of this hotel is good. Very convenient to walk to the Gas Lamp district and located right on the marina. We had awesome views of the marina from our rooms. However, be warned: trains pass in front of hotel across the street and loudly blast their horns at all hours of the day and night.
Like many hotels today, this one is no exception, they charge for everything (like parking & internet). Luckily, because we had booked such a large block of rooms, we were able to get the parking & internet fees waived.
The rooms were average. Nothing special or spectacular with the size, layout, or furnishings. 
The staff was friendly and helpful. Large pool area. Starbucks was very busy at times and closed by mid-afternoon. We couldn't find any signs that specifically stated their hours.

title: “seriously, biting insects - stay away!”
text:
We stayed last weekend. The cons outweigh the pros. We were both bitten several times by some unidentified insect(s) in room 408. Now that I read reviews, i find many other people complaining about bedbugs at the Opal, including people unwittingly introducing the problem into their own homes. I was going to write the general manager, but apparently this is an old problem at the Opal so now I doubt my complaint would even fix anything.
Do not stay at the Opal! Now Im worried and will be washing EVERYTHING when I get home. I would expect bugs at a cheaper hotel - which is why i would never stay at one. This is ridiculous. The rooms werent even that nice (defective thermostat, shower curtain fell down, expensive parking). But this really settles it - NEVER going back.

title: “Perfect for Tourists don't love for Meetings”
text: This hotel has a great location directly across the street from the inner harbor within walking distance of most top spots in Baltimore. The rooms were very nice and spacious. Parking is hefty at 428 self park and $40 valet. As for meetings at this hotel unless you are taking over all space the meeting rooms are grouped together and registration areas in foyers tend to block each other/make it confusing for attendees.

title: “True hospitality!”
text: Truly the nicest people - from doorman to check-in to the hotel restaurant! Everyone was not just nice, but GENUINELY nice, and helpful. The hotel restaurant served very good and fresh food at reasonable prices. Being in a historic building was also a plus! The only downsides were: (1) a somewhat weak wi-fi signal/connection; and (2) less-than-soundproof walls and doors (noisy neighbors did not help but that certainly was not the hotel's fault).

title: “Small beds”
text:
The location is great, we paid extra for TS view. Was very sentral point for all our tours in Manhattan, we actually didn't use public transporation, for 7 days of touring manhattan.
Didn't use any of their restaurants as they are too expensive and did not offer attractive menus at all, while there are so many offering of better and cheaper food outside...
The only bad comment is the bad sizes. We reserved for two queens (one parents and one for the kids).
Problems we got something like two twins (less than 4 feet wide).
 Eventually I had to sleep on the couch (me any my wife are really small compare to avarage people so I really don't know how it can work out for other couples with kids)

title: “very nice place to stay”
text: I stayed here with the recommendations from my travel agent I found it a very nice quiet area to stay in nyc with an awesome market across the road, at a great stop for the subway from time square, the best cafe next door for breakfast absolutely loved it

title: “Perfect for Rock and Roll Marathon weekend in San Diego”
text:
Great location. Easy check-in. Within walking distance of restaurants, public transportation, farmers' market, ocean, marathon route. Very helpful front desk staff. I read several reviews of the Marina Inn at TripAdvisor that mentioned airport, train, and trolley noise. For me, that noise was noticeable but no big deal. It didn't go on all night and didn't interfere with sleep or overall enjoyment of my stay in San Diego. 
Room had an ocean view and was very clean. Maid service was prompt and efficient. But for a Midwesterner, the smell of the ocean was reason enough to enjoy staying at the Marina Inn and return again. It is certainly not a luxury property but was perfect for a long, busy weekend in San Diego.

title: “Soooo noisy”
text:
We stayed on the 3rd floor overlooking the road, and there is no soundproofing whatsoever. There was no chance of a good sleep at all. The plumbing within the hotel was noisy too - every time someone next door flushed the toilet or had a shower, it was like it was in our room. Talking, drawing the curtains, even footsteps were all very audible. The TV died when we plugged the laptop in. The handbasin plug is broken, won't let the water go. Check in staff were tired and unhelpful.
On the plus side, the bed was very comfortable and the room and bathroom were lovely and clean. The concierge was fabulously knowledgeable and friendly.

title: “Chandler Inn - You Might Want to Avoid It”
text: Disappointing hotel. Rooms are tiny, and bath room is even smaller. Only had enough floor space to open one suitcase, had to clear off a night table to open a second suitcase. Parking (self parking only) is a few city blocks away in a public garage. We were notified during our stay (and was well posted throughout the building and elevators) that power would be shut off from 10:00 AM to 12:00 AM during our stay. Since checkout time is 11:00 AM, there was no info on whether we had to checkout before, or if it would be extended. So we planned on checking out before. At 8:30 AM we received a call from the front desk advising that there was a change, and power would go out at 9:00 AM. So we rushed to packed our bags and get out. We got to the elevator at 8:53 AM, and found the power to them was already shut off. Inconceivable. So our luggage (two suitcases and two overnight bags) had to be carried down from the 5th floor to the lobby via the stairs. This was a planned extension to our trip to Boston as part of my daughters wedding. It was a disappointing end to what was a great week otherwise.

title: “Highly recommended!”
text:
The manager himself asked me at check-out how I liked my stay. I replied that I would be posting a favorable review online when I returned home, and here it is!
My room was exactly as expected, as was the Hampton breakfast. Staff were extremely helful, friendly and professional; I needed to add an extra night to my reservation, which was put through immediately without any hesitation whatsoever. My room was on the back, so I did hear the AMTRAK trains, but that wasn't a particular problem, and there was no problem at all with loud folks loitering at the Trolley station there. No on-site laundry; however, guests have access to to coin-machines at the nearby Residence Inn (2 blks), where the staff treated me as nicely as though I were staying there myself. I did not use the shuttle.
Frankly, I am puzzled by the negative reviews here, which do not reflect my experience whatsoever. For one thing, the Gas Lamp Quarter is way on the other side of downtown; I found the [Hampton's] Little Italy neighborhood very quiet at night.

title: “Great location for Hollywood Bowl”
text:
This Best Western is about a 5 minute walk to the Hollywood Bowl, and very close to Hollywood Blvd. We will stay there again when attending a Hollywood Bowl event.
The rooms are clean, beds are OK.
The air conditioning unit is rather loud.
The staff is pleasant, but may not know the area very well; they didn't know the closest liquor store was right down the street.
Parking spots are difficult to get in/out of due to being so close to the building.

title: “Great deal, great location and good hotel”
text:
Stayed at this hotel on a Saturday night. Arrived at about 11am and the hotel had a room ready for me to check in. Overall the hotel had a few kinks but I would still recommend it. The hotel is huge and it faces Market Street which is one of the main thoroughfares downtown. Took advantage of the valet service. Was about $35 for the night and you can keep it with the valet until the evening of the day you are checking out.
The room I got was a corner room on an upper floor. Two double beds, huge flat screen TV, desk, chair, table and bathroom. 
The hotel charges extra for internet service. Was at a Courtyard by Marriott in Boston the week before and high speed internet was included. I paid the $12 they require for 24 hours of service however the service was beyond slow so I upgraded to the high speed service which was only a couple dollars more. That service was horrendous too.
The room smelled of cigarettes even though smoking is not allowed in the hotel. I told the front desk and they offered to change my room but I had already settled so I declined. They did send someone up to deal with the smell. Didn’t help that much.
The TV is great however sometimes it wouldn’t turn on or it would randomly turn off. Seemed to be a problem with the cable maybe or the picture tube in the TV - no idea.
The location is in the heart of downtown - steps away from City Hall. The hotel is also a short walk from shopping at Rittenhouse Square, the historic district, and all of the city's museums. I walked everyone. Perfect location. Only downside to the location and this has nothing to do with the hotel itself and more to do with Philadelphia - Center City has a lot of homeless people. At times they can be everywhere. They seemed to be centered in Center City. I live in NYC and have to say we have nowhere near as many homeless people. Just be careful of your surroundings.
I did speak with the hotel and they didn’t charge me for the internet service which I had problems with.
I would recommend the hotel though I got a deal on Priceline which helped.

title: “Excellent Place to Stay!”
text: By far the best place that I've stayed while visiting San Francisco! The hotel's staff provided superior service and the restuarant, The Blue Mermaid, has one of the best waiters at dinner time that I've ever encountered. The room was also very clean and had a very comfortable bed. However, when I return to the Argonaut I'll spend a little more for the deluxe room as the window in the standard room didn't open so it got a little stuffy. The hotel is also in a prime location -- at the quiet end of Fisherman's Wharf but also within walking distance to many great places to eat and drink. I'm looking forward to my next visit to the Argonaut!!

title: “Spacious room, very comfortable, great location”
text:
Well first off didnt get the Crylser Building view requested at time of booking, not a problem, limited rooms have it.
Room we did get was very spacious and clean. Bathroom was a bit small relative to the size of the room but was adequate and clean without being amazing. We didnt use the kitchen as there is so many places to eat in NYC.
Hotel is in great location, 2 min walk to subway and 15 min walk to Macys and on to the other shops!
This was my 2nd time in NYC and will be definitely returing to Dumont as it was a great hotel. Our first trip we stayed at the Sofitel which is a more impressive hotel lobby wise etc but there wasnt a major difference when it came to the rooms and you do pay alot more for the Sofitel!
Would recommend.

title: “Excellent place to stay.”
text: We stayed three nights and enjoyed every minute of it. Rachel at the front desk was wonderful and helpful. Our room was nicely decorated, spotlessly cleaned every day and very quiet. We had a great view of the lake and really enjoyed sitting on the sofa and watching people boating and rowing. The restaurant was ok for a quick meal, not the greatest. The food from the bar was great, as were the drinks. Enjoyed the free popcorn in the lounge too. The people who seem to be complaining are the ones who booked discount rooms thru discount websites. Guess what? You get the crappier rooms with no view. Pony up and pay for the better room and view and enjoy yourself.

title: “Wonderful location for the price”
text:
My husband and I stayed in this hotel from June 16th to the 19th, 2005. After reading all the reviews (after we booked the hotel) we were a little worried, but to our relief, the hotel was just fine. We wanted to save some money, but stay in a great location in NYC. We found the lobby to be welcoming -- they are renovating the building, but who cares? It was never noisy or dirty. We stayed on the 10th floor (room 1014 to be exact) and it was surprisingly roomy and very clean. No, there isn't an alarm clock, but we used our cell phones instead. Yeah, it was hard to adjust the hot/cold in the shower, but oh well....a minor inconvenience compared to the great deal you are getting. Besides, who spends time in their room in NYC?? Our air conditioning worked perfectly too....
For a quick, cheap, and delicious breakfast or lunch...check out the Dunhill Cafe right next to the Hotel St. James. 
We would definitely recommend this hotel to people who are looking for a simple, clean, affordable place to stay in Midtown Manhattan.

title: “Forced Stay-cation”
text: Moved into this hotel for 2 nights due to a power outage. Although I've stayed at many higher-end hotels in Baltimore, I actually really liked this Springhill for the uniqueness it offers. This location has seen many changes of the years, from bank to Gucci to office to hotel and it was a pleasent surprise to find some Easter eggs nestled about the property, this really gave it some standout flair to me. Probably will not stay again, as I'm more of a full-service hotel guy, but hey if the Four Seasons is booked again I could see myself getting a room here just for the comfort and local flair. $32 for overnight valet felt a little high, but the service more than made up for it.

title: “Fabulous Hotel”
text: This well priced Seattle Hotel is tops for the money. The employees, especially Chris the Bellman were welcoming and caring. I had a serious fall in the airport on our way to Seattle and was very bruised and battered when I arrived. Chris and the registration people could not have been more helpful and caring. They brought me ice packs to use and made excellent recommendations for breakfast and dinner. We did eat in the Hotel restaurant for breakfast and it was perfectly prepared to our order and piping hot. The room had everything we needed. The bed was very comfortable and in spite of my injury, we spent a restful evening. We stayed here before a 7 night cruise to Alaska, and we stayed an additional night on our return. If I ever go to Seattle again I would choose the Olive 8.

title: “Incredible - Don't stay anywhere else in downtown Denver!”
text: This is not my first time at the Ritz Carlton, Denver - but it is my most favorite visit! We stayed 3 nights in the club level. We haven't stayed in a non-club level room so I can't compare. This visit was flawless. Valet and bell staff remembered us from last year. Tim, the manager, also remembered us and honored our request to be on the 12th floor and near an elevator. There are new club lounge attendents from our visit last year....Doug, Angela and Molly. Wow. These folks work tirelessly to accomodate your every need. They are always on the move and we've never felt more spoiled. Doug has worked in the Ritz family going on 27 years! I can't begin to tell you the special touches we encountered...for instance, while riding in the elevator a staff member asked if we were having a nice stay. I told her it was exceptional and how thrilled we were that Bvlgari products were brought back (at this time only club level receives these upgraded bath products) as last year's stay they had phased them out. I gushed how much I LOVE the line and she laughed as she could smell the lotion in the elevator! Upon returning to our room later, we found a small bag of a few extra Bvlgari products and a hand written note from Kisha - the staff member we had encountered in the elevator! The fact that she took the time to 1) find out who we were 2) write a lovely note and 3) leave a few extra of my most favorite bath products ....is an example of the amazing steps this staff will take to make you feel welcome. Additionally, our club attendent Doug (have I mentioned FABULOUS?) introduced us to his fiance, Karen, who also works at the Ritz in member services for the destination club. Although not her role, she went out of her way to make us feel special as well. In a nutshell - this place is amazing. Ritz Carltons worldwide have the plush bedding, amazing ambience and luxurious amenities and Denver Ritz Carlton is no different. What we love about this specific Ritz Carlton above all others is the staff....they truly make a difference in our stay. From Reggie the bellman, to Mark at guest relations to management with Tim - and all the smiling faces in between - they will make your stay incredible. If you plan on staying in the downtown Denver hotel - don't look elsewhere. We've stayed at them all; Hotel Monaco, Magnolia, Brown, Hyatt, etc., etc. - spend a bit more and experience amazing luxury at the Denver Ritz Carlton!!!!

title: “Highly recommend staying here. Very nice accomodations and wonderful staff!”
text: I will reserve for my family and friends personally anytime at this hotel. Top notch staff. They were very gracious and accomodating to me and my family. We ended up staying a week and a half due to their hospitality. Nice rooms clean and comfortable. Nice pool too.

title: “A great spot”
text: Went to the hotel for a convention. Found the hotel staff to be extremely friendly and the rooms were very nice. Would definitely go back...

title: “nice but noisy”
text: one of the better Best Westerns I've stayed in but even with the recessed doors it was noisy due to automobile and airplane traffic

title: “Great Hotel, Reasonably priced”
text:
We stayed here for 8 nights in March of this year for a trip centered around St Patricks Day. We wanted stay in or near the Lower east side/East village area. There arent many hotels in this area so this was the closest we could get at a reasonable price. 5-10 minutes walking brings you to countless dive bars and music venues which is exactly what we wanted. Home Sweet home and Welcome to the Johnsons would be two of the best we visited. 
Grand St Subway station is only 1 block north and serves the B&D trains. (Orange Line) You can get the J&Z trains (Brown line) from Bowery St which is about 4 blocks north. Also, Canal St Station is about 5 blocks west and the N, Q and 6 trains stop here. We got the train from JFK to Bowery St and walked the 4 blocks to the hotel. With two suitcases this was a bit awkward as the footpaths are quite uneven and crowded at the junctions but its not that far and we saved about $40 each way by not getting a taxi. We were first timers in NYC but being fairly seasoned travellers we werent fazed by the hustle and bustle in the chinatown area. 
The hotel itself was fine. Decent sized room with a nice big TV and very clean. Staff were very efficient and friendly and really seemed to care. There was a bit of a mixup when we were checking in but this was dealt with quickly and without fuss. Very quiet at night, we asked for a high floor so we would be further up from street level. I would recommend this hotel for travellers who want a nice, clean, safe hotel near the lower east side.

title: “Great place for a family on the go”
text: I stayed here with my husband and two children, 12 and 14, for the week of July 4th. We loved everything about the hotel. This was one of the few places I could find in NYC that offers 2 Queen-sized beds. The beds were comfortable and as long as we kept everything put away, it was not terribly cramped, even for 4 people. Good shower, plenty of pressure and hot water and the air conditioning in the room was great (it was over 100 in the city a couple of the days!). The breakfast was great, there was a rotation of hot foods plus waffles, breads, juices and fresh fruit every day. It was often crowded but we were always able to find a place to sit and eat. There is a Trader Joe's and a Whole Foods nearby for in-room snacks. The hotel has coffee and hot water for tea all day, and sometimes M&M cookies in the afternoon (or maybe every day but we were not always there at the right time?). The location for subway access is EXCELLENT- we were there to tour and we rarely had to walk more than a block in one direction or the other to reach a station that would take us to any area of the city we wanted to go. 23rd street (hotel is on 24th between 6th and 7th) has a subway station at every block between 5th and 9th, I think, so if you are headed all over the city like we were, it's really a great location- removed enough to be quiet but easy to reach the action. We were on the 15th floor and noise was never a problem. The only negative I can think of is that often, the only place you can get ice is in the basement (ice stations are closed part of the day on the 4 other floors they are located, and were often empty when we tried them when they were open). We brought a soft-sided cooler and a couple of ziplocs- we filled those with ice about once a day and kept them in the cooler with a few drinks, and that would last about 24 hours, so the ice being 16 floors down was a minor inconvenience. I would recommend this hotel to anyone and would definitely stay again!

title: “Fancy Hyatt in Downtown Seattle”
text: We stayed here for 1 night before heading to the airport. We arrived on the early side and were able to check in immediately. The staff member at the front desk was very efficient and did not waste any time. For no particular reason, we were given a handicapped accessible room-it was enormous. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone living with a physical disability.

title: “excellent location”
text:
just in the best avenue for shopping , for all the architect michigan av. in the real center for all , with lake´s view, the best area to walk all the great chicago place, as sear tower,
the river, the Washington library, frank Loyd right

title: “A Dissenting Opinion”
text:
Six nights in San Francisco and plenty of options to choose from. After a great deal of research, I settled on the Palomar. Reviews were stellar and the location seemed ideal. I had meetings all over town.
Yes, the staff here are superb, and the rooms are comfortable and well-lit. Free internet is always welcomed. Still, I don't understand why this hotel is held in such high regard.
A gap in the doors to the hall makes for a noisy stay. After one night on the infamous fifth floor I moved to the eighth, but still found my neighbors distracting. Also, none of the windows open. The lack of circulation made the room smell stale and eventually set off my allergies. Finally, room service was horrific -- bland and terribly overpriced.
I have mixed feelings about the location. Market Street is grittier than I remembered, and there aren't many restaurants in the area. I'm not a fan of the tourists mobbing Union Square, either. Next time I might try SOMA.
I don't know who to recommend this hotel for. Unless you need easy access to BART, there must be better options available.

title: “I am a travel agent and seen many hotels, this is one of my favourites in the USA!!!”
text:
Excellent hotel, great location and lovely friendly staff. This is a more boutique style hotel in Union Square and i loved it. I would definitley stay here again. There was noise at night, but staying in Union Square you cant really get away from that unless you spend money on a fancy hotel staying on the higher floors. 
They also have a great courtyard/pool area, cannot fault the hotel in any way.
I am planning to go back to this hotel again next year.

title: “Excellent 5 Star Hotel”
text: Just spent the weekend at the Mandarin in NYC. Great location, large beautiful rooms with a wonderful view. Excellent staff, great spa, 5 star property. Nothing not to like, we'll be back in November!

title: “Lovely Hotel”
text:
First the staff are very nice when you arrive. 
The suite was very nicely decorated and the bed comfortable with good linens.
The Bathroom is fabulous. Beautiful tub and great shower with good products.
Free Champagne & gift for special occasion.
We had a great view from our suite on the 12th floor.
Also great location for shopping and Art Galleries.
We would stay here again. Good prices.

title: “Avoid at all costs!”
text: Checked in at midnight after a very long 24 hour day of working. Walked nearly a country mile to get to my room. Passed a wedding reception letting out, full of drunk obnoxious people crowding the hallways. Tried to shower and get some sleep, there was NO WATER PRESSURE! Tried to lay down, had sleep number beds, but I found 2 dirty socks in my bed!!! Horrible housekeeping! If I had not have been awake for 24 hours already I would have just left. Had a terrible stay, not to mention the people in the rooms next to me were in and out all night long making all kinds of noise.

title: “yes but”
text: This is a large convention hotel located next to the convention center and on a branch of the Riverwalk. It is also an older hotel, which is good and bad. The hotel appears to be in very good repair and the design style of those days allowed for large rooms. Furnishing were very nice; the room was very clean, shower hot, TV was large flat screen. The location is only minutes walk to shopping at the Rivercenter or bars/restaurants along the Riverwalk. As a convention hotel, however, prices, exclusive of the room, were ala carte and expensive: coffee and bagels for 2 was $20; parking $25, etc. Other than these issues, it's fine. Book early for a cheap rate.

title: “A Perfect Boston Experience”
text:
Our weekend stay in Boston was terrific! The city was truely wonderful, and we got to see it all based out of our hotel room at the Charlesmark. From the moment we opened the door to our room, I was impressed. Soft classical music played in the room upon arrival, a nice welcome to a relaxing yet exciting weekend. The room was very comfortable, clean, quiet and well-designed. Cozy bed too, a plus for couples! 
The small hotel perks were not lost on us... hotel service was personalized and unique, nice to stay some place where the staff remembers your name!

title: “Exactly what you are looking for”
text: We have now stayed here twice. The first time in 2006 was just my husband and I and then again in 2011 with my parents, sister and her husband. Whether it be business or pleasure, this hotel has it all. Unbelievable location, great service, generous rooms as well as a spacious bar with great food. This hotel has everything you need, give it a try!!

title: “Roomy and comfortable”
text:
We had a suite which consisted of a bedroom, a sitting room and a bathroom. We enjoyed the separation of living and sleeping space. The bed was comfortable and we had plenty of pillows without asking. 
We asked room service for a bottle of wine and was told it would take half an hour. When I explained that we would not have time to have a glass before leaving, they found a way to get it to us much more quickly. 
The staff was friendly and went to great lenghts to help us find something, including printing out a map at the front desk for us. 
My only complaint wa that we were visiting for pleasure and did not always get up and out of the room at 8 a.m. The housecleaning staff was audibly (including vacumming right outside our "do not disturb" signed room) before 9:00 a.m. I do understand that they have to get their work done, but it was just a bit noisy and an incentive to get up and out. 
I enjoyed the idea of the free happy hour wine, but unfortunately am not a fan of Rex Goliath wine and we left most of the wine we took undrunk.

title: “Turned Me Off W Hotels (Almost) Permanently”
text: I have top tier status at Starwood hotels so I typically would try to stay at a Starwood property if possible (for the various benefits and points). I was traveling to Dallas on a weekly basis for work during this summer and tried to give this W Hotel a try for 3 separate occasions. Each time a new issue would come up (from being given rooms that was absolutely not what I had reserved, to terrible service at front desk, to issues with room service and potentially dirty food). In my subsequent visits to Dallas, I have switched to staying at the Ritz-Carlton which is exponentially better, for a similar price.

title: “Loved the Argonaut”
text:
We just returned from a visit to San Francisco and had a lovely time at the Argonaut! We weren't thrilled with our first room, but the helpful staff at the front desk made a real effort[though the hotel seemed very busy]to move us and they gave us a room with a partial view of the bay and the Golden Gate bridge. This was the first vacation we had taken in some time, so it was really appreciated.
 The staff is very friendly and down to earth and we felt almost like we were staying with friends instead of at a hotel in a big city, none of that attitude one finds at some other hotel chains. We didn't have the noise problems that some people have posted about here.
 We decided to rent a car to drive to Monterey at the last minute and the affable concierge, Ken[I believe is the name]helped get a great deal for us at the last minute. While in the wine country we thought maybe we could switch to a convertible instead because the weather was so nice and he arranged the switch and even called us back in the wine country. He sent us to a great Italian restaurant called "Antica" which was a ten minute cab ride from the hotel. He really knew the ins and outs of SanFrancisco as did the Doormen who we badgered with questions each day!
 We loved the wine hour where they serve California wine each night; and again you feel like you are visiting friends. The manager Jason chatted with us and showed real hospitality. We will definitely choose the Argonaut the next time we head out to San Francisco..Loved it!

title: “Very nice resort”
text: I could have sworn I reviewed this property soon after staying here, but that review never appeared - ?? When I saw it was ranked #2 in US resorts (I believe that was the category) I felt I needed to weigh in. While this resort is very nice, it wouldn't be my top pick in the whole country. The room is beautifully furnished, but not that big. I don't know that I'd want to stay there for longer than a few days before I'd feel like we were on top of each other. The bathroom was certainly the best part of the room -- spacious and well appointed. But the opening into the room made no sense to me. Our "shutters" closing this opening kept popping open and we had to have housekeeping come and fix them closed. As other reviewers have noted, some of the rooms have no usable balcony, which was unfortunately the case with our room. Why would you not have a space in some of the rooms where you could sit and enjoy the lovely scenic grounds? Yes, the service is outstanding and they truly want to help you however they can. All staff was friendly, saying hello in the halls. About the halls -- our room was way at the end of the building so we spent a long time walking in freezing halls. When the temperature is only the low 70's I couldn't understand why they over air conditioned the halls. Thankfully we were here with a business group and someone else was picking up the tab. I inquired about additional nights and found it is very expensive. It is a very nice resort, but I didn't feel it was worth the price. The main reason I'm giving it 4 stars is that we were consistently disappointed by the food. We had a few dinners and cocktail parties, and there were flaws with each meal. Perhaps I am being picky, but if it's a top resort the food should be great too. We had better meals in the town of Del Mar. The activities they offered were a wonderful addition to our stay -- I took a canyon hike and had friends who took fitness classes. As nice as it was, I have no desire to go back, which is why I don't understand it's top rating in the country!

title: “Great budget hotel”
text:
Positive.
1) Great location yards from Times Square.
2) Staff very friendly.
3) Good rates considering location.
4) Hotel and rooms very clean (tip the cleaners)
5) Free wifi.
Negative.
1) Outside generators very noisy during night . We initially changed rooms due to the droning noise however our new room was also noisy.(A bit picky I know but if you value your sleep take ear plugs)
2) Our room 415 had an adjoining door to 414 and we could hear every conversation, yawn and burp from next door, so again be aware of this.
Apart from the above negative comments my wife and I enjoyed our time in New York and would recomend this hotel for persons on a budget. We may have just been a bit unlucky with our room because after reading previous comments about this hotel , on the whole I agree with them, however we would probably try another hotel next time .
Make sure you visit the retail outlet about an hr from the city. You can get a bus from the Port Authority station.

title: “Great option near the airport”
text:
A good place to stay before or after a flight. This property met or exceeded all "Courtyard" brand standards. 
Service was terrific: airport shuttle was prompt when we arrived, and was made available to us for other local requirements (getting to car rental, etc.) The people were exceptionally friendly and accomodating all throughout -- at a level you'd expect from a 5-star that drills their staff on politeness, really.
We didn't use the in-room internet, but the business center was convenient. The fitness center was adequate as well -- with fresh towels and water even at the odd hour I used it.
Alas, the beds weren't as comfortable as they could have been, but once again, a high-end matress isn't part of the Courtyard brand standard (as much as perhaps it should be.)
Lobby breakfast was a continental "plus" -- eggs and waffles had to be made yourself on the provided griddle. Still, no complaints about that.

title: “A great place to stay with kids.”
text:
The Embassy Suites was a great family hotel.The rooms are built around a large atrium, so there is plenty of greenery and open space.A plesent change from the narrow corridors of normal hotels.The suite had two rooms of a good size for a family of four, very clean with a fridge. Breakfast was included with a chef who would cook you an omlete to order.In the evening at 5.30 there were free drinks and snaks for guests in the large lobby area.
I wouldn't get over excited about the pool as its not big and as we stayed in August it was full of kids most of the time.To be fair, they do have an adult only time later in the evening.There was free pc and internet access in the business centre.
It was about a 250m walk to either Dupoint Circle or Foggy Bottom subway stations.Georgetown was a comfortable 20 minute stroll along M street, with lots of nice resturants and shops.
The Embassy is a good, well located, affordable base to stay if you are exploring Washington with kids.We did stay in the summer holidays so there were lots of kids, so if you looking for a romantic stay away from yours perhaps its not for you.

title: “One night stop in NY”
text:
Stopped one night on Manhattan en route on a business trip.
Usual small room I have stopped in in previous visits to NY, but smart, clean and comfortable.
Location of hotel just off Times Square but far enough away from the bustle.
Staff very friendly and courteous, breakfast served next door or as room service.

title: “Quality hotel in a great location”
text:
I stayed here with my Mum 8 Sept - 12th Sept and we enjoyed it. Had a double double room which was a good size. Bed linen was lovely and had doubled headed shower.
Toilet sounded like an airplane loo so a bit of a rude awakening if you needed to go during the night!
We were on the 29th floor so good view and no noise issues even though the hotel is right by Times Square and Broadway.
No free internet access which I thought was a bit rich as it cost over £200 ($400) a night to stay in the hotel!

title: “The perfect place to stay in New York”
text:
Having been to NY 5 times and always stayed in mid town we were keen to stay closer to the areas we spend most fo our time in. And as a 7 month pregnant lady we wanted to make this trip memorable as it will be our last as a twosome.
We found this hotel on the New York Times website (always a good start) and couldn't fault a thing. From the moment we arrived we had such a warm welcome and the guys couldnt do enough to make us feel at home. The hotel itself is realy nicely done. The collection of old movie posters everywhere is a lovely touch and we were thrilled ot be in the Tony Curtis room (next door to the doris day room natch).
The room was spotless with a big comfy bed, nice ensuite bathroom with a good power shower. Not huge but bigger than many of the other boutique hotels we've stayed at in NY.
The breakfast being included was great too - lovely fresh coffee, muffins, bagels and doughnuts plus cereal, yoghurt and fruit set us up well for our days out.
And the location was perfect. A 10 minute walk to the magnolia Bakery and the gorgeousness of the west village on the doorstep. Then Pastis and all the other Meatpacking district bars and restaurants at the end of the street.
Don't miss the highline walk whilst you're there. A beautiful way to see the city and again right on the doorstep.
I coudn't recommend this place more. We are used to staying in lovely boutique hotels that cost twice as much but have not had as warm a welcome as we did here.

title: “Big Bang for your Buck”
text:
We stayed one night at the Comfort Inn & Suites on our way back from a 10 day trip just prior to going back to Hawaii and had a very good experience. Some of the positives of this hotel are:
1. The front desk workers are marvelous. They were fast, friendly, and very helpful to anything we needed. Check-in and check-out was a breeze and they took the time out to talk with me and answer some "tourist" questions that I had.
2. The rooms were in excellent condition. I hear other reviewers crying about how old the rooms are. To me, the rooms were in great condition especially when you consider the price. If you want custom decor, fancy carpet, a luxurious bathroom, etc. then shell out the dough and go to a 4+ star hotel.
3. Parking was only $8 per day. We payed $22/day (for 3 days) at the DoubleTree downtown which was very difficult to do being that we were hotel guests. Some people talk about lack of parking space or location of parking, but we found the parking adequate. Unless each room gets their own stall, you can't expect a prime spot all the time.
4.The location is in the Hotel Circle area. Very convenient to get on and off of the freeways. The outside automobile noise was non-existent once you went inside the room. It's also a stone throw's away from the Mission Valley and Fashion Valley Malls. There are also ton's of stores and eateries in the area.
Some of the things that could have been better were:
1. Breakfast was like a madhouse - People were everywhere and the food ran out quickly. It was amazing watching some of the guests take food and eat. You would think as though it was their last meal on earth. When things are free you notice some level of class goes down the drain but I guess that's human nature. A big downer was that breakfast wait staff were not too friendly and NONE of them were smiling. I've read a recent review saying that the breakfast staff seemed overwhelmed and that is very accurate. They looked like they weren't enjoying their jobs. Since the breakfast area is so small, we took our food back to our room as there were no open seats available. Having a complimentary breakfast is such a breath of fresh air and we really appreciated it. Maybe a bigger room and a friendlier breakfast staff (it's hard to look at long faces so early) would've made our morning.
2. Noise from rooms - We stayed on St. Patricks Day and there seemed to be various high school and college groups in the hotel. One thing we didn't like was that the noise level (after 11 p.m.) was not policed better. It would be nice if a security staff member come around after hours to maintain the noise level in on the floors. There were kids running around chasing each other in and out of rooms on our floor. As we walked pass other rooms on our floor, the loud laughing and screaming were very audible. We were glad that they weren't our neighbors for the night.
All in all, we had a great experience at the hotel. The staff's friendliness and professionalism made our stay comfortable. We definitely would stay here again and recommend it to our friends. Mahalo!

title: “Great location beautiful room”
text: We stayed in a newly refurbished king room, even though not overly large it was a lovely room. The staff were excellent and went out of their way to advise and help. It is right next to grand central station so very convenient to everything. Loved everything about this hotel and would stay there again. Best hotel we stayed at on a 3 week tour of the USA.

title: “Small but perfectly formed”
text:
Just back from 5 nights in New york where we stayed at the Distrikt Hotel. Local area is a bit shabby but never felt unsafe as there was always lots of people around. It is an easy walk to Times Square and the metro stations. 
Rooms were a good size, and shower rm was fine, but the biggest plus for me was the beds and pillows were incredibly comfortable, and i've stayed in lots of hotels were that has not been the case! Free internet was a plus, as were the complimentary drinks in reception. Only used the restaraunt once for breakfast but it was very reasonably priced and the food was good.
Would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Lovely hotel”
text:
I stayed here with my husband, and we both loved the hotel. OK the room was small but very clean. We had a room with shared bathroom, but this was no probleme at all. All the shared bathrooms were clean and tidy.
The location is superb (upper midtown),it´s a great neighborhood nearby tourist attractions as Top of the Rock and museums as MoMA.
Overall a great and inexpensive NYC hotel!

title: “Lovely Hotel, Great Location”
text: I had a wonderful stay for a long weekend in August. The staff couldn't have been nicer or more accomodating. Lots of nice little touches like bathrobs, Aveda bath products, wine in the evenings, etc. I really felt pampered and well taken care of. The location couldn't be beat! Just blocks from the Art Institute, Millenium and Grant parks, and easy access to public transportation. I would stay here again in a heartbeat!

title: “Decent value for a short stay”
text:
Stayed for a week with spouse while on vacation
PROS:
* great location, center Midtown, walking distance to 5th ave, many restaurants, stores, museums
* affordable price compared to other Midtown hotels
* very friendly staff at the front desk
* lots of TV channels to select from
* free wi-fi, although sometimes spotty
* one complimentary cocktail at the bar downstairs
* big fast elevators
* had several windows in the room even though it was tiny
* safe in the room
* free internet access in the lobby (via iPads)
CONS:
* super tiny room, can only stow about 2 mid to small size suitcases under the double bed
* transparent door/wall to the bathroom, you can pretty much see everything... not sure why the entire glass was not frosted
* room service is inconsistent... some days we got new towels, other days we didn't.. one day all of our unused shampoos/soaps were taken away and not replaced... bring your own toiletries
* no ice machine, although we were able to get some ice at the bar downstairs for free
* heating was super loud when it kicked in.. would recommend having it turned off at night - the building was warm enough in late November to keep the heat through the night
TIPS:
* parking is at the ICON garage off 3rd Ave between 37th and 38th... $25 per vehicle, $40 for oversized (SUV's) with hotel stamped ticket
* cocktails somewhat expensive at the bar - walk to Lexington for other options
* reservations are held until 11pm otherwise call to ensure you still have a room
* lots of good tourist info at the front desk - maps, directions, airport shuttle reservations

title: “Enjoyable stay”
text: My daughter and I were in Chicago for a couple of days during Christmas week, investigating potential neighborhoods for her this summer. We used Hotwire for our room. I emailed the hotel and requested two queen beds which they were kind enough to guarantee. It was an easy train trip from Midway to the Grand stop; then a short walk to the Intercontinental. It's located on Mich. Ave in the heart of the Magnificent Mile. We arrived at 10am and our room was ready for us. They upgraded us to an historic tower room on the 23rd floor. Very nice, big room with two large windows and two queen beds. The beds were quite far apart with a big night table between them that held two large lamps. There were upscale amenities as well as bathrobes. The bathroom was standard fare with a tub/shower combo. and plenty of good quality towels, as well as a 4 cup coffee maker and a hair dryer. Internet was for a fee. It is tricky when signing on --the higher priced option shows first at 17.95. Hit the down arrow next to it and the 14.95 option is visible. We paid because we needed internet access, but felt seriously ripped-off. If all you need is to visit airline websites for seat ressies and/or printing boarding passes there is free access in the lobby for that. There is a Starbucks just off the lobby. We did not try any of the hotel restaurants since there are so many outstanding choices in the area, but we did order room service breakfast our last morning. It arrived within the promised time frame and the table fit very easily in our large room. We ordered simply- fresh fruit, muesli, coffee, etc. Presentation and quality were good. We had a great time in a very nice hotel in a world-class city.

title: “Excellent staff and an overall friendly hotel.”
text: Great location, facilities, and rooms, but the service is what sets this place apart. I've stayed at all the high end chains in DC and these guys do it best.

title: “Great Location, Excellent Service”
text: This resort has an excellent location, within walking distance to the Mission Beach boardwalk and a short drive to Sea World. The staff are friendly and respectful and give very good service. The on-site lounge is a cozy place to hang out after a long day of meetings. As others on this site have commented, there is some variability in the quality and comfort of rooms, although the Bahia has undergone a slow yet steady renovation. One should try to avoid rooms in the main tower on the far south end of the property - lots of these rooms are musty with 1960s style. On this trip, I stayed in a newly renovated room in the 300s building. Not only was it spacious with an extremely comfortable bed, there was kitchenette and large flat screen TV. There is also free wifi with a great signal throughout the property. Will definitely consider staying here in the future.

title: “Good Value, nice place”
text: We stayed at The Laurel Inn for 2 nights in July 2011. Older building but clean rooms. Very convenient for public transportation use. Good Value! Enjoyed the free drinks from the hotel at the adjoining lounge, Swanks.

title: “Lovely Stay, made me feel at home!”
text:
Me an my husband stayed here for 3 weeks and I felt so much at home! Lovely helpful staff.
Very clean, free WiFi, lovely location what else do you need!
It was hard to leave the place...
I shall be back!
Best Wishes to The Inn at Union Square and each of the Staff Members!
Regards
Gauri Gupte

title: “Our perfect Family Retreat!”
text: A HUGE THANK YOU to the Ballantyne Hotel for the wonderful opportunity for our family to experience a weekend get-away! We are local to Charlotte and chose the Ballantyne Hotel for it's fine reputation. The service was exceptional along with the luxurious accommodations. Our children had such a great time enjoying the amenities of the Resort and especially the indoor pool. It was a weekend of great memories made for our entire family. We are already planning another weekend away. Thanks again to the caring staff that anticapated our desires and fulfilled even our uxpressed wishes! Gratefully, The Bennett Family

title: “Terrible Experience!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: My experience at the Renaissance was Terrible!!!!!!! I had a reservation set for a Saturday thur Monday. When I drove from South Carolina to finally het settled in my room I was told at check oh did any one contact you about our power outage? I said no! He continued to say we will have a power outage for the next two days. I came here for a surprise birthday weekend for my boyfriend and this was the start of a terrible stay! He told me I will give you free breakfast because of the outage but I already had breakfast figured into my bill, so he said they would transfer me over to the Mariott their sister hotel. I was so pissed but didnt have any other choice. We got to the Marriott to check in they told me my breakfast will not be in with the price any more because I receive military discount. So we went to the room walked in and the first thing that hit me was a molded scent. The room was nothing like I paid for at the Renaissance. It was soo much smaller... Sheets were molded and the cable kept losing signal during the playoffs... I will be writing a review for the Mariott also! When I did check out I was charged an extra $47.00 which they couldnt explain why it was charged to my account and then I check my bank statement and Rennaissance charged me $137.00 when I didnt even stay there. After going through about 3 people I finally got the manager and he didnt make it any better!! he said he would check on it to see if I could get my money back because I was charged for a no show fee. Which i was like how could you charge me that when you sent me to another hotel.. I then asked will I at least be comp a one night stay since I had to go through all of this mess that ruined my weekend he said no I dont see why I should!!! I will never stay at a Rennaisance or Marriott hotel again.. For almost $300 for 2 nights and i had to smell mold and ask for a microwave and refrigarator to be bought to the room and the cable kept losing the signal.. Never again and I would advise anyone else from staying at these hotels if you want to enjoy your hotel stay. Find somewhere esle..Horrible Customer Service!!!!!!!

title: “Always A great Value At the Blake!”
text: This was our second stay at the Blake and I was skeptical if it was going to be as good as the first stay. One word, BETTER! The staff is first rate, the doormen helpful as always, the rooms clean and comfortable. You cannot, i repeat cannot stay at a nicer, homier and friendly place than this. I love this hotel!! See you soon!

title: “What you pay for..”
text: is what you get. Just be prepared for planes, they come down so close it looks like they are going to land on the roof.

title: “Great Find”
text: Great deal for NYC at $155 nightly (with breakfast and during the holiday season). Excellent mid town location. Clean and newish looking. As for NY budget accommodations goes this is very reasonably priced. Recommended.

title: “Good Airport Hotel”
text:
Stayed here for 1 night.
Hotel: Very un-Sheraton looking. Sleek & Modern on the inside. Doormen did not offer to help with the bags but I guess we looked like we did not need assistance. They were pleasant though. The front desk was very helpful at check in and check out. Nice pool area with whirlpool (had leaves in it) as well. There was a bar and 2 restaurants (1 AM and 1 PM) and a Starbucks. Shuttle to the airport very early in the morning was spot on.
Room: Very nice. Horrible noise from the air con that the maintenance man fixed straight away. Comfy bed. TV had some sound issues. I could not get the broadband to work but that was my computers fault. Good size desk. Very little outside noise noticed. USA Today at the door in the morning. Adequate bathroom facilites and good towels. 
This is a good choice if you need a hotel at LAX.

title: “Excellent staff”
text: The hotel is very large in size and clean. Great for business groups and weddings. Mr. Henry and Miss Crystal at the front desk were nice, friendly, and very helpful with my questions. The food at the hotel was excellent. Our room was restocked with supplies and cleaned everyday by the lovely Mrs. Maria. The hotel shuttle service was handy for me. Mr. Leon took me to the small shopping malls across the street, and he told me about the local area. I love the array of restaurants around the hotel and there is a theater too. I can say that I ate delicious food inside and outside the hotel. I was always greeted with smiling face's from the staff. Which means alot when you're away from home.

title: “Well-equipped units in ideal location”
text: The Suites at Fisherman's Wharf was built as apartments decades ago, but the property has been nicely refurbished. The 24 units are located around a central indoor courtyard, with comfy chairs and a soothing fountain. Our 1 BR unit with full kitchen faced the nearby houses, so there wasn't any "view" - from the unit. (It was very quiet.) Some units do have balconies. The property has a roof-top terrace with a great view north to the Bay - and Alcatraz Island. The Suites are ideally situated on both bus and cable car lines, with an easy walk to two grocery stores. Great restaurants in the Fisherman's Wharf area are just down the street, along with all that there is to do in that area.

title: “Awesome Weekend Stay”
text: Wonderful hotel in downtown Denver. Rooms were great. Food was great. Allen from Valet was great. Allen went above and beyond assisting us with my daughters dance competition props. We will return. Only negative is that people smoke at entrance.

title: “5 STAR ONLY BECAUSE THEY DON'T MAKE A 10 STAR RATING”
text: There is not enough space here to cover our total experience. I have stayed in many 5 Star hotels in the last 40 years. MGM Detroit has found a way to excell far beyond the 5 Star rating. From the greeters at the door, Shawnee, and the incredible person(s) in charge of cleaning our room, we felt like we were the only guests in the hotel and it was everyone's job to spoil us. I intend to write a complimentary personal letter to the hotel manager for putting together such a remarkable team.

title: “This Hotel is Ideal for Everybody”
text:
This hotel is marvelous. The rooms are spacious with great views and a huge lovely shower. The bed is plush and the TV has many stations including a Broadway channel so you can see what show strikes your fancy.
The morning breakfast is ridiculously good and varied, get there early and enjoy it!
The staff is fast and helpful. Special thanks to Javon who was so kind and funny and made our stay that much better. The bartender was knowledgeable about her product and the surrounding area, and the maids were quiet and effective with helpful tips of their own.
I would stay here again. You are close enough to the action but far away enough to have safety and peace.

title: “Customer service was top notch”
text:
My husband and I recently visited the Andaz San Diego for a weekend staycation. The customer service at this modern boutique hotel was absolutely the best thing about it, not to say that there was really anything bad about it. From the moment you walk in the door, the staff does everything possible to make you feel like you are the only person in the room. They offer you refreshments as you are waiting for your room and make sure that you know everything the hotel has to offer. We arrived before our room was ready, so they stored our luggage and took our information so they could contact us when our room was ready. The room we requested was not available (a king bed) so they offered us a queen and, for the trouble, brought up a bottle of wine and cheese plate. The rooms are not very big, again not a big deal to us, but they are modern in their decor, beds are very comfortable and have plenty little extras (refreshments) to make up for the size. 
The bad - lots of noise at night (which is why I gave it very good instead of excellent). 3 nightclubs on the property, I believe. If you are looking for a nice quiet place to get a good nights sleep, this is not it. However, I think most people that stay here are more interested in the night life.
I wouldn't suggest this as a family hotel, definitely not a place I'd bring my children. Especially with the "adult toys" available, for a fee, in your room between the jelly beans and M and M's. Think of it kind of like Las Vegas in the middle of San Diego. Overall, a great place for a couple to get away, a girls weekend or to be in the middle of all that's going on downtown.

title: “Nice, but soooo small!”
text:
I stayed at the Hudson with my husband for 6 nights at the beginning of July. I was pleased with the service, cleanliness, and location of
this hotel. I know all the reviews have mentioned how small this hotel is, and I would have to agree. We stayed in the standard queen bed room and were fortunate to get a a bathroom with a bathtub. Unless you're willing to pick up everything every morning so that housekeeping can even get to the bed or into the bathroom, this isn't
the place for you. While this hotel would be okay for a night or two,
there's just no room to spread out and relax at all. The TV is a tiny
corner unit inside a cabinet as well. I understand that no one comes to NY to stay in their room, but after a day of sightseeing and walking starting at 8 or 9 in the morning, you're ready to relax at least a couple of the nights. Also, getting a room higher up is a must if you want quiet. The disco/bar really starts to crank up the volume starting at 10:30/11:00PM and will continue through 1:30AM. We
stayed on the 16th floor and could still hear the crowd shout out occassionaly even with the air conditioner on. Overall, yes the coolness factor is definitely there, but for 6 nights the cramped quarters will definitely start to get to you.

title: “The place was first class all the way”
text:
They did ask when I checked in if I was going to be dining tonight, this is run like a big buck hotel (for as as I know about big buck hotels). Lots of help, addressing people by name when you call the front desk, high ceilings, glass and shiny stuff everywhere. The couple ahead of me looked as out of place as I did, a young couple in their early 20’s with just one small backpack between them.
Anyone who has read my other reviews knows that I'm often staying in motels that are $30 or less if I don't fear for my safety. Cheapest online rate for this motel tonight was $185, but I'm here on an airline voucher.
The place was first class all the way, my only issue was when they wanted to charge me $12.95 to use the internet, sorry, I can wait until I'm back to the airport. (Remember, I'm cheap)
This is the kind of place you go for special occasions.

title: “Great location”
text:
We arrived at the Hilton Gardens Inn Times Square around 7.30pm after a long flight and checked in immediately and had a couple of very tasty complementary cookies from reception. The hotel is in a great location - 8th Ave between 49th and 48th Sts 
The rooms were nicely presented, and the bathroom was a good size - I expected the room and the bathroom to be cramped, but was pleasantly suprised that we didn't feel that way at all. There was a small refrigerator and a microwave as well as coffee making facilities and these came in handy because we bought some cereal and milk and had that for breakfast - unfortunately breakfast wasn't included in our room price.
For Australians booking a room, I'd suggest booking a King Room because their Queen size beds definitely appear smaller than the standard Queen back home. However the free WIFI was a bonus which really came in handy.
As for location, it was great. It's easy walking distance from the colourful and vibrant Times Square, tons of theatres and lots of restaurants too.
Close to the Hotel is a supermarket (8th Ave/49th St) where you can breakfast or grab a frozen meal or perhaps heat something up in the microwave in your room. 
Also very close by are a couple of entrances to the subway which was very handy after a long day, and on 8th Ave between 47th - 48th, the (red) HOHO buses depart from here - as a matter of fact, their office is across the street.

title: “LOVED the Argonaut Hotel”
text: I cannot say enough good things about this hotel--the extremely well decorated nautical theme makes you feel sophisticated and comfortable all at once. Service is excellent, and not "snobby" at all.
