The room was spotless, the furnishings amazing (internet access great, despite a fee), friendly leopard print robes contrast nicely with the nautical theme, and the bed with high quality linens was superb! Complimentary wine hour each day in lobby. The hotel was actually part of the old Cannery buildings, and the exposed brick and wooden beam connections inside each room is an amazing detail. The hotel connects to a National Park museum, and it has a great display of maritime pieces. It is also a short walk down the street to an additional larger National Park Maritime museum, short walk to all Fisherman's Wharf activities (try the Boudin Sourdough Bread shop and museum), and right next door to the Hyde Street Cable Car turn-around point and Ghirardelli chocolate shops. I much prefer the fresh, new, nautical themed Argonaut to any other hotel I've been in. Plus, they will match any internet advertised rate, so it can be very affordable considering it is San Francisco (we paid $143 per night in February). You will enjoy this adventure!

title: “OK but not what we'd hoped for”
text:
We recently returned from an OK but not great 1 night stay in the Magnolia in Denver.
First, the good - the location is great - 1 block from shoping on 16th street and within easy walking distance to many other sites like the Capitol and Mint. The staff we spoke with were all very courteous, friendly and helpful. The breakfast selection was good, with a number of premade warm selections, and ample seating, at least at 9:45, just before closing.
The 'bad' wasn't really bad but made the stay less enjoyable that I'd anticipated. Our double queen room was quite small but clean. It also, like many other rooms in the hotel, looked out on what could perhaps be called an 'inner courtyard' but which was really just the entrance area far below - 20 feet across from our window was another resident's window. In fariness this could have been because I'd asked for a quiet room. The lobby was somewhat small and too dark, and the hallways and room felt quite stuffy (the latter was rectified by turning on the too-loud AC). They put us in 1 of two adjoining rooms, with only a thin door between us, and the other room's occupant included a crying baby - on came the AC and accompanying noisy fan all night even though I'm quite sure there were plenty of vacant rooms that evening - why do they always put people right next to each other? The 'milk and cookies' evening treat turned out to be 'cookies' - the milk was all gone and no one was in sight to help with the issue - I ended up buying my daughter some water. Parking was $26 for 1 night - yes its a city but this is still too much. Vending and ice appear to be on one floor only - not a big deal and perhaps quieter but made for quite a few elevator trips. The bathroom vanity was only slightly wider than the sink even though there was perhaps 16" of unused bathroom space just to the side of it - why not fill and use that space so we can put out all our things? We weren't at the hotel for the happy hour but the concierge was kind enough to provide us with slips of paper entitling us to a free beer at a nearby restaurant.
All in all we expected to love the Magnolia and you can tell we didn't. There are many other choices near 16th Street - we'll check out another next time we're in town.

title: “Just fine, thanks”
text: We stay here often -- the price is good and the rooms are mostly decent-sized. Breakfast is good. It's really close to the subway and the windows actually open. Two complaints: The lighting in the rooms is pretty dim and takes a while to get up to full brightness. The toilet paper holders drag the toilet paper over the wet bathroom wall. Oh, and if you've got anything long you want to hang up, ask for a room with a full-length closet -- some are only torso-length.

title: “Nice, new and clean . . . but nothing nearby”
text:
As written elsewhere this hotel is quite new and aside from an equally new HGI adjacent there is nothing at all here. No fuel (vehicle or human), no coffee shops, no quick mart. NOTHING.
Literally 2 minutes from the airport, it doesn't get easier than this.
Nice room - shandard Hampton but very clean and everything worked. Front desk staff couldn't have been nicer. Breakfast was better than usual for Hampton.
I'd probably stay one exit back and across I70 at the the Hampton Plainview next time only so I wouldn't have to scout so far for food and gas but if being really close to the airport is a major consideration you can't do better than this.

title: “Average hotel in a fantastic location”
text: We recently spent a week at the Crescent Hotel, it was everything the other reviewers mentioned. We had a room at the front of the hotel and it was very noisy, but we spent so little time in the room that we didn't bother complaining or trying to get moved, on the plus side the room was a good size and the bed was really comfortable. I thought the reception staff were friendly and helpful. What this hotel has going for it is the location and the price. We booked on hot-wire and it cost approx $60 a night and it is right downtown and for this reason I would stay there again

title: “Great value for the money”
text:
Got this room for $50 on Priceline. Needed a hotel for a pre-cruise and post-cruise stay.
The location was a little iffy. We walked by some people that made us feel unsafe. I would not walk around as a single or couple after dark here. Lots of homeless and seedy characters in the downtown area.
The hotel itself was fine. We detected a musty odor in the rooms on our first visit. A little street noise, not too bad. No smell in the room on the second stay. The rooms were clean, if not a little dated looking. Bathroom was also clean.
We tried the hot tub and gym on the lobby floor and they also were clean. The gym had 2 machines, I think, very small.
The free breakfast was great: fresh fruit, yogurts, pastries, muffins, bagels, bread for toasting, waffle irons, coffee, tea, milk, etc. We took afvantage of breakfast every day.
There is a Whole Foods Mkt closeby that has lots of meal selections. We ate lunch at the Korean place across the street, it was good. We also had dinner at Two Bells Tavern and it was GREAT! Voted best burgers in Seattle. We also had pizza delivered from Paggliaci's and it was surprisingly good to us finicky NYers.
We were close to the Space Needle and it took us about 20 minutes to walk to Pikes Market.
The front desk staff was very accomodating and helped us with transportation and took care of our luggage when we could not check in early.
Note that this is a completely non-smoking hotel and you sign a waiver stating that you will be charged $250 if you smoke in your room. There even is a sign outside that you cannot smoke within 100 ft of the building.
All in all, a good value for the price. Gotta love that free breakfast!

title: “Impressed with this property”
text: My husband and I recently stayed at this Holiday Inn for two nights during the first part of our trip to Boston. I had some concerns after reading other reviews here but was pleasantly surprised. The location of this hotel is what makes it so great. Right in the heart of Beacon Hill, within walking distance of many wonderful things to do and see as well as lots of good restaurants and bars. The hotel was a quick ($20) cab ride from the airport. We were upgraded to the Executive Floor so we had a great view of Beacon Hill. The room was nice and the bed was comfortable. The bathroom was clean but the shower water was not very hot so that was a bit disappointing. We were also given free coupons for the continental breakfast--glad we didn't pay for it, not worth it at all. The staff was nice and helpful. I definitely recommend all Boston tourists hotel jump a bit, staying in various neighborhoods. And when you stay in Beacon Hill, this is a good choice.

title: “Hidden Gem at a great price”
text:
We stayed here this past weekend and it was great! 
The staff was very friendly and attentive and the location is perfect. Right next to a subway and it's a great area of NYC.
Now with the bed bug problem in NYC we were worried but everything was very clean and the beds were comfortable. The only complaint I had was that my 6'4" husband had to duck and walk in sideways into the very small bathroom. Was not a huge deal because it was actually pretty funny. I will definitely stay here on my next visit.

title: “Nice Hotel in downtown Denver”
text:
Stayed at the Magnolia for 4 days in June 2012.
Nice rooms, excellent location in downtown Denver -15 minutes walk from the convention center, and around the corner from the pedestrian shopping street.
The only criticism that could be made of the hotel would be the strong smell of food overflowing from the kitchen to the lobby area.

title: “Old New York Charm in a great location --- great bed and good value”
text: We got a great deal on two nights ($139). The hotel staff was efficient and friendly when we checked in. Of course, the rooms were small and the king sized bed took up the entire room. But, the nice linens and comfy bed made up for it. The shower had two temperatures ...SCORCHING HOT and ICE COLD. Since we were there for a short time, we suffered through it. The hotel looks a bit old...but in a charming way. Grand Central Station is literally accross the street and Times Square is just a few blocks away. The decor and feel is kind of a throw back to early 20th century New York and Eddie the bartender at the lobby bar had a great sense of humor and took good care of us. I would stay there again since we had such a wonderful time---but I would also want to experiment with other hotels. Great location and Great bed for a good price.

title: “bedbugs”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 5 nights in April 2012, on the 3rd night bumps started showing on my neck and hands. I did not really know what bed bug bites would look like so I thought they were pimples or maybe allergies, but my friend saw a bug on the bed. We planned on letting the desk know the next day – we did not know how serious having a bed bug bite/infestation was at that time. We were very busy with the convention that the bed bug issue was forgotten. Also, unfortunately, the bumps were still not itchy while we were at the hotel. But 2 days after leaving the hotel, more and more bites are showing and getting worse on my fingers, hands, arms, chest, neck, face and feet. They are severely itchy that I can hardly sleep and function. The welts/ redness are also very embarrassing and I am suffering from anxiety whether I brought home the bugs. One of my colleagues who shared the room with me also has bed bug bites on his legs and feet that manifested several days after we checked out.
Bedbug bites are terrible! I should have read the review here that indicated the presence of bedbugs in this hotel.

title: “Dark, small rooms, understaffed”
text:
Now let me first say that I stayed there during Hurricane Irene, so some of their staffing problems could have been (and probably were) caused by the fact that the hotel was pretty full and the staff couldn't get there. That said, the staff didn't seem eager to get customers into their rooms or checked out too quickly. I stood in line for 15 minutes while one staffer counted out money to a befuddled European tourist and the other was giving detailed directions on what to do and where to go in NY. All I wanted to do was check out!
The internet was non-existent, the restaurant expensive and not very good with long waits and uncomfortable seats that resembled cafeteria-style buffet service. Despite this they were "nice" enough to include suggested tips of 15, 20 and 25%. 25% for a guy who brings you a drink while you have to get your own food?
The room was nearly as small as the bed. The toilet so small it was hard to sit down. I felt like a giant in this place. Everything was dark with little seating in the lobby. The bar was a nightmare with tourists cutting the line and drinks that were priced at obscene levels. 9$ for a Heineken.
I will say the staff was friendly, if not very helpful or knowledgeable, the room was clean (although because of the hotel not made up on the 2nd day). The bed was stiff, cheap and uncomfortable but the pillows were feathered and fantastic. 
I would recommend staying elsewhere while in NYC. There are much better places.

title: “Excellent hotel, great service”
text: We stayed here for our honeymoon for 10 nights. The staff here are so helpful and friendly, you can certainly see that these people love their jobs here and the city, nothing is to much trouble. We were left some goodies in our room for our arrival congratulating us on our wedding, which was a very nice touch. The facebook page this hotel has is so helpful and gives you lots of information on the city and things to do. The rooms and lovely and clean and I cannot thank the staff enough for making our honeymoon special. Our room had a lovely view (30th floor) of the Hudson River on the right and the Empire State Building on the left, perfect to wake up to on a morning.

title: “Amazing staff and customer service at this beautiful hotel!”
text: We had an amazing experience at the Muse! The staff went above and beyond to help us out in a stressful situation that included a trip to the emergency room for one of our party. I am a frequent traveler, but don't think I had ever come across a hotel staff that took care of us like these guys did. Linda and Sarah (and the rest of the staff) rock! I'm not sure what kind of customer service training they do, but it is the best! Stay here!

title: “Step into the time machine, and stay in the 1980s”
text:
We loved the Park Lane for a number of reasons, the most obvious of which are the views of the park and the snob value of directing your cab to "The Park Lane, please". 
The hotel is so desperately in need of a refurb that it is actually cool to stay in a junior suite with brown corduroy couches and a pink shaggy rug. We really felt like we could bump into JR Ewing in the corridor at any time. Don't let the ageing nature of the hotel put you off - it makes such a change from the usual shiny new hotels that a step back in time is awesome. 
The wifi is patchy and the breakfast was okay, but otherwise everything including the service and the fading photo of Mrs Helmsley in the foyer is simply superb.

title: “Great Suite”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel on a Sunday night for our anniversary. I booked the room through Hotel Allegro's website and got an excellent sale rate for a 2 room suite complete with a 2 person jacuzzi tub. The room was fantastic! There was a very large living room with a flat panel TV , couch, table for four and a desk. The bedroom was a perfect size with a comfortable king sized bed with comfy bedding as well as an additional flat panel TV. The jacuzzi was excellent - big enough for 2, square in shape. 
The lobby is very tastefully decorated. We attended the wine hour in the lobby and enjoyed some Chardonnay and Merlot. The staff was pleasant enough, especially the bellman. 
We would definitely stay here again, as long as we were able to book a suite.

title: “Pretty, but dull - and tiny!”
text:
The Carlton is a classic old school hotel - grand lobby, beautiful furnishing and TINY rooms. The photos posted on the web of the "standard room" which showed an armchair, bed and desk were nothing like the room we had, which had a bed, a small desk and desk chair and about 1 square foot of space. No where to put a suitcase (it did have drawers and a small closet, but this meant unpacking for our short stay). Nowhere other than the bed to sit. I know that New York hotel rooms are small . The bathroom was beautiful and had a bath and a shower, but again, did not even have a shelf or any other space to put your toothbrush & toiletries. We also had an extremely loud heater/air con that kept me awake much of the night. 
The area appears very safe. To me, having stayed downtown in the past, it was dull and lacked places to eat nearby. That said, the concierge was very helpful at making reservations or suggeting places to eat. It is close to the some of the shopping areas and the empire state. It's about as far away from a subway station as you can get in Manhatten (which is still not that far)

title: “A GREAT stay.......!”
text: We stayed at this quality Hotel on Sunday the 26th of July, 2009. We got the room through Priceline, and paid 1/2 of what the Internet rate was, so I was not expecting any "extra special service". We got to the Hotel at 12:00 noon, and asked if we could possible check in 3 hours early. Brandon was at the desk, and he not only checked us in early, but he put us on the 12th (top) floor, and gave us a room with a perfect view of the Ft. Worth Water Gardens. We were celebrating our 28th Anniversary, and he really tried to help us make the stay the best that it could be. That afternoon.....we got a knock on our door, and when we opened it......there was room service standing there, with a bottle of Champagne, and a plate of Chocolate covered strawberries! This place just rocks! Bed so comfortable, free internet, newly renovated room with a modern look, indoor heated pool. So much to like, so little time to enjoy it! We will most certainly be back, and will recommend it to anyone traveling to Ft. Worth. Thanks again to Brandon, and the entire staff at Sheraton Ft. Worth Hotel and Spa......you helped me treat my wife like a Queen!

title: “Good deal. Good deal. Good deal!”
text: I found a room in Roger Smith hotel which is located on Lexington Avenue and about 47/48 St for just about $160 on hotels.com. For this price and for this location, it's an amazing deal! It's extremely rare that you'll find a room right in the midtown area for such a low price. The room wasn't small either. We booked a 2 queen beds room and we could walk comfortably without running into things. I also like the fact that there were two computers in the lobby for us guests to use. The bathroom was also pretty big for NYC standard. Though, there was one thing about my bed. It made noise when I twist and turn. I'm sure this doesn't happen to every room. Bottom line is, if you see a good deal at Roger Smith, go for it! Don't doubt that it's going to be bad just becuase it's cheap. It will worth the price!

title: “Fantastic!”
text: This hotel was just fantastic. The room was exactly as it looked on the website, if not bigger and was really quiet (15th floor - loft suite). Breakfast was available in the Penthouse which had a view of the Empire State Building. Tea, coffee and water were complimentary at any time of day. A lovely place to rest and enjoy the view both day and night. We even spotted the balcony from the top of the Empire State. I can't fault this hotel, it was excellent value for money, the staff were really helpful and it was perfectly located for walking just about anywhere. We would definitely stay here again and can't wait to go back.

title: “Amazing and so needed!”
text:
My best friend and I did a short weekend stay Friday-Sunday; our first time in Charlotte and in this hotel. It was beyond amazing and we plan to return regularly. It’s the Ritz, so it’s expensive but truthfully I have stayed at other hotels which were more expensive or the same- and it’s really beyond compare.
My room rate was 305.00 a night- and included valet parking (30.00 a night) and the Carolina breakfast for two (20.00 each).
 Everything about this hotel was amazing. The staff was beyond helpful, pleasant, and overall friendly. At check in, were served a glass of champagne. Check in could not have been easier and the staff was incredibly helpful. 
Our room was spotless, beautiful, and roomy. Great closet space (two)…. All the amentias you could want- including a coffee station and a place to charge your phone. All lamps and lights had dimmers- including an area where you can push a button indicating you are ready to have your room cleaned or turn down service. 
The bathroom was large, double marble vanities and a built in flat screen TV in the mirror. Separate (large) all glass shower, separate tub, and large area that were closed off and separate from the toilet. Again, light dimmers- great bathroom. 
The lobby had a great overall feel to it… not pretentious- just very comfortable and great service. Nice bar and on Saturday night had a relaxing jazz like band- really good. BLT Steakhouse is on premises and if you stay there would defiantly recommend. Food and service is excellent! 
We loved the spa area… the top floor is a “aqua lounge”- a great pool, comfortable (padded) lounge chairs which overlook the skyline and have ceiling to floor windows- relaxing music and the pool was great. I had the best massage I have ever had (Tiffany) - and the general area was relaxing and very serene and high end. They have an amazing shower and have all the amenities you could want. 
The only complaint I could really say is like what other reviewers wrote- there is a club (several bars and such) across the street which don’t close until 2am- and are very, very loud. (There is a white noise machine in the room which helped). I mentioned it at the front desk… apparently there is no noise ordinance in this area- so it was loud. 
However, the one night we did go clubbing and it was nice to just walk across the street. Plus, it was the weekend. I’m not sure I would have been able to tolerate it though if I was there for work and needed a good night sleep. 
Housekeeping was beyond compare- really, everything was just fantastic and I could recommend this hotel to anyone. It was a fantastic stay! Loved this hotel!

title: “Crowded...but still very nice...”
text:
We happened to stay on a Saturday and I couldn't believe how crowded the parking lot was when we arrived. Apparently, there was a soccer tournament in town and some weekend meetings going on in the conference rooms. It had very little effect on our stay, though.
The bed was very comfortable...probably one of the most comfortable I've slept in at a hotel. The employees were very nice and helpful. Check-in went quickly and we had no problems with our room. My biggest complaint was that there were no towels at the pool. I know that it was crowded on and off all day, but I think there should have been someone who was responsible for making sure that the towel supply didn't get completely depleted. I saw employees walk by outside of the enclosed pool area many times, but apparently they had other jobs they were doing. There was a fire pit by the outside pool area which was very nice. We also used the indoor hot tub, but it had a green tint to it, so I had some concern about how clean it was. 
The hotel provided breakfast, lunch, dessert and snacks for the event we were attending. I was pleased with the food that was provided.
Overall, it was a good stay.

title: “Great Place to start your Journey”
text: We stayed one night on the way to Olympic NAtional park Coast. Clean, Centrally located with a nice coffee shop in the lobby, helpful staff. We booked on Priceline one did really well. Family Friendly ... we walked everywhere.

title: “Great stay”
text:
Stayed one night before flying back to UK. Wish we had stayed the 4 days at the beginning of our holiday as it was superb. The staff were really pleasant and the refurbishment amazing.
Our room was modern and beautifully decorated, complete with a wetroom instead of the dreaded bath, and a duvet on the bed. Heaven

title: “My home away from home...”
text:
I love this hotel. I've stayed at On The Ave almost every trip I have made to New York since 2001, and have nothing but raves for its staff, decor, and rooms. The modern-but-not-stark look and boutique-but-not-snobby attitude of OTA make it a hotel I truly miss when I leave.
About the only negatives I can offer are the lack of a pool and the fact that the views toward Central Park are now obstructed by a new building on 77th and Amsterdam...but hey, what are ya gonna do? It's Manhattan.
I also highly recommend four spots for food nearby. Breakast/lunch/brunch: Sarabeth's on Amsterdam (lemon and ricotta pancakes...say no more). Lunch/dinner: Shake Shack on Columbus (truly amazing burgers). Dinner: The Fatty Crab on Broadway (sort of like an Asian tapas thing). Dinner: Isabella's on Columbus (affordable and delicious...with a Dark Chocolate Bag dessert that comes complete with steak knife).

title: “NOISY, NOISY, NOISY - YOU WILL NOT SLEEP THE NIGHT - TERRIBLE LOCATION!”
text: My college daughter and I spent one night in New York City, we had a great time at the museums and in the surrounding area. We were given a room where from 11 p.m. to about 3 p.m., there were sanitation trucks that were dumping garbage and bottles dropping into containers that woke me up every time I tried to fall asleep, pretty awful and jarring. Constant beeping from cars too, no insulation in the walls (warehouse windows I believe are part of the problem too). Also the location (it's near warehouses and auto dealerships) does not warrant the hefty room and tax charge of about $460 for 2 beds, wow! This is not good value and if you're looking to stay here, I'm here to urge you to reserve a room elsewhere.

title: “Excellant property”
text: Four days well spent, off season, recouperating from a high stress life. Reviewed hotels online and this was the best price for a 4.5 star resort in a park setting for my goal of walking, yoga, massage, reading and swimming. Good beaches, well kept. Multiple swimming pools. Two good restaurants but cheapest is a bit pricey still. Loved spa massage. My sleeping cabana was on an inside lagoon perfect for relaxed sun and reading. NOTE: December maybe in the 60's but its cold and damp so bring at least one heavy sweater or coat to enjoy outside. I flew in from -10F and still was chilled. Room heat was personal control and good. Loved discovering the baby sharks and skates in the small tidal pools.

title: “i had a good time”
text: I had a great time. it was amazing!

title: “Great Location”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights with family during our trip to Washington. Great location - just across the Union Station. Room was ready on arrival . The room was little cramped though with double queen beds. Concierge was very helpful.
While booking, I was looking for a hotel with breakfast served as we had to go out everyday early morning for tours. Called up the hotel before booking to confirm and I was told there is breakfast for all rooms booked. I assumed they provide complimentary breakfast included in the room rates. But on arrival, I was told that they have A la Carte breakfast and not included in the hotel room. I wish they could have been more clearer upfront . Union Station Food Court saved us from the breakfast blues.
Could have rated higher without this confusion

title: “Okay Stay”
text:
Great location for a Nationals Game. Very close to the Metro. Hotel was clean and room was in good condition. Not a good area if looking for a resturant. Not much around the hotel. That was a big downside. Also, did not like the parking garage. We had to drive to dinner. When we came back. They had to park our car on one of those stackable slots.
I really didn't feel comfortable with that, but the car was fine.

title: “historic hotel,great location, but:”
text:
We stayed June 17,2004 through June 22 and this hotel was in a great location in hollywood,and it was very historic and interesting place,however the pool area was closed along with the cabana bar area that we were looking foward to that was advertised on all web sites and they put us in a small room at first with a small bed,however they did let us change rooms. some one from the hotel came into our room at 2:30a.m. and scared the crap out of us while we were asleep. also they had NO DRINK MACHINES!!!!!! 
 Everyone there was very nice and courtious,especially the valet people even though it cost $18 a day. I would probably stay there again when the pool is finished.

title: “The Staff Is Wonderful!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: Great location, wonderful staff, and huge suite with full kitchen. Stayed at the hotel for a total of seven days with a one day break in the middle because they were sold out on that day when I made my reservation. The special deal was soooooo good I did not mind going somewhere else for a day then going back. The first junior suite we were in was great, but the second one was dumpy. The carpet was dirty and stained, the recliner had some sort of stain on the side of it and there was obvious water damage and mold on the wall near the windows, plus the wallpaper was peeling off in that location. Other than that it was great and I would stay there again if the price was right.

title: “Brilliant place - great location, service and view!”
text:
We stayed here in Oct. We asked for a room on a high floor - and got one with a fabulous view of the Chrysler building on the top floor. Room was large for New York - perfect cleanliness and luxurious standard of furniture and fittings - all very clean. Great service - friendly lobby and concierge - we tried room service and it was very quick - nothing better than having breakfast overlooking an amazing view!. 
There is a diner down the road for breakfast and it is a great location to get to Times Square, Grand Central station. Its on a quiet street so you feel like you are away from things and very safe. It is worth paying for!. There is internet connection in the lobby where we arranged our yankee tickets!..

title: “Plaza Central”
text: We stayed at TRYP with no previous experience with this brand and were pleasently supprised. There was a warm welcome from knowledgeable the staff. The room sizes are well above the average for NY, where most of the time you have to stand on the bed for the other person to move around the room. Free wireless internet access, a definant plus. The restaurant was a great experience with a nice selection of Tapas and a selection of TRYP signature drinks. I highly recommend experiencing TRYP whether your visiting or from NYC

title: “Great find”
text: Great location. Friendly and genuinely helpful staff (made a pot of coffee for our 4 am departure to airport). Rooms were compact but efficient. Parking is off site but rarely need car given proximity of T stop and walking distance to theatre, Fenway, museums, etc.

title: “Very nice budget hotel, perfect location”
text: I made a spur of the moment trip to NYC and needed a hotel fast...found great rates at the New Yorker Hotel. It's about a block from Madison Square Garden/Penn Station. The first thing I noticed was that it was clean, well kept and well secured by all-night guards...nice when you are traveling alone. I came in very late, and was kindly received at the front desk and upgraded to a renovated room (I didn't see the unrenovated rooms, so I can't comment). It was small but comfortable. Bathroom fixtures were all new, and the bedroom furniture was new. There was a window air conditioning unit which was pretty loud, but I got used to it. It worked fine. The bedding was very comfortable and higher quality. It was extremely quiet in my room except for my A/C unit. I was extremely pleased with the stay. Knowing that New York hotels are unbelievably expensive, this was a great option at under $200 a night. The location was fantastic. I would stay here again.

title: “great value for 65$ a night.”
text:
first of all, we didn`t expect much. if you only pay 65$ for a double room with bath and shower enclosed, that couldn´t be located any better, you shouldn´t think of hilton. we also read the reviews posted here, so we expected the worst conditions, just hoping not to be eaten by bugs. 
contrary to our expectations the service was friendly, the beds were very comfotable and made every day. you have tv, (working) aircondition and our room was totaly quiet. sure and you will find some dust if you re looking for it and there is not panoramic view but a dirty backyard seen from the window, but the price-value ratio seems unbeatable to me. 
reading some of the older reviews i guess there must have been some kind of renovation since. again: it`s clean, it perfectly located, they help if you need them and its very very cheap!

title: “I will be back”
text: With the rodeo in town, all of the hotels near MD Anderson were booked. So, I had to look a little further away and found the Drury. We have stayed at Drury properties in the past and had good experiences. This was no different. At first I was concerned because this property is south of Hobby Airport, but it was fine. Chris on the front desk was very friendly. He gave me the medical rate of $65 which was the best yet. This helps a lot when making frequent trips to Houston. The room was clean and comfortable. It was quiet even being near the freeway. The breakfast was very good and was well stocked. No need to check in and go find a restaurant with the kick-back in the evening.

title: “Great classic hotel, quality, clean, wonderful but very very busy”
text:
This hotel was fantastic, beautiful lobby and rooms, very clean and very spacious. No complaints aside from the fact that so many conventions were held in the hotel that at times the lobby was insane and way to busy. 
The staff was very nice and willing to go above and beyond for the guests. 
Great classic hotel but very modern, I loved this hotel and I will be back!!!

title: “Perfection in Chicago”
text:
Check-in was fast, friendly and courteous. We were happy to hear our two requests were granted. One for a high floor and that foam pillows were in our room already. So far, so good!
Room was super clean, large, and over looked Mag Mile, just like we requested. The bathroom was also mag. Lots of counter space, especially liked the separate toilet room. Small refrigerator, large safe...large enough for a MacBook Air. Two bottles of water, delivered each day. Comp coffee in lobby in am, fruit water in lobby in pm. Concierge was helpful in finding local restaurants. There was even a staff member waiting near the elevator to press the button for us and offered us bottled water one day!!! Doorman was always there to open the door with a smile and helpful with walking directions! Since it was 102 degrees out, it was wonderful to be connected to the mall. There is a Cosi right across the street for a quick breakfast which was really good too. Perfect location, walkable to everywhere. 
Overall the Conrad exceeded our expectations in every way. The price was less than you would expect too. They also accept AAA for a small savings. I would stay here again in a heartbeat!

title: “Was perfect for what we needed”
text:
If you are on a sight-seeting break then you can do no wrong with this place. As everyone says the rooms are genorus in size with a lovely Chaise-lounge, big TV (all the channels you will need) and the minbar and wardrobe tucked away in an alcove, further helping with the feeling of space. There is also an ironing board/iron which is always so useful. 
The bathroom is not luxurious, as a little tired and basic, but again good size with nice white robs, towels and toliteries. We had a problem with a slow draining/leaking sink which they fixed immediately. 
The bed is GREAT - slept better than did at home. 
Air-con is noisy, like sleeping in a plane. And as it was 40 degress (100f), we had no choice but to keep it on all the time. But luckily so tired each night it didn't keep us awake. 
The bar downstairs is great, funky and quite a hot-spot it seems. 
At reception they had a nice touch of putting out little cakes on a daily basis. Guys on the door are lovely. 
Location is excellant.

title: “Great Place to Stay near Pike Market”
text: The people at the desk were amiable and helpful. They recommended a place for brunch right down the street that was super and really reasonable called the Local 360 where I went every day. One of my favorite things about the Belltown was that they had free bikes to loan which came with helmets and two locks (cable and u lock). The room was clean and comfortable and had a fridge and microwave and coffee maker. I was able, therefore to make my oatmeal in the morning and then go to the 360 at 11 when they opened. They have 3 computers in a room near the front desk to do email etc so all my needs were cared for. It isn't fancy but I saved lots of money on my stay which I spent eating dinner at upscale restaurants with my friends.

title: “Consistently Top Notch!”
text: Been about 6 months since my last visit to W New York. Derron, my favorite doorman, jumped to my assist. Recognized me immediately and took care of me throughout, during a very hot summer week. As always, that kind of service is much appreciated and is consistently demontrated by the full staff. I'll definitely be back!

title: “Shopping in New York? Stay at THIS hotel......”
text:
Every year we go to New York for a girly "retail therapy" trip and this is the first time we've stayed at the Hampton Inn NY Empire State Hotel......but what a find!
Very competitively priced, we were absolutely delighted with our room - big enough for the three of us - but what stood out for us were the staff who, without exception, were really helpful.
We have seen other reviews that have been negative with regard to breakfasts but throughout our stay (5 nights) there was never a shortage of food whilst the selection and quality was very good.
The hotel is ideally situated being VERY, VERY close both to Macys and to the subway station.
You can see from other peoples recent reviews that our experience of staying at this hotel has been similiar to other visitors so, if your going to The Big Apple, you couldn't do any better than staying at Hampton Inn Empire State Building Hotel.....have a nice day!!
Jen Woodward (& daughters in law)

title: “Convenient and relaxing”
text: Stayed for 4 nights in early May 2007 and had no complaints. The room style is basic and, as a previous reviewer said, they are not suites but were very comfortable and well provided. I also agree the lighting in the rooms was a little poor. We found the staff helpful and efficient and the pool area very peaceful and relaxing and virtually deserted when we used it about 6pm after a day's sightseeing. We found about three other restaurants within easy walking distance but only tried one - the Bali Hai at the left hand end of shelter island as you drive on to it. Most of the meal was excellent although I did have to send my main course back. However I think this was an isolated problem, I just got an undercooked one and they dealt with it without any qualms or arguments. For most people I suspect the clincher for or against the Humphreys Half Moon is their series of summer concerts on their open air stage. This year's schedule includes the Beach Boys, Huey Lewis and the News, UB40, Steve Winwood through to kd Lang, Lyle Lovett and Queen Latifah plus numerous others. It's worth checking out their web site to see who's playing during your stay. Tickets prices look quite reasonable - particularly with the current exchange rate against the £ - but you can probably hear them for free from the pool.

title: “Outstanding service and location”
text:
We have stayed at this Travelodge many times over the last 5 years as we travel from
Portland Or. to San Francisco. During our stays, the manager, Roger, has always been
helpful with rooms and prices depending on the season and events. He is very considerate. The rooms have always been fine even though the motel has been there quite a while. The continental breakfast is always fresh and enjoyable and the location is excellent since the trolly is close and we can travel to meet
our needs throughout the city. We plan to stay there again this July
Donald J. Averill and Carole Averill

title: “Perfect for families”
text: We stayed at the Residence Inn for two nights. I was traveling with my husband, our 2-year old son, and my parents. We stayed in a 2-bedroom suite. It was an easy walk to the Alamo and the Riverwalk. Breakfast was comparable to other hotels that offer free breakfast. Happy hour food was about what you'd expect. The suite was clean and nicely updated. The kitchen items were somewhat limited (pots and dishes) but we had enough to cook basic food for our toddler. What really impressed us was that the hotel loaned us an umbrella stroller when we realized we'd forgotten ours. The 2-bedroom suite was an excellent value for us.

title: “Not your typical Hampton Inn - In a good way! 8.5 out of 10”
text:
Room Type: Standard
Rate Paid: $149 per night
Reason For Stay: Business
Overall Average Score: 8.5/10
Location - 8/10
Very convenient to the subway, a short walk from shopping and dining options, get directions first. Downside: the hotel is RIGHT on one of the main roads to the tunnel, making traffic a mess at peak periods. Cabs cannot get in, it's a lot easier if they let you off around the corner (note, since its a new hotel, some cab drivers are not familiar with it, tell them its at Watts and Varick downtown). Also, the extra traffic means a decent bit of additional road noise during peak periods.
Room Design - 9/10
The room is small by US standard, but fine by NY standards. What space is available is well used, with plenty of storage options. The bathroom is ok sized. I would not recommend this room for more than 2 people.
Room Amenities - 9/10
Standard Hampton in toiletries. Nice touches included a screen saver feature on the LCD TV with music and the Hampton alarm clock. Drapes closed tightly, always a plus in NY.
Design and Layout - 8/10
Unlike 'traditional' Hampton Inns, the hotel has tried for a more modern look and mostly succeeded. The entry area is fairly inviting but very small, if a lot of people are checking it at once that could be very problematic. 
Amenities - Non Club - 8/10
There is no executive club at this hotel. There is a small but decently appointed fitness room at the basement level and the breakfast area serves as a large seating area during the day with 24 hour coffee available.
There is no gift shop or other location to purchase sundries. The nearest drug store is about a 10 min walk.
One lack was wireless internet in the room. However, the provided cord is long enough to reach almost all around the small room.
Club Room - Not applicable
Hotel Staff - 10/10
I was very pleased with the hotel staff. All were friendly and knowledgeable and willing to help. Housekeeping was great each day, room clean and freshened.
Dining - 10/10 (Breakfast Only)
There is no dining in the hotel other than the included free breakfast. A small bar is still waiting for license to open.
Breakfast itself was very well done. Each day included a different hot selection as well as breads, fruits, cereals, etc. The seating area was well lit and kept clean and the food was always hot and well stocked. 
Comments and Notes:
The hotel is very new (2 months?) and is offering very low rates to attract travelers. With easy access to the Tribeca/SoHo area and good downtown location, its a value not to be missed right now.

title: “Nice rooms not sure about location”
text:
We only stayed one night and the room was great,very comfy and staff were incredibly friendly. However opposite us was a big group of people having a get togetheron their balcony which was 10 feet away from our room. One of the guys looked a bit shady and worse for wear and kept eyeing up our car as we parked it as his was a battered old car and ours was a shiny new rental ( Buick Enclave). Anyway, they were really noisy into the early hours by which time I had resorted to ear plugs and turning air con up high to drown out the noise. Also next door was noisy ( thin walls). I slept fine thanks to my earplugs and I'm sure the staff would have asked them to keep it down but we didn't want to complain unless absolutely necessary. Everyone says San Diego is lovely but we didn't quite get it. We were expecting something spectacular from peoples comments ( like San Franciso which is fantastic). It is a nice city by the sea ( like many in Britain) and does have lovely weather. However
1) The area directly around the Gaslamp ( on a friday night ) is to be avoided unless you want to join the party ( quite a few shady characters spotted on our drive through at only 7pm). The Gaslamp itself, in our opinion, is pretty much like many british city centres. Nothing special
2) The Coronado is lovely and would probably stay here if we came again as it had a nicer feel than Shelter Island
3) The "word famous " san diego zoo was nice but really not as good as London zoo and really hot and humid with really steep trails and animals very spread out and not very visible. I feel American tourist board are very good at hyping up their attractions ( fair enough it is what they are paid for ) and we fall for it and are often disappointed. Don't get me wrong the zoo was nice but not worthy of it's world famous build up.
4) The museums at Balboa Park sounded great and we visited the Natural History museum first and were shocked the the cost $100 for all four of us and seriously it had so few exhibits. Having been to London many times and had free entry to the museums, there we were genuinely shocked at the value for money. It made me appreciate our museums and the free entry scheme. We decided not to risk another!
I wanted to love san deigo and shelter island but I could do neither and found myself wishing I had stayed an extra night in Newport Beach. However, if you do stay in shelter island this hotel is good as long as the other guests behave, but this is not the Hotels fault and I must stress we did not let them know so it is not a reflection on them but it is a true and honest account of our visit. I don't think it was as good value as some of our other hotels on our 3 week trip.

title: “Great Hotel for Butler Parents!!”
text: Great, Clean Hotel! My wife hates to travel fearing hotels experiences, she has named this hotel the best we've ever stayed at. We were in Indy for our Daughter's recital at Butler and loved this hotel. We will be staying again for her graduation! Hotel seems brand new although it is several years old now. Convenient drive to Butler University.

title: “Would stay again!”
text: I was staying with a group of friends in Houston for a dog show. The hotel was dog friendly and had a good place to walk the dogs. My room was right by the lobby, but the noise wasn't too bad. The breakfast was nice, but we were only able to enjoy it one day due to the time we had to leave. On two of the three days I stayed, the amenities in the room were not replenished (soap/shampoo/coffee). The evening staff was great!

title: “Nice desk people! Room variable”
text:
We booked two rooms three people each, ended up over $1200. which I thought was steep. No free breakfast or discounts because it was a school holiday week. The desk people are very nice! Door man too. Rooms big for new york, little worn and seedy . Problem with the shower was very frustrating. Couldn't stabilize water, so the water was mostly freezing, then boiling for a second--old worn out shower head didn't help. Asked daily for repairs--nothing happened. Paid extra for three people, but got only 2 washcloths, one little shampoo, two mugs, so we felt a little burned for $1200 bucks 2 nights.
The location is great, the elevators fast, if I got a deal like other people did at this hotel I would go back!

title: “Been there, done that.”
text:
We booked 2 nights here after learning that Boston Harbor Hotel (our favorite, bar none) was full. 
The rooms are nice--large, carefully decorated. We had no trouble booking connecting rooms for our kids and the reservationist was nice about allowing the dog ($25 charge). It felt a bit out of the way. The layout with rooms in different buildings is actually quite nice, although you miss the doormen if you are not in the main building. Housekeeping was in our faces on the last day, waiting for us to leave (we left at 10; they were trying to get into the room by 9.40; checkout is 11).
The HarborWalk is extremely cool, and well worth seeing. I thought breakfast at the hotel restaurant was ridiculously expensive ($100+ for 3 adults and one child), and the service was polite but pretty distracted (we got our second cups of coffee right away, but by the time the extra cream arrived they were cold).
There is no dog-walking service on-site, you have to book with the Dogfather of North End. (We did not, so I cannot review.) There are not too many places to walk a dog close to the hotel.
There is no Concierge per se. The front desk will book reservations for you but they lack a concierge's knowhow regarding events in town. They're friendly and trying to be helpful, but they're pretty much doing as they're told. Not much expertise.
No Pool.
This is inexcusable, in my view: you had to pay for WiFi! There was a nice little "technology kit" for laptops, and free Ethernet, but WiFi was $15/day per person. We had dinner at Boston Harbor (Meritage) and got free WiFi.

title: “Lovely Hotel”
text: We stayed for two nites recently. We paid $199 a nite through their own promotion. The hotel is quite beautiful. The lobby is gorgeous with pretty furnishings. We had a king size standard room. It was nicely furnished and very comfortable. The bed was awesome. The amenities were a bonus. We especially enjoyed the complimentary morning beverage service and the robes. The location is excellent. We walked to most of the attractions. We were very pleased with the service provided. We would love to stay here again.

title: “Great Staff and great at accommodating their Guests !!!”
text: My wife and I were at the Hyatt Regency for vacation. I'm here to tell ya'll that the staff was very accommodating. But, our highest compliment goes to Velia Da'vila. She's employed as a housekeeper at the Hyatt. My wife accidentally drop a large sum of cash money out of her purse and it fell on the bed(not noticing what had happened). We left for the day and upon our return,we happened to pass by Ms. Da'vila and she told us what she found on the bed. She honestly put in on the night stand for us to find. Our highest regards and respect go to this very honest lady.We would recommend this property to anyone. Also, the location was great and the bed was very comfortable. All staff was extremely helpful and kind. It is our intent to stay at this property again and is definitely recommending it .

title: “Very disappointing--i dont "get' the great reviews”
text:
To say i was disappointed (based on the numerous 5 star recs on TA) is an understatement.
The hotel is average in nearly every way.
One young woman, Tory, was very friendly and helpful. A man on Sunday afternoon was quite helpful about the route to Dealy Plaza. Other front desk staff were fine, but nothing above what one should expect. Most were pleasant, but not of the outstanding level that some reviews implied. True and typical Texan friendliness--which I find nearly everywhere in the state--was not that evident here. 
Some staff were worse than average. The man at the breakfast buffet Monday morning was just plain rude, when i asked where i could put the used plates (it was a self-service place, after all).
I called a "guest service" person to ask where there was an ice machine. She curtly told me to go up to the 25th floor. I get in the elevator--NO 25th floor on the panel. Thinking i might have heard wrong,I got out on 26th floor(where the hall carpet was filthy, as if a vacuum cleaner had unloaded excess dirt and dust in a pile) No ice. I returned, empty ice buck in hand, to my room on 21st fl. Call guest service lady again. She replied, impatiently,that i have to go to the one elevator (of 4 or so) that goes to 25th floor, and look on the side of the elevator door to call the one for the 25th floor. That would have been nice to know in the first place.
We checked in on a Saturday. Sunday morning, friend had run 13 miles in the weekend's half-marathon (the source of many hotel guests) . He returned, achey and exhausted, at 1:30 pm, just wanting to nap. Room not refreshed or made up, so i called guest service and ask if room can be made up, so friend can nap without being awoken by housekeeper. Two more calls later, after two more hours...finally housekeeper shows up, at 4:30 pm! When i asked guest services guy why it was so late , he said, "We had a lot of people checking out." OK--but what about people who were paying for an additional night--don't we get to have clean rooms by afternoon ?
Scary elevators mentioned elsewhere on TA--yes, quite unpredictable Each elevator has a metal plaque warning of this--forewarned is forearmed-- in a cute humourous way. However, the signs were scratched up, lending an air not of historic charm, but just plain old.
That was my sense of the entire hotel. Historic charm was less in evidence than drab and dull. Hallway and room were dark--could barely read or see even with all desktop lamps turned on. (There are no ceiling lights.) Only the shower had a bright light (in a glass wall recess) . Colors of room--yellow and brown. A room can be basic, but at least "inviting" enough to enjoy just kicking back and wtaching TV,etc. This room was so drab and dreary, i didnt want to spend any extra time in it. There was one bathrobe in a two- bed room. (They must figure the second person can do without one) No folding luggage rack--so had to open suitcase on one of few surfaces--the desk--making it unusable for other purposes.
On the plus side, beds were comfortable, and breakfast itself was very good, with scrambled egg and cheese dish, plus oatmeal, and bagels, etc. And people at the evening liquor reception were having a blast!! The lounge on the second floor was lovely.
Perhaps "free" liquor explains the positive memories and high ratings.
Also, do not use the valet parking. There are public lots within a block or two--much cheaper. Across the street, the one for "Nieman-Marcus " was officially about $10/24 hours--and both Sunday and early Monday morning, had free exiting.
Upon return home, i rec'd a survey email from Magnolia askeing that i give them top scores so they can be #1 on Tripadvisor!!! Maybe that explains a number of once-only, one sentence, reviews here. At least in my experience, the glowing reviews are not deserved, unless the free alcohol is a big draw for a prospective guest.

title: “Location is tough to beat”
text:
we have just returned from 5 days at Hotel Monaco. It is in a beautifully restored historical building and is quite lovely. The rooms are small, nothing spectacular really but the location is fantastic. It is located right across the street from the Verizen Center, so very easy to attend hockey or basketball games if that is of interest. It is also across from the subway (under the verizon center) making it very convenient for almost everything.
It is within walking distance of the mall, so access to all of the smithsonians and monuments is easy. The National Portrait gallery is also right across the street, the spy museum is next door...you get the idea. Lots of restaurants and bars nearby.
It is expensive, but worth it because of the location. The beds were very comfortable and I loved the bedding. The people were nice enough.

title: “Location, price, and appearance are right but there are a few problems”
text: Hotel is in a great safe location w/ nearby restaurants and quick access to I-465. Plenty of parking and exterior appearance was decent with very nice abundant flowers in front of the lobby area. Check-in(arrived at 3:15 p.m.) went smoothly and the male attendant was friendly. I was assigned a 2nd floor room 222 which had a king bed(although I believe it was closer to a queen size). I was surprised at just how comfortable the bed was to sleep in, although you should definitely bring your own pillow(s). The bottom sheet was a flat sheet instead of a fitted sheet like a previous reviewer mentioned so by morning time I was laying on a bare mattress. The restroom/shower room area is a little cramped for space but it did the trick. The drain in the shower was apparently partially clogged though so I was standing in ankle high water by the time I finished my shower. The only other problem is that if you are on the 2nd floor, it is difficult to use your room key card to call the elevator up to the 2nd floor. I had to try on average about six times with my key card before I was successful in calling up the elevator. The FREE continental breakfast was nice and it ran from I think 6 a.m. to 9 a.m.. I got down there at 8:00 a.m. and there was still plenty of food(waffle maker, cereal, milk, banana). If you're looking to save some money(paid $59 w/ tax for one night) on a short stay and don't mind a few minor problems it's an okay place.

title: “Will NOT stay here again”
text: the room smells, there is no parking, and the desk clerk is rude. Only visit SA once a year but will not stay here again.

title: “Just conveniently located.”
text: This Hotel has nothing memorable. We went to this hotel for Los Angeles Half marathon, and chose it because it was conventiently located near a metro station for transportation from the finish line and it was near some Hollywood attractions... the room was not clean, the smell was awful and the hotel seems a little bit unkempt... the only thing good about it is that the room was big.. that's it.

title: “Wouldn't recommend”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for one night during my first trip to Hollywood. We pretty much called on our drive out there and booked over the phone because the price was right. 
The staff was friendly and lobby was very nice so we thought we lucked out. However we were not very happy with the room. It was small, dark and outdated. Also there were dark red stains on the box spring! Overall we had a decent stay for the night but I was repulsed and would not go back. I would recommend the Grafton on Sunset which was much nicer and in a better location (alittle more $ but worth it). I also stayed at the Farmer's Daughter once which was very cute and affordable.

title: “A Beautiful Place to Stay”
text:
My family stayed at the Hilton as a family treat while we were traveling at Christmastime. We had tickets for a show at Second City and decided to splurge on our hotel. When we booked we realized it was not really a splurge - our rooms were $90/night before taxes (and the extra charge for parking and the dog) - a real deal!
Our room was quite luxurious by our standards. (We're used to staying at economy hotels on our trips to and from Illinois/Maine.) The beds were beautifully appointed with the most comfortable sheets/blankets/pillow-top mattresses. The 2 bathrooms had heated marble floors - one bath had a tub and one had a shower. We had a corner room with a view of Grant Park and Navy Pier in the distance.
We toured the hotel to check out all of it's nooks and crannies - the many ballrooms were really beautiful. We spent an hour in the fitness center which is the nicest I've ever seen in a hotel. It is huge, with state-of-the-art machines and a running track. The pool was next door and was being used by several families. It was clean and there was an attendant on duty who was keeping everything neat.
The hotel has a great deal of security, which I found comforting. There are security guards and bell-man at each of the entrances, and when we came in at 2:00 in the morning we were required to show our room key card.
There were a few downsides of the room: it was very hot and we had to open the windows to cool it off because the heating controls didn't seem to be working. Internet was not free. (I believe it was $12.95/night.) There was a bag of laundry and a small pile of room service dishes out in the hall upon our arrival. The laundry was picked up after we called the front desk, but the dishes were there all night and still there when we checked out the next day. For this reason I gave the hotel a 4 rather than a 5 for cleanliness.

title: “Enjoyed my stay”
text: This hotel is in a weird section but I still felt very safe while staying with friends. The room and beds were very comfy. The staff was super friendly and informative. Love the new renovated look to the lobby and outside of the building.

title: “Loved the Carter!!”
text:
I read the reviews of the Carter and was a bit weary, but booked none the less, who could pass up the $124/night rates?! I had no trouble booking the room online, and the staff was super friendly when I called to check my confirmation. We arrived on a Friday afternoon, the hotel was refreshingly cool in temp, there was a doorman who carried my heavy luggage up the short flight of stairs that lead to the lobby, the check in went fast and the staff was very friendly. The hotel is older, but I knew that from the reviews I read.. so the 14th floor wasn't all that scary, and the room was way better than I thought it was going to be. The room was clean! The sheets were clean! The bathroom was clean, stocked with towels, TP and soap! The AirCon worked (really well)! The TV worked, and there was a remote! The next day we asked for more towels and were given more than enough. We had no troubles with elevators, all three were working fine and were quick to respond. Who really cares that the front desk has plastic barriers (not bullet proof glass, jees!), do you touch your hotel employees anyway? There's a sweet little deli downstairs that served me the best grilled cheese sandwich I've ever eaten! I never saw one bug or other 4 legged creature in the place. If you're on a budget this is a great hotel right in the middle of Times Square, I LOVED my Hotel Carter experience and would have no objection to staying there again! 
Thanks Hotel Carter for making our trip great!!

title: “Awesome!”
text:
This place is fabulous!
I too arrived early at the Austin Bergstrom Airport. My flight arrived at around 9:40 in the morning. I was downstairs and in my rental car by 10am. The Enterprise people at the Austin airport are very speedy!
My first business meeting was at 2:00pm so I called the hotel to see if I could check in early. They said that would be fine. Only about a 20 min drive to the hotel. Parking is a bit of a problem. However I found a garage behind the building but if you need to get out after 10pm you are stuck or you will walk. 
When I arrived they had run out of regular rooms so I was upgraded to a king suite. Very comfortable and lavish. They bathroom was outstanding. Full tub with seperate spacious shower complete with peach marble tile and extremely clean. The bed was so heavenly to sleep in and the staff is very accomodating!
Convenient to everything downtown. 6th street is a fun place to go in the evenings. Just a few blocks from the State Capital and Downtown Austin is very interesting. I highly reccomend the gym. Fully equipped with bottled water, a jacuzzi tub, private dressing rooms and a lap pool. The restaurant is decent but a little pricey.
I would highly reccomend this hotel!

title: “The LaJolla Hyatt Club Level is excellent!”
text:
Stayed at the LaJolla Hyatt for three nights earlier this month. Booked a room in the Club Level and it was worth the extra charge.
This is a newer hotel and is in the business district, so if the point of your vacation is to stay in a tourist-y spot, do not stay here. This hotel was definitely a business hotel. Staying on the Club floor provides opportunities to meet other travelers for breakfast or afternoon hors d'oeurves. There were very few children on this floor, and those that we did encounter were very well behaved.
The included continental breakfast was the same food as in the hotel restaurant, as far as we could tell. The granola was to die for! Added to vanilla yogurt to make a parfait - YUM! Also their fruit was awesome.
In the lounge, there are two computers for travelers to use. Some people are very inconsiderate and do not abide by the 15-minute request. Those people should just pay the additional charge and work from their room if they have a laptop. Some people were surfing the web. I used it briefly a couple times to check work emails, but many times there were lines of people waiting to use them.
The rooms were freshly redecorated with quality furniture and bedding. The linens were high quality, which was nice. There is nothing worse than scratchy towels and bedding when traveling. Well, there is a lot worse, but that is a pet peeve of mine.
Elevators were very fast, but it would be nice if the top levels had their own elevators. While the banks are split from lower to higher, it can take a long time to get from the top floors to lobby level when it stops at every floor. Some people do not know elevator etiquette and jam themselves in an already-crowded elevator instead of waiting for the next one. But that happens everywhere, not just at hotels. It just would be nice to have express elevators for the top few floors (similar to some hotels in Las Vegas).
Everything was clean clean clean! Mrs. Clean and Mr. Fixit must work here. Everything was in tip-top shape. The employees were extremely nice, every single one we met.
Parking was expensive, but what do you expect? You're in San Diego. We enjoyed the in/out privileges in the garage and parking was plenty.
Overall, it was a great experience and we will stay here again.

title: “Good, well located accommodation”
text:
We visited the Tuscan Inn as part of a holiday (but needing to work while there) in San Francisco, primarily to visit the opera, but decamping to Fisherman’s Wharf for a bit of rest and recreation. The location is no more than a block or two away from all the main attractions.
We found staff to be friendly and helpful. The bright and airy room was large enough for our needs. There was a good sized table. It was good to have a machine into which you can plug six appliances – helpful if you have a laptop, iPad and Blackberry with you as I did.
The room we stayed in had the benefit of a fridge and coffee maker. Wardrobe facilities (I was told that this is closet in American!) were sufficient for our needs, staying four days. I found the bed to be a little on the hard side but I suspect that this is a matter of taste.
There was a large, if a little old fashioned TV with sufficient channels to maintain our interest. WiFi access is free and reliable and the speed was fine for business use. An ironing board and iron are provided. Everything was clean and well serviced.
The bathroom was well appointed and functional though the shower took a little manipulation to get an acceptable temperature.
There were ice making and vending facilities on the floor we stayed on.
We didn’t eat in the restaurant. Breakfast prices seemed a little on the high side, but of course there are many options within walking distance. The wine hour between 5 p.m. and 6 p.m. was a pleasant idea and a good opportunity to meet other guests – don’t expect premier grand cru though! The lobby area is spacious and well appointed.
Overall, we found nothing to complain about and much to admire.

title: “Great NYC hotel”
text:
This hotel is great! wonderful location right off Times Square. The hotel staff is just incredible-they are so welcoming and helpful. They make the whole NY experience even better.
The rooms are clean and very stylish.

title: “Great bargain hotel.”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for 4 nights at the end of August. Being New York, we were expecting a small room but we were there to see the city so didn't mind. To be honest, I thought the room was an ok size. The bathroom was very small but clean and functional. We were lucky to be on the 12th floor at the front of the building and had a view of the Flatiron building. Overall the room was clean, with a comfortable bed, plenty of towels and nice toiletries. The concierge was helpful and even booked a table at a restaurant for us at our request. We ate in the hotel restaurant for breakfast and thought it was good - I'd avoid the buffet upstairs though as it is a rip-off. Overall, I'd recommend this hotel as it is in mid-town with a sub-way station outside the door making it very handy for tourists who wish to explore the city. I agree with another reviewer who recommended avoiding the Korean restaurant next door - probably the worst meal and worse service I've ever had in my life!

title: “Smelly rooms unless in tower”
text:
Looks great until you enter your room. They smell like mold. The help said they smell all the time. Our first room was really bad. The next one was half as bad. We were ready to leave when they moved us to the Tower (which the woman at the front desk said could not be done). The tower was fine. Beds comfortable, nice view, no smell. Upon checkout they hit us for $30 extra per nite for the tower, something they didn't tell us. Didn't mind paying it, but should have been told up front. The smell seems to be in the first floor rooms throughout the complex. Frankly, they should burn those buildings and rebuild absent what appears to be a ubiquitous mold problem. Food was marginal. Good conscierge.
Excellent workout facility, nice pool.

title: “Dont Hesitate, Extremely Good Hotel.”
text:
My partner and I travelled to NYC on the 16th Sept - 21st Sept.
We arrived at Newark, waiting for us was a driver which I booked through the hotel's website, very proffesional and friendly, this cost me $90, which is not too bad as we did not have to wait around for a taxi and the car was really nice.
We arrived at the hotel, and on first impressions i thought to myself i have done the right thing as the hotel was well furnished bright and elegant, the check in staf were all smiling, happy to help and quick at getting us checked in.
I had already emailed the front office manager (Glenn Merone) and pre booked a room with a view at a extra cost of $10 per night (BARGAIN) he was quick with his responses and everything was done without fuss, we stayed on the 37th floor and Glen had given us a wonderful room with a view of the empire state, the room was very clean, well furnished and of a good size for a couple. The house keeping was very good, sheets changed when asked and towels replaced when asked. The rooms are equipped with a hairdrier, flat screen TV with a range of new movies, phone, fully controllable AC/Heater, showers are powerful and the water warmed up quickly, beds comfy.
The hotel's location was great, only a couple of blocks from MACY's, and a very short walk to the empire state and times square, there are plenty of shops nearby for food, toiletries etc.... There are people who have said they felt unsafe in the area, personally i felt safe throught the city day or night and the area where the hotel is located i found was no problem at all.
The Tick Tock Diner, was a great place to start your day for a breakfast and served pretty good coffee, although we did not eat there in evenings the food im sure is pretty good.
So all in all, a very good stay, we have recommended this hotel to numerous friends as it seems everybody is visiting NYC this year, two of our friends have already booked it.
**********DO NOT BE PUT OFF YOU WILL ENJOY YOUR STAY************, im not easily impressed with hotels and this is a place i would return for sure! But make sure you go for a high floor with a view, just send them an email prior to arriving and the staff will be more than happy to help!

title: “My new favorite hotel”
text: My husband and i travel to chicago a couple of times per month for leisure and for some reason have never stayed at this hotel before. Now i will stay no where else. it is the most beautiful hotel with old classic charm. From the ceiling to floor windows to the dark rich wood throughout, there were so many things about this hotel that you do not get with the newer trendy hotels. It felt homey, spacious, and very comfortable and the staff and check in were delightful. Would recommend this hotel to everyone...it was a fabulous stay.

title: “Great Experience”
text:
We booked this hotel for friends trip to San Antonio.. It was a great stay and great experience.. Nice sapcious rooms with great interiors. Cooperative and humble staff. Hotel is close to the famous river walk, the most happening place in San Antonio. This is the first hotel where i see two bathrooms in a double room.. 
Hotel doesn't have parking space. You have to park to nearby pay & park lot. 
Overall great stay & good value for money.

title: “Great for the Price/location”
text: The rooms are huge with 2 queen beds and 2 TVs. The pool was decent size and refreshing for July in Texas. The breakfast was fantastic, but a bit crowded a few of the days. You can catch a trolley a few blocks away or walk to the river about 3 blocks away and follow it downtown. The hotel was clean and comfortable. If there was a downside, it would be that the A/C did not kick butt, but it was sufficient. And, the breakfast was a zoo 2 of the 4 days we stayed there. I would stay there again for sure. Parking was not a problem. We found a spot every night in the lot.

title: “Decent Stay”
text:
Nice and Clean Hotel.
Just what I expect for the money and HIE, hotel is updated, nice sized room, clean, breakfast included and Happy Hour.
Couldn't ask more for the price.
Good and friendly stuff .
I have to come back in few more weeks so I will book again.

title: “What a Deal!”
text:
Traveling on vacation for 3 weeks with my 13 year old son, I wanted to budget lodging at 200.00 a night. I felt fortunate to get a rate under 200.00 with my AAA card at the Hyatt for 7 nights. Because we could not get a room our first 2 nights at the Hyatt, we ended up paying 350.00 at another hotel.
The other hotel was in a better location (Back Bay) and the rooms more luxurious but the Hyatt was just as comfortable.
The Hyatt staff were all so nice and we never heard any noise in our room...sleeping in during our vacation!
Upon arrival, I too was concerned about the location since we were using the T during our stay and returning to the hotel late at night but if you walk from the T and enter the Hyatt from the parking garage entrance, it's just 1 block and a much quicker walk. We never had any problems.
 I highly recommend this hotel. It was perfect for us.

title: “Fab location, Fab staff GREAT BAR!!!!”
text:
As previously stated on reviews not much to look at on the outside, but cant rate it highly enough inside. Rooms although small by UK standards were spotless clean and immaculate, everything you needed iin them, TV, Ironing board and iron, tea and coffee, fridge, safety box, hairdyer. Cleaned every day we were there 28th Nov - 3rd December.
Location great walked just about everywhere, myself and friend had both our two young girls ( 9 and 10) and had a double double room, both girls slept on the sofa bed and altho made the room cramped we were only in it to sleep. Latest we left the hotel was 9 in the morning and earliest back 9pm!!!
Reception staff - one of whom is a Brit were extremely helpfull when one of the suitcases was lost in transit eventually delivered 3 days later and the piece de resistance for 2 single parents - the bar!!!
Owned by Nick and his partner along with Patricia and not actually by the hotel we spent 2 very long nights in bar whilst girls quite happily played on the internet adjoined.
Breakfast altho simple, bagels, doughnuts, muffins and lashings of coffee, tea and orange juice and cereals was just right and very nice. Staff extremely helfull when we booked helicopter trip from 59th Street, and cheaper as well..
Tip - book any trips you intend to go on direct with the company in the US much cheaper especially due to exchange rate. Viacom.com for thetare tickets excellent seats for Les Miserable.
Alreday booked for a girlie shopping trip in Decmber this year at hotel...

title: “Nice little hotel”
text: The location in is really good. Lots of thing to do in the near surroundings if you're into Lower Manhattan. The subway is a short walk away. There was nothing major wrong with the hotel itself either. We had asked for a non-smoking room, but were given a smoking one instead. But we didn't even pay attention to it until the next day when we noticed the ashtray. So no cigarette smell what so ever in our room! When we first arrived in our room it smelled odd though, like no-one had been there for a really long time. But the smell soon went away. There was very unpleasant dampness on the floor. I wouldn't want to see what's under the carpet! Some people on tripadvisor warn about cockroaches and even mice. We didn't see any during our stay, even though we sometimes had food in our room.

title: “A Very Good Spot for Extended Stay.”
text:
I stayed here for 28 nights in January from the 8th to Febuary 4th. I have to say that the hotel met all of our needs, the distance to South Street, the subway and Old City District was great. 10 min walk to eat and we only went to the same place twice.
The room was clean, and taken care of regularly by the housekeeping staff. only a couple of times in 28 days did the room not get attention. but it was easily solved by one phone calls and the attention was immediate. 
Noise was not very present, I was on the 17th floor south side i room over from the elevator. The only time I was disturbed was by rowdy guests and that was only one occurrence.
The bell staff were excellent, and the front desk was also quite accommodating. No problems. The only thing I thought was a bit off was the price of the business center, $7 for 15 min when I needed to print off 2 confirmation sheets was a bit steep. 
Ernie the valet was exemplary, top service and truly a stand-out employee of the Park America company that takes care of the parking. 
If and when I have to go back to Philly, this is my only place to stay.

title: “Great weekend in Seattle”
text: We spent the weekend here for my daughter's birthday. The staff were top notch - giving her a gift box with chocolates and a little souvenir book when they learned it was her birthday. The view was fabulous from the room, over the city and the sound. Walking distance to Pike's, right by the cinema, etc. All in all, very comfortable, with great service.

title: “wow, worried at first :) but then WOW great”
text:
Dont judge a book by its cover, or in this case the hotel by its outside or area.
When i entered the lobby, the frst thought was , WOW, nicest Hampton inn lobby and breakfast area Ive ever encountered.
The front desk staff at check in were some of the friendliest and courteous Ive met.
Great experience, will stay here and recommend to others.

title: “awesome hotel with great service”
text: I've stayed at hotels around the world, and this is one of the best. I took the red-eye from Los Angeles, and arrived at 6AM. The hotel was beyond accomodating, and made sure that the first room available would be ready for me. I stayed in the Grand Deluxe room, with a fabulous view overlooking the Hudson. From the moment you enter the hotel, you are completely taken care of. The room was spacious, chic, with lots of light. Room service was a little pricey, but worth it after a long flight. Even if you're going for a short period of time, you MUST go to G-Spa, and treat yourself to the Fitness Facial, which was designed by Sonya Dakar, and uses silica-rich Fiji Water to hydrate. G-Spa is great if you're sober...but it's amazing after a night at Bungalow -- it's dim lights in the spa are perfect for a hangover. Regardless....it's a fab hotel. World-class.

title: “Made welcome at a perfect location”
text:
