Great location - really near the meatpacking district. Staff were friendly and welcoming. Rooms felt really unique, total opposite of most generic hotels. Loved the daily newsletter they put under your door with hints of things to do for the day.
We were on the third floor and it really isn't a drag at all walking up the stairs so don't let that put you off!
Would definitely stay there again next time I'm in NY.

title: “Best Kept Secret”
text:
This is a great Hotel well located for Downtowm and Brooklyn Bridge. Subway is just a short walk and can be uptown in no time at all.
All staff very friendly, search for a price on the net, we stayed for three nights for £207

title: “Wow...”
text: Wow -- what a great place. The location was great for anyone who's in SF to do the tourist thing. Service was incredible, room was wonderful, beds were comfortable. Loved the little touches, like the complimentary wine tasting every day. Would definitely stay again.

title: “Wonderful Hotel and Excellent Location”
text:
Love this place. I even loved it more that we got it for half price on priceline. The location is excellent...in the middle of everything. Just south of of Chicago River and N. Michigan Avenue, West of Navy Pier, East of the L loop, and North of Millennium Park and such. Everything is within walking distance.
Some reviews are complaining about the size of the hotel... I guess they are uninformed that this hotel is the largest hotel in the Chicago. That being sad, we were not treated like a number. Check in and check out were simple. The concierge is more than happy to help with your needs. The rooms are standard size and the beds comfy. 
Nothing was lacking. 
Someone noted that the refrigerator could not be used to store your food as there would be a fine as it was filled with stuff already. Folks, this is standard for a big city hotel. And if you need to refrig. something be creative. I took the ice bag, filled it with ice, and placed it on top of our pizza container. Then, the next day I put our drinks we purchased from the store in the ice bucket. No problem. 
Our room was very close to the elevator and It was somewhat of a distraction, but considering we paid half price via priceline I wasn't complaining.
The room service is great, fast, yummy and friendly. We had appetizers and drinks at the "Big Bar" which we good and the service was good as well. 
Yes, the hotel is huge and there was a ton of conferences going on then, but we felt that met every need, and would stay there again.

title: “Location, location, location!”
text:
This my 25th trip to Chicago and I have stayed in multiple hotels.
Just spent 2 nights here and found the location to be just about perfect. You can walk to Navy Pier, Magnificent Mile, Hancock Observatory, Rush Street etc. Anywhere else is a short cab ride. Hotel is well laid out with a central location for breakfast (included in room rate) and bar (Free drinks and snacks 5:30-7:30 every night). Very fast elevators, never had to wait more than a couple of minutes and the hotel was full. Our room 1502 has nice views which included the NBC Tower, Trump Hotel, The lake. Could not believe how quiet the room was, no noise from traffic. Definitely will return to the Embassy Suites Lakefront.

title: “Loved the room and location!”
text: I traveled with my husband and baby to Chicago for a fun getaway. I chose this hotel because of the great price I found through Travelzoo and the fact that they have a free breakfast. I read a few reviews about this hotel, but since it was so new, there weren't many at the time. We rode the train (which I would recommend to anyone coming into Chicago if you have that choice. Driving and parking in Chicago is crazy and expensive!! The train was so easy, inexpensive, and there is plenty of public transportation available!) in and actually arrived at the hotel at about one o'clock. I wasn't sure that we'd be able to check-in right then because it said online that check-in wasn't until 3. I called prior to our trip to make sure that if we couldn't check-in when we arrived at the hotel, that we could at least leave our luggage there while we walked to have lunch. They have a room where they can hold luggage if you arrive early, but to our surprise, our room was ready and we were able to check-in at one. Our room was great!!!! My husband and I thought that the building must have once been apartments and now it's been transformed into a hotel. Our room was like a little one bedroom apartment. It was so convenient having the kitchen to prepare and rinse bottles for our baby girl. Also, I didn't see this before we came, but they have pack-n'-plays that you can request for no extra charge. Unfortunately I didn't see that before we came, and we lugged our pack-n'-play all the way to Chicago. We really enjoyed the free breakfast. There was a waffle maker, danishes, fruit, coffee, juice, toast, bagels, and there was like a special each morning. We were there for two mornings and on the first morning the special was eggs and bacon, and on the second morning, there were eggs and slices of ham. While at the hotel, we did notice that our air conditioning wasn't working and we called the front desk. They sent someone up promptly and he couldn't fix the problem. They asked us if we would mind changing rooms, since we had stuff strewn about the place (bottles, pack-n'-play, stroller, suitcase, stuff in the bathroom). We didn't mind at all, and they actually were able to move us to a room on the same floor. It was another wonderful, clean, spacious room. As far as location goes for this hotel, it's in a great place. We were able to walk to Navy Pier, the Magnificent Mile, the water tours, and restaurants. We only took a cab once, and that was from the train station to the hotel. We also went across the street and bought a bus pass and rode the bus to the zoo and back. On the last day, we took the bus back to the train station. Public transportation was really easy there. I was a bit apprehensive about it, seeing as though I had never really done that (other than the Disney buses, but that doesn't really count). When we got on the bus, I just asked the driver how to use the pass and he let me know. Each bus driver we encountered was very helpful. And the hotel is in a perfect location to bus stops; they're everywhere around the hotel. The last aspect of this review that I want to comment on was the fact that I felt safe. It was very important to me that we stay somewhere that I felt safe, and in this location, I felt that way. Overall, this review is very long, but I wanted to cover each aspect that I look for when reading other reviews. I loved this hotel and have actually already recommended it and have family staying there soon.

title: “A Beautiful Hotel in Charm City!”
text:
This was our 3rd time staying in Baltimore with this hotel being situated on the harbor, we were in the middle of everything. The room was very nice and clean. The beds were very comfortable but the view from our room was of a parking garage. The front desk staff was friendly and checkin was quick. Our room was on the 7th floor directly across from the indoor pool which got a bit noisy at night in the corridor. I believe the pool closed at 11pm as we didn't hear any outside hallway chatter afterwards.
We only stayed for one night so we didn't use their fitness facility but from the website pictures, it looked very nice. 
We booked through priceline a few days before and got a GREAT RATE so that made the stay even more enjoyable.
As with any center city or area of attraction, parking was expensive. The hotels parking garage was more expensive than surrounding garages. We found a garage on 122 E. Lombard St. for $19.00 a day which is directly across the street from the hotel. The hotel will charge you $28.00 for the self park and $40.00 for valet.
The hotel does charge $12.95 a day for internet.
Would stay here again.

title: “Not what I expected from the Brand - I expected more.”
text:
Pros:
Affordable price. Convenient location to the interstate. The front desk staff was very professional. The exterior of the building looked nice, as did the lobby and main stair. The complimentary hot breakfast was a nice touch. Nice light-block curtains in the bedroom. Comfortable pillows and bedspread. Great wi-fi reception.
Cons:
While returning to the hotel on our 2nd night during a heavy rain, the awning/drive up area was filled with cars that had no people in them. After having to unload packages, etc. in the rain and walk it in to the building, it was clear that the cars belonged to staff members and some friends of staff who were on smoking breaks and taking up the unload space in the front. The hallways and rooms had worn and buckling carpets. The upholstered furniture in the rooms was very warn and stained, and the sink and showed plumbing had low water pressure. The pull-out bed was so uncomfortable that I slept on the floor (the edge of the sofa pushed the mattress springs right across my back, and I am not very picky!) While we had a non-smoking room, the room smelled of smoke as did the hallway and common areas. The fridge first froze our fresh vegetables the first night, and then completely thawed and went warm the next day and our food was ruined. The spare blanket had a bug sealed in with the bag - which we would have easily overlooked had the property not otherwise been so shoddy. Noisy A/C unit that was not powerful enough to cool the front living area/pull0out sofa area. HBO did not work.

title: “I Wanted So Bad for This to Be a 5 Star Stay”
text: The Guest Services Manager Dustyn P. works very hard to maintain the #1 rating status of this hotel, but for us the stay did not quite measure up. We encountered several small issues during our stay including getting woken up by housekeeping even though we had a do not disturb sign on our door, rattling pipes in the shower, an elevator so slow that we needed to take the stairs from the 6th floor just to get out of the hotel, a desk clerk that ignored us when we needed an extra laundry bag, and an unsightly and poorly organized/managed breakfast area. On a positive note, we were assigned to a very quiet room on the 6th floor at the end of the hall, just as we requested thanks to Dustyn. We had a peaceful night's rest though expect to be woken up by hallway noise/other guests who are early risers. After traveling 3,100 miles and camping for 13 days, we were happy to stay at this hotel.....just did not live up to the expectations we had as a #1 rated hotel.

title: “Great Rooms, OK service.”
text:
Stayed at the Hilton Times Square 5 nights for a business event. The rooms were above average for NYC and the were very clean. The service wasn't great but it was OK. 
After getting a room on the 41st floor and a great recommendation for a sports bar around the corner, the quality of the service went down hill. 
When I asked the concierge to help get a reservation to a new restaurant in the city she wasn't aware of it. Ted's Montana Grill opened the week that i was there and I wanted to get some buffalo steak. She found a place called Ted's IN Buffalo that she could get me into. I had to give her the url and number of the place to call. 
Great location if you need to be in the center of everything!

title: “Exceeded expectations”
text: Booked for my b- day weekend. For the price (although discounted) I must say that the entire experience at the Chatwal exceeded our expectations. It was a 5 star experience. An attentive staff combined with a plush-swanky accommodation and atmosphere that created an exciting yet pampering stay. Lot's of room on our balcony to enjoy champaign in the evenings and selected cigars from near by Nat Sherman. The Lambs Club and the bar on site are a must for at least one evening during your visit. Great live entertainment and we bumped elbows with a few celebs on the way out. Times Square and the shows only a few foot steps away! We'll be back!

author.location: Panama City Beach, Florida, United States

title: “GREAT PEOPLE!”
text: I was in the scottsdale area on business and this was my first time at this location. I picked this location due to the brand, you can never go wrong with a FREE made to order breakfast and drinks in the evening. The staff at this location went out of their way to make my stay as comfortable as possible. Everyone smiled and some even remembered my name! Next time in this area I am booking this hotel. Thank you for the great service!

title: “grand old beauty”
text:
Was lucky enough to get a great deal for this hotel via hotwire, otherwise I doubt I would have been willing to pay the usual rate.
The hotel has the montgommery BART and MUNI lines out front, and all the light rail along market st is at your door step too. This makes getting around to see the sights of SF very easy and cheap.
Room was quite large with a lot of storage space. The bathroom was quite nice too - love a full length bath for a good soak after a long day of walking.
There's a decent gym on the 4th floor, along with an amazing swimming pool.
Staff were great at the hotel. Always willing to help and you really couldn't walk anywhere in the hotel without being greeted with a smile.
Some negatives about the hotel:
* area at night feels unsafe
* windows are not double glazed so you hear everything - cars, sirens, fights.
* if you face the new Montgomery side the whistle the doorman blows to attract taxis will drive you crazy. you hear it practically all day long from early morning to late at night

title: “What an excellent value (and nice people, too).”
text:
I have been staying at the Old Town Inn for at least 6 years. They have always provided me with a fresh, clean, well-maintained room, comfortable bed, ample breakfast, and a wonderful staff! Their pool is in a quiet, sheltered area that allows you to relax. The Inn is a short walk to the San Diego Trolley system, and near the Airport. Old Town is also a short walk for food, drink, and entertainment.
Many of the staff members are long-timers and actually make you feel like they care about you being back for another visit. Beatriz and Anna are two of the managers whom I have met and they are very proud of their establishment and its employees.
I highly recommend the Old Town Inn.

title: “Beautiful Grounds”
text: I stayed here for a conference for 5 nights and found the property to be well taken care of. There are fountains everywhere and the grounds are meticulous. From the moment you pull up you get immediate attention, checking is easy enough and they show you too your room as the property is very large and can be intimidating at first. This is the second time I have been back because of the welcoming experience. The rooms are very clean and the bedding is very comfy. During the conference the staff was very attentive and always made sure there was water and the tables were kept clean. The food cooked during the conference was amazing and better than the restaurant. The offered rides to surrounding restaurants and to the mall which was nice as the first time I was there I did not have a rental vehicle. I would return again, however I would make it at the same time as the water park is open as it looks enjoyable.

title: “Military Reunion”
text:
Our group the VQ Association recently (September 13-17) held our annual reunion at the Holiday Inn Bayside. What a terrific time we had there !! Jodie, Pat,Manny and the entire staff treated all of us like V.I.P.s Housekeeping,Restaurant services and the front desk exhibited kindness and caring along with attention to the details that made the event very special for us.
 The numerous hotel amenities allowed us to relax and enjoy ourselves without ever having to leave the premises. We did enjoy San Diego also. The rooms were well appointed. The food for Fridays Reception and Saturdays Luau Banquet was well prepared, presented and tasted really great. All in all it was a wonderful place to hold a multi-day event such as our reunion.
Frank VQA.

title: “Good room, great service”
text:
We stayed two nights on either side of dental implant surgery next door to the hotel. We booked a "junior suite;" it was really just a large room with king size bed, sofa, desk, easy chairs, and a separate bathroom as big as some European and Asian hotel rooms I've stayed in.
The suite was a corner room with large windows facing both Sutter and Powell. Those windows were effectively soundproofed.
Following the surgery I was not at the top of my game. I checked out forgetting that I'd left an Asus notebook computer in a desk drawer. Two hours later, from home, my wife called the hotel. The clerk said they'd found the computer and would either mail it to me or hold it for me to pick up. Given the number of items I've lost to theft in other hotels, this was remarkable.

title: “An oasis just off Times Square, small, comfortable, friendly”
text: We stayed five nights in late November 2010 and choose the Casablanca after reading lots of positive comments in TripAdvisor reviews. And we were not disappointed. Our welcome at 1am was friendly, room was not large but had all we needed, Location was excellent for what we wanted, (to be in middle of action in NYC in a smaller quality hotel), the first floor lounge was the real asset, where we could slip back there for a quiet recharge of coffee, papers, TV, internet, than back out into it. Staff were all very friendly, hotel was clean, everything worked, only about 44 rooms, so nice and intimate. 100% satisfaction

title: “A Winner”
text: My wife, sixteen-year-old daughter and I stayed for three nights, April 17-20. We loved it. The facility has the weighty feel of history and that's a wonderful asset in historic Boston. The suite was very nice and we loved the location; steps from Quincy Market, Boston Massacre site, State House and Freedom Trail etc. Boston is a "walking" city and the Custom House is a great stepping off point. It's nice to return to at the end of the walk also. My family is clamoring to return and I'm certain we will. Note-hotel parking is costly; on-street parking in the area however is very difficult. Perhaps investigate local, cheaper, overnight parking. Once in the Custom House you will probably walk to most destinations.

title: “Loved the Overalls!!!!”
text:
The Farmers Daughter was an fun and unique experience. The staff was not only friendly and accomodating but gosh darn Hee Haw cute!
The Farmer's Daughter offers a lot of bang for your buck. Confortable, casual, and affordable. 
Make sure before you check out that you get one of those T-Shirts!

title: “Great Stay at San Jose Marriott”
text:
In March, my husband had to go out to San Jose on business, so I joined him for a few days. This Marriott is lovely! Our room was clean and comfy. The internet worked well, and the beds were extremely comfortable. The restaurant, where I had breakfast, was somewhat pricey but very good. I had a really lovely breakfast! One day I had breakfast at the cafe, which was fine but nothing spectacular.
It was a bit chilly, but I still managed to use the pool, which is a very good size. The hot tub was great, too. The valet parking was great. The hotel staff was excellent, too -- particularly the front desk staff. Staff members were always more than happy to help me with suggestions, directions, and local info. I rented a car one day, and they were helpful in instructing me how to find a rental place. They also gave me clear and easy public transit directions. When I rented the car, I drove to Santa Cruz and then down route 1 to Big Sur -- what a drive! I highly recommend it -- so beautiful!
The location is fine, but San Jose does not have a ton going on, so the location may seem like it's nothing to shake a stick at. There is an art museum (lovely!) and the Technology (nice -- esp. for kids) museum just a few steps from the hotel. But if you want to go sightseeing or shopping, you'll have to find some sort of transportation. Overall, we really enjoyed our stay at this Marriott. The only thing that might prevent us from staying here again is the fact that San Jose isn't that exciting.
The location of the hotel was fine.

title: “Great!”
text: Very nice, quiet hotel in a great location. All the staff were friendly and helpful. Try this hotel - it's a gem

title: “Great place to stay in the center of Boston”
text: I went to Boston for a meeting at a local law school and stayed at the Nine Zero. The Hotel could not be more convenient to everything in Boston. It is just accross the street from the Boston Commons. So my afternoon run through the Commons and Boston Gardens was a treat. The staff and the accomodations were first rate. The rooms are not the largest you will find but they have everything you need to make a home away from home. The wine at 5pm in the lobby at Klimpton's is a really nice touch after a long day. I plan on staying there again when I return to Boston.

title: “Just read my review”
text: Okay so I see some reviews on here that are negative. Maybe, I stayed at a good time. Lol The only thing I have to say is some off the staff aren't to friendly that work on the floor and in the dining area. They can be rude. Also, the smell in front of the hotel is bad. It is a cheap stay compared to other hotels. The breakfast was good. You can't want to much for the price. The room was clean and the bathroom was nice. Wifi threw the hotel that's free. Close to downtown with free buses.

title: “Great stay at Parc 55”
text: I booked our hotel through Hotwire, so I didn't know where we were staying until after booking. Then I read reviews online and I must say that they were all over the place -anywhere from poor to excellent. So I was a little concerned and I called the hotel directly to see what our room would be like. I was told I could make a request for the type of room and location, but that they couldn't guarantee I'd get that. When we arrived to check in, the clerk said "I have the perfect room for you." She was absolutely right because she gave us a corner room on the 17th floor and we had a fantastic view of the city through two huge picture windows! The room was bright, clean, large, and quiet. The shower had great water pressure and we had absolutely no complaints. The staff were friendly and helpful and the location was perfect for us. It was close to all public transportation, restaurants, and shopping. All in all, it was a wonderful experience.

title: “Fantastic”
text: What a fantastic, luxury hotel that's a really great value. Beautifully appointed room and great robes! One of the best touches was the courtesy wine from 5 - 6 p.m. in the lobby! Everything about the hotel was very easy. From the minute you step out of your car, the staff is very accommodating and friendly.

title: “Definitely not my favorite”
text: I booked this room through Hotwire, and will avoid picking this part of town again (Hayes Valley/Civic Center) in an effort to avoid this hotel. I am a frequent traveler to San Francisco, and understand the concept of small rooms here, whether they market it as "boutique hotel" or "european style". I can honestly say this is the smallest room I have ever stayed in. My view of the fire escape doesn't help. Total claustrophobic hotel, with poor service. Not a great location to walk to things to (except Civic Center and Opera House), and poor service in bar/restaurant. They seem to run on their own hours, with no consistency. Not sure how Hotwire rates it a 3.5 star hotel.

title: “Concierge lounge”
text:
I recently stayed at his hotel for almost 2 weeks. I was fortunate enough to utilize the executive concierge lounge. Rosie was so great. She always greeted myself and my colleague with a big smile and knew what we wanted to drink after one night. She would even save us a couple of our favorite cookies to take with us back to our room. 
If you are lucky enough to get Rosie, you won't be disappointed!

title: “Modern, fresh, and elegant”
text:
Our 10th floor room was well-appointed with an incredible view of the city. The bathroom was modern and sleek, with a frosted glass sliding door and all new fixtures. Be aware that the glossy tiled floors are slippery when wet. Put a towel down for traction.
We were able to have breakfast in the Executive Lounge each morning before setting off into the city. There was a wonderful variety of food and beverages laid out beautifully. Traveling with one adult, one teen, and a toddler, we were glad to find a selection of items appropriate for each of us.
The valet staff was very responsive and patient, even when we needed to get into our car to find some missing Halloween costumes. The gentleman who waited with me was a great conversationalist as I tore through suitcases to find an item. And the cold citrus water near the lobby entry was refreshing after a long day sightseeing.
The only unfortunate encounters were with the security staff. Once, a security staffer rolled his eyes and refused to answer when we asked him a question. Another time, a guard hinted we should leave the elevator as he brought on a VIP. If he had outright asked us to leave for security reasons, we would have left. But he instead made a snide comment that we should get off because he was going up to the Executive Floor. Well, so were we. This VIP got to ride up with our family and guess what, he survived his encounter with the hoi polloi. Interactions with *all* guests should meet a minimum standard of courtesy, no matter what their rank or title.
Overall, our experience was positive, and I would stay again at the Washington Hilton. We are loyal Hilton guests and Diamond Elite members with over 100 nights per year at Hilton properties across the country -- this is a lovely property that we recommend wholeheartedly.

title: “Best Hotel in Boston!”
text: I recently stayed at the ames hotel in Boston with my girlfriend over Memorial day weekend. As soon as we walked in we were greated with smiles and a free upgrade to our room! This doesn't happen often but was nice as a first impression. The staff was extremely helpful and knowledgable of restaraunts, the city and different attractions to see. I had also requested a late check-out the morning of our last day so that we could go on a tour and they offered me an even later check-out time than I had requested with out any problems. This to me said they were willing to accommodate my needs as much as possible which I appreciated greatly. I recommend this hotel to everyone deciding to travel to boston. The location is perfect, the rooms are clean and amazing with a very modern feel, and there are plenty of attractions within walking distance from the hotel which is always nice. The staff was unbelievable and very curteous always willing to help and I must say that any time I have friends or family traveling to boston I will recommend this hotel every time. I will definitely visit boston again and I will be sure to stay here. The price of a 2-3 star hotel, with the amenities, rooms and staff of a 5 star hotel...You cannot beat this place! You will be missing out if you pass this hotel up for some big name chain. They are an up and coming hotel in boston that will only continue to rise through their service and professionalism!

title: “Friendly and Clean”
text: Our recent stay at the Marriott Marquis on Times Square was quite refreshing. The staff was incredibly friendly and most helpful! Rooms were clean. The internet and Wi-Fi did not work like it was supposed to. That created a bit of communication problem while being away from home.

title: “location yay, parking Nay”
text:
As a previous review mentioned, location - this hotel is located a few steps from Faneuil Hall/Quincy Market which makes it convenient to do a lot of walking. 
Parking, however is at a STEEP price. The hotel does not have any on site parking but does offer directions to the 75 State Steet Garage up the street. We parked there for 2 hrs (+2 mins) before deciding to go out. Big mistake. While I travel quite a bit for business, I am aware that parking can cost a bit, I certainly was not prepared for $35! Anything over 2 hrs is the daily rate of $35. (not posted anywhere) When I inquired about the rate at the front desk, I was told, well if you got your ticket stamped, you would've received a discount...maybe 20% (?!) Uh, maybe you should've told me that BEFORE I tried to leave the garage.
Renovations in this hotel are as previously stated - loud, dusty and not noted when the reservation was made. Had I known of this I would have selected another hotel. Doors were slamming all night. Not sure why.
The room was clean, bathroom clean but in need of a refresh and a bit more water pressure would have been nice. No Yellow Pages phone book in the room and no directions on the use of the phone. After the parking fiasco, I sure as heck was not even going to touch the phone. 
On the plus side - they do have internet access in the lobby to use and they offer complimentary coffee/tea/cocoa.
If you just want a place to stay for the night, this hotel is fine. Longer than one night, there are other places available.

title: “Perfect Location and Great Price”
text: This hotel has a perfect location and is very clean. Check in was a breeze and staff courteous and very helpful. Roof top bar was enjoyable, indoor/outdoor seating you can enjoy gazing at the Empire State Building next door. Macy's and Daffy's are just around the corner as is the subway. Cabs are always passing by and easy to flag down. Room was decorated nice and most importantly as two females we felt safe and the room was very clean. Would select again for future trips. Free continental breakfast.

title: “Good Location if you have a Car”
text:
We stayed at this hotel while visiting the Zoo and Sea World. The actual hotel was fine. The rooms were spacious and clean, but we found the location inconvenient as we did not have a car. There was a bus stop out the front of the hotel. This bus took us to the trolley station, where we changed lines to get to the Zoo & Sea World. This was not a problem, but apart from a quite pricey restaurant on site, there were no other places to eat within walking distance. If you have a car this would not be a problem, as there were plenty of places about 10 minutes drive away.
The free breakfast however, was fantastic. Plenty of food and a good variety. Also, a nice pool & spa.
The hotel itself was fine, but I would not recommend staying here without your own transport.

title: “Great location & Rooms but indifferent staff”
text:
This hotel has a really great location if you're looking to jump off into the South End or head into Cambridge and a nice stroll to Boston Common. There really is no bad spot in Boston to stay, I soon realized when booking this hotel.
I didn't really know what to expect location wise but it was great for what we were looking for.
We arrived around 6 in the evening and the check in was very smooth. The gentleman who checked us in was very courteous, helpful, and friendly. He was a little stiff for my liking but this is what you must expect when staying in a Sheraton/Westin. They were not hired for their personality..more so their talent and to work like a machine and spill out the same information over and over 500x's per night.
The room was a junior suite and was very nice. I even discovered that the sofa pulled out to be a bed as well, when needed. The view was very nice as well looking out into Cambridge. The only real complaint on the bathroom was the 'rainfall' shower head that was installed as a regular shower head. The design is off and in doing so the pressure suffers for the decor.
The next complaint comes in the way of the evening concierge team; both men. I called down to the desk from the room inquiring about a restaurant a friend of mine had suggested. The concierge was unfamiliar with Myers+Chang so he looked it up and placed me on hold. He came back on the line and stated once again that he was unaware of the restaurant but the address was 'x'. I asked him what the cross streets were and his response was 'I do not know'. What concierge doesn't know how to use the zoom tools in Google Maps? Google should be their best friend. I let it slide. On our way out of the hotel to dinner i stopped by the concierge desk again and inquired what are the cross streets of the restaurant. Different guy this time, he had heard of the restaurant but was unfamiliar of the location. He pulled out a map and said that it was on washington and then pointed on the map between a 4 block radius. Again, not able to give us a cross street. I am not sure why these two gentleman who's sole purpose is to aid and guide the guests were so unhelpful...and the tone in their voice and their attitude was completely unacceptable. We decided to walk to the restaurant. Once outside we asked the doorman which direction was Boylston street. He said that he didn't have his glasses and just stood there. Unbelievable how many rude people we ran into in just a 1.5hr time period. I hate to think ho room service and the housekeepers act!
Had breakfast buffet both mornings..service was very friendly and the food was mediocre. It is a buffet after all.
Apart from the long negative paragraph i would still recommend this place. I am hoping that my experience was just a fluke - maybe not though? The rooms and location were very good!!

title: “Tired Old Hotel”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nts Mar 1, 2, 3, 2012. GREAT Times Square location, looks great from the street, lobby looks beautiful. Super nice front staff. We were upgraded to the 8th floor (large corner room) - NW CORNER - facing Broadway out one window & Times Sqaure out the other window. AWESOME VIEWS! 
Once at the 8th floor, we noticed the halls walls, carpet & paint was worn, dingy & just plain tired looking. Our room looked the same, wall paper was yellowed & bubbling, sink was off color, our sink stopper was out, laying on the counter - later in our stay the sink backed up - we called & they sent someone to fix it, it helped for a while, but it was draining slow when we left. The bathroom was tiny... I banged my foot on the toilet getting into the shower. 
The bed was great, slept like a log every night. The subway runs right under the sidewallk below the room & about every thirty seconds you hear it. (It didn't bother us tho). Our TV was a large flatscreen, that we couldn't get to come on half the time without going to it & turning it off & back on (to reboot it).The picture was fuzzy & had lines all thru it. Not terrible, but not clear. 
There is no fridge in the room, so we used our bathroom wastebasket lined with a plasic liner filled with ice to keep our wine & beer cool. Plastic cups, cheap (vegetable) bath soaps...really? Gees. 
You have to pay for internet service in the room (I used my 3g phone & MIFI for my laptop for free)...however the connections were S L O W... They have free internet in the lobby & several computers & printers.
The hotel has a nice restaurant that is only open for breakfast. No Bar. Strange to us. People are up, milling around at all hours of the night, we sure would have liked to have had a drink in the hotel bar.... if there had been one. 
Would I stay here again??? Maybe. Only if the price was right (as it was this time - they offer a government rate). To pay their regular price, I'd stay at several of the MANY other hotels in the area with the same price range. The Park Central is just steps away, as is the Sheraton (both in the same price range). 
I've actually stayed in nicer Holiday Inn Express' & Hilton Garden Inn's. 
Starwood needs to upgrade this hotel...it desperately needs a refurb, desperately. And a full time restaurant with a BAR! Hope they are listening.

title: “Helpful young lady at the steakhouse”
text: I've stayed at several W hotels around the world but this hotel really honored the motto of "Whatever/Whenever." The room was fairly small & the upstairs bar was a bit loud, however, the staff was very pleasant. What made my experience more pleasant was my interaction with a young lady who works next to the concierge desk - I believe her name is Jasmin. The concierge was away from his desk and she was friendly and helpful with assisting me with making reservations at another restaurant outside of the hotel and made certain that I had the directions on how to get there. Also, she informed me of the different museums and local attractions that I could take my kids to, etc.. Great Stay!

title: “A really nice stay...with things to know about...”
text:
This was our first stay at the Drury chain, and our first stay in North San Antonio. I think we all can say we had a pretty darn good time! 
To us, the location is fine. There are lots of restaurants, retail stores, strip malls, and such all around. The Hotel is on the north side, which is a one-way Frontage road, so anything you want to go to that's before the hotel, you'll need to take the Frontage road all the way to the next turn-around, and trek back. Not the end of the world, but you should be aware of that.
The parking lot is somewhat a challenge for spaces, but of course, you can park at the huge Drury Plaza right next door.
Hotel staff were pretty good, and pretty responsive to our questions.
The whole Drury concept is beyond us. How the heck can this hotel stay in business offering all that FOOD for $0.00! Night-time "Kickback" with hot foods, cold drinks, and free alcohol teasers...wow! Add in a relatively full hot breakfast buffet, afternoon/evening (AWESOME and FESH) popcorn, and you can feed the kids for free and plan a nice evening dinner less the cost of the kiddos.
The food, to be honest with y'all, isn't exactly top-level food. Hot dogs, nacho chips, salsa, cheese, baked potatoes (which were actually really YUM!) and salad. Each night is supposed to feature a different "highlight", but we were there on both Friday and Saturday nights, and there wasn't much of a change either night. But, considering what was offered and how much it cost ($0.00), you really can't complain. For the adults, a pre-dinner snakc; for the kids, possibly enough to feed'em!
The pool is sufficient for kids, but way too cold for us adults. We didn't make it to the hot-tub, "saw" the work-out room, witnessed the laundry facilities...and enjoyed the ambiance.
You should be aware (but remember, this can happen ANYWHERE!!): During breakfast, one of the guests irresponsibly left her purse on a table while she went to fetch food at the buffet. Well, two unsavory characters walked in through the front door, located the unattended purse, and you guessed it ...swiped it and ran! A late-witnessing guest made a yell for it, but the two were gone in a heart-beat. Remember folks, you're a travelor, probably carrying some kind of valuables, and thus, are a target for criminals. This can happen ANYWHERE, but it did happen...here. So, beware! Other than that...the immediate area did not really seem too worrysome.
We highly recomend this hotel for families with kids... Give it a shot! We'll be back!

title: “Generally okay, but quite run down”
text: I would call this hotel adequate. I booked via hotwire.com because I was being conscientious about travel costs for my company, but I would not stay here on my own dime. The hotel was quite run down. The room was clean, but just generally shabby. The bedding seemed a bit overused and in need of replacement. This place is just badly in need of an update. Judging by the pricing on their website, better accommodations can be had elsewhere for similar prices.

title: “What a Hotel!”
text: This was our second visit to LA and we stayed at the Bonaventure both times. The rooms are spaceous and have fabulous views, the glass lifts (elevators) on the outside of the building are amazing as are the views from the cocktail bar. The staff were all very polite and helpful and gave us a walking tour map taking in all of the intersting sights without having to worship celebrity status LA has a wealth of culture to enjoy and we thoroughly enjoyed our visit.

title: “Under the Radar San Diego Treat!”
text: Since it's renovation, the Sofia Hotel has definitely become one San Diego's best finds! The staff is incredibly helpful; the rooms have a "W" Hotel feel with their soft beds and modern furniture. I slept like a baby! If you're staying in the heart of Downtown San Diego and you want to party and not have to worry about taxi's or driving, I definitely recommend this hotel!

title: “Great hospitality at value price in prime location”
text: It was enchanting experience at a great price.Beatiful location and free continental breakfast.They also provide discount to neighboring restaurents........And there are pleny around the hotel. Very good check out experience too. Nice and clean hotel.

title: “Great Location”
text:
Great Location, right on the train line. Walk to Ground Zero, Wall St, Little Italy and Chinatown. Train at the door.
Rooms a bit small and lift very slow but otherwise good.

title: “The Moore Hotel Rocks !”
text: If you drive a Lexus and your wife has had expensive augmented surgery, you'll likely not like this hotel. But if you live in the real world, it's awesome !!! beds were VERY comfortable, shower was perfect. Toilet was great! View was great. TV worked and rug was clean. Staff were friendly and knowlegable. Eco friendly.

title: “A Wonderful Hotel”
text: I stay at the Sofitel New York for business every month. When it came time to travel to Chicago for pleasure, we immediately decided to stay at the Sofitel Chicago. The hotel is beautiful and well-located and the staff is friendly and helpful. The Sofitel Chicago is one of the best hotels in the city, if not the United States. Thank you to the staff for making our stay perfect.

title: “Great location, happy hour, breakfast. Large, clean rooms.”
text:
I spent three nights in this hotel and thought it was great. The complimentary breakfast and happy hour were a nice added touch to the overall experience that included large, clean rooms and a beautiful, spacious lobby area. The location couldn't be better with direct access to the Riverwalk and about a 5-10 minute walk to the convention center. I would definitely stay here again.
My only complaint is the long, somewhat confusing trek to the new tower, but the size of the rooms and balcony view make it worth it.

title: “Great hotel, good neighborhood”
text: It's an old traveler's hotel on US 101, but it's been well maintained and renovated. The rates are great! The rooms are clean. The bed is comfortable. Our bathroom was huge. There was a nice work area in the room. We found the hotel's wifi to be great in the mornings, but very slow in the evenings. There are several open wi-fi networks in the area that you can log onto instead when that happens. The hotel has parking, but we took the bus everywhere -- the hotel is a short walk from many bus lines. About the only thing we didn't like about the room was that they didn't use fitted bottom sheets, and for me that's a very minor issue. Overall, a great place to stay. We loved it and we'll stay again.

title: “1-Star Motel, not 3 star”
text:
Me and my gf booked this hotel for one night through hotwire and was told it was a 3-star hotel that provided complimentary breakfast before finalizing the reservation. Once I finished booking it the breakfast option disappeared. In the morning when we went to the cafeteria for breakfast and were told that we had to pay for it. Called hotwire and they refused to do anything and the guy accused me of not calling the last night.
The only good thing about this motel is their staff are friendly, thought they make mistakes such as giving you a key that doesn't work. And also the location gets you to main attractions really fast.
There is no way that hotwire rate this place a 3-star hotel. It is precisely 1-star or lower.The room smells musty and humid, the bathroom is tiny, and the A/C doesn't work. The knob of the A/C is broken and once you turn it on it smells even worse than the room itself. The place is pretty spread out and you have to constantly get outta your car to find room numbers because they are way too small to be found.
If you have chosen this deal with hotwire then congratulations you have overpaid.

title: “Perfect location, great hotel”
text: Set between 5th Avenue and Broadway/6th Ave with the Empire State Building a block away, Macy's on the end of the street and a subway station on the corner, you couldn't ask for much more from a central New York Hotel! The rooftop bar was an excellent bonus, with views directly to the ESB - breathtaking! Especially welcome during the hot weather we experienced during our trip. The free continental breakfast was a great feature, although the area did become quite busy. We stayed in a standard double, which was perfectly adequate for our needs, spacious enough with a built in wardrobe, flat screen TV and i pod dock clock radio, with a large comfortable bed. The hotel was clean and well kept, and all staff welcoming and friendly. The attached restaurant/bar is also worth a visit for lunch/dinner. We were in a room at the front of the hotel, and there was a lot of street noise from traffic and roadworks etc, but nothing a pair of earplugs didn't sort out - after all, you are in central New York City, not a quiet retreat!

title: “Okay for the price...just don't get a room by the street!”
text:
We had gotten the Jolly Madison through Priceline for $85/night through the busy Christmas weekend. When we saw our first room, we thought it was a joke...it was located behind the elevators in what we thought was a broom closet! We asked for a new room, and they kindly upgraded us to a Superior room on the 4th floor. Unfortunately, their version of "Superior" is still smaller than any other NYC hotel I have stayed in. 
That night, however, was absolutely horrible. At around 4am, the city started to do some emergency road construction on Madison Ave. Since the rooms appear to only have single pane windows, the jackhammering sounded like it was being done in the room itself. This went on for over two hours. Unfortunately the hotel couldn't change our rooms until the next day, but noted that half of the hotel complained about the noise. But they did change our room for the second night as we had requested, into a top floor room away from the street. All in all, it was a decent stay for the price. The room and floors are pretty outdated, although the bathrooms were beautiful. I'd give it a 2-star room and a 4-star bathroom (which probably accounted for their 3-star rating).

title: “Convenient, comfortable, quiet...”
text: Stayed at the Fairfield 2 nights after landing in Denver from the UK. It's very convenient for the airport - easy to locate and far enough away not to get any noise. There is a free shuttle to the airport if needed. It's also close enough to be able to get easily into downtown Denver. The rooms were clean and comfortable with giant TVs and coffee facilities. The breakfast was a good choice of cereal, toast etc. Coffee was also available on tap in the lobby - being from the UK we asked for tea and they supplied us with a variety of tea bags. Well recommended if you need a base close to Denver for a couple of nights.

title: “Great stay”
text:
This stay was great from start to finish. The gracious staff and amenities made up for the parts of the hotel which had not yet been renovated.
Although I arrived early my room was ready and they allowed me to check in. They apologized that my snack and beverage were not yet in the room and that they had not yet put my hospitality basket [for the event I was attending] in the room. They offered to have a staff person carry the hospitality basket to the room for me. 
When I returned from lunch and a little bit of sightseeing they had placed a bottle of wine, a box of crackers, cheese, a bottle of water, a pretty glass plate, a cloth napkin, silverware and a wine glass in my room. The wine, cheese and crackers were all high quality products. There was enough that I and my roommate used them for a light lunch the next day.
Saturday morning we ate in the restaurant. About the time that the waitress should have been serving our breakfast she appeared very apologeticlly. The cook had just told her that they were out of smoked salmon [an ingredient in my omlet] and would I like to substitute something else or order another dish. I ordered another dish and it was out very quickly. Not only was my breakfast comped but also my roommate's breakfast was comped.
Saturday night when we arrived back from the dinner and party there was a voicemail message. The manager had called to find out if I needed any help the next day when I was leaving. She also wanted to know how my stay had been and if there had been any problems.
Sunday at noon [check-out time] the hotel system shut off the key cards for all the rooms. They called the event host without prompting and apologized. They offered to make new key cards for anyone who needed them until they left.

title: “It Is What It Is, a Business Persons Hotel”
text:
Pros:
Very Comfortable King Size Beds
New contemporary room fixtures 
Free coffee pot and coffee/tea service in room
Away from the main street so noise is minimal
Walking distance to small shops and restaurants in Town and Country outdoor mall
Chain restaurants close by. Black Angus and Chilis.
Comforatable lobby with Wired internet access and shared printer
Free USA Today Newspaper delivered to room each morning
Various breakfast options available - for a price
Free coffee in lobby 24 hrs
Wired Free Internet access in room
Cons:
Noisy box air conditioners
Not much to do if you don't want to watch TV in the lobby or hangout by the pool
Priceier then most business hotels in area
No complimentary breakfast - local restaurants don't open til late morning
Wired Internet access only, no WI-FI available in whole Hotel or conference rooms
Minor Peeve - TV changer was slow and you could not go directly to TV channel. You have to scroll through each channel until you get to desired station.
I've stayed at better, I've stayed at worst. This hotel met my objectives, since I was at a week long conference at the same location.
Recommended for buisness, but not for weekend getaway or family fun trip.

title: “Pretty ideal for an easy going family on a budget”
text: We stayed here over the holidays. OUr family includes two small children and we were all quiet pleased. We are a conventional firmly upper middle class family who are not scared off by sparse amenities or less than stunning rooms. That said, we know when to say when and I was very concerned about many reviews I had read and considered cancelling my reservation. I am very glad I did not. The rate was insanely low for the location (the north-west side of Central Park around the 100 block and near Broadway) and the room was very well suited for our needs. Understand this is pure no frills, ie. no tv, shared bath, standard sheets, no comforter. The showers went cold fast and if you slept in, getting a shower might require a wait (we got up well before most in the hostel). The staff was considerate and accomodation, but pretty busy. For example, we had to shovel out of heavy snow and they happily lent me a snow shovel, but I had to wait quiet a while to get it. The rooms were clean, though pretty run down. Our room was very convenient and spacious, though I heard that other rooms had tighter dimensions. The beds were comfortable; though we were glad we brought extra blankets. There was some street noise and hall sounds, but nothing we could not sleep through. We had wi-fi in our room, which helped entertain my wife and I after the kids went down for the night and we were trapped in the darkened room. The common space was small, but bristling with interesting people and discussions. The location was very convenient and we got premium street parking right in front. The neighborhood was very walk able and pleasant. And most of all, the price was the best you are likely to find in the City. Be aware, this is no frills and best suited for those who plan on spending most of their time out and about, but we will probably check in hear in the future rather than staying in tight quarters with friends when we visit the City .

title: “Not a single issue”
text: My girlfriend and I stayed here this past weekend May 31-June 2 it was very clean and the room was really pleasant,she still has not stopped raving about it,the bathrooms were so modern and the bed was so comfortable, you cant beat the price very reasonable,we will stay here again in the heart of Hell's Kitchen.

title: “Good for New York, even if not a Good Hotel”
text:
As many regular travellers with a "normal" nightly budget will know, New York may be one of the World's Great Cities, but its greatness is in no way based on the quality of its middle-of-the-road hotels: these tend to have small rooms, aging decor and poor customer service.
So although in any other city this Holiday Inn would be "just another cookie-cutter Holiday Inn", these attributes in New York, in particular the room sizes, elevate it above much of the competition.
And the location, not far from Columbus Circle, is very convenient.
Would I go back? Yes, I have been doing so for years.

title: “Houston Embassy, we have no problems!”
text:
Just finished a great three night stay at the Embassy. The hotel is located downtown right across from the Toyota Center and very close to the Minute Maid ballpark. Nearby is some shopping and restaurants but not a ton of other activity.
The hotel was spotless and in fact, so much so that I thought that it may have recently opened. The room was typical Embassy - very spacious with all of the usual amenities. A really nice gym and a great outdoor pool. The other typical pluses of staying at an Embassy were actually extraordinary. At the Manager's Reception they gave you a nice draft beer, in a nice real pint glass (as opposed to the usual plastic cups). Same goes for the wine.The free food was also excellent. Fresh veggies, cheese, nuts, chips/salsa and a varying hot appetizer. All laid out very nicely. Breakfast the next morning was just as enjoyable.
I would also compliment the staff. Everyone from the valets, to the front desk, to the servers at breakfast, were all very, very friendly and happy to assist you.
My only subjective concern (not a complaint) about this hotel is its decorative sustainability. The hallways and rooms were trendy but also had some sort of "green" (as in environmental) theme going on. Cute-sy now, but I suspect it will look dated very quickly.
Overall, a great stay and I would certainly stay there again.

title: “Typical Super8- Good!”
text:
This is a typical Super8 hotel- no thrills but good value.
Check-in efficent. Room clean and tidy. Good wireless internet access. We found a local mexican restaurant in the Wal-mart centre on the opposite side of the freeway. Area is dry, so be prepared to show your driving licence if you want a beer!
Like many of these hotels (other brands as well) proximity to freeway means traffic noise at night, so don't plan on a full sleep!
Overall, no major complaints for the money.

title: “Have a sense of humor about it.”
text: Okay, everyone. Calm down for a second. I booked this hotel a few weeks ago for a last-minute trip to New York without really looking into it much. Once I started reading the reviews, I was terrified to stay there, but my friend and I decided to give it a go anyway, and it's not that bad. Yes, the lobby is grimy and some of the staff members are pretty shady looking. The carpet was pretty dirty and disgusting, and I wouldn't suggest walking around barefoot. Bring flip flops for the shower or something. Anyway, a soon as we entered the room we tore the sheets off the bed and flipped the mattress to look for bed bugs. We didn't find any and neither of us ever had any bites, so I have no reason to think that there were bed bugs. We did, however, buy some cheap blankets at a Walgreens around the corner and we slept with those rather than under the sheets. There are basically zero amenities, so if you were expecting the Hilton, you should probably stay somewhere else. However, not many people I know go to New York City to sit in a hotel room, so if you're like us and just need a shower and a place to sleep, this will be just fine. I wouldn't want to stay there for a long period of time, but for just a few days, it served its purpose. If you have a good sense of humor, it's actually pretty hilarious. It just added more character to our trip, and now we get to say that we survived the dirtiest hotel in America!

title: “Quirky but pretty”
text:
I was a little skeptical when I opened the door and was greeted by a funky smell. Then I looked around the room and was disappointed at how tiny it was. 
As the evening set in, all of a sudden it was like the room was transformed. The lighting was perfect, the size didn't seem to matter as much, the funky smell was replaced with my perfume and lotion and the bed that looked lacking of linens was extremely cozy. 
I enjoyed the claw footed bath tub - that was a nice touch. Despite being about 2 blocks from Union Centre it was quiet. The floors were creaky but that's expected with an older building. 
The breakfast could use some work. Why go half way - it's a very French place - breakfast is served in the Jeanne D'arc restaurant - complete with statues and what looks like instruments of torture - serve a French breakfast. I would gladly pay an extra $10 for that.
The staff was extremely friendly and helpful and was a welcomed addition to the overall experience.
I would say it's my favourite place that I stayed at (out of 5 places) during my week long trip to California.

title: “Reserved a room during their $20/ night Jan. 2nd promo. $20 is $20 too much.”
text:
This was, hands down, the grossest hotel room I have ever stayed in. Or have ever NOT stayed in, I guess I should say, because we didn't stay overnight.
Back in December, Red Roof Inn ran a promo where it was $20. and change to stay one night (January 2nd) at any of their US locations. Since we live outside of Chicago, I thought this would be something fun for my husband & I to do. $20 hotel, great location, what's to lose?
Normally I research hotels to death before booking, but I could *swear* I'd stayed at this exact hotel years ago, so I didn't research this at all. Big mistake, because I stayed at the hotel across the street, not the Red Roof Inn! This hotel's location is fantastic: 1/2 block off Michigan Ave., 8 blocks from Navy Pier, close to tons of restaurants. It's a perfect location for Chicago shopping/touring. It is safe & very "walkable."
Upon check in, the employee looked absolutely startled to see us, perhaps because I am not a hooker? I do not know. In hindsight, I should have known right then that this was a mistake. He was very, very nice. Check in was quick, the rate was correct, we were in our room in minutes. 
The room was so outdated- like nothing I'd ever seen before. Seriously, my retro 1970's cottage is more 'up to date' than this hotel. The room was small, which I can handle. It was a bed, a dresser with a flat screen tv and a desk. 
The walls were dingy. I could literally see through the sheets. The sheets were stained. The carpeting was disgusting- like keep your shoes on disgusting, because the Red Roof Chicago apparently doesn't include vacuuming with their cleaning service. There was so much lint/ crumbs/ random debris along where the carpet met the walls, I nearly gagged. We reserved a smoking room, so anticipated a smoky smell, again something I can handle. However, there were ashes all over the desk, floor and bed. My husband had to use the washroom and didn't even wash his hands afterwards because he didn't want to touch the faucet! 
I would recommend staying anywhere else but here, even if it means buying less while shopping, it's that bad. Remember, this was a $20 room that I wouldn't spend $20 on! I have no idea what the regular rate is, but there is no way I would pay money to stay here. 
We immediately checked out & were told that we wouldn't be charged. I would have happily paid $20 NOT to stay in this hotel, so I couldn't care less. All in all this ended up being 19 minutes of my life & $6 for 19 minutes of parking that I am ok losing. We ended up going home & having dinner locally, lol. 
Would I recommend this to a friend? I wouldn't recommend this hotel to someone I dislike, let alone someone I might see again!

title: “A great find!”
text: We chose this Inn after finding it in the Rough Guide to California - after a long drive from Flagstaff, AZ, we were looking for a 2 night stay. When we arrived we were permitted to see the room and we decided to stay 3 nights - the place just had a lovely feel to it. We had a great time, chilling by the pool (which was clean and had lots of pretty flowers and plants around) Breakfast was a bonus, really generous with pastries, waffles boiled eggs and cereals, staff were really helpful - better service than you'd receive in a motel and the price here was really good too. Can't fault the place at all!

title: “WHAT A DUMP”
text:
This hotel was the worst place ever..... the room was the size of a closet
 the TV didnt work, there was mold all over the bathroom floor, furnishing was in such bad taste, this place was a dump.....

title: “Excellent place to stay in uptown Charlotte”
text: My wife and I stayed here on wedding night. The staff was amazing and was top notch. The hotel was clean and immaculate. Everything from the bathrooms, to the linen to the flat screen televisions were simply the best. Far exceeded my expectations.

title: “A Great Experience”
text:
This was a great place to stay in San Francisco. It is a relatively inexpensive place to stay in a great location. There is free parking for those with a car or if not, there is plenty of public transport close by, including the cable car route which is only a couple of blocks away.
The room was clean and roomy (and included a fridge). The free breakfast was one of the best, with plenty of fresh fruit, a variety of pastries, juice, coffee, hot choc, etc.
I travelled with my husband and 6 & 4yr old and we always felt safe in this area, even walking around at night. There are heaps of great places to eat and a supermarket and pharmacy within walking distance. There is also a laundromat close by.
The only problem we had was with a blocked toilet on our last morning, and when I went to report it, I was given a plunger! While we managed to fix the problem, we thought this was a bit odd!
Overall though, it is good value for money and in a great spot.

title: “Best Drury Inn we have stayed at !”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights after driving a rental car to Grand Canyon and Moab, Utah. It is conveniently located on W Pinnacle Peak Road just east of I-17. You can easily see the building driving down the Interstate. The two of us were impressed right when we walked thru the main entrance with the huge lobby area. We felt like we were inside a luxurious hotel compared to the usual places we stay at. 
The check in lady was very friendly and welcoming. I reserved our room with 2 queen beds online and asked for a room on the top floor (7th). She happily gave us a room on the 7th floor. Our room is good sized along with a spacious bathroom. We could hardly hear any traffic noise at all which was nice since Im a light sleeper. 
We loved the pool which is half inside and outside. I sat in the hot tub for 15 minutes before going outside to lay out in a lounge chair and catch some sun. It only took 15 minutes before my skin started to turn red, so I came back inside before getting sunburned. 
As other reviewers noticed, the toilet has two buttons on top which Ive never seen before. "Liquid" and the more heavy duty "Solid" waste buttons. The shower stall has 3 attached dispensers for shampoo, conditioner, and shower gel which is also convenient. Also the bathroom has an exhaust fan which is always sucking out air for constant ventilation which was nice. 
The free breakfast and kickback dinner were excellent ! For breakfast you can make your own giant waffle along with getting other hot food like scrambled eggs, sausage patties, etc. Kickback dinner is also good with 3 drinks included. I ordered 3 rumdrivers to go with my hotdogs, baked potato, and other hot foods that change every night. No hotel we've ever stayed at offers a hot dinner like Drury Inn does, making it an excellent value.
If you are visiting the Phoenix area, I highly recommend staying at this hotel. Convenient location, excellent value, and great food !

title: “amazingly fantabulous !”
text: i went here with my school and it was GREAT , there was 41 of us and we all had a fab time its so close to resturants such as mcdonalds and burgerking also for breakfast we had dunkin' donuts ! jus a 2 min walk if that to the subway and u could go anywhere ! , the beds were sooo comfortable ! the bathroom was lovely clean ! spotless ! and we got a plasma screen t.v! what more could you want ! the hotel was clean -very clean and very silent ! the staff were friendly seen as though they had 41 kids staying with them . all i can say is i would definatly stay there again ! people who say it was rubbish are probably snobby so please stay here it was amazing !

title: “This hotel totally exceeded our expectations!”
text:
From the very beginning, we were given above standard service. The staff were kind and courteous. In our case we were guests because I was having a medical appointment at UCLA Medical Center. We booked for one night, but after our appointment I felt I needed another night. They had no problem meeting our needs. We immediately were escorted to a new room. 
The rooms were beautifully decorated and the beds were clean and comfortable. The wide screen HD tv was very cool. The toiletries were of good quality which is always a nice surprise. The room service was great and the food was delicious. I was too ill to go to the on -site restaurant, but by our next appointment I definitely plan to enjoy a yummy dinner on the 17th floor. Again,, the staff are what makes a hotel stay what it is and these staff were just the greatest!

title: “Most comfortable bed ever!”
text: Our room was small, but comfortable and spotless. The bed was so comfortable that I called the hotel after returning home to find out the brand. I wanted that bed at my house! Staff was helpful and friendly. Great location.

title: “Great for a business trip, too”
text: I stayed here for a quick business trip that required I go in and out of the hotel several times. I appreciated the free, no hassle, self-parking. It was really hot but each time I could find a little shade under a tree in the open parking lot. I used the business center which was easy to use, had free internet, and the printer actually worked! I also agree with all the good stuff everyone else says about the comfort of the room and friendliness of the staff. Fancy and luxurious but easy to work out of too.

title: “A Gem in the Rough”
text: Stayed here by myself for 5 nights to visit my daughter in Asutin. Uncertain at first from the look of the outside, but inside is newly appointed and updated and very nice. Room was spacious, clean and quite, and it had been recently updated. State troopers stay here while attending classes down the highway, so I felt VERY safe. Complimentary breakfast was GREAT - eggs cooked to order, bacon or sausage, biscuits and gravy, in addition to the regualr bagels, cereal, oatmeal, fruit, etc. Only complaint would be that the lighting was rather low, due to the CF bulbs. I plan to stay here every time I visit my daughter in Austin.

title: “Not bad for the price in NYC”
text:
Paid $155 per night through priceline, which is a pretty hard to beat deal for a nice hotel in Manhattan. We stayed in a Cozy Room on floor 14, which was teeny tiny, but that is to be expected in New York. No major complaints, but based on the room amenities alone, this is more of a 3 star than a 4 star hotel. Bed was very comfortable, bathroom was sparkling. Lighting in the room was minimal but sufficient. Plenty of room in the closet for hanging clothes, but there wasn't a good place for us to put out luggage. 
Had a fabulous facial and a mediocre manicure at the Bliss spa. Living Room in the lobby was a very pleasant place to sit and relax with a drink.

title: “Ramadas used to be reputable”
text: I should have read the reviews before I stayed. I had to agree with all of them. Shady characters hanging outside by doors making noise under my window. Dirty windows, dirty carpet, dirty bathtub, stuffy air, hard bed.

title: “Smallest rooms ever”
text: Room was so small there was about 1.5' to walk around the foot of the bed - you had to do this to get to the dresser and desk. Had to stand to the side of the toilet to be able to close the door to the bathroom. NOISY - heard every slamming door all night long.

title: “Typical business hotel”
text:
Stayed here for a conference. It was OK.
Cons
1. 14 pieces of tired exercise equipment in a hot room. Not adequate and no fans.
2. Found a few hairs in my room. 
3. Tired decor around the hotel.
Pros
1. Comfortable bed, decent linens. 
2. Convenient location. 
I wouldn't stay here for pleasure, but it worked for business travel.

title: “Crummy hotel in a decent area”
text: This hotel has great potential since it is in a nice, friendly walking neighborhood that is just a 10 minute bus ride from everything that is great about this city. The rates are decent for this area as well. However, the poor customer service of the staff/owners, noisy parking lot and somewhat questionble character of other guests there (fights in the parking lot in the middle of the night and several really noisy neighbors partying all night) make it a place I would not stay again. The Greenwich Inn in the Marina area is much nicer for about the same price.

title: “Smells like feet”
text: This hotel is nice, and normal enough from what you'd expect from a Hyatt Regency... Until you get to your guest room. It smelled awful, like that of dirty feet or dirty laundry. Thought it was just my room, until 4 out of my 5 colleagues all had the same complaint in separate rooms on separate floors, not to mention the room next door to me, who I overheard the woman staying their yelling at the hotel staff for how horribly her room smelled.

title: “Great well run hotel”
text: This hotel really is well run, the check in staff are friendly and efficient, offering a class of champagne as you check in. The rooms are large and the beds very comfy. The public rooms are well furnished. The pool area is stunning and the two pools are clean and well tended. The free transport is good within 3 miles, however the driver demands a tip saying this bus runs on gratuities when he drops you back at the hotel, is this official policy?

title: “A 100% JEWEL”
text:
Please don't consider another hotel if you value a condo sized room with incredible views of the bay. Forget check in. A breeze. No lobby, no restaurant, no bar and no real health club. No matter. 
The rooms are a work of art. Spacious, tastefully furnished, and perfect in every respect. This property gives new meaning to the term suite. The beds are wonderful, linens superb. The bathrooms, three in our two bedroom unit, are perfectly adequate. Park Hyatt Chicago luxury? No, but damn close. No tub and only one sink but not an issue. Large walk in showers are a pleasure. Use the spacious bathroom upstairs or the half bath downstairs. 
A fully equipped kitchen with a wine cooler and all top of the line appliances is adjacent to a beautiful dining room and living area with a gas fireplace. A flat green tv along with a dvd player and stereo is standard. This place is just as home. Oh, I forgot the washer and dryer.
Jeremy is the go to concierge. Joe is also an all star. The rest of the staff is eager and professional. A house car is available for drop off and pickup. The director, Mr. Sylvester, made everyone feel right at home.
The continental breakfast is outstanding, with fresh fruit and yogurt, as well as a selection of pastries, eggs, and beverages. 
Bottom line- don't stay anywhere else.

title: “Surprisingly excellent overnight stay”
text:
We stayed here for one night, choosing this property only for proximity to the airport and not expecting much more than a basic room. I was pleased to find a comfortable, well appointed room. The manager's happy hour which was in progress upon our arrival featured delicious pizza.
The staff was as helpful and accommodating as any personnel in much higher end hotels. The complimentary breakfast was generous with hot and cold offerings.
My experience with this property was totally positive and will make choose the Hampton brand when possible in the future.

title: “Gem of a Hotel :)”
text: My boyfriend and I usually have had great experiences at Kimpton Hotels, so we thought that it would been a safe move to book Hotel Alexis for our 3 nights stay in Seattle. Loved the fact that we could take the Link Light Rail directly from the airport to University Street station that is only about 3 blocks away from the hotel. The hotel staff was extremely friendly and helpful. One of them recommended Etta's for happy hour for seafood which ended up being a great find. We were surprised how quite the rooms were though the hotel was close to everything. The hotel was also 5 min taxi ride to Amtrak when we took the train to Vancouver. Just loved Seattle overall and Hotel Alexis was perfect for us to come back to relax and rest up for the next day.

title: “Wonderful stay at Holiday Inn Philadelphia-Historic District”
text: We had a pleasant stay at the Holiday Inn Philadelphia-Historic District. Daniel was very welcoming to us when we checked in. The hotel is in a very convenient location to local attactions.

title: “Noisiest place I ever stayed”
text: Convenient location but didn't seem to be in the safest area. We stayed for 4 nights in a fairly clean room. The lobby was dirty and the staff was not at all friendly. This hotel is too close to a very noisy freeway and we would never stay there again. We saw some very nice looking motels within a mile that would have been a lot nicer. The only good thing about this place was the price.

title: “Perfect quick getaway”
text: My husband and I stayed Sat through Tuesday for our Anniversary. The resort is just gorgeous, staff friendly and close to what we wanted to do. We were unhappy with the room view upon check in, but we asked and we were quickly moved to a great view of the pool area. We paid extra for the Griffin Club, which was beyond our expectations. The use of the club made our stay 1000 times more enjoyable. We ate all our meals there...it was like hanging out in your living room!! Saturday and Sunday the main pools and lazy river were pretty busy with families and kids, but Monday and Tuesday were very quiet. They had a lot of conventions each day, but it did not affect our stay at all. My husband played golf at the two courses and loved the desert scenery as its so different from NJ courses. We would absolutely recommend this property to anyone visiting the area.

title: “Far and above the rest!”
text:
I began my love affair with Kimpton Hotels 3 years ago with the Hotel Monaco in Portland. I have since traveled to both Kimptons in Portland and all 3 in Seattle. This crazy rushed world simply slows down to a friendly, welcoming pace once you walk through the front door. The style, elegance, comfort, and customer service prove that traveling can be a five start experience! I recently filled out an online comment form and mentioned a very minor detail...and within a day I had an unexpected personal response with an instant remedy for my concern. It is personal touches like that that make me a loyal follower! 
Our Springer Spaniel, Maggie Clementine, travels with us about half of our visits and the pet friendly atmosphere is priceless! Our whole family will always recommend Kimpton Hotels! Thank you!!

title: “Very nice stay”
text: We had a very nice stay at Sofitel. The rooms and bathroom were quite large and well-maintained. The bed was one of the most comfortable I have slept in, and came close to derailing our plans as it was hard to get up! Evening turn-down was a nice touch, with macaroons, evian, and a pear left on the table. Nice hallways with nice bright lightning. Didn't need to interact much with the staff, who seemed nice, although the front desk staff were sporting such French heavy accents that they were almost unintelligible; my husband tried to engage one in conversation in French, and it quickly became evident that the accent was a put-on! Funny! But it is NYC! Location is very good in mid-town with good access to grand central station and 5th avenue.

title: “Very nice”
text: It is not in the main riverwalk, but a simple map search told me that. It is also NOT a mile away from the nearest entrance. It is no more than .5 mile from anything. Walked to the Alamo carrying a 5 yr old on my shoulders with no difficulty. I would not have walked the Riverwalk at night with the family, but would not have thought twice about it by myself. Hotel itself is very nice and everything I saw was very clean. In fact, I saw a customer have his breakfast cleaned off his table while he waiting on a bagel. That is not indicitive of a dirty hotel. Staff are very friendly. Rooms are very large. Bathroom is small, but I don't choose a hotel for bathroom size. Would definitely recommend if you are willing to walk a LITTLE in order to save some money.

title: “Central Location”
text: Just spent two nights in LA and the JW Marriot was a nice fit. The hotel appears to be only a few years old and certainly in great condition. The staff was very friendly and accomodating. So much so that they opened the house store after hours to get me some Aspirins after I asked them where the nearest convenience store was. I also found the rooms well appointed and the towels were soft and body friendly. I would recommend staying there just don't walk more than a couple of blocks away as the terrain changes drastically with the homeless, graffitti, and trash.

title: “Comfortable and Accomadating”
text:
I spent a week here and was very pleased at the hotel and services. There were only 2 negative points that I would have to make about this hotel. 
1. It is a non-smoking hotel (and I am a smoker - but for those of you who do not smoke, disregard this comment).
2. The rooms only had intenet in the living rooms. Although the quality of the on-line services was good, it was not wi-fi but ehternet, which limited it to the living room. Cables in the bedroom would be nice.
Other than those two points, the hotel in general was outstanding. The rooms were clean and comfortable, and the staff insured that my needs were satisfied. 
I would be remiss if I did not mention some specific staffers at this hotel that insured that my stay there was as comfortable and pleasurable as possible.
1. Andrea Carter, the assistant hotel manager. She was a valuable resource, as well as going above and beyond in order to help not only me, but many of my colleagues with details concerning room accessories and travel arrangements.
