2. David Grossman, who was a valuable resource and helped insure morale of the group was maintained after we returned to the hotel in the evening.
3. Geoff Merriman, who was a great resource of things to do and places to go int eh evenings.
Overall, my stay at the Brookshire was a wonderful experience and I would recommend this hotel to friends and colleagues for future travel.

title: “This is a perfect place to stay in Downtown Detroit.”
text:
It is close to the people mover, Comerica Park, Ford Field, Opera House, Fox Theatre, etc. 
Great beds, small bathrooms but adequete, nice tv's and room furniture, breakfast looked good. All around nice place to stay and enjoy the D!

title: “Great views on the lakefront side”
text:
We had a free night with Marriott points and thought we would splurge on a night at the Blackstone. The room was nothing special but the view was superb. We were lucky enough to be upgraded to a higher floor with a lake view which was breathtaking. The boats, Buckingham fountain and a distant view of the museum campus and Navy Pier. It was hard to leave the room! The bathroom was huge with a great rainfall shower and well appointed although the outlet didn't seem to work. Very clean.
Our check in was wonderful and kudos to Drew, who was warm and welcoming and provided superb service! We came in early after check out from another hotel, and she had us in a room before noon, which was perfect. 
We also had Club privileges on the 23rd (?) floor which added a lot. Evening heavy hors d'oevres and cheese, desserts in the later evening (which we missed) and a hearty breakfast of bacon, eggs, fruit, toast, oatmeal. Didn't care for the eggs, but cereal, toast and fruit was fine for me. It was lovely to have table by the porthole windows overlooking the city. Cozy and comfortable.

title: “Ok hotel but wouldn't stay again.”
text: This is an ok hotel in a pretty good location but we found the beds really small and uncomfortable. The rooms were missing 2 important things for us, a fridge and a safe in the room and for those reasons we would choose a different hotel. Wifi is also very pricey however the staff at this hotel were very accommodating and friendly and the room was very well cleaned.

title: “location location”
text:
stayed one night in park central in april. 
after having experienced a horrible flight, we arrive early at the hotel at around 12 and where able to check in early by the great receptionist without even having to ask. i've been in hotels who are extremely snobby about staying true to their check in times even though its clear there would be rooms available. i was very pleased by this and my friend and i both extremely great full. 
the hotel is quite nice, very modern lobby with nice paintings around the common area. the rooms were quite standard a nice comfortable bed facing a nice flat screen tv. bathroom area was quite small but no different to any other hotel and its amenities were nothing great. only problem with the room is that, unless we are quite stupid, we couldnt find a mini fridge/ cups utensils anywhere. that was disappointing however who wants to eat in their room when you are in NYC. 
best part was definitely the location, you can't get better than that for the price you paid so would recommend for that reason!

title: “Very nice hotel with excellent value for money”
text:
We stayed three nights in this hotel in Little Italy, although this part has already been swallowed by Chinatown in recent years.
The hotel is rather new, which is always a plus. The rooms are very clean, the staff is friendly. We had two kings size beds for two persons. We rather had a room with terrace, but coudln't upgrade due to full booking.
We were on the second floor, and were somewhat afraid of noise at night, but there was no problem, possibly due to the slow season.
Breakfast is in a little diner a few houses down the road, and is a plus, although not enormously luxurious.
The subway (Canal street) is a 5min walk, and a lot of attractions are within walking range. For a budget hotel (in Manhattan, that is), this offers very good value!

title: “Nice Hampton Inn”
text: This is a very clean and well maintained Hampton Inn. It is actually in a fairly quiet location in a nice part of town.

title: “bachelor hotel”
text:
stayed there for a week with two kids (13 years old)
-good location ( 100 m far from the parc)
-nice terrace
-suite 700 OK / although most of the equipment start to age!
-very dark in the room - almost no light to switch on!
-club atmosphere in the lobby - loud music at night! 
-too loud if you are over 30!!!
-clearly not a family hotel
-

title: “Good location, terrible rooms!”
text: First room had loud banging pipes and right next to elavator even though I asked not to be near elavator. After hearing what sounded like a hammer on a pipe every 15 minutes we moved rooms next day. When we got new room it turned out to be a handicapped room. This is the first time ever I wasn't asked first if I wanted handicapped room. Shower was horrible. Would flood entire floor. This place was just gross.

title: “Great Location”
text: The interesting thing about this hotel is that is on a narrow island in San Diego Bay connected to the Point Loma Peninsula by a causeway. As a result, the hotel is surrounded by water on two sides. All rooms either face a marina and the peninsula on the west, which is the best view, or the bay and downtown San Diego on the east. Our room was clean, the amenities were modern, and the staff was friendly.

title: “Awesome!”
text: We had tickets to the Star Wars In Concert show at the Hollywood Bowl and decided to spend a little time in Hollywood at the same time, since we haven't been there in about 20 years. First, we couldn't have picked a better location for our trip. The shuttles to the Bowl were about a 2-3 minute walk from our hotel. The mall at Highland Ave is about 100 feet from the hotel. Hollywood Blvd is maybe another 100-150 feet or so, through the mall. Right next door to the mall, sort of part of it actually, is the Kodak and Chinese Theaters. Ripleys, Guinness Book and both wax museums are within one block. The El Capitan Theater is right across the street. Any little shop you might want to visit is pretty much right there, as are many night clubs (within a couple blocks) and places to eat. It seems all of the bus tours start from Highland as well. So location is just awesome. We parked our car on Saturday afternoon and didn't need it till we left the next afternoon. As for the hotel itself, it appears that it was possibly an apartment building way back in the day, probably the 60's? And at some point it was converted into a hotel. So the rooms are pretty old, sure. But everything we saw was very clean and well kept. We're fairly picky with that stuff (though willing to take chances) but we had no complaints at all. The rooms are very good size, including bathroom and kitchen. It's plain style but "cute". The hotel is the same, neat little layout and felt comfortable. It was interesting to walk up to the roof to see the patio area. The pool area is small but seems nice. The parking garage is underneath the building and there are plenty of easy-to-get-into parking spaces. The garage and the hotel itself are locked, you have to use your key to enter. The staff is very friendly and helpful. I stayed here just with my wife but we're planning on taking the kids with us to sight-see and we're definitely staying here again.

title: “Best Hotel in NYC”
text:
Where do I start? The location is perfect for going up or downtown. Extremely quiet. Wonderful restaurants within walking distance. The hotel has very friendly and helpful staff. The breakfast in the morning in the lobby is the best start to the day. Followed by the evening reception with drinks and appetizers, assorted cheeses and vegetables, not just pretzels with a piano player. The rooms are large for NYC. The bathroom as well. 'Comfy' bed with nice linens. You do not have to bring your umbrella or bathrobe because they supply those for you.
I highly recommend staying at this hotel.

title: “very mixed feelings”
text:
I was unsure when I booked this hotel, I still am. We booked a corner king with balcony, we found it to be bleak to say the least, there is nothing in it, a bed, 2 chairs, coffee table, stool, lamp. There is no decoration, at all. For storage there was a wardrobe with hanging space and nothing else. No desk, no drawers, no shelves, no suitcase storage. In the bathroom, hardly any space round the sink, we were here for a week and could not stay here. We upgraded to a suite at a cost of $80 a night. This was better as there were two wardrobes one with shelves, the living area was a reasonable size, bathroom the same small size, bedroom so small there was barely room to walk round, at my side about 12 inches.
The views however are great, you do get a lot of flat roof, but from the suite, windows were North and west facing so we could see the Empire State building and Chrysler building, even from the loo! The views are what people go here for.
There were some really odd ideas though, There were no bedside lamps, no bedside tables, the bathroom cut the suite in half, tucked in a corner you could have had a magnificent space. There are floor to ceiling windows, but most are frosted, below the waist, so sitting down you can't see out! The curtains are so long that they have had to take a portion of the bedroom to hide the drawn curtain behind, about 8 inches along one wall. The yellow bathrooms are hideous, and the glass tiles in the shower floor get very slippy. There is no magnifying make-up mirror and no mirror at the desk to use as a dressing table. The wardrobes are in the small corridor between the bedroom and living area , they don't open flat, so to unpack I had to put the suitcase on the sofa and constantly open and shut the wardrobe doors to get back and forth, if I was trying anything on my husband had to stay put, he couldn't get past. The full length mirror was the most unflattering I have ever experienced.
Mini bar hideously expensive, the worst I've come across. Apparently all prices in bar and mini-bar have been recently increased. Two vodka and tonics at the bar $24, plus tax and tip. The restaurant dinner we had was standard American fare, nice, nothing special, it has changed recently it is Levant east not Thor now. Room service was fine except for a very overcooked bit of Salmon. Breakfast is very basic, but well worth getting up for, no OJ, just tea coffee, cereals, fruit and bread.
Nightclub is obviously not hip any more, we found it staid and we are in our forties, it was a deathly experience.
The area is good for bars and restaurants, but the streets are in a dreadful state in the area, not dangerous just broken and grubby, we much prefer, Greenwich. Soho, nolita and the west village.
I feel I've criticised too much, the views are great, staff are great, food is fine. beds very comfortable, linens and fabrics are lush. It just needs something more.

title: “A solid hotel”
text:
Great location, nice rooms, good service, I had no real complaints. 
Our party arrived early to check in, about 11am, but our two rooms were still not ready till 2pm, ahead of check in, but later than we would have perferred.
Also, their breakfast buffet is not your best option. We had it on the weekend with the expanded service (and price) to include an omlette station. The price is too high for what you get ($30 each I believe) and the food is rather bland. There are so many places to eat in Boston, go elsewhere.
On the other hand, Turner Fisheries was a delight! Excellent service and ambience, the food was wonderfully presented and tasty (although portions were rather small, seafood appitizers are not meant to be shared) and the price in line with other local restaurants. 
The hotel bar was also quite nice. It was very lively each night of our stay and althought we went elsewhere for our entertainment we found ourselves stopping in for a nightcap on our way back to our room due to the atmosphere.

title: “Enjoyed our stay”
text: The staff was friendly and very helpful. The room was clean and pleasant. The location was excellent, close to where we were going, restaurants were near enough. And the scenery of the nearby foothills was beautiful.

title: “Sloppy”
text:
As others have noted the lobby is spectacular. There are lots of elevators, so it's never a long wait to get to your floor. 
I reserved a newly upgraded room, and the first one I was sent to was barely vacuumed or cleaned, including the closet which had layers of dust in it. It was also relatively close to the ice machine which was pretty loud. I requested another room, which was better, however there was still hair from other guests on the bathroom floor and the carpet was pretty dusty. Disappointing for a hotel of this caliber. 
Suprising also for this level of hotel that there was no bottled water in the room, coffee, tea, kettle, or even a shower cap. 
As other reviewers mentioned, the little market downstairs while friendly is super-over priced, and you'd be better off going to GCS or other small cafes for light meals. 
The location can't be beat though.

title: “Extraordinary Lodging experience”
text: VERY good service. Great value. The neighborhood is primarily small businesses. The breakfast is Japanese and not to my tastes.

title: “Great location in San Francisco”
text: We stayed for 3 nights at the start of our Californian road trip. Great location 2 minutes from Union Square and a great base for exploring SF. Staff exceptionally courteous and friendly. Concierge helpful. Room large and very comfortable and clean.

title: “This place is a dump! Room smelled like vomit.”
text:
We stayed here on July 4th thru July 7th, 2008.
The room smelled like vomit - It was embedded into the carpet. The shower door was falling down. The A/C cycled on and off all night about every 15 minuites or so. One day when we came back from Sea World we did not have ANY towels, and the front desk did not have any to give me. The breakfast was terrible. But the Staff at the front desk were very friendly. Deffinately a $29 a night Hotel. I obviously payed way too much. But I know that I will never stay there again. I will sleep in my car first.

title: “Always my first choice”
text: Staff here is friendly, check in quick and rooms always very clean. Always helpful on good dining options in area. Shuttle drivers are some of the best I have ever experienced. All things an A plus for this hotel. Very convenient for car rental return and to airport. When in SA this will always be my first choice to stay.

title: “Our stay curtailed by Sandy”
text:
We were supposed to stay 3 nights, arriving by train from Connecticut. But Hurricane Sandy had other ideas and we finally made it, by car, for only one night before moving on to Charleston to get on trip back on schedule. So we didn't have time to fully investigate the hotel or DC. However in our all-too-brief stay we found the hotel staff enormously friendly and helpful, the room was massive, I'm sure I didn't book a suite but we could have held a party for 50! So we were very happy bunnies.
We got out to have a quick look at the monuments and something to eat before retiring for our early start next day. Slept well.
When we go back to DC, this is where we will stay!

title: “Great idea, but poorly executed”
text:
I really loved the look of the hotel and I loved that the room was just as I had hoped, albeit on the small side. It even smelled like the ocean. However, upon looking more closely, I don't feel that this is a four-star hotel. A solid three-star, yes. But it's not a four-star. When they remodeled the previous building, they didn't bother to remove the popcorn ceiling. There was no place to hang any towels in the bathroom, although it was quite spacious. And there was a pretty ugly-looking stain in the hallway outside my door. 
My experience was pleasant until I ordered room service. That's when it all went downhill. An hour after ordering, I called to ask about the order and the phone just rang and rang. Five minutes later, I called back only to be told the food was on its way. For my trouble, they offered to throw in a free drink. In my case, this was a bottle of water. Oddly, the food arrived in a brown paper bag with no silverware to be seen. I then realized that the food was not what I had ordered and had to call back twice more to correct the order. My food finally arrived. Cold. And without a bottle opener, I was unable to open the water that they sent me, one of which I paid for. I'm not a complainer by nature, but I was feeling pretty irritated.
Perhaps they just had an off-night, perhaps not. But their room service needs an overhaul if they expect to ever reach four-star status. That and they need to pay more attention to the details, including the common area women's bathroom. Pretty unimpressive given the way the rest of the hotel looks.
Overall, I'd say there are better places to stay in the area for the money. I really wanted to love it, but the reality fell short of the executed concept.

title: “Get's it right”
text:
I read the reviews saying how great the service was and I was a bit skeptical. However, I was very impressed by the level of service and the attitude of all who worked at the hotel.
The only place that could use improving is the Amaya restaurant. We didn't dine at Addison, the highly acclaimed gastronomic restaurant at the hotel (because we were with the kids) but I think that the menu at Amaya should be different. It is attempting to be more gastronomic than it truly was. I think a different type of menu would be a good contrast to having the highly rated Addison and the chef isn't up to the menu presented.
Also, the management of the restaurant was a bit off. We were kept waiting for 30 minutes for our reservation one night, yet there were many empty tables. Also, the large banquettes inside are horrible, awkward shapes for conversation with spotlights beaming down. The only people I would imagine enjoying these are the middle aged men with their 20 something mall chick girlfriends who were seated in two of them one night we were there. I guess they like to show off their...um..."catch" or that they can still "catch" something?
Anyway, I didn't like Amaya but I loved everything else at the hotel. The pool area, the room the service from the pool to the concierge to the front desk...it was all fantastic. And the kids gave very high reviews to the Explorers Club.
If they just tweaked Amaya a bit the hotel would be perfect....

title: “The motel 6 of Westin Chain”
text:
Stayed here 2 nights because of proximity to my client at Park Central and LBJ. Can't go wrong with Starwood property right? WRONG. Front desk clerk was knowledgable and efficient, not bad. The room was a nice size and well appointed. The tub was the same one found at motel 6 (small and cramped) nothing to write home about and flooded the floor, as for the plumbing, its noisy and poorly designed. While I showered it ran hot and cold unexpectedly. The room was dirty with stains on the furniture and sheets and sand or sugar on the desk chair. I didn't taste it. I had the sheets changed. The wireless phone near the bed was not working. The elevators were so outrageously slow, I opted for the freight elevator and complained about this to the front desk and security personnel I met in the kitchen. 
To sum up, find another hotel. I got it thru priceline at a greatly reduced price, I would not pay what they ask on the name brand sites, and won't go back well maybe for a 50$/day rack rate I would.

title: “Very pleasant hotel in a fantastic location”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel while traveling to Chicago for pleasure. The hotel is well located directly off of the Magnificent Mile. It is a bit of a walk from the blue line stop (if flying into O'Hare), but not too bad. The hotel was nice, and we were received excellent service.

title: “Basic digs a bit above”
text:
This hotel works if you are coming in late and headed out to the airport early. Good value $99 rooms are worth it for a few hours. But if you are used to a higher quality boutique hotel, this place will disappoint for a longer vacation stay. I am 40 and see this more as a 20 something hotel. The hotel is on a VERY busy road and not really walkable to anywhere you may want to go. They have good marketing, it worked on us, but it is not the type of place I would stay at normally, except for the airport reason I listed above.
This hotel is nicely decorated, new interiors, and clean. The walls seem thin, there is no in-room safe, pool area is teeny, bed is cheap, hardscape echoes outside the door. I didn't really find the staff overly friendly, but they were fine.
Assess your wants and needs before booking.

title: “Great Hotel Location”
text:
We stayed there for a week, during the summer July 1st to 8th. 
The hotel is located within walking distance to most major NY important attractions. 
Rooms very clean and the staff is always ready to help you in your needs.

title: “Fantastic Place with Phenominal Service”
text: This was a fantastic hotel. THe valets, counter staff, housekeepers, (well, everone!) was friendly, helpful and spent as much time talking to you as you wanted. All the extra touches (like when you get your car from the valet, they put chilled water bottles in the cup holders) really make the stay enjoyable. The fitness center is great and the spa prices are reasonable for a tourist area. Pike Place Market is a bit of an uphill walk but not too far. The food and shops around Pioneer Square are really close. Definately recommend the 1000!

title: “I loved it!”
text: This was my first stay at the Plaza and it met every one of my expectations. I booked the Rose Deluxe Suite and could not have been any more pleased. The suite, including the bathroom, was beautiful, plush and so comfortable. Every person from the bellman, front desk, bar staff and housekeeping was absolutely kind and attentive. I cannot wait to return and am sure that I will only stay the Plaza from this point on. It is well worth it the pay the money to get such a beautiful room and prime location. I will also try the Food Hall on the bottom floor of the hotel, due to time I wasn't able to try any of the food but it looks wonderful!

title: “Business Travel Gem”
text:
I was in town for a conference earlier this week and was impressed with the friendliness of all staff that I encountered. The were helpful and wiling to fond solutions for my colleague's challenging allergies throughout the conference. The conference meals (there were 7 in total) were all creative and for the most part had a wide selection of healthy choices--which is rare!
When i wanted to explore a bit, the hotel arranged my car rental pick up and drop off and I was offered to option for forgo housekeeping in return for 500 Starwood points per day which I was happy to take. The only suggestion is to offer free internet to Starwood members as a standard of business. Its very frustrating to have to pay 14.95 per day while attending a business conference at the hotel.

title: “Great hotel in convenient location”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights during October, it was a treat for my 40th birthday and I was so excited about my first visit to NY that I hoped the hotel wouldnt be a let down...and it wasnt.
Check-in was a good experience, having just stepped off a long flight and not much sleep the night before. We were given a nice room but it the window faced into an iternal lightwell, so we asked for a change (I wanted to see out onto a real NY streetscape!) and they obliged with no fuss at all. It did mean that we had to take a room on a lower floor, but the sound proofing was great so this was not a problem during the stay.
We really liked the room decor, it had all the modern facilities with iphone docks etc in the rooms and large comfy bed (they even had an 'adult pack' at the mini bar, between the nuts!). The bathroom only had a shower, but it was large and glass walled into the room so I guess the novelty value made up for lack of soaking facility - not we would have had time to have a soak anyway! The bathroom products (Kiehl) were really nice too, it was all top quality stuff.
There is a bar and french themed restaurant attached at the ground floor (cannot remember name) but you can grab breakfast, coffees etc in the morning - and in the evening the restaurant is very busy. We ate there one night and the food and service was great. They also have a bar/nighclub in the basement which we stumbled across when we decided to see where all the 'beautiful people' were heading from the bar - I thought it was the way to the toilets but no one was coming back out so I went to have a look. It was a great find as we wanted to stay up and have drinks, but could not be bothered venturing around NY late at night trying to find somewhere to out liking. At least here we could just leave if we didnt like it, and be in bed 5 minutes later. The music was a bit old skool, and they had booth areas. The only criticism was we sat in a booth and someone came to tell us it was reserved - I said we would leave when the party turned up but they never did. It seems that they try to keep certain areas for people who buy bottle of champagne, which we had no intention of doing! There were also some quite annoying 'trendies' floating around, but I guess you get that everywhere.
The location was good for us, as we wanted to see the Meatpacking district and Greenwich Village as well as the more well known tourist areas. It was literally 2 blocks from Ground Zero, and there is a subway station almost immediately outside the front door so it was easy to get everywhere else.
Highlights of the trip would include Sunday brunch at the River Cafe (Brooklyn Bridge), helicopter trip up the Hudson, breakfast at Pastis in Gansevoort (on corner of 9th Avenue / Little W 12th Street) - I'm sure all my other highlights are already covered in spades by other reviewers!

title: “Excellent”
text: Stayed in the Brown Palace for a weekend. Staff very friendly. Rooms very nice, its decorated in an old fashioned way, which was a nice change from all the new modern hotels. Dinner on our first night in the Ship tavern was excellent and great service. The Sunday Brunch is not too be missed - it was amazing. An unbelievable choice of food! Will defo be back.

title: “Don't Stay Here”
text: I planned to stay here out of desparation, as my original plans changed. I had no luck getting lodging nearby for the night and had a reservation here the following night. I decided to try this place. At 9:30 am, I was told I could check in now if I liked. My baggage was at the hotel I had stayed the night before. I was charged up front for two nights before even going to the room! I headed back to where I stayed the night before and checked on one more place (a nice major chain) they had a room for only $30 more. I returned to this place and told my change of plans. I was told I would not get a refund for the night as I had already checked in and it had been more than 30 mins. My reasons were: very small room, very outdated and worn furnishings, overwhelming smell of cleaning solution and portable space heaters! They would not listen and insisted I had checked in (I guess according to there computers). The offered me another room. When I went to that one, there was plaster chipping and falling off the wall at baseboard level. I decided it was not in my best interest to stay and they refunded the next night, which was $20 chaeper than the current night. The time lapsed from my charge and credit was 37mins/40 secs. I most likely spent 7 mins or so trying to get a refund and checking out the other disgusting room. The condition of this place should warrant $50 rooms. There are numerous affordable (some even cheaper)rooms nearby but they were not available. I guess this would explain why there were so many "Ready" rooms at 9:30 on a Saturday morning. Never pay up front and price is not everything!

title: “A good place to stay”
text:
I stayed here as a chaperone with a small group of high school students who were in Dallas for a conference. The front desk (especially Joseph B. who helped us organize a complicated trip) was patient and helpful and not at all irritated with our (well-behaved) teens. Every time I asked for advice I was helped politely. 
The staff had good knowledge the surrounding restaurants. There is a great breakfast spot near the infamous grassy knoll (Cindi's, I think). We also enjoyed a sushi place near the aquarium. For better or worse, we ate at Chipotle a lot. The best restaurant by far was Sushi Ya, an independent restaurant within walking distance of the hotel- it was amazing. The West End is sketchy (but still has many great restaurants) and towards Main it has a more uptown feel. 
The room is clean and decent. The dressers could use some updating but overall, it was totally fine (but not posh.) I had a great view and enjoyed sitting by the pool. On the weekends, the hotel bar/nightclub is very popular.
I would stay here again.

title: “Best NYC Stay Ever!”
text:
Great location, great service, exceptional room, fantastic value for dollar ... we are definitely going back ... 
M.

title: “Best Hotel for the price I paid”
text: We had stayed in this hotel to attend a convention at Denver Convention Center. Hotel is located in a convenient place, very close to two highways I-25 and I-70. We are 100% satisfied with great customer service, cleanliness of the hotel/room, free hot breakfast and complementary shuttle service. We did not have to spend a single penny to attend our convention everyday, since curtsey shuttle dropped us off and picked us up within a very reasonable waiting time. Hot buffet Breakfast was awesome, beyond my expectation. Breakfast includes Biscuit with gravy, Ham, Scramble eggs, muffins, freshly cut fruits, waffles with syrup, fruit juices, cereals, milk, breads and more. Onsite Restaurant does not have lot of choices, opens until 9:30 PM, but Village Inn Restaurant (opens for breakfast through late night dinner) is just adjacent to hotel. Downtown Denver (has 100s of restaurants) is just 10 minutes away from the hotel, free shuttle dropped and picked us up anytime before 10 PM whenever we need. Can’t expect more than this for the price we paid. I will definitely come back and recommend to everyone.

title: “Better than average with some quircks”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for several nights. It is in a borderline area of San Francisco (Union Square on Gear Street). Union Square can be seedy and there is a fair number of "street culture" in the immediate area. To be fair, most of the hotels in the area share a similar ambiance given the area's proximity to the sketchy "tenderloin" area.
This hotel is trying very hard to be hip and pet friendly. If you have a pet, thats great. If you dont care for dogs, you may have an issue with this place. Dogs are privileged guests here. Several are on duty at the front desk area. Its cute but again if you dont want to be around canines, suggest you look else where.
The rooms are comfortable, but can be noisy if they face Geary or the side street. No views to speak of at this hotel. The evening wine hour is a nice perk if your around but I missed it most nights of my stay because it ended around six. 
Check out was not great as the computers were down. The gym was a good cardio set up, also a small spa facility was a plus.
Overall, a cute hotel if your in the mood.

title: “Feel like home while away”
text:
I was attending a week long class in the area with my business associate, Jason. The hotel is comfortable and clean. The complementary Monday-Thursday breakfast, dinner and wine/beer is wonderful. It was relaxing after a day of class! Note some nights we did head out to local restaurants which are very close to the hotel. There are lots of good choices.
The staff (Katie, Anat, Junior, and Julia) made our stay great. They made sure our needs were met ... getting dropped off at our class, recommendations for / rides to restaurants, and just chatting. Also, the ladies who run the breakfast/dinner area are friendly and serve up some tasty food.
If you have the chance, stay here! You will not be disappointed.

title: “Okay Hotel”
text:
The hotel is so-so. I recently stayed there because I was going to a conference.
The room was fine- clean but nothing special.
Every night I heard garbage trucks going by- and I was on the 18th floor (although it is New York)
The room service was fine and the location is great.
Right neear 7th avenue shopping, Times Square....
The only major problem is that that high speed internet service did not always work. When I called the front desk they told me that too many guests were trying to use it.
I would not stay there if I was travelling for leisure.

title: “Great hotel, great bed, big rooms!”
text:
I want to start off by saying that we got our room for $105/night on priceline, so I would try booking there if you can. That is an awesome deal for this hotel.
I really enjoyed the Westin. The rooms were huge, especially by city standards. There was a big king bed (and the beds are so comfy with tons of pillows...), a big desk, flat screen TV, cool single serving coffee maker with Starbucks coffee and cups. Great bathroom with a pretty big tub.
Good location. We walked to all the historic sites and it generally took about 20 minutes. The hotel is connected to the Liberty Place Mall, which was actually nice. We used the mall as a shortcut, or to grab a quick drink. 
There is a great restaurant about 2 or 3 blocks away (on Chestnut towards the historic sites and across from Olive Garden). You can sit outside and the food is great. I did notice, though, in the area right around the hotel, we got asked for money everyday, several times a day. Even twice while we seated outside at a restaurant. It really didn't bother us and we never felt threatened. It was just annoying.
I HIGHLY encourage going to the Tut exhibit, it is so amazing. The Liberty Bell building was near empty on Monday afternoon, but had a 2 hour wait on Saturday. And the Betsey Ross house is really cool. I was very disappointed with the Ghost Tour, however.
Overall, I totally recommend the Westin. It had a good atmosphere, helpful staff, and you had to use your room key to access the elevator which I liked for safety. The ONLY bad thing I can say about it is the housekeeping was TERRIBLE! There was actually a dirty glass left there when we checked in. They never replaced the glasses, or the ice bucket bag, and never even emptied the trash! I even left money for a tip! Finally I left more money and a note. Only then did they leave new glasses but still didn't empty the trash. Other than that, I really liked it and will return, I recommend it highly.

title: “A couple of problems but worth staying at.”
text:
I really like this hotel. I have visited it twice and would strobgly recomend it.
The location is the best, 20 second walk to times square which is brilliant for things like eating the cinema Virgin Mega store and of course most of teh theatre's. Not to mention a great Toys R Us.
The first time I stayed was better than the second. Room 2107. Amazing view and nice room. The second time i was on the 42 floor and felt slightly out of it and the room was not quite as nice as teh other one. Also sadly the check in service was appauling the second time. Ruined the first day the girl was so rude. We complained and they gave a free meal in there fairly expensive hotel. I also complained when I got home as even though the meal was nice we felt upset about teh check in as she was really really rude. Anyway next time we go back they are upgrading us to a suite!
I would still really recomend this hotel though but do advise if you have any problems with the hotel to ask to talk to the manager straight away.

title: “You are better off sleeping in your car”
text: We spent 4 nights in the Seattle area and since we were flying out early in the morning, we thought we'd save money and stay at Motel 6 Seattle Airport. This was the biggest mistake we made. Our room was a health hazzard. There were blood stains in the bathroom and we found a drug syringe in the roll of the toilet paper. I complained to the hotel manager and she didn't even apologize. You're better off sleeping in your car.

title: “The overall best experience I have ever had”
text: I have already started recommending this hotel to everyone I know. Not only is the hotel beautiful and warm, the staff is amazing. Everyone is very friendly and made me feel very welcome. My room was gorgeous and very clean, the food at the restaurant was wonderful. The hotel is a walk away from Georgetown which i loved. I enjoyed every second of my stay. I can's wait to return

title: “Wonderful Stay at Hyatt”
text: Just stayed at this great property. The hotel has gone through a $30 million renovation & looks updated, modern, & fresh. Beautiful public spaces to enjoy as well. Pool area was lovely, & spacious. Get a room facing the ocean & pool...lovely to see West Hollywood & the Santa Monica mountains as well. The rooms are large for a city hotel & with the terrace it feels even larger. The rooms are clean and very well decorated. The staff was incredibly nice. Very prompt service, and personalized as well. They always try to use your name, which makes this large chain hotel a little more personal. The concierge arranged our tours & restaurant reservations with a keen idea of our needs.......a family "LA" experience & made excellent recommendations for us. Especially enjoyed the tour they recommended from the hotel. Nice not to have to drive into Hollywood to get it & it's a small co. that offers a very knowledgable tour. Originally had hoped to stay in Santa Monica, but after this experience would definately return here again. The location was superb-centrally located to everything. Less driving as a result. Also nice outdoor mall across the street which had a nice food court. A great option when you just don't want to get in the car or eat at the hotel, although we did enjoy the restaurant here too. Going to LA with children, I would highly recommend this location & the hotel. It was fantastic!

title: “i love hotel!”
text:
hotel has very great service. i will stay here every time i come to Los Angeles. employees are are very nice and helpful. Especially Estera Estrede. she took very well care of us. Theres many hotels in this area but the The Sheraton gate way by lax is my 1st choice. 
 Thanks Again to Estera Estrede she was the BEST!!!

title: “Don't waste your time or money $$”
text: I often wondered about the mind of a person who writes reviews, and now I know....it's out of frustration & disappointment most times, this no different....The Dylan is a total waste of time and good luck getting the "night manager's" sympathy if your room is an oven....in fact, he'll even lead you to believe an engineer is on the way.....and when he doesn't show up and you call him on it...the fact that I'd been waiting for an hour and a 1/2 on an engineer cuz he said he would be sending someone up "right away"..when I phoned & he said they've been working on the system for days and when I asked if the thought it profession to lead me to believe someone was on their way and weren't he said "YES"....he clearly needs educated in customer service..my advise is to head to the Helmsley just one street over, it's FABULOUS and where I headed after 2 nights at this dreadful, overrated, EXTREMELY SMALL hotel

title: “Wonderful home away from home”
text: We stayed here for ten days in November with two teenagers. We especially loved the breakfast AND kitchen options. The kids LOVED the free Internet! Hotel staff was wonderful and went out of their way to be helpful AND friendly. We found it a great location too, quiet and convenient to everything. Lovely experience.

title: “WOW!”
text:
I travel to San Antonio frequently and stay at the Riverwalk I was very upset when I found out that my company had booked their event at the Doubletree by the airport 
I was very surprise when I arrived and saw the beautiftul hacienda but even more with the friendly and caring staff, the banquet facility was and food was great ALL around GREAT all I can say is WOW and Im NOT going back to the riverwalk wait until you try their beds and have a warm cookie waiting for you

title: “Fabulous time!”
text: I went for the Final Four Women's College Basketball Finals. I stayed for 6 nights. The room service meals were excellent as were the meals at the Ship Tavern and Ellyngton's. Don Stevens, Waiter, in the ShipTavern was spot on for being nice and good. Elaine Schulte - Housekeeping kept my room perfect and met my every need. The evening Housekeeper was also very nice. It was nice to be down town for the events and the Hotel was the guest hotel for the Standford Women's Team. I also enjoyed seeing the Colorado Capitol Building that my Grandfather Jake Bramwell was a child teamster that helped bring in the granite blocks to build it.

title: “Good price for good location”
text: Nice location. Walking distance to outdoor mall (10 min) and even to rodeo dr (if u don't mind a 20 minute walk). Across the agree from a grocery store. Hotel seems to be renovated and modern. Very friendly staff. Can get private car to airport for $45.

title: “Great hotel and great location”
text: We have stayed here twice on New Year's Eve and were very pleased both times. The hotel still feels new and is always very clean. The staff is very friendly and helpful. This year they upgraded us to a junior suite and we even had a view of the fireworks at Victory Park. Fearing's is wonderful for brunch.

title: “Excellent A+++”
text: My mom and I booked the Grand Hyatt because it was centrally located in Union Square. We had awesome help from the conceige before we arrived (transportation to/from SFO, around the city, etc) Check-in was a breeze once we got there. Our room over looked Union Square on the 31st floor. We caught the Culture Bus to California Academy of Sciences (GG Park) a block away and were dropped off even closer to the Grand Hyatt. I would recommend to anyone that wants a hotel in easy access to everything. Cable cars were a block away on Powell (didn't ride them in this trip, but I love them). The view from the Grandviews lounge on the 36th floor is to die for (We caught it on an afternoon where it had rained the night before and you could see the Bridges (GG and Bay), Alactraz, and Transamerica building)

title: “Was probably a "jewel" in it's day...”
text:
First, the pros: This "resort" has great meeting space which I think is why it is still in existence. The staff members were friendly. They have porters that will take you and your luggage to your room in a little golf cart. It is convienently located next to the MTS trolley system and Fashion Valley Mall where you can get reasonably priced food. The fitness center has 3 new treadmills and 2 clunkers that still work though. They also have a rack of free weights, ellipticals and exercise equipment for strength training.
The cons: The rooms and property need serious updating. Perhaps they should use the money they charge you for internet use ($9.95 a day) or the $5 I paid for ONE EGG at the Terrace Cafe to go towards renovations. I stayed here to attend a conference so it was convienent for me to be on site, however I would not stay here if I was vacationing and spending my own money.
I read the trip advisor reviews prior to going so I was not disappointed in what I saw...I knew what to expect. The blue carpet in my room and the hallways needs replacing. They charge you $5 a day to use the fitness center. 
Bottom line, stay here if you are attending a conference, otherwise don't waste your $150 plus a night.

title: “Great hotel at great price !!!”
text:
We stayed at the Old Town Inn for a week in June. It is an excellent hotel.
Great location :
- Walking distance from Old Town (Good restaurants and shops)
- Close to all main attractions (SeaWorld, Zoo, Beaches, ...) and downtown San Diego.
- Even if the hotel is near the highway, we did not hear a noise.
Great price and service : 
- Around 100 $ (AAA price) for a large room with 2 queen beds (wich are very very comfortable) and a kitchnette.
- Good breakfast included (waffles, bagels, cereals, ...)
- The service was excellent and very friendly.
If the Old Town Inn would just upgrade their amenities like the soap bars and shampoo and add some shower caps, it would be comparable to a Hampton Inn wich is more expensive.
We had an excellent stay and would definitively stay there again.

title: “Finally an American hotel with top Asian service”
text:
As a regular business traveller to Asia and sometimes Europe, I am always telling my friends how I am so spoiled by the great hotels of Asia and how American hotels, even the top ones really ----.
Well I now stand corrected. My wife was having a "milestone" birthday and I decided to take her to NYC for a surprise weekend. After reviewing many hotels and using tripadvisor I decided to spend a little more and stay at Trump International. For the money I was paying I could of stayed at a suite at the Peninsula in HK or my favorite hotel Raffles in Singapore, so I was not too excited to spend that kind of money for a NY hotel.
I was very surprised upon arriving that this hotel had a very understated and small lobby which I liked. I was greeted at the door by the doorman then by the front desk staff, who were excellent. We were informed that we were early for check in but that our room should be ready in an hour and suggested we go and relax in the spa or take a short walk for breakfast. Upon check in we were upgraded to a corner suite! The room was GREAT. Two bathrooms a kitchen, bedroom and a living room dining room with views of Columbus circle and the park. My only complaint was the size of the bathroom in the bedroom. A bit small.
Overall the room was great! I did not want to leave the hotel. In fact one day (Sunday) I had guest over for breakfast (the room had a small dining room) and we just hung out looking at the great views and watching some sports on the nice flat screen TV while my wife and friends shopped on 5th avenue ( a short 2 or 3 blocks away).
During my stay I had a Fed Ex delivery and I can say that everytime I needed anything from the staff they were excellent and very polite. In fact after checking in, the first time we left the building the doorman said goodbye to us and called us by our name. It really felt as we lived in the building.
I will never stay at another hotel in NYC other than this hotel. This is really a first class hotel with world class service and GREAT views!
Good job Donald!

title: “Great location, cool hotel”
text: We stayed in the Buff Monster room which amusingly is porn inspired (?) and had a shared bathroom, which was basic but fine. Breakfast was bagels and fruit we could take back to the room. Great location just opposite the china gate and made a great base for a stop over in San Fran.

title: “Hidden GEM! Amazing Location!”
text:
There are hundreds of places to stay in chicago, we got an excellent rate online and I didnt think it would be to bad. The place is right off of michigan avenue. Its within walking distance of everything great that chicago has to offer.
If you drive a car, thats ok its close to a great parking garage too.
I didnt know what to expect but its so close to all the shopping and sights.
The room i had was a little small, the bathroom was tiny but most importantly...very clean. We rested very well.

title: “Great Location”
text:
Great Location and Great Place. You are in a walking distance from the main places in the River Walk and only about 20 minutes away from Fiesta Texas and a bit longer for Sea World. The rooms are well kept and good size. If you are traveling with kids you can send them to the living room to watch tv or play nintendo while you relax in a seperate room. 
The pool is small but little kids don't mind much. 
The only complaint I would have is the valet parking. $20/day and they do take anywhere from 30-40 minutes to get your car in the morning when people are either checking out or need their vehicles for anything else.

title: “Several pleasant stays”
text: I've stayed here several times, each time quite pleased. This is a bustling, fairly noisy hotel that caters to people doing business on Capitol Hill, various meetings, and families on vacation. I've always found the staff to be friendly and helpful. While some reviewers have noted run-down rooms, I've always stayed in nice rooms, modern with flat screen TVs. The gift shop is large and well stocked, and the fitness center is spacious and well-equipped, surrounded a somewhat small indoor pool. The restaurants and bars are overpriced, but there are alternatives around the hotel. The immediate surrounding are a mixed bag, with some other upscale hotels, offices, but also some rundown streets. The hotel is just a couple of blocks from Union Station, and the US Capitol. Overall this a perfectly reasonable base for either business or sightseeing in DC. If you get a room you don't like, just go down to the front desk and ask for a better one.

title: “Certainly a DREAM!”
text:
I travel to New York all the time for business, this trip was more of a hybrid mixture of business and pleasure. I came across the Dream Downtown and decided to try it out, the second I stepped out of my cab I was greeted by the doorman who instantly offered to to assist with my bags. The lobby area is certainly breathtaking, as I approached the reception area the gentlemen behind the desk Daniel greeted me by name very nice touch! I arrived around 5pm and my room wasn't ready he quickly apologized for the inconvenience and assured me the room would be ready in the next few minutes, he offered me a complimentary drink at the lobby bar while I waited which was also an amazing display of customer service. I waited in the garden area near the lobby within minutes the gentlemen approached me with my keys and directed me to my elevator bank. The entire stay was very pleasant the beds are amazingly soft and comfy the staff goes above and beyond for your every need I have already recommended this place to a few friends and I plan on being back within the upcoming months. 
Also, if you eat at the steakhouse in the lobby try the sliders they're to die for also ask for a room in the south tower if you want a little more peace. The club upstairs is the place to be in New York, I encourage you to let the doorman know you are a hotel guest it seems to make it slightly easier to get it.

title: “Great value...”
text:
After reading many of the less-than-favorable reviews on this hotel, I was quite apprehensive. I must admit, I was pleasantly surprised once I got there. Don't get me wrong, the hotel was older with several dated features, but for me, the location was well worth it; my boyfriend and I either took the Circulator bus or walked to many of the sites we wanted to see.
If you're looking for a "posh" hotel to stay at while in DC, this may not be the place for you. If you're looking for a decent place with friendly staff, a clean room, which is conveniently located... give this place a try!

title: “Ordinary aging business hotel”
text:
I've stayed at lot's of Crown Plaza's around the world and I must say that this one is feeling tired. It definitely needs a refresh. 
It's a standard US business hotel but my bathroom was tiny. Also for the price that you pay you would at least think that you would get some quality goodies in your room. 
It's well located and it has great service.
In addition to the oldish feeling of the hotel, the restaurant that is attached to it (Elephant and Castle Pub and Restaurant) is awful. I had the worst food there during my stay in Philadelphia. Fortunately there are lot's of great restaurants in the neighborhood.

title: “Mildew smell, sticky blob, and valet parking frustration”
text: Room smelled strongly of mildew. Carpet in room and hallway stained and filthy. Why hotels in hot humid climates insist on carpets is beyond my comprehension. Found a sticky black ball of something under the entertainment center as I searched for a dropped vitamin. Valet phone extension was busy at checkout. Arriving downstairs, after handing my claim check to the desk clerk, she told me my car had been called. Waited outside with my luggage in the heat almost 10 minutes before I was told that I had to check in at the parking desk before my car would be brought down. Maybe for a charge of $32/night the valet manager could communicate with the front desk about the hotel policy, so that the guests might know what to expect? Loved the hotel years ago before it was owned by Omni. Will not return.

title: “a week in dallas”
text: Overpriced and No bathtub was available. Other than that the overall experience was pleasurable with good food and a staff that was very pleasant and helpful.

title: “Romantic Escape package AWESOME!”
text: We stayed at the Omni for a Bills-Jags Football game. It was right downtown, across from the Jacksonville Landing. Eating establishments like Hooters,Mexican and Steak Houses with live entertainment in the "Square". Located within steps of the water it made for a great night and fun atmosphere. The package we had included a long stemmed rose, chocolate covered strawberries, chilled champagne, a gourmet dinner for two ($75 value) at Juliettes, their OUTSTANDING restaurant inside the Hotel, along with Buffett Breakfast for two to boot. As a select guest, we received turndown service, USA TODAY & mints too. They even upgraded us to a corner suite, that was the best view in the hotel, overlooking the water..WOW. Room was nice, TV was a little small for my liking and some of Guest Services people gave us wrong directions to a few places..beware. But, overall the food was incredible and the overall experience great. I recommend it if you use the package it cost us only $190 for everything and was well worth it!

title: “London Hotel NYC - Excellent”
text: Stayed here for business Feb 2012 - excellent hotel and services (particularly the fitness centre) (although room service is a bit pricey). Rooms are nicer and much better value than the nearby Hilton or the Marriot Grand where I have previously recently stayed in NYC. I also booked through WhatAHotel website which worked very well and included breakfast, room upgrade and internet for the same price as a booking without those perks on the hotels own website. Recommend both the hotel and the WhatAHotel website to book it.

title: “Top notch Marriott”
text: This hotel was awesome. Marriott's can be hit and miss, but this one was top notch. The front desk staff was very helpful, though I did have problems with nobody picking up the phone when calling down from my room. The front desk had a bunch of rad candy to steal, so our stay was Pixy Stix'ed up. I got lucky, too, because I was able to book this hotel for around $100 on priceline.com. Only complaint was the $30/night for valet when I figured out after that I could have parked in the same lot they used for $16/24 hours. Oh well.

title: “Small but excellent value and location.........”
text:
I was a bit concerned at shared facilities as I have never done that. Booked a sinlge room which was small but clean. The bathrooms were plenty and clean all the time so no need to worry. The lift stops at recption on the way up which is a good secuirty measure. Fantastic location in Bryant Park area around the corner from Times Square.
If you want to have somewhere to put your head down for a few hours , drop the shopping off and live out the ride that is NYC then this is the place.
For the location and price I would stay again in an instant.
Many thanks
Perry - London - England.

title: “A Good Deal”
text:
I was satisified with this Ramada Inn. Some of the negative items are true, like the curtain wall reduces fresh air circulation. I bet this is appreciated in the winter. In the summer I found it only mildly offensive.
It's true the T shuttle can fill up, but timing ones activities could eliminate that problem. For instance, I didn't have a problem if I stayed in the city until 7 PM.
They charge for local calls, but will cut internet access by half. There is several restaurants and shops near, do be careful crossing the streets. The pool has a life guard.

title: “Obsessed with Inn at St Botolph”
text: I stayed at this hotel for one night with my dad while visiting colleges in Boston. I don't know which was more enjoyable: seeing colleges that I loved or staying at this hotel? The hotel was absolutely fantastic-- it was super clean, designed with excellent taste, had great appliances, and had a great view. We have to go back to Boston this June and I know that I will definitely be staying at this hotel, perhaps even for a longer period of time!

title: “Amazing”
text:
The breakfast is the most amazing buffet i have ever seen it has every food you could want.
A very good Hotel
Location is the best you can walk into times square!

title: “Great price, central location, awesome staff, comfy beds!”
text:
When I initially booked this hotel thru priceline I didnt expect anything spectacular espcially considering the price I paid (below $140 including taxes) BOY what a shock I received!
Took the bus from DC and the bus stopped right across the street from the hotel (31st Street and 7th avenue) - 1 block away from Madison Square Garden. The outside of the hotel was a bell man and baggage handler which I found to be great. The front desk was extremely busy but you could see they took their time with each check in to ensure each guest had everything they needed and all questions were answered.
We checked into room 1013 which is right off the elevator but still far enough removed from the noise. I walked in to a HUGE living room which had a table for 2 with a hanging light on the right, a nice size couch in the middle of the room with a large leather foot rest & TV. On the right, there was a kitchen with full range stove w/ pots & pans, microwave and fridge. There was also a breakfast bar but no stools.
Off to the left there was a desk with chair, large coat closet and full bathroom. Beyond that is the private bedroom with a queen size bed and twin bed, TV, dresser, large walk in closet, double mirrored sliding glass door closet and another full bathroom.
The beds were extremely comfy and the hotel room was very quiet. Centrally located near Penn Station, MSG, Macys, short walk to Times Square and near the 1, 9, 2, 3, A, B & C trains. Overall I have no real complaints other then suggesting they maybe replace the living room couch (it was a little tattered). I'd definitely stay here again but I cannot say I'd stay here for the rack room rate @ that time ($400).

title: “Nicely updated boutique hotel”
text: It had been several years since I had stayed here and I was pleased with the remodel and updates. The room was completely refurbished with new comfortable amenities. The shower was very nice. I love the quiet location just off the Mag Mile. Very convenient to everything. Front end service was fast and efficient.

title: “All around great”
text: I was a bit concerned about staying here after reading some other reviews. I honestly have no idea what they were talking about. Parking was no problem, the hotel looked great and the room was luxurious and clean. We stayed here simply because of the location to the HP Pavilion to see a Senators vs Sharks game. Lots of fans here...it's worth it. A pre-game snack is served in the lobby and you are literally steps from the arena. People walk further from where they park for the game. Continental breakfast was very impressive. Great selection of coffee/juices and most hot and cold breakfast foods.

title: “WOULD STAY AGAIN - IN A HEARTBEAT!”
text: This hotel was fabulous. Perhaps the best staff I've ever encountered at a hotel. Extraordinarily well-trained. The room was fabulous. The location perfect unless you want to be in the middle of the shopping (it's still close to it). It would be the first choice for us next time in Seattle!

title: “More than a Fair..mont”
text: I just returned from a conference at the Fairmont. I stayed in a queen room in the main building. The room was lovely and clean. The bathroom was huge with a bathtub and separate shower. It looked as though the room had recently undergone an update. I had breakfast room service twice, and I was very happy with the service and food. I would most certainly stay here again.

title: “Excellent Service!!!!”
text: The main point, EXCELLENT SERVICE!. Every level of employee is friendly, greets you, offers to help and has common courtesy, lacking in many of today's hotels and restuarants. Beautiful grounds and pools. Rooms were clean. We needed extra towels and a mini fridge, arrived within minutes to the room! Needed a corkscrew, arrrived in 5 minutes! The hotel is greared towards the conference industry but families and couples can also find their niche. JW brand still stands for excellence and it shows.

title: “Great Hotel for its Location and Price”
text:
After reading mixed reviews on tripadviser, i was really concerned about staying at this hotel. I'm pleased to say that it was pointless, staff at checkin were great, friendly and informative. We had a couple of night of being awoken by a rowdy group of teens, hotel were great in there dealing with this matter, we were offered a free breakfast and given and offered a change of room.
Room we stayed in was clean and in relatively good condition and was fine for what we needed ant that was somewhere to sleep.
We had a problem with the heating called the front desk, a handyman came to the room in minutes and sorted everything out.
If your in two minds about staying at this hotel go ahead and book you won't be disappointed and i will definately be visiting again.

title: “Love it!”
text: This was my 3rd time staying here. Each time gets better. The location is great, service is great and now that all the rooms have been renovated, they are wonderful. Plus, the beds are wonderful! I absolutely love this hotel and hopefully will have a 4th visit.

title: “Wonderful Stay!”
text: I don't understand why this hotel has such bad reviews. You get what you're paying for! The service is great, seems to be family run. Yes, the bathrooms are shared but the facilities are quite clean. The rooms have a fridge, microwave and comfortable bedding and television. The location is great surrounded by many excellent restaurants, galleries and shopping opportunities and many modes of transportation avialable around the area. Great place to stay if you're travelling on a budget, with friends, or just looking for an adventure!

title: “Trellises Grill fantastic for client events”
text: We had a client breakfast event on 20 February that was fantastic at the Trellises Restaurant. Pati Muklevicz, Emilio and Jesus provided fantastic service and made sure we had everything we needed for a great event. We will do more events at Trellises Restaurant as a result of the courteous staff.

title: “GO FOR IT!!”
text:
We're just home from a perfect stay at Inn New York City. If you are planning a trip to NYC, just go for it and opt for the Inn. We had a warm and welcoming, but inobstrusive, visit to the Spa Suite. The bath and in-suite sauna are fabulous extras you will not find in a high-rise hotel!
Cuisine was our primary objective in New York. After dining at Per Se, Le Bernardin, and Jean-Georges, Inn NYC was the perfect "pamper yourself" complement. It is located in the PERFECT neighborhood. We were able to walk EVERYWHERE - The Metropolitan Opera, Metropolitan Museum of Art, Natural History Museum, Broadway and ALL the restaurants. Also ... try the recommended Cafe Luxembourg. We did and enjoyed every bite.
It's worth every penny!

title: “Location is Perfect if you need to be downtown”
text: This hotel is in the heart of the city. Lots of places to walk to for food and drink. This was my first stay at this Marriott. I was not disappointed. My room was big, the bed was awesome. The staff were spot on. Could not walk anywhere without them saying hello, good day, or how are you. This place must have good mgt. If you have the opportunity to be on the concierge floor, its worth it. You get lots of snacks and drinks. Breakfast will filling. I would recommend this place for a business trip or for family. Some of the restaurants i visited were: PF Changs, Webber Grill, and Ruth Chris. All within walking dist. I did a tripadvisor on each of the restaurants.

title: “Great location, but grungy room”
text:
I'm an HHonors club member so I see Hiltons all over the place. Sad to say, this is one of the less impressive ones I've run across. The average Hampton Inn is nicer than this and for the same or less money. 
My initial impression upon arrival around 3:45 pm on a Saturday was not good. The lobby was somewhat small and crowded with what appeared to be at least one large tour group. I figured there might be a line at check-in since that's close to check-in time, but I was not prepared to stand in line for upwards of 20 minutes while the line got longer and longer behind me. There were three desk clerks on duty and they were all taken up with three customers who apparently needed a significant amount of extra help/ service beyond just the 5 minutes it takes to check into one's room. I don't see why there couldn't have been one clerk helping the people in line, who like me, probably mostly had 5-minute transactions, so 30 people didn't have to wait for the three people at the desk to have their 20-minute discussions with the managers or whatever. I was in town for a concert, and the main performer for the night was also having to stand in line several persons behind me, which I know must have inconvenienced him since he was due at soundcheck (he finally left the line). My friend who was attending the concert with me and staying in a different room said he had arrived at 3 pm and was told his room was ready but he wasn't allowed to check into it yet - so he was stuck in line too. It was totally ridiculous as the line eventually ran the whole length of the lobby and was still going on an hour later when more friends of mine checked in!
Once I got past the bad lobby experience and up to my room, I found it a bit run down and grungy. The tub had a big rust stain, the sink had a big crack and the toilet seat was about the cheapest imaginable. The carpet seemed old and not clean, the bed only had one very thin comforter and when I got out the extra blanket from the closet and put it on the bed, the blanket was very old, stiff (like it hadn't been washed in who knows when) and contained several moth holes. When I opened the refrigerator, a three-foot piece of the cabinet housing it fell off - it was loose - and landed on my arm. The entrance hall of the room also smelled like smoke (I'm pretty sure this was supposed to be a non-smoking room) and there was a lot of noise from the hallway. 
While I was getting settled into my room and in and out meeting friends, etc., the front desk clerk who had just checked me in called and left a voice mail message about was I satisfied with my room and give her a call if there was anything more she could do. Unfortunately, when I saw the message light flashing, I tried to pick up my message by pressing "voice mail" on the phone. That key did not work, so I had to call the operator, which rang for a very long time before anyone answered. I finally got the operator who told me a number sequence to press to pick up the message. After wasting 5 minutes on this I was not happy to find out it was just a message from the Hilton staff. I appreciate their concern but given that I was only going to be in this room overnight and had already wasted a lot of time in the check-in line I was more concerned with getting to my dinner and show engagements than I was with talking to them. 
A few positives: The location of this hotel is very convenient to the Trocadero Theater (where the show I was seeing was held) as well as to Chinatown (good restaurants) and the market (around the corner). I liked that the room had a fridge, coffee, microwave and decent wi-fi, the TV was nice, the room had a small scrap of a city skyline view, and the free bath products were nice (though I wasn't going to use them in that grungy tub, I took them home). The free breakfast was also good and the restaurant has nice views, though I do wish it and a bunch of meeting rooms hadn't been located directly on my hotel floor (more noise). However, overall I would expect more from a Hilton. I would only stay here again if I was staying for just one night to go somewhere in the immediate neighborhood. The value for what you pay is simply not that great.

title: “Beware priceline guests!”
text: Expect a very poor front desk attitude when you book through priceline. I haven't stayed at the hotel yet but based on my phone room request i guess i won't have a high expectation, and just have to manage fine without expecting service. I won the room through priceline for $89 a night, what a steal right? Why would i be complaining already? Well i was very excited, right after my reservation was confirmed, called the hotel directly for room request eventhough my trip to SF is still 4 months away. Priceline stated that special request on rooms should contact the hotel directly, so i did. I never ever been treated so low before at any other hotels i've stayed in. Through some of the reviews i read i guess a lot of people that have booked the hotel through priceline feel the same way? I'm not really fussy at all when staying at a hotel, my only request was just to have a room with 2 queen/2 double beds and maybe a refridgerator since i'm still breastpumping. The lady i spoke to (Georgia)refused to let me make any special request and keep stating that I book my room through Priceline( as if I don't have rights to make any special request, and just be happy that i even got a room at the hotel for such bargain) And she also didn't want to even let me know what type of room i'll have. Feeling frustated I contacted Priceline and they took care of me. This is the first time I booked hotel through Priceline. I really recomend Priceline for their customer satisfaction and profesionalism but Do Not recomend this hotel even if you have a good deal. I will write another review after my SF trip.

title: “Different opinions”
text: I am afraid that I can't compliment the hotel and agree with the other comments further down. A truly mediocre hotel with slapdash service.

title: “What a great hotel!!”
text: We stayed here for the first weekend in July - we were in town for a convention. What a lovely hotel! The lobby was beautiful, the pool was wonderful, the staff was exceedingly helpful. Just so people know - downtown Charlotte closes on the weekends! So, there is a shopping plaza below the lobby and one across the street attached by a catwalk - but all of the stores are closed on the weekend. However, the concierge was able to make good recommendations for shopping and printed out very clear directions for me. The room was very nice - maybe a little on the small side - one easy chair and desk. The only complaint I had was that there were no channels for kids - no cartoon network, no nickelodeon. Granted, we did not travel with children - but I have to admit that I enjoy cartoons.

title: “FAIRLY CENTRAL VALUE FOR MONEY”
text: when we arrived at the hotel we saw scaffoling outside and i said oh no to myself. we went in and the girl on check in was very polite and helpful we were asking about sighting like the hop on hop off buses and the statue of libatery ectand she checked out the times and costs ect for us. our room was not in the hotel and two doors up like an apartment. the room was a nice size with a table and chairs and a walk in warddrobe. there was a kitchen with a cooker and a mircowave and fridge (we didn't use them but it was nice to have the choice especailly since eating out can be.) its about a 5 min walk to grand central and about a 15/ 20 min walk to time square. i found it to be clean and noise free.didn't get to try the food in the hotel. the breakfast i thought was 2 dear. found it to be clean and noise free. the only fault i could find is that the decorate in the rooms is a bit dated.

title: “Fun boutique hotel!”
text: Great decor, and fab location, close to cable cars, and union square! Rooms are cute, but not modern...eclectic old school decor, could be modernized but definitely quaint. The lobby and bar are fun, and staff are very friendly and helpful!

title: “Central location is only plus point”
text:
So this hotel is an example of how the larger chains want to focus more on volume of guests rather than hospitality. The wing of the hotel where we stayed seemed to be old. Frayed carpets, crack in the wash basin.. not what one would expect in a Hilton property.
However, the location is great for the price.. and if like us one wants to have a good San Fran city feeling, then this hotel should be fine.

title: “Comfortable, convenient hotel”
text: Stayed at the Wellington Hotel last December (2003) before Xmas. Very comfortable, relaxing rooms. Was never bothered by any noise and the room service was great - hot plain pancakes with butter and maple syrup!! The location of the Wellington is absolutely perfect, and i'm staying there again in March! Would definately recommend. It's not the Ritz, but hey, it was clean warm and cozy.

title: “Why did I wait so long before staying here...”
text:
I've had the option of staying at the Palmer House several times in the past but always chose a different hotel. Now I'm asking myself, "why?"
This is a classic old Chicago experience - as soon as you walk in to the hotel lobby area (second floor) - you are immediately taken by the opulence of the the walls, ceiling and flooring. "If only the walls could talk" ran through my head. Stunning.
Desk staff greeted me cheerfully and quickly got me to my room, which was surprisingly large.
One downside to my room - when I entered it had an odor of cigar smoke. I called down and informed the front desk, they offered to move me, but since I was there for one night I opted for housekeeping to come to do a second "cleaning" - whatever that meant. When I returned it smelled much better (not a febreze smell either).
Definitely spend some time in the lounge area - and look up, it was pretty darn impressive.
Could use some sprucing up but it is an old building/hotel.

title: “Very Surprising!!!”
text:
I stayed at the Hyatt Regency last week on business and have gotten used to the less than fabulous accomodations I am forced into through my company. However, this place was great!!!
I was a little confused upon arrival because the registration/check-in is on the 3rd floor and I completely missed those signs upon entering. Once I found the registration area, I was quickly checked in and in my room within 5 minutes. The lobby area is kinda cool. It kind of reminds me of a version of the ride inside of the Epcot sphere at Disney World...The World of Tomorrow or whatever it's called. The lobby is kind of futuristic yet slightly dated. I know that sounds like a weird description for something I am saying is great, but I really like the vibe I got from it.
I was starving upon arrival so I ordered room service as soon as I dropped my bags on the floor. I was told it would be 45 minutes, but got a knock on my door within 10 minutes. The guy who brought me my food was named "Fast Andy". He was great and I was very thankful for him 'because I think I may have passed out if it had taken 45 minutes. I orderd the avocado and tomato salad along with the chicken tortilla soup...SOOOOO GOOD!!! It was so good, I also ordered it the next night for dinner!!!
My only complaint is that my window faced the bay and the Port of San Francisco building (probably not what it is actually called). This building houses a clock tower that dongs and dongs and dongs every 30 minutes. Quite annoying!!!
This hotel is in a great location, is very clean, and quaint. I would defintely suggest this hotel to most anyone.

title: “Under construction!”
text: The entire first level is torn apart. Rooms are fine. Good location. I had a power strip at the nightstand. That was nice. Disappointed about the construction.

title: “Good Hotel For Family On Budget/Good Location”
text:
Our destination was Cooperstown, NY for a youth baseball tournament. My husband and I were traveling with our kids, ages 15 and 12. We flew into and out of Boston to see the Red Sox as part of our trip. 
I had read reviews on this website for various hotels and chose the Midtown from them. The reviews were right on and we were happy with the Midtown. Good price, plus a discount using AAA. The staff was friendly and helpful.
The hotel is older, but everything was clean and well kept. Our room was a good size. Parking underneath the hotel was reasonably priced and fairly secure.
The location is great. Nice area, easy walking to the Prudential Center and Fenway Park. The subways are very close for farther desintations in the city, which we took several times.
I would definitely recommend the Midtown for travelers on a budget, especially families going to see the Red Sox (note: do not buy grandstand seats if your family is tall!).
I would not recommend this hotel to travelers looking for higher end accommodations.

title: “Excellent Hotel with a great staff”
text: My wife and I stayed at the W for our anniversary and had an amazing time. The W is in a perfect central location and that makes it very easy to walk to almost anything you would like to do. The hotel is amazing and our suite had an amazing view of times square. Their Whatever/Whenever agents went out of their way to help me plan an absolutely amazing trip and were more than helpful especially since this was my first trip to New York. I would highly recommend this hotel and will definitely use it on my next trip.

title: “Superb service, soulful unique place.”
text: Soulful old hotel with exceptionally friendly, helpful responsive staff. Not a large hotel nor are the rooms hugs as it apears to be a late 1800's/turn of the century building that has been updated. Beatiful decor. Nice (free) continental breakfast each AM and (free) wine every PM.

title: “Enjoyed our stay!”
text: The location was great, the rooms were clean, the price was a fantastic value, the Texas-shaped breakfast waffles were cute and the staff was very courteous and helpful! A very enjoyable stay. Thanks!

title: “Excellent location but watch out for the extra costs!”
text: Stayed at the Sheraton from July 6-9. The location is perfect!. It's right in the heart of downtown. Close to some serious shopping and walking distance to the Pike Place Market and an abundance of restaurants. The rooms are plain and clean, they're nothing special to write home about, but who cares when all you do is sleep in them anyways. The electrical outlets were old and worn. I tried to plug in my blowdryer and straightener and couldn't, they just kept falling out. I was charged an extra 10.95 for Wi-fi access that barely worked.
