I called the front desk and was told they would waive the 10.95 charge. Parking is NOT included in the room rate. Be prepared to cough out an extra 36.07 per day plus 7.93 WA state parking tax. My estimated total when i booked online for 3 nights was was 508.86 including taxes. My actual charge was 652.01 > 145.00 per night, room tax 22.62 pn, Seattle Tourism tax 2.00 pn and the parking fees pn.! Also i was still charged 10.95 for the Wi-fi that was supposed to be waived.. an error on the hotels part that they corrected.

title: “Great customer service”
text:
Stayed 3 nights and were very pleased with the staff responsiveness to all requests. They have an excellent can-do attitude which was refreshing. The rooms are small with minimalistic decor. The bathrooms are very tiny- with a stall shower and no countertop space for personal toiletries. We found space for our stuff on the rack below the sink. The bed was very comfortable, decent closet space with safe, and the Bliss amenities were excellent.
The location is terrific located on 47th just off Broadway so everything was accessible by foot. The only problems we noted were the connecting room doors are very thin and we heard every conversation held next door- and the dark hallways and elevators, while attractive made it difficult to navigate.
We'd stay there again, but would suggest if you are older and/or have any vision problems e.g., reading menus in candlelight, you'll have problems in the elevators and hallways so consider another hotel.

title: “Unsatisfied”
text: Stayed at the new Hampton Inn at Green Oaks Road. Have stayed at several when traveling with family. This was a business trip and stayed with room mates. Our schedule was rigorous and we started our meetings at 8 and ended at 10 or later. We spent most of our valuable time at the front desk trying to put fires out and fixing our billing. This is not usual for Hampton Inn and most are run very well. This one needs the kinks ironed out and Management communicating with staff. We would never survive if we ran our business like the Hampton Inn at Green Oaks.

title: “2nd stay”
text:
this place is wonderful .. clean rooms and friendly staff . this is our 2nd stay ..we were in san fransico in june and it was a perfect stay then too... we stayed in the suite and it was so spacious and cute decor... i dont mind paying more for a hotel ....and have peace of mind that i wont take home bed bugs ...and that never crossed my mind at this beautiful hotel... love the fire pits ,, if youre a smoker you will love the smoking section
best location, if you go there on vacation dont forget to stop and see the sea lions at the end of pier 39....it is in walking distance from this hotel.

title: “Amazing value, superb location, great staff!”
text:
Stayed 3 nights at the end of May 2010 using the "parking package". Dropped off car at indoor parking garage next to the hotel and checked in around lunch time, got a lovely room with cool views of the Empire State Building. Great stay, from start to finish - nothing to complain of in the least!
Pros: 
- Location (a block from the subway, a few blocks from Times Square - just far enough to be quiet!) - the street is just fine, no safety concerns beyond the norm for NYC
- Personnel (very amenable and friendly, a gem in NYC!)
- Comfort (great beds & pillows, spacious bathroom)
- Decor (clean, modern)
Cons:
- Elevators (they're slow... but so be it; if you're a light sleeper, make sure to ask for a room that is not between the elevator cages)
- Popularity of breakfast (very nice breakfast, included with the room, however the breakfast room was way too crowded!)
- Prices are sure to get higher and higher - we had a great deal as the hotel had barely opened when we booked

title: “Totally Disappointed”
text:
The reception was terrible, the valet - that's why service is not a part of their title, the bees, not the best addition in a room with an infant. We stayed there almost a week when my wife was at a training at the Hilton. I am a Marriot Rewards member, but surely that did not do much in their eyes. From the start we were treated as though we did not belong there. There was no formal welcome except from the Valet service. We wanted to park ourselves, big mistake. We traveled with an infant and had many things, but the Valet told the bellboy to take our luggage off his cart. The Valet would't even budge to open the door in the absence of a greeter. You have to climb stairs to get to the lobby from the outside. Even with all the luggage that comes with traveling with an infant, the Valet didn't even think to tell us that there was an elevator. We had to discover this on our own. 
We were in line, but the front desk served someone else better dressed than us first. Then we got the "room with the view" that also came with wasps. We complained to the front desk, but we had to again ask, this time with the housekeeping staff. They caulked up the hole with no guarantees. We asked to be moved and no help was offered in moving the crib and everything else we had to lug ourselves. 
We talked to the manager and got a plate of stinking cheese. We complained after getting back and got an email for more information. We responded. It is now a month and a half later and yet not a response. We should have stayed at the Hilton across the street. We will use up all points and cut the rewards card. Thanks Blackstone for ruining a good relationship.
The best thing about the stay were the nice housekeeping folks. Management could learn alot from them. For those that are wheelchair bound, go somewhere else because you have to open the doors yourself and the elevator is too small.

title: “Very good stay, steep price”
text:
I stayed here last week for a conference and meetings at my company location nearby. It is all around more expensive than my usual choice in SFO (Grand Hyatt), from the rooms to the services and food. 
That said, this property has great historical significance and it was great to learn about it. The room was well-appointed. Relatively quiet but did hear occasional sirens (not nearly as many as I hear in Union Square). Can't stand the Starwood standard thermostats that are motion-detection activated - and to top that off, housekeeping turns the thermostat OFF each time they service the room. Not a nice feeling to come back to a warm room after an afternoon walk.
The location can't be beat if attending an event at the Moscone Center.
On a side note, I took my family back to the hotel for Sunday brunch after moving to the Hyatt for the 2nd half of my 8-night trip. The brunch was pricey, but SPECTACULAR. Everyone loved it!
This hotel is a no-brainer if you can get a good deal.

title: “service”
text: The service from this hotel is excellent. They provided some of the best assistance I have ever received and i have traveled around the world and stayed in all types hotels. They will provide assistance for you and seem to really be pleased to provide whatever you might need. This is a top quality hotel.

title: “Nice location”
text: the best part of this hotel is its location. its close to the park, all midtown attractions, and the subway stop is a stone's throw away. otherwise, there is nothing extraordinary about this hotel.

title: “Nice Lobby, Decent Rooms, Great Location”
text: We went to Philly for the weekend because I had never been. The hotel was in a great location, we loved the fact that it was across a street from Reading Terminal Market and walking distance to just about everything except for the Art museum. The rooms were average Marriott rooms, nothing extremely fancy, we requested a top floor and the few was pretty at night. We had a Marriott Certificate so we didn't pay for the hotel. The parking at the hotel is extremely expensive, they a good about allowing you to leave your car in front of the hotel while you check in. We parked around the corner by City Hall and pay $17 for 24 hours where at the hotel it would have been $42. We also left the car in front and ran to do a little produce shopping at the market and we had no problems.

title: “Good value at Times Square”
text:
The renovations are complete inside, and bar started to operate in the middle of our Stay.
Great Location for tourism as you are in the middle of New york.
Staying on the concierge floor, to be honest could not find what the difference is. ( not dedicated check in, concierge, lounge....) Maybe the bathrobe and some extra lotion!!
Rooms nicely refurbinshed. Water pressure is disapointing.
Choose due the great rate I got ( 289USD), comparing to other chain hotels in this area, and Breakfast ( above avarege) was included.
Overall, deliver what we expected. Would Stay again for this same price!

title: “Great place to stay.”
text: The Drury Inn is awesome. We stayed there because it was close to the Metrolina Expo, but the clean rooms, friendly staff, and extras were such a special bonus. Every staff member I met was beyond friendly and very helpful regardless of the situation. The hotel is nicely decorated and very clean. The kick-back hour (free drinks and heavy snacks) filled us so much we didn't bother with dinner. The breakfast was tasty and generous as well. I think this is the best place to stay in Charlotte!

title: “OK, but not for that price!”
text:
This Hotel has definitely seen better days. The rooms are quite nice but the bathroom is way too old and seems to be always a little dirty, maybe because its quite old! Taking a shower is no fun in a bathroom which feels dirty. You have always the feeling youre standing in the middle of someone elses dirt which is awful. They have to renovate them definitely. 
All in all the Hotel would be OK, but not for that price. You get better offers for that money! 
The airconditioning is very loud and we had to turn it off in the night!
However the Garden is very beautiful and at nights all is illuminated with cosy lights!
This could be a great place if they would renovate certain things!

title: “Nothing special - a bit of a let down”
text:
This hotel was good, but not what I was expecting. 
The location is a big plus. You can't beat it. Around the corner from Union Square. 
The room was nice, but the bed and pillows were terrible. Very uncomfortable. The bathroom and shower were good though. 
However, the biggest disappointment for me had to be the Grand Club facilities. The breakfast choices on offer were poor and the fact that alcohol during the evening "happy hour" service had to be paid for was amateurish. I've previously paid for the same type of benefits when I stayed at the Sofitel in Melbourne Australia and their offering was a lot better. The breakfast was better quality and all drinks and food was free to club guests between 5pm and 7pm each night. Charging people for drinks when they've already paid extra to use the club facilities is a disgrace.

title: “four star service at economy price”
text: My family and I stayed here for our weekend trip to San Francisco. This Travelodge is located in a quiet area sandwiched between the beautiful park-like Presidio, the upscale Pacific heights neighborhood, the Palace of Fine Arts, and the Golden Gate Bridge. The staff were wonderfully helpful and accomodating, especially Raymond. The rooms were a bit small, but very clean, and equipped with a fridge and a self locking safe. The pillows were new and fluffy and they gave you 2 per person (8 pillows with 2 queen beds). The beds were new as well, on the firm side. I slept well and never heard any of the other guests on the busy Valentine's weekend. We brought our dog and he was greeted with a gourmet doggy treat bag and the same personable treatment by the staff that we received.The high-speed internet was very fast and the connection was excellent. There is a parking lot, but it fills up fast. The neighborhood has plenty of free overnight parking however so that is not a problem. The staff were very friendly, taking care of our every need from calling us cabs to giving us advice on museums and restaurants. I was very impressed. If you stay, ask for Raymond. I will definetely be staying here the next time I am in San Francisco.

title: “Beautiful Lobby, Great Location!”
text:
Located right on I35, the hotel was in perfect location for just about everything. Dallas Market Center, American Airlines Center, Love Field Airport, Fair Park, Medieval Times are all very near and to make it even better, the hotel offers a complimentary shuttle within a 5-Mile radius. The hotel offers complimentary Wi-Fi as well.
The hotel is in good condition and the Texas weather was great! Staff was very friendly. The best part was the location. Nothing is too far and that shuttle makes planning your activities stress-free.
My room was pretty spacious with a decent sized TV. The hotel was nice and the people running it were better. Simple, quaint, but in a great location!

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
Stayed here for 2nts after a skiing trip in Vermont. Excellent service, modern interior with a lively bar area (the bar food is excellent by the way!!)
Rooms are very large and modern.
Only thing this hotel lacks is a swimming pool or jacuzzi.
About a 15min walk into the centre of Boston.
Excellent choice if travelling to Boston!!!

title: “Friendly and honest staff”
text:
We enjoyed two nights at this wonderful Omni. The staff was very friendly and always willing to give personalized advice about the city. The room was clean and comfortable. The bed was also comfortable as was a roll a way. I had lost a sapphire earring and housekeeping had it when I called two days later. WOW!
Great location also, on cable car line downtown. It is close enough to the tourist destinations but not too close.

title: “A wonderful hotel with very friendly staff.”
text: Went back home with my 13 year old. His first time in the city. Our room was not ready, early check in, so they upgraded us! No extra charge. Room was very clean and comfortable. Staff was the best I have ever encountered in this city. Decent breakfast every morning. Can not say enough about this hotel or the staff! Highly recommended!

title: “I love staying here”
text: The place is very accomidating and can't do enough to help. even give free stuff from time to time

title: “Location, location, location”
text: We stayed here for two nights on our first trip to Philly and could not have been more pleased. This hotel is located right in the historic district and was very convenient to the attractions we wanted to see. The Visitors Center, Independence Hall, Liberty Bell, Constitutiion Center, US Mint, and Big Bus Tour were all within a few minutes' walk. The biggest bonus was the roof-top swimming pool--our teenagers enjoyed swimming and we enjoyed the cool evening breeze up there. You do have to pay for parking but we got a free parking deal on Gophila.com.

title: “Upgrade going on here, some improvements”
text: I stopped here because I was exhausted after driving from Deming, NM. Needed a place to stretch out before getting back on the highway. Lots of work was going on. New paint, new flooring, etc. The room was large but didn't have any chairs. Desk but no chair. It appeared the furnishings were incomplete. There was a used wash cloth hanging in the shower. Ick. The rest of the place seemed clean, however. Internet connection cost extra, which I paid for, but I didn't use it because I was just too tired and went straight to bed. They allow pets. No frills. Be glad they give you tiny little soap bars (2). I didn't see any bugs.

title: “One night stop”
text: Good clean hotel. The rooms were roomy, clean and quiet. A very clean Hotel. The staff were very friendly and helpful. A little far out of the centre of the city for sight seeing but taxis and bus serices were cheap and good. You could also walk if you wanted too. It felt safe to stay there and walk around day or night.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text:
Perfect for anybody who wants a large , luxurious hotel in a great location. Was extremely impressed with the impeccable service and friendly staff who go out of their way to make you feel welcome.
Our stay was enhanced by the fact that we were upgraded on our arrival to the boutique Waldorf Towers at no extra cost. The hotel is usually very busy with business meetings, wedding receptions, graduation parties etc and can appear quite formal and as such may not suit everybody, however this is only a minor gripe and didn't detract from our stay at all. Overall it was a pleasure to stay in such a landmark hotel. Highly recommended.

title: “It's not a palace, but did you expect it to be?”
text:
If you do choose to stay in this hotel, do not stay in the front two rooms (101 or 102). These rooms are right at the entrance, essentially in the lobby. So you can hear everything that goes on there. I stayed in 102 for a night, and when I asked to move, the staff was helpful.
Still, the hotel isn't terrible. It's clean, although run-down. The rooms are not at all homogeneous. Some may be missing a coat rack, or an alarm clock, or a night stand. One room may be fairly large and quiet, while others are cramped.
Point is, you're taking a chance when you stay here. You may end up satisfied with your stay, or you may be appalled. The rooms ARE kept clean, though (no bugs, sticky carpets or whatever else you may have read), and the staff is helpful. If you end up with this hotel, check in early, and demand that you get a quiet, spacious room, and you'll have a reasonably pleasant stay.

title: “Nice, but no hot tub”
text: We stayed April 10-12th. This is a newer hotel that is very convienient to get to as well as otherarea attractions. Rooms are nicely appointed and spacious as well as immaculately clean. The pool is big with "bathwater" temperature. But it was aHUGE disappointment to find a hotel with a great indoor pool area that didn't have a hot tub. Staff was friendly and helpful.

title: “Early Rude Awakening On Saturday Morning.”
text:
Sorry Hyatt, I was not happy with the cleaning services knocking on my door at 8:35 a.m. on a Saturday... Not once, not twice, BUT THREE TIMES!!!! Enough already!!! I was sound asleep, I was rudely awakened and extremely startled and that put me in a anxious state the rest of the morning. I was hoping to rest, relax and sleep in as checkout was not until 12 noon. I did call to the front desk and asked to speak to a manager. I was told that management was in a meeting....code speak for please don't bother me with your petty issues?? Ouch. 
I called house keeping, and after 15 minutes if insistence I was allowed to spek to someone who apologized and stated that housekeeping should not start knocking on doors until after 9:30am...... Dude, check your clock!!! 
 I blame this one on Hyatt Management who schedules Housekeeping service to start so early. I blame Hyatt Management for not having a system in place that notifies Housekeeping of when guests actually check out, as opposed to knocking door to door and waking up guests, which in my book is tantamount to thank your for your $$ now get out...... I know this sounds harsh, but if I wanted Motel 6 treatment, I would stay at a Motel 6. Perhaps my door was on the end of the floor that housekeeping begins its cleaning service routine, BUT PLEASE, NO EXCUSE FOR A 8:35 a.m. Knock on the Door, and to make matters worse, 3x!! PLEASE ENOUGH! 
Now, if you think I have gone overboard, well the plot thickens. At the prescribed checkout time, as I was walking out the door of my room, there stood three maids, one asked if I was leaving and I said "yes". Then she swiftly ran in the room before the door could close...... Really? I instantly felt that they were hovering in front of my room, just waiting for me to leave!?! REALLY, WHAT GIVES? Rude and Insensitive to me as a guest. I felt like they were saying Get the Hell Out!!
Management, please look into the Scheduling issue. Management, please make yourself available to guest criticisms and concerns. Management, p,ease allow guests to leave a voice message when you are not available.
I have stayed at this hotel many times and am very surprised at the poor quality of service and lack of accessibility to management to voice my criticism in a timely manner.

title: “Location, Value, Comfort”
text:
I have had the pleasure of staying at the Brookshire Suites several times, and they never disappoint. Me and my Fiance love to go there as a little getaway that is driving distance from Philly. Baltimore has alot of nice attractions that are either walking distance, or a REALLY short drive from Brookshire.It is in a prime location that is perfect for walking to the local Harbor attractions. When we first started going to the Harbor we used to check out all the local attractions and the staff are always knowledgable about the area. Now that we have been there several times, we are quite content to enjoy the comfort of our 2 room suite. The beds at the Brookshire are soo comfy you wont want to get up!! But then you do because you know there is a great breakfast buffet waiting for you in the Cloud Club. Did I mention breakfast is FREE!!!!!! And its a real Breakfast with bacon, sausage eggs etc. You can even make your own belgian waffle!!! 
Let me take a moment to talk about value. I almost dont want to tell you because if everybody starts going to the Brookshire I might have trouble getting a room. LOL Anyway This place is ALWAYS running some kind of BOGO deal!! We stayed for 2 nites in a 2 room suite, breakfast included, we received a $25 gift check for use at a few local resturants, right in the heart of the harbor for under $200 tax included!! You cant beat that! 
Customer service at the Brookshire is always excellent. i really have nothingn bad to say about this place, and if you are trying to decide where to stay while at the Harbor, you should stop looking and make your reservations.

title: “Stop looking--the Lenox Hotel is the place to stay!”
text: We'd never stayed in Boston before and we wanted our first trip to be really special, including staying at a great hotel. We booked a room at the Lenox Hotel based on the reviews we read in tripadvisor. We were not disappointed! First, the location is perfect. It's in the heart of the Back Bay section, where there are lots of wonderful restaurants, shops, and beautiful residences. The historic sites are also easily within walking distance. But even better, the hotel itself was fantastic, every aspect of it! The staff couldn't have been friendlier or more helpful. The room was spacious and elegant and had a huge walk-in closet. One thing we really appreciated is that the refrigerator wasn't fully stocked with items to buy. The only things in the fridge were complimentary bottles of water that were replenished each day of our stay. There is a huge list in the room of complimentary items the hotel will provide if you need or want them. We asked the concierge if there was a soda machine in the building. He asked what we wanted and I told him Diet Coke. He asked if Pepsi was OK and I said no. Within 5 minutes, he delivered two cold bottles of Diet Coke to our room personally, no charge! The hotel has a turn-down service and left chocolate truffles on our bed each night, there was free wireless service, a regular check-out time was later than most hotels, and fruit and cookies at the front desk for guests. This hotel does not nickel-and-dime its customers! If we had to identify anything negative about our stay, it was only that the bottom of the door let in a little too much light at night. That was easily remedied by putting the pillow shams against the door.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text: I work in NYC so it's rare I have to stay in a hotel in NYC since I live only an hour away. But I had decided to book this last minute due to the freezing rain conditions in and around NYC last night. It is in Times Sq but not in the middle of all the noise so I was glad for that. Lobby and bar are very nice. Rooms are on the small side but otherwise very clean and comfortable. The bathrooms were also small - if you are plus sized you may want to ask for a room with a bathroom that is bigger (if they have rooms w/ larger bathrooms). But everything was clean and worked perfectly in the bathroom and in the room itself. I would definitely stay here again, too.

title: “Recommended for everyone!”
text: Me and my family stayed at the motel for a few days and had a great time and experience there. The location was close to all amenities and was close to the downtown core and it's attractions. The rooms were very nice and comfy, and we found them to be very clean. The service was friendly and hospitable and we had no problems while staying here. The prices were reasonable and we had an overall great time.We highly recommend this motel for everyone in need of a motel.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
This was a lovely place to stay after flying in from the UK. It was close to the airport but not too close to be bothered by noise from the planes. In fact, we didn't hear any noise at all from anyone else for the two nights that we stayed there.
We had stayed at another Hilton Suites on a previous trip to the USA and were pleasantly surprised to have the exact same room at this one, so they must be standard throughout the chain. Lovely big room with a big, comfortable bed. Fully equipped kitchen if required.
The only downside was the complimentary hot breakfast. It wasn't very hot. The 'hot' water for tea was tepid. Having been to the USA on many holidays previously, I was prepared for this so it is only a minor gripe.
The staff were very friendly and helpful and we would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone else.

title: “Typical Best Western”
text:
Stayed here in Sept '10. Hotel is located in a part of town with lots of traffic because it's close to the entrance to the Lincoln tunnel and the Javits Center is a couple blocks away. With that said it's location is also a plus because the Port Authority terminal and Penn Station are within walking distance. The best thing about being in this part of town is that feels a lot like NY did before it started it's latest renaissance of sleek condo towers and chic hotels and restaurants. In this part of town there are a pizza stand that has no sitting area, a classic bagel place, and small family owned bodegas and the best part is the price reflects it. Of course there are also the newer restaurants and other places trying to make it, but they are sprinkled throughout and not necessarily concentrated in one particular area.
Picked this hotel after canceling a reservation at another nearby place. It was last minute and wound up being lucky because I got the last room. A couple came in as I was filling out paperwork and they were told the hotel was full. Whew! Although it was just me, I wound up with a room with 2 full size beds. The room was just big enough to fit both beds, TV console with TV, and small desk with chair. The room's decor seemed outdated. The bathroom was basic and not much to write home about. Breakfast was simple and the dining area was a bit small. Just got my little bit of food and ate up in the room. Again, plenty of options to eat around so just treat yourself elsewhere.
For the price it was not bad but had I planned better probably could have found something better for less. Since it was just a place to sleep at night, no major complaints.

title: “Hilton Hotel Chicago, 720 S. Michigan Ave.”
text:
The Hotel itself is really old fashioned, especially the rooms & lobby. Every additional service costs extra, for example the gym, internet, baggage storage for a couple of hours etc.
The only good thing is the location however there are more modern hotels at the same location, I would personaly not go back there.

title: “Great location small rooms but cozy”
text: Excellent location in a great part of downtown Boston. Walking distance to Fenway. Rooms are small but functional. This Marriott doesn't give free breakfast to gold members (only platinum). Also parking is $42/day across the street. The price you pay for the location I guess!

title: “Awesome stay, great location”
text: Staff very friendly, great location. We stayed there hoping to find a place for us to stay in Houston as we travel there frequently. After our visit, we will stay here again

title: “Outstanding Location and GREAT Value!”
text: We stayed at the Park Hyatt for Valentine's weekend and were very impressed. We usually stay at the Westin, but found the price at Park Hyatt was very reasonable. Infact, the only thing the Westin had left (we booked on February 11th) was a room with two double beds for roughly the same price. This surprised us as we had tried to stay at the Park Hyatt several times and couldn't book anything under $400/night. The room was wonderful, overlooking the old Water Tower on the 11th floor. There is an enormous soaking tub and separate shower. The hotel is very quiet and the service was impressive. The dining room is spectacular (NoMi), but be prepared to pay dearly. Our dinner cost more than our room for one night! Yikes! But it was worth it. The concierge managed to find us an open table at Zealous, the next night, Valentine's Day. which is a great local restaurant. My husband liked the fitness center and there's free internet access stations off the lobby. We would definitely go back again.

title: “would stay again in a heartbeat”
text:
After being in countless hotels, it was a delight to be in hotel where the room walls are not all white and the room has some charm! I adored the painted green wall & the green chairs. it added some life to the room & made it feel very cozy. 
it was a very chilly SF summer during my stay & the heat could have been better in the room. luckily there was a portable heater in the closet. 
Friendly staff, comfy room, clean and a great view. 
btw, if you're not used to city noise, ask for a room in the back. i got trolley noise which was fine by me but i'm sure others wouldn't be happy.

title: “Soho Grand is GRAND!”
text: We chose the Soho Grand because it is in an area we love, and because it welcomes our pet dogs with open arms and doggie treats. As an added bonus, the rooms are extremely comfortable, the service is impeccable, and they give very good discounts to their returning guests. I would highly recommend the Soho Grand for anyone visiting New York.

title: “Good location, tiny room, the usual nutty W decor”
text:
Well, I don't think people stay at the W because they want a spacious room. Because the rooms are so tiny, New York tiny. And since we're in NYC, what can one expect? 
My sister and I went to NYC over Thanksgiving and I arrived at the W hours after my sister did. She'd requested that we be moved to a larger room because apparently the first room was too miniscule for two people. 
The bathroom was really small, and the doorless shower didn't get water all over the floor like the shower at the W Times Square. Nice decor, but the illuminated photo of a woman's bare back above the bed did not provide enough reading light. No nightlights at the W. The fitness center was amply equipped, though the first day (only the first day) I worked out they were out of towels. 
The bar is apparently a hot spot of sorts (drawing a much younger crowd than the Waldorf across the street) and the W provided complimentary holiday truffles and hot apple cider every night. The concierge was very helpful and the staff was friendly.

title: “Amazing”
text:
We stay at the Roosevelt every time we come to LA. This year, there was a mistake in our reservation. We were not in the type of room we booked. I was told to bring it up to the manager early the next morning.
Without any hesitation we were moved to the proper room. No hassle at all. 
Mistakes happen all the time. What matters is how you handle them. The staff at the Roosevelt clearly knows how to handle problems.
Well done!

title: “Ask for a river view!”
text:
Being a Starwood Hotel member has its perks. While checking into The Westin Chicago River North, I was updated to a suite. The suite had a 'sweet' view of Chicago. I was overlooking the river and most of downtown Chicago, able to watch the sunset each night. The location of this location was perfectly located to many restaurants/bars. The House of Blues was right across the street from the hotel. 
The theater district was a short walk across the river (about 5 minutes by foot). The suite was very large, had a chaise lounge, large desk with plenty of counter space in the room. The hotel bar located near the check in was adequate, nothing amazing, but with so much to do outside of the hotel, this wasn't an issue. I have already recommended this place to other friends.

title: “Beware Room 411”
text:
Overall, we had a nice stay. I got a good deal on Travelocity airfare/hotel package at Hotel Kabuki. We checked in on a Wednesday afternoon, we were given our keys for room 411. At first glance, the room looked ok; that was until we opened the curtains and looked out the window. All we could see were cement walls and the restaurant exhaust system - an ugly, rusty sight. When we looked straight up, we saw a tiny bit of sky.
I went back to the front desk and politely asked if we could change rooms and have one where we could actually see something out of the window. The hostess asked if we needed a king bed or a japanese tub. I told her that we could do with a queen bed and the japanese tub was unnecessary. She said she would upgrade us at no cost to a King room on the concierge floor with jetted tub. We checked into room 2504. It was very pretty with a big, wide window with rice paper screens that opened to reveal a view of the city in both directions and the hotel Japanese Garden below. The jetted tub was very large and deep.
Concierge floor means complimentory continental breakfast. Thursday morning at 7:30 they set up coffee, fresh fruit, large sweet rolls, cereal, milk, and juice. Friday morning - no continental breakfast, not even coffee. We were in a hurry to go sight seeing so we didn't bother asking. Saturday, Sunday, and Monday, they left a sign in the breakfast area saying that there would be no continental breakfast but we could pick up a voucher at the front desk to use in the hotel restaurant. The voucher was worth $12 pp and was to be applied to our restaurant bill. The breakfast food was good. One day the service was very slow and the next day it was fast.
We enjoyed our room and the hotel. We loved the Japanese decor, modern lobby, and Japanese Garden. Japantown is a little bit out of the way from tourist attractions but is on a main bus line so transportation was easy and convenient. We enjoyed the serenity of Japantown after the fast pace of downtown. The area was clean and the malls and stores were fun and interesting.

title: “Fantastic stay”
text:
When my wife and I were planning our honeymoon there was one place we both agreed that we wanted get to regardless of everything else and that was New York. 
We were lucky in that I have a friend who has lived in New York his whole life and he was good enough to pick us up at the airport and take us to the Millenium Hilton. It wasn't the easiest for him to get to the hotel with all the roads being cut off for the construction work at the WTC, but he did a fantastic job and got us there with very little hassle.
The hotel was very nice. We had a king room that overlooked the WTC site. I remember reading reviews about the construction noise being an issue, but we didn't hear a thing during our stay. The room itself was well appointed and suited our needs perfectly. It was very comfortable.
On the first morning before we headed out to explore the city we stopped off at the concierge desk. While we were there Joseph booked us tickets to Jersey Boys for that evening and also booked us in for dinner before the show. He was a great help and very courteous.
Thanks to our friend from New York we had a good grasp of where to go and how to get there. The hotel has is within a short walk of three subway stations which was the easiest way to get around the city. We took the R train right outside our hotel to 34th street (Herald Square) which put us right next to the Empire State Building. From there we explored all around the city.
That night we had an absolutely wonderful dinner where I had possibly the best steak of my life. Then we saw Jersey Boys (in very good seats). It was a great day spent in a great city.
The next day we spent some time shipping some things home which only took a short walk down the street. Then we walked to Battery Park and took the Staten Island ferry across the river and saw the Statue of Liberty. After that we walked around Wall Street, Bowling Green and onto Brooklyn Bridge. There is plenty to do and see in lower Manhattan and we took advantage of staying in that area to its fullest. Later that afternoon we had a well deserved dip in the pool to cool off our tired feet. That night we had a nice meal in the hotel restaurant.
On our last day we were able to check out and put our bags into storage so we could spend a few more hours seeing the sights before we had to catch our plane. We could not fault the hotel or the staff as they were all very helpful. We would stay here again in a heartbeat.

title: “Ideal for arrivals via Penn Station. Great location, great view.”
text:
This is the second time I have stayed at this hotel. We were upgraded to a "view room" (room 3717), which had spectacular views of the skyline, including the Empire State Building and the Crysler building. The room was small, but I was there to sight-see, not lounge in my hotel room - and the location and view made up for the small size anyway! 
We arrived via Penn Station, so we only had a very short walk to the hotel with our luggage. Our room wasn't ready, but it was before check-in time, so this wasn't unexpected. The staff was curteous and helpful, checking our luggage and giving us some directions. When we checked out, the bell staff even checked a flower in a small vase for us while we finished our sight-seeing.
Hint: This is a VINTAGE hotel. Expect it to be older (smaller elevators, rooms, etc.) It is well maintained and has a lot of character. I personally prefer a vintage feel. Beautiful grand chandelier in lobby.
My only small complaint is that the bathroom could use some renovation, as the tile grout is stained, which doesn't give the impression of spotlessly clean. That said, the room (including the bathroom) was very clean and comfortable. We all slept very well!

title: “Very close to hospitals and food”
text:
This was an OK hotel. I stayed here for business and found the check-in staff to be nice, but not knowledgeable and the check-out staff to be more knowledgeable but not very friendly or helpful. There seemed to be a lot of confusion around being "tax exempt".
The room was fine, but nothing special. The bathroom tub didn't drain well and the towels were really thin. But it was really cheap compared to the other hotels in the area, so it was OK. 
Because it's near the hospital there are several food choices nearby. Mostly fast food, but they're within easy walking distance. 
As an aside, it bothered me that the hotel parked its car in the fire lane. 
I wouldn't recommend this hotel to a friend unless they had to stay near the hospital. If they did, this hotel would be OK for the money.

title: “Worth sacrificing location for amazing cutomer service”
text: A little far from Phila proper (we were going to PMA adn the Franklin Inst), but easily accessible to the train; this place was a pleasant surprise. We traveled wiht a baby and four year old, and the room was spacious, the people who work there were extremely helpful, and kind. Warm cookies, and off street parking, this place was not only affordable, but well worth getting lost (full disclosure, I could get lost in a Miata without trying!).

title: “Old school charm in a relaxing environment”
text: We stayed there for 5 nights in our first visit to Los Angeles. The overall experience was great, the staff is helpful and polite, our room was spacious(two queen beds) clean and nicely decorated. the parking much cheaper that other hotels in LA. We had a noise problem with our first room, they were very understanding and changed us to a quiter room on the other side of the hotel. I think the LAAC has the potential to be a really great hotel if they only pay attention to some small things. For example, breakfast was healthy and tasty but kind of the same thing every day and that's so easy to fix. The hotel has such a relaxing feel to it, that the noise from the street becomes such a turn off. Just change the windows and the problem is solved. I would definitely stay there again, if i am back in LA, cause LAAC is more than a hotel, is a private club that accepts guests and you really feel lucky to be accepted. I just wish I had more time to enjoy the wonderful and free sport facilities. Next time.

title: “Charming Character”
text: Beautiful historic hotel on 6th Street. We stayed in a curio room (servants quarters) very small but charming and comfortable, very tall ceilings. We could not hear the street noise in our room. Very comfortable beds. Nice size bathroom, but no counterspace with it being a pedestal sink. Mini bar and snack bar in room. The hotel bar is very large and beautiful with Texas charm. Valet is $30 a night, should have looked for a spot on the street. 2 nights withe tax and valet was almost $600, very pricey even for the least expensive room.

title: “Close to airport, everything you would want”
text:
This hotel is perfectly situated near to the Seattle airport. The free shuttle is good and the staff were very helpful.
The rooms are well kept, the bathrooms clean and spacious. Everything was as expected, and combined with a Hilton summer sale offer this turned into a stressfree stopover.
Additionally, the restaurant was wonderful and the steaks are highly recommended, although not cheap.

title: “Top quality hotel, great location, comfort, brilliant!”
text: We stayed at the Affinia Dumont from 26/03/09-31/03/09. I spent hours and hours researching hotels in New York before booking as there are so many to choose from and due to the expense of such a trip we wanted to get it right! Well I'm very pleased to say that this hotel was absolutely everything we needed and more. We got a yellow taxi to the hotel from JFK, set price of $45 plus $5 for the toll charge, we were greeted at the hotel by some very friendly door porters who grabbed our suitcases off of us to take to our room number 1504. Check in was quick and very friendly. Our room was massive and clean, big bed, nice bathroom, nice separate kitchen. Maids cleaned the rooms every day, I have to say the maids were so so sweet we loved them, one even collected the shoes and socks I had thrown everywhere and balled up all my socks and put them in rows inside my shoes! (bless). The bed was sooo comfortable and believe me you will need it after all the sightseeing. The location of this hotel was superb. It is on the same street as the Empire State Building and Macy's. Murray Hill is a very nice area, very expensive though but if you're worried about that then seriously dont even think about visiting New York as even the supposed rougher areas are still expensive. The subway is only $2 per trip and this hotel is a great base to get everywhere with easy access to the subway system. The only thing's wrong with this hotel (and this is being very picky) were that the door porters were often too pushy, they were falling over themselves to help you, hail you a taxi etc and you did always feel like you had to keep tipping them, the mini bar was too expensive, and on one day the toilet was making a continual flushing sound, something to do with the ball bit being in the wrong place and easily was fixed. In my opinion these are not good enough complaints to not stay there as overall the hotel was faultless, very plush and spacious, amazing maids, great location. We had a fantastic time!

title: “It's OK......”
text:
I really didn't want to write the rest as everyone else, but most of it is true!
The Location of this hotel is absolutely brilliant, you couldn't be in a more central location, and I have to say this does make up for the shabbiness of the hotel.
We had a queen bedded room which was clean, however the bathroom could have done with a 'proper' clean, instead of just a quick wipe round! I think the dust had been settled there for years, and the corridor carpets looked as though they had never seen a hoover!
The staff at the hotel were ok, not the over friendly american type, but then again this is a City and thats what I was expecting!
Overall a good based hotel, with a great location! Would I go back..... Lets just say I would check other hotels in the same area first before booking this hotel again!

title: “Loved it”
text: I stayed in the Pointe Hilton in Fall 2002. The rooms were comfy, reallly big remembering me rather on suites in other hotels (two rooms). Besides enjoying my stay only because it was phoenix I really spent several evenings at the hotel just chilling and relacxing because of its beauty, tidyness and above average service. And, folks, remember to visit the pointe-view restaurant. It has a terrific, well :-), view over Phoenix.

title: “Very nice urban hotel”
text: Spent Memorial Day w/e here and it was a very nice hotel. Room was large and comforable. Large bathroom and a deep tub and seperate shower. Really nicely and newly decorated from the room, to the halls and the lobby. Easy to get around town. A 6 block walk to the art museum and Millieum park.

title: “The way a hotel ought to be”
text:
That's just it... it's not that there's anything so fancy about the place (except the pool... that is a wonderful luxury!). It's that the Phoenix feels like such a reasonable, comfortable place to be! Friendly, normal people (normal to me-- artists and musicians staff and frequent the place), a nice earthquake-safe-feeling low-profile building, a courtyard with some space to move around, combine to make this heart-of-the-city hotel feel like a small-town, old-fashioned roadside motel. The free parking lot makes getting around San Francisco easy, by just forgetting about the darned car, and walking or taking the Muni. Also, the price for our room was quite reasonable for in-town SF.
 I have only stayed at the Phoenix twice, but highly recommend it. (Actually, i don't know why i would want to promote this place, as it's hard enough to get a reservation-- but not at all times. Be advised... plan ahead... or if you just want to experience the mellow vibe, go at a low-occupancy time and enjoy the pool all by yourself after midnight!)

title: “another great kimpton hotel”
text: we always try to stay in a Kimpton hotel on our travels, the staff were great, I came in on a hot day and the concierge immediately got me ice cold water. I was upgraded to a spacious suite, and as usual the happy hour was very good, and very well attended. My friend had never stayed in a Kimpton Hotel before and is now a convert!

title: “Cockroach in my room!!”
text:
I called up front desk and they sent someone to catch the cockroach. When the guy came in, he said, "wow! that's a huge cockroach!" .. and I agree with him. It really is huge. Probably fed by hotel food, huh? Anyway, the guy caught the cockroach with a face towel (oh gosh! i hope he throws that towel in the garbage!). However, he was careless with the way he handled this pest and so it flew and crawled back to the floor. The guy immediately looks for it and squishes the freaky creature. I heard a crunchy sound, ahh, finally, cockroach is dead. What is a 5 minute ordeal felt like eternity to me.
Anyway, I was here for the JavaOne conference and you expect it to be crowded. They handled check-in and check-out pretty well. They gave me breakfast coupons being a Hilton HHonor gold member (and that includes Free internet).
Rooms are typical. Nothing great really. Size is just about right.
Just don't expect much from this hotel. You are paying for the location.

title: “fancy food winter show sta at the hilton union square”
text: All staff was very friendly, welocing, and helpful. In partiuclar ront Desk staff, and Concierge.. (Especially Concierge, I was trying to get Airport shuttle information, and I was put on hold, the Concierge actually called me back , as my extension must have appeared on his phone)

title: “What more could you ask for?”
text: Quite simply put what more could you ask for. Great location, good coffee in the AM, large rooms with a patio (with our room), comfortable beds, quiet upper eastside street, even a large TV to watch. I could see this room being absolutely great for a family. It was just my husband and I so we had a lot of room to spare. Really liked this place. I'm a New Yorker so I know what I'm talking about:)

title: “The Best for Majestic Theater!”
text: We had a wonderful one-night stay at the Gunter to attend a musical at the Majestic Theater. The hotel is beautiful! Our room was unexpectedly huge and very clean and comfortable. The best thing for us was the location. It is right across the street from the Majestic Theater--we just walked across the street ten minutes before the show started. We can't wait to come back and stay at the Gunter every time we want to see a show!

title: “Not Worth the Price”
text:
While the proximity to Inner Harbor activities is good, the hotel is way overpriced for what you get. We paid over $300 for a "stadium view" room and then had to pay $18 for parking to boot. We had reserved a harbor view room online but were not given one. When we brought this to the attention of the front desk, we were told that their records showed we had reserved a city view room. I rechecked our confirmation when we got home and yes, we did reserve a harbor view room. I called the hotel and our bill was adjusted by a few dollars, but we received no apology.
The vanity top in the bathroom was cracked and the overall appearance of the room was worn. Next time, I'll stay at the Hyatt.

title: “Old school style and close to everything”
text: The Wellington Hotel is a real gem. It retains it's Art Deco elegance but has all the mod-cons to make your stay worthwhile. Proximity to the Park and Broadway, as well as a Subway station directly underneath, makes The Wellington Hotel a great option. It is reasonably priced, and upon arrival in late May, I was upgraded to a Suite with no charge - very impressive and a real treat! Breakfast at the diner located directly off the Lobby makes for an easy location - it's good quality food, nothing too fancy but enough to fuel up for a day's exploring. Overall The Wellington is clean, economic and located in the heart of the City. You could say that the hotel is 'appointed in period-style' but its more likely the old-school bathroom fittings are close to originals, and as someone who appreciates good quality and Art Deco architecture, it all appeals to me. My sister only stays at The Wellington and recommended it to me, and I am happy to recommend it to others.

title: “Like stepping back in time!!!”
text:
I booked the hotel as a surprise venue for proposing to my fiancee whilst in New York.
We were greeted by welcoming staff and they showed us to the room.The room was extremely dated and not what I had expected.I looked over to my fiancée and I could tell she was as dismayed as I was!!.
In fairness to the staff they then offered me two different suites, the final option being the 'Presidents Suite', obviously at a surcharge,but although it was the size of a football pitch,it was again extremely staid and smelt 'musty!'.
We politely declined and retreated to a more 'regular' dwelling.An unexpected beginning to a great time in NYC....and she said Yes....a happy new husband!.

title: “Our NYC Home Away From Home!”
text: This was our 10th annual holiday trip to NYC and our 10th stay with our group at the CP Times Square! The entire staff from the group sales office to the doormen (especially Hector) to the bellmen to the custodial staff to the bartenders are all excellent! Combine that service with a fantastic location and this hotel is THE best choice! We always enjoy our time there and will visit again next year!

title: “Our choice hotel in San Francisco !”
text:
We have to fly half of our company up to San Francisco MANY times per year and are always met with the greatest accommodations at the Clift Hotel. 
The staff always takes care of us and are so nice and helpful. Sometimes, we have to coordinate multiple rooms for different dates and our requests and needs are always met with ease. The rooms are really nice and the hotel itself is central to everything. For being a luxury hotel, I'd have to say the value prices are incredible. It's the only place we stay. 
If you're ever in SF, stay here!

title: “My family loves Palomar Hotel Dupont Circle! Everyone made our stay extremely pleasant and memorable!”
text: I am happy we choose to stay @ Palomar Hotel! My husband, children 8, 10, 11 and I were very comfortable in the two room suite. It was so large they had plenty of room to literally run around in. It was very clean and services were friendly and prompt. Great fitness room, large with many machines and free weights! The little ones ate a good dinner every night so they could order the complimentary milk and cookies @ bedtime. Dupont Circle is a hip, hopping area. There were plenty of restaurants, stores and bars to walk to. We felt very safe walking around @ night, even with the children. Metra is a short walk or a $15ish cab ride took us to the Capital and the vicinity. The complimentary morning coffee bar, afternoon tea and evening wine reception was a nice bonus. July was so hot, it was nice that our hotel was convenient to site seeing. Almost every day the kids enjoyed jumping in the pool to cool off before going back out for dinner. The entire family agreed that the hotel staff went above and beyond our expectations in service and friendliness. Our children wanted stay longer. We stayed @ two more hotels during our vacation through Virginia and even though they are nice, they say "It is not the Palomar!" We would definitely come back or look for Kimpton hotels. I recommend becoming a Kimpton member to get the free internet and raid the mini bar. Also, if you are a fan on facebook you can get the password for a special gift @ check-in. The hotel appeals to many different guests, mix of business people, couples, families, students, pets. Fun to hang out in the lobby and check out the action!!

title: “Excellent Nine Zero”
text: Really enjoyed my stay at the Nine Zero. Great location, beautiful room, very good service. The free wine reception from 5 - 6 each evening was a nice way to wind down and meet some of the other guests. Would recommend a stay here.

title: “Good hotel”
text: We arrived at the hotel at 3 o'clock, the 3 rooms which we had booked were not ready we where told to wait in the lounge and the rooms would be ready in half an hour. The first two rooms were ready in about 1 hour, we were then told the 3rd room would be ready in 15 mins, after 1 hour we had to enquire again and was told the room was ready. We had booked double rooms with time square views, but was told we wolud have to pay $20 per night per room which we paid. The views of time square from the rooms was wonderful and well worth the money. To get the best view for Times saquare you need rooms ending in 03, 04 or 05. The double beds were quite small, the rooms were very clean and the bathroom was small but okay, but anyway you dont come to New York to spend much time in the bedroom. There are 2 lifts which take you from the street to the lobby, and then 4 others which take you to the rooms, the ones to the rooms can sometimes be very busy. We did not eat any food in the hotel so I cant comment on it, the breakfast wolud cost about $20 which is quite high, considering there are many places to eat in the area, the art cafe below the hotel was very good and well priced. This hotel is right on Times square. There are many broadway shows with in easy walking distance, hairspray in right next door. You can pay tickets from ticket booth on 45th street for about half price. We where in New York for 5 days and seen all the sights, and cant wait to go back. This hotel is very good and I would stay in it again when I good back.

title: “AWESOME”
text:
A great place to stay on a budgeted trip to NYC. Very friendly staff, very close to subways, and walking distance from the west side of central Park. 
Getting to the City is very easy by subway. 
The place is great value for money! 
Loved my stay!!

title: “Worst Hotel I've ever stayed at”
text: I left the Tremont hotel angry. This was the worst hotel experience I've ever had in my life. First off, there is only one elevator for the whole hotel, and although it is not a big hotel, it definitely needs more than one. They allow you to take the freight elevator, but avoid it unless you like going in grimey, stinky, small spaces. We were told by the front desk that they can book an architectural river cruise tour and that we will get $10 off the regular price and that when we return, we will get the $10 back. This was a complete lie and management did NOTHING to resolve this issue. The worst about this hotel? The PAPER THIN WALLS. The first 2 nights we were there, we were woken up by the sounds of a woman in the next room making and receiving calls before 8AM. We could hear EVERY SINGLE WORD uttered. The third night was the best though. At 3AM, we were awoken by 2 drunken young girls swearing and laughing about their night out on the town. Of course the daily alarm clark that went off in the same room next to us at 9PM was wonderful too. The staff ignoring our request for them to turn the alarm clock off completely, and not just for that night was of course ignored.

title: “Beautiful Hotel, Friendly Staff”
text: I had the oppportunity to visit Ink 48 the hotel is absolutely beautiful, the roof top bar is breath taking I had such a nice time the price of the drinks are reasonable I just wish they had food on the menu I would defenitely come back again! the staff is very professional I met one of the night managers Peter, He is very helpful, friendly and makes everyone feel welcomed

title: “Great Stay”
text:
The Westin was perfect for our Memphis getaway: a block from Beale street action, a close walk to the South Main area. Our room faced the arena across 3rd street - not directly facing Beale but not facing away either. We had no problems with the noise, staying on a weekend. Service was very attentive. In need of a refrigerator, I cleared about a dozen canned drinks out of the minibar on arrival before realizing they would be charged upon removal. I called customer service, who after chiding me a bit, got back and said the charges were taken off. They sent the maintenance man up with a mini-fridge for our stay, at no charge. Everything was new and clean, though the elevators were getting some interior work done, and one was out on Sunday morning. The conciege service was top notch. Recommended: breakfast in the adjoining Sole restaurant. We went in April, the rate was a great deal. Good time to go, with the May festivals it looks like rates zoom up everywhere.
Tip on nightlife
If Beale Street gets too crowded at night, try the Center for Southern Folklore a block north on Main. Good authentic blues in a coffeehouse atmosphere. And they serve beer too. Barbecue - the ribs at the Rendezvous were the best we found.

title: “Great stay”
text:
Great stay, friendly staff, clean room, and best breakfast I've had. We found a special deal online. The front desk staff even gave us a card for a free appetizer at a nearby restaurant and maps on how to get to the airport. Cookies and butter mints were available at the front desk.
Breakfast was good and real dishes, utensils, and glasses were used.
Everyone was friendly and helpful.

title: “Great Location; Not a bad place”
text: Walking distance to most attractions (5-10 min). NO RESTAURANT but Ample fresh breakfast, plenty for lunch and dinner. Converted bank building makes for some funky room layouts

title: “The true 'Cadillac' of hotels..”
text: I could sum it all up in one word for you... Fantastic!! Everything about this place was great.. The staff were friendly, fun, and knew a heck of alot about the area.. Any questions that I had were answered. The place was clean, well kept, and safe. Location is awesome too.. beach front. Cant ask for more than that if you are an avid beach goer. You've got it all if you stay at this place.

title: “Exceptional service and location”
text: I was able to stay here on business at the end of August and was delighted by the location and the exceptional customer service from the check in to the valet. The beds were incredibly comfortable! I had breakfast in the hotel twice and the service was attentive both days. The quality of the food for me and my traveling companions was of good quality, quick and priced as you would expect a high end hotel. The proximity to the famed 6th street and warehouse district was close enough to walk which ranks high if you plan on having a coule cocktails.

title: “Lovely hotel with a perfect location!”
text:
We stayed for two days in a 6th floor room. The location was perfect for hollywood sightseeing, and if without a car, getting a ticket for the hop on hop off bus is ideal if you want to see further afield.
back to the hotel: checking in was no hassle, and the staff behind the desk were nice and polite, as were the concierges we dealt with. the room itself was lovely, if a little small. As previous guests have said, they arent extremely well lit but we found it ok for the little amount of time we were there. 
we ate at the 25 degrees burger bar for breakfast, and also tried theyre burgers, both were good meals at reasonable prices! we didnt try the formal restaurant as we had reservations elsewhere, but it looked funky. As for the pool, we didnt actually go in it as we just didnt have the time, but went for drinks one night, and there was a playboy party going on! I had read that sometimes they close the pool var to guests when parties are on, but we had no problem walking through the bouncers and sitting at a big table by the pool for cocktails. We actually were sat down next to Bam Margera and family, which was a bit odd!
Overall i would definitely recommend this hotel, moreso for the under 30's. I would not bring kids to this hotel, but for young couples wanting an ideal sightseeing location and trendy digs, it is ideal!

title: “Good Place To Stay”
text:
I am just finishing-up my stay here at the Gaylord and thought I would make a few comments...
My room was nice, and besides the normal noise of the City, I didn't hear any of the so called "construction" noise. Being a traveling nurse, one who sleeps during the day, room noise is very important to me and again, I didn't have any problems.
The staff is nice. It is rare that a place has all genuine people working behind the desk. People who will talk to you as you're picking-up your mail, and take a real interest in you. 
The building is beautiful. Walking into this lobby always brightens me up.
Who's the guitar player? Some guy, a bad version of Seal, sits in front of the building and plays guitar. It's horrible, I wish someone would tell him the truth and tell him to keep his day job.
Overall, I was looking for a nice place at a good value, and in the Gaylord I definetly found it. I'll comeback for certain.
 - Laurie of Norfolk, VA

title: “The W was the prefect hotel for our first time vist to Chicago!”
text: The W's staff were very friendly and helpful, the rooms were comfortable and clean. The style and color was calming. The location was prefect for our downtown visit. Thanks to Eden Bernal for making our trip so wonderful.

title: “Everything Was Fine”
text: I’m puzzled by all the negative reviews, because we had a delightful stay here, with no problems! We had a Jr. Suite (Rm. 219, Bldg. A) & it was great. Everything was pretty much as advertised except there was no breakfast buffet. Contrary to other reviews, we had a microwave, refrigerator, plenty of bath linens, 2 new TV‘s, & there were even complimentary bottles of water in the room. The bed was very comfortable & the pillows were better than the usual motel pillows. Air conditioner worked fine. But just FYI, in case it matters to you, while the toilet & shower/tub combo are in a separate room off the bedroom section, the sink & vanity are in the bedroom with the beds. The only reason I’m not giving this motel 5 stars is because the lighting above the vanity was inadequate for putting makeup on; and the Starbucks morning coffee available in the lobby was $1 a cup. However, the room did have a little coffee maker so you could make your own (but of course that wasn’t Starbucks).

title: “Far West and Deep Downtown”
text: I stayed here for business for two nights. When I arrived at the desk, everyone was friendly and helpful. I thought I was fortunate to be helped by the front desk manager who assured me that I would be in a great room. I guess I should have asked some more questions because this great room on the 7th floor was next to the ice machine. Being a light sleeper, it was not the most ideal location and the noise did wake me up a couple times. However, the room was nice and pretty spacious for a NY city hotel room. It had a modern décor, with only a few minor worn details i.e. the tub looked like it could have used a good bleaching, the desk had a chip in it and the iron had a piece of plastic missing. The room was a little more spacious than my co-worker’s down the hall and had a vanity area in the bathroom. The bed was absolutely delightful, spacious and had very soft comfortable bedding. The lobby of the hotel was a little small, so if looking to hang out with friends it is not the ideal place, but there is a bar and restaurant. Prices in the bar were expensive as expected and two drinks were well over $20. The restaurant on the other hand was pretty moderately priced and the food was decent enough. The bbq sliders were tasty and the calamari was fried a little hard but well seasoned. The hummus was fresh and the salmon sushi roll was as fresh as could be expected for an 11pm meal. The best part of the meal was the sweet potato fries. They were really good and came with an interesting sauce. Though this hotel is located far west, and a little off the path of night life, there were a steady stream of folks walking up and down the street so it felt safe. All in all a good experience.

title: “Pricey, but tolerant”
text:
A couple of my girlfriends and I stayed here for a "girls night" last spring. 
The hotel is nothing out of the ordinary -- decent sized rooms with okay views for a high price. But that is to be expected in this area and it could definitely be worse for the price we paid.
The staff is all super friendly and were receptive to our late night antics :)
Would stay here again if we were in the city. 
One bad thing -- SO hard to find by car! and I even live in the city and had a hard time getting here. Parking is super expensive as well.

title: “Classic hotel - elegant and classy!”
text: From the front desk staff, to the concierge, the bell men, and restaurant staff - everyone seems proud of their role at the Adolphus and you are greeted with friendly and efficient service. The hotel is classic elegance from a more romantic era. The bedding is first rate and comfortable. The marble bathroom is spacious and rich. The Adolphus is a very good hotel experience.

title: “Nice hotel, minor defects”
text:
That's, all in all, a nice hotel, located in good a midtown location (a few blocks from Times Square).
Rooms are spacious, clean and well furnished (the ipod dock station is really nice!)
Some minor annoyances: 
- breakfast is poor, and the breakfast room is too little; I suggest you not to pay for the breakfast, and go to one of the many breakfast places outside
- the elevators are slow (which is a problem, especially around breakfast time, if your room is at the 18th floor)
- acoustic isolation is inadequate 
All in all, I'd suggest this hotel.

title: “Wonderful experience”
text: We stayed at the Silver Cloud Inn on a Saturday night and were very impressed with the cleanliness, service and quality of the room. Our accomodations overlooked Lake Union where we watched float planes take off and others boating. Restaurants are near as is Starbucks! I highly recommend the king suite especially if you're staying a few days. We will stay here again on our next visit.

title: “This place is GREAT!”
text: This hotel is magnificent. The location is GREAT, right in the heart of downtown Boston. The staff was friendly and gave me and my family great reccommendations on how to get around (even though we have been to Boston numerous times). The rooms were very nicely decorated and kept cool, which was nice in the summer heat. I highly reccommend this hotel if you can afford it!

title: “Loved It !!!!!”
text: We were thrilled with this hotel! Yes the rooms are small and no coffee in the rooms but the history and beauty made up for it. Our room overlooked the Alamo and after 7pm the horse and carriages arrived, which we took one evening with a wonderful guide. The front desk staff were extremely polite, since we had a late flight on the day of checkout we asked for an extended stay and were able to leave at 1:30p instead of the normal 12p. We needed extra pillows after our first night and they were delivered while we were out when they cleaned the room. The breakfast buffet was excellent, fresh made waffles and omelets. The location was ideal, 1 block from the riverwalk and in the heart of downtown. We were there for our sons graduation from Lackland and the drive there was very convenient. The pool area and courtyard were stunning, and the bar was very inviting. Check out SaSave for a great price. There is no actual parking for the hotel, however they do offer a valet service for 17.00 a day which we found to be very convenient no waiting for a spot and your car ready when you call ahead can't get much easier than that. The trolleys run late so we didn't even have to drive anywhere except the the air base. Would definitely stay again if we ever return!

title: “Unsanitary”
text:
Dead Rat Found Under My Bed at the Best Western Plaza  6700 S. Main Street Houston, TX 77030 Near Medical Centre.  I don't recommend this Hotel for any patient undergoing Chemotherapy, An Infection can be fatal.   I called the Police to protect My rights but they made Me pay My stay, Including the evening I left the Best Western. My rights where not respected, I caution all foreigners to avoid this Hotel, You will be abused.
 Stayed July 2012

title: “Perfect location, so-so hotel doing the best it can for its age”
text:
The accessibility to the main areas in Chicago is really terrific - at most 15 minutes walk from anything and nearer just a few.
Free wireless internet - good. Gym - small but with half-decent running machines. Staff - helpful but require a more disciplined approach (wrestling with one another in the elevators?). TV in room - very good digital quality. Air conditioning - effective but somewhat noisy. Bed - excellent as all Starwood properties are. Bathroom - adequate but dated, like the rest of the furnishings.
We were on the 8th floor which was relatively quiet (we had no view and the external air conditioners kept a white noise constantly). 
It comes to this - do you want location and relatively inexpensive (we used only 7,000 Starwood points to stay per night) or do you want the 4 star hotel experience like a W or JW Marriott?

title: “Appearances can be deceiving....”
text: I stayed at this hotel with three other guests for a national conference at the convention center accross the street. The location was fabulous...the room not so much. The staff could have been friendlier. They messed up our reservation. We were on pins and needles wondering if they could secure us a room for our last evening. Our room heater was broken. We were given a cheap space heater instead of a different room. Also bathroom was extremely tiny, especially for four women.

title: “A Good Bet for Downtown Charlotte”
text: I spent one night at this hotel on business and was very pleased. The room was exactly what you expect for a Courtyard. The Wifi was free and the breakfast options were excellent. The front desk make an excellent recommendation for dinner, King's Kitchen, and steering us away from all of the national chain restaurants crowding out local places. I would definitely go back.

title: “beware of bogus bill charges”
text: We visited Chicago for the Taste of Chicago over the 4th. When we arrived at the hotel we were pleased with the rooms and found them to be very clean and well kept. The beds were very soft and I found it hard to sleep. The bar in the hotel was nice but over priced. The nacho's were pretty good but don't waste your money on the calamari, I am still not sure if it was calamari. Several people had gotten stuck in an elevator for about an hour and there were elevator issues the weekend so we took the stair most of the time to the 4th floor so that we would not become trapped. The location for the Taste was very bad and that was my friends fault. If you want to spend a lot of time near Grant park or Navy Pier this is not the right Hotel for you. The only major issue was when we went to check out we were charged for room service we did not order. Another man leaving at the same time we were was upset because his bill showed he had rented movies which he states he did not do. So if you decide to stay at this location make sure to check your bill out closely. Also, if you choose this location and like breakfast check out Meli a great breakfast restuarant about two blocks away from the hotel. Its a little spendy but worth it.

title: “Over the top service!”
text:
We are in town for the NAPS convention, and loved this hotel. The staff, food, and amenities were excellent. I left my iPhone charger in the room when we checked out. I did not realize until we got home. Ms. Amanda Sanchez in Security went out and bought us a new charger, and mailed it to our home. That is Over the top service! We will be back next time we are in town. THANK YOU!
Kevin Kalstad
Indiana

title: “Very dated in rooms, public areas stunning, noisy pipes!”
text: The entrance to the hotel made us expect great things as it's beautiful in its design. In the room we stayed in, however, it was totally different. Room itself was a reasonable size with comfortable bed, the room was also clean. No tea or coffee facilities were available in the room which was a little disappointing. Sever lack of anywhere to plug in phone and camera chargers. Iron and board provided, although iron couldn't have reached the board by the time we found a hidden socket. Bathroom very very compact and dated. Light switch only on the mirror as a shaving light but to access this you had to try not to burn yourself on the main waterpipe which was hotter than the sun! At approx 5am each morning the heating pipes starting clanking and banging, this didn't stop until around 9am. The rooms were very dated and in serious need of upgrading, this seemed to be going on in some of the rooms around ours. Breakfast left a lot to be desired, only available via a ticket system in the diner next door. We couldn't order from the main menu, just a limited choice which the hotel obviously set for the price. The main attractions for this hotel are the price and the location. Just 50yds from Times Square from one exit, and directly onto Broadway the other.

title: “Great location!”
text: This hotel is in a wonderful location....very convienient to the metro and lots of great restaurants. We were able to walk to the National Mall (with our 6 year old) and see the monuments and museums with no problem. We would definitely stay here again. The staff is very friendly and helpful.

title: “Nice Hotel, Good Service Except For...”
text:
I was in Dallas for a business trip. The hotel is very nice and clean. The rooms are pretty standard for an above average hotel (comfy bed, nice TV, good desk for working, etc.). The restaurant food is very good and reasonably priced. Internet isn't technically free (For the price you pay on the room, why not?) but if you sign up for their rewards club at no charge, you get free internet.
I only had one problem with my stay. (In hind-sight it wasn't that bad, but in the moment it was very frustrating.) As a member of their rewards club you get free shoe shines. My shoes desperately needed a shine, but I had an important meeting in the morning. I called the front desk, told them my situation, and asked if my shoes would be done in time. They guaranteed me everything would be fine. As you can guess, 30 minutes before I had to leave my shoes had not been returned. I called the front desk and they said my shoes would be returned within 15 minutes. Thirty five minutes later, my shoes came back. I threw them on in the hallway and ran to my car, making my meeting just in time.
I hate for that one event to sour my experience, but it strikes me as a little unprofessional for such a nice hotel. All in all, I would stay at the Omni again.

title: “Great stay in Memphis”
text:
This hotel has a great location although it is a little hard to get to. GPS & hotel website gave wrong directions. Should take r on Monroe, r on Front then R on W court., but hotel had a great decor & was very clean. Room was spacious (2 queen beds) and the breakfast had hot & cold choices, something for 
everyone. Was within walking distance to lots of restaurants. Staff very friendly. Overall a great stay.

title: “Great location for theatre!!”
text:
We booked this hotel specifically to stay close the Goodman Theater. We saw the Christmas Carol at the Goodman and they had a special deal with this property. 
The pool and hot tub were excellent to use after the cold weather while ice-skating. 
The Goodman and other theaters were right outside the ‘back’ door to the hotel. The House of Blues is across the river and Michigan Ave is a short walk away. The south shoreline from South Bend (Randolph and Michigan Ave) is a short walk to this hotel about two blocks.
The buffet breakfast was 20.00, a bit steep considering it was not extraordinary. However, there is a Dunkin Donuts across the street out back. The concierge was very helpful in pointing out alternatives to the hotel dining for breakfast. 
Overall, I would stay here again, especially for plays.

title: “Well, it's a Doubletree. Pay a lot -- get an average stay.”
text:
I know how seriously the DoubleTree likes to take itself. They charge a pretty premium rate for everything from the room to the water bottles inside to the restaurants downstairs. I know they're aiming for the business customer who can expense all of this stuff, but for the casual traveler, it's just not worth it. Way overpriced for what you get.
But beyond that, the rooms are obviously just papered over from an old 1970s-1980s design. The If you look beyond the carpet and the linens, you'll see the old edges of this place showing through.
