The bathrooms are dank and dark and the ceilings (with ceiling tiles!) are low. The place has wooden doors. It's just not modern and it's just overall kind of cruddy, particularly given the price. I stay here often and the heating and cooling systems often don't work so I have to adjust with blankets. 
Staffing is also awful. We frequently have to wait a very long time to check in. Housekeeping almost always walks into my room when I'm trying to sleep, sometimes barely even knocking before bursting in. 
The location isn't so awesome, either, unless you have a deep desire to be near the airport. The nearest light rail stop is a mile walk away under the freeway and past some sketchy street corners.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Monaco 5 nights. Aug 10th to the 15th. I'm happy to report that expectations were exceeded. I compare the feel of the Monaco's public areas and rooms to that you'd expect in a "W" with the service of a Ritz Carlton. We stayed in a Junior Suite which gave us plenty of room to stretch out, the free wireless internet was a bonus, the honor bar was our very own in-room sundry shop. The complimentary morning Starbucks and paper in the lobby lounge and the afternoon wine reception complete with mini-massage and tarot card reader were a special treat. They even provided hot baked cookies at the reception desk at check-in and check-out. The doorman was always there to open the door and hail you a cab to anywhere you needed to go. I felt the value I got for what I spent was worth every dime. Rate paid was $239 per night which included parking and a suite sized room.

title: “Modest Small Hotel near Universal Studios”
text: The BLVD Hotel is in Studio City on Ventura Blvd. It's very close to 101 Freeway and near Universal Studios. Our room faced Ventura Blvd & Freeway so had significant street & freeway noise. Rooms with odd numbers face away from street & freeway. It had nice TV with DirecTV. The king size bed was comfortable. The bathrooms only has a shower, no tub. Our hair dryer didn't work. There is free WiFi in room, but ours was slow and only worked in corner of room. WiFi was available in lobby.There was a party in room next to us till 3 am, and sound carries easily in this hotel. Parking is $15, but some free parking on street in front of hotel. Little bar and breakfast area in lobby (continental). Very small indoor-outdoor pool off of parking lot under hotel. Refrigerator & microwave in room. Coffee in room. People were nice. With air conditioner running street noise not so bad. Modest hotel but clean & comfortable.

title: “Save yourself the hassle...”
text: What a dump. For $30/night, you get smelly roach-infested rooms. Also, this "hotel" has some sort of contract with the government that allows homeless women and their kids to stay there. These women are rough-looking and the children are unruly. The staff is horrible...the skinny black guy with glasses used the "f" word a few times when I asked him he name of the manager. Worst hostel experience EVER!!

title: “Great deal”
text:
This place is a secret treasure. Yes, it is dated. Yes, the funiture in the rooms needs to updated and walls need painting, etc. But... it is two blocks from the mall! That is worth a lot. Also, if you are lucky, you might get a room with a waterview. This hotel is used by tourists or business people.Both classes of visitors are out of the room all day and only need a clean comfortable place to stay. This is it. 
After reading the reviews, I was fearful of what I would find in the room. As it turned out, it was very comfortable. Beds were great. Service was great. Staff were friendly. The American Grill restaurant and the adjoining pub were very nice. 
It is down the street from a new playhouse, Arena Stage which is a fantastic place. The city is beginning to redevelop the waterfront, so waterfront walking may be uncomfortable for the next few years.
I thought the parking price was high, but probably typical of downtown locations. It cost $35 for overnight parking and $45 for valet. There is very limited street parking. The parking height limit is 5'10" which is too low for most SUV's. So,SUV owners are forced to pay for valet parking.

title: “Best Concierge”
text:
I spent two weeks in Dallas for work, and found downtown to be quite... dull. Frustrated, I tried my luck at the concierge's desk. The concierge (Rita Martinez) was very knowledgable and directed me to a bunch of fun places walking distance from the hotel. This made the rest of my stay much more enjoyable.
Thanks Rita!

title: “One of the best Embassy Suites I have stayed at.”
text: My husband and I try to stay in Embassy Suites when traveling. The lady who checked us in was very nice. The room was clean and the bed was comfortable. The Mangers reception was excellent. We ended up not going out for dinner because we had so much to eat and drink at the managers reception. I have not done this since my sister and I were staying at the Embassy Suite in downtown Portland, OR years ago. The breakfast was excellent too. Check out was quick and it a short distance to the airport.

title: “Great location, shame about the hotel”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the hotel for 6 days from 30 Dec - 5th Jan 07. We arrived at 3pm but due to our room requiring cleaning had to wait an hour to checkin. This was because we had requested a room with a King size bed, rather then one with two double beds.
The room itself ( room 502) seemed fine, clean and spacious for a NYC hotel with a large comfortable bed (I'm 6'4), plenty of space for our bags (as well as seeing in the new year we were here to do some serious shopping) and a large bathroom with shower/bath combo. 
The breakfast which was included was suprisingly good, typical NY fair, cereal, porridge, boiled eggs, waffles and vairous bready things as well as plenty of juice and teas/coffee. Although the downside is that it is only open from 7-9am so if you have had a late night or your body clock if having difficulty adjusting you may have problems getting up in time.
The location itself is excellent, the area is known as the Garment district. The hotel is located on 35 West between 7th and 8th (useful to know when your getting a cab) and with 10 mins walf from Times square. There is a subway nearby (which we did'nt use) and Macys literally around the corner.
Now for the downside, on our third night at the hotel we were woken up at 2am after suddendly noticing that the room was getting very cold. After checking the air con controller which we had switched off we could see thaat the vents were still blowing cold air into the room. So we called reception who said someone would be up in a few minutes. 30mins later and my wife and I getting v cold I went down to reception to see what had happened. The employee agreed to have a look at the problem. After fiddling around with it for another half hour he could'nt seem to fix the problem and his only suggestion was that we put the thermostat to blow hot air!!
We insisted that he change our room (by now it was 3am) so he came back with key cards to a room on the floor below and disappeared, not offering to help us move our luggage.
The new room (401) had 2 double beds which were too short for me and due to the 2 beds the room was much less spacious, but the air con seemed to work properly.
The following day when we came back to our room in the early evening we noticed that it had not been cleaned, so we rang reception and after explaining this requested some towels, which did'nt arrive and once again I had to go down to reception and ask for them in person.
On the day before we left I requested a service car to collect us from the hotel and take us to the airport at 4pm the next day. Guess what 4am that morning we get a call saying the car is waiting!! The car which came at the correct time then charged us $69 for the journey which shocked me since two years previously we were charged $45.
Overall as you can probably guess I would not recommend this hotel. The staff although friendly don't provide the level of service I would expect.

title: “Great Location , overall a very good hotel”
text:
My mom and I stayed here over Labor Day weekend. I got a great deal on Expedia. Comfy beds and pillows! I wish I remembered her name but the girl in the cocktail was excellent. It was great that across the street there was a little store that had liqour and had great breakfast sandwhiches. At the advice of others on TA i asked for a room away from the train and that's what I was given. 
A couple of little things. No mini bar in the rooms....not that big of a deal. Parking is $35 a night but you really don't need a car unless you venture outside of the area. It would have been nice if breakfast was included but I can't complain since I got such a great deal on the room.

title: “Wish I had read the reviews - Shabby, worn out and cramped”
text:
Stayed here for three nights with 2 adults and 2 kids 8 and 12. Will not stay here again. The location was good but the place is worn out. We had non-smoking room but right outside the door is an ashtray and an area where smoke comes in through the inefficient window air conditiioners. The room is cramped small and dingy. The grounds are nice, parking spaces too small to escape dings.
Continental breakfast was so-so but no real expectation there. The suite had bunkbeds which were not made up prior to our checking in. The mattress pads, spreads and blankets were nasty! Towels always felt like they had sand in them. Fan in bathroom does not work efficiently, luckily there is bathroom window to let shower steam out. The airconditioner is horrible. The fan between two rooms does not do adequate job. Drapes have stains and are nasty. I guess they figure if you have kids you don't mind but we don't live that way and certainly don't expect to when we are spending hard earned money! The refrigerator was a decent surprise and a convenient one, however the rest of the room made a Motel Six (no offense - to Motel Six) look like a resort. The mattress on the king bed was broken down and the bedding was horrible. You had to remake the bed in the middle of the night to keep from having the bare mattress underneath you. The room had corners where it was apparent a vacumn never touched, dirty windows, peeling wallpaper, etc etc. 
Location was only positive. Pool area was ok and kept up. I have stayed at a lot of Comfort Inns but this one will not receive a return visit. When checking out talked to desk clerk about stuff and he didn't bother to write down just looked bored and said thank you for telling him. Even when we brought up fact that in the bathroom we kept finding an article of clothing that did not belong to any of us. Left note for maid about same, no response.

title: “Just Okay”
text:
The friendly staff, attentive bellmen, and great location unfortunately can't overcome the slightly bedraggled state of the hotel and rooms, rendering my vote for the place as simply average. All in all, everything is a bit shabby. I've stayed at the Warwick down the street and much prefer it to the Latham.
Positives - They let us check in a bit earlier than the 3pm check-in, which was much appreciated after some weary travel. The room had some beautiful old furniture and marble bathroom, but it all looked a bit knocked around on the edges. The room was nicely stocked with Philadelphia travel mags and the key holder had a very handy city map. Amenities included a coffee pot, iron, ironing board, hairdryer, etc.
Negatives - We were in a non-smoking room that smelled like smoke and had a few cigarette burns in the carpet to boot. Carpeting also had a stain. Bathroom was rather dirty (hair in the corners). The television had a line running through the picture and anything on a scroll along the bottom was nearly illegible. The location on 17th street made for some noisy nights from honking horns. The bed was squeaky, although comfortable enough.

title: “Good Hotel that could improve in a few areas”
text:
Spent 4 nights at the Hilton for a conference. I had a very comfortable experience. My room was perhaps a bit smaller than other hotels in the same price bracket, but it was well appointed nonetheless. I really enjoyed the nice quiet room and was able to get a great nights sleep. 
Pros:
Good water pressure in the shower
Clean room, comfortable bed and nice amenities in the room
The hotel has everything you would possibly need. Some nights I didn't want to leave the hotel after a long day. Plenty of food and drinks to select onsite.
Cons(All related to food service):
I ordered a couple room service items on different nights. While the club sandwich was good and flavorful, the pannini looked like it was done on wonder bread and not a higher quality roll or other product. Really disappointing.
My other complaint was the main bar service the first few nights. Granted the Hotel was busy, but the wait staff was way, way understaffed for the size of the crowd. I even noticed a manger standing in the corner for a while with his hands on his hips. Really? Go help your crew get the drinks out! We left both nights and went across the street.
I can say I did stop in the bar my last night and had a good experience. It wasn't busy and the bartenders did a nice job putting together drinks in a friendly manner.
Finally, I did have breakfast one morning in the restaurant. While the omelet was good, I felt like the potatoes came off the buffet line. I expect more when you order off the menu and don't want cold taters on my plate. 
I will stay at this hotel again. For sure. Just tighten up the food service end a bit and you will gain my full 5 stars.

title: “Error in our Bookin”
text: I had booked 2 queen rooms (for 2 couples) for 2 nigths... When we arrived to the hotel they tell us that there was an error and the only solution could be to share a room with 2 queen beds. We had a bad night and they didn't compensate with anything. After this bad experience, the next night we had a beautiful room with sights to Empire State. The Breakfast was fantastic and all very clean. I could repeat but I would call before to be sure that my book is correct

title: “Good value; you get what you pay for.”
text:
I found this hotel to be clean and efficient. Excellent location. My room was on the small side , but not uncomfortably so, and had been recently modernised. Bed was soft but very comfortable. 37" flat-screen HD TV (but all channels analogue!?). Modern bathroom fittings, but little else in the way of ammenities. In short; Servicible, clean and comfortable. Mine was on the 28th floor so the view was great. 
I have seen some reviews complain of noise from the rennovation work. I found it very quiet, though the rumble of traffic was discernable even from the 28th floor. Closer to the ground the rooms must be noisier.
Some reviewers had trouble with long queues for check-in/long waits for lifts. I experienced neither of these; never had to wait more than a minute for a lift and it usually appeared in seconds; check-in took about 3 minutes and check-out is just drop key in a box (if you don't have to settle a bill).
My one gripe is the 15 dollars a day charge for use of wi-fi. This seems to be quite standard in NY hotels, but I refuse to pay that. Use free wi-fi zones instead; plenty of bars restaurants have them.
In short; for the price I felt I got excellent value and my stay was comfortable. I would happily syat there If in New York again, though I would probably go somewhere in a different part of town for the new experience..

title: “Cool structure, not within walking distance to anything”
text:
Nice hotel. Great for business travel. On the grounds of the airport. The restaurant staff was very friendly. The food was decent. I usually don't eat in hotels, but it was late and the hotel is not close to anything worth staying up late. 
If you are into architecture, the hotel is interesting. It's shaped like a donut with a large skylight at the top. The walls are thin, but aren't they all? I'd stay there again, but I'd make sure to schedule time to get into the city to eat.

title: “Fantastic Girls Weekend”
text: We were a group of 4 women, 3 coming from Toronto and 1 from Victoria. The 3 of us checked in Friday June 29 a little past midnight with absolutely no issues. Slyvia was at the Front desk and she was incredible.We checked in and went to our room, we were in a room in the low 30's. We had a great view of the river, comfortable beds. The next morning we were meeting the other woman from Victoria and checking into a different room. We asked Slyvia if she could put us higher and with a different view. She put us on the top floor (38) and the view was on the city, empire state, chrysler building and the river. beds were comfortable, big screen tv, bathroom was clean. The hotel IS UNDER GOING RENOVATIONS! so one tower is completely closed, so within some time this hotel will be a modern gem. It was an absolutely safe hotel. The UN diplomats offices are under the hotel and there is always a K9 dog outside sniffing bags. Very friendly dogs! the bellmen were vert gracious and always able to lend a hand. Stephanie at the concerige was also great as well with setting up my aunts shuttle to airport. Overall this hotel is of great value and will def be going back, any questions just message me!

title: “BEST TRIP”
text: Thank you so very much for all of your hospitality! Our stay was amazing! Your hotel is beautiful! We enjoyed staying there. The king bed was so comfortable and the room was great with the view of the Gaslamp area. Thank you for the "special" touches of cookies, strawberries, milk, and the sweet note you wrote. Also, each person on your staff was so friendly and helpful. My mom had the BEST time! Thank you for giving her this amazing experience. She wanted to extend our stay!! I look forward to hopefully seeing you again some day.

title: “Excellent Service and beautiful grounds”
text:
I stayed here for a 3 day conference. Upon check-in our rooms were not ready but the clerk was very nice and helpful to acccomodate our needs. Every hotel employee goes above and beyond to help you when you need something. 
The rooms are very large but the furniture is very dated and looks small. There are not very many outlets for the growing technology that guests bring into a room these days. 
I do like where the hotel is located because it is very close to shops and easy access to the highway to go downtown to 6th street. I had a rental car so it was a quick trip for me.

title: “A Wonderful Stay in DC”
text: We traveled to DC to meet with our Congressman and were fortunate enough to stay at the Willard. From the valet to the front desk we encountered friendly, professional staff. The hotel lobby is beautiful and the rooms were plush, clean and spacious. We ate breakfast in the Cafe du Parc and enjoyed a French buffet that filled us up for a day of touring. When in DC I can't imagine staying anywhere else!

title: “Fabulous Bed!!!”
text:
A bed is the most important feature in a hotel for me. The bed at this hotel is awesome and brings the overall experience at the Gaslamp Hilton to the next level. The sheets are 100% cotton (feels like at least 300 thread) and the down comforter is covered (wrapped) between two sheets. Therefore, there is a clean, soft cotton sheet on the top of the comforter too, so you never have to touch any part of the bed that isn't brand new clean for you! The bed is a pillow-top and the mattress pad also has a pillow-top. Finally, there are five down pillows on a king size bed.
The location of the hotel is great. We had dinner and drinks in the lively Gaslamp quarter; we walked to and from dinner and the bars. Petco Park is about 3 blocks away and we almost made it to a game. The area is very alive when the Padres are in town; also, with at least three universities around, the spring break night life was vibrant. The Gaslamp entertains a predominately young crowd, but we never felt out of place there. Every morning we ran down to the harbor from the Hilton and there is so much activity along the marina, with many shops and restauants. Again this area is not even a mile from the Hilton.
The service at the Gaslamp Hilton was perfect. The staff was helpful with giving directions and gave great advice about restaurants and places to go. We had a great dinner at the Strip Club (steak house, not girls), and a wonderful breakfast at Club 222, both in the Gaslamp.
I would definitely stay here again, but I would ask for a room far far far away from the train; I didn't think it would bother me, but it did. And, I will try to avoid the $30 per 24 hour garage, which we couldn't avoid one day. 
We have two children and would stay elsewhere with them, probably a resort style hotel in Mission Bay, but for my husband and I this was perfect and I toured a couple other 4 star hotels at the beach and the Hotel Del too.
*Go on a Seal Tour, similar to Boston's Duck Tour: amphibious boat tour that lasts about one and a half hours, and takes you through downtown into the San Diego bay.

title: “Great for the price”
text: Located very close to SoCo, 6th street, and downtown. It's a great place to stay for the price and convenience.

title: “If money is no object....”
text:
If money is no object then you should be satisfied with this hotel.
The check in staff seemed to be friendly until they realized I had booked with Priceline, then I was treated as a 2nd class customer.
The room wasn't cheap even through Priceline, then they charge extra for internet 15.00 usd which is pretty much necessary when you are traveling.
They charged another 17.00 usd for parking per day!!
Then I messed up I called a local number who put me on hold..... LOCAL CALLS ARE NOT FREE!
The staff is quite busy and hard to talk to at the front desk.
Now the good part is that the bed was the softest and the sheets were crisp and clean, there was a bit of airport noise all night which surprised me in such a high priced place.
The halls were noisy too, with people coming and going and doors closing.
There is NO BUSINESS CENTER and with no free internet.... very inconveinient indeed.
The rooms are built on pods and there are steps to the parking lot which are almost too steep, BE CAREFUL!!!
All-in-all, you better hang onto your wallet, they seem to be good at getting every penny they can out of you, I only stayed 1 night or they might have gotten more!!

title: “Very cool place”
text: We stayed for one night at the Liberty. Upon arrival we were offered a glass of champagne (sparking wine) while checking in. The room was beautiful and the interior of the hotel very unique. Loved that it was once a jail. Molton Brown furnishes the toiletries which is nice. Bed was comfy and they had a turn down service. Water bottles furnished in the rooms. In the AM they had a self serve coffee bar in the lobby with great coffee! When they brought our car to us after valet they had left two water bottles for us. I think they were very detailed oriented and it is a fantastic location. In the morning walk down Charles street for a fantastic "locals" breakfast at the Paramount, great food at amazing prices.

title: “Location Location Location”
text: This is a great location to see and do all the typical tourist things in San Francisco.The access to the cable car line a few blocks away lets you explore and experience more than just the pier area.As other reviews have stated the garbage trucks do wake you up at 5:30, but that just gets you up and going to be able to enjoy more of what the area has to offer.

title: “Great place to stay, even in October”
text: We had a wonderful night in Venice Beach Hotel with the seawind over our bed. It actually was a real suite; nice to have a little kitchen to make your own breakfast. Eventhough it was autumn and rather cold, it was great to dive into the Pacific and immediately take a warm shower. The location is perfect, parking advice in the area was a good one. Staff was very friendly and restaurants on walking distance very good. Loved to stay here! We will surely come back (if ever we return to Venice Beach).

title: “Great staff, but we felt a little ripped off”
text:
The hotel itself is beautiful. The room was spacious and clean. The staff is 5 star all the way. One of the doormen (I think his name was Michael) stood out as exceptional. He went out of his way to be courteous and helpful. The Cellar Bar, and the Happy Hour special was also a very high point of the stay. The bartenders were great, and the vibe of the room is top notch.
The reason I can't give the place 5 stars (and almost gave it 3) is very simple. We booked the room several days in advance and paid a substantial price for a junior suite. There was no discount on the room. The hotel did not inform us that they were doing construction at Bryant Park on the skating rink across the street steps from the hotel TWENTY FOUR HOURS PER DAY for the entire 3 days we were there. It made it impossible to have a restful night of sleep for the entire trip, as the construction was extremely loud and went on all night long, which was quite surprising. We were awakened regularly throughout each night of the stay by very loud shouting, clanging and banging. I would think a fair move by the hotel would be either to sharply discount the rooms during this construction period or to at least warn customers at the time of booking so that the customer could make an informed decision. I felt like it was sheisty of the hotel not to mention this very significant issue or to account for it in the price of the room.
It's a shame that this was a significant black mark on an otherwise perfect experience. As evidenced by the 4 star rating I still gave the hotel I am not one who likes to trash businesses or to be one of those nerds who complains about everything. However, I did feel it necessary to make this known in the text of the review without completely trashing the hotel in the star rating process.

title: “Great Hise Rise Hotel Downtown Seattle”
text: Great location, upscale romm and amenities, and a reasonable $130 night price through Priceline. The concierge was very nice and helpful to find a good restaurant on the harbor. The Space Needle was not the thing to do the day of boarding the cruise though; we were just a bit dizzy from the ride up & down.

title: “Not bad”
text: Just stayed one night at Hilton Times Square. The rooms are nice, comfortable bed etc. However, I would like to warn you that the hotel is located in one of the busiest street of NY, so it is quite noisy. In addition, I think the breakfast buffet is below 4 star standards and the service (especially concierge) could be better.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: Staff is very friendly and accomdating. Breakfast is very good. I travel often to San Antonio and this is my favorite hotel. They have a bar so I can have a drink in the evening. Nice pool. Beautiful atrium. Very comfortable.

title: “Best, most relaxing home away from home ever”
text: Excellent suites, pool open until midnight! Free build-your-own-omelet breakfast and manager's reception!

title: “Great weekend in DC! Modern Hotel, friendly staff!”
text: Stayed at this hotel over the weekend. Very clean hotel, modern interior with a cool swanky lobby. Walking distance to most monuments. The hotel bar/restaurant was very modern (Bill and Emilio of the bar good guys, gave us some knowledge of where to go at night). Happy Hour with Kimpton from 5pm-6pm in the Lobby was nice with free wine and beer. Rooms are very modern with platform bed; however not lit so well. They should add more lighting near the closets. Bathroom has a modern cylindar shower that sticks out into the room with frosted glass for privacy. Great street view from most all rooms as well.

title: “Loved the Hudson, great place to stay in NY!”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed at the Hudson in January and we both found it to be a great hotel. We had read several reviews referring to small cramped rooms and unfriendly staff, but found this simply not to be the case.
Yes the rooms are small but how much time are you spending in your hotel room while in New york?!! We upgraded the room to a superior and had more than enough room to put our luggage and shopping. I am over 6ft and didn't find the rooms to be that much trouble. The coridoors are dark, but consistent with the rest of the hotel and we did not find them 'dangerous' or 'ridiculous' as previous people have referred to them as.
As for the staff, checking in and out was seamless and they were more than happy to help us out at any time, even booking us restaurant reservations and giving out some valuable tourist information.
If you're looking for a cool hotel located right next to the park and within easy reach of Times Square and 5th Avenue, then this is the place. The older generation might struggle to get to grips with the low lights and funky bars, but then again, it wasn't designed for the over 50's... no offence!!
All in all, its a great place to spend a few days in NYC, while the bars and restaurants in the hotel may be pricey as you'd probably expect it to be ($9 for a bottle of Corona....hmmmmm!!) Its just as easy to pick out some nice restaurants and bars locally and breakfast round the corner in Flames was a great place to go in the mornings.
Recommended for young couples and groups of mates looking for a bit of a treat of a stay in a great city.

title: “Tranquil retreat”
text: We just returned from a long weekend at The Houstonian. This was our first visit and the hotel more than lived up to our expectations. The setting is lovely, a wooded retreat just minutes from the bustle of Houston and its freeways! The hotel is beautiful, large well appointed rooms and the staff is extremely friendly and helpful. As we were visiting my son and his family, the pool was the highlight of the weekend. Actually, I should have said pools as there are three. The three year old and even the baby loved "swimming" and this area was very family friendly. While I did not use the services, the spa and workout facilities looked first rate. Food and service in the restaurant, Olivette, were all so top quality. We will definitely make this our Houston base of operations in the future.

title: “Let's be Frank”
text:
Hotel Frank was a disappointment. Went here for a romantic getaway and was let down by the lack of romantic details, a little dingy and way overpriced!
Meh!

title: “Great location, fun hotel”
text:
I stayed here for 4 nights on business and found it to be a great location for getting around Seattle, both for meetings during the day and then for a little bit of sightseeing in the evenings. It's 2-3 quick blocks from the University St. station on the new light rail (and bus tunnel), diagonally across the street from Rem Koolhaas' beautiful public library building, and within 5-10 minutes' walk of major downtown sites like the Pike Place Market, Convention Center, waterfront, and ferry terminal.
Rooms are decorated in that funky Kimpton style that you will either love or hate. Personally, I thought the decor was fun (leopard-print bathrobes!) and my room, though not huge, was more than adequate and very clean. It was also nice and cool despite the heat wave in Seattle at that time. I heard very little noise from the street below and the curtains actually closed all the way so that I could keep out unwanted light.
Check-in and check-out were both easy, and on arrival I found a little "welcome" note from the staff in the room, along with a bottle of spring water and a bag of sweets from a local chocolate company - a nice touch.
Breakfast at Sazerac was delicious and the staff were very friendly and efficient. There are some nice little touches like fancy trays of jam & butter to go with your croissant and interesting Asian-style teapots. It would have been helpful if they opened earlier than 7 am; each day I had to sit down as soon as they opened in order to have time to eat before my meetings.
My only quibbles with the hotel were (1) they are not yet 100% non-smoking, and this was not obvious on their website; it might be worth calling them to confirm that you will have a non-smoking room, and (2) the hotel staff were not terribly knowledgeable about the downtown area when I asked for directions. But these are pretty minor complaints compared to the otherwise pleasant experience. I would be inclined to stay here again on my next trip to Seattle, whether on business or on vacation.

title: “Austin digs”
text:
This was my second stay at the Driskill Hotel and not much has changed. The rooms are clean, spacious and comfortable and overall the hotel staff were friendly and attentive. 
The service at the 1886 Cafe was a bit slow at times but the food was good. The food and service at the Driskill bar were good. The only issue I had with my stay was an erroneous in-room bar charge for $20 somthing dollars. The front desk staff member corrected it with no problem but I would highly recommend going over your final bill with a fine tooth comb.

title: “First time in NYC!”
text: I must say that I traveled to New York last week for the first time. I enjoyed every bit of it that I want to go back again! I was able to check in early and they were nice enough to hold my suitcase for me while I toured the town until my official check in time. I find this hotel convenient to the subway. There is Starbucks right across the street which was really nice since I'm a coffee drinker! I traveled by myself and was able to get a double bed! It was nice because I was on the 20th floor and the view was ok....seeing rooftops and other buildings. I didn't feel like I was in a hotel though. I felt like I was in a penthouse. The bed was very comfortable. I have no complaints. The only thing is that the shower stall curtain is short. So that means when you take a shower, water still ends up on the floor. I didn't mind because the housekeeper gave me plenty of bath towels and I used that to clean up the water. I will definitely return again!

title: “Great Location, Hotel what we paid for”
text:
Me and my partner have just returned from a four night stay in NY and had an excellent time.
Check In was fine, no problems, no queue. We were given a room on the 8th floor, had a view looking over 57th Street. Room was quite large, we had 2 double beds. Bathroom was clean and had what we needed. The room was a standard 3 Star and the hotel isnt pretending to be anymore than this. I was a bit weary before i went with reading some of the reviews but i know i paid for a 3star and that is what i got. The rooms were spacious and clean and really that is all we needed. Only complaint was some noisy guests coming in at all hours but that was no fault of the hotels. Didnt sample any of the food in the hotel so cant comment on that but the room service prices are expensive. Location was fab, walking distance of central park and times square. We got a taxi to battery park to get the ferry for statue of liberty and this only cost $15 which we thought was ok for the other side of manhattan. We landed into Newark airport and the taxi fare was $56 plus $10 toll fare plus tip so it worked out about $70, but returning the hotel arranged a shuttle transfer for us and this cost $24 per person (cheaper to JFK) so this was quite good.
Overall, for the price and location this is perfect for anyone just wanting a bed for the night and wanting a base to explore new york!!!

title: “Terrible experience!”
text: The front desk clerk was rude. My room that I reserved was not available when we got to town. We asked for a king room and we had to take a double instead. The clerk wasn't even at the front desk when we got there. We had to wait over ten minutes before anyone came to the front desk. The clerk told us if we did not want the room that she had left that we could go somewhere else! Our toilet leaked water all over the bathroom floor every time you flushed itt and the lighting over the sink did not work. If I wasn't pressed for time when I arrived I would have done just what the clerk said and went somewhere else!

title: “ARE YOU SERIOUS?!?!”
text:
long story short... four people checked into the room. Hotel was clean but eerie. Dimmed Hallways, dim lights in the room. Our stay was going to be 4 days long. There was only two sets of towels in the room. We used one for our hands and the other for the floor since it would be slippery coming out of the shower. We call down to get more towels. We were told "No, you cannot have 5 more towels!!" 
We told him the situation and he sent up 3 towels. What was he thinking...that the four of us would share towels? Crazy customer service. We asked for 5 because sometimes we use the extra towel for our hair.
We checked out that morning.

title: “The nicest La Quinta ever”
text: This was by far the nicest La Quinta Inn I have ever been to. I was shocked when I walked in, very contemporary upscale lobby. Nice hot breakfast with scrambled eggs, bacon, sausage and biscuits and gravy. The staff was very welcoming and acted like they were truly glad I was there. They even serve a light dinner with beer and wine Monday - thursday.

title: “Great Service!”
text:
I happened to stay at the Sheraton a couple of weeks ago, whilst attending a Convention in Philadelphia. It's a comfortable, well-priced hotel which is situated quite close to the Convention Centre.
It has a very good seafood restaurant, Philip's, and a pleasant bar area where light meals are served. My room was also comfortable.
One of the highlights was the service I received from a lady at the Concierge - unfortunately, I don't have her name, but she is a slightly-built, dark-haired lady with glasses. She went out of her way to point me in the right direction on several occasions, and she made some great recommendations of restaurants, things to do etc; nothing was too much trouble. Service like this needs to be recognised in my opinion.

title: “Home Away From Home”
text:
We loved our stay at Inn at Union Square. The room was quiet and comfortable. The front desk staff was variable. Some restaurant recommendations by the front desk were awful. Please note: Ann at reception is a gem. Some of the beds are more comfortable than others. They tend to be a little soft. There is no A/C. A recommendation I would make to management is to vary the wine and cheese selection at happy hour and offer higher quality breakfast ingredients (cage free, FRESH eggs, better pastries, soy milk, e.g.)
Also the telephones are outdated and need to be replaced.
Still, I would recommend this hotel and would return there.

title: “Great location, fantastic staff”
text:
We picked this hotel from the many in San Francisco based entirely on the Tripadvisor reviews and were very pleased we did. For a family of four (daughter aged 17 and son aged 14), the two bedroom suite was the perfect choice, as it afforded us sufficient space for a four night stay without us getting on top of each other (daughter bagged one of the bedrooms, son slept on the sofa bed in the huge living room).
Breakfast buffet was light but exactly what was needed; the two fire-pit terraces were largely unused, and a great place to chill (literally, it was summer in San Francisco, after all) with a bottle of wine, bought from the liquor store across the street, as there is no bar in the hotel.
The front desk staff were extremely helpful, and managed to make restaurant and theatre bookings for us at the times we wanted; the free first-come first-served limo service within a two mile radius of the hotel was also very useful, although its cut-off time of 10:30pm meant that on a couple of occasions we had to look for buses or taxis - not the easiest matter in certain parts of the city, but all part of the fun.
The location, just off Fisherman's Wharf, was ideal - Blazing Saddles (bike hire for the Golden Gate trip) just around the corner and Pier 39 for Alcatraz a couple of stops away on the tram.
Expensive - yes, but all things considered, value for money.

title: “If you want to stay here, get a suite!”
text:
I just wanted to add my two cents. My wife and I purchased three nights at the Drisco from one of the luxury deal Web sites and stayed there in late October-early November of 2004. We had a suite with an unobstructed view looking southward -- nothing particularly spectacular, but still quite nice in that it gave the room a very airy feel. And the room itself was drop-dead gorgeous, just like the photos they publish on the Web site. It was very clean (and the hotel cleaning staff were very nice too), and we felt quite taken care of there. The breakfast was wonderful, probably the epitome of "continental breakfast" -- everything was fresh, and the atmosphere was first-rate. The front desk staff was a little hit or miss -- sometimes imperious, other times very accommodating -- but that was a minor quibble. It was so nice to be away from the downtown noise; the early morning hours there were downright serene. As another reviewer mentioned, parking is hard to find, but it's not impossible.
One thing I'm picking up from all the other reviews -- if you're going to stay here, you probably need to get a suite. There are a few horror stories among the reviews, and it seems like all these bad stories come from those who didn't have a suite.
If we can afford it or find another deal, we'll definitely be staying at the Drisco the next time we go to San Francisco. The hotel itself was one of the high points of our trip.

title: “Accommodating and gracious; fabulous location!”
text:
The Georgetown suites may look in pictures like a behemoth of a hotel, but upon entering via the entrance's sweet, brick courtyard, you wonder if you aren't going to stay at a large cozy house. Very well done!
Once inside, true, it's more like a Holiday Inn -- not much character to the check-in desk, or the too-big silk flower arrangement at the entrance; but the people are warm and very accommodating. I came for a one-day jaunt to the Smithsonian and did not arrive until 1:00 a.m. (do call the hotel ahead to let them know, even if you put that in your comments at hotels.com.) The clerk at the desk was very accommodating and helpful.
When I finally got to my room, I could hear the traffic from the highway and knew I wouldn't be able to sleep on account of it. Immediately I called reception, and in less than 5 minutes the clerk returned my call and gave me an opportunity to take another room, this time on the first floor. He asked if that would bother me, and it didn't. I appreciated the opportunity to change (and to have a choice).
It's important to note that the room included a kitchenette -- full refrigerator, dishwasher, stove, toaster, small breakfast table; and desk with lamp, an easy chair (which swiveled, rather annoyingly, but some people would prefer that) and a decent-size bath (full, with tub and shower). A nice large closet included two spa bathrobes, which one could purchase for $75 each. You could stay here comfortably for a week or two or longer, given the huge fridge and full-size dishwasher. My room was plenty big for a couple and even a small child, too.
The bed was too soft for my taste (again, some would prefer its softness), but the room was absolutely spotless. It felt welcoming and fresh.
This hotel is reasonably priced and extremely convenient to the main street in Georgetown -- only 1 block away. On the same street were rowhouses from perhaps the early 1800s. Federal, quaint architecture, antique stores, boutiques, and interesting places to dine were a mere block away. It would be a great choice for parents visiting students, or students visiting their friends at Georgetown. It's not posh or polished, but rather simple and clean; and the people are lovely. I'll take that any day over a stiff white-gloved approach.
The location was a 20-minutes' drive via cab from the train station (with no traffic, that is), and a quick 10-15 min. walk to the Foggy Bottom Metro stop.
Would definitely book there again, but this time, I would ask specifically for a room that didn't face the highway.

title: “Night event at Ultimate Ransom - Zaza Hotel”
text: I had my night event at the Ultimate Ransom - Zaza Hotel, Houston, Texas last March 22, 2012 at 6:30 PM. The event was very successful partly due to the well coordinated effort of Mr. Kleibert Estrada. The food was delicious. The whole set up was so awesome. The room was not only sophiscated but at the same time had that cozy feeling. Juan, the maitre'd was so professional and accommodating. The guests were so pleased with the presentation. I will definitely have my event at Zaza Hotel next year.

title: “New Year's eve in NYC”
text:
the location is as good as you can get in NY, between the 53rd and 6th. The room and the bed were small compared to the standards in USA, it was anyhow quite clean, quiet and enough comfortable.
The staff was helpful and the concierge helped us book a restaurant on new year's eve very last minute. The hall was often too crowded and too many people sitting on the floor connecting to the internet: this made it look like a train station.
We did not try any of the restaurants.

title: “Spectacular views - but hotel needs to be updated”
text: The hotel is in a great central location (on top of the Sun Times building) - next to Merchandise Mart and walking distance from both the L and Michigan Avenue. The service was friendly and the hotel bar overlooks the river. The rooms have great sweeping views of the both the river and the skyline. It was spatious and well equipped with a desk and outlets to recharge laptops/phones etc. The only drawback is that the bathroom desparately needs an update, as does the furniture in the room. Apart from that, it was a great place to stay.

title: “Functional, Friendly and a little bit Funky”
text:
This hotel is in a great location, yes it can be a little bit noisy at times, we were there during the Harry Potter frenzy, but the upside was I had a great view of the red carpet from my hotel window!
Just a short walk away from Central Park, great if you fancy hiring a bike and cycling around the city.
The interior was very modern and funky in design, the room was average sized and had a really comfortable bed.
We didn't eat there but we did eat at Ed's Chowder restaurant next door, which was excellent!
The pool on the roof is small (not surprisingly) and it had a cover over it, which spoilt it a little, however great location to have a cocktail and watch the sun set over Manhattan.

title: “Couldn't be better!”
text: We stayed at the Conrad for two nights when we came to town for a basketball game, using my husband's HHonors points. The hotel is beautiful! The bed was super comfortable, and the bathroom was great with a big soaking tub and a TV. Nice big TV in the bedroom. The indoor pool was maybe the nicest I have seen, and the gym was great. We especially liked the evening turn-down service. The location cannot be beat - you walk out the door and in all directions are tons of bars and restaurants (Champp's, Rock Bottom, Weber Grill, Buca di Beppo, Palamino, PF Chang's, Morton's, just to name a couple) Easy walking distance to Conseco Fieldhouse. The hotel is connected to the Circle Centre Mall so you don't even need to go outside if you don't want to. Valet parking is a bit steep at $33/night, but whatever - we'll definitely be back when we return to Indianapolis.

title: “Great find in New York”
text: I have just come back from a 4 nights stay at Hilton Garden Inn at Times Square. It is a very well priced hotel considering all that it offers. Having a microwave and fridge in the room was wonderful. The business centre which gives free internet access is also a big plus. The bedroom was spacious and, although a bit on the small side, the bathroom was fine. I found the staff very helpful and pleasant. I was on the 3rd floor and I could vaguely hear the subway noise occasionally but it certainly did not disturb me in any way. I had never stayed in the Times Square area before and was a bit hesitant about it being so crowded. This is really not a concern and it is a real buzz to know that all the great shows and jazz clubs are within a 5-10 minute walk from the hotel. Anyway, I would recommend this hotel wholeheartedly for anyone wanting a comfortable, safe stay in New York city.

title: “Great Place!”
text: I have stayed in many motel 6's but this one was awesome- wow, must have been recently remodeled. Beautiful interior, nicely decorated and quiet despite the fact that it is large and was completely booked. I look forward to staying here again the next time I am in the El Paso airport area.

title: “Conference Hotel”
text:
We stayed at this property during a VERY busy conference.
Due to an 18-hour flight delay from London, we missed night one of our booking. We did manage to cancel the first night after a frantic phone call from Heathrow and assumed we would also lose our Diamond suite-upgrade.
Indeed, they had no record of our suite upgrade request (despite it being confirmed twice in the previous month). They finally admitted it was their error as they had not read the electronic notes properly and offered us additional points for the inconvenience.
We had a fantastic view in the West Tower on the 35th floor, while not a suite, the room was okay. My complaints about the room were mainly design ones – 
- insufficient drawers for clothes
- not enough space in the bathroom to lay out things
- water pressure could have been a little better
- my partner hated the sink design 
- no fridge
- And for a full-service hotel, there were limited choices of channels on the TV.
The bed was very comfortable and we slept well.
Thankfully, we were just around the corner from the Exec lounge, which served continental breakfast in the morning and evening drinks (for a very reasonable price) and nibbles in the evening. It did get very crowded in the morning due to the conference crowd. However, the lounge staff could have been a little more efficient refilling items, rather than sitting at the front desk trawling the Internet for hours and chatting with each other.
The “Big Bar” in the hotel was lovely, but the drink prices were eye-watering and the hours were limited. In fact, none of the bars in the hotel were opened during the day, which seemed a little nutty while a busy literary conference was taking place. The hotel lost a lot of money in F&B because of this.
The location could not be beat and was close to lots of shopping and restaurants.
Checkout was quick, although there were a number of errors on our bill. However, they were adjusted without complaint. Staff were excellent and very friendly.
Solid 3 ½ out of 5 stars

title: “Decent hotel, pretty bad service”
text:
I stayed at the New Yorker Hotel on business but often travel to New York for leisure as well. The hotel is not very close to Times Square and is actually in a very well lived area. The street is very busy and pretty noisy. The entrance was large and the initial staff were very pleasant and helpful. Check in was uneventful and I made it to my room fairly easily.
The room represents the smallest hotel room I have ever stayed in. It is obviously a very old hotel and many of the doors looked to be original. While the bedroom and bathroom were small they were clean and well kept. The bed was fairly comfortable and the linens were clean and well maintained. The air conditioning was very, very cold and I found that I actually had to turn the unit off. One of my colleagues did not have the same experience and remarked that his room was constantly hot.
The bathroom is really tight on space as well. You have a pedestal sink and a small glass ledge to place any items on. The shower has a lot of pressure but I found that the temperature seems to fluctuate wildly on its own. I had the same comment from one of my coworkers. One second it was hot, then it was cold, and then it was way hot. 
We did have a chance to use the concierge service which was interesting. The lady was obviously stressed out and wasn't dealing with it very well. We waited for about 15 minutes to be acknowledged while she shuffled phone calls. We listened as she started arguing with a person over the phone. She stated "you sure you talking to me" and was just extremely rude and loud. When we finally had her attention she wasn't very helpful and kept with the attitude of someone who was being bothered by our restaurant request. We finally decided that we could do better on our own. When we left I remarked to my colleague that going to the concierge was not very helpful. Evidently she heard this and started yelling at me. She started in again with the "you talking to me, you got something to say, you got a problem with me". She was pretty insane so I didn't address her and we kept walking. I ignored her since she was obviously unstable and hated her job. I actually felt sorry for the people that were waiting behind us for help. 
All in all, the hotel was adequate. However, I have stayed at multiple hotels in the area. The Hilton is still my favorite and I would say that this hotel is my least favorite. The concierge showdown was interesting to say the least. Why they would put someone in that position with an attitude I don't understand. 
All in and all it was good for the location of the event I had to attend. However, based on the overall experience I will not stay here again and would steer friends and family away from this one.

title: “Palace good and bad”
text: The position is great. The rooms are spacious but there are some drawbacks. The lobby is like the departure lounge of a busy airport. The room service is extremely expensive. The concierge is overworked and needs to be chased up. However, the pluses considerably outweigh the minuses.

title: “Basic Lodging”
text: The hotel was basic lodging with a noisy air conditioner. We were there for a wedding, so when we got back to our hotel and were trying to sleep the noisy air conditioner had to be turned off. The morning breakfast was sub standard and not refreshed enough.

title: “Bay Club By Far The Best”
text:
The Bay Club Hotel & Marina in San Diego was by far the best hotel that we stayed in on our road trip around California this summer.
The Hotel itself is a large building right on the water, with a superb view from the front of the hotel and back. The staff were the most friendly that we encounter in our many hotel stays along the way. They were helpful, funny and very polite. 
Rooms are very spacious, with balconies over looking the Marina if your room faces the back. And a view of San Deigo Bay & city skyline if your room faces the front. The rooms have HBO and satellite television & films to order. The rooms have good sized bathrooms equipped with bath and shower. The rooms also have coffee pots, fridge and a safe.
The inclusive breakfast is not to be missed out, this breakfast includes cereals, coffee, tea, juice, bacon, eggs, sausage, potato, bagels etc. All served buffet style.
In the evening the hotel restaurant was very busy, but did not slip into the pattern of if its busy you'll be waiting, As we were seated and sereved within minutes, the food was brilliant and the price was reasonable.
The hotel also offers a bar, pool, hottub, shop, internet access, wifi. All round this hotel ticks all of the boxes as far as im concerned it was very pleaserable base to an excellent stay in San Deigo.

title: “Loved it, loved it, loved it”
text:
First the Location was very good. Georgetown is unlike rest of DC. It has nice boutiques, old brick roads and it has charm like old european town. We could take a Circular buses by walking right outside to Union Station . Foggy Bottom Station was closest but was about 10 blocks and not so close, probably being the only disadvantage. However a lake was close by where we walked down and it felt lovely in evening
The room and the hotel was just so wonderful that i would recommend that eveyone stays here only. The rooms were excellent. They had a kitchenette attached. We cooked food at night of our choice. Across the street was a CVS where you could get stuff you liked. Its best suited for business travellers and tourists not intending to spend time in the hotel itself because it dosent have a Pool or other such facilities. The rooms was nice and spacious. 
I would definitely go there again

title: “For the price you can't get better”
text: I spent a lot of time looking for a hotel in NYC for a reasonable price. After reading the reviews I settled for the Cosmopolitan. It didn't let me down, the rooms were great (7 of us stayed here) and the location excellent. A metro stop is right outside and you can easily walk to Brooklyn bridge, Statten Island ferry and Ground Zero. I would doubt you could find a better one for the price.

title: “Surprised by this Comfort Inn”
text: This is not your standard Comfort Inn. Be sure to request a street-view room, since the alley rooms can be noisy. Full breakfast provided, and its great. All people we met were very friendly and helpful, and finally found a hotel with quick elevators. Rooms are new, and beds are very comfortable. Overall, an excellent downtown "value-priced" hotel.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: It was a nice and fun stay during O's game. Love the receptionist and service. All the stuff are helpful. Gym is outstanding. Swimming pool is abit tiny. It has a Gift-shop but it wasn't look like a gift shop. Felt like it Just put snacks on a picnic table and looks tacky... Great location... Would stay here again if I ever come bk to bmore.

title: “Had a great stay at the Elan!”
text: I was drawn to this hotel because of it's location, and I was very satisfied. It's located in a very SAFE area - a major factor when considering where to stay in LA. It's a 3 minute walk from the beverly cente, and you also have a 24 hour pharmacy across the road. As for the hotel itself. . .it's not glamorous. . .but it does the job. Check-in was fast, and our room was clean and modern - although a little small. I was also pretty happy with the in room cable tv package - it even had a channel that showed all european football (soccer) matches! Also the continental breakfast was decent. It's served in the lobby cafe area where you can find a free to use internet station. Regarding value, we paid approximately $150 per night - that's great value for Beverly Hills. However a downer is cost of the valet parking service - $15 daily!

title: “not disappointed”
text:
I have stayed at other suites and still think this one is the best for the money. The rooms are big and I like the door separating the rooms. 
I had a problem with the restroom. Maintenance came very quickly and fixed the problem. GOOD SERVICE

title: “Good place to rest your head”
text: We stayed one night here over the weekend. Booked through priceline, no problem even at last minute. Easy access to highways since it is on the corner of 290 and I35. It has been recently renovated and you can tell if you look closely, but overall it was a good place to crash for the night. The bed was comfy (not hard), the new decor was nice. Bathroom still a little small, but serviceable. The only downside is that they really do need to pay closer attention to cleaning the bathrooms. The shower really should have been wiped down....

title: “lovely wedding venue”
text: Just had my daughter's afternoon wedding reception in the pavilion and it was fabulous. The food was delicious...beautiful views...and impeccable service. Not living in the Austin area, I was worried my guests staying there would be happy. The amenities...pool, nature trail, tennis, golf [mini golf too] were enjoyed by all. The rooms are very nice, not extravagant, but I wish they had mini refrigerators. The food is expensive...you have a resort tax on top of regular tax. Knowing that ahead of time, just relax and enjoy superb service. I should have stayed longer!

title: “First time staying in LES area”
text:
I went to New York to see a play, and chose the Thompson LES hotel because it was relatively close to the theater (Public Theater on Lafayette St. near Astor Place). I was generally pleased with the hotel.
My room was on the 11th floor overlooking Allen Street, with nice views in both directions. But be aware that there is a nightclub adjacent to the hotel at street level, and the music can be heard well above the street. I found that keeping the HVAC fan running produced sufficient white noise to cover the sound of the music.
The bed was comfortable, though the pillows were too soft for my taste. (I did not ask if the hotel had any firmer ones, so that's on me.) Bed was low, on a platform with no box spring (may be an issue for some people). Room decor is minimalist: white walls, black floors. Bedside alarm clock/ipod dock showed the correct time, but I could not get the alarm to work, or any of its other functions. Again, I did not contact the front desk about this, but I should have.
I was disturbed by occasional noise from the hall, particularly the elevator bells, which seemed exceptionally loud. I didn't sleep well in general, but I don't blame the hotel for that. A room away from the elevators may have helped.
Front desk and door staff were very courteous to me. I arrived earlier than expected, but was able to check in around 2:30 pm. I also stored my luggage for approx. 2 hrs. between checking out and leaving. Everyone I interacted with in the lobby area was great.
Subway entrance (F train) is right across the street, on the corner of Houston, very convenient. LES neighborhood is very interesting, worth spending some time exploring. It's less polished than other parts of Manhattan, feels more authentic.
Cleaning staff took away a couple of plastic water bottles I was planning to refill for my trip home. I had left them on the desk, so in my opinion they should have been left alone. Perhaps they thought it would encourage me to get a $5 water from minibar? It's not like Thompson is the only hotel chain trying to make money off room amenities. However, I do think that in 2012 it comes across as somewhat greedy to charge for wifi when there are plenty of other hotels that offer it for free. If I was traveling with a computer I would have considered staying elsewhere for this reason.

title: “A Gem in the heart of the Gaslamp Quarter.”
text: My husband and I found the Horton Grand Hotel while driving around the historic Gaslamp Quarter. It is a lovely hotel, and the staff are very friendly and helpful. It is walking distance to many restaurants and shops. We highly recommend and would certainly stay there again.

title: “Excellent Value: Great Hotel/Apartment”
text:
Stayed in the Marmara for a week and would highly recommend the hotel. From the minute the taxi dropped us off at the airport, our luggage was taken care of and the reception staff were very friendly and polite.
Check in was swift and we got a room on the 7th floor. One thing to bear in mind about New York is the noise, at night there is still a substantial amount of traffic and other noise, we were ok, but could still hear quite a lot, other reviewers asked for a higher room, but I felt the noise was bearable as I expected it. 
The room itself is huge, (bedroom suite) we had a double bed and a further bedroom with a bathroom, kitchen and large TV's in the living area. I was told that for New York this was great! 
The area is reasonable, there are roadworks just now for the 2nd avenue subway, a 5 minute walk down any avenue and there are plenty of lovely restaurants and bars to choose from. The subway is only two blocks away and gets you downtown in 10-15 mins, however most of the time we walked downtown to look around the avenues.
All in all a great hotel, they provided us with good places to eat and were even willing to sort out a private transfer to the Airport, which was cheaper than the taxi. Each room has its own free wi-fi which was an added bonus! Would definately go back and stay there in the future.

title: “Best Hotel in Town! Great Staff and Rooms”
text:
We stayed in a suite for three nights, just after the New Year and it was great. There were only two suites in the area. There was also a door which we could shut if we wanted more privacy. Only guests with keys to the two suites behind the door have access to the area. 
There was a walk-in robe, a very spacious bedroom with a very comfortable bed, separate bath and shower and a separate lounge room in the suite. 
Staff at the hotel were also very warm and helpful. Bellboys were keen to assist when we arrived and one staff looked genuinely concerned and offered to assist when he saw the amount of luggage we had. Check-in process was smooth and staff were very welcoming. The hotel had a ‘homely’ feel to it which was great, especially since we’ve been travelling around for about a month before getting to this hotel. Having stayed at many other luxury hotels on our travels this is definitely the best!
 We’d highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting New York and we’ll definitely return.

title: “simple and clean”
text:
lucky I could trust the past reviews. 
it was exactly what I needed, clean without problems and a short drive 
to my client. 
I did not find the parking to be an issue like the other poster.
my Internet access was fine 
the bathroom was spotless and the room was clean. 
I did smell the cigarette odor but I really did not mind. 
I felt safe, and the front desk people were very Nice and gave me direction to the famous place where they make Philly cheese sandwiches. (that's a funny story, waiting on line and I stuttered and they kicked me to the back of the line again, but it tasted great and worth the wait) 
would I book this place again, truth is yes but only if get another client in the area

title: “Concierge Lounge - Rosie”
text: I recently had the opportunity to visit the Concierge Lounge for an evening appetizer and beverage where I met Rosie our concierge lounge host. As I was staying at the hotel for several nights I visited the lounge 2-3 times. Rosie was absolutely wonderful - cheerful, professional, attentive but also knows when to leave you alone. She made sure that I new where everything was and that I was taken care of and comfortable. Just a delightful person. So if you are staying at this hotel and have concierge privilages make sure to stop in as Rosie will make sure you have an enjoyable visit.

title: “Excellent central San Diego hotel”
text: Location in Gaslamp District, 5-10 minutes from Convention Centre. Rooms with mini kitchen and fridge-freezer. Helpful, welcoming staff. Also close to San Diego Padres baseball ground - 'ballgame' special deal was good value.

title: “Nice but very small room”
text:
Pros: Location, Cleanliness, Design, Restaurant in the lobby
Cons: small room and dark if you get one that as a view...ito the inside part of the hotel

title: “too many add-on fees”
text:
My stay at this hotel came as part of an airfare package. I took the "business plan" at an extra $40 a night, which included a full breakfast and in-room wireless Internet access. These items are usually fee-based and would have cost at least $40 alone; the business plan also thows in free US long-distance, a Wall Street Journal or USA Today, a $4.50 bottle of water on your nightstand (with its price sticker prominently marked), and one blouse pressing per day. So the Hyatt gets you either way. Fact is, I can get most of these items free or for a few dollars at almost any chain lodging. Granted, the food at the Hyatt is much better, but....
Physically it's a lovely hotel with wonderful and informative displays on Texas history (ask for the self-guided walking tour brochure at the front desk). The furniture in my room was a little dinged-up, surprising for a luxury hotel of this ilk. The location behind the train station means that (surprise) you'll hear trains. I liked this, but you may not. Temperature controls were good. 
Walking into town involves climbing a few small hills and passing under a rather unpleasant underpass. I would not have done it after dark. Watch the drivers in Dallas--they are cowboys (haha), and I say that as a bona fide NY jaywalker.
I planned to have dinner at the hotel's Italian bistro, but it was closed the nights I was there--"low occupancy" was the reason. The adjacent Centennial Cafe was open. Pricey but good.
Service is excellent. Waitstaff and housekeeping staff members are obviously well-trained. Somehow they make their eye contact and smiles seem genuine. One front-desk person was a bit ditzy, but the waiters made up for it.

title: “Wonderful hotel!”
text:
Besides the fact that this hotel is JUST opened, it is beautiful! Everything is clean, the beds are MAGNIFICENT!
Breakfast is good, and the hotel has such easy access to I-25.

title: “Lovely clean room with fantastic views!”
text:
We arrived at the Dumont the last week of August and stayed for 10 nights - so our stay overlapped into September. The rooms had been renovated, with new carpets and tv installed shortly before our arrival. We had two rooms - both one bedroom suites on the 27th & 34th floors. Views were stunning - really couldn't of asked for more. Rooms were always exceptionally clean and staff extremely helpful and friendly. We could walk everywhere from the Murray Hill neighbourhood - and for us it was an ideal base as didn't want to be in the madness of Times 
Square! All in all, a great stay and will definitey be returning! One added bonus would be free wifi in the rooms - especially as so many hotels offer this. But that would be my only complaint!

title: “14 reasons why to book here. And why to not.”
text:
Whatever your expectations, The Fig will surprise you. This treatise will help you determine if you're going to be "good" surprised or "not good" surprised. I wish I had read this before booking.
1. Do NOT book this hotel thinking you're getting a luxury boutique hotel. It is neither. It is very much a tourist class hotel that just happens to be decorated with a unique flair. That unique flair includes very cheap furniture in the (often very small) rooms.
2. DO book this hotel if you want to sequester yourself in a weirdly charming old hotel space in LA in order to write the next great screenplay about a writer in a timewarp.
3. Do NOT book this hotel if you like fancy coffee or lavish breakfast. See #1. The restaurant reminds me of the old "hot food" line in the back of Smith's Bar on 8th Ave in NYC. It has a charming feel to it because there are signs by each item ($1.00 for potatoes), but food should be tasty, not charming. 
4. DO book this hotel if you need to be downtown and don't like the sterility of the Westin, or hate malls, or despise name brands in general.
5. Do NOT get wooed by the website, as I did, which gives a mistaken impression of, well, sophistication. No. It's only sophisticated FOR WHAT IT REALLY IS, which is an old-school downtown budget hotel with cement floors in the rooms.
6. DO book this hotel if you're on a budget and you want to be surprised by how much color you can get for your dollar compared to the Travelodge. Way more. Way better.
7. Do NOT book this hotel if you want an easy late-night check-in. The door is locked, and you have to ring the bell and wait for the put-out Seinfeld character to buzz you in. 
8. DO book this hotel for the parking prices. Best in LA. Hands down.
9. Do NOT book this hotel for its lavish toiletries. Nope.
10. Do NOT book this hotel for anything else in the bathroom of usual interest, like a good shower or fluffy towels or good shaving light or a swell vanity made of marble.
11. DO book this hotel if you like the toilet to have a "freshly cleaned" paper band around the bowl like you remember from when you were a kid staying in motels off Rte 66. 
12. Do NOT book this hotel if you're a business traveller. Really. Just trust me there.
13. DO book this hotel if you like having a scratchy muslin duvet or a kitschy leopard chair from a garage sale.
14. Do NOT book this hotel thinking you're staying somewhere exotic. It's painted. It's not Morocco. 
I always prefer to spend my money on a hotel with a unique sensibility - one that doesn't remind me of another chain someplace in Anywhere, USA. Aces on that front. Figueroa Hotel and its oddball-meets-exotic-decor has that in spades. It just isn't ideal for all guests. I have my LA favorites. This is not one of them. It is, however, one I truly appreciate just for being so unexpected.

title: “Incredible place to escape”
text: I made reservations for a weekend getaway to this hotel after reading an article about it. Very nice and in the best location to the ballpark and nightlife. The bar is pretty cool, and we liked the designer pool area (gets sun ALL day long!). We'll go back!

title: “Big Mama strikes again.”
text: It times of need, and disparity, Telethia came to the rescue without hesitation. It was as if she had been wearing a cape under her Dupot Hotel robes forever. With the 'T' on her chest, she was able to get my group out of a pinch, effortlessly, making our stay much, much, much more enjoyable. As if that was not enough, she gave us homemade cookies, which were delicious.

title: “Cheap, perfect and Location, Location, Location!”
text:
We didn't quite know what to expect before arriving at the Cosmopolitan. Our expectations from the photo's were low but a friend
and trip advisor painted the accomodation in a different light. When we arrived our expectations couldn't have been more wrong. Aside from
the service, which isn't bad but not what we're used to and the noisy
street at night this hotel was perfect. The room was tidy, more modern than expected and perfect. Situated right out the front of the subway if you're staying here you must go to Bubby's for breakfast around the corner.
If you're going to New York to explore and spend minimal time in your
hotel this is ideal, don't hesitate and see for yourself.

title: “Lovely but not for families”
text: This is a lovely hotel in a great location, great food, great staff - and a fun lobby/lounge experience on the main floor. However, although I am a Starwood member, I don't usually stay at W hotels, so was not completely attuned to the fact that the rooms and style are designed for younger couples, singles and business travelers, not for families traveling with children. I was with my two daughters, aged 11 and 14, and although they thought the hotel was great - they loved the brownies in the lobby in the PM and the lounge scene - we did not really fit in the room comfortably since each room only has one bed. We got a rollaway cot eventually, but I am used to having the two double or queen beds in the Sheratons e.g., so was brought up short when I first saw we were supposed to all sleep in one slightly smallish queen sized bed. The staff was great at responding to my quandary here, but I think the hotel website could have been clearer about what was REALLY in each room in terms of sleeping space. On the other hand, we really enjoyed ourselves on the East Side, and loved being so close to the subway, to Fifth Ave. and Central Park. Also loved the Japanese restaurant right around the corner...

title: “Would never stay here again. Ever.”
text: They advertise that they have free airport shuttle service. They don't. On arrival, they told us to take a taxi for which they would pay. They did. But when we had to go back to the airport the next moring, we had to wait for more than 30 minutes. The worst thing was the room itself. It was a two story suite, with a second bedroom upstairs. When we arrived late at night, all the lights were on inside, including the upstairs bedroom. Freaked us out. Then we discovered we couldn't lock the door. It had been forced open sometime in the past, and the metal lock plate on the edge of the door was all bent so the dead bolt could not be extended. The other surface mounted lock had been ripped off also, and was dangling from the door. And to top it all off, none of the three phones worked at all. When we asked for another room, we initialy were told we would have to pay more. Eventually we got another room, but the whole experience was very unpleasant. Would never ever stay there.

title: “Affinia Extra Facts”
text: If you book a guest room you can request a coffee maker for the room. You get a drip coffee maker and coffee, tea bags, sweeten, sugar and power creamer. We also requested a "kitchen set" which is four plates, bowls and cutlery. The New York Kit is a guide book plus various walking tours . The Walking tours are very good because you can take 4 x 6 card . Pedometer is also included. Tthere is a mini refrigerator stuffed with water bottles, Liquor, pop, and various snacks. You can get cheaper booze etc at Food Emporium on 3rd ave and 32 street. The food price were a lot cheaper than the corner stores. There is a very good diner at 32 street & Lexington - Murray Hill Dinner. Behind the hotel on 3 rd street is Duke's . Great for dinner. There is also a pillow menu check their website for further details. Very Friendly and helpful staff. This hotel didn't have any recycling boxes, the only fault in a perfect stay. And I have express my concerns to the management.

title: “Most Definitely Stay Here Again!”
text:
I did a tremendous amount of research before I booked my room at Astor on the Park. After reading the reviews, and also debating the price, I'm so glad I chose to stay here. We were greeted immediately by an employee, who graciously took our bags to our room while we started the check in. The elevator is a very tight fit, but we occasionally used the stairs when we didn't want to wait. 
The room is very cozy and clean. It is small, but I loved the fact that we had a private bathroom. Anytime we needed towels or assistance, someone came to our aid in a timely manner. The beds were very close to the walls (double bed room) and at first I thought I may have trouble sleeping incase any other guests were rowdy or coming back to the hotel late, but I had no problem getting a good nights rest. 
It's also in a great location. Not too far from the subway stops nor from drug stores or anything. 
I would definitely stay here again when I come back to visit!

title: “very good for the price”
text:
stayed just one night on 2-28-12..booked online directly with them about 1 month in advance. Had problem finding me system at first, but with conf # jumped right to it
the room I had seemed a little small, it is basically a small bedroom with an attached bathroom and walk-in closet, where there is an under counter fridge, microwave and coffee maker
Bathroom sink is really a bar sink with garbage disposal, very unusual but 100% functional
The desk staff is friendly and very helpful, pointing me in the right direction to Little Italy and good food
This place is no $500 a night hotel...it is exactly what it claims to be...a good bargain, with free wifi and a continental breakfast....I felt safe and slept soundly while there...I'll be back if ever in the area again

title: “Customer Friendly Hotel Staff”
text: This hotel has an excellent staff! I travel with toddler twins and it is always wonderful when hotel staff are extra nice to my children. When we ate breakfasst in the dining room, the wait staff was always checking on me to see if I needed anything for my children. Also, the front desk provided directions to Zilker Park and another kid-friendly activity since we did not know the city very well.
