title: “Great Thanksgiving stay at the Fairmont!”
text: Fantastic hotel. Very clean and spacious room, attractive lobby, very friendly staff. Will definitely stay again.

title: “Nice Hotel, Great Location!”
text: The hotel is in a great location (2 blocks from newbury) and pretty much attached to the prudential center and copley place. There are definetly a lot of things to do around the area. The T is also very close and convienent. The rooms are nice and clean, but nothing fancy. I was unable to use the pool, as it was closed when I was there, but it looked nice. Parking was expensive, but I think it's expensive in every hotel downtown. If I was to return, I would definetly consider this hotel again if the price was right.

title: “I was expecting more.....”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Sheraton Boston for three nights for the Boston Marathon. I understand that room rates were escalated for the event but for $350+ per night for a hotel room, we were expecting something special. The hotel room was clean, ok decor, nice linens, but not overly spacious. Nothing that I haven't seen for $150 per night elsewhere, and we do quite a bit of traveling so we've seen many hotels. The hotel is in a great location, connected to the Prudential Center Shopping Mall, has a nice lobby and the staff was friendly but beyond that I can't say that I would recommend the hotel to others, at least not for what we paid. There are many other hotels in the area and I think if we are back for the marathon next year, we will try a different hotel in the same neighborhood. Would have liked to give this hotel a better review but after spending over $1000 for three nights, I'm feeling a little "taken". Sorry Sheraton Boston.

title: “Everything that one would expect for a Westin”
text:
This is the 2nd if 3 hotels that I stayed in during my 1 week stay in San Francisco for memorial day weekend. 
Great location, nice rooms and amenities and exceptional service.
Everything was within walking distance - dining, shopping, conference facilities (moscone convention center very near), public transportation. The staff was very helpful and we felt welcome during the whole stay.
Would definitely choose this hotel the next time I am in town.

title: “Good service, bad rooms”
text:
Good: Pleasant service at front desk, friendly shuttle drivers who went out of their way to give us a ride to the office in the morning (partially due to long wait for cabs out on the highway)
Free breakfast on club level is satisfactory; includes mini boxes of cereal, toast, pastries, scrambled eggs, fruit, etc.
Bad: Room was very outdated. Had a 2 bed suite that felt very cramped. Did not sleep nearly as well as I do at the Westin in downtown Dallas (which was sold out). Stiff couch and scratched up desk in living room .
Outdated bathroom- moldy tub, poor lighting.
(Mind you, this was all on a Starwoods Club Floor. I have platinum status, so I'm assuming I was put in one of the better rooms) 
Gym- Out of the four **old** machines there (two bikes, treadmill, and stair climber)- only one of the bikes worked properly (barely) Other machines did not 'turn on' at all, or seemed as if they were about to give out (treadmill made a horribly loud noise every time you took a step... not good) Weight machine was as old as the machines, and equally useless.
If you have a choice of Starwoods hotels in Dallas, stick with the W or Westin. I was very dissapointed with the Sheraton Suites.

title: “Super stay, especially for dogs!”
text:
My husband and I have wanted to stay here for ages, ever since my husband found out they will put a goldfish in your room on request. Last year we got a dog and found out this chain charges no pet fees and is very dog-friendly, so we wanted to stay even more. We finally went on Easter weekend. They had a good deal on that was like stay 2 nights, get 15% off. (I see that a recent reviewer won this on Priceline for $100 the same weekend, and I'm jealous!)
The service was extremely friendly and unpretentious. Our room was gorgeous and huge, with a separate sitting room. I couldn't get over the awesome interior design. Our dog got a little gift bag with a toy and a treat. 
You really should join the Kimpton rewards program, as it is free and you get free wi-fi and a $10 mini-bar credit with it. 
We loved our stay and will be back.

title: “easy commute to downtown Boston”
text: Took my grandchildren, 11 year old twins for visit to Boston. Commute was a little complicated we went around the 'round-about' three times before getting it right. Welcomed to the hotel by Mariane at front desk who promptly offered everyone warm chocolate chip cookies. The kids were happy and so was I. Room was clean but could use updating. We caught Doubletree Shuttle to South Station the next morning. From there onto Hop On Hop Off Tour bus. Spent the day shopping and touring; taking advantage of the Duck Splash option on the tour bus and viewing Boston Harbor. At the end of our day we made our way back to South Station and caught Doubletree Shuttle back to the hotel. One of the best deals ever. Drivers and Staff at the hotel were warm and friendly. Starbucks Cafe which offered sandwiches and drinks needs some work. Service is confused causing long lines even if you're just picking up a soda. You end up waiting while everyone gets their sandwiches or eggs. Friendliness lacking too. The first night there they seemed more interested in getting out and closing up than they did on serving customers. I would definitely go back to this hotel but I'd pack a sandwich.

title: “Nice Hotel in a good location”
text: Just got back from a three night stay and found almost everything to be excellent. The only problem is that the hotel is retrofitted and uses window unit heating and cooling. This lets in a good bit of noise. We talked with the front desk and they told me that they are ordering sound buffers to go around the unit. This should help alot. Otherwise the room is small but about average in NY. Certainly not the smallest I have stayed in. Don't stay in room alot in NYC. The staff is great. The location is good. The grab up breakfast is good. Just know there is nowhere to sit. The beds are nice and comfy. Hotel is clean, newly remodeled and good especially for a short trip.

title: “Great business hotel”
text:
I've been to this hotel several times while staying in New York for business.
The staff are always friendly and my room is alwats spotless clean. I find rooms smaller than the usual standard but I hardly spend any time in them. The bed - usually a King size - is super comfy and the views are often iconic for the Tribecca/Soho area. The room has an iron and ironing board and a coffee machine. The hair-drier in the bathroom is pretty OK - although I hardly ever find a decent hair-drier in hotels.
The last time I stayed I was upgraded to use the lounge on the 21st floor and it makes a huge difference, so upgrade if you can. You have access to a free breakfast and evening buffet - the breakfast one was pretty comprehensive with lots of healthy options. if the weather allows, don't eat in the inside area (which is not very stylish) but go out to the amazing terrace with stunning views. Drinks are also cheaper here than in the ground-floor bar plus you get free wi-fi in your room - otherwise you have to pay for it.
Another thing is the ground-floor bar is always very lively and open until late (and the drinks are strong!) and it also has a Starbucks shop.
Price wise I find New York quite expensive, so I find this hotel expensive but for the city/area, it's not too bad.

title: “Don't Stay Here!”
text: We arrived to this Ramada at about 11:30 at night. The area is a seedy, scary part of town. When I parked our vehicle in the underground parking, I saw broken glass right beside the stall we parked in. Not a good sign. When I walked into the lobby, I was overwhelmed by the stink of cigarette smoke that saturated the entire area. Though the room appeared fine, there was a large crack between the bottom of the door and the floor that let in light and cigarette-smoke-smelling air from the lobby, plus the room was cold. We put our kids to bed, then I tried to figure out how to turn on the heater. The heater was broken. I told this to the front desk. Though they offered to put us in another room or have a "maintenance" person fix it, it was already 11:30 at night and neither option was good. We elected to sleep there without heat. It was minus 2 degrees celsius outside and we froze. When I complained to the front desk the next morning, he kind of shrugged and didn't offer to do anything for us. When we returned from our 9-day trip, thankfully our vehicle was fine, but the broken glass on the ground was still there - they hadn't cleaned it up! DONT STAY HERE. There are many better options. I will try the well-reviewed Sleep Inn next time.

title: “Cute and Clean”
text: This is a nice and clean limited service hotel. Note that it is a non-smoking hotel, but they have patios out front and out back for smoking. The standard room was $119, and after my third trip, I decided to pay the extra three dollars for a suite (rate: $122) and it was MUCH nicer. The suites have 2 TV's, a separate bedroom area, microwave and fridge.

title: “Great Experience”
text: We had a wonderful stay. The staff was very friendly or, at the very least, cordial. The bell hops speak english, most as a first language. My husband (who's a native Texan) enjoyed the "Soprano-like" accents very much and I was glad to be home. The hotel is located on Lexington 1/2 block from the subway station -- you can't get more convenient. The beds were comfortable, the room was very clean, and we enjoyed the automated check-in terminals, which we used to check into the hotel as well as to print out our boarding passes for the trip home. I booked our room through Priceline and, except for one snotty telephone reservations clerk, we were treated very well. About the clerk -- I hung up on her and called back and got a very helpful clerk. It didn't matter though, because when I checked in I was given the option to change the room I'd been assigned from a one with a queen beed to one with 2 double beds. Then I asked the bell hop for a rollaway bed and it was delivered within 10 minutes. The only thing that's keeping me from giving this hotel an Excellent rating is that the room didn't have the lighted makeup mirror and similar (luxury?) appointments that I was hoping for. I would stay here again, but I also would have liked a little refrigerator.

title: “Good hotel in a good location”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Donatello for one night during October. The room was nice, spacious and clean. We dined at the hotel's Italian restaurant which was not on the cheap side, but worth every cent. The restaurant is run by Italians and the food was delicious ! The hotel is located in the union square area which is convenient for accessing shops and restaurants by foot. One word of advice: there is no free parking around the hotel. There is a valet parking at the hotel which costs 30$ per day. Take this into account when booking as hotel prices around this area aren't cheap. All in all, it was a good stay and I would recommend this hotel to people wanting to stay around union square. In my next visit to SF I will probably consider a cheaper place outside the town center, providing I have a rented vehicle.

title: “Distrikt Lives Up To Its Rating”
text: My wife and I stayed at Distrikt a few weeks ago on a weekend night. The hotel comes highly rated on this site and we were able to find a great rate for our stay. We booked and were very excited to be staying in NYC for a great price and at a great hotel. The staff was helpful and Peter, at the front desk, was very helpful. Each time we saw him passing in and out of the lobby he asked about our plans and provided helpful reccommendations as we went exploring the city. Our room was large for NYC standards and clean. We were placed on a high floor and had a beautiful view of the west side of the city. We had no issues whatsoever with it's location as it is in the heart of the city. A quick walk and you are in Times Square and by several metro spots (both bus and subway). It is in a location with a series of hotels and is a safe area to walk to and from wherever you need to go. I certainly would stay again at Distrikt Hotel when I come to the city. It was everything that the rest of the reviewers have raved about. The one regret that I did have was that we did not have the free continental breakfast there, however, we made up for it by going to Clinton Street Bakery for one of the most memorable breakfasts of my life. I heard from other guests that it was a nice continental breakfast and another nice addition to your stay. In conclusion,you cannot ask more of a NYC hotel if you are coming, going, relaxing, exploring and enjoying all that the city has to offer.

title: “Great place to stay or hold a meeting”
text:
My travels were for business. I taught a class in one of the hotels meeting rooms on Saturday and Sunday. The hotel was unremarkable from the outside, but right across from Love Field Airport. They have a shuttle.
The inside of the hotel is very nice. The front desk people are accomodating and friendly. There is a better than average restaurant/sports bar attached with happy hour. SW Airlines uses this hotel a lot, apparently. There is a small but clean pool outside, and a fairly well stocked workout room - lots of equipment for a hotel. It is clean. 
The meeting rooms were very well prepared, set up perfect, looked nice, water, mints, pens & pads for the guests. The lighting was good. The room temperature was good. The catering was great. Accolades go out to Miguel, who took fantastic care of my needs without me even asking. He is definitely an AAA+ employee. This hotel has fairly good meeting room and catering prices, and really good room prices.
The hotel rooms are very well appointed and clean. They thought of everything a traveler needs. Clean, soft sheets, lots of pillows, good TV, good work space, a refrigerator, a microwave, a bar area to set things, a comfy chair with a flip desk top and plugs in the side of it, lots of lighting, good towels and my favorite: nice "bath and body works" amenities. The bathrooms are way too small, but I could overlook that because everything else was great.
The second night when I was working in my room, a bunch of teenagers were partying in the hall. I called downstairs and they told me there was a big party that had a band playing until 2 AM, so they brought me a key to move me to another room two floors up. It was inconvenient, but I am grateful I didn't have to suffer.
They also have a gift shop and a cool computer touch screen in the lobby to flip for directions for shopping, etc. Nice touch.
Thanks Wyndham!

title: “Great Location”
text:
This hotel is in a great location. The staff are friendly enough and were always happy to help. Our room was on the 19th floor and was of an OK size. The bathroom was a little gruby and I dont think they vacumed very often. I requested a quiet room and got exactly that apart from when a teenange dancing convention arrived for the weekend ( I am sure they were all on our floor) still this did not dampen our spirits as we were so tired from the sighs and shopping to notice much. We did not eat in the hotel as it was much more fun looking around for somewhere to eat. We did however find a great cafe ( I think its called Pershing Square) just under the Park Ave bridge accross the road from the hotel which did a great breakfast. We did have coctails in the hotel bar which seemed expensive at $14 each but you would only need a couple as they were very strong!! All in all we had a great time at this hotel and I would recommend it to anyone for location alone.
My one tip would be to go to the Top of The Rock instead of the empire state. I have been to New york before and went up the empire state building which took about 2 hours in line! This time i tried the top of the rock and I was at the top within 5 minutes of buying my ticket!!! I could not believe the views, they were even better than the empire state building. Granted i went on a very cold and windy day and there were only 2 other people up there with me but I never saw a line all week.

title: “Super, yet again ...”
text: Thank you for yet another enjoyable stay at the Hampton Inn. I arrived at around 11.00 prepared to drop of my bag prior to hitting the streets of NYC, but the very nice girl on reception said if I would like to wait 10 minutes my room would be ready, and it was. Great, comfortable rooms with ample space. The room was spotlessly clean and the beds are very comfortable after all the walking entailed in a day in New York. I love the location of this hotel - just across the road from Macy's and close to the subway and good bars and restaurants. The breakfast also really sets you up for the day!

title: “Affordable chic boutique hotel in the heart of San Francisco!”
text:
My husband and I live about 2 hours away and wanted to getaway for a few days but not spend too much money on hotels. I'm a bit picky when it comes to the type of hotel which usually causes us to pay more. Luckily we snagged a deal on this place and only paid $89 a night for The Crescent Room (single queen bed). 
Here are the pros: It's in a prime location! You are in the heart of downtown and within minutes you can be in Chinatown or Union Square...if you want to take the Bart or bus...you don't have to walk far. The hotel is very chic and modern. It's very crisp and clean design makes you feel like you're in one of the pricier hotels. The staff was very friendly and accomodating. We planned to bike through the city so we brought our own bikes. They were willing to store the bikes in the back and even allowed us to do so before check in. We were going to a 2pm showing of Wicked and did not want to leave the bikes in the parking garage. They also allowed us to check out late and store our our bikes/luggage after checking out so we could grab a late lunch before leaving the city. We stayed 2 1/2 days and got the reduced parking rate of $28 a night...essentially our last day in SF we were able to park for free since we were leaving later in the afternoon. 
Here are a few cons about the locations: For some reason our keys kept zeroing out. Each day we had to get new keys which wouldn't be so bad if we weren't on the 6th floor. There was an iron, but no ironing board and the refrigerator was their minibar and full of mini liquor bottles so it's not even possible to store anything in it...not even a bottle of water. One of my pet peeves are hotels that either don't give you wash cloths (i.e. European hotels) or in this case when they only give you 1. We had 3 bath towels and 1 wash cloth. It was an odd combination... Lastly, we knew about the free breakfast but were not too impressed. There was a selection of pastries, fruit, and cereal but it was nothing to really brag about. I'd recommend eating at one of the many amazing restuarants. 
One tip on finding the place, in order to get to the hotel by car you need to go through the Stockton Tunnel. The parking garage they use is located on Sutter about 1/2 a block from the hotel. Overall, the pros outweighed any of my cons so without a doubt we will stay here next time we decided to stay the night in SF. If you're looking for a clean, modern and affordable hotel in the heart of downtown this is the perfect place.

title: “A truly spectacular property!”
text: This property is truly amazing! We stayed in the Gold Coast suite which was beautiful! The room service was fantastic and was a european bistro style. The location was also great, just off Michigan avenue and close to the lake! Recommended restaurants in the area are Boka, Naha, and Topolo! Can't wait to go back!

title: “Great stay!”
text: Stayed here via Priceline to attend an event at the Lucas Oil Stadium. The hotel was a short drive to the downtown area. I requested double beds and had no problems. The rooms seemed average size to me with outdated furniture, but a fantastic bed. I swear it was one of the softest hotel beds I've ever had and I travel frequently. The towels were very large and fluffy also. Flat screen TV was nice. We didn't eat in the restaurant and I was a little disappointed with the lack of a fitness center. The hotel is in the process of becoming a Wyndham. The front desk staff was very helpful with directions and assistance with area restaurants. We would definitely return.

title: “Very average for a Marriott, maybe a franchisee?”
text:
Not up to Marriott corporate brand standards, ok but not great for $200/night!
Tiny room. Restaurant menu very pedestrian and way overpriced, boarding pass machine not working, digital tv service went out (during Ryder Cup final round!!). In fairness to Marriott, other brands in area probably not much better!

title: “Excellent Value, Perfect...if....”
text:
The hotel staff was very helpful upon my arrival, and did everything possible to find me a room so that I could check in early. The room i received was a two bedroom - two actual bedrooms, with a living room and full kitchen! suite that was immaculate, nicely decorated and recently remodeled. i had chosen the hotel as i thought it was close to the gas lamp district. it is not as close as i had thought, but it is nevertheless close to many attractions in the city (Balboa Park San Diego Zoo, etc.) The gas lamp district is actually quite a few blocks away and I would not want to walk in that area at night. It is somewhat equidistant from the gas lamp district and university avenue, which also has a lot of shops and restaurants.
It is important to point out, in case it matters to you, that this hotel is gay friendly. I am not gay (not that there is anything wring with that ;), and had no problem with it, but it is worth pointing out. There is no pool in the hotel, and dont be confused by the sign outside that says Manor Suites, that is the old name of the now Inn at The Park.
It is an old building and floor noises (from people walking the floor above you) is common. There is also some street noise but it was very tolerable when I was there. Valet parking is $15 a night, which is quite reasonable.
However, IF you plan to party in the gas lamp district, do not expect this hotel to be a manageable distance away once you have imbibed several alcoholic drinks, it si quite a walk, and not always a good one. It is however a very good value in a very good area and once remodeling is complete all the rooms will be as beautiful as the one I received

title: “Good location for shopping dinner shows and tours but room was a let down”
text:
Stayed at hotel April 25 - 29. Location to Union Sq was great we could walk to great shopping, dining, hop on hop off bus stop, cable cars etc 
The Daily Grill is the in house dining and was awesome recommend.
The room was below average. The bathroom was meh and the sink is in your bedroom lounge room area? I thought we would have a window... We did, that looked straight across in to another hotel guests room, make sure you get a room with external window! 
There was no free wifi which is not cool in this day. The door staff were lovely and genuine but I found the concierge disinterested. 
For location can't beat it but don't expect 5 or even 4 star.

title: “No thanks to Hotwire”
text: Not at all deserving of the 4 1/2 stars they claim. New, yes, but the finish construction in our room was no better than a lousy roadside chain. Nothing "hot" about it-the place was empty on a Saturday night-and the accomodations are one step above a college dorm room. The designer should be unemployed; very poor space planning. We are both Starwood Gold and were not upgraded. Check-in lengthy as they were understaffed. Missed the Ground Zero experience because the concierge didn't know what she was talking about. No bellman showed when we called for help on check-out. All around, a very disappointing experience.

title: “Worth considering”
text:
As an airline crewmember and frequent hotel guest, my recent stays as this property have been short, but have been comfortable. The rooms have been recently updated (it looks like they went to an IKEA show room) and for the price are competative with other bigger brand names along Century Blvd. Free wireless and Shuttle service between the hotel and the airport. Parking is available as well. The shuttle service is a contracted company that serves a majority of the Century blvd hotels and is lacking in timely service. You should give yourself at least 30 minutes of travel time to go the relatively short distance from the property to the terminal. The bus fills up quickly during peak times, and this is the last pickup prior to the airport, so you may be standing. Dont expect quick service from the front desk, either. checkin times can be lengthly, especially in the evenings. There are several fast food selections near the hotel, however for your personal safety I would avoid walking east of the 405, especially at night.
If you what your looking for is a clean economical hotel near LAX, you could do better and certainly do worse. This hotel is worth the consideration for the business traveller who needs consist of a clean room, free internet, and an iron.

title: “Would not recommend this hotel”
text:
This hotel had a great appearance and could have been so much better. The service wasn't very good unfortunately. When we checked in with three people we were given a room smaller than some single Japanese rooms I have stayed in. When we went back to the desk we were given a lecture about how we should know better (They charged us extra and we were ok with that because we got a great deal with priceline). We had to call the front desk to get more shampoo and conditioner. The internet is charged daily and the price is extremely high but when we complained they gave it for free (apparently complaining gets you thing there). When checking in we were told that parking was $30/night. A little high but it was in downtown Seattle. At the end of the stay they added tax without telling us until checking out. The guy then told us we should know better and obviously there would be taxes added on. I've never had this at other hotels in Seattle, San Francisco etc. If you're given a parking rate it should have taxes included (the price is all made up by the hotel anyways)
There was garbage under the bed (the we know wasn't from us). The housekeeping did a poor job of cleaning the room and we had to call and request new shampoo and conditioner.
We got great rates through Priceline so that was awesome but a lot of the service was bad. They even spoke poorly about Priceline. If you don't like Priceline don't use the service.

title: “So beautiful, but had a bad experience.”
text: This hotel is so lovely, that I was dissapointed with all the problems I had. It was probably just my bad luck the few days I was there. No one was there when I arrived late at night and luckily a stranger on the street kept a drunk guy from getting in my taxi while I was still in it. When you arrive late, the hotel should assume you are traveling. I was traveling for 36 hours and was put in a room overlooking construction and woken up very early with construction noises after only 4 hrs of sleep. I also smelled smoke and was too tired to even get up for that. There were water and security problems also. But, they gave a good discount for Berklee College visitors and the food and drinks were good. So , maybe I just had a rare bad experience....... I was moved to an allergy room and the air was really good in there.

title: “SSSHHH- Don't tell anyone about the Salisbury”
text: What can I say, this hotel as everyone says is a little dated, the lifts are tiny and slow and make some very scary noises, but the location is fabulous, the rooms are huge, high ceilings, big windows, loads of storage space for all the shopping you've done in NYC, fridge and microwave are a bonus, although some crockery and cutlery would have been helpful too. We loved everything about the Salisbury, proximity to Carnegie Hall, 5th Avenue, Central Park, and good food options.

title: “Had a wonderful visit!!!”
text: I was a little concerned about going there after reading so many bad reviews, but figured it was just for one night with the kids so we would survive. The check in manager was extremely nice and gave us the kids club suprise gift which turned out to be 25.00 in arcade tokens and a free bag of dirt for mining. I have three girls, 4,6, and 10. We had reserved the Cisco bunk room which turned out to be very nice and clean. I never saw any bugs anywhere. Our girls LOVED the bunkbed with their own flatscreen T.V and so did we! The bathroom was kind of small but I really appreciated the mini-fridge and microwave.We played in the waterpark until 9pm when it closes and then cooked microwave dinners for the girls. They had a picnic on the bunkbeds and had a blast. The next morning we packed up and still got to enjoy the arcade and waterpark. There was never a shortage of towels like I had read, even though we took our own. The staff in the giftshop, the bar, and the arcade were very nice. The lifegaurds were very attentive which I appreciated. My husband and I even went out front in the evening and sat outside for a breather which was nice. The other thing I want to mention is how clean they kept the waterpark. My kids dropped some fries on the ground under our table, and it wasnt long before a staff member was coming around with a broom and swept them up. I was impressed.The a/c in the room was working extremely well, so much so that we had to turn it down. The kingsize bed was great, and the sheets looked and smelled clean. I was very pleased. No the T.V was not a 32 in flatscreen but thats not why I was there. My kids and I had a wonderful time. Oh...dont pass up a bag of the mining dirt. They have a sluice where our girls got to wash and pan for "gems". My husband and I were worried there wouldnt be much in it. I was WRONG. Each of the girls got a very nice size bag of gems and an identification card. We got some great pictures and they are still showing off their finds. Overall my husband and I agree, we will definately go back. It's not a Westin or a Hilton, and trust me Ive stayed in both. It is a nice family resort and the staff made our visit even more enjoyable. The kids will have a ball. BTW...they also have a 30 person jacuzzi with 18 and over only allowed in it. It was wonderful! It was great having one so large. Personally, I cant wait to go back.

title: “Hudson small room but comfy”
text:
Some friends went there few years ago and liked it a lot so we gave a try. It is very casual. The rooms are small and the bathroom smaller. The bath products are great!
The situation of the hotel was perfect for us and close to a very good icecream place (try the peanutbutter), sushis place and next to the subway. Tghere is a duaneread at the corner and a place for breakfast juste few meters away.
The terrasse on the 15th floor is nice and the cosmos are good.
We did not try the breakfast and had no problems at all. The personal we met were nice and friendly.

title: “Great hotel, great price, would stay there again!”
text:
This hotel has been getting a bad rap, but it doesn't deserve it. I just returned from a four-night stay at Hudson and they were very accomodating. You just need to do your homework when evaluating a hotel and you should be fine. You should know going into this hotel that the rooms are tiny. The bathrooms are very tiny. If you know this in advance, that should help with not being disappointed. On their website, they show a photo of the room, and that photo is the whole room by the way, and they give the square footage, so there should be no surprises. If you make your reservation online, just call the hotel directly a day or two in advance to confirm your reservation and any special requests. Again, there should be no surprises if you do your homework. It's just common sense. 
The room was clean, but the bed in my room was extremely hard, so after the first night, I asked to be moved to another room for the last 3 nights of my stay. They did move me. The new bed was excellent. I was closer to the 15th-floor rooftop lounge music, but other than one night when the music played until late, it was really quiet. Even that night wasn't too bad as the air conditioner covered up much of the noise.
To sum it up, this is a great hotel. They offer some excellent deals on their website. If you don't mind a tiny room and bathroom - and most people don't go to New York to spend time in their hotel rooms except to sleep - then this hotel is worth the money. Just do your homework and go into this hotel knowing what to expect, and you should enjoy yourself. Hudson doesn't deserve the bad rap it has been getting on this website. Be realistic with your expectations. It is a different and unique hotel. Definitely worth checking out. And it's within walking distance to Times Square and the The Theatre District. I walked back and forth every night. So I have no complaints. It was a great vacation!

title: “Great Expectations-San Antoino BestWestern-Sunset Suites”
text: My wife and I visit san antonio several times a year.We had never stayed at the bestwestern suites before until aug, 09.The service was great from the front desk(ashley) to the maids. We stayed again in dec, 09, service and rooms where just as great as the first visit.We are coming back in april for Feista and looking forward to staying here again.also the trolley stop is right behind the parking lot which is very/very convenient. The they have different routes that take you all over the city,also stop in and visit the sunset train station at th opposite end of block across the street,very nice

title: “Great place for families”
text: Staying at a Days Inn can sometimes be chancy. Not so here at this hotel. My wife and I were very impressed for a facility of this nature. The morning complimentary breakfast had juice, coffee, breadstuff, cereal, and even fresh fruit! The room is wonderful for a family as there is a fully equipped kitchen and an excellent bathroom. For the price in this area, especially for a week-end, I would highly recommend staying here.

title: “Friendly staff and well maintained property.”
text: Stayed at this Fairfield Inn for three nights using Marriott points. My wife and I were impressed by the friendly staff. The hotel is a bottom tier Marriott property but has some nice amenities with an indoor pool, breakfast and complimentary wireless in the room. The room was clean and comfortable. It is relatively easy to access from the interstate. We could hear some traffic noise but it wasn't terribly loud. I would stay here again next trip to Dallas.

title: “On a Group business trip”
text:
June 21st thru the 25th. 2 out of 3 elevators broke down during our stay.
rooms do not have microwaves or mini-fridges. Did not use their other amenities.
Breakfasts are typical Hampton faire. The staff was nice and pleasant. We walked to wherever we went... be it business or pleasure.

title: “first and last time”
text: I found the room clean and comfortable , The staff lacking in social skills and a most disturbing incedent at one thirty am when a security employee tried to enter the room with out any notification , when the front desk was called they said it was a mistake that he was to check empty rooms onlyI dident sleep well after that to say the least and wont stay there again.

title: “A different experience”
text:
I've always wanted to stay in a creepy mansion-type place and this place was perfect. However, I'm a big wussy and get scared easily. This place was scary, and it didn't help that I checked in at night. They have one clerk on duty in a study right beside the front door. They are pretty friendly people.
We stayed in one of the Romeo and Juliet rooms on the first floor. The bathroom was huge and had a jet tub (I don't think they cleaned it very well though. They definitely didn't clean it while we were out the next day--we stayed 2 nights) It is an old house and it shows. Their bed linens are starting to wear thin and had a musty smell to it.
Good points: The rooms are all distinct and they leave the doors open if they are unoccupied so you can roam around and look. Apparently they have a wine and cheese every night for guests to socialize but who wants to do that?
I liked the breakfast in bed. You get a card that you tick off what you want for breakfast the next day and what time for them to bring it and hang it outside your door. The quiche is very yummy! Just continental breakfast basically but pretty nice.
There is about 5 or 6 parking spots and you can park on the street.

title: “GREAT PLACE”
text: First of all I must say this hotel is not for everyone,it has no elevator,pool,breakfast etc,but what it has is charm you cant hardly find today at any price.The building is great and the lobby is amazing,when I walked in,I felt I was back in 1927,the room was very clean and the staff was great,they went out of there way to meet all our needs and the best part, with a smile.And you could see Griffith Park and the Hollywood sign from our bedroom.The price was right and it has free parking.We will be back

title: “Great Family Night”
text: We had received a 50% off coupon last Christmas after bringing toy donations to the Magnolia for a local charity during a holiday stay there. We decided to take the boys for a local getaway before the start of school. We had a suite room with a kitchenette which was ideal. The lounge now has a dinner menu so we enjoyed the wine reception as well as dinner. The pool and hot tub on the roof were very relaxing for all of us. Then back to the lounge for nightcaps and cookies and milk at the evening reception. The beds were so comfortable as always and the kids enjoyed watching TV from the sleeper sofa. The breakfast buffet was fresh, hot, and plentiful. All of our service was great as always. This is my favorite place to stay.

title: “Always a Pleasure”
text: Whenever I visit Chicago, I make it a top priority to stay at the Sheraton Twin Towers in Downtown. Located on the Chicago River, it's very scenic, has top service and is optimally placed for visiting all the local hot spots (restaurants, museums, shopping, etc). My only critique is the cost to park at the hotel is extremely high ($41/night), but parking everywhere in Chicago is rather expensive. If you don't need a car, get a cab/shuttle from either O'Hare or Midway airport (for ~$20-25) and save the money on a nice dinner. Recommend Shula's Restaurant in the Sheraton...it's fantastic!

title: “Had a great time a the Belvedere”
text: I organised a surprise trip to New York for my Boyfriends 30th Birthday at the start of October for 4 nights. I had originally booked the Milford Plaza in New York and after reading reviews I decided not to stay there!! I was so glad that I made the decision to stay at the Belvedere....the hotel was great....!!!! I paid £755 for the 4 nights, which compared to some prices of hotels in NYC was reasonable!!...We stayed on the 11th floor and the room had 2 Queen size beds (one which was great for holding all our shopping)....it also had an ironing board and an Iron (this was a real plus since my boyfriend never irons anything b4 packing it)....it also had a mini Kitchen with a fridge. Our room was cleaned everyday, which was great..!!!...The location of the hotel was just perfect we walked almost everywhere....the only time we took the underground was to visit ground zero....!!...After a hard days shopping and sightseeing we visited a lovely shop right beside the hotel that sells all different kinds of oils and lotions. I got some lovely bath salts and relaxed in the hotel, which was great and set us up for the next day...! Without a thought I would book to stay at the Belvedere again and I have already been recommending it to others! During our stay we got engaged which made our trip to NYC even more special..!!!

title: “filthy, infested, dangerous... and no one cares”
text:
First of all, being a Hyatt Gold Passport cardholder doesn't mean squat. Requesting allergy free room connecting rooms was ignored. Given dirty smelly connecting rooms and when I refused them because of smell, I was "upgraded" to what I had actually requesred in the first place. They claimed they were full and "accommodated" me because of my status. The rooms we got were supposed to be allergy free. Please see my photos. They were filthy and dirty. The sheets had blood and ink staines (see photos). The floor had someone ELSES black curly long hairs all over the floors. I used my washcloths to wipe the floors-they were SO filthy! These floors are NOT EVER cleaned. This wasn't from just one customer...this was months of dirtiness on the bathroom and foyer floors. There were what looked to be BLOOD stains on the wall near the floor next to the bed...remember these are premium upgraded allergy free rooms! HA! The leather ottoman had pen marks all over it and holes in it and the complimentary robe was tattered and torn (see photo). PLEASE be warned if you go to this hotel you will be disappointed if you expect a normal degree of cleanliness. I am sure this will be followed up with their obligatory service manager apology. Um.. let me stop you before you bother. When I filled out the Hyatt Guest Satisfaction email, I complained about all of these things... yet have not gotten ONE single response. They only respond here because they want YOU to think this is an anomoly. Nope. It's not. Enjoy the lazy river and all the mosquitos form the stagnant water...because that's where they breed. In stagnant water. They are not breeding in the pool water so it is probably their french drains. Are they bothering to spray? Nope.
Oh, I almost forgot about the elevator that FELL a foot and a half. After complaining, they never bothered to service that elevator. Two others were out of order at that same time.

title: “Wonderful loacation and staff”
text:
Spent 3 night is this wonderful hotel, staff couldn't do enough for us so helpful and happy to speak to you. From getting a cab to recommending restaurants or filling up the mini bar everything was done with the greatest of efficiency.
Hotel decor is really lovely bedrooms are of a good size with all amenaties you would expect. The only downside and it is only a little one is that the walls are a little thin so we could here nextdoors cell phone if it went off and if children run up and down the corridors it sounds like a heard of elephants. This is but a minor concern though as the location of the hotel, the decor and staff far out weight it.
Couldn't have a better location in San Fran in my opinion just round the corner from the trolley car turnaround and at the end of the main road through fishermans Wharf.
I couldn't recommend this hotel highly enough and if I ever get the chance to visit San Fran this will be the only place I stay!!

title: “Just right”
text: This hotel is fantastic. It's located in a great neighborhood, with a food market just across the road and a close subway stop too. I would highly recommend staying here! We got food delivered from the cafe downstairs, which was also good.

title: “Staff was Rude.”
text:
The room was mostly clean, but the staff was rude. Big crack in the window. Walls are very thin.
Don't want to stay here again.
The curtains are white and very sheer- no way to shut the light out.
breakfast was ok, internet worked well.

title: “Hotel with average rooms but a fantastic location just up the street from times square”
text:
The Wellington is quite an old hotel and the room we stayed in was not small but not very big either. It was a basic room with a double bed, tv bathroom. But to be honest, in New York that is all you need as you spend a lot of time out and about. If your a light sleeper I'd take ear plugs because the air conditioning units are built into the windows so the noise from the street comes through.
For me the hotel did what it needed to and the staff were helpful and friendly. I spent most time out and about site seeing. The location is great and with this hotel that us is what your paying for. You have central park one direction and times square/ broadway in the other.
New York as a while is a busy city so some people might not like the hustle and bussle.
I loved it but wouldn't return as I've seen all I needed to see.

title: “Great Location, Excellent Hotel”
text: Within walking distance of the State Capitol, and not far from the U.T. Campus, as well as all the night spots on historic 6th St. We had a 2 BR suite on the 8th floor. Staff are very friendly and courteous. Room was pretty good sized, flat screen TVs, up to date room furnishings, very nice bathrooms (read that as plural). Decent view of the city. If you drive, there is parking available underground, or you can use valet. One word of warning though. If you use the underground parking, it is cramped, so don't expect to fit a larger vehicle like a full size pickup, big SUV, or something like that. You'll have a tough time. It isn't the cheapest thing around, but in my view, you get what you pay for. By the way, they do take pets.

title: “Good Inn!”
text: Overall a good Inn. Service was good, the room was clean and came with a microwave and mini fridge. Only compliant was that breakfast was only coffee and the area seems kind of sketchy but the parking lot was fully lit at night. Location is good, 20min from LAX and 30min to Hollywood, etc. Satisfied with our stay here.

title: “Great property”
text: I've stayed at this Hilton multiple times. Very consistent solid service, good food at the Urban Tavern rest. Workout facility is excellent.

title: “Unprofessional”
text: I stayed at the Mayfair in celebration of my birthday. I was mislead about the size of the rooms. I asked for a king and was dropped down to a full. They then attempted to charge me full price. With some complainin and running around from manager to manger the price was reduced. One of the employees was even drinking on the job (I sneakly snagged his name Dave,) I over heard numerous sexually orientated comments from this same employee......Altough the price is very fair and the location is excellent i would advise NOT too stay here. The way I felt durin my stay was very akward. I must say Thank You too Robert And Joseph for there excellent customer service.

title: “Great Staff, Great Location/Value”
text: I was very happy with how clean the staff kept the hotel. Breakfast was very good and the staff was on top of making sure things were organized. The location was great! Just a short walk to restaurant row and Times Square. I will definitely stay there again.

title: “Great location for visiting museums”
text: This hotel was very contemporary, welcoming and well located. We were in town to visit family but also wanted to walk to the museums, visit the Capitol, etc. In addition, we had our dog with us and they were very pet friendly!

title: “a great location, nice suites, great staff”
text:
I had to come on an emergency to take care of a family member. This hotel is comfortable, clean and has good people working there. The kitchens are big. There is a seven eleven up the street and a saveway and cvs pharmacy down the street at Watergate. Great location. I would stay here again. It's all about location and I am looking at Watergate, the Kennedy Center, Hudson River and Bridge from our 10th floor room right now.
The planes are flying to Ronald Reagan airport. It's only a $15 cab ride from the airport..

title: “Their finest hour.”
text:
What can one add to this huge nuber of extremely positive reviews for this true gem of a Manhattan Hotel? Well, I try.
In first place, things went pretty wrong. We coming from Vienna/Austria were on our annual works outing, (overseas and extended this year in order to celebrate full decade birthdays of two of my secretaries) I had booked two double rooms and one suite for our party of six. We were given three double rooms, although I had presented the e-mail booking confirmation at the reception desk. I was assured that the one room with the king size bed was meant to be the "suite". It was at the (wonderful) breakfast the other day, when we realized that all of us had been given double rooms. I was pretty upset at this moment, because my intention to reward my secretaries for another year of hard work at my law office seemed frustrated. So I turned to the reception desk, and within little more than five minutes, the helpful man at the reception not only had apologized for the mistake, but also had come up with a solution, we never ever could have dreamt of. Simply amazingly perfect management! 
My main problem for the rest of our stay was to get me and my party out of this hotel to the streets of NYC. And think, this is a Hotel without a restaurant, without a bar, without a spa, without shops, without so many things other hotels boast of, but with a truly unparalleled combination of competence and atmosphere. And consider further that the streets I am talking about that the five women in my company almost refused to go to were Broadway and Fifth Avenue!
Now, if You ask, why such small hotel can rank sixth among approx. 400 other New York hotels, I only can advise you: Find out yourself.

title: “Very nice”
text: Have stayed here two times before -- once before renovation. Great views, good location. Fairly priced hotel in university location, so lots of university-shopping nearby (e.g., grocery, pharmacy, bookstore, restaurants). Great parking lot (free). I asked for high floor facing mt. ranier and got a view of it only if I got right to the window and looked 90 degrees to the right. I paid extra for the view and still didn't get as good of a view as on my previous two trips (where the U of Washington picked up the room cost directly -- maybe they get priority on rooms). But my room faced EastNorth, so i didn't get as much noise from 45th street, so that's the advantage. Also, the air conditioning could work a bit better but it is an old hotel. All in all, a great place to stay.

title: “Great Find!”
text: Looking for an affordable hotel to stay in while in NYC that was clean, convenient, had a private bath and was under $250/night landed me at this hotel. I was not disappointed at all; it met all of the requirements! Suggested to our friends they stay here as well and they were equally as satisfied. We would definitely return.

title: “Ok, but dated”
text:
Stayed 3 nights, ok property but needs updating.
Popcorn ceilings, fire alarm on the wall in your main field of view, black line/spots where the wall meets the ceiling, the carpet from the room to the bathoom was torn all the way across the opening. Stain on the curtain (blood or makeup?), TV remote was very slow to respond. Really baic user things in my humble estimation- - The GM should be aware of these things on walkthroughs and correct prior to guest staying. i'd fire them.
Staff was the saving grace. very friendly, and helpful. Attentive to every need. From the valets, fron desk, bellmen, and especially Debbie the head conceirge - she will try her best and beyond to get you set up!

title: “airport hotel”
text: although i believe it or not the room that we had i never heard an airplane but i did hear the bin men!!! staff were pleasant, only had luxury room left but let us have it at a reduced price coz we said we were out first thing in morning so all good, room clean, bed nice clean sheets, shower good, thats were it ends for me coz thats all that matters and this is a airport hotel so no views or anything else to comment on, except maybe the really weak coffee in the morning that you have to go downstairs to, really not worth bothering, although when we were down in the coffee room we did see coffee makers in boxes which would have been lovely to have had in the room, ho hum !!!

title: “Great facility - rude staff”
text:
I enjoyed my stay at the Intercontinental Hotel. The room I had was quite nice and was just as the photos showed. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom huge. I liked the in-room safe that fit my 15" laptop computer. The desk was very nice in that the plugs and modem connections popped out of the desk. The room lighting was very thoughtful, including the mood lighting in the panels to the sides of the bed, the motion sensitive lighting and the reading lamps, all of which were accessible from the bed. One pet peeve, the cordless phone near the bed did not work. 
The fitness center was also very nice with free bottled water, which I was able to take with me to my room rather than use the mini-bar. 
My biggest issue was with the front desk. On the whole I found the staff to be very curt and rather unsympathetic with any concerns. On several ocassions, only one person was working the desk and the waits in line were lengthy. Although I checked in early, there was no room available and they would not commit to when the room would be available other than by 3p. They did not offer to call me on my cell when the room was ready. Thus, I had to wait in line twice to check-in. 
The bell staff was friendly and helpful. They kept my bags, allowed me to access them and helped with ice when I finally did check in. 
On a separate instance, I asked an individual at the front desk about getting a reservation at the hotel for the following week. I was advised that I could be put on a wait list for a regular room at nearly 3x the price. I advised that I would not pay that price, at which time I was advised to contact the Holiday Inn. 
While at the hotel, I needed to print a document. I was directed to the hotel's business center on the third floor. I was able to printed a couple of documents-but because I was in a hurry, I did not inquire on price. When I went to check out, I shocked to find that each page cost $1.50 to print. this showed up as a charge for over $100 on the bill. When I told the person who checked me out that the cost was outrageous, I was informed that the business center was an independent contractor and that the charge "is what it is." I begrudgingly paid it, but then complained to Intercontinental Hotels. I recently received a refund of half of the charge of the printing. 
Bottom line, I got the impression that the staff wasn't interested in provinding any value, or helping the customer. Perhaps they are only interested in guests that have tons of money to blow without giving it any thought. While the facility was very nice, I would be reluctant to stay at the hotel again.

title: “Nice Stay in La Jolla”
text:
Our family stayed at this property for one week during our visit to the San Diego area and we enjoyed our stay. This is a good hotel for families. The suite provided plenty of space for my wife and I and our 2 boys, age 3 and 7. 
The room and public areas, including the pool area, are very nice and clean. There is a great breakfast (come early or you may have to stand in line), including a nice buffet and cooked to order omelets. My wife and I did enjoy a relaxing cocktail after a day out with the boys, as well.
There are also may restaurants and a mall within walking distance. If you are going to be in San Diego this is a very good option that we recommend.

title: “Couldn't be happier”
text: My wife and I live in Denver and we wanted to get away for the weekend. Staying at the Four Seasons felt as if we were in another state. Could not have been happier with our stay. The food, spa, pool, and staff were fantastic.

title: “Comfy and hip in downtown San Francico”
text: Lovely rooms and excellent service. Loved the bliss beauty products and the Buda statue that glowed a cool pink. It is a good location and has a hip bar. I definitely would return.

title: “A Detroit Jewel!”
text:
We purchased a romantic package room with champagne, chocolates, a dozen roses and a whirlpool bath in one of the restored historic homes at the Inn on Ferry Street. It's located in Detroit's cultural center of the city next to the Detroit Institute of Arts. 
The Inn is a Detroit jewel! CDs for our room player featured excellent, locally produced music of Mack Ave Records. Free Wi-Fi is available throughout. The reception area in the Scott House served coffee and pastries from the Great Lakes Roasters and Avalon Bakery close by. Free shuttle service was provided for any venues within a five mile radius. 
Our room and the public sitting areas in the Pungs House were decorated with influences from the Victorian era. Everyone there was pleasant, helpful and dressed professionally. The food offerings were fresh and tasty. One could choose to mingle in the dining area or sit and read the wide selection of newspapers by the fireplace.

title: “My wife did a good job finding this place.”
text:
I called my wife and asked her to make a reservation for me somewhere in Houston, because I was down here for some business. I had left on Friday morning without making a hotel reservation anywhere. I needed to be close to where I was going to be conducting business, because you know how Houston is - it takes forever to get from one side to the other! Anyway, after some much sleuthing my wife called me and told me that she had found a hotel close to I-10 after Addicks Rd, which is what I needed. I enjoy staying at Holiday Inn Express, but some can be downright nasty! This one was not. When I pulled into the parking lot I was pleased to see a beautiful hotel lobby with an enormous breakfast area.
Check in was very smooth and I got into my room very easily. I was pleased with the size of the room - not too big yet not too small at the same time. It was just right for what I needed. The bed was as comfortable as can be and I loved the padded headboard.
The only negative I can say about this hotel is that it is located on I-10 which seems to be constantly under some sort of construction, so getting in and out is somewhat of a challenge. Aside from all of that - everything else was terrific!

title: “Dirty Rooms”
text:
My husband & I stayed here for 6 nights. We would have stayed less if we hadn't booked through a non-refundable web company. When we arrived we were put into a queen room even though we booked a king room. After talking to the front desk and manager, we were moved to a 2 bed room, which was a lot bigger than the queen. We asked if we could keep the 2 bed room, but we were moved into a king room the next night. 
The nightstands were really dusty (and stayed that way our entire stay).The bathroom walls were dirty and had black marks all over them. I thought they were scuff marks until I was easily able to wipe them away with a piece of tissue. The lighting in the room was practically nonexistant. Our tollet backed up and we had to have maintenance come fix it. On one of the following days we were out all day and came back in the evening to find a "turd" in our toilet. Neither of us had done this before we left in the morning, so either there was another plumbing problem or someone used our toilet while we were gone (I swear I am not making this up). This is when we checked to see if we could get our money back for the rest of the stay and move to another hotel. Unfortunately, we could not.
On the positive side, the majority of the staff were really nice. Jazzlyn, Walter, Carlos, and Ramel were very friendly and had great attitudes. The staff in the bar/dining area were also really nice. The location was really good and our room was really quiet.
The elevators are tiny as were the king and queen rooms, but if they had been clean we could have better dealt with that. 
We would not stay here again, nor recommend it to others.

title: “A pleasent stay”
text: Stayed here for three nights on our three week tour of the east coast. Nice reasonably sized rooms. Well decorated but no free wifi in the rooms, only expensive ethernet. Other than that a nice hotel in a good area. Didn't eat or drink in hotel although parking was $28 per night. Wahington in general was good however the mandatory "gratuity" added to your restaraunt bills does get a bit tiresome at times.

title: “Ya just don't get what you expect..”
text: They say they have a steam room. They don't. They tout their wonderful view of Denver from the Altitudes bar on the 27th floor..closed for a private function for the entire 4 days I was there (Sunday through Wednesday). Room service, after a 15 minute hold, finally came about 40 minutes after the order was placed. Waiters CONSTANTLY ask "is everything ok, is everything ok, how is your day going, it everything ok"...Arrrrggghhh!! SO disingenuous and annoying. Can't they see I'm mid-conversation or reading the newspaper? If I need something I'll look up and summon some help, otherwise, LEAVE ME BE! Coffee, WEAK!, next pot, BITTER!, next pot, OK. And I only need ONE waiter! Or y'all need to communicate because I don't need two pots of cream. And to the valets and bell staff, MIND YOUR OWN BUSINESS! My day is fine thanks, and it's none of your business. And please don't yank my car door open as soon as I pull up. I'll open the friggin' door as soon as I get off my business call. And again, it's none of your damn business if I've had a big day or not. Look, I appreciate the effort, but it's all a bit disingenuous and frankly ridiculous. I wish this place would just stick to providing what they claim to provide and leave it at that. Oh, and they claim lobby wifi..not. In addition to that the room wifi is VERY slow. The rooms are fine otherwise. The bathrooms are very average with the obligatory big door you have to shimmy around. The food is decent and I would say the breakfast buffet is very good. Excellent walking proximity to nice downtown restaurants.

title: “Wonderful location, great staff”
text: We recently held our family reunion at this location. We were there 2 nights with twenty rooms. The staff (Andrea) was beyond wonderful in making sure our every need and concern was addressed pleasantly and professionally. The rooms were nicely appointed (stovetop, microwave and refrigerator) and the beds were extremely comfortable. The pool was a popular and enjoyable spot for the youngsters and adults as well. The location was perfect for our out-of-town guests as they explored the extensive shopping and restuarants. I would enthusiastically encourage staying at the Extended Stay Polaris whether just booking one room or multiple rooms. The staff will go out of their way to make it a pleasurable experience. This hotel/location can't be beat.

title: “Very comfortable, good location, pleasant staff. Good holiday atmosphere.”
text: Upon arrival offered glass of champagne while checking in. Pleasant helpful staff. room comfortable, clean. Good location for everything in Boston. Lots of restaurants locally. Certainly would stay again if in Boston.

title: “Excellent service, excellent value.”
text: The 4 Points may not be the newest or poshest, but they offer nice rooms, great service, and excellent value. I always stay here when I fly out of LAX and I have never been disappointed.

title: “The hotel is nice but not the extra charges...”
text:
The staff is very nice and helpful. Our kids were impressed with the staff handed out the hot cookies at check-in counter. 
Our room was in the main tower so and too much walking for us. The size of the room is quite big and nice. The beds are quite comfortable. However, I will not book this hotel again even if there is a special rate due to the extra charges. In the same class hotel in the area, there are free internet in the room and the self-parking fee is much lower.
These are the fees that I unfortunately found out afterward (my bad...booked the room in a rush).
Fee for in-room wireless Internet: USD 14.95 (for 24 hours, rates may vary)
Fee for in-room high-speed Internet (wired): USD 14.95 (for 24 hours, rates may vary)
Self parking fee: USD 21 per night (in/out privileges)
Valet parking fee: USD 26 per night (in/out privileges)
Pet deposit: USD 50 per stay
Refrigerator fee: USD 15 per night
Rollaway bed fee: USD 25 per night

title: “Not Bad!”
text: I've stayed here a few times now...The hotel is slightly dated, and I don't really like outside-access room (where your door opens to the outdoors instead of to a hallway), but with the rooms I've been given here, I can hardly complain...As a Hilton Gold member, I've always been upgraded here to a GIANT 2-story suite...The layout is amazing. I shared the room with a friend from Grad School and we could have gone without seeing each other for days inside this room! Internet worked great, the room was clean (although not the most modern I've had). The included breakfast was good, although it's a bit of a pain getting to your room...The property is several unconnected buildings...If you can't get parking in front of your building, it can be a hike to your door. But I'll come back again and again--hopefully getting the two-story room again!

title: “Only One Glitch”
text: The Peninsula is an excellent choice when visiting Chicago. Great location for walking up and down Michigan Ave. Close to great restaurants on Rush and an easy walk to the river for any kind of boat cruise. I loved the tv's in the both the bedroom and bathroom. I also loved the 2 dressing areas in the bathroom. The best part of our stay was, of all things, housekeeping! These people know how to make you feel like one of the rich and famous. Every day the room was spotlessly cleaned. Clothes folded, toiletries organized, shoes lined up in rows, etc. Every night there is a turndown service with slippers placed by the bed and fresh towels put in the bathroom. The only glitch in our stay was the fact that we like to sleep in and there was some reconstruction work being done in the room above ours starting about 8:00 AM. We opted not to change rooms and they offered a free massage (which I was too busy to use) and a bottle of wine along with a very nice apology. Over all, I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel!

title: “An elegant hotel that provides a relaxing stay.”
text:
We stayed at the Back Bay Hotel to attend a wedding at the hotel and it was a great experience. The Back Bay is a luxury boutique hotel that avoids the mass crowds of the more run of the mill chains, and the staff provides very personalized service. The location itself is convenient to several attractions in Boston, and in particular it is only a couple of blocks away from the Commonwealth Avenue Mall. The bar downstairs is quite good and it was pretty packed at nighttime. 
What really impressed us, however, was the hotel staff's service on the day of the wedding. There were a number of logistical details that we were helping the bride and groom with, and at every turn the hotel staff (bell hops and managers alike) was quite willing to help us out. The wedding turned out wonderfully and it was due in no small part to the hotel staff's assistance.
You won't go wrong staying here.

title: “Weekend Staycation”
text: From time of arrival we felt so special. The front desk was personable, friendly and never did a smile diminish from her face :) Wed decided to have a drink in the lobby bar, that was not so exceptional, so we left. Arried into MaryJanes to a bubbly, smiling bartender who took exquisite care of us. Our room was fantastic! We felt like "Rock Stars", at least for the weekend state of the art technology, comfortable beds, linens to die for - and our bathroom I could have stayed in there the entire trip! My huisband had a few questions, so via phone to the operators who was on top of things - answered all questions timely and politely. We again visited Maryjanes for breakast and again the warmth and friendlinest - couldn't have asked for a better weekend - thank you HardRock!!!

title: “Great in every way .. HIGHLY recommended”
text: Blue Moon is on a quiet side street, immaculately clean and cozy decor .. there are no room numbers, each is named and themed after a classic comic .. We stayed in Sid Caesar which I think is the smallest room; still it was roomy with a queen bed, small fridge and two large windows. Bathroom was bright white tile, huge deep shower tub and classic details. The desk staff were all smiles and very helpful with dinner recommendations. Free light breakfast and coffee was a welcome surprise. The top "penthouse" room looks like it would be amazing. Love the neighborhood .. very funky with great shopping right next to Chinatown and a few blocks from Little Italy. Also the LEAST expensive hotel in lower Manhattan .. a great value.

title: “Favorite place to stay in the City”
text: This is a long overdue review as I've been staying at the phoenix regularly for a few years now, but this is my favorite place to stay in the City. It's close to Polk, Union Square, BART/Muni and unbeatable cocktails (Bourbon & Branch, Tradition, etc). The remodeled Chambers bar is a fun place to hang out and is great for a nitecap. The rooms are spacious and comfortable, parking is a *huge* bonus in SF, but my favorite thing about the phoenix is the staff! Everyone working there is incredibly friendly and helpful and I feel it's very much a home-away-from-home (there's nothing more welcoming than being greeted warmly, by name, after a long day of travel). Join the joy of life club and have a welcoming bottle of wine in your room.

title: “Small and friendly”
text: Stayed for 5 nights. Staff very helpful. Small and cozy. Clean. Good area. Walking distance to all interesting places in SoHo and Greenwich Village. Only stairs, no elevator, so its for the young and able.

title: “Good for a lay over”
text:
After missing a connection to My final destination, I was advised that my best and quickest chance of getting to where I was going was to take a somewhat circuitous route from LAX to Dallas and stay overnight in Dallas for a very early flight the next day.
After checking TripAdvisor I was disappointed to find that the Grand Hyatt at DfW was fully booked. The next option was the Hyatt Regency.
As I landed at 9.30pm, it was wicked hot and I had no idea of how frequently the shuttle ran, I hopped in a cab and for $7.00 (money well spent in my book) I arrived at the GH approximately 5 minutes later. Yes it is super close to Terminal D.
A speedy check in was provided. The room was above average and comfortable.
As I was literally using the room as a place to shower and sleep, I didn't try the restaurants or room service.
Express check out and a shuttle that runs every 20mins starting on the hour, had me back at the airpot in just a few minutes. Very friendly bell boys, concierge and drivers.
I am not sure that the hotel is sound proofed - I could still hear planes, which is probably hardly surprising given that the hotel is right on the edge of a runway!
No free wi- fi which I always find seriously irritating.
Overall, would recommend if you find yourself having to take a room for just a few hours at DFW as you wait for a connection.

title: “Lovely Hotel, Expensive Phone Calls!!!!!”
text:
As a former San Franciscan, I have always wanted to stay in this gorgeous hotel. I finally got the chance ! The rooms were very nice, and quiet. Honestly, we didn't encounter much service, as we are very familiar with this area of the city, and didn't require help navigating. The rooms are fairly austere, but very high quality, and very comfortable. This may sound odd, but the air conditioner was very quiet and the air felt clean.
The Pied Piper Room with its Maxfield Parrish mural, and rich wood interior is not to be missed. I went there for drinks when I lived in SF, as well as each time I have returned home. The truffle french fries rock!
The hotel is in the Financial District, so be aware that during the weekend a lot of restaurants in the immediate area are closed, or have limited hours. 
For those concerned about coffee (and believe me, I AM concerned about coffee) there is a Starbucks about a half block away on Montgomery, and place called Specialy's about 3/4 blocks down @ Montgomery & Mission. They have coffee, pastry, and are known for their excellent cookies and bread. On the other side of Market St. on New Montgomery, there is another Starbucks as well as Peets Coffee, and Tulley's coffee in the Crocker Galleria.
If you are staying at the hotel during the week, consider lunch at Belden Lane , a small street in the Financial District that has several great restaurants (French, Spanish & Italian). If it's warm, you can eat outside. Belden Place is about 4 blocks from the hotel, and out of awful Union Square, where oddly, there is not much good fare.
On to the bad news about the hotel....
$17 PER COMPUTER/ PER DAY for internet service. Now, c'mon --There is something very wrong for a hotel of this caliber in tech saavy SF to charge for internet at all! Why don't they have wireless??? 
A 17 minute long distance phone call was $47. The cell phone reception in the room was not great, and we had to make an important phone call to the tune of $47. 
We had to send a fax from the business center which was grossly expensive (I'm not sure, I think that it was $8 per page),and the woman at the business center was less than pleasant with her huffy-puffy attitude. 
All in all, this is a beautiful hotel, in the best location, and most importantly, the best public restrooms in the city.

title: “I was ok until a roach the size of Rhode Island ran across the bedroom floor”
text:
This a nice place for extended stays. The free happy hour is cool and the location is great. The rooms ( mine is a one bedroom ) look like cheap apartments with dingy white paint and downscale furnishings. The beds are very comfortable and the pillows are good quality. But y'all I just killed a huge roach in my bedroom. The missed wakeup call is one thing but this is unacceptable.
The staff seems caring so maybe they will look into this unfortunate issue SOON. 
RL

title: “Hotel Restaurant Dining”
text:
I have made the Hilton Woodland Hills part of my monthly travel routine for nearly two years and the hard working morning breakfast staff is one of the highlights. The food is always well stocked, fresh and tasty.
Roxana is always welcoming, attentive and friendly and the comfort of her patrons is clearly a high priority. I highly recommend having a breakfast in this location if you are in need of a fast fresh meal to start the day.

title: “Great location”
text: I recently attended a conference in Philadelphia and originally chose a different hotel but changed it to Palomar when I realized it's location. It is at a perfect location for shopping, going to restaurants, attending various artistic venues such as concerts, plays, opera etc. The hotel itself is also very clean with a friendly staff. My room was very nice with a good layout. It was clean and smelled fresh, none of that mildewy old smell that a lot of hotels get over time. I liked the fixtures and fast internet speed. The only drawback in the room was a noisy air conditioning unit right above the bed. For two nights it prevented me from deep sleep and woke me up when it kicked on. Then I realized I had a set of ear plugs with me and wore them the third night and I slept well without waking up as it kicked on. I walked everywhere, to the convention center, shopping, restaurants and events and felt perfectly safe because there were so many people walking around until late in the evening.

title: “The Belvedere - Service at it's best”
text:
Staying at The Belvedere was a great experience. The hotel itself was beautiful. The rooms were spacious and confortable. The service was more than we expected. I loved everything about staying there. On the same block there was a corner florist. The flowers were gorgeous and really set the mood everytime we walked past it back to the hotel. 
The best feature was the pricing. Because it was a few blocks from the "hub" of Manhattan, we were able to pay a lower rate than had we stayed right near Times Square. However, it was so close, it was just a few minutes walk to that area. And being in NY, walking was half the fun. 
I have recommended this hotel to many friends and family. I look forward to another visit.

title: “Yes and No”
text:
We (me and my boyfriend) stayed at W NY times square with another couple this past weekend. We stayed from Friday to Sunday and we were in NY for business and some shopping. We had originally planned to fly back home on Sat night but there was a freak snow storm (in October!!!) in NY and our flight was cancelled so we had to book another night here. 
The W is somewhat of a commodity and known as a destination in its own right. It's a famous hotel yes and being situated right in the heart of times square, it is a very busy place. And also since it was a weekend, you can only imagine how busy this hotel was. 
I was actually a little disappointed with the crowd at this hotel. There was a lot of families and lots of big travel groups which caused long line ups and noise in the lobby. 
We got in the city early and tried to see if they would let us check in early but the rooms weren't ready so we had to wait about 4 hours until 3pm to check in. And then of course at 3pm, bus load full of tourists arrived with their giant bags and large groups causing massive line ups and delays. 
The room was fine. Everyone says it's really small on travel advisor but it's New York. It really doesn't get much bigger than this. I thought the size of the room (i think i stayed in a fabulous room) was ample for two people although yes, the bathroom is a little tight. I found the room to be clean, modern and comfortable to stay in. The rooms do get all the street noise (I was on the 28th floor) but again, it's right at the heart of times square, it's expected and it's really not the hotel's fault. 
The staff at this W was great. My hair dryer was not working and when I called to have a replacement, there was someone at the door within 3 minutes which was impressive because the hotel was at max. occupancy this weekend. 
The concierge and everyone else from the door staff to maintenance staff were all wonderful. Everyone always held the elevator door open for you, they always said hello, the door staff were always more than willing to carry your bag and hail a cab for you. It was very pleasant to interact with everyone who works there. 
My true review is really a 3.5. But the staff really makes it a 4 I guess. 
Although modern, the hotel is starting to look a little tired... especially the bathroom (the lobby bathroom and the room bathrooms), also I thought the bar was really not all that great but the drinks were very over priced. (also the bottle of water in the room was 9 dollars). 
I think that for the same price, you can probably stay at a better boutique hotel. If you like modern boutique hotels, there are so many other options at a better price. 
Overall, it was not a bad experience but for the price I am sure we could have stayed at a cooler, newer hotel.

title: “Great Place To Stay”
text: Stayed here to attend a wedding held at the Mask & Wig Club which is literally a half block away. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Parking garage is 2 blocks away but walking, bus & taxi are easy (& preferred) ways to get around this city. Very close to Reading Terminal & convention center.
