Free breakfast was quite good with lots of choices including fresh local pastries & breads - even fresh grapefruit halves and other fruit. In the past we have stayed at another boutique hotel in Old City and I really prefer these smaller hotels. My husband thought the bathroom was too small but it didn't bother me or our daughter. Loved the architecture and the old switchboard on the 4th floor.

title: “Good Location”
text: Such a good location just a few blocks away from Rittenhouse Square. I especially like it, for it is easy to get to Amtrak Train station on 30th St via subway. Always a friendly staff and rooms that are always clean and well kept with coffee maker and refrigerator.

title: “SMH”
text: It feels like your in a lunch box. The room is extra small. You can hear people walk by your room and I'm sure if you had a intimate night everyone would know....smh. This is definitily not a place for couple to spend there wedding anniversary. This place should be a hotel for shorts stays, like by the hour if you know what I mean. If your only going to use this room for only to sleep then all is good. Oh, and last but not least, there is no air condition or fan. Have at it

title: “BED BUGS”
text:
I work for a 6 week university-affiliated summer program that has been staying at the Hotel Harrington for over five years. I am writing this review after being moved to a different room by hotel staff upon discovering my bed INFESTED with bed bugs. 
I stayed in a quad on the third floor and woke up the next morning covered in large, red welts on my forearms, hands, legs, and torso. My roommate tried to convince me these were spider bites, and I would have believed her had I not woken up the second night and seen these things crawling around near my face. 
They were present in all three single beds as well as the double bed. The desk receptionist seemed reluctant to assist me, even after I showed him the allergic reaction and bites on my body, until he found out that we had taken photographic "evidence" of the bugs in the bed and on our pillows...

title: “Excellent Hotel - Great Staff, Service & Location”
text:
Let me start with the staff - ALWAYS willing to help. Check in / check out was a breeze - no counter - just walk in & they greet you with a glass of wine - doesn't get any better than that. There's always someone at the front door - always willing to help you or provide directions / advice on restaraunts, shows, transportation, etc....
Location - it's great - 5 min away from Times Square - so close enough, but, far enough away from all the choas. Close to alot of attractions to visit - as it is New York, there is no shortage of places to go / see. Of note - bring REALLY GOOD walking shoes - you're gonna need them.
The hotel - 4 rooms per floor - very comfortable and quiet. Rooms are very clean, had a King Bed - best bed I've EVER slept on - in a hotel. Watch the corners of the bed frame - you'll hit your shin(s) once - I guarantee it - lol. The restaraunt is very good also.
The hotel also has two nice balconies for guests - on the 19th & 20th floors - briing a bottle of wine, relax & enjoy the view - and the fact that you are in one of the greatest cities on earth.
It was just my wife and I visiting - celebrating a "milestone" B Day for her - the hotel went out of their way to make her feel special - I cannot thank them more.
OK, would I return ?? - Yes, in an instant - I highly recommend this hotel - you will NOT be disappointed,

title: “Comfortable Hotel very close to John Hancock Building”
text: Lovely hotel, staff helpful and courteous with exception to the Front Desk... they weren't great. But that aside I would recommend this hotel and also it is in a very nice location.

title: “EVERY STAY AND VISIT IS FABULOUS”
text: I stayed at the Tremont Suites Hotel in Baltimore again and it was perfect. The really nice thing is that the service and everything about the hotel is CONSISTANT. I adore the help and especially the DOORMAN, Sean Deanes, who welcomes you back with a warm smile and makes everyone feel special. All of the Front Desk people are wonderful including management, I have never had a room that was not 5 star or above. I highly suggest the Hotel. Warmly, Rose S

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Nice place to stay if you get in late or have to leave early. Clean , quite, and the staff at the front desk was very nice. There was no airport noise. Would stay again only wish we had more time to enjoy it.

title: “Great location.”
text: Great stay. Very close to North Beach and China Town. Close to lots of public transportation and great restaurants. The only thing I can suggest is they needs to upgrade there keys to key cards come on its not 1980.

title: “It was the best hotel experience I've had in NYC.”
text: Room was comfortable and great size - especially for NYC. People were friendly, funny, engaging and knowledgeable. The entire experience was a pleasure. Definitely will return.

title: “Absolute worst motel I've ever stayed in.”
text:
Desk clerk is sour, unfriendly. We only got one key, although there were two adults in our room. The one key would not stay magnetised for more than one swipe. Had to go back to the desk to have key remagnetised EVERY time we needed to get into our room. 
There was no coffee available, no clock in the room. Phone was not functional; the volume was so low that one couldn't hear thru it and the volume wouldn't adjust. Two tiny bars of facial soap, no bath soap. Not even any shampoo.

title: “Great price, great hotel”
text: Great hotel! The staff was very helpful and our room was comfortable for 3 adults. Good location. We will stay here next time we're in New York.

title: “Can't go wrong”
text:
The Chicago Four Seasons located atop the luxury mall '900 North Michigan Shops', did not disappoint in any area. The customer service was attentive without being overbearing. The rooms were very comfortable. Room service was prompt and the food was excellent. The Sports Club and Spa were top of the line. 
Our room had a beautiful view of Lake Michigan. 
My only suggestion: create a lap pool. The swimming pool is beautiful, but not as functional as most swimmers would like.

title: “A charming transformation”
text: Kimpton's Topaz property continues their practice of buying older properties and fixing them up with Kimpton touches. The staff is uniformly helpful, well-informed and empowered. Topaz was an apartment hotel called The Canterbury in its previous incarnation, along a lovely street of rowhouses in Northwest Washington. The rooms are spacious and well-equipped. The rates are good for this location. The area abounds with good restaurants of many ethnicities and in many price ranges. If you are there on a weekend or arrive at night you can even park on the street. I have started making this my preferred hotel in DC.

title: “Staybridge To The Rescue”
text: After a bad storm in our area, we were forced to find a hotel that allowed our dog to reside with us. The hotel that we would have selected that was a little closer to home had no vacancies because of the storm, everyone was rushing there. After having had lunch at the Chili's in front on this hotel, I'd noticed that it looked very clean from the outside. So I called and asked about the pet polices and to see if they had any vacancies, they were very accomodating in getting me the best price with such short notice. The room was very spacious and clean, and they a great accomodations that we were not there long enough to utilize. The only problem I had with the hotel was the fact that we only stayed from 1:00 AM - 10:00 AM but were charged for an overnight stay, in other words, we were still required to check out by noon. When I asked about it, the representative at the front desk basically said that's just how it is. But the reprentative that check us out was great, her name was Valim. I would definitely recommend.

title: “Unsavory Savoy”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for one night in mid-August, booking the 2-2-2 special the Savoy advertises on their website. This package includes dinner at the Millennium restaurant (vegetarian), located in their lobby, plus an overnight stay, for $200. Considering that dinner would add up to around $75 or so, plus getting a decent room near Union Square, I thought this would be a good deal. After our experience, I'm not so sure. I always try to be fair in my writeups, and the Savoy did have several good points, but it also had some negatives to consider before booking a room:
1) When we arrived, there was a sign for the valet, but no one there. My wife went inside to find someone, and they said they would call someone to pick up the car. I waited outside by the car for about 10+ minutes until I finally went inside to ask what was going on. The clerk responded that their offered parking and valet service was through a garage around the corner, and that he had called someone to come over from there to get the car. He also warned me that prior guests had been ticketed and that the SF police would tow a car parked outside the hotel during afternoon rush hours. So he suggested that I drive around the block a few times while we waited for the valet to appear. I was surprised by this disorganization, but decided to wait a few more minutes by the car instead. When no one appeared after several more minutes, I finally got in the car and drove it to the garage around the corner myself. The attendant was surprised to see me, and said he was just sending someone over to the hotel to get the car. 
2) The room we received was decidedly European in its character. By that, I mean cozy, but nice and well-appointed. The double pane windows helped screen out much of the street noise, even on a lower floor (3rd) and the ceiling and walls were decorated with whimsical pictures and entertaining quotes. The bathroom was a little dated, but all in all, it appeared to be a pretty decent room. However, upon closer inspection as we were getting ready, the drain in the tub seemed to have standing water inside it. When I pulled up the stopper to see if there was a clog, there was a fairly thick clump of long brown hair attached. And the water was still there, so there must have been a good deal more of it down the drain a bit. It didn't look like this tub had been thoroughly cleaned for awhile, and my wife was not about to take a bath in it after seeing that.
3) Twice during the night we were awakened by a screeching sound in the pipes just below our room floor. I still don't know what caused this horrible sound, but it threw us bolt upright twice from a dead sleep, once around 12:30 AM and once around 2:30 AM. It lasted only about 5 or 6 seconds in all, but it was a startling and very unpleasant experience. Twice. If we hadn't been so dead tired and not wanting to pack up, I would have requested another room immediately. 
I wanted to like this place, and from surface appearances, it looks like a nice place and a good value. We really enjoyed the Millennium restaurant, but the hotel was disappointing. The drain situation was somewhat offputting, but even then, the stay would have been alright, except for the shrieking sound of the pipes. The front desk was too busy the next morning to worry much about our problems, so I just wrote the whole thing off as a learning experience. As you might imagine, I just can't endorse this hotel to others, as we may dine there again, but will probably not be staying there.

title: “50/50 rating”
text:
Positives : Good location for Fisherman's Wharf attractions. Friendly and helpful staff. Free parking in an expensive area to park.
Negatives : Quite scary to get back to at night - not very well lit externally and many tramps hanging around nearby. No air-conditioning - hell during our 2 night stay. Parking, although free, was pretty tight - especially for our hired SUV.
Would I stay again? - probably not.

title: “superb!”
text: Great hotel; great service and ammenities and top of the line furnisihngs - We highly reccomend it!

title: “Good location for DFW travelers”
text: My spouse and I have stayed at this location on several locations. The hotel is conveniently situated on the DFW property near the C terminal with shuttle service to and from the terminal, along with a flight arrival and departure board located in the lobby area. The lobby is clean and spacious, the staff helpful and pleasant, the rooms are comfortable with a modern decor, although somewhat dark. The hotel stamps the DFW toll ticket and parking is free for guests.

title: “Comfortable room but inconvenient location”
text:
I stayed 3 nights last week for a trade show at Dallas Convention Center. The room is clean and comfortable. They also have a small fitness center. The continental breakfast is nice. You can choose from bread, toasts, muffin to waffle. My room faced the freeway, but I didn't hear the traffic noises in the room, nor the noises of people walking on the hallway. The only drawback is the location. Car rental is definitely needed.
-- No shuttle bus to Dallas convention center. You'll need to wait for about 15 minutes for calling a taxi to the Dallas Convention Center, fare $17.
-- The only place to eat something within walking distance is "Jack in the Box." However, if you get a car, you can drive about 10 minutes to Restaurant Raw where lots of choices are available. 
BTW, although I could use wireless internet well in my room on the second floor facing the freeway, my colleague staying at the third floor on the opposite side of the building couldn't use the internet in room. He had to work in the breakfast dining room every early morning to use the internet.

title: “"Different breed of Hotel Manager"”
text:
My wife and I checked in to this hotel for a one week stay at the end of July. We were warmly welcomed by the valets who helped tremendously with our off-load. We parked at the top of the block and they came running! Thanks Eddie! (The location is VERY busy...so be prepared.) There is an opulent entrance and a warm welcome at the front desk. 
We were given a room that does not face Powell and it was quiet in terms of outside noise. However, the walls are very thin and all noises around will travel through to you. Our bathroom window did not close and we found it cold in there at night.
Expect small rooms here. )It was built a long time ago for a generation that raised 4 kids in a two bedroom house, right?) Anyone who has stayed in this city knows that this is pretty common with the hotel chains.
That being said, here is the skinny: Nice shower products, very hard bed. Easy to use TV and very good cleaning staff. Thanks Feng! There is no coffee maker in any room, so expect long line-ups at the Starbucks (Thankfully, there is no shortage if these here...)
Hint: If you want a quiet floor, ask for a lower one. A few we talked to complained of the noise higher up.
The location here cannot be beat! This is the reason people stay here, I am certain. The bar downstairs is well-equipped and you will likely be given a few complimentary drink tickets for your stay. (Bonus)
There is an in-room safe however, no bathrobes here. The workout area is nice and very well-equipped with modern machines. 
I think this hotel reflects its management. I have never met a GM like Jim. We talked for a few moments in the lobby and during our conversation, he sees a lady carting a heavy bag up the stairs. He excuses himself politely and then jumps to her aid, carrying the heavy bag a few more flights! I think this says a lot about the kind of people that work here.
Thank you all for an enjoyable stay.

title: “My favorite in D.C., but not perfect”
text:
All things considered, this is my favorite hotel in Washington, but it's certainly not perfect.
I've always stayed on the Club Level. The rooms are quite nice; I've stayed in better rooms, but they're certainly in line with what I'd expect from a Ritz-Carlton.
The location is excellent and one of my favorite things about the place. One can easily walk to Dupont Circle and Georgetown.
The service, however, is uneven. None of the employees has ever been blatantly rude. But they're sometimes clueless. And many of them don't really go out of their way to provide excellent service. At the restaurant, one waiter is quite "snooty." In the lobby bar, service is courteous but often quite slow. In the club lounge, the staff are often in the back room, leaving the lounge totally unstaffed.
Some of the staff are indeed excellent, and I can think of many examples of excellent service there. But consistency is definitely a problem. If this were a Hilton or even a Westin, I'd say that the service is fine, but I think that most people expect more from a Ritz-Carlton.

title: “Location, location, but....”
text:
I had been in the Grand Hyatt previously for a meeting. The location was next to Seaport Village and just yards to the water. The grand reception area can take your breath away. Friendly staff at check-in, restaurant and bar. The view out our window was spectacular of the harbor. 
Now, my down side of this place. When we had arrived, there were hundreds of teenagers in front of the hotel. In the parking structure, the teenagers were screaming. There were staff members operating the elevators, the kids running up and down the halls. I was told there was a teen event at the convention center this weekend. I wished the Hotel's website (Meetings & Events) would have mentioned this noisy event. Internet cost is $10 per day, and restricts location where you sign up (which tower, lobby or room). 
Overall, the stay was nice and convenient (location).

title: “One of the best hotel near Indianapolis airport”
text: This hotel used to be holiday inn and has been recently renovated and has one of the best interior that I know of. It is located very close to indianapolis airport. Staff are very friendly and they have free airport pick up too. highly recommended

title: “A wonderful experience”
text:
We recently had the opportunity to stay at the Chatwal NY for the first time, and my wife and I were extremely impressed with both the hotel itself, and the staff. 
As we were only at the hotel for a brief two nights (with a very late arrival the first night), followed by a very busy schedule the next two days, we didn't have an opportunity to see or take advantage of any hotel features beyond our hotel room and the lobby/reception area. 
However, what we did see and experience, we loved. We found the hotel room to be impeccible, and the design details in the room and bathroom were outstanding. Every detail spoke to quality, and attention to detail, right down to the leather handle on the bathroom and cupboard doors. When we left the room, it was cleaned to perfection, and we didn't even see a misplaced fingerprint on the shiny stainless steel bathroom fixtures.
But beyond the beautifully appointed hotel room, and extremely comfortable bed, what made our stay special was the people who worked at the hotel. From the doormen, to the concierge, to the front desk staff, everyone was polite, friendly, and noticeably helpful. However, the icing on the cake was when we arrived at the airport after checking out of the hotel, when my wife noticed that her backup 'diabetes pump' had been left in our room, in the fridge area. We called the hotel from the airport 6 hours after checkout, and spoke with the conscierge on duty(Philip). Philip very calmly handled this stressful situation, managed to locate the diabetes pump, and then arranged to have it couriered to our home.It arrived safely and intact two days ago.
We have nothing but great things to say about the Chatwal NY, and have already started singing your praises to our friends and relatives. We hope to stay at the Chatwal NY again in the future. Until that time, thank you and your wonderful staff for a great experience at your hotel.
HHK & MTK

title: “Poor Housekeeping”
text:
I would like to warn anyone planning on staying at this hotel for more than one night that you will not be provided with any towels on the second night. In the morning after our first night we left for sightseeing, when we returned around 5 to shower and prepare for dinner we noticed there was not one towel or washcloth in the bathroom. We called the desk to request towels and they said they would send some up. After one hour and three phone calls we finally received two towels and one wash cloth. Very disappointing. Also if you are expecting a top sheet on the bed you will be dissappointed. You will have to sleep under a bedspread that has probably never been washed.
I agree with other reviews that the front desk does not care about anyone staying at the hotel. The elevators are very slow too.

title: “Not bad for the price with starwood points”
text: I had a perfectly comfortable night in the Sheraton but was left wondering what the refit had actually achieved. The decor was a rather gloomy dark brown 70s style, there was no underfloor heating in the bathroom, no safe (although they are to be fitted soon), no fridge, no telephone or speakers in the bathroom. That said, the bed was comfortable and there was a huge flat screen TV. The bathroom was large but there were nothing extra appart from shampoo and the water pressure was poor in the shower. I had no view at all because I looked out onto the interior courtyard. The windows didn't open and the room had a rather stale smell that I was unable to get rid of. There were about 6 or 7 computers for guests use in the lobby which was really helpful. The breakfast buffet was good but not included in the price. The location was excellent, at one end of 16th Street Mall so near lots of restaurants and shops. The City Hall and other buildings were nearby as well.

title: “bang on location”
text: me & my fiancee stayed here for 4 nights in october.....this hotel is ideally located,times sq is a 5min walk & the tube is right outside the hotel the rooms are quite small but clean & comfortable the staff are friendly & helpfull (and they love the tips) we would definetly stay here again :)

title: “3000 SPG Starpoints & I had a free room”
text: Spent one evening - Clean, quiet, nice bed, -- Four Points is a great brand @ a very fair price

title: “Too noisy”
text: I have just returned from 8 nights at the Best Western and felt compelled to share my experience with others. I had a Bay view room which indeed offers lovely views of the ships and sea. However, the noise from the trains was intolerable. I am a usually a heavy sleeper but was woken every night by the 1.30am and 4.30 am trains and was always then subsequently wide awake for the 6.30 one! For someone experiencing a 8 hour time zone change and trying to minimise jet lag this was really awful! My colleagues suffered from similar interupted sleep. The hotel staff were very friendly, especially given the demands on them by the hotel being full from the conference in town. However the resturant staff were very rude and unhelpful. Breakfast is complimentary but we never returned after day 1. The hotel is in a very quiet area but a short walk to the harbour. However, I would recommend staying in either the Holiday Inn Harbourside or Hampton Inn on Harbour Drive.

title: “Gross”
text:
I was looking for an inexpensive hotel to stay in on my way to San Antonio. I didn't expect luxury. But a place should be clean at any price. The bathroom was molding and dirty. The shower drain was clogged which I noticed when I tried to rinse the dead bugs down the drain. 
I moved the couch out to use the outlet for my computer and I won't tell you the trash I saw back there! 
Some kid tried to bum a cigerette off me when I was bringing in my luggage. I had to kick the empty beer cans off the patio and walk around all the trash on the grounds. 
I normally stay at Holiday Inns and decided to take a chance. No more Travelodge for me!

title: “Good hotel, centrally located”
text: We stayed here for two nights and enjoyed the hotel's convenience to Times Square and numerous restaurants. We easily walked to Macy's on 34th street and up to the Today Show at Rockefeller Center as well as the Letterman Show on Broadway at 53rd Street. Based on earlier reviews we expected a tiny room but found that the room was plenty big for our needs. It was nicely furnished with a comfortable bed and a large flat screen TV.

title: “Chicago adventure!”
text: The first room was quite small and when i took my shoes off I found the carpet to be wet. I called the front desk and they immediately told us they would give us another room. Much nicer room! This is our second stay and we would do so again. I love that it is downtown, across from Grant Park and Buckingham Fountain. It is close to Navy Pier and the Magnificant Mile. We have been to two of the restauants with the hotel and were pleased with the service and food.

title: “Very comfortable!!”
text: For my first visit to Houston, I couldn't have picked a better hotel. Don't pay for valet or garage parking, park in their free parking next to the Walgreens on Sage Road, which is on the side of the hotel. The hotel staff was friendly, and the king guest room was spacious and beautifully decorated. I was on the 14th floor which gave a beautiful view. I was able to actually see my car in the parking lot outside of my window. There is an A/V jack on the side of the television just in case you would like to bring a DVD player, or you can pay $12.99 for a pay per view movie. The toiletries are upscale, and the large spa like shower head gives a wonderful shower. The best thing about the room is the bed, the bed, the bed!!! I know there are about 8 pillows already on the bed, and two more in the closet.

title: “Great Location... Rude staff”
text:
Me and my friend stayed at the Wolcott hotel on 2nd Sept- 5th Sept.
Fantastic location right down the road from empire state building. 
I loved our room also, nice and big, comfy beds right down the hall so it was very quiet..The shower wasnt very good but oh well. 
Staff Were a bit rude.. didnt really say hello when we came in, kind of spoke to us like we were stupid and when we asked about things in new york like different attractions and how to get to them etc none of the staff really knew and one even gave us wrong directions.. you'd think that working in Manhatten you'd have good knowledge of Manhatten especially if your in the tourist industry..
All in all if your not really in the hotel much and are just looking for somewhere to sleep in a great location this is a really good hotel.

title: “Good Hotel - not near anything but really nice pool.”
text:
Pros: great pool, on the water, refurbed rooms 
Cons: over charged me multiple times for breakfast, front desk leaves much to be desired, not anywhere near downtown

title: “Wonderful Staff & Wonderful Stay”
text: From the time I called to place my reservation to the time the Valet waved me off, my Stay at the Silversmith couldn't have been better. The rooms were clean, and had everything you might need. The staff from top to bottom went above and beyond to be sure my stay and that of my friend who was celebrating a birthday was spectacular. Can't wait to stay again!!

title: “Good value, great location”
text: I have stayed at this hotel twice in the last three years and on both occassions found it good value for money. Ask for a high level room (27 floors) and you are guarunteed a great view of the bay or city skyline. The roof top pool also feels special, since it is so high up. Best of all is the location. You aren't stuck out in Fishermans Wharf, but much closer to the heart of the city. If you only have a day or two in town then I guess the Wharf is OK. But if you're in town for longer I definitely recommend this more central hotel.

title: “Friendly and helpful staff”
text: The hotel was pleasant and cosy and the room was a great value. The staff were very accommodating to my requirements. Thank you Natalie and Sandeep!

title: “Low Quality Inn”
text: My one major complaint throughout my stay was a sewer water-like stench coming from the bathroom. The water was shut off throughout the building for about an hour at one point. I'm sure it was for maintenance issues but why take the chance. The whole place just looks unmaintained. Daily servicing of the room was good. There is a $5 a day parking fee. The parking lot is very small, so finding parking on the hotel lot is not garanteed. Would have dished out a little more $$ for a little for quality.

title: “Great Service, great location”
text: My husband and I stayed here from May 21-26. The Front Desk sfaff was very friendly, helpful and informative. We asked for a late check-out on our last day. No problem! The room and bathroom were very clean, somewhat on the small side; however, we did not spend much time there anyway. They provide you with earplugs due to the street noise! We asked housekeeping for extra coffee and they promptly delivered it. The hotel's restaurant was a pleasant surprise. The food was very good, well presented and the wait staff excellent. The location is great! It is only a short walk to the Smithonian museums and the Mall. Also there is The Circulator stop nearby for the bus to Georgetown

title: “Great combination of Traditonal and Modern”
text: We stayed at this hotel while visiting family. It is in a perfect location, in the trendy LoDo area. The hotel's in a coverrted 1911 office building which has kept many of its historical attributes (marble, lighting, etc.). The rooms however are very modern and comfortable - a great combination. The hotel is located on a quiet street but is walking distance to all downtown amenities and Coors field. We were able to get a great price on the room because it is now competing for customers with the Four Seasons which recently opened in the area.

title: “ABSOLUTELY THE BEST STAFF !! WILL DEF STAY AGAIN !!”
text:
Just booked this 24 Hrs before on a whim. Location was GREAT, but one STAFF Member in particular was AMZING ! If u decide to stay here ask for Vanessa... I travel ALOT & I cannot tell u HOW INCREDIBLE she was to make my ONLY ONE NITE STAY a COMPLETE PLEASURE ! My Orig Room was Beautifiul but had a Broken AC.. The Next Room some IDIOT Smoked in & Vanessa gave me an UPGRADE to a LARGER ROOM AND a LATE CHECK OUT ! Where in NYC do u find this ?
ABSOLUTELY THE BEST !! Hotel was CLEAN & VERY COMFORTABLE. Walked to everything I needed to do, so saved $$ on Cab Fare & taking the Subway. Im a NAtive NYer but live in LA for 20 years now.. It was a JOY to be treated like this ! 
SOMEONE NEEDS A PROMOTION .. & A HUGE RAISE !! 
The only DOWNSIDE is that I didnt have a chance to say GOODBYE becuase she was off that day, but Ill be back !!! :)

title: “A good choice for Baltimore's Inner Harbor”
text: We spent one night here in June. My husband and I were in town for a concert at the nearby First Mariner Arena. The hotel staff were friendly and attentive. Restaurant and room service quality and service were excellent. Very comfortable bedding. Great views of the Inner Harbor from our uniquely laid out corner room with King bed and floor to ceiling windows on two sides. I highly recommend requesting one of these corner rooms. The Hyatt's location is perfect for activities in and near the Inner Harbor; walking distance to shopping, restaurants, sporting events, and aquarium. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “STAY HERE!!!”
text:
AMAZING!!! We were upgraded to a corner room viewing the Hollywood sign. Granted it was in the distance, it was pretty cool!! Our room was flawless! I don't say that lightly. We had a balcony so we could walk out and see the sign and night sky. The surrounding area directly around the hotel is nothing special, but don't let that stop you. You are in the heart of it!!! Since it was our anniversary, we were sent champagne and chocolate covered strawberries with flecks of edible gold flakes on the chocolate. The swimming pool is salt water and at a perfect temperature year round. The hot tub is a perfect temperature. The gym is small, but filled with new equipment! We were a little surprised that the locker rooms did not have hot tubs and were not extensive, but that was ok. The locker rooms in the Baltimore and Palm Beach FS were immense and luxurious! The locker rooms at the Beverly Hills were much much better than average, don't get me wrong! 
While staying here, we saw Paul McCartney and the Chicago Bulls basketball team. Justin Bieber was staying here as well, but we did not see him. Top tier people stay here. We say a Bugatti sports car with $2 million dollars pull up. In addition, RRs and Bentleys. This is NICE! They have house cars that take you a few miles around the hotel. One is a 2012 Mercedes and a 2012 RR Ghost. No joke. 
This hotel is secluded from Rodeo Drive and smaller than the Beverly Wilshire (a second FS hotel) hotel (next to Rodeo drive) less than 2 miles away, but you can probably tell, it is still beyond amazing. At the time, the Beverly Wilshire was under construction (including half of the hotel and the pool). The Beverly Wilshire is the "pretty woman" hotel and is fancy, but I prefer the secluded Beverly Hills Four Seasons. You can walk between the two hotels, but it takes a good 15-20 minutes. For car people, you see very high end cars ALL of the time. Very cool area. We wanted to see a movie and went to the Grove. We were dropped off in a Mercedes and picked up at night in the Rolls Royce. AMAZING!! Some FS will have a house car and drop you off somewhere, but not pick you up. This FS picks you up as well, but you have to call and it might take 30 minutes or so, so relax and have it sink in that you are in Beverly Hills. Enjoy!!

title: “Warm, clean and luxurious stay - Not to be missed!”
text: One of the best hotel stays ever! Clean, clean, clean! Beautifully decorated - AMAZING staff. Felt like I was on vacation in the room even though I was there for work. Everyone was personable, attentive, warm and welcoming. The room was spacious - CLEAN - and super comfortable. I slept like a baby after an incredible room service meal that came to my wacky specifications - love this place and highly recommend!

title: “Pretty good”
text: The room was clean and almost prepared. I was mistakenly charged for the minibar, but they fixed it. The staff were helpful, but the valet were extremely slow -- I had to wait over an hour for my car. My major complaint was the air conditioning didn't work. The room was too hot for me to sleep comfortably. The lounge was so-so, not as good as the Marriott near Wardmann Park.

title: “Can't wait to enjoy again!”
text: Was not sure if we were going to spend the night in Detroit originally, but did some research the night before. When we decided to stay I gave them a call sat night at 8pm, they still had a room left! They were very nice on the phone and gave us directions from where we were. When we got their, I just wanted the basic room 99.00 which they were out of but upgraded us to the king suite for the same price! They also had complementary star buck’s HOT coffee, tea and fruit in the dinning room next to check in! The room was excellent and included free DSL line and Cd's to listen to. Then bed was unbelievably comfortable, I wanted to take it home with us. If you are looking for a regular hotel this is not it. If you want a step above for the same price, then I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Amazing Location. Clean and Comfortable.”
text: I stayed at this Hyatt and honestly it was great. The location was perfect, close to all the amazingness that makes a dream trip. I do want to include that Jason Jones, who works the main desk, was the main key to making this dream trip possible. Hey Jason- if you read this, my Wife and I thank you so much for everything you've done. We'll see you soon.

title: “Comfy hotel”
text: Nice exterior. Beware of the tax added on your bill. It's about 14-16%. The king bed room we got was amazing. My dog was very at home as well. The room all together was about 89$. Free breakfast which is make it yourself waffles,hard boiled eggs(which are over cooked),fresh orange juice,bagels,muffins,toast,ect. Free wifi works great. And the tv has what your watching at the bottom of the screen,which saves you from flipping back to the schedule channel. The bathroom was very large and very clean. The bed was soft and the blankets were very comfy. All in all one of the best la Quinta inns I've stayed at. Highly recommend staying if you get a good deal. Ask for military discount!!! ID required.

title: “Clean, elegant and very spacious rooms”
text:
The title says it all: for NY standards, the size of the rooms is quite impressive. Decoration and room set-up (furniture, bathroom far away drom beds, foyer entrance, etc) were very well though through.
Great location too if you intend to shop, dine and visit mid town mainly. 
I am very picky when it comes to hotels, and have tried quite a few in NYC, but this one is by far the best one i've encountered so far. Would go back again, definitely.

title: “Housekeeping was GREAT”
text:
This hotel is always good but I was impressed when after housekeeping finished a supervisor came by to check and ask if everythink was cleaned completely. I hate that I missed the sausage grave yesterday but I guess they do not replace the breakfast items toward the end of the serving time so guess i need to get there earlier. 
 Everything else was just fine!! Will be back.
TJW

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Travelled to Los Angeles for work and had a couple of nights as free time so checked into this hotel. The staff were very helpful and the rooms clean and comfortable. Located just off the main drag (near the Capitol Records building), the hotel is ideal for a visit to the area. The adjoining diner was good. Good location, friendly staff, clean. The complex is chalet/motel style and the centre point is the good size pool. Couldn't find fault. The free WiFi was good too. Definitely recommended.

title: “FABULOUS STAY!”
text:
What can I say! 42 floors up and a fantastic view from our corner room-Hudson River to the right Times Square to the left Room lovely- huge with 2 big double beds and lovely bathroom. Traffic? What traffic!? 
We could see the long long queues at discount tix but who wanted to stand for hours in 97F for tickets. We went to theatre and got front row balcony for $66 each to see Kelsey Grammer and Douglas Hodge. Absolutely brilliant!!
Drinks were a bit dear but on last day we had a huge turkey club sandwich which did the 2 of us for $11- well it did come with potato waffles too! Delicious!
Lifts were great-staff helpful-position excellent - brilliant coffee machine- would love to return!!

title: “Great location!”
text: Large and clean room with nice beds (checked for bed bugs but no sign). Bathroom in need of renovation though - especially the plumbing: toilet was nearly impossible to flush and the shower tricky to adjust. Stayed there 4 nights in April and the room was quite cold - had to sleep with a thick sweater on. The location is great though - just a few minutes walk from Central Park, Times Square, subway... Helpful staff. Overall, I'd stay there again.

title: “Maybe the best in Boston”
text: It's tough to beat waking up to the boats on the harbor (get a water view). The rooms are large and the beds are sweet, but with that location you won't be in the rooms much. Steps away from Faneuil Hall, you're a short walk to Little Italy and the Seaport and Chinatown--- it actually might be the ideal location. The restaurant is good (not great, and a bit pricey) but the best eaterys in town don't even require a cab... Overall, its not the cheapest spot in town, but if it fits the budget it's worth it.

title: “Fresh, bright and a great hotel”
text:
A very modern hotel. The colours inside are beautiful and bright, the suites very spacious and well appointed. Crisp, white linens and towels & housekeeping does a good job of cleaning. Good bathroom amenities. 
The microwave is inconveniently located, it is low and inside a cupboard making heating anything a bit of a challenge. The faucet in the wash sink is a spray rather than a stream and that is inconvenient too. 
Each floor has an entry door to the actual corridor that can only be accessed by a room key. Good security touch. 
The electric panel at the desk did not work after our check-in. A maintenance engineer came & checked it but could not fix it then as the wiring was inside the wall so he provided us with an extension cord. Problem solved. What is impressive is that by the next day we returned to our room after a day out to find the panel fixed and the extension cord gone! This is service. Be aware that the hotel charges 25$ per night for valet parking as the nearest self parking is half a mile away. 
A good choice in a very good location- just minutes away from a lot of cool places.

title: “This place is stupendous.”
text: This was a great place to stay. It was,right on the,ocean and there is a,dog park near by. There are plenty of shops and restUrants and everything is in walking distance. The courtyard of the hotel is beautiful. It also has an ice machine and a washer and a dryer. The rooms are small , but cozy. It wasa perfect place for my fiance and I. Surfing lessons and khayacking , and beautiful walks down the pier. We loved it !!!

title: “Terrible service for afternoon tea”
text: We went there for afternoon tea and booked several days ago. Time limit is one and half an hour but we were 20 minutes late because of the trains. Maybe I just expect too much, but... I don't think afternoon tea should be like this way... We had very rushed courses one after another because of our time. They served u next couse before u even finished the last one. We feel so uncomfortable worrying about they will ask us to leave next minute. I feel so guity for my friends cause it's all my fault to suggest this place to "enjoy" our lazy afternoon. Can't forget it. Really bad experience in NYC..

title: “Much more than a fantastic view...”
text: I'm a well traveled soul and this resort was more than expected! When I booked a room I was expecting to pay for the view... we received much more than the view. The pool area and swim up bar(food and drinks available) have the feel of the Caribbean. There is a 3 tiered infinity pool and hot tub for 21 and older and a nice large water slide area for families. Plenty of poolside chairs/umbrellas around both pool areas and a few cabanas are available in the family area. Friendly staff and a fantastic view from the lake side rooms. Better than average exercise room. Free drinks for an hour in the afternoon (5pm - 6pm). The food was good at the restaurant and the view was outstanding. We didn't try the spa but I would expect it to be up to par.

title: “The best hotel I've ever stayed in.”
text: Walking into the Greenwich is amazing. From the outside you wouldn't even look twice but similar to many things in NYC the true beauty is going inside and exploring. There is an amazing pool (the only complaint could be that it would be great if it were heated) - and steam room. All of the common areas oozing old Hollywood charm. Considering that Robert De Niro owns the hotel this doesn't come as a massive shock - his taste is classy and inviting. The service was impeccable, the room was amazing and the whole place was complete luxury. We saw many movie stars there including Ted Danson and Cameron Diaz. Perfect place to celebrity watch.

title: “Noisy room, nice renovation”
text:
I'm staying here for a week long conference and I'm loathing the next 4 nights. I got stuck in a room immediately next to a service elevator in Tower 3. Throughout the day and night I hear the engine purring. I thought eventually I would get used to the sound and ignore it, but it's still very noticeable.
The room otherwise is nice -- immaculately cleaned, with quality linens and amenities. I think it was renovated, since everything looks new and slick. Prime downtown location. Unlike other reviewers, I had no trouble with the internet speed or service -- everyone has been cordial.
Just that it's so noisy I'm desperately craving some silence and peace of mind. One night down, four to go.

title: “tiny flaws but great overall”
text:
My mother and I spent five nights at the Affinia last week and, for the most part, very much enjoyed our stay. 
Our room, with two double beds, was very large and divided into two semi-levels. The bathroom and bar area were on a landing at main-door level and the beds were three steps down in sort of a sunken-living-room set-up. The beds and linens were clean and we had more pillows than anyone would ever want or need, though the down comforters were a teensy bit worn and discoloured. The bathroom was roomy and spotless, with ample towels, but there wasn’t much counter space, so we used the desk outside its door as a place on which to keep our toiletries. 
The flat-screen TV in the room was wall-mounted and swiveled, which was handy, though we did notice that it occasionally lost reception quality if turned in one particular direction (likely due to a loose cable connection somewhere). The leather recliner was very comfortable and clean, and a nice touch.
We had a great view south along St. Clair, and found the room to be fairly quiet. We did hear other guests in the hallway outside, as well as ambulance sirens occasionally, but never loud enough or long enough to cause excessive disruption.
As other reviewers have noted, it’s a bit of a shame that many basic amenities (e.g., local phone calls, internet) come with an additional charge. We were also disappointed that we were unable to use the mini-fridge in our room – it was stocked full with beverages and, when we asked if it might be emptied so we could use it for our own snacks, we were told it *could* be emptied out... for a $50 fee. That seemed a smidge exorbitant, so we just moved things aside a little and had room to keep the occasional yogurt or bottle of water inside overnight. (We always ate or removed our own items in the morning, lest they be taken out by the mini-bar inventory-control clerks.)
We found the staff to be consistently friendly and accommodating – we were always greeted with a “good morning” or “hello” if we passed anyone coming or going from the hotel – and any questions we had were always answered happily. We smelled cigarette smoke out in the hallway one evening (the entire hotel is non-smoking) and were pleasantly surprised at how thankful the guest services staffer was when we called down to let her know.
We also used the complimentary (we were sure there would be a fee, but there wasn’t!) service whereby guests can print out boarding passes before heading to the airport. We found it efficient, and the young woman at the front desk (I forgot to get her name) who assisted me was extremely helpful and patient despite the extended seat-selection process and printer snafus.
Overall, as mentioned, our experience at the Affinia was a very good one. We've visited Chicago many times before but this was our first stay at this hotel and we look forward to staying again next time we're in town.

title: “Perfect value & location: our home for a week in NYC”
text:
The Candlewood Suites Hotel was a perfect choice for our one week stay in NYC. I am a person that loves to walk, so I was amazed by the short walking distances to so many sights and attractions of NYC. Furthermore it is very close to Penn Station, which is perfectly connectd to JFK airport. Here a few examples (all walking):
Times Square: 10 minutes
Penn Station & Madison Square Garden: 10 minutes
34th St (Shopping & Macy's): 10-15min
Empire State Building: Less than 5 min from Macy's
Rockefeller Centre (with Top of the Rock = best view in town): 20 minutes
....from there a few more minutes to Central Park
The High Line Park is also in proximity to the hotel.
I loved the location for the fact, that you could just go out in the evening at any time and walk towards Times Square and enjoy the rush of the city, walk on the many avenues, or see a play in one of the Broadway theatres in your neighbourhood. If you want to go to Southern Manhattan you can just take the metro, the closest station being on 42nd St and 8th Avenue.
The hotel is an appartment hotel, so the laundry and towels are only changed once a week by them, OR on request. All you need is to call the reception and within a few minutes they'll bring you fresh towels. Generally I have to say that the reception was fantastic. They were always helpful and friendly, but not "overdoing" it in an annoying way. If you need something, they are there and they'll help you, if you don't need anything, they won't bother you....and that's what I want. 
The rooms are not too big, but really enough for a couple. The bathroom has a bathtub, there is a small kitchen at the entrance where you can prepare yourself some small meals or breakfast and enough place for a nice table to eat. And most importantly: It is CLEAN and all looks pretty fresh. 
The building is a very slim and high building (only 6 rooms per floor) and surrounded by other high rise buildings just across the street. This means, that from most floors your views will be limited to some other windows. However, on the entrance side (39th st), the appartment building opposite is still under construction, so try to ask for a room on a higher floor, and when you're lucky, you might still enjoy a nice view facing south (including the Empire State building). 
The Candlewood Suites really where a comfortable, nice place for our one-week stay in NYC. When you stay in a city like NYC, you want to be close to the hotspots, but also have a quiet place to relax....and this is exactly what you get (in our case also for a reasonable price). We would definitely come back again!

title: “Well managed Hotel..”
text:
Stayed at this hotel during my trip to San Diego.
It's near a lot fo offices in the Rancho Bernardo area and there are pickups and drop offs to some offices as well.
Hotel is within walking distance to Pearl's Cusine Restaurant as well as other restaurants. Conveniently located!
Has gym facilities as well as a pool.
There is a cafe that serves breakfast (but no lunch or dinner)
Will definitely come back and stay at the same hotel if I visit San Diego again.

title: “Nice hotel, great architecture details...”
text: Nice hotel with distinctive architecture you are not going encounter these days. The staff was great. Very welcoming. Rooms were large and comfortable with flat screen TV's. Would stay here again. A little noise creep but not bad.

title: “Great deal!”
text: We wanted a room for Nov.6-9, 2004, not realizing that was the weekend of the NY marathon. The Comfort Inn was the only place under $300 per night we could find. We booked it, expecting the worst. To our delight, it was wonderful! Clean, cozy, and incredibly convenient. The view from our room of the lit-up Empire State Building was an unexpected bonus. Even if you can afford a more expensive hotel, I'd recommend staying at the Comfort Inn and using the "extra" money on more shopping or fancier dining out. Terrific experience!

title: “Very good hotel, great location, great lobby”
text: There's free Wi-fi in the lobby, so even when I come to Chicago on a day trip, I often stop here if I have some time to kill. The rooms are fine, though not great, but it's the location and the vibe (very busy lobby, good for people watching) that keep me coming here.

title: “Snowy return to AFFINIA 50 - warmest experience ever!!!!!!”
text:
This trip came during one of the worst storms I have experienced in New York. Left SFO 60+ degree weather and landed in 16 degrees. Upon calling the hotel to make arrangements which Sandra, a manager helped calm me while making my arrangements effortlessly, as I was TERRIFIED sittiing in cab into Manhattan from JFK among giant snow flakes. The bell staff greeted me 'warmly' at the door with big hello and 'welcome home'. Check- in was seamless and my luggage was taken to my nice extremely warm & beautiful room. The staff had provided a lovely amenity, even remembering that I (always) need extra hangers. 
Maintenance staff & in-house IT manager spent over 2 hours assisting me in connecting my computer so I could work. The front desk staff upon hearing of my dilemma, IMMEDIATELY showed me optional(upgraded) rooms to move to in case they failed, generously offering any and all assistance I may need. Even the housekeeping staff was concerned with both my physical comfort and calm...This is a superlative hotel with the most professional staff in EVERY DEPARTMENT,anticipating my every need and/or request and delivering with service above my expectations. I thoroughly enjoy this special treasure in Midtown 
and will continue to recommend it to everyone!!!!

title: “Could of been better for a Sheraton.”
text: I have always liked staying at Sheraton hotels in the past, however this one lacked the finesse of others. Rooms were small. We stayed there for 5 days and housekeeping never vacuumed our room. On the weekend, there wasn't enough places to sit by the pool. Staff did nothing about it. The beds were comfortable.

title: “Nice room - friendly staff”
text:
The hotel is currently under construction. We only stayed 1 night, on a Sunday, so we were not disturbed by it. I chose this location because we were having dinner at the Space Needle, and heading to the airport Monday morning. It was a very easy walk to the Space Needle and the drive to airport was against rush hour traffic, so it took less than a 1/2 hour. 
The breakfast was different than the other Hampton's I have stayed at. You had to heat the food yourself, but we didn't mind. We took the food to our room and used the microwave there. 
The room was well equipped. Frig, microwave, sink.
Overall, it was what I expected from a Hampton Inn. I use the chain frequently.
Hhonors Gold Member

title: “Great Stay!”
text: Very clean rooms and good check-in check-out service. A great alternative to the very expensive hotels in the area.

title: “Great Service - Older Rooms”
text: I have wanted to stay at this hotel for a long time. When I saw the great deals in January, I could not pass it up. I have stayed in a lot of NY hotels and the service here is outstanding. I think that I was greated by 6 different people before I ever reached the front desk. The lobby area is quite grand and beautiful. The rooms were much more bland than I had imagined. I have stayed at much cheaper hotels that have much better rooms (ie The W). Despite having old and dated rooms, the beds were quite comfortable. I had a good nights rest, no issues with noise. There is a nice lobby bar as well as another attached on the east side of the building (Bull and Bear I think). My husband and I enjoyed 5 cocktails and our bill was more than $100. Steep even for NYC. All in all, would I stay here again? No. But I did check a box off of my Bucket List - so it was worth it in that regard.

title: “Meh...be sure to specify a high floor to avoid noise, and watch for icky housekeeping”
text: I hope other travelers won't have the yuck experience I did at this Westin. Housekeeping was WAY sketchy in the first room where I was put - totally off the mark for any Westin and down in bad two-star territory. Moreover, the noise level from the renovations penetrated an 11th-floor room and I had to be moved, at about midnight, to a much higher floor in a different tower - after the desk asked if I could "really hear it, or could the noise be somehting else?" No, jackhammers against concrete are pretty distinctive, thanks. The second room was quieter and had actually been cleaned but it was still a less-than-Westin experience. If you're compelled to stay at this Westin, make absolutely sure that you ask the front desk for a HIGH FLOOR ROOM that is as far away from the renovation as possible.

title: “More like a Courtyard Marriott”
text:
I recenty stayed at this hotel for 3 nights for a business trip. I agree with the people that have written about the excellent location, but the hotel itself being not that great. The lobby is large and pretty, but the rooms were not worthy of the "JW" name. I think the hotel is calling it a "JW" Marriott so that they can charge more money and due to their prime location.
My room was on the 7th floor. The room itself needed major updating. It was in no way luxurious or upscale. It still had nasty old fashioned motel syle bed speads- yuck! I was thoroughly dissapointed with the bedding. I will say that it was quiet at night.
One thing, you have to call to get a room service menu to leave on your door at night in order to have it arrive in the morning. I got room service 2 days in a row for breakfast. The food was very tasty and arrived on time, if not early. I did get the wrong order one morning though. 
All the employees were friendly and helpful. I did not eat at any of the restaurants or use the gym. I was too busy sight seeing. 
All in all this is not a bad hotel, it is just not what I envisioned for a "JW Marriott" which are supposed to be the chain's upscale hotels. The room felt more like a Marriott Courtyard. 
Enjoy the sights of DC! It is a wonderful city w/ so much to do!

title: “Best Place I Have Stayed In Downtown Philly”
text:
Stayed here for a week while attending training in Philly. I can see no reason to stay anyplace else next time I come to Philly. Here's the deal:
- Very friendly staff
- Nicely appointed rooms. Very clean. With Coffee Maker. Flat-screen TV.
- Comfortable beds
- Great internet connection
- Very nice bar and restaurant
- Convenient to lots of good sites and restaurants in Philly
I tried to think of any negatives or areas for improvement, but I really could not think of any

title: “Great value, nice place to stay, can't fault it.”
text:
Hotel Carlton was great - the staff are friendly and sure do love to make a joke! They were helpful whenever needed. The hotel decor is really nice and pleasant and new, giving it a really cosy exotic feel. Everything felt clean.
A lot of people mentioned noise but this wasn't a problem for me,although I do sleep with earplugs.
The location was about 10-15min walk from the town centre but the walk is safe PROVIDED you walk in the direction opposite of the tenderloin.
Only complaint would be that the shower soap/shampoo dispenser was really annoying to use, a lot of pumps didn't give much output. Would stay here again. I researched all my hotels well before booking and I think HC was the best value for San Fran.

title: “Greal Location clean Rooms”
text: If you are a member of the Omni Select you get a nice Turn down serivce and free drink in the morning. they forgot mine but compensated it with a free breakfast.

title: “Fantastic. Four Seasons nails customer service.”
text:
Four Seasons has a leg up on all other hotel chains I've ever used: they know how to make the customer feel special. I got a great "introductory rate" and through American Express Fine Hotels and Resorts also got an automatic upgrade to a wonderful corner room. The room was absolutely gorgeous, the free-standing oval bathtub next to the window a particularly nice touch. 
We used the Spa, too, and got the best deep tissue massage ever (ask for Kristina and tell her not to hold back). It was refreshing to be given the bill and see only the charges you expected (lately a lot of spas are adding "fees" and even automatic gratuities).
Finally, we had dinner at Edge (the on-property restaurant), which was fantastic. Read my separate review of it.
Again, the best thing about the 4 Seasons (this one in Denver and others) is that they know how to make a customer feel like they've made the right choice in hotels.

title: “Excellent place to stay”
text:
After a brilliant stay in 2007 we decided to return to the Orchid Suites in September 2012 for 4 nights and we were so glad we made that decision. Next time in Los Angeles, we have decided we will spend all of our time at this hotel.
The staff are wonderful. We arrived at the hotel at 9.30am after a 13 hour flight from Australia with two young children in tow. The staff were very accommodating to our situation and went out of their way to check us in this early so that we could all rest, which we were very thankful for!
As many of the other reviews state, the hotel’s location is superb and it is very clean. If you plan on using public transport while in L.A. the location is great due it’s close proximity to the metro red line station and bus stops.
The room we stayed in was equipped with everything we needed including a full kitchen. The pool area is very well kept and a lovely way to relax after a long day of sightseeing.
We found the breakfast on offer (which was included in the price of the room) very satisfying with a great range of cereals, bagels, toast, fruits, and muffins.
We also found the free internet service with free printing very useful also.
All in all an excellent stay and I highly recommend this hotel to anyone staying in Los Angeles.

title: “Wow - good value for Beverly Hills”
text:
Highly recommended. This hotel has it all!
Incredible design, comfy beds, a bath room to die for. The only negative is; the bathroom has no ventilation. The humidity can't go anywhere and is 'killing' the light bulbs.

title: “Location, location, location”
text:
Right on the boardwalk at Mission Beach, the Blue Sea Lodge offered us an upgrade to oceanfront and we were very happy. Great people-watching in the daytime and lulling surf sounds at night. Two good restaurants nearby - the World Famous Restaurant across the street and the Green Flash a couple of blocks along the boardwalk.
Blue Sea Lodge checkin staff were efficient, friendly and helpful - and offered fresh baked cookies to take to our room.
The room was clean and comfy and a small balcony gave us a chance to catch the sea breezes. Nice swimming pool but it was too cool for us to try it out.

title: “Good Place To Stay”
text:
This Super 8 is in a very good location, less than five miles from San Antonio's downtown, convention center and The Riverwalk. Easy freeway access, very good staff. 
If you book ahead of time by phone or online and have a special request, please let them know. They actually listen to and/or read your comment.s
Do yourself a favor; head south to Rigsby Avenue, turn left, immediately look left and you'll see "Ruben's Tamales". Ruben's is a San Antonio legend. Try a dozen - or more - and you'll understand why.

title: “Four-diamond hotel my behind”
text:
Do not stay here. Period. First, they advertised online as a $300 a night hotel, and my wife thought we had a great online discount of half off. So we booked the rooms at $150 a night, then our friend came up for a spontaneous visit and was quoted $150 a room at the desk. They had the same kind of room we did. Misleading marketing practices right off the bad.
Second, the room is on par with a $89 Red Roof in. The hotel has many four-diamond award plaques on the walls. Maybe those are from days gone by. There is nothing about this hotel that merits a $300 rate (which they advertise). 
Third, we pre-paid the whole stay and didn't touch the mini bar. I'm now dealing with and extra $75 in charges that magically appeared the day after we check out. So not only is the hotel crap, uses disingenuous marketing practices, but now they are trying to rip us off after we left town. 
Austin is a fantastic vacation spot I would recommend to anyone, but do not stay in this tourist trap of a hotel. 
Also, don't trust their photos of the "swimming pool." Looks great online, it's a one-lane lap pool that's about thirty feet long. Total garbage, more disingenuous marketing practices.

title: “Great place to stay, but stay clear of the insanely rude reseptionists!”
text:
We will recommend this hotel for its location, room sizes and not the least for the efficient and competent house-keeping personnel.
The reception personnel should all be fired for being dangerously incompetent and right out rude. On our first night we experienced a fire in the basement. A real fire, not just the alarm sounding. Full NYFD action with 12 huge cars and smoke-divers to put out a fire in the basement. Smoke filled the corridors. Hardly anyone reacted and the reception did not care and certainly offered no information. 
Checking out, we, as foreigners, apparently pronounced Newark airport wrong, which the receptionist found good enough reason to to make a lengthy, public don't -understand-what -these- idiots-are-trying-to-say-number. Rude and totally unnecessary. 
If you meet prepared for this, you will enjoy your stay, and we will consider a second stay.

title: “Very good value hotel - luxury lovers pay your money and book elsewhere!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for 9 nights in September 2004. We were concerned about some reviews. However, the negative reviews did not reflect our experience. The hotel staff were pleasant and helpful, the room was large and clean, breakfast was fine (seating not always available) but got to remember the breakfast was complimentary. The area was not affluent but we encountered no hassle off any person. It appeared safe to walk during the daytime, we would be cautious at night - but as in any area we were not familiar with. There was some noise but it only disturbed us on one occasion. Public transport was good and the shuttle bus was an asset. I would be happy to recommend this hotel, but of course if you wish to live in the lap of luxury and be waited on hand and foot (along with the price tag!!!) book in somewhere else. This hotel was very good value for money.

title: “Perfect Location. Average Hotel.”
text:
This hotel is in a great spot just a few feet from Times Square but the hotel itself is dated, it was under development when we stayed and most of the rooms on our floor was empty and in the process of redecoration.
The staff were friendly enough but the cafe is a little "touch and go" we had no idea what would be brought to the table each morning for breakfast even though we ordered the same thing everyday, it never looked the same twice.
We stayed on the fourth floor and the huge flag hanging outside our window kept us a wake all night with the chanins clanging in the wind!
This hotel is great for people who want a central location and are not planning on spending much time in the hotel, Its clean and value for money in that respect. But if its luxury you want, give this one a miss!

title: “Fun, trendy place to stay...”
text: We only stayed here one night as a stopover - would have loved to stayed longer - as the property was fantastic. The location was pretty good - close to shopping - a bit farther to the Waterfront and Seattle Center - but a nice walk on a dry day. Very sleek and mod. We booked 2 adjoining rooms and it was very spacious - the second room had an entry hall with lots of space - great when traveling with 3 kids. The bathrooms and layout of rooms were well thought out and very comfortable. Liked the LEED features such as the key as a master "on switch" to prevent waste of energy due to lights left on, etc., green roof. Expected the floors to be wood or recycled hard materials as in the advertisement and web - but it was still carpet - maybe some type of environmentally conscious type of carpet? I did think it was odd that the shampoos, soaps and conditioners were still provided in the small bottles that end up becoming consumer waste. Thought that they would have refillable wall mounted containers in the showers/baths to prevent excessive waste. The Spa/lockerroom did have this feature.........and the spa, pool, fitness center were all TOP NOTCH! Would stay at this hotel for that feature alone. Great saline pool, fitness equipment, steam and sauna rooms and very well equipped locker rooms.

title: “Terrible Hotel”
text:
There were not parking lot available for hotel guests. The hotel should have informed us that they are having construction work done on the premise. The construction work permitted us to find parking spaces. The construction noises started by 6:30 in the morning. 
Both phones in the hotel room do not work. The carpet looks dirty.

title: “Great location”
text: Hotel is where the 405 and 101 highways meet. Great locations, everything is within walking distance. Hotel has indoor parking garage connected to hotel which was very convienent but very expensive. Rooms are clean, decent size with a refrigerator. Would stay here again, but the room and parking prices are very expensive. There aren't many choices for hotels if you want to stay in this area.

title: “Amazing”
text:
Fabulous hotel. Close to great shops & restaurants. We didn't sample any of the nightlife locally, but it was just a short cab ride to Sunset Strip. Easy access to public transport.... Santa Monica one way & Hollywood the other for under $2. Staff were helpful, rooms were immaculate, and luxurious & we had a huge balcony we could sit out on. Pool area was nice, although we didn't use it. It was always lively. Huge shopping mall literally on the doorstep was a plus!
A very up-market hotel we booked through Priceline & got a great deal on! Impressive to say the least!

title: “great location but dont expect the ritz”
text:
I stayed at this hotel recommended to me by a collegue at work for 5 nights in late Feb 2010.
The hotel is a great location, not even a five minute walk to Times Square and about 5-10 minutes away from Central Park. Walk to most places we went to, apart from going to and from the airport and also when we went to Grand Central Station we took the subway, which only took 15 minutes.
The hotel was clean and comfortable, staff all really nice. Was on floor 25 out of 27, and had a lovely view...of the building opposite! But didnt mind at all as we were only going to sleep in it! Bathroom was really small but it made do for a short break.
One word of warning, dont eat in the restaraunt next door which is a Greek restaraunt as its really expensive. The Park Cafe which was the other side of the hotel on the corner was really nice, friendly staff and went there every morning for breakfast.
Another thing, the staff in the gift shop arent that polite!!!
This is only a 3* so dont expect the ritz. Yes it is a bit basic and dated but i chose this hotel because I knew i wouldnt be in the room all the time. New York is amazing, and will definetly go back, but when I do I'd pay more to stay at either the Park Central (opposite) or the Sheraton Hotel and Towers or the Renaissance which were both down the road nearer to Times Square.
Also advise anyone to pre-book a car back to the airport via the bellman, $55 flat rate including toll.

title: “Great people”
text:
I took Mother to see Spurs for a second year in a row. Stayed there last year and will stay there next year. 
Maribell-was a wonderful, delightful hostess. Very friendly, courteous and helpful. 
Mark-very helpful, friendly and gave us many tips to avoid problems and make the most of our time in San Antonio. 
Willie-What can I say? A very friendly and colorful personality. Loves to talk basketball and is former NBA star. He added a fun dimension to our visit.

title: “Great Location”
text:
The best thing about this hotel is the location. It is literally minutes from the very touristy Fishermans Wharf and is even closer to bus and cable car stops. There is nothing flash about the hotel but it does provide a quiet, relaxed base from which to explore San Francisco.
The room I had was spotlessly clean and was a decent size although the bathroom was a little compact. Having said that, the room had everything needed for your stay. In room safe, tea/coffee, hair dryer, iron, etc were all included free of charge. The huge bed was comfortable and provided a sound nights sleep.
Breakfast was disappointing. The continental selection was small and the only warm food available was an apple cake. It wasn't bad, just that I prefer a cooked breakfast, or at least the option of one.
There is a small fitness room in the hotel with six or seven exercise machines available free of charge.
The hotel has no bar but the one directly across the street (knuckles) is excellent and I'd recommend the BBQ pizza which is big enough for two and only costs $13.
The Holiday Inn Express is designed for the customer who only uses the hotel for sleep and rest and they have got the balance just right. It is a perfect base to explore San Francisco and have a restful nights sleep after all that hill walking.
I would use this hotel again

title: “For a short overnight stay it'll do the job!!”
text: After searching for this hotel w/my GPS I actually found it by having a nearby hotel look up the phone number for me. There's no iron or alarm clock in the room but they do have wi-fi. The front desk clerk was nice and the rate was great ($65) for this weekend-there is a slight odor in the room, that's my only complaint.

title: “NIGHTMARE HOTEL!”
text: I booked a room for 4 nights online. Their web site makes it sound really nice. The lobby looks really nice, and that's it! The girl behind desk didn't speak/understand English very well. The room not only looked dirty but felt dirty. They should have spent the lobby $$ on the rooms! They don't provide rooms with the things their web site says (clocks- they ran out!). No screen on window, electrical outlets coming loose from walls, no one was friendly. Someone kept trying to get in our room. We left next day, they still charged for the 4 days. BEWARE!!!! Cheap is not always better! I've stayed in cheaper places and they were 100% better!

title: “Good location for day trip to Little Tokyo and Garment District”
text:
Stayed on 14th floor overlooking garden. The room was pleasant but there was a wedding event and you can hear the music and the loud DJ even from the 14th floor. Those windows need to be updated. Conveniently located in Littel Tokyo with plenty of restaurants and shops and aproximately 6 blocks of walking to the garment district. Its an urban area with homeless people (downtown Los Angeles) so be prepared. We got a great rate for $129/night which included two breakfast buffets and free self parking. Parking I believe is $30 and buffet is $20/pp which I didn't think was all that great. Just standard breakfast fare except for the miso soup.
Pros:
- great downtown location for Little Tokyo, Garment District
- Clean room
- Big TV
Cons
- Noise from below
- Weak shower head
- expensive parking

title: “What a let down”
text:
We had been traveliing around California for two and half weeks and we were all looking forward to staying in one place for a few nights, we booked into the Kona Kai as it seemed to tick the boxes. 
Not cheap but we'd wanted somewhere nice to stay for our last leg in California, 
Pool 
Beach
Gym
Bed & Breakfast included.
Well our room was onto the beach but it is a manmade beach which leads to the Harbour which I didn't appreciate, this aside our first night was spent listening to a group of teenagers hanging out on the beach followed by the constant echo of doors slamming into the night. To be fair the staff did say that we could move rooms but as the majority of rooms are in a similar position and we'd now unpacked there seemed little point. 
The included breakfast was for two only, apparently children don't need to eat in the USA and the cost of additional breakfast orders were ridiculous. We opted to use our vouchers for all of us then head to Dennys for the remaining mornings.
The other nasty surprise (should have checked trip advisor first) was the $15 a night parking fee. This was not mentioned on our booking confirmation and so we were totally unaware of it. Also the addtional cost to use the gym, had the staff been a little more pleasant at the time of check in we would have thought 'oh well our mistake' but the arrogance of the check in clerks especially when i mentioned about the parking and the breakfast costs, immediately made me wish to spend as little money in this hotel as possible. I cannot therefore tell you about the restaurant because we ate out every night. 
The hotel views are nice if you like looking at other peoples boats, otherwise go elsewhere.

title: “By far the Best Best Western this trip”
text: I stayed at this hotel back in Nov 2011 when I returned to this area I knew that there was no other place for me to stay. The first night we arrived so late that we stayed at the BW near the airport (more on that one) and when we stayed in Austin this trip we stayed at another BW (later for that one too) Anyway I was given the same room that I stayed in the last time which was big and roomy. Nice king size bed, frig, sink, coffee area. Nice ouch with the welcome basket with water and chips. Sofa, desk, coffee table and huge bathroom. We styed here two nights then to Austin for 2 nights and tomorrow we are going back to San Antonio so as soon as I am done with this review I will call them to book there. The staff is friendly, nice huge breakfast (you can make a waffle in the shape of Texas, CUTE!), walking distance to the riverwalk, safes at front desk, free parking and stop by the front desk to get a discount on the trolley fares. I loved it here the first time, loved it here again. Thanks to everyone at this BW

title: “Cheap Hotel and It Shows”
text: First of all this wasn't a terrible hotel. It is a good hotel if you just need to stopover for the night. However you get what you pay for. In my room, one of the lights in the bathroom was out and the walls are really thin. The hallway was a little dirty, but at least it was interior corridors. Note though that this hotel is right next to a strip club, so if you're near the front of the hotel you will hear some noise, and obviously this is not a hotel for children. No extra amenities like a pool or even a breakfast. Again, not a bad stopover hotel, but wouldn't stay here more than one night, you get what you pay for.

title: “This Time Was Even Better Than The Last!”
text:
LOVE THIS RESORT! I've stayed here for biz many times, about 15 years ago. In 2007, we came as a family and had THE BEST vacation! But, last week, we returned and the resort is completely renovated! Our suite was SWEET! VERY spacious! Every suite is in a great location! The pools are easily accessible from each building. 
And, speaking of pools, they are SO CLEAN (& I'm very picky:)! We had a riot on the slides! Families join each other for fun games of water volleyball! And, the "Dive-In" movies at night are so much fun! My 15 year old daughter and I were just exploring the resort after dinner and ended up at the pool for the evening. Great bonding time! 
Moving on to the golf course, our daughter and my husband LOVED playing it! Reasonably priced and beautifully maintained (our daughter beat her dad:) 
I'm a fitness fanatic. I was VERY impressed with the health club! Equipment, classes, spa...it's all there! Again, our daughter and my husband LOVED playing basketball on the indoor court!
You can rent bikes and bike South Mountain or you can just lace up your shoes and hike it. We did (right from the hotel) and the view was magnificent! 
But, lots of resorts have beautiful suites and great amenities. What sets the Arizona Grand apart from the others for me (and I've traveled extensively) are the people. The staff is welcoming, accommodating, friendly, funny, problem solvers and make you feel right at home!
