From the front desk (Tim, Ryan, Royce, Ginger and so many others) to the bell men, to housekeeping to the concierge, EVERYONE was there to assure our vacation was everything we wanted it to be...wait...they made it MORE than we ever expected:)! It was our 18 wedding anniversary and our daughter's 16th birthday (almost:).
THANK YOU ARIZONA GRAND! We're already planning our return for late March 2013, with our nephew, his wife and their 3 children:)! Any villas available:)!?

title: “Good choice”
text:
Just returned from 5 nights in New York. I'd been keeping an eye on the reviews of the Belleclaire so it already felt familiar to me when we arrived. The staff were friendly and helpful. 
The room was on the small side but was fine. We went for the shared bathroom accommodation and it was ok. Our room was one of three in it's own lobby behind a swipe card operated door. The reason for this is to keep our allocated bathroom for use only by 3 rooms. One downside to this was that there were now 2 extra doors banging whenever any of the other guests in our little area came through or used the bathroom. Some people seem happy to let doors swing shut loudly as opposed to closing them gently. Oh well. 
Our room overlooked the corner of 77th Street and Broadway and although it was on the 9th floor it was a bit noisy. New Yorkers love to use the horns on their cars! Also the local fire station was nearby which resulted in us being woken by loud sirens in the middle of the night a few times.
We breakfasted at the Manhattan Diner opposite the hotel where you can get a filling breakfast for $5-£6. The local subway is about 3 minutes away so getting to other areas was easy. There is a cinema about 5 minutes walk away. Central Park is nearby and genarally the area feels safe. Barnes and Noble bookstore is also about 5 minutes walk - a very nice shop. And yes the lifts are a bit slow - so what?
If you want decent basic accommodation on a low budget, I'd recommend this hotel.

title: “I checked out after 2 nights.”
text: I checked out after two days. The hotel's designer seemed to mistake cheap, sparse decor for good design. Yes they were trying to work with small paces, but aside from the large windows providing light, there was nothing that constituted good design. Lighting was dark in the bathroom, and in the bedroom it was poor. There were no chairs except for an uncomfortable felt-covered stool and a black vinyl bean-bag chair. The hotel had just opened yet already the shower seemed to be backed up and a light was broken. Storage in the bathroom was non-existent. Front desk staff was friendly and felt slippers were provided to shield feet from cold hard concrete floors.

title: “5 day break”
text: I have just returned from a 5 day break in New York where I stayed in the Crowne Plaza hotel in Times Square that turned out to be the perfect choice as a central base to visit all the main attractions and shops,including Central Park, 5th Avenue, Trump Tower, Rockerfeller Centre, Maceys and the Empire State Building. The hotel was excellent, with all the usual accessories in the room we had on the 38th floor that had spectacular views of Manhattan in all directions. The breakfasts were great with a large variety for all tastes and prices to suit all pockets. The staff were all very helpful and polite at all times and the concierge service was well organised especially their storage service for those who had night time flights back home. All in all the right choice for a short stay in the big apple and if you go at thanksgiving day, the shops are all half price the next day.

title: “The hotel was clean, cozy and had excellant service”
text: I enjoyed staying at this hotel, the rooms were a bit small but very nice, everything was new and the service was excellant. The price was good, too. The location was good, as it was on a small side street, but very close to a major street. I will stay here again.

title: “beautiful decor”
text: had a beautiful corner room with a view of the park, staff was helpful and attentive

title: “Very good”
text:
This hotel is in an excellent position in NYC, literally 20m far from Times Square.
Room is small but clean and OK to sleep (what else would you do in your hotel room while you are in NYC?). I also had excellent support in arranging the transport from JFK airport and in getting hints to arrange my visits around the city.

title: “Needs to be Renovated!”
text: I've stayed at several hotels in the Philly/Center City area, but this has got to be my biggest disappointment. At a rate very comparable to the other hotels, this one did not measure up to standards. On the front door is a sign that says, "Hotel Suites from $895 per month". This has to be the first sign that something is wrong. The hotel is filled with young, college students, renting there because they get cheap monthly rates. They should just convert it to a full apartment community. But to keep it as a hotel/apartment home is a disappointment. The rooms need cleaning, the appliances are old and need maintenance. I'm shocked that this is a Marriott Execustay property. I expected a whole lot more from a Marriott!!! Please renovate this hotel, fast !!!

title: “Honestly, I liked the Hotel Felix”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights this spring, and it was an enjoyable experience. Yes, the room I stayed in was small, but entirely adequate for my needs. I loved the interior design and the H20 products. My room was quiet, and I'm a light sleeper, so would have noticed if it wasn't. Everyone on the staff that I dealt with was very polite and friendly -- absolutely no issues there. I also really liked the location -- really just a short walk to Michigan Ave, and plenty of restaurants and conveniences located nearby. I'd stay here again.

title: “Pricey but very nice and great location”
text: I stayed here in June for business, when I moved from the Hilton when its power went out for many hours. The Jemeirah is very nice and a big step up from the Hilton. Great service. Easy check in. Beautiful decor. Bed is very comfortable and there are all the little extras in the room. The hotel is just opposite the park and very close to the Time Warner building where you will find Wholefoods and some good shopping. The subway is close by too. My only gripe was that, because I was a last minute booking, they charged me over USD$650 (incl tax)...way overpriced especially as they lowered it by $300 for my following two nights and I stayed in the same room. So, beautiful hotel but a bit expensive.

title: “Hampton Inn Downtown San Diego”
text:
I stayed here one nite, very nice and clean, Hall ways were hot,
Room was nice and clean, but small. 
The train runs behind the Hotel until 10p, so that was tolerateable, 
The plus was being able to walk a 2 blocks to the ocean and the Star of India (Ship) 
I think $160 was a little steep, but if you want to be close to the action, this is the place to stay, 
Checked out early so I didnt get a chance to try the breakfast, 
I Will add that I noticed someone from security that walked the halls at 6p and at 4a so that makes me feel like they were wanting to keeps the guests safe.
I will stay there again.

title: “Great Location - Does exactly what it says on the tin!”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights on our honeymoon. Read all the reviews beforehand and expected a 3* hotel in an old building with small rooms, but in a great location. And that's exactly what we got.
Was a bit disappointed with the room initially as ours was facing inside the hotel to a fire escape and was so dark we had to have the light on during a sunny day. Did consider asking if we could swap, but my wife (typical Englishwoman!) did not want to cause a fuss so we stayed put. In the end the room was fine and we were out exploring most of the time anyway so it was no big deal.
Didn't visit the bar and restaurant as there is so much choice locally, but all the staff were friendly and helpful. It was our first visit to San Francisco and we loved the city - so much to do and see, we could have stayed a week and cannot wait to go back again one day.
If you want a base at a reasonable price in a great location, then I would recommend The Chancellor, just don't expect The Ritz or Vegas size suites as you will be disappointed!
p.s. Loving the Managers feedback to some of the reviews on Tripadvisor. Good to see a human touch with a bit of humour, rather than the usual corporate robotic hotel rep's comments. Keep em coming and keep up the good work Chancellor!

title: “Economical room rates and excellent location!!!!! Could not be happier!!”
text: My family and I just had our second Spring Break stay at the Hotel Edison. The hotel is clean, has a friendly staff, and most importantly has an awesome location. It is right off Times Square!!!! My kids loved it!!! The hotel may not be the fanciest in New York City but it is so nice and very economical. The rates were so much less expensive than all the other hotels in the area. My family and I were out everyday sight seeing and came back every evening and just crashed on the nice clean beds. I definitely will be back.

title: “Heart of Little Tokyo-Close to Amtrak Station”
text:
My husband and I recently did some traveling via Amtrak. We had an overnight stay in Los Angeles so I chose a Hotel that would be close to the Amtrak station. The Miyako is in Little Tokyo, I did realize this when I made the reservations but didn't realize what the situation would be. Much of the information in the room was in Japanese so I couldn't read about anything that the Hotel had to offer. 
We arrived rather late in the evening. The hotel lobby was a little scary to me at first and I was really worried that I had made reservations to stay there. Our room was ok, nothing special. I really did enjoy the linens on the beds though. They also had down comforters, something you don't find in a lot of hotels these days. They do charge for phone calls, even when you have a calling card. I had to get the front desk to allow my call by giving my credit card number to them once again. Most Hotels where I have stayed do not charge for calling card calls. It wasn't a big deal just somewhat of an inconvenience.
The following morning I made a trip to the lobby and was surprised by the difference from the night before. They have a gift shop and a small cafe that was opened and it really helped brighten up the look of the lobby.
I had hoped to check out some nearby restaurants while we were there since we had time before we needed to catch the train but my husband wasn't that comfortable so we just headed back to Union Station.

title: “Eastgate met all high expectations!”
text:
I've stayed at Eastgate Tower Suite hotel from July 10th until July 24th with my wife for our honeymoon trip. After thorough search (mostly through Tripadvisor), we opted for Eastgate based on reviews, and then location, price and amenities.
We've booked a junior suite directly with the hotel even though we could've found a better deal through some other travel agency. I would've used that 'card' if found in a situation to argue the quality of service.
Fortunately, it wasn't needed at all. In my reservation I had mentioned that this was a honeymoon trip, that we want to make it as special as possible and that we'd like a non-smoking suite with street view above 5th floor. What we got was beyond any expectation: great suite on 22nd floor with street view (everything is street view from that height which we found especially interesting and NY-ish), path from the door to the bed of rose petals, bed covered with petals and a couple of roses, more petals in the bathroom, couple more roses on the table, a personalized greeting card from the hotel, two small boxes with chocolate candies, a book of love poetry, champagne and, erm, can of whipped cream on a silver tray in the fridge. We were hoping for something extra but this was really nice! Suite was great, very spacious for the two of us, much light from outside and also many lamps inside, furniture in very good shape, comfy bed, all very clean, even the carpet which is usually in poor shape in many hotels. The bathroom was also in an excellent shape and as clean as possible. Everything was functioning properly: AC, TV, phone, microwave, stove, fridge... Closet space was more than enough for a longer stay like ours (for 2 people, anyway...). Towels and sheets were changed daily and cleaning staff was respecting our daily late-leaving. Surrounding didn't seem any dangerous and we didn't mind some walking from and to the hotel (5th Avenue is 5 blocks away, subway at Grand Central station also 5 blocks away, Loews movie theater 7 small blocks downtown @ 2nd and 32nd, several 24hrs convenience stores in the same block, many fine delis all around the neighborhood (we especially liked Food Merchants @ 40th st between Park and Madison for breakfast). Didn't try the resident Sogno restaurant, though...
Staff was also exceptionally nice, as expected based on the reviews. As we've had a late flight back to Europe, it was no problem to check-out at 6pm.
Any bad things after all this praising? Well, the elevators could be somewhat faster, the lobby is very small, as well as the corridors on the floors. Wood furniture (tables, bedside cabinets, drawer cabinet...) would look finer in dark wood than in ivory-colored combination... These aren't really bad things: if we wanted giant lobby, spacious corridors with armchairs, superquick elevators and mahogany furniture, we'd look for the most expensive hotel in NYC. For all other details, Eatsgate was just as fine. 
Have we just been fortunate or treated better since it was a honeymoon? I doubt it. I guess that some rooms might be in different shape but I'm sure that a staff this helpful can overcome each issue with a guest. We didn' have any, really.
Eastgate Tower has met all our high expectations and we will surely come there again, hopefully already next summer for our 'honeymoon re-run'.

title: “Excellent get away”
text:
We had a wonderful time. The hotel and its staff where excellent. When making your reservation request a room in the tower and a high floor, the views are spectacular. The spa was great, to cold for the pool, but from what I could see the kids loved the slides. 
When booking and using your debit card be aware that there will be a $75.00 hold on funds, this is for any incidentals. We where told upfront so there where no suprise charges. We would definitely stay again. The Red Marlin a bit over priced but the food was excellent.

title: “Beautiful Hotel Not So Great Staff”
text: This truly is a gorgeous property and the rooms are beautiful as well, however, the staff leaves something to be desired. The staff at this hotel came very close to ruining a good portion of my wedding day because of their lack of attention to detail. I had worked with a staff member to preview and book a suite in the hotel at the end of July for my wedding that was in early November. Two days before the wedding one of our family members called to pay for one of our nights at the hotel and NO RESERVATIONS! The person we worked with was less than helpful to fix the situation and the two other people we spoke with took a totally indifferent attitude, it was unbelievable. We had to resort to yelling at the person and requesting several times to speak to a manager, who has still yet to return my calls. In the end they gave us a room similar to the one I was supposed to have, but not without a whole bunch of unnecessary stress two days before my wedding. The suite that we had was beautiful, PNW ballet themed, and had a great view of the water. I found the front desk staff to be annoyed with any request we made, and we were not particularly high maintenance only asked for some extra pillows and blankets. I wish I could say that my husband and I would be back to celebrate our anniversary next year but I just cannot justify the price for lack luster service at best.

title: “Clean, elegant, friendly and ideally located”
text: If you can give this hotel a negative review, then you're standard of living is in the stratosphere. First, this location cannot be beat. I am an Honors member and they gave me a wonderful, large suite. Beautiful finishings in the bathrooms. Wonderful seating area. Exceptionally clean. Staff was great during our entire stay.

title: “Pay attention before you book”
text:
This can be a good choice but you need to pay attention.
The hotel is next to the new convention center. That means construction noise. The contractor is permitted to work 24 hours a day - fortunately they don't do that often. However, expect them to start making quite a lot of noise by 7 am. It may be as early as 6 am and you might get lucky and avoid noise until 8 am but the noise will happen. If you have ever been around a construction site you know that in addition to noise that also means dust and fences that block the sidewalks. 
Now, if you are looking at this hotel and thinking of a suite - think twice. The suites all face the construction. That's because when they built the hotel it made sense for the nicest rooms to have a great view. However, that great is now being turned into a convention center. So if you really want a suite I'd stay elsewhere. If at check-in they offer to upgrade you to a suite, I'd suggest that you ask if it faces the construction and, when they say yes, politely decline the upgrade. Note, when the construction is complete the suites are very large and nice. But as of April 2010 they barely have the floors in place so don't expect the construction to end anytime soon.
The regular rooms are a different story. If you get one away from the construction they are very quiet. The lowest numbers are the farthest away (i.e., rooms o2, 03 etc are great - as in 403 or 803 etc). Because this is an older property the rooms are good sized. 
The hotel itself is a lot nicer that the typical Hampton Inn. It clearly used to be something else. It is a little old and tired, but not dirty. Keep in mind that you are in downtown Philly and the only thing that isn't old and tired costs several times more than the Hampton. The staff are excellent. I found them to uniformly helpful and intelligent. 
The hotel is about 3 blocks from the Reading Terminal. That means about 4 blocks from Market Street (a main drag). It is an easy walk. However, you won't want to take a train from the airport unless you don't mind hauling luggage. That brings me to the only issue I saw which is cabs. The hotel is a little off the path and with the construction mess there are no cabs outside the door. However, one call to the front desk and a cab was there within seconds so it's not an issue.
Overall, a good spot if you don't need a suite.

title: “Doesn't deserve such high ratings”
text:
The good;
Friendly staff.
Breakfast would have been good if it wasn't in the lobby while they renovate restaurant.
The bad;
Noisy bed. Asked the staff to try and fix it, but they couldn't do anything about it. We had to detach the headboard (the source of the noise) ourselves.
TINY room. I think we were really unlucky here - the pictures other people have shared make the rooms look reasonably sized. However our room barely fitted a double bed. We booked our standard ballet room over 3 months in advance. We paid the same as people in reasonably sized rooms. Seems somewhat unfair.
Noisy hotel. The walls are paper thin. I now know the people in the next room are looking to buy property. Not met them but feel like I know them intimately.

title: “Just a great hotel”
text:
Ok, so the service isn't something to write home about. But I managed to crack a few smiles from these tough cookies.
I stay in nyc very frequently, for business and pleasure. After tiring of crappy hotels uptown, downtown, all around town I decided to either stay at the Stanhope (my favorite NY hotel) or the Excelsior which provided a convenient location for my business at hand.
The lobby is lovely. Large but cozy. Very nice. Immediately the place struck me as clean and classy - and wasn't pretending to be.
When checking in I jokingly suggested that they should upgrade me. 
Well, upon entering my room I found they did! It was a junior suite and very nice. A cozy entrance with a work-table and large closet welcomed me. Walking thru my french doors I entered the main room. The view out the window was of a brickwall, but so what - im not at the hotel for a view. The bathroom was perfect, even over-the-top. PLENTY of towels.
Now, the bed? WOAH! My cranky back just loved this bed. I slept SO well. Really, I woke up and was just shocked at how well I slept. The blanket was so warm and cozy! I felt like I was at home under my own blanket.
Just a great hotel. Not quite the Stanhope - but definately in the same league.
The Excelsior will have me as a guest again.

title: “Great vacation”
text: We stayed at the Dana this past weekend and had an amazing experience. We stayed in a first floor room in the new section of the property and had a beautiful view of the bay. We enjoyed the bay pool with our 2 year old son, and had a great view of the nightly fireworks over at Sea World. Customer service was good at the front desk and pool. We would definitely go back in the future!

title: “Perfect location”
text:
First time visitors to Washington,perfect location for sightseeing. Suite spacious
spotlessly clean and had everything you would need. Staff amazingly helpful
and extremely courteous at all times. Easy walk to Georgetown's many restaurants. Easy access to train to centre of Museum district. Close cab ride to Arlington Cemetry (or long walk). Had a fabulous 4 days here, would recommend it to everyone. Certainly would love to go back.
Aussies on Holidays

title: “AMAZING!!!!!!!!”
text: My family and I decided to travel to Chicago and stay downtown for a week. Our daughter found the hotel online, and we looked at the pictures and liked it. When comparing the prices with other hotels, it was cheaper, so we decided to book it. Booking the hotel for a week was the best decision we made! We were two blocks from the parks (Millennium and Grant), and within walking distance from the Art Institute. The staff was amazing, friendly, and helpful! We can´t wait to stay there again next year! We highly recommend it!

title: “STAFF GREAT!! HOTEL, NOT SO MUCH.”
text:
The only reason I will not stay here again is the lack of hot water and the staff being unable to resolve the problem. With the knob all the way to hot the water was only luke warm at best and when there were more than a few guests drawing from it the water was uncomfortably cool. And other than quite a few inconsiderate guests slamming their doors at all hours our stay was pretty good. The staff were very friendly and considerate, the breakfast was good and better than the HIE I am staying in right now. 
The hotel is dated and needs some updates including internet speed, new electrical outlets, door closures to eliminate slamming and waking guests, door seals to keep interstate 35 noise from infiltrating rooms, ect., ect., ect.
Overall it was an average hotel.

title: “Excellent experience overall”
text: I and several colleagues stayed at the Andaz for a week-long business trip, and it speaks volumes for the experience that not one person in the group of frequent business travellers had a single complaint, and instead most had praise and made sure we were booked here for our next trip. That never happens! The staff is very helpful (although someone did try to check us in again every single time we came in with rolling briefcases!), but it is the overall atmosphere and approach that makes it a nice change from your typical hotel. There is more of a boutique/living room feel to the lobby, and guests have lots of places to sit and enjoy the complementary wine in the evenings while clearing emails or catching up. It is very inviting, as is the bar on the concourse level. The rooms feel more like an apartment to me than a hotel room, and were very comfortable. The Respire rooms are great if you have allergies - I was put in one after merely asking for foam pillows, and it actually made a big difference for me. For the rates charged in NY, it is nice to see a hotel including soft drinks and snacks in your room at no charge, along with wireless. If you have any reason to stay downtown, the Andaz is a great choice for business or leisure, and is close to the subway - I was able to easily get to midtown for a business dinner by hopping the subway, although you do have to allow about 30 minutes. Great hotel, we'll be back.

title: “Good location/price, but not good sleep & shower”
text: I stayed here when it first opened so I knew the rooms would be small (plus price & location must equal small rooms). I booked thru hotwire after out train was seriously delayed so definitley cant complain about price & location. I do agree with other reviewes about location and style. However - a few warnings, the double bed was smaller than a normal double bed which made sleeping very tough (we were two) especially coupled with a LOUD A/C that would not cool down to lower than 73 degrees. Walking in to the room, we immediatley noticed that the door clasp was missing so no extra "chain" lock. The ipod dock was also broken. After a very long day (& warm for NYC in Jan.) we really needed showers - the water pressure was terrible and there was only one washcloth. We were on the 18th floor and it's an old building so I guess I cant expect much - this is just a warning to others not to expect the two things needed from a hotel - good sleep and a good shower.

title: “It's okay”
text:
For some reason I was thinking this would be more of a hotel experience but, as the previous reviewer states, it is a motel with little frills. We were on the second floor so we weren't close too the parking noise but we did hear our upstairs neighbors walking. I felt bad for the neighbors below as we traveled with our 3 children so having them walk quietly was a challenge. 
We got a 2 queen room with a kitchenette. The beds were comfortable, and the small kitchen area was appreciated. The kitchen had a small 2 burner stove, with a mini fridge and small mircrowave. It was nice to have the silverware and dishes provided as well. Just wish they had provided more than just 3 of each with a family of 5. We had to have the kids eat first, then dish ourselves up. But we managed.
The pool was nice and we did take advantage of that during our trip. The kids really enjoyed going during the weekend to attend the pool side movie they played. My only compliant is I wish they played the movie a little earlier. It didnt start till 830pm so wasn't over until close to 10pm. My younger two passed out both nights around 9pm so it wasn't worth it for them.
And I have to agree, the resturaunt was not very good at all. We went because kids eat free so thought we would give it a try. The food wasn't very good and when we got our bill, were upset to find out that the Happy Hour specials were not combinable with the Kids Eat Free specials. The waiter or the flyer for the Happy Hour specials never mentioned this so we ended up paying full price instead. 
I don't know if I would stay at this hotel again. It's a great place if you don't plan on staying in your hotel at all except to sleep. With 3 young children, I think it was a little too cramped for us.

title: “Will always come back”
text:
I've stayed here twice when visiting SFO for businesse and will stay here every time I can. 
Food is very good, love the lobby bar and rooms are amazing. Best bed EVER! 
The View Bar is one of the best views of the city and a very nice place to grab a bite. Great drinks too! 
Location is very good. I don't like hotels that are closer to Union Square, stayed there before and they are way too noisy.
Fitness Center is amazing, great pool!

title: “We will be back !!”
text:
Stayed at the Fairmont from May 20th - 26th. My #1 suggestion to anyone staying here is to join their executive club (its free) BEFORE staying or checking in at the Hotel. I had to have a late night battle with the clerk who said that I would be charged $14/day for high speed internet access since I didn't sign my membership card BEFORE I sighed the check in form. 
Great things about this hotel include:
* One of the best Hotel gyms I have ever used. If you don't belong to the executive club (see above) you have to pay $15/visit. All the equipment is brand new.
* Great room (#750) overlooking the central courtyard. We opened our balacony doors and let the cool breezes blow in during the day
* Close to Georgeown (Nuff said)
* Close to Metro stop (4 blocks)
* Free shoe shines 
My only complaint
* The fire alarm went off three times during our stay. We received no explanation from the Hotel staff on why this occured.
In short, we will be back.

title: “Courtyard DC/US Capitol”
text: This Marriott is in a great location for federal workers traveling to GSA or ATF's central offices. It's an easy metro ride from DCA and just one stop past Union Station. There are some places to eat within walking distance, but many more just a redline metro trip west to Gallery Place. Overall the hotel is new and clean. The staff is friendly and helpful. Other than free internet, there really isn't much offered to Elite Marriott members, e.g. no free drinks, breakfast, etc.

title: “Hate to do it in case rooms are hard to get in the future, but this place is GREAT!”
text:
The staff, staff, staff!! Amazingly friendly and helpful, every single one of them. Truly made you feel as if they were glad you chose their hotel. I hope the management appreciates all of the staff!!
We stayed in one of the 19th floor suites, and it was sweet! The best shower ever, with multiple shower heads. I realize the other rooms don't have them, but worth the additional cost. And the 19th floor rooms come with amazing views of NYC and the Empire State Building etc. 
Quiet area, adjacent to the Holland Tunnel, so driving home was a snap. 
Great beds, great free breakfast, etc. Can't wait for them to get their bar license, then it will be perfect!
Cons: No free wifi in the rooms, but there is free broadband hookup in the rooms. Save yourself some aggravation . . . if you want to order food to be delivered, skip the americatogo that the hotel recommends (doesn't work, takes forever, and the restaurant prices turned out to be cheaper) and just google Soho restaurants with delivery. 
Within walking distance to Little Italy, Chinatown, and even Greenwich Village (just wear comfortable shoes). Great shopping in the area too. 
One of our great surprises/finds . . . The French Culinary school is within walking distance and has a student run restaurant. Great food at a really great price.

title: “One of the best Marriott properties in the world.”
text: From the time you enter the Denver Cherry Creek Marriott, you are greeted by a cordial, professional and extremely friendly staff. They certainly make you feel at home. Having stayed at Marriotts all over the world - this Marriott stands out due to the extraordinary staff - from the valet attendants, to the front desk, the bellmen/bellwomen, the concierge, the folks in the restarant and bar, hotel managers and the room attendants - all in their own way make your experience remarkable and needless to say, pleasurable. A great team of professionals working diligently to make your stay memorable!

title: “Wonderful stay at the Intercontinental”
text: We came to Chicago for the Thanksgiving Holiday with other family members. Service was wonderful, room and all the amenities very comfortable. We had the holiday dinner and wine pairing in Zest and also found it to be excellent quality and quantity, as were the morning buffet breakfasts. The package we booked also included the valet parking which worked very very well.

title: “not Bad if You Don't Mind Soiled Underwear by Your Bed Upon Check-in...”
text: I normally love Renaissance Hotels. For this one, however, I have one HUGE complaint that left me absolutely turned off to this one. When my girlfriend and I entered the room, we found trash and soiled underwear by the bed. It was completely disgusting. If we ever stay at another Renaissance Hotel, it certainly won't be the one in Denver!

title: “Expecting More”
text:
This was my first stay at the St. Regis NYC, the flagship property. I've stayed at most St. Regis properties in the USA. I had been in the lobby a couple years back during a day trip to the city and said then I had to come back soon to stay here. I brought my parents from Mississippi to the Big Apple for their first experience in the city. We picked three Starwood properties to stay in while in town...W Times Square, The Chatwal, and the St. Regis. I rank the St. Regis 3rd out of these three. 
The staff is quite friendly, always someone to open a door and greet you. The old time charm is nice. The King Cole Bar meets up to the hype (although I was told that I was not appropriately dressed with my shorts on as I walked around the property snapping a few photos with my iPhone of the bar). Our butler was wonderful and gave us a bit of history about the place as he took care of having some clothes pressed for us. We were told that tea and coffee would soon arrive after our checkin, but it never came (the chocolates, fruit, and bottled waters were nice though). We did get coffee and tea at wake up call. The turndown service was nice. 
The only real disappointments came as we were not offered any kind of upgrade for SPG platinum and our room was quite dated. The carpet was worn, the bed sank to one side, the wall paper not appealing, gold bathroom fixtures needing updates, and the tv must have been one of the first plasmas ever made. 
Overall, wonderful service but needing a complete update of all rooms. May stay here again. The Chatwal has it all in NYC.

title: “It was a nightmare”
text: They did not give the price quoted once we arrivered in Phoenix, the security was awesome, but the front desk clerks were rude.

title: “great place, great location when you head in for a one night stay!”
text: I had stayed at this hotel a long time back and while the rooms seem in need of a bit of an update, they are by far larger than most in the downtown magnificent mile for the price! Staff is extremely friendly and attentive--hitting the elevator buttons when they see you coming toward the elevators, etc. . .--the only complaint I have and it is partially my fault, is that at check in, I wish, the front desk had briefly gone over my paperwork with me--inside were my coupons for the free beverage of choice dropped off at my room in the morning and paper--i didn't realize it until the morning when looking over my things and wondering why there was nothing available. . .i wish she had mentioned to hang it on my door before 2am. otherwise--everything was just wonderful!

title: “Good location”
text: Stayed for three nights in February 2012. Central location. Rooms are so tiny and wifi is terriblly poor. Staff was helpful and no complains about them. No noice on the 13th floor room.

title: “Perfect for exploring on foot”
text: Just stayed for 5 nights at the Hampton Majestic - started our break going to Jersey Boys, right next door - what a beautiful theatre! Our room was the quietest we have ever had, and the beds were extraordinary - we slept like logs. Breakfast was surprisingly nice, with great coffee, and then we would set out for the day. Not only could we walk everywhere in the vicinity of the Loop, but stops for all the metro lines, were around the corner. I just don't think the hotel could be more conveniently located. It was our first trip to Chicago, and staying at the Hampton allowed us to make the most of our visit.

title: “Nice king suite in older property”
text:
My husband & I stayed for 1 night (a Friday) the first weekend in June. We checked in around 6 pm and didn’t have any problems or wait. The staff was very friendly and helpful in showing us how to get to our room. We had a king suite on the ground floor. The location was perfect, not to close to the river ranch, but not too far. The room and bed was comfortable and the couch in the living area was great for lounging. The property itself is older and could use a good power washing on the outside but it was not run-down or dirty and our room was fine. 
The night we were there the hotel was having its “dive-in-movie”, which I think is great and we would have enjoyed watching but decided to float in the lazy river instead. There was a ton of teenagers staying not just younger kids and most of them were in the lazy river while movie was on. It looks like a great place to take your kids to enjoy so we decided we would go again next year and take our son who will be old enough to enjoy it then. 
We chose to eat dinner at Hole-in-the-wall on the outdoor patio. I felt the meal was overpriced, one beer, one mixed drink, a burger & pork sandwich for $45.00! Next time I’ll eat dinner off-site. We chose to eat breakfast offsite and found a cute little place a few miles away called Scramble. Food was good and it was kid and pet friendly.
My only gripe is that I think they should have at least 2 complimentary bottles of water in each room. It is Arizona after all! I wouldn’t normally be bugged by this except that the Rodeo Drive store closes at 8:00, the bar at Hole-in-the-wall didn’t have any bottles to sell me & 3 vending machines that I checked were out of water. I ended up having to walk to the lobby & run into the store there as they were closing just to get a bottle. 
We did go back to the river ranch area around 10:00 Saturday morning and it was not overcrowded yet. We tried to lounge up by the lazy river, which had cushions on the chairs, but my husband kept getting bitten by mosquitos. So if you’re like him and attract mosquitos bring DEET. We moved from the loungers & got in the pool until it was time to check out. 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a relatively inexpensive overnight or weekend getaway with family.

title: “Excellent Location, Clean Rooms, and Great Service”
text: The hotel is on the same block as the Metro station which is extremely convenient. The area was safe but there were homeless people around which I guess a sad fact of city life. The room was nicely appointed and very clean. I liked the fact that they use cotton duvet covers. You could tell they were laundered after each quest as they were a bright white. The hotel is walking distance to the White House, Washington Monument, Spy Museum, Smithsonian, and Fords Theater. A lot of nice restaurants nearby including the hotels - ask the Concierge for a list. The valet parking (only option) was expensive at $35 a night. There are quite a few parking lots nearby so you could perhaps do better in price. Overall, It was a great trip due in part to such a fine hotel with excellent service!

title: “Better than Expected”
text:
I had fairly low expectations because of some of the lukewarm Tripadvisor reviews. It outperformed those expectations.
The rooms really are suites. Mine had a living room, full kitchen, and separate bedroom. Two TV's with HBO. The kitchen was stocked with coffee, popcorn, and a candy bar. There were some plates, sliverware, and kitchen utensils.
Adequate parking is provided and, again, is free.
Breakfast was included. Nothing special, certainly, but good enough. Cereal, waffles, bread, a limited selection of juices, and coffee/tea. Similarly, free wireless internet is also included. A little slow, but adequate. It measured in the 600 kps range, whereas a really good connection would be 10 times that.
Somewhat unexpectedly, the hotel lobby is on what it calls the 1st floor, but what everybody else in this country would call the second floor. It's a little confusing.
Downsides: it definitely has what I think is the smell of chlorine from the pool. It didn't bother me, but it would bother those who are sensitive to such odors. It is clean but shopworn. Not fancy at all.

title: “Overrated!!”
text: Not sure why so many people like this place. I was very disapointed, maybe that's because I'm used to the great service and great rooms at the Hotel 1000. Tried The W for wife's bday to find my room dirty (holiday Inn cleans their rooms better). The customer service was horrible. The front desk person was like a robott or on something. Kept asking me how I was doing

title: “Positive Experience Good Value”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Hawthorne Suites in March of 2007. We found the staff friendly and helpful. Our first room was a bit small, but adequate. We upgraded to a suite and found it very spacious with all the amenities we could hope for at a very reasonable price. The breakfast buffet provided a wide range of options. There was scrambled eggs, bacon, potatoes, a variety of breads, juices, fresh fruit. In the afternoons there was complimentary beer, wine, soft drinks and snack foods, all of which could be enjoyed by a beautifully landscaped pool. We would definitely return to this property

title: “Great Service and very convenient”
text:
We stayed at this hotel after being offloaded from a flight home and the staff were great. checkin in was a bit slow but that was due to the large amount of people checking in. The staff were very helpful. Unfortunately when we used the hotel laundry , it marked all our white clothes. less than impressed but when we let the manager know about this, she was very apologetic and comped our lunch for us, asking if there was anything more she could do. the gym was fine and we didn't use the pool. 
As we were fronting up to the airport each night to try and get on a plane home, the hotel was very helpful in holding our room in case we didn't get on. this went on for three nights so we really appreciated it. 
Great hotel if you are at the airport and the shuttle was very convenient and quick

title: “Loved it”
text: Comfortable beds, extra things I've always thought would be helpful in a hotel - ear plugs, eye mask, clip on curtains for when they don't block out all the light, sleep CD - they had them all for you in the room. Hotel close to freeway but I never heard any freeway noise. Nice pool. Polite staff. The best stay we've ever had.

title: “good location and value”
text: We called around and chose this hotel because it was close to the university and had a reasonable price. The staff was helpful and so nice. Our room was spacious, big enough to accommodate four people. The beds were comfy as were the sheets. We enjoyed our stay.

title: “Great Stay”
text: We had an excellent stay. Everyone was friendly, the room was clean and comfortable, and the location was VERY convenient. The metro stop is in the lower level of the hotel and we used it to get all around DC. While we had a car and did use it on occassion, you could probably get anywhere you wanted on the metro.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
We loved the hotel. It was beautifully decorated, well maintained and ideally situated. The bathrooms are huge and contain a garden tub and a separate shower. The mattresses may be a bit firm and the pillows less than desirable as other reviewers have suggested; however, the positives greatly overcome these minor inconveniences. 
 If we are ever in Boston again, we definitely will stay here.

title: “Radisson Blu me away”
text:
This is a great property. One of the best hotels in Chicago, if not the U.S. Very few hotels make everything work and when they do it is typically an expensive experience. The Radisson Blu Aqua is able to provide an amazing experience at an outstanding value. 
The hotel is in a great location, within walking distance (or short cab ride) to many attractions. The hotel is absolutely stunning both inside and out. The lobby is gorgeous, and you can tell the rooms are new with beautiful decor, and excellent amenities. The view from our room, 1723, was amazing with the Navy Pier and lake views on one window, and Millennium Park on the other. 
I stayed in a business class room and have to admit this is was on of the best lounge experiences I have had. The lounge was never crowded with a decent selection of drinks and snacks. They even will loan you an ipad for your stay. 
All that being said, what makes this hotel amazing is the staff. From wishing my wife happy birthday at check-in (I had put a note when making the reservation) to consistent smiles and friendly attitudes the Radisson Blu has a superb staff. As an example, one evening we were in the lounge and attendant, Scott, asked us what brought us to Chicago. I mentioned we were going to a concert for my wife's birthday, casually mentioning the band we were going to see and the location. The next day we ran into Scott, and not only did he remember us but specifically made a point to ask us how we enjoyed the concert and the venue. Talk about service! 
I'd highly recommend this hotel to anyone. There is a reason all of the reviews on here are superb, this is a world class hotel.

title: “Location is good, but outdated and overpriced”
text:
I dont consider my expectations overly high but clean and comfortable is always expected. This lcoation is close tot he airport but is not in the safest location as we were distracted numerous times during our week by sounds of cops and heavy traffic.
Location is outdated showing its age, staff is attentive and very polite. Easy access to public transit.

title: “Nice overall, but beds had me begging for 4-star”
text:
Things we loved: The view, the security in that only keyed guests have access to parking garage and rooms building, the staff is friendly, the shuttle is an OUTSTANDING service, free parking, the breakfast is decent and convenient, the room is quiet, the bathroom was exceptionally clean, maid service is great and we never had to shuffle around carts (they worked when we weren't there), all in all a great value.
Things we hated: The beds. And while I loved EVERYTHING about the hotel otherwise, I can't sleep on crummy beds. There was a smell coming from the headboards perhaps b/c they were new, which gave me migraines every night, so, after 3 nights of this misery, we had to check out and go somewhere else in town for the rest of our 8-9 day trip. My husband also had a migraine, which he's never had before, and my kids acted a little berzerko at bedtime (which was highly unusual), so I think the fume eminating from the headboard and nightstand was toxic. Possibly formaldehyde which is found in particle board. So, if you have sensitivities, allergies, what have you, you might want to stay somewhere else. Sad to me b/c otherwise the place is really quite nice! 
*P.S. The migraine experience would start when we'd come back for naps in the afternoon, and then would not relent, so I missed dinner a couple of nights, and if we did go out I would feel good, but then come back for bedtime and feel awful again. So I KNOW it was those beds. Sniff.

title: “Definitely not Westin quality I have come to expect”
text:
I recently stayed at the Westin Market Street for a week with my mom. It is in a pretty good location to the downtown amenities and to the transportation system. Unfortunately that is really the only thing I really liked about the hotel. 
I found the staff to be very rude and not willing to help. The concierge didn't give proper directions (which in turn sent us on a bit of a wild goose chase to our destination), and did not really want to look up the answers to some other questions I had. The valet and greeting staff were gruff and brushed us off when we asked for a recommendation for a quick bite to eat in the area. They never said good morning or went out of their way to be friendly. From staying at other Westins I know this isn't usually the case. As well, the men at the baggage counter were rude to my mom when she asked a quick question about the Giants. Granted they may not be Giants fans but hey, at least be a little more polite to your customers. The staff in Ducca were no better. It took 15 minutes for us to be asked what we would like to drink on our first night at the lounge. Against our better judgement, we went back to the restaurant for breakfast a few mornings later. The service was terrible, we ended up pouring our own coffee refills because we weren't given a carafe like the other tables (not sure why when they also ordered the same things we did) and the server never came to check on us. The carafe finally came when we were ready to pay our bill.
The breakfast in Ducca was extremely disappointing. We chose the buffet and a lot of the food was cold, a day old or just not good (the eggs were powdered). As well, the appetizer plate we ordered at the bar was not complete (it only had about 3/4 of the items on it that were indicated on the menu). 
Internet cost $14.95 a day. We bought it one day, but the connection was horrible; we kept getting kicked off the system. We were also told that we could print our boarding passes for free in the business center. When we tried to however, the computer didn't recognize our airline so we had to pay to print them. When we mentioned it to the concierge, she nonchalantly told us she could have done it for us, but too bad we didn't ask.
Our room was ok, but not what I expect from the Westin. There were lots of hand prints on the window, an odd big blue spot on the ceiling (it looked like shower gel or something had exploded) and a blood spot on one of the bed skirts. It was tidy but not overly clean. You could tell the floor hadn't been vacuumed under the beds or in the corners in a while.
Unfortunately I wouldn't stay here again, especially for the price. I have come to expect a much higher quality from the Westin and will be thinking twice before I book with this hotel chain again.

title: “Great stay. Great location.”
text: Great stay. Everyone told me to “stay on the riverwalk” and they were right. I choose this hotel because: 1)accepted pets 2) location. We really enjoyed the location. It is on a quieter side of the riverwalk, which we enjoyed. It is an easy walk to the restaurants and shops on the riverwalk. You can also walk to the Riverwalk Mall, although it’s a little farther, we did with no problem. We walked to the Alamo from here also. We stayed here 4 nights and never used our car. We did take the trolley a couple of times with no problems. I consider this motel expensive. More than we usually spend, but worth it for the location. We were able to get a good discount thru the S.A.V.E. link on the website VISITSANANTONIO.COM. A big drawback is nothing is complimentary, so knowing this in advance we never used anything. We did not open the stocked refrigerator, knowing we would be charged. We never even got ice. Overall a good motel. I would stay there again.

title: “New Year's Eve”
text:
We have always stayed at the Hyatt in Mission Bay and wanted something different so we booked a night at the Manchester Grand Hyatt on New Year's Eve . The hotel was beautiful and our check-in was a breeze. Our room was on the 22nd floor over looking the bay and the USS Midway. We loved it! The view could not have been better. The room decor was a little out-dated. The bathroom had only one towel-- very disappointed. We had to call room service for more. It took our heater almost two hours before it started blowing hot air. We were cold. The room was clean; the carpet was a little run-down with stains here and there, but overall a beautiful hotel. We loved, loved the location. It was close to everything and would stay again.
Breakfast buffet at Lael's is a must. Delicious!

title: “outstanding”
text: We arrived early and the front desk staff was outstanding in getting us into our room as soon as possible. The staff as a whole was informative and very friendly.

title: “Noisy but nice”
text: Stayed here for a week in August. First impressions are of a funky, modern hotel - staff greeted us warmly and were very obliging. Rooms a little small for my liking but nicely presented. Unfortunately we were given one of the worst room locations on offer - on the sixth floor which is one floor below nightclub and positioned directly behind the lift so could hear swooshing sound all night long. I did comment this to staff about mid way through our stay and he kindly offered us another room but, by then, it was after Sunday and the next few nights the nightclub was closed. On the Sat night we had young girls screaming and giggling loudly till about 2.00am - I rang reception at about midnight to complain but I think guest floors should be restricted to guest use only as it seemed a little out of control (perhaps signs in lifts should be posted to remind nightclubbers that there are guests sleeping). Overall, the location to Gaslamp District was good - get up early to rooftop pool if you want to secure a sun lounge. It is a nice place to stay - perhaps would have rated higher if I hadn't had to deal with the noise issues (and hadn't been given the worst room in the house!)

title: “Great location, great room with view”
text: I liked it! Beautifully updated room with a nice view of the city. Very close to Times Square, I walked everywhere, MOMA, Central Park, restaurants, shopping... I would stay here again. One of the more reasonably priced hotels in the city. I would have given it a higher rating but the room was too warm no matter how much we fiddled with the thermostat and room service was slow (1 hour wait for breakfast).

title: “sublime”
text: excellent facilities, cosy and well maintained. very business like, functional. the space is managed very well and the gym was good too!

title: “Hotel's Policies Make This One to Avoid”
text:
I stayed at this hotel with my wife and two children and was very dissapointed by the hotel's unwillingness to satisify it's guests. Before checking out, I went to the lobby to get a luggage cart but had it yanked out of my hands and was told I couldn't have one. When I aksed why I was told the carts are only allowed to be handled by the bellmen. I explained to the hotel management that I wanted to take the cart to my room so I could pack my belongs myself and also because I was tired of tipping hotel employees everytime I turned around. I was told "Sorry, but that is our policy for your safety". Apparently Marriott management feels it is safer for me to carry 11 bags down by myself rather than use one of their carts! 
Otherwise, the room was quite small but the hotel location is excellent. The hotel staff (with exception of management) was kind and curteous. For the price, however, the sort of treatment we received from hotel management is unacceptable.

title: “Great value for money”
text:
I was really surprised with this hotel.
I had such low expectations given the really low price of the rooms. I found a large room with a confortable bed. The only complain I have with the room is that it had a background smell like cigarrettes. It was quite obvious for a non-smoker that in the room was once allowed to smoke. It was not a big issue for me, but be aware of that fact if you really cannot stand the smell of cigarrettes.
The breakfast was basic and it was held in a really large area next to the pool.
The pool area was really good. A large size swimming pool is sorrounded buy a few palm trees which provide good shadow.
I had no car when I stayed at the hotel. At walking distance I could find several restaurants. In general, the sourrounding area of the hotel was nice.
One thing I do not reccommend is dining in the Italian restaurant located in the hotel itself.

title: “Do NOT stay here! Be warned!”
text:
I booked this hotel a month in advance as my husband is here for travel for work and my two kids and I decided to tag along and make it a fun trip as well. After driving a good few hours from LA to the hotel, we were excited to check in as we are Hilton Honors members and often stay at the Hilton hotels when we travel. Well, never again! We unloaded our luggage and our two young kids and then at check in were informed by the front desk that they were sorry but there were NO rooms available! They did have confirmation that I had booked, but all they said was they were sorry but there was nothing they could do?!? I asked to speak to the front desk manager and was told the same thing and the reason she only gave me was that sometimes people refuse to leave when they are suppose to check out?! I was so upset as I had just received confirmation welcoming our arrival from Hilton San Diego Bay front a week ago. After I voiced my concerns over not being guaranteed a room when you book a month in advance and then having to pack up with my kids she offered ONE free night hotel stay at a neighbouring hotel and that was the best she could offer. I was told I could pay the rest of my nights at that hotel or check back in with them the next day. Why would I unpack all my belongings after one night and drive back to that hotel with two young kids? My husband is here for work and would need to leave early in the am. I cannot believe that such a large and respectable hotel chain would do that to a customer who booked and got an e-mail confirmation a week before the check in day. They also never attempted to e-mail or call me (they had my contact info) before the actual check in day to tell me that they had no room for me anymore. 
I am so shocked as we have travelled and stayed at many hotels both for business and pleasure and never once have heard of this happening. Upon check in at the suggested hotel (we had to leave to have a hotel to stay for the night) they did confirm that this has happened with Hilton San Diego bayfront before as well. Interesting....I think it is not an honest mistake but they oversell the number of rooms they have on purpose. It is a disappointing experience as prior to this happening we were even thinking of purchasing a Hilton vacations club in the future. I just hope you think twice before booking as you don't want to be surprised with no room upon check in. I usually never comment on trip advisor but have sought advice from travellers here myself and thought it was important enough to warn fellow travellers. Just be careful. There are plenty of new and better service hotels in San Diego that are worth checking out.

title: “Perfect location and awesome staff”
text: I sent an email to the concierge after booking and he made recommendations for restaurants and had a wonderful surprise of complimentary wine and snacks as well as a signed birthday card for my spouse on our arrival. This made our start to our SF holiday very special. We had a corner room withe two breathtaking views of the city (including the gates to Chinatown). Joe made sure a rental car was delivered to the hotel for the second part of our trip and we always felt very welcome by the staff. We signed up early for the Kimpton rewards and received our chosen newspaper each day, free wi-fi and a $10 "raid the bar" coupon. It was a great place to start and finish each day and it must be one of the most unique hotels in the city -- definitely not a cookie-cutter corporate hotel experience.

title: “A FABULOUS hotel in a FABULOUS location!!!!!!”
text: We enjoyed five nights at the Hampton Inn Times Square North. Our stay was perfect!!! From the moment we entered the hotel to check in to the moment we checked out, we were treated by ALL staff members with utmost kindness and consideration. Everyone does their job extremely well!! We dealt with two concierges. Both were very knowledgeable. They answered our questions and gave us some very good suggestions. The location of the hotel is GREAT!!!! It is within walking distance of Times Square, Rockefeller Center, Central Park, theaters, etc. The breakfast is excellent!! There are many delicious food and beverage choices. The rotating hot entry is a nice touch!! We are early risers, so we did not encounter crowds in the breakfast room. The guest rooms are large by New York standards. The room are furnished and decorated tastefully!! The beds are super comfortable!! The 24/7 coffee, tea, and hot chocolate is a nice touch....as is the large basket of apples in the lobby. The hotel has a convenient little gift shop with competitive prices!! All in all, we can't say enough about the hotel. We will definitely stay here again, and we will recommend it to our friends!!! Bravo to the entire staff at The Hampton Inn Times Square North, and THANK YOU!!!!!

title: “Close to SBC Park”
text: We were in San Fran for a Giants game. The hotel was relatively close to SBC Park. Rooms were VERY clean and quiet, but a bit small. Had 2 young children so the King bed and pull out couch worked nicely. Hotel staff was wonderful and even got us some milk for the baby's bottle at 10pm. Was told walking to Muni would be fastest to SBC Park. . . Was quite a walk to muni with the 2 little ones. Game was on Sunday when Muni runs less often so would take a cab right to the park next time and save an hour! Rate was found on Marriott.com which gaurantees to be less than other hotel websites. Paying $30 for valet parking was a big surprise. Overall, very good accomodations and would stay again.

title: “Excellent value and great quality”
text: This conveniently located hotel is perfect for mid-town visitors, who will enjoy the comfortably appointed and elegantly decorated rooms, as well as the pleasant bar area and the breakfast room. Staff are pleasant and friendly, including the general manager, whose experienced vision of customer service can be felt throughout the hotel. It was a real pleasure staying there and I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Very Nice, SUPERB Staff..... Pros and Cons Listed”
text:
I will make this black and white, I will post the pros and the cons
Pros: Unreal Staff from maid to manager greeted you with a smile, and could not have been more helpful
Pool water was nice, lovely little jacuzzi, indoor pool
lovely breakfast
nice size room
Rooms were cleaned early in the day, last time I was at an Embassy the room did not cleaned until about 4
Nice open lobby
Cons:
Pool was not maintained enough
-Large party was at hotel for reunion so the pool was full most of the weekend. Knowing they had this reunion there should have been extra staff buffing the pool, making sure towels were always there, the water should have been whisked away from the pool
- no out door chairs off the pool
Lobby was not well lite enough for my liking - I love light
No ear phones on the treadmill so you could watch TV, while you lip read
There were a few trays of room service left out side of peoples rooms that were there for HOURS this is GROSS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Great hotel for a Washington Getaway”
text: We had a wonderful trip to the Hotel Palomar this past weekend. The staff were all extremely pleasant and helpful. The lobby is welcoming, and the afternoon we arrived they were setting up for "kids hour" from 3:30 - 4:30, which included a Wii and popcorn. Our room was far larger than a city hotel room usually is, with a large bathroom with enormous jetted tub. We were upgraded to a "Motion Room" as members of the Kimpton Club (worth joining for the free internet), which included a recumbent bike and television right in the room (but away from the sleeping area). Hotel Palomar is an easy walk from the Red Line and from Dupont Circle, with its many restaurants, cafes and shops. The first night we were there, we ate in the attached Urbana Restaurant and Wine Bar, which was delicious. We will definitely return to the Hotel Palomar.

title: “Great Stay”
text: This hotel was in a great locationl. It is right across the street from Penn Station/Madison Square Garden. It is 1 block from a MTA subway station. The hotel is 3 blocks from Macy's and one Ave. from the Empire State Building. The rooms were very clean. They include a small kitchen. My husband said that the pillows were the most comfortable pillows that he has ever slept on. The staff was very helpful and friendly. We were delayed 7 hours arriving in New York and missed one night at the hotel. They did not charge us for the night that we missed because of our train delay. I highly recommend staying at Affinia Manhattan.

title: “Very good hotel”
text: its a five star hotel in the heart of Manhattan.Everything is walking distance from there.its strange that the reception is on the 8 floor ,but its no problem.the breakfast is ok but there are many deli's around.the revolving restaurant on 44 floor is nice for a panoramic but no gourmet dinner.

title: “One of the best hotels not from the big brands surprisingly but makes it as comfortable as all big star hotels”
text:
After reaching in Seattle - we had a nice cab guy who got us to the hotel. We were awe-struck with the ambience of the hotel rooms and the way they have been maintained. The rooms were so clean - I never wanted to spoil them. The staff were so helpful and polite - that you can forget the bumpy landing of Alaskan Airlines. There are some hotels which can't be defined by words alone - you need to stay there to believe it - here's one the Silver Cloud Hotel, Broadway.
Please take full advantage by taking the courtesy shuttle to West lake center - you can't resist yourself in draining out your pockets in that location.

title: “Classic yet Modern and in the heart of downtown. A great vintage!”
text:
The Vintage Park is an older hotel in downtown Seattle. It has been upgraded to modern standards and is a beautiful place to spend time. A modestly sized gathering area just off the lobby offers free wine and cheese every evening, in keeping with the "wine" theme of property. Each floor and room has a wine theme that carries through to the decorating. 
High rise nature of hotel kept street noise out. Roomy and comfortable standard king.
Highly Recommended!

title: “GREAT HOTEL!”
text: This was my first stay at this hotel. so glad i did.i went for a thanksgiving holiday. walking distance to radio city music hall and fifth ave for shopping.this hotel was a excellent choice. the room was very clean and the beds were very comfortable. they had all the extras. kouric coffee maker and all toiletries. blow dryer with a nitelite attached beautify soft towels.front desk and housekeeping were so helpful. peter at the front desk checked me in quickly. the stay here made my trip .beautifull large flat screen tv. i will stay again. beds were very comfortable. you won't be disappointed.

title: “great place to stay in NY city!”
text: We spent 4 nights at Chelasea Pines Inn. It was the perfect location: close to the underground station, close to the exciting meat packing dristict and to the delicious bleeker street. The staff was very nice and helpfull: they gave us good tips to go around the city and to eat well, plus they provided us with good tickets for Broadway. The breakfast which was included in the rate, was very rich and good. The free business center was very usefull. We definitly raccomend it!

title: “Nice hotel, great staff, GREAT ROOM, not so great location”
text:
Loved it here. Great room with full kitchen! A real rarity in NYC...staff was fabulous, breakfast and happy hour were great!! Location is crap - but I am a New Yorker so did not mind being near Port Authority...I can handle panhandlers and porn DVD shops..but may not want my kids or naive tourists to have to deal with it. Parking is really difficult around here. Recommend ICON Parking via www.bestparking.com
I still recommend it and would stay here again.

title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text: I booked this hotel as a one-night stay over for an early flight. I must say, this is THE nicest La Quinta Inn I have ever stayed in. I was only there for one night and left at 4am the next morning but it was a great location at the airport with free 24 hour shuttle service to the airport. The lobby area was very clean and nicely appointed. It had free breakfast starting at 4 am with the basic breakfast items including eggs. The room was quite large and the bathroom was large, clean and neat. Everything was attractive about this hotel. The staff was polite and professional. The price was right for our stay. There are several restaurants within walking distance if you don't have a car. Two thumbs up!

title: “Great for long periods, strange otherwise”
text: Staying here was very strange as a solo traveller because it is more like a house than a hostel. People are living there for 2-3 months at a time for internships and the like. The floors haven't been vacuumed in a long time. There was one shower between about 15 girls which meant you had to plan when you needed to shower and keep checking if it was free. I am a female travelling alone and I didn't feel particularly safe in the neighbourhood after dark. The train station is about 4 blocks away but not too long a walk. Not a party atmosphere at all as the lounge is like your tv room at home. I recommend it for long periods and if you're into the homely thing. Don't go expecting to get advice on where and how to see DC they don't have maps of any kind.

title: “Horrible, rude and cramped”
text: The Straford Hotel was miserable. Once you put your suitcases down, there is no room to walk. Our shower door didn't close and our window didn't close either. There was no screen and our view was of a brick wall. The bed felt flimsy and the sheets were scratchy. Don't count on getting much sleep, it was loud in the hotel regardless of our window being open. If you are still in college and ready to party all night, this might be the place for you. The location was good but I would pay more money next time to keep some sanity while on a vacation.

title: “Not perfect but very charming”
text:
Family of 4 (two adults and 9 and 12 years old kids) stayed for three nights over Thanksgiving break. We arrived very early (before 11 a.m.) and were given very big room 976 on the corner of Lexington Ave. Check in took less than five minutes, no wait. Hotel shows its age in some parts (closet doors, scuffs in wallpaper, not very strong heat) but very clean throughout. The bathroom was very big and beautiful; all marble. Lobby and elevators have a luxurious feeling. Personnel was polite but not over the top; door men very effective in getting you a cab. But the room service was not without its flaws. We forgot the "don't disturb" sign all day once and even though we requested service in the room at 6:30 p.m. nobody had come once we returned to the room at 10 p.m. 
But the location cannot be improved. And the hotel has retained its charm throughout the decades. It is not the Four Seasons, but its rates are very reasonable for its location and charm. We would stay here again!

title: “Needs a remod bad.”
text: Stayed 3 nights week of sept 19. Only went with this hotel b/c of price, $345/night. Cheapest we could find during the UN general assembly week all hotels were blacked out. Lobby and check in were easy. I reserved a queen bed rm non smoking. They gave me a smoking room with double beds. Double beds were not a problem but the smoking room was DISGUSTING. Could not stand it in the rm so went downstairs and waited 2 hrs for a nonsmoking rm. Not the way I like to start my stay. pros-close to times square, grand central station but i'msure there are plenty of hotels in ny which are. Cons-rooms seek desperate need of remodel. I would not sit in chair in rm was dirtyandnasty shower has caulk and grout lines which are oldand crusty this hotel has a bunch of facts about how it's one of the oldest hotels in ny and it sure looks the part. As you can see from my review I won't be staying here again any time soon.

title: “Love this hotel”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights in May whilst holidaying in NY. It was absolutely perfect in every way - the best shower I've ever had, the bed felt like a big fluffy cloud and I loved just sitting in the window seat watching the world go by (with a coffee feom Balthazar across the road). The staff were incredibly helpful and friendly. The bar is funky and the sitting room is so beautiful. I don't think I've ever had a better hotel experience. It's not cheap - but perfect for a special occasion splurge.

title: “Nice out of the way hotel near the airport”
text: We had two room for five days. The rooms were very nice with easy accessability for me with a handicap. The biggest problem was people without handicaps parking in handicap parking leaving me having to find some other place farther away to park. The rooms were clean and the beds comfortable. The rooms we had would have easily slept 5. We had rooms 116, and 117. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking to be near Sea World, the beaches or even the airport to use this hotel. There was no inside pool which would have been great for my 5 year old nephew because it was too cold to swim outside.

title: “Great Location, Nice Rooms , eat breakfast elsewhere”
text:
We were there for Thanksgiving. The location is great and the rooms are big and cozy, staff friendly . The breakfast is terrible , go elsewhere (there's a great coffee shop nearby ) for breakfast. 
We really enjoyed Philadelphia and the location of the hotel is so central that you can walk everywhere.

title: “Nice rooms but overall disappointing”
text:
I have stayed in several 4* in LA (beverly hills area) such as SLS, Mondrian, London. Being a member of Luxury Hotels of the World I gave Mr C a chance on this trip for half of my week. I thought top quality would be there but there were quite some flaws.
- Rooms: I stayed in a premium room (corner top floor - hills view). Room is very tastefully decorated and you get lots of light. Wifi is complimentary and works fine. Size is 350sqft. Bathroom is tiny (just a shower) and water pressure was quite bad (9th floor).
- Housekeeping: They really did clean the room very well and would even fold all clothes and put them in the closet. They did forget a snack I had on the balcony for a full day (guess they did'nt bother looking outside) but the most shocking was to find that my door hadn't been properly closed while I was out on the second day. Nothing was stolen thankfully but that is rather disappointing. You have turnaround service.
- Breakfast: There is no buffet. Just a continental breakfast which is quite a disappointment (3 pastries and some fruits). Some other a la carte items. Not impressive.
- Pool area: Very unimpressive. It is on the ground floor so no views. No effort has been put in decorating the place. They just put 3-4 cabanas and some chairs. Pool is very small. First day I wanted to try it it was close for a private event and no form of compensation was given (for instance in London hotel they would provide you with some free cocktails at their bar - at least there is a gesture). Second day I tried again, initially there was no music, no one to provide towels, no bartender! Had to get inside to get a barman, a towel, etc... never saw that. 
- Pool menu: quite a few options but overall not very good value for money.
- Valet Parking: you get your car rapidly which is a good thing. They made some mistakes though (first day I managed to be charged more than the maximum daily rate).
- Location: somehow you are in the middle of nowhere. You are not too far from rodeo but around the hotel there is nothing really. I prefer to be on sunset or on rodeo. They have a hotel car as well which can drop you (3 miles radius).
Bottom line, the hotel fell short of my expectations. For the price you can probably get a larger room than a rodeo hotel, however I'd rather stay at London Hotel or SLS.

title: “Location can't be beat”
text: Had a 6am flight. This was defiinitely the best choice to simply walk to the terminal. Rooms are very comfortable and clean. The property is just kind of sterile. But it's an airport hotel that sells its proximity. If you want the Four Seasons or a resort, then not sure why you'd even be looking here.

title: “Great experience with our group!”
text: We booked 30 rooms and had a great experience. The staff was well organized, friendly and helpful. The hotel was recently updated and looked great. I really liked the room design and comfortable bed. Would definitely stay here again!

title: “Fantastic Hotel!”
text: Me and my 6 friends stayed at the Waldorf Astoria for 4 nights in March 2012. We were there for my friends 40th birthday. Before we went, I emailed the hotel to ask if we could have an upgrade as we were sharing 3 and 4 to a room. When we arrived at the hotel we were delighted to find we'd been allocated a suite each with 2 bathrooms. We were also given a voucher each for a cocktail to have in the bar. The hotel itself is very grand with a stunning lobby. The staff at the Waldorf were very helpful and professional in all areas, from bar staff to concierge and reception staff. The rooms were very clean and spacious. The hotel is located 5 mins walk away from the Rockerfeller Centre, 10 mins walk to Grand Central Station, 15 mins walk to the fabulous Times Square and 15 mins walk to Bloomingdales. A fantastic location! Our rooms were booked on a room only basis which wasn't a problem as there were many places to eat breakfast near the hotel. If you're stuck for places to go in the evening, ask concierge as they have a great deal of knowledge of places to go. We all enjoyed our stay and will definitely staying again!

title: “Perfect Vacation”
text: Just got back from 8 nights in San Diego. The last 4 nights were at The Paradise Point Resort. We had a wonderful time. The room we had was very nice and clean. The service at this hotel was impeccable. Whenever we needed something(family travelling with 2 children) they treated us like we were the only guests and met our needs promptly. The restaurants were very good. Pools were great. The location was perfect for getting to area attractions. Overall this was by far one of our nicest trips. March 6 - 10, 2004.

title: “Excellent Hotel!”
text: We were thrilled with our stay in Indy. The hotel was clean, the staff was very accommodating and friendly, and the breakfast was incredible! We only regret that we didn't have more time to stay so that we could enjoy the pool and fitness room. The only negative was that the rooms face I-465, but they offer earplugs if the noise is too much! Overall, it was a wonderful experience, and we would stay there again. (And having a Culver's next door was an added benefit!!!)

title: “Classy. Living museum”
text:
The Waldorf Astoria. It's a legendary place, and I was most impressed with the building.
The maintenance of the older property will always be difficult, and it was understandable that there will be a few issues, but there does need to be a heavy clean for the room I was in.
I didn't expect to see dust on the crevices of the door, nor mug rings on the surface at the TV at the WA.

title: “A great stay - good location - wonderful staff”
text:
We chose the Affinia based on reviews here - and as is usually the case we were not disappointed. The hotel is very clean and quiet and the room and kitchen well- equipped. Top quality toiletries in the bathroom. The cleaner was very friendly and helpful and got a slight fault fixed within minutes. The bed was one of the best we have ever slept on. The reception and porters were very helpful and well-informed.
It is situated on E34th Street with easy access to the Metro system although we walked a lot - bring good shoes if you do.
The "Dog" restaurant was ok but no great shakes on quality or variety of breakfast - there are quite a number of markets and restaurants nearby.
