We had another outstanding meal at the Tavern on the Green restaurant - an absolute must if you have something special to celebrate - but make sure you book in advance online.
The Museum of Natural History was a disappointment compared to other similar establishments.
The deli in the basement of the Turner building on Columbus circle is an absolute must - so much choice of hot / cold foods at reasonable prices - so much indeed we had trouble choosing between them. 
Macys recent update is not a move in the right direction - its old world character has gone and now is just another department store - very sterile.

title: “The Embassy Suites is a great place to stay”
text: The Embassy Suites is a great place to stay. The suites are spacious and very comfortable, with all the amenities I can think of. The complimentary breakfast is top-notch, not an ordinary continental breakfast, you can have made-to-your-liking omlettes, among many other choices. The complimentary happy hour(s) provides hors-d-ouvres as well as cocktails. They provide free computer kiosks to access the internet. It is in a very convenient and desirable location. The only thing negative I have to say is it doesn't have the best water pressure, but it's not too bad and I can live with it. I highly recommend the Embassy Suites to everyone.

title: “Good value 4 star property in downtown Seattle”
text:
I was originally going to book at the Hyatt Olive 8 hotel but found a 4 star mystery property on hotwire for $88/night. I booked right away and was happy to discover the Alexis Hotel. It's a newly renovated 4 story hotel located in downtown Seattle. It's close to Pike Place and the shopping core. The rooms are very trendy with plush pillows and mattress. The room we had was shower only and had a queen bed (if this is a problem for you, confirm before you check in). 
I didn't use the steamroom but I believe that is complimentary. Also free wifi and a managers cocktail hour between 5 and 6 with wine and hot toddys in the library bar. 
I believe it's dog friendly but couldn't hear or see any evidence of dogs in the halls or my room. Overall, this hotel feels posh and is nicely decorated. 
My room was facing 1st and I could hear the traffic slightly when I woke up in the morning. 
This hotel does have valet parking but I parked on the street and saved money. Seattle has free street parking after 6pm on Saturday and free on Sunday.

title: “Worst Hilton I have stayed in”
text: Stayed here for 3 days room was small and stunk of mould and mildew and this was the executive floor. For almost 400 dollars per night I felt completely ripped off. Cleaners were the friendliest people in the hotel and the bar tender in the lobby bar was a complete misery. A bottle of beer in the bar was 11.77 with the tip that they automatically added. Will never stay here again

title: “Shabby Chic?”
text: I spent four days on business in this traditional hotel. I got more or less what I expected. The service was good, the location in the financial district is superb not only for business but also for sightseeing. What I find increasingly embarassing, however, is that you are charged for everything without any measure of price/performance ratio. Nine dollars for a bottle of water in the room, twelve dollars for "high-speed" 24 hrs internet access (plus taxes, of course). What they call "high-speed" are ridiculous 60-70 KB/sec on average. Perhaps, this should help making the use of Skype less efficient and motivating desperate people to use the phone service. And one must really be desperate and having lost your smartphone doing so. The first minute to UK costs you alredy $ 18.70, a chat of 5 min is a steal for "only" $ 33.40. I would enjoy my stay much more if the room rate would be $ 30 higher, but water and internet would not be charged extra. This would be cost neutral but a much nicer feeling. Last not least I took a picture of my window, which looks onto the Franklin Street. It's "shabby chic" par excellence, quite trendy in the nineties, if I remember correctly.

title: “Good location and large rooms”
text: Ok, this place is not a boutique hotel.. But it doesn't set out to be either. It's clean. It's tidy. It's got great beds and nice showers. A fairly good Wifi service and ok TV's. Compared to a lot of other hotels in Manhattan, the rooms are fairly large. We had a great 4 nights stay. The breakfast was good (served in the grill next doors.)

title: “Nice Stay”
text: My wife and I stayed for 2 nights in August - dropping daughter off at school. Nice size room, but the bathroom was tiny. The concierge team was very helpful and the price was great (less two hundred $). Location was good - near the Commons and the "T" (subway), and Starbucks in the lobby ;) Would stay again.

title: “What a hidden gem”
text:
Chelsea Pines Inn is a great quirky little hotel in the middle of a Chelsea street. The inside lobby is clean and modern. The rooms are an adequate size (I might have had to squeeze to get around the foot of the bed but it was never really any problem) but the beds are big and comfortable. The best part are the people running the place: Jay and Al were immensely helpful and pleasant and really made us feel at home. Everyone else from those running the front desk to those keeping the break area stocked (and it was always stocked with fresh items and little snacks) was absolutely courteous, professional, and happy to just chat about how things were going. Although the rooms are up some flights of stairs, the people working there moved our luggage for us. The noise from the street was never a problem, and I never heard anyone in any of the other rooms through the walls. The location was perfect for seeing local sights, and I have to agree with others here who say that the High Line is a must-see.
I would feel comfortable recommending this to anyone I knew, and I know they would come back raving about what a great place this was.

title: “Kyoto Grand Recent Visit”
text:
The staff is superb. Management's decision to discontinue the excellet breakfast included with the night stay is a poor decisio! I have stayed at the Grand Kyoto no less than 10 times over the last 2 years. Unfortunately, this was my last visit to the Grand Kyoto.
When and if the DoubleTree takes over the hotel, I hope the great breakfast buffet previously served and included with a night stay at the Kyoto Grand is not replaced with the cheap "continental breakfast" consisting of some cold cereal and cardboard like waffle.

title: “Good Hotel but Hallways Stink”
text:
The arrival experience was great and the parking guys did an awesome job (even during night and day). We were coming there to spend the weekend with the kids and go to Seaworld.
The Hotel looks nice, has a business feel to it. Room service was good - the server again was very nice. 
It is apparent that these guys spend a lot of time on training on customer service as you can feel it all around the Hotel.
My only issue was the smell in the hallway. We were in Room 1163, the hallway smelled like someone crapped on it. It may the old carpet and someone steaming it, but other than this minor item the stay was very pleasant and enjoyable.

title: “Milenium Hotel Broadway”
text: Top location, friendly staff, quick and easy check in/out. room clean comfortable but wish they had tea and coffee facilities in room but Starbucks next door and couple of Delis across road from 45th street entrance.

title: “This hotel was perfect for our stay”
text:
We stayed at The Chancellor for 3 nights in April. We had a fanastic stay. We had twin beds. The rooms, staff and location were all excellent. We stayed on the 11th floor, the street noise wasn't bad at all, It added charm to our stay - I loved hearing the Cable Cars go by. The strength of the free wifi was always excellent. Occasionally heard the footsteps from the room above but only ever for a few seconds. Showers were really good and the wardrobe was very spacious but we never used it. We had both our suitcases out in the room and there were will plenty of space left. The beds were awesome, great nights sleep after long days sightseeing around the city. We had originally planned to return to the airport using the BART but our bags were quite heavy and there was no problem booking the Shuttle bus with Lorries with short notice. The tea and cookies in the lobby were a great way to start the morning.
We will definately be returning in the future.

title: “Nice touch”
text: My wife and I were going to stay in nearby DC overnight to check out the sites at night and be downtown in the morning for a White House tour. I had booked the hotel on-line based on the recommendation of a friend, so I was unable to add any comments about it being our 25th wedding anniversary. I called the hotel during the day in an effort to let them know, but was just passed on to an automated confirmation desk. When we checked in I mentioned it to the front desk clerk CJ but didn't really think any more about it. We were quite surprised to return from an evening out to find a chiiled bottle of champagne and a plate of chocolate covered strawberries in the mini fridge and a nice card signed by the staff. Thanks. Well done.....

title: “Adequate”
text:
Hotel OK. Lobby is shabby and bullet proof glass over counter made me nervous!!! But room was not too bad - pretty clean although very dated/tired eg carpet threadbare etc. Bed was comfortable enough and not too much noise even though room right on roadside. Aircon worked well albeit noisy, but fridge was bit temperamental. Icemaker available. Location wasnt too terrible - in fact excellent location for Paramount Studios (two blocks - easy walk!!) for me to see Dr. Phil show!!! Can walk to Hollywood boulevard but good half hour esp when tired at night. But lots of taxis available. Seemed safe enough when walking around though. No iron/ironing board in room and one for use from lobby small and awkward to use. Breakfast was very minimal - english muffins and iced donuts!!! But coffee was good so thats what matters right?! In room coffee maker also. No computer for guest use although wireless internet available if you have lap top.
Pretty average overall but cheapish and close to Dr. Phil! And we were only there to sleep after all- too much to do and not enough time!!!

title: “Great value in a terrific position in central Chicago”
text: We recently stayed for a week in this Chicago hotel which surpassed our expectations and is fantastic value for a central position close to all the superb attractions of this wonderful city. We were given a terrific suite with a large lounge and kitchenette with TV. Very good bedroom with a wonderful view over the cityscape - which we never tired of looking at - also with TV. NIce bathroom and separate area with wardrobes/washbasin. We were very happy there. The breakfast was extremely generous and well-cooked. For 4 evenings there was supper included (with wine) which was very welcome. There are constant free hot drinks available and a small shop which comes in very useful - all this helps to keep the cost of the holiday down. Every member of staff was unfailingly charming and helpful. So, we have very fond memories of this hotel and would like to thank everyone there for helping to make our holiday so enjoyable.

title: “Really superior hotel, very well managed,”
text: I attended a two-day business conference at this hotel and stayed over for two nights. The hotel just did everything right. the rooms were lovely, Marriott-comfortable bed you just don't want to get out of, clean bathrooms, nice flat screen TV, lots of power outlets. the facilities at the hotel were all top notch. The conference room was good, there were lots of other meetings going on and we did not hear their meeting through our walls. The food service was outstanding. Much, much better than typical. We had two lunches there and a cocktail hour with heavy horsd'oeuvres. The cocktail food was fantastic! And I am a foodie. You just do not expect this type of food at a business hotel. I did not have the opportunity to try their restaurant, The Yard, but if the meeting fare was any indication, this should be a very good restaurant. If you are going to an Orioles game, this hotel has a great location, literally the gates are right across the street. Good, but pricy parking in a connected parking deck.

title: “Suited our needs”
text:
Apologies for the late post, we stayed at the Affinia Manhattan for 4 nights in mid-May 2006.
We chose to stay at the Affinia Manhattan because of it's location. It's right across the road from Penn Station, and as we were flying into and out off Newark, using the NY Transit from the airport gave us a quick, easy and cheap option for arriving in NY.
That said, nightlife wise, there's not too much in the close vacinity, so if you want to be in the hussle and bussle of bars and restaurants, this place may not be for you. Having said that, there's a great little bagel shop that does good breakfasts across the road (as you walk out of the hotel, it's across 7th, to the left, on the corner of the block), and a block down from that a bar called Mustang Harry's which does great bar food if you want something quick and handy (we had the burger and a half chicken, which were great, and we had the Chicken Satay starter which was even better).
To give you an idea, the hotel is within 10 / 15 mins stroll to Empire State and Times Square respectively, and 3 blocks from Macys.
As for the hotel itself, it's not the best hotel we've ever stayed in, but for the price, location (for our needs), and for the fact that this is NY and square footage is not usually a luxury, the Affinia Manhattan was great. The room was spacious and clean, the bed was large (hey, it's America) and having a fridge and the kitchen has to be considered a massive bonus. We stayed in a room on the 5th floor and never waited an unreasonable time for the lifts. The staff we met were all very helpful and polite, so no complaints there.
On the downside, the bathroom is small and slightly dated and the decor in the public areas (excluding the lobby) was dated. 
We'd absolutely recommend the Affinia Manhattan - with those few caveats mentioned above. But if you're happy with them, then go for it.

title: “Perfect stay at the Renaissance”
text:
I loved my recent stay at the Renaissance. It seemed like the majority of the guests were there for conferences (many held at the hotel), but I really enjoyed it for my vacation base. The location is great with easy walking distance to the waterfront, Pike Place, great shopping and restaurants. The rooms were a little small but very nice, with large flat screen tvs, extremely comfortable beds, and furnishings that seemed new. Service at the hotel was outstanding and is what I think really sets this hotel at a higher level than some of the other chains at similar to slightly lower prices. The breakfast buffet was really good, and we enjoyed both hotel bars (one on the first floor and one on the top floor). Drinks were a bit expensive but tasty, and the views from the top floor were nice. My room was on the freeway side but the noise didn't bother me at all. It was just like a steady buzz.
I booked this with a good deal that included free breakfast for two (buffet) each day plus a 25$ Visa gift card for each night I stayed. I think that with these perks the value was excellent.

title: “Under construction”
text:
Lots of nice things about the hotel - great location, beautiful views from top floors and just a few blocks from BART. Unfortunately, the lobby is currently under construction. It's quite a mess right now. 
I would stay here again for the right price, though there are so many great hotels in San Francisco that I tend to move around.

title: “Excellent hotel, but . . .”
text:
Stayed for three nights over Thnksgvg Day holiday. Wonderful old-style NYC hotel, top quality amenities (bed, soaps, etc etc etc) BUT . . . charging $15 per day for wi-fi access in a room costing almost $1,000 a night all in is too cheap for words. I think you simply have to adjust your expectations in NYC hotels. We thought we had and although we were taken aback at first with the tiny room (and especially tiny bathroom), we were won over by the top quality furnishings and the relative silence of the upper east side. The staff are almost TOO friendly (where do you see elevator attendants anymore, although I suspect they are required not so much as a luxury but more to keep the travelling riff-raff from running around on floors reserved for permanent residents). The view to the south from our 31st floor was almost worth the room price in itself, but as luxury hotels go, we have had more value for money at the Waldorf and the Standard, and the Peninsula in Chicago. 
Unfortunately, elevators are also very tiny (old-style) and apparently don't have room for the usual luggage trolleys, so the bell staff sort of work in teams to move your luggage by hand - kind of weird and inefficient, but unfailingly polite and gracious. Also, the old walls are very thin, so that you can easily hear a normal conversation the the adjacent room (and when you share your floor with the sort of inconsiderate boors who ought not to be staying there in the first place and can't grasp the concept of considerate quiet at 0700 on a holiday morning, then you REALLY realize how thin the walls are, but you can't blame all that on the hotel.)
We might return for the location and the wonderful old-style class and charm, but we might also check out The Mark in the same location. Even though I didn't even use it - I had my own handheld - I was very irritated by the effrontery of charging extra for wireless in such an expensive hotel room but maybe The Mark is the same . . . ?

title: “Great choice”
text: Found a discount rate on their web site for a king room on a higher floor, breakfast included. Was much, much cheaper than other hotels in the area. Requested room facing inward, not much to see but very quiet for NY. With the air cleaner in the room turned to low, was very quiet and comfortable, and no bedbugs! Breakfast was OK, not many choices and almost impossible to get a glass of water from the waitstaff (had to ask 4 times), but was included in price for room. If bought separately may be too expensive. Subway stop very close to hotel. Gave me later checkout than usual to wait for status of my flight out of LGA during the storm, desk staff were very accommodating.

title: “Great”
text: Great! The only negative (and its not really a negative) was the elevator was mid-way thru the building, not in the lobby. Price wise, best deal for the $$$, period. Pool and spa were clean and neet. Resturant had good food and friendly environment. We will definately return!

title: “LOVE the Revere Hotel!”
text:
We spent five nights at the Revere in mid-September and could not have been happier with our hotel choice. Modern design in lobby is beautiful; friendly staff was ALWAYS ready and willing to help with anything.
Our room was quite spacious – again with nice modern decor. Loved having a balcony! Good bed, pillows, linens and bathrobes. And the shampoos, conditioners, creams were out of this world – SKOAH!
The location was terrific – two blocks to Boston Common and the T. On the edge of Chinatown, so we took advantage of the Thai and Vietnamese restaurants.
There is a beautiful rooftop outdoor area with plenty of lounge chairs, umbrella tables, etc. that is just outside the pool/spa/workout area. 
Would definitely recommend this hotel and hope to stay there again in the future!

title: “Perfect property!”
text: Great location, very nice rooms, the staff could not be nicer.

title: “Upper East Side Gem but with 3 slight flaws”
text:
This hotel, which we booked through SniqueAway, is a gem with fantastic and friendly service, a quiet location just off Central Park near the boutiques and restaurants of the Upper East Side, a great spa and excellent rooms (we booked a Grand Salon at a very reasonable price). Michael, the concierge, is superb: he was able to find two center orchestra tickets to Memphis 24 hours in advance at face value, ie no markup to a broker. He also handed us two free entries to the Whitney Museum which is just a block away. Cafe Boulud, the hotel restaurant, is reputed in NY, but (flaw 1) kept us waiting a half hour for our hotel-booked table and 2) seemed to forget about our main course for about an hour. However, they made up for this by offering us several complimentary glasses of wine.
The 2nd flaw, which is the only one that really bothers me and might lead me not to return, is that the hotel seems to have entered into a pact with the devil in terms of their internet service provider. From what I can tell, the hotel blocks all data services to force you to use their $14.95/day internet service, which apparently need to be purchased for each data device. Given that most of us walk around now with 2-3 devices that need connectivity, this is a real pain. What's worse is that they don't tell you. So I spent an hour of my anniversary weekend on the line with Amazon Kindle tech support trying to find out why there was no connection. Similarly, we were unable to do a quick "Around Me" check on our iPhones. There truly is no excuse for this and the hotel needs to change it immediately.
The 3rd flaw, which only pertains to those of us with back issues, is that the beds are too soft. Of course, some like it that way but these were about the softest I've experienced. 
For these reasons, I'm afraid that we're unlikely to go back but that should not deter you. This is an incredible hotel!

title: “Super”
text: Best location, huge bed, Nice bathroom, very nice staff ! From here new York can be visites very easily. I would go there definitely again.

title: “Hot location, hot room”
text: Travelling with my teenage daughter our arrival was impressive, glass of champagne iced cucumber water and friendly staff. Lobby and ambiance was classy. Location was ideal for our aims of touring the city. Room itself which was on the 10th floor was just getting to the faded stage and granted it was the hottest weekend on record but the A/C unit did not really perform (much cooler in the corridors, lobby) and was noisy into the bargain.

title: “Awful!”
text: This place is a dump, in the heart of a red light district. Filthy, smoky, disgusting, I was afraid I was going to get bedbugs or my dog was going to get fleas. Other guests looked to be mainly prostitutes and their clients. Avoid at all costs.

title: “Quiet but close location.”
text: I was initially surprised at how expensive this hotel was. But compared to the expense of staying closer to downtown this is a great value. Hotels downtown are twice as expensive and don't offer much more. Fifteen minute walk to 6th street or 2 minutes to Lady Bird Lake. Staff was very accommodating and friendly. Rooms are a bit small but why are you spending that much time in it anyway with so much to do in Austin. Breakfast was subpar and over priced but that's the only complaint I had. Seemed like a safe area. We walked just about everywhere at all hours and never felt unsafe. Seems like this city never sleeps. I would stay here again without hesitation.

title: “Nice hotel but”
text:
A nice hotel very convenient to the sights and in a great neighborhood with a lot of interesting restaurants just a block or two away. 
Had a comfortable room with a handy fridge and big flat screen TV. A not so nice view of the building next door from our room but the view from the rooftop patio was superb. You would think a rooftop patio would be easy to find but there is no signage directing you to the correct stairwell.
You might want to call the hotel directly to find the best rate. They beat any rate I found on the web and even better then their own website.
Only problem I had was with one of the front desk guys. At check in when I told him we were checking in and gave him my last name his response was, "credit card and picture ID". That's it. Not a welcome to our Inn, not a thank you Mr ____ for chosing us, just a quick "credit card and picture ID". Do these people know how many choices we have in hotels? Front desk personal need a refesher in customer service.
In spite of that guy i would still stay again.

title: “Fabulous Location & good service”
text: The Hilton times square is a great location, it's located right next next to the New Amersterdam Theater. The location worked out wonderful and we were able to walk to 5th avenue, central park and many other touristy destinations. The staff was very helpful, they gave us the exact trains we needed to take to get to the Yankee's game. The hotel bar was charming, a bit pricey but something I would picture in NYC. Our room was spacious for NY standards and the room was very clean. I would definately stay here again!

title: “Great location, well appointed hotel”
text:
Having stayed on previous trips in the Times Square area, this was a very pleasant improvement. The location was ideal for walking anywhere - right in the heart of the action but a quiet corner. We were in comfortable walking distance from the Met, Rockefeller, even walked home after a show on Broadway in no time at all.
The staff of the hotel were very good, without exception - helpful and friendly. Join the loyalty club (free) to get free wifi and even better, complimentary beverages each morning to your room. Proper coffee in the morning is a must.
Will definitely return to this hotel - great price for a well location, clean and well appointed hotel.

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text:
Another great stay at the Dallas Park Central. I have been a frequent guest at that property since 1982.
Fantastic customer service from the front desk staff, especially Younis. He always makes me feel welcome.
Service express manager Michael delivers "great service" regarding room service anything to make my stay great.
Finally, Glen the front desk manager is fantastic. Makes sure that everything is going great with my room or services.
A great place to stay, centrally located for all areas of Dallas.

title: “Great location/ excellent service”
text:
Had previously stayed at the Carlton during it's transitional period from Welfare hotel to it's current revamp. At that time, some floors were renovated and others still had their long time occupants. There are still vestiges of the former hotel, but one has to look hard to find them.
The overall first impression is that the overhaulers did a fabulous job. The lobby is sexy. The check in was smooth and professional. The room was smallish, but really, how much time would one spend in the hotel when NYC is right out the door?
The complaints are small - there was no counter space in the bathroom, so no room to lay out toiletries. There was no bath gel included in the complimentary bath items. The maid threw out our Sunday NY Times, but the hotel managed to provide another copy.
We got a good deal on the summer special (<$1000 for 4 nights). If I were paying $400/night, I'd say not worth it, but if you can get a good price, it's an excellent place to stay.
The location is great - walking distance to Union Square, the Village and 34th Street.

title: “Don't Expect Luxury, but Great Value and Location”
text:
We stayed at the Columbus Motor Inn for two nights. The hallways were dingy, the elevator creaked, the rooms were a bit dated, the neighborhood wasn't one you'd want to wander in at night, and the front desk staff was surly. 
That having been said, this hotel was a great value. We had a "family suite" which was enormous with two separate rooms and a bathroom. Plenty of room for a family of 4. The view was fabulous. The rooms were clean. Internet access worked. The parking was free. And you couldn't ask for a more convenient location!
I'd definitely recommend the Columbus.

title: “Cool building, cool location, cool rooms, cool staff.”
text: Very charming hotel, with helpful friendly staff. Unbeatable location (100 yds from Union Square). Hotel's restaurant is attached, but standalone restaurant, which I would be happy to eat at anytime, even if not staying there. Great price. It's my regular hotel now, whenever I'm in San Francisco.

title: “Convenient”
text:
Excellent hotel for a one night stop. Car rental is just across the street.
Rooms are typical for a motel, but clean nevertheless. Not a lot of parking space.
They have a free shuttle to the airport (LAX).

title: “Prime Location at a Fair Price”
text:
Having read some of the reviews here I was a little worried about the hotel, but I really shouldnt have been. The room was large clean and newly furnished. We had a view onto the street which was fine. The staff couldnt do enough for us, and were really helpful every time we asked for it.
The breakfast was great, if yu didt eat the egg products, everything else was fresh and tasty, plentiful and there was a lot of options, a fantastic free breakfast.

title: “Absolutely Beautiful Wedding”
text: I had my wedding at the Maple Manor Hotel this past April and was extremely pleased with the whole experience. Monique, the wedding coordinator, was a pleasure to work with and a great resource. She is very organized and planned the timeline of the reception "to-a-T" which I appreciated. The service was great, the food was delicious, and the venue was beautiful. The guests when on and on about how they loved the place! It is such a unique and charming venue full of romantic, Victorian character. The bridal suite, which is included when you host a wedding at the hotel, was equally nice. It is a huge room with an equally large bathroom and jacuzzi. I would highly recommend the Maple Manor to any bride looking for a unique venue with great staff and service!

title: “No complaints - meets expectations”
text:
Our family of four stayed here for three nights - two rooms side by side. The location is perfect for Midtown sightseeing and shopping. Close to Central Park as well. The staff were all very friendly and helpful. The rooms were a good size - enough rooms for family to visit us and hang out in the room during endless rain storms. Very clean and quiet all day and night. Too bad we couldn't empty the minibar and use it as a fridge. The pool was great for kids to swim at all hours. Never too crowded. We splurged and had breakfast at Norma's our last day - it was fantastic! At $140 for four, not an everyday thing, but worth it at least once. Also loved the Burger Joint hidden away in the lobby - worth the crowds for a quick burger. 
A few minor complaints. The parking was over $50 per day which seems crazy, but may be typical for NYC. There is a charge of $16 for wireless or wired internet access, which is ridiculous for a hotel in this category. Motel 6 provided free internet for heavens sake! The room key cards are an odd elongated shape which makes it hard to fit them in a pocket. 
Overall, a great place for a family to stay in NYC.

title: “city break”
text:
When we checked in after a long flight, was surprised that the hotel wanted to take such a large amount on our credit card for items such as room bar, or meals. However when we expressed our surprise, this was reduced.
The room was very comfortable, best hotel bed we have ever used.
Staff extremely helpful and accommodating. Excellent location for all the tourist attractions. Bought a 7 day CTA pass and used the local transport which is incredably easy. Loved the city and being able to walk to the beach was fantastic.
Room was cleaned every day, and towels changed regularly.
Would recommend this hotel, and when we return to Chicago, plan on staying there again.

title: “Not worth the $$$$”
text: I am so upset to have to write this review as I am from Dallas and have always admired this hotel from afar. Unfortunately we picked this hotel to stay in the night of our wedding. Big mistake. We were married on a Saturday and this hotel was a ghost town. Not to mention all the amenities we were promised, free breakfast, possible upgrade, were not granted. Even when we showed up in a wedding gown and tux they could have cared less. Our room was decorated in beige and brown and the TV was the size of a computer monitor. The bathroom was small and our view was of an office building about 100 ft away. Multiple times we tried to remind the staff we were newlyweds and that our reservation included breakfast, etc. and it fell on deaf ears. It was honestly so depressing to arrive at this hotel after the biggest night our life and quite frankly the biggest waste of our money. Upon learning our reservation was not honored (a few days later), they comp’d our bill $30 for the breakfast, and said they would look into the matter. Naturally we have not heard from them since. I do not recommend this hotel at all as there are plenty of updated, fun, reasonable hotels in the same area.

title: “Fun Hotel - has gone downhill”
text:
This was our second stay at the Night in 9 months and we were a little disappointed - it has become much less impressive just in that short time.
On arrival the hotel was booked out and we were placed in an appalling room on the 2nd floor at the front of the hotel. Of course they are digging up a construction site across the street and it sounded like a constant thunderstorm early each morning. To add to the sleeping difficulty, the blinds/curtains in this room were not functioning properly and light would stream in. This was especially annoying since what we loved about the Night last time was the way the curtains blocked out all of the light.
Although the receptionist claimed this room was larger than other king size rooms in the hotel it was awkwardly laid out and we preferred the arrangment of the room we were eventually moved to - after considerable complaining! The staff were reasonably accommodating but not exactly sympathetic.
Some of the neat little things are gone, like the tiny LCD screens with the number of each room. They are just switched off for some reason. The complimentary business cards personalised with your name were fun to have on our last visit - they are also gone.
The attractive smiling doorman is gone in favour of a threatening and unfriendly one. The hotel had lost the sense of style it had previously.
The airconditioners are running very loudly. Although it is possible to sleep through them, if you are a light sleeper I would beware.
There's supposed to be a turn down service. We stayed for 6 nights and received the service zero times. Our friends who were staying in another room got it once.
Good things -
Great location for midtown sightseeing, shopping & theatre. It is not very close to any one subway station but it is within a few blocks of several which allows you to catch most lines direct.
The huge TV and unlimited channel selection is a huge selling point and they have Bose clock radios that your iPod hooks into. There are a lot of other cool things in the room like the office chair and the black and white paper/pencils.
The decor in the room in general is really impressive and makes you feel more like being in the real new york than a chain hotel would.
It's a really good shower but it leaks water all over the floor. Make sure they leave you lots of towels.
Reception will give you passes to the local Equinox gym which is very well equipped. They cost $12
The Night hotel is still fun, but there were just too many errors for me. 
I think next year we will try a different hotel if we come to New York.

title: “Horrible experience”
text: This was an absolutely awful experience. From the garbage on the floors, smelly sheets, the room smelling like smoke, mold in the bathroom,hotel personnel and other guests keying into my room and housekeeping using clean wash cloths on the vanity to wipe down the sink area and then replacing the dirty wash cloth back on the vanity. Unreal, totally unreal! I will be encouraging my company to terminate their relationship with this hotel and would encourage anyone considering a stay at this hotel to give it a serious second thought.

title: “Electric avenue!”
text:
We stayed here for four nights in feb 07, in a junior suite room. There was four of us, so we had to use the sofa bed, which we knew before arrival so was fine. Having never actually seen the hotel/read reviews before arrival, and relying on our travel agent to pick a nice place, we were very shocked by how big it was for the price we payed. The room was more like a small flat than a hotel room. It had a spacious double bedroom, a bathroom, a huge living room with TV, desk area and coffee table, as well as a sofa bed, and it also had a great kitchen (cooker/lots of cupboards and a large fridge), which was also well sized. On arrival, we couldnt belive our luck! 
However, the only thing that dampened our love for the hotel was this crazy static electricity that was there all the time. When lying in bed (especially the sofa bed, but the other as well) you can see electricity bolts fly across you and because your subjected to it quite alot, it does begin to hurt and we lost a lot of sleep because of it. We think it came from the cover that they used over the sheets, and then just spread into everything. Had it not been for this then the hotel would have been perfect. If management or anyone reads this, then i would highly reccommend that you try and sort the problem out. However, i would still go back to the hotel, but just be more careful and awark about the static.

title: “Great deal at great hotel.”
text: All of the staff were very helpful and pleasant. The park and cruise package is a really good deal and the fact that the hotel is very nice made the deal even better.

title: “A good choice”
text: We were there for a wedding, and the venue was next door. The location is excellent, can walk to North Beach, the Embarcadero, etc. Breakfast in hotel was very good, both in service and food. Of course, one paid top dollar for it. It's a busy place with a helpful, friendly staff. No complaints about anything.

title: “Chuck and Ilona”
text: I loved the room and the skill and attitude of the trainer Sam in the fitness center. We were comfortable and well taken care of. The proximity to the downtown area made almost all of our destinations a simple stroll. Great stay!

title: “A good hotel, would stay here again”
text:
We stayed at the Westin St Francis in September. After
an 11-hour flight from Heathrow with no in-flight
entertainment (due to an onboard fault soon after
takeoff), we arrived in San Francisco. It didn’t take
us long before we got the transport to the hotel. 
When we arrived at the hotel, it didn’t take long to
book in - just a matter of minutes. We were given a
room on the 9th floor of the old building, the room
was large with a king-size bed and it was well
decorated and clean. We are Starwood members, which is
free to join. We went to have a look around San
Francisco, and upon our return we found in our room, a
tray of fruit, bread and cheese, and water. This, we
found out is afforded to Starwood members and which
just adds a nice touch. By the way, we had a side view
of Union Square. We would recommend this hotel and we
would stay at this hotel again. It is close to the
shops and also for the Cable Cars to take you to
Fisherman’s Wharf, which we did, on quite a few
occasions.
We went on the Alcatraz trip. We did the 9.30am
booking, and we would advise anyone wanting to do this
trip is to book it before you arrive in San Francisco,
We booked it over the Internet, and we are so glad
that we did because the four days that we were in San
Francisco the trip was nearly fully booked up and the
queues to try and get tickets was long. In the
afternoon we went on the City tour with Blue and Gold,
and that trip was excellent, saw parts of the city
that we wouldn’t have seen otherwise on our own.
We did the day trip to Yosemite, we had read that it
was a long way to go just for a day, but we thought it
was worth it, as once again we saw some lovely
countryside on the way. We had a couple of breaks
before we got to the park. We only had 2½ hours there,
but it was well worth it as it gave us the insight, so
if we went again we would stay over at least for a
night . The driver was very knowledgeable, and told us
quite a bit about the park and the areas that we went
through. When we came back over the Golden Gate Bridge
at sunset, on the way back, that was the icing on the
cake at the end of a wonderful day. As I said earlier,
if you don’t mind coach journeys the trip is
worthwhile.
One trip that we would recommend that is different
from the normal City trip is the trip on the Fire
Engine. Well worth the money. Once again, we booked
this trip on the Internet, as we did with all our
trips. A husband and wife crew, who are very friendly
and cheerful, operates the trip. Also you get to be
dressed up in a fireman’s jacket. The vehicle is a
1950’s fire engine. They took us to some different
places of the city that we hadn’t seen. Also, we went
over the Golden Gate Bridge and stopped at a place
where we had our photo taken on the fire engine with
the bridge in the background using our own cameras so
it didn’t cost us the extra for a souvenir photo. When
you have your photo taken, you also get to wear a
fireman’s helmet.
I

title: “Westin "Getaway" - in a highly populated city”
text: As ambiguous as it may sound, our vacation with two teenagers was a getaway in densely populated NYC. The Westin at Times Square enables you to be in the midst of all the excitement of Times Square, Broadway shows, Fabulous restaurants, Shopping and Night-life - however when you're ready to take a break or get a great night's sleep, you have a wonderful room waiting for you. This has been our hotel of choice for 6 years in a row.

title: “Old world charm tucked amid the hubbub”
text: We stayed at the Kensington Park for our 25th wedding anniversary and it was the perfect place! The personnel were all professional and efficient. We had a welcoming bottle of wine, bottled water, and lovely bathrobes to help us settle in on our "mink" bed throws, which are the icing on the cake to some incredibly comfortable beds. The bathroom was spacious, well lit and the shower had great water pressure and seemingly unlimited hot H2O. The owner graciously phoned us to congratulate us on our anniversary. The KP has a lovely european feel, for those who prefer not to be in cookie cutter style hotels.

title: “Business hotel. Not so much leisure.”
text: The hotel was super nice and the rooms were great. However, I wouldn't recommend this hotel if you want a laid back hotel and there is some sort business convention type thing going on. There were business people everywhere and walking around the lobby in shorts in a t-shirt felt weird for the fact that there were people with brief cases and suits everywhere. The pool area is nice, while the pool itself is small for such a large hotel. The only thing that needed updating I saw was the TV. I do not rate the hotel negative as it was nice. Just saying its not really a family or relaxing type of hotel if a event is going on.

title: “excellent”
text:
When we bid on Priceline for $150 per night for a weekend getaway we were delighted to get this hotel. It is right on the Chicago River cnr of State Street - within moderate walking distance to almost everywhere. We walked to Sears Tower, the Shed Aquarium, and all the way up to Millennium Pier.
The complimentary in-room Starbucks coffee was a treat, as was the good quality (Lather Inc) toiletries in the beautiful bathroom. Pity that breakfast was $18 each (so went a few blocks south and enjoyed "Corner Bakery" instead). The lounge bar is very reasonably priced for a relaxed/casual dinner.
Would definitely recommend AND return.

title: “We loved this hotel!”
text: This hotel was beautiful and we would love to go back. It was very clean and conveniently located to a lot of NY attractions. The staff was also very sweet, helpful and accommodating

title: “Impressive and Smooth Hotel”
text:
I stayed for 5 nights. Stay was good apart from few issues. My flight landed JFK at 630 am and i was at the hotel at 8 am after a long flight of 17hrs..... I was shocked to hear the room will be available only after 130 pm. I was so tired but had to spent time out side the hotel though staff told me the way to washrooms if i wanted to get refreshed. Any way i was offered a room after 4 hrs at about 12.30 pm. Rooms are nice and bigger in size, location is good very close to times square on 51st. It takes about an hour drive from JFK to the hotel and Taxi charges are appox 50 -55 usd.
I loved the breakfast and appreciate the room service staff for their work and nice behaviour. they have 3 lifts and they are good in speed.

title: “Great value, convenient to airport, very nice staff”
text:
I held an internal sales meeting here over two days in August. Jim M. handled my reservation quickly and professionally and the price was right, too. (We had the 'Boardroom' conference room for two days and several hotel rooms for us out-of-towners.) Besides being a very friendly and professional person, Jim was also very helpful, as indeed was everyone on the staff there.
The rooms were clean. The wifi was remarkably fast for a hotel system. The only reason I withhold 5 stars v 4 is that there were some issues with my room (toilet didn't work properly, shower made a very loud noise and the desk chair was very squeaky), suggesting they need to pay a bit more attention to maintenance. But I would definitely stay here again when in Denver, just because of how helpful and professional the staff was. For example, by the time I returned to my room in the afternoon, they had fixed the toilet problem. And in a very good indicator of dedication to customer service, when I filled out the post-stay survey and noted the maintenance issues, I got back a person response within hours. 
Bottom line: definitely recommend this hotel in you need an airport hotel in Denver.

title: “Wonderful stay....planning our return in the fall”
text:
We spent four nights at the Palomar over Memorial Day weekend, and our stay couldn't have been better. From the moment we arrived the staff was warm, friendly & helpful without being obsequious. Our room was larger than the average hotel and very comfortable.
This trip was for fun, but both of us travel frequently for business, and typically stay in properties like the Four Seasons and Ritz Carlton. The staff at the Palomar was the best I have ever dealt with, a real pleasure. 
Dupont Circle is a great neighborhood for restaurants, convenient to the Metro, etc. 
Special mention for Joe & Suzanne at the front desk, Philip at concierge, and Nabil, at the front door. Each of them helped make our stay special. Philip even helped us on the phone before we arrived. We will be back!

title: “Disappointed in Hilton”
text:
I've stayed at many Hilton hotels around the country, so I feel qualified to say that this hotel is an embarrassment to the chain. I was really disappointed in this hotel, though there was no one specific thing the management could have done to change my experience. The entire hotel needs updating: carpet is old, doors are old, carpet pad in my room had long gaps making the floor uneven, the configuration of the hotel is very odd with a long walk from the lobby to a separate building to access guest rooms (going outside and back inside again). And one of the elevators isn't in operation because supposedly it's being updated, though I didn't see any work being done and I was there 2 full weekdays. The parking lot is also a little distance from the hotel so that is another inconvenience.
As far as Hiltons go, this was worse than most Hampton Inns I've stayed at. This does not at all meet the standard I've come to expect for Hilton Garden Inns.

title: ““Convenient And Comfortable””
text: Excellent staff who made our stay there very comfortable. Relaxing pool and wonderful facility to exercise. Clean and comfortable rooms. Everyday began with a wonderful & tasty Breakfast Buffet overseen by a staff member who kept everthing refilled.

title: “Best value hotel-grand old ldame of San Francisco”
text: I was somewhat concerned about booking here after reading so many bad reviews. We had a fabulous room with a view, $165 a night coupled with their free decadent breakfasts every morning. The staff were exceptionally nice and it was a terrific value for a luxury "grand old dame" hotel. Couldn't have had a nicer stay. Highly recommend.

title: “Beautiful rooms and friendly staff!”
text: Very pleasant stay in a safe area of Jacksonville at a great price. The rooms are beautifully decorated, yet comfortable. The staff was friendly and helpful and I couldn't have asked for more. Michelle, Mitchell, Billy and Maryon were particularly nice and made my stay extra special. I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a clean, nice, safe and friendly place to stay in Jacksonville.

title: “elegant, nicely located.”
text: I had requested a Deluxe King room and was "upgraded"? to a queen room with kitchen on the 33rd floor. I hated the noise in the room though: air conditioning + air circulation + refrigerator simply killed me. And this made the price to be too high for the quality of my stay. I did not try the Alex breakfast (I believe breakfast is far too expensive in the hotels as a rule). In front of the Alex, just across the street on your left, you may wish to have a great breakfast at "Comfort Diner". A real New York breakfast experience.

title: “Value for money”
text: Well it's a nice hotel.Rooms are clean and well maintained.Service is good all throu-out.Reception desk assistants are very friendly and ready to help you with any issue.Location is near the main road giving you the ease to access various amenities which are available near-by.The place is truly a value for money.Definitely I am going to use the services again in the future.Thanks.

title: “Won't go back”
text:
I stayed here a few months earlier and thought the hotel was okay, so the next time I had to spend a night by LAX, I booked this hotel again. Big, big mistake. I stayed here because I didn't want to drive the hour and a half home that late at night (around midnight).
When I tried to call to gaurantee check in that late, I was transferred no less than 7 times and hung up on twice before they finally figured out how to get me to the front desk.
When I arrived at the airport I called the hotel to ensure that a shuttle was running. I specifically packed for that trip so I would not have to wait for baggage claim in LA- what a joke. Everyone had claimed their luggage and was waiting for the shuttles before any showed up. Actually we waited and waited and waited and waited. After over a half hour another shuttle driver for a different hotel took pity on us and dropped us at the Hilton. 
Then there was the check in. There only appeared to be two people ahead of me in line so I thought it would go smoothly. Over an hour later I was checked in. The man at the reception desk kept helping people from a tour bus that pulled up after we got in line before he helped us. 
Whe it was finally my turn, I commented on the wait, all I got was an extremely surly attitude. Way to treat any customer, let alone one of your gold members Hilton! Then the bar closed early- luckily the bartender took pity and made me two drinks to take out into the lobby. All the poor people behind me in line who tried to get a well needed drink were turned away.
Needless to say I won't stay here ever again. By the way, I could have been home sooner than the Hilton got me into a room right next to the airport.

title: “EXCELLENT SERVICE”
text: I am a travel agent that traveled with my granddaugher for a Soccer Tournament in Morgan Hill. I am also a Marriott Specialist. All of my stays at a Marriott property have been great, but I really felt the need to comment on this property. The service was EXCEPTIONAL. From the time we walked in the entrance we were greeted with happy employees who gave us bottled water and a treat (cookies). The room was spotless. The breakfast was great, and all the employees we encountered were friendly and helpful. It is so refreshing to stay at a hotel that goes that extra mile to make you feel welcome. Kudos to the Staff! I will always recommend this hotel to clients that need a stay in that area. Everything was perfect! What a great job the staff at the hotel does!

title: “Stay here only if you need to.”
text:
I feel sorry for those in charge of running this hotel. 
The location is very good, but can't so much more than that on the PROs side of things.
Plenty of CONs:
- price: seems reasonable, but for what you get/hassle it is actually too much. e.g. $180 for a room with two double-beds (on a booked-solid conference weekend across the city)
- condition: The place is old and falling apart, literally. Not only furniture and decor, but basics. In our first room, when I turned on the sinks hot water some brown sludge came up, momentarily. The blinds were ripped and had holes. Both my friend and I had incessant trouble with the magnetic keys opening out room door. (Staff said don't store them close to a cellphone or iPod is would demagnetize them.... ya, right!). The final straw in that room was that the door would simply not lock when leaving! We requested a room change at that point. (We were no frills travelling but there are basic essentials that must be met!)
- infrastructure: in the "new" or second room, there was low water pressure and hardly hot water. The same room key problem remained with that roomlock too, however, at least it locked. The elevator was VERY slow.
- service: given the above we requested a reduction in room price. They were resistant, although I am quite sure that these issues and complaints repeat with every second visitor. Eventually we got 25% off (they originally suggested 10%). As mentioned, I do feel sorry for the staff. With a building like this, you are in a losing battle. It needs a complete overhaul. So, they cannot be happy service providers when they know that most inquiries are probably going to actually be complaints.
- location is very good. BUT, watch where your room is located. If on the west side of the building the L-line will be going past you and it can be quite loud.

title: “Very nice but...”
text: Based on the excellent reviews of this motel, I decided to go for a couple nights. The manager was *very* friendly and accommodating! The motel is situated in a nice area of San Diego, near the Harbor. Only one small caveat, the rooms are ridiculously small! I apparently stayed in the smallest room with the firmest bed. :( I wasn't too happy... but its value, along with the friendliness of the staff, can't be beat.

title: “Loved Chicago”
text: The hotel was less than 2 blocks from Michigan Ave, located almost right in the middle. Room was large and spacious. Would stay again. Highly recommend the river tour of the architecture of Chicago. Staff helped arranged. Very accomodating.

title: “Not great.”
text:
This was basically the only decent hotel left during my recent business trip to San Jose, and the only room available was a 'suite'.
--The neighborhood surrounding the hotel is not great. Not too bad, but next to the freeway and not great. 
--Check-in was fine, the hotel looked to be recently renovated, but the room was pretty basic. Since it was a 'suite', it was large but it was basically a huge room with a bedroom off to the side. It looked like they tried to update it, but didn't really follow through.
--The furniture in the living space was sparse, and placed haphazardly for the size of the room. It looked like someone tried to decorate, but the space was just too big so they gave up. 
--I tried to use the coffee maker, but old discolored water started dripping out of it so I skipped it.
--The bedroom was fine except the bed was not very comfortable. 
--The bathroom was not cleaned very well, as there were a few random hairs in the shower/tub combination, which pretty much ruins a hotel stay. The shower was inside the oval shaped jetted tub, so it was awkward getting into it.. Also, the jets looked dirty (what hotel renovates and doesn’t replace an 80s-style jetted tub?). The plumbing by the shower head and the spigot was coming out of the wall (see photo). There's no excuse for this kind of disrepair at any hotel, let alone a higher cost 'suite' at a Holiday Inn (a brand that markets itself as mid-range hotel option). 
This hotel is fine to crash for one night, and maybe some of the other renovated rooms have a better layout and a nicer bathroom, but I won't stay here again.

title: “Stayed in Sept 2009 actually - cosy rooms! by cosy i mean tiny!”
text:
This hotel was actually very nice, I have stayed in NYC once before at the Belvedere and what one hotel lacks, the other gains.
New Yorker was very close to Macys, opposite madison square gardens, and had a fantastic view of Empire State Building. It was also a stones throw from the Bus terminal (which was actually a negative...but about that later)
It was a shotr walk to Times Sq and Broadway, and my advice would be where sensible walking shoes if you wish to visit here by foot, and even more so if you plan to walk to madison ave, fifth ave and central aprl - which are all must see's!
We walked everywhere in Midtown, but it is advisable to get a subway pass or even better but more costly, a hop on/off open tour bus pass, as they stop all over and go to financial district, brookyln, all over midtown, harlem and all the points of interest you will ever need!
Right about the Hotel, 
The hotel (we think?!?) from Dunster Checks in...
The lobby is lovely and they have kept it contemporary whilst being sympathetic to its original era (I think its the 1920's)
Anyway, its been done up lovely, but the rooms are soooo pokey! Well ours was anyway! No room for a safe, a teeny wardrobe, small bathroom (but adequate) and just enough walking space around the bed - no vanity area - the TV on the wall and just a small side table to fit an ice bucket on - no coffee facilities!
The staff were wonderful and they even dropped us at back to Newark airport for a lot less than taxis and not much more than the buses - we booked it only about half hour before needing to leave as planned to get the bus.
There is a fantastic diner attached to the hotel - which I recommend for breakfast visit even if you dont stop in this hotel! It was very reasonably priced, always got a table (always a small queue but went down very quickly) and table service is quick without feeling rushed, and coffee is served constantly.
There was also a bar attached which was a plus with this hotel as the Belvedere didnt have this and they always had a happy hour (if i remember rightly from 5-6ish) and was perfect when we pulled up from a hectic day in the city! It serves meals which we didnt try but the bar snacks were nice - which we used when we had to rush off to a show! Cocktails (and drinks) were pricey but the locality was definitly a plus point!
Now regarding that bus stop problem! Great for getting the bus to the airport - and all over USA by the sounds of it...becasue of this there is every kind of shop you need close by - chemists, electricals, McDonalds, Starbucks, Adult vids (didnt enter but cant not notice them ;D ) The negative is that its the biggest bus station either in the US or the world maybe?!?! - it caters for many undesirables! There are tramps / homeless people galore! The police go past constantly. we actually counted 25 police going past at one point - but could have been a drill! Beggars are everywhere and people asking you to buy there CD's, crap theyve made etc! You'd think you were in a flea market! and everywhere smells of urine! honestly, avoid this area! lol
Other than that a fab stay here! I preferred the Belvedere, but the facilities here were better...again regarsdsw to locality - I preferred Belvedere as we were right next to Hells Kitchen and Times sq - which I loved all the restaurants and was able to eat there every night - at a much less and much tastier than typical NY eateries.
I have visited NY in Nov 2007 which was lovely to see Rockerfella Xmas tree and decs but preferred the visit at end of Sept 2009 as the weather was lovely - like a hot UK summers day everyday - no rain, no cold and lovely wakls with ice cream around central park! - Although the heat made the bins stink! 
Only gave 3/5 for sleep quality as this in NY sirens and horns are going off all night, but beds were comfy!

title: “Loved it”
text: I had a great clean room house keeping was very friendly and i enjoyed talking to them. When i checked in front desk was very informative and provided me with directions to the restaurants i wanted. I had two maintenance issues one w/ my toilet and another w the ac both were taken care of promptly and effectively. When coming to work in the room were very friendly and cleaned up quick. Great hotel and staff thanks.

title: “Mini Bar No I didn't”
text:
We stayed there 2 nights. The room was beautiful as was the view of the Washington Monument. The service was excellent other than at the bar where getting service was like pulling hair. 
The reason this not a 5 star super happy review is the Mini bar games the hotel is playing. When we checked in the bellhop told us it was weight sensitive both in the Mini bar fridge and on the tray that they had situated at the end of the desk. We gave it a far berth. We didn't even open the fridge one. We didn't even touch it by accident on the desk. 
When we checked out they slip the bill under your door and my husband checked it carefully. It was fine although they charge you for internet. Why is that the more expensive the hotel the more they charge you for internet? At a Holiday Inn Express it's free. 
Fast Forward one week: I got an emailed itemized bill and what do I see? 4 Mini Bar charges totally around $25 that had not appeared on that bill under the door. So now I have to call them. This is sketchy. How many people don't even check after they get that bill under the door?

author.location: New York, New York, United States

title: “Great location, don't believe all that you read”
text: I stayed at The Wellington for 4 nights from 14th - 18th November. I was a bit concerned after reading some of the previous reviews that that hotel would not be up to much so I was pleasantly surprised on arrival. Yes, the lobby is crowded, but check-in was quick and easy. We never had to wait more than a couple of minutes for an elevator. We were shown up to our room by Richard the Bell-hop and on discovering that we had been allocated the wrong type of room he went back down to reception and got us keys to another room without delay. We had booked a one-bedroom suite (room 1220 if you're interested!) and we were very pleased. There was a spacious living room with a sofa, table and chairs and tv, a small kitchenette and large bedroom with 2 beds and another tv. The bathroom was small but fully functional. The beds were lovely and comfortable, in fact the only problem was that the central heating proved to be a bit hit and miss but a visit from an engineer resolved this. The diner attached to the hotel does a great breakfast! The location was great and overall we were really happy with our stay.

title: “Good hotel in good location”
text:
Our 4 day stay started as Renaissance and finished as Loews, although not much changed that quickly.
The room was adequate without being brilliant although did benefit from a sideways glance of the Hollywood sign.
The heated pool was a really nice refuge after a day's site seeing. The pool bar was alright, but the barman kept disappearing for 5-10 mins. If you stand in the right place you can just about photograph someone in the pool with the sign in the background!
We found out on day 2 that there is an exit on the 2nd floor that goes straight into the shopping centre and also provides easy access to Hollywood Blvd.
You really don't need a car at this hotel. There are many restaurants of various quality and price brackets in close proximity. I'll just mention Mel's Diner; not the original (walk down the hill and across Hollywood Blvd), but still a good breakfast experience. 
Trips out can be done by taxi - we went to Warner Studios VIP tour (recommended) and by the metro - we went to a Dodger's game (Dodger's Express (free bus) from Union Square) - or of course walking. The Hollywood things are right on your doorstep and even the Hollywood Bowl is very walkable (up the hill) if there is someting on - we enjoyed the whole experience of the bowl. We also did a "tour" - just over 2hrs from LA City tours - personally I wasn't interested in which star lived in which house but no trip to Hollywood would be complete with getting away from the Blvd and seeing the "nice" areas
There were a lot of "bums" about so probably walking would not be so savoury after midnight.
So in summary good hotel in good location (at an OK price) - we will have to see what Loews do to the hotel

title: “Very old Hotel”
text: I took this very good branded Hotel, so I could not go wrong, This hotel has not being reonvated for years and years, Hope they do it they have the best location, Has two building and you must go from one building to the other in a overpass so far and old

title: “Uptown ease”
text: Nice secure location with easy access to uptown venues. The staff was nice, bed was cofortable, and we'd go back again.

title: “Staff Was Helpful - Other Guests, Not So Much”
text:
I was on business in Indianapolis for a week in April. It was the same week of the National Firemen's Conference. Most hotels were packed, including the Embassy, but they fit me in partially based on my elite status with Hilton.
Upon check-in, there was a line of 9 people. There was no line at the Hilton Honors Check In. I presented myself to the front desk clerk at the Hilton Honors Check In, and she was very warm and friendly. The third guy in line was not. He began swearing at me for cutting the line. The desk clerk explained to him that I was an Honors member and was able to do so. (Which I had attempted to explain, but the guy was adamant that I had cut the line). He became hostile and belligerent. The desk clerk called security to stand by me through the remainder of check in.
Upon getting to my room, I found that it was non-smoking, which was not in line with my reservation. I proceeded back downstairs. The desk clerk apologized profusely, and handed me new keys . . .to a two level penthouse suite with a porch overlooking the city as large as the room I had just left. 
Kudos to this hotel for a quiet pleasant stay. The staff was top notch, the room was spacious, and they treated me like a person who consistently spends money on hotels in the Hilton family. The desk clerk handled an obviously bad situation with professional courtesy and corrected a problem in my favor without hesitation.

title: “Great experience at this hotel!”
text:
My wife and I had a great experience at this hotel. We were vacationing for five days for our anniversary and to run the San Antonio Marathon in Nov.
The hotel was very clean and the staff were excellent to us, especially after we finished the marathon. Charlotte at the hotel lobby bar was awesome, and Eric, the assistant manager for food and beverage, treated us as VIPs.
The hotel is convenient to all the major attractions in the city, and the hotel is located right next to all the action at the Riverwalk.
We will definitely stay again at this Hilton if our travels take us back to San Antonio.

title: “What a Wonderful Hotel & Wonderful Staff that Really Made My Stay Enjoyable!!!”
text:
This hotel is located directly next to the Time Warner Arena (Home of the Charlotte Checkers Hockey & Charlotte Bobcats Basketball)
The location is awesome since your within a mere 2 minute walk to the Bus Transit Station and Subway, as well a mere 5 minute walk to the Entertainment Mecca area full of top name restaurants, bars, shops & nightclubs...
Check-in was a breeze and we were given a room on the 15th floor (Room 1515) facing the downtown & arena)
Pros:
Complementary Hot Breakfast Included in Rate
Free WIFI 
All Rooms have a Modern Feeling & Very Good for Business Travelers
Complementary Business Center (Located in the lobby area with 3 computers and printers)
(Nightlights Attached to the top of your bed for reading or working at night and not bothering the other person if you have two beds
The personal touch was definately there as well, everytime I entered the hotel or left the hotel the front desk would say "Enjoy your afternoon or Enjoy your Evening" and when I returned they would say "Welcome Back"..
The hotel also has a very nice bar with flat screen tvs for watching sports games or news etc located right in the lobby..
Last but not least the outdoor heated pool on the 7th floor with patio and gas fireplace, a very nice touch to say the least.....( I did use it when I was there in the end of December with it being 40 degrees outside).
...

title: “Not up to Marriott Standards”
text: Our recent stay at this property was disappointing at best. After just staying at the Courtyard property in Tyler, TX..we were sorely disappointed in the Fossil Creek property. Although front desk staff was very friendly and accomodating, the overall appearance and upkeep of this property was poor. At the outside entrance we used, there were food products, and various other random items left near the trash, but had obviously been there for quite some time. Door glass and handles were very dirty. (In the hotel's defense, there is a lot of construction in that area) Our room was clean, but very small, with dated furnishings, and the overall arrangement of the room was not comfortable..they even still had very large TVs, that were on a console alongside the beds making viewing difficult. They have not updated furniture or electronics. The air conditioning unit had no thermostat, and was terribly noisy. The room felt very humid, to the point that the carpet seemed moist. Would not recommend. Definitely disappointed in this Courtyard visit..which hasn't been our experience at other properties.

title: “wonderful hotel”
text: We had a great 3 day stay at the silversmith. Nice, clean and staff very helpful. Loved the location. With in walking distance of many of the major Chicago sites. Close to all lines of public transportation. Will definitely plan on staying for our next visit.

title: “Perfect NY base”
text: Having read some bad reviews on here before we went to NY I was a bit anxious. But on arrival we were totally impressed. Beautiful lobby and bar area, very helpful and polite staff. The room was very stylish and compact with great finishes like quality linen and Aveda products. TV and stereo were great, and it was handy to have a safe in the room rather than having a main reception one. The corridors and stairways were gorgeous too. The location as well was perfect, a coupld of blocks over from Times Squre, so very central and there was a great diner over the road for amazing breakfasts in the morning (thought the hotel also provided a good free continental breakfast. Would definitely stay there again. Brilliant.

title: “Marvelous hotel”
text: Club Quarters Rockefeller Center was centrally located both to Times Square, 5th Avenue shopping, and bus loop areas. For those travelers who wish privacy and quiet, this is the hotel for you. The room was spacious for two people, a/c, well lit, clean, nice view of the cathedral--although the bathroom was small, it had a full shower. I was very pleased with the staff, courteous and very helpful. My stay in New York City was a hit.

title: “Good place for medium term stays”
text: Nice hotel near everything (Civic Center, BART within walking distance, Muni infront of the door, close to Mission District and just around the corner of the nice shops and restaurants around Gough Street). It has clean, handsome furnished rooms, very friendly and helpful stuff, good wekly rates and great service. There's free coffee all day in the lobby room and the guy at the desks helps where he can! Defintly a great place to stay!

title: “Great location”
text:
Stayed at this hotel four nights .
Room was extra clean , comfortable , quiet , well furnished .
Staff members without exception were very polite and ready to assist .
Special mention to the concierge staff for their kind service .
Only one restaurant on the pricy side not very useful for quick light meals . 
Although well kept , the place will most likely need refurbishing in a near future ;
It's O.K. but getting old ..............

title: “Atrocious Stay”
text:
I was appalled by the condition of the hotel and level of service, given the price.
The following incidents occurred:
1. Upon arrival late Thursday night, my sister and I were given a suite with a Queen at a rate of $389. I recalled that we had a King, and the next morning on my way out the door, I asked about it. The woman at the front desk would not give me the King without my confirmation or unless I would pay an extra $30 or $40 a night. I didn’t have my reservation confirmation with me, but I found it later that day, and our reservation confirmation stated we had a suite with a King for $369. This was remedied Friday afternoon upon another visit to the front desk. We were ultimately charged $389 for the room, but on Sunday when I checked out, I was able to get the price adjusted to the quoted rate.
2. When I woke up in our suite with a Queen on Friday morning. I went to the bathroom to shower and inside the tub there was a brown/black splatter liquid everywhere. It looked like mud or sewage or someone had been violently ill all over the tub. I immediately called the concierge to have it fixed. I waited a half hour and no one came. I had an appointment I had to make, so I called back. Someone finally came within the hour. He cleaned up the mess but said that he’d need to come back to clear out the drain. I had to shower and get ready to leave, so I showered in water that literally came up to my knees. Disgusting. 
3. We switched rooms Friday afternoon. Again, the shower in our second room filled up to mid calf every time we showered. This is absolutely filthy.
4. Our second room, like the first, mysteriously only had one robe. I requested one on Friday afternoon. None arrived. I requested one late Friday evening. None arrived. I called for a third time Saturday afternoon for a robe, and finally one arrived.
5. Upon arrival in the second room, I went to grab a glass. The glass was covered in “protective/sanitary” plastic, but it also was covered in a yellow fugusy film around the rim. I called for new glasses. None arrived. I called for new glasses with the robe late Friday evening, and they finally arrived. In addition, it was quite shocking that housekeeping did not remove this filthy glass from the room when they cleaned it on Saturday.
While all of these things were unacceptable for a hotel with such a high rate, what was so baffling to me was the fact that no one asked me how my stay was (even on check out when I was getting our bill adjusted!!!), tried to remedy any of these situations, or seem to really care about our stay. I have stayed at hotels with wide ranging price points, and this was by far the worst service I have ever received.

title: “Nice Place for a fair price”
text: I stayed her many times when it was the Aku AKu and always found it ok. The remodel and switch to Best Western has made it much better. The rooms are nicely done, not fancy but clean and comfortable. The staff is very friendly and the pool was clean and warm, and mostly empty which was nice. There are indeed some nice places to eat within easy walking distance. If you like sushi, Somethings Fishy is excellent and right next door to the hotel. As far as this being a bad area, that is non sense. This is one of the safer areas in the valley, of course use common sense at all times in all areas. As far as the Best Western its lots of bang for the buck and I will for sure stay again.

title: “Comfortable albeit sexist convention hotel”
text:
I stayed here four nights at the end of July for a conference. The hotel is convenient to a nice little entertainment district, on 6th St., though Congress, the Capitol and the University are a bit of a hike in 100-degree weather. Rooms are extremely spacious, with a large desk and a loveseat, and the bathroom was also very nice, with upscale amenities and great water pressure and temperature. Heating and cooling in the room was also up to standard, and the hotel was quiet, though I suspect this is not always the case on weekends (we saw large teen groups coming in and the "no partying in the rooms" sign goes up on Friday night). Room service was fast and the food was hot and tasty. There was nothing really special I can point to, but all of the above was appreciated!
Now for the not-so-good. I didn't like the fact that all of the health and convenience items you would normally find in a hotel gift shop were behind the counter in the coffee shop, so that you would have to announce to the world if you needed feminine hygiene products or etc. The conference rooms were not heated and cooled properly, so that all of the interior rooms (not on an exterior wall) were boiling hot and the ones on exterior walls were freezing. Conference staff was extremely helpful and hospitable so that made up for the discomfort.
The worst--I checked in with a group of five women and three men at about 2:30 in the afternoon. ALL of the women in the group were told they would have to wait for an hour if they wanted the King room they had reserved, while ALL of the men were given a King room immediately without comment. I should point out that the men were not dressed better than the women, and they were scattered at random in the check-in line, so I can only conclude that they were given preference for early check-in to preferred rooms. This is completely unacceptable for a business hotel in the US in 2011, and made me wonder what other subtle preferences the men might be receiving during our stay.

title: “Simply excellent”
text: The hotel was just great: central location, wonderful (clean, modern facilities), great architectural design. LOVED the fact that there was a kitchenette as well as terrace. And very affordable. Definitely hope to stay there again!

title: “Nice Location”
text: The Georgetown Suites were well equipped and comfortable in a very picturesque area of Washington. Good local restaurants with good connections via public transport into downtown Washington. The photographs on the hotel website give a rather better impression of the hotel than real life. However, overall a good place to stay in Washington

title: “A great place to stay”
text: We have been staying at Ocean Villa Inn for about five years now. Not only is it close to the beach, dining and shopping, the staff is FANTASTIC. We always reserve a 2nd floor room and the balcony in the evening with the view can't be beat and the continental breakfast is a nice feature. We have never had any complaints. We are looking forward to our stay at the end of July 2010.

title: “excellent beautiful rooms/ Miel restaurant and sushi offer splendid food”
text:
Beautiful rooms- try junior suite specials with a good view on the water. Very friendly staff and above all extremely good food- Miel restaurant is sfinetely a place you should visit.
