Rooms top notch modern, and clean.

title: “Excellent Location”
text:
Just returned from 5 nights in New York (couple and 20 year old son) spent at The Blakely.
We chose this hotel due to its location - very close to Central Park, Broadway, Times Square and well withing walking distance to all the other central attactions - Empire State Building, Top of the Rock, United Nations Buildings, Grand Central Station to name a few - and we were not disaappointed.
The hotel was ideal for us - the staff were extremely helpful and booked restaurants, taxis etc for us and our two rooms were on the 16th floor at the front of the building were well furnished, but probably smaller than others we have stayed in previously in America (but never before in New York) - but quite large enough for our requirements - usefully having microwave, fridge and tea/coffee making factilities should you need them.
The hotel has a computer in reception which the guests can use which is very useful when you have "young adults" with you that need to check their e mails/view face book etc!
The local Delis are good for breakfast, lunch and or dinner and serve a variety of things very quickly - and are packed with New Yorkers as well as tourists.
We did a huge amount whilst we were there - dining at Michael Jordans Steak House (in Grand Central Station) was brilliant (expensive at £50/head) but a great experience. Helicoper ride over New York great fun and the shopping ... well that is something else! If you are not a shopper there is still loads to do and experience - but be prepared to walk and if you go in the Autumn/Winter take a warm coat as even if it is sunny the wind is very cold.
Great place would certainly return if the opportunity arises!

title: “Very nice place to stay, great price”
text: I really enjoyed the stay here. Very nice staff, great downtown location, very convenient. Also they have really really good cookies and a great restaurant downstairs.

title: “What a great hotel!”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights in January and absolutely loved this hotel.
Check in was fast and easy, we asked for a high floor at the time of check in and it was no problem at all for the staff.
The room was spacious and the bed & pillows were the most comfortable. I want to buy a pillow from the company website now, it was so good! The bathroom was great, and the tv sound was even piped in! Huge shower. 37inch telly, lots of info about the hotel and the city provided. The mini bar was v expensive ($6.50 for a Kitkat!) so we bought soft drinks and snacks at the nearest Duane Reade branch (a bit like the UK's Superdrug, but better).
The lounge and bar area is lovely, with big screen telly and they make a mean Mojito!
Step outside and you're right in Times Square. The TKTS booth is just steps away as is the pick up point for the Grayline buses. 
The reception, bar and housekeeping staff were most friendly and helpful.
A great hotel and would love to stay there again.

title: “a perfect place for us!”
text: We found this location to be a perfect spot for us. We used the hop on/off bus as our transportation for our 3 days and the stop is just 2 blocks away. Our room had a view of the Brooklyn Bridge. It was quiet and comfortable. The breakfast area is small but a decent selection. Staff was helpful.

title: “Excellent stay, I recommended!!!”
text:
PROS:
- Staff helpful, polite, and well qualified.
- The hotel receives packages without charging any fees.
- Relaxing pool, nice!!
- Excellent breakfast, with several options, like a banquet. Extremely cheap, only $3.90/person.
- Large rooms, comfortable beds.
- Hotel organized with preserved installations.
- Safe place.
CONS:
- Many crickets outside the hotel, and some of them were able to get inside the room. (I don't know how, lol).
- The pool closed too early, it could close at midnight.
- The fitness center needs to improve, a multi-station would be fine.
BOTTOMLINE:
- The breakfast and the staff (10/10).

title: “My stay at Marriott Fisherman's Wharf”
text: Very convenient location and close to everything. Good size rooms and bathrooms with excellent lightning. Comfortable bed with good linens and pillows. . Although very clean, the bathroom towels are of very poor quality for a Marriott. Service in general is excellent and I would stay there again.

title: “I wish I was still there...6 nights was not enough”
text:
Our family of 7 stayed at the Beverly Garland Hotel for 6 nights in September 2012. We had stayed in Las Vegas for the previous 4 nights and had driven down.
The hotel was easy enough to find just of the Hollywood Freeway and down Vineland a short way. Anybody making the trip to Los Angeles from Las Vegas should make a stop at Peggy Sues Diner, it is about halfway and serves good food and is an interesting trip back to the Fifties.
We were checked in quickly by Sky, a very helpful young lady, and given rooms, on the 3rd floor, in the Portola section, which was ideal as it was well away from the noise of the freeway. She also gave us complimentary drink vouchers for the adjacent Decoy Lounge, which is a really nice bar; we had a few happy hours there. We decided to pay a little extra to park in the hotels secure car park rather than risk off street parking (bin collection days/residents only parking issues) across the road, well worth the few dollars it cost. You also get to park up close to your room.
The room looked newly refurbished and was well furnished with a 40 inch flat screen TV and coffee maker. You even get a choice of hard or soft pillows. Nice touch! We even had a small balcony overlooking the tennis courts. I nearly forgot……….there is free Wi-Fi.
The hotel location is perfect being an easy 20 minute walk to Universal Studios and Universal City walk, or there is a complimentary mini bus from the hotel to the Studios, running every 30 minutes. Could I suggest that you ride there and walk back, it’s easy and safe. The Metro station is also close and gets you to Hollywood Boulevard for next to nothing. It’s clean and punctual.
Also, there are plenty of eating places close at hand, therefore no need to drive (have a beer with your meal!) Places we dined at were, Micelis Italian with singing waiters, China Wok and an authentic Indian Restaurant and at Universal City walk Bubba Gumps was good fun. But one of the best places to eat is on site at Tulas Restaurant. Breakfast, Lunch or Dinner are all excellent. Nice décor and terrific serving staff. Highly recommended. There is a Starbucks just down the road. If you want drinks for the room try Ralphs for some really good bargains.
A nice run out is the drive down to Malibu and lunch at Coogies, excellent food and the staff and locals were very friendly. Then drive on PH1 coast road to Santa Monica and park up and walk down to Venice Beach, which is always a must.
If you want to do the LA Tour talk to Andy or Freddy (concierge) who are usually to be found working outside the front doors to Reception. They fixed the 7 of us up with a tour with Hollywood Fun Tours, in an open top 12 seater. It took us to the Hollywood Sign, Hollywood Boulevard, Farmers Market (try Bobs donuts) , Rodeo Drive (we even saw a Bugatti Veyron parked outside a shop) Beverly Hills and many more places to numerous to mention.
Back to the hotel, the swimming pool is well equipped, more than enough sun beds, lots of towels, a sauna, a gym, a bar and movies for the kids at weekends.
So to summarise, great staff, great location, well furnished and well maintained. There seemed to be quite a few Brits there so it had to be good. Would go back in an instant

title: “Mixed feelings”
text:
On one hand, it was a very nice hotel. The lobby was nice, it had a great gym, the beds were super comfy, there was free coffee and tea in the room, the restaurant was ok, the location was sort of ok if you’re a good walker. There is a subway entrance right outside the door. On the other hand, *some* of the staff and *some* of the clientele were a little sketchy. I can't quite put my finger on it. There were some people milling around that made me uncomfortable. I sensed some of them were professional women. But I can't be sure. Maybe it was just a fashion statement. 
I had a nice, large, comfortable room, although not in top notch repair. It wasn’t horrible, but it wasn’t superior. There was a bit of confusion because I stayed two nights with two separate reservations. Because of that, my room never actually got cleaned, and the housekeeping manager barged right into my room without knocking. (She did offer to have the room cleaned for me, but it really wasn’t necessary). Plus, I got locked out of my room on the second day (my key was deactivated), but really, I can't fault the hotel for that at all. I’m the one who made two separate reservations.
There were abundant towels, pretty nice toiletries, and lots of fluffy pillows. The gym had the most up to date and properly working equipment I've ever experienced. But the pool was a disappointment. It was very small and full of kids. With over 100 degree temps, I would have really liked to hop in that pool, but I just couldn’t bring myself to do it. 
As far as value, I found the hotel a BIT pricy. I chose it because there was an event there that I was attending. The internet was not free in the room. You have to go to the lobby for free wireless. That’s a bit inconvenient, and old fashioned in my book. Especially during certain hours when the elevators are DREADFULLY slow. There is no mini-bar in the room-meaning no refrigerator. You can rent one for $20/per day, which I also think is over priced. You might as well buy your own mini fridge for that price. And despite the rather high cost of my room, breakfast wasn’t included. I paid for the buffet anyway, and it was ok. But now I wish I had gone to Reading Market to have pancakes with the Amish, as the concierge recommended. Little did I know I wouldn’t have that option on Sunday
I’d say stay there if you need to be in that neighborhood. Otherwise, find something cheaper and newer, with more free amenities.

title: “Little Gem in the City By the Bay”
text:
Whoever wrote the previous review must have very good imagination or must went to a wrong place. Here I am sitting in the lovely lobby of Grant Hotel, cozy and quiet, enjoying the free internet access. I noticed the lobby entrance is wheelchair accessable. 
I have to admit that the service is basic, there is no doorman or fancy decoration as some big hotel would have, but the room is very clean and the staffs are nice and helpful. We are here for the city, not the hotel anyway. I would rather stay in such a reasonable priced hotel right in downtown than paying higher room rate for the doorman, decoration and some room amenities that I don't even bother to use.
I am really enjoying my stay here.

title: “This was all part of our dream-come-true holiday and we were not disappointed!”
text:
The Orchid Suites are most obliging to travellers needs. A simple continental breakfast was an ideal way to kickstart each day. There's a pool, but we were way too busy to go near it. The location is prime, as long as you're not here for the view. Proximity to everything is at your doorstep - shopping, theatres, nightclubs, eateries, public transport, museums, LA tours. Adventure begins at your doorstep!
We expected older style rooms, a clean suite with a kitchen. And that is exactly what we got. How good is that! You don't get a view but the payoff is that you are there - right there, smack bang in the pumping heart of Hollywood. 
We were lucky enough to be there when Grauman's Chinese Theater hosted the red carpet premiere of Fantastic Mr Fox. And what a sight it was to see people camp out for days to have their latest Twilight book autographed at its midnight release. 
We went everywhere around LA using the Orchid Suite as our "home-base". We will definitely stay there again, our home-away-from-home.

title: “Marriott IAH”
text: Hotel is very costly. Week nights $300 plus and they charge extra for internet. Tried card keys three times and still did not work for $300 I was put in the south tower which in a long walk from the front desk after three different card keys they change my room. We waited in the hall until they could get us a room they the card key would work. They did not offer anything for my trouble, didn't have any trouble add up the bill. I would say the cost far out weights the service.

title: “Neat clean nice, but loud”
text: We stayed here in a wedding block and all in all, it was a good experience. The staff was friendly and helpful and the rooms were clean and spacious. I liked that our room had a mini-fridge and microwave, which both made traveling with young children a bit easier. The location was a bit noisy with many trucks and emergency vehicles going by at all hours of the day and night. The hotel provided ear plugs, which was nice, but with kids in the room, I didn't want to use them for fear I wouldn't hear my children in the night. Also, i felt the complimentary breakfast was a bit lacking in variety and protein. It was starch and sugar and sugar and starch!

title: “Does the job”
text: If your destination is somewhere close to the IAH airport then this hotel is something you would want to look at. The hotel is relatively clean and has very nice staff. It is however far away from downtown if that's where you want to be. The pricing is pretty decent compared to other hotels in the area. Check in and check out are pretty straight forward. The rooms are average and so is the sleep quality. The rooms are not sound proofed from each other and you can be easily disturbed by the people next door. I even once had to involve the hotel staff to keep the next room quiet. Housekeeping will knock on adjacent doors and that alone is enough to wake you up from the deepest of sleeps. The bar in the hotel is small and the restaurant is just a sorry excuse for one; overpriced, the food isn't great and above all nothing about is Mediterranean as the name suggests. Overall, I would stay here if I am on business or if I want to be out of the downtown area. Although it's worthy to note that the prices aren't so much different than downtown.

title: “location,location,location”
text: This hotel is one-half a block from time square.The staff are great,rooms were clean,the beakfast was good. Rooms on the small side but well maintained. Would return next trip. Canada loves New York City

title: “Booked me at one price, and tried to charge me another”
text: I booked my room a few weeks in advance of my trip to S.F., and when I called the night before to confirm they wanted to charge me DOUBLE the price we agreed to when I made the reservation. Since they only accept cash there is notpaper trail or record of the price they promise, so they feel entitled to lie when you book and try to rip you off when you arrive. Thankfully I called the night before and was able to rebook, but when I cancelled they had the nerve to write ME a nasty email. BEWARE!

title: “TOP 10 HOTELS I HAVE STAYED AT”
text: Great location. Rooms are beautiful. Perfect. Everything you can imagine. Amenities are great - cool restaurants, workout room great. Pool is sleek and nice. Location is perfect and accessible to everything.

title: “Great Hotel, always our first choice.”
text: We discovered the Iroquois several years ago, and its always our first pick for trips to New York. We love the rooms, and although small, are furnished and decorated very upscale, and very comfortable. The hotel is very near Broadway shows, but far enough that you don't feel like you are in the midst of the hustle and bustle. You are also only a short walk from 5th avenue, Bryant Park and Grand Central. Try the Triomphe for an excellent pre-theater dinner, and we like the Red Flame just a few doors down for breakfast.

title: “Nice Chic Apartment style hotel”
text:
What I notice right off the bat was the service which is excellent. Before I even reach in my purse to pay the cab..my door was open and a firm hand was reaching out for me with my luggage. 
The hotel is very chic,sexy and modern which may not suit everyone taste. The rooms are very clean , simple, modern kind of Ikea-ish ( in a good way).
The cellar bar has a great happy hour with a professional crowd. The onsite restaurant is Koi which has great sushi in a fashionable atmosphere.
The hotel is in great location for restaurants , shopping( Alice & Oliva is right down the street). There is a coffee shop right next door. The Bryant park Grill is across the street.
Great hotel for business or a sexy weekend in the city.

title: “Definitely stay here again!!”
text: I read some of the reviews for this place before we left....harsh. I have to admit being concerned that either my guaranteed reservation wouldn't be honored or the place would be a dump. To my delight this hotel was wonderful. We stayed here for only two nights on our way in and out of PHL. Everything was clean, the decor looked rich. The first night was great, we were so tired flying in from Anchorage, AK, once we hit those comfortable beds, nothing but the wake-up call in the morning woke us. On our way back, we had the opportunity to eat at the hotel restaurant. Very good food, and the service was great. Some people might think the food is pricey, but it was comparable to what we pay in Anchorage for a similar meal in a casual restaurant. All in all, this hotel was exactly what I expected from a Hilton, we will definitely be staying with Hilton again when we travel.

title: “Terrific place”
text: We chose this hotel because it allows pets and had a smoking room -- for some reason, that combo was in short supply. Also, it allowed cancellations up to 6 p.m., which is important to us because we sometimes get sidetracked and want to stop somewhere else. This hotel was not our first choice -- the somewhat low rate ($74) almost scared us into thinking it wasn't very nice, because most others in the area charged $100+. But we were delighted with the room -- very clean, though it showed a few signs of wear. The bathroom in particular was very basic, with none of the luxuries we've come to expect (hair dryer, shampoo, lotion, fancy showerhead that never works right). But the beds were extremely comfortable, the staff was friendly and helpful, and the hotel just looked nice as we drove up -- grounds were beautifully landscaped (with a dog you get to see all those things), even though it was an airport hotel. After 12 hours on the road, good first impressions are very comforting. The kitchenette was a nice plus though we didn't use it -- it made the room bigger and cheerier. We look forward to staying here again.

title: “Excellent Retreat at Omni”
text: Unfortunately I only spent one night in the beautiful hotel for a short retreat but everything was wonderful. The room itself was most spectacular, the art work, the beds, furniture and tv couldn't have been nicer. There is even a tv embedded in the mirror of the bathroom! I didn't get a chance to try the restaurants although every meal was catered to our group and it was very good. All meals were buffet style and the service staff was most accomodating. After having the service of the Hotel 1000 in Seattle, I don't think any hotel will ever live up to that. The check-in was sufficient, yet it wasn't like I was someone special, like that of Hotel 1000. My expectations of service will never be the same! I did get to have a spa treatment, a massage, which was very relaxing an my therapist was awesome!

title: “Rich History - Modern Hip Rooms”
text:
What an amazing little gem of a place!
Found this place on a whim - had no reservations and got a decent rate.
This is another fine example of how an older hotel is revamped into something hip & new!
Each room is decorated with an eye for design & detail. Very clean & modern.
The hotel has a way cool glittery elevator too.. Everything is done right here!
Staff was very helpful. If you are there to sleep, make sure to opt for a room not directly over the pool. If you're a history buff, you'll appreciate reading about the history of this hotel which is documented on the wall, just between the lobby and bar.
Restaurant has great food too.
Convenient location if you need to be close to the airport.

title: “Old wordly charm!”
text:
Beautiful hotel and lobby, room was very large and centrally located to everything. Rooms could be updated soonish though. Concierge arranged my ticket to see Chicago White Sox, with full instructions on how to get there, tips etc. I arranged architecture walking tours myself on the advice of concierge also, as its just around the corner from the hotel.
TIP
Brilliant bakery downstairs (not in the hotel complex) for coffee, cookies, soups, panini's etc

title: “Ichiban convention”
text: Staff very friendly. Nice convention center and lobby. Takes about 15 minutes to walk to epicneter. Rooms needed some touching up but other then that a great place to stay

title: “Leaves a lot to be desired!”
text: I stayed at the Broadway Plaza Hotel in November 2006 for a business trip. The hotel is in a marginal area of the city, which appears quite deserted and seedy in the evenings. The hotel is obviously much older, but appears to have recently been remodeled. It was very clean, but seemed a bit rundown. The continental breakfast consisted of danish, bagels, and doughnuts served in a tiny room with very few tables. The hotel has no restaurant and no bar. There are also very few upscale or even midscale restaurants in close vicinity. This is definitely NOT a place that I would choose to stay again, even for the low price. With the Broadway Plaza, you get what you pay for...

title: “Super Cool inAustin”
text:
Stayed at the hotel during the recent record heatwave and was blown away by the positive vibe the front door crew had given the sauna they were working in. 
We were inside away from the inferno and thank god the hotels air conditioning was excellent keeping it beautifully chilly. Great staff in the lounge where we spent quite abit of time, excellent service but down to earth and genuinely super approachable, "real" people. The food was fab, great leading edge stuff and plenty of "good ol" comfort food. They have a clear tomato juice "Bloody Mary" with horseradish ice cubes that is INSANELY good. At around 8pm we were advised by the staff to walk down to the river behind the hotel, (took less than a minute) to see the famous bats head out for the night. A very very cool sight. After that the concierge dialed us to head out, sending us off to the warehouse district to a bunch of bars and then the Continental for live music. We were completely blown away by the venues and the bands all of which were just 5 minutes from the hotel. Just a fabulous night in Austin that I've always wanted to do and a "bucket list" experience tick off that we are all very likely to repeat.

title: “Great Place to stay.”
text: This hotel/hostel is definitely one of the best i have been to. I like the location, service was really good, people at the reception were always willing to help. There is nice kitchen with fridge where you can prepare your own meal, I was staying in the room for 2, which i find really good for that price. I booked this palce 2 motnhs ahead, for 47 usd per night, which is not bad for the location. Would definitely come again.

title: “We Will Be Back”
text:
A great small hotel with such friendly and helpful staff. We enjoyed it so much more than a large impersonal hotel.
The location was great - near Union Square, shopping and Cable Car stops. As a result we were amazed at how quiet our suite was - we had taken earplugs just in case. We were awake early due to jet lag and the complimentary coffee and newspaper were ideal to start the day until we were ready to meet the world.
We had no problems during our stay but all the contact we had with staff was friendly and efficient. Our kids particularly loved Max who is the receptionist Jeffrey's Pug. He definitely adds a real homely touch and even has his own face book page.
Due to its size, the hotel does not offer a huge range of amenities but what they do offer they do well and touches such as a complimentary glass of wine in the evening were very welcome.
We would stay here again.

title: “Nice, but pricey hotel”
text: The Hyatt is a very clean hotel with nicely updated rooms. The location is the best part - within walking distance to most major Austin sites. 6th street is a 6 block walk, the capital is practically within sight, & the bat bridge is right out your window (depending on what side of the hotel you're on). (Warning: If you want to see the nightly bat display, be prepared - they don't always put on a show! We waited 2 hours & finally saw them leave the bridge around 10pm, when it was too dark to see anything! We could only see them by looking up at a street light & watching them fly overhead.) The SoCo area of Austin, where the hotel is located, is a great spot for a hotel. BUT...the hotel is very pricey for what you get, which isn't much other than a room! No free breakfast (although we got free breakfast b/c of a AAA special, & the breakfast was really good), parking is $10/night (valet $15), bottles of water in your room are $4.25. Overall you pay a high price for a pretty basic room, but no other complaints about the hotel.

title: “Élan hotel near Beverly Center”
text: I stayed here several times and always like it. The hotel is small and quiet. There is a continental breakfast and wine and cheese. Staff is very helpful. Rooms a clean and modern. One caution parking is expensive but valet is very speedy.

title: “Great stay”
text: Arriving late into Phoenix, we made a good choice in this hotel. A social hour was going on with enough great food that we didn't need to get our tired bones to a restaurant and could just relax and enjoy the free food and drinks. Others in our party were arriving even later and instead of leaving to pick them up in our rental car, the free shuttle delivered them to the door in minutes. We had a pleasant, quiet room and the lobby and pool were beautiful. The staff was helpful and always had a smile. The hotel was very reasonably priced. We would stay again and we have added them to our list of places to stay.

title: “Great Visit!”
text: Location is wonderful--walking distance to great attractions. Room was HUGE, linens were much better than expected--especially towels--big and fluffy--not usual in a large chain hotel. Staff was polite and welcoming and my room was spotless and well kept all week. I loved the walk in closet and extra space for getting ready in the dressing area. Be sure to check out Serious Pie for a pizza while you are there--room service or right across the street! I'd recommend Hotel Andra to a business or leisure traveler. It was a great week!

title: “outstanding staff!”
text: I spent almost a month at the Crowne Plaza under unusual circumstances: I was directing a theatrical production at the nearby St. Joseph's University, and just before arriving I fractured my left kneecap, so was on crutches the entire time. The hotel's location a couple of miles from the campus was excellent, and during my long stay I experienced many aspects of the place. The outstanding aspect of the hotel was the staff: without fail everyone was friendly and helpful, going out of their way to be kind and make things easier for me--opening doors, saving a copy of the local newspaper in the morning, not minding the way I needed to sit in the restaurant, getting cabs, letting me use the service elevator to get to the laundry room--always treating me like a guest, not a burden. Especially outstanding were bellmen Dean Kenner and Ben Rayburn and restaurant staff Serinah Thompson and Mac Chowdhury, but truly everyone was great, even when the hotel was full and everyone was busy. The restaurant has good food at reasonable prices, too.

title: “Slowly Going Down Hill”
text: This used to be one of the better airport hotels. It isn't anymore. The first change that I really don't like is the airport shuttle is shared with other hotels. What this now provides you is a longer wait for the shuttle and when it does arrive it is full. After waiting to go back to LAX the hotel staff told me they had no control when it would come and taxis are available for $20 (for a 2 minute ride). The staff here has also become less than pleasant, even in the platinum lounge. You know it's bad when you give them a tip & they don't even smile or acknowledge you the next day. Many of the reviews here comment on the slow elevators, so I will just say a five minute wait to get to the lobby is typical here. I ate at the hotel bar each night and the food was very inconsistent, even for the same meal. BBQ shrimp was good one night, lousy the next. I do think the rooms here are pretty good. Flat panel TV with a good selection of channels. Given all the negatives, I would only consider this hotel again if I could get it for under $100 a night.

title: “Wee-ooo wee-ooo wee-ooo”
text:
That's the sound of the firetrucks that go by on a regular basis... all... night... long..., otherwise, excellent, attentive staff, nice bed, all the necessities. Inexpensive with a view of night-time goings on across the street. Window coverings not appropriate for a hotel, they are just wood blinds that don't provide much darkening, nor privacy when the room next door has windows facing yours.
Unusual restaurant in building, offers adventurous choices.

title: “Horrible!! Terrible!! Don't Stay There!!”
text:
No coffee cups. Front desk said they don't have any. I go to breakfast area and find coffee cups .No remote for TV. Waited hours for that. No HOT WATER for nearly 6 hours last night. I have never been in a hotel that ran out of hot water. Numerous calls to the front desk brought no results. They kept telling me any minute. Finally at 2:00 am I gave up on my shower and went to bed.
People are dealing drugs in this hotel. People parking cars, running in, running out. You wouldn't believe the types of people I saw in this hotel. I will have to contact the Memphis PD. I am requesting a refund. It was a horrible experience and it was my birthday celebration. 
There are no blankets on the bed. We had a king size bed with 3 pillows........shouldn't there be 4 pillows on a king bed? You sleep with the flat sheet and the bedspread. The bathroom door was broken. Not enough towels or shampoo. People yelling in the hallway. Yelling in the parking lot. Trash all over the place. 
Horrible, horrible.

title: “Loved the room. Service could have been much better.”
text:
We stayed here for one night before an early morning flight. The room was fantastic (big, clean, cool decor, big bathroom, great amenities) and the beds very comfortable (firm mattress and lots of pillows). I don't usually sleep well before a very early flight - but slept like a log this time around. There is some noise from the airport (planes landing and taking off). However this is to be expected given the proximity and you should bring earplugs if you're a light sleeper. 
We used the internet access both on our two netbooks (in the room and in the lobby) and on the supplied PCs in the lobby. No issues connecting or working. 
My only complaint would be that services wasn't what I would have expected. Getting information (example: shuttle departure times) felt like pulling teeth. At a place like this, I would expect more than a two word answer and wouldn't expect to have the exact same thing repeated to me again when I asked for more details. When we were leaving in the morning there was no one at reception to check us out and we came very close to missing our shuttle (we were there with plenty of time to spare). Not cool given this airport is geared towards airport layovers. I'm typically very low maintenance when it comes to service - but thought the aloft staff were way too sloppy and this didn't match the quality of the rest of the experience. Maybe we were just there on a bad day... (As an aside, the shuttle drivers were great. Friendly, accommodating and timely.)
As others have mentioned, on-site food options are limited and expensive. But once again, this is pretty typical of airport hotels.
I would stay here again.

title: “Awesome Hotel- now part of the Marriott chain.”
text:
This hotel is now formally a Fairfield Inn and Suites, one of the Marriott brands. I have been an occasional business customer over the years and wouldn't hesitate to be a repeat customer. Yes, renovation continues, but what the critics don't mention is how much improvement in the property can be bought with 4.5 million dollars. 
The makeover is impressive, and you're met with a lobby that has been completely renovated. It's bright, welcoming, and user friendly, with a business work area that includes computers, internet access, printing capacity, etc. Check in was responsive and fast, as was checkout. In the interim I experienced their breakfast offering, which was more than adequate. In addition to the requisite cereal, bagels, OJ, etc. they offer the capacity to make waffles and have a selection of Jimmy Dean Bacon or Sausage and Egg muffins that can be microwaved. 
The rooms have been totally re-done and they are comfortable, roomy, and very nicely appointed. Mine came with a King sized bed, a comfortable easy chair and ottoman, a work desk and chair that were very comfortable and functional, the usual flat panel cabled TV, new carpeting, a small fridge and microwave, and all the other amenities that usually come with a room (coffee maker, hair dryer, etc.). Internet access was easy and the signal was strong. 
My room overlooked the courtyard, and that was especially impressive. New french doors ensure a clear view of the courtyard but if you are so inclined you can open them, access a small balcony, and take in the sights and sounds below, to include the water fountain, palm trees, flowers and bushes, etc. The pool and sauna areas have been renovated as well, and are in the courtyard itself. 
As regards my interaction with the staff and the manager of the hotel, I was impressed. They were always responsive, friendly and accommodating and certainly made me feel at home while away from home. 
Lastly, and the real kicker, is their location, which is directly adjacent to Old Town. I would estimate a walk of no more than two or three blocks to get into Old Town. The property is just off I-5 but you won't notice noise from the highway. The entire property is "gated" so you should feel safe, with the surrounding area being upscale and very nice.
I would highly recommend this hotel to the business traveler, to families and to those who want a pleasant stay with very nice accommodating staff. It's location is ideal and the improvements to the property are impressive.

title: “Excellent Family Destination”
text:
This facility has all the amenities needed to keep a young family busy and occupied. Location is close by to other popular kid related facilities. Staff was very courteous and helpful. 
The only downside is I would not recommend this as a quiet getaway for folks without children.

title: “Excellent value boutique hotel”
text: This is one of the best value hotels we have stayed in in New York. The rooms are smallish (though no more so than elsewhere in Manhattan), but this is offset by so many little touches that make this place stand out: complimentary bottled water is left in the room each night; complimentary wine and cheese every night in the lobby; complimentary tea, coffee, and filtered water is always available in the lobby together with a selection of newspapers (and little surprises like a tray of marshmallows when we came back on Tuesday night); complimentary tickets are available to the local NYSC gym (you can even go along to their studio classes). The service is also smart and attentive (noticeably better on this trip than on our previous stay, two years ago, when it was bit more casual).

title: “User Friendly”
text:
Good value on an older Suites style hotel. This Place is clean and the rooms are spacious. Kitchens are adequately stocked, Refrigerator and dishes were clean. Combine this with easy access and a friendly staff and you have a user friendly hotel.
This place shows its age and the Maintenance crew (If one exists) needs improvement. Housekeeping is very good.
Still it's often about location, service and value. This place should be considered.

title: “Funky... Modern... and fun!”
text: I loved the Hudson. It was funky... modern... and fun! It was a very small room, but it was clean. The location was great and the decorations were fun! I would stay here again!

title: “Enjoyed our stay”
text: Stayed at the Inn at the Park for three nights in early September and we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. The location is excellent, walkable to all that Balboa Park has to offer and also to Hillcrest. Room was comfortable, had a balcony with excellent city and bay views. Enjoyed the new room decor, a little funky but everything was good, nice bed and housekeeping does excellent job. Would have given hotel 5 stars, but renovation is not complete so some things in the room were not working as of yet. Overall had an excellent stay and would return next time we are in San Diego. Thanks Katelyn and the very friendly staff.

title: “Very classy hotel”
text: Stayed here 2 nights. Extremely comfortable and classy hotel. Rooms were very spacious and modern. The bed was super comfortable and plush. The bathroom was very big and featured a double-headed shower, which is always good after a long day sightseeing. From our hotel room, you could see the Capitol Building. It was situated close to Union Station and bus routes. The staff on hand were more than helpful, and helped make our stay just that little bit better. There was a restaurant on site, but we found it a little pricey. Although we had no need for it, there were business amenities on site. Given the close proximity to tourist sites, the street was relatively quiet at night. Although it was on the expensive end of our budget, it was a good hotel and we would stay here again.

title: “Good location but needs improvement”
text:
We've spent 5 nights there with our little baby and our cousins. The location is awesome since the hotel is 10 min to Times Square, 5 min to Central Park and 5th avenue. The subway station is just a few steps away. There is a Starbucks next door. Therefore it's very convenient to stay there especially with a baby.
The room is big enough, the bathroom is OK, generally clean and comfortable but the heating system is a complete problem! It's very noisy when you turn it on and it gets so hot in the evening that you need to turn if off and it gets freezing! Adjusting is impossible.
There is no coffee machine or a refrigerator in the room.
The elevators are a mess too. You press your floor number first and you wait and wait... Especially it's so slow when you wait on your floor. Imagine you have a stroller and you can't use the stairs! It gets really frustrating.
And last point is the lobby. It was so crowded each time, not different from Times Square. I have no idea why all those people were hanging out there and I doubt if they are all hotel customers.

title: “Make sure you check your statement on checkout!”
text:
Precursor: I have been a Gold Starwood Preferred Guest Member since 2006 and I stay at Westin Hotels frequently.
Cleanliness: During our stay the room was cleaned daily and we were provided fresh linens and replacement soaps in a consistent and timely manner. The hallways and lobby also appeared well kept. The windows overlooking the promenade could use a good Windex by housekeeping.
Location: I was in-town for a conference and this was one of the recommended hotels. The hotel is located in the financial district. During the week the streets were very busy and the hotel was within convenient walking distance to buses and other ground transportation. We also stayed through the weekend and the area became very quiet. The hotel is in a good location if you have business in the area but the hotel would not be my first choice if I was visiting San Fran on holiday. There are a lot of comparable hotels in closer vicinity to the attractions.
Rooms: We stayed in a Gold Starwood Preferred Guest suite. The room was what we expected for a Westin Hotel room.
Service: Front desk was very friendly and professional. Management could revisit the concierge desk. The gentleman that assisted us with our weekend excursions was not friendly, at all, and gave us the impression we were bothering him. Either he was clearly in the wrong job or he was having a bad day. 
Value: I used Starwood Points for the week which I believe was 10,000 points a night. The weekend rate was $129.00 which was a terrific rate against comparable hotels. The discounted weekend rate is likely because of its location in the financial district which becomes very quiet on the weekends.
Sleep Quality: Bed was very comfortable and thermostat worked fine.
Overall: I would "consider" staying at this Westin San Francisco Market Street again but I am not completely sold. I think I read somebody's review, prior to staying there, to put an additional set of eyes on the bill before checking out. I was also warned by the front desk person to double check the statement and sure enough there were multiple charges made to my room from the restaurant, parking garage and Internet service. It was a bit ridiculous. The front desk person removed the charges but I was still charged for parking later on. I did not even rent a car. I put it on my AMEX so they are handling for me but I think management should definitely have a discussion with Accounting as this could be a detractor for future travelers considering a stay at the hotel.

title: “Excellent”
text: Excellent hotel. Room was great with good storage and big bathroom (lovely toiletries replenished every day). Housekeeping excellent and room was lovely and clean (and warm). Location is great. Right next to the Empire State Building (which we could see from our bedroom window) and Macy's. Reception staff were very helpful. Business centre good for easy access to emails. We did not have breakfast in the hotel but did enjoy free coffee from the lobby in the morning. We did have breakfast at The Brooklyn Diner, The Oxford (just round the corner from hotel) and Cafe Metro - all were excellent. All the sights were in walking distance but subway is next to hotel if you need it and taxis are all over New York. We walked most places and took a taxi a few times. I would highly recommend visiting the Empire State Building not only for the view but the inside is fantastic art deco. We went at 8am Sunday morning (no queues). Top of The Rock - fantastic views (evening). Also visited The Grand Central Station (wonderful), and the World Trade Centre Memorial Centre (very emotional). Went to Little Italy, Soho, Central Park, Greenwich (all really good and different architecture to see). Would highly recommend Ellen's Stardust Diner at Times Square for a fun way to eat. We also bought tickets from the TKT booth - half price to see Mary Poppins (seats were ten rows from the front). As others have commented I would recommend walking over the Brooklyn Bridge in the evening and waiting till half way over till you look behind at the Manhattan Skyline. Awesome!! South Street (Pier 17) good for shopping and of course Macys and Bloomingdales. We also took the Staten Island Ferry (free) to see the Statue of Liberty up close. Wonderful city.

title: “Fabulous White Swan Inn”
text: Wonderfull Inn, awsome decorating, large room and the best breakfast (included in your rate) you could ask for. The downstairs living rooms were spacious and well appointed, free sodas, water, wine and cheese daily. Couldn't ask for a nicer hotel or staff. Close to everything in San Francisco and reasonable rates. This is a must go to Inn and my wife and I will be returning. Couldn't have asked for better.

title: “Successful meeting started with a great stay”
text:
If you're planning a sales meeting, the Roosevelt is the place to stay. Great location, walking distance to Pikes Place Market, and restaurants. We had 25 people stay here and the rooms were great, but the meeting accomodations were even better. We had a personal asssitant with the hotel to help us with any technology and food and drink. 
Very impressed with the friendly staff and accomodations. This hotel has a buzz that led to a great envirnment for our meeting. Highly recommend you have your meetings here.
Areas Sales Manager

title: “It was OK”
text: Just remember, you get what you pay for. The hotel is a place to sleep and clean up. There is a pool but not much else. The room was clean and the bed comfortable enough for sleep. The hotel is close to the airport so it is noisy from time to time. However, if you are looking for an economical place to stay that is close to Graceland and close to downtown, then this fits the bill.

title: “Modern new hotel”
text:
Stayed here for a quick 1-night stay before an OSU football game and would definitely come back. The hotel is very new in an industrial part of town that is being modernized. There's nothing nearby in terms of a neighborhood or restaurants, but the hotel itself is beautiful.
It's a very short drive to the OSU campus or to the Short North neighborhood for restaurants. Our double queen room had a large sitting area with a desk. The sink is outside of the bathroom which is a feature I always appreciate. A very nice hot breakfast was served including breakfast "mcmuffin" sandwiches, fruit, yogurt and cereals. The hotel ran a shuttle to OSU game.

title: “Love the green incentive”
text: Stayed for three nights as part of a conference. Nice size rooms and amenities in the room. I loved the fact that they offer you $5.00 green incentive for not having your room clean every day. I hope that more hotels do that to encourage green ideas. Comfortable bed overall I would come back. Internet was not as good as one would hope but the hotel addressed it right away.

title: “Budget hotel that wants to be Boutique.”
text:
I can handle a tiny room and an inconvenient bathroom with no storage and an elevator that literally took 15 minuets to come and even to a certain extent, a loud room, but uncomfortable bed/pillows is just unacceptable. You don't get much for your buck in NYC but I would, if nothing else, expect a comfortable bed; not even a large bed, just one that doesn't feel like it was made from various sized rocks shoved inside a mattress. It isn't a backpackers. Sleeping out on the sidewalk would have been more comfortable. We complained, asked if we could change rooms but were told it was too hard to upgrade as we were staying to long. (Didn't ask to upgrade - obviosuly $300 per night doesn't warrant a comfortable bed, you have to upgrade for that?) In the end were given one spare pillow and an extra sheet for the bed, which fixed the problem about as well as you might imagine.
It was also INCREDIBLY loud, they obviously haven't heard of soundproofing for outside or between rooms. One poor guest near the elevator had a hand written sign begging people to be quiet. I wore earplugs most nights. 
Some staff were very helpful, others couldn't be bothered.
On the bright side, the location was good, and safe. Immediate area was not very pleasing but over by Gramercy Park is beautiful. Great proximity to Noho/Soho/the village/chelsea and the great restaurants/shopping/markets in those areas. Internet lounge upstairs is very useful and rooftop garden is a nice addition.
Overall I thought it was pretty low value for what it was. A budget room with a zebra print cushion and matching lamp does not a boutique hotel make. Next time I would still stay downtown, but closer to Chelsea. 
Probably perfect for someone on a short trip who is planning to pass out rather than sleep, where comfort isn't a major concern.

title: “Brilliant!!!!!”
text:
What a lovely hotel. This was our first time in NY and we cant wait to go back. We arrived on Fri 1st Dec around 5.30pm, to find our room wasn't ready, all though we only had to wait around 10 mins i would of expected us to be able to go straight in. Never the less the reception were lovely, they made us welcome with friendly smiles and the door men are brilliant. They are really helpful and will get you taxis, book helicopters flights, do anything you need - obviously they expect a tip after!! But they make the stay all the better.
We had booked a king size suite and that it was!! It was massive. The front room was huge with dining table at the end of it. The tv was gigantic! The kitchen was small and dated but then we only used it for the fridge and kettle. We weren't planning on eating in any night! The bathroom again is small but lovely and clean. The bedroom was huge. The bed was gigantic and could of fit 4 of us!!! It was so comfy i didn't want to get out. We had loads of cupboards/wardrobes space. We faced out onto the street which we loved. All though u can here the traffic late at night we didn;t mind as we wanted to watch it all going on. If your a light sleeper then i;d ask for a room at the back if noise bothers you. We'd had a few drinks before going to bed so we slept through it. 
Mon - Thurs they have free wine, coffee etc on the 2nd floor which is a nice touch, all though we didn't go there.
This hotel is in a great location for anyone to get about NY city. The hotel doesn't have a restaurant like most of them dont, but with the cafe a few doors down delivering to the hotel free of charge your sorted for breakfast. 
We would def come back and stay at this hotel and recommend it to anyone

title: “Great hotel in centre of town”
text: My wife and I are in early 60s from Australia. Booked hotel in conjunction with Extranomical tours. The room was quiet (ask for internal facing) but rather small. Staff and housekeeping v friendly and accommodating. B'fast was help yourself to toast, danish and coffee etc. Fabulous location for touring city, just stones throw from cable car terminus and right in Union sq shopping precinct. Recommended.

title: “color ful”
text:
it waas colorful n bright hotel.we syayed in a standered double room,it was a good room,with city, courtyard,river view,double bed,wi-fi, flat tv,in room spa serviece,the bar was good with nice interior,cafereria ,library were really very gud.there was a private park with antique and modern garden furniture. i really liked the 
sky terraces Located on the 15th floor, it is the perfect combination of sweeping city and Hudson River views

title: “I loved it the staff was GREAT and service was EXCELLENT”
text: I stayed at the Lenox Hotel for my birthday. I had a hard time deciding which hotel to go to but in the end the Lenox seemed like the best option. I have stayed in a lot of good hotels but I will say the Hotel staff is among the best I have experienced. When I checked in they called me 15 mins after check in to make sure I was happy with my room. They left me champagne and chocolate for my Birthday with a letter. I ordered room service and it was good and came very quickly despite the fact that it was 2 AM. Everyone was so nice I felt like I was at home. My only complaint was that the room was pretty small but everything was clean and the Aveda toiletries were excellent. I would definately go back! Suggest trying to get an upgraded room if possible.

title: “An elegant hotel in the ideal location."”
text:
Our 3-day stay at The Taj Boston was at the end of a wonderful Holland America cruise from Montreal to Boston. The Taj's location could not be better, just across from the Public Garden, with the Boston Common just beyond. 
Our room, 707, was ideally located facing the Public Garden, with views of the trees, just starting to change color, and a peek of the gold dome of the State House. It was a spacious well-appointed room. The windows actually opened -- fresh air! The hotel staff was unfailingly courteous and helpful.
From the Taj you can walk to most of the historic sites. We used the Boston Trolley HO-HO for an overview of Boston, and to get some of the more distant places we wanted to see.
Our favorite dining venue was "Finale", about 2 blocks away, where they specialize in incredible desserts, preceded by light entrees called "Preludes". Casual ambiance and perfect dining choices for our tastes.

title: “Memorable experience at the remarkable St. Regis Washington, D.C.”
text: The St. Regis is known for it's "above and beyond" service, their attention to detail and the intimate feel you receive from the surroundings as well as the people. That being said, having stayed at other St. Regis properties, the St. Regis Washington D.C. was by far my favorite! The location is spectacular (right down the street from the white house), the accommodations are truly elegant, but the people are exquisite. The associates in all facets met every need, want and desire. We were greeted by a welcoming Front Desk Associate upon our arrival, the lobby bar associates were instinctive and friendly. We had the joy of meeting Alvin and learning about the pearl making process for the bubbly they serve there, and the Oh, the coffee is absolutley delicious! Best coffee I've had in a long time and I'm from Seattle!! I'd also like to highlight the "trail berry" or "berry trail" martinis, as they are devine! We met Ammar Samad, Director of Rooms, who was absolutely pleasant & charismatic beyond words and he ensured our stay was perfection. Leslie, the concierge gave the perfect recommendations on what to see in just a short, yet packed, weekend. Leslie was genuinely helpful in every way. All in all, it's one of the best trips I've had, even in the frigid D.C. weather, and the reason it was so enjoyable was after a long day of sight seeing, walking and soaking up as much of beautiful D.C. as possible, we knew we had a beautiful, serene, & comforting place waiting for us upon our return. Thank you to everyone at the Washington D.C. St. Regis as you made our first visit to D.C. truly memorable. We will return!

title: “Would definitely stay again!”
text: Booked this hotel at expedia.com for a pretty good price for 2 nights. This hotel was rather cheap which honestly scared me, I figured it must be run down to be in NYC and so affordable, but boy was I wrong. The outside of the building looks like an average tall building in Wall Street. The inside is very elegant and clean. The rooms are amazing!! I would definitely reccommend this hotel for a quick 1-3 night stay or if you're going to be in the city but outside your hotel most of the time. The beds are very comfortable, a lot of news channels on the tv, the rooms very clean, as were the hallways and elevators. I would definitely book this hotel again!

title: “Location,Location,Location”
text: Fab old traditional hotel overlooking cantral park, I was a little bit apprehesive at first after reading some of the reviews. But what a pleasent suprise. Rooms were large and clean no wall paper hanging off a little dated but that added to it's charm.The beds were so comfortable I slept like a log every night. I wouln't hesitate to go back.

title: “Perfect Location”
text:
If you're not looking for amazing views out your window, Four Points Sheraton in Soho is in a great location. It's located on the West Side right near the 1 train that takes you uptown, if you please, or downtown, if that's where you're headed. It's also walking distance to the West Side Highway for great water views and if you go in the opposite direction, you'll head into fashionable Soho and Broadway -- a shopper's delight. 
The hotel is very clean, beds were very comfortable and for me it was a plus since my office is right down the block.
I will mention that when I got there the toilet was not flushing. On my way out I asked the front desk to have them take a look at it and by the time I got back, it was taken care of.

title: “Good Stay”
text:
In light of the other reviews on this site I didn't know what to expect when staing at this property. I stayed at this location as a result of almost all hotels being full when I was booking last minute.
The hotel was a bit dated and did show it's age. However the room was adequate with 2 queens and in reality the beds were very comfortable. The carpets like another review indicated are not so hot because of the cheap carpet they used you can see stains and such. Over all, the room was satisfactory for the cheap rate we paid.

title: “Great price, great location, friendly staff”
text: I just finished my second stay at the Wash. Square Hotel and it was great, once again. Yes, the rooms are small, but that's NYC. However, the rooms are clean, well-styled, and the beds are comfortable. Secondly, the price and location are hard to beat. I stayed for three nights for $205 a night, before tax, in a lovely and easily accessible part of the city where I felt safe wandering around late at night discovering new places. Thirdly, the staff is wonderful, as they are all helpful and welcoming. I can't comment on the continental breakfast that they serve because I didn't eat there in the morning due to my work schedule. Sure, it's fun to find new places in which to stay in NYC, but I like this hotel and would be happy to stay there again.

title: “Great stat at a new, hip hotel.”
text: I really enjoyed my stay at this dog-friendly hotel. The staff were very nice and the room and common areas were very clean. There is a restaurant/bar on the first floor. My steak was so-so, but the rest of the meal was great. If you don't mind walking four blocks, you can get to the San Diego strip (5th Ave.). I wish there were a microwave and fridge in my room, but the nice amenities made up for it. One request: please make over-the-counter meds (aspirin, benedryl, etc.) available at the front desk. I was told I could walk 3 blocks to CVS for meds, but that's not acceptable when you are sick. This hotel is a great value and I would recommend it to my friends.

title: “Peerless”
text:
As and when I retire, the Carlyle stands every chance of being my new home. I have stayed there countless times and it is flawless. Service is outstanding in every respect, the staff are friendly, greet one by name and are extremely good at what they do. 
I now gravitate between two rooms in the Tower, both of which have recenlty been refurbished and with their jaw dropping views over Central Park and beyond are just fabulous. Are they full of gizmos and gadgets? No thank God, they are the bedrooms of an owner with exquisite taste.
The bar, the cafe, the restaurant are all outstanding in every respect and again with outstanding service with great classic and simple food, perfectly presented. The cafe buzzes with its line up of evening cabaret and I don't think I have ever seen a bad performance. Most recently Sutton Foster and Judy Collins offered two very different evenings but both were brilliant and brought the place alive.
The spa is very good with great therapists and great amenities.
My only gripe is that I don't think their laundry service is as good as it could be, shirts come back without that refreshed look and perfect press that say the George V delivers in Paris. Please make that one small improvement and I shall be ready to move in for good.

title: “Great location, poor service.”
text:
I'll start with the good - location was unbeatable. We had a rental car but didn't use it for the first day and a half of our 4 day stay because you can walk to so much around Fisherman's Wharf or take trolley/cable car to some sights.
The concierge was friendly and very helpful.
That's it for the good.
When we checked in we were told that our adjoining room request was not going to be honored because someone extended their stay and, "there's nothing I can do for you". That changed to "i can move you tomorrow" when I suggested that I would check back in the morning for an adjoining room or find another hotel. So we were in a total of four rooms while staying here - each room had hair in the tub (from the previous guest), and one had hair on the bathroom floor - even as a guy I think that's gross.
The sleep number beds are awful, even if you want a soft bed, the ridge around the outside of the bed stays hard and with two people in the beds you need the outside of the bed!
The rooms are beaten down - one of the first rooms we were in had a sink in the bathroom that was coming off the wall and the exhaust fan was broken in one of the other bathrooms. They were all small rooms...I know hotel rooms are small, but these seemed very small.
The front desk service was poor - my kids independently nicknamed the woman who checked us in "Happy Jack".
There was enough here that even for the stellar location, I would not recommend this hotel or stay here when we go back to San Francisco. We paid $189 night for two rooms and I expected better for the price and the name.

title: “GREAT SERVICE and GREAT HOTEL for the Convention Center”
text:
This convention was on my own bucks. Couldn't afford the Hyatt, Sheraton, etc. and am not an status member.
Booked the Roosevelt on Priceline and got a great rate for the convention. When I checked in Caleb and Patrick at the fron desk get me a great room and made me feel like I was a VIP traveler. Simple things helping me with the business center and just the overall "can do" attitude blew my expectations away. 
If you are going to the convention center and need a great value, this is the place. Great restaurant with good food and good value, too.

title: “Great Location - Room adequate”
text: I booked one night on Orbitz & called to add another night. We paid $147 per night. The location is great - right in the middle of everything. The room iwas very, very small. We booked a "King" size room thru Orbitz. When we got to our room, it was a queen. When we went to the front desk, they said they didn't have king rooms. We paid $10 more for the king. We told the front desk but didn't even acknowledge it. I have since gone on the Orbitz site and they have removed the "king" room. The bed took up the whole room. The bathroom was very small but extremely clean. Our room was right next to the stairway and it just happened that there was some kind of run/walk going on the next day. The walls are paper thin and the runners were on the stairs at 5:00am. Our room looked out at a brick wall. No air but didn't need it. We learned real quick that San Francisco is not very warm, my husband ended up buying a winter jacket! There was a couple checking out the day after we checked in. They did not have a working toilet for the 2 days that they were there. There were no other rooms available and the hotel offered them $20 off a night. The couple said it was not acceptable but the girl at the desk did not back down. They left with an open credit card bill until the manager could get back to them. Would we stay again? Probably not - there are other hotels nearby.

title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text:
The service and the staff of this hotel is outstanding.
The location cannot be beaten in downtown Chicago.

title: “Good, solid hotel - just not an impressive one.”
text:
This hotel is solid - they provide the basics just as they should. However, its just missing that "wow" factor to make it an impressive one. The rooms were clean, maid service was timely and everything in my room was functional. The staff, while efficient, just didn't have that "pop" to make it a great property. While they weren't rude, it felt like they were just going through the motions to provide check-in/check-out service to us. We called for an airport shuttle and were told it would take 20 minutes. It took 40. We arrive and the desk clerk checked us in, but it took 15 minutes for two rooms. The only noticeable exception - the conceriege when he was at his post. He knew the area extremely well and guided us to perfect restaurants and shopping. However, we tried to visit him six times - only two times was he at his post.
Overall, a solid, well-functioning hotel. Just not one that will stand out in our minds.

title: “Great value, Conveniently located”
text: Property has been very well maintained and rooms recently renovated. Al aspects of the stay were very good. Rooms very comfortable and clean. Lobby areas very well maintained and very clean, Grounds very well kept. Very friendly and helpful staff that have been trained in guest service. Free breakfast had nice selection although could be improved,

title: “Surprisingly terrible”
text: I have been staying at Holiday Inns (and other InterContinental Hotels Group brand hotels) frequently over the last 3 years, and this is the first time I have been disappointed. In fact, I have stayed at this location previously and was pleased with it. This trip, I was disappointed to find this location has deteriorated. The service was mediocre, the ammenities were lacking (closed bar and other features) and it just seemed runned-down. I do not recommend this hotel for travel unless you absolutely must stay in the immediate area. There are other options not far form here within the InterContinental Hotels Group brands.

title: “Frequent Guest of Homewood Suites”
text: During 2011, I stayed at the Homewood Suites for 192 days. The staff became part of my life and I enjoyed all interactions with them. They were always courteous, professional and pleasant so I was disappointed when someone would leave. I always returned to a clean room, plenty of towels, and any assistance I needed from using the grill or having food delivered. The location is a positive along with the room set up which feels like a small apartment and not a kitchen in a bedroom. Our company required early hours and management was able to accomodate us by providing breakfast earlier than scheduled. Breakfast offered a good variety as well as the evening reception. The meal offered enough food and beverage with a great atmosphere to relax. I have spent many evenings on the patio enjoying the quiet and beautiful San Antonio breeze. I will continue to patronize Homewood Suites and recommend this hotel without hesitation.

title: “Sketchy Sketchy”
text: We arrived at this hotel for an event. When we got here it took forever to check in and the hotel staff could barely speak english. It was a hassle. We got up to our room and it wasnt that bad. We parked near our room so we could watch our old car. The bottom floor had people with barbeque grills outside there windows grilling out. We were too nervous to get into the pool because it just felt very unsafe. Later that night the halls were loud and I think someone was even knocking on our door. We looked out the window and there were tons of people in the parking lot partying. It was right down town! It was ridicilous. The kids were scared to even sleep here. It had to have been the worst we've stayed at.

title: “Amazing view and not bad for a NYC hotel”
text:
My husband and I were combing through reviews before we decided on staying at the Bentley Hotel for 3 nights. It is totally out of the way when it comes to the main attractions but it was also nice to be amongst native New Yorkers. The room was a lot roomier than expected and the bathroom was decent as well. It is a good 10-15 min walk to the nearest subway and about a 15-20 minute was to Central Park. If you are going to spend most of your time in SoHo or Times Square then I suggest booking another hotel. However, if you want a quite hotel away from the grit of the city then this is a nice hotel. As for the updating of the hotel decor, "Who Cares?" It was clean and there were no mystery stains on linens or flooring and that's all I can ask for. I would stay at the Bentley Hotel again.
On a different note, there is an amazing diner about 2 blocks away and on 60th and 1st there is a delicious Italian restaurant names Angels. (Don't quote me on the name I could be wrong.) None the less the food portions were huge and the price was very reasonable.

title: “Exactly what we needed for our holiday”
text: We stayed for 5 nights at the Hotel Stanford during October 2007. We were three 20 something girls who came to New York for a shopping trip. The hotel was exactly what we needed. It was very central, perfect location. It was 5 min walk to Macy's and 10 mins to time square. There was a subway stop right outside the hotel. For us, we basically wanted somewhere clean, safe and central and this certainly delivered. It has been recently refurbished (although not necessarily to my tastes!!!) but was spotless. The room was big enough for the 3 of us to share (2 double beds) and was very cheap. I think we paid £240 each for the 5 nights. Originally we booked for 6 nights but BA was overbooked so we got compensated £420 each to stay in london in a hotel and returned the following day to the airport with our shopping money! The hotel staff were very nice and refunded our first nights stay with proof from BA. The bathroom was very clean and new and the shower was massive with a large "raindrop" head. We stayed on the 5th floor and could not hear a thing. The air con hums at night but this was fine for us. There is a new flat screen tv in the room. Also, there was a small window which looked out to another building so you never saw any natural light but we didn't mind as we just had the room for sleeping. All in all, I would definately stay there again, especially if you want to save more money for shopping!!

title: “Want to Get Away for the Weekend in Chicago? This is your place.”
text:
We live in Chicago and decided on pampering ourselves by staying at the Trump. The room was comfortable and had an amazing view of downtown and the river. We stayed during the St Patty's Day festivities and saw the river dyed green (well, they made it greener than it usually is). The staff was friendly and attentive. We had a great meal at the restaurant on one of the upper floors and even saw a former NBA star dining with his spouse. The lounge was cool but the drinks were a little too pricey. 
In all, this is an ideal place to take your significant other to stay for the weekend in Chicago- especially when you're in the doghouse with your wife like I was! I'd definitely stay here again.

title: “An Amazing stay at The Lenox”
text:
We have just returned from an amazing five night stay at The Lenox. The first thing that greeted us was the most amazing fragrance in the lobby, the receptionist explained that it had been especially created for the hotel. The check in staff were excellent and we were promptly taken to our room. On inspection of our room we discovered we did not have a bath tub, therefore another room was available immediately and we were transfered.
The Hotel is spotlessly clean with very comfortable beds. The rooms are well appointed with, air con, flat screen TV, fridge, iron and board, hairdryer and great Aveda hair and body products, oh, and Lindt chocolates at turn down!!
What really made our stay at The Lenox extra special was the amazing team of people who work there. Everybody was polite, helpful, friendly and genuine. Jimmy (60 years service) and Vincent (20 years service) the guys in the lobby, really made us feel at home and we really had a great time chatting to them about Boston. 
We cannot wait to stay at The Lenox again in the future.

title: “Number 1 Hotel if you are going to Universal Studios!”
text: I heard mixed reviews about the hotel, but it is very nice. I have stayed in first class hotels many times and this one falls way short of that, but the price and location can't be beat. Staff greeted us warmly upon check-in, there was a free mini-buffet in the evenings at the bar, rooms were clean and ready when we arrived and there was always someone there to push the elevator button for you! The hotel was not overly large, allowing a nice feeling. Also, if you want to go to Universal Studios, you can just walk there (or take their shuttle - but remember the shuttle does not leave until 10:00 am and the park opens at 9:00. There were many people waiting outside before 9 am for the shuttle and apparently did not know.) We walked and were there in 10 minutes. Perfect for coming and going from the park!

title: “Unhelpful Front of Office Staff”
text: Not a bad hotel in general but the room cleanliness left a lot to be desired with dust all up the walls and you did not want to move the bedside table - Yuk!! However the beds were very comfy and clean and for New York a good sized room. Beware the price of drinks in the bar - $30 for 2 gin and tonics! Had a problem with the room safe and after 4 asks to have it fixed with no show of a repair man we gave up. Front desk staff very business like and robotic but the information desk were VERY helpful. Good location as 2 blocks from Central Park one way and you could see Times Square in the other direction. Also right on top of subway with access to anywhere in the city. Very good Cafe opposite called Fluffy's for fantastic breakfast

title: “Excellent Value in Houston”
text: The Holiday Inn Reliant Park is a super place to stay. Excellent customer service especially from front desk staff member David. Property is very clean, newly renovated, has a shuttle service to the Texas Medical Center and is a very reasonable price especially at the medical discount rate. Remember to bring a swimsuit because they also have a super pool.

title: “Good location for the price”
text: My wife and I stayed at the hotel at the end of May 2011 for our 1 year anniversary. The hotel was clean, well kept and had slightly bigger rooms than some of the other hotels near Times Square. We liked the location the best. It was 1 block down and 1 block over from Times Square and a block down from some great restaurants. It is only a block or so from Broadway and close enough to walk to Central Park. The only thing we didn't like was the view. This is a smaller hotel and gets dwarfed by some of the bigger buildings, but this was not a deal breaker for us.

title: “Should be named "Last Resort Motel"”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights and would have checked out after one if it wasn't for the fact that we were in a group and would have been a hassle to find something different. We had to move out of our first room because the TV didn't work, but the next room wasn't much better. The stool didn't flush properly and the tub didn't drain. The floor was sticky and dirty. There were no cups for coffee. The others in our group spoke of black stuff in the shower and clogged drains. The most offensive site was the tattered American flag out front. That should have been our clue to head down the road. Avoid this place unless it's the last resort

title: “Soulless, mediocre staff - handy for Georgetown”
text:
Had three nights here at the Westin and had it not be for the deal I had, I would have gone elsewhere. The hotel is located close to Georgetown, but in an area of DC where at the weekends there isn't a lot going on. 
The bell staff and concierge were fantastic, but sadly thats where it ended. Despite having an upgrade confirmed by the hotel, and arriving way past the usual check in time, the room had yet to be vacated and there was no hurry in getting this done so we were downgraded to a luxury room. They are ok, if a little boxy. Usual hotel standard, but nothing to write home about. They have two restaurants, both of which were soulless and no one in either. Breakfast was expensive, but no where else to go.
Won't be returning, and would recommend you found a hotel with more character and in a better position if visiting DC as a tourist.

title: “Can't Beat This Location”
text: Venerable hotel, opened 80+ years ago, but not rundown or seedy. Central location can't be beat; walking distance to Times Square, New York Public Library, more, plus easy public transportation. If I had to describe the hotel in one word, it would be Convenient. Paid $169 through Priceline.

title: “A Real Gem”
text: Every city needs a hotel like this. Clean, reasonable and friendly with all the things a traveler could want.

title: “Average stay this time”
text: I've stayed at this hotel many times for work and this time was not one of my favorites. the hotel seemed to be having issues with not having enough employees staffed when needed. My room was clean and fresh as always. One very major pain was that one morning I discovered that I had no bath towels in my room but unfortunately did not notice this until after I had already showered and was dripping wet with only a hand towel to dry off with. I needed to get to the office so had no other option. As I was leaving to go to the office, I saw a maid bringing towels to a room several doors down from me so I guess that problem was not mine alone. I also had to wait about 15 minutes the day I was checking out to get my bill. Even though I do have other options when i come to Dallas for my work trips I will probably still give them another try and hope for a better experience next time.

title: “Great hotel, excellent location”
text: We were very satisfied with this hotel. Room was of good size (for NY), clean, well decorated. Location is superb. Highly recommend it if you plan to stay in Midtown.

title: “Far better than we expected”
text: We had heard that around Fisherman's Wharf it is noisy but this hotel is tucked away a couple of blocks from the action and in an ideal position for everything. The room was excellent and the concierge very good at explaining sightseeing options. The complementery wine reception in the afternoons was very welcome and although we had booked room only we were given vouchers for continental breakfast in the very nice restaurant. We would thoroughly recommend this hotel.

title: “Great place in DC”
text: Our second visit and still one of the best in DC, especially the location just two blocks from Union Station. We arrived early and not only were we sent directly to a room, we were upgraded to King. Comfy bed, great TV, spacious bathroom with shampoo and , conditioner and bodywash dispensers in the shower. The only problem was that the minibar had too little room for us to chill our water bottles overnight; well, we took stuff out so we could. Friendly staff, complementary ice water and tea in the lobby each afternoon and weekday happy hour of wine and sangria. Easy walk to Mall museums, and Metro access at Union Station (also lots of choices for a quick breakfast at the station).

title: “Nice”
text:
Good location - I walked to all the museums and the park. However, when I was headed back, I was looking for a place to buy a bottle of wine and it got dark out.
DC is a little scary when you are on-foot after dark. If you are going to walk exclusively while you are there, I strongly recommend getting back to your hotel before the sun goes down.
Rooms were clean and nicely decorated. Beds very comfortable. Restaurant food and salad bar were pretty good, but also kind of pricey. Overall, great stay.
Would recommend.

title: “Great Experience!”
text: This website helped me in picking the Casablanca. We stayed there back in May during the first leg of our honeymoon. New York doesn't typically sound like a honeymoon destination, but I had never been there and it was always a dream to go- so much to do! The Casablanca was absolutely wonderful! After a scary cab ride from the airport, I was nervous to see what our room and hotel would be like. I was beautiful. We had a queen room, which I didn't think was small at all.
