Beautiful marble floors in the bathroom. The lounge/sitting room on the second floor was always great to come back to after a long day of walking. Free internet, drinks, snacks, etc. Every night we'd ask the staff for suggestions on where to go for dinner, drinks, etc. They even helped us with a route to take on the day we wanted to explore the shops around Greenwich village and SOHO. We had a wonderful time in New York, partly in thanks to the Casablanca. We will definitely stay there again. I HIGHLY recommend staying there!

title: “Big Rooms and Great Service”
text: I have stayed several times on business at this hotel. I keep coming back because the rooms are spacious and the service is excellent. I am treated very well by all the staff. The front desk staff is very courteous, the breakfast staff is fast and attentive and the rooms are clean, well-appointed and quite roomy. The flat screen TVs are a nice touch and the bed was one of the most comfortable I've slept in on the road in years! I'll definitely be back.

title: “Great hotel in downtown Chicago”
text: Very nice hotel. Great downtown location. You are within walking distance to theaters, shopping and restaurants. The staff is great, beds are great and room was very clean.

title: “Great Hotel with a Few Glitches”
text:
My three boys (ages 12, 10, and 7) and I stayed at the Hotel Giraffe for four nights. We loved the hotel itself: it was decorated beautifully, had wonderful amenities, and was in a pretty section of NYC. Our roomy suite had a little balcony which overlooked Park Avenue. The hotel staff, including bellhops, front desk staff, and housekeeping were all friendly and helpful.
I enjoyed the complimentary continental breakfasts and wine and cheese hours in the afternoon. They had a nice selection of food and beverages at breakfast. There was also water and biscotti cookies available at all times. Lemonade was offered sporadically.
The only issues I had were that one of the elevators was broken and made for some longer wait times to get to our room on the 11th floor. Also, the manager and one of the waitstaff on the rooftop deck were rude to my friend who was visiting us in the hotel. My boys didn't like that the bathroom door had a window which was partially see-through because they thought it wasn't private enough.
Overall, my children and I loved this hotel and would definitely stay here again, despite my few minor complaints.

title: “all the fluff without the doubletree substance”
text:
I'm poor artist trash but a road warrior with 1,000,000+ miles logged. Love the doubletree chain.
Checked in here last minute because of s change of plans. When you do that, they screw you with the highest rates. Okay, as long as I can rest - had just driven all over the bay area teaching dance workshops. Just wanted a quiet room.
Want on the fewest side, but the staff were having a LOUD conversation outside my room early early am. There was a service door nearby and I think that was the one slamming all night long.
Check in service was personable and friendly. Check out serbice was valid and unconcerned with my lack of rest.
Ceiling in room had obvious water damage, and crumbling ceiling tiles. Drapes were stained.
Would expect this and be fine with it for a lower price. When I pay a premium, i'd expect a premium experience. Next time might stay elsewhere. Might be looking for a new chain for my loyalty programs since this is my second negative experience in a month

title: “A bit of a disappointment”
text:
First the pros: This hotel is in a great location, so much to see, do and sample in the Union square area. The restaurant (daily grill) attached the hotel offers a great breakfast. The room is a good size with a nice sitting area and the fridge came in handy. 
The downside: This is the noisiest hotel I've ever been in. Our room was a 'premium king' which opened to the pool. This might be great for families but was not suited to a couple that might sleep in or want a pre dinner nap. Maybe it was the echo, or just the horrible screaming kids and parents that stayed while we were there but it was truly inescapable distraction. The hallways weren't much better, we heard every cart, staff member and 7am whistling patron walking near our room. 
The $76 for 2 nights parking does not include tax. Just a word to the wise... 
I realize it's an older building and these are complaints that can't be fixed readily but it is the sort of thing that would cause me to shell out additional coin for a newer hotel in the area.

title: “Worn out facility -- great staff -- good food”
text:
The room in the east tower was 80's holiday inn quality sans shag carpet. Cracked faux marble sink/counter, dirty grout, no fan in the bathroom, in general smelled like old booze and cigs. Window was filthy.
Staff was generally extremely gracious and accommodating, except concierge gals, a bit haughty as we were in tee shirts they may have mistaken us for street people, or something. 
Lunch dinner in the 151 lounge area was great food well prepared and served timely.
Place just needs a good remodel. Apparently taken over by some Korean investors and not being well maintained. Too Bad . . . the staff is loyal and cares . . . hard combo to find in many places. 
Would not stay here again but would come back for meals.

title: “Small, Dark, Noisy, Peeling Paint”
text:
Staff was very friendly and helpful. 
Stayed on a business trip for just one night, so the extremely small size of the rooms didn't bother me much. I was only sleeping there. What did bother me was:
* Dark dreary hallways
* No dresser in room, just tiny night stands
* Peeling Paint on the door and door frame
* Broken enamel on the bathtub
* Paper thin windows. The noise from trucks driving over street steel plates prevented me from getting even a wink of sleep
You get what you pay for.

title: “Had a fantastic honeymoon here”
text: My husband and I spent the first 4 days of our honeymoon in NYC in the Hilton. It was our first time in NYC. We had booked an executive room for which we had to check in on a separate floor. On arrival we were very impressed with the service. We were made to feel very welcome. Our room was just big enough and excellent. We loved the modern style and the 42inch plasma TV! We were even more impressed with the bathroom and shower! Inlcuded in our rate we had free breakfast every day and free wine, spirits, beer with food in the evenings. There were even delicious cookies throughout the day. We were very surprised with the short walking distances to most attractions. We only used the subway once to get to Battery Park. We are already planning when we can return and stay here again!

title: “Good Hotel, a few teething problems”
text: We spent 5 nights here in April and had a good stay. The hotel is well located close to the subway on the line which is good for times sqaure and downtown to Battery park. Rooms are small but well equipped with comefy beds and clean modern bathrooms. Some problems when we checked in as we had booked a city view room but the roome they allocated to us was facing a fire escape. We rang down to be told all the rooms with views were booked. They gave us a free breakfast (not very nice) and free wifi for the week. So not all bad. All in all a good hotel, but perhaps not the best in terms of organisation and reservations.

title: “Average property - but on the small size”
text:
The hotel is in a decent location - about a 10min, $15cab ride from the airport. It was a 15min walk to the Gaslamp area and about a 5min walk from the waterfront.
I am a Starwood Platinum but did not receive an upgraded room. The room I got was tiny. It basically just fit a king-size bed so I would not recommend families staying here who need more space. The pool area is also the smallest I have ever seen. The pool is maybe 15 feet long and only has 4 pool chairs. Overall the hotel was a lot less "jazzy" then other W properties I have stayed at. The Westin Hotel around the corner offers a lot more space and a better value.

title: “FRIENDLY AND ACCOMMODATING”
text: We arrived in Chicago at 9 am and the room was ready for us to drop off our bags and they even let us help ourselves the the breakfast buffet! So we ended up getting 2 free big breakfasts. The check in guy gave me several helpful pamphlets without me even asking, one had a great map of the city that we used. Checkout is at 12, and they even held our bags until our train departure at 6!! The doormen were SO friendly and helpful. When we needed a cab, two of them stood on either end of the street til they finally got an unoccupied one. For being right in the city, I would expect a small room for the good price. You want a big spacious room, go spend $300 on an overrated 5 star.

title: “Friendly hosts, rooms OK. Bit noisy though.”
text:
We arrived here from LA to go to Six Flags Magic Mountain, which is about a 45mins drive.
Checkin was fast and flawless. I needed to print our tickets to Six Flags on their computer, no problem! The rooms are of decent size and clean. Unfortunately it wasn't possible to make it dark enough for us, and there were lots of people running around at night, cheering and yelling (Nothing the hotel can do about). Breakfast was OK, but the breakfast room was too small, so we had to take ours to the room. Pool area was nice, with a (cold!) larger pool, and a hot spa. The railroad is closeby, so be prepared to hear some trains pass by regularly. There are lots of shops & restaurants within close range as well.
We had a nice stay, but due to some ignorant people, not a perfect night sleep.

title: “A-V-O-I-D”
text:
I've stayed in my share of one-star motels, but this was the worst. It was conveniently located right off I-55, but it was also in a very run-down area (complete with abandoned buildings) and felt kind of isolated and unsafe. I booked online through Hotwire, but if I had seen the place beforehand I never would have stayed here.
The room was somewhat dingy, the bed uncomfortable, and there was a lot of noise from outside (could have been the elevators - I didn't see a single other guest on my floor). This didn't bother me too much, but the mold in the shower did. The toilet stopped working on my first morning there, though the guy at the front desk was apologetic and had it taken care of immediately.
This is the only time I've ever considered moving to a different hotel even though I likely wouldn't be able to get my money back. Definitely a place to avoid.

title: “Worth the Stay”
text:
Upon arrival, the front desk agent directed us to complementary coffee, tea, cookies and fresh popcorn, which was nice since it was 9pm and we were hungry.
The room was very nice, comfortable beds, and flat screen tv.
Everything was in good working order....microwave, refridg. etc.
Breakfast was good, lots of food you won't go hungry.
Good location, right on and off of 9A and close to lots of stores, and airport.
If you need one night or an extended stay, worth the $$ and ask for AAA rate if you have it, you get their best rate. Enjoy! I did!!

title: “ABSOLUTELY EXCELLENT!”
text: I've stayed at many hotels from Excellent to horrible and I must say this hotel was very impressive! CLEAN, CLEAN, CLEAN, sheets, comforter, bathroom, floors, tables, counters, toilet, shower, towels, everything sparkled! No I am not exaggerating. Water bottles outside of room to drink, complimentary mixed nuts, candy , and chocolate for FREE, we had a KING Suite which looked like an apartment/condo, excellent view of Ground zero lobby beautiful, Security of the hotel excellent, felt safe. Only negative is the location but understandable due to construction going on at ground zero. Took us a while to find the hotel. Prepare for Parking, cost 45. Other than that I would def book here again in a heart beat!

title: “Will definitely return”
text:
Just returned from our first trip to NYC. Our one-bedroom king suite was more than I expected it to be. We had a good rate at $264 per night...the lowest I saw in the two-months I was looking... I almost expected to get the worst room in the hotel but we didn't. It was room 801 actually right next to the elevators but overlooking Lexington. I saw a complaint on the boards about the elevators being horribly loud and slow; we did not experience any of this. Perhaps one time we waited as long as three minutes for the elevator.
We didn't experience the hotel restaurant or bar but did use room service a couple of times. Yes, they are a bit expensive but this is typical for room service anywhere. For breakfast we would either go the the Luncheonette next door or the night before we would pick up scones and muffins from the store at 51st/Lex to have the next morning. We also loaded up on snacks and drinks from a convenience store on the SW corner of 47th or 48th and Lex. (this store was much larger than others closer to the hotel). Had a great Italian dinner at DeGrazia, just head east down 50th St past 3rd Ave on the north side you'll see a black awning with "DeGrazia" in white lettering leading you down to the bottom floor of the building.
I can't say enough about the hotel it was great including the staff and the nightly turn-down service. The location was great, close enough to everything but far enough away to regain your sanity from a day at Times Square, Soho, Rock and 5th Ave shopping.

title: “Great value!”
text: I spent the night before my wedding with my maid of honor (my sister) and an out-of-town bridesmaid at this hotel. We had such a great visit! The mattresses were very strange (some sort of foam), but they were very comfortable. Having the mini kitchen was really nice for snacks and water. It was a little tight for three people, but my bridesmaid & I shared the queen, and my sister slept on the pull-out, so we survived. You can book a larger room, but Priceline just gives you what it does. The continental breakfast is nice; juices, breakfast bars, fruit, cereals, etc. Check-in and out went fine, and they do provide a shuttle between the hotel and the airport, which is probably quite handy. If you're looking for a comfortable place to stay, this is a great choice!

title: “AMAZING HOTEL!”
text: I love this hotel! The service was amazing! From the minute we checked in everyone was so friendly and helpful! The valet even parked and emptied our car for us and brought it up to the room! The room was spacious and elegant with an amazing view of the city! We were within walking distance of so many fabulous stores and restaurants as well as two malls! Overall it was amazing and I would recommend the Moroccan to everyone!

title: “Do Not Stay Here!! These People Only Care About Your Money!!!”
text: Due to a delayed flight, my wife (5 months pregnant) and I arrived at the Nob Hill Motor Inn after the office was closed this past Wednesday night (7/18). There was no phone number posted, just a sign reading, "Office hours 7:00AM - 11:00PM" so I called information and paid the $2.50 to get the local number for the motel because all we wanted to do was get to sleep. Finally a gentleman came down to meet me and was shocked to hear that my wife and I were there to check-in to our room (that was prepaid and for which I had a voucher that explained the room would be held for us until 7:00AM the following day). He said that they already gave our room to somebody else. As you can imagine, I was less than satisfied. He explained to me the reason for his mismanagement (i.e., not holding a prepaid room for a guest who had not canceled) on this particular occasion was because the motel didn't actually get paid yet and typically does not get paid from brokerages such as those with whom Otel.com contracts until after the guest checks out. While I can understand his "business" purpose for not holding our room, I still don't understand why the customer (who already paid for the room) is the one left out in the cold - literally...and in this case at 1:30 in the morning with a 5 month pregnant wife in tow. Please, for our sake, do not stay at this motel. And if you do, please convince them to change their policy/arrangement with their suppliers.

title: “Unbelievably Horrific & Unacceptable Service”
text: This was the go-to hotel for my fiance and I whenever we wanted to have a weekend getaway in the city. We live in Brooklyn but loved staying at the Jolly Madison because of the affordable rate and the super modern rooms that they offer. We've always had wonderful experiences at this hotel until our last visit two weeks ago. We booked one room for three nights and arrived at 11pm. Upon arrival, the front desk told us that they overbooked and our room was NO LONGER available so they were going to DOWNGRADE us and then switch us the next morning. Furious as I was, they escorted us in the elevator to a smoking floor which smelled HORRENDOUS. I told the gentleman that we could not have a smoking floor as I am allergic to smoke. He then brought us downstairs again and introduced us to the manager to see what he could do. The manager escorted us to a new room and opened the door. Not only were there other people's belongings in there (!!!!) but there was also a leak. At that point, he said that the smoking floor was the only thing he had available for us. I explained AGAIN for the fourth time that I am allergic to cigarette smoke and he said there was nothing else he could do. In a nutshell, it was 11:45pm, they had overbooked our room and the only thing left for us to do was to stay in a smoking room even though i am allergic to smoke. No APOLOGY, no offer to put us up somewhere else for the night, no offer for a complimentary night for our next stay...NOTHING. We had no choice but to go hotel to hotel in hopes of trying to find another place to stay at midnight and wound up paying twice as much as the Jolly Madison charged as there was nowhere else to stay. The best part was that when i looked for a corporate phone number to contact on their website in order to complain, the website was one based in Italy and had no email address. I would have to pay international fees to call and complain. What a disaster. Never again will I go to a hotel that lets its guests leave to find accomodations at midnight because they overbooked.

title: “Large, comfortable room, great price”
text:
We were going to be in San Francisco for vacation with my wife, pre-teen daughter and teenaged sister-in-law. When looking for a place, we wanted to be in the city, so we wouldn't have to spend a lot of time and money getting to the main sites in the city. Space was also a concern, since I didn't think we could spend 4 days in a "regular" hotel room (2 doubles). Happily, we found this place and booked a king suite in March for what I considered to be a very reasonable price. Then as I checked back during the summer, the price on their web site kept going down, so they changed my reservation to give me the better deal. 
The suite had plenty of room, and with the refridgerator and microwave in the room, we were able to buy cereal and other breakfast items to eat in the room to save money. There were even self-service laundry machines on two of the floors, which was convenient. The indoor pool was good, as well.
The only real drawback (if you could call it that) was that it was about a 10 minute walk to points on Market Street. However, you could still walk to Union Square or the Ferry Building from the hotel, so it really wasn't that bad at all. There were casual restaurants close to the hotel, so its not like there was nothing nearby,
All in all, a great place, and I thought the price was very reasonable and fair.

title: “just lovely”
text: wow what a lovely hotel, with lovely staff. We arrived for a 4 day stay,we had a great room and loved the quiet setting of shelter island. The location was fantastic, with plenty to do nearby. The staff were very helpful and printed us off directions and information about things we wanted to do. It was nice to stay somewhere so relaxing on such a hectic holiday. The hotel was clean and well managed and the setting was palm trees and blue skies.We loved the ducks and the beautiful birds in the gardens. Would love to go again.

title: “Could have done better”
text: Write ups looked promising but we were a bit less than impressed. Spent >half an hour discovering $14/ night internet did not work. Vents in the room needed cleaning. Water at 7:30 in the morning was warm not hot. No in room breakfast available. Not really worth the $360 total cost even in New York..

title: “Great experience, will stay again”
text: Loved this little gem. Very friendly and helpful staff, big rooms, free tea and coffee in the lobby daily from 7am-11am, lots of linen and towels, clean rooms, reasonable shower, comfortable beds, great price. Make sure you request a quiet room (avoid rooms facing Bowery St). Only negatives -no phones or fridges in rooms, steep stairs (no elevator!) but the very friendly doormen will carry your bags for you. Not located on the prettiest of streets but only 2 short blocks to fabulous Spring & Prince Streets and subway stations. My friend and I had a fabulous time at the SoHotel and I highly recommend staying here. Tip well! It's deserved.

title: “Excellent service at the Westin”
text: I woud highly recommend the Westin for any type of traveler. The service was outstanding and the hotel was a showplace - beautiful and extremely clean. I did not eat dinner here, but did enjoy cocktails in the lounge while listening to a three-piece soft jazz group and enjoying the ambience. The best part of my room was a toss-up between the luxurious bed linens and the wonderfully appointed bathroom, complete with bathrobe and two-head showerhead. I have nothing critical to report, just an excellent stay at the Westin. Job well done, folks.

title: “good hotel in great location”
text:
I have stayed there twice now and have enjoyed both times. The rooms are standard Westing decor...modern and clean looking which some may find spartan. Its a great location particularly if you are doing things at Yerba Buena arts center or going to SFMOMA. Also convenient to shopping and public transportation. I ate at the Venetian restaurant Ducca at the hotel and it turned out to be great meal...would highly recommend for the food --its not a generic hotel restaurant. 
They have a nice outside bar with a fire which would be great weather permitting.
The staff has for the most part been very accomodating. The only quibble I would have is the at the latest checkin the front desk made ia big deal about my arriving early and saying the room may not be available. etc. etc. For the life of me cant figure out why they say that without first checking on the room...which was indeed available.

title: “The best extended stay hotel in San Diego”
text:
Myself and 4 other coworkers stayed at the hotel from 3/20-4/22. During the first couple weeks of the stay the hotel was completing a massive renovation. Other than a couple of areas being blocked off for the guests safety and seeing the workers during off hours, it was never an inconvenience. Being a returning guest, the renovation brought much needed changes. The rooms now have updated stainless steel appliances, new carpet, wall coverings, furniture, beds, and the best addition, Flat Panel TVs. Wireless internet in all of the rooms would be nice, but they do provide a patch cable for access to the free internet in every room.
The hotel also has many other great features that added to the stay. The breakfast is real food every morning (not just pastries and coffee). Make sure to get down stairs early on the weekend or you will be eating with a crowd of other guests. Make sure to try out the waffle maker, best waffle you will ever eat. Dinner with dessert was served Monday-Thursday. A couple times they served soup on back to back nights (almost asked the staff if I could make a waffle), but the free beer (not the watery stuff, brews like Shocktop, Stella, and Long Hammer on tap) and wine more than made up for the soup. If you have the time, I recommend that you take the time for the manager night activities on Thursday night, whether it is Karaoke, Poker, Bingo, or Smores on the fire pit, the hotel staff always makes sure the activity is fun and there is the potential for Marriott points to be won by the guests...Also, if you like to Grille, they have two that are available for guests. You just have to request use and they will supply the gas, spatulas, and even light it up for you.
The hotel is also within walking distance to Old Towne San Diego and 15-20 minute drive to downtown or the attractions. I recommend that you check out the Cosmopolitan for a dressier dinner (best food in Old Town) or hit up Fred's or Cafe Coyote for the drinks and above average Mexican food. Just expect a long wait if going out on Taco Tuesday... 
Overall, the stay was the most fun I have had on a business trip in a long time. Every single person on the staff was courteous, professional and would also engage in casual conversations (often needed when out of town for a long period of time with the same 3 people). I have been coming to the hotel since 2004 and plan to go back next time I have business in the area.

title: “Perfect location in Hollywood!”
text:
We were looking for a central place close to Hollywood Blvd that was not too pricey and comfortable (after all - you don't go overseas to sit in a bloody hotel room do you!)...this place was excellent.
Just a short stroll from the Walk of the Stars, a neat clean and comfortable room. Everything worked. The staff were friendly and helpful; the shuttle bus knew where we were to be picked up etc....
The place has a great hollywood theme with pictures etc - our Son who was 11 during the trip really liked this hotel.
And as for Mum and Dad - we got a good nights sleep and a hot shower etc. Not really much else we needed. For the price this is a place that I would stay again.

title: “LOOKED LIKE A HYATT TO ME.”
text: I did not actually spend the night here but instead visited some friends. I did nose around and use some services though. Valet was good and they had a parking garage connected to the hotel by a enclosed walkway. The food I had in the restaurant was good and so was the starbucks coffee in the lounge. I frequently had staff asking if I needed help. In a nice sincere way, not wondering what I was doing! It was upscale like Hyatts are but maybe not as grand as some. I visited the 18th floor, several suites. Very nice with great view of the river. They were very spacious and nicely decorated. Beds were great, yes I sampled one. I can not answer as far as the regular rooms condition. The pool is on the 19th floor (top) but seemed pretty small.It definitly was being enjoyed by many.I can only say that I did feel like I was in a Hyatt and not motel 6. I wished that I would have stayed here instead of the other place I chose. The reviews here had scared me away though!!

title: “FANTASTICO!!!!!”
text:
My lovely wife and I decided to go check out the San Antonio Riverwalk for July 4th. I booked a deluxe river view room with a king bed at the Omni La Mansion del Rio. This is a charming Spanish style hotel. The property seems pretty old but it is well maintained and is a quality place. 
Pros:
- convenient location at the sweet spot of the riverwalk
- clean, comfortable room
- great service, very welcoming front desk
- just a great old place with lots of charm
- the balcony of our room overlooked the riverwalk, it was AWESOME!!!
- nice powerful shower
- inexpensive, safe self parking directly across the street (thanks for the tip Trip Advisor reviewer!)
Cons:
- the door to the room was not sound proof, you can hear people walking in the hall
- the shower drains slowly
I would definitely stay here again. The Makora directly across the riverwalk is also an Omni property with a nice spa.

title: “Nice staff, poor facility”
text: What a shock (and disappointment) to have the Marriott name attached to this property. On the plus side, the staff couldn't be nicer...courteous, accommodating and willing. The rooms, however, left much to be desired. Paper thin walls allowed me to hear the occupants walking above and talking in the room next to ours. Those same thin walls also allowed me to know when they were using the bathroom. Not good!!! Also, when the fan/blower kicked in for the AC, it did so with a bang each time. This is not conducive to a good night's sleep. The kitchen area was hopelessly outdated and made me not want to even use the kitchen. The TVs are not flat screen or hi def. It's hard to go backwards on this when you are used to viewing hi def. The TV in the bedroom was basically impossible to watch. This facility is desperately in need of an upgrade. Shame on the Marriott for even letting it get to such a point. For what I paid for my room, it was a rip-off.

title: “Awesome Hotel Staff”
text:
I spent two nights a few weeks ago at this hotel. The staff was very very friendly! Upon checking in, the woman delightfully welcomed me to the property, giving me all sorts of information on where to eat and what to do while I was in Austin. I forgot her name, but I remember that she said that she had just moved to Texas from Germany! Wow! She was so friendly as she even introduced me to other members of their staff! 
The next day, I noticed that I haden't packed my dress socks into my bag, so I asked a sharply dressed felow (I assume, the manager) was able to inform me to the closest store that I could get a new pair of socks. He offered to give me a ride to the store, but I declined, due to the fact that I was trying get some exercise at the same time. I was just amazed that he actually offered. Thank you, sir! The rooms were nice and clean, too! The decor was a bit outside of my taste, but I did not mind it at all! Thanks again, Hampton and all your staff!!!

title: “Great Staff - Great People”
text: They always take great care of me and anything I may need. I stay here once or twice a month and love it. Shaila and the whole crew are great.

title: “I love the Parker House! I have traveled throughout the U.S, and Europe, and PH is the best!”
text: Ok. Why do I say that. The rooms are a little small, but who stays in the room when you are sitting in one of the most historic settings in the world! Within five minutes you can walk to Boston Commons, Fanuiel Hall, Old State House (where the Revolutionary War began) , Kings Chapel, and more and more --including of course the Boston Harbour. The restaurant in the hotel -- ever heard of Parker House rolls, how about Boston Cream Pie--all discovered there. How about the historic people -- Jack proposed to Jackie, Babe Ruth -- when he played for the Red Sox stuffed himself with the steaks, and let's not forget about Charles Dickens reciting his novel "The Christmas Carol", in front of the mirror on the mezanine floor. Sadlly, the hotel and restaurant is the same place that John Wilkes Booth likely planned the murder--of Lincoln, which happened only days after his stay! If you don't like history, or fabulous food, or comfortable surroundings --and a wonderfully pleasant staff -- do not go . I have stayed there at least twenty times in four years, with family. I highly suggest staying at the Parker House.

title: “hard to find but comfortable”
text: Hard to find, tucked behind a restaurant and another hotel. Friendly staff. Clean. Nice room. Very comfortable bed and nice bedding. We paid the same for 3 different hotels in different Texas cities from priceline's name your price. This was by far the nicest we stayed at on this trip. Staff friendly and helpful.

title: “An excellent hotel”
text:
My husband found this hotel on the internet and after reading the Tripadvisor reviews, we booked our stay for 3 nights in Midtown NYC. The hotel is central and in a calm street. We arrived with a rental car at 8am and we were pleasantly surprised to find a parking right next door to the hotel. 
The person at the reception was very nice and even if we had booked the hotel the night to come, she offered us to go and take the complementary breakfast in the lobby. In the meantime, I asked her to find the address of a pizzeria in Brooklyn and she printed the pizzeria's info and brought it to me.
The room was supposed to be ready at 3pm but as it was ready before, we were able to go to our room at midday. It was a one bedroom suite with 2 Queen beds + 1 sofa bed. Perfect for a family of 4 with 2 children who didn't want to sleep in the same bed!
We were told that there is no view as it is a small hotel (18 floors) but it was a view for us (see photo below)! 
The hotel receives a lot of Spanish speaking hosts and it is nice and cosy family hotel. Each and every of the employees we met during our stay were nice and helpful. A man at the reception even did a magic trick to our son who laughed in delight. Complimentary umbrellas were offered to use when it started to rain which was much appreciated.
We found restaurants all around and the area is nice and relatively calm which was good as we were able to choose different food depending on our mood.
A hotel we will definitely go back to. A very good place to sleep and spend calm and quality time to rest.

title: “great venue for a seminar”
text: Great venue for a seminar with wonderful food and luxurious surroundings. The best service from friendly people in the Midwest.

title: “When you go for New York, go for the Warwick Hotel!”
text:
A fine hotel with an interesting history. The room was fresh, nice and big. The location is super, MOMA across the street, Rockefeller Center a few blocks away and if you go north you have Central Park some blocks away. For shopping you have 5th Avenue and Park Avenue close by. If you want to go to the theatre it is also very convenient.
The staff was very helpful and service minded.
Björn and Lise-Lotte from Sweden

title: “Pleasant stay”
text:
I had a large, clean room located in the middle of the hotel. It overlooked a tiny courtyard so there was no view but at least there was no street noise whatsoever. The bed was comfortable and it was great to have free local calls and free internet (not wireless). The free continental breakfast was very nice and the front desk staff were very professional. I opted to stay here because of the above and their no pets and no smoking policies.
The only negative point I have is that the only heat source in the room was a very noisy window mounted fan. I had to turn it off during the night as there is no way I would have been able to sleep with it on. Do not be put off staying here because of the location. I felt safer in Pioneer Square than parts of downtown (2nd, 3rd & 4th Ave street corners for example). I would not have a problem staying here again but think I'll opt for somewhere a bit more modern.

title: “Filthy & Rundown”
text:
Although the location is superb - just a block off Beall St and within walking distance from riverside Park, the place was FILTHY. 
The hall carpets hadn't been cleaned in years, the arms of the sofas and chairs in the lobby were positively grimy and greasy looking and the cookie, sip-stir and cigarette butt that were on the lfoor by the elevators at 10:30 p.m. was still there at 10:30 a.m. 12 hours and no one had bothered to clean it up. 
Granted we had a corner room on Union St- but the traffic noise was very loud - even at 2:00 a.m. I feel that the windows could have been retrofitted with double pane glass which would have significantly reduced the street noise.
One of the elvators didn't work, it came to the floor when called, but wouldn't open. Due to the fact the the "brains" of the call system believed that a car was in fact waitng for us on our floor, one was forced to wait until some other poor wretch called it to their floor before another car could be called.
The hallways were hot and stuffy, and the service was attrocious.
We ordered a continental breakfast from room service to the tune of about $8.00 each. It came with styrofoam cups (not stoneware or china) and one tiny, little, cold, blueberry mini-muffin each. We sent it back. The free breakfast at the Comfort Inn is MUCH better than the garbage the Doubletree was trying to sell.
To top it off, upon checkout we weren't even asked if everything ws to our liking. She probaly knew better. She would have gotten an earfull.

title: “Rosie in the Concierge Lounge”
text: If you can swing an executive level room with access to the concierge lounge, Rosie will treat you like a King. I had to stay for two weeks on company business and Rosie made my stay almost like home. She is a tremendous asset to the Hilton in Woodland Hills CA.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: My wife, 10 year old son and I just returned from 4 nights at the Latham in a two level Carriage Suite. Abandoning our original plans to stay near the Smithsonian museums based on repeated comments about the lack of anything to do at night was a great decision for us. The Latham's location in Georgetown (a short cab or a long walk to the White House) provided an endless supply of shops and restaurants to choose from in the evening. The hotel's small pool was a welcome oasis after long days at the museums. The staff was efficient but not effusive. Services were restricted as you might expect in a smaller hotel. Breakfast at the adjacent patisserie was good. Frequent comments from other travellers about the noisy air conditioning were correct but the windows open and light sleepers could bring ear plugs. The property could use renovations (upholstery was a little threadbare and our shower controls lacked a handle) but the bed was good, the maid service was excellent and the hustle of M Street was offset by quiet walks along the historic canal at the rear of the hotel. Weekend rate was unbeatable. Would definitely return here for a family weekend in DC. Perfect? No. But probably a perfect compromise of value, facilities and location for travellers like us.

title: “Mayflower Park hotel”
text: This hotel was centrally located near boutiques, restaurants and Pike's Place. Rooms are small but workable. Only one night stand next to queen size bed, however. Staff was helpful and the hotel had a lovely sitting room up a small flight of stairs, opposite a very nice bar.

title: “Pleasantly surprised!”
text:
I booked this Hotel via a "Bid" on Priceline.com. We stayed one night and flew out the next morning. My Bid was 100.00 and that was for a standard room. 
Upon arrival we were offered an upgrade to a "Renovated" room for an extra 20.00. Of course we accepted because it offered extras like a big screen, pillow top king bed, and a few other tweaks.
Well worth the extra 20.00!!! We had a lovely room with a decent view. 
We will definitely stay here again next time we are in L.A.

title: “Five minutes here and I'm in love with this hotel.”
text: Friendliest hotel staff EVER. Beautiful restoration and fabulously funky. Ask for Rashid for anything at all. Even a copy of Alice in Wonderland waiting for me in my room. And love the early check-in!

title: “Great Stay at the Milford”
text:
Stayed at the Milford from April 8-15th with my husband to celebrate our 10th wedding anniversary!
Check in was very easy, I asked for a mini fridge to be sent to our room and it was done so immidiatley!
The consierge was AWESOME!!! Always ready to help with subway directions, suggestions on restauraunts, plays, and tours.
The location has been commented on already and it really cant be beat! Midtown, steps away from times square. The only thing is you really are in the thick of things! Its BUSY!! 8th ave is crazy! But subway is close and its an easy walking distance to many attractions!
The room is super small but clean, and modern. Housekeeping was always on the ball....ready to clean your room by 8:30am so if you want a sleep in day dont forget to put your "do not disturb" sign out, we learned that one the hard way. LOL
I didnt find the beds that comfortable and a queen sized looked really small to me...
All in all, great stay at a great price, I was really hesitant to book, alot of locals on the TA NYC forum were adament that this place was a dump and dubbed it "The Mildew Plaza" I was pleasantly surprised!
For a first trip to NYC it was a great choice, although now that I have an idea of how the city is laid out, i think I might look outside of the Times Square area next time for something a bit quieter and more quaint. A suggestion many TA forum experts encourage and now I can understand why.

title: “Great Hotel for the price”
text:
Just got back from spending 4 nights at The Jane..Yes the rooms are small. but for as little time I spent in the room it was great..Very clean. Good Beds..(NO bed bugs) Clean Bathrooms and yes they are down the hall. Every time I went to the bathroom nobody was there. GREAT STAFF..Everybody friendly and willing to help you..Be sure to check out the bar. Really nice..A little over price for a drink. But still nice.
Great Location. Not to far from the subway. Be sure to go across the street to the bay for a nice walk. Or use one of the bikes the hotel has for you to use. Lots of great resturants in the area. And the area was very safe. 
If you are traveling solo like myself. this place is worth it..Why pay extra for a room that you will be hardly in. 
Will stay there again next time in NYC..

title: “Perfect Location for Shopping in SF”
text: My friend and I recently took our two 13 year old daughters to the City for a Holiday shopping trip. The Handlery was the best location -- right in Union Square and walking distance to the Westfield Mall. It was super convenient, very reasonably priced, very clean, and we felt 100% safe in this location. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to stay in SF. The staff was helpful and friendly.

title: “The Muse is pure perfection...”
text: My husband and I just returned from a four night stay at The Muse. The service we received at the hotel was superb. The staff was courteous and attentive, the hotel is extremely clean, loved the decor, all new interiors, great location, the bed was extraordinarily comfortable and there were so many other special touches that made our stay truly unforgettable. We highly recommend The Muse.

title: “I Loved New York”
text: I loved the Waldorf Astoria it was very beautiful the people were nice people they greeted us with the up most respect anything we needed they were right there to make sure we had it i would definitely be going back i am taking my kids to see the tree at rockefellar center

title: “Try It!”
text: Great hotel at a great price. Also , you HAVE TO try their SPREAD restaurant, some of the best sushi, and otehr dishes ive ever tasted. This is a small boutique type hotel. Yes, you DONT get frequent flyer miles, nor do you get any bonuses for your trip, but you are rewarded witha clean and comfortable room that is tastefully decorated, in a nice NYC area.

title: “Enjoyed the stay”
text: Overall, I was impressed with this property. Bell man and front desk extremely helpful as far as activities to do in New York. Good location in the financial district. Only a block or so to the train that you can get anywhere on. My room had a great view, was on the end so had two full windows looking out with a slight view of the river. Great meeting rooms and wonderful food. Staff did everything they needed to make it a more pleasant stay, and the housekeeper was great!!

title: “boring business hotel”
text:
I was there for a work conference. The rooms are a bit dated. The location is not great, it is right near Chinatown and it looks a bit seedy just around the hotel. I will note that the Boston Commons is about three blocks away. I went to buy a bottle of water from the gift shop thinking it would be cheaper than the mini bar. No, it was a $5 bottle of water. Ridiculous. 
The room temperature could not be well adjusted, I was either too cold or too hot. Three things bothered me
1. the mini bar is one of the mini bars that if you touch the bottle you get charged. I might have bought a wine but could not move it to tell if it was a white wine I would like
2. cocktails at the bar were expensive and there were no pretzels or snacks to go with it
3. and the thing most business travelers can't understand, how is it that the holiday inn can provide free wi fi and a Hyatt which is set up for business conferences charges you a daily fee
there was at least a comfortable chair to read in with a good light nearby
on the one plus side the hotel staff seemed nice and the lap pool was nice
This would not be the hotel I would stay in again if I was in Boston

title: “Classy without the snob-value”
text:
This was a great place to stay, from the moment wewalked in those enormous wooden doors and were greeted by friendly, sincere staff, to opening the door to our incredibly clean, modern & comfortable room.
The tree-lined courtyard is amazing - a little hidden retreat in the grungy East Village. Perfect for relaxing after walking the streets all day.
All up, this was a great stay, and I can't really think of a bad thing to say about it.

title: “disappointing”
text: After experiencing hotels of the same status across America this was very disappointing. small room, no coffee making facilities, Wifi was not free (standard in most other hotels) and reception staff very unfriendly. The toilet kept blocking, the bar is franchised and closed at 11pm also couldn't take drinks out of the crowded bar into the more comfortable hotel lobby. To top it all every member of our group was presented with a bill at the end of our stay even though we had already paid for our accommodation involving further complaints with an unfriendly receptionist. Will never stay here again - looks fine but service is dreadful for the money paid. .

title: “Great location/Hated the mattress”
text: The location was great and close walk for all the "must-sees" in Chicago. (Willis Tower, Millenium Park, etc). Lots of great places to eat on every corner. I also enjoyed the fill up your own water bottle dispensers they had on each floor. Downside, the mattress was terrible...old spring mattress, and was very uncomfortable. No way my back could have stayed more than one night. Would not book there again.

title: “This hotel has bedbugs!”
text: We were attending a conference at the Hilton. I woke with what I thought were mosquito bites all over me. When my son found a bug crawling on his pillow, I took it down to the desk at 1AM. They denied it was a bedbug. I came back and found a mature bedbug on my pillow. I checked the mattress--it was crawling with them, and the maids had to have known by all the bedbug feces on the mattress. It looked like they had tried to zip them into a mattress cover, but it didn't keep the infestation contained. I took three bugs down to the front desk in a Ziploc baggy, (but wouldn't surrender the evidence.) They finally changed our room at 2AM--I wanted to go straight home, but my son wanted to attend the last day of the conference. They didn't charge us for the room, but we had to strip on our deck and leave clothing and bags outside in case of contamination. STILL haven't brought that stuff inside the house. Bedbugs survive up to a year without eating, and anything strong enough to kill them is really unhealthy for humans. I would NEVER stay there again.

title: “Excellent value for Hollywood”
text:
An older hotel but major refurbishing a couple of years ago. New windows and doors, air conditioning units, bath fixtures, the works. Kept neat and clean on a daily basis and given a deep cleaning when necessary. I've stayed here regularly for several years and watched the improvements. The hotel is built around a courtyard with a pool and pleasant and well kept garden. I often pick a lemon from the lemon tree. 
Secure parking via an electric gate adds to security. There's a great supermarket adjacent with a full deli and a Starbucks. The hotel provides in room coffee and a hair dryer. 
A month ago my family and stayed at another Hollywood hotel, paid twice the price, plus parking and had a dirty room because I wanted an indoor pool for the grandkids. Back to the Econolodge!

title: “Treated like royalty!”
text:
At first, we were bummed out about staying here. Our son and daughter in law live in the Back Bay and we have stayed at the Hilton near Prudential Center now for nearly 4 years. We always brought our beloved dog, whose last visit was in the fall of '11 before she succumbed to cancer on November 1. The Hilton was literally across the street from their apt.
This past weekend was our first time traveling anywhere with our new dog, a 6 year old beagle whom we rescued in April. I was all set to book the same hotel when I noticed they were no longer dog friendly, apparently due to a new owner. Hence, the not so near Double Tree. ( which we had stayed in many times since 2000 when our sons were enrolled in college nearby)
I called the hotel to request an upgrade based upon our HH diamond status and also because the day we were checking in was going to be our 37th wedding anniversary. I spoke with Wendy who assured me that she would try her best to upgrade our room.
We arrived Friday afternoon and were warmly greeted at the front desk with anniversary wishes and the signature Choco chip cookie. We went to our room and what a treat to find a 2 story dwelling with floor to ceiling windows! There was a half bath downstairs, with a huge wall mounted flat screen tv, of course couches, chairs and table... Microwave, sink and fridge. The sink in the half bath was awesome! See picture.
Upstairs was the bedroom with full bath and a fabulous shower! The best surprise was the tv that was built into the mirror!! 
The bedding was plush and there was a great mattress.. There was a railing overlooking the downstairs and views of the Charles River from the multistory windows.
Kudos to Wendy and her warm and sincere staff. All personnel were genuinely cheerful and friendly.
We look forward to staying here again!

title: “Tiny room but good deal anyway.”
text:
I stayed at Hotel Fusion from September 20 to September 28.
When I checked in it was a little chaotic because there were a lot of people there for the Oracle Convention but the staff managed to get everyone checked in quickly.
Unfortunately when I got to my room I saw that they did not gave me the room I booked thru expedia. My fried got the room he booked, i.e. a standard room with a queen bed but I was stuck with a tiny tiny room with a double bed. I went back to the lobby and I asked for the room I booked but they told me that there were no vacancy and they could not relocate me in another room. They added that the reservation I had only specified that I requested a queen bed, not that they would garanty that I would get one. Even after speaking to the manager and to expedia I could not get another room and I understand that it would be very difficult because it was full booked but I will do a complaint to expedia because the booking information was very deceiving.
The only other problem that I encounter there was the lack of climatisation in the room. The window opened in the "interior" section of the hotel, so there was no ventilation at all in the room and it got quite hot. But they provided a fan (stored in the closet) so putting it on the ledge of the windows would did make the room a lot more confortable.
Other than that two minor problem I had a great time there, mostly because I almost never was in the tiny room. But if you plan to be in your room a little more (for working for instance) this could be a major reason to go elsewhere.
The room was very clean, the bed was small but confortable, the location was great (you are near everything) and the staff made all they could to make you feel welcome. I heard people complain of the noise at night but it did not bother me at all.
The "business center" is on the third floor and there are two computers available most of the time. But you will have to pay extra to print (1$/page).
The free continental breakfast is on the fifth floor in a small area and it is very basic (bagels, toasts, muffins, coffee and juice).
I would probably stay there again if the price was right, but I would definitely require a confirmation for a bigger room.
Bye

title: “Mario as always A+”
text: A quick Pre-christmas trip with the family made better by Mario! Even before our arrival Mario had taken steps to ensure our check in was seamless and everything was in place. We didn't get to see him until following day-but when he did, he had his trademark warm personality and wanted to make sure our stay was going well. We even enjoyed a glass of champagne! As SPG preferred guests we have many options of hotels but the wonderful service we receive still makes ithe W on Lex our number one choice.

title: “A memorable stay”
text:
Just returned from 2 nights at the Omni Shoreham. Location is superb for access to the Metro but we actually only used it once. My wife and I like to walk everywhere so Washington was no exception. From the Omni we were able to walk to the Zoo (just up the street) & National Cathedral on day 1. The second day we went to Georgetown "M" Street, Whitehouse, Capital, Smithsonian Space and Air Museum and of course took in all the architecture and beautiful scenery along the way. After 10 hours of walking on day 2 we took the M Redline for $1.65 ea back to the hotel.
Had dinner at Roberts restaurant in the hotel on the back terrace. Thank-you Irma for making our evening memorable. The grounds are stunning and so well kept. Could see some of the 4th of July fireworks through the trees. Food was good. 
The room was very spacious, bathroom small by today's standards but I have to say that overall it was an extremely positive experience. When I registered online I added a comment that it was my wife's birthday. They were nice enought to acknowledge this with a comlimentary birthday dessert delivered to our room and birthday card.
I recommend becoming a Select Guest Member (free) as it provides complimentary internet, morning newspaper and choice of morning beverage plus a few other perks.
Parking is Valet (in/out privileges) only unless you are able to find a spot on your own.
The Omni Shoreham has much history and they showcase it througout the hotel. We will definitely return again. Thank-you to the Omni Shoreham Team for making our stay enjoyable.

title: “It was fine”
text:
We checked in here on a very busy night and the staff seemed a bit harried. They were somewhat helpful but I felt that they could have been nicer. I was expecting a package to be waiting for me at the hotel. The front desk staff was able to confirm that the hotel had it in their package room and sent me to the bell stand. The bell-staff informed me that I would have to pay $5 for them to get it for me at that time as the package room was closed for the night - I felt that they were strongly discouraging me from getting the package right then because they did not want to deal with it. I was able to retrieve the package myself the next morning for a fee of $2 but that was an unpleasant experience as the package room must be close to the trash room - not a good smell!
The room was fine - not to far from an elevator. The size of the room was the best part - we did have a couch and chair area in addition to the beds. I'm not sure how my husband and I ended up with two double beds. One bed had been requested when the reservation was made but we were so tired when we got to the room that we just went with it. The pillows were those horrible hotel pillows that have almost no stuffing and leave you with sore neck in the morning.
The room was clean but the shower curtain had a good deal of mold on it. The shower itself was pretty bad - not much water pressure. There was more water coming out of the tap when the shower was on then coming out of the showerhead. Also, the toilet made a horrible high pitched noise when flushed.
Overall, if booked into this hotel on business again but I would request to stay elsewhere. If traveling in San Francisco personally, I would definitely not stay here again.

title: “SLS IS AWESOME”
text:
So we arrived in Hollywood at our first hotel and were not impressed with the attitude at the front desk of the hotel we originally booked. The hotel had a great rating on trip advisor the rooms were ok but we decided to go with the second hotel picked. We took a taxi drive over to make sure we were making the right decision on changing. As soon as walking in to the SLS we felt that we had found our home for the next 4 days this is what Hollywood should look like and the location was perfect.
So after checking in we had a great night the service was great the people were friendly and all of the staff was accomodating. Then next morning there was Tres the restaurant downstairs it had a great breakfast and we totally scored with an incredible waiter Jacob Young he was right about the yogurt I just cannot get over it! The concierge staff was great and always got us where we wanted a special thank-you to K.C.. This hotel is a trendy fantastic hotel and I would recommend for anyone to stay there. 
Cons yes just a few small ones that are easy to over look they are 2 to be exact they are the big bottles of no name brand refillable shampoos, conditioners, lotions etc. and the fact that they were not enough plugs between Blackberry's and Hair dryers.
The locatiopn is Close to tons of shopping walking distance and they even have a house car to take you to Rodeo drive and the other shopping areas.
Our trip to LA will be longer next time and we will definately be staying at the SLS cannot wait to see Jacob and the other staff again!

title: “Great stay...great location”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights to see the Red Sox. I had booked this long ago or so I thought. I inadvertently did not confirm it. They were able to find us a room for 3 nights. Originally we were put on the 3rd floor. Because this hotel is in the heart of the city on a busy street you hear all the noise on a lower floor. The 2nd night we moved to the 9th floor and it was much better. You could hear a pin drop inside the hotel...it is very quiet.
The hotel staff were very friendly and more then happy to give us directions daily. Free bus around town is right outside the door!! They also take pets here...which u never hear any noise from them. They had a Labordoodle staying with them. His owner would be at the hospital 12 hours a day. The front desk staff would take him behind the desk every day and take him out for walks. 
Breakfast is 630-930a daily and contains many hot items...scrambled eggs, oatmeal, sausage, waffles, etc. Inner harbor is within walking distance with many restaurant choices. We never even needed a cab the whole 4 days we were there! Camden Yard is an easy walk there or take the free bus!!!

title: “given Drisco's top rating I feel it's okay to be a little nit-picking on a few p”
text:
My husband and I stayed at Hotel Drisco last month -Sept 08- our first visit to San Francisco. We selected the hotel largely because of its top Tripadvisor rating and excellent reviews. 
On the whole we were not disappointed - I would be happy to stay there again - the rooms are good, the neighbourhood very up market (a 10 minute brisk walk to shops restaurants etc.) and the hotel staff extremely pleasant and helpful. However given Drisco's current top rating on tripadvisor, which influences decisions, I feel it's okay to be a little nit-picking on a few points:
Breakfast - rather disappointing - almost no fresh fruit (apart from a boring bowl of apples, bananas and oranges) 
Overall ambiance - the decor throughout the hotel is restrained and tasteful, and generally for an old building, it is well maintained. However it is all rather bland and hotel-like, and creates an atmosphere that is impersonal and stiff. The primness of the breakfast room for example, where very, very subdued generic orchestral music accompanies breakfast, drove the couple at the table next to ours to hold their conversation in whispers!
So while Hotel Drisco serves what is probably its target market - middle-class, middle-age middle-everything - very well, it is definitely not the place for non-conformity - though in my opinion that is just what it lacks.

title: “Affordable, clean and good hotel close to the Central Park”
text:
I travelled with my 2 very young kids and parents, so we had to take two rooms: a double and a quadruple. 
The rooms in general are small, but were very clean and pretty new, with flat screen TV on the wall and new bathrooms as well. 
The big problem of the quadruple room was there is not place to hang the clothes on (no closet, no cupboard, nothing), so it was not comfortable from that perspective. There was no crib at the hotel either (one of my kids is 1).
The location of the hotel is very convenient with metro station, restaurants, CVS, etc. around. The car can be parked on the street quiet easily. 
One of the staff at the front desk was not very polite when dealing with a couple of issues. 
Value: it was very good, I think it is very difficult to get a similar hotel at that price in Manhattan. 
Summary: very good hotel for the money you spend. Definitely I would go back if travelling with my wife alone, but not with the complete family.

title: “Clean, comfortable, convenient, would recommend”
text:
Trip was with my two daughters, my 75th birthday gift from them. We stayed 4 nights. Our room was clean, lovely, beds comfy. View wasn't great but certainly interesting. The hotel staff was extremely friendly, efficient, courteous and helpful. When our return to JFK shuttle did not show up for our 4:30AM pickup, the bellman quickly arranged for a cab, the cost of which was actually a little cheaper. Taxi fare to and from JFK is a flat rate. I would not choose the shuttle again. The desk clerks even printed our Jet Blue Boarding passes for us.
If you don't mind walking, the hotel is fairly convenient to transportation, Macy's, Empire State Bldg., etc. Even though we had done our homework and were well provided with maps, etc., we weren't prepared for the confusion of making our way on foot. We booked tours on NYSightseeing buses and used these as our transportation as well as subways and an occasional cab. If I had it to do all over again, I would probably just use cabs. More expensive but so much quicker and NO WALKING! We wasted a lot of our time trying to figure out which way to go. Didn't get to see nearly as much as we would have liked to. 
We enjoyed dinners at the Barking Dog Restaurant next door and Caliente (Mexican) Restaurant around the corner on 33rd. Prices were very reasonble. There is a 24-hr deli/convenience market on the corner with everything you could possibly need should you choose to use the well-equipped little kitchenette in your room. There is also a diner around the corner on Lexington with fairly decent food. Lots of other choices nearby we didn't have time to try.

title: “Good vibe!”
text: Location is not too good, but the Vibe is super relaxed. Good stay.

title: “Convenient location but lacks customer service and comfort.”
text:
Stayed only one night (THANKfully) and the smoke alarm would not stop screaming during the night. My husband had to get dressed and go to the front desk. Someone then came back to the room, turned on the lights (at 3:30am) and had to remove the smoke detector (AND it was one that spoke saying carbon monoxide had been detected!).
After all this, we were still charged full price. As we were heading out for breakfast, the front desk told my husband feel free to check out between 12:00pm - 1:00pm. When we checked out at 12:30pm, we were told that due to our inconvenience through the night, they were waving the late check-out fee which is normally an extra $50-70. How about telling us upfront that we could check out late due to the inconvenience or have $50 taken off our bill when we check out on time?!! I am completely fine with paying for what I asked for, which was a room for one night, but I think it's bad customer service when the facts are not laid out up front only so they get what they want in the end with no regard for the customer.

title: “Great location”
text: This hotel was a bit overwhelming at first although the location was awesome - just opposite Penn Station, when I went to check in there was a huge line. However, this moved quickly and I checked in for my 2 night stay. The room was really nice, especially for the price. It had a lovely bed, Tv and bathroom, very spacious for NYC. I would recommend this to anyone who wants a good location for Empire State building and Macy's and of course Maddison Square Garden opposite too.

title: “Not bad, but not outstanding either”
text:
I have mixed feelings about this hotel. Not entirely due to faults of the hotel itself though. 
First, it's downtown. I'm usually a LES kind of person. UNlike the LES, this area is more of a working district than typical Manhattan mixed-use. I'm spoiled by the LES' abundant restaurants, bodegas, and near-constant activity. This location feels more like the downtown area of a smaller city -- people come there to work, then leave, then the place shuts down by 6pm. Indeed, most of the restaurants in the area close up shop after business hours. 
Second, it's next to WTC. Literally, one block from WTC. Yes, there is constant construction noise, but that's not really what bothered me the most. Instead, what rattled around in my mind the entire time was what actually happened there on 9/11. I've been in the WTC, also WFC. I had friends die in Tower 1. Needless to say, sleep was elusive. Again, not a fault of the hotel itself, but something travelers should keep in mind. Others who aren't as connected to 9/11 probably won't have an issue with this. 
As for the hotel itself, the recent renovation is appreciated and the elevators aren't anywhere as slow as they used to be when I stayed here in '07. The heater seemed to have a mind of its own and would sometimes get stuck in the heat or cool position regardless of what the thermostat was set to. Annoying and uncomfortable to say the least. The lobby was decorated beautifully for the holidays, which is always appreciated when you're traveling for the holidays. 
Housekeeping was unpredictable at best. Their cleaning ability was definitely proportional to the tip left. No tip the first night meant I was left with a single towel, single washcloth, and beds hastily made. Leaving a decent tip and suddenly appeared a bath mat, more towels than I knew what to do with, a well-made bed with extra pillows, and a completely spotless room. While I do appreciate that a hotel housekeeping job pay is low and housekeepers endure some absolutely disgusting things, good service is what will get you tips. Not the other way around.

title: “Grubby, rude staff, dodgy area”
text:
My friends and I stayed at the Adante Hotel for 3 nights at the beginning of our two week tour of the West Coast.
First impressions of the lobby area was that it looked clean enough. We were then informed that breakfast was served in the lobby. Yes, that's right, the actual lobby right next to the reception desk!
Breakfast was dire. Tea, coffee and toast. There was no milk, only coffee whitener which does not taste good in tea!
We went to our room and the hallways were dingy and the carpet old fashioned and dirty. The halls stunk of weed!
The room was very small and cramped with two double beds and a desk. The wardrobe was large but had no light so was pitch black.
The bathroom was tiny but it was clean with lots of towels and toiletries.
The carpet was filthy and the room had an air of griminess about it. I must admit, I felt a bit depressed and wanted to go home when I saw it!!
There were constant police sirens outside during the night and fights. One night it sounded like a riot was going on!
No aircon and you couldn't sleep with the windows open due to the noise. On a different note, we opened the window and found that someone had discarded their underpants on the windowsill!
The ceiling was painted blue with seagulls and clouds on it, bizarre!
If you come out of the hotel, do not turn right (which I note a previous reviewer did too!!) as you will be entering the Tenderloin area of San Francisco, which is very rough. We did this on the first day!
If you turn left, it is a short walk to Union Square. There is a lovely diner nearby called Lauries that does delicious breakfast.
On our last day, we chose to eat breakfast at the hotel and put our cases next to our table whilst we got our breakfast (I hasten to add that they were not in the way) and the male at reception tutted and said to his colleague "English" whilst looking at us. Not sure what point he was trying to make there, but I assume that it was derogatory!!!
Overall, we really enjoyed San Francisco but would not return to this hotel. It was not worth the money. I agree with another reviewer and would pay the extra to stay somewhere nicer.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: We stayed at the Villa Florence 3 years ago and when a conference brought us back to San Francisco, chose to stay there again. The location is fantastic - 2 blocks from the Powell/Market transit station with easy access to BART, the subway lines, F trolley line to Castro, Ferry Terminal and Fisherman's Wharf, and the terminus of the Powell/Hyde and Powell/Mason Cable car lines. Chinatown is about 4 blocks away and the Moscone center is about 4 blocks in the other direction. The Powell Street/Union Square area has lots of shops, restaurants and activity. The hotel itself is a lovely older boutique hotel. The rooms are a bit small and a bit spendy, but that's pretty typical for hotels right in San Francisco. We had an outside room on the 3rd floor and heard a fair amount of noise, especially with the drumming street musician setting up on the corner each night, but we really didn't experience enough noise to prevent us from sleeping. The staff is very professional, efficient and friendly and made us feel very welcome. This is a great little hotel in the heart of San Francisco and a great home base for exploring this lovely city.

author.username: So Many Places, So Little Time

title: “Location, Location, Location......”
text:
After reading earlier reviews, we were nervous about arrival at our hotel. We booked a double/double and there was plenty of room for my husband, me and our 17 year old son. Admittedly the Hotel has it's quirks, it is in a very old building. Our room was a double/double and was recently renovated. There was new a/c which cooled down the room quickly. We loved the area. Lots of restaurants, a Starbucks, a Carribu Coffee and a Whole Foods market all within a block. We were able to walk everywhere we went and only took the Metro a couple of times to save a few steps. 
Maid service was adequate, but not perfect, and there were NO bed bugs or roaches as in some other older reviews. They are continuing to renovate, but if you are up and around by 9:00 a.m. this shouldn't be a problem.
The staff was courteous and friendly and helped us with directions and restaurant recommendations. I would definitely stay here again and recommend this Hotel to friends on a budget.

title: “Noisy, no soundproof”
text: This was my second stay in this hotel and the same problem again. There was not enough of sound isolation between the rooms. I could hear my neighbors like there were no walls between the rooms. The hotel was half empty. They could easily separate guests by few rooms apart but for some reason they put guests into neighboring rooms. Unfortunately this hotel is in a preferred list in my company so I had no other choice but I hope this would change soon.

title: “I don't know what any of these people are talking about!”
text:
So, I'm not sure why some of these reviews are so poor!! Perhaps they had random unfortunate things come up, but my stay here was absolutely flawless!
Let me begin first by saying that this was most likely our most pleasurable stay at any hotel in the recent past. We like to take frequent weekend trips to various cities in Texas for mini-vacations, concerts, etc. This time around we got tickets to see the Australian Pink Floyd concert in Austin, and we also wanted to experience 6th Street for the first time. I searched around for a few weeks to find a hotel that A.) fit our budget B.) had decent reviews and C.) had the amenities that we needed for our extended stay. We found all of this and more at this hotel! I had even booked a room at a cheaper hotel before I changed my mind and booked with this hotel. 
We arrived at check-in time on Friday, October 5, 2012, and were immediately greeted by the absolute nicest front desk employee (her name was Jessica). Jessica instantly made us feel welcomed and ready to help us with any needs we had. She helped us to get extra textiles that we needed for our room: towels, a pillow, toaster oven, etc. She helped to give us directions around town and gave us some ideas of where to go. She also was sure to call our room shortly after our arrival to ensure that everything was to our liking. She was an outstanding employee, as nice as could be, and never hesitated to help us. There was even one time that we went to the counter to ask her a question, she took a phone call, helped us, and another customer all at the same time...we were quite impressed with her ability to multi-task while keeping a smile on her face (and the customers')!!
After such a wonderful welcome, we made our way up to our room. We had asked for a smoking room which is exactly where we were placed. Obviously the entire third floor is meant for smoking guest, and it did smell like smoke. This was not a problem for us since we smoke. (NOTE: If you are a non smoker obviously request to stay on the first or second floor so you do not have to worry about the smoke smell!!) The room was very clean, and had all of the amenities that we needed: a full size fridge, stove top, microwave, coffee maker, etc. The television was nice and had a beautiful picture (great for watching that Saturday's UT game)! The bathroom was spotless and had tons of storage space, and the shower had good water pressure and plenty of hot water to spare. And the bed...I wish I could have stayed for another week just for the bed alone! The sheets were clean and soft, the bed was plush and comfortable, and pillows were oh so heavenly. Wish I could have taken the whole thing home with me...lol! 
This was our first time ever to stay at a Candlewood Suites Hotel, and while I cannot speak for the other locations, Austin-South was an absolute pleasure. We will be sure to stay here the next time we find our way out to Austin because this hotel definitely far surpassed our expectations. When I first booked, I was slightly apprehensive as some of the reviews on TripAdvisor.com were less than flattering. However, I don't know what any of these people are talking about. From check in to check out, our stay was flawless!

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: This Omni is a great hotel. Good food, including 24-hour room service, excellent rooms, great service, in proximity to restaurants and night life. We stayed in a king corner suit with a city view on two sides, including a wall to wall window over the bed. We were able to walk to several restaurants (or take a quick cab). Serious shoping with-in walking distance. I think it would be rare to have a bad expierence here. Is it expensive - it can be. However, any decent hotel in Chicago is pricy. Definitely recommended.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Palomar at the start of our honeymoon for three nights. On arrival we were upgraded to a motion room which was huge. We had our own cross trainer! and a spa jacuzzi bath for two! We were also given complimentary breakfasts during our stay and a voucher for the mini-bar. We were on a high floor away from the lifts (overlooking the pool) which I had requested prior to our stay, The staff were very welcoming and were always on hand to help.
The lobby is very stylish with lovely fires and we took advantage of the free wine between 5-6pm one evening which is a nice touch. The hotel is situated in a good area with plenty of cafes and restaurants nearby. The metro station is a couple of minutes walk away (turn left when you leave the hotel) although its not well signposted. It is easy to use and quick to get to the main sights.
We had a wonderful time in Washington and had some fabulous meals. We would recommend Zaytinya which is a greek restaurant near the mall and Tabard Inn and Pizza Paradiso which are both near the hotel.
We would not hesitate to return to this hotel and will be recommending it to all of our family and friends.

title: “Comfortable, if a little small”
text: This lovely hotel was beautiful. As you walk in, the large, airy and atmospheric lobby of the hotel beckons you in. The staff were friendly and helpful. Rooms are on the small side. Comfortable with luxurious bathrooms. We were upgraded from a double to a king room. Views were of the back of the hotel and pretty non-existent. Overall, I would rate this hotel highly because of its location, price and pleasantness.

title: “Yee haw.”
text: I had a great stay at the Hotel Palomar. Nice room, excellent staff and perfect location to visit SMU. I took one of the most exhilarating yoga class of my life at Exhale Spa. The wine hour in the lobby was a huge hit with my group. Yummy snacks. Simon, the chef at the hotel restaurant, personally greeted my group, hung out with us and sent some yummy desserts for us to sample.

title: “Nice hotel.”
text:
Clean and beautiful. Rooms are a bit on the small side. Valet parking was SLOW! After checkout, we waited 15 minutes for them to bring our car around.
Still, good staff, good location. We got a great deal on travelocity at $99/night....supercheap for the area, so I was thrilled. I'd stay again.

title: “Great hotel in awesome location!”
text: I Stayed at Bristol hotel with my boyfriend on fourth of July weekend. The hotel was kind of pricey but well worth it! The staff are very helpfull and professional. The hotel comes with complimentary wifi in the room you stay in....it was a bit slow, but a nice convenience. The hotel has valet parking that costs about $26 per night but if you have a hybrid car it costs about half that. The room was cute and we could see the ocean from our window. The bed was very comfortable and there is an ipod docking station in the room as well as a flat screen tv and fridge. The hotel has a restaraunt and other numerous places to eat around the hotel as well as a grocery store (i think its a ralphs) down the street. The hotel is walking distance to the downtown area which we enjoyed very much. If you go downtown and like pubs i reccomend The Field for food and drink....try the boxties they are amazing! We drove to sea world which is really easy to get to from the hotel...it maybe took us 15 minutes to drive there. There are busses and trolleys right next to the hotel if you are interested in using that. after all the fees (like valet parking) the hotel came out to about $170/night. If that is too much for u i reccomend looking into staying into the little Italy area of san diego like the porto vista hotel or la pensione which will be anywhere from $100-$130/night.

title: “We would rate this property 10 Stars if possible!!!”
