text: We had a wonderful experience at the Affinia 50 in late June -early July (6 nights)! From the helpful, efficient front desk employees, to the smiling, welcoming bellmen, to the responsive, hard-working housekeeping staff, to the approachable, service-oriented General Manager, Brian Gehlich........EVERYONE at the Affinia 50 was there to insure that our NYC visit was memorable!! We live in California and are well traveled, but this was only our second visit to NYC. It will not be our last, and we will always stay at the Affinia 50. Everytime we returned to the hotel after an outing, we were greeted with a smile and the words "Welcome Home." That is exactly how we felt! Details: We appreciated being upgraded to an Executive Suite. We left 2 items in our room (airplane pillows!) and the housekeeping staff promptly mailed them to us in CA. The complimentary Happy Hour (6:00-7:00pm) was very comfortable and appreciated before heading out for fine dining. The full-sized kitchen enabled us to have breakfast in our room, hence saving money and time. Front desk folks directed us to some great restaurants. I could go on and on......please stay here and experience great hospitality, warmth, and professional service,

title: “Great hotel in a super location”
text: We have just returned from a week in New York with our teenage children. We all absolutely loved this hotel. The beds were super comfortable with great quality bedlinen and a very clean bathroom topped up every day with kiehl products. The staff, especially the doormen, were very welcoming although a restaurant recommendation from reception wasn't that great. The housekeeping staff were fantastic with every little request met immediately with a smile. The location of this hotel couldn't have been better with shops, cafes and restaurants on your doorstep. The area is safe and our children (13 and 15) could explore on their own during the day or hang out in the local Apple store after a day of sightseeing. Spring Street subway is minutes away making getting around town very easy. I would certainly recommend this hotel to friends and family and is a perfect choice if you are traveling with teenagers who like cupcake shops and Apple stores within popping distance!

title: “May, 2011”
text: Most helpful and professional staff, all staff. Great location. Irish rest./bar @ 1st floor, u can watch soccer games ( real football) and ur team will win :-)

title: “Nice place in the heart of the theatre district”
text:
While the rooms here are a bit smaller than the typical Doubletree, finding an all suite hotel at the hub of activity around Times Square makes for a nice stay, especially if you have a younger child or two that won't mind a sleeper sofa for a few nights.
Located at the NE corner of Times Square, there are a few rooms on each floor that give you a view of all the neon and people that makes this area so visually appealing. An easy walk to most of the major theatres/shows makes this a great location for the theatre goer. Families with kids who like the comfort of tried and true food chains will also enjoy this as close by are Planet Hollywood, TGI Fridays, Hardrock Cafe and others. For those who like to try smaller, local restaurants it is only a few minutes walk to a large selection of nice places including the collections of Italian restaurants along the periphery of Hell's Kitchen.
The hotel itself is clean, with a uncluttered loby that includes a small bar/lounge area, a restaurant with a nice breakfast buffet and a fitness center. The rooms are bigger than your average NY hotel room with a sitting room and a separate bedroom. The bed was extremely comfortable and the bathroom was a bit bigger than other NYC hotels where I've stayed. 
Overall, this is a great place to stay if you want to be in the middle of the hustle and bustle that is Times Square.

title: “Good hotel”
text:
Standard fare Sheraton Hotel, good location for Fishermans Wharf and the Tram / Streetcar / Cable Car system into the main city centre.
From the outside this looks like a mid 80s motel but after what looks like a major refit the interior is bright, cheery and relaxing with influences of the bay in the colour scheme.
Good sized rooms, comfortable beds and well maintained, the bathrooms while small are functional and work well, the only issue was the air con system is a rather dated looking chunk of machinery in the room that at times sounded like a jet engine, thankfully when we went it was barely needed.
The only issue i have with this and many other hotels is the need to charge for in room internet, in 2012 we are still been charged $10 / $15 for 24 hr access, this is just extorinate, if smaller hotels can make this a free service why can the chains not ?
One bonus that we has was that there was a "Dollar" car rental outlet attached to the hotel which helped us in picking up our rental truck for our onward journey

title: “Very overrated”
text:
Never having stayed at a Hyatt before I was expecting more for the money. Granted there were four of us in a room, but for the amount of money you pay at least let's have a decent size bed - there are double beds and double beds it would seem! (do they think we are all slim and short?). Apart from not having enough towels, shampoos, soaps etc where on earth do you put your clothes and suitcases for four people!! You get more room in a youth hostel. Also felt the room was not cleaned that great. Being treated by some rude Hyatt personnel when putting the suitcase in storage for a couple of hours also added to an overall feeling of being treated like 'just another Jo from out of town'. Of course I am sure if you can afford one room you are probably treated like royalty.
The splendour of the entrance/foyer should be cut back and more put into pleasing people (us regular Jo's)and the 'Amentities' on the Hyatt web site is a bit of a joke - nothing different than what you get in a Sandman Inn! (isn't a hairdyer, clock, table, TV etc the norm?).
Overall, disappointed.
oh yes - the shower fell apart as well.
thank you

title: “Not that Grand”
text: Even with the remodel, it's pretty obvious this hotel is old. The newly remodeled rooms do not even have flat screen tv's. They still have the "box" 27" in the bedroom and larger size in the living room. You can hear people walking and talking outside your door. We expected more based on the visuals of the website.

title: “Fantastic - Brilliant hotel”
text:
This hotel was lovely. Huge spacious rooms with a kitchen area, Aveda products in the bathroom too.
This hotel was in awesome location, couldnt wish for better.
The staff were really helpful and polite and nothing was too much trouble.
Would recommend this hotel and would love to stay again.

title: “Big rooms, Clean, Great Breakfast!”
text: We stayed here for three nights and had a great time! The service - espacially the bell hops- was great! Very friendly, helpful caring staff. The breakfast was great with a good choice of cereals, waffle, eggs, etc. Very nice breakfast staff too. It looks like our room had just been remodeled - everything looked brand new. Location is great too- very central to most tourist spots. If you have a car you can park it in the lot across the street. There is a fire station across the street but they will give you earplugs. Nice pool and hottub too!

title: “Reasonably comfortable, but a few misses”
text: We spent two nights 4/27&28 at this property. Earlier reviews were quite complimentary but we felt painted a little brighter picture than we found. It is an older property with up-grading in process. The lobby area makes a very good impression and the there are three internet sites for use by the guests, good idea!. Everywhere you go inside and out there are two to three steps up or down. Only one cut out was found so if you need wheelchair access I would avoid this hotel. The double room we had was pretty basic and not really in keeping with the "Suite" theme. It was nicly decorated and equipped. The bath had not been upgraded. It was small and all white, and lacked a soapdish in the shower and no grab bars with a rather tricky exit required out of the shower/tub. The breakfast was average despite being called a "hot buffet". The only hot items were scrambled eggs, institution style and some very good hash browns. A sausage or strip of bacon woud have been most welcome. They did offer the opportunity to make your own waffles.

title: “Nice Place Great Service and Location”
text:
Just had a sales meeting at the Andaz, Great service and location. The employees are eager to please and take care of all your needs. Rooms were very nice and the location in the gaslamp district is super.
 Parking is only Valet and 35 bucks a day so be aware. About the same everywhere downtown...

title: “Front desk as great as the property!”
text: I arrived at the hotel at around 11:00a.m. after a redeye from Hawaii and a drive from LAX. I honestly did not expect to be allowed to check is so early; but when speaking to the young lady and telling her she said I have a room ready for you now, which I thought was so considerate of them. Room were very nice and beds very comfortable, enjoyed the small area outside the room to seat and enjoy a drink the property is also very nice. Wish I could have stayed longer but this was an add on to our vacation and was mainly to visit the San Diego zoo, would definitely recommend!!

title: “Good and Bad”
text: This is a tough one. Reserved and prepaid on Westin's site for a Grand Puget Sound View (confirmation says "sweeping views of Puget Sound") yet upon arrival at 1:45 AM they say ithe room type is only a request, not a guarantee. They offer a room with a view and 2 double beds for our stay (celebrating a big anniversary) or a king city view. We take the two beds thinking we'll make it work. Well, we did have to sleep sepperately for our first of three nights. We were moved the next day, but not promptly or without a struggle to explain our stay in Seattle was going to be short and that we couldn't use up too much of our time to attempt a room change. Miraculously, a room with a view and a King bed became instantly available at 4PM. The room was great and the view was nothing short of stunning. We asked that our first night be comped, and it was after a few tries at checkout. First they kept all of the nights and added $90 then removed the $90 and then finally removed one nights charge. Overall, I would have preferred to stay someplace that operates more efficiently to avoid the time spent moving around and negotiating the hotel bill.

title: “Not as good as we expected”
text: I travel extensively on business spending a lot of time in Japan, so my comments are not from an inexperienced city traveller. My wife & I booked a New York break for a big birthday and chose the Kitano from one of their promotional ads in a brochure. While the Hotel is clean and quiet, the service is just OK and the rooms are very small - we had booked a "superior king sized room" only to find that this means standard small room really (good marketing or misrepresentation) The view from the fourth floor in a $480 a night room is appalling - look at the photos. I complained explaining that we were on a special holiday and had hoped for views of New York out of the window but was advised (of course) the place was full and there was no other rooms available. Strangely, the public rooms, foyer, breakfast and restaurants were never busy during our stay. It's the last time the Kitano will be seeing me!!

title: “Worn down and noisy but great location”
text: I just spent 5 nights at this hotel for a trade show and found it to be a mixed bag. On the positive side it is on the lower end of the prices you will see for a Xhicago hotel and it's location can not be beaten. The down side is that the despite ongoing renovations the hotel is showing it's age. The elevators are old and slow and frequently out of order meaning long delays getting to and from your room. I stayed on the front of the hotel on the 19th floor and the noise was terrible resulting in quite a sleep deficit. I did not eat at the resturant so I can not comment on it however the bar, like the hotel has not aged well and it shuts down quite early forcing us to go across the street for a drink. If you are in town and looking for a cheaper place to stay consider this hotel but be very aware of it's down side.

title: “A great value for the money.”
text:
I can't say enough about Candlewood suites. Our stay was brief but fantastic. It's clean, the prices are reasonable, the beds are comfortable, the little kitchenette comes in handy. Best of all, it's about 2 blocks from Everything...really you leave the hotel turn left, walk 2 blocks and boom - food, drinks, shopping at your fingertips. Try the sticky wings and Texas margaritas at Dallas BBQ on 42nd. 
The staff takes great care of you too. They have free, fresh baked cookies every evening. I'm definitely going back.

title: “Cleanest hotel I have every stayed at”
text:
Wonderful Stay. Staff was great and very helpful, (especially the concierge and the bellhop). Room was gorgeous. Everything was incredibly clean. It was like we were the first people to ever stay in that room. Hotel is located very close (2 blocks) from b.a.r.t. and a Powell St. bus station. Neighborhood was safe. We walked from the hotel to the Orpheum and back at 10:00 pm with no problem on a Thursday night. If possible take the bus or b.a.r.t. into the city because it will cost you $55/ night to valet your car.
Do yourself a favor and book a room at the Intercontinental.
By the way, President Obama stayed there while we were there. A little inconvenient when we tried to leave and were locked in hotel for 20 minutes, but worth it for the memories.

title: “Nice location noisy rooms”
text:
we arrived at hotel frank. 
The room is connected to another room by a door, which is closed. We hear The neighbours very clear. They were just talking en we hear them like they are standing next to us. As they are watching tv we hear that very clear!
Yesterday we fell a sleep late and this morning we woke up early because of the neighbours  alarm clock at six. This is not what we expect from a quiet room! 
Down stairs at front desk we hear the hotel is overbooked. They can't offer us a similar room.  Front desk said we are already in the quiet!! section of the hotel.  There's nothing they can do for us. The only possibility there was is that they move our luggage during the day to a  room which is smaller with 2 small beds, on the noisy side of the hote at front 
Why do they call this the noisy side? Because every morning at 7 there will be an hour protest. This is not an option for us. We paid for a large room with king bed.
At front it's noisy because of the protest and street. In the quit section theres noise from your neighbours. 
At front desk they have earplugs wich you get when you complain. 
Enough said. 
The hotel looks good and the location is also nice. But I also prefer a good night sleep.

title: “Excellent in every way!”
text: This hotel has a wonderful location. Parking is immediately adjacent. Rooms are incredibly spacious for NYC, and the staff was so friendly that I could not believe I was in New York City! :-) Everything works in the room, and everything was new or almost. We had a wonderful time and consider this the finest overall hotel we have stayed in in NYC (and that list includes the Waldorf Astoria).

title: “DC stop on way down to OuterBanks”
text:
Friendly staff that was so helpful and pleasant - the open wine tasting each evening was a great touch - very good with our dogs and for those without dogs you are not overwhelmed by those traveling with their pets. 
Staff were helpful with directions and very attentive to any questions / needs we had.
Stayed in another Kimpton Hotel in Baltimore on our return trip from the Outerbanks and had a very good experience their as well. 
We will be a return guest and will recommend to our friends.

title: “Big factory...”
text: We have lost a complete day in fixing our booking problems : we booked one room with 2 double beds, we got 1 double bed in the room. Rooms really old and in very bad conditions, not refreshed. Staff (except one) not ready to give you time. In one word it's a big factory...

title: “Roomy & comfortable in the middle of Back Bay”
text: Very spacious room, very clean and well-equipped. The staff was very accommodating, glad to hold our bags a few hours after check-out until we needed to head to the train. Excellent location on the green line subway and just off Mass Ave. Surprising to find a 2-story motel in this area. We found are room to be nice and quiet. Only negative was no free wi fi or lobby computer.

title: “Basic Hotel - Never Again”
text: This is a hotel, which doesn't offer much more than an uncomfortable bed. If you're staying only a few nights and want a clean place to stay then this is for you. If you're after a hotel with a comfortable bed, a plush pillow, amenities or a fridge this isn’t the place for you. Had a few problems with the hotel over charging our credit card, we wrote three emails and sent a fax from Australia, however we didn’t even receive a reply. We had to rectify the situation when we arrived, quite a hassle! Last thing you want to do when you arrive. Our view was also bad, a brick wall! Hotel in need of a renovation.

title: “Great Location - Great Hotel”
text: We stayed 2 nights while visiting area universities. This is a great location - and a lovely hotel. The reviews are all right on. The staff is very friendly and room was perfect - with a really great shower! The food at Eastern Standard is also top notch. You will not be disappointed.

title: “By far, the nicest place for the price, location & staff anywhere in SF.”
text: The quiet street & park access is great. Public transportation let's us park the car for our whole visit unless we head out of the city. It's the staff which really keeps the place humming and provides everything possible for guest enjoyment. They watch out for your belongings [once we left for the day w/ car doors & trunk open which they noticed & locked for us]. They are the best source for local events & info on everything 'city' you need to know. Tyler, Raymond & Nikki get extra cudos for going above & beyond in assistance and pleasant attitude, even at the end of a long shift. If you have a YMCA membership elsewhere, you can get a discount to the nearby Presidio YMCA for $3/day.

title: “Amazing location, staff, and romantic setting for a getaway”
text:
The Bryant Park Hotel exceeded every expectation I had - and they were high after the other reviews I read! At check-in we were upgraded from a Superior room to a Junior suite on the 21st floor - for free!! We had an amazing view of the city. Location is perfect - less than 10 minute walk to Times Square without the chaos of being in the middle of it all. Bryant Park is a great spot as well, with tons of shops and food (free samples!) and a free ice skating rink in winter ($14 skate rental). The room was gorgeous. Comfortable bed, spacious bathroom, more than enough room for two people (especially for a New York hotel). The staff was friendly and helpful, giving us great recommendations (we went to their suggested breakfast spot twice because it was so good!). They were very helpful in check out as well, and let us keep our bags their for hours and offered help in obtaining transportation to the airport. They even had water bottles at check out for our travels. 
Nothing beats the vibe of the hotel, which you cannot adequately describe in a review. Even the elevator had a romantic vibe. It truly made the weekend feel like an escape. Definitely a location for couples, not families. We never had the chance to check out the cellar bar, but from the line to get in (guests skip the line), it seemed like a hot place on the weekend. Well worth the price. I hope to visit again.

title: “Great Location, great service, great hotel”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for three nights in October. Due to a big delay on our flights, we arrived very late in the evening. The staff was very friendly, and even though the parking lot was full, they still let us park onside. 
Overall the hotel is very well located, the staff is really friendly and it is a perfect place to start your journey through San Francisco. 
The breakfast is real nice, due to the bad weather we couldn't eat outside, so we ate it in our room, which was really spacious, so not a problem at all.

title: “Nice location”
text: A nice hotel in a location within walking distance of Pikes Market (5 blocks), Light Rail stop (4 blocks) , NCL cruise terminal (4 blocks) and many restaurants. The hotel is well maintained and the desk staff very helpful and friendly. The only drawback would be there is no room air conditioning. This wasn't a problem for us since it was September, but could be a factor in the summer if the temps get in the 80's. No continental breakfast ( in-room coffee), but a local Artisan bakery 1 1/2 blocks away. About the least expensive hotel ($150) in the area if your catching a cruise ship.

title: “Missed a Beat”
text: Wouldn't be fair to hold this against them so I haven't in my rating but....when you pay top dollar and expect the best, staff have to be careful not to disappoint. I had a long wait at check in. When it was my turn to check in one of the staff left leaving only one to attend to guests. Had to ask for them to bring out more staff which they did....but after flying half way around the world I didn't want to be managing their front desk. Beautiful suites, great location - walk to magnificent mile, nice staff. Wish their Michelin starred restaurant opened on Sundays as well as their bar.

title: “Lovely hotel”
text:
I've stayed at the Westin Galleria numerous times for business trips over the past two years. Being a Starwood Preferred Guest allows me to stay on the SPG and Executive Club floors, which I thoroughly enjoy. The Executive Club lounge is quite nice. With the Oceanaire restaurant on the first floor and the Galleria mall adjacent to the hotel, there really is no better place to stay in this part of Dallas. 
If they had to change one thing, the breakfast at the Executive Club could use some sprucing up. Their fruit bar is fabulous, but the only hot food available is cheesy eggs and oatmeal. Possibly some protein (bacon, sausage) or breakfast sandwiches would really make that experience great.

title: “Loved the Palms Hotel!”
text: Recently stayed 3 days during our Spring Break. Upon check-in, we were told we had been upgraded to a Suite! Corner suite with separate 2 queen bedroom, huge master bath, living area, kitchen and private patio. Wall to wall windows across the entire back of the suite covered with large plantation shutters overlooking the yacht marina. From our private deck/patio we had a view of the bay across the street from the hotel. Very clean, quiet. Grounds are impeccably groomed. Did not use pool as it was a little too cool. However, the pool area was nice - plenty of chairs and nice jacuzzi. We did not have an opportunity to dine at the restaurant so, I cannot comment on that. Situated on Shelter Island which is a great location. Easy to find and very little traffic. Nice walking/running/biking path across the street from hotel which runs parallel to the bay. Beautiful sculptures, nice little playground and a fishing pier. Parking was plentiful and free. Wish we had more than 3 days to enjoy our stay. I will definitely stay here again on my next trip to San Diego.

title: “Good location - Clean rooms”
text: We enjoyed staying at this Hampton Inn. Just down the block from the subway station. Easy access for our 1 week vacation. Breakfast - Go early - Fine start for the family for the day. Gift shop onsite.

title: “Perfect Hotel on Upper East Side”
text: The Surrey is a wonderful boutique hotel. It's located on East 76th Street at Madison Avenue. This location is perfect if you plan to walk to any Manhattan attractions, such as the Museum of Modern Art, Central Park, FAO Schwartz (love that store!). The rooftop Patio is not to be missed. The weather was very hot during the day and by the evening, there was a slight breeze on the roof. At dusk, large candles are lit and the atmosphere is magical. We stayed there for 3 nights and found ourselves on the patio every evening before dinner. One of the attractions of this small hotel is that it is not located in the middle of the craziness of downtown. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The concierge recommended a few restaurants which turned out to be excellent. Will definitely return.

title: “Overrated”
text:
This hotel was adequate but I was expecting great things after all the brilliant reviews on trip advisor. Our main gripe was that although we booked a room for three of us (two of us intending to share a king size bed and the remaining person on a sofabed) when we arrived the sofabed wasn't made up as a bed (although the hotel knew to expect three people). When we tried to make the sofabed up we couldn't get the sofabed to fold out due to the layout of the other furniture in the room. We phoned reception who sent up a maintenance man who said he couldn't help us due to the kingsize bed being nailed to the floor. In the end we managed to get the bed to unfold but only after we had hauled very heavy furniture about the room ourselves. Then it transpired there was no duvet for the sofabed and only one pillow - we had to phone reception again to get proper bedclothes. Then on the second day when our beds were made up the maid (very strangely) took the sheet off the kingsize bed meaning we had to sleep right next to the duvet (which I don't like the idea of given that duvets are not changed with every traveller). We had to phone reception to get the sheet back! On another occasion the maid just didn't make up the bed (she had been in the room but I think didn't make up the bed because there were items on it). Sorry if the foregoing is a bit pedantic but the hotel did know there would be 3 of us sharing a room and the missing sheet was just strange. 
The hotel was clean enough, in a good location and the free breakfast was good but the hotel make a big song and dance about how they want your stay to be 100% and on this occasion I'm afraid it wasn't. The phone in our room also broke and the maintenance man just said he couldn't fix it, although it did start working again a couple of days later.

title: “Sofitel was so so”
text:
I agree with the previous review... 3rd floor room was like being in a bunker - dark and musty. A "city view" was actually no view. Looked straight into the wall of the mall. Worse yet was that the bathroom had not been adequately cleaned before our arrival. 
On a positive note however, the breakfast in the restaurant was very good.

title: “Generally good and polished”
text:
I've stayed here several times. Each time has been a very good experience. This hotel is located in the "West End" of DC, which is near Georgtown and GWU; not the most convenient to downtown or the Mall, but DC is small anyway. Rooms are fine, and I've found the staff friendly and helpful. They have a huge, very upscale health club attached (I was not charged to use it, but maybe that was a mistake...).
I'm surprised by the number of negative reviews of what is basically a fine hotel. There are a number of other luxury hotels in DC as well, so maybe the reviews are based on dissapoinment compared to expectations. (Ritz Carlton doesn't always run the hotels that carry their brand name, so I tend to have lower expectations than, say, the Four Seasons.) Overall, this is a fine place to stay. If you are paying top dollar, though, take a look at other choices in DC.

title: “Excellent base to see the sights and throw in some retail therapy!”
text: Good location, staff very helpful - room was great as we managed to get a room in the "Tower" section - cannot speak for the older part. Although we did not choose to eat in the hotel the rest of the factilities were good - only downside is they do not offer free wifi which was disappointing. We would definately stay there again - fascinating history too!

title: “Great Value”
text: Stayed for a week in March 2003. Was excellent value for money. Breakfast was pastries or bagels, and tea or coffee (included in the price). Stayed in a queen room which had plenty of room. Was very clean. Only thing was the room had no hair dryer. Would strongly recommend it to anyone wanting a nice comfortable place to stay. Its basic but nice!! The location was excellent, right in the centre of everything, only about a ten minute walk to times square! And one block from central park!

title: “Old World Charm and the feel of Times Gone By, Wonderful and Great.”
text: If your interested in modern formica and spending a ton of money, this is not for you, but if you like old world charm, clean, comfortable and a room that you don't need a mortgage to pay for, this is the perfect hotel for you... The New Owners were there to welcome us and they are young and charming with lots of new ideas to make the hotel better yet. The location is close enough to walk to any of the tourist attractions, and you can be in Congress in a few block walk. We stayed in one of the larger rooms more like a mini-suite and the bill was still shockingly little when we checked out. You can't go wrong staying here for business or pleasure unless your company has no restrictions on how much you spend.

title: “Exceptional view and convenient location”
text:
I had never stayed at this hotel before and to be honest I didn't realize that it would be so convenient a location when I booked it. It's an unusual set up where you enter the building and have to take an elevator up to the hotel lobby on the 5th floor. The hotel is housed on the 15-19th floors of the hotel. When we checked in they mentioned "corner view" room but I didn't know what they meant.. well.. if you stay here, get a corner view room! Two of the room's walls were almost completely glass. One view was of the river and the other towards the city. At night it was gorgeous! 
Our first night there we didn't know where to eat and the woman at the desk suggested Lou Malnati's .. for it's traditional Chicago Style pizza. The restaurant was a quick walk to blocks over.
The next day we were able to walk to Michigan Ave, the Navy Pier and back to the hotel.
That night it was a $7 cab ride over to the Hyatt Regency for the event we were in town to attend.
I would definitely stay at this hotel again the next time I visit Chicago.

title: “Lovely hotel”
text: Thoroughly enjoyed my stay. Staff are great, room large and comfortable. Rate included breakfast and early evening drinks. Free wifi too. This hotel gets it right. Others should take note.

title: “Convenient, comfortable, affordable”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for four nights with our three boys (age 8, 10, 11). The one bedroom suite with pull out sofabed in living room was enough space for us. We also had pre-ordered a cot. There was also a mini kitchen area with a sink minature fridge and microwave which was nice. The overall suite was clean including an adequete size bathroom (but keep in mind it does not have a fan so bring air freshner!)
One of the reasons we chose this hotel was based on the reviews which I can agree with now that we have stayed there. It is a "family" hotel so you can expect children to be there which can be noisy. But that is not a major issue for us. The breakfast every morning was convenient and good. Yes, it is busy and you may have to stand in line for a while but, it was free with a great location to feed your family rather than fighting a.m. DC traffic to go to an expensive resturaunt. And although you might not be able to find a table, you can always take your food back to your room which we did each day. 
The hotel is also in the middle of a shopping center with convenient stores and resturaunts we used (CVS, Cheesecake factory, Stein Mart, AMC movies across street etc.)
The only minor issues we had was the following:
-Having to get your parking ticket stamped each day
-No in-room suite or large sutie at desk for your valuables. (wanted to lock up laptop)
-Very slow elevators to your rooms, which also seemed to be the only 2
-Missing preordered items to be in our room before we arrived 
-We left a note for housekeeping on what we wanted to be done which they completely 
 ignored but still did a good job cleaning
-Slow delivery of items we requested (towels and washclothes) which we had to call for each day for more. 
Overall, we believe this hotel is a great place to stay for your family.

title: “Good location”
text: The Vertigo is a small hotel in a good location for touring the city. There is no dining room but there are a good selection of places to eat nearby

title: “Nasty dirty hotel”
text:
The Sterling Hotel was the host hotel for the North Texas Square and Round Dance Association annual Round-Up October 26,27 and 28, 2012. And, we wanted to stay there so we could have the after parties. I knew that it was an awful hotel. However, some of the rooms were to have been updated. I don't think they were. We had a two bedroom and sitting room suite. It was not as bad as some. But there was mold in one bedroom and a bad musty smell throughout the suite. The carpet was dirty and the linen on the beds in one room looked dirty and there were only two towels in the bathroom. One of our group's room had a hole in the wall where a mouse or something larger had dragged a candy bar partway into the hole. another came home with fleas and had to bug bomb their house. The list goes on and on. The elevators did not work Sunday morning at check out time.
Back in the late 80's the Round-Up was held at the Sterling, and even then the hotel and rooms were dirty. The ballroom was ok. The dance floor was not too bad. We will never go back and will encourage others not to stay in the future.

title: “Nice”
text:
Currently staying at the hotel for a conference my wife is attending. While its about 5miles to downtown, its a good location for me since I'll be exploring Denver all day while my wife is working. Its very close to the interstate, restaurants, and shopping. Free parking is a plus too, hate to spend $20+ on parking when staying at downtown hotels.
Two downsides to be aware of: If you dont have a car, be prepared to dine in the hotel as the very busy road nearby has mainly chains, but not sure I want to walk to those places (6 lanes of traffic). Also the gym is very small. It looks to be a guest room converted to the gym, that's how small it is. It has 2 elipticals, 2 bikes, and 2 treadmills. One weight bench with free weights ranging from 10-50lbs. All exercise equipment had TV's, but 3 of the 6 weren't working.
Nice though, nice accommodations, nice staff, etc..

title: “the hotel was great”
text: The hotel is situated right off times square near Toy's R Us. we got upgraded to the premier bit which was excellent. the room was spacious, modern, clean and tidy. we got free contiental breakfast and in the evening they do complimentary cheese and ham and free drinks (only in the premier bit) we paid around $299 dollars a night as we booked way in advance but throught it was excellent value for money.

title: “great location, great apartment”
text:
We stayed at these apartments after good reviews on Tripadvisor. We were 5 girls ( from 15 up to 61) and booked a 2 room apartment because we needed space to spread out and not be restricted by a hotel bedroom.
There was a kitchen (with dishwasher) and bathroom with shower.
The bedrooms were big with built in wardrobes and the beds even bigger!
The lounge was spacious with enough seats for everyone (one of us was on the big sofa bed). There was also 3 tvs.
Breakfast was brought up by the maid during the day and was ample including, bread, pastries, muffins, bagels, spreads, fruit and juice. It was plenty for us, as we were trying not to eat too much after hearing about the enormous portion sizes in NY!
It was clean, and handy for all the attractions. The building work mentioned in other reviews was mostly finished just leaving a couple of boarded up areas on the front of the apartment block.
Noise was not an issue with us, as we didnt have the air con on. (it was too cold) We even went to bed at 9ish (as we were weary with lots of walking) and slept really well, but i suppose its how light a sleeper you are.
All in all i would recommend these apartments. It only cost us about £250 per person for the 4 nights which i think is good for NY prices.
We went to see 'Mamma Mia' as well. I booked this from the official website beforehand. Right at the back for $65 each but a great clear view. 
You must go to the top of the Rockerfeller centre ($20 per person) and go on the free staten island ferry for great views of the Statue of liberty. Macys and Bloomingdales for shopping of course and go to Times square at night. Its got a great buzz.
All in all a great experience.

title: “Overpriced, but pleasant”
text:
4 nights in October, including the night before 30,000 marathoners began lining up on the street below at 5am the next day, were made a little more peaceful with the provided ear plugs. The ancient windows were single pane and while they could be propped open a few inches for fresh air, even closed they didn't adequately muffle the all-night carousers below our 8th floor little room.
Our queen-bed room was quite small, but modernized.
Staff were very responsive, eager to help with recommendations and transit questions.
We avoided the restaurant below and instead had several great meals at Lefty O'Doul's two doors away, including excellent take-outs so we could watch the first debate.
Travelocity total bill averaged $290 a night. It had promised free parking. I double-checked and found it was over $50 a night, just in time to cancel the car which we found unnecessary thanks to reasonable cabs and superb public transit.

title: “Good Value, Friendly Staff”
text:
The hotel is very large for a Holiday Inn. When we arrived, there was a line of about 10 people waiting to check in. However, there were soon three agents who promptly helped all of the customers.
The rooms were clean and reasonably sized. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The rates were very attractive given the accomodations. There was a mini-refrigerator in the room. All in all, a nice deal!

title: “Last choice , better not living there. Cheap but...”
text: Room is clean but I think there is some kind of bugs bite me on my hands arms and back, very itching and unconfortable! Room is ok , shuttle means nothing, if you have a early filght, shuttle did of go anywhere. The front dest people are ok, but did or really help. Bed sucks, there is a hole on my door, not feel so safty. No internet at room , Mac cannot get connected.

title: “The Benjamin is a Great Midtown Hotel, Will Stay Again”
text:
Have stayed at the Benjamin twice so far on business trips. There were a couple of issues on the first stay, and the manager followed up with me via email and was kind enough to upgrade me to a 1 Bedroom suite for this trip. All in all, this is a good choice for a midtown hotel, nicely appointed bathrooms, small kitchenette with microwave and refrigerator, very comfortable beds and pillows. Here is a breakdown of my experience. 
The Good:
The location is great, easy walk to the Park, Broadway, Rockefeller Center, shopping, Grand Central, etc. Lots of coffee/deli/pizza options all around for quick snacks, breakfast or late dinner
Huge suite, windows on both sides of the rooms, even windows in the kitchen and bathroom. Love the natural light!
Great king size bed with nice feather pillows and comfortable linens
Large walk in closet
Extra closet in the living room
Nice little bathroom, shower works great with good water pressure and nicely set up with a three tier shelf to put shampoo, razor, soap, etc. Had plenty of room for my stuff on a little tile inset by the window
Living room was large with a sofa (including fold out bed which I didn't use) and chair, plus a little office area 
Large flat screen TVs in both rooms, pretty good channel selection
Cute little kitchen with dishes, glasses, plates, silverware, microwave and refrigerator including ice maker. Everything I need/want for a hotel stay
Maid service was great, friendly staff and top notch service
Front desk staff and doormen were also very friendly and efficient
The Bad:
Could have used more electrical outlets to charge blackberry, kindle, laptop, etc. It was hard to reach the one available plug in the bedroom. There were two available on top of the desk, but it would have been great to have more available in the bedroom
Concierge did not respond to a voice mail request (never heard back at all)
Elevators can be a little slow to respond and are tiny
All in all, this is a great property in my opinion and I will definitely stay again for future business trips. There will always be some minor issues with any hotel and for me the good definitely outweighs the bad here.

title: “good location”
text: We always stay at a HI Express because they are consistently clean, friendly and the breakfast is good. It is surprising there are any hotels left that still allow smoking, but we took a smoking room just because that was all that was left. The room was a bit smaller than some others we've stayed in (especially lacking in bathroom counter space!), but fine for our needs. Our toilet also had issues - mostly just making flushing noises way after it had been flushed. They offered to change our room, but we had already unpacked and it was more hassle than it was worth. Our towels were damp so we asked they bring us fresh ones. We had to ask twice, but it seemed they were perhaps short staffed. I saw just about the same faces behind the desk every time I passed by. But they were all friendly and helpful, recommending places to eat and helping us navigate around town. Good place to stay because it is very near downtown and lots of good places to eat, but not right in the middle of all the hustle and bustle on Beale St. We would stay there again.

title: “Wonderful service, lovely accommodations!”
text:
The front desk staff just couldn't be any better. Courteous and prompt - personable and friendly! It's an older structure but you can tell they took pains with what appears to be a recent remodel. We stayed in a 6th floor room with a balcony overlooking the street and although the front desk staff said we may hear some street noise and if so they'd move us - we had no problems. It was lovely sitting out there and when the glass doors were closed the wasn't any significant noise that bothered us.
We would absolutely stay here again and have already recommended it to friends.

title: “Lovely view - Efficient staff”
text: Overall, a good stay. We booked via hotels.com, and therefore prepaid. In our requests (noted that it could not be guaranteed) we asked for two double beds as we are traveling as a couple with our 6 year old daughter. Upon arrival, the valet service was impeccable, worth it - but be prepared for $51/24hrs. At check in, we discussed our request with Esteve. While he was efficient, he was not overly friendly or necessarily helpful. He indicated that there were no double rooms remaining. Fine, so we requested a rollaway bed. He checked on the rollaway to discover that no rollaways remained either. So, our predicament... while we've spent many a night with our 6-year old squeezing in bed between us, we'd hoped to avoid that situation. We agreed we'd make do. (Esteve indicated that they had been giving a second room to those who were traveling in quads...we suggested that was probably not necessary for our family.) The solution ultimately was a $50 room credit - which covered all but $1 of our parking, and vouchers for the $24.99 breakfast buffet. So, in all, we were "comped" $100 for our trouble, and our daughter was exhausted enough to crash out on the floor with the feather duvet. For the price, the location was perfect - walking distance to Navy Pier. ~$10 cab to Willis Tower. Cleanliness was average - bathroom was slightly dated. Room was small, with just enough floor space for our daughter's campout and tip-toeing around.

title: “You can do better...”
text:
You can do better than the Dylan, which fails to live up to the modest hype the website aims for. This is a wannabe "boutique" hotel, from everything from the quality of the rooms to the classiness of the staff, both of which are lacking.
The rooms have an old feel to them, and that's not a compliment. For example, you'll find worn down carpets and flimsy sheets, and a TV that doesn't get good reception on any channel. I mean, what kind of hotel in NY can't get good TV reception? It's not a big deal if you don't watch TV, but it gives you the sense of the attention to detail you'll find at this hotel.
The staff is pretty indifferent, and not in a cool way. I felt like I was at Blockbuster Video. Nothing to really complain about, but not very professional. Two staffers were chatting in the lobby one morning, one of whom was in his undershirt and hadn't put on his shirt for the day, which he held in his hand.
Overall, the Dylan tries to be a boutique, but its more like an middle aged Ford Escort that's been fancied up. It's not a dump by any means, but not quite what the website would have you believe, either. I give it a pass, but wouldn't recommend it as a top choice.

title: “Vastly overrated!”
text:
We -- eight colleagues and myself -- were in Chicago end of November for a 6-day business stay and we all stayed at the W Hotel on West Adams St. Our ages range from 26 to 55 years old. There wasn't a one of us who was NOT annoyed and displeased with this hotel for many reasons. None of us had a positive thing to say about it, except that it was possible to check out and leave. 
The overall interior design is as tacky and pretentious as can be imagined. When you walk into the lobby, you think you are walking into a Las Vegas disco. There is a mirrored ball circling day and night. Various garishly colored LED lights everywhere. The color schemes used throughout the hotel are otherwise extremely dark and just plain ugly. In fact, the entire design looks like a cheap imitation of Las Vegas -- as if Las Vegas itself weren't a cheap imitation.
There is disco music blasting in the lobby and elevators 24/7. Why do they impose this on guests who have a wider variety of tastes? Why not just keep it quiet? Enough of us have our own music in iPods etc, we know what we want to hear and don't want the hotel to dictate their taste to us! 
High-Speed internet access in the rooms is a rip-off $15 per 24 hours. There is no better deal for stays of multiple days. WiFi is free in the lobby, but then you must listen to *their* choice of loud music. 
The rooms themselves are ridiculously small: The closets are so shallow, that it is impossible to hang up shirts/jackets in there and still close the door. There is no chest of drawers. There is about 18 inches space between the bed and most walls, so if you want to get at your clothes, you must do so from the suitcase. And to get into your suitcase, you must put it on top of the bed -- that's how cramped these little cells are. 
Never again. Next year it will be the boring Embassy Suites again, with its spacious rooms and breakfast included. And a much better location to boot.

title: “What a pleasant surprise!”
text:
Went to the Chicago/Lakeview area to visit family - the closest hotel was the Best Western. I really was not expecting much as it was a "Best Western". What a surprise! This hotel was fabulous. I had a 2 bedroom, one bath with a den and kitchen. The room had been recently renovated and had 3 flat screen's and a fabulous mirror that lit up! Near grocery stores so stocking a few items was easy! 
Heading up to the area this week and am staying at the Best Western Plus Hawthorne Terrace Hotel!

title: “Terrific 5 night stay for mom & daughter”
text: Took my 5 year old daughter to Chicago for spring break week and booked for $70 per night via Priceline. It's just what we wanted - great location close to bus & train stops, very clean, comfy bed, and cheap enough that we could splurge on other things. Highly recommend for solo travelers and couples who don't mind cozy quarters. Will gladly book again when I travel to Chicago on biz, and hope the painfully slow WIFI will get an upgrade by then.

title: “Great location but don't expect to want to spend much time there”
text: I stayed in this hotel for 2 nights. The hotel has a great location within walking distance to everything. The outside is pretty old and rundown looking but they have free parking. We were lucky enough to get room 109 which is the only one in this hotel that has a kitchen in it. The rooms are 1980's and could really use a redo. The bathroom had no plugs so I had to do my hair in the kitchen. The hotel is right on an alley so it is loud if you sleep with the windows opened. I felt safe and if you get over the place being a little older you will enjoy your stay. Wasn't bad and wasn't great. The rooms are really small and we actually got some giggles on how run down the place was. If you are looking for a cheap place and want what you pay for this is it. I read reviews before going and we didn't run into any drug dealers, prostitutes, or fleas so that was good.

title: “Great Service”
text: After flying all day with 3 connections due to Hurricane Irene and losing 3 days of vacation, we were pretty tired and in frustrated. When we arrived late at night the staff was very friendly and accommodating. The rooms were great and after a restful night sleep, the breakfast was just what we needed. The food was very good, hot and fresh and the wait staff was efficient and eager to serve. We stayed for 3 nights total, too bad we lost the first 2 due to the hurricane. Pool was nice along with the other amenities. The rate was was very affordable, as well as the staff prior to making the reservations. When I go back to San Diego I will definitely book here again. Thanks for being a good part of a messed up trip.

title: “We absolutely loved our stay at Inn at the Market!”
text:
After reading many, many reviews on this website, I contacted the manager directly to see if he could assist me in making plans for a short 2 night stay in Seattle for our wedding anniversary. He promptly responded with an offer that I couldn't pass up! 
This past weekend my husband and I stayed at the Inn in one of the town house city view suites. The hotel & staff were amazing! We absolutely loved this hotel and will for sure be back in the future! I have already told many friends and family that next time they're in Seattle, this is "the" place to stay! 
When we first arrived, there was an anniversary card and a special dessert for two waiting in our room! It was delicious and such a nice gesture! Typically we would go out for a nice anniversary dinner where ever we happen to be. At the Inn, there was a set of dishes for two in our room, so both nights we decided to get takeout and bring it back. Fixed up our plates and headed to the deck on the 5th floor. Amazing view and plenty of space! Even though there were other guests out there, everyone had their own space and it was wonderful!
The room was very spacious and super clean! Two big flat screen tv's... bay windows that look out on two different streets, one with partial market/water view. The location couldn't be more ideal! Steps from Pike Place Market which is always one of our favs when in town for a visit. 
Thank you Mr. Watkins & thank you to your staff! We really enjoyed our stay at your hotel and can't wait to come back! This was definitely an anniversary to remember!

title: “Very much Satisfied”
text:
I should start off by saying I booked this 2 night stay (9/6 to 9/8) through my sister who works for Starwood. This might have had some impact on the room I was given & my experience.
Check in/out was quick even though we were early for check in by a few hours.
We were on the "starwood preferred guests" floor. I don't know what that entails. I was in room 2665 which had a king size bed, desk & chair, flat screen tv (32 inches I think), sofa chair w/ foot rest, small ottoman under a full length mirror, and a cushioned bench at the foot of the bed. The mattress was VERY comfortable. The room was clean. It had 2 huge windows (corner room) which had fabulous views of boston.
The maid service was good. Replaced all towels & toiletries & tidied up. 
We used valet parking. It was about $40 a day. They ask that you give 30 minutes notice that you need your car but they will get it to you in about 10 minutes.
Internet is $4.50 for 1/2 hour or $9.00 for 24 hours. Doesn't make much sense to me but we went with the 24 hrs.
We also had some phone charges when the only thing we called was within the hotel. We probably should have questioned it. It was a couple of bucks.
The bathroom was clean. Not the newest but it was pretty nice & clean. The toilet flushed SO loudly. It was almost like an airplane. It woke up my husband one night when I used it in the middle of the night.
We ordered room service breakfast one morning. The lady who brought it was very nice & rolled it into the room & set everything up for us. The food wasn't that great though. I had a coupon for 50% off otherwise it would have been very expensive for mediocre food.
All in all, I liked the hotel & would stay here again. The negatives I listed didn't affect our stay very much and as my husband says, I am extemely picky & notice everything.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: The Donatello is in the heart of downtown san francisco, great location, the rooms are large,clean and modern . We enjoyed our stay . The staff are friendly and courteous. Close to everything including Union Square, cable car, great restaurant and bars

title: “Couldn't Have Been More Perfect!!”
text:
I was hesitant to try out a new hotel in Charlotte because we had enjoyed the spot we'd previously stayed but, the location, free internet and breakfast won me over. I couldn't have been more pleased and will stay at Hotel Sierra for all my future trips to Charlotte. 
We had a king studio room. It was very comfortable, spacious, very clean, and the decor is awesome. LOVED the bed and the shower. My only complaint was that the bed was so comfortable we had a hard time getting out of it in time for breakfast!
We came to Charlotte to see a couple Checkers playoff games and this hotel is right on top of Time Warner Cable Arena. Very convenient to all of the area restaurants and the Epicenter. Valet parking was quick and convenient--the valets were all super polite as well. All of the staff was very friendly and even the housekeeping staff all spoke to us in the halls. The front desk staff was efficient and there were no long waits at any time during our stay. We came in late one evening but needed some food and the front desk staff was super helpful in arranging for some takeout delivery for us.
The wireless internet was very fast and we encountered no issues. We also enjoyed the expanded cable offerings. As hockey fans, it's always difficult to find a hotel room with Versus on the cable system and we were thrilled to get to watch some playoff hockey without having to find a bar. Carolina Hurricanes fans who might be in town checking out the Checkers will be pleased to know the hotel has FSN, as well.
As with any hotel in this area of uptown Charlotte, I worry about nighttime noise on weekends. We heard nothing at Hotel Sierra and were able to get a wonderful night's sleep every night of our stay.
This is a fantastic and stylish hotel with a lot of little extras and a great location. I cannot recommend it strongly enough!

title: “Worried about reviews....don't....Very Nice Resort.”
text:
I, like many others, was worried about staying at this resort after reading so many of the reviews. While this resort is not perfect, none are 100% perfect. Put your mind at ease and if you are booked to stay here in the future, rest assured, you will enjoy your stay.
The resort itself is beautiful, from the fountains to the grounds, to the golf course, the lobby, all very pretty. 
The rooms are clean and very spacious, bathrooms clean, my only complaint would be the TV's which are very small and very old. But again as many have said, most people are going here to sit in their rooms and watch TV. There are nice flat screens in the lobby bar to watch the big games.
Golf was enjoyable although it is a difficult course with target golf being the order of the day on the back nine. Definitely worth playing a round. 
The waterpark was a blast, slides are fun, beware the high speed tubes will beat you up a bit from the impact at the bottom. Lazy river is great relaxing fun. Wave pool, etc etc etc. All a great time and plenty of chairs no matter what time of day you get there. I think most of those bad reviews were spring break time in which case what do you expect. It will be like that no matter where you go.
All in all, very nice place and I would stay there again in a heartbeat. Enjoy your stay! If you are one of those that find something to complain about or to trash a place no matter where you go, then yes you will be able to find some things to complain about so don't worry you will accomplish your goals as well. Maybe the walk will be too far from the lobby to the room or something like that. In which case why even go on vacation.

title: “Great location, great rates”
text: We stayed at this hotel when we met up with some friends for shopping. It's almost across the street from the North Star Mall and all the area shops. Also close to the airport. The hotel is very nice, a great lobby and out door seating with fire pits and plenty of chairs. Our room was clean, bed comfy, and noise at a minimum. staff was friendly and fast. I will stay here again next time. We got a great rate off the hotel website that was unbeatable!

title: “it's okay but don't expect much”
text:
Just returned from a trip to NY, staying in this Days Hotel at Broadway/west 94th street. The staff was unpolite (except for the concierge, great guy!!). I booked a room for my son and me, booked for double beds but got a room with one bed double sized. So as soon as I noticed this I phoned the reception and told them that a mistake happened, as I made a pre-paid reservation for a room with two beds. We're sorry this is what you can get, was the reply. And they added: we consider a reservation as a request. Excuse me??!! A pre-paid reservation for a room with two beds, considered as a request?
After I got a bit upset and spoke to three (!) people at the phone, while still in the wrong room, they decided to give me a room with two beds. I think my determined attitude made them decide to give me another room. What if you're not so determined as a guest?
The room was shabby, the bathroom dirty (and stayed dirty). Beds were clean and allright. The carpet smelled a bit. The fan/airco made a lot of noise. Okay, I used the hotel and room to sleep. And the beds were okay. So what else did I need? Maybe a staff that acted a bit more polite?!
The location of the hotel is fine, near a subway station and in a fine quiet area.
Conclusion: it's minimal, okay for the night but that's it.

title: “No hot water, staff extremely unhelpful, rooms noisy.”
text:
Awful hotel with rude staff! We were positioned on the 17th floor where we had no hot water. We advised reception, who told us just to run the tap for a while and we would get hot water. Eventually after half an hour we go hot water. We complained every day of the stay where they kept telling us it was fixed. On complaining to the manager again she said her staff had checked it and said we had hot water so we must be lying!! She compensated us with a free buffet breakfast all of which was overcooked and disgusting... 
The rooms are very noisy and you can hear conversations of other guests and housekeeping staff.
The hotel is positioned near a hospital and a busy intersection and you hear sirens and traffic constantly!
On asking reception for a transfer to the airport the next day they informed me they didnt offer this service. the next day when checking out the bell boy asked if we had transport booked or if he wanted reception to book it for us. we informed him that we had been told we couldn't book the transport, he informed us this was wrong and they could.
Staff do not want to help you! Manager unfriendly and rude. Service the worst I've experienced.

title: “Best Friend Couples Getaway”
text:
We had a great time at this distinct and special resort, but there's some room for improvement, specifically:
 - No free morning coffee, in fact a small coffee in a paper cup cost $4.10
 - horrible self parking options (e.g. long walk with bags) 
 - no ice near hotel room (guests must call room service and wait long for delivery)
 - fitness room too small/ crowded
 - no ability to make tennis reservations prior to arriving at resort
 - lots of reserved signs on poolside lounge chairs that never got used (at least 20%)
 - significant daily resort fee
Even with the above issues, it's stll a really nice resort: 
 - buildings, grounds, fountains and artwork are top notch
 - service was professional, efficient and friendly
 - food at Frank & Albert's was very good
 - loved sitting by firepit and fountain
 - free 18 hole putting course was fun and good way to enjoy grounds
 - nice tennis courts
 - comfy beds
 - lots of pools

title: “Staff was great!”
text: Room was in good shape and the staff was very friendly, responsive to needs, answered questions. It was just a pleasant place to stay as a business traveler.

title: “Old but Decent”
text: It's difficult to find an affordable hotel in Boston. This one is adequate. The rooms are small. One admonition...make sure that you don't get the room closest to the antiquated and LOUD elevator.

title: “We were disappointed”
text: We were disappointed in this hotel. First, the front desk sent us up twice to a room that was not ready and did little to help accomodate us in the meantime. Second, we had chosen this hotel primarily because of positive reviews of the swimming pool, and my kids were so excited to go swimming. The pool was great -- but it was closed for two of the three days we were there, which was a BIG disappointment to the kids and us. Again, the front desk had no alternatives to accomodate us when the pool, which actually belongs to an adjoining health club, was closed. On the plus side, the location was excellent for visiting the inner harbor, aquarium, and children's museum and there were nice restaurants near by.

title: “Don´t stay here !”
text: Rude and arrogant front desk staf. When we flush the toilett water came out on the floor. Bath tub filling up with dirty water from the sour when guest next door taking a shower. They didn´t offer us a new room and they couldn´t fix the problem. But the worst was the arrogant behavior from the front desk staf. This hotel must have new guests all the time. I can not imagin that a previous guest ever goes back.

title: “Days Inn equals A-Plus”
text: The check in was fast and easy. Every staff member I encountered was extremely friendly and polite; from the front desk, the housekeeping the security and the maintenance. The entire hotel was spotless.

title: “Great Property, Great Location, Great Price”
text:
As a Hilton Diamondm I stay in a lot of HH properties, This one is clean, convenient, and the people, especially Meagan, were really accomodating and made sure that everything we needed was taken care of.
We WILL be repeat stayers here!

title: “Good room, good location, pool lets it down”
text: Very convenient for Fisherman's Wharf, which seemed a much nicer place to stay than the city centre proper. Room was very large (especially compared to New York where we'd come from) and pretty well equipped. However, we were put in the annex, a block or so down the road, with a Denny's in the lobby. The biggest annoyance with this is the lack of access to the swimming pool because the main building has no changing facilities - and the pool isn't great anyway, located in the car park as it is. Aside from that, you get what you'd expect from a Holiday Inn. Oh, and parking seemed to be extortionate.

title: “Top Hotel - Top Location!”
text:
There's a reason the Sofitel in DC is rated the number one hotel on Tripadvisor - it deserves it.
We stayed 3 nights over Cherry Blossom weekend in April and were very happy with our experience at the hotel. From the minute you enter the hotel, there is an air of intimate elegance that envelopes you. We were quite pleased with our room, both it and the bathroom were spacious and well appointed. A top criteria of ours is cleanliness and the room was immaculate.
We got a great rate right from the hotel's website, under $200 per night. These rooms face the interior of the hotel, so if you are into views, this class of room is not for you. We asked for a high floor and therefore we got plenty of light on sunny days. The room was extremely quiet and that probably had something to do with the construction of the building, caliber of the clientele and the interior facing room. For an additional $30 per night city views were available.
The location of the hotel can't be beat, a stones throw from the White House yet far enough away from the Mall to not be inundated with tourists. The Metro is about 2 blocks from the hotel and there are some very good restaurants within a 5 minute walk. We particularly enjoyed both Georgia Brown's (Southern food) and Old Ebbitt Grill, and for something more casual the ESPN Zone was surprisingly good. There is also a Starbucks right up the block for a quick snack or caffeine fix.
We ate breakfast in the hotel restaurant one morning, but we found it semi vacant and with a cold atmosphere, there are better and less expensive choices within a block or two of the hotel.
All in all we would highly recommend the Sofitel DC and will stay again when we have occasion to return to DC.

title: “Great hotel but extras are expensive”
text:
I couldn't believe how wide the hallways were (weird I know) and the rooms are very comfortable with great lighting and effective/efficient desk areas. Bathrooms are large.
Extras get you: Wifi $13.00, onsite restaurant is a bit expensive for dinner, even the business center minimum $5.00. But this is a full service Hilton (unlike a Hilton Garden Inn where many options would be free) so you are paying for a full service Hilton. 
Obviously the number one item is the location next to University of Pennsylvania and the UPenn Hospital system.
Restaurants are with a block or two of the hotel with many different types and price ranges. 
SEPTA station is a few blocks away (we stopped at the University SEPTA station instead of 30th Street and it is a bit shorter of a walk (but may not seem like it)).
Only issue: UGH - come on: 15 or so television channels!
Highly recommended if you have business at UPenn.

title: “Perfect hotel”
text: The Hotel Metro in New York...is perfect! That's the best summary I can do! It's in the center of New-York so a very good location, the breakfast is huge and you can eat everything you want (and the coffee is free 24/24 h)! The room is changed every day and the staff of the hotel is very nice! And yes of course, the bed is BIG! And the high spedd Internet is free in each room! The value of this hotel is perfect! It was my first time in New York and it was PERFECT! There is nothing else I can say! Thank you to the Hotel Metro!

title: “At the right rate, a decent downtown hotel”
text: A busy hotel during the day with lots of meetings and conferences. Very quiet at night. Unlike the other posters, I was thrilled to not have to wrestle my bag away from a bellman, there were none to be found. Lobby is huge and clean. My Queen room was large, clean and reasonably well maintained. It took 10 minutes to figure out how to open the door of the in-room safe (pull the key straight up and a big steel plug will come with it permitting one to open the door). Breakfast buffet was typical and typically overpriced. The bar was small, but the food available was excellent and reasonably priced. For $123/night (government rate), a good deal for downtown LA.

title: “It's me and my girlfriend's new spot!”
text: I really enjoyed the whole place. And Kenya at the front desk was especially helpful! The valets were pleasant and helpful and the accommodations were pleasing. A good experience.

title: “Great Service”
text: I stay with my family for a week and the rooms were always clean, everyone was helpful specially john in the lobby telling us great place to visit and shop, also a good breakfast, the rooms are old but the location of the hotel is great near little italy and the harbor, also great rates.

title: “beautiful hotel in a great location!”
text: wow. we stayed at the hotel indigo in san diego and absolutely loved it! you can't beat the location. you walk out the lobbys' front door, look to your left, and you're practically staring at petco park. the hotel is easily within walking distance of so many great places in the gaslamp district. and if you have a car, it's only a 5 minute drive onto the island of coronado (please make sure you go to the brunch at hotel del coronado!). the hotel room we had was really nice, with a REALLY comfortable bed. we had a beautiful walk-in shower complete with a teak seat. the hotel has all the amenities you would expect and they go out of their way to please you. i highly suggest this place if you're staying in the gaslamp district.

title: “Good for a quick get-away”
text:
Good hotel to meet up with wedding group. Central location to everything in downtown Austin.
Pool looks funky, so never used it.
The mattress is a sleep number, but one of the worst quality. My back was hurting.
There was a big hair ball in the shower drain, so the water was backing up.
Employees are attentive and friendly.

title: “Chef Eugene Schlaff was very courteous and interesting. Nice job. Great place.”
text: Chef Eugene Schlaff did a great job. Restaurant had good food and great service. Riverwalk location was quiet and peaceful. Visiting from New Mexico and returning here for our second visit. Good breakfast buffet. Nice weather and shaded table outside.

title: “What A High-End Hotel Should Be”
text:
My wife and I were stuck in Chicago for "Thundersnow", the 2011 blizzard in Chicago. We stayed at the Elysian and have not had a better experience at a hotel. Ever. First, the design of the hotel is beautiful. The architecture is majestic outside, with a cool roundabout courtyard that you won't see anywhere else in Chicago. Inside, the feel is chic, accessible, and comfortable. The staff is exceptionally welcoming, calling me by name from the first check in, and happily accomodating any request I had. The room was large, with a nice sitting area, bathroom, and bedroom. There is ample closet space and I wish I could take that showerhead home with me. It was what a high-end hotel should be--it has the best of everything and a fantastic, accomodating staff.
Also, both of the restaurants in the hotel are fantastic, the Michelin two-star Ria, and Balsan. I even had food in the room and it arrived hot and perfectly cooked. Go to this hotel, you won't regret splurging here!

title: “Lobby is Nice... Room is a different story”
text:
When we pulled up to the hotel, all I could think was "Wow." The lobby is large and has plenty of comfy seating. The front desk personnel and concierge were first-class. 
Then we got to our room on the 17th floor and opened the door. Initially, I was impressed with the room. The king-sized bed looked comfy and inviting, the granite countertop in the bathroom looked classy, and the view of downtown Phoenix was a great sight. 
But once you lay on the comfy bed and stare at the popcorn ceilings or go into the bathroom and see the 80s-style wood laminate cabinets holding up the granite, the room loses its shine. 
It was a 95-degree day. Forget about fidgeting with the air conditioner, which apparently stays at "70" (it felt warmer to me). The best "air conditioner" is to close the heavy drapes!
Other than the room itself, the location is great. It is within walking distance to Chase field, US Airways Arena and bars, bars, bars! If sports and/or drinking are not your thing, then there's not much else for you.

title: “JW Must Be Proud, Exceptional Hotel, Great Visit, Why Go Anywhere Else”
text:
What a surprise to find this hotel so nice. I loved the room layout, albeit a little on the small side, but nicely decorated, good quality materials, and tasteful. It is a very comfortable hotel, clean and fresh. I asked if it was new to find out it opened after a complete renovation about a year ago. 
Seriously, I will look at rates on my next visit to Chicago, but there is no reason to stay anywhere else. 
Service was very good, the lower level lounge nice, gym very nice...I have found a home when in Chicago.

title: “Great Stay! Amazing Staff - Very Attentive!”
text: I work in television production and traveled my crew down to Charlotte from New York City. From day 1 of booking this trip, Maureen Mullen took care of us with an amazing attention to detail. It made our stay so much more enjoyable knowing everything was taken care of. The entire staff made us feel very welcome and went above and beyond to make sure we had whatever we needed whenever we needed it and I look forward to filming in Charlotte again and I know where I'll be staying. A+

title: “A beautiful spot to stay in Seattle!”
text: A beautiful hotel to stay at when traveling to Seattle. I always find the service excellent, the food outstanding, and the rooms impeccably clean. It is so lovely to find an historic hotel so well cared for and yet still modern in its response to guests. That attitude is what makes me a loyal Fairmont customer as I find this level of excellent service at most of their hotels in the US and Canada.The Olympic is a favorite and I'll be back again.

title: “Good four night stay”
text: We stayed four nights while attending a convention at the convention center, which is within walking distance. Our room was very nice, and overlooked the Camden Yards ballpark across the street. We were disappointed the Orioles weren't in town while we were, as we couldn't take advantage of being so close. Housekeeping was good and, as we requested two of the mornings, cleaned our room while we were out so I could be in the room to relax later without being disturbed. The hotel staff we came in contact with were friendly and helpful. Even though we liked the hotel, and would stay there again, there were some negatives I feel I should share to help others make an informed decision. There was a lot of outside noise audible in our room. A couple of streets outside the hotel are heavily traveled, and traffic noise, especially trucks and motorcycles were heard throughout the day and night. Also, a helicoptor would make multiple trips overhead daily and that was also heard. It wasn't unbearable for us, but it would have been nice if the room had been better soundproofed. Also, the sink is outside the bathroom, which is always annoying for the person who is still trying to sleep. Breakfast choices weren't as good the one morning we ate at the hotel. There were plain cheese omelets, no crossaints as there had been the day before, and my husband had to wait for bagels to be brought out, and then there were only raisin bagels and he doesn't like raisins; you would think there would be a choice of plain bagels for picky people like him. So you might like the breakfast, or you might not. Also, we did not park a car, but it seemed the hotel does not have enough parking, as it appeared the vehicles were parked where ever they could be, including in the area that is usually the entrance and temporary registration parking for most hotels. Cars were parked two or three deep in that area, and very close together, as well as on the street and it looked like in a narrow alley behind the hotel. Even though the valets/bellhops were very friendly and helpful, and I'm sure capable and used to dealing with those circumstances, we were glad not to have to worry about a vehicle. Not to mention that parking is expensive, especially considering the parking conditions.

title: “Affordable luxury in the very best location!”
text: Our Valentine getaway was magical in the most beautiful city in the world and the only thing that could make it better would be to stay in a fabulous hotel. The Westin St. Francis on Union Square was the perfect hotel for intimate and splendid. The location is right in the middle of everything! and the staff is from another time - our comfort, relaxation and satisfaction were their only goal. Thanks to all at the Westin St. Francis for memories to treasure.

title: “Very nice hotel in a not-so-nice location”
text:
This was my first experience with Country Inns. I chose this one primarily because it was located close to where I had to be for an early morning appointment in Columbus.
The Inn is located in what I'd call a "motel ghetto" and although I don't normally use that term in a disparaging way, in this case it fits. This nicely kept property stands in contrast to some very grungy-looking neighbors: Unkempt cheaper motels and what appears to be a former Hampton Inn that must have been converted into apartments. My first impression was not positive.
Fortunately, the accommodations turned out to be pretty much what I had hoped for: Clean, comfortable and mostly attractive. The lobby is especially impressive. My one-bedroom suite was well furnished, although there were some signs of wear here and there. The king bed and pillows were quite comfortable. The bathroom is quite dated, with just a small wall-mounted sink and few surfaces on which to set things (other than the toilet...yuck). The shower was pretty nice, however, and I had loads of towels.
The lighting in the living area could use some improvement, and the two TV sets were the most low-definition sets I've seen in a long time. But then, what do I expect for the price? I paid a AAA rate of only $58.50 which is an incredible value for the amount of space.
One other negative: This inn is perhaps 300 feet from I-71, which means constant highway noise. I knew that when I chose this inn, but it has been so long since I've stayed in a roadside hotel that I wasn't fully prepared for the racket of traffic all night long.
Still, I was impressed with this Country Inn, especially the spotless housekeeping, decent breakfast offerings and efficient staff. I'd stay here again but I if I could find a similarly priced alternative in a quieter, more attractive location I'd consider that too.

title: “Fabulous hotel, definitely will return to the New York Palace.”
text: My friend and I stayed three nights over the Memorial Day weekend. I can't say enough about this lovely hotel. We were given a room on the 34th floor, overlooking the cathedral, the view was amazing! The service was great. The location is excellent. When I return to New York, I will stay at the New York Palace again, and I would recommend it to anyone planning to visit this fabulous city.

title: “We always stay here when we go to Denver.”
