text: We absolutely love this hotel, the staff is incredibly friendly and helpful, the rooms are clean, and the evening reception is a nice treat. We will continue to stay here when we visit Denver.

title: “Perfect One Night Stay”
text:
My family and I recently stayed one night using points before flying out the next morning. 
They put us on one of the two executive floors (9th & 10th) -- the room was very modern, decor, flat screen TV, comfortable beds , and very quite despite having a few of the airport runways. 
We also utilized the hotels free shuttle that runs every 15 minutes to either the terminal or to the train station which we took to downtown boston -- it was literally a 10 minute ride to Quincy Market. 
I would definitely recommend staying here if on business or flying out the next morning.

title: “Fabulous Service (Ted!), great rooms and fantastic views!”
text:
I checked into the intercontinental for my long stay.... TED on the front desk could not have been more helpful and gave me advice and recommendations for the city of LA. He told me some great restaurants and places to shop. He also told me to come to him for anything else i may require during my stay. I was very impressed with TED and his service as he was very friendly and helpful.
I was automatically assigned a great room. The bell guy, FRANK could not have been more friendly as helped me to my room and showed me around. I was more than happy with my new home for the next few weeks! 
So far, I am having a fantastic stay with the intercontinental. The staff are all very friendly and can not offer me any more help / advice. I am especially impressed with the services I have received from Ted as i have been back to him on a few occasions to ask for assistance during my stay at the hotel. 
Great hotel staff, GREAT BAR STAFF, great stay... so far!

title: “Fantastic Rooms”
text:
My husband was staying at the Conrad for a business trip, so I joined him in the hotel. I was immediately impressed by the modern style of the hotel, and then astonished at the size of our room - the biggest I've seen in NYC. 
The front desk staff was great, the gym was good, and the location was very peaceful - near a lovely waterfront park, but far from most tourist attractions. 
My one complaint was that the housekeeping staff let us down a bit. Twice, they came in while the DND button was pressed, and both times they never returned in the day (even though we were out of the room w the "service" button on for more than 4 hrs). Eventually, after calling downstairs, we were able to have the room cleaned.

title: “Average airport hotel with a few issues”
text:
The hotel is average. Good location for airport and freeways.
The rooms are ok but there seems to be a bad dour in some corridors.
Not sure if cleaning or drainage issue. Stayed on two different nights. First room on 6th floor was ok and clean. A room we had on the 4th floor was a little dirty, the bathroom floor was dirty.
Was woken up one morning by some kind of workers' union protest. Two males on megaphones/bull horns screaming at the top of their voices about the hotel. Not really sure what the dispute was about. Free wifi but keeps cutting out. 
Expensive parking. Couple of cheaper airport parking multi storey blocks nearby(about $8.95 for 24hrs). 
Breakfast buffet not great value. Friendly reception and breakfast staff. 
Average Holiday Inn.

title: “Very good stay. Clean and a great value.”
text: Very nice and clean. Location provides very easy and quick access to downtown. The bed in my room was as comfortable as at any hotel I have stayed in. Located within walking distance to several very good restaurants. Staff very nice and helpful.

title: “Real space in a great location”
text:
Real suites, i.e. separate bedroom and living room, at a very good price considering a large convention was in town (I was part of it.) The bedroom was larger than some hotels where I've stayed in NYC. Spotless housekeeping; large, spacious bathroom; spacious wetbar in the living room. All the amenities of what you expect in a good business-class hotel, i.e. coffee maker, ironing board, TV's in two rooms, room safe, toiletries, etc. There is a small microwave oven if you want to deal with leftovers or semi-cooking. I did not check out the fitness facility, but there is one.
The location is right on Times Square across from the TKTS booth, 47th and 7th Avenue. Like many new hotels in this area, there is a very small security lobby on the ground floor that allows only guests to the upper floors. The main lobby is on the 3rd floor, helpful concierge, etc. Very easy walk to Fifth Avenue, theaters around Broadway, and subway access.
The restauruant and bar are on the 5th floor -- pretty nice, but it's too bad that these rooms don't have a view onto Times Square like some of the other hotels (e.g. the Renaissance, almost across the street.) The lights of the Square would add to the ambiance. Still, the public areas are handy and nice places to relax -- the bar quieter than the enjoyable circus at the Marriott Marquis. (I've stayed at a few of these area hotels over the years -- all good experiences.) There is also a decently-priced grab-and-go coffee bar in the lobby with good coffee, fruit, Krispy Kreme donuts, and (what I miss living in a different part of the country) a really good corn muffin.

title: “Nice hotel, good location”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for one night after returning from a cruise. The hotel was conveniently located downtown, only a short walk from Pike Place Market. The Space Needle was about a mile walk, and you can take the monorail to shorten the walk. Very friendly, helpful service at the hotel, especially the bellhops. The room was nice and clean. My only complaint was the room doors which were older and noisy when people shut them, which woke me up a few times.

title: “Friendly, clean, and convenient!”
text: Stayed two nights at the Hilton Phoenix Airport: 10 minutes from the airport and 10 minutes from Mill Avenue, south of ASU, where there are plenty of restaurants and shopping. The hotel was exactly what we needed - clean sheets, fresh towels, and the staff was EXTREMELY helpful and friendly! The 24-hour airport shuttle was only minutes away and came to get us right when & where they said they would. In fact, the airport shuttle driver took us later from the hotel to Mill Avenue for free, because we needed to get dinner and didn't have a car. I would absolutely stay here again.

title: “Nice Plan, Can the Noise”
text:
I stayed here for the great Priceline rate of $63 a night. A steal, really. It's a nice hotel. The staff was decent, not great. The pool area is very nice. The grounds are well-kept. There is a pricey restaurant, but also an Einstein Bros (with limited hours) on the grounds. You have to walk outside to get anywhere, including the gym (which is small but nice, but has a yucky locker room), which isn't so pleasant when it's chilly.
Overall, I'd give this hotel 5 stars, but for the fact that they insist on piping in loud music to the pool area, which you have to listen to if you sit by the pool, if you're just walking to your room in the tower, or eating at the poolside cafe (open on weekends this time of year). 
In a world of ubiquitous Ipods, why the noise pollution? If I want to listen to loud music, I can bring my own, thanks! 
(BTW, I had a room overlooking the pool, the windows were great--I couldn't hear the loud music at all from inside the room).
One more hotel quirk: no coffee maker in the room. I'm not a coffee drinker, but this may bother some people, you have to walk to Einstein Bros and pay $4 instead.

title: “Exceeded expectations”
text: From the moment the doorman greeted us we felt welcome and at home. The Fairfax provided many nice extra touches: fresh ice in the bucket every day, bottled water at night, free newspaper and more. We like the location very much and totally enjoyed our stay. I do recommend that visitors avoid the steep parking price and park their car elsewhere. There are garages and street parking nearby.

title: “Loved the Vagabond!!!”
text:
We had 15 women stay at the Vagabond while we attended a conference at the Cox Arena. EVERYONE loved their rooms! It was just remodeled with microwave, refridgerator, complimentary breakfast - and the staff was very helpful and friendly!!!
It was a great deal for the price!

title: “Great value and location”
text: The room was very small, but when you're in NYC you don't go there to be in your room! Got a room with two twin beds and had a cot brought in because there were three of us. The room barely fit the cot in between the 2 beds, but we didn't care - we were just sleeping there. The shared bathrooms were totally clean and the window air conditioner kept the room very comfortable. They even gave us a room with a view of the ESB when we checked in early. The location of the hotel is great. The only quirk about the hotel it the small, ancient elevator. If people from more than one floor trying using it at a time, it's very slow. We were on the fifth floor and just walked the stairs to go down. Except for checking in though, we actually had pretty good luck getting the elevator for going up. Our room was sometimes hard to open with the card key, but overall, I would definitely stay here again for the price and location!

title: “Excellent Value”
text:
I recently stayed at The Drury for two nights before embarking on a road trip. The location was OK; not the plushest of areas, but I felt safe enough. Initially I was allocated a room next to the vending/ice machine and could hear the buzz of the machinery through the wall. I was moved to another room without fuss.
The breakfast is more than adequate and the freebie nibbles/drinks in the evening were appreciated. The room was clean and quiet, albeit a little way out from the centre of town.
I wouldn't say this hotel is luxurious, but for the price you can't go wrong.

title: “Incredible hotel”
text: From the beautiful toiletries to the excellent location (across the street from the ball park!), this hotel is first class. Clean, friendly and did I mention the excellent location? I love Boston and this hotel is somewhere I would love to stay in again and again.

title: “nice location basic room”
text:
hotel was great location. just in theater area. and steps from park and New berry street. 7 eleven in next block. and you can walk any where in city.
no Swiming pool and GYM is very small and basic. i think furniture budget was cut. Lobby in nice place to have a drunk and bust always. 
free car ride around city. try that. Conceraige is very helpful . .

title: “Don't leave anything behind. You'll never see it again.”
text: The hotel was okay. Unfortunately, when I got home I realized I forgot some personal property. I immediately called the hotel and asked them to send it to me, offering a credit card to cover the shipping charges. After a week went by with no returned property, no phone calls, I called them again. I was told they didn't find my things. I called them on that, telling them I was absolutely, 100% positive that I had left it there. They told me that they would look again and call me back. I'm still waiting. I contacted their guest relations. Still waiting. I can replace my property, but it's the principle that has me irate.

title: “Ok for the price”
text: The room was ok for the price. The room was a bit small and the hallways needed a good paint job. My boyfriend went down to the continental breakfast 10 minutes before they were to close up, but they already had. Outside our window people were screaming at eachother at 6 am and when you are out till 2:30 in the morning thats not something you want to deal with. Even though I know that is out of the hotels hands. Overall for the price, it is a bed and a shower and that is all you really need when you are in New York City.

title: “Best Spot with Access To The Castro”
text: Becks Motor Lodge is Classic Hotel. Affordable, Spic and Spam clean with a friendly staff. You can catch a train quickly easy access to downtown, fishermans wharf and china town. Me and my partner just wanted to hang out on the Castro and that what we did, it just a five minute walk from this hotel. Also there plenty of good food in that neighborhood too. We will be staying there again!

title: “Outstanding Customer Service”
text: I'd like to compliment Maggie Longoria for her excellent customer service. While attending a conference at the hotel, she went out of her way to take care of me so early in the mornings. She demonstrated the traits necessary for customer satisfaction.

title: “Great get away”
text: Stayed here for a night while on a business trip and really enjoyed it! It's close to all the good Venice/Marina Del Rey/Abbot Kinney hot spots and two blocks from the beach! The decor is fun and modern and the rooms are comfortably sized with little balconies facing out. The bed was beyond comfortable and love the Philosophy brand toiletries! They also have free wifi and breakfast which is always a huge plus! Parking available for $7/night (such a deal). Last but definitely not least, the employees were all extremely helpful, friendly, and accommodation. I will definitely be staying here again if when I come through LA.

title: “Not worth Marriott's name - but Japanese Rest close by is TOPS!”
text:
Check-in was fine. The room wasn't as we had booked it, as we wanted a king bed and got 2 doubles instead. There were no more kings available. The suite has potential, but wasn't clean: the bathroom had mildew in the shower and the tables & desk had all sorts of schpeg on them ~ we cleaned them ourselves with wipes we brought. The sink & tub had broken drain plugs.
The breakfast buffet was OK, but not very good. Overall, if they are going to put the Marriott name on this hotel, they have a lot of work to do. We travel all over the world & won't stay here again as we were expecting what we have experienced at Marriott hotels ~ and that is not what we got. One really positive thing that had nothing to do with the hotel is that the Japanese restaurant close by (Kan-Ki) is OUTSTANDING!

title: “Excellent Location...hard as rock bed, elevators stuck”
text: This has got to be one of the best locations on the Gold Coast, near all the great shopping and restaurants and near the lake. Check-in was easy, but they had not left us a bag that someone had left for us, they did not send it up until the next day. The beds were hard as a rock and the pillows were bumpy, but the rest of the room was nice and fairly quite, except for the sirens. There is a modified mini starbucks int he lobby and a restaurant we did not eat in. We left a wake up call for 7:30 am on Sunday that never came. And when we were rushing to get downstairs after no wake up call with our bags..only 1 out of 3 elevators came twice in 10 minutes full to the brim each time with people who would not let us in. We hiked down 6 flights of stairs with our bags. Glad I wasn't on a higher floor. Price is about right for what you get.

title: “Highly recommend it”
text: Stayed here with my family for a weekend away. Got a great price from priceline otherwise would not have stayed here because it is very pricey if you book it the traditional ways. The staff is very friendly and the rooms are a decent size. Overall a very nice location in phila for most restaurants but a bit far if you want to see the liberty bell and independence hall etc.. I found street parking for the whole weekend otherwise their garage is over $32/day. There is no pool which is a downside to the hotel if you are there for the weekend. All in all...would recommend the hotel but only if you get a deal on the price because it is not worth more than $200/night in my opinion.

title: “Taste o' Old San Antonio”
text:
Lizardy: that's a good word for this complacent sunbaked pile. I wish I could say Fredericksburg-Roady, with all the, uh, charm that implies, but fifty dollars for a night? You can buy a lot of duct tape with that kind of money, and the owner apparently did. It was all around the doorways. The dramatically canted mirror on the wall seemed a nice touch, until I realized it was STUCK that way - I couldn't straighten it! Bathroom in well-advanced decay. Curiously lumpy pillows: what's INSIDE these things, mushrooms? But I did sleep well - gotta give it that much. I did not expect to sleep well, as right after my check-in, the neighbor started pounding and yanking his door. Perhaps he was being cuckolded. We can hope.
The clerk was efficient, perhaps because he wasted no time on things like changing his shirt. Either that, or he owned several with "Suck Head Eat Tail" printed on them. I suspect you can get a bulk discount on menswear of that sort.

title: “Excellent service, location and very accommodating with my young kids”
text:
We were originally booked in a room with one bed. I called their reservations department and explained I was travelling with 4 year old twins. The agent owned the situation and immediately upgraded me to a suite with curtains to seperate the sleeping areas. 
This is a semi-typical boutique, city, hip hotel. Not the place you would expect the staff to want to deal with 4 year old twins. Everyone there could not have been better. 
Arrival was good, door staff and front desk were very friendly and accommodating. Room was great. Room service was good throughout our stay. I requested my coffee and breakfast at 5:45 am each day (an hour before listed times) and they had no problem filling that request. 
They have seating and lounge type areas on all the roofs and they are spectacular. The furniture is showing some signs of fatigue but the setting and views make up for that. 
Good location in SF for kids as well. The trolley loops all start directly behind the hotel. You can take the trolley to the Wharf or up California and connect with North Beach, etc...very convenient. 
Parking is a block or two away but that is expected with the location. Overall, fantastic place.

title: “Average Hotel for 'Trailfinders'”
text:
Standing on the corner of East 38th Street and Madison Avenue, (a 10/15 minute walk from the Empire State Building and Macy's on 32nd Street) this was a fairly central location for the aforementioned Empire State and Macy's as well as the Chrysler Building, Times Square, Grand Central Terminal to name but a few - All within easy walking distance of the Hotel. The staff were genial and friendly. The concierge on duty the day of our departure, Jose, organised a stretch Limo which we shared with another couple as our airport shuttle to Newark. It actually worked out slightly cheaper than a Taxi would have cost. 
Our room which was on the ninth floor overlooked the gap between the buildings at the rear, with the corresponding noise from the building's ventilation systems when the window was open (which it had to be because of the heat in the room). I never thought to try and upgrade to a room with a view or one with air conditioning as I have read in some of the other reviews. For this I can't really blame the Hotel although it might have been nice to know that the option was there.
The room was clean for the most part although there was a little dirt on a pillowcase and a couple of hairs on the sheets that we could not account for. We got the distinct impression that the bed linen had not been changed but we couldn't swear to it. Other than that the room was fine although quite small. Using Trailfinders as we always do on medium-long haul trips we expected a little more for our money and it is for this reason more so than any other that we felt a little hard done by, as Trailfinders has always provided us with our expectations worth, in the past. But maybe such is the way of it with New York Hotels!?!!
However all this said, it was a great location and what problems(?) there were, they did not deter us from enjoying this incredible and wondrous city.

title: “****Warning****Don't take your family here.”
text: This place sucks and this is no place for a family to spend a weekend or a day in its infested with bugs and the police is constantly being called out not safe at all the conditions are poor and they really need to shut this place down.

title: “Wow”
text: I have a complaint...one of the elevator lights was burnt out. Everything else was absolutely perfect! The facility was perfect, it was perfectly clean, the employees were perfect, the manager was perfect, the location was perfect, etc. You could spend hundreds of dollars more and never get the quality and grandeur of this hotel. Bravo

title: “Westin in NY at Times Square”
text:
With reference to that we ended up at The Westin due to the storm Sandy on the 29 October 2012, it might not be fare to totally judge this hotel, but as our impresson was positive enough, why not. 
We were over the phone, while booking from our first hotel, Sheraton on Canal Street 370, from where we had to be evacuated, and got a promise that the given price, 399$ night, would be much lower, down to 265 if we stayed the remaining week - which we wanted to.
Once we were there, we were told "no that is not the case, the price is 399€ per night. 
That I found rather nasty. 
However Mr Jonathan Lomitola who received us, a very accommodating and nice person, said he could nothing about the price itself, but that he could give us internet complimentary. All we had to do was to sign in as if for pay and by check out this amount would be taken out of the bill.
Unfortunately, this did not happen, hence we paid for internet full out. 
That I found rather nasty.
But on the other hand, the guy who checked us out on the 4 November instead compensated the whole mess a bit by giving me a reduction on the bill. Not a full compensation but a gesture.
All in all, it is a bit negativ when money issues are handled in a greedy way.
The hotel itself is pleasant enough, not enormous or spacious rooms but clean, functional and nice beds.
Staff is overall very pleasant.
Although Times Square is not my favourit place, I simply loved the proxy to "restaurant street" and walking distance to many of my favourite museums.

title: “Fantastic accommodations and excellent service!”
text: Having just recently returned from a business trip in San Diego, I felt compelled to send in my review of The Westgate Hotel and my fabulous experience. The rooms were beyond my expections in comfort and decor, meals and service excellent and, to top all of this, the Bell Captain, Sergio, went above and beyond in providing service. Specifically, after the taxi called for us left us at the curb, Sergio directed us into the shuttle and personally drove my co-worker and me to the airport. We were totally impressed with his attitude and service and he is definitely an asset to your establishment.

title: “Business trip for eight”
text:
We arrived late in the evening. The desk clerk was courtious and helpful. Found the room to be clean and stocked with towels and cups. Everybodys room had a fridge and microwave but mine and when i letr the manager know he had them brought to my room.
A few of our party left after the first week. I asked the manager for a refund and he graciously prorated the time spent and refunded my card.
In all, i would recommend staying at La Casa to anyone

title: “International Old World Flavor with More Comforts than Home!”
text:
My husband is attending a conference, but we didn't call for reservations in time, so I looked around for accommodations nearby. After reading lots of reviews online, I decided the Taj would best meet our needs. In reality, our expectations have been far exceeded.
A quick walk through the Public Garden takes my husband to his conference, and we feel quite fortunate to be staying at the more intimate Taj. I have Newbury Street to enjoy, and the T is a block away -- Boston is such an accessible city, and the Taj is central to everything. 
The staff is courteous, attending to guests' every need. Rooms are quiet and comfortable -- I want to bring the bed home with me! Breakfasts and dinners have been delicious, and offer lots of variety. Portions are just right. Don't miss afternoon tea on Saturdays & Sundays -- a rare treat!
The Taj will appeal to travelers who appreciate Old World flavor, with attention to every detail.

title: “Great NYC hotel!”
text:
We had a great stay at the Affinia Manhattan in NYC! Chose this hotel mainly based on location, and on the terrific reviews from other travelers. Stayed one night, Jan. 20 to 21st. Booked one week before our trip through Expedia, which offered a great discount. Arrived early (about 1PM) but they had a room ready for us and we were checked right in. Staff was very helpful throughout our stay. 
We had a corner room on the 21st floor with a fantastic view of the Empire State Building (check out the picture!). Could still hear some honking and sirens, but noise was really not an issue on our floor. The room was well-decorated and clean. We didn't need the full suite, but the refridgerator came in handy for late-night drinks and snacks. Bed was large and comfortable, and didn't have that typical hotel bed smell/feeling. The bathroom was indeed small, but modern and clean. We only had a shower (which was fine) but you might want to ask ahead if you're really looking for a full bath. Loved the Aveda products and soft towels.
Can't beat the location! Across from Madison Square Garden and Penn Station (perfect for Amtrak travelers like us). Two blocks from Macy's and the Empire State Building. Quick 15 minute walk to Times Square. Close to two subway lines for heading up or downtown. Overally, highly recommended for a comfortable Manhattan trip!

title: “Great place--great service”
text:
I needed to make arrangements for several business associates and chose this Holiday Inn DFW South. Working with a representative to block off rooms there was a good and easy process and my associates said the rooms were very nice and clean and the amenities were A+. 
We will happily use them again for any visitors that we have come to our area.

title: “Highly Recommended!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for a week and after reading some of the previous reviews, I was a bit dubious. I arrived at the hotel at 1.30pm and was served by a friendly lady called Angela. After checking if my room was ready, I was advised to return at 4pm. I returned 15 mins earlier and Angela recognised me advising my room was ready.
My room was a lot bigger than I expected, especially as they had offered us a 2 double bed room, when there was only 2 of us staying! We even got a view of Broadway and Speedy's outside! The room was on a high floor so we had no problems with smoking rooms or any safety problems encountered by others. We got 2 bottles of complimentary water on the first day and everything was replaced daily, apart from the first day but a housekeeper came to check and it was replaced within one minute.
The reception, concierge and bellhops were all very friendly and helpful. The hotel is located very centrally, next to a metro stop and also 2 blocks from some fast food chains and shops and also round the corner from Macy's and Empire State Building. There is also a shop called Walgreens which is 2 blocks away, round the corner from Empire State Building, where we purchased many American goodies for a decent price. We didn't eat in the hotel's restaurant so can't comment, but Speedy's is conveniently across the road. If not, there are lots of other places to eat, Starbucks being on every street in NYC!
The only negative was the hotel is opposite some building works, so if you have a room facing that side of the hotel, then beware of some construction work which could wake you up at 7am! But if you're an early riser or can sleep through anything, then you won't have a problem!
Overall, I found this hotel to be fantastic, in a great location and I would highly recommend! Don't forget to bring some $1 bills as tipping is everywhere in this city!

title: “First Class Choice!”
text: My 2 daughters and I were visiting New York City for a week for the first time and as my husband was unable to accompany us- I was looking for somewhere central in a good location. I think I read every review on "Trip Advisor" for central New York hotels - and although this one was slightly above my budget, chose it, as it appeared to be well located and also seemed to be about the only one without any negative reviews.( We booked as part of a package only 2 weeks before and paid around £300 for the room per night which I think was probably over the odds due to the late booking) However- what a fabulous choice we made! The location couldn't have been better- less than 2 minutes walk to Times Square, a subway near the entrance, Mc Donalds a few doors down, plenty of deli's nearby to pick up breakfast and actually within walking distance of virtually all the big attractions,although New York cabs are very reasonably priced. Although on a very busy road, on the 41st floor where we were,( the hotel doesnt actually start until the 15th floor) there was absolutely no traffic noise and though it was of mainly tall buildings, we had a wonderful view over New York with the Hudson river on the right and the Empire State Building to the left.The beds were very comfortable,the room large and spacious and bed linen and towels were changed daily.I honestly can't comment on the staff as we really only spoke properly to them on arrival and departure as we didnt have any problems, but they were aways very polite,friendly and courteous as we walked in and out of the hotel..The concierge ordered us a taxi to return to the airport which was the same price as we had paid on the way there (ie $51 + the customary tip of $9)We were a bit disappointed there was no fridge ( except the stocked bar) but discovered there is an ice machine a the end of the corridor on every floor, so used the ice to add to drinks and sat drinks in a bucket of ice overnight so we had cold drinks in the morning.Our flight was late evening and although they were happy to store our luggage - it would have been nice to have been able to have had a late checkout or a room available to have a shower rather than just have to get changed in the Ladies washrooms in the reception area. Having said that - that is the really the only negative comment I can make.If you are a tourist ( particularly a first time tourist ) in New York - then this is the place to stay.We will certainly return!

title: “Overpriced but fine for work travel”
text: Just back from 4 nights at the Hyatt Regency Capitol Hill and very happy to be home. This is a hotel for corporate travelers. Room was basic but clean. I was disappointed that there was no mini fridge/mini bar in the room. Mattress was decent but the bed frame is a hard wooden box that I kept kicking and hurting my short legs on -- not pleasant. Good water pressure in the shower. Location is good and there was always a line of taxis ready to go.

title: “Great!”
text: For 4 women on vacation, the bunkbed room was fabulous and just perfect for us. The included breakfast was also wonderful and almost unheard of in New York City. We had a great time while there and loved our stay. Had a couple of burned out light bulbs which we asked several times to be replaced and got no service, but other than that we were pleased with everything.

title: “perfectly located on the water”
text:
We loved this place on the water, our view from the balcony first thing in the morning, sitting there with a cup of coffee, watching the fog disappear or sipping a glass of wine in the evening. Ok, rooms could be a bit bigger, but we got along (with 3 big bags). We liked the decoration of the room with lots of wood and a somehow 'vintage' touch. Perfect for cooler evenings: the fireplace!
Space for potential: concierge service

title: “Business Trip”
text: The staff was extrodinary, went out of thier way to ensure that I was informed and had everything I needed for a comfortable stay. I recommend this hotel due to location, ameneties, and most importantly service. Not only to I recommend The Westin but would also stay again next time in Austin.

title: “Happy Return of a Prodigal Couple”
text: Having just dosed the nearby Eliot Hotel with words of disappointment and recommended the Lenox instead, it's great to write in praise of the better hotel. You've got to love a good hotel that keeps an oversized 1950s neon sign announcing itself on its roof. Shows some humor and a bon vivant spirit. Like the Eliot Hotel, the Lenox is family-owned and run, but unlike the Eliot, the Lenox has a very big heart, a great cheery feel when you walk in, warm happy rooms, and the sense that they have thought of everything. My husband and I have stayed in smaller rooms and in the Judy Garland suite at the Lenox. We loved them both. We once mentioned to reception that we liked their choice of table clocks and they ordered one for us --gratis. We arrived on one visit off an evening flight from Europe, woke up the next morning at 4 am, and spent a few hours online so as not to disturb others with early morning TV. Reader: the internet was free and came up fast as a pitch. (At the Eliot, no such luck on their pay as you go system). The New York TImes, our favorite paper, was at the door by around 5:00 and coffee was available early in the lobby. The attached restaurant served a perfectly good breakfast, after being crowded with upbeat locals and guests the night before. The large, backlit bar off the lobby is obviously a big draw too. Upstairs, you don't hear any of the socializing below and sleep well on comfortable mattresses. In the morning, you can walk to the upscale shops at nearby Copley Place, dash into Lord and Taylor right next to the Lenox, or stroll down to La Voile on Newbury Street for something French. No more straying for us: the Lenox is perfect.

title: “Great location, but noisy and small rooms, otherwise OK”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Time Hotel (49th and between Broadway and 8th) in July. The location is fantastic. Just half a block from the end of Time Square and in the center point of most of the theatres.
The staff was quite friendly, although one of the concierges seemed very uninterested in helping us out, the rest of the staff (including the cleaning lady!) were very nice. We asked for help with getting to the airport, and the staff booked a shuttle for us. Very good!
I recommend dining at the Serafina, the cafe/restaurant in the 1st floor, as this place provided a very good breakfast at an OK bargain (20% discount for those staying at the Hotel, ~$10 per person incl. bread, croissant, jam, fruit, juice and coffee.
There was free internet in the rooms! Yup, completely free wireless lan. For those who haven't checked in there's even free internet in the 2nd floor lobby / bar.
The rooms are noisy. This is really my only negative point. There's an air conditioning unit in each room, and this unit is very noisy. When it hits its high note (approx. every 20 minutes) it feels like you're in an airplane at cruise altitude. So for those who can't sleep in a noisy environment, stay away!

title: “Best hotel in SJ”
text: This hotel is really good! It's in the middle of a very nice shopping area, with restaurants, movie theatre and lots of entertainment. I've been there several times and wouldn't go anywhere else. The only thing to be careful of is the noise. because the hotel hosts many parties, some rooms may be noisy so make sure you ask for a quite room at reception. The staff is helpful and the breakfast is good. Gym and pool are quite small but functional. Recommended!

title: “convenient location”
text: Two blocks from the hand center. Great place. Clean, easy to get to. great service. Would stay here again.

title: “Excellent Stay!”
text: Had an excellent weekend stay recenly when my wife and I visited Austin. The room, as usual, was great and the staff was very helpful. The concierge had excellent recommendations for restaurants, nightlife, and hunting up some longhorn cattle. The hotel is in a great downton area with lots of interesting shopping and small restaurants nearby. Not cheap, but you get what you pay for.

title: “Perfect Plaza Crowned Our Holiday”
text: I spent about three hours on the internet one day looking at hotels for our five days in Chicago - three hours well spent when I found the Allerton Crowne Plaza. $65 a night, for two people in a king size room with all perks and mod-cons included? There had to be a catch, but no - when we arrived we found it was the perfect hotel in the perfect location - right on Michigan Avenue near the top-end designer stores (Tiffany, Armani etc.) between the historic Water Tower square and the Chicago Tribune building, five minutes walk from a metro station. The price doesn't include breakfast but there is an upmarket (i.e. well lit and soul-less) restaurant and bar if you are too lazy to stroll down the street to one of Chicago's many brilliant eateries. Spotlessly clean, utterly modern, friendly and helpful staff, quiet, secure, and comfortable. What more could you ask for?

title: “Best hotel in town”
text:
Excellent hidden hotel especially for couples, best comfortable bedding with lots ofpillows, very modern room, the best shower in the whole world.
Very clean room and bathroom

title: “No running water, no apologies!”
text:
The good: location (for my meeting)
The bad: tiny room, no coffee maker (expect one in a $250 room!), had to travel 3 floors to find a working icemaker, took 10 minutes to check in, room offered a bottle of water for the low low price of $8! (COME on. They also offered an $8 bottle of wine for $58.)
The truly lousy: I awoke to no running water in the room! I called to the front desk and got only a "Yeah, they're working on it." No prognosis or ETA for repairs, seemed kind of surprised that I wasn't just accepting "they're working on it" as an answer. Kept pressing and finally got a "we can give you a pass for the fitness center a block away." KEPT pressing and finally got a "MAYBE we can give you a key to a vacant room that has water." You mean the hotel has water? Then why on earth didn't you offer this to start with?
Eventually I got a shower though had to go to another floor to do so. Was late to my meeting. And grumpy. And no one ever did say "sorry for the inconvenience."
Do yourself a favor and skip this hotel.

title: “Very Tired Property and Dirty”
text:
Stayed two evenings in May 2004 for a conference. Despite being a Silver Elite Marriott Rewards member, was told Executive Level Lounge was so small only Gold and Platinum could use. 
Room was per reservation, but seemed like miles away from the lobby- again especially for Silver Elite.
Room was very dated and tired as was the entire hotel. Dirty carpet in hall ways. Parking was $12 a day, which was ridiculous as other near airport hotels don't charge. 
Only positive was the bell staff (when at their station) and shuttle bus driver. 
Very disappointing and will not stay again ever.

title: “Great hotel-super location, room and services”
text: We arrived in the hotel at 5:30am but since there was only a double bed room available we decided to wait and walk around. The desk called us at 9:30am and told us our king bed room was available-no waiting til official check-in time. The room was great-very large and a super view of Times Square area. The gym is very large with lots of new cardio equipment and weights. We also enjoyed the lobby/bar area-very large and very attractive. Service people were friendly and helpful-couldn't ask for better service. All in all, a great hotel with an unbeatable location.

title: “unparalleled hotel, but we stayed in a suite”
text:
The boyfriend and I stayed at the Mayflower for just one night at the tail-end of another trip. Because we both travel so much, we are pretty picky and yet we had a really lovely time at the Mayflower; I was very surprised to log on here--after the fact-- and see so many mediocre reviews. A lot of the complaints seem to stem from the “basic” double-rooms, and while I admit we booked one for $160, because of our Marriott Platinum status we were updated to an $800 suite (which actually only goes for $240 during some weekdays) Service was EXCELLENT: beautiful furniture, one of their king “dream beds,” lots of amenities in the bathroom, turndown service with chocolates, unlimited US calls and high speed internet for $9.95, etc. The Executive Floor services, food and concierge, were great as always. 
 My only complaints: yes, the valet service can take up to at least the full 30 minutes they warn you about…apparently the cars are parked off-site. I thought the lobby was looking more worn than the rooms, but really you are not coming to sleep in the lobby. And the suite was actually fairly small by Marriott standards. But, then again, this is an older hotel and rent on this location must be at a huge premium. 
I can’t speak for the basic rooms (though from the ones that were open for cleaning on the 3rd floor, they looked equally lovely), but we had a great experience. If it’s a special occasion, and you can afford it, try to book a junior suite

title: “Business, not pleasure”
text:
I just got back from a week in San Antonio for a big tradeshow. Our company stayed at Holiday Inn, Riverwalk, San Antonio.
I had to go straight to the convention center from the airport upon arrival, so on my way to the hotel I was able to walk along the Riverwalk... So beautiful! The Hotel is conveniently located right on the Riverwalk and they have a rear entrance (with elevator access) directly from the Riverwalk. You could even take a $5 river taxi to the hotel! 
Checkin was easy and I went straight up to my room. I started unpacking and began ironing my dress shirts. One shirt in the iron snagged on the front section of my shirt and ended up burning/melting the material and ripping it! I was so upset. My favorite work shirt -- ruined by a crappy iron :( The hotel manager was happy to send up a new iron (immediately) and offered to comp continental breakfast for the week or add points (enough for one-night stay at some locations) to my Holiday Inn Account. I opted for points. There was some confusion the next day when I stopped by the front desk to collect written security that the points should appear in my account--the currently manager "had no idea" who I had spoken to the day before. After getting up to my room, I got a phone call and they had figured it out and assured me the points would appear in the next few business days.
Kinda of a hassle, but they were trying.
THe last day of my stay, my roommate woke up with three little bites on her ankle. She was convinced we had bed bugs so we ripped apart the linens and mattress pad and inspected the mattress and box spring. I couldn't find any definitive proof, but I did find some water damage on the bed skirt with mildew growing -- likely the explanation for my sniffles every morning.
Not a terrible stay, but I had moments where I wished we had booked with a different hotel.

title: “THE GOOD AND THE SUGGESTIONS”
text:
Chose this hotel for 2 reasons. Location and Marriott affiliated. Stayed one night to do the holiday thing with the kids. We are frequent visitors to NYC. We are from LI so know a lot about the city and try different places to stay depending on location. Wanted to be close to the tree so this seemed the perfect pick. 
THE GOOD:
STAFF WAS JUST LOVELY. SO HELPFUL. SO FRIENDLY. CAN'T SAY ENOUGH NICE THINGS ABOUT THEM...THANK YOU!
The restaurant on site "Opia", although independent of hotel (I believe) was great. Food was excellent and atmosphere was wonderful!
Rooms were clean and efficient. You didn't need or want for anything. 
Beds were comfy. :)
Flat screen TV. 
Plenty of storage space. 
Location was close to everything. Quick walk to many major attractions. 
THE SUGGESTIONS
I am not one to complain too much, especially b/c I am so loyal to Marriott, but instead of giving the negatives, I will give a few suggestions.
1. Ask for a room that is not ON 57th Street. The traffic noise was pretty bad and made for a rough night sleep. But we managed. :) 
2. Skip the comp breakfast or go super early. The room they host the breakfast in, although nice and clean and warm, is beyond small for the amount of people, who like us, are late risers and rush to breakfast before it ends, lol. You can eat comfortably in the Opia restaurant if you want to pay for a nice breakfast. 
3. Check-out is a busy time and the wait for the elevators can be a little long. Small elevators so they fill up quick. Just be patient. :) 
Other than that, this was a nice hotel with an exceptional staff. Thanks for a lovely stay!

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: Hotel is centrally located, near many of the city's tourist sights. Registration staff friendly and helpful. I'll stay here again on future trips to the city.

title: “Did we stay at the same hotel?”
text:
My fiancee and I visited this Ramada the first weekend in December. The rooms were clean and we had no problem checking in or out. There was a security guard in the parking garage at night as well as closed circuit cameras so we felt safe. The location is convenient to most of the attractions we wanted to see.
The breakfast, however, was not exactly what was described here. It was 3 types of sugary cereal, stale bagels and donuts. Oh, and bad coffee. That's it. Given the reviews here, I was expecting something slightly more substantial or at least tasty. Plan on eating breakfast out or bringing your own food to keep in the fridge in the room unless you love donuts.

title: “Dirty and not safe”
text:
I stayed with a large school group. I think there was pee in the corner of the stairwell. There were beer cans in between 2 adjoining rooms. One room smelled of marijuana. Hair on one bed. Hair in the tub.... No blankets on the beds (you had to find them in the closet). Extra pillows had no cases. Something yucky smeared on the bathroom wall. And, probably most dangerous, cords would just fall out of the outlets in my room. When trying to get it to plug in, the whole outlet would wiggle. I could not get my phone to charge in the room because the cord fell out every time I plugged it in. I ended up charging it in the bathroom. 
I would never go back. It's a dive.

title: “Great location, room, and hotel”
text: We stayed here for only one night but wish it had been longer. The location of the hotel was perfect for our family of 4 ... we were able to walk to the Park, Central Park Zoo, FAO Schwarz, and, most importantly,Gray's Papaya! The staff was very accommodating; we were arriving from a hotel in Brooklyn and when I contacted this hotel, they allowed for an early check-in. The one-room suite was ideal for us with our two younger boys (5, 8) and the kitchen area was was perfect. The room was very clean; the bed was very comfortable; and the hotel was very quiet. We didn't hear a peep from anyone else in the hotel! We will DEFINITELY stay here again.

title: “Excellent hotel but loud AC fans”
text:
Very nice hotel, located in a new, quiet part of North Phoenix. 20 min. drive from airport in off-hours.
Friendly, helpful staff. Lovely, hot breakfast (eggs, pancakes, oatmeal) made to order with a great variety of fresh fruit, breads, cold cerals as well. Beautiful rooms, spacious baths ($10 per person but well worth it!!). Grill also serves dinner beginning at 5 PM, pricey so you might want to drive to other restaurants at a nearby mall.
My only dislikes:
Very loud roof fan engines outside an entire side of the hotel. Make sure you ask for a room on the side of the hotel facing AWAY from these fans, which sound like a freight train. Also, the AC vent outside the elevators do not work properly (or perhaps just not opened during my stay). Very hot when you stand by elevators.
But overall, a great hotel at a great price!! And one of the BEST breakfasts you will ever have at a hotel!!

title: “Wonderfully Comfortable, Convenient & Friendly!”
text: I am not a fan of this particular chain of hotels having experienced some dumps around the country associated with this brand. The Ramada Eastside is the exception. First of all, the staff is awesome! A special thank you to Julie at the Front Desk, the woman put up with a lot yet managed to stay cheerful through her shift. The housekeeping gentlemen was always quick to deliver toiletries, towels and what nots when needed and I swear I think he lives there :) I was there for a week so I got to witness their professionalism for quite some time. Second, the room is compact but nicely appointed...and the bed put me into a deep, dreamy slumber every night. Only thing I did not like was that the chair kept on hitting the bed due to the small space between it and the desk (note to hotel: you may want to re-arrange that work space area a bit). Other than this little annoyance, it was a great experience and the price was right.

title: “Nice hotel...good views”
text: This was a serviceable hotel with very good views of the monument circle (which was closed off while we were there). Good service and clean. Only issue was with the Cooling system, we cranked it all the way downa dn it still didn't get overly cold. other than that, we had no issues with the hotel.

title: “Just as good the second time”
text:
This is our second stay at this hotel and it lived up to our previous good impressions. While the entrance and lobby may not be as grand as some, this was more than made up by the friendly staff and the excellent rooms.
We particularly liked the fact that we could do our own laundry and the views from the top floor bedrooms are just typical NYC.
We'll go back to this hotel next time!

title: “Excellent choice”
text: My wife and I stayed a night here, we received a great greeting from the entire staff. The grounds were very well maintained. The boardwalk is right at the door step. We will be back and recommend to all our friends.

title: “Stylish, comfortable, affordable hotel”
text:
First of all, the location in Washington, DC, is ideal. The hotel is located in the Capitol Hill area of the District, just a few blocks from the United States Capitol grounds. The hotel itself is a former Holiday Inn but it looks nothing like a Holiday Inn these days. It has been completely renovated and updated and has turned into a swank and modern, but comfortable and unpretentious, hotel. The only drawback (and it was not even a big deal to me) is that the on-site restaurant is not open yet; it is still being remodeled. The hotel does offer a complete in-room dining menu for visitors who do not care to venture out into the District for a meal. The prices are a bit steep, as one would expect, but for some it might be worth the convenience. Every member of the staff that we talked to was incredibly personable, friendly, and helpful. One of the bell captains even gave us his cell phone number in case we were out elsewhere in the city and were unable to find a taxi to get back to the hotel. He was willing to call for one and have it sent to us, wherever we might be. The room was attractively decorated in modern brown and light blue hues, with complimentary Aveda products in the bathroom, and a half dozen down pillows on the beds to sink into after a long, tiring day of exploring. The hotel also has a rooftop swimming pool bordered by a huge deck. There are plenty of deck chairs for guests, as well as several huge, bed-type loungers with tons of pillows. The pool is open from 10:00am to 10:00pm, and on weekends the rooftop grill is operational. Guests can sit by the pool and enjoy burgers, hot dogs, and the like. We spent one evening on the deck, enjoying some peach mojitos and the comfort of the pillowy lounger.
This hotel is highly recommended for location, comfort, cleanliness, and the awesome staff. I will stay there again on my next trip to DC.

title: “DO NOT even think about making a reservation here!”
text: We booked a Vertigo Queen room at this hotel a few months in advance of our trip to SF. When we arrived to the hotel we were told that there had been some glitch in their booking system and they did not have a room for us. Very matter of fact about it. No other explanation. When I looked down at their desk I saw that they had also done that for several other people. I had read some so so reviews of this place with similar horror stories, but I thought how could that happen to us. My sense is that they overbook the place thinking that some people will not show up. Very poor management philosophy. The only reason I give them one bullet rating is they got us a room in a "sister" hotel nearby and paid for our room. Fortunately we booked through Orbitz and I got a call that my credit card payment was being reversed. The other hotel we stayed at was certainly not even close to the kind of room we expected when we booked at Hotel Vertigo. I will save that review for that hotel. Very poor management at this hotel. DO NOT book a reservation here. You may not have a room when you get there.

title: “For Washington DC $$, its a good bargain”
text:
We stayed the week before Easter and had a great experience. Our room was more than adequate, since we were rarely there for more than a few hours a day. The room was cleaned every day, with fresh towels. The bed was comfortable. For two people, we had plenty of room (12x12), with a decent sized closet. Ask for a mini frig before you show up. It was nice to be able to relax with something cold in your room after a long day of sight-seeing. Plus it is nice to be able to store left-overs from the night before. The temperature was just right, thus we did not need to worry about heat or air conditioning, and can't comment on that aspect of the hotel. Sure the place is old, but it shows its age well.
It has to be one of the most convienent places to stay. Not only easy walking distance to the mall, but a whole slew of bus stops to anywhere in the city within a one block radius, and 2 blocks from the metro. There is absolutely no need for a car if you don't plan to travel outside the DC area.
The morning breakfast place in the hotel is very convenient, with lots of freshly made hot meal choices. We always showed up early to "beat the rush", that was never all that crowded anyway. It was just a bit on the pricey side, but not outrageous considering the convenience.
The attached lunch and dinner restaurant was always crowded, including the outside seating. We never tried it, had too many other "fancy eating places" to go to.
Considering the next least expensive place we found while researching downtown hotels averaged $175, the $99 price tag was a real bargain for what you got. I would have no qualms about staying here again.
On another subject: I have to say that we had a great experience with all the workers who make things go in Washington DC. Everyone we had contact with, from the bus drivers, hotel staff, wait staff, museum staff, everyone, all these people were considerate, friendly and helpful. Washington DC is a unique American city that everyone must experience at least once.

title: “wonderful luxurious hotel”
text: This hotel cost more than I usually pay, but I stayed here because the conference I was attending was at the hotel. I loved it! It has an old fashioned elegance and charm. My room was gorgeous, large and extremely comfortable. I loved it that the windows actually open. Great attention to detail; nothing felt shoddy or mass produced. Near some excellent restaurants; Lebanese Taverna 2 blocks away has great and very interesting food-try the marinated baby eggplants with pomegranate seeds in the stuffing--! and First City cafe across the street is dynamite at all hours. The hotel is right on Rock Creek Park, and 2 blocks from the metro station. Loved it!

title: “Perfect for overnight stay in LA”
text:
Booked one night at this hotel through work with a staff discount rate. Complimentary shuttle bus from airport to hotel every 15 or 20 minutes, all day and night. Bus also stops at 1 or 2 other hotels on the way and very efficient, always on time.
Plane arrived at 7 and couldn't check in until 11 as no rooms were available. This is understandable though as the hotel was full and they had to wait for people to check out.
The reception staff were very kind and always saying hello. Joe the concierge is brilliant, happy, funny and fantastic at his job. He literally goes at a hundred miles an hour, organising and booking tours for people constantly and efficiently. 
The room I was given was at the end of a hallway and perfectly sized. King sized bed, clean, very comfortable, good pillows, flat screen tv, room service, hairdryer and basic amenities (hairdryer and toiletries) also a safe. 
Location is great for those overnight travellers but there isn't much at all around the hotel. A Mcdonalds, couple of gas stations and an internet cafe and restaurant across the road. If you go further down the road though Im sure there are more options but I wasn't fussed and got Mcdonalds for dinner. 
I would give this room a 5 if it weren't for the tiny blood stain on the top of my blanket cover and the shower shooting the crap out of me. It didn't spray, it shot out like 3 hard water pistols.
Checkout was simple and very fast.
Overall this hotel is perfect if your just in LA before another flight.

title: “Great DC value - good location & full kitchen”
text: Just a few blocks from the National Mall / Lincoln Memorial, the State Plaza Hotel has been a clean, convenient place for myself & son. A full kitchen in each hotel room and next door Foggy Bottom Market + 24/7 CVS lets us get milk, juice, yogurt, cereal and other food and have breakfast before we started our day touring the Capital. Nearest Metro is 10-15 minute walk (Foggy Bottom) and CVS sells SmarTrip cards. Beds are comfortable, lots of clean linens & blankets, attentive service, complimentary toiletries, and fast room service. This family friendly place did result in one early wake-up when I heard a parent calming a toddler having a fit at 6 am, so not soundproof (but few hotels are). Good safety / security for buildings. Will come again for next visit.

title: “Best Budget Hotel for Business”
text: The title says it all. This is a great find for a business trip on a budget. The room was clean this includes a clean bathroom, mini fridge and microwave. The internet was easy to access. The desk was spacious and the office chair was a nice touch. The Hwy access is perfect. The staff was courteous and friendly.

title: “Abhorrent service.”
text: I had an unexpected issue with my car as I arrived, and the valet service was vile and reprehensible. I inquired about parking my car in the garage until car service was available the next day and they refused. I had to get my car towed to a nearby public pay parking. I have never experienced such unaccommodating personnel and will never stay at an establishment that employs those who encourage me to,"Just start it again...just start it again." The hotel should consider changing their recorded phone message that states that they are 'friendly and helpful', because that is far from the truth.

title: “Can't beat the deals that can be found here.”
text:
I have stayed at the Courtyard several times now. I book through priceline name your own price (avg $50 2 1/2 stars) I enjoy it everytime. The location is great, the staff is great, the price is great. They do serve tea and coffee in the mornings. 
I would suggest finding a garage to park your car. The hotel charges $26 for uncovered parking but it can sometimes be a mess. If you know you won't need your car (and therefor the in and out privileges, there are garages to park for around $12. 
It is a tad annoying to always need a key card to get up to the elevator so I had to give the desk the names of my friends who would be in and out visiting so they could get keys to save me the trouble of having to be downstairs when they arrived.
All in all.. it's a good spot.
Try priceline for a good deal! Was far better than their Marriott Friends & Family rate.

title: “Very Nice, in the heart of Fishermas Wharf”
text: Very nice, clean and recently remodeled. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was amazing. Definitely recommended.

title: “Fantastic!”
text:
Apart from the check-in mix up (we were sent to the wrong room - someone was still staying there!), we had a wonderful time!
The hotel was located close to Union Square (it was closer the Orchard Hotel). The staff was polite, helpful and wonderful (they even let us borrowed their staff microwave). Not to mention they provided free internet service (they got WiFi too but bringing a laptop to the States was such a hassle). The room was clean and tidy.
What more do you want?

title: “excellent place with great staff”
text:
I was very surprised to see all the bad reviews on this hotel when i went to write this review. Everything that has been said about this Holiday Inn Express was way different than what I experienced. From the minute I walked into the lobby they were there to take care of me. It was a quick check-in and their attitude was wonderful. There was an exceptional young man named Jon at the desk.
My room was in great shape, the housekeeping was fast and complete, and the breakfast was much better that the other local hotels I have stayed in. I will most definately be staying at this hotel from now on. I would recommend it for anyone willing to pay just a tad more for better quality and service.

title: “Great Hotel Restaurant”
text:
We had a room with a view of Mission Bay. The room was spacious and clean. It had 2 queen beds and a sitting area with a sofa bed and coffee table. There was also another table with an ethernet cable on it. The hotel has free WiFi, but the WiFi was really slow when using my laptop. My iPhone kept dropping the signal. I ended up giving up when using my phone and just used 3G instead.
We were most surprised that the on-site restaurant, Firefly, was really good. We went for lunch when we first arrived to San Diego and sat outside, overlooking the marina. Everything we ate was delicious. We went again for dinner on the last night of our stay. Again, we had a great meal and sat outside. 
Another bonus is that you can see the fireworks at SeaWorld from the pool area. I would stay at this hotel again because of its comfortable rooms, the yummy, convenient restaurant, and its proximity to San Diego attractions.

title: “Best place to stay in the Village”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel 3 times over the past 10 years and find it very suitable for what i need when I'm in New York. This hotel is all about location, location, location. There really isn't a better place to stay in NYC and the village and surrounding neighbourhoods are perfect. After a day of sightseeing/Shopping it's a great place to retreat too. You really feel like you're a local when your walking around. The hotel rooms are very small and if you get an internal room, which we've had twice. This can make them dark and abit claustrophobic. We have stayed in a front facing room too but these are noisy and we found it very hard to sleep. The art deco theme in rooms is nice and the bathrooms are clean and have everything you need. There's a TV, Docking station, hairdryer and safe in rooms but no tea making facilities or minibar. The only negative I really have is that everytime I've been the hallways have always looked really scruffy and in need of a paint. The subway is about a 2min walk away.
I'm sure I'll return to New York and when I do I'll definitely stay here again. I can't think of a better place in the area for the price.

title: “OK, but watch out for parking”
text:
This hotel is located in a rather strange, circular building. Until a few years ago this was military property and in fact the airport was an Air Force base. The room we had was very average but we got it at a really good rate ($50) on Priceline. Two beds, three people. There was an internet plug in the room no charge, but wireless was like $12. Wireless was free in the lobby. Go figure. The worst thing I could say about the hotel was that the carpet in the hallway had ripples. That's always a turnoff for me. Nothing is within walking distance.
 After we got there we found out about the mandatory parking fee. $11 overnight, $3 for short term. We were told it's a city parking lot. So overall we had no complaints about the deal we got. If we'd paid the "standard" rate of $180, however, I would call it a real loser.

title: “Slamming doors all morning!”
text: The location is excellent, The rooms are spotless, exceptionally comfortable and well appointed and the staff were very friendly. The problem is we got no rest at all. The construction wasn't the problem ironically, the problem was the room doors have absolutely no sound proofing and the housekeeping staff were literally letting the doors behind them slam all morning from 8 am to check out it was a continual stream of slamming doors, knocks, elevator bells and talking that could be heard clear as a bell from bed. I don't know how anyone can sleep here without ear plugs. I choose a hotel on the UWS and on the side facing a brick wall for some silence, but I got the loudest and inconsiderate hotel experience ever. I would have extended my stay, but in the AM I realized there was no rest to be had. The front desk was very nice about my complaint and apologized, but they couldn't do anything as I prepaid on hotels.com. I can't recommend thia hotel, because all I use my hotel in NYC for is sleep and that need was not met here, it's sad too, because otherwise it's a great hotel.

title: “Hawaiian-style paradise on Mission Bay”
text:
I had a great first trip to San Diego at the Catamaran. The Hawaii-inspired resort put me instantly into a vacation mindset - there was no transition time from the work week I left behind into my relaxing week at the Catamaran! I spent lots of time wandering from the jacuzzi to the pool, to the bay, to the beach. I tried paddleboarding on the Bay one afternoon, rented a bike for several days and rode around the Pacific and Mission Beaches and Mission Bay. Whenever I took a drive to do sightseeing, it was always easy to find my way, and traffic was not a problem. I enjoyed the food I ordered from room service and loved the variety of restaurants that were a short walk from the resort. All of my interactions with the staff/personnel were great and they took care of whatever I needed. My room was kept spotless. The grounds are well-maintained and it is enjoyable just walking around the resort in the morning or at the end of a busy day.
The only thing that could have been better was the cycling rental - this may be common in the area but I was surprised that they only had beach cruisers, and that some of the bikes were a little rusty or in need of repair. Check out your bike carefully before heading out. But the staff are very nice.

title: “Much to be Desired”
text: I recently stayed at the Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile for a medical conference. Upon entering the lobby, I was very impressed with the upscale decor and ambiance. The staff was friendly, prompt and courteous. That’s where it ended. The rooms left much to be desired especially at a rate of $300/night (which was a “discounted” conference rate). The décor was very dated. The bathroom had marble countertops, but nothing else. The bathtub had rust and mold was growing within the caulking. The carpeting, décor and lighting in the hallways was so dark, dim and gloomy that I thought I was in an Alfred Hitchcock movie classic. The ice machines did not function properly, so I had to travel up several flights of stairs, to find one that actually worked. Granted, these were small problems, but I had higher expectations for the brand name and price. However, on a brighter note, the location was superb!

title: “Very Helpful Staff”
text: Stayed there last week, and although our room was small, this hotel boasts a staff of friendly and helpful people who did all they could to make our stay pleasant! Fun place to stay and great location!

title: “Nice hotel with neat perks”
text:
This was the first time I had ever stayed in a Drury Hotel. After using Trip Advisor for advice we decided to stay at this hotel for four nights for a long weekend Spring getaway. 
The price was fair (and when we got there we actually found out that our room would be cheaper then expected) and the area seemed decent, with easy access to the I-85 highway and downtown Charlotte.
We also needed a place to stay with our 30lb. dog, which there are no extra costs for having a dog, which was another nice perk. They also gave us a room with easy access to the rear door so we could walk our dog in and out. 
A hot breakfast was available every morning, free fountain drink are available during the day along with freshly popped popcorn. The pool and hottub were open and in good shape and all together the property was kept in good condition. 
The room was decent. The decor was a little out of date and the exterior wall was brick, but it was clean and housekeeping was attentive. The walls are a little thin so we would often here our neighbors coming and going, but it wasn't that bad. The bed was comfortable. 
Wireless internet is available and they even offer a free 24-hour helpdesk for internet issues which we used. They solved the connection problem quickly.
The parking lot is secure and gated and you must use your room key to enter and exit. There are many places to eat within walking distance and the university area shoppes are near by, so there is plenty to do. 
After this experience I would stay in this hotel again if in the Charlotte area.

title: “Best Sales Department”
text: I did not stay at this hotel but I find hotels for our group to have classes. Sandi Robinson in sales was very helpful and made sure all bases we covered. The person from my office that was involved with the group said it was very clean and there were great restaurants close. For entertainment, everything was withing walking distance. I would highly recommend this hotel for a group. Thank you Sandi!

title: “Great short stay”
text: Stay over one night this month and was extremely satisfied. Great location, next to Metro Center. Room was quiet and comfortable. We will stay here again during our next visit to DC. You can get to anywhere you want to go from this hotel. Staff very helpful and friendly. Super great buffet breakfast.

title: “Still under renovation”
text:
Stayed here for one night before international trip. It is still undergoing renovation and we got an old room. Small with poor temp control and outdated bath. It was clean but the wallpaper was bubbled. At 8 am the renovation crew started drilling into our outside wall with a jackhammer. It was deafening. We had to get up and out early. 
The front desk people were helpful but the lobby is almost non-existent with nowhere to relax. This is a bare bones place that is in transition. We have stayed here before and the real draw is the location and proximity to Times Square and Broadway. If you can get a good price and don't mind some hassles then it may be OK for you. Don't expect much.

title: “Mesa is ok”
text: This is a no frills facility. It is clean and has a nice pool but a Hilton it is not. I have stayed there many times but my wants are simply a clean bed and linen, somewhat quiet, and a nice pool.

title: “Decent Rooms, But Horrible Gym”
text:
The location is next to art museum and convenient to Market Street and nearby tourist areas. The rooms are of relatively decent size and the building has a lot of corners, so there are a large number of corner rooms, which is nice if you can get one on a high floor.
However, if you are looking for a hotel with a good gym, don't stay here. The gym is extremely small and there is almost no equipment. I got a better workout by doing pushups in my room. And the pool is not even big enough to swim in.

title: “Bad Choice!!”
text: From the valet parking to the front desk check in this place is bad. First sign was the lack of a bellman to assist in the parking of our car. I actually had to go in to the hotel and ask. Next upon checking the guy at the desk told me I reserved a deluxe queen room when Imhad reserved a deluxe king. He said they were all out of kings. So I went back to my car and got the print out showing my room choice. When I got back to the desk he said he did have a deluxe king room on the 3rd floor. So we got into the tiny 3X3 elevator and went to our assigned room only to find a small dirty window overlooking a dark air shaft. The bathroom was dated looking with a small bathtub and plastic curtain. I called down and complained that this was not a deluxe room so the guy agreed to move us to another room on the 3rd floor with a view of Broadway. Yes this room was better for sure, but still not deluxe. The room was loud with all street sounds entering the room. I could clearly hear the tv in the room next door and all conversations as well. The room is worn with tears in the leather headboard and worn room furniture. The lighting is stark and offers no reading lamps. But the most odd to me is the lack of drinking glasses in the room. I hav never been to a hotel that did not have drinking glasses. When I called down to ask about this they told me they would send some up. Well after waiting over 20 minutes someone arrived with champagne glasses. I said I did not need champagne glasses only drinking but he told that's all they offer. There are small plastic cups by the bathroom sink. I would expect glasses in a hotel that is charging $400 a night. The bathroom has no where to put anything so we kept our toiletry bags on the floor and in the main room. There are so many nicer places in New York. I think this is the worst property I have stayed in ever. Do not book a room here unless you have to and then be prepared for a bad experience.

title: “Perfect”
text: Stayed in a Gold Coast Suite for Valentine's Weekend; went in with high expectations from all the reviews here, and as I have stayed at the other 5 star hotels in Chicago. Everything from the hotel, to the service, to the food was flawless. I honestly can not think of one complaint. I usually ignore reviews like this, that are over the top, but the hotel is over the top. Anything else is a far removed second place. We at Brunch at Balsan, and had some drink's at Bertrand's and were very happy with everything there as well. I can not comment from experience on the fitness or spa area as we did not utilize it, but I am certain from the rest of our experience they are fantastic as well. If it is in your budget and you are considering staying here, do it.

title: “Five Star Weekend”
text:
The employes are eager to please. The room is large, cozy, with a fireplace, nice touch.
Fabulous bed, best night's sleep in ages. 
Wine and cheese Happy Hour delightful, very conducive to chatting with other guests, also very good breakfast.
Surprise great treat, the contents of refrigerator in room are complimentary.
Walking distance to Union Square and Restaurents.
I highly recommend this charming boutique Hotel.

title: “Fantastic hotel!!”
text:
We stayed at the Marriott Wardman Park for 3 nights in June 2008.
The hotel is in a fantastic location, with the metro virtually next door and lots of shops/cafes close by.
The zoo is also walking distance making it a great place for families to visit.
We stayed in the 'newer' section of the building, and the room was great- very spacious and very clean-and great toiletries!
The surrounding area is also very beautiful and safe- great for taking a long stroll!!
Overall, we had a fantastic stay at this hotel and I have no complaints. I will most definately be staying at this hotel again when I next visit DC.

title: “Best Hotel”
text: We just got back from New York and stayed at the Duane st. hotel. It was amazing! Central to soho, canal street and rebuilding of the twin towers. The room was so clean and the beds are so comfortable. The staff are absolutely incredible, so helpful with everything. A delicious breakfast was also included in our stay. I would most definitely go back to this hotel at my next New York visit.

title: “Great Location but a few minor issues”
text:
Stayed last weekend, needed a hotel near Union Station and the Capitol, &the Hotel George was in a perfect location, less than 5 minute walk to the station and a bit more than five to the Capitol; also close to the Mall, Supreme Court and Library of Congress. 
Balancing the other pros and cons, the hotel is worth a visit. Other pros:
Most comfortable beds.
Friendly hotel staff.
Complimentary wi-fi and $10 free mini-bar with Kimpton In Touch free membership.
Free afternoon hot chocolate, and wine reception afterward.
Quiet rooms.
Uncrowded fitness center.
Taxi always waiting outside front door.
Fair room rate.
Cons:
Satellite tv that went out often due to wind, most frustrating.
Bathroom shower tiles/grout could use some clean-up, though bathroom was otherwise spotless.
Sofa showing a bit of wear, room not as cutting edge as the usual Kimpton vibe.
There is also a good restaurant located right at the hotel, Bistro Bis, very convenient after a long day on the town.

title: “Perfect!”
text:
I recently stayed at the Hotel Metro for 4 nights. I had booked a Premier Room as all the Contemporary Rooms were sold out and was pleased with the room we were allocated – on the 10th floor, with lots of wardrobe/draw space and a lovely new bathroom with huge walk in shower and a choice of three shower heads!! 
The hotel is in a great location, just a couple of minutes’ walk from Macy’s. The free wifi came in very handy and we also used the business centre to print out some tickets – we were pleased to be able to use this service free of charge. It was a bit cold for the roof terrace while we were there but we went up and had a look anyway – there were great views of the Empire State Building and I’m sure it would be lovely to sit out there in the summer.
It was nice to have breakfast included in the price, and while it wasn’t anything special, the toast, croissants, cereal and yogurt set us up for the day. Like some previous reviewers, I wasn’t too happy about the usage of paper plates and plastic cutlery (so bad for the environment!), but that’s obviously not a big deal.
Housekeeping came every day and the room was always clean. We didn’t have a great deal of interaction with the staff, but those that we did talk to were friendly and helpful. The night before we left we asked the front desk to arrange a taxi for us for 5:45am and it was ready and waiting when we came downstairs the following morning.
I would highly recommend this hotel and haven’t a bad word to say about it. I’ll be looking forward to staying here again next time I travel to New York.

title: “a really luxury hotel,excellent location,fantastic value!”
text:
we were in Los Angeles Omni hotel for 4 nights and we were surprised from the high level of this hotel.everything was perfect:
1)very elegant and high class hall.
2)fantastic rooms ,full of comforts,elegant and spacious.
3)staff very kind and avalaible,always ready to help you and satisfied all your expectations.
4)wonderful location,very close to Walt Disney Concert Hall,Moca and convenient to join very quickly all the most important and known places in L.A.
5)very good breakfast,we had the continental,rich and various for only 16 $.
