we have a very good souvenir of this hotel,well managed and with a fantastic staff.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
I was worried after reading reviews of this hotel. People are either too picky or born with a silver spoon. 
This hotel is nice. Beds comfortable, staff nice, and good location(near 30th Street Amtrak Station).
We paid less than $80.00 a night, w
hich was a bargain for a great hotel.
Recommend it and would stay again.

title: “Wonderful Hotel- Always enjoy staying here”
text: We decided to spend our New Year's in SF. After checking many hotel sites for prices, we turned to Hotwire saw a great room deal for a 4 1/2 star hotel, and by the comments figured it was Le Meridian. We were frequent Park Hyatt customers, so were anxious to return. Well the hotel is the same, with high quality standards. We checked in quickly, and had a nice room with two sliders opening to a view of the Bay Bridge and Ferry Building through the Embarcadero office towers. Nice big bathroom and really comfortable bed. Room was spotless. Our bags were delivered by the bell man, and he filled the ice bucket before he left us. We had contacted the concierge before arriving for help in making brunch reservations, and what a pleasure it was to deal with the concierge staff- very friendly, helpful, and professional. Would definately return to this property, it is very relaxing to return to after a day out in the city.

title: “Good IND airport option”
text:
Pros:
- very close to airport, the shuttle gets you there in under 10 minutes
- hotel has very new appearance
- room was good size and super clean, one of the cleanest I've seen
- staff was friendly
Cons:
- breakfast (except for coffee) was absolutely terrible. The omlets and other items were cold and tasted awful
- as others mentioned, you will probably get a wake-up call from a FedEx plane at about 6am
- gym is small and has only very basic equipment
Overall, it's a very good airport hotel and I would stay here again. If you are just staying the night and especially if you have an early flight, you can't beat it. As others mentioned, you are in the middle of a field so your dining options are pretty limited. If you are staying in the city longer, I would probably check out the options downtown.

title: “Lovely, relaxing hotel”
text: Stayed at the Excelsior in October 2006. We wanted somewhere out of the hustle and bustle of NYC yet close enough to be able to walk into the madness and the Excelsior provided that. The room we stayed in (915) was medium size and very clean and comfortable. The staff were extremely helpful and pleasant and I could not say a bad word about the hotel. I would definately staff there again. We found a fantastic cafe a couple of blocks down on Broadway and 82nd called Cafe 82 which I would recommend. The area where the hotel is is lovely - National History Museum just opposite, Central Park 2 minutes walk away and subway also 2 mins walk away. Very convenient to everything, yet relaxing at the same time. Highly recommended!

title: “First Rate Hotel in a Great Location”
text: Our four night stay at The Blackstone was first rate in every respect. Our room was ready for early check in on arrival. This heritage building has been beautifully restored. Our lakeview room was spacious and comfortable with modern decor. Great beds and bathroom (shower only). Spotlessly clean, as were the hallways and entrance lobby. Friendly, helpful staff. Excellent location close to the Art Institute and Symphony. An easy walk to the Chicago Architectural Foundation store where bus tours of the city's architectural heritage are available. Glad we elected to spend the little extra for a lakeview room. The view from the 12th floor over Grant Park to the lake was lovely at sunrise and through the evening. We tried the restaurant for lunch and enjoyed our meal.

title: “Amazing Service”
text:
Probably the best level of service I've experienced - every member of staff was a fountain of knowledge. The hotel itself was immaculate and set in a perfect location. The only complaint I have was the level of noise from the housekeeping staff. Unfortunately, our room was right next to a supply closet and the maids were constantly slamming the door and crashing things around in there. We were told it would stop around 10pm, and it did quieten down a little, but there was still the occasional room-shaking crash through the night. We were offered another room but it was late and we didn't want to have to move at that point. Still, other than that one complaint, everything was great!
ps. didn't see a single dog!

title: “Very nice hotel, relatively quiet area”
text: We booked this hotel after reading the positive reviews about it on TripAdvisor, and we were not disappointed. The hotel is located at Park Ave and 39th - a nice, relatively quiet part of the city. The room was immaculate, fairly spacious, and we looked right out onto Park Ave - great views! I loved the clean, fresh smelling toiletries and the fact that you could heat your bath towel! You are even provided with a green tea machine instead of a coffee machine in your room - it was all very relaxing. The only drawbacks were that there was not a hairdryer or ironing board in the room. However, I would absolutely stay here again and would recommend to others looking for a hotel in this area.

title: “Location, location, location!”
text:
This hotel is in a great area of down town Chicago. Everything is within walking distance, shopping, dining, the "L". You name it, it's close by. Our room was neat, clean and had a great kitchenette. New GE stainless steel refrigerator, and microwave made reheating the awesome leftovers from Maggiano's easy-peasy. Our suite room had a large king-sized bedroom with a large flatscreen LG television. The bathroom had a granite countertop sink area, large closet with a safe and a clean bathroom with a large shower/tub and toilet room. The living room had a comfortable pull out sleeper sofa and a desk area. The kitchen has a nice granite counter top peninsula - great for eating and stashing all of our shopping packages. 
We were very concerned when there was a sign in the lobby and another one as we exited the elevator on our floor, offering us earplugs, in case we needed them, available at the front desk! What? Why would we need earplugs? When we saw that our room was right next to the elevator bank, we knew why. A gentle humming of the elevators was our constant companion. We had even requested not to be near elevators on our reservation form. The outside noise was not an issue for us, we were on the inside or backside of the hotel. This was our only 'complaint' of our visit. We would make sure that we did not stay in room #312 again, or any other room next to the elevators.

title: “Great deal on airport parking, clean and comfortable”
text: We had an early flight out of indianapolis so decided to stay one night here. The hotel has a great deal on parking--$20 for 10 days of parking (if you stay the night). Since we booked the hotel through hotwire, it ended up being a total bargain. Rooms were spacious, clean, and comfortable, check in was a breeze. Airport shuttle left promptly in the morning. Would definitely stay here again

title: “Fantastic Staff and a Wonderful Valentine's Weekend in NYC”
text:
The W Hotel downtown has a fantastic staff! The doormen went out of their way to take care of our bags, find a taxi (not always an easy task by ground zero), and advise us on the best way to get around.
The concierge staff were extremely responsive, answering questions prior to my arrival and arranging dinner reservations on the spur of the moment. Not to be outdone, the cleaning staff were particularly friendly as well.
Its a new building and the room was larger than I'm used to in NYC however some of the hallways were quite dark, its party of the trendy atmosphere perhaps but it made my significant other feel uncomfortable.
BLT, the restaurant in the lobby was also fantastic... I ate the BLT burger and shared the Tuna. Great staff there as well!
Overall, thanks for a wonderful stay
- Cameron

title: “Great experience,staff, & location, worth the money.”
text:
My husband and I decided to stay at the Sofitel Philadelphia after reading reviews, comparing and contrasting this hotel with others in the area. We were torn between the Palomar and Sofitel but decided to go with this one. We reserved a package that included free parking, so upon arrival the valet took our truck and parked it for us which was definitely a plus. The lobby is very classy and upscale. It's modern and inviting. There is a lounge/bar/restaurant when you come in, so if you like to stay up late and like to hang then you have that option. Our check-in was very speedy and the staff was wonderful.
Funny part...my husband and I along with another couple we didn't know were trying to use the elevator and thought it was broken because it wouldn't go up or down. Well, duh, apparently we were supposed to use our card for access. At least I can say the hotel is very safe and without your room key you can't expect to get very far! When we got to our room we found it was VERY spacious. The bed and all the trimmings was ridiculously comfortable! Basically...it felt like you were sleeping on a cloud. Your body sinks into the softness and it feels like your floating. I slept SO well! I could've slept for days. On top of that, the bathroom has a shower and a nice large tub so if you want to shower or bathe..well you have both options. 
The location of this hotel is excellent! It's pretty much right next to everything. Restaurants, shopping, sites are right within walking distance so once the valet parked our car we didn't need it anymore. We had reservations for Fogo de Chao and it only took us seven minutes to get there. Did I mention the shopping that's around the area? For me that's a MUST. H&M is right around the corner along with Express and a variety of other stores. I loveddd that we were able to walk everywhere. 
In addition, when we got back to our hotel room from dinner we were greeted with a cute little tray of delicious desserts and a welcome card that basically said, thanks for choosing the Sofitel. I love things like that! The extra touches are important in my opinion. Also, after you check out you are allowed to leave your car parked with their valet until 6p.m. free of charge which I think is pretty awesome. That way, if you want to shop or check out some of the sites around the city you don't need to worry about paying for parking again. The only thing that would make this hotel even more amazing would be a pool! I would be pretty happy with that. Our package included free breakfast but we had to leave a little bit earlier because I wasn't feeling well, so I can't comment on the food..but if it was anything like the service then I'm sure it has to be amazing. I look forward to staying here again, this hotel is right up my alley.

title: “Bare Bones Hotel”
text: Hotel lobby has reception desk and a business center just inside the front door. Small restaurant for breakfast and evening cocktails and dining. Rooms are very stark in their symplicity and most have only showers. Biggest problems were with the doors to the room which stick and have to be slammed to close. The first room we were given would not lock because the door was out of alignment. The other problem was with the card entry system. The cards which allow entrance to the room and use of the elevator were constantly failing and had to be reprogrammed at the front desk. The staff was friendly and very helpful. The main thing this hotel has going for it is it's central location particularly if attending an event at the convention center. Would probably make a different choice next time.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text: This has been one of my best experiences in a hotel. Staff were very accommodating and very helpful, brilliant value for money. Rooms were spacious, beds comfortable. Great location. Every thing we needed for 5 days we were in NY. If any criticism we had to queue for breakfast on the first day but we worked in all out, but hotel does have a breakfast on the run offer worth taking. Ditto to all the other great reviews!!!!!Well Done Hampton Inn Times Square North

title: “Not Good”
text: This hotel is really quite bad. Undoubtedly one of the worst ive stayed at. I was put on level 1, it potentially may be much better on higher levels as I've heard they may have been more recently renovated. The room was very small, which I can dealwith, but everything felt very worn and drab. The bed was not great and the hallway had a bad smell. It really felt quite creepy in the hallway and the community room felt like it had sat there suspended in time from the 60s. The positives -it is a budget hotel, it is in safe and quite location and close to central park and The people working in the hotel were all lovely and the clientele seemed decent even though you felt like you could be in the middle of the Bronx in the 80s.

title: “Location and quality”
text: What can I say-on the beach in PB? It's not the Ritz, but for a quality room, AWESOME LOCATION, good customer service, and comfortable night's sleep-this is the place. No, I wouldn't spend all day in my room, but its San Diego-why would you? Microwave, fridge, nice shower, comfortable bed, and you can fall asleep listening to the Pacific Ocean with the next morning's surf session waiting for you!

title: “Cockroaches in the bed!!!”
text: My wife and I stayed there for one night in mid March, room 464. In a prior review someone mentioned cockroaches in the ceiling... Well imagine discovering an inch-and-a half cockroach amidst your bed sheets, after you slept in that bed all night - Yuck. This place sucks!

title: “Top Pick for Biz Travel & Conferences”
text: This is a terrific hotel for business travel or conducting business conferences. We have done business here for many years and the service, rooms and conf. staff at top notch first class--actually world class.

title: “Incredible Staff at This Hotel”
text:
I stayed 9 nights and left on Thursday May 26th. I was in room 312.
I am in the travel industry and I was in San Francisco for work.
Although I think the rooms at your hotel are a “little tired” and need some updates the staff make the hotel one of the best I have stayed in for a long time.
I travel extensively for my company, in fact 10 months of the year, usually out of the USA so I am in many hotels worldwide.
Each member of the staff at the Diva went out of their way to assist me with anything I needed. The front desk people are truly incredible, also the room attendants and maintenance personall.
Apparently the hotel is undergoing big renovations with new carpets, furniture and wall features so I cannot wait to return later this year to see all the room changes.
The hotel is in a fantastic location as well!

title: “Better than previous reviews”
text: Based on the reviews I read I was anxious that I had made a bad choice, but the Manhatten hotel -Times Square was a great choice. The location can not be eat. We were able to walk to Rockefeller Plaza, Radio City Music Hall, Times Square and Central park. It is one block away from a subway station. There is no in room wi-fi. but we did not find it to be a problem. The computers in the lobby were available at various times during the day. Staff was helpful Two week after Sandy we had alot of questions about what was or wasnt happening and staff was great. . We got a double bed room. It was clean and in good shape. If you want a quiet room , no outside or hall noise ask for 2129, it was a great room.

title: “Loved this hotel! Great Location!”
text:
Due to a change in our travel plans (originally 3 nights booked at the Algonquin through bidding Priceline) turned into 4 nights without a room for our first night. Algonquin direct pricing was way too much to get a room there for that first night nor did we have any luck bidding for the Times Sq area... so we expanded our search to bid in the Empire State Building area.....and luckly got the Affinia Dumont.for our first night in NYC. Beautifully decorated "large" rooms with kitchen. Great location (way better than Times Sq for shopping Macey's), easy walk to sights. 
Having had the opportunity to stay in two hotels....much preferred the Affinia Dumont over Algonquin.

title: “Excellent hotel downtown LA”
text:
The hotel has a modern architecture style, with round towers and panoramic elevators. it's itself a tourist attraction. I stayed on the 30th floor. Awesome view of other towers. Staff is polite and the coffee shop at the lobby can solve your food problems for breakfast and other meals. Very good food, indeed! Excellent room, clean ,new, spacious etc
The location is not so great if you have children, or stay there over weekends and holidays. It gets really desert around the hotel, not welcoming you to walk around, although it's near the Walt Disney Music Hall , the opera etc...For business must be a superb location, however.

title: “2 bedroom suite”
text:
Stayed here, as we required a 2 bedroom suite. We only had 1 bathroom, so be sure to clarify if you need 2, as they do exist at this hotel. 
The furnishings are a little odd in the living room - the couch and chair are made for smaller people that we are! Yet the dining chairs were somewhat oversized. Anyway, it was sufficient for our 5 night stay. The curtains are very heavy and held onto cigarette smoke. This was mentioned to the staff and freshened before we returned that evening. 
Walking to Times Square is only about 10 mins. I quite liked the neighbourhood that this hotel is in. The Amish Market up the street was great for fresh food, and the new deli on the corner came in handy. The Irish bar next door was a little too convenient some nights with their outdoor terrace upstairs!
Overall, if you're looking for a 2 bedroom suite, then this hotel offers it with a good location and a good amount of space for you already stretched NYC dollar.

title: “Nice upgrade”
text:
We were fortunate enough to be able to upgrade to a larger corner room...that extra room was really nice with 2 adults and 3 kids. They had a refrigerator we could use that was great! Nice room. Workout facilities were also nice. Did get crowded in the morning for the cardio equipment. Unfortunately no pool....fortunately no need, we were way too busy. Friendly staff. Location was not that ideal, but manageable. 
Only Complaint- I had to call the Hyatt customer service line to try to verify which of the many Hyatts in Chicago I was booked. I have stayed at each of them before. The help line was a nightmare. I at first got a live person, who when I asked I just wanted to verify what Hyatt I was staying sent me into Voice recognition hell. 15 minutes later I got the simple information I needed.....you are staying the the Hyatt on Wacker.

title: “Not a nice experience...”
text: Unfortunately we had a bad experience at this hotel. I had asked in advance for a feather free room. When I arrived all the pillows and the duvet were feather. On complaining these were replaced with three very small polyester pillows (each) and two nylon blankets that were literally full of holes and did not arrive in sealed packages but were just slung on the bed. In addition the room had a 'wet dog' smell. It just didn't feel clean and when I complained to the hotel's staff they just shrugged their shoulders and said it was all they had. The only good things I can say about this hotel is that the bathroom was fairly new and that it is in an excellent location.

title: “The rooms are too expensive to not be fully furnished.”
text: I had a double queen room. There was a very compact fridge and no microwave in the room. For the price I paid I expected a little more luxury. You also have to pay for breakfast, nothing free there

title: “Nice”
text: Went up to Indy for a overnight getaway. Check in was a breeze, place was clean, neat, updated. Valet was pricey..........but when isn't it? Got a great deal with my AAA card. Capitol View on 11th floor for $89 including breakfast for two. Hotel restaurant for breakfast was a tad slow on keeping food stocked, but no big deal. Location is ideal for downtown anything. If I had to name one thing I would change it would be to update the bathrooms.

title: “Awesome experience”
text: Stayed here celebrating a 60th birthday, and never felt more pampered. Hotel has a rooftop pool with beautiful skyline views of NYC. Norma's restaurant is pricey, but worth every penny. There is a hidden little burger joint inside the hotel near the bar, where the food is to die for. I do highly recommend this hotel for a week or weekend of being made feel as if you are the ONLY guest there!

title: “Lacking at best”
text: Well, the rooms are small which I knew from reviews. Not a problem. They do conserve so they request that you re-use your towels for 3 days. We didn't have a problem with that; however, they took our used towels the second day and didn't replace them the following day, nor did they replenish toilet paper, replenish those tiny bottles of shampoo and conditioner, or clean the coffee cups. A light was burned out by the entry way. Forget trying to apply makeup if you are female because the lighting is terrible. I made the reservations on line and specifically requested a room with a "tower" (Tower of America) view. I got a view of the roof of the 1st floor atrium and pool. They don't honor your reservations or requests in that way. The hotel is on the riverwalk, but it is VERY far from all the restaurants and shopping if you are walking, especially with young children. Again, that was not an issue with us because we hoped to use the river taxi, but it is not worth the money because I see no perks of staying there with all things considered. Oh, the hotel restaurant is mediocre at best. I don't know what kind of eggs they used, but they didn't taste like any eggs I've eaten. The hash browns were questionable. I told my husband that McDonalds was better and that is sad. We are not picky people at all. But for the price, you are better off staying elsewhere. We will not stay there again.

title: “A decent place to stay”
text:
A nice enough hotel, in a good district. Bed linens were very good (a big thing with me). The room was clean. Breakfast was reasonably priced, and cooked the way I askied for it.
A couple of beefs - there was the usual sign in the bathroom about saving the planet by not asking to have towels washed, but no place to put damp bath towels, face cloths etc. Also, while fuming over the internet daily charge, I watched a TV commercial advertising the free internet connections at Marriott Courtyard (a less expensive line) hotels! This strikes me as a needless irritation to customers on Marriott's part!

title: “Good clean hotel right next to the freeway.”
text: Stayed here during the Miramar airshow. It was a fantastic location which allowed us to walk to the show and enjoy the $5 margaritas! Even though its practically on the air base we could not hear any noise from out room at all, total silence. which was sad for me as I love jets but i guess that would be a plus for most people. On the other days it was great to be straight on the freeway and to San Diego city in 20 mins. Also the night we arrived the new manager made us feel right at home instantly and was very good to us. Also right across the road is a great chinese restaurant called Chin's. Would stay here again no worries.

title: “Awesome”
text: Venice on the Beach is a wonderful hotel situated in a perfect area. We loved our stay in Los Angeles so much and a lot has to do with the wonderfulness that was the Venice on the Beach Hotel and its manager Greg. Greg was so helpful, always ready to answer any of our questions and was just a really friendly guy - he made us feel so welcome. Venice on the Beach is literally located on the beach which is awesome and is situated in the nice area of Venice. When we booked it we were a little sceptical in that by staying in Venice we thought we may not be in the "heart of it all", however once we travelled to the where all the "action" is, Hollywood etc we were SO glad that we had chosen Venice as our area to call home. It was nice to be able to drive into the crazyness and awesomeness that is Hollywood and Beverley Hills etc but it was so refreshing knowing that we could go back to peace and quiet each night in Venice. We travelled all over LA including, Beverley Hills, Hollywood, Santa Monica, Anaheim, Laguna Beach, Redondo Beach, Newport, Malibu, Calabasas etc and loved every moment of our holiday and we also suggest that you hire a car if you want to visit as much as you can in LA! Would recommend Venice on the Beach Hotel to anyone and everyone, it is perfect!! Will stay here again :). Also our rooms were perfect. Perfectly maintained, elegant and cosy. The beds were the most comfortable beds we have ever slept on also!!!!! Free Wi-Fi is also a bonus oh and the free car-parking.

title: “Nice Place”
text: This was the second Double Tree we stayed in. It was nice. Didn't seem to have the up keep as the previous one. But still very nice and comfortable.

title: “"Wingate Wyndham NYC" is a great place to stay!”
text:
Absolutely loved everything about our stay here! One of the very nicest staffs ever! Everyone was so kind and helpful and they really seemed like they cared that we truly enjoy our time in New York. The rooms are so nice and clean and the beds are super-comfortable! The location is the best...we were so close to "Macy's", "Tic-Tock Diner" and even "Times Square".
Felt very safe in this neighborhood.
The breakfast was very good...lots of items to choose from and they had "4-Star" coffee!
Would definitely recommend this hotel and we will certainly stay here if we return to New York for a visit!

title: “Clean, safe, fabulous Midtown hotel with really friendly and helpful staff.”
text: I traveled to NYC for a few days of leisure. First let me say - the hotel is definitely not a 5 star hip and trendy hotel - BUT - for a heavily used NYC hotel across from Penn Station - it's affrodable, very clean, and quite safe. Cleanliness - they passed the behind the toilet test with flying colors. The Bed - The bed was soft, fresh and also very clean. The Kitchen - Yes, the room has a kitchen - including a stove and a refridgerator. The View - It's NY so the view was of other buildings but who stays in the room in NYC? Noise - there is a firehouse next to the hotel so if you aren't used to city noises, you might want to request a room on the ther side of the hotel. I was on the 10th floor and it didn't bother me at all - but I'm from a big city. Room Service - the room service was pretty good and the staff were very friendly. Problmes - the only problem I had was with the heating. At some point at the beginning of my trip the temperature drastically dropped 20 degrees which resulted in a drastic change in my room temperature. It was pretty chilly. At first I assumed the radiators needed to get going but that wasnt the case. Anywho, I mentioned the problem to the front desk on my way back in from a late night show at about 11. By 11:10 the engineer was in my room - sealing the A/C, checking the other windows and adjusting the heating units. Turns out a window was open at the top, and heating units needed a little fine tuning. He was very nice, very knowledeable, and quickly fixed the problem in about 10 minutes. It was warm and toasty for the duration of my stay. Convenience - If you are looking for a hotel within walking distance of Times Square, all that shopping, most of the major shows and nearby Penn Station (it's literally across the street) - you should definitely stay here.

title: “Best Location Near Union Square”
text:
After reading other reviews, I reserved a room in the Club Level (Floors 27-32) at this hotel. It was a wonderful room with a 180 Degree view of the Bay and the city. The location was perfect for us as we were right on the bus line at Powell & Market and right across the street from the Nordstrom (Westfield) Mall and only 4 blocks from Union Square. The staff was the friendliest I have ever experienced to include the housekeepers, the wait staff, the concierge and front desk staff. The 2 night trip couldn't have been nicer.
The hotel is very contemporary inside with stark, minimalist decor. The Bed and Breakfast package we booked included a plentiful morning buffet breakfast and as a club member we had access to the club on the 31st floor where appetizers, desserts and drinks (and honors bar) were served from 5pm to 11pm Sunday - Thursday. A continental breakfast is also served at 6:00am in the Club Room.
The only slight negative was that we were surprised that there was no coffee maker in the room, but that was minor. The room was spacious with a very comfortable bed and flat screen TV. A perfect getaway!

title: “Pretty Nice Hotel”
text: Considering that this is right by LAX, I think it is one of the nicest airport hotels I have stayed in. However, we did have a problem during check in. I booked and guaranteed a king non smoking room; however, when we arrived, all that they had was two doubles. Also, there were no wash cloths in the bathroom. The bathroom wasn't that fancy either; however, it was clean. Other than that, the room was nice and the beds were very comfortable. There was a great view of the runways and you couldn't hardly hear the noise from the planes. I've stayed near LAX before and this is by far the best hotel I have encountered. I would probably stay here again if I had the opportunity.

title: “excellent location, excellent sleep quality”
text:
Great location, specially if your first time in NY. The hotel is near by Brodway theaters and shops, Moma and Rockfeller center.
Service is excellent. Staff is extremelly friendly and helpful. Rooms are ok, they call this hotel "boutique", but it's not, furniture is worn. Rooms are very small, but it didn't bother us at all. Shower is great and bathroom is spacious.
Sleep quality is great: comfy pillows and bed, dark windows.
I ordered breakfast once and it was very good, except for the "hot chocolate". There was no chocolate in it. The restaurant is always very busy, might be good.

title: “Elvis Presley visit”
text: While dated and in need of some basic repairs (the power points were loose), we enjoyed the stay. The room was spacious and the hotel situated close to the attractions we wanted to see. My only suggestion (and this is for all the hotels we have stayed in on our trip in the USA), try providing real milk in the rooms as opposed to the powdered milk :(

title: “Never Again!”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for a week in May 2006. We had been to New York several times previously and we chose this hotel because of its proximity to the Lincoln Centre as we had booked to go to three operas. The location is fine - not the best bit of town, but quite acceptable and safe and the room was very spacious. However, the price was far too high and I felt that the room was dingy and unappealing. The bathroom was even darker and very old fashioned and the lobby doesn't have a welcoming feel about it at all. While we were there various groups of young people were staying and so the entrance area always seemed to be full of luggage, people and noise. I did not think it was up to what I would consider to be Holiday Inn standards and I would never stay there again. I did try to change hotels after a couple of nights, as we hadn't paid in advance, but unfortunately it was around graduation time and most hotels were full.

title: “This is our "Official Hotel" going forward, when we go to Bmore....”
text:
BALTIMORE is one of our favorite getaway towns in the east coast, this hotel made it special....We were very impressed after recently staying in a Fairfield Inn that was not to lovely, and the suite was sour :( ....This location is exceptional, from the moment we arrived the staff was attentive, professional, and extremely friendly. The valet staff ( Jospeh and others were great), front desk (Makeba and Santia) sweet as pie, even the maintenance guy Tony was very helpful. They assisted us in every way possible, and referred many places to eat and go....The room was amazing for this property, very clean, airy, and well decorated. We missed the breakfast but they referred us to a place that was incredible across the street ( Miss Shirleys/ see review). 
The location was walking distance to most of our favorite restaurants and inner harbor attractions. The valet parking is a tad expensive yet worth it, for convenience. We decide we will probably only stay in this property going forward during our future Bmore visits.
 Wish we had more time to stay long but we'll be back...

title: “decent room but BAD service”
text:
stayed here for 1 night and during check in, the front desk guy was very rude and unfriendly. no smiles, throw the credit card on table, sulking face. 
rooms are ok but had an overwhelming sanitizer smell. yucks! we used coupon for $50. so it is ok value for such a room.

title: “great view and fun place to be”
text:
We enjoyed our stay very much, especially the fantastic views from both sides of the building which is def the hotel's USP. the rooms were ok and the eye catcher of course the top to floor windows and the mini bar. we liked the mini bar.
other than that the outlets are a fun place to hang out at be it the le bain on the roof top which was my personal favourite, or the uber cool standard grill with yummy food and cute salt and pepper shakers ( we bought a pair before we left ).
so if this is what you are looking for when coming to nyc you are definitely at the right place!

title: “A Classic Resort! Elegant Design. The Wright Stuff!”
text: Please visit this timeless walk in history! The venue is private and quiet! A gem in the desert is the Arizona Biltmore! The weather in November is warm! Lounge around the pool or sit on the patio and relax! The management and staff knock themselves out! What a delight!

title: “Adorable hotel with great service.”
text: We came to the Town and Country with a large group for a 3 1/2 day convention. The hotel is was so cute, very clean and the service was great. They have flower gardens all over the grounds and 3 pools to choose from. Pati in the restaurant was such a great server. She was helpful if we had questions, friendly and made you feel right at home. The only thing I would say is that the rooms are very small. While they are very clean it is a tight squeeze.

title: “Good value close to Times Square”
text: This hotel was a real find and I would definitely go back there again. It's only a few blocks from Times Square and is above average compared with other hotels of a similar type. We arrived early and our rooms were not ready. The front desk was very helpful and stored our bags until our rooms were ready. This allowed us to go out & explore NYC. When we returned all the paperwork was ready and check-in and bag return was very speedy.

title: “Diamond in the rough”
text:
This hotel is in the heart of San Francisco. The rooms where very clean and tidy. Recently redone. There is only one very small elevator and is quite tight by the time you get your suitcase in there. 
The staff were extremely friendly and helpful. My room was serviced daily. It is a old hotel but has a lot of character.
There is a bit of homeless night life outside but I never felt scared and i am a solo female traveller. You just walk past everyone and it is fine. 
There is a deli right across the road where you can get bread and milk and other esentials that you may need.
All in all I had a great stay at this hotel and would most definately stay there again on all my future trips to San Francisco

title: “great location!”
text: This is an old hotel but they did pretty good upkeeping this. We had a great time here. Location was perfectly located and everything was walking distance. At the end of the night, we relax at their lounge which had a billiard area where we played pool and darts...Would def want to stay here again when we visit Chicago another time

title: “Top Notch Hotel! Should be 5 Star!”
text: Recently returned from my 2nd stay at the Hotel Commonwealth (HC) and I highly recommend! I travel to Boston often, and usually stay at the Four Seasons because it is closer to my headquarters, however, decided to return to HC for a change from my usual routine. Honestly, I believe this hotel to be very close to that of the Four Seasons quality. The Commonwealth Room (jr. Suite) is huge and comfortable. 2 TV's, 2 phones, huge comfy king bed, Wi-Fi, great decor, extremely clean, (especially enjoyed the L'Occitane products, again, same as you'll see at the Four Seasons). The setup of the room is especially nice, as you can separate the sleeping side from the "Business/lounge" side with a huge curtain if necessary. Also, loved that the bathroom has a door separating toilet from bath/sink/dressing area. The service was impeccable. Front desk extremely courteous and helpful. Loved the nice touch of a personalized letter at turn down, thanking me for returning, along with some yummy treats. Gym is a tad on the small side, and that is the only partial negative I have of this hotel. The location is great, too. This hotel really feels like top notch luxury, with a bit of a twist (decor is not your average hotel decor). I can't wait to return during my next business trip.

title: “Nice hotel-Bad service”
text: The hotel was nice,the location was good,but the service was very bad .

title: “An Absolute Delight”
text:
We stayed at The Plamer House on the weekend of Jan. 23-24, two couples celebrating a 58th birthday. The lobby was just as amazingly beautiful as is was the last time I'd seen it 40 years ago! I'm guessing low occupancy that weekend allowed both couples to upgrade, upon arrival, to full king suites at a very minimal upgrade charge. While we were not on the "Executive Floors", the suites were beautiful full 3 room/2 bath suites with lovely views of the city. 
From the moment we walked in the door the entire staff ensured that our stay was enjoyable and comfortable. From the refreshingly friendly housekeeping staff to the waitstaff, any request was cheerfully and quickly fullfilled. The conciege desk is a treat. We did not paticipate in the Afternoon Tea that was offered in the hotel lobby, but seeing it being served, it is a definite recommendation.
Great location. Magnificent decor. Superb service. Great restaurants nearby. 
Save yourself a bit of $, and take the L in from Mid-Way, if you fly in there. (Orange Line/Wabash-Adams stop) Purchase a 24 hr. CTA (Chicago Transit) card for $5.75 for unlimited travel on L, Metro, and Bus. It was most convenient and inexpensive transportation to/from the airport, Navy Pier, Water Tower Plaza, etc. We felt quite comfortable at all times using the public transportation there.

title: “happy returns”
text:
We returned to the Fairmont for the 4th time in 2 years and loved it even more if possible.We have travelled very extensively and even been to the Burj Al Arab in Dubai, which calls itself the best hotel in the world but the Fairmont is in a different league because the view is so amazing.We love the incredibly comfortable beds and linen and the new tower,where we always have a suite is quiet and enjoys the most spectacular views.Try to stay on high floor as this takes you away from the street noise.
The restaurant could and should be better but the staff are superb and there are so many wonderful eating places on hand you don't need to eat in.A good tip-The restaurant at the Ritz Carlton just down the hill is world class(so are the prices).
Don't miss this hotel if you are in San Francisco!

title: “European Hostel Chic with a Helping of Disrepair”
text:
I stayed with a colleague for a conference center at the DC Convention Center. I did not book the hotel but had researched prior to arriving to know what to expect. Despite what I read, I thought there was a possibility that the hotel would be okay (not posh but at least the quality of a Hampton Inn). It was not. I would not stay there again. I am not sure what my company paid but I would choose to stay at the Holiday Inn on the next block or metro in from Silver Spring. 
First, the person at the check-in desk lacked customer service. He did not welcome us ask if we had a reservation. When I asked where the elevator was, he told me it was broken. According to other postings this has been a chronic problem. Carrying heavy luggage up three flights of steep stairs is not pleasant. 
Walking up the stairs, paint was chipping, the rugs were dirty, and the walls grimy. 
When we got to the room, the floor was full of stains or burns of some sort. Doors were chipping. There was wiring that ran against the wall. Outlets were falling out of the wall. There was a hole in the ceiling above the fan. The side window view was of wire conduit and sealer. A huge crack between the window and the window casing meant that if it had been warmer it would have been easy for insects to come in. Furniture holding the tv was chipped. Ceiling tiles in the bathroom were stained and were askew. The vanity lighting was missing a bulb and the socket had black electrical tape over it. The pillow cases were a mix of high quality cotton pillow cases and scratchy, polyester-blend pillow cases. The hotel and room appeared that someone had recently tried to improve the hotel but had hired someone who didn't understand attention to detail. 
On the plus side, there was no evidence of bed bugs. The double bed was comfortable. The front window had a nice view of the street. The hotel was two blocks walking to a Starbucks, a few small restaurants, and Whole Foods. The shower felt palatial in comparison to the rest of the room. The size of the room was fine if you didn't plan on spending time in it. It is a hike to the nearest metro so if you have a lot of heavy baggage, I'd suggest a taxi either from the metro or the airport. 
The hotel has the ability to be a classic hotel but fails to execute it. The pictures are not an honest representation of what the hotel looks like.

title: “Not Impressed”
text:
My company paid $199 per night for this room... YES.. $199 a night in Jacksonville??!!??!!! This should be an $89 a night room without the problems. 
First let me say that if I paid $89 for this room I would have been satisfied. I will just go through the list now of why this place was not good, and very dissapointing for a Marriott (which my second favorite chain next to Embassy Suites).
1) for $199 a night, I was given what was clearly a priceline room. On the second floor, just over the roof line of a function room and facing a wall (about 30 feet in front of me). Beautiful view...NOT!
2) The handle on the toilet kept popping off when I tried to flush it, and stuck out about 4 inches from the side of the toilet unless you pushed it in.
3) Sink would not drain properly. Kept overflowing.
4) Key cards kept demagnetizing, so I was locked out of my room 3 times!!! yes..3 times.
4) Indoor pool was so dirty that at only 4 feet deep, I could barely see my feet due to the fogginess. Try cleaning it once and a while.
5) Business Center was soo hot, it was felt like a steam room when other people where in there. In fact, it must start stinking, because they have a deoterizing mechinism that sprays every so often as you sit there. How about pumping some airconditioning into that room!
6) Ordered a sandwich at the bar and it came smothered in Brie (nasty!). How about adding that to the descriptions of your sandwiches!
In Conclusions....Stay at the Radision two doors down if you want to be happy. People seem to love that place. I have told my company, I will absolutely not stay at the Marriott Jacksonville again. Either they put me somewhere else, or I don't go.

title: “Location 5 stars.. but Old style..need upgrade”
text:
Been there as diamond member , been given a room on 40 floor.. outstanding views of Central park. Lobby and reception huge and a lot of confusion during peak hours. To get lift often you have to wait a lot. Executive Lounge with complimentary breakfast and appetizer but alcohol non included. Room quite big for NYC standards. 
I personally think that this hotel needs a huge upgrade . Old style.
Location is the reason to chose this hotel.

title: “4th of July”
text: We took our family there for dinner on 4th of July. Came early and met friends that were staying there in one of the rooms. The rooms look very nice and big. The place is beautiful we walked all around the grounds, and the pools and into the gift store and than dinner. The food was great (a little pricey). Every person we in met was very friendly and helpful they even gave me a ride around in one of the golf carts. Then we went and sat on the beach in the back with friends watching all the fire works around San Diego Bay. This is a place that I would absolutely love to go back to and stay for a few days.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
I loved my stay at the Sheraton. The rooms are spacious and well updated. The bed is really comfortable and the staff is friendly and helpful. I traveled to Seattle on business and had a wonderful trip. The gym was one of the best around and has a fantastic view of the city.
Great hotel and loceation.

title: “Great Historic Hotel!”
text: A friend of mine and I stayed at the Palmer House for 4 nights in July. We loved it there! The lobby is beautiful and our room was beautiful and spacious. I thought the hotel was very clean and the staff friendly. We had a room with 1 bath and 2 double beds, so it was quite spacious with a sitting area around the TV. Now granted, it's expensive as far as internet, valet parking and the gym, but this is downtown Chicago so it's to be epected. We didn't eat or drink there, but by looking at the drink menu, they were quite expensive. As for location, it's great! Right by the theater district and Millenium Park. If you're interested in taking a tour with the Double Decker Trolley, there's a stop right outside the hotel. The Double Decker was very convenient and informative and we used it like a Taxi for the 3 days we were there. Overall, this is a beautiful hotel in a great location and I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Can't beat the Sheraton”
text: My husband & I visited Seattle for our anniversary and used our Starpoints to stay at the Sheraton. We were able to check in immediately and were given the option for a higher floor for a partial view of the Sound (which we took). The room was very spacious! We were in the older tower, so the decor could use a bit of updating, but I have zero complaints about the property. The location was superb - made an excellent base for exploring the city. We used the updated fitness center a couple of times to work off all the great Seattle food. We also found the boarding pass station in the lobby to be very helpful. If you're visiting Seattle, you can't really go wrong with the Sheraton.

title: “Great overall service and experience!”
text: The staff and the service was great. Have no complaints about this hotel. Joseph and Chris were very helpful and made my stay very enjoyable. Very convenient location and close to everything. Great food, restaurant, beautiful floor top bar with great view.

title: “Think I would pass”
text: Although the price was good (for Seattle), the room needed a good cleaning and updating. We have stayed at Holiday Inn Express that have the comfortable beds with new bedding, this one was disappointing. The toilet was plugged when we got into the room, there was a bag of food left in the microwave, the carpet was dirty, the curtains had a big stain on them and the blankets also had stains. The room had a busy freeway right out front, so I would suggest earplugs. We typically stay at holiday inn express because you know what you can expect but think I would pass on staying at this one again. On the upside, the staff was very friendly and we did have a good view of the space needle.

title: “Good place but know what you want from a location before booking”
text:
We hadn't booked accommodation about a week before we were due to arrive in NYC, so many of the TripAdvisor top recommendations were booked up. Added to that, prices were very high for anything that didn't look like too much of a gamble.
We stayed (3 adults and 1 child) in mid August 2012 and found it to be a good place - but there are some qualifications to that statement: 
1. As we stayed over a weekend, we noticed that this Marriott had a comparatively good rate - if I had payed midweek rates I think I'd have been (much) less impressed.
2. While the location is right by the Trade Centre Memorial and is convenient for Battery Park Ferries, there is little else to see beyond Walls Street. However, the subway network is very good indeed from the location and therefore getting around is very easy, especially if you buy the Metro passes. 
3.Because the hotel is situated on West Street, its is also easy to get a taxi uptown or to the East side quickly and quite cheaply.
As for the hotel itself, it was clean and well appointed. Everything the Marriott usually is and promises. Check in was efficient and staff in general were polite and friendly. The rooms were clean and spacious and the bathroom well appointed.
We ate one evening in the restaurant and it was disappointing for the price - we found other places around and about to be much better quality.
Because the hotel seems to principally cater for weekday visitors, we found it to be a bit soulless and lacked any real charm. The only common area was a rather scruffy lounge with poorly laid out seating. 
All of that said, for the rate we paid - about £200 per night - it represented much better value than much else on offer at the time. So provided you don't mind taking the subway and aren't expecting an interesting hotel with a lively nighttime scene, then it definitely does what it says on the tin.

title: “nice but not worth the cost”
text: me and my mate went for new years eve 06/07 we arrived 27th dec 3pm new york time, 5hrs in pasport control, not a good start, got to the hotel after some very bad traffic at 11ish. they had give our room to someone else so had to share a bed with my mate, they gave us vouchers for a breakfast each and a dinner in the hotel. room was very clean, we got a paper for just 1 day then never had another 1 for the rest of the holiday, the hotel is in a good location, close to a lot of sights rockefeller centre is only a min walk, the only problem with this hotel is the price, we paid about £600 each just for new years eve and new years day, but we couldnt get in anywhere else so had to pay it other than that it was nice

title: “Good value”
text: We recently stayed there for 3 nights on a family trip. The rooms were small but comfortable. We had a room with two queen beds and there was just enough room left over for us to walk around. The bathroom was also small but well appointed. The chairs in the room were leather, which was a nice touch. The service we received was generally good and friendly. Parking was expensive but on par with the other hotels in the city. They had a nice restaurant and we had a great breakfast every morning that was included in our package. We were happy with out experience and would return again.

title: “Holiday Magic”
text: My wife, sister in law and brother in law spent a delightful Christmas weekend at my favorite hotel, the W Union Square. The hotel had a festive atmosphere for the holidays, and the extraordinary staff took every opportunity to make the holidays special. Both couples had fantastic views of Union Square, which had a terrific holiday shopping bazaar set up around the southern end of the park. We also enjoyed the farmer's market on Friday and Saturday, which is always a treat. At this point, our expectations for this hotel are enormous, and they never fail to meet or exceed them. The Olives Restaurant and lounge also were delightful. Christmas in New York is always special, but even more when one stays at the W Union Square!

title: “Great Value, Great Staff, in a Great Location--Enough said!”
text: If you are looking for a clean, comfortable room and friendly staff--this is the place for you! My Family and I stayed here for a week as we toured San Diego. It is only minutes from the zoo, from the Beach, from shopping---the location is A++++. The rooms are simple but clean. The staff is extremely helpful and friendly. The pool is clean and beautiful---9 ft deep which my daughter and other children there loved. The Waffle Spot has AWESOME Coffee and good breakfasts. The wifi isn't always easy to connect but if you came to San Diego to surf the net---your missing out. The Laundry room was perfect since we packed light. The value here is great as we only needed simple lodging as we were sightseeing most of every day. I was pleasantly surprised at the value and I cannot say enough about the 5 star staff. We will definatly go back as soon as we are able---This hotel made our trip possible and memorable!

title: “a real treat!”
text:
The Grand del Mar is beautiful, this is one of the few 5 star hotels in the US that can keep up with the European 5 star standard. Everything is of great quality, and not only appears to be. The furnishings in the entire hotel are vary tasteful. The pool facilities are gorgeous and please everybody by having a quiet pool for adults, another one for children and an extra one for babies and toddlers. We had snacks at the pool and ate at the Amaya restaurant every evening of our 3 night stay because it was so nice. The seating outside is beautiful and you are not rushed like in many restaurants in US.
Service was excellent. We stayed here with two children 9 and 14 and really enjoyed our stay. Unfortunately we are not golfers, but I am sure the golfing is also excellent

title: “Welcome home!”
text: We really did feel at home at this great hotel. The rooms were spacious, clean, the beds georgous and the kitchenette just fine. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Evey time peopöe got back from sightseeing or shopping they were greeted with "Welcome home". The location is perfect: Safe, pretty and quiet area, interesting places close by - you could even walk to the White House, it´s only 20 minutes. You find great places to eat, bookshops or supermarkets in the neighbourhood. We are definitely going to stay there again!

title: “Great location, super comfy bed”
text: Stayed for a long weekend and really enjoyed the comfort and location of this property. Also, we were conveniently able to rent a car from a desk inside the hotel and picked up in the front driveway when we took a drive out to Sonoma. The atrium was very impressive as well.

title: “Convenient airport hotel”
text:
First do not order the $10.95 breakfast buffet at check in. Go to a nearby resteruant or pick up something at Ralph's grocery store next door. The breakfast is a typical free motel, eggs, one day sausage the next bacon, oatmeal and fresh fruits. Juice will cost an extra, I believe $4.95/glass. 
The rooms were clean with low platform Bed and flat screen TV. There is no dresser or refrigerator or microwave. Bathroom small with pedicel sink and tub/shower with rain shower head. 
Staff was friendly and helpful. Free airport shuttle. The lounge was nice. The area seems safe with many resteruants within walking distance.
I would stay again just decline the breakfast.

title: “Best hotel pool ever”
text:
The rooms are so-so and the walls between rooms are paper thin but the outdoor heated pool makes up for it. (NOTE: The hot tun as of November 3rd, 2007 is under construction).
This hotel is not central and requires a bus ride to the downtown (number 15 goes right to broadway so no problems there).
The bar in the hotel was actually pretty decent as locals from the area also go there...
I would stay here again just for the pool.

title: “Great Location”
text: Lovely Hotel to stay in very clean & lovely modern rooms. Great location right off Michigan Avenue, only 2 blocks for the Water Tower place shopping centre, 2 blocks from my fav restaurant in America The Grand Lux Cafe (600 North Michigan Avenue at Ontario above Ann Taylor), Gino's East pizza right next door, close to beach – 4 blocks, John Hancock centre – 3 blocks. Would definitely stay here again. The only slight downside was the sirens we could hear even at 5 floors up in room 511, the back of the hotel may not be as bad though. That said it was not that bad, we did not ask to be moved or anything. Word of warning watch out when crossing the roads, Chicago drivers pay no attention to the red lights & continue to drive even when the green man is giving way to to pedestrians.

title: “Clean, but spare.”
text:
This hotel is a year old and very clean and well kept. All the furnishings and fixtures are in excellent condition. The breakfast is pedestrian. Eggs, sausage, bacon, cereals, waffles, rolls, bread, bagels, juice and coffee are available. The breakfast people sometimes let the coffee run out..
The room have microwaves and refrigrators. Somewhere in the specs it says "full kitchen." It has really nice, empty cabinets. There isn't so much as a bottle opener in the room. All the glasses are plastic. The refrigerator is the cheap kind - no freezing compartment. There is only one lamp in the room where you would expect three, one by the sofa and two by the bed. Overhead lighting is okay.
The bathroom has a crappy little sign warning you that they are checking on you daily and if you steal any of their cheap, crappy, thin white towels you will be charged for them. It always nice to start the day being threatened, Sort of like dealing with the IRS!
The hotel is next to the airport, so expect a little noise. There isn't any late at night.

title: “Higher class for The Marriott brand”
text: The beds were incredible. I actually purchased the pillows from the Marriott site after this visit. The bar was great and the ambiance was very nice. The only thing weird about the stay was the voice for the elevator. It sounded like the person was from long island which made me laugh every time I was on it. The staff was very nice and seemed to know their frequent guests which I find very informative. I travel for business frequently and I appreciate it when the staff goes out of their way for you. This hotel is newer and has balconies so make sure you get a room with one.

title: “Ooh la la”
text: What a great hotel. The location is wonderful. Right on 46th St (Restaurant Row) and within 2 blocks of Times Square and Broadway Theatres. The breakfast is adequate and certainly a bonus. The rooms while small have everything you need including a fridge and a Keurig coffee maker. The rooms are spotless and a free newspaper is a lovely addition. Great L'occitane products in a good sized bathroom. Minor complaint - not a lot of shelf space in bathroom and therefore the addition of a lid on the toilet pedesal would provide some addtitional space.

title: “Nice Hotel in Downtown Philly”
text: Marriott Hotels always seem to do a good job. This one was no exception. Plenty of amenities. In particular I enjoyed the indoor pool, fitness center and their in-house restaurant/lounge - Thirteen. My only disappointment was the fact that they charged for Wi-Fi. Even the small budget type hotels offer free Internet! This should be a Marriott included amenity. In any case, the hotel is walking distance from the main Philly attractions and the staff is very helpful in everything from arranging a shuttle to the airport to making some dining suggestions.

title: “Hit or Miss”
text:
I stayed at Hotel Indigo once before in a suite and loved it! This time, I booked a regular double room and was pretty disappointed. First, we arrived on Friday night and had trouble valeting our car. The guy didn't seem to be in a hurry even though there were 3 cars in line for valet (we were car #3). Since we were checking in, we were told to wait for valet rather than handing off our keys at the front desk. We sat outside and waited our turn only to have the valet guy pass us up and go inside where he took the keys of the guy in line behind us. The valet staff on Saturday and Sunday were MUCH better (and professionally dressed while the valet guy on Friday night was not). 
My second complaint is that, on our first night, we received a phone call from the front desk stating that they had received a noise complaint on us. This was disturbing because we were honestly just sitting in our room discussing our plans for the next day. No TV, no radio. Just talking...without any laughter. We were informed that the walls were very thin. Later, we realized just how thin they were as we could hear entire conversations taking place in the hall.
My last issue with this stay was the toilet. Every time it was flushed, it made a high pitched squealing noise.
Other than those issues, the hotel is bright and cheerful. Beds are reasonably comfortable. Shower pressure is great. And they have a nice casual restaurant in the lobby. While I loved it after my first stay, this second stay will probably keep me from going back again.

title: “Loved the Menger”
text: We loved the menger and everything about it. ideally located next to the Alamo. Unique atmosphere and decoration retaining its originality but capable of catering for the discerning guest. Staff very friendly. The hotel had an ambience of calmness and captured the essence of days gone by. If you like modern contemporay hotels this is not for you. If you like history, antiquities and nostalgia you won't be disappointed. we are going again in 2006.

title: “No Detail left undone.”
text: Recently we decided to try out JW Marriot for a short leisure trip. We were not disappointed with the attention detail that the staff was focused in on. Every single employee there was cheerful and overly helpful. The rooms were spotless and cozy. The pool areas were clean and kept nice and warm for swimming in Feb. We did enjoy one site rest., Cibilo Moon. The food was made to our order and very tasty. Local entertainment was easy to get to outside of the resort and the front desk was helpful in finding local events. If you get a chance go downtown San Antonio and eat at Green Rest. on S. Flores--absolutely a must! Overall we got what we expect from a JW resort.

title: “More like LA than SA...”
text: My husband and I stayed here for our anniversary. This hotel is nice, but not my favorite. It is very contemporary and very dark. We prefer the Watermark hotel's design. The Valencia is a good value for a nice room. However, our room smelled like a smoking room and it was non-smoking. The bell boy told us it was the new fragrances being used to scent the rooms. The hotel is in a quiet part of the riverwalk which is nice. Don't stay here if you want a pool, there isn't one. If this is your first visit to San Antonio, I would stay elsewhere to get a true Texas experience.

title: “Disappointed”
text: Luxury Hotels website sold us the idea that although the Hotel was away from other bar scenes, this hotel has two very popular cool bars to enjoy. When I checked in I was excited and could not wait to try their roof top and inside bar. On our first night we were very disappointed to learn that both bars were closed for PRIVATE EVENT so we decided to go somewhere else. On our second night we wanted to have a drink in the afternoon before getting ready for dinner and again the bars were closed til 9 pm. Well they lied after having dinner and looking forward to coming back to our hotel to enjoy the facilities, the inside bar was supposed to be closed for a PRIVATE EVENT until 12:30. We waited in the lobby until 1:30 am and they would not allow us in. I found it very insulting to be paying top dollar for a hotel whose premises are closed for other events. One of their employees told us that they frequently rent the bars to a local company that books events for them. In conclusion, the hotel was very nice but if the only available part of the hotel is my room, I rather go somewhere else.

title: “Stay at this hotel and experience the worst customer service ever”
text: Do not stay at this hotel! The customer service is horrible, we only booked with this hotel because they promised 2 beds. We were booked for 7 nights for the first 3 nights my cousin (male) and I (female) had to share a double bed.The front desk just ignored our requests and said no room was available. We finally got a room with 2 beds on night 4. To say the least this made our trip very uncomfortable. I have been calling, emailing, phoning the hotel to try and get some response from management and they have never bothered to even reply. The hotel is run down and not worth the price. That combined with the customer service, makes it a bad place to stay.

title: “Very pleasant hotel in the middle of stunning busy-ness!”
text: I was at the Marriott for a conference and it was a nice experience. My room was on a high floor - I think the 20th and had great views. The only drawback to that was that the elevators were incredibly slow, at peak times of course, but also other times. The service, room, meeting facilities were all excellent. The location is very interesting too - it's in the middle of a complex of many other hotels, shops, and a giant mall, so there are lots of alternatives for food, drink and general meetings. If you're looking for a pleasant, reliable Back Bay hotel where you don't need a car and can buy just about anything, I'd recommend it.

title: “There are other hotels near by with friendlier staff”
text: Not nearly the quality of stay you'd expect for a Hyatt. Manager and staff and rude, and obviously dont value the guests. My advise is go stay at the Hilton or Roosevelt. Same quality hotels, but with much better staff.

title: “Nice Hotel, Would Return”
text:
We stayed here July 9-12. Overall our stay was very nice. 
We arrived a little before check in but they had our room ready. We were given a room on the 36th floor. The rooms are a tad tiny but for the time we were in it, the space was fine. The rooms have very large windows and our view was great. We could see the lake to our right, Gino's East right below, and the Magnificant Mile to the left. Our king bed was very comfortable. The shower/bathroom was a little small but we managed. We had problems with our wireless internet the first night but tech support walked us through. The air conditioners have sensors and kick on when you walk through the door. 
The elevators were pretty quick. Sometimes they were on the sluggish side but I never complained. The front desk was helpful when it wasn't real busy. We did ask for priority seating for Gino's East since there was a really long line and received that. 20 mins later we were seated!! We never went swimming but the water is heated and it has a great view. We also never had a chance to eat at the two restaurants.
Parking is steep . . .$49/day, but that is Chicago. I wish they would offer some type of discount for hotel guests.
Our last night there was also the worst. We had a group of young adults on our floor. When we seen security there once around 8:30 pm, we knew we might be in for a long night. About 1:00 am the group returned and were extremely loud, slamming doors, foul language, yelling/screaming at each other. We called security and they came up shortly after. They were warned. They were quiet for a little while and then a couple was outside our door arguing and yelling at each other. My husband then called security and they came a second time. Shortly thereafter the cops arrived. I'm not sure what happened but luckily I was able to go to sleep and tune it all out. I would have liked to see the hotel escort this whole group out of the hotel so the other guests could get some peace and quiet. A group shouldn't have to be warned more than once to be quiet. Also, I may have felt different if they sounded like they were having fun, but it was more fighting than anything.
I really enjoyed my stay and I would recommend this hotel to everyone.

title: “This place is a dump with rude management & fleecing.”
text: First of all, when you arrive, with pre paid reservations they suprise you with a $250 deposit charge on one of your credit cards. The manager lady said it was in case we smoked in the room. This is a ridiculous charge and while traveling this is a suprise charge, what if I didn't have the money on my card? The lady said we had 2 options, pay it or get out. She would have easily thrown us out on the street unless we paid. We travel a lot and have never experienced this charge nor the rudness. Here in town for the Mary Kay convention was supposed to be a fun experience but staying at this hotel was the horrible hello to Dallas we didn't want! Other people were in the lobby shocked at the extra charge also. One guy said he was charged $250, another person was charged $200 and we were ultimately charged $150. Sounds sketchy to me. The rooms stink, musty, old. Who knows what germs are stuck to this place. I will never stay here or another hotel with the word Night in it again.

title: “Fantastic staff, Spacious and Comfortable Room, Noisy Plumbing”
text: I stayed at the Donatello on a recent business trip. The staff was so helpful and friendly from the moment I arrived until the moment I left. The check in was friendly, housekeeping was great and brought me up new pillows to replace the feather pillows (I'm allergic), I bonded with room service over Giant's baseball when they delivered my meal, and all the staff were friendly and efficient. The club levels offers free coffee, tea, hot chocolate throughout the day, and a nice place to watch the sunrise. The room itself was spacious, it was comfortable and was equiped with a microwave, large refrigerator (as hotel refrigerator's go), and a tv in the mirror in the bathroom. It was easy to walk to nice restaurants and shopping at Union Square. My only complaint would be that it was very loud everytime my upstairs neighbor flushed their toilet. But, that was a minor difficulty that I overlooked because of the friendly staff..

title: “Perfect location, awesome rooms with great value.”
text: Good staff and perfect location for a weekend trip to SF. I have been in this hotel for the last three weekends and had nothing but a good experience each time.

title: “Convenient location, neat neighborhood, very well maintained!”
text: Very well maintained and clean hotel. I've stayed at a Silver Cloud hotel in Portland, and this one met my high expectations. I especially love the big bowl of candy in the lobby--always a nice touch. Staff were very helpful with maps and directions to area attractions, including neighborhood cafes and parks.

title: “Nice Clean Room, Very Quiet”
text: We just stayed here for three nights. The room was not huge, but was very clean and quiet. It was located in a great area within easy walking distance to may atractions and great restaurants. the only complaint that I would have is that they way the bathroom doors are (they slide) it does not offer much noise suppression or privacy which is not ideal as a couple. However the staff was great and we enjoyed our stay.

title: “Beautiful Boston”
text: We stayed in Boston form Thursday 29th Dec 2011 to Saturday 31st Dec 2011. It really was a wonderful trip. The holiday Inn Beacon Hill is prefectly located for visitors to this fabulous city. We were within walking distance of many local attractions (Fanueil Hall, Quincy Market, Boston Common, Beacon Street) and also a stop on the trolley tour around the city was just outside our hotel. There is aslo a very good pharmacy and whole foods store located directly beside the hotel so if you wanted something nice up to the hotel room and weren't keen on anything on the roomservice it was just a short pop over to the store. The trolley tour around the city is definately worth it. For $34 we had great value and learned so much about the culture of Boston. The drivers were so knowledgable and really great fun as we went around the city. Would really recommend Boston as a short stay city break.

title: “The Marriott Rivercenter is basic accommodation.”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Marriott Rivercenter for 5 days - I was at a conference and she was vacationing!
The rooms are the typical basic, comfortable hotel room. The room rate was $280 plus the $14 per day for internet/phone access. The fitness center has acceptable equipment. The pool / hot tub were always filled to capacity.
The hotel is close to The Alamo, the Riverwalk, and a mall. The Alamo is a must see and a stroll on the Riverwalk is always nice.
We learned quickly that the locals never eat at the restaurants on the Riverwalk as the food is mediocre. If you want good Tex/Mex food, then take the walk or ride the trolley to Market Square which is west on Commerce Street about one mile. Mi Tierra restaurant has the best Mexican food and I've eaten at many great Mexican restaurants over the years.

title: “Better value elsewhere”
text: I stayed here two nights...it took forever to get a room. The room said it was non smoking but smelled of cig smoke and deodorizer. There was only a sheet and light blanket on the bed and the room was cold. I did get an extra blanket the next day which helped. There was no coffee pot and apart from a breakfast spot there was only the lounge which like the gift shop opened whenever they wanted to. Although easy to get around via the subway from this location there isn't much around it for places to eat etc. Basically there was other places in this region for the same price but with better rooms and service. I would recomend you check out other choices in the area!

title: “Great view, great location!”
text:
We were in room 4236, had a nice view of downtown. We could see a little bit of the lake, not too much though. Still, the views of the mountains and city were unbeatable. The location was great, right near everything. The walk to Pike's Place Market was short, and there were so many restaurants nearby. We also saw a movie theatre just a stone's throw away, but who wants to go to a movie theatre on vacation? 
The room was smaller, but well appointed. The bath was standard hotel bath, with nice countertops though. The room itself was very clean. the linens were crisp, not wrinkled at all. 
The best part about this hotel was the concierge service. It's got to be tough to deal with newcomers all day, every day, but Judy and Ted (I think that was his name) both did an excellent job. They were courteous, friendly, and very willing to help. 
Overall, an amazing stay to make it an amazing trip!

title: “Another very satisfied customer!”
text:
Well, my wife thinks the Magic Castle was the nicest hotel in terms of service quality that we have ever stayed at. Nice work Tripadvisor and reviewers! 
Nice refreshments at check-in, nice big room(s!), and great location for checking out the sights around Hollywood!

title: “Had A Blast in Memphis!”
text: We were passing through Memphis for Spring Break and just had to stay at The Peabody Hotel since we'd heard so much about it. The kids loved the Duck Walk which happens twice a day. Also, what i was most suprised about was to find such great shopping in the lobby of the hotel. The Lansky family has 5 shops in the lobby, each with a different concept. Bernard Lansky was known as "clothier to the king" since he dressed Elvis Presley. He is 80 years old and was there everyday of our stay. He was so friendly and had so many stories to tell about dressing Elvis. He works in a fine mens shop and I bought my husband some great Nat Nast sportshirts. but i was most excited to find a pair of jeans that fit. Lansky 126 is this trendy denim boutique that easily could have been in New York. Needless to say, I now have a cute new wardrobe. The hotel is in a great location. Our favorite restaurant was Rendezvous BBQ! We also went to Graceland, Sun Studios, and the Zoo to see the pandas. We can't wait to return and would definitely stay at The Peabody again. Check out [--].

title: “Hip but way too noisy”
text:
The Nolitan is no doubt very cool. It's stylish decor and location in one of NYC's hottest neighborhoods guarantees that. However, Kenmare is so noisy that I would never stay there again. Starting at 5 am trucks begin deliveries on Kenmare, and all I could hear was the beep beep beep of trucks backing up all morning. 
Other than the fact that it couldn't actually be used for sleeping, I thought the room was a typical boutique hotel stylish room. I wasn't a huge fan of the shower that has a clear view into the room and out the window since I have no particular desire to be an exhibitionist, but it was easy enough to cover up with the drapes.
One nice touch was a little packet of discounts to local upscale boutiques. One less fortunate aspect was that it's not easy to come by a taxi out front and the staff just watched me walking aimlessly around with my luggage rather than offering to hail one for me. Otherwise everyone I encountered there was friendly.
Alas, the noise was a deal breaker. Although I love the neighborhood, I won't be back to the Nolitan!

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
This was our 2nd stay at the Omni Parker House and we will be back again. Location is great, lots of attractions within walking distance. It is a short ride on the T from the airport.
Staff is very friendly.

title: “great upper west side hotel”
text: this hotel has some unique features- old style charm meets contemporary style. very friendly staff and great location, the rooms could be more spacious however it is something you can ignore with all the other perks. also well priced!! the power did go off in typical NYC fashion but it was 100F!!! CLOSE PROXIMITY TO A LOCAL MARKET FOR GROCERIES IS A BONUS!!

title: “not recommended”
text: I recently "stayed" here for a nearby wedding. The price was only $99 but it was worth about $39 even in Boston. I say "stayed" as we did not even stay over night but used it as a parking/changing station; it was too shabby to attempt to sleep in - and the windows were so old that the freezing winter air just rushed through them, no matter what. The room was very musty and moldy, everything was very old. I would say it was as *clean* as it could be but that cannot overcome the old, run down nature of the place. My friend and I said we would've stayed overnight if we were young again and had too much to drink at the wedding! ;) Instead, we just cut our losses and got out - it was just far too uncomfortable with the dinginess, old, old blankets and sheets and carpet, bad smell and insecure locks to contemplate getting a good night's sleep. As others have said, it is a good location and it is inexpensive, but it just wasn't worth it for us.

title: “Upper upper east side”
text:
Walking wise it is Located quite far away from times square etc but located just less than a minutes walk to the subway station. Therefore you can easily get to anywhere in nyc with a short journey. used it everyday to get to and from the airport ($5.25 one way) times square, china town, the area where u board boats to get to the statue of liberty and single journeys cost 2 dollars or so.
