Room is clean, clean bed, clean bathroom. The shower takes a couple of minutes to heat up. Hairdryer was broken but they said if we needed one they would send one up. Iron and tv in room. Air con worked. Soap etc supplied. The room lacked sparkle and wow but it was still clean. I would consider staying there again as it was one of the cheaper hotels in newyork whilst booking at last minute. Do not expect this hotel to be plush and grand. A mix of people stayed at the hotel ranging from couples in their 60s to younger guests in their 20s. Felt safe in the area and in the hotel at all times. Located in a busy area with lots of restaurants and shops.

title: “Perfect EXCEPT FOR---”
text:
The BED BUGS
The Poice Raids, no me, but twice while I was there and that was only 2 nites and 3 days.
The RUDE managers
The DIRTY SHEETS
The SMELLY ROOMS
...and the list goes on.
Don't go here, sleep in your car...before staying here.

title: “Love This Place!”
text: This hotel is great! I travel a lot for work and frequent Fashion Valley about 5/6 times a year and have stayed at other places along Hotel Circle and really didnt feel safe (as some of the other places had room access that was available to the public). I feel extremely safe here as the parking is secure with a arm gate and the entrances to the lobbies are all well lit and staffed and require key access after a certain time, although, the back parking area is quite dark. The rooms are updated, the linens are clean and the beds are comfortable. Its close to everything, not too far is the Fashion Valley Mall, and trolley station that will drop you off right at Qualcom Stadium. There are several other shopping centers in the vicinity and Sea World is not too far away. This hotel has a bar/lounge area and a marketplace and deli that serves up hot and cold food, and even serves Starbucks coffee!!There is a heated pool and a 24 hour fitness center that is rather large for a hotel and has new, clean equipment. The only thing that wasnt so great was the internet (WiFi) connections. I've stayed on different sides of the hotel and neither one was better than the other and I had very limited coverage with my cell phones each time Ive stayed there (1 Verizon, 1 Sprint) so this made it difficult to work from the comfort of my room. Another concern I had on my last trip was a foul, rotten odor that seemed to seep into our room. I read another review that it could have been the drain from the ice machine and as my last room was right adjacent to the ice machine on my floor, I am fairly conveniced thats where the smell was coming from. It was horrid and literally woke me up in the middle of the night! Also it gets so quiet at night that you can actually hear the ice machine working, so If you are a light sleeper, make sure your room is no where near the ice machines! Overall I am extremely please with this hotel and will definitely be staying here again as my coworkers and I expect to make approximately 8/9 trips to SD this coming year. We travel on governmant per diem rates and for the price range, this is by far the best we have stayed at in the area!

title: “magnificent stay near Magnificent Mile”
text: Homewood Suites has got it all: great location for restaurants, shopping and attractions,comfortable suites,free breakfasts and internet,friendly staff,etc. A super place to stay in Chicago.

title: “Amazing Service!!”
text:
I got married in Los Angeles and had my guests stay at the Orlando. First of all, booking all of the rooms was very easy, and Nick was very accommodating. Also, there is no fee if you don't fill up all of the rooms that you reserved. I really just want to commend all of the staff on their amazing customer service. I have never been treated as well in an hotel. Some examples are: We had a little after party in our room, went across the street for some booze and the bar gave us a cocktail shaker so we could make our own cocktails! Also, I bought some cheese and nuts and such at Joan's on Third and asked if they could bring up a serving platter and a knife. Within minutes I got a wooden cheese board and cheese knife. So amazing!! All of my guests truly loved their stay, and the location is so perfect if they don't have a car. So close to the Beverly Center, Toast, Joan's on Third and The Grove. 
Everytime I came into the lobby I was greeted warmly by name. That really means something, and it's all of the little things that count. 
The rooms were very clean and comfortable and very nice beds!
The only minor thing I could say is I wish their hourly valet was a little cheaper for people who are not staying the night at the hotel but just visiting for a while. But the valet is prompt and friendly. 
I would absolutely have guests stay at this hotel for sure! It is great and with all of the other expensive hotels in Los Angeles, this one is a real bargain and you will be treated like a king/queen!

title: “Very handy for Jacob K Javits convention center...”
text: What can I say, for 105 Euros a night you can't complain. Small (by US standards) room but not in comparison with other (much more expensive)hotels in which I have stayed in Manhattan. Clean, though my colleague - a smoker - said her room was a bit iffy. It is a bit of a walk to the subway, but during the day that's fine - the area is not crawling with dodgy characters. I walked back to this hotel at 3am without feeling threatened, but I guess you wouldn't want to do that as a woman alone. Staff friendly enough and very helpful trying to connect my laptop to their broadband internet connection (but it didn't work!). Easily hailed cabs in the area - just not right outside hotel. Walk up to 10th or 9th Avenues and hail there, no problem. Breakfast very simple - bagels, tea, coffee. Plastic plates etc. I would stay here again for the price and the location near the convention center, but if you want to be right in the middle of the action, or can't walk more than 10 minutes without complaining, then look further. As I said, for the price you cannot complain.

title: “so-so hotel”
text:
We stayed there in late July as part of a wedding -- the room felt cheap. And the see-through shower was ridiculous. Some of our friends who were sharing rooms as friends were very uncomfortable at the exposure. The rooms were unimpressive -- clearly it was an office building before becoming a hotel and it has not lost that antiseptic feel. Service was generally quite slow though also friendly-- it's clear they don't employ enough staff. Maybe that's because they seem determined to employ hip-looking young people who look like models and maybe cost more money. Service during the day at the rooftop bar was nonexistent and the bartenders were rude when people asked for a waitress.
The hotel is trying a little too hard to seem "alternative". For example, there was no button on our phone to call room service, although there was a button for "hell" and one for "alibi". 
Before coming to Los Angeles, I learned that a gigantic outdoor rave was being held near the hotel. I called the staff and inquired if this would present a noise problem and was assured they'd never had any complaints. The noise kept my wife up all night. We are not ancient -- we are 30 years old -- but listening to raving until 4 am was a little much.
I left some items in the room at check out and my messages to "hospitality" were not returned.
But overall, for about $150 a night, it's hard to complain. Hotel is fine for the price. And the food was quite good. Good restaurant and room service and excellent mojitos though they appear to use some sort of mix.

title: “Nice, but underwhelming considering the price”
text: I could tell this hotel is trying to be high-class, and the public areas are very upscale, but the room was very mediocre. The best that could be said about the room is that the bed was comfortable. My conference was in the basement, and the meeting rooms are very nice as well. The location was okay, as I said conference right downstairs, 2 blocks from the Metro station, and you can walk down NY Ave a few blocks to the White House.

title: “Great Customer Service!”
text: The accommodations were good enough for what we needed. Keep in mind it is a motel and thus the great rates. They definitely made up for it with great customer service and shuttle rides available to the airport and train on a whim. Very convenient and perfect for saving money on a business trip.

title: “Excellent service by attentive staff.”
text: We travelled to the Westin Georgetown with our 1 1/2 year old recently and the staff was increadible. They upgraded us to a larger room to accomodate the crib and were exceptionally helpful getting us in and out with our bags and bellongings - especially Ahmad the bellman. Thanks!

title: “Park Yourself Somewhere Else”
text:
Location is the best feature of this hotel provided you want to be in a neighborhood setting as opposed to Mid-town location. We have stayed all over the City so this is not our first rodeo but, by far, our worst experience.
The biggest flaw with this hotel is the terrible management and absence of leadership when there are legitimate problems present. I encountered guests complaining at the front desk 4 out of the 6 days in which we stayed at this hotel. The desk clerks handle problems without guidance or direction from management -- or perhaps just incompetent and indifferent management decisions. Staff are left to deal with the frustrated (and sometimes angry) guests while the manager hides out in an "office" somewhere out of sight. The result is a woeful attempt at service that is lackluster at best and incompetent at worst. It is too bad because this hotel has great potential to be a real gem in the City.
THE PROBLEM: Our first evening in NY we returned to our room at 11pm to find the a/c broken and leaking water all over our bed, my luggage and the floor. Throughout the remainder of the night, I was soaking up water with towels (15 towels in all) and alternately shutting off the unit to reset the thermostat. The front desk clerk explained there was nothing he could do until morning---not great news, but understandable given the late hour. The issue is that my husband has a heart condition that is adversely affected by heat and we needed to have a cooler room for him. I spent a good deal of the late evening (or I should say, wee morning hours) calling other hotels trying to locate another room for the evening while also attempting to keep the air conditioner running without leaking water all over the room. The front staff did not offer any suggestions for other hotels, a phone book or even a courtesy phone call (since my cell phone did not work in our room --- all calls were made by me in the front lobby). At approx 2am, the front desk contacted me to say they had a room available due to a late cancellation. It was a single, but I could move my husband to the room while I stayed with the children in our sauna suite. Turns out the room was offered to me for the evening; however, they would charge for my current room, which was already a higher suite rate, and also for the additional room at that posted rate of 170.00. I could hardly believe my ears! To have a room available and not offer it at no charge is unbelievably discourteous -- particularly in view of the health issue involved for my husband. In addition, the next morning, the housemaid told me I would have to pay extra laundry fees for the towels used to soak up the a/c leak. Unbelievable! Three attempts to speak with the manager resulted in these comments: "you just missed her" -- "she just left the building" --- "she just went into a meeting." The final offer of compensation was to remove the tax for one night's stay...a grand total of less than $20 --- which, by the way, I have yet to receive.
It may be that if nothing whatsoever unusual happens during your stay, you will be fine. However, if you have any issue crop up....you will live to regret this stay. Personally, I will not risk a stay here again, EVER!

title: “Hard Rock rocked our conference!!”
text: Our leadership retreat was planned for this location and boy did it ever rock the event. Every staff member I encountered was filled with service and a positive attitude from the minute we stepped out of our car, to checking in and even riding up the elevator with some facilities people. The lunch they served was delicious. Our staff felt they were treated like a "rock star" and so our retreat was the best we have ever had. Amazing job everyone!!

title: “Amazing location and hotel”
text: Me and my wife stayed here for 4 nights while on our honeymoon. The room was amazing and the bed was so comfy, you get Starbucks coffee in your room which is a treat :-), the location is amazing it is a 2 minute walk and you are right on the front where all the shops and restaurants are. I loved pier 39 and would recommend going there, we also did the tour bus that has an office just down the road from the hotel, we saw all of San francisco in a day and had a good time doing it. The hotel told us that the wine country is a good tour and we can now say it is true, we had an amazing time and the hotel booked it all for us. We also went to china town for tea one night and went to brandy ho's, the hotel recommended it and arranged a private car to take us there. We would stay here again as the location is amazing and the hotel is perfect.

title: “Can't go wrong”
text: We stayed Saturday night just 1 night, but I would stay again, clean and comfortable. Nothing flashy, but for the price DEFINITELY worth it! You can pay more nearby, but if all you want is a clean room, comfortable bed, give it ia try.

title: “Best NYC location for the price”
text:
This was our second, 4-day stay @ the QT!
We arrived very early, and were able to check our bags, scope out the city, and returned in the afternoon to an upgraded room...still small, but the large bathroom made it seem bigger.
the bed is extremely comfy, even though the flat screen tv seemed very close ( b/c it WAS!)
i awoke about 6 AM to the baking aroma of the fresh muffins served at breakfast ..yummy..and they were! Clifton, the breakfast guy, couldn't be nicer...the coffee is a Starbucks equal!
we didn't use the pool this year ( didn't have time!), but, i loved it just being there!
the location was PERFECT for us, since we saw 4 broadway shows, and were able to return to the room and change for "clubbing" w/ little effort. All the subways were less than a 5 minute walk.
I can't WAIT to return to the QT in '07!!!

title: “SOOO LOUD!!!”
text:
My husband and I arrived at the Hotel Teatro late at night, completely exhausted from the trip. My husband was also not feeling well, so we were dying to get to our room and go to sleep! The valet and front desk was pleasant to work with, and we quickly checked into our room, which we found to be a bit small, but nothing we haven't seen before. 
We got about two hours of sleep before a bunch of young people started coming home from the bars - loud and roudy as ever. My husband and I are in our late 20's and early 30's, so we are usually pretty forgiving about that sort of thing, but the walls at this hotel are seriously PAPER THIN. Really. We could hear absolutely everything going on in the next room - the TV on, conversations at 3 AM and yes, even other nighttime activities, if you know what I mean. We kept trying to sleep through it, hoping they'd go to sleep after a bit, but that never happened. At 4 a.m., I finally called down to the front desk and asked for another room - their quietest one that didn't have anyone next door, ideally. They unfortunately didn't have any rooms that didn't have guests next door, as they were nearly sold out, but they could move us to a corner room that would hopefully be quieter. 
We had to pack up all of our stuff, and the bell hop brought up a key for us to change rooms. We ended up in a room that was somewhat quieter (because we didn't have the noisy neighbors), but we still were right by the elevator, which we could hear operating all night long, and did have to deal with hearing the TV in the next room the following night. The A/C was also really loud. We woke up every single time it turned on and off, and eventually just turned the thing off and dealt with the heat. This room was also MUCH smaller than the one we were originally placed in. 
Needless to say, THIN WALLS. It's fine other than that though...clean and in a great, convenient location. The staff was nice, although they never offered us any type of consolation for the inconvenience of having to move rooms at 4 in the morning on our first night there. Valet is pricey, like every other hotel in the city, though. 
If you're looking for a place to stay after a concert or a night of partying in downtown, I'd say this is your place, but if you're anyone else trying to get a decent night's sleep, I would recommend trying somewhere else! We left completely exhausted, to say the least.

title: “Fabulous value and quality for the price”
text:
My teenage daughter and I stayed here for 4 nights/5 days for a mini-break. This was a 4 star resort style hotel at chain motel/hotel type prices. 
A choice of places to eat, an outdoor pool, a nice spa and the best fitness room I have seen for a very long time at a hotel - over 20 different pieces of equipment plus freeweights. There are several lovely outdoor patio areas for cocktails and snacks/light meals.
The room was nicely done with very large queen size beds (4 pillows plus cushions) and large flat screen TV, plus nice touches like a decent coffee maker and good toiletries (Gilchrist and Soames).
There were a couple of niggles - my breakfast order was mixed up and room service is quite expensive, and the lunch order on the patio was also not delivered quite as ordered. A couple of things in the room were a little shabby - the curtain was hanging off its rail somewhat and the base of the basin was stood on rather antiquated plaster board.
It's also a bit south of downtown San Jose - about a 10 - 15 minute drive to the center in a residential neighborhood, although close to good roads (it's right off the Camino Real) and next to a nice park.
Overall though I gave this 5 stars as for the price I really don't think I have ever done better and I would definitely, definitely stay here again.

title: “Certainly worth a visit.”
text: In short: the entry/foyer/"atrium" (if you know Embassy Suites) is not much to speak of in comparison. The in-house store was never truly stocked. The staff were amazing, great smiles, friendly attitude, and seem like they enjoy themselves. I would compare this properties staff to the genuine and amazing people in San Antonio at the Riverwalk location. They are both cut from the same professional cloth. Breakfast was good, although the space is a bit smaller than expected. I stayed three days and the lady cleaning my floor was pleasant and helpful. I had a great converstion with Kim at the Front Desk, again very pleasant. The valet staff could be more personable. The location is ideal if you are attending a convention or just wish to be in the downtown area of Houston and not deal with the crowds othwerwise associated with the city central hotels. Thanks to this team for a good stay.

title: “Great Hotel for the price”
text:
We stayed here one night in July. We booked through priceline and got a great deal!
The location of the hotel is very convenient if you are in San Diego for a conference as it is very close the convention center. The gaslamp is walkable (if you are not wearing heels!) or is a short $8 cab ride. The view from our room was spectacular, overlooking the habor and the pool (which is nice). You are right next door to Seaport Village and across the street from kansas city BBQ (hole in the wall with great bbq, known for having some Top Gun scenes filmed there). I like that you are close enough to the gaslamp to party if you choose too, but the hotel is far enough away to remain family friendly and not cater to the booze hound crew that over takes some of the other hotels directly in the gaslamp. We got a 2 queen room, it had a little sitting area and was comfortable. The hotel is not outdated but not modern (again like other gaslamp hotels). It was very clean and I didn't feel like it was old. The parking is $36 for the night - which is lame but in the range of most hotel in downtown area. I would definitely stay here again, great location. We will be back!

title: “Great value and very clean”
text: We stayed here for one night last month. The room was small, no-frills, but very clean. There was a small TV with cable, the towels were organic cotton, and we could tell they were eco-conscious. The best part about the hotel was their back patio- a beautiful place to rest and hang out, although we weren't able to use it since our day was packed with other activities. There was some noise above us in the late night and early evening coming from travelers lugging their stuff up the stairs (no elevator), but nothing my ear plugs couldn't fix. Also, bring your own shampoo, etc. as the kind they have is in one of those dispensers attached to the shower wall. They did provide hand soap and cups though. There is also a small continental breakfast and they had tangerines all the time in the lobby. Overall a great experience, great price, great location, and I would stay there again.

title: “A class act in Downtown Denver”
text:
Nothing dissapointed. From the heated floors to the rain shower, unique lighting in the sinks to the TV that appeared in the mirror, this Four Seasons rated at the top of the list. An amazing surprise was the hotel mini-bar and the room service---it was a valued price, no gouging..
Spent a rainy day in the spa and it was well worth it. The heated pool had surround sound and was larger than most rooftop pools. The spa was decadent with a relaxation room, plenty of reading material, and men/women saunas and spas. 
Bring a sport coat or jacket if you visit the Edge Bar for cocktails.

title: “Family trip”
text: I was surprised by the service and how clean this hotel is. The employees are very nice and always ready to help.

title: “10 out of 10!!”
text: Stayed here November 2004. Was anxious when booking a hotel in New York as I had heard alot of bad stories about hotels in NY. The Belvedere is exactly what you want when visiting New York. This hotel is close to everything; Port Authority bus station, Central Park, Fifth Avenue, Broadway, Time Square, etc. Walked everywhere and just used the subway to go down town. We left the hotel early every morning and returned late in the evening. The bedroom was cleaned everyday we were there (our pjamas were even put under our pillow!!!!). We didn't eat in the hotel, we preferred trying places outside which there are alot of in theh area. Enjoy your stay here.

title: “Is that the White House?”
text: W hotel - pretty much your standard trendy W hotel - funky lobby - pricy drinks and food - and boutique ambiance. Good service from reception - pretty slow at breakfast- best to go out for brunch and get much more value for money!! One tip - we stayed on floor 9 - and could hear banging nightclub music from the roof top bar on the Friday night - so stay on a lower floor! We did the bike tour - through City Segway tours - the Segways were fully booked - but the bike tour was brilliant - 3 hours for $35 pp. Will, the tour guide, was excellent and full of American History knowledge... A tip for brunch is the Front Page at Dupont Circle - all you can eat buffet - with $5 extra - endless mimosas - bucks fizz to the Brits.. Georgetown district - fab for shopping too - A great city break!

title: “Sad to see this hotel and area going down hill”
text: We loved this hotel when we stayed there many times in year 2001. We went back in May, 2005 and found glory day was over for this hotel. Starter, there was no bellman in front-unthinkable 4 yrs ago. Front desk staff was pleasant but all negative, "no", "nothing". Very thin staffing. We booked suite-no view, looking over concrete roof, but the bed was worse. My side smelled so bad, if I were not that tired, I would have checked out. My husband side was ok. Furniture were old and cracked. It was obvious that upkeeping was not done well. There was no bath salt as used to be. They did not even replaced my shampoo. I had to call for extra soap for bath tub. One sign how bad hotel is doing is that their flagship Jer-ne restrurant is closed(!). It was an expensive but a beautiful restrurant. Now it is gone. Sports club LA-boston was still going strong and I see more young members. We enjoyed working out there. But the area itself-it was up and coming then-is now going down hill. Ritz boston common condos are still not sold, new movie theater is expect to close down. Sad to be back there -but we still remembered watching new year firework @boston common in our ritz suite-Best view in town. We will go for the old ritz next time though.

title: “Free OnDemand, Very Comfortable”
text:
We chose this hotel because it had a great rate during the middle of the week and we wanted to stay slightly outside downtown Chicago. The Jr Exec Suite has a small living room with two chairs, a HDTV, and minibar. The bedroom was huge. Desk, dresser, HDTV with free OnDemand and well integrated internet via keyboard AND the remote. We wanted a quiet day to relax and this was the perfect place for that. We walked a block or two to pickup food - liked Yango's BBQ Beef with Jamba Juice from around the corner. It was a $15 cab ride into downtown. We also stayed at the Palmer House on this trip and I'd say the experience at both hotels was equal, although, The Willows did it with far fewer people.
I would stay here again for the breakfast alone. Lots of options, good juices, and BAD coffee. Boxes of cereal were great as well as trays to bring everything upstairs. The elevator is slow but it is an historic building. It is very well kept for being as old as it is. My wife loved the room's lighted mirror.

title: “Would definitely recommend.”
text: We only needed one night and didn't want to spend a lot of money. My husband found this two bedroom apartment for $199. It fit our needs just right. The only downside to the room we had - 410 - was the cigarette smoke that seeped in from the other apartment. The master bedroom, bathroom, and closet reeked of it. So we were fortunate that there was another bedroom that was not affected by it. We were able to walk up to City Center for our show and walk to dinner too. Very convenient.

title: “New York”
text:
The Benjamin is in a good central mid-town location, walkable to shops and theatre.
The rooms and service are good, the restaurant food delicious (best pancakes on our trip) and the concierges Sarah and Anya were very helpful, friendly and efficient.

title: “bed bugs! itchy, crappy, bed bugs in 304!”
text: The hotel appeared nice. But I came home with about a dozen bed bug bites. The hotel offered me ZERO compensation for this & were basically idiots. I'm so disappointed, I always try to look past things....but this is ridiculous. There was also such a seedy crowd surrounding the hotel! "How could you not bring me crack?!" was a conversation I REALLY heard outside. Ugh.

title: “Wouldn't stay here again!”
text:
Spent 3 nights at the Deauville Hotel, although location was close to Empire State building I wouldn't recommend staying here. Beds were comfortable but bathrooms were grubby and bed linen and towels although washed were very thin and still had stains on them from previous users.
Staff were not particularly friendly or helpful apart from one male member of staff.
There are a number of hotels of much higher standard at a similar room rate which will give you a much more enjoyable experience. We stayed in two other hotels which far surpassed this one in quality of room and service.

title: “Steer clear”
text:
I stayed at The Iroquois with my 17 year old daughter for 3 nights last weekend. I usually stay at The Warwick (which I love) but wanted to be closer to theaters as my daughter and I were going to four shows over the weekend. I recently stayed at the nearby The Muse (and liked it) but decided to try The Iroquois based on recommendations from TA. BAD DECISION!!! The Iroquois is my first BAD hotel experience in NYC after years of visits. 
My initial reaction to the hotel was disappointment - small lobby area, excrutiatingly slow elevators, and a miniscule room with virtually no daylight. I've heard about NYC hotel rooms like this but have never actually stayed in one before. I thought about upgrading our room but I found the hotel so depressing and uninviting that I knew we would spend as little time as possible in it so decided against it. Indeed, we left the hotel early each morning and returned late each night. 
But that was still too much time spent at the hotel as I woke up covered in clusters of red raised bites. I showed the hotel manager the bites and she immediately moved us to an upgraded room and assured me the hotel would investigate. A different hotel manager called me on my cell after I had checked out to inform me that the room was checked for bedbugs and the report was negative. He suggested that the bites might be mosquito bites but I told him that they were definitely not mosquito bites - the location, pattern and symptoms of the bites are most consistent with flea bites but could also be spider bites. He called me a few minutes later to say that he would comp one nights stay on my credit card (which he did but only the room rate and not the taxes).
I did not make a fuss about the bites other than requesting a new bed. The hotel management took the bites seriously, were very apologetic and responded quickly. However, despite their response, I will not stay at The Iroquois again as I've stayed at nicer midtown hotels which do not have bugs. The last thing I want to deal with during a short visit to NYC is getting bitten by bugs in a hotel bed!!! Too itchy, too icky!!!!!!!!

title: “Great location - request renovated room”
text: Our first room that we were in was old with outdated furniture and a bit musty. The air conditioner was loud and leaked and the bathtub had a constant drip. We did call the front desk and they were very helpful. After visits by housekeeping, we were transferred to a different room on a newly renovated floor which was very nice and clean. It was roomy with nice amenities. The location was great and not a bad walk to all of our destinations.

title: “Good last-minute hotel”
text: I found this hotel on Yelp while driving from Ventura to LA and decided to take a chance. I was very nervous, but the price was within our budget and the reviews looked promising. The hotel ended up being very nice, and our room was modern and updated. Onsite parking and close location to a great sushi restaurant made this a worthwhile stay!

title: “Peaceful place with dimmed light”
text: The room was beautiful. The lobby and breakfast room too small because of the pool. Friendly service.

title: “Great Staff and Clean Rooms”
text: Hotel feels like new with clean rooms and updated decor. Staff was very helpful. Very convenient location right off I-35. Great value!

title: “Refreshing stay; great location; complimentary shuttle”
text: We love visiting San Diego and discovering what's new and re-discovering what we've seen before. This Westin hotel is perfect in so many ways, starting with the complimentary airport shuttle (Eric, our driver, gave us many suggestions on what to see/do). Front desk allowed us to check-in early and check-out late. Purchased a 3-day trolley/bus pass (a real bargain at $12/per person) and rode all over. Trolley station is just 2 blocks away at Sfe Depot. Go 2 blocks more and you're at Broadway Pier. Lots of restaurants nearby. Rooms were clean, comfortable (love the Heavenly Bed), quiet with a fridge, bottled water and coffee. Staff for the most part was attentive. Kudos to Melissa in the lounge who knows the meaning of service. Only negative is the $12.95/day Internet charge. Even so, we will return.

title: “The Worst!”
text:
1. Stayed 4 nights for a conference earlier this month. I initially booked the room directly via phone over 2months prior to the conference and was told I would recieve the conference price. I recieved a confirmation from the hotel verifying this, and when I checked in I was told the price of the room was > $100.00 more for each night. Upon questioning this, I was told that there were a limited number of rooms reserved at that price, they didn't know what happened, but that, oh well, sorry, no more rooms at the discounted price available. Having never been to Boston and not know the area at all, I felt stuck, so I stayed. 
2. The rooms was small and very, very noisy. The walls are paper thin and you can hear a lot of noise, especially from the bathrooms. 
3. The last night of our stay, there was some sort of Fire in the hotel and the alarm system came on, annouced the situation, and instructed us to wait for further instructions. The message kept playing, but we recieved no instructions. I kept looking out our 10th floor window at the fire trucks below and the growing number of people gathering on the sidewalk. Upon trying to get information from the front desk, I was told that no one could talk to me about the situation. VERY UN-NERVING. After 20min of getting no where, we left the room and walked down 10 flights of stairs, met other guests who reported the same sense of uneasiness, not being able to get any information. When we reached the Lobby, my husband was again told that no one could talk to him. There seemed to be a lot of confusion. We sat on the sidewalk for over an hour before we were finally let back in, and were never told anything about the incident. When we checked out the next am, the desk clerk asked how our stay was, I mentioned the fire incident the night before and she just laughed, shrugged it off and said "oh, yeah, that". NO apologies for sitting outside for an hour at 1030 at night, nothing. I couldn't believe it. Will never stay there again, nor would I refer anyone to stay there. The staff and facility highly over-rate themselves.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Palomar Hotel for 3 nights. The room with 2 queen beds was spacious. It was a pleasure to come back from sightseeing every afternoon to relax with a glass of wine at the complimentary wine hour. Location was great - close to the metro and lots of nice places to eat. We will definitely stay at the Palomar again.

title: “What an ordeal”
text:
We arrived at 5:25 pm on a Friday night (check-in starts at 3:00). We were informed our room (2 beds non-smoking) was not ready yet, but they offered us either a smoking room with 2 beds or a non-smoking room with a king sized bed. We asked how long it would take until it was ready and they called housekeeping. 30 minutes later we still didn't have an answer. An hour went by and the room was still not ready. We offered to go up and either check the room ourselves to see if it was done or clean it ourselves. Long story short: we got in our room 2 hours after we arrived (4.5 hours after check-in begins). We were not charged the upgrade fee for having 2 beds, and they gave us a certificate for 2 free breakfasts. Then we get to the room and it's tiny...I guess we should've taken the room with the king-sized bed, but who knew.
Overall, the location is great and the hotel is beautiful, but the room we got was tiny and there seems to be a bit of a communication break-down between the front desk and housekeeping.

title: “Outstanding Value”
text: If you are going to stay here, but expect the Rits Carlton..or even Holiday Inn. Its priced like a basic motel because thats what it is. However the staff is friendly. Its Chinese owned but they speak good English. Several nice restaurants within walking distance. The bus stop is across the street. Its also relatively clean.

title: “Worse Customer Service Ever! Will Never Go Back!”
text: This has been the WORSE hotel stay I have ever experienced. My fiance and I checked into the hotel on Sunday, May 30th and had a room in the 100 villa. Our patio was walking distance from the pavillion, where a wedding was going on. By 8pm, you can hear the loud music coming from the wedding. I called front desk to ask when the volume was going to be lower and when the party was going to be over. I was told that the noise level will decrease by 10pm as it was their "hotel policy" and that the party should be wrapping up around midnight as the guests and vendors had to leave by 1am. 10pm came around and the noise level was louder than it was at 8pm. I gave wedding until 12am to decrease their volume before I complained about the noise again. Midnight came and all I could hear are drums and loud music coming from the wedding. Called the front desk and was told that they would call security and have them lower the volume. 10 minutes had past by and nothing. I got so frustrated that I went to the front desk where one of the workers and the night assistant manager, MATT, rudely told us that he could do nothing for us. Another couple complained about the noise (they were in the building across from the pavilion) and as we were complaining he rudely told us that he could do nothing for us if we continue to talk. Then he told us that he could do nothing about the situation. He was getting so defensive. What kind of Manager gets defensive when you have a irate customer who is trying to get some peace and quiet at a hotel they paid money for? He was so unprofessional and rude. He lacked the customer service skills that managers need to solve issues and complaints made by their customers. That was the WORSE customer service I have ever had. Worse of all, the party ended around 3am and they would not do anything about the noise. They did comp our night, but that wasn't until many complaints and frustrations about the noise issue. It was as if they let the party go on until 3am because they comp our night. They should have thought about the noise level before assigning guests to the villas and rooms near pavilion. How inconsiderate! Worse of all, they charge and arm and a leg for parking...$25 for a night. I would stay away if I were you!

title: “Issues but all fixed”
text: We had an isue with the wrong room the first night but Heidi to care of it for us. The best part of the trip was the massage I received from Amy. I average a couple a month and this had to have been one of the best ever.

title: “Unique, Quiet, Relaxing”
text: They have a pillow menu where the front desk will bring you a different type to try if you don't like the already super comfy one in the room! How's that for unique? The living room area has free snacks and water. You can use their free shuttle to take to/from the airport and if you want to go downtown, use the free shuttle to get to the light rail. We stayed here on our way back home from Hawaii because it was close to the airport, but we wish we would have stayed here on our 2 night stop on the way to Hawaii instead of staying downtown. The amenities are worth the distance from the city center. They also have a 5 star restaurant called Cooperleaf where you can get everything from gourmet lamb and seafood dishes to burgers.

title: “In Denver - The Palace to Be”
text:
We have stayed at the Brown Palace in early October and had one of the best Hotel experiences in Denver. This hotel is unique and truly the Grand Dame of the City. Tastefully restored with all the amenity even a new hotel could offer. Check in was nice and attentive – the Bell Staff was very welcoming and the two ladies at the Front Desk even welcomed us back with a great smile and a professional attitude. Superb. Our rooms were very spacious, great bathrooms and as I mentioned before a luxury taste of Colorado. Awesome beds and linens. 
Looks like there are several newer hotel in Denver but for us the Brown Palace experience is different and hard to be matched.

title: “Good, Clean Accomodation”
text: For the price we paid & the location you cannot go wrong. Even though this hotel is dated, it goes out of its way to provide a comfortable stay & the staff are so helpful. We were a family of five & the rooms are spacious enough with a separate master bedroom. The kitchen is adequate with everything you need. The only problem I had was the walls are thin so we heard the people next door, however I would not let it deter you from staying here. The hotel is a walk to Kodak Theatre, restaurants, attractions & shopping. We caught the Metro to the ice hockey, just a great stay.

title: “Perfect weekend getaway”
text:
I stayed at Jet for my friends birthday. My room was large and spacious and colorful not cookie cutter like most hotel rooms. the lobby turns into a nightclub on the weekends and after some drinks and revelry it was very nice to be able to head upstairs to bed. The room was quiet and the bed and pillows very comfortable. in the morning there was a free continental breakfast which was a perfect ammenity. i had a great time the staff were very professional and helpful. i would tell everyone to give Jet a try if you are looking for something special and very unique.
-K

title: “Great location, great hotel”
text: Very comfortable rooms and beds. So close to good restaurants, cable car, the muni for trips out to Golden Gate Park and shopping close by. The staff were all extremely friendly, pleasant and very helpful. Great central location.

title: “Alright airport hotel”
text:
Checked in on Friday for early Saturday flight. Leaving car for week in underground parking. The signs for self-parking are confusing but the good news is for extended parking (greater than 3 days) the fee is only $11 per day. Tax included. That's a better deal that the "Parking Spot" which is right next door. Only complaint is that shuttle to/from LAX is every 15 minutes. The shuttle service is provided for by a third party which means that the shuttle also stops at Four Points Hotel. In my opinion, 15 minutes is a long wait considering that the airport is only 1.5 miles away. 
The room was pleasant but nothing special. It wasn't noisy at all, which was a surprise since the Hotel is actually close to the runways. Directly across the street is United Airlines Cargo building with the runway right behind it. You can watch planes take off and land from the upper floor rooms. Since this is an airport hotel, there really isn't anything within walking distance interesting to see or do.

title: “Amazingly helpful staff”
text: The hotel it's self is very hip and modern with a cozy atmosphere! The staff were all very friendly and extremely helpful. They all pronounced my first and last name correctly, which never happens! The room was big and the beds were comfortable. The shower was amazing! It was a fantastic stay and the next time I am in the city I will book a room here!

title: “Loved it can't wait to do it again”
text: From arrival to check out the hotel and staff was great ,Melissa Humble was great and very knowledgeable about the on goings in San Diego ,Thank you Melissa , we loved all the W had to offer

title: “Value in Chinatown!”
text:
We only stayed 1 night here on September 27 2012, but could not fault it.
The staff were so friendly, helpful and polite. The room was clean and the bed was way more comfortable than the soft mattress we copped at the Intercontinental the next night - at twice the price too!
The price paid relative to the service received (& throw in the breakfast too) makes this a 5 star experience.
In terms of the area the hotel is located in, if you don't like the grime & chaos of a Chinatown-setting, maybe it isnt for you, but subways are closeby & fruit marketeers are on every corner. I had the best vege-dumplings I've ever eaten too, a few blocks south - 6 for $2.50! Unbelievabe value!

title: “Big hotel that works”
text: The San Francisco Marriot is a very large hotel but I found that everything worked very well when I stayed here. The room was what I had expected and I was always treated well. The bar on the top floor has the most stunning views of the San Francisco bay and is well worth the expensive drinks...

title: “Free parking...YEAH RIGHT”
text: Called and made my reservation on the phone and specifically told them that I would be parking my car there for a week. I specifically asked if there was free parking. Every time I talked to them they said "Yes, free parking". Get to the hotel...guess what...they want to charge me for parking! They told me that I needed to purchase the "stay and go" package...otherwise they're going to charge me $5.00/day for parking. My room went from $53.10 to $72.00+tax...a grand total of $92! HUGE PRICE DIFFERENCE! I was forced to purchase the room because it was already late and my flight left at 6 a.m. so I had to eat the extra cost.

title: “really bad one”
text: its got bed bugs in room 316, absolutely unclean, room cleaning service only changes sheets, doesnt vacuum or clean bathroom. it sucks.. thanks to this crappiest hotel i and my husband have bed bugs bites all over and in our luggage too

title: “So much fun!”
text: I really loved staying here. The staff clearly enjoys working there and were so helpful and polite. I pricelined this hotel and ended up with a great deal. Their "secret password" also gave me free parking (a $30 save). I loved the happy hour and the decor of the place. So unique and such a nice change from the typical boring hotel.

title: “Can a Hotel Be "Too Nice" ?”
text: I guess some hotels are "too fancy" to have complimentary breakfast (this one's is $22 per person), free wireless Internet ($13 a day), or free parking ($48 a night for paying guests). The water pressure was mediocre and the room temperature was always a little too warm. What you're really paying for is the location, which is very good, and there are five restaurants attached to the hotel. The experience of walking through the lobby is spectacular; however, you can get that experience for free without staying here. Overpriced; I would not stay here again.

title: “Not a suite, but still a nice stay”
text:
We stayed here with a friend during a convention. Although it was nice that the room was divided in two for privacy, it did make the room seem rather small. The fridge was also very small. If you are looking for an actual suite I would suggest the Staybridge. I liked the fact that the bathroom was in two parts (a shower area and a toilet area), especially since the shower areaway big enough to fit a playpen for my daughter. However, it is a little weird that the toilet bathroom is right at the end of the bed. Now I know why in most hotels the bathroom area is far away from the bed! 
All these small complaints aside, the hotel is very new and the hotel staff were super friendly.

title: “Modern Hotel in the Heart of NYC”
text: Modern and very clean rooms just steps from the subway and few blocks from the Rockefeller Center. The staff was very friendly and helpfull.

title: “Fabulous Hotel”
text: Caught the train, First Class from New York and was able to talk two blocks from Back Bay Station. Fabulous rooms, great staff thru out the hotel. Food was good, bar platters were great. Great location walking distance to all attractions. If visiting walk to Boston Common, 10 minutes and do the Historical Walking Tour from the Information Office, other side of the common, Fantastic run by historians. Easy walking. Back Bay Hotel is the one to stay with in Boston.

title: “Great location”
text:
When looking for this hotel, there were two websites to book it on. www.radisson.com and the other was www.radissonlexingtonnyc.com. The later had much cheaper rates then the former. When I phoned to ask why, they said that the only legit website was radisson.com. So we booked on radisson.com and then completed a price beat form, and what do ya know, they beat it. So it turned out very cheap. 
The rooms are small, so I wouldn't have anything below the Executive room with King bed. We were on the 10th floor and there was still a fair bit of street noise - perhaps ask for a higher up room. 
Great location in mid town Manhatten. Only a few blocks to 5th and about 10-15mins to the Park. 5 mins to Grand Central Station.
Staff were very good, however found it a bit strange that housekeeping tended to clean up our belongings maybe too much. 
Great place across the road Cnr Lexington and 48th for breakfast. $2.49 for egg and bacon roll!! The cafe downstairs next to the Starbucks was a bit expensive and even charged for a pot of hot water!
Overall, good location and hotel, just get a big room.

title: “Not the Embassy Suites we are use toooooo....”
text:
Outdated and not maintained to say the least..... This hotel has not be updated in at least 10years and I am being nice at that. Meet family there from LA and MO to have a little weekend get together. Made me look like I didn't do my homework.. which I didn't and that was my fault. There were a number of items that I noticed that were either dirty (walls/doors), stained (carpet) or torn (couch cushions). I asked for more bedding and the blankets had holes in them. I will pass on this Embassy Suites when in Dallas next time. 
Plus there was some band playing or some sort of music playing until midnight that rang thru the hotel.....

title: “THE MOSSER IN SAN FRAN”
text: We thought the Mosser was just great. The staff was very friendly and personable compared to the service you get from one of those chains. The rooms were small indeed, but comfortable and quiet and very clean. Location is close to serveral types of public transportation and to nice restaurants and bars. We'll definitely return!

title: “Great hotel, great value”
text: We stayed here during a weekend in Indy to meet friends. Check in was smooth, bed was comfortable and clean and accommodations were great overall. We appreciated the sleep-noise machine with several choices. Good complimentary coffee in the morning. Staff was polite and professional. Would definitely stay here again. Location was good for both downtown and Broadripple areas, which we visited.

title: “Amazing Hotel!!!”
text:
We stayed here for two nights and we love this property...have stayed here several times in the past and they will always have our business!!
The Grand Club service is so awesome from the service attendants to the food served!! Highly recommend upgrading for this service!!
Used the mobile web check-in which was so fast and easy as well as check-out the same way!!
Our breakfast was included with the room rate and the buffet is definitely worth it!!
This is a beautiful property and customer service is great too!! 
Loved the stay fit gym used it both day's!
Can't wait to go back next year!

title: “Pretty good stay”
text:
Just got back from a weekend trip to San antonio. We stayed at Hotel Contessa for 99$ a night. For 99$ a night this hotel was great...now I have read some people paying upwards of 300$...if I had paid that my opinion would be a little different. 
Let me start off by saying the location could not be any better. We explored the whole city and never had to drive once. In part because of the location but also San Antonios public transportation system. 
When we first arrived we were a little confused, since this was out first time we didn't know what kind of overnight parking we could do. Instead of the hassle we just figured we would valet it. Well it was $28 a night...not sure if that is good, but walking around I saw we could get it a little cheaper if we didn;t mind the extra walk. The hotel staff is so friendley, they are really wonderful. 
Our room was LARGE. I was suprised at the size. I thought everything was laid out fine and nothing really to complain about. We don't spend a lot of time in our rooms when we go away so this is not such a big deal to us if there is something we don't like. 
The public areas of the hotel were very clean and beautiful. Did not try the restaurant or bar, but heard good things about it. 
Now my only complaint was that it did take a little time to get our car, but it's really not the valets fault. I thought the review below was a bit rude in assuming the valet employees were incompetent. They were understaffed it seemed. We still only waited 20 min and we were not in a hurry at all so this was fine.
If we had to go back to San Antonio, I think we prolly would stay here again. As long as the price remained the same.

title: “Good Location”
text: Excellent location for visiting the city. Room we had was fantastic with great view of city on our side of building. Everything close by that you need. Good transport links as well

title: “Location okay BUT!!!”
text: We had to pay 2 times for holding our bags extra on really expensive rate, no check in before 4 that was the first holding fee, room was terrible from a loose socket to no sockets at all next to the bed, mattress was covert with cover because it's so old, I would let my dog sleep on it. The old duvet only covert with sheets, so you basically sleeping between covered dirt And hotels.com talked about bed bugs. We only stayed here because got booked trough work when we found out what they payed without breakfast it was horrible. Then the staff is so unfriendly they ratter be on the phone with friends then give customer service I would not recoment this hotel unless you get it for a 2 star rate. Because off it's location as earlier mentioned by someone else stay on the lower floors for some water presure And on the outside of the building because on the innercourt no light and no phone reception. Good luck with this hotel because the city is great and stay anywhere but here

title: “fantasic service and food - Cafe Sienna”
text: we had a group of people who had dinner reservations in the private room of Cafe Sienna and have to say the food was absolutely delicious, service was great, and above all the best touch was having the chef come out and ask us how our dinner was! Kudos to Cafe Sienna's staff and Billie Walker ,the Director of Catering, who put this dinner event together for me.

title: “"WANNA BE HIGH CLASS HOTEL" EXPENSIVE N ABSOLUTLY HORRIBLE”
text: I usually dont usually take the time for writing reviews since i don't have the time for it. nevertheless, this is such an specific case i have to. I want you to know what i terrible mistake i made by chosing this hotel. As soon as i got there they could not find my reservation in the system and made me buy a bigger more expensive room. This girl i dont wanna mention her name (the only at the hotel on that sunday night) had a very bad atitude. The hotel was empty so i parked my car outside at the door. It wasnt valet, they kept the key and still charged me an extra 25 for that. I arrived around 11 at night and left at 6 next morning, so my car was exactly where i left it. The room costed me around 220 plus taxes and valet costed me around almost $300. The room was very old. The air conditioning/heater had to be turned off cuz of the loud noise it made I couldnt sleep. Everything and all the equipments are very old. The location is very unaccessible and horrible. Im not very familiar with Dallas but that location seemed dangerous to me. the breakfast is very deceiving also. PLEASE DONT GO THERE! The price is really not worth it. they are absolutely insane to have prices like that for such a low quality and bad services. Honestly if you stay at Motel 6 it will feel more luxurious than that! I have originally chosen to stay there cuz of the price, i thought it should be good for that price! I was very wrong! I went next night to the Crowne Plaza and had a blast! I was very amazed with the friendly stuff, great food, great location and FREE accessible parking right in front of the elevators! All of that for half of the price! New comfortable rooms i felt in heaven after the horrible time i had at the Springhill Suites. I have to go back to Dallas several more times and will never ever go back to the Springhill Suites.

title: “Buyer Beware”
text: We booked 2 Queen beds a month ahead. I called to confirm the room before we left and to also add on a night. I had to book the additional night separately. After many calls, I finally got through to a manager who could help me put the reservations together so we didn't have to change rooms the last night. That person cancelled the first 4 nights of our stay. When we arrived, we had no reservation. They put us in a King room, though there were 3 of us, since they had no Queen rooms left. We also asked not to be near the elevator, but they put us right next to it! We were on a non smoking floor, though there was obvious smoking as soon as you stepped off the elevator. On top of that, my credit card was billed for the last night as a "no show" a week later even though we had already settled the bill. The room was OK except for the silverfish we found in the bed.

title: “Nice hotel with convenient access”
text:
The hotel is nice. Has just gone through a renovation. I'm not big on being that close to Times Square but having the subway entrance to the B,D,E train was excellent. So easy to get around Manhattan from this hotel. If you enjoy the Times Square thing, this hotel will be even better for you. 
We were on the 46th floor and noise was still an issue. I've stayed in a lot of NYC hotels and this one seemed to be one of the noisier in terms of blocking noise from the hallways, adjoining rooms and outside. Not the end of the world to me but if you are a light sleeper, this could be an issue. Outside of that, it was an all around good hotel.

title: “A birthday treat.”
text: My family and I stayed here for Labor Day Weekend. It happened to coincide with my birthday and the hotel and weekend lived up to our expectations and hopes for a great time. From the time you walk in the door of the hotel you are welcomed into a cocoon of peace and tranquility, just steps away from the madding crowd of Times Square. One person who really stood out was the concierge, Osilla Stewart. She was there for us when we needed advice and was able to secure our dinner reservations exactly when we wanted them. We saw Billy Elliot which was beyond compare, and truly an electric performance. Thank you Doubletree, money well spent.

title: “Not bad for an airport hotel”
text:
The Renaissance Montura is located conveniently very close to LAX - we picked this hotel for the convenience of the location, the competitive rates and because everything was booked where we needed to stay.
Overall I'm not sure why this hotel is rated 4.5 on tripadvisor. It really isn't that good. The rooms are very small and uninspiring. The area around is unattractive and doesn't feel safe. Having said that it can't really be faulted for an overnight stay and an airport hotel - the beds are very comfortable and you will have a good night's rest in complete silence. If that's all you're looking for and can secure a good rate you shouldn't be disappointed.
Be aware that the hotel was just raising its parking rates to $18 as we stayed there which is outrageous for the location. The Manhattan Beach Marriott 3 miles south is in a nicer location and charges less for parking. If you don't need the airport shuttle I would prefer staying there as it is also near LAX but has nicer rooms and views.

title: “Relaxing Stay, FANTASTIC location!”
text:
We traveled to San Diego and were so delighted with our stay at the Mission Bay property. Our room was more like an apartment, it was HUGE! The location was near the pool, we had a front deck, porch with seats and we could sit there in the shade, drink wine and enjoy the landscaping. It looked more like Hawaii to me than CA. We were not in the high rise building, but on the ground level free standing building. 
Parking was discounted to $10 a day because my husband was attending a medical conference while we were there. Breakfast was not served but there were several restaurants there. 
This location was SO close to everything, the beach, the airport was 6 min. away. It was great and can't wait to return.

title: “Comfortable, nice staff and central”
text:
We stayed in one of the suites of The Moore hotel during last June, and I must say it's the best I've ever experienced in Seattle.
The room was spacious, and so was the bathroom, there was also a living area that could have been more comfortable, but was good enough for us, with a kitchenette and a dining table.
The decoration was simple, modern and very nice, combined with some old features, such as the radiators.
And it's true that they fold the towels in animal shapes. We had a dog (although my husband believes it was a rabbit... whatever... it was puppy, believe me :P).
The location is perfect to go out at night, to go shopping during the day, and it´s only a couple of blocks away from the seafront and the market, and a short walk to the EMP, International fountain, Space needle, etc.
The parking is a block away, and it's 12$/night. You can request a card in the hotel to request in/out privileges. BUT! it closes at midnight and opens again at 7, so if you're going to be late at night, you better take a cab to avoid having to park on the street.
Back to the hotel, the staff was very helpful and friendly at all times. 
The only rude person we met was the bartender of the bar next to the hotel, but we're unsure whether it belongs to The Moore or not.

title: “Good for a short stay in New York”
text:
Good location, room was clean, not huge but had a nice bathroom.
Just used hotel for sleeping, didn't use any other facilities so can't comment.
Recommend Pershing Square opposite Grand Central Station for breakfast, magnificent!

title: “From the time you drive up to the door til the time you settle in your room AWESOME”
text: Everything about this hotel is above and beyond what i would expect. Drive up and someone is right there offering to help with luggage. Check in was easy and front desk staff was friendly. We were escorted to the elevator by front desk person that helped us. Our room is on the 8th floor with views of universal. Our luggage arrived soon after we checked out our room. That person was friendly and gave us good info on area. We ordered breakfast the next morning and it arrived on a table wheeled in by a waiter. Food is exceptionally good!!!! Before coming here I read reviews everywhere about Hilton and Sheraton both near Universal. Without hesitation I know I made the beat choice. A truly perfect stay and we have 3 more nights to go!!

title: “Worst hotel I've ever stayed at in my life!!!”
text:
We "accidentally" booked this hotel thinking it was another one we had stayed at and BOY, was that a HUGE mistake. I can honestly say that this is the absolute worst hotel I've ever stayed at in my life. It makes Motel 6 look like The Hilton. 
First of all, it states that it's 1 mile from the Zoo and UCSF (we were going to both), it's actually more like 4 miles. Secondly, parking is very scarce. Third, we walked in the room and it reaked of urine, there was hair all over the blanket, urine on the comforter and mattress. It was filthy. My 2 daughters, ages 4 and 7 were crying and begging us not to stay there. My 7 year old actually wanted to go sleep in the car. If it hadn't been so late when we arrived (11:30 PM), we would have left and found another hotel. 
We decided to just stay the night and felt and heard the Muni train all night. It felt like an earthquake. Not to mention people yelling and screaming across the street the whole night. We also kept hearing loud bangs. I don't know how many times I jumped that night and needless to say, didn't get any sleep.
 I felt like I was getting bit by fleas the whole night as well. This was honesly the worst hotel ever. We chose it because it was close to the Zoo and the hospital, and we thought it was one we had stayed at another time, but I would have gladly stayed somewhere much further and paid much more. The price was outrageous ase well. $108/night. You couldn't pay me to stay there another night.

title: “Wonderful staff and a cute boutique hotel”
text:
We requested to be transferred to this hotel at the last minute by Expedia after a terrible experience at the Hilton Union Square (they offered us a room with only a sofa bed and then refused to refund us). After a late night arrival and much stress at the Hilton, walking into the Galleria Park was like entering a little oasis.
The staff at the Galleria Park are outstanding, very helpful and happy to give tips on transport, restaurants etc - even volunteering extra information without being asked. The hotel is very clean and well maintained with hip boutique style decor. Small rooms but this is hardly surprising for San Francisco.
They also have a large outdoor terrace and jogging track, which was very nice in the morning to step outside and get some sun and fresh air before venturing into the city.
They don't have a restaurant at the moment but it will be opening in January. All in all, the Galleria Park was a warm and welcoming experience and I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Best staff ever!!”
text: Shin from Wheels is the best!! Also, Elizabeth at the front desk is SO great!! Everyone on staff is very friendly and helpful. I travel here 2 weeks out of the month for work and they all make my travel experience very easy.

title: “Awesome”
text: This is a Manhattan find. Three doors from Times Square, but you wouldn't know it inside. Quiet, upscale, wonderful amenities and a friendly, helpful staff.

title: “Great Place”
text: Our stay here was great. We had two rooms which were very nice. The hotel's location was very convenient for us and FREE parking that was a big plus as most of the hotels that we checked on we would have to pay every day to park ($22 a day and more). The hotel staff were really nice, especially at the Front Desk. They were awesome and so very helpful with anything and everything that we asked about regarding our stay, room needs and sightseeing suggestions...very informative. I also saw this with other guests as I went through the lobby. It was our first time in San Diego and we had lots of questions...especially on directions. We ate breakfasts at the hotel restaurant and also had dinner there one evening. The restaurant staff were very accommodating to our needs. We all enjoyed our breakfasts and dinners very much. I would recommend this hotel. It was great for us and our needs. Hope that you will like it too.

title: “Stay away!”
text:
We booked a room for 4 people, and when we arrived we got a room with one large bed. When we complained the staff told us that they could not guarantee us a room with 2 beds. We had to book another room at another hotel.
The customer service was just terrible!
Stay away!

title: “Warning”
text: I left the Lincoln Inn after a few hours. I heard either gang or prostitution activity in the rooms around me. Homeless live in the alley behind the building. The door frame on the room I provided, #211, had been broken into possiblity, and didn't look like it would take much to get into again. I am sure there are better options near by.

title: “Wonderful place”
text: I loved this hotel. Rooms are huge and so is the bathroom. This cleaning service was awesome. The complimentary breakfast was much better than I expected and there was plenty of food at all times. I did also liked very much teh manager's reception. You could have free drinks for two hours and also snacks! The staff was always willing to help, they sure made my stay very comfortable!

title: “Perfect Hotel for Us”
text: We just spent 5 nights at the Elan and it was the perfect spot for us. We (myself and two 14-yr-olds) left first thing in the morning and didn't get back until late in the evening so it served our purpose of having a clean, comfortable place to sleep and a good breakfast in the morning. The ease of valet parking was nice too. It really is in the perfect location- we did beaches, Hollywood, Burbank, Culver City, Beverly Hills, Downtown and felt right in the middle of things although walking is really out of the question (other than to the Beverly Center across the street and about a 20 minute walk to the farmers market). Staff is friendly and helpful. If I go back, this is where I'll stay.

title: “Good location, clean rooms and superb staff”
text: We flew into NY for a weekend of sightseeing, Yankees game and to see a Broadway show. The hotel was located in a great area to do all of the above as it was centrally located to several subway stations. The hotel was very clean and the rooms seem to have been updated. The best part of the entire stay was the overwhelming hospitality of every staff member we came in contact with. Everyone seemed to truly enjoy their job and wanted to ensure that all guests felt comfortable, welcomed and safe. We all loved our weekend and look forward to our next visit to the city. Fairfield Inn will be our choice from now on!

title: “NYC hotel experience”
text: I stay here because of the hotel's location, the variety of room choices, the hotel staff (housekeeping, reception, doormen and concierge service) and the great bar next door (Niles). I will stay here as long as I continue traveling to NYC.

title: “Good value but a little distant and careless at service”
text:
The location of "Vertigo Hotel" is on the border of lower Nob Hill, but be aware that two blocks down really gets you to the sketchier part of the Market and two blocks west into seedy Tenderloin, known for drug addicts, hookers and quirks: so rather always walk down east to Union Square/Chinatown/Financial/North Beach. Lobby is chic, Hitchcock's movie on constant screening in the back of the front desk (scenes were allegedly shot here). Renovated rooms are nice, comfy beds, fresh smell (non-smoking establishment), new bathrooms a little tiny but equipped with modern shiny fittings and pleasant natural bath products. No A/C but a well-working overhead fan. Cool style, cosmopolitan, orange leather armchair, enough storage room (well-lit walk-in closet with iron and board), free local calls, flat TV, spacious and really extremely clean and well-kept - the maid service was incredible - more than up to date for all those aspects. Downsides on the room: poor TV channels (about 20, unsorted, why not screen Vertigo on there too??? When I came in seeing the film behind the desk I was urging to watch it in my room), poorly-working refrigerator. Internet: wouldn't say high-speed but free, so still okay. No coffeemaker. Outdated, slow elevator (emphasis: not historic), but okay it's an old building and there's not too many rooms: there's a tolerance.
The biggest problem of the Vertigo - as many have written that before and I must underline it again - is its service. There could really be some coffee in the lobby round the day, or at least just not until 10am only. The friendliness at the reception is average, nothing cordial or welcome to it, they really don't care: business as usual, they kinda run it all but without effort (some even rather play computer games on their screen instead of smiling or even giving some faint sign of recognition): Out of six different people we saw throughout our three-night stay, there was only one guy very friendly. If they worked on that it could be a really wonderful, special place. 
Still renovated rooms are great, location is good (restaurants on Russian Hill, in Union Square district, North Beach and Chinatown are all walking or short cab (low cost) distance), unless you walk the Tenderloin, valet parking was polite & reliable, and overall the stay's value for money was absolutely acceptable in pricy San Francisco.
So work your room entertainment and desk service, Vertigo...

title: “Great Location for a Great Price!”
text:
I found this hotel on TripAdvisor and checked out the reviews before booking. 90% of the reviews were positive and they were correct.
The hotel is in a handy location for the subway and lots of restraurants. We paid for a private bathroom which worth the money as we stayed for a week. There was heat wave and the air-conditioning felt like it was saving our lives. All staff were courteous and polite.
As for the actual holiday- we will defintely returning to new york, but at colder times of the year. The Heat and humidity was really very difficult, but it did not marr the experience. 
If I had some advice is make sure you only wear the most comfortable pair of shoes you own, the whole time you are there.
And if you walk the same 4 blocks across and 2 blocks up everyday, don't! Take a different route everyday as you will miss some nearby gems of parks and restraurants.

title: “Excellent hotel in great position”
text: We really enjoyed nine nights at this hotel, and were made to feel very welcome by every member of staff we came into contact with. We had a large room on the 12th floor, with two wonderfully comfortable double beds, and an excellent amount of space. Whatever requests we made were met with efficiency. The Concierge team was excellent, helping to plan and organise days out, and advising on all manner of things. Service throughout was similarly first class. The public areas are very imposing, though can hardly be described as cosy. The hotel is in an excellent position, with bus, trolley bus, tram, underground rail and cable cars immediately outside the hotel. The BART is literally a door to door service from the airport. The trendy Ferry Building is right opposite, and Fishermans’ Wharf, China Town, Union Square about a 20 minute walk. We wouldn’t hesitate to stay at the Hyatt again.

title: “Great spot to meet someone near 9-11 Memorial”
text: I had a business meeting in the lobby bar - called Liquid Assets - last week. It was the perfect decibel level, the seating was comfortable and the service was great. The lobby is impressive. I will definitely go back for business and pleasure.

title: “OK...but nothing more”
text: Well, I have stayed at quite a few Sheraton hotels across the world and this one was nothing special. The rooms were OK, nothing fancy, but by no means bad. To get to the hotel you have to go through a mall (which was kind of creepy at night) which was not very nice. Location is ok, a lot of traffic at night, which woke me up several times. The subway is right across the street, as well as several restaurants and fast food joints. I would rate the hotel as below average overall (by Sheraton standards) but it was in the process of being remodeled.

title: “Classy hotel, exceptional staff”
text: We got a great holiday rate through TravelZoo meaning we could stay in a classy hotel for a budget rate. All the staff were extremely courteous and helpful--concierge, bell captain, desk, restaurant servers. The rooms are huge with a separate seating area. Bath space could be larger. Restaurants are first rate. Valet parking adds $24 + tip to the rate. Cheap parking is available 2 blocks away at about 1500 Commerce (at Lane).

title: “Felt a little ripped off”
text:
I used the 'hostel' part of this motel, with it being the only hostel in downtown Memphis I had pretty much no chance anywhere else, it'd basically a small room with two creaky bunk beds in it, 
Upon arrival it was just before a grizzlies game, the receptionist a guy checked me in pretty quickly charged me for what I thought sad the price of both my nights stay then left to look after car parking as it is very close to FedEx forum, the room was situated right at the back of the motel, the room was VERY DIRTY, VERY HOT AND VERY SMELLY. It was as if the room had not been cleaned for years, not months, years!! Had to take a top bunk as both bottom Bunks were in use, the bathroom was very disgusting and felt unsanitary, there was no toilet tissue, it was quick yucky. Had two nights off the worse sleep ever!! The beds were really creaky even if you moved your arm the bed would creak, imagine 3 people in a room all night, the beds were really uncomfortable too
The breakfast which I thought was included I don't think it, as there are signs on the lockers in the room with a price list for different breakfast items.
The next day when I returned to the room my key was not working, so I went to reception to find out why, the very condescending and sarcastic receptionist (a woman this time) told me " it's because check out was at 11am" so I told her I had booked and paid for two nights! She then asked me what my name was etc..and told me the guy didn't check me in properly, and that I had only paid for one night, she sorted this out for me. I felt she was unnecessarily rude. 
Overall I DO NOT RECOMMEND this motel/hostel, go somewhere else maybe try the other hostel in midtown.
Beside the okay location nothing else is going for it.

title: “Great value, clean, friendly staff.”
text: My partner & I stayed here for the weekend from Sonoma County, California. The room was small but clean and newly remodeled. The staff was helpful and friendly. A bit noisy on Saturday night.

title: “Spartan”
text:
It's new. It's clean. And it has the heavenly bed and a comfortable sitting area. I will probably stay here again when I'm in the area. 
I didn't love it, however -- my expectations were probably too high -- and it felt like a stripped down, spartan version of a Westin, or maybe a very nice dorm room. Some negatives to note:
-This was my first stay at an Element, in a studio suite. There was not a separate bedroom area or sleeping alcove and the bed is only a few feet from the refrigerator, which was not quiet.
-Starwood properties usually have very good bathroom amenities, but not here. In the shower there are wall-mounted dispensers of average quality shampoo and body wash. I had to ask at the front desk for a bar of soap to use in the sink.
-Much more hallway noise and room to room noise than in Westins or W's. Also, in the hallway you can hear conversations in the rooms. The last refuge of the road warrior, turning on the fan for white noise, doesn't work because there is only 'heat' or 'cool', no full time fan. The window only opens about 5 inches.
-The evening reception promises "hand-selected regional wines . . . and enticing appetizers" which turned out to be some 1.5 liter bottles of Woodbridge wine and cut up celery sticks next to a bowl of cream cheese. That was it for wine or food. (there was beer too) However, the lobby and adjacent patio provide a pleasant area for socializing with colleagues, and a family was BBQ'ing their dinner.
-Breakfast was good -- cereal, eggs, breakfast burrito, yogurt, etc.
-Wireless worked well.
-You need a car here. The adjacent shopping mall has a few restaurants and there is a morning/evening shuttle to HP, but there is not much else around and there are no sidewalks to walk anywhere safely.
Overall, it's a good low-cost option for the business traveler, but I shouldn't have believed all the hype.

title: “Great Value -- Definitely No Bed Bugs For Us”
text: I was a bit concerned when I read about someone's experience with bed bugs. I am happy to report that we had three separate rooms and not a single bug! The room was extremely clean and the hotel was great. The concierge was very helpful in booking a car for us and steering us toward good restaurants. This is an elegant old hotel with beautiful views and classic rooms. Water pressure was not great but the bath products more than made up for that!

title: “Great accomodations”
