text: The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was well appointed, clean, and comfortable.

title: “Great location and value”
text: This hotel is centrally located, mere steps from Penn Station and close to Times Square, Empire State Building etc. We had a fantastic 34th floor view of Manhattan's skyline. Room was huge by NYC standards and seemed newly renovated. For all of this, it was the least expensive among those we searched. Lobby was undergoing renovations. Adjacent diner was OK (not associated with hotel). Lobby is beautiful. By all means seriously consider the New Yorker on your next visit to NYC.

title: “Nothing to recommend it except convenient to City Hall, courts, opera”
text:
When I checked in, I walked to the front desk and waited. Nobody responded. "Hello?" I called out. Movement from the back, then a person came out, saying nothing. I said "checking in" and gave my name. Still without any response or greeting, the person shuffled the reservation list until she found my name. It was not a good start. 
Then she told me the hotel parking lot was full, so I could not valet park. She told me to drive one block and then left one block, couldn't miss the parking lot. I asked if there was an attendant, because it was night, and dark. No, she said, you just swipe your credit card. I followed her directions, parked, and found the kiosk to pay. It dd not take credit cards. It was hard to read the sign in the dark, which said if you want to use credit cards you have to pay across the street. The hotel should have told me that. It's not the best area to be running around after dark, waving cash or a credit card.
Room was okay, nothing special, somewhat rundown. I had three lumpy puffy pillows, which made my neck crook at a funny angle. I called the front desk and asked for a flat pillow. "Flat? You mean deflated old pillows? No, we don't have any of those." 
In the morning, the hot water was not very hot. Breakfast was continental only, which was a disappointment, because I had a long day ahead of me and wanted some scrambled eggs. Bad cheesy christmas music was playing too loudly in the breakfast room.
It's right next to City Hall, the opera house, Davies Hall, and state government buildings, so the location is good if that's why you are there. Otherwise, give me the Hotel Rex or Adagio downtown any day.

title: “Pleasant Surprise”
text:
I gambled and tried the Expedia "mystery hotel" bid and ended up booking at this hotel. I have to say that I was a little nervous after reading reviews. You don't see the name of the hotel until you have paid so kind of stuck. Well, it was great. It was quiet, clean, spacious, and the hotel staff was very nice. The location was fantastic! There are several places to eat nearby including McD's, Dunkin Donuts, Wendy's, and little new york locals. All within easy walking distance with kids (literally a block or two). There was even a little market on the corner with fresh fruit, flowers, etc. It was a easy two block walk to Central Park. Free wifi. It was a little dated but they are in the midst of remodeling.
The only complaint was no soda machines even at the gift shop. I didn't want to necessarily go to the resturant late a night when I am tired, in PJs, and just want a quick soda or water before bed. Good to plan ahead but no fridge to keep cool. Ice bucket works though.
The price was very reasonable and felt about right. The toliet is a bit loud but on the plus side we had great water pressure :)
Would definately stay there again.

title: “A wonderful experience!”
text:
We spent 2 nights at the W for my birthday in July 2010. We had a wonderful experience. After reading some reviews, I was worried it would be a little too "trendy" for us. It wasn't at all. Every single staff member we encountered was friendly and welcoming. The lobby was beautiful. We requested a high floor, and we were given that. We were on the 15th floor and the view of Downtown Dallas was wonderful. My husband told them we were celebrating my birthday before we got there. When we arrived in our room there was a yummy little chocolate cake with a Happy Birthday card from the hotel. Very nice touch. 
The rooms were a *little* on the small side, but it didn't bother us at all. We loved the rooms, very well decorated, very clean. The bed was large and the mattress was very comfortable. The TV was a large flat screen. The bathroom didn't have walls, just a curtain you could close for privacy. It made the room feel a lot bigger, so I liked it. The shower was wonderful and the water pressure was great. 
My husband and I workout a lot. Typically a hotel gym will have a couple of treadmills and not much else. Well, the W was not typical! They had everything we needed to get in some great workouts. Plenty of exercise machines, bikes, ellipticals, treadmills. As well as a lot of hand weights, a bar bells, mats, med balls. There were windows surrounding the gym and it was also on a high floor so the view was great. All the equipment was very well kept, new and clean. 
We absolutely loved the pool. We got up there early so there weren't many people. The pool was clean, plenty of towels, the lounge chairs were comfortable and clean (and cute!). You needed a key to get in and out of the pool area and there was a guard there. It made me feel very secure leaving my purse on our lounge chair while we swam. There was also a bar there and a sitting area so you could order food and drinks.
I can't say enough good about this hotel. We definitely plan to return on our next trip to Dallas.

title: “The real scoop .....”
text: The location was very convenient, right downtown. Staff was very accommodating and helpful. Parking was a bit of a problem if you were arriving late - past 10:00 pm. In the hotel's defense I have yet to stay at a hotel in a large city with an abundance of parking. The elevator was painfully slow, allow extra time or get some exercise on the stairs. Continental breakfast was very good and the room was clean. Noise was fairly minimal, again when you stay in a large city you have to expect some noise from the high activity. If you are wanting a quiet retreat, consider a different destination all together. Five blocks from the Space Needle and about a twenty minute drive in high traffic to Safeco Field. Overall a positive experience and would use this hotel again.

title: “nice hotel , great location”
text:
We stayed here recently and really liked it. We got a very good deal on Hotwire , but I would recommend traveling to the area when the congress is not in session , since most places will decrease their prices. It is conveniently located just 2 blocks from Dupont circle metro station. This is a historic building, recently rennonvated, well kept and nicely old style decorated. We had a decent size room which was very clean with very soft linens. Decoration was old style and victorian . Hotel staff were really polite and helpful. Business center was okay with 2 PCs and a printer. 
We didn't try the restaurants on site and I cannot comment on them. The only really negative point was thin walls ! I travel a lot and have never experienced such thin walls even in cheap motels ! The noise from next door is easily in your ears ! First night people next door were really noisy, but we were lucky that they checked out the next day ! 
But this was such a charming place that I cannot remove a star for this problem ! 
I would stay here again if get a good deal again. Great place .

title: “Rough and Ready!”
text: After reading the reviews I wanted to cancel my reservation, but since they had my credit card number I decided it probably wasn't worth the hassle. It was about an $8 cab ride and ten minute trip from the airport. Nice location downtown, near little Italy. The other positive aspect about the hotel was the bathroom appeared clean. However, do not look too closely at the rest of the room. Unfortunately, I looked under the bed and noticed an extremely thick layer of dust. Also, the pillows are yellowed and stained in places. I had to drag my luggage up the stairs since the elevator was not working. I happened to look out my window in the morning to the view of a bum picking through the garbage about 10 feet from where I was standing. The continental breakfast consists of thinly sliced muffins and breads sitting on a tray near the coffee. The clerk who checked us in was not friendly at all and inflated my agreed upon price (which I clearly understood to include taxes and fees) by about $4. It wasn't worth arguing about since we arrived late in the evening. I would only stay at this place again if I was very desperate for a room in downtown San Diego, otherwise there are plenty of other more comfortable options.

title: “Great location”
text:
We had no issues with the Sofitel. The location cant be beaten. Being a Platnium Aclub member, we were upgraded to a higher floor. No view. Received a welcome drink on our first visit ( we stayed 2 nights then went on a 2 day tour, then checked back in for another 2 nights) but on the second visit, didn't receive one. 
Room was small, but as this is our first visit to the Big Apple, not sure if this is the norm. 
Beds are up to the Sofitel/Pullman standard, very comfy.
Overall a nice place, but not sure if worth the $350 average a night price.
Ken

title: “Nice and conveniently located but a little dated”
text:
I stayed here one night on a business trip. The hotel is relatively close to the airport and the shuttle was about a five minute ride. Check-in at the Honors desk was fast but a line quickly built behind me so I'm glad I walk fast from the shuttle to the front desk. There was a variety of cookies for guests on check-in and not sure if it was because of Christmas or they do this all the time. The front desk was extremely friendly and helpful, one of the best I've encountered at a Hilton property.
The room was on an upper floor in a non-smoking room. Upon entering the room, one can tell that the hotel looks like something from the 80s or maybe very early 90s. The carpet was clean but the overall room looked tired with its older style furniture and lamps, and color scheme that is anything but uplifting; rather dark and drab but probably to compensate for the high wear and tear on airport hotel properties. The beds were typical Hilton with the white bedcover. The sheets were nice, tightly installed on the mattress, and there were four pillows at my disposal. The bathroom was efficient but not over the top, yet it was clean, and if anything, maybe just a little stark and institutional. Shower worked great. The PTR amenity products of shampoo, conditioner, and two bars of soap were available but not the enriched liquid yellow soap that other Hilton executive floor properties offer. Seems like several Hiltons I've stayed at do not automatically put this in the rooms anymore. On several ocassions, I've had to call housekeeping to bring a bottle or two at other Hiltons, but I was too tired to call housekeeping given my late arrival after 9 pm.
I wish there was just a little more lighting in the room for nightime. The bulbs could be brighter. The area upon entry could use a floor lamp just to brighten the area where I unpack my clothes near the closet. 
The breakfast buffet in the hotel lobby the next morning was adequate but not the highest quality of food but they did have smoked salmon with accompaniments. Again, the restaurant was adquately lit in some areas but where I was seated, it was so dark, I could barely read the paper. The wait staff was a little busy that morning so getting beverages wasn't so timely.
Check-out was fast and easy and the shuttle back to the airport quick and convenient. I would stay here again as there was nothing inherently wrong with this Hilton but it just wasn't one of the better ones either. At least I will know my expectation next time I stay here if I come to Philadelphia on business.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
This is a very comfortable luxury hotel with top grade staff who, uniformly, appear to be pleased you chose their hotel. We stayed on two consecutive weekends and the quality was identical. Rooms are spacious and well appointed - although we were advised that floors 7 & 8 on which we stayed were newly refurbished so other floors may vary.
Location is good in that it is a 25 minute walk, 5-10 minute taxi to White House/Capitol/Smithsonian in one direction and a 10 minute stroll in the other to the restaurants of Georgetown. Plentiful taxis available outside the hotel.
I thoroughly recommend the Fairmont.

title: “We loved every minute of our stay!”
text: I was in San Francisco for a conference & my daughter flew out to meet me on the last day. There are so many hotels to choose from in the bay area, it was overwelming. A family friend who lives in Oakland recommended the Argonaut, as her company put her up there when she moved to CA. We could not have picked a more wonderful hotel!! The staff is terrific, not at all snobby like you find in so many big cities. We used the concierge services every morning to help plan our day & directions for getting around. Our room was always very clean & up-to-date with amenities. The Blue Mermaid restaurant adjacent to the hotel is marvelous. We could jump on the cable car across the way for quick access to the city. If you stay at the other hotels I saw located at Fisherman's Wharf, you have to deal have all the tourist traffic & confusion (we were there over an extended weekend) but the Argonaut is at the end of the wharf where you don't get all the noise & street people, yet it's within easy walking distance. We even made it to one of the 5-6 p.m. wine receptions they offer daily in the lobby (Australian wines were being served that evening) - cool idea, very relaxing, & you will meet other guests from all over the country. I spend fifteen years in the hotel business in the 80's & 90's & all I can say is: great choice, you won't regret it!

title: “Hotel average, personell terrible, club ok!”
text:
This is typically one of these places where they put a doormen that has *NO* power in his life, only in his job. Depending on your looks/car-size/female-company he will decide if you can get in and how much you have to pay.
I have been here many times. Completely random they request a cover charge (friends of mine allready inside did not have to pay). When confronting the doormen with this they wanted to kick me out? And trust me, I look very civilized and modern and I'm very nice.
One other time friends of mine had to pay and I just used valet service for my car (a huge Audi): no questions, no payment, etc. Next time I swapped cars and we did the same thing: I had to pay, and my friends did not..
Back to the club: Excellent views, nice environment, nice music (club/lounge). Drinks are expensive. Food is average. I have met some nice people in this club.

title: “OK for us”
text:
Booked room via travelzoo.com---Rate on Fri. March 16 and Sun. March 18 was $179, rate on Sat. March 17 was $219.
I agree that check in is extremely slow. We had only one family in front of us, but still waited over 15 minutes. Not sure what the problem is.....plus only 2 clerks working and I heard one of them mention the hotel was sold out. Management needs to work on that!!!! After driving thru the ice storm on Friday, we were ready to relax and unwind, not stand and wait.
We were given a corner room on the 36th floor which had a nice view of the Chysler Building. Room was decent size, king bed, decent bath, good water pressure, safe in the closet was nice.
On arrival, one pillow sham had a black mark on it----pretty obvious, front and center---maybe someone's mascara----I didn't say anything. After maid service the next day, the sham had not been changed. Tacky!!!! The next day, I left a note on the sham, and at that point was given a clean one. Also, one day we were not left clean wash cloths.
The location was great. We walked everywhere.....restaurants, Jersey Boys, Mamma Mia, Fifth Ave. for the St. Patrick's Day Parade. There were plenty of Irish pubs right out the door. There was security present after 11pm---you had to show a room key.
One thing I noticed, the hotel advertises a 24 hour conceirge. This is not true---sometime in the late evening a sign is put on the conceirge desk that if you need help, you need to see the front desk. Well, you all already know the front desk is understaffed.....and not near as knowledgeable as the conceirge.
I was disappointed by this, because on Sat. evening the conceige was busy, so I thought we'd stop by on our return to the hotel (wanted to ask about Sun. Brunch places, tickets, etc). Well, they were closed!!!!
Also, parking is $45 a night. That's a little high, even by NY standards.
Overall, a decent hotel. The whole check in process needs to be expediated!!!!!! Would that change my mind about staying here again? Yes.......we weren't buying a new car, we were checking into a hotel, and we already had a reservation!!!!!!! Why have 2 people checking in a hotel with 52 floors of rooms. The first rule of hospitality....make a good impression!!!!! It makes you think......where else do they try to cut corners???? Maid service needs to spruce up. With all the hotels in NY, this place needs to tighten up on customer service!!!!

title: “Good price and location.”
text: If you don't mind driving on the highway for 20 minutes into downtown Baltimore, then this is a good place to stay. It is only a few blocks away from the highway, gas stations, stores/services and a major shopping centre. The price was right. Ask for a room on the oppposite side of the highway or facing the pool. (as it would be noisy on the wrong side). The breakfast room could do with more chairs and tables. There was a computer and printer for guests to use free of charge. Dinner was at the mall at an all you can eat buffet (roast beef, seafood, dessert among many items) for only $11 per person. A great value at "Cactus Willies".

title: “Great Location, Great Price”
text:
We arrived early but our room had not been serviced. We were offered an upgrade for a supplement thus allowing us immediate access to the room which was really useful. The bed was very comfortable, the room was very spacious and everything was modern and clean. The best thing about this hotel was its location. It is literally just off Times Square and extremely competitive in price. I would definitely recommend staying at this hotel. 
There are only very minor negatives with this hotel. The bedroom and hotel corridors were very dark. This is not helped by the dark furniture and decor. Struggled to find a table at breakfast. There is a small conference room next to the breakfast area which could be put to better use at breakfast times.

title: “Comfortable hotel, pleasant room..”
text:
This was a great hotel. The room was very large with a walk-in closet and kitchenette. Lots of elbow room which was very nice. Comfortable bed, everything clean...
I would definitely recommend this hotel. I usually prefer staying in the UWS but this location was good since it was only a block from CP. (If you like being in the midtown madness, then this is definitely the place for you!). I would stay here again.

title: “Glass half empty or half full?”
text:
There are good things and not so good things to say about the Crockett Hotel
Good- Start with location, it is right next to the Alamo. You can walk out a door of the Crockett, cross the street, and there is the back entrance to the Alamo. The Riverwalk mall entrance was across the street, too. The included breakfast was quite good and had enough choices for most people. The staff is extremely friendly and wants to help if necessary
Not so good- The rooms are very small, barely enough room for the 2 full-size beds. There is NO space to put one's toiletries at the sink. I was forced to use the window sills. Finally, although this is not a big deal, there was a constant humming noise that seemed to becoming from the Riverwalk Mall exhaust fans. These happened to be located on the side I was staying.
I am not sure if I would stay here again, but I would not rule it out, either

title: “We loved it--great location very nice staff”
text: The Conrad is a modern hotel located in heart of Chicago's gold coast. Easy walking to the shops and attractions. Room was very large and great walk in shower

title: “great hotel”
text: This is a new hotel on the riverwalk. It is an excellent choice since every one there went out of their way to be nice . The food at the riverwalk restaurant was very good and reasonably priced. The rooms are new and the views were outstanding. If you are at the convention center this hotel is right there! It is not one of the tired hotels that are now on the riverwalk. Good stay and very good beds as well.

title: “Loved this little hotel”
text: Tucked in between other buildings on 45th Street between 5th and 6th Avenues (closer to 5th), the Holiday Inn Express almost disappears between its neighboring buildings. We weren't quite sure when the taxi stopped in front of it that we were actually at a hotel. But what a treat! This for a mother/daughter trip to New York. We checked in at the compact lobby, then took the elevator up to one of the higher floors (about 4-5 rooms per floor) to our cozy double-bedded room with window overlooking 45th Street. The beds were comfortable, the room and bathroom clean. And for New York City, we were surprised how quiet it was in our room. Although a continental breakfast was included, the tables were full and we chose to go across the street to Cafe 45 where we could choose from the generous buffet and pay by the weight of our food.

title: “Best Western a Great surprise!”
text:
What a pleasant surprise! I can't lie...when I heard "Best Western" ... I was a little bit worried. I was pleasantly surprised at the nice room and the excellent service received at this secret gem of a hotel in the most perfect location on Michigan Avenue! Upon check-in, the desk clerk could not have been any nicer! He upgraded me to a corner room on the 19th floor which I am assuming was larger than most rooms. We had 2 double beds (see photos), a nice TV unit, a table, 2 chairs and plenty of space!
The bathroom was small but very adequate. (photos) It was lacking in any counter space or hooks, which was a bit difficult with three of us sharing a room.
I can't think of a better location. I have stayed on North Michigan Avenue, and also near the Wacker Bridge...but this location was so central, that I really think it was the best of both worlds. The views from our TWO windows were great! (photos)
The concierge was VERY helpful with directions, suggestions, bus information, etc! If she was not there, the front desk staff knew lots of info, too!
I would definitely stay in the Inn of Chicago again for the great rate that we got.

title: “Goo value, but too noise!”
text:
Great location, good value, clean, confortable. Realy cheaper for the location.
But it is too noise because the street and the plumbing inside the room. It was dificulty to sleep well.
Another thing that worth to comment: one guy tried to stole us right in front of the hotel! I know this is a safe area, but........
Good hotel to stay 2, or 3 nights at maximum. If you don´t have problem with your budget maybe you would like to try another one.

title: “Highly recommended”
text: What a nice stay! My kids loved the ducks and the garden in the atrium that had a stream with fish in it. Wonderful breakfast! We took advantage of their zoo excursion package and the zoo was great!

title: “Not that good”
“Very comfortable and great location”
text: Lovely hotel, convenient location for tourism without being noisy (we had an inside room with no view but appreciated the quiet after a long flight from UK). Staff very friendly and room spotlessly clean. Continental breakfast included in our package, but could pay a little extra for cooked breakfast - good choice. Lots of restaurants within walking distance. Car parking expensive, but cheaper car parks nearby rather than using valet parking. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Excellent location and service”
text:
I spent a week at this hotel with my husband and toddler son, because my husband and I were both attending a conference held jointly at the (attached) Hynes Convention Center and in the Sheraton itself. Since we were travelling with our child the location was critical for us, since we needed to move between our hotel room and conference quickly and easily throughout the day.
We booked a junior suite for $220 since we wanted a bit more space. The room was really nice, with a separate bedroom and living room area (separated by doors) so we could still use the room while our son slept. We were on a high floor and the view from our (very large) window over the Charles rive and Cambridge was amazing, especially in the evening.
What we were most impressed by, however, was the friendly service and how helpful the staff were to businesspeople travelling with a young child. They provided us with a baby crib, small refridgerator and microwave in the room free of charge, without us even needing to request these. All of the staff, including desk staff and cleaning staff, took a moment to smile and chat with our son, which we did not expect at all for a business hotel. The cleaning staff in particular always took the time to check before entering if our son was sleeping, and ask specifically (each day!) if we required any extra amenities (towels, toiletries etc) because of the baby.
As a side note, the conference facilities in the hotel were also entirely satisfactory.

title: “Good Hotel, Great Location”
text: My friend & I spent Nov 18-21 in Manhattan, staying at the Hotel Metro (located on 34th street b/w 5th & 6th.) After doing MUCH research on where to stay that was reasonably priced (read lots of reviews), I choose this hotel and can honestly say that I was very pleasantly surprised. The hotel itself was clean, decorated well, centrally located and the staff was VERY friendly. We didn't spend that much time in the room as there is so much to do in NY but it was clean and comfortable and it had a refrigerator, which was a plus. The only negatives I have is that the bathroom shower was VERY narrow & hard to move in (we're petite girls)so if you are of a heavier set, it could cause quite a problem. The complimentary breakfast was OK - & the restaurant on site wasn't bad. The hotel itself is less than a block away from Macy's & other shops like Gap, Vicky's, Express, H&M, Steve Madden, Deane Pharmacy and more. It is 1 block away from the Empire State Bldg & about 6-8 blocks from Times Square. A couple of bars are located on the same street of the hotel as well as Subway, a Chinese place and nearby is McDonald's, Burger King & Wendy's. Around the corner on 35th street is Keene Steakhouse - which has excellent fillet, if you are looking for a very nice place to have dinner. Definitely recommend the hotel if you are looking for a reasonably priced place where you can lay your head down after a long day of being out and about on the town.

title: “Tapas bar at Standard Hotel New York”
text:
This new seasonal restaurant in front of the Standard New York (where one can ice skate in winter) 
Not a nice experience, I had to wait long time to have my food served..the " the pulpo salad" was reduced to just beans...the grilled shrimps far too salty. My beer was room temperature..I asked the waiter to bring a chilled or fresher one...I waited for 25 more minutes, when it finally arrived was too late, I had to go...so I asked for the bill ...waited for another 20 minutes , could not wait any longer... To speed up the transaction I had to report myself at reception desk explaining the situation and bill to my room. Second timer at Standard New York. Am not sure I ll be back.

title: “Great Location to Times Square”
text: We recently stayed here for two nights in December 2012. Fantastic location, only a block away from Times Square and a short walk to Rockefeller Center. The rooms are a tad bit small, but very clean, and especially, no bed bugs!!! Friendly staff. We will definitely stay again the next visit.

title: “Boston's Best Kept Secret; Highly Recommended!”
text: The atmosphere is pleasant, comfortable, and welcoming. Staff was EXCELLENT. Very clean! AND very affordable!! I will definitely stay here again! Perfect downtown location.

title: “NIce room-- Otherwise feels like a Hampton Inn”
text:
Service is not great at all, in fact on verge of rude... Lobby is pretty but small, yet beautiful. Rooms are very well put together. I would say this is a great hotel for the 50-75+ set considering the design. It just looks like the kind of hotel that middle aged and older adults would enjoy. 
Room was comfortable, yet felt a bit pretentious or maybe geriatric in a way. 
This hotel felt like a hampton inn or a limited service hotel b/c there didn't seem to be much beyond the room that would make this a 4 star hotel. Let alone a 5 star (as it is on priceline!). 
Location is superb and the hotel is pretty comfy, especially for the older traveling set. Room service food was EXCELLENT, by the way. i would say this is a major benefit to the hotel!

title: “Cheap, clean & convenient”
text:
This hotel was voted the cheapest budget hotel in Manhattan & it lived up to its reputation. We arrived in NYC after a long haul flight from Sydney, Australia. We were greeted by Monica, she was extremely pleasant and helpful. We were allowed to check in early 9am which was a welcomed relief :)
Our room was surprisingly spacious and clean (thanks to Ursula our housekeeper), the bathroom was large and had a huge bath for those long soaks after a big day out sight seeing. The bedding and mattress were very comfie! Complimentary tea/coffee machine downstairs, no kitchen facilites. Laundry & dryer were also available onsite.
Yes our room was on the noisey side (street frontage) but hey your in New York its loud, busy and bustling so its to be expected.
Would we stay here again...? most definitely! do we recommend this hotel to other travels....? for sure!! if your on a budget and looking for a central location (2 blocks away from Macys and Penn Station) then Herald Hotel is for you :)

title: “Terrible Neighbourhood and windows don't hold back the noise from the street”
text: The rooms are spacious enough and clean, the staff o.k.. But if you want to have some sleep at night - take another hotel! I rember the 7 eleven truck delievering the store at 3 a.m. and the homeless people jelling all night in front of the hotel very well.......

title: “Great Room. HORRIBLE Restaurant.”
text:
Love our corner room -- spacious and very comfortable. 
DISGUSTED by the bugs (Still kicking!!) that were served with our breakfast. The staff didn't even remove the cost from our bill when we brought the problem to their attention. They just served us MORE!

title: “Great Location, Great Room, Friendly Staff.”
text:
Stayed at Novotel with my wife and 2 children for 9 days in July. Our stay was great, from the bellhop to the front desk to the cleaning staff and everything in between. The room was spacious and functional, the view of Broadway was great, the staff was friendly, the exercise room, although small, was quite adequate (the free fresh fruit was a nice touch). The location couldn't be better, and Gallagher's Steak House a couple of doors down was excellent.
We would DEFINITELY stay here again, and highly recommend it.

title: “Elegant hotel”
text: Booked after reading reviews on this site. Elegant setting. Followed travelers' advice in asking for high floor away from elevator, great suggestion. I was charged for internet but then fitness center was free. Nice pool. Spa on site. Got a room and breakfast deal on the hotel website for $195 + taxes. Walking distance from Boston South station but need a map and not with heavy luggage.

title: “Well pleased- would stay again.”
text:
I stayed here on two occasions. Rooms were well maintained and the staff very friendly. Everything you would expect from a Hyatt Place and then some. Layout of rooms was typical to other Hyatt Place properties.
Thoughts/tips:
One of the beds in my room was very close to the AC system which caused that side of the bedroom to be very cold.
Very clean rooms.
Property feels hidden with no signage. Make sure you put the address into a GPS system instead of simply exiting and expecting to see the property or a sign.
Pool is a bit on the small side, but no one was there the two times my family used it so that presented no problem.
The Hyatt breakfast was more than adequate with typical Hyatt offerings -everything seemed very fresh.
Price of room was very low compared to surrounding properties of its caliber i.e. Holiday Inn Express, etc…
I did not use the service, but I noted that the hotel offers lodging/parking/ transfer service for cruise ship passengers. Given the cost I would think this a good alternative to paying the daily parking rate at the seaport.
Overall I would happily stay here again if my travel plans took me through Jacksonville.

title: “Excellent location and staff (although no king bed) but DO NOT book it via Expedia!!”
text: We stayed at that hotel in May with our 3 young children. Overal, the hotel is excellent, very clean, very well located and couldn't say enough good things about the helpfull and welcoming staff!!! Therefore, the hotel has a slight issue : they didn't have enough tables for breakfast which made it difficult to enjoy our breakfast. But that's a minor issue... The major issue we had was that we had to book it through Expedia (when you call the hotel, you are sent to Expedia). That was a total nightmare!!! Expedia told us that we could book a one bedroom suite with a king size bed (it took about 30 minutes to book because the girl on the phone couldn't hear us, there was a party going on behind her). When we checked in, the problems started : there was a reservation for us but for a two bedroom suite with only queen beds and for a higher price of course. We said to the front desk person that we specified a king bed and just one bedroom (my husband is quite tall and we have a king bed at home...). The lady was very sorry : there was no king beds at all in the entire hotel!!! So considering all that, we decided to cancel one of the 2 nights we booked but Expedia didn't want to, until we told them we recorded all that discussion and we would send it to our lawer, which actually was true (the persons on the phone at Expedia would not consider our call and put us on hold each time we would explain the situation!!!). So we finaly canceled one of the 2 nights BUT on that same night, the lady at the front desk asked us if we had visitors coming over on that night... Turns out, behind our back, Expedia had booked a second room under our name!!!!! Thanks to the hotel Manager, we only had to pay for the big 2 bedroom suite for one night. He was very sorry for what happened and mad at Expedia... Otherwise, I would highly recommend that hotel if you don't mind sleeping in a queen size bed!

title: “Top location, good value by NY standards”
text: This hotel is on the corner of Broadway & 53rd, very well placed for Times Square, the theatre district and Central Park. MoMA is about 5 minutes walk away, ditto the Rockefeller Centre. The blue subway line station is only a block away which is a big help. The vibe and the decor, room layout etc are straight from the standard Novotel playbook. We enjoyed the strong French feel, with many francophone tourists and also Air France crew (how is it that they all look so stylish, by the way?). We went to see Jersey Boys, literally across the street from the hotel entrance. The singing diner on Broadway is a great spot for an entertaining breakfast. About the only negative was the relatively small number of internet stations for the size of the hotel, so there were often queues for access.

title: “Awesome NYC Hotel -- highly recommend!”
text: For NYC, this was a great value! For under $500, we had a gorgeous, spacious suite, comfortable bed, fabulous location on the south end of Central Park, and the service was fantastic. When I told the hotel we were celebrating our anniversary, they sent complementary chilled champagne and truffles upon our arrival. They couldn't have been nicer or more accomodating. We would definitely stay here again, and will recommend to our friends and family.

title: “Very Nice”
text: this was my friend's first trip to SF and I wanted to be sure we had a hotel that afforded us the mobility we needed the hotel is in a great location, has friendly staff-any questions asked were answered, nightly wine, and a decent room-the closet was a great size(better than i expected) while my friend stated the room was on the small side-which i expected since i read the previous reviews-it was still comfortable enough for us and her monster piece of luggage ;-) the only negative about the room was the bathtub but as long as i was clean in the end, it didn't matter too much the restaurant within the hotel was lovely, gorgeous decor and the food was filling and delicious if we go back to SF, staying at this hotel will be the #1 choice

title: “Small Rooms, but great vibe at hotel”
text: I have stayed at this hotel previously and loved the vibe. The rooms are terribly small, however, and no upgrade was available at check-in. The rooms are very clean and well appointed, but I had to ask my husband to get up from the chair at the desk every time I wanted to cross between the chair and the bed. Or, I could have scampered across the bed like a monkey. The bathroom was also very small. While there was room for a toothbrush, my makeup bag had to remain on the toilet tank lid. The common areas of the hotel are fabulous and I thought it was a decent value in Chicago.

title: “Staycation”
text: This is a great LA historical hotel only a few blocks off of the subway and within several excellent downtown LA restaurants. On top of friendly staff, a cozy room, complimentary upgrades, and perfect proximity.... The rooftop pool lounge feels like an exclusive retreat.

title: “Good hotel in great location with a price that won't break your pocketbook”
text:
We usually stay at either Hotel Lucerne or The Peninsula but decided to give Park Central a shot.
Positives:
Hotel is well located near Central Park & a 10 minute walk to Times Square. Rooms are clean and adequate (though bathroom small). $300/nt seemed reasonable by New York standards.
Negatives:
we asked for upgrade (as room was small) -- none available (so book a larger room if space matters to you). We asked for tiny fridge & one was promised but never delivered. Included breakfast package disappointed us as sternos were "out" at 0830 making ALL food cold. Next day ordered Breakfast .. took 40 min. for eggs benedict (cold again). 3rd day we had breakfast out of hotel at Rue 57.
Last, but not least, we returned one day at 3pm & room STILL hadn't been serviced. A manager apologized & brought us fresh towels while the wife & I made our bed.
When we complained about all of the above the on-duty manager, to her credit, DID give us a $100 bill deduction for our inconveniences.
Would we stay here again? Perhaps, perhaps not.

title: “Unlike everybody else we had a terrible experience”
text:
If you park your car in this hotel, BE CAREFUL! You will have to park near the front lobby to be safe. We had a terrible experience. A thief siphoned our gasoline COMPLETELY (a full tank) out of our car gas tank. He cut the filler hose to the tank so we could not refill it. The manager was nice to lend us a DUCT tape so my husband can tape the filler hose together so we can go home to California. My husband made it work but the experience dampened our stay there for 3 nights.
On top of that , we had a terrible experience during our 1st night. We were assigned to a room near the elevator. All night long, we could hear the elevator going up and down and we slept poorly. The bed was good but the sound was bothering us. I don't know why anyone was assigned to that room at all. We should have asked for them to move us in the middle of the night but we didn't want to repack our stuff in the middle of the night.
They moved us to a room in the corner (end of the hotel). The room was just ok but the bed was terrible. In the beginning of the night it was firm but by morning, my side sank down like it had a leak or something. We parked our car at this end and I think it was a mistake.
I wanted to give 1 star but the service from front desk was great in helping us to recover our bad experience. Also, the room was clean and nice (despite the bed). It is not the hotel's fault that a thief stole our gasoline so I gave a 2 stars. But overall experience was so bad that I can't give more stars.
The hotel should provide more security and install a security camera in the premises. The gasoline that was stolen costs us $60 but to fix the hose, it costs us $160. It was the worst driving vacation for us.

title: “a good stay”
text: Was there last weekend, which was accidentally timed with Fashion Week, Chinese New Year, and the long President's Day weekend. The hotel was packed but handled it gracefully. Was not in a tower room but had a Park Avenue room, large, with decorative fireplace and modern bath. While not quite as fresh as the tower, it was well-maintained and service was very good. It can absorb a crowd. Very professional staff.

title: “Exceeded all expectations”
text: We had an awesome time at Trump Chicago this past weekend. Our suite exceeded all of our expectations (and, we have high expectations - we typically stay at the Ritz, Four Seasons or Peninsula in Chicago). We stayed in a deluxe one-bedroom suite. It was at least 1,500 square feet. The kitchen and both bathrooms were beautifully decorated, stocked and appointed. The fireplace in the living room area was a very nice touch. The bedroom part of the suite was huge and included an enormous dressing area just outside of the master bathroom. This hotel clearly anticipates guests needs and delivers - in most high end hotels, you have to request what you need for a bath (salts, oils, sponge, etc.) - Trump includes all of this with the room. In the kitchen, we had a very nice selection of high end teas and an espresso machine. The Sub-Zero refrigerator was stocked with all sorts of alcoholic and soft drinks. In fact, the suite was so nice that we canceled our dinner reservations at a nearby restaurant, visited a local grocery store and made dinner in the suite! The staff at Trump delivered a bottle of chilled champagne and a tray of chocolate-covered strawberries to our suite as we were arriving - we enjoyed these treats as we prepared dinner. I should mention that our suite had very high ceilings - the drapes were so long that they opened/closed electronically, by pressing buttons on the wall. The huge expanse of ceiling to floor windows overlooked the Chicago river and nearby buildings - very urban - we felt like we were downtown Chicago residents. All of the lights in the suite were on dimmers so that we could create some very romantic conditions throughout the suite in the evening. I could go on and on - but, I'll wrap up by saying that Sunday brunch at Sixteen was awesome - especially the dessert selections. And, the pool area/fitness center was in line with a 5-star resort - very impressive. Finally, I loved the staff - everyone who we encountered went over the top to make sure that we had everything that we needed and wanted right when we requested it - from simple things like a DVD to watch on Saturday night to stocking my favorite green tea in the suite - no request went unanswered - and every request was handled professionally and timely. I couldn't have been more impressed.

title: “2nd Wonderful visit at the New York Palace!”
text: Stayed for the second time at the New York Palace June 28th. Great deal through hotels.com for a double with cathedral views. What a lovely experience. From the moment we walked in the gorgeous lobby till we checked out we had a great experience. Check in was a breeze, the room was ready hours before check in which was helpful so we could drop off our bags and head out into the city. The room is lovely. Good firm beds, the best of any NYC hotel Ive been in. Always a super plus for me...a great shower! Super hot water,lots of water pressure, large Egyptian cotton towels. We were on the 21st floor with a view right out on to St. Patrick's cathedral. Amazing to see the sun set right between the buildings. The hotel being on Madison avenue is a nice plus. One block from Rockefeller Center but far enough from the crowds. The M4 bus runs right in front of the hotel. The doorman is always there to get a cab for you with a smile and a nice word. And unlike many hotels in the city, the doormen didn't seem to be pushing for a tip. My only beef, and its minor, is the lack of reasonably priced food choices. While delicious, $33 for a hamburger is a bit much even for NYC. Overall a really great stay. Expensive but worth every penny.

title: “great find”
text: what a great find...free parking, only a few minutes from downtown,great rooms and views, down comforters, and all the other luxury amenities...front desk staff was great...very clean....all for 99.00 .....

title: “nautical charm and near-magical service”
text: The Argonaut Hotel proved to be full of nautical charm and near-magical service. I was overwhelmingly impressed with the care put into every detail from the precise-yet-whimsical maritime decor to Ernie the bellhop's never-miss restaurant recommendations. Iced tea is offered in the lobby at 4pm, wine from 5-6pm and lemon ice water throughout the day. Expedia made me pay extra for the "wine reception" but every guest is welcome so don't fall for that. The Argonaut's staff truly make their guests feel at home while ensuring that their stay is also a luxurious one. We stayed in a King View room and waking up to the Golden Gate Bridge shrouded in fog was amazing. The only downside might be the location, as Fisherman's Wharf had throngs of tourists -that I don't remember from my last visit in 2001. I would definitely recommend The Argonaut Hotel to anyone wanting an authentic San Francisco vacation. Watching gleeful trolley riders hang on and ascend, we ended our trip with an Irish coffee around the corner from The Argonaut at Buena Vista Cafe.

title: “Always Stay Here when I am in NYC”
text:
Great location, used to be a Day's Hotel NYC. The rooms are much nicer now with the Hilton Flair. Flat Screen TV's Big Rooms & great location. right near some great bars and Time's square just a few blocks away. Great Prices! Can say enough about this place. Never used the fitness center, just did a lot of walking around the beautiful City. Stayed here during the Valentines Day Blizzard of 2006.
Great Value for NYC

title: “Great location / Helpful Staff”
text: I stayed at the Courtyard with a friend after we went to see a play on Broadway. Our room - with 2 queen beds - was a generous size by NYC standards. The room was modern and clean and the beds are the new Marriott beds - quite comfortable! The front desk staff and the concierge were both extremely helpful in making arrangements for dinner and the trip to the airport the following morning. For the price, location & staff courtesy, this hotel is highly recommended.

title: “Absolutely pure dead brilliant”
text:
This was our first time in New York and the hotel met all of our needs and more. My boyfriend (now fiance!!!) had emailed Valerie beforehand and she ensured that we had an amazing room on the 26th floor with a balcony. My boyfriend had advised that he was going to propose and wanted to make it extra special, the hotel went out of their way to accomodate!! I woulld definately stay here again and recommed to all of my friends. 
The location was central and 10 minute walk to times square and empire state.
We never to got to thank Valerie in person as she was setting up the new Affinia in DC, so Valerie from both my fiance and me I would just like to say a big Scottish thank you for making our time extra special. You really made my whole New York and engagement experience so much more special. A thousand Thank You's and maybe we will see you when we return.xx

title: “Great Meeting”
text: Held a regional conference for 225 attendee's first week of October and couldn't be more pleased with the customer service and quality experience we had. Great hotel, Great location, Great city.

title: “Freeway noise is ridiculous”
text:
We showed up on a Friday night around 10pm. We had requested a king bed but were told they sold out and would have to settle for two double beds. Not uncommon checking in late on a weekend so what could I say? Once at the room we were immediately greeted with the noise from I-5 right outside the window. I could not believe how loud it was and thought maybe the window was open. I was disappointed to find out the windows were in fact closed but the 6th floor put me right at the freeway.This place is very outdated with aluminum windows that provide no sound insulation.
We decided to call down to the front desk in hopes of getting a different room. To my pleasant surprise we were told a gentleman would be on the way up with new keys to a room on the other side of the hotel. He then proceeded to take us to the 23rd floor and gave us a room on the other side of the building with a king bed! This room was much better with no freeway noise as you can imagine. However, I was a bit confused as 10 minutes prior I was told there were no king rooms available.
I was very disappointed in the overall quality of the rooms and hotel. This place is very tired and in need of a remodel. I have stayed at several 4 star properties in downtown Seattle and this one was by far the least impressive. If you do choose to stay here make sure you get a room opposite the freeway. This place is planted right on I-5.

title: “hate the noise”
text:
Nice room and amenities. Very warm staff. The noise was awful all day , but unbeareable at night with the garbage trucks working all night in front of the rooms located at the front.
never return to this place.

title: “Great sleep in the heart of Chicago”
text: Hotel is very close to the Magnificent Mile - shopping and site seeing. The guest room, while a little small was well appointed, bed was very comfortable and the bathrooms were very nice. Make sure you don't miss "the Bean" at Millenium Park.

title: “doubletree Guest Suites. Perfect position for tourists”
text:
My husband,myself and 2 sons aged 15 and 13 stayed for 4 nights from Oct 28th. First the pros.
1. Hotel rooms very clean and comfortable
2.Security was excellent. We felt very safe.
3. Because of its central location we did not have to take any public transport. and could walk most places
4. Everything teenagers could want, ( i.e Virgin Megastores next door, Hard Rock Cafe, Element etc ) If they are happy we are happy!!!
5. Conciege very helpful and advised us and booked all our trips.
Now the Cons;
I booked and pre paid for a Premium 2 bedded suite on a high floor with a city view. We got a room on the 20th floor over looking the back of the hotel with big air conditioning units buzzing all night. When I enquired about this I was told that 2 bedded suites did not overlook the city. 
Why do they advertise this if it is not available..... I could have saved myself $150 and just booked a regular room. 
I was told I should have got an email. I did,but this just confirmed what I had already booked and paid for.
Apart from this blot on an otherwise good hotel in a good location I would definately stay at this hotel again but would be confirming by telephone that I was going to get exactly what I paid for.

title: “location, location, location”
text:
This was our 1st visit to San Francisco. We chose the Beresford having seen details in the Lonely Planet and checking out their own website. I wanted somewhere central and thats exactly what I got - literally a couple of blocks from Union square and the cable cars. By American standards the rooms are small - but they are clean and lets face it the hotel is a base only, if you want the bells and whistles (which I never have time to use) then you need to be looking at one of the larger chains which have a much pricer rate. No aircon which could be a problem in the summer. 
Had breakfast one morning in the hotel and after that ate out - the cereals are a little too sweet for the english tastebuds and I wasn't keen on plastic plates ! 
According to him who must be obeyed (in his dreams) the Bloody Marys served in the bar are to recommended
Had a mini bar in the room which had a very reasonable dry white wine for $10 per bottle - although there a couple of shops a couple of doors away 
Several restaurants within easy walking distance
Can recomment Cesario's which is the Italian on the corner down the hill from the hotel. Don't make the mistake we did and try the one on the other side of the street and up the hill - which can be seen from the hotel enterance many of the staff did not speak english. 
I would consider using the Beresford again and we will be passing this info onto friends. Great value for money 
Finally book direct with the hotel via their website - we saved nearly 50% on the price quoted by a well known online booking agent - enjoy your time in San Francisco

title: “Best Hotel in Chicago”
text:
Great rooms and spacious bathrooms, fantastic service and thw best restaurant on S. Michigan Ave.
The staff is delightful with an incredible sence of customer service . . . Great smiles and total knowledge of the local attractions.

title: “The Hilton Squaw Peak is a very nice resort, with exciting things for the kids and relaxing for adults.”
text: The room was nice for a family of four. It had 2 comfortable beds and a pull out couch. The location was easy to find from the airport and easy to get around the city. We all loved the amenities with the lazy river, pools, restaurants, gift shop (we utilized for breakfast, great selection) and business center.

title: “There wasn't anything we didn't like about the Monaco!!!”
text: From the warm greeting upon our arrival (and the early check-in!), to the nicely appointed rooms (with good product!) to the afternoon wine and snacks (and complimentary massage if you signed-up early enough!), to the helpful doorman (who got us taxis and gave directions and "the local's" restaurant recommendations.....we had a fantastic long weekend, made all the better by the great accommodations at the Hotel Monaco.

title: “Great deal in great location...”
text:
Last week we (my wife and 3 year old boy) had a pit stop in NYC for 36 hours. 3 days before our stay we reserved a room at the ACE hotel. The hotel has a good location, great energetic staff and very cool rooms and reception. Rooms has best minibar in town, robes for everyone, old retro record player but also connection for all your Apple gear for itunes music playback. Service level is high and energetic. Overall a great brand kept very consistent throughout the hotel and booking experiance. 
Only a few comments from being perfect. On our floor ()12) there was a lot of party noice (3 hours) and that kept us awake more than we wanted. The hotel also recommended the THE BRESLIN BAR & DINING ROOM next door for a steak. We dinned and I ended up paying $109 for a steak, which needless to say is outragious. On the menu it did say F(fair)MP (marketprice) and the waiter never told me I was eating a small fortune! 
I will for sure go back but order a salat next time!

title: “We had a great time”
text: We just got back from the Catamaran and we loved it. We stayed on the 4th floor of the tower and had a great view of mission bay. I recommend the 4th floor or higher on the mission bay side. The hotel is right accross the street from the ocean where it is like city life and then you enter the hotel grounds and it is like Hawaii. Birds singing, ducks on the grass and fish in the many pools. We went bicycle riding on the the beach walk and sailing in mission bay. This hotel was in the center of the action but also in its own oasis. Had a great time and recommend it.

title: “Excellent upscale hotel in convenient center city location”
text: We stayed at Le Meridien on a Saturday night. The hotel is convenient to Museum Row and an easy walk to Rittenhouse Square (loaded with good restaurants). The hotel is an interesting mix of modern and old architecture. It has an exposed brick interior and very modern and stylish rooms. The hotel is not large but has a nice restaurant and bar. The fitness room is small but nicely done. If you want a large fitness facility, there is one connected to the hotel. I self parked three blocks away for only five dollars a day!! Philadelphia is an underrated city and we highly recommend it. Le Meridien is an exceptionally nice hotel. The Concierge was very friendly and helpful.

title: “Awesome”
text: This historic building is awesome. The place is clean and the rooms are clean. Kinda reminds you of those old black and white movies. The staff is friendly and helpful. Love it!

title: “Perfect Place”
text:
This hotel is a little ways away from the hubbub of Washington Mall but the commute was easy. The hotel is near the Vice President's home. The bus picks you up across the street and drops you off wherever you need to go. Or, you can have the shuttle bus drop you off at the entrance of the subway and give them a call to pick you up. The driver may tell you some things going on in the city while on your drive. 
The beds were great. May have to get one those expensive mattresses some day.
They have a couple of front loading washing machines and dryers that cost only $1.25 each and worked great. The vending machine to buy soap took my money, but the front desk sent the husband back down with a cup of liquid soap.
Oh, the front desk people were wonderful. Everyone was friendly and helpful. The most 
informative front desk personnel ever encountered. Even the people in the garage where we parked our vehicle were friendly!
If I ever came back to Washington DC, I would definitely stay here again!! Wonderful Job
Savoy Suites!!

title: “Very good hotel, reasonably priced”
text: Stayed for 3 nights, spacious (for NY standards) 7th floor room with direct view to balcony and outside (the window room is by the balcony, so someone there may view inside). The bed was very comfortable. The hotel is small (about 3 rooms per floor), well located, and the staff friendly. My only complaints were the noise coming from the corridor whenever someone was there (it´s a fairly tight corridor and the room door does not provide adequate sound-proof), which happened only seldom, and some of the bathroom towels needed to be better cleaned (stains not completly removed eventually because of defective washing). Altogether minor complaints, compared with the obvious advantages. It was a good staying and I will definetly recommend this hotel as a very good option for New York.

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text:
We stayed for two nights at the Hilton last week. The location is outstanding with Chinatown starting on the opposite side of the street. The hotel is an excellent base to hit Chinatown againa nd again without having to worry about parking. (The excellent Wok Wiz Chinatown we went on tour also starts in the Hilton lobby). A good tip I heard about is that the views from the Bay Side of the hotel (compared to looking back the other way) are excellent. I therefore called up prior to our stay and requested a high up room on the Bay Side. The hotel was happy to oblige which makes me think if you don't ask you stand a greater chance of not getting the bay Side view. Our view from the 21st floor was stunning. The room itself was very tastefully decorated and felt "new" & trendy compared to your usual plain / average room. There was also free WIFI in the room and the service must have been good as my son said it was ridiculously fast! We didn't eat at the in-house restaurant Seven Fifty but it looked appealing. Adjacent to the restaurant is a very nice bar. When you enter the bar you pass by a shelf incased in glass. Within the glass is a permanently burning fire coming out of pebbles which was nice to look at. Pleasing to me was the bar had decent beer on draft (Anchor Steam). Another tip is not to use the hotel valet which is expensive at $42 a day. There is a public parking garage opposite the hotel, Portsmouth Square Garage, where you can self park for less. In fact, we were in San Francisco for only two days after staying elsewhere in California. We decided we wouldn't need a car in SF as parking is an expensive challenge all over SF so we parked at the Portsmouth Garage, checked in, immediately left the hotel, picked up our car ($2.50 in parking), and drove & dropped it off at Avis in Fisherman’s Wharf. The remaining taxis we took during our stay, including to the airport, were a fraction of what we would have paid in rental + parking charges if we had kept our rental car.
All in all we loved our stay at the Hilton Financial District and there is no question we will stay there next time we visit SF

title: “Not impressed by the Hyatt”
text: We travelled during 3 weeks. Seattle was the last stop before going back home. We stayed in this hotel because of the location and for the free continental breakfast. We had a room on the third floor but on a side of a busy road, it wasn't possible to move because the 2 queens bedrooms were located on that side. If you can avoid the noisy street with the gas station. Beds were comfortables, towels were cleaned.The breakfast was simple not delightful. It's close to the downtown but far from the waterfront.

title: “Perfect stay”
text: We stayed at the Skyline during the week between Christmas and New Years. We arrived at 10 am and instead of just dumping our luggage, we were shown to our large updated room many hours prior to their official check-in. Service was first class and all employees from the concierge to the cleaning staff were most accomodating and helpful. Location was good including a few good places to eat nearby. We would definitely return again.

title: “Great stay! Great location!”
text: I love, love, love this hotel. The staff was AMAZING and extremely hospitable! Edita. at the front desk, made some wonderful recommendations of things to do in the area. The location was so close to everything we wanted to see and more. The only downside was the noise which I knew about ahead of time (thanks to Tripadvisor). The floors creaked above us and you could hear every step that was made. The street noise was pretty loud early into the morning but nothing too extreme. The rooms were clean and well maintained. My next trip to San Francisco will include the Hilton Fisherman's Wharf!

title: “Not up to Marriott Standards”
text:
Positives: very professional, cheerful check in service and great breakfast service in Marsten's the next morning (manager very courteous and checked on us along with great server during buffet); since the club level lounge is being renovated, we were given free breakfast buffet coupons and a free appetizer coupon. Comfortable bed in room. Great location close to US Airways Center and Chase Field. Restaurants/bars within walking distance.
Negatives: late night lobby bar drinks and food at a table---I had to ask twice for our check by walking up to the bar. The first time, the female server said "Just a minute, maam. Sorry.". She seemed very flustered, even though the bar was not crowded. So I waited another 10 minutes at our table while she proceeded to check on about 6 other customers and served 5 cocktails. Seems like they cater to airline personnel who stay at the hotel regularly? I went up to the bar a second time and said "I just want to charge this to the room." She finally, grudgingly gave me the bill. And there were 3 people working at the bar area! Excuse me-----and this is a Renaissance?
Also, again since the club level lounge was being renovated, there is a "Quiet Lounge" on the 18th floor with snacks and drinks. The sign outside said "Have you heard? The Quiet Lounge is open Sunday at 5:00 PM to Friday at 12:00 PM." We wanted some water at 10:00 PM on a Wednesday after returning from a concert, and the room was locked and dark. My husband called the front desk, and was rudely told that the Quiet Room closes at 10:00 PM as shown on all signs. 
Lastly, hallways smelled of cigarette smoke and there was mildew on the walls.

title: “Conveniently located Elegance & Charm”
text:
For years stayed at hotels around Union Square, but last two visits to SFO, stayed at the Palace Hotel in the financial district (Market/Montgomery) after hearing about it from others. 
Location: From the airport, if you wish to take BART ($8.10 each way), the stop/entrance is just outside the Market Street Entrance of the hotel. For quick bites, it is an easy walk to good eats and treats/weekend markets at the Ferry Building (Slanted Door, Delica, Miette) and also at Westfield Center (Bristol Market, The Straits, Out the Door, Beard Papa) and to Union Square (Macys, Saks, Neiman Marcus, etc.)
Room: High ceilings, well-services, wonderful bedding (ultra soft linens), in room safe, small refrigerator that is stocked with complimentary water daily and room for your own snacks, Gilchrest & Soames toiletries, good shower water pressure and hot water is hot.
Garden Court Restaurant: Beautiful atrium setting, always a magnificent floral centerpiece, and Sunday buffet musicians. Meals there were very good and attentive service. Maxfields was also a nice place to stop for drinks and a quick meal (whether pizza, a hearty burger or roast chicken, etc.) Kyoya, the Japanese restaurant surpassed expectations.
Price: both times secured very reasonable rates ($189 - 200) via Expedia, Cheap Tickets.

title: “Nice staff, actual accommodations so-so”
text: I stayed at the Elan for 3 nights a few months ago. In town for work and the location was great for my purposes (getting to and from Gower Studios quickly). I already knew the neighborhood well, and it is a great one for seeing Hollywood, Weho, and pretty much anything you'd want in LA. The staff was nice and seemed helpful, although again I didn't really need info or anything from them so my contact was minimal. My issue with the hotel is simply that actual bed etc seemed barely over motel class. There was nothing particularly wrong with it, It just wasn't wasn't luxe by any stretch of the imagination. Bed was very hard, pillows were flat, linens were scratchy. The room was very warm, and although there was an outside "balcony" it was on street level facing a run-down apartment building and wasn't exactly enticing. At the time I stayed there was no onsite restaurant or bar so after a long day of shooting, relaxing in the evening and having a drink at the hotel was not possible. I think I paid just under $200 per night for the room, which frankly didn't seem worth it, especially compared to other hotels in LA at the same price point that had more to offer. Most likely I won't stay again.

title: “Loved the Cabrillo Garden”
text:
I just wanted to let you know that this hotel was really GREAT.
Instead of feeling like hotel, it felt more like staying at someone's home. The staff was very friendly and willing to help out if we needed anything. It was the first time I felt like a guest instead of a customer. You should be very proud of the service this hotel offers it is exemplary. I will definitely be staying again.

title: “I really like this hotel”
text:
The Sofitel is my favorite hotel to stay at in New York whether for business or pleasure. There are surely fancier and more expensive hotels at tonier addresses, but the Sofitel is certainly no slouch. And it is consistently quiet, comfortable, and convenient. 
Last weekend, I stayed at the Sofitel for the first time ifor pleasure with my wife. I had stayed their previously for business probably 10 times over the last 3 years. 
The lobby at the Sofitel is small and luxurious. You get the feel of a small hotel although the Sofitel is actually quite large. When I arrived last Friday it was bustling a little more than I remembered but was still relatively quiet. When I checked in at the desk, I was informed my room was on the third floor, which I somewhat expected given the price and category I paid for. When I asked if there was another room on another floor, I was told there was not one in the same category. That did not suprise me because I already knew the hotel was sold out. But what did suprise me was that I was offered a suite for a $100 upgrade on a high floor.
Our suite was beautiful with an excellent view of the city. The bedroom and bathroom were virtually identical to a deluxe king room (I had booked a queen room) but you had the addition of a separate sitting room with a large flatscreen tv and desk. 
As usual the service at the hotel was attentive but understated. We used the concierge several times and they were always helpful. I thought the staff was very friendly. 
The only meal we ate at the hotel this trip was a quick early dinner one night on the way back to the airport. I had no complaints with the service or food. I have always found the restaurant in the hotel to be a step above most hotel restaurants.
We did go to the Red Flame diner down the street for breakfast one morning. It was fine, nothing to write home about. It is a good cheap diner. 
We also went down the street to one of my favorite sushi restaurants, Sush Zen. Really exceptional sushi and sashimi, and less than two blocks from the Sofitel. Sit at the sushi bar. Very expensive, but worth it. 
You should be aware that for reasons I don't understand (or maybe I do) they don't air condition the hallways in the guest room floors. In the heat of the summer that can create some concern as you are taking the short walk from the elevators to your room. But don't worry, the guest rooms and lobby stay plenty cool. 
I had been telling my wife about the Sofitel for some time. I think after this trip she understands why I prefer to stay there over some other high end hotels. It is simply comfortable and you can't beat the convenience.

title: “Do not even consider this hotel!”
text: This hotel is disgusting. We stayed here in 2004 and it was ok for the price. Now it is positively disgusting. We asked for a non smoking room and got a smoking room that smelled terrible like pets and smoke. At the front desk do not speak to Navi she was rude and has zero personality to be in customer service. This hotel needs to be closed and revamped. Do not stay here!

title: “A great stay!”
text:
My partner and I stayed at the Hotel Grand Union from the 8th - 11th July.
GOOD POINTS:
Large, nice rooms.
Good location- short walk to the Empire State Building.
So cheap for NY!
Internet services available in the lobby (at a price). 
Captains Cafe next door is a great place for brekky!
Air-conditioning.
Staff are very accomodating and frendly. 
BAD POINTS:
Slow lift.
As you can see, I don't really have anything negative to say about this Hotel.
It was one of the cheapest Hotels we could find, but it exceeded our expectations!
I would stay here again, and recommend it to everyone!

title: “We stayed for 7 nights and this was a great hotel choice for our family trip to D.C.”
text: Staff was super-friendly and helpful. The manager (Eddie) even knew our names and greeted us each time we came into the lobby! Very impressive. The hotel was clean, the room was comfortable and quiet, and we thoroughly enjoyed the buffet breakfast every morning. The rooms don't have much of a view. The lobby is a cheerful place to hang out and there was plenty of staff available to answer questions or give touring advice. We appreciated the complimentary water and cookies after a long day of sight seeing! There is a Metro station right across the street. Our room wasn't ready for over an hour when we arrived in the late afternoon, so the manager sent up a plate of strawberries and wine. Very nice! We would definitely consider staying here again.

title: “Great location”
text: We stayed at the Dupont Circle over Christmas weekend and found it to be a great value in a terrific location. Only criticism is that the front-desk staff misdirected us regarding food service on Christmas day - which was very frustrating. Would go back.

title: “Great staff help - I'd Stay Here again”
text:
Walked in under less than happy circumstances, (someone in the local hospital) and was very pleased with the place. While yes, it is aging somewhat and breakfast buffet is way too expensive ($15) the staff was so kind and so helpful, I'd stay there again. My rooms beds were very comfortable, everything was clean and in order, shower was fine, internet worked and was free. Plus the pools were fine as was the jacuzzi. AND all the gym equipment worked well. My room was quiet, ...parking, check in was easy. 
It ain't the Ritz and I am not sure I'd book a bigwig convention there, but overall, I thought it was a fine place to stay.

title: “Hurricane Sandy”
text:
My wife and I stayed with you on October the 26th just before Hurricane Sandy. We had a very nice stay and would recommend your hotel. It is in a great location in Georgetown. The are is very active with many wonderful restaurants within walking distance. Shopping is only a few blocks away. 
B Pultz

title: “Outstanding Service”
text: We arrived early and our room wasn't ready but the staff eagerly stored our bags and the concierge made some excellent recommendations and assisted with reservations. When we returned the desk clerk inquired if we specifically wanted a corner room or would we like one with a better view just down the hall. Within an hour of getting in the room Jennifer delivered a bag of goodies with a smile...an extremely nice touch. We will most certainly make this hotel one of our first choices when returning to NYC.

title: “Great location”
text: very close to michigan avenue and state street. right below the hotel are lots of places to eat. very convinent especially during bad and cold weather.

title: “Yawn...and not from the beds”
text: This hotel is supposed to be new but it feels like I've stayed here before under a different name. Overall it's an okay hotel--but nothing special. The lobby is nondescript so you don't get a feel for what style it's aiming for. Then the rooms are minimal but not really from a designed pov. Almost feels skimpy moreso than understated 'cool'. The room is small without a real closet. The bathroom is large enough, but the shower isn't fully enclosed so it's a bit of an odd experience. NO coffee maker! Why? : ) Frankly it's several small amenities that are lacking that hurt the experience. I like the fact that it's very clean and refurbished but I am simply not impressed enough to recommend it as a great NY hotel.

title: “great!”
text: Hubby and i stayed here for two nights. Got great rates of their website. Room was very clean and very tasteful decor. Good location close to space needle. I would have given it a 5 star if there was a restaurant in the hotel. But there are great restaurants nearby within walking distant. I love that the hotel give comlimentary bikes, we rode the bikes everywhere and covered alot more grounds than walking. Would definately stay here again.

title: “Disappointing and Tired.”
text: Our first room had one king size bed and NO room to walk around! The furniture and duvet were very tired, needing updating. The bathroom was clean...room 802 is not one I would recommend to a friend. The front desk were helpful with some problems we had with our booking through Expedia, and did try their best to right the situation. However, I do feel this hotel is overrated and needs renovation.

title: “Elegant,hip and comfortable”
text: We were pleasantly surprised,stately building with the hippest decor and a very cool vibe.Definately the place to be on a Friday night.The rooms although small were extremely comfortable and well appointed and extremely clean.The bar transforms from evening happening into a very quiet library coffee bar in the morning with great coffee.Close walking proximity to restaurants and shopping.Definately going to stay again.

title: “Great location, room and staff!”
text: Just got back from NYC and of the 4 times I have been there I would have to say that this is the best hotel that I have stayed at. Great location with the number 2 &3 trains being one block away. The staff was always super helpful and very friendly. Would definetely go back and recommend to others visiting the big apple.

title: “Sleep Hot! On Tiny Pillows”
text: We were able to check-in early. The room was beautiful but we like to sleep cool usually 67 degrees. The thermostat wouldn't allow us to go lower than 69 degrees. I'm all for being Eco-conscientious but NOT when it comes to my sleeping comfort. They should have told us this up front. The king bed had 4 small not even STD pillows that my head would roll off of. Elevator was SLOW. Restaurant was good and free drinks with priority club membership. Free WIFI -AWESOME!

title: “Amazing Service!”
text:
The staff at this hotel are above and beyond when it comes to enthusiasm and hospitality. From check in (the desk agent carried my suitcase up the stairs for me and was very knowledgeable about the area for recommendations on restaurants, coffee houses, and locations for my meetings) to check out (accommodating a last minute request for a late checkout) they responded promptly, politely and delivered 110%. 
Room and public space were all very clean. My room was near the elevator but, surprisingly, I didn't hear it at all through the night. The layout of the room works well. The bed is in its own alcove so plenty of space to move around. The bathrooms are small but functional, they got creative so you have plenty of vanity space; downside is the shower curtain blows in on you since the shower has the straight instead of curved bar.

title: “Disappointing Sheraton Property”
text: When the best thing you noted about the hotel is its fast elevators, you know it is only an average hotel. The elevators in the Tower Building are among the fastest I have experienced in a hotel – true statement. But the room, while decent in size, was underwhelming in features and comfort. There was no view to speak of, even though I was on an upper floor. The rooms seem a bit dated in their décor – old fashioned is how I would describe it. Navigating the interior of the hotel was also a challenge – you enter at the Plaza Building, meeting rooms seem to be on the Mezzanine floor as well as underground between the two buildings – just an odd layout and hard to remember your way around. On the plus side, ample parking (though expensive at $25 per day) and a great location right on the 16th Street Mall round out the somewhat memorable experiences. I do not visit downtown Denver often, so my comparators are limited, but I will try a different hotel next time though I am partial to the Starwood brands…

title: “Never again AppleCore Hotels”
text:
We were in NY for our Honeymoon. It was the last station for a three weeks trip. But unfortunatley already at our arrival was a mess. I called from the airport in Las Vegas to inform the hotel of a late arrival.
