When we finally arrived at the hotel we were transfered to another hotel down the street at 1:30a.m. There we had a smaller room which was at least clean but for the same price which was totally inadequate. Next morning we wanted to check out but first stuck in the elevator. Then we had to carry all our luggage back to the hotel @ Times Sqare. Our room was ready but smelled badly. As it was not possible to open the window we turned air condition on but that also couldn't improve the air quality. The aisle was also smelling badly like there would be untreated mold somewhere but I thought next day they will fix it. But I had to remind them two days later before something happened. Also the advises from the front desk were more bad than helpful and cost me a lot of money. The reaction from the Hotel: Sorry but we cannot do anything. You get 5% next time. There will definitely be no next time.
I can just summarize that the hotel might be cheap for NY but I strongly recommend spend a few more Dollars and take another one. This is NOT worth your money.

title: “Great Job!!!”
text: We booked a room for a special Birthday and "No Problem" was the motto! Everyone from the Concierge, Front Desk, Hospitality Staff were very cordial and accommodating. They made sure that you knew everything about the facility and made you feel like you were at home. Oh and the bed??!!! The Sleep Number Bed is fantastic... I found my number and have not had a better night's sleep in a long time! Would highly recommend this Hotel !

title: “Comfortable, Clean & Very Helpful”
text: Rooms are up to date and very clean. Hotel is under renovation but you can hardly notice. Terrific service, and you can't beat the location. Would definately bring the family.

title: “Nice rooms and presentation but hotel was understaffed had poor service”
text:
I feel like I am out on a limb on this review with all of the positive reviews on Trip Advisor but we didn't have a great stay and would not stay here again.
The lobby, in a restored bank building, is beautiful and cool but other than that we didn't find too much else to like. The studio room that we stayed in was too full of furniture and hard to move around. You had to contort your body to walk from the bed, past the tv, into the living room area. 
Worse than the cramped room was the front desk service. The night we checked in we had to wait over 15 minutes to check in due to only one employee at the front desk. This was not an isolated occurence either because the next night we noticed only one front desk employee again and a long line. 
The valet service was also poor. The hotel only offers valet parking (at $20/night) and every time we dropped off our car we had to wait several minutes for valet service. There is a only a very small and inadequate area in front of the hotel for valet dropoff. Cars would continually pile up in the area without being moved, which would eventually block the street. For $20 a night you should expect a flawless and efficient valet service. 
Finally, the poor service extended to the breakfast area. Both mornings we went down to breakfast and found most of the food gone and it being replaced at a very slow pace. Since there were no garbage cans to throw out the food and there weren't enough staff to clean the tables, food and dirty glasses would pile up on the tables, making for an unappetizing setting. 
Maybe we hit this hotel on a busy weekend and it is better during the week.

title: “Stay Here”
text:
My wife and I were in SF for 2 nights and wanted a place to stay that was central to all the typical tourist things. However, we didn't want to pay the super high prices of most downtown hotels and although there were some that I saw were cheap, they also had terrible reviews and looked dirty or run down. We reserved for $85 a night, mid-week. Our room was only about twice the square footage of the queen size bed in it, so yes, they are small. It had only a sink in the corner with the bathroom and shower rooms (shared) down the hall. This scares many of you away from staying here, but it shouldn't. The shower and bathroom, both completely tiled, were always spotless and we never had to wait to use either when we needed them. The lobby area and employees are super. The location, can't beat it. 1 block from BART and many MUNI line options including cable car.
My only complaint was that the room was a little on the warm side. The highs the days we were there were about 65 with lows dropping to about 50. We had the heater OFF. Had the window completely open for breeze the entire time (on the 7th floor) and it was still only comfortable for me to only sleep with the sheet. Ceiling fan in room helped. Not sure why it is so warm in there. I did read from other reviews that it can get hot and I would be that in summer it could be worse. Also, with window open, there is fair amount of night garbage and delivery type truck sounds coming and going down below. But we could also hear some type of building exhaust fans out below too which created a "white noise" that I like anyway.
So, if you can take a little city noise and maybe a slightly warm room, this place was awesome!

title: “Quaint. Bob & Gill Morgan. Exeter, UK.”
text:
Found by recommendation from Times newspaper in UK.
A cute, quaint hotel with friendly, helpful staff. Across the road from a wonderful shopping area with fantastic cafes, restaurants and bars, fabulously decked for Christmas. Next door to a bank and handy for the Hollywood sights.

title: “Good, Clean, comfortable, convenient”
text:
Great place to stay during a wedding weekend. When you first arrive, pay attention. Finding the hotel entrance on the busy highway can be difficult. 
Breakfast was very very good with many options! However, I found a rate with breakfast included. If I had been asked to pay $20 separately for my wife and I to eat I might not be so enthusiastic. Still though, it was a far superior offering to a comparable hotel with included breakfast, I suppose that's why it can't be offered totally free.
Bathroom is a little small for 2+ people, but I don't see that as a problem if you're there only 1-3 days.

title: “Started off not so great..but it ended well!!”
text:
So we checked into this hotel just this last week. Our two full bed room was tiny....and I mean smaller than what the photo on the website shows it as... we were missing a chair and two benches that goes at the end of the beds..because the room was that small. Anyway we were like whatever, but two hours after we checked in my sock got wet when I went into the bathroom. Carpet was soaking wet. Called and told them, someone came up and said Oh it was from previous guest ironing. Okay nice...she brought us slippers to use. Next morning I found that the carpet was even more wet and in the closet and to the first bed. We told front desk and they said to pack our stuff and they will move it later as they were full. When we came back that night our stuff was moved to another room and it was the room showed in the photo, we had two chairs and two benches at the end of the bed. It was a better sized room for 4 people and luggage. After we got into the room no problems and had a great stay!
Free wireless internet, make sure to just sign up for their little thing when you connect and its free.
Wine hour every night, awesome. Wines for free! and sparkling cider..and some food.....AND free back massages. There was a tv and a wii...a couple kids were playing some sports on it during wine hour. Thought that was cool.
Morning, you have free coffee, tea and hot chocolate, it was all good.
Jacuzzi was really nice, big too. 
Pet friendly hotel, so we got to see Oliver (dog) during wine hour..he was great.
Great place to stay!

title: “Perfect Hotel, Amazing Staff”
text: This hotel was great. We booked 2 rooms for my step daughter's sweet sixteen birthday. Upon arrival the front desk clerk wished her happy birthday and that evening a very nice chocolate dipped treat was brought to our room. The morning coffee and tea service was delicious and they even have a great wine happy hour event in the evening. Location was great. I mean what more can I say, except VIsit Chicago in the Summer time.

title: “Stayed one night, wish it was more....”
text: Had a great time in the Palace. Only stayed for one night, but will definately return again. We stayed in a Towers room, which was much bigger than we expected and extremely clean and well maintained. The staff in the hotel were excellent. Extremely friendly and polite and especially the concierge desk, who did more than most, to answer any of our questions. Only complaint is that their is no swimming pool and the sauna could do with a renovate, but besides from that, possibly the best hotel we will ever stayed in

title: “Broken thermostats in all rooms and poor house keeping!”
text:
I have stayed at the Washington Hilton a few times before The time I thought I just had a room where the a/c doesn't kick in so they gave me a new room but the other room had the same problem! Every time I have stayed here the thermostat goes up and then goes down giving you sweats and for a second you're cool throughout the night it tends to be very uncomfortable! I thought maybe it's just me.. maybe I don't know how to work it so I called for help and waited for an hour (probably bc the elevator is close to a half a mile from the room!) he came in, fiddled with it, and left not a changing a thing! It is most uncomfortable when the temperature in your room is blowing out heat when it is 81 degrees outside and all you want to do is come into a cool room. 
I didn't receive room service the first day so I also gave that the benefit of the doubt thinking that I may have left too late out of the room but the next day I didn't receive room service either so I called it in and they said they ll take care of it but when I came back to the room the room looked like just the bed was made and sloppy at that! The used coffee bag was still in the coffee machine and no toiletries were replaced in the bathroom and the towels were still wet and on the floor! the garbage was still on the table! This is not my idea of staying at a "Hilton" hotel! What happened to comfort and luxury? I'm really surprised that the company is not on top of this and I just warn you that you will deal with this if you stay here! Its definitely annoying!
What an awful experience!

title: “Just What We Needed”
text: I headed down to Memphis for Elvis's 35th Death Anniversary and wanted to participate in the candlelight vigil. The price was excellent for our stay! We were able to check in early and Jessica (front desk staff) was very nice, she gave us a goody bag that head some Elvis stuff in it for free! It's not far from downtown Memphis and is near the Wolfchase Galleria Mall and is also easy to get on/off the Interstate. The rooms were clean, spacious and just what we needed! Overall a great stay, we missed the breakfast b/c we slept in, but if I travel to Memphis, I'd stay here again!

title: “A funky hotel in the heart of South Congress wildlife”
text:
This is a classic motel, very retro and very hip. The rooms are typically sized and comfortable with basic amenities. 
The staff is very friendly and accommodating, and the lobby provides coffee and tea in the mornings.
There is a lovely pool so bring your suit. The attached restaurant, Snack Bar, is excellent for food and drink, and they will even deliver to your room! Jo's is excellent for coffee and snacks next door.

title: “Lobby is gorgeous but rooms are cheap...”
text: Lobby is gorgeous but rooms are cheap. Our room was just "okay". There was hair on our bed, burn marks in our sheets, and the room just felt very cheap. The only reason we went with this hotel was because of an Internet deal. I would not recommend this hotel. The front desk guys were not very friendly or kind and the parking is too expensive.

title: “Would have been mad if I'd been the one paying”
text:
My husband attended a huge conference at the Fairmont, and I tagged along for a mini vacation. The hotel is beautiful. And there is nothing in San Francisco that matches the lovely flags lining the front of the hotel.
Other pros: Good cafe in the basement for breakfast. Tonga Room is fun for drinks and appetizers.
Cons: Location isn't great if you're interested in exploring the city; doors in the main building are REALLY loud when they close, so avoid it if you're a light sleeper; but the real problem is this hotel's service: it's is poor, particularly given the Fairmont reputation and price. 
1) My husband joined the President's Club to take advantage of free internet service in the rooms. Personally, I don't think a hotel of this quality should be charging $14/day for the internet. But my husband had trouble accessing it (probably because he was new to the President's Club). When we checked out, instead of taking his PC number and taking the charges off the bill, the woman at the front desk spent 15 minutes telling him that he didn't log in correctly. Finally, she took the charges off.
2) Upon check out, we called the bell desk for help with our bags. We weren't leaving San Francisco until that evening, so we wanted to store them at the hotel. The bellman told me that we could just leave them in the room... he would be right up to get them. Guess what? When we returned that evening, the bellman on duty (not the one from the morning) couldn't find them. Turns out that they were sitting in our vacated room ALL DAY. And to add insult to injury, the bellman took my husband over to the front desk and explained that we had never checked out properly or this wouldn't have happened. Since we spent 15 minutes with the first rude front desk person to get a new receipt, we pointed out how that was incorrect. And again, instead of just apologizing, the bellman and the front desk employee went on and on about how we shouldn't have left without a claim ticket. 
Certainly not superior (and in my mind, not even acceptable) service for a top tier hotel. Thank goodness my husband's employer was paying for the room.

title: “Great hospitality but the rooms lack space”
text: The staff is very helpful and welcoming. The rooms are just ok, but small. The bathroom is extremely small with no counter space. Overall a great location. I got a great rate online by booking early, so I was ok with the room. However the full rate is a little high for the amenities.

title: “Comfortable, convenient and with those signature Kimpton wine tastings.”
text: Very friendly staff, comfortable lobby, complimentary yoga bags, good location near art museum and Pike's Place Market.

title: “For train fans”
text:
Stayed for business trip and was placed in room away from active train station.
Quiet room and perfectly fine for work and relaxation.

title: “Finally someplace I dont mind staying in ELP.”
text:
I come to El Paso about once every six weeks on business, and given the high hotel costs here, I am usually very dissatisfied with hotel quality here. Well, finally, I found a clean, quiet, reasonably priced hotel near acceptable dining options. 
The exterior of the hotel is cookie cutter Holiday Inn Express. The inside of the hotel clean and nice looking with a nice lobby with two large TV's and a roomy breakfast area. The breakfast is typical Holiday Inn Express- Continental, plus eggs, biscuts, an a meat item. 
My room was a nice two queen bedded room with a large widescreen HDTV. Rooms are spacious and very clean. One tip - if you get frustrated because you can not find the TV remote - they put it in the dresser drawer where you put your clothes. I could not find it for quite a while. (I rarely use the drawers on business trips.) Also they dont deliver newspapers to the room, but have them available downstairs. 
They small business center downstairs with two computers, and two printers. (One computer did not work during my stay) High Speed Internet connection was available wired or wifi. 
They have an indoor pool and hot tub of typical size for a Holiday Inn Express. They also have a workout room with elliptical, treadmills, bike, etc. The basics but clean. 
There are plenty of dining options (mostly chains) in nearby driving distance, (you could also easily walk) along with some shopping options. The entire area seems to be relatively newly built up. 
I will continue to stay here when the need arises to be in the area. Front desk staff was plesant and they had cookies out each evening.

title: “Good Hotel, Nice Area, Close to LA tourist sites”
text:
Nice hotel in the LA suburb of Woodland Hills in the San Fernando Valley. Stayed 3 night here for my LA visit and the hotel was pleasant. Room was fairly nice and the bed was very comfortable! The hotel is about 20 minutes from Universal Studios, 25 from Hollywood and about 40 from Disneyland. Not too bad as far as location to the major tourist sites of the LA area. 
The immediate area around the hotel was upscale and several very nice restaurants nearby including Ruth’s Chris steakhouse (great steaks!), Cheesecake factory (right next door) and a PF Chang’s . Overall, it was a nice hotel in a nice location. Yeah, I would recommend staying here.

title: “STAY AWAY, NOT KIDDING”
text:
I am in the hotel as I speak, and spend my time on writing a review BECAUSE I have never been more disappointed with a hotel, let alone a Starwood property. 
I travel 4 days a week for work, and think I have a pretty good grasp on the hotel scene in the US and can provide an objective comparison.
This property, supposedly fresh off a renovation, looks like a sad, dingy, rundown place. Issues I have ran into during only 24 hours of being here:
- Room key card machine broke down for about an hour. Unable to check in to room or go to the gym, had to have a guy escort me around with a master key
- First room I got was next to the elevator banks. Huge bangs heard every 10min, had to ask them to switch my rooms, which I do say is a plus, they handled well and I got a room further from the elevators
- This property of 21 or so floors has 4 very old and scary elevators. Don't be surprised that the average wait can easily be 10-15min to just get out of the building. Oh, and this morning 3 of the 4 elevators WERE OUT OF SERVICE, you can imagine the chaos it caused, and how fun it is to walk up and down to the 11th floor
- No ironing board, no iron, no hairdrier, no luggage rack, no coat hanger of any sort in the room.... They must have done furnishing in a hurry...
- Toilet overflow - The toilet appears to flush, and then 2min later everything that you thought you flushed down, appears again. Then if you are lucky, 3 or so flushes later, the stuff finally goes down...
- Dirty (dark brown on the bottom) bathtub with lot of leftover hair hanging out in it, nasty; makes me question how clean is the rest of the room
- Ordered one salad entree through room service, got a completly different salad entree. Ate it without complaint, but how hard is it to get one order right?
I am glad I am checking out in 10 hours from this nightmare, before anything else breaks or goes wrong.
It's especially unfortunate because Starwood typically has excellent properties associated with its name, I highly suggest they revisit their choice. Travelers - save your money, if you are in the area go to the Aloft; nice, clean, and organized property.

title: “Nice Hotel. Fantastic Location”
text: Stayed here before the rock n roll half marathon and it was extremely convenient. You can walk everywhere: convenient store, restaurants, parks, convention center, etc. The rooms are HUGE, but if you're looking for luxury...this is not it. Again, it's a good place to crash for a quick stay, very roomy, comfy beds, convenient to everything, and fairly clean. I didn't rent a car because the airport shuttle is only $10 and I didn't need one for my short stay, but friends drove in town to support me during the race and parking is expensive like most major cities. There is parking in the building behind the hotel which was fairly cheap at $11 for 24 hours so they parked there.

title: “Great Hotel with Some Drawbacks”
text:
As a DC area resident, I'm a fan of the Kimpton properties. The Solomar has some great pros and a few cons, which may be significant to you.
Pros: Perhaps the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in - soft, but supportive; The decor (in the room and hotel) is very modern; An amazing number of electrical outlets, which is such a pleasure (usually I have to crawl under desks or unplug lamps); The windows actually open to get fresh air!!!!!!; Lots of mirrors; The location is great - just a block from the Gaslight District, and a few blocks from the Convention Center; The pool has a very cool vibe, and you can borrow towels to take to the beach; A VERY friendly and helpful staff.
Cons: The modern bathroom sink has a high faucet and shallow sink, which means that water will ALWAYS splash on you/your clothes; The sink counter is simply too high for shorter people (I am 5'3") so it's very hard to use; The room had a musty smell; There is no coffee maker in the room - only in the lobby - so if you need coffee before you face people for the day, you're out of luck; The room could really use more lights; No dresser (but large closet); Not enough staff at the pool bar/restaurant so you have to wait a long time to get served.

title: “Service Excellence”
text:
My husband and I recently stay at Magic Castle on our honeymoon. It was by far the best hotel experience either of us have ever had. The hotel isn't brand new so the rooms were a little old, but always very clean and well maintained. The customer service at this hotel is second to none, and all the little extras like the free snacks just added to our experience (even if you don't eat them it's nice to know they're there!)
The location is also very good, very close to Hollywood Blvd. Being able to go to the Magic Castle Club was also pretty cool - it was an experience!

title: “Weird hotel/hostel hybrid”
text:
Spent a week here in February. Booked a hostel room as it appeared to be best value for the location. Two blocks to the subway was excellent, and felt like a safe area. 
The hostel itself was interesting, the front area is nice, with hotel vibe but head up the stairs and turns in to a sterile environment. I found the common area a bit small and really loud. It was the only place I could get wifi too. One fridge was available for all guests and the kitchen area was tiny, I wouldn't recommend for the traveller who likes to self cater. I also found it hard to meet new people here, there was a very mixed demographic of guests. Young familys, a group of high school kids, older businessman and standard backpackers. 
Room was pretty standard for a hostel, mine smelt like wet dog however despite seeing cleaners everyday. A two person room travelling solo is quite awkward, especially when you have a male bunker. Maybe it was just my luck, but I would have been a lot more comfortable with a female roommate. A table and chair or some hooks to hang coats on wouldn't be astray here either. 
I was a little concerned with the Warning sign on the front door too- Looked like some type of official notification. Everytime I went to read it, the doorman opened the door so I couldn't however.
Overall, I would be indifferent about staying here again.

title: “Clean and great location”
text: Pleasantly surprised with this property. The price was great and we didn't even have the cheapest room. With taxes the total was $102. For a Saturday night! It is in the Financial district so pretty dead on the weekends. We accidentally parked in the wrong garage and it was $7.00 for overnight! It closed at 11 and didn't open until 9am but we didn't need the car so it was great. The pub adjoining the hotel was nice for breakfast. I read the review about needing an ironing board and all that kind of stuff is in a closet for guests at the end of the halls. Extra pillows,cases,shampoo etc. And right next to that is FREE water bottles and purified water. The next time we go to a giants game we are definitely staying here.the only downside is that the walls are thin and our neighbors had a crying infant.

title: “Clean and green”
text: Best location, excellent service, clean rooms, great oatmeal!

title: “Brilliant....Loved It”
text:
We stayed at the Beverly Garland on the second destination of our tour and it was brilliant. set just outside of universal city, the hotel takes you up to universal studios free where you can catch the metro to pretty much everywhere. You can even walk to the metro as it is only a few minutes away.
the room itself was good, decent sized, great view of the hollywood hills and free wireless internet. the hotel breakfast was not so great though. 
overall, enjoyed the stay and would recommend to any young travellers on a budget... it doesnt get better then this.

title: “Great stay!”
text: We just returned from a 3 night stay at Sofitel. We were very pleased! The room was very spacious for New York and the bathroom was fabulous. As other reviewers had mentioned, the room was very quiet, so we slept very well. The staff was very helpful and polite. The location was perfect and only a short walk to all the major attractions. We would certainly stay at Sofitel again!

title: “Good Location”
text:
I stayed here with my wife and 2 kids this past week.The room was cramped for 4 people but we managed,given the short periods we spent in there.The staff were pleasant enough,not excessively rude or overly friendly.As the other reviewers have said,the hotel is in an excellent location but I was expecting a little more for $180 dollars a night. Would recommend for location but I'll be trying elsewhere the next time I visit Manhattan. 
PS
Ask for an upper floor room,we were on the 6th floor the first night and never got any sleep because of the noise the cooling fans make outside.I asked to be moved and we were given a room on the 21st floor which was better.

title: “Great Hotel and Great Staff”
text:
Stayed at OTA for seven nights - on the recommendation of a friend who has stayed here many times. On previous trips we had stayed in the Times Square area and we were not disappointed with this Upper West Side location. It was a pleasure to return to the hotel at the end of the day and get away from the crowds and traffic. The hotel is located in a great neighborhood with many restaurants and shops; is a short walk to the subway, to Central Park, and some of the other "must see" locations. What could be better! Our rooms were very comfortable, nicely appointed and clean. The front desk staff and concierge desk was most helpful with any of our questions - after a couple of days we felt like family! Management was excellent in providing information about the hurricane and on the Saturday night (Aug. 27th) maintenance, security and housekeeping staff stayed in the hotel . . . we felt pretty confident that however severe the storm, we would be safe. The General Manager mingled with guests throughout Saturday and was most reassuring. A special hello to her, and to Anna R., Joe and Danny from your Canadian friends! We will be back!
What would we avoid next time? The airport shuttle service which we had booked on line. Our flight to NYC? Four hours and 3 minutes. Airport to OTA time? Four hours and 10 minutes . . . . for our return to Newark, the hotel arranged our transportation and it was a pleasant trip!

title: “Always stay here, great location”
text: Our family of four visits San Jose frequently and we always stay at the Fairmont. We get a suite and although it is usually reasonably priced (@180/nt), this time it was double but they did give us some vouchers. I like the extra space for our 4 and 6 yr old to play and they have their own t.v. The hotel always brings up two rollaways (which when we ask them not to charge, they don't)for the kids to sleep. The bathrooms are nice and housekeeping always does a great job cleaning. The real upside to this hotel is the location. There are cafes, restaurants, bars and a park NEXT to and all around the hotel. This weekend I took the kids across the street and just let them run around the large grassy park(there is no playground) and in the Summer they have large water fountains for them to run in (all literally across the street). The pool is also great with food/bar service. There are also museums, including the children's museum close by. I also use the gym which is great with , machines, 6 treadmills and a locker room. The hotel has a large bar area that plays sports on large t.v.s during the day and has great bands with dancing at night. It is family friendly, in that, there are kids hanging with their parents, dancing along. I don't give it a five because I have stayed at "5"s and they have something that gives it a wow factor, beyond expectations. The fairmount always meets my expectations.

title: “Poor Front Desk Service”
text: When we arrived at the front deak after 8 hours of driving we were told that our room was ready but that they had no roll-aways left. I had reserved the room with a roll-away bed. Lucky for me I had a copy of my e-mail confirmation. When I inquired as to what I should do with my daughter they said that she could sleep on the floor. I was, to say the least, flabergasted. Eventually, they agve us another room (not ajoining). After that front desk staff was sullen towards us and in fact down right rude. Breakfasts were poor. I would not stay here againg nor would I reccommend it to anyone.

title: “Excellent hotel in great location!”
text: We stayed here for three nights before our Alaskan cruise. The room was large and clean and very quiet. Recommend the bay view, was outstanding! The location is excellent, can walk just about anywhere, markets, piers, shopping. The staff was excellent and attentive but not overbearing. The infiniti pool with fireplace wasbeautiful place to relax. This hotel had a lot of little complimentary touches that added to the overall stay. The restaurant was excellent for food and service! Our only negatives were two: our bed size, had to book room with two doubles and when you are used to a King, it's very small, might book the King with two rollaways next time but beds were very comfortable. Second, the internet fee was per device! We all had iPads so it added up quick! Overall, stay was wonderful and can't wait to return!

title: “Meh”
text:
The W Hotel chain markets itself like it's cool like no other, understands the latest trends, and provides this luxurious stay. The expectations are high because it's not cheap. The two chatty doormen didn't come help get my stuff out of the cab and I opened the door for myself. Later in my stay I would see a staff door marked, "talent" and it seemed rather...
Supposedly, you can call the "wherever whenever" desk and you'll get immediate help. I arrived late at night and wanted to get a healthy meal. A request for a sushi restaurant that delivered totally confused people. I held on the phone while they Googled on the other end for twenty minutes. Finally, I was connected to a takeout hotline where not a soul answered. I rang back. Other hotels in the heart of a busy city can make some healthy food happen. They have a steakhouse which is overkill. I know now Old Ebbit (next door) stays open very late but I found that out later by myself. 
 I moved on to the W's roomservice which is just bad. I'm not a picky eater but I tried to get some fresh veggies to no avail. Penne pasta and a salad swimming in blue cheese dressing layered in bacon came to $50. The magic hotline can not book spa appointments or arrange transportation after hours. Everything felt like chatting with a magic 8 ball: "Ask again later."
For the price the room should come with a bathtub. The bathroom decor is going for the sleek look but mostly it's just weird with a steel ladder in the middle of it. The bedroom area has weird red lights that make it look live the devil's suite. Those went off first thing and stayed off. 
Going to print something out required $5 for ten minutes. Upon entering the room someone had written on the notepad on the desk, "don't blow 300 dollars!' I am not making that up and I regret not taking a photo. $9 for a Fiji water? Please. I'll spend the extra money if I feel like I'm getting the quality experience I imagined.

title: “Amazing Waffles!”
text: Stumbling out of bed and wondering into the community breakfast area where other travelers are already gathered I expected to see everyone being just as groggy and somewhat grouchy as me. That wasn't to be the case. The atmosphere was almost electrified as if by some unknown force. That unknown quantity I discovered was the young man who was diligently making waffles for everyone. His name is Michael and he is honestly a delight! Helpful, full of conversation, energy and with a magnetic personality that electrified the entire room. It was impossible to be groggy and grouchy. Thank you Travelodge for having the wisdom to employ an individual such as Michael. If you are a traveler and happen to stay the night at the Travelodge Seattle University, do yourself a great favor and stop in in the morning and have the sun rise as Michael's personality and waffles make your day a delight.

title: “Better than average convention hotel”
text:
This is a new, high-rise downtown convention hotel. The rooms are well furnished and comfortable. They could use a bit more storage. The fitness center and pool area are excellent. There is a nice internet cafe in the lobby. Service staff were friendly and capable. My only complaint was that when we pulled in to the arrival area, we were told that the attendant did not think there was any self-park space available, so we had to use the valet service. That proved not to be the case, so we were out a few dollars each day.
The restaurant looked good. The location is right in the middle of the arts and sports section of the city. It is across from the Arizona Center which has lots of restaurants. 
The concierge service was helpful and friendly.

title: “Perfect Ending”
text:
We took the kids on their first trip to Disneyland and Universal Studios. To save money we chose a standard room for the Disney part of the vacation. But I opted for a Kid's Suite for our stay at the Beverly Garland and I am so glad that I did. 
Our room was spacious and well appointed. The kid's bunk worked out great. They were able to watch TV from the bunks while we enjoyed a show in our area. Since this was the last night of our vacation I figured we would sleep better with the kids in bunks and we did. I slept like baby. They had some kind of memory topper on the mattress and it was sooo comfy. I passed out in record time and slept through the night. This was the only good night sleep that I got that week and it made the drive home the next day that much easier. Also, checkout was at noon so we were able to relax and take our time to get on the road.
If I am ever in the Hollywood area, I will definitely stay at the Beverly Garland Holiday Inn.

title: “Good solid Accomodation”
text:
The Salisbury is a good, comfortable, solid, and reasonably priced hotel, in a central location. It is near a subway station, and times square is a ten minute walk. Central Park and the Time Warner building are literally around the corner.
It was perfect for my partner and I as first time visitors to New York.
The rooms were large and airy, the staff friendly and helpful, and the breakfast good value and filling.
If you are stuck up, or too used to the Ritz, this isn't for you, but anyone else cannot go wrong here.
When we go back to New York, which we plan to do soon, we will be going back to the Salisbury.

title: “Downgrade instead of upgrade”
text:
So I am only a Gold Starwood since I switched to Hilton as my main hotel of choice.
This property is nice but for you out of shape people don't get put into the Lani section of the hotel unless you drive your car over to that wing.i don't have a car and from the lobby I could not believe the distance for my room.easiest way to know if you are being thrown into the labyrinth is the desk clerk pulling out a map that resembles the outcry of Italy.
As a gold member you no longer get club access which to me 8 out of 10 times the apps are fried items.they now expect 25.00 for use of this club room.no free movie as an option either only wifi which used to be free.
Anyway other then my lack of amenities the hotel is ok but overpriced for the brand
Good thing: View of the marina and updated with the latest Sheraton features
Bad thing: Baton Death march to your room.

title: “Extremely Dissappointed”
text:
Although a beautiful hotel, I can not give the Mandarin Oriental Hotel a favorable review. After watching the fireworks show, and walking around the city, my sister and I accompanied, a few friends back to the hotel. We were staying at the Swissotel and after hearing them boast about how beautiful their hotel was, we decided to go see it for ourselves. 
 When we arrived there was no doorman to greet us at the door, he was actually at the front desk chatting with the front desk clerk. When we passed them they stared at us blankly, and then asked us if they could help us. The whole exchange was quite cold, not at all what I expected from a 5-star hotel. 
 The tip of the iceberg was when we were on our way out. We left through the mall exit, after searching for an ATM machine, and returned to the front desk so that my sister and I could get a cab to return home. It was 4:30 in the morning and pouring rain outside, yet once again we had to open the doors ourselves. Now I’m not sure if it was the fact that we were young or Black, or a combination of the two but the same doorman and front desk clerk we had not passed but a half hour before, asked us if we were guests at the hotel. My friend replied that yes we were indeed guests. Incredulous, I asked the front guest clerk why the doorman asked this question when then they both saw us come in. To this she replied, “Well, we saw you go in, but did not see you go out.” 
 Stunned we went outside to wait for the doorman to hail us a taxi. While waiting, we observed the doorman who had previously neglected to open the front door for us, open it for a different group of guests at the hotel. The final insult came when after trying to hail a taxi for my sister and I for about 5 minutes, the doorman pointed us towards the umbrellas and told us we were better off standing on the corner and hailing the taxi from there. My brief visit to the hotel was terrible, and I would not under any circumstances visit there again.

title: “Nothing special, but ok”
text: This was my second stay, which means the hotel is overall quite good. It is nearby the highway, so very good for travellers. The area around the hotel is not very nice, but there is a gas station nearby, what is also good for travellers. The hotel has a washing room and the breakfast is quite good for typical American standard. The rooms are small but nice and clean, the bathrooms are refurbished. The pool area needs to be renewed. The service is good, the price low. Overall a good deal for one-night stay travellers.

title: “Troy is the best manager ever.”
text: Troy is the manager of this wonderful hotel. He goes way above and beyond to service his guests. He is a one in a million person! You will not be disappointed when staying here.

title: “comfortable rooms but i did not like location”
text: A new hotel with very nicely appointed suites, good hot breakfast included in price, rooms modern design and I like having little kitchenette when i travel. all very modern and new. BUT the location!! Excellent to walk up into the Hells kitchen area which we did, and ate in a great french restaruant called Marseille. But to walk in the other direction it is a bit sleezy. For all the places to stay in New york I would not stay again in this location.

title: “Small, attentive, and perfectly located”
text: I stayed here for two nights over the holidays and was very pleased. The room was immaculately clean, particularly the bathroom. My room had a fireplace in it, which came in very handy because the weather was frigid - less than 10 degrees F. I did not spend much time in the hotel but the amenities were much appreciated - good toiletries from Fresh, a hotel car that took me to the airport, a newspaper delivered in the morning, and speedy room service.

title: “The Best In SanDiego”
text:
From check in to check out we had great service. The staff always had a smile-all of the staff. Front desk answered all questions, got us where we wanted to go without one problem. By mistake we left expensive jewelry out in the bathroom one day, not touched, trusted the maid like no other we have experienced. 
 Beautiful room, Great view. Only problem was the weather, but we're not willing to blame the hotel. 
 This is the only place we'll ever stay in SanDiego! Exceptional! Thank You Pacific Terrace.....

title: “Poor level of service, staff underwhelming”
text:
I checked into the Dream Downtown yesterday upon the recommendation of two friends. I actually moved out of my other hotel (The Trump for this week) to try this place out for two nights. I was told the roof is a great place to hang out at night and that I would have a great experience there.
From the second I arrived, I was severely disappointed. I checked in and asked if any other rooms were available (my travel department booked for me) as I wanted to upgrade, even if for a fee. I was told no, the hotel is sold out for two nights. Fine, I accepted that and was given a bronze king room on the 5th floor with a balcony.
I jumped on my computer to just take a look at the website and decided to check the reservations log and saw a NUMBER of rooms available still. I am flabbergasted as to how a front desk employee lied to me with such a straight face.
Furthermore, I was given NO instructions or welcome upon entering the hotel. At a hotel that is supposedly middle to high end, one expects a certain level of service and accommodation, which was nowhere to be found - and on a Wednesday, when they weren't busy! I was not told how anything in the room works - e.g., the light controls, phones - nor was I told basic information such as where the gym is (I ended up wandering to the 3rd floor, as was stated in the guest services book, only to find no gym. Upon calling the front desk, I was informed it was actually in the north tower of the hotel, so I had to walk down, find the north tower elevators, and then go up.). Again, that's honestly ridiculous. The Holiday Inn tells their guests where things in the hotels are upon checking in. The guy at the front desk seemed like he was trying to get rid of me. I actually didn't know how to react considering that a real 4+ star hotel walks you through all of the hotel's offerings to make your stay easier. 
And, to top it all off, my luggage was brought in by the doorman, however, he left in the middle of the lobby, where, after checking in, I just grabbed it. It was COMPLETELY unsecured, anyone could have walked away with it as he just dropped it off and vanished after saying so and so would be taking care of it. This is actually unbelievable and should be a real concern for travelers.
On another note, with regards to the rooftop - it states that only until 9:30pm are guests guaranteed access. Fair, I can understand that. However, a private party was taking place till 11pm. One would imagine, then, that the hotel would reorganize the timeline to allow hotel guests access for a period of time after the private party ended. This, of course, was not the case and instead it was a HUGE hassle to get upstairs just to enjoy the view. The FORCE a charge of $175 onto one's credit card and then, without warning, add a 20% gratuity "for your convenience" - ludicrous considering the level of service.
In sum, I believe this place is a nightclub that happens to have rooms. Therefore, the behavior of the staff is also that of a nightclub, and most certainly not that of a real, highly rated hotel. They also place a preference on patrons of the club over guests (which, economically, makes NO sense) - e.g., every member of the staff I interacted with happened to be male - those same staff members were bending over backwards for every girl that walked in wearing high heels. It's almost comical.
As a 20-something guy in town on business, look elsewhere to have a good stay and enjoyable night in NYC. It is by FAR the worst hotel I've stayed at in NYC (probably anywhere), and I would recommend avoiding it unless you like being lied to, mistreated, and conned out of money. I look forward to checking out bright and early tomorrow.

title: “Nice Rooms but No Hotel Amenities”
text: I would not recommend this hotel for a family with teenage or young children. For a relatively newly constructed hotel, we were disappointed in the overall cleanliness. While the staff was friendly and helpful, the upkeep of the hotel is lacking. The indoor pool area is the smallest we've seen (maximum pool capacity was posted as 7 people, and that would be very crowded). The water was too cold to swim in and the pool area and pool itself were very unclean. Additionally, the elevators were not vacuumed/clean. Our room was large, the beds were comfortable, and it was clean but showing some wear and tear. The biggest disappointment was the hotel location. There is a run-down Waffle House restaurant adjacent to the hotel and nothing else. The desk clerk gave us a list of nearby restaurants (all about a 10-15 minute drive away along IH 35). This hotel is only really suited for the business traveler who wants close access to the airport. The breakfast buffet ($9.95/person) was very well prepared and the dining area is very nice. Overall, a big disappointment for a Marriott Courtyard hotel.

title: “Fabulous!!!”
text: Very helpfull,friendly and professionel employees. Location is perfect for a first impression of the city. Clean and spacious room. Good price/value for a city like this. Lot of possibilities for breakfast,lunch and diner at walking distance.

title: “A little gem in the big apple”
text:
This little hotel is one that stands huge on quality,service, and everything else that a visitor to New York would need.
A wondeful breakfast buffet, included in price, along with a wine and cheese reception every day.. it was fantastic.
As for the staff all I can say is that eveyone of them were excellent an they went out of their way to be helpful.
We will definately visit again.
Cheers
Joey and Sinead McLoughlin
Ireland

title: “Classy and comfortable”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights for a conference we were attending in Philadelphia.
We were immediately impressed with how classy the hotel looked when we walked inside. Check-in was fairly straightforward, however there just happened to be another guest with the same name staying there also which was easy enough to straighten out once the guy on the desk actually checked my booking reference. 
We had a King Room on the 4th floor. It was lovely. It had a very comfortable king bed, desk, large tv, fridge, coffee making machine, free wifi, and lovely clean bathroom with big shower. There were also robes in the cupboard and an iPad which allowed you to access the guest services. We tried ordering room service on the iPad but it didn't work and we ended up going out anyway.
We had breakfast 2 mornings in the restaurant which had a lovely buffet and also a chef who was able to prepare eggs however you wanted them. Lots of fruit was available including a big tray of bananas (fantastic for us Aussie's who haven't had bananas in months), cereals, bagels, cakes, muffins, bacon and eggs, french toast, yoghurt etc. 
Our only criticism of this hotel is that it was a little away from the main part of Philly, we did have a free shuttle to the conference each day which made things easy for us. Also, other than the restaurants in the hotel, there wasn't many dining choices within walking distance of the hotel.
All the staff we encountered during our stay were very polite and helpful. We would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a comfortable stay in Philadelphia.

title: “Lovely hotel, great location”
text: A lovely friendly hotel in a good location, a great base for exploring a wonderful city. Rooms were very clean and big, we stayed in a four person room and there were two huge double beds. Would recommend!

title: “Great!”
text: One of the nicest hotels that we've ever stayed at! The rooms were large and the beds were comfortable. The rooms had a small fridge and microwave in the living room part of the suite. The location was easy to find, thanks to my garmin! The hotel is in the right place to hit many restuarants and bars, I really liked the location, especially for the trolleys because they stop across the street which was really handy! The managers reception and breakfast was great and the employees were extremely helpful and friendly. I would say that I found it weird that my husband and I, who are deep sleepers were awakened by the toilets flushing in the rooms above ours. I would not dare stay anywhere else, this place is great and I would stay here again in a heartbeat!!!

title: “Nice property but not super special”
text: This hotel is very nice and in a great location, but I'm not sure its 4 stars. The rooms are very standard. I would give is a 3.5, but that wasn't an option

title: “Total taken care of...”
text: My wife and I had an outstanding experience during our stay at this W hotel. I travel a lot and have stayed at numerous W hotels. You can expect the same high level of comfort and service here and then some. This place is obviously well managed as the staff are spot on with all of their mad service skills and attention to details. They also know how to engage you in a way that makes you feel comfortable and "at home" or like one of the many celebrities they must pamper. Kudos out to Cassie and Marci as some of the best servers and hosts.

title: “Average”
text:
We arrived on the 24th of may, and first impressions were average. Nothing really stood out.
As it was bank holiday in America, the hotel was packed full of people, and out rooms had to be moved, so they upgraded us to 'Palacio del Este' which was abesolutely georgous. 
The service is outstanding, but the hotel in general was poor. The River Ranch was full and there were a school full of kids going there on a trip, which i found abesolutely outrageous as its a hotel not a theme park!
I would reccomend going to eat at 'Gallahers' opposite the hotel, which is a sports bar. The Fasion square mall and Chandler mall are also great.

title: “Meh.”
text: Well, we waited too long and all the rooms at the Hilton were booked so we settled for the Millenium. Rooms are average size for a Manhattan Hotel (small.) Beds are very hard. Pillows are hard. Even the chair is hard. No frills here. No coffee in room. Upside is that it is clean and the staff is pleasant enough. Decent location if you want to be in the heart of Midtown and close to Times Square. Decent value for the rates we got but not a luxury hotel by any means.

title: “Excellent hotel, great location, friendly staff”
text: I have been to NY many times and have stayed in many hotels. This is the best hotel I've stayed in yet. It was a reasonable price with a clean, adequate sized room. It is in an excellent location - walking distance from Penn Station and Times Square. It was QUIET! This is the first hotel I've stayed in where it was so soundproof, you aren't kept up all night from honking and police cars. And the staff was very friendly. I highly recommend it!

title: “OK for a Pricelined room. Not what I would expect from Marriott, though”
text:
We stayed here one night using a group Priceline rate. For the rate we got, I was ok with the room, but would not pay a regular price.
When I checked in and got to our room, it smelled horrible as if someone had just lit up a big stinking cigar an hour ago. Also there was a bathing suit hanging on the bathroom door and hair clips on the chair--a sign of sloppy housekeeping. I do give credit to the friendly front desk for immediately giving me another room and offering vouchers for their snack store. But I still think it's unacceptable for a Marriott property to have a room that smells that strongly of smoke in a non-smoking hotel. 
The hotel is dark and dreary. The halls are dimly lit and smell of mold and oldness. It's kind of depressing, really.
The new room was better. Beds were comfortable. A/C worked fine. Cleanliness was ok. There were no issues with noise. 
The pool area was small and the water a little cloudy and dirty. 
Basically this facility just needs a good remodel and some attention.

title: “Minimalist for sure!”
text: Very old and dirty. Room carpet dirty. Sink in bedroom old, right side spigot stripped, soap dish rusty. When bedroom window open for ventilation could hear person in next room snorring! Bathroom down hall dirty. No place to leave used towels (which you had to bring from your room), when I left used towel in bathroom it was still there next day, along with used soap bars from other people etc. I would not stay in this hotel again.

title: “Still Beautiful Even Though Same for Years”
text: Spectacular Atrium , looking the same for over 15 years, still does not disappoint. 2 Room suites are always a plus. Nice glass elevators to get you to the rooms. Breakfast included in room rate is exceptional. Indoor pool and nice exercise room . You will be hard to find a more beautiful hotel off of I95 in Florida.

title: “Comfortable, good service and adequate without being particularly special”
text:
I stayed at the Nikko for a week whilst in SF with work.
First of all on check-in the staff were really helpful, as I had 2 colleagues who were going to be delayed but needed their rooms secured. This was sorted with no problems and I got checked-in very quickly.
In my room I was dissapointed there was no mini-bar as had been advertised, but the room was pleasant enough, although dominated by the large bed, which itself was dominated by the huge amount of cushions. In fact, if there was an emergency you could strap them all to your body and jump out the window and have a pretty comfortable landing. I stuck most of them in a corner but the maid insisted on putting them back on the bed each day.
As work paid I am less price sensitive and did order room service, where the menu prices weren't bad but the service charges make it very expensive. The food was good though and well presented.
Internet was I believe $13 extra each day, which is not bad by some hotel standards but some may find too pricey.
The room was clean and the en-suite perfectly acceptable.
On several nights I hit the hotel bar for a glass of wine or two - the bar in the restaurant has the much better wine and on one afternoon when I popped in for a coke as I was thirsty they gave it to me free - and I also got a few glasses of wine free over my stay.
All the staff I encountered were really helpful.
It is reasonably well-located - with Union Square and much else walking distance (for an englishman - Americans will probably want to take a cab), although you should be careful as not far from the hotel (in the opposite direction from heading towards the square) there are some dodgy looking neighbourhoods with lots of liquor stores, etc.
I'd stay here again, but would probably be tempted to try one a little higher up the rankings on this site. The ratings that give it 1 star though are way off the mark. I try to be fair with all my ratings, although my failing is that as it's often with work I don't pay enough attention to the costs.
That said I did have breakfast in the diners around the hotel - the one which was more modern and not on a corner was the best - and saved about $15 each day by doing so.

title: “Our New Boston Favorite”
text: Loved it. Great location, superb service, very comfortable beds, and lots of eye candy at the front door.

title: “Great Stay!!”
text: We stayed one night at the Mayflower on Connecticut Ave, Thursday August 31,2006.. The staff, from the doorman, valet, front desk, housekeeping, concierge, etc.......were just great! Smiling, helpful and polite. They seem to truly enjoy their jobs! Our room was spotless and the bed was quite comfortable. My one and only very small complaint, is the location of the television in relation to the bed! Nice room set up, but almost impossible to watch TV while in bed. I have to say that we stay at Marriott properties quite often. We chose the Mayflower because of a promotion promising additional Marriott Reward points. We usually stay at the JW Marriott on Pennsylvania Ave, it is a bit closer to the White House and Mall. But the Mayflower location has so much more to offer in the neigborhood. Lots of cool shopping and restaurants! We will stay here again!

title: “Gem of a hotel”
text: We got a discounted price and upgrade on this property which made it a bargan for its location right in the heart of the theatre district. The bistro Saju next door is a great place to dine especially for the great breakfastes which were part of the upgrade. The freebie cocktails the first night was a nice treat too. The rooms are really small but fairly typical of NYC rooms so I would really recommend paying extra for the larger room. But even with this upgrade the bath is really small with no surface area to put clothes except on the toilet seat and there were no AC outlets in the bath. Room was nice and fresh and comfortable and there was good lighting for reading (a feature that is getting hard to find these days). Bed was very comfortable. Walked across the street to our musical one night and around the corner the next night. Will certainly check out them out the next time we are in town.

title: “Great stay, as expected”
text:
Very nice stay, exactly as we expected from reading previous reviews, and from Hilton Garden Inn brand name. We appreciated the quiet atmosphere, which apparently isn't an accident (all guests are asked upon check-in to sign an agreement to observe quiet hours or risk being kicked out). Comfy bedding. Cookies on arrival, free internet access worked easily. There wasn't any outdoor storage rack for our bikes, but the front desk staff said it was fine to bring them in the room. The only negative was that, unlike Hampton Inn, the breakfast buffet isn't free, it's over $10 per person.
Great Location: We took advantage of the location to visit the Ikea less than a mile away and the Bengies Drive In theatre, a few miles away, and the Northern Central Railroad bike trail, about 20 miles away. There are also tons of restaurants in the immediate area.

title: “Excellent and Great Value for Money”
text:
Stayed here for a long weekend vacation in LA, having stayed here a few years ago, when at a conference down the street at the LA Conference Centre.
Prompt and friendly service at check-in.
Stayed in the central "column" of the hotel, adjoining the "red" tower. Could hear one of the hotel's trademark outside evalators from within the bathroom, but not in the bedroom fortunately.
Enjoyed my stay then and thoroughly enjoyed my return visit. Judging by the carpets, the place has been refurbished recently. Bedroom was large in my opinion, with plenty of space around the king-size bed. The famous "Heavenly Bed" was just that. Temperatures rose outside while I was there, so I had cause to use the air con. This was very quiet...the quietest I've ever experienced in a hotel...so kept the room chilled at night, but without disturbing my sleep.
Bathroom was a good size too and the double-headed shower was a bonus. Clever idea that delivered a great shower experience. I was on an SPG floor, so not sure if the wide range of bathroom products is normal. Impressed to find not only a toothbrush but a small tube of Colgate toothpaste and a small canister of shaving foam. If I had one negative comment to make, it would be that the bathroom could have benefitted from one more light above the sink, but that's a personal perference matter.
Minibar was really only an empty fridge, in which I put my SPG complementary bottle of water.
Used the wireless internet connection which cost €13 per day. The system did suffer from some reliability problems. Every now and again, the connection would be lost altogether, but would either correct itself within seconds or, if it didn't, I was able to "repair" the connection quickly from my laptop without any problems. It was only a minor inconvenience...."niggling" more than annoying.
I ate breakfast in the atrium poolside restaurant. Wide choice, piping hot food and beverages and a chef on duty to prepare eggs and omlettes. The $20 buffet was good value, when compared to ordering off the a la carte menu. Friendly wait staff too, although the one on the first day did slip in a pre-filled out feedback form with my bill, that needless-to-say gave her a glowing rating. I would have marked her highly anyway, but it was still a bit cheeky.
I also had a meal one evening in the lobby bar area. Not a wide choice from the bar menu, but good value and very tasty.
Hotel is on the edge of the downtown area. I wanted to be close to the opera house and it was just a 10/15 minute walk (uphill). Superb fish restaurant (McCormick and Schmick's) around the corner, at the top of a staircase feature (Bunker Hill Steps) on 5th Street.
Considering I had only paid $159 per night, via the SPG.com website, when neighbouring hotels wanted between $209 and $249, this hotel offers a great value for money experience.

title: “Did not like management”
text:
I stayed at the mediterranean inn couple of times and did some monthly stays.
There were problems: 1) Although most of the staff is welcoming and nice to the guest - the management is not.
Jim Farley - the frontdesk manager expects the person to do the housekeeper job (all crumbs have to be removed, trash removed etc). 
Maybe the reason is that housekeeping does an average job when they clean?
And if you sleep in longer and housekeeper cannot enter the room - the front desk manager will be angry at you and believe me - he can display this.
Anger is something that the front desk manager can show and can make your stay unpleasant.
The rooms have internet access. If you happen to have a virus in your computer and it affects the network then you will likely be disconnected permanently and you will never be able to use internet in your room in future visits. The network is setup that if one computer has a virus then all of the network can go down.
So in essence I felt that the management gives you a privelage to stay and not the other way round. The management tends to be rude and impolite.
2) Although the hotel has underground parking, high speed internet, and is located in the heart of nice district in Seattle - rooms are small.
3) I have noticed that little maintainence is done here. The rooms are acquiring more and more scratches, stains etc. They still look respectable at the time of the review.

title: “The Drake”
text:
The hotel was in a great location,very central to shopping sightseeing and restaurants. The public rooms are beautiful,and our hotel room was very nice with a good view but very small.The key card stated that complimentary wine was served in the evening and morning tea and coffee was available,on enquiry I was informed that the wine was discontinued and that the morning tea/coffee was available between 5 and 6 am only! As there were no facilities in the room I found this disappointing.
all in all though I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Professional service at a clean safe hotel.”
text: Kenneth at the front desk is professional, informed at ready to serve. Rick in the bar provides the best bar/restaurant service I've experienced in any of the downtown San Antonio hotels I've ever stayed at. Give them both a raise, they are worth it!!!!

title: “Great location, nice rooms, and nice breakfast options”
text: I'm not sure what upset a previous poster, but I like to find clean, modern hotels for lower prices in good locations. And that's what I found here. The rooms were updated, large, and had everything we needed. We had a room facing a church which had bells every half hour. We only noticed it in the evening before dinner so I think it stops by bedtime. Honestly, it's not that loud and I thought it was nice. I definitely felt like I was in the city. On the flip side of that, I never heard street noise nor traffic. So I'll take bells chiming over that. I found the staff friendly and professional. We ate breakfast one morning there. They have a great set-up that I would like to see the Hilton chain copy. They have bagels, pastries, boiled eggs, juice, etc. And they have in a fridge breakfast sandwiches to heat, cups of diced fruit, water, etc. Whatever your culinary challenge is in the morning, you can find something here. This is a solid choice for the moderate market. 20 minute walk from Union Station, 15 minute walk from the White House, and 10-15 minute walk to the mall. We found it to be a good base right near a subway stop if you need it.

title: “Great Location, Tiny Room, Funky Place”
text: I frequent the city, so I am accustomed to the smaller than average room sizes. This, however, was a small room (even after I upgraded). The rooms are appointed OK. Internet was flaky. The lobby is cool. I did not care for the Monday night pool party activities. Other nights were fine. Location and price were terrific. Few bars and restaurants next door, but Times Square is just around the corner. The gym was a joke - but Central Park is close enough for a great run. I would recommend for someone that does not plan to be in the room and looking for a place to stay close to Times Square. If you need to conduct business or require more than just a bed in the room, you may want to consider some others in the area.

title: “Book this hotel for business or pleasure”
text: I recently stayed at Hampton Inn Times Square North for a business trip. I booked this for a conference, with myself and 3 colleagues. Conference was on 6th Ave and 52nd, so the walk was only 10 minutes west. Free breakfast saved $$ for our group of 4. Nearby restaurants provided great variety, quick service, and ethnic diversity. Nearby Diners save us money for lunch or a quick dinner. Hotel was clean, front staff mostly helpful and very friendly. Concierge was able to handle all her requests. I did mine by phone. Would give her my requests and she would call me back with suggestions, and reservations. Bellman helpful when needed 430 am ride to airport for 4. Will definitely stay here again, for business or for pleasure, because it is located in Times Square area and close to theaters, Broadway, and subways stops to take you anywhere you want to go.

title: “Lots of Bad Luck on This Trip”
text:
I will start with the pros, because I don't want to sound too negative. The hotel was very nice, stylish, and modern. The location was superb, and the price was cheaper than most other, older hotels in the area. The staff were professional and still conversational. Also, the room's HVAC controls allowed me to run the room fan all night. I like the white noise of the fan, so room's with that feature get a big bonus in my book.
On the downside, there were quite a few things that did not go well while I was there. The television AND internet were inoperational when I arrived (the TV was fixed promptly, but the Internet was down until the next day). The iron had a leak in the water reservoir, which caused all of the water to spill onto my shirt as I began ironing it. I cut my finger on one of the metal studs that adorned the decorative pillows on the bed. The bed pillows were actually too soft; so soft that they didn't even seem like they were there. Finally, there was a false fire alarm on the second night that forced me to run down 12 flights of stairs in the late evening.
I don't get to Philadelphia much, but if I do get the chance again, i will give the Palomar another shot. I would love to experience this hotel on a good trip.

title: “Best of Memphis”
text:
This was my first trip to Memphis, and it couldn't have been improved in any way whatsoever. The staff at the Peabody did everything in their ability to make sure I was completely taken care of. Even when things went wrong, which they inevitably do, the staff worked to make it right. For example -- did you know that those keycard swipey dealies on your door are run by batteries? So inevitably the batteries will get weak and/or die. This happened to us, so despite getting new keys, we couldn't get into our room. We had to wait close to 45 minutes to get in, but during that time we had 3 staff members (concierge, manager, mechanic) all working on it, apologizing, and offering to comp us. I even got a personalized letter of apology. This is all it takes. When things are inconvenient, it doesn't take much to let me know that you are working on it -- that's what they did. As a patron, you just want to know that they care and are sorry. 
Besides that everything was smashing -- the duck march, the turn of the century feel, the location, the BEST BEDS EVER! There was even a TV in the bathroom -- I've stayed at 4 star hotels like the Ritz and 4 Seasons and even they don't have that (not that I needed it, but it was super swanky). 
I definitely recommend staying there, getting an old fashion in the lobby/bar, and checking out all memphis has to offer (particularly the food).

title: “Best Hotel/Best Location in D.C.”
text: Staying at the Dupont Circle Hotel made our vacation in Washington, D.C. absolutely perfect! Upon arrival and throughout our stay, we were greeted by a very friendly and helpful staff. The hotel has recently been remodeled, and it is gorgeous! Our room was very quiet and the modern decor was beautiful. The large shower, heated tile floors, and huge bath towels made showering pure joy. All the meals we ate at the hotel were excellent, with friendly and courteous wait staff. Computer/printer set-up was excellent. The hotel is in a perfect location in a great neighborhood. The metro is not even five minutes away, but many times we thoroughly enjoyed walking to the mall area and museums. We got a good feel for the city this way. There are so many lovely, fun restaurants in every direction from the hotel. You are steps away from beautiful and interesting Embassy Row and charming streets leading to fantastic places like the Phillips Collection art museum. The hotel is also across the street from lovely Dupont Cirlce Park, with its fountain, trees, and benches. Our trip to D.C. was great, and staying at this incredible hotel played a big role in making it so!

title: “Served its Purpose, Excellent Location”
text: After reading most of the reviews, I expected the worst. My Boyfriend and I stayed for 9 days, arrived on a Sunday at 3:15p, waited for check in less than 10 min (not bad at all). It was clean, location was great. Two things, is that you could tell it is an old hotel, and we asked for late room service the next day after 3p, they never cleaned it. But everyday after was clean. Checked out was on a Monday took about 40 minutes. My man asked someone and found out, check out could be done from the TV in our room. So I definitely recommend anyone doing that to save time leaving. If your willing to spend twice or three times as much as you would any place else near this location, there are several hotels that charge an arm and a leg a night. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Over Priced for the condition and age of the hotel”
text: We were never told parking would be extra. We never read it in of our confirmation or when we booked. The price they charge Parking should be included or maybe $25 for your stay. Not almost $20/day. I never heard of such a thing and I travel. The breakfast was good. The air quality in the hall was awful.

title: “Had a Great Stay”
text: I recently stayed at the hotel for both leisure and business and was very impressed. My room was on the 22nd floor and had the most amazing view of San Francisco Bay - the rooms have really large windows. Staff was great - special thanks to the head concierge, who took the time to explain many great things to do in the city for this first time visitor. I actually had business at the other Hilton in Union Square and I would choose to stay at this hotel over that one anytime. If I had one complaint, it would be the cost of the breakfast buffet at a whopping $23 - for a pretty standard fare. Food was great and I ate multiple mornings - but I think $23 for scrambled eggs, bacon, sausage, and hash browns was a bit much. An omelet station would have made it a little better. Overall though, a really nice hotel.

title: “Convenient Location, Nice grounds, nice view”
text:
I stayed here October, 2005.
Positives: Convenient location with lots of restaurants (seafood, Thai, Sushi, fast food, Mexican) all within easy walking distance. We had a roomy suite with a nice view of the Bay on the 5th floor of the Tower Building. The room was very quiet. Bathroom shower had good pressure and water temperature. The fitness center was free and the equipment was new and in good working order. Nice walking path around the Bay. Lots of parking (self-park was $9 per day). The staff was helpful with giving driving directions and restaurant recommendations. The grounds are pretty and well maintained.
Negative: The beds were not firm at all. The spa was expensive. A 50-minute massage was $110 and some of the other procedures cost as much as $185.
As for the neighborhood...yes, we did see some homeless people, but in my experience that is not uncommon in Southern California. We felt safe walking to and from restaurants in the dark for dinner.

title: “I had a wonderful experiance!!!”
text: I had a wonderful experiance, the only thong is that there are no refridez in the rooms!!! I stayed on the club level and I enjoyed all of the perks!!! I think that they should have drinks furnished all day long and that the floor should have special access to get on! Anyone can get on the floor!!! But my overall experiance was great!!!

title: “Pleasant stay & no complaints.”
text:
We weren't looking to staying at the Ritz for the third time and decided to go with 4 Seasons. 
Everything from the check-in to room service to personal services like laundry & alterations was handled professionaly and VERY fast, most of the time much sooner than the time frame given.
Our executive suite had courtyard & city views and while I'm not crazy about the shabby chic decor, it was clean and spacious.
While the food was nothing to rave about, we tried the Swann Lounge for lunch, the friendly service made things a bit easier, especially when compared to the Ritz. Overall, the staff at the hotel is eager to please and does so, it seems like, genuinely.
No problems with housekeeping encountered. We wouldn't hesitate to return to this property next time we're in town.

title: “My New Favorite at SeaTac”
text:
Don't get me wrong -- I still love Cedarbrook Lodge near SeaTac. But this trip I went for the Hilton because my flight got in at 1am after a trip lasting 27 hrs. All I wanted was the nearest hotel with a great bed, and boy, did I get it!! Fantastic!! 
My timing was superb for the free shuttle & I was whisked to the hotel in 2 minutes or so. Check in was courteous & fast (I'm really not sure how coherent I was, so I appreciate that checking in travel-weary patrons can be difficult, I'm sure). 
After a hot shower, I collapsed into the bliss of a wonderfully comfortable bed made with very nice linens & possessing plenty of perfect feather/down pillows. I detest bouncy pillows. The room was typical sedate, comfortable Hilton. The towels adequate, not great. 
The hotel has a very nice central garden which my room faced. I had the breakfast buffet which was a bit pricey at $20, but really very excellent. For an airport hotel, I find it odd that they charge for parking. The restaurant & bar are off the lobby, very comfortable, very relaxing, very nice.
I've slept in many of the hotels near SeaTac and this one, so far, would be pretty darn hard to beat. I will certainly be back.

title: “Outstanding”
text: This hotel is approximately two years old, and most of it still seems new. The public areas and guest rooms are clean. Rooms on the back of the hotel have a nice city view. The breakfast, included in the room rate, has improved since my last visit. The staff was fully helpful and kind. Note that the neighborhood is "hip" although somewhat off the beaten path.

title: “Classy Place Expensive Stay”
text: This is a classy place conveniently locater at the downtown boston Harbor front. The room is extremely good. Clean and cozy. The hotel has a nice ambience with bar and restaurant at the ground floor. The service was really nice. Its walkable to most places in Boston downtown area with a nice great view. The only thing that sucks is the parking, it cost 30 40 bucks to park the car. No free parking, so with expensive rates and parking fee it becomes a costly stay.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Stayed here for a business function great hotel. It is on quiet side of river walk but for a few nights stay and work it was ok. The upper floors are older but the hotel has been remodeled. The downstairs lobby is nice and there is a good brunch and lunch spot right on the river. If you want to stay on the river walk with less crowds stay here.

title: “'Zonies only”
text: For loud families and tourists only. Pool packed with bodies. Spa with nine children and seven adults at once. Basic amenities in room. One shampoo. Cheap/broken hair dryer. Bad coffee. Front desk people are clueless. Placed us on third story above loud whirling industrial fans and garbage drop. Otherwise, great bay view.

title: “Fantastic”
text:
We spent a week there recently, we found the hotel to be excellent - especially for the price.
We were immediately upgraded to a suite which was huge. Massive sitting room, large bedroom, dining table and small kitchenette containing fridge, coffee maker & microwave. 
The $3 breakfast is excellent value - all you can eat fruit, bagels, toast, doughnuts, cereal, coffee, fruit juice, croissants and pastries.
The hotel & rooms are spotlessly clean with towels & sheets changed everyday. Everything is in perfect working order and we were glad of the air conditioning!
The only problem we experienced was with the staff at the front desk - several times when people called for us they were told we had checked out - we hadn't. Our friends from the UK tried to organise a bottle of champagne for us but gave up after an hour of getting nowhere with the front desk staff. To top it all, on our last day Demetri at the front desk 'forgot' to book our car back to the airport resulting in us nearly missing our flights.
We'll defintely stay here again but will organise things ourselves next time!

title: “FABULOUS Stay at the Alex Hotel - Great Staff and Amenities”
text:
I had a fabulous stay at the Alex Hotel. I got a superb rate for the weekend of 7/31-8/2 and they upgraded me to the 1 Bedroom Suite. Which was huge, looked like a 1 bdrm NY Apartment. Not sure what the other reviewer was talking about. There was plenty of seating in the living room, plus a dining room table, a Sub Zero Fridge/Freezer, Stove, dishwasher including Pots & Pans.
