Plenty of amentities! It's New York, why would you stay cooped up in your room!?
What I like about the Alex is that the floors only have 4 other rooms which makes for a really quiet stay. You can't go wrong with the Alex. It's 2 blocks from Grand Central station, it's easy to get a cab and travel back to your hotel late a night with safety.

title: “No Prob on the Nob”
text: MH hotel was great! The location is perfect. Views everywhere. Rooms, spotless and have everything you need. We brought the pup, but you could not tell this was a pet friendly room. We had drinks at the Top Of The Mark which I highly suggest. Too many martinis to choose from, so we had 3! Staff was so friendly and helpful. Huntington Park across the street was perfect for the pooch to do his daily. I could stay in the MH and not leave but it's too close to Union shopping that you have to get out. Will go again and stay in the MH again for sure.

title: “Convenient, easy access, very friendly/helpful staff”
text: This was the hotel for a conference, and I found the staff very helpful and accommodating. The shuttle driver was great - knew everywhere. Room smelled musty and old, but the bed was fresh, and the conference rate was very reasonable. The Breakfast buffet was delicious. It was NOT hard to get in and out of downtown and the loop driving...

title: “Okay place”
text: We vacationed in L.A. in June and stayed at the Raddisson by the Airport. Upon arriving, we paid for our 1 week parking in full but after 2 days, we where called to the front counter and told we hadn't paid. After they contacted the lady who took our money the night we checked in, it was then she confessed to taking our money and then it was taken care of. I was told on the plane by a resident of L.A. TO NOT TRUST ANYBODY while we where there. That was so true. She was still working there the morning we checked out 5 days later. I wouldn't trust to stay there again. The hotel was nice but the housekeeping ladies spoke no English and getting towels and etc. was a nightmare as well as getting our room cleaned (even when the sign was on our door to clean). L.A. is an okay place to visit but, I 'll stick to my good ole country life in Kentucky!!!

title: “will return for cleanliness, location and price, not for light sleepers!”
text:
We used to live in new york and return often for long weekends. we don't hang out at the hotel so what it had to offer other than bed/bathroom was of not much interest to us, so the only comment I have for that is that the lobby is nice/artsy. oh and free wifi. Our room was small, which was fine and expected as many hotels are around the city. The bathroom was surprisingly functional and comfortable, as was the bed. Tons of storage in our double. linens were clean. I NEED the private bath but i hear the shared ones are of tolerable cleanliness.
The only problem we had were some relatively rude neighboring guests who kept their door open (b/c the rooms were too small for 4 to hangout comfortably I assume)and the group spoke loudly until 3-4am. We ended up having to ask them to be quiet, and failing that had to call the front desk to rectify the situation. That really reduced the sleep quality in an otherwise very quiet neighborhood of NYC. I will come back here with an update next time I go, maybe it was just a fluke this once.

title: “Fantastic! Amazing!”
text: We and about twenty of our guests stayed at the Hotel Montgomery surrounding our wedding. My family is hard to please, but we were astounded by the superior quality of our rooms and the service offered at this hotel. The location provided great access to downtown for our out of town guests. The rooms have an eclectic aesthetic, but everything was clean and plush. A few of us stayed in the spacious and well-appointed suites, with lovely windows throughout the living room. Every member of the Montgomery staff, from the linens people to the parking attendant, greeted us and smiled. The front desk bent over backwards to help us with the details of the hotel, delivering guest packages and arranging dry cleaning services, so that we could focus on our wedding. I cannot recommend them highly enough.

title: “Excellent place to stay in downtown Columbus”
text:
I have now stayed there on three occassions. 
The Westin has a great ambience, is clean and well managed, and has very friendly and professional people on their team.
The bar is great for winding down at the end of the day.
Parking is close and free, and access to the interstate is a plus too.

title: “I would not stay anywhere else in San Antonio, Westin is superb!”
text: I was so impressed with this hotel that I had to write a review - which is something I never do. What put this hotel so far above the rest is the staff. Any hotel can be beautiful but when you have a good attentive staff it makes your stay go from good to amazing. An extra thanks to Marques, he was attentive and beyond helpful. It makes you feel good when you feel like staff cares about you and your needs which is exactly what Marques did for me and family. I will recommend this hotel to all, it was fabulous!

title: “The amenteties are outstanding; not to mention the fabulous, warm welcoming staff at the attached Dine restaurant and bar, I fel”
text: The rooms are very modern with amazing shower heads and faucets, great balcony, and comfortable beds. The Dine restaurant and bar had the most amazing service, with smiling bartender, waitresses, and hostesses. The management is top notch, stepping in to help out when things get busy, down to knowing my first name before meeting him!

title: “Huge Rooms - Great Service”
text: My company booked this hotel for a mid-summer event we held at the hotel. We had over 1,000 guests stay at the hotel and everyone was very pleased with the entire stay. My room was huge and it was the base room! The views weren't that great, so try and get something that overlooks the park. I visit Chicago 2 - 3 times a year and will definetly book this hotel for my future visits. The snack bar downstairs has a staff that weren't very friendly, but I overlooked that because of all of the other great things about this hotel.

title: “Very nice!!”
text: Stayed here for conference. Got a room in the tower section. Grand lobby entrance is very elegant. Our room was nice. Soft bed. Tiled walk-in shower with granite countertops and dressing table area in the bathroom. The food and drinks in the hotel were very costly. Also, you were required to be an honors member to use the gym facilities. I think it should be complimentary to the guests. Plenty of space for a large event/conference. Overall, a good experience.

title: “Quiet, well-located midtown hotel”
text: We stayed on a Saturday night and the hotel was quite busy. Nevertheless, we were upgraded to a 30th floor park-view room without even asking, due to our Gold SPG status. We were impressed with the lack of noise.

title: “Everything we were looking for”
text:
My family had a very good experience at the Embassy Suites LAX North. It had everything we were looking for: an indoor pool, complimentary breakfast, large suites, a shuttle to LAX and was near the car rental companies. I also requested and received WIFI as part of my rate b/c many other hotels at LAX inc. free WIFI. 
The hotel has 8 floors and all the rooms are situated around the huge Atrium (see pic). On the main floor of the atrium is where they host Happy Hour and breakfast so every sound carries up to the rooms. However, you would only hear that if you were sleeping on the sofa bed (luckily, my daughter is a heavy sleeper). The king beds have a door to the room so we slept very comfortably. The suites are all renovated, spacious and gorgeous.The bathroom was heavenly. 
The one annoyance I have with all the hotels (not just this one) is that when I book a room for 3 ppl and that is clearly stated on the reservation, the room only has 2 towels or 2 pillows. This was the case at Embassy also where there were no blankets or pillows for the sofa bed.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: Stayed here for two nights last weekend on Hilton points. Front staff very friendly and helpful. Room was very clean with a small refrigerator and microwave which was great. Bed was very comfortable. Ate breakfast one morning in the hotel which was just ok. For $10.00 per person you order the hot food you want and help yourself to the cold food. Not much of a selection of pastries and cold food. It was very crowded when we were there and the food was gone quick. There is a Bob Evans right next door for a much better breakfast at a cheaper price. Hotel is in a great location near Ohio State University. I would definetely stay here next time I need to be in the area.

title: “GREAT LOCATION and STAFF”
text: Stayed here for one night in May with an old friend. We needed to be the in West Hollywood/Beverly Hills area and this was a great location. Parking wasn't all that great but we found a space. Reached the Grove and Beverly Hills in very little traffic. The rooms were clean, but the beds a little hard. Great stay and the staff was very helpful. Would definitely return.

title: “Great location, bed very uncomfortable”
text: The hotel is right next to the Alamo, one block from the Riverwalk Mall and river. Check in was quick, room very clean, bed very uncomfortable to be a pillowtop mattress. Breakfast was good with a variety of selections, waffles, eggs, yogart, fresh fruit, cold cereal, bagels. This hotel is one block from a fire station, heard fire trucks and ambulances all night. There is a parking fee that was not advertised.

title: “ONE WORD......KYLE! (talk about a stand up guy!)”
text: I have never had a hotel experience better than this, and the reason is simple...Kyle! This man is not only a great bartender, but the reason your establishment is successful. I am absolutely astonished with his service. He really connects with visitors on a personal level and is one of the most sincere people I HAVE EVER HAD THE PLEASURE OF MEETING! You are incredibly lucky to have him as part of your staff. He is engaging, courteous, and sincere. There is no doubt I will return to this hotel if I am within a 100 mile radius because of his service. Also, your night shuttle driver LeDoris was astounding! Very personable, and just a genuine and fun person to be around. I enjoyed all of my interactions with her and she made sure to see how i was doing on a regular bases. I believe she is one of a kind as well, and I would like to express my gratitude, These two individuals have made me feel right at home....almost like part of a family. I have NO idea how you keep them on your staff!? Obviously the GLUE to your organization and I hope the are recognized for their stellar service. Kayla was quite pleasant as well. one word to sum up these individuals..... AMAZING!

title: “Horrible service--very rude”
text: We stayed at the Fairmont in April. We booked two connecting rooms--one for my husband and three boys, the other, for my brother, a quadriplegic, who needed handicap accesibility. I found the valet staff upon arrival very curt and unfriendly, Neither the valet, or, his staff welcomed us with a smile, or a "Welcome, to the Fairmont". I was instantly irritated with this considering my great experiences with other "higher end" hotels, and their courteous and accomodating staff. I was always under the impression, as far as hotels go, that you get what you pay for. This is not so at the Fairmont, strike number one. The amount we paid for each room went as follows:(first night $199, second night $299, third night $522). As we checked in, my husband asked if he could have the bill split two ways--one bill I would pay for my room, the other to my brother, for his room--The clerk replied with "We can't do that." strike number two. We wanted a hotel with a pool, so the boys could swim. We were charged $10.00 each day, for use of the pool and the fitness center. The children were not allowed into the fitness center, this was evident by the large red signs stating no one under the age of 18 allowed. I understand this, but when my son, came into the fitness center to find me, and ask a question, he was hounded by a fitness staffer. It was obvious he was not supposed to be there. The children were designated to swim in a very small area of the pool, and not allowed into the whirlpool, which was two feet away from the pool, or, the sauna, which was three feet away--Not even the option "children allowed if accompanied by an adult". My husband was so enraged with this, he intentionally went into the sauna with my boys and was asked to leave by a man, who was sitting in the sauna. Strike number three. The second day, I was to meet my neice and her boyfriend for lunch, I suggested eating outside in the open air atrium, where they have many table,chairs and umbrella's. I aproached the staff person and said my neice would be meeting me for lunch, and we would love to eat outside. She replied with "We are not set up to do lunches outside". I turned to my left and pointed out the women eating a lunch at one of the tables, in the atrium. She turned in a huff and asked her manager if this was o.k.. He reluctantly agreed, once again pointing out that it was not set up for lunch. Strike number four. I could write more, but I think I've made my point. This being said, I would not recommend the Fairmont to anyone with children, husbands, a upscale place for outside dining, , or, for someone who equates higher priced hotels with excellent service, and a friendly, accomodating staff.

title: “very relaxed place”
text:
minimalist hip, yes - rooms, pool and grounds. 
quiet, yes - surprisingly. 
good and relaxed service, yes. 
pricey, also a BIG yes. a bit too pricey for what you get. 
i spent $1k for three nights in a petite suite with no outdoor space, and with my blinds shut and AC on the whole time for privacy and quiet. 
i'd recommend it, BUT would grill them on my room location - asking for something out of the way where i could have some natural light and outdoor space. 
i think it would be fairly priced in the $250-$275 range for weekend nights. $325 is a bit much for a saturday evening in a room with a bare bones bath (no tub, some cruddyish tile) and lousy TV service. plus, it's austin, not san fran, miami, etc. 
without the tiny pool and Jo's coffee/food place next door, i would have a tough time recommending this at all.

title: “Superb”
text:
The Palomar exceeded expectations. Check-in was a breeze, friendly and efficient, and I was upgraded to a King Spa Premier Room. The room was gorgeous -- spacious, stylish modern decor, colorful well-arranged furniture, and meticulously maintained. The huge bathroom, clad in beautiful sand-colored marble and granite, was stunning, with an enormous soaking tub with whirlpool jets, large glass-enclosed shower and gleaming fixtures. The king-sized bed was extremely comfortable, with high-quality linens, and faced a 37" LG flat-screen TV. Signing up for Kimpton InTouch resulted in a $10 minibar credit and free in-room wireless internet, with a strong signal.
Breakfast in the Sable restaurant was two poached eggs, pepper-crusted bacon, home fries and sourdough toast at a fairly priced $11. Fresh-squeezed OJ, hot strong coffee, and excellent raspberry preserves. Check-out was also a snap.
I highly recommend this outstanding hotel and look forward to returning the next time I'm in Chicago.

title: “Good value for money”
text: Nice and clean room. Free breakfast with a lot to choose from. Small but clean pool where our kids played for an hour without complaining.... And I really appreciate the free guest laundry and the possibility to buy snacks and drinks from the shop in the lobby for a decent price. Also good location with easy walking to both the Galleria and different restaurants.

title: “Loved the Park Savoy”
text:
We stayed here at default really becasue we could not find a reasonably priced one at the time. I telephoned the hotel and they had a cancealltion so we got the hotel for 4 nights for $350 we were a little scared as there were some negative reviews about this place, but i can honestly say it was great very clean although a bit on the small side but we were not in NYC to spend time in our room. The only downside was the 1 lift which was out of service on 2 occasions throughout our stay we were on the 9th floor and after 10 hours walking about i nearly cried when we found out it was broke, there is no view apart from another apartment block but it was 1 block away from central park and columbus circle. 
If you stay here you must go to 6th ave cafe it was gogeous really tasty. 
Would definately stay here again without a doubt.

title: “Great Location and rooms! A hit for fans!”
text: We stayed here for a Monday night football game and besides the outcome (!) everything was great. We had a large group with us and everyone's experience was perfect, which is saying a lot when you have 5 different rooms and personalities. Not one complaint from the entire group. The rooms were extremely quiet and clean. I was worried about the noise from the fans but it was NEVER an issue. To get to your rooms or anywhere in the hotel you have to use your room key to access the elevator. After the game when the place was packed there were many employees present to make sure everything went smoothly. The shuttle is the best as you can park your car and never have to deal with the Seattle traffic. I would definitely stay here again. A MUST if you are attending any game whether NFL or MLB.

title: “Good hotel. No probs.”
text: Girlfriend and I stayed here for 4 nights in June. Very enjoyable. Lovely quiet rooms. Staff were very friendly. Old world charm. Close to public transport. Bathroom is small but didn’t worry us. Good rate for a good quality hotel.

title: “Worst hotel I have ever stayed in and I just checked in”
text:
I have been here a grand total of 15 minutes. First impression walking in. The pony reeks of pet urine and feces. My company put me up in this place. I decided to go ahead and check in thinking maybe a pet just had an accident. NOPE THE ENTIRE HOTEL INCLUDING ROOMS SMELLS THIS WAY. 
On the amenities list it says there is a data port. There is not only wireless. Most of the lights in the room are burned out. Switches are bad. Did I mention this place smells. Bed linens are not clean. I wont be staying here long at all. Oh just saw. ... empty TP roll too. Mold around tub. Yes I am taking pictures. DO NOT STAY HERE. THIS PLACE SHOULD BE SHUT DOWN BY THE HEALTH DEPT.

title: “Great Business Hotel in Easy Location”
text: I have stayed at the Hyatt Place for two weeks over the past couple months. Overall, it’s a comfortable business hotel. I enjoy the layout of the rooms (especially for an extended stay) because they are divided into two separate areas. There is a sitting area with a wet bar that is separated from the bed and bath area. The breakfast is nice because you can order warm food or stick to the simple continental airport. Walking distance to the hotel are several good dining options including Saltgrass Steak House, Outback Steak House, Razzoo’s (Cajun – very good with cheap draft beers), Joe’s Pizza and Pasta (great pizza and pasta in very casual setting), and Cousin’s Bar-BQ. And a Target too, which is great for stocking up on water. Overall, I had a great stay and will stay there the next time I am in Fort Worth.

title: “Comfortable, and great value for the money”
text:
Nice little hotel in a central location, albeit just off the highway. Hotel staff are very helpful and friendly. there is also a business center with free printing. There is a nice movie collection if you want to stay in for the night or have kids. breakfast is great - lots of choice, and constantly monitored/replenished by the staff. We had to leave really early when we checked out and the staff made sure to open the dining room for us to have a quick bite.
on the other hand, our room was in the older building and farther from the main building, so wifi didnt work. if you go, try to get a room in the main building - apparently it is newly renovated. towels were thin and rough, and we went to the front desk for an extra towel each day, which got annoying.
however, we still recommend old town inn - it is a great place for the price!!

title: “Decent but don't expect too much”
text:
I stayed here on a Friday night prior to catching an early flight at the San Diego Airport. I've stayed at Hampton Inns before and am not necessarily a fan, but this was fairly close to the airport and it was reasonably priced (about $100 with tax). It's not in the best neighborhood (some strip clubs and bars adjacent), but I wouldn't label it as a dangerous area.
The rooms are typical - nothing fancy. My room was very clean, although the entire place, even the halls, had a funky cleaning-fluid smell. The staff I encountered were reasonably nice and helpful.
My only complaint is the loud doors. A peeve of mine is that there is a certain type of hotel visitor who doesn't care when their door slams behind them. The doors in this hotel were very loud and shook the walls. It was very annoying.
The hotel shuttle runs once an hour on the half-hour starting at 4:30 a.m. I used this service and was satisfied.
While I probably would not stay here again, I don't want to discourage the budget-minded traveler or somebody who wants to stay close to the airport or Sea World. You really do get what you pay for, and this Hampton Inn is not a bad place. Trust me - there are lots worse.

title: “service”
text: when is san diego my wallet was stollen with my hotel key and room number in it ,we got back to our room about 9 pm and the hotel staff were very understanding and changed our room so I would feel safer even though they only had to change the room code they gave us a new room ,I will forever be grateful for the safe feeling I got and the wonderful service ,not to mention the great nights sleep every night

title: “excellent”
text: Upon arrival, we were upgraded to an Edwardian suite. Staff were fantastic throughout our stay. If going to NYC, will always stay there! The only down side was there were a couple of small hairs on the bathroom floor

title: “Extremely Lavish Place”
text:
We stayed at the Omni the nights of December 28th and 29th, in order to go to the Meineke Car Care Bowl. The hotel was extremely lavish and comfortable.
The building is centrally located in Charlotte-and, as Charlotte isn't exactly the biggest city in the world it is a relatively easy walk to any attraction (for example, the Bank of America stadium was only a 15 minute walk). 
The lobby is...nice. It's somewhat oddly shaped, with the front desk and the (very small) concierge desk located in an area next to the bar, while if you go down an escalator you get to the "mall" area-this houses a convenience store, as well as some other interesting shops.
Now, for the rooms. This is the one spot where the hotel truly shined. The beds were AMAZING, and the room was extremely spacious (with the exception of the bathroom). Our travel partners stayed in a room marketed as a "mini suite", and their room was not much bigger than ours-imagine the size of a decent sized kitchen table that only housed a pull-out couch.
We LOVED the fact that they gave us chocolates on the beds each night, as that was a nice treat after such a long day. The first night, they just gave us little packages of chocolate mints. The second and final night, however, they gave us this extravagant Godiva chocolate box (interestingly enough, they left the price tag on it-$15.50).
The TV's have the ONCOMMAND movie software, so you can order movies directly to your hotel room (albeit at a higher price). As well, the alarm clocks have MP3-in jacks, so you can plug in your iPod to listen.
It's probably common sense-but don't bother spending money on the in-room bar. The candy bars were extremely expensive. Also, they put out an Evian bottle, but then have a tag on it that says that if you open it, they'll charge 6 dollars to your hotel room!
Now, are you guys ready for the drawback (which may not bother some people)? The pool is outdoor, and is DISGUSTING! It looked as if it had not been cleaned in a long time, and it wasn't even particularly large-i'll just swim in the bathtub in the room!).
If you're interested, the exercise room was...just that. Not big, not tiny, but a decent room with a couple of machines.
All the people that worked at the hotel were very nice and welcoming. In all, I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to anyone, and I would stay here again in the future.

title: “Convenient Location, Good Food, Comfortable, and quaint bar”
text: Convenient Location, Good Food, Comfortable, and quaint bar - Great staff will make your stay welcome!

title: “Great time... and it smells great too!”
text: Even before our arrival we were sent an email about things going on around our hotel. It was super helpful and we were even able to get VIP passes to the Willis Tower sky deck compliments of the W Hotel and Laurelin Hefter! It put us to the front of the line and got us right in. Walking distance from the tower and Millenium Park - we look forward to our next trip!

title: “Stay away.”
text: Room 1137 we are currently in. The walls are covered in dings and black marks. The outlets are not covered. Room is tiny and reeks of smoke. This is a "non smoking room". Bath tub had two pubic like hairs in it upon arrival. Bed spread looks dirty but sheets are clean. For 350$/night, would expect much better. Will not come back. Staff rude and a no name rapper was rapping in 11th floor lobby for two hours and filming. Complained to security. They ignored. What a dump!!!!!!!!! Rip off. Also waited 35 min in check in line. Terrible.

title: “New, clean hotel for a great price in a...”
text:
New, clean hotel for a great price in a terrible location. Staff slow and uneager to help with information but will eventually get around to getting you what you need. This is probably due to understaffing. 
Location of hotel is in a neighborhood with high crime adjacent to a bridge that shelters the homeless. 
There are few restaurants in the area and too far to walk to inner harbor but, hotel does provide a shuttle. 
Our car was broken into and window smashed in hotel parking lot that does not contain any security,including cameras, although the police stated that our car was the 10th this month to be broken into in this lot.

title: “Perfect walking distance to anywhere you want to go”
text:
This is another favorite stay when I'm traveling for work. The rooms are clean and the staff is friendly. It is a short walk to Pike's Place and all the other wonderful spots down there. 
The rooms are comfortable but there isn't much of a view. You can order breakfast to be delivered when you want in the morning but it's pricey. 
One complaint... The wifi isn't free!?!?! What business hotel doesn't have free wifi?

title: “A real Gem”
text: This hotel is a real Gem. Very customer service oriented staff. Great location too at a really good price. I'll be back to this one!

title: “Hands down the best place for hosting a large group!”
text: This conference center is accessible, economical and the service was superb. The food was plentiful and the choices were vast. The beds and sheets were very nice and each room has a balcony. The grounds are beautiful and in a great area. Close to light rail and restaurants. Great gym and the snack stations throughout the property are always stocked and open 24 hours! The conference center has free-wifi throughout and in every room and a business center that doesn't charge for copies and computer time!!

title: “Kensington Park Hotel - Fit for Royalty”
text:
Everyone knows that traveling can be expensive. On tight budgets, oftentimes the first place you cut is your hotel quality because all you really need is a place to lay your head at night. However, this can be one of the most important parts of your trip. Who wants to share their bed with bedbugs or mites after a long day of sightseeing? That can truly ruin a good time, don'tcha think?
My experience at Kensington Park Hotel in San Francisco has been wonderful. It is one of the Personality Hotels in SF and is located at 450 Post Street, right in the heart of Union Square. I stayed there in November 2008 for a couple of nights and again on my recent weeklong adventure from May 5-11, 2009. 
Why'd I go back? First off, the price was right. Obviously, from looking at its website, Kensington Park can be a bit high for most budgets. However, remember that you're in SF and that everything is pretty expensive. I got a great deal for air and hotel from Honolulu so I booked it right away. There were other air/hotel deals out there (believe me, I combed all the usual sites and then some), but when Kensington popped up within my budget, I jumped at the chance to stay there again.
What I learned last fall is that their beds are truly heavenly, especially after a day of walking up and down hills or in and out of stores. I have never slept on a bed better than this one, and this includes my own bed at home. I don't even know how to describe it to you. It's just the right firmness and softness to ease your aching body to sleep every night. You melt into the comforter and are engulfed by softness.
Another good quality about this hotel is that the staff is very accommodating. My flight arrived at 5:55 a.m. and by the time I got to the city it was around 7:15 a.m. Despite this ungodly hour, the staff allowed me and my BFF to check in way ahead of schedule. (When we called to double check that they had our reservations, we put in a request for early check-in but they said they couldn't guarantee anything.) I can only imagine that either we looked pretty had-it from the red-eye flight out of Honolulu or that the staff was very, very accommodating. I like to believe the latter but cannot be sure.
The room we were given (#4 on the fifth floor) was a bit smaller than the one we received on our last trip. However, this could also be because we were only two people and last fall we had three. Even though the room and bathroom were smaller than before, they were still very satisfactory. Everything was clean, which was a definite plus. There was no mold, mildew or hair in the bathroom. The beds were made and everything seemed to be in order. For a peek at the rooms, check out their website. Yes, those are probably professionally done pictures and no doubt are enhanced with a little help from Photoshop. But, trust me. That's exactly what the rooms look like, if not just a tad less bright and vibrant. Still, the beds and rooms definitely live up to the PR/marketing hype of the website.
Another good thing about the staff is that they're very friendly. I hate to admit it, but for the life of me I cannot remember the name of the guy at the front desk. There were actually three different people at the front desk at different times of the day and night. However, the night shift/early morning guy definitely stood out. He's the guy who checked us in (this time and last time if I remember right). Every time he saw us, he'd greet us with a big smile and address us by our names. Yeah, he actually remembered our names! Amazing when the hotel seemed to be almost fully booked. This kind of customer service is a sign that Kensington Park is really going the extra mile for its guests.
If you're not convinced by now to try this hotel on your next SF visit, let me add that it's only a skip away from all the shops at Union Square, steps away from the Muni (cable car and buses) and just a couple of blocks up from BART. The location is hot, hot, hot. So definitely try Kensington Park Hotel because it's fit for royalty.
--------------------------------

title: “Charming and very comfortable”
text: I stayed here for 6 days in October and was very impressed. This is a "boutique hotel" ie "small" but don't let that put you off. The rooms were extremely comfortable and quiet (although I believe that there are rooms at the front that are noisy due to the proximity to Times Square ). There is no view but I didn't find that a problem and everything the hotel offers, more than makes up for this. Ricks Bar is a very comfortable lounge and the complimentary wine 5-8 each evening plus nibbles is a treat ! This hotel is like a little oasis of calm and relaxation in the heart of Manhattan. I would have no hesitation in returning. Ooh and the staff are lovely too !

title: “Average Small Room - Dreadful Internet Connection”
text:
I stayed at Holiday Inn – Downtown/Soho from 19th May to 21st May 2008. I should mention that I have spent a substantial amount of time staying in hotels, with over 200 hotel nights in some years due to my job. I’ve stayed at everything from 2 star motels to 4 star hotels and everything in between.
Check-in was good at the hotel, and the bellman brought up my luggage very quickly. My room was listed on the Holiday Inn website as an Executive Room, which I thought would provide me with a larger size room and that it would be located on the executive floor. Wrong. It was a fairly small room, and not located on the Club floor as Holiday Inn calls their Executive floor.
There is no in room safe, no mini bar and 2 exceptionally small drawers to store anything. The closet space was laughable, a 3 foot area beside one of the double beds that can only be reached by a narrow space beside the bed - I usually do unpack and hang items in hotels, and for the first time ever, I didn't bother in this hotel due to the lousy access.
The noise from the street was clearly audible, even though I was on the 10th floor (the hotel has 14 floors) and the window was closed (it doesn’t open). So it seems there isn't any soundproofing. I've stayed at many hotels in city centres and never had the massive street noise that I had at this Holiday Inn.
And the constant rumbling from the subway below the building was annoying too – and yes, the floor in my 10th floor room shook each time the subway passed by.
The blackout blinds were too short to cover the window, so the bright sun shone into the room very early each morning.
The bed was ok, though short for a double bed (I wouldn’t recommend it for anyone over 5’10”). There is a small coffee machine which I didn't use (as in the lobby, you can get coffee with unlimited refills which you can bring to your room for US$ 3.79).
The wireless internet connection was terrible - I was able to stay connected for about 5 minutes before it would cut out, and the only thing that seemed to work was rebooting my laptop - so not a great solution. One of the main criteria for me in choosing this hotel was that they had internet access, so this poor service was unacceptable. I spoke with the front desk, and they had one of their engineers restart the router on my floor, and that time, I was able to connect and stay connected for 10 minutes. But afterwards, the same situation happened with very poor connections. I would not recommend anyone travelling for business to stay at this hotel.
I had the breakfast buffet one morning, and it was ok, offering basic items, though as with most hotels, overpriced for what you get – you’re much better off going to a restaurant outside the hotel.
The location is ok if you want to be in Little Italy or Chinatown. But if you’re planning to see a number of Broadway shows, then this location isn’t great as the theatre district and Times Square are several stops away using the subway, and it’s definitely not within walking distance as it’s over 50 street blocks away.
If you are planning to stay for a day or two in New York, and if you feel the need to be near Little Italy and Chinatown, and don’t need internet access, this hotel is ok, but not great. If you want a good hotel with excellent value or if you're coming to New York for a longer stay, I would highly recommend the Hampton Inn - Times Square North instead as it’s cheaper, better located and much higher quality of room and services.
All in all, I won't be returning to this hotel.

title: “Good value, comfortable, good location”
text: When booking an accomodation in a city you aren't familiar with you rely on the internet and the reviews of others. This hotel is convienently placed (although we found out later that it was in the "tenderloin" area which is supposed to be bad) we had no issues with safety, although did not walk around in the middle of the night to look for trouble. The hotel was clean and comfortable. It is dated (built in 1910!) but this gives it it's charm, if you are looking for a modern new hotel this is not it. The breakfasts was great, coffee, tea, hot chocolate, danishes (non-stop supply) and fresh fruit (melons, apples, bananas). What was nice is that you could meet your fellow occupants while having your coffee or not. Free internet. Front desk staff were helpful and answered all our questions when needed. I would recommend this place and would return if in San Fransisco.

title: “Less than thrilled”
text: I was less than thrilled with my stay here. The room was nice, the decor was modern and tasteful but there was no refrigerator in the room, and I like to keep cold drinks in my room. The complaints are all about the money. To me $36 a day valet parking is unreasonable, as is a $19.95 breakfast buffet with cold scrambled eggs. In my opinion there are plenty of nice hotels in San Diego that offer more amenities and a much more competitive price.

title: “great stay”
text: great staff beautiful rooms, very qiet, but pleasant....

title: “Great for work meetings, nice accomodations, great location downtown!”
text:
I recently booked a last minute work meeting at this hotel and the staff was wonderful to work with. They were very attentive and Travis F was most helpful. The meeting space was great and the hotel accomodations were quite nice. First time visit to downtown portland and was very pleased.
Beds were soft, rooms were spacious and clean, nice views from some rooms. Restaraunt and lobby bar in hotel as well as Startbucks onsite. 
There was a pool and fitness center but did not have time to see either. 
Easy to walk to many restaraunts and shops in the heart of downtown. Great location

title: “Generally a great place”
text: We stayed at the Le Meridien during Columbus Day weekend (which was packed in SF!) and had a great time. The hotel is clean and our room had a nice view of the bay (although we were rarely in it to enjoy the view!). The fitness center was particularly well appointed and I enjoyed the coffee/tea in the lobby each morning. The only real "problem" we had was that the key to the minibar didn't work. Overall, a good hotel in a good location.

title: “The most un-Super 8 Super 8”
text: This hotel is unlike any Super 8 I have stayed in. It's fairly new, and close to the airport, though not always easy to find. We stayed for two nights as it was much cheaper than anywhere in downtown Austin (not far to drive), and probably much better too. We stayed in the Asian Suite, which came with a swing! The bed was one of the best I have ever slept in, with proper white bedlinen and quilt and thick pillows (not the usual synthetic fleece blanket and thin pillows). There was a pillow menu if those provided were not to your liking. The hotel has a selection of DVDs to choose from, reliable wireless and an excellent hot breakfast. I highly recommend this hotel, even if your travels don't involve Austin airport. The only downside is that since it's off a highway, the only eating options are a Jack in the Box next door. Otherwise, an excellent stay.

title: “Awesome-even at full price!”
text:
Stayed here for one night while seeing a play downtown. Booked it only because of the Groupon deal, so the room was about half price. We walked in, expecting the "no such thing as a free lunch" adage to come into play, but...oh...my! Everything we experienced exceeded expectations!...corner room, facing Northeast, so we had a view of the Michigan Ave bridge over the river (with Wrigley Building and Tribune tower), and a sliver of the lake between buildings facing east. The room was big (Super gi-normous by city standards? VERY comfy king bed, little hallway from the hotel corridor by the elevators into the actual bedroom, so noise from people going to/from elevators was low...good sized, bright bathroom. Helpful and nice front desk staff...bellhops....bartenders in Angels and Kings...and the reason we booked it: location. Right by the river, near the lake, not terribly far from the train stations...
Only negatives we could find were very slow elevators (tried to take the stairs down one day and got to the bottom floor and the sign said "No exit-go back up to the second floor and take the elevator"--how silly did we feel taking an elevator down 1 floor?), and street noise. We were 8 floors up and I realize my city is loud (yes, we're suburbanites who went into the Big City for a night). I can't say we are complaining about the noise, just seems they could've tried a little harder to block it out.

title: “Worth the top spot”
text:
Stayed here with my wife for our 10 yr anniversary. After an 8 hr flight we were welcomed by a very attentive front desk. The hotel itself is located at time square (an ideal spot for a all over NY expedition) , has cozy rooms, a nice complementary breakfast. It is a small hotel and feels quite like city hotels in European cities.
 It is however the staff attitude, attentiveness that sets the hotel apart, simply great.
We look forward to returning.

title: “Expected more from a Radisson”
text: We had to stay at the Radisson when our flight out of NY was cancelled. After staying at a few Radissons in the past, we expected more in terms of comfort, space, and cleaniness. Yes, we were staying in NYC, but even for NY the hotel room was quite small and dated.

title: “AMAZING in every way!”
text: We went down to San Diego to see the Packers vs. Chargers game, and had such a wonderful weekend! The staff at this hotel are completely amazing; the room service was stellar and the cuisine in the restaurant was beyond compare. It would be impossible to find enough superlatives to describe the quality of our stay. Chef Jimmy and his staff provided the most wonderful dinner (pumpkin ravioli, a creme brulee trio) the night before the game! After the game, we treated ourselves to room service, and enjoyed far too much food (pizza margherita, a chicken sandwich, bruschetta, etc.) served with excellent care. I cannot give a high enough recommendation for this hotel; needless to say, I will be back many times, if this is any indication of how guests are treated at this lovely hotel.

title: “Good night's rest”
text: I got a great deal to stay here, but was unsure what to expect. Pleasantly surprised to receive a great check-in and enjoy the new lobby makeover. Our room was very cozy and had comfortable down comforter & fluffy pillows. The bathroom was super small, but very clean. So enjoying a great night's sleep was not the end of my family's stay at the Sheraton. We had a very good breakfast buffet to conclude the trip. Everything throughout the hotel had a modern feel and was clean. Do make note that the hotel charges a parking fee.

title: “Good value, spacious 2 bedroom suite, conveniently located.”
text: We were traveling in a group of 6 and booked the Hotel's 2 bedroom suite which comfortably slept us all. It also had a functional kitchen, dining and sitting area. The service was helpful and the Hotel was conveniently located near a subway station and convenience shopping. I would be happy to stay here again.

title: “Excellent location....”
text: Stayed here prior to a cruise. It is really within walking distance of the cruise pier if you don't bring much luggage (doubtful for a week's cruise). The gaslight district, the San Diego Trolley, the railway station, the waterfront .... they are all right nearby. It is clean and well appointed. The price was right since we got a discounted room in conjunction with the cruise.

title: “great room, great location, great hotel”
text:
My husband and I are just back from New York having stayed for a week at the Grand Hyatt. This was our first time and it was a birthday treat for me. The hotel is really lovely and when we got there we got an upgrade to a deluxe king room which was huge!! 
The staff were all very helpful and the lobby was beautiful just to chill out in after a days walking in New York. We never ate in the hotel but I would recommend getting breakfast from the food concourse in Grand Central Station. The hotel is linked to the station so you don't need to go outside. We had breakfast there every morning and it was fabulous - the station is so beautiful and the food area is amazing and has lots of healthy options and fairly cheap prices.......
We had a fantastic trip and would definately stay in the grand hyatt again - location is great - new york is great!!! ask for an upgrade - you may be pleasantly surprised!!!!

title: “For better or worse, it's right on Times Square”
text:
Being on Times Square is the main strength of this hotel, but also the main weakness. For travellers who want to be right in the middle of the action, it’s a great place, that’s why I voted 5 in location. But the action may be too much as the area around it is ridiculously overcrowded, to a point when it’s hard to walk on the streets. Much worse is the constant noise, mainly coming from cars honking like there’s no tomorrow and the non-stop ambulances/firefighters/police frenzy. To be clear, I was up on the 32nd floor and all this can be heard from up there (especially at night), even though the windows seem to have very good sound insulation.
That aside, the hotel is all you would expect from a W. The reception area has constant loud music, lots of people at the bar and uncomfortable seating, but that’s all part of the W package, I guess. The front desk being on the 7th floor is a little odd, but it doesn’t affect the experience badly. I can’t say anything about the restaurant downstairs as I didn’t try it.
The room was very comfortable and decent sized, and also spotlessly clean. The mattress was new, the LCD TV worked well and the shower was good. It’s a little tricky to figure out how to make the water work on the sink, but you’ll get it after 2 minutes of poking around.
The internet on the room was very pricey, but the great news is that it was free on the lobby, so Kudos for the W on offering that option at least. And I must say, it worked pretty well for the when I needed it. There was also a Mac available for people to use.
Finally, the service was professional and pleasant all around. They didn’t do anything out of the ordinary, but didn’t mess anything either. And that is a lot more than I can say about several other hotels.
In conclusion, I would recommend this hotel if a) you know that’s the style of hotel you want, and b) you really want to stay in Times Square. Now I know I don’t.

title: “Great Boutique Hotel Near Chinatown”
text: My wife and I spent last night at the Orchard Garden Hotel during a quick, one-night trip to San Francisco. This hotel was a great discovery for us as it is in a great location, is staffed with friendly and knowledgable people and is very comfortable. Our room was simple and small but very comfortable and well-appointed with a European design. We had an interior room that was exceptionally peaceful and quiet. This hotel is especially "green" and is known for being the first in the United States to incorporate the use of guest keycards for managing energy delivery to each individual room. A very unique and energy-efficient concept. Highly recommend and would definitely stay again.

title: “A Terrific Hotel”
text:
The wife and I are here on business/leisure. 
From a busines perspective excellent (business centre functional). Front office staff very helpful under Roseanne's management. 
From a leisure perspective the Lifetime Fitness free memebership to one of the largest gyms we have ever seen was a real boon. An this gym is literlly next door.
Catering staff extremely pleasant & knowledgeable under Domingo's leadership.Very nice food indeed & a lovely breakfast. A great place to stay & we will be here for a very long time indeed!

title: “Excellent Location & Good Value for NYC”
text:
We stayed here for a weekend in NYC and although I do usually choose Marriott, we selected this particular hotel due to a combination of price, location and solid reviews on Trip Advisor. Overall, we can have no major complaints and would happily stay here again.
We had a long flight in from Europe so were very happy to arrive at our hotel with two tired kids. I requested a room on a high floor so we could have a view and we are actually quickly checked into the very top floor so off to a good start. The room itself was quite large (king and sofa), with the usual Marriott amenities and free wifi. 
All the staff we encountered were very friendly and helpful - from reception to concierge to breakfast to security guard - everyone would say hello and offer help/advice. (We had a nice Italian dinner close to hotel on recommendation of the concierge - Angelo's Pizzeria).
Location of the hotel is perfect for both subway, or if you actually want to see the sights, for walking around.
The breakfast was very good here. We stayed in 4 different hotels on this trip and breakfast here was definitely the best one. Fresh fruit, granola, waffles, etc.
My only minor complaint would be that the hotel could maybe use a bit of a makeover as some of the decor was a bit faded. However, I can appreciate that this place is very full, very often, so it is not hard to see how things wear out.
Overall though, a very good stay at a Marriott once again.

title: “Excellent location, decent hotel”
text:
The location is the best feature of the hotel. Its at the Chinatown gates and walking distance to many restaurants, shops, and tourist attractions. It feels very safe walking there at night, and the hotel is walking distance to public transportation. 
The hotel itself is old and a little run down. The furniture is a little dated, but everything seemed clean. The bed was comfortable and there was plenty of heat and hot water. The breakfast was the standard continental breakfast and was restocked constantly so nothing ever ran out. The staff was very nice and helpful with giving directions, offering advice on good restaurants, etc. 
I would definitely stay here again. You just can't beat this location and deal.

title: “Great Family Hotel”
text:
Our family of 5 really loved this hotel.We booked a family room that turned out to be very spacious and had 2 single beds,a double bed and a Queen sofa in 2 separate rooms.
The location itself cannot be beat,close to Union Square,with great shopping and restaurants and the Cable Car basically at your door.
John the Concierge is very helpful with directions and tips and although parking is a bit pricey,although typical for San Francisco,it is very convenient.
We loved our stay in San Francisco made better by choosing to stay at The Handlery Union Square.

title: “Everything was excellent and I would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in Chicago”
text: Staying here for one night the first week of September, we we were warmly greeted and upgraded to a suite without even asking, which was very nice. The bathroom had a glassed in spa shower which felt wonderful after plane and train travel all that day. The room was essentially quiet during the night and we rested well. There was an indoor heated pool which looked good but that we didn't get to. The full breakfast on Sunday morning was really good and unlimited and there was a nice, sunny dining area beside it. I had to print several things off and the business center was quiet and private. The room is very convenient to the El train (half a block) and we were able to walk or to take a bus to everything that we wanted to see that weekend. The Chicago public transit system is very effiicient and we enjoyed our stay in the windy city very much. It is one of the few cities/hotels that I will definitely visit again.

title: “Going Downhill - Fast”
text: This was obviously once a lovely hotel. The staff was friendly and the bed was comfortable. Unfortunately, that's the only good thing I can say. There was coffee, but no cups, and despite a request and a promise, one never appeared. I also had to request a lightbulb and soap. I overheard another guest ask the housekeeper for soap and a cup, and she admitted to having neither. The website advertises room service (none), a business center (closed), and "Our signature restaurant, La Musique, a Cajun restaurant, serves an inspired menu in a hip and elegant room that features stage costumes and memorabilia from past Motown hit makers" which has been closed for months. I heard a vacuum cleaner, but there was no evidence that it picked up dirt. The ceiling in the bathroom was falling, and there was a beer bottle and chicken bone in the elevator. Where did they find food? The clerk reported that the hotel had new owners, and is hoping that things will get better. I hope so, or this hotel will suffer the same fate as many of the other buildings we saw.

title: “Met my expectations”
text:
After reading many good reviews on the web decided to bring my family to stay in this hotel for our 6 day trip to NYC (our first trip to NY, too). Overall, I liked staying here, excellent location, room new, clean, and quiet, beds very comfortable. However, on the first day the bathtub in our room drained very slowly, as if clogged. We told the front desk and it was fixed the next day, but the problem came back in the next few days---standing in ankle deep soapy waste water during a shower became quite irritating. 
Front desk staff usually are able to helped us when we asked for it, but were not always very warm and friendly, depending on who was there---questions are replied with curt answers; however, room service and the technician who came to fix the safe in our room (it was locked up when we first tried to use it) were all very nice and helpful. 
All in all, I would come back to this hotel, because of the great location and clean, spacious rooms, which are most relevant to a comfortable stay; Some of the front desk staff and clogging bath tub drains could use some fixing.

title: “Great location lovely hotel”
text:
This is a fantastic hotel for anyone who has never stayed in New York before or wants to be in the centre of everything. The hotel entrance is from Broadway with a lift up to the lobby, once in the lobby you dont event realise you are in the middle of Times Square and can hear no noise. The staff at the hotel are really helpful and we used the concierge a few times. We were also upgraded which was a really nice addition to our holiday. 
The room we had was on the 43 floor and had really fantastic views of times square and the skyline just what you want when you go to this city.
The room was very spacious, bed extremely comfortable with plenty of pillows and great flat screen tv with plenty of channels to watch in bed when you have been walking around all day.
There is also free tea and coffee making facilities and they will provide as much tea and coffee as you like if you just ask.
A nice touch on arrival was a pocket size map of New York handy rather than always getting the guide book out.
We really enjoyed our stay and would certaintly stay at Hilton Hotels again as we have always had a great experience.

title: “Excellent for a city trip”
text:
Stayed here with a friend 2 nights. Second time (stayed for 4 nights with my son last summer) and got an excellent room rate I would think because of the work going on in the hotel and construction in nearby street. Neither of these spoiled our trip though there were a few loud metallic noises early the first morning.
Location is perfect, being two minute walk to Broadway and 6th and right by Macys and other well known stores. Subway to other areas is right on the street corner. Easy walking distance to Rockerfeller Centre, Empire State and other downtown locations. Good eating places around the corner, Pax for excellent sandwiches and fresh salads and it's handy having a fridge in the room to store snacks and drinks. Duane Reade drug store on the corner of the street too.
As previously, staff were friendly and very helpful but I imagine it's how you treat them if you have a bad experience! Received a much appreciated and unexpected room upgrade. 
Breakfast is good but if you're looking for full service then this isn't for you. It's help yourself but a good selection of muffins, pastries, bagels, bread for toast, cream cheese and jams, yoghurt, and always a fresh fruit salad and bowl of fruit. Plenty of fresh tea and coffee and juices. Never had a problem finding anywhere to sit! 
Business centre has free access and good internet speed. Paper provided for printing off your boarding card or other documentation where other hotels charge for internet and printing. 
All in all you can't go wrong. The hotel is clean and the maid service excellent with clean towels daily. Most bathrooms in Manhattan hotels are small by the way! Plenty of hot water and good water pressure in the shower.
Highly recommended by a fussy traveller!

title: “Disappointing since I love the Joie de Vivre Hotels normally”
text: The fact that they say they have a fitness center is a joke. It's a couple machines in a cramped stinky room that was not built to be a gym (not ventilated correctly), which whatever, that's common. What made me mad was the hours-7am-9pm. Those are working hours! This hotel is near the financial district, how silly to assume we aren't up before that, and after that. Everyone broke the rules, but even if you'd sneak down at 6am, the gym was already packed because it is too small for the amount of rooms. The room was also cramped, not set up the most logically with walkways tight to cross the room. The bathroom had no space to put hairspray, face wash, etc up. I understand small space, but it just wasn't set up with usable shelves or anything, poor design and planning, just not a very feng shui area, I did not feel relaxed squeezing through and storing my stuff on the floor for a week. My co-worker told me her street facing room was horribly loud and she didn't sleep all week. The staff was gracious, wine hour was nice as always, but their facilities could use a good revamp, it just wasn't logical.

title: “Massive yet comfortable!”
text: Stayed here with my son and his team mates for a tournament. Very comfortable and fairly spacious rooms. Would definitely stay here again. Plenty of places to eat nearby, especially Plaza of Americas across the street which is connected to the Sheraton by a covered bridge, thus avoiding the merciless heat of Dallas!

title: “a charm of it's own”
text:
It's hard to write a review of a place you liked so much when you know that yes, she does have some flaws that the very fussy might have issues with. We just fell in love, warts and all.
The Majestic is on a quiet residential street in Lakeview a half block from Lake Shore Drive. We arrived by train, then bus, so had no questions or issues with parking. 
Even tho it's a very small hotel, there was always someone at the front desk and always very helpful with questions. At checkin we were given a map with dining options and we referred to that map several times during our short stay. 
The carpeting in the front hall was showing some wear, but it matched the Old World charm of this place so well, I certainly overlooked that. We thought the tiniest elevator in the world was more amusing than annoying. It was actually one of the slowest too, so we often took the stairs. 
The room was very clean and looked like the bathroom had been recently remodelled. Nice shampoo and lotion in a stand bolted to the wall. I like that, no waste. There was a wonderful large showerhead, now that's important to me. Bathrobes were a pleasant surprise too.
The window had no view but the fire escape and brick from next door, but we weren't there to look out the window. We were there to go and do and after a long day, this was a great retreat to come back to.
You know what's great when you're just relaxing, a snack. and these were the best mini bar prices I've ever seen anywhere. My husband grabbed a bag of cookies first thing we walked in the room and when I immediately snapped "don't start that", he handed me the menu and said "Why not? they're only a dollar"
We really enjoyed our night at this hotel. We sat on the bench out front at night and noone was around but the occasional dog walker. We made the short walk over to Lincoln Park in the morning and enjoyed even more serenity, just us and the lake. It's a short walk to restaurants, wine shops and Wrigley Field only a few blocks away. 
When we caught the express bus just around the corner and went downtown,where we usually stay, it was like going to another world. I don't think I've ever seen so many people(the Taste was going on). It made me realize that this time we made a good choice,yeah we'll be back..

title: “A relief in a city of disappointment”
text:
The hotel is one of the few buildings in the city that actually has some character. Formally the Four Seasons it is in a building that looks like an old finca, with red tiled floor and the sound of bird song around the entrance. The staff are very friendly and helpful, providing in-room gym equipment if needed! The room was VERY spacious for the $249 per night rate. (double room). The bathroom wasn't enormous but was enough. There is wireless web access in the rooms too for $9 (i think) per day.
Other people have mentioned the thin walls but i must have been lucky with my room as i didnt hear a thing (and i am a light sleeper)- so room 340 is a good choice if you need quiet!
In a city of tawdry excess and modern dull buildings, this hotel provided some much needed tradition and good service. 
I should add that i moved to this hotel after realising how hideous the residence inn was- who on earth stays in those places?!

title: “Small but very nice.”
text: The decor was nice, but there was not much space in the room or bathroom. Overall though, I liked the place. The staff was really polite and helpful. The location was really nice if you were in Seattle to shop. It's right in the middle of it all and only a 10 minute walk to Pikes. Even though it was a little small, I would stay there again.

title: “Probably really nice about 4 years ago”
text:
No problems at all. 
Epic location. Right in the heart of the theater district and very close to Times Square. Everything that is super touristy in NYC is walkable. 
The room was fine. Big enough for me. 
The bed was rather comfortable. Although it was very short. I am only 5'6" and my feet were hanging off of the end when I stretched out a bit. Sort of weird. 
Air conditioning was great. TV was great. Lots of channels to choose from. 
Shower was good pressure and plenty of hot water. 
Cracked tiles and mildew in the shower is always a bummer. 
The staff was great. Everyone at the front desk (especially Leo) was super helpful and always cheerful. No ice machines so they send it up to you. That always worked out well for me (within 10 minutes). 
Not really any problems, I can just tell that it is aging a bit. 
Internet was mediocre.

title: “A nice hotel but service lets it down”
text: I spent 5 nights here recently on business. I would rate it as a good but not great business hotel. The hotel itself is nice enough but it falls short in some key areas. The main failing is some of the service staff. The person at check-in was very friendly but when I went to the front desk to ask a simple question later in the day, it was as if I was bothering them to have to speak with me. On two separate occasions I had the Privacy Please sign on the door and yet staff still rang the doorbell. On another occasion when I didn't have the sign on the door, a staff member simply rang the bell and opened the door all in the same motion. Thankfully I was only working on my computer at the time but this is not acceptable. Another irritation was that the in-room telephone had a Guest Service Hotline button but each time I tried to use it, it transferred me to the restaurant who then told me to dial a different number. There was a conference taking place during some of my stay and at certain times the elevators could not handle the load and I had to wait an unreasonably long time for an elevator. You have to pay for WiFi but it is VERY slow. These service short comings are a pity because it is a nice hotel in a good location.

title: “The Elegance of the Mansion”
text:
We stayed the first two nights of our honeymoon in the Mansion and every part of it was magnificent! Our late arrival the night on the wedding did not stop excellent service and friendliness. The bellman even offered to take a picture of us "crossing the threshold" - a memory we can keep forever. We never had to wait for service and they
helped with every detail in a friendly and professional manner.
Our room was outstanding. Spacious and perfectly clean. The thing that sets the Mansion apart in my mind is the attention to detail. I felt like I was at home because of the comfort and ammenities, but it
was definitely a retreat into luxury. The bed and pillows were very comfortable and the bathroom was roomy and well-supplied. Our room had several windows that overlooked the beautiful front courtyard of the hotel. And even though we were in the middle of Dallas, the hotel's location just off of the major road allows it to be quiet and peaceful.
And the food - WOW! As if the luxury of the hotel isn't enough. Our breakfast the next morning was some of the best food I've ever tasted. I definitely recommend the French Toast. The fruit was beautiful and fresh. And we couldn't leave witout trying the Mansion's famous Tortilla Soup. It sounds strange, but it's delicious
and a real Texas treat.
If given the chance, we would do this all over again, and I have no doubt that it would be just as good the second time around.

title: “Great value for the price.”
text: Really enjoyed this small but very well placed motel. Room was a little small but very clean. A few driving minutes to nearly attractions. The owners are really nice & helpfull. Good little continental breakfast included & free parking. Why spend too much this is a great place, Highly recommended. Fridge in room.

title: “very handy hotel, great location”
text:
My wife and i have just returned from a 5 night stay at the grand union and had a very pleasent stay. I booked the room direct with hotel via email, i feel i got a good price and everything was in order when we arrived to check in. You pay when you check in not out, i dont know if this is standard practice in the US but we were fine with this. I did see other guests who were a bit wary if this.
The room was a good size and was clean and tidy, the bathroom was spotless. Decor was a bit out of date we weren't there to study the inside of the room so it was fine. The bed was comfy. There was also a tv and fridge. Rooms dont have safe deposit boxes so if you paranoid leave the family jewels and wads of cash at home. Although we had no reason to suspect the hotel was insecure.
There are no food facilites but the hotel joins to a great diner next door, which serves great breakfasts, ideal to fill you up for a days sight seeing.
Hotel has internet access for guests who need it.
Staff were helpful when we needed them.
NYC itself is like nowhere else we have ever been, soo many things to see and do i could go on forever. We did the whole sightseeing thing for which the hotels location was excellent, less than 5 minutes to the empire state building, 15 to times square and 10 to penn station (subway to just about anywhere you would want to go)
Overall i would recommend this hotel to tourists who are going to be out and need to good base to go back to each night. Location could not be any better. Great value for money. Would definitly stay here again.
Finally my tip for new york.. if you want to do the statue of liberty, book it online and get up early enough to be on the first boat its well worth saving yourslef the queues.

title: “Pleasant Hotel in a convienient location, shame about the down and outs.”
text:
The Phoenix Park Hotel is in a great location, just accross the road from Union Station (both the metro and long distance trains go from there) and within walking distance of the Captiol. I stayed there with my mother for 5 nights in August 2007 and the minute we arrived there was a porter waiting for us ready to collect our luggage and take us up to our room. As we were going up in the lift he was more than happy to tell us about the facilities the hotel had to offer, which include a gym & a computer room for those without a laptop, though it is rather expensive to use one (40 cents a minute).
The room (a two bed room) was very spacious and decorated in a very traditional style. 
There were a couple of hiccups, including waiting for 20 minutes for the bill after eating lunch on the first day, our waitress seemed to have disapeared and other staff ignored us. On the first night you could hear people sitting in the bar outside, when we asked to move to a room at the back of the hotel they told us they didnt have any, however we were not disturbed again.
The last problem was not through any fault of the hotel, but if you are considering coming with small children then you might have to think again, as the pavement/sidewalk and adjoining wall from the hotel up to Union Staion, were home to many down and outs, some of whom were begging for money, even living in a big city like London, this was a new expereince for me, and not a pleasant one.

title: “Convenient location for a convention”
text: We spent 4 nights at this hotel for a recent convention. The location to the convention center is great. It is only about a 5 minute walk from the convention center. The pool area was very nice and even on crowded days, we were able to get a lounge chair by the pool. We dined at the Garden Cafe, which is on the 2nd floor, one time for breakfast. We had the buffet, which was a little pricey (about 17 dollars a person) but nice. The concierge was helpful and we used him/her a lot to ask about local restaurants and night spots. He/she helped us numerous times with making reservations for up to 18 people at a time. Our room was standard for other Marriotts we have stayed in. It was generally "clean" for hotel standards. One nice feature was the laundry room on the 4th floor that is complimentary. Of course, you have to purchase laundry soap, etc. but it was nice to be able to throw in a load of swimsuits, etc. without having to pay dry cleaning services at the hotel or take home wet suits. The beds were very comfortable and our particular room on the 19th floor was generally quiet. I don't know if I'd consider the hotel excellent or outstanding, but it was nice and you really can't go "wrong". We would stay there again.

title: “Elegant spot to stay especially for seniors”
text:
Quiet, comfortable and well furnished. On Park Ave. in the upper '30's Murray Hil district, across from a pretty church and 2 blocks south from Grand Central Station. One block east of JP Morgan library/Museum (a gem) and 2 blocks east of Lord and Taylors, so culture lovers and shopping lovers are happy.. 
Dining room is on the expensive side, so we ate at Scandinavia House next door, a fun place with good foodm moderate prices and a museum upstairs.

title: “Great hotel”
text: View of times square from the dining area, looked out onto 7th Ave. from our room. The rooms were clean and very nice, renovated a few years ago. Charges for wifi, but most hotels do.I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Nice place overall”
text:
Stayed here with a friend last weekend and we were overall very pleased with it. It was actually nicer than I expected it to be. I believe the hotel was refurbed in 2008 and it has been well maintained.
Checkin - We checked in around 6pm on Saturday night. The hotel staff was extremely pleasant.
Room - We were given a top level, double room facing the airport (although view is actually of the other hotels nearby.) It was very spacious, large entry way and plenty of floor space. Didn't care for the door to the bathroom - it's more like a closet door, does not lock and there is no sense of privacy if needed.
We could not access the free in-room wi-fi that was advertised both online and on the in-room documentation. There is however a modem in the room and being the geeks that we are, we had a router and some extra cables for multi-user access. Once we figured out that the bottom plug from the wall outlet was not working, we were able to get things wired and functioning for a little mindless surfing.
We were here during the Republic of Texas biker rally, so we heard motocycles all night long. It was pretty loud and I had trouble sleeping when the ac wasn't drowning them out. Once the choppers quieted down, the airplane noise took over. Calgon, take me away!
Business Center - Amounted to nothing more than a PC and very basic printer. We needed to print something and fought with the printer for a little while. Finally figured out that it was not allowing multiple copies of anything to be printed. If you sent it to the printer one at a time, it printed without hesitation. This was only frustrating because the front desk person was watching us the whole time and never offered up any assistance as we messed with the paper tray, etc.
Breakfast - Pretty basic stuff here, with Texas waffles, fresh fruit, yogurt, microwavable hot links, cereal, etc. It was enough to satisfy our hunger before heading down to San Marcos for a day of shopping.
Location - This location is, of course, near the airport. It is also not far off of the 45/130 Toll road. Highly recommend the nice, quiet toll road over the hassle and stress of I-35, especially if you will be traveling during peak times. Also, it's a quick drive to Barton Square Mall and that general area.
Overall we were pleased with the hotel; if I were to stay again, I would be turning the ac down lower in hopes of sleeping through the road and airport noise.

title: “Memorial Day Weekend”
text:
This hotel was excellent. The front desk girls went out of there way to ensure that our party had a great time. Great free breakfast, good rooms, great location, good rates... 
The only negatives were the empty room next to us had the worlds loudest alarm clock that would go off at 5am each day until we called the front desk to have them send someone up to turn it off & the hotel running out of diet soda.

title: “Stay away from the freeway side”
text:
Located in the business district. If you are staying in that area this is a great place.
Make sure you get a room not facing I-5. Even with windows closed it is still very noisy. 
Being a business hotel the Concierge lounge was not open over the weekend. So you lose out on food and beverages.
If you are looking to stay near the tourist area I would stay at the M. Waterfront.

title: “Nothing Impressive”
text:
While my recent stay was okay...it seemed to be run of the mill Staybridge. Nothing to brag about...
That's too bad, because I did have a complaint. The wireless service was terrible. Slow and unresponsive. I know I wasn't the only person to complain. I heard other guest with similar issues.
This is really too bad. It can make or break a stay when you are on business.

title: “Great hotel, great service, great location”
text:
I stayed at the Courtyard Mag Mile on Ontario St. June 24-27 2010 and was really impressed.
I was originally on the 15th floor but upon looking at the room, called the front desk, and asked for a higher floor. She immediately gave me a room on the 19th floor and sent up the room cards with a bell man to save me a trip back down to the desk. That room was nice and quiet. Yes, there was some noise, but I totally expected it. With the windows closed, and the drapes closed. I didn't hear much, and I'm a light sleeper. 
Unfailing, I had the door held open for me, I was immediately greeted with a smile whenever I encountered any of the hotel staff, and the staff tried to please whenever they could.
There are restaurants galore and the hotel is a short walk to N Michigan where there are city buses that connect to the CTA subway system. 
The lake is but a short walk east where there is a beach and bikeway.
Kudos to the staff of the Courtyard which made my Chicago stay so enjoyable.

title: “Brilliant !!”
text:
We stayed here in room 1500 from September 22-28 on vacation from England. I'm afraid I do not have anything very original to say except that we had a great time! We arrived on the evening of the "manager's meeting with guests". It was good for the manager's to be "visible" and most helpful to be able to chat with them. 
A few "non hotel" tips which other guests may find helpful-
* Always book your Alcatraz trip in advance
* If you are in town for any length of time buy a MUNI travel pass.
* A matter of taste of course, but think it is better to stayhere rather than Fisherman's Wharf - more central for everything.
* Suggestions for eating - "Loris" for breakfast which is just nearby. "Mortons" for steak-it is just around the corner.
As a lot of other contributors have mentioned the main difference with this hotel - it is the "customer service" ethos of the staff, We found everyone helpful and friendly, especially the bar staff.
I think this service level is epitomised by Wes Tyler himself.
I contacted him prior to arrival as it was a special trip for my girl friend's 50th birthday. On arrival there was a gift in our room along with a voucher for the restaurant - how thoughtful.
Wes also helped us with "tourist information" before our arrival. Fortunately we got the chance to meet him and thank him in person. I am sure if you let him have any requests before you arrive he will do his best to help.
All in all we had a great time and delighted we consulted Trip Advisor and selected this hotel. We would say you definitely get what you pay for - and then some!!
As a general point, I am very surprised that other hotels do not respond to customer feedback in the way the Chancellor does - it seems a strange omission to me in a service environment.
Once again, thanks to Wes and his staff for a great stay in San Francisco.

title: “Don at the front desk made me feel very welcome!!”
text: Outstanding hotel with great customer service. I will stay here on all future visits to the Indy area.

title: “Excellent Service , great location”
text: We stayed in a family room for four and was very impressed with all aspects of this hotel -the reception had a wonderful smell every time you walked through - the lifts were sometimes a pain but the rooms were well equipped and clean - the location was perfect for sightseeing both by foot or by subway -the staff were incredibly helpful ,even booked our Phillies tickets and hand delivered them to our room - nothing was too much trouble - I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Nice Getaway”
text: We stay here a few times every every year as a couples getaway. The first floor dining and bar area are quite comfortable. The rooms are modest in size, but the view is fantastic. We highly recommend the spa. The spa staff is great and we feel fantastic when we are done.
