title: “Great Experience - Will Be Back!”
text:
My daughter and I stayed here for a long weekend - can't say enough
good about the facility and the staff. Large enough room had 2 comfortable
double beds, adequate bathroom, complimentary bottles of water, relaxing
decor. The breakfast/lounge room was large and comfortable, plenty of
newspapers and a computer that was almost always available. Great
iced tea at all hours - very refreshing after coming in from the 90+
degree heat!! Evening wine and cheese was perfect to tide us over
before a show and late dinner. But best of all were the polite and
helpful desk clerks - they made tour bus arrangements, restaurant
recommendations, gave maps and detailed directions all in a great
good humor and with the most helpful attitude. Would recommend
the Casablanca in a heartbeat to anyone heading to NYC.

title: “Office Tower/Hotel”
text: I just couldnt feel the hotel office building concpet, not for me. Service eas not bad but nothing exceptional.I saw a great location review, I would disagree as I found the heart of the district in driving distance not walking.

title: “Fantastic Location”
text:
We have just returned from a 5 night stay at the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square and as other reviewers have mentioned its in a great location just one block from Times Square
Best Bits
Walking distance from Rockefeller Centre, Central Park, Bloomingdales, most of the theatres & 5th Avenue - Saks etc.
Staff: Very polite and friendly - Abigale on reception very kindly recommended a restaurant and obtained us a copy of the menu & if he's working try and guess the age of Donald the bell man!
Room: Beds are very comfortable and the in room fridge and microwave are a nice touch, the rooms all have flat screen HDTV’s and the rooms were clean and tidy 
Restaurant: The Pigalle is really handy for breakfasts and dinner, reasonably priced and very hand if you have just landed and are after dinner without venturing too far.
Bad Bits
Room: Only a minor point, if you have the room next to the main air-con vent near the ice machine (we did) it does tend to make a racket but eventually you may get used to it.
The Loft Lounge: Bit weird this, we couldn’t find it!! Nor did we really ask for it, but it’s detailed on the Hilton website you may need to do a bit of exploring to find it!
Overall we really enjoyed our stay at the HGI and would recommend this hotel.

title: “Perfect location, Great Staff”
text: My wife and I stayed at 6 Columbus on 8/4 for the Coldplay concert in NJ. We picked 6 Columbus for the location and due to our history of staying at other sister properties. It's a great location for shopping, restaurants, Central Park, access to public transportation and not far from the Henry Hudson Parkway if you are driving in. We booked a room with a king bed, but while checking in, the front desk told us we were upgraded to the Penthouse! This was completely unexpected and let me say the suite was amazing. 3 balconies with 2 overlooking Central Park. It was a loft style setup with the 'bedroom' on the upper level. The room was very clean and the amenties were impressive...several large flat screens, kitchen and an awesome master bath which included a huge walk in steam shower. The front desk staff and bell men were very friendly and remembered our names hroughout the stay. The bartender at the adjacent Blue Ribbon restaurant was great and so was the sushi. Overall our stay was great. We even debated about enjoying the suite versus going to the concert. I highly recommend this hotel and I continue to be a Thompson Hotel fan/customer.

title: “A Quiet Oasis”
text: Even though we live in the East Bay, we like to play tourist in San Francisco. Discovered The Omni while participating in the annual "Dine About Town" this past January. From the moment we walked in the door, we were transported to another era. Loved walking EVERYWHERE...Ferry Building (and the Saturday Farmer's Market), Red's Java Hut, a walk to SBC Park, SOMA, The Irish Bank, ending a full day at Bimbo's 365 Club for a fabulous concert, and of course a walk back "home". Have and will continue to recommend The Omni to everyone!!!!

title: “Nice for a middle of city hotel”
text:
I avoid these large, tip for everything,hotels in big cities but I was there for a conference and the hotel was very nice. It was convenient to metro rail, lots of great restaurants and shopping around. Easy to get around and short walk to Pike's Market. 
The Westin White Tea fragrance in the bathroom products was a nice plus. 
It was fine, expensive but typical for a large city, conference center. 
Nice experience!!

title: “Expensive, but refined”
text: I stayed at this property for two nights recently on a business trip and was impressed with the level of refinement. The staff were courteous, attentive and knowledgeable - a rare feat it seems these days. The rooms elegant, simple, luxurious and quite comfortable. I agree that the rooms are pricey, but this hotel is a great choice for business travelers.

title: “6 phone calls to get a cab.”
text: nice hotel but could not get them to schedule a minivan cab to drive us 2.5 miles. they wanted me to take 2 cabs for 5 people. they were trying to force me to call a private car service. i am not stupid, and i can tell when someone is getting kickbacks. i expect this bs in a small city, but in Seattle? really? watch out for the staff

title: “Great Value if Travelling with Family and want Upper West Side Base”
text: Prior Reviews are very accurate. We booked a suite for one-night for $300. We have a 6 and 8 year old and like to have 2 rooms when travelling, if possible. Also, since we were only going one night, it was nice to be able to park once (on the street for free!) while being able to walk to the Natural History and Metropolitan Museums plus have close access to Central Park. The hotel has a nice lobby, a sitting area, free computer access, and free hot apple cider, and a small exercise room. The elevators are slow. The rooms are spacious though the decor is circa 1970s. The rooms had 2 TVs, full cable, a VHS and a DVD player,a small kitchenette. The bathroom was large. A prior review mentioned a wobbly shower door. We also encountered the same thing. You would think this is something that the hotel could improve at a minor expense. In all, the hotel was clean and the staff were helpful, but it's clearly not the Ritz Carlton and so long as you don't enter with unreasonable expectations, you will be very satisfied. We also did not care about decor because we liked the large rooms and really liked the neighborhood. You actually feel like you are a resident of the city more than a tourist. There is a world of difference between the Upper West Side and being in Times square, which is where many of the tourist hotels are located. This area is quiet with lots of great restaurants, playgrounds, shopping all nearby. The museums were not too crowded and at least with our kids, I really try and plan ahead which sections to see. At the Met, we saw the Roman & Greek sculptures, Egypt, and the Armor. At the Natural History, we stuck to the dinosaurs, evolution of man (my favorite) and gems. Otherwise, it is just too overwhelming. Some might feel that if you pay the suggested admission, you feel obligated to see everything. We chose to pay 1/2 the suggested amount, feeling justified given that we knew we were only going to be in the museums for 1-2 hours. Finally, we wanted to go the Central Park Zoo, but the kids complained that it was too cold so we passed. Finally, if I was just with my wife, I would have stayed more luxuriously than the Milburn and if we wanted to see/do things downtown with kids, I would have chosen the Embassy Suites. But for our needs, Milburn was the right choice.

title: “Central Location for our Stay in LA”
text:
My daughter and I spent 8 nights at this hotel. The location was great for us. Check-in was a breeze, and our room was spacious enough for the two of us. Unfortunately it faced Sunset Boulevard, which carries a substantial amount of traffic. After a few nights we moved to a room across the hall, which was much quieter. We had a nice stay here and I would have given them a higher review except for one thing - we had no internet service in our room. At first we were told it was because we have Macs. Come on people - Apple products will find wifi before you can even blink! We were in room 322 initially and then changed to 321 in the hopes of getting wifi. We got a quieter room but no internet service. I am surprised that no other reviewers have complained about this. In the second room my daughter was finally able to connect her MacBook to the internet via an ethernet cable. (Same cable did not work in the first room.) I had to sit in the lobby with my iPad when I wanted to get on the internet. For a one or two night stay, it would have been no big deal. But for eight nights it became more than an inconvenience. I will also point out that the wifi is unsecured - no password is needed to login so be careful when you use the internet there.
I also wish that they had a workout room at this location. The other Comfort Inns we stayed in on this trip had them, and I certainly could have used it for this many days. Other than that we enjoyed our stay here. The breakfast area was nicely maintained and there was a nice variety of items available, which we appreciated with our long stay. As others have mentioned, there are only a few tables so we did end up taking the food back to our room a few times. I would definitely consider staying here again when I come back to visit my daughter.

title: “Business stay”
text: The hotel is very clean, close to downtown, good price and good service. I was there three times for work.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location, Great Price”
text: We came to Philly to see the Barnes collection and found that its location was great for not only that but for almost everything else we did that weekend. The beds were so comfortable for my 7 year old that she slept in and extra hour on Sunday. Every staff member was extremely helpful and my kids really enjoyed our stay too!

title: “Lovely Hotel”
text:
I really enjoyed my stay at GPH. It is lovely and comfortable. The rooms are small but well appointed. 
The $16 per day charge for interent access is certainly a thing of the past with free access most anywhere. 
Having access to the private Gramercy Park is is wonderful. It is an oasis in the city.

title: “Great location, spotlessly clean but overpriced”
text:
Great location in heart of times square and a really clean hotel, towels changed sometimes twice a day which was a bit overkill, however, we had a cosy classic room which was way too small.
We asked to be upgraded but the staff didn't have the courtesy to get back to us on the upgrade despite us asking twice.
The double bed was barely a double and we struggled to fit in as an averaged sized couple, couldn't open the windows as the smells from next doors italian restaurant were too much and the noise from the fan outside our window to kill the smells kept us awake at night!
Added onto our final bill was over $300 of taxes which really made this an expensive stay. So, no I'm not sure I would recommend this hotel amongst all the other choices available.

title: “King of the World”
text:
The greatest city on earth and one of the best hotels in the world. In other words - hard to beat.. You really feel like you are the King of the World for a few days.
We have stayed here 7-8 times and I still get a kick out of walking through the soaring IM Pei-designed lobby each and every time we enter/leave the building. Love it.
My favourite thing is probably sitting down for breakfast in "The Garden" early in the morning when it's still almost empty. Eating, reading the NY Times and watching the hotel and the city waking up. Great service, great atmosphere, great food.
But I like almost everything about the hotel - the rooms, the Spa, the service, the design and the overall atmosphere.
The evenings is kind of slow in the area next to the hotel which is basically the only negative argument I could think of. Yes of course it would be nice if the room rates were lower, but this is the FS New York and you can't do anything about the rates.

title: “Great stay during SXSW”
text: I've stayed here the past two years during SXSW Interactive. The hotel is about a 10 minute walk to the Convention Center or a 2 minute ride in the hotel shuttle van. Each time we wanted to go in the van there was always someone available to drive us (we could also call from the convention center to get a ride back). The central atrium of the hotel was great for meeting with colleagues to plan our day or prepare a talk. Evening social hour and made-to-order breakfast also make this a great place to stay. The hotel is located at the end of the Congress Street bridge so it's always a plus to see the bats come out at dusk.

title: “Great location; still alot of walking”
text: We arrived way before check in and they got us our rooms straight away! 2 double beds for two of us. They did upgrade us on the second room to a small suite, where three people had a king and a pull out large sofa bed. Great again. Staff was very helpful on several occasions dealing with storing luggage after check out. Clean place. The wine reception was wonderful treat, dont miss that. IT is a bit pricey but for the money in that area it was ok.

title: “Great hotel”
text: We stayed at the Country Inn when our flight was cancelled. What a nice surprise. Very clean rooms, friendly staff, free airport shuttle, free Wifi, free computer. Within walking distance to a couple resturants. I would stay here again. If you are wanting to stay in a hotel with a pool, I might choose another. The pool is very tiny.

title: “Old world charm with up to date facilities”
text: Really enjoyed my stay! Rooms are a bit small but very adequate. Super comfortable beds!

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text:
Stayed at the Sofitel for three nights, what can i say thats not already been said, wonderful hotel, great location and hugh rooms. Been to New York several times and this is by far the best hotel we've stayed in. Booked a suite which was hugh with a seperate sitting area, large bathroom and a bed thats really confortable.
Staff where really friendly and concierge sorted us out a great resteraunt.
Next time we go to New York, this is where we will be staying.

title: “This was our second visit to this hotel -- we love it!”
text: Great hotel -- friendly and helpful staff, nice clean, modern rooms. Great location close to shopping, movies and restaurants.

title: “Top Notch!”
text:
What a find! You really should stay here!
Our stay at this hotel was quality. Our room was huge, incorporating a small kitchen, dining table, sofa, closet, very comfy bed and good sized bathroom. We did have a little trouble with our toilet not flushing properly but the Front Desk staff were very helpful with this.
I can not believe the price I paid, it was a real bargain.
The complimentary breakfast gave lots of variety including waffles, fruit, yoghurts, juice, muffins, bagels...
Another good thing is the location. Although Downtown DC has a lot to offer in the daytime, I think it is somewhat short in shops and places to eat at night. This 29th Street location in Georgetown means that you only need to walk a few blocks and you and right in the middle of DC's best nightspot.
It took us about 15-20 mins to walk to the Lincoln Memorial from the hotel, but you can catch a bus from just a few blocks away to a connecting Metro station if you require. A cross-town cab from Georgetown to Greyhound bus station (near Union Station) only set us back about $15.
You really have to stay here, its almost too good to be true.

title: “Hotel Sax chicago”
text: Recently stayed for a business trip. Loved the hotel. Very unique. Beds very comfy and clean. This is my second stay for this hotel. NO free wi-fi however.

title: “Excellent service, knowledgable staff”
text: This was my first time to San Diego. I was there for a conference. I was alone and the staff was so very nice to me in many respects. They had a shuttle to bring me to and from the airport at no charge. They gave me directions and maps to the trolley and the conference center, they helped me with places to eat and even helped me get to the zoo on the city bus!! The hotel was very nice with excellent beds and plenty of room. It was quiet and clean. I was very happy with my stay. The only drawback was, it is a far walk to the conference center but the trolley stop is right around the corner and it gets you there quickly for $5 all day pass.

title: “Poor management”
text: If I could give this place 0 stars I would. I and a few others stayed at this establishment for a weekend. I clearly want to express my disappointment. The front desk, assistant manager, and other staff members including the general manager are racist and discriminate carefully. Before entering the room we were discriminated and treated with no respect. After having issues at the front desk we received a phone call from the front asking “we just saw a 2 people come in are they in your suite?” At that point I had enough and questioned the caller “are you making assumptions that they are with us? Why don’t you call every suite and ask the same question?” The assistant manager who called clearly said “I assume they are with you.” After a few minutes I discovered the individuals who had came in were in fact African American so she “assumed” they were with me. I must say I’m very disappointed in management. I called to speak to the general manager a few days later and only received a negative tone and the constant question “what are you trying to get out of this? I would assume the same thing if it was a group of people!”

title: “Exceptional Stay....”
text:
We used the Fairfield East for our family to stay from Alaska and New Jersey, to attend our Aunt's 80th birthday party. I blocked 10 rooms with Debbie Matthews and from day one we were given the most outstanding service and consideration.
Our rooms were located on the 2nd and 3rd floors facing the Marriott parking lot. Not much of a view, but I think the other side was worse. Some of us checked in on thursday -the rest on friday. Some stayed 3 nights- some one week. Regardless of length we were given the negotiated rate which was only quoted for friday to monday. The rooms themselves were clean. The only complaint I can give on the room is the air cond/heater. It blows directly on the person in the bed closest to it and is VERY loud. Had to turn up the TV everytime it came on. The free internet was great- hooked up my laptop and surfed all weekend in my room. Of course you could still go downstairs and use the area with their computers and printers. The bath tub was a little weird- didnt really feel secure in my footing- tub had a curving to it, so be careful.
They didnt have any meeting rooms at this facility, so they allowed us to use the lobby area to kind of hang out as a family, that was awesome. The kids LOVED the pool. Too much chlorine for me, as soon as you walk into the area it burns your eyes..not good. Everyone that used the pool and the whirlpool enjoyed it.
I found the breakfast options accommodating for our needs, there is a Bob Evans right behind the hotel if you desire more. There was also a fast food chain at the corner - cant remember what is was - I think it was Burger King- didnt use it.
I found staff VERY professional and friendly - from the front desk to maintenance. Erin, Natalie (front Desk) and Dawn (maintenance) made me feel very comfortable and always had a smile. They each took the time to hold a conversation and were always extremely pleasant.
I would stay there again.

title: “Nice hotel, get a room away from the construction site!”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights over Memorial Day weekend and into the following week. Stayed in a king bed room on the 9th floor.
The room itself was really nice. Large flat screen tv on the wall with HD channels, very comfortable king size bed (which has others have pointed out is extremely high), fridge with some room to store a few things, and a nice but very small bathroom (but really, how long do you spend in there?). 
Great location, minutes walk to Union Station, short walk to the Capitol, takes about 25-30 minutes to walk into the city center where all the shops/restaurants are, but you can easily take the metro from Union Station. 
Wireless internet is promised, but in the room we had the signal was not strong enough to connect. Used the ethernet connection supplied and it worked fine.
The biggest problem we had with this hotel was the noise from the construction site next door. They did not work over Memorial Day weekend, but come Tuesday and Wednesday morning they began very early - we were woken up with loud beeping noises at 5:20am on the Tuesday, and not long after that on Wednesday. Make sure you get a room that does not face the construction noise! Ridiculously early to begin work, particularly with a hotel right next door.
Apart from the noise this was a really nice hotel, the room was small but lovely, and the location was great. If you can get a room that did not have the noise problem then i would highly recommend this hotel. Otherwise if you value sleep and do not appreciate being woken up by construction noise at 5:30am then look elsewhere.

title: “Great 1930s gem”
text: I was able to make a reservation with little notice and the owner stayed up till late in the evening for us to arrive and was very helpful and friendly, even upgrading our room. It was perfect as a romantic getaway, a little gem set by the sea and away from the hustle and bustle of the main city. It felt like we were transported back to art deco days and added to the atmosphere. We'd happily come here again.

title: “wonderful location”
text:
Great location for this hotel.
Some detail could be a bit "seasoned" but the accomation is very clean and comfortable.

title: “A fabulous hotel that enhanced our stay in Chicago by 100%”
text: We travelled from the UK to stay at the Affinia Chicago at the beginning of May, and before we travelled we knew nothing about the hotel. It turned out to be fabulous - clean, modern, well-furnished, thoroughly serviced, and in an excellent location for shops, Magnificent Mile, the lake, tours, buses and trains. The staff of the hotel were really great, and nothing was too much trouble for them. Everyone smiled, whether they were bar staff, waiters, reception staff or room maids. Especially helpful were the staff on reception - I can't remember all of them, but certainly Steve, Andre, Kara and Peter were great. Somehow they seemed to know our questions before we'd asked them, and knew exactly what we were looking for and pointed us in the right direction. Ray Palmer.

title: “Lovely retro motel, clean and fun, good location.”
text:
Prior to staying at the Pheonix in August 2005, I read reviews on this site that warned of nighttime noise and other problems. While the place is famed as a rock-n-roll hotel (and the earnestness of the staff's rocker "look" is a little funny/silly), we didn't find it too loud at all. However, it's not the kind of place you stay if you're in town for early business meetings. We stayed up half the night entertaining friends in our room, but we did not receive any complaints from our neighbors, nor were we at any time disturbed by them. 
I remember from years ago that the hotel bar here was very fashionable, cool, and fun, but this no longer seems to be the case - it was pretty much a dud, very dark, deserted, and too loud. 
But the pool and pool area were lovely, the staff were friendly, and the room - while certainly not luxe - was clean and comfortable. It could have been a little bigger, though, seeing as how we had a king-size bed. See the attached, very blurry picture for an idea of how pretty the courtyard looks at night.
The Tenderloin is wacky, for sure - NOT the cleanest or calmest of urban areas, but that, to me, is part of the experience. My boyfriend and I walked to and from the hotel after dark, but you may want to avoid doing this if homeless people cause you alarm. 
I would highly recommend the Pheonix for people travelling for fun with friends or partners.

title: “Comfortable Stay”
text: I was in town for my brother's funeral. I checked in late so I got up late. I had a coupon for a free buffet breakfast. However, I was sure I missed breakfast. To my surprize the buffet was still open. I got a great breakfast & the staff were so kind & helpful.

title: “Perfect Location for Family with Young Children”
text: We had a wonderful stay at the Marriott's Custom House in Boston. We traveled with our two-year old and it was so convenient having the small kitchen area to fix her snacks and meals. The location couldn't be better! Just steps from the Quincy Market and Aquarium. It was also great being so close to the Italian District. We loved this hotel and hope to stay there again soon! The staff was very friendly and the rooms were spacious and clean. Great vacation!

title: “Excellent Location”
text:
This was our 3rd time in nyc & definately the best hotel! We stayed in The Carlton on Madison & the Helmsley on east 42nd both of which were far more expensive but the Novotel is a better all-rounder. 
Location is the main reason we picked this hotel & we were not disappointed- times square & broadway are on the doorstep & all other attractions are easily accessable. 
We did not used the subway this time but opted for the sightseeing tourbus (around $50 each for 48 hours & well worth it!)
Room was very spacious for nyc & had a great view of the buildings around us. Also very clean & modern.
We used the gym twice which is open 24 hours, great views as you work out! Be sure to have a drink on the patio looking over to broadway & times sqaure- this was my fav part of the hotel!
Already planning our next trip to nyc & will definately stay in this hotel again!

title: “A Boutique Gem”
text:
I love nice boutique hotels when I travel, which is one reason I selected this one. I stayed here only one night - business. it was charming! The lobby was beautiful with its red walls and crystal chandeliers. I walked in to music of Ella Fitzgerald and Frank Sinatra - which I grew up with. It was delightful! Check-in was easy. All staff were very pleasant. 
Room was cozy and comfortable - not huge - but I dont need huge. I had a queen bed that was very comfortable. Room is beautifully decorated and clean. Lots of pillows on the bed - which I like - and large flat screen tv. Only thing missing was a coffeemaker, which I would have used. Bathroom had tub and shower and was very clean too. Electrical outlets for phone charging were sparse or not convenient, but that is common with older hotels. But I was able to find one. 
I got in around 7pm and had work to do so ordered room service. The meal was fabulous! Lobster bisque, sea bass over risotto, rolls and creme brulee'. Portions were very good. 
Rates were very good - I happened to get a special deal, perhaps because it was the week AFTER the super bowl. Location downtown was very convenient to my meeting that day and it was fun to see the area as I have never been to Indianapolis before. 
I would definitely go back here, especially if the special rates were offered. If I paid the regular rate, I would expect a coffeemaker in the room. 
I wasn't able to take advantage of the morning continental breakfast. Weather was cold so the concierge quickly got me a cab for a short ride to my meeting. He was very nice.

title: “lovely energy !”
text:
modern,cosy,stylish.... warm and friendly.
Rooms and restaurant are perfect...terrace wonderfull and warm even in cold weather.
the bed with one side to the wall...little bit difficult when you are over 20 years old ;-)

title: “boutique feel; friendly, personalized service”
text: I had a convention, and my husband decided to join me for a 3 night stay so we could do some fine dining while in Boston. What a lovely surprise the Colonnade turned out to be! The decor is understated, sort of mid century, but elegant. Spotlessly clean. The room was a little small, but very comfortable. The service was extraordinary. Everyone was so friendly and seemed genuienly interested in top notch customer service. We did not eat at the hotel's restaurant, but we did order room service for breakfast each day, and it was out of this world yummy (French omellette). The location is prime, close to everything, close to the T. I can't wait to go back!

title: “Nice hotel - a few problems”
text:
Overall this hotel was lovely, big spacious rooms, quite modern. nice gym and bar. Staff are very friendly and helpful! 
However, eating at the hotel was quite expensive, particularly room service! Also, the hotel was very quiet (as we were there in february) so the hotel closed the starbucks and turned off the escalators. We didnt mind the escalators too much but the starbucks was a big inconvenience as the hotel is located away from everything else so theres no where else to go for a morning coffee or breakfast!
Also, the fire alarm went off one night and we had to evacuate. Afterwards (even the next day) none of the staff could tell us what had happened or if there was even a real fire or if it was just a drill.
Overall i did like the hotel and im sure its a lovely place to stay in the summer!

title: “Has come down in the world...”
text:
When I stayed at this hotel for the same conference three years ago, everything was fine except for the lack of a swimming pool. This time the rooms had become dingy and worn and the cleanliness level was very low. There was dirt and scrap paper on the bathroom floor when I checked in. After my room had been made up on the second day, my dirty water glasses were still all over the room. My co-workers had similar stories. 
At break, catering provided cookies with hidden peanuts. You need to be upfront about the presence of major allergens.
We recommended to the conference sponsors that they find a new venue for next year.

title: “Fantastic Hotel with Really Helpful Staff”
text:
We found this hotel by calling the 1-800 number for Marriott when our other hotel turned out to be less than expected.
This Marriot hotel is very well located. It is right off the highway to get to downtown Dallas, and a short drive away from House of Blues (which was a great place to snag a late night dinner!).
The rooms, although not big, were clean and comfortable.
But, the reason I will definitely come back is the incredibly great staff at the front desk. They were all friendly and welcoming from the start, and were happy to help us with any questions we had. The hotel has detailed, printed directions for all the major attractions in Dallas, and the staff is happy to help you print off mapquest or googlemap directions to anywhere else you need to go.
The business center at the hotel was very handy and helpful -- with two computers and a printer. Every room is hooked up with WiFi as well. 
We were very satisfied with our stay and will definitely be back!

title: “Clean hotel in a great location”
text: The hotel is situated in a convenient location on the edge of Chinatown and accross the road from North Beach. Stayed here for one night and really wish I had stayed here for two nights rather than the other in Union Square. The hotel room was clean, quiet and comfortable. The staff friendly and helpful. The hotel is convenient for exploring both Chinatown and North Beach, with many delightful-looking restaurants and cafes nearby. Would strongly recommend this hotel for the surrrounding location. If you like good live music, make sure to get along to The Saloon bar across the road too.

title: “Great to be there”
text: The Westin Grand is nicely located at the beginning of Georgetown, with lots of choices for quality time. Room was great, everything you need, including a box with plugs for iPhone and BB. The only thing which is not nice is the fact that the hotel didn't discovered fresh air, here I quote an hotel tv channel advertising, meaning the windows are fixed. Otherwise the sleep quality is great! Very friendly with kids at all ages. Buffet breakfast is available only in weekends. For the working part of the week is a la carte and it's @ 28$... Better go to La Paine Quotidiene few streets further on M Street... Swimming pool is only for summer.

title: “Hotel run by teenagers for teenagers”
text: With over 30 years of business travel I found this hotel to be the worst hotel I have ever stayed. The reception staff has little or not trainging and the rooms are small and poorly designed. Noting is where it should be. This hotel put all of its money in the lobby and little or none in the rooms or in staff training..

title: “Definately not up to par”
text: A very average hotel.....kind of what you would expect at a decent Marriott. Pool was extremely small.....not enough lounge chairs to go around for the people laying out at the pool. Room was average at best, tiny bathroom, air conditioner squeaked the entire time. Best part about the room was the shower head pressure. MOST IMPORTANTLY!!!......you must valet park to the tune of $22/day. Unbelievable! In Phoenix!!! Every major resort in Phoenix/Scottsdale has free self parking, so make sure you factor that into your rate. Also, the cheap RitzCarlton chooses to charge $10 day for internet access. Come on guys, do you really have to nickle and dime us to death. Overall, there are far better places to stay for the same $$$, with significantly better amenities and ambiance.

title: “Great Value and Location in Chicago Loop”
text: Convenient location and good bang for the buck make this Kimpton Hotel a great choice for business or leisure stays in the Windy City.

title: “Yet Another Great Stay”
text: Just back from a four night stay in New York and or second stay in the Marriot Marquis again this hotel has come up trumps, the location is second to none step out of it and you are in the centre of Times Square which is just great. The room well we could not have asked for more it was a junior suite with a times square view on the 25th floor plenty of room and the bed a very large comfortable bed both my wife and I slept well all four nights which on a trip to New York is what you need as it is non stop the bars in the hotel are great and we went to the View restaurant for a drink and we were lucky to get a window seat watching the skyline of New York going slowly by, the staff in the hotel we very helpful right from the moment we checked in to the end of the hoilday they made it that bit more special, we have stayed at this hotel twice and will do again on our next trip to New York and when friends ask me were to stay in the City I will always tell them to go there, the only down side of this hotel is the fact you have to leave but I will be back.

title: “very impressed”
text: Just came back from a really nice stay at the Memphis Marriot. Very spacious, clean room and comfortable bed in the king tower. Easy check-in/out and friendly staff. Never used the pool but looks great from the pictures. Hotel is located on outer edge of the somewhat eerie empty business district but is located right next to the slow moving but cheap trolley line. (For only a dollar you can reach Beale Street.) Other than that though, there isn't too much to do for entertainment. The closest movie theater is a good 1/2 hour away by car and restaurants would require about 10-15 minutes of walking or trolley. Should have tried getting over to Tunica since close (by car), but ran out of time. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Pretty but not the best”
text:
I stayed in the KEY room and it was large and dated looking. Sheets unironed, musty smelling. A lot of noise from other guest doors and street noise from Broadway since windows are not soundproof. It is a cute old home and common areas are lovely, but bedding was hard and uncomfortable as well as pillows.
I would stay there again if I have to, but would not choose this property.

title: “Great Atmosphere and location”
text: We stayed at the W New York while my husband was interviewing for a position a few blocks away. The hotel is beautifully decorated with a very accommodating staff. We were there in the middle of the heat wave and they provided bottled water, fountain water, and apples to keep you going. This hotel's location is just a few blocks from hot spots like 30 Rock, NBC Studios, and my personal favorite, Magnolia Bakery. It is also very close to the subway which is very convenient. Our room was pretty small so if you are traveling with another person, I say upgrade so you have room to spread out a bit. Overall, an excellent experience!

title: “No tranquility at this Westin...”
text: Where to start?? Our suite wasn't available to us until 6:30pm. At 4pm they sent us out for a 30 minute wait which turned into 2.5 hours and left us hurriedly changing for our 5pm event in a temporary room down the hall. (They did offer us another better suite, but with no bed for our college aged daughter who was joining us.) It took 4 phone calls and a full day before the extra pillows were delivered. An all night party in a nearby room led a neighbor to scream at the top of his lungs at 3am. The coffee that we really needed was undrinkable due to a pot that didn't work properly. They did discount our room from $610 to $500, but given our experience, we won't be going back.

title: “Excellent location and very helpful staff”
text: This was our second stay at the Radisson Martinique. The location is excellent for families visiting NYC - whenever you want to go shopping (Macys 2 min away) or sightseeing. We were offered an upgrade to 17th. floor with some more space - and enjoyed it! The restaurant is worth while visiting - not only for breakfast. The staff were very helpful and could provide a good offer for taxi to the airport.

title: “Looks Can Be Deceiving”
text: Well, where do I start? If you want a place close to Fenway Park this is it. You can't beat a 5 minute walk to the ballpark. As for the rest, don't rely on their website pictures to make your choice. Pictures do tell a story but, not this one. This place looks like the diamond of Kenmore Square from outside but, once you find the entrance to the hotel you find that it's only cubic zirconia. You feel as if you stepped back in time. A long time.... The rooms are somewhat difficult to locate, the general condition of the entire hotel is not that great. The place is undergoing renovation (well needed) and hopefully once it's done things hopefully will be better. We likened our stay to be one step above camping. Our view was niether of Kenmore Square or Fenway, we had a beautiful view of the middle four innermost walls of the building. There were not enough electrical outlets and you could not plug the microwave and fridge in at the same time. Extension cords were in use to operate a table lamp and alarm clock and our TV had several broken buttons and several channels were nothing but snow. Our bed was the equivalent of plywood on springs and the bathroom really needed help. Like I said hopefully renovations will take care of these things but, it will take quite a bit to do so.

title: “nothing too special”
text:
Hmm - this one I don't really get. #2 in Chicago? Boutique hotel?
I stayed in the Palomar for 6 nights in October and had a one bedroom suite ($429/night - not quite cheap, right?) and based on the reviews and its website I'd expected something better. Wherever I looked this hotel was just ordinary, nothing special at all. I could not tell the difference between my room and a typical Hilton, Sheraton or the like. Not that anything was bad, but it was simply quite boring. If I had to choose again for a boutique hotel, I would pick the W chain. After the stay and a $3000 bill I felt somewhat cheated and I doubt I will return again.

title: “Great hotel and staff”
text:
Held two meeting here, one in August and the second one in Oct. Meet with Casey who handles the meeting arrangements. Everything was perfect on first request and second meeting two months later was set up exactly as requested with no additional communication necessary. She handles the events flawlessly!
The hotel is beautiful and clean. Staff is excellent to work with and very dependable. I own a small business in Greenwood and its the best location hands down to hold your next meeting or event!
Enjoy!

title: “Funky Modern Contempory hotel”
text:
This hotel was a very funky and modern hotel, which we loved staying in.....
We got to the hotel and was greeted by the gentlemen on the door which was opened for us every time we went in and out of the hotel which was fab
We checked in quick and the reception staff was very friendly and always happy to help, the reception area was funky too with the big chair.
We stayed in a superior king room on floor 6, the room was really modern and funky again and very spacious and was everything which we loved.... and had a big flat screen, massive bed and a nice sized bathroom, big closet and a fridge and snack which was a bit pricey and so was the room service menu but i am sure the food would have been great 
We stayed here 4 nights and we was so happy staying here..eveything was so close by....
We also tried the bar on the Saturday night which was busy and was really nice to go too. We only had a few cocktails which was nice.
i would recommend this hotel highly........its a very good hotel for somebody who is looking for a modern contempory hotel centrally located....

title: “Credit info stolen”
text: Upon my return I was noticed my credit info was stolen - I strongly believe this happend at this hotel. I would advise pay by cash.

title: “Great Hotel, Fantastic Staff, Fabulous Location”
text:
Just returned from a 5 night stay at Cassa and all I can say is great things, the location is perfect one block away from Times Sq and near all the main Manhattan attractions. The room was excellent and extremely large really nicely decorated with a huge comfy bed and great bathroom with huge shower.
The staff are simply excellent probably the best I have ever experienced, anything I wanted or asked for was taken care off in seconds. Eric and Stephanie just to single a few out are a big credit to this Hotel but really all the staff are friendly and helpful,Thankyou so much for looking after us and on my next trip to NYC there is only one place I want to stay Cassa!!
We stayed in room 2708 a great room!!
Many Thanks again the Halls!

title: “Had a wonderful long weekend at The Benjamin”
text: We stayed at the Benjamin for a business conference that my husband's company was sponsoring(April '07). We took our 2 children, as we are from NY and have close family up there. Our room at The Benjamin was amazing. We had a 1 bedroom and, with the way that real estate is in Manhattan, we can truly appreciate being able to spread out a bit with our kids. They had a large living room w/pull out sofa and my husband and I had our own bedroom. We also had a kitchenette with a full size fridge with a small dining area. The location, in midtown manhattan, is priceless. We would definitely love to return!

title: “Customer service”
text:
If you stay in these kinds of hotels, then little about this one will surprise you. The property has some cool features (glass elevator, for instance), and the rooms are good.
But what made my stay here really stand out was the customer service. A guy named Nate at the front desk was personable and funny and did everything he could to make me feel welcome and comfortable. He followed up on our conversation later by leaving a note and something to drink in my room. Thank Nate!

title: “Pleasant Stay”
text: Very nice hotel compared to the price paid. I really expected less of a hotel, however it was overall very nice. Rooms were small, but it will be good for 1-2 guest. We took alone 2 children, which made the room extra small. The full breakfast came in handy helped save some money for breakfast. Very good location and very nice hotel for the price. I would stay here again.

title: “Great experience!”
text:
I was very pleased with my stay at Ink 48.
To begin with, we were there for Canadian thanksgiving / Columbus day, which meant the hotel was very full. We got there quite late in the evening, and the category of room we had booked was sold out so we were upgraded to a suite. Upon arriving in the suite, there was a bottle of bubbly and a box of chocolates for the guest who had cancelled. When we called to advise them of the error, they told us we were welcome to have them at no charge. Quite a nice welcome!
The rooms are very nice and comfortable. Room service was good though a bit slow. The staff was very helpful and courteous. 
We went for drinks at the lobby bar, but did not have supper. The ambiance was nice, not too crowded. Unfortunately, the rooftop bar was reserved for events every night. This was a bit of a disappointment. 
An important point for me was that this hotel is very dog friendly. We traveled with our two small dogs, which they accepted at no extra charge. For any one who travels with their dogs, I highly recommend Ink 48. They provide food and water dishes and a doggy bed in the room. A large bowl of dog cookies is at the entrance to the lobby. All staff was very friendly to the dogs. This is an important distinction to make as some hotels accept dogs (or barely tolerate them) while others truly are dog friendly, as was the case with Ink 48.

title: “Dirty and old!!!!”
text:
We attempted to stay at the Renaissance in philly for a quick weekend trip to visit family and friends. We drove up from the DC area late on Friday. We were super tired as it was after 1a.m. when we arrived. We selected this hotel on the strength of the trip advisor reviews; so that's why it's important that I write an honest review. Please note that we were traveling with our 7month old.
I knew there were issues when standing outside of the hotel were people drinking and smoking. Talking fisting drinks in one hand smoking with the other---just tacky! No bell hop, at first no one at the front desk.
The hotel is very old and in need of a serious renovation. So once in our room I prepared to get the baby to bed first and transfer him to the bed. I always check the sheets and mattresses for concerns about cleanliness and signs of bed bugs. The sheets had hairs and were stained up. Very nasty I took pictures. My husband called the front desk and they transferred us to a new room supposedly an upgrade that included free breakfast. Again, I checked the sheets. Still dirty and we decided to leave and not stay. It was 3:00a.m.!!! They did cancel the reservation and are supposedly giving us rewards points for two free nights at any Marriott. We decided to stay at a nicer hotel in center city -- you get what you pay for!

title: “Excellent place to stay and great location”
text:
The hotel is very clean, nicely appointed and the rooms are pretty spacious for a "city" hotel.
The location is excellent and within walking to distance to Union Square, the mall and the trolly stops. The entire hotel staff was very friendly and very accomodating during the entire.
A great experience!

title: “Pretty Nice”
text:
After reading some of the reviews I was quite frankly, a little apprehensive to stay at this hotel, but I was pleasantly surprised. It turned out to be one of the best hotels we stayed at on a month long road trip, 
From the moment we pulled up the parking attendants were very helpful. Every staff member was very friendly and helpful. When we asked a question, if they didn't know the answer they immediately found someone who did. All of the staff seemed genuinely interested in pleasing the guests. This was probably the best service we have received at a hotel in the continental U.S. 
The hotel is walking distance to the U.S. Mint and Capitol, so you don't have to worry about driving and finding a parking spot. 
As priority club members we were given a free drink in the lounge, and a choice of a suite upgrade or free parking. We chose the suite upgrade because we felt we really needed the space, as the regular rooms are a bit small for families. Parking is $22. We felt platinum priority club members should have been given free parking also, as room upgrades are supposed to be given automatically to club members. 
It was nice that when we pulled up we were asked if we wanted a valet or preferred to handle our own bags. So many places will force a valet on you.
Key cards are required to access the elevators which made you feel safer.
Our 2 room suite was very spacious and had 1 1/2 bathrooms, 2 TV's, and a HUGE closet. It looked to be recently renovated and had nice touches like nightlights, lighted makeup mirrors, and clips to hold the curtains shut. We also had a nice city view. The only thing I didn't care for was the depth of the vanity. It was difficult to reach the sink.
We thought the restaurant prices were fairly reasonable for a downtown hotel. Selections were a little limited, but everything was VERY delicious!!! They really ought to add a kid's menu though. Most Holiday Inn owned hotels allow kids to eat free from the kid's menu. 
Lobby restrooms were first rate, with real cloth handtowels and free toiletries. 
Unfortunately, we didn't get to try the rooftop pool as it was raining during our stay. 
Would definetly recommend and will stay here again when in Denver.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Hampton Inn and Suites are usually very predictable for a good, clean stay and this was no exception. There was nothing over the top wonderful, just a predictably good experience very convenient to the Houston Texans stadium, Rice University, and the Medical District of Houston. Will definitely stay here again if I'm in the area.

title: “Highly Recommend the Hotel Commonwealth!”
text:
We traveled to Boston for a family member's wedding and the reception was being held at the Hotel Commonwealth. After careful consideration, we booked a room at the Commonwealth and we are very glad that we did! It was an excellent hotel. 
We arrived after having been traveling literally all day and we were exhausted. From the moment we stepped out of our sedan from the airport, the doorman assisted us immidiately and made us feel very welcome. Check in went fairly smoothly although they told us the rate was $20 more per night than what they had told us when we originally booked the room. That aside, everything went very well. The bell hop took the bags up to the room immidiately which was very much appreciated. 
The rooms are very large and spacious --you definitely will not feel as though you are sitting on top of each other. I know one of the other reviews stated that the furnishings try to "look antique but fail" and while yes, I do see what they meant, it is really a non issue in my opinion. The room was immaculate and the furniture seemed sturdy and it did compliment the room well. The beds are hands down, the best beds I've ever slept on at a hotel, coming in even above the Four Seasons. The sheets were very soft and they didn't have a "cold" hotel feel at all. The matress and pillows were fabulous. If you are one who likes a firm matress and/or pillow, you may not find it as comfortable as I did so that is something to keep in mind. 
The bathroom was also spacious and the tub was very deep. If you need a lot of space for your beauty products or whatnot, you will love the huge counter top. The L'Occitane bath products were a welcome addition as well. 
The hotel offers nightly turn down service which was included in our room rate. It was a very welcome addition to return to the room after a full day of activities and have classical music playing and have lovely cookies on the pillow. 
The hotel also has a house Mercedes which is available for guest use. It was free of charge and our driver took us just about everywhere we needed to go, whether it was shopping or to various wedding festivities. A very much appreciated touch! 
I would definitely stay at the Hotel Commonwealth if I travel to Boston again. It is an excellent hotel and they exceeded my expectations. When we got the bill at check out, we were happy (and suprised) that the hotel had removed the extra $20/night they had added for the extra person in the room. I highly recommend the Hotel Commonwealth. You really can't go wrong here. If you don't mind spending the money, don't hesitate to check it out!

title: “Return trip as good as the first!”
text: We first stayed at the Orchard in August 2010. Loved the spacious suite and convenient location for walking, cable cars and BART. In August 2011 we returned to visit the spots in San Francisco we missed. Of course the Orchard was our choice and did not disappoint! The ameneties, i.e., refrigerator/wet bar, 2 rooms, cleanliness, polite and helpful service , huge bathroom and comfortable beds make the Orchard an incredible value and luxurious stay. Will not stay anywhere else in San Francisco!

title: “great hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Peninsula in early December for a quick getaway weekend. Not much more I can add here beyond what other positive reviewers had to stay, but wanted to add if you are traveling with children to let them know when you make your reservation.
Upon returning to our room the first night, our girls found two little Christmas teddy bears, a Peninsula makeup bag filled with soaps, gels, toothbrush, floss, and kid toothpaste, and a fun dessert tray with popcorn, cookies, gummy bears, jello, water, and nuts and fruit for the adults. This hotel is beautiful and treats kids wonderfully. My girls thought it was very fun and felt special from the treatment they were given by hotel employees. The pool and hot tub didn't disappoint, and the location is superb. Peninsula makes it hard to stay elsewhere - will return.

title: “A Pleasure to Stay Here!”
text:
Thank you Trip Advisor for leading me to Hotel Metro. It's an older, quaint property in a great location with a super friendly and attentive staff. The 'family room' was great for accomodating my family and I as we took my mom to NYC for a celebration of her 65th birthday! 
Location is superb.. short walk to Empire State Building, Macys, Fashion District sites and New York Public Library. Bryant Park not too far either - slightly longer but very manageable walk to TImes Square and Broadway plays. Jimmy's around the corner was recommended by the doorman and had good all day food choices. 
Hotel was always clean. We had a problem with our toilet not flushing the first morning and maintaince was up within 5 minutes of us calling. The TVs didn't always work exactly as intended but someone came to look at that as well and we weren't in the room long enough to truly care about it anyway. I wouldn't hesitate to stay at Hotel Metro again.

title: “Excellent 5 day Vacation.”
text: I stayed at the Langham from May 17th to May the 22nd of 2012. I was in the area to attend 2 College Graduations and had an excellent stay at this hotel. I loved the room, the central location and the staff were all superb. Due to my hectic schedule, I was unable to enjoy the amenities and had to pass on the morning newspaper deliveries. I can easily recommend this classy hotel to friends and family. All the staff stood out and both Dan's and Keith are great. I will be back.

title: “Mixed feelings”
text:
I did enjoy my time in the w but there are certainly big negatives to this hotel. 
First and foremost, the parking. 35 bucks a day for guests is seriously steep. The valet guys do not appear to be employees of the hotel and instead work for ace I think. On my first day the valet advised me that the cheapest parking was in (an ace) car park around the corner, they were in no way phased when this turned out to not be true and i had to valet my car later in the night when the carpark totally emptied apart from my car, with rental gps visable as you cannot disconnect in hertz rentals, in a dark corner of town. I mentioned this situation to the concierge and reception who literally said "sorry you will have to talk to ace as we do not run the parking". I am lucky to have been to some great hotels on hols and with my job and have never seen such a relaxed response before to such a problem. Crap attitude really and indicative of the "boutique" vibe whereby the focus is more on being cool rather than helpful.
Also I asked for the directions to the nearest Starbucks and the guy pretty much just said "round the corner" before returning promptly to his computer.
The room was nice to be fair, and clean. The tv was not fully tuned in and with limited channels. As part of the boutique feel the bathroom had a roller screen rather than door, strange for an expensive hotel. Drinks and food are crazy expensive so we did not sample and walked downtown instead. 
Pool is small, unattended by drinks staff and loud. Gym is quite nice in fairness. 
Overall as I say not bad but also not great. If there was less of a focus on changing the mats in the lifts to say good afternoon rather than good morning and more attention to actually helping paying customers it might be better. As a final indication of the vibe at this place they closed the rooftop bar to guests on Saturday night we were there to hold a private party, no apologies for this but we're offered tickets at 25bucks a piece,....great, paying to go to the bar in our own hotel!

title: “Loved it.”
text:
We stayed in the hotel as part of a business group and loved it. Coming over from Europe we were very tired. As we didn't have much time we wanted to enjoy LA and relax. We found the ideal location on the roof terrace, enjoying the views. If you are arriving and just want to relax, I would recommend eating there and I would make a reservation. 
I love the fact that they have free wireless internet. 
The staff was very helpful with calling a taxi or renting a car. 
The bathroom was great, a bath for two, clean, modern, all the comfort you need, ...
I loved having the ability to make your own coffee and tea (the tea was delicious by the way).

title: “Customer Service”
text: I was new to the area and needed a place to stay until my residence was ready. Bill and the entire staff treated me with true hospitality. He was amazing when the MSU and Michigan State team played. He help make waffles and really made me and others feel right at home. Way to go Bill and the entire staff at Comfort Suites at Commonwealth.

title: “Great Value a Bit Dated”
text: Nice value by LAX but the rooms are a bit dated and internet kept disconnecting. The have a great Beer Lounge. I stayed during the week and seems a large number of flight crews use this hotel. Parking is an uncovered lot and the area is not the best but seems safe for parking.

title: “The Wit is hip and cool - great place!!”
text:
I was impressed - I came in through priceline to spend two night in town for a wedding, and I was very surprised with the service, the rooms, the styling and everything. The gourmet cookie was a very nice touch, I loved the contemporary feel of the place, and to top it off, they seem to have one of the hottest night spots in the city up on their roofdeck. It's great being able to jump right past the line with the htoel pass and feel like a rockstar!
All this, and being able to sleep very comfortably in a quiet room right below the party. Hands down, my favorite spot to stay in chicago from now on....

title: “Tropical setting, nice room decor- restaurant is awesome”
text: I initially found this little gem because I attended a summer concert (small venue) here and loved the views of the Marina and the look of the hotel. I was not let down. The rooms are great, large tv, the grounds are well kept. Nice pool. The summer concert series will now have me back regularly. I have to say that the restaraunt was excellent on all accounts. Service, Food and atmosphere. The bar attached had great live jazz music.. Over all a wonderful get away. Only issues I had was with the front desk at first check in. I actually left and called the hotel instead of furthering my frustrations with the staff at that time. Systems were down, and they lacked the thought process to manually look for rooms other than a print out in front of them. I almost contacted the VIP lince of Expedia to move me. Instead I chose to eat lunch then call- and when a better employee picked up and easily solved the issue. I was happier..... Customer service matters!

title: “Small but nice”
text: Great front desk team. Rooms are a bit on the small side but we are in Manhattan. Elevators can be slow at times, but can be overlooked. Good proximity to Koreatown and the subway.

title: “Good but service could be friendlier”
text: We had a good stay with such a great location. I do feel the staff could be more polite esp when we are paying so much. Rooms were nice and didn't notice the excess noise others have complained about.

title: “Perfect location!”
text:
Novotel is in a perfect location, very close to Times Square, just a little away from the all the crowd and noise. You have theaters and great restaurants around, and a supermarket on 49th and 8th street which makes it perfect if you don't want to eat out all the time.
The rooms were nice, clean and big for the price we paid. Not expensive at all for a hotel so close to Times Square. Breakfast is a bit expensive (21.95$ for a breakfast buffet) but the view from the restaurant is amazing so it's worth eating there at least once during your stay. Will definitely stay there again. Parking is right across the street you pay 30$ a night instead of 40$. My only complaint was no free wi-fi, but they do have 3 Macs in the lobby that guests can use for free.

title: “Excellent service from beginning to end.”
text: From the time I checked in the hotel staff gave excellent service in each and every category. The facility was neat and clean, room service as well as restaurant service and food was excellent.

title: “My Kinda Hotel ... !”
text:
We've stayed here a few times (4 ?). Name has changed since the last but it is the spot we'd always pick first. There are better hotels I guess - but we like this one.
We stopped here first many years ago on a trip from Oz. We had a Rt 66 tour starting. Since then we've picked it as our hotel of choice 3 more times. To give you an idea - last time we arrived it was a catastrophe happening. Water broken - and bathrooms unusable. We were told they were fixing but if we wanted they would transport us to another hotel. We said we'd chance it - much to the surprise and thankful reponse of the lady in charge. The water was fixed quickly and things got back to normal very quickly. They are an efficient bunch.
We stopped in our normal room - not the swankiest in the hotel - but we like it. Front of the hotel - about 7 floors up. They have an awesome restaurant - where you can feel the atmosphere and almost see the ghosts of old crooners and mobsters of days gone by. 
Easy walking distance to the Mag Mile, fabulous restaurants, and even Navy Pier. A short block to the lake and an easy walk to the train stop if you want to go to a ball game. Or an early morning walk is lovely - just you and the squirrels.
Almost every restaurant style you could want nearby.A wonderful bakery around the corner for brekkie too.
When we think Chicago - we think this hotel ! Would love to go back soon.

title: “Excellent christmas time experience. "Gangam style"”
text:
Stay for Bussiness. At midday they have a flash mob with Santa clause at "Gangam style". We have a lot of fun. I have never expect to have that experience in a DC hotel. 
Regarding my stay, I always recommend to stay at the club level. You have your coffee and snack at all time. Also you have space for informal, short meeting with some peers w/o invasion to your room. 
For those who love the National Monuments, the hotel is far away, but metro and hotel shutters are available.

title: “Horrible at any price”
text: I booked this hotel on Priceline and I was so happy to get a location somewhat close to the Wachovia center.The fact that it was a name brand Sheraton made the deal seem even better. I thought that I had gotten a great bargain at $70 for the one night that we were in town for a concert. As soon as I got into the room I knew that I was the one who had been had. The room reeked of mold. The ceiling paint in the bathroom was peeling and the bathtub was worn. I slept on the pull-out sofa, which had the worst mattress ever (and I don't expect much from a sofabed). As other reviewers said, noise travels up from the center courtyard, so we were awoken the next day by other travelers checking out for early flights. Another noise issue was the elevator, which had an alarm that went off loudly a few times. The redeeming characteristics of the place were free wireless internet and large suites.

title: “Looking to return in the summer!!”
text:
Just returned from a 5 day trip with daughter, mum-in-law and niece...Our stay would not have been the same if we had not been booked in at this hotel. The staff are all highly professional and customer focussed, desk staff, doormen, bell hops and the room attendants. Accomodation is top notch..we were orginally booked into a side facing room on the 22nd floor, but went back to front desk to see if we would be able to upgrade to a Times Square view, lovely lady (Tila I think) said that we would be able to change rooms, but advised that the room with the better veiw was much smalled (corner situation on the 19th floor - overlooking the ticket booth and all of the signs)..us being used to European room sizes, this was no problem..I.could have comfortably stayed there for a fortnight.
The hotel is perfectly sited for getting around - subway at the hotel entrance is great for downtown/uptown along 5th Avenue/City Hall, a short distance to the main Times Square subway and you connect to the lines that run from the Bronx right over to Brooklyn.
Eating is no problem something for everyone right on the doorstep (some places definately more expensive given the location - tip - avoid Hard Rock etc as they charge premium prices for fairly mediocre food). Big thank you to the concierge who advised us to use the Evergreen cafe (out of the door, turn left on 47th street and further down on the left hand side)..here we got our first taste of real New York!
I can honestly say that this hotel deserves all the praise in the world...at the risk of offending people I would say for fellow British travellers, to take some of the worse reveiws from US patrons with a pinch of salt...remember that they are used to far grander hotel accomodation in the states than we are in Europe (well for this price anyway)
Give it a go..i have and will happily return in the summer to get the warmer perspective of New York!

title: “Comfortable, Clean...Nice”
text: Nice quiet place to stay. Our room was large, clean and very comfortable. The linens were top quality and made for a great nights sleep. The view from our room was down to the ice skating rink located in the center. Staff was friendly. Parking was adequate and spaces were decent size for a parking garage. There are several restaurants in the bottom of the hotel area, but we arrived shortly before 5pm and everything was already closed, or in the process of closing. So we opted for the bar just inside the hotel. Great choice! Try the Chocolate Strawberry Margarita...heavenly. Expensive...but heavenly!!! (I had two...regardless of the sticker price!)

title: “Very disappointed with the Plaza”
text:
It has long been a fantasy of mine to stay at the legendary Plaza Hotel. Finally got there this year, and what a disappointment!
The room was nice, but that's about all I could say about it. The bathroom was really beautiful, lots of gold.
The service in the Champagne Bar and the mezzanine level bar was woeful, we walked out in disgust. We felt as if the staff thought they were doing us a favour by being there, very unpleasant!
Our room wasn't made up by 5pm when we got back after a busy day sightseeing on our second day there, and we had to ask to have it done, there was no apology from the butler, just a casual "oh, would you like me to get it made up?"
I have never ever stayed at a hotel where I had to request that my room be made up!
The location of this hotel is perfect, but as for value for money - forget the Plaza! Overpriced and under-serviced.

title: “Relaxation with style”
text:
We found this hotel quite by accident. And we are please to report that it was a very happy experience. We had been travelling for about 2 months prior and were ready for a chill out and relax period by a beach in the sun and the location of Tower 23 fitted this requirement perfectly. We stayed for 5 nights in one of the rooms overlooking the sea. (and above the restaurant). The room itself was was very sylish and contemporary and we loved sitting on the balcony watching the world go by. We found it was a real bonus having such a great restaurant in the hotel and also had food delivered to our room. We had great service from pretty much everyone we encountered. There was some noise from the restaurant in our room but this stopped around midnightish and we didn't find it a real issue at all. Overall we thoroughly enjoyed our stay.
C & A Loader, Auckland, New Zealand

title: “Red Roof - Great Value”
text: A Good hotel for the cost. Central Location, one Block from Empire State Building. Rooms were clean and spacious, staff friendly. Complimentary breakfast was a Orange Juice, Unlimited Tea or Coffee, a bagel donut or Toast and a piece of Fruit, which was more than adequate. Overall above average hotel for the money they charge

title: “Where is the management?”
text:
I booked this hotel following a great review by Conde Nast. We drove to the front door and were ignored by the doorman who continued his conversation with a friend. He eventually ambled over without any enthusiasm or polite greeting. The check in staff were much more pleasant but when we went to access the elevator, the bell boy, with our cases on his cart, stood by watching us struggle to press the call button with our arms full of hand luggage. The carpets in the entrance hall and elevator are grubby and the glass on the door into the much vaunted Cruise Bar was smeared. So far, so poor. Aren't first impressions so important?
Ok the room, clean. The good sized king bed had only three pillows and one of the sheets had a tear in it. The bathroom, clean. The plug in one sink was stuck requiring it to be accessed from underneath to empty. The shower, attractive glass stall, could only be turned on by standing in front which of course meant you got wet. The head was angled so that unless the door was closed the water spilled on to the floor. The hand held shower over the bath leaked on to the floor whilst the bath was filling unless it was placed in the bath.
All of this was irritating but we were only staying one night. I thought that I would mention these glitches when we checked out. Of course the front desk staff would ask if we had enjoyed our stay. They didn't which is why I am committing my findings to this review. To cap it all, the doorman as we left was so elderly, although charming, that my husband felt obliged to stow our bags in the trunk.
PS Don't bother with breakfast

title: “Not what we expected.. worse”
text: This was a disappointing stay.I reviewed this hotel as I do with all of our vacations,and the reviews are usually right on the mark. We were assigned room 1000, a corner room with lots of windows,and 2 queens like requested. the room was dirty when we entered, llike mowed grass off shoes on the carpet, the room had 3 wet moisture areas, with one corner area in the living room part with black areas and getting larger-?mold? The windows were filthy outside so you couldn't see, we had requested a riverwalk room and told this "was one and a great room". A great room in size, but not in cleanliness or view. The mgr. Jennifer Hill offered to move us to the same type of room the next day and did move us, but I request the refrigerated items would be put in the refrigerator, and they were not when we returned 7 1/2 hours later. They were sitting on teh table. AND we were moved to a double bed room. The ironic thing is the price was not changed from the previous rooms we had been in and they were all too happy to charge the same price until I stated it was not the same room type and we were given doubles. The room we were moved to was smaller, one 4x4 window which the wood was rotting around the glass. This was supposedly a room that had been redone after millions renovations. I am not sure, but if that was a renovated room, then the Hiltons really aren't paying attention. I would say stay away from this hotel. If this was our experience with 2 rooms, I cannot imagine what shape some of the other ones are in. There is also mold in the bathrooms, with little ventilation of course, visible growing around the bathtub caulking. The second room had toothpaste splattered all over the hand towel bar area,and quite visible since itis brown wallpaper. I wouldn't waste your money. A clean room is essential and this hotel wasn't honest with us about the rooms/price we were moved to and the condition wasn't much different than the first, minus the many water stains on the ceiling. when you go on vacation all you want to do is relax, not move rooms 3 times! We were glad we didn't rent a car for downtown-walk or take the trolley that you can get off and on at scenic points. San Antonio does not have adequate parking ramps or spots.

title: “Paying for "SELF PARKING" sucks!”
text: Having to pay for parking on property of a hotel where you park your car yourself, really sucks. At the toon of $18.00 a day! I can understand if they park for you, but when you do it yourself, it does not make sense to me, and I own a boutique myself. We stayed 4 nights at this hotel. The hotel itself is wonderful. My teenagers said we were in "Barbie's Dream House". The house keeping was good. No complaints other than the parking situation. We did not know about this fee ahead of time and the access gate was not working the whole time we were there. We had to keep calling the front desk as we came and went from the hotel. These rooms were paid for with AMEX points, but when we arrived home, we noticed the rooms were also billed to my credit card by the hotel as well. We called the hotel and with in the day, they refunded our money, NOT the parking fee's though. I will NOT stay at this hotel again, for this price if I were to have to pay for parking also.

title: “The Place to stay in Dallas”
text: The caring staff, hotel ambiance, and downtown location of the Adolphus make this an ideal place to stay when visiting Dallas. We stayed for 3 nights and the entire experience including service, dining, complimentary drivers, and the room accomodations made for a perfect getaway.

title: “great location but melrose is showing its age”
text: we booked our room via priceline and we were pleasantly surprised by how central the location was, it is literally two blocks from georgetown. We also upgraded to a suite for a reasonable upcharge. Our room was decent enough but looked and felt a little dated. The biggest problem came when the hot water quit working for roughly 18 hours on a friday. This was a minor inconvenience for our family but would have been much worse if we had been travelling on business. I will give them credit as they comped us our bar tab and nice breakfast for our trouble, roughly $100 value.

title: “horrible”
text: no one there knows what is going on i will never stay at this hotel again or have any thing positive to say about hotel it should have stayed a hampton inn with same owners it could do with out the knew ones awful experience very rude staff from the bottom to the top

title: “great stay!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for 3 days this past weekend - one room had a king bed and the other had 2 queens. The rooms were big and roomy, especially the king room. The lobby, hallways and rooms were very clean and everything looked new (I believe they had recently laid new carpet). I thought it looked great! The service was wonderful - everyone we encountered was super friendly. It's in a great area near lots of shopping, restaurants, and the freeways. Downtown was 5 min away and the beaches were 10 min away. I will definitely stay again!

title: “The Wit - just not funny”
text:
I looked up The Wit before I travelled as it had been booked for me by my company and first impressions were not good. Their website irritatingly puts "The" infront of everything (THE reservations, THE Contacts, THE photos...) and this wears thin very quickly. Arriving at the hotel, with loud music blaring at the door, I was immediately hit by an overpowering smell of air freshener in the lobby, the same kind as a car air freshener. Those things give me a blinding headache and make me feel sick. Not a great start. 
Upstairs the corridors have continous animal sounds (frogs, birds, cockerals...) and running water sounds 24 hours a day. Not amusing after the first half hour (you can hear it in your room). Also the hotel is right next to an elevated railway so you get train noise all night as well.
I was also horrified to discover that internet is $15 per 24 hours, on top of £209 per night plus taxes for a room. Appalling.
After a long day at work we arrived in the bar at 10.25pm for a nightcap. We were told that the bar was about to close by a very grumpy barman, Turns out the bar closes at 11pm, he just wanted to go early because he had to be up at 5.30am. How hospitable.
On the plus side, the room was large and clean and the bed comfortable. The bathroom facilites were good. However I would not stay there again.

title: “The Dump”
text: Please be aware if anyone thinking of staying in this supposed "hotel" then think again, yes its cheap but at what cost. We arrived to be led down winding corridors that had the most foul smells, there were rubbish bins emptied out on the floors. After being shown into a dark dingy "twin room" which had no room to walk about in, we asked to see the bathrooms only to be met with the most disgusting site ever and i wont try and explain im sure you get the picture. The smell just made you want to vomit, we left as fast as we arrived. I cant believe this place is allowed to operate as a hotel, please stay away!!!

title: “Horrible!!!”
text: For the kind of money you spend to stay here, invest it somewhere else!!! There are no ammenities. i.e., pool & jacuzzi. Channel 25 & 29 are Cinimax & Showtime (East Coast Stations) so...they begin showing "PORN" @ 8pm @night! I was HORRIFIED when my 9 yr. old made this discovery! Management and/or Best Western Corporate could have CARED LESS!!! The managerS were awful. VERY rude and combative to my "porn concerns". The homeless were lined up like sausages in their sleeping bags along their front sidewalk. Parking's awful. You have to pay $10 p/nt. and we couldn't find a space! The electricity went out for 2 1/2 hrs. our 2nd day-delaying our day. Rooms are clean, but walls are paper thin. You can hear everything. NEVER again will I saty here!!! I tried to book another hotel immediatly...however; it was the 4th of July weekend and nothing was available for under $350.00 p/nt. I was STUCK in this torture!!! RUN!!!
