title: “Excellent stay, customer service shines”
text: Spent the night here after a Red WIngs game. Stayed with 3 other couples. I got a great deal on Expedia for $159 including tax, so the price couldn't be beat. Everyone single employee of MC that our group dealt with had just the right amount of professionalism and friendliness. The rooms were all very clean and well-maintained. The toiletries that are in the room are also those used in the spa (sadly, didn't avail myself of any of that service) and I really liked them. Wonderful Turkish bath towels and robes as well as most any amenity you might imagine. I've read numerous complaints about the neighborhood, but if you're staying there, do your due diligence and just drive to Greektown and park there for free (usually) if you want a walkable area. The hotel property is secure and the hotel parking is great. Drive right to the heated entryway and wait for the valet ticket. There is no navigating through a huge casino to get to your room either. We didn't use the Wings shuttle available from the hotel since we ate dinner away from the hotel, but it's there to use if you like.

title: “Really nice hotel in a really great location.”
text: We stayed here in July 2011. We really enjoyed the hotel. The room was very large, the bathroom was huge. It is in a great location. We enjoyed our stay.

title: “Nice Hotel, I would absolutely stay there again!”
text: I just got back to Boston from Dallas today and as tired as I am, I wanted to write this review. I am VERY picky person when it comes to cleanliness and safety and The Fairmont is a pretty nice hotel, the room I was in (King bed) was a good size fairly update and there was a few dumb things like the pool being drained and re-tiled, flat panel tv was nice, and the room was clean- except I have to be honest, they do need to vacuum around the bed frame legs... anyhow I always wear slippers, but, it was clean, the bed had failry crisp white down feather pillows and blankets, in another review someone complained about the throw at the end of the bed being dirty, I think its the fabric that makes it appear that way...crushed velvet type of fabric. Anyhow, I went to the Hyatt at Reunion Blvd, where my colleagues where staying and it was nasty- the rooms were old and dated, and a street person was roaming the lobby asking for money! The Fairmont is really safe, they dont even allow pizza delivery people up to the rooms, you have to come down to get it. The bellman is an older man and the valet guy as well, both are really helpful and awesome! Checking in was a breeze, but make sure you check your itemized bill, they accidently charged me for 1 day of parking @ $21.00- I called the desk and it was taken care of before I checked out... Check out was so simple, no waiting at all.

title: “Great breakfast”
text: Our room was with breakfast included. It was a grat value. We paid extra 10 dollars for the room. We have 2 adults and 2 kids. If we had to pay directly, it would have been over 30 dollars. The room is clean. Due to heavy rain, Charlotte was flooded all over including the south park mall. The hotel lobby had 5 inches of water. But they cleaned up so quickly, we were very impressed how quickly they took care of the situation. Would stay there again.

title: “Super Hotel”
text: Great all around. Close to Metro station, central in DC. Courteous and helpful staff. Clean, comfortable rooms / beds. Baths were roomy. Nice restaurants. Breakfast buffet was large with wide selection. Dedicated airline check-in station to print boarding passes quickly. Exceptionally affordable in DC, excellent value.

title: “Incredible upon entering the lobby, welcoming and beautiful!!”
text:
Our experience at The Palmer House was excellent, when entering the front door into the lobby, it felt so incredible, we were in "awe" with the light/art fixtures and the art work, the ceiling blew me away. The staff at the front desk was extremely friendly and was very welcoming.
The room (standard) was very comfortable, the bed linens were beautiful, (both with a very upbeat decor). We also had the opportunity to have lunch at the Lockwood, the food and service was excellent.
I would highly recommend The Palmer House to anyone planning a trip to Chicago!!

title: “Fabulous hotel!”
text: Wow. This hotel is BEAUTIFUL. It has an ultra cool, modern vibe that you instantly feel when you walk through the door. My boyfriend and I were in Chicago for the weekend to see the Red Sox play the White Sox at U.S. Cellular field. It was our first time in Chicago and our first time staying at a W hotel - we were very pleased. The room was great, the staff was friendly and helpful, the living room bar was super cool and fun and we were within walking distance to a lot of great attractions and restaurants/bars. If we were going anywhere further away, we just hopped on the subway or the bus around the corner. It was great. We will DEFINITELY be back. One thing I will say is don't open ANTYHING in the room or you will be charged a fortune. NOTHING is free. Even the mini can of Pringles was $5. The bottled water was $9, I think. Stay away from all that like we did. Otherwise, it was fabulous!

title: “A Delight!”
text:
My fiancee and I spent the Thanksgiving holiday in Fort Worth visiting her family. Stayed four nights at the Ashton. We were upgraded to a junior suite. Spacious, high ceilings, wonderful bed. Decor was classic with contemporary touches. All with an attention to detail. We watched the Fort Worth Christmas Parade from our 3rd story windows. The restaurant was very, very good. The staff was attentive, knew our names immediately. After one day they remembered, I like my coffee black and she drinks green tea.
If I could find a negative point, it would have been the bathroom. Spacious, but dated in design. The attempt to modernize it falls short. The traditional feeling of the rest of the hotel and our room was in juxtaposition to our bathroom. That is the only"negative" I can think of.
I would not hesitate to stay at The Ashton Hotel again and rest assured I will.

title: “Good value but noisy”
text: The staff were very friendly, helpful and polite and booked in advance the price was very good. Our room was very spacious and clean but the noise from the street kept me awake at night. Parts of the room were a little bit tired and it feels very corporate overall. The bathroom didn't have a full bath. The location is excellent - very central and you can walk to most places.

title: “Nice Place”
text: We stayed here for two nights with my daughter's softball team. The hotel was very nice, very clean, and the staff was efficient and friendly. The location is right off the freeway and convenient to a lot of restaurants. The continental breakfast wasn't anything to write home about, but then again, we weren't expecting much for the price we paid.

title: “Good but not great”
text: Good location, close to subway and Times Square. Friendly and helpful staffs. Breakfast was good but same thing for 5 days and dining room was too small.

title: “A very pleasant place to stay”
text:
Weare in the second day of a two day stay, and we think this is a lovely property. The suites are large, clean, and nicely furnished. The free evening meal last night consisted of two good soups and fresh salad fixings. Breakfast today included bacon and sausage, eggs, bagels and other rolls, canned peaches, yogurt, cereals, etc, and we thought it was very good.
The only negative is the very loud A/C. We shut it off finally late last night and opened windows. For that reason, I probably would not stay here in summer. However, any other season, I would look forward to returning.

title: “Great hotel with comfortable beds.”
text: We stayed at the Argonaut in late December. The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful. The rooms were clean and comfortable. The only minor issue is that we had a room overlooking the main street - it was a little noisy at night. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Stay out of the basement”
text:
Having read the reviews, we decided to give this place a go anyway. We were in the basement room which I think is the deciding factor about whether people enjoy this hotel or not.
We had to climb over a pile of trash bags to get into our room (should have been a clue, but we were still determined to like the place at that point). On the plus side, the bed was comfortable and the linens were clean, so we were pretty pleased with it until we tried to go to sleep.
There was no bolt on the door to the room, which was a bit worrying as the door out to the alley was proped open two feet from the room. We were woken up regularly by the loud airconditioner which we eventually had to turn off and the basement windows didn't open so the room got really hot. Later we were awakened again by a mouse loudly going through the trash bin in the bedroom. After shutting the mouse in the bathroom (along with a cockroach which had appeared in the shower) we spent the rest of the night lying awaking wondering what else was going to happen. 
We considered asking for an upper floor room, but in the end we moved to another hotel instead. The place isn't terrible, but the combined effect of many little things, made us just want to get out of there.

title: “Guest Rooms Need An Update”
text: For the price of the room I think there are better choices in the same area I was staying. The room I stayed in was showing signs of wear and tear. My average rating was made stronger by staff. They are well trained, responsive and friendly. The common areas of the hotel were nice. It is a great location connected to a couple of malls and close to Newberry Street if you like high-end window shopping. The bed was comfortable, the view was nice it just lacked the luxury feel for what I thought was a luxury room rate.

title: “A good hotel but not fantastic”
text:
The room we were given was fine and quite large. We found it to be quiet and restful but with no view. Again not a problem as the quiet location made up for that. 
The staff on the reception desks etc were generally pretty unhelpful and not particularly friendly. In my view they made no effort to associate with the guests.
Drinks in the bar are extreemly expensive. $35 for two glasses of wine - even if it was good quality thats too expensive in my view. 
The housekeeping couldn't be faulted. We never saw them and the rooms were perfectly cleaned etc. Turndown service is a bonus.
We travelled to New York to celebrate a special birthday. I informed the hotel that it was a special occasion via email as I was hoping they could recommend some special treats - i.e. somewhere nice to eat etc. They made no reference to the emails etc upon arrival and I would have expected some achknowledgement however small from such a reputable hotel with high rating.
The staff could make this hotel really special - I think they are missing a trick....

title: “Not the best DC Hotel Experience”
text:
I have stayed in many Washington DC hotels, but this was my first time staying at the Grand Hyatt. We were there for a national Disability Policy conference, but unfortunately, by the time we booked our room there were not actually any truly accessible rooms available. We got a moderately "accessible" room with minimal space and closet with lowered rods (although the hangers were still up high) and a regular bathroom with a shower chair that we had to lift in and out of the tub (and was extremely heavy- I would not have been able to do it if traveling alone)
Before I get to the good things- another thing that was a huge pain, was when I had a package delivered to the hotel. I was at a reception the day it was arriving and called the hotel to confirm it was there and I could pick it up when I returned. After going back and forth, respelling my name, and finally giving them a tracking number, they confirmed it was there and I could simply have it brought up to my room when I returned. However- when I did return, that was not the case. I spoke with a bellman, and there were some language barriers to begin with, but he called me back numerous times asking me to respell my last name (which is CYR. 3 letters) Then saying if he couldn't locate it, he would call me to come down and look WITH him. About 10 minutes later, he did not call, but came up to the room (wearing dark sunglasses... at night, inside?) and instructed me to follow him. Luckily my boyfriend was traveling with me, and I had him come with us, as I would NOT have felt safe doing this alone. We truck all the way down to the mail center, and as soon as we enter the room, we turn our heads, and my boyfriend says, "There it is." Right immediately in front of us was my package, at eye level. Finally, at about 10:00 pm (this conversation started at around 6:00) we were able to have it brought up to the room and be done with it all. This same bell man also made me go into the luggage check room with him the next day to identify our bags, then questioned me when I told him which suitcase was ours...
Aside from those things, this is a great hotel. We were able to walk to Capitol City Brewing for dinner which is right across the street, there is a Starbucks and cafe in the lobby (huge, as I am completely incompetent with hotel coffee makers) and when we dined in the restaurant, the manager came over and asked up about our stay, what we would change and was very receptive to our feedback.
Overall I would stay there again, but if you need accessible accommodations, be sure to plan ahead!

title: “Horrible”
text:
Right now I am laying in a bed that is so broken down you can feel the springs. You almost need to be duct taped in the bed to not roll off. The mattress is so worn that it has this huge sag in the middle. And the new sand paper sheets don't help either. 
This is a very strange hotel. It isn't a hotel. It's a cross between staying on a ship and in a dormitory.
There is a small front desk check in area and then up to the small narrow hallway to your small prefab room to sleep on the broken down bed and sand paper sheets.
Two positives are it's clean and you can open the room window to get air.

title: “Perfect base for touring New York City”
text:
My wife and two teenage daughters stayed at the Salisbury for 6 nights in July 2010..we had 5 nights here, then moved to Boston for 4 nights, and returned to the Salisbury for our last night before flying home to the UK the next day.
Although an old building, the Salisbury's rooms have been pleasantly updated with high quality traditional bedding and furnishings and huge amounts of space. We had suites both times (the standard type room at this hotel) and our daughters had their own self contained area as did we - we only had to share the bathroom. The airconditioning was a Godsend in temperatures of 90 to 95 degrees, and we had our own mini kitchen area with sink, fridge and microwave.
The staff were professional, courteous and helpful. We had the $6 breakfast on 2 mornings, our only adverse comment would be that the breakfast was too weighted toward sugary, doughy foods such as doughnuts, pastries, and cookies, with little fruit and no hot cooked options such as scrambled eggs and bacon. The food that was offered was, however, fresh and of good quality of its' type.
One of the best features of the Salisbury over and above its' rooms is the location. Between 5th and 6th Avenues on West 57th St, many of the landmark buildings such as Times Square, The Empire State and Central Park are a short or comfortable walk away.
All in all we heartily recommend this hotel, its' staff and its' location, and we will stay again if we go back to NYC.

title: “Cheap and cheerful!”
text: Strange little place but not bad for the money. Rooms are basic and in need of updating but very cheap and in a good location with free parking and free WiFi. Also, staff very friendly but if you need the reception you have to either call externally or go down as no phone in the room. Rooms have air-con but too noisy to have it on at night.

title: “Good stay.”
text: Overall my stay at this hotel was pretty good. Check-in was a breeze and the room I was assigned to was a corner suites which was very quiet and quite spacious. The only thing which is kind of odd is that the bedroom itself is not that big while the other room is much more spacious. Everything in the room was in working order but while the coffee pot was available, there were no coffee pods, just tea. Room service was quick and the food was decent. Bathroom does not have separate shower and bath tub.

title: “good location”
text:
arrived from uk and offered cookies at reception...nice, room was on 2nd floor overlooking outside bar and had booked an up-grade to higher level, though they say they had not recived it, they did offer us a room on 8th floor which suited us, though still a lot of street noise early hours.
apart from that this hotel suited our needs, was close to everywhere we wanted to go, and because of jet-lag was up early doors and we were the first up the empire state building 5mins walk away, so no ques ;-)

title: “Excellent hotel would book again”
text: I booked this hotel after reviewing it on tripadviser and I was not disappointed. For my purpose which was seeing the sights I found it just right. Staff were helpful and friendly.

title: “Great people”
text: I would like to commend: Andrea, Elizabeth, and Jamie for their professionalism and commitment to assuring that I received personalized service at each visit to the Hotel lounge. They are knowledgeable and customer friendly associates that should be recognized for their contribution to making my stay at this Westin completely satisfying. Please extend my thanks to each of these great associates!!

title: “You get what you pay for”
text:
The front desk staff are very helpful. They allowed us to check-in at 10 am which was helpful since we had been driving all night. The location is very convenient, walking distance to harbor and a lot of restaurants. 
The hotel itself is in an old building. Everything feels very dark and tiny. The room decor seems like a strange mishmash of contemporary furniture, tacky bathroom (mix of glitter vanity with black and white swirl bowl), and generally run down. I think the room would have been better if the lighting was brighter (we only had a small window facing a wall), and had basic contemporary decor. I felt like they used the cheapest materials to update the room, rather than having a cohesive decor. It just ends of feeling creepy.

title: “Excellent value hotel for stopovers.”
text: Not expecting too much from an airport hotel, we booked the Crown Plaza for an overnight stay enroute from Australia to Ft Lauderdale. We were extremely tired and so we were pleasantly surprised with the quiet & and spacious room we were allocated.. A large comfortable king bed with soft pillows and block out curtains ensured a good nights sleep, and the large bathroom with decent sized vanity and shower with supersized showerhead was a bonus. We ate at the restaurant downstairs which had a variety of excellent food at reasonable prices and there was a pleasant bar/lounge area with live music. We could have happily stayed a few more nights.

title: “Understaffed, insufficient wireless capacity, rowdy guests”
text:
I should have known better than to expect decent wireless access in this remote outpost in the MIDDLE of SILICON VALLEY. I'm still laughing about it now. The wireless signal--which I paid $12 or $13 for--was basically nonexistent and/or overwhelmed. Well, I had work to do, and my laptop doesn't have a firewire port because I live in the 21st century. I went to a nearby cafe and used their wireless instead.
I didn't even bother trying to get it taken off my bill when checking out, because one hapless clerk was staffing a line of customers nine people deep, and I had a meeting to get to.
My colleague, on a different floor, was kept up all night by teenagers who had rented a room or two for an all-night door-slamming-and-screeching-laughter party. A bellman brought her earplugs.

title: “Good but with a few issues...”
text: Convenient to the airport. Very Very short walk from terminals. Nice rooom, refurbished. Nice public spaces. Awesome gym with a big weight area including free weights and machines. Couple of issues. First was the elevators. They have about eight elevators but only three were working when I was there. Long waits which sucked. Another issue was being overcharged for breakfast. There were four of us at breakfast. it was a business meeting where two people ordered the buffet one only had coffee, and one had coffee and asked for an english muffin. The person did not get the muffin from the buffet but ordered it off the menu. The bill camae and it was 85 dollars. The waiter had charged everyone for the buffett even though only two people ate off the buffet. The waiter did not handle the inquiry very well and it is my opinion that he deliberately charged us for four buffet's as this was a bsuiness metting and we were all very involved with discussion. I think he thought we wouldn't bat an eye at the bill. Besides this, the hotel is OK.

title: “Nice hotel, but soooo expensive.”
text:
The Marriott East side looks very impressive from the outside. It's in a great location. Close to everything.
This is my first stay at a NYC hotel. I don't know how it is in comparison to other NYC hotels, but compared to other hotel rooms overall the room is tiny. I guess that comes with the territory in NYC. 
$500 a night is outrageously expensive for such a tiny room. The only reason we stayed here was because my husband has platinum status with Marriott. The only thing that made this stay so special is their concierge lounge on the 16th floor. It's a beautiful outdoor terrace with view to both rivers. The breakfast they provide is phenomenal. The concierge lounge was worth the stay, but only if you're a Marriott member

title: “Fine once you are inside but badly organised and unhelpful staff”
text:
Look, this is an airport Holiday Inn so it does exactly what you expect; clean, comfortable and very near the hotel. BUT unusually this was a very bad HI experience.
1) the we are a family of four and our kids normally share one double bed and us the other but these were so small we each had to share with a child to have room for two. i slept terribly although the bed was comfortable so I'd have been fine on my own.
2) The shuttle from the airport took ages to arrive so we stood, late at night, tired and hot waiting at the terminal.
3) As I said we had arrived late, tired and desperate to get to bed but the check staff were disorganised, uncaring and unhelpful. Although we had a reservation we had to queue behind plenty of people who hadn't; none of the three staff would separate those with reservations who could be processed quickly. The queue was very long but they didn't bring out extra staff for ages. Although my kids were tearful and tired they paid no attention and were incredibly slow in handling those ahead of us, chatting away as we and others stood waiting. We literally spent 15 minutes waiting to check-in. From now on we'll choose Marriott first.

title: “ABSOLUTELY LOVED IT”
text: Great place, loved the fact that the parking is only $12. per day and we can come in&out as many times as we want. Our friends are staying at a diff. hotel here downtown, and their parking is $28. per day........crazy. Riverwalk Plaza is incredibly close to the Riverwalk, very nice staff, rooms are the most comfortable beds you will ever sleep on and not to mention the wonderful pillows. Great place to stay at and have a very relaxing, great time in san antonio.

title: “"Great Place"”
text:
Great Staff!!!! I loved the shuttle (Trey) taking me to the shopping area. At first I thought I was going to be stranded at the hotel or walk a long distance, until an Front desk staff member said that the hotel provided a shuttle to where I needed to go. Great !! This was my first experience in a hotel ,I finally had a rested vacation . Unfortunately, I did not take advantage of the gym or pool... which looked great. Breakfast was great. I'm sure I will do that on my next visit to Jacksonville, it was perfect.
Thank You (all staff members) Hyatt Place Jacksonville, Florida

title: “Fabulous Hotel”
text:
Perfect location, right near Bryant Park and Times Square. Central to everything! The rooms are fabulous! They are renovated, clean and the beds are so comfortable. The bathrooms are a great size as well. Free wi-fi for Kimpton In Touch members. Wine hour every night in the lobby, you can't beat it! And the lobby and restaurant have just been renovated as well, and are just beautiful!
Service is great. I was checked in within minutes and when I forgot my computer cord, they found one in lost and found and brought one to my room immediately for me. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “A hidden Gem Of A Place”
text:
Having read some of the reviews of this hotel we arrived with some uncertainty about the hotel. The immediate area is, admittedly, not the best to be found in New York. But it proved to be fine; some somewhat tacky shops and occasional street traders, but neverthelessa an interesting area and felt totally safe. Our interactions with the local street inhabitants were all very friendly and extremely courteous. It also felt very safe at night.
The hotel itself has a very narrow entrance with the reception desk some way down a corridor. The receptionists, concierge and doormen were all very obliging and helpful. The public areas and our rooms were exceedingly clean, tidy and well decorated. The bedrooms were also of a very good size, much bigger than we have had on previous visits to NY. We had asked for views of the Empire State Building and were given two adjoining rooms on the 11th floor, both with a view of the ESB.
We didn't use the breakfast facilities but did use the 24hr coffee services to take back to our rooms. There are lot as of delis and other places to eat in the area.
We really enjoyed our stay at the hotel, and will certantly use it again when we are next back in New York

title: “Enjoyed our trip to NY and our experience with Marriott”
text: My wife and I just stayed in NYC at the Marriott Marquis for 4 nights. We had major concerns about the bedbug issues in many hotels in NYC and chose to stay at the Marquis after reviewing many hotels regarding the various bedbug incidences in NY. In fact, I was traveling to NY for a conference that was held at another hotel in NY that had experienced major issues with bed bugs and we opted to select the Marquis over the conference hotel at a slightly greater price due to the incidents and to also enjoy a higher quality hotel stay. Upon check-in at the Marquis, while we were not able to get a king room upon our late check-in at the reserved price, the hotel had an upgrade king room with a times square view that was a reasonable upgrade price and we accepted. We were most pleased with the room and value. The room was a lot larger and had a view overlooking Times Square directly across from the Disney store. We checked the room, bed and all the most common places for bed bugs and the room was clear of any signs of bedbugs and was spotless in terms of cleanliness. We were very pleased with our entire stay at the Marquis. While we had an incident in our room regarding a leak int he ceiling of the bathroom, the staff, engineers and housecleaning staff were very attentive and resolved the issue within a one hour period. We all know that bad things happen, but how well you respond to meet challenges is the sign of how the operational staff can resolve issues. These folks did a great job and provided excellent service and correcting the problem. The only meal that we enjoyed at the hotel was a late night dessert selection at the rotating restaurant at the top of the hotel - The View. The views were spectacular and the food was outstanding! This is the third time that we have stayed at the Marquis during our NY trips and it is our favorite of all the various hotels in NY. The hotel has the best location - period. The size and quality of the rooms, staff, amenities and convenient access to great shopping, theatre and restaurants is wonderful. We highly recommend that you select the Marriott Marquis for your next stay in NY.

title: “Great Stay!!!!”
text: I must say our stay was enjoyable. Parking at NO additional cost was very helpful to our budget. This location is awesome as well, easy walking distance to whatever you desire. The room was clean and comfortable and attached is a very good restaurant, you should try it!! The customer service is OUTSTANDING!!!! WHICH SPEAKS FOR ITSELF. My husband and I will definitely stay here again!!! Keep up the great work BEST WESTERN STAFF!!!!

title: “fantastic hotel!”
text:
So many good things about this hotel--where do I start? Per TripAdvisor's recommendations, my boyfriend and I stayed here for 3 nights in January 2009. The rate (through Travelocity) was $140 a night. We arrived earlier than the stated check-in time but they let us check in anyway. The available room was bigger so they upgraded us at no extra cost. Five minutes after arriving in our room, the front desk called to ask how everything was. The room was large, with soft, comfy beds, a big bathroom w/ hairdryer, toiletries, & extra towels, mini kitchen w/ a microwave and full-size fridge & freezer, iron & ironing board, flat-screen TV w/ free HBO, free wi-fi, and an hour's worth of free long-distance available on the room phone. The furnishings were elegant and comfortable, with three huge windows overlooking the city. 
The second floor of the hotel was a giant meeting area: in the mornings, there was a free full breakfast buffet (eggs, sausage, the works), in the afternoons, free fresh popcorn, and in the evenings, free (alcoholic) drinks. There were two jacuzzis and a heated pool on the roof--the view was incredible. There was also a fitness center, an indoor pool, a 24 hr. business center (we didn't bring a laptop and were very happy that we could still access the net for free), and a 24 hr. little store next to the front desk where you could purchase non-standard toiletries (floss, deodorant, Advil, etc.) as well as snacks and drinks. There was a giant spiral staircase in the center of the hotel that went all the way down to the riverwalk. The riverwalk is shaped like a horseshoe with the ends pointing west and a straight north-south section connecting the ends to each other. This was the only hotel along the (very short) north-south section. Most of the restaurants were along the northern half of the horseshoe, so from the hotel it was just a matter of turning right onto the riverwalk and following it around about a quarter of a mile or so. In a nutshell, we were close enough to walk to where the action was in under five minutes, but far enough away that there weren't loud drunk people hanging around at night. 
This hotel used to be the headquarters of the Alamo National Bank, and a lot of the original decor had been refurbished/restored or was on display. A lot of it was pretty cool--there was even a safe in the basement. We were amazed at how fast the elevators were--in a bank they don't forget that time is money! The walkway along the riverwalk was built recently and donated by the hotel developers to the city of San Antonio, and the restaurant area in the center of it looked finished and ready to go--just waiting on a chef/restauranteur to make a good offer and set up shop. The lack of both room service AND a restaurant was this hotel's only imperfection. But hey, the restaurant is in the works, and there are a ton of others nearby in the meantime. With all the great things we got out of this hotel, we didn't mind. Thank you TripAdvisor! The Drury Plaza Hotel (and it sounds like the entire Drury chain) is a great find!
*Tip* Turn left instead of right on the Riverwalk (or circle around) and eat at Zocca. Order the fettuccini dish--it was AMAZINGLY good!

title: “lovely place to stay”
text: stayed for 4 nights 19th to 23 rd march, lovely room, great bed ,no complaints at all, free breakfast was more like a buffet and eat all you want very good value all round, great location for the wharf and most other things you will want to do and see, plus a bar right across the road doing food and cheap beers, would go back here any day loved it all , many thanks to the staff ,

title: “Loved it inspite of big conference”
text: I just finished my 10th stay at Hotel ZaZa! Best one yet! The hotel was extremely busy with some sort of conference going. That was so cool! They had a big party at the pool and invited all the guests then had a singer/piano player on Monday night. It was awesome! The staff could not have been nicer even though it was obvious the conference had some attendees that were over the top rude! I will be back in a couple of weeks for stay number 11! Great job, ZaZa!

title: “Best Hotel, Very Elegant, I always go back!”
text: When I walked in the first time, when I was a young child, I thought a princess lived there. The staff was excellent, and so was the food. The beds were extremely comfortable.The bathroom was amazing, a seperate bath and shower! Almost impossible for other hotels. I always go back there even though I live in San Diego!

title: “Fun Hotel With A Few Quirks”
text:
Don't expect to see anything like your normal Best Western here. After taking a few steps DOWN from the street level, you will find yourself in a brightly lit lobby that is home to gigantic ovoid couch, three TVs playing anime videos, vending machines of gadgets, and crazy ceiling murals. Staff are generally helpful and pleasant, but nothing out of the ordinary. 
The rooms are decorated in IKEA-like furnishings of natural wood, and a low platform bed. One wall of the room is home to a cute Japanese-inspired mural that covers the whole surface.
Beds are quite comfortable and the television had quite a few channel selections, including a few HBO channels. 
The in-room noise levels are not bad for being on the street corner of a major city. We were quite close -- maybe 30' from the restaurant -- but were did not notice any excessive noise or smells coming from that area. We did get breakfast at the restaurant one morning but found it only average.
The only two complaints we had were about heating/cooling and parking. The heating/cooling system is quite odd and seems to ignore any manipulation of the thermostat -- it seemed to be either on or off which is problematic if you find the room too warm and the sytem only wants to blow out warm air. The parking is very limited, there are maybe 20 - 25 spaces for all the hotel guests. This means you either have to circle around the street hoping to find a spot or park at the Japan Center garage which is more than a block away. This could be a hassle when you realize that you forgot something in the car when you are in your room.
These complaints aside, the Hotel Tomo is a great experience and a great departure from the normal hotel design. It's proximity to Japantown and short drive time to everything else in San Francisco are a plus.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Handlery for 4 nights, 4 very comfortable nights! We are missing the comfort of our Handlery bed. We usually get home and are thankful to be in our own bed, but not this time! We took advantage of the shuttle to Sea World and the Zoo. It is fantastic! We even called and asked to be picked up early one day and the shuttle was there in about 10 minutes. The shuttle driver is a very nice man. 
The hotel area is great, only a short walk to a mall and a train. We spent one day riding the train to different areas: seaport village, gaslamp district, and it cost $5 for an all day ticket. The train was very easy and convenient to use. The front desk gave us a map of the train routes. 
I had read some bad reviews about the free breakfast, but we loved it. The breakfast ticket cards make it seem like you can only pick one item on the card but this is not true. We had delicious fruit every morning, strawberries, and melons. There was yogurt and muffins and you could ask for toast, bagels, english muffins, cereal, and oatmeal. They left a pitcher of coffee on the table for you to help yourself and it was very good coffee. We always looked forward to breakfast. 
All the staff at the hotel were very friendly, I felt like every time I passed anyone I was greeted with a smile. The people at the front desk helped us out multiple times. Our room was always very clean. The maintenence man helped us one day with our balcony door. He was there in about 5 minutes and fixed the problem very quickly. Very nice man. We had a balcony in our room, which I highly recomend. It does not cost much more and it is so nice to have fresh air and a nice place to sit. 
The hotel restuarant was a little pricey for us (i'm sure it compares with surrounding area prices) so we ate elsewhere. I highly recomend the spaghetti factory in the gaslamp district, really good food and prices! We did have the restuarant pizza one night and it was delicious!
I was surprised when we checked out that we had a water fee. I just didn't realize that it cost something, if it had a little tag on it with a price I would have known. 
I was pleasently surprised with how quiet it was at night. I normally am awoken a lot when I stay somewhere, but it was very quiet here. Maybe we just got lucky with our neighbors, but it allowed me to get a nice nights rest on my wonderful bed!
All in all it is a great hotel and I would stay here again!

title: “A good central hotel.”
text: We stayed at the Warwick for just 2 days at the start of our extended trip and found the rooms excellent and the hotel was central for everything. The hop on hop off bus stopped just outside it so you couldn't get better than that. Would recommend

title: “Great location”
text: Good location and nice rooms, the price is accordingly.

title: “Simply awesome”
text: We had a wonderful time. The resort grounds are beautiful, the rooms comfortable, and the amenities are outstanding. This resort is a perfect getaway for families. There was so much to do. We rented bikes, visited the pools, fed the ducks, used the Spa and especially enjoyed taking the resorts water taxi to a private entrance at Sea World. I read some of the online reviews that say that rooms are not up to snuff, but I disagree. If you are expecting a high rise cookie cutter hotel, then this is not for you. The resort is located on a private island and the bungalows are spread over many acres, so you never feel like you are in an overcrowded resort. The staff is extremely friendly and really gave us the feeling that they tried hard to help us with whatever we needed. Don't forget to visit Barefoot. The kids will be entertained looking at the fish and sharks in the ponds while you sit and relax watching the sunset over the bay. We definitely will be back.

title: “Good value near the Magnificent Mile”
text:
My husband and I only stayed one night while we were in town for an event (and basically only needed a clean place to sleep since we would be out most of the time). The Fairfield Inn & Suites is located in downtown Chicago--specifically Streeterville--and is close to the Magnificent Mile, the Water Tower, and Northwestern Memorial Hospital. In fact, our room actually faced the hospital and the sounds of ambulance sirens were heard throughout the night--if this sort of thing bothers you, you might want to specifically request a room on the other side. Otherwise, the room itself was clean and updated with flat screen tv, alarm clock with i-pod dock, and duvets on the bed. The duvet covers were a little on the thin side, but the bedding was clean and comfortable. 
The bathroom was pretty basic--certainly nothing fancy, but again, it was clean and everything worked properly, which is plenty for a brief overnight stay.
We booked our room directly through Marriott's website and couldn't have been more pleased with the low rate--for a room in Chicago, it was definitely a good value. Valet parking with in and out privileges was included in this particular rate along with free wi-fi and free continental breakfast. The lowest rate at the time of booking (other than the one we selected) did not include parking but would be an incredibly good deal for those traveling without a car (the Red Line is a few blocks away). Parking is otherwise pretty expensive, so it's nice if you're able to travel without a car and save some cash. Be sure to look at all the available rates (standard, special packages, etc) when booking to see if there's anything more suited to your needs. I would definitely recommend this hotel to travellers who want to stay downtown without having to pay the usual high price for downtown convenience. 
I also want to add that the staff was really friendly and welcoming. After we checked out, we wanted to walk around a bit more and grab some lunch before heading out of town, so the front desk nicely stored our bags for us and we were able to keep our car parked through the valet long after check-out. 
We had a good (albeit short) stay at the Fairfield Inn and Suites and would definitely consider going back next time we're in Chicago.

title: “Nice stay in good location”
text: We recently spent a long weekend at the Palomar in Chicago and found it, overall, a good experience. We informed them ahead of time that we would need an early check-in but, upon arrival, that wasn't available. They did hold our luggage while we went out for brunch and some sight-seeing. The room was nice although not very large. The bathroom was very nice with a great shower and tub. The location of the room on the 12th floor and the end of the hallway was very quiet as far as hotel noises but it is hard to escape the noise of the nearby fire station! The free coffee in the morning as well as the wine hour in the evening was a very nice addition to our stay and gave us some time to socialize with the other guests.

title: “Superb position with good quality service”
text:
The hotel is positioned just away from the busiest part of Times Square. We had adjoining rooms on the 16th floor which were larger than I expected. This was a special trip for our Silver Wedding Anniversary with our 3 daughters (only one a teenager but that seemed the nearest box to tick!). Our bedroom had a huge bed and the bathroom had a huge shower. The girls' room had two double beds and the bathroom had a bath with (powerful) shower over it. For such a busy area there was relatively little noise, although there was such nighttime drilling outside on the last night - not the hotel's fault. Frankly we did so much walking, nothing would have kept me awake. 
The staff are really helpful and happy to chat especially those on the concierge desk. You can also check in online using the hotel's business section computers. 
I can't think of anything adverse to say except the position of the hotel was too close to American Eagle which only encouraged my daughters' shopping habits! Compensation? It's close when you're walking home having paid the bill at 1.45 am!
Seriously there are some fantastic sights to see in New York. We visited Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island, the Top of the Rock (gives wonderful views of the Empire State Building), took in a Mets baseball game, walked and (husband) ran in Central Park, toured Grand Central Station, had lunch in Bryant Park, walked onto Brooklyn Bridge, visited Ground Zero and used the subway quite a lot as we also did some shopping. The highlight for most of us was the baseball game and a visit to the Lower Tenement Museum on the Lower East Side.
We can't wait to return!

title: “Historic Building and Great Location and Views”
text:
This is not your average hotel, in fact it’s not a hotel but part of the Marriot Vacation Club properties (timeshare) and one of their only urban locations. The rooms are actually 1 bedroom villas with a bedroom and separate living room/kitchenette. It’s great for when you want more room than a typical hotel room with the living room and kitchenette (small fridge, microwave, bar sink and misc kitchen items – blender, toaster, dishes and silverware). Rooms are nicely appointed and the building is so unique and full of history in a perfect location for seeing Boston. Yes is can be a little noisy on weekends as the next block has several busy bars, but it wasn’t too bad but could be an issue on lower floors. The views are great and the higher you go the better. The bed was good but may be a little firm for some and didn’t seem to be the typical Marriott mattress. 
It sounds like the villas are all great but we stayed in one of 2 Eagle Suites on the 21st floor and would have to say they were very special due to private the two private balconies. One balcony was fairly large (4’x20’) nestled between two of the Custom House Eagle statues on the side of the building that had an amazing view of the city and a smaller Balcony (2x4) overlooked Faneuil Hall and the North End. Even if you don’t have your own private balconies the open air observation area on the 26th floor has got to be one of the best views of Boston and it has seats/tables to relax and watch the city and harbor. 
We will be back and already talking about brining family to visit to this property for a unique Boston experience.

title: “Excellent Experience!!!”
text:
Although this may be overlooked, I feel that I must bring to your attention thru this letter the outstanding customer service that I received from Gisselle Suazo from your Reservations Team.
I am, of course, very delighted to have had the pleasure of staying at your hotel on my recent visit to New York on this Thanksgiving weekend. I travel often to the Dominican Republic as well and also stay at the Intercontinental V Centenario.
Gisselle Suazo’s professionalism, courteous attitude, knowledge and attention to details were very important to my complete overall customer satisfaction. She was very sensitive to all my needs and I am deeply appreciative of her assistance and support.
She handled all my issues as if they were her own, and I’m completely satisfied. And thanks to Gisselle, upon my return to New York, me and my family will continue to stay at the Intercontinental Barclay Hotel.
I am sure that you will make a note of this and hope that you will pass the thanks on to her.
Sincerely,
Mr Jose Rotger and family

title: “Just ok... somewhat disappointing”
text:
We stayed at the Boston Park Plaza Hotel for 3 nights in November 2011, including Thanksgiving.
I'll start with the good points and our main reasons for choosing this hotel in the first place:
1) The location of this hotel is pretty good, a 2 minute walk to Boston Common, and from there you can walk easily to many attractions including the Freedom Trail, the Boston State House, the Old State House, the Irish Famine Memorial, Faneuil Hall and Quincy Market. Its also about a 20 minute walk to the shops at Prudential Centre, and very close to the shops of Newbury Street (nice for window shopping, not so nice for your credit card!)
2) The bedroom and bathroom was clean. 
3) We got an ok rate online, not exactly cheap or a great deal, but it fell within a reasonable budget and it seemed a bit cheaper than many other hotels in the city.
And now the bad points:
Firstly, the "ok" rate we paid for the hotel did not include breakfast. The hotel did not offer complimentary wi-fi access. There was a charge of $10 a day for this service. 
While on the subject of additional charges, we got a taxi from Boston Logan Airport to the hotel for around $20. Not bad. On arrival, I was surprised to see in the information packet in the room that the hotel offered a shuttle service to the airport. It did not say whether or not this service was complimentary, but instructed us to book a place on the shuttle through the concierge staff. When I asked the concierge she picked up the phone and began the process of booking our place on the shuttle, and then informed me that she would need my credit card details. I asked how much it would cost, and was told that it would be $19 per person. Thats $38 for 2 people, compared to the $20 taxi ride on our way in. I told her "no thanks, it would be cheaper to just take a taxi" and I apologized for wasting her time. She smiled and said nicely, "Yes, you're right, a taxi really is much cheaper." This little tidbit of advice would have been helpful at the start of our conversation, before she picked up the phone to call the external company that handle the airport shuttle service. Tip: Take a taxi to/from the airport to avoid getting ripped off!
Another negative in my opinion: while the hotel is an historic building, and quite "grand" in that sense, it also feels a bit tired and stuffy. The fondue restaurant on the premises only highlights this extremely dull and dated image.
The walls are very thin! From our bedroom we could hear every sound made in the next rooms. Maybe we were unlucky enough to have extremely noisy guests on either side of us, but we did have to turn up the volume on the tv at night to drown out the loud voices, and we had to complain to the front desk to eventually get them to stop the racket. In fairness, once we did complain, the hotel staff knocked on the door and asked them to keep down the noise. (Again, we could hear all of this word-for-word from our bed!) Maybe we could have asked to switch rooms, but for a 3 night stay we decided to just stick it out. The noisy guests woke me at 3:30am on the second night, and while they seemed to have checked out by the third night, they were replaced by a family with squealing children in the room to our other side.
While walking down the corridor to our room one day I heard a dog barking from inside one of the bedrooms. It made me think 1) I'm lucky we're not staying next to that room seeing as the walls are so thin, and 2) As much as I love animals it made me shudder a little because I didn't think to ask for a room on a floor that doesn't allow pets. 
There was a really large queue at check-out (perhaps due to the Thanksgiving holidays) but what bothered me was that while the queue stretched across the entire width of the lobby, there were only two staff checking-out the guests. At the next desk, the two concierge staff seemed to just stand there and watch. It would be better for all staff to be trained to help out in each area when busy, or else just stay out of sight instead of blatantly standing there looking bored. 
There are perhaps a few other negative points, but I'd put that down to our bad luck, and won't get personal in the actual review. 
Overall, the hotel is just ok. I wouldn't recommend it to a friend, and if you can get a good rate in a similar location I'd take the chance with another hotel.

title: “Review”
text: The staff was very personable and friendly. Would have liked more breakfast choices - perhaps small boxes of cereal, more fruit, etc.

title: “Honeymooners only hotel”
text: The hotel is very nice, and luxurious. From a personal point of view, i would highly recommend the hotel for clubs and honeymooners (the hotel is very calm, cozy, and kinda romantic).

title: “A Wonderful Experience At Nine Zero”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for three nights. We drove through a blinding snowstorm New Years Day for 4 and 1/2 hours and arrived as you can imagine pretty worn out. From the first moment until our check out the hotel staff did everything to make our stay relaxing and memorable. Our room, a high floor with a terrific view of the skyline, was spacious, especially for a large city hotel (we're used to the shoe boxes we stay in for twice the price in New York). The whole atmosphere is classy but not pretentious. We had been vactioning in Maine, skiing and hiking, and we felt completely comfortable at Nine Zero in our jeans and sweaters. The evening wine reception is a nice touch. The housekeeping staff was so accomodating with a coffee pot and extra pillows. The front desk was so helpful, right down to printing our boarding passes for our flight home. The restaurants recommended to us were all universally terrific. Just the right feel for our casual vacation. I would recommend this hotel for a romantic get away or celebration as it never felt stuffy - just fun. Great design, great staff. A terrific experience.

title: “This can't be Westin standards!”
text:
We were sooo looking forward to this vacation that when we opened the room door we were stunned by the floor-to-wall window view of the space needle. But that was the high-point... As other reviewers have pointed out, the carpet was simply dirty and needs replacing ASAP. Next, the bathroom was stinky. It smelt like mold. Maybe the shower curtain needed to be replaced as well. Wi-Fi was chargeable - really in this day and age it should have been free.
Pikes place is a good walk from the hotel and the monorail to the space needle is close by.
Westin seems to nickel-and-dime you on all little amenities that you get for free at other places.
We would definitely look elsewhere for our next trip to the great northwest.

title: “Good location, rooms starting to show wear and tear, lower floors can be noisy”
text: Great location right by Times Square. I stayed here for three nights in February 2012. I was on the 52nd floor which is a good thing considering the windows do not insulate very well against the noise. The room had an OK size for New York, but what was once a very modern hotel about 10 years ago is now starting to show some obvious wear and tear. The bathroom has a frosted window to the bedroom, so you get a pretty good view of what your room-mate is doing in there. Also, since the sliding door to the bathroom didn't really close completely shut, you would hear everything as well. The bar is nice, busy and trendy, with great cocktails, and the concierges are quite helpful.

title: “Two Thumbs Up”
text:
My fiance and I stayed at the hotel this past weekend and we really enjoyed the location, the room, and the customer service. I was disappointed we had to pay $50 a day for parking. I do have a few minor complaints, the toilet paper was super thin, the shampoo/body soap did not lather well so bring your own shampoo and soap, and no mini refrigerator in the room.
The hotel lobby decor was really trendy and I would definitely stay in the hotel again for the same price I paid online.

title: “Excellent stay”
text:
We enjoyed our stay at the Hilton Union Square very much. Check -in went very quickly despite the many travellers visiting this hotel. We had reservations for two double rooms, since we're a family of six, but were upgraded with one double room and one suite. The suite turned out to be very comfortable during our stay with teenage kids. The hotel is situated within few minutes of walking distance to very many points of interests. China town, Mario Botta's building of Moma, beautiful gardens, great shopping area, nice restaurants.
We had a great time in San Francisco and one of the reasons I would without any doubt visit this hotel again in the future is the great service of the staff.

title: “Dallas favorite”
text: Very comfortable room, great bar and excellent location

title: “This historic hotel has some pleasant surprises”
text: The DC Fairmont has some pleasant surprises...the delightful view of the courtyard lit at night with a myriad of little white lights along with the sound of fountains provided a relaxing atmosphere to enjoy from the balcony. The fountains also help block out noise inevitable in a major city. The room was not really big or really small, but it was nice to have a little sofa to sit or put your stuff on. My room curiously did not have a mini bar, although it had a spot for it. Vending machines are only on a couple floors, so it was an adventure to get ice and a soda. The bed was comfortable, and the shower water pressure okay. Beautiful lobby.

title: “big bright room, affordable price--great option for midtown Manhattan”
text:
After relievedly checking out of a truly dismal hotel 2 blocks East, we had low expectations for this place. Well...what a nice surprise! The room was ready early, and was far larger and brighter and nicely furnished than the internet photos conveyed. Yes, as some have said, walls could use a fresh coat of paint, but the few scuff marks were a minor detail.
We had a corner room on 11th floor. Beds were fine, the room very large, with a small kitchenette. We tried some of the pillows on the "pillow menu" but came back to the basic ones. The building was originally an apartment building, which explains the large number of closets, unusual in a hotel.
Having a refrigerator was a nice plus--we did not cook in the room, but there was a small stove. We did not like the open inviting "wet bar" and asked if , assuming we had kids, the candy bars, etc, could be removed, and they said yes. Beware if you arrive with young kids (or sweet-loving hungry adults).
The second floor public area is nice and roomy. On one side, there's a fireplace, and movies are shown (DVD on large screen) on Friday nights, a nice and cosy idea for a rainy evening when we didnt fancy a wet walk. ON the otehr side, there is a coffee maker where you can make espresso drinks, but i never did figure it out!
Front desk and concierge were professional and polite, not overly warm. But one of the door men was fantastic, a true New Yorker--a big smile and greeting whenever we left or entered. Real New York City friendliness, IMHO! (disclaimer--i lived there for 20 yrs!)
Also, the young lady who managed housekeeping was terrific, caring and very friendly and helpful with some situations we encountered. The housekeeper must've been a bit distracted--one day leaving a bed unmade, another leaving a window wide open (in winter) with the aroma of fast-food from the McD's on street level filling the room when we returned. But what made an impression wasn't that these events happened, but the speed with which they were sorted out by the manager, making a good interaction from what could have been a negative.
There is a 24 hour food shop one corner up (on 3rd at 51st) and we stocked up on late-night goodies there. The neighborhood felt quite safe for two women, at any time of day or night. 
For the return trip to JFK we used Execucar, with an excellent and helpful driver. It was less money than one recommended by the hotel concierge.
One aspect in which the hotel could improve is setting up computers in the second floor lobby and offering free internet use.

title: “Perfect San Francisco Hotel”
text:
We just returned from our Easter trip. My family was pleasantly welcomed by the door man "Ken" He gave us tips on the area and chatted like he was a dear friend.
Next we approached the front desk and again, greeted warmly ! Then our sweet "Benji" took us to our room (Our home- sweet- home for the next 4 days)
We requested a gold fish for our 8 year old daughter. She was thrilled with "Spacehog" THANKS !!
We were amazed at the warm greetings (by name) each time we passed by staff. Rooms are charming and have style. Great wine hour. Nice restaurants. A perfect hotel and I'm VERY picky. Tuscan Inn and MacArthur Place could learn from this place. Miss the Monaco already !

title: “Decent hotel with standard amenities. Great area for dining, shopping and night life”
text: Stayed at this hotel for an overnight trip in Boston. Staff was very friendly and acccomodating. Room was spacious with a lot of area to move around. Only complainant was the low water pressure in the shower. Standard amenities. Lobby had a beer tasting in the evening which was nice. Ample space in the lobby to relax and unwind. Hotel is close to restaurants and shopping.

title: “Good location with a few minor flaws”
text:
We just ended a 5 day stay. The room was comfortable, albeit a little small. A view of an air shaft and an alleyway. That's fine with us, as it was very quiet. Comfortable bed with a really icky cover over the foot of the bed that just screamed to be folded and put away. Looked like a real great place for fleas and germs and whatever. The elevators worked fine, and their little wine reception at 5pm was a nice try, although with cheap wine and not enough seating, we only really went once. Breakfast was good, with a nice view of an old cemetery across the street. You can look right at the grave site of Sam Adams! 
The restaurant in the building is, I was told, closing soon. Oddly, it is not aggressively promoted by the hotel. The food is REALLY first class as was the service. One of the very best meals we had in a 9 day trip to NYC and Boston. It's in the same space as breakfast, but a complete transformation at night. Fabulous service too.
No coffee maker in the room!! Big negative for us. After getting home, I saw a small charge (about $5) on our debit card. I called them. No response, so I guess we just eat it. It looks like a phony charge from the mini-bar which we didn't use at all. I thought nice hotels had stopped doing this. For $300 a night, they should maybe ask when you check out. 
All in all, a great location, but not quite worth the money. We had a much better value at the Hilton in New York.

title: “Great Location”
text:
Remarkably great for tourists, near the Pike Place Market & bus lines. Had zero construction problems. Rooms were clean, neat. Staff & Service were as expected. 
Didn't like the ridiculously high nightly fee to park the car

title: “Completely profession, value for money”
text:
this is a best place to stay if you need to attend anything at Moscone Centre. This is located just a block away from this business centre.
it was very comfortable stay over there, Room rent was slightly on a higher side but worth paying that money.

title: “Nice hotel experience”
text:
I stayed at the Hamilton Crowne Plaza for four days after Thanksgiving 2007. The hotel has an intimate feel compared with other large chain hotels. The staff were always friendly and courteous, the room was spacious and most importantly, clean. The extra touches of the drape clip, night light and Sleep Advantage CD made my stay a wonderful experience.
The hotel is in a good location - in walking distance to the White House and other Washington monuments and a CVS drugstore is just up the street for any last minute requirements 
 Would I stay there again? You bet I would.

title: “Great location in old style hotel.”
text: Good place to stay in heart of San Francisco without doing the hotel chain deal. Room felt quite modern and was spacious. Nice pool area too w heated pool. Just one block from Unipn Square's shopping and an easy walk to convention center if your in town for meeting.

title: “Great staff”
text:
I had high expectations after reading about staff quality on tripadvisor. It showed within the first minute of contact. When I phoned from the airport to request the complimentary shuttle bus, I was given clear instructions of where and when to board. Once the shuttle arrived, the very courteous Berlon ( bellman who also acted as driver ) apologized to us that he had to go to terminal 1 to pick up a couple more guests. Upon check in, Melissa was very professional, and offered us 500 Starwood points if we chose to decline housekeeping( we picked this over the $5 coupon for food and beverages) The snack " buffet" table was a nice touch. Fruit flavoured cold water was also highly utilised.
The day of check out, I approached a manager and asked about complimentary shuttle , and found out that his name was Nathan, but NOT that Nathan. The hotel staff called THAT Nathan "Tripadvisor Nate" so they really enjoyed being written up here!
I did not give 5 stars in my rating due to (a) no free wi fi in room, and lobby wi fi was not comfortable as almost all the chairs were exposed to the wind whenever the front door opened. We were there on those breezy days, so guests who go at better weather days would not have that issue and (b) in room cups were very flimsy, of the very cheaper and light weight variety. Four and a half stars would be my assessment.

title: “Didn't get much sleep...”
text:
My husband, myself and 2 year old son stayed at the Wyndham. We are Wyndham members and like to usually stay at a Wyndham if there's one in town. My husband stumbled onto this one for $87 a night. 
When we checked in we got an average room. It didn't have that "Wyndham" quality that I've encountered at other places. This place had a cheaper feel to it. Mu husband also noticed some kind of smoke stench in the room. (we did book a non-smoking room). And what drove us nuts about the room is that we didn't have a clock. What hotel room doesn't have a clock?
When we were ready to put our son to sleep, we heard a huge concert starting up in one of the banquet rooms on the 3rd floor. Well, this concert kept going til 3am. My husband called down to complain at 2:30am and they only thing the front desk could tell us is that it was only supposed to last 30 minutes more. 
On the way down to check out the next morning after only 3-4 hours of sleep, we noticed that the whole 3rd floor smelled of marijuana. Disgusting. We complained about the concert and they treated us to breakfast. The least the hotel could have done was to warn the guests of this concert or put us the furthest away from the music. Totally disgraceful.

title: “PERFECT LOCATION”
text: I loved this hotel! I was so concerned about getting around NY without a car... but the taxis are always right outside the door. MacDonalds, Subway, a great Chinese restaurant are all within a block. Market too. Taxi rates are more reasonable than I thought. (My husband and I tried the subway... didn't quite work out!). Hotel older but very clean, friendly, 25 stories, great street, kitchenettes, large windows... loved it!

title: “Staff nice, but....”
text: We stayed here as it was the only Seattle airport hotel that was available through "airmiles". We wouldn't do it again. The staff were pleasant, I'll give you that. The shuttle driver for the airport transfer was very polite and friendly. The rooms are standard Best Western, depressing and showing wear and tear. What really got us was the breakfast area. The carpets are filthy and there were 2 buckets placed out in the middle of the floor to catch the water from roof leaks. The floor around the buffet area was sticky, and the food selection (hard boiled eggs kept warm in a crock pot, cold biscuits with a nasty congealed white sauce with some kind of chopped up meat to pour over them- I could go on, but you may want to eat again sometime soon) There is an IHOP close by and that would be the best bet if you need to eat there. All in all, we really couldn't recommend this place and we won't stay there again, even just on as a stop over spot.

title: “cosy and budget, but excellent location and ambience”
text:
Tiny cabin room, but perfectly formed and retro - really looks like a ship's cabin. Very comfortable bed. Quite noisy aircon if staying in humid summer and need to have it on.
Right in the heart of meatpacking district on safe street. 
View of Statue of Liberty from bathroom.
Stunning and authentic hallway.
Shared bathroom with lots of people - don't know if would have been a wait if using at peak times
Some rooms rented by long-stayers dating back to when it was a YMCA, but didn't realise til was told. Adds to the atmosphere.
Very helpful front desk staff 24/7 - keeping baggage stored for extra days, recommending bars, taxi spots, internet locations, helping with phone use

title: “Homewood Suites Phoenix-Biltmore Hotel”
text: Generally, the hotel is good and clean. Service is also good. The price is reasonable and included everything that you probably need. Free Wi-Fi is a plus. There is a kitchen inside which includes a large fridge, a stove, an oven, and a microwave, and this allows you to buy fresh food from a local supermarket, Trader Joe’s. Even if you are too lazy to cook anything, just buy something off restaurants.

title: “Not worth the cost of parking”
text:
We have stayed at this hotel before. It is a nice hotel, with a nice upper floor restaurant and lounge. The food was delicious, I believe a little over priced for such small portions.
The room itself is nice enough. 
We self parked in the garage of the hotel. It cost $30 per night. We could have had the valet park for the same cost. I do not think the room or the hotel is nice enough to pay $60 in parking. I realize this is the going rate, but the hotel should maybe have specials with parking included for guests fo the hotel. We will not be staying her any time soon

title: “Location, location, location!!”
text: This hotel was literally behind Hollywood Blvd, the location was perfect, we would walk out of the hotel, up the street and we were on Hollywood Blvd, it took approx. one minute, this is how close we were. As for the hotel, it's not very fancy by all means, but it was quiet, we slept very well. Our room was cleaned every day by housekeeping, and we always had a change of fresh towels. I did have a few problems with the TV, I had to ask them twice to come and fix it and they did. Also, the toilet did make a bit of noise, like I said it is not a fancy hotel, but we didn't spend time in our room anyways, it was a place to sleep and that was all. As for the breakfast, you can expect bagels, toast, muffins, cereal, orange juice and milk! I would recommend this hotel if you just want a place to lay your head and be close the action!

title: “Great place to stay!!”
text: Rooms were great! Good food in the lounge. They had a soccer tournament with groups staying here so it was a little loud, once in the bedroom you couldn't hear anything. Hotel staff was very nice and friendly.

title: “GOOD BUDGET HOTEL”
text:
Myself and 3 friends stayed at the hotel. I think we stayed in a suite but they put a double bed in the living room so we paid less. It was a bit of a squease with 4 girls in there but we had 2 bathrooms, the second being quite small but it did the job & we had a bath in the main bathroom! The beds were made everyday and there was a phone in the room, 2 tv's and a hairdryer (which was a bit slow so take you own but with the voltage difference my own was painfully slow).
The staff were eager to please but the lift was a pain as it stopped at every floor on the way down and up! They organised our limo to the airport as one of the waiters new someone and got us a cheap deal.
There is a diner under the hotel which serves good food at a good price.
The hotel is in an excellent location to Times Square but not too close to hear the noise, about 5 minutes walk.
I would not hesitate in recommending this hotel if you are on a budget.

title: “OK not brilliant”
text:
Stayed in this hotel because my boyfriend was doing a marathon in DC..(NB not great for getting taxi back from finishing line! most streets were closed off around the hotel and taxi driver didn't know how to get through the road closures...)
Expecting same standard as Mandarin Oriental Boston and very disappointed when we entered the room. Very tired looking and no wow factor. Average service at the reception/concierge with some deficiency in local knowledge.
Location is good if you want to visit museum but absolutely no where to eat nearby at night. Starbucks and CVS pharmacy opposite the hotel were the only thing around. In fact it was like ghost town after 5pm. Had room service one night. It was the most awful but the most expensive crab sushi i have ever tasted in my life.
Good gym though.
Don't pay extra to stay in this Mandarin. Stay only with corporate discount.

title: “Convenience and comfort merit return trip”
text: The downtown location next to the Museum of Contemporary Art and the Disney Concert Hall was superb. They have a free shuttle service for trips within 3 miles, which we used to go to Union Station. The bed was extremely comfortable. The breakfast buffet, although expensive, was very good. Minor complaints include no reading light near the lounge chair, having to ask twice for a tourist map of the area and charges for parking when we didn't have a car. We plan to stay here again for our next trip to L.A.

title: “Always Great”
text:
I go to SF at least once a year, sometimes twice and have for almost ten years now.
Consistanly, the Parc 55 hotel is always a pleasant stay and a reasonably priced hotel to stay in. Another key factor I like about Parc 55 is there seems to always be a room available.
It's not the only hotel I have enjoyed in San Francisco, and it's not the only one I will return to, but it's one of the few I can say I loved the stay, I loved the room, I love the view, the price is always reasonable (comparably) and I will be back. Try to get into one of the higher floors.

title: “elevator is frustrating”
text: We just got back from the Red Roof Inn in NYC. We stayed there last year and it was fine so we went again this time. It smells of roach spray which was new, and they apparantly have no service elevator so you usually have to squeeze in with a maid and her cart or a janitor and his junk! I know it's not a fancy hotel but for $239 a night you don't need to have to deal with that. It's OK, room is clean and overall just a place to sleep when you are in the city. The Tudor Hotel seems to be alot nicer for just a little more money, we will go there next time. TIP: feel free to use the rooftop bar at LaQuinta across the street! They are owned by the same company, not that anyone asks you anything when you walk in...it's a nice place to have a beer outside on a pleasant night.

title: “Two things not up to Marriott standards”
text:
It is fine except that the air-conditioning never really got cool enough. I think it's one of those systems where if the outside ambient termperatutre goes below a certain point, the compressor turns off.
Also, the pool -- besides being one of those wacky shapes that makes it impossible to swim laps unless one of your arms is shorter than the other -- had more chlorine than any pool I've been in since the 1980s. Even more than the Washington DC drinking water.
A word to travelers who are taking cabs to their destination the next morning (as opposed to the two other options LA offers -- renting a car or walking). Don't hang at the main entrance if there is a line, which moves slowly. Simply walk down the driveway to where the cabs are waiting. Faster, and you save the obligatory doorman tip.

title: “Great Hotel in ideal location”
text: After looking at the Ritz and the Essex House, we decided to stay at the Helmsley Park Lane and were pleasantly surprised! I was a little worried since we only paid @ $300 for one night and I also knew that the hotel's rooms were slightly older. HOWever, it was the perfect place to stay. My husband and I will definitely stay here again. We arrived early (1pm) and our room was ready for us complete with an amazing view of Central Park below! I believe we were on the 33rd floor; the view was incredible. We invited one of our friends up who lives on the Upper West Side in Manhattan and even she said she had never seen a view of Central Park like ours! The rooms were well kept, clean, luxurious, and HUGE. . . for NYC, at least, and the bathroom was very nice, as well. Yes the decor is a tad older. . . imagine you are staying at your very wealthy Grandmother's apartment for the weekend. For the price we paid ($300/nite is a really good deal) you can't beat the view. Take a look at our pictures to see for yourself. The only thing we didn't like is that the Helmsley didn't seem to have a good bar to enjoy drinks at, so we went to the Ritz just a few hotels down. You're right there on 59th Street (Central Park South) and 5th Ave; the location is unbeatable!! Don't miss breakfast right next door at Sarabeths. You can't go wrong with the Helmsely. I dread the day they remodel as prices are sure to skyrocket. Just remember: Location, Luxury, and View. The Helmsley is a beautiful hotel with tremendous value.

title: “Would Recommend 100%”
text: Great, Safe Location. Would Definately stay Again. Very Clean, Friendly & Helpful. Shared Bathrooms, but they were always clean & available. Just across the road from a great 24hr cafe. Very Affordable. Lovely good sized room.

title: “It was the best of hotels, it was the worst of hotels”
text: We spent 6 nghts here, thanks to the world's best points credit card (Hyatt). Lesson #1 from our experience: get that card. They give you 2 free nights at any Hyatt...and that's before you start accumulating points. Here's what is best about this place: the room service, the pillows, the bathroom (and the vanities you can take home). Here's what's worst: perhaps they could add a little water to their chlorine. It might have enhanced the swimming experience. Our whole room still smells like chlorine. Also, usually when you ask for two beds, you get two doubles. We got two singles. Looks like a college dorm room. Next, you are nowhere near a Metro station. Finally, the breakfast is thoroughly mediocre. I'd recommend crossing the street and getting the full buffet from the competition.

title: “Awesome hotel, great location!”
text:
It was our 10 yr anniversary and I had mentioned it was in our reservation. Via Tripadvisor got 10% off. It was great from the very beginning! They even were prepared and greeted us by name.
The hotel was not huge, but it was enough for where you would normally need to go in SF. Lobby was nice, had some refresher drinks ready every day so when you came back from your long walk or journey you could just get some cups and get something there on that table. Nice touch.
Rooms were really nice.. great views. We got the cheapest King size room facing the street, but it was totally fine. You won't miss anything if you look for the lower priced rooms.
Hotel also gave us some chocolates to just say happy 10 year. Unexpected. 
The location I have to say was really great. It was in the middle of everything (drugstore, shopping, taxi's etc) so you don't have to worry about being in the middle of nowhere or far from where you want to be.
Tip: certain more expensive taxi's have some agreement with the hotel. If you want a cheaper taxi, just walk out of the hotel and then flag a taxi down. Those hotel taxis are nice for a date or something but if you just need to get to Chinatown or something you can save $10 or so.
I hear it's great with children but we went as a couple this time :)

title: “Wonderful service from the Concierge”
text:
I needed some help in a city far from home and Mr. Matt Blitch, the concierge on 3/6/12, surpassed my expectations. I told him I needed event tickets at a local venue but knew little else about it other than the name of the performer. He found the event and booked me a ticket in about five minutes. It took him less time than it took me to explain the help I needed.
Many thanks to Matt and the other fine staff at the hotel. I will definitely visit them again in future and recommend them to friends.
mw

title: “Location, room size, service and value are all outstanding”
text:
This hotel has a fantastic location, right in the heart of downtown walking distance to all attractions and the best restaurants and bars. Despite being on the busy Michigan Avenue the room was very quiet and being at the front had a great view.
