The room was unbelievably big for a city centre hotel with a good size bathroom, a bedroom, and a large lounge with kitchenette sofa and desk. They also all have washer/dryers which is a great touch.
The staff are all very friendly and helpful. Breakfast is included and is quite passable.
The bes thing about this hotel though is the price you get all this for, it is an absolute bargain.

title: “Hip Hotel amid all the action!”
text: This hotel is really cool...great location where you can walk around and find great restaurants, unique and very hip shops, street stalls and food, music, people watching and more - Austin at its best! The staff is pleasant and accommodating. If you are looking for an opulant room, you will not find it here, but you will find an extraordinarily well-designed, well organized room with great linens, bath products, water pressure in the shower and a terrace/balcony for every room. We love this trendy, unique hotel and would return every visit. We didn't get to dine, but they have a great-looking terrace bar/restaurant that was appealing and popular.

title: “Right on the river....”
text: Great location right on the river, at the top end of city. Quiet area more the business area and hotel serves mainly as a meeting place with many conferences and events held here. The lobby is huge and well decorated Its a very busy week for them whilst we are here but they accomodate everyone in a timely manner, rooms are lovely with everything you require. Taxis are instant when required at the front entrrance. We stayed 4 nights and the concierge was extremely helpful with anything we enquired about. Took the 3 day trolley hop on/off and with 14 stops could see the city extensively over those days or just catch it to a stop we required. Great idea and would recommend it to everyone...they are very funny tour guides also.. Great time had,

title: “Great Place to stay!”
text: I spent one night here and enjoyed my stay. It is located in a great location of Charlotte. You are within walking distance to the wonderful South Park Mall and several great restaurants. The rooms were very nice and the check in ladies were very friendly. You will not regret staying at this hotel.

title: “Oasis in Great Location Close to Theatres”
text: The Michelangelo was the perfect choice for our NYC weekend! Gershwin Theatre ("Wicked") only 1 1/2 blocks away; the red line direct route to ferry for Ellis Island 1 block away; short walk to Trattoria Trecolori just off Times Square for delicious Italian meal; 4 blocks to St. Patrick's for Sunday mass and a quick taxi ride for brunch at Tavern on the Green in Central Park. Entering the lobby from the busy street, all of a sudden everything was peaceful and calm. Ney, who helped us with our luggage, was pleasant and really friendly. Our room (#629) was tucked away in a very quiet corner of the hotel on the 6th floor - view from window was a wall, but it was like a skylight and the room was so nice the view didn't matter. We had one of the less expensive rooms - $199 special, but we found it very spacious, tastefully decorated, new? cream color carpet, really comfortable king bed, Bose radio, big fluffy towels and bathrobes. The extra taxes came as a bit of a surprise - our total for 2 nights was $491.42, but we still thought a great value. Don't know why we hadn't found the Michelangelo before, but it will be our hotel of choice from now on for special weekends in NYC.

title: “It was clean and cool not much more”
text: I was there overnight on business. It was late so I appreciated they had a shuttle pick me up. it was clean and the AC worked. I've stayed in Sleep Inns before and their breakfast rooms have been nice and organized. However when I arrived at at 7am, the tables weren't cleaned off. The layout was confusing and the person taking care of it was not "customer service" oriented; short unapologetic responses to requests. Giving her the benefit of the doubt, the place seemed short-staffed.

title: “Loved The Peabody's location”
text: Our room at the Peabody was nice. It looked like it had been recently renovated. The bed was comfortable but the pillows were horrible. The bedding was double sheeted with a down blanket and a nice duvet and throw pillow accents. There was a sitting area with a couch, chair , and armoire. The bath was small but clean and well appointed. One complaint is that they charge a $7.95 hotel fee for use of the athletic club, wireless internet, a daily newspaper (which we didn't receive), morning coffee from 5:30 to 7:00 a.m..(Too early for me), and unlimited local calls. This charge is added to the bill whether or not you use any of the services. Most upscale hotels offer this as an option and charged only if you use it. The location is great. It is in the heart of the Beale/Peabody Place action. The traffic tended to be noisy so make sure to ask for a room not facing Union St. Didn't eat at the restaurants as they were all very pricey. Parking is a nightmare, so simply spend the $21 per night to valet. Lastly, double check your bill before checkout. We had a $100 error that needed to be resolved before we were able to checkout.

title: “Great Hotel - Good Rates - Close to everything”
text:
We enjoyed our stay very much. We are not the type of travelers who require a lot of attention and this hotel more than met our standards; friendly, comfortable, affordable, clean and convenient.
This hotel is very nice, just completed a renovation and it shows. Beautiful! The rooms are sized just right, and it seems there is not a view thats is bad in DC. We faced the city but didn't have any spectacular views of anything special. We stayed with our 3 children on the 10th floor which is the executive level. We had breakfast, snacks, drinks etc everyday till 11pm in the lounge. 
The beds were comfy and plush. Down comforters and down pillows made our nights enjoyable. We had a flat screen tv in our room that worked just fine, no complaints. The remote had some issues but that may have been batteries. 
The hotel does have a pool that we used one evening when we were not busy. It was clean, and had a nice atmosphere. Quiet pool deck with the Washington monument in the far distance. Nothing fancy, just a rectangular pool and kiddie pool, but nice none the less.
I only have one complaint, our last night the ac keep shooting out hot air every hour or so. so it was hot then cold all night. We did not call anyone until the next morning because we had a long day and it didn't start until about 10pm and we were exhausted. Other than that, the hotel was perfect, courteous staff, efficient bellmen and doormen ready to call a cab at a seconds notice or open the door as you approach. 
Location was very convenient to Metro station in Dupont Circle and plenty of known restaurants.

title: “THE GRANDUCA DISAPPOINTS”
text:
I have been a frequent guest at the Granduca. I guess I kept hoping it would improve, but it hasnot. The Granduca has disappointed me for the last time and I will not return.
1. Do not order room service. I called and ordered a chesse plate one evening when I was working late. The menu desribed three types of cheese and grapes. An hour passed- no cheese plate. I called. The woman who answered the phone promised to look into it. She never called back. Another 15 minutes passed and I called. She said she was looking into it. She never called back. After another 15 minutes, I called. The waiter answered and explained he had delivered it to the wrong room. I suggested he make another and he seemed surprised at my suggestion. Finally, he brought me the "cheese plate" -- three large hunks of some white cheese a few crackers and some relish. When I complained that it was not what was described in the menu, he shrugged and left. I called the front desk and ask them to have the General Manager call me. She never did.
2. Do not use the laundry service. They are incapable of accounting for clothing. Most recently, they lost my navy blazer for a day before finding it and they lost all of my laundry for the last night of my stay and then argued with me about whether I gave them any laundry. When I explained that I personally gave the bag to the front desk at 7 am, they acted as if they did not believe me and began calling people who were on duty at that time. After three more calls, I walked down to the front desk and asked to see where they kept the laundry. They refused me. The finally found my laundry at the clearners they use. They told me I would have it by 9 am the next day because it was "in a machine and wet." I explained that a suit should be dry cleaned and it best not be "wet.". They again said I could get my laundry by 9 am--small comfort since my flight was scheduled to leave before they wanted to return my laundry. After makiing me wait for a couple of hours, they finally brought me my laundry. It was not wet. It was finished and hanging. So, they kept me up for a couple of hours waiting on my laundry and they did not seem to care. Again, I asked to speak to the General Manager. She did not call me.
3. Do not use the mini bar. They only re-fill the mini bar when they want to do so. During my most recent stay, they tried to do so only once-- when I had the privacy sign on the door. Indeed, they just opened the door and attempted to come right in. They never tried to re-fill it again. On the last day of my stay, I took a soda bottle from the mini bar and when I tried to open it, it exploded and glass cut my lip. I grabbed a towel and tried to stop the bleeding and when I finally got it under control, I called the front desk and explained what had happened. They said they would send a maid to clean up the glass and a first aid kit if I needed one.The maid did not arrive in the 30 mins that passed before I had to leave. Nice eh? If I ran the hotel and a guest had a soda bottle explode from the mini bar, I think I would have gone to the guest's room and apologized and expressed concern. The General Manager never called me to explain how a soda bottle might explode or why and they charged me for the beverage that exploded.
4. They are greedy. I stayed for almost a week before the Final Four in Houston and needed to stay for five more days starting on the Sunday when no game was played, including Monday-Wednesday nights. I have a regular corporate rate with Granduca that is reasonable and I am a frequent guest. Yet, the Granduca jacked up my rate to $650 a night for Sunday and Monday and refused to reduce it claiming the Final Four generated demand for the rooms. That might have been true before Butler and U Conn won their semi-final games and there were cancellations all over Houston by fans of other larger programs who hoped to see their teams in the finals. The Granduca has no customer loyalty at all and they took advantage of me and they know it.
5. There is no management. I have asked the front desk staff to see a manager on a half dozen cocassions. Most of those were met with blank stares. The only place I ever saw the General Manager was on the hotel channel on the TV where she promised to take care of my every need. I have never seen her on property in any of my visits and she has never once responded to any of the messages I left at the front desk to have her call me to discuss each of the aforementioned experiences.
6. They are unresponsive. If you call the front desk, the standard reply is "I will look into it." Apparently, "looking into it" rarely involves calling you back to let you know what they are doing about it. There is no sense of urgency in responding to my requests.
7. They are unreliable. You might get business packages addressed to you or they may end up in another guest room. It is a crap shoot. Sometimes, your TV's work and sometimes, they do not. Sometimes, your bedside clock is right and sometimes, it is not. Occassionally, the bedside clock alarm goes off because they forget to clear it before giving you a room. 
The Granduca has good bones-- a nice building; great rooms with lots of space and small kitchens; and a good location. But bones do not make a great hotel. A great hotel is about the service and there is no service at the Granduca.

title: “Hyatt does it again”
text: What a nice hotel! I had a spacious and beautiful room with a view of the bay bridge and the ferry terminal. Comfortable furniture and bed and and ipod dock. Convenient to the embacadero and bart. I'll stay here the next time i'm in san francisco, for sure.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for my bday weekend and we were very happy with the stay we had at the Westin. We were supposed to get a room from floors 1-7 but we mentioned it was my birthday and the front desk was very kind and moved our room to a higher level with an AMAZING view! The room was pretty small but they made everything fit and we had everything we needed. 
The hotel is located in central Union Square, so it was a great location and you can walk or catch a ride numerous ways at this location. The staff was very friendly and all in all we were very happy with our stay. We would definetly stay here again for our future visits to San Fran!

title: “No Complaints - did the job”
text: I stayed at the Edison last April with 3 girlfriends. We had a quad room for the 4 of us, because we were on a budget - we wanted the money to shop! Having read some of the bad reviews - I thought I'd write one - because we thoroughly enjoyed our stay here. It's not a palace - it's old fashioned, but our room was cleaned every day, and was big enough for the four of us to manage easily. When you go to New York, you don't go to spend time in your hotel room - so as long as it's clean it's fine. The staff on the front desk were always friendly, and the same applies to the Cafe Edison, where we had breakfast most mornings. I would recommend for a perfect location, and nice clean rooms.

title: “Excellent staff, great service,perfect location”
text:
Located one minute from Times square, close to Broadway, MOMA museum, with pleasant rooms, nice bar in the hotel, modern interior and above all- excellent staff this hotel is a perfect place for young people! 
Concierge at the hotel, girl named Ana, was very attentive. She helped us find the best tours around the city, tickets for Broadway show, advised us about City fast pass - that helps you save money and wait less for seeing attractions ... you name it.
The only drawback of the hotel was internet- we had to sign in to some site in order to get free internet in the room- took us some extra minutes but it was solvable.
For sure i would try to get the same hotel when i come to NY next time.

title: “Excellent!”
text:
We stayed here for Labor Day 2012. Checked in on Friday, our flight arrived early at about 10:30 and we had no problem getting an early check in. We had a relaxing day at the pool each time we were there. At no point did our glasses (both margarita's and water) ever get below half full before we were asked if we would like another! 
The valet staff was wonderful with recommendations and directions how to get to places both withing walking and driving distance. And even though it was a busy holiday weekend, the valet staff always greeted us by name!
Both the bar and restaurant and totally and completely top notch! Delicious drinks and if you go to Brunch have the Paper Bag Fried Chicken. It is amazing. The people watching at the bar is the best people watching ever.
We went to a concert at American Airlines and were offered a ride to the concert in the hotel Jaguar, we took a cab back but the offer and the drive were wonderful.
Make sure to go to the spa and get the Margarita Scrub treatment! It was heavenly and the spa staff was very friendly! 
Overall it was a heavenly 5 day stay and we can not wait to return just to stay at the hotel!!

title: “Not a good start but it got better”
text: We got to the hotel and our room was not ready yet. We decided to take the shuttle that the hotel provides to guests to the inner harbor area for lunch but it was running an hour behind schedule. We decided to walk. We finally checked in and our room was FILTHY, so the hotel switched our room to a much nicer one. The hotel manager (I believe her name was Claudia) wasquite generous and ensured that the proper wine and beer was delivered to our room. We were ready to head to happy hour at the Pier 5 hotel and once again the shuttle was running behind schedule so we decided to stay at the here at the hotel for the complimentary happy hour. This is were our day took a turn for the better. Dorien, the bartender at happy hour, truly made our day. He was great!! He turned a terrible day into a much better one. We were not happy thus far and Dorien was able to turn our day around. So much so that I came right back to the room to comment. I hope the rest of our stay continues to be positive, but I am skeptical.

title: “I almost forgot places like this still exist!!”
text:
I stay in hotels often and this is the first time I've actually been compelled to write a review!
When I arrived, I was greeted by Phil, an extremely gracious doorman, who had my luggage on a cart and my car off to the valet garage faster than I could blink! He brought me inside and promised that my items would be well taken care of. There were a few people on the line, and while I waited (only about a 5 minute wait), the manager Chris walked up and engaged me in conversation. He seemed to genuinely care that I was staying at the Adolphus! I've never seen a manager take the time to wander the lobby and greet his guests, finding out why they were staying here, if it was their first time in Dallas, etc. I overheard some guests telling an agent that it was their anniversary - Chris must have overheard this as well, because as soon as the couple was out of earshot, he jumped behind the desk and ordered up a complimentary bottle of champagne sent up to their room! How classy is that!!
The young lady who checked me in, Liz, I believe, was as sweet as can be. She took her time to find me the best room that they had available and introduced me to the bellman who would be taking my bags up (unfortunately, I have misplaced his name, but he was very professional and efficient). As I headed up the escalator, under the opulent chandelier, and into the incredibly gorgeous upper lobby, I really felt like I had been whisked away to the golden years!
My room, a standard room I believe, was large and spacious - much more so than your Hiltons or Hyatts - and adorned with vintage-looking though well-kept furnishings. I had one of the best sleeps of my life that night on the ridiculously comfortable bed.
The next morning, as I headed downstairs, there was Chris again, in the lobby chatting up guests. I swear - does he ever go home? I was surprised when he remembered me by name and asked how my room was and if I needed anything. The hotel appeared to be quite busy - how could he remember one guest amongst hundreds? He's a treasure, to be sure.
Eve, or Eva, checked me out that morning - efficeient and friendly. There was a bit of a delay waiting on my car, but nothing worth docking points for. There were some grumpy people not happy about the wait - seriously, folks, calm down a bit! Is that 5 minutes of your life really worth getting your blood presure up?
If you're tired of staying in carbon copy, boxy "modern" hotels where you're just another room number, try the Adolphus! These guys know how to do it right!

title: “Overall a good stay”
text:
I just returned a few days ago from a weekend stay at the Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden. I chose the hotel based on price, and it's proximity to Penn Station, as one day of my trip was going to be spent on the Jersey Shore, and I wanted to be close to Penn Station for when I needed to catch my train.
We (there was two of us) arrived Sat morning, and the room wasn't ready, but the desk clerk let us store our bags and let us know the free breakfast was still available, so we went and had something to eat. The breakfast room was very nice, a little crowded, but the food selection was good, and also tasted very good. They had bagels, muffins (kinds changed daily, the blueberry were excellent!), a couple hot dishes, like eggs and another that changed daily, we saw sausage and gravy one day and just sausage patties the next to make biscuit sandwiches. There's also some fresh fruit, 3 different types of cereals, juices, coffee and tea (served all day). The seating area does also contain two outside tables. 
The room itself was small, but nice. We had two double beds, which were VERY comfortable, a TV that was mounted on the wall, a desk and chair, and a closet. If you want to watch TV and sit in the chair, you may have to move it and sit between the beds like we did, if you prefer not to sit on the bed. There's also a lap desk to hold your laptop if you don't feel like sitting at the desk. 
The room was clean, overall, though there was some ground in stains in the carpet near the window, and the shower curtain had a blood stain on it. The high speed internet access was very good, it only went out on me once briefly, and it's free, which is a huge plus. The hotel writes an access code on your keycard packet at checkin, so make sure to look for it, or ask the desk clerk to point it out to you. We had to call down and ask them where to find it, as they didn't point it out to us at check in. It also expired the morning of check out, before we even checked out, so we had to call down to the desk and get a new one. There's two bottles of water in the room, be aware that their $5 a bottle if you want to have one! 
The staff overall seemed friendly enough. They replaced our keycards with no problem when asked when one got deactivated and no longer worked. There's a 24 hr fitness center on the lower level, and a "business center" in the lobby, consisting of two computers, which are always busy. Their hooked up to printers if you need to print out a boarding pass etc... 
The hotel is in a great location if your attending an event at MSG, or need to be near Penn Station, both are only a short few minutes walk up the street. Times Square is also a nice, leisurely walk, and there's also a subway station a couple minutes away from the hotel that will take you right to Times Square, or all the way down to Coney Island. Macy's is a few blocks away as well. Across the street is Jack's 99 cents world, which has, literally, everything. The store is 3 levels, and VERY crowded, and closes early, even during the week, so keep that in mind if you want to go over. Down 7th Avenue a few blocks was a nice coffee shop called Andrew's. Great food, great service, great prices, and only a short walk from the hotel. 
I do have a couple complaints about the hotel, besides the few cleanliness issues of the room I mentioned above. The hotel is very small, or I should say, narrow, in the hallways etc... The rooms are small, but small rooms are a NYC standard, so I expect those and don't mind that. The elevators, there's only two of them, they are very small, and EXTREMELY slow. We waited at least 10 mins to come down from our room on the 12th floor a couple times, including when we were heading down to check out. Also, we stored our bags when we arrived as our room wasn't yet ready. I was dismayed to come back some hours later, and see that the lobby was being used for luggage storage! The small lobby had bags stored all over it, including ours, of which one bag contained a VERY expensive laptop. Other hotels will store laptops in separate areas in the luggage rooms, this hotel stored bags all over the lobby, in plain sight and unattended! This was UNACCEPTABLE, especially with a laptop! I know there was a luggage room, as I saw it everytime we came in the front door. I just couldn't believe it when we got our bags, and pulled them out ourselves from a corner of the lobby! The lobby is also very small, made smaller from the luggage being "stored" in it! 
Overall, our stay was good, and I would stay here again if I could get a good rate again and if I needed to be close to MSG or Penn Station. That's the only way I'd choose the hotel again though, if I needed to be close to those places, otherwise, I wouldn't. I booked in April originally with a AAA rate of $179 a night, then was able to find a lower non AAA rate for $159 a night (and it wasn't a pay in advance rate) in June, so I changed my rate with no problems through the hotel's website.

title: “Needs Improvement”
text:
My girlfriend and I book the room with the shared bath and upon arriving, it was nothing like what was on the website. I was told that the rooms with the shared bath were going to be the last to be remodeled. The room that we were placed in consisted of a regular television, a queen bed, old carpet, a refrigerator, a sink and a heater (like the ones you see in ‘I Love Lucy’) that made A LOT of noise. The bathroom itself wasn’t any better, it had green tiles that were past its time.
At this point, I had to go down to the lobby and upgrade my room because there was no way I was going to be miserable for the next 7 days in New York. When I asked for an upgrade, they told me there was an extra charge of $50 dollars per night and without any hesitation, I agreed.
The upgraded room was a lot nicer. It looked like the one in the pictures on their website. There was a plasma television, hardwood flooring, a refrigerator, I pod docking station and a private bath. Unfortunately, the heater made a lot of noise and the bathroom that was in my room wasn’t remodeled. It had the same miserable tiles that I saw in the shared baths . . . which was a big disappointment.
Finally, my last complaint, which is a legitimate complaint in my opinion. The room that I was in had cockroaches. I killed 3 in the bathroom and 1 got away out in the bedroom. I am disclosing this because when you go buy food, make sure you don’t leave it out. Don’t throw the wrapper in the trash can in the bathroom, take it the lobby or throw it in the trash cans in front of the hotel. I can handle a lot of gross things in life but to see the cockroaches in my room was the last straw. With all the money I spent on the hotel, I felt that I could have gotten a nicer one. 
So when you are considering this hotel, take my review into account. If you do decide to stay here, the location is great because it’s in a safe neighborhood and the subway is extremely close and also, the hotel staff was really friendly.

title: “good value”
text: Nice Hotel, Very helpful and friendly staff, decent room on 7th floor. The wine reception was a nice touch, but keyboardist so loud as to be painful. A few Police/ambulance sirens at night but not unreasonable for urban hotel. HUGE walk-in closets we could have sublet....Free wireless internet a big plus. Excellent transportation to airport..Not as convenient to public transportation as I would have liked but only because Powell St. cable car was broken down during our visit. would stay there again

title: “new york new york”
text: spent two nights here the hotel was top class ,very comfortable and excelent all round. situated near central park which was a lovely retreat from the city but we easily got around by underground. the cosierge wasnt that helpfull helping us get to new jersey for cruise but joe the taxi man outside was brilient and got us there and picked us up at the end of the cruise and took us back to new york then the jfk airport so look for him . his charge was very good and a lovely man. would stay here again

title: “Horrible Stay - Lousy Management”
text:
This was my WORST experience at a Holiday Inn (or any other hotel for that matter). I was travelling with four little girls and had an early morning flight out. We had prepaid the room, which was not very clean and smelled very moldy and damp. At 12:30 in the morning ONE OF THE BEDS BROKE AND ONE SIDE FELL TO THE FLOOR! Upon calling the front desk we were told "no manager was available" but they could move us to another room at the other end of the hall. I had to wake up four little girls, repack our bags, carry our own belongings (no one even helped us to move our things!). In the morning I received an additional bill for a movie that the girls had watched the night before. I was furious that they would even consider billing
us for an incidental item after the horrible service. They told me I'd have to speak to a manager and, you guessed it, "none was available". It was horrible. I called the corporate number and was told they would take care of it, but three days later those charges mysteriously showed up on my credit card. To date, no manager has bothered to return ANY of my calls. BE WARNED: this is a horrible, dirty, smelly hotel with LOUSY customer service. If you are thinking about staying here - don't. In fact, I am rethinking a stay at ANY Holiday Inn hotel after this experience.

title: “One of the best hotels in boston”
text: Amazing hotel right on the harbor. Excellent staff, pristine rooms, awesome mattress on bed. Close to all sites. Would stay there each time we visit. Evening movies and entertainment right out back of their hotel with dining. First time visiting and absolutely loved everything about this hotel.

title: “Non-smoking hotel!! Yes!! :-)”
text: It's been 6 months since we stayed in this hotel over the Xmas season but I just wanted to say how much we enjoyed our stay here. Yes, late but still, I'm sure things don't change that much. We were apprehensive about the hotel before arrival from reading about it and the fact that it is a very old hotel in the downtown area. I was nervous that it would be in skid-row. Heehee. It wasn't. It was great that way. What sold us was that it is a completely NON-SMOKING hotel! YES! That did it. When we arrived, the room was small and seemed old but it was very clean. It could use more light. The washroom is very tiny like everyone says. Still, the location is GREAT and the room was very quiet. We faced the library, away from the main street. We enjoyed the easy access to everything so much that we left the car parked in the parking lot for 4 days. Yes, it did cost $18 a day to park. Ouch. The lobby/mezzanine area was actually bright, large and inviting. It was more contemporary and newer with sofa/reading area and free internet computers. Still, we loved our little cubby-hole and would definitely stay there again! It isn't a 4-star hotel but we were open minded enough to enjoy the old world charm. It's CLEAN and feels very safe. Those are the things that are important and oh... the price was good too. About $70ish a night. -Mae

title: “Hotel of Choice”
text: I have stayed here a number of times on business trips and the staff is very friendly and helpful. The hotel is non-smoking and when I was given a room that had a strong smell of smoke the front desk moved me to another room. Location is great. It is located across the street from the landing and is in the down town area which provides equal distance for the place I need to visit for work. The Omni is the first hotel I look at when staying in Jacksonville for work or personal trips. The hotel offers valet parking or there is a $10/day lot across the street.

title: “Couldn't have been more convenient!”
text: I just returned from a 3 night stay and I couldn't be happier. Hotel was within walking distance to Telegraph Hill, North Beach, and Russian Hill. Due to the proximity to the waterfront, we were able to enjoy Pier 39, etc. early in the morning without the crowds. Great access to public transportation (F-line, Mason-Powell cable car, and the 47 bus line). Also, a Enterprise rent a car across the street allowing us to take an easy day trip to Muir Woods. Ridiculous number of breakfast options within in 1-3 minute walk. We had room service the 1st night - decent but not great - with the exception of the chicken with cippolini onions which was fantastic. Hotel was bright, cheery, and clean with a very helpful staff. Would absolutely stay there again!

title: “Crosby Street Hotel, hidden gem, simple and elegant”
text:
The Crosby Street Hotel is now my favorite or perhaps second-favorite place to stay in New York, depending on the neighborhood I want to stay in. Its understated elegance matches its location, on a quiet back street, secretly tucked away between the bustling SoHo shopping district and Little Italy. You get all the convenience in a quiet atmosphere. The rooms are beautifully designed to be roomy yet cozy and warm. The staff are a delight, always with a smile on their face, always willing to help. Walking distance to some great little places, one of which happens to be a favorite, the McNally Jackson bookstore on Prince St. Also a block away from a fantastic newsstand, the Lafayette Smoke Shop on Spring & Lafayette, open 24 hours. The Crosby Street bar and restaurant serves a great bloody mary! Bonus: If you get an upper floor room with an eastern exposure, you get a great view. 
The hotel is part of a UK-based company, and it indeed has a British accent. A padded dress form punctuates the corner of many of many a room (if not all) adding a touch of class and a nod to the city's roots in fashion and garments, perhaps. That's how I imagine it. While that adds a feminine lilt to the air, the feel is quite understated, not overbearing in personality. Walls are covered in wallpaper that feels like garment fabric, like wool or cotton, in yet another sartorial undertone. The effect is comfort, warmth and high style. In-room mini bars are well stocked, something that is still important to me. Room service is reliably good, and the fixtures in the rooms are very up to date without going overboard on gadgetry. The bathrooms are high style and spacious.

title: “Would got 3.5 stars if I could”
text: I'll preface my comments be saying I'm not overly picky with hotel rooms. My wife is another story. Went for a weekend with friends. The service at this hotel was outstanding. Our suite was ready way before check-in but when we got there my wife was bummed as there was no bath tub. She's high maintenance, what can I say? One call to the front desk and they hooked us up with another one immediately that had a tub and we were set. The suites are the size of a normal smallish hotel room anywhere else but hey that's NY. The bed, however, was great. We slept very well. The showers all have the stupid half open set-up which I just makes no sense. When looking closely, you could tell a full door used to be there but they decided to be 'trendy'. What's not trendy is having to cover the toilet paper holder to avoid the open shower splashing it. Ergonomics people....get some. The hotel lobby was gorgeous and a nice place to chill. Location was great..we were able to walk to many places. I'd heard about noise problems from the bar if the room was high up, but we were on the 8th floor and never heard a word. Speaking of the bar....we hit the rooftop loungeone night and it was wall to wall packed. Hard to tell much. Based on the location and service, I'd stay there again.

title: “location, location”
text: this hotel is all about location. it is a bit dated but spotlessly clean.staff that we met were all extremely courteous and friendly but then again, on the whole, we didnt meet one unpleasant person in new york. this was our 1st time in new york and i choose this hotel as it was so central. it's not cheap @ nearly 1200 euro for 5 nights (no breakfast included). turn right and you are at central park in 5 mins and turn left you are on time's square in 5 mins. on the minus side, these are 2 very busy areas so going out for a cup of coffee meant hitting the crowds always. our room was small but i think this is normal in such a popular area. i would have loved a coffee making facility in our room as take away coffee is just so expensive. we were on the 22nd floor but getting the lifts was never really a problem. my advise to anyone is if you have only 2 days or so, stay here but if you have more, save your money and move further from the center. we had one issue, we had a problem with our air con. the 1st night, although we mentioned it at reception, nothing seemed to have been done. we were exhausted and slept with the windows open, the noise not really bothering us. however, the 2nd night - i got very little sleep as still nothing had been done about the a/c prob. the next evening it was repaired and the repair man was v apologetic as a circuit had to be replaced. i was annoyed it took several trips to reception for it to be addressed. also, i regret being too polite about the problem and not demanding it to be fixed immediately - after all we were paying enough for it. to end, i think management could have acknowledged the problem also. i might add, the heat and humidity in new york was extremely high when we were there. overall, a nice hotel, with excellent staff, a nice ambience and a brilliant location. would i recommend it? - definitely but dont be afraid to speak up if you are unhappy with something

title: “Location is wonderful, room was enormous”
text: As a solo business traveller, the room was enormous and the bathroom ridiculously large! I really appreciated the impressive pressure in the shower. The room was standard business chic, quiet though it was across the hall from the elevators. I stayed in room 587 in the second tower. There is a zipcar lot up the block, several decent restaurants around. The breakfast is ridiculously expensive in the hotel restaurant, but the train displays on the way are very distracting.

title: “Frightning experience during our stay”
text: My son, 9 year old granddaughter and myself stayed there for two days and paid extra for the American Girl package. We stayed Oct 11 & 12. When I checked in with my granddaughter standing with me they never said anything to her about registering her and her doll. I had to remind the clerk that she had the AG package and only then did they ask her to step aside and fill out the registration. On or second evening there my son and granddaughter were going to go down to the pool. They came back up and and said that they could see from the glass elevator that there were alot of people at the pool. This was a little after 9:00pm. About every 20 minutes he would take her down to see if the pool area had cleared out. Finally around 11:15 they went down to check again and this time they did not return to the room so I assumed that they were in the pool. So I am sitting in my room on the 11th floor watching TV when I heard loud noises, at first I didn't think that much about it since it was a Friday night and I thought maybe some people were walking down the hall a little tipsy and being loud. I soon realized when the noise got louder that something wasn't right. I went out of my room and looked over the ledge and I saw all hell breaking lose down below. There were young men throwing chairs at each other and alot of screaming going on. All I could do is think of my son and granddaughter down there amongst the meyham. I had good reason to worry, I heard the elevator door open and there was my son and granddaughter and they were very scared. My son had went to the pool area and all these young men that were fighting had come into the hotel and were not guests. I guess they were asked to leave earlier but didn't. My son and granddaughter were walking to the pool when all this happened. My son grabbed my granddaughter and pulled her around the corner so that she wouldn't get hit by one of the flying chairs, She was frozen in fear when he grabbed her. My son was peeking around the corner to see when would be a good time to tey to make it to the elevator. He took her and made it to the elavator and the next thing he knows a couple of the gang looking young men also came into the elavator. They were both scared not knowing if guns were going to be pulled and shots were going to start while all this was going on. I feel that the hotel staff should have known that all the gang looking youth that were all over the atrium and pool were not guests. Like I said they had been going down to check to see if the pool was clear since a little after 9 and here it was almost 11:30 by the time the police were called. We saved and planned for this trip for my granddaughter to the American Girl store so that we could have a nice family time together. Now I am afraid that her memory from this trip will be how her and her daddy had to hide and were scared that they might be hurt from all the gang bangers and the chaos from that evening! When the crowd had cleared my son went down to the front desk to explain how upsetting the whole incident was he was told that the desk clerk was there and didn't see him or my granddaughter. At this time another hotel employee over heard them talking and said "Oh yes, he was there and he had a little girl with him" at that point the desk clerk appalogized. It would have been nice while all this was happening if security would have noticed a child guest amoung the chaos and tried to escort her out of harms way or the very least called our room to check to see if they were ok.

title: “Great location for what we paid.”
text:
My husband and I spent a 3 day weekend, with 2 nights at the Palmer House. We used Priceline and for a cost under 80.00 a night, we coudln't have found anything close to this hotel at that price. The hotel lobby truly is gorgeous in its character of Old Chicago. We requested a King bed which we got at check in. 17th floor. Very friendly front desk staff and concierge service. We DID get a small room. But it was fine for the short while we spent in it. No view as it just looked across the way into the next wing of rooms. Bathroom....when people say small I guess I didn't believe HOW small. The area in front of the sink is exactly 2X3. We counted the tiles:) In order to close the door you have to literally slide between the toilet and tub in the 12 inch space between the two. So...if you need space or are a bit "fluffy", this wouldn't be the bathroom for you...think airplane size. We DID have plenty of hot water and good pressure in the shower/tub. No space to store toilitries, but there is a large clothes closet (as big as the bathroom) with shelves and plenty of space for everything. Two out of the 3 drawers open in the tv stand for more storage. A desk and two nightstands. That's it furniture wise. CLEAN room! The bar in the lobby is fun to people watch. Wine..$9.00. Beer..7.00. Not bad for a hotel. Try their kobe sliders....yum! Went down to starbucks for morning coffee each day. The Corner Bakery is right next door for good lunch sandwiches/salads, sweet rolls , breakfast sandwiches etc too. 
Location is the highlight as everything is in walking distance. Parks, river, shopping, restaurants. Took the city bus straight to Shedd from stop right outside hotel. 
Would we stay again? Yes. For a longer stay, might want to try the tower rooms where the rooms are larger. But then we'd have to weigh the cost difference.

title: “Pure Magic at the Waldorf”
text:
Having read some of the less than glamorous reviews of the Waldorf, I was a little apprehensive about staying here. However, I firmly believe that a trip is what one makes of it, so I decided that it would be a treat for my wife and I to experience some Christmas magic at the Waldorf.
I booked an "executive king" room through the Hilton website. I am a HHonors Silver member and made a request for an upgrade if available.
We were very excited to be staying at the famous Waldorf Astoria...my wife more so because Brad Pitt maintains a residence at the top floor of the Waldorf Towers. More on that later. 
From the moment we arrived at the Waldorf we were treated like old friends. The staff is extremely helpful and nice, and we were even escorted to the main lobby for check-in. The main lobby is a destination unto itself guilded in gold and decked out for Christmas. People watching must be a time honored tradition. The front desk associate who checked us in informed us that we would be staying in a "lovely" accomodation. That was an understatement.
We apparantly were upgraded to a top level suite (still within the Waldorf proper)...complete with an enormous balcony that measured approximately 60' by 15'. We had a perfect view over Park Avenue and St. Bart(s) church below. The suite had an entry foyer with mini-bar. To the right was a living room complete with desk, full-size couch (with sleeper bed) a chair, faux fireplace and TV credenza. The bedroom was down the hall and was magnificient. The suite was gorgeously appointed. There was access onto the balcony/terrace from both the bedroom and the living room. How rare is a balcony let alone one you could play catch on, in NYC!!! 
The suite bathroom also did not disappoint. It was a little small, but this hotel is seventy-six years old, built in 1931. Everything back then was a little smaller. Water pressure was fine, but the toilet ran, which caused there to be a lack of hot water for the shower. Just a jiggle of the commode handle fixed that issue, hot water restored. 
We dined at the fabulous Peacock Alley. It, too, was a magical experience with excellent food. The two highnotes were the scallops appetizer ($9 a scallop...but oddly it was worth it), and the New York Cheese cake, which was more like creme brulee without the ramikin. 
After dinner we explored the magnificient Waldorf. Do the same. The Park Avenue lobby had a huge 20' tree next to the Cole Porter piano. We even slipped into the Grand Ballroom, which was also decked out for the Holidays. The hotel is so grand and storied that they even have a small museum (Ok, a display case) showing some of the history. Almost every president has stayed there, JFK campaigned outside the Park Ave entrance during the 1960 election, and foriegn leaders have stayed here. This hotel is part of American History.
The mattress was a cloud, and we had a great night sleep save for the famous New York soundtrack of sirens and horns honking at all hours (but, after all, its New York). 
We were there only one night, but loved it and would certainly return. However, we are going to have to request the suite again or try out the Waldorf Towers. For the rest of our trip, we stayed across the street at the Marriott East Side (look up review for that). 
New York, and the Waldorf, is magical during Christmas, and we will make this part of our Christmas Tradition. Oh yea, about Brad Pitt. We actually rode the Waldorf Towers elevator up to the top floor. There was a security guard at there but he merely said "hello." We walked the length of the L shaped hall walk were it dead-ended. We walked back to the elevators and the guard said there wasn't any windows to get a good view (but he didn't give us any attitude). We feigned surprise. Then he said most people come up to try and find Brad. "Really," my wife said in mock shock. "Is he here...right now?" my wife asked, in her best attempt at disinteredness. "Oh, yes," said the guard. Sorry, honey...no Brad Pitt sighting today.

title: “We love it”
text: We found this little gem surfing the websites and was very pleased with it. We stayed here for 7 nights and found it very hip, comfortable and accessible. The coffee joint on the ground floor was terrific and the staff are helpful. I must say you need to stay on a higher floor though as the traffic noise is very audible otherwise. NY has a constant stream of sirens running through the day and night so move upstairs! Hallways are a little too dark for our liking but thats about it

title: “Clean and Close to Times Sq / Theatre District”
text: Stayed 6 nights at this hotel. It is about a 10 minute walk to Times Sq and many theatres which made the location very convenient for us. The hotel is about 4 years old and we found it to be quite clean. The rooms are fairly small especially with two adult children staying with us. The rooms were cleaned well every day. We stayed on a lower floor - no view. Would suggest a higher floor would give a good view - the hotel is about 30 stories. For an additional fee we had breakfast included. The hotel cost while expensive compared to any other place, it was less expensive than many hotels in the area. (We booked through booking.com). There is free wi-fi. The breakfast buffet was better than the average hotel buffet. The restaurant was clean and staff courteous HOWEVER the last morning there my daughter found a hair in her omlette. No apology was offered by the server. This was the only bad experience in an otherwise good hotel experience.

title: “Handlery hotel San Diego rocks”
text: We stayed at the Handlery hotel in San diego In jan 2012 and we had a great time. We had a guy called geoff looking after us and he drives u anywhere u want ands it's complimentary. The hotel is clean,friendly and great value for money. We will definitely be staying there again next year.

title: “great romantic stay which ended with a proposal”
text: Me and My girlfriend stay at the hotel for a romantic evening to celibrate our two year anniversary of dating when we arrived check in was fast they send us to our room the first room we got was very small i am 6"2 and my legs were hanging off the bed so my girlfriend called down and the manager came up and gave us a bigger room which we were both happy with. The concierge lady i believe her name was maureen was very nice i had to ask her a question about my surprise that i had planned for my girlfriend and she said that the rose petals and flowers would be in the room at 9pm i said cool . Niles Restaurant next door to the hotel was excellent the food and atmosphere was amazing so we went to our show which was spiderman when we got back from the show my girlfriend open the door and see the flowers and rose petals and was in total shock then i got down on one knee and proposed to her she immediatelly said Yes. The Next day we got room service which was on time the server was very nice also the bellman who came up to help us with bags was also very nice and helpful we ask him if our ride was here and he went to check he said yes so all in all great stay thank you to everyone there my only complained is we got beer in our room and no cork screw came with it we had to call down for one.

title: “Great place!”
text: Great location near Dupont Circle and the Metro, loved the happy hour complementary snacks and wines, newly renovated lobby and chic/comfy bar/restaurant area and our room was incredibly spacious and beautifully appointed. I was most impressed with the return of my lost earring. As i was traveling home on the train, I realized that one of my very valuable diamond stud earrings was missing. I immediately called the hotel and they said they would relay the information to housekeeping. I never expected that the earring would be found and/or returned, but a few hours later I was contacted that my earring had been found and would be shipped back to me. I was thrilled by the staff's honesty and efficiency. I highly recommend this wonderful boutique hotel. (An added bonus: they are also right next door to the Tabard Inn where we went for their AMAZING brunch. Make sure you reserve a month ahead.)

title: “Wonderful”
text:
We originally stayed at The Roosevelt in February as a package deal (hotel, theatre show, dinner). We, along with other couples, purchased this for Valentine's weekend. The hotel and dinner were great, however, the wrong tickets were printed for the show at the Paramount. At first it looked like it was going to be a disaster, but the Paramount remedied the problem; however, the seats we received were not comparable as the ones we should have had.
Anyway, long story short, the Roosevelt Hotel and Broadway Across America went above and beyond what we ever imagined. They gave us complimentary tickets to another Broadway production at a later date and a complimentary room (upgrade) at The Roosevelt on the night of the show. We will definitely recommend the Roosevelt to our friends and family.

title: “Wonderful experience!”
text: The Argonaut is a wonderful hotel. The staff are very helpful, from the doormen and the front desk to the concierge and housekeeping. A lovely surprise is the 5pm wine tasting in the lobby. The guestroom is very comfortable and we have plenty of space to spread out. There are even Aveda products in the bathroom! Considering the hotel is right on Fishermans Wharf, you'd expect a lot of noise but we didn't have any issues - it was very quiet, almost soundproofed. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: Hotel is EXACTLY what it shows on the hotel's website. Our room was small (hey, that is New York) but we did not feel cramped at all. Great use of space. The Reading Room on the second floor was a peaceful place to get away and read the paper, eat breakfast, etc. Lots of books to look through, movies at the front desk. The staff was very helpful. Wonderful location right near Grand Central Station. Would definately stay there again.

title: “About what you'd expect - very good”
text:
The best thing about this place is the location. Very close to where our meetings were and where our reception dinner was being hosted. Since it is located in the Tech Center it is convenient tot he highway and not too far from the airport.
The rooms were a little small, but clean. The hotel restaurant was pretty good, I loved my tuna tataki wrap for lunch one day.
If you need a good hotel in this part of Denver, it is a very solid choice.

title: “Ritzy Camping :)”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here for his birthday in August, it was a beautiful place, but not really for us. We had a garden lanai room, but ended up with a bungalow in the end.
Pros - 
1. The grounds - are beautiful. It is like your own little island, they do try to make it so you don't need to leave. They have pools and spas galore, dinning, and activities everywhere.
2. Rooms - VERY large rooms. The bathrooms and rooms were quite big, with hardwood floors very nice looking, even though you can see the buildings are older.
3. Front desk - was a little slow but very friendly and was quick to upgrade when we had a buggy issue.
4. Food - We couldnt reach room service :( and the little grill we went to was underwhelming, but liked that we were able to bill it to our room.
5. Night - We walked the area at night, which was great. We landed ourselves a firepit and befriended a second couple :)
6. Activites - You can rent water skiis etc, a little buggy to ride in as a family or separately, croquet, swimming etc...so much to do!
Cons-
1. Buildings - are old. They've been somewhat renovated it looks like, but we didn't have any issues.
2. The room - the bed was "springy", I could feel the springs poking me. Ok, I'll admit I may have spoiled myself into being a bed snob. 3 years ago we saved a ton of money to buy a really really nice memory foam mattress and ever since everything else sucks, so I may be biased.
3. The grounds - BUGS. Lots of bugs haha. My boyfriend is a weenie and flips out if he sees even 1 bug...which is a little overboard. However, unfortunately we walked into the bathroom to see a massive amount of bugs in the sink in our Lanai room (It seems someone poured a soda down the sink) that had spread to our towels and toiletries on the sink...really gross. Less than 3 minutes after check in, we walked back and asked for a different room and had pictures of our unwanted roommates. The front desk agent woman apologized profusely and upgraded us to a bungalow. They did take care of us :) But there are bugs, keep that in mind, if you HATE bugs I wouldn't suggest it. This place is tropical-ish and bugs come with that!! :)
It was a really fun place, lots of things to do and plenty of ways to spoil yourself or significant other, like the title says it really reminds me of ritzy camping in a tropical area. I just cant come back with my boyfriend he cant handle bugs or camping.

title: “Great service”
text:
Service was very good, particularly Amadou and Erwing at the door.
Location is very nice, a couple of blocks from Georgetown.
Nice pool.

title: “Excellent location, nice rooms, friendly staff.”
text: You cannot beat the location of OTA, a few blocks from the subway, walking distance to Central Park and museums. There are two restaurants attached that serve good food and there are many nice cafes within a few blocks. The rooms are clean and spacious by NY standards. The staff are superb! My only complaint is wifi is only free in the lobby. Small gym and not much else the hotel offers. I would def. stay again.

title: “Perfect!”
text:
I stayed here for four nights and was highly pleased!
I looked for a low cost hotel in Manhattan for a trip that I was attempting to do at as low cost as possible. I found an AAA rate of $119 per night for this property on the hotel website.
The location was wonderful even though it looks out on the gigantic and ugly Port Authority Building and when turning left from the front door one encounters some less than lovely areas. However, if you make a right you are just a short block away from the hub-bub of Times Square. You do have to walk by an adult bookstore but as a solo female traveler I was not at all intimidated or bothered by anyone on the street and I was in and out at all hours with no problems.Go up a few blocks and turn left and you are in the Hell's Kitchen area where every type of dining experience awaits. I would not go into this area by turning left from the hotel only because you must walk under an underpass area by the Port Authority and a large crowd of men hang out in this area. I felt uncomfortable the one time I did try this route so I just walked right and up a block and then to the left from then on.
Go into the Port Authority building and downstairs to the Subway -- so convenient!!
The hotel room itself was small as NYC hotels are prone to be, but the space was well-designed. I would have liked another shelf in the bathroom--the very deep sink has no lip or shelf around it to speak of so storing my toiletries was a bit of a pain. There was no tub but the glass-doored shower had great water pressure and the door made the space seem larger than it was.
The bed was comfortable. The view from the window was not wonderful but I could see the lights of the New Yorker building in the evening as well as the spire of the Empire State Building so it was not the worst view I have ever had out of a New York hotel. I could see blue sky and tried not to see into the windows of the nearby apartment building, but all in all I was happy.
The folks at the hotel were great. One staffer would push the elevator button when she saw me coming in and often ask how my day had gone. the concierge found a great seat for me at Hair when I grew weary of standing in the half price line for tickets one day. Several times I asked them to make change for me which they did readily at the front desk and they were always cheerful. One day I needed utensils for take-out I had picked up and a staff person went in the back and came back with plastic forks, spoons, and knives. I was just so pleased by the caring attitude of the people at the hotel. They delivered a fridge to my room so i was able to buy take-out and food from markets and eat in when I chose.
I did have a problem with other guests who allowed their children to spend great lengths of time on the lobby computers. These kids would be playing games when I needed to print my boarding passes and I think a sign that says please limit your usage of computers in consideration of other guests or something would help. There were two machines and one night a teenager was instant messaging her friends for more than an hour and I finally asked her if I could please have the computer just to check the schedule of one event and then i would return it to her. She grudgingly agreed. On the night I needed to print the pass i did not think the parents of the kids would ever allow me a turn, but they finally did leave with their kids in tow.
I would definitely stay here again. The location is great. it is on a quiet street and there is little noise on the backside of the hotel. The rooms have nice flat panel TVs with premium channels, comfortable beds, and are very clean. There is a small wardrobe in the room--no closets and the dresser area has drawers to store clothes--there is free internet in the rooms and good lighting. 
The only thing I missed was the lack of room service but there was one menu of a nearby place that delivers and a list of places nearby that offered delivery so in a pinch that would do.
Do try the ethnic places in hell's kitchen. I plan to write reviews of many of them when I get time as I had some great dining experiences at very low cost. 
The entire trip was just under a thousand dollars and it included multiple plays, transportation, great food and lodging for five days so I met my goal of biting off the Big Apple without breaking the bank!

title: “Great Hotel!!”
text:
My husband and I ended our honeymoon here and stayed only 2 nights. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay. At check in, we were upgraded to a luxury king room and enjoyed complimentary champagne and chocolates. The room was like a small apartment! It was fantastic! We had a fire place (and since it was chilly in San Fran during our stay - the fire place was great!)
Breakfast in the morning was nice. Fresh fruits, eggs, toast, cereals. The evening wine and muchies were great as well. We enjoyed talking with other guests and it really did become a bit of a social hour(s) :)
The location is perfect as well. Only a block from the Powell line cable car stop and 2 blocks to Union Square. 
It was a great end to a great trip! 
Thanks!!

title: “Just perfect...No complaints”
text: We stayed here November of 2009. Brought my boyfriend (now fiancé) here for his birthday. The service was pure perfection. I loved the French doors which opened to the balcony. Beautiful, well-appointed, nice bathroom. The staff helped make my boyfriend's birthday memorable by bringing up a cake that I had delivered from a local bakery. The moment your cab pulls up, you are greeted by staff who opens your door. They hailed us a cab when we needed one as well. Great service overall. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Good place”
text: Excellent customer service and rooms. my only complaint was the noise coming from the ice machine.

title: “Great value - but wait until you get a bill”
text: We stayed at Affinia Dumont in Dec '04, and was quite happy until we checked out. The room is spacious as a New York standard, and people were very friendly. But, we were surprised to find a mini-bar charge on our bill when we were going to check out. In general, my husband and I would never touch on anything from a mini-bar because we always get drinks and snakes from outside before we head back to the hotel. And that was the case for this stay as well. We told them we did not consume anything, and they checked with housekeeping and took out the charge from our bill. Well, a months later when we got our credit card bill, we found another attempted charge!! Of course, we insisted that it has to be mistake, but the person we spoke to said that she had to get back to us, so they have not yet cleared this charge. Be sure you check your hotel bill and the credit card! I would hope that this hotel is not trying to trick their customers, but it is wired that it happened twice for our one stay. Its a nice hotel, but only pay cash so they can't sneak charges to your credit card after you've left!.

title: “Fabulous hotel - Always a step ahead with great service”
text: This is our second time to stay at the Conrad. From the moment we arrived they were there to make our trip stand out as well as the city of Chicago. We checked in and we were asked if we would like a coffee pot delivered. I did not have to ask. Our luggage was delayed and they were on top of it. The concierge was also superb. Her name was Meg and she made great suggestions. We even ran into a small problem and she followed it through. Loved the beds and the amenities. It was great being connected to Nordstoms too! Would definitely stay again.

title: “One of the best Hilton hotels out there!”
text: We really loved this hotel - from check-in to check-out. Hotel's location is just perfect. The rooms are large (especially compared to European standards) and well appointed. Our room was always clean - we never had to ask for or complain about anything. The building itself is so magnificant and historic. It's just so grande. Breakfast was not included in the rate so we had to pay which was probably the most expensive breakfast we have ever had anywhere. That was the only drawback. Would recommend this hotel to anyone and would gladly comeback myself.

title: “Wonderful Anniversary Weekend!”
text: We stayed at the Four Seasons during the weekend of 7/29-7/31/2011 to celebrate our 5th wedding anniversary. With the exception of some hotel-wide TV issues that lasted most of the day on 7/30/11, everything about our trip was perfect and the staff was very pleasant to us. Our room was very clean and comfortable. Plus, the curtains are on overlapping tracks (not just one track where the curtains meet in the middle), so the room was able to be completely dark in the early mornings. We had wonderful breakfasts at the Fountain Restaurant (the Crab and Asparagus Eggs Benedict was fantastic). The Afternoon Tea at the Swann Lounge was delicious, as well. Also, the pool and spa areas are great. We ended our trip with amazing massages (80 minute Total Tranquility and Deep Tissue). Someday, we will come back again for another special weekend!

title: “Cant tell a book by its cover”
text: Dont let the neighborhood deter you; everything about the hotel is first class. The staff is among the best of any hotel we have stayed in, at any price point. The rooms are very spacious, very clean, and even have a small kitchen area. The baths are extra large as well. We walked to Old Towne with no problem, though you do have to cross a large street. The van to the airport was fine, though would have preferred a more flexible schedule than hourly.

title: “Great service”
text: Hotel is centrally located in downtown right on the riverwalk and across from the convention center. Staff was super friendly and helpfull. They even mailed my post cards and did not bill me for the stamps! Rooms were very comfortable and clean and reasonable priced Easy access to the Riverwalk and Alamo. I would stay there again should my travels take me to San Antonio.

title: “1st Trip to New York”
text: This was my 1st trip to New York and to have been lucky enough to have chosen this hotel to stay made the trip outstanding. The customer service was outstanding; Norma's was the best breakfast experience and the Burger Joint was awesome. I would definitely stay here again and recommend it to others. The only suggestion I have for them is to fix the business center; I could not print my boarding pass. However, the staff took care of it for me.

title: “Overpriced Shabby Dump!”
text: Myself, and 3 pals went to go to NYC for a fun long weekend. I have travelled extensively but this was my first trip to NYC. We stayed at the Park Central May 19th to the 23rd because one of the group had stayed there before and insisted on staying there again. Why I cannot comprehend. As a new trip advisor member I had checked this place out and was very much afraid of what we would find on arrival. Anyone reading this review, pay heed to any negative reviews on the trip advisor as they are very accurate. Most of everything negative I read about, I suffered on my trip. On arrival, we were lucky to come at a time when there was little lineup at the check-in desk so that part was quite prompt. The wait for elevators to get to the room was long, due to the fact that several were out of commission and during our entire stay that was true every day. I noticed every time the elevator stopped that the hall area of each floor was dirty and shabby looking; wallpaper peeling, stained dirty carpet and worn out looking mouldings. On opening the door to one of the rooms (we booked two double rooms), my first impression was WHAT A DUMP! The room was okay in terms of size, but that was the only good thing about it. The carpet had several large stains and was very dirty looking. The furniture looked like it had endured several decades of use, scratches, dents, and looked very worn out. The decor of the room was dark and very shabby. The bathroom had mildew and mould in the bath/shower area and several tiles looked like they might be in danger of falling off. The tub and sink had some rusty looking spots and there were only towels for one, despite that this was a double and could sleep 4. The best part was turning down the bed the first night to discover the sheets on my bed were ripped! and I had this happen two other nights. The second room we booked was no better. Check-out was painful as the lineup was so long, it took an hour wait. The only thing for which I am grateful is that I did not see any bugs in our room as another reviewer did. For any who think I am too fussy or overly critical, let me say I am a very well seasoned traveller as I like to go to a different place each vacation and have seen all of Europe and Canada, and most of the USA, Mexico, and the Caribbean, so I have had my share of bad choices in the hotel department and stayed in a few dumps in my years. But I have never stayed in a dump and paid such an exorbitant fee for doing so. Thank God the city was so friendly and fun that it made up for the lousy accommodation otherwise my trip would have been ruined. Do yourself a favour and stay away from this hotel. NYC has so many choices there is no need to stay in a dump no matter your budget and certainly it is an insult to pay a high fee for doing so.

title: “Most Horrible Stay Ever!”
text: I booked 4 rooms for my guests to my bachelor party, 8-27-11, at the DoubleTree by Hilton in Center City Philadelphia. At 3:30 PM, the first guests arrived and actively pursued to their room by the GM for carrying a cooler. The GM was told the group would be out all night and will return for bed. GM approved. At 2:30-3 AM a noise complaint was lodged and security arrived and warned one room. 5 minutes later security evicted 3 rooms for the complaint of one room into Hurricane Irene and state of emergency. At 5 AM security and police woke up room 4 to evict for association. Police convinced security there was no issue. Asst GM agreed after 30-45 mins for us to stay in lobby to my fiancé after we were already forced to seek shelter elsewhere. Rooms were also charged smoking fees for bogus claims after an expired cigar was found. Cameras out front would prove we had smoked and extinguished outside. Repeated attempts to resolve this with GM proved disrespectful and unsuccessful.

title: “Would never stay at the Wellington again”
text: We have just come back from New York on the weekend of the 'Blizzard 2005'. The heating in our room did not work. We asked twice for it to be fixed, but it never was. The room was shabby and on both days there we found the maids hair on our towels. The bathroom was so small that there was hardly enough room to sit on the toilet. Bad service and grotty hotel.

title: “Loved it”
text: I enjoyed this hotel. They were even nice enough to hold our luggage when we checked out so we can go shopping. Perfect location to the fashion district and the 40/40 club, Times Square, 34th (shoes shopping), and Penn Station. I think this will be the only hotel I stay in now when I come out to the city from Long Island.

title: “Still pretty good after all these years”
text:
Memories. In the 90's, we used to play tennis at the rooftop club then go around the corner to reward our exercise with a feast at Palm Too. We often would recommend the hotel to friends and relatives visiting as it was always reasonable and comfortable with a hint of class.
While searching for a room at the last minute, the hotel came up with a decent rate. Just the hotel name made me smile. I decided to try it out. It did not disappoint. The staff was quite helpful and friendly. The rooms are nice, but the carpet in my room had one massive stain. The view was perfect. The location might seem a bit out in left field, but it actually is not too bad. 
Bottom line, I would stay there again.

title: “Great value great location and friendly helpful staff”
text: Everything about this hotel was great. If you are looking for luxury this is not for you. But if you want helpful super friendly staff and a great location book a room now. The free bkfst really helped the budget.

title: “Motel not a hotel”
text:
The location was good for where I had to be, but otherwise the quality reflects the price. It looks reasonable from the outside but once you step in, you know the place has seen better dates. Dated, faded, neglected, stained carpets, just generally grotty.
The front desk staff are fine but really had little interest in helping, not rude, just not very interested. The room was clean and the bed comfortable. The ac was noisy and not very efficient. Room cleaning was done in parts, but the bathroom was hardly touched and if you did not use the shower, the bath would not have had any cleaning at all.
Food was fine, just lacking in variety and inspiration.
It's a motel really and the quality is reflected in the price of the rooms. You don't pay too much and you don't get too much.

title: “Smell of Smoke in Non-smoking room”
text: The non-smoking room we had a faint smell of smoke. We found some peanuts on the floor that we had housekeeping vacuum when we arrived. No other complaints. The beds and bath and the rest of the hotel was clean. The quality of the breakfast was good and the eating area and the rest of the hotel was clean.

title: “Best place to stay in NY!”
text:
After checking out some recent positive reviews of the Gansevoort on Tripadvisor we booked a 5 night stay there from the 12-16 November. We always try to stay in a different hotel each time I go to NY and so the Gansevoort has been our favourite by a long way.
The hotel is located on 28th and Park Avenue South away from the hustle and bustle of the busy tourist areas. Saying that it was only a short walk to the Empire State Building (34th St) and Time Square (42 St) and a couple of blocks from the subway. It is also a spa hotel although we didn't actually have any treatments.
We arrived about 10.30pm after a flight delay and checked in within a couple of minutes. Our room was on the 9th floor with no particular view but that wasn't an issue for us. Waiting in the room was a bottle of wine and welcome note which was a nice surprise as was free wireless internet all around the hotel. The room itself was big by NY standards (340 sq ft) as was the bed, LCD TV and the bathroom. As the hotel is only a few months old everything was more or less brand new and very clean.
Other than the large room size we were really impressed with the free breakfast provided on the top floor of the hotel. Not only was there a fantastic view (and outside terrace) but the selection of food and drinks was excellent. It was buffet style but consisted of juices, tea/coffee, cereals, yoghurts, bagels, muffins (even healthy ones), bread (brown, white, rye etc) with every type of butter spread possible. The best part of breakfast for us was the selection of fresh fruit which included blueberries, raspberries, kiwi fruit and melon to name a few. Even the tea selection on offer consisted of a premium brand (Tea Forte) and included flavours such as lemon and ginger, green tea with jasmine etc. We literally had to drag ourselves away from the area although had we been there in the summer we would have definitely had a swim in the small pool (heated) on the roof terrace. 
The staff in the hotel were always very polite and unlike other similar style hotels it was not pretentious nor hugely expensive in comparison to other highly ranked hotels.
Overall a great experience and a hotel I would definitely recommend!

title: “Best Hotel on Fishermans Wharf”
text: Fishermans Wharf is pricey and you pay extra for parking, but Courtyard looked like the best deal around. It was very clean, pleasant staff and parking was less than the other hotels around. There were three of us and we had roomy queen beds instead of doubles. Room and bathroom were large.

title: “Great place to stay in Seattle!”
text:
Sadly I was only in Seattle one night - I had never been to the city before so I wanted to stay somewhere that was in the middle of things, that way I could see as much I as could in the short time I was there. The Inn at the Market has a great location - right at Pike's Place Market and surrounded by great places to eat and very close to LOTS of shopping (which makes every girl happy :) ) 
The room was very clean, the bed was SOOOO comfortable, and the people in the hotel couldn't have been nicer. I did the valet parking (work was paying, so why not?) which wasn't much more than the nearby lots and very convenient - so even if I was paying for it I would have done it. When I needed my car I just called down to the lobby a few minutes before I planned to leave and my car was waiting right there for me when I came downstairs. 
When you first walk in, the lobby is very warm and inviting. Any and all questions I had were answered by the people working the desk and they were extremely helpful. I had a light lunch at (what I think was called) the Pear Deli around the corner. It was just a cute little deli with a couple of little tables and my sandwich was awesome. For dinner that night I went over to the restaurant across the street (whose name escapes me - but the guy at the front desk recommended) and it was amazing. I took a nice long walk all through the market and then up towards the center of town where there were lots of cool shops and cool people. 
After having a great meal and a nice stroll I came back to my room to see that my bed had been turned down, complete with chocolates (not on the pillow, but on the desk next to the bed lol) I had to do some work (Which is why I was there in the first place - Boo!) but when I was finally able to go to bed, the bed couldn't have been more comfortable. Slept great, got out on time to go to my meeting and then was off to the airport. If/when I go to Seattle again (I hope it's more a question of 'when' since I would have loved to explore the city for more than a couple of hours) I would absolutely stay at the Inn at the Market.

title: “Small and Comfortable”
text: The W Hotel is centrally located. I was able to walk to most locations for dinner and drinks around Union Square, China Town, and Downtown. I had a great view of the city and the Bay Bridge. The rooms are clean and spacious. The only drawbacks were the check-in lobby and valet parking: the lobby is under construction and the valet is $55+ per day.

title: “Hip boutique hotel”
text: The website does this W hotel a disservice. We were afraid we were going to find a golf focused country club themed property. Instead we found a very modern boutique hotel that happens to be next to a golf course. Pet friendly, green (reserved spaces for hybrids and parking spots with chargers for electric vehicles), with the kind of modern style usually found only in new hotels in major cities.
