Very friendly service. Room was of average size and very nicely appointed. Only complaint is plastic cups--not what we expect at this level of style and at this price.

title: “Friendly, helpful, personal touch”
text:
The service was incredible. I received an email prior to my arrival to choose my preferences. The concierge arranged a chilled bottle of champaigne and sweet treats to help us celebrate our anniversary. The concierge that took my info made a point to meet us at the front desk when we arrived. Very welcoming touch. The entire staff was helpful when asking for directions and recommendations.
I never stayed in NY before, so I thought the room was pretty small, but all the reviews say the rooms are huge. Just a matter of perspective, I guess. Our room was very clean, very comfy bed, and modern decor. We had a corner room with windows on both walls, with a view of the Hudson River and Times Square. There are shades on the windows, but light still gets through, not the darkest at night. I heard NY has a problem with bed bugs, but there were none in sight--I did check. I was so happy to have a clean room in NY! It would be nice if they could include a coffee maker in the room for convenience, but they do have free coffee in the lobby every morning.
Location was excellent. Just enough off the beaten path so it wasn't too noisy, but close enough to walk to everything. Subway is in Time Square which was only a 5-10 minute walk, so you can get anywhere. Tons of cabs also driving by all the time. The rooms had everything you needed, and there are complementary items if you forgot anything. Internet was easy to access from the room, and free if you are a Kimpton In Touch member.
Loved that the staff gave that personal touch, was very helpful when asking for restaurant recommendations, and had a friendly smile every time you walked through the lobby. Loved the clean room and comfy bed. The doorman was great, hailing cabs for us and asking about our day/plans. We felt very welcome there. I would recommend this hotel and will definitely stay again.

title: “BEST PLACE TO STAY IN COLUMBUS BAR NONE!”
text:
i have stayed at this hampton previously and enjoyed the stay. this time was no different. Jill, the desk clerk was friendly and helpful, the room was clean, and well appointed (no refrigs. here except in suites).
the bed comfortable, the hot breakfast plentiful and with fruit, cereals, yogurts, etc.
this hotel a little off the highway so it's pretty quiet. highly recommended! happy trails

title: “Nice place - Great Staff”
text: Convenient location. Hotel could use a little updating, but very clean and staff is very friendly and helpful.

title: “Excellent stay”
text: Great value, a bit far from the action downtown but well worth staying if your in town for a short stay. The bartender Jennifer was great! The front staff was about as helpful as any, I'll be back when I'm in town.

title: “Affordable central location”
text:
I stay in LA few times a year on business, but I've never stayed in this area. I must say that this is actually quite a convenient and central location (if there is such a thing in LA). You can walk to a number of places from the hotel, the Beverly Center is the most notable, but there are also a few restaurants and bars nearby as well. If you have a car, you'll find that you can get to Melrose Ave, Hollywood, Beverly Hills etc quickly and easily. Santa Monica and Venice are about 20mins away via the highway.
The hotel is an older style building that has had a recent renovation, and they've done a decent job of it. The rooms are spacious and light, with decent size bathrooms. The beds are comfortable, and they have good free wifi across the hotel. The room we had was right on the road, which is busy both day and night - however we didn't notice it as the rooms are well soundproofed.
The staff are all very very friendly and helpful. The Elan offers valet parking for a fee, but it comes with in/out privileges and they're more than happy to bring up or collect your car at anytime. And by comparison the Elan parking fees are well below the average $30+ charged by most LA hotels. Frankly this is a great place to stay in LA if you are traveling with a car.

title: “Great location!”
text: Traveled to NYC for the first time to meet friends and sightsee. Le Parker Meridien was a great choice for us. The location was wonderful. We were close to Central Park, Times Square, Rockefeller Plaza, shops, restaurants, etc. The rooms were of modern design. Clean and comfortable. Hotel staff was friendly and very helpful.

title: “A comfortable stay in Manhattan..”
text: The hotel was basic,no restaurant facilities,but spotlessly clean. If I had one criticism, it would be its location in relation to Manhattan Island, I would have preferred to have been nearer to "Midtown".Having said that it is within 40 yards of a station, with trains running every few minutes, "Uptown or Downtown".Not expensive by N.Y. standards.

title: “New Years Eve we stayed and my God!”
text:
We needed a cheap place to stay (my husband and I) on NEw Years Eve and boy did we get it. We got a room on the 3rd floor and learned w/help that there is a "trick" to unlocking the door w/the key.
We finally got in the room and it was the size of a box. It smelled and the bathroom was gross to the point I refused to shower the next morning till we got home.
They had the vaccuum going in the hallway at 9 am on New years day in the hallway and it soundedlike a train coming though. Plus, I don't know what they were vaccuming cause the place is a dump!
Also, u cannot control the heat in the room and my husband and I almost wanted to die during the night. It was like a sauna and honestly had to be almost 80 degrees in there.
Would I ever stay again? NO!

title: “Comfortable Stay”
text:
This hotel is listed in historical hotels book. It is a nice building in a god location and is about to undergo a major refurbishment. While the appearance of the internal finishes is still reasonable, it will certainly benefit from the refurb.
The room we had was very comfortable and was on one of the club floors but we were told by one of the reception staff that we were not to use the club facilities - why put you on a club floor if you are not supposed to take part. After a day or so, when the people providing the club facilities asked why don't we partake, we decided why not. Club facilities are very handy when your traveling - continental breakfast, drinks, hors deuvres, fruit etc 
The rooms and the hotel generally, appeared to be cleaned and maintained well and I would also recommend the restaurant in the hotel - food and service was very good and the price was comparable to other nice restaurants of this standard.
While the hotel was within walking distance of the Smithsonian, it was easier and pretty cheap to just get a cab each way - also it meant not wasting time - so many things to see in DC. Once your in the museum area, there is one museum after the other and you are walking all day, so the last thing we needed was another walk back to the hotel.

title: “Would Recommend This Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Milburn for 9 nights in September, 2004 and were pleased with the accommodations. As other reviews have mentioned, the location is only a short walk to either the 72nd or 79th St. subway stations. There is an abundance of nice restaurants that are really inexpensive and we never seemed to have to wait for a table no matter how busy they were. They have room air conditioners but the rumble of them can drown out any street traffic, although that was not even a problem. The living room and bedroom we had were very spacious (and we liked having TVs in both rooms). It was great having the little kitchenette (nothing fancy but very functional - and the market was around the corner-very convenient). My only "complaint" was with the bathroom. It was very tiny which I'd expect in Europe but not here. It also seemed a little run down. And then there was a bit of a bug problem. Let's just say that under the bathroom sink there was a roach motel and this was a good thing. So, if you like sparkling and spacious bathrooms, you might have an issue here. However, all the positives of this place outweighed any "bathroom blues" since we spent so little time in the room. I'd go back.

title: “Update to home away from home”
text: Wanted to give special thanks to Shavonna,Catherine, Angela and Stephanie. Shavonna sets up my room and the rest help fill in the rewards. This is also a thanks to the other staff members from Robert at the bell desk, Gaby in the bar area, Helena my coffee wonder. Walking down the hall one of the bell men said hello Mr. Garrett as did those at the front desk when I arrived. Had a meal at the bar and the service and quality of food was very good. Of course so is the wine selection. Westin and its other affiliations have been very good to me and also my wife Bunny when we travel. The Westin and W in Chicago and other places as well. Staff is the core of any great stay and the Westin Group does a great job.

title: “Good value for Boston!”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights. Boston hotels are notoriously expensive and this was the best deal we could find (on Expedia). The room was unexciting initially but clean and comfortable and spacious for a hotel which seemed to be a labyrinth of corridors. The staff on reception were very helpful and friendly and the complementary continental breakfast was very good (kept fully restocked and fresh).
The hotel is next to Fenway park (Boston Red Sox home ground) with plenty of bars and restaurants nearby (within walking distance). It's also close to a T stop (the underground) and bus stops so easy to get into the main tourist areas. It's also easy walking distance to most places in the guidebooks. As a rough guideline - you can walk to Copley Square in ~15 minutes, ~25 minutes walk to Boston Public Gardens and the Freedom Trail and in ~25-30 minutes to the Aquarium and Quincy Market. And it's a nice walk!
p.s. do a Duck Tour!!!

title: “You Get What You Pay For”
text: Booked through Expedia to see the Phillies play at Camden Yards because rates around the Harbor were terribly high. The 8-block walk to the water wasn't bad, but I'd only really recommend doing it in daylight. The desk staff were polite and helpful, but housekeeping knocked at 8:30 a.m. and again around 9:30 a.m. The interior of the room was shabby and both the a/c and the tv remote control didn't work great. Didn't do the breakfast, and the public parking garage across the street didn't make us feel overly confident. Next time we'll pay for a nicer place downtown.

title: “A good hotel showing it's age”
text:
This is my 2nd stay at this hotel. I bring my son (Who is now 10)here ever time this year. Baltimore school system starts the first week of September so all the local attractions are empty. No lines no crowds. 
Complimentary access to the health club that is sharing the building is nice. Location can not be beat. Walking distance to Science Center, Aquarium and ships. Zoo is about 30 min. This is a the real selling point to this hotel Esp. when parking is very expensive in this area.
Staff is friendly and accommodating. The room is clean & comes with a full kitchenette. They have upgraded to flat screen TV's. Beds are soft and comfortable. Excellent sound proofing between suites. The Furniture and carpet are showing their age. A wear/ stain here and there. Not bad but but four star caliber.

title: “Good Value Great Location”
text: Stayed 4 nights at the Capitol Hill Suites. Was looking for a mid range hotel in a good location at a reasonable and came up with the Capitiol Hill Suites. Was not disappointed. reception and the public areas have seen better days but the room was top notch and the breakfast was more than adequate. If you can get this hotel at a reasonable rate take it. You won’t be disappointed. Great location for tourist activities only a couple of blocks from the Capitol. Staff were friendly and courteous at all times.

title: “A Recommended Business Option in a Central Local”
text:
I stayed at the Capitol Hill Suites for 4 nights in December 2011 while on a work trip. I got a wonderful deal on the rate via Travelzoo. The location was perfect, one and a half blocks from the Metro South subway stop – very central on the Orange and Blue lines. C-Street is quiet and full of beautiful residences (I learned that young House Reps often rent places here) The hotel was walking distance from the Hill and just a short block from a lively strip of Pennsylvania Ave with lots of good dining options. (I enjoyed Pound the Hill and We the Pizza, and wanted to try the Sonoma Wine Bar!)
My room was clean and nice. It was very comfortable to have that little sitting area, free fast wifi, a good robe, a microwave and a fridge for restaurant leftovers. There was also a great desk – so all in all the room was a perfect place to actually get work done. As mentioned before the breakfast was good - continental with plenty of fruit, cereal and toast/bagel options and spreads. I liked the way they offered a to-go coffee station and had staff coming around to pour coffee at the tables if you were dining in. Very well done. There was also coffee available at all hours in the hotel lobby – a welcome touch.
The staff was quite friendly. The only thing I would say – is that if you are the kind of person that depends on a good deal of concierge services – this wouldn’t really be the spot for you. There aren’t really tourism brochures or addition information available downstairs and the front desk was not really able to assist me book a shuttle pickup to return to the airport. The Capitol Hill Suites is geared toward business travelers and does the job very well.

title: “Had some problems but they reduced rate in the end making it quite fair after al”
text: Booked 2 rooms (1 king, 1 with 2 doubles). We had 5 in our party traveling, 2 adults with 3 children. Checked in was massive chaos for every one, their computers were down. We got 2 rooms each with a king bed (does not work for 5 people) at opposite ends of the hotel. Went back downstairs to very rude staff that did not seem willing to help with our situation. I told them our rooms had to be closer since we have children and they needed 2 double beds. They finally found what we needed. Total check-in time was about 2 hours. Hotel condition was great, lobby was absolutely beautiful. Rooms were good and spacious for NY, although ours did not look like the one on the hotel website. There was a lot of street noise even 6 floors up, maybe that is normal for NY though. Had some other minor trouble with check-out and luggage, but the day manager ended up reducing our rate by $70/night/room. Quite fair. Great location for subway, Grand Central was 2 blocks away.

title: “Nice hotel great location - but ripped off by the concierge”
text:
A nice hotel in a great location close to 5th AV, Rockefeller Centre and Times Square. Just beside a subway station. But the concierge left a bad experience.
We booked a show, but the concierge charged us double the price. We wouldn't mind a fee or commission but not twice the ticket price.

title: “It has a pool”
text:
This is the least expensive place to stay in Manhattan with an outdoor pool. The rooms were a good size, and it is fine value for the money. You get what you expect from a Holiday Inn. There are free
local papers at the front desk. It is on a main street, and so the rooms are pretty noisy. The lobby is often busy. It is convenient to several subway lines and the Park.

title: “it's great place to stay”
text:
We stayed there for 5 nights in level 19. All staffs are really friendly. The service is good. The location is good, really close to the 42 street port authority bus terminal, if you need take subway to go somewhere. 7 minutes walk to the Time Square. 
Before we got to N.Y., we traveled from L.A. to Las Vegas to San Fran. By the time we are in N.Y., we got a load of washings. The free laundry just what we needed. Also, the full kitchen facilities are great. As we had been traveled for more than 2 weeks, dinning out all the time is killing me. It is so good I can cook some noodles with boiling veg. :) 
The hotel also provide free print service if you need to print your tickets or boarding pass. 
A great rate for NYC, free wireless internet, free laundry, full kitchen facilities.

title: “Great Service”
text:
I stayed with my family and extended family. Asked for two rollaway beds and they were delivered fast.
Breakfast was plenty and good. Rooms and hallways were always clean. Staff was very helpful giving acurate directions.
Best of all is that's located away from the noisy big streets but you could always walk everywhere.

title: “Not Impressed”
text: We use to live in Phoenix and decided to stay at this resort for a few nights during a week long trip to Sedona and the grand canyon. This place is a disappointment. We did book and receive a nice sized 1 bedroom suite. The suite was dated as was the hotel. This place needs a make over...I would start with a fresh coat of paint everywhere. The pools were very crowded especially on the weekend. The bar tender at the pool said they let locals in for a charge to use the pools in the summer months when business is slow in Phoenix. The pool was an all out free for all..there was no way to relax. Way too overcrowded. The only plus to this place was the breakfast...it was awesome especially on Sunday morning...they do a real nice brunch. I am a Hilton diamond customer and stay in Hilton's 3-5 times a month on business...there are much better places, even Hiltons to stay at in Phoenix. Not impressed.

title: “Bed Bugs”
text:
Stood at the four points not too long ago. I absolutly loved the front desk staff. They have to be the best staff I have ever met. The location is great, next to everything. The room is small and dark and a little too much money (you can stay at the W new york for less) but that is somewhat compensated for the service. However there is one serious problem that will cause me to unfortunatly never stay there again.
During my stay I noticed 2 sets of matresses outside of the hotel, wrapped in sheets. Out of my own curiosity I decided to take a peek and see why these mattress were being tossed. To my surprise they were infested with bed bug droppings it was ABSOLUTLY DISGUSTING! I immediatly went back to my room to inspect my bed, thankfully there were no bugs in my bed. The discovery of this led me to not have a very good nights sleep. 
So word to the wise CHECK YOUR BED! Don't let the bed bugs bite!

title: “Great hotel to stay while sightseeing in Chicago”
text:
We had two rooms for five nights, not a complaint from us. The staff are great, so helpful; the location is great; short walk to subway and buses; block and a half from Michigan Avenue, three blocks from Lake Michigan and Navy Pier. 
The rooms are light, clean, and comfortable. 
There are no fridges or microwaves, which we could understand, no need for food in your room. The complimentary breakfast is great, 24 hour a day coffee. The exercise room is small but adequate.

title: “Great room, expensive breakfast”
text: Tough place to get a cab from at 7:45am, and they threw me in a town car and took me to BART. Great service and a killer price from Hotwire ($139) for a hotel this nice in the city.

title: “Cute, chic hotel in Boston's South End neighborhood”
text: I moved here on my 2nd night in Boston after a less-than-stellar stay in a hostel in the Back Bay area. I was lucky to book a one-bedroom with a queen size bed for two nights at 1:00 in the morning. The price was pretty decent given that the average going rate for bigger hotels at the time I visited was around $200+/night. Since my move was last minute, I didn't do enough research (I moved here because of the price and availability), but I was pleasantly surprised. Overall, the location can't be beat (a few blocks away from a "T" station, Trinity Church/Boston Public Library and Boston Common). The staff was helpful and friendly, and the Sports Bar attached to the hotel had decent brunch Sunday morning. The hotel room reminded me of boutique hotels in Europe. The bathroom was a little on the small side, and one can sometimes hear conversations in the hallway, but for the price, location and cleanliness, it can't be beat. I will stay here again if I ever come back to Boston.

title: “Pretty Good Hotel”
text: I had booked the concierge level room -- nice room, higher floor, clean, and great amenities including chocolates, mints, bath & body works products in bathroom. Concierge lounge is just ok - they have fruit, water, and soda and a few snacks but not sure it's worth an extra $30-$40 night. I didn't get to see what they had for breakfast. Restaurant was pretty good for breakfast and lunch. Gym is modern. Staff was very friendly -- no problems getting a 2 pm checkout. Also, bell desk staff was very attentive and helpful. Good choice for a San Jose Hotel.

title: “Great Hotel and Great Locations!!!! Only One Concern”
text: The hotel location was great. Extremely clean. Close to ChinaTown and the shopping district. My wife and I stayed her for two nights and were able to walk to everything. Hotel offers a discounted rate at a nearby parking garage which worked perfect for our stay. My only negative was the noise in the room next to the elevator. The elevator cable beat the walls when moving from floor to floor. I think rooms 201, 301, 401.... are next to the elevator. Other than this one detail, I would highly receommend this hotel.

title: “Living on a Name”
text:
Room not ready when we arrived late afternoon. Room dirty - used tissues in drawers. Moved to a different room - one intended for disabled customers. Electric sockets not attached to walls, exposed wires on socket next to bathroom sink, incredibly noisy toilet (could be heard from the down the corridor). Handle to help people out of the bath came away in my hand - thank heavens I'm not disabled! Towel rail hanging off the wall. Took two days for anyone to come and look at problems and only one of them (the bath handle) got fixed during 4 night stay. No shower gel, etc, in bathroom. £8 for two glasses of coke in the bar - not allowed to put on room bill. 
The Waldorf Astoria has a great name and reputation, but it totally failed to live up to any of our expectations. I really would not want to go back there!

title: “Clean, Neat, and Close to Everything”
text:
This is a very neat, clean, and quiet hotel that's close to everything in Charlotte! It's right off 85 which is very convenient. You can't beat the price at $50/night!
I had coffee in the morning but I didn't partake of the free breakfast, but it looked fine if all you are looking for is cold cereal and milk. At this price point, I wouldn't expect much.

title: “One of the best kept secrets in Hollywood area”
text: remodeled with all new furnishings, marble spa shower and bathroom, marble kitchenette wet bar, great mattress for sleeping, collectible quality autographed artwork on the walls, spotlessly clean guestrooms, cute pool in the courtyard, and an amazing top notch diner restaurant off the lobby (the food is really THAT good, service fast and friendly). Walking distance to the Hollywood & Vine Metro subway stop, and just 2 blocks off the #101 Freeway, secure parking is worth the valet fee. It's maybe 1 mile east of the 'heart' of Hollywood, but certainly close to everything and a bargain for it's location and upgraded condition. Look forward to staying here again.

title: “Nice, cosy hotel with a personal touch.”
text: A group of us stayed at the Serrano for 3 nights. It is located in a quiet area of San Francisco, although is close by foot to shopping, nightlife and restaurants. Front desk and concierge staff are friendly and efficient. Rooms are average size and have character rarely found in other hotels. Hosted wine reception downstairs was a great way to meet fellow travellers and work up an appetite for an evening meal. The fitness centre is well equipped with a sauna. Breakfast is a little expensive (coffee and tea provided free), but there are good options a short stroll away.

title: “Great Stay as always”
text: Stayed here for the second year in a row, while in town for business and a little R&R with wife. We got the same exact room as we did last year. And it is now our favorite. We had a room by the atrium which was no problem to us with people downstairs. You can't go wrong with the free food and drinks in the evening, and breakfast in the morning. All the staff was very friendly and helpful. We had a king room, which had the mini fridge and microwave. Will stay again without question.

title: “Clean, reasonable, good location!”
text: A clean, reasonable hotel in a good location is always a plus in San Francisco. This older property doesn't have lots of bells and whistles, but you can count on a safe, convenient location and a very reasonable rate. Our charming, historical room was a tad "worn", but very clean. The tiny bathroom was clean, well appointed and complete with a generous clawfoot tub. The hotel is just a few blocks from the fun shops and restaurants of Fillmore St and Japantown, however, it feels residential. The cozy bar was perfect for an evening glass of wine and appetizers. The hotel staff was polite and friendly. We have stayed in more outstanding places in San Francisco. But, for a pleasant, convenient, reasonable place to stay, The Hotel Majestic will fit the bill.

title: “Pleasant one night stay in NW Indianapolis”
text: We were able to use a Roomsaver coupon for $42 at this place right off the Interstate. We got a quiet room in the rear, away from the main road, There were two beds, 2 pillows each. The lights over the beds were a good touch. No breakfast included, but there is a McDonalds right behind the motels. Free Wifi.

title: “Not clean & damp”
text: The room was not very clean, found hairs all over the bathroom. The a/c in the room didn't work, when we walked into the room for the first time the room was damp

title: “Almost perfect”
text: Booked this hotel for a last minute, one night stay after checking Tripadvisor as usual and was lucky to get the last room they had. Location is perfect, as I imagine most hotels are as the city is so easily walkable. The welcome you get from the staff is very friendly and nothing seemed too much trouble. So the room wasn't huge but for these prices you should not expect luxury - what you get instead is cleanliness, comfort, friendly service, humour - all the things that make for a great little hotel. I'm coming back here in October and would recommend the hotel to anyone.

title: “Noisy Guests in Hall ways”
text:
Our room was clean and kind of different in a modern way, but nice.
The girl who checked us in was very pleasent.
The bartender was very friendly and we enjoyed the very cool lighted bar top.
We did experience much noise from the room across the hall . People coming and going most of the night. Did not sleep well.

title: “Great location - really good hotel”
text:
Really liked this hotel and would not hesitate to stay again. The rooms are big and clean, plus you get a quiet nights sleep even though it is centrally located.
Here is a list of the things that were important to me :
- 15min walk to Central Park, 10min walk to Times Square, 5min walk to Rockefeller Centre, 5min walk to 5th Avenue, 20min walk to Grand Central, 20min walk to Empire State Building. Subway very nearby. 
- CD player and TV with a good choice of channels.
- two hob cooker, with fridge.
- free internet access in their 'Business Centre'.
- seperate bathroom and toilet.
- free (micro) copy of Time Out in the foyer.
There is room service for the food, but I thought the prices were a bit high. Plenty of deli's nearby, particularly heading west past 6th Avenue (Digbys was my favourite).
Despite a couple of isolated occasions, staff are generally friendly and helpful.
We were on the 18th floor and the lifts could be a bit infrequent, but not a major hassle.

title: “It's PERFECT if you remember it's a HOSTEL.”
text:
Just a few lines to speak well about this HOSTEL.
I read this forum before going there but after i did the
reservation ONLINE and I was really SCARED.
There are lots of people that love to scare with all that dangerous comments.
Finally the hostel was perfect. YES! simple rooms and shared bath but if you
want just to sleep is a perfect place. The beds are the best.

Don't be afraid with the area. the 96th with broadway is full of live and
it's not absolutely dangerous.

least 10 people or more.
Pedro.

title: “Stayed 1 night and all went well.”
text: Right off the highway and between a mechanic shop and buildings. Front desk was super friendly. Lobby was nice with a clean, decent sized breakfast area (dry cereal, waffles, fruit, pastries, muffins, toast, coffee and juice). Room was clean and good size with a king bed (springy but also very comfortable) and sofabed, micro/fridge, desk and chair, cable tv and internet (which had to be used from a cord in the wall but worked fine). A/c was great! Pool looked small but clean. Bathroom was clean and decent sized with hot water but a weak shower stream. Had a bottom floor room at the end of some stairs and heard a bit of that noise as well as the neighbor's door closing and opening, but other than that had a peaceful sleep. Would consider staying again if the price is right!

title: “NIce place to stay”
text: The staff is great here and make you feel at home. The rooms were recently remodeled and are clean and comfortable. Not much soundproofing inside or out, so if you are a light sleeper probably not a good place for you. Not a lot of frills, but nice basic place to stay.

title: “Big rooms bad neighboorhood”
text:
Well, the price is fair for Hollywood area. The room (213) was big with an king-size bed. Has air-conditioning, iron table, big bathroom. The room was very clean. Very big windows.
Free parking for guests which is a good thing in Hollywood. 
A big food market near the motel, little bit expensive.
The motel has one Internet position near the reception desk at the rate of $1= 10 minutes use. No ink in the printer.
Now, the less good facts:
Getting a king-size bed at first floor was conditioned by acceptance of a bad phone in the room - it's ringing every 20 seconds. The phone have been not repaired during my 3-nights staying and I disconnected the cable without possibility to be called.
While the hotel it's on Hollywood boulevard, it's located quite far from the hot areas of this boulevard in a bad and poor neighboorhood in so called Thai Town. Not a very special security feeling at evening hours. 
My room has the windows in the backyard at 15ft from a 4 floors block of flats. This caused a lot of noise from the tenants and their children and cannot leave the window open for fresh air. 
Beginning 8.00AM a lot of noise is coming from the maids on the corridors.
The so-called DeLuxe continental breakfast is very poor and is served in a very small room. Some cereals, few old donuts, no butter, no milk no bread. 
The little restaurant near the hotel is open only few hours per day, is very dirty and poor food and service. Do not enter in this place. 
The reception clerks, were quite OK while of not much help if you asking for road directions or points of interests. Unfortunately, arriving home, I discovered they mistekenly charged me with another night while the receipt says $74 less. I'm still waiting for refund. 
The motel is very far from points of interests and no decent restaurants or fastfood on at least 1.5 mile radius. 
There are better places to stay closer to hotspots on Hollywood Blvd at slighty higher price.

title: “Tiny rooms”
text: ShockIngly small room. Kind of like sleeping in a closet. However, super close to the Gershwin theater is you are going to see Wicked. Clean enough. Very loud- like the window is open due to window air conditioner. Rooftop has potential when it's done.

title: “Fantastic Stay”
text: Just got back from a fantastic stay at the Hotel Monaco. Thought this was excellent location for a downtown Seattle trip- only a 10-min. walk or so to the Market, or to the Monorail to Seattle Ctr., and generally positioned right in the middle of things. Further, thought the staff was very friendly & customer-service focused. Concierge gave great advice; cleaning staff was very good; front desk very friendly. Enjoyed the "wine" happy hours they host for free in the lobby every night. Room was very pleasant, however, our room didn't have any view (it looked into a wall), so if that's important, may want to look into that ahead of time.

title: “Outstanding experience delivered by well trained customer focused personnel”
text: My wife and I have visited California on many occasions during the last few years, we found the Magic Castle Hotel some 2 years ago and have seen significant improvement particularly in the infrastructure of the building during our visits to Hollywood. We were always impressed by the overall friendliness of the hotel staff and their desire to always help and go the extra mile. The management of the hotel have undertaken a strategic room by room refurbishment which is beginning to match the staff's enthusiasm for delivering outstanding service.

title: “Great Find in great location”
text:
We planned a girls weekend and were looking for decent place without the huge pricetag. The Newbury Guest House fit the bill! 
It's centrally located on Newbury St among shops, restaurants spas and anything else you could need. For a boutique hotel, the room was very spacious and ultra comfortable. There was limited parking in the back (you have to leave keys with desk in case they need to move it), but it was nice to know we could just park it & leave it until we left 2 days later. The Copley Station was only a couple blocks away and made it so easy to get around the city. Would totally stay there again if and when I get back to the city.

title: “Great value!”
text: This hotel is easy to find and located in the heart of restaurants and shopping galore! The staff is extremely friendly and welcoming, the room and grounds were clean, the pool and hot tub were relaxing and the breakfast was wonderful! If you are looking for a comfy and clean room at a great value this is the place for you!

title: “we enjoyed our stay”
text: we were very suprised at the quality of the room and services for the cost that we paid. it was a good central location for everything we did in houston. It had one of best free breakfast at any place we stayed. Service was very good also

title: “Disappointed - avoid”
text: Had high hopes for this hotel but were very disappointed. This hotel sells itself on fantastic views but despite a request from our travel agent for a room on a high floor, we were given a room (which was very well appointed to be fair) on floor five overlooking the bins and horrible buildings behind. We asked reception if we could move but they were totally disinterested and very dismissive. Overall it left a bad taste in our mouth and we won't be back. This is an expensive hotel, even for the 'lower' rooms...there are better value options nearby.

title: “Very Nice - Very Difficult to Find”
text:
We reserved a room as a half-way point on our trip to Disney World. We were exhausted after driving for 7+ hours and had a very difficult time locating the hotel. It is very far off of I-95 when you are traveling south and get onto S-9A. 
Despite the extra time, this was a nice hotel! The lobby was very contemporary looking. The front desk attendant made check in a breeze. There was limited entry to the facility from the parking area, but it was well lite.
The rooms were very nice with a frig. The beds and linens looked new. The bathroom was very clean. I would recommend putting extra floor mats/towels since there are only shower stalls...no tub. Water got EVERYWHERE when trying to assist my little one with his shower.
We needed to find a grocery store before leaving town. The second attendant was very informative on giving directions and was very helpful.

title: “Great location but that's about it.”
text: This hotel's biggest plus point is its location. Staff is friendly. However, the rooms are tiny with barely enough room to move. Super thin walls and minimal amenities. Only WIFI access is in the lobby area and there is zero phone reception in the rooms for some reason. No frills stay.

title: “Amazing Small Hotel, Amazing Location”
text: Myself and Girlfriend stayed here for 3 nights to celebrate my 24th birthday, upon finding out it was my birthday the hotel sent up a free bottle of champagne. The room itself was on the small side, but as they say less is more? The room was well appointed and was spotless, the bed was extremely comfortable, and was quiet. The staff done everything they could do to be helpful, and the free nightly wine and cheese tastings was a really nice thing to come back to after a strenuous day of sightseeing. Would recommend anyone to stay here. A TIP - we flew to/from Newark, we got a taxi from the airport to the hotel, it was around $90 after tip(the taxi driver asked for more tip saying it was not enough what i gave him, the only thing i hate about the US!) We got the train back from the hotel, it cost $15 each and took 25minsto get to airport vs the 1hour to get to hotel in traffic, will get the train next time from airport, its is 2 stops on nj transit from penn station and is much easier than you may think.

title: “Excellent budget accommodation”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here in a Junior Queen Suite for two nights and were very happy with the facilities. Capitol Hill Suites offer clean and modern serviced apartment accommodation, located only a block away from the blue and orange subway lines (easy access to the National Mall and White House areas) and within very close proximity to the Capitol Building, Library of Congress and US Supreme Court. Some restaurants and cafes are also conveniently located nearby.
Our room was spacious with quite comfortable bedding and a nice flatscreen TV, which we were more than happy to just chill out and watch after a long day of checking out museums and monuments!
I would definitely recommend the Capitol Hill Suites to anyone staying here for leisure or business - the place provides very good value for money and the staff are both helpful and friendly.

title: “Very Poor Service & Hotel Maintenance”
text: I spent quite a bit of time selecting this hotel. Very disappointed in the service and noise. Throughout our stay various items in the room didn't work and had to have maintenance come to room multiple times to fix. They charge $23 to valet your car and it might take about 23 hours to get your car back. We were told to expect 10 minutes. Well, we did that and we practically missed an appointment we had because we waited about 30 minutes for them to bring around our car. Hardly worth $23. Don't expect to be able to use their safe. Never properly worked after multiple maintenance requests. Expect noise. Asked for a quiet room but lots of noise from the area. And if you want to use the toilet without any issues, well good luck to you. Maintenance, no doubt, will probably need to be called. When I called regarding the toilet, as I had just checked in, they asked, "Didn't you call earlier about your toilet? No, I said, it was probably the guest before me." Maybe they should have fixed it then. Not impressed at all.

title: “Perfect Beverly Hills Experience”
text:
Just stayed at the SLS last weekend. Peninsula Chicago was my favorite US hotel... until staying there. It's a combination of a W on steroids meets the service of The Four Seasons and the hipness of The Cosmopolitan. 
Make sure to check out the pool on the weekends.

title: “Perfect Hotel”
text: We were welcomed with a glass of fizz and a cheery smile and so continued the high quality service we received at the River Inn. We sipped a glass of champagne overlooking the Mississippi River and dined in the French restaurant, Paulette's. The food was excellent. Breakfasts were delicious and certainly set us all up for the day. The bedrooms were charming, with chocolates and port supplied each evening. I would absolutely recommend this hotel.

title: “I felt like I was VIP!”
text: My stay at the Lenox was nothing short of wonderful. The staff was very accomodating and my room was spacious and comfortable.

title: “Fabulous Location, Fabulous Time”
text: I originally booked the Best Western President after reading the reviews on Tripadvisor and searching for a centrally located hotel within Manhatten. Well, I certainly got that. This hotel is right at Times Square and is perfectly located for everything. Central Park is within easy walking distance and the subway station is just at the end of the street so everything else is very easy to get to as well. This was our first time in New York and I have to admit I was very surprised at the level of service you get everywhere and how safe I felt whilst walking around, even at night. You hear all sorts of bad stuff regarding the States but, it can't be further from the truth. We had a fantastic time and I would definately recommend the Best Western President.

title: “Keep personal items safely with you.”
text: Beware of housekeeping. They ignore the do not disturb signs and enter your room. My room had personal items removed so "they could clean" even though we had late check out prearranged and a do not disturb sign on the door. I was so glad I had taken my laptop with me!! Hotel is not well maintained - smelly and dirty.

title: “Awesome Hotel - Clean and Great Service”
text: I stayed at the Downtown Inner Harbor hotel prior to going on a cruise. The manager Abraham was most accomodating to help us make our cruise transfers to and from the port. The rooms were very clean and comfortable. It is within walking distance to the Inner Harbor area. I strongley recommend the hotel for any stay in Baltimore Md. Make sure you use the stay and ride program for any cruise holiday, it will save you money!!!!

title: “Location is the best”
text: The location of Hollywood Celebrity Hotel was fantastic, only 2 min walk from Hollywood Blvd. This hotel was very clean and well maintained and the staff was very friendly and helpful. Rooms were large and clean.

title: “Great location, recently renovated.”
text: This is the second time we have stayed at this hotel. The location is excellent between Central Park and Times Square and easy access to the Metro. The hotel was recently renovated, and the rooms were very clean and comfortable. Rooms are on the smaller side but normal for New York. Free WiFi is available only in the lobby.

title: “Awful hotel”
text: This has got to be one of the worst hotels I have ever stayed at. I checked in and the "owner" complained that Expedia are taking 30% off his profit and that he should block all Expedia bookings. Then I got to the room where NO towels were in the room, the bed had cigarette burns, the ceiling had mould stains, furniture just had stains everywhere and I would hate to guess what type of stains they where. The cleaning staff were total useless. How this type of hotel can stay in business is beyond my comprehension. I paid for the full week and stayed one night. I stayed with friends 50 mins away from Houston due to no availability in Houston. While this was inconvenient it was better than staying in a fully paid shanty that should have been condemned years ago. Pathetic and shame on Expedia for giving this two stars. I have provided pictures. Don't waste your money here. The only reason why I even tried this hotel was because ALL Houston hotels were packed.

title: “location,location,location!”
text:
30 second walk to subway, tourist bus stop & times sq. 
handy drug store at end of the road to fill up the room fridge with drinks. 
we were staying over the weekend, the bar was closed Sat & Sun but when was open the happy hour prices were very good and so was really quite busy. Breakfast limited to pastries, bagels, coffee.
Overall a good stay, would recommend & stay again without doubt.

title: “Great hotel for the family”
text:
We stayed at the Residence Inn from May17th-May 23rd. We booked a one bedroom suite for my self, wife, and our two young boys.
The room was spacious for a downtown property and very clean. Each morning a breakfast is served the lobby and in the evening there is a happy hour with a light dinner. These are included with your stay. Huge money saver for a family. We did breakfast each morning but never made the happy hour. Waitstaff was excellent and friendly. Food was fresh and a wonderful selection.
The fitness room on the 8th floor includes an outdoor patio and hot tub. The fitness room it self is on the small side. 2 treadmills, one bike, one eliptical, and some free weights. Does the job and is clean. Coin laundry located on the 9th and 12th floors and again maintained and clean.
Location is great. 2 blocks from 16th street mall and free bus along the street. You can hop on a 2 minute free bus ride and walk to Coors field within 5 minutes. After the game my son and i took one of the carriage bike rides back the the hotel. The riders work on tips only.
Also very close if driving to Children's Muesum, Denver Zoo, and many other family attractions.
Covered parking takes up the floors 1-5 and cost $13 a day with in and out service. Worth the money.
Our next visit to Denver will be spent at the Residence Inn City Center. Loved it.

title: “Wonderful experience at Riverwalk”
text: My family and I stayed at the Westin Riverwalk this past weekend and had a wonderful time. Not only is the hotel exquisite, but the staff is extremely helpful and generous. Our room overlooked the river and the view was great! We were right in the middle of all the action on Riverwalk and were able to enjoy the sights and sounds of San Antonio and then come home to the luxury of our hotel after a long day of fun. We will definitely be making reservations for a return visit very soon.

title: “Great Location”
text: Hotel is great for us. Close to Freeway and family. Bowling alley and restaurant Close (Like next door). Family loves it and will return

title: “Good price, excellent location & quiet - Stay here!”
text:
My boyfriend & I stayed at the Galleria Park in San Francisco in June 2007. We had a four-night stay, at $225 (including tax) per night. This was a great price compared to other hotels in the area (a lot of which had bad reviews on this site). We were very impressed with this hotel.
The location is great. Shopping starts one block away. 3 blocks from Union Square & Powell Street cable car and a few blocks to Chinatown & other areas of interest.
As stated on other reviews, the hotel offers coffee in the morning & wine in the evening, which was lovely. While we were there, one of the elevators was closed due to maintenance (upgrading to a better/faster one the sign said) - although we were on the 5th floor, this did not inconvenience us and we were never waiting longer than a minute. The staff members we encountered were polite and efficient.
The room was a good size. Big double bed - with 4 large pillows - extremely comfortable! Built-in wardrobe, walk-in - with ironing board, iron & bath robe. Bathroom was extremely clean with lovely white fluffy towels and good products. Shower worked well and had a more powerful setting. TV was quite large with many stations. Mini-bar was full.
We were at the back of the hotel in an inner-corner room, which didn't have much of a view, but that didn't matter to us as we were out-and-about most of our time there.
We had no noise from traffic & we were never disturbed by the cleaners or anyone else (although we did put the DND sign on door just in case).
Overall, we had an excellent stay here!

title: “I like this place”
text:
The street it's on is not very attractive, but this is not the Upper East Side. But it's safe, and well-located near numerous subway and bus lines. I have stayed here several times, and the best rooms are the higher floors on the street side. (There is a bar with a big outdoor terrace adjacent to the back side of the hotel and it gets very noisy on nice evenings - earplugs required.) The rooms are small (especially those with 2 beds), but well-appointed.
As for the restaurant, the bar snacks are good, and I've never eaten dinner there. I would skip any breakfast package -- the service is slow and the food mediocre. For dining options, head south on 7th Avenue -- once you cross 23rd Street, start reading menus in windows, or search Chelsea, Gramercy and Flatiron in OpenTable. I like Singe Vert, Trois Canards and Eolo.

title: “Total Satisfaction”
text: Our recent stay at The Argonaut Hotel could not have been better. The entire staff was courteous, helpful and friendly. We have never been greeted by such a friendly front desk staff. Our room was great (King Suite). It was spotless, comfortable and beautifully appointed. We've stayed in Union Square, Nob Hill and near the Ferry Building and we find the location of this hotel to be perfect. Every mode of transportation is right at your fingertips to get you to any place on your sightseeing and dining adventures. Don't think about staying here - book a room and find out for youself.

title: “Wonderful hotel in ideal location!”
text: Stayed recently at the Hyatt downtown for Austin City Limits festival. From moment one the hotel was overly accommodating and truly a great place to spend the weekend. From the free lemonade and iced tea in the lobby, to the late night eats guide they printed and distributed, to the impeccable views of a beautiful city, the hotel was a highlight of our trip! Room was very nice, comfortable bed and amazing view of downtown Austin and the amazing bat bridge. We dined in the hotel late night (midnight after shows) one night and the food was great. Eating on the outdoor porch with couches and fireplace while overlooking the water was a great way to end the night. Very clean hotel and amazing service with lots of amenities such as computer kiosk room check-in, coffee shop in lobby, and a place to print out your boarding pass before your trip to the airport. This hotel could be in the middle of nowhere and be great, but the location is really unbeatable. You are a 5-10 minute walk across the bridges to downtown Austin and all its amazing restaurants and bar scene. You are about a 25 minute scenic walk over to Zilker Park and the springs and you are a 20 minute walk down to South Congress area, with its quirky shops and great bars/restaurants. We were first timers to Austin and were thankful that the hotel was so centrally located so that we could really explore the city! Can't say enough about this hotel! If you want to introduce yourself to Austin-come here!

title: “Stay”
text:
My mother and I took a quick trip to LA in January and stayed in the Bungalow suite for two nights. It was very charming and private, with adequate space for 2-4 people if you don't mind a cramped bathroom. The Bungalow is tucked behind the main house and feels secluded, with very little street noise audible from inside. I'd highly recommend the Villa to anyone looking to stay in Hollywood. I'll definitely make an effort to go back the next time I'm in the area. It's lovely.
My only warning is that if you have a large vehicle, parking may be a challenge, particularly if you're in the Bungalow, as the spot is all the way at the end of the driveway. It's a small space around a tight corner. Backing out with a large rental car was difficult.

title: “cheap, clean, great location”
text: We are a couple of 60 something guys who came to town for a baseball game and some gambling. Although it is old and lacks some amenities, we found it cheap, clean, and in a great location. We walked to Comerica Park, Greeektown, Casino, RenCen, etc. Hotels a block away were $100 per night more. I'm a suburban Detroit native and I was surprised at the huge amount of weekend night life in the area. Which leads to some advice. Get a room on an upper floor to get away from the street noise. I should note that our wives probably would not have rated it as high as we did.

title: “This is the One!”
text:
I booked this resort through a getaway from Interval International.
I booked a 2-bedroom unit for my husband and me and my sister-in-law and her husband. We arrived early and the clerk was very nice. The unit was a 2-bedroom lock-out so the studio unit was not cleaned but we were able to leave our luggage in the one-bedroom until the studio unit was available. The grocery store and mall was no more than a mile away and easy to access. The resort also have a shuttle bus that will take you the mall (no charge) and to JW Marriott. The Marriott Canyon Villas resort is very clean! The weight room and exercise room are nice but sort of small, which is fine because it was never crowded. Also it is open 24 hours. There are 2 pools at the Marriott Canyon Villas, these are nice but the real treat was the lazy pool at the JW Marriott! We were able to relax to the fullest in the lazy river pool and I really enjoyed the sliding board! All residents at the Marriott Canyon has access to the pools at the JW Marriott Resort. The JW Marriott resort is beautiful! The green grass, tall shady trees and decor is marvelously. The JW Marriott has 4 pools including a nice sprinkler for the little ones. The front desk clerks were exceptionally kind at the Marriott Canyon Villas. They offered to Mapquest anywhere we wanted to visit and made some very good suggestions of activities off the resort. The front desk clerks even offered to print our boarding passes for our return back to Cleveland, Ohio. The Marriott Canyon Villa also had a scheduled sheet for all the activitites on the resort for each day.
I would recommend this resort for everyone! I hope to return soon. What a good time we all had! I don't think you could go wrong at this resort even if you are picky! :-)

title: “Excellent Stay for Good Price”
text: Booking a trip during the Chicago's taste fest was hectic! I use travelocity's site for their top secret hotels and had a 10% discount as well. I booked this hotel and was amazed by everything. The hotel was beautiful, the service was spectacular and the location was perfect. We were an 8 minute walk from the taste fest, a 5 minute walk from shopping locations and the surrounding was nice as well. Even though your right next to the subway, you can barely hear it, and it does not disturb you at all. The rooms were spacious, the beds were so comfortable and the historic appearance is just charming. I'll defiantly book this again :)

title: “good location”
text: found an excellent deal for this place via Hotwire.com good location for the sights of Denver plus the train station. Unusually building lay out but everything was clean and tidy and the breakfast was great. Would liked to have stayed on another night but could not afford their normal rates!

title: “Not What You Would Expect from Westin”
text:
This hotel is below expectations for a Westin. My husband and I stayed at this hotel for 4 nights during a business trip. The location is good for walking to San Diego's business district, and plenty of restaurants and shopping are nearby. I would recommend this hotel to business travelers, but not for vacationers. 
Below Average: Valet Service is poor for the heafty $27.00/night. The bathroom was small and the drains were clogged. Elevators were very slow. The decor was odd - very modern furniture in a very outdated room. Hallways are narrow and confustng to navigate. 
Good Points: Location. Friendly Service. Downtown View.

title: “Amazing Value in New York City”
text: We came in on the bolt bus on Saturday to stay there for a Valentines Weekend and the hotel could not have been better. Rooms are beautiful and brand new with lots of nice touches (they fold and seal the Toilet paper!) The beds were really comfortable and we actually slept in later than we thought we would. Ninna at the front desk was really welcoming and courteous. Pretty sweet views on the upper floors if you can get a room up there. Overall, if you want to stay in times square but don't want to pay the ridiculous prices like the W or Marquis, this place is the way to go.

title: “Great location”
text:
As a travel professional, I practically live in hotels, and I was very impressed with the staff at the Conrad Chicago.
From my first contract with the bellman, everyone was universally helpful and friendly without being patronizing.
Our corner suite had a great view of the John Hancock Building and if we looked farther north we could see Lake Michigan. The furnishings were a bit worn, but the bed was wonderful and the bathroom, very large and well-designed.
The staff did a great job of taking care of my family (we used Hilton Honors reward vouchers to pay for the rooms) and the next time I stay in downtown Chicago, I hope to stay at the Conrad Hilton.
(Also being connected to Nordstrom's and the shoppng mall was very convenient.)

title: “A hidden gem”
text: A really great place to stay! Close to the subway, very friendly and helpful staff, spacious rooms and a very good breakfast buffet. I travel quite a bit and am very critical of conditions - wear of furniture/linens, outdated furnishings, even amenities - I have nothing negative to say about Hotel Giraffe. I will defintely stay here again and would recommend it to other travelers.

title: “First and last time.”
text: Stayed one night at the Marriott. Upon arrival, we were told by the valet staff that the parking structure was full and that we would have to use the valet service at $21 per night. Checked in and received a smoking room, although we had requested non-smoking. Front desk person told us that since we were on a "group rate" and didn't pay full price, nothing could be done. Tried leaving the door to the room open for a while, but the smoke from the hallway was just as bad. Asked for a late checkout (at this point I didn't have much confidence, and the Marriott didn't let me down) I was told late checkout was not permitted unless we paid $40 for a 3 hour extension. I don't have high requirements when I stay at hotels. In my opinion the Marriott made no attempt to make our stay enjoyable. There are simply much better options in downtown Indianapolis for less money.

title: “A FAMILY HOMERUN AT THE HOTEL COMMONWEALTH”
text:
Our April 30th stay with our married daughters and their families was a homerun memory for our family! The adults and the children thoroughly enjoyed the wonderful accomodations and the luxurious amenities. The cookies and milk with the welcoming baseball-themed gift bags that greeted the 4 children were a thrill. The Sox may have lost the game, but the Keating grandchildren were winners! A sincere thank you to the Commonwealth staff for a wonderful, family experience. You're the best!
Looking forward to our next visit,
Susan and Tom Keating, Monroe, NJ.

title: “Dissappointed...........”
text: I have to say I expected a little more than what this particular Westin offered. We picked it because of the location of where we were spending our New Years Eve. So, the pro was the location. We also enjoyed a sandwich we picked up from a little sandwich shop in the hotel. We were told the rooms had been renovated recently. Although they looked okay, the beds were extremely hard. In fact, both our bed and the other couple who stayed next door to us, complained about how UN-heavenly the beds were, not to mention the shower and shower head, which needs some renovation. When we complained to someone at the front desk she stated, "Oh it's probably because the bed is new and needs to be broken in." Trust me that is not it at all. There was also a weird creaking sound coming form the bed frame every time I sat down on it. I would have to say the Westin Bonaventure is a "Has been.". One last thing, when we went to check out we saw some dog feces sitting on the Starwood Preferred mat, in front of the reception desk. I have stayed at other Westins and have never had a problem.

title: “Execellent Hotel”
text: Overall the Hotel was excellent. Service and the staff was top notch, and amenities were top notch!

title: “Best value and location in Manhattan”
text: I have been staying at The Marcel for the past two years every time I visit New York and decided this time around to write a review which is in fact at the age of 42 and traveling all around the world for the past 22 years the first time I ever write a review. The purpose of the such is to give justice to people who constantly strive to deliver the best value for money, service and are dedicated to their profession on one hand and on the other hand to give the best advises to my fellow frequent travelers. The Marcel offers for a very reasonable price (for New York) an exquisite location, a knowledgeable staff when needed, spotless rooms with excellent amenities and last but not least above average sized rooms in each category. I wish to equally praise "Inoteca" for offering till late in the evening a reasonable choice of food and beverage at affordable prices. Thank you Nalini (the General Manager) to have upgraded me last week which was a very generous and kind gesture of yours! I will be back soon!

title: “Great..slightly expensive!”
text:
I've camped at this hotel for over 5 months now and found this a great place to stay at along with some other downtown hotels I've reviewed earlier. Expensive, if you dont have a priceline price or a govt rate. Else, this place is super comfortable.
Well appointed rooms, the beds and linens - nice, great newly done bathrooms etc. Onsite restaurants that are open until 10pm, food that you may not find anywhere else nearby if you decided to eat a late dinner. 
Some of the previous reviewers have mentioned bedbugs here. I,ve never been putup in a room with one though so I would doubt those claims.
The downside..noisy elevators if your room happens to be close to one. In a nutshell, I'd always stay here if in the area..

title: “my favorite place to stay in San Francisco”
text: Beresford Hotel is a small hotel in a very good location. About 2 blocks to Union Square. The staff is very friendly & helpful.The rates are a bargain & the rooms are small but very clean. Some of the employees(front desk) have been there 30 + years & they remember you when you arrive. They even include a continental breakfast & free internet!!!

title: “Nice place”
text: I stay here for work, once a week. For an airport hotel, its actually pretty nice. The hotel/rooms/grounds are extremely clean and the staff friendly. I also like the new rooms and furnishings. Being close to the airport, you actually don't hear much noise. I would definatly stay here and recommend it to anyone needing an overnight accomodation near Midway.

title: “What all other hotels should strive for.”
text:
A truly accommodating experience filled with a warm, lavender frangranced hand towel upon check-in, comfortable beds, complimentary wi-fi, and excellent staff. 
The most discriminating tastes would be impressed.

title: “Dirty Dump--Stay Away”
text: I ended up here after getting stranded in Charlotte due to a missed flight connection. From the outside, the hotel looked nice and well kept, and the lobby also did. However, the room I was in was about the worst I could have imagined. Nonsmoking rooms smelled of old smoke, wallpaper was falling off, all the furniture was full of dings, bedspread had holes, sofa bed's upholstery was ripped, toilet seat was broken...and on and on it goes. In addition, the carpet was stained and the walls had dings and marks, and there were 3 settings apparently on the shower water--hot, scalding and lawsuit-pending-it-was-so-hot. I'm so sorry I didn't move to another hotel and recommend anyone to pick one of the many other choices than this tired, run down property.

title: “Thanksgiving”
text: Family relatives spent Thanksgiving weekend at the Embassy Suites and could not be more pleased. Lots of room, a suite at the price of a regular hotel room and an indoor pool. We scored. The kids had a field day.

title: “Fast and freindly for those on the go.”
text: Stayed at the hotel for business, check-in/out was quick; perfect for business. Complimentary breakfast and afternoon reception fit the schedule nicely. The rooms have plenty of space if you'd have a few people with you even though that wasn't the case for me. Proximity to interstate gets you quickly on your way.

title: “My weekend get away from everthing”
text: Had no prior reservations but front desk staff have me in a room withing 10 minutes of arrival even that check in is 3pm I was in my room by 1:40 pm. Room was very clean and bed comfortable. Even with a location facing the pool had no problems getting the rest and sleep I needed. Location is great close to freeway access, close to restaurants and entertainment. Definitely will stay here again.

title: “A quiet and sophisticated choice”
text:
I only stayed here for one night but it was the first time I ever enjoyed such a quite room in NY.
The room was really nice and spacious and the attention to every small detail was well thought out and executed.
The cherry on the cake at the Alex was the bed, I sleep in so many hotel beds throughout the year and only very rarely can I say that the bed was really comfortable. 
For NY this is definitely a hotel I will select again if I manage to find a good deal, otherwise it is out of my usual budget...

title: “What a great location for a great price”
text: The staff here is friendly, helpful and eager to please. I stay here often and always feel at home. The location is fantastic and close to many wonderful places. The price is perfect. I always recommend to my friends.

title: “Convenient location next to Metro”
text:
We arrived around 10:30 am to check in but there were no clean rooms available. Not a problem, we were able to store our luggage on the first floor with the security guards so we could begin exploring the city until our room was ready. The hotel and guestroom was spotlessly clean! We had prepaid our reservation by booking a travel package through Travelocity and there were no glithces, check-in was a breeze! The bed was a foam mattress and was VERY VERY COMFORTABLE, ensuring a good nights sleep after a long day of sight seeing. The bathroom was very clean and large with a double sink which was great for 3 girls staying in 1 room. We were given a large corner room on the 4th floor which did face the train tracks. Although other reviewers said they could hear the trains at night, I am a light sleeper and I didnt hear a peep! The security desk on the ground level was a plus as you needed the room key to gain access to the elevator and guest room floors. We felt very safe our entire stay.The security guards were not very friendly but they did do their job! 
The location of this hotel is literally right next to the New York Avenue metro stop (red line). A couple of stops away is Gallery Place metro stop which has transfers to other metro lines to get you anywhere you want to go in DC. There is a 7 eleven next to the hotel which is convenient for snacks and drinks. All in all very convenient location to see the sites DC has to offer which are easily accessible by metro and the hotel is wonderful, clean and new! I would definitely stay here on my next visit to DC!!

title: “My favorite place to stay in NY!”
text: I have visited NYC MANY times for business and pleasure for the last 15 years. Whenever I have a choice of where to stay, this is my preferred hotel for many reasons. The location right in Times Square cannot be beat for shopping, eating, seeing shows and easy access to transportation. The rooms are clean and they are LARGE, which is unusual in many of the nicer NYC hotels. The staff is always helpful and the conciege can help arrange show tickets, transport to the airports and just about anything else you need. Across the street is a convenient deli/store for any quick food and beverage needs when you arrive late at night, and next store is a cute little French restaurant with great food. If you have kids, the Toys R Us is right next store too! Prices are average for NYC, but often they offer special deals. After 15 years, it is getting a bit worn here and there, but I still think it is the best all-around location and value out of all the places I have stayed in the city.

title: “Nice Hotel, Great Location”
text: Stayed here this past weekend and had a great room with all the amenities. The breakfast was wonderful especially the biscuits and gravy served Sunday morning. The pool was the perfect temperature and our granddaughter had her first swimming lesson given by her grandmother. All of the staff were very helpful and we will stay here again.

title: “Great Location - Good for families”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights last summer, with three boys, 10,11 and 5, and took up the loews family package whereby you get a two bedroom suite which was surprisinly large for manhattan... however.... it is located on the corner of Park Avenue and is quite noisy, especially if you are sensitive to noise. The rooms have not been renovated recently and it is a little dated but the size of the suite and the kindness of the staff more than made up for this. The staff were all, especially by Manhattan standards, very gracious kind and helpful and really made my children feel welcome. The food was standard plus, the location is wonderful. Enjoy!!

title: “"Don't do it"”
text:
I booked a room here for one and when I arrived i was shocked. The hote didn't look like the picture on line. The picture must have been a new one not recent one. They didn't honor their promise with expedia.com, they want all the money up front and a deposit of $20.00 for an iron. The area was run down and scarey. I found another hotel and lesson learned. They knew the Congress Convention was in town and thought they would make some fast money. Make sure you know what you are being discounted on! comfort or safety!!!
I'll pay extra the next time!

title: “Fantastic hotel that has it all”
text:
Staff were fantastic - both friendly and helpful.
Room was great - very large with decent beds and a nice bathroom. 
Location cant be beat with only a few minutes on foot away from Hollywood Bld and all the major attractions such as the chinese and kodak theatres as well as the walk of fame.
The hotels breakfast was toast, juice, and a selection of fruit, cereal and baked goods that isnt amazing but very handy to start your day.
The hotel offers free snacks and softdrinks to its guests which was a great touch.
The hotel had internet but it was slow and expensive.

title: “Wish the money was spent in rooms rather than common areas”
text: The common areas were very nice. However, the rooms were small (our room didn't even have a full-size closet). In addition, there was mold in the shower, and the wall paper in the bathroom needed replaced. Both check-in and room service were slow.

title: “Small, good location, but watch out for the priorities!”
text: Our stay at the Jane was part of a 5 month trip through the Americas - part of a sabbatical from work. The place is a novelty for sure. The rooms have a narrow spare to operate in so you need to be tidy if there are two of you. You will bump, bounce and scratch on the fixtures and fittings. But its ok and the location is great. Collecting water from the lift (elevator) is strange but ok. The place models itself on being quirky and cool. The latter is its downfall. Every night, bar the last night of our stay, I heard the music and felt the vibrations from the ballroom - where hte whos who of NYC seem to hang out. It is very cool, but when you're in NY for 5 days and want to be out and about in the morning you should consider the impact of this on your following day. Lets just say getting to a spacious christian womens hostel in Boston was a relief ... surprising for us too! However, Sunday night the Ballroom is closed so no staying awake til 3-4am ... one night you can sleep. i must say, however, the management responded to my complaint and offered the possibility of moving to a quiet room. We had when booking requested a quiet room and being on the 3rd floor assumed it would be. All in all its fine, cool, quirky but ought to make the guests a priority rather than the club nights. One night we were told to move off the steps by two bouncers - we said we were staying at the hotel, but were told to move! Priorities in place and this place is very good for location, price etc in NYC but be tidy!

title: “Great location for price!”
text: I made reservations at this hotel for a work conference. The conference was at the Marriott which is less than 2 blocks away, but almost $100 more per night. It included free breakfast and free wi-fi in the lobby which none of the other hotels in the area included. It isn't anything fancy, but it was spotless! I couldn't find anything wrong with this hotel and the price was great. Obviously the breakfast wasn't gourmet, but it served it's purpose for my husband. I would definitely stay here again. There is a cable car stop about 2 blocks away and the buses and street cars are also nearby. There are several good restaurants just down the street and you will also find Starbucks (next to the cable car stop, but you can't take your coffee on the cable car!), Trader Joe's and a Safeway. If you want something clean and conveniently located in Fisherman's Wharf, then this will serve you just fine.

title: “Loved it!”
text: I have stayed in a few NYC hotels and this one was by far the best ever. I stayed in a queen size new room, loved the hardwood floors! I didn't have to worry about whose been on the carpet! Bathroom was beautiful and spotless! Only problem was it took awhile to get warm water but it's an old building. Bed was defiantly comfortable and amazing! Brand new tv with great channels! Close to subway also!

title: “Fine Small Hotel Adjacent Times Square”
text: I was torn whether to give it 4 or 5 stars. Hotel selection in NYC is much a matter of preferred neighborhood. This was a father-daughter tourist stay in the 'Apple' (2 queen beds/4 nights + the Belmont Stakes). If you want a fine small 'boutique' hotel steps from Times Sq. in the heart of the theater district, this is great! The decor is Arabesque Art Deco adopting the Bogart movie as a theme. Those that want a huge 'Oh Wow!' hotel may be disappointed. The staff however seems to know that gracious attentiveness will make the difference - and it does. Property condition and room upkeep was very superior. Room service connected to the adjacent restaurant was punctual and very satisfactory. A very minor critique was the moderately high decible window a/c. Pricing is upper mid-range for the city (upper $300's); inclusion of breakfast and afternoon/evening wine and snacks is convenient though plus a daily value of >$50 per couple. I'd happily stay there again.

title: “They made the unpleasant pleasant”
text: Thanks to Houston security being an absolute nightmare when my partner and I returned to the US from Guatemala, we missed our connecting flight. We were already tired, cranky and now frustrated with the lack of consideration shown to us at the airport. Nobody cared about the inconvenience and that didn't feel good. So the idea of spending a bunch of money at an over-priced hotel was definitely not what we wanted to do. However, the man at the ticket counter as we rebooked the flight gave us a voucher to call so we could get better rates on our accommodation. We tried the Red Roof Inn first and although I was a wee bit grouchy, (probably alot grouchy) the receptionist was more than pleasant. Soon we were being whisked away in a complimentary shuttle to the motel. We ended up with a lovely room, 2 double beds, very nice bathroom, convenient location to get something to eat and all for $55 plus tax. We were shocked at how nice it was for the price, considering the city and the location. We had expected to pay twice as much for a lot less. Everything about the place was top-notch. Staff was fabulous and we had another free shuttle back to the airport in the morning. The whole thing was inconvenient and unpleasant but the Red Roof Inn made it good and we really appreciated that.

title: “really awful service”
text: For the price you pay you think that you can leave your luggage for few hours. We party of 40 people checked out at 7 am wanted to leave luggage for 3 hours. they told us they can't do it. REally sucky service for $420 per room.

title: “Bad from start to finish”
text:
Pulled in a bit road weary with our 2 kids and we were first hit with a $10 charge for them! What?! I've never been charged for kids before. Then after laying down for much-needed sleep the smoke alarm started beeping around 2am. As if that weren't enough the sheets were so stiff and uncomfortable that they crinkled every time anyone moved an inch. We got a couple hours sleep all night. To top it off, breakfast was just gross with eggs that tasted like they were from a powder mix! We paid extra and went out of the way to stay here...BIG mistake!
NOT CUSTOMER FRIENDLY

title: “Great Value for the price”
text: My first stay-over in Charlotte returning from the Cayman Islands. Very close & convenient to the airport, the rooms were clean and very modern with all amenities even the most picky person could think of. Service was friendly and helpful. Overall, you can't beat this property for the price!

title: “Excellent hotel, great location!!”
text:
We spent the weekend at the Trump Soho for a special occasion. The hotel was beautiful and the service was superior to many other hotels that we have visited. We frequent NYC as our vacation spot at least 5 times per year. This trip exceeded our expectations in every area.
Even before we arrived the staff was more than accomodating and was always there for us!! 
We are going to be visiting the Trump Soho whenever we go to NYC!!!

title: “Very nice. Hard to complain.”
text:
Great little hotel in a newly developed strip near OSU. We had an okay view of Columbus (not exactly NYC, but whatever) and could see trains pass by in the distance and a few CMH planes fly overhead.
The rooms are new, quite large, and well-conceived. There’s a living room study combo area (large desk) slightly separated from the main bedroom, decent sized dressing area, and respectable bathroom. Good lighting throughout. Bedding was new, and super plush Sealy Posturepedic pillowtop mattresses were very comfortable (although I wish they had foam instead of feather pillows). Free wireless is strong and secure. Parking, local calls, and fresh fruit are also free. Large LG flat screen TV. No bed bugs (we always check, especially around Columbus). Rooms are nicely equipped with bumpy “massage” soap, face soap, shampoo, conditioner, and even Aqua Fresh toothpaste. Pleasant service downstairs. The women on duty (especially Melissa) were responsive and genuine. 
Breakfast was different than usual but still very good: Starbucks coffee, choice of juices, the usual sugary pastries, oatmeal with all the fixings, some cut fruit, and three types of homemade breakfast sandwiches. 
Respectable pool could be a tad warmer (no jacuzzi). Still, it's well-maintained and certainly better than nothing.
