Even the color coordination was remarkable. I liked the Hyatt orange in the rooms, on the walls, and even on the attire worn by staff. There’s a certain amount of class here that you just don’t find elsewhere. 
Suggestion to management: get rid of uncovered glasses in the hotel room. Studies have shown that housekeeping does a poor job with hygiene. Nobody knows if our cups are fresh out of the dishwasher, “cleaned” with the same towel that was used to wipe toilets, or, in our case, masking residue of a previous tenant’s drink. 
All in all though, hard to complain about much here. Good job, Hyatt Place!

title: “Always great!”
text: This was our second visit to the Taj Boston. This hotel has an amazing location, the rooms are comfortable, filled with the details of a 5 star hotel. We enjoyed breakfast in the hotel restaurant every morning, and though a little slow, the food was very good. We especially enjoyed the hotel bar which is elegant and has excellent service.

title: “No other way to end a perfectly planned engagement. She said YES!”
text: Well being that I don't normally take the time to rate hotel experiences this is a first. I took my girlfriend to Houston for a special trip. Long story short I asked her to marry me there. We returned to Austin and stayed a night at Lakeway Resort and Spa. The resort is in absolutely gorgeuos location. You probably would never notice it was there unless you looked for it. It is settled on what I think looks like a penninsula facing the waters of Lake Travis. They cater mainly to conference style busines, but I felt more than at home as a leisure guest. The hotel was very clean and open. I didn't feel like I was walking into a small motel. Guest services was very friendly and open to help me with whatever I needed. The room was really big. I didn't expect so much room at such a competitive price. My room came with a balcony facing the lake which I would definitely recommend. As per request there was a bottle of iced champagne and chocolate covered strawberries waiting for me and my bride to be. I have stayed at many 5 star hotels including the Emily Morgan in San Antonio, the Hilton Anatole in Dallas, and the Hilton of Americas in Housotn. Lakeway Resort and Spa rivaled them all with its small town hospitality and big city charm. I was so impressed with the location that I am now planning on doing my wedding in their all glass Vistas building.

title: “A great hostel in new york”
text:
First of all if you´re looking for a clean,well located and secure hostel in New york.. You´re in the right page.
the most important feature here is the LOCATION! i´ts situated in times square 41st and the subway is just about 5 steps from there.right down the street.
yes is a hostel, so you share the room with other people but.. its safe also there are safeboxes so you can put your valuable belongings. now if you´re not okay with the sharing room thing they also have private rooms wich are still quite cheap having in consideration its located in times square and Im almost sure there is no way you can find this fares so close to that area for a private room. breakfast is included ( several types of cereal,yoghurt,fruit,bread,orange juice,coffee).and the staff was corteous and friendly, I´ve never stayed in a hostel before and I shall say it was a good experience.
if you wanna go to New york with a low budget and considering staying in a hostel, dont think about it anymore this is the one.

title: “Best Location, Fabulous Hotel, Amazing Restaurant, Hot Bar!!”
text: For our first time trip to NCY we couldn't have chosen better. Great location, very helpfull staff with the bonus of an amazing restaurant on the premises. The cellar bar was a great place to start the evening and a nice spot to end the day too. The rooms are spacious and the views spectacular. I do like to stay in different locations when visiting cities but on this occasion my next trip will see me heading straight back!! We were also lucky in the fact that we opted to get a ride to the Airport with the hotel driver, yes more expensive than a yellow cab but well worth it. The driver, gave us a detour (to avoid rush hour) showing us places we would not normally have seen...Fantastic!!If you can afford this Hotel GO!! if you can't then visit the restaurant (Koi) and cellar bar...Well worth it!!

title: “Fabulous service!”
text: I stayed at the Courtyard Century City for business. I have to admit I was a little bummed when I arrived that the lobby was under construction. And..it is an older property with small but updated rooms. But..the staff more than made up for it! The valets were particularly helpful with a greeting and smile and excellent directions and help. The lobby will be done soon and I look forward to staying at this hotel again!

title: “Just opened with a complete renovation...”
text:
Just reopened, I think it was under a different name, happy they changed to Westin. The room was the new Westin look, comfortable and classy and the views are great. 
The restaurant wasn't open yet and their meeting space is nice with natural lighting.

title: “Upgraded and on Hotwire”
text: Stayed 2 nights; good value and location especially if through a discounter. Rooms are small but seem quite new and spotless. Waiting for elevators was a pain. Beds were comfy but the lumpy cotton filled comforter was a bit odd. I'd stay there again for a similar bargain rate.

title: “bed provided back ache/uncomfortable bed/old beat up furniture or chair/not comfortable”
text:
With a name like Hilton, one expects a comfortable bed at least. We have stayed in many hotels, many years..not just in the U.S.A.,but in Europe. 
 This was the most uncomfortable, soft squishy mattress we have ever experienced. I am an average sized person,and my husband has some lower back problems.
 Had we known the bed would have been this uncomforable, we would have left sooner,but we had an event to attend at a nearby restaurant...the restaurant fare made up for the poor sleep we both experienced. We stayed only one night,and paid over 130 dollars for this discomfort.
 The following day we checked out as early as possible. We did tell the management about the poor quality of sleep...however, their attitude was one of " too bad...we've got your money now".
 I'm not sure if our credit card company could so something about this,but it was the worst back ache I have had in my life.
 This hotel used to be another hotel...and I think the Hilton bought it out , not sure when. It is within walking distance of Masraff's restaurant. 
 I highly recommend Masraff's ! It almost made up for the terrible hotel bed !

title: “Location”
text: Location, location, location.... The Marriot Marquett located on Broadway and 45th Avenue, overlooking Time Square was just perfect for an inexperienced "New Yorker". We were thrilled with the central location and that the hotel welcomed us to an early check-in upon arrival. Our room was on the 20th floor, I believe the hotel has 48. The room was spacious with lovely decor...blues and yellows. The view of Time Square was spectacular. The service was top rated. The elevator system was tricky. It was located centrally in the hotel. Key pads allowed you to enter the floor number and then directed you to the correct elevator. It was amusing to watch people enter their floor number and then scramble to find the correct elevator. Of note, the elevator system was not always efficient. I took the stairs,down 20 flights, on more than one occasion. We dined at the View Restaurant. The Prix Fixe, "New American Cuisine" ran $64.95. The service was poor and the food was just fair .The view, however, was spectacular. The restaurant rotates 360 degrees, allowing for panoramic viewing of Time Square. The highlight of the trip was that 1/2 price ticket sales for Broadway shows had relocated to the 46th St. entrance of the hotel. We were able to purchase same day tickets for 50% off. It was very convenient . We saw two shows, "The Color Purple" and "The Odd Couple", both for 50% off.. and the seats were very good! The fitness Center, located on the 23rd floor was very nice. It had a number of treadmills, eliptical trainers, exercise bikes, steppers, free weights and assisted weight machines. Water, towels and head sets were available. The fitness center was open 24 hours/day. Downside was that there was no pool, sauna, whirlpools or steam baths. The hotel does not have a spa. If a massage is desired, it must be arranged and done in the privacy of your hotel room.

title: “Just OK”
text:
I have stayed at the Omni a few times for Business. The lay out of the room is not very comfortable.
The big Flat Screen TV is across from this small uncomfortable sofa and in the bedroom is this old school small TV. 
Lots of small spaces and doors but it doesnt flow well. On this trip they were replacing all the in room safes and started working on this at 6:30am and they were very loud. Check in was fast and my bags were brought up quickly

title: “Great Hotel....Great Location....Great Value....”
text: I stayed at the Ameritania Hotel for 1 night on 9/28/12. It was a trip for business/pleasure. I have traveled to NYC many times and I just discovered the Ameritania Hotel. I would highly recommend it and I plan on returning there on future trips. The location was perfect for me. Just north of the busy Times Square area but a short walk there and to the theatre, shopping and many restaurants. The hotel is very nice inside and although my room was small....it was stylish and beautifully decorated. The bathroom was gorgeous. Very clean room. The staff was super friendly.....especially the Concierge Renaldo Moore. He was most accomodating in allowing me an early check-in @ 1:30pm so I could freshen up before my appointment at 3:30. The bellmen were also friendly and held my luggage before check-in on Friday....and after check-out on Saturday so I could do some shopping before leaving at 5pm. Now that I have discovered the Ameritania Hotel....I am looking forward to returning there on my next trip to NYC.

title: “I appreciate your awesome staff!”
text: It has been a month since I had an unexpected visit to Houston due to a medical emergency with a family member who was flown there for heart surgery.  As it turned out it was necessary for me to stay for two weeks, and I chose to stay at the Doubletree in downtown Houston, due to it's proximity to The Methodist Hospital as well as affordability. Let me just say how impressed I was with my stay here!  It was southern hospitality at it's finest! Not only was the staff extremely professional and pleasant (especially my morning breakfast waitress!!), they made being away from home at a very stressful time a whole lot easier.  The room was very comfortable, clean and quiet, and of course the chocolate chip cookies an added bonus. Doubletree Downtown Houston, you have earned my loyalty.  Thank you!!!

title: “Ok for a 3 Star Hotel - This is NOT a 4 Star property by any means.”
text: I made a mistake and used Priceline to book a 4 Star hotel in Wasington DC and I ended up with the St. Gregory Hotel. In no way, under anyone's check list is this adaquate property a 4 Star hotel. It is an "OK" 3 Star property that was overpriced and forgettable in a city of memorable hotels. The staff was friendly, the place wasn't dirty, but it is a glorified mother with AC in the window that blows on your face during the night. There is an awkward Marily Monroe satue in the lobby that looks out of place. The location is good for Georgetown and Dupont Circle, but not very close to a metro stop. I felt betrayed and ripped off, but that was my fault for booking it through priceline.

title: “Well worth the stay”
text: If you need a hotel room when traveling through LAX, I highly recommend the Radisson. The staff is friendly and helpful. The cost for your stay is a bargin as compared to the other hotels and you do not have to give up ant amenities. The rooms are big and clean. Stop in at the Palmira lounge and ask for Trino! He will be your gracious host.

title: “Not worth the $$$$”
text:
For a five star hotel there are many little things that just don't meet 5 star standards. The location is great and the staff is polite but something is just missing here. The rooms are chilly and the temperature is impossible to control. Both thermostats are located right next to the windows (genius) so the heat is always running but it doesn't seem to get warmer. 
Turn down service was very late in the evening, well after we had already turned in. The on site restaraunts are nice buy very pricey, be prepared.
The hotel is pet friendly so if you are allergic be aware, pets have been in your room.
Our tub didn't hold water and the wallpaper was peeling a bit. Some of the carpet looked worn and was coming up. 
We did receive a complimentary newspaper in the morning and the checkout is not until 2pm which is nice. The bath products are aromotherapy which was also a nice touch. The very tiny chocolates left with turndown service were very good as well. The towels were not soft at all nor were the robes. 
The bed was large and very comfortable. 
So I would say nowhere near worth what they charge but if you got a great deal or want to splurge it's ok....but just ok.

title: “Quiet and convenient”
text: This was a one day business meeting. I took the train into DC and was easily able to walk from the station to the hotel. Check in was efficient and I found the room clean, modern, and well appointed. You have to pay for internet use but there are computers for airline check in in the lobby. The rooms are secure with door latch and peephole. There are about 40 channels on the flatscreen TV but many are second rate filler. No international channels were noted. There was no traffic or room noise in my 6th floor room. You must go down an escalator to get to the lobby and access the elevators for the room. The hotel is very close to the Capitol building and the Mall and not far from the Metro. The Newseum and National Gallery are about 4 blocks away. Other Mall museums are a somewhat longer walk. We had breakfast and lunch served for our meeting and I though both meals were very well prepared, attractive and fresh with interesting bends of flavors considering they was served to a group. I did not use the fitness center but many folks run the loop around the Mall to the Washington Monument and this is a good launch point. I got a good deal for DC with a $180 senior discount.

title: “Nice location”
text: Great room and nice location. If you are looking for something a little different. Try this hotel.

title: “Great value for your money”
text:
A great business hotel with a European feel. The only complaints I have is that they charged $35 dollars for a late check-out (45 min late) and when I called to change a reservation it was just after 12 and I was charged an extra nights fee. But I can also understand these charges as I'm sure it keeps their costs down.
The rooms are nice with personal touches such as books that you can read. On every floor there is a filtered water dispenser with empty plastic bottles for free. The bathrooms doesn't have a bath tub, only a shower which I prefer so I was very happy for that. Maybe in the suites there are bath tubs.
I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Awesome hotel in a great location!”
text:
I really enjoyed our stay at Hotel Indigo. When we arrived and during our stay, we were not disappointed once. The lobby is very stylish and inviting, and the service was excellent. We were always greeted with friendly smiles by any of the staff members. Our room was wonderful! I love the wood floors, and everything was immaculate. I didn't see spots on the sheets or on the walls. Being so clean, I felt at home and comfortable immediately. There's free wifi in the room, so that was very helpful as I worked from the hotel.
The hotel is located walking distance to many shops and restaurants. In fact, if you're in town during baseball season, you are 2 blocks from the stadium. 
There is a full service restaurant downstairs which we never ate at but we did visit a cafe about 3 blocks away called Cafe Chloe. What a gem! Definitely go there for lunch or breakfast. The food was great! They do server dinner as well but we didn't have dinner there.
If you're looking for a massage or facial, Urban Calm, which is across from Cafe Chloe provides wonderful spa services. 
Enjoy your stay in San Diego!

title: “Great hotel in downtown Seattle”
text:
I was looking for a reasonably priced hotel in downtown Seattle with good reviews on Trip Advisor for the start of our trip to the Pacific Northwest, and decided on the Hotel Vintage Park. We paid $112 + taxes per night for a King Premier Room for a 3 night stay in mid May, which I booked through the hotel's website.
The hotel is in a great location in downtown Seattle, close to all public transportation. We decided not to get a rental car and took the light rail from the airport to University station, which is about 2 blocks from the hotel (although you have a steep uphill climb between 3rd and 4th). The light rail was bargain at only $5/person for the round trip. Compare to paying $30/night for valet parking at the hotel. Seattle has a great public transportation system for tourists and we rode the free buses in the downtown area or walked to all of the sights. 
The hotel room was really big, and included a sitting area with a couch, chair and desk. Free wifi in the room (only if you sign up to be a Kimpton rewards member). The bed was really comfortable with great pillows and duvet. The room was clean...the only sign of wear was some mould along the grout lines in the shower, and a slightly dinged up coffee table in the sitting area. There is no free breakfast, but plenty of coffee shops in the area of the hotel. The hotel also offers a free wine tasting in the lobby every night from 5-6 pm which was a really nice touch.
I would definitely recommend this hotel as a comfortable place to stay in downtown Seattle. The room rate was outstanding, and bumped my overall recommendation from very good to excellent.

title: “Best hotel in NYC”
text: I stayed at the Eventi right before Christmas. The service was by far the best I have ever received in a hotel! The extremely friendly, helpful staff, specifically Victoria, who helped check us in, and got us set up with everything we needed for a great trip to NYC. The complimentary wine happy house was a great perk. We had a view of the Empire State Building from our room and the location of the hotel was within walking distance to all the Christmas destinations. It is a pet friendly hotel and they even brought a bed for my kitten. It was truly great experience!

title: “A celebrity in my own mind”
text:
First I would like to thank TripAdvisor and all of the reviewers for leading me to this glorious hotel. My daughter and I stayed for two nights. Our trip was booked through the hotel directly at the low price of $225/night prepaid. They obviously knew we had paid a discount rate and that did not appear to have any influence upon how we were treated. They gave me the feeling that I was a celebrity. We arrived extremely early (before noon) and were taken immediately to our room. The double queen room had more square footage than our recently sold Printer's row apartment. Clean, calming, extremely comfortable in every sense. Fabulous bathrobes, thick luxurious towels (and plenty of them). Bathroom was outstanding with the double sinks, massive shower and huge soaking tub. The bar area was incredible with the refrigerator drawers completely stocked. My first regret is my daughter is underage and therefore, we had to pass on partaking of the myriad of tasty beverages provided. Next time.....
The service was excellent. Our luggage was brought to our room by this tiny darling young woman. She heaved those 75 pound suitcases onto the suitcase racks without batting an eyelash. I am sure they weighed more than she did. I was politely informed that there is a no-tipping policy at the hotel. I must say, that did surprise me. We were greeted by name every time we went in or out. I contacted the concierge both nights to get a recommendation and reservation for dinner. We enjoyed fine meals at Pelago and Rosebud Steakhouse. I would not have chosen either of these places on my own. A pink envelope containing our reservation details was slipped under our door both nights. The room was technologically stunning: lighting panels, HD TV/DVR, TV in the bathroom behind the mirror, and WiFi that worked great. 
Departure was a breeze. We were running late returning to the hotel to check out, so I telephoned them to gather our belongings. When we got back to the hotel we were given ice cold water (temp that day in the Windy City was 102 degrees), and informed that our bags were loaded and a cab was waiting. Wow. My second regret is leaving this hotel and moving to Hyde Park. This was a college tour for us. Huge mistake. We should have stayed right there at the Elysian where we could have continued to be pampered and treated like a Royal and sleep like a rock. It was by far the best hotel experience we have ever had.

title: “Better than I thought and heard! 1901”
text: Room 1901 was pretty small for 4 adults and 2 children. There were double beds, tv with on a few channels, a small closet, very little walking space, small shower with great water pressure, no bath tub, sink faucet water pressure sucks. Plenty big towels but no wash rags, and no laundry room in the hotel. But it was not a bad stay for the location is in Times Square.

title: “The London NYC, a really good spot”
text: I was recently at The London NYC with my wife for a week. Everything went well, as expected. Great location, big rooms, excellent service, sober decor, fair pricing for what you are getting. We love the Four Seasons, but I can honestly say that The London is a perfect alternative for those looking for a better deal to their wallets. It is a good choice. Go ahead and book your stay.

title: “Love this hotel!”
text: Stayed in this hotel for 2 nights and loved it. The rooms are quite small but most are in NYC. Small but well designed, amazing views over the Hudson and a brilliant location. The Standard Grill was great - delicious menu. The hotel were very friendly and helpful - something you don't always find in NYC's trendier hotels.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: I stayed for one night. I was upgraded to a very nice suite. The hotel has a free happy hour from 4-6 pm (unusual for Hilton) The location is great, nice outdoor firepiits/pool. Staff was all great. I was very impressed, especially for the price. Check my other reviews, I rarely give a 5.

title: “Hotel good, service was bad”
text: Front desk staff at check in refused to add my Wyndham rewards information. I have travelled for over a decade and have never had this happen. I was told that because my company travel department paid for the reservation, I was not eligble. If that is the case with Wyndham properties, I will have to not choose hotels in this family in the future.

title: “"Keep Looking"”
text:
Lets just say this hotel needs some work.. FOUR MAIN Problems this hotel had.. Went to stay there in advance of a broadway show with girlfriend.. I am 25 and we have been to NYC before.. 
The only thing this hotel has going for is its location. 
1)Rooms had paint peeling off ceiling
2)IF YOU DON"T LOCK YOUR DOOR HOUSEKEEPING BARGES IN
 (I had just gotten out of the shower and she was just standing in my doorway.. no knock or attempt to see if anyone was there) THIS HAPPENED TWICE
3) ROOMS WERE OVERLY HOT (We were told rooms have no control over heat/cooling) not a comfy nights sleep
4) Hot water was so so.. don't expect a really hot shower with nice pressure in the morning,, i've had better luck at my kitchen sink
Overall not the best stay,, i was REALLY steamed after the second barging in of the housekeeper.. the only thing i can say in a positive not was the General Manager comp'd us a nights stay for our troubles.
Like i said.. KEEP LOOKING

title: “If room size matters less than location, this is a gem”
text: Just behind Rockefeller Center, this tiny hotel has an impeccable location. Within walking distance of all major places you are likely to go to (and there is always the metro which is also within walking distance), New York becomes a lot easier to move around. Small but well kept, it was always a pleasure to come back to it after a long day's walk or a show on Broadway. When you are so tired, the last thing you want is to have to travel a long distance to get to your hotel and if all you do in the room is rest for the night, you don't really need a big room. They could upgrade their lifts though. Waiting for the lifts was always a chore.

title: “DON'T STAY HERE”
text: This hotel was such a disappointment . My closet is bigger than the room. Took forever to get hot water for a shower and there was no way to regulate the heat. We faced 79th street and it was so noisy. Couldn't tell whether it was the noise of the heat coming up, the noise of traffic or the noise of the other guests going in and out of the communal bathrooms all night. I did not get a wink of sleep all night. Sorry i picked this hotel.

title: “Small rooms and noise from corridor”
text: I know this is Manhattan, but, given the price, the room was tiny. We were woken up almost every night by doors slamming in the corridor. (The doors close very loudly and I'm sure something could be done about this). We were also annoyed by our maid, who kept fishing for tips (which we were not inclined to give given the standard of cleaning and service). The hotel is on a particularly dodgy part of Canal Street and walking near the hotel did not feel safe. We would not stay here again. I am sure you can do better for the money.

title: “Great Place, Area And Staff!”
text: I have just returned from New York and loved Club Quarters Midtown. It has the perfect location to everything like Times Square and 5th Ave. The staff was very helpful and polite. Our check in and check out was quick and handle very professionally. They even hold your bags at check out so you can do things if your flight is later in the day! Cafe Manhattan across the street is a great and affordable place for breakfast. We went there every morning! The room was a nice size and so was the bathroom. We were only in the room [pretty much to sleep and just get dressed so size wasn't that important! I will go to this hotel again for my future visits and I hope you will too! It was worth it!

title: “Best place in Austin for runners to stay”
text: Perfect location, beautiful facility, the helpfulness of the concierge really puts this one over the top. Perfect for active couple and families who want to have access to jogging trails, kayaks and be able to walk to nearby restaurants.

title: “Good to explore Frisco”
text:
This was a hotel that I had to pay out of my own pocket and it was dirt cheap. I did not expect anything but was pleasantly surprised really.
Good location everything walking distance, OK folks at the counter and next door iss a great diner called Mel's. I sat there most of the time, 
Do not expect anything special such as the Westin St Francis (which is very nice indeed - but pricey)!

title: “Nice hotel, great location”
text:
We had a room on the 11th floor, so we had no problems with noise from the hotel. The room was smallish but very comfortable and attractive, with nice amenities. Everything was clean and functional.
Free coffee in the lobby all day, pleasant reception staff.
Short walk to Chinatown, South Station, Copley Square.
Boston is noisy at night, I used earplugs and had a goodnight's sleep.

title: “Beautiful rooms, helpful staff, pleasant surroundings”
text:
The room was beautiful and clean, also fairly quiet (even near the elevator). We had the option to let the fan run on the ac/heating unit and it provided a good white noise background.
The bed wasn't as soft as I like but adequate. The only peculiar thing in the room was that it was booked for three people but there was only one serving of regular coffee and decaf in the room. We were able to secure more from the staff the next day.
The breakfast buffet might seem a little high ($17) but it has a wide variety of offerings including an omelette station. Food was good with standard breakfast fare from eggs, meat and potatoes to cereal, yogurt, fresh fruit and pastries. The coffee was bold and they have great fruit smoothies! A small sampling of the daily smoothie flavor along with orange juice and coffee were included in the buffet.
The facility is top notch. I attended a function while there and the ballroom was more than adequate. Water stations with iced water and glasses were provided in several places in the lobby to accommodate the 900 plus attendees.
Another plus is that there is shopping literally 5 minutes away. Directly across the street is Home Depot, WalMart and Sam's Club, several restaurant choices including IHOP and Panera Bread (a personal favorite!). Additionally, there is a Ross, Famous Footwear, Party City and more.
Head north on Quebec just past I-70 a couple of miles and there is a beautiful shopping area called Northfield with lots of restaurants, a theater and great shopping including Charming Charlie, a fun jewelry and accessory store!

title: “Fun Weekend!”
text: I took a weekend with my wife in NYC and we stayed here. Cool hotel, location, lounge, bar, etc... Rooms are small but nice (it's New York - all rooms are small). Love the location in Tribeca. Two subway stops near by. Able to walk to Soho, Greenwich Village and our new favorite Nolita which has lots of trendy shopping, restaurants and bars. The front desk was very friendly. There was a door man who always opened the door and greeted us with a friendly hello. The concierge was very helpful and gave us good shopping and restaurant recommendations. The Church Lounge is a great place to congregate and have a drink. It has a fun energy to it. Cool place... I highly recommend it!!!

title: “A wonderful choice for a little bit of TLC”
text: We stayed here for two nights in January, and everything about the hotel and staff was great. The room was very comfortable, and the "rent-a-guppy" program is a nice touch! The location makes walking in The Loop and up to the Magnificent Mile very easy (even in the 'Arctic Blast'), and we will definitely check out the rates for a return trip to Chicago.

title: “Location, value, service: 10/10”
text: As a former DC resident, I have to say that this is the place people should stay. Fantastic location, excellent and spatious rooms, decent breakfast included -- it has everything you need for a business or vacation stay in DC.

title: “A very good hotel for the price”
text:
I stayed at this hotel in August 2007 for nearly a week, and I must admit, it's well above the average of what you will get for this price in San José. 
The good things:
1) Location is great, you have the HP pavillon not far, the convention center at the Faimont is only 20 mins walk, and the train|metro station is 5 mins walk
2) Rooms are big and clean and have air-conditioning
3) Price is excellent, I even had a jacuzzi for 100$ a nigth
3) You get breakfast for free + some food in the evening.
4) Staff are very friendly.
5) It has a microwave + coffe macine in the room, and the grocerry store is right next door.
The bad point:
1) It looks a bit old at some places, so it could do with some maintenance.
2) the food in the evening is really basic, and hardly changes so really not worht it.
But overall, a really good hotel.

title: “Riverfront accomodations that were good!”
text:
My wife and I stayed here the last weekend in March for her birthday and it was very good! The hotel staff was friendly. We got a riverview king size room that was spacious and clean. We did not try Keating's restaurant, but the prices were expensive. The location is close to Old City and the South St. area, but it's away from Center City and Rittenhouse Square where a lot of the historical stuff is located.
We had dinner at Ristorante Panorama at the PennsView Inn at Old City. Our food was awesome and it's got to be the best Italian cuisine in town. You have to try a flight of wines which other restaurants should start doing.
Overall, our stay was good. Mainly, if you want to get away from the crowds in the center of town, this is the place to stay.

title: “Perfect stay, very central”
text: Excellent location, good service, nice rooms, good food. I was surprised how close it was to walk to all major sights around Washington, the conference facilities at the hotel were good too. Would recommend if coming to Washington in business, tourism or as a couple.

title: “December 2012”
text:
Nothing special at all.. We stayed on floor 6 (interior) which was very noisy due to the air conditioning shafts and the nightclub next door - 3:30am !!!!
Not much storage space at all. Avoid the minibar at all costs - total rip off.
Concierge was very helpful.
Good location - but no more than average - OK for a night or 2, no longer.

title: “Staff and location”
text: Three friends celebrating a big birthday - 3 days stay - loved the welcome, the staff could not have been more helpful. Nothing was too much trouble. Food and drink great, bedrooms clean and well maintained but this hotels greatest asset was its staff. From front of house to restaurant and bar all we got were smiling faces and friendly banter. Shopping within walking distance - would stay there again in a heartbeat.

title: “a disapointment”
text:
my granddaughter and i were to stay 3 nites.only stayed one.room was dirty,dirty sheets,air vent was clogged up,mold around tub,plug in tub was out,lite bulbs needed replacing.carpet was a mess.for 119.00 plus taxes this place was the pits! we moved uptown after one nite. breakfast was so so ,not a clean area.this was a disgrace to elvises name.place should of been in tip top shape.wouldnt recomend staying there at all. area around hotel is run down.graceland was trhe only wonderful experience we had.stay uptown and take the drive out there to visit graceland.
thanks norma
seymour tn

title: “Perfect!”
text: Halfway through my weeklong stay at the Monaco, and I'm so impressed I am compelled to write a review. As a business traveler the free coffee and tea service in the morning, and free wine hour in the evening, are great ways to start and end the day. The staff is friendly, welcoming, and efficient. I had chocolates in my room when I arrived, which was a nice touch. The property is clean and well-appointed - but the thing that really impressed me is that the housekeeper left a quart-size baggie on the counter for me today for taking the toiletries on the plane - without my even having to ask. It's the little things. The hotel is about four blocks from Union Square shopping - parts of the surrounding neighborhood can feel a little sketchy, but that just reinforced the feeling of the Monaco as a welcome oasis! Love it. Will certainly return if my travels take me back to San Francisco.

title: “Comfortable and convenient for the price”
text:
My friend and I stayed here for five nights in March. It is definitely a boutique style hotel, the wallpaper in the room was definitely bright and it was quirky. We had a twin room which consisted of a double and single bed. My bed was comfortable but very squeaky, but the place was exceptionally clean. 
I was initally concerned about the shared bathroom situation, as all patrons on each floor have two bathrooms to share. The bathrooms were cleaned regularly and I did not encounter anything unpleasant at all - it is just important that you remember your swipe card as you would not want to lock youself out of your room wearing just a towel! The same went for the toilets, they were exceptionally clean. 
Our room had a TV, two large windows which opened up to air the room, an airconditioner which we did not use, a dressing table with large mirror as well as hairdryer, and small wash sink with mirror. Overall we could walk from the hotel to the subway in 3 minutes and could walk to Times Square in 30 mins. We walked the entire time and only used the Subway once and we saw everything we wanted to during that time, from Brooklyn to Greenwich Village etc. There are two great diners very near the hotel which serve amazing pancakes - an authentic American diner experience and a great way to fuel your walking each day. There are also some cute little bars very nearby as well. Oh just one point - I think other reviewers have mentioned this - internet access looked to me quite bad in the rooms based on seeing some people sitting in the stairwell with laptops so perhaps this is not great if you want to take your laptop along!
All staff on reception were very helpful and even called the shuttle company to book my bus for me for my very early flight out of the US - this was only $15-20 and saved me lots of money on a taxi.

title: “Love the view and the service”
text: We spent 1 week at the Bayfront Hilton and had a great time. The Service was wonderful and the spa was a treat. We had two small dogs and they were very accommodating. The walk along the marina and seaport village was a great way to start the day. We found ourselves exercising a lot because of the location. So close to everything we needed for entertainment and food choices. Love this Hilton

title: “Good Value, but beware of the shuttle times.”
text: Nice, clean place with very friendly service. Would stay here again, but be aware that the shuttle is VERY VERY slow. Waited an hour to be picked up, and at least half an hour to be dropped off, so add that to your travel time.

title: “Good value”
text: Rooms were decent. I had a king size room that had a microwave, fridge, and separate seating area. Free airport shuttle and free wifi are the two main amenities I wanted and this hotel has both. Tried the free continental breakfast one morning...not bad, but not great. Overall good value considering amenities provided and proximity to airport.

title: “Marriott Marquis Times Square New York”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights in June of 2006. The location of this hotel is perfect. However, overall, I was very disappointed with this hotel. The rooms were very tiny. Our first room was so tiny that we asked for another one. The second room was just slightly larger. 
The huge bank of elevators can be confusing. I suppose for the average hotel guest, they would be quite efficient, however, our case was different. We were originally on the concierge floor, but when we switched rooms, we weren't on that floor. Certain elevators only go to certain floors, so we could not directly get to the concierge floor without taking the elevator all the way to the lobby and then back up, which was quite annoying when you just want your breakfast or a quick snack.
The concierge lounge was also disappointing to us. It was not as large and there was not as big of a selection of food at breakfast as what we have had at other Marriott concierge lounges. Although it was still nice to have access to the free snacks and breakfast.
The workout/fitness center was very cool. It over looks Times Square, so you can watch the action while you work out.
Like I said before the best part about this hotel is the fabulous location. The half off ticket booth for Broadway shows is literally at the base of the hotel on the street level and the theaters are also within a 5-15 minute walk. The nearest subway stop is less than a 5 minute walk away. There are tons of choices for restaurants and entertainment since you are in the middle of Times Square. 
If you are a taxi person, there is a huge line of people waiting for taxis at the hotel starting around 5pm. It would be faster to walk or take the subway if you have to travel at rush hour.

title: “Great Place to relax”
text: Found this place in a tourist brochure, checked it out here and booked a room for an impromptu weekend in Seattle. Got a good deal with our AAA discount and completely enjoyed our stay. This is the former WAMU leadership/conference center and some signs have not yet been changed. It is incredibly quiet! The gardens and water features all around are very relaxing and soothing, nice fitness room and the convenient snack bar in the living room of each building was very convenient for grabbing water before we went out on the town. The only thing we missed was a swimming pool or spa but that was not really missed too much. Reasonable price and great accommodations, where we were not nickel and dimed for every amenity, Free parking, wifi, water and snacks. We saved 50 a day on those things alone. Great find, we'll be returning when we need to be staying in Seattle.

title: “Clean and Friendly with an Excellent Location”
text:
I stayed at the GEM Chelsea this past weekend for a solo getaway to NYC. From check-in to check-out everything was excellent at this hotel. My room, while small, was well appointed and clean. The free water and coffee in the rooms is a nice touch. The free wi-fi was fast and dependable. I liked the fact that you could open your windows to let fresh air in, and that the window sheilded street noise when closed. The neighborhood is excellent with many places to shop and eat right outside your door. Very easy subway access as well. 
I usually stay in the Mid-town/Times Square area when I go to the city, but not anymore. The GEM Chelsea will now be my first choice.

title: “The Alpha and The Omega for Our Vacation”
text:
Although we travel to the U.S. annually, it's almost 4 years since our last visit to Boston, and to the Lenox Hotel. This trip was a roadtrip from Boston, through Vermont and into Quebec (and back again). We decided to stay the first and the last night in the city. 
We had no need to check out competitor hotels, it was an unanimous decision between my husband and myself that we would stay at the Lenox. In fact, we didnt even check rates of other hotels in the city. The Lenox was where we wanted to be. 
Our arrival was greeted with the same friendly efficiency as our last visit. We hadnt expected our room to be ready, however the very pleasant Receptionist advised it would be ready in about 20 minutes and suggested we have a drink in Solas bar if we wanted to wait. As promised, approximately 20 minutes later she came to get us. However, the biggest surprise was when we went to pay for our drinks - they were complimentary and a "welcome back" from the hotel. What a lovely and not expected gesture.. 
Nothing has changed much décor-wise, but that’s what happens when you furnish with quality. No signs of tiredness around the hotel at all. Everything was as clean and fresh as our last visit. It was nice to have the same familarity as our last visit.
Our first night was in one of the superior rooms. Warm, comfortable and just as we expected. However we were pleasantly surprised when we checked in on our second occasion - we had been upgraded to a Suite. Wonderful views over the Boylston Street and the city. Only regret was that we couldnt light the fire as it was so humid and warm! Loved the array of L’Occitane toiletries and little extras. Although being centre city, we both had a great night sleep with no noise pollution on the 9th floor.
We had drinks in Solas bar and a bite to eat in the City Restaurant during our second stay. Great food and reasonable prices. Nice atmosphere and great to grab a late night snack as City Restaurant takes orders to 11pm. Nice cosy atmosphere in a funky environment, and seems to be a popular spot for local courting couples to have dinner (we were surrounded by them!). I’m not one for visiting Irish bars (whether “themed” or Irish owned) when travelling (can do that at home), however Solas is a nice spot for a drink, and judging by the plates of food passing us - popular for food too. Didnt get the opportunity to visit the City Bar and try some of their moreish cocktails, as we met with friends in Solas, and it was probably a more conducive environment for a "chat". We didnt have breakfast either mornings, as we were anxious to get out and on the road during our first visit. However, the complimentary tea/coffee in the lobby was welcomed, and we headed off to pick up our rental car, armed with a large cup of coffee (Starbucks I think it was). 
We took the Hotel car to the Airport for our flight home. $30, as opposed to $25 'ish for a standard taxi. What’s $5 for a little luxury? Highly recommended. I wasnt aware that they had a hotel car and it is something I would consider for future visits.
I like the fact that the Lenox still maintains a personal service and you don’t feel that you are just a number passing through an international chain-type hotel. It has a warmth and homeliness to it still. Any staff we had dealings with was pleasant and efficient. 
Each time when we passed through and employees wished us “welcome home”, as cheesy as it sounded, it was actually true in our case. For us, when visiting Boston, the Lenox is our Home Away From Home and I can’t see us changing in the foreseeable future.
One of the Receptionists gave me a “High Five” when we were checking out when she learnt that we had started/ended our vacation with them and were repeat guests. 
High Five right back at ya Lenox Hotel. You deserve it.

title: “Great value good location”
text: Great value for the quality of the hotel, despite the construction which was going on around the hotel the only impact was with the car park. The quality of the breakfast was good but the organisation of the breakfast could be improved, leave yourself plenty of time if you are planning breakfast.

title: “Large hotel in a great location”
text:
We've stayed here several times before so it's a nice familiar location for us.
It's only a few blocks from Millennium Station. We had a wonderful view of the river, Navy Pier and Lake Michigan. Check-in and out was fast and friendly. Very nice, clean room with 2 queen beds. large bathroom, large closet, chair, desk area, large tv. Plenty of room for 4 of us. We did not eat anywhere in the hotel. Below the west tower are several quick restaurants and service businesses which cater more to the business traveler during the week. McDonald's is one of them but they do close early.
We were able to leave our luggage with the bellman after checking out so we could explore the rest of the day until it was time to leave.

title: “Great time in NYC at the Hudson”
text:
We booked for 4 nights at the Hudson through Priceline and were sceptical due to lots of negative reviews on this site. 
However, don't be put off by these - we had a good time at the hotel. Yes, the rooms are on the compact side - but they were spotless (cleaned daily) and so well designed that it never felt too cramped. There was plenty of space for 2 adults, 2 large suitcases and plenty of shopping. Shower was hot and had a variety of power settings.
The lobby is a bit TOO dark, but check in was speedy and efficent.
Drinks and food were expensive at the hotel (both in the bars and room service/minibar) but there are plenty of reasonably priced diners nearby.
Location superb - just round the corner from Central Park and a 2 minute walk from Columbus Circle Subway with easy access to all the sights.
Recommended

title: “Nice cozy stay at Club Quarters WTC!”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for 4 nights (Oct. 6th-10th) and had a great time! As mentioned by others, the hotel is new (approximately 2yrs old) and located right beside the WTC Memorial. While the area surrounding the hotel is bustling during the day, we found it conveniently quiet at night. 
There are plenty of stores, restaurants, etc. located within easy walking distance. While there is a restaurant located on the 20th floor of the hotel, we chose to venture over to nearby O'Hara's Irish Pub for a few drinks. The atmosphere in there was great, with in-depth stories, pictures, etc. about the pubs situation during the horrible events on 9/11.
The hotel itself was clean and modern, with fantastic staff who were extremely pleasant and professional. We had a studio room with kitchenette facilities which was awesome. The room was very clean with a comfortable bed. We ended up having a rear courtyard facing room so there were absolutely no noise issues. And yes, the water station situated in the hallway was a great asset to have as well.
I had an opportunity to use the gym located on the 6th floor and it was very functional and clean. While this hotel is by far the most expensive we have stayed in during our travels, it was not a disappointment! We would certainly stay here in the future, especially when we come back to see the memorial full completed.

title: “Loved the room and the BIG tv!”
text: I am all about the comfort of the bed. It was so comfy and the sheets smelled so clean. A big screen tv hung in front of the bed ,Samsung good picture. Very clean room up to date decor. Just everything was nice for the price. The only inconvenience was parking. There wasnt a whole lot of spaces. You don't cross any major streets to get to the beach. Less than a 5 min walk. Busy casual beach area. Would stay there again!

title: “SMALL, SMALL, SMALL with NO AC”
text:
As much as one can enjoy the old and eclectic atmosphere, this one is over the top.
The rooms are smaller than any studio apartment… no room in the bathroom area to put anything at all…. I mean nothing!!!!
OK – so NO ac, which is fine with regards to the fact that it is cool in San Francisco….. But, if you were looking for some peace and quick, forget it… because you have to open the window… Hello this is San Francisco, do you know how much noise is here… Hello….
The worst part is you can find better hotels in walking distance for the same price…
So the water is either hot or cold…No warm….
Why book here if you don’t… just saying…

title: “Not at all up to Novotel Standards”
text: I have stayed at few Novotel Hotels before and this has to be the worst among all of them. The location of the hotel is just perfect and hence i booked this hotel. But the rooms are so tiny. Staff is not helpful at all. Rather rude at some times. The building has Air con and heating problems. Not a great hotel to stay if you like your sleep.

title: “Just Fine”
text:
My husband and I recently stayed here, along with our good friends, during the Indy 500 weekend. We'd booked the rooms almost an entire year in advance. Typical of the majority of hotels in the area on race weekend, the rates almost double for Friday, Saturday and Sunday night. Can't really blame the hotel for this practice.
Anyway, we had a fine stay. Our rooms were nice and the front desk worked hard to get us rooms close together. In general, the staff was friendly and helpful.
We spent some time in the pool/jacuzzi; a bit of a chlorinated smell in there since it's totally enclosed and the jets on the jacuzzi went off after five minutes (a bit of a hassle to keep climbing in and out to turn them back on) BUT there were towels laid out on all of the chairs (a nice touch) and it was clean.
The rooms were fine; we were next to the ice machine but for the most part, we hardly heard it. It was really quiet, too; great, considering what weekend it was. It seemed to us that the crowd there was definitely in the "want to have fun but aren't crazy about it" category. Average age seemed to be 50s.
We ate breakfast three of the four mornings. Nice enough; a continental plus type affair.
I did think it would have been nice of them to offer the breakfast outside the standard 7-10 on race day since the majority of the patrons left the hotel by 6:30 am to get to the track. 
They did, however, leave out cookies (and punch, I think, don't know, didn't try it) each evening in the lobby.
So, if we're ever back for the race, we'd definitely stay here again. It was very convenient to the track as well as to numerous restaurants (chain and local) and a fantastic grocery store across the street.

title: “The Hamptons was a lovely experience.”
text: Our one night stay in a suite was an excellent experience. Our room was ready upon arrival, and check out was automatic. Everything was immaculate. The suite was spacious, quiet, reasonably priced, and would have been a great place to spend a week or two if we had the time. We are non-smokers, and were pleased that only one floor of this facility is occupied by smokers. We never saw or smelled any smoke whatsoever.The only shortcoming of this motel is that pets are not accepted, so we had to leave our little dog at home.

title: “Would Stay Again”
text: A group of 4 girls stayed here at the end of February 2010 during the snow storm in NYC. Hotel was very clean, still new. Location close to time square, maybe a 10-15 min walk. Hotel was located on an ok kinda dirty street but would stay again if the price is cheap. If you are on a honeymoon or a romance type trip, i would splurge and pick a better hotel. Hot continental breakfast was a big factor on our decision for this hotel. It was a very nice way to start our day as we did ALOT of walking. Front desk people was very nice and informative. The room was fairly small but that expected with NYC. We got a room with two double beds, they were full size instead of queen size so that was dissappointing. Good thing we are petite, or the beds would not accomodate for the 4 of us.

title: “Great hidden find at an incredible value”
text: Excellent hotel, location (close to everything and great quite area), excellent staff. Super clean and an air of simplicity and "coolness'. If your looking for a location with no car needed and easy walking distance to everything and great neighborhood then this is it.

title: “Best stay in a long time”
text: You just never really know, even with researching on Trip Advisor what you are going to find until you actually get there. WOW, IS ALL I CAN SAY. We were in room 27B (27th floor), a suite with two full bedrooms with flat screen TV's and two full bathrooms, a living room, again with a flat screen TV, kitchen area with microwave, silverware, glassware, table and chairs. Every room had all amenities needed (Crabtree and Evelyn) and then some. The quality of the furnishings is incredible and the beds are super comfortable. Robes, slippers, patio overlooking the city, fantastic doormen and bellhop. The heating/cooling system was very old but it worked for our stay. The location is good. Overall it was the best hotel we've stayed at in a long time. Thank you Kimberly. We will be back.

title: “Attractive, comfortable accommodations; friendly, courteous staff”
text:
The staff at St. Gregory's was some of the most gracious and accommodating that I've encountered. The suite was well appointed, clean, and comfortable. 
I'm not planning a return trip to DC in the foreseeable future, but when and if I visited again, I would definitely plan to stay here.. and would recommend same to friends and family.
As Ebert would say: two thumbs up!

title: “I (heart) The Prescott!!!”
text: Just returned home from a wondering three-night stay at the Prescott. This is a very cute smaller hotel with a very friendly staff and lots of character. Our room was super-nice and clean with a great view of Post Street. Public transportation, wonder shopping, restaurants, theatres, night life, and museums were all within a short walking distance. There is a bike rental shop around the corner, with 24-hour drop off service, which was great for biking around the city. The staff was great, from allowing us to check-in at 11:00 AM (!!!), the complementary wine hour, and allowing us to store our bags on our check-out date due to a late flight. We also enjoyed the free in-room wifi. We will be returning again and again!

title: “they employee genuinely nice people”
text: Pretty standard fare for a Hampton Inn with this one close to most everything in the city. Only 9 rooms per floor makes this a tall narrow hotel. The rooms are city small. . It was very clean,a little rough in spots where renovations were still taking place (the breakfast area) but nothing bad. What struck me was how polite and pleasant the staff were. They always had a greeting either in passing in the hallway or in the elevator or on the phone and in all my encounters were pleasant. They were helpful with information and problem solving. While some of that comes with training it also comes from empowering.

author.location: the Berkshire Hills of New England

title: “nice, relaxing”
text: The Omni was a great, relaxing hotel. Nice lobby, very helpful front desk staff (Maria is the best), good gym, nice array of toiletries and extra like chocolate on your bed and the ice cooler already filled to the brim :). The rooms and bathrooms were spacious for a NY hotel - I stayed in both a king and 2 doubles, and the room with 2 doubles was slightly bigger. Also, of course the location is great - a few short blocks from St. Pats and Rockefeller Center. The only things I had issues with were the so-called business amenities. Wireless is not free, but you can sign up to their select program, which is free, to get free wireless as a perk. Very complicated! The prices at their business center for printing and faxing were also ridiculous. Other negatives: No continental breakfast, no coffee maker in the room, and no complimentary lounge area with snacks or drinks. Overall, just your typical upscale NYC hotel - nothing special, but you can't go wrong staying here.

title: “Located near Central Park, Subway & walking distance to shops, theatre, etc.”
text: Good quiet location, very close to Central Park, Subway access & Carnegie Hall. Easy walk to Times Square and shopping on 5th avenue. Many food & facilities nearby. Room basic, I miss having a fridge to keep milk & water cold, but otherwise acceptable.

title: “weekend at COSI”
text: It's a clean, kid friendly hotel. The kids enjoyed the pool and the manager's reception. We had dinner at the hotel restaurant and the service was awful and the food was not much better. Overall the hotel is very nice, I would order pizza or go out for dinner though

title: “Nice looking, skimpy on all that makes a fine hotel”
text: Six reception computers, two receptionists, one very long line. Our key card fit a room occupied by a woman who'd already checked into it... one more wait in line to straighten that out. Told there was room in underground parking, we toured the entire cramped levels: full. Told that therefore valet parking would be changed to regular parking fee, that bill came to $30. for one night ($6 less than valet). Told the 28th floor restaurant was excellent, we had to ask for fresh pepper, and the soup needed lots of it; service was inattentive, meal was stronger on writeup than cooking. Great views, excellent downtown location, extensive brunch...but overall truly disappointing. It seems the Marriott attention to their profit margin overrides attention to services and presentation.

title: “comfy and clean but not beautiful”
text:
My husband stayed here Wed. through Fri. night as a conference attendee. I joined him for Fri. night.
Positives: clean rooms, comfy bed, courteous staff, comprehensive (but not cheap, about $17) hot breakfast buffet with free juice refills, nice location on the river
Negatives: no room service (or any food service) after 10:30 pm--vending machines only, location seems to be in the business district (i.e., not as good for weekend shopping or daytripping), atrium architecture and decor is utilitarian and sterile

title: “Fabulous Stay”
text:
The positives:
1. Rooms are modern, clean, beautiful; beds lovely.
2. Views are wonderful (we were on 31st floor).
3. Concierge was extremely helpful with rental car, planning trips, etc. 
4. Regency Club was AMAZING. I miss it already! (huge high-quality food selection, super clean, lots of space & areas to sit, very friendly & professional Regency Club staff). 
5. As usual, the ventilation for the rooms was fantastic (typical Hyatt).
6. Perfect Location!
Negatives:
1. Rooms a little on the small side
Thank you Hyatt! You made our stay in San Francisco wonderful!

title: “Amazing staff, Great Hotel, Overall Fabolous Stay”
text: Overall great stay and experience. I spent two great weeks at the W Hotel, and the staff made it a great enjoyable time. The folks at the hotel were always ready to assist, and provide great customer support and assistance during my time. Overall I would like to thank each and every staff employee at the W Hotel. It was by far my best stay at a hotel thus far in my life!!!! A++++++++++

title: “Good Hotel; Great Rates; Nice Breakfast”
text: Stayed here for one night at room 220. No noise, large room and very good rate. Five munute drive to downtown Dallas. Free parking. Full american breakfast. Very good bargain.

title: “very good hotel in a great location!”
text: We just stayed 3 nights to see some shows and this location is great.The hotel is a wonderful place. It has perks most NY hotels don't. Free wireless internet. Free phone calls-local AND long distance(US only). Good continental breakfast. Meticulously clean room. No problems. Only wish they had a min-fridge.

title: “Very enjoyable visit”
text: We were with a group convention for three days and everything was great. Rooms were very nice and staff very pleasant.

title: “Why go elsewhere?”
text:
I just wanted to personally thank you and your team for the great hospitality. It was a great experience all around. I would like to point out a few people who I thought exemplified great core values and teamwork. 
First, the impression made by Magdalena at the desk could not have been better. Even though my room was not ready (which is perfectly fine, didn't expect it to be), her genuineness and constant follow up made quite an impression. Worth the wait!
The banquets team was superb for our dinner Thursday night. The only thing that should have happened was that I should have been more diligent in getting their names. I believe one gentlemen's name was Tom who seemed to step in even more as needed and was quite knowledgeable about the specialty drinks. He constantly checked in on our end of the table. But they all gave a great experience which along with unbelievable course selection created a unforgettable night. 
I had a quick dinner at the bar Friday night and got to see Tom and Bruce at the Grant Grill. What a fine example of team work. They knew their returning customers, educated on the wines specifically (the guest next to me was pretty detailed in what they wanted), and how they helped each other's covers added a nice touch to what can sometimes be a territorial area. Great job.
Finally, I have to give credit to Nathan. He showed an all around great presence in the lobby and around the hotel. A great addition to your team and he will definitely grow the high standards already being displayed. 
Thanks again for making this a great experience. I don't think I could have asked for anything better this week.

title: “It was okay...”
text: It definitely had the chain hotel feeling vs. boutique. Lobby area was the best part, very pretty sitting area, fruit flavored water out all day. But the room felt worn around the edges and out of date. (like it was chic 7 years ago kind of style) Previous time in Boston we stayed at the Liberty hotel and preferred that times a million. Will definitely be back at the Liberty next time.

title: “good hotel in a great location”
text: Stayed here for 3 nights recently and it was great.The location is really good,opposite Penn Station and Madison Sq Garden.The suite we stayed in was huge,well big enough for 4 of us,we had a lovely large new sofa bed,the most comfortable one I've ever slept on. We stayed on the top floor(28)the view wasn't great unless you looked sharply to the right and you could see the Empire State building.Highly recommended.

title: “elegant, grand hotel”
text: The staff were very courteous and the room was very quiet, at the end of the hall. The room was pretty small, though, and there was no regular coffee left in the room for the second morning, only decaf! And I wish nice hotels would realize that most people need more than one cup of coffee in the morning....aside from that small detail, we loved the location which enabled us to walk to the waterfront and the monorail and museums. It is an old, elegant hotel and a good value for the location.

title: “Great location, nice rooms”
text:
I chose this hotel mainly based on the location and the positive Trip Advisor reviews. Several of us were coming in for the weekend via buses that dropped off near Penn Station, so this was a short walk for everyone. Not the most charming location in Manhattan, but there's a subway stop very close by so it was easy to get around. 
Some typical NYC hotel issues are to be expected - the room was compact, and the elevators were occasionally crowded and slow. But you don't spend much time in the hotel room anyway! The room seemed recently renovated and had a decent size bathroom. Even with 2 double beds taking up most of the space it accommodated three girls and our weekend bags. We had a nice view of the Empire State Building right outside the door. Plus the staff was nice and I enjoyed the free cookies - I would definitely stay here again.

title: “great stay”
text: beautiful hotel. great views from the room of the bay.

title: “Perfect Getaway For Two !”
text: I reserved this hotel for my husband & I for a weekend getaway. We wanted to be close to Union Station & within walking distance to BART. This was perfect! A charming, clean hotel with a nice atmosphere. The room was small, but we enjoyed it just the same. The lounge area was nice, as was the staff. If the rooms were larger we would have no problem staying here with our kids (7 & 10). We would stay again, no problem.

title: “Nice Hotel, Excellent Location”
text:
Stayed at the Post Oak from 6/12 to 6/14. Very enjoyable stay and the location was excellent. I had never been to Houston before and was amazed at how large the city is! 
I spent some "down time" over at the Galleria Mall which was very nice, loved the indoor skating rink! Many nice restaurants as well as a CVS and a Walgreens nearby.
Very friendly staff and the room was more than adequate.
One small complaint was that maid service arrived very late in the day to clean the room. I had wanted to take a little "catnap" before going out for a dinner meeting but ended up having to kill sometime at the nearby stripmall because they hadn't gotten to my room yet.
Other than that everything else was fine and would definitely stay there again.

title: “excellent stay”
text: i can honestly say this is the best hotel i have stayed in. the staff are very friendly and cant do enough for you, highly recommend this hotel if your are visiting dc.It also in an ideal location for visiting all the main tourist attractions .my family and i visited the east coast dc boston and new york and this hotel was by far the best quality and value for money we stayed in .

title: “You are not valued at this hotel....”
text: We booked the hotwire.com, got a great value, but upon arrival, it seems they treat us differently because we didnt book directly thru them. No apologies when our King room wasnt available...was moved the next night to a king size bed....ON THE 13th FLOOR! I wasnt too freaked out about the 13th floor until we barely missed being hit by a car and hearing gunshots....most hotels skip floor 13....we became freaked out and asked to be moved to a different floor to ease our comfort level....we were told to ask for Eric and he would take care of us. Im assuming Eric is a front desk manager, but he was gone by the time we got to the desk. I lady by the name of Mary was cold and unaccomodating from the moment i began talking to her. I explained my situation and she told me she had no rooms availble...3/4 of the hotel was empty!!! Then told me to explain it with management in the morning......it would be irrelevant by then! I told her Eric wwas working with us, but she said he left no notes for her...i asked her to make something happen to satisfy our request, then she got on the phone and claimed she was being discriminated against!!!! The only ones discriminated against was us....we prompty left the hotel and called to check out...all she did was say, you wont get refunded....if you want to be treated badly, stay here. If not, I advise you to look elsewhere. Happy New Year....

title: “Great hotel centrally located”
text: We had a room with double queen beds. It was clean, spacious and pleasant. Beds were comfortable and enabled a good nights sleep. Hotel staff were exceptionally courteous and helpful. The hotel is both pet friendly and pet owner friendly. I can recommend Loews and will be staying here again.

title: “Once A Great Place”
text: March 14, 2008 I Stayed at the Grand View Inn and Suites. I was amazed when I arrived at the property dispite the bad comments I have heard from friends that it wasnt all that bad. The hotel is currently going through remodeling. At one time im sure this place was booming. Grand View has an indoor pool, a bar and restaurant. Im sure in June when they have their grand opening busiiness will be booming once again. I enjoyed my stay Friday night. My kids and I enjoyed the swimming pool all the way until closing it was very peaceful. I would love to see the property once everything gets going In june.

title: “Great hotel - great location”
text: Great hotel, location and staff. Nice concierge lounge. Right on the waterfront as the hotels name suggests.

title: “Excellent Location - Nice Property”
text: From the start this was a good stay. The front desk staff were pleasant and very accommodating with my early check-in. The room was decent and well distributed. Overall, this was nothing less than I would expect at an Intercontinental property. The location was awesome with everything a few steps away, literally. I would stay here again.

title: “Great stay and excellent location”
text:
I love the Topaz. And like most Kimptons, the level of service here is superb. 
Rooms are spacious, comfy and quiet. I love that my room had a little alcove off the bathroom to get ready in.
The wine hour is a nice touch, although I was only there one night for it. 
They don't have a fitness center on site, but give you access to the YMCA just around the corner. The Y is a little dated, but is enormous - you can always find a machine, and the pool is great.
The bar is nice and usually not too crowded - although I wish they offered more food choices - especially on a cold, snowy January night. 
This is one of my go-to hotels in DC since its close to my office and will definitely be staying here again one day!

title: “Perfect”
text: Staff were friendly. Hotel was clean and nice. Pool was refreshing. Was nothing short of my high expectations.

title: “Good hotel”
text:
This is an older hotel which has been modernized several times and is well maintained. It is an excellent location for business near the airport or an overnight layover at the airport for connections to flight, cruise, etc. It occasionally offers excellent value internet rates. It is about a block down from the main SEATAC terminal and can be walked in about 10 minutes, however, there is a shuttle service to the terminal. There are several decent restaurants within easy walking distance (remember it rains a lot here). One may also walk/shuttle over to the airport parking garage and catch the light rail directly into downtown Seattle, travel time about 25-30 minutes.
Hotel motif is NW Pacific rustic but it wears it well. As it is an older hotel the rooms are quite large and fully equipped. The rest of the hotel amenities are as advertised, think four star here. There are a number of other hotels in the immediate airport area but this one presents an excellent compromise between price and hotel condition.

title: “Cool Lookig Hotel”
text:
The Hotel has great decor wihich is funky young and upbeat. I would give it 10 for styling. Great location close walking to all the sights. Staff was less desirable. I drove to the hotel and decided to use the valet parking for $30 dollars a night, this worked great. 
Typicaly hotels will have a bell boy to help there clients, no one was there to great us, or help us with our luggage. Went to check in... not even a hello "Do you have ID" was the opening line, sorry guy's but this is not customs. 
I had high hopes for this hotel but I gave it an average rating do to the average care that I was give while stayng there.

title: “Poorly Maintained”
text: I had had good expriences with Microtel on the East Coast, but this was a different story. It appeared to be another motel that microtel had bought. The halls reeked of cigarette smoke. The carpets were stained, and the funishings looked old and worn. The refrigerator in our room was big and appeared to be missing a panel.

title: “A Great Stay”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel a couple of times when it was The Wyndham! I LOVE this place. Even if ere is something wrong with my room etc., they have always made it right! Rhonda who works in the bar are is such a sweetie! I would highly recommend this hotel!
Stephanie J.

title: “great relaxing location!”
text: thank u island palms for a fabulous long weekend in san diego! i picked shelter island to have a relaxing experience which is what we got! the Blue Wave Grill and bar was delicious! the staff was very welcoming. thanks to the front desk for informing us of the bus stop right down the road from the hotel. we didnt want to drive on our vacation and for only $5 day pass u can use any bus or trolley which goes to many locations. the bus and trolleys were clean and very easy to find. just ask the front desk for an attraction map which was very helpful with which bus and trolleys to take for where u want to go! we had an amzing view from our room on the 3rd level of the casa marina buliding. we would definitely recommend best western island palms hotel and marina to others!

author.location: Lake in the Hills, Illinois, United States

title: “Classic hotel in downtown Denver”
text:
This property is very charming. A little noisy on the street side which didn't bother me, but it may a light sleeper.
My pet peeve with hotels, especially 4 star properties, is when they gouge you for internet service. Good grief! The Hampton Inns have free WiFi, which as a HH Diamond member I'll stay at occasionally. 
I'd stay here agin if the price was right.

title: “Best Hotel in Downtown L.A.”
text:
Whenever I travel to downtown L.A., I always stay at the Checkers. 
Quite simply, it's downtown L.A.'s best hotel -- the service is impeccable, the hotel has charming architecture, and the rooms are well-appointed. The bathrooms are also decked out in gorgeous marble and granite. The Checkers has a great on-site restaurant as well as fantastic room service. It even has windows that open to the outside, which is particularly nice if you have a high floor and a cool L.A. 
night.
The pool deck and hot tub provides one of the most stunning downtown settings anywhere. After a long day of working in L.A., I suggest grabbing your favorite drink, heading to the roof, hopping into the hot tub, and gazing at the Library Tower and L.A.'s other great buildings. 
The Westin Bonaventure, Biltmore, and Downtown Marriott cannot hold a candle to this place.

title: “Best of the best”
text:
I have been there for 7 days for holiday seasons. I have booked 1 queen studio but found an issue that bathroom door was broken, then switch the room. However, I also noticed that heating system did not work. So, I requested a room- upgrade to the front guy, Dan. He was one of the best front persons I have ever met. He offered me a King bedroom suite, but it was smoking room. Then, I also asked to Ann, general manager to switch the non-smoking room, and she offered me two queen bedroom suite. It was amazing. Everyone working in this hotel is very friendly and helpful during the stay. They are always customer’s side. 
They also have free parking, free internet, free breakfast with meats and free dinner with red and white wines and beer during weekdays (5-7PM). 
This hotel is way better than 5 star hotels I have ever been regarding overall services, price and etc.

title: “Great location and great price”
text: We have stayed at the Park Central a few times when visiting NYC. There are often great prices on the Internet and we have always been pleased with our stay. The location is great for just about anything we want to do in the City. The rooms have always been clean and quite nice. I would definitely recommend it.

title: “Great Times Square location with some drawbacks”
text:
Unlike some other reviews, I won't call this hotel charming. Not when the room winter heating makes odd clunking noises throughout the night. The front desk told me that is normal. Perhaps this is not a problem in the summer then. Make no mistake, this is not a new hotel at all, but very old, barely updated, and generally vacuum clean and yet everything in my bathroom worked. I looked for bedbugs, but saw none, thankfully, because I thought this might be the "that" kind of hotel.
In older hotels I often feel a bit unsecure, but I also felt safe knowing that several NYC police cars often hang out outside across the street, perhaps as a ready response force for anything that might happen in nearby Times Square or some nearby business buildings. 
The hotel does not offer any food at any time of the day, but that is ok. Next door is a deli that makes great breakfasts and lunches. At the end of my stay, my overall assessment was that this is not a bad hotel for the money, since it is about half the cost of the Hotel Edison which is very nice.

title: “Small but Charming”
text:
If you are traveling with children or expect to put more than 1-2 people in your hotel room, this is not for you. However, if it's just you +1 this is a wonderful place to stay. The decor is euro-chic and cozy. Great cocktail bar and the staff is very helpful. I would definitely stay here again.
Good to Know:
no gift shop or coffee shop in the hotel
don't miss the front door! it's small and would be easy to walk right by, but there is always someone there to open the door for you and let you know if you're in the right spot
there is a window between the shower and the room with 2 sheer-ish panels you can close, but does not provide total privacy

title: “Room nice but general experience just ok”
text:
Got this hotel on Priceline for an overnight transit through Boston, worked out cheaper than any of the "airport hotels". 
Arrived around 9pm...nice large bright lobby but SO noisy..there was some sort of reunion party going on in the main bar/restaurant and you could hardly hear yourself think in the lobby. Check in was efficient.
Our room was large and airy, with lots of floor space but the usual problem of not enough electrical outlets to charge all the electronics for our next day of travel.
Went down to the Irish bar for some dinner....food and service was just average...and not an Irish staff member to be found (I actually asked as there was some particular information I needed that would have been a word of mouth thing).
Decided to try the concierge but the desk was unstaffed for the 5 minutes we stood at it. Went back to our room and dialled the number but it rang out and eventually went to voicemail, we opted to give up.
