There was free wifi in the lobby area and two levels of paid wifi in the room. As there was something we needed to see from home online we opted for the Gold service (which the info said was required for streaming) at $19.95. Signal was poor and unstable and crashed at least three times in the hour (the charge was refunded at checkout when we mentioned this)
The bed was large and comfortable. En suite bathroom was also a decent size and had the all important magnifying mirror. Double shower head with a notice about Westin's famous dream showers...and information on how to get the second head working. Well it certainly wasn't the shower of my dreams, even with both, pressure was poor.
The location is great if you're going to the convention centre and a relatively short cab ride from the airport. The location has little else going for it...I would stay there again only for transits such as this.

title: “Radisson at Fisherman's Wharf”
text: We stayed here for three nights 23rd-25th May. Contrary to some negative feedback we read about this hotel, which made us a bit apprehensive before going to SF, we found it to be clean and comfortable, and unbeatable for location, being at the heart of Fisherman's Wharf, with easy access to some of the major attractions and restaurants. Our room was well appointed and equipped, with two Queen sized beds and good facilities including coffee making equipment (although the coffee/tea/sugar/milk was not replenished particularly well) . The power shower in the bathroom was one of the best experienced on our Californian holiday. It is true that there is road noise from frontage bedrooms, but this did not unduly bother us, and to be honest ear plugs blotted it out anyway. The staff were helpful and polite in providing useful information on attractions and directions. There is a small snack bar in the reception area, which is quite useful if one needs to grab a quick coffee and danish. There are some very good restaurants locally (we loved Alioto's) and the Wharf area is hyper active and very 'buzzy', with something for everyone. Boudin bakery is great for quick meals and one can watch the bakers at work. The sea lions at Pier 39 are a great attraction. Boat trips abound, with excellent trips to Alcatraz (has to be the ultimate experience) , the Golden Gate Bridge and other attractions. The best way to get around is by bike, tram or cable car, all easily accessible locally. We got our breakfasts at ITOP which is located right next to the hotel, and there is a local Safeways within easy walking distance. Most of SFs main attractions are accessible from Fisherman's Wharf, and many, like China Town and Union Square/Macys can be reached on foot if one can cope with the hill climbs (take the cable car otherwise). Open tour buses operate from just round the corner from the hotel and the cable car terminal is a short walk away. The hotel has a small swimming pool, although this did not seem to be well used while we were there. There are several entrances to the hotel, which makes accessing rooms, which are loacted along lengthy corridors, easier. A top tip for SF, and particularly Fisherman's Wharf, is that it can be quite chilly due to winds coming of the Pacific, so take something warm to wear. The shops here do a roaring trade in Fleeces and other warm clothing....! Little wonder, as most tourists are caught out.

title: “Excellent customer service!!!”
text: This was our first family trip with 3 teens and an 6yr old. We took the crew to Fiesta Texas which was very close to the hotel. We even bought discounted tickets and parking pass from the hotel. The check in was super fast and ANGELA was very sweet and friendly. She even brought us extra towels at 11:00pm. With teens who are always hungry the free snacks and breakfast was a brilliant idea! We enjoyed the clean room and excellent housekeeping. We love this hotel. Very family friendly. We stayed for two nights in a double room. It was plenty of room for everyone and very clean. We had a great vacation!! Thank you again!

title: “Excellent Customer Service!!”
text: I absolutely LOVE this Hilton Garden Inn. The customer service here is OUTSTANDING. Robin Davis, the front desk manager is amazing. Always polite, professional, and she pays great attention to detail. I am a business traveler, and I have stayed at this hotel many times over the last few months, and I will continue to come back!

title: “Always a welcome refuge in Philly”
text:
I stay at the Sofitel in Philly about 30 nights a year. I rate it highly because not only is it a lovely hotel with excellent service -- it is consistently this way, no matter when I have stayed there. This consistency sets this hotel apart from other hotels in the city.
The French flair of the Sofitel is apparent from the first 'Bon Jour' you hear as you enter. All of the staff has been trained to look each customer in the eye and greet them warmly. You feel welcome every time you enter. The front desk is efficient and very well-trained. 
The rooms are spacious and the beds are heavenly. Although like most Center City properties, the views are limited, there are still large windows that let in light. The bathrooms are well appointed and robes are always in each room.
The gym is small but fully equipped. There are even disposable ear phones in case you forget yours and want to watch the personal TVs while you jog the treadmill.
The bar and restaurant are comfortable and lively. Nice food options. Full breakfast buffet. And if you have no time for that, grab a complimentary croissant and coffee on the way out.
The location is fantastic, in the Rittenhouse area where all the good restaurants and shops abound.
It's reall very close in experience to the Four Seasons at a much better price.

title: “Excellent Property and Highly Professional Staff”
text:
I've been traveling to New York City for business for many years and have stayed at several other properties. The Bryant Park Hotel is one of, if not THE best hotel accommodation for not only my business needs but personal as well. 
The staff at Bryant Park is very well trained and provide outstanding customer care. Adolfo Ramirez is increditable about making sure his guests are well taken care of. Kelly Kato, is one of the best Events Corrdinators I've worked with.

title: “My Worse Hotel Experience Ever!”
text: When it comes to customer service, this hotel gets the thumb down from me. I stayed at this hotel from December 24, 2011- December 29, 2011. Every service from check-in to check-out was terrible. Although confirmed, there was no shuttle service from the airport to the hotel. Upon check-in, I found out that there were no fridge or microwave, which were promised at time of booking and the hotel did not make one accessible to the guest. Although breakfast was provided, guests were not allowed to take food to their rooms although there was not sufficient seating available at anytime and breakfast staff was rude and inefficient. Hotel employees were generally rude and not at all helpful. The rooms were too small and not very clean. The television was out for at least 3 of the 5 nights that we stayed and although promised that we would get a refund for the inconvenience, we did not receive it at time of check-out. The front desk clerk named (Tom) was rude to a family member trying to reach us at the hotel. In addition, we were advised that calls within the US were not free when the actually were. The employee working in the business centre was extremely rude. Front desk refused to assist with getting a cab to the airport although we check out at 5 am in the morning. Internet service was weak and there was always problems getting online. I seriously did not feel like I was a paying customer but as if someone was giving this vacation to me but the really did not want to give it. I will never stay at this hotel again and would not recommend it to my worse enemy.

title: “Not The Ritz Carlton, But Is A Great Value”
text:
The Travelodge LAX is a very good value. While it is an older motel-style venue, they keep it very clean. I have stayed there many times over the years. The staff always remembers me and makes sure my stay is acceptable.
They recently added new beds in nearly all rooms. The walls can be thin in some units, but that can be the case in nearly any motel/hotel that you stay at. 
So, for what it is, The Travelodge LAX is a good place to stay if you need a place near LAX.

title: “GREAT HOTEL!”
text: We have stayed at many hotels in the city of AUstin over the years, this time we opted for a hotel not right downtown in the heart of things. So glad we did. I loved this hotel. We asked for a room on the quieter side of the building & were promply accomodated. The desk clerk was awesome (I don't remember her name right now, tho). The hotel is beautifully decorated in contempory styles. The rooms are also beautifully appointed. Did I mention... I LOVE this hotel. The price was GREAT! They have a bar, but it's only open on the weekdays? Butm that was ok, we walked across the lot to a nice restaurant & had a few drinks. The room was super quiet & we really enjoyed it. The morning FULL breakfast was part of our package & it was very good. With all the restaurant options in Austin, we never eat at the hotel, but we thought we'd try it as it was free. So glad we did! We were right on the freeway & it was an easy on - off when we headed into town. 15 minutes from downtown, easily. If you ever need a room in Austin & the Arboretum area is not too far north for you, stay here.

title: “Great potential, mismanaged to feel noisy, tacky and chaotic”
text: This is a great property in need of a new manager. The basic facilities are close to perfect. In our first view hours on Friday afternoon we thought we had found everything we wanted in our vacations for the next few years: great waterpark, for our children, a classic elegant resort for us. By lunch Saturday the problems started. An excruciatingly loud live musician replaced the quiet poolside music, preventing all conversation. The pool manager agreed it was too loud and asked the singer to turn it down with little effect. Personally. any live music at a pool would be a problem. If I want a loud frenetic atmosphere I go to a public beach -- I don't pay $300 a night for resort. The behavior of guest seemed to sink to the level of the music. People would "reserve" chairs and inner tubes first thing in the morning leaving the rest of us with neither. There was a great deal of shoving and line cutting at the slides. We have been Platinum Elite Marriott members for years and love the Marriott experience This place is geared to and attracts a very different audience. It's shaken our faith in the whole Marriott brand.

title: “Wonderful Hotel with Spectacular Views”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Fairmont on the last part of our honeymoon. We were upgraded to a tower room on the 21st floor with amazing views of the bay, golden gate bridge and Alcatraz. I don't think that we have had a better view anywhere else we have stayed in the world.
Our room was very comfortable and the hotel lobby is gorgeous - very ornate and a glimpse of America from days gone by. We arrived at the hotel late on our first night and ordered room service. Although very expensive, the food was very good.
The hotel is near the cable car lines, although we never used them as they are expensive and were always full. The hotel is easily located to walk into the main areas. However, we never walked back to the hotel given that it is located at the top of Nob Hill! and we didn't find the taxis too expensive.
We did the night tour of Alcatraz which we would highly recommend. It was very foggy on our visit which added to the atmosphere. Make sure that you wear warm clothing as it is very cold on Alcatraz in the middle of the bay. 
We also went on a Napa Valley Wine tour which was fantastic. All of the wineries were in beautiful settings and we came back to the city via ferry and got really good views of downtown.
We ate at Boulevard Restaurant on our last night which was very good and clearly very popular. I think that you would need to book in advance in order to get a table.
We loved our time in San Francisco and would not hesitate to return to the Fairmont.

title: “Great place fresh flowers in lobby”
text: We enjoyed the fresh flowers in lobby. The breakfast was above average in a large ,clean, sunny room. Could get lost in the big rooms. Polite desk staff. Driver to the airport was efficent and helpful. The Moonlight Dinner next door was a fun place to have lunch or dinner.

title: “Good stay”
text:
Came to houston for 2 days. Had a good time staying here. 
Nice pool. The breakfast was free but just adequate. 
Had airport pickup. The driver was so helpful. I didnt have the charger for my phone. He drove me to a place where I could buy a new cheap charger. 
It is near to the CS test site, so would definitely recommend for the test takers.

title: “Nice Room - Until the AC Came On”
text: The Pacific Terrace is a nice looking hotel, on the beach (across the walkway, anyway) with a very nice staff. Our room, the Presidentail Suite was large and well-furnished and everything seemed great. Then the air conditioning came on and it felt like we were on the taxiway at San Diego airport. There is one large AC vent just above the headboard of the bed and the noise from it was deafening. Our solution was to cool the room as much as possible before going to bed and then turn off the HVAC system. Unfortunately the room became hotter than the outside temp and we needed to switch on the AC at 2 AM. No sleeping in this room! While the hotel is nice, the surrounding neighborhood is a bit run down. Expect to see frequent homeless folks on benches just next to the hotel (and do not use the public restroom nearby - it is the dirtiest one we've ever encountered). In the future, for $400 a night plus $20 for parking, I'll go elsewhere. PS - They did refund the parking fee when we complained about the AC noise - woo woo!

title: “Would totally stay here again!”
text:
Stayed here for a week while in New York and loved it! The location of the hotel was amazing!! The room was pretty spacious with free wifi. We also took advantage of the happy hour, we would walk all around New York and come home just in time for happy hour, rest and then go out again it saved us a lot of money.
I can't say much about the people working since we were in and out of the hotel but when we did ask them for anything they would answer with a smile. I hope this hotel doesn't become so popular that the rates starts to go up. Staybridge would be my first choice when going to NYC again!

title: “Luxury on the small side”
text: Stayed here with a conference. Our king-size bed room was comfortable, but certainly small---and the bathroom was even smaller! Yeah, like you had to kind of step around closing the door. Now mind you, these inconveniences were made up in part by the glorious lobby, the ever-friendly Midwestern staff, and the attentive hosts and clerks. Expensive, yes. But a short block from the Art Institute, Millennium Park, and the Willis/Sears Tower. Situated south of the river in the Loop, it was a bit of a walk to the river but at the edge of the theatre district. Having stayed at the north end/Gold Coast side of the city last summer, I found the two areas quite different. Seems to be more night life up north!

title: “Great location, Wonderful Staff!!”
text: We spent 5 nights at the Warwick, and were pleasantly surprised by such an helpful staff. from the front desk to the bell staff, someone was always there to help with our questions about Denver, or directions and suggestions that always seemed to be "spot on". Enjoyed the rooftop pool on the 16th floor, and the workout room on the 15th floor had a great view and some very refreshing lemon-lime water. Loved the balconies on all the rooms...great view of Denver and the mountains in the distance. Located right between downtown and some eclectic neighborhoods, we could walk everywhere, and 3 blocks from the 16th street mall and free bus transportation. The rooms were well appointed and very clean, and had the charm of an older hotel, but had recently been updated. Certainly would love to go back next time our travels take us to Denver.

title: “A Touch of Class”
text:
I stayed in this beautiful historic hotel for 3 nights while visiting LA. The gorgeous lobby and bar area gives you a feeling of nostalgia. The home of the Oscars in the 30's and beyond, this hotel has a special air about it. The gallery bar was a busy but fun place to end our evenings.
We arrived early in the AM fully prepared to leave our luggage and check in later in the afternoon. We were pleasantly surprised when they checked us in immediately and we were in our room by 10 am. Our room was very large with plenty of space for the 4 of us to spread out.
The beds were comfortable and our room location was very quiet.
The Concierge was extremely helpful in hiring a driver to take us around LA for the day as well as recommending restaurants in the area thatt were outstanding.
I would not hesitate to recommend staying at this hotel and can't wait to stay there again.

title: “Best in SoHo”
text:
I love this hotel!!! It is like staying at your own privately owned NY loft...only someone comes and cleans your room every night, leaves you bottles of water, refreshes the flowers and brings you the most amazing food. 
There are hardwood floors. It''s contemporary, but not stuffy. Clean and so fresh feeling. I did stay in one of the larger studio suites, but my husband stays here frequently and said that even the smaller rooms are nice. 
Great room service, great food in general. You feel as if the staff knows you and you are close to shopping and wonderful choices of dining if you don't dine in the hotel. 
I highly recommend staying here if you are in NY and want to stay near the shops.

title: “Girls' Dreams Come True”
text: Our stay was definately a dream come true for our family! The location is ideal for all of the shopping on Michigan Avenue, especially the American Girl Place!! As soon as we walked in and saw the American Girl doll, my girls couldn't contain their excitement! The staff was so welcoming and made us feel right at home! The room was perfect and the view, simply breathtaking!! We can't wait to come back!

title: “A great place to stay!”
text:
SpringHill Suites was even better than expected! The reviews sounded wonderful which prompted me to make reservations here. The staff was very kind and the valet was very quick! The rooms were big and generally clean. I did find one empty bag of chips behind a dresser but that didn't really bother me. The breakfast was amazing and the location is pretty great. Yes, it's not in the heart of downtown, but I liked that it wasn't. It is still pretty close though and since we had a car, it was no problem at all. I really liked this place and was pleased with the service. Before I checked out, the whole staff and management had a team meeting in a small meeting room. I overheard them discussing their standard of service and how their goal is to have only 17% of customers make a complaint. I think currently they're at 21%. It sounds like a lot, but whatever the case, it looks like their turnaround to solving a complaint is very quick. My friend's bathroom light wasn't working and it was fixed within the hour.
Anywho, overall, I am very happy about SpringHill Suites and will definately stay here again! I can't think of a better place!

title: “Friendliest Big Hotel”
text: We recently stayed at the Omni SF and were very surprised at how welcome we felt before we even walked in the door. Every person goes out of their way to make you feel welcome. The location was just a 25 minute walk to AT&T Park to see the Giants play.

title: “Oh What a Beautiful Morning...........”
text:
We spent 4 nights at the Mandarin Oriental in D.C. and we had a wonderful time! Upon waking the first morning and opening the drapes to our amazing view of the Jefferson Memorial and surrounding areas was just breathtaking. Even in the dead of winter we could not have asked for a better view. 
And I have to mention how comfortable our room was. After sightseeing all day and to come back to such elegance and fine appointments really was the icing on the cake. The bathtub was so relaxing and the entire bathroom was very spacious and well thought out. 
Also the location is very good. With in walking distance to many Museums and Monuments. From the staff at the hotel and the restaurants, rooms and location I would highly recommend The Mandarin Oriental.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
I stayed here in order to attend a friend's wedding. I booked a double room but they were able to give me a king size bed room when I arrived. I had to rely on public transportation since I don't drive and this hotel is right across the street from the metro. It is also across the street from Walgreens and CVS (or was it Rite Aid?) so picking up nick knacks was easy. I liked my room on the 9th floor but it can get noisy out in the hall way. I would hear people walking back and forth and workers wheeling things. I ordered room service one night and find it to be a bit expensive but my salad was delicious. It was nice that they have computer free for use in the lobby for up to 45 minute intervals. That allowed me to check my email quickly without having to pay for wifi. I ventured out to the mall next to the hotel and found this beauty store down stairs. I got my brows waxed there for $7.5 and thought that price is not bad, but she almost freaked me out because she took 30 minutes doing it and she had to find her glasses mid-way. My brows turned out great but the time she spent and the whole experience did get me worried. 
All the staff that I came across (check-in staff, room service person and delivery staff, staff that I see in the hall) were all courteous and looked willing to help. I liked my stay here and wouldn't mind staying here again.

title: “Absolutely stunning!”
text: I am very loyal to Hilton hotels, not only to rack up HH points, but because I trust the brand. This experience exceeded my expectations! Having stayed in the Hilton New York (which is where I stay every time I'm in the city) only a week before this trip, my expectations were high. The price was reasonable, as we received a conference discount. The service...I've never had better in all my years staying at a Hilton. Wow. Everyone from the front desk associate to the conference staff to the incredibly handsome concierge associate was extremely polite, helpful, and created a wonderful experience for my co-worker and me. I had a beautiful, over-sized room, which was very clean, had a comfortable bed, and everything worked as it should. The location was also great. So close to Millennium Park, shopping, great restaurants, Lake Shore Drive and the Navy Pier (which was a sweet perk for runners like me). I will definitely be returning to The Palmer House.

title: “Great Location, Great Amenities”
text: We stayed three nights at the Doubletree. The hotel itself is clean and very well maintained and all the staff are extremely helpful and friendly -- always a smile! There were three of us in a double room (two queen beds and a large-screen TV) and the room was very comfortable. The location is very convenient and within walking distance of Magnificent Mile (Michigan Ave.), Navy Pier, John Hancock Observatory, Museum of Contemporary Art, to mention a few points of interest. Free WiFi is provided in the hotel lobby, but a fee is charged in the room. There are also many pubs and restaurants within walking distance.

title: “One Bad Holiday Inn, ALL BAD HOLIDAY INN”
text: Checked in Sunday, Checked out Sunday. An incident regarding my Priority Membership led to my ultimate departure and ties WITH HOLIDAY INNS Forever...For the last 3 months I've been livin' it up in and out of Hotels, of my getaways, Holiday Inn has been more than visted than others (6 times to be exact). Todays departure was based on bad behavior in part of front desk and manager on duty. I, as guest should be treated with respect in any manner or situation; but that was not the case today 11-18-12. Obviously, the situation was never resolved to MY SATISFACTION. I thought it was best to walk away. I no longer want to give MY Money wheather through HOTWIRE or walkin because of front desk and manager on duty...

title: “Great Staff and Location, Very SPG Friendly but Parking was a Problem”
text: This Westin had one of the best trained staffs I have ever seen. Kudos to a great manager! The front desk clerks were particularly good, asking all to the right questions and offering the right information before I even asked. Its location was right on the river and conveniently located near theaters, a large number of great restaurants and between two major shopping areas. As a Platinum SPG we had access to the club lounge which was good sized and had a lot or easy to eat at tables...the evening hors d'oeuvres were nothing special but the continental breakfast, while basic, was quite good and fast....even though the lounge seem to have been invaded by a sizable group of (very well behaved)young people who may or may not have belonged there. Our upgraded room really felt like an upgrade, being a larger corner room with a great view of the river. The parking was valet only and the most expensive ($52/24 hours) and slowest ( 25 minutes when expecting < 10minutes at 1:20 pm on a beautiful Sunday afternoon at time there were very few guests checking in or out) I have ever encountered.

title: “Good Experience”
text: Hotel is not that far from the Gaslamp, we took a taxi one way ($5) but walked back. Our room was on the 25th floor, corner room and had a great view of the Coronado bridge. Room was a good size and we liked the room divided between the bedroom and living room. We also had breakfast at the hotel dining room, food was good. I would recommend this hotel to others.

title: “Location is everything”
text:
I have just stayed at the New Yorker for 4 nights – 19 to 23 October. This was booked before I read some of the varying reviews here, and I have to say that your opinion will be dependant on your expectations.
If your preference is for the hotel to BE the holiday, then you may be disappointed. However, if the hotel is just a base for the holiday, then I don’t think you will be disappointed.
Firstly, the hotel is currently undergoing renovation, so expect some daytime construction noise – however if you’re in the hotel during the day, then maybe you aren’t doing it right? We had a double/double room on the 19th floor (myself, my wife and son). This was a refurbished room, and had clearly been two separate rooms at one point, as it had two bathrooms and two closets. It was very spacious and comfortable with two queen size beds and a large flat screen TV. Free wireless internet is available. Note that the rooms do not have tea/coffee making facilities, although I believe you can request it. Our room was on the north (35th Street) side and was so quiet that it was almost impossible to believe where we were – very little traffic noise was evident. The room position (see photo of floor plan) did mean that we had very little in the way of view though – again, we weren’t planning on spending much time in the room so it wasn’t an issue. If you want a view, request an upper floor room or one on a corner – I was told this costs an extra $30 per night. Two restaurants in the hotel – Coopers (which we didn’t try) and the Tick Tock Diner, which we used every morning – good food. Note, there are a lot of cheaper places for breakfast around (easy to spend $40-$50 for 3 people here), but it was convenient and the waffles were delicious!
The best thing about the New Yorker though, is its location. One block from Madison Square Garden and Macy’s. Two blocks from the Empire State Building. Times Square, Broadway, Grand Central, NY Public library, Rockefeller Plaza, Fifth Avenue, the Flatiron – all in easy walking distance. About 1 mile to Central Park. There’s a subway stop right at the hotel if you need to go further. Using Google Earth, I worked out that we walked 22 miles in four days there, although it didn’t feel as much as that. Walking around also felt very safe, even at night (more so than central London).
Some people have commented about rude and unhelpful staff at the hotel. I wouldn’t go that far, but some (especially front of house) could be described as being indifferent. Room cleaners and diner staff were better. I get the feeling that this is a general NYC attitude, as we came across it in several places. Get though their personal ”walls”, though and it gets better.
A couple of local eateries to try-
Andrews Diner (just west on opposite side of 34th) – Good basic food – apparently good for breakfast, but didn’t get a chance to try it.
Shutters Café (1 ½ blocks west on 34th) – excellent food, but don’t look too closely at the décor. Looks the sort of place the locals use.
Stagedoor (1 block south on 8th) – good food, large portions.
W Café (corner of 5th and 36th, so further afield but on a good route to places listed above) – the best sandwiches, etc, we found anywhere.
One general tip (as a first time visitor). Empire State is obviously a must, but the one thing you can't see of course is the ESB itself. Do it in the daytime, but then do the Rockefeller (Top of the Rock) at night. That way you get to see the ESB all lit up, and the overall view is arguably better.

title: “Nice looking lobby, terrible front desk”
text: When I made a reservation online, I got an eStandby Upgrade offer. When I asked an eStandby Upgrade, the front desk told me there is no guaranteed upgrade based on availability. I would need to pay $20 extra to upgrade to Executive floor even though they had Executive Floor rooms available. They didn't honor the offer, and she ended up assigning us a room right above three commercial air conditioning units (outside), out of the entire 22 floors in the building. Those machines never stopped running all night. With the terrible sound insulation, I couldn't fall asleep. What I want to say is that the front desk probably assigned a mediocre room to a customer who has snagged a lower rate. This hotel was not sold out that day (we made sure to check), contrary to what the front desk told us. I have been a Hilton Honors Silver member for years, this is the first time I have been treated badly like a free-nighter.

title: “Expo 2009”
text: After a last a minute decision, my boyfriend and I decided to go to Indianapolis for the weekend to catch the concerts at the Expo. To our surprise we were able to get a room at a responsible price. The front desk staff, Wanda, was extremely helpful with guiding us to the local activities. The room was spacious, clean and a great deal. We Loved it!!!

title: “Excellent location, helpful staff”
text:
Three friends and I stayed here Saturday night during a visit to Philly. The location couldn't have been better: right in the heart of the gay neighborhood, within walking distance to the city's gay nightlife and restaurants. I can't think of a better place to stay for the gay traveler.
A few other things I liked: the chocolate chip cookies at check-in; the fast response to my request for more towels; the friendly staff; the amazing corner view of the city from our room; breakfast buffet included in the price of the room.
A few things I didn't like: the elevator in the garage was very slow and small; the buffet had a lot to offer but the food was only OK; the tiles in the shower needed a little work. Mostly small quibbles.

title: “A solid stay at a Grande Dame... mind the renovations, though.”
text:
Stayed here for a three night stay with Mrs. Gardiner and Kiddo. Upgraded to a very, very nice suite.
We’d stayed here (all 3 of us) in 2005 for a large conference, and they needed a renovation then… Well, renovation now partially completed. (More on that later) Our room was terrific, well appointed and clean. Beds were comfy, and flat screen tvs were nice. 
That said, there were touch screen computers on the desks, and access to anything of value was behind a firewall. At check-in, I was given instructions for wifi (which worked great), but the desk computers are clearly designed to be little profit centres. Please, don’t throw fancy tech at me and then give me a choice between my tech for free or your tech for cost… you’re going to lose. I used the USBs for charging ports, but nothing more. Couldn’t even get weather on them… which I CAN get at a Courtyard…
Also, I was disappointed that in a 2-room suite there was NOT an in-room safe. You got two mini-bars and a dorm fridge in there, but no in-room safe. Big omission for a property of this caliber.
Then (and I write this first half of Dec 2011) they had only ONE restaurant open, and that was Kitty’s Pub… Either they have spent enormous amounts of money to hire Disney to engineer and recreate an authentic, dark, grungy, dirty, well worn Irish pub, or they have a dark, grungy, dirty, well worn pub that badly needs to be renovated. We ate there one evening, and certainly never went back… Kiddo had dinosaur chicken fingers and mashed potatoes… they didn’t even get those right. There were four adults and one Kiddo for dinner, and NONE of us finished our dinner. Jeepers. So, until they have other food options, be aware of this. (Nice looking restaurant reno across from Front Desk, but that’s only open for Breakfast, so you’re at their mercy for lunch/dinner) In short, a dire lack of in-house dining.
Nearby, I can verify that Eleven Deli (Wabash at 11th) was quite good, as was Tamarind (Asian, on Wabash, 200 feet from Hilton’s porte cochere ). Both are a short walk from the Hilton. (Of course, short walk is a relative term in Chicago in the winter…)
Concierge Lounge was reasonably nice. Evenings had two hot dishes and a full selection of soft drinks and coffees. Wine and Beer selections were available, although they never tell you precisely what wine they served. Also, $8.50 for a glass of unidentified Pinot Grigio was a bit steep when a very nice Kiwi Sauv Blanc was available in the lobby for $9. GM, please help me out here… make me feel like you and Hilton want me back.
Breakfast was Continental, with NO hots, no chafing dishes. Big bagel selection, variety of pastries and cereals… Fully acceptable, and the staff was friendly and helpful.
I did use the Parcel Shipping Center, and the gentleman there happily taped together two boxes for me, and wouldn’t charge me. Nice. Very nice.
So, this was our second visit to this Hilton property. Looks much nicer now, but the lack of restaurants is a serious drawback at this time… If eating in will be important to you, check what is open/finished there.
Would I return? Probably so. I’ve stayed at the Hyatt Regency, the Hyatt McCormick, the Sheraton, the Marriott, the Allerton, and so on. It depends on what I am doing and where I need to be. Yes, I’d go back, but if location was not an issue, I’d probably choose further North in the city. 
It was a good stay, not great... Maybe if F&B had been better, I could've gone with four stars.

title: “Great Service, Location and Setting”
text: For my birthday weekend, I reserved a room at Palomar Hotel. It was a blast. The overnight parking with unlimited in/out in a city is rare and the first set of great news upon arriving. They took my luggage, and gave me free drink tickets while the final touches were but on my room. The complimentary wine, truffle popcorn, and slice of chocolate cake made my check-in fantastic, and the room was amazing. The staff was friendly and helpful. On the day of my check-out, they held my luggage in storage while I strolled the local shops and had brunch. I can only hope that other Kimpton Hotels are as great as this one, since I am now a convert!

title: “Excellent, exquisite and lots of character!!”
text: This is a beautiful boutique resort with exceptional service and beautiful grounds. Everything is maintained and clean looking in every direction you look. The resort has a beautiful Spanish feel and is very romantic and floral. The resort fee covers all valet, bell service, concierge, etc so you don't have to worry about tipping everyone every time you need something. The staff is friendly and helpful. Get a room looking at camelback mountain on the third floor. The suites on this floor have beautiful day beds and soaking tub, steam shower and a separate room with king bed and TV. Perfect layout for couples. Can't say enough about the uniqueness and beauty if this place. I am so grateful we chose to come here! Wish we could've stayed longer.

title: “Great Beds/Remodeling”
text:
Hyatt Place is to be commended for re-branding the AmeriSuites. The rooms have the same floor plan and same small bathrooms as before - but all new furniture, carpeting, bedding, etc. I loved the comfortable bed, the living room "pit" furniture, the 42" flat-screen TV and the free WiFi. FREE PARKING!
However, I REALLY needed more drawer space. There are only two drawers to use - both in a small cabinet that makes up part of the bathroom vanity. I would remove the decorative shelves under the TV and add a shallow dresser for those of us who want to unpack for trips of 4+ nights.
If you plan to travel to San Antonio and want to be "on the Riverwalk" - please call ahead and talk to a member of the front-desk staff where you want to stay. There are many definitions of "Riverwalk" when booking a hotel in San Antonio. I'd stayed at this property in its' past life (AmeriSuites) and knew it's not on the main portion of the Riverwalk. But - it is VERY close to La Villita (street side) - a short two block walk. Pack your walking shoes and you'll be fine.
This hotel is also extremely accessible to the AlamoDome / IH 37 / IH 35 - something to keep in mind if you plan to attend any events there. 
The staff were all very friendly and were easy to spot in their Burnt Orange knit-wear tops. Someone was always available to help.

title: “Fabulous location but poor room sizes”
text:
Hotel Union Square Date: 10th Sept 07 
Reviewer: Carol - London UK.
Apologies for late review. Arrived from UK looking forward to our stay in the Hotel Union Square especially after seeing their website, extremely disappointed. We asked for a non smoking and quite room, we got room 425 on the 4th floor overlooking the car park, refuse to take this room, you could not swing a mouse let alone a cat in that room, it was the smallest closet I have ever seen, and the bathroom was smaller that a cruise bathroom. My husband immediately went to see about changing rooms, they then offerred us room 415 on the same floor - the bathroom was larger, the closet was walk in but still small just enough to put the cases in, but the room was still small, we had no drawer space hence had to live out of our cases. The coffee machine was on the top of the TV, but to make coffee the machine had to be placed on the floor because the flex wire did not reach the plug socket. The view from our bedroom was another guest's room, our windows were opposite each other so when they were in we had to close our curtains. The reception staff were helpful and friendly. But the location is excellent and right in the centre of everything. On leaving the hotel I asked how many of the rooms they had like the one on the website and the picture by the lift, the receptionist told me that they were doing up the rooms and the website is very misleading to guest booking that hotel. Would not ever go there again. The Trading Standards dept in San Francisco should investigate this hotel as it is totally misleading people who book this hotel.

title: “Moved 3 times”
text: I had never been to Chicago before and chose to stay at this hotel. I was promised an upgrade the day prior to checking in because of not being able to use my discount from work and no upgrade. The first room was dirty; bed not even made. The 2nd was a handicapped room, I'm 37 really, and the final room was just what I had paid for. I thought an upgrade by this time was indeed due. I went to Chicago to see my daughter who now goes to school there and I will be visiting quite often, I am now leery of where to stay. Are 4 star hotels really what they should be.

title: “Great Wedding Venue”
text: The Scott/Battle wedding was 6/4/2011. It was a beautiful event and I was very pleased with the wedding planning assistance from Peace Sanchez before she left the Wyndham. Gina Hengst did a wonderful job for us. Danita Matthews, Julius and the banquet staff were all outstanding. The professinalism and level of service we recieved made our wedding event the most memorable day imaginable. Our ceremony was spectacular and the Chef and banquet staff served a delicious dinner that our quests really enjoyed. I would highly recommend the Wyndham Jacksonville Riverwalk Hotel as a great wedding venue!

title: “Great Stay”
text: I headed to Charlotte for a game at Bank America Stadium and stayed here. The hotel is beautiful, the rooms are very clean and comfortable equipped w/a mini fridge and microwave. The bathroom was very spacious and clean. The front desk was very hospitable. The only issue I had was being told Bank of America Stadium was 15 minutes away when booking the room. It was longer than that, but it was still an enjoyable stay.

title: “Stay here!”
text: Skeptical about mixed online reviews of this hotel but booked room because it was affordable and convenient to event we were attending. Delighted with studio room #711 which has a view of the Empire State Building. Yes, we've had cleaner, newer rooms and softer bedsheets elsewhere at higher prices but this was comfortable and quiet and $159. The immaculate kitchen is well-equipped and offers standard range and refrig. We were surprised at how instantly we got cabs here, even at 6:30 a.m. but being next door to a huge medical facility probably explains that.

title: “A great place to stay and have a meeting”
text:
It's going on 5 years now that we've used the Westin New York Times Square for our corporate meetings and guest rooms. We love staying there...perfect location. They are just one block over from Broadway and Times Square which is great for 2 reasons. 1) It's right near everything!! 2) Because it's one block over, it's just a tad more peaceful. You've got the best of both worlds. Great views from the rooms too. Get yourself a suite, you'll be glad you did!!
Now for meetings, it's a great place to have a meeting or reception. There's a variety of meeting and ballrooms that can fit almost any need. The service is excellent and what you would come to expect from a Westin. The food doesn't disappoint either. The on sight restaurants and bar are great too and this hotel is attached to a movie theater with other restaurants as well.
We keep coming back!

title: “Comfortable and Fun- Great Value”
text:
I really enjoyed my stay at the Hard Rock Hotel in Chicago. The facilities were clean and elegant and the view of Michigan Avenue from our room added to the ambiance. The trendy lobby bar was a good place to relax, and the service at the desk was polite and timely.
The highlight of the stay for me was the room. It was a spacious room with modern decor. The beds were the most comfortable I have ever slept in. I truly melted when I laid down. The small touches added a lot - the guitar embroidered on the pillow cases, the CD player, the coffee machine, the bath robe, the huge shower... The only thing I can complain about is that the blow drier in the room didn't work. 
I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Excellent location, subway on doorstep, staff very friendly and helpful.”
text: You do not need a car in downtown Chicago. Traffic from airport terrible but can get to Homewood Suites from Terminal 3 at O'Hare on subway. Blue line to Jackson then Red Line to Grand. Exit right beside Homewood Suites. Subway on the doorstep is very useful. The suites cannot be described as luxurious but functional and have everything you need. There is also a guest laundry. Breakfast is very good. Supermarket just one block away. Lots of restaurants and shopping very close by. Easy walk to lots of attractions such as Navy Pier and River cruises.

title: “Good Location | Large room | Otherwise Average”
text:
Although the London NYC has received many good reviews, we failed to witness same. We booked through AMEX FHR program with an high expectation level set and unfortunately wished we had not. Yes, the location is excellent: Columbus Circle, Broadway, Fifth Avenue, Subway... All good. And Yes, rooms are larger than many in NYC, but overall we would have opted for a smaller room if the details were taken care of. Check in was like having your Miranda rights provided. I did ask for an upgrade which is available with the AMEX FHR, subject to availability, but no... this was not available... surprising for a hotel with some 500 rooms on 54 floors. We were given a room on the 15 floor. I was hoping for a room with a good view. We were told it was a larger room and, too, was a corner! So be it... Turns out the room was not a corner, not larger, and to disappoint even more so must have been the poorest view vantage available. We were just some 20 feet from an old residential building that wraps around the north and east corner of the hotel. So what are the odds of getting a low floor out of 54 and to worse view of which maybe only 20 out of 500 get. To add to the disappointment AMEX includes a promotional item explaining how we have received $450 with of benefit through booking with this program. What we got was an average well sized room, on a low floor, zero view and a "pardon me you are interrupting my day" check-in. We did receive complimentary breakfast (cold buffet) and "high" tea. The tea... not devon or clotted, but whipped... They provided one pot given we order the same English Breakfast and when asking for some more, provided more hot water with the same single tea bag. How many cups of tea do they expect to get out of one bag, only made more shocking that we were at a Afternoon Tea? And the scones... so dry they crumbled into many many pieces when trying split them to add jam. Not what I would have expected from a chef regarded as always seeking perfection. We decided not to make a reservation for his restaurant given this experience. The room... In need of some attention... Damaged furniture, worn carpet, needed new batteries for remotes, etc. Last item... Inconsistent "service" at the restaurant especially form the hostess.
We have many gold and platinum hotels loyalty cards... Shame we decided not to use them on this trip and settled for the London NYC. The problem is obviously not the staff, but the management to allow such mediocracy! It should be removed from the AMEX program and personally I would not choose to stay here again.

title: “Fantastic stay at the Waldorf Astoria”
text:
It is just an amazing experience ariving at the Waldorf. It is so steeped in history and we had a very warm welcome from the doorman to the reception area where we were checked in. Mary took us to the diamond reception for check in and Mary and her colleague Jackie were full of chat and entertainment and it was obvious there were happy to greet us and made us very welcome indeed.
Mary took our passports for checkin and I informed her that it was my wifes 40th birthday (although she doesnt look a day over 30 if you are reading this hon !). She promptly gave us a fantastic upgrade which was the perfect start to our break just after the long flight from Ireland.
We regularly used the concierge and they were always happy to provide us with all the information we needed and recommended a super restaurant for our second night there. 
The only part that was less than superb for me was the bar. We were told in books and by the hotel itself of the history and classic bull and bear bar that people came to visit from all around - found it very average myself - nothing to do with staff or drinks just found the bar to be average.
Location is fantastic with proximity to Central Park, Rockafeller Center, Times Square, shopping in 5th and Madison - list goes on.
Overall fantastic trip to New York and wonderful experience at the Waldorf. We'll be back.

title: “Great Location and well kept Days Inn”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Days Inn from 9-6 to 9-12. It was our first time to San Diego. The Days Inn was recently renovated. The furnishings were attractive and the window curtians and bedspreads were tastefully done. It was very clean. The room had a small fridge, coffee maker, hair dryer, and iron and ironing board. All the necessities to make the stay more comfortable. They have a restuarant on the premises, called the Pam Pam. We ate their many times at the end of a busy day of site seeing. It was very convenient. They have a pool and hot tub. We used the Hot tub each night, which helped relaxe and soothe us for a good nights sleep. The Days Inn is located near many of the more popular sites, Sea World, Zoo, Old Town, and beaches. Most were only a 5 to 10 minute drive away. If you don't have a rental car, the Days Inn does have a courtesy van, which will pick you up and take you back to the airport. They also have a shuttle van transport to Sea World and the zoo. There is a bus stop in front of the Days Inn for another way to get around town. The staff were always courteous and willing to help with any questions or problems that might arise. We would stay at the Days Inn again.

title: “Great place to get away from it all!”
text: The rooms have a great view and very relaxing. Lots of trails and activities to keep you fit.

title: “Comfortable and Spacious”
text: Comfortable appartment with more facilities than I use. Spacious site, not a horrible tower block. Eating and bars within reasonable walking distance. Good breakfast range but not much fresh fruit, some days only apples. Wish they would put tea bags in the rooms but you can get them from the breakfast area.

title: “Unbeatable views”
text: The Ren Cen is a cool hotel with a lot of history. It has all the amenities of a nice Marriott, a Starbucks and food court in the building, and is located right on the riverwalk (which is nicer in Summer than Winter). The views from upper floors are amazing - looking out the window at some areas with dark and dirty-looking buildings and other areas that have been rejuvinated - it makes me feel like I'm playing Sim City. And the San Diego Chargers were staying there, autograph hounds take note.

title: “Two nights in Seattle”
text: We booked a hotel package to visit the King Tutankhamun exhibit, selecting the Mayflower Park as our base. We weren't disappointed! This is an historic, refurbished hotel in an excellent location--a few blocks from Pike Place Market, in the thick of the shopping district, and connected to the monorail so very easy access to Seattle Centre. Every staff member we encountered was polite and friendly, and I was happy to get a room on one of the upper floors, as I had requested. The room itself was on the small side, but adequate, and very clean and tidy. I appreciated that as well as a desk, it had a comfortable armchair and good lighting for reading. I had been apprehensive about noise, being in this downtown location, but it was surprisingly quiet. My only small complaints would be that the pillows had a synthetic fill and weren't very comfortable; the TV was set up with closed captioning and we were unable to figure out how to turn it off (and the front desk was completely unhelpful); and the heating system was loud enough to wake us up every time it kicked on. We solved the last problem by turning it off at bedtime, and the room was then quiet and comfortably cool for sleeping. We enjoyed our stay very much.

title: “Decent rooms, good breakfast, friendly staff, great location”
text: We stayed at this hiexpress hotel in Old Town for a couple of days. The hotel is very conveniently located from Seaworld, Old Town trolley station and several fantastic Mexican restuarants in Old Town. The check-in was smooth, the front desk staff were courteous and helpful. The room was decent and clean, we got upgraded to a room with a jacuzzi. The hotel provides free internet and complimentary breakfast which I'd recommend. The best part of the hotel was that it provides drops through its shuttles to all locations nearby any time of the day until 11 pm. The only drawback of the hotel was its proximity to the freeway. Overall a good experience, would have expected better rooms for the price we paid.

title: “Older Hotel, but within walking distance”
text: It is an older hotel located on the end of the riverwalk, about a 10 minute walk from the main area. The parking was tight, and not enough spaces for the number of rooms. Rooms were small, but clean with fridge & coffee. Outdoor pool isn't heated, so don't count on it until April. Has a nice commons area with fireplace, couches, tables, and books.

title: “Don't recommend”
text: Arrived for a sports tournament on a Friday afternoon. Asked for 2 queen, was told by supervisor that none were available so checked into king room. Went online and found they had additional king rooms available. Went back down to desk to ask for additional king room. Was told there was a 2 queen room available by another employee which I was able to get. All this within 20 minutes. Rooms are sparse. No fridge or microwave, small desk. Asked for late checkout (additional hour) on morning of checkout. Told by supervisor wasn't possible as about 20 people had already asked. Informed her that I was a Gold Elite member which she said didn't make a difference. Next time will stay at Hilton Garden down street when returning to area.

title: “I was comfortable,and would stay here again w/out a doubt.”
text: I stayed here for 10 days while on a work assignment in downtown and surrounding areas,close to all,every night I walked to Trader Joes up the street a couple blocks no problems,nice brkfst every morning,free secure parking is a big ++as i had a car,kinkos not far for printing alot or use pc&printer @ hotel,free wifi,nice clean room w/fridge&micro.,staff was great. There was more shopping nearby like Nordstrom rack,bed bath & beyond,etc that could walk to just never got to it......

title: “No issues here”
text: For the San Antonio area, this was a nice place to stay without any hassles. The room was as expected, and the free internet and nice hot breakfast are really great complements. The facilities were clean, and the staff was friendly. It was a very comfortable stay without any issues. Great value for the money.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: This is a nice hotel which provides good value. Free dinner Mon-Thu was a nice extra. Breakfast was good. Parking was $25/night but that is lower than most Downtown DC hotels. Room was good, staff was nice. Only minor complaint I had was that the rooms did not have WIFI- you had to connect to the internet using a cord.

title: “Six days in Seattle”
text: Good location; helpful and knowledgeable desk staff and best of all, the room was clean, well-appointed and very comfortable. Easy access to public transportation...check out Westlake Station for trains ($2.50 to the airport) and buses to everywhere.

title: “4.5 stars for outside appearance, 3.5 for inside”
text:
We stayed in South Tower on the 16th floor for 3 days and I have mixed feelings.
First of all, I’d be upset to pay $300 per night for the cheapest room here because rooms are pretty outdated and bathrooms don’t have a ventilation fan (hello, 2007!). On a bright side, the hotel looks stunning outside and the view from top floors facing marina is amazing. 
The pool area is lovely but it gets overcrowded during day time because it’s not big enough for the size of the hotel. If you want to relax, come there after 6PM.
Mattress was too soft for me, but I guess many people like it to be soft. 
Small refrigerator wasn’t working and when I called front desk to inquire about it, they said that it wasn’t a refrigerator but a cooler and I could bring ice in it. I just don’t like when instead of accepting a problem, people try to make you look stupid. I know how refrigerator looks like and I can clearly read a label inside of it which says “refrigerator”. Well, you cannot blame Marriott for one rude front desk person, can you? ;)
When we checked in at 12PM, we didn’t have any problems; the guy at the front desk was courteous, polite and fulfilled my request of getting a top floor room and 2 beds instead of one. I don’t have any status with Marriott and I was quite impressed that they gave us a requested room that early.
Location is the best part about this hotel – it’s close to almost every major attraction in San Diego and proximity to Seaport village is a big plus.
Many reviewers mentioned train noise, which can be very annoying but I think that all neighbor hotels have the same problem. If it potentially maybe a problem for you, better look at different areas of San Diego or bring earplugs.
Overall, for $300 per night out of your own pocket it’s a rip off, but if it’s a corporate event =you’re paying $0) or you can get the room via discount hotel sites for +- $160 per night, go for it!

title: “The best hotel in New York City! I wouldn't stay anywhere else! :-)”
text: The entire staff, from Front Desk, to Doormen to Housekeeping Staff, are the best in the world! :-)

title: “Great Location!”
text: My sister in law and I stayed here for the Rock N Roll marathon. It was so convenient to the convention center and everything we needed was within walking distance. We were in the popular GasLamp District so we had plenty of restaurants and bars to choose from. We walked 2 blocks to the PetCo field and caught a baseball game one night. The light rail was 1 block away. The hotel had a cafe which was perfect for hot chocolate after the game. And of course, the accomodations were terrific. Although we didn't use the pool, it looked very comfy with the day beds. The only complaint, and this was our fault, as it is the Hard Rock... loud music into the night when we were trying to rest before our run the next morning. Oh well, we were too nervous to sleep anyway.

title: “Historically Perfect”
text: The Brown Palace Hotel & Spa is THE perfect place to holiday while you are in the Denver area. The historical significance, architecture and beauty-coupled with the modern amenities of the beautiful spa and dining make this property more than a hotel. It's a destination get-a-way on it's own.

title: “The worst ever - stay here at your peril”
text: This was booked on impulse as the hotel we were due to stay at we cancelled as we believed it was bad. This was even worse. If we had seen the reviews already posted would not have ventured near. The room was dark and hard to tell whether clean or not. The drawers had not been cleaned out and one was totally broken. The bedside cabinet drawer had receipts and leaflets from previous occupants. Opened candy was found on top of the TV unit. Several lights were not working which took two days to repair. Smoke alarm hanging off the wall. Several holes in the walls. Upon inspecting the bed lined body hair was found. All this was reported to the front desk. The cleaner finally arrived and did a few basics. It couldn't get worse we thought how wrong!! Over the next few days we were invaded by ants and bed bugs. Again this was reported and was dealt with as though it was just an everday occurence. Despite the room being sprayed the ants just continued to return. The pool well we looked and that was it as leaves floating in and didn't seem to have been cleaned for a while. Only one member of the front desk seemed to be concerned when problems reported. My wife physically went to reception to report problems as we did not trust them with taking telephone messages. On the third occasion they just said 'Ah room 206 isn't it' before she had even finished. On checkout I was presented with an invice which included a dailyutility fee of $2.00. When asked what this was for told it was a tax of some kind and he could not explain what for!!!!!!!!!! No way would we reyurn to this place even if offered free accommadtion. How Best Western can allow a property to be as bad as this is totally beyond me. I would say stay here at your peril.

title: “The most "washingtonian" place in town”
text:
I have had the honor and pleasure of staying at the Beacon Hotel about three weeks ago and I could not be more satisfied ! I do travel quite a bit and visit lots of hotels, but the Beacon Hotel & Corporate Quarters has really impressed me !
The Staff is extremely welcoming and friendly, the rooms, which are actually fully equipped luxury apartments, are complete with anything one could ever need or imagine. Breakfast and brunch are a memorable experience which I highly recommend. I have lived in Washington for many years and honestly can tell that this hotel truly is worth every penny. The location is superb, and the atmosphere is very washingtonian. If you are looking for a warm, friendly, yet upclass place to stay then the Beacon Hotel is it ! Cheers !

title: “A gem in Manhatten”
text:
SO glad we found this place! Reasonable rate for Manhatten. Only stayed here one night but wish we had stayed more. Had a room with a King bed. Entire hotel is clean and luxurious. Room was very comfortable. Walking distance to Guggenheim, Met, and Natural History Museums. Easy access to bus and walking distance to subway.
Location is very upper east Manhatten so it is on the far end of the downtown NYC action but with the transit systems in NYC it makes for a nice getaway location at the end of the day. Parking fee is also reasonable $20 for a 24-hour period.

title: “Cannot fault it”
text: Stayed at the hotel after reading other reviews. Perfect location - close to Beale st but we were on the 4th floor - non smoking - and never heard any noise. Rooms very clean. Beds exceptionally comfortable .Excellent hot breakfast. Business Centre for checking internet etc. saw the indoor pool but never used it. They say there is a parking charge but we never paid anything - may have been included in the room rate we had (included visit to Brookes Museum and an excellent lunch at the Museum restaurant - for only an additional $10 dollars. The value of the ticket was £35 dollars!) Cannot find fault with anything!

title: “Quirky place !”
text:
Our first stop on a California Road Trip. Hotel beds really comfortable and room very clean. Didn't use the restaurant so can't comment however they were happy for us to have a drink in there at the bar. Good quiet location, 30 min walk up/down hill to Fisherman's Wharf and a bus journey back kept the kids happy (17 &14 years) .
Japan Town is across the road with plenty authentic Sushi bars. All mod cons of internet/wifi, ipod docking and TV. Clean , comfy, hotel.

title: “Just awful”
text: I stayed here the night before a sports event in San Jose. They put me in a smoking room which smelled awful. The floor was gross and the bathroom had mold on the walls and ceiling. The previous guest's cell phone charger had been left behind. The kitchen appliances were noisy and the microwave was precariously placed on top of the fridge. When I checked out in the early morning, a group of police were there interviewing someone in the lobby! I didn't feel safe or comfortable all night. When I returned home, I came down with the flu. I would never stay there again!

title: “We loved this place”
text: I stayed at this hotel June 18-21 and thoroughly enjoyed it. The staff was knowledgeable about the area and activities going on. They told me the best times to get on the interstate and when I might want to avoid them. I asked for directions to a restaurant and they gave me a special coupon for a free item there. My check-in was quick and efficient and I was greeted by the staff and asked how my stay was going every time they saw me.The room was very clean and had no faults that I noticed and I took pictures to prove it. I read a review that said not to walk at night but I did and felt completely safe at all times. There is a charge for parking, but it is half of what it costs to park elsewhere downtown. I would recommend this hotel to anyone and especially family's looking for a place to explore downtown San Antonio.

title: “Nice business hotel”
text: Nice clean airport hotel next to LAX. The breakfast in the hotel is excellent and was the best I had for a month,when I was in the US.

title: “Great staff, great breakfast, great location”
text: This is a great hotel. We were kidding the staff at checkout that we didnt get cookies on Sat. & Sunday evening. Went to breakfast and the morning manager, John had cookies baked especially for us. Staff is very conscious of the needs of their customers. Hotel is directly across the street from the Bank of American Football Stadim. Very convenient is you are planning to go see the Carolina Panthers - may be very loud if you are not planning on seeing the game. Within walking distance of uptown Charlotte. Charlotte is a great city to visit

title: “Great Rooms and Service”
text: Each time we are in El Paso, we choose to stay at the Amerisuites. The facility is clean, the staff is friendly and always is willing to accommodate your needs with a smile. They serve an above average continental breakfast with several choices. In the evening, they have popcorn available for the guests and complimentary coffee, tea and cocoa. The location is superb, not too far away from the airport and Ft. Bliss, the main highway is right in front of you and the area is very easy to maneuver. The beds are always comfortable and if you need extra towels, pillow or blanket, they are always willing to accommodate you. We stay at least 2-3 times a year and each stay is always good.

title: “Great stay-Apart from Fire Alarm and internet!”
text:
We stayed as a family of 4 from the 11/8 till 14/8 and on the first night was awoken at 5.30am by the fire alarm, which when we finally made it down 9 floors there was little or no co-ordination or information, after some 20 minutes we were told it was a false alarm! On finally making our way down to breakfast again no apologise or explanation, so after going to the front desk and enquiring i was given a complimentary breakfast voucher. It was while sitting at breakfast that we over heard this had happened for the previous two nights and was down to a faulty control board!! 
I am glad to say that it did not happen the next three nights, but we had continual problems in room 914 with no WI-Fi, despite the management informing us daily that it had been fixed?
Overall the hotel was very comfortable and in a good location and they offered us assistance in providing transport to Cape Cod which was excellent.

title: “Great location, although a bit tumultuous”
text: The hotel has excellent location and amenities in the vicinity are great. The movement is that ends up messing up a bit by the uproar caused, mainly with the works at the hotel. But the service provided at reception by the official Marcelo is impeccable and made it much easier for everyone. It would be hard to imagine a stay so enjoyable without the staff, polite and always attentive to that.

title: “Great location. Clean room. Great view.”
text: We were checked in by a man named Angel. He was very nice. We told him that it was our first time visiting NYC. He noted that the room that we were scheduled to have had been having hot water issues, so he got permission to upgrade us. He told us that the view would be "the best". Boy, was it! Great view, hotel room overall clean. The bathroom was clean, but old. Very basic bathroom tub/shower combo, pedestal sink, toilet next to a paper thin lockless door. No fan in the bathroom either. So muggy and hot for a while after everyone showers. Really though, the bathroom was functional and clean, so I was fine. The hotel itself was huge. I wish there was a doorman @ all times. The rotating door was out and we were fighting suction/winds just to get a door open. Angel is the only staff member that we encountered on our 4 day/3 night stay, which to me is odd, but at least he was friendly! Nearby...Drugstore on the opposite corner for anything you forgot. Lucy's outdoor bar also on opposite corner had great drinks and a quick bite of food.

title: “Very Good Value And Location”
text: This hotel offers a cheap option in a central location just off Union Square. The staff were freindly and very helpful, the rooms were small but clean and the bed comfortable. The complimentary breakfast of juice, coffee, toast, and muffins was adequte rather than paying 10 dollars each morning. I was wary because of the price i paid but had no complaints and wouldnt hesitate to stay here again. I only encountered a couple of homeless people near the hotel most seemed to be on Powell Street and were no problem at all.

title: “Cool stylish and very retro.”
text:
First things first: I like this hotel! I really really like this Hotel. Reminds me of "The Overlook Hotel" in Stephen King's "The Shining" (without the twins, the scary elevators and so forth).
The hotel is dark, charming, has a great big bar with a roaring fireplace, pooltable, internet access and a friendly staff.
I've read some reviews that the rooms are too small. Get Serious! I found it to be spacious, the bathroom was really cool.
All in all - I am coming back to The Doubletree Artic Club.
one small thing though.... from friday to monday morning, the streets around the hotel are very quiet and not many people around. Within two minutes you can walk to a busier area on 1.st and 2. ave - but if an empty street makes you anxious, and you are visiting in the weekend, you might want to find another place further uptown.
But let me say it again - The Doubletree arctic Hotel in Seattle ROCKS!

title: “would never stay here again!”
text: We had an insufficient amount of towels, washcloths daily and had to call for more, one day NO washclothes were left. Air conditioning insufficient. We finally put the thermostat on 60 so get the room to a tolerable level and we never put the thermostat that low before. Dining room and wait staff were rude. One waiter ran our bill on another diner's credit card and then refused to give us a copy of the void slip. This was reported to management. Dining room was slow to get our order and we were told they were not expecting this many guests until the next day. However, reservations were in the computer and I feel sure the dining room staff had access to it.This hotel is NOT on the river as the name would have you believe. We were told by a hotel staff person not to use the elevator to the riverwalk as it was unreliable. However it was reliable. No newspaper delivered to the room as stated on website. I will never stay in this hotel again. It does not deserve a 4 diamond rating and is very over priced.

title: “Alright, but be prepared for........”
text:
Let me say that this hotel is not all that it seems in either the ads or in what you are told. It will be simpler if I just list what our pros/cons were:
1. Deluxe Suite: Nice sized bedroom with comfy bed, but the sofa bed in the living room area was NOT COMFORTABLE for adults, but would be adequate for acouple of young children. We had 4 adults/2 couples and a baby. So do not expect to have really comfortable sleeping arrangements if you are planning on having 2 adults take the bedroom and 2 take the sleeper sofa. It is only about 3 inches off of the floor when you are sleeping on it, and not easy to get out of, and just does not sleep comfortably.
No airconditioning in the bedroom, just a window that opens out to a VERY VERY NOISEY court from the German restraunt next door. So if it was warm weather and one couple shut the bedroom door, you would not get the air conditioning into the bedrroom, as it is in the living room, and you would be uncomfortable. The noise down below goes until 1 or 2 am, and we heard other people mentioning the fact that the noise was an 
issue.
2. They did give us a really nice crib for 1 yr. old baby, but if you would need that, be prepared to have to squeeze it in somewhere, because there is not much room in the bedroom and with the sofa bed out, there is not much room there, either.
3. They have a "limo" service that is very handy and will take you anywhere you want to go with just afew minutes notice. The cost is reasonable, and during busy rush-hour traffic with a taxi meter ticking, this is probably a less-expensive way to get from Soho to Midtown.
4. There is a brand new "Whole Foods" Super market within about 2 1/2 blocks walking distance. It was very handy. There is also a very classic NY neighborhood market 1 block over that is not always open, but open during the day for pop/soda (which Whole Foods does not sell), chips, and other things you might need.
5. We had a place with our own bath (Deluxe Suite). The bath is a good size. It was a chore to get towels/washclothes for 4 people. When we asked we got them, and enough to do all of us.
6. Don't expect "maid service". There is a charge for your room to be serviced. We were there for 4 days, made the bed up ourselves, but some sweeping/vacuuming would have been nice.
7. The kitchen in the suite was great. Micorwave, full stove and 
fridge. Silverware, pots and pans, dishes, glasses. We cooked in the room afew times and it saved us money. 
All in all I would say if you can handle the noise, probably sharing a bath if you don't get a big suite, want somewhere that can get you were you want to go if you choose not to taxi or use subway, and are ready for classic NYC walking and want to be down in Soho, this would be a good place. I imagine the prices are about the same as other places, no better, no worse. It is a'
place you could depend on to be clean and safe.

title: “Wonderful cozy place!”
text: I was here for just one night while we did some siteseeing in DC. It's definitely a smaller boutique hotel geared for adults, not families. At the reception desk, the staff was very friendly and invited us to the wine and cheese hour. We already had other plans and therefore did not take advantage of this. I loved the bathroom with the wonderful dual showerheads. We appreciated that when the curtains were closed, almost no sunlight came in, allowing us to sleep in. I wasn't able to get wifi access working despite the fact that they gave me a card with the password upon checkin, but I did not pursue trying to speak with the staff to figure out why I couldn't log on. I would definitely return here in the future.

title: “24th Anniversary was great”
text: Recently stayed here with my wife to celebrate our anniversary. Hotel staff upgraded our room once they found out. They even sent up a complementary chocolate desert! Valet pointed out a spot on the street I could park in so as to avoid the $40 overnight fee. Package included breakfast for two in their restaurant--it was really amazing all the food we were offered. Cooked to perfection. Workout facility was very nice also.

title: “Great Experience”
text:
I was in New York to move my daughter into her residence for school for the summer. It was a great location in Midtown. Rooms are large enough and very clean. Check in staff were friendly and very helpful.
Valets were also excellent as we had are car and we were moving in and out a lot and the car was brought up very quickly. Lounge was lovey and staff were very nice. Overall stay was wonderful and we had everything we needed. Great location easy to get around the city on foot or by car.Would come back anytime.

title: “Great experience - will return when I'm in DC!”
text: I went to DC for a weekend trip with some friends. It was Howard Homecoming weekend, so prices were high, but we were able to catch a great deal at the Topaz. I am a huge fan of Kimpton hotels in general, but this one definitely takes the cake. The hotel decor is fabulous, the room was spacious and well kept, and the staff provided impeccable customer service. From receiving an email from the hotel manager even before check in to make sure I was all set for my stay, to the wonderful comfort of the hotel, it was definitely a great experience. The location is fantastic - in the heart of DuPont Circle so easy access to restaurants and the metro. Parking can be a challenge (we had a rental car) but we were able to find spots within 10 minutes or so. I'll definitely be staying here next time I go to DC.

title: “Nice hotel to stay”
text:
A friend and I stayed at this hotel in mid-May. The room was small but functional. We got clean sheets & towels everyday. We did not have a view on the park but that was okey. Reading the reviews about the noise at night got me a bit worried but we did not have any problems. No noise whatsoever. Staff was friendly & helpful. The room could use some new paint though.
The nearest subway is on 103rd street, maybe a 3 minute walk. I'd stay there again.

title: “Nice place to return to after an exhausting day visiting NYC”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights on my first visit to NYC, and I was very satisfied with the choice I had made (it had taken me quite a long time to find something decent and half-way affordable): It's location is very convenient (next to the subway station Lower East Side 2 Av, different restaurants and delis nearby), the place was really calm and quiet during my stay (though you could hear the traffic in the room that had its window facing East Houston street), the room was not huge but very clean with a fancy bathroom, the staff friendly, free wi-fi that worked, and a great view of the city from the roof. Breakfast (included) was ok (a buffet with a choice of cereals, yogurt, bagels, cheese, orange juice, coffee - you have to make do with styropore cups, plastic knives and paper plates) though the room in the basement doesn't make you feel like staying there longer than necessary. Cost: almost 600 US$ (taxes included) for 2 nights, not exactly a bargain, but apparently that's what you have to be willing to spend in NYC...

title: “Great for business travel”
text: Stayed here twice on business travel. Very nice place in great location. Rooms are large and nicely appointed. Staff is extremely courteous and professional. Location is great and close to many restaurants. There is a movie theater across the street as well. Liked it so much I stayed there on my second visit and brought my wife along. It is a little pricey but you get what you pay for.

title: “Complete Satisfaction!”
text:
My family passed through New York on our way to a wedding, and we decided to spend one night in the Mid-town area to catch a Broadway show (Phantom of the Opera) to celebrate our wedding anniversary! (I know... didn't have a choice, we had to bring the kids with us...) We chose the Westin NY at Times Square mostly bacause of the overwhelming number of positive reviews at this site!
Well, let me tell ya, they were well deserved, and I'll add our vote to the list! We had an amazingly satisfying experience! We do have a couple of nit-picks, which I will go into later, but they were insignificant in comparison to our overall positive impression of the hotel and its services.
