The hotel is ideally located for anyone who plans to visit Times Square and/or catch a Broadway show while in NY! (Is there any tourist/visitor who doesn't fit this profile?!) It's a small city block away from several major Broadway theaters, and one large block away from Times Square...close enough for an easy short stroll, even in a drizzle like we had, and far enough away to not be affected by the bright lights and loud noises! I think it took us 3 minutes to walk from the Westin to the theater for Phantom. Also, we had a rental car, but for guests who don't, there's a subway station right next to the hotel, and the Port Authority is 1 small block away! It can't get any more convenient!
When I made our reservation, I had requested an early check-in and a room with 2 beds. So, upon our arrival in NY, I called the front desk to check on the room availability and was very pleasantly surprised that they had upgraded us to a corner deluxe king room!! Unfortunately, we couldn't take advantage of it because it only had 1 king bed... (It was my fault, I didn't change the default "1 Adult" when I made the reservation.) But, alas, the front desk clerk quickly found a room with 2 beds for us. The room wasn't cleaned yet, so we drove to the TKTS office to pick up our show tickets and had lunch before calling the hotel again. This time our room was ready! Even with the room change, we were still able to check-in about an hour before the standard 3 pm check-in, so it was early, just not as early as we had hoped. But, the front desk lady was very friendly and helpful in rearranging our rooms and apologizing for the delay!
When we finally drove up to the hotel -- my first nit-pick -- none of the door men were friendly. They were efficient in unloading our car and welcomed us to the hotel, but it was spoken like a recording without warmth or even a smile. But everyone else at the hotel during our short stay were friendly, courteous and helpful! In fact, when we found out my daughter left her doll on the car, the bell boy, who was busy unloading luggages in our room, quickly called downstairs. Unfortunately, our car had already been driven away to an independent parking garage a block away. If we were to ask the garage to return the car, they would've charged us another $40 parking fee again!! So, the bell boy volunteered to show me the location of the garage. Thankfully, I was able to retrieve that #%@&ing doll before all hell broke loose...
Our room was located on the 40th floor with a huge window facing toward the Times Square direction!! What an amazing view of the city skyline!! We can even see the pedestrians and the neon lights of Times Square in between the buildings. But, it was surprisingly quiet because we're so high up. The street noises were very muffled and barely audible. As my wife said, we couldn't have asked for a better room location!!
The room itself was very clean, modernly decorated and furnished. It was very spacious by NY standard. Even with kids and luggages, we didn't feel cramped. My wife loved the iPod dock on the stereo alarm unit! There is a big LCD TV, but we didn't try it because of our short stay and the Phantom show. Last, but not least, the 2 Westin Heavenly beds were soooooo comfortable that we just had to order one yesterday after we got back home!!!
The bathroom was highly functional and roomy as well! My kids loved the 2 sprayer shower head! They thought it was the neatest thing. But, that brings up my 2nd nit-pick. The counter space in the bathroom was too limited and too shallow. My kids accidently tipped a bottle of lotion on the counter, and it fell into the toilet below. As many of you know how young kids are, sometimes they don't flush... Let's just say, it wasn't pleasant...
Oh, the biggest surprise of our stay was the room service delivered a complementary bottle of champagne and 5 chocolate covered strawberries to help celebrate our anniversary!!! WOW! We were shocked!! My wife and I had to pick our jaws up from the floor when we found out!! Afterwards, we were giddy with that generous and considerate gesture!! (or, maybe it was the champagne that made us giddy...)
Oh, oh, to top it off, I got an email from the hotel customer service apologizing for mixing up our room and not having it ready when we arrived into NY. As a gesture of their concern, they have credit my Starwood account with 5,000 points!! All I can say is what else can a hotel guest expect and ask for?!!! It's been one incredible experience of exceptional customer service! I must take my hat off to Maryanne, Westin's hotel manager, who have made our stay so special and memorable! I know where my family will stay in our future visits to NYC!!

title: “Good hotel in the heart of the historic district”
text:
We stayed here for a 2-day trip to Philly to see some of the historic sites. The hotel is OK but it could use a bit of freshening up. The lobby and room carpeting looks a bit worn. The staff was helpful. My kids liked the rooftop pool. I used the 2 day package from http://www.visitphilly.com which included free parking. 
The hotel is within walking distance of the Liberty Bell, Independence Hall, Constitution Center and other sites. There are also many restaurants nearby within walking distance.

title: “Great location”
text: I always choose this hotel when staying in chicago. Like any W Hotel,you don't stay here if you are looking for a quiet ambience. The bar at night is always raucous , and there is a buzz and fun vibe about the place. The hotel has fantastic views of the lake. The staff are always welcoming. W has to have one of the most comfortable beds in the world!

title: “Go For It!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel from August 20 to August 31, 2010. I have no complaints other than that one of three elevators was down for the last day or so of our visit, making it a bit of a wait to go up or down. That's it! Pictures of the room are posted for your review. The room and bathroom were kept very clean, to me the most important thing of all! Toiletries (shampoo, conditioner and moisturizer) were replaced daily as needed - never had to ask. Nothing was lacking - we had a fridge which we used a lot, a microwave and coffee maker which we didn't use at all, a chair with ottoman for reading and a great T.V. The bed was so comfortable I slept through the night - most unusual for me. I loved the duvet and pillows. Despite previous postings of noise from the fire station down the block we weren't bothered, maybe because we live downtown and are used to City noises. All the staff were friendly and helpful and we encountered no "attitudes". The breakfast was adequate and we were able to get seats the times we did go down. You can get coffee anytime. There is a business centre with free internet so you can Google or print off your boarding pass. We didn't use the pool so I can't comment on that. The cost of the room was $149.00 per night plus tax.
One of the things I liked best about this hotel was the location. It is about a 4-5 minute walk from the Grand stop on the red line. We were even able to use the transit system to take the El from the Airport to the hotel by taking the blue line to Jackson, and then transferring to the red line to go north to Grand. It worked with no complications other than that I have to get a lighter suitcase for myself...a younger, stronger person would have no problems. We bought a weekly pass for the El and used it to go everywhere - Andersonville, Chinatown, Oak Park, Bucktown, etc. etc. The hotel is also an easy walk to the Magnificent Mile and the Loop. As for restaurants and cafes, there are many in the immediate area. Some I would recommend are Lou Malnati's, Portillo's and Ed Debevic's. The place we enjoyed eating at the most was Ann Sather's (Swedish) in Andersonville. In the end result, there's no shortage of things to do in Chicago and I 
would go again anytime, booking at this Hampton Inn.

title: “Insanely good price- great location-wonderful staff-will stay again and again”
text:
I stayed 2 nights at the Gem Soho (not really anywhere near SoHo) 13 &14 March. I was in NYC for a music festival that was held 2 blocks down the street. What can I say. I spent $145 a night in Manhatten. GREAT DEAL! Lovely room, small, but expected. CLEAN. Incredible front of house staff who were funny, kind, helpful and seemed to really enjoy working at this hotel. We had a room facing the park, street noise wasn't anymore than I would expect from a hotel on a street as busy as Houston. You can walk anywhere from here. Very convienient to subway stops. 
*Only complaint, they ran out of coffee packets for in room service and only had decaf. ummm, nope, that wasn't so cool. No coffee for the whole stay. Though plenty of great cafes within blocks. 
I also wish the drapes could have closed to add more room darkening. The pull down shade didn't quite black out. I am not complaining though. I will stay there again and again for the good rates, the wonderful staff, immaculate rooms, and great location. GOOD JOB GUYS! (also if you are there visit the Local 269 a great pub just a couple blocks away at 269 E. Houston. You will be made to feel at home here.)
The GEM SoHo is a hidden gem. Hopefully the next time I will be able to get such a great rate!- Oooh, also right next door is a knishery, super yummy!!!!

title: “Horrible place!”
text: Horrible place! I made my reservation for a single room a month before going there (unfortunately!). When I reached the place, they first denied that they have a reservation. I was jet-lagged and with my baggage, and she finally asked me to wait for 3 hours before they can clean up a room. The staff were rude and misleading. The water wasn't draining through the sink! The room was dirty. Never had a worse experience at an inn or hotel in the US. Not worth a dollar paid for.

title: “Good Hilton.”
text: Stayed there for one night, everything was very efficient but not extraordinary. Room was large, bed comfortable, but internet speed was terrible. Good location downtown, this makes it easy to walk to good restaurants in the area.

title: “Wonderful Way to Experiance Downtown Denver”
text: The Hyatt Regency at the Colorado Convention Center is a quiet refuge in a busy city! I was very impressed by the kindness of everyone we encountered. The room was classy, clean and comfortable. The food was filling and incredibly tasty! And the massage was fantastic. Everyone is respectful, as well as friendly. And it's a block from the 16th Street Mall, well within walking distance, which is nice! We parked ourselves at the Hyatt, then walked the mall up and down without worry about a meter running out! One little tip: Spring the extra $4 for vallet parking to make your visit just that more luxurious!

title: “One of the best hotels stayed while travelling 3 weeks in the US”
text: We travelled 3 weeks in the US in various states ending in San Fran. The 4 nights in the Hyatt hotel rated as some of the best. The staff were very friendly and professional in all aspects. The rooms were clean, comfortable and big enough to sleep 4 easily. There was no fridge in the room which may bother some people, us not!. The location close to the Fishermans wharf, and next to the end stop of the Tram, was perfect.

title: “Great resort”
text: My husband, six year old son and I spent 5 days at the resort from Oct 1-5. Request a room in the Falls Village area, our room overlooked the pool and it was close to the hiking trails. The room was recently renovated and we enjoyed having a seperate sleeping area. The resort overall is very nice. The concierge and all staff friendly and helpful. The Pointe in Tyme restaurant had great food and service. We also went to the Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak, our son enjoyed the Lazy River and the Water Slide. Nearby is a Walgreen's, McDonalds, grocery store and restaurants. Overall it was a wonderful vacation.

title: “Great hotel in an awsome location”
text: Stayed there with a friend for a spur of the moment fun trip to NYC. Picked the hotel over the internet, so we were a bit apprehensive. We were extremely pleased with our accommodations. Yes, the room was a bit small, but space was well used and it worked fine for us. And the rain shower was awesome! Location being 1 block from the "bleachers" on Times Square, it was safe walking at night for 2 women. The staff was absolutely the best! - friendly, personable, and always ready to help with whatever our needs. The Continental Breakfast was very nice. We could go down and get quick breakfast and be on our way. I would definitely stay there again!

title: “Nice grounds and history, surprised by the steep resort fee”
text: Stayed at the Biltmore for one night and was excited to see and experience the history associated with the place. The grounds are nicely maintained, rooms well-kept and clean. We found the service to be very good, but our perception of the stay was significantly affected by the $28 resort fee. Probably would not stay there next time.

title: “Not a great experience”
text:
My experience at the Palmer House Hilton was terrible. Although I was there for a conference, my family was with me. The room was small and offered only two double beds. The bathroom was tiny, not even offering the rounded shower curtain rod to help the shower feel larger. 
For the conference, which was suppose to be a team building experience, the set up had the participants sitting classroom style, instead of with round tables, which would have made it more conducive for conversations with colleagues. 
For the conference luncheon we were jammed in a hallway with 8 people rounds, but they were set for 10 place settings. The wait staff were rude and rushed us out of there. 
As for my room, the air conditioner was not working properly. Upon returning to my room with my family one late evening, I found it was warm and stuffy. I called the front desk to see if there was a maintenance man available at this late hour (12:40am). She said yes and assured me he would be right up. I clearly asked, "He will be up right away? If not, we can do this in the morning. It is late and I have children I would like to get to bed." She said yes. By 1:10am, I called back down and cancelled the maintenance man, stating it was too late and we could handle this in the morning. The front desk lady told me she could send up a fan, however I declined again stating it was too late. At 1:25am, the maintenance man came to our door - even after canceling the call. I begrudgingly let him in. He bumped the air controller down to 65, bent a couple of vent slats downward with a screwdriver, and claimed the fan was not on but it should be fixed now. The room continued to feel warm even with the air set at 65 for the 2 days my family and I stayed. 
Our final night here, I returned from a baseball game and went to the lobby bar/restaurant for a late meal. The bartender stated the kitchen was open until midnight, so I still had about half an hour. I contacted a server, and stated that I wanted to order food to take back up to my room. He told me to go up to the room and call down the order and it would be brought up to me. I explained that my employer would not reimburse extra fees, and that I just wanted to order a sandwich and bring it up. He again stated to order from the room and there would be no extra charges. I went back upstairs to my room and called down. The person taking the order now stated that there would be a 18% gratuity, a 3% service fee, and a $2.00 delivery charge on the order!!! I went back downstairs with the in room menu that also stated these charges and showed it to the server. He did not really say much, but acknowledged the charges. When I tried again to order, he said he would have to check to see if the cook was still available. It was now 11:50pm. He and another server came out and said that food was no longer available for the night.
With the exception of the maid service staff and the doormen, every other employee made me feel like I was burdening them with my questions and that they did not have time to assist me. 
My family and I will never return to the Palmer House Hilton. We stayed at the Marriott Renaissance Downtown for the remainder of our trip, for less, and had a fabuous time! They offer larger rooms, two QUEEN beds, hospitable staff, and an overall much better experience for downtown Chicago.

title: “Breakfast at Zocca”
text: Went to have breakfast at Zocca Monday, May the 28th for my brother birthday, our waiter was Angel and Chef Nati Moreno was very accommodating, pleasing and gave great service with a smile all the time. Angel our waiter was also very pleasant and quick to give service. Once they knew why we were there Chef Nati and Angel surprised us with a small cake for the birthday guest, my brother. That was just over the top of what we where expecting but it was very thoughtful. Had a wonderful time and have been recommending it to all my friends. Great job Westin!!

title: “Thumbs up for the San Carlos Hotel”
text: We enjoyed a relaxing week-long stay at the San Carlos Hotel. The location couldn't be beat (walking distance to 5th Avenue shops, wonderful 2nd Street restaurants, theatre, etc.). The frontdesk staff and doormen were friendly and provided excellent recommendations to nearby restaurants. The only complaint was the extra firm bed that bothered our backs. But when you're in New York, who has time to sleep!

title: “Best Hotel in Downtown Dallas”
text:
I stayed here on a weekly basis during this summer for business purposes. I've tried a few of the other alleged 4-5 star hotels and those that are rated higher here on TripAdvisor and I cannot understand why Ritz-Carlton is ranked so low. The other hotels, quite frankly, are not comparable. The Four Seasons in Irving is the only other comp but the location is completely different.
The drawback I've found at this particular Ritz is the front desk hotel staff. Arguably the worst front desk hotel staff at any Ritz-Carlton globally I've stayed at (I stay between 30 - 50 nights at Ritz-Carlton globally per year). However, since I try to minimize the amount of time I'm at the front desk, it's not a real issue for me here.
The rooms are nice and just what you would expect for a city Ritz-Carlton in the U.S. Location is quite good with many good restaurants within walking distance (although it's insanely hot to walk around in Dallas during the summer). The gym and pool are also quite nice and very good for a hotel. Service in other areas of the hotel, including the spa and fitness center, was very good. The in-hotel restaurant is also excellent, definitely worth a try. 
Hope this helps!

title: “Wonderful beds and great location, service a bit "if-y"”
text: This trip was my daughter's birthday present. The two of us were there the weekend of February 5th. I reserved a room with a view so we were on the 43rd floor. I'll start by saying the beds are extremely comfortable. Our room was very clean, nicely decorated and the location was great. We were only a few blocks from the theater and a couple of blocks from Times Square. I would not say the staff was friendly. When we asked one of the guys at the front door desk what subway we needed to catch to get to China Town, he seemed annoyed by the question. Our second night there the guest in the room next to us was very loud. At about 1:00 in the morning I'd had enough and called the front desk. No-one answered the phone the first time. So, I tried again and someone finally answered but she didnt' realize she'd taken the phone of the hook and so I got to listen to her private conversation with another hotel employee. When I finally got her attention and I explained the problem she said she'd send someone up. When the loudness next door didn't get any better after another ten or fifteen minutes, I called again and needless to say I was a bit upset. I told her that I didn't understand why I could hear every single word in this guy's conversation. She apologize and said they'd already sent someone up and heard nothing. Maybe the guy was on the phone and took a breath. She finally sent a security guy up and he came to our door and asked what the problem was. I explained it again and he finally went next door and very politely I must say, asked the guy to please keep it down. And thankfully he did. I chose this hotel because of the great reviews here and I must say I was a bit disappointed. I may give it one more try. We also had breakfast at Shula's which was a bit pricey but definately worth it.

title: “Perfectly Small in a Big City”
text:
In large cities choices abound, and sometimes the best are the smaller boutique hotels that combine the cities history and accomodations enjoyed by a much larger upscale hotel. Hotel Burnham does both beautifully. Never thought you'd want to stay 24 hours at the office - but even though this hotel has retained this historical office feel and unique look - it is what a hotel should be clean, comfortable, spacious and inviting. Rooms are ample, baths are spacious. Housekeeping is top notch. Staff is excellent, the hotel sweats the details for coffee morning service in the lobby (even putting out a spread of donuts, croissants, muffins and juices when the restaurant (very popular) was closed for breakfast due to the holiday.
Location is excellent to several El lines within blocks, shopping, Millenium Park, the theatre district, numerous restaurant and pizza choices and Sugar Bliss cupcakes!!! Yea!
Excellent value - interior architecture and design feels like your living Mad Men. Beautiful!

title: “Clean, comfortable, and at a great location!”
text: The hotel is really close to the North Station and Haymarket metro stations...the main attractions of Boston are only few stops away and some are at walking distance. I just wanted to hang out and see the city and didn't wanna spend a lotta $$ so this hotel gave me exactly what I was looking for. Do not expect glamor but a nice, clean and comfortable place to stay at good price!

title: “Great historic hotel”
text:
We were very happy with this hotel. The staff was friendly and accommodating. After requesting an upper floor during check in, we were extremely happy with our room location (7th floor over looking a small garden). Hotel building is shaped like a "U' our room overlooked the center of "U" not on the street. After reading numerous complaints re: noise level we were quite surprised that the room was extremely quiet. Once or twice we heard sirens from a firetruck...but one must remember that downtown San Diego is located in a city not the country. The rooms were a nice size and were updated with a mix of contemporary and historic decor. We really liked the bathrooms, the shower doors and travertine tile gave the shower a clean look/feeling
Restaurant row in the Gaslamp Distict is about a 5-6 block walk. I had no problem walking in high heels to and from...As with any city there are some homeless people but no one bothers you nor asks you for money. There seem to be a fair amount of police patrol cars around the Gaslamp District so safety never seemed to be a factor. We decided to forego the hotel parking and found a $10 a day lot around the corner.
I would definitely stay at this hotel again!

title: “Would not recommend this place...”
text:
I chose this hotel "despite" the other reviews as we really wanted it for location across from the NASA Space Center. Yes the location is ideal. Also a short drive to the Kemah boardwalk.
We stayed 2 dreadful nights here.
Night #1 -- started out not so bad -- the room was ok (1st floor), the hall smelled and my son pointed out that some fo the room on the other side were "smoking rooms" thus I figured contributed the to the smell. The room was clean, the A/C, TV and fridge worked. The back entry to the hotel was a concern as it didn't close properly and anyone could walk in if people don't shut it correctly. All was well..until 3:48 am and I hear a Big Foot Convention or Stampede in the room above. Just when you think it would stop, then someone would be running around or heavy stepping/jumping around the room. Finally by 5:30, I called the front desk (no answer), got dressed and walked down there -- only to find out that there are kids/teens in that room and they are staying another night.
Night #2 -- We were given the option to move to a different room down the hall -- so we did or put up with possible no sleep again. (why couldn't they move the teens?). Anyway this next room had a stain on carpet, smaller refrigerator, no coffee maker, the toilet won't flush properly, but we figured since it was our last night, we'll put up with it. Then we are about to go to bed and the DEAD BOLT won't work!! ..Too late to move now and again with the Back entry to the hotel not closing properly this is now an unsafe place to stay.
We told the front desk about this and hopefully will get some discount back on our credit card for the crap we put up with -- I'll be checking on that this week.
I don't think I've ever stayed in a worse hotel and would rather spend extra $ just to make sure I have a room with a door that has a dead bolt lock.

title: “Way too small”
text:
We tried one of the anonymous low priced-room hotel finders for the first time last weekend. Our room was very narrow and very short. It had a double bed, a hollow end table, a tv/cabinet and a hanging desk with a chair. We had to knee walk across the bed to get to the end table on the other side. The windows didn't fit so the air was frigid. The bathroom had no where for personal items, there was a small sink, no vanity, a toilet, and a shower, no tub. We had been promised no less than a queen sized bed and other standard features. We talked to other guests in the bar and 3 others were staying in the same kind of room. All were paying more than we were so it wasn't just because we were trying to go cheap for the weekend.
Entrance to the hotel was ground level, freezing in there. Elevator to either floor 2, restaurant/bar or 3, the lobby/check in/out. Then cross over to elevators going to the guest rooms. Long waits for elevators. The room was nicely appointed but extremely small. 
When we checked in and were told it was a petite classic I asked what size bed? double. I said we need to have a queen sized bed, we have a confirmation. Ok, queen it is. The bed was a double bed with a queen-sized headboard.

title: “Just below average”
text:
I stayed at the HGI Charlotte for an event recently and the stay was below average. There are numerous issues with this hotel, including the following.
The hotel room smelled like deodorizer
The common areas (hallways) were freezing cold
The breakfast was just okay, but I saw one of the most disgusting things I've ever seen, deep fried bacon.
The staff was wonderful in the morning and very weird at night
The parking was almost full, but for some reason they didn't have the top floor of the parking garage open.
The thermostat was manual, which seemed weird in such a new property
The pool was just outright scary looking..
The TV had HD, but it was fuzzy. I didn't know that was possible...
The only thing positive I would say about this is the room (outside of the deodorant smell) is the HGI finishes were very nice, great bedding, nice chair, and good bathroom.. I would be amazed if this property retains its HGI name.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: This hotel is absolutely beautiful! I've been looking at the prices for a while and it was a little high but we decided to stay here last minute after I saw a great 48hr sale on the rate for $350 for the entire weekend! Couldn't get over how pretty the whole place is and the valets are extremely friendly. We did not use the hotel parking and instead parked across the street at the city garage that sits above the Police Station for $9 a day. Check-In was extremely quick and easy and the staff were super friendly. The rooms are gorgeous and very clean. We went and toured San Antonio with our kids and came back late...about 11 p.m. and forgot that we had not asked for a roll-away for our oldest (we have 3 kids). Even with it being so late, one call to the front desk and we had a roll-away in about 5 minutes! They even sent milk and cookies to our kids and left "worry dolls" on the pillow when they turned down the beds. The only issue we had during our entire stay is the little yapping dog across the hall that barked most of the day and half the night. Fortunately, we were so tired each night, that when we finally did fall asleep, we stayed that way. I loved the hotel and my husband and I will most likely be back.

title: “Excellent all around”
text: The customer service sets an excellent hotel apart from the merely good ones. Customer service extends from the check-in to the housekeeping to the check-out. The Ritz in Denver was excellent. The rooms were spotless and comfortable. The onsite restaurant was excellent, and the employees were friendly and helpful. Access to the Forza Fitness Center, which is beautiful, is a huge bonus. I would return in a minute.

title: “Average Airport Hotel”
text: If you are staying at the Philadelphia Airport there are not a lot of good options. Marriott is the best of the bunch among very average choices and ofter prohibitively expensive. When that is the case I choose either Sheraton Suites or Aloft depending on price with Sheraton being my preferred choice. Sheraton suites is certainly showing its age these days and could use an update. It is in the same part as the aloft and 4 points and all hotels share the same shuttle service. The hotel is a standard American Airport Hotel and cannot be recommended as a must stay but cannot be faulted either as it gets the job done. I look forward to when the hotel is refurbished but at $120 AAA rate there are much worse options.

title: “blonde lady at front desk sucks”
text: First I asked for a non smoking room the room smelled like a hooker bar. The front desk black lady with the blonde hair attitude sucks. Very bad service. Need to.up grade TVs and cable .the rooms were ok refrigerator and microwave was very helpful. Would I go back . Probably not.

title: “nice hotel..great location”
text: really liked this hotel. its in a great location thats so handy to times square and all of manhattans attractions.The beds are the most comfortable i have ever slept on..like sleeping on a cloud. The only problem I had was constently being asked by the doorman to see my room key. I understand this is for security reasons but even after telling him I would be there for a week he still asked me everytime..very disapointing and this will stop me coming there again. if you ever get new door man message me and I might change my mind!!!

title: “Not bad”
text:
This hotel is in a good location on w51st so definitely walking distance to times square. 
The rooms are extremely tiny though and the girl who checked us in advised that we had been upgraded to a slightly bigger room...would hate to see what the smaller one looks like. 
The service wasn't good, the check in girl seemed like she couldn't be bothered and the doorman was no where in sight, which was a bit annoying when the entrance is only stairs and you have big suitcases. 
Apart from that it is a good budget hotel if you want to be in the thick of it all. Although I'd recommend booking something like airbnb where you actually stay in someones apartment - we did that for the remainder of our trip and it was amazing. For the same price we got an apartment with a kitchen and computer with internet.

title: “Michelangelo is the best!”
text:
Our third visit (leisure) to the Michelangelo and it continues to be marvelous experience. Everyone from doormen to reception to concierge to housekeeping is invariably helpful and kind - just a perfect way to buffer the hustle/bustle of Manhattan.
Rooms are larger than what would be expected - we were upgraded from deluxe to Junior suite with sofa, coffee table and comfortable chairs along with desk separate from sleeping area. King sized bed very comfortable with lovely linens. Everything was impeccably clean and yet the only time I saw housekeeping was when they were doing turn-down service. Very quiet in AM, allowing for peaceful sleep. Just love this hotel!

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Went to New York to set my son up for Culinary studies and so after researching the net for over 6 months and comparing hotels I settled upon "The Kimberly". Very glad I did. Centrally located to alot of what you go to New York to see. The staff (everyone included) made our stay most enjoyable. We were there for 12 days. I got to know several of the employees by name and they knew me and my family by name. The staff at the adjoining restaraunt "George O'Neills" was just as friendly. The service was great and the food excellent and they have a staff that they should be proud of - as I know they are. Loved the outside cafe. Thank you Vince for putting up with me just sitting outside soaking up the city and people watching. The conceirge staff at the Kimberly were very helpful in anything that I inquired about and very knowledgeable. The suite was good size and very clean and the noise level was hardly noticable. Slept like a baby. I was very impressed. Would I recommend this hotel to anyone - YOU BET. Thank all of you for the help, directions, watching over me, the ideas and most of all good service and great food. Will be going back in March and hope to see everyone again. - till then - the Matthews family.

title: “Chicago Favorite”
text:
I've stayed at half a dozen nice hotels in downtown Chicago, and The Drake is my favorite. I enjoy staying in well maintained historical elegant hotels and The Drake does not disappoint on that account. The service is on par with the reputation and the location is excellent for Michigan Ave. / Magnificent Mile shopping, dining and entertainment. With any historic hotel, rooms can vary greatly from tiny to grand, so your experience may vary accordingly. It's worth booking at least one room category above the lowest price to set you up for a possible upgrade and keep you out of a closet (albeit an elegant closet) of a room. If you get lucky you may have a special experience. I booked a Drake Suite, and, upon request, was upgraded to a Gold Coast Suite with a large bedroom, separate parlor, marble bathroom with large Jacuzzi tub and separate shower, plus a killer view of Lake Michigan and Lakeshore Drive. If you are Hilton Honor's and get the breakfast benefit, that will be in the Drake Brothers Restaurant with menu availability against the credit, far preferable in my opinion than an executive floor lounge breakfast. Make it a point to have a drink in the Coq D Or' - claimed to have opened the day after Prohibition. Afternoon High Tea is another highlight in the Palm Court. If the rates for my dates are relatively reasonable, The Drake will remain my first choice when staying in Chicago.
Parking Tip: Hotel valet parking is $55 / night. On the north side of Walton Place first driveway just west of Michigan Avenue, 1/2 block from the front door, park at the One Mignificent Mile garage for $29 / 24 hours (no in/out, cash only).

title: “Good value for money”
text: We stayed here for four nights in October and were pleasantly surprised. We originally only planned to stay for one night as it was the first place we arrived at after exiting the freeway. The rooms etc may not be ultra modern, but they were spotlessly clean and huge!! The staff were excellent and gave loads of helpful local information and so we decided to make this our base to explore San Diego. Breakfast was included in the rate and was nice, the lady serving it was really funny and kept us entertained. There is a pool etc but we didnt use it as the weather was fab and we hit the beach instead! Overall this place is a smashing base to explore San Diego and the nightlife etc in Hillcrest was brilliant!

title: “The best value for your money in NYC”
text: Second time I've been to this hotel. My bf and I loved it. Near all the attractions yet not too loud, clean and affordable, could not ask for anything more. Maid service is great, staff is helpful and the breakfast place next store is good and nicely priced. I don't think I'll ever go to another hotel in New York, stayed 4 nites and paid 105$ a nite, amazing deal! Will be back this summer for sure!

title: “Nice hotel and great service!”
text: We stayed at the Westin Georgetown for 1 night and had a great time. The location is just a couple blocks from Georgetown and is a quick ride to the monuments and sites. The service was exceptional. Ahmad the bellman was extremely helpful with everything from parking tips to sightseeing to restaurants. We will definitely stay at this hotel again the next time we're in the area.

title: “Top Notch Experience!”
text: Our weekend stay was wonderful. We arrived at noon and were pleasantly surprised to find our room available already (which was lucky.) Our room was spacious and clean. Even though we barely used the kitchen, it seemed very well stocked with supplies and quite clean. The coffee pot was even above average with a stainless steel carafe and large capacity. The staff was absolutely terrific. All the girls working the desk were very nice and helpful. The breakfast buffet was a big plus. The seating area is big but still crowded. The food options included oatmeal, eggs, waffles, pancakes, sausage, yogurt, cereal, fruit, pastries, toast, bagels, granola and beverage stations with juice, coffee and all the fixings. The staff at the buffet were very helpful and pleasant despite the big crowds and multiple requests. The location is about 1 1/2 blocks from a Metro station which is very convenient. The one and only bad thing is that there are very few restaurants that are open late into the evenings nearby. The neighborhood seems to shut down by about 5 or 6pm. Great stay!

title: “A real gem!”
text: Our stay at the Elysee was perfect in every way. The room was charming, clean and comfortable; breakfast was outstanding. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful. Location of the hotel is very convenient. Highly recommend this "gem" and look forward to returning.

title: “Special one year wedding Anniversary!”
text: Got to the Westin on Saturday June 18th at noon and our room was ready. I told Farrell at the front desk about our 1 year anniversary and he upgraded our room to the riverwalk side with a furnished balcony overlooking the riverwalk. The room and balcony was outstanding and really made for a great anniversary. Farrell gave us outstanding service when we checked in to the hotel. Melissa at the front desk let us get a later checkout and was very nice. The service was outstanding and we will be back every year for our wedding anniversary. Westin riverwalk is the best hotel on the river in San Antonio.

title: “Nice rooms, but did not like it much, lousy breakfast”
text:
The Hyatt Regency is located close to Terminal C of DFW Airport. It went through a renovation a couple of years ago, so I was curious if the rooms lived up to the hype compared to a visit a 5 years ago.
In short, they do, to an extent. The rooms are indeed nicely decorated and look quite elegant. I did not feel very comfortable though, as the windows did not get a proper soundproofing, so the noise of the starting planes and the car traffic was to hear loud and clear.
In terms of room features I found irritating that the room did not seem to have a fridge. The bathroom also felt a bit spartanic.
Breakfast has severely suffered over the years. 5 years ago the buffet breakfast for 15,95 contained omelettes to order, nice selection of fruit and other niceties. Now it's just scrambled eggs made of eggs from the can, a meager selection of fruit and some (nice) pastries. Coffee and Juice were extra. 
All in all the Hyatt Regency was quite a disappointment. The rooms were nice, but the overall package was disappointing. I am not sure if I will stay there again.

title: “Comfortable & good value.”
text: I was a little hesitant to stay here based on the reviews I read, but I was quite pleased. We arrived early and wanted to do some sight seeing, so the front desk held our luggage for us until check in. The cookies were delicious and the bed was comfy. If you are worried about the wallpaper or furniture, you are probably spending too much time in the room!

title: “Mid-tier Hampton”
text:
I stay at this Hampton a few times a year and find it adequate, although of a lower quality than the top tier Hamptons (Oklahoma City Bricktown, East Aurora NY, etc). The air conditioner is noisy, there are no sheer curtains on the windows so your choice is darkness or visibility from passers-by, the shower faucet may be slightly askew, and no decaf coffee in the room.
These are small things but show a lack of attention to detail. On the positive side, the location is freeway-friendly, the parking is free, and the shower drains rapidly. I'll stay here again but won't expect as luxurious an experience as other Hamptons provide.

title: “Perfect place to see Seattle”
text: Very friendly and helpful staff. Staff made great dinner suggestions throughout our stay. The location of the hotel is within walking distance of downtown Seattle, or a short (cheap) cab ride to further destinations. I will stay here again if I ever come back to Seattle.

title: “Fantastic and ghostly....”
text: My wife and I spent 5 nights in Jan. as a getaway. Loved the hotel, the location, and the staff. On our first night I saw what I can only describe as a ghost. Not once, but twice within a 15 minute period of time. My wife was sleeping and I was watching T.V. when I saw what looked like a woman in a robe in profile.Not to alarm my wife I put the nightlight on, shut the T.V., and went (or tried to go) to sleep, not mentioning a word to my wife who would think that I was suffering from jetlag or dengue fever. Three days later, over dinner in the North end my wife said that she had to tell me something but she didn't want me to think she was delusional. It seemed that, the night before she had seen a ghost. Yes, it was a woman, and yes it was in profile. Still not saying a word I asked her to draw, on a cocktail napkin what she saw, and I did the same. When we were done the drawings were identical, not close, identical. I then told her what I had seen as she couldn't understand how I could have drawn what she thought she ahd only seen. After 3 glasses of a very nice Tuscana we were sufficiently freaked out to attempt to return to our room. I have never, in 65 years seen a ghost or anything like it, nor had my wife.The rest of the trip was filled with good food, laughs, and not another visit. After we returned home we read up on the hotel and found that it did indeed have a history of ghost sightings and was named one of the 10 most haunted hotels in America. Have a great trip.

title: “Terrific Hotel in a perfect location”
text:
I was recently in San Antonio for business, but seeing as how I'd never been to the city before, I decided to stay downtown. I was very pleased with my stay. 
This hotel is in a great location, right on the water in a quiet area of the Riverwalk. The hotel has a bar and restaurant with a patio right out on the water. It's a Spanish themed tapas restaurant with pretty good happy hour food/prices. You're a short, enjoyable walk to the very touristy area with all the bars, restaurants and shopping of the Riverwalk, but without the all the crowds. 
The room was large, a suite setup, with a seperate bedroom and living room area. The room was clean and comfortable. I didn't pay the extra $$ for the "Riverview" room, and I don't think you need to, though I would recommend a room on a higher floor, as the skyline is cool in all directions.
They do charge you a good amount for parking, and it DOES take a good 15-20 minutes for the valet to bring it around. This would probably be my only complaint. Besides that, I highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a reasonably priced, upscale hotel in a very cool area.

title: “Stayed For Dental Convention”
text:
#1 it would have been nice if the front desk would of told us that, you need to put your room key in the elevator, instead of us having the doors open and shut on us 3x's before someone else came on and we saw how to do it.
#2 We asked where we could smoke and was told there was a bench out front. So we kept going there for 1 day/night. Then was rudely told we couldn't smoke there we had to go down the sidewalk to smoke. Only to find out on our exploration of the hotel on day #2, That they have a smoking "OASIS" patio outside in the center of the hotel, which NOBODY told us about. Which was wonderful until we got dirty looks from people on the first floor in their rooms that face it.....SORRY, But we had so much fun out there!
#3 Other than a bumpy start, Our rooms were clean,Coffee in the lobby AWESOME and we never really had any interaction with the help.

title: “Super choice!”
text: Just returned from 3 nights here and had a great time. The room had stunning views of the Golden Gate and Girhardelli's. It was tastefully decorated on a nautical theme and extremely spacious. The bed was particularly comfortable. The complimentary wine in the hotel lobby each evening was well received! The location could not have been better. Although Fisherman's Wharf is a busy place, the hotel was a peaceful haven. I would definitely recommend the Argonaut.

title: “Highly Recomend! Great service! What a treat!”
text: We travel frequently and stay at 3 to 5 star hotels. This hotel is now one of our favorite. It's not large, rather a smaller boutique hotel with a wonderful decor. The rooftop pool and spa are small but quaint and with views of downtown L.A. We found the location convenient to the Staples center - about a 6 block walk (we walked during a business day and felt safe, the bellman said to taxi at night and we'd probably taxi on the weekend as well). We found the service impeccible everywhere. The bell staff, front desk, dining were each exceptional. They accommodated several of our special needs, including a 8:30 am arrival due to businessand an upgraded room request (wonderful view at no extra charge). Dining ends at 10:00pm but there is a nice sports bar with a sandwich/salad type menu across the street at the Biltmore.

title: “Above average accommodations at the Homewood”
text: Travelers should not have any significant issues with this hotel, especially business travelers. First impressions upon entering the building are positive; nice decor. The common area used for manager receptions and breakfast is also well appointed. Front desk staff was friendly and professional. Hotel was clean and well maintained. My room was excellent (I stayed for two nights). Housekeeping did a great job. Pillows and mattresses were extremely comfortable. Dual zone heating system kept me warm. Showers had ample hot water. The room had everything I expected for a Homewood Suites. Yes, I-465 skirts right by the front of the hotel. For me, the road noise was not bothersome. Late at night there just isn't that much traffic, plus when the heater kicked in, the blower fan muffled any road noise (by the way, the heater noise was normal for such a unit). Ask for a rear room if you think traffic noise would be a problem. Big breakfast fans will be pleased with the neighboring Cracker Barrell restaurant within walking distance. Of course the food offered at Homewood is adequate for most people. This is a nice hotel worthy of your business.

title: “Doesn't come close to being worth price"”
text: This place doesn't come close to being worth the price. Rooms are way past ready for renovation/update - carpet frayed, chipped paint, worn furniture, drapes with stains to name a few things. The $12.95/day cost of internet is a joke. Once you fork over this ridiculous fee just to be able to do some work in your room, you are seated at one of the most uncomfortable and old desk chairs imaginable. Room never completely cooled. Sink in bathroom had no cold water. I could go on, but ...

title: “A Peaceful Oasis”
text:
My friend and I got a great rate on Priceline to stay here two nights Sept. 5-7. I had a terrible cold and had to spend a lot of time sleeping during our trip. The beds are SO comfortable--I have never slept so well in a hotel bed. In our two-bed room the beds were double-sized. We loved the look of the rooms--sort of Japanese modern with wood and olive trim. We called ahead and requested a room with a bathtub.
Our room was located on the sixth floor, which I anticipated being dark. But it was actually just fine--about one-third of our window view was sky, so we had nice sunlight.
The hallways are so cool--they are dimly lit with the room numbers glowing in cobalt blue.
I want to stay here every time I visit--our room was such a pleasure to rest and relax.

title: “Good value in downtown San Antonio”
text: My sister and I stayed here to attend a family reunion in San Antonio. The Fairfield Inn is a nice, modern hotel, on the west side of the downtown area. Compared to many other hotels in the vicinity, it offered good value. The parking lot was large, but the breakfast area was small, hot and crowded all the time. On the plus side, the staff was very friendly and helpful. We needed advice how to reach a restaurant in the nearby Market Square district and the young man at the front desk was very good at giving us excellent directions, plus a map. Also our family rented a meeting room at the Courtyard by Marriott next door, and the staff at the front desk put up a sign directing our group to where we would meet. I thought that was nice of them. Overall I had a good opinion of the Fairfield Inn.

title: “Awesome location, definitely stay here again, just small!”
text: Surprised at how good the location was - very close to trams, huge Westfield and Union Square. Great atmosphere and felt very safe. Made up for the very small room - we had a room with 2 double beds and that was literally all that could fit. Had to half-climb over one of the beds to get to the bathroom, but it wasn't a big deal for us. The only bad thing was the that toilet seemed to block very easily and didn't flush all the time but we just put it down to old plumbing, if it had gotten any worse we would have told management. The elevator was tiny as well and the walls were pretty thin we had a noise complaint not very late one night. But all in all we were very happy with our stay! It had a warm european feel, free internet in the lobby and plenty of seats to relax while waiting for check in/out!

title: “What More Do You Need?”
text: A really nice place to settle down amid the bustle of activities just outside the door. Staff are very attentive and the hotel shuttle to local attractions is a wonderful touch of class for guests. Rooms are simple but just right. The location is one of the best near the mile and Rush St. Avoid room service costs by buying what you need at Trader Joe's across the street, including cheap but good wine for the room. A short walk to Eggsperience will remind you how great breakfast can be when on vacation.

title: “Great rates and service”
text:
While traveling north on I-95 we wanted to stop in Boston to do some shopping. We have a dog we take everywhere with us and the roundhouse is pet friendly so we gave it a try.
Clean rooms, secure parking, and a great location outside of downtown. There is a nice bar and grill across mass ave and convenient subway access.

title: “eWomen Network International Conference”
text: We have had the pleasure to stay here for the third time and have enjoyed each and every trip to this hotel. Check in was fast and food service was well made. With over 2000 women in our group alone the hotel had not trouble in taking care of our needs. Although the rooms are in need of renovation, it was quite adequate. At check in I told the young lady it was our 31 st. wedding anniversary and we were given a upgraded room. We were given a free upgrade to a junior suite / city view, and it was very roomy. The view was very nice at night. Staff was superb and the 4 days we were there was without incident. The pool is not up to standards and was the biggest let down of the trip. Very smmal pool and very hot, no shade provided and not family or guest friendly.

title: “Excellent Choice for Seattle Visit!”
text: My husband and I decided to take a long weekend in Seattle. Having never been there, I read a lot of reviews on Tripadvisor and selected the Mayflower Park Hotel for our stay at the recommendations of many. It was great! Our flights came in very early and left really late, but they were able to accommodate an early check in and a late check out with no problems. I had booked their Rise and Shine package, so we had a delicious breakfast sent up to our room every morning. And it's true what others say---Olivers is great! We enjoyed their cocktails (especially the infused Bloody Mary) each night before having dinner in town. The front desk staff and concierge was very helpful and polite. We got a room on the 12th floor in the corner, so we had great views. Although the room was smaller than an average sized hotel room, it suit our needs perfectly. Also, at the suggestion of others on tripadvisor we took the Downtown Airporter through Grayline for $18 each, roundtrip. It picked up/dropped off at the Westin less than 2 minutes away from the Mayflower Park. This was a super easy alternative to taking a cab from the airport/downtown. We had considered renting a car, but glad we didn't in the end. Everything was easy to get to without a car. Location wise the hotel was perfect for our needs. We walked to the Pikes Place Market everyday. Also, having the monorail and Westlake Center (food court/shopping) attached to the hotel made travel to Seattle Center easy. We celebrated one night with dinner at the Space Needle restaurant. It is overpriced as other say, but it was worth the experience and views. Plus you have to consider the $16 per person you'd spend just to go up it, so it worked out! We also went on the Savory Seattle Food tour through The Pikes Place Market and it was great! Well worth the time and money. Overall, we had a great trip to Seattle and the Mayflower Park Hotel is probably the biggest reason why! Thanks to everyone on Tripadvisor for your suggestions!

title: “Excellent Location”
text:
There are a lot of complaints about this hotel in Trip Advisor Reviews and as a result we were very nervous about staying here. 
We found the reception staff very pleasant and helpful. They had our reservation at the price we expected and when we wanted to book again at the end of our stay in the USA they were very obliging.
Whilst the hotel is undoubtedly quite old, with paint peeling off the walls in some areas, the room was clean and more than adequate for our family.
The breakfast advertised was disappointing and you should not make your choice based on this inclusion. However, excellent restaurants are located only a very short walk away. There are also small grocery stores around where it is possible to buy breakfast cereals etc.
Overall a good choice for the budget minded traveller wanting a hotel in an excellent location. This hotel does not deserve all the bad press.

title: “Terrific hotel!”
text: Just spent 2 nights at this wonderful hotel in a good neighborhood (West 24th St, off 6th Ave.) With a good chain you know what to expect, and this exceeded all expectations. Comfortable beds, very clean, excellent shower, and outstanding buffet breakfast (included) with hot and cold selections in a lovely breakfast room with outside patio. Subway around the corner. Good restaurants. We had to be near St. Vincent Medical Center for family surgery. It is 12 short blocks away or 1 subway stop. Nothing in NY is cheap, but we felt that this was well worth the money. Will definitely return.

title: “Wonderful, wonderful, wonderful!”
text:
I directed our organization's national conference here. We could not have dreamed of a better place to host our conference. Many of the conference rooms have gorgeous views of the harbor for the floor to ceiling windows, there is a great balcony overlooking the water as well! SWANK company took care of all technology needs and worked with our budget! And everyone on staff was helpful and professional. Plus, they gave us an unbelievable price on the group rate for hotel rooms.
The best part was that all hotel guests have access to their fabulous spa! The spa is separated by genders. Both have incredible amenities that I highly recommend And - you do not have to have a spa service to enjoy the spa!
There is a hot tub with lounge chairs under the water, steam room, sauna, relaxation rooms with tea and dried fruit, private balcony - where you can lounge, drink, and enjoy the view of pier 6 concert venue! There are showers, lockers, towels, hair dryers, robes, everything you need. 
I live in Town and I can't wait to plan my next anniversary celebration in this new Baltimore gem!
I never got a chance to enjoy the spa during the conference I was so busy - but the hotel staff was wonderful. They will store your bags and you can enjoy the spa on the day you checkout!

title: “A Hotel with fabulous staff that looks after you”
text: I quitted Ritz Carlton Amelia Island for this one. With free internet in-room, close to a local shopping complex (with Wal-Mart, restaurants, best burger of Jacksonville, etc), this is a nice hotel to be in. It was opened only a few months ago, so brand new. Fantastic and spacious room. The only problem with the room is the fairly big and noisy air conditioning. The restaurant was small and the food selection was limited. The free continential breakfast was included, however, the milk that was served that morning had turned bad and was sour-taste. The staff apologised profusedly and quickly changed it. The FrontDesk staff were very friendly and helpful, such as brought the scale to my room to weigh my luggage, dropped me off and picked me up from the nearby shopping complex no matter how late it was (and with big smile greeting me back), and of course to the airport not far away. Definitely will stay there again, and Hyatt Place.

title: “Feels more like a posh residence, then bustling hotel”
text: This property is beautifully maintained, and while the Battery itself lacks city charm, the views of the Statue of Liberty from our room and easy access by foot to the landscaped walking/running trail along the Hudson River makes up for the otherwise dull neighborhood location. Service was excellent, from the bellman to the bar, although we sorely missed the lovely terrace bar we remember from a prior stay. That was the number one reason to return, and I can't believe the hotel has chosen to close it down, in exchange for a lobby bar location. That said, we had great service and really excellent food in the bar for a late dinner following a long day in the hot sun at the US Open. Your a quick walk to the subway and an express train to either Grand Central or Time Square, so getting from here to there is a snap. High marks still.

title: “I stayed at the Sheraton for 4 nights for...”
text: I stayed at the Sheraton for 4 nights for an industry conference and found everything at the hotel from room to food to ballrooms to even the public bathrooms to be very clean. The staff was great and had great service from everyone especially Maggie at the lobby bar. She was very friendly and made sure we never had to search for her when more drinks were needed.

title: “Clean and comfortable, well maintained Hilton in DC”
text: Stayed one night for a function in the hotel. Unfortunately due to the event, we arrived too late for valet parking, but registration easily removed the charge (as it was included in the rate). Quick and efficient check in, friendly staff. Again, clean and comfortable room. For the number of rooms in the hotel, the service was amazing. One complaint was the adjoining room feature appears that the gap at the bottom of the door allowed for a lot of our neighbors noise to come through/under the door. And unfortunately they we loud talkers - stuck and extra pillow and blanket at the door jamb - and it helped a little -but still a nuisance. Overall, very nice experience, great room, super friendly wait staff for AM breakfast in the dining area - good food and coffee too. Definitely would recommend, as well as would stay here again.

title: “Excellent Place to Stay!”
text: The Alexis is a smaller high quality boutique hotel located in downtown Seattle. While usually "boutique hotel" is code for old, cramped and dusty, this hotel is quite the opposite. The rooms and service are outstanding. The rooms are decorated in an art nouveau or deco style, the staff are always friendly and helpful. The free coffee and wine served is wonderful. For those who are into TV, the room has a large flat screen TV. The hotel is close to Pike's Market and lovely shops. I stayed with them on business but will definitely stay there again whether business or pleasure.

title: “Great Experience”
text:
My wife and I stayed for six nights in a executive king bed room at 
the Iroquois in July. We chose it after we have read a lot of good reviews about it. The room size is NY standard, whereas the bathroom is pretty big. We really liked the personal approach of its staff.
A little draw back for us was that fact that one is not able to switch off the AC. (I solved this problem in my way though..)When reported to the GM, he substiuted us to a free dinner at the superb Restaurant Triomphe downstairs. Great gesture! When my wife got sick, the concierge called a doctor she personally knew well and organized a quick appointment for us. I have never experienced this kind of personal treatment in any of the big hotel chains. We will be back at the Iroquois.

title: “Family reunion”
text: Wonderful hotel with tons of amenities. Fabulous pool and bar. Didn't get to eat at the restaurant, but the food looked lovely. Very attentive staff and the location can't be beat! We were there to visit the entire family and stayed there because my sister in law lives at the Residence at the Hotel Palomar. We had our little ones with us and they thoroughly enjoyed the pool. It smells like roses throughout the entire place, not like a spay, but like real roses!

title: “Not Worth the Free Parking”
text: We chose this hotel exclusively for the location and the free parking, both of which we did enjoy. It was a great location for us to catch the trolley across the street at the Hard Rock McDonalds. And we dined at nearby Ginos, Hard Rock Cafe, Rainforest Cafe, and McDonalds, all within a minute walk. It also should be noted that the staff, every single one of them we encountered, was super helpful and courteous. That being said, I would not suggest this hotel because it is very old (don't be fooled by the "remodel") and lacks amenities. I kid you not, they replaced the entire AC unit in our room 2 of the 3 nights we were there! The walls are paper-thin and you can hear every noise around you as if they were in the same room. Elevators take several minutes, even in non-peak times. Also, we found the bathrooms too small.

title: “Try the pool.”
text:
We stayed here with our two young kids. The staff were all extremely friendly, from the room attendants to the Pool guys. 
Granted, the rooms are a tad tired, however the hotel makes up for it with personality. 
Now, the best part was the Roof top swimming pool. My five year old thought he was on the set of the new Spiderman movie. Real magic moment. 
Thx for a fun couple of days guys.

title: “More like a bed and Breakfast”
text: I used to live in Seattle so generally when I return, I stay with friends. But this trip I had relatives with me who have special needs so I opted for a motel. This Travelodge is very close to the Univ of Washington, the freeways, Lake Washington, the Arboretum and downtown Seattle and giant classy shopping area of University village, yet the neighborhood is very safe, and the rooms were super quiet. The price was very reasonable and parking was easy which is hard to find anywhere near downtown Seattle. Two ladies named Sandy and Shirley are the managers and they were amazing. My group had wheelchairs, walkers and some special requests that were all handled with the personal attention one experiences in a Bed and Breakfast, not a motel. But I should say the breakfast ( waffles, sausage, fruit, cereals) was fresh, constantly restocked and very tidy. Yes, the decor is not the newest, but the helpful staff more than makes up for that in my opinion.

title: “First impression: Awful.”
text:
My check in experience here was a disaster that soured the rest of my stay:
In the interest of full disclosure, I completely messed up my reservation. I'd reserved for a day earlier than I'd intended on arriving. I discovered this at check in, and felt foolish. I was also informed, in no uncertain terms, that I'd be charged for the night I'd "missed" --- whoa! I'm still trying to get over my silly mistake! The check in clerk continued, from this moment forward, to fail at every turn. 
I'm a Hilton Gold Member, and an IHG Platinum Member. I travel a lot. I'm used to receiving a little bit of priority treatment at the hotels I visit, so I didn't think asking for the missed night charge to be reversed would be an unreasonable thing to do. The desk agent looked at me as if I'd asked her to chop her leg off and give it to me. She refused to let me finish my sentence! And this is where the whole experience really turned. I asked her to speak with a Manager. She said she would. I watched her walk down to another person behind the desk, and walk back within seconds to report the Manager had also declined my request. It was physically impossible for her to have had a conversation in the amount of time I witnessed. Insulting!
Defeated, I accepted my punishment (that's what it now felt like) and headed to my room. There was a giant greasy forehead shaped smear on the window to greet me, and several yellow pillows that were missing their pillow cases. After this, I collapsed on to the bed and logged on to Facebook to post a complaint on their local page about my experience. 
The Manager called me almost immediately, and apologized and took care my initial request, but by this point the damage was done. I'd been made to feel inferior, and had been greeted by a depressing room.
The rest of my three day stay? It included daily charges for wifi, and a missed visit by Housekeeping.
In the future, you'll find me at the Hilton down the street.

title: “good location, thats all it has going for it”
text: the location of the hotel is the only good thing about it, apart from the impressive lobby, service is non-existent, we got a single room instead of the double we booked online, the room was dirty, mouldy and smelled of damp, with practically no view whatsoever. i found the hotel staff(the few who spoke to you), very unhelpful and unco-operative. if you are not fussy and just want a good location to stay in ny, then its ok, but if you are looking for a bit extra..then forget it..would i stay there again....? not sure.....

title: “Gets the job done.”
text: No frills clean hotel, with great staff. It's absolutely not worth the $160-180 prices I've seen, but a great place to stay if you get a discounted rate on hotwire or another site. I've stayed in this hotel many times and if the price was eight would stay here again.

title: “Great location, but noisy and outdated”
text:
We stayed at the Affinia Manhattan for 2 nights. 
Pros: 
- Convenient location, across from Madison Square Garden, Penn Station, Subway stops, Macy's Herald Square
- Spacious rooms
- Kitchenette with sink, refrigerator and microwave
Cons:
- Location next to NYPD substation and fire department made for a very noisy stay. We were on the 11th floor and the street noise, sirens, etc. still kept us awake. I had to go buy earplugs and sleep aids to help me get a good night's sleep on the 2nd night of our stay.
- Lobby is beautiful, but it appears that the renovations were only to the first floor. Hallways and room decor were outdated.

title: “Beautiful hotel, great location”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for two nights. It was an easy walk from the T station (Park St.). Hotel is located literally in the middle of history. Boston Common down the street, the Granary Burial Ground across the street, lots of bars, pubs, restaurants, convenience stores in the area. 
Front desk check in was quick and helpful, always friendly. The room was fantastic, great linens, not big rooms but plenty of space for the two of us. The best was our huge window that overlooked the city. We did sleep with the window cracked open just a bit and the church bells across the street started a little too early in the morning for my liking, but really it just added to the atmosphere. :)
We did have brunch at the hotel restaurant one morning, service was rather slow, but it was a nice brunch, good selections and food was well prepared. 
We hope to return to Boston soon and will definitely stay at the Nine Zero again.

title: “Nice Marriott, but had some issues...”
text:
The hotel was beautiful, but we were not informed of some of the amenities that they offered. We have 14 month old twins and we BOUGHT 2 playpens so that they could have somewhere to sleep in the room. After arriving to our hotel room, we read in the hotel directory that the hotel provides cribs for guests. We were surprised to hear that but upset that neither the hotel reservationist nor the hotel lobby clerk mentioned that to us! We did mention that we were a family of four (with toddlers) when we booked the reservation. Wouldn't they know that if we had toddlers, that we could use the cribs they provided?
The other thing that we were not happy with was the whirlpool/hot tub was not working properly. I had a slightly sore back at the time and I was really looking forward to sitting in a nice hot tub to sooth my muscles. But, of course I couldn't since there was no workable hot tub. One of the other guests told me, "You have to inform the maintanence worker and he has to turn on the primer each time for it to work." She also told me that they won't have anyone to fix the hot tub until the following Monday. HA! What a joke. So, nevertheless, I ended up keeping my sore back till the next day. But, it would have been nice to have that feature, since we WERE paying $100 a night.
As for the cleanliness & professionalism, they were very nice and the rooms seemed very clean. The hotel was fairly easy to find and the checkout was easy (express checkout)!
We went to the Dublin Irish Festival which was absolutely fabulous. They had games and activities for everyone, most importantly toddler events for our twins!

title: “Love the decor”
text: There is a Starbucks in the main lobby and the hotel is attached to the mall. There is also a free parking garage that makes it nice and convenient. The bed was extremely comfortable. Not so much the mattress itself but the pillows, sheets and comforter....I didn't want to get out of bed. I stayed at this hotel in July andI also was back for a conference in late September. I did not stay the second time however, the same elevator seemed to not be working right. It was slow and making funny noises. I am not one that is scared of being in elevators but I immediately got off and switched rides. Other than that, I loved my stay at this hotel.

title: “Great little hotel”
text: Very nice hotel near Love Field and Stemmons. Easy access to everything. Rooms were very clean and management was very responsive when the hair dryer didn't work. Suite faced back of hotel and was very quiet, though don't expect any million dollar views. Breakfast was good and fresh. Free wifi with no fumbling around for a password. Business center with printer came in handy for printing boarding passes. Overall a great place to stay close to Love Field.

title: “Good location and price”
text:
Boston is an expensive city that I love to visit! The Holiday Inn Government Center is a perfectly adequate hotel, but nothing overly special. However, both the price and location are ideal. 
 I pre-paid $200 a night (that includes all the taxes) for this hotel that is located only 10 minutes from a major T-stop that includes both the Green and Blue Lines. Faneuil Hall and the waterfront are an additional five minutes from the T-stop. The Charles River and the Museum of Science are within easy walking distance. 
 The hotel is located on a side street right around the corner from Cambridge Avenue which is a MAJOR street in the area, so there was some noise in the morning from traffice. However, Cambridge offers every service you would need, so it was worth a little disturbance. 
 I included two photos that were taken out of our hotel room. We had views of both downtown Boston and the Charles River. 
 Really not a bad choice at all. I had considered staying outside of Boston and taking the T in, but both my son and I agreed that we just love staying in the city and this hotel made that possible without breaking my budget. Give it a try!

title: “Excellent Stay”
text: Excellent stay, super quick and friendly check in. Very clean room and pool was clean and plenty of towels available. Front desk staff friendly and helpful. Great location easy access to all areas of Columbus. Many restaurants and shopping nearby.

title: “Great Rates; Great Rooms; Great Service!”
text: Don't bother looking around Expedia or Travelocity. Call the hotel directly or check out their website, and you'll get just as good a rate. Now, for the money, this is MY kind of place! The rooms still smell new (all non smoking) and are in tip-top shape. Nicely decorated, too, with some Asian touches. The DVD surround sound systems are awesome, and they don't charge for rentals at the front desk. The beds are very comfy, and the Aveda stuff is really really nice! Bathrooms are large for a "boutique" style hotel. Marble all over. The DSL worked like a charm, and apparently they offer wireless now, too, in some rooms and the restaurant. The Bellmen are awesome. Cornell and James are too cool. Reception staff was very helpful, always smiling. Even when it rained! (They had these huuuge umbrellas you could check out free of charge). The breakfast is a nice touch, and where else do you get a buffet included in the price of your room??? That alone is worth probably 25 bucks... Now, this is not a 5-star hotel, but it's certainly among the best in its class when it comes to delivering expectations. You definitely get much more than you pay for - compared to other places I've stayed.

title: “What A Find!”
text:
In the past when Ivisited Dallas I usually stayed at a Sheraton or a Clarion Hotel. This time I decided it was time for a change and chose the Bradford. What A find! The clean well appointed room was just right. A real home away from home. The welcome basket of goodies was a nice idea. The staff was polite and eager to answer any questions.
I definitely plan to return and would recommend the Bradford to anyone.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: Excellent hotel in Washington DC and up to standards with the Mandarin Oriental brand. Large beautiful room, excellent lobby, and high quality service.

title: “Very busy convention hotel. Small room...”
text: Very busy convention hotel. Small room and bath but great view of the River. Long waits for elevators and service.

title: “Great Views and Location_DvB”
text:
This hotel is a little dated, which means smaller rooms with less placement planning . I would still recommend that you stay here at least once, and probably twice. On my next visit I plan on asking them to reserve a room for the first two nights on one side of the tower and for the next few nights on a different side or different tower… This is because the cylindrical towers offer large semicircular windows offering expansive views of the city.
It’s tough to provide a more detailed review, because of the combination of standard Westin features, like dual showerheads, heavenly beds, and brilliant location of outlets with lamps for laptop and other charging needs, with issues like slightly worn towels, a goofy bathroom door that nearly forces you to close it to maneuver, and lots of crevices that confound the cleaning ladies (I dropped a tissue and knelt to pick it up, and realized that there were large crumbs under/beside the bed hidden by the overlapping comforter and frame).
Still, you should stay here at least once. Forty-six floors up you can see the city and waterfront and take spectacular photos. The location offers a great base for excursions to Pike Place Market and several good restaurants. Also, it’s a little closer to the Space Needle than some other top-tier lodging options. The staff was friendly, the Wi-fi connection I the lobby was slow, and there are numerous pros and a few cons that I could expound upon, but why?
You should stay here at least once, end of story.

title: “Great airport hotel in Boston”
text: We stayed at the Embassy Suites at Logan airport for 3 nights post cruise before flying home. The hotel itself was your basic Embassy Suites with a large atrium for the bar/breakfast area. The service in the hotel was very good and we had a pleasant stay even though the weather did not cooperate. It rained heavily two out of the three days we were there. The location was very convienent for those of us having early flights. They have an airport shuttle every 10 minutes and the breakfast service starts at 5:30am which was great. It is a 5 minute or less drive to the airport from the front door of the hotel. Also all the flights are listed in their lobby so you can do a quick check to see if your flight is ontime even before you leave the hotel. There is a business area with free computers and printers. Overall a very nice stay (other than the weather)

title: “brilliant hotel to stay in”
text: just come back from a 4 night stay at jolly madison, the hotel was lovely, clean,hotel staff were friendly and very helpful offered to book tours etc,stored luggage on last day,room was nice view unusual but didnt need view was out exploring sights.didnt eat in hotel but theres a great deli round the corner from hotel so got drinks food from there.would definetly go back there its a good location for exploring ny,its a nice area with lots in walking distance have read other reviews so was a bit worried but doubts unfounded as had a wonderful time in new york cant wait to go back

title: “Simply Lovely Stay-SLS”
text:
The SLS is a cut above other high end hotels but it does so without having its nose up in the air like other 5 star hotels are prone to do. The SLS is contemporary, stylish...hot! but its staffed with people who truly care about your stay. 
It's the Staff that makes the difference. 
This was our 2nd stay at the SLS and there will be more. 
Note to those traveling with families; the SLS is not really for kids. They would have more fun elsewhere. But you and your spouse on your own? now you are talking!

title: “Trip Advisor rating is not always right!!!”
text: We had a great time staying here for a week visiting family. Rooms were clean and the complimentary breakfast was great as well. They were very accomidating by helping us get 2 rooms near each other since we had a larger group.
