My only concerns was our window did not lock and we were on the main floor, and our rooms were quite small aand a little cramped for 3 people. Overall it was a good and suprising experience considering the ranking on trip advisor. They should be in the top 20. =-))

title: “Great location, great service, great room”
text: Our Living Social deal was a fantastic value already, enhanced by the friendly efficient service and lovely surroundings of the Allerton Hotel. Check-in was quick, even though there was a line. The bell boys got us cabs quickly and our car was retrieved in 1/2 the time we were told to expect. I love a hotel where the rooms are not cookie-cutters, and this was the case at the Allerton. My only complaints were a noisy heating system when it cycled on and less-than-luxurious towels.

title: “One renovation away from being a great hotel.”
text:
This hotel has the best location of any hotel in Seattle. It is literally on a dock along the city's waterfront harbor. The views are simply spectacular.
But you pay dearly for location. 
The decor is a little odd and the interior halls are badly in need of renovation. They have spent money to upgrade the rooms which are interesting, but they've not spent anything to upgrade the interior halls, etc.
The hotel was built probably in the 50s or 60s and in some spots it looks like it.
But the rooms are nice, albeit a little inconsistent. The waterfront balcony rooms have fireplaces and balconies where you can walk outside and enjoy the spectacular views.
They are in a kind of rustic Northwoods look.
The bathrooms are simply to die for. Nouveau chic style with marble counters, cut stone floors, big fluffy bathrobes, an interesting table top sink bowl, a walk in shower with thick doorless glass and the best showerhead I've ever used. The kind with a BIG oversized head that's practically like being under a waterfall. 
But the motifs of the bathroom and the room are in total contrast. The mix is not very appealing stylistically, but they are comfotable.
The management doesn't get high marks from me because of the sign that says they want to save water so they will only change sheets every three days and towels only if you put them on the floor. But then the toilet and shower are not low flow and there's no sink drain stopper, so you have the leave the water running for ten minutes while getting ready. So much for water saving...it's clear they only want to save money not water.
But they don't return the savings. While this is a very nice hotel in a great location, it is terribly overpriced. I was on a business trip that was prebooked, but when I saw the rate I about died. Waaaaay too expensive. 
If they would do an interior renovation to clean up the hallways and bring down rates, this would be a spectacular hotel.

title: “Classic Hotel with Modern Amenities”
text: Upscale lobby, restaurant, great food, service, classy hotel. Only worth it if you can get a deal. The top restaurant (top floor) is outstanding and has a great dance scene where the locals apparently dine out and dance. Very upscale, dinner dress/suit type of deal. Nice staff, elegant, marble lobby, old world charm in a modern hotel. The celebrities stay here, like Connery and others, and for no wonder. Highly recommend this place to anyone staying in SF for business or pleasure. Very expensive overall, but very exclusive, private, quiet, and accomodating staff above all. Well-run place, we loved the place.

title: “Nice staff, clean, probably will not stay on the first floor again”
text:
All of the standard things you expect from a hotel are here. Friendly staff, clean, etc., etc. We stayed in room 117, which had a sliding glass door to the parking lot. It is probably just me, but it gave me the feeling of a Motel with access to the outside, instead of a hotel. If I was a female, no way would I stay on the first floor. I woke up all night hearing noises outside. My recommendation would be to get a room on one of the higher floors. Those seem safer. Our bathroom was tiny, with a little sink and since I was traveling with my wife, it was not enough space to put all her belongings on.
I am gold status with priority club and usually get a free breakfast with my room at Holiday Inn. I was told by staff when I asked that priority club had changed its policy and no free breakfast. I did eat the breakfast and it was OK, nothing spectacular. Kind of like a meal I would expect for free at Hampton, La Quinta, or the 100 other similar brands that have free breakfast, so Poo Poo to you priority club for taking this away from us. 
It is a three block walk to the Riverwalk, so this is a good, much cheaper alternative to the riverwalk hotels.

title: “Not what I expect from Embassy but still better than many.”
text:
This hotel was a disappointment as I have stayed at many Embassy Suites in the past. It would be a very nice hotel for those that are there for vacation or a quick stay but as I spend more time in hotels than I do at my home it was less than I had come to expect from the brand. 
The Homewood suites and Omni across the way are a far better investment of your money. 
The room was spacious, as is typical of Embassy Suites, but the actual hotel was very old and dirty. The breakfast was less than I have come to expect as the omelette's were small and the line reached across the dining area. The quality of the meats and vegetables that they stuff the omelette's with is questionable as well. They were VERY bland. Also, they may have a buffet later on in the day (I saw them setting up one day when I was off to a late start) but unless you are on vacation you have no access to it. This means that there are no eggs or bacon or any other breakfast of substance to be had unless you wait in the line (the chef behind the omelette counter has them under her supervision and only dole's them out upon request). So unless you are happy with Yogurt and bread in the morning get up EARLY to stand in line.
It is very difficult to get around for those that are not from the area as well for since it is located on one of the highway sideroads you must loop around the freeway in order to return to the hotel.
Due to the fact that their "shop" with necessities that you may have left at home was badly stocked I had to leave the hotel to try and locate some items. I received directions from the agent behind the counter and ended up driving around San Antonio for 2 HOURS before I could find my way back to the hotel.
On the flip side I did get directions to my office from a competent young lady behind the counter the next day and made out better from that point on. The young lady that I spoke to that AM was the only genuinly helpful agent that I spoke to behind the front counter during my entire stay. Not to sound snobby but I am a Hilton Honors Platinum member so I have met many of their employee's and this hotel definetly lacked much of the courtesy I have encountered elsewhere.
The business area is very outdated, as Embassy suites does not offer free internet connectivity I was made to use the area a few times during my stay. However, every time I tried to switch web pages it would knock me off the internet.
The restaurant is disappointing as well and has a very limited menu so be prepared to eat out quite a bit.
Bottom line is: Great for short stays, late risers (possibly), and vacationers but not top marks for those that are traveling on business or are there for a longer period of time.

title: “Stay Somewhere Else!!”
text:
I would not recommend this hotel to anyone. The rooms are very noisy from street traffic and in need of updating. My room was just above La Madeleine restaurant on M Street, and they started cooking at 5:00 am - very smelly!!! Worst of all was the lack of hot water for a morning shower! 
Don't stay here - there are lots of nicer hotels than this in DC.

title: “Had a great stay!”
text: I had a very great stay. My friend was getting married so, I stayed at the four points for one week. My room was cleaned everyday. The staff was very friendly, always helpful whenever I needed something. The pool was clean, the fitness center was nice and clean as well. I would definitely come back. Everything was just right besides the parking fee :(.

title: “Perfect Washington Gateway”
text:
We booked the Weekend in Washington package which included parking, breakfast and late check out; it was a perfect way to celebrate our anniversary. We were overjoyed with the way the hotel treated us; not only were they expecting us, but we got an upgrade to a beautiful large room with a huge bathroom, a chocolate fondue set up in our room with fruits, brownies and marshmallows and a bottle of champagne; what can be better?
The hotel is perfect in every sense, service is extraordinary, location could not be more convenient; after visiting a couple of museums we returned to the cool and quiet of our room. Thank you Four Seasons for making our celebration so special.

title: “Grand MGM!”
text: We had a fantastic stay at this hotel. The staff at reception were great and very helpful and friendly. Unbeknown to us, there was a Red Wings ice hockey match on during our stay and we asked the concierge if she could possibly get us tickets. The service (Jessica) provided was second to none, and we got really good seats and had a great evening. We were able to eat at Hockeytown just before the match and that was an enjoyable experience. The hotel provides a complimentary limo service within a 5 mile radius, and we were able to make use of it a few times. Again, the service was fantastic. We ventured into the vast casino one evening and spent some time wandering round and taking it all in - we had never been in such a huge place. Unfortunately, as smoking was allowed and we are non smokers, the atmosphere quickly became unbearable, which was a shame, as we would have liked to have stayed in there longer. But all in all, our stay was absolutely perfect and we would love to stay at the MGM Grand again.

title: “Great stay”
text: The hotel is elegant and modern and close to many stores and restaurants. It is also very clean and the rooms are quite comfortable. The staff is courteous and frinedly- Loved it! I would definitely stay their again

title: “Beware of the sea lions!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here for 4 nights..... Four sleepless nights... We stayed in 'The Suites' building that runs along the length of the marina and there were sea lions barking all night long every night that we were there. We tried to get a fan from the front desk to help drown out the noise but apparently fans are a hot commodity and there were none available. The bed was lumpy and very soft. The hotel doesn't use fitted sheets, so if you move around too much, the sheets start to shift and cause rolls of lumps that are not very comfortable to sleep on. The pillows leave something to be desired as well.... They smoosh down as soon as you lay on them and provide zero support. Another thing was this stench near the bed. It smelled of urine. I couldn't quite pin down where the smell was coming from, but it seemed to be coming from the carpet and/or the bastketweave fabric-like headboard. We actually went to Target to purchase Febreeze to help cover the stench. 
As far as the room itself, it is decent. It's a good size but with mildly ugly decor and a nice patio overlooking the marina. The fridge is a pile of crap. There is a warning sign on the fridge that says "Refridgerator can not safely store medical or dairy products", so if you're a milk drinker or need to store your insulin, you're out of luck. The fridge is very small, not even large enough to store a couple beers and a leftovers container. 
I did not try any of the restaurants on site so I can not comment on that. The pool area is nice and the bar by the pool serves a decent cocktail. 
I'll finish with something positive.... The hotel staff are friendly and courteous and the cleaning crew does a good job of remaking the bed and filling the towels and such. The hotel is in a good area with very easy access to highways and to downtown. The view of the marina truly is beautiful and is very nice to look out upon in the morning. 
As far as my ratings go, I'm giving cleanliness a 2 only because of the awful smell. Otherwise, the cleanliness is average of Hyatt - clean towels and linens.

title: “A great place to stay”
text: I really enjoyed my stay here. The room was a good size and was very clean and very comfortable. The ensuite was very satisfactory also. I found the staff to be friendly and helpful. I would have no hesitation in recommending this hotel.

title: “An Excellent 4th of July Visit”
text: This was our second year in a row for the Fourth in Boston. This year's stay was even better than the last. We had an awesome room on the 20th floor overlooking the Charles River which was picturesque by day and very convenient for fireworks watching - no rain! We enjoyed the personal attention of Claudia (front desk) and Claudia (breakfast nook) and being remembered by the lovely Jasoda (breakfast). Staying here was like staying with family, only in much nicer surroundings! With the convenient location to the MTBA train, the rental bikes at the Hubway, close to the MFA and all that Boylston and Newbury streets have to offer, we wouldnt stay anywhere else.

title: “Aged American Grand Hotel - a Queen”
text:
The Hilton Chicago has charme - the Lobby is fantastic, the staff is very friendly and the location in Michigan Avenue close to the lake makes it a fantastic location for shopping and also if you wanna make a run at lake Michigan.
The rooms itself are ok - a bit aged and with carpet, which is not my preferred option but in good shape and you can can open the window a bit - which is a very rare treat for a hotel nowadays unfortunately.
No minibar - Hilton Honours Members get bottled Water at the Reception (an interesting concept)
I would stay again - much better then many American Chain Hotels I have stayed before...

title: “Stay away!”
text: My friend and I stayed there last week. The hotel is fairly close to Hollywood, which is why we choose the location. Upon arrival we were informed that her credit card was already charged, so we had no choice but to stay. The parking lot was empty which was suspicious from the start. When we got up to our room we found that one of the two entrances were open, the windows were open (with no screens), and the room was about 100 degrees. The only way to describe the room would be crack head chic...we did stay since the room was charged, but we felt neither safe, nor comfortable. I wouldn't recommend this hotel/motel/sh*thole to my worst enemy.this is clearly a rent by the hour type of establishment. Pay $20 more and stay somewhere else...we should've!

title: “Location is perfect!”
text:
We stayed here for 8 nights. The location is about as good as it gets - walking distance to Chinatown, a few minutes to Union Square and a bus stop right outside the door to take you to Little Italy and Fishermans Wharf. Rooms are small but clean and comfortable. Not much of a view - our room faced on to an alleyway, but if you're planning to be out and about all day, this is a great little hotel. Staff were friendly and the breakfast was fine for the price we paid.....although they have the slowest toaster in the world!
If you're looking for somewhere fairly cheap, with a good location and simple but comfortable, would highly recommend the Crescent.

title: “Great location - inconsistent service and style”
text:
From reading the reviews if you are upgraded your experience is great - if you get what you booked well it is a bid dodgy. We waited 20 minutes to be checked into what was a crappy room. No coffee maker in our room either and there is no free wi fi. Our room had awful carpets, housekeeping was touch and go, concierge was also touch and go. 
Location is great however - near Central Park, Times Square, Rockafeller, shopping and MoMA. 
If you can get a great deal to stay here I would say go for it. If not I would try somewhere else. The hotel won't add any extra pizzaz to your stay.

title: “Think twice!”
text: Two things to note regarding my stay: 1. Check your baths towels before you start using them when you get out of the shower, two of the four towels had long strands of brown hair folded into them - disgusting is right! 2. Beware of having your vehicle valet'd at the hotel ... my vehicle returned with significant front end damage. It might be worthwhile parking on the street.

title: “Great Location!”
text:
I have stayed in several locations at prior visits and I enjoyed this location the best. Lets start with staying in, NJ. Prices may be good, parking usually free and then there is the cost and time dealing with bus service into Manhattan. Also stayed at the Waldorf a few times. You stay at the Waldorf to say you did. The amenities are fantastic but the beds were so uncomfortable, you were limited to your walking distance in Manhattan and then there is the price.
So, now for the Hilton Garden Inn. Location was great especially if you like to walk. One day we walk to the Chelsea Piers, through Grenich Village, to SoHO, lunch in Little Italy and eventually to Sea Port and Ground Zero. Yes, it was a full day but it was still manageable. The other way was a few blocks to Macy's and the Empire State Building,, Bryant Park, Time Square and then easily to 5th Avenue or Central Park.
The room here was very comfortable. Two very comfortable queen beds, refrigerator, microwave and good size bathroom. Staff was very friendly. As a Hilton Honors member you get free bottled water. Our view was of the flower district which was nice to look at in the morning when you open your shades. Within one block was McDonald's, Panera Breads, and Dunkin Doughnuts if you were looking for a quick bite. Breakfast at the hotel was steep at $16.99 per person so I didn't venture into the restaurant. One night we stopped at the hotel bar for a drink prior to heading off to bed. This was our only disappointment. My husband got one bottle of beer that as he said was "skunked" and I got a small glass of wine. Our total was just a few cents shy of $20. I thought that was high. This neighborhood was very safe. Never did we feel uncomfortable, day or night. The parking ramp was only about a block and a half away. With a hotel validation it was $30 or in our case $40 because we had an over sized vehicle (Explorer). It was a secured location and you don't have to worry about theft or damage. One more point, it's quiet at night. You can stay on the more populated area's but you will constantly hear traffic. Not here. It gets nice and quiet at night. 
Overall I would stay here again in the future and not even hesitate to recommend it to anyone who plans on doing a lot of walking to see all the sights that NYC has to offer.

title: “Outstading property!”
text: Great property with great amenities. Stunning rooms, plush bedding, decadent shower. Great food at Urbane. We ate 2 meals here. Wow! Will definitely stay again!

title: “Disappointed”
text:
My husband & I stayed here while I was in town for a conference. The only reason I didn't leave after checking is was b/c the stay was prepaid by my office. The front desk woman, I believe Khyla, told me the room wasn't paid for & didn't try to look for the notation that said otherwise. I had to call my office, & the booking company to get it sorted out. Aparently the note was on the computer had she justed scrolled down instead of telling me I was wrong. 
The corner room was tiny! I am a small person and had to angle by the foot of the bed to get between it & the radiator. The windows didn't function, neither opening nor able to shut all the way. Therefore the cold air and traffic noises from Michigan avenue were quite loud. 
The toilet was stuck, flushing for five minutes each time it was used. The front desk sent up the "engineer" and afterwards, the toilet flushed for only a minute each time. 
The room appeared very worn with noticeable stains on the capet, chips in the wall paint, and sadly, the curtains didn't close, which would have been nice to block out light. 
The one thing the hotel had going for it were the concierge, 2 extremely helpful and nice people with great advice.

title: “Love the hotel atmosphere.manager Sherida...”
text: Love the hotel atmosphere.manager Sherida Green was very helpful, courteous, and went above and beyond to help us with all of our needs

title: “Very nice staff”
text: The welcome I received at the Doubltree Downtown Boston was quite warm and the staff were all very friendly. The beds are comfortable, as at most Hilton brand hotels. The building, I think, must be rather old because the elevator was tiny! The room could use some updating and new carpet, but other than that is just fine. I wish they didn't charge for WiFi!

title: “Very nice stay”
text: Room was well-appointed and quiet. Location was great for North Beach, the Embarcadero, the Wharf, the Marina District, and even the Golden Gate Promenade was a nice walk. Really appreciated the coffee in the lobby and the Trader Joe's and Safeway nearby.

title: “Incredible Service and Trustworthy Hotel”
text: Recently stayed two nights at The Joule in Downtown Dallas. I travel a lot for business and for leisure and I like to stay at the nicest hotels available. The Joule exceeded my expectations. With the vibe of the "W" and Hotel ZaZa but with exceptional service. We ate one breakfast, one dinner and Brunch at Charlie Palmer....it was outstanding. One individual I would like to commend is Trey Schultz, the Director of Security. I had left behind an entire bag of jewelry in the dresser. I called Trey immediately the following day and he quickly called to let me know he recovered it! I was not expecting this. He also FedEx the package to me on their dollar. Again, that is going above and beyond! We will be a regular at The Joule!

title: “Eww...”
text:
After backpacking in Central America for the last three weeks I was looking forward to staying in a hotel with a little higher standards. Unfortunately we didn't check the trip advisor website until after we had checked in.
The bathroom reeks of urine, and, although it says it's a non-smoking room, the room smells like stale cigarettes mixed with a musty odor. 
The bathroom is filthy with moldy grout in the shower, a dirty floor, and the toilet was cracked with a nasty toilet seat so old that it had turned yellow. There are pubic hairs all over the bathroom and counter.
Outlets don't have faceplates and the phone jack was ripped out from the wall. Very dusty and grimy.
The airport shuttle driver couldn't be bothered to hang up his personal phone call to help us with our bags.
Although it is August, and 95 degrees the pool is closed, and looks like it had been for a while. Don't be deceived by the pictures. This place is gross.

title: “Great location”
text: Located right by old town, which is great for restaurants etc. rooms clean but fairly basic. The rooms open off veranda type long balconies. This looks lovely, however there were tables and chairs out there which were used primarily by smokers,and by people chatting late at night. This did keep us awake and we were annoyed. The hotel shuttle bus on the other hand was excellent. It took us not only to the airport but also to the harbour one day saving us a taxi fare.

title: “Excellent.”
text:
I stayed at the Biltmore for a very busy business conference, so I was not able to explore all of it, or use many of its facilities. I also don't know what the rates are like so I can't really comment on the value. I hear you can get VERY good rates at this resort during the summer months.
The rooms were excellent. Sparkling clean, very large, very comfortable, and all of them seemed to have nice views. The bathroom in my room was huge and well equipped with a luxuriously deep tub and separate shower stall, heat lamps, two sinks, a separate vanity with stool, and a totally separate room for the toilet. The bed was so comfortable. My room was part of a building that had a small very private feeling pool in the courtyard. Just beautiful.
The grounds were immaculate, but you hardly ever noticed the staff around working on them. I did not get to see the entire resort. It was August, and I'm Canadian. So even just the walk from my room to the meeting centre left me breathless from the heat.
The surrounding neighborhood seemed very safe and well kept. It was nice to be able to take a walk off the resort and see the local architecture. Very different from my home!
There main pool was huge, clean and beautiful. There were private cabanas with cool mist.
The meeting facilities were excellent. Very large and well equipped. And there were several of these large meeting rooms available in a few different buildings.
The food was excellent. Even the buffet type snacks and lunches were fantastic.
I don't remember the service being remarkable, but it was not lacking either. I'm Canadian, so I find most Americans a bit rude (they don't apologize constantly ha ha). I do remember feeling that they were very polished and professional.
I think my favourite part of my stay was having drinks on the patio in the evening. The heat was tolerable after the sun set, and the grounds are lit in such a beautiful way. It was so comfortable and relaxing.
I did not get to see the golf course, but my colleagues were talking about how nice it was.
I did not get to use the spa facilities either, sadly. No one else in my party used them either so I can not comment on that.
I would definitely recommend this resort for business or pleasure. Especially if the prices in the summer are as reasonable as I heard.

title: “Could Use Some Improvements”
text:
Stayed here for one night and here are my observations on the plusses and minuses:
Plusses:
1) Great location
2) Terrific water pressure in shower
3) Comfortable bed
The minuses:
1) Lots of street noise (I was on 12th floor). Having stayed in many other midtown hotels, this was by far the noisiest. Windows must be original construction
2) Flat screen TV's, but no HD! It's 2012 folks. Watching a standard def picture on a flat screen tv is ridiculous for an upscale midtown property
3) Others have observed that you cannot adjust the room temperature by yourself. You must call the front desk to have someone come up. Not very practical. I returned from an evening engagement at 11 o'clock to find the room chilly. Was I really supposed to call the front desk at that time and wait for someone to show up to make the room warmer?
I do hope that the hotel will consider improving on these points.

title: “Great for the price, free shuttle, no breakfast included”
text:
This hotel is very good for the price and I would stay here again. Good things: there is a free shuttle to/from the airport, which runs every 25 min ***or so***, there is a good gym with great equipment, the bed is good, the room is nice, the soap is quite nice (for hotel soap).
The bad: the shuttle doesn't come very often. It is shared with other hotels. We took the Hilton Doubletree shuttle when we arrived, the driver agreed to take us because the Hilton LAX is on the way anyway, that was really nice of him. The hotel has carpeted floors everywhere, which I hate since I am allergic. It is very clean, but could be cleaner. For breakfast, you either pay 20 USD for a buffet style breakfast or you can get a 10 dollar sandwich or a bagel at the deli. I thought there should be a 10-dollar option that would not be as bad as having a sandwich for breakfast. And options to dine at the hotel are not great either. Either a quite expensive Italian restaurant, or a sports bar. We went to the Marriott and ate there, it was quite nice, just a couple of blocks away.

title: “Awesome views, perfect location”
text: I have stayed at this property many times for work. Arriving at the Island Palms is the highlight of my work in San Diego. You can take in the grand views of this beautiful city without leaving your room or balcony. Great beds and large bathrooms are like being at home. I prefer rooms with a Marina view but the rooms facing the Harbor and city skyline are equally impressive. The staff (Danny/Kaiser) go out of their way to know your name and follow up once you check in. They truly seem to want to make your stay as nice as possible. I highly recommend this property to anyone considering visiting San Diego. It is very close to all the main attractions of the south county.

title: “Perfect for a health concious business traveler”
text:
I was shocked that this was the most affordable available in my company's booking system. I signed up for the rewards, had a "get fit kit" in my room (includes a yoga mat, wrist weights, and a resistance band). So assumed since they had that benefit, their gym would suck. Not so! They had tons of machines with individual tvs on the cardio stuff, was open 24 hours, and had a giant bowl of apples and oranges available for free every morning. My rewards also got me a free wake-up beverage of my choice at a time specifically listed by me. Everyone was incredibly nice, and my room was great as well. Just couldn't believe how well an old classic hotel catered to those trying to stay fit while traveling, not typical.
My room was out of an elevator and then right, but I heard from a co-worker that out of the elevator and left isn't as nice, and is noisy at night, so you may want to request a room change if you are there.

title: “Perfect”
text: I have stayed at Ghirardelli Square twice over the past 18 months, but haven't written a review until now because quite frankly I had nothing to add to the comments from others. We stayed in a one-bedroom suite with a terrace and bay views. Superb quality of furnishings, a kitchen better equipped than my own, supremely comfortable bed and bed linen. The only shortcoming was no bath, but really........that is being very picky indeed. I like this location because it is walkable from Fishermans Wharf but much quieter. The San Francisco bus system is excellent, and there is a stop right outside which takes you through Chinatown to the centre of the city - we only used the complimentary car service once, because we didn't need to. The staff couldn't be more charming and helpful - their restaurant recommendations were first rate, and they even managed to organise our (second) booking at Garry Danko at a day's notice. So..........in summary if there were six stars available they would be worth it.

title: “Great muffins”
text:
This hotel is perfect. The deluxe rooms inc your own bathroom which is well worth doing. The room size was as expected from other reviews but that was not a problem and neither was any noise (room 716). Consider asking for a room off the main street. 
The hotel seemed popular for young people and business. 
Other reviews said the hotel is dated but we didn't see this at all. We found it modern in style, clean and well presented.
Getting to the hotel from SF Int airport on the BART was very easy and the hotel is at the centre of the bus, tram, cable car network. Tip: buy a Muni pass (all buses, trams and cable rides inc but not the BART) for the time you are there, it was $21 each for 3 days. When you consider a single on the cable is $6 and the fact SF is so hilly you will use the pass all the time.

title: “Nice location. Average hotel.”
text:
The two things that Hotel On Rivington has going for it are it's location and the rooms.
We stayed in a high floor room with Japanese soaking tub. The room was a good size but in need of a lick of paint. We had a fantastic view of downtown from both the bedroom and bathroom.
The hotel bar is fairly dull and also in need of some care and attention. It gets busy for after work drinks but apart from that there isn't much going on. You're better off going to the bar next door.
Breakfast was a continental buffet affair with anything hot involving an extra charge!
I would look elsewhere in future.

title: “Stylish, small rooms, attentive staff, an oasis in the theater district!”
text:
My daughter and I stayed here and had a wonderful time. We felt very special and pampered, entering the oasis-like calm and dark from the tourist-bustle of Times Square. Staff were helpful and nice. Our room had some burned out lightbulbs and they changed at least some at our request while we were out. 
The lobby, bar, and rooms are newly renovated and chic. We enjoyed the lounge music and the Marilyn Monroe movie playing in the bar. Our room (a standard queen) was small but elegant and well-designed, like a ship's cabin. I'd recommend they add a second mirror, though, perhaps over the desk. With the small vanity it was impossible for us two girls to get ready at the same time. We liked the bathroom area open to the room (pull across a curtain for privacy when showering) and the swanky glass-and-marble shower and vanity. The bed was very comfortable and the linens fine and crisp.
With the small, cozy room size, this would be great for a couple.
We enjoyed the complimentary continental breakfast, as well, which included mini bagels, croissants and pastry, cereals, fruit, coffee, juice, etc. I especially enjoyed the warm boiled eggs.
Unfortunately the TV was out because of construction, but they comped us one pay-per-view movie as compensation. The heating/cooling unit was quite loud and despite tinkering it turned on/off all night which was not terribly restful. Without it on, the room was too hot. But because the room is so small, it flipped back and forth quickly between heat/cool mode to keep at the desired temp. Not sure how that could be helped...
All in all, we definitely enjoyed our stay. Without spending a huge amount, we felt pampered and special. Thanks, Sanctuary!

title: “Unfriendly”
text:
Hotel foyer looked great, we were expecting good things from a 4 star New York hotel unfortunately that's where the good things stopped. No help from door staff on arrival, the reception staff were unfriendly and unhelpful, even on asking a simple question felt like we were just an inconvieniance to them. The room was shabby and tired looking, an electric socket was loose and half hanging out the wall, the heating unit was noisy and also coming off the wall.
Worst hotel i have stayed at and i have stayed at quite a few all over the world

title: “Convenient to airport and comfortable.”
text: This is an okay place to stay convenient to the airport. The room is clean but the bed isn't very comfortable.

title: “Great place and friendly staff”
text: Got a great rate on priceline here (around $55)...the staff is wonderful, they do charge for parking but its not too bad- like $10 a day or so when i was there....its close to a T stop and takes like 20 minutes to most places in Boston. All in all this is a very solid choice for cheaper accomodations in the Boston area (more accessible than Cambridge).

title: “Great hotel and fantastic location”
text: My wife and I stayed here for five nights on the 40. floor in the Tower suite, an excellent room, spacious with a magnificent view of The Empire State building and the Chrysler building in the other direction. Fresh softdrinks in the fridge every day, very clean and very good beds! We loved staying at this hotel. Close to Times Square, Macy's, The Empire State building, Fifth Avenue, Hells Kitchen Area... The staff was very friendly! Breakfast in the sky-lounge was ok, not a lot to eat, but ok. In weekends you get a voucher for breakfast at the Tick Tock restaurant. That was also ok. Next time we visit NY, We will come back to the New Yorker Hotel!

title: “The Place to be in North Hollywood!”
text: Just got back from a five night stay at the BG Holiday Inn and thought it was comparable to a Marriott. This facility is self-contained; pool, restaurant, coffee shop, and bar all on the well-manicured premises. Great central location for touring Hollywood. Reasonable rates and friendly staff. Only downside was the[--] in the blond wig holding a mop who knocked on the door at 2 a.m. one night claiming to be "the Beverly Garland" and asking if we needed house cleaning service. Maybe this was just part of the Hollywood experience.

title: “Excellent”
text: We were referred to this location by a friend. We staying in a king suite. We had a door in our room which took us right to the pool. The room was clean. The bed was comfortable! The pillows were awesome...so awesome I just ordered 2 from the Homewood Suites Collection. The parking was good, customer service was excellent, and the price was affordable. I saw some ratings that said it had seen its better days... I disagree. Completely satisfied and will stay when we return back to Charlotte.

title: “A+++”
text: Amazing hotel! I can't say enough about how much I loved my stay here. I arrived on opening night and needless to say there were a few small details that were still being ironed out, but the staff made sure to go above and beyond in making up for it. The front desk staff and housekeeping couldn't have been more friendlier or helpful! The view was great and I loved the overall design and feel of the lobby/restaurant areas. Very chic! I will definitely stay here next time I find myself in NYC. Plus, this hotel has turned me on to all the great boutique hotels that are part of Ascend Collection like the Distrikt. I'll now look for these hotels everywhere I travel. Love Ascend and Love the Distrikt!!!

title: “My Second Stay Here Was Even Better Than The First”
text:
About two and a half years ago, I stayed at this property before making a connecting flight to Australia. This time, I had an overnight layover between my flight from home and my flight to Auckland via Tahiti.
I booked my stay through Hotwire, same as last time, and was happy with the low rate.
The hotel is great if you are using terminal one (Southwest, USAirways) as it is just across Sepulveda Blvd. from the terminal. Shuttles run every twenty minutes or so and can be crowded, but are a great convienence.
The lobby is clean and nice, with sitting areas,a bar, restaurant, and gift shop. There are a number of conventions held here.
The sleeping areas were quiet, and the room I received clean and comfortable. The double glazed windows are a bit dirty, but I was OK since I was more interested in the blackout curtains.
I had lunch in the bar area. The prices a bit high for what you get, but the food tasted great, and the service was excellent. I reminded myself how much I saved through using Hotwire and enjoyed my lunch.
I walked down Century Blvd. in the night. It was alright, but a bit dark. There is a Subway restaurant a block or so to the east, a Denny's and a Carl's Jr. about a mile east, past the Hilton.

title: “Always a great stay!”
text:
Whenever I travel to San Jose I stay at The Fairmont, this is the best place in San Jose. Always a nice experience, great staff, clean and very spacious and comfortable. The Grill has excellent food and the lounge in the main lobby always has great entertainment, a true pleasure! 
I travel often and since my 1st stay at The Fairmont San Jose a couple of years ago, I now stay at The Fairmont Dallas and The Fairmont Boston at Copley Square.....Whereever I travel I try and find a Fairmont location to stay at.

title: “Very so-so for as highly it is rated”
text: I booked a suite for a vacation in Chicago at over 500/night. When I got to my room it was dirty, the carpet stained and the furniture in bad condition. I went to the desk and their answer was 'oh the suites have not been redone yet but are due". Oh great. The space was nice, it was great to have 2 baths (lousy shower head) and nice view. But very "3 star" not 5 star at all. They offered me a free breakfast for the condition. They have a house car, but it seemed to always be booked and not available on Sunday and Monday. The pillows were so soft I got a head ache and the beds were not very comfortable. The room was dusty and not well cleaned and the dirty carpeting was a real turn off. It is a great location but certainly did not live up to expectations. Outdoor bar was great.

title: “Silver Cloud Inn - Never Disappoints”
text:
We stayed here after a long flight home from LA.
Before the flight we stayed near the airport and just had an awful experience. So we decided to just go with what we know for the trip home. Yes, it was about a 20 minute drive from the airport, but at least we know what we are getting when we stay at any of the Silver Cloud Inn's. A clean comfortable room. With beds you can just sink right into. I love that the parking is gated, not that it's going to stop someone who is really bent on breaking into your car, but it was nice.
The 24 hour pool was great to come to, since our kids were just wired from the flight, and it was a great time to just go down there and let them relax.
We got up too late to enjoy the breakfast, but if it's anything like the other ones we have experienced at other Silver Cloud Inn's, I'm sure it is wonderful.
If you are looking a clean comfortable room with great customer service this is the place to go.
We will definitely stay here for our next trip to downtown Seattle.

title: “Excelent Hotel”
text: This hotel is close to Union square and the trolley cars. The rooms are clean and spacious with great views of the bay. The staff is friendly and always go the extra mile.

title: “Very Inviting”
text:
Just enjoyed 3 nights at the Hotel Indigo Chicago Gold Coast. The staff could not have been nicer. We wondered if they might have a cribbage board we could use - not having one the manager actually went shopping and not finding a cribbage board brought us a checker board and some chocolates. Talk about above and beyond!
Also the rooms were clean ,the showers hot and the neighborhood was quiet and we felt we received good value for the price.

title: “Good Family Hotel”
text:
Staff: was extremely accommodating - we asked to switch rooms to have a courtyard room and they did everything to assist us, even called us the next day to remind us that a room was available 
Cleanliness: no complaints
Amenities: pool water clean and warm to swim anytime, breakfast was good and well stocked even after close, they still tried to feed latecomer's. Lastly, need new mattress on hideaway bed - OUCH!
Location: great, can walk to many good shops and food. With a car much is within a short distance drive.

title: “affordable and confortable”
text:
I loved the hotel, it is a small hotel with great service and spacious rooms,
they have a shuttle that took me to downtown everyday and also picked me up!
its great for families, they are friendly and clean,
breakfast is ok, the hotel nothing luxurious but everything comfortable!
I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Wonderful Boutique Hotel right in the middle of everything!”
text: This elegant little hotel is tucked away right in a perfect location in the middle of the Theatre district of New York. The staff is fantastic, the rooms are spotless and nicely decorated. We found we were only a few blocks from Times Square, a subway station, the best restaurants, and the play we wanted to see. We even took the open air bus, and though we usually don't like tourist type things, we really saw a lot of the city without too much walking! The tour guide educated us on great tidbits such as the restaurant grades that are posted on the window of each establishment by the health department! The fact that the Museums are free, though they "suggest" a price. The wonderful architecture of the buildings is so much more visible from the bus!! I am not running into people! We will return often!

title: “Great location but you get what you pay for!”
text: The best thing about the hotel is the location and the cost. The staff on arrival were not very professional and didn't seem to what us there. Our room had an off-putting smell (we had to spray perfume to cover it) and all the furniture was tired and old with the fridge hanging off the wall. The bed was very soft and not very comfortable. They claim to have a garage but our car (Mustang) wouldn't fit in so you may as well add $20 fee for each 24hrs you wish to stay the accommodation costs. Breakfast was very limited but the cookies and muffins were nice. In a nutshell cheap and cheerful but a central location and you just need somewhere to sleep.

title: “Excellent Location”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Warwick Hotel for one night after our cruise. The location was great. Only 2 1/2 blocks to subway station, one block to 5th ave, and a couple of blocks to the rockafeller center. The room was huge and clean. It had a huge walk-in closets and a mini bar area. However, there are a couple things that they can update, such as the window curtain in the room and the carpet. They were quite dirty. The staff was very courteous and polite. I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Brilliant location.”
text:
This is a great place to stay if visiting N.Y. and you want to do all the usual sights and sounds of the city. You can walk to most popular places and there is also a subway right by the hotel...ideal!
In our experience some Hiltons can be a bit hit and miss but here the staff our great and it´s all very clean and a comfortable place to make as your base. We were on 4th.floor and could hardly hear the train at all. Everything was spot on, and although we never ate at the hotel so can´t comment on that, we thought that this hotel offers excellent value for money considering where it is located and the good standard they provide. Of course there are numerous places to grab a bite to eat everywhere, so whatever your taste you´ll be happy. We would stay here again on our next trip to N.Y.

title: “La Quinta is Spanish for..."Next to Denny's"”
text:
Stayed here for a Friday night trip to the Riverwalk. I was not expecting the hotel to be as nice as it was!
Check in was standard. Went up to the room and discovered there were some small black curly hairs lingering in the shower area. Eww. Went back downstairs and explained that housekeeping should probably revisit our room. Was promptly moved to another room and given two free drinks in the hotel bar. YAY!
I certainly wasn't about to let those drink coupons go to waste, so we got dressed and returned to the bar. For a Friday night, the bar was empty and that was perfect. I forgot all about the problem with the first room...thank you, drink tickets!
We spent the rest of the night on the Riverwalk which culminated in a trip to Denny's on our walk back to the hotel. Yes, Virginia, there is a Denny's right next door. 
If you are wondering, the hotel is about 1/3 of a mile away from the Riverwalk itself and right off of I-35/I-37. Well within walking distance to major downtown landmarks and across the street from the Rivercenter Mall.
The room itself was well-sized, comfortable and clean; full of useful amenities. We didn't make it to the breakfast buffet.
Parking is extra, and they do offer valet service but it really wouldn't be worth it as the regular parking lot is right in front of the main entrance. 
Overall, we were very happy with our stay and would visit this hotel again.

author.location: Austin, Texas (We're full...so come visit, then leave)

title: “great stay”
text: My husband and I had a great stay at your lovely hotel. We visited Seattle to attend a baseball game or two. The hotel is a nice walk from the stadium Super location, room appointments and service. The location is ideal for forays into Pike Place Market. Thank you.

title: “Positive experience. Would go there again.”
text: The rooms are not too small. The lack of bedside lighting was not good. I was tired after a day of sightseeing and wanted to put my feet up and read while the other person in the room slept. I had to sit in the less-than-comfortable desk chair to do this. No shelving in the bathroom a problem. I don't like throwing my clothes or towels on a bathroom floor. I called ahead b/c I was traveling with a sick teenager so I requested a quiet room. They gave me one, but with one double bed. Kind of a curious choice since they knew w/ whom I was sharing the room. We were ok w/ it, but how many people would feel the same? Other than that, a very positive experience. Lively lobby scene, fantastic location, helpful staff. Housekeeping knocked at my door at 8:30 a.m. on Sat. Not a problem for me, but maybe for some people. For the price I would definitely use this hotel again.

title: “Nicest staff I have ever encountered”
text:
The best advantage is the wonderful staff. They are all friendly, personable, joyful, and helpful. They are more than happy to serve you. We were able to get discount tickets to Willis Tower, advice about the free trolley to Navy Pier, and they made reservations for us to the Wendella combined boat tour. We were able to park early in the day and ride the "L" to Wrigley Field. Then, leave the car the next day until 5 pm while we ran around the city. Even the parking staff are so pleasant that they offer to move your car out of the parking place without even asking. I have been to many places across the US and to several foreign countries. This is the best staff I have ever seen.
Otherwise, the accomodations are just as good or better than a Holiday Inn or Hampton Inn that we use regularly. We took advice from these reviews and asked for a larger double room. We got a room on the south of the main tower that was quiet - no sirens or vehicle noise.
The location is fantastic. Only a few blocks from Pizzaria Uno, the red line "L" and the free trolley. They are a block from Hard Rock Cafe and many other fine restaurants. We walked to Michigan Avenue and Trump Tower. 
The value for the location and helpful staff is worth trying this place out. We will definitely visit here again. I have already recommended it to others at work.

title: “The Sportsmen's Lodge Is A Winner”
text:
My stay with the Sportsmen's Lodge was excellent.
The greeting by the hotel staff was the first level of excellence. My room was squeakly clean and the bed was so comfortable.
The grounds are unbelievable, once you pull in the parking lot it is easy to forget that you are in the city. As you explore the poolside area and see the area that is available for outdoor events you will be amazed and the buffers for sound like the waterfalls and foliage. Yes, it is a beautiful spot for an outdoor event.
Parking in LA is a huge issue, the Sportsmen's Lodge has ample parking.
The Sportsmen's Lodge has been chosen as our host hotel for the upcoming Welcome Home to Jericho Charity Event scheduled for April 2009 and I am extremely pleased this hotel has been our winning choice!

title: “Great location and staff, room location is key”
text: Second time staying here. Great location for Times Square and Theater District. Rooms are comfortable, clean. Rick's lounge is a great bonus for breakfast, tea and cookies after the show, etc. The staff had told us that there would be construction across the street until midnight and offered to move us to another of their properties. We thought would be fine since it would be that late before we went to bed. The noise did stop at midnight, but then returned from 1:30-2:00 am. I would suggest asking for a room not facing 43rd street. There were no sound issues in the interior rooms.

title: “great staff great hotel”
text:
We booked this hotel with a great deal from Priceline. The last time we used Priceline the hotel staff did not seem very nice nor would they respond to special requests even though we spent a lot of money in the spa and for golf.
THE STAFF AT THE PARKER IS WONDERFUL. When we mentioned it was our anniversary they upgraded us to a king bed on the 38th floor with a park view. It was wonderful. The room was lovely, bed and bedding fabric was clear. They delivered ice within minutes and just treated us great. 
I can understand why some might dislike the burger smell but the burgers (wish we could have tried one but not enough time) must be great since there are always long lines. 
I can't say enough about this hotel. the pool is lovely. the bar is beautiful. the room service was great. 
We can't wait to go back

title: “Very Nice”
text: My family and I stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn on Eighth Avenue during Christmas. We were in the city to shop and catch the Radio City Christmas show. The rooms were clean and the hotel was quiet. The restaurant next door is great - especially breakfast. The staff was helpful. I was provided with certificates for free breakfast for our family of five for three days. The manager on duty was born in a town near us and was very friendly. There is a firestation near the hotel, but I only heard one siren during my entire stay. The firemen were also friendly and told me about the men they lost on 9/11 - my children were impressed by their stories. In all, this is a nice, clean hotel at a great price. My only gripe was with the television in our room. It was a new, digital flat-screen and the channels changed very slowly. I usually stay at the Waldorf-Astoria, but decided to try a hotel a little closer to the theater district.

title: “Excellence on Exeter St!”
text:
We stayed here for one night on Feb 10th.
This hotel truly is top class for the the money. It is not too big in a convenient location.
The staff were very helpful in recommending restaurants, bars and what to do in the city in the short space of time we had.
The room served our needs perfectly and the bed was up to the usual Marriott comfort with the featherbed topped mattress and duvet.
They were serving a chocolate fondue in the foyer/breakfast area just after we turned up this was complimentary and good fun, I believe they do something similar everyday.
We had the continental breakfast buffet the following morning which was very good. Plenty of fresh fruits, yogurts, cereals, pastries, coffee & juice, particularly enjoyed the granola topped yogurt with the strawberries in the base!
We would stay here again for sure if ever in Boston again.

title: “Doesn't get better”
text: When we checked in, we were pleasantly received by the reception office. The room smelled beautifully. Everything worked. The room was very clean. The internet connection was excellent. The lobby area was very delightful, especially since we were there to celebrate Elvis' life. Everything in the lobby was Elvis. The pool was well maintained. I would definitely stay there in the future if they will have me. One more thing: this place truly observes "southern hospitality".

title: “Déjà vu all over again, which was great…”
text: We stayed at an Embassy Suites in Washington last summer (reviewed) and this was very consistent. We liked the big rooms, full buffet breakfast and happy hour drinks and snacks and pool (which like the one in Washington, was very small indeed). The inside is unique in that all the rooms open into a 10 storey atrium, so it’s like staying at a 1980’s mall. The common area décor matches the theme. If you can help it, avoid rooms facing the back alley and parking lot as early morning garbage pickup will serenade you each day (crash, boom, bang go the big containers). Also, WiFi is a bit of a cat and mouse game. They charge for it but you can get comp passes and on the second floor, you can sniff out other free WiFi from places like the next-door Starbucks. My theory of more expensive hotels charging for WiFi (whereas cheaper hotels don’t), holds true. Still, a great deal and stay for our family of four.

title: “Great hotel”
text: This hotel was excellent. Clean and comfortable rooms. Great staff. Nice gym. And next to great shopping and tons of restuarants. This is my preferred hotel for future business trips to the area.

title: “A Pleasure As Always...”
text: This is for a review of the smaller building where the rooms are bigger. I recently stayed at this hotel again over Thanksgiving 2012 for 10 nights. This place was as good this time as it was back in May of this year - except it was better! All of my reservation requests were met, there was not 1 problem at all the entire stay, and any and all interaction that I had with the staff was nice. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone that wants an affordable place near the freeway so that you can get all over whatever parts of LA you want to visit!

title: “Wonderful hotel!”
text: My husband and I also just stayed in room 708 (see other recent review) -- and yes, the room IS small! However, we didn't mind the size because the room and hotel are so great in all other respects: the decor and amenities are modern, stylish, and clean; the staff was courteous and professional; the continental breakfast was fresh and delicious; and the location is terrific -- 1/2 block from the subway and surrounded by amazing Indian & Southeast Asian restaurants (try Chennai Garden)! We would happily stay here again, and would recommend it to anyone looking for a NYC hotel.

title: “Stay here if you're transiting through DFW”
text: From booking online months in advance to checking out, our experience was fantastic. Booking was easy, rate was fantastic and included breakfast. The room and facilities were excellent and every single customer service staff member encountered went above and beyond to make our stay that little bit extra special. The nachos was the biggest serving of anything I've ever ordered!

title: “Marriage Island Wedding”
text: We got married on Marriage Island, which is right outside the hotel's river lobby. We had several out of town guests stay. Everyone got a riverview room, which was nice. The hotel is beautiful! The Cork Bar and the resturant are on the expensive side, but I would recommend the Sunday Brunch. Don't expect any free extras here. Even the internet will cost you $10/ day. I would stay there again, but will make sure I bring a fatter wallet.

title: “Great deal at Homewood!”
text:
My family and I, (3 kids) really enjoyed this hotel. Plenty of room. 
The kids liked that there were two tvs. The complimentary hot breakfast and the light dinner were perfect ways to start and end a day of touring around the city and helped save alot of money - since meals at all the tourist spots were hughly inflated. Lots of room, very clean, very friendly. All this leads to a great family vacation. One negative was no pool.

title: “Classic New York hotel”
text:
Stayed in this hotel in June 2008. Paid £108 a night plus taxes through priceline. Beautiful lobby area with huge flower display. Rooms were quite small but all in taste of era of hotel. Was between two subway stations about a five minute walk from each one. Concierge service was good.
Entrance to hotel was not that clear when accessing from subway station.

title: “AWESOME EXPERIENCE”
text: I stayed at the SLS Beverly Hills on December 2 & 3, 2012. The hotel was very clean and my room immaculate. The staff wonderful. Leah welcoming and respectful. Raheleh extremely kind and genuine. Fredo helpful and outgoing. Lisa K. friendly and professional. The yogurt was amazing...not the typical yogurt. I only had breakfast there, but it was fresh and good. Valet staff courteous. Definitely recommend staying here.

title: “Not all it's cracked up to be.”
text:
Very surprised this hotel is #1 on tripadvisor - very surprised. I booked this hotel based on its rating.
I travel frequently on business...this is NOT I repeat NOT a hotel for the business traveler.
The room is nice, it's upgraded with a nice layout. 
BUT: 
-I waited in line at checkin for 10 mins. Finally checked in and was given my key, went all the way up to my room with all my stuff and the key didn't work. I schlepped everything downstairs again, received a new key with no apology. 
-The carpeted stairways are dirty. Visible crumbs and whatever else.
-An elevator door opened to see two 'bell racks' the racks used to transport luggage. Just two bell racks, no bell person. Thought was a strange occurrance only to have it happen again with another elevator. So they just leave the bell racks in the elevators...don't put them on service. You can't get in unless you're very small.
-The sheets in the room are flimsy, and thin. Surprisingly they spent money on the refurbishing of the room but not a penny on the linens. There is no duvet on the bed - just a sheet and cover. If you have a tendency to get cold, prepare by asking them for extra blankets.
-There are no toiletries provided except for a mini shampoo, and it's cheap.
I can see how this hotel appeals to families on a budget with the convenience of free breakfast, but if you're used to traveling and staying at 3 plus star properties, this is not the place for you.

title: “Another great W location”
text:
Recently stayed at the W hotel in Austin for business was quite impressed with the hotel. The service was top-notch, the rooms was modern and well thought-out, and the restaraunt and bar scene are what you'd expect from the W. We had to go over the convention center and the doorman insisited that the W's courtesy car drive us over which was a nice touch.
The only negative on the property are the heavy guest room doors which make quite a bit of noise when closing them,. If you're neightbors come in late or leave their room early, don't be surprised if you're awakened by what sounds like someone slamming the door.
I definitely plan on staying here again.

title: “We would stay again”
text: Having lived in Washington, I knew that I wanted this hotel for its location and interior. I bidded 4 star on Priceline in Woodley Park and got it. It's right over the metro, yet well removed from the noise on Connecticut Ave. Rooms are clean, spacious and modern. Free wifi. Overall I'd stay here again.

title: “Top Notch all around!”
text:
Loved everything about this hotel. I stayed here on business and brought my husband along for the ride. Check in was a breeze...as we entered the building, they called up to the front desk and by the time the elevator reached the lobby, someone greeted us, walked us to the front desk and got us checked in in record time. Our room was beautiful; large and spacious with a floor to ceiling window with a great view. There is also a very comfy window seat and the windows opened! The bathroom was marble with a shower and a separate oversized tub.
I had drinks in the lounge and ate several meals there during our meetings. One night I tried to book a late massage but they did not have any appointments left so the concierge arranged for an in room massage that was excellent.
The hotel is in a great location within walking distance to the Ferry Building, China Town, Coit Tower, etc. and public transportation is right outside the front of the hotel. I would stay here again anytime I visit San Fran! Thanks to the staff for all of the great service!
Food Tip: The Grove is a great place for breakfast or lunch which is about a block away from the hotel. Super yummy!

title: “Decent hotel”
text: We stayed here for one night before heading to Kauai. We did call the hotel for the shuttle and it arrived within 5 minutes. The room was dated yet, it is clean with a comfortable bed. We did ride the hotel shuttle to the lightrail station (two minutes ride/ten minutes walking); the shuttle driver was profesional and courteous. We ued the lightrail and connect the famous monorail to Space needle (the fare=$18.00 for two people travel time one hour); instead of renting a car, lightrail is the way to go; we ate at the Space needle restaurant with the money we saved from transportation. The view at the rotating restaurant is amazing; food is decent. We had a wonderful time and excellent rest before our flight to Kauai. The hotel's close proximity to the airport and courteous service made our trip really enjoyable and hassle free. We had breakfast buffet at the hotel restaurant before hopping on our morning flight; it is okay.Overall, we enjoyed our stay at the hotel and ompliment to the Radisson management.

title: “Small stay, but very good”
text:
I was there for just one day, but had a great experience nonetheless. 
The check-in was very quick, and the front desk lady gave me a corner room, which offered great views of the Beverly hills, and I could see the "hollywood"sign from my room. The room service and house keeping was great, and the food in Culina excellent. 
Highly recommended.

title: “Really nice cozy Hotel”
text:
Me and My Wife stayed at Vintage Court Hotel in June 2000 for 6 nights in a Standard Deluxe room. We did have a very nice time and staff were really nice and funny. Room was nice with a partial view of Bank of America tower. Nice bed and a cozy atmosphere. We also liked the lobby with the nice fireplace.
Hotel Vintage Court is located in Nob Hill with short walking distance to Union Square and Chinatown. 
We really loved this hotel. And we are returning in May this year with 2 friends.

title: “Wasn't planning to stay Wait staff made the difference”
text:
This is a "hidden" gem in Washington DC. It's not pretentious like four $ restaurants and Hotel but their food quality is great. We tried going to a French bistro for a spur of a romantic moment but the French apparently can't pick up their phone. Then I remembered the 14 k Lounge in the Hamilton Crown Plaza.
My mom raved about their brunch when she stayed at the Hamilton Crown Hotel (14k Lounge is their on-site restaurant). I've had their salad for lunch year prior and remember it being expensive but good. The atmosphere is of a bar and dining room. It doesn't scream romantic but the lighting, the quietness (not many people were dining in the part we were in) and the attentiveness of the waitress made our night. 
The server was a professional, a professional waitress MaryBeth or as she said MB, how all waitress/waiters should be. She knew exactly what to say, do, didn't hover, didn't make me feel bad that I didn't order dessert. 
We started with Tuna tartar and continued on with mixed green salad and oven roasted tomatoes drizzled in Balsamic reduction, the Filet Mignon, and Grilled Trout wrapped in bacon the a crab corn stuffing (Seafood special of the day).
The tuna tartar: artistic perfection and fresh tuna. The chips that came with the appetizer had the perfect amount of crunch that fared well with the softness of the the tuna. The salads were excellent. The balsamic reduction was sweet and was an amazing combination. 
Marybeth asked if I wanted my steak medium or medium rare. This is how I know she knows what he is doing. Steaks should only be enjoyed medium or medium rare. Since you should just go to the butcher and skip the restaurant if you want to eat rare, and anything cooked beyond medium is basically horse meat. I've never had a horse, but I heard their meat is tough. 
The filet mignon melted in my mouth. So juicy and tender.
TheTrout Filet was so juicy and flaked off with a hint of a touch. No need for lemon since the fish was fresh and almost creamy in the mouth. The sides, I had the mushroom and he had the grilled veggies, were cooked to perfection. The mushroom wasn't soggy but juicy and the grilled veggies were had the smokiness that paired well with its own juices and balsalmic dressing. 
The service was great, and our server was happy to answer any questions we had about the entrees and to make suggestions on the wine selections. I don't drink a lot of wine, and when I do it's usually a super sweet like moscato, but both the dinner and dessert wines she suggested were not too dry for me to handle. I can say we had a little to much to drink to drive buzz drive home. The waitress suggested for us to see if they had any room. She went to the front desk and asked. We were able to get a great rate for downtown DC on a Friday night. We decided to stay the weekend. 
Such an wonderful location to be staying while visiting Washington DC. We had a room that faced the park and it was such a great view to see the architecture at eye level and then look down and people watch. The room was Not too spacious and open but fit the bill. Shopping is at your fingertips (as we did not plan to stay the weekend) If you are looking to venture out a bit, the Metro is really close or my favorite way to explore a city is just to walk around. Washington dc is an extremely walkable city but if that's not your thing then their Metro system is pretty good too.
This Crown Plaza is kind of in the middle of everything with the hustle and bustle of 14th and K right there you can pick a direction and just go and you'll get somewhere where you want to be. North, South, East, or West point and go. Location means a lot when picking a hotel and this is a great one.
The concierge Innocent is so friendly and even funny to boot. Very informative. Great suggestions whether you give them something to go off of your tastes and likes or not. It's a really Beautiful historical hotel. That Saturday night we went to dinner again looking for Marybeth and was told she was there only to find out she was off. Our service was horrible. A waitress was very bubble but you could tell she was getting off soon as I heard her say she was going out. I saw her on her phone in a little room in the middle of the restaurant. I had to ask the bus person to get the check so we could go. ALL in ALL. I enjoy the stay. Food was good rooms were clean and a great Location.IF you stay I would really try and get Marybeth as she know her stuff. also Ryan at the front desk was so helpful with the toiletries bag as we were not planning to spend the night. I will come back and send my friend even though I live only 30 miles away in Maryland.

title: “A very nice place to stay; convenient.”
text: Stayed here for business. It was convenient and the staff was very helpful. Rooms were spacious and nice. Free breakfast and evening reception were an added benefit.

title: “Awesome hotel--trendy, clean, great staff, cool amenities”
text: I booked this hotel as part of my husband's birthday celebration based on reviews and pics I had seen of the hotel, and we were not disappointed! It is one of nicest hotels we have been to and we would definitely stay there again (and in fact we will definitely check out other Kimpton hotels if we ever get a chance to do so). The decor is very trendy and the complimentary beverage stations (hot chocolate, wine, and coffee/tea) are a great touch. Every staff member we encountered was very friendly and helpful and went above and beyond to make sure we had a wonderful stay. I can't say enough good things about it!

title: “Great people, great location, great hotel”
text:
We had a fantastic time staying at the Distrikt recently. For a hotel that is so central the service felt really personal and it made an amazing trip to New York even better. The rooms are lovely and they couldn't have done more to make us feel at home and make our trip special.
Time Square is minutes away and there are plenty of restaurants/bars close by. Despite being right in the heart of things the rooms are nice and quiet and of a good size. It would absolutely be our first choice next time we go!

title: “Great Stay!! Great Location!! Great Staff!!”
text:
In the service industry, it is the little things that really set places apart. The Catamaran really shines on the little things.
I got a really early start, and went to the Catamaran about 8:30 am or so to check it out and to see what the neighborhood was like. I stopped at the front desk to see when the best time to check in would be. I was only staying one night, so I did not expect them do do very much in the way of accommodating an early check in. Sure enough, they didn't have any rooms ready for me, and the best time to check in on a Saturday is around 4:00pm. I was a bit disappointed to hear this, because I wanted to spend some time on the beach. But then he said that he had a room that was scheduled to be out of circulation for maintenance. What he would do was he would give me a card for that room, I could put my luggage in there, use the key to go in and out of the parking lot, use the key to get to the beach or the pool, and use the room to take a shower in. At 4pm, just see him and he would give me the key for our actual room for the night.
He then gave me some great recommendations for on breakfast and coffee places around the hotel. Just great service. At 4pm, there was an envelope at the front desk with our room keys. 
No muss no fuss! 
The room was clean, and just as we ordered. We were in the 700 block of rooms and found it to be very quiet. We spent a great night.
The beach was a white sand beach that is combed daily. It is free from glass or anything else that might cut your feet. Very close by there is a place that is operated by the hotel to rent, paddle boards, little sail boats, and even jet skis. Complementary beach umbrellas and chairs were right on the beach as well. There weren't very many of these, so you have to get to the beach early to claim them.
The little things matter, and the front desk could have very easily just said, "Come back at 4" and done with me. Instead they went the extra mile to make my stay very enjoyable!

title: “Excellent D.C. Hotel”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for several nights when on business. The hotel is older yet has been updated to high standards. The staff was friendly and accomodating. 
My room we very nice and included a coffee maker, refridgerator and free wi-fi which worked well. They also provided free bottled water every evening delivered to my room as well as a morning newspaper. Both the room and bath room were spotless. It was very quiet and the bed comfortable.
The hotel has a great outdoor pool perfect for the very hot summer days. Having a pool was a great way to cool off and there are not a lot of hotels in D.C. that have pools. They also have a great poolside cafe with frozen drinks and food.
The hotel is about a 10 min walk to the Metro or to the White House. There is also a Capital Bike Share rack across the street from the hotel which is a really easy and inexpensive way to get around or to tour.
Overall a great place to stay and if you watch the specials you can get some really good prices as well.

title: “Great value”
text: Stayed four nights at the Hotel Deca and found it very accommodating with friendly staff, good shuttle service and in a great location in the university district. Will definitely stay there on my next visit.

title: “Excellent service, nothing they couldn't help me with”
text: I stayed for the night and lost my baggage with a cancelled flight. The very kind manager, Juan, helped to direct my to a local suit store and let me borrow his tie for an appointment I had the following day. They also changed my room to a very quiet one and had a b'berry charger for me to borrow. Finally, they gave me a bag to use for my return to Europe. The trip would have been a total shocker were it not for the service at The Marcel.

title: “Wow”
text: Great hotel, nice rooms and perfect location! Highly rec!

title: “Great value and good Marriott quality experience”
text: Very good value, great clean room with nice amenities. Very loud lobby.

title: “Great hotel”
text: The service at Hotel Valencia was excellent and the staff was extremely helpful. use of the TV in my guest room was not user friendly. My colleagues expreienced the same problem. Our meeting room was at street level and the traffic noice was a distraction during the meeting.

title: “Great location - good experience”
text: My husband attended a conference and I tagged along. Steps away from Convention Centre, the light rail train was at the door. Great spot for all the banks and near many attractions. We did find that the shower door made a huge puddle on the floor - but the bathroom was spacious and bright. We thoroughly enjoyed the stay. The bed was comfortable, everyone was extremely pleasant. The only complaint we had was Sunday everything in the area closes down because it's the financial district, so at lunch time everyone decended on the restaurant. The food was very good and reasonably priced, but my poor hubby almost got indigestion because we waited so long to be served. Wewent back a couple of days later, and while there weren't as many customers, we did have to wait a fair bit for the waitress to settle up. We were able to walk about the downtown area and were even able to find a small grocery store.

title: “Bed bugs”
text: Very filthy, we discovered BED BUGS in the morning,we notified the front desk, they did not care and tthey we're definitely aware of their infestation. We did not receive an apology or any sort of compensation . We will definitely not stay at an Econo lodge again.

title: “Terrible! Do not be fooled by their website!”
text:
We stayed for five nights. We booked an oversized room. It had indeed 450SF but no furniture! No table, no chairs. Just an old sofa and a desk. Barely something to put your stuff on. We had to squeeze our toiletries on the small artificial marble shelf surrounding the sink. The sink was clogged the entire time. The bathhroom was dirty at our arrival. We complained and they really sent someone to have it cleaned. Still, there was dust everywhere. Do not go if you have allergies! The room did not have enough lighting. Do not book a room if you are depressed! An old CRT-TV was mounted to a pole in the corner. Attached was a VCR (Yes, a VCR - not a DVD player. Welcome to the 20th century). The bucket of ice we ordered at arrival was never delivered.
In general: The bathroom was tiled with very cheap tiles, the upper part of the walls were painted in dark gray. The room was more like in a two star hotel in Rumania: Dark, dust everywhere, outdated! I assume they did not do any renovations in the last 30 years.
New York is a great destination. Me and my wife go twice a year. But in this hotel never again!

title: “Small rooms, but good location.”
text:
Stayed for 5 nights...the check-in was easy and staff were very nice. They originally did not assign us a room based on our request, which was to be on a high floor away from the construction. They immediately switched it before we even went upstairs, but only on the 5th floor. We had a "king" bed, which was actually two twins pushed together. The room itself was small but plenty for what we needed (a nice, clean place to sleep and rest). The bathroom was also small but clean. Had lunch in the restaraunt and were the only ones there, so service was fine. Views of the memorial were spectacular. Went back one night for a drink and views at night, which were also great. Had a nice dessert at the W hotel across the street. 
The best part of the hotel was being right near the memorial. There were three subway stations in a 5-10 minute walk. The place was surrounded by NYPD, which made me feel very safe. Plenty of bars/places to eat nearby. 
Staff arranged car service to Newark for us and it came right on time, but cost $75.
For some reason I have two holds on my credit card for almost $1000 each, and my bill wasn't even that much, so hopefully that will get fixed soon.
No bed bugs! My husband even complained that our room was TOO quiet.

title: “You can't beat this location”
text:
Location location location! This is the best location in NYC. It is right across the street from the Bus and Subway terminal so if you like exploring outskirts you wont have to walk long. It is literally 1 block away from Times Square. The rooms are very typical Westin type rooms, with the amazing heavenly bed and the Miller office chair.
