The only negative comments I have is that sometimes there where a lot of people dwelling at the Lobby and they were clearly not guests at the hotel and there is no security for going up to the rooms so if that is an issue for you do reconsider your lodging stay. I also have a bit of an issue that they charge you for using the fitness center....
However, if you want a really great bed with a hard to beat location, this is the hotel for you!

title: “Fatal Flaw”
text: We were looking for a nice place to spend our anniversary. On paper, Lakeway seemed perfect. The Spa services were nice, if a bit pricey. The hotel room was nice, but as another reviewer mentioned, cheap sheets and a motel six bathtub. The fatal flaw was the pounding on our door at 8:00 AM by housekeeping. We weren't planning on sleeping that late, but is 8:00 AM is a little early for being forced awake. After asking housekeeping to come back later, they began vacuuming in the hall in next room. So instead of leasurely morning, we were in our car by 9:00 AM with no plans to return.

title: “Exceptional”
text: We treated ourselves to a Bridge to Bridge view room, although expensive, it was well worth the price. A large corner room with a view from the Golden Gate to the Bay Bridge on the 41st floor. In fact the guest rooms begin on the 38th floor. The room is well appointed, the bed was superb, and it is very quiet. We have stayed at many of the finest hotels in the City, including the Four Seasons, and this is the best. Everyone is gracious, attentive and efficient. It feels more like the best boutique hotel you've ever stayed in. We had the full American breakfast in our room, and it was as good & hot as if we were in the Brasserie.

title: “Absolutely Fabulous!”
text: The location is great and service spot-on. I had a truly wonderful and effortless stay. Kudos to Eliecer Garcia who provided an much needed evening libation with my popcorn. Definitely will stay at Hilton Fashion District again and recommend to my friends without hesitation.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: This hotel was very very clean. Also very quiet! I have never been at a hotel with elevators that were so fast, we were on the 13th floor and never waited longer then a minute going up or down. The pool and the area surrounding it was also very clean with plenty of chairs and towels. the view of the water front and city was a bonus.The work out room had plenty of equipment to do any kind of work out you needed, weight, cardio or core. This area was also very clean with towels even had cool towels in a refrigerator and water. Also nice sauna. They have a restaurant we did not try and also a little cafe for coffee, cake or a breakfast sandwich. You can walk into town from the hotel I did, and you are right in the middle of Penn's landing. I have to reach to say anything bad, and here it is they could have used a few more channels on the TV. Recommend this hotel highly.

title: “Very Nice”
text: Enjoyed this hotel - very nice and clean, with the best beds we've had. Only concern is the location - but still not bad.

title: “Nice Hotel - Basic Amenities - Good Value”
text: This hotel is incredibly positioned for the future - once all the construction is done in lower Manhattan it will be in a prime location and, as another reviewer noted, the prices will probably soar. At this point, it's in the midst of a maze of construction - but that is truly not a hindrance. Like all Club Quarters, the rooms are designed to maximize space efficiently and there are fewer amenities. There is no restaurant or bar in the hotel. Nice to have a fridge and microwave, I would imagine, for longer stays. Irons and extra pillows are found in the "guest closet" in the hallway and you take them as wanted. No bathtubs - just "gym-like" showers with curtains. That said, the room is very well laid out and comfortable. Incredible views from the floor-to-ceiling windows. A number of places to eat and drink within short walking distance. Free high speed internet. The staff need a bit of polishing in terms of customer service, but not rude.

title: “Great stay at Clarion”
text: We had an excellent stay at the Clarion and will return. Staff went out of their way to make us feel at home. Room was A+. Food was exceptional

title: “Friendly MGR”
text:
Location is OK, still can walk to the Hollywood Blvd. Price is good. 
Hotel manager(?) was very friendly and gave my wife an eyewash when she has a trouble with her eye. If you are looking for a reasonable price hotel, this is one of them.

title: “Extras without any extra payment!! Fantastic”
text: What can I say? After reading the reviews on tripadvisor, I booked this hotel and was not disappointed. Upon arrival, was greeted by cheerful staff who quickly reallocated us to a quieter room as my husband didnt want to be disturbed by passing traffic (its located off the freeway). The room was spacious and very, very clean. Had hair dryer, ironing board and iron, microwave, tea and coffee making facilities plus fridge and TV. Would have been great if it had a safe, but that's just a minor point. There is a small pool, gym and you can buy snack food at their "pantry shop" - though supermarkets are within 5 mins drive. They also have an onsite laundromat so you can wash and dry your clothes for about $1.50 each machine, which we did. Great "kick back" at 5.30pm, we saw many guests eat this as their main dinner instead of pre-evenings snacks. They served hotdogs with buns, baked potatoes, salad, chicken breast bites, crisps and popcorn. Each guest is allowed 3 free alcoholic drinks and soft drinks are limitless during this period of time. Also on site, free wi-fi and access to printer, free printing (if you needed to print your boarding passes) and one hour free international calls each day, and local calls are free. My husband and I enjoyed our stay here, even though it was not a fancy 5 star hotel which we usually stay in, it was a pleasure to stay here and I would not hesitate to book this place again when we next visit Houston. Location was great for shopping at the huge Galleria complex and equally great for dining local fare like Taste of Texas, Goode & Co, Saltgrass and Kata Robata.

title: “Excellent”
text: Fantastic location. Friendly & Knowlegable Staff. Large comfortable rooms. Great Restaurant. Highly Recommended.

title: “Good value and location”
text: Nice bedding, clean room, flatscreen tv, good continental breakfast, bar in hotel, safe area, friendly staff. Within walking distance of Empire State Building and Times Square. I would stay there again and overlook the unreliable hot water, the disappearance of some of our small toiletry items from the room, and the tiny, slow elevator.

title: “First Class Contempory Hotel with Excellent Service”
text: The Hotel staff was very friendly. They welcomed us back everytime we returned from being out. The hotel lobby is very relaxing and inviting. The wine Happy Hour everynight was enjoyable as we meet people from all over the world. It is close to the metro and every kind of cruisine you could image. Great clubs nearby also.

title: “Good Room for a Quick Stay”
text: We stayed at the West Los Angeles Airport for less than six hours on our way to Kauai in April. We arrived at the hotel approximately 1:30 in the morning and we found the person at the front desk very friendly. The bed was very comfortable. We had to be back at the airport at 7 a.m. We used the free shuttle to and from the airport and we found the drivers to be very nice and helpful. The hotel is only a few blocks from the airport, so it is a great place to stay if you have a layover in LA.

title: “It is what it is !”
text: Where were the pictures of the rooms taken for this add ? in another Motel they don't look like the room my wife and i had during our trip on the weekend of 4/20/2012 . No wash cloths no shower curtain , no frig. ,no microwave , air conditioning sometimes when it worked . What is the deal with the free breakfast ( packaged snacks ) ? but the coffee was good ! $92.00 / night with tax . Like i said at the start ( It is what it is ) All in all we had a Great time in San Antonio and we did have a place to sleep out of the weather for the most part . To the owner i hope the renovations that you haven't finished go well on the room we stayed in room #150 i would suggest after scrapping your ceilings clean up the mess and re-install your fixtures ,the handle in the tube fell off on my wife's foot and vacuum the floors, after seeing the other pictures on this sight I and my wife can support them as well .

title: “Very pleasant surprise in the middle of the Loop”
text: Lovely stay.. The arts and crafts decor was very tasteful, nice wood, lovely bathroom, all very clean, lots of space to keep organized.

title: “amazing stay”
text: My family & I had the opportunity of staying at Hotel Angeleno for my cousins's Bar-Mitzvah. Everything was excellent & everybody was friendly & professional. However, two people stood out amongst the employees. The first was Joseph at the front desk. Besides being friendly & professional, he went the extra mile with any & every request that my family or myself had. He treated us like we were royalty.He is a great resource for the hotel in repeat business because we will stay at the Hotel Angeleno on our next trip. We hope Joseph is still there. We're sure he'll probably be the manager on our next visit. The second person we'd like to recognize is Emilio in the restaurant. I ate breakfast there a few times & he was very polite & attentive. The food was excellent & the service immpeccable. Thank you for an enjoyable stay. Miles Warren

title: “Very Nice”
text:
I recently spent 4 nights at the Maxwell Hotel. I was very pleasantly surprised by the overall feel of the hotel; Modern, yet cozy. I particularly liked the ease of connecting to high quality internet in the room. On the plus side - Feel of space in the room that was decorated in a minimalist theme, comfortable bed, great location, free on site parking, mini fridge and microwave, in room safe.....
On the negative side; low pressure in the shower head, small table-top ironing board, and not enough hanging space in the closet.

title: “A pleasant surprise at the Hotel des Arts”
text:
We reserved a room at the Hotel des Arts after seeing it recommended in a New York Times article. We were a little apprehensive about it. After all, what can you expect for $99 a night in San Francisco?
We were very pleased with our experience. The room was clean, quiet, and comfortable. The location was great. And the breakfast was a plus, with good coffee and muffins, bagels, and yogurt.
After staying at so many cookie-cutter hotels with the same trite pictures on the walls, it was a pleasure to stay in a room that had been spray-painted by a New York graffiti artist and to see work by other young artists in other parts of the hotel.
We would most definitely stay there again.

title: “A pleasant experience”
text: This hotel whilst not outstanding ticks the respective boxes for somewhere to stay on a budget in New York. Its location is fine only a short ride on the subway to all the main attractions and the staff were helpful when required. Yes the rooms maybe could do with alick of paint but other than that i thoroughly enjoyed my stay. However be careful when using the lift as it is an experience to behold.

title: “Double Dipping Bookings”
text: Stayed November 11th in a "wedding block" room-no particular complaints as the room was fairly quiet, adequately appointed, although it was difficult to shut out city lights and attain a level of privacy, and despite temperature controls, the night was chilly and there was no extra blanket in the closet. The real issue was that we stepped out for breakfast the next morning from 8:30-9:30, and, although we did not check out and were not planning to do so until close to the 12 PM check-out time, our room had been cleaned and given to another couple in the hour that we were out! When I explained this unfortunate situation to the manager at the front desk, and described how four people were made exceedingly uncomfortable (we used our key card to re-enter the room and were aghast that a couple was occupying it), all I received in the way of a response was a perfunctory "I'm sorry". Am I cranky or this this situation absurd and unacceptable? The short stay was $319.31 including tax.

title: “Exceptional Service”
text:
We had an amazing visit to the Hotel Commonwealth this past weekend. From minute one we were wowed by the impressive Samuel Famuyide. When he politely inquired what brought us to Boston, my daughter replied that we were celebrating my birthday.
Settling into our lovely room and planning our day, we were surprised by a knock at the door. We were given a bottle a Prosecco and yummy chocolate truffles accompanied by a sweet note from Mr. Famuyide.
It doesn't end there. At dinner off-site, I was given a mini-dessert with a candle once again the result of Mr. Famuyide's intervention. 
We also loved the restaurant Eastern Standard and ate there twice. Staff and food were both terrific.
I would -- no will -- visit this hotel again.

title: “Home Away From Home”
text:
First off, Worldmark is a private club and you must either be an owner, or know an owner to stay at any of their locations. My wife and I have been owners since 1995 and we have never regretted the decision to buy into the resort. We also have provided many of our friends, who are not owners, the ability to stay at the locations. 
The Worldmark Mission Valley is located just off the I-8 freeway within a stones throw of downtown San Diego. This particular location was formerly an apartment complex that Worldmark bought and converted into the condo format. It backs up to a sheer hillside, so if your unit backs up to the hill, that is your view - dirt. Worldmark does not let you request a particular unit, so you are at the luck of the draw when it comes to your room view. For us, that is not a big deal, just be aware. This location has an excellent front counter staff. They are friendly and knowledgeable and are eager to point out local attractions. All parking is free and is underground - dry and safe. The units are large and all include a kitchen for eating in. The TV in the living room is really too small for the unit. It could stand to be bigger, but it certainly is not a huge negative. We have stayed at numerous Worldmark locations and this is one of our favorites. There is a swimming pool and hot tub, a recreation room featuring pool tables, big screen TV's, movies to rent and more. El Torito restaurant is directly across the driveway, and every Thursday they feature $3.00 margarita's during happy hour. One point of irritation for me is the check-in process. All of the Worldmark locations are going to this format - after you check in, you are sent to another desk to "pick up your parking pass." All this really is, is a sales pitch to get you to attend a presentation. They will offer you a $50-$75 gift card for dinner, but you have to attend a one-on-one presentation where well trained sales people will hammer you to buy a membership. Unless you have two to three extra hours you want to waste, my recommendation is to politely decline. 
Overall, this is a great place, great staff, wonderful rooms and clean surroundings.

title: “Does not live up to hilton name - bad service”
text: Typically, I think of hilton having good customer service. Not at this location. First off, I dropped my wife, kids, and luggage off at the front since I wanted to go park on my own and save $20 a night. (btw....if you park behind the hilton, it's $25 bucks a day versus $45 in the Hilton). I asked my wife to check in for us. She waited in line for 10 minutes, and then I received a call. She told me they would not check her in since it's under my name. I asked her to put them on the pnone, and she said they would not talk with me. 3 minutes later, I walked in and by then they had already moved on to the next customer. Of course, I was mad, but I figured I could handle waiting in line for a few minutes. Then, another line started to form as many people began to arrive at once. I realized we were all standing in the Hilton Honors line, and others were entering on the main line. So of course, the clerks started helping those people just arriving in the other line (not the Hilton honors line) before us! Why are there two lines and if so, shouldn't they be helping us in hilton honors line first regardless (i'm not sure most people noticed the difference in lines and no one was helping funnel traffic). So there were 3 desk clerks to help the 20 people in line. I thought they were short staffed for such a nice hotel. Of course, there were 7 bellmen waiting to grab our luggage! Maybe they should switch up their staffing and prioritze what guests really want? fast, speedy check ins after long drives in traffic. When I got to the clerk, I told her it was rediculous that my wife couldn't check us in? She never even asked for ID to see if the same address and last name? Also, I put a sign on some pizza boxes to throw away each day, and they never threw them away. the bar (not the irish place) has sllow service too! Overall, a nice looking hotel with horrible service.

title: “Great hotel for sound sleepers”
text:
First time stay.
PROS: comfortable layout, clean linens, room and bathroom, comfortable beds (but not pillows), nice and helpful service at the front desk and all the other workers, swimming pool and whirlpool were clean and nice (but a bit too small and had no place to change). Quite efficient free breakfast.
CONS: noise from the street (which could be eliminated with the closing heavy draperies on the window) and noise from the heater/air conditioner (particularly when it goes ON and OFF). Light sleepers will only “survive” with the earplugs. 
Still I would stay here, but next time with earplugs.

title: “Great location in an Elegant Hotel”
text:
Stayed here July long weekend for two nights. It was a great way to start off our stay in Chicago. Gorgeous decor with a swanky bathroom. The bed was comfortable. There is a Starbucks attached to the hotel.
No bed bugs.
The staff were very professional. My husband forgot his toothbrush and they gave him a complimentary one. Valet parking is a little expensive but it's the price you pay for the convenience.
Most of the tourist attractions are within a 15-min walking distance. These included the Art Institute, Sears Tower, Tastes of Chicago, Aquarium and Metra. We got the CityPass which is highly recommended, especially on the July long weekend. 
I would recommend this hotel.

title: “The Strand”
text: This is the best hotel for the money in NYC. The rooms are very clean, no noise and good location...We had a problem with flight cancellation in St Louis and Mavis(?) on the front desk was the very best in helping us out. Went way out of her way to help, the whole staff was GREAT..You may get a little cheaper price in NYC but, I will alway go back to the Strand as we visit our son about twice a year.....Vern, Scottsdale, Arizona

title: “Great fun, very stylish, very comfortable and convenient”
text:
We really enjoyed our two-night stay. Perfect service, nothing ever amiss, absolutely clean. Chose the Executive King, which was very spacious. Every detail of the room was just-so. 
The location was great for hitting the theaters, all the new and old Tenderloin restaurants, shopping. Starbucks right there, essentially in the hotel. No view from the room, but that wasn't a surprise. Quiet room -- ours was in the back, windows looking on another part of the building. But the fun, racy designer window shades made up for it.
There are numerous common-area lounges in addition to the business center. Cool artifacts to be found in all of them. One lounge was full of high-concept designer lamps.
It's definitely urban, but didn't have any worries about the folks we encountered on the sidewalks. Nice restaurants in both directions, and the American Conservatory Theater right across the street.
Would definitely stay again.

title: “Worst Marriott Ever”
text: The most of the staff was difficult to get anything from. The hotel has more rules that I have ever heard of, each room only gets 4 towels, 2 blankets, etc...Although the rooms are really large for a NYC hotel that is about the only thing this hotel has going for it. The elevators are so crowded sometimes you can't get in. I would call it more of a factory than a hotel.

title: “Middle of nowhere but close to everything”
text: Looking for a room just a week before the visit and really wanted to stay right in downtown Seattle. Found nothing cheaper so I booked one of the last rooms available. It was in the middle of nowhere (nothing interesting around the hotel) but walking distance to a lot of attractions including Pike's and the Space Needle. Showed up fairly late with a reservation and got the dog of the rooms - balcony was over the top of the neighboring yoga studio so all you could hear is the rooftop AC unit going. View was of neighboring office building. The front desk was polite but unable to produce any pillows when requested (the room had a queen sized bed with 3 very small pillows). If you use the pull out sofa bed keep in mind that you many not be able to use the desk provided without climbing over the top of the pullout. With 4 people we only had 3 very small pillows between us. How many hotels run out of pillows- really? Decor was fine. Parking was free but extremely tight. Leave behind anything larger than a minivan. Breakfast was the basic stuff of the free breakfast moderately priced places. For $220 it was not a place you walked away feeling good about it, but downtown Seattle is surprisingly expensive. Would I recommend it? Not really but if it was the last room left, I would say it was only marginally better than the alternatives.

title: “The comforts of home in the convenience of Midtown”
text: I've stayed at The Benjamin countless times over the past 10 years. While convenience to my office is what initially attracted me to the hotel, it was the atmosphere and staff that kept me coming back. Staff members are friendly, helpful and always willing to go the extra mile to make sure guests get what they need. The rooms are a good size with a soothing color palate and to my knowledge, most have refrigerators, sinks and microwaves. This is essential for both business and leisure travelers who like to keep their own stash of beverages and snacks without having to fight for space in the mini-bar fridge. Overall, I recommend The Benjamin to anyone staying in Midtown who wants to be close to the action without having a lot of extraneous noise and people milling around like other nearby hotels have.

title: “Very Nice Downtown hotel”
text: I stayed there for a weekend getaway with my wife and we were truly amazed with the excellent service and added amenities. If you are a member of the Omni Club program, you receive plenty for your money. The room we got was spacious and clean overlooking the fountains on the Plaza. The hotel atmosphere is nice and the staff very friendly and welcoming. I recommend for weekend getaways, business travelers and families who want to be in the city center close to Hollywood and the underground.

title: “Great location... but noisy!”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for three nights en-route from Hawaii to the UK. 
We were located on the 3rd floor in the annex building. The room was spacious and comfortable, and our bathroom was huge! We got a free newspaper delivered every morning. 
The best thing about this hotel is it's location - it's opposite Fisherman's Wharf and all the attractions around the bay, e.g. Ghiardelli Square, Pier 39, tourist ferries around the bay / Alcatraz, etc. We walked to Lombard Street (up an impossibly steep hill) and back in approx. half an hour. The terminus of the 'F line' tram to the Ferry Building / Market Street (where all the main shops are) / Castro district was literally across the road - it's only $1.50 each, which includes a free transfer within 90 minutes. The terminus of the Powell / Hyde cable car was also only a few minutes walk (I'd recommend getting there early to avoid the queues. We got there at 9.30am and got straight on. It's expensive though - $5 each per journey.) 
The only downside to the hotel was the noise from the street. My advice if you're staying here is to ask for a quiet room (there were some rooms overlooking a central 'courtyard', which may have been quieter) or bring earplugs! We also encountered lots of noise from hotel staff, e.g. banging doors, so don't expect a lie-in!

title: “Great stay in NYC”
text: Beautiful boutique hotel in NYC. Good location ... far enough away from the major crowds of Times Square, but close enough to walk. Hotel was very clean with friendly, knowledgeable service. It's not a 5-star hotel so don't expect anything over the top. The ice-cold, fruit-flavored water in the lobby was perfect after a long day in the 95+ degree heat. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Horrible horrible service.”
text:
We arrived at the Ramada Inn Hotel in Chatsworth on Thursday May 19th for a four night stay on the occasion of a close relatives wedding.
The wedding was set to take place at noon of sunday, may 22nd. At about 10am on the morning of the wedding we went down to get something out of our car, to our alarm the car was nowhere to be found.
We rushed to the front desk to ask if they know anything about our car being gone. The receptionist explained that the due to construction in the parking lot, our car has been towed and suggested we call the towing company.
When we asked why is it our responsibility to contact the towers and retrieve the car instead of hers, she replied " well because it's not my car...". This very rude response offended us deeply.
We next asked to see the manager. The manager on duty was Mr. Ben [--]. When we explained the situation to him he responded in basically the same manner as the receptionist, apologizing but maintaining that his hands are tied and it is solely OUR problem. We then inquired for the reason we were not informed in any way about the construction nor of the possibility of our car being towed should we park in the hotel
parking lot that morning, to this he replied by saying that there were signs saying it hung in the parking lot, and that they have told the guests in person that they should not park there. Needless to say there were no signs in the parking lot, just in the lobby, into which you have no real reason of entering at any time during your stay. The second
part was just a blatant lie, as WE were not told in any point in our stay about any of this.
Frustrated, we asked him to try and think of solutions, since we had to attend the wedding at noon and were in great need of a transportation. He offered to order a taxi. When we asked who would pay for that taxi he responded that, you guessed it, it is our responsibility. 
At this point we asked what would be the cost of freeing our car to which he replied "around a hundred dollars".
We insisted that we should not pay neither for a taxi nor for the releasing our car from the towing lot and that we see it as his responsibility to take care of the inconvenience caused
to us and to compensate us in full. He replied that he is not authorized to compensate us for any amount larger than 20 US dollars, and that he needs to speak to his manager Mrs Marichu [--]. We asked him to contact her and get the permit to compensate 
us. He called her cell phone, but she did not pick up. We demanded to get some sort of response, especially since we were pressed in time. He promised he'd get back to us in ten minutes.
We went back to our room and waited for 15 minutes to no avail.After this we went back to the front desk to ask if there were any news, he said he still could not reach Mrs [--] and asked us to wait in our room and that he would call us when he reaches the manager on
the phone. We waited for 15 more minutes until he called the room and told us the manager was nowhere to be found. Also, he apologized for giving us the wrong number before. Turns out the price of getting our car would be "more like three hundred dollars". Meaning, the hotel
to which we are paying customers, fined us a sum greater then the charge for our entire stay.
Finally we realized that if we do not retrieve the car by ourselves as soon as possible we would miss the wedding completely. The towing company employees were in the hotel parking lot again towing other paying costumers cars, and they agreed to give as a ride to the towing lot. When I asked the manager why they keep towing cars instead of calling the people who's cars are being towed he again lied and said he tried calling but they didn't pick up.
We retrieved the car, payed 293.70$ and drove to the wedding, an hour late. Again, this wedding was the sole reason to our visit.
Upon arriving back to the hotel later that evening, a different receptionist told us he was aware of the incident that happened earlier that morning, but that he too had his hands tied. He advised 
us to wait until the following morning to speak to Mrs [--] in person since she could not be reached during the whole day. We would have appreciated the opportunity to finally speak to her. Unfortunately, she was said to arrive at 9am while we had to leave at 8:30am to our flight back to New York. We mentioned to the receptionist that it is quite odd for a manager to not answer her phone for an entire day. He agreed with us and yet again apologized but left us with no real response. 
We were appalled by the horrible service, rude responses, and the act of towing a guests car without even trying to contact him in any way. It is important to note that the hotel had both our car and personal information the entire duration of our stay, thus able to contact us via our cells or the room phone, prior to ordering the towing company to take our car.

title: “Outstanding Food & Front Desk Service”
text:
The front desk people were tops and they handled the checkin/out cordially and quickly. Staff was very friendly and helpful when advising on directions and restaurant recommendations. I felt that their service was top-notch and professional. 
The room itself was very clean, from a well made bed to nice towels to a bright and shiny bathroom. The was also nicely laid out and very well decorated, I mean very hip! 
As my business was downtown, its central location couldn't have been easier, walking distance from the business district. Getting to the hotel from the airports was easy too because the hotel is just a 3-block walk from the "El" stop. 
All in all I was very impressed, thanks Sax!

title: “The perfect getaway in Seattle”
text:
My wife and I FINALLY had a chance to stay at the Inn at the Market. We have stayed at several hotels in Seattle over the past 9 years and the Inn, by far, is the best. Best location, best service (and this is quite an achievement considering all the fine smaller hotels in Seattle), friendliest staff, beautiful, and quiet rooms, and dining that is superb. We booked a water view room and were upgraded to a deluxe water view room. It was fantastic. 
We dined at Cafe Campagne and it reminded us of many small, but excellent, restarurants that we have enjoyed in Paris. The food was excellent and our server, Courtney, was a gem. 
We will definitely return.

title: “reviews were right. we loved this hotel!”
text:
after much research in tripadvisor and other travel sites, we stayed at this hotel for 3 nights this summer. the location is perfect with several great italian restaurants, bakery and coffee shops nearby. 
the room was clean and the decor really cozy. i cannot say enough about the hotel staff and front desk who were very helpful in ensuring our needs were met. i would stay there again on my next trip to san francisco.

title: “A Nightmare Hotel; Do not stay here!”
text: When I arrived the lobby was clean and renovated. I had to change my room two times and the lack of customer service was awful. The manager of this hotel should go through every room and inspect everything! It was gross and much needed repair! I booked through Expedia and was upset that they promote this horrible hotel to people! They should stay in the rooms to rate them! This hotel needs new management who will take the maintenance and housekeeping to new levels! What a disgrace for the money that I paid!

title: “quiet city center hotel”
text:
A small city center hotel near to the Empire State Building, half way between downtown and uptown and with the underground station just nearby.
A very good breakfast included in the room price is waiting for you.
..................................................................................................................................................

title: “COMFORTABLE and friendly”
text: very helpful staff, THE most comfortable pillowtop beds, great location for sight-seeing

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Love this hotel and staff, they were so accomodating. The free wine hour in the lobby was a great perk to my stay. It's an expensive hotel, but I booked it using reward points and will probably book for future trips with or with out using reward points

title: “The crew at this hotel makes your stay worthwhile - especially Ms. Robinson!”
text: Great staff. Great location. Needs renovation but all in all a great place to stay.

title: “Best Bed I have EVER slept in!!!”
text:
My husband and I booked this hotel on Hotwire and got an amazing deal!! We stayed at the James from July 13-July 15 and could not have been more impressed! First off, we saved about $250/night by booking with hotwire and we weren't sure what to expect but the hotel website displays the hotel rooms to the tiniest detail!
Our check in was a breeze...we were worried about getting bumped to another hotel (this has happened to us when we booked with hotwire previously and the property was sold out) but I called the night before to confirm. Our room was incredible! My only complaint was we were put in a corner room on a lower floor with very little view and a handicap accessible room so I don't know if all the rooms looked like ours or not. I am guessing that's where they put their guests that don't pay close to full price for a room. We didn't mind too much because we didn't spend too much time in the room. The bed was a king and was the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in....better than my own!! They have a featherbed on the mattress, down comforter, feather pillows (5 on the bed), an Ipod station/mp3 player, a HUGE 50" plasma TV, closet, full length mirror, electronic safe, iron/board, hairdryer, very modern furniture. The bathroom was completely tiled and had a huge sink. Only complaint here was little room to lay anything down, hardly any counter space. They provided robes, slippers, shampoo/conditioner, lotion, shower gel, q-tips and cotton balls.
We had very quick housekeeping in the am and had nightly turndown service with "mood lighting" (all the lights are on dimmers) and treats on our pillows with the music turned on! The shower was enormous, easily fits two people with a handheld nozzle (no tub). Bath towels were very soft and extremely large!!
My husband and I went to the gym on our first morning there...incredible!!!! The treadmills, ellipticals, and bikes all had flat screen tv's attached to them with personal remotes and headphones. They had a large variety of new state-of-the-art weight machines with racks of free weights, multiple swiss balls and even BOSU trainers with mirrored walls throughout in addition to fresh towels and pitchers of ice water with sliced oranges and lemons in the bottom as well as a personal trainer wandering around. We didn't get a chance to try out the spa, but it looked amazing also!
The J Bar was smaller than what I expected and never was very crowded, but definitely had that "lounge" feel to it with comfortable seating and candlelight. 
The concierge gave us great recommendations for dining and even gave us business cards to give the hostess if there was a wait to get us "moved up on the list". We never had a wait, so we didn't get to use them. Check out wasn't until 2 pm, so that was nice also and the front desk tagged and stored our luggage for us while we spent Sunday in the city!
My only complaint would be that the valet cost was $42/night, but it's Chicago! It's probably that much anywhere and they were very prompt and courteous.
Would I choose the James again???? ABSOLUTELY!!!!! I don't know if I would pay $400/night to stay there, but if you want to try your luck that you will be placed there, I would try hotwire. What a great deal for the nicest hotel I have ever stayed in the U.S. (I have stayed previously at Hilton, Wyndham, Marriott, Crowne Plaza, etc)

title: “A terrific extended stay in a great neighborhood with great staff and amenities”
text: This was our second stay at the River Inn in Washington DC. We love the location including the safety of the neighborhood, the direct, short walk to the GW/Foggy Bottom Metro stop, walk to the nearby Trader Joe's or Safeway, walk or take the quick shuttle from Foggy Bottom to evening concerts at the beautiful Kennedy Center. The staff at this hotel are outstanding -- friendly, responsive to questions and problems, and welcoming. The River Inn is very clean and suite rooms are spacious. We require having a kitchen due to dietary needs, and the kitchenette provided is terrific, especially the fresh coffee beans for grinding each morning. We will continue to stay at the River Inn and recommend to others.

title: “Attractive clean hotel in great New York location”
text: Our room was very clean, nicely furnished, lovely bathroom,well serviced each day. Staff are attentive and friendly, and pride themselves on their level of service. Love the location - close to train station, easy walk to diners and restaurants, and a fabulous deli. Bed was so comfotable! Our only niggle was that we found the room to be very warm. We mentioned this to front desk staff, who immediately offered to send a technician in, but we declined, as it was not a major discomfort. There is free internet access in the lobby, and once you are logged on, you can access it from your room for the next 24 hours. Just go to the lobby to renew each day.

title: “Great Service - Left behind my Ipod and they sent it to me!”
text: The hotel was very comfortable and in a great location. I would agree with a lot of the reviewers that the AC was kind of loud. I rate the place very positively though because I left my ipod behind and they were so helpful and prompt about returning it to me. I think their service is excellent! The bar was also a fun place to hang out at night.

title: “Basic, clean, close to everything”
text:
This hotel was a great value. I stayed Sept 11- 15, 2010 with friends. We had 2 rooms, one with one double bed, and the other room with two double beds. The room with the 2 beds was considerably larger (understandably) but both were good. The rooms were somewhat noisy from being very close to the street but that's to be expected when you're on the second story. The rooms were always clean and the bathroom quite spacious. 
The hairdryer in our room worked surprisingly well, in hindsight it was a waste of space in my bags to pack my own. Our room didn't have a fridge which was a bit of a downside when having drinks or food in the room, but there is ice that can be used if necessary. 
We only attempted the continental breakfast on our first day, it was bagels and muffins. We couldn't find a toaster and it didn't look that appetizing so we walked down the street to Dunkin donuts. At 6th and 23rd (right down the block) there is a great place we got breakfast called corner cafe, as well as a place called toasties at 7th and 23rd that had good and cheap breakfast. 
While the staff weren't overly friendly that's not what I was looking for in a hotel anyway. It was affordable, close to everything (subway stops right across the road), and clean.

title: “bring your bulletproof vest”
text: The only reason this hotel even deserves one star is that the front desk attendant was very courteous and made every attempt to be of service. No A/C, No screens on the windows, absolutely NO ICE MACHINES anywhere in the hotel, no soap, no remote control for the TV, leaky ice bucket (don't even know why they had ice buckets since there are no ice machines), stains in the toilet, immense amount of dust and dirt in the fan in the bathroom, sketchy neighborhood, and the WORST pillows EVER!! Yes, we only paid $40 for the room for one night, but this hotel lacks even the basic amenities you would find if you paid the same price at a Motel 6. don't be fooled by the website...this hotel is far from "chic and elegant" as they claim!! Bar/restaurant was not open at any point....spend a few extra dollars and DO NOT stay at this place!!!

title: “Nicely located - clean rooms”
text: Our experience with this hotel was good - the rooms were clean and big. The pool was very nice even though it closed down really early. The only BAD thing about this hotel is that the walls are paper thin - we woke up to the alarmclock from next door for example!

title: “Nice hotel, comfortable beds”
text: We stayed at the Courtyard for a convention at the Moscone Center. It was about a 3 block walk from the hotel to the convention; not too bad, there is one block of a steeper incline that can challenge those that are less physically fit. The Powell/Hyde cable car line is about a 5 block walk to get to, the F line trolley car lets off at 2nd street and its about a 2 block walk and there are several bus lines that run a few blocks away. The only transportation we did not utilize was the BART (subway) or a taxi. The shuttle transfer from the airport and back was very convenient and easy to use. Our room was on the top floor, #18. We very rairley heard neighbors; the only noise we heard occaisionally was the wind but we got used to that after the first night. We had a nice view of the AT&T stadium and a cruise ship docked at port. Our room was always clean and neat and I found the staff to be very friendly and helpful on all occasions. We used the pool and hot tub several days during our stay...we never saw another soul using the facilities...amazing for such a large hotel; the hot tub felt great after a long day walking around the city. We took a long bus trip out to Yosemite park...a must see if you manage it. I loved the park and want to see more, the few hours we had was not enough. Overall I had a fantastic time in SF, the people were friendly and there were lots of things to see, it was easy to get around and I enjoyed the hotel.

title: “More fountains than Rome”
text:
I recently stayed at the Arizona Grand for four nights for a conference. 
First and foremost, the staff were exceptional. Groundskeepers said a cheery hello, kitchen and wait staff could not do enough for us. Most importantly, my packages were waiting for me at the conference center when I arrived. At most hotels, I am forced to hunt down packages that are delivered prior to the conference. They also did this at a minimal price. (And all packages were shipped back just as easily using the business center.)
I was given a room in the Sedona suite. The resort is expansive, and I followed a bell hop, who was driving a golf cart, to my room (I had a car). There is plenty of free parking.
The room was nice with a separate living and bedroom area. The king bed was super comfy. The internet was very fast. The room was spotlessly clean and cleaned nicely every day. I also liked the high end shower amenities (especially the Gilchrist & Soames body butter). There is a cash mini bar which I never used. I do wish they had an empty fridge for people who bring their own drinks (but obviosly I understand that mini-bars are big money makers). Two small things about the room: the safe is located on the top shelf in the closet, almost beyond reach for me and I am 5'5"; also, there was a lovely fountain right outside my room, but the chairs on my patio had torn and dirty seat cushions. Quite surprising.
I really appreciate that the fitness center opened during the week at 5:00. I am an early riser, and enjoyed the variety of equipment at the center. Easily, one of the nicest fitness centers that I have ever seen at a resort, with plenty of treadmills, ellipticals, bikes, stair climbers, rowers, and weight equipment (even a basketball court and lap pool). I also got a massage at the spa with Roxanne. There is a lovely waiting patio with a faux stream outside the spa area - very relaxing. Roxanne did an excellent job and was very sweet.
By far, the food at the conference was some of the best I have ever tasted - bone in porkchop for lunch, are you kidding me?? Fabulous.
We had a business dinner at the on-site Rustlers Rooste. You will need to drive or call for a golf cart, because the restaurant is located at the top of a steep hill (dynamite view, though). It was a bit loud for a business dinner (there are bands playing), but the service was good and we loved the magician.
By the way, anytime we called for a golf cart, someone picked us up within one minute. Of course, you should tip the drivers, so keep that in mind if you are on a budget.
We also ate at the on-site Aunt Chilada's. There is a path across the front lawn, so it is an easy stroll. Dinner and service were both very good.
There are several small pools scattered throughout the resort besides the waterpark. There was a pool outside my room, which actually was quite large enough for swimming laps. There was also a lovely built in jacuzzi. There are also water coolers located near the poosl, which is a nice touch. I used the pool/jacuzzi almost every day (even if only for 10 minutes).
I did not realize until check out that a $3 housekeeping gratuity had been automatically added to my bill. I travel every week for work, and had never seen this done before. I always tip housekeeping anyway, so they must have really loved me. I guess I made the housekeeping staff happy, so I can't complain. Just be aware of it.
The hotel is located directly off Baseline Road and there are lots of dining options nearby if you choose to go off resort.
In general, I loved all of the fountains located throughout the hotel grounds (dozens and dozens). I thought the resort was well kept and the landscaping was beautiful. It was an excellent choice for our convention.

title: “Good Place”
text: This is a convenient hotel to stay at when traveling to/from Los Angeles Airport. The rooms are very clean and comfortable. The courtesy bus is handy. the staff are all friendly and helpful. There is a Denny's at the entrance to the hotel for convenience of meals. Hotel has it own little shop for supplies and souvenirs. The breakfast is very nice and a good way to start your day. I have stayed here both times when travelling from Australia and will the next time also.

title: “Did not sleep”
text: I had to be moved to another room after a few hours because I found hugh bed bugs.

title: “Good location, comfortable rooms.”
text:
This motel is well located to visit all of LA's attractions. We drove to Hollywood & Beverly Hills in less than 20 minutes. Checkin was good, and were pleasantly surprised by the nice, clean room. A standard motel room, but not too old. Everything was there, even refrigirator & microwave oven. The pool gave us a nice cool down after a long hot day. Large supermarkets are just minutes away, as are many restaurants and gas stations. WiFi working OK
We originally came for one night, but wanted to stay another. Unfortunaly there was a footballgame on saturday, so everything was sold out.
Definitely a recommendation

title: “Hotel great, beach shabby”
text: Enjoyed our one night stay at this very nice inn. It was very easy to find, and the location is 2 blocks (an easy walk) from the beach. The greeting we received from the front desk was welcoming and made us feel like they were really glad to have us. What a personality he has!! Even gave us his own cookies when we were looking for the homemade cookies in the lobby after our excursion to the beach that night and they were gone! A good variety of restaurants in the area.

title: “Great stay!”
text:
We stayed a few nights in this hotel in New York last May. We read all the good reports on Tripadvisor and we have to say it's true. It's a great hotel and cheap compared to many others. We had a room with a shared bathroom and that was not a problem at all. The bathroom was next to our room, very clean and was almost never taken, so it felt like our own bathroom anyhow. 
The room with a double bed was not very big, but newly decorated, clean and comfortable. And the hotel is really centrally located, so we think it's a really good stay for a cheap price!

title: “excellent hotel !!!”
text: We just returned from this hotel today. We stayed over a weekend with our two older teenagers. The kids had their own room. The staff was the most cordial and attentive we've ever experienced and we've stayed at some of the nicest hotels in the world. The restaurants and bars were great. The Concierge was great as where the parking attendants, bell hops, counter people, even the people who clean the rooms. The rooms were excellent, super clean and the turn down service was great. We were floored by the low rates compared to other todays we've stayed in and we will most assuredly be back. Do yourself a favor and stay at this hotel.

title: “a secret gem”
text:
My mother was coming to visit me in Houston from PA, and I had looked into several spa type of options to treat her to when I came across an ad for Travassa. We had planned on visiting my son at UT Austin, so this place sounded like the perfect excursion for her visit. We stayed at the Driskill downtown on Sunday night, then drove only about 30 minutes Monday to get to the resort, staying Monday and Tuesday nights. We were very warmly welcomed and given a schedule of events and map of grounds upon check in. The room was second floor overlooking the canyon, and much to our delight there was actually some nice fall color (in October). There was no activities that afternoon, so we just walked the grounds and then I had a short workout in the fitness center while Mom lounged by the pool. The views and pool area are beautiful, and I joined her there to watch the sunset. We had dinner at the restaurant, outside on their lovely patio and were very well attended to. The food was well prepared and featured some local, fresh ingredients. The next day we participated in a few classes, including yoga, a core type strength class, juicing lesson and intro to salsa dancing. The staff there was wonderful and knowledgeable. I had a massage in the spa - very relaxing and enjoyable. 
Only negative was that on weekdays there may not be as much offered as weekends. I would have liked to do the challenge course but it wasn't available. The mechanical bull was also not available. I think this resort was newly acquired or under new management and it seemed to still be working out some kinks - but overall still highly recommended.

title: “Over rated!!”
text:
My husband and I stayed in this hotel for 5 nights with our 2 year old son, having seen a review of it on the Holiday Programme (BBC TV) and can only say what a complete disappointment it was. The rooms were extremely small, dark and not at all sound proofed - again street entertainers kept us awake. Really not worth the rates and would not recommend it to anyone. The staff were quite unhelpful and although we changed rooms immediately after squeezing into the first room the second one we were given was really no better!
The only positive to this experience was the excellent restaurant downstairs.

title: “Cute but Noisy”
text:
I came to San Francisco as a Bone Marrow Donor so I didn't have the choice of where to stay. The NMDP put me up and paid for it. The front desk staff was clueless about the situation & the process & put a hold on my personal account. It took two days to get everything figured out and was an added stress I didn't need. The manager was grudgingly helpful, not friendly helpful. The weekend day staff was friendly and helpful but the evening staff was a lot less than friendly.
The hotel was very cute & fun with its art deco decor. It was nice to have the restaurant, although the menu was very limited, burgers only for lunch or dinner. We ended up preferring the coffee house across the street for breakfast. The worst part of our stay was that our room was on 2nd floor near elevator and the staff breakroom and laundry room. We had an extended stay where we would be in the room most of the time and need lots of rest. Between the housekeeping staff's noisy chatter all day and the poor architecture of the building that allowed you to hear every sound, we did not get good rest. The courtyard style floor plan is cute but makes every sound echo and the tile floor lets you hear every suitcase wheel as they go by. Plus there was a lot of a late night crowd coming in from the baseball games & mingling in the courtyard areas. We were woken up at least three times every night and Security always seemed to be five minutes late in catching the culprits. We should have asked to move rooms but we didn't. If you stay there try to get a room in a non-traffic area if there are any. Another really inconvient thing was that (probably due to the cement walls) we had no cell service in our room and had to go outside to use our phones. The stay also would have been better if they'd had refrigerators, which they don't. It wasn't the worst place I'd ever stayed but not the best either. I guess it depends on what you're staying for if I'd recommend it or not. If you're going to be one of the loud late-nighters downtown, sure go for it. If you need peace and quiet find somewhere else.

title: “What a surprise!”
text:
For the price we paid, it was a fantastic hotel!
Location: the hotel is located just off the Magnificent Mile, which big shops such as Guess and Forever 21 being right around the corner. The John Hancock Tower is just a couple of blocks away. It is on the other side of Chicago to the museums, but Chicago is very walkable.
Room: our room was quite spacious. It was clean and had a modern furnishings. There was a large TV with a range of channels and the bathroom was of a decent size. There is no complimentary wifi directly into the room, but there is complimentary wifi in the lobby. We didn't have a view of anything through our windows, but it was still quite light and airy.
Hotel staff: the staff are on a whole friendly and helpful.

title: “good, but could use some attention to detail”
text:
Overall, very good - the room was very clean and reasonably set up, quite comfortable. Construction was handled well, as other reviewers have noted. The staff were friendly and helpful. The breakfast was convenient and the coffee very acceptable. The little convenience-store corner by the front desk was very convenient indeed, particularly as there are not many alternatives nearby. Check in and out went very smoothly.
On the other hand, some attention to a few details would have made a good experience much better. My room had a brand-new shower, but no matter how carefully I closed the door, it leaked. A new door did not seem to be soundproofed, at least on the 1 night that a neighbor was home late from the bars. No staff member ever asked how the room was, nor was there a comment card. They leave a card that says to limit ecological impact, they launder towels on request - to wash, leave on the floor, to keep, hang up. No matter how carefully I hung towels, they were changed.The breakfast was much as you would expect from a business hotel buffet - not bad, not exceptional, but I *detested* eating off plastic plates with plastic utensils. (To give credit where credit is due, they did have ceramic coffee mugs.)
No restaurant, but nearby is the North Market and Knead - both are highly recommended.

title: “Nice Beachfront Hotel”
text:
My wife and I celebrated Valentines Day on Saturday by leaving the kids with the grandparents and coming down to the beach. We will often just head down to PB and wing-it, finding a room that day (as opposed to booking in advance). My wife had stayed at the Beach Cottages in the past but this was my first time here.
All in all, not a bad hotel if you're looking for a beach front property. This hotel is old and shows it's age, but our room was fine. It was quite small but since it was just the two of us, it worked out perfectly. It also wasn't too pricey but it was off-season, so I'm sure it would have been twice as much during the summer months.
We got a room on the 3rd floor in the main building and the view was spectacular. We were able to park for free in the hotel parking lot (a definite plus in PB) and walk to wherever we wanted.
Because of the location, price, parking, and the view, we will definitely consider staying here again, especially for off-season visits to the beach.

title: “Stylish Renovations”
text: I stayed here a couple nights during a business trip and was very impressed with my accommodations. It's an older Residence Inn, but they were in the final stages of a complete renovation with a bright, modern decor and technology-friendly rooms. The lobby and dining area weren't quite done when I was there, but it looked like that area will be equally as nice. Plus, the service was great and probably the homiest of any chain hotel I've stayed at in awhile. A definite recommendation!

title: “Highly recomended”
text: Everything was great. The King bed studio room was huge, with a sink, minifridge, microwave. The large bathroom mirror had an embeded tv screen! The bed was extremely comfortable, the staff was very courteous, very good location off Union Square, nice Italian Restaurant/jazz lounge on the second floor and an enclosed roof top lounge that served coffee and tea.

title: “Excellent hotel in Chicago”
text: Must be the cleanest hotel in America! Excellent location with good bars and resturants very nearby. 10 minute walk to the 151/156 buses which will take you to all the attractions. Lovely rooms and beds. Excellent complimentary breakfast. staff endlessly helpful. Even stored our cases when we went away for three days. Diversey is a very nice area to stay in. fairly easy access to the L-line train from O'hare airport. Just get off at lake and get a cab. Again..this hotel was spotless. Highly recommended. Punches well above its star rating..

title: “Awesome Choice”
text: This was a fantastic choice: Especially great service, extremely clean and updated, fantastic location.

title: “Excellent hotel in prime position”
text: I don't think you can beat the Sofitel. Its in a great position. We did an awful lot of looking up hotels and background work (on tripadvisor). It takes us ages to decide on a hotel as it can make or break a holiday. The rooms really are comfortable, luxurious, cosy, fluffy towels, soft furnishings etc. in other words you want to come back to this hotel when you are tired after a day out. The way it should be. The concierge at reception always knows where to everywhere is etc. You can always get a good deal, book ahead of time and not on their own site. When you walk out the front door you are only a few seconds from the Magnificent Mile. Turn the other direction and you are very close to the beach. So either way you get to see everything. Just around the corner from the hotel, there is a lovely little restaurant that does breakfast. Breakfast in the hotel itself (bad value). Potash is a little grocery store around the corner where you can buy orange juice etc. Line a waste paper bin with a plastic bag fill with ice from ice machine and hey presto, good to go.

title: “Don't Bother”
text: Please stay somewhere else. Manager at front desk rude and condescending. He claimed that our reservation was for a different type of room instead of what we reserved - Times Square view- basically called us liars. Thank God I had the original email confirming reservation, because he claimed that the confirmation number we gave him was for a different type of a room such a BS - never had such an issue at any other hotel. Even when he was proven wrong, he never apologized. The whole episode spoiled entire weekend. Needless to say, we will not be staying there again.

title: “Top notch service in a great location”
text:
A football reunion for 12 men was planned a little late but the Marriott came through brilliantly. They were able to accommodate early arrivers, later arrivers and still work out the costs to our advantage. If Ashley is at the front desk when you arrive you will be treated wonderfully. She really aims to please and helped make the weekend worry free. The hotel is in walking distance to most everything -- shopping, church and the stadium where the Panthers play. The fitness center has tons of equipment and the indoor pool and jacuzzi were clean and well managed.
Since this was a sports filled weekend, a lot of time was spent in Champions, the hotel's bar. There we were again treated royally (food and drink) mostly thanks to the divine Ruby. She was the perfect bar server for this group. In addition, one night we ate in the hotel's restaurant and everyone enjoyed their meals while being attended to by three servers for 8 diners. Good stuff for a chain!

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: Me and my girlfriend went to California for a Oakland Raiders game. The hotel was in a great location. The room was a nice size and very clean! The lady at the front desk was very helpfull. She gave me a map and marked directions to specific sights. i stayed on the 16th floor and had a nice view. Breakfast was a little on the pricey side. i would stay here again

title: “Great Location, Tired Property”
text:
This property was in a great location and it had free parking. It was clean and the staff was friendly and helpful. We left our car (it was safe) there during our four day stay and walked to all the great sites. The bus was close to take us to the Golden Gate Bridge. There were several great restaurants just three blocks away from the Warf. The towels were thin and rough, being on a busy street made for a noisy stay. Upon our return, we will stay here again and would recommend this motel to you if you are looking for a good location to the Fishermans Warf. We will bring our own towels next time.
We selected this property for its location, great price, free parking.

title: “Great value!”
text:
We stayed at the Holiday Inn at the end of April 2011. We are a family of five and the Executive Suite with two queens and a sofa bed was perfect for us. The rooms were clean and exactly as they appear on the website. The room included a very good breakfast which includes hot food, varying daily. This was excellent value and filled the kids up before we set out each day. USA Today was also available in the foyer and breakfast area.
Staff were very helpful. The self service laundry within the premises was great with family. There is a computer room outside the breakfast room with two computers with internet access and a printer which was great for printing boarding passes and emailing family.
The hotel is a short 5 minute walk down Highland Ave to Hollywood Boulevard. There is a vacant allotment next door and there are a number of homeless people in the area. However, they did not bother us and we did not feel uncomfortable walking around the area. There is a small supermarket and a Starbucks located across the road.
A number of tours and the hop on hop off bus all depart from Hollywood Boulevard. The Highland Centre on the corner of Highland Ave and Hollywood Boulevard has good shopping and some nice restaurants. We were also able to take the bus to Santa Monica from Hollywood Boulevard. 
This was the best priced hotel of our US trip. We would certainly stay here again if visiting LA and would recommend it to anyone looking for a modern, clean and well located hotel at an affordable price.

title: “W San Diego Staff Rock!”
text:
I work in hotels and I have never before mentioned staff by name when checking out, nor have I ever logged onto Trip Advisor to write a review. 
On arriving at the W San Diego, we were met by Kacey who was was welcoming, polite, entertaining...she is a true asset to the W team. We dined in Rice and had a lovely server called Kimberley who made our experience even better.
I really enjoyed my stay at the W, everyone was happy, smiley and helpful. even though we drove 5 hours there and back we felt refreshed.
Thank you San Diego Team!

title: “Very limited options for vegetarians who visit the hotel”
text:
Attended a 5-day conference in this hotel and so I had to settle my meals in here for most of the days. 
Tried the Sprig Restaurant on day 1 and there was only black bean salad on the menu for vegetarian. The other mains or soup dishes were all for meat eaters. The salad wasn't great and the price was too much to ask for at $12 when it was just black beans, vegetables and some croutons etc. 
Went to the Japanese eatery on 2 other days but the sushi bar was closed. This time it was a different western menu available and again only Caesar salad was the only option for vegetarian. I would say that the Caesar salad was slightly above average. 
On day 3 where the Sushi bar was available, fortunately there were vegetable rolls and Egg tamago roll available. However, the vegetarian rolls came in a manner where a serious Sushi master would give a "F" grade to the sushi maker and there were only 4 pieces of sushi roll. Tamago came in 2 pieces and I would say that the egg roll in food marts would easily excel the ones here in Hilton.

title: “Ideal New York Hotel”
text: Hadn't really heard of this hotel but through travel agent was booked with partner for a week in September. Location was ideal walking distance to many places and also by subway station. The check in was very efficient and friendly and as I had requested a nice room view as partner had never been before we got a room on 32nd floor with Empire State building right outside to see. Room was good, not the most modern room I've been in but good size and nice decor.Free wifi was excellent. Busy hotel and staff very friendly. We ate in the Tick Tock diner on a number of occasions and it was very good, very busy in the morning. Would recommend this hotel and will certainly go back.

title: “Nice budget motel.”
text:
ok, first of all, the front desk lady in the mornings was so sweet and helpful. great person.
as far as the hotel. i went to houston on business and had this hotel booked for me, without seeing it. so i looked on the reviews at various sites and saw horrible reviews. 
ill be honest, it scared me to read them. they said bed bugs, i personally checked for them since my husband does pest control and he told me how. no sign, sheets were clean beds decent, room was clean. there were some things that could have been cleaner, such as they didnt vacuum the corners, and the bathroom door had some cleaning stuff or something on the door... it did not effect our stay in any way, the stuff that counts was clean.
one reviewer said bad neighborhood, couldnt get out of car, drug dealers and prostitutes in the parking lot. i was a female traveling with other females and we came in at 12 midnight all 3 nights and didnt see anyone or anything suspicious. 
the breakfast was waffles, cereals, and pastries, with coffee, oj, and milk. they also had oatmeal packets. the front desk person was always tending to it. it was never overly crowded. we traveled in january. the only thing even close to an issue was that i saw two roaches in my room. that was a little icky, but i only saw one on one day and one the next, none the next. you never know what people bring in their bags, so they could have come with the previous occupant. lol. anyway, if you just want someplace clean, that you are only going to be sleeping at while you travel or lay over... it is fine. it does have outside doors, but that didn't cause any issues. the neighborhood isn't bad, it is right near all of the most expensive car lots around.. you drive down the street and see luxury car dealer after another. oh the tv was unplugged in the back, and they fixed it immediately. i never felt threatened or unsafe. we came in until 1 a.m. traffic from airport was a little loud once or twice..... not enough to keep me up.

title: “Nice place, great service”
text: Stayed here on a weekender in SF. Great location, easy walk to everything. Tough to get a cab unless you walk across the street to the mariott (?) The upgraded king room with jacuzzi tub was nice, but unremarkable, comfy bed. Great view of market street but not much noise on the 8th floor which was nice. The tub accommodated two very comfortably.... Etro bath products smelled great and all were replenished daily (since they all ended up in my bag) You could hear the plumbing activity in other rooms, although it was not disruptive, probably since the building is old. Staff is typical Kimpton, excellent all the way. Daniel at the front desk was amazing, making sure all my particular desires were taken care of. Doorman and bellhop went out of their way to jump in the street to find cabs. At the $230ish/night on the aaa rate I was pleased. I've seen this hotel much higher, in which case I would have sought something more posh. Biggest complaint is that the restaurant does not serve breakfast (room service is available). I would definitely stay here again, provided the price was right.

title: “Great Hotel - Great Location”
text:
We recently stayed here 3 nights and I have absolutely nothing negative to say about this hotel. The front desk was helpful, the room was clean and quiet, the price was great, it was located near the subway stops. Downstairs there were washers/dryers, soft drink machine and an ice machine. Off from the lobby were tables/chairs for the complimentary coffee/tea/hot chocolate.
It was everything good you hope your hotel will be. An added bonus was that we were able to check in early, a welcome surprise we had not anticipated. We had fully expected to store our luggage in their lockers, which we did on the morning we checked out and stayed in the city the rest of the day and picked up our luggage late that afternoon.
 When you check in, pick up a brochure of the history of the hotel, it is very interesting. I hope to go back to NYC one day and the first thing I will do before I go is make my reservation at the Herald Square Hotel!

title: “We won't be back here”
text: Check-in was 3pm. We arrived an hour early and were told to come back later. Room was not ready until 4:30pm. Staff were inefficient, did not speak English, and not very friendly. We booked a room on the second floor, but were only offered one on the first floor. Carpet was dirty. NO WATER PRESSURE. No ice machine working on the floor. Overheard every guest with some non-function or problem with their room. EXTRA FEES: parking, parking fee (two fees for one car???). No newspaper available in the morning. Only compliment: the free breakfast was very good: eggs, yogurt, fresh waffles, fresh fruit, good coffee. But we will NOT use this hotel again. Booking fee was $119, but added fees got us for $159.

title: “I LOVED IT!”
text:
The hotel staff has great customer service skills! especially the hotel restuarant. there is a lady by the name of "mari". she is awesome! request her as your waitress. she goes above and beyond for her customers, plus she does it with a smile. i could really tell she loves her job. she needs to be promoted to front desk supervisor, because she has the skills to keep customers coming back year after year. Thanks for such a great trip! we will be back next year!
At $45 per night from priceline deal game! wow

title: “Fabulous hotel for the price”
text: We were at this hotel for 2 nights prior to an Alaska cruise. Rooms are nicely appointed and had one of the most comfortable hotel beds I have ever slept in. It is also within walking distance of some good restaurants. We ate at Dukes Chowder house (was recommended by hotel staff as a "locals" place) and we were not disappointed. Nice breakfast buffett. Only complaint would be the staff on the night we checked in were not too friendly or welcoming. They seemed bored and fairly indifferent. After an exhausting days worth of cross country air travel , it would have been nice to have experienced a little more hospitality.There is a free hotel shuttle to Pikes Place, Space Needle, etc. and the dirver(s) were very nice and accomodating. Will definitely stay here again if we ever get back to Seattle. hope so :) What a great city.

title: “We enjoyed our stay”
text:
We chose this hotel because it seemed like a good location and value. The fact that the rooms have a fridge/microwave, breakfast and afternoon snacks are offered, and you don't have to pay for parking like in the downtown hotels.
The staff was generally helpful (the maintenence man helped us figure out our tub drain, and the lady working the breakfast buffet was super nice. The front desk staff was a little less helpful in helping us with local attractions.
The room was clean (housekeeping was thorough). The pool looked nice, though we didn't take a dip. There are many restaurants nearby, and we were able to reheat our leftovers in the room!
All-in-All, highly recommended for a simple good value.

title: “Okay for the money”
text: We stayed here because the website it was booked on (Red Roof Inn) gave a lower price than other hotels in the area. The website didn't specify the age of the child, and upon check-in, was told that a child over 13 must pay an additional $15/day. A little misleading, I think. The room had a very strong mildew odor, we ended up buying our own air freshener. If you're shy, this is not the hotel for you! The bathroom door is clear glass. What is up with that? We figured out if you kept the light off, you'd have some sense of privacy. Continental breakfast was adequate- instant hot cereal, assorted cold cereals, yogurt, pastries, bagels. The location is "Little Korea," and is 10 streets plus 3 avenues away from Grand Central Station (20 min walk). Very good restaurant on this street is Haru Hana -beautifully presented Japanese cuisine. French Bakery next door to hotel, also very good. Elevators were a bit slow. Front desk people perfunctory at best, not very friendly.

title: “Bad Parking and Lame Breakfast”
text: We were in San Francisco only for a couple of nights for the Oysterfest. Unfortunately, most of the other hotels in the area we wanted were all booked and we didn't want to pay an arm and a leg, so we stayed here. The parking situation is pretty bad, as noted by others. Spaces are small and there aren't enough for everyone. Breakfast was a joke--a lame little packaged danish and coffee. We ended up at IHOP across the street. The room itself was okay, but it didn't have that "clean" feel to me. It just didn't seem like it had been thoroughly cleaned and I didn't feel like I could walk around barefooted. It was okay, but nothing to write home about.

title: “Great location for just about everything”
text:
My wife and I had a lovely time at the Chancellor Hotel. We only stayed for 4 nights, as part of a longer holiday, and found the Chancellor to be all that we had hoped for. The location, right on Union Square, was perfect for exploring San Francisco and, despite being right in the hub of the city, the rooms were very quiet. The hotel staff were friendly and the free coffee and cookies in reception were a welcome treat and something not experienced at other hotels in the US where typically nothing is 'on the house'. 
My only complaint was that the rooms were a little on the small side and the bathrooms were a little dated but for the price and location the hotel is difficult to beat on a budget.

title: “Pricey but Pleasant”
text:
We stayed at the Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites for 3 nights when we first arrived in the USA and it was, all in all, a very pleasant experience. 
The hotel is perfectly situated for the pedestrian tourist ... we were able to walk comfortably to Hollywood Boulevarde where attractions like Madam Tussaudes, Grauman's Chinese Theatre, Ripley's Believe It Or Not, and the Disney Soda Fountain await. Across the road from the hotel itself (within less than a block) are conveniences like Subway, a liquor store and a grocery mart, so those without transport are very well catered for. 
The hotel itself was tastefully appointed, the rooms were clean and modern, the bathroom was spacious and the shower was hot and strong. The beds were comfortable and we didn't hear a thing from the neighbouring suites for the duration of our stay.
We stayed on the 5th floor so it was just a short ride down to the breakfast room on the 4th floor each morning for a great variety of breakfast foods on the house. We were able to choose from cereals, toast, scrambled eggs, bacon, patties, bagels, muffins, pastries, hot coffee, yoghurts, juices ... you name it, it was available. We didn't have a problem with breakfast seating either because we always arrived around 7:30am, but things do start do get busy by around 8:30am.
The staff were polite and professional without being overly friendly and if I was forced to find a downside to our experience, I would say that the front counter staff could have been more friendly and welcoming. The other downside of course would have to be the price. The room was very overpriced for what it was and parking at $22.00 per day is practically highway robbery, but I guess that's the sacrifice you make for staying in the heart of Holllywood. However, we'd accepted the pricing before arriving and aloofness from the front counter staff did not really affect our stay in any meaningful way. I would certainly recommend the Holiday Inn Express to anybody who was looking to stay in the heart of Hollywood. We thoroughly enjoyed our time here!

title: “Large comfortable rooms”
text:
As a frequent traveler to SA, TX. I enjoyed the 1st time stay at this HI Express location. I chose this location as opposed to a preferred downtown Holiday Inn location due to this hotel's lower rate, free parking and hot breakfast. 
Check in was brisk and I the room type reserved was correct. I even received complimentary bottled of cold water and snacks at check in, a nice touch after a long drive into town. Reception staff were courteous and friendly. 
The king executive room was VERY large. Room was also very clean. Although it had slightly dated furniture and sofa, the bathroom was newly updated with granite counter tops and new tile throughout. Bedding was new / clean, and king bed was comfy. 
The hotel is near the airport and we had a room that faced the interstate highway, and our room was very quiet. Access to the expressway and all areas of town was very easy from hotel and it was just minutes to downtown. 
We utilized the exercise room and all equipment was new, working, and professional grade.
Only downside was that there was a long line for free breakfast buffet, but it was worth the wait. Hot breakfast was typical Holiday Inn express fare, and had no reason to complain about quality.
I would definately choose this location again for the price.

title: “Room & service ok - nothing special”
