text:
The room is standard Westin - comfortable bed, good in room coffee, decent sized room, good shower. Check in was efficient & bellmen helpful. Food at Embers - limited menu - one good meal, one very mediocre. Nothing really special about the hotel. Was there for a business meeting & huge banging next to our conference room which made it very distracting during meeting. 
I typically stay at the Hilton when in Charlotte for business & that is my preference as location is better for me & more dining options close by.

title: “ok hotel”
text: This hotel is ok given the price in NYC. If you expect a nicer place to stay, go for the more expensive ones.

title: “Great customer service and location”
text: The staff was very helpful in giving directions to area attractions and shopping! The room was great and the morning breakfast was excellent! A great place for the corporate traveler and families. I look forward to another visit.

title: “Awesome Experience”
text:
Fantastic golf and overall customer experience. We stayed in the Casita which I highly recommend if you're traveling without kids.
A quick tip: Call just before your trip to get a lower rate. I called the day of and they gave me an unpublished rate of $279. The lowest online was $389.
Talk about your awesome customer experience... I was tweeting pics as I was playing both courses and @westinlacantera was responding in real time. As I was finishing up my last round, I tweeted that they should send me wife a bottle of champagne so I could keep playing. Sure enough they delivered one. Over and above the already great service that Westin hotels consistently delivers.
It's a resort so things won't be perfect and you'll have some hits and misses w/ service folks but the complaints on this thread are way off. Great hotel. We will definitely be back.

title: “Lovely Boutique Hotel”
text: This was a short trip, 4 women, so I will start by saying for 4 women it was a little cramped but for the two, the room is lovely. Breakfast was a bonus ,being able to go out your door and grab juice, coffees croissants, cakes and cereals. The staff were extremely nice and helpful. The Happy Hour was a very nice touch, lovely anitipasta style appetizers, lots of choices of wine and mixed drinks. This was attended by a lot of people and everyone just chatted and shared their Chicago experience. I would definetly go back to this hotel .

title: “Not worth the money!”
text: This hotels retails for $500/night and its a DUMP. The double room was small. It was old. there were no towels in my bathroom and the towels they ended up giving me were extremely worn and old. Plus, I have to pay for $60/night for parking, $16/day for Wifi, and $20/breakfast! I'm sure there are much nicer hotels in the city!

title: “Great location and nice clean rooms.”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for about 7 nights towards the end of June/early July. We truly enjoyed the restaurants and shopping in the area. Oak Street beach is approximately 7 minutes away by foot. The beds are extremely soft and comfy. However, if you suffer from back issues like myself - slipped disk, you might want to reconsider. The hotel room was super clean and the mini bar was well-stocked. We did take a few items and they replenished it the next/same day which was a nice touch. There was no tub in our room but the "Rain" shower was nice. Room service was great and the bell-hops were so pleasant and helped to give us clear and concise directions. 
Breakfast was really good. I had the Eggs Benedict with the Spinach and my husband had the Texas cherry chocolate french toast. Our waiter Andre was by far the Most Polite we've met in all our travels. We were saying that if we ran a restaurant, we would offer him a position! The orange granola pancakes we had on another day was so fluffy and sweet. Mmmm.
The housekeeping and room service staff were so attentive and were all smiles. They even remembered us and thanked us for the small token/tip we gave them. You almost feel like you've known them for a while.
There are a few things to note however. The internet is charged at $9.95 per 24 hrs. What we did not know was that it was PER device. We were charged twice on some days as we were connected to the Internet using our tablet and the occassional phone. So please be careful. We were advised that it is in the hotel terms and conditions so we were obliged. The reception did take 1 internet charge off the first night. 
Secondly, we ordered room service at around 1025pm one night and we were advised that we could only order from the late-night menu. It clearly states that the late night menu is from 1045pm. There were only 4 things to choose from, one of which was a cheesecake and there were nothing fish/vegetarian. We decided to skip it altogether.
The John Hancock centre is located on the next block along with Jamba Juice or a beautiful Italian cafe/bistro L'Appetito for a quick breakfast. There is also the cheesecake factory for the little indulgence late night. The hotel is very close to many fine dining restaurants like Joe's Seafood and Prime Rib, RL restaurant, etc. The great deep dish pizza restaurants like Gino's East, Uno, Ora or Giordanos are also walkable.
The hotel is reasonably priced. considering its charm, cleanliness, and great location.

title: “BEAUTIFUL ROOM,AFFORDABLE, AND EXCELLENT CUSTOMER SERVICE”
text: My daughters and I booked this hotel not knowing anything but the reviews that I have read on Trip Advisor which were mixed. We attended the Lady Gaga Concert. We were going to stay at the Marriott,but the rates were very high for one nite stay. We chose this hotel because of the rates and the location next to the Staples Center. This hotel does not look "chic or fancy" in the lobby or elevator, but the rooms are gorgeous. Comfortable beds, nice bathroom, all new showers,decor. Very very nice! When we left, I noticed the next day that my wedding ring was gone. I was sure I left it there as I had taken it off to wear something else to the concert. Long story short, the manager, John Kelly,went over and above ANY customer service I have ever had in my whole life! He searched the room inside and out and called me back several times to try to console me and showed so much compassion on what I was going through. Eventually, I found the ring and called him back to let him know. He was so genuine in his concern for everything. This kind of customer service is so rare, and even if I hadn't found my ring, I still would have had positive thoughts for this hotel. I def will stay again!!!

title: “GREAT HOTEL ( would go again and again)”
text: Great hotel with a fab location,loads of shops near by and basement bargin departments. I went with my husband, sister, mother and 2 1/2 year old. Be warned they charge extra for the cots;( . Lucky we had the big double room so my daughter had a double bed to herself( hasnt helped she wont get out of ours since coming back!) There is a fire station near the hotel which knowbody else has put in their reviews, which wails like a cat being strangled day and night. My daughter loved it and would run to the window to see the cat truck as she called it. The guys at the station even let her in the fire trucks and have a look round the station, which was very very nice of them( we called the station fire master the "daddy" which he liked). The adults didnt like the wailing truck so be warned. Next to the station is a fab chinese called the cottage. I would advise to got early as it the size of a living room and gets very busy, but excellent food(plus free bottle of house wine) Also loads of great bars again passed the the fire station. There is also another chinese which looks like it needs the health inspectors in, but again excellent take out( was very surprised) thats right as you go out of the hotel(the opposite way from the 24 hour market). The 24 hour dinner across the way also has excellent choice and a very filling breakie. There also another breakfast place which is right again think its 77th street sorry can remember the name. Next time we book for new york we will be going back to this hotel, theres loads of shops, dining, five minutes walk roughly from central park. Theres also a childrens park again pass the fire station, pass the chinese cottage. Its brill my daughter loved it (good for burnout before afternoon nap). Ive read all the reviews myself about this hotel and think that there is toooo many people moaning. Number 1 why moan when your in new york. Number 2 your spending to much time in your room( get a nyc life saddo). And number 3 you wont her the cat cat truck lol!!!! Also for the shopping mums theres a shop called harrys which sells childrens ugg plus other shoes and adult uggs(right out of the hotel near 77th st). So you dont queue at the ugg store!!!. Next to the hotel theres a childrens department store called the childrens place and right out of the hotel is finnies department store(near to the other breakie place and harrys shoe shop) which sells juicy couture, dkny, sunglasses bags etc the mummies out there will have a field day. Hope this helps enjoy new york babies !!!!!! xxxxxxxxx

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: I loved the location of this hotel very well appointed and close to just about everything. The front desk staff was very helpful and courteous, our room was upgraded to a higher floor with a smaller bed. This was a very good Hotel for the price and I was happy with just about everything...I would highly recommend!

title: “Absolute luxury & elegance!”
text: Of all the high end NYC properties, this is hands down the best service I've ever received. From the very moment I arrived, front desk staff were helpful and diligent in getting me the best possible room available. Even with checking in a tad early (2pm) they were gracious and accommodating and even gave me an upgrade one tier above the room for which I paid and it was spectacular. The rooms (suites) were extremely clean, well-appointed with elegant furnitture that's in good repair, huge flat-screen tvs, and absolutely spectacular bathrooms with Hermes toiletries. The bed was one of the most comfortable I've ever slept on and the linenes were wonderful. Room service was prompt and delicious---worth it! The restaurant/bar Gaby's was also a great choice with very reasonably priced, delicious food. I now find it very difficult to stay anywhere other than a Sofitel. Book it--- you won't be disappointed!

title: “Very comfortable luxury hotel”
text:
The hotel is about 16 miles out of San Antonio and out in the country so if you have no car, you are stuck. It is an uninteresting box-like structure from the outside with a functional appearance. However, inside it is luxurious, with excellent air-conditioning. I stayed in a suite with a seoarate living area, bedroom, bathroom and toilet. It was all very comfortable. The bedroom air conditioning had an annoying little buzz to it which was a bit distracting during the night but otherwise I could not fault the facilities. The week I was there, the dining room did not seem to be used much but the food we had at lunch time in the form of a buffet in the bar area was excellent quality. The staff were really friendly and helpful. I took the courtesy bus from the hotel one day to the nearby Sea World and had a marvellous afternoon watching the dolphin, killer whale and seal shows. It is a must for anyone in that area.
Outside the hotel there is an area wih swimming pools and a hot dip pool which all looked to be attractive with gardens in an enclosure. Unfortunately, the week I was there the weather was pretty awful and so no-one was swimming.
It is quite an expensive hotel and even though I was there on a company discount scheme, it came to over $170 per night for just the room (including taxes). A short walk up the road there is a petrol station at the back of which is Rudy's. It is a totally unpretentious eating place where you queue up for absolutely wonderful roast meat, stuffed into slices of bread with some Texan side dishes. Including a beer, it didn't come to more than $10. Next door there is a slightly higher class eating joint so there was no need to spend a lot of money at the hotel if you didn't mind eating at wooden tables under the stars. Wonderful.

title: “Amsterdam Court”
text:
Tiny room that smelled funny. I'm not sure if it was smoky or just old.
But for $100 a night, couldn't beat the location!! 
The staff was always helpful.

title: “Noisy - Thin, thin walls!”
text: The price and location were great but the walls are paper thing. I am a travelling rep. and stay in a lot of hotels and this place is noisy, noisy, noisy. Light sleepers beware. Other than the noise, the place is clean and does have wireless.

title: “Wonderful hotel, staff and location!”
text: My sister, best friend and I stayed here from 12/4 - 12/6. We were there strictly for a shopping trip only. The hotel is in a very quaint location with cobble stone streets. We felt very safe here. It was a few blocks to the subway to take us into midtown. Lots of shops and places to eat nearby though. The staff was phenomenal from the front desk staff to the housekeeping staff. Everyone was extremely friendly and helpful!!!! I can't stress enough how friendly everyone was. I highly recommend this hotel. I've never written a review on another hotel but thought that this hotel deserved me taking the time out to recommend it to everyone interested.

title: “Great location, great building, tiny room for the $$”
text:
This hotel is ON the freedom trail - right in the middle of everything cool in Boston. The hotel itself is a work of art, with ornate carvings and the elevator doors are the best I have EVER seen anywhere! 
That said it is expensive for a very small room. What it gained in the hotel lobby and decor it lost in value resulting in an average mark from me.

title: “What a room”
text: Stayed here while attending a high school reunion. The room was super, breakfast... wow and happy hour a great place to meet. Convienent to all highways, etc.

title: “Good Location But Nothing More”
text:
If you are attending a convention this is a great location. Two blocks away is the DC Convention Center. Less than a block away is a superb restaurant, Acadiana, that serves terrific Cajun food. The lobby of the hotel has been completely remodeled but the rooms have not been and are simply okay. Bathrooms are dated and if you are away from the street you probably look into an adjacent office building which will guarantee you little or no light in your room.
The walls are pretty thin and room service trays can be in the hallways a fairly long time. The doors to the hallways do not fit well....streams of light running in the sides. Very odd.
Room air units run most of the night....get accustomed to the noise.
Bottom line...if you are at the Convention Center all day stay here. If you are visiting DC or are in the hotel room for an extended period of time, you can do much better in DC.
They need to get to the rooms and bathrooms. A makeover is needed.

title: “Revisited”
text:
Please see my previous review for more details...
To summarize:
The Pike Tower is the older side. I had a priceline deal, and when asked to go to the newer Union Tower (like other priceliners have received when asked), the gentlemen said that it was a $20/night upgrade. Oh well. The only parking onsite is valet, charging $44/night. There are a couple of public parking sites within a half block of the hotel for $26-30 per night, with in/out privileges. I usually park next to the cheese cake factory, which is across the street from the back entrance to the hotel. 
We stayed in an --08 room, which is literally across from the elevator and the ice machine. Not too loud though, but the door for the ice machine swings back pretty loud. 
Save yourself a room cleaning, and receive a $5 voucher for food in the hotel. No free wi-fi in the room, but plenty of free terminals in the lobby and free wi fi. The rooms are decent, nothing to complain about. Good water pressure for the showers. 
Overall, a great place to stay in a very central location (pike place 5 minutes away, shopping malls 3 minutes away).

title: “Nice location, gross rooms.”
text: Stayed here for my cousins graduation. From the outside the hotel looks pretty nice close to shops, the lobby looks up to date, but on the inside of the rooms is a bad hotel horror scene. Exposed screws, chipping wood, dead bugs in the lamps over the beds, curtains that are torn and electrical sockets that don't work. The only reason I gave the service a 3/5 is because of the free happy hour drinks and food. This hotel needs some serious remodeling if they want to attract more visitors.

title: “Not Bad, but not Amazing”
text:
My wife, myself, and a friend recently stayed at the Hampton in North Dallas. Although the hotel wasn't bad, it wasn't great. 
Cons: The furnishings seemed outdated to me, the lighting was also not very good. The pool was not open. Although it is an outdoor pool and it was in the fall, I still thought it would be open. The biggest thing was I didn't care for the decorations, etc... It was not on part with many of the other Hamptons I have stayed at. The tv programming was also annoying because it kept switching to the programming channel when you were watching it. Also, it is next to a night club and I believe I could hear some of the music from the night club at night. It wasn't too bad and didn't cause me to lose any sleep, but still another factor.
Pros: The breakfast was good and the bathroom was nice. The staff was also very pleasant. Check-in was also very easy. 
It isn't a bad hotel, but just not an amazing stay. I wouldn't stay there again, but that is just my tastes.

title: “One Night in the Shadow of the White House”
text:
We had one night in town before heading out to the Maryland burbs for a wedding, and wanted to stay right in the middle of things. The Hay-Adams did not disappoint--what a great location! Service was top-notch, property is traditional and very beautiful. Room was gorgeous and while small by modern standards, I actually found it quite roomy for an urban property and for a historic hotel. Bathroom was very nice indeed--I really liked the bath products :)
Breakfast in The Lafayette, while pricey, was still quite a treat. Beautiful room and EXCELLENT service. 
Would stay here again in a heartbeat; was sad we had to leave after only one night!

title: “Hated it, website description inaccurate.”
text:
The absolute only thing this hotel has going for it is its location- right in the downtown core. Upon check-in, we were advised that parking would be an additional charge of $19/day. We were then given a "superior" room on the top floor and were greeted by a cracked and peeling ceiling, dirty walls and baseboards, and a run down bathroom. We complained to the front desk and were able to switch rooms. The only improvement in the second room was that there was actually a dresser and the ceiling was in better shape. But we took it. 
Let me restate, the bathroom alone is reason not to stay at this hotel. All of the fixtures were ancient, despite the sites' claims of a recent renovation. The tile was also old and the grout stained. The toilet flush, I'm sure, could be heard two rooms down on either side- it was seriously THAT loud. Plus, it was so small you couldn't close the door until you were actually sitting on the toilet. The counter space (or lack there-of) did not have sufficient space for my make-up bag, and it's hardly a suitcase. 
The walls were thin and we could easily hear conversations next door, along with our neighbors own plumbing issues. 
The radiator was not working which sucked because the building was freezing cold.
One last thing: this hotel is definitely not handicapped friendly. There are stairs leading from the front desk to the elevator. I'm not handicapped, but it was hard dragging my luggage up a flight of stairs.
Because my husband and I were so disappointed, we left a day early and drove back home to Vancouver, BC. Thank you, hotels.ca, for the apology and refund!

title: “Nice Newer hotel”
text:
Nice hotel in an industrial area. Hotel appears to be newer construction and in good condition. Parking lot is kinda hard to get in and out of with a bigger vehicle. Kitchen only had two each of cups, plates etc in it; most Candlewoods have at least four of every thing in the room. 
Overall not a bad place and will probably be back if I have a project in the area again.

title: “If I too, can live in a hotel.”
text:
Wow. 
Let me begin by saying that I expected it to be good, but not as good as it turned out to be. I was so very, happily surprised.
I booked a king waterview suite which acutally had a better view of the Bay Bridge and some water. 
Valet were professional and nice. Check in was quick, actually, we checked in at 7pm on a saturday night. Anna at front desk, was nice. Americano was happening with corporate types and hipsters.
The room. Wow. 
I mentioned on online reservations it would be an anniversary weekend for my boyfriend and I. 
They placed rose petals in the shape of a heart on the bed
and a complimentary bottle of champagne in an ice bucket with two champagne flutes on the table, a 'happy anniversary' card, and a cd playing electronica (the more relaxing kind) on the beautifully lit bedisde table. Didn't cost me extra. It was all complimentary. 
We loved it. What an awesome staff.
We had dinner reservations at Foreign Cinema, so we asked if they could call us a taxi. Actually, there is a shuttle car on site. It cost us $20 excluding tip. Better to take a cab if you want to save some cash, or are not going on a date. But in our case, we were on a date so we went with the Lincoln shuttle car instead.
When we came back from dinner, we were actually still quite hungry. (Though tasty, yes, Foreign Cinema serves small portions).
So we went downstairs to Americano. Unfortuantely they stop serving food at 11pm. The barback, Louie is a really cool person. 
We took our drinks outside on a small table near the heating lamp and enjoyed the ambiance on Embarcadero and the water.
After that, we returned to our room at about 1 am, still a little hungry. Apparently, guests were ordering Pizza as there was a pizza delivery man going back and fourth from floor to floor delivering food.
We're glad we ordered from Cable Car Pizza. Pretty darn good food for delivering at 1am. Good tiramisu too.
We drank champagne, even in our beautiful rainfall shower, lol.
I don't find this negative, but you can hear people in the halls. Muffled though. I even heard a sneeze. I didn't care, but what if they heard us? Oh well. lol!
The Sugar Fresh products are so good. Smells light and lemony.
I love love love the pillows! I will be calling the hotel to see what kind they are so I can buy a few!
In the morning, Discovery Channel was taping a bike race outside our window on Embarcadero. We watched most of it while getting ready for the day. People were crowded around, taking pictures of the bikers and getting autographs. A cool thing to see.
It was check out time, unfortunately. Anna, at front desk, offered to hold my bags til I got back from shopping around the city, even though I was already checked out. I still was able to leave my car with valet til 5pm too, not a problem.
I will definitely be back. Definitely! Great staff, chic, modern relaxing decor, great services, great view! Loved the place from start to finish.

title: “Great Room., Super Service, Excellent Location”
text:
We travel to Chicago regularly and have always wanted to stay at the Hilton Chicago. We booked a PriceLine room on the weekend of the half marathon. The place was busy, but the staff certainly found time for each individual guest. 
The room was nice and just what we expected. The pool area is also very nice for a downtown hotel.
The location was great as we were taking in the Bears 49ers game on a Thursday night and a Sox game on a Friiday night. 
We would certainly stay there again and would recomment it to others. 
Great quality even at the regular room price.

title: “Not for you if you desire the hot spots of the Riverwalk and Shops”
text: Upon arrival not greeted by anyone or an available bellboy to carry our luggage we were told they were too busy and didnt have one. The appearance of the hotel on the website is very deceiving and the rooms nor the lobby looked anything like the pictures. The hallways while dragging our luggage to the room stunk as well as our room which was also so small and not comfortable. The ONLY thing I can say about the room was the A/C felt great and blew hard and cold. Last but not least we had to walk very far to get to the actual Riverwalk, shops, Alamo etc. because there was NOTHING around the Hotel as they portray it to be. They are located on the DEAD end of the river walk with nothing around. Needless to say we packed our stuff and left around 11 PM and went to the Hilton Palacio Del Rio which was wonderful!

title: “Great Stay - nice place for a conference.”
text:
Was here for a few days for a conference, it was very nice despite poor weather. Rich at the front desk upgraded our room, which likely made a huge difference in our experience. We ended up having a wonderful view right on the beach. 
The weather wasn't great, but we still rented Kayaks, roasted marshmallows by the pool, relaxed in the hot tub, and walked along the beach. The only issue we kind of had was that my wife tried to book a tennis lesson and it was quite a hassle.
I can't really speak to the value/ pricing of the resort because I was here for a conference and on the company dime. I probably would have been annoyed with the resort fees and the parking fees, etc... luckily I didn't have to worry about all that. 
We ate at one of the restaurants. It was decent. Happy hour drinks were reasonable. Prices were about right for hotel restaurants in CA. 
Overall nice, good if you want to stay put in one place and relax, probably not a great place to explore the San Diego area from.

title: “Very Nice”
text:
This property is an upscale facility nearby shopping and restaurants in the SouthPark section of Charlotte. There is ample free parking as well.
The staff is very friendly and the rooms are well appointed and very clean. My only complaint was the housekeeping staff was a little skimpy with the replacement of coffee cups, towels and soap/shampoo.

title: “A romantic getaway - KNOCKED OUT OF THE PARK”
text: I wanted to plan a romantic night out for my husband....... I called and spoke with Kevin and he helped me book a room and plan a surprise dinner for my husband. Shortly after hanging up the phone with him, Malcolm called from the restaurant to help set plans for dinner in stone. I had to call back and leave a message for Malcolm and then I called and confirmed my arrangements with Kevin. Shortly after, Malcolm called back to confirm our order. Upon arriving, Tim checked us in and even called our room after we had a few minutes to settle in........wonderful experience. Would stay again any time......

title: “Beautiful hotel with great, large, quiet rooms...”
text: Peninsula Hotels are always good but the one in Chicago is especially nice with a great location near Rush Street restaurants and a block over from the Magnificent Mile of high end stores and sights. The rooms are very large and nicely appointed, with huge beds and views from higher floors. I like quiet and the rooms are quiet indeed. I lost a button on my jacket and called for repair and it was back and pressed in my room in an hour. The restaurant in the lobby is very nice with an afternoon tea and a good luncheon. I would stay no where else in the windy city.

title: “Great property, service and location in Washington DC”
text: This is a great hotel to stay at for business or pleasure while in Washington DC. The property is an older building converted to hotel many years ago. Rooms are unusually large and this is one of very few central DC hotels with outside pool. I had only one request - quiet room - and they put me on back side on 9th floor and my room was very quiet. This is good location, lots of shops and restaurants within easy walk and about three easy blocks to DC Metro system. Staff friendly and helpful and my request for late checkout was accommodated. The M-F managers wine tasting is nice touch.

title: “Best price/quality ratio in town”
text: My third stay at the Chancellor was as good as the first two. Five star location, five star service, and little added touches (a mini-safe in the room, an umbrella for rainy days, an iron to press your clothes, coffee/tea/cookies/popcorn in the lobby)... Very clean rooms, recently refurbished with new large screen LCD TV's, new lamps, fans, etc. You can see this is a very well run hotel that is built on customer satisfaction. In my view, the Chancellor is the best choice for smart travellers.

title: “Do not stay here!”
text:
The hotel looks beautiful, but looks are deceiving. We had a convention there June 9-16, 2007. One of our staff couldn't sleep because she felt "something" crawling on her. Her bed was full of fleas! I kid you not! She was on the 11th floor. She called the front desk who sent someone up and turned the mattress over and yes it was infested with fleas. They told her they only had one room available, so they moved her. The "new" room was a smoking room and she nearly gagged from the smell. So they had to move her again later in the day when one opened up. 
The carpet in the hallways and meeting rooms was disgusting. I'm talking unbelievably FILTHY! The restaurant was severely understaffed and could not handle 5 people much less the nearly 300 that was coming to our convention. So they had to set up buffets. We were told that many people would NOT be a problem, but the restaurant manager apparently never got the memo. The food was really, really BAD, too.
Don't expect to print a boarding pass in their little business office. It's only open from 9-6 and closed on weekends.
Our conventions are set up 2 years prior to the event. My husband who is the Executive Director of our group and the president of our group visited the Wyndham Greenspoint 2-3 years ago and everything was perfect! The hotel looked nice, it was maintained well. Since then, the final details were handled over the phone. NOT ONCE were they told that the hotel had been sold and had run down.
The hotel bar is off the lobby and near the front entrance. It is "smoke heavy". The smell is atroucious! You can't help but smell it when you walk by and the smell drifts into some of the closer meeting rooms.
One of the porters told us that it was becoming a Hilton soon, so the Wyndham people could care less how the place looked. Lets hope the Hilton family will do some major cleaning up!

title: “Absolutely wonderful”
text: Stayed two nights while in town for a rally. From check-in to check-out the experience was great! The room was huge and well appointed. From the reception in the evenings to the breakfast in the morning the service was incredible. While we didn't eat at the restaurant we did spend our evenings in the bar. The first evening we met what I believe may be the manager of the bar/restaurant. She was awesome! She is what all service should be. Actually everyone I had contact with were very nice and helpful. The location is also nice as it is close to the Mall and it's attractions. Will certainly stay here again if I am ever back in Washington.

title: “great breakfast and comfy beds”
text:
Perfect hotel - set back a few block from magnificent mile
Cheaps eats nearby
Big, Safe & Friendly
Free evening cocktails a bonus
Rooms were perfect , fluffy towels etc etc
Pool on ground floor was perfect

title: “costomer service”
text:
You and your staff was very friendly and helpful. But I want to give my thoughts to your evening front desk person and express our graditude whos name is Angela. She found out by me that we were taking our son to his first ever NFL game between Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals. She retrieved parking information and printed it out for us and letting me know where I should park and how to get around and also about the stadium itself. Any needs that we had inlcluding my wife who has MS disease and touble walking also gave me handicap information that would benefit her. We want want you to know that Angela is a real customer service representive of your company. With people like her you will have plenty of repeat business. When we come back to Phoenix we will be looking forward to staying with you again. Thank you again. 
Ray and Lorraine

title: “Yearly Siminar”
text: Each year I attend a 2 day seminar at the Wyndham. I always have a pleasant stay and look forward to the next year. My room is clean, beds sleep comfortable, and staff are always helpful and polite. Our food is teasty, hot and well prepared.

title: “Great staff, enjoyable stay”
text:
I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at this Intercontinental. The staff was great and really friendly and helpful. Front desk/check-in, room service, concierge, valet, everyone was extremely professional and seemed to genuinely care.
The breakfast at the business club lounge was a great value. The food wasn't anything special but definitely good. Really, the staff made it a nice experience and dealt with my grumpy morning self in a great way. In fact, it made my day a whole lot better.
I'll definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Locale”
text: My family of four (kids ages 3 and 7) stayed here for just over a week. It is in a great location, and is new and clean. The free continental breakfast is great (the Texas shaped waffles were a huge hit with the kids) It is also very quiet and we even got to go swimming thanks to the heated pool. Only one complaint, the beds are quite hard. Both my husband and I had trouble sleeping through-out the night and would wake up with sore backs. Make sure you look around online for the best price, it varys greatly from site to site. We will definitely stay here when we come back.

title: “Shouldn't have opened until they'd ironed out the kinks.”
text:
I had booked this hotel as it was literally across the road from the venue I was attending, which was my whole reason for being in Baltimore. It's a lovely building, and the room was of excellent quality. There were a few missing items; no general information about Baltimore, and no Guest Directory, but as I knew this was a relatively new hotel, I overlooked this omissions.
What I can't overlook is what happened when I tried to do a load of laundry before I left. Unbeknownst to me, the guest laundry was not operational. As there was no indication AT ALL that this was the case (not even a simple "OUT OF ORDER" sign on the machines or door), I loaded the (apparently working) washing machine with my laundry and detergent, but could not start the machine. A call to the front desk confirmed that it wasn't working. This knowledge would have been helpful before I'd soaked my dirty laundry with detergent.
As I had 90 minutes before I had to leave to get a bus to Philadelphia, I accepted the offer for housekeeping to do my laundry for me. Ninety long minutes later, I still didn't have my laundry back, and I had 20 minutes to get to the other side of Baltimore to catch my bus. Eventually after practically begging for my clothes back, they were returned (still wet) and despite the best efforts of the young man driving the hotel shuttle, I did indeed miss my bus and had to forfeit my prepaid fare, then fork out $70 for a train ticket in order to get to Philadelphia in time for a pre-arranged engagement.
To say I was upset and disappointed is an understatement.
If I was in Baltimore in a year's time and needed to stay close to the same venue, I'd consider it, but would probably stay elsewhere and fork out for the cab ride instead. Particularly as they charged me for the shuttle because a cab would have taken even longer to get there.

title: “Elegance in Japan Town”
text: The Kabuki is a lovely respite in a great location. Fine service. Good restaurant. Lots of event space. The catering staff, particularly Rick Bacon, put together wonderful weddings, parties and corporate events. I've attended a few at the hotel and was always impressed with the creativity of the event and the service. I've had family stay here when they come to visit me and they loved it. Recommended.

title: “Large rooms and free parking”
text: This is part of a group of 4 or 5 hotels in the same area. All have been there for a while, but are still quite adequate for a stay in San Francisco. The biggest bargain of all is that they all include free parking, which is a godsend (both practical and financial) in The City. Our room was larger than usual and just fine in every way. Although right on Lombard Street (Hwy. 101) the street noise wound down and we slept just fine. I have stayed at the Cow Hollow previously, and that hotel was similar to this and just as nice. You can walk to Fisherman's Wharf and there are plenty of good restaurants nearby.

title: “Very diasappointed”
text:
Have stayed here several times before and very impressed. This year not impressed... Coffee pot never cleaned x 2 days only bed was made by maid those two days.
Dishwasher never emptied and any dishes in sink were left in sink.
 On Saturday night, no parking spaces were available for this paying customer due to a large party being thrown at one of the suites. As I circled the parking lot numerous times, I did see one spot become available. When I attempted to enter the spot, an individual was standing in spot and told me he was saving it for one of his friends. When asked if he was a paying customer at the hotel he told me none of my business and to move on. The next morning I noticed the trunk of my car was keyed! Also next morning moderate amount of garbage in courtyards from above mentioned party...plastic cups napkins, magazine pages just to mention a few.
I have never written a negative review of a hotel before. Very very hesitant to return next year.

title: “Great hotel on all accounts! Nice and attentive staff, great for families with the Omni Kids stuff, perfect for business, close ”
text: We mixed business and family into a fun week in Charlotte. Our stay at the Omni was great! Everyone was very nice and helpful. All of our needs were met there and we will be back!

title: “Gorgeous Place”
text: We did not actually stay at this hotel, other family members did and we spent some time there with them. Their room was lovely and they had a great view of the Alamo. Gorgeous lobby and friendly staff. Would love to stay here some time. Right in the heart of San Antonia. Everything within walking distance... The price they paid was very reasonable.

title: “Busy, central and exciting”
text: I stayed with my family for a few days before heading west. Although there was a small problem with payment when the card paying displayed an error and the bank was not contacted properly when we got to our room it was very acceptable. Only problem was that the family room was two doubles but that seems pretty much standard in the States and wasn't a huge problem. Ice machine and vending machines in the corridors were a cheaper alternative to mini bar. The hotel lobby is phenomenal and there was plenty space to wait about - also a variety of shops, coffee and a couple pay phones which meant that we could avoid paying extortionate moblie charges from our foreign phones. The breakfast buffet was insane and the omelette and waffle chefs were entertaining. All of the staff were friendly and the waiters all took the time to chat. Breakfast was expensive and we hadn't got the deal that included it so the other days we went to a cheap café round the corner. Great location and a really exciting, busy NY hotel. There was a desk that could organise trips and a really friendly guy fixed us up with our tour tickets and recommended the best deals, prices and trips. When we left the doormen easily secured us one of their cars and the driver was once again of a high standard.

title: “Good stay, bad sheets”
text: We attended a business conference in downtown Philadelphia during the week of 15 October. The Courtyard is conveniently located in the inner city and within walking distance to Independence Hall. An older building that has been nicely remodeled, we enjoyed every aspect with the exception of the bedding. A good nights rest is important on extended stays and although the beds were okay, the sheets were terrible. Several times during the night we had to get up and stretch the thinly worn sheets back over the corners. Why Marriott goes to the nth degree to make all the amenitiies comforting and provide old worn out sheets on the beds is beyond us. Also, though we booked well in advance and requested a King bed, and received confirmation of such, we were provided two double beds when we arrived.

title: “Needs upgrades”
text:
The hotel is located about a 10 minute walk on the riverwalk from restaurants. The area of town is a little sketchy afte dark and I have been approached several times by panhandlers during the day. 
The rooms are showing signs of age. I was in a room for a multiple day business conference. The size of the room was nice with a king bed and nice couch. The tv was old school 32". No high def. The bathroom sink was cracked. Water pressure and temperature was not a problem. The fitness area is at least 20 yrs out of date and multiple weight training machines were not functional. 
On a positive note, the staff were very friendly and helpful. The hotel really needs some physical improvements.

title: “Nice stay”
text:
When I travel to NYC I prefer to spend my money on shopping, wining, dining and so on. Therefore, this "budget" hotel was a great deal. It was clean, friendly and had good location.
It is not a hotel for people that are looking for a fancy stay.
The area is smocked with tourists so if you don't wish to spend 40 dollars on a breakfast for two you should try to eat somewhere else.
Aircon, computers in the lobby big plus.

title: “Inn at Union Square is Excellent”
text: Our stay at the Inn at Union Square was very comfortable. The Inn is in a great location and very convenient to shopping, public transportation and sites such as Chinatown. A small lobby, but each floor has a small lobby/sitting area where they serve hors d'oeuvres in the afternoon, cookies in the evening and a very nice continental breakfast. There is a refrigerator, ice, and coffee/tea supplies, etc. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful and the room amenities were top-rate. Granted, we were lucky enough to get a courtesy upgrade, so we had a living room, bath and bedroom, but the rooms were charming. I would definitely recommend this Inn. For the price- it can't be beat.

title: “Great for Groups”
text:
We have used this hotel in our group touring business for several years now. Never had a problem with the property to date and our customers are considered the most picky of consumers. It accurately rates 3-stars and is a good value. The staff is good compared to other hotels in the same category (not Waldorf standards but also not motel standards). 
Breakfast prices are a little out of this world, but that's SFO. (Can also enjoy the Terrace Cafe nearby-especially on holidays when the hotel restaurant is closed).

title: “Good Location - Good Value”
text: Used as a stop over for one night. Easy access to bypass around Indianpolis. Clean, comfortable, could actually open the windows and get fresh air. No complaints.

title: “Great Location, Clean, Updated Rooms, Good Value”
text: We stayed at the Comfort Inn by the Bay last week and were pleasantly surprised. We usually stay at higher-end hotels, but this time we just wanted a bed and bath since we'd be spending most of our time seeing the sights. We'll we couldn't believe what $130 a night got us at this prime location (AAA rate). The hotel is only blocks from Fisherman's Wharf and the less crowded, cable car turnaround. We were in easy walking distance to plenty of very nice restaurants and right across from famed Lombard Street. The hotel was recently remodeled and everything was clean, fresh and bright. Plus we had an outstanding view of the Golden Gate Bridge from our room. We would definitely stay here again. And parking was only $25 a night (which is cheap for SF).

title: “Good location, convenient”
text:
The hotel is in a nice and convenient location. Across the street is Central Park. Shopping on 5th Ave. is a few minutes walk away. The Metro 5th Ave/59 St. station is directly across the street from the hotel. There are two entrances. The front faces Central Park (59th St.) and the back faces 58th St. There are eateries close by the hotel. For something quick and simple, there is a small cafe next door on 58th street (Green Cafe) where you can get coffee, hot/cold drinks, soup, sandwiches, etc.
I had a nice room with a queen bed. Robes, slippers and in-room safe are provided. Toiletries are provided and refreshed daily. Continental breakfast is available on the 2nd floor. It may, or may not be included in your booking rate. There is an adequately equipped gym on the C level. Wifi is available for an additional $10 a day charge.
Two desk lamps were not working because the light bulbs had burnt out. I asked for a non-smoking room and was assigned a room on the 14th floor. When I was there, there was a constant smell of smoke from cigarettes in the hallway and faintly in the room.

title: “Very Good!”
text: This hotel has only been open for a few weeks, but I can say it's done a good deal to repair my impression of the Hilton brand. (See my other reviews for my impressions.) My wife and I stayed for 5 nights in April. We were upgraded for being a HHonors Gold, and then again due to our first room having an electrical issue. As a result, we stayed in a corner suite, which was incredible!

title: “Beautiful, modern new hotel”
text: Very contemporary, pretty new hotel near Beverly Hills. Nice rooms, good beds, and awesome views of the city. Pretty rooftop bar and pool. My only complaint is the cable tv. It was sorely deficient, with no ESPN, or PPV movies.

title: “Awesome time & money well spent”
text: First time stay but not last ! From the time of check in till the time I left there was nothing but good things I could say about the employees and the service. The check in front desk staffer Erin was very friendly and made me feel like a returning guest.The location of the hotel was in walking distance of the Union Station, a taxi ride to any scenic sights didn't cost and arm & a leg! The room was spacious and modern, the bed felt great everything was clean. Room service was prompt.There aren't enough good things to be said about this place, I will definitely be a returning guest for a weekend getaway.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
This hotel is a great find in Boston. The location in the Back Bay area is perfect - it is close to everything including shopping across the street (both food and major mall).
The room we had was very large with two queen size beds (hard to find in Boston). It was well decorated and very quiet. The hotel staff was great, the breakfast in the morning was great. The whole experience was wonderful. I would highly recommend it and would stay there again in a heartbeat. Very reasonably priced as well.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: The hotel was very clean and staff were very helpful and courteous. The elevator situation was a little annoying. We were on the 7th floor and if you were wanting to go down around check out time, you needed to ride the elevator up first and go down, otherwise the elevators were already full by the time it got to us. But the location is great and I would definitely stay there again, just on a higher floor. "The Burger Joint" on the main floor is amazing! Definitely need to try it while you're there (huge line ups all the time).

title: “Perfect for Catching a Game!”
text:
My husband and I had tickets to see the Astros on Saturday and Sunday, so we stayed at the Inn at the Ballpark. I really wanted to love this hotel, but we were in Suite 317 - an “interior” room.
What is great about the Inn at the Ballpark
- it is literally one block from Minute Maid Park (diagonally, across the street)
- service is outstanding, valet and check-in both were great experiences, as was breakfast service the following morning
- the concierge will happily hold your luggage and the valet will keep your car even after you have checked out of the Inn on Sunday, while you attend the ballgame
- the décor is beautiful and very clean in the lobby and lounge with plenty of areas to sit and relax or visit
- the décor in the suite is also quite beautiful, it has recently been updated so everything is new and housekeeping does an excellent cleaning job
- in our suite we had both a bathtub and a shower, there was plenty of water pressure and hot water (yea!)
The reasons that I will not return
- our suite had magnificent double-doors opening into it…they turned out to be two very thin doors, with the bed against the hallway wall, just inside the doors, we could clearly hear every conversation in the hallway all night long
- our suite was the closest room to the elevators so we could hear the 2 dings of the elevator each time it stopped on our floor
- the room was bordered by the hallway along one long wall, and there was a long, solid wall of windows over-looking the lounge area on the other side covered only with wooden blinds (no drapes). This posed two problems: first, there was nothing to insulate against the noise and music rising up from the lounge, so it was very loud (fortunately it does stop a little after midnight when they close the lounge); second, the bed faces the wall of windows and first thing in the morning the light comes streaming in around the blinds right into your face, and without drapes there is no way to block it. Since the music starts again a little after 8 a.m. along with the elevator traffic, it’s not that big of a deal because it would be impossible to sleep late anyway.
Things that were just inconvenient
- the shower head in the bathtub was perfect, it was nice and high, but we preferred to shower in the shower…but the shower head in the shower was almost too low for me at 5’6” and way too short for my 6’3” husband!)
- there was not an a/c vent in the bathroom so it was really warm in there with lights/shower/blow dryer/etc and no way to cool it down.
- the closet (in the suite) is very, very small so two people could not hang clothes for more than just a weekend
- the only mirror was in the bathroom, so there was no full-length mirror for dressing and if someone is in the bathroom with the door closed there is no way to finish getting ready (putting on makeup, curling hair, other mirror-required activities) at the same time.
Other things you should know:
- valet is the only parking option and it is $23/night
- there is not a swimming pool or hot tub
- if you do not plan on a quiet stay (like if you will be in the lounge until midnight) and just need a really nice place close to the ballpark because you will be at the games, this is a beautiful hotel and you will receive excellent service.

title: “scary people hanging out around this hotel”
text:
The biggest problem with this hotel is that we did not feel safe here. There were many seedy looking people that appeared to be living at the place. They didn't appear to be the average tourist and just hung out, watching other people. At night, a security guard patroled the place, but there were still loud obscenity filled arguments, thrown bottles, gunning engines and loud music all through the night. We dead bolted our door and hoped for the best.
The room was supposed to be non-smoking, but smelled of smoke. There were cigarette burns in the furniture and blanket. The room was reasonably clean, but run down.
The price advertised on the sign out front was $20 dollars or so less than what we paid through hotels.com, which was also non-refundable.
I do have to say that the staff was very pleasant and helpful, but the look on the faces of some of the other tourists checking in reminded me of a deer caught in the headlights. I think they were scared to stay here too.

title: “Fabulous location”
text:
The staff were friendly and very helpful, the rooms and public areas very clean, and the beds are just so comfy. We had a few issues with the shower, which seemed to have a mind of it's own, it went from freezing to very very hot, as the maintainence guy was unable to fix it, we were moved to another room and as compensation we were given free buffet breakfasts for the remainder of our stay, 4 people x 5 days!! 
Would I stay here again - Definately! - even without the free breakfasts, which incidently were amazing.
.

title: “Staff bent over backwards to assist and accommodate our conference”
text: The James A. Michener Society chose this hotel for its annual meeting and loved the hotel! The value for what we received could not have been better. The staff was warm, hospitable, and accommodating; the rooms were very clean and comfortable, and the meals were served hot and delicious. The complimentary shuttle service made access to the Riverwalk so convenient. The hospitality suite was perfect for our group to meet and relax.

title: “Don't stay here if you plan to sleep”
text:
I'm in Room 1803 in the Allerton, which faces MIchigan Avenue. Every minute or two a traffic signal on the street below emits a series of loud beeping noises. It's extremely loud -- imagine an alarm going off in your room. I called to switch rooms but the only rooms left are facing Michigan Ave., so I guess I'm out of luck. I guess I won't be getting any sleep tonight.
They brought ear plugs to my room, so that may help.
Also: There is a work desk in the room, but there's no lamp on the desk. So it's a desk you can't work at during the evening because there isn't enough light. Argh.

title: “Great Hotel For The Price!”
text: We Stayed here during a shopping trip to chicago. Although the room was really small it was big enough for two women and ALL their Christmas shopping bags (and thats saying alot!) The price and location of the hotel made up for the room size.

title: “Great Location, as good as the reviews say”
text:
I took my GF here for Christmas as a romantic suprise, (and to propose to her - thankfully she said yes :), naturally I wanted a great hotel with a perfect location to set the mood for a magical christmas.
we arrived well before booking out (3pm), as as expected our room wast ready. after having lunch and exploring a little, our room wasn't ready an hour and a half later, so they upgraded us to a bigger room, which was greatly appreciated.
our room was immaculately clean, and well detailed. we returned to our room ever night to a box of chocolates and 2 bottles of water, which was a nice touch. the bed was in a league of its own - every bit as amazing as people have mentioned! I knew they were reknowned for their comfortable beds, but they were dangerously comfortable - often you'd lie down and find you didn't want to get up again!
we abstained from the hotel breakfasts, instead opting for a more American style breakfast at the Red Flame Diner (a few doors down), which turned out to be very affordable, with tasty food and generous portions. 
We hadn't booked any restaurants, and the concierge were of great help. every question asked and request we made was dealt with efficiently and accurately.
Location wise, its between 5th and 6th ave - 2 blocks from Times Square, which is very central indeed. we walked most places, and caught the subway to Macy's and other shopping areas like Prince St and even Century 21. (line R) we caught cabs to various restaurants around Manhattan and on average spent between $10 and $15 each way.
Our 5am checkout took all of 2 minutes, so overall a very happy stay at the Sofitel Hotel . We will definitely be back next time we go to New York.

title: “easy access”
text: We stayed at this property while attending a memorial service. We were landing at noon, and leaving at 8am the following morning. This is close to the airport and the rental car returns. The hotel itself at night was a bit noisy as we could hear people in the hallways, but that was the extent of it. The rooms were very clean, bathrooms had everything you need. Beds were very comfortable. Everything you expect from a Hilton property.

title: “Great location and staff!”
text: They really rolled out the pink carpet for us for the Susan G. Komen 3-Day for the Cure. It was a real treat to get a bag breakfast for our 4:45 am bus ride to the opening ceremonies!

title: “Great Experience!”
text: I had a great experience at Hotel Rex. The staff was friendly, professional and helpful. My room was well lit, clean and beautifully decorated. There was a nice large flat screen tv, comfortable large bed, wifi Plus the valet service was a deal. I will refer friends and family. I hope to stay at the Rex again.

title: “Great Place”
text: We were pleasantly surprised at the great service and amenities at this hotel. Every employee was eager to serve. When we asked for additional pillows, it took 2 minutes for them to bring pillows......and they brought 2 more than we requested! They had chocolates each night and when we checked out they asked if there was anything they could have done better. They had complimentary drinks each evening, complimentary breakfast, and we could hear the waves crashing on the beach as we slept. It is a ways off the freeway but we would stay again......eagerly!

title: “Nice Hotel. 1.5 miles from the Mall. Metro station 5 blocks away”
text:
Friendly Staff…Valet parking only @ $25 per day. No wireless internet, just CAT 5 cable only. During my 4 night stay, my internet did not work in my room and was never resolved by calling tech support. Was lucky enough to find an unsecured wireless access point and connected or connected via their business center. Requested king non smoking room via reservation and was told only a smoking king available. Settled for a room with double beds which was not as comfortable, but was not about to switch rooms after unpacking everything.
This was like a nice small 1 bedroom apartment. 2 TVs. 2 phones. Everything you need. Nice modern furnishings and décor. No separate work area/desk. Just the kitchen table. Kitchenette – D/W, frig (w/ ice maker), microwave. 24 hour convenience store. DVD player. Complimentary breakfast and Dinner is served Mon-Thur. Check-out time 12 Noon. I would stay here again.

title: “Great location, wonderful place to stay”
text: We stayed at Palomar over the Christmas holiday. We loved it! The rooms were spacious and the staff could not have been more helpful. Our room was clean and quiet. We are planning another visit to DC with friends and will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great value !”
text: Stayed night before our flight and then on the way back again. Clean rooms, nice complimentary breakfast (kids loved the waffles), efficient front desk and timely/very friendly shuttle service to the airport. Would definitely stay again. Everything you need from an airport hotel. Pleasant surprise :)

title: “Comfy stay in Times Square”
text: I stayed 2 nights at the Marriott Marquis and had a great time. I did not realize the check-in desk was on the 8th floor so I needed some guidance when entering the hotel at the street level. The staff was very professional and courteous in helping me. The assigned elevator system is a bit unique but I actually enjoyed the quick speed and the dramatic views. Only once did I feel crowded on my elevator rides. The room itself was clean and nicely furnished. Bigger than most hotel rooms in the city. I was on the 29th floor overlooking Times Square. Magnificent view! The bed and pillows were super comfortable. I did not experience any neighbor noise at all just some sirens from the street, but hey this is NYC!! I ordered pizza and wings from room service one evening during peak dinner hours. The service took about 40 minutes but the price was reasonable for a New York hotel. Food was tasty! The concierge desk suggested this great little diner nearby for Sunday brunch. The type of place you would probably not find on your own. During checkout my travel guest and I requested that the billing be adjusted so that we could evenly split the charges for our expense accounts. The desk staff handled this within 2 minutes and without any hassle. No complaints about this hotel. So if you're looking a good-sized, comfortable room and want to be in the middle of it all in Times Square then the Marriott Marquis is an excellent choice!

title: “dark night”
text: I loved this hotel, my husband not so much. What I loved - - utterly quiet, very comfortable, clean, dark, cocoon-like, chic. convenient. Did I mention quiet? After a day in NYC it's lovely to retreat to such a place of calm and peacefulness. My huisband just thought it was dark. I loved the black and white wallpaper. The beds were VERY good. My husband slept really well but muttered about the lack of natural light. Oh well, the window was a window well. But who cares? I imagined being a vip guest in Batman's own guest suite in the bat-mansion. Yes, that cool. The staff was great, they got it just right. Everything was very easy, all taken care of (car whisked away and brought back in sceonds when needed, anything amiss fixed instantly) so absolutely no complaints at all.

title: “A Nice Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Washington Jefferson Hotel on a weekend trip to New York. The hotel is in a great location, close to central park and times square. Its also only a block from a subway stop and close to a pharmacy that has almost everything in it. The rooms at the Washington Jefferson are small and simple. For New York city the price is very reasonable but to some extent you get what you pay for, the rooms are small but clean and with everything you need in them. The hotel does not have ice machines on every floor and does not have room service. The front desk staff are very helpful with directions and whatever you need. I would definitely go back and stay there.

title: “Above and Beyond”
text: This is our second trip to The Magnolia for procedures done at Baylor Hospital. There is no hotel that would bend over backwards for us as has The Magnolia. This included not only a less expensive "hospital rate," but brought a driver in hours early to get us to the hospital at 5:30AM. We would not even think of staying in another hotel in Downtown Dallas.

title: “Nice location”
text: Very nice experience. Friendly, efficient staff. Priced right and location great. Nice and clean with comfy bed and bedding. Negative is breakfast area is inefficiently set up, cramped and food is very blah. Close to public transportation to get you anywhere you want to go. Will stay here again if opportunity presents itself.

title: “Average Conference Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Westin Copley Place in April for a conference. We had three rooms in our party. The higher floors definitely have a better view, but the location of the hotel is fantastic. It is steps from the Liberty Trail & the Boston Public Library. Our room was average, but loved the Starbucks coffee machine (like Keurig) in the room. And we always enjoy the Heavenly bed of Westins.

title: “great location,but nothing else”
text: stayed at the wharf on the 16th. Got a pretty good price of 130.00 a night. what you pay for is the location, it is right across the street from the wharf. most of the rooms are not bay views. if you take a car it is an extra 45 a night including tax. you do not need a car if you are staying here, so don't get one. the sleep number was nice, did not hear and disturbing noises because of thin walls. if i had to do it again i would stay at the holiday inn, it has a free breakfast, parking was not as expensive and it is a block from the wharf. or i would rent a car stay across the golden gate and take a ferry to the wharf if ou wan to see it. best view to eat on the wharf was bubba gumps, food was over priced but everything is in san fran. i can only recommend this hotel for the location.

title: “Not the "jewel" as advertised”
text:
The marriot was okay, nothing special. The rooms are very small and remind me of an old holiday inn. The room service food was horrible. I ordered a hamburger, VERY well done, no pink. They brought a rare hamburger, and the fries tasted horrible. The hotel does have a great valet service, with a ton of taxis waiting. I liked the bar/lobby area. It was very high-tech with flat screen tvs everywhere. They also have free internet service in the lobby/bar area as well as great connection in the rooms, but there was a charge, of course. i recently stayed at the Conrad and the internet connection was almost non-existent. i requested room internet service, at a price, but whenever I tried to log in with my ipad it would not connect. They need to move into 2012. (The Conrad!). 
Every staff member was very welcoming and friendly, although sometimes a little too freindly.
It was clean and very new. I would much rather stay at the Marriot than the Conrad. It was terrible!

title: “Home away from home”
text: The staff and the quality is very good. They have good dinner service after a day of work. The staff even remeberd my name. Hope to go back soon. The place is close to different restaurants and also good shopping places

title: “Outstand staff--from Maid Service to Back office”
text:
I very recently had an extended stay at your newest Houston hotel, Crown Plaza, River Oaks. It is impossible to put in words the excellence of your staff at this hotel, especially during such a difficult time, personally.
My wife was a leukemia patient at MD Anderson. She stayed at your hotel for the week of March 22 while being evaluated for a clinical trial. We subsequently returned to your hotel, and I stayed from April 5, until checking out on April 28, two days after my wife died.
I cannot tell you how impressed I was with your staff. Everyone, and I mean everyone, was as friendly and as helpful as could be. I could probably go on for paragraphs, but I want to take the time to thank--by name--some of you staff. On the Front, Desk, Chris Clay, Roxanne, Kristy, and Jackie. Your shuttle drivers Nazar (Nick), Anas, and Daniel. All the housekeeping staff, especially the Director/Manager (I believe his name is Mike) and the ladies that work the third floor. Although I didn’t get their names, I don’t want to exclude the gift shop or restaurant staff. I didn't get to meet many of the back office staff, but I was fortunate to meet Debbie Hollier, Director of Sales and Market and discussed this review with her. I told her that if someone feels strongly enough to write a derogatory review for poor service, then they should feel equally strong enough to write a good review for excellent service. She graciously provided me the information to do so. Along that same vein, I'm sure if an employee was singled out, by name, for poor service it would be brought to his or her attention immediately. I expect the same thing to happen regarding this review. 
My understanding is that you recently purchased this property from Holiday Inn. If this is the same staff, it is certainly Holiday Inn's loss and your gain. If not, congratulations on picking a winning team!
Again, thank you for a memorable stay during what was a very difficult time for me personally. If I am ever in Houston again, you can be assured that I will only stay at the Crown Plaza, River Oaks.
Respectfully yours,
William Murdock

title: “No longer "Americas Worst"”
text:
I came here for a business trip & stayed here with low expectations. I was greatly surprised though. The hotel staff was very friendly. I arrived at 2 am & had to be at a meeting downtown 5 hours early. The staff was kind enough to give me a wake-up call.
Breakfast was small, but better than most Americas Best with Waffles, pastries, fruits & juice. They gave me an extended checkout.
Wi-Fi worked good. Rooms are large. Flat screen TV. Ended up staying an extra night. Great motel for people on a budget. In a good safe area too. Has an indoor pool which I didnt use.

title: “A Pleasant Stay With Very Friendly and Helpful Staff”
text:
I stayed in the Elan hotel with my girlfried at the end of April 07, based on the reviews on trip advisor. The location of the hotel is good (not too far from either Beverly Hills or Hollywood - though I wouldn't recommend walking), the staff are some of the best (if not the best) I've come across and the room was a decent size. It also had nice little touches like leaving chocolates on your pillow and putting classical music on after your room had been cleaned.
However, the hotel perhaps isn't quite as great as some people seem to be making out and isn't too special. For example, it doesn't have a resturant and the food they can order for you (from the cafe over the road) leaves something to be desired.
Overall though a good stay and somewhere I would certainly recommend!

title: “good position”
text:
Me and my wife were last week in this hotel for 4 nights. It's clean hotel with simple and small rooms. Room was equiped by aircondition, satTV, bathroom, fan. They cleaned room and changing towels every day. 
Personal on reception was unfriendly and boring. Hotel is equiped with free wifi.

title: “The New Yorker, August 2012”
text:
My partner and I stayed in the New Yorker over 5 nights towards the end of August 2012. 
We had settled on the New Yorker after an extensive search of NY accommodation ahead of our trip. We were not disappointed, although the room was small (we were expecting smaller!) it was cosy, clean and comfortable. The housekeeping staff are excellent also, cleaning our room everyday to a high standard and replenishing towels, etc when required. 
The location of the hotel is ideal, many attractions are a short walk away, but you also have excellent public transport links. There were plenty of great eateries close by too. 
This was our first time in New York, and as many visitors are advised ahead of visiting, very little of your time will be spent in your hotel – this is true – considering this, I would highly recommend the New Yorker as a comfortable, clean and good value (considering it’s location) hotel. We were delighted with our stay, and would happily stay in the New Yorker again when we return to New York.

title: “Absolutely fantastic”
text:
We just got back from Seattle and we stayed for one night at the Silver Cloud Hotel Stadium. Previous comments complained about the valet parking at $22+tax - it is not cheap, however, we drove around the blocks and thought that the hotel's parking was the safest esp. when there are events going on at the 2 sports stadiums. Valet service was very good - very polite and wait time was minimal. 
Check in was a breeze. And we got upgraded to a suite :) That was a really nice surprise. Also we got the lowest price booking the hotel through their website than hotwire/priceline. The room was a 5 stars, with comfy couches, a microwave and a mini fridge. The vending machine on our floor sold pops and water for $1 (awesome deal). We got a great view of the Safeco Field on the 7th floor but the best is going to the rooftop and enjoying the pool/whirlpool while enjoying the scenery of Seattle. The pool is not very deep (3ft9 deepest) - so ideal for children while parents get to suntan and relax on the lounge chairs. There is also a phone that directly allows you to order food from the restaurant/bar (Jimmy's) downstairs. The servers bring the food up to you. 
The shuttle is one very attractive service offered by the hotel. You just have to reserve a spot at the front desk and they are on time. We went downtown and had dinner at the crab pot. The shuttle took us just in front of the restaurant. We called to have it picked us up, and within 10 min (as they said it would arrive), the shuttle was ready to bring us back to the hotel. 
Only downside - we were not able to book the hotel for another night because it was all booked up :( This is to say how awesome it is! :)
We would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone who is going to the game at either Century Link Stadium or Safeco Stadium and to whoever is not picky for walking 15-20 min to downtown or take the complementary shuttle!

title: “Perfect Location”
text: I booked this Hotel using my points with Choice Privileges for one of the coldest weekends of the year ending in 2008 (Zero*), the Hotel was in the PERFECT location in NYC, the room was very comfortable, very warm, and up to date, especially the bathroom for the wife. You will not be disappointed with your stay at this Hotel and yes I will return to this Hotel for further trips to NY City in the future.

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: We stayed in the Marriott Metro Center for one night this April 2006. This is an extremely clean, beautiful hotel. We have stayed in lots of hotels in the DC area and this is quickly becoming our favorite. The rooms are clean, large and have very comfortable furniture. The hotel staff was very helpful and polite. The location is right at Metro Center with the entrance on the South side of the hotel. Lots of activities in the area and walking distance to most of the area attractions. The hotel security is polite but efficient and we did not mind a bit being checked out since they are looking our for us and were so nice about it. We did not eat in the restaurants, but did have coffee downstairs and walked around in the Regatta Raw Bar. Large and plenty of space around the tables and booths, so you are not crowded.

title: “Tammy's customer service is outstanding!”
text: Tammy & Tracy( manger) treated us with outstanding customer service! I highly recommend this hotel. Not only did we receive amazing customer service but it's very clean and modern. The rooms are large and the beds comfortable. You will not be disappointed if you stay here.

title: “Nice surprise. Safe, comfortable and clean for those on a budget.”
text:
This was my first trip to NYC, I've read read so many horror stories about $100USD accomodation but couldn't afford much more - so took the tripadvisor steer.
I was pleasantly surprised. The location is perfect for a first trip to NYC - 2 blocks from Times Square, short stroll to 42nd street, etc. Ok, die-hard New Yorkers will tell you there are more culturally refined places to stay, but to get your bearings and a taste of the city there is no better first stop to be in the middle of it.
Slight apprehension as I entered - the lobby felt a fraction scruffy and laid back, but my room was charming, warm, comfortable, safe, had some character and was splotlessly clean. Bathroom had a cute 1930's style, but again was again completely fresh - with new tiles, sanitaryware, plenty hot water, and again spotless. 
I gradually started to leave my laptop, bb and phone out while away - although never sensible, I didn't have any problem. For the price it was a safe and cosy little paradise.
Only one very minor objection - the heating was a little high for my liking so despite it snowing outside (in january) i chose to open my window into the lightwell at nights. It seemed a couple of pidgeons had moved into the lightwell - and the sound of them flapping and cooing early morning was a bit gross. This could be solved in an hour by management putting some spikes on the window sills.
I still rate 5/5, for the price and location i will definately return.

title: “Very good hotel”
text: This hotel has lots to offer: great location near Universal Studios, good service, nice rooms and a good restaurant. Our arrival was greeted professionally, and the room was ready. The hotel is constructed in several buildings and ours was six stories. The room itself has little that is special, but the rooms were clean and the beds were good. A tiny balcony brought in a bit of fresh air. Although the hotel is quite near the freeway, the noise was not a problem. The restaurant was nice, although a bit pricey. Miguel, our waiter, put a smile on our faces both mornings with his infectious energy. We would stay again.

title: “Very Nice, Comfortable”
text: We were in Ft.Worth to celebrate a birthday and stayed at the Hilton downtown, the rooms were comped so I'm not sure what the pricing is but I think reasonable for the area. The hotel was clean, comfortable and well staffed. Our room was large, clean and well appointed though a little dull on the color scheme (mostly beiges and browns). The staff was helpful if not cheerful, but I attribute that more to management than the acutal personnel. The restaraunt staff was friendly and the waiter "Joe" was very nice and friendly. The location is fantastic if you want to be down town, relatively easy to access from I35 and easy traveling to the FT.Worth Stockyards. We did have to pay for parking in the hotel.

title: “Great location...”
text: I loved San Fran, and this hotel was a pretty great find, comfortable rooms, and amazing location... There were minor things that were annoying e.g. the shower rod holding together the shower was broken, and the cleaning lady walking in as i was asleep at 9 am, these things were only a small annoyance, but i still would recommend this hotel, really friendly staff, and they were very accommodating to hold our luggage when we had a late flight, a great price too, the only thing that was a bit of a pain was the wi-fi was not free, and every hotel i have stayed in in the usa has had internet included free, but still would highly recommend hotel

title: “Great Front Desk Service - Very Welcoming”
text:
First the gripe; Stayed here for weekend convention center event in August. The place was sold-out with many if not most of the guest part of the convention center events. The problem is that management did not think or made a decision not to staff up for the shuttle transportation for the evenings and weekend. A major inconvenience and oversight in my opinion. When we had time to wait we took Molly or walked in the evening heat. A couple times we shared a cab. 
Anyway that said, the room, front desk staff and overall experience were great. We were very busy and didn't spend a lot of time around the hotel but is was very comfortable and welcoming. Front desk did their best to help out despite being very busy.

title: “good hotel - great situation”
text:
We loved this hotel. There are some reviews stating that the decor is a bit faded. Personally we hope that they do not "modernise" it any time soon. It has real quality and character.
Oviously the bit problem at the moment is the noise. In our case the hotel was top notch in getting us a suite on the quiet side of the hotel - five star. However I am afraid to say that if you cannot get a room on the quiet (South Side) of the hotel I could not recommend that you stay here - my wife had a head ache in the first hour and you litterly cannot hear yourself speak.
The hotel is doind its very best with the situation but if you have a noisy room you just cannot enjoy your stay.

title: “Great stay ... will definitely return.”
text:
Just home from a five night family stay (2 adults, 2 children). We were very impressed with the quality of the service and the overall facility. Our 2 queen room was large enough for the four of us, the beds (especially the pillows) were very comfortable and the fridge was a much used addition.
