Each and every staff member we encountered were friendly and very helpful.
We appreciated the "guest of the day" gift in our room at check-in and the water vouchers in our key envelope. The girls really liked the fresh cookies in the lobby in the evenings. Free internet access was reliable and easy to use.
The location is fantastic, especially for visiting with a family, as we were able to return to the hotel for quick breaks between activiites. The hotel is very close to theatres (we saw "Rain: A Tribute to the Beatles" just around the corner) and convenient to public transit and shopping. The "Olympic Diner" across the street was great for breakfast and the "Food Emporium" on the next corner was convenient for picking up fruit, sandwiches and muffins - their hot food also looked great (eat-in or take out).
We had a great stay and hope to return again!

title: “Breakfast, Pillows, Points, not so good”
text:
There are dozens of hotels from which to choose in Charlotte. I chose the Holiday Inn because I already had some points and wanted to reach teh free night level (I know - it is my own fault). I had 2 trips planned. When I arrived on the first trip, the clerk told me that if I signed up for this special program, I could get double points, but only if I stayed twice. I checked in, signed up, stayed twice, and not only did I not get double points, I get less than expected for normal points. Well, the program has a sign-up in advance or that night doesn't count and then once you sign up, if you only stay once, you get nothing (the program is double or nothing). So I felt cheated and won't go back.
As far as the room, my chief complaint was the pillows were worn out. Also, the elevators were slow, and I was quite a ways up.
On my next stay, I stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn. The breakfast was 10 times better (hot and made to order). The pillows were soft, and the shuttle will drop you door-to-door.
I will always stay at the HGI from now on.

title: “O.K for City Break”
text:
We have stayed here for three nights.
Location of this hotel is brilliant just across from Grand Central. Breakfast is a la carte and we were fully satisfied every morning. Patio bar was handy.
I would recommend to get the room without facing the street , street can get very noisy from the trucks arriving to the building right across the hotel in ridiculous hours (3 am, 4 am usually)
But overall good hotel for New York city break.

title: “Worst Staff Ever”
text:
I have stayed twice at this hotel because it seems to have all the accomidations I want, a nightculb in the hotel, a pool, and the hotel is lovley. The first time we had a party. My credit card was charged twice, and the staff hounded me DURING THE PARTY when my cc company wouldn't take the second double charge (thank you B of A). My biggest complaint is the staff. They are not helpful, very "I'm too busy to help you" attitudes. I had a very difficult time nagivating my way to the room and no-one would take time to help me. When I went to the nightclub, the ASSISTANT MANAGER was so unfriendly and straight RUDE we even had an argument and I left. I will not go here again.
P.S. SUPER expensive parking with little validations availiable

title: “Wow!”
text:
I had the pleasure of staying at this lovely resort and I was totally happy with everything! The room was spacious and lovely and the bed was beyond comfortable - I told everyone it was like sleeping on a cloud! I ate at Josie's and the food was amazing - I have never had fried green tomatoes and I am a total fan now - but only if Charlotte makes them! And the Lemon Icebox Pie with Meringue was flawless (Don't tell my grandmother!).
The front drive staff was genuinely friendly and very professional and of course, you can't beat the location - it was absolutely gorgeous! I can't wait to get back there again!

title: “No tv and no free internet”
text: Every thing was just ok. My family and I walked in and were greeted by a outgoing man, who quickly tried to help us and our service needs. We got to our room put our stuff down and left. After getting back I turned on the tv and it did not work, thats fine with me as long as I had my internet but loo and behold I was first to pay $13 for it. So I thought maybe they would give me something for the nonworking tv like a $5 show, movie, or internet they flatout said no. this problem has happening for four days and no fix.

title: “Management and staff are awesome”
text:
Manager LaTonya is wonderful. She Is very accommodating and friendly. I have been here over a year and have never had a problem that wasn’t resolved in a very short period of time. Cleaning staff does amazing jobs in the rooms and the front desk staff know me by name and have always been a pleasure to talk too. 
If you need a place to stay in the Northwest area of Houston, I HIGHLY recommend Extended Stay America on Hollister. A+ Facility all the way!

title: “DO NOT STAY AT THIS HOTEL !!”
text:
As part of an 80th birthday celebration for my aunt and 60th birthday for a dear friend of ours, 16 members of our group stayed at the Hotel Milano for 3 days. To start off our horrible experience, a wheelchair that I had ordered from a medical supply company for my aunt had been refused by the front desk staff. Had I not heard the front desk agent on the phone with the supply company mention that he did not have anyone with my last name due to check in, I would have blamed the supplier for not having the wheelchair on site when they promised. The hotel was notified and agreed that they would store the chair for us if it came before our arrival. When asking for assistance to have the chair picked up, or find a provider closer that could get a wheelchair there so we could begin our city exploration they had no willingness to help us at all.
Upon check-in our rooms were not together. Some on 3rd floor and some on the 7th floor. While I am not a hotel manager, it seems logical to me that reservations made as a group should have rooms held together for check-in. Again, no regret and no willingness to make accommodations.
Two of the rooms booked were for four people ... even with two people in a double queen room, I've never heard of only having two towels in the room!! It took a few calls to the front desk to have additional towels and pillows delivered. After housekeeping serviced the room the next day - calls for additional towels needed to be made once again!
The air conditioning in one of the rooms was not working and did not work the entire time we were there. Nor, were the people in that room moved to another room to ensure their comfort and quality of stay.
The carpet in the lobby was filthy ... the computer for boarding pass printing did not work. We asked to borrow a few glasses from the connecting restaurant assuring them we would return them in less than 30 minutes. They must all be in business together, as they were just as uncooperative.
Add insult to injury - upon our return home we found that we were over charged by several hundred dollars. Parking for one car was charged to multiple rooms. 
Both my daughter and I spoke to Condo in accounting to straighten out the billing issues. The uncooperativeness, rudeness and lack of concern for customer satisfaction permeates through all staffing levels at this hotel. When asked if there was some type of customer satisfaction survey or a way to submit issues and concerns to management, Condo told me he was the only person to talk to. There was no general manager for the hotel ... AND, that he really didn't care what my issues were!!!
The one bright spot during our stay was the housekeeper outside our room once we checked in. There was no help in the lobby for luggage. My husband had to go to the medical supply place across town to pick up the wheel chair, so I was dragging our bags to our room by myself. The housekeeper saw me struggling and was extremely helpful in holding the door and assisting me to get the bags inside the room. PLUS - she spoke fluent English and could communicate.
The location is extremely convenient, but NEVER, NEVER, NEVER would I ever spend another dollar or recommend this hotel to even my worst enemy!
As an added reason to stay away, while I was taking my bags up in the elevator, a young couple that was honeymooning in San Francisco asked me why someone downstairs wasn't helping me. I didn't want to ruin their time by giving them my horror story even before I got to my room. They quickly shared that they couldn't wait to get out of there. Their room was filthy, the staff was rude and the rooms overpriced for the level of service that was being provided.

title: “Top quality. Excellent location.”
text: Eli in VIP check in is a tremendous asset to the HARD ROCK. My Favorite place to stay in San Diego.

title: “Overall a good place to stay for a visit to the Inner Harbor”
text:
My husband and I booked the New Year's Eve package at the Brookshire. This was our second trip to the harbor. Previously, we stayed at the Hyatt. 
There were a few things that I would recommend for improvement. They have no onsite self-park. You can pay $29 a night for valet. There is a self-park next door that you can use. Our room was not ready when we arrived at four for check in, as they told us "house keeping was a little behind". The person in charge of housekeeping walked by and mumbled "its gonna be a while." we left our cell phone number, and they did call within the hour. Luckily, we were just next door at the Gallery mall. The room was clean when we arrived, however the next day housekeeping did not do a very thorough job. The rug seemed to not have been vacuumed and there were some crumbs on the counter. Even though they were our own, it would have been comforting to think they were doing a thorough cleaning job all the time. One other thing that they might want to do something about is the keeping an eye on the people who linger around the property. Several times when we were leaving, we were approached by individuals asking for money. It became a little uncomfortable after the second time.
 Despite the things I mentioned above, if you can get a good rate or package, it is a good place to stay when visiting the Inner Harbor. Our room was very large, with a bedroom and living room. The breakfast buffet was very good. They have both cold and hot items. The staff was on top of the clean up as well. They seem to go out of their way to be sure everyone was comfortable and had a place to sit and eat. The night reception was limited in food providing crackers and cheese, but was abundant in local wine and beer. The location may be the best feature of this hotel. It is within walking distance of all the local attractions. We were even able to walk to Fells Point and Little Italy. 
 I would stay here again on my next trip to Baltimore. Also, if you have pets, they are pet friendly for an additional fee.

title: “Great Location”
text: The Marriott Downtown is near the Reading Terminal Market. Fabulous prices at restaurants in the market. Cheap fresh fruits and veggies, and rare Amish made cheeses, fresh fish market, beef, and chicken. A Maggiano's is across the street as well as a Hardrock Cafe. The staff is friendly and security roams the halls. This is a great location to also view historic Philadelphia.

title: “Beautiful, historic hotel”
text: This hotel was in a great location, and absolutely gorgeous. The rooms were slightly on the smaller side, I'm assuming because the hotel was built a long time ago. Wonderful service, the staff was welcoming and very helpful. This was a great experience.

title: “My new hotel in NYC”
text:
This is now the only place I will stay in NYC. I booked a long weekend trip to the city for my mom and I. We were greeted and then were referred to by name anytime we went in or out. My mom loved it! 
The location was close enough to a subway station that my mom had no trouble. The ability to choose my pillows was wonderful as my mom actually uses one of the special types. 
Our view was on the higher floors with a corner room and we had 2 full walls of windows. What a view!

title: “Avenue of stars!!! 2 night stay. The constellation not movie stars!”
text: Oh dear, what a disappointment. We arrived at 7am in the morning from Hawaii as our flight was messed up. My husband and I were exhausted after a long flight. Only one guy on duty, which was ridiculous for such a big hotel. No one to drag our cases to our room. Just given the keys. Managed to take our credit card details fast enough! Went straight to bed as so tired, no courtesy water, just two small bottles the cheapest at $5.00 each.Got up couple of hours later to the noise of generators and a view of them also. Awful. Was too tired to complain. Went down to reception and they wer quite helpful when I asked for maps and directions. They offered a courtesy car whic takes you to a mile and a half of where you would like to go and a free pick up when you request it. We asked them to take us to Rodeo Drive which took about ten minutes which was great and gave the driver a small tip. He stated that if we wanted to be picked up we would be, unfortunately we waited 45 minutes after phoning to pick us up and they failed to appear. We got a cab back which cost us a tiny bit more than the tip we had given. When we got back to the hotel they had no excuse and no apology. Would never recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Exceptional Value”
text:
In Mahatten for 1 night (business meetings the next day). The hotel is very convenient, just a few block from the "E" Subway station (53rd & Lexington). Took about an 1 hour to get to/from JFK (via E subway and Airtrain). 
Obtained room via Priceline, and was an exceptional value. May have been reason why I was offered a room on the 2nd floor (209). Thought about asking for a room higher up, but usually do not have any problems sleeping. Despite being a corner room, it was surprisingly quiet. With 1 king bed, it was a decent size room. 
The best aspect about being on the 2nd floor was I was able to use the Wifi signal from the Staple store accross the street. Was able to avoid the hotel internet charge of $13? a day.
The fitness room was well equipped and is located on the 2nd floor (in addition to the club room). The ice machine is on the 4th floor.
Definitely will try to stay here for upcoming trips.

title: “We loved the Hotel but Parking charge was unacceptable”
text: Hotel was great. Rooms spacious and clean. Staff was responsive but the $34 a night charge was outrageous and fraudulent. I can understand charging for people who are not staying at the hotel to park but to charge someone who is staying at the hotel $34 a night to park their car is unbelievable. It clearly is a bait and switch where you are charged a lower amount for the room so people book a stay at the hotel and then the hotel gets the money back by charging an outrageous parking fee. I guess you could charge $20 a night to stay at the hotel but charge you $100 a night to park. I am not going to walk to San Diego, so I have to have a car. Parking somewhere else overnight tends to be a hassle and I like having my car close in case I need it. Marriott should be embarassed by this practice.

title: “Location, amenities and service ensured we mixed pleasure w/our business”
text: In Chicago on business, but couldn't help but feel we were in the city for pleasure trip because of the great location (close to Rush St., shops of Michigan Ave., and simply the feeling of being in a quaint neighborhood w/in the city), the hotel style and amenities (great lobby & patio lounge, comfortable/modern decor, fantastic rooms w/ great beds, separate soaking tub and shower in roomy bathroom, great bath amenities), and very efficient service.

title: “Don't take your gun”
text:
We spent three nights in a suite in April 2007.
The hotel is in a great location, 1 minute from I40 just 20 minutes drive from the airport and downtown area. Parking is great, with a huge parking lot right outside. All the main restaurant chains are within a 10 minute walk, unfortunately if you tried to walk after sundown, you wouldn't last 10 minutes.
The hotel staff were extremely friendly and helpful, although they did manage to check in some other guests to our room and they walked right in on us. Fortunately I don't own a gun so nobody got hurt, and the manager did give us a free nights accommodation to compensate for the intrusion.
The room was pretty clean although the bathroom was quite dilapidated and my sons toy snake didnt look out of place in the tub. Decor was OK for a budget hotel ($109 for a double and a sofa bed). The suite had 2 TV's, a microwave and a refridgerator but to be perfectly honest it was a bit run down and needs a refurb.
There is a pool and hot tub. Both were clean and the pool water warm, quite a lot of chemicals though to irritate the eyes.
Breakfast was good although you need to get down early to avoid any toaster related congestion in a pretty small food service area.
In summary, we wont stay there again unless or until refurbushment.
C

title: “Very good hotel good service good rate”
text: I am very satisfy with all I received in this hotel.I feel very well with the staff members. The only i would suggest is to put a safe box ( for the passports) and a microwave

title: “More of a bar than hotel, informal service but great location 3+”
text:
We were a tad disappointed with our stay at the Royalton It was our first visit to NY and we came 15-18 December so sorry for late review!
On arrival on a Thursday night - the bar was booming and check in was difficult and slow, although easy to find. 
The room was nice and clean and high quality toiletries. Shame we did not get the bathtub or fireplace as this would have made it a much better stay.
Its a great place to explore NY though, Close to lots of major attractions.
We did Helicopter tour which was great, walked from Wall st to central park which was some going!!
Be warned after you walk down broadway after wall st, the area is not the best and we narrowly avoided a very nasty incident in McDonalds. (Basically a disagreement between 2 chaps - it was like a scene from boys in the hood!)
It was Christmas time as well which is magical. I took my wife for surprise 30th and she loved it. Horse and Carriage in Central park is magical, as was the shopping etc.
We found some nice Champagne bars, one was Campbells I think around 50thst.
5 Napkin burger was quite good as well for beer and burger!
We had a meal at the rockerfeller cafe and got seats by the ice rink The service we got was incredible and we had free drinks and best seat in the house. Do what I did and ring them to say you are celebrating a special occasion.
It was truly memorable and topped off with a proposal on the ice rink!
It was difficult to find a hotel not knowing NY. If you want contemporary with a good bar scene this is the place If you are looking for quiet and traditional, the Royalton is not the place!

title: “George Washington University Inn, Washington, D.C.”
text:
Small boutique hotel in the Foggy Bottom section of D.C. It's hard to find, tucked behind historic rowhuses with a small sign. Check for the address as you drive down the road, and you'll see the driveway into the small entry courtyard.
Room was spacious and bed comfortable. I made last minute reservation day of stay, and it wasn't in the system when we arrived because, the desk clerk said, someone has to enter the reservations manually - kind of antuquated - and it hadn't been done yet. But I had the confirmation print out, so all was fine. Desk staff was young and friendly. Only parking here is valet at $35! 
Hotel is located a few blocks from both George Washington University and the Kennedy Center, so very convenient for visting either. Lots of restaurants nearby too. We walked to Georgetown - about a 40 minute walk - through historic neighborhoods with interesting architecture. 
Buffet was only breakfast option available at their restaurant. Cost was $15.00 including tax and gratuity. Pretty basic with eggs, potatoes, sausage, bacon, fruit and cold cereals.

title: “Great Location, but Not Great at Maximum Capacity”
text:
This hotel is perfectly situated near Herald Square and the famous Macy's. Like most visitors, just pop into Macy's to check out the vastness. But if you've got a Macy's in your hometown, don't bother shopping. We went while the Flower Show was going on. Beautiful floral arrangements on the main floor, but so crowded! 
Now, for the HOTEL. The lobby is welcoming, and the staff is down-to-earth and friendly. Not snobby at all. The room was clean and tidy and although we only stayed two nights, our room was made up when expected. Here are the NEGATIVES regarding this hotel, which we felt were strong enough to skip it next time we're in town:
1. There are 20 floors and TWO elevators. There are no service elevators, so the cleaning crew has to use these same two elevators. How they got all the rooms cleaned on time was a mystery. Waiting for an elevator at peak times (breakfast from 6am-10am, dinner time when folks are heading back out, etc) took at least 10 minutes. There should be a rule - if you're on the 4th floor or below, no elevator for you!
2. Breakfast supply was low, but was replenished as best as possible. It was obvious this place was sold out this weekend. Milk for the cereal had to be replenished, fresh fruit replenished and empty within 10 minutes, hot foods - same situation. A great little hotel ends up feeling like a shoe that fit 10 years ago but no longer does when at max capacity. Almost no place to sit once you did fill your bowl/cup/plate with food/coffee.
3. Hot water in the showers was hard to come by. The room and bathroom were just fine. No complaints here at all. But on a rainy, windy, cold weekend in NYC, a hot shower is a relief we couldn't quite grasp because of the hot water issue.
4. Security - really, I never feel unsafe in the city. But I found it a little odd that access to the floors where the rooms are was totally open. In some hotels, you need your key to access these floors. Not here. Really, anyone can walk right into the lobby, hop on the elevator, and make their way up to your floor. Obviously, don't be stupid and open the door for strangers, but still - it feels VERY accessible for just about anyone. I thought, homeless folks that clean themselves up can walk in, use the restroom, grab hot coffee/tea/juice/ice water and be on their way. But like I said, this city is very safe these days. Just a thought.
If you're traveling to NYC during low visitor season (when is that?!), this hotel is probably a good enough option. Its proximity is great. Close to the subway, walking distance to Bryant Park/Times Square/Broadway/Rockefeller Center/Empire State Building. But if you're looking for a quaint getaway within the city, skip this one.

title: “Deep in the Heart of Big D”
text:
My husband and I enjoyed an overnight stay at the Le Meridien Dallas by the Galleria and were completely in awe of the hotel's charming atmosphere and hospitable staff. The hotel is right across the street from the Galleria and near all of the action.
The lobby is impressive and engaging with free wifi and Apple computers available to check your email, etc. There's even a full service restaurant.
Our room was quite comfy with a great bathroom and flat screen TV. While there's no view, there's plenty of room and you're so close to everything the Galleria area has to offer that you don't spend too much time in the room.
It's a real gem deep in the heart of Big D! We'll definitely visit again!

title: “Relieved!!!”
text: I was so relieved when we got to this hotel. After reading many negative reviews, I even called Pricline and questioned why they would offer such a nasty hotel and they informed me that if I was still disappointed upon arrival, to call them back. The hotel is very old and could use some updating, especially in the bathrooms, but overall it's in good shape. The staff was very friendly and helpful, the room was clean, and I did not see any rats, ants, or anything else. The location was great for us...a nice, pleasant walk to the Inner Harbor. The parking garage they put you in was just across the street, and well lit. We parked our car on Thursday and didn't have to move it until leaving on Sunday. I did see several people waiting long periods of time for valet parking so I wouldn't recommend that, but really there is no need to. We did not see any homeless people or beggars anywhere. I am a VERY PICKY traveler and I would stay at this hotel again.

title: “Very nice facilities, expensive parking”
text:
This hotel is in a great location, near Seaport Village and close to many San Diego attractions. Excellent breakfast and happy hour. Rooms are a very nice size. Beds are very comfortable. The staff was very friendly, but slow. Nice pool and hot tub.
I prefer to self park, and this was not an option at this hotel. I feel that the $29/day is excessive for parking. In addition, then you have to tip each time they bring your car around. The hotel itself is a good value for the money, but I think they make there money back on parking, internet and other fees.
I heard trains at night, but I didn't find them to be disturbing. (Maybe I'm used to it.) To me, it sounded like they were off in the distance, certalnly not anything that I lost any sleep over.

title: “Most helpful staff”
text: I stay in hotels for a few nights almost every week. the staff of the Downtown Sheraton in Phoenix is the most helpful and friendly hotel staff I have ever encountered. My room was exceptionally nice. The thermostat was in my control and it worked. The view was great. The restaurant menu was diverse, with some small finger-food stuff I like to eat. People at the bar looked like they were having fun. The business center was easy to use (not always the case.)

title: “Marriott hires the best employees”
text:
Brandon, the Valet man, explained the process to us clearly. A very polite young gentleman. Renee at the front desk gave us a Bay View room and recommended an excellent restaurant nearby for lunch. The next day an employee who has worked for Marriott for ten years held our luggage while we went touring. I forgot her name. We talked quite a bit.
Very comfortable room. Lots of walking around space.
We walked all over downtown and the Pioneer Square area.

title: “Large nice room, quiet stay”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for about a week while preparing for an exam. The location was close to the airport and the hotel was quiet. Nice large room with a king size (?) bed, large chair and desk, The room also had a small fridge in which I was able to stock up with cold drinks and snacks for long nights. The room was located on the back side of the hotel which most likely was a lot quieter then the front side, which borders International. 
Hotel staff was friendly, and the breakfast was your standard Best Western, good for a day or two and then you will want probably something different. The swimming pool, fitness area and hot tub was adequate, but nothing great. The computer room was a nice touch, as it allowed me to print off a few things, including my boarding passes. 
It is a little further down the road then most of the hotels directly outside the airport, but only by a couple minutes. I would definitely stay here again when traveling through Seattle.

title: “Great rate, great location, would stay again.”
text: We stayed on a weekend with a rate of $45 through Expedia. Hotel was clean, indoor hallways, and available luggage carts. Room was clean. Only two concerns were a spot of mold on bathroom ceiling and noisy a/c. Free wireless. Would stay again.

title: “What a gem!”
text: We booked this hotel via priceline. We got a great rate and wondered about the quality. We were greatly impressed! The staff were tremendous as we were traveling with 2 teenagers and a 10 year old. The hotel is within walking distance of Liberty Hall, and the Constitution Museum (which I highly recommend). I highly recommend this hotel for the service, value, and friendliness of the staff.

title: “Really really good stay”
text:
Stayed here from Sunday to Thursday.
Book a room through a conference happening at the hotel and got a cheaper rate (about 170$/night) With this cheaper rate, we also got free Wi-fi (otherwise contra-cost).
However, we got one of the okay rooms, with a regular tub and shower, whereas the ones not booked through the conference will probably give you a walk in shower and a nicer decorated room.
Had a double standard bed room with view of the marina.
Clean, spacious, mini fridge, safe in the room.
Loved their Aveda toiletries.
On the negative side there was the bath tub issue and parking.
 Parking was a ridiculous 42$/night for a guest!!! Wait, didn't I already pay a lot of money on the room itself??? And then they want you to tip the valet at well. Please!!!!
Parking for people eating at their restaurant: a reasonable 30$.
Would I stay here again? YES, for the same rate or cheaper.

title: “and i joked about staying in a crack den...”
text:
I thought I would go for the budget option as I only wanted a place to sleep. Arrived about 11pm, paid about $300 for 7 nights. spent 30 minutes in my room and went down to reception to ask for a refund. Choked out of $70 for that one night. 6am next day googling another place to stay at a much greater cost. tick the boxes for- cockroaches, bugs, the window fixed 4" open permanently, no heating, a solitary blanket on the bed, a dirty towel to use in the shared bathroom, which is meant to be cleaned no less than 3 times a day?? Congealed blood in the bathtub, sticky taps... enough of the bathroom. The door didn't shut tight and seriously doubted if it actually locked properly. There were holes in the walls which were like a mini West Side Inn for the cockroaches. Holes in the ceilings around the pipes, which were stuffed with mould ridden damp newspaper. Don't go barefoot, the carpet is alive. The plug socket was hanging out of the wall. There were a few people screaming along the corridor at about 3am. The bed linen will make you itch for a good few days.
The website is totally totally misleading. I complained to the manager the next day and he could not care less. Said it was my choice to leave and noted the window being stuck open. Shrugged his shoulders at the comparisons made between the website pictures and the actual reality. Not helpful or sympathetic at all.
check out the pictures, then compare to their website. surely there is some law in the U.S against improper descriptions of total holes?

title: “Fantastic location”
text: Great lcation right between downtown and dupont. 3 blocks to subway. Parking was $29 per night, valet only. Good deal if you pay under $120 or so, any more and there are better options. Great brunch at the beacon bar and grill.

title: “A few kinks that need to be worked out..”
text:
This hotel opened two months before my stay, so I expected that there still might be a few bugs that needed sorting out. I was correct, but I really think this hotel has the potential to be really good..
I booked my room using Starwood points. When I arrived to check in, they could not find my reservation and asked for my confirmation #. I stay in a lot of Starwood hotels on points, and have never been asked for the confirmation #. I had to go out to my car and get my laptop, and show the lady the email that they sent me, which included the conf. #. She still couldn't find it, and finally just made me a new reservation. That was fine, but I was wondering what would have happened if they didn't have vacancies- I'd probably have been out of luck. Another reviewer mentioned this happening- this is a pretty serious thing- they really need to take care of the people who have chosen the Starwood brand.
Lobby was pretty nice, they had a bar with cool modern seating and light fixtures. I didn't have a drink there, so I can't speak to how good the bar is. They also have a little "store" close to the check in desk. It has toiletries, snacks, drinks, sandwiches/wraps, salads, etc. Prices were a little high (as expected.) My wife and I split a wrap, and it was similar to what you'd get out of a convenience store cooler, only more expensive. 
The room was OK, but there were a few things that didn't really make sense. First off, the overall look: pretty cool. There was exposed brick and huge concrete columns, it looked like.... well... "a loft.." Even though we were on the 8th floor, views from the windows were so-so, and we only had one window in the main room. The bathroom is pretty cool looking, there was another window actually IN the shower that they put a see through shade over. (Hopefully, you can see out, but no one can see in.) Kind of weird to be standing naked showering by a full length window that you can see out of. 
So as I said before, there were a few details that didn't make sense. On one wall, there are two tables/desks separated by sort of a bench. Even though there were 2 identical desks, there was only one chair. When we ate our wrap from the lobby, we wanted to pull both chairs up and eat together on one table, but we couldn't. 
Closet- luckily, we were only in town for a couple of days. There isn't really a closet to hang suits/jackets or dresses. There was a little alcove that had a couple of hangers in it where you would have to hang your garment parallel with the wall (with the front or back facing you, instead of the shoulder like in a regular closet- I hope that makes sense.) Anyway, I guess you could have hung 1 or 2 garments, but not more. 
Amenities- they give you a fridge, which is awesome. Free WiFi. There is also a coffee maker, and you get complimentary coffee and bottled water. There was something that was missing- and I don't know if I've ever stayed in a hotel in my life that didn't have this. There were no glasses/plastic cups, and there was no ice bucket. The front desk told me that ice was available in the little "store." I don't know if they charge for it, or if you just pick it up. I saw some little "ice bucket size" bags in a freezer in the store. I didn't get a bag, but IF they charge for it, that's ridiculous. Even the Super 8 doesn't charge for ice. I inquired about getting glasses (I was planning on having a few cocktails in the room, but we ended up staying out so late that I didn't) and the guy told me that when the bar opened, they could get me some glasses.. Again, seems like that could be easily solved by putting some plastic cups in the room- I guess they feel like the bottled water takes care of that..
Parking was fine, it was $6 a day, and right on the hotel property (you didn't have to walk far.)
Shuttle- I was told when I checked in that there's a shuttle that would take you from the hotel to the West End. This was awesome- only problem was that in 2 days, I never saw it. Cab rides to the West End (tons of restaurants, bars, shopping, etc.) were $6-$8. Location of the hotel was great- really close to JFK museum, Dallas Holocaust Museum, West End, House of Blues (if you are in town for a concert/show as we were- it's about an $8 cab ride). 
All in all, there are some weird little details that should be fixed, but overall I thought the hotel was pretty cool, and has the potential to be really great.

title: “look for good internet deals on this classy hotel in the heart of Georgetown!”
text:
I was nervous about the Latham based on some reviews on this website, but my nervousness was replaced with relief when we entered the hotel!
The Latham is right in the heart of Georgetown, and excellent deals can be found on the internet. We paid less than $100 per night for a comfortably appointed room close to shopping, restaurants, bus lines, and the waterfront.
There were a few slight snags. Somehow, they checked us into the wrong room at first, which was smallish with one bed instead of the two I'd requested. We decided just to stick with it, but later that night, when we were told of the mix-up, we decided to switch into the room meant for us which was double the size with two beds. The room was hotter, but right next to the pool. 
The beds are reallllly comfortable, the decor is nice enough; only the bathroom area could use some updating. We saw a few unoffensive bugs, probably because of the heat and the proximity to the pool. We were impressed with the professionalism of the staff, the lovely lobby, and the location, and while the outdoor pool is tiny, it is a welcome extra on a 100 degree day.
If you can get a good price, I would highly recommend the Latham.

title: “Business trip”
text: Went here for a conference. It was great for the business trip, but I wouldn't pay to stay here out of my own pocket. The view was pretty, and it's close to the convention center and down town. Walked down to searsucker (restaurant) and syrah wine parlor (bar). The bar was great, getting in is half the fun.

title: “Nice little hotel - emphasis on “little””
text:
The Topaz is located on a beautiful and quiet (for DC) side street near Dupont Circle. The hotel definitely has its pluses and minuses, and while the rooms are lovely and the staff are excellent, you should carefully consider your travel style and the purpose of your trip before you choose this hotel.
If you’re traveling here for business or just want a quiet place to hang your hat, the location is good and the rooms are great - the lighting is good, the desks are large, and the wireless internet is free if you are a Kimpton points member. The beds are very comfortable. The hotel is also quiet – very well soundproofed considering the basement is a club and the first floor primarily consists of the Topaz bar. I was on the fourth floor and hear almost no noise outside my room. The bathroom has great lighting (although the makeup mirror being bolted into the wall only 3 feet off the floor was odd) and is very comfortable to use. There is a tiny room with one computer and printer that is the “business center", which is easy to use but has high rates for printing. You are very close to the Dupont Circle metro stop, which is convenient.
However, this is not the hotel for you if you plan on spending a lot of time in the room or if you want a vibrant lobby or bar scene. The TV has very few channels, there is only a kettle and some tea bags (no coffeemaker) and the minibar, while reasonably priced, contains only snacks and drinks. The hotel has no restaurant, and while room service is available for breakfast, dinner, and late night, lunch isn’t available here. I also was not happy with the quality of the room service breakfast that I ordered. There is no spa/pool, though the hotel provided an access card for the YMCA across the street during my stay. The lobby is indeed miniscule and the first floor bar very tiny. The hotel almost feels more like a bed-and-breakfast in that sense - the rooms are nice, but there is very little else in the way of energy, atmosphere, or amenities. If you want more people and energy around, the Kimpton hotel Palomar is only a couple of blocks away.
The staff are wonderful and the service is impeccable, so I have no complaints there. They took very good care of me in terms of ordering cabs, room service, and the like. They called my room the night before I checked out to bring me up some snacks and ask about whether I needed a wakeup call or a cab for the next morning. They also refunded the cost of my room service breakfast when I mentioned it at checkout. While I enjoyed my stay there, I like for a hotel to be larger and more vibrant than this one was, so I will most likely choose the Palomar on my next visit. 
I do want to correct a complaint by a previous reviewer - the front doors are electronically locked at all times, but not for security. The hotel is so small that they only have one set of doors, and for the purposes of allowing wheelchairs in, they modified those doors to be ones that open outwards electronically, and you just have to hit the wheelchair access button on your way in.

title: “Not Impressed”
text:
The hotel looked grand from the outside and so did the reception area, but when we entered our room we were very disappointed. It was very small and the decor was very old and depressing. Don't get me wrong it was clean and we had a decent TV and a fridge, but the room was very dated. My husband carefully selected this hotel out of many he looked at for my 30th birthday and it wasn't in the cheap range. The promised Manhattan view was out of a very dirty window.
The lock on our door was loose and the staff all looked depressed. They didn't crack a smile or ask us if we enjoyed our stay when we checked out.
We really expected much more from a so clled 'famous' establishment that has appeared in various movies.
There was a world leader conference on that weekend and we think maybe the upper crust were allocated the nicer rooms. We also had a smoking room, which I thought may have played a part also. Never the less - my hubby paid for the room our of his own hard earned cash (unlike the world leaders) and just because I smoke doesn't mean I deserve a depressing room.
My husband wanted to complain, but I wouldnt let him - I wish I had let him now when I think back. Lesson learned.

title: “Not worth the price”
text:
This was a last minute arrangement since our San Francisco trip was cancelled. My husband booked this hotel the morning we left the house so we didn't have a chance to do much of a research.
Location..
Next to the Marina. If you're looking into launch your boat or anything that requires boating, this might be your perfect place. Otherwise, it is close to Sea World, it does offer shuttles from hotel to Sea World three times in the morning and three times in the afternoon. Departure times are 9:30, 11:30, and 12:30, returning time 4:30, 5:30 and 6:30 (could be a bit off since I'm working off of memory at the moment). Since we have smaller children we prefer not to take the shuttle for the flexibility, so on top of the parking we're paying at the hotel, we're also paying for the amusement park parking. Walking is 15 mins or so, which also doesn't work well with younger children.
There are kayak and bikes for rental, but scenery is much limited. Our kids looked at the boats for about 2 minutes and got bored with it. There aren't any shops to browse.
Hotel room:
We paid the $40 upgrade to get the Marina view room. Let me describe the buildings first. It reminds you of those motels you have a open walk way and everyone's windows are facing the walk way. If you don't open up the shutter blinds the room would be quite dark, but once you do, you're pretty much open to the entire building guests that walks by.. trust me, everyone walks by just couldn't resist to take a look into your room. Since the walkway is open to the parking right infront of the building, you hear people talking in the parking lot on top of the activities in the hallway. Lucky us happens to have some guests yelling from parking lot to building 1am in the morning.
Our room does have marina view... but you have to leave the blinds open to see through the hallway to see it, which was total waste to us. I do noticed a newer building somewhere on premise, but I do not even want to know how much more it would cost us. Room is quite cramped. Two beds fills up the whole room, and they managed to squeezed a tv and seating into it which makes it impossible to move around with the 4 of us. My side of the bed which is close to the window barely allows me to stand up and walk sideways, and I'm a skinny person. Windows shakes when our neighbors slams the doors or stomps in the hallway. Bedding is firm, and pillows are small and fillings aren't fluffy anymore. Room seems pretty clean, our feet stayed clean even though we're walking barefeet.
I've stayed around San Diego area numerous times. This is the first place I'm incredibly disappointed with and will not return. It truely made me feel like I'm staying in a motel 6. We paid $156 plus $10 plus parking which we could've paid for a larger, more recognized hotel that we stayed in before.

title: “Location, location, location. Nostalgia, nostalgia, nostalgia.”
text:
This motel was exactly where we needed to be so we gave it a try. It is like an aging Hollywood beauty queens, past its prime and relying on makeup.
The hotel is a throwback to a couple of decades ago. We had read other TripAdvisor reviews an much of what we read was accuate.
1. The hotel is aged, but it appears to have been repainted and remodeled a bit.
2. The ceiling creak when someone above you is walking around, not a huge problem as our upstairs neighbors were pretty quiet and next time we'd ask for a thrid floor room.
3. No high tech, high speed computerized check in. They use an old fashioned "sign in" process and run the credit card through. Not an issue.
4. Room was very basic, but was clean and the remodeled bathroom was better than some newer, fancier hotels we've been to.
5. No hot coffee in the room, but a hot tea, coffee and cocoa vending machine in the lobby.
6. Rooms use a real key, haven't seen one of those in a while.
7. Old tube TV, but lots of channel.
8. Air conditioning was fairly modern but noisy.
It was fine, in the perfect spot, and the price was right.

title: “Hidden gem in a quieter part of NYC”
text:
I chose the HGI TriBeCa for a business trip to NYC because it was conveniently two blocks from my client. When I checked in, I was pleasantly surprised to find that I (a HHonors Diamond) had been upgraded to the penthouse suite. This was a two room suite on the top floor. It had very nice furnishings with a poster bed and and an entertainment center with a large flat-screen TV and full (and I mean full) cable with foreign language and HD channels. Of course it had the HGI fridge and microwave as in all HGI rooms.
The front desk and bell staff were accomodating and friendly. I had no problems storing my luggage on my last day until my car service arrived.
Breakfast was included with my rate and the connected restaurant offered a typical buffett with made-to-order eggs/omelettes. 
The neighborhood is much lower key than Midtown. There is a subway entrance literally right outside the door (A,C, E lines, if I recall correctly) for venturing to the rest of NYC. As a tourist, this property would probably not be my first choice, all else being equal, but if you need to be in/near the SoHo/TriBeCa/Village area, this property is highly recommended.

title: “Great hotel in superb location!”
text: Having read all the Tripadvisor reviews for the Chancellor Hotel, my wife and I booked 4 nights for our first ever stay in San Francisco. Having read many good things and being particularly impressed with General manager Wes Tyler's responses on this site, I am pleased to say that the hotel lived up to all our expectations. We had a friendly welcome upon check-in by Steve, the guy who dealt with us and the process was quick and very efficient. He also gave us a map and told us to come to reception with any queries. I had made a request to Kevin Vossen prior to travel for one of their reburbished rooms on a high floor with a good view of Union Square and they were able to fulfil this request so thanks very much Kevin!! Brilliant view of Union Square day and night and the windows did a great job of blocking the noise out. The room was nicely decorated and clean. It was more than big enough for our needs and the bed was very comfy! Bathroom was clean and maybe a little small for some but we were happy with it. Having complimentary coffee and tea available (along with the cookies) is a really great idea and gives the guests so much freedom and free use of their computer for internet access is an added bonus. One of the best things about the hotel must be it's location to Union Square, the San Francisco centre and everything else. It's fantastic! We could spend all day sight seeing and then spend the evening shopping with it being so easily accessible! Union Square is also close to all the main transportation routes so is ideal as a base. We were originally going to stay on Fisherman's Wharf but upon visiting it are very glad that we didn't. Too touristy for our liking and a bit further out. Our recommendation is stay around the Union Square area, you won't regret it! So, to get back to it, we throughly enjoyed our trip to San Francisco and our stay at the Chancellor Hotel. San Francisco as a city is really great and our stay was made all the more better with us staying at the Chancellor Hotel. Well done Wes and co. keep up the good work! We may not be heading back to SF for a while yet but we hope that when we next return, the hotel will still be keeping up it's high standards and we'll be staying there once again! One last thing! A nice and thoughtful touch is to have an umbrella in the room closet for us to use - came in handy on our last full day when it absolutely rained all day!!!

title: “Totally Terrific Experience!!!”
text:
From the moment we checked and until we left, this hotel made us feel welcome, comfortable, cared for and as if we were long-time gracious friends. It started with the Desk Clerk who checked us in and continued until the Bell Captain hailed a cab for us at departure.
Our room was spacious. It provided a most comfortable bed as well as ample room to read and relax. The wet bar, microwave and refrigerator enabled us to snack in the room and have a glass of chilled wine before dinner. We were fortunate to have a room with a landscaped terrace.
The roof-top club, which provided a Continental Breakfast daily was convenient and casual. Full concierge services were also available there as well as in the lobby. Knowledgeable staff provide terrific recommendations and guidence.
Not to be forgotten, the hotel is convenient to theaters and to all that the Union Square area offers.
The restaurant, which is adjacent to, but not part of the hotel was excellent. We enjoyed two first rate meals that, for San Francisco, were well priced. Their bar had an almost "Cheers-like" atmosphere. Very pleasant --- and they mixed an outstanding drink.
We'll say it again . . . our stay at the Donatello provided us with a Totally Terrific Experience!!!

title: “Nice view”
text: Nice view on Detroit downtown. The room is ok the service are very good. The monorail are just in front of the hotel and you are at 10 minutes of the joe-louis arena, comerica stadium and the ford stadium!

title: “If Apple married IKEA, this would be their baby!”
text: Very hip, laid back, high tech (iPads on the walls for you to use and a 40" interactive map) WiFi throughout the hotel and my experience was great reception (room 201). Yes, very small rooms but if you are okay with that (which I was) they are very comfortable and cozy. Beds are great, sink in your room, bathrooms (I shared and there is 4 on each floor and impeccably clean ) were NEVER an issue, in fact I never encountered anyone in the hallways and the hotel was booked. I had the 1 bed and everything I needed was within reach (seriously) and kinda nice. I was here for 4 days (alone) and there was plenty of room and nooks/crannies for my stuff. I felt safe the entire time, sat in the lobby with drinks, and worked. Very convenient to everywhere via the Greenline and nice little pubs/bars/restaurants within 1/4 block. I would totally return here and for sure check out Pod 39 (?) next time as thats a cool NYC location as well.

title: “Would come back.”
text:
We picked this hotel primarily for the location and the Sea World & Zoo ticket deal was also attractive.
Having just stayed in a very large suite in Las Vegas, I have to say the room felt very small. There were 2 beds, I would say doubles rather than Queens. There was very little drawer space to put our clothes and overall it felt very pokey.
On the plus side the room was clean and the location was ideal, just minutes from Seaworld and the zoo. dont agree with the fairly high parking charge though. Would come back.

title: “excellent, only good things to say”
text: We stayed at this hotel for 8 nights December 30th through January 7th. There were 5 of us (2 adults 3 kids) the first 2 nights we were in a king bed suite as all the 2 beds were gone. We got a rollaway bed for the 2nd night. On the day we moved to the 2 bedroom suite the staff told us to just pack up our stuff and leave it all in the room and they would transfer it over for us. We went out for the day and the room was ready with all our stuff in when we returned including all the stuff from the fridge and freezer and the rollaway bed. There was no charge for the rollaway during the entire stay. The suites are spacious, the maid service excellent. We sat out each morning in the courtyard to eat breakfast. Its 5 minutes from the airport so you hear the planes going over when you are o/s but no noise from them in the rooms. Breakfast was more than adequate, always eggs and some kind of meat, waffles, oatmeal, yogurt, fresh fruit, cinammon buns and muffins, tea, coffee, juice. Dinner 4 nights a week the menu is posted on the fridge in your room was varied and always they were filling up when things got low. It saved us a ton of money that we could then spend on trips. Beer and wine were complimentary. We used the barbecues in the courtyard one night, the pool was great and so was the hot tub. Staff were extremely friendly and i had no complaints about anything. Used the business centre to check emails and would definitely stay here again. The only tip i would say is if you arrive late by plane and want a transfer you need to use a regular call box or cell phone and call the hotel using the local number to arrange for pick up. It stops doing regular trips around 11.

title: “This hotel has had its day! ”
text: We stayed here for the last 2 nights and having been on a driving holiday in California and stayed at a range of different hotels and standards did have any specific expectations. On arrival the lobby and everything on that floor looked beautiful all the original features have been preserved but on arrival at our room this grandness disappeared and we were in the most basic room we had stayed in so (and not the cheapest price). The room was noisy, hair dyer didn't work, the cost for wifi was very high considering everywhere else we stayed was free they even charge $10 a day for you to use a fridge! The bar prices are also very high at $4 for a small Club Soda!! The location if you are looking to visit all the sights in LA is also pretty poor! All in all I would say don't stay here!

title: “GREAT TIME.. THANKS!”
text:
I love this hotel and this location. Great friendly staff... in a perfect location. EVEN though a fire interrupted our stay. The whole weekend was perfect. We used the location for biking, walking and enjoyed the people we met along the way.
 I plan on going back as soon as possible!

title: “Not Bad -Needs Updating”
text:
We just got back from a one week stay at the Catamaran. The loaction is good, grounds are very well maintained but the rooms are in need of considerable updating. We booked a studio as we wanted a kitchen with appliances in order to prepare breakfasts and some lunches. The original room they provided was nothing like the picture we saw on their web site (it was much smaller with no sitting area and pull out sofa) so we asked for a room change. The staff was very accomodating and promptly gave us a larger room. The room itself was dated but relatively clean (although there was some mold in the bathtub). The kitchen appliances are at least 20 years old and are not in the greatest condition. This is a good family spot but I would not recommend this hotel for a romantic getaway. To be fair, this is a 3 star hotel and not the Del Coronado, but unless you get a discounted price off of their posted rates, you will be overpaying for what you get. Overall ratings:
Staff: A
Accomodations: C-
Cleanliness (rooms): C-
Beach Area: A

title: “Fantastic hotel”
text: Definitely would stay here again. We arrived very late at night. Room was beautiful and clean. They had our Wyndham By Request amenity waiting (wine & cheese), just what we needed after a long day/flight. Friendly and accommodating staff.

title: “great perks!!”
text: I stayed at this hotel with three children in a large room with two queen beds. It was clean, comfortable, and in the heart of the river walk. The best thing about this hotel is happy hour every night with three drinks and snacks, and the free breakfast, with real food. I was very pleased with the rate, and there is a steakhouse right on the riverwalk that is below the hotel. I didnt know what to expect but I will use drury inn again.

title: “Not quite the boutique experience”
text:
I was fairly disappointed with this hotel. I travel frequently to NY and have stayed in all different type of hotels from boutique to large chain in the city and I haven't been this disappointed in a hotel in quite a long time.
First the positive:
1. Location. It is steps away from Grand Central, and better yet, to the express bus stops to all three NYC airports, with buses that run every 30 minutes from 4 am to 1 am or so. No need for an expensive cab or subway to train transfers. I used the bus ($13) to make a Newark airport flight - left at 3:15 and arrived at 4:20.
2. Size of Room. I booked an executive King and got a rate of $349. Being mid-October, this was about one of the best rates I could get for an upgraded room at a decent hotel. It was on the 15th floor and was definitely commodious. There was no view, but I was high enough to get 
some view of the sky. The windows opened, which was a plus.
3. Internet. Complementary laptop access through ethernet. There was a wireless network, but I could not get a network address assigned -- I have a brand spanking new PC and never have any problems elsewhere, so I suspect there is something wrong with the wireless network. I didn't bother calling down, since I was fine with the ethernet cable.
Now the partly negative.
1. Staff. I had read the recent reviews about the staff and I usually read these with some level of cynicism, as I have witnessed my share of rude and unreasonable customer scenes. 
But I think there may be some truth to the criticisms I have read here. My experience checking in was fairly negative. The front desk person was not rude, but he certainly was not friendly or welcoming. I guess I don't expect the staff to be subservient or ingratiating, but a "Good Morning, Welcome to the Dylan Hotel!" and a smile might have been nice. I received neither. When I went up to the desk and told them I was checking in, all I got was a cold, sighing, "What is your name?" "I'll need your VISA card." The desk person just seemed bored and aloof, and not particularly happy about his job. Bad way to start the stay. 
I should say that it was only the front desk person on that Saturday morning that behaved that way. The other times I had dealings at the front desk, it was decent. The bellhops, doormen and maids were wonderful, however.
2. Common Areas. Having stayed at the Hudson and even the smaller hotel in the same group as the Dylan, the Time, I was disappointed with the common areas. The lobby area is small and nicely furnished, but the waiting area directly accross the reception desk is small, basically a couple couches. There's no lounge area or bar or library or places to hang out that you would normally find in a boutique hotel. In fact the Dylan had far less amenities in that way than even a high-quality chain hotel. Basically, the Dylan reminded me more of a dormitory than a boutique hotel. The photos on the websites really make the hotel look far more "hip" and modern than it really is.
3. Room. Wasnt as nicely furnished as it appeared in the photos. The room I had was on the interior light well. Though the windows opened to let fresh air in, there was a huge ventilation fan going the whole time. Furnishings okay, big King bed was comfortable.
4. Heating/AirConditioning. I was there in mid October. The weather was in the mid 70s. I arrived to a room that had the heat going. I tried to get the air conditioner to work, but was told by the desk that their HVAC could only do heat or aircon, and that they had already converted it to heat for the season. Therefore, the only thing to do was to turn off the unit. I had to open the windows and prop open the door to cool off the room. It wasn't so bad, but I feel sorry for the person who is there during an unseasonal cold snap or heat wave! 
***
Overall, I would say that if you can get a cheap rate for this place, its probably a good value. It was not worth the $350 what I paid. If location is key and you want the small hotel experience , the Library Hotel is up the street from the Dylan. I have stayed at the Library before, and it has smaller rooms, but being on the corner, better chance for views, as well as a great lounge areas and a well-trained service-oriented staff. Or if you don't care about boutique and don't mind big, the Grand Hyatt at Grand Central, which is right next to (on top of?) the terminal is a fine high-quality choice.

title: “So-so”
text: Missing some standard room amenities like a rack to hang clothes, blow dryer, iron, mini fridge. Although, I did ask for a blow dryer and iron at the front desk and they were sent right away. Shower head was too high pressure, it hurt!

title: “Fantastic hotel with a lot of style in a great location”
text: Stayed at the Helix for a few days in July with my family (including our dog). Great location, easy walk to everywhere downtown. Easy check-in and check-out with very friendly and competant staff. Love the hotel decor and vibe. Will definitly go back next time we visit DC.

title: “Excellent hotel and great location”
text:
We stayed here 2 nights in Jan 2012 while visiting relatives in DC. The location is excellent, it is very close to the metro and was a quick 1/2 hour trip from Dulles airport. It is also only about 2km from the memorials so we spent a half day walking to the Lincoln Memorial and on to the Smithsonian museums.
The rooms themselves are excellent. We used points for the stay and they gave us a top floor double which was huge and extremely comfortable. It is very modern and clean, and the beds are extremely comfortable. To do provide a couple of computers in the business centre including a printer. They also provide 1 hour free wifi each day in the reception area.

title: “PERFECT. PERFECT...... PERFECT!!!”
text: Absaloutley loved this hotel, great location! I was a bit nervous as never been to America before but the staff at Candlewood Suites were so helpfull and really nice! Very understanding and accomodating to any request! only 7 minute walk from Times Square, in same street there is Starbucks and everything you need in a 2 minute walk! Room was great, amazing Lazy Boy chair and the bed was SOOO COMFY!!! you get free cookies and they have a free gym and when you leave to go home they hold on to your bags all day and dont make you feel pressured to tip or anything like that! Great hotel and would recommend anyone to go there, if your thinking about going, just book it, you wont regret it! ALMOST FORGOT, Free Wireless internet in the rooms!! WOW!!!! i was doing face time with my family back in england on my iphone 4 for free!

title: “very economical and fit for purpose”
text: it is near to majority of LA locations. Convenient stay for the price you pay. Parking is free, which can save you around 15 - 20 USD. per day.The breakfast is ok as well. Fit for purpose budget hotel.

title: “A truly wonderful time at The Time”
text: Just discovered this really GREAT hotel in midtown Manhattan on my recent trip to see friends. Wonderful and friendly staff, very cool and hip bar Inc Lounge and very good food - they have the restaurant Serafina in their hotel - fab Pizzas. From the doormen (I think it was Eddie and Gilbert) to the concierge and the front desk folks - I was made to feel so welcome. If you like theater (like I do) you cannot find a more perfect area as I walked to all the shows I saw. I can only recommend this hotel on a very positive and very high level. I will be back at the end of this year!!

title: “Great hotel to enjoy SF without breaking the bank”
text: I was really pleased with this hotel. The staff was very friendly and polite. I don't know why anyone would think different. One of them even helped me to use the coke machine. Really nice people. The room was in immaculate condition with an old time feel to it but like new appearance. There is a large safe in the closet that so big I could put my laptop in it when I left the room. The elevator has a small door but it is big inside, I guess due to the time period of the building. All in all I was very satisfied and I recommend the Baldwin to anyone.

title: “Courteous staff- great central location.”
text: It had been several years since we stayed in Seattle. I knew we wanted to be in the downtown area- so I looked up DT hotels on line. Hotel Monaco was a four star hotel that came up along with several others-a bit out of our price range, but in looking at their web-site- they offered a better rate for two days. It was perfect for us. The hotel was beautiful- the staff were very courteous and most helpful. They had great suggestions for resturants and places to visit. The rooms were spacious and super clean. Great showers. We will definitely be back!

title: “Ideal location!”
text: We booked during a special and were very pleased. Location was perfect; shopping, food, access to trains, buses, cabs, cable cars. Eay ride to Fishermans Wharf. Close to BART. Small rooms, but we just needed it for sleeping and showering. Neat and tidy. Took a gamble on a boutique hotel over a name brand and very happy we did!

title: “Pretty Run Down”
text: The location is great here, but the overall hotel is run down and dirty. Our room had a thin layer of dust on the dresser and hair on the shower wall. The hallways have seen better days as well.

title: “Best service of all time and I know of what I speak!!”
text: I've been in the meeting/incentive industry for over 20 years and some years, can spend over 200 nights in hotels, all over the world. But the best service I've ever received, ever, was the little Westin Park Central in Dallas. This was in the early 00's but I've never forgotten the amazing staff at that hotel, especially in the Banquet Department. Those men and women under the leadership of the best of the best, Mike Tej, surpassed every banquet department I've ever worked with, before and since. Extremely attentive to every detail, personal attention to myself and my staff, but best of all, the same amazing attention to my attendees. Which, to me, is the most important of all. A little hotel in the middle of what I call The Corporate Jungle of Dallas, it's probably overlooked by anyone other than business travellers and the meeting industry, and that's a shame. I love that hotel and that banquet staff!!!

title: “Find somewhere else!!!”
text: My in-laws stayed here and I wish they hadn't wasted their money. They put them in a room right next to the pool that was getting resurfaced so every morning they awoke to construction equipment and workers yelling. The room was overrun with crickets and when we asked for maintenance to spray they said they only do outside. The customary workout room is not provided so you better have a gym membership and drive 6 miles if you want to workout. Your guests might as well take a cab to visit you because of very limited parking. The garbage disposal reeked with sewage stench. This place and the staff were very disappointing. Avoid this place at all costs!!!

title: “Staycation”
text: My girlfriend and I stayed here for one night to celebrate a delayed valentines. After having dinner and bar hopping throughout fenuille hall we came back to the room to crash. The location could not have been better and though our stay was short, the little touches like our towels folded into elephants and warm welcoming receptionist made us feel like we were valued regulars. This cozy nook is our new secret staycation and will be seeing more of us shortly.

title: “Comfortable and central”
text:
We were struck by the personal welcome by members of staff who were keen to help. Although we were attending a conference in the hotel, the central position meant that we were able to explore Philadelphia. The proximity to the Reading Terminal Market was certainly a bonus, especially for a picnic lunch between sessions. The bed was extremely comfortable and the room quiet. There were great views over Philly! 
We would certainly stay again.

title: “Great location - Very Expensive”
text:
Room wise there is nothing spectacular about this hotel. Rooms are actually small. The beds are comfortable, the rooms nicely appointed albeit the size. Internet is not free and I had some small problems with the bathroom which I wouldn't expect paying $250 a night. Parking at the hotel is outrageous, and if you park there during a conference it takes forever to get your car. There is a restaurant and bar at the hotel and they ar ok, but once again very expensive! $17 dollars for breakfast, and the average price for a drink is $10. 
You cannot however beat the location of this property. If you are looking for a spot that is a short walk to the White House, Washington Monument etc. this is the spot. Most other attractions are a short taxi ride.
Good property but expensive.

title: “Very convenient”
text:
We were here for four nights over Labor Day weekend 2011 for a little family vacation - I requested a king bed and when I asked for two queens instead upon check-in, they were very accommodating. Our room was great - clean and spacious and serviced quickly. Plenty of towels, pillows, etc. Even with the jazz festival nearby, our room was dark and quiet enough for some good sleep. 
As other reviews have noted, the showerhead was cool but water pressure was somewhat poor. We did not make use of the fitness room but it was probably the nicest hotel gym I have seen. The location was great, we had a CityPass for the various museums and we walked to all of them except the Museum of Science and Industry, we walked to Willis Tower, etc. Lots of nearby restaurants. All in all, a very nice hotel and I'd be happy to return someday soon!

title: “Mediocre Marriott”
text: This hotel was not the quality expected. We registered a complaint about security, and it was brushed off with a sincere apology. While waiting to check out, another guest had a complaint, and it was brushed off again with a sincere apology...but no action.

title: “Excellent amenities for airport location”
text:
I picked this location because I needed to catch an early flight the next morning. It is easy access to rental car return and terminal. Note that it is 5-10 min drive and not across from airport like some cities. Within walking distance of several other similar hotels, gas station/convenience store and restaurants.
Hotel was very new, clean and bright. Rooms were small but packed with amenities - kitchenette, sofa, flat screen, desk, large bed and bathroom. Wi-fi is free in the room. Free dinner and breakfast in a nice lounge area. Hotel is situated in an open prairie which provided for an amazing sunrise upon departure. Construction is underway nearby but wasn't a distraction during my visit.

title: “Central Location”
text:
I chose this hotel after viewing reviews on Trip Advisor and was not disappointed. The location is perfect for many reasons but mainly because it is across the road from the famous Prudential centre and more importantly just a few steps away from the "T" which is the Boston Underground. We bought a 7 day ticket giving us unlimited travel by T or bus for 18 dollars each. I mention this also because Carlos left his station at the hotel and came to the underground with us to help us purchase these tickets. 
Our room was not large but more than adequate. It had two double beds, large TV and multiple channels. We were delighted to see we had a coffee maker, iron,and hair dryer. Ice is available from an ice maker on every floor. Wine glasses and champagne flutes along with ice bucket are in a cupboard. Bed was very comfortable and large windows gave a lovely bright room throughout the day. 
The desk staff, concierge, bellhop, and door staff were more than helpful. In fact I have to mention Nuala, Carlos and Norman as particularily helpful and going out of their way to assist us.We only had one meal in their restaurant Brassiere Jo. Menu and food was excellent and pricing was similar to other places we ate. My only moan would be the price of drink. They only serve draught beer in a small glass which cost 8 dollars. My wife had two cocktails and i had two small draught beers ( 1 pint ) so our drink cost 36 dollars. I would normally have two pints of beer at night on holidays. we rarely drink while at home. This would not deter me from staying at this hotel again. For some reason the lifts were always available and we never had to stand waiting for one.

title: “Good hotel”
text:
I stayed here for a conference and overall, was impressed with the hotel. The rooms were small but clean. It is an old hotel (remodeled) and has that old hotel room smell - a bit musty. The hotel had a very nice fitness center. Business center only had 2 computers but adequate. The location was across from the Waldorf and next to the W. 
The one thing I must say is that the rooms were extremely hot. I was there during one of the coldest day in NYC history and had to open the window and turn on the a/c! Overall it was a nice hotel.

title: “bad stay”
text: when making reservations ask for bottom floor cause of handicap needed 2 beds when we arrived no 2 beds on first floor then when to take shower closed bathroom door dirty towels on back of door next day when we came back room smelled like mold next nite when we came back no towels or soap up stairs wow dont think my family or i will stay at any more wyndhams any more we you go away with family you dont need to put up with this when you are on a family vacation

title: “Surprisingly nice, friendly staff -- good value”
text:
We stayed here one night in November 2008. We chose to stay at this particular property because they were offering 5000 Priority Club points as a bonus.
The hotel is relatively new, or at least recently updated. Furniture, carpets, etc. were all in very good shape. The rooms are pretty large; I would suggest you ask for 1 king or 1 queen bed to take advantage of the additional space since all rooms are sized the same. A 2 bed layout will obviously take up more room than a 1 bed will; in the extra space you get a nice comfy chair and ottoman for relaxing.
The location of the hotel isn't the greatest in terms of being easily walkable to much to do, as it's a slightly industrial area -- although at the corner of Monterey & Curtner a new shopping center has been built with a few fast food options for dining. 
The beds are very comfortable, towels are large and fluffy, and we love the cinnamon-scented toiletries.
The one downside is that the hotel is set up motel style, with all rooms opening up to the parking lot. This means you hear lots of cars being locked/unlocked electronically in the wee hours when you're trying to sleep.
Staff was very friendly, check-in and check-out was efficient. We got to breakfast a bit late, and the room was crowded with families with children. We managed to snag a couple of cinnamon rolls though. Eggs were awful.
We'd stay here again, especially if they were offering the bonus points deal!

title: “House keeping and maintenance”
text: The clean lobby and restaurant did not reflect the condition of the suite. The first problem was the Air ducts were caked with grease and dirt causing my wife copd. To act up. They took the vents to maintenance and reinstalled them the next day, leaving open holes all over the suite overnight. The grease in the kitchen, food scraps,and refrigerator had to be cleaned. The carpeting was filthy and there was dirt accumulation behind and under all the furniture. Needless to say we moved to another hotel. The employees were polite but complained of being under staffed in house keeping. We will never stay there again, even though we make numerous trips to md anderson cancer clinic. The Rolando family

title: “W Hotel Lakeshore Terrible”
text: checked into the W lakeshore on thurs. nov. 6th...I have always been a very big fan of W Hotels, unfortunetly, this W Hotel along with the two before this, were absolutely horrible...I had reserved a superior king room for three nights at the W Lakeshore. The lobby was nice, but it ended there...when we exited our cab the attendants stood there as we lifted all of our bags out of the cab by ourselves and opened the door to the hotel as they stood and talked to each other...the rooms are incredibly small, they are run down, dirty, smell, and are very loud...for the amount of money they charge it should be a crime. It is basically a holiday inn express that has been painted with odd colors and had a large W slapped on it...on friday morning I spoke with a manager who allowed us to check out two days earlier because of all the problems...we switched to the Penisula Hotel (what an amazing hotel, i'm here right now)...Overall, W Hotels have gone way downhill, the lakeshore is a total rip off and so small you can't get out of your own way...they charge a gratuity on the mini bar of 20% (i have never seen that before, nor did a waitress pop out of my minibar to serve me a drink). The rooms are disgusting, they smell and are very loud...I really did love W Hotels, I don't know what has happened, but spend your money elsewhere, this hotel is expensive and you don't receive anything but dirty, smelly, loud rooms with an extremely rude person at the WHENEVER WHATEVER desk...I truly would not recommend this hotel. Thanks to the manager of the hotel for allowing us to leave after being there only 10 hours...that was the best part...for a few dollars more you can stay in hotels that are 50 times better...even a few dollars less you could probably get more...shame on W Hotels for ripping people off like that. I will never stay at a W Hotel again...Whatever happened when Starwood bought them has been a HUGE mistake...

title: “CAN'T IMAGINE STAYING ANYWHERE ELSE!”
text:
Just got back from a wonderful Christmas in NYC - it was an awesome trip! 
We stayed at the Eastgate Tower again. This was the fourth time we have stayed there and I simply can't imagine wanting to stay anywhere else in NYC. Travelling with two teenagers, the two-bedroom, two-bathroom suites (apartments) are just perfect. Loads of space, a huge sitting/dining room and a fully fitted kitchen where we could throw together breakfasts and snacks - essential for a family like us with two teenage sons that seem to need to eat almost constantly.......
Great staff all round - reception, doorman and cleaners. OK the decor of the corridors and apartments needs freshening up and the furnishings are not plush but in my honest opinion, you get more than value for money with the spaciousness (is that even a word?) of the apartments.
We can't wait to go back.

title: “Overpriced and dissapointed”
text:
We recently stayed in the Hilton and as the name and reputation would suggest we treated ourselves.
