Unfortunately we should not have bothered, the foyer was very impressive and the staff friendly but the room was a real let down. I found the hotel overpriced and the accomodation was no better than your average $100 hotel, the bathroom needed replacing, the water came out yellow at first and really smelt!
We left early in the morning as we had to catch a train to Vancouver B.C so did not have time to complain, but thought this would be a good way of letting people know not to stay here.

title: “Extremely clean and friendly.”
text:
7/21/2011
Front desk checkin person Justin was a pleasure. Very pleasant and answered questions with a great attitude. My room was on one of the club floors, and allthough very small, it was extremely clean and adequate. The first thing i generally check when going to a hotel is the bathroom. The tub had these disgusting big paint flaking spots on them. It was a huge turn-off. Other than that the room was great. And extremely clean. I'm a bit of a nut when it comes to hotel room cleanliness. (I bring my own pillow-case)
If the concierge floor club room is important to you, (it is for me), then this is not the hotel. It's empty most of the time. Nothing there at night at all. You can't even get a beer and enjoy the views. The breakfast was ok in the club room, but nothing great. The club room at this facility is not much of a benefit at all. The only real advantage to the club floors here seems to be the free internet, and the continental (very small ) breaqkfast
Overall, the hotel is very friendly and extremely clean and well kept. (except for the tub in room 2703). I'll be back.

title: “Nice place! -_-”
text: Stoped at this microtel after workin sett the jags stadium. Nice place & very friendly staff.When I got in my room my microwave didnt work!!!!!! The front desk had another one at my door in 2 min flat!!!!!! Killer service!!! Microtel never lets me down..............:) -_- ===D~~~

title: “Met Expectations”
text: Extremely comfortable, well located with charming staff. It's monotonous dining in the same restaurant for all meals and the in room dining was not flawless but will definitely return.

title: “Do not stay here!!!! Credit Card # Stolen”
text: In December I read the reviews for this place and though it only had one bad review, my husband and I decided to stay here. One because there were no hotels available the week before Christmas and two, being in a band you don't have alot of money to spend on a place to sleep.We arrived on a Friday and were met by a friendly front desk person. We were shown to our room in the non smoking section of the hotel. The building is old, and looks like it, but hey, it was warm and and the doors had a lock. The bed was clean, the room was clean and the shared bathroom was cleaned. We were to leave on Saturday but decided to stay an extra night. This was not planned but they put us up with no trouble at all.So why not stay here? BECAUSE MY CREDIT CARD NUMBER WAS STOLEN!!!! Along with another couple we know that were staying there. I was lucky enough to catch the charges before they got outrageous. But my friend's card was charged over $1,000!!!Again, do not stay here....Lord knows we won't and we will be telling everyone we know not too.BEWARE!

title: “Stylish, boutique hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed here last weekend for our anniversary and thought it was nice. It's a cool, stylish hotel that's not self-important. Small room and really compact bathroom. My husband said the shower was too small and the shower curtain kept clinging to him. I had a hard time regulating the temperature; it seemed like it was too hot or too cold as you can't set it to maintain a certain temp. Nice bed/bedding and decor. Of course parking was expensive ($30 plus taxes); all city hotels charge crazy parking fees these days. Great location for walking to Pacific Place, shopping and the movie theater at GameWorks. We didn't try the restaurant, but it looked nice. Everyone we came into contact with at the hotel was very friendly. We live locally and were just in the city for an occasion so we'll likely try a different hotel next time, but I'd recommended it to out-of-towners looking for a nice, affordable city stay.

title: “Great hotel. To Westin standard.”
text: Great hotel within walking distance of all key attractions. Very much to the Westin standard look and feel. No disappointments and good service. Good breakfast buffet. Rooms on the smaller side but to be expected.

title: “Not for people who prefer clean rooms”
text:
My wife and I stayed here with a friend for the 2010 International convention.
We were charged $120 per night for the 3 of us but it wasn't worth half of that. The bathroom floor had hair on it. Several different kinds. It looked as if it was a bathroom floor at a frat house. Ok, maybe not THAT bad but it was still pretty gross. The bathroom floor looked like it hadn't been mopped with clean water for at least a couple of months. 
The stairwell was horribly filthy. Not just dirty, filthy! A good power-wash could have removed about 4-5 shades of darkness. I was afraid to use the ice machines because of their lack of cleanliness elsewhere so I can't review the ice. 
The room was pretty small and only allowed enough room to walk around the beds (double beds BTW, not queen size.) At least there was a long counter for the bathroom sink. One of our blankets was completely frayed around the edges and was pretty beat up. The other blanket had a cigarette burn through it (in a no smoking room.) There was a tiny closet to hang some stuff up and that helped a little. Overall, I was able to sleep somewhat comfortably (I'm a dude) but the women were pretty grossed out by the lack of cleanliness of the motel and had trouble even touching the sheets. I imagine we could have tried to find another room in SA but with a convention in town of around 90,000 people, rooms had been scarce for months.
The breakfast was somewhat Ok. They had 2 waffle machines but there was no sign to tell you that you needed 2 cups of waffle mix per waffle (instead of one.) Maybe a sign would have saved the need for 2 machines and saved them a little on the cost of batter as well (people tossing the 1st attempt.) The only eggs they had were hard-boiled but they provided no tongs for the fishbowl they were in so people stuck their hands in the bowl to grab them. Nastiness! They provided yogurt, which was cool but the service was without a smile. I watched the girl stock them and was a little shocked at her method. She seemed to like to throw them in the bowl versus just setting them in there. 
That girl was a pretty sore subject for several customers. She seemed to scoff at anyone that was in her way (she was a bleach blonde just in case management is reading this) no matter how friendly they were to her. One man even greeted her and asked her how her morning was going after she forced him out of her way. She grunted a garbled response and pushed her way through the rest of the line. 
I would suggest breakfast elsewhere. There was a Starbucks in the next parking lot but they don't serve breakfast. There was also a Taqueria next door so if you prefer recycled food then maybe you can check that out.
The only saving grace for this place was the friendly and helpful staff at the front counter. They were quite a bit more pleasant than most hotel/motel staff I've come across and we were grateful. Unfortunately, that one positive aspect was way overshadowed by the inept ability of the rest of the staff to provide a decent experience.
I would highly recommend that you try a different hotel.

title: “Large beautiful rooms and great location, very good value.”
text: The hotel is not large but is classy and attractive. The entrance is not grand - you step down a few steps from road level into the lobby, but once inside the lobby is is very nice and rich looking. The service is very good - no dissappointments. Best of all are rooms and location. The basic excecutive rooms are about 400+ sq ft (not bad for NYC !) and nicely and expensively decorated (following the theme of the lobby), comfortable bed, classic furiniture, nice bathroom. It was also quiet.The room was very clean and in "like new" condition. Good room service and mini bar, but pricey. The hotel is only about 3 or 4 or blocks blocks north of Times Square and 8 blocks south Central Park - easy walking distance. The other couple we travelled with upgraded to Junior Suite at check in - it was very large with a nice bar and seating area - this is a recommended upgrade and it was not too expensive. Solid 4* - we would stay here again in heartbeat.

title: “Great Price for hotel after night at Fenway!”
text: We stayed at the Roundhouse on a Friday night, after going to a Red Sox game at Fenway. The hotel is a little bit further from Fenway than I would have like to have stayed, but it was very clean, had a free shuttle, free breakfast and is a suites hotel. The area where the hotel is, isn't the greatest but it's a city so really should be expected...The shuttle is very crowded and busy, but it's FREE so it's ok...The breakfast food was fine, the area to eat is really the lobby and just can't accomodate the amount of people who want to eat, we took our food back to our room which worked out. The staff was pleasant and answered any questions and needs. We did have our car with us and the parking was also free, just not alot of spots, most people are allowed to park in the gas station parking lot behind the hotel...

title: “Nice Hotel in an Inconvenient Location”
text:
I paid $85 plus taxes per night on Priceline for a four night stay in late December. The hotel is clean, has excellent service, a nice pool area, and a good bar in the lobby area. 
As a Priceline customer, everything other than the room was an extra charge: parking-$20 per day, internet access-$12 per day, gym use-$12 per day, no free coffee in the room- overpriced Starbucks in the lobby store, no free newspaper, etc. As a result, I parked on the street, went to the coffee shop about a mile away for free internet, and swam laps in the pool for exercise.
The location is inconvenient if you want to walk to go anywhere. There's really nothing except for an expensive steakhouse across the courtyard and then there are several office buildings. This location doesn't seem to be the best place for a luxury hotel. It is convenient enough though if you have a car and don't mind driving as it is just off I-5 and a few minutes from I-805.

title: “nicely renovated with a bit of character, but...”
text: Stayed here for the last three nights of a two-week long multi-city US business trip. I was somewhat jaded with living out of a suitcase and pretty tired when I got here, but the staff on the front desk were welcoming and friendly. Also, luckily they had a room already ready early. I was warned that it wasn't the best room in the property - but hey, an early check-in was more important at that time. No view from the room apart from straight into a wall/window of another room (I was warned so can't complain). The room was on the small side for a US hotel - but perfectly adequate for one (or a couple). Queen bed, small desk, hanging space with wash basin in the corner and only a shower (fine for me) no tub. Fridge and microwave (handy for a slob 'night-in' when you just don't fancy another restaurant meal out!). Gaslamp district with its attractions a few minutes walk, and the convention centre probably about 15 minutes walk - which in San Diego weather is just right. On top of the no view issue with the room - I also found it quite noisy - even with the airco off there was a rather loud buzz/hum all the time I think due to airco system in other rooms? Bed was comfy though and I was very tired - so I slept fine in the end. Guests with sensitive ears - take ear plugs! Hotel restaurant and bar - OK. Very friendly staff (chef in particular) and the cocktails were great. Very nice gym facility with a small yoga studio (though not sure they actually have classes - but there were some yoga DVDS you could select yourself). Overall, a nice conversion of a historic building. Gave it some character over other big chain hotels I've stayed in before in the city.

title: “Great Service”
text: The employees at the Wingate Hotel were very courteous and helpful. We had never been to Indianapolis, but they made us feel very at home with great restaurant referrals & directions, as well as went out of their way to make sure the complinentary breakfast met everyone's needs. The hotel was very clean & comfortable.

title: “Good Value, Surprisingly affordable tasty food, good service, what's to kvetch”
text: Good hotel, meals and value overall, as long as you don't have Hyatt or Four Seasons expectations. Rooms have fresh new furniture, carpeting, comfortable bed with lots of pillows - and the dining is surprisingly good. Buffett breakfast has excellent fresh orange juice all you want, ripe variety of fresh fruits, hot and cold cereal, pancakes, scrambled eggs, decent coffee, bagels with cream cheese, even smoked salmon all for $11.95. Staff is very accommodating and one doesn't have to wait most of the time for service - wi fi had a weak signal in my room but it's free, price is right, when are they going to step up with in room safes for laptop, valuables and cash not used during the day? - it's 2006 Four Points, match the offerings of other good hotels. No complaints - if you're a Gold or Platinum status local calls and toll free calls are free. A surprisingly good set of cookies and fruit awaited my arrival with and they noted it was a return visit for me. Room is quiet and it's interesting eye candy to watch the conferences, weddings, variety of people coming in and out of this hotel. Their new signature pies are not worth tasting. Seems professionally run - good value, location, near bus line and Burger King! ATM machine only doles out $200 for a $2.50 charge. East Wing is better am told.

title: “overall comfortable stay”
text: was here for two nights. we had a jr suite connecting with a double. the connecting doors were awkward to use. beds were very comfortable. we noticed there wasn't a coffee maker in the room. the sitting area was very nice, pleasant furnishings. some wear and tear here and there, but not too bad. the bath products were quite cheap. the body wash smelled just like the tamarind sauce i eat with indian samosas! really! the bath was very large, though. our toilet clogged the last day. would definately stay again if i could get a decent rate. $500/nt was too much.

title: “excelent Value- great staff”
text: our first visit to NY , visiting our daughter who has been there for 5 months, grat location, very comfortable bed, plenty of hot water, staff were very friendly and efficient, had a room at the back on 4th floor, quiet , as mentioned buy others lift can be slow

title: “Hotel staff is horrible”
text: We stayed in this hotel for 1 day on our unplanned vacation to Washington recently.The room that we stayed was good .On the first day when we just checked in hotel staff were behaving very friendly.But next day when we had to checkout we asked till what time can we do the checkout as we were going out for sightseeing so it could be late by 1-2 hrs after 12 noon which is generally the checkout time.The staff agreed and and said he is fine till 2pm and late charge will be applicable till 2pm max.Later on the day when we came back after sightseeing at 2 pm and about to do the checkout the manager of the hotel came and told us that we have to pay for the late checkout.We were shocked to here it.They all made a plan to just extract money.The late checout amount they asked us to give was around $200 which was far beyond the price of one day stay in that hotel.They were not agreeing and asking us to pay....they reduced the price till $130 but then my husband some how managed to made them argee for no late charge ...as they asked us to give good feed back in websites and that is the reason they told they won't charge us.This was all the game plan I think they might be playing with many other also.

title: “NYC's best kept secret”
text:
This hotel truly lives up to it's name. It was the star of our trip to New York City. 
Budget hotels can often disappoint in quality, but not the Chelsea Star. It was cute, classy, comfortable, cozy, and super clean. The location is perfect, only a few blocks from the Empire State Building, Madison Square Garden, and Penn Station; and easily within walking distance of Time Square, yet we were still able to find free street parking. Great restaurants were with in walking distance as well, and Molly Wees across the street is the best little Irish pub in NYC.
The staff was extremely friendly and helpful on our trip, and the housekeeping staff kept our room / bathroom spotless. Our room even included a tv with a dvd player. There was the cutest little courtyard on the first floor which allows travelers from all over to meet and greet in a relaxed setting.
The best part on an extra hot weekend in the city, the air conditioning went up to full blast so we were able to sleep comfortably!
I will stay no where else on my trips to NYC!

title: “Rent a bed”
text:
I stayed at the Club Quarters for 6 days. The service at the front desk is overall poor. Examples of poor delivery during my stay include the following:
1. The room was never dusted. a banana peel sat on the counter for 4 days
2. I was evicted from their only public area/business center which was used as the overflow for their restaurant. This was done without a posted notice and with no regard to basic hospitality practices. Left without a place where to charge my laptop I was forced to conduct a conference call from the nearest Dunkin Donuts. This was done after I had checked out early as a courtesy to the hotel to allow them to prepare rooms during a very busy Friday
3 I left towels in the shower floor to be replaced only to find the same pile and new towels stacked on top of my side chair.
4. I waited in the pub to be acknowledged or sat down for 20 minutes. Nobody even made eye contact with me
The hotel does not effectively cater to the business travel. Poorly managed and a shame to the Club Quarters organization

title: “LA Custom”
text:
Convenient, clean, easy access. Great staff and valet's who remember you. Sheets and bed are
quite comfy. More like a European hotel than the average domestic hotel.

title: “What a great surprise!”
text: I must admit, following the comments of some people on this website, we were panicking big time! But on arrival, despite the first room being too small for an 8 day stay, they moved us to a larger room with no problems at all and it was a great room, exposed brick walls, large window, air con and ceiling fan, huge marble bathroom with large marble shower cubicle, tv, wardrobe, two bedside cabinets and a large chest of drawers, they even lent me a hairdryer for the duration of our stay.. The room was cleaned every day, with fresh bedding and towel, EVERY DAY! When you walked in the door at the front of the hotel, you could smell the freshly cleaned aroma of disinfectant. The staff were lovely, polite and helpful. Free tea and coffee in reception each day. For the money, it is well worth it. Room 315 if anyone wants to ask for it. Ignore the comments others have made about cockroaches etc - it was spotless throughout. The location is to die for - within walking distance of 5 - 10 mins, you have little italy, SoHo and SoHo's Bloomingdales (yeah, what a nice surpise), Tribeca, Chinatown etc etc. L'orange Bleu was a great restraunt too - a brill stay! Well don to SoHotel and I will be recommending you to all my friends and collegues.

title: “Great hotel, terrible room service”
text:
Location: nothing beats coming off a long flight and walking to the airport.
Note 1: this applies if you come into Trml E (intl) and Trml A - Trmls B and C require a longer walk going through Trml A in both cases...and a walk through the parking garage if you come into Trml C
Note 2: Note to hotel - a few better direction signs from the airport would help...and more importantly from inside the hotel to the airport. Right now one goes through a seedy corridor coming from the airbridge and not the best first impression.
Transportation: again, great. One can either take the free Silver line to S. Station or the free hotel shuttle to the T-station and Blue Line
Rooms, front desk etc: standard but nice Hilton rooms and friendly open front desk. I get free Wifi as a HH member so didn't check the paid rates
Food: this is the weakest point of the hotel. Very few choices and all expensive. The room service is a disaster as many others have also commented. I was leery trying it at their rates $18 for a burger plus 15% svc, plus 3% admin fee, plus $3.5 delivery plus 7% MA state tax - nice ripoff. The experience started at 5pm when the room service is supposed to open - nothing but the silly msg repeating the timing. Called front desk - they could not reach them either. At 5.45pm the jokers at room service decided to open for service - took 30mins and delivered the wrong order. The front desk was nice enough to take the charge off but one remembers the experience.
Summary: if you're coming off a long flight or taking an early one, go for it...and avoid the room service

title: “very nice hotel”
text: I stayed here for a conference and thought it was really nice. It's very close to Millennium Park and the Chicago Art Institute, and it's possible to take the Blue Line right from O'Hare for 2.25 and end up right around the corner from the hotel. There are a lot of stores nearby, but if you want to go shopping on Michigan, you have to walk about a mile and a half or take the Red Line. The rooms were nice, but small, and the housekeeping staff did a great job. It was really hot outside, but the AC inside was great. The lobby is really beautiful and extravagant. I also love Hilton's new Peter Thomas Roth bath products. :)

title: “Just so-so hotel with exhorbitant wifi charge”
text:
We spent 4 nights at this hotel the week of Oct. 7th while my partner attended a seminar and to visit family. The location is sort of out the way from most attractions in Phoenix, a reason the front desk used to justify the $15 per day charge for wi-fi. The rooms, while large, are rather dated and not in the best of shape. Our room (actually a 2 room suite had wallpaper that was loose and dirty carpeting. In fact, housekeeping did not vacuum the carpets for the first 3 days. While we had 2 flat panel TVs, the selection of stations was very limited.
Some things to beware of if you choose to stay here: The $15 a day charge for wi-fi (the rooms at one time allowed hispeed connections, but that has been discontinued; no coffee is available in the lobby after breakfast (you can buy a cup for $3.50 at the bar; the bottle of water in the room costs $4.95 per bottle (not a big bottle either); and beware if your credit card is also a debit card. They put a hold on a significant portion that can take up to 3 weeks to get released; I found it interesting that when I commented on the wi-fi charge, the person at the front desk later tracked me down and gave me an article on hotels charging for wi-fi. The basic premise is that since people now use cell phones, hotels have lost a big source of revenue from the use of in-room phones so thay make it up with wi-fi charges. When I stated that many hotel chains and mom & pop motels provide it free, the person argued with me and said he had worked in a number of hotels and they all charge for wi-fi.
I am amazed that companies and organizations continue to use Embassy Suites considering these inconveniences. I have run into these things at 3 different Embassy Suites in the last year. 
I would recommend choosing another hotel, there are many in the Phoenix/Scottsdale area.

title: “We Loved the Inn at Queen Anne”
text: The Inn at Queen Anne is a great place to stay. Where else can you get a nice room with a kitchenette and walk in closet for under $125. a night? All the staff was top notch - from the maintenance men working outside the building to the desk clerks to the shuttle drivers. They were all very friendly and helpful. We would recommend this hotel to anyone and if we visit Seattle again, we will definitely stay at the Inn at Queen Anne. Thanks!

title: “Just Terrible”
text: The hotel had an odor, the carpet in the foyer was dirty it needs to be changed. The room was to small to house a king sized bed. the bathroom was nasty-the tub, shower and toliet had not been cleaned-we went out and bought bleach and comet and cleaned the bathroom before using it. We had to actually go to the front desk and ask for clean towels-(that we didn't use) again we went out and purchased our own towels. I would never stay here again. The price was great but the accomodations was terrible.

title: “To market to market”
text: Very nice hotel. CLEAN and the staff was ever so helpful. The breakfast was incredible and they even had Espresso coffee drinks and Soy milk. The rooms are spacious and quiet. The beds are comfy and towels soft.

title: “Extra Nice Hotel with Great Location!”
text: This is a very nice hotel on the Riverwalk. We snagged our 3 rooms through Hotwire and got a better rate than any published rate, but not a super-great deal. We self-parked right across the street for $15, so not bad. The biggest bonus was having one of our rooms upgraded to a junior suite so we could have adjoining rooms. The associate at check-in, Farrell Sledge, was very helpful and it is his help that raised a good stay to great. We were able to get together in the suite and enjoy the extra space while we had some drinks and snacks before heading out to the Riverwalk for dinner. Even though we didn't have a river-view room, the view was nice enough. The pool was great for the kids, and you can see the view of the river from there.

title: “Surprisingly better than I thought it would be”
text:
This is an above average 3 star hotel. It is beautifully decorated. And they are also working on re-doing the hotel rooms , and adding plasma screen TV's to each room. 
My husband and I live in San Diego, and we stayed at this hotel for his 30th High School reunion to spend more time with his classmates. It had a great banquent room on the 9th floor, in which the roof opened up above the dance floor which was really nice. Great seeing the stars while dancing.
The positives. 
1) Clever decorations, kinda of Art Deco. Flowers in vases at every corner. 
2) Very comfortable bed. 
3) Nice mini bar. 
4) Close to the happening spots in Downtown. Great price for the location.
 5) Great breakfast food in their restaurant. We ate with 6 people and everyone enjoyed their breakfast.
6) Front desk gave us a room away from the bus station so we had a good nights sleep. 
7) Nice banquet room. 
8) Nice bar to meet up with friends. 
9) Very nice lobby with lots of very comfortable attractive furniture.
The negatives. 
1) Dark lighting in the room
2) Therefore bathroom needs a make-up mirror. 
3) Not much storage space for clothing for 2 people if you are going to stay awhile. Our room had 3 little drawers. 
4) No drawers in the bathroom to store toiletries. 
5) Not a safe location to walk around in at late at night, take a taxi if you want to go somewhere. If you are walking in a large group you will be okay. Just don't go out alone at night.
 6) The banquet room could use some noise absorbing carpet or something, as it got very loud in the room with the sound ricocheting off the tile floors, the walls and windows.
All and all it was a very nice experience, and quite surprising. I think if the hotel did a couple of extra things, it can easily increase it's rating to a 4 star hotel.

title: “Small, quiet, lovely area. Convenient location.”
text: I travelled to NYC to meet up with some friends to walk in the Susan G. Komen Race for the Cure. This hotel was a little gem on a quiet street. I had a view of the small park across the street. The rooms were small, but immaculate. The bathroom was also small but immaculate. The bed was very comfortable. It would have been nice to have had a small coffee maker in the room, but Starbucks was less than a block away on Columbus. This hote was convenient to the subway, museums, Columbus Avenue and Central Park. The staff was friendly and professional. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking for something in a beautiful, quiet area after a day in the big city.

title: “Fabulous/beautiful facility; superb, friendly, helpful staff”
text: One of the nicest places we've stayed at in NYC; great views of midtown (that you can't get when you are in midtown), convenient to Holland Tunnel, great areas to walk around nearby - Soho, the Village, Chinatown; Beautiful rooms

title: “Hostile Customer Services / Ghost Hotel Manager”
text:
August 2009
 This hotel looks respectable from the outside, but don't let that fool you.
 We called to confirm our reservation the day before arrival and was connected to a rambling phone attendant. This "old" woman could barely enunciate English, together w/ her hostile tonation gave us a real laugh. When we repeatedly asked her to transfer our call to the front desk, she said she is the front desk and when we asked to speak w/ the hotel manager, she said there was not one available and said "you have to deal w/ me". 
 This strange and semi-terrorist conduct from this hotel's hired employees surely puts us on guard! 
 We know that there is a current contraction w/ the global economy, but this certainly falls of the rocker to getting travelers to spend for services. At best, this hotel is a front for some Halloween house intended to intimidate paying guests. At worst, they employ unqualified people to run the business into the ground.
 Who do you call ? Not the hotel manager of their customer service dept. in Dallas, TX. One plays ghost, and the other will surely jive over your head with their overmedicated and undereducated talks.

title: “Where do I begin? Let's start with awful.”
text:
First of all, my bad for not realizing that this hotel is 20 miles from the airport. Second, my bad for not researching that you have to sign up for the airport shuttle 24 hours in advance. Now, with that said, I will tell you what ISN'T my fault. 
-The young guy working the front desk, couldn't have been more rude. In fact, I don't know if I have ever encountered a ruder front desk clerk in all of my travel days. 
-Since the hotel is so far away, and I had to pay $45 dollars for a taxi ride to the airport, I most certainly signed up for the airport shuttle a week in advance. I didn't want another $45 dollar taxi ride back to the hotel. So, six days before I arrived back to Phoenix and got to speak with that same rude front desk clerk. Here's the conversation. 
Me: Yes, I would like to sign up for the airport shuttle.
Rude clerk: Ok.
Me: So, I will be arriving on July 14th at 11:00 a.m
Rude clerk: Ok.
Me: Do you need any more information from me?
Rude clerk: No.
Naturally, I feared that I probably wasn't going to get picked up since the guy didn't ask what airline I was flying, or my name, or anything else. So, I called back the day before my flight arrived back to Phoenix, to double check that I did in fact have a reservation for the shuttle. I did not. So, I made another reservation. This time I was asked for all of my flight info, so I felt confident that I would be picked up by the shuttle. Wrong. The next day, after my flight arrived, I phoned the hotel, and let them know that I had made a reservation, but I needed to know what the shuttle looked like. The clerk told me, and I waited. And I waited. After 30 minutes, I phoned the hotel back and let them know that I hadn't seen the shuttle, and I was waiting. They clerk was indifferent and was like, oh yeah, there a lot of traffic and the driver will be there in 20 minutes. I think you get the gist of this long drawn out story. The shuttle never came after an additional 30 minutes of waiting and two angry phone calls later. Guess who ended up taking another $45 taxi ride back to her hotel in NO TRAFFIC???? This girl. This place is awful. It's horrible. The staff is rude and I wasted $90 on taxi rides to and from a "park and fly" airport. DONT. BOOK. HERE.

title: “New, Trendy and Convenient”
text:
My girlfriend and I went to NY on July 2007. After doing a lot of research on expedia and tripadvisor, we decide to book this hotel from expedia. We booked this a few months before departure and got a good rate for about $150 US per night. We notice that a lot of the hotels in New York City are very old. We want to find some place where it is clean, convenient and with free wireless internet. We are aware the size of the room will be small (220 sq ft), but since there are only 2 of us and we spend most of the time outside, room size is not a matter for us.
From JFK, taxi is about $32 w/tips to Hotel 373. We arrived at about 11am (before check-in time) and get a room immediately. This is a standard one double bedroom. It is smaller compare to the average North American style hotel. But this is New York City, what can you expect? For those with bigger body build, might consider paying a bit more for Queen Bed. The room is clean and trendy. Mattress is comfortable. Hotel staff is nice and helpful. The hotel is just one block from Empire State Building and close to subway station. There is a street with a lot Korean restaurant one block away.

title: “Good Low cost option in LA !!”
text:
Opçao custo benefico boa . bom cafe da manha , quartos limpos , banheiros necessitam de reforma ( existem alguns buracos na parede) mas sem insetos (baratas, bed bugs , ou mosquitos) . atendimento frio , mas adequado . custo estacionamento muito caro por dia assim como todos os estacionamentos em LA ) . vale para poucos dias em LA . Ao lado do metro . Vizinhança duvidosa.
It's a low cost option , clean room , bathroom need to be refurbished, but i didnt find any bugs (cockroach, bedbugs or mosquito ) good breakfast (limited options), non frendly frontdesk , but honest and functional , close to the subway . Expensive parking per day (as the all parks in LA) . I stayed for 11 days , and i should go back again. I recomend if you want to be in La for few days .

title: “Disappointing Wedding Anniversary”
text:
My husband and I planned a four-day trip to Chicago to celebrate our wedding anniversary. After researching a number of properties, we chose the Park Hyatt Chicago.
Upon arrival, the front desk staff was very pleasant, greeting us by name and offering us a complimentary tea service. Nice touch. But that's where the personal attention ended. After the first day, none of the staff seemed to remember our names. The doorman could rarely be found to open the door, and the tea service, which we planned to make a nightly ritual, was not offered again. Two of the four nights we did not receive turn down service, and when we requested that the water in our room be replenished it took house staff 45 minutes to bring up two bottles of water. 
To my disappointment, though it was noted in our reservation itinerary, not one staff member could muster a "happy anniversary". In fact, our anniversary was not acknowledged in any way by the hotel. 
We are well traveled and have received much more personal service from supposedly lesser properties. 
The location pf the Park Hyatt Chicago is excellent - right on the Magnificent Mile - and the view from our room could not have been better. But if you are looking for personalized service and a special experience you might want to look elsewhere. For us, the Park Hyatt did not deliver.

title: “Safe and clean”
text: Nothing special about his hotel but much better than expected. Clean and safe place to stay. I cant really say if its far away from attractions as we only stayed here for one night to get some rest before traveling back home. It was very cheap ( think 36 $ for a room with breakfast) and for this price it was great. We would stay there again.

title: “Can we go back?”
text:
I booked this hotel for two nights through Priceline and feel like we got a bargain!
Check in was easy-peasy and we stayed in a 4th floor room with two beds facing the golf course. The room was clean and had plenty of space and a large bathroom. The beds were comfortable and the linens soft. There was a bit of noise from the hallway, but nothing too annoying. 
The hotel is fairly isolated and surrounded by the golf course. We liked that the hotel was so close but yet so far from the big city. 
The only thing I could complain about is the parking lot is not very well lit at night. 
We will choose to stay here in the future.

title: “The Place to Stay”
text: You know, I'm not sure what would prompt anyone to write a negative review of this embarrsingly affordable, funky (over-used, I know) & friendly motel. We made our first trip to Austin last summer and part of our memories of that great time always includes the Austin Motel. For us, it is part of the experience of taking in Austin.

title: “A Good Bargain, friendly, roomy and clean”
text:
Bottom line - a good hotel at a good price.
Pros - Very Clean, very friendly and helpful staff, above average size room, convenient to all of Times Square, Restaurant Row, Hell's Kitchen eateries, and anything else in mid-town, great bargain ($174 at Hotel site) for what you get.
Cons - Noisy from outside (try to get higher level room - we were on 5th floor facing street), tiny bathroom (usually not a problem, but you could not sit straight without knees hitting wall), hot room with no thermostat, beds hard as a rock, elevators small (VERY small) and slow.
Would I stay again? Absolutely - but I would make sure I have a higher level room. The staff was great, the rooms were emaculate and roomy.

title: “What's not to like?”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the University Inn for several days in late August. As so many others have said, this is simply a great place to stay while in Seattle. We stayed in a premier room that had a very comfortable bed, sofa, mini-fridge, microwave and a view of Mt. Rainier. 
The staff are very accommodating, and provide great service. The shuttle is a real plus if you want to visit Seattle attractions and leave your car behind, and a fine breakfast awaits you at the Portage Bay Cafe next door. Overall, an excellent experience, and we will return.

title: “Low class”
text:
My boyfriend made sure since I was arriving early that I would be able to check in before him. The girl at the front desk REFUSED to let me check into the room even though they had his credit card information and they had spoken earlier and come to agreement about my coming early (big deal - we do this all the time). She said without a credit card I was unable to enter. She said only with a huge deposit put onto my credit card could I go into the room. My card was at its max at that point and it didn't go through. She was so rude, and REFUSED letting me into the room, after a long day of traveling, luggage and all. It took a long time to speak to the manager who finally let me in my room. She purposely took her time, even rolled her eyes at me. I was flabbergasted. When we checked out we didn't receive a discount. We really wished we had stayed at the W Hotel :(
Rooms decent nothing special. Bar/restaurant downstairs had decent food. All nothing special. Would never return even if it were free.

title: “Embassy @ the airport”
text:
We spent the last 3 nights we were in BOS @ the Embassy Suites & were delighted. The suite was very large & fairly new. The facilities were fabulous as were the happy hour (but no alcoholic beverages) & the large breakfasts.
The hotel was about a 7 or 8 minutes walk to the Airport T station, although the staff was not very helpful in locating it. It's down a path which runs by a soccer field & was very easy to use after the 1st time.
It was so convenient getting around via T & not worrying about a car. In addition, I thought the hotel might be noisy due to planes flying overhead, but the hotel must be well insulated because we rarely heard a thing.
I would definitely recommend this hotel to families. My kids enjoyed having their own TV & so did their parents!

title: “Clean, reasonable price, good location”
text: Stay here about every two years when going to San Francisco. While its not downtown, it's only about 2.5 miles out. Ask for a room on the Moulton St. side, it will be much quieter than staying on the Lombard street side. The free parking will save you about $40 from staying downtown.

title: “Nice hotel if you need to be in that area”
text: This was the team hotel for a lacrosse tournament we were attending. It's nice, rooms were okay - bathrooms a bit smalI l and towels not super, but sufficient. Honestly, I would have preferred to stay across the way at the Embassy Suites and had a bigger room and free breakfast! Walking distance to some restaurants, but really need a car. Not the place to stay if you are coming to "see" Houston because it's a ways away from the sights.

title: “excellent value; nice stay; check address!!”
text: This is the third time I have stayed at the Comfort Inn at 129 West 46th Street. I mention the address because I have seen if referred to comfort inn midtown and comfort inn time square! and I see some pictures posted from the one on 35th! Anyway, this hotel and the staff are wonderful. Rooms are updated and clean, beds are comfortable, we were on the fifth floor with a front window and the noise was minimal and only a block from the center of time square!!! thanks again to the great staff.

title: “Girls Weekend”
text: Fabulous location. The STAFF, from the Drive-Up Valet to Check-out were SUPERB !!! Professional with personality and care for our stay. Clean, clean hotel and the Heavenly Bed was just that = HEAVENLY !!!!

title: “Very disappointing”
text:
I stayed here with friends. When we arrived at 6.30pm after a very long and tiring flight, We were informed that our room was still not ready (check-in on our documents stated 2pm??) and they asked us to come back in an hour or so. We went out to dinner, and came back at 9pm wanting to check in. We were informed that it still was not ready, and to come back later. I was furious and asked to speak to a manager. The manager was very disinterested in my complaint, but managed to move my room and put me up straight away. I asked the front counter staff to include breakfast free due to the inconvenience, she just laughed in my face. 
When we got to the room, it was very dated. The bathroom was tiny and the tap was leaking. There was no effort on the hotels behalf to fix this, so instead water was constantly being wasted. 
I tried to book a dinner show on broad way with the concierge. He told me he was very busy that day and that I should just go outside and book it with a street merchant instead.
Overall, service was incredibly poor. I was disgusted with how they treated their clients and the attitudes that most of them had. The location of this hotel was fantastic- you couldn't have gotten much closer to Times Square. They also offered free internet in the hotel lobby. Unfortunately tho, this would not be enough to make me stay at this hotel ever again, and I certainly do not recommend it.

title: “Loved the Location”
text:
We stay at many Marriotts. The Renaissance Parc 55 was what I would classify as fine. The lobby was pretty, however the hallways and the rooms were just average size and were a little worn. The service was very good, however we had a major problem with the doorman and a limo company, which has yet to be resolved.
The location was wonderful. You could walk virtually everywhere, or take the Powell Street Cable car 1.5 blocks away, the BART across the way, or an inexpensive taxi to most sights!
I would stay here again.

title: “Location, Location”
text: We spent two nights at the Flatotel, spacious room and very clean. Continental breakfast every morning was included. The concierge/reception staff were excellent. The location for sight seeing and shopping was great, Times Square just a short walk... would stay there again.

title: “Great Stay - cation Spot”
text:
I booked for a night over Labor day weekend. They had a Staycation package with a hotel credit. We planned to use the pool and room service and it all worked out as planned. Even without stepping foot in the Casino, we had a good time. I had heard that the Burgers in the restaurant were good, so we ordered. Yum - carmelized onions, etc... yes it was more expensive than a Big Mac, but its a rare treat. We were on the Concierge floor so even better. We could avoid using the mini bar and just grab a few sodas, coffee, etc.. I don't drink, so the light stuff is fine for me.
The room, very nice. Comfy bed, robe, etc... Since the hotel is newly built, it has all the amenities and then some including a Bose sound system and TV in the bathroom, dual head shower, etc... My only slight surprise is there was not a tub in my room. Not sure if you have to ask for one, but the shower was very nice. Everyone in my family went in and stayed for a long time. 
The pool was a good size. A little shallow, a little cold at first, but no one was there, so we had it to ourselves. Nice cabanas to sit out. The hot tub was in the shower area. Again, nice showers, steam room. I didn't have time for the spa, but maybe on another trip.
If you're close by and need a night off, I'd recommend it. Only down side is its not really downtown, so you can't walk to anything, nor is it River Front, but the valet will arrange for your car to come around and valet parking is included in the price (unlike many hotels in Chicago, etc...) All you have to do is tip.

title: “Watch out for additional fees”
text:
Upon arriving at the hotel we were informed that parking was an extra $20 per vehicle, per night. We had brought 2 cars as one member of our party was splitting off. No where was it listed that parking was not included, and thats unacceptable.
We got into our room and the whole place smelled of cigarette smoke, despite being a non-smoking room. The windows had rust around them, and the AC vent looked like it was about to fall off. in addition, every time the AC kicked on it sounded like a small jet had just landed making it hard to stay asleep for the light sleeper.
If you aren't going to Fenway (which is right behind the hotel), this place isn't worth it. Go deeper into boston, pay the extra $50 bucks for a night, and get a better stay. After parking fees it won't be that much of a price difference.

title: “Very nice hotel in the Inner Harbor with great rooms!”
text:
We arrived at a very popular and busy time of day, and the service was great! We got our room and our bags quickly to our room. Our bellman was awesome and made the girls feel very welcome. Our room was spacious, clean and had a great view of the patio on the 5th floor. The open patio is a must for any visitor to go to. It was not highly occupied, and it would have been a better idea to go grab dinner and eat it out there overlooking the harbor than to have spent over $100 on a meal at the restuarant...
the indoor pool is very nice, and they have a lifeguard on duty, which is comforting!
the only negative is the parking. it is across the street and a convoluted mess to go from the lobby to the parking garage if you forget anything in the car.
The major positive is that they harbor shopping/eating area is a short walk from the hotel. the only scary part is that there had been some sort of "issue" the night before down at the harbor with a someone getting shot, and we had no idea as we walked around after dark! According to the news, most ciitzens don't feel safe down there at night any longer. But, I never felt threatened or scared with my 3 children in tow.
overall, i would stay here again if ever in Baltimore again! It's a great hotel for the price we received!

title: “Almost there, but not quite.”
text:
My husband and I wanted a night away from the kids so we booked a room in the Tribeca Grand. At first, it was great. We liked the small size of the hotel, great location etc. They even have these great white noise systems that you can use to cancel out the noise of the city (or so we thought). At about 11:45 pm, our white noise system broke and the music from the bar was outragously loud. We called reception and they sent a technician up to our room and by about 12:30am it was clear that the machine was broken. We then moved rooms and all was well. But the television wasn't working in our new room.
The hotel markets their bar as a scene and place to go on the weekends, so it is clear that their priority is to making the bar crowd happy. The design of the hotel is an atrium, so all the noise just travels right up into the rooms! 
There are so many great places to stay in NYC that I would not recommend the Tribeca Grand. We definitely won't stay there again. For the money, it just should have been smoother.

title: “Nearly 100 and looking good”
text: Rooms are small and compact, as expected in a hotel of this age. But they're clean and comfortable and the hotel is in a great location. One block from the cable car turnaround, two blocks from the hop on/hop off bus and a convenience store and large mall with restaurants just around the corner. Coffee and cupcake muffins do not really constitute a continental breakfast; but that aside, our stay was great.

title: “Under my expectations.”
text: Before i made the booking at this hotel i read many good reviews in tripadvisor. The hotel overall is good but is not a gem as many reviewers describe. First of all, i didnt like the breakfast. They serve the coffee in paper cups... the choices are donuts donuts donuts... and maybe a yoghurt and a piece of bread ... Not enough tables for the customers. The rooms are spacious and the beds are very comfort. Also the bedlinen were really good. The location (Midtown) was fantastic, MOMA museum, Rockfeller center, 5th Ave, were just steps away.

title: “Good Budget Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Marcel Hotel last week with a few apprehensions after reading the reviews on this site about the lack of heat. But, my friend recommended this hotel to me, saying that it was a decent place despite the very small rooms, so I decided to give it a shot.
The sleeping rooms are definitely small, but if all you need is a place to lay your head at night, it'll do. The bathroom was pretty nice with marble floors and tiles and a pedestal sink. I love pedestal sinks, but there wasn't much space to put my toiletries down.
The decor of the hotel and the rooms is minimalist chic and reminds me of IKEA furniture. I liked the furniture decor in the lobby and the lounge.
A nice feature is that the Marcel offers free bagels, orange juice and coffee in the morning...not too many places offer complimentary food anymore!
My biggest complaint is that my room was way too hot for me! (opposite from other reviews I've read here) It was an oven when I walked in and I had to turn on the cooler which helped me that evening, but when I woke up the next morning, the cool air turned into hot air and I was sweating and roasting again! I called to complain and ask about the heating/air controls and they told me it was central heating and could not be controlled in individual rooms, so they sent an engineer up to help me open my window which helped immensely!
The down side was that my room faced E. 24th St. so since I had to sleep with the window open so I wouldn't sweat to death, I ended up not sleeping well due to the noise from the street below.
The walls are thin, the hallsway are narrow, and the elevator is tiny, but it's still a decent hotel for the price you're paying.
I liked the area because it was less touristy and more residential (it's near a college) and it was a nice walk to Greenwich Village and Soho.
The price I got for this hotel was $109, but I think it could be a little less for what you get...like $89-99.
But, since it's New York City, $109 is probably still a good deal.

title: “Had to sleep on a cot or pay $50 extra!”
text: We arrived at 11:30am and were told that if we wanted to check in at that time we would have to pay $50 extra. We were told that checkin was at 4pm so we asked to have our luggage stowed and toured the city until we returned at 4:15. When we returned, we were told that only a room with 1 king bed was available- there were 4 of us! We reserved a room with 2 double beds and were told, rudely that we checked in too late! Huh?! So basically we were being extorted into paying $50 to get the room of our choice. I have NEVER had this happen at any other hotel. So 2 of us were forced to share a cot which was so sunken in the middle that we had to put the mattress on the floor for some support. For the amount we paid per night this was unexceptable. We also had to ask several times for more towels and we never received our complimentary newspapers on either morning of our stay. Staff was obviously incompetent, there is no free parking here or free internet. The location and cleanliness were the only positives about this hotel. We noticed that there were many other hotels around the Inner Harbor area, whose location was just as convenient. Next time, we will try one of those!

title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text: Had hotel reward points, so ended up at this Ramada. The staff was extremely helpful and friendly. We couldn't believe how willing they were to go out of their way to help with directions, recommendations, etc. The hotel's location is hard to beat. It was no more than a 10-15 minute drive anywhere we wanted to go. It was also nice to have a few fast food restaurants and drugstores within walking distance. The rooms were nothing special, but they were clean and spacious enough. I'd definitely stay here again.

title: “Love this hotel and its staff!”
text:
We were so happy with this hotel. The room was large, clean and comfortable with a nice view of the river. The buffet breakfast had so many delicious choices, and the service was great. The staff went out of their way to be helpful, even giving us a little extra time for checkout. And the location was just perfect, close to the mall and everything we wanted to see.
Thanks to the hotel and its excellent staff for making our Washington trip so special!

title: “JAZZZY Time!”
text:
Me and my wife went to the Jazz festival this weekend, and oh la la la, we had such a great time. This hotel had such great customer service, it's close to everything, free breakfast and parking(which is a big deal in hollywood!), free wifi, it's clean, and affordable. 
The front desk agents were so friendly and informative, especially that really cute guy, I think his name was Jasper. He helped us out a lot! Will definitely be staying again!

title: “Pleasantly Surprised”
text: Staying at this hotel was a pleasant surprise. I booked the last minute and wasn't expecting much after reading some other reviews. But everything was great! Check-in and check-out were a breeze, our room was clean and spacious, the staff was cordial and helpful. Plenty of counter space in the bathroom. Linens were changed every day. Coffee, shampoo and conditioner were replenished daily. Shower pressure was strong and temperature was as hot as I wanted. The concierge was available every day until 11pm and helped me immensely. I loved the location; even though we were a 10 minute cab ride or short metro ride from the memorials/monuments/museums, we were in walking distance to at least a dozen restaurants and CVS. My only 2 complaints: we had to pay for internet service and no safe in the room. Feel free to contact me with any questions you may have: Lami86@aol.com

title: “Comfort & Location in San Francisco”
text: My wife and I visited the Marriott at the end of a cruise across the Pacific and spent two days prior to flying home. We cannot praise the attitude of the staff here enough, who made us welcome especially getting off the ship at 10am in the morning and being offered a choice of room for immediate check in .The room was excellent with a lovely comfortable bed and big flat screen tv. Due to the excellent location of the hotel we did not dine in at the hotel as we were spoilt for choice with restaurants. We took advantage of the complementary airline check in facility the hotel offered and our check out was as smooth as our check in. A very pleasant two night stay

title: “Exactly as expected”
text: Stayed for a weekend getaway combined with Christmas shopping. The Hotel was as described. Great location for Uptown Dallas. The only thing that kept me from giving it a 5 star rating was the noise in the hallway each morning. The T/X bar had crowds coming and going each night, restaurant was very good. A/c was adjustable ( turned ours down to 68 at night) and worked great. Service was fine adn vallet always knew us when we walked up. Will stay again

title: “Good Location, friendly staff”
text:
I recently stayed here with my husband and teenage daughter in a room with 2 double beds. I have mixed feelings about this place. The room is small with each bed set against a wall, leaving a small space between the beds. There's not much space available for things like suitcases, or even for just moving about in the room. I have a hard time imagining 4 people in this room as it was hard enough for 3 of us. On the other hand, how much time do you really spend in a hotel room? The beds themselves were very comfortable. The bathroom was a decent size, but mold was starting to show in the shower- this surprises me as I was under the impression that this is a recently renovated hotel. I do have issues with housekeeping. We arrived on a hot day and I opened the refrigerator to put in a large bottle of water. I had to first discard a sandwich and drink left in there by a previous occupant. The next day, another hot day in the city, I returned to the room and went to get my cold bottle of water, only to find that housekeeping had discarded it. Given how hot it was, I was a bit annoyed. There were other small issues, such as only one washcloth, the small bottle of shampoo not being replaced, and the fact that the shower door didn't close tightly so the floor always got flooded
The two best things about this hotel are the friendly staff and the location. All of the staff that we met, from the front desk to others that we came across in the elevator, were friendly and seemed to genuinely wish a pleasant stay for us. I also found the location to be ideal. We arrived at Penn Station and it took us less than 10 minutes to walk to the hotel. There's a subway station around the corner and another line a short distance away.
Would I stay here again? We payed $239/night plus tax. At that price, yes. For more than that, no. My favorite hotel in this area is the Hilton Garden Inn on West 35th- I would look there first. It is because of the price, the staff, and the location, that I give this place 4 stars instead of 3.

title: “Excellent”
text:
The staff was very friendly, the room was great, very good american breakfast.
We stayed in the Towers.

title: “great stay”
text: This is a luxury hotel with a spectacular lobby. Snacks/drinks are served directly in the open, comfortable lobby. There is also a Starbucks available. The only main dinner restaurant appears to be an Irish Pub which is run independently from the hotel. Food here is good and in a fun atmosphere. This is a clean ,immaculate hotel with superb service. If you are attending an event at the conference center, this should be your only choice...even if it means paying a little more. If you are not with a meeting , location could be an issue. You are removed from the main hub of the city and require at least a 10 min cab ride. Cabs are always available. If money is an issue, give up a meal , and splurge for an upgraded suite with harbor views. This is worth a trip to Boston alone!

title: “It really was a bad experience!”
text:
I booked this hotel and was impressed with the location and price so was determined to accept that it would be basic but acceptable. What I was not prepared for was the number of bed bug bites I with which I awoke in the morning.
Check in was satisfactory and the room was simple and very basic but functional. The bathroom was OK, however, the bed was uncomfortable.
I received a large number of bites from bed bugs that took a number of days to clear. 
DON"T STAY HERE!!!!!!

title: “Loud noise, tiny space”
text: Some of the tiniest rooms you've ever seen in a New York hotel. You may find this funny, or charming, or insulting in the rip-off sort of way (considering the price), or claustrophia-inducing. Some of the rooms do have nice showers (not bathtubs) with marble and open glass. No lobby to speak of. When you come in, you feel like you're coming in to a high priced hostel. Everything is cramped all through the place. They do charge quite a bit for amenities. The guys at reception, particularly the manager, clearly did not graduate from the School of Basic Customer Service. That's a shame when you pay this much. This boutique chain has it's ups and downs. Most of the them offer free capuccino, etc in the lobby. That's okay-- but at the Mansfield, the milk is sour and about a week old. Also, apparently in many rooms at Hotel 41, they allow guests to bring cats. That's okay-- but then if you're going to rent it out to a non-cat-owner who has cat allergies-- it's a good idea to ask them about it first-- especially when the room reeks of cat urine (which was our case). We were in a room on second floor facing the street, and right before curtain call for the theatre every night, a group of percussion street musicians set up shop for two hours-- right below our room. Cat urine and two hours of banging percussion-- come on.

title: “Tiny Rooms, Big Price, Big Attitudes”
text:
Girlfriend and I, lifelong New Yorkers, decided to stay over in Manhattan for two nights during the transit strike, especially when we saw how low the rates were for this hotel: we got a king room for 150/night, and were upgraded to a king junior suite because of our Hilton Honors status. Despite the lower-than-usual rate, this place was still a bust. 
The "junior suite", on the 19th floor, was the size of a normal small hotel room anywhere else in the continental United States. Welcome to Manhattan, kiddies. And because this hotel is in midtown Manhattan, you get no view. The top floor of this place is the middle floor of the skyscrapers surrounding it. As if the room itself wasn't small enough, the toilet and shower were crammed next to eachother in the "bathroom" to the point where if you stood in the middle of the room, you would be unable to fully extend your arms in either direction. The whole place has a very claustrophobic feel to it, and remember, this is a top-floor junior suite! 
The real kicker is the front desk attitude...twice, from two seperate employees, my polite inquiries or standard dealings were met with the tone of voice normally reserved for the exceedingly little of little people. 
Any good...location is alright, the sheets were clean, and the heat control, though carefully hidden, worked quite well once discovered. Also, the elevators were surprisingly fast for a hotel this big/busy. Would stay here again only if it was the lowest rate in all of midtown.

title: “A surprising 5 stars!”
text:
Finally after travelling to many places in the Bay Area, we found this hotel by mistake due to the Hyatt Regency Santa Clara was sold out. We were reluctant to reserve our room at this hotel but we gave it a try since it is a Hyatt chain hotel.
To our surprise, the hotel is newly built this year. The price was very reasonable for our stays compare to other hotels in the area. The breakfast was a full buffet which was for free of charge. After my husband had his breakfast, he said it was the best meal he has had for the past week.
We will definitely return here with our family the next time we come to San Jose.

title: “NICE WEEKEND”
text: We stayed at the hotel 2 nights while we went to a convention there.It was very convenient and pleasant. the staff were all friendly and helpful, the rooms very clean and updated since we were there a few years ago. the was good food for a fair price with big portions. we did get a special rate which made the stay even better. our king room is normally about $200, which i would be reluctant to pay. my only gripe is that they charge for internet.

title: “You Get What You Pay For...”
text:
This hotel was selected by a colleague that I was travelling with, most likely due to the low corporate rate. I read up on the hotel here, on the tripadvisor site, and was apprehensive. I decided to keep an open mind about the property and see what happened.
The first room that I was given in Tower A smelled like a cigar bar. The front desk staff insisted that it was a no smoking room, but was more than happy to provide me with an alternate room. My second room smelled much fresher, but was a bit stuffy. I would later find out that air conditioning in this hotel (or at least this room) was seasonal. This would make for a hot, humid night of sleep on an unseasonably warm November night. Because of the rodents described in other reviews, I moved some furniture around to make sure there were no flat-mates. The vacated spaces revealed a severe lack of thorough cleaning, as it looked like some of these spaces had not received attention in several YEARS. I also noticed the bathroom mold that many of the other reviewer mentioned.
While the hotel may be receiving renovations, I would not recommend this hotel. The only exception to this would be if you are cash strapped, and understand what you are getting yourself into. I will be taking better advantage of the expense privileges on my next visit to NYC.
Positives
- Staff was friendly, but did not have an "above and beyond" attitude
- Location, location, location (Near Columbus Circle)
- Affordable price for mid-town Manhattan
- Rooms are sizable
- Free in-room wifi internet
Negatives
- Hotel lobby was dated, and room was not well kept
- Room was only cleaned in visible areas
- Tube TV (I am a TV snob and expect all hotels, especially in NYC to have flat screen TVs)
- No AC due to season
- Mold on wall and ceiling of bathroom

title: “The staff at the front desk was amazing”
text: I left my laptop at the cab, when I arrived. The staff at the front desk was very supportive and finally found the taxi driver! What the TLC was not able to do, they did it.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Southgate Tower for 6 nights in April 2004. We had previously stayed at another hotel in New York but due to travelling with friends decided to try somewhere different with more room for us all.
When we arrived at the hotel the reception staff were very friendly and apologised that our room was not quite ready. After about a 5 minute wait we were taken to our room with our luggage.
We were pleasantly surprised with the room. It was very spacious and perfect for 4 people sharing as there was plenty of room for us not to feel as though we were living on top of each other for the next 7 days. After taking a look around the room we noticed one of the blinds wouldn't stay down, we called reception and within 5 minutes they sent someone to our room to fix it. We had no further problems after that.
The suite we stayed in was perfect for us. It had 2 bathrooms, the bedroom had 2 double beds and plenty of space for clothing, the living room was very large and the sofa coverted into a sofa bed, and the kitchenette had all mods cons - fridge, microwave, tea/coffee making facilites, microwave. We also had an iron and ironing board and a television in the living room and bedroom.
The room was very clean and the chambermaids came round every day. They restocked the tea, coffee etc and always left clean towels. They were also happy to come back at a more convenient time if you were still in your room.
The hotel was in a perfect location, Madison Square Gardens is over the road, Macy's and other major stores are a couple of blocks away and so is the Empire State Building. We also took taxis to each end of the island and walked back to the hotel (which is roughly in the middle on Manhattan), this way we got to see more of Manhattan and did some shooping on the way.
There is a fire station underneath the hotel which can cause some noise, but nowhere in New York is quiet. We found that the noise didn't bother us and slept with the window open most nights.
The restaurant and bar that is connected to the hotel is also a place to visit if you don't feel like going too far one night. Although we didn't get chance to dine in the restaurant we found the bar staff very friendly and they made us feel very welcome. 
The hotel staff were very friendly and recommended places to eat, they also pre booked a taxi for us when it was time to leave as we needed a people carrier to transport us to the airport.
We have looked at other hotels we could possibly stay in when we return to New York, but due to having such a great time at the Southgate Tower and due to it being in such a prime location we have decided we wouldn't stay anywhere else. We would recommend this hotel to everyone.

title: “Way too expensive for what you get”
text: The location of the hotel is right on Capitol Hill, great for visiting all the sites, very close to Union Station for easy access to the metro. However, that's where the advantage of staying here stops. I can understand that in a prime area you have to pay more, but for what we got in return, this hotel definitely overcharges for what you get. We were clued in to the cleanliness of the room as we rode the elevator and walked the hallway to our room. The general impression was one of grubbiness. That may be okay in the public area, but you would expect a certain level of comfort and cleanliness in the room itself. Nope. Our shower had a used bar of soap with a hair on it--this definitely grossed us out and made us feel like the room was not cleaned very well. Towels were so hard that when you wiped your face, it actually scratched. We had to call down and wait for room slippers to be brought, and judging by the lack of cleanliness, we were not too crazy about walking on the carpet without slippers. The room size is pretty small, even by D.C. standards, and an odd configuration. You can hear a lot of room noise from next door and hallway noise. Room service was exhorbitant--$48.00 for a hamburger and salad anyone? Includes charges tacked on. I had no choice because it was late and I was hungry. Internet is available, for a fee--most boutique hotels I've stayed in offer free wireless. It seems that this hotel has gone downhill, from the previous reviews. We moved out as soon as we could and stayed at the Hyatt and got much better service, and a much cleaner room--for a third of the price!

title: “Very nice”
text: Loved the downtown Sheraton. Excellent location and great service by the staff. Room size and view was fantastic. Enjoyed both the room service (excellent presentation) and breakfast in the restaurant downstairs. The food was very good, while not being too pricey. Would definitely go back again.

title: “Nice little touches”
text: What is there to say about this Super 8 that hasn't already been said? All the positive reviews are right on the money. My husband and I just got back from an 8-night stay. Victor (the manager) was very nice and welcoming - he checked us in and immediately upgraded our room because we were staying so long. The suite was a good size with a flat screen TV, the bed was very comfortable and the pillow selection was unexpected but very nice. The room and the hotel itself were very clean, and the complimentary breakfast was really good (Texas shaped waffles, eggs, fruit, yogurt, cereals, etc.) and open until 10:00 am, which was nice for late risers like us. We took advantage of the B&B-type touches, which included lending of DVDs and books and the 6:00-9:00 pm dessert that was left in the lobby. The only negative is that there's really nothing right around the hotel, but it's close to a lot of roads and highways that can get you anywhere in Austin relatively quickly (I'd say a lot of options are in a 10-15 minute drive). For the price (we got a deal on the Super 8 website), you can't beat it.

title: “If visiting New York, consider Chelsea Pines Inn”
text:
This was my best stay ever in New York, where Accommodation is concerned. The staff was great and the service could not have been better. Maybe a stronger cup of coffee would have been good, but that is only because I have now lived for 10 years in Europe.
With the location so close to the 14th Street E station, and only a short hop away from the subway station on 7th Ave at 14th Street, I got around easily with public transportation. 
When I return to New York, I will stay with the Chelsea Pines Inn!
Patt Howard
Munich, Germany

title: “Adequate but past its prime”
text:
Rooms are small and a bit worn. For an airport hotel, however, it was reasonably quiet. The sleep number beds are awful -- glad I never bought one!
There was a huge line up at check out. But I am glad I waited -- there was a restaurant charge on the account that was not ours.

title: “You listen to toilets flushing all night long all over the hotel”
text: This location is ideal for MD Anderson patients however you will pay the price by listening to the toilets flushing all over the hotel. They sound like "bombs" going off all over the hotel. Additionally, management made no adjustment on my bill for the inconvenience for 1 night of no air conditioning out of 4 nights stayed. I've tried to call them and escalated the matter to the Manager Omar but he would not return my call. Bottom line.....don't stay here.

title: “Perfect ending”
text: We have travelled a lot over the past 7 years and this has got to be one of two spectacular hotels we have ever stayed in by far. The staff were all very helpful and friendly. It really was the perfect ending to our holiday..

title: “Very courteous staff and wonderful gardens”
text:
We were here to attend a conference for four days. My colleague has trouble walking and the staff bent over backward to accomodate her (AJ and other bell men). They were always on hand within 5 minutes or less to pick her up at the door of our room and take her around the resort, to the nearby shopping center, or even down into Old Town San Diego. They were courteous to the max and made us feel very spoiled.
I also had my hair cut in the salon and got a new style from Patti, which I like very much. There was another Pati who served us lunch at the Trellis restaurant who was very gracious.
I really like the gardens with the variety of roses, foxgloves, etc....beautiful flowers and plants throughout the site.

title: “Our Recent Stay At An Amazing Hotel”
text: My wife and I recently stayed at the Tryp Hotel. When we checked in we were immediately taken to our beautiful, modern room where the beds were amazingly comfortable, the bathroom spacious and a great flat screen TV. Before dinner, we had their wonderful martinis and a great selection of Tapas. The next morning we enjoyed a delicious buffet breakfast. All of the staff were well trained and very courteous. The parking garage was right across the street. My wife and I both agreed that from this point forward, this is our hotel of choice in New York City. Roger and Nancy L.

title: “Clean, quiet, close to shopping, wonderful service!”
text:
My daughter and I were in Indy for a volleyball tournament. The front desk made sure we knew of a gathering spot for the girls to mingle during quiet time. The inn was in a great location for the fair grounds, where the girls played, shopping, drug store, variety of places to eat in the area...
Clean, quiet, will be back!

title: “The new hot spot”
text:
Great location, artisticly designed, great food, great location and gettin better by the minute, and supperior rooms. I recomend u go there (it's the new hot spot ).If you dont go then your missing out on a supperior experience in an extrordinarily new hotel with its own. I love it.
Sammy

title: “Great location, Great Value”
text:
I stayed at the Dylan for 3 nights over Memorial Day weekend, my parents stayed for 4 nights. We had a queen room and a King room. Given prior comments I was expecting the staff to be less than friendly or accommodating but found them just the opposite. They let me check in at 10:30 a.m. , get a late check out on departure, answered numerous tourism questions patiently for my parents, greeted us on the elevators and even went out of their way to get taxis for us around the corner. And the rate we got for NY was pretty darn good ($219/night). 
Given it is NYC the rooms were a decent size, you could walk freely around the beds and there was room to keep luggage stacked around if you so desired. Prior reviews on low lighting is true, more for style than illumination and the ceilings are enormously high so the light does get a little lost. Television reception was a problem in the fourth floor room but not in the 10th floor room. Hallways were not air conditioned so prior reviews were on the money there also and it was a warm weekend, the wait wasn't bad though.
The location 1 block from Grand Central was great for all our sight-seeing and there was even a bonus street festival on madison Ave. around the corner on the day we left.
I was very pleased with our choice, the hotel was comfortable, quiet, and a good value.

title: “Spg platinum member review”
text: There was no room upgrade. The hotel is run down with paint coming off the wall. They are trying to fix up the property, during our stay the flooring was removed and relpaced. It is an old hotel in a cool,part of the city. As a platinum member I will not return.

title: “A "find" in a city of expensive hotels”
text: We just spent the weekend in this unassuming Courtyard Marriott and were very pleasantly surprised. The hotel has a great location, near Central Park, shopping and dining and for $188 a night with breakfast on a AAA rate was really a bargain in Manhattan. Our room was up on the top (31st) floor and was large and clean with two comfortable queen beds ( also something unusual in NYC). Actually, the room would have slept 6 with the pull out sofa. Our view was priceless. We overlooked the Chrysler Building and the city itself and it was so breathtaking that we kept our curtains open at night! Breakfast was delicious and was included in our rate. Do not hesitate. This is really a find in NYC and we will return.

title: “will stay again”
text:
Wonderful room. location was perfectly in the middle of everything and even has a connection to metro. Will definitely stay again.
We did have travel with their costumer service but received an email with apologies which was good en for me

title: “Unique Great Hotel. Great Fun Location”
text:
I live in San Diego so I don't usually stay in San Diego hotels. However, I had the opportunity to view the Keatings rooms when they first opened and I always wanted to pay a visit. Last Friday, my wife and I spent the night at the Keating and had dinner at The Merk (The Keating's restauraunt). The restaurant was fantastic!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
