The hotel was also great. I won't try to describe the rooms. Look at the pictures online at the Keating's website. The rooms are different that any other hotel I have ever seen. There are only 35 rooms in the hotel. The staff knows their guests and treated us very well.
The locatioin in the heart of the Gaslamp was perfect. I know some people have complained of street noise. We did not have any problems with noise.
The next time we need a getaway from the kids, we will return to The Keating.

title: “Good Hotel”
text: I was reasonably happy with this hotel. The location was excellent and the price was OK. Service and cleanliness were generally OK. We had two bedrooms and the toilet in one was not great; prone to backing up and not flushing properly. Staying in New York in January, there was an obvious worry about the cold. However, the opposite problem was apparent. The rooms were way too hot. We had the windows open while the outside temperature was below freezing and the rooms were still hot.

title: “Excellent as usual”
text: We stayed here in route to Florida for spring break. This hotel continues to be an exceptional value. We are a family of 5 and the room layout is a wonderful treat as we usually have to get two adjoining rooms to accommodate our family.

title: “You get what you pay for!”
text:
Visited the Hotel Pennsylvania in November 2007 for a four night girls holiday. The trip was booked in March 2007 by one of my friends and didn't have any input in the choice of hotel until after it was booked. As soon as I had confirmation of the hotel I checked it out on Trip Advisor and was quite concerned about the trip after reading many of the reviews posted. With that in mind I advised my travelling colleagues not to expect too much and steeled myself for an "interesting" stay.
Upon arrival (1pm) it was just as had been previously described, long queue to check in and we couldn't get into all of our rooms until 3pm. However one of the rooms had been cleaned and we managed to dump our bags and went for a beer until we could all check in - which was a help as we were pretty bushed after a 6am check-in.
We had requested three rooms next to each other, however one of the rooms was on a different floor and the two on the same floor were on different corridors. Although it would've been nice to stay together it didn't detract from the holiday.
On intial inspection the room was much better than I was aniticipating (!) although it was VERY worn - especially the bathroom. The enamel had come off the bath in many places and was rusting - you wouldn't want a bath! And at one point I thought I was going to pull the shower taps off the wall as they were so difficult to operate! 
However, there was plenty of hot water (once you got the temperature sorted), the towels and bedlinen were clean (bleached to within an inch of their lives), and the HUGE telly was great for catching the weather forecast.
The room was warm and functional, after all it was just a place to sleep - you don't come to NY to spend all your time in your hotel room. There wasn't any view, but we were able to open the window so that we could let fresh air in during the night otherwise you stood a chance of roasting to death! 
A kettle and cups would've been nice, even if you had to purchase your own tea/milk etc, not being able to have a brew first thing in the morning was a bit of a downer.
The only thing that really bugged me was the noise that came though the internal adjoining door - you can hear everything (especially when the occupant of next door tried to come into our room at 3am on several occasions!) and the noise that came through the main room door from the corridor outside.
As a pretty experienced independent traveller I would rate it as a glorified hostel with your own bathroom, which is fine if you are used to travelling like that. Some of my travelling companions were a little disappointed, however for the money we paid (£400 for flight & hotel) it really could've been much worse!
The politest people I met all trip were the guys in the basement of the hotel controlling the left luggage - they were fantastic - even though we asked to add extra bags and kept going back to put things in the bags they didn't ask for any extra money - they were the only people worth tipping the whole trip!
The location is AMAZING, for the money you really couldn't pick a better spot. Ten minute walk to Times Square / Empire State Building and access to the Metro (subway) on the corner or across the road in Madison Square Gardens. I would recommend using the Metro to wizz around - very clean, efficient and cheap and really, really easy to use in Manhattan. As a lone female traveller I wouldn't be concerned with using the Metro.
Avoid "Fat Annie's Truck Stop" diner next to the posh irish bar on 33rd street - a COMPLETE RIP-OFF! It doesn't matter how tired you are DON'T GO THERE!
Also consider taking the AirTrain back to JFK $13 (if your luggage permits!), we had a limo inbound and it took 45 minutes from airport to hotel. Outbound back to the airport it took 2 hours and we weren't even in rush hour, the unneccessary stress of checking in an hour late wasn't worth a limo trip even though it was only $20 each (7 people).

title: “Great Hotel and Great Employees”
text: Great Hotel and Great Employees. They do NOT charge for parking like the Doubletree downtown. Clean rooms and not overpriced.

title: “Special Thanks to Hotel Associates”
text:
To the staff of The Westin Hotel at Los Angeles Airport.
I have had an opportunity to stay at your hotel on several business trips and the staff has been very professional and supportive in accommodating our needs.
I would like to personally thank Sangeetha, the associate who assisted with my check-in. Great job at anticipating the needs of your guest. You deserve an award for your customer care.

title: “Very comfortable hotel with friendly and helpful staff”
text:
I stayed here for 2 nights on a business trip and my room was very clean and comfortable. Hearing about the recent problem with many NYC hotels and bed bugs, I made sure to check very thoroughly and was happy to see NO signs of them here! As is typical in NYC, the room was "small" compared to rooms in other parts of the country, but I've stayed in this city before and knew what to expect. 
The staff was very friendly and always there to help with any request - I saw them ask quite a few guests who were on their way out the door if there was anything they could help with, like directions or suggestions, without even being asked first. They also managed to get me a cab to JFK on a Friday night during rush hour, which was a small miracle!
Nice location here, too - 1 block from Times Square, 15 seconds to 5th avenue, and subway stations closeby to get you anywhere in Manhattan or beyond. 
Free internet in the room was also a great bonus!

title: “Historic Building and Great Location”
text: My wife and I really enjoyed our stay at this hotel. It is a very nice and clean boutique hotel with spiral staircases and good breakfast bar. It is very close to the Symphony as well as tons of dining on Charles street. We had a very positive experience.

title: “No legendary Four Seasons standards, but overall a good stay”
text:
I was in Chicago with my sibling for 3 nights in September. The hotel is located on the Magnificent Mile itself, about a 45 minute cab ride costing about US$40 from O'Hare International Airport. Upon arrival, check in at the front desk was without incidence, and we were offered an upgrade to an Executive Suite, and also given a discount card for use at Bloomingdales which is located below the hotel.
Our room was very nice, very spacious, clean and elegantly decorated. Being on such a high floor, it afforded great views of the beautiful city of Chicago. The night view is particularly breathtaking. Very spacious seating area with writing desk and chair, and a separate bedroom. Despite the little notecard by the bedside warning of noise at night and provision of earplugs, which was a nice touch, the room was very well insulated, and I had a very good nights' sleep. The bed was, needless to say, very comfortable.
The hotel is situated in a very convenient location, lots of shopping and great restaurants all around the hotel. We had no lack of choices for brunch over the weekend.
The only issue that prevents me from giving this hotel a higher rating, is due to the lack of amenities that I have come to expect of a hotel like Four Seasons. This is the first Four Seasons hotel I have stayed in that did not provide for tea/coffee making facilities. Bottled water was only provided at night. 
Toiletries provided in the bathroom was the most puzzling. There was only one tiny travel size bottle of each of the shampoo, conditioner, shower gel and body lotion provided. There was no dental kit, not even sanitary bags in the bathroom. We assumed the toiletries will be replenished the next day, between the 2 of us, it wasn't difficult to use up most of the toiletries provided, but it was not. We requested for extra bottles of shampoo and conditioner to be sent up to our rooms, but had to repeat our request twice before we were given an extra set of toiletries. 
Turn down service was not consistent. Glasses we have used in the day were taken away, but were not replaced. One night we had the white floor mat laid out on the bedside with slippers placed just so, on another night, this was omitted altogether.
Overall however, service cannot be faulted and I would still recommend this hotel. Front desk and concierge service were very helpful on all counts, giving directions, maps, restaurant recommendations, right down to the friendly porters and doormen. It's just that in comparison to other Four Seasons hotels, I found this one to be slightly lacking.

title: “Serves the purpose for an early morning flight!”
text: We stayed here the night before a 7:30am flight to Los Angeles. Got dropped off by a family members and checked in around 9pm the night before without any problem. The room was tiny, a bit shabby, but clean. The bathroom was clean as well and water pressure just fine. We slept well, no problems with noise, bugs, anything at all. Got up early, grabbed some of the continental breakfast bagels and juice, and took advantage of the free airport shuttle. This place is perfect for a quick overnight like this near the airport. What else could you need for $60 (or expect for that matter!) I'd go back if another early flight was in my future!

title: “Excellent Hotel, Great Location”
text: I had a very enjoyable stay here this past week. Rooms were spotless and service was second to none. Room price was a little high but you get every penny of what you pay for. I will stay here every time I visit Boston.

title: “Quiet Hotel in Good Location”
text:
Just stayed here for the second time after getting a great rate online. Stayed alone but was given a room with two doubles. It was a small room with a view of a brick wall which made the room dark but otherwise it was clean , fresh , well decorated and the beds are very comfortable. The bar/room service is overpriced and with so many diners nearby save your money.
The location is the best selling point. It's central yet on a quiet street so there's no noise and it's easy to forget you're in the city so you'll have no problems if you're a light sleeper. I also heard no noise from the corridor/ neighbouring rooms.
The only caveat I'll give is to Irish visitors: It is not as nice as we are led to believe! Unless you're in the Gerry Ryan suite it is nothing to write home about and only choose if you get a good deal. I know people who have paid 2,000 plus for 4 or 5 nights and it is not worth it!

title: “Perfect location, great stay”
text:
The hotel is in what I feel is the perfect location to explore San Francisco. It's a 5 minute walk or less to the Ferry Building, BART, Busses and Cable Car stop. Downtown shopping, museums and restaurants are easily accessed via a "flat" walk or public transportation. This is also true for walking to North Beach and Fishermans Wharf and the assorted Piers. It's a bit of a walk (less than 1 1/2 miles) to these areas but great if the weather permits and you're up for it.
Regarding the hotel itself we were very pleased. We got a great rate ($130.00/night) on Hotwire and were placed in what many have referred to as the "older" section of the hotel on the 9th floor. The rooms were large, clean and well maintained. The bathroom is fairly small and the amenities fairly limited but this is a solid 4 Star property. Check-in could not have been easier. We actually arrived at 12:30 pm and were immediately assigned a room. The whole process took about 5 minutes or less. Every staff person we came into contact with treated us with respect and kindness. We would unhesitatingly recommend this hotel and the area it is located in. One final note: Yes the area has its complement of homeless, urban "character" types but at no time did we feel unsafe. These types of individuals are found in every city I have ever visited. The noise factor also wasn't a problem. It's there but not terribly bothersome.

title: “Great Hotel worth a visit”
text: Great hotel, good location next to staples centre, Good rooms, Cant fault it.

title: “nothing not to like”
text: just completed a week's stay and couldn't have asked for a greater place to be for a leisurely vacation--in the heart of gaslamp district, walking distance to trolleys, buses, petco park, convention center, shopping center, seaport village, city center, great restaurants,(one on premises), streets safe for walking--- great roof-top area to read or sun, quiet rooms, marbled stairway, plush carpeted, chandeliered, friendly service throughout, airport pick-up, morning papers--actually this sounds like an ad--well, it could be--and , oh, yes, the rooms have got to be some of the most reasonable of any of the gaslamp hotels--it will always be my spot in san diego

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Okay, let me just say my husband and I stayed at the Tremont during Christmas. We had a great experience, will DEFINITELY be back very soon. Not sure what some of the negative reviews mean.....please do not base your decision on the negativity of some people.

title: “Above-Average Doubletree Near Seattle Airport”
text:
Over the past month I’ve stayed twice at the Doubletree Seattle Airport and was happy with both stays. The hotel seemed large for a Doubletree, but not overwhelmingly so. Staff were helpful and pleasant. It’s certainly a step above other Doubletrees I’ve stayed at recently. The rooms are sufficiently roomy and were clean and well-kept. This is the first hotel I’ve stayed at for a long while where there was actually a light over the bathtub/shower: it’s a nice touch, since so often the curtain blocks the light and makes it dark in the shower.
The convenience to the airport cannot be overstated: if the weather is nice and you’re up for it, it’s just a quick ten-minute walk from door-to-door. Of course there’s a shuttle that runs regularly but being able to walk to the airport is nice if you don’t want to walk or would like some fresh air before your flight. You can see the hotel from the tarmac and, if you get a room facing in that direction, you can see the tarmac and terminal from the hotel.
As Hilton Diamond I wasn’t upgraded either time, but, then again, I never am at any Hilton Family property. 
This is a good place to stay if convenience to Sea-Tac is important to you and also if you need to be in that part of the Seattle area.

title: “Very good - Would definitely stay again”
text:
Booked into the MaVe for two nights. Excellant service, the staff went out of their way to be helpful and gave advice on local sights/restaurants etc..
The room was stylish and fitted out with LCD tv and ipod doc although I was out most of the time so had no need to us them. Only criticism of the room would be that it was not particularly large but I don't think many NY hotel rooms are and this is probably nit picking.
The breakfast was coffee and pastries of which there were plenty and thay were fresh both mornings I was there.
As regards sightseeing the location of the hotel is ideal. I walked to it from Penn Station with a large roller case in approx 15 mins. Its not that strenuous and its all on the flat. The empire state building is a short walk away and the Flatiron building is very close.
I had a great stay here and after searching for ages I think as other reviews have suggested this hotel compared to others locally will exceed your expectations of a reasonable city boutique hotel.

title: “Loved It!”
text:
The location of the Yotel is perfect. It's three blocks from Time Square and steps away from restaurants galore (Hell's Kitchen is on the doorstep). Broadway theatre venues are also basically around the corner. It's close to the action, but far enough away that you are not bombarded by noise like you would be if you were in Time Square. There is a Food Emporium grocery store right across the street (great for picking up fresh fruit for the room, as well as drinks). There is also a large drug store on the other side of the street. 
As for the hotel staff, the best staff are the front-line guys who welcome you outside and in the lobby. Check-in is automated (no front counter staff - just a funky computer screen), so anticipating some less than savvy clientele, the front-line guys are right there to help computer-phobics! For all others, the process is uncomplicated and fast. Once you check in you enter the elevator and go to the fourth floor - interestingly named "mission control". The front counter staff were o.k. - sort of your standard front counter staff you find at any hotel - the guys at the entrance were much better! Overall however, everyone was pleasant and made sure we were well looked after. 
The room was awesome. My 13-year-old daughter and I stayed in one room. The bed is a futon that folds down into a bed at the push of a button. The room is entirely wired for laptops, i-pods, etc. and had a a flat screen tv in front of the bed, so my daughter was kept happy. The rooms are small but don't feel like it because they are designed with every detail in mind - think of an upscaled version of an IKEA room. The shower was beautiful. The only minor fault was the bed was somewhat hard for my taste, but after hard days of shopping, eating and sight-seeing in New York City I could sleep on the floor!
The continental breakfast was fine. They served good hot coffee and great tea (I'm a tea drinker so I appreciated a decent cup of tea). The muffins were delicious. There was a cost for juice, fresh fruit, etc. but that wasn't an issue because we bought ours across the street. On each floor there is a "galley" that houses a water and ice machine (we refilled our water bottles there each day), as well as a great coffee/mocha/cappachino machine (free of charge) for a pick-me up during the day. They also provided cups for drinking in the room. There was also a fridge and microwave in the galley. Very convenient. We didn't try the breakfast restaurant or the Japanese restaurant, nor the outdoor roof patio (beautiful but it was too hot!). 
When it was time to check out we had time to kill prior to flying home. Opposite the computer screens on the ground floor is the YOBOT - a giant computerized arm that stores luggage in large compartments in the wall (kind of like a bee hive). Everyone stands around taking video and pictures of it. It's fun! We had no problem accessing the YOBOT or our luggage at the end of the day. The young man outside found us a taxi on a Friday evening during rush hour - we were most appreciative. 
All in all, a great brand-new hotel (you can still smell the new paint) that is spotless. I would go back in a heartbeat. The only problem is, we booked the YOTEL at a special grand opening rate of $149 a night. Now the same room is almost $400! Unfortunately it's out of our price range so we can't go back. For those of you that can afford it, definitely don't hesitate in booking a room.

title: “Great location”
text: My husband, daughter and I stayed last Nov & had a great time. Everyone was very helpful & friendly & the location was close to EVERYTHING. My husband was on crutches so having a subway station and cabs right outside our door was wonderful. The suite was very comfortable and clean and great to come back to after a big day walking or touring NYC. Would defiantly stay here again!

title: “Great Price, But, You Get What You Pay For”
text:
This was our Spring Break trip 2011, we have family in Peoria, AZ, so this hotel was close to where we needed to be. We had an excellent weekly rate and couldn't pass it up. Upon reading the reviews, we thought this was a great choice. They have a pool and hot tub which our young daughter was interested in. 
We had a long flight from St. Louis to LA, then to Phoenix. It was a tiring day because we have to drive 3 hours to St. Louis, then a four-hour flight to LA then another nearly hour-long flight to Phoenix. When we arrived in Phoenix, one of our bags was missing, so we had to wait to deal with that, then wait for a rental car. We finally arrived at the hotel after 10 PM, which would be midnight Central Time, our key did not work, had to go to the office and get another one. While waiting outside for my husband I noticed the paint was chipping on the building and it was very dated. It was not a good first impression. Then we entered the room and smelled strongly of smoke--it was a non-smoking room. I was not pleased with that at all. Really, I only noticed the smell the first night.
After the first night, things were better. The hotel staff was very friendly and accomodating. They had our bag from the airport the next morning. My daughter loved this hotel, especially the large pool and hot tub. The pool area is very nice, and there is a covered patio to eat breakfast outside. The free breakfast is small, they have yogurt, fruit, cereal and make you own waffles. It got very crowded in there each day. 
The beds were small, but comfortable. The room was quiet and the service was great. They could just use an update. I'm sure this was a very nice hotel 20 yars ago.

title: “The Best”
text: My husband and I have been spoiled. Once you stay at this hotel nothing will ever compare to your experience afterwards. My husband and I were married here and just like our stays it was beyond our expectations. The service is incomparable. We have been 4 times and every time we are there we are never disappointed.

title: “Perfect location :-)”
text:
First time in new York, hotel was in great location, and staff was amazing!
Ricky at front desk was terrific.

title: “value for money stay”
text:
My third stay in new york and this hotel was the best as far as value was concerned. Rooms are small but as expected. Given early check in at 11am. Front desk staff were excellent and heeded to my request for a third floor room. Breakfast was enjoyable and we were always there at 7:30am when it was always quite. Good location with easy walk to all attractions.
For USD200.00 per night for a family of 4 including brealfast exceeded my expectations for a New York Hotel!!
Remember you just need to plan to beat the crowds at breakfast and request a lower floor room..Therefore book early and youll also get the best rate!!

title: “Great location...friendly staff...so-so room”
text:
For visiting the area you can't beat their location; walking distance to the convention center and the Padres baseball stadium. 
Positives: Staff was friendly; some of the best views of the city skyline and Coronado Island. Hotel is adjacent to Seaport Village.
Negatives: As others have noted, the hotel looks dated. Carpet in our room was warped and worn. Coffee shop hours were lacking; offerings were mediocre at best and overpriced. The people working were polite though.
Overall: Everyone we ran into was polite, but the hotel is dated.

title: “Best of Seattle”
text:
Stayed at Inn at the Market November 2011 for a Seattle Seahawks game. Spent 3 nights. Was truly the best location and best hotel I've stayed at in Seattle. Literally steps from Pike Place market make it perfect for early morning coffees overlooking the Sound. Was cold when we were there, so the deck you could sit on overlooking the Sound wasn't used, but its views were excellent. Valet parking was fast and efficient as well. Rooms were modern and clean as well. Great to be right on Post Alley as well and steps from Kells Irish Pub. Go there for great local bands. 
Also, we paid for the cheaper rooms and still had a great view of the Sound. Not sure why I'd pay more, but I'm sure it would be worth it.
All in all, perfect hotel, perfect location.

title: “Great value”
text:
I got an incredible rate for a room here by using choiceprivileges.com. Even if I had paid the full amount ($60/night), I would have been happy here. The property lives up to its name "Comfort." 
The bathroom came with shampoo, conditioner, and lotion. It had 4 large towels, some wash cloths, and 4 hand towels. My bath and shower were pleasant.
My room had a clock radio, fridge, and microwave. In the room, I had a desk with a lamp that provides good light; the room is well lit. The flat-screen TV provided cable channels in Spanish and English. The room was clean. The heater worked when I turned up the temperature on the thermostat high enough.
Breakfast starts at 6 a.m., which is good for people who must leave early.

title: “Michael - Asst Mgr - Rocks”
text: At 1:30 AM - Michael - the Asst Mgr - accommodated my son and mom after they missed a flight at JFK. He was quick, efficient and very helpful - after other nearby hotels were not. THank you MICHAEL - it was much appreciated. We will highly recommend your hotel.

title: “Still the BEST of San Diego”
text: Stayed one week at Crystal Pier. Love the location, the cottages and the ambiance of everything. Pricey, but well worth it. Save $$$ by BBQ'ing on your patio and fixing Bfast in the Cottage. Love the fact that they close the pier after sunset and open around 8 a.m. Save all year for this one week of enjoyment.

title: “great hotel”
text: A great hotel, clean with helpful staff. Well situated for Time Sqaure and Central park as well as close to the subway. When we were staying there was some road works outside the front so was a bit noisy from about 7am as well as some traffic noise. Would suggest trying to get a rear room if posible.

title: “Steven Colbert Stayed Here, Too!!”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Fairmont last October to attend the Rally To Restore Sanity, and, to my surprise and pleasure, were joined by Steven Colbert and his entourage! (a little shorter than I would have expected...)
Nothing undersized about the hotel, however. A major renovation is winding down, but all the public spaces have been completed and one would never know the work was going on. The staff is young, vibrant and very attentive --- not a single stuffed shirt. Our room was well-appointed, bed was very comfortable (firm mattress) and the down comforter and bathrobes made us feel very special. Recommend getting a room facing the inner courtyard, especially on the lower floors. We only dined for breakfast, which was slightly above average (they do offer a unattended daily breakfast buffet).
A short walk from the hotel to Georgetown for shopping and eating, and a slightly longer walk to the Metro station for sightseeing. A little out of the way for heavy sightseeing (the Mall is six or seven stops away on the Metro), but perfect for a leisurely DC visit that includes a lot of time in Georgetown.

title: “Could be a 100% Class Act with Better Room/Facilities Maintenance”
text: This hotel focuses on convention/leisure activities rather than business -- any hotel that still charges for internet access clearly doesn't cater to business travelers! So, keep that in mind in selecting this hotel. The beautiful lobby, excellent convention halls, top-notch gym/pool facility and overall old-world charm certainly play to convention/leisure travel. The beds (my room had two doubles) were absolutely comfortable with great pillows. A/C worked perfectly. Room was very quiet. Plenty of elevators so little waiting. Very friendly staff and great cleaning service. Decent selection of TV channels and plenty of paid TV options. // So, what's the problem? Well, my room suffered from shoddy maintenance issues: The bathtub dripped (and I don't mean just a little); the sink faucet was coming loose; the cable to the TV kept the curtains from closing properly; the TV remote was missing upon arrival; the clock was set too fast (and can't be reset by you -- I had to call an engineer). The gym's Precor/Icarian equipment is some of the best, but you'll find minor maintenance issues such as broken pins. I heard other stories of similar minor maintenance issues going unfixed in other rooms. This seems to bear out my experience with other Hilton properties. This is a shame because this Hotel has so much going for it, including a convenient location with very good access to Chicago's subway system (the El), many near-by tourist destinations and good convention and local food choices.

title: “Great place, well taken care of.”
text: Went last month with my wife to see a show and enjoy some fine dining. Colin and the staff took great care of us and made some great recommendations during our stay. Our room was clean and a generous size considering some of the other places i have stayed in NYC. For the price there is not a better deal in the city -will definitely being going back soon.

title: “VALUE FOR MONEY”
text: I stayed in The New Yorker for one week with my 12yr old neice.Although i had been recommended to stay in this hotel it certainly lived to my expectations.The room was clean and beds very comfortable. Bathroom is reasonable size with bath/shower.The Tick Tock diner was great to use for breakfast and evening meals good food and lovely service from the staff.Location is great and 2 minutes walk to Penn station subway and all other amenities.Staff are polite and helpful at check in desk.Excellent security in the hotel.

title: “Great hotel with a great location at a very affordable rate”
text: This is a great hotel located about 15 minutes walking time from the White House and National Mall. It was clean and comfortable and the staff were some of the friendliest I have encountered. I searched the area and this was by far the most affordable given its proximity to the museums and monuments. The resturant was good and kids under 12 eat free. We had a great experience and will be back.

title: “Lynn from Baltimore”
text: Stayed for weekend family gathering with reservations made in advance. Friendly greeting and accommodations made in a timely manner. We also had excellent service provided from two very warm and friendly employees, Rosland and Henry. After inquiring, they also recommended a dinner menu that was excellent. We had a great dining experience, the food was warm, seasoned appropriately and the meats were very fresh. The suites were large, clean, had the best sleeping mattresses and a nice balcony view! Enjoyed our stay and the friendly services provided throughout our weekend. Would recommend and would gladly stay here again!

title: “Our stay in New York”
text: We stayed in The Hotel Deauville, New York on 24th September 2007 for 3 nights. It is a 2 star hotel, and although it was booked through a travel agent, I have to say that I was a little nervous about what it was going to be like. I needn't have worried. As we walked through the door we were made welcome by a very nice lady at reception, and were booked in without any problems. We were then taken up to our room in a nice old fashioned lift. We opened the room door and found the room to be a good size, it was clean, we had our own bathroom, but the furniture was rather dated, but again clean. There was no kettle or cups in the room, so as we went out to explore, we asked for a kettle and by the time we got back to the room, a kettle and mugs were there. The only reason I have not given it an excellent mark is because there was no view, but that does not take away from the fact that the hotel was good value,clean and every member of staff we met were friendly and helpful. We would recommed this hotel to anyone and would stay there again if we go back to New York

title: “Flipping annoying lifts”
text: This is a pretty good hotel. Excellent location for the financial district, comfortable & clean rooms (although they're pretty small) and a pretty decent, but small, gym. I have two main issues with this hotel - the breakfast is distinctly average and there are not enough lifts for the number of floors/rooms. You may end up waiting 10+ minutes in the morning, or walking down 20-30 floor... Having said that, I'll probably stay there when I'm next in NYC for the points!

title: “Really great value for money”
text: This hotel is in a really good spot for the city, and is right on the main street where the trolleys run between the Castro and Fisherman's Wharf. Value for money was exceptional, especially if you mention the 'pay now' discount' when you can get a 20 percent discount when you book. I ended up getting the discount, and not even paying until I checked out anyway. The room was smaller than it looks on the website, but is very clean, with a nice bathroom. There's nothing else which compares to it in the city in this price range. It was a non smoking room, but we ended up buying scented candles and Febreze to get rid of the smoky smell. The decor was also a bit dated, and could do with renewing, but no major complaints there. There is a free breakfast buffet each morning in the lobby, with coffee, orange juice, cereal, toast, fruit and pastries. It does get busy though so don't leave it too late. The service is good, and the guy who seems to live and work there cannot do enough to help, even though his English isn't so good. Overall, a perfect no-frills option in the city. I'd definitely go back.

title: “Great Location for a short stay”
text: We just stayed 2 nights, one full day in San Francisco and the location was perfect. We were able to walk to everything we wanted to see. The room it self was very nice, clean and well decorated though small. While we told that the windows were able to keep out the street noise the sound of garbage trucks early in the morning did wake both my husband and I up. The location, with all the shopping, restaurants and sight seeing, tours, cable cars right out side the door more then made up for in on a short stay such as ours. Oh, and it was our first time paying for valet sercive. Found it a bit much at $36 a night, not to mention the tipping. We would look around for somewhere different next time just because of that.

title: “Lives up to the Ritz-Carlton name”
text:
We stayed one night in this hotel and really enjoyed it. The service was outstanding, the rooms comfortable, the bathroom was one of the best I've seen in a hotel, and the gym was great. Although not cheep, we were able to get a second companion room for some friends for $100. From what I understand it is a special that they have based on availability and an existing reservation. Two rooms on the 26th floor for $400 is not bad in a 5 star hotel.
There is a bell tower nearby that bothered my partner, but I didn't notice enough to even say if the bell chimed at during the night or not.
We ordered room service for breakfast and the meal was fantastic, but not cheap. Well worth it for a romantic morning in bed though.

title: “positioning in the city - lokalizacja”
text:
Hotel fantastycznie położony, w samym centrum około 50 metrów od Times Square. Trudno mi sobie wyobrazić, żeby mógł być zlokalizowany lepiej.
The hotel is placed in the best possible place in Manhatan. Very close to Times Square appr 50 m. so in the very center of the whole life which is happening there. Service very good, infrastructure acceptable.

title: “Dawn Evans rocks!”
text: My colleague and I stayed at the W last week and had a great stay. Beyond the hotel being trendy and centrally located, the service was great - especially Dawn Evans. She was so warm and friendly. Both mornings at breakfast she checked in on me to ensure I had everything I needed. Her fun and welcoming demeanor made my stay that much more enjoyable.

title: “Fits the bill (even though the bill is pretty high)”
text: The hotel was very good location and amenities were great for family of three. We were able to walk to subway, shows, and even some of the attractions such as top of the rock, wax museum etc. check in was very organised and check out was very easy if they provide the account on the television menu to approve so no lines. Everyone at the hotel without exception was polite and helpful. Free internet is on the lobby floor so we found it quite relaxing to do light supper in the bar and trawl our emails and internet after a big day of touring was a good end to the day. Its entrance is covered so no weather problems, and the taxis are easy to get from the entrance. Business centre has free internet for printing boarding passes but you pay for everything else. Overall it is costly but we would pay again as everything worked for us

title: “Nostalgic”
text:
I have read some of the recent reviews fo the Canterbury and I am happy to say we did not have any of the bad experiences of others. My husband and I were looking for a location to spend an overnight stay for our anniversary. The best word I could use to describe the hotel is nostalgic. The décor was absolutely beautiful! If you are looking for a place with “old school” charm, this is it. We were greeted by a friendly and extremely helpful bell hop that assisted us not only with the valet parking but also getting our ice for the room. Everyone was extremely pleasant and helpful. Note: They do not have an ironing board or iron in the room; however, housekeeping with provide you with both and they are very quick.
Our room was just the right size for us and the king bed was very comfortable. The nostalgia is evident down to the gold plated fixtures in bathroom and throughout the hotel. The negative side was that the water pressure in the shower was low and it took about 10 for the water to get warm for the shower. Additionally, the carpet in the room had a warn spot (about the size of a quarter).
It is located in the heart of downtown and we had a very nice view of Lucas Oil Stadium. We were within walking distance to food and entertainment. It was a wonderful evening getaway and we will definitely return.

title: “You get wha you pay for / great location / great staff terrible old rooms”
text:
Locatio is a 10 / staff is a 10 / rooms are terrible / need renovation. Beds ar comfortable baths have had a superficial renovation.
Stay here and be ok / spend 10 or 20 more a night and be wowed at many others. = this is Not a 4 star hotel

title: “Walking in Memphis”
text: Great hotel, couldn't fault it. Our room looked out to the Mississippi river. It's in a quiet but very safe neighbourhood but it is easy to get to Beale street and other downtown locations, it's a 10 min walk to the main street trolley and we paid 9 dollars for taxi back. Downtown memphis is quite rundown so this hotel is a good choice to stay.

title: “Great location and courteous front desk”
text: We were in NY for more than a week and found our stay in Park Central New York very comfortable and neat and clean and the location was great and , Drita the front desk manager was very helpful and courteous .

title: “Great hotel in an excellent location”
text: We came into Chicago via the South Shore Line and this was just a short walk away. We were more than pleasantly surprised by the spacious lobby, the friendly reception from both the bell staff and front desk. Our room was quite large as was the bathroom. We have no complaints.

title: “Poor service, ok rooms”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel 3 times (to get Priority Club points) and each time my experiences were consistent, so think this review is representative of what you can expect at this hotel.
This hotel looks fancy from the outside -- the entrance and lobby are very nice -- but the rooms are nothing special. The bed is comfortable, but the covers on it are so thin that you feel like you're sleeping under a sheet. There is very minimal counter space in the bathroom -- you get two tiny shelves, which are located precariously above the toilet, so you have to take care not to let your personal items fall into the loo. There is an old tube TV made by Zenith (do they still make TVs?) in the room. In most of the nicer hotels these days, you get a flat screen. And this hotel charges $13 per day for *wired* internet. There is no wireless internet in the lobby and, I was informed, there is a half-hour limit on the time that you can use the wireless in the lobby -- why? Does the hotel not want their guests to be comfortable? 
This brings me to my next point -- customer service. It's okay, maybe what I'd expect from a Motel 6. For example, on one occasion, I stayed at this hotel and was in a rush when I left, so I did not have time to get a copy of my final bill. Had to call this hotel repeatedly (4 times) to get them to email me the bill. They finally did. That's crappy service. And on my most recent stay on 5/6/10, when I went to fill my ice bucket, the ice machine on my floor was empty. I called the "instant service" line at 11:45 p.m. to see if ice could be delivered to my room. I was told by the female desk clerk that "room service is closed." She offered no solution. I asked her how I could get ice in my room, and she told me that I could go to the next floor up to get ice. So I'm supposed to wander all over your hotel because you don't keep your ice machines filled? Sounds very "Motel 6" to me.
On the plus side, I have to credit the hotel for offering healthy options on the breakfast and dinner menus. Also, the equipment in the fitness center was good -- but there is no water fountain/dispenser, so you should bring your own.
I come to NYC often and, all in all, it is hard to pass on a hotel when I can earn points on a trip. However, I think I'm going to stay elsewhere next time I'm in NYC.

title: “Good hotel with small cut backs”
text:
Wee stayed for two nights at TheWestin Copley Place. The hotel has a great location and we were lucky to get a corner room with view to back bay and eastward. I cannot really complain about anything. The room was great, the bar was well equipped and very friendly personnel. We used the good concierge service, too. My average rating is just caused by the high room rates that are asking for. This is even above 5 star hotels in NYC!
I would only recommend to stay in this hotel if you get a good price.

title: “Very pleasant stay”
text: I stayed from 8 - 13 jan 2007 on a business trip on a reccomendation from a colleague. The entire stay was a very pleasant one. The entire staff was very friendly, helpful, accomodated every need, and basically bent over backwards to be helpful. The room was clean and kept that way every day, as well as the rest of the hotel. There were an assortment of pillows to choose from, which is usually a complaint of mine at hotels because they are so small and tend to give me a headache. The room wasn't huge, but was adequate for my needs. I would stay here again.

title: “Conveniently located and comfy hotel”
text:
Beautiful and comfy rooms and suites. Bed mattresses are excellent and ensure a good night's sleep. High level of air quality and circulation.
In house catering for meetings was hit-and-miss but the staff were always quick to address and rectify their errors.
Reception and concierge staff are very knowledgeable and helpful to guests.
Excellent proximity to conference venues downtown (quick hop on the free 16th Ave shuttle).

title: “Great bar and Restaurant”
text: Was staying at the Hudson for two nights last April. The location is not ideal as not that close to the main attractions in the area but I believe the hotel is a venue by itself. The bar is just amazing with a unique ambiance. The food at the restaurant was great. My only concern was the size of the room... very small.

title: “Great Boutique Hotel in Union Square”
text:
I attended a trade show at the Moscone Center and Hotel Adagio was on the list of places to stay. I booked a room along with one at the Powell Hotel but after reading reviews on bed bugs at Powell, I canceled it to stay at Hotel Adagio. Im glad I did. The lobby was nice, the front desk people were very helpful and so was the bellman who gave a list of great places to eat out. There was a large glass carafe of lemon-cucumber water in the lobby for guests. I loved that added extra.
My room was HUGE and renovated with a big king bed, lots of pillows and soft sheets. It was nice to have a flat screen tv as well. There was an electric kettle in the room to have tea each morning. They had bags of Republic of Tea in the room and also served at their tea time around 7pm in the lobby. Loved that. I needed to mail a package back home and the front desk people found me a box and then handed me a 1/2 bottle of cabernet - just because. The hotel also had free WiFi and a fitness center which I planned to use but never quite made it.
The walk to the Moscone Center was perfect for me. I wanted to walk and The Coffee Bean & Tea leaf was on the way. The hotel is also a block from a Walgreens which was convenient. If you are into shopping then staying in the part of town is good. All the major stores are in walking distance. I even walked to the Ferry Building which was a great walk! But you can hop on the cable car on Powell or on Market which is close by. 
Id say the only thing I would have liked would have been HBO and BRAVO channels. It was basic TV with Showtime only I think. The other thing is that there are lots of tourists in this part of town and quite of few homeless people asking for money. Otherwise...Loved this hotel. Will stay there again for sure. I see that others on TripAdvisor werent as enchanted with their experience, but mine was perfect. Evidently my room was larger than rooms at the Monaco and some of the other hotels nearby. I was quite pleased with Hotel Adagio.

title: “very EXPENSIVE for NOTHING”
text: no pool, small rooms NO AMENETIES, 100$ PARKING FOR 1 NIGHT. ARE YOU KIDDING ME???? plus the room was for 500$. really there is nothing worth in that hotel..

title: “Clean hotel, Great location”
text:
I stayed at the Marriott Marquis with my sports team, so we got a nice group rate on the rooms. Overall, there's nothing wrong with this hotel. It's very clean, the staff are helpful and the location is great. 
We stayed in a room with two queen beds, which were very comfortable. Our bathroom did not have a fan and after talking to my teammates, no one seemed to have a fan in their bathroom either. No big deal, but was kind of strange not to have a fan in the bathroom. Keep in mind that the snacks on the table are on sensors. If you remove the snacks from the sensor, your credit card will be charged. 
The hotel is located right in the heart of downtown, just off Market Street. It's close to Union Square, Powell Station (where you get on the famous cable cars), and many major stores, like Macy's, Saks, Bloomingdales, Old Navy, Marshalls, Ross, Walgreens, Nike, Apple Store and the Cheesecake Factory. 
A tip for the Starbucks lovers - the Starbucks just outside the hotel is cheaper than the Starbucks in the hotel lobby. It's just a 1-minute walk south of the hotel.

title: “Hit and Miss”
text: This place definitely had it's pluses and minuses. It's in a pretty good location, and the room was a suite. Not quite as nice as an Embassy Suite room, but comfortable nonetheless. The staff was pleasant, and the food was pretty good. On the negative side, this place's layout is extremely confusing. It's hard to find your way around. Also, it is spread out over a large area. To get from one place to the other can sometimes be a pretty long walk. In addition, multiple elevators were not working. I'd stay there again, but I'd probaly try something else out first.

title: “Poor Service, dirty room”
text: The hotel room has mold growing in the bathroom, water marks on the ceiling, holes in the furniture that seems to have secured a TV or something, and staff that seems indifferent. The nice flat screen TV isn't secured, so could be tipped onto small kids. The breakfast offered no fruit at all, the waffle ran out of batter and when I told the care taker, she said she knew and walked away. And the wifi wasn't working.

title: “Great Girls Trip”
text: We had a wonderful girls trip to SF recently, made that much better by a stay at the legendary Drake, which did not disappoint!

title: “Awesome clean hotel”
text: We have come to siggraph 4 30 years and have not had the chance to stay here. This place is a gem! If anyone has any complaints they should go somewhere else. Very clean, everyone so so considerate and no long waits 4 the elevator's like at the other expensive hotels. Thank u everyone at the Figueroa Hotel!

title: “Room looked nothing like the website photos”
text: Went to NYC to get engaged and thankfully she said yes! Aside from the lovely time we had in the city, the hotel was a bit of a disappointment. The website images make it look styish and modern, yet the room we had was dated and tatty. Also, the breakfast is very average and expensive... mainly, because the waiters pretend they can't hear your order properly and push your bill above the threshold for a much larger tip by giving you items that you didn't order. All-in-all not a keeper, definitely not a hotel we would recommend and won't be returning...

title: “Good”
text: Good security with many food outlets around the vicinity. Banks and supermarket just around the corner.

title: “We had a wonderful time in New York, New York”
text: Great location, close to the subway and some great restaurants and bars in Gramercy. We really enjoyed walking around this part of NYC and felt safe doing so, day or night. The room was small but nice, exactly what it looked like on the internet, helpful staff (thanks for pointing us to Posto Pizza yum) clean and stylish little boutique hotel, with a great roof top lounge with views of the empire state - loved our stay and happy to recommend!

title: “Hilton on O'Farrell St.; Tower 2 room; review and suggestions”
text:
I have a confession to make. I hate San Francisco. But just for the first day. By the end of a week I usually fall in love with the city all over again.
Arriving at SFO is a hassle. Finding the sky bridge to the air train to the BART train, and then figuring out the crazy BART ticket machines is always a challenge, no matter how often we visit. 
Arriving to a downtown San Francisco jammed with summer visitors and then waiting in the long line at the tiny kiosk for MUNI passport tickets adds to the first day frustrations.
Which is all the more reason to treat oneself to a really nice hotel room, like ours was at the downtown Hilton. 
A quiet, comfortable, and conveniently located hotel room is a great refuge from the craziness of the streets below. Especially when it is available at a heavily discounted price on the internet (more about that later).
Some people prefer venerable old hotels for their local color. Others prefer trendy boutique hotels for their urban chic. We prefer four star, big box, business class hotels for their worldwide comfort and reliability. 
The San Francisco downtown Hilton is located on O'Farrell Street (between Mason and Taylor) a few blocks northwest of the Powell and Market Street BART and cable car stations, which is a convenient transportation hub for cable cars, buses, trams, and subway. 
The hotel is within easy walking distance of the Union Square and Market Street shopping districts. It is a longer walk to the SOMA district and Moscone convention center. It is a short tram ride to the Civic Center museums and concert halls. It is in the middle of the theater district.
It is also near the Tenderloin district, which lies between Union Square and Civic Center, a typically American juxtaposition of urban wealth and poverty. As in other cities, the homeless and scruffy street people are generally harmless, but the hotel maintains a reassuringly visible security staff.
This Hilton is huge. It fills an entire city block and has several separate towers of varying ages. 
Even though we had reserved and pre-paid a standard room, we were given a nice 14th floor room in the business class tower-2. An upgrade to a city view room in a higher tower would have cost $75 more, so we declined the upgrade.
Best of all, our kind receptionist (Nathan) let us check in early (11 am) after our pre-dawn flight. At the end of our stay we were also allowed to check out late (1 pm) for our afternoon return flight. That is more generous than at most hotels.
This review is based on our tower-2 king room. I do not know what rooms are like in the other towers, although they are probably similar. Some rooms surround the 16th floor outdoor swimming pool deck, which is filled with families during the summer.
Our room was a bit larger than average, about 300 square feet, and was decorated in pale gold with burgundy accents. Furnishings were in a modern Federalist style. The king bed had a wonderful mattress and ultra-fine linens. Bath towels were extra large and thick. 
Room amenities included a coffee and tea maker, a mini-bar, an iron and ironing board, a wall safe, a flat screen (but not HD) TV, a large desk with an internet plug, and an armchair with reading light and ottoman. 
The travertine and tile bathroom had a single sink and a tub-shower combo. There were no bathrobes or slippers, no shaving (adjustable) mirror, and no bedside reading spotlights. A small table near the armchair (for drinks) would have been nice.
A USA Today newspaper was delivered to our room on weekdays. The windows did not open, but the climate control worked well, and there was a small fresh air vent below the windows.
Our room was wonderfully cleaned and restocked by our housekeeper Arnel. We always leave several dollars with a note each day as a tip for housekeeping rather than waiting till the end of our stays, and this seems much appreciated. 
We did not use room service or eat at any of the hotel restaurants. The room service menu was limited and rather expensive: soups $12, sandwiches $24, and main courses $36. The breakfast buffet was about $30. These prices sent us to other nearby dining options, which I will describe later.
The hotel staff was uniformly friendly and efficient. We had one question each day for the concierge staff, and they were eager to help. They (rightfully) give priority those waiting in line, so our phone calls were occasionally answered by voice mail or placed on hold at peak times. In a hotel with 2,000 rooms this is understandable.
The hotel public areas are attractive and quite busy. Although there are lines at the reception desk, they move quickly and one can easily check-out by phone.
Hotel parking rates are high (over $50 per night I believe), but the huge parking structure across the street on the north has lower rates. Even if you do not have a car, be sure to stop by the Hilton parking garage entrance (in the southeast corner of the building) to see the decorative and humorous murals -- they are great homages to the San Francisco scene.
As I mentioned, we enjoyed our stay at the downtown San Francisco Hilton. Our only disappointment is that most hotel chains (Hilton included) are surcharging and over-pricing more and more amenities, just like the airlines do.
For example, use of this Hilton's fitness center is an additional $15 per day for hotel guests. An ordinary candy bar from the room's mini-bar is $7. 
(At Trader Joe's on Bay street near Fisherman's Wharf we bought two bottles of wine, a loaf of sourdough olive bread, a wedge of brie, a cantaloupe, and a quart of strawberries for the price of two Hilton candy bars). 
Any personal item forgotten in the mini-bar results in a $12 "cleaning" fee. An internet terminal in the business center costs $24 per hour. 
Savvy travelers can avoid such high prices and surcharges, but it would be nice not having to worry about being ambushed by them (I always check our folio well before check-out time to assure no mistakes are being made). 
The price of the room itself was very reasonable since we bid (blindly by hotel location and class rather than identity) on the Priceline website. We paid a non-refundable $85 plus $15 in fees per night for our stay. The Biddingfortravel website documented even better bargains for other weeks during the summer.
We often travel for pleasure: so far this year we have vacationed in Paris, Hawaii, London, Shanghai, Chicago, and Vienna. Priceline provided great hotel deals in each location (except Paris which was a disappointment, and Shanghai which we booked directly to assure a convenient hotel location near the Bund).
Large business class hotels with excess capacity benefit by selling rooms on Priceline, and we are happy to purchase them whenever we can.
As a price comparison, for our travel dates in San Francisco, the usual large internet booking sites were offering the Miyako at $99, the downtown Hilton and the Mark Hopkins at $109, and the Stanford Court at $119 per night (all plus 15% tax and all discount rates non-refundable). Generally, the hotel websites have higher prices, and their "best available price" often is not.
For those interested in San Francisco sightseeing and money-saving options, read on:
SFO airport transportation: the BART train is still the cheapest option from SFO to downtown at $8.10 per person each way (allow 60-90 minutes for the journey, depending on waiting times). Surprisingly, the SFO BART station has three employees standing about, but they do not sell tickets in the station. One must use the ticket machines (cash or debit or credit card). These machines are bizarre. They automatically start at $20 and like a "Dutch auction" one must reduce the fare by repeatedly pushing dollar and cents buttons to bring the fare in line with one's destination, then push the "print ticket" button. Each passenger must have his own ticket to enter and leave the BART system. Half price tickets are available for seniors and disabled, but one must find a BART agent in the international terminal to purchase one, and they are sold in high denominations (much more than the airport fare) only. Go figure. Any public transportation in Europe or China is easier and more user-friendly than BART.
Buses and cable cars: The best option for travel within San Francisco is the MUNI system, which includes buses, cable cars, trolleys, trams, and subway. One, three, and seven day MUNI "Passport" tickets cost $11, $18, and $24. Since the cable car alone costs $5 per ride, these tickets are a relative bargain. Seniors over age 65 can purchase a $15 monthly pass instead. Passport tickets are available at MUNI stations and at the Powell and Market Street sidewalk kiosk or underground visitor center. A MUNI map of the city for $3 is essential to use the system efficiently, since not all bus stops have a map.
Sightseeing: The best deal anywhere is the series of free guided walks offered by SFcityguides, a volunteer organization sponsored by the public library. Their website lists the walks, which cover almost every neighborhood and hidden gem in the city. There are usually several walks offered each day. A donation (most participants give several dollars) is requested at the end of each walk to offset their office expenses. We have taken more than a dozen of their walks and have never been disappointed.
Free venues: We always enjoy the Ferry building (bus #12 or the F-tram) and its thrice weekly farmers markets. The #28 and #29 buses stop at the brink of the Golden Gate bridge, where one can walk over the bay and along the coastline for fantastic views, if there is no fog. Golden Gate Park has a nice free arboretum and rose garden (in season) near the de Young Museum. The nearby Japanese garden is free for the first hour on some mornings. The huge new downtown public library in the Civic Center area (F-tram) has 15 minute free internet access and occasional free programs. A walk along Stockton Street in Chinatown is like visiting an Asian street market. Some museums offer free admission during the first week of each month -- check your guide book for listings. Fisherman's Wharf is free but junky. The nearby Hyde Street Pier, however, has nice free views of old ships and a nearby free visitor center with park rangers.
Food options: We always start our day by taking the Powell Street cable car or bus #30 to Pacific Street just west of Stockton Street in Chinatown for dim sum at Y. Ben (#835) or Dol Ho (#808). The former is a larger, better option for those new to this Chinese tradition. Just take a seat and point at the plates of food you want as they are rolled by. You will be charged by the plate, and we have never been able to eat more than $7 worth per person (each plate is about $2). Our evening meal is usually a picnic in our hotel room. There is an expensive gourmet market in the basement of the Nordstrom (Westfield) shopping center on Market Street near Powell. We prefer Trader Joes or Safeway grocery stores -- check the internet for locations near your hotel. We usually stop at one on our way back to our hotel at the end of the day.
Near the downtown Hilton: The Parc 55 Hotel diagonally southeast of the Hilton has a tasty and inexpensive Thai restaurant in its northwest corner (enter from the street level diagonally across from the Hilton parking garage entrance, or from the Parc 55 lobby). Most meals are around $7 and they are open from 11 am to 10 pm. An older restaurant across the street (Thai Siam) has the same name, but we have never eaten there. The west side of the Parc 55 building has an internet cafe which charges $7 per hour (as opposed to Hilton's $24 per hour). A donut and bagel shop is located across from the southwest corner of the Hilton. It looks clean and good, although we have never tried it. Mini-markets and liquor stores surround the Hilton, but we prefer the larger Safeways farther away for larger purchases. Boudin's Bakery has a sandwich shop on the street level at the back of the Union Square Macy's department store. They have famous sourdough bread. Early in the morning (8 am) one can usually board the Powell Street cable cars (without waiting) at the southwest corner of Union Square for the trip to the Chinatown dim sum parlors described above. 
Enjoy!

title: “Great Place for a Family Reunion”
text:
This past weekend my extended family had a reunion at this hotel. The facilities, the amenities, were just wonderful. My cousin and her husband and my wife and I shared a large two-bedroom suite that provided plenty of room for the family to congregate- share stories, show photos, etc. It worked perfectly. The breakfast in the morning was substantial and along with the hotels' evening cocktail hour, provided us with daily scheduled opportunities for the family to congregate and enjoy the camaraderie. The Hotel's location provided easy access to other social and educational opportunities. The hotel staff was most helpful and accommodating. The one downside is access to the internet. Even in the specified public areas where the internet was to be provided at no charge, it was impossible to connect. The dated computers in the business center were terribly slow. Attempting to do most anything on the internet with them was frustrating. In spite of that, it was a great weekend.
Thank you Embassy Suites, San Diego Bay.

title: “Hotel Needs A LOT OF HELP”
text:
There is a reason why there is no eye contact when you check-in. They know that there is a 50-50 chance that the elevators will work, or that few of the advertised room ammenities will actually be available. The wallpaper is coming off in sheets. Messages don't get delivered. Washcloths & pillowslips are deemed frivolous.The lighting in the UNHEATED bathroom was low wattage. If there is a multi million dollar renovation going on, there was no evidence of progress.Conversations with other guests confirmed that this place no way lives up to the internet claims of customer service.
The amount of broken or unavailable "ammenities" boggles the mind.
Everyone we talked to had requested an "upgrade"....but there were none to be had.
Isn't it unsafe not to post a notice when an elevator isn't working?

title: “Fantastic Hotel!”
text: After a long journey in California we decided to spend the last night in Intercontinental in Los Angeles. The hotel is simply fantastic and has all the you expect from a 5 Stars Hotel: extremely friendly staff in all the hotel (congierge, reception, valet parking,.etc), very good rooms with a superbe view over Los Angeles,etc. Bathroom was simply a dream! The hotel offers also a nice swimming pool and a SPA. We booked a package with breakfast that was very good. At all an excellent experience. Nothing to complain about!Sure 100% again to Intercontinental Centry City.

title: “Gives me the creeps!”
text: This hotel was disgusting! The bed was worn and "hump backed" in the middle. Very uncomfortable. I woke up with a sore back every morning. The towels in the bathroom were grey instead of white, were fraying, felt like sandpaper and looked like rags that were used to clean the floors. The wall paper was peeling and the overall state of the room gave me the creeps. It just wasn't clean enough for me. It lseemed as though they were running the hotel with a skeleton crew. The bell captain doubled as the concierge and the front desk staff (if there was someone present) was not very helpful, polite or friendly. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Expensive but Great Location”
text:
We stayed a week at the Wingate Inn as I was attending a conference at the Jacob-Javits centre which is a ten minute walk away.
The hotel is tucked away down a rough and ready side street but is superbly located with Macys, Empire State, Times Square all just a small walk away. The hotel is only a stroll away from numerous subway lines.
The rooms are not that big but well appointed with comfy beds and nice bathrooms.
There are few facilities in the hotel but hey this is New York where everything is only a quick stroll away. Breakfast is good quality but a bit chaotic.
In summary a well appointed, well located hotel but was exptremely expensive - especially for those carrying british pounds.

title: “More Splash than Cash!”
text:
At least my fifth stay in the last two years. I keep coming back to the Mosser because it is convenient, excellently located, intimate, priced well, not stuffy or snobby, clean and ALWAYS consistent. 
From the lovely and efficiently low-key door-man to the front-desk staff et al, I can always count on a pleasant experience. 
For those whose hotel room is not their destination, you can count on this quaint little bon-bon- right off Market, Union Square, shopping and major/minor theater venues and the BART station, cable-cars and Amtrak bus pick-up.all within a blocks walk. Why stay anywhere else?

title: “A total sham”
text:
We paid for a two night stay in advance based on a solicitation to buy a time share on a recorded phone call.. We were to receive a $150 American EXpress gift card and a $200 Hilton gift card. Instead they tried to pawn of six $25 gift certificates on nearby restaurants and when I complained they offered me a $100 AmEx gift card and when I refused to accept they came up with the $150 Am Ex gift cards. The $200 Hilton card turned out to be a certificate for one night stay in a Hilton only, not Conrad, nor Garden Inn etc as on the phone call. You stay one night and pay for it and mail them the bill for reimbursement. 
By this time I was too mad to argue more. Beware of the scam!!!

title: “Very Pleasant Stay”
text:
Enjoyed my 5 nite stay at the Phoenix Park. It was clean and well kept, the staff was friendly and helpful.
The location was great for the Capitol, sightseeing tours, the Metro, and Union Station. It is also close to Georgetown Law School.
The rooms are small but adequate, if location is a big consideration. The food at the Dubliner was very good, service was a bit slow. There is also another pub next door. I would stay here again.

title: “BEWARE OF THEFT!”
text: I stayed at this hotel in August and was robbed of everything while I was asleep in the room!. The hotel video cameras showed that the robber came in thru the supposedly locked outside doors, not once, but twice, and came into my room, since the door didn't automatically swing shut and latch. When I asked the hotel about the failure of the doors to close automatically, I was told that it often happens because the chips in the doors need to be replaced and they dont replace them very often because they are expensive. Please be VERY CAREFUL if you decide to stay here. I wont be again.

title: “Worst Sheraton I have stayed at.”
text: Stayed at this hotel for a NYE party. Outside of the hotel looked very worn we pulled up. Check in was quick and easy. Room was a decent size, however it just felt dirty. The windows were old and so fogged up you could not see out of them. The indoor pool was a joke and was very tiny. The dinner buffet was so gross, no flavor and no class how the venue was set up. We were very disappointed and would never return to this Sheraton again.

title: “Mixed bag”
text:
You get what you pay for...
The rooms are clean and of good size. The breakfast if adequate and prepared hygienically. The people here are always friendly and courteous but I personally hardly ever have problems with rudeness wherever I go. I guess it's about communication?
When I got into the room it was a little musty. This I think is from the airco. The airco is noisy but at this time of year it's not needed. Turning off the aico solved the problem. One other slight downside is the beds are soft. I like a hard mattress. At least there was a choice of pillows.
For the business traveller - the wifi is pretty good. It's fast, free and stable.
The price was fine for this level of hotel - in fact very reasonable.
What isn't good here? The neighbourhood. It's not really safe outside at night. There is no bar and as the only way to get around here is by car or cab then best to factor that into your stay.
I see a few negative comments about the gym. There are a couple of treadmills and a cross trainer. You could say that this is not a lot. I'd be more tempted to say "you get what you pay for".
All in all pretty standard and adequate.
Would I stay here again? Yes - it's very convenient for where I need to be and as I normally don't have a car then it's a no brainer.

title: “Nice pleasant stay”
text:
Hyatt at Olive 8
The hotel is in a good location, close to a mall and restaurants.
Nordstrom, Macy's are within walking distance.
The fitness center, swimming pool are very nice.Large stretch area at the gym, equipped with stretch bands and swiss ball, something not available in any other hotels.
 Shower area by the pool is super clean, lots of stalls  and furnished with thick towels. 
Staffs were friendly, nice pleasant stay.
Only complaint: No free wifi even in the hotel lobby.

title: “Good Value, Great Location, Friendly Service”
text: We traveled to Arizona for a week of recharging our batteries after a tough couple of months. Arizona is just what was needed. I was able to book this hotel after about an hour and half on the phone. The online reservation system accepted my reseravaton with e upgrade request, but never sent me an email with the actual reservation confirmation. The e upgrade came through. No one could explain it and even the supervisors couldn't make the reserves. Finally we called the property, directly, and they were able to make the reservations. Once we arrived at the property we were greeted at the front desk by friendly, helpful agents. The clerk was very nice and was even able to get us an upgrade to a king suite, after we told her about the reservation problems. All the rooms on the property are suites. Our room was close to the lobby and overlooking two of the many pools. My only complaints were with the rooms. The A/C was extremely noisy and we had the engineer come into fix it. Good A/C is a must when it is 102 degrees. There were mini bars in the rooms, but no fridges. There seemed to be a space for one, but it would have been nice to have a small fridge in the room. Also, in this day and age it seems amazing to me that a company as large as Hilton would still charge for WiFi. They had a daily rate, but no weekly rate. Rather than mess with it we would pack up our computer and take it to a local restaurant to plan our day. So the Pointe missed out on our using their restaurant for breakfast every day. There was a large group at the property for part of the week we were there. Everywhere we turned we were turned away because the group was having an event. The property needs to have a little more attention paid to cleanlieness. The large pool area had plates and food that would not be picked up for hours. The staff was always extremely friendly and would bend over backward to make sure you were having a great time. We went to dinner one night at the Different Pointe of View and it was lovely. The staff, from the cocktail lounge to the dining room were professional, friendly and helpful. The food was excellent and we had a beautiful evening. Do not miss the view from here, if even only for a drink. It was a good week and the hotel is a good value for the money. This hotel was very quiet. We were really surprised considering the amount of people that were there.

title: “Great Location! Overall Good Experience”
text: I did quite a bit of research before booking a NYC hotel near Times Square for 5 day graduation trip for my daughter and me. I selected this hotel's Premier Club level for the location by Times Square and the amenities of daily breakfast, evening cocktail reception, free wi-fi and fitness center. We were pleased with the experience overall. Some of the of the prior reviews were consistent and some were not. Yes, the bathroom left a little left to be desired with low pressure shower, aging fixtures/caulking and low pressure toilet, but the bed was comfortable (maybe I prefer a firm mattress) and pillows were fine. The rooms definitely could have been deep cleaned a little better, but the location and other amenities compensated for it. FYI - There are no ice-machines on the floors, so you will have to call for service to deliver ice and there are no refrigerators. Again, overall a good experience for the location, price and amenities.

title: “It may be good enough for the Labrador but...”
text:
This is a nice hotel in a good location in the wonderful city of Boston. 
It is over-decorated in the public rooms to the extreme (which I happened to enjoy for the camp value) and the general appearance of the place is good.
My room was very comfortable. Good quality linen on the bed, nice bathroom. Ipod dock. More comfortable than many hotel rooms. But it was also very small, which I didn't like - especially as a business traveller spending more time in the room than I would if I were on holiday. The cable was useless too - with very limited channel selection. 
All this would have been fine but what really left me annoyed was the desk staff. They were hopeless. Very young, and clearly in need of training (they mastered 'Hello Mr ____' whenever I walked by, a curious feature of upper level American hotels which always leaves me unnerved - what's wrong with 'sir'?). I checked in at about 5pm only to be told that my room wasn't ready and I'd have to wait an hour. This is pretty poor form for 5pm by which time the rooms should really have been turned around - especially with a check in time of 3pm advertised. Did they offer me a free drink in the bar with a newspaper whilst I waited? Somewhere to sit? (bear in mind it was FREEZING outside) Anything at all? Nope. Even the worst B&B in the world would give you a cup of tea and the local paper rather than send you out onto the streets. 
I returned in an hour and the room STILL wasn't ready. So I waited in the lobby on a chair, still not being offered any apology or refreshment, but able to make eyes at 'Catie Copley' the hotel's 'Canine Ambassador' (that's Boston soi-disant-posh for 'dog'). I was clearly considered a huge annoyance for arriving at 5pm - two hours after my paid for room was meant to be available to me. All I wanted was a shower and a gin.
Eventually I got my room, but there was a difficulty with payment as it was meant to be handled from the UK by my office. We had failed to send things through properly. Fine, I put the deposit on my card and waited for payment to come through from London. This caused all manner of problems - I had a form faxed through to the hotel. They didn't get it. They said they didn't have it at the desk. I could SEE IT WITH MY OWN TWO EYES FROM IN FRONT OF THE DESK. They still maintained it wasn't there and refused to let me point out to them where it was. Eventually after having finally communicated its location they were able to process things, but it was like something from a 60s farce. Admittedly there was lots of stuff going on at the desk and the duty manager was stressed (which she seemed to blame on me) but really! I am unfailingly polite to hotel staff. I know that often if something is wrong it's not their fault. And it wasn't. Fairmont clearly haven't spent the money to train their staff in any level of crisis management - or they haven't employed people with enough experience to work at a managerial level. 
The upshot? When you have this many headaches to deal with you suddenly realise, that the gym is rubbish, there's no sauna/steam room (pretty standard in 'luxury' hotels now), the public areas amount to an overdecorated lobby, the breakfast costs $30, and the internet is so expensive that you need to take out a mortgage in order to use it. 
When all these add up you think, 'yes the shampoo is worth nicking and the sheets are made of natural fibres, but why am I here?'

title: “Good location, but not much else”
text:
We recently stayed here for a wedding, and paid about $150 a night, but had been given the option of another nearby hotel for an additional $30 a night, and we now regret not paying the extra $30!
(I would actually be giving 2 stars if it weren't for the location.)
Website says mattress was pillow-top- Definitely NOT! Just a regular old mattress that sagged uncomfortably towards the middle. Ugh. And the sheets were the worst sheets I have ever had in a hotel- very stiff and uncomfortable, almost scratchy!
Very nice lobby, but 1 of the 3 elevators was broken, and so it sometimes took FOREVER to wait for an elevator during busy times of the day.
Our room did not match the public parts of the hotel. Some things in the bathroom seemed nice and updated, but some parts of the wallpaper had watermarks on it (yuck!) and/or was peeling, and the carpet seemed old.
I wish we had done our research *before* staying there, as I am saying the same thing as other reviewers. :-(

title: “Bastion of old San Francisco”
text:
