Can't understand what the fuss regarding hotel staff is all about...I suspect some folks are very difficult to please. 
Our experience was excellent from the moment we arrived. The main lobby and parlor are exquisitely furnished, balancing the old world feel of a bygone era with slick modern design and lighting. The public areas are elegantly decorated with redwood bonsais and orchid blossoms in crystal cylinders. WIth high backed settees and deep club chairs the feel is rather hushed and decidedly unhurried, which is such a treat to escape into from the bustle of Union Square just outside.
We found we could not be upgraded as is our custom because the hotel was hosting a massive contingent of Prom revelers, yet the registration clerk Alexandra, was ever so accommodating in dealing with our disappointment. 
Our room in the new tower was spacious with an interesting view of the Starlight Room across the way. When the fog cleared the view extended out to the bay and beyond. Bathroom vanity was enormous with plenty of counter space for mine and my sister's mountain of make-up, hair equipment and assorted toiletries...and large enough for the two of us to primp together without causing a scuffle. We needed extra towels, wine glasses, pillows, etc and all were whisked up to us within minutes of our contacting housekeeping...and very cheerfully delivered as well.
Plenty of room, period... great seating area around desk and roomy closets with plenty of hangers.
Two quibbles: the T.V. located in the room's armoire...ridiculously small in this day and age, and the mini bar with obnoxious notice warning guests not to store personal items in fridge lest being charged for items removed. We ignored this and chilled our champagne and O.J. and were billed for the items misplaced. This was resolved at check-out however. Still, this practice is irritating.

title: “Good choice!”
text:
We were scheduled to overnight in NY and picked Le Parker Meridien because of price, location and availability. We were upgraded to a room--still small but very efficient and comfortable--with a magnificent view of Central Park. Very modern, minimalist decor everywhere but well designed and executed.
The hotel really shone, though, when my spouse became very ill and we had to call for EMS. Two from hotel management stayed with me from the time I went to the concierge until he was placed in the ambulance. Every day I extended my stay one more night. Staff recognized me and asked regularly how things were going. I could not have asked for more personal, caring service at a hotel that charged twice the price. 
Every night I ate in the little French bistro--good food, great wines by the glass, fair prices. My daily in-room continental breakfast included genuine fresh squeezed OJ and excellent breads and pastries. 
The view from the rooftop swimming pool has to be one of the best in the city.
Only one complaint--indifferent, ineffective doormen. I waited 20 minutes for a cab in mid-afternoon and they suggested I should have engaged a car service if I needed to be somewhere on time. Luckily, the hotel is between W. 56th and 57th, between Broadway and Fifth Avenue, so I could walk almost anywhere I wanted or needed to go.

title: “Great value and location - good for families”
text: Spent 6 nights at the hotel over New Year's 2003 with husband and child. Thought it had comfortable, decent sized suites with useful wet bar and fridge. We ordered a lot of room service, the quality of which was ok, but certainly arrived quickly. Staff professional and responsive. Two super good things about staying in the hotel: The fantastic indoor swimming pool on the 35th floor, with skyscraper and lake views that can't be bested. Second, the location at the top end of Michigan Avenue, next to the Hancock, Cheesecake Factory and Filene's Basement. Deal booked via Expedia inclusive of flights was ?1200 pounds sterling - not bad at all.

title: “Great Value, Room not for everyone”
text: Stayed 3 nights over Memorial Day Holiday. Great location, took Airport Shuttle Bus to Port Authority Terminal (42nd/8th) short walk to the hotel, also close to most subway lines. Rooms are adequate size. Bathrooms great with large counter, shower and toilet rooms, includes refrig. Small open closet had enought room for hanging, floor space used for shoes, purchases, etc. Platform bed has walls on 3 sides, this makes it extremely difficult for climbing in and out. Bed sits approx 36" from the floor, padded railing aids in access. Complimentary Cont. Breakfast was good, cold cereal, pastries, whole fruit, coffee, tea, juice, served on 2nd floor just above pool. Housekeeping did not replace glasses or toiletries each day. No accessible ice machine, had to have it delivered. Front desk staff, while very pleasant, had little knowledge. Thank goodness for "google" on their computer. Everything was clean and bright. Consider it a good value, but not right for everyone.

title: “Very, Very Basic!”
text:
On arrival, the building looked very run down and dirty. The inside is a little better, and clean. Cheap bedding and fittings throughout (IKEA), though the beds are comfortable.
Unfortunately during our stay, there were baseball games at the stadium across the road on the 2 nights we stayed. The management sell parking spaces to the patrons, which made it an absolute nightmare for the hotel guests. The underground parking garage was packed, including double parking in the lanes. No room for those of us who had secured a park earlier. Felt sorry for the poor guy who was at reception complaining that his car was blocked, and couldn't get out.
The shuttle service (Royal Trolley Tours) into DC is a one way affair. Find your own way back! The driver we had on the 2 mornings was not the friendliest, not even a thankyou or goodbye after we gave our non deserved tip. But, it is free!

title: “Crown Plaza Hotel Staff”
text:
My family (2 sisters and mom) stayed at the Crown Plaza the last week of June 2012. The staff was incredible!!! Kenny made sure that our cabs were arranged and when we were ready for the airport, he had all our bags loaded and ready to go. Demming was our bartender and was always ready with beers and great conversation. My sisters and I were there to be on the Price is Right. Long story short, we didn't get into the show and when we returned to the Crown Plaza, everybody was asking how we did. We had to tell them our sad story and they gave us free drinks at the bar!!!
The rooms were always clean and comfortable! Anytime we needed extra towels, they were delivered immediately. The staff members were always cheerful and respectful.
We had breakfast at the the Crown Plaza restaurant and it was delicious and a lot of food. Our hostess and waiter were very sweet. 
We were about 1 mile walking distance to Rodeo drive. There were plenty of restaurants and markets within 4 blocks. 
I would highly recommend this hotel if you are planning a trip to Los Angeles/Beverly Hills area.
Thanks again Crown Plaza for making our trip memorable and enjoyable.

title: “Favorite spot in NYC”
text: If you are in NYC arou d the holidays and want a spot near Rockefeller, great dining, and central park...this is a great spot.

title: “Urban Hotel in a Historic Building”
text:
We spent one night here. The hotel was originally a bank and the historic details remain. Even the halls still look like there are offices instead of hotel rooms in the building. So it's kind of fun when you come off the elevator to your room. The front desk is the teller station - another nice touch. Check in was friendly and efficient. Once inside the room, the decor is standard. It was clean and comfortable. The bathroom was small but well laid out and had a big window, which was neat.
Parking is valet, and expensive. There are not really any other options. The valet service was efficient and they have it set up so you can text down to have car brought around, which is nice.
The location is at the far end of the gas lamp district, more towards downtown. It’s at the opposite length of the district from the convention center and a bit of a walk if you were doing it daily. Location is the one not great thing about the hotel – it’s just about one block off the touristy area, you have to get past the check cashing centers and just into the downtown. Downtown is looking rather gritty these days – I would not say it’s unsafe, but definitely you need to be aware of your surroundings.

title: “First La Quinta Stay”
text:
Excellent room. Very comfortable bed. Very easy to get to. Lots of choices of restaurants and shopping in the area. Close to Interstate. Friendly staff.
Would definitely stay here again, and recommend it to any one travelling to the Columbus, Ohio area!

title: “Family weekend”
text: Took our nieces 8 and 5 into the city for a sleepover. This hotel was great! Right next to the 911 Memorial, there's a playground across the street, Seaport within walking distance, rooms were huge. Most NYC hotel rooms are not this big. The girls got a stuffed bear when we checked in. Breakfast was included in the price of the room and it was very good. Can't wait to go back.

title: “Not a good choice for San Diego convention”
text: Felt a bit like a time-trip, back about 20 years, before hotels cleaned-up their act. A/C wasn’t working at first, sliding door to small balcony was not quite fitting - leading to strong soundtrack from the kids playing in the pool. Staff were friendly but it all felt a bit like a motel. Plus it is several miles removed from downtown area. Ah well, that’s what happens when you book without any prior local knowledge!

title: “Very satifsfying”
text: We had a large, clean, quiet room for a very reasonable price. Maybe the hotel has gone through some changes since previous reviewers have stayed here. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Wonderful Hotel/Fantastic Value”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Topaz for three nights and absolutely loved the place. The location is perfect...only two blocks from Dupont Circle and the metro stop. This hotel is very zen-oriented....serenity stones on the bed, a yoga channel on the TV, and they even have specialty rooms for those who are really serious about yoga. The rooms are immaculately clean, uniquely decorated and the staff is exceptionally friendly and helpful...especially Daniel at the reception desk. We got a great deal from Expedia, which made it an unbelievable value for such a nice hotel in the center of Washington, D.C. You can't go wrong staying at athe Topaz. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Fantastic”
text: Booked this hotel for a corporate sponsored team building, and they couldn't of done a better job in making everything perfect for every guest. They are so professional and accommodating. The facility was beautiful, the spa was excellent, the rooms were luxurious, and the staff were polite and friendly.

title: “Excellent Choice very Clean - Would stay there anytime!”
text: I stay at Hampton Inns all over the US for my company and this one was in the top 5 for quality & clean. Some times I question Hampton Inns but not this one. Everyone was very nice & presentable. Very close to Easton Town Center 1/2 mile & $25/night cheaper than others @ the mall.

title: “Easy to get around , affordable, comfy pillows”
text: Harvey at front desk made our stay the most pleasurable and Keith is an excellent bartender.

title: “Slice of Style”
text: This place was an awesome slice of LA style - cool colors, funky, laid-back. Not cookie-cutter at all - this place was not a chain and it didn't feel like you could be anywhere except LA. We booked a package through them for 360 total which included two nights, museum tickets, fanastic fresh breakfast, and $60 towards dinner at a nearby trattoria. The breakfast was hands down the best complimentary hotel breakfast I have ever seen - granola, wheat bread, bagels, real bakery pastries, fruit, fruit, fruit, great coffee. Bed was super-comfortable with high thread count linens. Bathroom was tiny but acceptable, bathrobes a nice touch. Common areas looked like they were either being renovated or in need of renovation but all in all, the Elan puts money into important stuff (bed, linens, funky decor, breakfast) and as for the rest, who cares if the hallway looks a little shabby. Finally, the front desk was phe-nomenal. I'm not usually a P.I.T.A. but I was without a car in LA and wanted to go to off-the-beaten-track places like Japantown and they helped me find bus routes to these random places even though they didn't know where they were - which means they took the time to research my P.I.T.A. requests - all with a smile. Finally, on the last night, I had planned to use my restaurant voucher but the place was closed on Monday nights and the front desk scored me a voucher to another restaurant even though we didn't make reservations like we were supposed to. They also arranged our super shuttle for us and had them wait for us when we were tied up at dinner. These people gave us 5-star service for a 2 star price. If their manager is reading, Jorge and Jordan deserve a raise. They were outstanding.

title: “Very uncomfortable hotel that's lost it's way!”
text:
My husband and I have just returned from a Wedding Anniversary weekend in New York City. it was the first time that we'd been on holiday without the children (4years) so we were looking forward to partying late into the night and having long lazy days in "The Loft" (60 Thompson's equivalent to a Penthouse Suite). 60 Thompson seemed the perfect choice due to it's location and the apparent luxury of The Loft.... how wrong we were! 
Firstly, I think it's worth noting that the girls at the Concierge were fantastic, friendly and would go "the extra mile" and managed to get us into nearly all of the bars, restaurants and club that we requested. 
However, everything else about the hotel was very below par:
1. The layout of The loft seemed to be designed for a business man that doesn't have many toiletries, rather than a couple or a woman. There was one small shelf in the bathroom, only just enough space for moisturisers, toothbrushes, toothpaste and mouthwash. We had to remove the complementary cotton wool, cotton buds and drink glasses from the bathroom into the bedroom in order to make room for our toiletries (this made the bedroom area very cluttered immediately). 
2. The bath was 3/4 the size of a normal bath. Obviously in a city where space is tight you would expect small baths in hotels but certainly not in the best room in the house. 
3. In the shower there were two small shower-heads, one of which was plastic!
4. Also quite shockingly both the bath and shower had shower curtains rather than transparent doors... I would always worry about the hygiene of having shower curtains in hotel rooms. 
5. After I had my first shower I obviously needed to dry my hair and straiten my hair but there were no power sockets next to the full-length mirror. I called reception and asked them to find a solution but the response that I received was that guests used the power sockets in the bathroom for the hairdryers and irons!!! I was flabbergasted as you will hardly ever find power sockets in bathrooms in the UK because of the health and safety implications, especially when you have to balance hot hair irons on a wet sink! 
6. I had the same problem when I needed to apply my make-up. Whenever I've stayed in hotel suites I've had a dressing table with a mirror... but not at the 60 Thompson! There was a desk but alas no mirror. During my previous conversation with reception about hairdryers I did ask them if they had a desk mirror that I could place on the desk so that I could apply my make-up in a normal fashion... the response was negative.... apparently women apply their make-up under the false light of the bathroom. 
7. The bed was presented nicely but the mattress was about 8inches too small for the bed itself, so our pillows ended up on the floor between the gap in the headboard and mattress covered in dust!!!! 
8. Attention to detail in our room was severely lacking.... one of the staircase lights was broken when we arrived and didn't get fixed for the duration of our stay even-though we had informed the management. 
9. The room service food was terrible, especially the breakfasts. The burger and fries was so terrible that when we needed food in our room we ordered a delivery pizza - coincidentally we saw another guest taking a pizza back to his room. 
10. on our last day I asked for a pot of tea for our room but I wanted large mugs (same as what they used for coffee). I was told that this wasn't possible as all of the large mugs smelt of coffee and they couldn't get rid of the smell - I suggested they wash them properly. 
11. The bar was beyond noisy and quite cold. We wanted a pre-dinner cocktail at the bar but the DJ was on early and the decibels were comparable to the nightclub that we were at later that evening. 
12. There was only one doorman at the door at anyone time, so this was a problem if several guests needed cabs hailing at the same time... in the end we would walk up the street and find one ourselves. Out of all the doormen we met, we only really got good service from one of them. 
13. I had phoned the General Manager several times during our stay and left a voicemail for him but I didn't receive a call back from him. On our final day I was quite furious and asked to speak to the Duty Manager. When I finally made contact with the Duty Manager he told me that the General Manager doesn't work on weekends and he hadn't been working on the Friday either. I gave the Duty Manager our list of grievances, he was very apologetic but he said that he didn't have the power to address any of them! I told him that we'd been given a guaranteed late check-out upon booking (we were due to leave for the airport at 6pm) but he said that he couldn't let us have the room after 3.30pm. His solution to this was to give us the best available room in the hotel to leave our bags, freshen up and relax in until we needed to leave for the airport. We accepted his suggestion but we were left dumbfounded by the box-room that he'd given us... it was extremely small, dark and hugely depressing, we stayed there for all of 1 minute and decided to walk the busy streets of NYC for 2 1/2 hours. 
14. When we checked-out (they didn't give us a discount to compensate for very poor service and sub-standard "best room in the house") the Duty Manager said that the General Manager would call us the next day.... one week on and we haven't heard from him..!
I hope this will be helpful for anyone thinking of staying at 60 Thompson. I certainly wouldn't return and I wouldn't recommend it. We hugely regret staying there.

title: “Don´t you want to stay one "Night at the Museum"?”
text:
This hotel is amazing, just at the lobby we can see many peaces of marines´ history, including they have one floor only to place a true museum.
It´s very well located, and counts with great rooms and great staff.
The restaurant, in the 12th floor is wonderfull counting with a especial sight of San Francisco down town, some part of the bridges and a beautiful vision of the bay.
As they are a marines´s club, you need to book your stay too early because it´s often full.
To do business or vacation, it´s a great deal. I really recomend.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text:
We stayed here at the Marriott Residence Inn 6/28 - 7/1. The hotel is in a great location. We walked all over the city & saw so much. One of our main reasons for going was to take our 10 year old daughter to the American Girl store, this hotel is not far from there. 
The staff was very nice & helpful. The breakfast every morning was great.
We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Comfy, clean, and convenient for a lot”
text:
This hotel is very good for what it is worth. My party had no problems with check-in at all. They were very nice at the check-in counter, and were very helpful in sending toiletries up when I needed them.
The room itself was comfortable. The beds were pretty good, the TV was good, the shower was good, and I liked the free internet.
It's an awkward location for this hotel, with it in a corner right off the Sam Houston Tollway and the Westpark Tollway, but it works. It's very easy to get on BOTH Tollways to go wherever from the hotel (although for the Westpark Tollway, you'll need what they call an EZ Tag, and to go eastbound, you'll have to drive down Westpark Dr or Harwin Dr to South Gessner and get on there.)
I also liked the fact that the hotel is very quiet. Considering it's flanked by two freeways, that's great. (I was in a room facing away from the freeways.)
I didn't try the restaurant, but it did look busy. May be a good sign.
So, this is a good, cheap hotel for Westchase, and very convenient for what we were doing.

title: “Loved it!!”
text:
We had originally not planned to stay at Hotel Monaco; however, after a bad experience at another well-known hotel, we were fortunate enough to be able to move to this wonderful hotel. The staff was friendly, helpful, and seemed genuinely interested in our well-being. Walking into the restaurant in the morning, the first thing you smell is wonderful baked bread. We were told the restaurant bakes all its bread, scones, and muffins. There's nothing like freshly baked bread in the morning.
Happy hour in the evening is like spending an evening with good friends. There is wine for the adults, back massages, and video games for the kids. The hotel is pet-friendly and some people brought their dogs down to socialize. All in all, a great experience.
The rooms are lovely, bright, and comfortable. The front desk staff was amazing and eager to recommend good restaurants. Even the parking staff was wonderful, as we did arrive and leave quite frequently with our car. We never had to wait for more than a minute or two.
All in all, this was a great experience. We visit Denver at least once a year and will definitely call the Hotel Monaco our home whenever we are in Denver.

title: “Lovely hotel”
text: I live in the Seattle area, but we like to stay in the city some nights to enjoy the nightlife and dining. This was our second stay at the Hotel Andra and it was lovely. We had a King junior suite on the top floor. The rooms are tastefully decorated and the amenities in the bathrooms are nice. A couple of really positive things about the Hotel Andra...free Wi-Fi, comfortable beds and furnishings, and it is a great location (walking distance to anything touristy). I like that it is a smaller boutique hotel...so there aren't large conventions or long waits for elevators. The staff is very friendly and accommodating. It is one of my favorite hotels in Seattle.

title: “Close proximity to USF and very easy access to public transportation.”
text: This is the second time we stayed at The Laurel Inn. We initially stayed here based on its location and proximity to USF. We have come to realize that the hotel location also makes it very easy to get around the city using public transportation (right outside the front door!). The hotel staff is very accommodating and willing to assist with any and every request. We love the neighborhood and can walk to many restaurants and there is even a movie theater a block away. The continental breakfast (included in the room rate) allows you to start your day without reaching into your pocket!

title: “It is now 5:28 and we still haven't been...”
text: It is now 5:28 and we still haven't been able to get into our room. I have been here since 3:00 and my room still isn't ready. Pretty ridiculous to wait 2 and a half hours for a room that was reserved over two months ago

title: “nice hotel”
text: me and my bf spent a night in the hotel (08/05/2012 room 704) and it was so enjoyable.The room was very clean and comfortable with a nice view for the bridge. Staff is very gentle and friendly. Houskeeper are always smiling to you and during the breakfast we found out that the waffles base was ending and the server filled it up in just one minute. Breakfast was really really nice. I hope we will come there again bc it was exactly COFORTable :)

title: “Beautiful, Colourful Hotel”
text:
This is a lovely hotel. Its new and decorated in bright, cheerful colours.
Our room - 2 queen with sofa bed - was very spacious and very clean. The beds were very comfortable.
The indoor pool was small but we had it to ourselves. The hot tub was nice and hot. 
Breakfast had plenty of choice and the breakfast area was kept very clean. 
We enjoyed our stay at this hotel and would recommend it.

title: “The Pod: great small hotel in NY”
text:
We came across the Pod Hotel after a lot of googling, but it was well worth the hassle: this place has many great features.
Location is perfect, really close to various subways and to Park Ave.
The area is great also for restaurants & bars: we loved a tiny japanese eatery next door to the Hotel: Tanaka, very cheap a surprisingly good.
The hotel has a funky lobby, with Lichtenstein-like paintings, and very friendly and helpful staff.
We got a room without bathroom, but we didn't have much problems: commonal bathrooms are very clean and confy.
The room is very small, but fully equipedd, with a huge LCD TV, Ipod stand and a sink.
As a bonus, there is free-wifi, which came quite handy, for using skype and calling for free.
Overall, if you are searching for a bargain right in the heart of Manhattan, this could be a good place to check

title: “Large Rooms but small bathroom”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for a weekend out with friends. It's in a very convenient location - close to Copley Place (shopping), Prudential Tower where you have an amazing view of Boston in the "Top of the Hub" and Newberry St (high end shopping and restaurants).
The hotel room was very large (then again I had two double beds), the view was great. The only little thing that annoyed me was that the bathroom was a little small. It was ok for only me, but if there were two or more people staying in this room, which is what it is equipped for it seams, I would look elsewhere if you're looking for a spacious bathroom.

title: “Nightmare”
text: I just returned from a one night stay at this location. It was a shock to discover that the room was, in a word, "filthy." The ceiling had mold on it, the mini fridge leaked all over the carpet, (The water from the fridge actually ruined the entertainment center finish also) there was a huge gap underneath of the entry door allowing light and great heat and humidity to enter the room, while I tried to run the noisy, inefficient air conditioner. The bathroom and bedroom walls were marked up with some substance and the tile floor looked as if it hadn't been cleaned in a long time. Needless to say, I wore my sandals the entire time in the room. I only regret that I booked the room in an unfamiliar area, and then was stuck! The nightmare continued, as the next morning, when readying to shower and leave, I discovered there was no water! The front desk assured me that they would have it fixed in three hours or so, well after my check out time, so I used the bottled water I brought in to brush my teeth, packed my bag and left. The front desk could do nothing to assist me or adjust my bill. The young student Jolene, who spoke with me was polite, but was unable to help me. Frustrated, I headed home and have contacted the reservation center and been assured I will receive a refund.

title: “Excellent Stay”
text: Had heard bad reviews recently about the Soho Grand, but had good experiances there in the past. Stayed over the weekend and had a wonderful stay as usual. Beautiful room with a great view of NY. Attentive service, particularly at the front door.

title: “Great location, free parking!”
text:
This is my second time that I've booked at this hotel and I was still not disappointed. It's pretty hard to be disappointed for a well-priced hotel with free parking (parking can be 35$ a day in NYC). The thing is, is that you need to be a quad occ. to make it a good price. A would say that the hotel is basic and nothing was not good. I went to this hotel maybe 6 years ago and got a room that was with an entry outside (the room of the door was outside the main building, around the outside pool which makes the hotel look like a motel sort of. That room was a little damp and older, but maybe since then, they done renovations.
I even shipped a parcel to the hotel, and they received it (at first, the person from security didn't remember receiving it, but then confirmed the name of the person who had signed for it, and then remembered...).
You also need to book at this hotel in advance and with its 24hr cancellation policy, it's worth booking in advance and just cancelling if you're not leaving to NY finally. Last minute bookings at this hotel must be impossible. I always book directly on their website and get the best rate.
This hotel is literally 2-3 blocks from Times Square and maybe a block from the bus terminal. I couldn't ask for better for the same price.
To finish, I think it would of costed us the same price to stay in a hostel further so you really get the best price for a greatly located hotel in NY. Nothing luxurious, but the basic (anyways, do you stay in NY for the hotel or to be in the city?!!) Oh and there's a 7eleven and a Duane Right a block away!

title: “Nice workers, But What a Dump!”
text:
All the employees were very nice, but this place is awful! No hangers, no wastebasket, no cold water, and no lightbulbs in the 2 badly worn lamps. We had to make 3 calls to get the lightbulbs.Good thing it wasn't too cold, because there were no blankets on the bed.A lot of the wallpaper was coming undone too. I would NEVER go barefoot on that carpeting either. In bad need of renovations, except for the lobby.
 If they tell you the Penrose Diner across the street is a 4 star diner, they must not get out much. Average food and average service. 
Spend a few dollars more and stay at a Comfort Inn or chain hotel.
Thank God we were only there 1 night to see Barbra Streisand at the Wells Fargo Center that is close by. Be careful of Cabbies too, we got ripped off 2X, until we wised up.

title: “Loved It ”
text: i stayed at this hotel Feb 18 2007. Long line at checkit but it went very quickly. The front desk staff are very efficient. We book a club room and got upgraded to a king suite which was on floor 30. What a beautiful room(S) had a foyer with fridge, huge bedroom, bed was wonderful, bathroom was across the hall and was nice, living room was great, and the view.......WOW It evn has its own big deck. Tastefully furnished. Only drawback was outside our bedroom window was the hotel air con units...very noisy!!!!! 3007. I could not sleep, i called down at 1.30am to see if they could do anything about the noise, the maintence worker came up and was going to put some insulation strips on to help drown out the noise but i asked for earplugs instead...sort of helped. However it was such a fabulous room that i was happy even with an hour or two of sleep. The club room had a great view, good food and great staff. We had lunch from the Thai place in the hotel, very yummy! We took BART so didn't have to pay parking and everything is within walking distance. We had drinks at First Crush across the road, very nice.

title: “Horrible hotel with aggressive and rude staff”
text:
I stayed at the Penn in July 2012 and I had an awful stay. I was happy when my stay ended. The room was filty, the shower didn't work properly and it was smelly all over. There was very rude staff at the front desk. Myself working as a hotel manager was treated in a very bad way. The queue upon check-out time was huge and I was waiting to do my check-out for approx 1 hour. When it was my turn, three young guests went to the desk and I asked them to go an queue as well as everybody did. The receptionist was shouting at me and insaulting me. She told me that it is her who is deciding who will be next at the dest and who has to wait.
There was one manager, I suppose it was the GM of the hotel, watching all the people queueing and was just standing there. One guest asked him for an information and he sent the guest to queue as well. What a horrible service from the top to the bottom...
I will never ever stay there again

title: “great location”
text: the wellington is in a brilliant location and , if you can get a good deal it's even better.right opposite the park central hotel and also the Carnegie Hall.walking distance from the Moma,columbus circle and time square.for a 1st time in new york ,we had a 22 floor bedroom with a view on 57th and 6th avenue.brilliant.small room but nice and clean.fabulous shower.if you got any probels the staff are very efficient and sort you out in a minute.

title: “Okay Airport Hotel”
text:
So this hotel really doesn't have anything going for it other than that it is close to the airport and the rental car returns of Avis and Hertz. It is a standard Hilton without really any charm, including the views, which are nothing compared to the Hilton Bay Front a few miles south. Do not stay here if you are visiting San Diego for pleasure, as it is too far from anything but the airport.
The rooms are fairly standard, perhaps a little bigger than the average Hilton room, though the furniture is a bit older, and the bathrooms certainly small. Air system is fairly loud and the top floor rooms are alive with the humming produced by the hotel's HVAC system part of which sits on the roof of the hotel. So at the very least avoid the top floor, which also has a low false ceiling in the hallway, making it feel dingy.
They charge you here even if you park your own car a hefty $15 fee. This seems a lot when their is ample parking and no one is there to greet you at the door anyway.
Customer service was fine, check-in efficent. Check-out the same. Stay here if you have an early morning flight, otherwise seek the Hilton's further to the south.

title: “Far better than the similarly-priced Marriott Suites down the road”
text:
It's better than average, but they've got a ways to go before it could be called nice. The area is kind of dicey and there's absolutely nothing to walk to except Whataburger. The best tip I can give is to avoid rooms x01-x09; go for x10-x19. In the lower-numbered rooms of each floor, you will hear street noise. 
Rooms are a nice size with two TVs, full kitchen except for stove. There are burners for cooking. Pots, pans, dishes and silverware are in the cupboards.
The best thing they've got going is the evening meal. Usually you can fill up on something decent for free. Breakfast is free and not too bad either.
The outdoor pool is nice and big and over-chlorinated. The indoor workout room is small and skimpy.
There is a laundry room with two washers and two dryers, usually busy, $1/load.

title: “Awesome Hotel!”
text:
Stayed at the hotel in march, kept a fairly open mind about the place. my room was great, cleaned everyday(if you wanted it) at a very good standard, staff were great, location was pretty poo but nothing but a short taxi ride couldn't sort out.
I was a alone female travelling and the staff made me feel really welcome, felt very safe in the surrounding areas at night on my own.
WOULD RECOMMEND!!!

title: “Outstanding Service for our Memorial Service Group”
text:
Nikki Brame was fantastic! Our large group contacted her from across the country, in short notice, to stay to attend a Memorial Service of a married couple killed in a tragic car accident. We were all in shock and she patiently worked with each caller to book and rebook us based on our needs. We also were able to gather in the Connexion Cafe the first evening, which was very helpful. The other staff were kind and responsive.
The Nexus is a stylish remodel of what appears to be a motel. Low cost, the beds are comfortable, hot breakfast and a pool. The restaurant on the property has fantastic Indian and Mediterranean food. We loved it!

title: “Nice hotel, JW Marriott Quality”
text:
Stayed at the JW on business for the month of January. Got a nice room on one of the top floors with a nice view. The rooms are big- king size bed with a couch. They provide free internet for platinum members so that was a plus. I don't spend much time in the hotels since I am there for business but I was impressed with this hotel. Overall, had friendly staff, good amenities (restaurant, bar, Starbucks, workout facility, Concierge floor) and a good location.
Pros
- Friendly staff
- Good restaurant
- Concierge floor (hot breakfast every morning, snacks in the evening, desserts at night)
- Workout facility
- Starbucks

title: “Great place”
text:
We stayed here with our 3 kids for a sport tournament and it was great. First off this place is beautiful & interesting, they have a brochure for a self guided walking tour. A nice change from the standard chain hotel. We had a junior suite because they were all out of rooms with 2 beds. It was quite spacious & comfortable. I loved the complimentary computer & printer in the lobby which came in handy to print passes. The staff was very friendly. We had a low drain in the tub, I called & it was fixed immediately. We were away from the hotel but they left a note & even followed up with a phone call to make sure it met our needs. The pool was small but our kids still had fun swimming. The buffet breakfast is very good. Loved the outside sitting areas & bars, very pretty outside area with fire pit, you can order a cocktail & food too.
We would definitely stay there again, only 1 hr away from San Fran & in a great location near lots of stuff.

title: “You get what you pay for - an average hotel”
text: I chose this property based on the many positive reviews I read on the TripAdvisor website. Overall, our stay at Humphrey's would be considered "average". Basically, you get what you pay for. A fair description of the service would be "cordial"(at best) but nothing special. After reading the reviews, I expected a higher level of service with the staff extending themselves by going the "extra mile" whenever possible. We were not welcomed at check-in or thanked at the end of our stay. The front desk did not have change for the laundry facilities. The room was spacious and in a good location however, the carpet was due for cleaning(or replacement). You could feel the dirt on your feet as you walked across the room...yikes! The cleanest area of the room was the bathroom which included a shower curtain that allowed water to pond outside of the tub and a heat lamp that illuminated only for a short period of time. The closet doors had to be placed back on the track whenever you moved the doors. The oversized door frame to the room allowed the light and wind to enter from outside making you feel less secure while in the room. On my next visit to SD I will pay the additional dollars for uncompromised service and accommodations at the Hilton Gaslamp or the W Hotel instead.

title: “Reasonable lodging for a very low price”
text: The staff were very friendly and helpful, breakfast provided, the rooms we got were great for the price which was very affordable. Basically, if you're out looking for a cheap but comfortable place to stay during your travel in San Francisco- I'd recommend it. Situated very close to the Fisherman's wharf - almost everything is walking distance or you can take the bus!

title: “Clean, cheap and great location”
text:
We stayed at the Chandler Inn for two nights in late December as part of an around the US trip. Initially we thought what have we done as we walked down the dingy corridor from the elevator but were pleasantly surprised by the modern rooms that awaited us. They are smallish in size but both modern and clean. The location is great - we were basically able to cover Boston on foot from our hotel.
The reception staff were great also - always willing to help or offer advice ( particularly Vaughn - hope we got the name right). Free coffee in reception also a nice touch.

title: “Too Many Unpleasant Surprises”
text:
A little background – during a weekend in New York, my traveling companion was admitted to the hospital. There was no firm date for release so I had to book hotel rooms at the last moment. After staying at four hotels, I finally checked in to the Marriott East Side. I had a series of one night reservations so that I could cancel and leave with only a day notice (reservations required cancellation the day before arrival.) Some of the nights used Marriott Reward Points and some were paid. The stay extended into the weekend of the New York Marathon so hotels were full or very expensive.
When I arrived at the Marriott East Side, all went well. Check-in was easy and I mentioned that I had a series of one night reservations. No problem or so I was told. My room was exactly what I had requested. Since this would be my home for the next several nights, I unpacked and was relieved that I’d not need to pack/move/unpack again. I had done that four days in a row and it gets old. As an elite member of Marriott Rewards, I enjoyed a visit to the Concierge Lounge before departing for the hospital to visit my friend. 
The next day, I returned in the afternoon from a hospital visit and found that my key no longer would open the door. I went to reception to get new keys and was informed I’d have to change rooms. At check-in they had forgotten to block me into the same room for all of my reservations. They had already blocked my room for another arriving guest so I had no choice but to move. I don’t know what they would have done if I had not returned until later that evening – my stuff was in the room. So, for a fifth day I packed and moved to a new room. 
Now the problem began. I could not get WiFi reception in the new room. I called and was connected to their technical support service who seemed to know about the problem. They said it was most likely the router on the floor and they’d have that reset. However, the next morning I still could not establish a connection to the Internet. In the hallway, I had no problem establishing connection but my room was a dead spot. On my way to the lounge, I saw another guest sitting in the hallway with his laptop so I’m guessing the problem occurs with more than one room. That’s inexcusable for a business hotel.
I thought I would simply use the computers in the lounge or at least connect to WiFi while in the lounge. I then learned that the lounge would not be open after breakfast hours on Friday until Sunday evening. In other Marriott properties, you can at least access the lounge even if there are no other services available in the lounge. Not at this property! When the lounge is closed, no one can access the lounge. I asked about breakfast on weekends for elite guests and was told there was no option. That was a surprise and I learned a “loophole” in the Marriott Rewards program. If a hotel does not have a lounge, certain levels of elite members are given breakfast in the dining room. If the hotel has a lounge, you’re given access to the lounge instead. If they have a lounge but it is closed, you’re simply on your own for breakfast. After complaining, I was comped breakfast for the two days the lounge would be closed.
I was very surprised to learn the lounge would be closed on the weekend. The hotel was sold out and they were charging premium prices due to the marathon. Seems to me this would have been a good weekend to keep the lounge open.
Even though this is an older property, they do have the new Marriott beds and they were comfortable. Housekeeping did a decent job of cleaning the rooms. Water pressure and temperature in the shower did vary a bit during a shower but not enough to make me get out of the shower. There was very little counter space in the bathroom. Wake-up calls arrived on schedule. Overall, the hotel and rooms feel older, dated, and occasionally shabby. Internet service was spotty as mentioned above. Even when I tried using the wired computers in the lounge (when it was open), the response time was terribly slow. There frequently was a line at reception but my waits were not overly long.
Maybe I was being overly critical because I was preoccupied with my friend’s hospitalization. My stay in New York had become unexpectedly extended and I really needed the Internet to keep up with issues at work. This was a time when I needed Marriott to come through and provide the services I’ve come to expect. Usually that happens, but it didn’t happen at the Marriott East Side.
On Sunday (the day of the marathon), I was happy to check out and move next door to the new Hyatt Lex58 . But that’s another review….
Overall, I was disappointed in the property, their handling of my reservations, and the awful state of Internet service in the hotel. I’d certainly encourage others to look elsewhere at this price point and in this neighborhood. There certainly are plenty of other options within several blocks.

title: “A Great Place to Stay”
text: We used to live in Columbus, so when we go back, we wanted to pick a nice hotel for us and the kids. The Hilton Columbus at Easton fit the bill. It is primarily utilized by business customers but the service and hotel are excellent. The buffet is very delicious and reasonable and one of the best features is being 100 yards away from Easton Town Center - a one-of-a-kind outdoor mall with very upscale restaurants (Brio, Cheesecake Factory), and shops along with a movie theater and great ice cream shop. We have been back several times and each time the stay is enjoyable with pleasant staff and a nice indoor pool. This will be our hotel of choice when we visit Columbus. The only thing to note is that if you are interested in a suite or other special room - you should book early (especially if it is on the weekend as they sell-out quickly).

title: “Very good for families”
text: Overall we had a pleasant stay. Clean, comfortable good location. Mainly families with kids. Breakfast was ok but queues of kids. No room service if you arrive late. Would be back if with family.

title: “Loved it!”
text: I just stayed for one night last week but the hotel was fabulous! The rooftop bar was great and the rooms are terrific....I'll be back!

title: “Lovely grounds, service could be better”
text:
We stayed in the Tropical View guest room. 
The room had a small area for basic refreshment making including a microwave and a fridge but no kettle (which is kind of an essential to Brits who like tea), it has a coffee maker. To be fair the hotel’s website does state the room amenities and to be honest if you want more extensive facilities you should book the suites.
The room was clean and beds were very large and comfortable. There was a big TV in the room and all the usual bits.
It was nice to have a small patio area with chairs and the grounds are well maintained and have a Hawaiian feel. The pool and hot tub are nice too.
Although we didn’t go to any concerts, we heard a couple. They don’t go on late so we didn’t mind, in fact it’s quite good to be able to listen for free!
The best thing about the hotel is the tropical atmosphere, beautiful grounds, clean comfortable rooms and the location. The free shuttle bus from the airport is handy too. There are a few shops and restaurants within walking distance and it’s nice to walk along the island and watch the pelicans etc.
The Sunday buffet is good, lots of choice and a great view over the harbour.
Negatives:
Parking is extra, $10 a night. There is some parking nearby but be careful as some of the parking notices are obscured by trees and you usually have to move your car very early in the morning because of street cleaning.
Service could be better – we politely informed reception that they had left our room door open, they seemed to ignore this as it happened a few times. We weren’t happy as we had laptops etc in the room, luckily no one took anything. 
When we stayed in June/July it was sometimes quite noisy during the day, but our room backed on to the main garden area, the grounds were well used by families for weddings etc. Also, some guest’s children used the manicured lawn for playing ball games and were very noisy. We don’t mind noise but at times it was excessive. Staff either did not notice or did not bother to do anything. This could be a problem if you wanted a peaceful place to stay etc.

title: “Great stay in nyc”
text: Staff was wonderful everyone greets everyday . Love Carlos the bellman,Maria check us in. Had a good room on 5th floor Riingo pancakes were great .

title: “shopping trip”
text: just come back from new york, stayed at affinia manhattan for the first time, stayed in 1 bedroom suite with the terrace, everything was as expected, very good room with good service from all the staff, all very friendly and helpful, stayed on 24th floor so no noise problems that other people have complained about, son slept on the put u up in lounge which he said was very comfortable, 4th visit to new york staying at different hotels each time but would be very happy to stay in this hotel again or recommend to other travellers.

title: “Good price, but you get what you pay for”
text: We stayed at the Red Roof Inn in Phoenix in March of 2006 and ended up moving to another hotel after one night. While the price was right, $65 during the very busy baseball Spring Training/Spring Break time, the hotel was average. There were very few ammenities and we had a lot of problems with our air conditioning, which can make a stay in Phoenix quite uncomfortable. There are a few sports bar/restaurant type places within walking distance (e.g. Applebee's), which was convenient, but the location is basically within a strip mall. If you are looking for a bargain hotel that you are just sleeping at, this place would be great, but if you actually want to enjoy your stay in between your other activities, I would suggest an upgrade. The staff was very nice however.

title: “Not as noisey and loud as most say it is”
text: The hotel was much more "Hollywood" in person than it appeared in pictures online. It was very elegant, clean and the staff were all very accommodating. We stayed in the basic King size bed room on the 6th floor over looking the pool and fireplace. I didn't hear a peep from the near by 405 freeway which was a plus considering the other reviews which complain so much about it. Our room was clean. Our bed was fluffy and sturdy. The LCD screen tv was do'able. My only gripe was the expensive valet and the cleaning lady barged into our room while we were watching tv. It was one of those knock-knock "HOUSE KEEPING" all in one instance situation. Overall, my experience at Hotel Angeleno was excellent and I would definitely stay here again. Thank you

title: “Great place, great location”
text: How tough is it to pick a hotel in NYC!? Very tough I would say, there's so much choice. After lots of research we chose the Westin Times Square mainly for the location. We were not dissapointed, the hotel is very good. It's a big place, but you don't really have that feeling when you enter it (which is a good thing I would say). Pay a bit extra for a room at the higher floors so the outside noise won't bother you so much. The room was clean and quite spacious, the bed was comfortable.

title: “Nice Hotel, good staff, Great for Party Time!”
text:
We have are San Diego locals, and have been to the Hard Rock a few times. The decor is very hip and modern. The hotel staff courteous, young and attractive. Most staff members are college students who do not have a long term investment in the job. This type of staff is fun and energetic, but has little interest in the job of solving guest issues. Every time we were next to the front desk, multiple parties were having room and service issues. It seems that a manager is very hard to locate. 
This is a very nice new hotel if you are looking for an All Night Party. The hotel floors are always full of guests on party nights. People book a room hand have large groups pack in to the rooms. There are rules about how many people and limits on outside alcohol, but these are not enforced by the staff. Do not get me wrong, this place is fun, it feels like Las Vegas. It will keep you up all night. Lucky for us locals, we can just go back home and get some sleep. I did feel bad for other guests from out of town who selected this hotel for a vacation and not a bachelor party. There are much better vacation spots in the same area. I have to give it a poor rating as a hotel.

title: “Perfect Stay at the O'Hare Hilton”
text:
This was our second time staying at this hotel. I am from Chicago and have stayed at a wide-range of hotels in the area from the suburbs to downtown. In my opinion, waking up well-rested at the airport before a flight is a luxury no other property in Chicago can offer. 
Access could not be easier from both the terminal and the city. The hotel is connected to the terminal by underground walkway, literally a 3 minute walk from terminal 2. The same underground walkway also houses the Blue Line train to the city (30 minutes to downtown). Trains to the city cost $2.25 each way per person and leave every 15 minutes. Why would you want to drive in horrible traffic and have to park downtown? We were in town for the Taste of Chicago and to meet friends for dinner. Chicago is such a great walking city.
The facilities at the hotel appear recently renovated as do the rooms. We had a wonderful (though a little expensive) Sunday brunch at the restaurant. Their homemade muffins are to die for! Our tenth floor room had a fantastic view of the terminal and 2 runways. Being plane enthusiasts, we loved this. The bedding and towels were plush and the walls were well sound-proofed. The staff was friendly, especially at the restaurant.
We left the Hilton feeling very rested to face our long double connection flights home. We will definitely stay there again when visiting my home town.

title: “It was accommodating, helpful and friendly”
text: This place is easy to find right off the highway. Check-in is at 3:00 PM and we arrive at 1:00 PM, but they were very accommodating and allowed us in our room at that time. This made our stay wonderful because we wanted to freshen up before we headed out for a graduation party. The service was great the people were very friendly and as always we have a free breakfast with Our stay.

title: “Great idea, poor execution”
text:
In theory, this is a great idea -- a self-serve hotel for a lower price. However, there are some serious problems with staffing and stocking. The decor is great, and if I were rating the hotel on decor alone I would give it 5 stars. Beautiful lobby, huge plasma screen tvs, decent-but-smallish pool. However, despite the remodel there are already signs of deterioration and the breakfast experience is a nightmare.
We stayed a Friday and Saturday night, for $119 plus tax per night. The room was very comfortable, if a bit tight. The sink faucet was tilted at a funny angle and was loose, and there was only a shower (no tub). But overall, the room was acceptable.
 However, the "free continental breakfast" is inadequate on every front. On Saturday morning, we went downstairs to discover sour milk, only one toaster with 4 slots, chemically tasting fruit, and an inadequately stocked tea display. Another gentleman pointed out the problem with the milk and placed it at the bakery window, where it sat for the next 40 minutes while we ate. I pointed out the problem with the tea. I used the kiosk to order the breakfast burrito, and I can't recommend ordering any hot breakfast. My $7 burrito arrived at the window 25 minutes (!!!) later, and was announced with a bark, "Burrito!" It had a raw-tasting tortilla, lukewarm eggs, unmelted cheese and canned salsa. The "hashbrowns" that came with it were a lukewarm glop of herbed mashed potatoes that had been barely cooked on one side to maintain integrity. Come on, I could have microwaved this myself and it would have tasted better.
Fast forward to right now, Sunday morning: no caffeinated tea, no decaffeinated coffee, no spoons, no juice, almost no cereal (healthier choices gone, froot loops and frosted flakes left), no bagels, no cream cheese, no half&half, no glasses (just mugs). I walked behind the "bar" to grab a packet of tea. Instead of continuing to stock his breakfast area, the gallery host came out to shake his finger at me. I told him he had absolutely no tea and that I had pointed this out to him 24 hours earlier. I'm amazed that he was policing the tea bag "theft," rather than taking care of his customers. Also, they are the same tea bags that are theoretically available in the continental breakfast area. To his credit, as I am typing this, I just saw him go behind the bar and grab the entire tea display and move it to the continental breakfast area. So maybe I'll give them 2.5 stars instead of 2.
The 2 desk hostesses have been incredibly nice to us and to our children. They are helpful and polite, but apparently they are not allowed to leave the desk area? It seems to me that on busy mornings, there needs to be one more person in the breakfast area to keep up with the larger groups of people. And a little respect from the manager/kitchen dude wouldn't hurt.
The next time we come to Austin and want the low-price, self-serve experience, we'll go to the La Quinta on South MoPac at Southwest Parkway: bigger rooms, better breakfast, nicer staff. Decor isn't as nice, but the total experience is better.

title: “Convenient Location”
text: Good location, very close to transit and great shopping. Took a cab from the airport instead of BART because the plane was very late and was traveling with older family members. Cab ride was only $35 to and from the airport. Hotel is close to all of the union square shopping, less than one mile from China Town, and we used the "F" street car stop to access Ferry building market place, Fishermans' Warf, etc.. Staff was friendly, rooms were clean, and service was prompt. Try not to park at the hotel - the fees are $48/night + tax. There are other lots around town that are a better deal and you really don't need a car in SF unless traveling to Napa. Also, the neighborhood west of the hotel is not very nice - stick to the areas north and east towards Union Square.

title: “Nice place to park your head in the burb's”
text: Not our first choice in Charlotte - but it will do. In town for the Giants game and the downtown hotels were full. Picked Hyatt Place as it was near the airport and a great value. Located in a corporate park it has a decent sports bar across the parking lot. Rooms were new and clean, staff was great and breakfast included. All in all a decent night.

title: “Great Hotel, but tiny bathrooms”
text:
We only stayed here 1 night, and maybe that's why they put us in what was possibly the worst room in the hotel. It was on the 4th floor at the end of the hall, with a winding staircase beside it. It looked like maybe an after thought, or where a much larger suite had been divided. We had a great view of a brick wall from the window, but the tiny bathroom is my biggest complaint. It was so small in the sink area, that when you went to brush your teeth, your elbows hit the side of the wall on the left, and the side of the shower on the right (I'm not kidding). 
I rated the hotel average for this reason, because there were many other good things about it. Although the room was small, it had beautiful bedding, super confortable bed, flat screen TV, and granite counter top in the bathroom. The entire hotel was spotless, including the room. I especially liked the pool/Courtyard area- beautifully decorated with flowers. There were rooms around the pool, with patios and balconies, but I guess we didn't pay enough for one of those. :-( , and as they say, location, location, location--was great. Right across the street from Union Square, and the Irish restaurant next door, Lefty O'douls, had great food with great prices. I'd recommend this hotel for a 1 or 2 night stay, but not any longer....unless you pay enough to get a larger room, with a full size bathroom.

title: “Crowne Plaza Downtown review”
text: Fantastic visit, very close to 16th Street Mall, room was great, resturant and hotel staff very friendly and helpful.

title: “A+++++, YOU WON'T BE DISAPPOINTED”
text:
We stayed at the Carlton Hotel from 22 November for 3 nights and to be honest I tried to change our booking following reading the negative reviews on tripadvisor. I couldn't get the booking changed so held my breath and hoped for the best. How glad I am that we had to go to the Carlton. The hotel is situated on Sutter Street which is about a 15 minute walk from Union Square, I know everyone keeps going on about the front desk staff but they have to be seen to be believed they are so helpful and friendly, really genuine and really do go the extra mile to make sure you have a great stay. Our room was based at the back of the hotel and had a massive bed, the room and bathroom were both tastefully decorated. 
The hotel is near the Tenderloin area which is not the best area in the city, but the staff do warn you on checkin not to go near it, we unfortunately wondered into it and did feel very threatened and vulnerable, although no one approached or even spoke to us, but we had been warned and should have paid more attention to where we were going.
Other reviews have also stated that the walls are paper thin in the hotel, I can categorically state that I am a light sleeper and I did not hear a single sound from the other rooms during our entire stay. I certainly could hear traffic and fire sirens but hey what do you expect if you are staying in the middle of a major city.
I really don't know what the negative reviewers are talking about, I am so glad I took a chance and stayed at this wonderful hotel.

title: “Just can't say enough”
text:
Dear Shannon and Thomas,
The Eventi makes its guests feel like family, and its staff exemplify professionalism.
I can't thank you enough! You and the hotel staff have taken such good care of me. I just adore Jocelyn, Caitlyn, Colby, and Dwayne. They are superb. Great examples of Kimpton customer service!

title: “Great location for family and friends for Chicago wedding”
text: Our family and friends stayed at the Hotel Monaco Chicago for our daughter's wedding. We all had a great time and enjoyed our stay. Thanks for the great service and helping to make this a memorable event for all of us!

title: “Hip But Still a Chain”
text:
I was at the W on business recently, and have stayed there before. The hotel has many things going for it (terrific pillowtop mattress, nice linens, Bliss toiletries, spacious rooms). The bar is, as already mentioned, pretty well-known in Seattle for its scene (although not as much as some Belltown places) -- but that's part of it being a W. 
My only gripe with the W is that after spending what, for Seattle, is a small fortune, they still won't provide free internet or local calls. If Starwood truly wants to build a boutique hotel brand, they should try acting like a boutique hotel, and stop trying to nickel and dime their customers.

title: “Terrible Room”
text: I needed a room for about 6 hours during a layover between flights. The room was dark, dingy, and had a VERY strong odor of tobacco smoke. The room was saturated with smoke odor and leaving the front door propped open for 2 hours was no remedy. Upon check out, the reply of the desk clerk was simply, "Here is your receipt". $125 for a 5 hour stay in a stinky, dingy room. PATHETIC. Avoid this hotel. It is old and smelly and there is NO customer service. Also, it appears someone had entered my room and used my bathroom while I was out having dinner.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text:
I just completed a 3 night stay at the Liaison with my wife and 2 teenage children and had a great experience. 
The kids loved trying out the specialty pillow selections and the beds were quite comfortable. The shower gel, shampoo and conditioner in the shower was also a nice touch.
The location was exactly what we wanted and allowed us to park the car for entire stay, and walk everywhere we wanted to go including the Capital, Union Station, all of the sites on the mall, the White House, etc. 
The staff was extremely helpful both before arriving (working with me to find a way to minimize the high valet parking expense) as well as during our stay. A really nice touch was the votive candles that lined the lobby hallway each evening when we returned to the hotel after long days of sightseeing. Very warm and inviting!
The hotel restaraunt, Art and Soul, is pricey, but we found many reasonable alternatives in the area including the Capital Brewery and a number of places in Union Station.
The only substantial complaint I have is that free internet access in the room was not included, especially after having stayed at a Sleep Inn the night before arriving here, and having gotten a cheaper rate that included not only free wireless internet but a deluxe continental breakfast in the morning as well!
All things considered though, I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Can’t believe how dirty the rooms are”
text: If you like mold, you’ll like this hotel. I booked 3 rooms to attend a weekend wedding. The shower curtains have mold at the bottom, so are the bathroom ceilings. The bath tub has black hair on the side. I guess the cleaning lady forgot to throw them in the trash. The wallpapers are peeling, and the bed sheet is thinner than a tissue. I was so embarrassed to have booked for my relatives from overseas for the wedding.

title: “Strapped for cash but need to be on the Upper West Side?”
text:
My go-to neighborhood is the upper West Side..Yes there are better deals in Times Sq etc, but it is so noisy and crowded.My husband and I stay over in Manhattan at least three times a year and I can tell the economy is coming back, because my usual West Side hotel, the Excelsior, has gotten a bit too expensive for my still recessionary budget. So, I went to a discount travel site and got On The Ave hotel. I read the reviews here at Tripadvisor, and decided, despite the tiny rooms, etc, I would book it. The travel site I used called this a 4 star hotel. That is a real stretch, but it did have some important things going for it. First the good: Very comfy bed, pillows; nice modern decor, QUIET, Very nice staff, without exception, gleaming chrome in marble/slate bath, good toiletries, nice linens (except for the comforter with the black X in magic marker that stuck out from the cover.. not sure what that meant), ,Kuerig coffee maker in room, flat screen tv; nice neighborhood close to my fave French breakfast spot, The Petit Matin, in the hotel Lucerne. Close to subway(2 blocks)..And high hat lighting which is dimmable. NIce touch -and a lamp on each side of the bed. 
Now the stuff I was not nuts about, but not major to me..room VERY small, even by Manhattan standards,( I got a standard sized king room, with equally skinny claustrophobic halls. If you are a person of size or claustrophobic, do take this into account! Although they put new caulking in the shower, there was a lot of brown gunk on the edges that just happens when some water leaks out. Some bleach and a toothbrush or a razor blade are needed there.. I mentioned it to the front desk.. Wallpaper ripped all along where the chair hit it. Yes, there is only one chair at a desk with no lamp. No other table and chair, so if you spend any time in the room, you have to be in bed or at the desk. There is not a dresser, but some shelves in the closet, and drawers in the desk. The bathroom is actually kind of cool in that it has a marble shower and a funky/hip stainless steel square sink. There is a hairdryer, and iron. I would go back. My husband would not. He said it looks like a renovation that did not pay enough attention to detail. He is far more meticulous than I am.

title: “Somewhat disappointing”
text:
We stayed at the Travelodge Golden Gate three nights (Thurs-Sun) in early December. Initially, I was mildly optimistic that we would have a good stay here. However, I left feeling disappointed and a bit cranky after three nights of broken sleep.
The Good:
1.) Good location. Easy to find, within walking distance of an IHOP, near some nice shops, pubs, and eateries (just walk one block north to Chestnut St.), near the Palace of Fine Arts/the Exploratorium. 
2.) Fairly up-to-date decor with some amenities (TV, microwave).
3.) Includes parking. (Parking can be hard to find/expensive in San Francisco.)
4.) Friendly staff.
5.) Reasonable price, when taking into account the going rate for accommodations in San Francisco. 
The Bad:
1.) The noise. The walls are thin. You will hear traffic from Lombard Street all night long, which earplugs may help block out. However, my earplugs were not able to block out the loud men in a room next to ours who shouted and guffawed from midnight to 2:30 am one night, nor the people who decided it would be fun to repeatedly pound on the walls of their room at midnight another night. Being a courtyard-style motel, and within walking distance of pubs, you will hear people coming and going into the early hours of the night, banging the heavy outside doors to their rooms. I am usually a sound sleeper, but all this noise was enough to break up my sleep and keep me awake for long stretches. 
2.) Uncomfortable beds and pillows. I found the beds too soft and lacking in support, which is typical of motels, and which might not have bothered me so much if I wasn't lying awake because of the noise. 
3.) Even though this is a non-smoking property, someone in a room near ours lit up a few times, and the smoke quickly infiltrated our room each time. 
4.) The parking seemed to be on a first-come, first-served basis. Although we always had a spot, there didn't seem to be enough spots to go around for everybody. Also, the stalls are narrow, so you will have to jockey your vehicle back and forth to fit. 
5.) While the room seemed to be clean, for the most part, the shower curtain needed replacing as it was mildewy. The exterior of the building definitely needs sprucing up. 
6.) Even though the staff is friendly, they were not willing to compensate us in any way for the three nights of broken sleep. They also do not seem to project an authoritative enough demeanor, hence I think many of their clients realize they can get away with disrespectful behaviour (noise late at night, smoking in rooms, etc.). 
Despite this motel's good points, I wouldn't stay here again. When you only have a few days to explore the city, you need a good night's sleep to make the most of your days. I might try Cow Hollow next time, which is just up the street from this motel.

title: “It was Okey”
text:
This is my first stay at Towneplace. I stayed for 6nights.
The location is good as you can go to restaurant or Burger King on foot. The room has full kitchen. But I was disappointed their breakfast. There is no table or chair to eat, and all cold food. The area is very small, and if there are five people, there is no room to be. Therefore, I always take some food to my room and eat it at my room.
The room was clean, but the housekeeping person left cleaning cloth in the room for twice while my 6 nights stay.
The other thing that I disappointed was the wall is too thin as StoneAlone mentioned... I could heat iPhone vibrating in the next room, and all conversation on the telephone of the next room. I could also heat foot steps of upper floor person, So if you are the person who care about noise, I do not recommend this hotel. Probably one or two night would be Okey.

title: “Can't wait to return!”
text:
Fantastic and very gracious staff. Beautiful decor and large rooms for New York. Great beds! Love the high-tech rooms (husband and I are kinda of geeks for that stuff), but could see how it could be confusing to some. I think this place will be amazing when it is done. My only downside was arriving to find out that neither the pool nor the spa was open yet. This was not clear on the website from which I made the reservation. I also was disappointed that our room was not the floor plan advertised for a "Deluxe" guest room (ours was smaller). While we paid for the "Deluxe" so that we could be on a higher floor; we were placed on the 21st floor (the lowest floor on which we could be and still be considered "deluxe") With the missing amenities (pool and spa) I would have expected them to make it up a little by at least giving us a better room within the same grade. I didn't need an upgrade, just not the least they could give us.
Overall though...fantastic place. I look forward to making this our New York home away from home and visiting the spa when I come back.

title: “Great location, shame about the staff”
text:
I have to agree with the previous review that the staff at the Kitano were in no way friendly or helpful. We also experienced struggling with our bags whilst the door man looked on. Reception were also cold, making no effort to engage in polite conversation - we were on our honeymoon and we didn't even get a contratulations. 
I could also smell smoke in our non-smoking room, but at the time I thought it was just me going potty so I didn't complain!
The other thing about this hotel that annoyed me greatly was the internet charge for wifi - $10 for 24 hours. I find this greedy when the room rates are so high.
On the plus side, the location is good - a short stroll to the Empire State, Chrysler, Grand Central Terminal, 5th Avenue, Time Square and Central Park
The rooms were well maintained and had adequate space and a nice bathroom. The view from the window was good - Empire state building.
I would visit the Kitano again, but because of the location and the fact that the rooms were quiet.

title: “A PERFECT 10”
text: We stayed in rm 2205 on 03/05/2011 and I had an amazing weekend getaway with my wife for her 40th Birthday. We've stayed at a lot of great hotels and this one is defnitely at the top. We were treated like royalty from the time we checked in until we checked out. The room was so spacious and the fireplace was a very nice touch.(Not sure if they are in all the rooms so that is why I specified rm 2205. The bathrooms are great too, the tub is enormous and the mirror with a push of a button turns into a TV. The location could'nt be any better walk to beach, bars, top restaurants, mag mile shopping. This is the first time I ever wrote a review, but felt I had to because this place is an absolute GEM. It made us feel that we were on a second honeymoon!

title: “Very disappointed with the room and lack of service”
text: My husband and I are not fussy and exacting travelers so when we had to drop off our daughter at college we thought we would give this place a try despite the mostly negative evaluations. However, sad to report, the negative evaluations are deserved. After we checked into the room, we realized that the (one and only) light over the bed was missing a lampshade and bulb. My husband went downstairs to ask for a new bulb, (because the room phone was not working!) and was told that if one could be found, it would be delivered. It never was. We expected traffic noise from the streets below, after all , the hotel is at a major intersection; however, we were not expecting garbage trucks in the middle of the night. The noise, compounded by the rather chilly temperatures, made for a poor night's rest. There were only 2 bath towels, 1 hand towel, and 1 face towel for us both. "Breakfast" was a tray set with two packages which contained a granola bar, tinned peaches, two tangerines, and 2 bottles of water. A mini coffee maker and packets of coffee and tea were also included. When I went downstairs at 8:30 to try to get a regular cup of coffee with cream, I was told by the lone person in the bar area that the coffee person was running late and that I would be able to get a cup of coffee in a half hour. At that point, my husband and I checked out .

title: “Housekeeping and maintenance becoming iffy”
text:
This was my second stay at this hotel. The location on Michigan Avenue is excellent, close to Millennium Park, shopping, restaurants, the Art Institute, and a reasonable walk to Navy Pier,the Field Museum, Shedd Aquarium, Adler Planetarium, etc. 
The front desk people were welcoming and friendly. As is typical for Comfort Inns, the bed was very comfortable. (When staying at chain hotels, I prefer this chain for their comfortable beds.) 
Alas, I found the facility becoming just a bit seedy. In my first room on this stay, several slats were missing from the blinds. Although maintenance promptly replaced some, the mechanism holding one of the slats was broken so that slat could not be replaced. Also, the blinds in one of the windows didn't properly close. The hotel changed my room. In the second room, the stove burners, apparently replacements, did not fit properly. The top of the toilet tank had cracked at some time in the past. Although the repair was sound enough from a functional standpoint, it was sloppily done. (Why not just replace the tank top?)
The quick cleaning administered daily by the housekeeping staff did not always include vacuuming. Also, on my second morning I left a few dishes in the dishwasher, intending to run the dishwasher after more had accumulated. Returning while my room was being cleaned, I was horrified when I saw the maid unloading the dirty dishes from the dishwasher, rinsing the dishes by hand in the sink with only tap water - no soap - then returning the dishes to the cabinets.
I ate breakfast at the hotel on my first morning. The eggs resembled rubbery yellow discs. After that, I passed on the hotel breakfast. 
Would I recommend this hotel? I'm not sure. The price is reasonable for the excellent location. Increased management attention to maintenance and housekeeping details would be welcome.

title: “Excellent hotel, beautiful rooms”
text:
I booked this room through Priceline at an extremely reasonable rate. The hotel is located in downtown San Jose. Valet parking was cheap for an urban area ($25). We chose this hotel because they allowed pets.
The rooms were large and well appointed. The bed was small (queen) but extremely comfortable. The bathroom had marble surfaces and included a separate tub and shower. The hotel had a very nice health spa. The restaurant was excellent, though pricey. I highly recommend this hotel and would stay there again.

title: “Nice Location for Shoppers”
text:
We stayed here in October while attending the Hardly, Strictly, Bluegrass festival in Golden Gate Park. We were given a room on the 21st floor that had a large picture window facing east with nice views of the city and the Bay Bridge beyond. It was fleet week, and they had a large fireworks show over the bay that we could see from our window.
As others have said, the rooms are somewhat small (but that is the norm for most hotels in the city) but they are well appointed. The bathroom was adequate but nothing special but there was good pressure and plenty of hot water in the shower.
The rooms have plasma tvs and a Sony CD component system. However, there was no high def available and so all you could get from their satellite feed was the standard broadcast "stretched" to fill the Plasma screen. For most this would not be an issue because you don't stay at the Nikko to watch TV but our visit coincided with the Baseball Playoffs and I wanted to catch some of the games. It would have been great to have seen them in high def.
