Also, the stereo system is very nice but there is just a cheap speaker box above the Sony components which did not sound very good. There should be a speaker system built into the walls or ceiling to get the most out of the music.
We didn't use the swimming pool or fitness center because they charged too much. That should be included at the room rates they charge. We also didn't eat in their restaurant but did have room service one night and found the quality and service excellent and not really overpriced at all.
As others have commented, it's not necessary to pay extra for the buffet breakfast because there is a Starbucks downstairs and across the street is a fairly decent and reasonable coffee shop that serves breakfast.
All in all, we enjoyed our stay at the Nikko. It was convenient to the buses we needed to take out to GG Park and we were also able to spend several hours over at the new mall that has Bloomingdales and Nordstroms. In the basement there is an excellent market that has many hot food offerings that are reasonably priced and looked very good. There are also several inexpesive restaurants to choose from. We ate here one night since I had a cold and had no taste buds so I didn't want to waste my money at the fine restaurants nearby.
The Nikko is in a great location right near Union Square and close to the best shopping and also the theater district. The surrounding neighborhood can be a litte seedy if you walk down the wrong streets but overall this area is far improved from what I remember it being in the '70s when I lived in San Francisco. They didn't call it the Tenderloin because there were good steak restaurants nearby. However, from our room, we could look down at Tad's Steak House which, as a starving student in the '60s, was one of the few restaurants I could afford. Next time, we will go check it out.

title: “Avoid this Hotel if you want the basics”
text:
I made the mistake of staying at this Hotel last fall. I made the mistake of thinking the pictures on the hotel's website was actually a real room at the hotel. This is an old, tiny, dirty and cheap hotel. Maybe some people like this type of accommodations but not me. I left this hotel after one night of misery and went to the Hilton at Time Square. 
I felt born again when I stepped into my Hilton room.

title: “We Thought Better!”
text: Good location to visit S.F. near Chinatown and Market Street. Room clean but not so renovated. Little breakfast. The staff was not so friendly like we thought when we booked (by mail).

title: “Its OK for a Kimpton”
text: This is a very boutiquish hotel with funky decor. The hotel rooms are pretty small with not much storage space. The desk was a bit small but adequate for doing work. The TV was nice with a somewhat decent amount of channels. The bed was pretty comfortable, but nothing great, and the air conditioner worked fairly well. The wireless internet here is very inconsistent. It kept dropping out frequently, but when it did work the speeds were decent. The bathroom was small, but the shower was nice. Overall this is an alright hotel. Nothing great here, but it is in a great location.

title: “Great value in nice neighborhood”
text:
We stayed for the second time within two months in this motor inn and think it is a great value for San Francisco. We paid - depending on the season- between $90 and $125 for a room and ZERO for parking. After paying up to $55 for parking in other hotels in SF we like the Cow Hollow Motor Inn even better. True, the rooms are plain, but I don't expect in this price range high end luxury. The staff is always helpful - our request for a room not facing busy Lombard Street was always honored. 
We also love the Cow Hollow neighboorhood with its nice, small restaurants, wine bars and coffe shops. Ate at Izzy's steakhouse on Steiner and roamed through the wine bars on Chestnut --- just delightful.

title: “Not a family place”
text: Stayed here for the LA marathon. Checked in a bit early and our room wasn't ready when we got our key. Went in the room and 1 bed wasn't ready and the white sheet had a bloody hand print on it!!! It makes you wonder what kind of people stay here. We asked for a different room and got a room with non-working TV and the hot shower was slow to get hot. We were worried the whole time and didn't sleep very well. We also heard our upstairs neighbor walking around. If you have no kids and just want to get through the night, this motel is very cheap for being close to the Santa Monica pier. I won't stay here again though.

title: “funky, comfortable rooms”
text:
We stayed at the Carlyle April 26th and 27th. We were pleasantly surprised by the art deco styling and large clean rooms. The lobby area and hallways were all redecorated and were fun and funky. We had a corner room with pull out couch, very nice small kitchen, and newly remodled bathroom- all with granite countertops and tile floors. The elevators were newly renovated and worked fine.
Parking is definitely a problem- you are better off without a car to park. We sqeezed our van in but it was the luck of the draw with very few spaces. 
The Dupont Circle neighborhood was outstanding with many wonderful small restaurants and outdoor patios. A grocery story is located nearby and was very convenient with the kitchen in our room.
This hotel would be great for an extended stay and feels more like home than a hotel. The staff was helpful with directions and most staff were friendly and helpful when prompted but did not go out of their way.
We stayed there with two boys ages 8 and 11- they loved the hotel. We will return, next time without a car.

title: “Not the best but definitely not the worst.”
text:
I have visited this facility( formerly the Baymont) on two occasions. Initially, I was pleased with the cleanliness of the room and facility. However, upon the second visit the room wasn't quite as impressive. 
This establishment is nice for the rate. They have complimentary breakfast and wifi which is always a plus. They do have on site laundry(one washer and dryer) for about $2.50 a load. The beds are comfortable not hard like most places.Most of all, the staff is firendly and helpful which is always a plus.

title: “WONDERFUL STAY!”
text: The Allerton is a quaint and luxurious hotel! My boyfriend and I booked a reservation (for 2 nights) for our first trip to Chicago and were MORE than pleased! The staff can be described as pleasant, helpful, informative, and genuinely interested in making sure we had the best possible stay. Working in the hospitality industry ourselves, we had rather high expectations and every single one of them was met, if not, exceeded! The bell staff informed us of all features in the room upon taking us in; the front desk was swift and gracious about switching our room to a different view per our request; housekeeping / guest services was prompt in servicing our room as well as bringing additional items we needed; the concierge was very informative and we were permitted to have our bags stored after check out while we enjoyed the city some more before leaving. Our suite was cozy, clean and provided a WONDERFUL view of the downtown Chicago area! We will certainly look forward to staying here again, additionally the value was great!!!

title: “Great hotel in a good location”
text: Hotel is situated in a good location, a little off the main routes so its not super busy outside the hotel. Concierge is great - good recommendations. Room was good, decent size, clean and comfortable bed. A few of the things that kept it from being 5/5 was a few little things that were not at or above peer levels - lighting controls in the room were a bit of a pain - for example, no controls on the side lamps (have to walk to them to turn off/on), blinds in bathroom didn't close 100%. But these are small things that separate hotels in the top tier charging a high tariff from being good vs great. The above being said, we would not hesitate to stay there again.

title: “Start of Route 66 Trip”
text: Location is excellent. We got the train into the centre of Chicago from O'Hare Airport and a short taxi trip to the hotel. Easy walking distance to the city centre. Walked to the river to take the excellent evening architectural tour on day 1. Walked to the Art Centre and Park where the Blues festival was taking place on day 2. Plenty of good restaurants near by. Hotel is typical Doubletree, clean, fairly modern and helpful staff. The only complaint was that WiFi was charged and was the only one that wasn't free throughout our whole 3 week Route 66 tour. The advert said lake view and I was thinking we'd wake up the a great view every morning. However the reality was that, yes you could see the lake, but only a small piece through a gap in the buildings in front.

title: “Great stay”
text: Fabulous stay at the ZaZa. Great funky hotel in good location. Lovely pool area with cool vibe at the weekends. We booked a standard room, which wasn't huge but was certainly well decorated and very comfortable. Excellent staff, special thanks to Spencer for taking care of us. This is what a hotel should be!

title: “Awesome Bronco Stadium View!”
text:
I got stranded in Denver after Greyhound overbooked their buses. Someone mentioned the Hotel VQ, so I stayed here. The rooms are spacious & clean; the staff is superb! On BRONCO GAME DAYS/WEEKENDS, their rooms to up to $140; that's super cheap, especially since you are literally backed up to Mile High Stafium's Parking Arena!
I'll definitely stay here again!

title: “single room”
text:
I stayed in a single room with bath at the cost of $99 a night. This is a great price for NYC. When I booked this room I was told it was a very small room, so I was prepared. The room itself was in the back of the hotel on the 5th floor. It was about 8 X 10 feet in size plus a private bathroom with a tub. The room was very basic, it did have a window that opened on to a air shaft. It allowed light to enter, the view was to a solid wall of a building. My bed was very comfortable and had only one pillow. The room was very clean. I did have one instance of a bug, when I called downstairs they offered to change my room and spray.
The staff at this hotel were very friendly and helpful. I did enjoy the tea and candies in the entrance area. The hotel had two elevators. 
A great location, very close to Penn Station. I do recommend this hotel. Be prepared for a very tiny room if you choose a single. I will stay here again.

title: “Great Hotel for what we paid”
text:
We liked the location of this hotel. It also has a great bar scene and the food is very good for a hotel. Hip and fun stay. It is in no way top notch. Light bulns burned out, not totally clean. you can tell people have rocked out a bit too much in each room. So do not expect 5 star. But it is very cool, food great, very nice bed. Do not Pay over $200 a night.
AGAIN, STOP NICKLE AND DIMING GUESTS WITH INTERNET. THAT KEPT YOU FROM A 5 STAR RATING.

title: “Still OK- but I'll look for other options on the next trip.”
text:
My review from March, 2011 still, mostly, holds true. This is dog-friendly hotel close to the interstate that we've stayed at a few times during the past several years. We had no problems with the most recent stay although the room rate was bit higher. In March our room rate was < $75. At that rate the hotel value/quality was above-average. For the most recent stay, the rate was nearly $100. Summer rates perhaps? At that rate, though, the value/quality is just average.
I would stay here again, but I'm definitely going to check out other nearby options.

title: “Only so so....”
text: It was a nice stay at the Hotel Sax over the long weekend. Room is spacious and bed is quite comfortable. Bathroom is huge and clean; nice having a hot shower after a long day. It is centrally located, most of the attractions are accessible by foot. However, one down side is the service. Concierge was not helpful and check in took a long time. We waited in line for half an hour with our luggages. When we checked in, the lady didn't have any smile and seemed like she was a bit frustrated. Given this experience, I would say Hotel Sax is average. It is not quite the boutique experience that it claims to be.

title: “Beautiful place and nice amenities”
text:
We just stayed there this past weekend for our wedding anniversary. When we drove up it looked like we were in some tropical island. Beautiful and lush landscape. Everyone from the concierge, the receptionist, the entire staff at the restaurants were very friendly. I recommend eating at the Barefoot Bar, it was great!
The hotel has 5 pools, one of them is just for adults. The bungalows by the beach are beautiful. They also have fire pits for everyone, first come, first serve. We casually mentioned to the staff it was our anniversary, they gave us some cookies and they also sent us a bottle of wine and a plate of fruit as a gift. Very nice! 
Our room was a Lanai Premium guestroom, it was very spacy and next to a lagoon. close to one of the pools. The only thing I would have changed here was the sliding door for the bathroom that never worked. There was also a little bit of a moldy smell in our room. the hotel is very close to seaworld. This is great for families traveling for a mini vacation to San Diego. Be prepared for an extra $32 dollars a day for parking fee and a $17 a day amenity fee. That was a little discouraging.

title: “Great location, Friendly staff, room was ok, but not great.”
text: Stayed here for one night. Staff was friendly and got a nice warm cookie at check-in. The hotel staff notified us that Prince Charles and Camila were in town and staying across the street from us, because of this there would be some street closures. They provided us a sheet with a map and the times the street closures would occur. Our room was on the 7th floor, and we faced Broad street. It was a little noisy in the middle of the night, but that was because of Prince Charles and his entourage arriving at 1AM and security erecting a security tent infront of the hotel. Had it been any other night, I think it would have been a quiet night. The bed was comfortable, with plenty of pillows. The ceiling could have used a new paint job, especially in the bathroom, where you could see some of the paint peeling. Got a decent deal on Priceline.com. I don't think I would pay full price for this hotel though. Parking was a little under 20 dollars. If you drive in, it can get a little confusing where to park during check in. Also because of the no left turns/U-turns on Broad street, had to go a little out of the way to get into the parking garage. Breakfast was not included, but did have breakfast on their second floor restuarant. Food was good. You could have either a buffet style breakfast or order something from the kitchen. Overall not a bad experience, would stay here again only for the price I initally paid for on Priceline.

title: “Beautiful Resort on a great location”
text:
We enjoyed our 3 days at the Catamaran. We did the bed and breakfast plan and enjoyed delicious breakfasts (esp. the belgium waffle with real syrup and whipped cream, blackberries and raspberries and candied walnuts.) Restaurant was too expensive so we would not have eaten there otherwise. 
Room is nicely decorated and comfortable. We were expecting a Garden view room and ended up on the 10th floor of the tower overlooking the bay and ocean....what a beautiful view. The room had a kitchenette and living area. Location is close to everything and only 1 block from the ocean and lots of restaurants.
The grounds are beautiful with a lagoon with fish, ducks, exotic birds and nice landscaping. There is a Polynesian feel to the hotel with a waterfall in the lobby. Sailboats and paddleboats are available for rental

title: “Very Nice Hotel, Friendly Staff Great Stay!”
text: I had a wonderful stay at this hotel. Everything was nice and tidy and my room was very nice and clean. The staff was very helpful and very friendly. I had a great breakfast in the restaurant and the waiter I had was so awesome. Had a wonderful time staying here and would definitely stay again. The price isn't bad either. Met my needs since we were only staying a night and we all enjoyed our experience.

title: “cute trendy hotel, but watch out for the ridiculous parking rates if you drive!”
text:
As many reviews have said, it's a cute trendy hotel. The bar is cool,
Room is small but this is New York City. If you like modernism design
you'll love the room. It's clean, the floor is wooden, not carpet, so
it doesn't feel as cozy but then you don't have to worry about how dirty the carpet might be. There is no sign on the front of the building so it's very easy to miss it. 
My biggest complaint is about the parking rate they charge. I parked my car there for 2 nights. I was told it was $49 when I checked out, which would be normal in NYC, but later found out it's $49 PER NIGHT!
They actually use the parking garage of Warner Center across the street and the posted rates there is about $25 per day. I wish they could have made it clear to me instead of giving me the little surprise.

title: “Did I stay at the same hotel as other reviewers?”
text:
Hotel Nikko has all the charm and appearance of an airport lounge. The rooms are spacious and fairly well appointed, nothing wrong there, and for a city hotel it's surprisingly quiet in the rooms, but from top to bottom the place is dated, sterile, devoid of personality and somewhat tired looking. The place had its heyday 20 years ago it would seem. I'm shocked few other reviewers point this out.
I stayed in an Imperial King room on the 24th room and had access to the 23rd floor lounge but everywhere I went, from the lounge to the Anzu restaurant, the facilities were sad. Anzu, supposedly a sushi restaurant had zero sushi when I went, mediocre service and I ended up walking outside to have dinner.
I'm writing this review from my Nikko hotel room right now and to be fair, inside, the room has a different (and better) feel than about the hotel.
Still for the same price (almost $300 for the Imperial King) you can find a much better place, and for another $90 or so, you stay at the Mandarin Oriental or Ritz Carlton, either which completely demolishes Hotel Nikko.
If you arrive by car, it's another $55 to leave your car overnight at the hotel, a price I found kinda exorbitant.
I don't find anything egregiously wrong with the hotel but I don't find anything really good about it, especially for the price.

title: “AWESOME LOCATION.. GOOD VALUE FOR MONEY”
text: The location of the hotel was great as you are right at the center of Manhattan when you make your first step from hotel to outside. However hotel staff was not as good as the location. As they were just average not very helpful i can't praise them..Rooms are quite tiny but clean . I would surely reccomend this place for the travellers who are looking for a budget and central place to stay in NY City..

title: “Great Value and Service”
text: I stay several nights a year at Fairmont hotels as a member of their free President's Club, and this hotel does not disappoint. With the President's Club comes free Internet, newpaper, health club, discounts on spa services, etc. If you stay 10 qualifying nights a year in a Fairmont hotel, you will receive certificates good for room upgrades and a free third night. Service is impeccable at this hotel, and they go out of the way for their guests. The hotel is within walking distance of great Chicago shopping, Downtown, Grant Park, museums and a large, upscale grocery store, should you want to pick up some prepared food or a good bottle of wine. The Concierge floor offers many amenities, nice city and water views, and a lovely spread of food three times a day. Valet parking is expensive at $58, but there are less expensive options nearby.

title: “Unbeatable location!”
text: Clean spacious room (and bathroom) with a gorgeous river view. Very comfy queen size bed and being on the 24th floor, it was very quiet.Hotel staff friendly and accommodating. The location was perfect! If I were to be picky, I'd suggest to management that they upgrade their toilet paper....

title: “Not so COMFORTable”
text: The rooms were roomy and clean, but the tv cable connection was not very good...it was fuzzy. The night shift was asleep when we arrived and my husband kept clearing his throat to wake the gentleman up. When we went to get the complimentary breakfast there was none because they didn't have any warmers working, and our vehicle was broken into during the night with some valuables stolen.

title: “Excellent Room, unscrupulous employee . . .”
text: The actual hotel and room was great- HOWEVER, I got screwed out of $20!! I had called ahead before my stay and was told that parking was a flat rate of $20. When checking-in the woman asked if I parked in the garage. I told her I did and she handed me a card with my room number and what not, and she said to show it to the parking attendant. She did NOT tell me though, that they would automatically charge the $20 to my credit card! I didn't know then, but aparently the card was just so that I could leave and come back in to the garage throughout the day. Upon leaving the hotel I presented the parking attendant with the card the woman gave me and $20. That man took my $20!! He had to have just put it in his pocket. Now I can't get my $20 back because the guy didn't give me a reciept. They need to train the ppl at the front desk to explain what they are giving the guests, and they need to explain what integrity is to the parking garage attendant!

title: “Good Choice for Midtown”
text:
We stayed here in late January for a very reasonable price. The location is excellent - just a couples of minutes on foot to Central Park, and about a fifteen minute walk to Times Square. There are two subway lines close by.
The rooms are spacious for New York, and the hotel is very clean - no bedbugs. There were two (!) large closets. It is, however, dated, especially the bathroom - about early 80's vintage. If that doesn't bother you, then book a room.
There were extra charges for everything, from local calls to Internet access to the continental breakfast. What bothered me about the breakfast is that they made it seem free with the "voucher" they slid under your door, but it costs $9 a person. Save your money and go to one of the diners all along 57th St.
The staff were polite enough but didn't go out of their way to help us. They weren't particularly knowledgeable about the city, and made it seem like an irritation to look things up. On the other hand, I never felt obliged to tip the doorman or concierge, which was a bit of a relief after some other places we've stayed.
57th St is very busy and noisy. There is major construction right across the street (Jan 2012) that will be on-going for a long time, from the look of it. We wore earplugs at night even way up on the 15th floor.
Overall this is a very decent place to stay in the Big Apple.

title: “wonderful stay”
text:
We just returned from 4 nights at The London hotel in New York city. Great location on 54th between 6th and 7th. 
Large clean rooms and great shower. We had a large sitting room off the bedroom, walk in closet and nice work area. 
Well priced and the location was in the middle of everything. Try it.

title: “Great location if you're a shopper”
text: The Hilton is located close to many malls and shopping centers. All the stores are conveniently located within walking distance. Staff was very friendly and helpful in providing directions to the various attractions. Rooms are decent, nothing spectacular. Grabbing a taxi from the airport to the hotel is expensive o I would suggest taking the metro or shuttle.

title: “Wonderful, caring employees”
text:
I had a wonderful four night stay at the Fairmont in Seattle. I was there for work and originally booked for three nights. Unfortunately I became ill overnight on my last night there from food poisoning from a local restaurant (not one of the ones at the Fairmont!). Being sick alone in a hotel room far from home is no fun, but everyone at the Fairmont went totally above and beyond to make me as comfortable as possible. Everyone I interacted with was very caring--the bellman who brought me some pepto-bismol from the gift shop below, the housekeeper to whom I apologized profusely (and tipped what I hope was generously enough) when she had to clean up the bathroom which was in not such a nice state after my illness, and everyone else whom I dealt with as I was recovering. The "Royal Service" agent who assisted me on the phone was helpful first with my request for a late checkout and then, when I realized I was not going to recover in time to make my afternoon flight, arranged for me to stay in the room for another night, charging the same (low) group rate that I'd had for my original booking. They even surprised me with a complimentary bowl of soup as I recovered--just what I needed. All of this gave me a very positive feeling about the employees and their care and attentiveness towards their guests.
Even before that I had really enjoyed my time at the Fairmont--very pleasant and well-appointed complimentary health club and pool and nicely decorated rooms with curtains that overlap to provide a true "blackout" for a good night's sleep. The decor style is classic and old-fashioned--if that doesn't appeal to you then you won't be at home here but I loved it.

title: “Enjoyed! Staff very accommodating!”
text: The room was beautiful! A/C wasn't working properly when we first checked in but they had someone up to take a look and everything was taken care of within an hour. Concierge was great! Wonderful Location!

title: “Great place to experience my first Destination Spa”
text:
So, I must admit, I have never stayed at a spa overnight before, and in fact, I have never even been to a day spa for a simple massage. That being said, this place was top notch. The room we stayed in was named after Lady Bird Johnson who has stayed there in the past. We had a private Hot Tub in an enclosed patio.
This was also my first massage. My girlfriend and I got the couples "Texas Starry Night" massage which was in the dark in a small enclosed area with private hot tub. This was my first massage and it was everything (and more) than I could have ever imagined. 80 minutes of bliss.
We also attended the Nautical Noodles class, a water work out with those floating noodles. Sandy, the instructor, was very nice and also lead the Boat/Hike the next morning.
Overall, the place is super friendly. The staff really seem to enjoy themselves here and love their jobs which is important at a place like this.
If my lady and I ever get the chance to experience a place like this again, I am sure we will return.

title: “Ok”
text:
we booked the hotel with a very good rate (99$ parking incl.) and we saw the regular rate in the room.... 400 and something.... too much
Our room was very big: kitchen, sitting room with sofa, nice bedroom ( confortable bed), small bathroom and 2 flat tv. Furniture are a little old and you feel this oldness all around the room. Position is fantastic, you are in the middle of georgetown and 10-15 block to the white house. Breakfast was included but it is basic and you should fight to reach a table. All in All i reccomend this hotel at bargain prices not at 400..... last but not least: free business center (you can print and surf) and free wifi in the room!

title: “Bed was nice!”
text: My husband and I just stayed here for one night. The room was clean and the bed was very comfortable! Would stay here again.

title: “Hidden Gem”
text: Picked this hotel as part of a vacation package and could not have been happier during our first visit to Chicago. Great location at the northern end of the Magnificient Mile and just south of the Gold Coast neighborhood and Lincoln Park. If you like to walk to various venues--as we do--this is the place to stay. Recent renovations are excellent, though not much room to move around in a single room that has a very comfortable king bed in it. But who goes to Chicago to sit in the room! Price was right, there was zero noise, staff was courteous and, judging from the ballroom usage during our stay, a great place to have a wedding and reception. Small lobby and no TV at the small bar, but the piano player in the evening was a nice touch.

title: “Horrible!”
text: 1. It is never a good sign when reception is behind bullet proof glass. 2. They tried to put us in a smoking room despite the fact that we had booked a king non-smoking room 3. People screaming at 2 AM in the hallway. This went on for 20 minutes with no intervention from hotel management or security. Finally, I heard another guest open her door to tell the people to "shut up". I heard the ignorant people in the hallway start to back talk her so I went out in solidarity. There were a lot of us in town for the Philadelphia Marathon and we needed a good night's sleep. This was completely unexcusable. 4. No amenities. NONE! Not even an alarm clock/clock radio. The room was dirty and worn down looking. The road noise was unbearable. 5. There was no breakfast provided or offered.

title: “Ideal location”
text:
My family (parents, sisters & fiance) stayed at Hotel Metro for 5 nights in June. We had an amazing time! The hotel is ideally positioned for all the major sites. It sits on W35th St between 5th & 6th - very near Macy's (1 min walk) and many other high street stores (Gap, JC Penney, Victorias Secret, Old Navy, Footlocker to name but a few) - a walk in the other direction brings you to Saks, Lord & Taylor and all the more upmarket stores of 5th Ave in approx. 5-10mins. Times Square is an easy 10 min stroll. On the next street is the entrance to the Empire State and from here you can pick up a tour bus for the uptown & downtown tours. 
As for the hotel itself, we were very pleased with the choice that we had made, it is pricey for a comparable hotel in the UK but it is New York! The room we had was right at the elevator, we worried that this might mean noise but no, all guests were very well behaved and all we had was the occassional footstep. The room itself was fine size wise, although this was the biggest of the 3 rooms we had. There was no view as we looked to the inside of the hotel, however my sisters had a room to the front with a view of the Empire State. 
The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful - any request we had was dealt with promptly. 
Breakfast is included which is an advantage - the breakfast room can get quite busy however we never found a problem obtaining a seat. 
There is a rooftop bar, we did not use this much, however on a Friday evening its very popular and busy with non-residents. We never ate in the Metro grill and have read mixed reviews of it, there is a happy hour in the bar on a daily basis. 
The gm is small but all equipment is well maintained and adequate for a quick workout in the morning. 
Would I stay at this hotel again? Yes definately!

title: “Pleasant Enough”
text: We stayed at this hotel Wed 15th Sept for 3 nights. I had pre-paid on expedia, but was not made aware of the valet parking, that you have to use at $14 per day, which was a little cheeky as there is no where else you can park, we were in and out a fair bit so with tips everytime they get your car your looking at an extra $30 or so. The hotel itself was nice enough, clean, comfortable rooms, and nice bathroom. We were on the top floor so had no view unless we went outside. The breakfast was really good I must say and served in a nice little restaurant with outside heated seating, this was inclusive of our cost. It is in a fairly good location, close to the airport, little Italy and about a $7 cab ride to the gaslamp district.

title: “Great Overnight Stay”
text: This was a great, economic place to stay for one night. We arrived a day early for a cruise out of Jacksonville. Staff was friendly and breakfast was nice too. Would stay again!

title: “Our SUV was vandalized and this hotel is doing nothing to help us!!!!”
text: We stayed Jan. 30th and left for our vacation early Saturday morning which all we thought was going great. The following Saturday we returned around 6:00p.m. to find our passenger side window was completely destroyed and shattered glass was all over the inside along with missing items. The airport shuttle employee acted like no big deal and made us carry our luggage to the check-in desk to talk to the manager on duty. After waiting for approx. 5-10 minutes for her to arrive she said there was nothing she could do about this matter!!!! I asked her when our car had been vandalized and she told me our car was one of three cars that this happened to. We asked her to call the police and while we waited for them to arrive she left us, not offering to do anything! After the kind policeman told us this happens alot in this area, we tried to find the manager again to ask her for a shop-vac so we could vacuum out piles of shattered glass on our front seats and floor. She said she would check for one and after 20 minutes went by, she could not help us with this either? When I asked for another manager to talk to she told me they would not be available until Sunday or Monday which she did provide their names to me. I then asked her if she could provide a complimentary room to us for our trouble and figure out how we were going to drive home 3 hours north without a window in 20* weather - of course she could not help us again and wanted us to pay a discounted rate - OMG!!!!! So then I asked her for some cardboard & heavy masking tape to make a passenger window to attempt to drive home ( waited another 15 minutes for these). While my husband almost froze to death constructing this window out of nothing, I asked her for at least a broom & dust pan to sweep all of the glass out of my car. She provided these too after 10 minutes of waiting and by this time I have FIRE coming out of my ears in extreme anger!!! Wouldn't you by now??? I then asked her to personally follow me out to my car so she could actually feel what my husband & I were going through but that was a waste of my time!!!! She said she knew what our car & the other two looked liked after days of them sitting in their parking lot and NOT getting a phone call to report this to us. We had our cell-phones on vacation and if we would have gotten a phone call when this happened we could have contacted people to help us during the week and not on Super Bowl weekend when everyone was closed. So I hope you are reading this Mark (General Manager of Crowne Plaza) and are willing to help us because so far none of your staff has!?

title: “Excellent 10 days !”
text:
I had an excellent 10 days vacation, when I was an Affinia's Manhattan guest.
Everything was great ! I really , would like to give my very special thank to ROZALYN,that works in the front desk. She is very kind, very polite and very efficient employee. Able to save situations in a fast,and best way. Congratulations for having this kind of friendly staff, be sure, that makes all the difference. Thanks a lot !
Armando.

title: “All requests were Completed to full expectation with a smile.”
text:
Customer service is what brings me back somewhere, and club quarters is doing everything right. A native resident in the area, a few friends and I reserved 3 Kitchenette suits with a full size bed and pull out couch to enjoy the evening in town. 
The rooms are amazingly priced and spacious. The room slept 5 comfortably (if you don't mind sharing A bed with your girlfriends) and the staff would make you think you are royalty. Julian ( the front desk attendant) was informative, professional, and eager to please all of the guests needs. There are even refillable purified water dispensers on every floor, perfect for hangover prevention. 
All in all, fantastic experience.

title: “Good Bad and Ugly”
text:
The staff of the hotel were good, helpful and friendly but the management of this hotel is abysmal. I am an "Elite Marriott Rewards Member" and booked for 3 nights because it was close to where we needed to be. However, we checkout early and moved to another Marriott property that was much farther but much better and less expensive. The food at this hotel was terrible. Do not eat here. The restaurant food was either overcooked and then served tepid or cold or undercooked and lacking of flavor.. None of the food items even came close to the level of bad fast food. The munchies in the Elite lounge were also bad - either overcooked meatballs with no flavor or half frozen uncooked meatballs with no flavor covered in a thick BBQ style sauce. Then there was the bed - the mattress was old worn and covered with several strange pads under the sheets - perhaps in an attempt to fill in the depressions. The flat screen TV reception was real bad - it could have benefited from a set of rabbit ears to improve reception and perhaps reduce the amount of snow and image breakup. 
I remain loyal to Marriott but I cannot recommend staying at this property. We stayed at three other Marriott properties in the area and they were all great.

title: “Overall Not Bad”
text: On our way from Michigan, me and my boyfriend stopped in Jacksonville to see what it was all about. Stayed at the Red Roof Inn on Lenoir. The hotel overall was not bad; its a Red Roof you get what you pay for. Clean room with free internet access. The only thing was the area. Never been here and coming in on 95 all we seen was ghetto. The whole stay we had an uneasy feeling about staying here; nothing happened though. Its right by the highway so its kinda noisy. Luckily there was a Applebees at the main enterance of the drive and a Waffle House cuz we did not want to go too far from the hotel. As far at breakfast goes there is none just coffee.

title: “Wonderful Stay!”
text: I found this hotel by chance and I'm so glad I did! I love it's boutique atmosphere and the room we had honestly reminded me of home - didn't feel like a hotel at all. Close to everything, lovely staff, hallways that smelled of fresh flowers...I will definitely be bacl!

title: “Great Place!”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 4 nights for a Lackland AFB graduation. The hotel was great but extremely frustrating to find. Because the hotel is new, the address is not available for those using gps. Placing 1400 Dove Canyon in the gps will bring you to the hotel though. Other than finding the place, the breakfast in the morning was pretty good and they also served an evening cocktail hour for free. The room was very clean and even had high tech touch screen thermometers in the room. Bed was made everyday and I would stay here again.

title: “Always a great Stay”
text:
If you’re looking for a Times Sq Hotel this is it, the Marquis is a wonderful hotel in the middle of Times Sq, for us this hotel is convenient since we take a bus into the city and the Port Authority is so very close. The rooms run the gamut as to what you’re looking for and so do the prices. For the number of times that we have stayed at this Hotel service has always been efficient and courteous.
The lobby can at times get crowded but it never seems to be overwhelming, a numbers of elevators run up the middle of the open air lobby, have never experienced any amount of crowded elevators. 
Check-in is on the 8th floor as is a Bar/Grill with a nice view of Times Sq, on this floor you will find a few stores and comfortable seating to relax on while enjoying a cup of coffee or a snack. 
Wi-Fi is free in the Lobby but forget about it, very spotty. 
Everything is convenient with this hotel, taxis, stores, shops, bars and places to grab a fast bite or a full sit down meal. The Hotel is one of our favorites but can be pricey at times.

title: “Unsanitary conditions with condescending and rude ownership”
text: I knew it was risky renting a room at a motel on the fly in a city center, but we were exhausted and needed a place to crash. For $55 a night, I knew it couldn't be beat, and I had my expectations set quite low for that price. Even with low expectations, I am disappointed. I was willing to forgive the owners condescending tone and casual saunter to our room when the key wouldn't work. I could have overlooked the dust covered room, old furniture, cigarette burned trays, and mildew covered shower curtain. But, when my partner woke up at 530 covered, literally covered, in bug bites, that was it. Luckily the motel does have WiFi so I was able to research what to do, but having just checked out this morning, we still are at a laundry washing and rewashing, and also spending $90 on new clothes so we don't take bed bugs back home with us. When I brought it to the owners attention, he did seem surprised and refunded our money, but please be wary.

title: “Great for the price”
text:
I've seen the reviews of this place as a mixed bag, but overall I thought it was a great deal and a solid experience.
Staff is helpful and friendly, room was nice and clean, location is great. There are all sorts of great restaurants, drinking establishments, things to do within a short walk or ride. I felt the neighborhood was safe, I had no issues walking around at night.
The parking is limited, but I had no trouble keeping a space as I was on foot in the evenings. The hotel is indeed located near rail service and the airport, so it has noise from that.. but the other hotels in the area are also near it.. and some are very pricey. I honestly don't feel my sleep quality was affected.

title: “what a wonderful place”
text: If you are ever fortunate enough to visit the beautiful city of San Diego, you can do no better than stay at the wonderful Marriott Hotel in the Gaslamp Quarter. On arrival you can use the valet parking, which is expensive at $28 per day or the car park opposite the hotel at $16 per day, but with this cheaper option there are no 'in' 'out' priviledges. However, we did not really need to use the car as the hotel is in such a great situation. On arrival you will be greated by the most pleasant and efficient staff you are ever likely to meet. The lobby is beautifully appointed and the concierge could not be more knowledgeable or helpful, even printing out little cards with directions to and from places of interest. The rooms are delightful, large, spotlessly clean with every comfort, including a filter coffee machine with excellent coffee, cable tv and the most comfortable beds and luxurious bed linen you are ever likely to sleep in. The hotel has the most amazing rooftop bar, open to the sky with fantastic views and a central fire, just fabulous. I was not impressed with the breakfast and did not try any other meals at the hotel. However, you are moments away from superb dining, I would particularly recommend the Australian restaurant, Bondi. Coronado Island, a mere 10 minute drive away is a must, although we did find Seaport very commercial and overpriced. The local shopping mall was excellent with some great bargains.

title: “Excellent Hampton”
text: Another greatly run Hampton by Hilton. The hotel is in Conveniently located to everything. There is a groovy Japanese sushi place, Chipotle, Starbucks and really nice Safeway in 2 blocks walking. Wha makes the hotel great is the staff. Everyone, I encountered seem to be in line with Hilton hospitality values. They are friendly yet professional. They listen and help. You can see the property is well managed. Complimentary wi-fi and breakfast. There is self-service waffle, cereal, juice, danish etc, bananas, apple. Perfect for complimentary breakfast. Used laundry service a lot, due to heat wave in DC. It was always on time and perfect.

title: “Third visit to this Hotel”
text:
This was our third visit to this hotel in the last 6 years. During this time there has been no visible evidence of updating their rooms. This time we stayed in the North Tower which seems to be more dated then the south tower.
Having said this the rooms were clean with older type TV's but there is a notice that they are replacing them. All the staff were very helpful and quick to assist with any issues.
The restaurant in the Hotel is very good for breakfast and opens at 6:30am if you have an early flight out.
The location is ideal for us as it is not in the middle of Times Square but only a 10-15 minute walk to get there. It is a block and a half away from Central Park.
There is a bus stop outside and at least 3 subway stations within 5 mins walk.

title: “HORRIBLE”
text:
The stuff does not know how to treat customers.
Disrespectful, unhelpful, by phone they tell you something and when you arrive there they tell you another.
The worst service i ever had.
I thought Sheraton was other thing..

title: “Excellent customer care”
text: The hotel wins high honors for taking very good care of its guests -- from check-in to check-out, they try to make everything pleasurable, easy, professional and comfortable. Room was comfortable and immaculate; view was spectacular. Very quiet. Very upscale. Only downsides: valet parking (the only choice available) was very expensive but was also very well run; room service was very expensive as well, but staff is wondereful; air unit was a bit noisy. Fortunately I booked via Priceline!

title: “Always the best!”
text: I wouldn't stay anywhere else in SA. I just got back from a conference there and as always, it was outstanding! I go at least once a year to enjoy the heavenly bed, heavenly bath and the wonderful service. This westin is by far the best I've ever stayed at. Highly recommend!

title: “Good value place to stay”
text: I chose to stay at Grand Hyatt mainly because of the location right next to Grand Central Station. It was very central and easy to navigate to many of the tourist spots. It is also a fantastic spot if you want to go shopping as it is only a short walk to Madison Ave and Fifth Ave. I stayed in a club room and the size was fantastic for New York, very spacious with a great king size bed, a big desk and a modular couch. There was plenty of room. The bathroom was small however the shower was great with fantastic water pressure and a big shower head. The only reason I gave this three stars is because I think the hotel is a little too large to give a very personal level of service. Housemaids were lovely and friendly and went out of their way to greet guests however concierge was inconsistent and not at all helpful. Elevators could be very slow at times depending on the time of day especially in the morning. One great feature is that each room has a small fridge which guests can stock with their own drinks. Overall a comfortable stay in a hotel in a convenient location but, a good stay but not a great stay.

title: “Redone Hotel at Universal Studios”
text: Hotel has been remodeled and is very nicely appointed, large pool good fitness facility walk or shuttle to Universal Studios Citywalk for a good selection of shopiing and restaurants. Convenient to Hollywood or downtown LA. Close to Burbank airport. Friendly staff.

title: “PM Manager gets an "E" for Effort - Concierge gets an "F"”
text: Stayed at the Harbor Court 1 night, Thursday April 8-9, 2004. Planned to stay 2 nights, but we cut our trip short. The Hotel is in a good location - right across the street from Baltimore's inner harbor. Rack rate for harbor-view room was $270. The hotel is elegantly decorated and very clean, but not quite up to its four star pretensions. The hotel does not offer rooms with 2 queen beds. The best they can do is two full beds. When I reserved our room over a month prior to our stay, the reservationist assured me that the renovations to the indoor pool would be complete by April 1. When I called two weeks prior, the person at the front desk assured me that the indoor pool would be open on April 1. When we checked in, we were greeted with a sign informing us that the indoor pool would not be open until April 12. After, the front desk staff was unsuccessful in finding us a room in a nearby hotel with an indoor pool, the PM manager intervened and agreed to comp our room and drive us over to a hotel with a pool. We accepted. When we arrived in our room, someone else's bags were there and it took a half-hour to get our bags. The PM manager then reneged on the offer to take us to a property with a pool informing us that the pools at the nearby hotels were too crowded. When we complained, he informed us that his boss told him that we should have not even have been comped for the room. We then sought the help of the concierge in finding activites in lieu of swimming for our young boys. The concierge gave us the wrong closing time for the Maryland Science Center (its 5:00 pm not 6:00 pm). Also, the concierge did not have tickets to sell to the National Aquarium ("We did't get them yet this year"), and did not give us accurate info regarding buying tickets to the aquarium. In the end, the PM manager did try to make us happy by comping our room and valet parking and by sending a very nice fruit basket to the room. The same cannot be said for the concierge who did not appear to be trying at all.

title: “Good Hotel, Great Value”
text: Not the best hotel in the world, but could be the best value in the world. Clean rooms friendly staff and a great breakfast at a good price. I will stay here again next time I am in columbus. Hotel is a little tricky to find.

title: “probably the best value in NY”
text: Just returned from my second stay here and am in love with this hotel. Where else in NY can one get such a super view (43rd floor) and really amazingly comfortable bed for under $140 for a night. The rooms are modern and tasteful with marble bathrooms (shower is not too powerful though). Location is fine if one is a fan of local transport (we are), otherwise it could get very expensive by cab. It is however a haven to return to in the evening after the hust´le and bustle of Midtown. Room service is surprisingly affordable with a comprehensive menu and very quick service. Breakfast is pricey however Starbucks is just around the corner and there are also plenty of deli's in the area. I highly recommend this hotel and know where I will be staying on my next visit to NY.

title: “Great hotel in wonderful location”
text: We did a priceline bid and ended up with this hotel for a great price. what a great treat. We went to NYC for 2 nights and loved the location. The hotel was quiet, clean and so well situated. We walked everywhere (including Penn Station with bags). It amazed me how quiet the lobby and elevators were at such a busy time of year in the city. We would stay here again in a minute and truly were thrilled with the Priceline price.

title: “Comfort for a layover”
text: We had an imposed layover in LA en route from Mexico to Seattle. We had pre-booked but the check-in was agonisingly slow - we had to wait more than 45 minutes. We also then lined up for 15 minutes to speak to the concierge who then couldn't answer our question. So our service experience was poor but the hotel and its rooms are of the high standard and comfort one would expect from a Hilton. A comfortable and quiet night's sleep with a smooth, short transfer to the airport the next morning.

title: “the bar”
text: The hotel was nice but we were very disappointed by the the bar. The bartender was not well trained. There was only one type wine at the bar and only one bottle of that. He ran out of ice. He did not know how to make a good, dry martini. He knew nothing about the Jacksonville area. He was not friendly. All of this was the bartender on duty between 4-5PM. Then later, after 9PM, the night bartender was just as bad. The bar location in the lobby was nice, the atmosphere was pleasant, but the service was terrible. Since we travel frequently, we expect hotel bars to be efficient and accommodating.

title: “Past its glory”
text: The St Francis Hotel in San Francisco is in a great location at Union Square-- close to shopping, China Town, SF sites. However, the hotel does not live up to its reputation. Rooms are small and a bit 'tired'. The hallways are, too. The best part of the hotel is its history.

title: “Great hotel, fantastic room, a must stay”
text: My girlfriend and I stayed for a night over the previous weekend. The staff was prompt, friendly, and quickly got us checked into our room. We had a 1 bedroom suite with patio on one of the recently remolded floors and I must say it was one of the nicer hotel rooms ive ever been in. Very well designed and spotless, gorgeous kitchen (not that we were cooking), overall I cant say enough about the room. If you have the chance definitely stay at the Affinia Manhattan, between the gorgeous rooms, friendly staff, and great location it is perfect hotel for your NYC getaway.

title: “A Great Experience”
text:
We stayed at the Hampton Inn for 3 nights while in San Antonio and were impressed with so many things.
1 - The service at the hotel was incredible. Every staff member went out of their way to help out.
2 - The breakfast had so many choices including fruit, breads, bagels, hot and cold cereals, waffles, and more. The cranberry juice was excellent.
3 - The room was spotless and the bed was very comfortable. 
4 - You are only a few blocks from the Riverwalk.
I strongly recommend this hotel.

title: “overpriced, ugly rooms”
text:
I recently stayed here as the conference I was attending was booked here. I had stayed at the sister property, Squaw Peak, 2 years prior, and remembered the rooms being very welcoming and serene.
We came a day early to celebrate our anniversary and explore Phoenix. The disappointment began at checkin, when we were told that though we'd reserved a king bed, there were none available, unless we wanted by the service elevator. "But we have a queen." Fine. Get to the room--double doubles; the rooms are all promoted as "suites", but they were small and felt cramped. I had a visceral reaction to the ugly colors of the room--kind of a chartreuse yellow and avocado green. At $179/night, I decided to look for alternatives. Called the front desk, and they checked Squaw Peak, but it was booked. They offered to move us to a larger suite, which was acceptable. "And how about a bottle of champagne?" I said that would be lovely; however, it never arrived. 
I wanted to enjoy a sunset drink in the lounge at the top--A Different Pointe of View--but it was closed for "special events" 3 nights in a row. I did eat there with colleagues, and it was a delicious meal--really the bright spot of the week.
It was fine for the conference, but my review is really geared to the rooms. I will NEVER stay there again.

title: “Nice hotel, very accommodating staff, pretty setting”
text: I stayed at the Charlotte University Place this month for a conference. It is an older hotel, but nicely appointed, with lots of nearby amenities. As the hotel is situated next to a man made lake, it provided a wonderful opportunity to step out during the breaks to sit out by the water.

title: “Mixed experience”
text:
Trendy hotel, deluxe room was nice except for the wet carpet near the open bathroom (even when I checked in - yuck). For some reason their "seperate sink, $hit, shower" layout involves an open tiled shower area that opens onto the carpeted entrance way. Across is the sink and then toilet area. Unclear what the permanent water damage will be, but does not seem hygenic. 
Bed was great. View was nice. Location is meat packing district so can be a slog in the cab to midtown, especially with all of Bloomberg's new one-way streets everywhere. Fun for leisure stay of shopping, clubbing, eating out. High Line Park is cool to walk. Lots of wealthy young European clientele (this place must be a hit on Opodo!)
Check-in - WORST EVER. I stood in line for 10 minutes before I gave up, dumped my suitcase with the doorman and ran out to my meeting. The front desk of 1 person was consumed with some foreigner's neverending random questions about New York. Meanwhile, 2 employees sat next to the front desk, ignoring the line, and not doing anything except surfing their Apple laptops and sometimes answering their headsets. odd and unacceptable. The checkin/out line was huge and I'm sure these young ladies could multi-task more than whatever they are doing (seemed like they operated a call center and were told to never make contact with actual people in line).

title: “Hot and bright a recipe for no sleep.”
text:
The rooms were well sized and nicely appointed. After reading other reviews I was anticipating a see through shower space--not the case. The bathroom door is frosted glass and then the shower is past another marble half wall. I thought it was plenty private. 
However, the two issues I did have at the hotel were with the temperature in the room and the blinds on the windows. 
The windows had wood slat blinds that may as well have been open for how much light was streaming into the room. I am not an early riser and even after a late night there was really no way to sleep past 7:30am. There were no curtains or even rods or hooks to try to diffuse the light with a sheet or towel. If you're up early or stay in the winter when it's darker in the morning you may be fine but if you're on vacation and want to sleep in you may want to look elsewhere.
The temperature in my room fluctuated between 73 and 78 degrees--yes that's right, nearly 80 IN the hotel room. After calling the engineer because it wouldn't dip below 73 we decided to move to a new room. The new room (west facing) received afternoon sun through the closed blinds which heated the room to a whopping 78. Though we had the thermostat set for 67 it never dropped below 73. We called the engineer in again to try to remedy the problem. Hotel staff informed us the thermostats didn't individually control the rooms because it would fluctuate too much room to room so it was controlled centrally by the hotel. When we complained it was too hot they apologized but said if it was changed then other rooms would be too cold. Needless to say I saw staff delivering box fans to guest rooms. 
If it were an inexpensive or discount/travel hotel you could probably write off the problems but for a nice hotel I expected much more.

title: “Nice Stay in Downtown Seattle”
text:
A nice hotel – clean and modern hotel from an older building in downtown Seattle. Close to Pioneer Square and about a 10 minute walk to Pike’s Market. The elevators need a room key to work and add to a sense of security. The room décor and furnishings were very modern. Comfortable beds.
The restaurant is a great place for a quick bite, to meet with friends/colleagues. The food was very good.
If you are driving, beware of the $35 valet fee. There is no parking garage attached to the building and the only parking is the valet. If you are leaving in the morning be sure to call to have you vehicle ready in plenty of time. One morning I called down 20 minutes ahead of time and had to wait about 30 minutes after arriving at the Valet station to get my car as there was only one person working. 
Overall though, excellent stay.

title: “Fantastic, but snobby.”
text:
I stayed at the Carlyle over my 21st birthday last year, and it was an extremely beautiful, old NYC place to stay. Now, I've been to NYC 4 times and on no occasion have I ever expected huge rooms. The people who expect big rooms to go with their big prices shouldn't have such high expectations in NYC, unless you're staying at The Plaza or rent an apartment. That's just the way it is in this city.
However, on arrival, (my partner and I at the time were checking in) we were told that they required a credit card - 'standard practice,' we thought...
No.
We were subsequently informed that we had not paid. I told them very politely that, yes infact the bill had been covered way beforehand as this was my birthday and we wanted no hassle with the room. 
Whilst they faffed around behind the desk, we retreated to the seating area very embarrassed and were taken into the bar finaly by an over-compensating manager who told the barman to 'look after us' and said the first round of drinks would be complimetary. No such luck, this was on our bill when we went to check out after our stay.
Anyway, this was all sorted out and it turned out they had put a lovely birthday suprise/cake/amenities in our room for me on my father's request so that was something nice to have. 
However, what I was NOT pleased with was that the reason why our check in had revealed we 'hadn't paid.' Their excuse was that their accounts dept. had not transferred the information that we had actually paid. Thanks. Absolutely ridiculous when you consider it's a 5* hotel.
So, among the strangeness was a REALLY loud minibar which we had to turn off every night, some food got taken out of our room that was in a brown bag that you couldn't see into and clearly NOT trash, and after we complained about this, we were given lots of things out of the minibar to have for free but they then appeared on our bill too which we refused to pay for. How hard is it to leave a note on our statement?
But the stay was infact really nice apart from these things! The room and bed was extremely comfy. View was good too.
Anyway, just beware of the seemingly variable service.

title: “Still the grand dame of lovely hotels”
text: This wast second time at the beautiful place. The whole aura is so grand. The rooms were spacious. My favorite part was the enormous walk in closet. I attended a corporate event. The food was great each day. The meeting rooms were spacious. You can't beat the location atop Nob hill. Truly a great experience

title: “Best dog friendly hotel ever!!”
text:
I just came back from my trip to Austin and stayed at Wyndham Garden and it was nothing like I expected it to be. I was very impressed by the dog friendly room. The carpet was above and beyond clean, considering that pets did stay there. The staff were very helpful and informative. Perfect location, easy access to the I-35. I loved the pet package with waste bags and dog treats. I recently wrote a review of my stay on my website so feel free to check out my overrall hotel experience. 
http://ibonafidepassion.blogspot.com/2010/05/wyndham-garden-hotel-austin.html

title: “Worst hotel of my life”
text:
I hated this hotel, it was horrible. I would never stay here again. The only good about the hotel is its location. I went to Chicago with my boyfriend. We stayed here because of the price and the location. Never again. 
The hotel was run down and old. There was paint peeling and holes in the walls. The beds were disgusting. I slept on my blanket with no pillow or covers because it was so hard and it stunk like mold. The bathroom was rusted and had a gross smell the whole time we were there. There was nothing special or even good about this hotel. It was really dark inside, especially the halls. The hotel made me feel like I was in an old horror movie at night. Never stay here, I would rather stay at hotel further away like a Marriott than stay here again.

title: “Great stay”
text: I stayed here in May 2012 for 5 nights and had a great stay. I chose this hotel based on previous reviews and close proximity to where my son lives in the LES. The room was neat and clean, small, but I expected that and didn't mind (I had a single room.) My room was on the 4th floor and overlooked Houston Street. With the window closed most of the city noise was eliminated, though I did enjoy having the option to open the window, especially when a couple of quick thunder storms moved through the area. The roof top lounge area was very nice. A good place to see the skyline, take some pictures and relax. The morning breakfast area was clean and well stocked. It had just enough variety to start my day (a bowl of cereal, juice, bagel, coffee, etc.) and 3 computers with internet access was an added plus, along with a TV to catch up on the news. The front desk was accomodating and friendly. The area is busy with lots of night life and restaurants, but I felt safe walking around alone going to and from my son's place over on Clinton Street and exploring the immediate area. Overall a very pleasant stay.

title: “cheap,comfortable,central,clean,come stay there .”
text:
I had read reviews of this hotel and wondered what on earth i was letting myself in for,even pulling up to the hotel i was rather dubious but once in the reception was greeted by the desk staff in a friendly way that put any niggling doubts to rest,lady behind the desk gave mummy and myself maps and lots of useful info and reminded us that the breakfast was complimentary .Rooms were a good size(by NYC standards) clean and had all we needed, at this point i must question the doubting thomases who complain about the rooms,what exactly are you looking for ? surely a bedroom in NYC is a base from which to explore the city,it is not known as a city that attracts people to book a room in which to stay in all day and relax,surely other wonderful cities would suit far better for"getting away and unwinding".
 Location is spot on,empire state building to the right,macys to the left,subway a hop,skip and jump away........now what more could you need ?
 Others have "dissed"the breakfast but my mother and i were very happy with it,oatmeal,toast,bagels,cereal,buns,donuts,juice,hot drinks-a lovely choice and if that doesnt set you up in the morning then sure you can go expand the waistline and arterys all you like in one of the many diners close by.
 If you have booked this hotel and are now worried about some reviews then please put those worries aside,by all means it is not the waldorf astoria but if that is your usual standard of hotel then pay an awfully lot more ,but for reasonable rate stay here,(all the more spending pennies for the shops) :-)
 Tip: transfers can be expensive-book super shuttle,hotel-jfk 2 people 38$. hotel will give you number.

title: “Big Hotel, Great Location”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights, the hotel was full, they had a conference so it was very busy. Rooms were big and spacious. The hotel was walking distance to many hot spots, restaurants and attractions. Across the street were the car rentals which was very convenient.

title: “Excellent Hotel...Great Customer Service..”
text:
Ok...If you are a couple and go to San Francisco...you have to stay here!! Best Location for exploring SF
Nice Clean Hotel, Free Hosted Wine Reception, Free Bikes, we biked all around the city for a couple of days...and he customer service was outstanding, the front desk staff at this hotel are world class....I really can't say anything negitive about this place ita ll

title: “Worth it's ratings”
text:
Checked in for a business ess trip without any idea it was the top rated San Antonio hotel and wasn't disappointed, rooms remind me of luxury British hotels, a feeling of quality and style without being flash. Stylish and lovely rooms and amazing bathrooms, seafood restaurant is also amazing - I spend many nights in hotels and this is the best for me this year and in fact for quite some time - would pitch it against the best, simply superb service and surroundings, stay here if you can.
Rob

title: “Great place to stay and caring employees”
text: I am on a cross country bicycle and I met Rich who works for the hotel in Florida at the airport. After talking for a few minutes he asked where I was staying. I didn't have a reservatIon in the area so he recommended the Handlery. He said it was nice and convienient to the area I needed to be in in the San Diego area. The room was very comfortable and the other staff excellent. The hotel was everything he said and more. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Not "minutes" but "40 minutes" from Beale Street”
text:
It was not the best week for Hiltons and me. This property advertises itself as "minutes" from Beale Street when in fact it is 18 miles and 40 minutes from Beale street. I got over that and surrendered to the fact that I would not be heading down there for the evening. After checking in, the smoking room that I had requested and reserved was not available but magically reappeared when I threatened to walk, I went to my room and dropped my bags. I went to get some ice and the ice machine on the 5th floor was inoperative, I shrugged and went to the 6th floor and discovered that "Ice and Vending" was really only "vending on that floor so I went to the 7th floor. After getting some Ice, I ventured to the executive lounge on the 26th floor. Very nice with nice attendant and great views. After a few ordures, I returned to my room to get some work done. The ten minutes that I spent looking for an ashtray resulted in more frustration. I tried to call the front desk, then pressed the little button for "one touch service" and then dialed an outside line and back into the main hotel number; repeat three times with no answers. 
At that point I came to the realization this property had plenty of money and did not need mine, so for the first time in 30 years of travel, I walked out; stopping by the front desk to explain the situation and get a "zero due" check out. The front desk employee apologized and made no effort to contact his manager. 
It is a shame, pretty hotel in a decent location but the overall level of service is not at Hilton Standards.

title: “Just about perfect!”
text:
Things got off to a great start when I was upgraded to a suite without even having to ask! The Sam is ultra sleek and luxurious. You never feel uncomfortable though becuase the staff is so friendly and helpful. 
My suite was v. nice although the "color scheme" was a bit too monochromatic for my taste. I think the bed must have been the most comfortable thing on this earth! I also loved the flat screen TV's and the gorgeous glass and granite bathrooms. Complimentary Town Car service within the downtown area was greatly appreciated. The Rivera Grill was a good spot for dinner too! Just an all-around fantastic boutique property. You must stay here if you're coming to Houston!

title: “A dream place in NYC”
text: This hotel is just perfect. It does not have the usual crowds you find in some strictly touristic places. Its location just across the Central Park is a blessing. The rooms are spacious and extremely comfortable. Continental breakfast is included and it offers a variety of delicious/nutritious options, even for those frugal eaters. Its architectural style sends you back to a different time of beauty and different lifestyles.

title: “Grand service”
text: The service at the Hilton was fantastic from the maid, customer service, bartender, and bell boy. The hotel was convenient to shopping and tourist locations. The hotel decorations were breathtaking and rooms were very spacious.

title: “San Francisco Sweet Spot”
text: My wife and I stayed at The Donatello in San Francisco for four days in July, 2011. We were VERY pleasantly surprised by both the room and other accommodations such as the Business Center and roof-top exercise and lounge facility. Our room was not only comfortable and quiet, but was equipped with both a mini-fridge and microwave which we found extremely useful for breakfasts (not an easy meal in that area) and snacks. There were plates, glasses and utensils making an in-room meal quite easy. This was especially helpful since my wife was handling some important business during our stay. Of course, The Donatello has a marvelous location just off Union Square with its shops and restaurants, but also a pleasant walk away from SFMOMA, the Ferry Building, and Chinatown. All this at an incredibly reasonable price. So, The Donatello will definitely see us again on our next trip the the magical city by the bay.

title: “GREAT CONNECT TO CANADA”
text:
The hotel is the bus stop for the Quick Shuttle from Vancouver and is a quick comfy 2 hour ride from South Surrey .. we did the hotel and then did a nice walkabout to the CBD too!!
Space Needle is a short walk .. we even did the big trek to Safeco and the ball game and bus back to hotel .. easy access for car and traffic .. have done a few times and would recommend the place as a stay!!

title: “ehh...”
text:
I'm generally a fan of Westin and more broadly starwood properties, so I continue to stay at this hotel despite routinely being unimpressed.
Pro's
-Occasionally has good rates
-Clean and adequate rooms
-A Starwood property
-Right on Union Square (this is a con for me, but some people really like the area)
Con's
-Rooms are somewhat dated. Not dirty, just not very updated
-Service is very hit and miss...particularly at the front desk, which never seems to be staffed appropriately
Overall the hotel is fine, but as long as your expectations aren't too high.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: I stay here often and always thankful for the decent staff, clean rooms, and . . . great location!

title: “A haven in the midst of the tourist frenzy”
text: Our original hotel choice turned out to be awful so we were delighted to find this haven in midst of Fisherman's Wharf for a reasonable last minute price. The staff is delightful, and the rooms are updated, clean & luxurious. We especially enjoyed the view of the GG Bridge thru the mirrors reflection from the couch!

title: “Nice Hotel with Hard Beds”
text:
Stayed in a two bedroom suite for 2 nights with business associates. The lobby is nice - the front desk clerks (especially Nikki) were more than friendly and and helpful. The evening meals and breakfasts were great. The room was nice - had one bedroom with a king bed and one wth two doubles. As many of the other reviewers stated, this hotel is very clean. Some of the best housekeeping I have encountered and I travel a lot with my job. Water pressure for the showere was good.
My only complaint was the bed/mattress. It was very hard and not very comfortable. I stay at Homewood Suites when I can and some that I have stayed in recently have updated their mattresses. This one hasn't. Even though I really liked everything else at this hotel, I probably wouldn't stay here again because of the uncomfortable bed.

title: “Great holiday getaway with your dog!”
text: This is a fantastic motel type of property where you can stay with your dog, where most private patios lead to a clean dog run, and is steps from the beach and an outdoor park like area. The beach is off leash for dogs, and you feel like you are in a small local town in this area of San Diego. Walk to the local restaurants and dog friendly shops, and enjoy the friendly staff at the Ocean Villa Inn. Free Continental breakfast is included, the rooms are clean, reasonable rates....I love this place and have been there twice in one year. Nothing fancy here, but down to earth and so relaxing...

title: “Afordable, Confortable, Quiet”
text: New spot. Rooms are large and confortable. Silent as well. Very well located if you have meetings in the commercial bulidings in the surroundings (walking distance). Nice staff and afordable price on breakfast. Recommend for business or leisure travelers. I paid some 200 usd.

title: “Good location to downtown!”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for ou/texas weekend. Great location, and the hotel was really nice. Northpark mall is really close too. There is alot of stuff on both sides of the highway, so plenty to do.
The beds were great. Very comfy. Had great pillows too. Big, fluffy, and each bed had 3 pillows, which was nice. I will say that we were on the side facing the highway, and it was pretty loud. It actually woke me up the first night, but I was so tired the next night, I didn't hear a thing.
The shower was nice and hot, and nice shower head. Also, the shower had a place to put shampoo, etc. I saw this because one of the last hotels I stayed at didn't even have a place to put soap, shampoo, etc.
This hotel has inside entrances also, so that is good. The doors are inside the hotel, instead of opening your door and you're outside.
The prices were a good 30% higher this weekend here because of the ou/texas game, but I think all hotels jack up the prices this weekend. Noticed the prices were much lower the week after.
We checked in at 3:30, and we had to wait about 10-15min for our room to be ready. Another guy was checking in at same time, and they told him at least 30 more minutes before his room was ready. This is annoying, because you either have to wait there, or go waste time somewhere else till you can go back. I've never been to a hotel and the room wasn't ready after 3pm!
They do allow dogs, and I know this because a lady down the hall had about 4 of them barking at 10pm. Then, she was up about 6:30am, and they were again barking. Pretty annoying. This would've been a problem, but we were already up, and getting ready to leave for the day. If I'd been alseep, I would've been pretty upset. 
WE also counted 9 Direct TV trucks in the parking lot. Don't know whats goiing on with that, convention or something? They were there all weekend though. Parking wasn't a problem, we were there by 10pm, so no problem finding a space. 
Besides the room not ready, everything was very good. Nice place, nice hotel, nice stay. I would stay here again, but if I have to wait on a room again, may not give them another chance.

title: “Amazing value & great location”
text:
We have recently returned from a fantastic trip to New York where we stayed at the Salisbury Hotel. I spent a long time researching where to stay and it definitely paid off as this hotel is amazing value for money especially as the breakfast was included too. Our room had two queen sized beds, loads of storage space, a small kitchenette with fridge, microwave & coffee maker & prefectly adequate bathrrom. Yes it was slightly dated but you couldn't fault it as it was all spotlessly clean & tidy. 
All the staff we very friendly and always more than happy to help.We had to queue for breakfast a couple of days but this can be avioded if you take your breakfast back to your room. The variety of bagels, muffins, croissants, doughnuts, cereals, toast, fruit salad, boiled eggs on offer was excellent.
We spent very little time waiting for the lifts but guess we were probably quite lucky! The location was perfect - within easy walking distance of lots of sights & very close to the subway station too. Angelo's Italian restaurant, two doors down, made fantastic pizzas - almost as good as the one's we had on the 'Slice of Brooklyn Pizza tour'. If your want an excellent supermarket head up to the Time Warner Centre & go to the lower ground floor to Wholefoods Market. You will find just about everything there including anything for special diets eg gluten free bread, cakes, biscuits etc.
We will be going back to New York as we didn't get round to doing everything we wanted to and we will most definitely stay at the Salisbury again. Thanks for a fabulous stay.

title: “Fantastic service, Fantastic staff, Fantastic rooms.............Fantastic”
text: How can anyone say that this is the worst hotel they have stayed in??? This was the cleanliest, friendliest hotel ever. The staff, especially the concierge and Gio the receptionist, as nothing was ever too much for them. The rooms were an eclectic mix of modern minimalistic style and New England beach hut (well thats what i felt!!) The rooms were so clean, not a bit of dirt anywhere, nothing out of place and nothing worn away. Yes the hotel was not on the Wharf but, lets get realistic, not all hotels in San Francisco are, the city is not just about the Wharf.
