It is ideally located a few blocks from the cable car route and me and my friend were actually quite pleased with this as it let us take a daily part in one of the defining moments of San Francisco, riding the cable car through the amazing streets. It is also close to the shops and bars/restaurants of Union Square. The Carlton Hotel is a hidden gem, just tucked away enough not to be too touristy but accessible enough to have the best of the city. Amazing stay, wouldnt stay anywhere else in the city.

title: “Outstanding staff even if a little dowdy.”
text: We happened upon this hotel by accident because we had a medical emergency while changing trains in Philadelphia. Our patient was taken from the train by ambulance to U Penn Hospital. We wanted to be nearby and found this hotel on the internet on our phone. They could not have been more accomodating starting from the time we checked in. When they found out about the reason for our stay they gave us a special hotel rate. We had Thanksgiving dinner in the hotel dining room and the food was excellent. It was surprising how many other diners were in there on that holiday night. The next morning we had breakfast in the regular dining room and once again, service was perfect and the food very good. The hotel could use an update on the furnishings but the staff more than made up for that. At every turn they were helpful - even giving us shortcuts on our many walks over to the hospital.

title: “It worked perfectly”
text: My daughter and I drove in from Ohio on our journey west. The hotel was everything people had said in their reviews. It was easy to find and a great location for our evening plans. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The suite was spacious, well-appointed, and very clean. Temperature control (one of my pet peeves in hotels) was great. We went out for dinner with friends so I can't speak about the evening meal. Breakfast was excellent with hot and cold choices. All in all, it was a great satay.

title: “Absolutely fabulous!”
text:
This hotel is absolutely fabulous! I was really impressed by everything the hotel had to offer, especially the anemities that I haven't been able to find in other hotels. Each morning, there's a fully stocked continental breakfast, and every afternoon there are treats for hotel guests (cookies, bars, etc.).
I felt very safe at the hotel at all times (even when I was picked up at 4 am for an early flight), and the hotel staff and management were always helpful and very friendly.
I was visiting the University of Washington, and the hotel was very close to both the school and a big restaurant district, making it very easy to find meals.

title: “Great location, small rooms”
text: Firstly, the location of this hotel is second to none. Immediate outside of the hotel is the cable car that takes you down to the Fisherman Wharf precinct. Within easy walking distance is the light rail as well that takes you up towards the Castro and down to the Pier (where you can catch ferries to Alcatraz etc). The rooms themselves are quite small albeit the hotel is quite old and tastefully restored. We ended up having 2 x single beds in the room which was unusual considering we had booked a queen room. We were dead tired by the time we arrived and chose not to query it. The lighting in the foyers and in the rooms were charming and elegant. Would stay again for the location, if nothing else.

title: “Average...very average”
text: The location of the hotel is very central with a 3 minute walk to the subway station and the bus station (Port Authority) right across the road. But the hotel is not helped by its modest look. The "modesty" continues to the room and kind of stays throughout!! The staff is helpful and I found them helpful. The gym is average, the breakfast average, the view average...it goes on... and I kept getting the sense that this is what the hotel was aiming for - Average. Try to get to the crowne plaza round the corner for a lot more happening view of Time Square...

title: “Decent”
text: The Lucerne has an excellent location, a helpful staff and quite reasonable prices. My family of four stayed in a 2 queen, one bedroom suite for $275. The bedroom was quite big, but the sitting room was ridiculously cramped. With a love seat and TV, there wasn't even enough room for a coffee table. They could also desperately use an upgrade on the beds and bed linens. If you're looking for a nice space to escape the NYC hecticness, this is not the place. But, if you want a no-frills room in a great location without spending $400 a night, you'll be happy with the Lucerne.

title: “Friendly with relaxed sophistication”
text:
We were delighted with our recent stay at the Eventi. We had chosen this hotel because of its proximity to Penn Station, as we wanted to use the LIRR to go to the US Open matches. The area in which the hotel is located is OK, but not exceptional--some of the streets looked a bit sketchy, but we never felt unsafe even when walking back from Penn Station late at night. It's an easy walk to Penn Station or Herald Square.
Although I had mixed feelings about the surroundings, the Eventi itself was wonderful. Every employee we encountered was friendly and helpful, our rooms were clean and well organized, and we loved the complimentary coffee or tea in the morning and the wine reception on the 5th floor veranda. After some busy days watching tennis and sightseeing, Eventi was the perfect place in which to relax and sleep!

title: “Girls Weekend”
text: My mother and I stayed here this past weekend to attend the North Wood Women's (?) Club dinner event. We mainly went to hear comedian Jeanne Robertson. As soon as you pull up to the hotel a valet comes up to your window and greets you and asks for your name. He brings a cart and puts your luggage on it (while you just stand there and watch) and takes you to the front desk. At the front desk I asked for a complimentary gold fish, that is advertised on the website (you can get one if you were unable to bring your pets with you since it is a pet friendly hotel.) They were out of gold fish at the moment, but Gavin said he would see what he could do. The bail boy will not only take you (he's pushing the luggage cart) up to your room he will unload the luggage cart and set the items neatly on the bed. In the closet you will find comfy animal print robes. We had two beds and one robe so I called the front desk and they said we should have had two and they would send one up. Not even five minutes later there was a knock at the door. We opened to a guy holding a black and white zebra print robe AND a vase with a gold fish. The room was pretty and clean but we didn't see where the full price tag came into play (we got a discount on the room due to attending the event.) There isn't a gift shop or vending machine anywhere but there are (pricey) snacks in the mini bar. The bathroom has a sliding door which is very odd as it doesn't feel as private as the bathroom should feel. There was a rattling noise throughout the night, but we never did pinpoint if it was coming from the vents or not. Even though we were on the sixth floor we could hear traffic as if we were on the first. We enjoyed a massage at the Exhale Spa (which is located to the right of the hotel) which was lovely. I had a hair and make up appointment at the Pompeo Salon (which is to the left of the hotel.) The Pompeo Salon was very up scale, it even had a bar while you were waiting. The lady who did my hair was nice (not to mention gorgeous) and so was her assistant (he started on my curls and then she appeared at the end to finish the style) but I wasnt impressed with my overall experience there as far as my hair goes. The only product she put in my hair was hair spray so my curls fell out and were flat and crunchy before the end of the night. The lady who did my make up did an excellent job. She was very down to earth and would talk to you. I dont think the hair stylist said more than 10 words to me the 30 minutes I was there. After the event we wanted to get something to eat but didn't want to fight the Dallas traffic so we asked Gavin, at the front desk, how we call a taxi, he offered to do it and then said if we wanted to stay in he had a couple of menus from restaurants who deliver until 3am (it was 1:30am). We stayed in and ordered spaghetti from Zini Italian and it got there at 2am. (Oh! They dont accept cash passed midnight!) The spaghetti was so spicy we only had a couple of bites and threw it away. The Zini bread is really good though. Overall it was a fun and exciting experience (we not only got to meet Jeanne Robertson we also got to hang out with her in the Palomar restaurant) but nothing real breathtaking.

title: “Kids loved it...”
text:
Join HHonors before you visit...they'll treat you like family! It's nice to be greated by name when you call the desk. The room was clean. Not Hilton-clean...but clean. The suite was quite large. We loved the HiDef widescreen TV in the living room, and the kids loved the video games ($6.95 per hour). The view wasn't much, but no big deal...we were there to sightsee not stare out our hotel window. The free shuttle was fine, just make sure you plan your activites the day before because you need to reserve the shuttle for your destination. Staff very helpful, especially concierge. The warm cookies were yummy, and the kids both received a neat backpack full of activites at check-in. Room service was good, as was both on-site restaurants we sampled. A bit pricey for this middle-income family of four, but nothing unexpected. Sadly, there was no dining choices within walking distance of this hotel that we found. The river borders one side, a large industrial site the other. Walking anywhere was a bit intimidating. Parking was convienent other than not being able to access the 2nd floor of the garage directly from the elevators. You have to return to the lobby and either walk up the stairs or board a second elevator. No big deal, I guess. Very close (1 mile) to Cambridge, wish we could have spent more time there.
Bottom line: the kids didn't want to leave but the hotel meal $$ was killin' me!

title: “nice assistence”
text: We were in NY at Park Central for two nights. It seems that our room was booked dubbel. Sean helped us very quickly to find a another room and was very friendly. The location is perfect: between TimeQuare and Central Park.

title: “Disappointing: far from Inner Harbor, bit shabby, neighborhood iffy.”
text: Location left much to be desired: we were told it was pretty close to Inner Harbor, which it wasn't; there is a trolley, but after dark, even walking a block or two from trolley stop to hotel was a bit scary in the deserted neighborhood. The long walk during daylight wasn't scary but also wasn't pleasant. Was less expensive than Inner Harbor hotels, but not by that much, and not worth the difference. Room itself wasn't too bad (good exercise getting to 4th floor walk-up, but no fun with the luggage), nice view of church across street, but was rather shabby.

title: “Good location, nice hotel for the price”
text:
This hotel is a great location and for those who like walking, its a great walk from there to Michigan Ave and Grant and Millennium Park and is right next to the tourist corner spot with the 50s McDonalds, Hardrock cafe and other popular spots and if you are there for nightlife, its a nice walking loop to a variety of bars and a great Irish Pub is just across the street.
The rooms aren't large, but the hotel is nice, clean, newer remodel and an eco-tique hotel, as very green and boutique style.

title: “The perfect Seattle lcation”
text: Stayed at this hotel with my wife and another couple for a long weekend. Great staff! The concierge was very helpful in planning a wine tour outside of Seattle (30 minutes away). All of the rooms are named after vineyards and the one we stayed in had pictures of the winery. Great location for walking around Seattle, close to the Pikes Fish Market, great shopping (for my wife, not for me). They had a complimentary wine hour each night we were there!

title: “Simply the Best”
text:
We celebrated our 13th wedding anniversary here and were very pleased. Started with a shuttle from the airport (Supershuttle) and we arrived at the Marriott to nothing less than full service. From the time you pull up until you get to your room, there is someone always asking to be of service. Room was very clean and was freshened up each day. This is a very busy hotel but this does not at all take away from the wealth of service you will receive. Everything you need to do or see is in walking distance. If you want really good food, don't pass up the chance to eat at the Fish Market in Seaport Village (also walking distance). The Horton Plaza Mall is a beautiful place to shop but there are other nice shops in the area as well. I would suugest the trolley tour (green and orange bus) to get a full version of what is in the area. This tour also allows you to get off and on as much as you like($34). You can get off at the mall and catch a later bus back to your hotel. This helped us a lot, as we chose not to rent a car. If I had to put a negative sign anywhere, it would be on the parking fee ($16 a day) and I would advise to watch the taxis, they are all over the place and some of them ride unnecessary miles to get more fare if you aren't careful. Do NOT pass this by...this place should be rated BEST IN SERVICE!!!
V and E Smith, Bessemer AL

title: “Ok but I would not rave about Chancellor”
text:
I would agree with most other reviews with one or two caveats.
Position and price are the main things going for this hotel. Staff were courteous and efficent.
Caveats are as follows:
1. Our room had no airconditioning, only a ceiling fan which was totally inadequate with the warm weather we enjoyed during our stay.
2 Breakfast was greasy and tasteless, quantity rather than quality, and not cheap.We only ate in on first day of our three day visit.
3. Bathtub was small
Otherwise our stay was satisfactory.

title: “Nice location with excellent attention to detail”
text: A wonderful location and a staff that takes care of visitors like family. The location is closely located to anything anyone would want to do.

title: “I like it”
text: Stayed here for a meeting which was at the drake. paid half the price and really like the room. It is small but very clean. If I was not by myself it would have been a problem as I like to have sleeping space. Can't beat the location. Would not hesitate to stay here

title: “Wall Street Wonder”
text: A great hotel in the financial district - the king room was large for Manhattan snd well appointed. The bed was like a big cloud - sooo comfortable and a very clean hotel.

title: “Good location, room fine, everything else poor”
text:
As the other reviews state, the location is excellent and if you can get a good price then the inconveniences may not matter. However, DO NOT use the phone on any account or you will lose all the savings you have just made. Also, don't expect to sleep in, as housekeeping knock on all the doors between 8 and 8.30 - there is no Do not Disturb sign.
The elevators break down frequently and are often too full to get in. You can hear them speeding past your floor without stopping, even though you have called them.
Internet access in the business centre is intermittent. Computers did not have adequate virus protection so every time somebody downloaded something they froze up. 
There is no breakfast room and nowhere like a lounge to sit at all (except a sofa in the lobby). In summer it is not a problem to go to the cafe along the street, but in winter it might be different. Yes, decor is rather sombre, bathtubs strangely flimsy and hot water temperamental.
We did not discover there was room service till the last day, as there was nothing to indicate it in the room - no menu or leaflet - In fact, there was not even the usual booklet of hotel services you generally get in hotel rooms. 
A friend who called us was told the hotel had no record of us - we had prepaid for a week!
One day we had clean towels in the morning and they mysteriously disappeared during the day.
Phone charges are truly outrageous. The desk clerk told us it cost $27 to pick up the phone for an international call, without actually using any time, and $10 likewise to New York. You could spend hundreds of dollars before finding this out. There is no information about it in the room.
We had an excellent trip and would have considered the hotel on balance a fair buy if we had not been royally ripped off on the phone charges at the last minute.

title: “Candlewood Suite”
text: Just stayed for the week with my wife- found it to be excellent in all apsects- friendly staff who can not do enough for you - nothing is too much for them- close to times square and subways- would come back again- this is the 3rd time i have been to New York - would have no problems in coming back here or recommending others to stay here. Thanks for all your help.

title: “Save yourself some stress ... don't bother!”
text:
Aside from the location, this hotel has nothing going for it! We were greeted gruffly by the reception clerk who then rapidly fired off a tirade of instructions abouth the hotel, none of which we could remember or were documented anywhere in our room. The concierge was friendly, but never there when you needed him - we waited 40 minutes for someone to even acknowledge us at the desk to make a tour booking. 
Room was comfortable and at first look, it does look nice, but it all ends there. We stayed for 4 nights in Room 201 from 15 Nov. After the first night, not one toiletry item was restocked - not even toilet paper! I had to call reception to ask for soap and a shower cap and despite them advising it "would be sent straight up", I waited 45 minutes and even then they did not get it right. After 3 visits to my room and a claim they did not know what I meant, I finally received some soap. The next day I left a note for housekeeping requesting they restock ALL items we had used - this was a pretty clear request. Again, nothing was restocked, so I called reception again to request a shower cap and shower gel where I received a very rude response that "it should be there", and technically, if housekeeping had done their job it should have been! I then had to explain that we had not had any items replaced for 2 days and I thought this was a basic and simple request. The housekeeping staff obviously decided they would be smart and delivered to me a huge bag filled with all toiletry items EXCEPT the ones I had requested, so I again called for what I needed ... I think you're getting the picture. What makes this worse is that my husband and I stayed here with friends who kept telling us every day that their toiletry items were being replaced, even the ones they were not using!! They were staying on the same floor but at the other end of the floor and obviously had housekeeping staff who cared about the guest comfort.
The room itself was incredibly noisy. The street below is horrendous and there is NO insulation from noise. There are no curtains and the shutters did not close enough to darken the room. So if you want sleep, avoid this hotel.
The locatioin is great - ony two blocks to the Metro and an abundance of restaurants ... but that's all I can say on the positive side.
On checking out I was asked how our stay was and I responed it was "fair". When asked why I explained my story and was haned a card with details of the Operations manager and TripAdvisor. The reception clerk recommended I write a review and that the Manager would respond. I could not actually believe that there was no apology, but the hotel's own staff suggested I should write a poor review ... so here it is! I'm not sure if I will get a response as it doesn;t help me after I have left ... I just would have liked some assistance at the time. All I hope is that my experience helps others NOT stay here!

title: “Not luxury but pretty”
text: The hotel was quite nice, there was a kitchen in the room and the bed was comfortable, the location was awesome, very close to Hollywood Bowl and Stars Boulevard. Though my boyfriend saw a couple of bugs in the bathroom at night and the sink in the bathroom was leaking for a short stay it's fine.

title: “Don't bother”
text:
We booked this place cos it's cheap and there was alot of positive reviews on trip adviser. We definitely got what we paid for. 
This place is close to the farmers market but it's still a good 10min walk to get there. 
The place is run down and very basic. The soap holder in our bathroom was rusty and the window in our room has 2 holes which has been patched up with some yellow stuff. Other rooms seem to have the same type of holes. See the photos I added and you can make up your own mind. The room is not sound proof - in the morning we could hear conversations in the corridor. 
The Parking spot is at the back of the place. It's in an alley way and it's unsecured. 
The room comes with plastic cups, an 80's style aircon, a fridge that's not plugged in cos the cable doesn't reach the power point. 
There was also no cover on our blanket. 
Conclusion - 1 night is bearable, any longer please don't stay here, especially if you have a family.  This is not hotel standard - it's a cheap motel at best.

title: “Near Chinatown Gate, but no chinese eateries.”
text:
Not very modern, but clean and well maintained. My room did not face the road and was very quiet. Free wifi. No breakfast.
Location is quite central. A short walk to the turntable for the Powell-Hyde historic trolley along Market St. You can also board the F-line along Market St that brings you to Fisherman's wharf, passing the Ferry Terminal Market along the way.
Even though the hotel is right at the Chinatown Gate, don't count on getting chinese breakfast in the morning. That stretch of Chinatown has mostly souvenier shops. Plenty of Starbucks, Subway and western eateries though.

title: “Good budget conscious accomodation”
text: This motel was the closest to our destination in South Pasadena, and was also on the low cost end of the spectrum. The neighborhood is on the edge of El Serrino which may look a little dicey, but we were pleasantly surprised and felt secure in the the property. It is set up in a fort style with one entry -- a two story building surrounding the parking lot. The staff was friendly. We opted for the king size bed, which was very comfortable, but tight for the room. The facility is definitely older, but had fresh paint outside, upgraded tile in the bathroom adn was clean. There was also a microwave and small refrigerator. We were on the upper floor, which was quiet. There was also a walk in closet, The heater was a little noisey during the night, but an adjustment on the dial set that right. The continental breakfast was modest, but adequate, with cereal, instant oatmeal, muffins and danish, eggo waffles, toast and juice -- no fruit. We stayed three nights, and slept well all three nights. It was not fancy, but was secure and comfortable, plus we loved the money we saved over other options.

title: “Memorial weekend getaway”
text: Decided to go away the last minute Memorial Day Weekend. Was very surprised when I called Omni reservations and found a hotel room available for a Sunday stay. Coming from Northern New Jersey we arrived early Sunday morning. The staff was very polite and helpful as they put all our bags in storage, preregisterd for our room which would not be ready till 4:00pm check in, and valet parked the car. The location in regard to the historic sites could not be any better, a walk up the block and you are at Independence park area. We were able to do a whole day of sightseeing before getting into our room all because of the hotel's hospitality.When we returned for our room at 4:00 we just had to pick up our key and our room was ready. It was a standard priced room, but larger than most as it had a king size which slept me, my wife, and the 2 year old baby. The sofa bed opened into a queen bed for my 7 & 10 year olds. A perfect room for families traveling. The only negatives, the indoor pool is only a lap pool and you have to pay for parking. Both of these are not that big a deal when dealing with big city hotels. Also wanted to add, the double decker big bus tour is well worth it, as it gives you a flavor for the rest of the city. An overall wonderful stay at the city of brotherly love.

title: “Great deal in Seattle”
text:
I came to Seattle for an important meeting and this was where the local company put me up. I liked this hotel a lot and made me look up other locations for when I stay in the Pacific Northwest. Reasonably priced for the amenities.
Short cab ride from the Amtrak station. The front desk was very helpful. Homey lobby feel. I wouldn't have minded a restaurant or bar in the hotel but there is plenty nearby. I walked around the neighborhood by myself at night and it didn't seem sketchy at all, in fact I started looking at condos in the area that night on the net.
The room was good sized and clean. Mini fridge and microwave. Free wifi. Large flat screen TV. Room was modern and comfy. Nice clean comfy bed. Nice vanity area and Aveda goodies. Bathroom was clean and fair sized.
Definitively a great deal for Seattle.

title: “We Loved IT!!!”
text:
WOnderful service, WOnderful hotel!!! Very impressed.
My husband arrived early and we had booked on Hotwire so we weren't sure what to expect. FIrst he was told we had full beds I believe. He asked if a queen was available....THey checked and told him to leave luggage come back later in the day. At check in time he returned and they put him into the newly renovated annex (gorgeous!!!) and I believe we had a king sized bed. ROom was SO nice!! We loved it. View was okay...we were on 7th floor so we couldn't see much!! It was in a great location!!!
Staff was very helpful!!
Great afternoon happy hour and morning breakfasts!!!
Drinks and hors d'ourves superb!!!
We will stay again!!

title: “FANTASTIC LOCATION....GREAT HOTEL.”
text:
We stayed at the Comfort Inn from Apr 4th to the 8th. They were fantastic...our fight got in really early in the morning so they let us leave our luggage and explore. We also flew out late and they did the same. The rooms were small but what do you really need??? By the time you get home you are exhausted from all the walking. The beds were comfy and there is a fridge and microwave which is nice. They also give you free water each day. All the staff was fantastic and the concierge was helpful. We have a great stay....New York is a fabulous city. This hotels is minutes from Madison Square Gardens, Times Square, Penn Station and Port Authority. It is easy to get anywhere in this City from this hotel.
I would recommend this place to everyone!

title: “Not impressed better go to the Algonquin”
text: Definetely a nice work on remodeling, but nothing else from there. The breakfast restaurant very expensive and regular how dare they compare it to Balthazar? Aside from that they do not have an executive lunch and business center is a theft. 8.95 to get 15minutes just to access our theather tickets, not to mention two dollars for printing them. These left me very dissapointed, cannot be compared tonthe algonquin, the other autograph collection.

title: “Very Disappointed”
text: I found this hotel through Amazon Local deals. Checked it out on the internet and seemed like a nice place. Unfortunately it turned out to be the opposite. When we entered our room it was extremely hot. No problem, I thought, I'll just turn down the heat. However, there is no thermostat in the room! I have travelled extensively and stayed in many types of hotels and have never stayed in a room where I couldn't control the temperature. I complained to the staff, but there answer was that the AC was turned off and I should open the window. As a result, the 2 nights I stayed in this room were horrible, couldn't sleep because I was sweating from the heat. Would never even consider this place on my next trip to NYC.

title: “Came back after staying at other Denver hotels for a few years”
text:
The Magnolia is back on the list of hotels we can stay at for work, it's a great hotel.
Free hot breakfast included scrambled eggs, sausage, oatmeal, fruit, bagels, muffins, yogurt ....
Clean, well maintained rooms, large bath and closet.. They have a free late afternoon happy hour and milk and cookies later in the evening.

title: “Good Hotel, near the airport”
text:
We stayed here twice last week for total of 4 nights. We were recommended this hotel because if its close proximity to LAX airport, in fact, its just a short walk across the road to Terminal 1.
Free shuttle bus to & from the airport & not far from Hire Car rentals. Valet parking at the hotel costs US$25 per night.
The hotel rooms were clean & proper, despite being quite dated. There was no in-room safe.
On our first stay, I found a cleaning cloth in the bathroom, seems like housekeeping left it there.
On our second stay, there was a chap-stick on the desk, presumably from the previous guest & the bathroom did not have any Shower gel / shampoo. Nothing too serious here.
The hotel has free wifi which is always a plus, decent connection speeds. Its been a while since I stayed in a hotel that still has CRT television sets but thats also not a problem.
The reception staff were helpful & friendly, & the cafe in the lobby had good selection for breakfast, it served starbucks coffee.
The only thing that I was not to happy with was the water pressure in the showers, it was quite weak & not what you'd expect from a hotel.
Overall, I was quite pleased with this hotel, its a good choice if you are staying over LA for a couple of nights, its close to the airport & car rentals & for the price, its a good deal.

title: “Terrific service in trendy accommodations”
text:
I have to say I had a great stay at Public! The service was incredible! They brought me hot water for my tea every evening (upon request,) they greeted us warmly every time we returned to the hotel, and provided band-aids for my friend's blister (too much walking!) It was freezing and I was able to get a late check out on the night if my departure so I didn't have to wander around in the cold all day! I will say the rooms are tiny, but I didn't mind. The hotel is very similar to The Standard hotel chain (same company,) so I knew what to expect of the rooms.
I came to Chicago just to eat (Alinea, Girl and the Goat, The Publician, etc.) but one of my favorite dinners was at The Pump Room (the Jean Georges restaurant at the hotel.) Great dessert! 
I booked my flight and hotel together on Priceline and got a FANTASTIC rate because of it! For the price I paid, this was perfect. Pretty good location (15-20 min walk from most shopping etc.) Great service. Good food.

title: “Hotel Airport best of a bad bunch”
text: Stayed here when my flight was cancelled and after i refused to stay at the Holiday Inn O'Hare (which is the worst hotel in the world). The hotel is in a good location on the airport, is clean has a good breakfast and comfortable beds.The wifi is not free which it should be in a place like this but otherwise an ok place if you have to stay at the airport.

title: “Definantly worth staying!”
text: From my personal experience this is a great hotel especially if you are wanting to stay as a family! Very affordable especially considering the location. It is about a $10 cab ride to the main part of Hollywood. Straight across the road is a supermarket and the subway next door. The reception staff are very helpful and the maintenance man is really good. The hotel is really cool and like no other it has murals everywhere! It has a nice pool and also laundry facilities. The room itself was good for us as it had a fridge and a microwave and also a coffee maker. There is a good amount of free parking. They are still doing some refurbishments but it is looking really good. My only tip for anyone staying would be if you dont want to be disappointed get to breakfast early as it becomes very very busy in the mornings and there is not alot of room in the breakfast room.

title: “Good for families for short stays.”
text: We have stayed in several Drury Inns and this one is like the others, but I was a little disappointed in a few things. The check-in was super easy and super fast...important for families with small children. The hallways had a weird musty smell to them and there was a faint smoky smell been though we were in non-smoking rooms. The shower was missing a shower curtain and the bedspreads had some nasty stains on them. Breakfast was well-stocked and fresh. Overall, a little disappointing from our previous stays at Drury Inns.

title: “Fantastic Time in Jail”
text: The Liberty hotel has everything you could possibly need, and if they don't have it, they'll get it for you. The staff were friendly, polite, and willing to go the extra mile for guests. Guests receive a glass of champagne when they arrive and the first night we were there the hotel was having a special event with complimentary wine. The hotel has numerous places to dine and even has bikes for guests to take out on the town. The room was very comfortable and bright. The housekeepers seemed to be a bit rushed. They were always on the lookout to see if you were leaving for the day so that they could make up the room. The atmosphere of the hotel was very sophisticated and was a great place to hold meetings. It was also a fantastic location - walking distance to most attractions and right along the water. The jail transformation is an added piece of character that makes this hotel unique.

title: “This is perfect.”
text: Absolutely well located, a few blocks from downtown Seattle, a few blocks from the Public Market, this Hotel has excellent service, great and spacious rooms, clean and comfortable. Wi-fi was also working in my room. Not to mention the Moore Coffee, a small and beaultiful coffee shop just for you. If you are going to Seattle, this is your hotel.

title: “Best Option for Luxury in Downtown Detroit”
text:
We chose to stay for a night in downtown Detroit before heading to DTW for a flight to Mexico. We had an airmiles reward certificate that was about to expire, so we decided to use the opportunity to explore Detroit a little and stay at the Westin Book Cadillac, which I'd been curious about since its opening.
Even though Mapquest told us to cross into Detroit from Windsor at the Ambassador Bridge, we took the tunnel as it just seemed a lot closer to the hotel--- which it was. It was easy to find and made a good first impression. We left the car with the valet, entered the rather nondescript lobby, and made our way up one level to check in. No other guests were in line, so it was a quick process.
Our room was on the 16th floor and had views of downtown and the river/Ambassador Bridge in the distance. We were immediately impressed by the sheer size of the bedroom and the bathroom-- huge by city hotel standards. Everything was in immaculate condition and there was lots of storage. There was only one bathrobe, so we called housekeeping and another one was brought up in a few minutes.
After a bit of a rest we went downstairs to have dinner. Roast had a 90 minute wait, so we went to the Spa 1924 Grille instead, where there was no wait for a table. The restaurant was quite busy with what appeared to be business travelers, and service was a little slow. We thought our meal was okay, but surprisingly priced similarly to the menu at Roast. Two appetizers, two entrees and a bottle of wine brought us to $145 after taxes and tip. In retrospect, we wished we'd waited for a table at Roast.
The next morning we had a great workout at the well-equipped fitness centre (with 'urban' views of an alleyway and abandoned building) and then headed out onto the city streets in search of a decent breakfast (the Boulevard Room was empty and menu prices were very steep). We ended up eating at a very cool little cafe inside the Guardian Building (the most impressive art deco interior I've ever seen). We walked around a little more, admiring the architecture, toured an urban vegetable garden across the street from the hotel, then checked out to drive to the Motown Museum and then the DTW Westin for an overnight stay before our morning flight.
We left feeling impressed with the city and the hotel, and would definitely like to return for a long weekend to explore the downtown a little more.

title: “Decent for short stay”
text: I stayed here for four nights recently while taking my daughter to USC. Easy to get to from the airport , convenient to USC, and not too hard to get to attractions of Beverly Hills, Hollywood, Santa Monica as long as you have a car. Usual good Marriott service. It could use some updating - the carpet in the lobby is atrocious! Room was clean and the bathroom appeared to have been recently updated, surprisingly comfortable bed (and I sleep badly at most hotels). We had breakfast once in the hotel, very overpriced mediocre food. It was a good value overall for what I paid, but would not recommend it for LA tourists given its downtown location.

title: “No Upgrade, A Miserly Breakfast Instead”
text:
We'd contacted this hotel well in advance before making a reservation for our first visit to Boston, our last port of call on a month-long tour of the USA. My partner holds a Hilton Honors "Gold VIP" card which entitles him to a room upgrade at Hiltons or, failing that, breakfast. When we Emailed the manager the implication was that we would be booking a pretty good room ("Superior Corner Room") but that an upgrade may be available to a "River View" room. This was not forthcoming so he was given vouchers for a "Continental" breakfast. We checked that this was correct as, at other Hilton-brand hotels we'd been given an excellent full breakfast in lieu of upgrade. But that was their policy so we suffered the meanest (ie most miserly) of breakfasts we'd encountered on our whole tour involving stays at 18 different hotels. Well done Hilton. This was worse than any Comfort Inn or Best Western Continental breakfast we had come across. 
Having said this, the waitress (from Eastern Europe, perhaps?) who was attending to breakfast could not have been more helpful and friendly. It's just a pity she had so little material to work with!
This somewhat spoiled our stay here as did the rather limited public space, much of which was taken up by a dreaded Starbucks.
Hotel staff (Bell hops and Reception staff) we friendly enough but this hotel did not have the feel of a big-city hotel as the whole approach was somewhat amateurish. There was no official valet parking but the guys at the door were happy to do this for you - at your own risk I guess!
The room was good. A nice view (away from the river!). The corner was wasted, though, as no extra furniture was provided. Just one lounge chair in the room when there was easily enough room for a 2nd comfy chair in the large empty space next to the computer desk. Two in a room so why not two chairs to sprawl in??
We loved Boston and Back Bay is an excellent location for bars and restaurants and an easy walk or ride (the subway is great) to all the other attractions.
Shame about the breakfast! We'll look elsewhere next time.

title: “Sorry I was only here 1 night”
text: This is a place I would have enjoyed to stay at for more than just the one night I was in Detroit Lakes. I was a little concerned when I found this place on the internet and it was listed as a Best Western. As a frequent traveler Best Western is not one of my top 3 or 4 choices to stay. This place has large rooms and really great bathrooms. All rooms face the lake and have either a walk out patio or a balcony. There are 3 levels to this hotel. The 2nd floor is street level and is where the front desk is, but on the lakeside it is actually the 2nd level-hence they consider it the 2nd floor. If you don't want to deal with elevators, ask for a 2nd floor room. The pool and hot tub area is hugh and well kept. The breakfast is pretty standard, although there was a hugh assortment of fruit-grapes strawberries and melon this particular morning. I can certainly see where this hotel and the Detroit Lakes area would and IS a vaction destination in itself

title: “Philadelphia and Le Meridian both exceeded our expectations.”
text: This was a great weekend for us. The hotel was convenient to everything, even in the cold, including the train from the airport. I would recommend this hotel without reservation, (well, actually you should make reservations, just don't hold any) especially the staff. However, I must admit we found the people of Philadelphia in general to be absolutely charming. People were genuinely nice everywhere so it is no surprise the staff were exceptional. As an example when you walk down the street only the tourists think they own all of the sidewalk and everyone should get out of their way. The natives very courteously move to one side and share the sidewalk.

title: “Love it!”
text: I love Hamptons and they are just about the only place I will stay. Every time I go elsewhere I am disappointed. The poo is just a little on the small side but the rooms are wonderful and the breakfast is fantastic. I would stay there again in a heartbeat. Great location!

title: “Comfortable room, great location”
text: We read many positive reviews of this hotel, but it was even better than expected. Check-in was quick and efficient. We had room #906 with a king size bed. Though small, it was comfortable and very nicely decorated. There was a small desk with a chair, bedside tables, and a larger unit that included the television. The best thing was the bed - one of the most comfortable I've ever slept in; I wanted to take it home with me. A minor irritation was that the flat screen TV was mounted to the side of the bed, not the best position for viewing. The bathroom was clean and had everything we needed. The location of the hotel is excellent- one block from Times Square and about 3 blocks to the subway. Yet 46th Street itself is quiet and noise was not an issue at all. There are several restaurants within one block, along with two deli's. We enjoyed St Andrew's Pub and Restaurant, right across the street. The continental breakfast at the hotel has the usual items, toast and bagels, a couple of cereals, pastries, yogurt, and hard boiled eggs. Everything was fresh and the breakfast attendant kept everything clean and stocked. The only drawback is that the breakfast room could use more tables - I suspect there is simply no room to expand. Overall, we were very happy with this hotel and wouldn't hesitate to return.

title: “An impressively appointed hotel with 5-Star looks but 3-Star service”
text:
Stayed at The St Regis DC back on April 10th for one night. I was planning on staying at the Westin but was offered a rate of only $250 at The St Regis so I opted for that option instead. I must start by saying that I have stayed at many higher-end 4 Seasons, Ritz Carlton, Mandarin, Peninsula, etc. but this would be my first stay at a St Regis. Given what I hear about the St Regis brand, I assumed that expectations would be just as high as those other brands.
I arrived by train into Union Station and quickly got a taxi to the hotel. Taxi was about $10 and was a quick 10min ride. There is a metro stop not far from the hotel and valet was $40.
Was pleasantly greeted at the door and my two small bags were brought to the small reception desk. The lobby was very small but was well furnished in a nice classical decor. Reception was smooth but was plain and mechanical. I was upgraded from a superior to deluxe room as SPG Gold. At this point my bags where sitting next to reception on the floor with no offer for help or any bellman in sight. Let me say that I definitely did not need help and if offered I would of refused because I could manage it, but I would expect the offer from the reception or bellman.
The room was very small but well decorated and spotless all around. I was very impressed with the materials they choose for the room and it was definitely on par with 5-star properties. I must say that if I was staying here for more than 1-2 nights, this room would be too small. There were a grand list of available amenities available but did not take advantage of any. The view I had was of 16th St, which was nothing special. However, I did hear 2 different people complain about their view, which must of been at the other side of the hotel.
Location was very close to the White House and the National Mall. Had no problem walking anywhere in those areas. The only problem I had found is beyond the tourist sites on The Mall, the hotel is not very convenient. You will need a taxi to any good shopping, nightlife or dining areas. That could get annoying after a few days. However, for me I'd rather be close to all the tourist sites given my 1 night stay
The concierge was no help at all. I went for help in locating a lunch spot and was disappointed with the food. The type of dinner spot I requested was not what I asked for when I got there. Finally the kind of nightlife I wanted was a complete opposite. I ended up going to a different place to eat and a different place to party. Checkout again was plain and mechanical.
Overall the property itself was very well appointed in high end materials and sits in a great location to see all the sites. The rooms were luxurious but the size was disappointing. The service is far below a 5 star property given the coldness of the reception and lack of knowledge of the concierge. I would stay here again if the price is at a lower end. Otherwise if you are looking for 5-star treatment go elsewhere in DC.

title: “Very Good Stay”
text:
All in all, a very nice hotel. First the positives:
- Location: In the Loop, so it's near State Street/Marshall Field's, central business and financial district, etc.
- The hotel's restaurants: There are two- 312 Chicago and Encore. 312 Chicago serves great "Italian-Inspired American Cuisine" and Encore does a nice lunch.
- Overall Decor
- Very Clean
- Very nice/engaging staff
- Pet-friendly
- The free evening wine was a great touch
...and just a couple of negatives:
- We booked a non-smoking room only to be told that the only room meeting our requirements (a double-double) was located on a smoking floor.
- Very small bathroom

title: “Renovation appears complete- this place is quite nice!”
text:
We were concerned after reading all of the negative reviews, but this hotel is really very nice and a great home-base for visiting Austin. We have stayed in many Austin hotels and would definitely stay here again. The lobby area is lovely, and the pool is beautifully modern and Texas-style with a fountain, comfy lounges, and a sunny courtyard. 
Our room was clean and perfectly comfortable. The bed is great with nice down pillows and high quality bedding. The bathroom has everything we need, and there is a spacious reading area with a couch and desk. I would recommend this hotel as a good, basic accommodation in a great location for enjoying the South Congress area.

title: “Pleasant stay in historic property”
text: This property was built in the late 1920s and was originally called the Boston Statler Hotel. The lobby and other common areas have retained their original charm, with sparkling chandeliers, coffered ceilings, and elevator doors with handpainted motifs. The hotel is around the corner from the Boston Common and public transportation options are plentiful. The room was comfortable, with two double beds, duvets, and multiple pillows. There was also a Keurig coffee maker, cable TV, 2 phones, reading lights, radio clock, a desk with chair, iron/ironing board, and a small armchair. The bathroom was very tiny and reflected the hotel's origins. Although some alterations were made to the tub/shower, the radiator heater, small sink, bathroom tiles on the walls and floor, and the small bathroom door all hinted at being from the 20s. We had an issue with lack of water in the sink when we checked into our room, but the reception desk sent hotel maintenance to look at it and it was fixed in no time. That was a very nice surprise, especially since this happened late at night. The area is full of eateries nearby, so there are plenty of options if you don't feel like trying out the restaurants and pub at the hotel. Maggianos, across the street, is a really nice option if you like Italian.

title: “Just "meh"...”
text: We stayed here for the River Lighting ceremony and the only good thing about it was that we had a nice view of the parade but paid for it (literally). Self parking means you have to leave the premises and make 3 rights to get to the parking garage around the corner, otherwise, valet is $39 a night. The rooms are nice but they should be for $209 (non-river view) a night. The 4 elevators couldn't handle the crowd before and after the parade so we ended up riding in the employee elevator to get back to the room. The burger joint was closed for a private party and the main restaurant/bistro had been booked for weeks. That left us with Dirty Nelly's Pub where a ½ lb burger started at $16. We ended up splitting a Chicken Caesar salad ($14) and rolled our eyes when we realized the dressing was just bottled. For that price, seriously?!? The bed and pillows were great but we'll be staying somewhere else next year.

title: “BED BUGS !!! RUN AWAY FROM THIS PLACE”
text: not sure what else to say other than i have horrible welts on my body and am scared that I brought them back to my house. The night I checked in there were no lamps on the end table, no ironing board, clock was wrong and the television was broken. I think the room was off limits and they gave it to me anyway.

title: “Perfect for short stay”
text:
I stayed in one of the Junior suites in the Central Tower for three nights in Oct 2012. First the positives: My room was spacious, bedding was comfortable, cleanliness was top notch, staff was nice, check-in/out was breeze. Now the negatives: Wifi is not free and is rather steeply prices at around 14 bucks/day; Even though coffee is complimentary in the room, water is not, No eating options in and around the hotel in the night (everything closes by 6pm or so). There are couple of restaurants in the hotel, I tried their bar at the lobby level which was overcrowded though food quality was decent. 
Would stay again if on business.

title: “Very good hotel, would definitely return.”
text:
I was very pleased with the hotel, very well appointed rooms, clean and spacious. Check in and check out ("zip-out") was very smooth as well.
The location was not that great (in terms of amenities), one definitely needs to drive around if you wanna go places, but parking is rather inexpensive ($14 self parking per day).
I would definitely return to this hotel.

title: “Others could take a lesson from these folks..the get it right”
text:
This is the fourth year I have stayed here and the service levels have been maintained even through the economical down turn. Hospitality is disappearing in the industry and it's truly refreshing to find one that hasn't squeezed guest's experience to inflate the bottom the line. Thank you to Rachel, at the front desk, for keep your genuine positive attitude while multitasking during check in! The doorman and Bell staff and always with a smile and observant of the lobby activities. Makes you feel like someone is keeping eye on things in a good way. 
Brewed Starbucks for the morning's Lobby coffee.
Revised and expanded menu for the breakfast voucher in Pigalle's was flavorful and served quickly. 
All and all a very pleasant experience. Thank you

title: “Magical Hotel ...”
text:
We actually visited this hotel in May 2010, and had a wonderful stay!! 
The best thing about this hotel is their staff, they are extremely friendly and helpful!
When we moved in, the receptionist welcomed us very warmly and offered us drinks.
We were asking him for places to visit, and poor guy he printed for us the directions for those places to visit them. Very very helpful!!
Something I will never forget, at one day I called the reception to ask for pair of sleepers for my room, and she told me that it is not available (because they do not offer it). So I was like "okay".
Then, when I went out and came back in that evening, I was very surprised to see a new pair of sleepers on my bed. That was "magical"!!
This hotel deserves to be called "Magic Castle Hotel", because it is like magic.. You ask what you want, and you get it. They will always try to make your stay comfortable, and if you need anything they will get it for you.
They offered DVDs and snacks/drinks where always available.
I would definitely return back to this hotel!

title: “Great service and location, rooms a touch dated but still a favorite”
text: While there are newer and more up-to-date options in the area, the Four Seasons remains my favorite. Service is top-notch. The staff has helped me with everything from reservations to organizing birthday surprises and taking deliveries prior to my arrival. Always welcoming. The rooms are very nice, if a touch dated. The larger rooms (I forget their exact name, but the largest room before getting to suite level) and the lower level suites are roomy and very comfortable. Nice bar as well. Recommended.

title: “Perfect Choice”
text: My daughter and I traveled to Houston from central Louisiana to shop for and purchase a car and stayed for two nights. Based on the reviews we saw for this hotel, it was the perfect choice! The room was extremely clean and the hotel was well managed by the courteous and accessible staff. Our room was on the ground floor near the back part of the hotel. The hot breakfast and continental breakfast options were adequate. But the room was the highlight! The comfortable beds were on par with those in finer hotels and the bedding included soft, high thread count sheets and heavy comforter. Flat screen television, wi-fi, in-room safe, coffeemaker, refrigerator, microwave, portable telephone, etc were great. The bathroom had a high flow shower head with plenty of hot water and curved shower curtain bar. The vanity area was roomy with plenty of counter space for my daughters cosmetics, hair care products, etc :-). The pool and hot tub area looked nice but we did not have an opportunity to enjoy it. Since we were near the airport, there was some jet noise but it died down around 10:00-10:30 PM both nights. Access to I-H 45 was easy. The hotel parking lot was a little tight but workable. The value could not have been better!

title: “So So Soho”
text: Nothing grand and nothing terrible about the Soho. Room was adequate but furniture was worn. Could use better lighting. Staff friendly enough. Room service sandwich was fine. Room faced construction across the street. All in all, an OK hotel but nothing more.

title: “Congested Rooms, pathetic location”
text:
I stayed at Rodeway Inn from March 19th to March 22nd. It is good if you are looking for cheap accomodation. I shifted from Inner Harbor as my meetings got over and I went around Inner Harbor. I wanted to check out other places. 
Small rooms, noisy, and pathetic breakfast.
But good if you just want to relax and catch up on your sleep. Subway next to the lodge is a great advantage.

title: “Perfect base for Manhattan vacation”
text:
Our red-eye flight arrived 2 hours late so we were very tired when we go the Surrey. Unfortunately, we were still a few hours early of check in. We dropped our bags off at the desk and proceeded to venture through Central Park while we waited for our room to be available. After a few hours, we strolled back into the Surrey only to be disappointing that our room was still not ready. However, this turned out to be a great thing because the terrific staff upgraded us to a suite because we'd been waiting for so long. We got to our room and were blown away. Exquisite furniture, fantastic bed, awesome decor. This room was great.
The Surrey staff is awesome. They take care of whatever you need. The hotel has a roof-top area with outstanding views of Manhattan and the park. The food is a little pricey and not really that great. We didn't eat at the hotel very much because it's New York and there is great food everywhere.
The location of the Hotel is perfect for venturing out into all of Manhattan. The location is right next to metro stations and major bus stops.
Highly Recommended.

title: “Couldn't get much better.”
text: We had a corner suite on 23rd floor with views of bay and space needle. With the floor to ceiling windows it was like being in a postcard, especially at night. Staff was outstanding. Hotel is within walking distance of all downtown. If you only have a carryon, take the light rail to and from the airport. It's $2.50 a person and you get off at Westlake, 2 blocks from hotel. Best deal is happy hour at Ruth's Chris Steakhouse in the lobby. In the lounge you can get prime rib sliders for $5.95, outstanding!! The reviewer who mentioned no carafe, the coffee maker in the room is designed to just have the cup put below the spout so it's brewed into your coffe cup. The only problem we had was solved without our even asking. I ordered room service breakfast for myself and a carafe of coffee for my wife, they we're a little late and my wife decided to go shopping instead of wait for her coffee. I asked them to take the coffee back when my breakfast arrived, then when I called to have them remove the room service table, they told me they'd comped the whole breakfast since it was a little late. Great service.

title: “Hotel Metropolis Review – “tries to be trendy, ends up feeling cheap””
text:
We stayed at this hotel for one night. Based on the Internet photos, I thought we were going to find something much different than what we ended up with. I expected a small room, but our room was so small we didn't have room to put our luggage on the floor. Additionally, the pillows and linens were visably dirty, and our shower was broken. The smoke alarm was hanging broken over our bed. Also, we could hear every word from the guests near our room as if they were in the same room as us.
Overall, I feel like the description on the Internet is misleading. The lighting of the photos definately was altered vs reality. The dirty room makes the comfort inn feel like a 5 star hotel. I would never go back to this hotel.

title: “There's a Lake, but there's alson construction!”
text: The RI Lake Union sees very little lake and a lot of construction. We did not walk in the area and had good luck parking all over, including pikes market. This RI must have been an Embassy suites, due to the interior courtyard design, which is also utilized as a breakfast area. The pool was set on broil, so don't put your head under- you may be served with drawn butter. The actual room was good quality and the location had "walkable" access to the space needle. The SN gift shop is awesome, but the needle itself is a rip. do the Smith tower in pioneer square or drive up Queen Anne's hill for an awesome view.

title: “Good value for location and amenities”
text:
We chose this hotel b/c it was close enough to Universal Studios Hollywood but not costing the high price like Sheraton or Hilton that was even closer. It does take about 15 minutes to walk to the base of Universal Citywalk but additional 15 minutes through Citywalk to get to front entrance of the Universal Studios Hollywood. No shuttle available as some reviews stated in past unless it was available before. Includes wifi which works okay. Includes hot breakfast which is okay as well - the pancakes were good - didn't care so much for the scrambled eggs or something else I didn't know what it was and they didn't label - but at least the choices were good. We chose a junior suite which includes extra sink with microwave and refrigerator - it's not a suite in the sense of having a separate living room space, but my guess it is slightly bigger than the regular rooms. We had 2 adults and 2 kids. The room was clean. A/C worked well but it makes a lot of noise and turns on and off or to low blowing fan so hard to sleep with it on. Beds were comfortable though. Traffic noise outside wasn't so bad with windows closed and A/C off. The soap and shampoo/conditioner they provide has a cinnamon kind of smell - can't say it's my favorite but will do. Plenty of parking available - didn't seem too crowded when we went. We paid about 156-170 dollars a night. We tried the indoor pool - a bit cold but my kids were able to tolerate such - it is a small indoor pool but still a pool. 
The area around seems safe enough but would only recommend walking when it is bright. Not too many people walking about - mostly a few stores nearby and then lots of apartments. Starbucks across the street. Hotel right off the highway. Overall this was a great choice to go to Universal Studios. We didn't drive unless we wanted to. We ate at Citywalk for most of the evenings or even at lunchtime instead of at the park.

title: “Wonderful staff, great location, comfortable accommodations!”
text: This was our first time at the Bulfinch, and we would stay there again. We stayed for four nights in a comfortable room with a sitting area and king size bed. Our view from the ninth floor was of the Boston skyline, including the gold dome of the State Building. We loved the location, just a few blocks from the Haymarket T station, Quincy Market and the North End. Where we couldn't walk to was only a T ride away. We ate breakfast in the Flat Iron Restaurant, and recommend the oatmeal! The front desk staff was friendly and welcoming each time we re-entered the hotel. We even liked the toiletries, especially the soap.

title: “Very nice rooms, good value, a bit chaotic”
text: I stayed at this hotel on a Sunday night between the end of the Formula One race and the start of a convention, so it was chaotic. But we got checked in and out easily, using the valet for our car was simple and fast, the rooms were very nice and well-appointed. Overall, a definite keeper!

title: “Lovely place to stay!”
text:
I stayed here with my two adult daughters and we absolutely loved the place! After a long time travelling we arrived at 9pm to be greeted with very friendly staff, so polite it was very refreshing. Particuarly the doormen. Check in was swift and our one bedroom suite was cleaned to a high standard everyday and the maid always left extra smellies for the three of us. 
Great cafe over the road which has already been mentioned, they serve a huge selection of breakfasts to choose from. (U.N Cafe) The Top of The Tower cocktail lounge has wonderful views of the city at night. The cocktails worked out at about six pounds each but was well worth it for the views. Again the waiters were very helpful and friendly. 
Location is okay if you don't mind walking, times square is about 15 - 20 mins. The grocery store over the road is handy too.(Also very friendly) There's a little pet boutique up the road which had some nice things, the gentleman who owned it was lovely and very chatty. The suite was huge and spacious by New York standards, with plenty of cupboard space with a walk in wardrobe too. Having a kitchen was great and it was stocked with all the extras you will need. Don't hesitate to stay here I am already planning to return at the same time this year.
BEWARE- When we arrived at La Guardia airport we were approached by a taxi driver (not a yellow cab) offering us the whole deal for a whopping $80 inc. tip claiming we would be waiting in the queue for a yellow cab for a long time. When we actually only waited for 10 mins and only cost us $30.
TIP - Do the empire state building at night there was virtually no queue! We went about 8pm, don't miss it the views are fantastic.

title: “Perfect”
text:
This hotel is located outside from downtown on the north side of the city.
We were terrified by the exterior of the building, but then inside everything changed.
Warm welcome, nice smell, nice modern decor, elegant restaurant, beautiful spa.
Room are a littlebit larger then other Palomars (ex P.Westwood), soft bed and crisp
linen (very appreciated), clean.. just perfect.
Still I don't understand why they keep placing that orrible bathtub instead of a modern shower which in my opinion will be much cooler..?!?
Don't know if I will ever be back to Dallas, but in that case I will sure know where to stay.

title: “Great location”
text: Stayed 1st of May 2004 for 5 days. Great location literally 2 minutes walk from Grand Central Station, 15 minutes from Times Square. Room clean but a bit of a musty smell although my friends said their room was fine. Fabulous bar but pricey.

title: “If you want to stay in a SAUNA this is the place for you!!!!!”
text: BEWARE the hotel is a sweat box. We stayed here well 1/2 a night after turning on the a/c and finding out from the front desk that it was hot or cold we left in the middle of the night at 1:00 AM. The room has a thermostat but, good luck it does not control the room temperature that is controlled elsewhere. TERRIBLE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “My new hotel in San Francisco”
text:
I am happy to report that I have found my new favorite hotel in San Francisco. The Petite Auberge has everything that I could possibly want. Quiet, peaceful location but easy walking distance to Union Square and Nob Hill. 
Comfortable beds, lovely decor, gracious staff, spotless rooms, amazing breakfasts...all those little touches that make you feel catered to. 
I have recommended the hotel to friends and now I recommend it to you.

title: “Great Stay”
text: Just back from first trip to DC. Stayed at the Carlyle Suites Hotel. Great choice. The staff was extremely friendly, helpful and very professional. The rooms were beautiful, spacious, comfortable and immaculate. Charming restaurants in the hotel where we had several meals that were all excellant. Great location, walking distance to Dupont Circle, Tour bus lines, and many restaurants. The Carlyle Suites Hotel was a great find. Would highly recommend staying there.

title: “I left the resort relaxed and in a great mood and ready to attack my Monday.”
text:
August 21, 2010-It has been a little over a week since we have been home from our Stay-cation at the Arizona Grand Resort. This was not our first time staying at the resort, we try to make it there for a family weekend at least once a year. We are still talking about our visit. We have some dear friends that also like the Arizona Grand, yet we are never able to go at the same time. This year we made a pact that we were going together.  We both have daughters about the same age so we were looking forward to a great time. 
When we got there we were greeted by very friendly staff, we waited in line to get our rooms and the relaxation was starting to already set in. We were all ready for a fun time.  When we got to our adjoining rooms we realized that there was a maintenance issue in our room. I do not consider this the fault of the resort, things do break. The only reason that I would be an unhappy guest is the way that that the situation was being handled. 
In this case I was not an unhappy guest.  
I called the front desk and in a few minutes someone was at our door working on the issue. It was determined that this was not going to be a quick fix. I contacted the front desk and spoke to the Manager, Ryan Moyer and explained the situation. He was all about making sure that we were taken care of.   I explained to him that we had our best friends in the next room and that we would need to move together as this was a group trip.  He asked if he could call me back after he had a solution for us.
A few minutes later, Ryan called and said that he was going to be moving us and that a bell-person would be coming up to move all of our luggage. A few minutes later a friendly staff member came with our new room keys and we were off.
Ryan apologized for the problem in our room and said we would be happy where we were being moved to. We were, the rooms are great and we actually were a bit closer to the park. Ryan got us rooms that were attached which really made for a fun time. 
 The service was outstanding! You can tell that the staff really cares about the guests. I am surprised by some of the reviews that said the staff was rude because we experienced nothing but hospitable, friendly and over-the-top service throughout the entire complex.  We all enjoyed our breakfast in the restaurant. The majority of our group are all "Bacon Freaks" the bacon that was served with our breakfast was delicious! It was not your typical thin as paper bacon, it was thick, crisp bacon. 
The price for the breakfast was very reasonable. The fresh squeezed orange juice was not served in a 4 ounce glass, which I appreciated. The small loaf of bread served with my breakfast was a nice touch.
The water slides are so much fun, this time we decided that this was going to be a very relaxing "lazy River" adventure.  I will say that as a parent, I appreciated and noticed the park's attention to safety. They had plenty of people working around the slides, the pools and the beach and the lazy river. . Also, this is a very clean water park, usually I am not a fan of water parks because they don't seem very clean to me.  The water was so clean and clear, it was great. This was a fun and relaxing Stay-cation. I left the resort relaxed and in a great mood and ready to attack my Monday. The Arizona Grand Resort was a great experience! 
We all cant wait till next year to do it again.

title: “Great location”
text: Close to pretty much everything. Nice park view. Free Internet and breakfast. Room is not super clean though but the beds are comfy

title: “Warm and welcoming, in the perfect location!”
text:
From the moment we pulled up, until the moment we pulled away from the curb- our stay at The Bryant Park Hotel was perfect. The staff at the hotel went out of their way to remember our names, remember the occassion we were visiting NYC for (a birthday!), and ensure that our stay was a positive experience.
I wish I had written down the names of the staff that were particularly helpful and accommodating to the guests in ourgroup- as they really went above and beyond to make our stay a memorable one. 
Overall, every person we interacted with during our stay was warm, welcoming, helpful and made each of us feel right at home. We even had cupcakes delivered to the room- along with a balloon and a note from the hotel- wishing the birthday girl a happy birthday! Definitely a nice touch!
I look forward to visiting and staying at The Bryant Park Hotel in the future!

title: “Our New Favorite Hotel in NYC”
text:
We stayed at the Trump Soho for 5 nights at the end of May in 1 bedroom suite. Let us start by simply saying Perfect in every way.
We have been traveling to NYC for years and have stayed in a large array (dozens) of 4-5 star properties both large and small. Some we like more than others and we usually leave with a list of items we had wished they did differently. Not the case here, from the quality and size of the room to the service and amenities and finally the neighborhood there is no other NYC hotel we will ever again consider before checking the availability of the Trump Soho!
Also the most comfortable beds we have ever slept in in a hotel.

title: “Nice for Downtown Area”
text:
I visited this hotel for an overnight weekend away with two girlfriends. We visit Houston a few times a year to shop and go out, but typically stay at the JW Marriott on Westheimer. We decided to mix it up and try something different, so we chose the Magnolia Hotel. Upon arriving, we attempted to park in the parking garage mentioned in one of the other reviews. However, it was very narrow, looked a bit scary for two 20 something women to be walking around in at night, and there were also no in and out privileges. So, we circled the block several times due to the streets being one way and finally settled in with the hotel valet. They were very courteous and we got checked in with them with no problems (although I still hate the thought of paying $24.00 a day to park at a hotel). The personnel at the front desk was very friendly and made a point to tell us about the hotel amenities before we were escorted to our room with our bags. 
The hotel decor is very modern, nice, but a bit dark and not really my style. We stayed in Room 1312, which had a great view of the city. Other than police and ambulance sirens going on all night, it was very quiet. The best part of the room without a doubt was the bathroom. The tub is a huge garden tub and gives the feel of a very luxurious hotel. The bedding was o.k. in my opinion, not super luxurious by my standards, and the room was also a bit humid during our stay. We visited the fitness center and the pool area, which I thought was pretty small for the size of the hotel. The pool area was literally only big enough for 1 small family to use at one time. We did not actually utilize the pool during our visit. 
Another perk of the hotel is that they serve a complimentary hot breakfast. The breakfast was delicious, and there was plenty of food and seating when we arrived at about 8:30. This type of breakfast usually costs my friends and I about $20.00 each at other hotels that we usually stay at, so we were thrilled with our $60.00 savings by enjoying the breakfast at this hotel. 
I enjoyed the hotel, but will not likely stay here again unless I have specific business downtown. I don't really enjoy the hustle and bustle of the traffic and people in this area. But, we are thinking of staying again when we go to an Astros game later this summer. It would be the perfect location for something like that, but not really ideal for a quiet girls weekend.

title: “not a good place if youre traveling for business”
text:
if youre coming for business i wouldnt recommend staying here
yes - its nice and a comfortable and modern
but the internet access is TERRIBLE
a good portion of my business is conducted over the internet
first off theres no wireless in any of the rooms
you can connect via hardwire
but you better bring your own cable
if you have more than one computer
and even if you do connect via hardwire
the connection is about the speed of dialup
which means that even sending out one email
you might get timed out
i thought i might get a reprieve
when they said i could connect wireless in the lobby
but even there the router speed is 11mbps
which still only allows me to send out the simplest of emails
and not get any true work or even googling research done
if you dont need to use a computer then this place is fine
but i find it truly ironic
that i have to come to the marriot lobby to use their wireless
to even write this review!

title: “Texas Waffles Are Awesome!!!”
text:
Check in and check out time were very quick, that is a plus.
There is a starbucks right acrosss the street in walking distance and a couple of eating places. My kids love the Texas Waffles at all the La Quinta's. 
I wish we would have had more time to stay and enjoy the pool but maybe next time.
The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was clean, and well kept. 
The location of this hotel was very convenient for my visit, it was about 5 minutes from my families house and there were plenty of restaurants and stores nearby to shop.

title: “OK Other than the train”
text: I stayed at this location for two nights, because I was attending a conference in downtown and the prices downtown were way too high. However, I had to rent a car in order to get back and forth, so didn't save much money after all. I made this reservation by phone to the Comfort Inn national phone number. I wanted a nonsmoking room with a king size bed, and paid a little more and gave my credit card number to hold the room for late arrival. They said I had a guaranteed nonsmoking king room. On the night of my arrival I phoned the hotel directly, from the airport, to confirm that they were holding me a nonsmoking king room, because I was going out to dinner and wouldn't arrive for a few more hours. The night manager said "I can't guarantee you a king size bed." I said "But that's what I reserved". Again she said "I can't guarantee it. But we do have a room for you sir. IS THAT OK? IS THAT OK?" I said no, "a room" wasn't OK, I wanted a king, nonsmoking room, definitely I said good bye, and phoned the 800 number for Comfort Inn and asked for a customer service rep. She phoned the location for me and said "I spoke to [name deleted] and she said they do have your king size nonsmoking room held for you. If you have any problems please call back." I arrived several hours later, the lady at the desk was polite, I got my key, hauled my stuff upstairs (the hotel has no elevator for 2nd floor rooms) and it was in fact a clean and comfortable king size nonsmoking room. I don't think I would have gotten it unless I phoned the national customer service number, because the place was full up and for some reason she was going to give it to somebody else if she felt like it; and one other reviewer mentioned that they didn't get what they had reserved, so I think there is a problem there. I was very pleased with the room. However, since my room faced the back of the motel, it faced the train track that is just 50 feet away. Fortunately I use ear plugs and didn't hear a thing; but if I didn't, I would not have gotten a good night's sleep because of the several trains blowing their horns during the night. The breakfast was good, the breakfast room was clean. Overall I would rate the location high for cleanliness, high for easy freeway access. It worked for me. But I had to call in some muscle to make certain I got what I wanted. The room had a small fridge and I think a microwave. There is a Denny's Restaurant next door to it. The outside photo shows some plants, and gives the impression there is foliage, but this is definitely just a place surrounded by concrete, not at all a "green" location.

title: “Cute Boutique, Perfect Location, Wonderful Staff!”
text: The perfect location, reasonable price for NYC, over-the-top staff! The staff made the expensively, simple, small room worth it!! Very clean room. The thin windows give you the perfect sound of the busiest city in the northeast!!

title: “Hotel was perfect for overnight stay to look at universities”
text: My son and I were in Baltimore to look at universities and needed an inexpensive place to stay for one night before we were off. Althought the hotel was in walking distance of the inner harbor - it was a healthy walk. Ms. Jackson greeted us at the desk and she was most helpful in helping us get transportation and to give us information about the area and schools. Our room was a bit small but we just used it to sleep. Television was hooked up to a satellite so when a storm came through we couldn't watch tv at night. The free wifi didn't work - we could connect but it wouldn't let us open the internet. A little inconvenient but we made do with the business room that they had. For the price it was great and the service of Ms. Jackson made all of the other quirks palatable.

title: “Front Desk and Customer Service is a NIGHTMARE”
text: Trusted that the front desk could take my credit card and make the appropriate charges - I won't make that mistake again. Despite having prepaid for the room on priceline.com, they tried to charge me three different times for the room.
