This billing nightmare persisted even after the front desk "manager" claimed to have fixed the problem. The whole credit card fiasco ruined my stay there. My experience with the front desk staff there was like dealing with the mafia trying to shake me down for money and harrass me. Still shake my head when I think about how awful the front desk staff was, and how poorly trained they are. The hotel property is beautiful in an excellent location with excellent amenities. The national, corporate office really needs to look into training for the front desk. Ironically, the rest of the staff in the house was outstanding. Check, check and re-check your bill before you leave this place. Even though Bostonians can be a bit annoying, these folks are over the top.

title: “Room for improvement”
text:
What a pity that for a visitor from the UK, our room looked out at a brick wall and a fire escape, not a street view.
It was also very small, with one side of the double bed pushed up to the wall, so you had to clamber into it.
However the bed was really comfy, the shower hot on all but one day.
Breakfast "Grab and Go" was weird, I suppose they may be forming an eating area from an empty space that is a work in progress, but I don't like eating in a bedroom, the only alternative to perching on a small padded stool.
It seemed an expensive stay, but we usually holiday in Europe, so maybe my ideas of price are not correct, as we found everything in New York expensive.

title: “Wonderful staff!”
text: I spend 15 to 20 nights in Country inns all over the country and my review is more or less compared to the rest. The staff was really really good here. When I brought the cart back down the clerk asked how the room was. that in itself was surprising but better yet he actually cared. I said a little stuffy and 5 minutes later he showed up with air freshener. It smelled much better! The hotel is clean and comfortable but it is aged. They hurt themselves right off the bat with horrible plastic flowers in the entry way. Better to have nothing! The hotel is smoke free but any nonsmoker will know right away it has not always been that way. The only real issue that would keep me coming back is the breakfast area was WAY too small for this size hotel. There were people standing around because there was not tables. A 3 floor hotel with 6 tables in the breakfast area is a disaster. The food was fine and it was clean though. So I would go back because it was clean but it needs work for sure.

title: “Fantastic Hotel!”
text: I found this hotel at a discounted price on Travelocity. We paid $110 a night - which seems like a lot, but in Hollywood, it really isn't. I had a hard time finding a hotel in Hollywood for under $150 that didn't look scary. The Hollywood Hills Hotel is truly a unique find. We talked to the owner a bit about it - it used to be apartments, which they are converting into hotel rooms as residents leave. They are not allowed to take the apartments away by force, so currently, it is half hotel, half apartments. It feels like you are staying in a bungalow - there is no one above or below you, only people on either side. The room we had seemed to have been an efficiency apartment at one time- it had a small kitchen, one huge room that had a pull-out couch and a king sized bed, and a small bathroom, closet, and a private deck. They have upgraded the appliances and counters, so even though the complex has been standing awhile, the rooms are still very nice. The best part is the breathtaking view. You are literally in the Hollywood Hills, overlooking the city. At night, it's gorgeous. You are within an easy walk of the touristy Hollywood stuff, like the Chinese Theater, Hollywood Walk of Fame, etc. My only complaint is that it was difficult to find. Take note that you actually check in at The Magic Castle hotel, which is visible from the street. Follow the hotel's website directions to get there - mapquest, yahoo maps, and google maps get you to The Hollywood Hills Hotel, but you can't check in there, so it's kind of confusing in that regard. Also note that there is a fee for parking, but that's the case with almost every hotel in Hollywood. Overall, it was worth the price paid - we had a fantastic stay.

title: “Location, location, location...”
text: 'Stayed here while attending a downtown convention. It was great! We were within walking distance of the convention and the entertainment district called Sundance Square. Lunch was available at several downtown eateries. Downtown Fort Worth was a very nice surprise. 'Thinking of going back for a weekend get away. We didn't have a room with a view but we didn't think to ask for one higher.

title: “Good Hotel for the price”
text: This is a good hotel for the price. It is clean, the staff is friendly and breakfast was good. The rooms are clean and well equipped. However, our room was very small and the walls were thin. But, it was still a good value and a great location.

title: “medium review... still positive”
text:
I'm not a casual hotel visitor, I nearly live in hotels for work.
this stay=1wk
 Parking is a huge hassle. chances are if you work outside the normal hours you will be without a parking spot. parking on the street is an option but it's not a nice area and you have to worry about moving the car early before getting a fine. hotel is old bank and the lobby is amazing. Rooms are standard HIE no frills. I'm a platinum at HIE and got zero benefits for being one so if your looking for a honey moon suite... look elsewhere. if you don't have a car I would recommend it for working visit. they have a shuttle to hospital and pier, it stops at 10pm. I wouldn't stay again due to the parking but if that weren't and issue I would have spent the whole month there while working.

title: “Great Place!”
text: My husband and I brought our 16-yr old son to NY for sightseeing, and we wanted the impossible--Manhattan, spacious, economical. Marmara fit the bill! We reserved a one-bedroom suite, but upon arrival, we were told that we'd been upgraded to a two-bedroom suite. Suite? It was an apartment! On the 17th floor, we had floor-to-ceiling windows that overlooked Manhattan to the south and the East river to the east. We had two bedrooms, two bathrooms (one with a whirlpool bathtub), a full kitchen, living room and dining room. Our son loved hanging out on the balcony and watching the street life below. We couldn't have asked for nicer accommodations for the price. The apt's decor was a little tired, but it was spotlessly clean, well equipped, spacious, and in a great location. We were close to the subway at 96th or 86th and Lexington for easy access to everything in the city. We were blocks away from the Museum Mile, a main reason for our visit, and we had our choice of neighborhood restaurants. Nick's, an Italian restaurant across the street, was especially good, as was Sabor a Mexico on 1st Ave between 90 and 91. The staff at the Marmara were kind and helpful and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it or to return to it!

title: “Mostly Great!”
text: The Blakely may be the best deal near Carnegie Hall, and since the area around Carnegie Hall is rather dark after performances, that's important. On 55th Street, it avoids the long dark haul down 57th to other, somewhat more cheaply priced venues. Likewise, the location is primo for the City Centre directly across the street, where the interesting Manhattan Theatre Club shows usually premiere. The new decor is great. Fully functional rooms with kitchenette and Jacuzzi. Nicely maintained. The restaurant downstairs didn't attract me, but the little food stops across the street did, and I got reasonably priced, cheap and good breakfasts over there, rather a comforting balance to the room rates, which while reasonable for midtown Manhattan, still seem a bit like the credit card has picked up a tapeworm! Seriously, I just booked a return trip after spending a couple of hours fruitlessly searching for a less expensive but just-as-good place in the Blakely's neighborhood. As to the noise reported by so many, I never noticed it. But then I go to sleep to opera on an iPod with noise-dampening headphones. Bellissima!

title: “the reviews are correct”
text:
stayed at this hotel the first weekend of june.
lobby nice, staff wonderful, room service great, location is perfect, bathroom was very big - entire hotel room super clean and like everyone has said - has great views. the lobby and hallways outside our room were kind of dark and dramatic - but they were nice. also, it rained while we there and they had umbrellas waiting right by the door for us .. that was great!
only snag was the beds .. i may have missed it in all the reviews i read before leaving but the sofitel is into european beds and bedding. i'm used to sleeping in a king - and was sleeping in a full at the soiftel - by the way, they have twins too. i'm 5'4 and felt the bed a little small .. very odd. also, they don't have a top sheet - only a bottom sheet and a comforter (duvet with feather bed). the sheet and the comforter are wonderful but i kept waking up looking for my top sheet. i'm sure i'd get used to the idea of not having a top sheet but not in just a few days .. i should have just asked for the top sheet and tried to not be european for a weekend.
there's a cheap (i'm pretty sure 24 hour) *cash only* restaurant to the right (as you are leaving the hotel). i think it's a breakfast spot for the locals and we had a mighty great breakfast. we found out about this place in our search across town .. we were over by millenium park and the guy at the hard rock said it was great .. we were like .. geez, we always turn left when we leave the hotel!!! there was a wait, but it went really fast. it was worth it; we couldn't find a good place to eat breakfast that didn't cost a zillion dollars. and this really was good. i love breakfast!
sorry about the messy room in the photo :), the kinda dark photo is of the lobby .. like i said it was kinda of dark .. hard to get a good photo w/my amateur camera.

title: “One of the Best!”
text: We decided to visit our daughter for her college Spring break instead of flying her back home to NY. We booked the Omni for three nights. We were welcomed with warm smiles and cordial, pleasant greetings throughout our stay. Our room did not have a thing out of place and all amenities met our expectations. Our first day was rain from morning to night. We took the China town walking tour, then did our own exploration. The hotel provided umbrellas that day for all guests. The hotel is centrally located for walking to many of the sightseeing highlights. If walking is not to your liking, the public transportation is nearby which I must admit we used at the end of the day. Having traveled throughout Europe, USA, Mexico, Latin America, and Mexico, this was one of our best hotel visits. Our ages, 67, 52, &20.

title: “Great Location and Beautiful Hotel”
text: We were close to everything and the staff at the hotel was very nice and attentive. A cool thing that they do there is complentary hot chocolate or coffee at you door in the morning when you wake up. The parking is expensive so try to use public transportation. It has a nice workout facility but you won't need it after walking all of those hills.

title: “Great new hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed here after a night out downtown. Great location near arena district, short north, and convention center. Within walking distance to many great bars and restaraunts. The staff was very friendly and accomodating. As expected with a new hotel everything was in tip top shape. We stayed in a king room with city view. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom was wonderful. The small things like the high end soap and shampoo go a long way. The large walk-in tile shower with seamless glass was a nice surprise for a Columbus Hotel. We had a few drinks at the bar which was smaller than I expected but still an attractive setting. We did not eat at the hotel but after seeing and smelling the breakfast on our way out I wished we would have. It's a no brainer to stay at the new Hilton over the other similarly priced downtown hotels.

title: “A little training can go a long way!”
text: We just spent the weekend at La Mansion, and I have to say I was very disappointed. There were three couples, and we all stayed in different areas of the hotel. When we met for breakfast,(which took an hour to get at the Watermark) everyone had a problem sleeping due to the noise. Even though the pool closes, there were people out there talking all night. We heard noise on the street side all night as well. There are many wonderful places to stay in San Antonio, but it seems to us that La Mansion is not one of them. I think it has had a grand reputation in years past, but the wait staff at the Watermark is struggling.

title: “Good...If the price is right”
text: We stayed at the Intercontinental over the 4th of July holiday and got a great rate for $139 a night for 3 nights. On the last night, the special was done and we decided to splurge on a suite for $289. We arrived and got upgraded to the suite for the whole 4 nights. This was great news! The room was okay, good size and comfortable, but I think I would have been disappointed if I paid upwards of $300 a night for it. It was great considering the deal, but it was not high end. The A/C is kinda random - it never really got cool in there. I suppose it was comfortable, but it was a bit warm at night. The bathroom is really nice, especially the toiletries, but I was hoping for a much nicer tub. It was standard and not all that comfortable. Oh well. We tried Zest twice for breakfast and it was pretty good. Expensive, but convenient and solid. It worked for us. I have one problem with this though, the last night we had breakfast included with our rate. We spoke to the front desk about it and they said that we had a $43 credit for Zest. The buffet was $35 for two, so with tax we figured that it was right on. We left our room number with the server and left a tip because it is never included in these types of deals. After checkout, they charged us for tax and tip anyway (and it was an 18% tip - for drink refills and clearing plates?!). This is ridiculous. We also had to wait over an hour to get our bags taken to our car and then they lost a piece and we waited in our car for about 20 minutes for that. These mishaps on the last day really made us wonder for next time. Of course, if I can get a suite on Michigan Ave. for $139 again, I would do it. On the plus side, most of the service was great, although they charge $75 for late checkout, which seemed ridiculous to me.

title: “Something different and a great new option”
text:
As frequent NY travellers who normally stay on the East side, 11th Avenue was something new for us. The West side is slowly regenerating and new companies moving in like the big advertising agency just relocated opposite Ink48 will help to accelerate this. However, the area is still a long way from being trendy (11th Avenue is a car showroom strip) and it's poorly served by the subway.
The hotel, however, is a delight and we agree with the previous reviewers. We stayed in a Hudson Suite overlooking the river and it's a great space with a big bathroom. There are some design weaknesses (virtually no drawer space and the myriad of blinds to pull each night and morning are a pain - they should be remote controlled!) but this is being picky as it's all rather lovely with the floor to ceiling windows giving a huge feeling of light and space. 
All the staff are friendly and helpful but a special mention to Stephanie the Front Desk Manager who went the extra mile to please us when we had a problem and Staling the Bellman who was always there to greet us with a smile.
We were on the 'rough draft' rate and it was amazing value for money. However, when the full rate kicks in I think they need to be mindful of the location as it's not the most attractive part of town. If they price it right we will definitely return - no question.

title: “Very Nice Stay....”
text: Stayed for 1 night only in town for a show...good location in South End...friendly, helpful, clean and generally very quiet for this location. Would stay again.

title: “A place to sleep in the big apple!”
text: This hotel is a bit far uptown on 103th/Broadway. There is a subway station in front of the hotel. For breakfast there is a Starbugs in the building. There is no elevator in the hotel but the staff is willing to carry your bags. Our room had a private bathroom which is a must for me. The hotel has a bar where you can buy a beer and relax after a busy day. NY had a lot to offer, so if you just want a place to sleep this hotel is a great value for money.

title: “Revival in name, revival in nature!”
text: Having read the reviews on this hotel I was unsure what to expect. I have stayed in a wide range of US hotels from the cheap to the impressive and from the expensive to the disappointing. What is important in this case is to compare like with like and the Renaissance doesn’t disappoint. The rooms are modern, well kept and clean. They aren’t the biggest but neither is the price. The staff were friendly, helpful and courteous, not what I was lead to believe of New Yorkers at all. The only reason I haven’t given five stars is that we weren’t told the restaurant was closed for renovation, but then, hey, you’re in the middle of Times Square so you won’t go hungry! One tip to protect the wallet is not to take them up on the offer of valet parking. $51 a night can really build up!

title: “Ok - not as bad as some of the reviews make out!”
text:
Before we stayed at the Hotel Pennsylvania - I read a million reviews. Quite a few were bad so we went to the hotel expecting the worst! Well.. I have to admit it really wasn't that bad.
The Room
Our room was on the 10th floor and it was a twin room with two double beds. The room was quite big although abit dark as only lamps no ceiling lights. We had a large TV, radio clock, mini fridge, iron and board. 
The shower was extremely powerful and always hot.
The room was cleaned everyday and we had fresh clean towels and sheets.
The Hotel
The hotel corridors are abit crazy and do remind you are the film the shining..so if you have never watched the shining do not watch it before statying at this hotel!!!! The door to the room again is abit crazy and does look like a big metal prison door but does a door really make a differance to your stay?!!
The lobby was quite big and always very busy. You are able to get a safe, which is free of charge and there is a little coffee shop and some gift shops and internet access.
The Location
The location was amazing! We were right next to Macys and a 5 min stroll to the Empire State building..10mins to Times Sqaure and right across from Penn staion so you can get to most places easily.
The Negatives
I will admit that there are some negatives. The staff were all extremely rude apart from the guys who looked after you luggage on departure! So dont go and expect many please or thank yous!
The hotel has a diner called Lindys - DO NOT under any circumstances eat here. It was revolting. We had a breakfast for $24 which is very expensive for New York and we couldnt eat it, it was horrible. There are so many other eating places which are cheap and edible so please do not go to Lindys! It should be on Gordan Ramsay Kitchen Nightmares!
Summary
Overall are 5 night stay was fine. We didnt come away hating the place. If you want a cheap room, which is basic but clean then I would recommend the hotel. Just remember its a 2 star hotel, so dont come here if you want luxury. I think if you go with the right attitude that this will be somewhere to just rest your head after a long day sightseeing then you will be happy with your stay.
Happy to be contacted if you have any questions..

title: “I'm sad to have to leave a bad review :(”
text:
Out of 7 reviews I have left in the last 10 months, this is my first negative one :( 
Firstly when checking in, (1st October) the reception staff were miserable, no one was smiling, and our lady barely spoke, she almost looked depressed and is clearly in the wrong job :( Not a good first impression. We are from the U.K and had been in Vegas for 5 days, were my boyfriend proposed :) so we were mega cheery and looking forward to the next leg of our trip in New York. We were in room 1632 and when we walked in I could have cried. It was very small, so old, and had a horrible musty smell. The carpet was all crumpled up, which caused a few trips from my fiance and I. The bed was brick hard, and it squeaked and groaned with any movement. The pillows had absolutely no feathers in them and were therefore so flat! The electicity sockets are a law suit waiting to happen. When charging phones or using my hair straightners, they made a 'sizzling' sound, and sockets were hanging out the wall! Jeez! The shower curtain was so grotty and ripped, and one of the towels had blood stains on it?! My goodness!! Our keycard for entry to our room very rarely worked and it took us 10/15 trys to get in! (Using both our cards!) 
Positives? errrrrrrrrrr...... there is always security men in the lobby who don't let you use elevators unless you show your room keycard which is great. The bar attatched (Rum Bar) is lovely, always buzzing and we seen an elderly gentleman playing the piano which was fab. Sofi's italian at the back was very yum! Yeah it is a great location but so are alot of other hotels. This was my first trip to New York and I will look to pay a little extra in the future (although the Edison wasn't even that cheap!)

title: “Great location with spacious rooms”
text:
The hotel is right by Penn Station, making it very easy to get to everything by train. We never even bothered with a taxi. Short walk to the Empire State building too.
Our suite was huge. The bedroom had two queen beds, TV and nice sized bathroom. The living room had a fairly comfortable sofabed, TV, desk, full bathroom and full-sized kitchen. Lots of cupboard and drawer space. We didn't bother to cook but the kitchen was well enough equipped. It would be comfortable for a week-long stay.
Only drawback - no table with chairs for eating meals brought in. .

title: “Beautiful hotel”
text:
I don't know what happened to the poor couple who stayed here around the same time my husband and I did, but we had a great experience. We found all of the front desk and bell staff to be extremely helpful and friendly, looking up concerts that were in town and acquiring sold-out Seahawks tickets for us. 
We did have a separate tub and shower and enjoyed the deep tub and water pressure in the shower. The toiletries are nice lavender-citrus scented, but for sensitive skin I don't recommend using the body lotion - it made my eczema flare up.
The location is awesome - 10 minute walk to Pike Place, upscale shopping all around, plus an Old Navy a block away. 15 minutes down 2nd are great bars and restaurants and the Convention Center is a block away.
Parking is $26 a day and it's valet, but that is to be expected in a nice hotel.

title: “Great location!”
text:
We stayed during a summer trip in July. The location was great! Within walking distance to so many things to see and close to a subway stop. The room was large and nicely decorated. We enjoyed the turn down service and foyer. 
We did encounter a problem during our stay- it was during a heat wave and the ac was not working in our room. My husband called down twice on 2 different days without any service. Finally he went down to the front desk and spoke to the right person. By the time we got back from our show it was fixed.
We did enoy the coffee and breakfast sweets in the morning! I thought the rate was very good considering the location of the hotel and the size of our room.

title: “Absolutely fantastic!!!”
text:
My fiance and I stayed in this hotel for three nights during the september long weekend. We were skeptical at first as we had stayed in another three star hotel previously that year and it had left us with bad impressions.
The hotel from the outside is very old school looking and really doesnt look like a hotel. The lobby is absolutely gorgous, small but very modern. The Elavators are tiny and they take forever.
Check-In: went fairly quickly althouugh are room wasnt ready yet but they stored our luggage so we could go out and start seeing the sights till we got back
Room: The rooms are small but very modern and in a city like New York you dont spend a lot of time in them. The bed was amazingly comfortable, even better than my bed at home, and the linens were so comfortable i wanted to steal them and take them home..but i didnt lol
Room Service: They dont have a restaurant in the hotel but they do room service from a litle restaurant across the street. You call the restaurant and order what you want and they deliver right to your door. Not the best food but still more than edible.
Aside from the rooms and lobby there is not much else to the hotel, i think there may have been a gym but not really sure.
When we go back to New York we will without a doubt be staying at this hotel again!! you get more than you paid for with this one.

title: “Classic New York hotel”
text: The Roosevelt Hotel is a classical old fashioned New York hotel with a fancy lobby and early 20th century design. The service is efficient and nice and the hotel is very clean. The double bad was very comfortable and cushy. No particular views from the rooms (at least the room that I stayed in) but the location is good - just a few steps from Grand Central station.

title: “Everything we needed. Loved it!”
text: My family (myself, husband and 3 children) stayed here on our adventure around California. As we had never been to San Diego before, we weren't sure what to expect but we left loving the area and this hotel. The staff were very friendly upon check in, at the restaurant, in the sports bar and anytime we passed someone around the hotel grounds. Our rooms were spacious and the food at dinner was absolutely delicious (and very reasonably priced too). We could not fault this place and the free parking, clean laundry facilities and complementary coffee were an added bonus. Do not stay anywhere else!

title: “Noisy with poor parking”
text:
I stayed here for two days after Christmas. On the plus side, the staff were extremely nice, and the rooms featured spacious small refrigerators and new microwaves. The hotel also has free wifi. 
On the down side, the hotel itself it a bit rundown. The featured continental breakfast was only coffee, cereal, and pastries (the juice machine was not working and there were no breakfast items that weren't mostly sugar). Inside the rooms, there were no available electrical outlets, and we had to unplug the light fixtures to be able to charge cell phones and computers. The rooms feature large windows that open onto the parking lot and admit a lot of street noise (more than what I would consider usual). The parking lot has very small spaces; when parked you can't open your doors wide enough to take out luggage. My rental was dinged on both sides during my stay here.

title: “Nothing to write home about”
text:
We were for a conference at the Convention Center, so you couldn't have found a more convenient hotel. However, being convenient isn't everything.
We arrived and checked in to a king room with not much more space than for the bed. And, it was quite warm in the room. It was wickedly hot, so we assumed the curtains had been open, so we turned the air down to 60 (it was at 64). Then, the toilet wouldn't stop running. So, we called the front desk to see if someone could fix it (we tried and couldn't). They said they'd send someone right up. An hour later, around 10:30 p.m., we called down and said we were going to bed so perhaps they could fix it in the morning. The next morning, around 10, the front desk called to see if they could send someone up to fix the toilet. Since my husband was in the shower, I offered to call them back at a more convenient time. Which, I did about an hour later.
We left and I returned around 1:00. The toilet was still running and it was still quite warm in the room. So, I called the desk and asked if they were going to have someone fix the toilet - and mentioned that it was quite warm in the room and asked if someone could look at the air conditioning. They said they would be right up. So, I didn't really want to be around while they worked on the toilet, so I decided to wander the hotel and check out the business center. (I had brought work with me but it cost $9.95 for internet access in the room.) So, off I went. The business center was nice, but the computers kicked you off after 20 minutes, so I kept having to log back in. I tried to find a comfy chair where I could curl up with a book and wait, but their chairs are definitely decorative and little else. There were no shops to speak of (one small gift shop and a barber) and very little else to do or see. So, around 2:00, I decided to go back up to the room to grab a quick nap. I walked in on the cleaning person. So, I took off again (the toilet was still running). I wandered the hotel again until 3:00. Again, I headed back up to the room, where I found the room cleaned but the toilet.was still running and the room was hot. Another call to the front desk finally got me an offer to move us to another room as it was going to take the plumbers a while to fix the toilet.
So, I packed our stuff up and moved to another room on the floor. It was a bit larger, and delightfully cool!
We found out later from friends staying in another room that they were told their room was warm because the chiller had gone out. They weren't offered another room, though. (Guess you had to have the combo toilet/air conditioner problems to get an offer!)
It was a quiet hotel. And, convenient to the Convention Center. But, that's about it. The executive lounge was nice, but really nothing special (we were able to access it because we had been inconvenienced). The light rail was right outside the door from the hotel so we could quickly get to other parts of the city (Greek Isles restaurant is quite yummy!).
Parking was very expensive.
There is very little around the hotel that is easy to find. It was so wickedly hot that we had no interest in wandering very far afield. Didn't get much of an impression of Charlotte at all.
Oh - they had a gym - the YMCA is located in the building. But, it cost an extra $12 a day to use it. Go to the Hilton Gardens down the block and use their gym (smaller) for free.

title: “Exquisite decor, excellent location, but small room”
text: This was our first night in San Fran prior to dropping our teenagers with family to go camping. We wanted to stay at a cool, hip place to impress the teens (15/17) and this was it! The location couldn't have been better with union square shopping only a block away & the cable car stops right in front of the hotel. Our only issue was the size of our room, it was 2 comfortable queen beds, but pretty tiny so we couldn't move around well & no place to put our luggage. Luckily it was only one night, there's no way we could have dealt with it for a week. My husband & I are definitely going back when it's just us. Almost forgot....the bell hop was hilarious & danced with the kids right in front of the hotel, very fun!

title: “Convenient - green & clean”
text: I was the guest speaker at a couple of seminars at this hotel in October 2011 so I decided to stay at the property too. My room was clean and comfortable as was the training room. The fitness center was great. The restaurant is less than impressive. The coffee bar was not open and coffee in my room was not replentished on the second day of my stay. The catering staff was excellent and provided everything we needed - even checking with me several times to make sure we were happy.

title: “Grand (Old) Hotel, Helpful Staff - but A/C not good on hot days”
text:
This the second year I have had a meeting (at the Chicago Hilton) during some of the warmest summer days in Chicago. The Hilton is a grand old hotel and just not up to keep things "cold" when the heat index is 105+ -- not a complaint , just a fact.
Given the Grand Old structure -- this place has to be a huge burden on the staff. For example, I had a meeting professionally recorded (Hilton staff) and the engineer agreed to deliver a thumb drive to the front desk in about an hour. Several hours later I went to retrieve it - not there. However, Carsarra, a Guest Service Agent , made call after call on both hotel phones and a cell phone until she tracked down the proper person. The audio engineer and supervisor came -- apologized for causing the delay (and explain a problem with some hotel software) -- the staff worked diligently to help me -- but it is apparent the "systems" available to them are dated (hotel opened in 1927 and was last remodeled in 1984).
Also, the sleeping rooms use an energy saving thermostat -- the room only cools to 73 degrees and the a/c turns off if you leave the room.

title: “Comfortable and convenient”
text: We were in town for a play at the Majestic Theater and we are so glad we booked here. It is a short, pleasant walk to the theater and there are several great restaurants nearby. It is also just a short walk to the riverwalk, the Alamo and Rivercenter mall. Our was so comfortable with great channels on the TV. Free breakfast was great. Best of all, the staff and valets are courteous and helpful. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and highly recommend it!

title: “Loved the Trendy decor”
text: This is an amazing and stylish hotel, really trendy with great staff and the room was very comfortable. The view over the Hudson river was breathtaking. It is so well situated for everything and we had a great stay. The only down point was that when we got home we found that we had a very large amount charged to our credit card after we had left the hotel and setlled the bill which was outrageous so this slightly dampened the euphoria of our stay. We got it all back but it was a bit tedious having to fight our corner to get it back. A bit of a disgrace on the part of the hotel and we know that this happened to the 2 other couples we were with as well so they need to sort this out. However other than keeping a close eye on charges I would thoroughly recommend this stunning hotel.

title: “Decent hotel, but not that great”
text: Hotel is clean an staff is fine. Location is not the most convenient in Chicago. You are better off staying in River North for the price.

title: “Beautiful, unique hotel, great location, friendly and helpful staff”
text: I liked the hotel because it did not look like every other hotel in the world. The furnishings are classic and beautiful and create a refined atmosphere without being stuffy. The location in Fell's Point is ideal--in the middle of some great restaurants, pubs, and shops. The hotel is connected to a pretty French cafe with tasty pastries and good coffee. The staff was genuinely friendly, efficient, and helpful and made me feel comfortable and welcome.

title: “Vanilla hotel only lip syncing "Boutique"”
text: A convenient location for Beverly Hills and the Miracle Mile, but nothing fancy here, except the room rates and the handsome Web site. Coat of brown paint, minimalist lobby and dimly lit halls dress up what is basically a plain vanilla, 1970s-era hotel building. An adequate stay, I guess, but the Orlando's true age and frail bones peek through tired bathroom fixtures, low ceilings and thin walls. Included breakfast holds limited buffet selection or choice of scrambled-but-not-fried eggs and a single pancake (or was it a hot-mitt?) with syrup from a plastic package. (Four stars to the fried chicken and cobbler at Cynthia's restaurant one block up 3rd.)

title: “Great Hotel - Will go back for sure”
text:
We had a great time in San Diego during the Thanksgiving holiday. This hotel was wonderful!!! They had a special Thanksgiving brunch and it was awesome. A little pricey - $35.00 per person, but it was certainly worth it. The beds were very comfortable, the staff were friendly and we had a great time. The shuttle drivers were great. We did not rent a car -- the drivers were able to drop off/pick us up at SeaWorld, Zoo, Old Town, Seaport Village, etc. They would also give you suggestions on where to go. Very friendly and down to earth!!!
This hotel was in a very convenient location. The City Tour on the trolley was also very good. Suggest you go early in the morning so that you can hop off at the various stops and get back on.

title: “My family and I would definitely stay in this hotel again!”
text: Initially the hotel's location concerned us. It's located in a very "commercial" area that has absolutely no character. However, once we were in the hotel, we were extremely pleased. Lobby was very modern and clean. Staff was very pleasant and helpful. Breakfast in the restaurant was excellent. Kids loved the indoor pool. Room was excellent and very clean. A/C unit was a little noisy. After driving around for a few days, we realized that the location was perfect. Lots of restaurants and shopping within minutes. Access to I-25 was only minutes away. Downtown was only 15 minutes away. Overall a great experience!

title: “Convenience and Value”
text:
Selected this hotel based on good reviews, price just under $200 and closeness to the theater district. In addition, Times Square is a fun area, close to restaurants and shopping and convenient to the subway. Although restaurant row is 8th Ave., my son and I found that 9th Ave. has tons of less expensive and just as good dining. The cab trip to the hotel from Laguardia Airport was $27 plus $4 toll plus tip. 
 The hotel itself was very comfortable and the staff very helpful. I was able to use the computer and printer in the business room most times when I wanted or had a short wait. Although it is a large hotel, the elevator was not slow or full. Check in and out was quick. The breakfast room staff was very good and kept the orange juice and coffee etc. flowing. A big plus is that the coffee in the breakfast room is available fresh all day! No need to use the in-room pot. The room also has it's own ironing board and iron and a hair dryer that works. The plus of the rooms is that they provide four comfy pillows per bed and the mattresses are good-not extra firm or too soft. We asked for a two bed room, which I later learned are all in a row on each floor and do not have a view of the street. The window is high anyway so it wasn't important and the location was very quiet. We were on the 6th floor and heard no traffic or neighbors.
 The only negatives we found was that the door to the bathroom was mostly glass and you could see through it! Amazing, huh?! We had brought a garment bag for wedding clothes and there was a hook over the door on the bathroom side that we could hang it and cover the glass. Otherwise no privacy in the bathroom-beware! Also, like most places, they could use an upgrade in toilet paper and tissue. I did like the design with the sink and mirror in the bathroom and not in the sleeping area.
 I would definately stay here again to be able to walk to the theater and dinner. The savings over comparable hotels is probably $50 a day. Great find!

title: “You Can Go Back Again”
text:
It always helps the romantic aura of a hotel to be across from the park where I began my art career: The Rittenhouse Park Open Air Art Exhibit was one of the most memorable events of my life. I always loved Philadelphia for its small town feel while being oneof the largest cities in the country.
The Rittenhouse Hotel, built on the site of the old Notre Dame School, seems to have absorbed some of the energy from the school: it is extremely well managed (perhaps the ghost of the old Head of School oversees the contemporary management), has a bit of old world feel while being very modern and glamorous. The room I was in (a corner, albeit) was a wonderfully laid out and beautifully appointed king size room with a sitting area and a separate desk nook. TV junky that I am, I loved the 2nd TV in the bathroom which had both a tub and separate marble shower. The space between the bathroom and the ample closet was put to good use as a "makeup counter" of marble with a lighted magnifying mirror (also one in the bathroom) and 3-angle wall mirrors. The ice bucket and glasses were here so they did not crowd any of the other surfaces. The bath amenities had not been altered or reduced in number as a result of the economy and the staff seemed far less unctious than at many hotels of this level.
I slept extremely well because the delicious mattress but alswo as a result of good sound-proofing and well-positioned drapes to cut out the daylight. I am rediculously sensitive to light in the morning.
The two occasions/meals that I had to taste the food was very positive despite the circumstances that did not permit me a full course meal to test out. I attended a conference where a wonderful breakfast spread was laid out. Similarly, a tea with family one early evening was very pleasant.
There is a very good health club and spa; good TV selections; nightly turndown and next-day weather report left in the room each night complimentary newspaper of choice; complimentary minor tailoring and travel amenities; the view over the park rejuvenating; the price (even for a conference) was very reasonable. I would recommend this hotel highly!

title: “A RUDE hotel in a GREAT location.”
text: Let me first say that this hotel is in a GREAT location and we would probably stay there again. Now, lets be honest here so you can decide for yourself. Pros: Great location (walking distance to everything!) and truly SMOKE FREE. Oh, and very good free breakfast before 9:30. Cons: 1) The rudest personel I have ever seen. From the front desk to the maids to the little ladies making breakfast. 2) On our last day we found a "critter" (the brown kind) in the bathroom. I killed it and left it for the maid to clean. 3) Bathrooms- water pressure and temperature fluctuate every few seconds. TP was the cheapest I've ever seen. 3) Nobody told us that frige is NOT on so we lost some things that went bad overnight. After we turned it on, it was very cold. 4) Their paking lot is very small so we had to park across the street at a discounted rate of $16 per day. RECAP: The rooms are overpriced for their size. The bathroom is only toilet and shower. Sink and vanity are in the sleeping area. If you can disregard the rude/unhospitable personnell, this New York City Style (crank windows) hotel is in a GREAT LOCATION. If they would just fumigate...

title: “1st new york visit”
text: as per previous reviews i agree this has character. however it is also grubby and rundown. location is excellent and could have been better if our room hadnt had benefit of ongoing air conditioning units and generators running nonstop ouside our window.( i would have upgraded but my partner wasnt bothered). the shower did'nt always run hot which is a shame as it was quite powerful. reception staff varied between total indifference and helpful depending on shift. customer service and concierge v. helpful and happy. due to location i may try again but would probably upgrade. if you want a drink you should try the glass tavern just down road

title: “Great hotel for business or fun...”
text: I've been staying at the Hilton every week for business over the past couple of months. They are in the process of upgrading their rooms (floor by floor), but even the older rooms are nice and quite comfortable. The one drawback is the location (it's on south michigan and a bit far from offices, shopping and restaurants), but the walk is nice and public transportation is very easy and convenient.

title: “Not good, but not bad”
text:
The hotel is in a very odd location, and the hotel does provide free round the clock shuttle service. However, you are on an industrial island so you have to get a cab to go anywhere. This makes going places very difficult.
The rooms are fine, the staff is fine, just nothing to brag about. 
The restaurant was so-so at best. It's a Burger Bistro but was not impressed with the food, and since you are stuck, your choices are very limited. 
For a one night stay, did the job but would consider other options if you can for staying business in Philly.

title: “Excellent Stay in NYC”
text:
Arrived 1 May, stayed for 8 nights.
What a wonderful hotel in a great location.
Small glitch meant we had to spend the 1st night in a low floor Junior corner suite, but were moved up to the 32nd floor the next day.
This is the best location for a holiday in Manhattan, Subway 5 minutes away and a short walk to the empire state building and broadway, only a nice gentle walk from times square, via lots of good craft ale bars.
Very comfortable rooms with a big TV and kitchen, the bed was incredibly comfortable with great pillows as standard so we didn't experiment with the choices available.
If you don't want to travel too far The Barking Dog is great for breakfast and the Cask bar round the block is great for drinks and food in the evening.
The Murray Hill Deli was very convenient.
With the North facing junior skyline the one downside is the early morning noise of traffic and sirens which are quite bad even on the 32nd floor, suspect better windows would fix this.
Even on the 32nd floor we never waited long for an elevator.
Can't wait to stay there again.

title: “Not at all what we expected”
text: I wish we would have taken the time to read over the reviews before booking this hotel because I wouldn't have stayed here. From the moment we stepped off the elevator we couldn't believe it....the carpet looked nasty and worn..the walls had handprints smudged...looked very dirty. Our room wasn't any better. I did not want to take my shoes off...the carpet was nasty. The decor was lacking and the two chairs in the room needed to be recovered..the material was also dirty...and the green leather ottoman looked like something found in the trash..torn and dirty shoeprints all over. The headboard needed cleaning...very gross. The bathroom...the ceiling tiles looked like they could fall any minute and had dust hanging out. The drain did not drain, the tub was water stained, the clean wash rag was not clean (yuck), the granite on the counter top was mismatched, I could go on. I was not pleased at all and would highly recommend booking somewhere else.

title: “Disappointed!”
text: My husband is a Marriott Rewards member, so we used his rewards points to book a room for spring break. We booked online and were given a free upgrade to concierge level. When we checked in, we were told we had to pay $30/day for the upgrade. But each time we went into the lounge, everything was gone! Marriott allowed several volleball teams access to the lounge so it was always picked-clean! We had also requested 2 beds for our family of four, but were told the only room available was a king. I explained to the front desk clerk that we really needed 2 beds, she smiled and reassured me that a king and a rollaway were actually more bedspace (like she was doing me a favor?) We cancelled our reservation for the 2nd night and lost our rewards points. The only bright part of the visit was the breakfast buffet - it was pricey but Donna was so friendly it helped cheer us up a bit. As we were leaving, Lisa expressed concern for our disappointment and asked how she could make things right. Marriott, we feel as though you treated us like trash because we had earned a "free" room. Let me emphasize EARNED! I would expect that you would treat your most frequent visitors with a little more courtesy. Your accomodations and staff are not worthy to be called 4-star!

title: “Not the best value around ! A lot of extra charges !”
text: I stayed here for a week while between apartments. The add online says it costs $119 a week. I ended up paying $270 bucks after all said and done. You have to PAY for your internet here! They don't tell you that till you get here! Then... The internet really sucked bad! I could hardly do my yahoo mail ! You also have to pay extra for room cleaning and maid service. It's bull crap and false advertising ! I will not be back.

title: “Great Location”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for an adult only getaway! This Hotel is within walking distance to everything! Right out our window was The Hard Rock Cafe and The Rain forest Cafe.
Free parking is great and they even allowed us to leave our car until 5 (after check-out)
We will be staying here again soon!

title: “Bigger than a breadbox”
text: Fair experience. We stayed for two days , booked through lastminutetravel.com. Cost around $150 per night. At check in staff wanted an extra $25 per night for the room upgrade to two single beds. Stood my ground , in that was what we had already booked , and we weren't paying any extra. Staff tried there hardest to extract the extra, finally relenting. Room was tiny , and somewhat dated. Nice shower, soft beds. Corridor temperature too hot the higher you went. Lifts were slow, odd system to get to the top floor gymnasium. Great central location, walk straight out onto magnificent mile. Wouldn't stay again. Much better value at Embassy suite hotel north state

title: “Best hotel experience in a long time!”
text: Lots of history in the Magnolia Hotel in Dallas. Those familiar with Mobil Oil Comapny recognize the flying Pegasus landmark. All the charm of an historic building, all the comfort of a first-class hotel.

title: “Perfect when seeing a show, close to the Market.”
text: Excellent price for the location, just blocks away from the the Market. The room had everything you need, and parking was very reasonable with the hotel discount. Very convenient walking next door for the wshow at the theater, and the hotel was quiet. Just wish there was more water pressure in the shower and Internet access in the room.

title: “The worst hotel ever we stayed.”
text: We stayed in last June. Ramada Inn's name on the room phone and other imformation. Unporfessional hotel stuffs. Very old and dirty. We had to wore shoes all the time. The top of TV was melted. The bath room door couldn't shot complitely. No shade on one of lamps. We had 2 rooms and none of light balls were on lamps. We didn't know that till after dark and we came back from dinner. We had to turn on the TV to have a light or open the bath room door. Bathrooms were dirty enough to take a bath. If we were not driven 9 hours the day and didn't have our pet with us, we went to the other hotel. We reported the "choice", but no respond from the hotel.

title: “Good price for a decent, no-frills place”
text:
My son and I were visiting the Peadbody Institute, and this hotel has a special rate for Peabody guests, which was a fantastic rate for the area. It is a close walk from here to the Peabody, which was great.
The room was large and rather plain, but clean and decent. No frills. Having read the many complaints on Trip Advisor about air conditioning, we were suspicious but discovered you simply have to turn the thermostat all the way down, and then it seems to work OK.
The free breakfast is extensive and better than most other hotels.
Location is only a few blocks from a light rail stop, and the walk to the harbor isn't bad if you're accustomed to walking.

title: “Sixth Avenue Sunken Bed :(”
text: If you are looking for a clean hotel in a descent location and NOTHING more then this is your hotel. I never usually complain or give bad revews but this hotel is NOT what they advertise. Our trip started by being told our room had been cancelled because we didn't show up one day early? Oops... I think someone screwed up! They then proceeded to tell us we wouldn't be able to have the room we booked with 2 queen beds but would have to have one with 2 fulls (for the same price LOL). After holding firm and having to waite a few hours we were finally given the room we paid for. Upon entering the room which was very clean but very old we noticed our beds were so bad you could see how sunken they were in the middle before you even layed in them (and this was not because they were pillow top mattresses because they weren't). On top of it, all night we had to listen to the comotion and sirens from the gentleman club accross the street along with the rattling of our in-room air unit. So needless to say if you are looking for a good nights sleep DON'T stay at the Sixth Avenue Inn!!!

title: “Don't Bother”
text: My meeting was a disaster. Internet repeatedly failed. Cell phones don't work well in meeting rooms. Temperature of room was either too hot or too cold. Management was unaccountable. The food made us queasy... The place has become dirtier since my last visit.

title: “Everything you would expect from a 4 star.”
text:
I'll start by saying we booked through Priceline and got an amazing deal. That being said, the hotel is in an amazing area. It's a short walk to the touristy stuff and eating with the locals. It's located across he street from several retail stores incase you forgot something (CVS, Gap , etc.) 
The hotel is beautiful and well maintained. There is valet if u choose. The rooms are moderate in size. Thy provide robes which is nice. 
The only real complaint was hat upon check-in my husband and I were offered 2 glasses of champaign... It was presented as if it was complementary...it was not. I can't remember he exact price but not less than $30. 
All in all...I'd stay here again...Priceline or not.

title: “Charming Host and Hostess!”
text: The hotel itself (motel, really) is pretty average--except that it is run by a very pleasant couple. That tends to elevate it. Would recommend as a no-frills place to stay if you need to be in the Fisherman's Wharf area of San Francisco.

title: “Would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Manhattan”
text: This hotel was fantastic and perfect for someone who is going to do all the tourist things in Manhattan. Its in a fantastic location as it's only a few blocks away from Macy's and other shopping centres, Empire State Building and Penn Station for the subway. I travelled with my friend to which we both were quite green at the whole experience and really did not know what to expect for the price we paid, but we were pleasantly surprised and relieved at the quality & location of the hotel we chose. We stayed over New Years and again, the price we paid we thought it was fantastic as other hotels were quite unaffordable for us. Would recommend this hotel to anyone as it made our trip easy and worry free.

title: “Great Value!”
text: I recently stayed here for an overnight getaway to NYC..it was perfect! Rooms are VERY clean, it is quiet and convenient to everything! Port Authority across the street--buses to connect to NJ, atlantic city, Newark airport, etc...short walk to Penn Station where you can get Crispy Creme donuts, short walk to Restaurant Row, Broadway, Times square..on Saturday and Sundays..Hells Kitchen street fair within walking distance--nice NYC getaway and worth the $127 dollars rate--plus tax approximately $147. That is is great NYC deal! But since its by Port Authority--just be cautious at night and also DVD place at top of the block..I did not feel unsafe though--just always cautious in the city.

title: “Excellent, clean, accommodations”
text:
I recently stayed at this NYC Hampton Inn. The front desk staff were professional and helpful. The room was spotless, and the beds beyond comfortable.
I own a B&B, so I was very impressed. Especially since I have not always had the best experiences in NYC. I would stay here again, anytime.

title: “Can't wait to go back!!”
text: Stayed there to celebrate valentines day. It was great! Everyone at the front desk was nice( Grevais, Heather, Sarah). The room was beautiful. Everything was great. Not one complaint, I am recommending everyone stay here for a nice get away.

title: “Very Nice Marriott”
text: I work at a hotel so I am leaving this review to help you hotel gain from this and maybe it would have gotten a 5 star from me. I arrived at your hotel on November 24 for a one night stay around 11pm and the guy who checked me in, I can't remember his name but he was a younger guy, I hope you find out which one because he needs a big appreciation because he was really nice and helpful and very polite!!! He made my trip the best!! Parking was easy. The hotel's pool and spa now here is where I am giving advice to make it much more 5 star. One day soon I would close the pool and spa for just one or two days and pressure wash the pool and spa walls to get all the dirt and nasty brown stuff off the sides before it sticks there forever, and it will if it isn't treated soon!! The fitness center was amazing and nice and clean. Now to the rooms.....THEY WERE GREAT!!! Very comfortable beds, nice view on the 16 floor. The room across from us was really loud but the hotel did a great job with sending security up their to quiet them down at 11:45. The bathroom had a little mold on the shower curtain. And also I would really try moving to getting better vents in the rooms because the little vents you have show the dirt really badly and isn't attractive and also doesn't get the steam out fast enough so it causes the ceiling to get water bubbles all along the top and will cause the paint to start to peel if that isn't fixed later on down the road. But overall this is a wonderful hotel and if we go back to Charlotte anytime in the future I will not second guess myself and will pick this hotel to stay at thanks to the young man at the Front Desk. So thank you again!!!

title: “Shuttle provides good access to downtown Boston”
text: My two teenaged grandchildren and I stayed at this hotel for our first trip to Boston in August, 2011. We chose this hotel because of reasonable price and free shuttle service to and from the airport and subway stop. The first night we were given a room with damages and in an unusual and inconvenient location. We were given a much better room for the following three nights. The second room was a good location, clean, and with comfortable beds. The layout of the hotel was very confusing. It was time to leave before I was comfortable that I could locate the front lobby by myself. I was very disappointed in the area and did not feel comfortable walking at night. In addition to the above, there was confusion regarding my bill and the "hold" on my credit card. The guest computer in the lobby was not working during our stay. The shuttle service was the greatest asset. We utilized it to and from the airport, and daily to the subway. It was extremely dependable. I would be willing to stay here again because of the reasonable price. I would know what the weak areas are and address them from the beginning so that there would not be problems.

title: “Mediocre...dirty, poor service”
text: As other reviewers have commented, this Hyatt is very disappointing, but perhaps worth staying there if you can get a very cheap rate. I had a weekend rate of $79/night. Hotel room was very dirty although I didn't notice the extent of it at first due to the dimness of the light. When the curtain was open the next day, it was obvious they rarely vacuumed and certainly not along the baseboards or base of the bed. There was plastic rubbish, dust bunnies, etc in plain site. All the furniture was dusty. When I called to politely complain, the manager was helpful and apologetic, and gave me a free amenity, which was nice, but surprising how poor the cleaning was. Also, construction was still going on and they started drilling and banging away at 8 AM. When I called to ask what the heck was going on, I was told, "we always start at 8". What kind of hotel starts major interior construction at 8 AM? Apparently this has been going on for some time (see the other reviews). Also, this hotel does nickle and dime you to death for every little thing. I had a very small package mailed to me there and they tried to charge me $20 for handling it. Also, after I checked out, some mystery charges appeared on my credit card statement, so now I am having to investigatge this.Fitness room, internet ,etc, all by fee. On the bright side, this hotel is located on top of a metro station, but since there are at least six major chain hotels located within 2 blocks of the same metro stop, this isn't a huge advantate. Also, there is no security in this hotel so people can walk straight from the metro stop to the elevators that go to the hotel. Two friends of mine did this and no one thought to ask them what they were doing. Overall, just a poorly managed hotel with little consideration for guests. I wouldn't stay here again given the dozens of hotels nearby.

title: “Great hotel”
text: I have stayed here several times and I am always happy with it. It is clean, spacious and staff is courteous. The rooms are two room suites with fridge and microwave. Rate includes a very nice breakfast too.

title: “LOVED it here - can't wait to go back!”
text: We recently visited The Dana for a trip to San Diego to celebrate our son's graduation. It was fantastic!! We had two seperate rooms and they were both beautiful and clean with comfy beds/pillows and a beautiful view of the water. The staff was great, very friendly and helpful and the price couldn't be beat. We will definately be returning!!!

title: “comfortable room, very friendly staff”
text: Stayed here for business. Hotel is a little dated but the room was clean, bed was comfortable, and the workout facility was also a little small and dated, but sufficent. What is nice about this hotel is the staff. Everyone greets you and the attendant in the Concierge room made you feel like you were staying at home. I will stay here again!

title: “A matures couple from Finland, Europe”
text:
Satisfactory!
My wife and I stayed in Hotel Penn for one whole week on March. The loacation is excellent and everything is near. We managed even visit Washington within a day since Amtrak trains leave a couple of hundred meters from hotel door. The rooms are adequate and they we cleaned often. We didnt notice any kind of bugs or that kind of thing.
The worst part in hotel is overworked reception where is constant 30 meter line in que. Since the safety deposit boxes are behind the same reception and are supposed to be taken care of in (non existing) spare time your mone will be perfectly safe in boxes from thieves and yourself. Unless you come to fetch your things 3 a clock at night. There was not much to be seen from hotel room window. In our case it was dirty tile wall 20 meters from our window.
But the room itself was old fashioned but good and we enjoyed our visit.

title: “Will not stay here again”
text:
My husband had eye surgery at the clinic across the freeway (Twelve Oaks Surgical Center) so I picked this hotel for the convenience and also the price. I did not want to fight traffic after his surgery and I wanted it to be close for his comfort. The lobby was very clean, the breakfast area was fine. Our room was the problem. It did not look like the pictures on the website; the pictures must have been taken of one of the rooms that was recently renovated. 
From the minute I walked in the room, I could smell water damage. After going through Hurricane Rita, I know what water damage smells like. The carpet in front of the A/C was soaking wet. Normally I would have asked for another room, but my husband was in no condition to move--he was very uncomfortable from the surgery. Judging from how strong the smell was, there's no way it was a new leak.
I informed the staff at checkout about the leak, which I'm sure they had to have already known about.
Granted, this might be the only room that had a problem, but I still do not recommend this hotel. We have to return to Houston in January for a followup surgery, and I will pay a few dollars more before I stay here again.

title: “Excellent Stay”
text:
Pros: 1 block up and 1 block over from Penn Station; close to Times Square, restaurants, subway,and 5th Avenue shopping; large room for NYC; comfortable bed; helpful and friendly staff; Keurig coffeemaker in room; nice modern decor in black/grey/white, and red; good sized bathroom with rain shower head.I especially liked the sky blue on the ceiling. We had to ask for extra assistance a few times and it was always done quickly and with a smile. We never felt as if we were a "bother". There was a great mix of guests from older adults to families with young children to backpackers.
Con: I really don't get those weird toddler sized chairs they provide. Much more useful would have been a second chair at the desk so two people could sit and look at maps and brochures. And that is really the only negative I can think of!

title: “we'll see what h we'll see what happen is the night going on”
text: I like to see people happy and smiling there was no happiness and smiling at the front desk but I understand be but I understand because as we talk she had a hard day what the customers but other than that no problems the room is average and it's quiet

title: “Great Character and Location”
text: I did not expect to like this hotel based on other comments on Trip Advisor but I really, really enjoyed it. The service was excellent, the food in the restuarant was great (and Starbucks was in the lobby) and the rooms were clean and comfortable, with SleepNumber beds, which was a great touch. The hotel is a historic hotel so it has a lot of charm and character and during the daylight hours, you can walk to the inner harbor in about 3 minutes. Overall, great hotel and I will stay again.

title: “Don't bring your cat”
text:
Ain't no room to swing a cat here! Barely enough room to swing a mouse!
But, Location, Location, Location.
A short walk to Central Park. Short Walk to Columbus Circuit and the subway, lots of restaurants not far away. 10 Blocks to Times Square (for the hop on hop off start point).
It's probably New Yorkers but 80% of staff were snobby, porters/bellboys more than reception (get over yourselves boys you move bags for a living).
Did I mention the rooms are small? Another reviewer said its like a cruise ship, Im sorry they were smaller than a cruise ship! I could literally rest my head on the wall in front of me while sitting on the toilet and I'm 5ft 4. My partner had to sit sideways.
Best hint I can give you is (put your stuff under the bed, heaps of room but just remember to get it all out.
Look, it was clean, modern, great location, reasonably priced just dont go in expecting you can meet your partner walking around, someone has to back up into the bathroom or get on the bed.
Oh and don't order a spirit (scotch and coke etc) from the bar unless your happy to pay over $10 each.

title: “The noise, noise noise, noise!”
text: Although the Hotel is centrally located to Boston's tourist district (Quincy Market and the Waterfront) and the structure and rooms were attractive and clean, I could not recommend this hotel in a million years! I had already booked the hotel when I read some tripadvisor reviews about the NOISE from the streets that was heard in the rooms but I took a shot and kept the reservation. What a mistake!!! The noise from the streets was ridicuously intrusive. No more so than when the neighboring bars (Several of them surround the hotel) let out at 2:00 a.m.! It sounded as if we were in the middle of a stadium with thousands of people around us. When things finally quited down a bit (around 2:30 -- 3:00 a.m.) and my wife and I thought we might finally get to sleep large trucks (I assumed sanitation vehicles) rolled in and kept us up for another 30 minutes! I would call the stay a nightmare but you actually have to get to sleep to have a night mare! Why couldn't they invest in some soundproofing and new sound reducing windows??? I would be shocked to learn that this hotel ever has a return visitor. If part of your expected experience in a hotel is to get some rest, any rest!...DON"T STAY HERE!

title: “Unbeatable Location”
text:
My wife was attending a one-day conference in the Boston area and my 8 month daughter and myself tagged along. I chose the Marriott due to its large indoor swimming pool and because of its indoor shopping options attached to the hotel just in case of inclement weather. Thankfully this was not the case and I was able to walk to nearby sights with my daughter and enjoy the sunshine. It was a comfortable walk for us to go to the Massachusetts State House and back while stopping at the Boston Public Library, Copley Square, Boston Commons and window shopping on Newbury Street. The next day the three of us walked all the way to the waterfront/aquarium and took the T back. There is a T stop at back bay on the orange line across the street from Neiman Marcus which is attached to the hotel via Copley Place so its only like a 5 minute walk from your room with only the street crossing on Dartmouth Street being outside. From that stop its only like a 45 minute train/shuttle bus ride to Logan Airport. Their is also a Shaw's Supermarket across from the street entrance to the hotel that is open 24 hours and a Starbucks on the second floor next to the hotel's sports bar.
We stayed on the 25th floor and never had a problem at all getting an elevator. The pool and fitness center were on the fifth floor with a large window overlooking the neighborhood and a large sky light. The pool was nice and large but it would have been nice to have steps to make it easier to get in/out with children. The jacuzzi was an extremely nice feature after all the walking we did. We had a harbor view from our room which was an AAA discount room. The windows were in need of a cleaning however. We were provided with a nice pack-n-play for our daughter and there was an ice machine on the floor but no mini-fridge in the room. The bed was extremely comfortable and we found the room to be quiet and the heating/AC unit to be quite functional. The TV was about 40" with around 13 channels in HD and a further 30 or so in SD. There was plenty of closet and drawer space for a king room and a nice sized desk. The mirror in the hallway was nice but it did reflect light onto the bed if the lights from the bathroom were on. The counter space in the bathroom was quite plentiful.
On my next trip to Boston I will definitely consider staying here again. We found this place to be quite reasonable versus other hotels in the area and it offered everything we could ask for including its #1 feature being its location.

title: “Friendly hotel”
text:
This is a pleasant hotel. We stayed in one of the ground floor rooms by the pool. It was very comfortable and even though it was one of the smaller rooms in the hotel, there was plenty of space for the two of us and our luggage. Everything is decorated in nice bright colors. The bathroom could have used some hooks for hanging up wet towels, and more electrical outlets for charging our gadgets would have been nice too. 
The staff were very friendly. We arrived a little early and they made efforts to get our room ready as quick as possible. The complimentary breakfast was okay - bagels, muffins, cake, toast, boiled eggs, orange juice and some really good coffee. It was served in the check-in area and you could either eat outside at the tables by the pool or take it to your room. The free wifi was quite reliable and it also worked fine in the poolside area. 
We chose this place because it's close to the Fort Mason Center (where I was attending an event). There are shops and restaurants close by on Union street, where you can also find bus stops. The location is not terribly convenient for sightseeing, but it was perfect for where I needed to be.

title: “Don't stay here, they tripple charged my visa by accident”
text: I travel for a living and have never had a problem with hotel stay. I was looking forward to this hotel and while I liked the room -- it very small but the view was amazing, the duvet was old and uncovered, there was always an enormous lineup for the elevator, front desk service was unbelievably rude and short and unhelpful - I could put up with all of that except the fact that guest services were incompetant. They chraged my visa 3 times for the room -- and blocked my visa for weeks on end and when I tried to get it resolved, they would assure me it was but then re-charge me again. I have never had this problem before. Be advised with this hotel, they falsely charge you and make it impossible to get a refund. I got a refund only after I got my credit card people on it. Horrible hotel.

title: “Nasty owner, just making money, but cant expect what customers want..”
text:
No good Motel, Not a user friendly people, & showing bad attitude,watching girls in a bad way, room are dirty, it seems not clean, stain on sheets with hair, some rooms are used for short time, breakfast should be inspected by Health department as it smells foul. 
Spa was with dirty water.
there is no way to get here next time to pay $79 bucks.
its built for prostitutions. if u dont take it seriously guys, you will be get bad experience.
so hell dont go to this motel.

title: “Great service, I feel like I'm home.”
text:
I came here in July for an interview with Siemens and the service and friendly smiles here at HI sold me on coming back! 
I returned this week (August) so I could search for apartments and Gloria knew me from the first time I was here. It's a great feeling to be recognized during the stress of changing jobs and moving.
I will "Highly Recomend" that our visitors stay here during their visits to our plants.
Keep the great job!
Mark Vandre

title: “An oldie but a goodie!”
text: I have to tell you I am not a fan of Sheraton hotels in general but this one could change my mind. I stayed at this hotel 20 plus years ago and recently stayed again on business. I realized this when I checked in. The hotel has been re-done inside (don't panic!) It is not dingy or have an old feel to it. The hotel staff was wonderful. They were fast to respond and VERY pleasant and accommodating! I was shocked my room service was delivered by the head chef. The food was delicious and hot. The sleep was VERY relaxing and restful. I highly recommend this hotel and WILL stay here again!

title: “Terrible Stay”
text:
I had booked the hotel through Hotwire and cost me about 50 bucks. I only had to stay there for a few hours because of my flight schedule. 
When I checked in, I told the hotel rep that I was checking out early. 
He told me that I had to pay an early check out fee of 50 bucks. Who ever heard of such a thing??!! To make a long story short, the time I could've used to rest before my flight was wasted on waiting for a manager to complain about the fee. When I finally got to talk to the manager, he said that the hotel rep was wrong to charge the fee. The fee pertained to a cancellation fee. So, that was the mixup. For compensation, the manager offered a free movie. You have got to be kidding me. I was already checking out, and he offers a movie. Nice gesture but ridiculous.

title: “DC is 'definitely cool'”
text:
recently stayed here for trade show at convention center. 5 blocks from Conv Cntr
Lodging: confortable and secure. great size room (about 250sq.ft.) w/coffee pot (coffee, tea, condients), refrigerator, hair dryer, iron
Restaurants: Gordon Biersch adjacent to hotel (access thru hotel). happy hour specials and tv's all around to watch Capitals and other sports. Cuba Libre 2 blocks away, Ruth Chris & Starbucks block away, Spy City across the street, and for the budget conscious, SUBWAY around the corner.
Walking/running path: Hotel offers 3M and 5M map that takes you around all the major sites. Took 3M in the morning
Workout room: basement level - fully loaded and 24 hours - worth putting in 30min a day :) Stay fit!
Cafe: basement level. OMG! You must get the breakfast ticket at the front desk (lobby) for $10 otherwise you'll pay more downstairs. Definitely suggest EVERY ITEM - fresh, delicious, and courteous and 'proudly serve starbucks' TIP: if you don't mind having regualar coffee, buy b-fast and juice for $10 and then go upstairs by lobby and get FREE house coffee - KA-CHING!
AND the hop on, hop off bus is right across the street. I can't wait to come here for wknd getaway!

title: “Disappointed”
text: I booked the room on the reviews from this site and was somewhat disappointed. I stay at a lot Holiday Inn Properties during business travel and wanted to try their attempt of an upscale retro facility. I was certainly not worth the extra $$ for the room. Bed was average. Parking was a hassle. Restaurant was good. I will not use this brand again.

title: “Great hotel by Chinatown”
text: Great service, clean and comfortable rooms, decent gym/pool/spa (spa was too cold to me), and great location. Located within a couple of blocks of the Chinatown Metro station, tons of great restaurants, teh Spy museum, and an easy walk to all the sites on a nice day. The area felt safe at night, also. They also had wi-fi available for free throughout the entire hotel - so nice not having to plug in to access the internet in my room! Very thick, cozy bed. Flatscreen TV, in-room fridge & microwave, and of course a coffee maker.

title: “GREAT DEAL!!!!!”
text:
A great character hotel. It felt very urban yet friendly.
It was clean and quiet. I loved the old wooden doors and staircases and the view from my room was fantastic. I would without a doubt stay there again. So, if you want a cheap hotel, but more importantly, an interesting stay, then it's a great place.

title: “Hooker infested dirty nasty place”
text: I stayed in this place during the week of the forth of July. It is awful. Very dirty rooms floors have not been cleaned in what looks to be years. They are nice people who run the place, they even allow the patrons from the zoo to park in the lot on "free zoo day" they charge them $5.00 to park while they are at the zoo. The only problem with that is that if you are renting a room you have to wait for a place to park. On the night of the 4th. I listened to a hooker yell the same line over and over to different clients all night. During one of her sessions her pimp even busted thru the door to let the guy know that "he did not pay for that". I assume he was in his van in front of the Motel monitoring with a baby monitor. It was a long sleepless night. This would be a great spot for vice squad to work the area.

title: “Relaxing and a Bargain”
text:
We stayed here from January 8 - 11, 2009. We escaped sub-zero temperatures of Minnesota and decided to stay in Phoenix. This is a great place to relax. The rooms are quiet and the pools are refreshing, While it was cool in the mornings, the afternoon sun at the pool was great. Check in was easy. Room was a suite for only $103 per night. We booked directly with the hotel.
Bed was comfortable and room temperature was fine. The biggest drawback is that if you don't have a car, you are captive to the two restaurants on the property. Looking at the prices of food, we only ate one meal over the four days. We ate dinner at the Hole in the Wall restaurant. Meatloaf for $16, and not that good. Nice place to stay and relax; but seek food elsewhere.

title: “Best value in Baghdad by the Bay”
text: As a former resident of San Francisco, I chose the Coventry for what I knew to be a good location (also due to favorable comments on Trip Advisor).
