Some of the best eating in the Marina District is steps away on Chestnut St and public transportation stops literally on the doorstep. What I didn't expect (for the extremely reasonble price) was the quality of room and service. The former was spotless and modern--and everything functioned as it should. The latter was superb--solicitous without being smarmy. On future trips to SF , I will most definitely stay at the Coventry or one of her sister properties. I also look forward to trying out their new place in the Napa Valley

title: “Wonderful”
text: Definitely book Towers rooms if you can - well worth the extra! Room was amazing, service was fantastic and the room service was lovely. We can't wait to go back.

title: “BEST PLACE TO BE IN NYC...”
text:
Stayed in september a five night stay and we had the hotel chosen for us by hotrate rooms as a deal.
And what a deal he locoation was perfect proper new york what i say times square and all main attractions in easy distance but this area where the hotel was named hells kitchen was a proper glimpse into how people live as its not all glitz in new york.
The hotel staff were amazing with there help we saved lota of money and got to see everything get ur self a 3 day bus pass just hop on and off and the night tour of brooklyn bridge was amazing the best.
The room was small massive bed memory faom matress and pillows just what u need after a very very hecti day! It was very quiet to lots of people complaining of street noise from the hotels closer to time squre.
Complementy breakfast was great juice coffee eggs waffels fruit cereal just everthing u can think of the breakfast room was small u may jave to wait but wort it!!! To some it all up we willbe back we made some great friends from the hotel and cant wait to se them again. Ive got loads of info feel free to get intouch to ask more questions x NYC X

title: “Baldwin Hotel San Francisco - Ghetto Paradise”
text:
If you want a place to leave your luggage, this is the place for you. If you need a place to pass out after a party, this is the place for you. If you actually need sleep at night - GO ELSEWHERE! Sorry but every other review must have been written by someone whoes only experience was their parent's home.
Small clean rooms and ABSOLUTELY NOTHING MORE. Expect to hear street musicians until 10 PM, tour buses till 12 PM, garbage trucks at 1:00 AM, recycling trucks at 2:00 AM, drunks screaming until 3 AM followed by delivery trucks and construction at 5 AM. No A/C and no central heat - either try to sleep in a hot/cold room or suffer the above. I will never stay here again.

title: “Loved the Affinia”
text: We booked this great little boutique hotel thru Travel Zoo at a very reasonable price. It was rated at the time the number 2 hotel in Chicago. The Affinia lived up to the ratings. The decor was very modern and simplistic . I have never stayed in a hotel that had real HD TV. The location was great - just one block east of Michigan Avenue in the high rent district. The staff was very helpful and friendly.

title: “Excellent home base in NYC for families”
text: We loved this hotel! Our room was very spacious and quiet. We had room 914, which is right next to the elevators, but we did not hear ANY noise from this at all. The bathrooms are large for NYC and the air conditioning was quiet. The beds were very comfortable! The free coffee, laundry facilities, gym, and pool are all located on the lower level. This hotel is located in residential upper East side, and is within walking distance of many reasonable places to eat. There is a hotel restaurant, but with so many options nearly we didn't use it. Our only complaint is that the hours that you can use the pool are VERY limited, which was disappointing, especially now that the weather is getting quite warm. They really should revisit this, because one of the main reasons we booked this hotel was that they have an indoor pool.

title: “Beware this hotel; it's not what you bargained for”
text: I chose this hotel based on generally favorable reviews in TripAdvisor postings, but I was very disappointed. It has two major flaws: one that the management can fix; the other perhaps beyond management's control. The fixable flaw: the beds are very old (>20 years old), very hard, and mine sagged such that I rolled all night toward one side. This is really unforgivable in what pretends to be a first-rate hotel, given that a Serta pillow-soft bed costs about $600 at Costco. The room rate (with tax) came to >$200, so for 3 nights of revenue the management should be able to buy a new bed that will last 10 years and provide its guests with comfort rather than insomnia. The second flaw is that there was construction going on at the back of the hotel, and loud construction noise (hammering of pilings) awakened me at 7:00 am on the Friday morning (November 4, 2005) of my one-night stay. This appears to be a long-term project, and management did not notify guests about the construction. Washington, D.C. hotels are expensive, and this one appears to be a relatively good buy only if you do not value your sleep. Why pay $200 for a poor night's rest?

title: “Great Hotel, Ideal Location”
text: I chose to stay in this hotel in Washington DC for a long weekend after extensive research on the internet. My husband and I booked a deluxe king room through Hotels.com and got a really good deal. The room was really big, a flat screen tv, robes, desk, internet connection, very clean with a lovely big bed, extremely comfortable. The bathroom again was big with a separate shower and bath, L'Occitane toiletries and fluffy white towels which were changed every day. The staff at the front desk were very helpful. I can't comment on the bistro as we didn't go there but it was always full when we walked by. We also didn't attend the wine reception at 5pm but we were invited to (too much to see and do). Although we didn't utilise the hotel as much as we could have had we been there for longer we couldn't have chosen better - it was in an ideal location, right next to Union Station with shops and restaurants (very reasonably priced breakfast places) and within walking distance of the Capitol, Library of Congress, The National Mall and museums as well as the Hard Rock Cafe and Legal Sea Foods, both of which I would recommend. The hotel is in the business district so it was very quiet at the weekend. I have absolutely no complaints, and would highly recommend The Hotel George. It was very exciting being in Washington just before the inauguration and we look forward to seeing all the places we have visited on the tv! I recommend the trolley tours which you can pick up at various stops around the city but Union Station is the first stop and at $35 each for two days it is very good value. Everyone we met was helpful and friendly. Other reviewers have commented on the homeless people around the station but you find this in a big city and we had no problems at all with them. The Metro system was very easy to use. HAVE FUN!

title: “Really great stay”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights, got a great deal. The hotel is nice and clean. The staff were friendly. The location is amazing. Would definitely go back.

title: “Good place to stay”
text:
Stayed in the Best Western for 6 nights, for business as well as leisure. The bus stops in front of the door and getting to the convention center takes approximately a 30 minute walk or a five minute taxi ride for 7 dollars. 
Rooms are spacious and are nicely decorated. The reception and halls are however a bit outdated. People at the reception are nice. The people from housekeeping were a bit strange though. The hotel has a nice outdoor swimming pool and serves a good and cheap breakfast in their indoor restaurant. There is also an indoor pub/bar. 
I wanted a relatively cheap stay not too far from the convention center. The good breakfast and the swimming pool were a welcome extra. I would stay there again.

title: “the worst experience ever - they treated me like a criminal”
text:
The whole story started in the afternoon. The manger named Walter E. called me with the information that my credit card has been declined. I told him that the credit card which I used for the reservation was not valid any more; however, they swiped my current credit card when I checked in. I told him – and he agreed - that I will bring my new credit card when I go for an evening walk. He gave me time till 11:30 PM to do it. 
Around 5:30 PM I left my room to go the club for the evening snack. When I wanted to come back, my room key card did not work. I went to the front desk and asked Mr. E asking for a new key card. He refused to do it and insisted that I have to give him first my credit card. I explained that I left my room only for a short stay at the club and did not have the credit card on me. Nevertheless, he insisted that I have to give him first the credit card before he can let me into my room. I identified myself as a platinum member with the Priority Club and Intercontinental Ambassador. Again, he wanted to have my credit card before letting me into my room. I asked to speak with his manager; however, he insisted that he is in charge. Finally, he proposed that the security or he himself would escort me into my room for my credit card. I refused to be escorted into the room as a common criminal or a prisoner under hotel security. After at least 45 min very stressful conversation he issued a room key for me, so I was able to return to my room. 
I just could not believe the way I was treated in that hotel, especially as a platinum member of the Priority Club. I felt that the personnel of this hotel treated me as a criminal. I never experienced a similar or equally stressful situation in any hotel, even the cheapest motel. I advice you to avoid this hotel and - especially - the front desk manager named Walter E. I do not plan to make any other reservation with the Priority Club chain (Holiday Inn, Crown Plaza, or Intercontinental). I am now switching completely to the Starwood or Hilton Hotels, which are usually in nicer location, much nicer, and the personnel is much better trained.

title: “Good location, decent condition, questionable value and service”
text:
We stayed 1 night on the 29th floor. Used Starpoints. This was our 3rd stay at this hotel. It's not bad, but we had some service issues this time around -- waited a LONG time for a cell phone charger to be retrieved and brought to the concierge desk. Communication among staff in different departments seemed to be the culprit.
The pool is nice. Fitness center looks very nice as well, although we did not use it. Newer equipment.
The Starbucks-style cafe downstairs was a bright spot. The PCs with free internet are located here (Sheraton Link) and the printer worked. Nice large 23-24" monitors. The bacon/egg/cheese croissant was tasty, and good value at < $5. Nice to have an option for inexpensive breakfast, because the restaurant on the lower level was priced super-high...seriously, $18 for an omelette?!
Our room, 2910, had a nice view of Navy Pier and Lake Michigan. We hoped for a Club Level room since we had to pay extra Starpoints to book our 'upgraded' room but were not successful (we are Starwood Gold but this was a Saturday night in the summer, so not surprising that our request was not granted).
Room was in pretty good condition, pretty clean, decent sized, decent beds. No big complaints, no superlatives either.
Common areas are very nice. Some cool computerized flat-screen game boards for kids (and adults) to use in the lobby. We did not really see any 'kids activities' per se, nor did we seek them out.
Very nice location if being near Navy Pier is important to you.
We wanted to try the 'W' hotel instead, but it was booked in spite of spg.com showing it as available. Sheraton pricing was about the same, but the W seems like a higher-grade property.
This hotel has not disappointed us in any big way, but it hasn't really given us any compelling reason to consider it for our next Chicago visit. We'll likely shop around and try somewhere new.

title: “Shady Housekeeping”
text: Dont accidentally leave anything in your room! My husband left his Armani suit jacket in the closet and called the same day he checked out only to be told....Sorry it's not here.... Then hotel management pretty much called him a liar by saying, you say you left a suit jacket yet there's nothing here..... How about, you'll look into what housekeeper cleaned the room and check their things, have a discussion with them, give them the chance to come clean and make a record of it so it doesn't happen again! Hello!!!!????

title: “poisonval”
text: This hotel is fantastic, everyone is friendly and helpful. The room was spotless and they was always putting in clean towels, sheets etc. Could not fault this hotel. Would deffinatley stay here again. Great location. Cannot find a fault with this hotel. They are having a refurbishment which you didn't notice was going on.

title: “Great hotel and value for money.”
text: After the diabolical experience at Hilton Anaheim, I was really not looking forward to this hotel, however I was pleasantly surprised. Very courteous staff, professional, helpful although walls were very thin. You could hear footsteps very loud from the room above, we advised the front desk and they moved us immediately. They had a note, box of chocs and champagne which was a nice touch for our honeymoon, thanks to all the staff there as it was a nice change from our previous Hilton stay at Anaheim.. all up 10 out of 10, could not mark you guys down for the noisy room at first because you handled the situation promptly and efficiently...thank you!

title: “The Best Hotel in Venice Beach area”
text:
We chose this hotel based mainly on reviews we had read. Our stay was for two nights and, in our view, it did not quite live up to its very high rating. It does have an unbeatable location and Greg, the manager, was very friendly and helpful. The rooms are plain and rather non-descript but adequately clean and comfortable. The room was not made up for us between our first and second nights, which didn't really matter to us, but which one might expect of a hotel rated as this one is. We were on the main floor and noticed that screens on several of the windows were either missing or damaged. If we left our windows open, as we wanted to do both for fresh air and to hear the sound of the waves breaking on the beach, we had a bit of a feeling of uneasiness that there was nothing to secure the louvered blinds or sliding windows from being opened from the outside. That said, there was never an issue. The pastries left for guest use did not seem to get rotated and we found one near the bottom of the pile that was mouldy, probably as it had been there for some time. We also found the walls to be rather thin as we could hear guests in adjoining rooms and the hallway very clearly. We very much liked the patio out front and alongside the hotel. It was a great place to sit and relax, read and people watch. The rooftop deck was a bit of a disappointment. It had only some stark wood benches and it appeared not to have been cleaned in some time. There was an overflowing ashtray, empty beer bottle and other bits of debris that appeared to have been there for a while. With a good cleaning and a few lounge chairs, this would have been another great place to spend some time.
As noted, the hotel is ideally located...right on the beach, at the quiet end of the VB strip and a few mintues walk to several very nice restaurants.
If you are visiting Venice Beach (and it is worth a visit), we have no hesitation in recommending this hotel but you should understand that you will not get the equivalent of one of the big chain hotels...nor will you get the attitude they sometimes give off. The VB is unpretentious and laid back. With just a bit more effort and attention to small details, it could be top rate.

title: “A pleasant surprise”
text:
I was a little skeptical in booking this hotel being unfamiliar with Colorado, fairly picky, and never having stayed in a Residence Inn. This hotel was our 3rd of the week during a business trip and it was a wonderful surprise. The location is extremely convenient being just off of the major highways, and being just outside of downtown Denver in what I believe is called the Highlands. Staff was very nice when we checked in. The rooms are efficiency suites, with a bed, couch, tv, desk, eating area and full kitchen. I found the size of the kitchen and spaciousness of the room to be extremely impressive, not to mention that it was updated and spotless. I have never stayed in a studio efficiency before but this hotel truly made all the difference during a week of hotels and constant traveling. It has a "make yourself at home" type of layout and feel. 
The fitness center has just been updated with new equipment and is bright and cool, providing water and towels. Breakfast is complimentary with plenty of options. Parking is also complimentary and there is security at night, as well as a shuttle that will bring you anywhere within 3 miles. 
We asked the employee at the front desk of a near by dinner suggestion, and rather than going downtown she suggested we walk 3 blocks up to Pasquini's which was absolutely wonderful after a long day in meetings and driving for hours. We will definitely consider this hotel again when needing to be in the Denver metro area.

title: “average at best”
text:
My wife and I travel to DC on business frequently and this hotel is very convenient to Capital Hill and the House/Senate offices. The Hotel itself is at best, average in most ways. The rooms are nothing to get excited about, although it was relatively clean throughout. One distinct negative was very frequent interuptions by the housekeeping staff. They knocked once at 8:30pm, "just to make sure everything was OK." Another time they knocked at 7am with a razor that someone else ordered.
Noisewise, although we were at the back of the building on the 7th floor the street noise/sirens were very loud, double pane windows as found in other hotels would have helped this issue.
High speed internet was free and reliable which was a plus.
A three star hotel.

title: “Ehh - it's okay I guess...”
text: After we missed our connection and the airline offered to put us up at the Hilton I was like - great that is the chain I actually prefer to stay at when I travel anyway. This Hilton did the job but not much more. The people and service were fine, the restaurant was fine - and the waitress especially nice. The rooms and the property were kind of dated. It had more of a mid-tier Hampton Inn feel than a Hilton that I would expect. Again, served the purpose and would stay here again I guess = but only as a result of another missed flight.

title: “Great stay”
text: My first time to Charlotte, visited on business. Wanted to stay close to downtown but not in downtown. Chose the Hilton University Place because the photos looked nice and it was close to the freeway. Checked in and was given a beautiful room on the Executive Level. Very comfortable king size bed, nice view (leaves were just starting to turn color), large, clean room. Check in was efficient, staff throughout hotel were very helpful. One of the nights, there was a domestic disturbance in the room next to me --very loud yelling at 11pm -- I called downstairs to report it, and a security person came up immediately and difused the situation in a very professional manner. Other than that, quiet and the executive lounge was great!

title: “Great Place to Stay for a Ballgame!”
text:
Staff were friendly. Upon arrival, they upgraded us to a mini suite with an adjoining room as this was the only thing available where we could have adjoining rooms since we were traveling with family. The rooms were nicely appointed, clean, and well stocked. We loved the turn down service which came with cookies, milk and a bottle water. They have morning beverage service and a newspaper; which we didn't take advantage of as we forgot to put our request on our door the night before. These are a few of the perks of being an Omni member! :)
However, with that being said we did have a few issues with the hotel. First, the television set in the master bedroom, had a control cover panel that was broken and coming off. The couch in the living room area, had a very large tear in the front cushion. Also, the sink basin in the master bathroom had several cracks. Then there was the stripping on the outside of the hotel that was loose and dangling down in front of the bedroom window. There was wind during the night which caused it to bang against the window. We didn't get a very good night sleep because of it. 
We had an issue with the room service. We had place a breakfast order and after waiting for over an hour, we had called down to find out where our order was and learned that it had been delivered to a different room. They did offer not to charge us for the order and delivered it within 5-10 minutes. The food was hot and delicious; but there was no salt and pepper on the tray... we needed this for our eggs and hashbrowns.
Even with this issues, we will definitely stay here again as staff were quick to remedy the room service problem and the other items were just minor things in the overall picture.The room, overall cleanliness, and other amenities exceeded our expectations.

title: “Close to Airport!”
text: I stayed here the night before flying out to Hawaii. The rooms were comfortable, but not fancy. Very close to the airport and they offer a shuttle service. Additionally, if you desire, they offer a park and fly option that is available when you make reservations direct with them. All employees were friendly and professional. I would stay here again if for no other reason then the ease of accessing the airport.

title: “Great location for a good price”
text: We wanted to stay in manhattan during our visit but didn't want to spend too much money on hotel so after checking around I came accross amsterdam court and decided to book here. The hotel was very good for the price we paid. It was quite a tiny room but we weren't planning on spending our time in the room! It has all the basic amenities you need, the heat wasn't the best as we travelled in early March when winter was now finishing (also we're from the Caribbean, where its alwasy warm) so we felt a bit cold at times. The restaurant downstairs had some good food, we only ate there once as we wanted to try lots of restaurants and "street food". Also the check in was quick and the staff were really friendly, they helped us with all our questions we had about moving around in NY. Overall I think this is a great hotel if you're just looking for a place to rest your stuff and take a little sleep.

title: “Good Location, Comfortable Beds”
text: The Embassy Suites at the San Antonio Airport is in a great location. It is just a couple of minutes from the airport (our room looked out over the airport and the highway). The room was not noisy from anything outside. The first two nights we had problems with a plugged sink and a noisy fan in the a/c-heating unit. They finally fixed them on the third day. I had asked for foam pillows and was assured I had them in our suite but when we got up there they were feather pillows. They did replace them very quickly when I asked. The cooked-to-order breakfast was very good. The spread during the week wasn't as large as it was on Saturday morning. The Manager's Cocktail hour was a joke as far as appetizers went. Drinks were limited; but what they did prepare were good. The maid service was good as far as keeping the room very clean. However, it seemed she forgot something almost every day. One day it was towels, another it was toilet paper and tissues. But those were minor things. The rooms were very clean and the bed was made up with fresh sheets when we requested them. There were two computers and a printer for guests to use in the business center and a small snack shop if you wanted to purchase anything there. They had a very nice indoor pool. The front desk staff for the most part were friendly and willing to help with anything. But best of all was its location. Two minutes to the airport, 5 minutes from North Star Mall and another mall, restaurants close by and easy access to Hwy 281 and Loop 410.

title: “Good hotel, location not so great”
text:
As many before have said this hotel is in the tenderloin district, and just down the road from a church that offers meals to the homeless in the area. We took the BART train from the airport to the civic centre station (only $8.25 each, so good value and quick), and walking up Hyde with suitcases in tow felt a little unsure about the area, however over the course of the next few days walked out around the surrounding streets frequently, and encountered no problems. The hotel does offer frequent shuttle buses to Union square and Fisherman's Wharf, but if they times don't work for you, then just walk up one street to O'Farrell and you will avoid the less desirable areas and church.
The hotel itself is very good - room nice and spacious, bathroom good, beds comfy enough, the breakfast is adequate, staff very helpful. Don't be put off the hotel because of the reviews on the area - it's a good hotel, and you can easily avoid the areas that seem less desirable.

title: “Great Location, but watch the construction next door”
text:
My friends and I booked 2 rooms thru Priceline and got a great rate for a 4-star hotel in Manhattan. We arrived about 1:00 pm on a Thursday, and gave the car to the valet. Valet parking (there is no on-site parking garage) is $40 per day. We were immediately checked-in to our 2 rooms. They gave us 2 rooms on the 12th floor, but both faced a building under construction next door. Biggest problem with this was not having a view, but there was also a little bit of noise Friday morning that woke us up. There was no construction going on over the weekend.
The room was nice in all aspects except for the small tube TV in the armoire. You would think a hotel this nice would have upgraded to a flat-screen TV by now! But we only watched the TV for weather updates and news at night. I also didn't like the "limpy" pillows that I had on my king bed.
Location is great - 1 block from a few subway stations, and 2 blocks from Rockefeller Plaza.
There was a street fair going on the Sunday morning we checked out, so it took over 45 mins to get our car out of the Valet. But all employees, from the valet to the front desk personnel were very nice and courteous.
As others have said, sign up for the free hotel club (I did it on-line), make sure your reservation has the club #, and you get some nice "freebies", such as free wi-fi ($10/day value) and free beverage service in your room each morning.
My problems were minor, and I did not contact the front desk/housekeeping/manager about them. I am sure they would have been taken care of if I did.
We ended up spending a lot of time in Times Square, so next time we will probably spend the extra $20 or $30 per night to get a hotel there.

title: “Remodeled and Refined”
text: We were a group of 4 friends traveling to San Francisco. My friend was sent an email on a deal for this hotel. We were very lucky since hotels were filling up fast due to the pro golf tour. We were surprised that we were given 2 tickets daily with our special for transportation; the wax museum or a boat tour. It was a nice perk. The rooms were very nice and very comfortable. We had two adjoining rooms. Ice was a little hard to find..It was a bit of an adventure! Ha! The coffee in the morning is great. The wine at 5 is a nice treat. The staff was extremely polite, sophisticated and helpful. I really wish that we had booked a wine tour through their concierge instead of on our own. I heard that that people who did were very pleased with it. I enjoy a pool or hot tub and they did not have one. Also, this was actually 3-4 blocks from the wharf. Those were the slight drawbacks. Great overall!

title: “Not the worst hotel I've stayed in, but not a safe area”
text:
If you're used to the Sheraton or Hilton, best to pass this one by. I booked this hotel through Travelocity's Top Secret Hotels (they did a little bait and switch on me--showed this property as having a higher guest rating before I bid than it actually had). So the price was right. But I wouldn't spend more than $80/night to stay here, even with San Fran's high rates. 
My spouse and I stayed here for a few days to celebrate our 5th anniversary. I thought we were getting a queen-size bed, but it was closer to full size. The room was one of the smallest on the floor (room 503). It was pretty antiquated, with no AC, which you can expect from this type of SF "boutique" hotel. There was a small fridge and free internet access. The elevator was working when we visited but it's definitely from a bygone age--this can be a positive or negative depending on your tastes. The continental breakfast was basic. The bathroom was fine, updated and clean. Front desk was friendly enough on the weekend. Maid service was OK but on our 2nd night I saw a cockroach scuttle across our fridge.
Parking is $20/night if you cut a deal with the nearby parking garage. Best to avoid the hotel's valet service--we chatted with another hotel patron who'd had her car dented by the employee parking it.
My biggest complaint would be that this hotel is located closer to the Tenderloin district than Nob Hill. The Tenderloin is not a particularly safe part of town, as pointed out to me by one of the area's denizens as I took my wallet out at a bus stop to get out a couple bucks for the MUNI. My husband was with me at the time, and this local citizen warned me that I'd better keep my wallet and purse out of sight because "this is crackhouse row" and "things happen down here." Needless to say, I took his advice.
I wouldn't stay here again.

title: “Ouch!”
text: My wife had stayed here before so we elected to stay here on layover while in transit from Paris to Minnesota. We booked the hotel on Hilton Honors points so cost was not a factor. Our room ( slight bay view on 7th floor) was nice bu nothing special. My daughter told mevthe pool was quite good. However: room service was slow, and the food was a disgrace. Parking prices ($38 per night) are insane even for Boson. Finally, in world where free wifi is rapidly becoming expected by clients, at this hotel Internet is available for a fee. I have stayed at numerous Hiltons and sadly report that this is one of my least favorites. The only outstanding aspect of this hotel is it's proximity to Logan.

title: “Great value!”
text: My husband and I took our daughter to Sea World last weekend and stayed at this hotel. Contrary to many of the reviews, we actually had a large, non-smoking room on the 3rd floor. Room 311 if you'd like to request it. The hotel was clean, the staff was very nice, and the parking was free and accessible. The free breakfast was also really good... they had cereal, eggs, muffins, oatmeal, yogurt, bagels, and toast. Totally enough to fill us up before heading to Sea World. The location is great because it's so close to the park. You won't get an amazing view or anything, but for the price... it's a great value.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
We attended the 2011 Solar Decathlon, September 28-October 2, 2011 and stayed at this property. It is above the Metro station by the same name. 
When you get off the Metro be sure to look for signs to the hotel or the promenade.
It is walking distance to many of the DC tourist sites and government venues. It is also walking distance to the Washington SW Waterfront restaurants, fish markets, marinas, excursion boats, etc.
Good deals on breakfast buffet with room. Great breakfast buffet.
Wifi did not work very well. It costs $$ extra. Not even free in lobby.

title: “Worst hotel ever stayed out”
text:
I have nothing positive to say about this hotel. We checked in June 18, 2003. At the desk we requested a room with a double bed. My husband and i were traveling with our 22 month old daughter. WE were given a room in the Regency tower. The room was fine, However, we were in the next the to back parking lot of the San Diego union tribune newspaper. The newspaper is a 24/7 operation. We heard trucks backing up all night beeping.
When we asked to move the staff was awlful fought with my husband and told him we were exagerating about the noise. Finnally we were moved. 
The second room was great. After arguing with my husband the hotel took $20.00 off the bill and gave us a free breakfast. The food was gross. 
and the restuarant had a funny smell of cheap cleaning supplies. When we went to check out, the computers were down and the resort did not fax my husband a bill until three days later.

title: “A MonteCarlo Jackpot in the Monaco Hotel”
text: the Monaco is our ONLY hotel in San Francisco. The concierge staff is amazing and helpful. The front desk is excellent. Our room attendant the her staff were the best ever. Not to mention the gorgeous decor of the place- from the street to the room to the tiny and wonderful extras that were everywhere you looked. We refer everyone to it, and will never book a flight to the bay without booking a room! Thank You Monaco Hotel!

title: “So beautiful, peaceful,wonderful fresh air in rooms.”
text: This hotel has been transformed. The aesthetics,linens,layouts give a luxurious feel. We even had a view which was a first for us in NYC. Staff were helpful for sightseeing tips and directions. The location is great.

title: “Broom closet for a room”
text: Small room, tiny bathroom - no shelf to put toothbrush on etc. No coffee making facility. No assistance with luggage.

title: “Very helpful staff”
text: We've stayed at this La Quinta twice over the past year for a total of 9 days while visiting friends and family. We've not experienced any problems and will definitely stay here again. The staff is a definite asset. On our last visit we failed to check the closet in our room and left behind several pieces of clothing. The very helpful staff rescued our clothes and mailed them back to us the next day.

title: “Great little hotel in an awesome location”
text:
The Allen Lee's location, within walking distance to all the main Washington sights and the Metro, is unbeatable. 
My single room was small but very comfortable. The room had cable TV, plus a small sink. The shared bathroom was spacious and clean, and the breakfast (along with free newspapers) was fantastic.
Given some of the negative posts (many of which seem to be quite out of date), I had my doubts, but the Allen Lee far exceeded my expectations and I can't recommend it highly enough to those looking for central, comfortable, value for money accomodation in DC.

title: “Loved this Hotel”
text: Excellent Embassy Suites. This one is a little different in that it does not have the typical atrium - love the atriums in the others but not the noise that you find in the other Embassy Suite locations. Outstanding staff who provided personable attention. Each staff member from front desk, to maid, to valet went out of his or her way to provide personalized service. Great rooms - comfortable yet with a modern touch. Free internet access was an added bonus. $28 to valet park but understandable given the downtown location. Breakfast could not be beat and the breakfast guy truly went out of his way to get each guests morning off to a right start with the great food he prepared and his friendly energetic demeanor. This will be my first choice in hotels when in downtown Houston.

title: “Convenient and Comfortable”
text: On The Ave is in a convenient location on the UWS, close to the Beacon Theater and lots of restaurants and markets. Easy walk to Central Park and to Riverside Park on the Hudson. Also a nice walk down Broadway to Lincoln Center, Times Square, etc. Close to subway. Staff was very friendly and room was clean and comfortable--small but had everything we needed, including a mini-bar. Comfortable bed. Free wifi in the lobby but we had to pay for it in the room. I would stay here again.

title: “The most enjoyable stay ever!”
text:
This is an excellent place to stay. It was very beautiful and has wonderful staff. The sleep quality was beyond expectation, so quite and peaceful.
Thank you Adolphus and staff

title: “Great value, great location, great history”
text: Love everything about this hotel! The location is perfect and the hotel has amazing historic energy!!! The Crockett Hotel and Menger Hotel are owned by the same people. The rooms are larger at the Crockett. I read several reviews that said the Crockett was noisy, but our room was right above the bar and lobby and was much more quiet than some 5-star hotels that we've stayed at. I can't imagine paying $100 a night for a room, located within walking distance of the Riverwalk, with the cleanliness and atmosphere of the Crockett and writing a bad review. We had planned to stay at a bed and breakfast, but there was not availability...but we are so happy we stumbled upon the Crockett. My boyfriend and I honestly loved everything about this place and will most definitely stay here during all future stays in San Antonio!

title: “A good hotel for regular folks”
text:
I should start by saying that I am a SF local, my dad was married by Cecil Williams of Glide (the church next door to The Mark Twain), so I am used to the less than stellar qualities of The City, such as panhandlers, sirens and triple parked cars. 
The mark Twain was nice. It had courteous staff and the room was simple but adequate. The base board was a little tattered in one corner and the paint in the bathroom was old. 
We used the hotel just as a base while we did the tourist thing, so the location is perfect for all that and at an affordable rate. I was also glad to not find ANY bedbug reports on the internet.
If you are looking for a ritzy 5 star stay go elsewhere but for simple and affordable with all the stuff you need The Mark Twain is perfect.

title: “Glad to leave”
text:
I stayed here with my husband and two teenagers for one night. Glad we weren't booked in for any more. The rooms have an outside corridor and coming up from the carpark up the stairs was a bit unnerviing. I half expected to be leapt upon by a drug dealer and a mugger. It reminded me old Council flats in London (are the called tenement blocks in US?). There were buckets of sand with dogends on the outside corridor. Not very pleasant.
The suite was divided in two by a sliding door - bunk beds in one half. You had to go through this room to the bathroom.
Space is very tight, lighting is awful. I really wouldn't want to spend any more time in this room than I had to. A/C was nosy and right next to the bed - everything is right next to the bed because there is no room to move around. Hotel is noisy on a busy road. 
Breakfast room was like a school canteen. 
I would not stay here again.

title: “Hotel Rouge is just a Quality Inn with a red elevator.”
text:
The rooms are poorly designed, there is no restaurant, the bar closes at 10:30pm as does room service, the neighborhood is sketchy and it’s a 15 minute walk to anything. Oh,and my iPod was STOLEN!
Be warned, the website is very misleading. On the web this looks like a luxury boutique hotel, it is not. We had the misfortune of renting two rooms at this hotel, one for my wife and I, and the other for my mother. So I can attest to the fact that it wasn’t just my room that was unenjoyable. 
We stayed in an “Executive king room” which boasts 450 sq foot rooms, but that must include the odd 100 sq foot hallway and another 80 sq foot area that looks like it should have had a table and chairs, but was just unused. So it is more accurate to describe the “executive king room” at around 300 sq feet. The walls were very thin, so we could hear children crying and dogs barking on different floors as well as the elevators moving all night, even though we were three rooms removed from them. I feel sorry for the people who were closer.
My mother’s room smelled of dog urine. Yes, this is an “animal friendly” hotel. The hotel’s remedy was to spray some foul smelling air freshener in her room. It also took them 2 days to replace a light bulb in her 100 sq foot hallway.
The staff, while friendly, is terribly shorthanded an inexperienced. During our three nights stay there never seemed to be more than 4 people working in the hotel; the front desk clerk, the valet, the bartender and a maintenance man. The Hotel Rouge appears to have been either a Quality Inn or some sort of efficiency condo building in it’s past life as the rooms are misconfigured for proper hotel use. 
In the evening after checking out, I remembered that I left my blue 16GB iPod Nano on top of the safe. I called the hotel to retrieve the item. After much waiting on hold I was told to call back when the head of housekeeping was in (apparently there is no protocol for items left by guests). Needless to say, the iPod didn’t turn up. I had to ask if guests where now staying in room 1010, there were. Well, could you please ask them if they found my iPod? I didn’t get a call back so I called again the next day. So either A) my iPod was stolen by housekeeping or B) housekeeping didn’t do a very good job turning down the room and the next guest who stayed in room 1010 stole my iPod. In any event this should give you a pretty good idea of what the Hotel Rouge is like. 
This is the first time I’ve ever had property stolen in a hotel. I'm very surprised that Kimpton Hotels would want to be associated with this place.
Bottom line: if you usually stay at a motel or at a Days Inn and you don't travel with any valuables, you may enjoy staying here, you might even think it's a nice hotel. But if you're accustomed to staying at better hotels, then go elsewhere. 
The only reason I gave it a "poor" rating instead of a "terrible" is that the staff was friendly and the bar looked nice (when it was actually open, which was rarely).

title: “Couldn't ask for a better stay”
text: The Chancellor is a smaller hotel that is perfectly located for any visitor to San Francisco. The Powell Street cable car runs directly in front and it is 2 to 3 blocks away from great shops and theaters. As has been previously mentioned, there is no air conditioning but none was needed during my stay. The staff was excellent (including Susan in the tour office) and the restaurant offered great meals. I will definitely be back and highly recommend this property!

title: “Very comfortable get away right near the airport”
text: Great place to stop if you have an overnight before flying in or out of Seatac. It's a little gem in the heart of suburban activity. 5 minute drive from the airport but feels like a world away. The grounds are very pleasant the and various water features help drown out the plane noise. The rooms are plesant and comfortable, nothing extravagant. The food was delicious at the onsite restaurant.

title: “In a class all it's own.”
text: First, this is not a hotel, it's a beautiful lodge. Very close to Seattle airport (but you can't tell). The main lodge has a restaurant and separate lounge. The food was very good. This location is peaceful. The room was very clean and comfortable. The little lounge area next to the rooms had complimentary snacks and water (a very nice touch). The only thing I would change is the size of the bed in our room. I'm 6'2, a little to big for the bed. All in all this is a wonderful place to rest and relax. Would stay again and recommend to everyone.

title: “They rolled out the welcome matt.”
text:
Although we live in NY, we felt a little stay-cation for the three day week-end would be better than the cost and travel time for a caribbean retreat. And it was.
The requirements were five-star, in a desirable location, quiet inside, and pet friendly.
We booked the king studio and got an upgrade. Parking was easy (no meters), and cabs were easy to come by for trips after we parked the car. Every single staff member was helpful and friendly. And, everyone was over the top happy with our little terrier. Each and every staff member seemed naturally pleasant. Nothing put on. True winning personalities with the door men, reception and check-in staff, and the bar crew (especially Nathalie - the manager) were what we wanted. Genuine, cool, easy-going, yet interested in providing top-notch service. I felt that every dollar was well-spent here.
The bar is a place that I wouldn't leave if I didn't have to do so. The drinks were inventive, and tasty. I do not know of too many spots that have Nicaraguan rum. The views from the bar are better than going to the top of the Empire State Building. Get out of the line, get up the elevator to this sky top bar, and have a drink while you soak in the views of river to river, as well as Empire Bldg lit up and the quickly rising Freedom Tower.
The room - cool products that you will enjoy using, glass bathroom with privacy shade, heated floors, rain shower, eco-friendly aspects, bottle of water waiting (great after a day of shopping in SOHO!), robes, slippers, natural fabric linens on the bed, reading lamps that don't keep your mate awake, ample closet space, and ample living space in the king studio.
The David Burke Restaurant is set to open Feb. 1st of 2011 (as they told me), and I would like to try that out!
Although it isn't in the middle of the stores in SOHO, I think that it is nice to have the space and the views that this building affords. There are even "zen" gardens - SPACE! Hard to get in a NYC hotel.
This apparently opened in October of 2010, and I didn't see service of construction flaws - this is a good sign for such a brand new place!
I look forward to seeing the great people in this hotel, and experiencing the warm welcome again.

title: “You get what you pay for!”
text: Not a bad stay at this hotel. Very good location and reasonably well maintained. Only gripe was the numerous stains on the bed linen, think one of them was a blood stain. Overall tho reasonable value considering the location. Staff were also ok.

title: “Great position for sightseeing in Boston”
text: We visited Boston for the first time and were lucky enough to pick the Omni Parker. Boston is an unusual city for the US in that you can, if you choose, walk to the majority of the interesting sites and the Omni Parker is in a very central giving you every opportunity to do just that. Indeed, We walked everywhere apart from our trip to watch the Red Sox when we caught the sub-way which itself is just two minutes’ walk to the nearest station. The rooms were a little small, as was the on-suite but both were well appointed and quite comfortable. On the other hand the concierge was excellent and nothing was too much trouble. The only down side we really encountered was on our last night we wanted to sit in the bar but it was shut! This was most disappointing as we really enjoyed the place on the other evenings during our stay.

title: “Bad Experience”
text: I booked a room through their toll free number. I had a couple a couple of questions for which the booking agent gave me positive answers. After the booking was made I thought I should confirm it with the hotel management and they gave me totally opposite answers which really annoyed me. Nevertheless I did not cancel the reservation. When I reached the hotel the day I was supposed to check-in they said the room I booked was not available and gave me a really bad room in its place, even though I had given my credit card info for holding the desired room. The management did not seem very friendly and were unresponsive. On top of that they charged me incorrectly for the stay and I've been trying to contact their billing department for the past 3 days to sort out the problem but get no response.

title: “Accepting charges for free items?”
text:
Check in was friendly and quick. Our package included breakfast and 4pm late check out. As SPG Gold members we also got free internet. This was strange: We were told to select a wifi option from their access page, accepting the charges and then dispute them at check out. While this worked very well, disputing charges at check out should not really be part of a well designed process. We were also offered a “green” option: No housekeeping during our stay in exchange for a few SPG points. Strange idea for a hotel of this class, we declined. A much better “green” idea: It would be more ecological, economical and pleasant if fresh air came thru the windows instead of thru the air conditioner. Windows are still locked. 
We had reserved a deluxe room and were assigned #724. Not sure if this was really a deluxe room. I don’t think that it was 340sqft (as promised in the confirmation mail). Also, there was no ottoman (as stated on hotel website) and no bathrobe either (stated on German language hotel website). Oh wait a minute: On the day of departure, when we were packing our bags at 1pm, two hotel employees wanted to bring us bathrobes. Ehm, no, thanks. Otherwise, the room overlooking Montgomery and the skyline was elegant and very pleasant, everything in good working condition. We didn’t fall for the booby trap, the 7$ water bottle next to the TV and consumed the free water bottles in the bathroom. We missed a coffee maker / water heater. 
Breakfast was taken in the Garden Court, a very nice location indeed. We still had to pay for the child breakfasts, very expensive at 19$ per child for a breakfast buffet without egg station and without fresh waffles. Otherwise, selection and quality were generally good, although one morning, the poached eggs were completely dry after remaining on the heating plate for too long. Another strange system here, very new according to our waiter: Even when customers present a breakfast voucher, they still have to sign a breakfast check, basically accepting charges. At least those charges did not appear on the hotel invoice at check out. 
The Palace is a very stylish hotel with a grandeur not often found at larger chain hotels in the US. While it is not in the center of tourist action, location is still very good: Right next to the F streetcar and BART stops, within easy walking distance of Union Square and all cable car lines.

title: “Beautiful room, excellent location, but who turned off the heat??”
text:
I travel as much as 15 days a month sometimes on business, and I have come to trust not only certain brands, but the reviews on tripadvisor. I chose this location based on the reviews on this site, and the fact that I trust Marriott. They weren't wrong at all! If you are looking for a nice business location, or a get away, this hotel is great! The location is perfect, easy to reach, and within walking distance of many sites, restaurants, etc. It is also within walking distance of the subway. 
The room was a nice size, with large, historical-style floor to ceiling windows, and the bathroom well-appointed. The folks working were very knowledgeable about where to eat, go, etc. The only complaint I had was the last night of my stay it was snowy and cold. Right before I went to bed, I realized that the heat was not as hot as it could have been. I turned it up, but when I woke up during the night, I realized the heat was not working. While I didn't call the front desk(I was traveling alone, and a call to maintenance at 4am was not what I needed to do), I did mention this upon checkout. The temp in my room was around 60degrees the morning I left. The front desk clerk's response to my concern was "well, sometimes people get hot, and so we turn off the main heat, so your unit in the room was just blowing cold air." I advised how cold it got, and that I could understand that during in between temps might warrant a cooler room, but this was BOSTON, in WINTER, and couldn't folks in rooms that were warm simply turn down their heat? There are individual heating units in rooms for a reason.
Don't get me wrong....my stay was marvelous, and folks were very friendly, but no heat? I would just be aware of it during the winter months. And call if it happens. I plan to stay here again, and definitely during the warmer months.

title: “Handy for Airport”
text:
Stayed on of last night before departing USA
Nice Rooms, great Pool, have shuttle to airport. About 5 minutes to Airport Car rental return.
Very limited selection of restaurants within walking distance

title: “Aaahhh wonderful nights sleep!”
text: Once we walked in we knew it was a top notch Inn and Suites The lobby was very clean and smelled good, no mold or musty smells, refreshing and clean. . We have ranked the Best Western Plus a Five comparing to the other Suites & Inn's we stayed in the past. The room was very nice, spacious, but most of all very clean. The service was excellent! In all the years I have been traveling and staying in hotels, I have never seen the management out front and personal. We were greeted by both managers when we walked in for the free breakfast buffet. The food was very good, but mainly it was exceptionally clean and sanitary. I was very impressed when I asked the managers, who by the way were very friendly, how old their hotel was and I was shocked to find out it was three years old!! I thought it was brand new maybe a few months old by the newness and the service. The location was perfect for us as we we traveling through headed east to Houston. Last hotel on rout I10 to Houston. I would recommend this hotel over any hotel I have stayed anywhere in the united states! That says it all! Great job to the managers!

title: “Super Hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed here for a weekend and found this Hotel was very nice for the money. The employees are just super friendly and always willing to help. The grounds are very well kept . The pool area was also very nice. The rooms are alittle on the small side. The bathrooms are also pretty small but you just make it work. Not that big a deal. Everything is VERY VERY Clean. We also ate at the restaurant and that meal was fine. The only problem we ran into is people that just let their kids yell inside the hallways. This shouldnt happen at any time of the day but when its at 7 am ........ well , just makes you wonder what the parents are thinking. Of course this is not the Hotels fault that people dont control their kids. But just the same the Hotel said they were sorry. While not their fault it shows they care. We would stay here again if in the area

title: “Great first stay in NYC - Hampton Inn TSN rocks!”
text: First visit to NYC, went for operas and shopping. You can't get a much better location than the Hampton Inn, on 8th at 51st, it's easy to get to just about anywhere in all of Manhattan. The subway station is one block away for northbound, 2 blocks for southbound (no elevators or escalators tho). Port Authority Terminal about 9 easy blocks. Wicked is LITERALLY 1/2 block away, and Hairspray down a block and over 1/2 block, Mamma Mia about 2 blocks. SAFE area at night, did not feel threatened once, even going to Ray's Pizza until 4:00 a.m. directly across the street, and 24-hour Cosmic Diner (recommend challah french toast!) a block away. Big 24-hour Rite Aid pharmacy one block north. Tasty D'Lite and McDonalds about four blocks south. "House of Brews" location steps away from lobby, with quite reasonably priced, excellent lunch/dinner fare and great beer selection. 6 blocks away from the heart of Times Square. Easy walk, even for a large person such as myself. Taxis are almost always waiting at the front, or just take the subway, wasn't bad at all. Complimentary hot breakfast can be crazy at around 9:00 a.m. but go earlier or 9:45 (ends at 10) and is much better. If you must go at 9:00-ish, bring someone to stake claim on seating for you! I set a magazine down on the counter with my coffee, and came back two minutes later to find someone had just moved them aside and taken my seat! Rooms were BIG, flat-screen TV nice, and FREE Internet (wired in rooms, wireless in lobby). No printers, but they have a print/net computer station in the office for guest use to print out boarding passes, etc. Just ask. Bathroom w/small but nice marble vanity with plenty of shelves below, GREAT shower and tub. Hotel very safe, they check everyone for room keys in the evening and all night. The bed was magnificent and puffy. Staff was amazing, including Sandra at the front desk, Eugene and Chris the concierge/bellmen. They said hi every day and evening, were genuinely interested in what we were doing, and gave many good suggestions. I would stay here again in a New York minute! Don't pay any attention to the bad reviews, some people just won't be pleased. If your'e going for the theater district or want a central midtown base of operations, this is the place!

title: “Looking forward to my next stay”
text: We were in the city for a special event and stayed at this hotel overnight. The room was quite comfortable and very clean and quiet. Plenty of hot water for showers in the morning. In addition, the stay came with a free breakfast. We got there relatively late for breakfast, so they were out of many things (like NYC bagels!), but what they had left was very good. Nice selection of breakfast foods, fruit, and make your own waffles. We are going to the same event this year, and are looking forward to our stay at the Hampton Inn Chelsea, NYC. We will definitely be getting to breakfast earlier this year, though.

title: “Great room, nice hotel”
text: I stayed at this hotel for one nought only during a recent business trip. I arrived very late at 11:30 pm. The check-in was quick. I was given a room at P floor. This was the first time I had to go to lower floors (lower than lobby). I was disappointed a bit, however the room was spacious with a very large bathroom. I guess this was designed to be an accessible room. The only reason I don't give 5 stars is that there was a loud noise from air conditioning through he night - so I could not get a good night sleep. I am assuming the rooms on the higher floors may not have the same issue. In the morning when I looked out the window, I noticed the room has a nice view looking right at a pool. Unfortunately I was not staying longer to enjoy the view. If you stay at this hotel I recommend to stay at higher floors.

title: “Excellent”
text: Was instantly welcomed when we arrived. Reserved a $375/night city view room, but was upgraded to a corner suite with a view of the water. Great service all around. Empress Lounge was nice. Did request engineering to fix the TV in the bedroom (seems to be a common problem), but decided to watch one of the 2 other TVs in the suite. There is one in the bedroom, one in the bathroom, and one in the sitting area. The one in the sitting area is a flat screen plasma TV. Very clean room and bathroom. Very comfortable bed. Bathroom was spectacular--great shower pressure. Will definitely be back next time I visit DC. Great value for the money!

title: “Modern and decent sized room.”
text: Went for a week with a friend and was very impressed by this hotel. We asked for a room with a view and got it. The room was good sized, especially for NYC standards, and must have been remodeled recently. The restaurant and bar was an added bonus, as the bar is on the roof and provides a nice view of the skyline. This hotel is also close to Grand Central station. I would recommend it to anyone, I felt very safe there.

title: “Boutique hotel with character”
text:
Hotel Boheme is a nicely restored building on Columbus Avenue -- the main street of the North Beach (Italian) section of San Francisco. It's a great area for urban hikers, especially if they don't mind some steep grades -- Russian Hill, the Coit Tower, and Chinatown are all fairly close, and may other parts of San Francisco are a long walk (or a cab ride) away.
Entrance to the hotel is tucked between patio tables of restaurants below, and you climb a flight of stairs to the concierge desk. Then, if necessary, another flight to your room.
"Stan" was our concierge, and he began making suggestions about where to visit before we even asked. "Charles" was equally solicitous on our way out. These guys really want you to enjoy your stay, and really know both the neighborhood and the city.
Rooms are small, cozy, and retro, with decor celebrating the "Beat" era of North Beach, and rooms painted deep colors. Our room was in very good shape save one patch of damaged ceiling.
Hotel Boheme does not try to be a full-service hotel. Room service consists of a limited menu of beverages only. Our room had a very small TV set (which we didn't need anyway). No fitness center or expansive lobby.
Complimentary sherry is provided from the concierge area in the evenings.
Here's the main thing: if you take a room fronting along Columbus Ave., you can sit near the window and watch the sidewalks below, which is fun. You also get a lot of street noise (Saturday night brought a lot of late-night revelry to the sidewalk cafes below; Sunday wasn't as bad). So either take the street-side room and be prepared (bring ear plugs for sleeping?) or else ask for a quieter room, or stay elsewhere.
We'll be back to Hotel Boheme -- with earplugs.
During our stay, we enjoyed a martini at the Beat-culture-soaked Vesuvio bar (next door to the famous City Lights bookstore), a focaccia sandwich and capuccino at Mario's Bohemian Cigar Shop & Restaurant, a decent dinner at Calzone's under the hotel, and a very nice dinner at Steps of Rome Trattoria. Nearby O'Reilly's Irish pub puts out a hearty brunch. Its hard to starve or get thirsty in this neighborhood. Don't worry, the hotel staff can point you to all these places & more; we also found the Lonely Planet San Francisco guide useful.

title: “Loved the Kimberly”
text: Our family of four loved our stay at the Kimberly. Ours was a spacious one bedroom suite with a full kitchen including dishwasher. There is a small grocer around the corner, so we stocked up on breakfast foods and we all ate well each morning before leaving to tour the city. The breakfast buffet is delicious but expensive and it was easier to eat in the room and spend the money elsewhere. The sofa bed was not comfortable for one of the kids so they gladly sent up an additional roll away. The staff was very helpful and accomodating and the doorman was a hoot. We took advantage of the Sunday river boat tour and enjoyed it immensely, even in the rain. What a great way to see the Statue of Liberty! We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Pleasantly Surprised”
text: We travel to New York a lot but this is our first stay at the Sofitel. You cannot beat its location being so close to Times Square. We are rather picky about beds, and these were extremely comfortable. We also chose to stay in and have room service for a dinner. The food came rather quickly and it was all warm! Overall, for a Manhattan hotel room, the room size was actually generous. (Most hotel rooms I have stayed in Manhattan are rather difficult to move around in because of their small size.) We will definitely stay here again in the future.

title: “A really nice place to stay”
text:
We recently completed a 21-day tour across the USA, concluding with three nights here. As it was a package, I was apprehensive that with NY being expensive, our tour company may have settled for budget accomodation, but no, the Hotel Beacon was great. Friendly staff, top class rooms, we were on the 22nd floor with marvelous views, and everything in the room was of a high standard. No food, but the excellent Viand cafe/diner is next door, and they do room service for the hotel.
The subway is three blocks south on 72nd Street, whilst three blocks east brings you to Central Park. The Fairway supermarket is right across the road and have all you need for a mid day lunch.

title: “a good stay, while on business”
text:
Spent 4 nights at this hotel during an industry function. None of the events were held at this hotel so cannot comment on conference ammenities. The Sheraton is by no means fancy, but compared to my previous stay down the street at the St.Anthony, it proves it's worth. The pros are it's proximity to the Riverwalk (albeit many other hotels are a bit closer), historical charm, nice big comfortable rooms (stayed on club floor however), friendly front desk and concierge. On the flipside, the club floor 'lounge' was nothing spectacular, but I'd go to starbucks if I want a good coffee/muffin, the restaurant is bland & uninteresting, and the McLeod's lounge is handy, but dark & not very inviting.
For what I needed the hotel for, it truly satisfied, and would definitely stay again

title: “excellent”
text: Stayed here midweek and really enjoyed the short stay. The room was spacious and you got a slight wow feeling as you entered the room. Very comfortable bed and all the extras in the right place. I needed to have my suit pressed late at night for an early morning meeting and they did it in extra quick time. Breakfast in the room service was efficient and good quality. I was disappointed to not have more nights here. The only drawback I could find was that access by car is at the back of the building and from North Michigan drive through the Nordstrom gallery. The reception is at the fifth floor. It does work because there are staff at the car entrance but a bit tortuous from the street. Guidance needed and only apparently one lift but as we were only there briefly there may be other ways in. Whilst I have explained this in detail its a great place to stay and the access is only a minor issue and the rooms and staff more than make up for the lack of prominence

title: “Best sleep ever!!!”
text: The bed was exactly what I paid for. I chose Four Points because I wanted to sleep well. The bed was so comfortable, the room very nice. I didn't want to get up the next morning to catch my flight. Well done. My only complaint is that the television didn't have a diverse channel selection.

title: “Clean, competent Hilton property beginning to show its age; very close to the White House”
text:
Up until a few weeks ago (see my review of the nearby Madison Hotel, which is my new favorite hotel in the district), the Capitol Hilton was my go-to hotel whenever I was in Washington D.C. The property is gigantic - I never have a problem getting a room, and the produce is very consistent. It is an easy five minute walk from the metro, and about the same distance from the White House, so it is close to everything. 
The rooms are decently spacious, and pretty quiet - you can hear a bit of traffic from the corridor and doors opening/closing, but overall pretty good, with attractive appointments that are just beginning to show their age. Marble floors in the bathrooms and nice linens on the bed. Overall a good Hilton property.
A few notes: some of the rooms have issues (e.g. I've had a tub that flat out wasn't working), be sure to ask for a quick change before you unpack. Despite having something like six elevators, I found myself waiting in the lobby or on my floor for as much as five minutes during high traffic periods (lots of business travelers like myself). The gym requires an extra payment to use, something I found rather annoying.
Still, this is a consistently good property, and is the property that I immediately call when none of my particular favorites have availability in the district. I give it four stars because that consistency of service can be somewhat difficult to find in D.C.
Don't shop in the hotel shop; if you do, expect prices 3x above the CVS that is just 1.5 blocks away, and with stale (and sometimes expired - check your Sourpatch Kids, as of 6/12 there were two packages that expired in April on the shelf!) food and candy.

title: “excellent choice”
text:
I came to san francisco in october for a conference at the moscone center and I stayed at the donatello for one night. I was pleasantly surprised. I have read excellent review about the hotel and they are all true. The rooms are large, very clean, recently renovated. Bed very confortable, bathroom very clean. The staff is very nice and proffesional. There is also breakfast served, but only few pastries ( all sweet) and coffee and orange juice. There is place for some improvement in that area.
Location is excellent, near the Union Square where all the shops and transportaion is convenienly located.
The only disadvantage was the noise, as already discussed upon. We were on the 12th floor but facing the main street ( the hotel is located on the corner, so it is facing 2 streets) . We had just arrived from an overseas flight and we had a 10 hour time difference, so I woke up at 2 am and couold not sleep for about 1 1/2 hours because of the noise ( some garbage trucks??). So I guess if your room faces the back or you do not have a jet lag, this will not be a problem.
Definitely excellent value for the money. I also stayed at a hotel twice the price but closer to the moscone convention center and that choice was not worth the money!

title: “Nice with solid friendly service”
text: I had a one night stay here.Check-in was a breeze, staff very friendly and several spoke to me by name. Room was very comfortable, though bath was dated and somewhat small. Room service was quick and food delicious. Parking is valet only ($27).

title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text: My family stayed here for one night before a flight out of Philly. Our room was very clean and recently renovated. The bed was beyond comfortable. My kids and husband enjoyed the pool and hot tub. We did order room service which was fast and very good. Overall this was a very nice hotel and we would definately stay here again.

title: “Warm and welcoming, a great place to stay!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here for a few days in the first two weeks of April, punctuated by a weekend trip to San Francisco. The location is a good compromise for easy access to the airport and the city centre, which was important to us because we wanted to do a fair bit of sight-seeing.
A few things stand out about this place, but first and foremost were the staff. We could always count on a warm smile and friendly greeting from them, no matter how busy they were, and nothing we asked was ever too much. A big thank you to all of you!
The free breakfast had everything from waffles, eggs and bacon to fresh fruit and oatmeal, with plenty of more healthful options to choose from. There are always fresh-baked cookies at the front desk, a nice touch which I took liberal advantage of. Also, most days there is a manager's reception in the afternoon at which guests can enjoy complimentary drinks and snacks.
We got a jacuzzi room, and were very pleased with the size and condition of the accommodation. Our window looked out on a car park, but we could clearly see the mountains in the distance, which was very exciting for my first time in Colorado.
We honestly enjoyed our time here more than at the respectable four-star hotel we stayed in at SF. Sure, the decor and the view were nicer, but the actual quality of the accommodation was not much different, and we got a lot more for our buck here. We will definitely be staying here again when I next come to visit!

title: “Huge Disappointment”
text: It all looked so good on the website. The doorman and the swish chandeliered foyer were very impressive, and we were looking forward to a comfortable stay. The room we were offered was appalling however. Wallpaper and paint peeling, tiles missing in the bathroom, and a very nasty smell. They changed us to another room which was just as bad, but half the size. At the third attempt, we were "upgraded" to a more expensive room at no extra cost. This was marginally better, but still tatty and dirty. Vacuuming was cursory, and the handbasin wasn't cleaned during the 7 days we stayed there. The whole corridor stank of cigarette smoke, and our room adjoined another, where Spanish was spoken loudly at all hours and the television was on full blast until the early hours of the morning, so we got little sleep. The Reception staff were surly. The hotel does have a great location, but there are so many others in the neighbourhood to choose from. We certainly wouldn't stay here again, and would advise anyone else to go elsewhere too. We love New York, but not the Hotel Pennsylvania.

title: “nice”
text: it was a nice hotel its near Disneyland and its affordable and it has good service the rooms are average and the rooms are spacious.

title: “"Many stays over 8 years"”
text: I am a flight attendant commuter who stays here in between trips. Rooms are always clean, the beds are comfortable, it is close to the airport and the van runs on time--these things are all important to anyone in the airline business.

title: “Charming hotel”
text: I am a Tribeca resident, and I needed extra space for the Christmas holiday for my family so I selected The Greenwich Hotel. I was very pleased! The hotel exemplifies understated elegance. From the moment you walk into the hotel it feels as if you've escaped from the hectic city. The rooms are a bit pricey, but I felt it was certainly worth it. Each room is individually decorated....a bit eclectic and minimalist, but everything in the room is high quality. The mattresses are Duxiana, and the toiletries were generous portions of Red Flower products (one of my favorites). There was even a wonderful complimentary snack basket in the room with treats such as Twizzlers, Tates Cookies, mints, etc. The public sitting area is beautiful and the restaurant Ago is a great meeting spot. Overall I think it is a great find and a nice change from the more traditional luxury hotels in NYC.

title: “Great, good value and wonderful location”
text: Great location and although the valet parking charge is $26, that was pretty reasonable compared to the rest of the area. The valet staff are really great, as are the rest of the staff. When I got back from Coranado having left my purse in a bakery there, the staff phoned the bakery for me and were really concerned to help me get it back. The rooms were immaculate and comfortable. It seemed like an old hotel that has been well updated. The location is excellent and I can't wait to go back!

title: “Awesome if you don't mind a view of brick wall.”
text: We stayed at The Michangelo the first weekend in Dec. The location of this hotel is perfect. Walking distance to everything ie times square, bway shows, Rockefeller center, 5th Ave, central park. We were given an upgrade when we checked in. Absolutely beautiful room, very spacious, well decorated, 1 1/2 baths. Just no view. Service was excellent. Answered every question, assisted when needed. We didn't eat in the restaurant or room service. We did use the mini bar in our room. Of course it's pricey, but it's there if you need it. The Duke store is next door, if you need snacks, or a meal, they have everything! $12.99 for Internet I felt was a little cheesy considering what you pay for the room. Overall very good experience!!

title: “Great location, great service, small room”
text:
I was in SF on business and this was one of the few places that had the number of nights I needed, six, and was close to the Moscone Center. I was able to get a corporate rate of $130 plus tax for each night.
The staff service was excellent. The bell captains helped me with a ride to the airport and were exceptional in their service, the housekeeping staff helped me with some laundry, the housekeeping staff kept my room neat and tidy, the wake-up service actually came to check on me when I was unable to get to the phone to answer the wake-up call, etc. This place had better staff service than grander hotels where I have stayed.
The room was smaller than some other rooms I've had, but it had a king-sized bed, a chair and ottoman, a desk, and a dresser. The TV was set on on a stand that wasn't in front of the bed, so it was uncomfortable to watch. My room gave me a view of Powell Street and I could hear the cable car bell occasionally, but overall, being on the 10th floor, the street sound wasn't bad; the only time it woke me up was when sirens were going by. The sleep kit they give you is really, really nice; I am a light sleeper, so this was very much appreciated.
The bath products are very nice. Herbal and spa like. It was one of the better lines I've had in hotels; even nicer than the Parc 55, where I stayed a year ago.
The location is great. There's a 24-hour Walgreens across the street, lots of casual restaurants nearby, a short walk to Union Square, a 10-minute walk to the Moscone Center, a short walk to Chinatown, a Wells Fargo machine nearby, etc. The location is far superior to the Parc 55, the only other SF hotel I've visited.
The drapes had a stain on them, and the carpet seemed old and musty, but otherwise, the room was furnished nicely. The bed linens seemed very clean, including the duvet cover, which is important to all travelers.
The hotel has a Cafe Fresco, which has great hours and a nice selection of foods to go, as well as some seating. For a business traveller, like myself, this was great.
My one complaint is that I could smell food smells one night. I don't know if a neighboring room had room service or if the smell came in from the heating and cooling units. It was gross though. There was no way to open the window to air out my room.
If I return to SF next December, I might stay there again, but I might try another hotel just to try something different.

title: “Nice Hotel - Great Location - Good Staff - Smallish Rooms”
text: Stayed here over the 2003 Thanksgiving Weekend. Selected the hotel on a recommendation. Loved the location and friendly staff. The hotel is small, but "charming". Everything was above average/good, except the room size. Small. Very small. Take that with a grain of salt, as this is SF, and hotels are going to be smaller. In another city, for the same price, you would get 30-40% larger size. The room was nice, but felt a tad cramped, esp. after a few days. Recommendation for breakfast by staff was best advice all weekend - Dotties True Blue Cafe (?).

title: “It ain't like it use to be!”
text: We have stayed at the Chicago Ritz in Water Tower Place for several years and it was truly one the US's finest hotels. We missed a few years and came back this December and it's gone from 5 to 4 stars. One example, how often do you pay over $400 a night then get charged an extra $10 a day for wi fi. It just isn't as classy a place.

title: “Basic, clean accommodations”
text: Basic, 2 star accommodations, just off freeway on Westside of El Paso. Right next to Cracker Barrel, a one minute drive or short walk to Cineplex. Decent, clean, basic place. A bit loud from freeway.

title: “OK for the price. Good if traveling with family and pet.”
text: This is a pet-friendly family hotel. The suites are very large with loft and 2 bathrooms and full kitchen and fireplace and 2 TVs. One of the two phones was dead and the hair dryer was broke. For the price this is a good place for a family to stay. The pool was nice, but the hot tub was still broken. A basketball court is also available for kids. Located next to I-71 made it noisy if you stay near the front, but very convenient to get around. Many good restaurants are nearby as well as a grocery store. A dog run up front provides a trashcan with pick-up bags for your pet.

title: “Lives up to the hype”
text: Great hotel to see New York from.
