Cosy, welcoming, perfect location, amazing genuinely nice staff especially at the front desk, some of the best sheets and comfiest bed ever and great complementary breakfast. Only minor points from making it perfect are the slightly temperamental plumbing (likely as a result of being an older building) and stairs which get the heart rate pumping when on the 5th floor (but staff gladly take care of luggage, even refusing a tip!). Will be returning.

title: “Fantastic hotel with only minor quibbles.”
text:
We stayed at the Mayflower Park last weekend, our room was a Classic Queen booked through an online site that gave us a wonderful deal so we can't complain too much. The room was immaculate, comfortable, tastefully decorated with free wifi and a good selection of cable channels. The bed was perfect, nice sheets, super cozy blanket. Loved it. 
Here's an odd downside: maybe it was the size of the room, a bit small, that led to the decision to only have one bedside table. My side, the one closest to the wall had no table and only about a foot of clearance so not only did I not have a spot to put jewelry, a glass of water etc. I had to shimmy along the wall to get out of bed. I don't think too much space would be taken from the room to move the bed over a bit for a table and more walking space. 
Also, the walls are not very well insulated, you can hear conversations in other rooms (among other things) and one morning we were woken up by loud tapping that sounded like it was right beside our heads. It was repair work going on downstairs, discontinued as soon as we called reception so I will add the service was polite, attentive and responsive. Also, the air conditioning unit, while moderately quiet when running had a very loud pop when it turned on, which woke us up a few times during the night.
The location is excellent, right next to Westlake Center, close to shopping, the monorail, attractions and really good food (not to mention a drugstore where we were able to purchase earplugs). 
I would've liked to see more options on their late night room service menu, they only had a cheese and fruit plate.
We would definitely stay here again, the staff were super friendly and helpful, and as for the downsides, we'll either try an upgraded room like the Deluxe Queen or just bring earplugs.

title: “Pre Cruise stay”
text: The hotel was great and it provided a clean atmosphere with easy access to the cruise ship departure and was reasonably priced

title: “Wish I had stayed longer !!!”
text:
Arriving in this hotel, my first impression was : This is the perfect American luxury hotel with the best location, near all shops and tourists' attractions.
At check-in I had the chance to receive a very warm welcome from Ms Chloe and the nice surprise of an upgrade to a Junior suite, very spacious and so well appointed, with all comfort and cleanliness, and with a spectacular view on San Francisco. The General Manager of this hotel sent me a personal welcome message which I so much appreciated. In the club lounge I was treated all the time as a VIP, the staff is so friendly and courteous, offering a great service and attention to detail.
The food was very tasty and the breakfast was gorgeous, plenty of fresh fruits, pastries, cereals, cheese, salmon, ham etc...
The hotel has a marvellous fitness-center, a big pool and a spa.
My check-out lasted three seconds, Mr Timothy wished me a good journey back home with a big smile. All in all, I loved my stay and regret not to have spent more nights..
Thanks again to the General Manager and to all his fantastic staff.

title: “The best of everything....”
text: I had spent some time reading hotel reviews on Trip Advisor before deciding to stay at the Elysee. We couldn't have asked for more. The service was efficient and friendly without being intrusive; our room was elegant, comfortable and super clean. It really did seem that a lot of thought had gone into the interior decor of the hotel generally and there were nice touches like the library where one could sit quietly and read. There was an atmosphere of friendly calm everywhere - an absolute delight. Just a tad noisy at night because of the air-con 'machinery' outside at the back of the hotel. We remedied this by sleeping with windows shut with the air-con on (it was quite humid). On reflection it might've been quieter taking a room at the front of the hotel, which we will do next time. In any event, it didn't spoil our stay which was wonderful.

title: “Perfect location, heavy on the wallet.”
text:
I stayed at the Novotel for one night during the NYC Transit Strike of 2005. My company decided to put me up here because it is literally one block away from my office building.
What I loved about the Novotel is the location - you are literally right in the heart of Times Square. A two minute walk and you are by Mars 2112, a Duane Reade and many different restaurants. The hotel itself also has a bar/restaurant. I didn't try any of the food offered there as I'm sure the prices are exorbitant, but the ambiance was just right. Not stuffy, but friendly.
Check-in was easy - we arrived around 7PM on a weeknight so there was no waiting. They have shoe polishers near the elevators, which I thought was a nice touch for the business travelers.
The room is a good size; I had two double beds and still enough room to walk around. There is a medium-sized TV with cable channels, Internet access at a charge and a minibar at a charge. Of course, this being New York, everything is just plain expensive.
There was something that I thought was interesting - the bathroom had wooden floors. I've never seen a bathroom with wooden floors and I felt like it was a nice and "homey" touch (although most people's homes don't have wooden floors neither). It just seemed less cold and uninviting to me.
Train stations nearby are the 1/9, the N/R and also the B/D/F/V at Rockefeller Center (just a few blocks away). Some notable landmarks are also the Rockefeller Center, Radio City Music Hall, 5th Avenue, the MoMA, the NBC studios... I'm sure there are many more but being a New Yorker myself, I'm not quite familiar with all the tourist sites.
All in all, a great experience at this hotel. But if you were travelling on your own budget, like many of the reviews before had said, it's way too much to pay just for a little bit of convenience.

title: “Great Hotel - Superb Staff”
text: A two night stay booked at a great rate through Priceline bidding. Hotel room clean, comfortable and airy. Lots of space to spread out - good table/business station (where I'm wiriting this now!). Free wifi and free breakfast. Staff at reception desk truly outstanding in greeting cutomers and providing information - a definite asset to the hotel. We will definitely stay here again when next in the Charlotte area.

title: “Nice visit - GREAT location”
text: The Fairfax was an ideal location for a first-time visitor. Great restaurants are all off the Dupont Circle, the Philips museum is across the street and Georgetown is a lovely 1 mile walk away. The hotel staff were all very friendly and they accomodated my request for a quiet room at the end of the hallway. We were lucky enough to stay on a weekend and lucked out as the Dupont Circle farmer's market was on Sunday. Speaking from experience, this was one of the BEST farmer's market! I would definitely stay on another visit.

title: “First Time to the West Coast”
text: I was traveling for business and this was my first encounter with the west coast. The room was beautiful and the staff was super friendly. Every morning when I left they would ask if I wanted a bottle of water, needed directions or a suggestion on where to go. they were very attentive and helpful. I only have two little complaints. One, I had to have something mailed out while I was there and the only option was fedex; while they brought everything to my room the was no pricing and no other option on how to send it. It eneded up costing me 30 bucks. Two, the number of homeless people around was upseting however I was told that San Diego has a ton. While these were just small problems (one being something they can not control), I will say they the valet who took my car the last night was extremely helpful as I questioned about leaving for the airport in the morning. He advised me on when to leave and who to call if the late night valet (who apparently is a slacker) doesn't answer. Overall I had an amazing time and would definitely stay here again.

title: “We're coming back!”
text: If you're looking for culture and easy access to all the touristy attractions, this hotel is located in an ideal spot. Easy access to public transportation, walking distance from hotel to local venues.

title: “overbooking problems”
text:
Stayed Thursday 11-11 through Sunday 11-14. I booked a King room with view 9 months in advance. Verified that my room would be available that morning and arrived to find that this room was not available. (I suspect as do other posters that they routinely overbook) So be aware if you plan a late arrival. To their credit they did give me a lesser room and credited the difference in price.
 That said the room was clean, the bed was the most comfortable hotel bed I have ever slept in. The location perfect and the staff friendly and efficient. This would have been a 5 star ranking without the check-in (overbooking) problems. They really need to work on that

title: “Better Than I Thought It Would Be!”
text: After reading several reviews, I was quite nervous about booking here, especially if I didn't get the guarantee that I'd be getting an renovated suite. I booked directly though the Hilton site and left a comment in my reservation that I wanted a King suite that was newly renovated (at the time of booking, all that was available was a Queen). My husband and I checked in on Fri. Nov. 2, the weekend of the NYC Marathon, and although the lobby and streets were RAMMED full of people, I was swiftly checked in, and placed in a renovated room (3202). Very very courteous and friendly staff. The room did not disappoint, superb quality, flat-panel tv, softest bed, clean linens, great Crabtree & Evelyn toiletries. The highlight of the trip was checking out on the Sunday...my husband and I had done a bit too much partying the night before and we wanted a sleep in, so we didn't want to check out at noon - we called the front desk, who told us we could check out at 1pm with no extra fee since it was the Sunday when clocks went back, and a lot of guests experienced confusion. I told the front desk we'd probably end up checking out later than that, and they told me I'd have to pay an hourly fee (which was fine). We finally checked out at 3pm, and they didn't charge us! They said "don't worry about it, have a great day"!! AMAZING! Oh, concierge staff are excellent - I told them I wanted to eat at a Thai place in the East Village, and within seconds I was recommended an amazing place. Would stay here again!

title: “Place to sleep”
text:
Howard Johnson LAX is conveniently located near the airport, is inexpensive, with several place to eat nearby. There is a regular shuttle service to and from the airport.
The facility is old and it's age is showing - stained carpet and old bathroom.
The staff are not helpful.
It is really just an inexpensive place to stay while transiting through LA.

title: “Perfect location to many NYC attractions.”
text: We recently stayed here during our first weekend getaway to NYC. We opted for the valet parking even though it was expensive. The hotel in general is nice and clean. It's just down the street from time square in the heart of the theatre district. Access to the subway is just steps away. We took the subway everywhere. The only complaint would be in reference to accessing the front desk. There is a large pillar that seperates the area which makes it hard to know who is in line next. Other guest just walk right in front of you not knowing that someone else is waiting. We were even offered complimentary umbrellas on a rainy day.

title: “Great Location with Fun Rooms and Staff”
text:
My husband and I recently stayed 2 nights at the Hotel Triton and looooved it. We joined the rewards club and received free internet as well as a $10 voucher for the mini-bar. They also included a complimentary bottle of wine in our room when we checked in. The nightly free wine hour in the lobby was fun. We booked online and saved a couple of hundred dollars a night compared to other area hotels. The staff was great and gave recommendations as well as directions. Every time we passed a staff member, they always greeted us whether it was in the lobby or in the hall.
The rooms are funky and adorable and are a great break from the standard hotel fare. I especially loved the huge bath tub.
The hotel is located just outside of China town and is just a short walk from the downtown attractions as well as public transit which will get you anywhere in the area.
The only negative is that parking is $40 a night. That's pretty standard for the area. Next time we won't rent a car.
We will certainly come back here again.

title: “very nice experience”
text:
The spa area is very nice with good equipment and amenities, much like a health club gym. Also a pool. The excercise room is open for 24 hours. Pool and sauna until 10. The rooms are ok, but starting to look a little tired. Staff was very pleasant and went out of their way to help you. We had a meeting here and food was very good and well presented. 
I would recommend a trip to Second City and the conceirge can arrange this. Book a couple days in advance.

title: “Wonderful hotel!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel for a short trip to San Antonio and we were delighted. The staff is friendly and they have excellent customer service skills. I love it, I recommend it and I would stay here again in a heart bit. Love the spa and the massage therapists but I wasn't that crazy for the pedicure, they did an ok job on this. 
The rooms are spotless, super clean and they do not stink. The only bad thing is that their windows must be really thin because I was able to hear the noise from the street in the middle of the night (well after all is right on the river walk and there's a lot of people enjoying themselves, drinking and partying).

title: “Great Hotel-Great Location”
text:
I recently stayed at the St Gregory over the Columbus Weekend. We visit the area often and like to try different hotels. The St Gregory met all my expectations and more. The 1 bedroom suite was well decorated ,large and very comfortable. 
The hotel staff was very cordial and helpful. The St Gregory is very close to all the Georgetown shops and restaurants and is within a short walking distance to the Dupont Circle Metro. Had dinner in the hotel restaurant and the food exceeded our expectations. For those visiting the landmarks of DC this hotel is a good find.
We will definitely stay at the St Gregory the next time we return to DC.

title: “GOOD SD HOTEL DEAL”
text: This hotel is very well located, close as good to the airport, downtown in San Diego. The reception was very good. The room was very clean and confortable. The prestation was very good for the price. I recommend this hotel.

title: “reccommended”
text: stayed 3 nights end of August 2006, hotel out of town but no great inconvenence only short taxi ride away or use nearby T. rooms large enough for two adults and 2 children, well equiped and spotless, pool wonderful for children. Breakfast pricey but diner only short walk. Large shopping mall almost completed next door. Staff very friendly and helpful, had a really relaxing and enjoyable stay can truly reccommend this place.

title: “Location and staff were a definite plus!”
text: The staff at the hotel was extremely friendly and helpful. We had no hot water on our 2nd day and we were immediately moved to another room. River-side rooms provide a wonderful view of the Ben Franklin Bridge. On several occasions the staff provided directions or assistance in finding restaurants or other locations. The complimentary breakfast buffet is an added highlight. The location was great - just blocks from the historic area. We were easily within walking distance to most Center City locations, but the hotel also has a courtesy shuttle service to many areas. We would definitely stay here again!

title: “Very Disappointing Second Visit!”
text: This was a tremendously disappointing trip to the Admiral Fell Inn. Let me start by saying that we stayed at the Admiral Fell last summer and loved it. It was quaint, in a nice part of town, well kept, and super nice visit. So, when we had to go to Baltimore again this summer for my step-daughter's graduation we booked five rooms at the Admiral Fell for ourselves and various family members. This year's room was not nearly as charming as last year's. The carpet was dirty. The bathroom door did not close. The sheets, and especially the pillow cases were pilled and rough. I actually checked to make sure there was actually a pillow case on the pillow. When we checked in there was only one person working, and he was dealing with a pretty hysterical guest who could not get her car out of the garage (it was flooded, and oh by the way, our valet is off). The valet was off? Really? He then turned to us and said he hoped we found parking because there was no valet on duty. Sigh. Nice start. He did find out for the hysterical guest that her car was on the third floor and was safe, not like the cars on the first floor, like another guest's BMW that was under 2 feet of water. Okay, more. Not once when any of us in any of our five reserved rooms called the from desk, was there anyone there to answer. My in-law's toilet broke, and my father-in-law had to go down to the front desk (as we were getting home from the movies), and he had to wait for someone to show up at the front desk, explaining that his toilet was not working, and why was no one answering the phone at the desk. The guy at the front desk said, "well, I have been trying to get someone without a reservation checked in all night. I will have someone look at your toilet." It was about 10:00 p.m. and he asked, "when?" Front desk man answered in a clipped tone, "Tonight." Really? You have an 83 year old man standing in front of you and that is your answer. When asked if there was a manager on duty the answer was, "no." Nice customer service. We did find out as the toilet was being fixed a bit later that there is one person who works as the handyman for three local hotels. Finally, the noise is untenable! The hotel was not crazy noisy last year. This year it was insanely noisy! There is a bar or something next door with live music, police activity, etc. It felt like they were in our room and we are on the fourth floor. It was just... not good. Not coming back.

title: “A premium but not luxurious hotel with a great location & good service”
text:
We stayed at the Hyatt Regency on our way to a week in Sonoma so I could finish up some business there and enjoy a weekend in San Francisco. This hotel has great weekend rates and we booked a top floor, Regency floor bayside view room for $149 a night with my Hyatt Platinum and AAA memberships. 
We stayed in room 1714 and it had a great view of the Bay Bridge and the Ferry Building below. The lady who checked us in, Kathleen, was very polished and welcoming. We valet parked our car-in spite of the $50 parking fee, parking in San Francisco is very expensive anywhere and a parking ticket is $73 minimum so with in and out priveleges, and our plans to drive up to Twin Peaks, Lombard Street, the beaches and Pacific Heights, we wanted that flexibility.
The hotel is updated 70's genre in a way that I'm sure will become classic over time. The glass elevators were featured in the movie "Earthquake" and are a bit of a thrill as they whisk you up to the 17th floor. The floors up to floor 15 have a different grade of decor from the 16ht and 17th floor. Our room was small by our own standards ( looked to be around 300 sf) but every inch was used well and decorated nicely in a contemporary way, with dark woods, nice stone floors and tile in the entry and bath areas and a "Mirror TV" inset in the bathroom mirror, that is nice for watching news or golf while you're shaving. The towels and toiletries were organized very nicely in Pottery Barn style bins beneath the sink. The bedroom had a nice flat screen TV but 2 things we didn't like were the sliding doors that only open one inch (the are bolted so they don't open any wider-I guess to prevent jumpers) and the ceiling height is uncomforably low. The building almost feels like a honeycomb of hotel rooms.We didn't use the mini bar as the Regency Club upstairs had just about everything we needed in the way of water, juices and drinks.
The Regency Club is an nice perk with great views. There is at least one employee always on duty during club hours and they were very accomodating. The breakfast presentations up there were very adequate with yougurts, fruits and cereals as well as smoked salmon, bagels and all the trimmings. On the weekends they actually are trying to "up it a notch" by adding bands and dancing until midnight for Regency Club members. 
If you are relying on public transporation, there is no better place to stay because right outside the hotel is BART access to the airport and BART routes, Ferry connections across the Bay, Cable Car stops and plenty of taxi's. Union Square is just a few blocks away and the Ferry Building has some great shops and restaurants. Just up the street is Tadich Grill, probably on of the best seafood places in SF, as well as the Carnelian Room-a great place for drinks on the 55th floor of the Bank Of America Building. Chinatown is only four blocks up the street on California and Grant and Nob Hill is a cable car ride away ( or a 10 block walk uphill). You can actually catch the cable car stop up there to the Fishermans Wharf/ Union Square cable car-very handy.
We had brunch on Sunday at the Mark Hopkins, an experience I'd highly recommend. The food is excellent with limitless champagne and caviar and some very nice brunch choices and the most incredible view of San Francisco. Over the years we've stayed a lot of places in San Francisco and I have to admit that staying on the 18th floor of the Fairmont tower is still probably my favorite place.
The Hyatt Regency is a true business hotel, more than a luxury hotel-more Toyota Avalon than Lexus but the service is great, and for the $149 price ( for their best rooms) you just couldn't beat it. And just one parting thought-if you call down to the valet about 10 minutes before you head down, they'll usually have your car ready-seemed to be the case for us the 8 or 9 times we needed our car.

title: “one word...excellent”
text:
I dont think there is anything different I can say from a lot of previous reviews...I should know as I have read most of them...and I booked our stay at this hotel on the strength of the reviews on TA. I can only say we were not disappointed and the hotel truly lives up to all the glowing reviews and more.
Our trip to New York was for my 40 th birthday and my trip was made extra special due to staying at this little gem of a hotel, the management even gave me a bottle of bubbly-I was really touched.
All of the staff from the boys on front desk, the lovely ladies in Ricks lounge and the maids were all happy, smiley and extremely polite with any requests made being promptly and effeciently met.
The whole hotel exuded and air of calm and serenity, youd never believe being in such close proximity to Times Square. It is spotlessly clean and the food available at Ricks was fresh and plentiful and inviting.
I loved everything about it, would return in a heart beat, and would thoroughly recommend it to anyone.
New York is amazing as well....Im longing to return.

title: “Another Nice Experience with my Family at the Palace”
text:
We are in the middle of enjoying another stay at the Palace hotel. My wife, infant daughter and 6 year old are enjoying the grandeur of the building and location. We especially like the distance to Yank Sing the best Dim Sum in San Francisco in our opinion. If you’re thinking about staying we recommend it however it’s very expensive so be prepared to pay for everything unless you’re a seasoned bargain traveler.
If you stay take the following note; parking at the hotel is $48 Valet only w/come and go. I recommend right behind the hotel is Hearst Parking garage almost like self park its so close and its $20 for 24hours flat although no come and go so if your leaving more than twice per day you may want to valet. The Valet tried to talk us into using the hotel parking and told me that hearst closes and has holiday hours but the hours are very manageable unless you’re a real night owl or have a very early flight.
Also I am Platinum with Starwood and have always gotten a two room suite upgrade but every time I have to be very persistent they offer one and two "level" upgrades and say no suites but I keep going back and politely asking for the suite and usually get it after no more than one night in a single room.
The larger single rooms are bordered by Market street which is very loud from early to late so being inside the hotel may mean smaller room but it will be quiter. The Suites are on the end with less noise and worth it if you have to pay.
The hotel is not the Four Seasons but it has consistently good service, very nice rooms and high qaulity standard and is in a beautiful back setting also they do very will with deals that cut out the expensive extras like including parking and meals in the rates. 
Enjoy your trip to SF!

title: “Noooooooooooooo!”
text: Splinters in the floor, cheap toilets, holes in the walls, and I didn't want to know what attention to detail *wasn't* paid to the rest of the room. It's cheap, close to the airport, and that's it. I was glad to get out of there and on my way. The desk staff was helpful and patient - good for them! The facility is NOT in good repair.

title: “Do not stay at Scottish Ins”
text: We went down to Florida - to go to Mayo - and decided to try Scottish Inns. My brother- who was watching TV until later - got into his bed later on - around 1 am in the morning. But he discovered that his sheets were dirty - they had blood spots, and also dirt marks. So he called the front office - and they told him, that they do never give clean sheets out - and that we would have to move to another room - and by now it was going to 2 am. They told us - we could sleep on the dirty sheets or move - how do you move guests from one room to the other - at 2 am in the morning? Doesn't it make sense to just give clean sheets. I complained to the owner about it in the morning - he said "that is our policy" Of course - my brother slept on top of his bed - because he sleep on the dirty sheets - which doesn't make sense - because the blankets/duvets smelled so bad - I could hardly bring them to my face.This is the address: 2300 Phillips Highway.If possible - find a super 8 motel - or La Quinta.

title: “An interesting visit...”
text:
Did not stay overnight at this hotel, but did go there with friends who had booked rooms, to get ready for a wedding. In order to check in early, my friends were given a TINY room, being told that was all that was available. It was quite interesting for myself (a female), the groom, best man, 1 groomsman, and my husband to all try and dress/primp at the same time. As small as it was, the room was beautiful. 
There was a broken beer bottle in the mini bar and the rest of the beers were frozen, but my friends were not charged for that.
Also, when they returned to the hotel there was a problem with a 3rd room that had been booked and they were upgraded to one of the 'theme' suites.
The next day my friends reported that they were quite pleased with the hotel, staff, and the way they were treated.
This hotel is gorgeous, with a lot of art, photography and generally an elegant & upscale but fun atmosphere. The pool is very nicely landscaped with cabanas and lots of poolside seating. There is a bar and food is available at the pool.
Note: This is a totally non-smoking hotel.
Also note: you will be charged for nearly everything. Snacks, minibar, music and movie channels, etc. Not suitable for someone looking for a bargain, but I supposed you might get a good deal on Priceline or some other hotel booking web site.
The best man had also booked a much nicer and larger room for the bride & groom for after the reception, but the balcony overlooked the air conditioners. I supposed that's not so important for a wedding night stay :)
I would definitely stay here if a room was available at a good price.
VERY attentive staff.

title: “Great value perfect location”
text:
We're Platinum members and were greeted and upgraded to a spacious room. The staff was obliging and terrace in the concierge lounge was a bonus we enjoyed for outdoor cocktails and breakfast too. 
We frequently stay at Marriotts in NYC and we will be coming back to this property.

title: “What is that smell ...”
text: Stayed here 4 nights. We were first put in a room with a funny, musty smell and one right opposite the lift, so very noisy. We complained and asked to be moved. To their credit they moved us to a quiet, clean room that didn't smell at all. The decor is faded and this hotel is badly in need of a refurb/refit. Location is good, about 5 mins from Union Square. I doubt I would stay again though.

title: “Airline Cabin crew come first”
text:
Just back from 4 days in the Radisson Martinique. Our only problem was checking in - we arrived on time to find we had to wait three hours for our room. After travelling from Belfast we were exhausted and disappointed. The attitude of the staff ranged from rude to very helpful. To be fair we did get a few drinks vouchers for the hotel bar and after complaining again two hours later we got a complimentary breakfast. To be honest I would rather of had my room to rest and freshen up in than anything else. The next day we realised that the hotel has contractual arrangements with at least one airline - they use rooms for as long as they need them - unlike Joe Public who is out at 11. Another thing, the so called free internet sucks!
Apart from that the rooms are clean and well looked after and the hotel location is excellent. Good luck checking in - you will need it!!

title: “Great Hotel, Highly Recommended !”
text:
It's not easy to find a hotel you will like on your first visit to a city.
It might take several visits and a bit of luck.
Gladly on my first visit to NYC, the pod hotel was right on the spot.
I was impressed by the reviews here and the hotel website, also
by the young spirit of the hotel.
The hotel proved to be all I hoped for and more.
The location is good in midtown and is a small walk from the metro.
Felt safe walking there at night too.
The staff was friendly and my requests were all handled.
The concierge was very willing to help.
My single room was very cool. 
One of the cleanest hotel rooms I've seen and cleaned each day.
The shared bathrooms were no prob, they were very clean, no queues
and handy status lights in your room to show you if they are occupied.
The hotel style is young in spirit and I liked it very much.
Music in the corridors, music in the showers :)
My room was not large, this is a budget hotel after all. 
But the space was used very smartly and I had no problems with space.
I stayed 9 days, I'll definitely be back in the future and I highly recommend this hotel !

title: “Great Service!!!!”
text: I was at this hotel having dinner with my fiance and I have to say the food is good but the service is great. I think our waitress name was Tanesha. She was courteous and served us with such a positive attitude. Only if other wait staff was as attentive as our waitress was. Even though it was busy that night, I had a good dinner.

title: “You won't be disappointed”
text:
We are pretty loyal to Hilton, and most of the time they are consistent, but sometimes you don't get the value you are paying for. This hotel is a very solid choice in San Francisco. The location is great. Plenty of restaurants and shopping nearby, yet away from the tourist mecca of Fisherman's Wharf. You can walk anywhere from here, or take a short trolley or cab ride to Chinatown, Fisherman's Wharf, the Ferry Building, whatever.
The hotel is very popular and the lobby is buzzing constantly. That said, check-in was fast and efficient. The room was very clean and quiet. The elevators were speedy and easily available. The Starbucks continental breakfast they offered us as Honors members was a surprisingly good value. This is a first-class hotel and you really can't go wrong choosing it if you want a big city experience. This is a big hotel, so if you are looking for an inn type experience this is not for you, although the name Hilton sort of speaks for itself on that point.
The only negative: parking here is absolutely outrageous. You expect that in SF, butiIn addition, the garage is somewhat dark, cramped and hard to get around. Avoid parking here if at all possible.

title: “Excellent place to stay in times square For business or for pleasure”
text:
I have stayed at many Hilton's and Starwood and kimpton properties. I like this Hilton in times square because of the service and the staff. Front desk is extremely friendly an helpful. And if they can check you in early they will. The rooms are nice, the only down fall is they only have king beds. No doubles or two queens. Room is always fresh and clean. 
Bell service and front door men are also excellent and very helpful with directions and getting a taxi. 
The hotel also offers breakfast that is included at Pigalle which is fabulous. The food there is delicious and they are always accommodating and service there is wonderful. 
I love love the business center, there. Extremely helpful with incoming packages and out going packages. Printers are always available at no charge. Fed ex picks up at midnight also. Excellent business hotel.

title: “Stunning - Absolutely Stunning!”
text:
We have travelled around the States quite a bit and have stayed at some very good hotels but I have to say that the Grand del Mar is the best so far. It is not cheap but then again you expect to pay for quality and this hotel has that in abundance.
The staff, without exception are polite, attentive and very professional and you feel that nothing is too much trouble. The room was exceptional, we were on the ground floor and had a siiting area outside by the Reflection Pool which was great as the sun was there all morning.
We ate at the Amaya, the Lounge Bar and the Clubhouse Grill. The food was of a high quality and reasonably priced. We also took the courtesy limo to eat at a Chinese restaurant in Del Mar. The Concierge arranged everything and even sent us confirmation.
I only have two negative comments. On the first night we ate in the Lounge Bar and placed our order with the waiter, after half an hour our food hadn't turned up and we raised it with the waitress. It turned out that the waiter had forgotten to place the order with the kitchen. This was quickly rectified and we weren't charged for the food. My second issue was that at check-out we were charged for some mini-bar items that we did not have, again this was quickly rectified.
Overall this place was amazing and I would recommend it anybody.

title: “Poor Execution of Our Wedding, Including "Losing" Our Gifts”
text:
Our wedding reception was at Mistral, a wonderful restaurant and event location (around the corner from the Back Bay) that we highly recommend. We held our ceremony at the Back Bay Hotel. Our guests stayed overnight there and we also treated everyone to breakfast in the hotel's Stanhope Grille the morning after the wedding. 
Planning with Tiffany [-] went smoothly and she was very helpful. She seemed to cover all the bases and reminded us of things we may have overlooked. I was confident things would go smoothly under her command.
However, the day before the wedding, Tiffany emailed me that someone named Marcelo would be in charge of the event because she wasn't working the weekend of our wedding.
We are pretty laid-back people. I used to moonlight doing a some wedding catering and I've seen it all . . . I also know that things go wrong and most things don't bother me.
But after our weekend at the Back Bay, all I could think was that it seemed like the adults had gone away for the weekend and left a bunch of college kids to run the place.
To begin, we had welcome bag/amenities we paid to have delivered to our guests rooms on Friday. We delivered them to the hotel around lunchtime on Friday. At 8 p.m. or so, my mom said she hadn't received her gift bag and we had to call the front desk to ask them to please deliver the welcome bags. 
On Saturday, I arrived at the hotel in my own car, in a wedding dress, with bags in hand. The valets took my car, but didn't help me with my multiple bags, which I struggled to get up the stairs. There were 3 valets just standing there, yacking with each other. I mean, how could you miss me in that big ol' dress? And how come the valets didn't know a bride was showing up?
Where was Marcelo? I never saw him. 
Next, incorrect names were on the hotel event monitor screens that announced our wedding, even though I specifically spelled out in the contract which names (and the correct spellings) we wanted. (I have been previously married, and they used my ex-husband's last name, not my own last name. Also, a guest told me that the day before the monitors had my correct last name, but that it was spelled incorrectly.)
A champagne toast with ginger ale option (specified in the contract) was supposed to be passed out as soon as my husband and I walked back down the aisle. No one from the hotel was there with the toast, and after waiting, I had to go to the front desk (where the staff was hanging around and joking) and ask them to please bring it out. It took them quite a bit of time to bring it, and when they did, there was no ginger ale for the kids and teetotallers. This took more time to rectify, which confused the guests, who were expecting a toast and couldn't figure out what was going on.
During the toast, which was a speech given by one of our closest friends, the staff at the front desk was still joking, laughing and chatting so loudly that one of our guests had to excuse himself from the room and go ask the desk to keep it down so we could hear the speaker.
My parents had invited our guests to breakfast at the Stanhope Grille in the hotel for Sunday morning. The hotel was supposed to apply the charges to our master account, but instead charged our guests for the breakfast. We had to have them back the charges out individually and reapply them to our master account. This was embarassing, because we intended to provide breakfast for everyone. Some guests who checked out prior to our realization of this error may have been billed for breakfast. I have to try to find out in a tactful manner who they were and try to rectify the situation.
When we left, the bellman took our bags out to the car. The silver cake stand that we needed to return to our bakery was with the bags. When I retrieved it from the trunk of the car to put in the front seat for the drive home, I noticed it had been dropped and had a large dent on one side. The dent occurred in the five minute span of time that the bellman had the luggage trolley with our bags. No one would take responsibility for it.
My husband had had enough nonsense by now, and went to the front desk to complain. He really got upset when the girl at the desk listened to him and then said, "Oh well, things happen."
Finally, I learned today that at least one guest had left wedding gifts for us at the front desk. They had requested the gifts be delivered to our room. We never received them. We are currently missing a few gifts, one was a magnum of Veuve Clicquot champagne. It's pretty uncomfortable when your relatives call you to see if you liked the gift they left for you and you have no idea what they're talking about. I don't even know how to go about asking people if they left gifts for us at the front desk, nor can I imagine a way they can make this up to us and my relatives who paid for gifts that can't be located.
The Back Bay Hotel is very nice, clean and seems like it has everything going in its favor. I was really shocked by the apathy and lack of focus we experienced. 
By contrast, definitely have your wedding reception at Mistral. Everything was executed in an exceptional manner. The staff is lovely, attentive and friendly. The food is exquisite and the room has a fantastic vibe. Couldn't be better. Just find some place other than the Back Bay for your guests/ceremony!

title: “Nice hotel - will return”
text: This is a pleasant, friendly hotel with excellent service. Room was clean, quiet (facing the marina, not the bay) and functional. Full breakfast was included and was much better than most 'breakfast included deals', with excellent service. The front desk was most helpful and provided us with pick-up and drop off at airport and several other locations during our 4 night stay. This is not a luxury hotel, but it is a very comfortable place and a good deal for the money.

title: “Was expecting more...”
text:
Was expecting more being a Marriott property. This is an old motel converted into a Residence Inn. Hot water was out for the whole property on the second night of my three night stay. I was notified of this via memo delivered to room. When I inquired when it would be back on the front desk staff didn't even know the hot water was out. She put me on hold and when she came back to the phone informed me that they hoped to have it up by 8am the next morning and that they would give me 200 Marriott points for the inconvenience...it was a long night quick shower and difficult shave. Even before I checked in they called to tell me they were over booked and that I needed to go to a different property for one night. Then I get another voicemail a few minutes later asking e to disregard the previous message.
Was just not a good experience overall.

title: “Action Packed”
text: Entertaining fun & original. Loved the Lobby full of Stumptown drinking Apple junkies ALL day and night. Breslin Restaurant outstanding. John Dory, so so..very expensive for what you get. We had one good experience there & one bad. Having the best coffee shop in NYC, Stumptown (arguably as Blue Bottle is also very good) in the lobby is a real treat. Loved the decor, flowers, the staff. The room was big. Comfortable bed, great minibar & fun snacks on offer. Closet totally inadequate for 7 nights and although plenty of room, only one desk chair for two of us. On the 11th floor it was bright & very quiet. The location central & very convenient. Good value for money. Would definitely go back.

title: “Great hotel in a fantastic location”
text:
My husband and I have just returned from a four night break in New York (Nov 24-28 2006) staying at the New York Hilton on Avenue of the Americas (also known as 6th Avenue). The hotel was absolutely ideal for our trip - we were looking for a good quality hotel in a fantastic location and it scored maximum points on both criteria.
Overall Hotel:
This hotel is huge! It has everything that you would expect from a 4 star Hilton hotel in New York - large reception area, bars, gift shops, restaurants, concierge etc. However, I know that Hiltons often have a reputation for impersonal and sometimes even inefficient service due to the size of the hotel - not this Hilton. Everybody we came into contact with at the hotel was lovely - friendly, courteous and professional. If they said they would do something, it was done and done on time - they even did a little bit more when they could. For such a large hotel in such a major city I think this is a big deal! 
Room:
The hotel is currently renovating some floors and unfortunately our room was on a floor that had not been renovated, so although it was fine, everything worked - it was getting just a little bit tired. I'm happy if a hotel has a nice bed, a good bathroom with a fully working shower and a minibar and it had all three! Believe me, I have been to some grand hotels that didn't have ticks in all of these boxes! If we had stayed in a room that had just been renovated I am sure that this hotel would have scored maximum points in all criteria - but because the room we had was a little tired (and the air conditioning smelt a bit funny) I need to mark the hotel down just on this bit!
Location:
This was the best bit! It would be hard for a hotel to be better located in Manhattan than the Hilton New York. 2 minutes walk to your left when you leave the hotel gets you to Central Park and 10 minutes walk in the other direction brings you to Times Square. Another 2 mins walk straight ahead will get you to Fifth Avenue and Rockerfeller Center - who could ask for more than this?

title: “Acceptable Place”
text:
This was not our first choice when we searched for a hotel for an extended weekend stay to be near family. We needed three rooms and most of Phoenix was booked due to sports events taking place in the area.
We could only find rooms here and at the Hampton on the other side of I-10 that would be anywhere near the area where we needed to be so after sending a family member to scout out the two properties, this one was deemed to be preferable. One reason it was preferable is that while it is close to the interstate it does not sit directly on it, but is located somewhat back from the traffic. There is a row of other budget hotels between this property and the interstate highway--a Travel Lodge and some local extended stay hotel. So you do not hear the traffic noise from the interestate in this property--some noise from McDowell, a five-lane busy street, but not loud enough to be annoying.
The hotel is new as the previous person posted and still had a banner proclaiming it as "Now Open" when we arrived 3/22. Our rooms were listed as suites and we paid $124/nt. for them. They were spacious with a separate sofa, two chairs, a round table, coffee table and desk with leather swivel chair as well as the dresser, two night tables, and the tall wooden cabinet that held the flat-screen TV and contained a fridge and microwave. There were two phones, one portable, and there was ethernet connectivity at the desk. The desk had multiple electrical outlets which was a nice feature.
The bathroom had a single sink in the marble counter and a tub with shower. Good water pressure. There was a coffee pot in the bathroom, and an ironing board and iron in the closet. The closet had a mirrored door and there was a full length mirror on the opposite wall--another thoughtful item.
The furniture appeared to be nicer than that found in many discount hotels and I did not have any problem with the bed or the pillows. Standard thin flowered covering on the bed, thin towels, and basic amenities in the bathroom.
The breakfast in the morning was adequate--two waffle machines to make y our own waffle--pastries, bagels, white bread, cereals, juices (orange, grapefruit, apple), fruit (apples,oranges, bananas), and coffee. There is a loud flat-screen TV in the breakfast area and the breakfast crowd seemed to be mostly young people with their coaches. Despite the large number of what appeared to be sports teams at the hotel the place was very quiet.
There were menus of area restaurants at the front desk and the staff seemed willing to help.
I did not visit the fitness room or business center nor did I notice if the pool was functioning. We did not spend much time at the property except to sleep.
There is a Sonic and a Pollo Loco within walking distance and a large Chevron station with a convenience store at the corner of McDowell and 51st. There is a Waffle House and several small local places across the five lanes of McDowell. There is a Food City Grocery, also across the street and within walking distance if one is up to crossing the busy street. Most of the businesses in the area have Spanish names and it appears to be a very bustling commercial district with what appears to be multi-family housing directly across the street from the hotel. I say appears to be because there is a high concrete block wall separating McDowell from these units.
I saw policemen pull cars over on McDowell on two of my trips back to the hotel at night so it seems to be an area with a lot of police presence, but I did not feel uncomfortable at the hotel.If I had been traveling alone I think I would have still felt comfortable as the parking lot is well-lit and there appears to be a fair amount of pedestrian traffic in the area.
The only problem we experienced here was with the elevator. We were on the third floor and the elevator often stopped on the second floor and refused to go to the third floor. On the day we were checking out with lots of luggage we waited with many others at the elevator. One couple waiting said they had been stuck on the elevator the day before. We finally gave up and walked down the stairs carrying our heavy suitcases. This was annoying.

title: “Excellent service”
text: We stayed two nights for a quick getaway with our kids. Rooms were very comfortable and spacious. The service was excellent from the bellmen, front desk, housekeepers, to wait staff. We ate at High Velocity, the sports bar, and all of the food was top notch. Location was within 5 min walk to shopping, football stadium, great restaurants. We could have walked to the in probably 10-15 minutes. the Etlejorg (spelling?) museum and state museum were across the street. Overall, it was a great experience. Definitely would stay again.

title: “The Right Choice”
text: Great Location and very friendly staff made our visit to San Diego fantastic. We loved the complimentary cookies and fruit waiting for us after our busy day on the town. The rooms are spacious and nicely decorated. We loved the pool and jacuzzi overlooking the ocean. Computers available on each floor as well as free wireless available in room. We will definitely come back for another stay.

title: “enormous hotel next to grand central station”
text: The hotel is HUGE... felt as big as the casino hotels in Vegas. The rooms are nice, a step above regular hyatts but a major step below park hyatts. The location is good if you're only staying for one night, but there are better places to stay if you're taking a longer trip. the room was clean and comfortable. Room value definitely depends on the rate you paid, anything under $175, I would consider a good deal for this caliber of hotel in NYC.

title: “I love this hotel!”
text: I stayed at this hotel and was amazed on how clean and how nice the rooms are... The Front desk people, the breakfast hostess are really friendly!! I will always stay at this hotel whenever I go to Jacksonville, Fl.

title: “We'll be back!”
text:
We chose the Hotel Elysee based on Trip Advisor reviews and we were not disappointed! The service couldn't have been better. Everyone was pleasant and very helpful. Our room was located on the 7th floor in the back. Though we had no view, we also had no noise, and the room was spotless. The location was perfect for us, between Madison and Park. We were able to walk to MoMA, Rockefeller Center, the theater district, and Central Park and were surrounded by shops and 
restaurants. The subway line was two blocks away. If you want a great take-out lunch, try the deli right across the street-it's filled with locals at lunchtime (always a good sign). During our four nights there we enjoyed the weeknight free wine and cheese in the evenings, and the breakfast of fresh bagels, muffins, fruit, juices, yogurts, and cereals, with wonderful service. 
We met a world traveler from Holland, who also found this hotel on Trip Advisor, and we all agreed that the atmosphere (more European) was much preferable to the large "famous" named hotels in NYC. On future trips to NYC we will certainly be staying at this hotel. Our 14 year old daughter can't wait to go back!

title: “Great location, nice view”
text: Nice view on the upper floors. Stayed on the 16th floor, could see some of the lights in the theater district. Bed was comfortable...location was excellent. Great place if you plan on catching a show and don't want to pay for an expensive hotel.

title: “Great location, great staff, superb value”
text:
I stayed here with my family (wife and 2 kids aged 3 and 1) for 3 nights. I would heartily recommend this hotel and am very puzzled by its lowly standing in the ratings on Tripadvisor.
I guess we got a pretty good deal due to the current climate: $394+tax/night for a Taj Club level 1 BR Junior Suite. The room was identical to the one available to view on the hotel's website virtual tour. It was very clean and well presented and there was a platter of cheese and bread and a nice bottle of pinot noir sitting on the table in the sitting room on our arrival.
The real wow was the view from the Taj Club windows. It is situated on the 15th floor and has a beautiful view across the Public Garden and the Common. Absolutely breathtaking on the sunny mornings we were lucky enough to enjoy. 
The catering available at the Club was lovely. Breakfast consisted of fruit, cereal, beautiful baked goods, patisserie, etc. and usually something like bagels with smoked salmon. There is a Nespresso machine, juice, etc. We were usually only joined by 2-4 others. There are also food offerings at different times of the day such as afternoon tea and evening hors d'oeuvres and a very nice selection of wines and other drinks available.
The real stars of this hotel are the staff, however. Abraham and Ray the doormen typify the friendly service we experienced at the Taj. Those guys are great.
As anyone who knows Boston will attest, the location of this hotel cannot be beaten. Right on the corner of Newbury Street and across the road from the Public Gardens: brilliant for heading out early in the morning with kids who are still working on British Summer Time!
So, all in, this was a great experience. I've only stayed at one other hotel in Boston, the Lenox. It was fine but nothing more. The Taj gives a lot more for a little more money. Well worth it in my opinion!

title: “Nice Hotel and close to everything I wanted to see”
text: The hotel was beautiful and comforting and the rates were good. I was booked at the different hotel and switched after the first night because it was a nightmare. Spent two nights and the Wellington. The staff was courteous and willing to help.

title: “Going above and beyond”
text: Staff went above and beyond "just good service" to help me move a dozen boxes from the hotel to the convention center. Technically it was "against union rules," but they got special permission to transport the boxes for me.

title: “Great Hotel and location”
text: We stayed here in July for 2 nights, the hotel was excellant, the location outstanding and the staff extremely helpful. A pet hate of mine is having to pay for internet access (for each appliance ie lap top I phone etc) when you are paying a high price for a room whereas you can buy a cup of coffee in the cafe nearby and get free access

title: “Liked hotel, good staff, but street noise problems”
text:
Like at least one other reviewer noted, there is a problem with street noise. Specifically, constant sirens of emergency vehicles, all night long. The hotel is apparently one block from a fire station. The hotel has individual heating/air-conditioning units, which vent directly outside, and apparently allow considerable noise to enter the room. We live in a far-out suburban neighborhood, and are not accustomed to sirens at all hours.
For a city dweller who was accustomed to this kind of noise, this would be a fine, reasonably-priced, hotel. But for us, we won't stay here again.

title: “Sharpest of the Club Quarter hotels I've stayed in”
text:
The Central Loop CQ is the cleanest, most polished and well-serviced of the CQ I've visited: NYC (all of the hotels), DC and Chicago. The best word I can find is "sharp." The feeling you get is that the people here care about the place, take pride in it, and want to provide you with the very best experience possible. The sitting room off the lobby is quite comfortable and the "living room" downstairs is about the best club room I've seen in this chain.
Yes, the rooms are small. But you don't go to Chicago (or NYC or DC) to sit in a hotel room. You're there to sleep and shower. Maybe work a bit. And the Central Loop CQ's club rooms seem to be a bit more spacious than those in the other hotels. 
The staff is pleasant and helpful. (I had a problem with the valet staff, but it was handled quickly and resolved to my satisfaction.)
The location cannot be beat. You are steps from most of what the Loop has to offer or within a block or two of access to the El for more distant destinations. 
We were in Chicago for a wedding and MOST of the guests invaded the hotel for the weekend. I really expected some kind of slowdown or hiccups with the service, but I experienced nothing but first-class service.
So why not FIVE stars? I had problems with the online reservation system. I originally reserved rooms over the phone. When I discovered that we wouldn't need to come into Chicago as early as I had expected, I went online and modified the reservations. WARNING: do NOT trust the online system to process your request. My changes were NOT processed and I paid the cancellation penalty. I was a bit nervous the night before we left, so I called CQ to confirm the modification in our reservations. Wendy, the CQ rep I spoke, couldn't find the changes but she helped me greatly in guaranteeing the balance of our reservation -- I did not want the rooms cancelled on us -- and she called the hotel itself to make doubly sure we were in good shape. She admitted to me, however, that the online reservation system isn't reliable. So take that as a warning. Always call, always ask for a NEW confirmation number, and always note the date/time of the call and the name of the rep who helps you.

title: “"THE BAY BRIDGE INN" IS A NIGHTMARE!!!”
text:
My 6 year anniversary with my girlfriend was almost ruined by the mismanagement and employee inabilities at "THE BAY BRIDE INN!" We made reservations at hotels(-) at least five days prior to arrival in San Francisco. But when we showed up to the hotel an hour early we had no idea what we were going to be getting ourselves into. The employee at the desk told us that our room would not be availible until an hour from now, so he promptly gave us a map to the city and circled sights that we should see. We weren't in to much of a rush to check in so we agreed to come back later. 
 We had lunch at the Fisherman's Wharf and came back two hours later. The man at the desk than told us that are room isn't technically ready. He than explained that the room we had reserved was not availible and that the guest who was supposed to check out chose to stay an extra night. The hotel gave him our room even though we had reserved it. The hotel than said that they had a smokin room availible (we asked for a non-smoking room) and that we should look at it. We walked in to find the room still in disaray, the bed looked like it had just been slept in, everything was disorganized, and there was a pungent smell coming from a dehumidifier plugged in at the corner of the room. We were enraged! Going back down to the check-in desk the employee than told us that was the only room they had and that it should be ok if we just left the dehumidifier on. THERE WAS NO WAY WE WERE STAYING THERE!!! He than said there was nothing that he could do and that's the only room they had and that his nose is sensitive and he didn't have an issue with the smell.
 After consoling my girlfriend we went to our car, we didn't know what to do, we had to make it to a show in about two hours and we don't have an acceptable room to stay in. After calling several hotels we found one "THE ADANTE" in Union Square. The whole time we were calling other hotels the family owner's of the Bay Bridge were stairing at us while we were in the car. The employee was also walking back and forth around the hotel arguing with someone. During a call we made the employee knocked on our car window to tell us he had an idea. He had a friend who lived at the hotel who could move out of his room and give us his for the night until another room becomes availible. He would move his friend's stuff out himself to the 'Smoking Room' and just tell his friend when he comes in that we were staying in his; there was no way!
 We made our reservations at "The Adante" and all we had to do was get a refund from this nightmare. Per our hotels(-) reservation for a cancelation we would be charged a $25 fee to cancel our reservations before 6PM. It was 4PM, when we went back in to talk with the employee again he said he would not give us our refund. He would have to charge us for a full night's stay and than give us back our money for the next two nights. We told him that he could not charge us according to the agreement with hotels(-) that per the paperwork there would only be a $25 charge. He argued with us saying that we were wrong and that he was trying to help us. We told him that we were calling hotels(-) about the situation. He than prompted to try to call them first so we would not be able to get all our money back!!! After what seemed liked hours everything was settled and hotels(-) fixed everything for us by not only giving us a full refund but not charging us a cancelation fee.
 For all you travelers I highly suggest you pay that extra fee to stay somewhere a little bit more expensive. You don't want an experience like the one we had. You won't want your room given to someone else, or realize that the only place you have to stay is somewhere with dirty bed sheets, and an odor of disenffetant that's trying to cover something the owners don't want you to smell. "THE ADANTE" was affordable, we checked in between an hour of when we called, it was close to everything we needed to go to, the rooms were a little small but they were great, the bathrooms were large, people were nice, and not to mention we got a card that gave us two free draft beers at the 24fps bar each night we stayed. Trust me, you shouldn't go through something like this during a time that's supposed to be a "vacation" a "celebration."

title: “Not up to usually Marriott quality”
text:
Stayed at the Residence Inn San Diego Mission Valley for 4 nights on 7/24. It was during the Comic Con convention and the hotel was packed. The location is close to freeway. Parking is secured but costs $13 per day. Check in was quick and room was available for early arrival. The one-bedroom suite was booked for 5 people but only 3 sets of towels were in the room. The suite was clean but the kitchen cabinets need intensive cleaning. 
Breakfast buffet was OK but the food area needs to clean up periodically especially when feeding so many people. Dine early as they sometimes run out of food choices. Even though everything is self service, the dining room tables need to be wiped down when someone finishes. There is a lack of service inside and outside dining area. Well after service is finished, dropped food can still be visible on the carpets or floors. One evening, a hotel guest bought in 5 or more boxes of pizza to be eaten around the pool area. The next morning, the empty pizza boxes were still sitting on tables around the pool area. 
Being a Marriott Elite member, I expect high quality and this hotel was well below average.

title: “I should have said something”
text: OK... I should have said something when checking out, but I wasn't 100% sure and I had checked out quite early. Both arms...BOTH ARMS...bitten by BED BUGS! I am not making this up and otherwise the hotel is OK. I know it's not a fancy hotel...it's a little aged and quite cute...but one cannot excuse the infestation of bed bugs. Stayer beware!

title: “UNSAFE DANGEROUS -- DO NOT LET $$ BE YOUR MOTIVATOR”
text: I have read countless reviews stating that they stayed here and would recommend it because of the "value, " even though there were "weird people, beggars, gangsters, and a guy that was just released from prison here that was staying here." Please do not mislead people. Yes, it's cheap, but this place can cost your life. Just today, a paramedic came on a call here, and just walking up the stairs, two men casually strolled pass him and stabbed him multiple times. Thankfully, the wounds did not puncture vital organs but if he did not received immediate attention, it would have been a close call for him. He's currently under observation at the hospital now. My friends are firemen and have to come on calls here all the time because of drug addicts who stay here and now the motel have recently been more infested with gang bangers, looking to make a name for themselves. DO NOT STAY HERE, EVEN IF IT'S CHEAP!! This is downtown LA and it's cheap for a reason!! The bathroom is even down the hall and not in your room! Come on people---Please don't give these criminals a target for senseless acts of violence. STAY AWAY!!!

title: “Expensive and small...”
text: The cleanliness of the hotel was good, there's no complaints there but our room was very small. We took our 1 year old daughter with us so once the cot was in it was even smaller. A huge disappointment was there was no kettle!!! We were relying on one to warm our baby's milk and food plus it would of been nice not to have to go out everytime we wanted a drink. This is the first Hotel we have stopped in that hadn't one. Had we of been told that the hotel was not really suitable for children we would of certainly found a more suitable one. We paid alot of money and feel we got little/no value for money....

title: “Never Again”
text:
We stayed here whilst on a shopping trip, overall opinion is over priced and over rated, our room was small but we didnt spend much time in it so that wasnt much of a problem, but it was very dated and the heating system was very noisy.
A couple of occassion we where not allowed to use the front entrance because of special events taking place and had to come in through the back and on one occassion we were not allowed to use the main lift because of an office party on the 18th floor, guests took second place over functions. 
We complained about our stay and we were offered an apology and was told we'd get a suite for the price of a standard room the next time we stayed and the confirmation would be emailed to us, still waiting although we wouldnt use it anyway I'd never return to this hotel.

title: “House of Mouse”
text:
I checked in on July 18 and was scheduled to stay in the hotel until July 23. I reserved a room with 2 beds and when I checked in they gave me a room with one bed. I went to the desk and asked to be moved into a room with 2 beds which they did. They gave me a room with 2 beds on the 10th floor. The room was really warm when I arrived and it did not get any better. It was around 80 when I checked in and around 78 when I woke up in the morning. I complained about the room temperature and also about the mini bar. I was hot and wanted something to drink shortly after I checked in and the bottle of lemonade that I selected in my mini bar was open with probably an eighth of the bottle already consumed. Needless to say, I did not eat or drink anything from the mini bar.
The desk staff said that they would take care of things. The next night it was still hot in the room around 79 or 80 and then I thought I saw a mouse. I dismissed it until I definitely saw a mouse run across the floor. I called the front desk and asked to move. They said they were full and couldn't move me until the next night. So, I called some friends and crashed with them. The front desk staff were nice, but the hotel is really pretty dodgy. I think the staff are aware of that and there is not much that can be done. I would never stay here again and I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Excellent value in a great location”
text:
The Four Points isn't going to win any chic-boutique hotel awards or pamper you with posh hotel amenities. What it offers is an excellent value (particularly my winning Priceline bid) in a prime location.
The hotel is located at the corner of Rush and Ontario, a block from the Magnificent Mile (the N. Michigan Ave. shopping district for the uninitiated). It's got a pleasant, calm lobby with a mellow, friendly vibe. Every employee you come into contact with is exceptionally friendly.
Check-in was swift and gregarious. My room - a comfy king single - was basic in decor, but generously sized. It featured a couch and table in addition to the workdesk, and also had a microwave and mini-fridge. The bathroom was also basic, but comfortably sized with plenty of good towels. The bed was comfortable, though I'm not wild about the down feather pillows.
I didn't take advantage of the breakfast or the attached restaurant (not in restaurant-laden Chicago). Numerous dining spots, including Lawry's Prime Rib the Grand Luxe Cafe, are nearby. (Though I prefer dining at Chicago's independent neighborhood restaurants, rather than the ersatz-chainy downtown scene).
The hotel also offers free internet access in the rooms, and a complimentary business center on the 4th floor. A pool and fitness center is on the 5th floor.
The hotel's location, again, is excellent for vacationers. For transit purposes, it's a short block to the many bus lines that roll up and down Michigan Ave., and a couple of blocks from the Grand/State Red Line El stop.
My only gripes were that the rooms could use a bit of freshening up (carpets, showers etc) and the slow elevators. But for the price, it's tough to find a whole lot to gripe about. If you can live with paper cups rather than glasses in the room, and won't die because the in-room bath products aren't from L'Occitane, you'll have a fine time at the Four Points.

title: “Typical marriott hotel”
text: Boutique like hotel close to the top of nob hill. Stayed in room 333 on the third floor. This was an upgrade that we were given at no charge. Probably since we are a Marriott Elite card member. It was a fairly large room compared to others we saw. Had two large windows, could see a decent view of the city. Still a lower floor than would be ideally desireable. The issue is if you have trouble sleeping. It is very noisy. I would say if you are a light sleeper then either request a high floor room, 6 th or up, or get a room facing the courtyard ( which has no view ). The cable cars run until 1 or 2 in the morning and start back up at 4-5 am. The noise is loud, bells etc. Otherwise, if you are a heavy sleeper, then it is a decent room as we were happy with it. We were able to check in early, like 11 am, so if you get in early dont hesitate to check in and see if your room is available. We had access to the club room, nice atmosphere views, snacks/food good. Had to pay for alcohol though. Concierge, excellent! Very helpful. Restaurant pricey, better choice outside hotel. Best advice overall, do alot of research at home ahead of your trip, if not youll end up wasting alot of time wandering around town and missing out. We took a bus tour on the first day which was helpfull and i would recommend doing the first day. Wine tour to napa, definately do if you have time it was worth it. Lastly, watch out for the homeless people that are everywhere. We saw a mugging on the cable car! The homeless are very aggressive and is one of the complaints i had with the city. Where are all the police? We saw two police cars the entire trip! No police walking around, no police on bikes? Amazing....also, i think the homeless people are unionized, believe it or not!

title: “Impressive, but they missed the little things”
text: The Hotel lobby was lovely, the staff attentive, the concierge were pleasant and always available. The room was comfortable; we had an Edwardian suite and it was roomy and the bedding comfortable. However, the bathroom doors were glass and there was no way to block the light from the bedroom. Since I am an early riser and my husband sleeps in, this arrangement was not to our liking. We had to call down for a room service menu, the birthday cake my husband ordered did not show up on time, we were missing a remote control, there was no coffee station in the room (forcing you to call for room service). Of course the location is fabulous, and I really liked their running station (a cart in the morning with fruit, water, and running routes). It was a pleasant experience, but we will try a different hotel next time.

title: “From Yoga to Art and Soul”
text: We had an absolutely wonderful stay - from morning yoga on the rooftop to an amazing southern nosh at Art and Soul, we absolutely loved our stay at the Liaison!

title: “So very very nice!”
text: Beautiful rooms 3815/3814 with views everywhere! Friendly and helpful front desk staff (thanks Christina!). Breakfast overlooking central park with excellent waiters and food. Room service made soup to order for our 11 year old. You can't go wrong here. Near all the shopping. It's where you want to stay and be pampered!

title: “What a rip off!!!”
text:
We got a room here on a very busy weekend so I guess I am to be happy to have had a room. The problem is it was just a room with a bed...as in the room was a bed. Literally you opened the door and the bed was right there. You could not cuss a cat in that room. Then we turned on the a/c and went out for a couple of hours only to return to a hot room. Guess a/c is not an option in November even if it was a warm day. Fortunately the window opened so we slept with it up all night. Then there was the noise of all the doors slamming and chatter during all hours of the night. Bathroom had no tub and was equally small with no counter space.
Lobby is a postage stamp. Two elevators for 18 floors so you often have to wait. worst part is we paid over $400 for this misery. Fortunately it was only for one night. Would never deign to stay there again, even though the location is a nice one of the quiet edge of the Mag Mile.

title: “Amazing Resort!”
text: Weekend to celebrate our anniversary and my birthday!!! What a great choice my husband made. The hotel is first class all the way, the rooms, the dining, the ambiance... we loved it.

title: “Great Value!”
text: At first, we have to say thank you to the front desk staff, think this is the best on the hotel as they are all amazing. The rooms are clean and spacious for NY terms enough for 2 people to open their suitcases and leave them on the floor..:-) The breakfast is not perfect, not that much to offer, but fine if you just stay 2 nights. I like the Chelsea Flower area and it is a good spot to expore the city as it is right in the middle. Subway lines are all 1-2 blocks away and you will always get a Taxi. Walking distance to Macy's. Great thing to mention as well, hotel has free Wifi. UNfortunately, the roof top bar were closed (in renovation) when we were there, but just heard good things about it.

title: “Great for the price”
text: This hotel had a great location, it was a block from the riverwalk and less than that from La Villita. It had a nice continental breakfast, but it is served right in the hotel lobby, so there is limited space and it can get pretty congested. Our room was on the road side, and traffic had been detoured down that road, so the vehicle traffic was pretty loud. The rooms are fairly small, but nice and clean. And again, the location was great, especially being that it is one of the most reasonably priced hotels in the area. They kept our luggage locked in the back room for us on the day that we checked out so that we could wander down around the riverwalk until it was time for us to catch our cab and leave. We were quite happy with the service. They did however charge $10/day for parking (we didn't have a vehicle so it didn't matter for us), but something to know so you don't get surprised.

title: “One night stay”
text:
We had a total of 5 rooms booked for one night - had to travel for a relative's funeral. I must say that the hotel staff were extrememly friendly and accomodating. The rooms were spacious and clean and the price was very reasonable. If we happen to be in the area, I would definitely stay again - 
One comment on the area - the restaurants next door are quite noisy at bar time, so might be best to not be on the North side of the hotel!

title: “Perfect bargain for the family”
text:
We stayed in rooms 611 and 612, in the 6B corner of the hotel for a week. The mini bars were actually affordable which is a real boon if you're travelling with children and teens. Also, there is a Whole Foods Market about 10 minutes away to fill up the fridge with healthy snacks and fruit.
We were near everything in Union Square. While we quickly discovered not to walk down Jones Street for any reason (except for Dottie's True Blue Cafe) because of the large numbers of assertive/aggressive homeless people, walking down Post to go to Powell was never a problem. 
If you tire of taking cabs everywhere, there is a bus that runs down Powell as well - the staff is very helpful with travel tips.
611 was the suite with two queen beds, full kitchen (fridge, freezer, microwave, coffeemaker, pots, plates, pans), bidet, and whirlpool bath - a delight. 612 had a single double bed and simple bathroom - none of the extras of 611, but he combination of the two rooms in 6B was PERFECT for our family. We left the doors to 611 and 612 open and closed the door to 6B.
The rooms were very clean. Because we have dust mite allergies in our family, it is imperative that all sheets be washed in super hot water. Even though the hotel did not have hypoallergenic pillows, no one had any allergy attacks because the sheets were sterile.
The hotel was lovely and quiet and the rooms were large - apparently a rarity in SF hotels. 
The morning coffee, fruit and donut situation was lovely, although the coffee was pretty weak (along with everywhere in SF but Starbucks). The evening wine with cheese and dates was nice as well, particularly if you have time before dinner. The hotel attracts a lot of European guests and these communal times were genuinely friendly.
The daytime staff were kind and well informed with information about bonded babysitters should you need, as well as fairly thorough information about the city at large. The evening staff was not as well informed, but still kind.
I would recommend this hotel to anyone who doesn't want to pay top dollar to stay at one of the finer hotels but still wants a nice room and good service.

title: “Excellent very well positioned Georgetown hotel”
text:
I stayed here with my 17yo daughter for a week at the end of October including 2 days hunkered down during Hurricane Sandy
Excellent hotel which handled the Hurricane superbly
Tip-join the Presidents Club on checking in which is free and gives you free internet in the room,free gym and other benefits
Superb Breakfasts-we did bed and breakfast
Price good-far cheaper than nearby Four Seasons
Excellent Concierge Desk very helpful with restraunys etc
Tip-get metro plastic travel card to save moeny and use on metro and all buses

title: “Great!”
