text: The Fairmont was a beautiful hotel. The lobby was stunning and our conjoining rooms were very clean and pleasant. It was very nice and the staff were very friendly. The only thing was if you want to use WiFi you had to pay $13.95. Apart from that everything was fantastic.b

title: “Lovely hotel, such big rooms!”
text: We stayed here from 29 Nov to 2 Dec and were delighted with the hotel. We were booked into one of their suites and it was HUGE! twin double beds in the bedroom along with tv with cable, 3 walk in wardrobes, huge living room with tv & cable, small kitchenette with pots pans and utensils etc. The suite was gorgeous, we were so delighted. staff very friendly too. the location uptown was great in that it was quite quiet but was a $20 taxi ride to downtown Manhattan. We didnt mind but could work out pretty pricey depending on what you are doing in town. Lots of cafes and restaurants nearby. the cafe attached to the hotel was great, lovely breakfast and superfast room service! Would definitely consider staying here again on our next trip.

title: “Excellent for the traveller on a budget.”
text: I am about to finish a very comfortable, friendly and enjoyable stay here. The hostel is clean and has a nice atmosphere, everyone is very friendly and helpful, both staff and the other guests, but I realise that the latter is luck of the draw! No meals are provided but there is a supermarket down the road and a great guy who sells all manner of fruit on the corner of Union Square. The transport links are great, with a subway station on that same corner ( roughly 3 minutes' walk) with connections to most of Manhattan available, and certainly all the major tourist sites. Only issue is that the window in my room didn't completely shut, but this was by millimetres, I was on the 3rd floor and noise wasn't a huge issue. I would definitely stay here if I were to return to New York in the future.

title: “Great Location”
text:
My husband and I stayed here in late August 2011, and had a great experience. The hotel is really clean, and they have a great staff. Our room was super quiet, which was great for a light sleeper like me :) The location is fun and funky, and the surrounding area was filled with flower dealers......flowers, trees and little patches of grass everywhere! The only downside was the "view" from our window......rusty pipes and grunge. But hey---that's not really the hotels fault, and besides, we weren't there to look out of the windows all day, so....
I'd recommend it as a good choice in the area!

title: “Excellent Stay”
text:
We checked in and everything was perfect from the start.
Yarnell at the front desk was corteous, kind and extremely helpful. Everything and everyone starting with check in and ending at checkout was the ultimate in professionalism.
We walked to Georgetown (even though it was cold, it was very pleasant) and also walked to the metro for other activities.
The hotel was super comfortable, even my daughter's rollaway was incredibly comfortable...Loved all of the White Tea scented toiletries!
Will definitely stay again!
Thank you all for a great stay.

title: “Enjoyable and Fun”
text: We stayed here recently for the first time with a group of friends and found the place to be exactly as described and then some. Our unit, No. 11, was great except for the fact the electrical outlets in the bedroom did not work. Other than that everything was great and we loved the atmosphere most of all. We had a pot luck dinner so it was handy to have a little kitchen complete with everything we needed to cook. The Bedroom is on the small side and all beds are queens but it was very comfortable and the sound of the ocean made for a great night of sleep. We have aleady made plans to return and would recommend this for anyone wanting a beach experience. Would not choose it for my honeymoon but definitely for a great weekend getaway. Do make sure to get an email confirmation we did not and found out later we almost lost our reservatioon since paperwork was not processed.

title: “Excellent for families and great value”
text: We stayed three nights at the Magic Castle Hotel and loved it. The staff were all very nice and helpful. The apartments were very spacious and had everything we needed. They are a little old around the edges but we didn't even care as the service, location and facilities were excellent. The swimming pool is heated and there's a laundry! There are also free snacks and drinks and a free breakfast! Unbelievable value in a brilliant location! If we're ever back in LA we will definitely stay here again. The kids have both compared every other hotel since then to the Magic Castle Hotel and found them wanting.

title: “Over priced and unfriendly. Very dark hallways.”
text: The W Hotel is very expensive for what it offers. The hall ways were dark and it was difficult to see the room numbers. The Staff was not very friendly.

title: “Brilliant - Hotel Grand Union NYC”
text:
Having previuosly stayed in New York i was not expecting much as standard in New York for hotels seem to be far less than if you stayed anywhere else in the US. But i was pleasantly suprised.
The hotel was great, great location, staff friendly and room cleaned daily.
The room was basic but clean. We stayed on the 9th floor with no view but then not many rooms in New York has a view. Air conditioning in the room which was great as the temperature was 83 degrees!
Would definitely recomend this hotel and would definitely stay here again on another visit.
Cafe that seemed to adjoin the hotel was great not expensive at all and friendly staff. We used this restaurant / cafe for Breakfast on Saturday and Sunday morning.
Monday morning there was a great place to eat opposite. Absolutuely huge with a great selection. Sushi made to order, bacon & eggs and the price was ridculoulsy cheap.
So all in all great hotel with great surrounding facilities.

title: “Great hotel with nice little extras”
text:
This was my first stay at a Kimpton hotel, and I have to say I was pleased. We had a very late check in, so I was happy to have a speedy experience at the front desk. We ordered a quick bite with room service, which was a nice to have available so late at night, and it arrived quickly. We had a Monaco King room which was pretty spacious, with a desk area, lots of room, and a really comfortable bed. The only thing I wasn’t really crazy about was our shower had built in dispensers of shampoo and conditioner instead of individual bottles. They do, however, offer a handful of amenities at the front desk such as toothpaste and the like if you forget to pack them (some free, others for a fee). We had an issue with our mini fridge, and not only did they service it right away but they immediately brought a cold drink from the bar downstairs since what we wanted from the fridge wasn’t cold. At every encounter the staff was friendly and efficient. Ask for a goldfish, and your stay is complete! 
It is centrally located so you can walk to many attractions in the city. It’s extremely close to Pike Place Market, and you can walk down to the original Nordstrom. They have complimentary coffee in the morning, and I think a cocktail hour in the evenings? We booked the $1 breakfast, which was okay – for $1 it’s a perfectly fine continental breakfast, but don’t expect to be full. There’s actually a great little bakery across the street down a block by the Fairmont that I would recommend for excellent pastries like ham and cheese croissant, cinnamon buns, etc. I would stay here again, and will probably seek out their properties in other cities. I also recommend joining their loyalty club for some nice extra perks like free WiFi.

title: “Great value and great location”
text:
I stayed at the Melrose over the Memorial holiday. Based on some reviews I was a little nervous. I was looking for and got a great deal (especially for DC) on the hotel website...$88/nite for the king. Everyone I dealt with was nice and not over attentive.
The room was great (and they should buy some new pillows) but I was very comfortable. I had a chair w/ ottoman and a loveseat and refrigerator. It's not luxurious but a steal at the price. There was no problem with early check-in and they held my bags after check out. I did not eat at restaurant or drink at the bar. The bar looked comfortable though.
Great access to public transportation. Easy walk to Georgtown shopping and restaurants. Ask for nearby food stores for snacking.

title: “2nd Worst Hotel We've Stayed In! EVER!”
text:
Located on the Sunset Strip between a Strip Club and a public library with drunks sleeping on the sidewalk. The manager was rude, and obviously was the cause of of the hotels decline. 
At one point in time someone had made the attempt to remodel the hotel, but had never bothered to follow up with cleaning the rooms afterwards. The carpet was matted down and black with dirt and sticky to walk on (your feet or socks were black within minutes). The sheets were not changed during our stay, and we suspected they may not have been before we moved in. The towels were thin, and we received no hand towels, just facecloths and bath towels. The room wasn't serviced until almost 6pm.
The parking lot is cramped and has fewer spaces than rooms, we just parked and walked everywhere. We booked through Expedia and I'm not quite sure why they rated it a 2 Star hotel. I think someone cooked the books on this one. And I can't quite believe the review here that someone stayed 3 months in this hotel?!!?!!

title: “One day trip to LA”
text: I stayed in this hotel with my husband one night. We wanted something sheap in LA and not very far to Universal studio (3 miles) and Hollywod blvd. Hotel is pretty nice but everything is old. We stayed on a second flor so we didn't need elevator but it didn't work. I asked about room with view on Hollywood sign and they gave us the room with the best view on it. On reception they honestly told us that it will be little nousy because of close to the road. Honestly it was very noisy and when I tried to asleed during the day I couldn't. But I slept very good at night because I was very tired after walking and riding in Universal Studio. One of the key to the room doen't work. We have some problems with TV and lamp but they came and fix it.

title: “Revisit the 19th Century”
text: The Palmer house is an old, stately, ultra service hotel. All the service pople employed were extemely attentive, punctual, and informative. Great little lobby bar.The rooms are clean but the bathrooms are smaller because of the age of the hotel. We did not eat here but the menu looked passable.

title: “Decent hotel but not overly impressed”
text:
I was expecting a little more from this hotel taking that it is part of the Sheraton. The location is across from the Port Authority (bus terminal) and about 10blocks from Times Square. The location isn't completely bad however you do need to walk to get into Times Square. When checking in it was fast and the staff were friendly, although not as helpful as I have experienced other places. 
The room itself was clean, but it was kind of small which is fine. The bed was comfortable but the pillows were horrible! They were really soft and I believe it was feathered pillows (which I'm allergic to). I was to tired to even bother asking the front desk for something else. I did notice a couple of stains on the bed cover and on a towel, which I did not like..again taking it's Sheraton my expectations were higher. Other than that the rooms were clean and we were able to sleep okay. 
I don't know if I would stay here again as it was farther than I had expected and to pricey for what we got. There is a restaurant that sells hot dogs at the corner of 7th and 40th and it was absolutely delicious!

title: “Great location! Nice stay!”
text: I stayed at the Wingate for 6 nights, in the beginning of October. I don´t have any complains, really! I got there at 10 AM. There was a room available on the second floor, but, as I´ve asked for a higher floor when booking the hotel, they asked if I wanted to go for a walk and come back later. And so I did. I went back at 4.30 PM. My room was ready, and my luggage had been kept safe behind the counter. The room was nice (King room) , enough space, it had a fridge and microwave, safe, coffee machine ... actually, all I could have asked for at a hotel room, specially in NY. And breakfast, which was included, was also great - yogurt, waffles, bagel, corn flakes, coffee...remember, the hotel is in NY, and most of the hotels there don´t offer breakfast included in the price! And, if that all wasn´t already enough, the hotel has a great location - close to Penn Station, Herald Square, Macys. I will definetely stay there again, and I am already looking forward to it! (they also have a small exercise room)

title: “Never again!!!”
text: I am so not happy with this hotel. The first time I stayed there it was perfect! The second it was awful! I stayed here for a wedding for two nights and might I mention I was the make-up artist for this wedding as well as the bride's brothers girlfriend. Everything was beyond screwd up. They put us all in the different towers and when I checked in I had them fix that and put us all in the same room. It also took 40 min to check in. And then they stuck me in a room with no A/C. Might I mention I live in San Diego and i was only staying here for the ease of getting the bridal party ready. So I was stuck sleeping in 80 degree heat! When I called they said in the morning they would fix the room since they were booked and could not switch me rooms. In the morning they came in and decided to start fixing it at 9am and when I told them at 10am I would have the bridal party coming in and needed the A/C fixed. They told me it would take longer and we would be without A/C. So finally they switched me rooms. And Frita the person in charge didn't even want to comp the night stay let alone give me a discount on the room. So finally they changed me rooms. I had to go down for the keys and I had to move my own luggage since the bell hop never made it up with my keys or to move my stuff. I will not recommend this hotel to anyone!!! Please dont stay here let alone block rooms for an event.

title: “A great find.”
text: Originally booked courtyard times sq, but they were full so transferred us here- 1 min walk. What a piece of good luck! Got an upgrade to a queen suit- which was excellent. Big bed, LCD tv, fridge/freezer/microwave/coffee maker. Just like a kitchen in your room (but no proper oven) ..but fine for the self catering tourist. Good location very close to Bryant park, acceptable for times sq, ESB and other mid-town stuff. Close to subway too. This is a new hotel so is clean and has a nice interior, including a waterfall in the foyer. Staff were very polite and helpful. Breakfast was free for me- if you can get this- take it..eat all you want, but may get busy (although it was labor weekend when i was there). There is a small bar overlooking 6th ave, they have a nice pool table. 4 nights cost 895usd, but this is cheaper than usual for the queen suit which is about 300usd per night. Expensive I know but shop around and see if you can get the same for less. Check out the official website- tells you all you need, and it's correct!

title: “left immediately after seeing the room”
text:
Got the place through the SWA website as the closest to Universal Studios. We checked in room 122 and noticed that the very old and dirty carpet has not been even vacuumed (looked like crumbs left over). The towels in the bathrooms had stains, yellow and reddish that seems were left over from the wash. The spredsheet/blanket were smelly. The sheets seemed clean. The mattress did not feel very comfortable either, soft spot in the middle. There was the typical smell of smoke even though the whole place is supposedly non-smoking. The air conditioner was missing the control knob to adjust the temperature. The single-pane window had smelly, old looking drapes, and it looked onto the side of the building where one of the workers just came down the stairs and dumped two black garbage bags. When I opened the window, it was stinking out there. 
Went out to the front desk and told them about the room condition and asked for a refund. Their answer was "no refunds"
We were very disappointed, just left and went elsewhere for the night. From their website it looks like a nice place, don't be fooled. The WORST place I have seen in years of world wide travel

title: “Exceptional & awesome experience here. Don't miss out on a chance to stay in this historical hotel!”
text: From beginning to end, a great place to stay. The staff is attentive to every detail & you will love the ambiance of the lobby and the rooms. So close to convention center, and restaurants, even the 7-11 was a treat to have close by! Enjoy!

title: “Lots of History and Great Location”
text: Fine and historic hotel in one of the best locations in the city. Ownership has really done everything to preserve the best of the past. Management really strives to supply the services one would expect today. Great staff. We stayed on the weekend for leisure and would definately stay again. Thank You.

title: “Good value for staying close to the airport”
text:
The pros:
-Hotel is a excellent value.
-Close to the airport, so very convenient.
-Quiet and clean
-Spacious rooms
-Staff is super nice and helpful.
-Great complimentary breakfast in the morning.
The cons:
-Far from everything else - but the airport.
- Not much dining options close by.
 -Gym center is small and not inviting.

title: “Never again”
text: Will never stay here again place gets worse the more you look around. Smells mouldy power socks don't have covers just to name a few issue. At least the wifi works..... I won't stay here again and lt leaves a sour feeling about Super 8 in general

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
A stellar example fo the Westin Brand. Can be a little difficult on the second floor with check in - not really a special line for SPG gold and platinum...
Rooms are awesome - especially corner, junior suites...beautiful locations and incredible views.
Being attached to Copley only adds to the charm and the ability to shop, have great sushi or chowder and get a feel for the Boston locals.
Right off the Green Line of the "T" - transportation ANYWHERE in the city is ideal.
If you are driving, the property is easily accessible off the Mass Pike and 95. Easy Easy Easy.
Rooms get pricey, really pricey - got hit with some $400/night rooms mid summer - guess Boston is a HOT destination...but I didn't want to stay down by the waterfront in "convention land".
No complaints, interested to see if they will do any "updating" or "facelifting"?

title: “Sweeping views”
text: We stayed at the Marriott for two nights prior to taking a cruise. This is a twin town convention hotel located right on the harbor and across from the convention center. But, because there were no conventions in town, the place was empty. We had a lovely harbor view room on the17th floor with a nice little baloney and gorgeous sunsets. The room was newly renovated with all of the Marriott technology, very clean and attractive. Like all Marriotts' a pretty safe choice. Only problem was, because the hotel was so empty, there were limited restaurants and bars open, but that was not a big problem. We plan to stay again when we return from our cruise.

title: “The hotel needs to be more concerned about security.”
text: While there were a lot of great aspects about this hotel, I did not feel very safe there at all and checked out early. Twice I saw people come off the street, walk in the main doors and help themselves to the free food that was out for breakfast/ dinner. They then went back outside and kept walking - obviously not guests. The hotel needs to pay more attention to guest safety.

title: “OK, But Not Fabulous Hill Country Resort”
text:
Hyatt Wild Oak Ranch is a Hyatt Vacation Club property that also rents rooms by the night. We were there for two nights because we had received an invitation for a cheap package if we did the timeshare tour. It was a very good value deal.
However, I can't say I really recommend this place. It is not a country resort at all because it is located in the San Antonio suburbs, close to Seaworld. 
When we checked in, the receptionist asked us which floor would we like to be on. We asked what he recommended and he said that the 1st floor was convenient but the 3rd floor had the best views. We chose the 3rd floor. The first room we went to had stunning views over - the parking lot! So we changed rooms and then got a stunning view of the suburbs and the freeway (and boy was that freeway noisy). Please see my pictures. I would suggest you stay on the 1st floor where you overlook landscaping and trees and thus can maintain the illusion that you are in the country.
I can't say I was overly impressed with our studio room. There was a nice big bathroom which could have easily accommodated a big tub, but the tub was narrow and shallow. The bed was one of the most uncomfortable I have slept on in a long time - surprising for a high end chain. On our tour we saw the 1 and 2 bedroom apartments and they were much better appointed, with full kitchens, big flatscreen TV, whirlpool bath and separate walk in shower. I would suggest staying in one of those instead.
The rooms are located in 3 story blocks that look like cheap apartment buildings with a lot of unfinished steel and corrugated steel balcony partitions. It's just not very pretty.
There is a heated indoor/outdoor pool with water slides and an unheated lazy river with a beach and surrounded by hammocks. That was fun and would definitely be good for kids. The kids will also like the gamesroom with its arcade games (but which you have to pay for - a bit cheap for a vacation resort). I also liked the firepit area where there are several wood burning pits which the staff will light for you. For golfers, the resort has its own golf course.
Being a timeshare resort, it doesn't have the bar/restaurant amenities that you would find at a regular resort. There is a smokehouse restaurant that is open for lunch and until 7, that serves perfectly acceptable comfort food. There is also a shop that sells basic food items for your room. There is an actual Hyatt Hotel Resort located about a mile away where you can go for full service dining.
We visited this nearby Hyatt hotel to see how it compared and it is a lot prettier. Also, it has been built in a dip, rather than up on a hill, so you cannot see the suburbs and freeway. I think it is unlikely I would return to Wild Oak, even with a cheap deal, but I can imagine returning to the hotel sometime in the future.
On our final night we went to eat at Grey Moss Inn which is in the village of Grey Forest, about a 25 minute drive into the country. The atmosphere, food, wine list and service was excellent. When you pull into the parking lot and all these little deer scatter off, you are already charmed!

title: “The "No Worries Stay"”
text:
I spent a very nice week at the Four Points recently. I was pleasantly surprised with a welcoming plate of fruit and outstanding "home baked" cookies (well they tasted like home baked cookies anyway!). 
Despite being able to watch the flights landing at LAX, with the windows closed, I did not hear them day or night. 
My room was always ready when I got back, even if I arrived back to work at lunch time. The pillows were to die for - I usually have to plump and rearrange them to get to sleep - not these - wish I could have brought them home with me! 
There was always 2 bottles of water left for me daily if I desired. Fresh fruit in the lobby was available most of the day. Free wireless internet was a breeze to use and plenty of bandwidth for my needs.
The bar had a most excellent selection of over 100 various beers from around the world. Who would have thought I could get Lowenbrau Dunkel in LA?? The Fish Tacos were excellent - I know, you're thinking "Fish Tacos"?? I did too but a friend had them the night before and wanted them again, so I said - "Sure" and was just amazed at their taste. The mango accompaniment was a perfect addition.
Will I be back - you can bet on it!! Thanks to all the folks who made my stay comfortable and worry-free!!

title: “Lovely hotel, infuriating internet”
text:
This is a really lovely "old money" hotel. The service was really exceptional, even the bellmen holding the doors were extremely polite without being overzealous. My room was LARGE, especially for an old hotel, although I was on the end of a block so I'm not sure if all them are so big. Had I brought my family, there would have been space for a crib AND a rollaway bed, plus all the luggage, etc. Very clean, too. Another nice surprise was the room service. I tend to order it when on business since I work in my room a lot (and don't enjoy sitting at the bar with other lonely solo travelers). One evening I had already eaten while walking around the city so just wanted something light when I got back, so I ordered an appetizer salad and slice of cake. The salad turned out to be meal size, and included rolls with a goat cheese spread(!) The cake was so large I saved half of it for the next night. It isn't often room service surprises you with more than you can eat. It was delicious too. Oh and speaking of walking around, the location is really nice. Four blocks from the waterfront, five or six blocks from the monorail. Easily walkable to most of the sights.
So why not five stars, you ask? Well, the wi-fi made my work almost impossible. They offer two options- standard access for $15/day, which already seems pricey to me, or "premium" for $25/day. Standard was included in my company rate, so I connected the first night and found myself having to manually disconnect and reconnect about every 10-15 mins or so. The next night I went for premium, which was marginally faster but crashed with the same frequency. The third night I used my dicey air card, which was a vast improvement. Save yourself some money and avoid it altogether if you are vacationing and/or don't need to send & receive docs.

title: “An absolute gem!!”
text: I stayed here with my family (wife and two kids both under 5) during a business trip. The hotel staff made our stay an absolute delight. From the minute we got there they made us feel at home and were so great with my kids. The food was great, the bar was comfy, and the rooms spectacular. I would stay here again in a heartbeat! Thank you Four Seasons!

title: “Delight in Denver”
text:
We had a great stay in the Four Seasons.
==Rooms==
The decoration was lovely, and the room was well equipped. We liked the nespresso coffee machines & TV in the bathroom mirror. The bed was comfortable, and we found the rooms to be very spacious.
For a modern hotel, the soundproofing could have been better. We could hear the nocturnal activities of several other guests in our room. It also seemed as though some people were having a party, and the noise from that travelled far.
==Staff==
From start to finish, we found the staff to be wonderfully attentive. Everyone, from the room service waiter to reception staff and valets were polite, enthusiastic and attuned to our needs. This was excellent. 
==Valet parking==
I don't stay in north american hotels often, so this may be relatively standard. However, $30 seemed steep for overnight valet parking. There are cheaper car parks nearby.
==Wi-fi internet access==
This is a personal bugbear, but I resent having to pay for wi-fi access in a luxury hotel. I didn't - there are shops/cafes nearby where you can get it for free. It seems a shame that it isn't included in the cost of the room. This is especially true when the room is much more expensive than mid-range hotels and hostels where wi-fi often is available, or at the least which have a free internet connection.
==Overall==
This is a fantastic hotel in the heart of downtown Denver. If you don't mind the extra charges, it's a lovely place to relax and see the city.

title: “Very Enjoyable Stay”
text: I chose this hotel based on price and Tripadvisor reviews and I was not disappointed! The location is perfect for exploring Chinatown and Little Italy, and the staff was ultra-friendly and helpful. Breakfast was very generous. I've stayed at Comfort Inns before and have always had a nice experience and this stay was just as enjoyable. I very much appreciated having a view of the bridge and what seems to be a community center where festivities were taking place with fun sounds and music. Safety was never an issue - I felt perfectly comfortable walking around in the evenings. I would've loved to have stayed longer to explore Chinatown and eat more dim-sum, but I had to move to Times Square to be closer to work meetings there.

title: “Excellent Service and Atmosphere”
text:
Arrived fairly late to the hotel (restaurant and room service were already closed), and the front desk staff were very courteous with the check-in and also suggested a couple of near-by restaurants. They also offered the use of the hotel driver to take us, since we were unfamiliar with the city. Although we didn't use the service, I really appreciated that it was offered so readily.
Room was very nice and I would definitely stay there again and I recommend it to anyone travelling to San Antonio.

title: “Watch your credit card!”
text: We were charged for a night that we didn't stay at this B&B!!! When we approached management to get a refund they were incredibly rude and unwilling to help us in any way. I would never recommend this B&B, simply because of the poor management.

title: “Good location, pricey for what you get”
text: Wy wife and I recently spent 3 nights at the Tuscan Inn at the start of a two week tour of California. We got off to a bad start as, despite having pre-booked a non-smoking king room weeks in advance, we arrived at around 4pm to hear that no non-smoking rooms were available. The smoking room we were allocated reeked. The only compensation we received was a cheap, complimentary continental breakfast. At least we were transferred to a non-smoking room for the rest of our stay, but the room was rather small with no view whatsoever. It was clean and quiet, though, and the bed was comfortable. The hotel restaurant was pleasantly bustling and the food was good, although pricey, as was the accommodation. I guess you pay for the location - the hotel is within a few minutes walk of all the Fisherman's Wharf attractions which is a boon.

title: “Great Value”
text: We were pleasantly surprised with the Belvedere. The price was great, our room was clean, the staff was friendly and accommodating and the location was perfect.

title: “Wonderful stay”
text: Most comfortable beds. Beautiful, sparkling clean room. Great service. We got a super price so took advantage of a $40 per night upgrade for our 3 nights stay and got the most spectacular corner panoramic view that we hated to leave the room. Lake Michigan, The Wrigley Building, Navy Pier all at a glance and fireworks at night. Wonderful stay. We'll do it again.

title: “Thins walls, older decor..”
text: This hotel is in a older building across the street from the Seattle Public Library. There is a Seattle's Best Coffee shop inside the hotel which is great. The staff are pleasant and very helpful. Unfortunately that isn't the issue. We stayed here Saturday night in a Queen Room. The walls are so think I could hear someone next door coughing every 2-3 minutes. Then the person on the other side of us came in from a night on the town very loud and drunk. Coughing on one side, talking on the other..needless to say we couldn't get to sleep. In fairness, I don't think the people talking were talking that loud but it was still very annoying. We called the front desk and they graciously moved us to another room at 1 a.m. This room was a King and much nicer than the queen. I would only stay here again if I had a King room and asked for a corner unit. The decor has been updated but you can see that they only upgraded the essentials. The bathroom in the Queen was small and cramped.

title: “Very helpful staff, great location”
text: A good hotel that did not seem overly expensive. Great staff supplied useful jogging maps, booked tickets (including getting A1tickets to wicked). Room was very nice. Only short coming was a group of boys enjoying the moment in the room next door on 1 night. Linen is very white an quite impecable. (A la the Delano in Miami) which adds to the comfort. Wireless internet could have been free (like most other places we stay in the world), Asia d Cuba is right up there. We are vegetarian and I can truthfully say this is the very best fare. (Asia d Cuba in London is as good)

title: “Beautiful hotel, great staff, great location”
text:
We were visiting our son who is studying for a semester in LA for 4 nights. We had a beautiful large, very clean, king room with 20 feet of windows looking out on to the Hollywood Hills, it was a fantastic view. The staff at the front desk were very friendly and eager to answer any question we had. The location is a quick walk to Universal Studios and City Walk where there is a variety of food options. It is also a short distance (although LA traffic is a nightmare) to all major attractions.
The parking rate is high but seems to be the norm in the areas we visited in Southern California, so just be resigned to fact there is not much you can do about it.
My husband and I are both in the hospitality business and it is very refreshing to go on vacation and receive the quality of customer care that we give while doing our jobs. The staff at the Universal Hilton was a delight.

title: “very clean”
text:
I visit Jacksonville about 4-5 times a year and this was my first stay at the Courtyard. I was traveling with a business assosciate and we both thought the hotel was perfect for our needs. I stayed in room 106. Had a nice king size bed, flat screen TV and beautiful furnishings. I am not sure of age of this hotel but it looked brand new. 
Good job Courtyard. Ill be back.

title: “Excellent experience”
text: Thanks to the whole staff for making our week long business meeting a great experience. Rooms are great. Service is great. Location is great. Awesome personalized attention. Highly recommend this to anyone going to SATX!

title: “Best Deal in NYC”
text: The best location, best price and perfect setup at a great price. Steps to Broadway,Central Park and Rockefeller Center. Comfortable bed and surpisingly relaxed room. Vana at the front was always there to welcome us with a smile and a laugh. Would recommend this for sure.

title: “Standard Business Hotel at the Foot of Shopping Area”
text:
Standard Sheraton in a great location for shoppers and 5 minute walk to Pikes Place Marketplace. 
Hotel Experience: 4 stars, out of 5
Hotel Class: 4 stars, out of 5
Service: 5 stars, out of 5
Room: Room on the Sheraton Club Floor
Pros: 
- Service: Very courteous and helpful staff, Nice upgrade to room with a view of the city.
- Location: 5 minute walk to Pikes Place/Shopping Areas, Close to good restaurants
Cons: 
- Table Lamp: Need to replace bulbs
Notes:
- Parking: Hotel Valet Parking was $40/night. Convention Center Parking might been $20 cheaper than hotel valet. "7th & Pike" Garage (Between Pike and Pine) was $28/night with in&out privileges if you get a hotel pass provided by the Sheraton parking attendant in front of the hotel (garage is a block away)
- Internet in room use: $10.95/day

title: “Trendy, Clean & so different”
text: We stayed there on April break and loved it. The staff was so helpful with any questions we had. It's in a great location if you want to see a broadway show or walk to Time Square. The breakfast is ok and dinner there was great. Rooms are cool looking with a terrific rain shower. I would stay there again without hesitation.

title: “Wonderful Breakfasts Made to Order”
“Excellent staff & location on Mich Ave - will stay here again”
text: In Chicago for sightseeing and shopping. Excellent location with restaurants and shops within walking. The best ever bell captain – snagged cabs on Michigan Ave and walked them back to the hotel for us! Concierge was friendly, helpful and very knowledgeable. Very good restaurant. Indoor pool was a bit small, but ok with good chairs and loads of towels.

title: “Disappointed”
text: We stayed 6 nights in early June. Upon check in, the clerk acknowledged that we prepaid for all six nights. We were subsequently charged again for all six nights. We complained and were told it would be taken care of, of course it wasn't. We complained again and finally it was corrected only to be charged again. We had a rental car and the charges for the parking were confused as well. After speaking to two different managers, all parking fees were removed. We were also promised a newspaper each day, and we never received even the first one. The room was just okay. On the plus side, the housekeeping staff was excellent. Overall, the hotel was really disappointing.

title: “Comfy hotel -- Very good amenities and location”
text:
My boyfriend and I just returned from a four-night stay at the Boston Westin Waterfront. We enjoyed the hotel and were very pleased with our stay.
Overall: This is definitely a business hotel, and we reaped the benefits of the expanded services offered by a business hotel, even though we were on a leisure trip. We took a red-eye flight so arrived at the hotel around 7:00 am, but they were able to check us in! I know this depends on availability, but I've been to hotels where they won't even check to see if they have openings that early in the day. The front desk and concierge staff was universally friendly and helpful, even sharing some restaurant recommendations and making change. Here's one feature I loved: The hotel lobby has two computer stations where you can log in, check on your flight, and print out your boarding pass. They also have a screen in the lobby (as well as a station on the in-room TV) with what I call the "departure channel," which lists upcoming airplane departure times.
Location: I saw some complaints about the location of this hotel, but we liked it a lot and found public transportation options very easy. We were a 30-minute walk to most of the popular locations in Boston. The T stop is right across the way, and we could be at South Station in minutes. I recommend the $15 one-week LinkPass. Also very convenient to/from the airport (just hop on the Silver Line, which is a bus, to the World Trade Center Stop, go upstairs, and walk over the pedestrian bridge to the hotel). The Old Town Trolley Tour picks up and drops off right at the hotel's lobby. We didn't use a single taxi for the whole trip. There aren't restaurants, liquor/grocery stores nearby, though, so plan accordingly. (Try MJ O'Connor's at the hotel, maybe!)
Room: Our room had a great view of Boston and a bit of the harbor. We put down the see-through shade but didn't close the black-out curtains, so we woke up every day to the lovely view. The bed was very comfortable. We had all the standard in-room amenities, like single-serve coffee maker, glasses, ice bucket, bottle opener, etc. The bathroom was comfortable and equipped with lotion, shampoo, conditioner, blow dryer, robe, etc. (no fan, though -- boo!). Everything functioned well, and we had enough room to spread out. The room was mostly very quiet, but we could hear people/housekeeping walking by sometimes. Everything was clean, and housekeeping was inobtrusive.
Dining: The in-room dining was very standard, but it's available 24 hours, which is nice. We ate twice at MJ O'Connor's and were very pleased with it. The food and drink were tasty (we had Dark 'n' Stormy cocktails and Harpoon beer for drinks and fish 'n' chips, chicken salad, pizza, and the fabulous hot dog platter for food), and the service was friendly and attentive. Highly recommended! We tried City Bar once, and the food was good (I think it shares a kitchen with MJ O'Connor's), but the service was pretty poor. We had breakfast one day at Sauciety. The food was pretty tasty, and the service was passable but not great. I'd call the food and drink prices very high, but it's a hotel, and it's in Boston, so we weren't surprised or put off.
I call this hotel a very good value in a very good location. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Warren Is a Prince”
text: The gentleman at the reception desk, Warren, was very kind to us when we checked in. It was a horrible rainy day and my sister and I were exhausted. Warren helped. The room was pleasant. We were only there for one night so I have nothing else to say.

title: “FABULOUS!!”
text: First visit to Seattle...first stay at a Westin....we loved both!!!! Our room was on the 36th floor with a beautiful view of the Space Needle! We took the hop on-hop off Grayline tour recommended by the concierge and it was great for getting to all the different parts of the city we wanted to see. At night we went to a Mariners game at Safeco field which was lots of fun.

title: “Not The Quality I Would Expect from a Hilton Family Hotel”
text:
Not really into writing reviews as it is all in the eyes of the beholder but I decided to state that unless you have to find anothher hotel. 
I am a Diamond Elite Member and one would expect to be greeted politely at checkin Neither of the front desk staff appeard to care about my status or anyone checking in. Very curt and unfriendly. No word about thanks for staying, hello or anything.
I called and advised them a car was in the parking lot with no wheels and up on cement blocks which concerned me. I was told a car rental company would get it. To date it is still there. Also in the key was a warning the area was designated high crime by the police. I wonder if this car had its tires stolen.
I asked about the shuttle to the medical center and approx how long it takes to get there. I was told they did not know and to ask shuttle driver. I would think a hotel advertising a shuttle would at least have some idea of time to drive to the center.
I would never stay here again and I have to stay again for 21 days in May but Marriott will get my nights based strictly on the attitude of the front desk staff. Oh yes I got a canned thank you (read by the manager of the hotel) Corny and dumb.

title: “Return to Lonely Street”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel for 3 nights - it was our second visit. Check in was busy, but they were friendly and efficient - unfortunately our luggage had gone missing and the airline had said that the bags would be at the hotel by 6pm, but the receptionist said not to expect them until the next day. She was right!
The rooms were large - we stayed in a King size room which had a large bedroom and tv, and a large separate sitting room and tv. It also had a small kitchenette with sink, fridge, microwave and coffee maker. Housekeeping came in every day - the rooms were always clean with fresh towels etc.
The hotel is next door to the Graceland complex and has its own side entrance. Walmarts and Southland Shopping Mall are close by. 
It is well worth going to Marlowes Ribs and Restaurant - we were picked up and brought back to the hotel in a pink limo, which made a great start to the holiday. The food is fantastic and the staff really friendly.
If you want a good day out - you can head to the Casinos at Tunica. It's about a half hour drive away, but well worth a visit.
This hotel is a must for all Elvis fans.

title: “Unbelievable!”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Gansevoort for 3 nights with our 4 year old daughter. I can't say enough good things about this hotel. From the moment we checked in (early) to the moment we checked out they were unbelievable. The view from the Rooftop pool/bar was fantastic - and having the Rooftop pool was a HUGE plus for us with a 4 year old. it does close early (for family swimming) but this wasn't ever an issue for us. On our first day there the guy that was "manning" the pool area brought out freezies for the kids (and parents) and it was such a nice thing to do, we were all in shock. We were pretty much the only people up there (it was overcast) and the fact that he went the extra mile was so much appreciated. The door/elevator staff were BEYOND great with the kids. They were always betting with them about which elevator would come first, and didn't ever roll their eyes when the kids insisted on taking the turn style door instead of the regular one. We had a meeting at the rooftop bar the one night as part of a contest win, and the staff at the bar were excellent - they went out of their way to make our daughter feel at home, even made her a Shirley Temple. They also didn't get upset when we took the kids out to the balcony to see the sunset and take a few photos. I didn't ever ONCE get the feeling that we were a burden because we had a child. Even the people partying at the bar were super friendly with the kids. I was shocked. The rooms are super clean, and the beds are ridiculously comfortable. The location was fantastic - with lots of great places to eat/see in the area. Highly recommend the diner on the corner, and also getting food at the Chelsea Market was really convenient. I would stay at this hotel again in a heartbeat.

title: “Highly Recommend!!”
text: Beautiful hotel with impressive 12-story atrium lobby. All rooms open into the center atrium. Floor to ceiling windows, PLUSH bed w/high thread count linens & comforter. Room was really spacious as was bathroom. Colors very appealing. Wireless internet (free) available throughout the hotel. Ate in restaurant which was equally appealing and food was very good. Great gym & atrium pool. Highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Value budget Motel in classy shopping district”
text:
Giving this Motel three stars is a bit unfair but at the same time there are things it can not better simply because of what it inherently is which is an old fashioned Motel but with an updated image. Built in I think the 1950`s the rooms are all facing out to a pool / garden with them all sharing a set of inner walkways which can cause noise when being walked on or if dragging suitcases along. 
So saying, this was not generally what kept us awake at night, that was down to young red neck guests who thought it funny to use the place as a play pen at 4.00 am.....The 24 hour concierge should have sorted this out however.
The interior of our room ( a standard king next to the stairwell on the first floor ) was nice enough with plenty of room, a good sized walk in wardrobe and table / chairs, T.V cabinet and draws. 
The room gave almost no view to the Street ( Webster ) due to a tree growing outside and no front view to the pool / garden so was also quite dark.. The bathroom was small and very basic with a shower only, no bath. 
There were dispensers in the shower cubicle for soaps, good idea.
However, the room was clean/ed every day and had no glaring faults that made occupation distasteful and we actually found it reasonably pleasant, I can only assume that the nicer / larger rooms looking out over the courtyard would be slightly better and more pleasant still.
Couples or families on a budget should find all this acceptable however, the funky interior paintings and wall colours brighten things up and gives a sunny `holiday` feel to the rooms and certainly is better than acres of beige/ white which i`m sure it would have been a few years ago. 
The big drawback was that there was no coffee maker, fridge or microwave in the room, no DVD or C.D player either. A clock alarm and a T.V were the only `extras` . Shame, but if you know thats what youre going to get...
Breakfast was very basic as is usual in America, muffins and bagels with some jams, cheese spreads, packet jogurt ( urgh), juice and coffee. I think some cereal as well. Okay but not gourmet by any stretch.Trays are provided if you wish to breakfast in your room ( we did, the only seating is outside which at 8.00 A.M in San Fran can be damn chilly!)
Parking, it should be noted is on the ground floor under the rooms with an overflow car park next door in a lot. There is also plenty of parking on the streets.
The best part of this though is the location, down near Marina, close to Chrissy fields, the Forts, Pier 39, Golden Gate and facing the other way a 20 minute walk into the City for Union Square and shopping. The Del Sol ineighbourhood is pleasant and busy, upmarket with many shops, cafes and bars with some good restaurants of all types and budgets catered for. We had Thai, Mexican and fusion fish all within about 200 yards of Del Sol and all were fine and well priced. 
I cannot really comment on the staff, at Del Sol, booking in and out was about my only contact but that was fine and friendly enough.
In summarisation I would say that this was a fine enough place for most to stay, its quite cheap ( for San Fran, we stayed at the Rex last visit and that has trebled in price in just 4 years), its location is superb, its quite fun and funky, it has a swimming pool ( not heated I don`t think and a bit open next to the street ), its on a quiet street and it`s safe. It is really a Motel still not a Hotel and does have comfort limitations but if you go with all this mind you should not be dissapointed. We would not rush back but we certainly wouldn`t boycottt the place either, especially if we were to return to be in that part of town.
A final reminder is that State tax and Room tax is additional to prices quoted even on Booking.com! Be aware, it adds quite a bit to a longer stay! WE paid about $150 per night plus tax.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location, Good value”
text:
Stay 2 night for business on Oct 13 to Oct 15. As my tittle, this hotel located on hollywood boulevard which is very good. Building is new in very good condition. Booked from Indonesia for about 250 USD per night which is good value in my opinion.
Very busy on the weekend as they use lobby for a club. Good for youngster, but not for senior guest who need to rest calmly and for who brings children.
Drawbacks are:
1. This hotel does not have cofee maker inside the room. Just found on 2nd day that they provide free coffee on the lobby, and just found after check out that I can call guest service to ask a cofee maker to be sent to my room. Hope further guest who read this review find this tips to deal with the lack of coffee.
2. My room does not have bath tub.
3. They don't have buffet breakfast.

title: “beautiful resort, warm and friendly staff”
text: We enjoyed spending two very relaxing days at Paradise Point; the staff is very attentative and caring; follow-up on requests was outstanding.

title: “Plaza Athenee”
text: Different experience. Nice hotel in quiet neighborhood on upper east side. However, very pricey. Room was nothing special and they said we had been "upgraded" so not sure what that meant. Staff was friendly and helpful. Didn't try the restaurant because the prices were outrageous. Nice for a special anniversary, but since one doesn't go to NYC to stay in a room, I'd pick something less expensive next time.

title: “great location staff is very helpful and effeicent.”
text: hotel is in a great location rooms are adiquit enough carpets could be newer but the rate is affordable staff is excellent . bar is accomadating alittle pricey need beer specials. food is excellent. if booking for a large group i recomend using itze alonso very helpful

title: “Excellent”
text: I stayed through the first week of June and the great stay started from the time I arrived. Though the check-in time was 3pm, the counter staff could tell I was exhausted, found a room ready and checked me in at 11am after a 24h flight. The room was well furnished, two great big queen sized bed, large HD TV, large bathroom, complimentary UStoday each day and daily change of towel (although the practice is to hang a towel so it wouldn't be changed, they still got changed daily). Aircon is really strong and effective for Austin's summer heat. It's just 5min walk from the famous 6th street and Austin Concention Centre. I stayed on the 10th floor facing the interstate and traffic can be audible at times.

title: “All-in-all a very good stay”
text: Stayed at the Park Central for several days. Despite some problems at check-in (very small room) the overall experience was very good. Customers relation (Elizabeth) is excellent, they provided a better room no charge. Elizabeth was professional, kind, helpful, and extremely friendly person - excellance service. Hotel is on a great location, very subway accessible. I had a great time and would stay at the Park Central on my next visit to New York.

title: “Club Lounge is in a temporary space”
text:
We returned to the Ritz Carlton last Friday through Sunday. In June, we had a good experience, booking the club floor with access to the Club Lounge. Although I reconfirmed and spoke with the hotel twice, they never mentioned that the Club Lounge was in a temporary location due to renovations. The experience was not the same. Check ahead if you are booking through March.
Also, normally our room would be located on the Club level, but this was not the case this time. When booking, we requested a room with a view of the Commons, but were not given one. The front desk said there were no other rooms available and didn't offer any compensation. A big disappointment. For our next trip we will be booking the Four Seasons.

title: “Spacious & Clean Rooms, Professional & Curteous Staff”
text: Perfect for an overnight stay to catch an early flight out of Logan Airport.

title: “Good price, dirty rooms.”
text:
Ask for an updated room upon booking! 
Otherwise it's not worth it to stay there. I made the mistake of not doing so when I reserved our room, as on the website they only post pictures of the new rooms. Imagine our surprise when we got our room, the lobby is fantastic...however it goes down hill from there. As of right now, only the first and fourth floors have been remodeled. Our room's shower had dirt clods and hair in the tub...upon running the water to wash it out, it backed up and things just got worse. Majority of the lights didn't work, unless you like ESPN or cartoons, you'll be bored with the channel line up. So upon the shower backing up I decided that was enough and asked to have a new room, an updated one. Our new room's AC doesn't work, there is a strange, loud, machine noise, but at least it's a newer room. Oh and the train coming through at all hours of the night is great for your sleep.

title: “Great Stay!”
text:
First of all, I must say that this hotel is at an excellent location, I loved it! Just a few steps away from Times Square. Wonderfull!
secondaly, the room is quite big, very clean and comfortable.
Every request that I had was filled to my satisfaction and last but not least, the price is great, a real good value for money hotel.
I enjoyed my stay and will return for sure.

title: “Another Day in Court”
text: This is one of my most favorite hotels to visit when in Houston. The front desk staff are always courteous and pleasant; they seem to go out of their way to accommodate needs and requests and to make sure you are comfortable. Of course the breakfast and afternoon happy hour treats are a plus. If I had a complaint, it's that they have switched over to wireless internet completely and for those who have not moved to that point this can be a setback. Of course, they have the business center available. Rooms spacious and clean with comfortable beds. Also as a coffee drinker, changing over to the one cup brewing pot is a minus but that's minute compared to the overall excellence of the hotel. The DISH network jumped in and out otherwise the channel selections on the TV were good.

title: “Just wonderful”
text:
My friend and I stopped over in NYC on the way to Europe. It was both of our birthdays so we decided to catch a show and be fairly close to Times Square. The Distrikt was wonderful choice for us.
At check in, we were pleasantly surprised when they sang Happy Birthday to me, (two different employees) which I thought was sweet. They also delivered birthday cupcakes to our room.
The room was comfortable and cute. The bathroom was very nice and had everything that we needed. The employees were very helpful and willing to give directions. There is a restaurant on the premises-- it was very good.

title: “Hotel was excellent, La Brasserie Restaurant was a horrible last day experience”
text: Like the title says, the hotel is fine. The service is all ok and the all the main staff were very polite. The only problem we had is on the last night we decided to go for dinner at La Brasserie restaurant in the hotel. The waiter was polite initially and then seemed politely impatient. It seemed as soon as my wife didn't order a alchohol drink, the mood changed. She doesn't drink what do u expect? This really bugs me when a guys about to spend money in a restaurant and tips are expected. Anyways this waiter (server: 245 Richie on the bill) was just that bad apple you get once in a while. If things don't go his way perfectly you get attitude. He spent more time on his blackberry than he did paying attention to us. I still gave him a tip, don't ask me why!

title: “Rooms like suites”
text: I really liked the set up of the king room; seperate living room and bedroom gave the feeling of staying in a suite. If you're planning a trip to Sea World or a military event at MCRD, this place is in a very good location.

title: “Awesome service”
text: The hotel itself is nice but not as nice as other W Hotels because its older. The views are awesome. The staff is awesome as well. Especially Trevell the living room attendant, she is down to earth and very helpful. She is your go to girl for sure.

title: “Great hotel in great location.”
text:
Stayed for 5 nights at the end of May 2011. Room was compact (very small), but didn't lack in anything we required. Bed against two walls so biggest challenge was if the person against the wall needed out in the middle of the night! Not a problem with noise - barely saw another guest even though we knew the hotel was busy. Traffic didn't bother us with the air-con on, which was essential! 
Room was immaculate - cleaned everyday and bedding/towels changed as required.
Didn't experience the "grab and go" breakfast, went to many a local diner instead. 
Staff were great, really helpful and their when needed. 
Would happily stay again.

title: “pleasantly surprised”
text: We booked it for the Price is Right, and were happy to find we were right across the street and a 5 minute walk to the ticket place. We had requested a room with 2 double beds, and were happy to find a nice room with a queen bed, tv and desk, with an adjoining room with another queen bed, tv and fridge. They shared one bath, but we were very comfortable. The only downfall was the parking. There is a tiny lot under the building that is scary to drive into....if I had a large car I wouldn't even try it. Although it is free, there are limited spaces and we grabbed the last one of the evening. Great location for Price is Right and a quick drive to popular spots in Hollywood.

title: “Pleasantly surprised!”
text: I had read the reviews in tripadvisor before booking the reservation, and as a result was quite hesitant about what i was getting myself into. We stayed for 5 days over Christmas, and thought the rooms were clean, staff was very courteous, and rooms were good for the price. It's not a Ritz Carlton, but then again you pay much less for a room if you bid through priceline. I would stay there again.

title: “Outstanding”
text: Outstanding place to stay. The hotel staff are exceptional in service and attitude. Rooms are always well kept and clean. When I have need information it was like having a personal concierge.

title: “Exceeded my Wildest Dreams”
text:
I stayed at the Affinia Manhattan at the end of May 2009. It was a birthday trip that I had decided to go solo on (at the last minute). From the moment I checked in, the hotel staff was super nice and accomodating. Although the room I had originally booked wasn't ready yet, they held my luggage & offered me THREE other choices of rooms in the meantime while I wait for my room. That was just the beginning of the large spectrum of wonderful service throughout my entire stay. 
The staff was so courteous & helpful; from the insider scoop on what to see, to the subway lines/stops to take for my day-to-day sightseeing, to directions on the theater for my Broadway show, I felt in good hands the entire time. It was the most personable concierge/staff experience I've ever had a hotel. They were just downright amazing. 
The room was magnificent, definitely elegant yet handy (with a microwave to heat up left-overs in the kitchen). Room was a good size, with a nice bathroom & walk-in closet. I also went online to their website w/ my reso # and ordered specialty pillows/extras (up to 2) free of charge! All in all, a great trip with a GREAT hotel. I will DEFINITELY stay here again!

title: “Convenient to all things downtown”
text:
Great alternative to pricier hotels downtown. Plentiful breakfast included as well as Mon-Thurs light meal and happy hour.
Suites with kitchen allow for dining in options as well.
Great stay for the week!
Great Italian restaurant next door at the Hotel Monaco.

title: “Great place to stay in New York”
text: We stayed at the Doubletree and loved it. It was off the beaten path but very, very safe and within walking distance of Times Square, Macy's. In our package we had a buffet breakfast which was great. Rooms were small but we were hardly there anyways. Very, very clean and staff were incredibly friendly and helpful.

title: “Hotel Room average, everything else great”
text: The hotel is convenient located next to Harvard Medical School and the guests appeared to be a mixture of patients/families and other visitors to the medical facilities. Hotel is about a $40 ride from the airport. For local transportation, it is within easy walking distance to the green T line. My room on the 7th floor was just average with a very small bathroom which had chipped and peeling paint sections on the wall. Toiletries provided were minimum (two bars of soap and one little bottle of shampoo). Walls were thin as I could here the conversations of my next door neighboor and the flushing of the toilet. Now for the good part. There was a great selection available from the room service menu which was reasonably priced with fast service and very tasty. The hotel restaurant also provides very nice service and a good bar. Accessible from the elevator on the second floor is a food court that includes some small shops and a CVS. Staff were very polite and the concierge was knowledgeable.

title: “Pleasant stay”
text: Although the location is somewhat isolated, away from the happening parts of town, this is a nice comfortable hotel with good service. The in-hotel restaurant is okay, though the bar area is nice food quality is just okay. Everything tasted kinda bland. I didn't use the pool though it appeared nice, hotel room was comfortable clean and quiet.

title: “Convenient location, large rooms, friendly service”
text: Stayed for one night over a September weekend. The location is great for all Ferry Building, SOMA access. Rooms are large and convenient, but could benefit from an upgrade (carpet, furnishings, etc.) to match great view of bay, exceedingly impressive atrium, with transparent elevators, hanging lighting, etc. The service was exceedingly (and refreshingly) friendly. At the right price, we would definitely stay here again.

title: “We would stay @ Paramount again every time we are in NYC”
text:
Great hotel, Rooms are nice and cosy, Some canbe small but very stylish , very modern and with all you need. A bath tub in all rooms we been to. This was our second stay at the PAramount and we would come to stay here again. Price / quality = top ratio
Brian and Edgar are top and friendly door men.

title: “Great place for a conference stay in Phoenix”
text:
We booked online and arrived for a conference not knowing Phoenix or this hotel at all. We had a room with two queen beds, a work area, an in-room microwave, small fridge and coffee maker, for $79 a night. Rooms were clean and smoke-free, bathroom was spotless, we enjoyed the outdoor pool, and the reception was helpful and friendly. We had a great experience. Our five-night stay cost less than $450, which we split.
I will definitely stay here next time I am in Phoenix--four blocks to the Convention Centre and main hotels like the Hyatt and Sheraton for after-event meetings, and other attractions. We felt safe walking back at night along well-lit Van Buren Street.
The owner manager Walt will arrange a tour to the Grand Canyon (4.5 hour drive) and/or to Sedona (1.5 hours). We will try to do that next time.

title: “Horrible customer service”
text:
DON'T RISK IT! Pay a little more and go with a reputable place that has good business ethics and customer service. These guys will make you feel like your business means nothing to them.
We showed up at Hotel 17 with all our bags in hand and weary after a full days worth of travel from CA. And, what did we find out? Hotel 17 had overbooked us and our room which had been reserved 3 months prior and then double-checked 1 month prior to arrival, was NOT available. Huh?! How much in advance do you have to book a room here?! 
After we got the bad news, Hotel 17 then called around and got us a place somewhere else, promising us that the price we were quoted at Hotel 17 would be honored at the new place. Boy, were we snowed on that one. We ended up having to shell out an additional $100 at the new place. The new place basically said that just because Hotel 17 gave them the business does not mean that they will honor the price we were initially quoted. 
At one point during the conversation with the person at Hotel 17, he said, well if you don't like it, then that's too bad and you can go somewhere else. So, our first time in NY after doing as much preparation as possible, and it's possible that we won't have a place to stay!? To say that they put us between a rock and a hard place would be putting it mildly. PLEASE, do not travel across the country and be at the mercy of these guys.
I can tell you that the front area where you check in is very small, dimly lit and smelt musty. And as far as the workers, think of those foreigners running 7Eleven's or QuickMart and there you have it. Rush, rush, rush, and absolutely NO customer service. (And this wasn't just a NY thing. It was just a plain rude thing.)

title: “Pleasant, Quiet and Conveniently Located”
text:
I went to Chicago with a friend for a jazz concert. We each had our own room on different floors. I must say that my room was very comfortable. I loved the decor - it matched my design taste. The bed was heavenly! I slept like a baby. I had one alarming incident while taking a shower the next morning. The steam from the shower set the fire alarm off in the room! I assume that's what it was because the ventilation in the bathroom was nonexistent. I had a similar experience in a San Francisco boutique hotel a few years ago. That hotel posted a sign in the bathroom to warn clients about the steam and what should be done to prevent an alarm going off. Perhaps the Essex could do something like that. 
Other than that incident, everything was great. From check-in to check-out my experience was flawless. I would definitely stay at the Essex again.

title: “Great for families!”
text:
Family of four with a 3 year old and a 10 month old. 
Everything about our 2 night stay here was great. We were upgraded from a one-room suite to a two-room suite with kitchen and living area, were given a high chair upon request and placed on the 3rd floor with easy access to pool and work-out room. The room was clean and well appointed with everything we needed, and there were no gross, never-cleaned bed spreads which was awesome! Beds were very comfortable and had many pillows of different softness and support levels. 
Internet was accessible and easy to use. 
We were able to have friends come visit for dinner and there was plenty of room and seating for everyone. 
The trolly was very conveniently located and easy to get to.
The pool has a hot tub and a kiddie pool, the one minor complaint was that the pool was a bit on the chilly side. 
The included breakfast was great! Fresh eggs, a waffle bar, oatmeal, fruit, cereal..something for everyone and very tasty. The seating area was very clean and comfortable with a nice water feature for ambiance. 
Also, the weather cooperated, I am sure the hotel arranged this. :) Overall an excellent stay and we will definitely be back and recommend this to family and friends.

title: “Grande Old Dame in want of a redo”
text:
I remember having my high school prom at the Park Plaza and thinking it was the most elegant hotel ever. But now, 25 years later, the gilding is off the lily. It's still lovely but the rooms are very small and it's in need of some modernizing. The bathroom is tiny with only enough room for one person (which is fine since I am here visiting my mom on my own) and there is room for a double bed in the room. The closet is miniscule and the door to the bathroom does not open fully into the room with room to get around the desk. So it's a tight squeeze. Additionally, the heat could not be turned off so the room was literally 79° which is not quite comfy at night.
But that said, there is a grand elegance to the golden swans on the curved elevator doors, the chandeliers in the lobby and the flower arrangements which harkens back to the age of elegance that the Park Plaza comes from. And no matter how cramped the room is, there is something nice about staying in an historic hotel.

title: “European style boutique hotel--delightful stay”
text: Our friends met us in NYC for a theatre weekend and booked us into the Michelangelo. We are from NYC originally, and come in from CT often, so we have had many varied hotel experiences over the years:from the Plaza to the Royalton, We were very pleasantly surprised and pleased. Our friends arrived first, and received an upgrade on both our rooms to a Jr. Suite. Our suite was quite spacious, well appointed, quiet and sound proof. Our room was tastefully decorated as were the halls and the lobby area. All rugs were plush, and everything had a feel of quality, not like cheap hotel furnishings. We overlooked 51st Street, but heard no street noise.There were blackout shades in addition to shears and curtains, wonderfully dark and quiet for a good night sleep. Toiletries were nice, service was quick and pleasant. Yhere was a complimentary shoe shine, but we didn't notice until it was too late to avail ourselves of it. The chocolates and turndown service as well as the morning NY Times, were signs of a first class hotel. Morning continental breakfast was an added plus, and included cappucino or espresso. We truly felt as if we were in Itlay! The location was wonderful, as we had tickets to "Wicked" which was less than a block away. Le Bernardin and China Grill are both within a couple of blocks and are highly "Zagat rated" restaurants. The MOMA is only a couple of blocks away as well and Carnegie Hall, Rockefeller Center and Lincoln Center are within walking distance. We had a wonderful stay and would definitely return to the Michelangelo.

title: “Loved the Moderne Hotel”
text:
++ : Very well located : near Time Square and subway station. Very convenient !
Very good mattress, clean room
Very good japanese restaurant just nearby : 'EAST' !
-- : relatively small room but ok for european standards, a bit noisy in the morning but also as many other hotels (Novotel in NY is also noisy according to friends)
We did not want a room giving on the street, so view on a wall (50 cm from the window ..)
A bit expensive (around 250$) but as many other hotels in the area
Overall, we appreciated

title: “Excellent will stay in Kimpton hotels again”
text: We had the warmest and most pleasant reception from the staff when we arrived at the hotel. Nothing was too much trouble for them, and they seemed to genuinely care about our stay at the hotel. Our room was very pleasant and extremely well-equipped. The location of the hotel was also excellent, and I would stay here again, as well as actively seeking out other hotels in this group again.

title: “Check into the Lucerne -- it's worth it!”
text: The Lucerne Hotel is a lovely hotel in a wonderful location and a reasonable price (given what it costs to stay in NYC). If you call first, don't be put off by the less-than-enthusiastic tone of the reservationists. From the moment you arrive, the staff are welcoming, helpful, accommodating. Our room was pretty and comfortable. There is nice natural light in the bedroom and bathroom. The shower was always hot with good pressure...plus, you walk outside and you are minutes away from the American Museum of Natural History, Central Park, Broadway, Zabars, hundreds of cafes and restaurants and more!!

title: “Comfortable”
text:
Very friendly front desk staff, clean rooms, good quick breakfast. 
This space should not be limited to 200 characters if one just wants to make a brief review or tip or guideline. Corporate should revamp this section. I could not get out of this review unless I wrote a more detailed explanation.

title: “A gem near downtown”
text: Los Angeles is not a great place to sight see without a car. Distances can be daunting. And it can be expensive. We traveled there by Amtrak and wanted a place close to Union Station but near enough to places we could walk to and accommodations that wouldn't break the bank. We read other reviews about this hotel and decided to give it a try. It was as good as advertised. The front desk staff was efficient, friendly and helpful. The room was tastefully furnished, quiet and attractive. The hotel was spotless. It was within 1 1/2 blocks of the metro line which could take as all over the city if we chose not to walk. It was well within walking distance of Olvera Street, Chinatown, some museums, some grand refurbished hotels (walk through the Biltmore and look at the photos of past Academy Award Banquets held there), Grand Central Market, Angel's Flight, the Macy's Center, on and on. And Little Tokyo was a delight to walk and is right outside your door. We didn't use the in hotel spa but it appeared to be quite popular.There were a couple of misses, but both minor. We chose he breakfast included rate. Breakfast is served in the little snack bar alcove and consists of croissants, yogurt, tea and orange juice. If you are used to a heartier fare then don't spring for the breakfast and instead walk a few blocks and get the more traditional repast. Second, if you wile away down times watching television the cable selection is minimal. Overall the experience was excellent, well worth the cost, and a place to return to.

title: “Good location”
text: This hotel is perfectly located for those going to a Lions football game or Tigers baseball game as it is a very short walk to both the football and baseball stadiums. There are also a number of sports bars and the Greektown casino within walking distance. Inside the hotel there is a restaurant with a decent breakfast (not sure about lunch), and what seemed to be a sports bar that looked decent, although we only peeked inside. The hotel is pretty nice and clean, which is all you need when going to a game with a bunch of guys. There is also a pool I believe, but we didn't have time to use it.

title: “Like most Doubletree hotels this one is fantastic.”
text: I love these hotels. The beds are fantastic! I appreciate the consistently good service, clean spacious rooms, and beautifully maintained common areas.

title: “Very good hotel with friendly staff”
text: We experienced a relaxed friendly atmosphere of all staff members including those in the restaurant where we were served by Mrs. Marites Sobreo

title: “Great location for attractions”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights. The rooms are small but clean and adequate. Our room was at the rear on the 12th floor. Although the view wasn't that great of the offices behind it was very quiet. 
We had a large jacuzzi bath which was simply delightful after a long days sightseeing. 
The breakfasts were better than expected. Cakes, fruit, yoghurts, limited hot items such as omelettes, scrambled eggs and sausages, more than enough to set you up for the day. 
Hot drinks are free and available 24/7 which again was nice coming in from the freezing winds and snow. 
The staff were always very helpful and friendly. 
Bags can be left foc on the day of departure which was also handy. 
Overall a good base for a short stay in the Big Apple!

title: “Nothing Better in the State”
text: Arizona has so much to offer that we locals have a tradition called a "Staycation". I have had many in this great state but none can compare to my recent stay at the Palomar! First, the location to activities is unequaled. The rooms are beautiful and modern. The service was a combination of small town friendly with big city class; from everybody's puppy in the lobby, "Boscoe", to the turn down service with laid out robes and chocolates! The entire staff made us feel like we we're welcome and important to them. The only down side is that I may not be happy staying anywhere else in this great state again.

title: “fantastic experience”
text: Leaving today after 4 days at the Beacon Hotel and definitely one of my top hotel experiences in DC. Hotel appearance very inviting from the curb appeal of flowers and manicured exterior to chic restaurant and bars - particularly on the sidewalk and rooftop. The location is excellent, very convenient to the Mall just to the south and Georgetown just to the west. The immediate neighborhood also had nice restaurants. The hotel bar was hopping, particularly at happy hour and on the roof. The best part was the staff, who were exceeding friendly and helpful, especially Kingsley at the front desk. All the staff we encountered, from the cleaning crew in the halls to the bell hops went out of their way to speak (beyond a simple hello). Kingsley remembered us to the extent he spoke when we ran into him on the street several blocks away from the hotel. The Beacon will definitely be the hotel of choice on my next DC trip and will readily recommend it to others.

title: “Wow!”
text: Remarkably attentive, friendly, and helpful staff, but neither obsequious nor obtrusive. Transportation a pleasant surprise. Outstanding room - spotless & comfortable with lounge chair, best desk I've used on the road, frig, micro, and silence. Limited restaurant menu, but excellent food. Can't say enough good about the place and its people, and can't wait to return. (Serious business traveler in need of peace & quiet, office services, and relaxing environs.)

title: “Bed Bugs!”
text: Bed bugs! Stay away, beware. My girlfriend and I were bitten everywhere. Also, they did not bother to change our linnens the two days we stayed there. They put us in the handicapped accessible room, even thought neither my girlfriend nor I are disabled. They seem to do this to people who bid online for their rooms. Anyways, my girlfriend and I were bitten all over our bodies after our stay here. Please BEWARE!

title: “Nice Old Hotel”
