text: After reading multiple reviews, I was a little hesistant about this hotel. Upon arriving the bellhop(s) retrieved my luggage, escorted me to check in and waited. This person also escorted me to my room and placed my luggage on the luggage rack. This is definitely door to door service. I received a Deluxe room which was decent on the 12th floor. The staff service was nice. The only issue I had was it's always a line to see the Concierge. I needed an umbrella to go outside and had to wait in the ine because the front desk staff would not pass one over the counter. The bar staff was very nice and I loved the warm peanuts. The lobby is so inviting and I LOVED the water/flower decorations in the middle of the room. Me and my co-workers just sat in the lobby and chatted for hours at a time because it was so inviting. I saw some of the smaller rooms my coworkers stayed in. Even though the rooms were small the cleanliness of the rooms was a plus. The rooms in this hotel are like a maze. I had some coworkers who complained about having to drag their luggage up or down the stairs to reach a room location. Overall this was a nice hotel that is close to the Freedom Trail and many other sites. The door men are extremely nice with seeing you off in a cab. If you have to catch a cab from the Airport (Logan), expect to pay close to $30.00. You have to pay an extra $7.50 just to come through the tunnel and this is added onto your fare.

title: “The Good, The Bad, The Nicely Handled...”
text:
The Good, The Bad, The Nicely Handled... 
The good part...Our dance school held its annual competition at the Warner Center Marriott Woodland Hills. The size of the conference center and conference rooms were great, They provided an acquit number of chairs in each room. The had a breakfast and lunch ala-cart that was priced at standard hotel rates but with a good wide variety of items. The rooms were nice, clean, & well stocked. The staff was friendly. 
The bad part - I had asked for a room with either 2 beds or 1 bed and a roll-way. Unfortunately, I got lost in the shuffle some how and they ran out of roll away. I ended up being provide extra pillows and blankets and made a bed on the floor. Can you say SORE!
The Nicely Handled - After talking GM he was apologized profusely and provide a great fit for the situation.

title: “Amazing view”
text: I stayed at the 34th floor. Spacious room, friendly service and amazing view. I will highly recommend it!

title: “Adolphus”
text: I Loved My Stay At The Adolphus It Is One Of The Best Stays I Have Had In A Long Time I Would Tell All My Friends And Clients To Stay At The Adolphus.

title: “a bit dissapointed”
text: I have been saving my pennies to stay here for quite some time and decided to splurge for one night last month. It was kind of a let down. My company had sent me to check the place out for a group of rooms we were interested in blocking but I tried in vain to get information about that from the staff. One said she was new and did not know what the rate would be nor the availability....and then tried to ask a collegue how pretty much said she was to busy. Shame. The room itself was fine. Small but nicely enough decorated and seemed pretty clean. I could however here pretty much every word the couple next door were saying while taking a bath...not my favorite So my review stays at dissapointed.

title: “Ideal location with great amenities”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights in August during an "education vacation" for my 9 year old nephew. We saved approximately $35 by taking the metro from the airport to the hotel instead of taking a cab. It was just a 3 block walk from the metro station (metro center) to the hotel and wasn't bad at all. We naively walked to the Metro Center metro station the first 2 days thinking it would be the quickest way for us to get to our destinations. We finally realized it would take just as much time (and would burn a few more calories/save a few dollars) to walk to all of the sites we wanted to see so we did that for the remainder of trip. All of the tourist attractions are in close proximity to the hotel. I highly recommend the area map given out at check-in. We found it so helpful that we ditched the $12 map we bought at Barnes and Nobles and relied strictly on the hotel map. We stayed in a larger king suite on the 11th floor and I highly recommend paying the extra few dollars for the larger suite. We all felt like we had our own space during the stay and weren't packed into the room like you would be at other hotels. One thing I truly appreciated was how fast the elevators were. The hotel seemed relatively busy and we never waited more than 30 seconds for an elevator at any point during our stay. The pool is small but serves the purpose of just wanting to relax after a long day of walking. We utilized the self-serve laundry room once and they even stock the room with detergent and stain remover which was really helpful. Breakfast lines can get very long very quickly so we made our way down within 30 minutes of its opening each day. We never encountered a long wait but felt sorry for the folks who came in after us. The Manager's Reception was nice and thought the nightly special drinks they offered were a nice touch. We thoroughly enjoyed this property and given it's close proximity to everything and the amenities recieved, we will certainly stay here again.

title: “Traditional Quality Hotel”
text: Excellently located in dowtown this hotel is very neat and tidy, has efficient staff and spotless rooms but you can't help thinking this elegant hotel is getting stuck in the 20th Century and will soon become dated. In the lobby you feel compelled to whisper as if in a great European cathedral, and the onsite shops are not at all inviting. There is a pleasant gym and pool and very helpful concierge but as in so many hotels I was disappointed to have to pay for wireless Internet. I don't get charged for soap or coffee, why this other essential of an hotel stay?

title: “Accommodating!”
text:
Although my reserved room was not acceptable (too musty and run down) the staff was extremely accommodating and relocated me to another room overlooking the pool and gardens. I did have to pay an additional $10/night in order to get this upgrade, however, since the base cost was very affordable this was fine with me. 
The Patio Cafe was good and the location was excellent.

title: “Front desk customer service”
text: We booked two rooms and when I called for an ironing board, which should have been in the room already, they said they would send it right up. After an hour it still had not arrived so I called the front desk again and was told it had been taken care of. I asked, politely, why then had I not received it and the guy was very impatient, saying "you will get it" and hanging up. Turns out it was delivered to the wrong room, mistakes happen but there is no need to be nasty to the customer. They could do with a little PR training as I saw the same guy being nasty to somebody else. Rooms are nice, breakfast is good although the layout of the self service is not too efficient. They only have one computer for guests to use and it was being used by kids to play games so dont depend on that!

title: “great experience”
text: I visited August of 2001 and had an excellent time. This trendy upscale hotel had excellent service, a superb layout, and is in a great location. The lounge is awesome, and because of the great time that I had there, I have planned another stay this May :-)

title: “Lovely hotel”
text: A very nice hotel ideally located for Times Square. If you get one of the higher rooms you will have excellent views. Would stay there again.

title: “GREAT Boutique Hotel in convenient location”
text: Hotel staff from front desk welcome to housekeeping could not have been more welcoming and helpful. More like bed and breakfast than std hotel since area where breakfast and afternoon wine and cheese are served is more intimate. Great way to meet fellow guests. Room was cozy, comfortable and clean. Location is just steps away from Union Square, shopping, restaurants, pubs, China Town and all modes of transportation. Would recommend hotel to anyone wanting a B & B feel in middle of town. Only drawback - no views.

title: “Nice hotel - great location, good service, terrible meals.”
text:
The hotel is located very close to the SMU campus. It's hard to get into and out of the valet/reception area. Service is very nice but what you would expect for $200/night. 
The food in the restaurant is AWFUL - don't even waste your time with appetizers. We ordered several items. The most memorable was a terrible fried lobster appetizer that was served with a completely unappetizing sauce (my daughter said it looked like vomit) and strawberry jelly on top of the lobster. ?!? With every item, we all thought the chef was tossing everything he or she could find onto the plate and hoping it might "work."
The fitness center is nice but small. We thought it was odd that the Palomar would offer bottles of water to their guests at valet but not in the gym. 
They offer a complimentary wine tasting in the lobby but we did not attend. 
The pool is beautiful. After driving 800 miles in one day, braving dinner in the restaurant and being absolutely exhausted, it was lovely to go up to the roof at 10pm (when it was still 95 degrees) and soak our tired legs in the spa. 
Room service and housekeeping were both terrific!

title: “Awesome Girls Getaway at Churchill”
text: Stayed 1 night for a quick girl's getaway with out of town friend. Churchill is elegant, sophisticated and well located. Though it is a bit of a hike from Dupont and coming back is uphill for some parts. The front desk staff were some of the friendliest, accomodting and professional staff I've encountered in a long time. Bravo ladies! Even though we booked on a discounter we were never made to feel less than first class, like some other hotels. The value is all there. Great restaurants nearby, eacy to get a cab if needed. Can't wait to go back. Highly recommend for romantic getaway!

title: “Relaxing stay”
text: We had a relaxing stay at Travaasa. The spa was great, the food was great and the activities were fun. Nothing was pushed on us. Would definitely return!

title: “Fab hotel”
text: Stayed here one night only on 28th December but wished it was longer. Travelled with husband, cousin and his wife. On check-in we were immediately upgraded to Executive King rooms which were really spacious, had a huge balcony and a lounge area. Bed was really comfortable and the bathroom clean and modern. Complimentary breakfast was buffet style with the usual cereals, waffles, fresh fruit, muffins, toast, cream cheese, ttea, coffee and fruit juices. Fantastic stay and helpful staff, no complaints.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text:
Fast check in and complimentary NA drinks upon arrival. We were hoping to stay downtown, but made the reservation through Priceline and expanded our search. So glad because doing so allowed us to explore more of the greater Denver area.
The bartender in the lounge was great but the apps were just okay. 
We had very, VERY LOUD neighbors. I have never reported a disturbance in a hotel but this was unbearable. Staff was understanding and remedied the issue in a timely manner. The walls are extremel thin. You can hear those walking in the room above and neighbors coughing, plumbing, etc. Not a lot of amenities, but the rooms were clean with modern touches. Very pleased.

title: “Disappointed”
text: I had never stayed here before but because it is billed as a resort I expected so much more. The room was noisy - traffic noise all night and I awoke each morning to the sound of the neighbors' crying baby. The room was very plain with limited table space. The sheets were rough and dingy. I was very disappointed.

title: “Location-Location-Location!”
text:
This hotel is located in a perfect location in Chicago, just east of Michigan Street along the river, which makes the theater district, dining, museums, and all shopping very easy to get to. We have stayed here several times, and like staying here more than other hotels in the area.
The hotel has been updated since our last visit. A completely modern room with contemporary furniture greeted us, which was a nice surprise as the last time the room seemed to be stuck in 1987.
The only issue we had this time was the vent covers in the bathroom and bedroom were both covered in dust and appeared to have not been cleaned in quite some time. This to me is totally unacceptable.
When in Chicago, we pay a little extra for the location for the hotel room so we don't waste time taking in the sites and attractions. The Hyatt on Wacker is ideal for this. We will definitely be back.

title: “Pros & Cons on the Biltmore”
text:
Pros - Grounds are very well kept and when you walk through from the parking area, the fragrance of all the flowers stay with you all the way to your room. Staff members are very friendly and take care of your every need. One time when walking toward our car, the room-keeper staff must have just received their assignments for the morning, so we stopped to let them by (must have been 30 or more). I’m sure that they were talking among themselves about their workload, but about one in 5 would smile, acknowledge our presence and said good morning. The Spa area and locker rooms with all the amenities were better than expected for an older establishment. We really enjoyed the fact that our area had its own pool & hot tub, which was much quieter and relaxing than the main pool with the slide & swim-up bar. Great view from the room on our balcony of the main lawn with fountain & view of various weddings/events, but still far enough away from the noise. The bed was very comfortable & liked the work table with side chairs. WIFI was good and easy to log in.
Cons – The room was older and there was a note above the thermostat from maintenance (probably meant for the prior guests) about the heater being fixed for them. Well, the temperatures outside were already plenty warm (we are from Denver), so we were hoping that the older building system had the ability to cool things off. Not so much. Unfortunately our room faced south and since cleaning was done after noontime, we were gone until the early evening and unable to close the heavier blinds to block the afternoon sun and its heat. So, we would keep our sliding door open in the evening to allow the room to cool down for the night - it was tolerable.
Overall – good experience. For those who play tennis or golf, it would be an ideal location. For those who follow Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives – you are within 15 minute drive of 3 really good-ones in the greater Phoenix area.

title: “Beautiful stay”
text:
We had a beautiful stay at the St. Regis. Although here for business coming back to thr hotel for quiet time was wonderful.
The rooms were very luxurious and comfortable with very fresh linens free of debris. The TV had unlimited channels, although, to watch movies a high payment was required. The bathroom facilities in the room were magnificent. A large bathtub was situated near a walk-in shower. 
The location was very convenient for both shopping and exploring. Also, the san francisco museum of modern art is just down the block. 
The St. Regis had some of the best staff service i have ever seen.

title: “Cozy & artsy”
text: Loved this place. We were able to check in early, got a corner room. Clean, nicely decorated. Staff was helpful. Great location for the price. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Boutique hotel in great location offering very good value”
text:
Overall good experience on well located boutique hotel with suite accommodation, very suitable for couples or small family of 3 like us.
Pros- great location, subway close, 10 minute walk to Lincoln centre, times square, rockefeller centre, fifth ave shops. Very close to dry-cleaning, restaurants, nail bars etc. Decor is boutique, old fashioned , very clean. Free breakfast and wifi included. We had a one bedroom suite. Very comfortable queen beds, small dark sitting room with comfortable sofa sleeper, nice bathroom and excellent spa bath. Noise not w problem away from 55th street. Elevators work fine, apparently were being fixed for 3 months hence others comments.
Cons- no outlook, dark rooms, 2 queens in main bedroom so a bit tight for space . Closet room sufficient. The breakfast is adequate, certainly saves money and time, but staff so rude that they all should be sacked. This restaurant is not the Blakely but allied to it and they should change as it reflects badly on them. Similarly room service food is limited and closes early. We found the lovely library entrance to be sadly lacking in warmth from staff for most of our 8 day stay, although the last 2 days we were suddenly noticed and assisted in a helpful way. The staff multitask and as there is no dedicated concierge or door opener or person to get taxi, if the is is important, maybe this is not the hotel for you. 
Overall- excellent value for money. Perhaps make contact with Andreas or staff downstairs early on to be recognized and/ or have concierge advice. No need for lower room- elevators are fine and there may be a little more light in room.

title: “Good Business Hotel... But Boutique? No Way!”
text:
We booked the weekend getaway to NYC as an add-on for a business trip and stayed at the San Carlos Hotel which came recommended. Initially, we considered staying in another hotel for our "vacation" portion of this trip, but were swayed by the reviews and by the hotel website to extend our stay here. In the end, good marketing is a great tool but buyer be warned. This is not a boutique hotel.
The furnishings were standard and while the room was nice and large, words such as "Plush" used on their website are an exaggeration... Spartan comes to my mind. So, this is at best a good business hotel with no frills. It has a comfortable bed, an uncomfortable lounge chair, a good desk and a small unremarkable bathroom. The towels were remarkable... how do they get them to feel so rough? The windows were small and our view toward the back of the hotel was a darkened alley.
The staff was great... Very friendly and helpful. I'll thank them for their excellent service. 
The complimentary breakfast was not great. The pastries were bland in keeping with a theme that included only two cereals - Corn Flakes and Rice Krispies. Yogurt, apples, juice, milk, coffee, toast, and bagels were also offered.
I can recommend this hotel - it is clean, the rooms are large, and the location is good. However if you are seeking something special for your NYC stay, you might want to keep searching.

title: “Wonderful Hotel and Staff!”
text:
I attended a Regional Upscale Meeting here, and was a guest for two nights. This is a beautiful, well run hotel! The Staff is absolutely amazing, from the General Manager all the way to Valet.
It was as though I was a VIP at all times. Everyone caters to you, and wants to make certain that you have everything you need. There wasn't one employee who didn't have a smile on their face, and a kind "How are you today" coming out of their mouth.
If ever back in San Antonio, I'll be their guest again!!!

title: “Super clean and great ambience”
text: this best western is a great value.......the price was right and the room was awesome. super duper clean.......service was very friendly and the motel was uptodate and modern. highly recommend.

title: “Generous Hotel in a Typically Cramped City”
text: This was a totally positive experience. I was traveling with my 19-year old son who was looking at Northeastern. We arrived by cab and were greeting promptly by a pleasant and attentive door staff. Check-in was painless and equally pleasant. All the staff seems to enjoy where they are working. The hotel itself is a new building (maybe 10 years old), which is definitely a positive - wide hallways, generously sized rooms that are simple but well-decorated, and amply sized bathrooms. All in all a pleasant change from some of the cramped accommodations typically found in Boston. The breakfast at Eastern Standard is pretty good (not great), but the prices are fair. The Eggs Benedict over biscuits is worth trying. The service there is not as pleasant as at the hotel itself, but it was sufficiently attentive. Lastly, the location is minutes away from everything (I guess what isn't in Boston?). Crossing the Mass Pike on foot is a bit of a hassle, but it was still a great place to explore the city from. Only downside was the tub is a little small & the shower head pressure was too high! All in all, highly recommended!

title: “Unhappy with the Wingate”
text:
I booked a twin room with 2 double beds via the Wingate reservations system. I made sure to read all the fine print, as I know that sometimes hotels will not guarantee separate beds in twin share accommodation, however the confirmation came through clearly saying that a room type with 2 double beds had been booked.
When we arrived, my friend and I were given a room with 1 queen bed.
I immediately spoke to reception, who told me that not only were there no other twin rooms available, but that the hotel had no roll-away beds either. When I asked whether we could be placed in a twin room the following day, they could not confirm whether this would be possible.
The manager was eventually called to talk to me and he was totally unapologetic and unhelpful. He denied that I had been guaranteed a room with 2 double beds. When I showed him the confirmation slip with the guarantee in it, he told me that the reservations system had nothing to do with the hotel, and that even though the booking was for a room type that had 2 double beds, the hotel never saw this (????). 
He then informed me that my booking had said there was only 1 guest in the room, so there would be no need for a twin room. Again, I showed him my booking confirmation that clearly showed I had entered that there would be 2 guests. He just said "well, our system shows only 1". 
At no time did I receive an apology or even an acknowledgment that an error had been made by the hotel. No matter what I said, the manager continued to argue with me and wouldn't concede that an error had been made. There was a total absence of customer service professionalism in the way he handled the issue.
Ultimately we cancelled our booking on the spot and went to another hotel. I recommend anyone considering staying here to call in advance and confirm the information that the hotel has on file to prevent disappointment.

title: “What a dump”
text: We are a family of 4 and we stayed there one night last week. When you enter the hotel, the lobby looks fine and the staff is really polite and helpful. But once you exit the elevator on your floor, you start thinking - oh my god what did I do. Everything looks old and beaten down. When I exit that elevator I felt like I was in some C production movie. Carpets are old, the paint is chipped everywhere, doors look beaten and scratched, and that kind of decor continues in the suite. The furniture is old and beaten, certain unknown smells in the certain parts of the suite. I tried not to think about it.One wall in the room had a huge mirror in it, now I don't know if housekeeping is blind but it looked so messed up and dirty, I think my 2 year old daughter could do a better job of cleaning it. Now I don't care if the mirror is clean or dirty but it shows overall attitude of housekeeping and they way they take care of the place. I was just hoping that my family would forgive me, they wanted to stay in the Hilton which was even cheaper, but I chose Radisson only because it had enclosed pool and I know that the kids would use it and I didn't want them to catch a cold at the outdoor pool in the Hilton. So when we saw where we are at the mood went down. I knew everyone was hungry so I ordered right away food from room service to cheer them up. 15 mins after I ordered it, they called me to confirm the order once again - so again I go through all the items that we ordered. Half an hour later the food comes and we start opening up the dishes to eat, we realize that my wifes food is missing. So she calls them again and they said they will take care of it. 45 mins later it still did not arrive so she goes down to reception and they said they will check to see what the problem is. The receptionist comes back and says that no one knew anything about it and then she put a new order in that would be ready in a half an hour. So what do you say after all that, how hard is it to take an order for 4 items. I know that this a human mistake and that could happen anywhere and I don't really care much about it, but being in a beaten, dirty and smelly place, it is something that bothers me.

title: “Faultless hotel, in a great location”
text:
What a fantastic hotel! I'd never been to New York before and had been warned some of the hotels can have tiny bedrooms. We stayed in a standard room at the Affinia Shelburne, it had more than enough room, an enormous bed, coffee/tea making facilities and a lovely bathroom with wonderful complimentary wash products.
The location is ideal. Just a couple of blocks from Grand Central Station and the Empire state building, and only about 20 minutes walk to Times Square...if you don't get distracted by shops and restaurants. Don't let it put you off that it's close to a "residential" area. There is loads to do close by, the subway is just a short walk away and it's also much quieter than being in the centre, which means you get a good nights sleep after all that sightseeing.
We ate at the Rare restaurant at the hotel - the burgers were incredible...one word of warning the apple pie for desert is enormous, so more than enough for two people!
There are plenty of deli's nearby for breakfast - a couple we tried were Blooms on Lexington Ave, and the Murray Hill diner. Try Balthazar in Soho if you want a very fancy brunch, but get there early because it's very popular. Also make sure you stumble onto 3rd Avenue for plenty more bars and restaurants.
All in all we had an amazing break, and would definately book the Affinia Shelburne if we travel to NYC in the future.

title: “Very good hotel. Older but comfortable.”
text: This hotel was pretty nice. It had an older feel but with modern touches. The breakfast was pretty awesome! I would go back just for the eggs! Overall it was a fun weekend, although there were about 50 sorority girls staying on our floor and all of them were having some sort of drama.

title: “Excellent in every way”
text: An absolutely brilliant hotel. From the moment you arrive, you feel welcome and looked after. The building itself is stunning and oozes charm and quality. The rooms are a little small, but entirely adequate, impeccably clean and very well appointed with big bathroom (complete with tv built in to mirror). All staff were very helpful, and I especially enjoyed the bespoke welcome snack. One thing to be aware of - they don't provide an ironing board but for $11 will iron a shirt for you.

title: “We love it!”
text:
Came here for a conference, but wifey came with for leisure. This was our first time in that far west, much less Seattle, so we didn't know what to expect. We arrived and the hotel was nice!!! Check-in is was pleasant and smooth...and we even received wine and fruit in our room. (had the family/friends starwood elite treatment) Our room was on the 15th floor or something, it was for the preferred guests. And they know how to treat preferred guests!!! The preferred guest lounge was top shelf with free food and a free happy hour on certain days. I even met the manager of guest services at the happy hour reception who was very nice and hospitable. (forgot her name, but she was Black)
My wife and I were so impressed with the preferred guest treatment, we felt like a king and queen. It was unfortunate though, that EVERY customer doesn't that same type of treatment. (people on the first 8 floors---the non-preferred "regular" guests) The stratification made us kinda sad, to see that certain guests were treated better than others. It was nice, but we wished everyone could have experienced what we did.
 We also ate in the restaurant lounge at the top of the hotel. (can't remember the name) But it was super top shelf with an AMAZING VIEW!!! Quite serene...Seattle has a great skyline. 
Although kinda small, the fitness center was modern and nice. The pool was nice too and had a chic feel to it. We even received free breakfast coupons, and the breakfast was superb. The service was a little shaky though, as they may have been understaffed. Great food though. 
Great location downtown; close enough to walk everywhere, but not too far from everything downtown. 
Overall this hotel really impressed us and gave us a really good percpetion and experience of Seattle. Everyone was so nice and professional. Please stay here!

title: “Nice, but not spectacular”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for a business conference when the hotel had just opened for several months. It was nice because everything was brand new and the property was gorgeous and resort-like. However, the downsides were that it lacked southern charm and an experienced staff, which mainly consisted of college kids from nearby colleges off for the summer.
Location-wise, the property is secluded so you'll need a car to get around or be prepared to pay for the taxi. A taxi ride to the Alamo or River Walk is about $50 - $60 dollars. There are several dining options on property, including the Cibolo Moon, which is highly recommended. High Velocity has really good buffalo wings. The hotel also has a list of somewhat nearby restaurants that offer van service to their restaurants. The mexican one (forgot the name) was really really good.
If the price was right, I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Fun in DC”
text:
the Capitol Skyling Hotel is bargain for the location. You are very close, walking distance, to the Nationals Stadium, the Capitol, the National Mall. 
I asked for and received a handicap accessible room for me with an adjoining for my son. Cleanliness is paramount to me and this hotel met my standard. The beds were outstanding comfortable. There is a small restaurant for a breakfast buffet or a cheaper option across the street at McDonalds for those with children. Poolside has s adequate selection of lunch items. The front desk and guest service staff were extremely helpful. Elevators to parking and a shuttle available for a small fee for drop offs around town.
It was a very nice experience.

title: “Possibly the best service EVER”
text:
Room - King bed with great view of the city. It was full of very modern furniture and when I say full I mean it. I was going to post pics but from the ones that have already been posted it looks like all the rooms were the same. Very comfy bed and a cool modern-deco desk with a huge lounging chair and ottoman combo that took up damn near the entire room. They obviously had someone with good style pick the furniture but then someone blind or perhaps with levitating abilities chose the arrangement because it made no sense being arranged traditionally. The bed was comfortable except for the pillows. I'm a memory foam person and always end up rolling up the pillows to get decent support. If you like pillows you can sink into, you won't have a problem. The bathroom was full of modern and stylish features and I think it was arranged best for the use of a slightly small space. Nice closet for winter coats. HUGE freaking mirror. 
Area - We were able to walk around and be touristy without trouble. I imagine in the summer the walk to the river would be pleasant. We tried out The Elevator brew pub which is a few blocks away. I believe it was in the German part of town as the full name had "Haus" in it. Ate dinner on Saturday night across the street from the hotel at Mitchell's Steakhouse which was amazing. Fantastic service (attentive without being intrusive) and amazing food. I suggest the bacon wrapped filet and creme brulee'.
Hotel overall - When we checked in there was some sort of high school volleyball tournament going on that had the place packed. They'd planned well for it though and had plenty of valets (I think it was $30/night) and front desk people. The manager was wading through the masses and just checking in with people "someone with be with you very soon" "we really appreciate your patience and hope you enjoy your stay". It was nice. There's a lounge/bar but we didn't use it because we went back across the street to Mitchell's and sat at their bar and had more desserts! Breakfast at the hotel restaurant was really good. The staff there was good. They had 2 options for the buffet which I thought was nice. I think it was $10 for the typical pastry/cereal/fruit combo or $14 for a dude to make you an omelet to order, fried eggs, oatmeal, bacon, fresh waffles, and a few other things that I was too full to explore. 
We came back to our room early on Saturday afternoon and encountered the cleaning staff who were friendlier than some of my neighbors. Generally, it seems this place has found the friendliest and nicest people in Ohio and somehow wrangled them all into working here. Fantastic stay.

title: “Great Position for New York Experience”
text:
Hotel in great position if you are sightseeing New York....A short walk from Times Square and smack bang in Theatre Land..Plenty of good restaurants closeby.Hotel has been refurbished to a high standard in modern design..Reception staff efficient and breakfast service in small hotel restaurant very convenient and reasonable priced at $13 for continental but plenty on offer to satisfy European breakfast tastes.
Hotel rooms very good standard but on the small size with bathrooms only 6x4 a tight squeeze with bath towels to match..All very plush but a problem if you happen to be on the big size...Housekeeping a bit on the hit & miss side with irritating shortfalls like not leaving toilet rolls,soap at times....Everything clean though.. All in all a good all round hotel ,reasonably priced for New York ,in a prime position but can be improved with a bit more attention to detail...Would stay again if in New York.

title: “Great hotel in a great location!”
text:
My friend and I stayed here in January for a girl's weekend and loved it! We purposely wanted to be away from Times Square and try out a different area of the city. There were plenty of good places to eat nearby and it was a short, easy walk (even in the snow!) to the subway. The parking garage was around the corner which was convenient (expensive, but it's NYC so we expected it). We had no trouble getting a cab outside the hotel either. This room was rather large (2 doubles, a bathroom and kitchen) by NY standards, obviously updated and very well appointed. The staff was very friendly as well! 
I recommend this to all types of travelers because it's an amazing value and location!

title: “Nice - but too many small niggles and poor staff”
text:
We stayed here on our last trip to NYC four years ago and had a great stay - so the obvious choice this time was the Barclay. We stayed for one night before a cruise and then returned for a further five nights.
First up the hotel is in a great location, about 15 minutes brisk walk to Times Square, Bloomingdales and Central Park. There are loads of bars and restaurants and delis nearby along with plenty shops. There is normally a great supply of taxis waiting outside, although the porters are selective in who they assist - if you're a female you've a good chance, guys don't hold your breath!
The service really lets this hotel down and I really don't think we will be back - which is really disappointing. But if you want a good central base this is a great choice. If you can put up with niggles and poor service you won't be disappointed.
Check-in at the Amassador desk was great and Lesley was extremely friendly. She also made arrangements to ensure that we would be able to access our room after the cruise at 10am - this really was welcome!
Our room for the first night was ok, a bit dark with it being at the side of the hotel but it was clean and comortable and perfectly adequate. Breakfast the next morning offered a good range of food, albeit the hot food isn't really that hot and a lot of the pastries were somewhat stale. If breakfast hadn't been included in our rate, I would not have been happy to pay the $36 price tag. In addition the waiters were grumpy, unattentive and one was down right rude.
When we returned after the cruise, Lesley again gave a lovely welcome and all was well. This room was a great size and was at the front of the hotel which made it lighter - although it was right beside the lift, there was no noise. However the cleanliness this time was disappointing - crushed biscuits at the end of the bed, dried fruit under the window and a used kleenex beside the bin. The bedside drawer was also broken. Knowing these would be easy things to fix, we unpacked and reported the problems before we went out for a walk. At first we were offered another room, but having unpacked we declined. We returned five hours later and nothing had been done! I went back to the Ambassador desk to see Lesley, but unfortunately she wasn't there so I spoke to another girl. She was less than impressed that I had issues to raise. Eventually the cleaning supervisor appeared claimed that the problems had been rectified - I had to show her the proof to counter her claim! So someone did come, hoovered and grumpily left - sadly she had missed most of the biscuit crumbs and was less than pleased when I had to call her back to try again. 
The bedside drawer, which was a safety hazard, was eventually fixed three days later after I reported it a further four times.
The bar tenders are pretty friendly when you are sitting at the bar. But don't expect any sort of friendly or prompt service at the tables. Again, the waiters were grumpy and unattentive yet they automatically add 15% - for that I expect to be acknowledged at least.
All of the issues we experienced were small and certainly didn't spoil our trip. But they all start to add up. Things go wrong, I know and I have no issues with that, but I don't think cleanliness and friendly staff are much to expect as a basic standard. We visiting the Waldorf, Marriott Marquis and Mandarin Oriental during our trip - and boy do they know how to provide service!! 
When we checked-out the duty manager came to speak to us, which I really appreciated. However the points she offered by way of apology have yet to appear in my account.
We travel extensively and always chose four star and above - this hotel should be great - and it used to be! But sometimes it's the little things that are so easily fixed, that make a difference. Sadly, the impression here is that the Barclay simply can't be bothered and has given up.

title: “A Bit of Old World Luxury”
text:
This is a great old hotel that has been well maintained and is well staffed. The service was friendly, courteous and helpful in all departments. The only complaint I have is as a country girl I did find the street noise distracting in the night - the windows are single paned so we could hear everything at street level. Be prepared for this.
Otherwise, great stay and I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Fine Place to Stay”
text: I stayed here last weekend of July to attend Otakon. From previous experience that crowd can be noisy in the hotels, pleasantly surprised that the small size of this hotel prevented that problem. Hotel itself is unique, I love all the throwbacks to it's days as a bank. Room was simple but comfortable. only complaint would be the tv not working on random occasions. the room could also use a bit more soundproofing, but the city noise was nowhere near unbearable. Staff was friendly, when I was accidentally charged for valet they were apologetic and quick to remove the charge. There were BCPD officers in the building providing security, felt very safe. Location is fabulous, albeit the inconvenient construction on light st: pretty sure it was damage from the water main break so can't fault anyone. I would happily stay here again.

title: “Overrated and not worth the cost”
text:
I just spent three days at the Crowne Plaza Times Square Manhattan for a business conference. It is not worth $400 a night. Regular rooms on the 20-floor range are tiny and average - nothing special. "Priority Club" rooms like mine, on floor 37, were nice but nothing extraordinary.
I had nothing but problems with the $15 wireless internet and it was frustrating to waste time trying to log on. 
no ambience, plain generic atmosphere and indifferent staff made this a hotel to skip on my next long visit to New York.
I wished I had booked at room at the Hudson Hotel - now THAT is a place that will make a trip to New York special.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
My friend and I stayed at the Sofitel on our trip to NYC. Our first criteria was to find a hotel with no bedbug report and a reputation for cleanliness. 
We enjoyed our stay at Sofitel. Absolutely no trace of bedbugs whatsoever and the room was generally spotless. There was a small tear in the wallpaper in the bathroom but nothing that bothered us. The rooms are somewhat pricey but for a hotel of that caliber right next to Times Square, it seemed reasonable. The rooms were quiet and the beds were extremely comfortable, however, some feathers from my comforter were poking through the fabric and sort of stinging me. My friend didn't have that problem­.
Unlike other guests who commented here, we found the service excellent. Polite and helpful. 
We would definitely stay there again.

title: “used to be my new york home, but”
text:
The first time I stayed here was about 15 years ago, it was a new boutique hotel opened in an idea location.
I stayed also in 2004 and 2007, so it gradually became my New York home while I have been tried some other hotels.
However, from my recent experiences I found that the hotel becomes to be disappointing level, for its service quality. Of all, the cleaning ladies were hanging around the small corridor speaking loudly and this does not make you relaxing in the morning till afternoon.
I think I have to find another home now even though the location is still great with this hotel.

title: “Excellent location in Hollywood”
text: I stayed here for 2 nights in September 2011. The hotel is in an excellent location, with Hollywood Boulevard, and the Kodak and Graumann theatres about 10 minutes walk. Although it is close to those areas, the hotel itself is fairly quiet. The rooms are fairly small, but have all the essentials and are clean. There is also free parking, which is a large bonus if you do happen to be driving and there is also a pool located at the back of the complex. The only downside to this hotel is the fact you have to pay extra for breakfast. I found it far cheaper to pick up something on the go from a nearby shop/bakery. I would recommend this hotel for a first trip to LA. If I were to go again, I think I would choose to stay in Beverley Hills, as for all but the central section of Hollywood Boulevard, in my opinion, the area has seen better days.

title: “Bad place!”
text:
I arrived at this hotel, no one behind front desk. Waited 20 minutes. Checked BA to see if desk person was sick. No one there! Shouted for someone 8 times. No answer. Finally, I yelled as loud as I could. A female came out from the shadows walking as slow as possible, glaring at me. Chilling! It was scary! She had my credit card number and I didn't know what to do next. I felt weird and very upset. I needed a cart to go to my room on 3rd floor. She was so oblivious & wouldn't offer to get me help. A stranger offered to find a cart or help me. He wasn't staying there, he was just there. No thank you! Flooding? Towels everywhere on floors.so elevators weren't working, had to lug my stuff up 3 floors.Called the front desk 3x's around 9:30pm. Loud noises above. water extractor running. Frt desk no help! Went up there myself to tell them to stop! I was right below a flooded 4th floor room. Very scary. I didn't sleep all nite. I am sickened by this treatment. It was much worse than these words can explain.
I have a bites that won't go away now!

title: “Home away from Home!”
text:
I feel really terrible that it has taken me two months to write this review especially since I will count this visit and the hotel as one of my most comfortable and fun trips. 
I found this hotel to have the right size ( feels like a little apartment building) where you get to know the bell hop, concierge, the wait staff at happy hour and become so comfortable - the service was just fantastic. I only spent 3 nights here and that was enough time to get this feel. Need a nice lemonade before heading out into the heat, no problem, need a recommendation on where to get brunch within $x budget, done with a smile, want a quick manicure within walking distance - done. Of course I could have checked all these out on my phone as the hotel has complimentary wi-fi, but part of the fun in travel is gettin the inside scoop from the locals and the Amalfi front desk never disappointed. 
Aside from the great service, everything was as reviewers said when I was searching, modern bedroom and bath decor, comfy beds, breakfast on your floor was one of the best things as we would wake up early, stash some yoghurt, scones, fruit and juice, head out for a run along Chicagos beautiful waterfront trails and have some breakfast waiting for us. $ saved. The happy hour was also a lot of fun, just show up on time. The " Amalfitini" was my go to drink and the waiters was just a pleasure. Please remember to tip them as I noticed several people being rude and not even tipping !! Oh and happy hour comes with snacks like bruschetta, veggies and dip, deli meats and pita bread. We used it as an appetizer so by dinner time we just had smaller plates. All in all, the happy hour was above my expectations. 
I tried hard to think of something negative about my experience but with the smiles at the front desk, bell hop, happy hour staff, nothing comes to mind. 
If you are looking for a boutique hotel, with an intimate feeling, within walking distance to most attractions (we walked everywhere!!) this is the spot. I hope to come back soon! Keep up the great work!

title: “One of the BEST places to stay in NYC!!”
text: Stayed here from Oct. 19-22 2012 with a friend. This is not the first time I have stayed here and there is a reason. You could pay more for a hotel in NYC but why? Everything you need is right there. Location could not be better, Hotel runs like a Swiss watch and you have Ellen at the front desk! Rooms are super clean (OCD here and VERY picky) big by NYC standards and quiet. I am in the customer service industry myself here in Toronto and wish I could hire Ellen to come work for me. No request is too much for her. I have never delt with a more pleasant person. We asked (as should you) for a higher floor (they are the quietest) and got it, then asked for a non smoking floor, and got it. Through work I have been able to stay at many NYC hotels over the years (some expensive boutique ones, but work was paying ) and did not care for them. If I am on a trip to New York for pleasure and I am paying for the hotel I will always book myself in at the Park Central. We stayed on the 20th floor and the room was great. As I said, quiet, really, really clean and and a big comfortable bed. Washroom was big and everything worked and agian really clean. Check for their specials on line (or call directly as I did) and make sure to mention you are a CAA/AAA member. If you are hung up on staying at a fancy expensive hotel expecting it to be better then go ahead. What a watse of money! Thanks Ellen for a great stay. Hope to see you again soon!

title: “Amazing”
text: I just returned from my trip to NYC with a friend and our mothers. The hotel was amazing, very beautiful! The people who work at the front desk were very polite and helpful. To be honest the whole staff was.. The doormen were extremly helpful with everything and very very polite. They helped us to get taxis, and basically anything else we had asked or we didnt ask for but they thought would be nice. They were a very nice bunch of boys. I honestly did not want to leave and they made the experience alot more fun. I wish I could have gotten to know them alittle better and to be able to stay in contact with them. All in all the hotel was beautiful way more then I expected, perfect location for everything.

title: “Horrible customer service...which is everything in this industry.”
text:
I am really shocked at some of the treatment we received while staying at the hotel for a wedding. You'd think that hotel management would make sure it's staff treats everyone with respect, but especially when someone picked their hotel as the recommended place to stay for a wedding.
Hotel staff was generally uninformed about event details even though the bride provided them with all the information and travel gifts for her guests (which weren't delivered in a timely fashion). Hotel security was lacking. Guests with the wedding had to actually leave the bar area one night and go somewhere else to avoid some rude random customer who eventually started a fight and was arrested. I can't say for a fact, but I don't think he was even a hotel guest. Regardless, is this a Hyatt Regency or Moe's Tavern?
And the icing on the cake was when the bride's computer was stolen while in possession of hotel staff. As if that wasn't bad enough, hotel management has not offered to reimburse her for her stolen property or done anything more than offer an apology.
Unfortunately service and value are everything in the hotel industry, especially in this economy. If all you care about is a comfortable bed then I guess this will do. For me I demand more for my money. The value is just not there for Hyatt Regency Boston.

title: “Great Botique Hotel”
text: Got a great deal. Right across the street from the St Francis on Union Square. Good room with king size bed. Hotel has a lot of charm.. Friendly staff.

title: “Too positive ratings in my POV”
text: We had a room at 20th floor. We booked the hotel b/c of the good ratings that we found on tripadvisor. However, from the 5 nights we spent, on 3 the TV was not working due to cable issues, Internet down 1 night and on the others, the WIFI signal was very weak so that it was nearly impossible to use it. Also, although the room was on the back side and on the 20th floor, it was very noisy b/c of the AC machines in the back. The room was also very dark. Lastly, on one night where there was heavy rainfall, the rain came in through the window - and this hotel is only a couple of months old. I would not go back to that hotel again.

title: “Highly Recommended! Will be back soon!”
text:
A gem and a great value in a fun location that we will certainly revisit! A true "boutique" with personalized service - not the type of hotel that uses the term "boutique" to cloak "inadequate" or as a euphemism for "no services." Rather, the Helix is a breath of fresh air that is full service, and can be a great vacation spot as well as a perfect spot for business travel. It's fun, has a great crowd, but is not the least bit noisy in the evenings, and the beds are the INCREDIBLE - best night's sleep in a hotel I've ever had. Kid friendly suites are perfect, and the service is relaxed yet high end. Relative to the tourist anthills, it's a bit of a walk to the monuments/mall with small kids, but this is easily navigable by simply grabbing the 14th street bus right outside the hotel and the Helix is close to other attractions like Embassy Row. In addition, some of the double decker "hop on/hop off" tours go right by the hotel. For adults or teens, the walk is completely fine. 
The restaurant scene around the hotel is unbeatable and not touristy, and the hotel is very close to business areas of DC. 
The only "con" I can think of is one shared by many hotels - with two elevators, the wait can be a bit long during "rush hours," but it clears up quickly. Just tack on a few minutes in the morning and you'll be fine. 
Bottom line: A perfect find for value, service and combination of practicality and fun and we feel privileged to have discovered this gem in DC!

title: “Great location, good for families”
text:
After such a long flight from Australia, it was so nice to stay at this hotel with its heavenly beds and very friendly staff. We were first greeted by the very friendly and forward-thinking check-in staff who offered us a small bar fridge in addition to the crib for my baby. (the fridge was so useful to keep snacks and drinks for my ever so hungry toddler) 
Our room is what we expected for a Westin: beautiful heavenly beds that were so comfy that we had the best sleep ever for the 4 nights we stayed in SF. The crib is not just a portable pack and play, it was an actual mobile crib and even the baby slept for a reasonable amount of time (didn't have to get up in the middle of the night for the first time since before he was born). 
The rooms were large and spacious (we had a 2 queen bed) and the flat screen TVs were nice to keep my toddler entertained. The view from our room was of Kearny street and since we were on a lower floor, we could hear some street noise but it did not bother us at all. The 2nd time we checked in, we were given a room on the highest floor (36th) which had no street noise but the view was fantastic: same aspect, but we could see Union Square, San Francisco Bay and the top of the Bay bridge on the other side.
Getting to and from this hotel from the airport using BART was no problem at all and it was convenient to other means of public transport (buses, the F-line, cable car) because of its proximity to Market Street. We were even close to the Amtrak bus pickup point just in front of the Westfield which was a few blocks away. Overall, I'd recommend this place for a hassle-free relaxed stay.

title: “Stay at the Staybridge”
text: All good - nothing bad. Room, service, pool breakfast and location all excellent

title: “Does not live up to the reputation”
text:
We spent a week here for our honeymoon. We found the experience somewhat lacking. We went straight to check in after a 10 hour flight. The staff were apprehensive about assisting us until, after they served several people before us, they discovered we were staying in a suite and their entire attitude changed. I found that approach mercernary at best. Our room was extremely large, however the bathroom was very small and not terribly moden. The whole hotel gave us the impression that it must have been something in its time but some modernising is needed here. 
We were on the 27th floor and we still found street noise a problem, however we soon learnt that this is a new york thing and therefore hardly the fault of the hotel. 
The lifts were not working properly for 2 days while we were there and as we were so high up, taking the stairs was dreadful, especially after walking around the whole of manhattan during the day. 
Our new york experience was somewhat disappointing all round. We found it a soulless, money hungry city.

title: “Tourist Trap!”
text: This hotel has something like 400 rooms, but facilities for maybe 40. As a result, there are long lines for everything. Check in, bag check, breakfast - all long lines. Call the concierge? Ten minutes on hold. Elevators? Wait five minutes each time, often watching cars pass, stuffed with people and no space to get in. The breakfast "buffet" consisted of a few muffins from some convenience store. There was juice and coffee, but no glasses. The staff - what few of them that exist - seemed exhausted and resigned to telling customers to wait and saying sorry. It is not just that it is grossly overpriced, it wouldn't be a nice place to stay at any price. Oh, and the executive floor room was dated and the bathroom tiny. Yes, the location is great, but give me a break!

title: “anything but a dream...”
text:
we chose this hotel because of it's positioning on line and we thought it would be fun.
our first bad impression remained as the overall impression. you enter a hall with a reception desk designed to handle very few customers and our staff was certainly not trained. The design concept is certainly interesting but they fail to do the hospitality part. in a nutshell we rented a room for 3 days not more.

title: “Loved the Grand Union”
text: The hotel was close enough to walk everywhere for both shopping and sightseeing - just a few blocks from Grand Central and the Empire State Building. We only needed to sleep in the hotel so luxury was not an issue. The beds were comfortable and most importantly the bathroom was clean. I found the staff very helpful and loved the attached diner where one could get pancakes in the morning.

title: “Home away from home”
text: I usually don't spend time giving reviews, either good or bad but I'm more than happy to make an exception this time. Yes, the hotel is on the small side but makes it up with great great staff that pays attention to detail..be it the front desk lady (the one that was on duty Saturday morning of 6/20/09) being so welcoming and accommodating and allowing us early check-in allowing my older parents to rest..to the bell hop aka jack of all trade helping a lady customer with her bouquet of flowers by putting it in a vase filled with water..to the housekeepers that kept our room clean and tidy..to the dining staff that made sure breakfast is going smoothly. The location of this hotel is so central to everything that it's just the perfect spot for us or for anyone else for that matter!!! This will be THE PLACE to stay for us whenever we come back to Manhattan. I love NYC!!

title: “Good value, a step back in time”
text: I have stayed at the T&C a few times, for a genetics conference that is held there each year. The property is quite expansive (>40 acres), beautifully landscaped, and if traveling for personal vacation there are a variety of different room options which would be attractive, including cabana-style options near one of the pools. The staff is very friendly; we had a wonderful waitress at one of the breakfast places, named Pati Muklevicz. Overall, a nice place though I should warn that the room decor for the rooms I have stayed in (usually one of the towers) is right out of the 70's, which may or may not be appealing. It is near a golf course as well as a nice, huge mall which has a number of restaurants. Overall a good place to have a conference and take a family as well.

title: “Excellent room, view and staff!”
text: We stayed at The Westin on our first visit to Seattle in August of 2011 and couldn't have been happier with our stay. They immediately upgraded my room for free and we had an awesome view of the Space Needle out of our window. It is also a great location and very easy to walk to many destinations (which is good since the transit system is very disappointing). The building may be a little old, but the important things to my wife and I (cleanliness and service) were top notch. Will stay here again on any future visits.

title: “Loud & Slow”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel in July of 2010 for his annual Coaching school. We only stayed here one night and thank goodness for that. They are remodeling the lobby and I understand that but they do not have to start working at 7 a.m. on a Sunday with a jack hammer and wake everyone in their hotel up. They also were working on the elevators with a hotel full of people their were only 3 elevators operating. It took my husband and I 30 minutes to wait on an elevator. I hope once they are done remodeling that everything is better, because I wouldn't stay here if someone paid me. One more thing I just thought of, My husband and I went up to go check out the pool that was located on the roof, lets just say that it is a really big bathtub nothing more! They really need to work on upgrading that....

title: “Loved the Roosevelt”
text:
Stayed at this hotel 3 years ago and i had a good time but since then the reviews have really started going downhill. Was staying the week before christmas so was a bit apprehensive when i got there, thinking how busy the hotel was going to be and would the be able to look after me. However the reception was brilliant and the christmas tree so inviting that the place couldn't be that bad... could it ?
The receptionist was nice and i got a room on the 5th floor, smallish bath and a small tv but the bed was huge, and the mattress was so soft yet comfy. Of all the things i wanted to bring back home, the mattress was the thing. 
For my 5 nights there, the room was freshly cleaned everyday and there were lots of channels on the tv. It was quiet and i was near the stairs but never heard anything, either outside or from my neighbours.
I think there most be some poor rooms in the hotel and maybe its just pot luck what you get when you arrive but for me, i enjoyed the Roosevelt and would stay again.

title: “Great location at a fraction of the price”
text: Location! Location! Location! 0.1 mile from the Empire State Building. Walking distance to shopping, restaurants and to the tour bus route. Continental breakfast served. Rooms though small and basic are clean. Request for a higher floor for better city view. Friendly staff. No concierge, any planning requests like taxi service or tour tickets have a fee. Plan tours on your own or ahead of time.

title: “Spacious rooms in convenient downtown location”
text:
I recently traveled to NYC for business but brought my five-year old for fun - I made the mistake of reserving a trendy hotel nearby that I could not stay at with daughter. We called the Omni which welcomed us at 11 pm with a gift basket for my daughter and a room upgrade. The Omni has unusually spacious rooms for a NYC hotel and it's worth becoming a member to enjoy the complimentary coffee and juice they leave at your door. The rooms are clean, the hallways are quiet, and everyone working there is lovely as well. 
My only complaint was the service at the bar during the daytime - we left without eating after waiting over half an hour. However, the manager handled it very well and offered us a complimentary meal another time.
ps great location if you plan to visit the American Girl store.

title: “Great for a weekend getaway!”
text: Stayed two short nights at this property and was very pleased with the staff, accommodations, amenities and location. Even though, we couldn't really walk to where we wanted to go, it was easy to jump in a taxi and head out. The room was extremely comfortable and I would defintely stay here again if I found myself in Dallas!

title: “Not the largest rooms, but great loaction and superior service!”
text: For a Wyndham resort I wouldnt say the rooms are quite as impressive as others, but that is easily made up for with the great location and top notch service. Who needs a big room in New York anyway? You'll probably end up only using your room to sleep! Of course, this is the city that never sleeps so you might not need your room at all! Make sure you book this one way ahead of time, its a real gem!

title: “Nothing Special”
text: I stayed here for a work trip. The room is nothing special. It's small, there is a TV (which I did not use), and a desk. I didn't have any issues with the internet, so no complaints there. The AC unit was next to the window, which did not relieve the stickiness of the room much in warm summer weather. The staff was friendly and the garden outside was a nice place to sit and relax. It is certainly not a five-star place but if you are just planning on sleeping here, it should be fine.

title: “Great Hotel, Perfect Location”
text: The location was absolutely perfect. Yes the room and bath were a bit small, but well appointed with comfortable beds, large flat screen TV, HBO and plenty of channels. The rooms were cleaned and restocked each day and they brought a wine opener upon request (no charge). The pool is also small, but they make up for it with the Jacuzzi, fresh fruit, water, and towels. The atrium is gorgeous with fresh exotic flowers and several grand chandeliers. I loved it so much I extended my stay an extra night! Good job Marriott. D.C. has happy hour deals everyday so you'll have no problem finding a place to hang out, have a drink and a decent meal.

title: “Don't overpay for this motel”
text:
This place was old, the parking a joke (I'm just happy my car didn't get broken into overnight) and breakfast just barely edible. Other than that, you get what you pay for if you get a $75 a night rate like we did. We were there for 2 nights to see friends graduate from the Corps. One of our friends was charged $125 for the same room. They seem to up the rates near graduation time. The shuttle's are old and run down and only seat 9. Waits at the base and hotel were up to 1 hr.. The neighborhood's full of strip clubs and bars but close to the base.
Time for a complete renovation!
PS: Somebody may want to complain to San Diego PD about all the bums camping on the street and sidewalk between the hotel's buildings.

title: “Nice hotel, good customer service, great location”
text: The Beacon was a nice hotel. The beds felt like i was sleeping on clouds. It was clean and had great customer service. Also, its in a convenient location. It is 5 blocks from the white house, a block away from embassy row and just a few stops on the metro from the Smithsonian, Washington Monument, Lincoln monument etc. My only problem with this hotel is that it was a little too pricey for what i was getting. Although there were some pros but a couple cons as well. There was no ice bucket, fridge, or shower cap. But other than that it was great.

title: “This is my new favorite place to stay in the city!!!”
text: I've been to NYC many times and stayed in several different hotels, but I can now say I've found THE place to stay. The Hampton Inn Soho is really clean, with a lovely breakfast dining room and courtyard. The staff are extremely helpful and courteous and the location is great. The #1 subway is a block away (providing easy access to midtown, times square and/or upper west side), and the nearby shopping is outstanding. There are many European boutiques to browse, several art galleries and lots of great places to eat. The rooms at the Hampton Inn Soho are somewhat small (it's NYC!!!) but extremely clean and the bathrooms are contemporary and spacious. I had a room with a king bed and it was really comfortable and had lovely European-style linens. There was a flat screen tv as well, with many channels and in-room movies. The complimentary breakfast was ample and the staff had even prepared "to go" breakfast bags for folks who wanted breakfast but didn't have time to sit down. There was a business center with two computers in the lobby. When the hotel gets a liquor license, travelers will be able to come back from a day of touring and enjoy a glass of wine. All of this, combined with a reasonable price, what's not to like?

title: “Excellent hotel . Very good staff . I strongly recommend”
text: Very nice hotel ;Helpful staff day and night , parking facility ,excellent room service . All this in a very good location

title: “A great nights sleep”
text: first time at this place. Loved the room and very comforable bed. The only draw back might have been the very long walk from the parking area.

title: “Great Time at the MARK”
text:
Had a great two days at the Mark Hopkins and found cheaper parking down the street at the Masonic auditorium ($30 per 24 hours) and also at Grace Catherdral ($27 per 24 hours). Asked for flatter pillows after the first night and were given these quickly from house keeping - great service!!! Wireless internet was 12.95 per 24 hours. Did not take the service. Had morning buffet breakfast at the Top of the Mark. It was outstanding.
Beautiful views form the top of the mark; get a seat over by the bar - a window seat if you can handle the heights!!! Well worth the few breaths you will lose as you sit there taking in the City.

title: “Great Location; friendly staff!”
text:
We chose this hotel for my wife's 50th birthday, and, thanks to tripadvisor, we made a grear choice! Small enough to be personal, yet well equiped and friendly. The position is excellent for midtown. Surrounded by great restaurants, it is situated between 5th Avenue and Broadway, and all the major sights and shops can be managed on foot. Special thanks to David James and Walter - concierges who really know their Manhattan and were able to recommend great restaurants for any cuisine or budget.
We are looking forward to going back already!

title: “AWESOME!”
text: Great hotel, very central to everything San Diego. Close to all transportation, shopping, & food. Good customer service througout the duration of our family stay. Staff is very friendly & accomodating for all requests. Great ammenities on the property.

title: “Stay away.”
text:
I stayed in NYC at the Hotel31 for 7 days in March 2004. I found their ad in a gay rag paper. Although they are not a 'gay hotel', they advertise heavily in gay media.
The hotel was way below what you can expect.
When I arrived, they couldn't find my reservation anymore; they blamed their internet company for that. I was lucky though, the requested kind of room was still available. The heating did not work in my room, it was freezing cold. A few days after I requested additional blankets I finally got them. Hotel staff did not fix the heating, they said simply that on the upper floors the heating system doesn't work properly. For several days the only elevator did not work. Not much fun when your room is on floor 8. TV didn't work either, and the telephone had its problems as well, due to a 'software problem', as reception staff let me know.
Most annoying was that the guy at the reception desk took money from my credit card account that was NOT AUTHORIZED by me. That's like taking cash directly out of your pocket without asking.
Don't need to tell you that there were no refunds for anything. I could add a few more things. 
Yes, Hotel31's rates are low, but you don't get anything but a bad hotel. Spend a few extra bucks and go somewhere more reliable.

title: “Loved loved loved it!”
text: My husband and I recently stayed at the downtown Sheraton! The service was great the room was wonderful and the manager was so helpful with directions and advice on things to do. Everyone was sooo friendly. Will stay there on every trip to Denver and will advise my friends and family to do the same!

title: “Location Location Location”
text: That is all this hotel has going for it, the check in line was rediculous. We arrived late afternoon and did not get into our room until after 9pm. The rooms were massive but smelled old and musty however the bathrooms were small and outdated. Paint chips and rust covered the bathroom. The room was over priced. I would not recommend this hotel, not even for one night which is all i stayed for.

title: “The best hotel in New York City...”
text:
you will see what I am talking about if you stay here.
The customer service is the best. My partner and I have been staying here for years. We will only stay elsewhere if they are booked. Which happens often.
They have a fantastic breakfast. If you have children or several people in your party you can have a full breakfast here. They have everything. Also for dinner they have light snacks, which you can fill up on and get a light dinner somewhere else.
We've requested late check out and they have always granted it. In the past we have also left late in the day and they never charge for that day like most hotels do. When we leave things behind they ship them to us.
There is a deli steps away and they have the best club sandwhiches in the city. The chinese place has amazing food as well.
I love this place and you will too once you've stayed here.
Cheers.

title: “Hip upscale property”
text: Stayed two nights 11/2-11/4. we were able to check in early at 1PM, front desk staff was friendly and helpful, which was nice after traveling by train for 4.5 hours. Bell/door staff were helpful with locations to eat off property and directions, as well as getting cabs quickly. Our room was very clean and had great finishes and nice linens. The rain shower was nice and soothing after after long walking trips exploring the city.

title: “Great Management Staff”
text: Especially Adriana, who is always cheerful and helpful. This last trip, my wife offhandedly mentioned that she was a few months pregnant, and Adriana had a wonderful and thoughtful personal gift waiting in our room when we returned after dinner. Heart-warming.

title: “Very good but one night was enough.”
text:
Our first day in LA we decided to stay at the Roosevelt to get a real taste of Hollywood. The location was absolutely perfect for us to take in the walk of stars and the sights. Check-in was easy and the staff was very helpful in getting our bags to the room. The hotel is very beautiful, kind of a mixture of old Hollywood with newer more modern accents throughout. While it is a very dark interior, it doesn't feel depressing or old. The room was on the small side. We had 2 queen, maybe even full, beds. There was a flat screen TV and a fridge with the honor bar. The bathroom was TINY. Hardly had room to move for one person never mind my kids. We had a great meal at the restaurant downstairs, even though the service was a bit slow. 
My main negatives about this hotel are:
-the hotel is definitely better suited for the grown up customer. At 2:00 AM we discovered through the paper thin walls that the couple next door had just returned from partying and wanted to chat for the next 3 hours. We could hear every word spoken. We actually kicked in the very loud AC to drown their voices.
-the room was adequate but not as nice as I expected based on the rest of the hotel decor. The rug appeared a bit worn and dirty. The bathroom was ridiculously small.
-No Marilyn Monro mirror as described in the website. We were told the room it was in had received a renovation recently and it was never put back in place. My husband and kids were quite disappointed at this.
-the pool area, while beautiful, appeared to not be a place to bring kids. An older scene was definitely in place during our stay.
Overall, we're glad we stayed here but with kids you just can't get the most out of the hotel.

title: “Great place in a great location”
text:
As cold as it was in Chicago, we still managed to have a great time, underwritten as that usually is by the quality of our lodgings.
The euro-chic approach of the sofitel is familiar to urbane British travellers, but it was still a delight to check in to a stylish lobby and then discover the spacious room we had been given.
You could'nt quite see the Hancock tower from the room, but the view wasn't terrible.
In keeping with what you would expect of a French hotel, the room was well appointed, the staff polite and discreet and the clientele seemed quite colourful, much as we kept ourselves to ourselves as we explored the city and spent too much on taking advantage of the strength of Sterling.
A 2 minute walk to Michigan Avenue, a proper local cafe and supermarket on the same block - the location was perfect.
I think the reason this gets 5 stars has to be the fact they have the most comfortable beds, a complicated construction of layers, but do they ever do the job in ensuring a restful nights sleep.

title: “A beautiful place and perfect location for historic DC.”
text: This hotel is just a gorgeous piece of historical preservation. The lobby is beautiful and the rooms are large and beautiful. The front desk was outstanding. You can walk to most historic locations and enjoy the area. Highly recommended!

title: “Good Location--Odd Hotel”
text:
This property is located on Michigan Ave. very near Millennium Park. Fantastic location. However that creates some issues. You have to drive to the Hard Rock Hotel and wait for someone from the Comfort Suites to walk over with a luggage cart.
The Hotel is very skinny--and tall. The "lobby" is a vestibule. There are only two elevators and they are tiny. Be prepared for waits.
We stayed Friday and Saturday nights. Breakfasts ended at 9 am both mornings. We had been out late at a concert and then a play. Most places with free breakfasts have later end-times on the weekend.
We asked for an extra hour for checkout and were told that we could have it for an extra 10 dollars. Really? We expected a yes or no. The charge was pretty funny and we declined.
We stayed here because of the rate--and would do so again to save as much money as we did. But there is no other reason to stay here.

title: “Very nice”
text: Great stay! Stayed one night and took shuttle to and from the airport. Timely shuttle service, friendly staff, clean room and comfortable bed!

title: “Beautiful, modern hotel with great service!”
text: I stayed here recently for a business trip and loved it. The design is gorgeous and welcoming, the desk staff charming, and it is truly full service. Very W like in terms of the feeling, which made it a restful place at the end of a long business day. Highly recommended.

title: “Hard to get in and out of this hotel”
text: This hotel was very pretty. The grounds were very nice, pool area was especially pretty. Breakfast was OK. The room smelled of cigarette smoke even though I requested non smoking room. Please put a trash can in the area where the toilet is located. A/C went out second night and I was not charged for this night of my stay.

title: “A Great Place to Stay”
text: We had a great time at the colannade. The room was very comfortable and the dinner was outstanding.

title: “Not bad”
text: I came to NYC for a short vacation. This hotel is almost 100 years old so I expected flaws. The lobby was very nice. The room was outdated with broken furniture and peeling wallpaper. The beds were comfortable and the bathroom was nice. Located right next to Penn Station and walking distance to Times Square and subways to other attractions.

title: “Like staying with Friends in NYC”
text: We stayed at the Chelsea Pines Inn for a couple of nights in October 2012. We stayed here based on the reviews at trip advisor (so thank you all)...this place is amazing. Every person who works for the Chelsea Pines Inn was very helpful! They spent almost 10 minutes telling us where to go for lunch and dinner as well as things to do around the hotel. The rooms were cozy and comfortable. The shower was amazing!!! Also, the included breakfast was awesome!! Fresh muffins (blueberry, chocolate, etc...)! We want to thank all the staff at the Chelsea Pines Inn! We will stay there the next time that we are in NYC.

title: “Great value, great location, great hotel!”
text:
I've stayed at The Pod in New York twice - once in 2008 and most recently in March 2010.
I think it is an excellent hotel. The location is superb. Very centrally located in Midtown on East 51st street - just a few minutes walk from Radio City Music Hall, Rockefeller Center and many of the other sights in central New York City. It is also very close to a Subway station.
The rooms are small, and mine had a shared bathroom. There are four bathrooms on each floor and usually only one or two of them was occupied at a time so it was not a problem to get a shower or whatever at any time.
