The bathrooms are beautiful - with great showers and facilities. For me it was not much of an issue that it was shared.
In my experience, there was little if any outside noise. The nearby street is not that busy and there was no notable noise from my fellow guests at the hotel. 
The staff does an excellent job when it comes to cleaning the rooms and the hotel at large generally feels very clean and tidy. 
The rooms come with a flat-screen TV with 30+ channels and an iPod docking station which I personally never got to use, but seems like a very nifty extra. There's also a small safe in your room that you can use at your convenience, and apparently free WiFi (I didn't bring a laptop).
The staff is friendly and wants to help. One cool service is that you can leave your bag at the hotel for a few hours after check out and come back to get it later. 
For the location, and the general quality of the hotel, the price of the rooms is pretty reasonable. 
All in all, I would highly recommend The Pod!

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
We stayed at Le Meridien the last 2 nights of our 17 day trip in California. October 11th to the 13th. We had already explored the fishermans Wharf area the week before, so this was a perfect location,.
Upon Check in I ask for a room on an upper floor with a bay view. She said lets see what we have and gave me a room on the 24th floor overlooking the bay. 
The Blue Angles were in town and we watched them right from the window of the room. The hotel was very accomodating I was not expecting this as we booked it through priceline and had a very very low rate. 
Room service was very fast and the food was hot. The internet use had a charge to hook up in the room, unlike our last hotel, but they had 4 user stations in the business center that we used instead.
The room was large, clean and had a cd player with speakers next to the flat screen television. 
The staff was so helpful everytime we had a question and Barb and Laura the concierge's on duty were above and beyond. 
When we were packing to leave we called and ask the front desk for tape for our box of wine, and they said someone would be up in 10 min or so. Moments later there was a knock on the door, I don't know how he arrived so fast.
Over all the experience was exceptional. We have stayed at many nice hotels, but the service here was 'OUTSTANDING"

title: “My favorite hotel in Denver”
text:
The Teatro is about as good as it gets.
Checked in for one of the those -- gotta get out of my crazy teenager's house ( if you have teenagers, you know, it's no longer your house).
Check in: Easy as pie-- Upgraded without being asked. Wow
Suite: Absolutely stunning. Was upgraded to a Jr Suite, not the best in the house, but great for our needs.
The bathroom is what made Teatro 5 stars. Granite everything, flat screen, jetted huge soaking tub, shower for 2 with multiple shower heads. AVEDA products !!!!! 
Even came with an option to have a professionally drawn tub. For $25 you can have the bath of your dreams, rose petals and aromatherapy.
Worth every penny !!!
The bed itself was reminiscent of a cloud. Soft and comfy. Sitting area well thought out, with a work station attached to the wall opposite the bed. The room was Wifi, and there was a printer hidden under the counter. Just terrific !!
Normally we would go outside the hotel for dinner, but Kevin Taylor had not 1 but 2 restaurants here, so what's another couple of bucks..right?
I'll review the restaurant separately, but for those going to another restaurant, take the free Denali wherever you want to go. I had a girl's lunch the next day, with a bit of shopping, and my driver was terrific. He dropped me on Broadway, and picked me up somewhere completely different. Just call the number and provided you're within a 5 or so mile radius, your ride is there is 10 minutes.
Checkout -- Just as easy as check in .
Note to Management:
The only " draw-back,", if you will.... 
Reservations needs to be advised of advertised specials.
As local Denver-ites, it's aggrevating to read the Denver Post, where you're getting Free Advertising for being part of specials as the Mile High Holidays, and $52.80 nights, only to call, and speak to agents who have no knowledge of the special rates.
I would have loved to stay there again, as we're interviewing hotel for our upcoming wedding, but am staying at the Oxford, who honored the advertised rate.
Hopefully we'll be able to try you again before picking the nuptial spot, and hotel where our NY family will stay.

title: “Best Hip Hotel”
text: Just returned from my stay at the hote on rivington. It was a get away weekend from my girlfriend and I and we couldn't have had a better experience. We had a great room with such a breathtaking view at night. The service was great and all the employees went out of their way to make us feel so welcome. We were both first time visitors and we fell in love with Ny and this hotel. I would reccomend this hotel to anyone looking for great rooms and service.

title: “Conveniently located downtown”
text: Impeccable rooms, wonderful staff and well-appointed for the business traveller. Only lose marks on price point for breakfast. Very expensive for the budget-minded convention attendee. I travel for government and the breakfast exceeded per diems by quadruple.

title: “good hotel but bring ear muffs!”
text: Stayed a week on business. Staff uniformily friendly and professional. Bedroom large and well equipped with excellent bathroom. Facilities in room very good but noise proofing was awful and from 16th floor I was disturbed every night and early morning by external noise. But for this I would have graded hotel excellent overall although more exercise equipment in the gym please!

title: “Very Good Location, But bad «money for value»”
text:
Very good location, near atractive places. 
Too many noisly students (groups of 30/40 boys and girls). Rooms are clean, but very old for 220,00 USD/per day, without breakfast. Very expensive.
Staff and service - Regular.

title: “Best hotel around”
text: Robert , Phyllis & Tanner are a lot of help , great workers! Not one complaint about anyone that works here , great group of people. I will return to this hotel every time i am in the area. The rooms are spotless , everyone is so professional and all services are above standard. I will recommend every single person that i come across to stay at the Hyatt Place. Fresh baked cookies are the best.

title: “Great Downtown Hotel & Staff”
text:
Spent a recent weekend at this hotel and was extremely pleased with the entire visit in every aspect. This was our first time ever in Denver but not our last. The staff was amazingly friendly, knowledgeable about the area and helpful in every aspect. We've met a lot of great people at hotel & rental properties but the ones at the Monaco in Denver stood out. Not only friendly but followed up on every inquiry we had, from room service, to champagne request, they would call or come check to make sure it was all OK and right for us. The cost of this room was also very very reasonable - I thought we had gotten a special deal (my wonderful lady is good at finding those deals) but after talking to others it turned out the hotel just had great weekend rates - In short, the value and services provided were exceptional for the cost. 
Rooms were very very well furnished and had everything anyone could want in your stay... Very comfortable bed covered with great variety of pillows. Every lamp had plugs in the base which was very helpful in setting up chargers and other devices. Mini Bar was well stocked, snacks, etc...
Room Service was extraordinary - probably the best breakfast in months and certainly in the top five every in our hundreds of hotel stays! hats off to the chef and folks that brought it up.
They had a free wine hour in the lobby where we met some other great guests and tasted some really decent wine - well above what we expected after coming in from a chilly walk around downtown Denver. Hotel is a couple blocks off the 16th Street Mall (fun place on pre-Halloween Saturday night). Walking distance to anything and everything downtown. 
In summary - we are planning another trip back to Denver in the near future and not a chance we would stay anywhere else. Highly recommend this hotel to all of our friends & Family.

title: “A dead ringer for The Addams Family home”
text:
We stayed here when working at the Convention Centre in Washington and it was incredibly convenient. The room was pleasant, the bed extremely comfortable, the shower was great and it was good to have a bath too.
The staff were mixed, we checked in late at night after a long wait at reception and a bit more speed and courtesy would have been great. We tried breakfast there twice and the service was slow and inaccurate so we ate in a neighbourhood diner after that. The one exception was the doorman who was a star at calling taxis.
The hotel is quiet and provides a good base in Washington, even if they hiked the prices over the period we were there.

title: “Weekend Away”
text: I was traveling out of the PHL airport and needed a hotel near the airport because of a very early flight. I had stayed at the Edison, NJ Renaissance before and found it appealing so I decided to stay within the company chain. The price of the hotel did not do it justice. For a Friday night stay it was well worth the money. I arrived late due to work and was exhausted and I still had to print my boarding pass and get something to eat. I arrived at the hotel and found Rachel at the front desk, after waiting in line for a short while because what it seemed like 2 airline crews beat me to the desk, she was amazingly helpful and kind. She showed me to their office area to print my boarding pass and then I needed help because the computers were not working. She spent a nice deal of time fixing the problem and helped me with what I needed. The entire time she smiled and was extremely guest friendly. She is a great asset to your team and I do plan on frequent this hotel when I can. Thank you for an amazing stay.

title: “Unhelpful”
text: Arrived at the hotel to register which was on 3rd floor for Queen Mary 2 passengers. Waited 20 mins for an elevator, our group was eventually taken in the service elevator in order to clear the lobby area. No chairs were available despite my husband being disabled. Next day the lift got stuck on the 6th floor for 25 mins until we were able to open doors and change to the second lift. I asked reception staff if they could confirm the time of transport the following morning back to the ship, no-one seemed to know anything about it and didn't want to find out. Before checking out we were told to leave cases outside the room for collection, on checking out we were told inside the room. After again waiting some time for an elevation, the maid was cleaning our room and refused to allow the cases back inside. After waiting for a phone call from housekeeping to clarify the situation, I took the cases to the lobby myself. I gave the room keys to reception and told them what had happened, again they were dis-interested. We had a wait of about two hours in the lobby area after returning our keys, again very limited seating was available and some people were obliged to sit on the floor. The last straw was having to ask a member of the cleaning staff to unlock the restrooms in the lobby with a door key. One lift was out of order and the other two were very slow, the hotel staff were totally unhelpful and unsympathetic. Only recommendation - the location.

title: “Expensive, but quite good”
text:
I would agree with that, although good, the Iroquois was not quite as good as I had expected, particularly for the price paid. The lobby is still under major renovations, and again this was not mentioned when I booked or apologised for. Service from front desk was efficient but not very warm, I was reluctant to go back for further information as it felt like you were bothering them at times. Given this is a Small Luxury Hotel, I would have expected more. 
The room and bathroom were small-ish, but fine, certainly by European standards. I very much liked the decor and fittings, and the bed was extremely comfortable. 
We had an 8th floor room with absolutly no view (a brick wall) and very noisy generators outside. We're not particularly bothered by noise, but this was quite noticeable.
Given that the stay cost approx £250 per night per room (and of course there's no breakfast included in that) this was an expensive hotel, and I certainly wouldn't call it value for money, but I'm not sure that that isn't typical of most NYC hotels.

title: “The Hotel Wilshire”
text:
I traveled to Los Angeles to be on an early morning show at KFWB Radio Los Angeles to promote my book "Save Your Home, without losing your mind or your money" I can honestly say it was a great find. The room was so modern and stylish, the bed and sheets were so comfy. I will definitely be back!!! Highly recommend this boutique hotel. The staff is friendly and it is centrally located. Finally a hotel that posts real pictures that are true to what you get....actually ...it was even better than the pictures. Smaller boutique hotel - fabulous. 
Anna Cuevas
Founder of askaloanmodguru.com

title: “Ideal for a Celebration with Family and Friends”
text: We selected Washington Plaza to celebrate a happy family event in the DC area with 20+ guests, ranging from teenagers to seniors and including some veteran travelers. The hotel offered an excellent location, close to the National Mall, museums, and the White House, easy access to public transportation, a beautiful swimming pool, and comfortable rooms. Our guests were most pleased with the amenities. The pool was a treat, especially as the temperatures was in the 90s during our stay. The lobby area is spacious and a nice place to meet. The restaurant serves an excellent buffet breakfast with several healthy choices, and the dinner was also very good. The staff was most accommodating, friendly and helpful. We highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Big dissapointment”
text: This hotel, which was fairly expensive and was advertised as a "premier hotel," was full of problems. The worst problem was the lack of parking for guests. There was a convention going on while we were there, and every night when we returned, there was no parking. We had to park in some office park around the corner (hard to find) and walk in the dark (with two tired children) quite a distance to the hotel. This was not accepable at all, and the staff barely appologized. We had two rooms: one had a terrible odor, the other had mold on the ceiling by the a.c.vent. Rugs were soilded, coffee pot broken. Breakfast in the restaurant was inordinately expensive, requiring guests to order the whole buffet, and not order more economical a la carte items. Difficult with children. Although the location was good for us, and I guess I could say it was Okay, I would not stay there again. With children, I would much rather pay less for an "acceptable" hotel, have breakfast included, and parking guaranteed.

title: “Average+ (Pool and gym makes it a big +)”
text: First of all, i don't go on holidays to sit in my hotel room all day long. As long as the room is clean, ac working and it smells nice, i'm satisfied. This hotel fullfilled all those demands. It also had a little gym and a clean pool. We were in the pool all day long, and it was very clean. It's not so much nearby, but if you have a car it's good. (We had) I'd stay again!

title: “Wow - old school American classicism at its best.”
text: I stayed here to celebrate a birthday and it was fantastic. We were on a high club floor and the views uptown were spectacular. Exploring NYC, we didn't eat in the hotel every day but if you get a chance to visit Bull & Bear, I highly recommend it (as a hotel guest or not).

title: “Average at best”
text:
I was in new York for work, and chose the hotel based on location, and had stayed there previously about 7 years ago. I'll start with the positives...
Location is great, the subway station for the R line is right outside the hotel. The R will take you up to union square, 42nd, 5th and 59th....so that is quite handy. 
View was great, it was interesting to watch the progress of the WTC site. 
Concierge was very helpful, knowledgable and very easy to deal with.
The downside? Where to start? Service is pretty poor, The standard response to any request is that there will be a charge. I.e. wi-fi access, room changes, late check out etc...I have gold status with hilton which means all of the above should be free....it was only when I reminded them of their own policies that they changed their tune.
To be fair, they upgraded me to a suit, provided a code for the wifi and agreed to a late check out, but they still came up to the room to "remind me" which was annoying.
The hotel is busy, with business travellers and tourists, and my guess is not a lot of repeat business so they don't really care much.
If you get a cheap deal and only need a bed for the night, give it a go, otherwise avoid like the plague.

title: “Business conference in Manhattan”
text: As places go, this one was very nice. A bit on the pricey side, but what do you expect for a weekday right smack in the middle of Manhattan -- literally steps from Time's Square. I had a business conference that was hosted by this hotel and decided to stay on property at their discounted rate -- which was less than any of the other properties nearby this time of year. You are one block from Time's Square, the subway is one block in either direction, Bryant park is a block away, and there are quite a few eating establishments right nearby. I found the pub called the perfect pint, just across the street, to be an excellent place to unwind.

title: “The best place on the Hill”
text: Although this hotel was being used extensively for several huge conferences while we stayed there, we were treated well, not like part of a herd, from beginning to end of our stay. Check in was a breeze--I reserved online. The room was generously sized and kept clean the two days we were there. Room service was zippy, and the bed was very comfy. Service personnel were friendly. Our checkout was eased by the attentive service of Nadim who made sure our boarding passes printed properly and gave us a map with instructions for our journey by metro out of the city. He made us feel like he really cared. We had a great stay here. Definitely recommend.

title: “TODD SOLIDAY was so amazing He helped me and my son with everything”
text: Todd and Kyle were so nice. The room was SO BIG you could have fit 3 queen size beds easy.It was so clean .flat screen tv.TRANSPORTATION IS RIGHT OUTSIDE THE HOTEL.I have already told all my friends.The PRICE CANT BE BEAT. STAY THERE TOM AND ZAK ERIE PA.

title: “The Talbott Hotel is the best”
text:
On a whim, we decided to spend New Years Eve in Chicago. We did a lot of research and settled on the Talbott. From the moment we arrived and saw the cow climing up the building to the moment we left, we were delighted about every aspect of our stay. 
The staff was incredible. Without fail, every single staff person we encountered smiled and greeted us and treated as if they were pleased we were spending our leisure dollars at their establishment. Such an easy way to impress customers...but so rare in the hospitality industry.
The lobby was cozy and beautifully decorated for the holidays. Our room (the one room suite) was clean, comfortable, and full of extra amenities. The beds were comfortable, the linens felt wonderful, and the bathroom was outstanding. We loved the bathrobe and actually purchased one at checkout.
We generally stay away from hotel restaurants, but we got behind schedule one evening and two mornings and found ourselves settling for the hotel restaurant. We were pleasantly surprised that the food was so good. For breakfast, we highly recommend the pancakes and the omlets. The only problem was a stale croissant on the second day. For dinner, we recommend the whitefish...it was outstanding. And of course, in keeping with the hotel standards, the staff was outstanding. 
The biggest miss of the weekend was the horrid internet connection. It didn't affect us much because we only used it to locate pubs, nightlife, and restaurants. But had we been there for work, it would have been a deal-breaker. Note to The Talbott...whoever is handling your internet service needs to be replaced. We are both in that line of work and it's not that tough. 
We will most certainly choose The Talbott Hotel the next time we visit Chicago.

title: “Walk To The Marine Barracks"”
text: The location allows you to walk to the "Marine Barracks, 8th & I Sts." for the summer Friday nite "Evening Parade" and dinner at the fine restaurants on the way. Room was quiet, clean and bed was just right. Plenty of space in room, a refrigerater with a freezer that works. "Continental" breakfast was more than enough choices as well as not crowded, but we had to walk to a different bldg. Not a problem in nice weather. Downside was $35.84/nite valet parking with no alternate choices. Though prompt service was noted. Decor is somewhat dark and shows wear, but well kept and excellent front desk service. Price was an excellent value and directly behind "Library of Congress" bldg, in a residential neighborhood. Upon leaving, noted a diner right up the street for add'l meals. Internet at 2 desks in lobby, always occupied by guests.

title: “Watch your property. Great location, Rooms dated; Good staff.”
text:
I've stayed in hotels all over the world and for the last 5 years normally stay in Hyatt's, Starwood's and Hilton's. As I know what to expect and exactly what I am going to get.
The Westgate was my bosses idea, due to it being a little cheaper than my suite at the Sheraton; which I was very comfortable in. The Westgate has a pretty decent lobby; seems quite inviting, though getting into the rooms is a big letdown. They were generally tired with stains on some carpets and seats; the pillows had definitely seen better days. The gym though small had most exercise equipment. No pull, and occasionally I had too remind staff that I had called for room service, etc. Free internet which is excellant (saves $15 a day or so) Staff in general were pretty helpful, though not all that engaging except in the bar and front desk. Basically its no match to the hotels I normally frequent on long business stays.
Lastly the additional fee's & taxes stink !!! After 23 days of staying at the Westgate, I will probably not stay there again as San Diego has a lot of hotels in equally decent locations.

title: “Good for the Kids”
text: I was in Arizona for school but my family and kids came down and went to the resort. They loved it the water was heated so even though it was a little cool when we were there the kids loved the water and had a blast. We even went to a park close by one night and went scorpion hunting with black lights great trip.

title: “Too ghostly, too dim”
text:
My 12-year old daughter and I stayed in room 37 in April with a shared bathroom. While the hotel has 'character' , I wasn't comfortable during the stay. The room was tiny - not helped by the extra furniture which made it look quaint but simply added clutter. As another guest said, the lights are very dim....far too dim....including in the bathroom. The curtain in our room was also broken, meaning there was very little natural light in the room. And the bed was more than firm - it was hard.
There's no lift or elevator...bit of a pain with luggage, but nothing major. Staff were generally nice, apart from one guy who was nothing short of rude early in the morning when we left. There's free internet access. The location is pretty close to the metro. It could have been a lot worse, but after having visted 5 cities in five weeks, it was the accommodation we enjoyed the least.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: I stayed at this hotel for business and found it to be a great place to stay. It was very clean and the staff were nice. The free wireless and wired internet are great. I will definitely stay here again.

title: “The Best”
text:
We live just outside Seattle, but when my husband and I need a romantic get-away from the kids, The Sorrento is where we head. The rooms are fabulous, the location an easy walk to the downtown area, the food is top-notch and the staff are outstanding. Without any prompting, we found a bottle of wine and a selection of cheese, crackers and fruit in our room when we arrived.
We cannot recommend this hotel highly enough if you are looking for a small, intimate, quiet and romantic place to stay as opposed to the larger chains. Wonderful!

title: “Will definitely return”
text: The Ritz Carlton sits on top of Water Tower Place right on the Magnificent Mile so the location can't be beat. You take the elevator up and it's like stepping into a little oasis of luxury and calm in the midst of Chicago. Rooms are well done and very comfortable. My room had beautiful views of Lake Michigan which I enjoyed. Great tubs in the bathroom and lots of nice little touches. Very comfortable beds too. The food in the restaurant is excellent and I ate there for several meals while I was there. The only negative was that service in the restaurant was spotty depending on who the assigned server is. The first lunch I had there, I had to make several requests to get a drink, menu and after asking for my check, ended up having to walk over to the desk to ask for my check a second time, although the restaurant was fairly empty. However, the manager was very apologetic going as far as picking up the check and having a bottle of wine sent to my room. He went above and beyond to make it better. Had different servers for other meals which was a big improvement. There is also a nice lobby bar which we enjoyed as well. All in all a very good service experience and a nice luxury property. I would highly recommend staying here and plan to return.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: This is one of the nicest Holiday Inns I have ever stayed in. Service was very good.....the front desk person Angela was the best! I would stay here anytime for business or pleasure.

title: “Nice for my discounted price; warm”
text: I got a preferred member discount and decided to give this place a try despite the negative reviews. Overall, this was a great hotel. Clean and comfortable. The hallways are very warm & my ac said it was 65 but it was more like 85. I have never sweated so much inside (sorry to be gross but that's how I felt). I would be happy to give it another try in the dead of winter. If you want clean & safe, this is a nice stop. AC not high on the list.

title: “outof towner”
text: I stayed here on SAIC parent's weekend. Location was great, my room was large with a very comfortable bed. the L train was outside my window but I barely heard it. the staff was friendly and very helpful when I lost my wedding ring and they were able to find it.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Our stay was great. Service was very friendly and very accommodating. The location is perfect, too. It's sometimes difficult to find your way around town if you stray from the Riverwalk. When we first checked in, we were put in a smaller room with no balconey. I called and they immediately let us switch to a room with two of them. They also gave us a late check-out with no questions asked. They say that their margaritas are great and they're not lying! Will only stay there from now on when visiting San Antonio.

title: “Convenient hotel in Times square”
text: The hotel was a block from the subway and close to Broadway, also walking distance to Central Park. It was a decent size room for NYC and it was clean. My boyfriend and I wanted to go out to a jazz club at night and the staff did not really have any recommendations so we just ventured out on our own. No fitness center available though, but you get enough walking around NYC.

title: “Don't get mislead by the Grand Lobby”
text: The problem isn't age -this is an old historic hotel. However, it is not well maintained. We were awed by the luxurious lobby but that's where it stayed. The wall paper in our room is falling apart and there is a crack in the ceiling (I hope it doesn't fall on us). The spaciousness of the room doesn't reflect the price tag. For the price that we paid, the room is small and dilapidated. The gym is a joke. Few pieces of equipment. The room smells unclean. I would recommend to stay somewhere else.

title: “They dont tell you about the 20.00 per day parking charge untill you leave”
text: Was not told that it costs an extra 20.00 for parking at check in so be warned. All parking is valet which I didn't really like. Everything else was fine, room was clean, TV was really nice, staff were very friendly, bed was very comfortable. Waiting to get my bank statement, If I was charged for parking, I will stay elsewhere next time I am in LA. High speed internet was not working too well but didnt really matter to me because all I wanted to do was sleep

title: “Great location”
text: We stay in Carlton Hotel on Madison Av. for four nights.We were satisfied with all service in hotel.Only one thing - first night the heating in our room doesn¨t work, and because was Thanksg. day, we must wait for reparing next day.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights in late April 11. The staff were very welcoming and friendly, particularly Tami who checked us both in and out on the front desk. We arrived at 9am and were very grateful to be able to access our room straight away. We requested a king bed but it hadn't been guaranteed and they weren't able to provide this, but the room was big and spacious, including the bathroom. They have coin operated laundry machines on each floor ($1.50 washer, $2 drier), they sell tide powder in the vending machine - it was great to be able to use this service. I swam in the pool once and the pool area was a lovely sun trap. They provide beach towels and the jacuzzi was very nice. We ate in the restaurant at 8pm on the Tuesday night - the food and drinks were fine but the service wasn't great - it was pretty busy but we ordered 2 cocktails which arrived 10 mins apart and my salad didn't have the chicken on it which I ordered - so I had to wait another 10
mins whilst my husband ate his meal - it didn't make for a relaxing dinner really. The waiter seemed more concerned with presenting an image of being very professional but actually could have paid more attention to getting our order correct. We took a town car booked through concierge to sfo airport for a flat rate of $55 including tip - it is $45 for a taxi so this was
well worth it. The area around the hotel is great, 10 mins to north beach, couple of blocks to the wharf, 15 mins (uphill!) to coit tower. We also stayed in union square for 2 days and much preferred the hyatt's location, it was all very relaxed and really helped you feel like you were on holiday. I'd highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Last minute emergency business trip turned into relaxation and serenity.”
text:
Had a last minute business emergency meeting come up and found myself frantically looking for accommodations during NYC's most impossible time of the year to get a room - early December. I had stayed at the Crowne several years earlier, so when I found I could book a room with them at a reasonable rate, I felt relief that i would be staying somewhere that I knew would actually offer a decent stay, a bit generic for my liking, but still decent.
I don't know if when I approached the desk if I just liked frazzled or stressed, but the staff tuned into it immediately and went out of their way to ensure that my time there would not only be productive but stress relieving. They upgraded my room and offered me a room that was far from much foot traffic going by, that was spacious, and offered me a free pass to their work out facilities that was exactly what I needed after I returned from my meeting. While in the gym a staff member answered questions I had in regards to work outs, as well as made sure that the next staff member coming on was aware of my questions. 
If you are looking for a hotel that is clean, spacious, with easy access to the Times Square area, reasonable rates and all of the bright lights of the city, and a staff that is efficient and in tune with their guest, I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “never again”
text: Me and my husband went in june 07 for a weekend we had just got married two weeks prior. it was bad they didnt clean our room till 530 pm on our second day and all they gave us where 1 free drink each. the beds where hard as a rock i dont think that this hotel is a 3.5 at all. i would stay at the hyatt. they offer a shuttle service no one ever picked up the phone to pick you up never again would i stay here and also at night not a good area to be walking in we took cabs at night

title: “Don't recommend, bad nasty!”
text: This is a " historic hotel", That I expected. But it desperatly needs to be updated, CLEANED, painted, and have the mold removed. Worst place we have ever stayed! Tiny unpractible bathrooms, dirty, no cold water, no water pressure. Nasty furniture, all beat up, & stained. Carpet was horrid, would not ever walk on without shoes that's for sure! Guest were fighting in hallway litterally all night, called front desk no response from security. Really can't say why anyone would give this place a good review.

title: “Another Perfect Stay”
text: If you're visiting the great city of Phoenix, and need to stay near the airport, this place is among the best. It's also within a short drive to many fine restaurants. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable about the local area and go out of their way to make you feel welcome and comfortable. The Soleil lounge is a relaxing place to enjoy a complimentary beverage upon arrival.

title: “Great Time at the Charlesmark!”
text: We thought this was a great place to stay while in Boston. It's centrally located and easy access to everything. The rooms are small, but they are very clean and nicely decorated. The lounge downstairs is very comfortable and we had drinks down there, enjoyed talking with the bartender. It was a Sunday night and kind of quiet, the owner came in and bought us a drink. We would definitely stay here the next time we come to Boston.

title: “clean, budget hotel”
text: Very bare bones room, bed was a bit on the hard side - no frills here at all, but service friendly. In room fridge, free wifi, free parking. Free breakfast (yogurt and giant muffins, coffee, and juice) in mornings. Good location - close to downtown.

title: “Overpriced but great location”
text:
I have a bit of a mixed review for the Baltimore Waterfront. I guess I’ll go with negatives first:
The bad:
Upon first arriving we were quite a bit early for check in as our flight got in around 9:30am. We went to the hotel hoping a room might be ready. However, only rooms with 2 beds instead of 1 king were available. Understandable, we thought this might happen. We were told we could check out bags in the mean time at the bell desk. We waited at the bell desk for approximately 15-20 minutes before anyone helped us. At first I was trying to be conciliatory because it was a very busy morning in the hotel as many wedding guests appeared to be arriving along with the couple getting married. I noticed a women in a hotel uniform in her upper forties early fifties about 10 yards away in the center of the lobby ignoring us as we waited and waited. Again I thought perhaps she was the wedding planner and waiting for the bride or something along those lines and that is why she wasn’t helping us. Every time I looked around and met her glance she turned away, which I thought was odd. Then she started speaking to some of the guests who were waiting to check in, and waiting for the elevators and cabs. A few minutes later she went to the concierge desk and started aimlessly shuffling papers around. As she walked past I tried to get her attention to ask how long the bell deskman would be and she ignored me. At around the 15 minute mark my fiancé became very annoyed and started to walk towards the front desk to ask if we could just leave the bags behind the desk as they were only 2 small overnights and a lap top case when he was intercepted by the same woman who was ignoring us. She checked our bags for us after all. I hate to think it but we both got the impression that she was ignoring us because of the way we were dressed and our ages based upon the way that she was looking at us, and her interaction with us when she finally took the bags. We are both in our mid-20s and were wearing jeans (granted with a nice top and blazer for him as well) while the rest of the guests she was chit chatting with were in the 50s and wearing pant suits and suits.
The rooms were about average. Considering what the normal nightly rates are at this hotel I expected the rooms to be much larger. As a hotel that is branding itself as a 5 star location, I must say the off-strip Hilton in Vegas was MUCH nicer than this hotel, both in size of rooms, size of bathrooms and the bedding (I’m a sucker for a great hotel bed) and the amenities. If we had standard sized suitcases we would have been hard pressed to find room to get ready and move about comfortably. 
I was also surprised how thin the walls seemed to be. I was able to hear everyone up and down the hall almost as if my door was open. I was also able to actually distinguish what the people in the next room did and did not crave for breakfast the first morning. I was also surprised to find that the refrigerator in the room was locked! Something that I have never seen before in a hotel with a note saying refrigerators were available to rent upon request. Very odd and annoying seeing as we were on vacation to celebrate our anniversary and wanted to chill some champagne. On the second night we were there we called down to get two champagne glasses for said bubbly and waited almost an hour to no avail. A second call finally brought someone up about 5 minutes later. 
The morning we left we must have somehow shut off our alarm in our sleep because when I woke we had about 10 minutes to leave and catch our flight. I realized at the airport that my fiancé thought I left a tip for the housekeeping staff and I thought he left a tip and felt absolutely terrible! Seeing as we were so rushed, our room was even more of a disaster than it might have normally been. I called the hotel the next day when we arrived back home to ask if they might be able to put a tip on the credit card I used that they had yet to charge and they said they could. However, I didn’t see it as a charge when they finally processed incidentals.
The good:
The views are great from the rooms and the location is fantastic for doing all sorts of great inner harbor things.
Cabs readily available on premises at almost all times and the one time there wasn’t a cab and we had reservations to dinner, the valet immediately got on his cell phone and had one rushed over. 
A young woman at the front desk in her 20s with dark hair named, I believe Kayla, or something along those lines. She was the one there when we first arrived and offered to call me when a room was available. She left a message that we found on the voicemail of the room when we returned asking if everything was to our liking in the room and we received our bags from the bell desk ok. She is also the girl we reached when I called down to the front desk a second time about the glassware. She was incredibly apologetic and quick to remedy the situation.
We purchased internet access for 2 days which was supposed to start at noon and go to the following noon, however because only used it once during the second portion of time, they only charged us for one day of usage which was nice of them.
I would stay here again mainly for the location, but only if I was able to get a great deal on Priceline again. I certainly wouldn’t pay half of what they charge normally.

title: “Do a Renovation NOW”
text: The desk staff save one member, their manager are stroppy and very terse with guests. The hotel is so old it doesn't deserve to have the Radisson name UNLESS they renovate the room -- SOON!! It is like a 1960's dive hotel you'd see on the Streets of San Francisco -- basic room, bed chair, no free internet. Avoid and stay at a slightly better property a bit more into towne.

title: “Not a bad choice”
text: Stayed here during a city wide event. A/C was not working in room the entire week I was there. Thank goodness there was a fan and the windows opened, though to a very loud and busy street. Fun decor, not the mainstream brand rooms.

title: “European Charm”
text:
I have a strong preference for small hotels with character and charm instead of the cookie cutter major chain hotels where the one in Washington feels pretty much like the one in St Louis. The Henley Park certainly hits the bullseye for my preference! The small sitting room off the lobby has very comfortable sofas and chairs, free Washington Posts, a working fireplace and a very European look with leaded pane windows. The dining room is equally charming architecturally, and the breakfast I had was very good.
The rooms vary in size and layout. The first one I was given, 802, did not have working wi-fi, and I was moved to 805 which was a little larger with more windows and altho there was a wi-fi problem there at the beginning it got sorted out quickly.
My only regret is the regular price. I got a very good weekend rate via booking.com and will probably be hard pressed to find as nice a hotel at such a good price for future visits to DC.

title: “Cannot be bettered”
text: My husband and I stayed at Hotel Solemar 30 August for 5 nights. This was our first visit to San Diego and cannot wait to return to this hotel. The hotel is faultless. It is spotlessly clean, the staff in all areas are exceptional, the rooms were beautiful, the beds are very comfortable and we had plenty of storage space for hanging clothes etc. The restaurant staff are very knowledgeable and welcoming and the staff at reception cannot do enough to help. My husband had left his prescription spectacles in a shop at Las Vegas Airport and the receptionists assisted us in locating them and helped us to track the delivery by FedEx - nothing is too much trouble for these guys. Although we did not eat in JSix in the evening, if the breakfasts are anything to go by I am sure it would have been delightful. The breakfasts are fantastic and we had a good deal with comp breakfast and anything else off the menu for $5. What a deal! As before, the wine reception is a great idea - I would have preferred 6 until 7 but I shouldn't complain. We spent several happy hours in the pool area of an evening and it is a great place to hang out. I can 100% recommend this hotel and have advised my travel provider to recommend this hotel to her future clients. Solemar is ideally situated for all that is going on in San Diego with its fantastic restaurants, bars etc all to hand. All being well we hope to return to Hotel Solemar in a year's time and this time we will make our stay much longer.

title: “Birthday trip”
text:
I choose this hotel partly on the recommendation of other Trip Advisor reviews and what I expected was what I got. I picked up a yellow taxi from JFK to the hotel ($45 flat rate 2 plus $5 toll), however two yellow taxi drivers had not heard of it so maybe it could be good to print off a map marking it's location for the taxi driver to see. There are some lifts that take you up from street level to the ground floor where the reception desk is located There are no alternative steps which is slightly annoying. The baggage room is also located opposite the lifts on the street level. The concierges were friendly and humorous and the check-in and out went smoothly. You can check out through your TV in your room if you wish. The clientel appeared to be mostly smart New York business people rather than tourists, but this mix could possibly change when it gets to the high season. There are two internet PCs in the reception area that are free to use. You just ask reception desk for the wireless keyboard and mouse. The room was of high quality as my photos show. I confirm the niggle that another reviewer found of single-ply toilet tissue! There is a free PIN operated safe in the room located in a drawer, useful for passports, tickets, money etc
Internet access is charged per day for use in the room. Maid service was every day and a complimentary copy of the New York Times was left outside your room weekdays. The breakfast room has a fantastic view of Times Square, however to eat there is quite expensive. I had a couple of minor issues with the room that I reported to reception and within minutes somebody was knocking at my room ready to fix it. Very good service. The hotel is in the heart of the city at great location to explore all the sight the city has to offer. There is a subway station (49th St) close to the front door plus a bus stop right outside the door. You also often find a yellow taxi parked outside as well. Seventh Avenue is a one way street in the direction of Times Square. Not detracting from the hotel's quality, in hindsight I might have downgraded to a 3 * hotel as I didn't really need the quality as much. In summary a quality professionally run 4* hotel in a great location.

title: “Is what it is...”
text: Functional office block style accommodation with depressing decor. Recycled warm stale air in the rooms, subartic in reception (the concierge had a bar heater on). A sign read 'voted best on the Boulevard'. Doesn't say much for the competition.

title: “Excellent Location, Wonderful Service”
text:
From the time we reached the hotel till we came out the next day, it was a pleasure. Not many hotels that i have lived so far have this level of customer service. Fabulous location, right on the center of Inner Harbor. Walking distance from National Aquarium, Convention Center, Visitor Center and Science Center. The staff were very friendly and helpful. We asked for a fridge, microwave, crib, a connecting room, view of the lake. Everything was done without questions. Only thing is the parking is expensive there (Twenty Seven Dollars Overnight). 
I would highly recomend anybody to this hotel. Adding a Picture that i took of the hotel.

title: “Very nice new addition to convention area, needs a little work”
text:
Recently went to the Hilton Bayfront Hotel next to the San Diego Convention Center for a weekend meeting. I was told that our group was the first large business meeting they have had. Apparently, they had completed their soft opening only the month before.
Very pretty hotel against the afternoon sunlight--bright white with glass. You drive up to the second floor to get to the lobby. Valet service and check in was quick and efficient. Lobby is a little confusing, but very high tech and airy in its feel. Very colorful light fixtures, murals and ceiling hangings. 
Hotel sits on San Diego bay, part of the view is very nice, but part of it is also industrial. Pool is outside, next to the too small gym, which has floor to ceiling windows. You can walk along the bay from the Hilton down to the Bayshore Village adjacent to the Hyatt Hotel. 
Room was good sized, I got room on 9th floor with southern view, two doubles. Told by bell captain, probably first person to stay in this room. Big flat screen HD TV, too bad not all features worked on the inroom TV service. Desk with wireless and wired internet service available for a fee. Inroom safe was available, but no robes/slippers, no refrigerator or minibar available. 
Bathroom average shower tub combo, I had no problem with water pressure or hot water, but a couple of my friends did not have hot water in the morning. Also no towel racks--leave on counter top or hang on small metal stud on wall away from sink, kind of odd. Also did not have a wastepaper basket in bathroom or a shower mat. A friend asked for a wake call, but the phone system was not working that well, the front desk sent someone up to the room to knock on the door at the appointed hour!
Food was OK, room service before 10 pm ok, room service after 10pm is likely to take a couple of hours. 
Meeting rooms were great, great setup, very attentive staff, took care of all details. Staff was available, knowledgeable and efficient. Would definitely hold another business meeting or event here again.
Had problems with elevators--they were slow and occasionally one of them did not work at peak travel times. Escalators also were kind of temperamental. 
FYI--valet $32/nite, self park $23/nite.
Would I stay here again, yes. Would I recommend it to a friend, yes. To get the best treatment, I would probably wait about 6 months for them to get all the kinks out. Definitely better than the Marriott on the other side of the convention center.

title: “A Sanctuary”
text: My bed in this hotel was absolutely delicious. Crisp linens, great pillows, comfy mattress. Some people complained about the street noise but my room (538) faced a courtyard so it was dead quiet. Free (and fast) wifi is a nice perk.

title: “Good value for the price”
text:
My husband and I stayed 5 nights at the Mayfair. The room was clean, comfortable. The staff, from registration to cleaning to concierge, were helpful and friendly. 
We walked to the Staples Centre and walked back in the evening and felt safe. The LA public transit is great and we could access it within a couple of blocks each way. 
Controlling the water temperature in the shower was a challenge but not a nuisance; facilities otherwise were very acceptable. We didn't try the downstairs' restaurant for breakfast (only open for breakfast) but were told by other patrons that it was excellent.

title: “Dont come here you will find a joint in the rooms!”
text: There was a weed joint we found Ac was crapy no elevator over charge my credit card this is the worlds crappy place but if your a cheapo go for it we left and went to a 4 star after the first night !

title: “Home away from home”
text: We've stayed in the Fort Worth Best Western Inn and Suites on numerous occasions and we left happy every time. The staff is very friendly, the rooms are clean and affordable, and the location is good. It is right off of I820, close to down town Fort Worth. We've come to think of this hotel as our Fort Worth home; we feel secure knowing that we can have a quiet place to retire to at the end of our busy days in the area.

title: “Watch your Bill for Charges!”
text:
I stayed one night at the Sir Francis Drake and had a great stay. The location is right in the heart of downtown and just a short cab ride to Embarcedero Center which was perfect for me. The room itself was nice...the bathroom was very outdated, but clean enough. 
The worst part about my stay was when I checked my credit card bill when I got home - they had charged me $21.90 for the mini bar which 1) I did not use and 2) did not appear on my final bill when I checked out. (I'm not sure if perhaps they had magnetic sensors on the things in the mini bar, so maybe if I bumped a bottle of water it would trigger a charge? Even so, $21.90??? They did not mention there were any sensors when I checked in or I never would have even opened the door). I called the billing department and the first representative said they would refund it...4 weeks later, still no refund. I called again and the next representative was extremely rude on the phone and said that it was unlikely I could get it refunded and that she would have to have her manager approve it...I asked her to do so and call me back....nothing for 2-3 weeks, so then I sent an email to the hotel using their website contact info...nothing for 2 weeks, so I called the billing department again and asked to speak to the manager of the department. I left a message on her voicemail and finally someone called me the next day and confirmed the charges would be reversed which they finally were last week (3 months later)....decent hotel, but not worth this kind of trouble at all...

title: “Awesome Boutique Hotel”
text: What a great experience. The hotel was very modern and well-appointed. The staff were very friendly and helpful. They gave us great restaurant recommendations, as well. Manager's reception with complimentary cocktails, wine, beer & snacks everyday and always snacks in the lobby. Continental breakfast each morning. We were able to check in at 11am. The hotel is within walking distance to many attractions and great food & drinks. Overall, a great hotel. Will definitely be back.

title: “Great location”
text:
Le Meridien was a great hotel. The rooms were clean and spacious. The bed was comfortable and the room (rm. 1607) was quiet. 
The staff was friendly. We were given free wi-fi during our stay, which is usually $12.95/day. We were upgraded to a bay/city view room. The concierge had great recommendations for dinner.
The valet was quick. Our car was always ready and waiting for us within 5-10 mins. of calling down for it.
We did not eat at or sit in the bar area but it always seemed like it was busy and fun.
This hotel is in the financial area. It seems like a lot of the businesses close early in this area, but it is close to other areas that do have businesses that stay open later. If you are considering this hotel, I wouldn't let that change your decision. This hotel really is in a good location.
Overall, I have nothing bad to say about this hotel. It exceded our needs and we would definitely recommend Le Meridien to family and friends.

title: “Two issues to consider about the Whitcomb”
text:
It was very interesting to stay at the hotel I had read so much about in these reviews before travelling there
For me there re two main issues here
(1) The Hotel and (2) The Neighbourhood
(1) The hotel is absolutely fine. I booked 2 rooms for my party and I was pretty pleased with them. Rooms were clean and bed linen changed ever day. Hotel appears to be built in the Edwardian period and probably suffers as a result. For example the electrics went off in one of the room due to overloading of the circuit when the hair straightners were plugged in. This was mentioned to staff who dealt with it immediately and it wasn’t a problem at all. The building probably need rewiring, re-plumbing etc but this would undoubtedly cost millions and would probably be uneconomic to do so on the part of the owners. However no complaints about the whitcomb hotel itself
(2) The Neighbourhood- I was very surprised by number of destitute people and those appearing to suffer mental illness on the streets of San Francisco. This hotel is in an area that is full of these people. I never had a problem with anybody myself, but I can understand why this issue has been brought up so much in previous reviews on this hotel. My party consisted of my wife and my 3 young girls, who are 10, 12 and 14, and I know that they felt a little uneasy about the area. If this hotel was literally 500 yards east of where it is, say from Mason Street onwards, where the main shopping area begins, then this hotel would probably be receiving rave reviews
However its not, and that is probably reflected in the price they charge. It is nevertheless in a good geographical position to get around the city, and public transport is almost right outside. Starbucks is next to the hotel and anyone wanting a decent breakfast should try “Sams” which is directly opposite the hotel
Would I book again- yes I would. Its not the hotels fault that there is destitution on the streets, but this issue shouldn’t be overplayed and I would be prepared to stay there again. Those who are a little bit more sensitive to the down and outs, should perhaps look elsewhere.

title: “The Magnolia is the best place to stay in Houston.”
text: Excellent service and a very nice botique hotel. We have stayed here multiple times and we always look forward to our return.

title: “Awesome Atmosphere!”
text: The front desk staff was very friendly and prompt. The room atmosphere was very welcoming and amazing!

title: “The right place to stay... even wih a Baby”
text:
We arrived few days ago, and will stay for another 2 weeks.
Well, let's spend first few words on Venice Beach... a lot of fancy and funny people... If my collegues Italians would see, they would probably not stay 1 more night... BUT if you just understand the easyness of this place, you will love. Somebody ask for 50cent or talk you ? Just a good smile and walk away, nobody will follow you.
Said this, the hotel is right in front of the WALK (no cars running here), in front of the beach, side of many restaurants, in the heart of the Venice Beach Life. People of the management is kind, gentle and present quiet all day long. Parking is 2 blocks from here and free, not very confortable... but Gosh we're on the beachfront! There are no air conditioning, but you don't need it... the ocean breeze is doing well :)
We are 3, me, my wife and a 10 months old baby, we rented a ground floor studio for 130 bucks plus tax, we're staying well, and inspite what others say, the cleaness and the hotel quality is on the average (i don't say it's a 5 star hotel but even the price is not like that!).
For sure SantaMonica has better beach and better nightlife (here after 8.30 it's quiet a desert) they are 20 mins walking from here anyhow... 
We're enjoying, and sure that for the price we paid, we cannot find anything similarhere in the front.
The pier at Santa Monica is a small Gardaland (Italian of my area knows).
Resuming, we are enjoying the stay ...

title: “Elegant but Awful”
text:
My experiences here pretty much mirrior reviewer Lou7477's, coupled with the fact that I was pretty much treated like dirt because I was there on a Priceline reservation. 
We checked in wearing ball game attire, but were otherwise well groomed and clean. The haughty clerk forced me to repeat my entire address twice even though my drivers license was right on the counter in front of her. Tried to upsell me twice during the transaction and reapeatedly mentioned that I was on a "Priceline" stay. The coup de grace came when the clerk asked my wife, who was by my side "what her name might be?" I've never had this happen anywhere, ever. I can only conclude that,since she did not record my wife's response anywhere or ask her for any ID, this was just further Priceline related harassment. I will complain vehemently to Priceline about this.
Also Priceline lists this hotel as located in the "Loop/ Millineum Park". zone. It is in neither. It is a $7 cab ride to the center of the Loop and is 5-6 long city blocks S of Millenium Park. Excepting the frontage on Michigan avenue, the hotel is surrounded by several blocks of shabby neighborhood. If you venture out, you WILL be aggresively panhandled, day or night. So if you bid that zone--my condolences if you receive the Hilton Chicago--which you likely will, as despite thier poor treatment of Priceline customers, according to several relevant forums they need Priceline pretty badly . The are the #1 supplier of rooms in that zone.

title: “Nice hotel...good service...met expectations”
text: Standard stay at a place like this. Staff was nice. No noise or cleanliness problems. No issues and close to TCU stff and Ft Worth zoo.

title: “great place for great value”
text: we stayed at west side Inn for 5 nights , rooms and bathrooms were clean , staff really freindly all depends of what kind of customer you are do not expect 5 stars service , you'll be fine there . maid service upon request ...

title: “tv-z”
text: Nice hotel, the only problem I had was noise from the water pipes. It happened on several occasions during the night. Staff was eager to fix the problem. The front desk staff were excellent! Kudos to Diane, Liz, Sophie, and Brenden

title: “Cheap, good location and excellent service, a little cramped and smokey”
text: Excellent locaiton (one block from Times Square) and very friendly, helpfull staff. Great if you are staying by yourself and want somewhere relatively cheap and safe to stay in a private room. Room I was in was small but adequate, but stank of cigarettes, and every morning I would wake up with a sore throat and headache. Free wireless internet and breakfast was a bonus. Great value for its location.

title: “OK place to spend the night but you need a car”
text:
I stayed at the Hilton Anatole when attending a conference at the hotel. My room in the Atrium section was spacious and had a bed and furniture in good condition and apparently updated decor. Tiny, tiny bathroom revealed the hotel's bones from the '70s. A lengthy hike separated most of the guest rooms from the elevators. Lots of walking was required to get from place-to-place in the hotel, so anyone who has difficulty walking distances may want to think twice before staying in the Atrium section of this hotel.
My room had wired high-speed Internet service that was extremely expensive (~$17/day). The hotel lobby had wireless Internet but its use required that you pay the costly daily rate. 
The fitness center was lovely and complimentary because of my Hilton loyalty program status. Without this, I would have had to pay another expensive fee to use the club. The fitness center has a large number of good-quality aerobic equipment and weight equipment. I participated in a group fitness class during my stay that was lead by a very enjoyable and encouraging instructor. A nice walking/running path runs through grounds between the hotel, fitness center complex and pool area.
This is a giant hotel and even with two meetings in process, the place seemed like a ghost town. Occupancy seemed to be sparse. Although the hotel has several restaurants on the property, only one restaurant was open, a casual cafe in the Atrium section. Because I didn't have a car, and because the hotel is so remote, I ended up eating in the hotel rather than burn up cash on cab fares. The food was surprisingly good, albeit expensive and overpriced. Healthy options were available on the menu, which is important for those of us who travel a lot and do not want to pack on the pounds.
Given a choice, I would not stay at this hotel because it is just too remote and does not have wireless Internet access in the hotel rooms. If I am required to stay here again because of meetings at the hotel, I would rent a car so I could escape the Anatole from time-to-time. It's not such a bad place to stay, and if you are attending a conference at the hotel, it is probably worth staying there, too. But there's other places in Dallas that are nicer and in nicer locations.

title: “Hotel was excellent”
text: We missed our connecting flight and had to spend the night in the hotel, without luggage. The hotel was very accomodating and helpful. The room was excellent. It was very easy to get up and make our new connecting flight with no issues.

title: “Beware”
text:
My family and I were traveling to Seattle for the graduation of our niece. This was a special time for us. A member of the family looked on the web for a hotel close to the graduation facility. All looked well on the internet for moderate priced accomodations for three nights. We called them directly and booked the stay. The staff was very nice and none of this review is meant to reflect on the them in any way. We understood that this was a moderate priced placed to stay but did not expect the what we found.
The rooms are dark and dank and look like something that comes out of film noir. The bathroom had paper rolling off of the walls; it took two to three flushes for the toilet to flush. it was the most depressing place I have ever stayed in. We knew immediately upon arrival in the room that we could not stay there for 3 nights, so we took steps to find other acommodations and were fortunate to find them. We had to stay one night and I spent that entire time awake. We were at the nearest coffee shop at 5:30 a.m. and left in a taxi by 8:30 a.m.
I write this review out of concern for others who plan to stay there. It was not a pleasant experience. Beware.

title: “We were very happy there, even during renovations”
text: We were a bit alarmed when we arrived to see that they were in the middle of renovations but apart from once having to use the stairs when the elevator wasn't working, we were totally happy there. The staff are wonderful. The room was quiet, as we requested, and huge. Loved the vampy decor, had everything we needed. Enjoyed the wine hour in the lobby and met some interesting folks, all of whom knew someone we knew well, across several continents! I would recommend it to anyone. Also the Logan tavern happy hour (bar only & a community table) which is a very short walk from the Rouge. Also City Lights of China for Chinese, a little further away. We didn't have our dog with us but we LOVED that pets were welcome.

title: “Excellent”
text: Very friendly,clean,nice wifi,central, will stay again Bastiaan

title: “Beautiful hotel”
text: We stayed at the Conrad for only one evening but it was such an amazing room we would have liked to stay longer! We were on the newly renovated 9th floor and the room was gorgeous and super clean! There was a flat screen, bose sound system and even an Ihome for our Ipod. Wireless was free and they bring you a free bottle of water at turn down. Everyone was very helpful and so friendly. We can't wait to go back again!

title: “Great hotel in a weird place (the Domain)”
text: The aloft is located in the Domain in north Austin. The Domain is a weird place that caters to well heeled cliental but the Aloft is a down to earth place. Friendly staff and nice rooms. I use this hotel a few times when I need to be in Austin for business.

title: “A Lot of gem for a little money.”
text:
I needed to book a hotel on pretty short notice for my sister and I. As I had to drive in 400 miles to catch a 7 am flight. I paid 32.00 (plus AZ tax) and I was expecting to get my money's worth (roach motel) my sister had actually brought additional pillows and blankets since she was driving to El Paso after my flight. 
First I'll discuss location. 
Though the neighborhood is less then desirable we needed a place close to the airport. this location took us 6 minutes to arrive at Skyharbor terminal 2 (Alaska/United). Plenty of fast food joints around Mcdonalds, Carls Jr, a little mexican joint. Though I really recommend driving to them as there are plenty of riff raff and panhandlers in the area (though for a large metro area on a friday night it could have been worse. The Hotel is off a busy road so there is traffic noise, but it didn't bother me too much. 
Now to the Management and rooms. 
We were met by the manager in the office, whose door was open and inviting. The manager was a very nice man (from Colorado) He made us feel very welcome and while at first we were worried about our vehicle in the neighborhood or fears were quickly eased. This man walked the perimeter of the hotel often if there was any riff raff he quickly moved them off the property (I personally didn't see any riff raff on the property, but witnessed him often walking the area, looking for them) I felt safe and had no worries after meeting him. 
The room itself was incredibly clean and very modern. The beds were soft and warm. The shower was well "OH MY GOD" I didn't want to get out, sparkling clean and the perfect water pressure and hot water stayed hot! AC blew nice and cold. New paint in our room and floors, granite counters and no funny smells that are the "norm" in cheap hotel rooms. I did not feel like I was sleeping at a cheap hotel in anyway. Once in the room I easily felt I would have paid much much more for this room. While I probably would not recommend this hotel if you are on holiday and are looking for amenities. I would recommend it for travelers needing quick access to Skyharbor, easy access to I-10 or business travelers or just people looking for a great room for their money. 
It's important to know I am from a small town in Montana, so I come from an area where I feel safe walking at all hours of the day. The neighborhood could have been "seedy" only in perspective. However, I don't see any reason to NOT utilize this hotel, it's a diamond in the rough and if your looking for a comfy bed and shower at a great price with easy access and polite staff, this is the place to do it.

title: “First trip to NYC”
text: We stayed at Hotel Mela April 13-15 and were very impressed. The bed was extremely comfortable and got a great night's sleep. We got a package through TravelZoo that included breakfasts at Saju Bistro and complimentary drinks at The Long Room (both are right next door to Hotel Mela). The room was clean and a decent size (we had a king bed). Right next to Times Square which was a great bonus. The front desk staff were very friendly and knowledgeable, even the cleaning staff were friendly and went out of their way to say "hello" and strike up a conversation with you to make you feel at home. My wife was ill on the last day and the front desk staff let us stay past check-out until 2pm which was truly appreciated. Highly recommend Hotel Mela - I would stay here again!

title: “THIS REVIEW IS A LONG TIME COMING - AMAZING ON EVERY LEVEL!!!”
text:
I have stayed at this Doubletree Hotel since November of last year and let me EMPHATICALLY STATE: Best hotel I have ever stayed in along with the best staff.
This Doubletree is like a hidden gem in the heart of New York City. The location is great - near MSG but away from all the noise and although it's a fairly big hotel, I feel like a VIP whenever I speak with any of the employees.
The rooms are up to date - modern with a selection of cable channels that any hotel in the U.S would envy - (huge selection of HD channels). The beds are soooooo comfortable with down feather pillows - I get great sleep every night.
The restaurant has a nice selection of appetizers, main courses and desserts. I would recommend the salmon(delicious). The servers go out of their way to smile and take care of your needs.
Yes, there are only 2 elevators but you know what?? I have NEVER had to wait very long for them and they are fast to the floor requested. 
Overall, the General Manager has put together a group of hard working and caring employees that separates this hotel from many many others. James(front desk manager) is in my opinion, a caring and excellent manager. Along with the other front desk mgr Will, they answer my every request.
I don't want to leave anybody out so I am giving props to every front desk employee I have dealt with: Nicole, Ashley, Eva, Judy. Miguel(Security) is always helpful as well as the house man Israel.
Bottom line is this: I don't work for this hotel, I travel a lot and I thank my lucky stars I stumbled upon this GEM of a property. I can't find anything to fault so I am not going to try and think of something. The rates are great, staff is great and amenities are great.
What are you waiting for??? See for yourself !!!

title: “Very much enjoyed our stay.”
text:
The Heartbreak hotel
Family weekend getaway
The hotel itself is thirty years old and some parts of it still have that late 70’s early 80’s vibe. The hallways are tight. There are only two elevators in this five story hotel. The wait sometimes can be time consuming. By day two my family and I were using the stairs. We stayed on the third floor in one of the “King Suites”
The “King Suites” amenities include two televisions, one tube and one flat screen television, a microwave, a coffee maker with coffee and cups, sink within the kitchenette, a sofa which pulls out to a bed, a game console (fee), a work desk with lamp, king size bed, shower bathtub, ice bucket with plastic cups (one ice machine located on each floor) and wireless internet in each room.
Our stay at the hotel started off nice. Moments after stepping off the plane we located the courtesy phone and dialed up the Heartbreak. A shuttle was sent from the hotel and within a half an hour we were at the hotel. The shuttle driver was great. We talked about Elvis, the hotel, our lives (where we are from etc.) and his work at the hotel. We were dropped off at the front door underneath a shelter area. We went right in waited about three minutes for the two person front desk to finish with another guest. The lobby has a 70’s décor that is fitting for the jumpsuit Elvis era. We were quickly checked in and then we were up in our rooms unpacking. We were than picked up in a pink Cadillac and whisked off to Marlowe’s for dinner. Marlowe’s is a fair to good place to eat. I did it for the pink caddy ride.
The King size bed in the room slept very good. No complaints on that experience. The sofa bed was just okay. Very thin mattress. The room was clean and we had plenty of towels and toiletry items. Housekeeping was very nice and only once did we have to request more towels. We called down and the housekeeping didn’t answer so it forwarded to guest relations. She said she would get right on it. But, unfortunately we never received the requested towels. Really the only bad thing that happened at the hotel. The night manager was my favorite as we spoke to each other several different times during our three night stay. She was very friendly and listened which is what is number one when it comes to service. She booked all our trips via the shuttle and even helped on our Sun Studios shuttle scheduling. The whole front staff was nice too. Our shuttle ride back to the airport was great with another wonderful driver.
The most important meal of the day was satisfying to all in my party of five. The hotel offered doughnuts, yogurt, bagels, bread, three types of cereal, milk, coffee, four types of juices, and a toaster oven and microwave. We never ate at the Jungle room lounge but a lot of other guest did. My sister said that food looked good. The wireless internet seems so but it could have been because the number of guest taking advantage of it.
Over all we really enjoyed our stay at the Heartbreak Hotel. I recommend for its location. Less than two hundred yards from the main gate of Graceland. I also recommend the VIP ticket when visiting the mansion.
Leave you on a good note. A new Heartbreak Hotel is in the pipeline so I can’t wait!

title: “Nice hotel and a good bargain”
text:
The Fairfield Inn and Suites Times Square has a lot going for it: friendly staff members, from the desk clerks to the housekeeping crew; really nice rooms; great location near to Times Square, Port Authority, and subway stations; bargain prices for NYC; and a free breakfast thrown in for good measure. We stayed here a cold and snowy evening last weekend, and the proximity to the subways was a godsend. The hotel is within easy walking distance to the heart of Times Square, too, with plenty of hotels, shopping, and sightseeing to choose from.
The rooms were lovely--this is NYC, so don't expect giant rooms, but these were large enough to be comfortable, with new and very nice furnishings, a comfortable bed, IPOD-ready clock radio/alarm, and flatscreen TV. Free wifi was included in the price. The room and bathroom were spotless and appeared to have been recently updated. The heating system was pretty noisy but the room was hot enough that we turned it off for the night and were very comfortable.
Because the lobby/bottom floor of the hotel is undergoing renovations, breakfast was served in the Sky Lounge, the hotel's rooftop bar. For a continental breakfast, I thought there was a nice variety to choose from: cereal, coffee, danishes, bagels, microwavable egg sandwiches and so on. Don't expect a cooked-to-order breakfast or even a hot buffet, but for the price (i.e., included in your rate), it's a pretty good deal.
The one downside we experienced was that noise from the hallway could be a bit much. Some IDIOT woman decided that talking on her phone outside our room at 3 a.m. was a good idea--my language and volume scared her off, but be aware that the soundproofing isn't sufficient to prevent your hearing the inconsiderate idiots loud and clear. Other than that one small blip, we had a wonderful stay.
Short version: I highly recommend making the Fairfield Inn & Suites Times Square your base the next time you're in New York City!

title: “What a view!”
text: This hotel was great! We were in the Presidential Suite on the 25th floor overlooking Michigan Ave and the Chicago River. The room was very spacious with windows everywhere. Seperate bedroom with TV for privacy. Location was easily accesible to sites, restaraunts, attractions. Hotel staff was very friendly, helpful. Valet parking available.

title: “Great Hotel... Awesome Value For The Price”
text: We stayed at the hotel for our anniversary. When we found out that the hotel was brand new, we were a little worried about how the service would be, considering that we have stayed at other Westin hotels in the past. Check-in was good, even though we had requested an early check-in, the room was still not ready until the check-in time of 3pm. They did though check me in and asked me for special requests for the delay. We asked for the highest floor available. When we came back about 45 minutes later, they had given us a top floor preferred guest room with a walk in shower with a king bed and preferred view. Only problems with the room were the decor was a little bland (the pea/sea green wasn't my favorite color) and the walk in shower leaked onto the floor everytime we showered. We didnt eat dinner at Urban, since we went elsewhere to celebrate our anniversary night, but we did have breakfast there. IT WAS GREAT!! I highly recommend the breakfast buffet (a little pricey, $15 per person, but WELL WORTH IT. The beligan waffle and omelettes made to order were soooo good!). All the staff was great, helpful, and very nice. All in all, it was so great, at the last minute, we decided to stay an extra night! We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Maybe location offsets water pressure?”
text:
The water pressure on the 8th floor was so bad that we could hardly rinse off razors and wash the sink after brushing, the shower was barely servicable. The toilets did flush and the floors were clean but not the walls...scuff marked and splattered on vinyl wall paper.The sheets were clean and the towels were fluffy but only medium sized. The hair dryer was broken but they did send up a temporary one and although it had a very short cord it was very powerful.
The air conditioning might have been turned off for the season? We could not get it to function. (It was an unseasonably warm December)
We did appreciate the location as we had functions to attend at Lincoln Center, in Times Square and in Rockerfella Center...all places are walkable from this excellent location.
Taxis from here are very easy to hail and plentiful. Subway stops are nearby. Staff outside did try to convince us to take a private car for $50 when the taxi cost was less than $20. I have to say he was honest to tell us the difference, AFTER I asked. He was just offering in case my daughter and I wanted to go in style as there was a limo going that way shortly after a stop at another hotel??? Be leary of this "option"
We were nearly charged $1.50 per bag to hold the bags since the room was not ready upon our arrival at 2PM
The internet access was $14 per day
The only coffee we found in large thermoses, in the lobby was $3 ( Starbucks brand)
