The elevators functioned with a unique system of "assigning" you an elevator by pressing a panel outside in the hall and everyone was getting caught going up or down in confusion.
We had a unique room with two small double beds separated by a closet/wall-on one side there was a TV but not on the other. This could be an advantage if you travel with small children and want alittle separation.

title: “Great stay on Wells and Randolph”
text: Really enjoyed our two-night stay in early August... Great location, in the loop and just around the corner from the Washington-Wells L stop... Walked, took L, bussed, had no trouble getting a cab... Rooms are a bit on the small side, as others have mentioned, but there was enough space to be comfortable... Staff all extremely gracious and helpful... Don't let the loud music near the entrance fool you, the hotel is cozy and quiet... And make sure to join the free Kimpton rewards program for some extra perks (free wi-fi, $10 mini-bar credit, etc.).

title: “Very nice, clean, helpful staff, would recommend.”
text: I stayed at Wall Street Inn for one night on 5/7/2010. The hotel is small with just 47 rooms. The staff were attentive to all of my questions and were very helpful. The room was clean and nice. My room faced several outside restaurants so there was some street noise late into the evening. The subway is close by with just a 5 minute walk. I recommend this hotel and would stay there again. They use a car service instead of taxi's. The ride from the hotel into Brooklyn Heights was just $19.

title: “Happy with Stay and Price”
text:
Stayed there pre-departure after a business trip because of an early flight at 5:40am. Other reviews had me a bit worried, but the price couldn't be beat and for a few hours sleep and airport proximity I took a chance.
I stayed in the tower as suggested in room 411 and it was NICE. A smoking friend stayed on ground level in room 714 and he said it was better than average.
The bar and restaurant are EXPENSIVE. Beer at $5, Hamburger at $8; but that's tolerable for a one-nighter. Two burgers and drinks with some colleagues brought the bill to $85 !!
Anyway, Shuttles every 5minutes, with only a few minutes to get to the airport.
I took the time to come back and write a review because I've come to rely on these (reviews). I travel all across the US and I wanted to help keep the record straight.

title: “consistently good experience, nice hotel, great location”
text: I have stayed here twice for work and both times were great. The rooms are nice and clean. There is a fitness center, restaurant, and coffee shop on site. You are walking distance to Union Square and many restaurants/shopping locales.

title: “Friendly staff but dated, shabby hotel rooms-definitely not 2 stars”
text: We really liked the staff. They were pleasant and helpful. No complaints. Also, the expanded continental breakfast buffet was clean and well done, waffles, eggs, bacon, plus the usual stuff also. But the rooms were a disappointment. Small, damp, dark rooms with faded shabby furniture. I paid $30 less for a much nicer 2 star hotel the next night, and I feel I paid way too much for this Country Inn and Suites. Lately I've had several disappointing experiences with this hotel chain. They used to be consistently great and now they are consistently mediocre at best. If I'd paid less I would have been less disappointed with the rooms. Not worth the money any more.

title: “I'd stay at the Mosser again”
text:
Since I was traveling alone to San Francisco, the Mosser was perfect for my needs. I stayed in Room 314, a single room with shared bath. While small, the room was certainly adequate for my needs, clean and with a very comfortable twin bed. The men's toilet was just two doors down, and the bath/shower room right around the corner. I never had to wait to use either one.
The Mosser underwent a total renovation not long ago, and the guy at the front desk told me they'll soon be replacing all the TVs and hall carpets. I liked how they retained many of the old touches of this vintage building, while making the rooms look modern.
I booked through the hotel website, and got very good rates. I was there four nights, checking in on the 26th and checking out on the 30th. The rates varied by day, but averaged about $108 per night, including all taxes and fees. In San Francisco, this is a screaming bargain, considering the location. It's just steps from Market Street and all the bus and train lines. The Metreon and Moscone Center are a block away. Since the Pride Parade went down Market Street on Sunday, there couldn't have been a better location to watch the fun.
The staff was cordial and helpful, and there was a basket of apples at the front desk most of the time. In the morning, tea, coffee and muffins were available for free.
There's not much I could criticize about the Mosser. I found it to be generally quiet (my room faced an alley, not busy 4th Street) and since I wore earplugs my sleep wasn't disturbed by any hall noises. The lack of any dresser space was a bit of a problem, so incorporating drawers into the platform of the bed would be a good way to solve that. Also, the light from the hallway shone into the room at night, the wooden blinds over the transom not completely shutting it out. But these are small things compared to the overall experience.
In sum, the Mosser was an excellent value in a perfect location for exploring downtown San Francisco. I'd definitely book it again if I was traveling alone. Since I didn't see any of the larger rooms, I can't offer an opinion on them.

title: “Check in was horrible but nice hotel for price”
text:
Had a reservation and arrived at check-in time. Had to sit in the lobby for 3 hours as they kept telling me my room wasn't ready yet. Person after person kept walking up to the desk, checking in, and going directly to their room. They already had me assigned to a specific room and wouldn't check me in to any other room even though all rooms at the properrty are identical. Finally I demanded at 4:00 that they give me a different room and let another person that hadn't arrived yet have the room that wasn't ready yet. Not a service friendly hotel. Also, location is poor, it's in an industrial area with nothing around it but warehouses. Have to drive approx 10 minutes to get to a restaurant.
Hotel was clean, but the poor service ruined the experience.

title: “Great service!”
text: I've stayed in this hotel many times while my boyfriend was job hunting in the city. They knew us already and were always friendly. The shuttle service would take us to nearby restaurants. The breakfast is hot and yummy, with healthy choices. The rooms are clean and no one is allowed to smoke, which I love! My bf finally found a job and moved into the city, so we haven't been back since February 2012, but it's by far one of the best hotels in el paso. Tip... Book through Priceline.

title: “Excellent Value & Service”
text:
We booked the Omni via a conference group rate for $175/night, two nights, Sat-Mon. While booking, there was an option to enroll in the hotel loyalty program, which I did because it was free. 
Laura, at the front desk checked us in and was wonderful. We anticipated not being able to check in because it was around noon, and leaving our luggage for a few hours. However, Laura explained to us that by joining the loyalty program we were awarded with early check-in, free in-room wi-fi, complementary pressing and shoe shine, and breakfast beverage service for each of us every morning of our stay. She tipped us off that if we order one coffee, there was enough in the pot for three cups, so it would be wise to order one coffee, and one juice to share. Made perfect sense to me and was probably not something I would think of myself, so that was nice of her (its the little things like that, that make me happy). 
We were given room #1108, which is a standard King. The hotel is in the financial district, so our room looked out immediately to other office buildings. Good location if you want a better chance of less night life street noise. I was a bit disappointed that the windows were not well sound-proofed, and what little street noise there was, we heard clearly. Unfortunately, the same could be said of the walls. For both nights of our stay we were sandwiched between guests with small children. We could tell exactly when the guests were in their rooms with the children playing, crying, whining, and the age-old argument between a wife complaining to her husband about not being able to shower because she had to watch the kids. 
The bed was very comfortable, even when we were shaken awake by the small earthquake that Monday morning :)
The wi-fi was actually decent!!! Both my husband and I were able to go wi-fi only at the same time, a rarity it seems at hotels. 
Although I don't use it, I liked that the hotel provided spray starch for ironing. Good business hotel touch.
The bathroom was spacious for a standard size room, the products were customized via Sysco but still nice, the shower pressure good, and well lit. I always appreciate it when hotels provide robes. 
The cons: Few. Aside from the "thin" walls and windows, if you stay on the weekend, all the really close-by breakfast food places are closed. I'm not a big breakfast eater, but I do like to be able to quickly run out, grab a pastry, and then come back to the hotel to get ready for the day. On weekdays this isn't a problem because there are many cafes that cater to the business crowd. La Boulange is right across the street and is probably the best option.
Overall, a very pleasant experience and I would recommend the Omni easily for the business traveler. I was immediately impressed by the loyalty program providing exceptional perks on only the first stay. A free pot of coffee is definitely a cheap way for a hotel to make a good impression.

title: “my third time, still a good hotel but some small changes”
text:
This is my third time at this hotel in four years, and my third review. It is still an excellent location (especially because of the subway lines below it) and generally a pleasant and hassle-free hotel. We avoided the breakfast, there are so many better choices a short walk away. 
A couple of small changes since our last time. First, the mattresses have been replaced by those adjustable-firmness things, which are basically air mattresses, and they feel like it. The pillows, of which there are supposedly two kinds, were all soft and fluffy, your head sinks right down to the mattress. I don't know if maybe they didn't give us any of the firmer type, or what. In any case it would be nice to have a firmer pillow.
The room price varies. Checking it regularly is a pain, but we made our original booking of a 'Tribeca view' double for $300/night incl taxes, and a couple days before arrival we rebooked it for $200/night incl taxes. The best deal was with the Hilton MVP corporate code (google it; you must join HHonors, but that is free and easy).

title: “good stay”
text: Stayed here for a meeting, and the rooms were clean, the airport is close or nearby, and the people were friendly and helpful. I agree the hotel is "tired" but the beds were soft. Food was okay, nothing to brag about, so we walked over to the restaurants across from the hotel. To get to the restaurant, we had to walk down the street as the train separates the traffic and it is fenced. Would come back.

title: “Great location, not much else”
text:
I can't believe all the 5* reviews this place has. It is in a great location, half a block from Times Square and an easy walk to 42 Street, Broadway, etc, but apart from that, this hotel is over priced and offers little.
Rooms are small, and there are no facilities at all. You enter the main door, and there is a reception desk. A little further in there are a few chairs outside the lifts. That's it. No bar, nowhere for breakfast, no gym, no pool, nothing.
I was there 3 nights, and on two mornings there was no hot water. AFTER complaining, I received a $50 reduction per night. As all they offer is a bed and a shower, I would have expected a much bigger discount when one of the two items I'm paying for isn't working.
I was at reception checking out while at least 5 other people called to complain about no hot water. None were offered discounts.
If it was cheap, I'd score it highly. The location is great, but it thinks it is a "boutique hotel" and can justify high prices by having some red sofas in reception. I'm not impressed.
Try the Millennium Hotel across the street if they have rooms.

title: “Nice stay-decent price”
text:
We stayed three nights for a busy weekend that kept us out all day and late into the evening, so we didn't do much but sleep here.
We were on the 16th (top) floor and found the rooms to be very nicely decorated. The bathroom area was large and very clean. The beds were very comfortable and plenty of pillows. Housekeeping was done well, pleased with cleanliness of our room. From the reviews I have read, maybe you want to ask for 16th floor??
The parking was $16 per day and that seemd a little high. Areas between the garage and the hotel were pretty much an eyesore. May be worth it to tip the valet and avoid those sights.
We had problems with the key not working each night when we returned to the hotel, that was inconvenient; most likely a training issue rather than a lock/key problem.
Next time in Austin, I will probably try a different place; not displeased, just not impressed. For the price, it was an ok stay.

title: “Typical Marriott”
text:
Older Marriott, clean rooms, impossible to get a cab! My husband was there for business, and I was there for pleasure. Our room was a king corner room, sufficient room for the two of us. The maids did a great job every day, we were there 5 days....the place was packed everyday...a side note...the View, the bar/restaurant on the 39th floor has the RUDEST bartenders I have ever come across. I don't quite understand why I have to put up with rudeness when i am paying $200 for around and a $40 tip...maybe they should have tipped me for putting up with the nastiness. I can understand if they was swamped, however, I was the only one waiting for a drink! What a waste! Apparently from the other reviews this is a regular occurrence! 
 Overall, the Marriott Marquis met our needs.

title: “An airport hotel that meeds your needs”
text:
I stayed at this hotel because I had a 6:30 am flight the following day. We arrived during what appeared to be a Filipino event. First, protestors convened in front of the hotel while other Filipino merry-goers flooded the hotel lobby. Fortunately, as a Gold HHonors member, there is a dedicated check-in making the process swift and efficient. We received a room on the tenth floor which also happened to be their updated floor. 
Soft carpets cover the entire room while granite countertops can be found in the bathroom. This is my first time here so I can't compare it with un-renovated floors. Nonetheless, the room contained basic amenities: coffee maker, fridge, cable TV. 
The hotel is home to a plethora of dining options. We opted for the restaurant because it seemed the most quiet from the cacophony of the events going on. The menu featured modern entrees such as seared salmon with cherry tomatoes and asparagus. For $25, one can also opt for the buffet, but I didn't have a chance to see what it offered. 
The room afforded a really amazing view of one of LAX's runways. Although the jet noise presented some noise problems, it didn't really bother us too much. Furthermore, after 10 pm, there weren't nearly as many flights. 
At $109/night, it's a very reasonable price. Proximity to LAX cannot be beat. The hotel is located on Century Blvd and is a few minutes drive to the terminals. 
I don't know when I would stay at the Hilton Airport again, but if I ever had an early flight, it would be my first choice.

title: “Probably the best urban hotel I've stayed at on the last five years.”
text: Service was great, the rooms were well appointed and clean, the restaurant was great. Not sure what worse you could ask for out of a hotel. I usually don't like staying at hotels this big, but the service quality was like that of a boutique hotel. The exterior light display is interesting as you pull up to the valet. Just like the high tech rooms, it's mesmerizing. The feature I liked the best in the rooms was the floor that lit up when you stepped out of your bed, guiding you to your destination when it's dark. The rooms were quite and comfortable and very large with a little seating area right by the window. Ask for a room with a view of downtown.

title: “Good location, nice hotel for the price”
text: Nice hotel. Good location. Clean & comfy. Beds OK. Fair price. Gym moderate sized, but nice (and free). Lots of restaurants nearby. They have breakfast available - about $20 for full breakfast, but easy to walk to other restaurants. There was a refrig and microwave in room. Small coffee pot - not so good coffee. Grocery store 2 blocks away on 8th.

title: “Great, upscale place to stay”
text: We just stayed here for the first time on 1/29/12. The hotel was in a good location but enough out of the way that there was not much noise or hustle and bustle so it was very relaxing. Check in/out was quick and easy. The room was beautiful. It was my birthday and the hotel gave us a free bottle of wine. The staff was very accommodating. There is a beautiful lobby with free refreshments and in the morning there was a complimentary breakfast. Our experience was very positive and I would definitely recommend this hotel and stay there again. And the price was reasonable for a nice hotel in NYC as well.

title: “THE BEST CUSTOMER SERVICE EVER!!!!DIANE PAUL VERLINA YALONDA ARLENE AND CHRISTA”
text:
I have NEVER experienced this type of customer service before! From the very moment I pulled into the parking lot until the very moment I left. The valet attendants were very attentive and prompt with great customer service. The front desk greeted me a smile from the moment I stepped into the door. If I had to think of one thing that was not to my liking, I would not be able to do so.
My visit to LA was due to the passing of one of my family members. With such short notice, I used Starwoords Preferred Guest reward points to book my room. When my points ran out, I relocated to the Radisson next door……BIG mistake. After being spoiled by the Sheraton, there was no comparison. I quickly changed back to the Sheraton...the very next day! With the great customer service and great accommodations, who could ask for more, right? Well, to my very pleasant surprise, the staff at the hotel wrote a handwritten note expressing their condolences in which all of them signed. The fact that a hotel would be so kind as to do such a thing solidified the fact that not matter where I go, I will always stay at the Sheraton.
Thanks for a job well done!!!!!
I would like to show special recognition to the following employees:
DIANE!!!!!! You are the best
Paul
Verlina
Arlene
Christa
Yalonda
Sorry if I misspelled any of the names.

title: “Fantastic Stay”
text: We stayed here for our anniversary. The staff was very welcoming and friendly and really made our trip special. There is a wine hour every day in the lobby, and a restaurant with a bar. The location is great, just a block from Union Station and a walk to great restaurants and other attractions. Wonderful.

title: “A relly nice hotel”
text:
We visited NYC for 8 days, we booked 2 room suite.
This place was awesome!
Evrything about our stay was great but we did have some rain.
who cares , your in NYC.

title: “Not all that bad...”
text:
I just recently spent two weeks at the Bahia for business. I was leery due to some of the comments I read here. Overall, I thought it was a good value and wasn't unsatisfied.
I was in the 300 section. My patio opened right up to the bay side beach and the front door was close to the sidewalk that leads to the "boardwalk" and beach.
Yes, the rooms are somewhat dated and worn, but mine was kept very clean. The staff was very attentive, accommodating, and friendly during my stay. The resort is close to the airport, convenient to bus stops, Seaworld, and the beach.
There are a few good places to eat within walking distance; I especially liked the taco shop on the nearby corner and the pizza place (Big Papas) just a couple of doors down.
I know that some of my coworkers weren't happy with their original rooms but the staff moved them to better ones. It also appeared that they were in the process of doing some renovating; I know that they were replacing carpet and furnishings in the section I was in.
Overall, I would not have any problem with staying here again or recommending this hotel.

title: “Excellent value”
text: We stayed for two nights for a wedding and were very pleasantly surprised at how good this hotel is especially given the relatively moderate price for a hotel of this quality in NYC. We had a very nice one bedroom suite which was more than adequate in size and quite comfortable, The staff was very friendly and the room service breakfast was very good. We also went to a brunch at the hotel for the wedding guests the morning after the wedding and it was excellent as well.

title: “A higher level Courtyard - very good!”
text: Both room quality and service at this "Courtyard" were of the quality that I would expect from a higher level Marriott hotel. We were visiting family in Sherman Oaks, so the location was key for us, but I would consider staying here too as a mid-point with good driving access to both Malibu and LA. I selected this hotel based on prior reviews and I found them right on the mark. The hotel is very close to the 405. While our view was of the highway, it's far enough so that noise was not a problem. The fitness room is small, but adequate with 2 treadmills, an elliptical, rowing machine, weights and one TV. The outdoor pool on the 4th floor is in a pleasant, quiet location.

title: “Great hotel, great location!”
text:
Just returned from a 5 night stay in the Affinia Manhattan and loved it! The staff were very pleasant, the hotel is in a great spot and the bed was really comfy!
We were on the 7th floor by the service elevator - I admit to being a bit worried as I'd read all the reviews on here about noise but it was fine. Yes you can hear sirens,and car horns (but i didnt hear the service elevator) but then its a city and like another reviewer said it all adds to the New York experience! 
I agree that there are parts of the hotel that may need a new lick of paint but it was clean! Our room was small with the kitchenette and bathroom but it was fine for what we wanted. The only small problem I had was that sometimes the room was cold. There was a letter in the room explaining the heating and I could have requested a heater from reception but I used it as an excuse to snuggle my hubby instead!
I liked having to show the room card to get to go in the elevators at night. All staff that we dealt with were friendly. Niles bar was good, we only had drinks but it was busy most evenings.
The best thing about the hotel was location! The location is great, so handy to get to Times Square, Empire State and the subway. 
I would most definitely stay here again and recommend it to friends (in fact we already have and they are booked in February!)

title: “Very disappointing.”
text:
We booked this hotel through Hotwire, so we couldn’t read the reviews before our stay, otherwise I would never book it.
The problem in this hotel is the very low service level. The location is great for LAX, the room was clean & the bed was very comfortable.
But the air condition didn’t work, on the hottest day in LA for years. So we called., 3 times, waited 2.5 hours in an impossible atmosphere before the maintenance guy arrived, and said he fixed it.
Well, he didn’t. And we had to wait another 1.5 hours before we were moved to another room.
I spoke with the front desk’s manager, who apologize, but didn’t do much more.
The next day, on our way to the terminal we called for baggage assistance. I specifically check the night before if I should call 30 minutes before. No they said. 5 minutes would be enough…
Mistake! We had to wait in our room for 25 minutes, called 4 times, and eventually, I walked personally to ask them to come.
I wouldn’t stay in this hotel again. There are much better choices in the area

title: “Perfect Midtown Location”
text:
My girlfriend and I wanted to take a romantic getaway to see The Tree in Rockefeller Center. We only live an hour from NYC, so we've never booked a hotel there. This time, however, we wanted to have fun and not worry about the drive home. If you want to be close to Rockefeller Center, and all that it has to offer, there is no better location than the Rockefeller Center Hotel. From the 7th floor Terrace Club you could almost toss a rock and hit The Tree, the skating rink, St. Pat's Cathederal or Radio City Music hall. Like all Club Quarters, the place is very 'efficient'. It's all business, but it's efficient, clean, hospitable and neat. I figure we're going to see the sights, not to hang out in our hotel room. The room rate was about half that of the Hilton, which is a couple of blocks away, though still expensive since we visited after the tree was lit.
Johnny Utah's, the restaurant in the basement of the hotel, was great, too. The food was so-so, but the atmosphere was fun, with a mechanical bull in the middle of the place and a packed house after 9:00PM. Bartenders were shockingly attentive and the wait staff was friendly and helpful. 
I'd definitely stay at the Rockefeller Center Hotel again!

title: “A nice gem in San Francisco!”
text: This is a very convenient hotel in a great part of San Francisco! It doesn't matter whether you are there on business or pleasure - it will fit anyone's needs. The staff is helpful and courteous.

title: “Short Stay, did what it said on the tin”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights. Hotel bar was quite nice, but hey your in New York youve got to get out and about. We used this place as a base and managed to get around to all the usual tourist attractions with ease. So therefore id say it had a good location.
Go and Enjoy, when your in New York why would you want to sit in your hotel room anyway.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: Chose the Hilton as it was close to relatives, and we wanted "our own bedroom". Reasonable price, room was immaculate, staff very friendly. Didn't try the restaurant/pool but if they were as nice as hotel, shouldn't be disappointed. We'll definitely be back!

title: “on our way to Disney”
text: wonderfully comfy beds with superb pillows. pack n play clean and tucked nicely in roomy closet for extra quiet. breakfast bountiful and yummy, clean high chairs and boosters. desk staff very nice and helpful. clean. a great restful spot to being our Disney trip.

title: “OK for the price but not great”
text:
My first impression was the snooty front desk girl who kept people waiting to check in. The manager and other staff were polite but not much friendlier. 
The first night was sleepless until the early morning hours due to a disco party on the second floor. Repeated calls to the front desk didn't change anything. Got a small compensation though.
The room and bathroom were clean but cold, the indidvidual heater for the room was VERY noisy (can't run it at night) and rather inefficient. 
The door lock worked only sometimes and the bolt was broken. The breakfast area is in the unheated lobby (bring your jackets!!), there was no juice, hot chocolate or decaf coffee. We had to bring stuff for our child. 
The website promises free cocktails in the lounge, this is not true.
Overall, ok for the price, would stay there again as the location is perfect but would dread the unfriendly staff.

title: “Just perfect..”
text: This was going to be my first time in New York, so we wanted to make our stay special. I know I have spent many hours searching for our best choice on the internet. We both have had our preferences on what we wanted, and location was key. The hotel is perfectly located almost next to Central Park, between 5th ave an Madison ave. We where impressed with the tastfull design of the interior and the super comfortable beds. There is a fantastic restaurant in the hotel called Boulud, we ate there twice because it was just so good! So yes, we loved our stay there, and I highly recommend it. It's not cheap, but I think it is worth it ;)

title: “Parking recommendations inside”
text:
We stayed at the Mark while attending a Holiday Party. My boyfriend won a free stay in his company raffle, and as we live 15 miles away, we went ahead and stayed the night.
The hotel is pretty average for San Francisco standards. A small room, nicely decorated, with breathtaking views. The staff was a disappointment, when I called to confirm the reservation, I was transferred 4 times and then hung up on. They weren't much nicer in person.
Parking runs something like $48.00 a day. That's (unfortunately) about normal for San Francisco. However, we shopped around online and saw that you can park at the Nob Hill Masonic Center, which is located at 1111 California Street (apprx. 1 1/2 blocks away) for $27 for a 24 hour period. And that's only if you need to drive. San Francisco has fantastic public transportation, so usually a car is not necessary.
The rooms were okay, the room service prices were ridiculous, $18 for a cheeseburger!! (but that's par for the course, I guess). 
The only reason I would recommend this hotel would be for out of town visitors who want some views and don't know which parts of the City to avoid (we do have our problem areas). The hill leading up to the hotel is one of the steepest in the City, so I don't recommend this hotel for anyone who has trouble walking.
Overall, we weren't really impressed with the hotel, but we didn't pay anything for it, so it was okay. I'd stay there again, but only if the room was free.

title: “Beautiful hotel in great neighboorhood”
text:
The hotel is very nice, but its best features are location and staff. 
Georgetown is absolutely gorgeous, it has great shops, bars and restaurants, and is always very lively. We took long walks to explore the area and really enjoyed it. 
We got a standard room, very beautiful and spaciuos, but unfortunately didn't have a view. We knew it when we booked, and it was not a big deal to us. The staff was wonderful, as always when you go to a Ritz. They really make a difference! They were all very nice, and recommended some really great places!

title: “Suite was Dirty, Dated, Dark and Dingy”
text:
We stayed in one of the oversized garden view suite. The room was a very good size with two 42 inch LCD TV's, a kitchen (albeit with dirty utensils) and comfortable sofa bed. Good points were the room facilities - it had just about everything including large refridgerator, toaster and microwave as well as a stove. Lots of HD TV channels available too. 
It is clear that the hotel had upgraded certain aspects of the room like the bedding and TV's, but the room remained in poor condition with a hole in the ceiling and a myriad of un-dusted surfaces everywhere, together with mold in the bathroom and a noticeable lack of any decent lighting. Whilst the hotels upgraded rooms may be nice, the suites certainly aren't! Many words come to mind including dark, dated, dingy and dirty.
Add this to the noise from the "low grade" guests this place seems to attract and the thin walls allowing us to hear the guy next door shouting in the middle of the night and you get the picture that WE WON'T BE GOING BACK ANYTIME SOON. Not that the hotel seemed to care as they never asked us how our stay was!
My advice is to book the Bay Club Hotel and Marina next door instead. It has half price parking at $5 a night compared to the $10 fee at Humphreys, much cleaner rooms and a free breakfast to boot.

title: “Great staff and I'll be back!"”
text:
I stayed at this property late July for business and couldn't have been more pleased. The staff at the front desk was very professional and knowledgeable. This property is a no nonsense hotel with all the amenities that one needs to conduct business. The breakfast was fast and offered options of both a buffer or off the menu items. The lobby is abuzz with guests using the computers and/or meeting and greeting that keeps the place hopping. The lobby area overlooks the outdoor pool that was well attended while I was there. This location has a handy shuttle service to and from LAX. I never had to wait more that 10 minutes or so in either direction. This property has two towers. In the tower closest to the main entrance the rooms are more fresh as they were updated with new decor. The other tower is going through renovations and frankly could use it. 
I have stayed at many LAX properties including the Hilton, Westin, Sheraton and Marriott and I now stay here as the WiFi is free, the staff is always bright and cheery and the room rates are much more reasonable. I will be back to this location for sure.

title: “Convenient”
text: We stayed at this hotel on our vacation. The location is great. It is easy to get to and close to everything. The rooms were clean and the breakfast was very good. The only thing we did not like was all the traffic noise since it is right off of I5. As long as the air was on you could not hear it.

title: “I was told by the reception staff to go back to my own country if I didn't like the service!”
text:
We have travelled around many countries and stayed in a variety of accommodation and we were fully expecting the room to be basic. But what we did not expect was the disgusting attitude of the staff which I have never come across in my life. 
It took over an hour to check in and I was met with a very aggressive man when I told him I was not happy with this.
The room was so poor we found it funny that they had the cheek to ask people to pay. 
The only thing going for it was the location which was good and the cleaners did a good job with what they were working with and that is the only reason it has a score.

title: “Large but nice”
text: You cant go wrong staying on Michigan Avenue. We were only here for one nite so did not get to experience everything they had to offer but from what we did experience, we liked it. The beds were very comfortable, amenities good quality, nice in room coffee machine , flat screen, pleasant decor. Having to pay for internet service though was a bit too much considering most basic hotels offer it for free. The front desk and bell staff went out of their way to be friendly,concierge sent us to a so-so Italian restaurant which surprised me considering the city we were in. They also told us it was a short walk, which it wasn't. I suggest doing your own research if you want to experience a good Chicago meal. The have a nice pub right in the hotel so if you are in the mood for that type of food, you don't have to leave the hotel. Self park is outrageous but not out of characer with every other hotel in the area so you cannot hold that against them. Its a safe parking structure and easy access to get to the lobby. I would stay here again.

title: “Fantastic beach value! Nice hotel right on the beach.”
text: I stayed ten days at this hotel and enjoyed every one of them. The room is clean, updated, spacious, and very convenient with a kitchen included. It is not a glamorous hotel, but it is unexpectedly nice for the price. Parking is limited, but I only had to park a block away three times in ten days. If you want a clean, safe, quiet, friendly hotel right on the beach, this place can't be beat. The hotel staff is friendly and efficient, which added to my enjoyment. This will be my first choice to stay next time I am in San Diego and I will be sure to bring the family.

title: “Great NYE Experience”
text: We stayed here on New Year's Eve and thought it was great. Right across the street from the Inner Harbor our partial view room looked directly at the aquarium. The staff was very friendly especially at the lobby bar where we went for drinks after midnight. Room furnishings and hotel decor was beautiful.

title: “Never Again”
text: This is the second year in a row we have stayed here as a family while I attended a medical meeting. If I go to this meeting again I will stay off-site. The room was average, I was able to get a rate of $399 since I am a Hilton Honors member, but I could have gotten a better rate at a hotel more central to Times Square and at a better rate (i.e. Hilton Inn Times Square). This hotel is a major ripoff. There is a $14.95 per day charge for wireless internet, most hotels are giving it away for free now. My teenage daughters did a lot of shopping in New York; I attempted to take a luggage cart from the lobby to our room to take all the bags downstairs, unfortunately, I was accosted by a bellhop who said I could not take it upstairs, only a bell hop could do that. In it for the tip of course. The elevators took forever, as I have seen on other reviews. The meeting room was terrible; there was so much noise from the room next door I could not hear our speaker. The location is really great, I must admit, it is quieter than Times Square, and nice for an evening stroll, but I must say it is overall a rip off. The hotel is living off the Hilton name but not living up to the reputation. Look for something in the same price range, but someplace else; I'm sure it will be better.

title: “fantastic location”
text:
If you want a central Hollywood hotel to be where the action is, look no further: The hotel is within 5 minutes walk of the walk of fame, Dolby center, Hollywood Bowl, and a 10minute drive from Universal Studios.
We had a hire car- it was $20/day for parking -valet parking but you do not need to pay each time you take the car out- the valets were helpful & courteous.
Reception greeting was friendly, helpful & efficient. The rooms were clean, well decorated & modern, beds comfortable & surprisingly not noisy given the location.
In the bedroom were fridge, microwave, sink, coffee machine. There is a small shop in reception selling food & ice-cream, or a small supermarket literally across the road which also does pizza. Also usual Subway across the road. If you want to eat out there are various restauarants in the nearby Dolby center, some cheap, some expensive.
There si an open-air swimming pool which although small is nice to cool off, though they never had any towels there so we had to bring them from the room- minor niggle.
Breakfast was lovely but too few seats for the number of people and sometimes we had to take our breakfast out to the pool area and eat on the sunloungers- it seemed to be worse when the more efficient lady was not on duty- as stuff ran out it wasn't replaced and consequently people stayed at their tables waiting for eggs or pancakes etc. This only happened one of the 5 days we were there, otherwise it was good. The kids loved the hotel, as did we. its a 10minute drive to the hollywood sign, 20min drive to Rodeo Drive, 40min to Santa Monica (but 2hrs back in rush hour!). Driving in the US is fine but get a satnav.
Walking at night was fine and the streets are well-lit and busy due to the location of Hollywood Bowl.
There are lots of leaflets for tours in the lobby: TIP if you have a hire car- go down to the walk of Fame & buy a Star map from the little machine on the corner- its $5 and shows where the stars live- we did our own tour using this, saw what we wanted, and saved $200 on an organised trip.

title: “A different kind of hotel with a fun vibe!”
text: We loved our stay at the Palomar. The service was supreme. The location was very convenient to everything you would want to do in Chicago. Everything about the hotel is fun, even the animal print lush terry robes. I was impressed with the breakfast. Everything they serve is fresh and local, even the sausage.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
Location is the absolute main reason to stay at this hotel! The blue metro line leaves the terminal at Reagan Airport and in about 20 minutes you are at Metro Center. Take the escalator up out of the subway and the hotel is about 30 steps away! The other advantage is the Metro Center (subway station) is where the blue, red, and orange lines all meet, so it makes for great transportation around the DC area. 
Our room was somewhat small, but OK for 2 people. Had everything to make us comfortable. One problem - we had adjoining door to the room next door and we could hear everything! And, all our neighbors seemed to stay out late and get up early, making for less-than-peaceful rest. Starbucks in lobby (however, it closes early). A number of nice restaurants, of all price ranges, nearby. 
We certainly would make this our base again.

title: “Great Treat”
text:
We stayed here during my first trip to New York, i was a little suprised at how difficult it was to find a car from JFK to The Plaza...but thats another story.
When we arrived, the concierge grabbed our bags and took us to the desk, where the staff were a little suprised that we had booked a suite, i dont know if it was the 7 hours flying or prehaps we just look young (probably the former). After that was settled we were taken up to the Rose Suite.
This was by far the most beautiful suite i've seen, the ebd was huge and perfectly soft, the bathroom was out of this world!
All in all, the staff are very friendly....but they like their tips. I dont know if its the Englishman in me, but i started to get quite put off by their waiting for tips.....after a day in New York, however, i realised this is the norm.
A Beautiful hotel, in an amazing location.

title: “Had a wonderful stay!”
text: I recently stayed at this hotel and I must say that I was definitely content, no, more than content with the service I received and the quality of the hotel. The reviews on this site are quite accurate. All the staff was extremely and genuinely friendly; I always felt welcomed. The room was clean and comfortable (and I am very particular). The complimentary breakfast that was offered was satisfying and delicious - fresh fruit, waffles, eggs, variety of beverages, hot/cold cereals, breads and pastries, and more. Whatever your diet, you'll find something that works for you. Moreover, the location was really good. It's right off of I-95 and I felt really safe. If I could change one thing about my visit, it would be the location of the room - I wish I had been closer to the elevator rather than at the end of hall - but that's pretty minor in comparison to a "real" complaint. Overall, my experience was great and I would stay again. Highly recommended.

title: “No for tourists, there is much better elseware.”
text:
We booked into Hojo for 4 nights and stayed 1.
- Staff were fine. Not entirely warming though.
- Room was basic and v. dated. Has TV, wifi, fridge, microwave what you would expect.
- Local area was poor. No attractions. 20 mins drive from Downtown, Point Loma and Gaslamp.
- Okay for 1 night, but locals suggested the area is dangerous and we smelt marijuana strongly from our rooms.
- Bathroom window was not secure so we felt unsafe.
- San Diego is beautiful, go somewhere else and you'll appreciate it much more!

title: “Could care less about their guests”
text:
Upfront I will say, we booked this hotel not only because of the decent location, but the price was impossible to beat. 
We arrived just fine, the check in process was simple and polite. Our room wasn't large -- but not expected or needed. The toiletries from Bath & Body Works was a nice surprise, quality wise. The halls were a little noisy, but nothing terrible. Things were a little worn and the bathroom was most definitely in need of some remodeling, but overall, we were prepared for an adequate stay. We don't spend much time in the hotel rooms anyway. 
Our major problem was with the showers. You would set them to a temperature that was comfortable and it would be fine, and then the water pressure would drop, and then stop, and then start up again and shoot out scalding water. After our first night, I reported this to the front desk. The staff's response was that they could essentially care less and we were told that it would just be reported to the building engineer. Whether this actually happened or not? I am not sure. We were not left any indication that the issue had been addressed, but assumed that if a problem of showers sporadically switching to scalding water wasn't fixed, that they'd have moved us to a room without that problem. 
After showers after our second night, the problem was even worse. Fortunately we were checking out and I again, reported the issue. Hello, Holiday Inn + inexpensive prices, I'd assume lots of family stay there. Would you want a small child showering in that situation?! Not me. This woman was even less apologetic about the problem, and this time we were much more upset because clearly it hadn't been addressed. 
Honestly, I think this is unsafe. I'd never stay at this hotel again, especially because of the apathetic employees.

title: “OK Business Travel - But a Great Location”
text: We were there for a combo business/conference trip during the day, and then used the weekend and evenings for some fun. While there are probably some rooms with great views, we had a corner room on the 7th floor of the south tower and didn't have that great of a view, unless you consider roof cooling equipment a good view.

title: “Comfortable 2 Star”
text:
Would rate this hotel as average 2 star property. 
Rooms are very much on small side. Beds are about 30" off the floor which is bit of shock to the body during the night. Little room other than for the beds. 
Free fast Internet was good. View looked out on to a factory. 
Bathroom on the small side. No bath but reasonable shower. No parking at hotel or nearby which was a drag especially at drop off. Coffee/Tea making provided. Room service fair priced selection.
Hotel common areas are kept clean. Reception staff are helpful and plenty of them so no having to wait. Had early checking, around 11am.
Heater keeps main room very warm but tends to result in cold bathroom area. Good TV with usual frustration of listing all the satellite channels that you can't access.
Would book again but think overpriced at £77 for what you get but guess that's New York.

title: “Not ready for prime time”
text:
I give this hotel props for honoring a long-standing reseration, but it was too much too soon for them. They should have put us up in a completed hotel. We were on the 8th floor and every floor below us was under construction. The staff was new and confused. No one seemed to know their jobs yet and the chain of command was missing entirely so that ineffciency was compounded by lack of communication. Often there were six people standing at the registration desk, none of whom could operate the computer and all of whom had memorized scripts that had little bearing on questions asked. 
The first morning in our room the bathroom flooded because the shower door was not properly sealed. We reported this to the desk, and "an engineer" came to our room and looked at it, but nothing was done. We requested extra towels to soak up the water. The shower flooded the bathroom for the next four days, our extra towels were taken away by housekeeping the first day and not returned. We were afraid to use the hairdryer in the bathroom. I wondered about the ceiling of the room below us, but It was probably unoccupied since that floor was incomplete. Each time someone from the hotel asked us about our stay, we repeated the problem with the shower. Each time a look of panic appeared in the asker's eyes. We finally realized that the hotel had much larger 
construction problems than our leaking shower, and they probably didn't have a room finished to move us to.
On the final day we were accosted in the elevator by a man who claimed to work for the chain. He quizzed us about our stay. We gave him honest answers which he told his assistant to write down. Who this man was we were never told. He told us we would be comped one day of our stay for the inconvenience. I told my friend afterwards that was as likely to happen as our having the shower repaired or being moved to another room. We laughed about it because the whole stay could have been a Marx Bros. farce.
On the plus side the location was great, the introductory price was great and we were the first people to ever inhabit our room.The room was quiet the beds were comfortable and the heating worked.

title: “The Magnolia is fantastic!”
text: I would and will stay there again and again in no small part due to the fantasic service we got from Tory at check-in and throughout the stay. The rooms are outstanding and the lobby and club areas are excellent... And then there's the breakfast, happy hour and late night cookie bar... A terrific stay.

title: “Always a good option”
text: It was the second time we stayed there. The hotel is very confortable, bathroom has a good size and location is great too. Easy acess to all exits from LA, and there is a supermarket within walking distance. We stayed 2 nights there.

title: “Loved Four Seasons Chicago”
text: My son and I were visiting colleges in the area. We arrived at about 10:30am, way early. They took care of our bags and gave us directions to the Cubs' game. During the game called to say the room was ready. When were returned, the bags were in the our comfy room overlooking Lake Michigan. Check out the view of the sunrise from our window. Throughout, the staff and concierge were very helpful with our many questions and requests. Sent up coke and popcorn for my son, too. We felt very comfortable and taken care of in unfamiliar surroundings, which was just what we needed. Gym and pool were terrific, too. Great location between Michigan Ave and the restaurants on Rush Street.

title: “In need of renovation”
text:
We regularly stay at Residence inns, so were a little suprised at how
outdated our hotel room was. They are clearly in a renovation programme - and it needs it. We had a 2 bedroom suite which was a good size for five people but with only one bathroom it was not ideal.
Our suite had everything else we have come to expect of Residence Inn's - it was just old fashioned. It was clean, comfortable and quiet - which are always my most important factors when chosing a hotel. It is in a great location too.
Given that the rooms are being updated - I would probably stay here again.

title: “rooms not worth a four star rating...”
text: the sheraton boasts a four star rating, but the room we stayed in was no better than a cheap motel. besides its small size, the fact that our tv had no remote and one of the wall's drywall was partially caved in, the only reason we stayed in the room without demanding a new one was that there were 5 of us staying in it and we fortunately got an online deal for much much less than the normal "going rate" (plus we were only planning on spending a minimal amount of time actually in the room). the lobby is nice and the location does have beautiful views of the river and lake.. but if you're planning on paying the price of a four star hotel and expecting the same quality from its rooms, definitely go across the river to the swisotel.

title: “Decent Hotel - Great if LAX is your main concern”
text:
Embassy Suites North LAX
Rooms – clean and large. We had two TVs and separate living spaces in our room. Not too bad for the cheap priceline bid for a standard room. The fridge/microwave were standard but nice to have. Internet access available for a fee (not free) so I was a little disappointed in that. Bathroom was clean and the shower was hot. Towels were adequate.
Beds – A bit soft. They didn’t seem as firm as the typical hotel bed. Many pillows.
Alarm clock/wake up call – We used the wakeup call. They called with a standard computer message. It worked.
Checkin/Checkout – Friendly and fast. Was able to checkout “express” by just calling when I needed to leave. They also allowed us to check in at noon (we arrived at 11 a.m.) and provided an area for the suitcases so we could enjoy a lunch at the restaurant while we waited.
Free breakfast – Great! They offered the usual cereals, rolls, and fruit but also had a grill to order eggs, French toast, etc… I had a delicious eggbeaters omelet.
Restaurant – Offered standard fare. I enjoyed a fish taco that was good but not four star. The fresh sourdough bread was excellent. 
Social Hour – Free social hour was offered from 5:30-7:30. Included two free drinks of your choice (alcoholic or non-alcoholic) and some snacks such as nachos, pretzels, etc.. Can’t complain about a little free food and drink.
Pool/Exercise Equipment – Pool was smallish. Exercise equipment was standard (treadmills, elliptical, a few weights) but worked fine.
Lobby – High cellings and lots of sitting area. No major complaints except it never seemed that secure (see below).
Security – I don’t know if I liked the “open” style of the hotel room (i.e. all rooms facing an atrium/lobby) – there seemed to be less privacy than traditional hotel floor styles. I heard a fellow guest complaining of a strange guy in the laundry room on one of the floors. I wouldn’t be surprised if people could sneak in past the lobby and “wander” around in that hotel. Door locks seemed fine with room.
Laundry room – nice big washers and dryers. I noticed that one of the dryers didn’t “dry” the clothing as well as I would have liked. $1 dollar a load so standard price.
Noise – Nice and quiet. Couldn’t hear neighbors even though they seemed to have kids so I assume the walls are well-insulated.
Shuttle bus – It was free and was on time. No problems. We called to ask when they left and got to the airport quickly. Hotel is close and quick even for a Monday morning at LAX. 
Neighborhood – Lots of other hotels nearby – Buisness/Airport-like. Burger King down the street and a few other “hotel” restaurants within walking distance for additional food choices. Not close to anything besides the airport so if you want to go “somewhere” a rental car/taxi/tour would need to be considered.
Tours – Hotel had a contract with a tour company that offered various “Hollywood” or area tours for an additional fee. We went on a “condensed” 4-5 hour tour of the area since we hadn’t been to LA before. We saw the Hollywood sign, the Chinese theater, rodeo drive, farmers market, etc… We were dropped off and picked up from the hotel lobby. 
Overall, it was a great hotel if you need something close to LAX esp. if on business or just “traveling” through for a day. For vacation purposes/longer stays, I would probably go into another hotel in LA closer to main attractions or the beach.

title: “Great downtown San Francisco Hotel”
text: Pleasant stay, very comfortable, helpful and attentive staff. Bedroom very high standard. Hotel has central location, convenient for sights, transport and shops. 'Breakfast on us' deal was very good, full breakfast in the restaurant of the lobby.

title: “While staying at this Hotel drink heavily”
text: I was needing a Hotel after the Hurricane Ike storm. All of the Houston Hotels were booked up except this one...Go figure. My first night there was right out of a script from a horror movie. First of all I booked the room on a credit card. When I arrived they had not reserved a room for me. When asked what they did with my credit card number their response was " I don't know". Sensing my frustration the girl at the front desk did her best to accomodate me. She put me in a room that somebody had checked out of very recently. Reluctant but tired I accepted because what was my alternitive. My only other option was to drive 70 miles back to my house that had no electricity. When I arrived in my room panic over-came me. When I say the previous people must have just left....I mean they must have just left. The room was filled with flys and mosquitos. The floor was filthy and bed I was to lay in had body hair in it. I arrived at 9pm and by the time I bought cleaning supplies and washed the sheets it was 3pm. I paid a whopping 409 dollars for the week on this dump. I had remembered calling this same hotel just prior to the storm and they told me it was 379 dollars for the week. So they were most definitely taking full advantage of the people who's homes were not liveable at the time. To add a few more side notes. The walls are paper thin so you hear everybody elses conversations. This would not be the place to stay if you were running from the law. The air condition in my room was noisy. So much so that you had to have a few cocktails just to ignore the sound to sleep. And finally....don't expect daily room service. Don't expect to relay you need room service to the front desk. Reason being the front desk only speaks English and the maids only speak Spanish. BRING YOUR OWN CLEANIG SUPPLIES AND BUG SPRAY!!!! You will need it. As an added bonus you can relive many of your past movie experiences at The Sun Suites Westchase location. Thugs gambling in the hallways. People drinking and fighting in the rooms and surrounding areas. Cheap prositutes if needed. And plenty of liquor stores all around to ease the pain of your stay at the Stain....I mean Sun Suites Hotel....ENJOY

title: “Comfortable Hotel”
text:
The hotel is very close to the airport. We stayed ovenight after arriving from out of the country. The rooms are very comfortable and quiet. If you don't want to eat in the hotel, you do not have a lot of options within walking distance. 
Shuttles run constantly. A lot of airline crews stay here and the shuttles are crowded in the morning. Three completely full shuttles departed before we were at the front of the queue. Plan accordingly

title: “Excellent hotel, loved the sheets & the bed!”
text:
Perfect location for my trip. Parking just down the road.
Would warn guests not to try to park even briefly in the entrance (circle). The bells boys and valet service go nuts on you, if your car is even there for 1 minute!

title: “No power and NO problem”
text:
As a professional pilot I get to see a LOT of hotels all across America.
Just so happened that my trip ended up in San Diego at the Sheraton Hotel and Marina.
That evening there was a complete power failure in the southern California area.
The city and 5 million other people were without power and in the dark.
As a crew for a major airline we went to check in at the hotel for the night.
That is where I met Mr. Scott Hermes. I think he was the manager of the hotel.
Anyway, he explained what is happening at the hotel that evening.
I was very surprised to learn that just about everything was running perfectly !
The elevator was working, the staff were everywhere with handing out glow sticks, and the
Restaurant was open for business!
I went to my room and changed out of my work clothes. I then went back downstairs to
Join the fun. The bar was open and serving cocktails, and people were in a calm and festive
Atmosphere. I was a little hungry and decided to get something to eat.
I waited maybe 4 minutes to see the hostess. She had a nice table for me with a nice candle lit near the water. Quickly a waiter showed up and told me of the buffet.
I went to graze the food. The staff had excellent hot and cold food to offer.
I had some sliced beef and some tuna salad. Both were superb.
My hat is off to the entire staff of the hotel. ALL were very gracious and concerned for their
guests. It was as if they do this disaster drill all the time. There were some emergency lights
on at the hotel and they were more that enough to see your way and enjoy the evening.
Except for my room not having any power, the entire experience was a enjoyable night to remember.

title: “Great overall stay”
text:
I enjoyed staying at the Hilton Time Square, they had everything I needed and more.
Great service from the whole team from front desk to concierge, and from housekeeping to bellmen. The gym was a surprise, as it was better than we had all anticipated.
As for the rooms, no complaints from me. Very clean, comfortable beds and bathrooms were a comfortable size. Parking was valet only, and it took quite long for our car to arrive but we understand that it's a busy city and for the driver to travel 3 blocks (which is where the parking garage is located) may require patience. 
Being in Time Square you would expect it to be noisy when it's time to sleep but the hotel was amazingly quiet and you forgot what surrounded you outside the second you got to your room. 
Location wise this is the best hotel I've ever stayed at in NYC.

title: “Don't Valet Your Car”
text:
We stayed at the Amalfi Hotel in Chicago for four nights; arriving late on Sunday and leaving early on Thursday. We left our sports car in the care of the Amafi's Valet Service. When we left the vehicle, it had ample gasoline in the vehicle. When they returned the vehicle, the gas tank was empty and the warning light on the vehicle's computer indicated only 21 miles worth of gas was in the car. The gas gauge was on empty. I then noticed that there was over 100 extra miles on the vehicle and white deorderant stains on the driver's door, where someone had apparently been hanging their arm out the window while driving. There was no manager on duty when we checked out so we voiced our concerns to the on-duty clerk. He assured us that the manager would contact us. Later in the day the manager of the contracted parking company called us and assured us that he would look into the matter and call us back. We have never received a follow up from anyone. We are disappointed. 
The hotel is clean and the staff was very pleasant and responded quickly to other requests. The view from a majority of the rooms is a painted brick wall. For the price, there are numerous hotels in the area that provide better service.

title: “A Place to Celebrate”
text:
We got a great price for a room through priceline ($71.00) plus tax. We were staying in the city so we would not have to worry about driving home after dinner out and drinks to celebrate the 10th anniversary of our civil union. When we arrived the concierge, Pavel waited on us because the other two check desk agents were helping others. He asked if we were in town for any particular reason and when we told him it was our 10 anniversary he without hesitation upgraded us to a King suite on the 18th floor. Pavel could not have been any more accommodating. He asked about dinner plans (which we had already booked) told us where we could get a cab and then told us about happy hour at XIX on the 19th floor. 
The hotel is a very old hotel and some areas need some updating (the hallway wall paper) but it is very clean and a grand ole dame. It reminded me of one of the great Parisian hotels. Our room was very up to date, spacious and a real gem. Contemporary, tasteful furniture and wall coverings. When you walk into the room, you are on a landing overlooking a sunken room a few steps below. Quite an impressive entry way. There was a large bay window overlooking an enclosed atrium, a balcony also overlooking the atrium. The room also had a full size marble wet bar with several chairs, cabinets, a sink and wine refrig. The bathroom had two very large closets, a separate sink/vanity area and then a toilet with bath/shower area. The TV was a very large flat screen and if you are a Hyatt member you get free Internet. The room was impressive and up there on my top 10 list.
The XIX restaurant/ bar had a great happy hour. Again very lovely grand ole space. Could use an update but really lovely. We didn't eat there but the drink specials were cheap and very good. I would love to go back to try the restaurant and sit on one of the two decks. The place had a very Paris feel to it.
All in all we had an awesome stay at the Bellevue and will go back again. Perhaps for our 15th

title: “Great position and friendly staff but...”
text: We chose this hotel on cost and next time I would spend a little more on a different hotel. There are ice stations on every floor but no fridge in the room. The room was small and dark but adequate. The breakfast in the restaurant was OK but the carpet desperately needed cleaning. The start of the Freedom Trail is within walking distance through the lovely Boston Common and the subway is very close by to access other parts of Boston.

title: “good location, poor services”
text: great location, a few blocks from times square. hotel is normal, lower level that what you would expect after looking at their website. in the morning had to wait 10 minutes for the elevator to come at my floor. when room was made, never got shower gel and always had to ask to get some. not satisfied

title: “Better than ever.”
text: I must say that some of the telephone operators left much to be desired, in the end, however, the hotel, was lovely. Breakfast in the Oak Room was wonderful and the service was perfect. Great lobby, great bar and slow, but wonderful cafe in the main lobby. In the evening, from the room, there was a little noise from Union Square below, but it was mostly a little sweet clanging from the cable car bells, and wonderful smooth jazz from musicians below. The view of Union Square and the slice of San Francisco life made for a memorable stay in "fog city."

title: “DISPLEASING”
text: The staff speaks broken english. When I arrived late at night, I had to wait in line due to one employee checking everyone in, in which she was extremely slothful. Then as my turn approached ( I felt as if I waited in line longer than in the roller coaster line at King's Dominion in the summertime), she had the nerve to ask me "Are you okay," I just looked at her as to give her a psychic reasoning as to why I looked aggitated. The rooms are overpriced. They do not come equiped with a fridge or a coffee pot, just beds, towels, shower, toilet, sink, and tv. There were no vending machines on my floor either, they are only located on two of the floors and NO drink machine! They advertise breakfast, however, it is NOT breakfast, it is a continental breakfast consisting of carbs, coffee and juice, bagels were stale by the way. There was constant noise coming from either another room or the adjoining building (loud music/bass etc.) which lasted all night long and through early morning. I am glad I brought my ear plugs. When I asked for the best route to a particular location, the staff member handed me a map and with broken english tried to tell me how to reach my destination, needless to say, I "winged" it. I hate to be so negative, however, the website that advertises this hotel did NOT meet up to the standards of what I would have expected for the price, considering this is not in the best part of town. I certainly didn't get what I paid for with this selection. I even had two guests that were gonna to accompany me, however, I told them to stay with our family at another hotel.

title: “Only Place I will stay in Dallas”
text: I've stayed here 3 times this year an every time the service gets better. The ladies at the front desk were the most helpful and friendly people during our stay. Even with a major renovation underway, the hotel and rooms were very clean. We had a newly redone room and it was exceptional and the extras are great.... Highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Everything was great...but the room”
text: The staff at this hotel was phenomenal from the restuarant to the bar, but the room was far from perfect. The biggest issue was the room noise from both the hallway and the street. Also something that they use for laundry causes me to breakout every time I stay there. I'm a Marriott Rewards member but had some difficulty getting my number added to my reservation at the desk. While this was supposed to be all suites, there was no separation between the living area and bed, which makes this just a regular room in my opinion.

title: “Perfect-welcoming and friendly :)”
text: Our stay at the new yorker was brilliant-they could not have looked after us any better. The room was fantastic-lovely and clean with lots of towels and toiletries. The maids were lovely, the safe box was super safe and they even booked our transport to the airport. It was refreshing to wake up every morning to lots of smiling staff, knowing they were there to help with anything. Would definitely recommend 100% if you want a safe, caring and friendly hotel.

title: “Huge room, good staff, and new furniture time warped in from 1984”
text:
This is a nice family run hotel in a great location. The rooms are bigger than most in town--I stay in a different SD hotel every three weeks. They're well lit, clean, comfortable, and quiet. It's the best "mid-budget" deal in town. (If you need "low-budget" try the Good Nite Inn Sea World.)
The only weird thing is the pastel/floral print decor. It's all clean and pristine, as if it had been time warped in fresh from 1984. I don't know where they get the stuff, but it's all new and well maintained. 
If you're nostalgic for the days of Blondie and Reagan, this is paradise. If you're looking for a good room at a good price, support some great people and stay here!

title: “The worst”
text:
From the time we walked in i knew we made a terrible decision.
There were all these people hanging out in the doorway. 
The front staff could careless about your happiness or their own it seemed
The room --well more the bathroom was so dirty--the only good thing is that we only stayed there one night 
There were also some shady characters in the elevators--I am not sure where these people advertise
PLEASE STAY AWAY!!!!!!

title: “Everything you want and more”
text: This was our second time staying at the Affinia, the location is amazing, its very central almost in the middle of the magnificant mile shopping. Its less than a block in from the magnificant mile(micigan ave). Everything is in walking distance to where you would want to go. The rooms are large and comfortable. Coffee maker, lots of storage and large washroom. The bed was amazingly comfortable and the soap products lovely. And this room had to be designed by a woman because there must be a dozen electrical outlets everywhere you would want one. Mirrors galore, makes it incredibly easy to do your make up while someone is still in the washroom. And very quiet, hallways, you can hear sirens from the hospital across the street but not at all bothersome. We will surely return again.

title: “A so-so, worn-out Ritz”
text: I stayed at the Ritz for a business trip and left quite underwhelmed. The lobby is beautiful, the service was great, but the room itself was disappointing and in need of a makeover. The furniture was worn and starting to look a bit beaten up, the towels were thin and worn, the bathroom showed signs of rust in various places, the bathtub's coating was peeling in several spots, the TV was old and didn't work very well, and the room service food was nothing special. I expected much, much more from a Ritz property.

title: “Bring Lysol and pesticide.”
text:
I stayed at the Best Western Innsuites at 2000 Beach Road for two nights with my husband and toddler in March 2005 because the organizers of our family reunion reserved a block of rooms at this facility. 
The room was filthy. The shower tiles had been painted over with white paint that was peeling to reveal a horrific thick black mold underneath that you could scoop up with a spoon. The pillowcases were stained with something that looked like blood or chocolate. I had to rinse hair from the shower walls and tub before giving my child a bath. The hot and cold water handles were reversed and the cold water would not turn off without tremendous force. 
We filled the refrigerator with milk and food for our child, went out for a late dinner, and returned to find the refrigerator off and warm. The front desk did not answer the phone so we had to go to the desk ourselves. The maintenance man explained that the housekeepers had turned the refrigerator off, which was strange because it was running when we checked in that afternoon and the room had not been cleaned since. 
At 9am we went to breakfast and returned to find that our room had not been cleaned but all of our towels were gone. At 2pm we still had no towels and the front desk would not answer the phone. I went to the desk and was told that I had to wait for housekeeping to get around to my room. I explained that we had to be at the reunion in one hour and needed something to dry off with, even if it was one washcloth for the three of us to share. At that point towels miraculously appeared. 
We returned from the reunion to find that our room had not been cleaned and was swarming with fruit flies. I opened the door and window and shooed them out. While my child was napping I stepped into the hall to buy a drink. The machine was empty and then I could not get back into my room to my child. The swinging metal bar lock was hanging loose on its screws and had closed behind me. The maintenance man broke into our room while I waited anxiously in the hall. My brother in law stopped to talk, and his socks got wet from water that had flooded into the hall from the room across mine.
That night I visited relatives in the same building and saw that their rooms were all dismal, suffering from fruitfly infestations, plumbing problems, filth, and peeling paint. My brother was in a separate wing and I noticed that his room was substantially better. I called the front desk for a wake up call - no answer again. 
There was no complimentary cocktail hour as advertised, and the bar would only take cash, no credit cards. My husband ordered a Corona. There were no limes and it took the bartender 5 minutes to find a bottle opener. At breakfast there was no coffee or orange juice and the staff was walking around yelling abrasively, "No coffee, no orange juice," as if the guests were the ones who had done something wrong. 
In summary, our room was swarming with fruit flies, the front desk never answered the phone, our room was never cleaned during our two-night stay (although our towels were removed), we had to take out our own trash and beg for towels at the front desk, there was no cocktail hour, and the breakfast staff was rude. Our room was so smoky that after we flew home and opened our luggage we were overwhelmed by the odor. We could not wait to leave.

title: “elegance and a glimpse of the past”
text: The Congress was a view to a bygone era. It is a lovely building with gorgeous architecture. The lobby is stunning, with a lot of marble, brass, and velvet. The staff was very pleasant and helpful. Our room was large, with a wonderful view of Grant Park. The beds were comfortable and the room was clean. The bathroom was roomy and clean. The location could not be better, as it is right on Michigan avenue with an amazing view of the park.

title: “An oasis of calm in a fast paced city”
text:
We stayed at the Library Hotel for 4 nights - Friday through Tuesday - and were very impressed. The staff could not have been more friendly and helpful - to the extent of confirming dinner reservations, issuing bus tour tickets etc.
The hotel is in the Midtown district and well located for a lot of the major sights. Times Square, 5th Avenue, Empire State, Top of the Rock, Central Park are all within easy walking distance of 10 - 25 minutes.
The building is small and friendly and each floor/room is themed. We were on the History and Geography Floor and had a selection of books according to this theme in our room. As the name of the hotel would suggest there is a reading theme and lots of interesting books to dip in and out of, both in the room and "communal" areas.
The breakfast room is small with only 8 tables of varying size though there was never a problem getting a space whilst we were there. August is off peak for New York though and I suspect this could be a problem at busier times. The breakfast itself was good and of a continental style, with a wide selection of cakes/pastries and cereals.
The same room is used for the complimentary wine/cheese every night between 5pm and 8pm. Again always enough room and a decent choice for what is only designed to be an opportunity to chill out with a quick snack and tipple.
There is a small roof top bar which is quaint and cosy.
The bedrooms were comfortable (though not massive - this is a small converted building after all) with plenty of storage space and all amenities - including lovely cosy dressing gowns.
We really enjoyed our stay here and would definitely recommend it.

title: “Archbishop's Mansion gets A+ for character, atmosphere and service”
text: Seeking a getaway without actually leaving town, I recently stayed at the historic Archbishop's Mansion on Alamo Square in San Francisco. Having traveled a fair amount in the U.S. and abroad, I was pleasantly surprised to find one of the most satisfying lodging experiences anywere right here in SF. The high-ceilinged, antique-packed rooms ( each named after a famous opera) were simply exquisite -- be sure to ask for a tour during your stay. And the Mansion's common areas are a veritable museum of 20th Century Americana -- from a chandelier featured in Gone With the Wind to a working player piano that once belonged to Noel Coward. Proprieter John Spear and his staff provided first-class service and made us feel at home from the moment we walked through the front door. They also had plenty of interesting stories to share from the Mansion's rich history. If you're looking for an alternative to the sterile chain hotels that dominate Union Square and Fisherman's Wharf, treat yourself to a stay at the Archbishop's Mansion. If my experience is any indication, you'll be very glad you did.

title: “Family Reunion trip”
text: We brought in family from varying locations for a reunion in San Diego as well as Mom's 80th Birthday. The staff was top notch and were so helpful. Location was convenient for an outing to Sea World and later a dinner in the Gaslamp district. The gathering went so well that we may do it again next year at this location.

title: “Everything I thought and more”
text: This is my first year to go to with a group of Quilter from southeast Kansas to the International Quilt Festival. We have never stayed in a hotel that was so accommodating. We were glad to see that the shuttle was extended for the weekend to accommodate all of us. Especially me when I forgot my prescription medicine and they were more than happy to take me to the pharmacy! Thanks you Jo, Sonny, John and all the other staff for making my once a year trip the best!!! I hope to you see you next year.

title: “Comfy stay, nice extra touches”
text:
Room was a bit more spacious than i expected. Nice, clean, new-looking. Free in-room WI-FI. They have 2-3 Internet kiosks at the lobby too.
Free coffee/tea/hot choc at the lobby all day (this was a saviour). There's also a huge bowl of apples at the lobby that's free for all. Nice touch. Free breakfast every morning - not the wide spread of food you get at big chain hotels but it's adequate. Omelettes, bread, danish, DIY waffles, yoghurt, fruits, milk, juices... Breakfast ends at 10am. Once, my friends were still eating at 10am and I went to the lobby to check something. Upon returning to the breakfast room, the guard at the door told me it's locked and I cannot go back in. Had to say please a few times and explain my friends are really in there before he told me to get in through a side door.
