Super near 50th Street station, and of course walking distance to Times Square. Diner, Chinese food, Mexican food, a few convenience stores all nearby.
Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great moderate Hilton”
text:
The hotel may not be a full fledge ***** Hilton, but rooms offers everything you need - great bed, flat screen TV, excellent shower. There is a roof top bar as well as restaurant by the lobby.
The main reason for staying here is the excellent location for a good price.
One and two blocks from the subway stops, three blocks from the Italian food emprium, Eataly, and three blocks from the High Line Park. The location on the border of the Chelsea district, you also have plenty of great restaurant options like Hill Country BBQ Market.

title: “Perfect if you like water parks”
text: Really nice resort with its own water park. Beautiful landscaping and very comfortable suites. Great Western restaurant on property. Very family friendly.

title: “Fantastic hotel !!!”
text:
Stayed here for 5 nights in August 2012 as part of a 3 centre USA west coast holiday. 
I was expecting this to be just another "standard" Holiday Inn hotel, having stayed in a number of Holiday Inn hotels in the UK. However, this hotel was so much better than those I have stayed in previously. Everything about the hotel was superb - the rooms, the beds, the public areas, the swimming pool area, the hotel's complimentary free shuttle bus which runs frequently to and from City Walk and Universal Studios - everything.
I have to also give a special mention to Carla who manages the reception. We had reason to seek her help and local knowledge on a couple of ocassions and found her to be exceptionally pleasant and helpful. 
This was by far the best hotel we stayed in throughout our stay and hope to return to LA on vacation again in the future. I will not hesitate to stay here again.
If you are looking for a great place to stay which is conveniently located for Hollywood, Beverly Hills and Universal Studios then you will not be disappointed.

title: “A lovely stay - thank you”
text: My daughter and I stayed for 9 nights whilst attending an event at the World Centre opposite. Everything was clean and staff (particularly housekeeping) were friendly and most polite! Room service was excellent and bar and restaurant staff courteous and meals reasonably priced. The doormen were ultra helpful and really nothing was too much trouble! We loved the tourist trolley service right from the hotel door and felt safe strolling to the eateries close by the hotel. Loved Boston - wonderful city and hope we can return someday.

title: “Nice hotel, noisy location”
text: We were looking for a location close to the TD Garden and this hotel is perfect for that purpose. The rooms are small, but well appointed and the staff friendly and helpful. The only disappointment was that there is a night club just down the block and the loud thump thump of the bass could be heard until the wee hours of the morning, ear plugs helped. Didn't seem to be much of a surprise when mentioned to the desk at check out. If you are looking for a restful sleep look elsewhere.

title: “Great location, okay hotel.”
text: This hotel is very clean and in a great downtown location. The downtown shoping area is right there and it's easy to jump on a the cable car or use any other public transportation to get around San Francisco. However, very similar to othe downtown hotels, they nickel and dime you for everythings, for coffe in the mornign to Internet in the room, and most of all parking. This is what's expected in big city hotels though and it's worth the stay if you want to be in a great location for a reasonable price.

title: “What a jewel!”
text: What an amazing spot! We came in here late on a Friday night and found a very chipper and friendly front staff. And we were also greeted by Jack Jack, an adorable little dog that was a wonderful greeter after our long trip from NYC. The place was quite easy to find from the Embarcadero spot on BART. Our room wasn't huge but nicely appointed and comfortable. This place was really cool. We missed the wine hour due to a VERY LONG walk up to Golden Gate Park from the hotel. But when we came back, Tina, one of the staff provided us with wine because she thought we could use a glass. This hotel paid such attention to service and courtesy. The front desk was caring and sweet but not pretentious or saccharine. My husband and I have travelled to many hotels due to his work in travel writing - this one stands out. I am definitely going back.

title: “Great service”
text: Had 3 stays in December 2010. Each suite was exactly as described when booking on the internet. Service at front desk was best I have experienced in 11 visits to the USA. Suites have refrigerators you can stock yourself rather than pay mini bar prices. Free internet on computers in the lobby. 5 minute walk to the Galleria Mall. Not all suites have safes so request on if you need one. There are also safety despoit boxes at front desk.

title: “Grant Plaza offers good location at low rates”
text: The Grant Plaza offers great location, views, and comfortable rooms at a low price. Located in Chinatown, you're within walking distance of Market Street, Union Square, North Beach, BART, and cable cars. Try to get a room on the top (6th) floor. My room was clean, had a good view of the financial district, and plenty of sunshine. The only complaint was that the bathroom fan was very noisy. Staff very helpful.

title: “Meets Needs”
text: This is pretty much a standard-issue Hampton Inn. It's got all the amenities of other Hampton Inns, but no more. Some of the Hampton Inns have little extras in the room. This one did not, but was certainly comfortable and very close to The Domain, which was convenient. Overall nice, quiet and workable.

title: “Good Business Stay”
text:
Stayed at the Marriott in October for 5 nights and it was very good. There are many hotels in this area and having stayed in another higher end one, I can say the Marriott does hold its own and is my current top choice for business stay in Denver Downtown.
It is accessible to restaurants,shopping etc.

title: “Attentive staff!”
text: I was at this hotel for a business meeting for just one night. Unfortunately I managed to trip and fall on the way into building. At least four staff members were immediately at my side to make sure I was ok. They got my car parked, me checked in, ice for my knee, and me to my room swiftly. All demonstrated above and beyond courtesy and respect. Room service was prompt. The staff throughout my stay were among the friendliest I''ve experienced at any hotel. The room was spacious and comfortable. I would stay here again. Thanks staff for worrying about my needs.

title: “Lovely elegant hotel”
text:
Close to the White House, close to the washington memorial and lincoln memorial.
Tip - visit the Lincoln Memorial after midnight. I arrived from the airport at 1am, couldn't sleep, went for a run down to the memorial. There was me, a security guard, and a stoned amorous couple. I had abe to myself. And the reflections in the water are amazing at night. Very cool.

title: “New hotel in a great location!”
text: My wife and I stayed here for a few days over the 4th of July weekend. The hotel is very new and updated with nice spacious rooms. The hotel is located in the heart of the Gaslamp Quarter and just a block or two from Petco Park. It made for a perfect location for us and puts you in the center of great restaurants and bars. Hotel staff was good and the valet guys were awesome! There is a fitness center and pool on the third floor. The pool is small and just OK but workable if you are there for a short stay.

title: “Beat expectations”
text: Spent two nights this week. Were skeptical about location until we served. Wonderful staff, free shuttle downtown and to ferry. Helpful staff. We illmstay here again. Dining was average but we did not really eat much.

title: “Great Location - Great Service”
text: I stayed at this hotel over a weekend for my brother's wedding....and several months later for a funeral in the Charlotte area. The rooms are spacious and very clean. The staff was courteous and helpful. The location is perfect for downtown events. (The only caveat to this statement is that it is very difficult to get to on a Panthers home-game Sunday because of the proximity of the stadium and the related traffic.) Because we had so many members of the extended family in town for the wedding, we took great advantage of the breakfast room/lobby - sitting around eating and chatting in front of a roaring fire. The staff was very helpful in distributing a "goody bag" to each wedding guest staying at the hotel. A parking garage is conveniently attached to the hotel and I don't remember having to pay for it over the weekend.

title: “Loved it!”
text:
We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Madison. We booked via Expedia for one night for New Years Eve 2007. Valet parking was expedient and efficient. Can't complain there. We had a king room and it was large and nicely appointed. The bathroom was as expected and lovely. There was a stocked refrigerator and corkscrew in the room which was nice. There were also treats like cookies and such on a counter in the room. We ordered room service and had the best jamabalaya we've ever had!! Seriously. It was that good. We also had the Kobe beef cheeseburger which melted in our mouths. Go for either one, you won't be disappointed. We ordered a bottle of champagne for the celebration but it took FOREVER getting there so the bar manager ended up sending it up free for our inconvenience. We wouldn't have ordinarily minded but it was 11:50 before we got it and the entire premise of New Years centers around 12 midnight so we were glad for the comp. 
The only real complaint I have is that the AC vent is directly overhead and facing the bed. It blew on us all night and all of us (including my 3 month old daughter) woke up sick. Grrrrr. The hotel never did respond to my complaint. The manager wasn't available when we checked out and I called and left a message and they never called back. Too bad. All would've been perfect but for that.

title: “Nice Hotel but traffic noise was terrible”
text: Nice hotel generally but it would benefit from double glazing. We had very little sleep for the 4 nights due to the traffic noise

title: “Very very small rooms”
text: The rooms are clean and have a nice bed, however they are very small with practically no closet space and no drawers at all. The bathroom is also very very small

title: “Very helpful receptionist ”
text:
Arrived later afternoon after 14 hours flight. We met a very helpful receptionist who recommend us a local italian food. 
A bit disappointed because there is no slippers and toothpaste and tooth brush in the room. We need to walk to cvs to buy.

title: “Great Location - Great Hotel”
text: I stayed here while on business and had a very comfortable stay. Having free access to the internet allowed me to keep up with email during the evening. The room was clean and the staff was quite helpful. The location was great, close to shopping, great restaurants and easy access to the public bus. I would highly recommend staying here for business or pleasure.

title: “Amazing NYC Vacation!!”
text: Just returned from 8 nights in NYC. The Hilton Graden Inn was in an excellent location. It was walking distance to Times Square, subways,attractions, theatres and a full service grocery store. The microwave and fridge were a very convenient bonus. The queen sized beds were comfortable and although the room seemed a bit small, I understand that this is typical of NYC hotels. One of the nicest gestures that I've ever experienced from a hotel was the fact that I received an email from a Customer Service Representative asking about our hotel stay preferences and when we went into our room, there was two gift bags with snacks and beverages! We loved our NYC vacation!

title: “Not happy”
text:
Beautiful, standard Four Seasons: nice room, large bathroom, and comfortable bed. Noise from the floor above to after midnight four nights in a row. No coffee maker in room. Unable to use fitness center because it does not open until after 7 AM on weekends when my meeting started. It is a very nice hotel, but not close to being worth the inflated price.
The week before my visit, Four Seasons sent me an email telling me I was eligible for a “By invitation upgrade” and suggested I use it on my next stay. When I tried to use it for this stay, I was told I was not eligible because my room was going to be billed to the meeting sponsor. Why they sent me the email only to reject me is beyond me. But it gets worse. I had to waste 10 minutes at checkout because they had the room billed to me! Then they asked if my customer experience was “superior”.

title: “Well appointed rooms and easy transportation options”
text: This hotel offers very nice amenities. Even though the rooms are a bit older, they are very well appointed and comfortable. The metro is just a quick walk down the hill and offers rapid transportation service into the heart of D.C. The staff was very gracious and helpful. We were even upgraded to a deluxe room when our standard room was suddenly inundated with water from above. There was no need to negotiate or complain. The staff knew about our dilemma and responded with an immediate upgrade. The restaurants on site were convenient and served excellent food. Be sure to try the breakfast buffet at The Stone's Throw Restaurant and the vegetable Chili at Harry's Pub.

title: “Fabulous location, loud heating system.”
text:
A quick shopping trip to Seattle necessitated a hotel near the downtown shopping district where we could park the car and walk. This hotel is steps away from Nordstrom, two shopping centres and only blocks from Pike market. We felt we couldn't have stayed in a better downtown location. 
When we checked in, the staff were very welcoming and professional. We were given a room that had the beds we had asked for and - bonus - two bathrooms. This is an older hotel that has been upgraded, so it's quirky like that. Having two bathrooms was really a plus for two women traveling together. However I cannot recommend room 1210 as the air/heating unit (not central) was very loud and buzzed. It wasn't so bad when we were awake and moving about the room but when it got quiet and we went to bed, it seemed really loud. 
Otherwise, this is what you expect from a Mayflower property. Old style furnishings, excellent linens, great amenities and very competent staff. The perfect shopping location makes this a place to consider staying if you are spending your Seattle time downtown.

title: “what a dump”
text: upon check-in there is some guy more intent on looking at his computer than helping a guest. He told me that I didn't have a reservation yet Travelocity said I did. I reluctently checked-in then went to a retitement party about 1 block away. When we got in the room we were tired but as soon as we sat on the bed I swore I was sitting on a peice of plywood. Then the traffic noise!! I thought I was in a truck-stop!! The windows were paper thin I couln't tell the difference between closed or open. after trying to sleep a couple of hours, we had to leave. I went in to the bathroom to find out we were not the only guests using the room. I stepped on about 5 cock-roaches in the bathroom. The towels were like sandpaper. I've stayed in a lot of hotels, motels etc around this continent but this was worse than a 3rd world country.

title: “No need to settle for this”
text:
There are way too many places to stay in this area of Chicago to settle for this place. First, let me list the good since it wasn't all bad:
1. My room was clean
2. The staff was very helpful and nice
3. Certain amenities were free, such as computer access, gym access, and a fridge for my room.
4. Some would consider the decorations attractive, but that's subjective.
Now for the bad:
1. The room smelled like old books
2. The bed was very worn out and uncomfortable.
3. The TV doesn't have a lot of channels and it's HD but most of the channels aren't so the picture quality is very bad.
4. The gym is very lackluster. Only three treadmills, three elipticals, one exercise bike, a very poor selection of dumbbells, and a life-style machine that I couldn't get the pin to fit into to adjust the weight plates, so I couldn't use it. 
5. The 3 computers they have for internet use are outdated, and you have to be standing to use them. It would be nicer if you can sit, and nicer yet if they would spend 40 dollars to get better mice than the cheap, rollerball ones they use that don't move very well.
6. Worst of all, my room was situated right above where the line forms for the House of Blues. No big deal when people are in line before the show starts because it's early. And even though there was quite a line before the show, it wasn't that bad. But afterward, it was a different story. I'm guessing most of the concert goers were drunk, because they were 100x louder after the show than before. The staff at the House of Blues manages the line before the show, so you would think they would tell people to leave the property after the show, but nope. There were people loitering there for hours. Literally, hours. They know there's a hotel right across the driveway, so if I was the manager, that would never happen. By that point, I was already in bed, and I didn't want to pack everything back up and get dressed to move to another room. 
You might say that I was stupid for staying here, and if I would have known this was the hotel I'd be staying at, you'd be right. But I arranged my hotel stay through Hotwire only knowing that it was a "4 star" hotel and a couple of the amenities. They did not say it was right next to a noisy landmark, otherwise I would have avoided this place like the plague. 
And even if it weren't for the location and lack of House of Blues staff dealing with people loitering for *hours*, this still doesn't deserve four stars because of the 5 other issues I mentioned.

title: “2 rooms out of 3....not bad????????”
text:
The Terrace Inn is very convenient, is well maintained, has a reasonable breakfast, and is reasonably priced for Boston.
I would have liked to rate this hotel 5 stars but an annoying thing happened when I stayed there recently. I made reservations for ***3 rooms*** at this hotel 5 months prior to the date because it was Boston University graduation weekend (my wife and I and 2 other relatives were coming up). I called several times over the 5 months to make sure we stil had our ***3 rooms***. Each time we were reasured the reservation was there for ***3 rooms***. We got a letter from them stating since it was a busy weekend our deposit was non refundable if we canceled within a few weeks of the date. Not nice but we accepted that since we were coming for sure. We arrived on the day, came in at 1:30 pm. They told us they had our ***3 rooms*** reserved but they were not ready yet. No problem, we would leave our luggage there, see the sights of wonderful Boston and return after dinner. Just to be safe, I called at 3:30 pm to see if we needed to do anything else for our ***3 room*** reservation. "No" they said, everything was taken care of, we had our ***3 rooms***. We returned at 9:30 pm to be told we had ????? 2 rooms, not 3. "We overbooked and since you had 3 rooms we thought you could get by with 2" they said nicely (I have no complaints about the weekend night manager, he was stuck with the situation he didnt create). All of Boston was booked, it was late, they gave us $20 off each room, and gave us two rooms- a suite with two rooms the relatives had to share and a room with two single beds for me and my wife. The next morning I requested and got an additional room. Upon checking out I asked the manager how this happened and he said "We don't do this on purpose, it just sometimes happens". That was it. You other travellers can tell me if this happens frequently to you (has never happened to me in 49 years) I emailed the Best Western office, they said I would hear within a week (haven't heard anything in 1 1/2 weeks) from the Terrace Inn. We got by ok for one night, it wasn't THAT big of a deal but my questions are: if you can take ALL my money if I don't show up, why can't you make sure everyone who puts that money up has a room? Have you looked into this "mistake" to see how often it happens? Wouldn't it be nice to respond to questions referred from the main office?
So I suggest they study the overbook policy OR drop that no refund policy on busy weekends. If you make reservations, you might want to have a cancelable reservation somewhere else JUST IN CASE.

title: “In the middle of everything to do in Manhattan New York.”
text: Convenient location to all the main attractions. Walking distance to Radio City Music Hall, Rockefeller Center, Central Park, Time Square, Broadway Theater District, The Metropolitan Musuem, and The American Musuem of Natural History. Easy access to transportation to all other New York tourist destinations. Had a spacious room with all the comforts of home. Friendly hotel staff through out the hotel!! Would love to come back!

title: “4 Seasons quality and ...”
text:
I may be a bit critical only 'coz of being a loyal Four Seasons customer that believe in their quality as well as the price paid for this particular property (US$695/nite excluding all other taxes and this is a B&B package). 
Having said that, I do like the rooms, spacious on the 23rd floor, with LCD TVs (one in the bathroom), a big glass shower with a sit down bench, a nice music pipe in system, marble bath tub (big), etc. Towels and bathrobes were thick and comfortable as were the sheets in the bed. See attached photo for room details. One thing that I had found that was unacceptable was the mold in the brackets that hold the shower bench together. For an expensive 4 Seasons, the cleaning should be more thorough.
We had a King bed and a little sitting area that overlooks a buidling that has a penthouse rooftop garden that was quite pretty to look at. I especially like the dresser area - big walk in with lots of room for his and hers and enough drawers for his and hers ! (usually most hotels have only 3 sets of drawer but this room has 6 !!!). 
Check in was swift and efficient, things (breakfast, gym, etc) were explained and indicated to us so we didnt have a problem finding our way around. 
Gym was adequate, I especially appreciate that they have a fridge stocked full of bottle water rather than the usual water cooler.
Breakfast was good (dont know the price coz we had a package) but nothing amazing. Location is great if u like to shop. We (husband and I) especially enjoyed the bar which makes a good martini (and what a variety !!!).
All in all, we had enjoyed our stay, staff are friendly, good amenities and location. We will return but this time if I see another moldy shower, I will inform the hotel about it. It is just not acceptable for a 4 Seasons that one has to pay $695/nite.

title: “Service, Service, Service, and all with a smile and going the extra mile.”
text: From the minute I arrived at the front door the attendant assured me my personal belongs were safe and, Dennis, protected my luggage while I parked my car. Then he brought everything to my guest room later. Jules, at the front desk was cheerful and extremely helpful. She mapped everything out for me so I could get around town with ease. Everyone that delivered something to my guest room; ice, food, was pleasant and smiled. It made my stay so pleasant I did not want to leave. The view from my room was excellent and the staff was great too.

title: “Nearby Shopping and Major Highway!”
text:
In June 2009 I went to San Diego for a wedding and booked a room at the Sheraton due to it's nearby access to the highway and shopping.
The hotel is very clean and staff friendly, and the location is close to Fashion Valley Mall. Finding this hotel is not that hard since it is an exit off the access highway parallel to I-8. However, we did get lost trying to get to the otherside of the highway for a shopping day at Fashion Valley. 
Sheraton are well branded hotel and very spacious. Our room overlooked the back so we didn't hear any sounds from the highway. Beds are very comfortable and the flat screen television was larger than most hotels. The only negative thing about this hotel was the parking situation. They do charge for parking in the front, however the gates were always up so you really didn't need access for parking. After the wedding we parked on the side, which needed more light at night. However, the side entrance to the hotel made it safe to walk from your car to the hotel.
The location of the hotel is great if you love to shop and go into downtown San Diego with direct access near the major highways. Since Fashion Valley Mall is literally across the highway, there are alot of places to eat at the mall and the surrounding shopping center on Camino Del Rio N. 
Based on the price, service, location, and comfortable bed, I would recommend this hotel for both business and leisure travelers in San Diego. There are alot of places to eat nearby, especially an In-N-Out Burger right across the highway. Fashion Valley Mall has extensive shops and major department store that makes a shopper experience amazing! Bon Voyage!

title: “nice hotel, great location!”
text: very nice large rooms, clean bathroom, great a/c. breakfast was ok. we enjoyed very much our stay.

title: “Not up to par - nickel & diming”
text:
I've stayed at the Westin Tabor Center for business a handful of times, and I can honestly say I would never stay there by personal choice. 
I will start with the pluses:
-Very friendly and capable desk staff
-Nice lobby
-Most beds are comfortable
-Great showerheads 
Now the minuses:
-The Westin will nickel and dime you at every opportunity. Want internet in your room? That will be another $10.60 a day. Even a Holiday Inn Express will give you free wireless! Room service prices are extortionate-around $18 for eggs and a side, and there is no continental breakfast provided by the hotel. Bottled water-usually provided complimentary at a hotel of this class-will run you $4. 
-The airport shuttle they advertise is just a run-down SuperShuttle that you will be paying for (if it even shows up). 
-Interior decor outside of the lobby is poor. Wallpaper in the hallways is covered with nicks and scrapes. The color scheme throughout the hotel is a dull brown/beige which is very unappealing. 
-Every time I've been there, the service carts have just been left sitting in the hallways. Unattractive and a hassle if you are trying to squeeze by with rolling luggage. 
-Stocking of the rooms is poor. Each time I've stayed there, a different thing has been missing from my room (bath towels, robe, soap, the "heavenly" mattress top).
-The last time I was there, the cable TV was down for the entire hotel. No apology from the desk and certainly no rate concession.
The bottom line:
The desk clerks will treat you very well, but that is the only thing that is "four star" about this hotel. I don't see any way they can justify $280 a night (realistically more like $290-320 after you get internet and other services).

title: “Great value, great location.”
text: I needed a room for new year's eve and this fit the bill: very nice for the price, staff is friendly, and the parking garage around the corner has a deal with them for overnight parking. It's just outside the Chinatown gate, which makes for great access to fun bars and restaurants.

title: “Rooms retained strange smells..and it wasn't me..”
text:
I chose this hotel on the basis of its location and all the positive reviews for it. I found the location fantastic - close to where I wanted to be, close to Metro and good food. The staff was very pleasant and helpful. When the tv remote needed to be fixed, they were there in mere minutes with battery replacement. When I needed a cab, it was quick and easy. 
My issue was with the room itself which had a distinct negative odor to it. They quickly and switched me out with a different floor and room, but sadly a lesser version of the odor followed. Something travelling through the vents? I don't know, but it was enough to make me not want to stay there again. 
Landed right on a wedding party floor. Crazy loud up until 4am. My fault for not complaining, but it was certainly the talk of the hotel in the morning. And not the good J Bar kind of talk.
Perhaps the James is a little classy for me, but next time I'll take one of the major chains in the area.

title: “Amazing experience...”
text: Great Value for the room (suite). Top notch, very impressive and comfortable. Every staff we dealt with (even guy mopping floors at 3 AM) was friendly and helpful. I can only say good things.

title: “Loved the sangria after a long hot day”
text: This hotel was stunning. Right when we walked in the front lobby we were impressed with the decor. This hotel was very clean and had greatly oversized rooms with very nice bedding. My only complaint was the lack of an exhaust fan in the bathroom. It got pretty foggy. That is such a minor issue that I still gave the hotel 5 stars. The best part was when they told me that I get a free night of parking because my car was red. After a long hot day walking around DC, we got back to the hotel and were greeted with sangria and water (for my underage son). Great experience. Great attention to detail. they are all about pleasing the customer. Breakfast buffet was very expensive and after looking we decided it was definitely not worth the $.

title: “Terrific stay!!”
text: Perfect location-near it all but not on top of it all. Extremely friendly staff!! Nice breakfast. Spacious room for midtown, or anywhere for that matter. Definitely a great pick for midtown!!

title: “Great value”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights. All the staff were friendly, helpful and cheerful. Our king suite was large with an airconditioner and plasma TV in each room. The king bed was very comfortable & was in a separate bedroom; although the mattress on the sofa bed in the lounge room was not particularly thick and was uncomfortable as you could feel the springs through it. 
There was also a fridge and microwave in the room which were both handy plus free wi fi. The bathroom was very large and the shower which was over the bathtub had good water pressure. 
The free breakfast was adequate & included juice, tea/coffee, cereals, fruit, toast, bagels, muffins etc plus a couple of hot items (eg scrambled eggs) and waffles. Each afternoon there were cold drinks and biscuits available in the foyer plus coffee and tea available all day.

title: “Not the nicest hotel, but great service and nice little touches”
text:
I stayed here on a Friday night in order to take my LSAT on Saturday morning at the nearby university. It was a great experience. I was warmly greeted every time I came into the hotel by the receptionist (who used my first name) and they had no problem taking my luggage for an extra few hours after my check out. I rode my motorcycle there, and the receptionist, who was a motorcycle guy, was more than happy to let me park in the garage for no charge. I also got a call a bit after I checked in to check up on me and see if there was anything that could be done to make my stay more comfortable.
The rooms themselves were average. No cool TV services or anything, but there is WiFi. Bathroom and everything else was just fine.
Overall, I enjoyed my cheap stay in Baltimore here. It's no luxury hotel, but it was perfect for a college student.

title: “For the price, this IS a Dream”
text:
My wife and I stayed at Dream over Christmas 2004 on the tail end of our honeymoon. We had booked it purely on the recommendation of a British newspaper before it had even opened and were extremely impressed. Despite arriving a day late due to flight problems the staff were most accommodating and upgraded us to a King sized room upon check-in.
The midtown location is perfect for Broadway, the well known shops and Central Park; all within walking distance. The staff were very efficient, the room was superb, the bed as good as they get, and all the little extras in the room and bathroom are a refreshing change from the norm. We had a 2nd floor room and the 55th Ave traffic noise was not a problem at all.
You must check out the Penthouse Bar for guests on the 13th floor. The music and ambience is perfect and the view up Broadway towards Times Square is excellent. If you're a smoker, don't fret because there's a balcony to have a crafty cigarette. Well worth a visit.
We're already looking forward to our next visit. Highly recommended!

title: “GREAT Location If You Need to Be Near The Airport Terminals”
text:
LOCATION – that is what you need in an airport hotel and this has it in spades. It is situated between Terminals B and C and is connected to all terminals by an underground people mover train, so no pesky shuttle busses. No airplane noise. However, the hotel itself is old and in need of updating (e.g. the TV’s are not flat screens, which are common nowadays). Rooms are reasonably clean, but improvement could be made. Staff were very helpful and professional. Includes a business center and nicely equipped fitness center (open 24 hours, a plus). Has a guest laundry which provides complimentary detergent which is a minor, but nice touch. Has revolving restaurant on the roof. I ate in the lounge/bar part of this; nothing special, but good service and cold beer.
Perfect if you have an early morning flight or have another reason to stay near the terminals. Not the best choice for a long stay.

title: “Good location, poor service and facilities. Wost hotel stay and value for money.”
text: If you are looking for location this the hotel for you. However, its an 80 plus years old building with no A/C hallways out of you room, slow elevators for a tall building, and renevation works that start every day at 7AM. The breakfast buffet is small with limited choices. The rooms although looks clean, i have injered myself from a broken glass that was not picked up from previous occupents. I had a package delivered to the hotel which was not delivered only after lengthy tracking from my side, which was pending with the conceirge. My stay never to be repeated.

title: “Noisy and Dirty”
text:
Don't stay on the side facing the fire station & police station.... two of the worst things to have outside of ones window in NY. But, it is a very safe area!
The lobby is nice, but the room felt dirty. YUCK!

title: “Customer Service”
text: I've stayed at plenty hotels throughout the last few years and I just want to say that this was one of the best experiences I've had. Ronna and Yolanda made my check in very enjoyable. I recently had a bad stay at another property but the staff here helped me to regain all the confidence I previously lost. Whenever i'm back in Ft Worth, this is the only place I will stay!

title: “Things have gone downhill”
text:
As locals having been to Fort Rapids with friends in the past, we had been impressed with the improvements made there this year. Well, something has changed, and not for the better - we are so sad to see a place like this become what it has. It was so nice to have a water park in Columbus, now we will have to travel to take the kids to a water park. 
Instead of the friendly and clean lobby we were used to, it was dirty and the girl at the counter was not very pleasant. We had some issues with the type of room, but it was resolved and we were on or way.
The room looked dingy compared to previous visits, but did have towels and clean sheets. No clock, or room service menu.
Trying to get a meal was difficult, as the restaurant was closed due to no business, a shame because my kids loved the fun staff and the kids buffet. 
The bar had some men that were very loud and seemed to have had a few too many, so we passed on eating there and had to settle for pizza in the water park.
We still had fun in the water park itself, but won't be back. The changing rooms were filthy (gross!) We heard too many guests complaining about their rooms and service so we knew we were not alone. 
The place was really nice just two months ago, the staff was amazing and we had a great time. It is not the same place it just feels depressing, dirty and not happy and I won't bring children there again.

title: “Location, Location, Location - I'd definately stay here again!”
text:
My family and I just returned from New York where we stayed at the Wellington Hotel (end of June). Weather was hot, but the air conditioning in the room worked great. I cannot stress how important a consideration location should be for anyone visiting New York - do your homework. This was our first time and I researced alot of different hotels and chose The Wellington - and it did not disappoint! Just minutes from Central Park, Times Square, 5th Avenue shops, etc. (we even walked to the American Museum of Natural History - 20 minutes) We decided to experience the REAL New York and arrived Sunday morning. Adventurous, we decided to forego the shuttles and cabs and spend $2 each to hop on the M60 bus right at the airport. We transferred to the subway (N) at Astoria which dropped us right next to The Wellington. The timing was perfect for this as it wasn't busy and we arrived in less than 30 minutes!
Room - we had booked 1 room for the 4 of us with 2 double beds. When we checked in, they gave us 2 rooms, side by side for the same price and even included breakfast on the house in the cafe. 
Atmosphere - it's not all glitz, but has a charm all it's own - almost like you've stepped back in time a bit (I loved this). No it's not all swanky and new, but things were very clean and well maintained.
Staff - every single staff person we encountered went out of their way to help us. They were not imposing, but always offered to see if they could help us out which made us feel welcome from the moment we got off the subway and walked in the front door. We arrived in the morning and had no expectation that our room would be ready, but the bellmen were very helpful and organized about storing our things until later in the afternoon when we returned to check in. I'd have to say that part of the atmosphere I enjoyed so much was because of the professional demeanor of the staff.
Computers for internet access for flight information, etc. was easy to find and very reasonable in price.

title: “Hoped for more”
text:
A great location and promising pedigree had raised our expectations, but candor compels the admission that our expectations went unmet. If the hotel were a liquid, it would have to called lukewarm. 
The hotel had our reservations just as we expected. Checkin was easy. Parking was not quite ideal, as valet is the only realistic option: there is no garage available for self-park. That's life in a downtown, perhaps. But both our rooms had key issues; it was never possible to get both keys to work. One key would work, and the other wouldn't. Strangely, that curse afflicted both rooms. Hardly life and death, but odd.
The bathrooms had no bath. There was a nice shower, but no tub. Pity. The bed was very comfortable, but once again, with a catch: the reading lamp and night table were on one side only. It was not possible for two people to lie in bed and read. Upon checkin, the bed cover was quite wet (all over). Likely it had just been washed, as it was certainly clean, and housekeeping rapidly replaced it with great energy. But the phenomenon was unsettling, as you can imagine. And after the fiasco with all the non-working keys, we began to conclude that the Brown Palace was more brown than palatial. 
Retrieving the car from valet the first time was easy. Retrieving the next time (upon checkout) was maddeningly slow, taking at least 20 minutes despite no great crowd. Again, nice staff. Just a puzzling disappointment. 
Visited the concierge three times. Twice with excellent results. Once with nobody there, for so long that surrender and abandonment became the only sensible solution. Yet again, it was a story of some very positive experiences, tempered by a disappointment. 
What's the bottom line? If you are forced to stay here, don't fret. You won't go badly wrong staying here. Nothing terrible will befall you. You may even have a great experience. Ours could have been one of those random glitches that happens to all human enterprises. But all things equal, our forgettable stay will lead us to take our chances elsewhere next time, not out of anger or even annoyance, just out of the firm conviction that we can do better.

title: “Clean, convenient and comfortable.”
text:
The Hilton at O'Hare is ideally situated if you have an early flight or are arriving very late and want to avoid the drive into Chicago. While the airport is only about 30 minutes from downtown Chicago, the drive could potentially take much longer if traffic is heavy. Thus it takes the worry out of the commute if you wake up and you're already there!
The rooms are reasonably large, and well-maintained. My room also had a large flat screen TV that had inputs to accepr HDMI, RCA or VGA from my laptop. A feature I'd like to see in all hotels! I even had a very comfy recliner to relax in. The bed was very confortable and the bathroom was spotless!
My only complaints were that the thermostat in the room did not go low enough (lowest I could set it was 65F/18C) which is a bit high for us Canadians used to lower nighttime temperatures. 
Also, the elevator noise was quite loud. While the front desk staff did ask me my preference of being close to or far from the elevators, and did also ask if 8 rooms away was far enough (which I answered would be fine), my room actually turned out to be 2 rooms from the elevator, and all night I could hear them going up and down (especially frequent starting at 4:00 am). You can also hear the occasional jet taking off, but it's pretty muted.
It is fairly expensive, but it's worth it for the convenience, Perhaps next time I'll really be 8 rooms from the elevators!

title: “rooms not ready”
text: we stayed at the hyatt last summer. it was 94 degrees. we traveled 5 hours. our rooms were not ready at the check in time. we had to wait 1 and 1/2 hours while our rooms were being cleaned.the staff could of cared less. they never even offered us a glass of water. i complained to hyatt and aaa but nothing was ever done.

title: “Best Little Hotel in the Best Location in NYC”
text:
Coming to The Casablanca from the Bellagio in Vegas was quite a culture shock - after the expansive room in Vegas it was a shock to the system to be in such a small room, even though we knew to expect it. It may have a small room but it had everything we needed and frankly we werent in NYC to lay around in our room.
The best things about Casablanca in our opinion:
1. Location, Location Location - you are in Times Square!
2. Fantastic service from every member of the staff - they genuinely were there to help and wanted to make your stay positive! Best 'genuine' service we got in USA, by far!
3. Ricks Cafe - Breakfast was fabulous, fresh and plentiful. Wine and cheese every night - again fresh & plentiful. Internet access - FREE and easily accessable. A great place to mix and mingle with the other guests
We would stay here again in a heartbeat and would recommend it to all - especially couples! Also check out Tony's restaurant next door - some advise, share a meal! Huge portions :-) 
Other advice would be to take ear plugs. The airconditioning units in the room are old and loud - but they do work. Also we had a queen bed - I am sure it was a very small queen, if you can afford it go for the bigger bed
We had a brilliant stay at Casblanca - thanks to all!

title: “"Away in a Manger"”
text:
We called approx. 30 B&Bs & hotels to find no rooms on Sat. 9/3. The Red Socks were back! We were wishing to stay one night after leaving Cape Cod to meet nephew for dinner in Boston, then travelling to airport in Providence for early flight. Not used to the late night Sat. freeway traffic in Boston, we escaped the freeway and paid a visit to 3 hotels. Thank goodness for the network between hotels .... one hotel (forgot which) called the Marriott South Boston and booked us into a room that just became avail. Thank you to Chester, Courtyard Front Office who made our plight worthwhile.You are the best! And so was the room. I slept in the bed which was the most comfortable I have ever slept in, and cousin Sue in the hideabed who raved about it as well. Thank you sooo much! 
Mary Beth King
Owner/Innkeeper,
The Green Cape Cod Bed & Breakfast,
Tacoma, WA

title: “Great Location - Nice Stay”
text:
Great location. The property is at the entrance of the Gaslamp district. There are a few bars/lounges nearby but the hotel is a few blocks from most bars/lounges which I actually preferred (less noise & foot traffic). There are several great restaurants a few feet from the hotel but beware; many close at midnight. I recommend the Strip Club (1 block over). Crazy name but it's a good steakhouse, nice atmosphere & the experience of grilling your own steak was fun.
I stayed in a king room in the Lofts portion of the hotel. Nice room albeit small. For those light sleepers in the Loft I suggest staying in a room that has a window facing the terrace (rather than K Street). My room faced the street and there was some noise from a terrace party at the Hard Rock across the street. The noise wasn't overbearing but might cause difficulty for some. There's a nice trail in front of the hotel for a nice morning jog. 
Pleasant staff. Concierge was helpful. Parking is expensive ($35/night) but given the area it might be standard. I received breakfast vouchers & it was a pleasant surprise. Also, it's a full breakfast; not just continental.
If you plan on being in the Gaslamp district I recommend considering this hotel.

title: “Wonderful Service!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel on business. I would recommend this hotel for business or pleasure.
First.....they start the evening with samples of wine. (All Complimentary)...
Second.....Valet park your car with *Free*parking (I stayed at the Opal on Van Ness and paid $25.00 per night parking and had to struggle to get help opening the gate)
Third.....Very clean, very nice...and helpful staff. I really couldn't get over how customer focused they were.

title: “it's ok”
text:
The room are small. compare to Texas hotel,but normal for New York. The hotel staff are super nice and friendly! the location is good. You're only a block away from grand central station. the hotel was really close to the subway. There is a deil called Charlie that open 24hrs and have some good late night food. PROBLEM: the sink is really small! when you turn on the water, the water will splash to the floor. You will you hit your head on the mirrow when you split into the sink( that how small they are). My friends had a room on the 7th floor and their sink was a bowl shape which was a little bigger but still tiny. the water pressure to take a shower was low. There were no counter space which made it hard to get ready for a girl.
I might stay here again if I came to new york by myself.

title: “Convenient location”
text:
Stayed here in April for a conference. The staff was lovely and attentive. The rooms are well appointed and the beds comfortable.
It was a nice convenience to have a starbucks in the lobby.

title: “Great Location - Nice Rooms - Expensive Parking”
text:
Spent 3 nights here while visiting NYC to show our teenage daughter the city and take her to a Broadway show. Upon check-in we were upgraded (for free) to Executive level which allowed us access to the Executive lounge for free continental breakfast and evening snacks. 
The Continental Breakfast was well done with bagels, fresh muffins, pastries, oatmeal, cereals, and fresh fruits. Several varieties of juice, and coffees. It was presented in a very classy and upscale manner. 
Evening snacks were substantial items like chicken wings, steak skewers, duck dumplings, bagel chips, etc. Free sodas, juice, water. And the bar opens for purchase.
Our room was on the 44th floor with a great view of area. We were able to walk to Central Park, 5th Ave, Broadway, Times Square.... this is a great location.
My only dislike was the parking rate is $50 a day.

title: “Dont do it...you can find 4 star hotels at comparable prices”
text:
Was looking forward to my stay here because I had taken advantage of Best westerns price match guarantee on a great rate i found on a competitor website. 
Prior to arrival I asked if the room type could be switched to 2 double beds and I was told that there was an extra $20/night charge for having an extra person. I told the staff member i had originally booked for 1 adult and I thought the rate was for double occupancy, but was told that was not the case. After checking online I found that the rate for 1 or 2 adults is exactly the same, lies from front desk staff to get the room rate increased to a rate closer to their normal rates, so much for my great find on a competitor website. Rate only increases if there are more than 2 guests to the room.
Second issue,upon arrival, there was a very long hair in the tub, i took pictures as evidence. I turned on the shower so that the hair would go down the drain, but all that happened was i saw how slowly water drained! I called front desk about the issue, but nothing was ever done! 
Third issue, prior to booking I was told that a free hot breakfast was provided for free. I specifically asked what items to expect since you usually get what you pay for. I was told eggs,potatoes,pancakes etc. Upon arrival eggs, oatmeal and biscuits were found in the hot food area, disappointing after having called to receive specifics.
Fourth issue, was placed on second floor, and the high speed internet was more like SLOW speed internet. 
Filled out a survey and followed up with corporate and all I received was an email from the hotel manager with an apology. Figured at the very least they could refund the fee they added to the nightly rate, but not the case.
Not very close to gaslamp, look into the W, Solamar, Se, or Omni. Ive found all those at under a $100 per night.

title: “More blankets please”
text:
Loved the location, the views and the general value for money. My daughter and I had booked a two bed room and found that there was only a sheet on each bed. Looked in the closet and found only one blanket (this is February). We requested another blanket but we would have liked a warmer quilt and to have had the option of turning off the heating at night.
Housekeeping also come tapping on the door from 8am every day wanting to know what time you are going out. They are not actually coming in then to service the room, just planning their schedule which is annoying when you've arrived late and are on holiday.
Don't let this put you off. It's a great place to stay.

title: “Decent but not great”
text:
This was a family trip with a 5 year old so that is the perspective from which my review is based.
Overall, I would say this hotel is just average, not sure why it has such a high rating on here.
Here are my pros:
- Unique hotel with vibrant colors throughout, definitely not your usual downtown business oriented hotel. Felt more like a beach front property than a downtown hotel. 
- Free Wireless Internet
- Very friendly staff. 
- Very clean. 
- Close to the subway. 
- Close to a couple supermarkets and the friendliest Dunkin Donuts I have ever been to.
- Fitness centre
Here are my cons:
- Rooms can be absolutely tiny. We were initially given a room with only one queen (very problamatic for the three of us). This room was the size of a shoe box, ridiculously tiny. Not sure how we would have survived if we had to stay in this room for all three nights (luckily we were able to get a bigger room with two beds after the first night). 
- tiny bathrooms with no tubs, only stand up showers (even in the bigger room we got - in fact the bigger room had a smaller washroom)
- Parking is absolutely insane (but I think this is more a commentary on Chicago in general). $37/night valet parking, I think I saw another self park place about a block away (near Rush and Division) for about $30 - still very expensive
- location I am putting under cons because I felt this was only convenient if you are interested in the night life area of town, for us as a family this was obviously not the case. Basically this is at the north end of downtown, so everything is either a relatively long walk, subway ride, or cab ride south.
- very overpriced if you try to book with them directly and even through Priceline I thought I paid too much for what I was getting
- no pool
Overall, I wouldn't really want to stay at this hotel again mainly due to the location and the fact that we might get stuck in a tiny room again (seriously the single-bed rooms are dorm-like tiny)

title: “Great Value for the Location”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Travel Inn from May 8-11. It is located in a rather quiet neighborhood (for New York!), about a 15 minute walk from Times Square. My wife and I felt very safe in the neighborhood, though there are many transients in the area (the bus depot is nearby, as well as a "home" for transients). The rooms are sparse, but pleasantly decorated. The bed was rather hard, but after walking all day, sleep was not a problem. We found the hotel staff to be very pleasant and helpful.
The hotel rates are a bargain for the location; and since we drove down from Boston, the free parking was a HUGE advantage.
I would definitely stay there again, and recommend the hotel to budget conscious travellers who want to be close to all of the action.

title: “Quality you can rely on”
text: Once again we stayed here as we have twice before. The location is the best. And everything looked brand new. This is the result of their continued renovations and upgrades.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: This hotel is located near Center City close to shops, restaurants, bars, attractions and public transportation. The staff was very helpful and friendly. If you are driving, please look for a parking garage one or two blocks from the hotel and park there. The hotel has parking, however, the prices are very high. The room was very nice and super clean. Love the bed!!! I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text: I recently stayed at this property and LOVED IT! In the future, I will definitely return. Rooms are small but clean. The AC WORKED!!!! That was important during this recent heat wave. It was very convenient having a kitchenette to save some money on breakfast, snacks, water bottles, etc. The room was very quiet. The location is GREAT. Very near the Port Authority train station. Duane Reade and Starbucks are on the corner. Walking distance to theaters, Times Square, many restaurants. Never hard to catch a cab, if needed. The front desk girls were awesome and very helpful. Comfy bed. Snack bar with lots to choose from. Try it, you'll like it!

title: “beyond dissappointing”
text: my wife and daughter stayed at this hotel because it was recommended by a national volleyball tournament. its the worst hotel they've stay in while traveling in four years. rooms are dirty. my wife had to have the sheets changed when she arrived because they were dirty. we had reserved a small refrigerator for the room for my wife's medicine but were informed they didn't have any more although we had one reserved. i don't know which person with the volleball tournament would recommend such a pitiful hotel and location. DO NOT RECOMMEND

title: “Old, small and lots of stairs”
text: Teeny tiny room with a bed right inside the door. Kept hitting my head in the tv located right next to what appeared to be dressing table.

title: “watch out the air conditioning”
text:
very noisy air conditioning,
could not sleep all night long!!

title: “I didn't actually stay here but was displeased with phone service”
text:
Last month I was calling quite a few Seattle hotels to inquire about a suite for a romantic in town get away with my partner. I specifically was looking for a room with either a sunken bath tub or a jacuzzi bath. Most of the hotel personnel that I spoke with were polite and accomadating. The only really negative response I got was from the Hilton.
When I called I stated my question and then the man I was speaking to listened and asked me to hold. I held for several minutes and then when he came back to the phone he seemed to forget what I wanted to know. I reiterated my request and he kinda laughed at me and said 'Oh yeah, you're the one that wants to know about the bathroom, it has a john, a tub, a sink. Do you neeed to know anything else?' I just couldn't believe this man thought it was professional to call a toilet a 'john' to a customer. How crass. I was not impressed and chose not to stay there as a result.

title: “Great for business traveler”
text:
I have always thought Marriott hotels lacked personality and creativity - found that to be true here in Charlotte also but in fairness, I've only stayed at downtown Marriott hotels that are primarily for the business traveler.
That said, they do the business accomodations well. Having just checked out from this hotel, I can say that it was very clean, well appointed and the service was excellent. 
The beds are excellent and not a spec of dirt in site in the whole room. Gym, indoor pool and laundry facilities also appeared above par. Staff were very nice in every setting. Only complaint I had about the rooms were the lack of an in-room safe and mini fridge. There was a cabinet for the fridge but not one in it (maybe just my room?).... Only other criticism is you can hear traffic pretty well from the street but again, this is part of what you get in a urban downtown setting - fortunately it settled down by mid evening. Finally, having to pay for WiFi irks me since many hotels offer this now as a perk - I didnt mind too much though since work was paying for it. :)
I would recommend this hotel for business travelers in particular. Also note that in the ajoining Hearst Tower (sp?) there is a variety of quick service food establishments so you're not just tied to what the hotel has to offer.

title: “Poor”
text:
I can't believe so many people list the room being clean as a bonus - isn't this a pre requisite for ANY Hotel?
On checking in we were greeted by rude staff who just seemed to want to get rid of us as soon as possible, the rooms were more basic than some of the smaller chains we stayed in, and the outside door to the car park wouldn't shut - not exactly secure.
still, the location for Fisherman's wharf is great, but unlike other city hotels, no information was offered on how to see the sights - strange in such a touristy area.

title: “thomases from omaha”
text: We took our adult children for a family vacation to Washington, DC. The hotel and staff were fantastic, which made our vacation wonderful, because of the location of the hotel, coming back from our daily activities was like coming home, everything at our finger tips. We will miss all of you at the front desk, especially Cedric Barksdale. You were friendly and helpful in every way. Thank you.:)

title: “Very nice hotel”
text:
We stayed at the hotel in August, 2008 - family of four - 2 adults and 2 teenage boys. We had a one bedroom suite and as others have written, it is small if you plan to spend much time in the room. The bed takes up the entire bedroom and if you unfold the sofa, it takes most of the living room. Fortunately we were out and about most of the time and appreciated being able to walk to everything - Hancock Tower, Michigan Ave shops, Art Museum, many restaurants (Hard Rock, Harry Carays, Weber Grill)
Pluses: Nice selection for breakfast, though much too crowded on the weekend days; great location; very clean; complimentary internet terminals (two); friendly staff; and the kitchen was very convenient.
Negatives: We had to ask for towels every day, as they only gave us 3 and we were 4 people. Sometimes we had to call twice. Had to wait for elevators frequently. Incredibly heavy door to the room, though it was quiet, so perhaps it blocks noise? Odd arrangement to have to enter in one lobby and then take another elevator to the main lobby, especially when you are carrying luggage.
All in, we would stay here again.

title: “it was impossible to have information and to reserve!!!”
text:
We´ve decided to write to Chalesmark Hotel to plan a travel with others friends in the next May 2009 after to have read the good references left by others travellers.
We sent to them 2 emails and they´ve not answered to us.
We call for them (from Brazil!) to know if the email address was incorrect and anyway if they have rooms.
Who attended to the phone was really ugly saying to me that they are a small hotel and they have only "few" rooms avaliable for the next May (now we´re in July 2008!!!).
I think just that they don´t want to reserve to us and this was really unpleasent.
Anyway they could answer to our email.
In my opinion REALLY overestimated!

title: “Great hotel in a great location!”
text: I found this hotel to be very nice and in a fantastic location! This was my first time in NYC, and I was delighted to discover that the hotel was so close to anywhere I wanted to go: Radio City Music Hall, 5th Avenue shopping, Diamond District, Times Square, Broadway! The room was tastefully decorated and clean. The staff was friendly and helpful. I am a bit of a picky guest, but I have no complaints whatsoever about this hotel. I would definitely recommend!

title: “Very Pleased”
text: Stayed at the Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan SoHo Village when taking my parents and sister to NYC for the first time. My husband and I have stayed in many different hotels in NYC and prepared my family for the tiny rooms in New York hotels, but we were pleasantly surprised by the size of the rooms here. The rooms are not enormous, but they were on the larger side when compared to other places we have stayed in the city. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The rooms were clean. I was pleased with the location, it's in a fairly quiet neighborhood, with the subway only a block away. If it is your first visit to NYC and are not traveling with someone who is familiar with the subway system, this may not be the hotel for you. It is not in the center of tourist attractions. However, it's great if you do not want to stay in a place like Times Square. I would absolutely recommend this hotel to others.

title: “Great hotel at a perfect location!”
text:
The Renaissance Hotel is located right by Time Square at walking distance of lot's of main City attractions. That is the most perfect location!
The hotel lounge is very beautiful with an amazing view on Time Square.
Our room was clean and had a very comfortable bed (bedsheets refreshed every day). Our bathroom had a double size shower.
Even though the hotel is located at one of the most busy places of NYC, there was no noise to be heard from inside the hotel. 
Finally, all personel is very kind and always eager to help.

title: “Great Dining Near LAX”
text: You get done meeting with clients and finally get back to the hotel and all you want is a nice dinner. I was worried when the Shula's was replaced by Paparazzi but let not your heart be troubled. I had a great dining experience at the bar in Paparazzi. They had the entire dinner menu available...which was very good quality, and the bartenders (Horacio and Kerri) made the evening very enjoyable. I don't mind eating solo nearly as much with a great bar and good menu. Thanks to Horacio and Kerri for back-to-back great dining experiences.

title: “Good value for the price”
text:
Stayed 6 days at the hotel. Appreciate that it is close of the metro station (3 blocs) as we did not had a car, but always travel with public transportation (easy and clean). Area is a bit scary but we always make sure to be back at the hotel before the sunset. Breakfast basic but good (always the same every morning, no variety).
Staff very helpfull. WI-FI was variable in the room but fast in the lobby. Computer in the lobby did not work during our stay, asked a few times why, but seems that the technicien did not come to repair.
Rooms: we were on the 3rd floor: clean, no bugs (checked completely), small and basic. Would need some refurbishind (carpet, linen and paint). 
Overall satisfied of the hotel and our first stay in LA. Would recommend as it is a good value for the price and close to downtown.

title: “Cool Design but Lukewarm Functionality”
text:
The design elements of this property are awesome especially the lobby and elevators.
However...
I need a full sized ironing board. I need a bar of soap and a small bottle of shampoo, not gigantic bottles that are refilled and touched by everyone who stays in the room and are an obvious cost cutting move. 
The mirrors in the bathroom are cool but I need a shower with good water pressure and adequate drainage. 
The concierge was very helpful and friendly but the front desk should be able to provide a very small but important amenity and not suggest I go to CVS down the street. 
The pool was small but had a cool design. I would have liked it more if the best sun facing chairs wouldn't have been "reserved" and sitting empty the whole time I was up there. 
I also would have liked a more conscientious valet service. Please don't make me take out all of my bags and bring them to the side and then wait for you to come over. Also, if I say I'm just running up to the room and will be right back please don't put my car away and make me wait for for it. 
All in all this hotel has a cool vibe but needs some major sprucing up on service.

title: “Above Expectation”
text: I had lovely stay at the Serrano SF back in December last year. Stayed there with a friend of mine in a room with two beds. Very friendly hotel staff. The bed was comfortable enough. In terms of location, the hotel is just few blocks away from Downtown SF with all the shopping and dining options. Comp. internet access for Kimpton In Touch members which is free to sign up. Wine reception at the lobby nightly as well. I will definitely recommend this hotel to my friends.

title: “Not at that price”
text:
We stayed at the W New Yourk for 6 nights.
The room bill came in at 2400 USD.
Room is very small - not unlike other NY hotels. Decor is very glam. Bliss spa is located on the 4th floor. This place is supposed to be the best in the state - very over rated and over priced.
You get the bliss spa products in your room. Thats a BONUS.
Hotel was usually helpful. However we came unstuck when our Debit cards would not work as the banks close off Sunday night Australian time NY Sunday noonish. Hotel would not change Aussie dollars. They told us they change amost any other currency but not Australian. Unfortunately the Half price tix place does not accept credit cards. Hence the problem.
Luckily the Waldolf Astoria next door did change our money.
At 400 a night NO WAY
At 150-200 probably.
The hotel has a bar out the front and one in the lobby - after work drinks for the single crowd happens every night. Very hip.
Their GYM is state of the art.

title: “great design small rooms”
text:
liked this property i am a fan of schrager-design-boutique concept so my review must be readed in this context
loved very much the restaurant bar and lobby area one of my favorite places in new york
like friendly and trendy staff must clarify that we are not service intensive
i think that everyone visiting must stay or at least have dinner in this property you can have a great experience for average budget
only complain is room size but must visit at least once so you can complain as everyone does

title: “Standard NYC hotel”
text: A standard room and a standard NYC hotel experience. Located near 4&5 and 2&3 subway lines giving pretty good access to the rest of the city. Great for business in downtown NY as most major offices are nearby. The room is standard by NY standards. Don't expect to make coffee or iron your shirt in your room. Neither are standard nor complimentary. I appreciated a copy of the WSJ every morning complimentary. Altough, most business oriented hotels are doing this. Be very cautious as the walls are PAPER THIN! And I mean to the point that the conversation next door sounds like its in your room. I didn't appreciate the 12:30am wake up to a neighbor vomitting in his bathroom. All in all an okay stay. I would probably not recomend just on the basis of no privacy with the paper thin walls. I'm also not a fan when the manager doesn't respond to the trip advisor complaints. A bit pricey midweek for this type of hotel in downtown NY.

title: “Wonderful experience”
text:
We had a wonderful experience at the Lenox Hotel. I can't say enough about how helpful and friendly the hotel staff was to us from the desk folks to the bellhops to the concierge. There was a slight mix-up in our reservations so they put us in a huge corner room that was magnificent! If any of you watch a Disney show called "the Suite Life of Zack and Cody", my kids felt like we were staying at the Tipton Hotel!
The aging hotel was been re-done admirably and in a classy manner. We ordered room service one night for dessert and the cheesecake and apple cobbler were just great! Also ate breakfast several times at the hotel's Azure Restaurant and, again, a high quality experience.
Rooms were kept very clean and twice daily service for our rooms including a turndown at night with luxurious robes on our beds.
The location was great, near a T stop, and also near the very cool Newbury Street neighborhood. 
All in all, our experience was just great and well worth a return.

title: “It's all about the lobby...”
text:
Stayed for 6 days in November. The first impressions are great. The lobby and public spaces are very hip, furniture and attention to detail is 10/10 but once you're beyond the veneer it's all a little tired and you can see where they spent the money. Bathrooms are sad, ancient water system with a shower over the bath that randomly alternated freezing to scalding. The room ac was almost noisy enough (but not quite) to drown the sounds of showers and flushing toilets in the adjoining room and the floor above but I could hear everything going on in the next door room (and my neighbours seemed to be very 'active'). Not what you would hope for in a quality hotel. 
The staff are really friendly though the breakfast service and food in the restaurant was not great and after the first day I used the Starbucks across the street rather than spend $28 for hour old scrambled eggs... 
On the plus side the beds are very comfortable and if you fancy a late party the bar is brilliant. 
I think I would come back because it's such a fun place but if you want real 5 star you might want to look elsewhere...

title: “Clean, big & a break from Midtown”
text:
After some nights midtown at La Quinta, this hotel was like paradise. Yes it is some distance from subways, Broadway and Times Square but with some exercise, it was relatively convenient to walk to Metropolitan Museum of Art and across Central Park to Museum of Natural History and walk to Roosevelt Island tram. We walked a lot in NY. There were numerous restaurants in the area for breakfast, lunch and dinner with reasonable prices and good food. 
I would definitely recommend it.

title: “I'm so happy I took the leap and stayed.....”
text: I was nervous about staying at the Inn of Chicago because of the reviews, I'm so happy that I went with my gut and stayed.......I am a very picky person and the reviews stated that the rooms weren't clean and etc. Sean was nice and changed our room from a queen bed to 2 double beds. Our room was small but it was roomy enough for us. The bathroom is small and it does need a vent *wheew* but it was clean and efficient enough for our short stay. The location was great. Oh and the lobby is too cute, the staff was so nice and helpful. Our window was facing a bldg but who cares, we weren't there to look out the window anyway! Yea, I can complain about the little things but I wont because what matters the most is that it was small yet clean.

title: “Nice stay”
text: Although I have read from others that your room varies based on the luck of the draw, we were pretty happy with ours and surprised to see the negative reviews from others. The room was small, sure, but immaculately clean, and with a quaint nice bathroom. Although the front desk staff was not initially super friendly, I was amazed and appreciative that they allowed us to check in very, very early. Those are small things that I will remember and enhance my experience of any hotel - especially a large one such as this in such a busy, oft-impersonal city. We also got a very good rate and found the location to be quite good. If we had the opportunity to stay here again, especially with such a good rate, we would certainly do so - and, based on our experience, we certainly recommend it to others without hesitation.

title: “Loved the Gansevoort”
text:
I recently stayed at The Gansevoort on a business trip. I found the location, service and facilities to be excellent. I had read that the rooms were small but I did not find this at all. They were spacish and modern and the beds were among the most comfortable I have slept in! The rooftop bar was a great place to wind down after a day of work and we were never disturbed by noice from the bar. Joel, the General Manager is so personable and nothing was too much trouble for him. 
The breakfast is another highlight....fresh berries and granola were delicious!!
I would defintiely recommend the Gansevoort and look forward to staying there again next year.

title: “Bring a sweater”
text: This hotel recently installed new digital thermostats on the HVAC units. The highest you can set it is 75 degrees. So if the unit thinks the room is warm enough, you had better agree. You have no way to make it warmer. Most ridiculous thing I've ever seen. I can't tell you how ofter I've shivered at this hotel during the winter months. Bring your sweaters, ladies!

title: “Great Stay”
text:
Have stayed twice now for business trips to Austin. Fun, Eclectic hotel. Rooms & bathroom are a great size and laid out really well. Staff courteous and very helpful. Great light affordable breakfast options. Great business mingling in the mornings as everyone grabs a bite and heads out.
Definatly will stay again.

title: “Pretty Good!”
text:
We traveled last week to San Antonio and stayed at the Hilton Hill Country Resort. 
The rooms are nice and the layout of the pool is nice. The pool is a little small but fortunately for us, we were visiting during the week, therfore it wasn't crowded.
The Hotel is situated a hop,skip and a jump away from Sea World and the hotel shuttles you back of forth throughout the day.
They have movie nights on the lawn in the eveings, s'mores at the firepits during the eveings, an inviting lobby to sit around and have a cocktail.
There is an open ballroom with kids games... (puzzles, boardgames if you think you need it) along with a lady that does hair braids and facepaninting for the kids. 
Over all we had a nice time!

title: “Loved our Getaway”
text:
Just returned for a three night stay at the Park Hyatt. My husband and I went away for a weekend sans kids and loved our stay. This was our first trip to Chicago and I did much research on hotels. I chose this one because of TripAdvisor recommendations and I'm a Hyatt Gold Passport member.
Our request for a high floor was honored by the hotel and we had a water view of Lake Michigan. I was disappointed that our room did not have the opening between the bathroom and bedroom that was advertised on the website but it did not spoil our trip. The concierge was extremely helpful and provided some nice dinner suggestions. You must try Cafe Spiaggia. Absolutely the best meal we've ever had. Wonderful!
I would recommend this hotel and it is a great location. Convenient to all the shopping. I would also recommend the Chicago Architecture Boat Tour. It was a great 1 1/2 hour boat ride on the Chicago River that really showed the great architecture of the city.
The only negative I would have was the carpet was in need of cleaning. For the cost of the rooms I felt the carpet could have been newer or at least clean. It showed wear and tear and many spots. Overall the rest of the room was great.

title: “Vvvveeeerrrryyy Nnnnnaaaasssstttyyy”
text: The star inn and suite in houston tx. is the most nasty place i've ever stayed the sheets had blood on them the first time second time a foot print we were there only 30 mins. When ask for our money back the manager curse at us and told us to leave and never come back it was with pleasure........ never go there you will vomit.

title: “unfriendly hotel in good location but dirty business area”
text:
newly refurbished hotel has clean air conditioned rooms near to madison sq gardens and penn station location in business district which is very dirty and hot in june
staff unhelpful refused to store luggage
breakfast room tiny but food quite good and tables outside if no room
internet in tiny foyer which is very busy and not very clean
one of the best things about the hotel is the outside tables in front and behind the hotel where you can sit with a bought drink
concierge never there and you need to ask if you are meeting a group as tiny notice displayed late in front of his tiny booth there are maps available but you need to ask as staff do not bother volunteering any information

title: “Extremely pleased”
text: After reading some of the earlier reviews of this hotel, we were a bit concerned about whether or not we would like it. We recently spent five nights there and were extremely pleased. The staff is very attentive and knowledgeable, the housekeeping is impeccable, the rooms are well appointed and the location is superb. We have stayed at several other Seattle hotels but this will become our hotel of choice in the future.

title: “Excellent Stay”
text:
My family stayed here for two nights in May using Hilton points. Our room was upgraded to a stadium-view room without asking. We had access to the Executive Floor lounge that served a complimentary continental breakfast and evening snacks and drinks. High speed internet access was free for Hilton gold members and above. Everyone on staff that we had contact with went out of their way to be helpful and friendly - truly - better than average!
Our room was clean and the view inside Orioles stadium - a stone's throw away - and the Baltimore skyline was amazing! Room furnishings were pretty standard for a Hilton. Mattress was comfortable. 
We had lunch and dinner at the hotel restaurant and it was very good. Parking is expensive - be prepared, and you really have no other option. This is not the closest hotel to the Inner Harbor and all its attractions, although you can walk there from the hotel, but it is right next door to the stadium and convention center. It is also a few blocks to the medical center and teaching facilities there. 
I was impressed!

title: “Very nice place”
text: We had a very nice stay and was welcomed by all the staff. We did not like our first room becasue of the location and the pronblem was quickly fixed.
