The front desk staff was very helpful in helping us plan two days trips. The room was very clean and the property was very well maintained. The pools were clean and always was well stocked with towels.

title: “nice location if you have business in the local area”
text: Even with the traffic and tourists circling the Ground Zero construction site, this is a good location if you have business meetings on the west side of Wall St or anywhere around the World Trade financial area. Many of the floors have been recently renovated, so the hotel is clean and nice overall. Note that there really is not a lot around the hotel - at least not as much as you would find farther north upwards into midtown. That said, the hotel is connected via a subway entrance only a half block away. Definitely a great place to stay in this part of town.

title: “Huge rooms!”
text:
This was my 2nd trip to the Plaza, and I have to say, the rooms
are quite large for non-suites. The bathrooms are very spacious and
luxurious, and the beds are absolutely amazing. It's hard to start the day
in NYC when you can't get out of bed due to it's comfort level. Hotel is
quite large, and can get busy in the lobby from passing tourists that like
to come in and take pictures. It's in a great location, shopping, Central Park, 
the Subway are all very close. The iPad in the room is a nice feature, that 
controls the room lighting and air conditioning. I would stay here again, if not
for the luxury of it all, but the spacious rooms, you never feel cramped.

title: “Expectations far exceeded! Loved it!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 5 days (joining my wife who had already been there for 3 days). The hotel is very conveniently located for travelers, about half a mile from the airport. It includes free transportation from/to the airport to/from the hotel. Be prepared to pay for parking - about $10 per day. The valet parking is definitely not worth it - unless you like to be pampered. I didn't even check the price.
The location of the hotel was surprisingly good. The airport's proximity had to be seen to be believed - the planes could not be heard at all. 
The check-in process was smooth. We had arrived by a late night flight that turned into a very early morning flight - around 2 AM. The staff were courteous, helped get the luggage to our room and we settled in.
The room itself was spacious. It was *not* the suite and yet we could place a rollaway bed in the room and have space left for walking around. The rollaway beds were nice too - not the folfing variety, but a stand-on-end variety that meant that the mattress was no too soft or springy. 
The bed itself (important for people with delicate backs) was not the best. I have slept on better beds. The bed (King size) was too springy. I would (almost) gladly have slept on the floor. The rooms were surprisingly well sound proofed.
My wife liked the 2nd floor exercise space - I myself worked out in the room itself (5BX requires surprisingly less space - look it up on Wikipedia), and my kids liked the swimming pool which they used once and even then it was too cold.
On the whole, we had a great time and liked the hotel as a place to access the best things in LA.

title: “a haven in a mad city”
text:
First time I have ever bothered to comment on a hotel but this hotel realy is the nicest my wife and I have ever stayed at. 
Lovely room and bathroom totally quiet which is hard to beleive as room is a stones throw from Times Square , The staff could not be more helpfull from manager to cleaning staff, we were recomended the hotel by friends and they were so right it is realy the best.

title: “Ok, but some problems that makes me scared”
text: JUst recently April 20 , 2008 we checked in Holiday Inn, right in the heart of the chinatown, NYC downtown/Soho .Our bedroom was really impressive, but unfortunately the rumbles of the subway underneath makes me awake all night long. The subway runs 24 hours and it really bothers me. It's like there's always an airplane attack on that area and sometimes the building vibrates. Scary and very tiring for the next day.

title: “Two memorable nights”
text: From check in to check out...the experience was sweet and special. Coffee was not delivered "hot" from room service, and that was my only complaint. The Library was a cozy spot to meet guests, and have a drink. The decor was inspiring, and the room was well designed, and comfortable...loved the view of Broadway and 28th Street. Was convenient to walk uptown, or down to Madison Square Park.

title: “Beautiful hotel & great location”
text:
We loved this hotel, the location and decor are great. We got a great big room on the 6th floor over looking the square which was perfect. It was spotlessly clean and well maintained.
Loved having the dog in the lobby, made it feel so homely. Would definitly try to stay on furture visits to Boston.

title: “Sadly Lacking Satisfaction”
text:
This the letter I forwarded to SLS, They ask you to make up own words to SLS.
 Thank you for your reply to my letter, I sent it a few days after we stayed with you and had wondered why no reply, yesterday I discovered my other email program had not sent so I apologize for my tardiness in contacting you. My concerns fall into three categorys. I travel a lot and stay in a variety of settings, including small motels, bread and breakfasts, larger motels and 4/5 star hotels. This holiday was shared with my sister who does not travel so often and was a special time for us to share, she did ask me how much I had paid for giving her the experience of SLS but I did not tell her, I was too embarrassed. You did however provide my primary reason for choosing your hotel, proximaty to The Getty Museum and safety.
1. Decor : I know you are proud of your designer and some features are striking. However I do not want to spend my time in someones fantasy of modern art. Our room with its many mirrors with no real benefit but one and the there was no ceiling mirror to enhance that one use. The mirror between bed and bath served no purpose As you could not even clean teeth from room side. The beds while comfortable are surrounded by edges that could do someone real damage if they slipped. I want to do my retail therapy in a shop not in my room, every where you looked things where being sold from the fridge to the bathroom. My sister and I where afraid to touch anything. There was no coffee making facility in the room, we where told on departure it is in the foyer, but who wants to get dressed to get a cup of coffee. The bathroom required a degree in mechanical engineering to turn on the shower, my sister after 5 minutes woke me to work it out and 5 minutes later we had success. There was no where to place cloths or towels for easy access after shower. Towels where placed to far from shower. I did notice a few hanging hooks but at 5' 2" a little out of my reach. The hand basin is large and to shallow resulting in water going every where when taps turned on. As retired nurse I have a pet pev about Wet surrounds around sinks and allowing germs to breed. While I am in your establishment it should be a place of succor.
In the dining room the chairs at the bar where we where sat, while lovely to look at where most uncomfortable. When we asked if there was no where else we could sit we where taken to the smokers area and seated in the only comfortable chairs we encountered. After dinner we where escorted to the sweets are where the tale of the torturous chairs continued. A comfortable 2 person lounge blocked by a heavy table requiring movement to gain access, on the other side 2 mismatched chairs of questionable comfort.
2. Dining Room: We where told about your signature restaurant being Tapas themed which I thought unusual but as my sister and I are small eaters sounded good. So I rang for a table, no room at the inn for paying guests and why we found ourselves perched on the afore mentioned bar stools. We choose 3 dishes to begin, the first a salad arrived quickly. However an hour later we where still awaiting the other 2 dishes. I finally asked our waitress what was going on after what seemed a heated discussion with another waiter our meal appeared not long after. at which time we received one plate with a very tasty base and a few pieces of rare cooked lamb, and another with 3 squares of chicken and 2 dates cut in half with a mustard filling. Both tasted delicious, however as a cook I know it did not take an hour to prepare, This was early in evening and in fact dining room was nearly empty. I did complain at the time and when we had dessert we where not charged for dessert. As I said your staff are excellent and have received good training . I recently had a Tapas lunch in Palo Alto a much happier experience more interesting dessert menu, featuring delicious desserts I had never seen before.
3. Add Ons: As previously stated I stay in many levels of accommodation it never ceases to amaze me that I have to pay for internet access and parking when I pay the most. 
When I am travelling I want comfort and easy access to a meal that I can enjoy, I thank you for your kind offer, but it is unlikely I will be Los Angeles again. I am a retired Director of Nursing and used to visit patients and relatives to make sure we where doing things correctly. What I took to be a satisfactory performance was if they said like being at home, or like staying in a 5 star hotel so you see I have a high expectation of comfort and caring. I know things have changed but I do remember when I would be greeted with a small bottle of wine or champagne and a chocolate on my bed when staying in a better hotels. Sadly those days have passed.

title: “The Belair:Off beat, Friendly, Cozy, & Safe.”
text: I actually have fond memories of the Belair Hotel. It was the 1st place I stayed at when I moved to Chgo 10 years ago. I didn't know a soul, I was low in funds, and my apt wasn't ready to move into. I was new to Chgo at the time, so I was a little frightened by the fast paced people. The residents though, turned out to be very nice people--a little avant gard and off the wall, but totally harmless. The ladies that worked behind the counter were very friendly, and treated me like they were my aunts.The hotel sort of had the feel of a dorm-like setting at an art school in New York's Village. Now that I'm considering moving back to Chgo, I think The Belair will once again be where I'll start out. It is within walking distance of pubs, restaurants, Walgreens, Lenscrafters, several bus stops, parks, a small supermarket, and STARBUCKS!!! As you walk down Diversey and turn onto Belmont, there are little shops and stores all along both sides of the street. There's just tons to do.Video stores and food delivery places make The Belair a cozy stay. There's nothing fancy here, but you will be safe and among people who will try to help you. I am starting over (again), and should I pick Chgo to come back to, I hope The Belair will welcome me back. Familiar hospitality is good ground to stand on.

title: “Simply Delightful. Enough Said.”
text:
From top to bottom, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The staff was attentive, efficient and friendly. Our room was absolutely lovely ... better than expected. We only had a short stay, and would have loved to have extended it, but unfortunately we did not pack accordingly.
The room had a comfortable sitting area with a desk facing Oak Street Beach, a flat screen TV, and a convenient wet bar, microwave and mini refrigerator (all nicely concealed in beautiful cabinets.)
The bathroom was quite spacious and tastefully decorated. It was accessible from both the sitting area and the master bedroom. Between the master bedroom and bathroom was a nice vanity area.
The master bedroom was also tastefully decorated with a very comfortable bed and a view of the lake. The bedding was top notch and what you would expect of nicer hotels. The hotel was very quiet, so you could really get a good nights sleep.
We took advantage of the complimentary breakfest and was pleasantly surprised at the wide offerings, the helpful staff, and the views of city life bustling outside the window. They also had an outdoor cafe.
All in all, if you're popping into the city for a short stay or long, I think you'll enjoy the staff, accommodations and locations of this gem. A great value for the money.

title: “good value”
text: Clean, modern rooms. Good choice at breakfast. Friendly helpful staff. The hotel is located a few minutes walk from Hollywood Boulevard and the Chinese theatre. It's also an easy drive to Universal Studios. The receptionist very kindly gave us money off vouchers. The car park can be tight. Would stay there again.

title: “Aging but still the Queen of Park Lane”
text: Had a wonderful stay mid-February for four days. We used to stay here often 10 years ago but had not done so in the last five years. Spacious rooms overlooking the Central Park, excellent service all around and very central location for all our interests reminded us what we have missed lately. Yes, the rooms and technologies may not at par with more modern hotels but at least for us, the above mentioned qualities definitely outweigh these minor concerns!

title: “Restaurant is comically bad.”
text:
The rooms at this hotel are clean but rather dark, especially the sitting rooms in the suites. Service is a little lacking - the phone in my room didn't work and wasn't fixed when I requested it. The balconies are nice. The gym is a poor effort. Proximity to Johns Hopkins Homewood is unbeatable.
The staff is a mixed bag. I have had nice conversations with a manager-type guy and with the maintenance staff. When I asked someone at the front desk for a suggestion of a good restaurant to take a business client downtown, she suggested Hooters...
I have stayed at this hotel several times, and it seems to me that each time I am there, the restaurant is under new management with a new name but the same clueless staff. I had a lunch there that was disgusting. Huge hunks of bread and undercooked chicken. The following morning I had a breakfast meeting that was absurdly bad. The buffet eggs were green and they only make one omelet at a time. Plus, the waiter brought us our bill before anyone had consumed so much as a sip of coffee. I've never seen that done before.

title: “Don't Judge A Book By Its Cover"”
text: The small maroon awning and enterance in the beteween perfume and trinket stores hides a great little hotel with clean rooms, nice service, great views of Empire state building from rooms 2 blocks from Park Avenue and one minute walk to subway. Definitely a bargain for Manhatten and never felt unsafe walking around block. Pizza place downstairs!

title: “Affordable with the Best Location”
text: Situated right at the heart of the Historical District, this hotel with its affordable pricing really stands out for budget travelers. This hotel had experience many faces in years

title: “Fantastic Staff”
text: I recently spent a night at the Dunhill Hotel for my 1st anniversary. From the moment we pulled up to the front of the hotel and the valet greeted my wife and I by opening our doors, introducing himself as Jason, and welcoming us to the hotel, my wife and I were amazed at the amazing service we received. We have not been treated with such service anywhere else in Charlotte. It felt as if we were on retreat in Europe. Everyone from the bellmen to the managers made us feel at home by calling us by our names during our entire stay. We have decided that we will not stay in any other hotel in Charlotte. Thank you for what was an outstanding anniversary. We look forward to returning soon.

title: “Fantastic experience...we plan on making it an annual pilgramage”
text: Stayed one night on 1/18 with four other couples. It was restaurant week so getting a reservation anywhere was brutal. We were literally walking out the lobby door to a third-tier restaurant when one of my party told the host at Bistro Bis of our predicament. They offered to put my group (party of 13) in the hotel's conference room, (effectively creating our own private dining room), and then let us order off the special restaurant menu. Service was exemplary, food fantastic, and we all felt like VIP's. Just a phenomenal experience. Maitre'd (George?) was all over us with great service..very attentive and professional, and a sense of humor to boot. We'll definetly be back.

title: “This food geek was stunned!”
text: Dinner at this resort's fine dining restaurant was stunning and I am a food geek not easily stunned. Best possible materials coupled with perfect execution. Patrick and other staff on the night shift dealt with uncharacteristically noisy fellow guests with courtesy and aplomb. For those who aren’t in the know, I found out about this hotel on the website Tablet Hotels who have a rather large assortment of some of the most stylish hotels in the world with great rates too! I’m looking forward to returning.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
This is one of the worst hotels that I have stayed in. We stayed in the Executive Suite and I been in stardard rooms at other hotels that were more aesthetic. Everything in the room (except for the TV) was very old and outdated. The desk lamp had to be replaced because the switch was sparking whenever I tried to turn it on, and eventually it stopped working altogether. I felt like I went back to the 1970's or 80's. I would probably never stay at this hotel again.
The only reason I did not rate this hotel a terrible was because of the staff. They were very good. Laura from the concierge lounge went out of her way to make our stay more pleasant. The valet Glen was also very good. I just wished the room was actually updated to this century.

title: “Good Location, good service, happy hour, Happiness”
text:
This is a late review. We stayed at this hotel just by reading the reviews on trip adviser. All the good things are true. We stayed here last December when it was minus 7 degrees.
Great location. Minutes away from the metro, especially in winter, you don't wanna be outside walking for too long. 
I requested for a humidifier in the room and I was provided with one with no charge. Nice large room, free wifi, little mini bar treat, $1 coupon breakast. Nice winter portion breakfast.
Plus, the happy hour! After a cold walk outside, we returned to a rightly timed happy hour of wine, crackers and tea. What a relief!
Staff is always smiling and helpful. Hotel is also walking distance to some shopping.
Two thumbs up.

title: “Does not guarantee bed type.”
text: My fiancé and I reserved a king bed room for the Brickyard 400 weekend. While the location was great, we were surprised to received a double bed room at check-in. When we asked for the king we reserved, we were told the hotel 'never guarantees bed type' and that the kings were sold outs had we known, we would have stayed at the Westin instead. Also---we went to the pool to have a quick swim and found the water to be really, really cloudy and gross. Pick another hotel, folks!!

title: “The most brilliant little hotel in New York”
text: We stayed at the Crosby St Hotel for 5 nights and did not want to leave. It is not only a beautiful and stylish hotel, but the staff especially the concierge staff, are amazingly helpful and lovely. The little touches like handwritten notes from the manager and the excellent turn down service at the end of the day were great. The restaurant and bar had fabulous food and was obviously a very popular place to be! Will be back again. Thank you for a great start to our US holiday.

title: “Not bad/not super”
text: If you are staying at the streetside of the building....it s sooo noisy I really couldn t sleep at night...it really was too much. They schould invest in soudproof windows....for the rest rather friendly ...lucky they are next door to the 101 coffeeshop ...fresh food,good service,no problem;otherwise getting a descent meal or breakfast seems to be hard to find over there....fast food no problem....but after a few days I've had enough hamburgers for a year....

title: “great service, nice room, ok location"”
text: We had a great room on the 31st floor. Very friendly and helpful staff. The room was very quiet and well furnished. The issue is the neighborhood -- the hotel is located between 8th and 9th Avenues, which is great, although we were looking to be a bit closer to Times Square. The hotel is right across the street from the Port Authority Bus Terminal. This block of 40th Street is ripped up b/c of construction at the bus terminal. In addition, the block is trashy, except for this hotel, which was very nice. Free Internet and Free Breakfast.

title: “Perfect summer spot!”
text: A girls weekend in Boston had me searching for an outdoor pool to relax during the day and The Colonnade definitely was the right choice. While the rooftop pool is small, so get to the pool by 10 a.m. if you want a choice in seating, the atmosphere and hotel service was fabulous. The rest of the hotel isn't shabby either as the rooms are well appointed, the beds super coomfy, and the hotel restaurant is GOOD - and reasonably priced. And the location in the Back Bay....excellent. The staff is very friendly and helped me with an early check-in -- 9:30 a.m. -- and a late checkout. The concierge was most helpful, and even offered an umbrella on a day the skies were threatening. Will DEFINITELY go back!

title: “The Grand Hyatt is GRAND!!!”
text: Our family of 4 enjoyed Christmas 2005 at the Grand Hyatt at Grand Central Station in NYC. The streets were hustling and bustling, and construction was in full swing outside the hotel, but once we entered...pure opulence and peace and quiet. The room was very lovely, and extremely clean. The lobby was absolutely magnificent!!! We were able to walk to many sites from the Grand Hyatt, and would highly recommend it to everyone - book early for the best deals!

title: “Great again”
text:
Second stay at this hotel... re-confirm that this hotel is situated in a great location, one of the best in New York, the staff are out of this world, great value or money... this is a five star hotel !
Only two constuctive points however, the bar restarant area hasn't found its best format yet,it has changed since last year and still isn't perfect. Second, we were lucky enought to be awarded an uograde to a skyview corner room, fantastic views, 31st floor, wonderful, only complaint (if we can) the noise of the street. The side which has a window that opens is situated on the main street, even though the window and curtains were closed I got 87 decibels during the night through traffic.... !!! Not good, but next day we bought ear olugs, problem solved !!! GREAT BED. Well done, we will go back.

title: “New with Views”
text: This highrise is a great city hotel. Nice rooms with big views of the city and mountains. Full wall size windows make all the rooms superb. The hot tub on the pool level needs to be raised about 5 feet to gain the views it could have had. The skyline bar around the 30th floor makes up for the hot tub view. This is a modern and classy property.

title: “Hampton Inn - always a great choice”
text:
We stayed at the Hampton Inn Times Square South last August and enjoyed our stay very much.
The hotel is quite new and rooms are modern and clean. They are a bit smaller than the usual Hampton Inn rooms but this is NYC. Location is great - Times Square and Port Authority are only a few minutes away. The street in which the hotel is located is not noisy. Others mentioned that is looks a bit desolate but we never felt unsafe and next to the Hmapton Inn there is also a Holiday Inn Express and I think a Fairfield Inn. 
Breakfast is good, though the breakfast area is indeed a bit small. However, we never had problems finding a table. 
The only minus is the elevators which are slow and not enough for a hotel this size.

title: “Way overpriced”
text:
We stayed at the Westin during GenCon. The price was one-fifty-nine a night, plus taxes, obviously higher than "non-peak" times. The hotel is attached to the convention center, which helped out a lot, particularly as my wife had trouble walking great distances.
They warned us about the minibar when we checked in, and we made sure not to touch anything in it. The pricing was high at $25 a day. We weren't going anywhere, so I didn't bother with valet parking. Regardless, they charged us valet parking even though we weren't in the valet section. They did remove this from our bill.
They seem to have trouble with their elevators. I saw another review about people stuck in the elevator. This happened to us (a total of 12 of us), too. Unfortunately, our 10 year old was skittish about elevators and all the way up to Indy he asked if we would get stuck. Sure enough, we did. We ended up missing a dinner engagement as we tried to calm him down. What did the hotel do to compensate us, given that we got grease on our clothes from the rescue? They had water available, and they called to see if we were okay. That's it. I'm not sure what I expected, but a laundry service would have been nice at the very least.
For the money, the hotel was absolutely nothing special. The beds were okay, but the padded cover is not elasticized and kept riding up on me at night. The bathroom was an okay size, maybe a little on the small size. 
The big cost ripoff is their wireless internet. It's free if you log in on the first two floors (well, the first floor, anyway) and ten dollars for the privilege of checking your e-mail from your room. Why they nickel and dime you on this is beyond me. I had to traipse down to the lobby every night to check e-mail. The free internet is free for 24 hours. You can renew, but once I tried to renew on the 2nd floor (having connected for free from the second floor) and it wouldn't let me in. I had to go to the first floor, disconnect from that server then reconnect before it let me in again. Totally unnecessary, and just another way of gouging you. 
The lobby looks nice, but behind the nice lobby is an average hotel with high prices.

title: “My best hotel ever”
text:
Wonderful, magic, exquisite hotel!!!
What a stay, what a room. most beuatiful hotel ever, cleanliness of the room, very welcoming staff, breakfast was excellent, dining room a pure marvel of architecture & decoation,...
Hotel lounge and bar beautiful.
Hotel location excellent.
Price vs quality ratio very very good
Will surely come back again.
Thank you gala Hotels!!!

title: “Beautiful hotel in a lovely city”
text: If you prefer to stay in a stylish setting with an attentive staff, the Four Seasons in Austin is for you. They are a welcoming group that will treat you like royalty, accompanied by plush rooms and delicious food and drinks. One of my personal favorite attractions--the amazing floral dispalys in the lobby that brightened my days. Just out the back deck of the hotel you can also enjoy the impeccable grounds that lead out to what is going to be your favorite place to jog (Town Lake Trail). Definitely a place that suits an ecclectic crowd, the Four Seasons is a place that any posh traveler, mother, child, or business person will enjoy while visiting Austin.

title: “Clean, good value - watch out for parking recommendations”
text: Place was clean, very very nice for the price -updated - would stay there again - no bed bugs. We were very comfortable- however beware of PARKING recommendations - this incident reported by another traveler was EXACTLY what happened to us - "...must use the public parking garage one block away. The hotel clerk claimed we would get 25% off of the $40 parking rate in fact we only got $5 off. The parking attendant pretends to not underrstand english whenever we asked about our entire $10 discount." Cheaper garages are closer - do NOT go with hotel parking recommendation - something FISHY going on. A little noisy at times but the rooms were so nice - if it weren't for the parking incident I would hardily recommend.

title: “A Solid Reliable Choice in Times Square”
text: Nothing negative to mention, and a couple pluses. Good size room - can be unusual for NYC. An empty fridge (at least in our 2 room suite) for our use. We were high enough (in floor numbers) that there was almost no street noise (and I would recommend you request this). It was no Ritz but all I want, especially in the city, is clean and comfortable and a bit of room to stretch out, and this fit the bill. Some will love the Times Square location - it's close to so many attractions - and some will not, but it's a fine choice for those who do.

title: “Better Than Expected”
text:
Stayed here for more than a month. Great location and almost incredibly quite for being so close to several very busy roads. Tha rooms are sizable with a recliner and small kitchenette included. They are somewhat Spartan but the A/C works well and the employes are helpful. Seemingly very safe neiborhood which is a big plus in Memphis.
Highly recommended for those planning on an extended stay. I paid 30/night and that was at least 10 dollars less than any other hotel I found in Memphis.

title: “Wonderful”
text: Too bad service like this is so hard to find! Stayed here many times, last time here was in January. Check in was great, got an automatic upgrade from jr. suite to suite. Great room, clean, luxurious and great views. Very quiet. Bar was busy that night, but wait staff was still attentive and friendly. Just an all around pleasure to stay at this hotel. Many think its too expensive, but if you're already paying a few hundred dollars per night, its really worth paying a little more to stay at this hotel. This is what service and cleanliness should be.

title: “Comfortable Opulence”
text: When I first arrived I was put off by the opulence of the Omni's lobby. I was traveling on business and needed to get down to business, not fuss. The Omni will allow you to stay on course while pampering you along the way. Rooms are very well designed and appointed. Beds are comfortable. Bathroom is a nice size and shower is good. Fitness center is very well equipped. Parking is free. Dining at the hotel can get pricey but the food and service won't let you down. I really enjoyed my stay here.

title: “Should have booked here in the first place”
text: After checking into another hotel in San Francisco and then checking out immediately, my husband and I headed straight down to Fisherman's Wharf and looked for another hotel. Since we have never had a bad stay at a Marriott, we were happy to be able to get a room here. Yes, it was more expensive than the hotel we left, but we could actually walk around at night in this neighborhood! All staff were extremely friendly and helpful and the room was clean and comfortable....something we have found at all Marriott's we have booked. It was so nice to be able to walk to so many sites from here and the restaurant recommendations we got we tops.

title: “Good place close to the CLT”
text: Great, inexpensive place to stay next to the Charlotte Airport. The rooms were new and looked like new showers. They have a limited menu at the bar, but it was nice as I got in after 9 pm and every restaurant in the area was closed.

title: “Disappointing, never stay here again.”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights, on arrival we were greeted in a friendly manner and told where our room was, the rooms are detached from the main building, more like a motel, when we got to the suite it smelt musty and horrible and the toilets didn't flush, we reported both, toilets was fixed the next day and we were offered air freshener for the smell, at first glance decor looks ok, but after wandering through the corridors several times you do notice it's out dated appearance and decor faults like coving coming away, dirty walls. Our suite was furthest away from the main building so a bit of a trek through corridors to get breakfast.
Breakfast was good and a lovely lady named Betty was fantastic, very friendly and helpful, really cheered my day up. Not what we expected from a Homewood Suite or the Hilton chain, very disappointing, we are travelling across USA and stayed in Hilton chain hotel and suites and this is the most disappointing by far, would not stay here again.

title: “Great room, great price for ny”
text:
We just got back from NY and we stayed two nights at this location. It was perfect. Close to penn station (10 min. walk) and Time square (10 min. walk). It was clean. 
The room are very big, the only problem was that the sofa bed was not comfortable at all.
It would be time to have their mattress to be change. Don't expect to get a nice room cause it's very old fashion decor. The only problem was we didn't have internet.

title: “Share an opinion with last review on State Plaza”
text: I agree completely with   "February 8, 2005:  A TripAdvisor Member, Durham, NC." Stayed there twice with great experiences. The last time was just awful!

title: “Excellent Experience”
text: Having never visited San Francisco before we booked on priceline. On arriving at the hotel I showed my hilton gold card and immediately got given a room on the executive floor with access to the lounge. Our luggage had been taken from us when we valet parked and reached the room at the same time we did. The room was wonderful, large for a city hotel and with a wonderful view of the city and Alcatraz. Room service food was excellent although a little expensive. We never used the resturants in the hotel but they were always busy. I had a massage at the spa and it was wonderful, one of the best massages I've ever had. All the staff were very friendly and we never experienced any problems. This is one of the most memorable hotels I've stayed at in a long time.

title: “Nice hotel on the Riverwalk”
text:
Stayed 5 nights while in town for business. We had a room on the 17th floor for honor members. The room with a king size bed was as pictured on their website. It was quite large and very clean. While there was nothing special about the hotel (the decor is outdated) or the room, our stay was very comfortable (especially the bed) and service was always prompt and very polite, from check-in, to housekeeping and restaurant staff. 
For the sake of convenience, we ate at all 3 restaurants on the property (Durty Nelly's, Ibiza and the sports bar). The food was good, albeit very expensive, but about the same price you'd pay at any other restaurant on the riverwalk. We also went to the Guadalajara Grill next door. The food was ok and reasonably priced. The Republic of Texas had great food, as did the County Line on the Riverwalk, but be prepared for the crowds. 
The Market Square is worth the trolley ride, as is a visit to the Alamo. If you get bored, the Rivercenter Mall is across the street with plenty of stores and a movie theatre.
All in all, if you are going to be staying on the Riverwalk and you can get a decent rate, the Hilton is a great place to stay. Be warned however, parking is very expensive.

title: “If you have to cancel your reservation be prepared to be RIPPED OFF!!!”
text: The Da Vinci Hotel ABSOLUTELY SUCKS!!! Do Not do business with them! They will RIP YOU OFF! I had to cancel my reservation for two nights because the show that we were going to see up in NYC had been cancelled. We were travelling to NYC just to see this show! Of course Da Vinci said that they were going to charge me a penalty charge of one nights stay because I cancelled within thier 7 day window. I tried to talk to the manager - I sent several emails - I called several times - NO RESPONSE! I was trying to get the charge waived or even credited to a later date.... NO RESPONSE! Da Vinci Hotel IS A COMPLETE RIP OFF! DO NOT TRUST THESE PEOPLE WITH YOUR MONEY!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Beautiful Modern Hotel, Fantastic Views. Service and Location Lacking”
text:
We stayed at the Hilton San Diego bayfront for a long weekend in March, after we drove from LA to go to San Diego Zoo and Seaworld (both well worth a visit).
The hotel itself was beautiful, lovely, spacious, clean, fresh rooms. We were in a middle-level corner room with a fantastic view of the bay and the Air Force base.
The bed was large and very comfortable, with quality bedding.
Whilst the location meant that we had beautiful views, it was a fair walk to the Gaslamp Quarter, where all the nice restaurants and bars are. We drove there in the evenings.
The service was a little bit lacking, little things like the way you were greeted, and the Valet guys counting how much you tipped them in front of you.
we ended up staying for tree nights, pay two get one free, so the hotel cost us around 
All in all, we thoroughly enjoyed the stay, because of the hotel itself, but I'm sure that would be better places to stay whilst in San Diego if you were to stay longer.
All in all a pleasant stay.

title: “Close to Carnival Cruise Line”
text: We love Holiday Inn Express Hotel. They have become our choice it at all possible when we travel up and down the east coast. We chose this one because of its location close to the port. As usual the room was clean, beds were comfy, breakfast was your typical quick but always filling foods. Will keep choosing HIE as our main choice of stays on the road.

title: “Robbed”
text:
Seen roach motels with nicer amenities. Rooms are deplorable, staff at valet is.horendous, rude, and parking is expensive. 
Front desk staff is the worst ive ever encountered. Management is discourteous and rude. Food isn't good quality either. Would rather just sleep in my car next time.
Good luck getting your free wi fi to work

title: “ALLERTON a dump?”
text:
I visited on 5th to 10th December, 2003. Hotel appears to have a fresh exterior, etc. Things are looking up here and in the whole neighborhood. Several new restaurants have opened and store qualities are rising.
Right on the corner of 8th Ave (One-way North-bound to Penn Sta) Bus #20 and short block from the tube station for trains 1 and 9 that runs from way up North to Battery Pk. 7th Ave is So. bound from Penn Sta. 
VERY handy situation but not for the very fussy.

title: “Memorable stay at Landmark Hotel”
text: I treated a friend for a night at the Fairmont for her birthday. There were three of us staying in a double queen room. It is much like several 4 star hotels we have visited, nice linens, good toiletries, great view, and comfortable beds. Note that you will pay $52 for parking. The service was equal to our stay at the Wynn in Las Vegas. Well attended and the staff was very pleasant. The only complaint I have is that we had to wait nearly two hours for our room when arriving at 2pm. Take note that even if the staff tells you there is early check in, you may wait. We sat in the cocktail lounge while waiting and had signature drinks which were very tasty and pricy. After visiting SF many times it is worth at least one visit but is a little overated.

title: “Will definitely be back”
text:
This is a belated review from last year . Stayed for 5 nights in Mar11 and can highly recommend this hotel for either business or pleasure travel. We have stayed in various areas of manhatten and having stayed here we will definitely be making this the area we always stay in .Short Walking distance to soho and greenwich village and so many nice bars and restaurants. Compared to other hotels we have stayed in in NY we thought this was very good value for money.
A large room by manhatten standards and an even larger bathroom , really comfy bed and no outside noise . All the staff we encountered we helpful and professional , we even had screaming teenage girls outside the hotel each time we arrived and left - rumours of famous boy band staying :) 
Will definitely be back

title: “Great Hotel for our trip to the Oscars!”
text: Loved the hotel. A close walk to the Oscars Red Carpet. A great breakfast and very attentive staff.

title: “Boston Marathon Weekend”
text:
I chose the Hyatt Regency in Boston because of it's proximity to the finish line for the Boston Marathon and the price offered by the hotel as a group rate for the Boston Marathon participants. My familiarity with the Boston area was nil. The hotel location turned out to be the center of everything we did for the 3.5 days we were in Boston. It was within a mile of the finish line. The Trade Center where the packet pick up and expo were less than a mile in the opposite direction. We were short walks, a mile or less, to all the areas where we wanted to dine and shop, North End, Beacon Hill, and Newberry Street. My wife and I are runners obviously, so proximity to great running is essential. My wife did not run the Boston, but was able to have great runs everyday along the river or the Commons Park and Commonwealth green way. So from this aspect the hotel was a 5.
The staff was really nice and very accommodating so I would rate them very high as well. Probably the only draw back was the "thinnest" of the walls. You can't necessarily hear conversations, but if someone's tv was on you knew it. Doors slamming, those kind of things. There is even a note on the desk to be considerate of others by keeping the TV volume down and conversations at a normal tone. That said, it wasn't ever a problem for us, we just noticed it.

title: “Great location. Clean. Great Price”
text: A few blocks from the subway. Easy check-in. We had the option of the kiosk or the receptionist gladly checked us in. Clean room. View of the world trade construction. Excellent price for the weekend. I would definitely recommend this place.

title: “Surprisingly nice for an airport layover”
text: We had an overnight layover and selected this site based on other travelers' comments. It's not the Ritz but it is quite pleasant and the service is excellent. The complex is spacious, nice for getting some breathing room after a long flight. The dining room is expensive but the food was of excellent quality and preparation. There is a well-equipped and decent sized workout room and if the weather is cooperative a large, landscaped outdoor pool. The airport shuttle is on demand and only takes a few minutes between points.

title: “My experience with this hotel.”
text: We were told the room was going 199$ than when we checked in we were told it was 229. When we finally got to our room, we got a text message from our bank saying we were overdrawn. We found out that without telling us the hotel charged 319. They never mentioned they charge 20% just in case we get room service. we were not planning on room service. They charged us 90$ more than they said they were going too. 90$ more than my husband signed to pay. I do not understand how they could charge and not tell us the actual amount. It ended up making it so we could not go to the Willis Tower because the money was being held. Very disappointed. Also, the lady checking us out forgot to ask us for the room keys. we didn't realize so we had to walk all the back to the hotel since we could not afford a cab. Location was great. The room didn't even have a fridge. The vending machines were right outside our room so we got woken up a few times by other hotel visitors during the night. For the price, I think it was an awful experience.

title: “A Great Place To Stay”
text: Excellent, clean accommodation and a lovely breakfast. If you want to put your head down after a flight into San Diego then this hotel is first class - including the service of the very friendly staff. Don't worry about the train. All I did was e-mail them in advance asking for a room at the front and they replied within 24 hours confirming this was in place. Excellent value for money. We only wanted a place to put our heads down for 1 night following a long trip from the UK and they delivered beyond our expectations. We had a minor hiccup with the courtesy transfer but the reason for this was well explained by the management. Location is excellent if you want to see the maritime museum, USS Midway and all of downtown, Littly Italy etc.

title: “Hope for good things.”
text: Im due to book into here on the 27th of this month,with my wife ,Its our one year anniversary and my wife is 4 months pregnant, were no strangers to NY as we travel almost twice a year to this city, We've chosen to stay in this hotel to try something new and different and after staying in a lot of hotels around the world and just back from Dubai ,I hope to be writing a favorable review of this hotel on my return to Ireland.

title: “great location”
text: This hotel has a great location. It is couple of blocks away from the walk of fame. Easy to walk to restaurants and shops nearby. Breakfast room was very crowded, no chair for my husband to sit on the second morning. Need more seating/ extra chairs that could be brought into room if needed. One thing worth mentioning is that everytime we walked by the building next door the smell of marijuana was so overwhelming. Front desk staff very friendly and helpful.

title: “Great Christmas stay at the Palace”
text: A beautiful and well kept traditional hotel in a fantastic location with amazing views. We stayed here for 4 nights in the week before Christmas and were very impressed by the service, the clean and large room, and the wonderful Christmas decorations within and outside the hotel. A special thank you to the professional and extremely friendly and cheery Concierge staff who made our stay that much better by providing insightful and helpful recommendations for public transport and restaurants.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location, Great Service”
text:
My husband went on a business trip from Oct 12th through the 15th. I tagged along and was very impressed with this hotel. The service was great. Rooms were above average. Great linens and beds. There is a GREAT conceirge serivce that is not stuffy or pretentious (as I had always assumed they would be). They suggested two great places to eat - Rioja (classified as Mediterranian). It was wonderul. Tip: Take the 16th Street free shuttle to Larimer St. It was a bit of a hike from the hotel. Also, my husband wanted to catch a few games on Saturday and eat pizza. We went to Wazee Supper Club. Good pizza (but if you are a Chicago or a NY pizza fan, you will be disappointed...but Denver isn't known for their pizza, right?).
There is an Enterprise rental car located right in the lobby. We rented a car for the day (we were supposed to get a small car, but all they had were trucks...nice upgrade for no extra cost) and saw Red Rocks and drove around. We didn't want to pay the huge cost to park overnight in the hotel ($25.00 valen, $21.00 self park), so we turned it in. Cabs are available by request (and my one experience with a cab the drive took me the wrong place and overcharged me by $2.00 because he was lost). Walking is sometimes easier. 
If you are looking for a great massage, book it at Spa Universaire (the sister company to their on-site massage) in the Belvedere Tower. Ask for Ken...it is well worth it.
The only bad experience we had was our luggage got lost on the way home...we checked our bags at the hotel. Although, not sure if it was the hotels fault or the airlines. It would be too hard to tell....so all in all I gave this facility an excellent rating.

title: “Nice hotel for business and family vacation”
text:
Our family of four (with 2 young kids) stayed here for 4 nights in August, 2012. It was my business trip (for the first 2 days), but I decided to bring the family alone since we had not visited Chicago for about five years. The hotel was fantastic. I was given a suite which was spacious. The room was adjacent to the "L", and I was concerned about the noise, especially at night. It turned out it was not an issue. Below were my observations:
Pros:
- Nice, clean, and spacious room
- Great bathroom: spacious shower area, separate toilet area, and a huge bathtub
- Good TV with many channels
- Large in-room safe
- Staff was very friendly and helpful
- Check-in and check-out were smooth. I had a little issue during check-in as the system did not have all the correct information for my reservation. The front desk staff was very helpful and made all the corrections. 
- Location was great, close to everything. Only a short walk to Michigan and State Avenues. Bus/L lines to many major tourist attractions were also within short walking distance.
Cons:
- Really not much to say
- Lobby was huge but could use more furniture/have more sitting areas
- Pool area was closed when I was there (that was another story)
Overall, our family enjoyed our stay and the trip. I would definitely stay at JW Marriott Chicago again.

title: “Very good situation”
text:
I chose this hotel for my last night in San Francisco for a small price.
Close to all "last call" shop and to the Bart station.
Room was small but clean and silent (5th floor). Shower and wc outside the room but very close.

title: “It's okay.”
text:
I had to book hotels for our stay in NYC on short notice. Thus, the cheapest but seemingly decent enough place that was still available was the Skyline. It's a very basic, no-frills type of hotel. I think the most extravagant service it had to offer was a bellhop, compared to other "budget" places where guests are made to haul luggage to their rooms by themselves.
As a family of three, we booked a "Double-Double" room. It was apparent just from the hallway that our room was old. The television usually turned off by itself while we watched a show. The toilet was small. Really, really small. The toilet bowl almost touches the tub. In the night, we heard sirens blaring and people shouting from the streets. The full NYC experience, I think. Despite these, our room provided what we needed.
After exploring the hotel (there's really not much to explore), we realized that out room was in the old wing. Double-Double and Twin rooms are in an older part of the hotel. Go past the vending machines on the old wing and you'll notice that the corridor widens, the carpeting gets prettier, and that the lighting gets brighter. Not to mention the faster, non-creaky, and double door elevators. The end result looks like a different hotel altogether. If you're willing to shell out a bit more, get the more spacious Queen-Queen or King rooms to stay in the better part of the Skyline.
The Skyline Hotel's strongest point (and redeeming quality) is undoubtedly its location. If one has the stamina for it, he can even make a trip to Fifth Avenue on foot and watch the environment change drastically. Times Square is a 10 minute walk away. Walk a few blocks and you'll end up right on Restaurant Row - which is exactly that. The Skyline does not have a laundry facility, but you can take your pick from the numerous laundromats within the district. It's deli/convenience store city along 10th Avenue too, so there's no need to worry at all. If you haven't been to NYC yet, the area might seem daunting upon arrival (as it was for my family and I), but once you get oriented with the strategic location of this hotel, you'll relish in its proximity to some NYC attractions.

title: “A+ Customer Service”
text: We stayed at this property the week of 8/16/04. Had wonderful mountain view room on the 9th floor. Absolutely the best service (valet staff, Concierge, Front Desk, Sundry Shop) of any Marriott we have been to in the past. Rooms are a little small, but bathrooms are large with separate glass shower and tub. High quality furnishings and very large flat screen TV. Great Concierge lounge and staff. Hotel located in a great area to walk around and shop, eat, etc...

title: “Average”
text: Good and comfortable location, has its own parking, friendly staff but nothing special. We had an executive suite - the interior was very average, hotel charged us 20 USd for bottle of wine that we didnt drink, more than that the mini bar was ABSOLUTELLY empty. Yet, strangelly enough they give you a key from the empty fridge.... Yet if i have to go to SF again i would stay at some other place close to the city center....

title: “Large room in heart of Financial District”
text:
New York is tight on space. At Gild Hall, a boutique hotel, allows me to forget that space is an issue.
Booked a king bed on the 5th floor and would return on my next visit. Here's why:
+ The room is pretty big. I had a king bed and it fit the bed without my having to skirt around it. Plenty of room to lay out luggage, get dressed, and just move around in general.
+ Bathroom is pretty modern and clean. Great water pressure. Slip into the Frette robe and wash up.
+ Flatscreen TV, desk, window seats, are all part of the room
+ Don't like "gym" then Crunch Fitness is only $10. I didn't use Crunch since I just needed a treadmill. "Gym" is in a small space that fits just that, a treadmill, a stairmaster, handheld weights and a bench. There is a water cooler and an air conditioner. Super basic.
+ Shelves by the doorway to throw your purchases, keys, etc. That came in handy.
+ Great library in the lobby area. Esconce yourself in a leather space and read up.
+ Great bed.
+ Nice reception and doormen.
And the not so +'s:
- It's in Financial District. Not know for nightlife. But it is close to the Fulton St station which may be convenient but its weekend schedule sometimes means you have to go to another further station to make it.
- Walls seem thin. I heard guests traipse down the hallway and sometimes even my neighbor. I can filter a lot out but it was a little annoying.
Overall great accomodations. I'll return because of the discount for staying at a boutique hotel that's not terribly inconvenient.
-

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
We have stayed in a number of hotels in New York over the last ten years, this hotel has been a good one, great location away from all the hustle and bustle of times square but only a short walk away if that's what you want.
Rooms are clean and serviced well every day, our only fault with the room was it was smaller than we have had in the past, there was not much room for cases and clothes storage.
Bed was comfortable although 2 pillows per persson would have been better.
the free tea/coffee in a morning were very welcome as we could have a drink before setting off for the day, then when you return in the afternoon there was hot chocolate to warm you up, after a rest, shower and change it was down for a glass of free wine or 2 before going out for the evening.
you could get a better priced high standard hotel as we have done in the past, but i would stay here again.

title: “You pay for what you get......”
text:
Of course, when visiting NYC you dont expect to stay in your hotel room for any length of time; however when you are in your room you want it to be clean and comfortable. First of all, you couldnt ask for a better location..subway right outside the door, Central Park a few blocks away and Times Square within yelling distance. The actual Hotel was a different story. After checking in (receptionist said she was upgrading us to room with a king bed), we followed her directions to what appeared a different part of the hotel. In the lobby there were elevators which appeared to access the front portion of the hotel. Our room on the other hand was located back in the "east wing" which was down a hallway where we had to take steps down to an empty , less busy part of the Hotel. There were 2 elevators which carried us to the 7th floor...room 76 to be exact.
The carpet in the hallway was dirty, stained and there was a stale smell on the entire floor. The carpet inside of the room was stained and the bed was a king was rather dated. Other items that caused concern was that the bathroom faucet continued to constantly drip, and the air conditioning didnt work. I had to call room service to ask for towels (no towels when we arrived) and for someone to fix the air conditioner. The view out of the window was really no view at all. We were able to look out of the window at other hotel rooms on the other side of the hotel. We couldnt even determine if it was daytime by the view. The room was cleaned daily but for some odd reason they always forgot the towels. I dont know if this was a way for the maid service to get a quick tip or what.
If you want ice, you have to request it from the front desk. You are given one glass in the room, any more must be requested through housekeeping. Overall, we had a great trip, but I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Good value”
text: Good location in Chelsea, easily walkable to many sites. The internet was a poor connection as mentioned by other reviewers and the buffet breakfast was less than desirable. The rooms were small but a good night sleep.

title: “Brilliant Value for Money - Highly Recommend”
text: Booked this hotel through lastminute.com after reading the reviews on Trip Advisor. We paid about £100 per night for a one bedroomed suite which was huge with a sitting room which had a sofa bed, a fully equipped kitchen (with dishwasher/microwave/fridge freezer/oven & hob) there was a separate bedroom and bathroom. Although the decor was 'tired', the room was immaculately clean with the cleaner even washing up the cups and glasses we had left in the sink during the day. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The Beekman was within easy walking distance of fifth avenue/central park and all the museums/shops. Also lots of lovely little restaurants nearby (including a brilliant curry house - Indigo - on 47th and 2nd). Would not recommend eating in hotel but worth visiting top floor for cocktails and the view. Excellent diner and deli across the road. Also worth using the hotel car service ($65) for a stress free and comfortable trip back to JFK. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great Place, Location, People and Value”
text:
We have stayed at this property for years. The best value in Phoenix. Always spotless rooms, the location is perfect for getting around as it is close to the Rte 51 exit, the staff is wonderful, good breakfasts and you cannot beat the value.
On this trip my wife was interested in a certain plant that was growing outside our room. We could not identify what it was until one of the staff took time to go online to help determine what it actually was. You won't find that kind of service too many places.
They even have a "happy hour" each night for the quests.

title: “Much Ado About Nothing”
text: O.k. this is a decent hotel, and I'm not trying to say it's gross or that the staff is really rude or anything like that, but there seems to be a lot of fuss about nothing. First, the views from the rooms are terrible unless you can get a room that faces Market Street. If you don't, you're going to be looking at the side of a building. Second, if you get a room that faces Market, the windows are definitely not "soundproof" as the hotel claims...you can hear the people, trolleys, and subways very easily. Fourth, the bathroom was o.k. but small...if you get a deluxe room it's apparently better. Fifth, the workout room was dismal. The SF Holiday Inn in Pacific Heights has a workout room much better than that tiny little thing. We never tried the restaurant since it seems it also was much ado about nothing. The best thing about this hotel was the free coffee in the mornings...the coffee really was delicious. The beds are fine, but definitlely not worth going on and on about like the hotel would lead to you to expect. I had large expectations for this place and was highly disappointed. Maybe if your expectations are low, you will think it's spectacular. I wish I would have been back in my 23rd floor room at the Argent. All in all, the hotel is in SF, and if your room sucks, at least you know the city doesn't.

title: “Large room”
text: Great location, large room, and friendly staff. As the others have said, the cable cars can be loud if you have a Hyde St. facing room as we did. However, we were not there to stay in the room but to enjoy the city.

title: “Location... GREAT. Staff... Very good. Billing... Not so much.”
text: Can't add much to what others have already said. Do be forewarned that they will charge your credit card OR place a hold on your debit card up front for the entire stay which, in our case, was over $1,200. In addition, they will do the same for $50 per night. In my case, this was over $1,400 hold on my debit card. Due to an "error", they placed a hold for another $200 (now over $1,600). I go to investigate the charges. Told they would reverse the additional $200. HOWEVER, they placed a hold for yet another $100! It was not until I checked out that I was finally charged the proper amount.

title: “Great stay”
text: No complaints here! Hotel is clean, modern and the bed is super comfy. Wifi worked perfectly and the hotel is situated in a great location. Close to shopping and restaurants. Staff was super friendly and helpful. I would highly recommend this hotel to anybody.

title: “fabulous find !!!”
text: i stayed with my family over the christmas break. we loved the hotel .the staff was very friendly , the rooms were clean and efficient ,the hot breakfast was amazing , well located , the fireplace in the lobby very welcoming ,the gym all top of the line equiptment , the laundry room very helpful to have , the complimentary dinner delicous and healthy !! my kids loved the hotel and we would definitely stay there again.

title: “3rd out of three”
text: Stay at the trump soho or the smythe, soho grand needs a remodel badly, very small rooms, besr art is Salume next door, they have great paninis with quality ingredients,

title: “The Wonderful Wellington”
text: To All- I've been to the Wellington Hotel a few times in the past year, and each visit is as wonderful as the one before. The doormen, front desk staff, and sales office are very friendly and have helped me with whatever I have needed. On one visit I stayed in a room with a terrace. It had such a feeling of "The Big City". I hope that you enjoy your stay as much as I did.

title: “Great hotel at a great value.”
text:
When I was looking for a hotel in San Francisco, I noticed that the hotels were expensive and parking at the hotel was outrageously expensive as well. I didn't even look at Omni at first because I figured that I would not be able to afford it, Omni being a 4 star hotel and all. To my surprise, Omni rate was very reasonable even the parking included. The room was small but that is the only complain I have about Omni. Everything else exceeded our expectations. The staff was extremely helpful and nice. The room was very clean and well furnished. Upon chech-in, the hotel gave my kids goodie-bags full of neat toys. As turn-down service, they gave us cookies and milk for the kids every night.
The location was unbeatable as well, situated in the heart of financial district with the cable car right in front of the hotel @ California street.
This is a great hotel with exceptional service at a extraordinary value.
Thank you Omni for a great stay.

title: “No hidden charges, wonderful front desk personnel”
text: Was searching for ocean front accomodation for my visit to SD. No help with my timeshare. Lots of options within walking distance to beach, but I needed to "hear" it, and I could, even with a partial view room. Included microwave, small fridge, coffeepot, kitchen sink, free wifi - but bring some plastic utensils.

title: “Very lovely hotel in great location”
text:
My daughter and I stayed at the Westin this past weekend, March 18th-20th, 2005. Great location, right next door to many Broadway shows and only 1 block from Time Square. If you want to be where that kind of action is, this is the right hotel for you. This part of town is a little to touristy for me, I'd rather be in the Village.
The double showerheads or the soft beds? It's a toss up as to which was more luxurious. The biggest rooms I have ever seen in a hotel in New York City. Maybe I just don't get around much.
It is a little pricey but I feel worth the price.
My daughter loved breakfast at Shula's. The best breakfast she had.
The service & security were wonderful.

title: “Working in NYC for 2 Months”
text: The Apartment is not bad and slap bang in the middle of Manhattan. But I have to say the noise is an issue. I'm on the 6th floor of this apartment block and the noise is a big factor here if you have a room facing onto 6th Avenue. There is constant beeping from annoyed taxi drivers and emergency vechicle sirens and this carries on all night into the early hours. There is a lull between about 4am-5am as the taxi drivers change shifts, part of the problem I think is that the road narrows just as it passes Macy's and the windows don't seem to be fully glazed. I used to sleep but wake almost every couple of hours and I'm a good sleeper. I now have ear plugs which is a lot better but last night (and this was unnusual) a pneumatic drill started up at 2.30am on the corner opposite my building- I was so angry. I have to turn my TV up to max to hear it above the traffic and if I want to lounge on the sofa on a Sunday then all I can hear are street hawkers selling knock off designer bags or for example a man playing the panpipes and it doesn't stop all day! My work colleague is in Oakwood on 36th and Madison and her apartment is bigger and quieter on a leafy road and is not very far from here. Take my advice and find somewhere else, you still have to walk places from here, ok there is Macy's and the Empire State Building but not much more before you need to walk or take the subway. If I was staying in NYC longer then I would ask my company to move me to another apartment block, NYC is noisy but this is ridiculous there are apartments that are quieter and still in the heart of the city. The AC is also clunky and noisy, it is a giant radiator with a fan, no digital temperature control.

title: “Beautiful boutique hotel!”
text: Much better value than the Omni where I usually stay, wish I had known of it sooner! Service was excellent.

title: “Treated like Royalty!”
text: We spent three nights of our West Coast honeymoon at the Mayflower Park Hotel. From the moment we arrived, the service was impeccable. We were immediately upgraded to a suite and comped for our parking. Each hotel employee was so friendly and all acknowledged us for it being our honeymoon. They even delivered a card of congratulations signed by much of the staff. The rooms are luxurious and the location the best in Seattle. We will surely stay at this hotel on our next visit to Seattle.

title: “SMALL!”
text:
I stayed there as part of a wedding party. The receptionists are cold and unfriendly the rooms are tiny, you fall into the bed on opening the door. I wanted to use the iron in the room and there was only one power point, in the bathroom! Do not drink the bar, Manhattan prices! 
The only plus points were that the rooms were clean, the location great and friendly door staff.

title: “Great Hotel with great location”
text: Just spent four days at the Wingate Inn at 35th & 7th in NYC. There were four adults sharing a room. The room was clean, beautiful and we had plenty of room with all the suitcases since the four of us were catching a 9 day cruise on our departure from NYC. The rooms are 300 sq ft which includes plenty of room for the beds, a large closet and a large bathroom. It was quiet, except the one night the garbage was picked up about 2:00 Am--the staff was friendly and extremely helpful with every request. The breakfast was very good--eggs,sausage,bagels,toast,waffles,cereal,fruit, juice, milk, & coffee. Free safe & free internet. Location could not have been better-1/2 blk to blue, 1 blk to red and 2 blk to orange subways. The street closes up at night, but during the day it is in the middle of the garment district. Restaurants are 1/2 blk west & 1 blk south, along with a drug store. We felt safe at night on the street, and just 2 blk to Macy's & 3 blk to Empire State Bldg. We would definitely recommend the hotel to anyone visiting NYC. In July, they are opening a Creole Restaurant also.

title: “Modern and Clean!!”
text: My husband surprised me with an overnight trip to Houston. He found this hotel while doing a search and they had great rates. This hotel is easy to find, right in the middle of everything and is clean and decorated with modern decor. There is a small kitchen with everything you need for cooking if you choose. Also a walk in closet ,huge sectional couch and a flat screen tv. We had a King room and the bed and bedding were very comfortable. They offer a free breakfast, but we slept in too late to enjoy it. I would stay here again! A plus is the parking garage that makes it easier to get to your room.

title: “Great for the money”
text:
I stayed at the Omni last Aug with a coworker to attend some business training classes. Check-in was a hassle, as my coworker did not get the room we had reserved. However, he was upgraded and moved to another room the next morning. The accomodations were clean and neat and the bedding was luxurious. The bathroom was indeed the smallest bathroom I have EVER tried to maneuver within! Everything was updated and extremely clean, but wow, talk about close quarters ! I had to leave the door open to be able to brush and blow dry my hair at the same time ! 
The Omni is an old building with lots of interesting history. If you are looking for something shiney and new, you won't want to stay here. I was most impressed with the location - it was absolutely PERFECT. It was our first trip to Boston, and we were thrilled at the opportunity to be there. The Omni was within walking distance of everything we could dream of. Close to the Harbor, close to the Commons, Close to shopping, Fanieul Hall, within walking distance of Little Italy, and Chinatown...we stayed eight days and LOVED it !
I would recommend the Omni Parker House for the location and the cleanliness, and I would rate it a good solid 3 star.

title: “Dream? More like NIGHTMARE!”
text:
Thump, thump, thump. I could barely get the heavy wooden door open in the gusty New York autumn night. The doormen were all MIA. The barely pubescent girl who greets me at the check-in counter has a voice to match her nimble frame. The lively NY cocktail scene is drowning out her and my words so I am screaming to get her to speak up.
The hotel is brand-spanking new and is not displeasing to the eye, but it already has a good deal of scuffing on the pretty wallpaper (who puts up wallpaper in a hallway without adding protective screens?),
I got to my room and the interior was as if made out of leftover Barbarella materials. Chain mail, metallic linen and wallpaper surfaces with a hint of Purple Rain lighting didn't exactly scream luxury, but hey, everybody's tastes is different. It looked like the workmen had been scrambling to get the job done on time, because the finishings were not so perfect. Scuffs, broken tiles and crooked joints.
Another nifty design feature is the cupboard with the porthole that has a bright light inside it that is impossible to turn off. In an attempt to switch it off, I inadvertently woke up my husband with the main lights going on and off. The solution to the problem? Yank out the cord. 
If you are out to party and not actually there to sleep, it may very well be a lovely place to hang out. In my case, I was there to sleep, so my experience was rather disappointing.
At midnight, I called down to the reception as our bed was vibrating (and not in a good way). The gentleman at the front desk quipped "what can i help you with SIR?". I can appreciate his manners, but no one has never told me my voice sounds like a man's. I complained about the noise, and remarked that I was indeed, a WOMAN. His excuse was that I had come up as Mr. on his screen. Are people so used to trust whatever is on a screen in front of them that they forget they have ears?!?.
In response to the noise complaint, he told me he would tell the DJ to lower the base. One our later, the base was still on at full strength and we called down again. This time, we were offered a new room. After getting up in the middle of the night, we were moved to a different room. When asked if anyone else on floor 11 had complained, our escort told me he did nothing but move people from that floor all night and that 1106 was DIRECTLY BELOW the DJ booth. 
We were moved to a room on the 8th floor which was if possible, even smaller than our last. The slanting walls with the straight curtains did nothing to help that impression but we were too tired to care at that point.
Upon checking out, we told the receptionist about what had happened and asked for a discount. He told us there wasn't much he could do but give us a discount towards our next stay. As we are never going to stay at that hotel again, my husband told him in an authoritative voice to do something about the price, which after a while, he did. 150$ rebate for a lost night of sleep. 
Was it worth it? - Absolutely not.

title: “Friendly and helpful staff and nice accomodations”
text:
I stayed there with my daughter and two young grandchildren. The staff couldn't of been any nicer and helpful. They also had a breakfast buffet that was great. They had biscuits and gravy one morning which made my grandchildren VERY happy!
The staff was helpful with any questions I had from hotel services to getting around Chicago.

title: “Good location”
text: Spent two nights in this hotel with my family. Perfect location, walking distance to main POI. Bike station near the hotel. Will recommend the hotel to my friend.

title: “Beautiful Building”
text:
The Icon is located in an old bank building in Downtown Houston and has retained much of it's historical charm. 
After reading reviews re the noisy location I requested a quiet room and was situated on the 10th floor. I can honestly say I never heard any noise disturbance during my stay.
The room was compact and quite dark but comfortable for my 4 night stay and the bathroom with it's huge walk in shower was great.
I never ate in the restaurant but did have a sneaky cocktail in the Whiskey Bar which was hotel pricey but enjoyable!

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text:
Walk in the front doors of this hotel and you feel welcomed! 
The decor is up-to-date and the front desk staff is friendly and ready to help you check-in.
The rooms are clean and the property is well kept! Great pool and fire pit are an added bonus.

title: “Nice veneer on aging building”
text:
The staff are pleasant and engaging, and Kimpton has put a nice facade in place, but they can't overcome the age and condition of this hotel's elderly bones. My deluxe queen room was on the small side of adequate, but the extension cords powering the lamps ran under the rugs; cracks in the plaster showed through the pricey wallpaper; the lovely marble and glass subway tile bathroom required me to scramble over the toilet seat to enter the shower. Lots of traffic noise reached the 7th floor. The Silverleaf Tavern's food and service are good, but a limited menu and being closed on Sunday limit its appeal.
Location is good, but cabs have trouble finding the poorly lit and signed entry. If proximity to Grand Central is your main qualification, you could make a worse choice, but I wouldn't put 70 Park Avenue at the top of my recommendation list.

title: “Overcharging their customers”
text: Firstly, the hotel's description is deceptive - hotel is in Chinatown and not Soho; there is a business center but it is not complimentary. Secondly, the hotel places a 'holding amount' on your credit card, as well as charging the amount of your stay to your credit card. In my case, they held $300 and also charged the amount of my stay which was $1620 (for 10 days). I checked out 5 days ago and still have not received the $300 holding amount back. Extremely dissatisfied with this hotel. The staff are very unfriendly and abrupt. I have now moved to a midtown hotel with a better reputation, location, and a fridge!

title: “Fantastic Hotel, Ignore the Other Reviews!”
text: Hotel was booked through Travel Zoo where it was a featured offer - superior room with breakfast. My husband and I went to New York for my 'much dreaded' birthday and we mentioned this at check-in. We were delighted to find out we had been upgraded to a suite which I later found out cost $1700 per night! The suite was spotlessly clean and enormous - we had a lounge with a sofa and two armchairs, coffee tables and two 42" wide screen televisions! There was a kitchen area and a dining room area for 4 people to eat! The breakfast was great and well worth having because you didn't need to eat for the rest of the day. Huge choices of cooked food plus omelettes (the omelette cook was pretty miserable but her omelettes were great) and waffles to order. Loads of fresh fruit and freshly cooked bread and pastries. The location is great, 5 mins from Grand Central Station and you could walk to 5th Avenue, the Rockerfeller Centre and most other places. We bought a one day bus pass (the downtown route is the best) and if your time is limited this is the best thing you can do. You simply get on and off as you want. The price for the ticket from the hotel concierge is the same price as at the bus stop and of course you can pay by credit card which you might prefer. I am sorry that other people didn't have such a great time as us, but I really can't fault this hotel in anyway. Special thanks to Paulette for the upgrade.

title: “Worst Westin Ever!”
text: I had booked a 2 night stay for business...it was a disaster from start to finish. Upon arriving, unless you want valet parking, you have to park blocks away from the hotel in the underground garage (which was sketchy at night). The front desk gave me the key to my room...when I got up there with my heavy luggage, I opened the door and the room was already occupied (occupant was out, thank goodness!) so I dragged my luggage back downstairs..finally got a dingy room with worn out carpet and none-too-clean bathroom (hair on the floor). The gym is in the OTHER Westin across the mall and there is no pool...so I made a reservation down the street for the Intercontinental Hotel for my second night and canceled at this shabby hotel - don't spend your money there!

title: “Superb Choice”
text:
We stayed at the Holiday Inn Express on 23 and 24 September. This hotel was an excellent choice. Our room (#610) was on the top floor and it had cathedral ceilings. The room faced Aurora Avenue. There was some street noise but that doesn't bother us. We did have a fabulous view of the Space Needle. Our room had a king bed and it was clean and comfortable. The breakfast was good and there was a wide variety to choose from. 
We spent the weekend in the downtown and harbor area so the location was good. On the Monday we took a cruise on the Mercury and we walked to the cruise terminal from the hotel. 
We will definitely stay there again.

title: “Cheap and good location!! But a COCKCROACH!!”
text:
We spent ages looking for the cheapest but cleanest with good location hotel in NY and found this. We were delighted with the location, 10-15 mins walk from Times Sq past the cute Byrant Park, and the price was fairly good compared to what you can pay, after all we wanted was a bed and a private bathroom.
We got the lowest priced double room, we had a direct view into some ones apartment about a metre away from our window, but we didnt care because all we did was sleep in the room.
Staff were ok, didnt bother too much with them to be honest.
Unfortunately one morning i went for a shower to find a cockcroach in the bath tub!!! I could have phoned reception but i knew my boyfriend would have moved hotels and it was too much hassle so i just gave it a WHACK with my boot.
