I was far more careful after that and put all our luggage on the chairs and didnt walk around without shoes.
Saying that however i am about to book for new year in the same place, as the location and price is hard to beat.
If you want to be nearer restaurants and clubs, bars go further downtown, we were a bit too far away

title: “Very nice hotel at a great price”
text: This hotel is like new and very clean with comfortable beds. The Wingate is a great value compared to other hotels we have stayed at in the area. The hotel is quiet with no road noise with highway 77 so close. The rooms are large but bathrooms are a bit small. We enjoyed the free breakfast including the self-serve waffle maker and large seating area with plenty of room for everyone. The outdoor pool and indoor jacuzzi were very clean and a nice size and never crowded. Although there are no open doors connecting the two so you have to exit the building to enter the pool. This may just be my perception that this hotel prefers business travelers. The few times we stopped by the front desk would always greet the business professionals with a smile but rarely spoke or even looked up as other guests entered the hotel. The hotel was fully booked with a large convention in town this weekend and the hotel was still very quiet and a nice place to stay.

title: “Obviously heading back to Seattle VERY soon!”
text: I’m not really a review person, but I felt compelled to write one for the Sorrento because frankly I hope they open one in every city around the globe! Even though there is much to explore in Seattle, I had a hard time leaving the cozy lobby of the Sorrento. With it's soft lighting and comfy couches, it’s easy to find yourself still by the fire- hours later-listening to someone playing the baby grand while sipping a glass of wine. My room was extremely spacious with big windows that you can actually open to get some fresh air, the bed was like a thick puffy cloud, and there were many tasty treats in the room. I'm looking forward to my return to the Sorrento Hotel very soon!

title: “Dependable Convenience”
text: I have stayed at the Essex House on a number of trips. It is just so dang convenient to Central Park, Shopping, Broadway Shows and, incidentally, to the offices I usually need to visit. My wife particularly enjoys the dramatic and impressive flower arrangements.

title: “Great location and restaurant but noisy inside and out”
text: If not for the noise, I would rate this hotel better than average. However, I could hear a lot of hallway noise and noise from the neighboring room that was enough to wake me up. The rooms are nicely renovated as long as you don't mind seeing the word "five" or the number 5 everywhere. The bathroom was a little dark, but still good. The location and surrounding dining options and attractions are great. Our room looked out onto the monorail which was cool. We ate breakfast at the restaurant in the hotel and were pleasantly surprised and the friendly and attentive service and tasty breakfast options. I wish we could recall our servers name - she was really good!

title: “Great rate, great location, great service.”
text: Stayed a night at this hotel. We came to San Antonio without reservation, This was the best place we could find that was not sold out. What a pleasant surprise. Great location, service, rates and room. Would stay here again.

title: “Classic and elegant hotel with an attentive staff”
text: Stay two nights at this excellent hotel. Was greated with an Amex Plat upgrade without having to ask. Staff alway smiled and usually greeted me by name. Doormen were super friendly and very knowledgable. Room was large and well appointed. Nice bar. Also the oyster bar, Shuckles, was terrific.

title: “Clean, modern and excellent location”
text:
We stayed 5 nights at this hotel in September when we were in town for a friend's wedding. The location is simply fantastic. As mid-town as it gets. Right off 5th Ave and block from Saks.
The hotel itself is very clean and modern. The rooms are spacious. The WiFi is complimentary. There are a few nice touches, such as a clean bottled water station on every floor, and a convenient locker where guests can grab an iron, ironing board, supplies for coffee-maker (in each room).
The only issue I noted is that the water pressure in the shower is abysmal. Gravity is pretty much the only reason the water pours down at all.
For $300/night or less, I very much recommend grabbing this hotel. If it's more for the dates you need, then get something a little less perfectly located and spend $10-20 a day on cabs.

title: “Once was enough!”
text:
I travel to New York frequently and while I have my favorites, I like to check out different hotels. Having stayed in the super hip meatpacking district before (the Standard) I thought I'd try this place. I like the "Old New York" vibe, i.e. the Bowery, so this looked like it would be cool.
First the pluses: Even though it's not really in the meatpacking district, you're just a couple blocks walk so you might as well be. The staff was very nice and really seemed to be trying hard, which had to be tough given what they have to work with. The food at the cafe was also very good. The rooms were generally very clean (save a few stray hairs in the shower).
Now on to the minuses: Being more or less ON the West Side Highway, this is a very, very LOUD hotel. Regardless of whether you can hear their club downstairs (i could not), it is impossible not to hear that highway. And, even in winter you will have your window open (as I'll explain) so you might as well be sleeping on the median strip. The reason you'll have you window open is that the entire hotel has one central radiator system, evidently installed when it was built in 1907. So, as the the front desk clerk told me, "unfortunately, there is no way to control the heat other than turning on your air conditioner." huh? Interesting. In this green era, imagine how ridiculous you feel running an air con unit full blast, and having the window open to the blaring sirens, etc., just to keep the temperature in your room below 95 degrees, in November!? In addition to being a total waste of electricity (and steam), it is pretty irritating to be simultaneously listening to: a) the highway, b) the banging radiator, and c) the air conditioner, all for about $300/night, all night! And lest you think this is limited to the "cabins," I was staying in one of the "captain's quarters" or the larger rooms with a king bed and private bath. Maybe I would have felt better about this if I'd had a decent window from which to look out over the Hudson but mine was about the size of a legal pad. Add to all of this the fact that the hotel has a single elevator the size of a broom closet (which was out of order part of the time I was there, thus treating me to a 5 floor walk up). Finally, given its location at the dead end of Jane street, you will not be getting any cab service at the hotel entrance and may be told (as I was), that I'd be better off walking to 8th Ave. and flagging one down for myself (and my suitcases which I was then towing).
In summary it was worth trying it out as I love the general area but next time I want to stay close to the meatpacking district/west village, I'll be back at the Standard. And the next time I want the 19th century New York feel, I'll be back at the Bowery where, for 50% more money you get about 200% more hotel.

title: “Very nice!”
text:
The Muse Hotel is very nice! It's proximity to Times Square, Broadway, Central Park... make it a great choice when in NYC.
The rooms are attractive and the evening wine and sangria are a nice touch. The only negative was the sound of the construction on the building directly behind the hotel that begins at 7 am Monday through Saturday. The hotel does provide ear plugs in the rooms.

title: “Two nights at the Moore”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed downtown at the Moore Hotel (just up the street from the market!) for two nights while we visited Seattle. Many eating and shopping opportunities around, and very central to many attractions in area. Affordable room rates, GREAT customer service, and inexpensive parking- the hotel gives you a voucher to park in a garage just down the block, $12 for 24 hours. We checked out but were planning to stay in the area for a couple hours and didn't want to move our car from the garage or put our belongings in the car. I called the front desk and before I could finish my question the lady said they had a large storage area and that we could leave our luggage there the whole day if we wanted! So we left our car in the garage and only had to pay 12 for half a day of parking downtown (as opposed to parking in a lot close to the market which would cost $45+!). I really liked the front desk attendents, very polite and wanting to accommodate our needs. Our room was clean and comfy. It was actually very nice for an older hotel. You can't beat the price, location, and charm of the Moore!

title: “Loved It”
text:
We have just returned home from visiting New York, staying at Yotel Hotel for 5 nights and we loved it.
We were greeted on entering the hotel by Emmanuel who was so friendly and genuine. Emmanuel assisted up with check in and went through everything with us about the hotel, assisted us to our room and surprised us with a fantastic view of the Empire State Building. 
The room itself was very clean, bright, different. I loved the purple lighting in the room, it was a lovely relaxing feature. The room is small but adequate. The room has everything you need including hairdryer, iron, safe. Also liked the tray feature that is available to enable you to get breakfast and bring it back to your room. I just felt the room had a nice feeling to it and felt cosy. The only negative thing was that the bed was a bit hard but we got used to it after the first night and I would not let this put you off. Great views as mentioned above.
There is a galley on each hotel floor which provides tea, coffee, hot chocolate, ice and a drinks vending machine which was a nice feature, it was lovely to get back from a day out exploring to have a cup of tea and relax in bed.
We found the hotel to be surprisingly quiet, I was expecting it to be noisy with a lot of young people, I am young but not the partying type but the hotel was fine, not noisy at all.
Breakfast provided each morning which consisted of tea/coffee and muffins which were fine, better than nothing.
We found the staff to be friendly. The hotel will keep your bags free of charge on check out if you have a late flight and want to explore New York some more. On returning to the hotel to get our bags, we needed a taxi to take us to Penn Station and Emmanuel got us a taxi straight away outside the hotel and brought our bags out. 
The hotel is in a good location, close to Times Square but a nice distance away from it to return in the evenings away from the hustle and bustle. Hotel is also close to subway at Port Authority and I would advise you to use the subway, it is a great, quick and cheap way of getting around (purchase the Metro Card which you can both use if you are a couple). We also did a lot of walking around the city so make sure you have comfy shoes with you.
There are lots of restaurants in neighbourhood, it seems to be in the Hell's Kitchen area. There is a really great pizza place just one block up from the hotel called Capizzi and if you like pizza I would advise you to try it, the pizza is delicious. The food in New York is great and I would recommend the deli restaurants located throughout the city, especially Olivia's Deli in the Downtown area (near World Trade Center) and the Pax Wholesome Foods which are located throughout the city.
If you are flying to/from Newark Airport use the Air Train (Penn Station) to get to and from the city as it is so much cheaper.
We would definitely return to Yotel Hotel and would recommend to friends and family.

title: “Love it!”
text: I stay here almost every time I come to Philadelphia. I really like the price, the central location, and the kitchen! Since I'm usually on business when I'm in Philadelphia, I don't need much, but this hotel gives me a lot for the price. When I do have time to do the museums, it's a short walk to the Franklin Museum of Science, the Philadelphia Art Museum, the Rodin Museum, and the Barnes. It's across the street from the Free Library and Bookstore, a real plus for me, and the shopping center and Rittenhouse Square are just short walks.

title: “Fantastic value with a few wonderful surprises”
text: I stayed here with a friend to celebrate my birthday weekend and would recommend it and book a future stay. The location is fantastic, close to the Alamo and River Walk without suffering through the late-night noise you get from a river-front hotel. The price was great and two of my favorite things were the very nice continental breakfast (with Texas-shaped belgian waffles!) and the Haagen Daz room delivery. They will bring you a pint of ice cream and deliver it to your door - and in the heat of the summer it was a great way to cool off after a day of sight-seeing. The only minor disappointment was the pool - it's not much to write home about - but we weren't there to swim.

title: “Great stay overnight before our cruise!”
text: I found this hotel through Cruise Maryland but wanted to share my awesome experience. I was cruising on Royal Caribbean out of Baltimore to Bermuda. We were coming by car from South Carolina. The hotel rate included transfer to and from the cruise port, and best of all, I was able to leave my car parked in the hotel lot for the duration of the cruise. Such a no-brainer! We were picked up at the time we wished to go to the port, brought back promptly when we disembarked a week later and only needed cash to tip the driver, who was amazing- loading our bags and giving us plenty of information as to where to go to embark and what to do when we arrived in port on our return. The hotel was extremely clean; the rooms a nice size- not overly large but perfect for 2 or 3 people with lots of luggage! Nearby (within 5 miles) a mall and drugstores/restaurants open late. Great experience overall.

title: “Nice Pool and large rooms, but pricey”
text: We booked this hotel in part because we wanted to be in the upper east side and because it had a pool. We rented through hotels.com and it was a bit pricey, at $300 per night with taxes. On the plus side, it was very quiet, the pool was wonderful, the room was very large and the staff was friendly giving us suggestions on restaurants and helping us with a broken phone and lamp. On the negative side, we had checked to see if the pool would be open late on the weekends when we arrived and were told it would be open to 10 pm. It closed at 6 pm on weekends so we could not use it the night we arrived. Also, the in-room refrigerator was locked and turned off so we could not use it to store fruit. We also could not get a late check out which made it a hassle. Finally, for the price it would be nice to have plush sheets and towels instead of threadbare linens. All in all, it was convenient and we liked the pool, but probably would not rent there again.

title: “Best Location in Downtown San Jose”
text:
I choose this place due to its location in Downtown San Jose, super close to museums and to nearby bars. 
I've only stayed in the room with the patio, but It was very spacious. The patio is nice and relaxing with sounds of the pool (During the day you will hear the people but it's very quiet at night). There is a nice vanity outside of the bathroom so it's great for getting ready. The only thing is the bathroom was outdated and didn't really match the rest of the room. 
They seem to have a lot of weddings here, so it's very nicely decorated. They also have live bands playing in the lobby, so it's a nice place to grab a drink and relax. 
It's easy to miss the entrance to the hotel, so start looking when you're near the area.

title: “A Special Treat in a Great Location”
text:
Since we were visiting the city as part of my birthday celebration, we didn't mind splurging a little bit to get a great hotel downtown near all of the sights. Luckily I was able to take advantage of a sale and got a little bit off of the price, so that was a definite plus.
After check-in, we went up to our room and were thrilled with it. Our room was a king with a sitting area. We loved the high ceilings, the large bathroom, and of course the great amenities. Each night there was a turn down service and the daily cleaning was impeccable. The bed was extremely comfortable and we slept very well during our stay. Essentially everything you could want in a hotel room was provided.
Staying here really set our trip off on the right foot. We were just blocks away from the Freedom Trail and several T stops giving us excellent access to everything we wanted to see. Overall the experience of staying here was very special and we're so glad that we booked our stay here. Would definitely recommend this to anyone wanting to add a taste of luxury to their Boston visit.

title: “Heaven - Didnt want to go home...”
text:
We stayed at the Library Hotel for our honeymoon last year and it was a perfect stay from start to finish. We arrived in the middle of a huge snowfall, and were delighted to find a small but well appointed room, cosy with heating we could control. Even better was the bottle of prosecco and card waiting for us! the staff were fabulous, so polite and helpful. the free brekky is great given that its free! fruit, proper coffee and juice, fresh bagels. all you need to get you started. the real treat tho is the early evening wine reception... it feels a lovely treat to get ready to go out, and spend an hour sipping a glass of champagne, nibbling cheese and reading the new york times.... roof top bar is lovely for a late night cocktail too.
lovely little pc room as well for checking emails, flights etc. very quiet too - at 8 floors up the outside noise was barely audible.
this may not be the cheapest hotel you find, but believe me its worth it. i would go back tomorrow!

title: “I couldn't ask for a better stay”
text: I stayed at the Brookshire suites for a visit to Johns Hopkins Medical School. I was pleasantly surprised at first by the friendliness of the staff when I checked in. I stayed in a suite with king size bed and the room was flawless. It was clean, spacious, modern and very quiet. The air control was easy to use and silent, unlike the air conditioning units you find in many other hotels. The bathroom was spotless, well-stocked with towels and supplies, and the water temperature/pressure was perfect. The hotel was gracious enough to provide evening refreshments including wine and cheese that were complimentary. The complimentary breakfast was complete, offerred a great variety, and fresh. Checking out was a breeze and the shuttle to the university was on time and courteous. Finally, the location is ideal. It is a block away from the inner harbor and only a mile or two from Hopkins or other great neighborhoods. In summary, I have done a lot of traveling and the Brookshire suites is one of the only hotels where I felt "at home" and felt that they were happy to have me as a guest.

title: “Beautiful and Huge; Needs Management/Staff Improvement; Prefer Hyatt HC”
text:
My husband had a business conference here in June, and my son and I joined him for almost a week. We are in San Antonio often and usually stay at the Hyatt Hill Country. I've wanted to stay here since it opened and was pleased to have the opportunity. It is quite a bit north of the city, in the middle of a residential neighborhood. 
Obviously, this is a lovely hotel. When reviewers comment that it is large, believe us - it is LARGE. Close to 1,000 rooms and the single longest hotel hallway that I have ever walked down. I needed to pack a lunch to get down the hallway. We needed golf carts to move around the hotel. The Starbucks (nice) is open from 6 am to 6pm (not nice) and is at the furthest possible point from the main pool area, as is the hotel gift shop/store. The spa is in a detached building and I never ventured that far in the stifling Texas heat. Their loss.
Our room was a king with a balcony and a view of the golf course/adult pool area. The room was average and while the bathroom was large-ish, it was outfitted cheaply. No shower cap, and horrible soaps/shampoos. Bring your own. We actually ran out of toilet paper one day and discovered that they do not even keep an extra roll in each room. Pitiful. Housekeeping missed our room twice in our stay when we were out of the room for hours. Irritating, especially when we needed our room restocked with towels.
Some areas for improvement: every time I walked past the Housekeeping Headquarters near our room, I saw stacked of used dishes, vacuums, used newspapers, etc. stacked in the hall. Unacceptable. At the huge pool area (great pools, by the way) I sat in the blazing sun waiting for one of the waitstaff to take my order. I was there an hour before I walked to the pool cafe to get my drink. There was no crowd, only young waitstaff socializing. I never returned in our several days there, and this was a disappointment. The same was true of the lifeguards - while they were plentiful, they were paired and much more interested in each other than the safety of the people and kids in the pools. Needs adult management before something serious happens. Also irritating to watch. At 8:00 pm the staff collects towels set out on chairs with seemingly no regard for the fact that the towels might be in use by someone in the pool. My husband lost his favorite soccer jersey in the towel pick up, and was unsuccessful in retrieving it from the lost and found, or in interesting any of the staff in helping us find it. 
Highlights: dinner at Cibolo Moon was delicious, and the valet staff are delightful, prompt, and earn every tip they get. My son loved the touchscreen tables in the lobby where he played endless games of chess. My son loved the pools/lazy river, but we swam only after the sun went down because the heat was stifling.
Conclusion: if you're comparing this hotel to the Hyatt Hill Country, know that the Marriott Hill Country's pools/lazy river areas/slides are superb, but with zero shade. The Marriott is MUCH larger and impersonal and more suited to a business clientele. We will be returning to the Hyatt Hill Country - we feel more at home there.

title: “The Standard”
text: Nice property - great views from the rooftop - rooms a little grungy for my taste. Restaurant was good for breakfast, dinner and room service. Probably a fun place to stay, but when you are there for work and need to sleep, not the best place!

title: “GREAT hotel!”
text:
The Conrad in Indy was an absolutely amazing stay for us. I traveled there on business and had a great stay. The rooms are well appointed. The bathroom was tiled in marble and had a seperate bath and shower - with a TV you could watch from the tub! The bed was extremely comfortable and the flat screen TV was perfect. Check in and out was easy and the staff was very helpful. There was some question about a can of soda from the minibar which was cleared up easily and quickly. 
The hotel is connected with the mall there and is in walking distance to downtown restaurants and the basketball arena.
Overall I loved my stay and I would stay there again in a heartbeat!

title: “The SLS Receives My Nod for Best Hotel”
text:
I travel to Los Angeles two to three times a year for work and I typically stay at the W Hollywood Hotel. I decided for my next five-night trip that it was mandatory that I stay somewhere else (the W Hollywood is unbearable after two nights). After some research and a reasonable rate negotiated by my employer’s travel agent, I decided on the SLS Hotel at Beverly Hills, a hotel of The Luxury Collection by Starwood. The SLS is located on La Cienega Boulevard, near the behemoth shopping center - the Beverly Center. 
Upon arrival, I was warmly greeted by the valet attendants and quickly entered the outdoor lobby, which is quite striking (i.e. crystal-like deer heads). The lobby, although dark, is nicely appointed with animal sculptures that double as lighting fixtures. Don’t be alarmed when you get into the elevator. The well-dressed people staring at you when you get on the elevators are only pictures but will require a double take because of their life-sized appearance. I stayed on the fifth floor in a Premier King room facing La Cienega where I could hear the hum of cars whizzing by the hotel. The decorative room with its large windows, mirrored walls, and moody lighting made up for the noise. 
The bathroom has two sliding doors: one that peeks into the living area and another one, which connects into the small hallway. The Ciel products in the bathroom were refreshing and I made sure to stock up upon checkout. The gym, located on the 2nd floor near Ciel Spa, has enough equipment to conduct a full workout. Altitude, or what I call it, a “Super Chic Pool Deck,” is abundantly staffed with affable waiters including a guy named Alex. What makes this hotel so amazing is its stellar approach to customer service. Everyone from the valet guys to the front desk attendants exude niceness. The SLS or “See Life Sideways,” according to its marketing materials, isn’t cheap (I dinned on a $40 dollar breakfast consisting of a pressed croissant and juice) but its well worth the price.

title: “disappointing...”
text: The location and price of this hotel are quite good, but I was disappointed by the quality of the room, the cleanliness, and most of all, the service. Perhaps I caught them on an off day, but I found the previous occupant's dirty socks in the closet and the concierge was glum and unhelpful. I am not sure how this hotel got so many positive reviews on TripAdvisor, but I would definitely not recommend it.

title: “Beautifully appointed and outstanding service”
text: Could not say enough nice things about our stay. Perfect!

title: “Front Desk Rocks!”
text: Great stay! They really stepped up. Front desk at check in was great. They helped to make sure all 4 rooms were ready for the rest of my staff to come in. They were very accommodating to all the needs that we requested. I enjoy coming every year.

title: “Excellent Surprise”
text: My husband and I spent three days in SF before heading to Monterey and Carmel. We were so surprised to find the rooms at this hotel to be very clean, large and the perfect location. We asked for the third floor, which we got. We had a balcony that we see Alcatraz and Coit toir. If you are looking for a clean, no frills hotel with a great location, this is a great bet!! Another thing is the parking is FREE, and there is a rental car place a block away. Also bike rental and North Beach is just down the street. I highly recommend walking to North Beach for pasteries and coffee in the mornings. Washington Square is very close as well and is very nice to watch locals and artists on the weekends.

title: “Great service and location”
text:
I stayed here one night, and it was my first time at this hotel (my usual place was booked solid)
The staff was very accommodating when my daily plans changed and I needed to be in the room around 1pm. The room was a decent size (and I guess large by NYC standards) but not quite worth the price - though with the last minute booking, I didn't have any other choice. Comfortable bed and standard pillow, though didn't try the pillow menu. Poor lighting in the room - bedside lamp didn't work and the others seemed to have low watt bulbs...Just not enough light. The bathroom was bright, all white and light grey, with a large window BUT there were a few stray hairs on the wall of the shower. Gross.
The location is convenient if youre on business in midtown east or plan to do some 5th ave shopping. it's a block away from the 6 train so that's helpful.

title: “Perfect location to hit all the hot spots”
text: We chose this place based on the fact that that it was closely situated to all the spots we wanted to hit during our stay which included Santa Monica Pier, Venice Beach, West Hollywood, Hollywood and Downtown LA. And we weren't disappointed. It was hard to cough up $18/day for parking but I guess that's what you get for wanting to stay in the LA area...

title: “Really liked the hotel”
text: The hotel is about a year old. Nice, clean and reasonably priced for the area. The room was good., nice bathrooms, comfy bed. This was more of a business trip so I can't speak to the sights around the hotel. Staff was very good. We had breakfast twice on the roof. Great way to start the day. Only one suggestion to management/owners - invest in some new towels. Cheap, cheap, cheap.

title: “Quiet location”
text:
I've stayed here twice in the past 12 months. The rooms are fine - both in terms of size and comfort, the reception and general areas are pleasant and its easy to pass some time outside of event hours.
Directly outside the hotel there is a great diner for breakfast, plus it's only a few minutes drive to Chuy's for a great feed.

title: “totally fine stay”
text:
stayed here for a couple of nights through priceline: $66 plus tax.
it isn't the best hilton i've everbeen to, but for this low price, i'm not complaining. 
lobby is nice, friendly staff. the room is nice and big and very clean.
nothing out of the ordinary, but totally fine - especially for the price. regular rate on hilton.com was $189.
the valet parking is a little unneccesary, but for $12 doesn't break the bank either.
all in all, a good business travel experience

title: “Great Hotel, location and exceptional service from staff”
text:
We stayed at the Magic Castle Hotel as the last stop of our family holiday and it was the best chocie that we could have possibly made. The location is fabulous being only 1 street away from Hollywood Bvld. The service was outstanding better than what i have recived in 5 star hotels that i have stayed at. The continental breakfast was a great start to our days of sight seeing and the free snacks amd wifi was a great bonus. 
I would hightly recommend this hotel to all my friends and family as it is a perfect base for a LA holiday.

title: “What a treat!”
text: We were absolutely 100% pleased with every aspect of our stay and will definitely stay at the Hotel Palomar next time we are in Philadelphia. We were able to check in early to a quiet room on a higher floor as requested in our online reservation. The room was spotless and very comfortable. The L'Occitane soap/shampoo/lotions were much nicer that what is normally available in a hotel and the bed was extremely comfortable. The whole hotel was tastefully and cleverly decorated. We enjoyed complimentary hot chocolate in the afternoon in the lobby 'living room' and also the wine hour with Wi games in the early evening. The staff could not have been more friendly or helpful. We felt like we really had a special treat and got terrific value for the money.

title: “NO HOT TUB SUITES”
text: After a very long trip of riding I thought I'd splurge a little and get my wife a hot tub suite to relax in. I was surprised to find a jacuzzi tub in the bathroom. When I asked the front desk if they had hot tub suites she said "yes, they have jacuzzis in them." So in other words, NO. Secondly, the air conditioner kept cutting in and out during that night, which left the room hot all night. And thirdly, their definition of hot breakfast was packet oatmeal and a toaster for bagels. I would not stay again.

title: “Bad from the start...”
text:
The quality of service should match the partnership of Preferred Hotel Group. Never have I felt as uncomfortable to stay at an establishment where management argued with guests. Policies are understandable when presented properly. However, when relaying it is company policy to not allow Early Check in and charging for a rollaway when double accommodations are not available, well that just undercompensates the notion of my stay.
The front desk manager was quite dandy. She seemed to welcome every guests, except for me to the hotel. Thank you for providing me with the level of service that I would expect from a 2 star hotel. Remember, it is the quality of the staff that makes the stay. Lead by example. 
Thank you.

title: “enjoyable”
text: I just returned from San Diego and had a wonderful time. I found the city to be very beautiful and the people quite friendly, including those at the Seven seas. The staff was always very helpful. The grounds of the hotel were quite pretty and well kept and our room was always clean. The room was, however, a bit smaller than expected and I was a tad dissapointed at how far from the pool we were, considering I had emailed the hotel requesting to be closer as I had two small children. One other thing I found to be a little inconvienent was that there was only one plug in for the fridge, coffee maker and hair dryer so you had to unplug one to plug in the other, not a huge deal but strange none the less. The trolley and bus were close by and easy to navigate. My best peice of advice if you stay in this area is try to spend as much time out and about as possible and return to the hotel late as there is not a lot of restatraunts (or anything) around to walk to, and the area was not the kind of place I would walk around at night with kids. (which I found surprising, being it the "hotel circle") Plus, the hotels restaraunt was way overpriced. I did order from one of the flyers I found stuck under my door and it was sooo good. (Im sorry, I cant remember the name, but it was a pizza, pasta place, very reasonable) There is a mini mart down the street but as I mentioned, go there in the day. My husband was followed by some sketchy individuals one night.(same goes for the fashion valley mall, its close to walk, but kind of weird after dark) They have a complimentary shuttle at the hotel which will take you to the attractions, just sign up the day before, but I found most everything to be close enough that a cab wasn't too unreasonable either. All in all, I enjoyed my stay at the best western seven seas. Like I mentioned, the staff were great . I do think, however, that if I return to San diego, I would stay somewhere that had more amenities around it, preferably closer to the beach.

title: “We chose well”
text:
we chose this as it was written up in a guide book as having great family rooms, in great location and not prohibitively pricey...the guide book was absolutely right.
We had a one-bedroom suite (i think all rooms are 'suites') which had 2 double beds in the bed room, large sitting room, small but adequate bathroom and plenty of extras (extra sink, microwave, coffee perculator, 2 huge TVs, big fridge, etc etc). Hotel's having a bit of a refurb it seems of some of its room but there was little disruption. Had a light lunch in the restaurant one day and that was very good. Staff were generally very good and genuinely friendly (not just on the look out for tips).
Location on East 50th between Lexington and 3rd was excellent. 
Negatives? Front desk was a bit sullen. Hotel only has two small lifts and so waiting for one takes a painfully long time, however they are in the process of adding a third so this should improve things.
Generally really very good and if we go to NYC again with the kids, we almost certainly would return.

title: “Just shy of top notch”
text:
The Residence Inn has a lot to recommend it as other reviews have pointed out. The staff is amazingly nice, friendly and efficient. Rooms were large, the kitchenette is a real nice dimension when you have children and want to bring back snacks for them. The breakfast buffet truly is a level above all of the other hotels who seem to think a toaster with several loafs of bread and cold cereal is "free breakfast." They had eggs, hashbrowns, waffles, excellent coffee, etc. 
The only down side was the small things. Not enough towels. The dishwasher with dirty dishes (really dirty, with chunks of food). Even in the folder with the various services offered in the hotel, when I opened up there was a small pile of potato chips fell out. And no remote control.
I'd still recommend it but give it an "above average." It simply needs to polish the rough edges.

title: “Good Deal”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Courtyard Marriott Midtown East last weekend and we found the location great. Right across from the subway and walking distance to St. Patrick's, Rockafella Ctr., Radio City and Times Square. Great deal for the price. Rooms were nothing fancy, but certainly clean and adequate. I would definitely stay there again. A very friendly and helpful staff!

title: “You won't find a better bed!”
text: We stayed here for a couple of nights after a 14 hour flight from Sydney & were glad we did. Other than a less than helpful bellman, we found the staff great. The room was spotless & very comfortable. We had 2 adults & 2 children staying in the room & had to keep asking for an extra glass or extra towel. The TV remote wasn't working properly but it was fixed quickly by a friendly maintenance worker.

title: “Excellent choice”
text: I like very much staying here. The rooms are really clean, the staff is very careful, the breakfast is great and happy hour is very relaxing on a great atmosphere. The lodgenet application for controlling the TV via iPad and iPhone is great to have fun with a very basic action, changing channels on tv.

title: “Great stay as usual”
text: Great location near Union Square, Muni/BART Train Stations. Well maintained facility and room. I usually stay on the higher floors so the street noise does not affect my sleep too much. I also ate dinner at the CityHouse restaurant at the hotel and enjoyed my meal. This is my first choice for hotels when I have to go SF.

title: “If you can stay here you must!!!”
text: What a fabulous hotel!! My family and I loved it here. The attention to detail is just unbelievable, and the personalized service. If you are considering any other hotel in Boston check our the Four Seasons before you book. The rate we paid here was the same as we would have paid at many other lesser hotels, thanks to a promo rate the Four Seasons was running. The location is great right at the public gardens and so close to everything! You can easily walk to many things or make use of their complimentary car sevice, which we did for a trip up to Fenway. The conceirge can help with all kinds of things and made some great reccomendations. Everyone of the staff is so friendly and helpful... what a great feeling that was. I can't say enough about this hotel what a beautiful place with great, great service.

title: “Older hotel, nice area, scary food, doesn't live up to Marriott reputation”
text: This hotel was older and needed some major renovations. After we unpacked (with pets) it was after midnight, and they had put us in the handicapped room which was pretty sterile and no counter space. It was at that time that we discovered we had no hot water, which was really annoying. We had to pack up everything and move to another room and although they let us change rooms, they didn't offer to help us out any other way, even though we were staying for over 3 weeks there. They offer a manager's reception, and it's awful compared to every other Marriott I've been at. The food was disgusting and we got sick every time we ate it, there was nothing good to drink, and the breakfasts were just about as bad. On the plus side, they are pet friendly and in an area you can walk around. We contacted Marriott about all the problems we had and never heard back. There are a lot nicer hotels in the area, and if we hadn't made a cross country move, to do over we would have changed hotels.

title: “This is a keeper”
text: The staff was very friendly. We got there at 9:45 with 6 kids, after 10 hours on the road. The pool was supposed to close at 10, but they let the kids swim for an hour. The AC worked great - the rooms were nice and cold. The breakfast was good, too. They had waffles, cereals, juice, coffee, and pastries. I would definitely recommend this place.

title: “Good all round performance”
text:
After a month traveling around the USA we loved the homely feel of this hotel. 
Our first impressions were very positive. We were welcomed on arrival and checked into a nice room on the 8th floor. The room was clean and had a nice view over Beverly Drive.
The service was excellent. The concierge was spot on with restaurant reservations and tours. The hotel is about 20 minutes walk to Rodeo Drive and has an excellent big blue bus service to Santa Monica available at the door. Be aware that things are not close together in LA. It is a 20 minute drive to Hollywood and a 45 minute drive to Warner Brothers at Burbank. 
There are excellent restaurants within walking distance and a supermarket close by. There is also a self service laundry close by. The hotel restaurant is good and there is a nice pool.
The Crowne Plaza Beverly Hills is a great midrange hotel that works well. The GM and his team have their act together. We will certainly return

title: “Well Located, Undergoing Renovations”
text:
Stayed recently for a 2 night business trip. The Hyatt is on the edge of downtown within reasonable waking distance to most of the sights and destinations in Boston. I was able to easily walk to the Quincy Market and North End area for restaurants and Chinatown is a stone's throw from the hotel. The hotel is also very near the downtown crossing T station for other destinations.
Overall the service from staff was nice. My room was large and comfortable.
Downside at the moment is the lobby is undergoing renovations and feels somehow off. It is on the 3rd floor from street level so 2 elevators are required to access rooms. The fitness center was just OK and quite a hike from the elevators on the 6th floor. 
Not a bad stay but I'm not sure I'd stay here again.

title: “Charming, but dated”
text:
I have really mixed feelings. They really try and the staff was great moving us into a room more fitting to what we needed with a toddler in tow. When booking online for this hotel, make notes, print the floor plans, whatever you need to do to remember what category you're looking for. I apparently got mine mixed up because we had a 2 double beds, 1 sofa Bay View Suite instead of the 1 king, 1 sofa Bay View Deluxe Suite for the first night. The BV Suites are in 2 story buildings and are like staying in a psycho ward. Very white, very institutional brick/cement block facade inside... it was a very strange room with a horrendous view.
So... we got moved to a BV Deluxe... a one story bungalow while still not in the best condition, was a world better than the first room we had with a much nicer view. The furniture and carpet are worn. The bathroom doesn't have much space to put stuff and no vanity (which the BV room DID have) so it's hard for a female to get her life together. The BV Deluxe had a stove which we didn't use, but we did use the other kitchen amenities for leftovers and snacks and it was nice. The windows didn't close which was a little disconcerting in the bathroom as the window was by the toilet and it didn't take much for people to see in. So I put up a towel.
The grounds of this place are lovely, their two rescued harbor seals are just precious and the beaches were very nice. I wish it had been warm enough to take more advantage of that part. The bay waters are so calm it's perfect for a little swimmer to try the ocean. There is a paddle wheel boat which doesn't run this time of year, but looked very fun. The breakfast in the morning is reasonably priced for the buffet and is hot and yummy. Our toddler ate it just fine. The restaurant staff are super nice and they love kids. The internet was free and parking was free.
So it's a mixed review. There are parts they get very right like staff and outside and the parts that are wrong are mostly things that somebody needs to spend major money renovating like interiors and furnishings. Definitely get a package or deal on this place. You will be very annoyed if you pay full price and see the space you're living in.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights on a business trip and enjoyed it. When we arrived we were greeted by very friendly staff. When I got to my room I found that I was upgraded to a huge suite which was very nice. I wasn't a fan of the antique decoration style of the rooms but the room was very clean and the bed is extremely comfortable!
This hotel is very large and its located right in the heart of downtown Philly. Pretty much everything you need is within walking distance. On that note, I wouldn't walk around in this area alone. It's a rough city and there are alot of purse snatchers, strange people lingering around so just be cautious, especially at night.

title: “It's average”
text:
I stayed here for only one night in January while attending a trade show at the convention center. Because I booked with the trade show group, they put me (and I assume everyone else associated with it) in their Tower building which is actually across the street from the main building. The rooms have been renovated within the last few years, but you can tell it's an old building. 
The room itself was a normal size for a standard king. The bathroom, though, was TINY! Unfortunately you couldn't open the windows in the room (really... not even a crack?) which is always a bummer at a hotel when you want some fresh air! The internet was, luckily, free (as a perk from the trade show) but as usual at a hotel... it was slow. 
I ate at the Irish pub downstairs for dinner and it was very mediocre with very slow service. I ate breakfast at the hotel's restaurant. The buffet was $15 and it's typical hotel breakfast food. 
The staff was nice... I'm only basing my entire review on one night, but I'd say it's an average place. If you get a good deal on this hotel, book it.

title: “What a treat!”
text: We had the opportunity to spend a night here following my office holiday party. Because we had the party at the hotel, we were able to get a discounted room. The room was beautiful, with a nice view of the Rose Kennedy Greenway. Everything about the place was fantastic, from the staff/service, to the rooms and the food that we were able to enjoy - both at the party and our breakfast at Miel. We enjoyed the buffet and were pleasantly surprised at the price tag. It was certainly more than we would normally spend for breakfast, but less than I was expecting at such a beautiful and classy place in downtown Boston. I hope that we hold future office parties here and that we'll again have the opportunity to spend a night or two.

title: “Surprised!”
text:
I decided to get a hotel in NYC through Priceline, as I had had some success with it before. I had to "up" my dollar amount to $205 per night before a hotel would accept it...that hotel was the WJ. It was a Friday night, so I can understand the high price...coming into NYC two weeks prior we were able to stay at the Radisson in a spacious room with two beds for $199 on a Sunday night! Anyway, after finding out the hotel was the WJ, I came on here to read reviews. I was floored. I tried to get out of it, but was unable to. Most reviewers gave it such a poor rating, and since I was taking my parents to the East coast for their first time, I didn't want to have them in a cruddy room. I just decided to warn them ahead of time that it would be SMALL and I wasn't even sure of the neighborhood.
Turns out I was worried for nothing! Yes, the roooms were small. Yes, the elevator was slower than walking up the six flights! But the rooms were clean and in good condition, and we were quite pleased. Would I chose the Radisson over the WJ for the same price? YES. But the WJ wasn't the complete horror I thought it would be. Considering I would have paid over $300 bucks a night to return to the Radisson on a Friday night, WJ wasn't bad at all.

title: “Fantastic Hotel in perfect part of town”
text: The Mandarin Oriental is a wonderful and luxurious hotel and couldn't be in a better part of town. Rooms are great, bathroom very spacious with good amenities. Staff is very well trained, friendly and attentive. All the extras in the hotel are very pricy and WiFi is an extra USD 15 per day. But the Apple Store is on the other side of the street. Hotel is next to Prudential Center (go up there at night to the bar for a drink with a view) and very close to shops and restaurants on Newbury Street. Overall: worth the money.

title: “good stay, bad game.”
text: The valet service was great, very timely, and very responsive to the needs of the forgetful minds who leave cell phones in their vehicles. The staff at check-in were great, the location to a coffee shop was great. The pigeons outside were a tad bit annoying, particularly with their waste, but what can you do. The location was great for walking to local restaurants and bars.

title: “Love this place!”
text:
A perfect place to stay and add to your quintessential SF experience. Bay view rooms are an obvious preference but all the rooms are smartly designed & appointed. Americano restaurant does a great job and the staff is great, especially the amazingly cordial housekeepers!
Hard to beat being able to walk across the street to Ferry Plaza, great location!

title: “Don't judge it only for external appearances”
text:
This Quality Inn is much better once you are in than what it looks at first sight. The building itself is actually quite old and green doors in outside corridors at not appealing at all. Nevertheless, once in the premises we found a deeply renovated room, wall paint and carpet included. Only bedding and pillows should be replaced soon as I felt they were at the end of their service life.
Outdoors, the hotel has a huge kidney-shaped pool and a second one for kids. Breakfast is served in a large Ballroom and rounds up continental breakfast with sausage patties.
Only real negative was window insulation as high noise from the freeway could be heard once inside the room.

title: “Clean, Quiet & Right On the Riverwalk”
text:
I fled to the Marriott Riverwalk at 1:30 am after a short and unpleasant experience at another hotel across town, where my business conference was located. The front desk attendant here welcomed me with great kindness and patience. Even though I was obviously desperate and in no position to bargain, she graciously let me have the government per diem rate, which was the same as I had paid at my other hotel. I had expected to pay out of my own pocket for a higher rate, considering what a nice place this is and the great location.
The room was very clean and quiet, with a great view of the Riverwalk and city. Deliciously comfortable bed. Wonderful room service food, and dishes left outside the door were promptly taken away. All facilities at this hotel are very robust and well maintained.
My check out after a 3 night stay, which was also at a weird hour due to an early flight out, was quick, accurate and easy, and I waited less than 10 seconds for a taxi- amazing! 
When I come back to San Antonio, for business or pleasure, I'll definitely stay here again, regardless of the rate. Really a great experience.

title: “Traditional elegance, friendly staff, well located, but..”
text: We were fortunate thru Amex Centurian to get suite upgrade and other perks. Stunning lobby, friendly and experienced front door and lobby staff, efficient check-in, pleasant conciege. Very prompt room service for coffee and meals. Phone requests handled quickly and efficiently, too. Well situated close to the White House, many dinner options within walking distance nearby. Did not eat at hotel's restaurant this trip. Disappointing small lower level fitness room but conciege gives free passes to full service gym across the street, nice for gym goers like me. My pet peeve at higher end hotels : ( this one no exception ) I do not know why hotel bathroom planners are so short sighted as to not to provide towel bars and hooks in reno'ed hotel baths. True the bath was big with separate tub and big shower and water closet with door, 2 sinks and high counter, but can't hotels provide a place for a man to hang his toiletry bag ? And why is the light so awful I can barely see to shave ? Forget the gimmicky in the mirror TV give me glowing mirror lighting so I can see, definitely poor hotel planning. I would stay here again when in DC. Other St. Regis provide lobby coffee this one does not, no big deal. High end hotel without the pretense.

title: “Not the greatest.”
text:
The Standard is a fun and hip hotel. The rooms are spacious and clean. The service at the hotel is very poor. The people at the front desk are not helpful, curt and very rushed. We we arrived at 8:00 at night our rooms still wasn't ready. Room service arrived with only half our order. The tray was still sitting in our room two days later. Our room was not cleaned by 6:00 in the afternoon, so we had to ask for service, and they still didn't remove the dirty dishes? Our room faced Flower Street and it was VERY noisey! Ask for a quiet room. 
On the bright side, the restaurant is great, and the help friendly and attentive!

title: “New Year at the Waldorf Astoria”
text: This historic hotel was amazing. The bed was devine and our suite was fantastic - but I would expect it to be so at $600 a night. The service was the very best and I would definately go there again. . .

title: “Nice room, disappointing service”
text: Our room was very nice with a gorgeous view. The beds were very comfortable & the bathroom nice & big & clean. But the girl working at the front desk got us off to a really bad start. She just was not personable or helpful in any way. They talk about their "warm chocolate cookies" in all of their ads, but she told us that they were out & to "come back later". We checked in at 4pm, so it wasn't an odd time of day. We went back down for cookies about 30 minutes later & there still weren't any available. We then asked about the advertised "free shuttle service" to nearby restaurants & were told that the driver was "tied up" and it wouldn't be available for at least 1 1/2 hours. We asked about restaurants close enough to walk to & she rattled off several that are at the mall across Interstate 35 -- not within a safe walking distance. I finally asked if there was a printed list of nearby restaurants & she found one after huffing away.

title: “Great hotel, great value”
text:
Good hotel, great location and the staff is very flexible. Easy to make reservations and book dates. 
I travel frequently and the hotel is no headaches and low maintenance as it relates to the typical travel problems we all encounter with hotels. 
Definitely a winner.

title: “You have to leave home, stay here.”
text: Sometimes the most resounding feedback is what you don't hear - and I never heard a single word of complaint from the members of our group. For my own experience, I saw that everything was in order from the get-go, your front desk people had all the reservation info quickly at hand (probably the fastest check in I've ever seen), the entire place esp including my room was spotless and the pool/hot tub were pristine. All personnel were pleasant and helpful. Overall, staying with you was a positive experience that I would gladly recommend to others, and your crisp arrangements were a big part of it.

title: “impresive and very satisfied”
text:
We stayed ther during Thanksgiving long weekend in 2010. Though it is more than a year ago, but we still remember this hotel very well. We travel frequently and usually choose high-end hotels. We got this hotel through "Priceline" though we may not select this hotel by ourselve because we want to stay within "Time square". But we feel so happy to be there from the first day to the last day. The people working in the front desk are professional, warm, freindly, and helpful. The hotel is not new, but it has been maintained very well with a lot of up-grades. The room is quite, well-decorated, and is very clean. It is a 4-star hotel and you do get 4+-star service. The restaurant is also great, so we ate breakfast there every day and also very enjoy the dinner there.
The only complaint we have is the parking service which is a totally seperate service from the hotel. The parking service belong to anothe company. We were charged twice on our credit card. Though finally we got out money back, but it took a lot of out time after we return to Boston.

title: “One of the best hotel experiences I've ever had--bar none!"”
text: This staff, Steve, Diliah, Terry, Jamie; the food manager, the bartenders, food preparation staff, everyone, everyone, everyone and all of the others whose names I can't remember were the most accommodating and pleasant people that i've ever dealt with in a hotel. No is not in their vocabulary. The early morning breakfast was superb as was the happy hour with unliminted drinks and snacks. We will always request this hotel when in Chicago. It this is an indicator of how other Embassy Suites operate, then I'm seeking them out. Not having to hustle breakfast and getting nutritious well prepared food was fabulous. The rooms are very clean, modern, comfortable, and relaxing. This whole atmosphere was esceptions. Please give this hotel 5 stars!!!! For service and convenience nothing has beaten them in my 63 years of world travel..

title: “Fantastic location--great value”
text:
Got a terrific rate on this fine hotel, and enjoyed our long weekend stay immensely. Room was nicely sized. clean and beautifully decorated, with a comfortable (requested) King -sized bed with great pillows. Fine quality overall, made all the more enjoyable given the price and location.
Short walk to Chinatown, Union Square, Grace Cathedral. Next door to the Top of the Mark (for high afternoon tea or drinks) and across the street from the Fairmont's Tonga Room. Cable cars at your doorstep (North Beach restaurants are a reasonable downhill walk, nice cable car ride uphill "home"). Service was great. 
Did hear the cable cars a bit (we were on the "outside", but not on the street side), but didn't bother us. TV great, chair lacked supportive padding. In room coffee great, room service and minibar prices borderline outrageous (no nearby cafe's or breakfast spots that we noticed). Shower water pressure weak, and shower head low. Didn't use the on-site bar/restaurant (looked attractive). 
Having stayed on Union Square and near Fisherman's Wharf, I would come back to this Nob Hill location and recommend it highly to all, if the price is/stays right for you.

title: “Gross.”
text: Biggest problem: my room smells. In fact, the room, the fridge, the hallway outside the room, and the elevator all smell bad and each in different ways. There was also a wet spot on my carpet, a stain on my duvet, and the bathroom light switches are grotty. I know different people have different standards, so for reference, in the past twelve months I've had 30 different hotel stays around the country, and this is the first hotel that seemed gross to me. This would be unacceptable at any price, and at this price it's an outrage. I tried to move, but everything is booked up for a conference.

title: “Chic factor is high; great value, to boot!”
text:
The hotel's car service failed to show up at the airport, as I had scheduled, so I was a little miffed when I arrived. All was well, though, once I took one look at this chic, sleek lobby and was warmly welcomed by the staff. My room was stylish and offered ample space for my friend and me, who were in town for a girls' weekend. The walk-in closet AND separate dressing area w/ mirror made it easy to share this room. 
The restaurant attached to the hotel is one of Seattle's best. In a three-day weekend, we ate at Lola three times. 
It was an easy walk to the Pike Place market, the ferry landing, the Rem Koolhaas library, great restaurants and the monorail. 
It's rare to find such a well-located, hip hotel that is priced right. Andra is a real gem.

title: “Training trip”
text: My stay at this hotel was for a total of four weeks and they took great care of. I couldn't have asked for a better room and service. Even during comic con they still took care of me as if I was there only customer.

title: “Loved the small hotel off the beaten path”
text: Metro is a small, off the beaten-path hotel on w35th St in NYC. It was clean and attractive inside. The room was ample enough to live, store luggage, and do some work. Free WiFi throughout the hotel is a big plus. The staff is super friendly, and the courtesy continental breakfast is excellent. It is a short walk on 35th St to either 5th or 6th AV, which are major thoroughfares through downtown Manhattan. Restaurant and bar were well above average.

title: “Perfect for a Relaxed Weekend in DC”
text:
My partner and I stayed at the Hay Adams for a weekend visit to DC. It really is the perfect place to stay for a quick and fun visit to the capitol and its many attractions and pleasures.
The hotel is small, intimate and quite elegant. Very much like a small European luxury hotel. We splurged for a junior suite with White House view, and while expensive, it couldn't have been lovelier, with large sitting area, ornamental fieplace, beautiful details and a sumptuous canpoied bed. The famous view is, of course, sensational, morning new and night. It gives you such a sense of place.
Service is impeccable, breakfast in the Lafayette room is charming, the conceirge is unusally helpful and made several terriffic resturant recommendations and facilitated a last minute trip to Mt. Vernon efortlessly. Add to that a perfect location, and I can't think of any reason to stay anywhere else in D.C.

title: “Poor hotel but great location”
text:
My company booked me a room here for my week stay in Boston for work. I arrived at the hotel around 1pm and I was told my room would not be ready until after 3pm. (this was a little irritating because I was sick with a fever upon my arrival to Boston, but that was not the issue.) I waited in the lobby area for over 2 hours. I watched countless people arrive and check into their rooms. After 3 pm I went back to the front desk where a very rude woman informed me my room was still not ready. I waited for another hour in the lobby!! Finally around 4:15 my standard room was 'ready'. I checked into the room and was about there for an hour when the front desk called and said they had given me the wrong room and I HAD to change. I had to re-pack my things and move to another floor to a room that looked almost identical. 
The room itself was old and the bathroom was tiny! (not to mention the huge dust bunny i found next to the bed!)Every night the person in the room next to mine had somebody smoking, and the smoke filled in my room. I called the front desk, and they informed me that it was a smoked free hotel, but clearly my neighbor did not care. And no surprise when I checked my credit card when I got home they charged for 2 rooms the first day. They did take charge off when I called, but it only added to the miserable experience.
I normally don't complain about a stay no matter the experience but this could not go unspoken. The staff was rude, the hotel was out-dated, but the location was great.

title: “Check your credit card statements after your stay”
text: This hotel has a tendency to over-charge you after your stay. For us, it's 4 months after we stayed there in Aug 2012. They did that to my brother too. Otherwise, this hotel is up to par with other Courtyards we have stayed.

title: “Great spot for layover or night before travel”
text: I have stayed at this location twice. It is very close & quick to the airport. The Beds are VERY comfy. Rooms are very nice. There is a small bar downstairs for drinks. Staff was very nice & helpful. They have a free shuttle to take you to the airport. There is also a nice Pizza joint just about a block down that is great for eating. I would certainly stay here again.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Great quiet clean hotel. We stayed with 8/11 year old. Breakfast included saved us money. Easy 4 block walk to metro. Would stay there again.

title: “This is a review of the restaurant ONLY”
text: I am a local and had the pleasure of eating at the restaurant within the hotel. They had only been open for a week or so and the level of service and the quality of the food were excellent. We had a party of four, were seated promptly, everyone in the staff was pleasant and professional. I had the steak tartare followed by a grilled duck with figs for the main course and we shared an excellent bottle of red from Oregon. Add two desserts for the table and the check was just over $100 pp with tip and taxes. The Chef has worked at Ducasse and Daniel Boulud's restaurants in the past and some of us were working (or still are) in the food industry and loved our experience there. It's a small space so reservations are a probably a good ideas, while they will certainly take walk-ins. You can make reservations on the hotel website directly via opentable or call them directly.

title: “Excellent Hotel in a good location”
text: Very happy with our stay at this hotel. The staff were friendly and very helpful. It is quite difficult to find a hotel that serves breakfast and we were unsure of what to expect but there was plenty of choice and it changed daIly. Is in a good location not very far to walk to times square.

title: “Great value hotel right in the heart of NYC”
text: Have just come back from 7 nights at La Quinta, West 32nd Street. Room good size. Bathroom fine - constant hot water. Room cleaned daily. Staff helpful and friendly. A big plus was the included breakfast. Only two lifts so a little slow at times but didn't bother us as we were never in a hurry and comfy leather sofas to relax on while waiting. Would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Good experience”
text: Having read several not-so-great reviews of this hotel, I did not have high expectations, but needed to stay in Chelsea for work. I thought this hotel was totally fine. The room (2 full size beds) was larger than similarly priced hotels I have stayed in in NYC in the past. It was spacious (for this price in NY) with a decent bathroom. Everything was clean and the bed was comfortable. The hotel has a nice business center downstairs with computers/internet access free of charge along with a printer. The front desk staff were very nice and helpful. I had no complaints at all. I also liked the location -- 7th Ave offers Whole Foods and other conveniences within a block or two, and taxis are very easy to get.

title: “Solid, trendy, 3 star hotel”
text: I'll confess, I got an excellent rate on Priceline - $89. I felt for the price we paid, it was exceptional and I was thrilled to stay here. The room was pretty clean, the staff was pretty friendly (what little interaction we had). Fine location and amenities. My disappointment was that I was expecting a 4-star hotel, as that was what I bid on, on Priceline. This is in no way a 4 star hotel, but it is absolutely a solid 3 to 3.5 star with great decor (although the rooms are dark). I had read here on TA that many rooms are very tiny, which is somewhat expected in NYC/historic hotels. I e-mailed management to let them know we were a couple that would be staying here and that I would be proposing to my partner while on the trip and that it would be nice to have (at least) a normal sized room or something on a higher floor with a decent view (again, just something besides a closet with no view) ...well, we arrived and checked-in to a closet with no view...I didn't raise any concern because of the low rate we paid. Overall, I would stay here again without hesitation, just not for a special occasion or romantic getaway.

title: “good value”
text: Always good hotels. A very good value. The only draw back is the location.

title: “Great Location / Average Service”
text:
The Omni Berkshire is very well located and just 5 minutes walk from Times Square.
Beside the location fact there is nothing special about this hotel. The rooms are average as well as the service.
What I didn't like at all was the breakfast which is served in a restaurant integrated in the hotel. The selection is pretty poor and I recommend to go out for breakfast.
The prices are OK for New York which doesn't mean it's cheap but value for money is OK.

title: “Excellent!”
text: We stayed at the Sheraton for two nights in December. This hotel is in a great location...easy walk to Times Square, Rockafeller Center, and Central Park. Rooms were on the small side, but as expected for NYC. Rooms were clean and modern. We had a little trouble with our room keys not working, but the front desk re-coded for us. The free wi-fi in the lobby was convenient, and the staff was very helpful. This was a very busy weekend in New York, and a lot of stores had lineups to get in. We weren't able to get tickets for the 9/11 Memorial. I do recommend that you order tickets online before you arrive/

title: “fabulous”
text: After checking out many of the "hot boutique hotels" in a New York Times review, none compare to Giraffe. We even aborted the list and went back to Giraffe. The value and service is unparalleled. Champagne, wine and hors devours on the cool rooftop, complementary bottle of wine, truffles and classic hardcover book waiting in room, The breakfast is perfect. The staff very pleasant and professional. And wait, they give you bottled water (and more chocolates) with turn down service!!!Where else? The price of the stay is affordable and the Giraffe truly delivers, and then some.

title: “VERY GOOD HOTEL”
text: Despite having a rehabilitation centre and sex shop near the hotel, I felt extremely safety. The hotel was situated about three blocks from Time Square, the subway has a lot of lines, and is one block from hotel. Helpfull satff, confy beds, Lcd tv, free high speed internet, quiet room...very good place to stay!

title: “Average for the high end. Contemporary Style.”
text:
I ended up at this property simply because all the hotels in the area were full. The rate wasn't bad considering the location and quality of the property, but that was only because there was no convention in the attached convention center. I have tried to get into this property when there was a convention and couldn't. So this time, I needed a place, others were full, and I gave it a try. 
It is VERY Contemporary which isn't really my style. If you like that, you'll like this place. If your tastes go more toward traditional luxury, then this isn't the place. To me, it felt minimalist, spartan, and cold. 
The breakfast in the status lounge on 18 was excellent. The lobby bar had a well attended live jazz group and the crowd was relatively young to middle aged and attractive. My room had loads of hot water and fast WiFi, so all in all it was fine. 
For the price and status of this place, it was just average. The Marriott is next door and there are many very nice hotels in the area that claim to be of the same quality, charge similar prices, and are outstanding. Compared to that class of property, this place is only average.

title: “We left our hearts in S.F.”
text:
This Inn is located in the famous Lombard St. We got the third floor room with a partial view of the bay & Golden Gate Bridge. The location is great, close to Pier 39, Ghirardelli Square, lots of nice restaurants, all in walking distance. Parking is free!
After having breakfast at Noah's Bagel (by Chestnut St.) we took a 20 min. morning walk to the Palace of Fine Arts Theatre. Good advice to wear a good walking shoes. We were very pleased with the room, decent & very clean!! The only drawback is the noise of the cars at night, if your room is facing Lombard St. So if you don't mind not having the view of the bridge, you may consider the rooms facing the other street. The beds & pillows were soft & comfortable. You can't beat the price! We really enjoyed our weekend vacation in S.F! 
For the budget conscious travelers, this Inn is highly recommended!

title: “Excellent Location but wouldnt pay a lot”
text: We stayed here for a couple of nights. The rooms are small,the size of an apartment den. There is hardly any place around the bed to move around. I think this is common in most European hotels as well. However the location is excellent. It is about a few feet from two subway stations and bang in the middle of the happening part of NYC. The room we got was the corner most room on the second level and at the street side. We could hear people talking all night on the street. It took me an hour to fall asleep,it was so noisy!!! The staff is very uptight and not friendly. We did try the bar and the restaurant food and it was excellent.That said I may stay here again due to the location but wouldnt pay more than 100$ for this hotel(which is what we did this time).

title: “A Unique, Fun, and Classy Hotel with Great Service”
text:
My daughter and I spent the weekend in Chicago and thoroughly enjoyed the Blackstone. It is both funky and beautiful all at the same time. We also appreciate the all of the history that has happened here. The check-in was efficient and pleasant, with excellent service throughout our stay. The doormen always greeted us as we had lived there forever. We enjoyed being walking distance to Millennium Park and the Art Institute of Chicago (and it was free on Thursday evenings--helpful hint to fellow tourists). 
We also highly recommend The Gage for dinner, across from Milennium Park after you check out the art. Also, grab some breakfast at Yolk, a few blocks south on Michigan. It was delicious and very reasonable. 
Back at the Blackstone, the beds were excellent and I was very pleased to have Aveda amenities. 
I would most definitely stay at the Blackstone again.

title: “Really good Hotel, and excellent value - great breakfast!!”
text: Stayed at this hotel for 2 nights and found absolutely no problem. Staff pleasant and room lovely. Great big bed and clean and fresh toilet facilities. No noise whatsoever at night. We got this room for £55stg per night and the hotel was great value for this. Breakfast was extra at $13.95 but well worth it. It is a little out of the way but area is safe and taxis freely available. Would absolutely stay again. Stayed another two nights in the ***** Fairmont Hotel on M Street and paid way more money for not a whole lot better!!

title: “Stayed here three times now”
text:
I have stayed here three times in the last year and a half, each time for a minimum of 2 nights. I first chose this hotel based on reviews here, and now have a few things to add myself. Here are the pros and a few cons. Overall the pros greatly outweigh the cons, and I will happily stay here again--it is always a good price for a more than decent hotel. 
Pros:
First, the location is very convenient. It is close to the Galleria, close to the North Dallas Tollway, and is right off the LBJ freeway. You can get anywhere in Dallas in not a lot of time--well depending on traffic, which in Dallas, is legendary. Yes, there is a ton of construction, but that's not the hotel's fault, and every hotel in 5 miles or more is effected by it.
The rooms are nice--a good size and clean. The hotel is decorated in an upscale funky kind of theme, but it works. I have had the rooms with the walk in shower only, and the one with the tub, but is supposedly smaller. I would happily stay in either. The AC works well and is quiet. I liked having an overhead fan in the room over the bed. In the 100 degree heat the days we stayed, it really kept the room comfortable. The beds are comfy and the best thing--the rooms are exceptionally quiet. I never heard any road noise, or even noise from the hall, and I am a very light sleeper. I have had rooms on different floors and different sides of the building all with no noise problems. Kudos for the soundproofing!
Breakfast is standard HIE, which is pretty good. I could have wished for more fresh fruit choices than just apples, but the rest was perfectly fine--eggs, a variety of breads, yogurt, juice, a pancake station, and of course, HIE's signature cinnamon rolls. The breakfast area/lobby is spacious and clean, with a large tv, a cosy fireplace when it gets chilly, and plenty of seating. The breakfast station was kept well stocked on all three of our stays at this hotel.
The Staff here are great. I have not met a single one who is not super friendly, helpful and just does a really great job making your stay all that you want it to be. The last time I stayed I was warned on check in that there was going to be an event in their ballroom with a DJ, and that I might hear vibrations, but that it would be over by midnight. When I replied that we go to bed early, and that I am a light sleeper, the staff member moved me to a room at the opposite end of the building--problem solved with no fuss. That made me happy.
Cons:
The wifi is free, but strength is spotty. I have had one room with great wifi, one with weak, and the last one, it was so weak it was not useable. Knowing that this was a potential problem, I brought along my Airport Express and an ethernet cable and set up my own in room wifi using the hotel's in room DSL jack. I don't know why the coverage is so spotty--they have told me they have routers on every floor. This is something the hotel should check on and improve. 
The only real issue I have is with the level of cleanliness in certain public areas of the hotel. The guest rooms were just fine. The lack of cleanliness in the public areas was less obvious at the time of my first visit, but by the third visit has become very apparent. Obviously this hotel is popular and gets a lot of use, and it is beginning to show. As part of the trendy modern decor, the downstairs flooring is a metallic looking tile. It shows all kinds of dirt and showed the results of high traffic. It needs more frequent mopping than it apparently gets. The elevators have a lot of shiny stainless steel on the inside, with metallic floors too. Frankly I did not want to even touch anything in there. There were sticky fingerprints on the walls and spots on the floor of the elevator that were a bit off putting. Since the same spots and fingerprints were there all 3 days we were at the hotel, I can only conclude that the elevator rarely, if ever, gets wiped down. Maybe no one ever cleans elevators, but if you are going to use shiny materials that show every speck of dirt, you better keep them clean. The last area is the carpet in the hallways of the upper floors. Frankly, it is filthy--spots, dirty areas all over it. Again, it is a pattern and colors that both call your attention to the carpet and then really show the dirt. Please, hotel management--clean your carpets!!! It's way past time. And I am NOT a clean freak. So if I notice it, it's getting kind of bad. 
If I had reviewed this hotel the first time I had stayed here a year and a half ago, I would have given it all 5 stars. I have to take off a star now because of the dirty public areas. But as I said at the beginning of this review, the pros still outweigh the cons and I will continue to make this my Dallas hotel of choice.

title: “Great Staff, Great Location”
text: I stay here about every 3 months for business trips. The staff always greets me like I'm "home" again! The Front Desk staff is so polite, very accommodating with the shuttle as well!
