The rooms have undergone some very nice changes including hard wood entrances.......and the bedding is beautiful and comfortable. I always enjoy staying there.

title: “Magnolia's Magnificent Management”
text: The service and care of the facilitites were unmatched in Houston. Upon driving up, the valet service was always kind and quick. The check in was efficient and quickly got me to my room. My luggage was brought up and the room was wonderful. I will tell you that the shuttle service was one of the best and with such kind service, I wanted to just drive around downtown Houston just to talk with them. It was such a wonderful experience all around with breakfast, entertainment, and simply to relax after a long day of learning. Keep up the wonderful work and continue to be the beacon of Downtown Houston.

title: “Good hotel, good loacation - watch out for extra charges”
text:
My wife, son and I spent three nights in the Chicago Sheraton Hotel and Towers in April 2006. We were able to get a good “on-line” price ($99.00 per night). Regular price is $259 per night. 
Although the room rate was good, additional “extras” can drive the overall cost much higher. Valet parking was $41 per night and the hotel wanted to charge $25 per night for a roll-away bed (we were able to have this charge dropped). Beware of the bottled water in the room – it will cost you $4.00. Use of the ‘smallish” swimming pool was complimentary, but use of the gym will set you back $20 a day. Internet access is $11.00 per day.
Our room, on the 22nd floor, was large (for two adults and one teenager) clean and comfortable, but certainly not in the “luxury" category. The bathroom was small and there was no separate shower. There was also a noticeable lack of electrical outlets. We needed to unplug lamps to accommodate the, now, standard array of devices we carry (iPods, multiple cell phone and digital camera battery chargers, PC, and CPAP machine). There was no microwave and the bar refrigerator did not function in our room. There was a coffer machine, but if you usually drink Starbuck's, you won’t be enjoying what brews up in the morning. The room was beginning to show its age – chipped bathroom tiles, loose bath/shower controls, scratched furniture, etc. We did not eat in any of the hotel restaurants.
The hotel is within walking distance of the “L” and there is a good variety of restaurants and shopping nearby. There is a Walgreen’s right across the street - we used it for snacks and drinks. Starbuck’s is a five minute walk and we became “regulars” quickly.
We were in Chicago for a week of baseball. The hotel is conveniently located in the “neutral zone” halfway between Wrigley Field and New Cominski (U.S. Cellular) Field. We used the “L” to go to both stadiums.
All-in-all, if you can get a good rate, while avoiding the very expensive extras, the Chicago Sheraton Hotel and Towers is a good hotel in a convenient location. We will stay there again - if we can get a very good rate.

title: “Small hotel, located in a busy area”
text:
I visited this property during Homecoming week for Howard University. Although I have AAA, I was able to get a better price through booking.com. I had to pre-pay to get the better deal, however. I was disappointed when I got there and the clerk told me that I was booked for a room with 2 queen beds. I had requested, and confirmed, with booking.com that I wanted a king room. The clerk said that the information they’d gotten from booking.com was for a 2-bed room. So I will go back to using AAA.
The lobby and restaurant area were among the smallest I’d ever seen, although they were well kept. The staff was friendly, and very helpful. Parking in the underground garage is free. I suppose this is for security reasons, but the elevator operation requires the scanning of your hotel room card. This also applies when you go to the garage. I had to get accustomed to this procedure; as a claustrophobic, it made me a little nervous when the doors closed and I still had not gotten the green light to push the floor I needed.
The pattern of the rooms upstairs suggested to me that the hotel had been refurbished. If so, they’d done a good job with the updating. The carpeting in the hall was starting to look a little worn. No meals are included with the stay, but compared to other restaurants in the area, I thought the prices were reasonable. I ordered dessert and a drink while I was there.

title: “Awesom”
text: In the past, I have ALWAYS seen a problem (even if it is minor) with every hotel/motel we have stayed in over the last 30 years. The Omni in L.A. was the only exception. From the time we checked in (I was in my real grubby clothes) we were treated like royalty by the registration staff, up to the time we left. I didn't have any complaints. The room was meticulous, it was large, the bed was huge and so comfortable, we had a great view, and the staff did everything that we requested. This hotel was a bargain. We paid $75.00/night on Priceline. I would have gladly paid $200/night knowing what I know now about it. The people in the "front" (the doormen) were excellent. We had our car in minutes from when we requested it, and they were so nice. They were so very helpful with anything we needed. I cannot say enough about this hotel. The location was also excellent.

title: “Excellent Stay at Embassy Logan”
text:
Extremely friendly staff at check-in and valet people were very helpful in terms of direction on the T, cabs, and getting around town. Very convenient location to Blue Line T, which is a must in terms of getting around downtown Boston. Maybe a 5 minute walk. Breakfast had a ton of variety and was of very high quality compared to some other Embassy Suites I have stayed at. Manager's Reception was nice as well, though no alcohol is able to be served. Room was great, in very nice shape and plenty of room to spread out. Great location for airport travelers or if you are just hanging out in Boston, stay here and forget about the car with the subway so close.
Nice thing with this hotel that you don't see with others is very attentive management who will personally help you out with whatever you need. Job well done!

title: “Good Location”
text:
The Roosevelt Hotel is in an ideal location and perfect for what we wanted. The décor in the lobby is very grand but when you go into the rooms they are less so. As this is a really old hotel we were expecting older furnishings, which they were, but the electrics scared us the most, we were worried about plugging things in as they seemed to be hanging off the wall in one place.
Other than the tired look of the room it was clean, the beds were comfy and we had no major issues. 
I would stay here again.

title: “nice place”
text: I stayed here 6/2/10-6/5/10 for a work conference.The room was really nice. A drawback was that we could not use the mini-fridge because it was full of drinks that if you took them out you had to pay for them. I wish for the price the fridge was usable. Also, I am a vegan and the food for the conference was awful. I could only have salad from the buffet, After notifying them of being vegan, they brought me a salad wrap. They were notified in advance of my diet. I went to a nearby mall food court to eat. Also, no free wireless internet, only in the common area. Otherwise it was pretty nice.

title: “Good hotel, good location, great staff”
text:
No complaints about my stay here. A great hotel for business trips particualrly given the enormous lounges and space available within the building. Good food and drink from the on-site restaurant areas (Bin 55 in particular) and a spectacular view of the city from "The View" bar situated at the very top of the buiding.
A central location, and a stay that does exactly what you'd expect of a good quality Marriot hotel.

title: “Clean, safe, reasonably priced, no frills”
text: It gets a 3.4 star. The hotel met and did not exceed my expectations. The staff provided friendly service, decently sized, simply apportioned rooms, no fancy lobby, no fancy decorations, working air conditioning (it got cold just like I like it), clean room, security, good location (three minutes from Grand Central), and was reasonably priced. There was a TV (not many channels...but who watches tv when in NY in excellent weather?), basic toiletries, clean towels, comfortable bed, no internet, no business center, no breakfast (plenty of offerings just a few steps away from $3 to $13). I would stay there again if I needed to be in midtown and didn't want to spend an arm and a leg.

title: “average bad nyc hotel”
text: looks old and does not feel clean. rooms can be incredibly noisy. AC did not work properly. would not stay again

title: “Nice Hotel, Great Location”
text: This hotel had almost everything, I say almost because eating choices nearby are non existent, unless you like McDonalds, there is a McDonalds right down the street but other then that you have to take the Metro. Very close to the Metro so you are near all the sights you want to go to or if you get adventurous (good walk) you can walk to the hill, monument, museums and such. The hotel was very nice, very new and the staff was awesome and very helpful. The train tracks are bothersome but I had a room right on the side and didnt bother me except one morning after 9am. Overall this hotel is great if they had nearby eatery would have gotten EXCELLENT!

title: “Nice airport hotel”
text: My husband and I arrived on a late flight into LAX and did not want the hassle of renting a car and trying to find out way around LA at midnight so we decided to stay here for one night. There is a free shuttle from the airport to the hotel that was easy enough to use. The staff was great and the hotel actually had very nice pool grounds for an airport hotel. We also used the trolley the next day, which has a pickup/drop-off stop in front of the hotel. Tickets for the trolley are only sold inside the hotel and are $5.00/person for a round trip ticket to Manhattan Beach- about a 30 minute ride. The trolley stops every hour here. Rooms were a standard Marriott hotel room- what made this place nice was the staff and convenience to the airport/beaches.

title: “Wish I was Still There!”
text: The Magnolia was a luxury gift from me to me, and I would go back in a heartbeat. We love staying downtown, but this was such a quiet and lovely place for a romantic getaway. We never heard a soul, despite the fact the place was bulging with people. No sounds from upstairs, next door, hallway, etc. I never saw any children. We upgraded to a suite, which made our bedroom small, but it was way cool to have the living room and kitchen available to us. We missed happy hour both nights, but the cookies were a plus. Breakfast was very hectic due to the Mary Kay convention going on, but it didn't effect the quality of the food. People were so friendly! I heartily recommend this hotel to anyone who deserves the best.

title: “Great stay”
text:
One of the reasons my wife and I stayed at the Inn at Cherry Creek recently was location. We found the Inn to be a great boutique hotel, centrally located in the Cherry Creek District at a great value. Staff is very friendly, our terrace room facing Clayton Street on the top floor had a nice view and the breakfast downstairs was delicious. We highly recommend it.
Ah...one more thing, the underground parking garage qualifies as a thrill ride!

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: Stayed for 5 days/4 nights in July (July 18 - July 22). Overall very happy with this hotel. Good for family with younger children. Centrally located to attractions (Wild Animal Park, Zoo, Sea World, Legoland, Beaches, Downtown/Gaslamp). Walking distance to Downtown, a mall and the Gaslamp Dist. Staff (especially the front desk staff) was top notch. Quiet, clean two room suite with 2 TV's, fridge, bar. Staff allows you to store personal items in the fridge. Nice beds/pillows. The only areas of improvement could be updating the bathroom and replacing the sliding doors with standard doors. Nice indoor pool, however it is small, but again perfect for younger children. The pool was very warm the first day, but it got colder each day. Nice jacuzzi and work out room. Self park is a little weird as you have to drive up several floors to get to the hotel parking on the 11th floor. Consider using valet parking. Would stay again.

title: “Great place with a pretty face”
text: Former Microtel with comfortable rooms and amenities. No large truck parking except a bobtail.

title: “Mixed feelings about the rooms”
text: I booked this hotel for relatives visiting from Europe and I had really mixed feelings about the hotel rooms. One was a room with two beds: beautiful decorations at the walls, new furniture and a lot of space. The other was a room similar to a studio (kitchenette with flatware, bedroom, living room with a sofa bed) but not particularly nice: the sofa bed and the carpets looked old and outdated, the bedroom was pretty dark and cold. The hotel Midtown location is extremely convenient for transportation (LIRR, subway), shopping (Macy's) and to visit Manhattan. The rooms are clean and the service outstanding.

title: “Very solid business hotel”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights. Very impressed. Very clean, comfortable, spacious room with very good view of bay and Coit Tower. Convenient location. A bit of street noise due to nearby construction. (I was on the 11th floor; higher might be better.) But otherwise no complaints. Would stay here again.

title: “Modern & good location”
text: Newly renovated, very modern, clean rooms! Walking distance to the arena district. Max & Erma's is next door.

title: “Magnificent Best Westerns”
text: We followed Route 66 from Chicago to Santa Monica over 23 days. We started off by staying in the BW River North and stayed in several others along the way, all of which were really quite good. The rooms were always clean and it was only the complimentary breakfasts that varied, from ok to non existent, but then it isn't difficult to find somewhere to eat in the States so that was never a problem.

title: “Too pricey, very basic hotel.”
text: We stayed over in September 08 when the weather is cooling. Location was close to Times Square. Staff at reception were quite friendly. Hotel is a very old building. Room was large and clean though. They tidy the washroom everyday. Close to main roads so quite noisy if the windows are open. Breakfast (muffins) were included each morning, but after the 1st day, we got bored because it was the same muffins and coffee/tea every day. Considering the price we paid, it was not worth it.

title: “wedding heaven”
text:
we had our wedding at the penninsula and stayed 3 nights. the room was excellent, the bathroom was huge and with walk in shower and toliet and marble bath with tv. i felt the check in staff was great, we even got a tour around our room by check in so we understood where everything was. the bed was the most comfortable i have ever slept in and i felt the cleaning was immaculate. the only negative i can mention was staff asked my father for payment for the wedding room in font on guests rather than calling him outside in private. still my father should have arranged this before the wedding, but he was a bit flustered!
we felt like royalty and the hotel was of excellent standard, i saw no bad carpets etc. room service was good and the tv with dvd and digital card reader was excellent.
on our wedding night the staff had left us free chocolate dipped strawberries and even left the radio on a romantic channel..what more can you ask from a hotel?
in fact we feel spoilt, no hotel will ever measure up!

title: “Just what you expect from Marriott”
text:
4 days here, right in the heart of times square but surprisingly quite room, we were not time square facing so maybe that was the reason. The lobby on the 8th floor feels more like an airport check in, with 45 floors of rooms it isn't what you would call a personal service, but everything is there that you need. The rooms were good, with nice fluffy towels and cleaned very well.
The only thing that I hate about this hotel, and it is a reoccurring pain in the backside with large hotels, is Internet access. It is simply unacceptable to charge 16 dollars a day for wifi. Free wifi in the lobby but what use is that? Marriott, pull your finger out.
Would I stay here again, yes if I had to, but if I was visiting new York again I would rather stay away from time square as I feel I've been there and done it now.

title: “Fun ,interesting hotel in a great location”
text:
Fun,funky,delightful hotel
We loved the futuristic lobby decorated with rock memorabilia.
Our room was very modern and very comfortable
The only problem was we were opposite the gym which is open 24 hours a day and we could hear people running on the treadmill at all hours .
Special thanks to the concierge,Robbie who was so helpful and friendly .
The hotel is opposite the trolley station making it easy to get around.
It is situated in the gas lamp area which is filled with amazing restaurants and shops
Our favourite restuarant was cafe 21....great food and delightful staff.
Great hotel...just different enough to make it a fun experience but still comfortable.

title: “great location and reasonably priced”
text:
We stayed for 3 days in early June and found the location great. On the edge of Central Park and easy walking distance of Times Square. We didn't eat in the hotel. the best breakfasts and snacks to be found in the Morning Star cafe just round the corner. Lots of good restaurants but we liked the Brooklyn Diner.
Only problem at the hotel we found was that the only choice of pillows are medium and hard. Just so uncomfortable. If you only want to doss after sight seeing this is a reasonably priced option.

title: “Park, Stay and Fly”
text:
We utilized this hotel as a park, Stay and Fly for our 10 day vacation. We arrived about 3pm and were promptly greeted by the front desk staff. The lobby is small but well appointed for such a small hotel. The desk staff gave my child a coloring book. We got our room keys and a registration for our car, which would remain in the lot and scheduled our shuttle to the airport and took one of the luggage trolly (They have several by the front door) and got our luggage. Our room was 2 double beds. Nothing really special, but clean and comfortable. We utilized the free wireless. 
For dinner, we went to a Steakhouse called Rustler's Rooste, where our child was able to Slide into the dinning room. It was a nice dinner and we would go back. 
When we returned we parked our car in the back of the hotel where they told us. It seemed perfectly safe there and we noticed many security camera in the parking lot. 
Breakfast on the morning was very simple, but it was okay... If I remember correctly... Microwave breakfast sandwich, Cereals, yogurts, Fruit and Waffles. Coffee, tea, hot Chocolate, Milk and Juice. Also seemed to have Coffee available all day, which was nice. 
The breakfast room is small, maybe only 10 tables, but most people don't linger. They have a TV in the room as well.
The shuttle was prompt and got us to the airport in less than 10 minutes. Pick up was easy, we just found a hotel phone at the airport near baggage claim and they told us where to meet and then once they picked up up, we got our car and were on our way. No issues at all.

title: “Quick stay”
text: I love staying at La Quinta hotels the rooms and bathrooms are clean. The only issue I had with this hotel was that the halls smelled like smoke and there was no air conditioning in the halls or ventilation for that matter. It was an older hotel. Overall I would stay at this hotel again but not more than a couple of days

title: “Perfectly adequate Hotel”
text:
This hotel is probably more for business travellers than holiday makers, but that said it was perfectly adequate for us. Front desk service was a bit snooty but otherwise teh service was great. We had room service the first night we were there as we had arrived late and it was great, but a little expensive.
Location wise, it's walking distance (just) to union square and AT&T park, plus the westfield mall is close by as well, so pretty good for San Francisco.

title: “Great base for tourists in San Francisco”
text:
Our room was a good size with King size bed and sofa. The hotel staff were pleasant and helpful. Our room overlooked the courtyard and was clean and quiet. The bed was very comfortable and we had a good nights sleep every night. Good Wi Fi internet access.
The hotel is at Fisherman's Wharf and hence is close to most of the attractions including Pier 39 and Pier 33 for Alcatraz Cruises. The Hyde St cable car station is just around the corner. There is also a Walgreens convenience store two blocks away which also sells Muni tickets (which cover transport on the cable car, streetcars and Muni Buses). Lots of restaurants nearby to chose from.
We had a great stay and wouldn't hesitate in recommending The Argonaut and would definitely stay there again when in San Francisco.

title: “Just like home service.”
text:
I attended the Rotary International 100th anniversary convention in Chicago. Since most of the hotels were out of reach for my social security pocketbook, I booked a package through Orbitz and received a reservation at the Inn at Lincoln Park. I was pleasantly surprised since the Inn had only a 2-star rating. My room was quite adequate, although the air conditioning unit might not do too well on the hotter days in Chicago, and the bathroom was certainly larger than expected. The continental breakfast included with the room was plentiful, fresh and served in a delightful "cafe" which just happened to be right across from my room. The residential area all around the hotel is charming and you can find anything you need to buy or eat.
 However, the major asset this place has is its staff. Every single person was courteous and helpful, responding immediately to every question and request. Morgan was outstanding! He by himself is worth a visit to the Inn.
An ironing board and iron as well as a hair dryer appeared almost instantaneously and every question was answered. The steakhouse he recommended was outstanding and I even walked back to the hotel at 11 pm at night with no trepidation.
If you are looking for an economical, charming place to stay--this is it.

title: “Okay Hotel”
text: Stayed here twice. Its a hotel where you get what you pay for. The blanket on the bed had hairs on it but the room and bathroom was clean. The front desk employees were all very nice and willing to help. There aren't any hair dryers or any other great amenities but is an ok hotel for staying a couple nights. The tv worked but had lines running through it and made sounds, better than nothing. I will give the housekeeping ladies an A+ because they were working hard and were there to help when needed. Plenty of parking and the hotel is close enough to things. Overall, I wouldn't stay here long but an ok place to stay for a short time.

title: “EXCELLENT HOTEL CLOSE TO LAX”
text: Hotel is very good value, rooms are big, clean and airey- room service very good, and they serve vege- burgers, shuttle is slow ,so u need to start out at least 15 mins earlier. big screen tv, and plenty of towels. comfy beds

title: “The place to be !”
text:
I spent 4 nights at the Grant and I was very happy with everything from the beginning until the end, one regrettable thing was the valet parking that we found extremely expensive .. They should give the option to their guests to park their car alone for a lower fee and keep the valet for the stars ! 
Room was amazing, you definitely feel you are staying in a historical hotel ! 
I wish I could go back there soon ! We also try the US grill and it was good as well as the service !

title: “Shows Its Age”
text:
On the Riverwalk, but in need of renovation. Can't believe that a hotel of this size still has cathode-ray tube TV's. Staff very friendly and helpful. Just I expected more and expected a more central location.
The wireless internet is free, but so slow that I reverted back to my 3G air modem. The fitness center needs a total overhaul with some modern equipment added.

title: “Fab Hotel!!!”
text: Me and my mam stayed at this hotel at the end of may which was memorial weekend, we went for my 21st birthday and found the hotel lovely. The rooms were reasonable sized very clean and cool. The mattress was great as you could control how hard or soft you wanted it. The hotel is close to times square, 5th avenue and bloomingdales which is fab for shopping, We walked everywhere and found it easy to see all the sites would recommend the sight seeing buses. We plan on returning hopefully soon and would stay at the radisson again. Fab Weekend unforgetable birthday.

title: “Extraordinary Stay!”
text:
This historic property is a lovely gem in the heart of the Loop. Walking in the front door, a gorgeous staircase leads you up to the second floor lobby, elegant and charming.
Our suite was modern and pleasant, with a separate bedroom. Everything was very clean and spotless. It was great to have a sofa, as well as a small dining table and chairs in the living area.
The bathroom is extremely small, with a jacuzzi tub. It is difficult to just take a shower, as the step up into the tub is quite high - - - certainly not recommended for elderly guests. The tiny sink was hard to use without splashing water all over the mirror and floor.
However, the king sized bed was very comfy and we slept well.
The hotel hosts an evening reception with complimentary drinks in the gorgeous lobby.
The entire staff goes out of their way to ensure your stay is perfect.

title: “Stay Elsewhere”
text: Just got back from a stay at the Super 8, and it is convenient to access the river walk and other area attractions. Never had to drive more than 10 minutes, but that was the only positive experience from a stay there. The maids were knocking at the door by 9 AM and would give dirty looks if you asked them to come back later. One side of our room lost power because of apparent faulty wiring. Maintenance flipped the breaker but within 5 minutes it had been tripped again. They told us to move the alarm clock to the other side of the room if we needed it. The tub was stopped up and the towels were coarse, thin, and were stained. The air conditioner failed to truly cool. The staff and other guests seemed to stare at you at all times. The walls were very thin as we could hear the noisy children in the room next door. The sheets were rough, and the beds were hard. Did not use the pool but they might as well not have a pool it's so small. In the end, just stay elsewhere there are so many better options in San Antonio.

title: “Loved New York”
text: We stayed at Le Marquis for three nights. The staff is friendly and the room adequate, but small. We found NYC to be very expensive, and the door staff, etc. are a bit pushy regarding tips for doing things like calling cabs. In fact, we found out from the cab driver that the doorman collected from us and from the driver for calling a cab.

title: “My first visit to New York”
text:
I stayed at the Beekman when visiting New York on business, as it was very convenient for the UN building. This was my first experience of NY and I was hooked.
The building has an interesting history, having been built for use by the Sororities of the US Womens Universities. It has an Art Deco look to it and it is still impressive in a city of skyscrapers!
The receptionist was friendly (must have been the Brit accent!) and the suite was more like a small apartment! It was clean, well furnished and each bedroom (2) had an en suite. The views were amazing, looking out over the East River and the New York skyline.
The only real letdown was the hotel restaurant/bar, which was very expensive and very limited. We decided to forgo the views over the city and head into the neghbourhood, where we found a nice Italian restaurant (which I have since been back to!)
The hotel is just a few blocks away from Central Park and the Empire State Building and we felt quite safe walking to the latter at night.

title: “useful hotel”
text:
stayed here on a 3 day whistle stop visit to new york.
Very large rooms that were comfortable and had everything i needed.
Found the staff a little rude and very abrupt but would not put me off returning.
Very useful from its location and panoramic views of the city and found it surprisingly quiet considering its location.
would definitely consider returning to it s it was what i have come to expect from a hotel of this nature.

title: “Excellent service, exceeded our expectations for our Christmas holiday. The staff really made the difference!”
text: From the very beginning with the bell staff greeting us to the ease of checking in, everything was perfect! We dined at the Barefoot Grill and the service and food exceeded our expectations. Keep up the great work Paradise Point!

title: “Not Good Value for the Money -- You Can Do Better!”
text:
I became a Starwood member after receiving fantastic service at various Westins and W Hotels. This hotel was the first Westin that was so dissatisfactory that we checked out early.
The employees were very nice. However, in a competitive industry like this one, you need more than "nice" staff members.
First problem, the room was too small. We had booked one of the "larger" rooms and even it was fairly difficult to move around in. The bathroom was tiny and the bath products were nothing special. For the price (ranging from $299 to $600 a night), I'd expect something a little more snazzy. Minor complaint.
Service was friendly, but haphazard. Items ordered from room service weren't sent, coffee cups in coffee maker weren't replaced, little things -- again, minor complaints, but when you are charging high prices for such a small room, you should be at your best in terms of service.
State of the room itself? Blah. It had recently been refurbished, but it was a step below most of ther hotels I've stayed in AFTER the refurbishing. I'd hate to know what it looked like before.
The final straw and why we "moved out" early was the noise level. The rooms would be quiet if it weren't for thin walls. As I mentioned, we were in what was supposed to be one of the nicer, more expensive rooms. Yet it was adjacent to another room where a couple kept fighing at 3:00 AM. We could hear everything, and I mean everything. 
I could have just asked for a different room, but I was so astounded at the disparity in service between this Westin and all others that I didn't even bother. They must feel like they don't need to work hard for business these days, and maybe they don't since the hotel had been oversold.

title: “Basic but funcional”
text:
Stayed two nights over thanksgiving weekend. The first room"s toilet was not working so were given another room that was larger and on the first floor. Bed was comfortable, room was clean (bedspread of first room;s bed was rather garish) with free WI-fi and free breakfast. Small room for breakfast but we wound up with a table. 
Good overall value for a hotel room in the middle of Brookline, Mass.. Would stay there again.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: Clean, comfortable, convenient to everything with an amazing staff. The only drawback was the cost of parking (but worth for the location). Called to the front desk to ask for the late check out and they were accomodating, however the person was really abrupt, though it might have been the check out rush.

title: “Nice Convention Hotel in San Antonio”
text: I stayed heare for a large convention (1400) held in this hotel. The hotel gave us parking for half price ($12) which was nice. The breakfast buffet is delicious. The hotel offers free internet if you are a Priority Club member but I was so busy I didn't get to use it. The room rate of $139 was a bit pricy but it was worth it to not have to drive home each evening since I live in San Antonio. the hotel could be a bit closer to the Riverwalk but is nice. I would stay here again.

title: “Very clean, very comfortable beds.”
text: I traveled with my son for a campus experience at St. Joseph's University. The hotel is minutes away from SJU so it was very convenient. We were in Room 611 and it was beautifully renovated. The room and bathroom were extremely neat and clean. The beds were made up nicely and looked very inviting when entering the room. They were also very clean and very comfortable with a down comforter. We had a great night's sleep. The lobby had plenty of seating contrary to other reviews. Staff extremely friendly. Pool and weight room very nice. We had a complimentary breakfast but were unable to use. On the down side, it cost $10 for valet parking but it was worth it so you didn't have a long walk after parking car since there was no actual parking lot at hotel. We also didn't like the fact that it costs $10 to use wireless internet. I believe that should be free since it is something guests would commonly use. One night's stay is little pricey but I would still highly recommend this hotel.

title: “What a lovely hotel!”
text:
I've stayed at the Queen Anne for a 5 night stay and I have absolutely no complaints about it! It was by far the best hotel I've stayed in my many trips on a budget! I was on my own for a vacation/businness trip in San Francisco and, after reading so many good reviews of this hotel, I decided to book it and I was certainly not disappointed. My room was very big, with a nice carpeted floor and a big King Size poster bed full of comfy pillows and cushions. There was also what I suppose was an "antique" wardrobe, a big table (with coffee-making facilities) with two big chairs, a big old dresser and a big television set with a dvd recorder. The bathroom was spottlesly clean and had a nice bathtub with clean towels everyday. The hotel was lovely all around, with Victorian paintings and furniture everywere...I went up to the third floor just to have a look around at the stairwells! They have a lovely living room downstairs with two fireplaces, loads of comfy chairs and sofas and a very nice piano, who anyone can play.The hotel offers a continental breakfast every morning, with lovely muffins, cakes, toasts and fruit juices of various sorts. They really offer an afternoon tea with sherry and biscuits until 6 pm but unfortunately I never got to taste them as I usually came back to the hotel about 7 pm. But the "thing" I enjoyed the most about their extra services was obviously Henry! Every week day morning (at 7.45, 8.45 and 9.45) he drives you anywhere you want in the San Francisco area (he took me to the Legion of Honor, the Golden Gate Bridge and the SFMOMA), most of the times even on a Saturday, and he also gives you a sort of guided tour of the city! while driving you around! You should really book the ride the day before, but if you hang around the reception area in the morning and his car is not completely full he will take you anyway!
The area the hotel is in is very quiet and is close to Japantown, home of many restaurants (thai, chinese, japanese, indian...) where you can go, order a take-away and eat it confortably back in your room (especially if you're on your own and don't want to stay out at night!)! To be honest, the hotel is quite far from the main places of interests, about 10 blocks from Union Square and a bit more from Fisherman's Wharf, but there's a bus stop just outside the hotel and if you walk down 3 blocks to Van Ness there are also many trams that will take you basically everywhere. And I have to say that I've also enjoyed the walk back from Union Square...quite relaxing, even after a day walking up and down San Francisco!
The only thing I'm not too sure about was the customer service at the hotel...some of the staff were very friendly and helpful, but others, although they weren't rude, just seemed not to be too bothered about helping out...but maybe it was just my impression! All in all I will definetely recommend this hotel to anyone, and will surely go back when in San Francisco again!

title: “Not as bad as the poor reviews suggest”
text:
We had a large room with two queen beds that was clean, comfortable and quiet even though the hotel is on a main road. Other rooms nearer the highway may have been noisier.
There was free wi-fi in the room and we had a warning message from our internet browser, but we used it and did not have any problems. 
There was a buffet breakfast and we found plenty to eat – cereal, bananas, muffins, cinnamon rolls, bacon, and the pancake making machine was particularly good!
We stayed for two nights in the Holiday Inn Express & Suites during October 2011.

title: “Never again!!!! Elevator is a death trap!”
text: All the big name hotels were sold out and we did not have reservations anywhere. Price was not bad compared to other hotels but for what we got I'd rather pay more to stay somewhere that was nice. Elevator is shaped like an old coffin and almost got stuck - going just from the first to third floor (there is no second) elevator kept jumping and stopped about 4 times. We ended up taking the stairs to the 10th floor since nobody felt safe in there. First room we had the air conditioner was broken-and its the old window units- which when we got one that finally worked was ok. Carpet was stained and dirty, but room over all appeared to be clean. Bed was hard and room is very small!!! I'd say the bathroom which is only about the size of a couch was the most decent thing in the hotel. Hotel is definitely not worth the 60 dollars we spent on the room. Had I not been drinking I would have drove the 3 hours back home.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text: Lovely hotel. Exceptional service and a fantastic environment.

title: “Popular place to stay”
text: Expensive valet parking but close to good places to eat.

title: “Should be shut DOWN”
text:
My stay at this hotel was the scariest experience of my life. My friends and I were staying here for the FL GA game and were excited about the location, until we actually got there. It was miserable. There were roaches, it smelled funny, there is a strip club in front of the hotel so who knows what kind of people frequent the hotel. Our taxi driver who picked us up the first night said "you girls better be careful in this part of town, you really shouldn't be here". When we got back that night there were police in front of our hotel because of something going on at the strip club in front of hotel. Need I say more! Very scary, very dirty, nothing redeeming about this place! Any place is better than this place, DON'T 
STAY HERE!!!!!!

title: “Keep Coming Back”
text: After my many trips to the Inner Harbor, I always leave saying how much I love staying at this hotel! This hotel is the best place to stay thanks to the location, staff and accommodations. I'm not very picky, but they always seem to surprise me with how attentive they are to their guests. The first time I stayed at the hotel, the concierge was extremely helpful in planning our adventures and even gave us passes to some nightlife around us. The second visit was even better because I discovered that just across the street in what looks like a very scary alley, turned out to be 2 fantastic bars/restaurants that I'm dying to go back to. We always wind up arriving early and they always have a smile and the room ready. Although we don't stay in the hotel very long, I always keep coming back to that hotel each year because they know how to treat guests who are just looking for a little weekend getaway. I always leave happy because the staff is helpful, the rooms are always clean and maintained and the breakfast in the morning is better than some diners!! See you in October for the Fells Point Festival!!

title: “Check out the room before you pay !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text:
I LEARNED MY LESSON: ALWAYS CHECK OUT THE ROOM BEFORE YOU COMMIT TO PAYING. The room I stayed in on October 17th weekend was so saturated with cigarette smoke, it was difficult to sleep. (My unused clothes had to be washed when getting home.) The TV remote was broke. The hot and cold knobs were opposite. There was loud music and ruckus outside until 5 a.m. I am wondering how clean the sheets and pillows were. The only positive was shower water was hot. 
 What a waste of 80 bucks.

title: “Classic, Pricey; Showing Wear”
text: This is a beautiful and grand hotel with lots of history that deserves its place among the best. Christmas decorations were going up already in the main entrance and very lovely (see photo)Service from maids to bartenders was top-notch(we really liked Tony, the older gentleman who took our bags); the quality of food and beverages (Have Noah the Bartender in the main bar by the lobby make you one of his cocktails. He knows his profession well) was exquisite. However, my one complaint is that for a hotel that was, at least for me, around $800 a night, one would think that wallpaper starting to peel at the seams, and other structural issues : the overhead beam joints on the ceiling were cracking open in several places, the bathroom also had old, ugly, dirty looking phone jack in the wall by the window, a 70's era, dingy looking push button ventilation fan that was duct taped around the seams that was on the wall near the floor by the toilet, and-- I found some weird,ugly, unused base plate for some long-time-ago mystery apparatus was on the wall in the shower. I am sure these all are resulting from years of wear and tear that should have been(and easily could have been) adressed and taken care of---especially with the reputation of this place. I stayed in Room 10A--on 10/23/11 to 10/26/11 in a nice suite with a living room type set-up and a separate bedroom and bathroom adjoining it. The beds were extremely comfortable--quality feather down covers and pillows were a nice touch. The large flat screen TVs in both rooms, decent chairs, and comfy sofa were nice touches . However, due to several little problems like those mentioned above are the reason I am not giving a perfect score. I wanted to get away in comfort to NYC for the Holiday Weekend. I did enjoy my stay and it was indeed comfortable, but, as stated already, I do feel that for the price and reputation of this place, they really should be more attentive to the conditions of the rooms.

title: “Was it a halfway house or Ramada”
text: Like other reviewers. I knew upon booking this place we were in trouble. We were looking for a hotel between $100 and $150. Even in NYC you can get better for a $125 a night. Crappy internet, Spotty electricity in the room. Dirty, smelly... Nothing more to say other than, I think part of the property is used as a halfway house of some sort. Shame on Ramada for allowing this motel to carry their name.

title: “great suite”
text: We had a great stay at the Affinia 50. Lobby was small and we expected a small room but what a great suite! My broyther and I decided to have a suite instead of renting separate rooms. It was worth it. Two Queen fluffy beds and 3 different types of pillows... (6 per bed!) The room had a kitchenette, a sitting area (large sofa) and a chair. Wiorking desk + internet (extra charge) . The heating was silent. Helpful staff. Busy streets around. Six blocks from Broadway Ave. but 10 blocks from Theaters. Definitely going back again!

title: “Secret Gem for 13 years for us!”
text: My husband has stayed regularly at The beautiful Mountain Star Lodge for business over a 13 year time period...2 days a week usually. I would venture to guess that he is the guest with the oldest history with frequency of stays. As a corporate vice-president, he is particular about where he stays when away from home. I accompany him for leisure about once a month. The experience is a treat! I'm shocked over one time stay visitors comments. Don't believe! Just had to respond to various comments b others giving an erroneous impression of this charming place. Crickets are common at certain times in Texas and are considered "good luck!" New building projects with malls, restaurants, churches, and businesses have been rampant in the last few years which uproot the homes of scorpions who search for alternate spots. Quite honestly, over the entire time we've stayed at this scenic spot, we've not encountered any vermin...even with a nature preserve backing the premises...which offers spectacular views from the windows and balconies. Wonderful hiking to exercise and observe nature behind Mountain Star in the preserve. The place is quiet and tranquil and serene. There is NO bar next door as stated by one complainer. This is a false statement. There is actually a Christian Science Church next door whose church members are quiet and respectful, so no interruptions to guests. The only spot that has occasional music is a Mexican restaurant serving delicous entrees several doors down and that is only on some weekend nights. Recommend eating there for convenience and culinary delight...walking distance. The rooms are large and spacious with amenities, beds comfortable, and breakfast offerings varied and healthy. The manager, Beth, is friendly and accommodating to needs. Our grandchildren have stayed with us here twice and they love the swimming pool and food! I frankly am amazed that this secret gem is not sold out every night. It is our favorite spot to stay at and we're quite picky! Consider credibility of THIS review over a 13 year period of time, with stays averaging twice a week over one time stay prima donna whiners. I recommend to family and friends and co-workers. All that have stayed have felt equally pleased.

title: “Mixed Feelings”
text: As a frequent traveler to Seattle, I was eager to try the very well located Maxwell during my most recent trip to attend a concert at Key Arena. I could not have been more thrilled with the location. The access to Seattle Center was super quick and I was at the arena or on the monorail to downtown five minutes from my door. My first impressions of the hotel are that it is stylish, spacious and welcoming. The staff was lovely, except for the maid who twice failed to see my "do not disturb" sign and knocked anyway, and the tiny cupcakes in the afternoon are a memorable touch. The rooms are unique and very comfortable for sleeping, working at a desk or watching the absolutely enormous televisions, not so great for eating in or reading as there is no "tea table" or really good cozy chair. I tried the DVD player but could not get it to work which was a disappointment. The wood floors were very attractive and I had no problem with room noise around me. As someone who loves a long soak after sightseeing, I guess the lack of a tub in the bathrooms my biggest drawback to this new property. While the open showers are hugh and aesthetically pleasing, it is impossible to get really warm in them because they do not trap heat. I thought a dip in the pool might take the place of a good bath, but that too was chilly and ridiculously small. It was my bad luck to be swimming at the same time as a rowdy family of five with dive bombing kids and there literally was not room for all of us to enjoy the water. I longed for a hot tub. I also wished for a few more food options coming in late from the concert or early in the AM. The tiny espresso bar in the hotel has mostly sugary junk food, sodas and juices. How about some upscale herbal teas, better baked goods or something savory like a mini quiche? Fortunately there are tons of eateries and a really fine upscale grocery store and deli within a few blocks.

title: “All the right ingredients, exceptional hotel”
text: Location is excellent right on Ghirardelli Square with direct access through the hotel. We stayed in a two bedroom suite + living room + kitchen, very high standards throughout. Free internet and breakfast. Complimentary Maseratti Quatropporte to drive or pick you up to a 2 miles radius. Small, less than 100 apartments. Unbelievable value. I will not even bother writing further. Take my word for it, this is the place to stay in San Francisco.

title: “Horrible Stay”
text: It was the only hotel left for our stay so we really had no choice. There wasn't enough parking so we asked if we could park at the Eithiopian restaurant next door. We were told we could as long they were closed. They were!!!! Woke up and our truck had been towed!! Cost us $200 to get it! Try had a credit care on file for our rooms and took the number for another card for " incendentals". They charged that card instead and said there was nothing they could do! We will never stay here again and I do NOT recommend!!!!!

title: “FAMILY TRIP”
text: I will never, never stay at that hotel again. Customer service was not good. It always help to sell the city and hotel which the guests are visting.

title: “Good mid-range hotel”
text:
Stayed 5 nights at the Bay Club and enjoyed my stay. 
The location is reasonably good - right on the water which is nice to look out at and for walks but it is not that close to any beaches and is quite a distance from any nicer restaurants. Having said that the freeways are close but it is several minutes drive at least to either a beach or nicer restaurant. 
The staff were friendly and helpful throughout my stay. 
The rooms are large, typical of american hotels such as these with lots of empty space. The decor is fine, a little dated but in good condition and very clean. The "patio" seating area outside the room is very small and close to the next room. It rather looked out on to the parking lot, although the first floor rooms looked like they had more room, privacy and a better view. 
The pool area is pleasant, although surprisingly items from the bar do not seem to be able to be brought to the pool. 
I did not eat at the hotel and so can't comment on the food. 
Overall I think the Bay Club Hotel is pleasant although not particularly spectacular.

title: “Favorite hotel of our 4 city trip”
text: We embarked on an east coast trip with our 3 children, well actually, there were 15 of us including grandparents and my brothers family. By far this was our favorite hotel of the trip. The room was large with a king bed and pull out bed - basically 2 rooms plus the bathroom was HUGE! Coffee downstairs in the morning. The bar was fun and breakfast was excellent. We could walk to all the historical sites and close to the subway when we went to the Phillies game. Highly recommend!!

title: “Excellent hotel!”
text: Very nice hotel! Great facilities for meetings/conferences; very nice rooms; though the building is older, you'd never know it! Nice fitness center; great bar & restaurants; I walked downtown one night across the Duke Ellington bridge and felt safe. Close to other neighborhood restaurants. A good choice, over all!

title: “Comfort friendly staff”
text: What a great location for our first trip to New York City! The hotel staff where friendly and helpful. The beds where comfortable, rooms a nice size and the complementary breakfast was very well done. We would absolutely recommend a stay at this hotel if you are ever in New York City.

title: “My favorite place to stay!”
text: Everything about this hotel is excellent - their people , accomodations , food - all of it!

title: “Everything was good but not great”
text: Nice hotel. From maps of San Diego, it looks like a short walk to the Gas Lamp, but its a liitle far. Valet parking is 23/day and a little slow(30 minutes to get car). High speed internet access is 10.99 for 24 hours. Rooms are nice, bathroom has separate shower and tub, mini bar, two tv's, sofa, chair and nice desk for working. If I were on business, this would be ok to stay. If I were on vacation, I would look for something closer to Horton Plaza or the Gaslamp.

title: “Pretty Decent”
text:
Room was nice and comfortable. The bar was terrible. Expensive drinks, bartender was awful. Had limes for drinks but did not want to cut them. He was stealing the place blind by charging for drinks but not ringing them up on the register. He added gratuity to the bill on the first night and did not mention it until I saw the receipt and commented. I have never seen an automatic gratuity added to the tab at a US bar. We didn't let our bar experience ruin our stay. The check in staff was outstanding and friendly. We liked Silver expecially.
Would stay here again. $85 one night and $130 for NYE. A bargain.

title: “Nice place”
text: Got this room through Priceline for $55 - was a bit disappointed that we had to pay $14 to park. Nice decor, bed was very comfortable and flat screen tv was great. I agree with some of the other reviews regarding the noise- we could hear very clearly people talking in the hallway. Would stay here again - although quite a distance to the heart of downtown - ( they do have a free shuttle)

title: “Such a classy place!”
text:
I joined my husband for a business trip to Washington DC.He had stayed at the Fairmont before and was very satisfied.This time we were upgraded to the Golden Conscierge Floor.The hotel is well situated,convenient.The reception area and the lounge/bar are very nice.
Our room was impeccable,the GC Floor breakfast and free internet loung facility a plus.
The reception staff and the conscierge service both at the reception and the GC Floor were excellent.Definitely going back!

title: “it is what it is...”
text: Ok, this hotel is what it is. Very central location - a couple of blocks from the Empire state Building & it's cheap - one of the cheapest we could find in New York anyway. Luxury, it isn't. The room was absolutely TINY! a bed against a wall, a small desk and a sink - thats it! Was very clean though! The decor was pretty dated, I guess i was expecting better after we had read it had recently been refurbished... The communal areas were very well kept and staff on front desk were friendly and helpful! We had a room with a shared bathroom - in fact, we were right next door to it. Never had to wait / que to use it although the shower was a big let down - it would fluctuate between scolding hot and freezing cold - not very comfortable... Having said all this, you don't come to NY city to sit around a hotel room so it deserves a good 3 stars considering the price... I think next time we go, we'll try and find something a bit more upscale all the same!

title: “Best ever!”
text: One of the best places I've stayed yet. This botique hotel is perfect the beds are super comfortabl . Lay In bed and watch the ships come in and the hustl and bustle of pikes place. I love this place

title: “Fantastic, exceeded expectations”
text: My husband and I just returned from a two day stay at Icon. This is NOT your run of the mill corporate hotel, rather it is a luxurious, well appointed, very unique, gem in the heart of downtown. The hotel staff, every ONE, from the car valets to the engineer who came up to stop the commode from running, was top notch, very friendly and courteous. If I had to say something was missing, a hot tub/spa would be nice. We enjoyed our stay immensely.

title: “A flawless experience compliments of the superior staff that understands attention to detailcreates magic!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text:
The best location!! The best people!! Boston at youe feet !!!!!!!!!!!
Walk to all of Boston's best;
Italian Food in the North End
The Freedom trail
The Public Gardens with the Swann Boats
irt

title: “Gorgeous, lush, and tropical!”
text: This resort was amazing. We live in San Diego and actually felt like we were away on vacation on an island! Its very lush, and tropical. Has many awesome pools with sandy bottoms. Great resturants. Theres a fancier one which I heard great reviews about, but we went to the more casual one. It was right on the bay, outside seating, very cool! I'd definately recommend it, can't wait to go back myelf!!!

title: “Absolutely wonderful”
text: The Jefferson oozes personality. The staff were lovely - very helpful, courteous, non-intrusive. The room I stayed in was spacious, luxurious and the room service was prompt. I loved the bathroom - sheer luxury with a television in the bathroom mirror, so that I could watch the news whilst brushing my teeth.

title: “Great hotel”
text: This is a very sleek, modern hotel. Kimpton generally has quality properties, this is definitely in that mold. Good location in an area of town with many restaurants and night spots. Close to Michigan for shopping. Overall a great stay.

title: “Fabulous Hotel”
text: This is my 2nd stay with a grandson at NY Palace. It is wonderful. The staff is engaging, very friendly and helpful, and just very lovely. Many have been there for 30 plus years. We had a room looking into the spiers of St. Patrick's Cathedral. Our room was beautiful and very comfortable. The flowers in the lobby were spectacular. I booked on Cyber Monday and had a great rate but received a 48 hour sale from the hotel that was unbelievable and even better! The location is close to every place and there is a car service available. The hotel caters to children and has a fabulous room service menu for children. Everyone there is nice.

title: “Excellet Hotel”
text: I had a weekend get away with my partner on August, 2012. We drove from Santa Fe ,NM to Dallas. I have to say that I was very impressed with this astonishing hotel. The Crescent Court is a beautiful building and stand up from the other ordinary buildings in Downtown Dallas. It's a luxurious property with a wonderful staff.

title: “One of the three most luxurious hotels in Manhattan, stunning views on Central Park and city”
text:
- Service level, facilities and design meet highest standards
- perfect midtown location
- one of the few Manhattan hotels with direct view on Central Park
- Very nice asiatic interior design in the hall and in the rooms
- spacious rooms, very large bathrooms
- all possible room amenities, free wifi
- excellent room service
- attentive front desk service
- average swimming pool with nice view on city
- Negative: bar and part of the restaurant with clinical ambience, like a train station

title: “Clean, safe, friendly & good location”
text: My spouse and 2 teens (16 & 19) stayed at this hotel for 3 nights during the Thanksgiving holiday while in San Diego for the Nomads soccer tournament. We booked the family suite (King + bunk beds + sofa bed) which is oversized, well furnished and very spacious. Arrived in late afternoon to a polite greeting at check-in which was quick and efficient. Room was well-appointed with microwave, fridge, coffee maker, and flat screen TV with a small but very functional work desk with electrical outlets in a fixture on the top of the desk so I didn't have to crawl beneath it to plug in laptop, phone chargers, or iPod. All the beds were reasonably comfortable as were the pillows. Due to the soccer game schedule, we did not have time to sample the free continental breakfast. Plenty of free parking between the "courtyard" lot surrounding the pool/spa and the overflow spaces next to the hotel. Location was just off I-5 and within walking distance (across freeway overpass) to Mission Bay Park. Again, due to soccer schedule we needed a late checkout and the front desk person was more than accommodating - even though I was not sure we would need the extra night I had reserved - I was allowed to keep the room until we found out if we would need to stay the extra night, which as it turned out, we did not need and were not charged for it. The housekeeping and maintenance staff were as friendly and efficient as the front desk and management folks. The only "negative" that I can recall was the flush toilet in the bathroom was loud, but apparently it wasn't loud enough to wake anyone during the night. I would not hesitate to stay at this property again and can recommend it to anyone looking for a clean, safe, accommodating place to stay in mid-San Diego that won't "blow up" the wallet.

title: “One of the Best Hotels in Boston”
text: I stayed at Hotel Commonwealth for a few days leading up to the Memorial Day weekend in 2011. Prior to our arrival a reservation agent, Emily Cormier, was kind enough to e-mail a map of the subway system for our convenience. Upon our arrival, we had an excellent experience with the hotel staff. We arrived around 11pm and were promptly greeted and offered bottled water. We stayed in a deluxe queen room with a Fenway Park view. The room was clean and very spacious. There was free high speed internet which definitely was a bonus. The bathroom was well apportioned. The location of the hotel is ideal. You're within walking distance of Fenway Park, Prudential Center, and other sites. Plus, Kenmore station is adjacent to the hotel which is very convenient for traveling throughout Boston. The hotel restaurants were fabulous. The Eastern Standard's breakfast is a good option. Also, you want to have at least one meal at the Island Creek Oyster Bar. The service there was first rate. Hotel Commonwealth is a great option if you are visiting Boston.

title: “New Old Luxury Lodging”
text:
The Monaco is a newly-opend hotel in a historic downtown building. This means the layout is a bit funky, but the rooms are large, the walls solid and the sleeping quiet. There is a happening rooftop bar (replete with short-skirted gals and slicked-up dudes waiting at the velvet rope), but its noise and hip happenings didn't disrupt my business weekend stay. Staff were notably friendly and helpful.
Great location- close to attractions, eating, bars and public transport. The K
Would I return? You bet!

title: “Awesome!”
text:
Great location, and great service.
This small boutique hotel was quite quaint! It is located right in the heart of Union Square with all the shopping you could want. I was there on business and it was a quick 10 minute walk to the financial district. 
Perks
Complimentary Breakfast, Wine & Cheese hour, and fresh cookies
Free wifi (for all devices). -I wish though you only had to log in once with your iphone not every time you grabbed your phone)

title: “I was pleasantly surprised by our stay.”
text:
After reading all the bad reviews I was a little nervous about how our stay at the Hyatt would go. I traveled with my daughter and 11 mo. old grandson. We had requested a crib in the room and it was there along with a complimentary travel pack of baby soaps. Check in was smooth and the staff was very friendly and polite. Room was nice and clean. Only time we had a problem with the room being hot was when we forgot to close the drapes and were gone for the better part of the afternoon. Bathroom was small but I don't spend alot of time in the bathroom. Pool is small but we were the only one in it both times and it worked great for what we needed. We did take a stroll around the Compass resturant but didn't have a chance to eat there because of company functions. The manager saw us struggling with a tired baby the one night and wanted to know if he could get us anything, some milk or something. He was very pleasant as was all the wait staff. They were always asking if we needed anything special for the baby. When they found out one of the ladies at our table was a vegetarian they offered to get her a different dinner.
Not much shopping in the area other than the one mall which was mostly souveigners but check out the Oak Creek store the lady there is a sweetheart and lots of local artist pottery and such. Plus if you purchase $35 or more they will ship it for free. Bought myself a beautiful piece and can't wait for it to arrive.
The light rail is easily acessible. Wasn't planning on taking it with luggage and baby but the super shuttle which was really vans didn't want to take us to the hotel as we did not bring the carseat.

title: “If you need to stay in this area,”
text: This is it! Almost perfect accommodations! River view rooms have telescopes!

title: “Best muffins!”
text: The breakfast muffins were wonderful. I was blown away by the chocolate, banana nut and bran muffins. The chef manages to make the muffin tops very crisp but keeps the centers light and fluffy. I couldn't get enough of them! The wait staff in the downstairs restaurant were lots of fun. When I complimented the muffins, they brought the chef out to meet me and he told me how I could make them. That was really nice!

title: “Service made the difference”
text: Stayed overnight while in town for the rock and roll 1/2 marathon. When we checked in our room wasn't quite ready. They offered to hold our bags and then call our cell phone when the room was available to check in, this was a very nice touch. We ended up with a room on the 14th floor looking towards the river. The bed part of the room was a good size and well maintained and clean. The bathroom needed a bit of updating (there was a crack in our sink and tub near the drain) but it was clean. We asked about obtaining hot water before their tea/coffee service began (needing it at 4:30 am before our 6:30 race). They offered a coffee pot for our room so we could prepare the hot water at our leisure. This was awesome and made it so smooth to prepare for our race. We stayed at a sister hotel (Allegro) for the Chicago marathon last year. Although also a nice hotel...this hotel had larger rooms, was more updated, friendlier staff and better sound proofing between rooms). Would be willing to stay at either again but this hotel by far would be our 1st choice by far.

title: “Stay at the Holiday Inn instead..”
text: Not as expected. Dirty rooms, dirty in general. Maid never came in once in 3 days. Had to try 3 different rooms before one was actually suitable. Staff was friendly. Don't bother staying here...there are plenty other big name hotels in the area.

title: “Good value, clean and very convenient”
text: I was a bit worried after reading the mixed revues of this Hotel. If you're looking for 5 star then you're way off. But, if you want somewhere that is in a great location, is clean and has the convenience of free parking, Wi Fi and supermarket right across the road, then this is definitely it. We were travelling with a group of 7 people and everyone enjoyed the relaxed nature of the Hotel, although it could get noisy at times.

title: “Great Hotel, frIendly, clean and well worth the money!”
text: I stayed for a week with my teenage daughter. We were concerned being to females staying across country, the staff was nice, the rooms were spacious and clean. It is a great deal. I would gladly stay there again and recommend it to anyone.

title: “Just doesn't quite make it”
text:
I agree with some of the other reviewers that suggest that you won't hate this hotel - but doubt you'll love it either. Perhaps we got off to a bad start as despite being a member of their loyalty program and entitled to a room upgrade and my only request being for a quiet room we were put in a room on a low floor on the busy street side - we had a terrible night with the noise - it was almost as if the window was open. That said the next day the staff handled our request for a quieter room (on the back side of the hotel) well and I would recommend you push this point if you don't like a noisy room. The rooms are adequate if a little small and a bit tired and the whole place has a dated feel to it. Thankfully we managed to book a deal that reduced the onsite parking to half price of $19 a day but at $38 it could be a factor for some.
We had 2 rooms and had an incident where we came home in the late afternoon to one of our rooms being unlocked, with the door catch propping it open. The manager was most apologetic but it could have been a real issue if someone had decided to make their way in there for whatever reason.
On the plus side the staff were helpful, the hotel is well located and we enjoyed our time in the onsite bar that has meals available. Check your invoice though as we were billed for calls we hadn't made. There is also an onsite self serve laundry which was most welcome.
In summary if you get a great deal give it a try - but we'll probably be staying elsewhere next time.

title: “Lovely hotel!”
text: I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Fairmont! It is centrally located to all in Seattle (shopping/arts/port). The service is beyond reproach. I am very surprised it is not a higher rated hotel for Seattle-I would not hesitate to stay here again!

title: “My April R&R”
text: My experience with the Houston Doubletree hotel is more than a casual business, the staff treats me like an extended family. They are all professional and provide a service that I LOVE. Thanks and continue to be Great. - Carl Busby

title: “Great location, great rooms, helpful staff.”
text: Good location for walking to almost anywhere downtown. The room was comfortable and well appointed- loved the bathroom style. I didn't get a chance to partake in the cocktail hour or milk/cookies hour, but both are great touches. The staff was very helpful- from front desk to the bellman. Only complaints... $23 per day for parking seems a bit steep to me. Housekeeping seemed a bit lacking. While the room was clean, I didn't get stay-over service and I stayed two nights. I also visited the bar & wasn't too impressed with the ambiance or service there. Overall & for the price, this hotel is a great place to stay in downtown Denver.

title: “lots of nice touches”
text:
The Casblanca have some terrific staff ,who delivered the best service I think I've probably ever had.
Everyone who raves about the breakfast and all day lounge and 
the evening wine and cheese is absolutely right and the selection is fantastic!.
The decor is eclectic but charming and everything is spotless with high quality goods thoughout.,right down to the soaps,sheets,towels etc.
Its literally about 20 yards from Times Square but once inside it is a haven of peace and tranquility away from the madness that is Times Square
With that said, the wireless internet worked only infrequently when I was there --probably not a problem if you are a tourist but more important if you are there on business as I was.The staff immediately offered to try to fix it (and there is a computer in the Ricks Cafe that guests can use) but they just weren't able to 
The room I had was a little smaller than I would have anticipated from the photos,It was a reasonable size, just not as large as I'd expected. Also It looked over the inner courtyard so was very quiet but basically had no view at all.It's a personal thing I know but I do prefer a room with a view!

title: “Great Place to Stay @”
text:
Front Desk Is very friendly and The place looks great.
I will Stay here every time I come to Fort Worth.

title: “Great location and patio”
text:
I stayed at this hotel in October and got lucky with the weather. It was sunny for most of my stay. As a result, I was able to take advantage of the fifth floor terrace overlooking the bay. I loved this feature of the hotel.
The hotel is located across the street from the Pike Place Market so it's ideal for tourists. The downtown business district is an easy 5 or 6 block walk. The Inn is a smaller hotel that has been well maintained but shows its age a bit. All staff that I encountered were very friendly and helpful. The hotel is well suited for both business travellers and leisure travellers, including families.
I booked a water view room which was quite large with fantastic views. The small sitting area in front of the windows was very nice. The bathroom was also decent size. I agree with the others who have stated that the mattresses are a bit uncomfortable. My room was on the fourth floor. I would stay at this hotel again but I would request a room on a higher floor as I experienced some eye opening late night noise from the courtyard below.

title: “Paper Thin Walls, but Great Staff & Location”
text:
The location of this hotel is perfect (26th St. & close to 7th Ave.). The rooms were spacious, clean and in great condition. The front desk staff, housekeeping and bellman were outstanding. I mention only them as they were the only people we encountered. 
Our rooom was on the 20th floor and I must mention that the walls were paper thin. We could hear everything in the rooms next to us. I say that because the first evening at around 12:15am our 'neighbors' were having sex on and off for about two hours. Good for them, but I really don't want to hear it. 
Of all the hotels I have stayed at in the US and abroad I have never experienced a room where you can hear everything that your neighbors are doing - earplugs would not have helped. Due to the thin walls I would not stay at this hotel or recommend staying here.

title: “Worst stay ever”
text: The room I had was nice since I was a suite with great views but the noise was unbearable! This noise was 24 hours and the hotel reservation had not warned me about this!!! I was not sure where they were located and I show up at a hotel across the street from the world trade center where construction goes on 24 hours. The front desk did not care and I was not able to sleep with ear plugs as they suggested. This seems like a nice property otherwise but the noise is truly unbearable and the fact that I was not warned makes me quite angry .

title: “Very impressive - a memorable stay”
text:
Reading through previous reviews on TA alerted us to the Maxwell Hotel, which we selected for our 4-night stay on the basis of the many favourable recommendations. No problems finding the hotel by car, although you must follow the driving instructions from I5 on the hotel website precisely as there are many one-way streets in the area.
We had been a bit concerned about limited parking spaces based on previous reports, but we needn'y have worried. The (free) underground car park has (approx) 50-60 spaces so there was never any problem getting a space during our stay. Yes the spaces are narrow by US standards, but we had no problem reversing our full-size rental car into a space. 
The large lobby of the hotel is very strikingly decorated, with lots of bright colours and looks very stylish. There are lots of chairs and tables, but as there's no bar, there was no particular reason to provide so much furniture in this area. Check-in was fine and the receptionists were very helpful and friendly - really making us feel welcome after a long flight.
Our standard "Queen Aria" room was more than adequate for our needs, and was like the rest of the hotel, absolutely spotless and new looking with very attractive furnishings and decor. We also liked the little touches such as the popcorn and the microwave. The bed was extremely comfortable and we slept fine despite some jetlag.
The hotel has a free business centre with 2 PC's plus printer, which was extremely useful for making travel bookings and last minute research on things to see - a really helpful facility that all hotels should have.
The local area is very quiet (in a good way), but well located for easy access to I5, and on foot to the Space Needle/monorail. There is a (limited) selection of about 7 or 8 restaurants/cafes in the area plus some fast food places, mainly about 4 blocks to the west, so within about 10 minutes walk. There's also a Thai restaurant right next door to the hotel which was pleasant enough on a rainy evening. As the hotel building is still very new, there are some unopened retail/restaurant units on the ground floor facing the street, so maybe one day there will be more dining choices on the doorstep.
We would definitely recommend the Maxwell Hotel and hope to visit again one day.

title: “Pretty nice!”
text:
We stayed at the Omni Houston for a cousin's bat mitzvah. I've never stayed at an Omni before, but the accomodations were quite nice. Clean, comfortable bedroom, convenient to the freeway, free parking down the street, free wireless in the lobby, and free wireless in the rooms if you join their (free) loyalty program. (If you don't, wireless in the rooms is a whopping $9.95/24 hours, which is plenty of impetus to join their program all on its own.) The staff was friendly and helpful.
One small suggestion that I would have for improvement would save the hotel money as well: Every time we left the room, we made sure to turn the lights in the room off. When we returned on at least one occasion, a light in the room was back on. While it's entirely reasonable for the staff to turn on the lights to perform room cleaning chores, it's a needless waste of electricity to have a lamp on for some unknown number of hours between when they do their work and when we return.
On a separate note, I can't exactly blame the hotel for having drunk wedding guests returning to their rooms on our hall at 3:30 AM and talking loudly outside our door for several minutes, but it would be nice for the rooms to be a bit more soundproofed from the hall.

title: “What a GREAT experience!”
text: Our trip to San Diego was abolutely fabulous and a great deal of that was due to the first person we met there. Jesse Melton, driver, bell-hop, all round super employee made our stay in San Diego one to remember. He sincerely took the time to listen to our questions and issues and solved them! He was extremely congenial and well mannered, well versed on his city and did a fantastic job of making us feel appreciated and welcome in San Diego. Every city should have people like Jesse working for them. The WORLD would be a much better place! Thank you!

title: “SPLENDID!”
text: My wife and I celebrated our birthdays (5/16 and 17th) at F26 an we had a fabulous time. The staff was very courteous. We enjoyed our stay very much! 2 Thumbs UP!

title: “Americas Best Value Inn Terrible”
text:
We were driving down from up north to Florida for a cruise and needed a place to stay just for the night. We found every hotel to be booked during St Patricks Day and this was our only option.
The place was nasty, filthy and old. Walls crumbling, paint peeling, and the place smelled. 
We double checked to make sure that we did not see any bugs (roaches or bed bugs) because we noticed some mattresses sitting outside by the dumpster. Thank goodness we did not find any. There were tons of huge gnats though. The beds were hard but despite the activities going on in the area we managed to sleep (not sure if we were just so tired after driving all day or what).
I would not recommend this place to anyone.

title: “This is a business hotel, not a luxury...”
text: This is a business hotel, not a luxury experience. The service is unpolished and the food is terrible. The pool is small and shabby. There are so many nicer places to stay in LA--and so many less expensive hotels in downtown LA.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: We stayed here for one night while visiting family in Jacksonville. Check-in was fast and easy. All the hotel staff were very friendly and helpful. The hotel is located on the Mayo Clinic property inside the gate. Our GPS kept trying to take us somewhere else. The room was clean and had a flat screen TV. They only have wired internet in the room so my tablet PC didn't work. For wireless you have to go to the lobby. This was disappointing. No complementary breakfast but they have free coffee in the lobby. They have a cafe in the lobby but it is a little pricey. Jacksonville Town Center is about 5 miles from the hotel. This a a huge outdoor mall that has just about whatever you're looking for and lots of restaurants. Very nice hotel, would stay here again.

title: “Best hotel”
text: This is our second time at this Ritz and just like the first time, it is wonderful, we love everything about this hotel, they sent an amazing cake,with a card from management when we told them it was my birthday...
