Very comfortable bed,shower/ bath is great,wife got a facial they,gave us late check out and I got a complimentary pass to the spa.

title: “Great hotel in fantastic location.”
text:
Spent 6 nights at the Salisbury mid November.I agree with some of the other reviews that reception staff are not overly friendly.For example when my daughter and I arrived from Australia my sister had already checked in as she had an enviously much shorter journey.After travelling for 30 hours and excited by my first trip to New york I expected a bit more than " the room number is "etc.There were none of the usual pleasantries and the same on departure.Just''Thank you "after handing back the receipt. Mind you I'm usually irritated by the gushing "How are you " ,"have a nice day" carry on so maybe I am just joining the grumpy old women brigade..Having said that Anthony who I encountered at reception during my stay was very helpful when organising a tour.The rooms was very nice ,[we had a 1 bedroom suite] ,and was very spacious. The wardrobe space was huge.
The beds were very comfortable apart from the sofa bed that my daughter [ age 17] slept on.You could feel the springs through the mattress.
Breakfast was very good value.Yes there is an ample supply of fluorescent pink doughnuts as other reviewers have mentioned but if you look carefully ,between the pastries and cereals you will spot a bowl of fruit salad cowering in the corner , so not as unhealthy as others have suggested.
I have to say 10 out of 10 to the maid service.Our room was spotless every day.Please leave them a good tip.
We were on the 12th floor at the front and didn't encounter much noise unlike other reviewers.
Great spot with easy walking distance to times square and central park {only two blocks away].
Good limo service back to airport arranged by hotel $60 inc tip etc.
Concierge helpful.
Very nice pizza at Angelo's next door.
Overall I would definately stay here again.Can't imagine you would find better for the price.

title: “You pay for what you get”
text: We got a cheap deal on this hotel and got what we paid for. The rooms were big and bed comfy but our window looked directly into an office block, if I opend my window I could have used the PC in their office they were so close, so we couldn't open our blinds at all mid week. The hotel was cleanish but we did not get our room cleaned everyday or our bed made. There is no concierge and the staff are uninterested in you, nothing personal about this hotel. It's a good location and near the metro. I wouldn't stay here again, Dupont Cirlce is not far and more fun area. Our room was next to the store cupboard and we certainly knew it!

title: “Nice hotel with a little flaws..”
text: The fairmont is a nice grand hotel with lovely features, the room was comfortable and nicely furnished, however the bathroom was small and a bit neglected. The location is ok if you catch a taxi or the cable cars. Overall we enjoyed our 4 night stay here.

title: “Rooms are plain but clean”
text:
The hotel is plain but the rooms are big and clean and the price are low comparing with the other hotels in Boston. 
The location too is perfect, near the Prudential Center.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
This Hotel was nice and clean and as long as you have a car is in a good location for Sea World, the Airport and the beach. Quite a way into city itself though.
The Hotel has 2 resident rescued Seals which is a lovely touch and our room was nice and spacious with a great view over the beach.
Only criticism was that the Air con was too noisy so could not have it on and watch TV or sleep. We slept with the balcony doors open which was OK as it was very quiet and we were on the first floor so felt safe.

title: “Excellent location, very comfortable hotel”
text: We stayed 3 nights. Very clean hotel, staff very courteous. Small lobby but very luxurious, great atmosphere. Hallways were clean and so was the room. We stayed on the 12th floor which helped with all the honking from the streets. Flat screen TV with full on satellite, extremely comfortable duvets and pillows. Cordless phone, ipod docking station, spacious bathroom. Free internet. My only complaint would be the Air conditioning unit. We had two double beds which one was right beside the A/C. It would run on and off throughout the night, made quite a bit of noise and shot out cold air on the closest bed. But wouldn't stop me from coming back! Location is AMAZING. Minutes from Times Square and 5th Ave.

title: “a elegant paradise”
text: Had a fabulous time at the w hotel with my wife. We had cocktails at the oasis bar and the bartender maryanne was a pleasure to be around. I would highly rate the hotel and service to anyone visiting the new york area!

title: “Great Location and Value”
text: Stayed at the Best Western Bayside pre-cruise. Handy location within easy walking distance to waterfront in safe neighbourhood. Shuttle picked up at airport as well as dropping us off at the cruise ship pier the next morning. Had bay view room on 10th floor ... nice and quiet as well. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great location”
text:
We have just stayed at the Affinia Dumont with a 9 month old baby and the hotel was great. We had to pay more to get a room with a microwave and hob to make and warm milk and baby food, but it was worth the extra. We had a big spacious lounge with small kitchen area plus a large bedroom. 
The location is perfect. With a buggy it's not easy to jump in a cab or on the subway, but we were able to walk pretty much everywhere we wanted to go. 
My only complaint about the hotel would be that it didn't have a bar onsite to have a drink. There was a restaurant attached to the hotel where we could get breakfast dinner or room service, but we would have liked a hotel bar. 
All in all- a great hotel.

title: “great location, great hotel - almost perfect”
text:
Stayed in the Towers section.
Unbeatable location. 50th and madison right behind st patricks cathedral.
absolutely excellent for walking to all major sights , times sq, 5th ave, museums restaurants etc. 
great views from the towers floors with excellent service. 
Very nice towers lounge although it seems a bit silly that you have to ride elevators all the way down to the 8th floor and then up again to the 39th floor on a different set of elevators. (they could have made a stair from 40th (the lowest towers floor) to 39th where the lounge is)
The lounge btw has great food incl breakfast. 
wonderful beds btw, just a bit silly that they were unable to confirm twin beds, which meant that 2 of our party had to share a king - in spite of having requested twin beds 4 months before when we booked the room - that is NOT 5 star service.

title: “CONVENTION OK,NOT VACATION”
text:
I just finished a 4 day stay for a business conference in Boston, where I traveled alone. 
Good: Loved,loved,loved the mirrors in the bathroom. The light goes completely around the mirror, so you don't have those hideous overhead shadows making you look like a ghoul! Ditto for the makeup mirror...such clarity! Loved the smell upon arrival, very clean and relaxing. In-room Starbucks coffee a plus, as was the nice comfy bathrobe (once I got it, see below). The lobby is spacious and calming as well, especially at night. I used the fitness center daily...loved the individual TV screens on the equipment!
Bad: Rude employees at Starbucks and the hotel giftshop! They did not greet me, nor was there a 'thank you!." In fact, the clerk never said a word during an entire transaction in the gift shop!! There is only one restaurant, which is OK, but overpriced. There are NO restaurants close by, so I hope your convention includes meals! Our conference did include meals, which were exceptionally good. The pool is to small for anything other than splashing around. My television recieved few channels, more news and sports than anything else. What I really wanted was nice background music, and all I had to choose from was a small bedside radio which was mostly static. I had to call for my 'complementary robe" that I found I was supposed to have from the note on the (empty) hangar on the back of my bath door. But the worst part about the stay was THE NOISE from the hallway!!! Unless you take great care in closing the door manually, they SLAM! And ANYONE talking in a normal voice in the hall is completely heard inside the room. No spa service, but the concierge told me I could have an In-room massage for $135.
Bottom line: if your conference is here, OK, but know you'll have to take a taxi for anything not provided by your conference. Also, bring earplugs or white noise to block the INSIDE NOISE.

title: “Southern Hospitality in NYC!”
text:
My husband and I were in New York in June for an overnight stay. Before going, I searched for days to find something affordable and something that would meet my standards. I'm from the south, and I am very picky about the size, the cleanliness, and the friendliness of a hotel and its staff. This is how we live and how we vacation, so let me just say that I was simply stunned with the service I received at the Fitzpatric Grand Central. 
The room was $199 per night but upon entering the hotel, of course it didn't look like anything great. The outside was nothing fancy. The lobby was very small, and we had to go over and sit down at a desk to check in. I thought, "Oh no - what have I done?" Neverthess, the people were so friendly and the rooms were small but had a cozy atomosphere. My husband and I agreed that we had never stayed in hotel room that was cleaner and more well kept.
Finally, the location is great! Our son is an attorney and works downtown Manhattan. He was able to walk over for lunch and walk back to work. We were able to move around and find what we needed on our own. I would stay here again!

title: “Great location! Good service but no free internet.”
text: Out of the 8 different hotels I stayed over the last 3 weeks this one was the most expensive one but the only one that did not provide free internet, pretty disappointing considering the hotel rate, it should be complementary. In addition the bathroom supplies were limited compared to what hotels in Asia provide.

title: “Nice Stay Great for the Kids”
text:
We stayed at Paradise Point in June 2006 with the family - 2 kids. The price was expensive $200 per night for a garden villa, which pretty much looked on to the road. The rooms we lovely and clean, beds were very comfy. The annoying thing is that the block out curtains only cover the window and not the door, so the room gets bright when the sun comes up . We used the towels from the pool to cover the door, and it worked a treat. The room we stayed are able to be interconnected and the sound does travel. It did not bother us, but it may affect light sleepers. Plus it is a real rip off for parking at $20 per night.
The kids loved staying here, breakfast was expensive but nice. The kids loved to look in the rockpool and look at all the fish swimming in it. The pools are fantastic. My kids swam here pretty much all day, and there is sand on the side of the pool, excellend for sand playing. It was wonderful to sit back, relax, watch the kids swim and sip on a (expensive) cocktail. On the downside, during peak summer periods they need to regularly clean the toilets as they get very wet, sandy and slippery. Not a nice combination. 
On the weekends in summer they have movie night at the pool, which my daughter just loved.
Overall we had a wonderful relaxing stay, with resort prices. Perfect for kids during summer. I recommend to save your money and get a garden room instead of a bay view. You will be pretty much in the pool, not in the bay. Try and get out and eat at the local restaurants, as the resort is expensive. Unos pizza at Mission Beach fantastic and great for the kids.

title: “Great location”
text: This hotel is centrally located and makes it very easy to get around the city. It is very close to the pier and cable cars. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The bathroom in our room was a bit awkward as the door opened into the room. There was also no ventilation in the bathroom which made it difficult to use after a shower. There are lots of places to eat in the area (Scoma, Ghirardelli, great happy hour at the hotel bar).

title: “Comfortable hotel for quick business trip”
text:
This hotel was comfortable, clean and modern and suited me just fine for a quick business trip. It's right near a main freeway so very accessible. All of the staff I encountered during my stay were very pleasant. 
I was surprised I had to pay for internet. These days I would assume that wifi is free for a hotel stay.

title: “Mixed emotions”
text:
I stayed in the Hotel Azure for 4 nights in mid October. The hotel had only been open a few weeks, so it's understandable they would still have some kinks to work out. But if a hotel isn't running up to full speed due to just opening, they shouldn't charge full price for their rooms. 
First, the positive: the staff is friendly, and the rooms are nice. Beautiful bathrooms with great showers. Comfy beds.
But...the location leaves a lot to be desired. Canal Street/ Chinatown can be a total nightmare with crowds (even by Manhattan standards) and it can take 5 minutes to walk 50 feet to the subway entrance because sidewalks are literally at an impass. Between traffic and constant blaring horns, and my bed shaking everytime the subway ran under the building, it's not exactly the most restful location to stay. I'm not new to Manhattan either, so I expect crowds and noise, but this was a little ridiculous.
Also, I didn't have a TV for the whole time I was there, despite telling the front desk twice. They were replacing the satellite dishes at the time, so people were in and out of my room on multiple occasions; to remove the old dish, to replace it with the new one, to get the old remote, to replace it with a new one. Not a big deal, but it seemed like everytime I laid down to take a nap, someone was knocking on my door to come in. Annoying. 
Bottom line: wanted to like this place, but definitely wouldn't stay here again.

title: “Cool in SoHo”
text:
This is definitely a cool hotel. I stayed in a deluxe room which was big enough (for NYC). The design is very elegant and the room I had had views over midtown and east river - "shockingly" good. Negatives? The AirCon is surprisingly loud. 
The cafe/restaurant downstairs is very, very good. It has a glass ceiling and the layout is fantastic. It seems to be a place where "in" people meet - but was never too crowded.

title: “We will be back!”
text: We own a small retail business in the midwest and work long hours six days a week. The Island Palms was exactly what we needed. It is in a beautiful location. Our quiet, comfy second floor room in the newest building was excellent! Our deck had a view of the bay and a friendly hummingbird breakfasting in the bloom of a large Bird of Paradise plant. Great food in the restaurant and very helpful people in the lounge and front desk. Love the sunrise!

title: “Great Location & Comfortable”
text:
I was in NYC on company business from Nov 15-17. Found out I was going only the week before and our usual hotel was booked. The minute I found out I was staying at this hotel, I got on 'Trip Advisor'.
I was comfortable with the mostly favorable reviews and most were dead-on correct.
The staff was helpful (asked me if I would like a "car" to the airport instead of a taxi and had one there in 15 minutes).
The elevators are small and slow but it is an old building. The rooms are small but clean and comfortable and no bugs! Good size TV with remote. The bathroom was small and had an issue with water damage in the ceiling at one time but was clean and had good water pressure. By the way, I had to step up to get into the bathroom. Tripped on it twice till I got used to it! Don't know if every bathroom has a step but my 10th floor room did.
Overall, a nice place to stay. Not nearly as expensive as most other big NYC hotels. Nice business/residential community. A 10 minute walk to the Empire State Building and just a couple blocks to the #6 subway.
Also, if you want a nice place to eat, try Penelope's. It is literally across the street! Turn left out of the hotel and it's right across the street on the corner!).
Email me with questions.

title: “Sad to say...”
text:
We've stayed at The Muse numerous times over the past four years, and I'm sad to say that our last visit was disappointing.
The hotel is lovely, and the rooms are comfy- but there's something missing since Kimpton took over.
We checked in on Friday, and had nightly turndown service until Wednesday. Then this lovely touch was discontinued with no notification on the part of the hotel staff.
On previous trips the turndown service included pillow treats, which my husband looked forward to. We received a 'treat' on the first night of our stay because of my Kimpton membership. After that it was just turndown. We're afraid that the evening housekeeper had been terminated because Kimpton didn't want to keep up the turndown tradition. When we asked about the service, the staffer at the desk spoke to us like we were morons.
In the bathroom was a 'convenience' menu of items that could be picked up at the front desk if you'd left yours at home. I sent my husband down to the desk for an item, and they didn't have any- and hadn't for a few days.
Suffice it to say, that with the rates going up considerably and the congeniality and courtesy of certain staff members going down- we're looking around for another hotel to call 'home' on our trips.
Kimpton will be doing a renovation of The Muse, which will include removal of the lovely ladies on the ceiling of the lobby.
Before our July trip, we would have given this hotel not only an 'Excellent" but would have raised it to 'Outstanding". Now it's above average, for the comfort of the rooms.

title: “Smallish room, but overall good stay”
text: Room had two beds and was VERY cramped, but that's to be expected in NYC. Staff was very nice, and everyone I encountered was extremely helpful. Room cleanliness ( deep cleaning) left a bit to be desired....dusty wallpaper above bed, and grime in corners of bathroom....but honestly overall it wasn't a big deal. Bed was comfy, nice big flat screen TV, free wi-fi, and walk able to great dining.

title: “Awesome, we will be back”
text: We stayed here for the National Powwow at Danville and found the staff rooms etc. to be great especially the staff who were very helpful, even found a Swiss to American plug for me. Breakfast was fabulous. Would recommend this hotel without hesitation. What made a good hotel great was the staff. If the manager reads this give your staff a raise.

title: “Excellent Boston Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Colonnade last month, and were extremely pleased with this hotel. The room was spacious and nicely appointed, and was clean and comfortable. We asked for and received a room on an upper floor that was in the back and therefore sheltered from the sounds of the street. I appreciated that they did not have one of those awful computerized minibars - that enabled us to store some OJ for the morning.
We liked the location of the hotel, which was right across the street from the Prudential Center, providing easy access for shopping and dining. A subway stop was just outside the entrance of the hotel - most convenient.
The staff is friendly and professional and works hard to please.
On future trips to the Boston area we hope to once again stay at the Colonnade.

title: “Hotel is new clean and functional but right across from Port Authority”
text: The location was my wife's only complaint, but she will not stay there again. Distrikt is in a building with three or four other new hotels, so there seems to be a demand for such a location. If you don't mind being on a side street next to a busy bus station, you probably couldn't do better than Distrikt. Friendly front desk people. Free NY Times in the AM. New and spiffy. Nice bedding, towels, and so on.

title: “Will definitely stay here again!”
text:
Our family of 5 loved this hotel - the decor, the amazing view from our room, the location. We arrived a couple of hours before check-in but they graciously had a room ready for us within minutes. Our teenage boys were quite impressed - as were we - with the room and the view of the harbour. We were within walking distance of North end but also very close to T station. And we enjoyed the walk along the wharf. 
Now, as with most Boston hotels, there is charge for internet (we declined as it was a family vacation) and parking (used garage across the street).
There is Starbucks in lobby and person who can assist with directions/ assistance. Very helpful. There was also nice Italian restaurant around the corner, Salvatores. We would definitely stay here again!

title: “Unimpressed!”
text: Extremely small rooms. This is to be expected, but I swear we were in a closet. The water was dripping in the shower. There was no pressure. Lots of construction going on. It was in between at least 3 subway stations, but all were within 20 minutes walking distance. Not so great.

title: “Fantastic!”
text: Fantastic hotel in an excellent location. Three blocks to times square and in a nice safe neighborhood. We stayed for 7 nights and enjoyed every minute of it. Rooms were great, staff were friendly and super helpful we will most definitely be back!

title: “Billing Issues”
text:
As far as the room and location goes, this is a perfectly average hotel. Our room was okay with some nice amenities including a sleep better CD, earplugs, and general tips for a restful night. The area has a number of restaurants and easy access to I-76. 
Check-in and out went smoothly. We booked through a third party service. Thus began a saga that is currently two weeks into being settled. No mention was made of any problems while at the hotel. When I get my credit card statement, I see I was charged a second time for the room even though I had paid the third party directly. I was given some mumbo jumbo about not accepting the voucher from the other company. They had no interest in making it right and told me to take it up with the booking agency.
I have called them and they seem to be able to get it resolved after many phone calls and back and forths with this clueless establishment. So the moral of the story is either book with the hotel directly, or better yet stay somewhere else.

title: “Very good service!”
text: After going to three other hotels as a walk-in, I was finally able to book a room here (the hotel I did have a reservation for was awful~ see my other review). The desk attendant was cheerful and very helpful setting up for the two cars we needed to have stay for three days. The shuttle was prompt and the driver was friendly, but not too friendly. Rooms were nice, we had a view of the airport. The fan in the a/c unit must have drowned out any noise b/c we all slept well. The breakfast was typical fare. Again, the shuttle was prompt. Restaurant right next to hotel offers room service. There is also a brand new Subway and liquor store within short walking distance. I would stay here again and recommend it to friends needing stay/park/fly in and out of Seatac.

title: “Great hotel for the price & location”
text: We stayed at this hotel for the weekend in January. We had a brand new very recently renovated room on the 18th Floor. The carpet even still smelled new. I'm not sure if they are going floor by floor, or the whole thing is already done, but if you're going I would request a renovated room. The rooms are decent size for NYC, and the beds comfortable. Brand new shower and sink in the bathroom. Only negative is the bathroom has a sliding door so you can pretty much see right in the bathroom, but it's not that big of deal. We had new carpet, tv and furniture. It was a great deal for the location, just 2 blocks south of Times Square. Subway station is on the corner and cabs are very accessible in the area. There is a restaurant in the lobby that offers breakfast, and several diners nearby if you'd prefer that. I would definitely stay again!

title: “Just based on reservation service, did not stay”
text:
I attempted to work with a reservation for several rooms for business purposes. The system was slow and archaic and I never received confirmations. Phone reservation service was unhelpful and somewhat aloof as well. Ultimately I was unable to make changes to my reservations through the system, and even the cancellation was difficult, with the Fairmont server having problems.
The system is not 2012, and surely not up to state of the art Seattle standards (as one who is living in Seattle).

title: “The Best for the Money”
text:
The Silver Cloud Inn is not fancy, but it's about the best deal you'll find in Seattle proper. It's located along a bus and trolly line, easy driving distance to the UW (if you know your way), Fred H., and downtown. It's also an easy drive to Magnolia, Queen Anne, and Fremont. 
My room was clean and quiet, although I didn't have a view. I had a shower and a bathtub, although the bathtub was in the room with the beds (it was a jacuzzi). Aveda soaps . . .non smoking, comfortable bed, free HBO, quick elevators.
Parking was great. I traveled along and did not feel afraid to park in the garage. I never struggled to find a spot. I used my room key to get into the locked and lighted garage. 
Free breakfasts are okay, not great. Lots of carbs, powdered scrambled eggs (that tasted fine to me), some meats, toast, bagels, muffins, milk, juice, tea and coffee. There were also a few waffle makers. Very few fruits. Cereals. 
There is a workout room that was adequate. I used an elliptical type machine without any problems. Clean and safe. The music was blaring but I was able to find the control and turn it down. 
Quick check in and check out. I highly recommend this hotel if you're not looking for luxury.

title: “Boutique hotel plus!”
text: We've stayed at Morgans many times and each time I've thought about writing a review, but other issues intervened; however, this is the time to say that Morgans is a wonderful boutique hotel without the "attitude" one has to endure in so-called boutique hotels. The staff, from the doorman to reception to room service to housekeeping, is uniformly courteous, attentive, and always willing to accommodate whatever needs one may have. Apart from that, the mid-town location is ideal and the hotel has a very chic ambience and decor thanks to the brilliant vision of the French designer Andree Putman. If you need a hotel in Manhattan and you want great service amenities, you could not do better than to treat yourself to a stay at Morgans.

title: “Location. Location. Location.”
text: Not the fanciest or best appointed hotel in midtown, The Millennium's great location makes it a venue to which we return frequently when in NYC on theater weekends. Especially with NYC taxi availability and service so awful (not just this reviewer's opinion--ask the hotel employees who try to flag down cabs for their customers), being able to walk to every Broadway Theater in a matter of minutes and having decent restaurants just slightly farther away makes this location worth the stay. Also, you can get decent prices. They should get Wifi throughout the Hotel and some of the plumbing needs work, for example.

title: “A Good for the Money Hotel, but......”
text:
Typical Double Tree Hotel. Comfortable, quiet, nice clean rooms. The restaurant wasn't bad and a decent value for the money. My one issue with this hotel was the onsite gift shop.
Charging someone $2.50 for a small bag of chips or 3.99 for popcorn that can be purchased for .99 at any convenience store is complete rip off and kind of ruins the the positive experience of staying at the hotel. I realize the gift shop is not part of the hotel, but not all guests realize that. Also, having some smart a$$ rude lady working there doesn't help matters either. My advice to the hotel, have these clowns get real with their prices or don't renew their lease. They really give an otherwise nice hotel a bad rap.

title: “Location not everything”
text:
6 Columbus is a fantastic location if you wish to be near Columbus Circle and the lower part of the Upper West Side. But that is the only positive thing I can say about this hotel.
My wife and I stayed at the hotel for two nights in mid September. I am amazed that there are positive reviews on Tripadvisor. It does seem that the hotel draws either very positive or very negative reviews. My view is firmly negative.
The hotel is in an old building - presumably a converted old hotel. It should not be considered a new hotel. Thompson seem to have kept all of the narrow corridors and small spaces. It reminded me of the inside of a two star hotel in Paris. Poorly laid out and cramped. There is one normal size lift and then a tiny lift the size of a cupboard. The colors are all dark and the place looks rather cheap.
We stayed in a king room the room was still very small - even by New York standards. There was no where to put the luggage bags and the only seat faced the door to the room. You could walk around the bed but there was no other space. The bathroom was very small and the shower was in the bath. The bath has to be the narrowest bath I have ever seen and it was an effort to not continuously stand on the plug. The bath was no narrow that your feet were partly on the curved sides.
We woke up one morning to no running water in the room. Apparently there were water pressure problems on the upper floors. It was fixed a few hours later. But I think it shows the limited job which has been done by Thompson to create this hotel.
The bed was comfortable - nice linen.
There was only a curtain across the window - no sheer, so you had to have the room in darkness or the people in the adjacent building could see in.
The room was poorly appointed. The only toiletries were soap and shampoo. No conditioner or body lotion. No ironing board. my wife could not believe the tiny hair dryer.
Our room seemed tired even though the hotel is new. It did not appear to be particularly clean. There were several marks on the furniture and one light bulb was out. The air conditioning was very noisy.
When I checked out I had to ask if the desk person was going to ask how my stay was. She seemed surprised when I told her how disappointing it was. 
I have stayed in other boutique New York hotels like The London and The Crosby Street hotel and 6 Columbus is a poor comparison. It is not worth $400 per night. It's rooms are tiny and the building is cramped. I would not recommend it. In hindsight, I should have more carefully looked at the website photos - tiny rooms with basic furnishings and a tiny lobby. Not good signs.

title: “Great Riverwalk Destination”
text:
We are big fans of the Omni Hotel chain and try and stay at one whenever we can. The hotel is historic, beautiful, romantic and right on the famous Riverwalk. We had our dog with us so they put us on the first floor...not where I would normally want to be but its there rule. We were given a very nice room that the pitio doors opened up right into the pool. The weather wasnt exactly made for lounging at the pool while we were there but it was nice to open the doors and sit outside in the late evening and ealry morning with coffee.
The check in staff and concierge were outstanding as usual for an Omni property. Checking in the gentleman was fast and very nice to deal with. We used the concierge to ask about restaurants and a ghost tour...again he went out of his way to help us.
The one problem, whuich to me was kind of a big one and kept this hotel for getting that fifth star was the valets. We chose not to use the $32.00 per night valet parking and elected to park in the public garage that is directly and I mean directly across the street from the hotel, its only $11.00 per day. We pulled under their very large parking area (I stress very large because you need to know we were not impeding and flow of traffic or taking up a valuable spot) Plus even if we were that what this area is for! Anyway as soon as these bozos found out were werent valeting thet because absoultly rude. There was no less than a dozen wheeled luggage carts and when I tried to use one they told me we coulnt and they were only for bellmen...whatever. I got our couple of bags to the curb alone and my wife waited till I went and parked. Im really upset that these guys had such a bad attitude...they need to learn from the valets at the main Omni in Houston.
Except for that we had a great time and will probabally go back. We didnt eat at the restaurant on the premises but it did look good and the in houst Starbucks was a convient treat as well.

title: “Nice place to stay”
text: We just returned from six nights at the Castle, and it lived up to all the positive reviews that it received on Trip Advisor. Although it doesn't look like much at first glance, the rooms are very nice, well equipped, and clean. The neighborhood is also quite pleasant, with good dining and shopping nearby. The people who work there are extremely helpful. They really go out of their way to make sure your San Francisco experience is enjoyable.

title: “Nice”
text:
I stayed here for 2 weeks for some work training in Austin. Just like every other Residence Inn, this one was pretty standard fare: 2 large rooms, 2 tv's, free breakfast, etc. I was impressed of the large selection of food at breakfast and its high quality. You could actually sit down for a real breakfast, not just a light snack. The breakfast room attendant was also extremely friendly and went out of his way to make your day. 
 I was also impressed on the housekeepings attention to details such as the "towel bunny" left on my bed and the general cleanliness of the room and hotel. 
 The hotel is a short 15 min drive to Austin, with no traffic, and 10 minutes to the South Congress district. For the room, location and service, I felt that I was getting a bargain for what I paid for, and rank this Residence Inns among the best. 
 Cons: The pool can get noisy sometimes at night, so try and request a room away from the pool, or the backside of the hotel. It closes at 9pm, but can be loud up to that point.

title: “"No to the no, to the hell no".”
text:
I had the pleasure of staying in the La Quinta Inn El Paso Lomaland, 11033 Gateway Blvd West, El Paso, TX 79935 for 5 days. (28 Oct- 2 Nov 2012) I thought that it was a really nice place to stay at for my week of work. I looked at some of the other comments written by some of the customers, and said to myself, "WOW", and I stayed there. However, the so-called breakfast was not what I was used to. The eggs were very, very cold, as though they were done yesterday and put in the frig for in the morning. It was just a "Plain Jane place".
Two thing that upset me was the mail send out system and the false ad they had in my room, " All high dollar items may be kept in the safe in the front office". (Not used to this) So, being nice I go and asked one of the clerk about a drop mailbox, and he should me an open inbox tray on the desk top where he wanted me to drop my mail in. I told him, "No to the no, to the hell no. I'm not doing that". You crazy!" Then I asked him about storing some very important things and to secure some money. He told me that there is no safe here at all for customers. I told him that why do you have that posted in the room if you don't have one inside the room or in the front office. You are false advertising this in the room, and I told him that it needs to come down off the inside door if you seriuosly don't have one. He just looked at me and said nothing. I told him that as a Federal Government Employee, that better come down or I'll address this at a higher level. I never will stay there again for no reason and will tell others to never stay there.

title: “Boutique hotel in great location”
text: My wife and I stayed for 4 nights in mid-September recently. The staff are courteous and helpful and the location is great for shopping along Fifth Ave and Madison Ave and close to Central Park. The E line subway station at 53rd/5th Ave is nearby if you need transport. The room we had was generally quiet with a king-sized bed and a small separate living room (very comfortable for two persons although the living room was a bit too cold to be used much given the weather). The complementary continental breakfast on the second floor was good and a great way to start the day. Excellent experience overall.

title: “Central Location”
text: I recently stayed here for a girl's trip over memorial day, it was centrally located to all the best parts of San Fran and the staff was very helpful and accomodated our special room requests without a hitch! I would highly recommend this hotel for tourists, especially on weekends. Even though the city was busy outside, the rooms were quiet and the beds were so comfortable! A high end hotel for reasonable rates - a great deal all around.

title: “Not a nice hotel...would not recommend”
text:
Although the staff was friendly and helpful,the Days Inn on Sunset Blvd. is not a hotel I would recommend to a friend. The matresses in our room were very hard (I don't mind firm but these were like cement). My son tried to sleep on a roll-a-way bed which was terrible, so he ended up putting the mattress on the floor and sleeping. The bathroom mirror was difficult to use since there was a window in the center of it. I don't expect too much when a hotel says it has a continetal breakfast, but this was not good. Mostly pre-packaged pastries and coffee that was just o.k.
I would have put up with all of this and not written this review, but the thing that bothered me the most was the musty smell in the rooms (we had 2 rooms) and the mold that was around the peeling wallpaper in the bathroom. I ended up with a sore throat because of it, so just wanted to warn anyone who is sensitive to mold to not stay here.

title: “Classy, great location, friendly staff and awesome rooms”
text: Perfect location for shopping, dining and nightlife. Easy access to all of the great forms of public transportation San Francisco has to offer. The concierge is always at the ready to help you get to where you need or wish to be. The prices are excellent, especially when you consider the area. I'm always booked for business, but I can't help but enjoy myself while I'm there.

title: “Above and way beyond”
text: I - and my service dog (hearing) - arrived late last Wednesday for an early business meeting the next day. John, the front desk clerk who checked me in, noted that they had me in an upstairs room which was not exactly the best place for me. Without my asking he said he could change it to a first floor room, possibly closer to the front so I wouldn't have that far to walk for breakfast and to get to my car. In 10 minutes I was set. You have no idea how much that simple kindness meant.

title: “Great location”
text: A great location right above Grand Central station. The lady at check in was extremely nice and helpful. The room looked like it had been recently renovated and it was very nice. It wasn't a huge room but it was perfectly adequate. We did eat in the hotel one evening and the food was excellent.

title: “NICE PLACE / GREAT LOCATION”
text: Sutton Place appears to be fairly new, with large, clean rooms. (Our bathroom had a large tub and separate shower stall.) Staff very friendly. Located at intersection of Rush Street and Bellevue Place - a half dozen or more great restaurants and bars within sight of the hotel (i.e. Gibson's Steakhouse, Lux Bar.) Streets are busy at night with people, but didn't hear a thing inside the room. Just down the block from Lake Michigan, a few blocks to the Red Line subway. Not cheap, but no place was in Chicago - think it was a good value for the money. Would stay again.

title: “Nice hotel!”
text:
This is a nice hotel that I find is suitable only to business travelers. I can’t see any other reason to stay here other than business, as the hotel is located in the nearby of a business park together with several others, and to me this place looks like the middle of nowhere. Nice green areas, but no attractions in the nearby and the closest shopping mall is about 10 USD away by taxi.
Anyway, I come here at least once a year just for work and the Jacksonville Marriott fits perfectly to my needs. As I use it only to wash myself and sleep, I find that rooms are spacious, very comfortable, very clean and equipped with big flat screen TVs. Food is also good and better than other Marriotts I have visited.

title: “Clean, Efficient and Friendly for Work”
text: I stayed 2 nights/3 days for a conference that was in the hotel. I only left the hotel once, but the location was excellent, near plenty of shopping and restaurant options. My room was clean and comfortable, and the bed was very comfortable. I was a little concerned when I read another reviewer's comment that this property was shabby and dated. I think they had the wrong place. My room was very good, as were the floor I stayed on, elevators, public spaces, etc. I was even excited that there were enough convenient, well-located outlets in my room that I was able to charge 4 devices at once. Also the doorman arranged a car to take me to the airport, and it was the same as the cab fare and much less creepy.

title: “A great value. Very nice stay.”
text: A great value. Very nice stay. Quiet and comfy beds. Restaurant is excellent. We will be back.

title: “Great bargain!”
text: We spend 4 nights at the Acme Hotel, and overall had a great stay. The breakfast and free internet were nice extras that we were not expecting. The location can't be beat, and the staff was very helpful in helping us find the most economical and simplest way to where we were going. We even had one staff member who walked us around the corner to point out which way. The room was spotless, and the hardwood floors were a nice touch. My daughter enjoyed the funky little touches in the room, and thought it was "very cool". The only thing that I would recommend updating is the A/C / heat units in the room. I bumped the A/C up a degree, and the heat kicked in and set off the smoke alarm. Rather unnerving!

title: “Some good some bad”
text:
Following a mix-up with our booking on needahotel.com we were given a room in this hotel.
Talk about good luck!
We stayed 12th to 15th June.
On arrival we were told they didn't have the room booked for us and we were moved into a better room, with a riverview, vouchers for the bar and access to the executive lounge on the 34th floor.
The lobby is immense, spotless and VERY busy. Everyone sitting in the area seemed to be working on laptops.
Check in was very smooth and quick.
The room was bigger than the average hotel room and certainly the biggest we've had in the USA.
A little off-putting is that they look for almost $8 for a litre of water. I didn't dare look at the prices for the mini-bar!
In terms of cleanliness it's impossible to fault the hotel or the rooms.
The executive lounge is lovely and the range of pastries available each morning is great.
While the use of the gym was extra, the pool is free to use. That said, the pool is pretty small and both times I went to use it, it was full of kids who seemed to be unsupervised. This made it impossible to actually swim. I'd strongly recommend that this is something the management look at.
The location of the hotel is great. It's just off Michegan Avenue and most of the places you'd want to see are in walking distance.
Would stay here again, but wouldn't be paying the rack rates!

title: “Langham hotel in july”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights in July. As we are a family of four (inc 2 children) we booked a suite with 2 double beds. The first mistake was assuming that "double" meant "queen" - probably our mistake but other guests should bear this in mind as the beds were small.
We arrived at around 3pm as check-in is stated as "from 3pm". This was another mistake as check-in is at the discretion of the hotel from 3pm rather than meaning that the rooms are ready after 3pm. We stood in a long queue with other guests facing the same problem. The whole check-in became a sorry draw-out joke. The desk manager promised that the hotel manager would contact me once I complained but I never heard anything. I mentioned this when I checked out and again was told that the hotel manager would email me (which never happened).
The pool was good and my children enjoyed that.
The restaurant staff were very helpful and made alterations to the menu to accomodate my children. However, the food was expensive.
The conceige was helpful but seemed busy quite often. The staff who carried our luggage were friendly and prompt.

title: “Could not have asked for better”
text:
Im taking time out from my 3 small children to tell everyone how happy and impressed we were with this hotel. We stayed here 6 nights while visiting the Zoo, Sea World, Legoland, etc. The hotel was very clean, new, and the staff could not have been nicer. The FREE buffet breakfast every morning was perfect, huge selection to eat from, waffle maker, eggs, bacon,biscuits and more. Then in the evening from 5-7 is a FREE dinner- yes free....with wine! This worked out super, bc after being at an amusement park all day we were all tired and hungry. It was great to go back to the hotel after a long day and enjoy a meal as a family and then all get in the hot tub and relax before bed. 
 Our hotel room had a large room with the king bed in it and full bath, then another separate living room with a desk, kitchen(very convienient for left overs and any groceries), and fold out couch and TV for the kids to sleep on and watch cartoons when they wake up. 
We would stay here again in a heartbeat!!!!! Perfect!!

title: “Best kept secret in New York.”
text: This hotel has everything from amazingly friendly staff who just couldn't do enough for us, to the most comfortable beds and pillows I've ever slept in. Nothing was too much trouble, from going out and buying us coffee filters for our in room coffee machine, to lending us a laptop for 20 minutes (FREE) so we could look up a few websites on things to do in New York. The rooms were extremely spacious and spotlessly clean and coming home from a "hard days shopping" to find our room where the beds turned down, the lighting dimmed and soft music playing, was fabulous. Wouldn't stay anywhere else in New York again.

title: “Fine to stay at but not the best”
text:
this is one of the hotels that have very good location & view but the hotel is little bit old style. but it is fine to stay at.
very good room service, & self parking service.
the shuttle bus service is very good, the hotel is very close to airport & sea world.
the rooms are very big & well equipped.
the elevators & pathways are not newly furnished.

title: “Everyone was so nice!!”
text: What stands out in my mind the most from my stay was EVERYONE, in every department was so nice!! From the front desk, to the bellhops to the valets, everyone was so nice and helpful, good eye contact and a genuine smile. When I checked in, the remote control for my television wasn't working, so I called downstairs and in less than 5 minutes, someone came to change the batteries. The front desk also called to follow up that I was happy with my room & they serviceman came, which no hotel I've ever been to has done. The lobby is big, with lots of couches to hang out in while waiting for friends and the downstairs bar had a good lively crowd and good service. While I'm on it, the breakfast buffet was EXCELLENT. Our waiter was very cordial and they had awesome breakfast wraps...yum! The gym was pretty big and their equipment was all high quality (I've been to a lot of gyms) and well maintained. Their hot tub and swimming pool are indoor and next to the gym, and my only complaint about the whole place is that the hot tub did not get hot enough. What made up for it is the heavenly shower w/the 2 showerheads and the super comfortable bedding...I slept so well and had a great stay.

title: “Loews - similar to Marriott”
text:
My husband and I stayed for one night at this hotel in June 2012.
We originally booked this hotel when it was a Marriott using points. When they switched to Loews we were told that our reservation would still be honored with the points, which was good to hear. 
Upon arriving we had the choice of valet or self park at the public (mall parking) ramp attached to the hotel. We self parked for something like $9 per day, but no in and out privileges. We did go in an out and just handed over another $9, but it was still cheaper than the valet service.
The check in line was a few people deep when we arrived around noon and it was about 10 minutes from when we arrived at the hotel to when we actually checked in and our room was available right away.
Our hotel room was on the club level with a nice view of downtown LA and the Hollywood sign. The room was of average size as was the bathroom. The only downside was the bathroom where there were no towel racks and only one sink.
We also had club access from our prior status and reservation with Marriott. The club was on the small side, but rarely did we ever see anyone else in it. We were disappointed with the tiny/mini water bottles they had in the club rather than the normal sized ones. Breakfast in the lounge was ok, but nothing amazing. It was what we would expect from a club lounge breakfast. 
This hotel is attached to the Loews (Kodak) theater and shopping mall. After a short walk through the mall, you’ll on the Hollywood strip with thousands of tourists and easy access to any Starline tours you might have booked. Overall, this hotel has the best location for easy Hollywood sightseeing.

title: “Great Service, Great Location”
text:
I stayed at Hotel Mela for 8 nights on a business trip. It was ideal for a base, half a block from Times Square, to run around to meetings all over Manhattan, watch a Broadway show and walk to various wonderful restaurants.
I was surprised by the pleasantness of everyone from the front desk to the cleaners. Everyone was cheerful, always happy to help and clearly cared about the facility.
I spent a lot of time in my hotel room, working between meetings. The room service from the restaurant next door was nice food, delivered fast and there was plenty to choose from -- breakfast, lunch and dinner. The room had everything I needed: iron and ironing board, lots of plugs for my laptop and phone charger, constant free wifi and a constantly tempting minibar.
The hotel atmosphere is fresh and fun, with beautiful dark wood and splashes of colour, with a modern sitting room by the elevators with a chess board and backgammon.
I would highly recommend this hotel -- my stay was flawless.

title: “A "Peace" of Green in the City!”
text: This hotel is a wonderfully peaceful hotel located on what seemed to be the only piece of green in Seattle! Having spent a previous evening downtown Seattle, it was a wonderful escape staying here. The room was large and very comfortable. We were pleased with the service; especially the shuttle service to the Link Rail system. We were minutes from the airport and had 2 wonderful meals during our stay. Our children loved the complimentary ice cream and malted milk balls! The continental breakfast was nice as well. Staying here was a treat!

title: “Easy for Parents”
text: This hotel was a great stay. We were relatively close to most major monuments and museums. Starbucks across the street - who doesn't love that! The pool is only 3 ft deep so fit for all ages. The breakfast bar had something for everyone and snacks for the day (makes up for the slightly higher room fees of nearby hotels), if you know what I mean. And lastly, the nightly managers cocktail party was relaxing after a day of sight seeing. Would definitely stay here again. One more, there is a common are and a bedroom area with a refrigerator for snacks and such. Very family designed.

title: “Friendly staff, hotel on I-10 access road, road noise loud in some rooms”
text: Although conveniently located on the access road to I-10, the road noise can be a bit loud depending upon the room. The rooms have been updated (redecorated, new AC/heat) since my last stay. They are much, much nicer, brighter and more modern. The staff is friendly and seems genuinely nice. I've stayed at this specific location a number of times. I have never had any issues with the wired internet service; performance has been fine. The hotel is close to a good 5 mi jogging trail - Buffalo Bayou Park Trail.

title: “If you're a light sleeper or don't like noise, give it a miss.”
text:
Rooms were clean and fairly spacious. Complimentary continental breakfast was basic and provided in the reception, which proved to be a limited space for so many people. The whole thing rather reminded me of 'feeding time at the zoo'. 
 Most staff were helpful, but not all. 
Vermont is a busy road and I found the noise of the traffic to be problematic. I changed rooms (to a quieter part), but this was next to the 'storeroom/boiler room' which by default was incredibly noisy. I just couldn't win. Combined with the general noise of other residents, it was a bit of a nightmare all told. I would be very reluctant to stay again, but if noise isn't an issue to you then.....
Lastly only one coffee bag (?) for the coffee machine is supplied as a matter of course.

title: “Beautiful!”
text: We paid $79 per night for a weekend stay. The lobby was very upscale. The room was beautiful and spacious. Bathroom was immaculate. The shower (no tub) was very large with beautiful tile (not typical bathroom tile) and a glass door (not sliding door). Only negatives: Some noise from nearby train and airport - but not bad in the room, never woke us up; no free breakfast - hotel restaurant breakfast was expensive. I would deifinitely stay here again! I have never had a room this nice for this price!

title: “compact but comfortable”
text:
I booked this hotel as a mystery hotel. For the price it was excellent value, clean tidy and accessable. We found a lovely diner across the road and access to public transport was excellent. 
On a down side the rooms are quite small so if you are travelling with more than 2 in your party book a second room. 
We recieved very good service from the hotel staff. I parked in the valet parking and didn't get the car out until we departed. Valet parking was easy to find once you figure out that it was around the back of the hotel, not at the front door like some.
A very good experience overall.

title: “Historic building, modern and luxurious services and stay”
text: Magnolia has done a fantastic job of creating a fabulous hotel with modern amenities from an historic building in downtown Denver. The staff were professional, friendly and courteous. We chose the location, because it was within walking (a long walk) distance from Coors Field and we were going to see a Rockies game. The front desk insisted on scheduling the car to take us. Evening wine and beer tasting and bedtime cookies and milk rounded out the great stay. I only wish it could have been longer.

title: “You really feel like a rock star!!”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Chicago Hard Rock Hotel in December last year and had a great time! As soon as you walk into the hotel you feel like you are a welcomed guest and it continues through the entire hotel. Staff at check-in are very very nice. The room we had looked just like the pictures of the rooms on the website (That does not happen very often). We will be back to stay again!!!!

title: “disgusted”
text:
Arrived in middle of night so had to stay.
Room dirty, stained and used sheets, cold, really bad odour, broken lock on door, shared filthy toilet. Didnt even want to clean our teeth, had to get out a.s.a.p.
We were out at 7.30am to find somewhere else quickly.
Brochure says basic, but very overpriced for a hovel.
Keep away!

title: “Fantastic Location”
text: Very convenient location in downtown Chicago. Close to the River and Lake and major downtown attractions. Within easy walking distance to restaurants, shopping, Magnificant Mile, Navy Pier and other attractions. We stayed on the Club Lounge level at the Hotel and enjoyed the room and the Lounge. The room was fairly modern, clean and attractive. The only complaint is the lighting in the bathroom and not enough towels for the number of occupants. Service was quick when we did call for more towels. We have stayed on Club Levels before at other Sheratons and were surprised this Hotel charged for alcoholic beverages in the Club Lounge. The food and the staff in the Lounge were superb but for the price you pay for this amenity, it seems a bit cheap to charge. The only other surprise that was disappointing was use of a promo code I had for the Hotel. I was surprised that, like airlines, this hotel has a limit on the number of rooms it will apply a promo code to. Despite making my reservation very far in advance, the Hotel chain would not honour the promo code when I called to use it. This was one of the factors in our decision to stay at this Hotel.

title: “Lovely hotel with a nice atmosphere”
text:
My friend and I visited New York mid-December for a shopping break and stayed for three nights at the Algonquin. 
The hotel has a large lobby with comfortable seating areas which always seemed to be a popular place for a drink and chat. It had a very nice and welcoming atmosphere, just the place for a cocktail after a long day's shopping. 
The staff are very helpful and courteous, especially Kevin. And Matilda the cat is beautiful.
We found our twin bedded room to be very clean and comfortable, although the bathroom was a little small and did not have a bath. The only mirror for the room was on the inside of the bathroom door, so could have done with another one over the dressing table.
Overall we were delighted with the hotel we had chosen and would definitely return and recommend to all. Great location.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: I having been staying in a different Embassy Suites for the last 5 weeks. I am impressed with this hotel. It was easy to get here on the L train and I felt safe being a single female. It is close to great shopping. Breakfast is good. They even had a decent evening snack. The last 4 hotels have just had pretzels and popcorn. This hotel had vegetables and warm snack.

title: “Great for a group”
text: Stayed here the last week of June. Booked the room directly from their website for $119 with tax and parking came out to around $160. Room was clean and a decent size, the two full size beds were comfortable but small and the sofa bed slept two people(room for a queen sized air mattress if you're looking to squeeze in more people). Great hotel for groups, there was plenty of room to get ready at the same time without feeling uncomfortable or crowded. For the right price I'd stay here again.

title: “We loved the Millennium Broadway!”
text: We stayed here 4 nights in Feb. 04. We checked in at 11 AM after a red-eye flight. Great room with fabulous view of the Chrysler Building- incredibly helpful staff. Got a great rate through QuikBook. Will definiitely stay here again!

title: “Great hotel, wonderful staff”
text: I stayed at the Joule this past week and will be back. The roof-top pool is very nice. The staff was great. The hotel has a "W" feel to it, but is more elegent. The art work in the hotel is also amazing. I took advantage of the comlimentary local transportation in the hotel's Escalade too!

title: “Great and friendly service!”
text:
Just wanted to send a quick thank you to all the staff at the W hotel in Boston. A group of 8 of us girls came down to watch a few of them
run in the marathon a couple weeks ago. We had great service at the hotel. All your staff were super friendly and helpful. Noah Derstien was very pleasant and helpful in setting us up at a few nightclubs and with ideas of things to see and places to go. He was always smiling and cheeerful.
Brittany, I believe that is her name, was also very friendly and helpful when we were in the hotel boutique. 
I will recommend to all my friends to stay at the W hotel in Boston when traveling there. We are looking forward to our next stay in 
the future.
Regards,
Junelle Grindberg

title: “excellent service for large group”
text:
We booked this hotel because they had TWO shuttles to get us to and from the airport for a very early flight. They got all 20 of us their in time just as promise and picked us up even though we only stayed there one night. They also let us park our cars there.
Excellent service, clean rooms and close to the airport

title: “Excellent hotel in perfect location, just around the corner from Times Square”
text: We booked this hotel, as the ratings on Trip Advisor placed it in the top 20 of 400 or so hotels. We were not disappointed at all. The hotel is close enough to Times Square but far enough away not to be noisy at night. The staff were helpful and Larry the Concierge was very helpful when we wanted to book the Uncle Sams Heroes of The World Trade Centre tour. I would recommend this hotel to anyone, clean, quiet and tidy with a great location.

title: “Fab Boutique Hotel”
text:
The Redbury is current and happening.
Has a cool restaurant called Clio, which is buzzing at the weekend.
Its in the middle of Hollywood within walking distance to most clubs (Avalon/The Colony/Eden etc).
Perfect here if you wanna party, if you prefer piece and quiet and nice place to walk around during day etc then head over to Beverly Hills.
Staff are very friendly.
Room is super cool, its a mix between current and funky and 60s/70s style. you get a record player in your room. room is massive too, there all like apartments with full kitchen, large living room and then sleeping area. Our balcony was looking down on to the courtyard also.
Those of you that want an early night probably not the best, as people are drinking and partying away in courtyard till 1am ish. But was fine for us as we were here to socialise and have fun.
Would definitely return, but only if wanting to stay in the Hollywood area.

title: “Very comfortable and the perfect location”
text: Some friends and I recently stayed at the Villa Florence on our weekend getaway to San Francisco. It was the perfect location and so comfortable. The rooms are beautiful, the furnishings and color choices are great. You can tell that the building is historic, but everything has been updated so nicely, that it is a perfect fit for San Francisco. The staff at this hotel are very freindly and courteous, and there is enough staff in the lobby at any given time to answer all of your questions. The location really couldn't be better. You are right in the heart of Union Square, and the cable car runs right up Powell street in front of the hotel. Once you are done with the hustle and bustle of downtown San Francisco, the Villa Florence is the perfect spot to come back to and relax. While the hotel is upscale, the atmosphere is very casual and relaxed, also our rooms on the 4th and 5th floor were very quiet. We will definitely stay there again and reccommend it to all of our friends.

title: “No Hot Water”
text:
No free breakfast as stated online.
No hot water when I wanted to take a shower, morning or evening. I complained about this each morning (3 days). There was hot water at 6 one evening, but that wasn't when I wanted to shower.
The rooms are nicely appointed and the beds are comfortable.

title: “A Great hotel in a Great City”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for 3 nights on the first leg of our month long vacation. We had been travelling for more than 24 hours to reach San Diego so were really tired when we arrived at the check in desk but the key card was already waiting for us. 
As I was celebrating my birthday during our vacation the hotel automatically upgraded us to a junior suite on a high floor where there was champagne and chocolate waiting for us.
The room was great, very clean and very spacious.
We were overlooking the pool and the railway line but I can honestly say that not once did a train disturb us either, by day or by night.
We had taken the Breakfast and parking package which we thought to be excellent value.......the breakfasts and the service in McCormick & Schmick's were very good and the portion size incredible!
The hotel location is great for shopping and dining.
We made use of the gym and the pool just once during our stay but both were very clean and well equipped.
The concierge was very knowledgeable, helpful and friendly.....we booked our trip on the tram tour through him.
We too were staying at the hotel during the earthquake mentioned in the previous reviews but knew nothing about it until someone told us about it the next day.......and as for all the comments re the bathrooms......it obviously wasn't a problem as we cant even remember the doors!
Our check out was as efficient as our check in. The valet guys asked if we needed directions to our next location and even gave us details of good places to see and eat en route.
We could not fault the hotel or the service we received from any member of staff and would book this hotel if we are ever back in San Diego.

title: “Excellent location”
text: Our trip was to celebrate a 70th birthday and we were accompanied by our 2 sisters. The hotel is in an excellent location, ideal for shopping and public transport. Initially we had a hiccup with our accommodation which was finally resolved. The hotel was clean and the staff extremely friendly and efficient. We did not dine nearby or make use of any other facilities in the hotel. We would have no hesitation in recommending to others.

title: “Yuck”
text:
Well, we wanted cheap and we got it. The location is good, the rooms are terrible. They weren't dirty, per say, but the whole room and halllway felt kinda ghetto. It's not cheap, but short of the hostels, it was the cheapest place we could find downtown. You get what you pay for, I guess.
On a positive note, it's not like we did anything other than sleep in there, anyway. The water pressure was good, bring your own soap and shampoo, and ask for more toilet paper. They have a safe, which is nice, and the staff, while not super classy, was helpful and knew what they were doing. I wouldn't stay here again, though.

title: “upgraded to a suite!”
text: We stayed at the hilton last July. When we first got there it was early in the morning and room was not ready yet, so they took our baggage and put it in storage. Easy enough, that way you can go start your sightseeing. We didn't get back until 4pm and we were given a room on the top floor. As well we booked a standard room and were upgraded for free to a Suite overlooking central park!!! The room was excellent and clean. Being in a suite it included breakfast which was excellent with fresh fruits and breads. We had a wonderful stay and will be staying there again!

title: “It'll a Do...Good location”
text: We visit NYC often but this was our first time staying a The New Yorker. Initially, we were pretty excited to stay at a somewhat historical hotel. Although the lobby is attractive with a nice retro feel, the quality of the rooms were a bit disappointing. The room seemed clean, and being NYC, the room size was not surprising to us. However, the bathroom was definitely in need of attention. It almost looked like the tiles in the shower/tub had been painted over and the door appeared warped as it was difficult to close. The shower head was unusually low - and I'm short. It also flowed a solid stream of water, like from a fire hose - not comfortable. However, this is New York, so realistically, how much time are you really spending in your room? If you're like us, you just need a clean bed and a place to shower. For that, it will do. We would probably stay here again if we couldn't secure a better option.

title: “Security? You decide.”
text: We left our vehicle for a week with their "Park and Fly" option, only to find our spare tire mount on my SUV cranked down and my tire gone. We were parked right beneath a light pole with a security camera attached to it. Security told us the lot is not patrolled between the hours of 3 AM and 7 AM. We will never stay here again.

title: “Loved It!!!”
text:
My daughter and I just returned from a five night stay at the Hampton Inn/Seaport. After reading some of the reviews I was a little apprehensive but no need to be at all. We arrived early in the day to a warm welcome by the friendly staff and since our room wasn't ready we were able to freshen up, leave our luggage and venture out.
We we returned to the hotel and were greeted with another warm welcome and were given a room on the 3rd floor (305), it was very clean and had everything that we needed. 
The breakfast in the lobby was more than enough to get us started for the day. Also when we returned from a very busy day we were able to grab a cup of tea to take back to the room. Again we were always greeted by the friendly staff and were asked more than once if there was anything we needed. 
This was not our first visit to NYC so it was a nice change to be at a hotel away from the crowds in Times Square. The subway station was close and very easy to use.
We had a wonderful trip to NYC and would not hesitate to stay at this Hampton Inn again. Wonderful staff!!!

title: “Do yourself a favor and stay at the Hotel Teatro”
text: We should have taken the miserable reservation process as a sign to NOT stay here. They couldn't get our reservation correct, and when the BP finally did get it right, they messed it up once again on our arrival. Front desk staff COULDN'T HAVE CARED LESS that our reservations were wrong--and their fault. We had to unpack, log on to our computer, pull up our confirmation and then? no apology. Complete and utter disregard for the customer's convenience & happiness. Rooms were large but stuffy, hard beds, decent bathrooms. But the snarky staff doesn't justify even the nicest accommodations. Stayed there 2 nights and then went over to Hotel Teatro with amazing beds, a better rate, windows that open & a fabulous, well-staffed restaurant.

title: “Decent value for money”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for a week with my girlfriend. Our room was larger than expected and everything was generally very clean, even the shared bathrooms, of which there were three on our floor. I rarely had to wait to use them, but I suppose February is low season, so there might be more people staying there during typical vacationing seasons.
The hotel is close to the subway. There's an entrance at Broadway and 94th to the 96th st. station where the 1, 2 and 3 trains all stop. Central Park is also less than 1 km away on foot.
The internet access in the room is decent, but you need a cable; there's no wireless network. You need to pay $10 in advance at the front desk (for each day until noon the next day) and if you don't have a cable already they'll provide you with one. The rooms also have TV's with a decent selection of channels, but seriously, you don't go to NYC to watch TV.
The staff is mostly very friendly and helpful. Nothing big to complain about there. They all appear to be 1st generation immigrants, Arabs, Indians etc, and sometimes act accordingly. But mostly they're very service minded, great guys that do their stuff by the book (whatever book that may be).
A few points of advice:
- Bring a few towels of your own, as sometimes you might only get small towels. 
- Don't get the guy at the front desk to get you a taxi to the airport or elsewhere as you will most likely NOT get an authorized taxi, but a rather expensive buddy of his that WILL try to scam you. He drove us through Harlem on the way to JFK, which I honestly didn't like, although it's probably a lot safer than it used to be, and might be the quickest route for all I know.
- The hotel does not have a safe, but they do have a pretty safe storage room for your luggage. I wouldn't leave anything valuable there, though, unless it's in a firmly locked suitcase.
- I've seen some people complain about the elevator being slow. I honestly don't think it is. If they're referring to the doors closing slowly, there's a button to close them instantly.
All in all, this is a very good budget hotel if you don't mind a few inconveniences.
Recommended for solo travelers or young (or young minded) couples, friends.

title: “Average hotel.....no more, but good location for bay front activities. Read on........ on...”
text:
This hotel is ageing and due to it's location a serious transit point for cruise line passengers with all the attendant bustle and noise. But then the location serves Bay activities like the aircraft carrier ( welll worth doing as I did with my young son........get there early and allow at least half a day ), Bay cruises and restaurants which are not that cheap. We found the Cafe 30 meters from the Hotel great with friendly service and good all round food choices. The Ruths Chris restaurant next door is excellent but not cheap a la carte. Go for the taster menu and they do not mind if one menu is shared between two.........given the size of USA portions it proved to be more than enough. 5 mins walk is the tram station which is great for access to Seaworld and the older part ( very touristy Mexican enclave of restaurants and shops ...but worth a brief visit ). We mainly visited San Diego for my son to see Legoland. It is quite a way out and takes time by train although scenic. Check economies by hiring a car. Also do check when the park is closed as we got caught out and wasted most of a day for nothing.
Downtown San Diego is pretty uninspiring and mostly empty with the rush hour being very early in the morning to connect with the East Coast business activities......during normal day hours a bit of a ghost town !! Otherwise, some good out of town shopping malls serviced by the tram network. Go for the day pass. But hey if you want people you will be staying in the right hotel !!

title: “Great Location”
text: This hotel was part of a package deal on Travelocity. The location was great! Easy access to the mag mile & opera. The room was very pleasant, clean and comfortable, although the dark modern-style decor seemed a little cold. The hotel was huge and getting to the room a bit of a trek due to the layout. However, it was good value for an upscale hotel and the location was great.

title: “Heaven in San Diego!”
text:
Checking in to the Catamaran Resort the staff was so helpful. Heading to our room amid phenomenal landscaping, exotic ducks, ponds and parakeets was enchanting. Our room provided an amazing view of the bay. We walked everyday along the boardwalk watching surfers,
boaters, kids playing on the beach, it was just wonderful. You can rent any type of water toy. The location was excellent. We just had a wonderful time and are already planning our next visit
to the Catamaran Resort Hotel. 
Marcia Vincent

title: “Central location”
text:
The Affinia Manhattan is extremely well placed for sightseeing and shopping - we could walk to Central Park, the Empire State Building, Grand Central Station, 5th Ave, Times Square, etc - and we were bang opposite Penn Station, so the airtrain/NJ Transit to and from the airport worked brilliantly.
We stayed in a one bed suite for four nights; our daughters had the sofa bed and we had the bedroom - but the lack of a window and aircon in the bedroom meant we had to keep the door open. Not a problem for us, but might not work for friends travelling together. Otherwise the room was good, nicely refurbished and the fridge in the kitchen area was very useful.
We had breakfast in the hotel on the first day ($19 each) but on the other days we went to the Cosmic Cafe on W31st Street, between 6th and 7th Ave (the hotel is on the corner of 7th and W31st) for about $20 for all of us. Wifi is expensive ($15 for 24 hours) so we had a cup of coffee in MacDonalds a couple of hundred yards up 7th Ave....
The concierge was so helpful - she recommended a good family diner, gave us maps, etc. you can also print boarding passes at the desk.
The only downside really was the noise as the windows really didn't shut out the sound of car hooters which go continually, all night. However, we felt it added to the NY experience!

title: “CAUTION CAUTION CAUTION”
text: Caution! Caution! Caution! This hotel is lovely and in a very conventient location, however, if you want to sleep at night before 3am, don't bother staying here. We got to our hotel at about 9:45 pm, crawled into bed as we had an early departure out of the city, and all we could hear was the music from the bar across the street and people out on the street. We called the front desk at about midnight to ask for a resolve and they said they wasn't anything they could do as we were the first to complain. We called the front desk again at 1:30am and asked if they had any earplugs and was just told no. If you stay at this hotel, make sure your room is not across from Mr. Dooley's Bar and higher up than the 5th floor.

title: “Fun, stylish, GREAT location and value”
text: Although the room was tiny, it accommodated three of us (partner and teenager) comfortably and was stylish enough so we didn't feel too cramped. LOVED the wallpaper and bunk bed lay out. Terrific value for NY -- and just two blocks from the theater where we saw a show that night. Good continental breakfast in the morning. Very European feel to the place.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights in September. Really nice hotel, very good welcome and check in. Room was good, didn't use any of the facilities but the pool and gym looked ok. Didn't dine here so can't comment on the restaurant. 
The hotel is ideally located for the trolley and the cable car, so most places within easy reach. 
Must mention the concierge, who was extreemly helpful and provides a wealth of local knowledge.
We would definately stay here again

title: “Another great Stay”
text: Have stayed here several times..usually for Sounders Matches......I always book a suite when possible and did again this time. I booked through hotels.com because it always seems to be cheaper than the hotel website. The only mix up was they initially gave me a king bed room instead of a suite. They corrected the error fairly quickly. this suite had a little different layout than the others I have had and seemed a little smaller but it met our needs. Staff is always friendly and helpful..rooms are clean...and location is prime...just remember the trains in the morning can wake you up, but just bring ear plugs. With this location you are always paying for location, location, location. Not gonna get free breakfast or parking..but the location makes the expierience. As far as the restaurant and bar(Jimmy's on first) never been a huge fan..always so so....but there are some options near the hotel like Elysian for good beer and food or Pyramid accross the street. Overall, another great stay at Silver Cloud.

title: “Great location and very nice (big) hotel”
text: My wife and I dropped our 3 kids off at Gram's and headed here for a night-out for just the two of us. Great location in the heart of the city. The convention center is near by (if needed). We enjoyed getting over to Reading Terminal across the street to see and taste the various food and drink items. Valet parking was easy in/out (Parking entrance is on Sansom St and NOT Market St.).
