We needed a taxi to dinner and the hotel shuttle gave us a complimentary ride. Room service was fast and delicious.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: We had a one bedroom suite - the rooms were small but comfortable, well-furnished, and very clean. The only negatives were that the bed was on the hard side, and that our corner room was across the street from 2 office buildings so we had to keep the blinds completely closed. The staff was very friendly and helpful, the breakfast and afternoon wine/cheese were wonderful (definitely exceeded expectations!), and there was fruit, cookies, and lemonade available all day. We liked the location - it was relatively quiet, very convenient to the subways and was easy to get uptown and downtown. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Front Desk Employee Pocketed My Cash”
text:
My friends and I checked in for an all girls weekend on Thursday, July 28 and was checked in by clerk Ikea. We were prepared ahead of time to pay for the total stay of four nights in the amount of $854.40 as we were informed of this when booking the room in March 2011. After we counted out $590.00 (three $100 bills, fourteen $20 bills and one $10 bill) in cash and asking for the remaining ($264.40) to be placed on a credit card, we were giving a receipt and we started our trip. On Sunday, July 31, one of my friends happen to look at the receipt Ikea printed for us at check in and noticed the receipt only credit us $490.00. We immediately went to the front desk and as we walked to the desk Ikea was there and immediately turned around and hid behind a curtain. After speaking to a female manager on duty, we were informed an "investigation" would occur the following day however in the mean time we were responsible for paying the additional $100. The manager never asked Ikea to step out behind the curtain to confirm she checked us in while continuing to inform us about the investigation and unwilling to assure us the hotel was equip with security cameras. This manager was also very stiff displaying a flat affect the enitre time we spoke with her; as I type this review we still have not heard the results of the "investigation."
In addition, other employees at this hotel were rude informing us we had to come downstairs to get food and drinks we ordered from the hotel while having to hale a cab most of the time on our own while the door man looked on. I would NOT recommend this hotel to anyone and will NEVER stay in this hotel again!

title: “John & Rachel Cape Town South Africa. "Good Location"”
text: We stayed with friends. The rooms were small but clean and the bed was very comfortable. Parking is a problem and very expensive. The complimentary breakfast was good. Within walking distance from Magnificent mile and shops. The staff was very helpful.Pity we stayed only 2 days.

title: “I expected more.”
text:
As far as room quality, I really expected more for downtown Boston. The rooms needs a serious face lift. Service was fair and every time we walked through the lobby there was an extremely long line at the front desk. Everyone was friendly and polite but didn't have a sense of urgency about them.
The location of the hotel truly saved the stay from turning more negative. The grocery store right across the skywalk/ street was wonderful and a great convenience. We walked over every morning for breakfast rather than eating the same old Marriott eggs. 
Also, note that valet parking is $44 a night. Not exactly cheap, but unavoidable for this part of the city.

title: “Very convenient”
text: We always stay here when we visit SF; very convenient to walk to many attractions/city transportation, plus the indoor free parking is great. However, leave your big pick-up or SUV at home because the parking is VERY cramped to say the least. Very nice, but small, rooms that are beginning to show a little age in the furnishings and fixtures. The last time we were there though the elevator had a terrible smell in it and the roof leaked at night in the hall and a light fixture crashed to the floor. Very quiet, in fact, one of the "quietest" places we've ever stayed in--you can't hear any noise from the halls, other bathrooms, etc. But if you stay on the Lombard Avenue side, you may hear traffic noise. A great little breakfast place up Lombard to the left, Lombardy Cafe. And a nice deli a block behind is the Fort Mason Deli. 70+ TV channels. Great rates during the week, and Bernard at the front desk is very helpful and personable. For the price/convenience/free parking in a VERY expensive city like SF, the Buena Vista can't be beat.

title: “Charming hotel on the Upper East Side”
text: This hotel was lovely. The staff was very friendly, the room was surprisingly large and it was a great location for shopping and visiting museums on the UES. Very fairly priced too. I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Comfortable stay”
text: Warm welcoming staff. Convenient to all. Clean comfortable rooms. Ask to see your room first though. Offered a city suite, which would have been nice for business entertaining, but inner view less than inspiring. Also, upgraded to a partial waterview, as a Marriott Rewards member, so how did my colleague, who is a non-member, get a prime waterview room???

title: “Great location”
text: I spent the week of the 4Th of July at the Marriott for leisure and location was great. Next to the Metro and within walking distance to Chinatown and museums, sites and restaurants. The king room was average but clean. Single serving coffeemaker in rooms great for morning jolt. Alley view but spent very little time in room as I was trying to see all D.C. had to offer. Ladies, T.J. Maxx was just 2 blocks away! Concierge Aurora was very knowledgeable and helpful with what's in the area and tours. WiFi in room available for a fee but free in public areas. Great workout area and there's access to washer dryer at no charge and a small pool. Would definitely stay again. Metro pass will be your best friend to get around the city.

title: “It's about the Staff; the most hospitable and gracious group of people imaginable.”
text: Our company sponsored a conference at The Stanford Court and necessarily required more interaction and assistance than leisure guests would. The assistance provided by them was remarkable. To a person, they were patient, responsive, helpful, and always expecting to provide just a bit more than was asked. They all seem pleased to be where they are and happy to be of service. If you're choosing a conference location - this is the place! We all agreed we would welcome the chance to return whether for business or pleasure.

title: “A quality hotel in a quality city”
text:
Just returned from a glorious Easter weekend in Chicago and 3 wonderful nights at the Sofitel. We were impressed from the moment we walked into the beautifully decorated lobby to the moment we checked-out and that is no small feat. Having travelled extensively for both business and pleasure, we're not easily impressed but the Sofitel succeeded in exceeding our expecations. 
The room was bright with a nice view of the city, spotlessly clean and well appointed with contemporary furnishings and a very comfortable king size bed. The bathroom was modern, spacious, well lit and again exceptionally clean. The turn down service with Evian bottled water and the weather forecast for the next day was also a nice touch. The staff were all extremely friendly and attentive. 
We did not eat at the hotel restaurant but the menu and decor looked impressive. The lounge bar had a great vibe and was perfect for having a night cap.
The location of the hotel was ideal...prime shopping, restaurants and nightlife were all within easy walking distance. Eating at Gibson's was a highlight with a table of Chicago Bears players to our right and Washington Wizard players to our left made for interesting people watching complimented by great food and service.
We paid $185 per night with a pre-paid internet special which was excellent value for the exceptional quality of the hotel.
We loved Chicago and our stay at the Sofitel only enhanced our experience. The city has a great energy, is very clean and we were particularly surprised by how friendly everyone was. If we have an opportunity to return to this wonderful city, we will definitely be staying at the Sofitel.

title: “DO NOT STAY HERE!!!!”
text: i recently stayed at this hotel and while yes the people were very nice at the front desk and the room was ok this is not a place you want to stay especially if you have children. We were to stay 3 nights and left a night early we felt so unsafe. no one tells you Graceland is in the "Getto" of Memphis my advice would be to stay closer to beale street in the heart of memphis do not stay anywhere near Graceland!!!!! we read the previous reviews and thought it would be good but we were decieved this is not a place you wanna be. Definatly visit Graceland but don't stay anywhere near it. There are two big gangs that are very close by and target tourists so im warning you from experiance to stay elsewhere. i wish someone had warned us because we didn't want to go outside once it was dark it was that scary. We were also warned people could knock on our doors so to be careful and look for photo id yep not what we expected!! so please take my advice and find a better place.

title: “Brilliant - rooms, location & service”
text:
We stayed at Belleclaire for 4 nights and throughly enjoyed ourselves. It was a very reasonable price too.
The hotel is having renovation work but we were not disturbed at all.
The room was spacious with a private bathroom (we paid a bit more for that).
Brilliant location, right near Central Park - we explored the whole city and liked the part (Upper Westside) that the hotel was in the best.
Only downside is that the air conditioning fan was very loud but luckily we didn't need to use it! Maybe in the height of summer this would have put me off but I loved the hotel.

title: “Best staycation in the valley!”
text: Arizona Grand Resort is now my families favorite instate spot for summertime fun...The resort offers so much for everyone in the family. My wife takes the yoga class at 9am and says it's great, the facility is beautiful and inviting...The water park is fantastic and very well maintained...The food is good too...I stay at other hotels and resorts in the valley, but this place is my favorite...Last summer we stayed there once, this summer we stayed 3 times...We know the place real well and feel like we're at home....Jason

title: “Great location, okay service, TINY and SLOW elevator!”
text:
We stayed overnight in Hotel Mela in the city for a short 2-day trip. It was half a block from times square, and right down the street was an adorable deli with GREAT food. The rooms were very clean, and the service was top notch. When we needed silverware or a bucket of ice, we just dialed "0" on the phone and it was brought up immediately. The value was alright for when we stayed. We payed almost $300 a night for a queen with NO view. I know it is NYC, but seriously? The rooms were a little cramped. But all of these things I can look past. The main reason we have decided not to go back is the elevator. Now, this may seem like I am picking on the one flaw, but it was so slow. It seemed to take 5 minutes for the elevator to come up, and then, only 4 people could fit in at once. It wouldn't have been too bad, except our room was on the 8th floor.
Overall, an okay experience, but we would not return to this hotel.

title: “DO NOT STAY HERE- Rooms are tiny, service is bad, not kid-friendly, and cable constantly loses signal”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel twice and I will never go back. The rooms are tiny and there is very little room is provided to unpack your clothes and place your luggage. Amenities are scarce and it took housekeeping 5 hours to bring extra towels. During my first visit, I received a room with a king bed, yet the tv was placed on the side wall, so it was nearly impossible to relax in bed and watch tv without having to contort my body sideways. During my next visit, I received a room with a queen bed. The room was so small that when we opened the door, the valet could not even get our luggage inside and he suggested we call the front desk to request a larger room. We did and, in fairness, they did move us to a slightly larger room witha queen bed. I was also upset that they charged me the same price for the queen bed as they did for the king bed during my first visit.
I opted for the the valet parking service with the understanding that we needed to phone the front desk 15 minutes ahead of time in order to have it brought out. I called for the car on two different occasion, and one tim eit ook 35 minutes, and the next time it took 45 minutes, thus making me late for my appointments.
They do serve a continental breakfast, however the lady that maintains it starts closing it down 15 minutes before she is supposed to.

title: “Great Location and friendly”
text:
Spent close to a week at the Chelsea Pines. Location was good close to Subway and easy to get around.
Staff were friendly, room (we stayed in 1 Bedroom) more than comfortable.
Owner (Jay) very hel;pful in providong suggestions for things to do.
Overall a great time in New York.

title: “Nice but some problems”
text:
Nicely furnished and decorated. Clean, many amenities, and a convenient location.
CONS: No pool....the roof hot-tub was out of order during our stay, despite the check-in clerk pointing it out as an amenity we would enjoy...it had not just broke down; it was out for days. Also, even though it was already 4:30PM when we arrived, our room was not ready for about 30 minutes (not the 10 minutes promised by the clerk).

title: “Fabulous! Love it!”
text:
This was our second visit to Hotel Chandler. When deciding to go to New York we had no hesitation in booking at the Chandler again....and we were not disappointed! The staff are friendly, the decor is lovely and it is in a convenient location close to the Empire State building. I love the 'turning down' service where they leave a chocolate on your pillow before bed in the evening and turn down the covers. It's the personal touch that really counts.
Another great feature is that you can have coffee from the lobby 24/7. The beds are comfy, bathrooms modern and very clean. Book at the Chandler, you won't be disappointed! NYC at its best!

title: “Never Again”
text: This hotel was awful, dirty bug infested and should be closed. It is under a bridge which is noisy all night, elevator is ancient, no service, scary, old rooms, some appliances work some don't. Let your car keep moving DON'T STOP!!!! I KNOW I WON't!!!!

title: “Excellent stay”
text:
Great location, close to NQR and F subway lines.
Rooms clean, comfortable
Free tea/coffee/hot chocolate machine in lobby was nice
Got a good deal online so was great value for money for a trendy hotel. 
Would definately stay again if price right.
Also there is a fantastic cheap & authentic little japanese restaurant next door with great food!

title: “Great Location and Property”
text: Took mom to Chi-town for architectural tours and museums, very glad I found this hotel. It's a twin Marriott, where the lobby and rooms are halved - one side is Springhill Suites, more utilitarian and budget, one side is Residence Inn, with nicer lobby and dining areas. Ample breakfast was complimentary every day, with healthy choices, and weeknites offered a free dinner and wine. Nothing fancy, more a cafeteria line, no choices, but great to just relax after a long day of sightseeing. An ideal property to visit as a solo biz or leisure traveler - very friendly dining room, warm vibe among staff and also travelers. Will suggest this to my single girlfriends for future visits. Location just a few blocks from O'Hare blue line, even closer to Red line. Hotel in the "steak district" just north of the river; many restaurants just a block away. Short walk to Michigan and shopping. Great experience, nice staff, value price - will stay again!

title: “Really Nice Hotel, but....”
text: I just loved the contemporary and clean decor of this hotel. Our room was beautiful and the Aveda amenities a nice touch. Check-in was excellent. A girlfriend and I who are mothers and were having our first trip together in over a decade were really looking forward to one night away. We were upgraded to a nicer room and all was going smoothly. Unfortunately, there was a party next door until 2:00 a.m. and I awoke with the worst headache and I rarely get headaches. Upon check-out I mentioned that there had been a very loud party and that we didn't get very good sleep and the young woman at the front desk who was nowhere near as hospitable as the older women upon check-in said "Well, this is a downtown hotel and it was Saturday night." Having been in the hospitality industry myself I was a bit surprised by this response and did not want to leave on a bad note so I didn't say anything further. So, would we recommend this hotel? Yes, but if you are wanting a restful night's sleep, one of the main reasons people check into pricey hotels, then you might want to request a room in a less occupied section of the hotel or next to a non-twenty something or blocked room for unknown guests. As far as the front desk agent who checked us out...I don't think she has a long-term career in this industry.

title: “Bizarre valet, but great location”
text:
This is my third trip to this hotel, this time bringing three teenagers along, one of whom is on his first trip to Seattle. We arrived at the end of a long day in the car and immediately upon exiting the car, the valet was right there. I let him know I was going to park the car myself and he said to me, "this is your first trip here?" and I answered that it was not. Then he said we should unload right at the front door. I told him my kids didn't want to get out yet and he asked me "why?" I shrugged, he stopped me again from walking in to check in and started explaining the parking ticket to me... um, yeah, it's not rocket science. I tried to take it from him and he pulled it back and said he would put it in the car himself. 
I was checking in at the desk when the valet came back over and made a strange face at me. I thought he must just be an oddball, and was definitely a little wound up... lots of weird energy going on. I returned to my car to find the three kids outraged and angry over comments the valet made to them in our car. He asked my kids if they smoke weed and if they had been smoking it in the car with their mom! My kids were shocked and more than a little put out. They denied it completely.. my kids DO NOT use drugs. He then insistently asked them again, and again. They were very mad. 
We parked the car and I spotted the valet in the garage. I asked him why he was talking to my kids and accusing them of smoking pot. He sighed at me several times, and said, "sorry, I thought I smelled it." Not only did he NOT smell weed in our car, he had no business talking to my kids about anything. What a creep! I wouldn't let that guy touch my car and honestly don't know if I will stay here again.

title: “Friendly, Comfy...and FABULOUS Views”
text: As newlyweds, we had planned a week long visit in the North Cascades / Seattle area. We skipped around and stayed at a total of 3 hotels during our stay in the area and we only wish that we had scheduled more time at the Warwick than the 2 nights that we did stay. We definitely plan on returning to the area in the future and the Warwick will be our first choice on our next stay. The service was top notch and very friendly - everyone was polite, courteous, and happy to help with a smile on their faces; the ambiance was elegant and classy; the food was fabulous and reasonably priced; and the views were breathtaking!!! Thank you for making our trip a memorable one.

title: “Not fabulous, but would return given value”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Grand Hyatt San Francisco for four nights. We arrived right at check-in time, but there was no line so we were into our room quickly. The room was visually nearly as expected overall, but there were some issues. The major problem was the level of comfort for the king bed. It ran a close second in terms of discomfort only to our stay in London two years ago where the bed was beyond uncomfortable. We figured we would attempt a night and see how it went, but we were up many times throughout the night due to the discomfort. We had a tour early the next morning, but upon arriving asked for another room due to the bed. One of the desk staff asked which floor we were on and when we told her the 9th, she said that the beds on (at least) that floor had not been updated, but other floors had been. They had no rooms available for that night, but agreed to move us for the remaining two nights. 
Once in the new room, the bed wasn’t nearly as good as the ones when we have stayed at Hyatt Regency Huntington Beach or Hyatt Regency Scottsdale, but was better than what we started in at this hotel. The hotel rooms do seem in need of some minor remodeling as it is showing its age. For example, the bath tub in both room had some mildew. Also, regarding cleanliness, the first room did not have washcloths and had hair on the bathroom floor.
The location of the hotel was as good as expected given our level of prior research. The nearest cable stop is very near and all the tours pick-up at this hotel. We did order room service and although very expensive by most standards, it was very tasty. Just a word of caution – I would not generally recommend walking around at night in the area due to the number of panhandlers. Overall, I would recommend the hotel due to the value and location.

title: “Great experience, will be back”
text:
My husband and I stayed for a weekend in mid July. Our room was attractive, very clean and bright with a nice decor. The bed and pillows were very comfortable, which we usually have a problem with. The room snacks also had some unusual options.
We really enjoyed the food in their restaurant for dinner - not overpriced, interesting food options, nice decor. We both had the mahi mahi tacos and also the sliders, a nice lighter option after a long, late flight from the East Coast. Breakfast was also good, interesting and pretty reasonable, a nice change from the usual overpriced hotel restaurant fare.
Even though we did not have bring a dog, we loved the dog-bone shaped message board outside with the names of dog guests and the bowls with water and biscuits. The lobby also had board games and magazines, and a bicycle that could be borrowed by hotel guests. Water is always available and free coffee in the morning, both in china cups and to take out.
We have already booked the hotel for our next trip to Los Angeles in September!

title: “Great location, awesome service ... crappy elevators?”
text: I really enjoyed this hotel! I was pleasently surprised on how nice the staff was. It was my first time taking my baby to a hotel and I was very nervous about it. The staff was great, we had them bring a crib to our room and they were quick about it. I also ran out of baby wipes and they gave me some. I checked out what they have on hand for babies and it is amazing, almost anything you would need. Even diaper genies! The only draw back was the elevators. Such a looooong wait. It might have been because of the holidays, but we had to wait around for an elevator for waaaaay to long and there were line ups! I guess you could avoid this by not using them during peak check in times. We actually got helped out by staff one night when we were on our way to the pool, we were waiting for so long he snuck us up in the service elevator. It was really kind of him. Location was walking distance to pike place and right by the monorail. So great! I would definitely recommened this hotel.

title: “Can't go wrong, if you like history!”
text:
Great staff, amazingly historical lobby, bar, restaurant and rooms! The grand piano in the lobby is a 9-foot hand-carved Steinway that was supposed to be on the Titanic apparently.. 
We stayed in a Junior Suite, which was spacious and well worth the upgrade if you like to lounge and order room service etc. No smoking in the rooms, of course.. so be prepared to bust out the rastablock. No ice machines on the floors either, so stock up at the 7eleven around the corner :)

title: “Heaven in Denver”
text:
Mountains, Diners, Drive ins and Dives and the Warwick Hotel. Check in, smooth. Room, King size bed I'd like to have an affair with(Never so comfortable), Balcony, nice place to relax after a day of sightseeing. Staff knew everything about the area and was helpful to the point you wanted to take them where you were going. Its been a long time I've been this relaxed on a vacation. Thank you for making my wife and my 25th Anniversary special.
Snooze, Jellys and Sams-Don't miss these places. There is Food in Heaven.

title: “awful and awfully expensive”
text: On our first night they stuck us in the smoking floor with our 2 month old baby and our five year old son; yes, we had reservations for a non-smoking room. That was all they had, obiously because they had over-booked. When they did move us they gave us a room next to a big humming fan that must have run the air conditioning. To boot, the place wasn't all that clean or nice. It had a smell about it. This is not a four star hotel, but rather a tourist trap that aims for the one-time customer.

title: “Outstanding”
text:
I have just finished a 5 night stay here and highly recommend it. Stayed on 17th floor in a Club Room. 
Room was clean, tidy and modern. Bathroom was massive - as big as the room nearly! Room was also very spacious. Found the room to be very quiet - minimal street noise and almost no hotel/ guest noise unless someone was outside the room. 
Excellent housekeeping service - they figured out we liked the soap so a few extra were left. Room was always immaculate. 
Beds are soooo comfortable - like a huge pillow of air. 
In room facilities were great - Internet was fast and there was a coffee maker (although we did not use it). There was a shortage of power points and in our room, no desk but we just used a side table and the ottoman easily enough. Air conditioning was good and enjoyed the ability to open the window. 
In room dining was prompt and usual fare for a hotel of this nature. 
All reception/ concierge staff were friendly and helpful. Doormen were lovely and remembered our names. Use of the town car was appreciated. 
Club lounge facilities were exceptional! We made good use of these - breakfast, high tea and cocktail and hors d'ouerves hour. Food quality and range was excellent. The staff in the lounge were exceptional - answering questions,arranging things for the room and helping with the medical service. Nothing was too much trouble for them. 
Top of the Mark - loved the view but found the menu (light dining) to be very limited. Good drinks but did not appreciate the attitude from front of house - found him to be quite rude. Despite being a hotel guest he did not want to give us the window table as he wanted to leave it for a group of 4 (we were a party of 2). 
Location - yes it is a little out of the way but that can also be a good thing especially when you encounter the issues on the street in other parts of town. Found the walk down easy enough, similarly got on to cable car quickly each time. Tended to taxi back up due to where we had been. 
Overall - Really enjoyed the stay and would happily return. Would be great to see day spa type facilities though!
PS - to the last reviewer re the 10 cent charge - that became law in SF in October. I encountered it in a number of places like Walgreens.

title: “Excellent stay!”
text: I didn't expect much for Super8, but reviews were great, my budget tight and my daughter & I are on a quest to visit all the state capitol buildings. The carpets could use some cleaning/updating, but in humid places, carpets always seem to be a bit dingy. However everything else about this hotel is fabulous & the breakfast is among the best I've seen in those hotels that still even offer any. The bed was extremely comfortable and even with our room facing the highway, we didn't hear a thing. I should also say that I am a woman traveling alone with a 13 yr old daughter, got in at midnight, and never felt unsafe for even a minute. We enjoyed our visit to Austin very much!

title: “Friends at The Travel Inn”
text: There were 3 of us and each wanted their own bed. The first room they assigned us was totally unacceptable to accommodate a roll away. We expressed our disappointment and the desk had us look at another room as a possibility. We had a view of the train tracks out the window and the room was much, much better that the 1st one assigned. We took the room and had a nice corner area to put a roll away and plenty of room to move around and enjoy the room. The train was not loud and really did not bother us. The free parking for our car was a wonderful benefit and we could get to the car to pick up or leave items easily. We had a great time in the city - the hotel was close enough to places we went that we walked all over. We definitely will stay here again and hope to get the same room.

title: “Beautiful Hotel in the center of the Gaslamp”
text: Really beautiful, up-to-date hotel. Very light airy rooms with modern amenities. Located right in the middle of the Gaslamp across from the Convention Center. The staff was very nice and the rooms were very quiet. We really enjoyed spending the weekend here. Parking is valet only but there is a parking garage a block away on 6th Ave that is just a short walk away. Lou and Mickey's steak house is downstairs and an excellent place to have a nice dinner.

title: “Many more pluses than minuses”
text: I've stayed at this hotel a few times for business. The hotel is truly located in Chinatown but you're only 1 block to the TransAmerica building and the rest of the financial district. The location is truly fantastic since San Francisco is a beautiful walking city and you'll get to different neighborhoods easily from here. Out front, the hotel has a spacious driveway which it much more convenient for arrival by taxi/car than other hotels in the city that don't have a real driveway. The lobby has beautiful, ornate Chinese lacquer furniture. The reception/check-in are friendly and efficient everytime I've arrived. The hotel has been kind enough to let me have early check-in when I've arrived before 11am. For a big hotel, there are only 4 elevators. There was one morning when some elevators must have been taken out of service because I waited more than 6 minutes for an elevator. I've stayed in the standard king bedroom. The room is about 300 sq ft. It's competently modernized, though not on the high-end in terms of material and design. The bed is comfortable. The TV is a bit small for a king room, about 27''. The blinds are manual operated. The bathroom has decent room, but it'd be difficult for 2 adults to start a morning at the same time in there. The toiletries are high-end Peter Thomas Roth. There's an umbrella in the room for those days when the fog turns into showers. All in all, this hotel has many more pluses than minuses.

title: “2nd Stay At This Hotel”
text:
This is the second time my husband & I have stayed at this hotel. The general concensus is that for the price, you can't beat this hotel. And I have to agree whole heartedly. It is so conveniently located. 
Many people have reviewed the hotel and complained about the noisy air conditioning, small rooms & old elevators. But, my feeling is that you're not staying there for these reasons. You're staying for the convenience to all that New York has to offer. My husband & I love NY and we would stay here again in a minute!

title: “all-u-can-eat-breakfast”
text: yeah the people were nice especially the filipinos. had a great 9-day stay there with us filipino policemen (PNP). the place was near sta monica beach, promenade, catholic church, best buy, yoshinoya, subway, fbi, etc.

title: “Valet sucks!”
text:
I stayed at the Loews Philadelphia Hotel from July 21-July 24. Impressive....far from it! Luxury....not even close. First of all, it is located in City Center, central downtown Philly, so you must use valet parking. I researched the hotel before I traveled so I knew this was my only option. Each day, I followed protocol, calling ahead 15 minutes from my room, got downstairs and waited 40 minutes or more for my car. At $35/day at a "luxury, high standard, customer service" hotel, this was poor. On one occasion, they asked to see my ticket 5 times as if they couldn't find my car. As a frequent watcher of "parking wars - Philadelphia version", this alarmed me immediately. 
The cotton ball/cotton swab jar in the room was so dusty that I steered clear of it. 
On my last night, my room was clean and serviced but they left me no wash cloths. I called the front desk 4 times in a hour to be told they were out of them and I would get some as soon as they got them. WHAT? A freaking "luxury" hotel that doesn't have wash cloths. You must be kidding me!!
The only good thing about the hotel is 24 hour room service which was very prompt and the concierge desk (all of them were kind, friendly, and accomodating).
Considering this is my second stay in Philadelphia in 6 months, I will never stay her again. It is not worth the luxury title!

title: “Would stay again”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel during the July 4th holiday. I figured that this would be a very busy time in the city and was surprised to get what I thought was a good deal on this hotel. It is an older building with renovations on the inside. The lobby has a very cute and relaxing feel to it. 
Our flight plans changed and we got to Boston much earlier than planned. The person at the desk was great. It was 9 am and he found us a room so that we could check in early. The room is a little smaller than what we were used to with hotels, but how long are you actually in the room. The bathroom is tiny, yes, but it worked for us. I put toiletries on the back of the toilet instead of the sink. The decor of the room is very modern and contemporary (which i love). There is turn down service later in the day, when they leave you bottled water in your room (a plus!).
This hotel is in a great location. The train is very close, which you can also take to/from the airport for much less than a taxi. It was a very short walk to the hotel from the train with luggage, which i didnt mind.
The staff was ALWAYS friendly and if asked a question, they were more than willing to help. We experienced a problem with electricity in our room and once they were told about it, they fixed it right away.
Overall, this was a good hotel and I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Saved the day!”
text: The hotel staff really went above and beyond to assist my husband and me during our stay at Hotel Edison. We were travelling from Canada en route to Puerto Rico for a cruise and decided to spend a day in NYC. Well, that seemed like a fantastic idea when we booked the trip months in advance....not exactly the case when I found myself 6 weeks pregnant and sicker than I have ever been in my life. I had a miserable flight down from Canada, was horribly ill and on the verge of a complete breakdown when we arrived at the hotel at 8:30am. I had checked in advance about early check-ins, due to the popularity of the hotel and being at full capacity nearly all the time, they don't do early check-in. I spoke to the gentleman at the desk, explained the situation, and begged for a room so I could lay down and try to beat the morning sickness. I can only assume I was some pale shade of green at the time. He took one look at me and started clacking away on the keyboard. Within 60 seconds he handed us a key and asked if there was anything else they could do to assist. I burst into tears I was so grateful and thanked him profusely. The room was great, king sized bed, sitting area and a retro bathroom. Once I was able to sleep for a few hours, we spent a lovely afternoon exploring the Big Apple. I cannot thank the staff of the Hotel Edison enough for such wonderful and compassionate customer service. I will reccomend them to anyone I ever speak to regarding accomodations in NYC and will certainly return for another visit down the road.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Unlike many of the reviews before this, I thought the place was rather clean. Initially, I wasn't expecting too much from this hotel but was pleasantly surprised. Amazingly convient: steps from many Express subway lines. One could hear road traffic and subway in our fourth floor one-bedroom suite, but it wasn't too loud. In-room WiFi was fast, and they had both a Mac and a PC for use downstairs along with free printing. Service, however, was a bit slow. If I had any complaints, it would be how the one-bedroom suite wasn't technically a "one bedroom suite," but rather, a one bedroom studio suite. Overall though, not bad, and wouldn't mind coming back if the price is right.

title: “Good location”
text: Andra has a prime location near downtown and Belltown for restaurants and bars. The hotel rooms are quite spacious and the staff is very both friendly and helpful. With great restaurants in the hotel and across the street its perfect if your trip will be rainy!

title: “Sweet 16th Stay”
text:
We travel to San Francisco once or twice a year and want the best of 
everything. . We just came back from a five nighter and experienced 
another great stay. The nicely furnished room was clean, very bright and 
airy with plenty of room, and the king bed was extremely comfortable. 
The bathroom was furnished with extra large, fluffy thick towels that 
were very soft, not old and scratchy, a hair dryer, and Bath and Body 
products. This was a pleasant surprise and not the usual generic bathroom 
products. The hotel again provides a safe environment, decor, and the ambiance as well as the service were all perfect. If you are looking 
for a hotel which is conveniently located to Union Square, San 
Francisco Shopping Centre, Cable Car turnaround, BART or MUNI METRO 
Station, and/or SF MUNI, stay here. We will never stay any where else. The front desk and elevators are so close to the entrance that you can save your energy for the streets of San Francisco. Everyone on this hotel staff that we came in contact with was caring and helpful, appeared to take great pride in their work, and thanked us for staying at the hotel.

title: “Great location/value in NYC”
text: We found this reasonably priced hotel right off Times Square to be clean and convenient. Room was a bit crowded for my husband plus our two teen girls, but we managed and expected as much in the city. With wi-fi and breakfast included & parking across the street, this was the best value I could find in this area. We frequented the little market around the corner & the small bar was just the place for my husband & I to escape one night to watch NCAA playoffs. I especially appreciated how quiet our room was. We'd stay here again!

title: “A Nice Surprise”
text: When our travel agent booked us at a Best Western I was not impressed. I didn't think that after traveling across the country we should end up in a Best Western. However, our agent was right, as usual. We took a taxi for $30 from the airport to the inn - which was another good idea - and were pleased to find the inn to be very nice and in a terrific location. The lobby and check-in were good, the "free" breakfast was a real breakfast including bacon and eggs and our room was of good size. The room and bath were clean and attractive and the bed was very comfortable. Our only negative thought was that it was a bit noisy late in the evening. But we come from VT and are not accustomed to any city noise- and we go to bed earlier than many tourists might. We would recommend the Tuscan Inn.

title: “Nice hotel with a great location in downtown Dallas. Love the concept of night time reception, cookies and breakfast!!”
text: This is a really nice hotel in downtown Dallas. I really like the concept of night time reception, cookies and breakfast included with the room. The room itself was large, clean and in good working order. Only negaitve we had was the elevators were a bit slow.

title: “Hot Breakfast, Hot cookies at night, and drinks on the house. GREAT.”
text: The hotel staff was very friendly and always helped out. My room was just the way I wanted it. Bed was very comfortable. I loved the Hot Breakfast with eggs, sausage, French toast and yogurt. Even orange juice!! We all met in the lounge for drinks at 6 PM. Fresh cookies at night were a good way to enjoy my SWEET dreams. I arranged tranportation to the airport which ended my trip on a VERY good note. No problems - just a nice place to stay away from home.

title: “Unclean and Dated”
text: On the positive, this hotel is well-situated outside of Denver-- near shops and restaurants. The neighborhood was safe and parking was free. The breakfast that was included in the room rate was quite good with many hot and cold options. All of this was over-shadowed by the fact that my daughter awoke with red bites on her torso. I am pretty certain it was bed bugs. The bedspreads and upholstered furniture is dated and just don't seem clean. The pool was another disappointment. It was so murky and dirty you could not see your feet. The hot tub was also broken. One of the elevators was also broken.

title: “Should have stuck to here all along!”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel twice now, once years ago when it was first refurbished, and again on this trip. This was somewhat unplanned. I had departed from an other hotel round the corner ahead of schedule.
The room - a standard king was large, and very comfortable. Great bed, thick duvet, and pillow topped mattress. Despite being at the front of the building and low down near the road the room was very quiet, and so warm that even in the mid winter there was no need for heating.
All the staff where really friendly and the room seemed to be in as good shape as when I first visited (about 5 years ago). for a good rate it's a great choice in manhattan.

title: “Excellent location, view and amenities”
text:
The Clift combines a sweeping view, a prime location and a unique charm that makes it a winner.
Just two blocks off Union Square, this property manages to meld Old World high-end seclusion with modern chic sensibilities. Colored-mirrored elevators combine with stalely redwood-paneled lobby decor for a decadent, yet playful effect.
The rooms are spacious and bright, with grand views of the city. Enormous mirrors and firm beds made the room a pleasure. Windows open to allow the city's breeze to cool you into a deep, relaxing sleep.
The amenities are endless, from concierge services to an extremely well-stocked minibar.
This is a hotel for the person who enjoys luxury, but enjoys it with a modern twist.

title: “good”
text: good value for the cost of the room. very clean. staff was excellent. driver to the airport was excellent and personable.

title: “Great stay”
text: I stayed at this Hampton for a recent business trip to Columbus. As the other reviews stated, this is a brand new facility, and they are doing a nice job keeping it that way. Rooms are up to usual Hampton standards with extra pillows, comfy beds, etc. Nice selection at breakfast- not all carbs like a lot of places serve for breakfast. The front desk staff was friendly and efficient- even asked if I had been inconvenienced since they were resurfacing the parking lot that date (and I wasn't- plenty of parking close by was maintained for guests). No problem recommending this Hampton for other travelers. Also- it is easy access on/off highway, close to Polaris shopping, about a 10 minute drive to Easton shopping as well.

title: “Great stay!”
text: Booked this hotel after several comparisons and reviews. Location is central. Hotel was quiet during our stay but lovely staff attention was still great. Slower paced than NY but what do you expect. Great neighborhood for walking and getting to know more of Downtown Charlotte which is growing by the day. Love the game console connection in room as my husband and I travel with our Wii for fun. Gym is located in adjoining bldg and is sponsored by YMCA. Complimentary if you mention you are staying at the Hilton. Loved my stay will stay here when we come back.

title: “BOG BOX”
text: I cant believe the sheraton would steep that low our rooms were a tack on i think or old offices one or the other painted up 1970 wallpaper and all rooms were entered by having to go through a door that had exit written on it?????? Even the staff wernt sure how to get to it

title: “Very comfortable stay”
text: Stayed at this hotel for 3 nights. This is a new hotel & they are still putting the finishing touches on around the building. We stayed in room 319. The room was very large - 2 beds a sitting area, wardrobe and good size bathroom. Good selection of foods at the breakfast buffet. Indoor salt water pool and gym on property. Good lighting in bathroom. Enjoyed our stay.

title: “Clean, Comfortable room and awesome breakfast options”
text:
Stopped here on a 1 night layover on our way to Europe. Shuttle Service from the Airport was excellent and arrived in a timely manor, after arriving at the Hotel at 1am - we asked the Front Desk staff if the Burger King on the corner 1/2 mile away would still be open, which we were assured it was. After the half mile walk along the dark Houston frontage road to the Burger King it was a little disappointing to find it closed, there was however a convenience store on the same corner, so we were able to get a snack before hitting the sack.
The Room was clean and appointed with several nice amenities including a Fridge & Microwave. Nice sized room and bathroom, very clean with a nice sized LCD TV.
One of the major factors in deciding to go with this hotel was the previously read recommendations about the breakfast. They were not wrong - this hotel offers a full and free breakfast buffet with Hot & Cold food, coffee, juice, cereal, waffles, toast - anything you could ask for before hitting the road. We wondered down from our room at 8am - an hour before breakfast was due to end and the staff were still on hand making sure the options were well stocked. Along with the awesome rate and clean room, I'd certainly recommend this Hotel to anyone travelling with a family.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
We stayed at the hotel for four nights for a conference at the Colorado Convention Center--about three easy blocks away. The double rooms have two queen sized beds that are quite comfortable. There is one desk and a chair as well as another upholstered chair in the room. The bathroom was modest sized with a regular tub/shower. The internet connection was priced at 9.95 along with unlimited phone calls locally and in the US, however, the connection did not work at first. The phone technical support person could not figure out the problem and decided to leave it at that. We fiddled around and figured out that the cable was bad. It worked fine after that. Maid service was good. The exercise room is open 24 hours with a selection of bikes, treadmills, stair steppers and ellipticals each with it's own television. Head sets are provided by the hotel, but bringing your own noise reduction headphones makes a big difference. The adjacent pool is open from early (5 AM?) until 11 PM and is big enough to do laps but has no lap lines to keep waves damped down.
The 16th street walking mall is only a block away and extended in both directions with a nice selection of shops, a movie theater, restaurants. There is a Walgreens on 16th about a block away and north for any sundries.
Overall, it is a great business hotel and would be a very good place to stay if you want to visit downtown Denver.

title: “Beautiful, but a few flaws”
text: This hotel is absolutely beautiful. The rooms are spacious and well appointed. The breakfast was incredible as was the manager's reception. The check out was a mess. The front desk clerks could find no record of my stay or credit card information. I will have to wait until it posts to see if they charged me correctly. Also, when I came home, I was covered in bites. My doctor said it looked like bedbugs. The room was very clean, but they need to change the sleeper sofa and bed linens daily to ensure this doesn't happen again.

title: “brillllliannnnnnnnnttttttttttttttttttttttttttt”
text: First class hotel !! First class location !!! superb staff from bell boy to the management !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! nothing in any previous review are wrong !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Its a complete Oasis in a "City that never sleeps" would reccommend this hotel to anyone !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Brilliantttt !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Mr Medlock

title: “Small and Practical”
text: Was in NYC for five days and four nights for my birthday. My first thought when we entered the lobby was it had a contempoary theme to it and it was nice, but we arrived around 10am and our room was not available so we waited in the lobby. The bellsman will hold your bags (they lock them together with other bags in the lobby area) if you want to explore the city while you wait for your room. Our room was on the 8th floor and it was a simple room with a bed, bathroom, small desk and chair. flat screen TV (mounted on the wall) and a small closet. My trip to NYC was not to be spent in our room but to enjoy the city, so it served its purpose for us to take a hot shower and go to sleep. Although the heating/cooling system was a bit outdated (when we entered the room the AC was on so we turned it off and turned on the heat which took a while for the room to get warm) but we were able to open the window in our room when it became too hot ( I thought that was weird I've never been in a hotel room where you can open the window). So if you are looking for a room where you will have lots of space then get ready to pay for the extra space.... the room was big enough I would not compare it to a closet size room maybe the size of a room that you would find in an older model home from the 70's or 80's but like I said it was practical.

title: “A substandard Hilton by any other name...”
text:
Yes, it SAYS Waldorf-Astoria, but it isn't, not really. This isn't the elegant hotel of the grand old days. This is a Hilton, and not even one of the better Hiltons. Think Hilton Garden with slightly more upscale decor and a gorgeous lobby. Lower your expectations accordingly and you won't be disappointed. 
The rooms, even the renovated rooms, are nothing special. There are some glaring short-cuts taken in the renovations which are simply not acceptable in a luxury hotel (see photos). Service is inconsistent. If you're used to true luxury hotels, you'll spot the differences immediately.
Doormen to assist with luggage? No, they're too busy hailing cabs. Hope you're in good shape and can cart your bags up the stairs from the Park Ave entrance to the lobby by yourself.
If you are Hilton Gold, don't get your hopes up. The room upgrade? That means you get one of the renovated rooms, not a true upgrade. Water? Forget it. No one gets water. That's because the mini-bars are empty. The newspaper of your choice? Only if your choice is USA Today. Some mornings, even that doesn't appear at your door. Access to the gym? Good luck.
Our request for extra towels received the response "that will take a while". They still hadn't arrived by the time we checked out two days later. Turn down service consisted of moving two pillows off the bed and closing the shades.
Contact the management? Sure. How much time do you have to wait on hold? Don't even bother with an email - still waiting on a response a week later. This hotel is definitely not a 5 star.

title: “New Hotel with Responsive Staff”
text: Although some might find it a bit ugly, the Hilton Polaris is new with up-to-date furnishings and fixtures. I found the hotel staff to be quite responsive to my needs. I had a noise problem in an adjacent room. Although I could not be immediately moved because I was told the hotel was full, the hotel staff changed my room at the first available opportunity and made an effort to put me in a room that they thought would be quiet. The hotel is located next to a shopping mall.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Excellent hotel with excellent service from the entire staff. Bill, Brie, Amber, Eden, Juan, Jose and everyone are always ready to help.

title: “Only place to stay in San Francisco”
text: My fiance and I stayed at the Inn for 2 nights in November. Our room was clean and decorated very tastefully. The bed and pillows were super comfortable. The breakfast and afternoon wine/cheese was delicious and really fun. The staff held our bags when we arrived early and sent them to our room when it was ready. We had the opportunity to chat with some of the cleaning staff and they are wonderful.. most have been working for the Inn for 20 years -- I think that is probably unheard of that line of service. Totally recommend staying here and when we go back to San Fran - this is the only hotel that we will think about staying in.

title: “Location Is The Only Good Thing”
text:
I have stayed at several different hotels in NYC and this one was by far my least favorite. The location (1/2 a block from Times Square) is the only thing good about this hotel. I took this trip with a few friends of mine. We booked two separate rooms each with two double beds. When we arrived at the hotel we were told they were out of the rooms with double beds and could only offer us on double bed and could bring up a roll away bed. The roll away bed was not comfortable at all but surprisingly it was more comfortable than the actual bed which was hard as a rock. The pillows were very flat and hard and I slept much better without it. 
If you want to stay in Times Square, spend a little extra money for a better hotel or you could always stay in one of the other fabulous NYC neighborhoods.

title: “And the winner is.........”
text:
I was in Houston for business and I needed to stay close enough to MD Anderson Cancer Center. Unfortunately, the Houston Hilton Plaza/Medical Center was booked as well as some other Hiltons so I decided to go with the Double Tree Hilton and I am so happy I did. My flight from New York arrived early so I was prepared to wait around in the lobby until it was close to check in time. However as I walked into the hotel, I was greeted by the valet drivers so warmly that I decided to take my chances and see if they would let me get a room. Well, there was a lovely lady Shelly who checked me in and off I went to my room with my card keys and warm chocolate chip cookie. My room was great. The hotel is conveniently located in the downtown area of Houston. Luckily for me, I did not have to go far to find something to eat. There is a Food Court located in the lower level of the adjoining building. This worked for me as I was able to order some food and take it back to the room. I snuggled under the covers, watched tv, caught up on some reading and prepared for the next day. In the evening, I went to the gym which is on the 4th floor. The gym is small but adequately equipped with sufficient workout machines/weights, etc. There are clean towels, water cooler, a basket which would hold the complimentary head phones. On my first visit, there were no head phones and I called the front desk - Shelly answered, within minutes, someone had come in and refilled the baskets with head phones. 
The down side was that there was no free WiFi (not good for business travelers). The business center was close to the lobby and in the open area (no privacy).
Overall, the staff was very kind, attentive and made me feel comfortable. The DoubleTree Hilton was great. In fact, I would dare say that they made me feel like a million bucks - in my eyes, they are the winner.

title: “Good value”
text:
Clean, spacious hotel at the end of the Riverwalk and close to everything. The free breakfast and afternoon hors d' oeuvres make this a real value. If you like Art Deco you'll love the lobby with 50 foot high ceilings, WPA type murals and a Model A Ford - a real treat.
The hotel would have rated 5 stars but the room had several maintenance items that the hotel dealt with in a half hearted manner. The maintenance man showed up prompty and fussed a bit but when he left the cabinet doors still wouldn't close and there were still tacks in the carpet. Really too bad.

title: “JW Marriott very nice hotel”
text: Our family of 3 recently stayed at the JW Marriott Hotel in Washington, DC and were very impressed with the rooms and amenities of this hotel. The hotel is huge but we couldn't have had faster, more prompt service. The rooms are fairly standard for a JW Marriott and nicely appointed. The bathrooms are a bit small but nice. The only downside is the lack of a fan in the bathroom--which makes it rather hot after showering. We had a room on the 9th floor with a GORGEOUS view of the Washington monument. It was amazingly quiet at night despite the fact that this can be a bustling area. I didn't hear a single siren or any outside noise while sleeping. Unusual in DC! We chose the JW for its proximity to an event we were attending at the National Press Club (directly next door) so the location was perfect. The hotel is also extremely close to the White House and surrounding sights. The lobby bar/restaurant is HOPPING at night -- great ambiance, good drinks and food and seemingly the "place to be" on a Thursday night. We had a great time there with a group of friends. Overall, this is a wonderful property with a very good staff and great service. I personally prefer to stay in the Foggy Bottom/Georgetown area because that is where I spend most my time, but if looking for a hotel in the downtown area, I would definitely stay at the JW Marriott again.

title: “No Hospitality Here! Bugged!!”
text:
Many other comparable hotels in the area to spend money with you...customer service stinks!!
First, we were put in a king room reserved for handicapped citizens. Whoever designed the hotel didn't consider the shower floor for any guest. Very European in design, however, the tiles were so large that anyone who showers on these tiles slip and slide and causes issue for agile guests; not to mention handicapped citizens.
Secondly, we requested a late check-out to be at 1:00 p.m. Communication between night manager and day manager didn't occur. I was bugged by the Maid, front desk clerk, and the walls were banged on "appearing to want me out" much earlier than the 1:00p.m. check-out.
I was lied to when I was told that my husband had turned in his key (which he never did)..that is why they were confused. WOW! Customer Service NOT! 
You all must be proud of your hotel! Your customer service is lousy and we won't be back!!!!

title: “Overall a nice hotel for the price.”
text: Disclosure! I am on business not vacation, so my review is based on the one and done premise. A different hotel tomorrow. This hotel in Jacksonville is nice because of the price and location. There are a few restaurants close and manageable to get to with a short drive or a casual walk down the sidewalk. The only real negative is the breakfast. Went in an hour before closing and they're was hardly anything left. They were not replacing anything. I actually waited for a while to see if they would, but no one even acted concerned. All in all I would stay again. But if breakfast is something you banked on I would look somewhere else.

title: “You can stay elsewhere in San Diego for a better value.”
text:
I stayed at the Sheraton the weekend of 03/04/-03/06 on a solo trip for myself and I expected a bit more. It was a overall ok hotel but the fact they charge you for everything and I mean everything makes absolutely no sense to me at all. $14.00 a day to park in the parking lot for real?? Not even a garage or Valet but self parking $14.00 is nuts. Then they want $9.95 for internet? Had I had known this I would have never stayed there. I travel a lot and most of the hotels I stay at offer free wi-fi nothing personal but they are better than the sheraton and I do not pay for internet services nor self parking. Then they have the bottled water in your room with a price tag of $4.00 what is the purpose? This might be minor to others but was big for me.
The last part is the fact that housekeeping woke me up not once but twice to clean my room after I answered like 3 tiimes they still persisted to come in and ask after I said "No" I could not fall back to sleep so that kind of ruined my first day of rest and my second as they did it both days. The concierge is nice they are very helpful but thats about it. The room is basic just with a large LCD TV nothing major no real amenities I should have stayed at the Hyatt in Mission bay as I was going to next time I will. Would I reccomend this to my friends no...it's not worth what I Payed personally your in. The Sheraton is now in the same class to me as Hampton inn.

title: “Would definitely stay there again.”
text: Great room - big, clean as was bathroom. Whole hotel looked very nice. Staff was friendly. DIdn't get to use pool, but it looked very nice also. I was disappointed in the breakfast though. My husband had raved about HIX breakfasts and he said this wasn't up to par for HIX.

title: “It's Just OK”
text:
Booked our 4 day stay because of a great stay at the same chain in Boise, ID years ago. We arrived to a nice looking hotel. Lobby had some over-scented aroma that my husband said, "Smells like they spilled a lot of Fabreeze." Very unpleasant--but did eventually fade to a reasonable level. Very modern looking and completely different than the hotel in Boise.
--Location
Close to Lackland Valley View gate. 15 min from airport and about 20-25 from Riverwalk.
--Room
very thin walls. Had one night of sound problems from the room above--the hotel staff took care of in a reasonable amount of time. You could hear very loud toilet flushing sounds from rooms next door. Maid service late afternoon. Uncomfortable hide-a-bed.
--Bathroom
No bathtub. Bathroom split into 2 separate rooms with frosted glass doors.There were some maintenance issues, large cracks in tile floor, big scratch in center of bathroom mirror, stains on the carpet, our door needed some adjusting--would catch and be difficult to open at times. burned out light next to our door never taken care of.
--breakfast
1 waffle maker that had a long line whenever we were at breakfast. Very, very slow toasters. Food selection was fine. Hot and cold options.
--pool
very small and indoor, no hot tub. Not that you would want one in the hot weather here.
I have mixed feelings about our stay. On one hand it was a nice hotel--on the other the issues we experienced above.

title: “Fantastic Holiday at the Holiday Inn”
text:
My partner and I drove from LA to San Diego without a booking or map and found the Holiday Inn Bayside quite by accident. What a find! Super friendly and helpful staff. Lovely restaurant and bar. Spacious clean room. All the facilites we needed. Our rooms were made up every day and restocked with coffee etc. We didn't have a view of the water but had a balcony to sit out on overlooking the pool that was very relaxing. 
Point Loma / Bayside is the perfect location to base yourself in San Diego. 5 minute drive to all the sites and the hotel had easy to follow driving directions to them. And free parking. There's a great pizza restaurant across the road (Nova) and the next block along has shops and a full compliment of junk food take-a-way places if you're into that sort of thing.
The best part was the price considering we didn't book or members of any clubs etc, and because we liked it so much we stayed an extra 2 nights. The staff were very accomodating and very helpful. We wish we could have stayed even longer!
And a tip if you intend to go to TJ - park on the US side and walk. It's 10 mins and you avoid all the queues and traffic.

title: “Worst stay for me and my family”
text: Rooms are terrible not hot wather , TV not working ,housekeeping 0, my kind found under the bad vibrator, my little kid. The front desk stuff very improfesional , after all this things happen I ask to talk with manager. The manager her name was Blanca and she was more improfesional then the stuff at the desk. terrible terrible terrible won't stay or recomand this place for anyone

title: “Not worth it”
text:
My fiance and I stayed for a business/travel weekend in October 04. I had reserved and confirmed a non-smoking room with a king size bed with my credit card. When we arrived we were told that no such rooms were available and that we could either stay in a smoking room or a room with a double bed. The management was less than helpful and were actually condescending. They made no effort to honor the reservation that was held with a credit card and offered us nothing to compensate for their error.
Also, the room was very small and noisy throughout the night.
We will never stay there again and will never recommend it to a friend.

title: “Wonderful Stay!”
text: My boyfriend took me to Philly for my birthday last year. We were very happy with our stay at the Homewood Suite!! We drove from the DC area and had a little trouble finding the hotel at first. I called and we quickly found it after that. Check in was easy. I believe we were on Floor 2 or 3. We were suprised how high the celings were. We had a standard room, king bed, small living area, and a kitchenette. I must say, the bed was heaven!!! Once you layed down, you could fall right to sleep. I fell asleep at 8 pm one night because I was so comfortable. The breakfast every morning was wonderful! Better that most other hotels free breakfast. One morning it got a bit crowded downstairs, so we just piled our plates with food, and took it back to our room. One thing to keep in mind, this hotel is not in the downtown part of the city. The hotel is situated right next to a college, so we felt pretty safe walking to and from the hotel to our car. The city was quite spotty with its shady neighborhoods though. Because we are unfamiliar with the city, we are happy we didn't choose a hotel downtown. Since we drove, we had a car to get around and didn't have too much of a problem with parking. You MUST go to Reading Terminal Market. We ate lunch there every day. There were so many choices!! Pat's Famous Cheesestakes is located in the market. We parked in a garaged the first day and walked around a city. I suggest finding an actual garage. I'm not quite sure what we parked in, but we decided not to go back there again. Anywho, we enjoyed walking aroud the city, although we were unsure about some areas. We did visit the museaum with the King Tut exhibit. SUCH A WASTE OF TIME!! We though we would see the actual scarcofagus. All you see is an image. Not worth it. We did enjoy drinking at a bar that is located across the street from Reding Terminal Market though. We met a very friendly guy who had recently gotten off work and dropped by for a drink. He attempted to tell us some things to do while visiting Philly. We also visited the Zoo. We had a wonderful time here. Very nice zoo, you definitely get what you pay for. Being from DC where the zoo is free, I was pleasently surprised how much nicer Philadelphia's Zoo exhibits where. We also visited the Art Musueam. It is a beautiful building, although they were doing work on the outside. We went on a Sunday when admission is free, so I suggest going then. It was a beautiful museaum. On Sat. evening we drove out to the King of Prussia mall. Anyone who loves shopping should visit it, however it has stores you will find in any decent mall. We made a night of it and did some shopping, had dinner, and went to a movie. In all, we both had a great time in Philly and cannot wait to go back.

title: “Cosmopolitan Hotel, Okay stay”
text: The staff at the hotel are fabulous. Rooms are very small, which is okay, yet there was one thing I did not like and had to switch rooms. My first room had the A/C unit level with the bed so the fan would have been blowing directly on me. (Room 503) Room 227 was bigger and had very tall ceilings - the A/C unit was high as in I couldn't reach it but there was a remote. As mentioned, the bathrooms are small. The room was clean. The bed and pillows were okay. As for the location, you are downtown.....walking distance to the 9/11 memorial. There is a very good restaurant across the street called Eccol. Back to the hotel...the elevators were slow. Overall it was a good experience once I changed rooms. I was on a work trip and there were many of us who did change rooms...again, the staff was wonderful in helping us.

title: “Great Anniversary Get-A-Way”
text: The location of this great hotel places it within walking distance of the bay, shopping, great restaurants and the sports facilities. We were able enjoy a baseball game and it was an easy walk to and from Safeco Field. We were able to use the monorail to visit Seattle Center since it is located at the hotel and shopping center. Great room and Excellent Service!!!!!!!!

title: “Loved it and amazing service.”
text: When i first arrived the service and greeting was so nice it made a very good first impression. I got to my room and at first glance i thought "this is a bit dodgy" however after staying in there the room had everything i needed and was very comfortable. There was no air conditioning but i was there in hot weather and at night you do not need air con at all. The hotel is in a great spot close to the monorail and lots of great restaurants. The bed was very comfy and my room had a great tv and also a dvd player which i thought was a nice touch, so i could watch my own movies. I would highly recommend this hotel because of the great location and fantastic service. It is also right across the road from a Safeway which was nice and handy. Having Starbucks in the bottom of the hotel was awesome as well.

title: “Horrible, I am out of here!”
text: The location is terrible. It is located close to sea world but it seems unsafe. you can hear every movement of the people in the rooms around you. Its very loud and the room is nasty. The carpet is so stained I dont want to walk on it. The bed is clean but not comfortable. I was supposed to stay 6nights but I am staying one and moving to days inn on hotel circle. I will make a post there once I see how that place is. All I can say is DONT COME HERE!

title: “The best hotel value I have ever experienced in New York City.”
text: The Mansfield is a wonderful surprise. I was initially quite concerned about what awaited me because the price was so low for a New York hotel. However, the room cwas spotless with a large flat panel TV and free wireless internet. There is a small but excellently equipped gym and the breakfasts, which were also included, terrific. In addition to the wonderful dining room/bar, there is a wonderful cozy library where you can read newspapers and have a drink. The New York Times is also free in the breakfast room. In addition, the staff are terrifically helpful and friendly. I will certainly recommend The Mansfield Hotel to all and above all look forward to returning.

title: “Great Stay”
text: I stayed at Omni Hotel at Park West for 2 nights in March 2005, with 2 friends. We got a great deal on the internet ($89 a night) and the hotel was excellent. I didn't think it's possible to get a hotel so great for so cheap. The service was great, the people were friendly, and we had a good time. We got a regular room with 2 queen beds. The room was very clean, spacious, and comfortable. The bar on the first floor has good food and drinks for a reasonable price. There is nothing within walking distance from the hotel and Dallas is about 20 to 30 min drive away. The hotel parking structure provides plenty of parking.

title: “Fantastic place to stay!”
text: Love this place! Had to stay at a hotel near the airport (Houston Bush Intercontinental) when Hurricane Sandy derailed my flight plans to New York. United Airlines had recommended Fairfield to me and said to call and ask for them and United even gave me a discount voucher for interrupted travel which cut quite a bit off the price of the room. The room was beautiful and clean, nice king sized bed, free wifi, and they even throw a dinner for you for free. Its a 'social' as they call it and quite a few guest came out for it and it's completely free and they do it quite well. Got a great burger, fries, salad, chips and drinks all for free with fresh ingredients and the burgers were tasty and they serve free breakfast as well. Bathrooms are clean and towels are soft. Very happy with the staff too! Nicole up front at the desk is a sweetheart and very professional and accommodating. I can't think of a bad thing to say about this place!

title: “Nice place to stay in SF, convenient for shops & restaurants”
text: I stayed at The Handlery for a girls night out of shopping and a birthday dinner. I asked for a room away from Geary Street and the reservationist at the front desk was very courteous and professional and I did indeed get a room away from the busy street. Great room, immaculate, comfy bed, and room service was prompt and friendly. There are 2 hotels and are connected by a walk way which was a bit confusing, but got the hang of it. I parked my car in their garage and that worked out very well, great service there also. I would definately stay there again. I booked my room through bookit.com and got a terrific price, much lower than my friends who did not use the inet for a booking.

title: “Great location!”
text: Stayed for a work event. The location can't get any better for those wanting to walk around the city and explore (but keep in mind it's a uphill walk coming back from Pike's Market... we can all use some exercise though). Check-in staff was pleasant. I appreciate the MAKE A GREEN CHOICE - 500 points! I see people complaining about paying for wifi... if you sign up for SPG rewards then wifi is free people! There is a beverage they have in the lobby during the afternoon that runs out too fast. Please refill it! It's delicious! My favorite part of the W chains - Bliss products and soft sheets! The halls could use a little better lighting (i know it's the trendy thing but it makes it difficult during the work conference to find the restrooms). Oh and the restroom by ball rooms need to be maintained especially if there is an event going on as it got pretty sloppy by mid afternoon.

title: “Very Decent Hotel”
text: We stayed here one night, and for the price we got, it was a great hotel. Very basic room with slight funny odor, but clean. The bed was amazingly comfortable and I slept like a baby. The breakfast was a typical hotel breakfast. If I was on a budget, I'd definitely stay here again.

title: “Not the best stay this time”
text: I have stayed here numerous times, and have usually had a wonderful experience, however this time was different. Check in was fast and the gal at the front desk was very friendly. Was not told that the hot tub was out of service, found that out after changing and entering pool area. The gal at the front desk then said we could use the pool at the property next door. Just would have been nice to know of this before booking or atleast upon checking in. Wanted to take the shuttle to the airport for supper, and to ask questions about my flight at the ticket counter the evening before my flight. The shuttle driver drove up ...threw peoples bags out, and before I could get on the shuttle...he drove off. I walked over to Super 8 and asked if I could get on their shuttle...they said no problem. (the driver even recognized me later on and stopped and offered a ride back) The following morning there was a reciept slipped under my door, and the price I was charged was not the price that I reserved for...so I went to the desk and the gentleman that was there was extremely rude and said that I should have said something when I signed the card at check in...I guess I didnt notice it then as I had been driving all day and was tired. (he fixed it but was rude) Then the others that I was traveling with had the same problem with over charging, and same rude comment to them. Breakfast was skimpy, and the coffee was empty on 2 different trips to the breakfast room that morning before 8 am. It may be time to check out other hotels in the area. I feel bad for those I have recommended to this hotel, as it has truely been wonderful in the past. Carpeting in the hallways needs to be replaced, as its a hazard with all of the big ripples in it.

title: “Lovely Hotel”
text:
My Partner and I stayed at the Beverley Garland for four nights from 23rd May 2011 and loved it here. We were very tired after a long flight from Australia and asked the check-in lady if we could have a quiet room so that we could get a good sleep before exploring LA. The room we were given was great - lovely and quiet in a wing away from the main area of the hotel. The room was very clean with a beautiful comfortable bed and a great shower! Two things that are important to travellers! There was also a coffee maker which we found other hotels that we stayed at did not provide. We love a cuppa before we get going in the morning and cannot understand why other hotels don't provide this basic service. Also another bonus at the Beverley Garland was having a guest laundry in the building we were in. It was great being able to do some laundry before heading to San Fransisco. All these things are included in most hotels in Australia but the Beverley Garland was the only place we had these in America - so thanks heaps!
We used the free shuttle a few times and this also is a great service. Very convenient.
A big thankyou to the ladies in the gift shop for all their help also. They go out of their way to help with any question a tourist has and also have well priced souveniers and little extras that a guest might need.
Overall, we found everyone at the BG was very helpful and friendly and a lovely place to stay.
Would definitely stay here again.

title: “As classy as they come!”
text: Four Seasons' brand new entry into the Denver market is a gorgeous place. Everything is what we've come to expect of Four Seasons. Lovely, calming modern architecture and decor. Spacious rooms. Capable, professional staff. Luxury in every way. Good downtown location. Plus the weekend rates are very reasonable. Don't pass up an opportunity to stay at this one.

title: “Humphreys is a winner”
text: We booked the "One Enchanted Evening" package for our anniversary and had an enjoyable stay. We arrived early and our room was ready. The gentleman at the front desk was very friendly and professional, as was every staff member we ran into. We had a bay view room which wasn't exactly on the bay. There was a parking lot, street, and a grassy parkway between the hotel and the bay, but we just put chairs up by the window and when we sat down we could only see the bay which was nice. We walked down the path to the end of the island and when we returned to the room there was a HUGE basket of fruit and king-sized candy bars plus a bottle of nice champagne. You get to keep the glasses as part of the package. It was very relaxing sitting at the window snacking on fruit and drinking the champagne and watching all the boats sail by on the bay.
