The room was very well appointed and nicely decorated. The bathroom was beautiful with granite counter tops and around the tub. The room was spotless and well-insulated from noise. The only complaint about the room was that it was the size of a postage stamp. There was barely room to put the chairs between the bed and the window, and maybe 18 inches of space between the other side of the bed (king) and the wall. It did have high sloped ceilings which helped. There was a concert the night of our stay and even though we didn't have tickets, we were able to sit on a small balcony and listen. The pool area was very nice, and the rest of the grounds were wonderful and full of tropical landscaping. We checked out the rooms on the marina side which I thought had a much nicer view because they were right on the marina with a nice balcony or a patio and a little grassy area (no parking lot), but my husband thought our bay room view was better because the ships and boats were moving in the water, rather than tied up to berths. I guess it just depends on what you're looking for. In the morning we recieved breakfast in bed and the food was presented nicely and the room service was actually 5 minutes early. The food was good, not exactly outstanding, but room service food never is. To sum it all up, I felt the only negative about our stay was the small (albiet spotlessly clean and beautifully decorated) room, but the great service, super-friendly staff, beautiful grounds, and relaxing atmosphere made Humphreys a winner.

title: “Boston on a budget”
text: This hotel is an excellent option for those on a budget as it has a substantial free buffet breakfast, free airport shuttle and free shuttle to three drop off points in Boston. The rooms are comfortable, however the front of the hotel is on a main road and is noisy. The nearest subway is about 7 blocks away, however we found the shuttles more than covered our needs. The hotel has a diner attached to it (Rudi's) which has good food and is good value. The hotel also provides free coffee, tea, hot chocolate and cookies in the lobby. Despite the noise, I would recommend this hotel and suggest you ask for a room at the rear of the hotel.

title: “Great Weekend....”
text:
We stayed at the Hard Rock Hotel in Chicago and had a great experience. From the valet parking to checking in was super easy. We got therebefore the 3:00pm check in time, but since our room was ready, they let us check in early. Our room and view was great!!! The rooms are pretty modern and each floor has a rock star theme! The location is close to shopping and not too far from Millennium park. You can pretty much walk everywhere. There is also a Walgreens right in front of the hotel in case you forget anything. 
We had to check out by noon, but we still had plans, so they can check your bags and you can come back and get them when your done. They also have the Chicago Tribune for free in the lobby for there guest, which I thought was great! Let me know if you have any questions.

title: “Doesn't disappoint. but oh those elevators”
text:
We have stayed here 4 times now and still love the Marquis. We had good service from front desk, in lounge, and from housekeeping. Admittedly we weren't there all that long this time so didn't use all services. But nothing beats the 8 fl lounge for nice cocktails, maybe the cheese platter, and a fantastic view of Times Square. You can also get literally ANYWHERE you want to go in just minutes from this hotel.
I did call the concierge for show tickets as I was told they can do that, but they forwarded me to a ticket service without saying that was what they were doing. The Marquis is also pretty overpriced. We paid about $550/ni and it is nothing more than a nice Marriott room. But we did have a nice flat screen tv, plenty of room, and a view of Times Square. So we just swallow the cost and enjoy the superb location, nice room, and good service.
The only thing is tha tthis trip the elevators were HORRIBLE. We had thought since they put in the new elevator system it was better, but we almost were late for a show after waiting sooooo long for an elevator. When one finally came to our floor we just squeezed in and held our breath.
I would stay again. And hope the price doesn't go up....

title: “Perfect location”
text: The location couldn't be better. Rooms were great. The only downside is that the wifi is so expensive. I think it was $13 per day. At the price of the room I think this is unacceptable. The beds are really comfortable.

title: “Rerun visitor and would stay again”
text: This was my second visit to the Pod (last visit in 2007). This time went with my sister and stayed in a bunk room with shared bathroom. Bathrooms very clean and we never had to wait for one. Rooms clean with daily maid service and fresh towels. The room was bigger than we thought it would be woth ample storage space for 2. Location great. Ess-a-bagel on 51st and second is a must for breakfast and is a bit of an institution. Hope to come back soon.

title: “Not the best”
text: The first room I was given the toilet and telephone did not work. There were two used hand towels hanging on the shower curtain rod. After notifying the front desk clerk, he was very accomodating and moved me to another room. The door on the second room was not closed when I went to it, so I was a little concerned. The rooms are in need of updates. The carpet and bedspread were worn and seemed dirty. Complimentary "breakfast" was coffee and 5 dried out mini muffins. I probably would not stay here again.

title: “An Average Hotel- Except for View”
text: Despite some of the reviews on this site, this is a thoroughly average hotel. It has received a light makeover from its past life as a Holiday Inn, but isn't at the level of the Pan Pacific or Omni. The only distinguishing thing for this hotel is the view from the side that faces Coit Tower.

title: “Not the best location for convention stays”
text: I stayed here during a week at a conference at the convention center. I have mixed feelings about my choice. Although it was only a mile away, it seemed a lot further than the hotels that were located east of the convention center. It feels like it is located away from everything else. If you want to go out for dinner with coworkers and such, you will be dining in restaurants that are much closer to the other hotels near the Gaslamp Quarter than they are to this one. Then if you walk back at night, you will most likely be walking by homeless people who are setting up their beds for the night. Other than the proximity to the convention center, I felt like this was a good place to stay. We stayed in the south tower, so we were a little bit detached from the main building. You might want to consider that if you are planning to use any of the amenities located in the main building. One of the elevators in our building had a view of the ocean which was always a nice perk if it was the one to take us up. I don't have any concerns about the room. It was clean, roomy, and well-equipped. I liked having the sink in a separate area rather than behind the bathroom door with the toilet and shower. We had a view of the ocean from our room. It was great at night and early morning, but in the middle of the day it wasn't as relaxing. There was a lot of traffic on Harbor Drive. In addition, there was a lot of construction right in front of the hotel. With all of that noise, I just wanted to shut the door. The hotel only has paid parking. We only had a car on our first and last day, so we were interested in finding a place to park to get the car loaded and unloaded. There are a few free parking spaces near the front door, but this wasn't very convenient to the south tower. There are also a few metered spaces on A St on the east side of the hotel, and there are metered spaces across the street. We used the shuttle a few times, but it only ran 4 times a day.

title: “Great experience overall, location is second to none”
text:
I stayed a couple of nights with my husband in a second floor room facing St. Mark's blvd. The room was tiny (about 10 x 10), but clean and comfortable with a queen bed against one wall, small mounted flat screen TV, large window to view the busy street below, sparse utilitarian furniture (only room to hang a few clothing items and a shelf). There was a 24 hr pizza place on the first floor. The bathroom was tiny, but clean. The staff were very friendly, helpful and accommodating, which makes a great impression despite the no-frills nature of the room. The location is perfect if you intend to see, smell and experience life in "the City". There are plenty of extremely interesting and exotic restaurants nearby - Japanese, Afghani, Ukrainian, Italian, Irish, just about every culture is represented. Lots of cool bars and interesting stores. The subway access is only a block away. We parked at a garage, also a block away - it was expensive (valet) at $24 a day, but worth it since we didn't want to have to walk a long way with all our luggage.
I would definitely recommend this hotel for youngish couples and singles who are mostly interested in a cool, clean, safe place to sleep and park your stuff in while you venture out to explore the city. The location is so convenient that you can keep returning to the room to rest or stash your shopping bags. I would not recommend the hotel for people with mobility problems due to the narrow steep stairs and small bathroom, or people with excessive amounts of baggage or small children. Also, light sleepers may want to request a room facing the back of the hotel, but you will miss the view of the busy street which is interesting itself.

title: “A long walk from american food”
text:
This hotel is pleasant, has great parking facilities, the staff are friendly. BUT, stay away from the attached restaurant, unless you are Korean. I sat and waited to be served for 20 minutes, after which I got up and walked out. I was seated, and given menus, but no one came to take my order. They kept looking at me, and I made it clear that I was ready to order, but no. The rest of the clientele were Korean and were being served regularly and politely.
It is also a long walk to find many restaurants which do not serve weather Korean food or Sushi. Give it it's due, it is in the middle of Koreatown, but still.... I would have liked a few more American restaurants to choose from. As it stood, I had a Sizzlers round the corner.
The room was also covered in some else's hair when I got in it, and it still was after the cleaners had been in the next morning. I had to leave a note for them asking for it to be thoroughly hoovered before they did anything about it.

title: “Meh -”
text: Decent hotel for the money. Basically clean (except for the large amount of hair in the linnens). Furnishings are showing their age, but overall not terrible.

title: “Quality and value”
text: We booked this hotel for a 4 night stay on the strength of reviews on this site, having previously always stayed in the Mag Mile area. This hotel was cheaper than places we had stayed before, and we thought we might be compromising on location, but we actually found this was far more convenient for all areas of the city. The hotel was super - the room was large, comfortable and clean and the bathroom spotless. Certainly it was more comfortable than some of our previous uptown choices . We had a room on the front and did not hear any street noise. The breakfast buffet and the happy hour were both great bonuses and we found both to be well stocked with lots of choice. All of the staff we met were friendly and professional. We will definitely consider staying here again next time we visit Chicago.

title: “Not bad but Valet people are not friendly”
text:
I booked our stay in this hotel via Priceline bidding and paid 292 dollar for 2 nights which is not bad. We arrived in the afternoon and they gave us a room on the 6th floor. First thing we noticed was that the airconditioning made a lot of noise so after we parked our car in the Common Garage (cheaper and nearby) we called the front-desk and they send someone who switched the airco off with a hidden button.
Our stay was OK but the VALET people were not friendly at all.
According to the hotel it's allowed to park for 15 minutes during check-in and check-out. They seemed not so happy when you ask for this and they directly tell you that if you're not back within 15 minutes they start charging you. I explained that I will be as fast as possible but that I depend on the front-desk-lines...
No excuse... "we will charge you if you're not back in 15 minutes"
Location is perfect and there are some nice restaurants nearby.

title: “good”
text: We had been to sfo and had stayed here.The location is very good. We were able to get the cable car and the taxis easily.We enjoyed our stay here.the rooms are spacious,airy and neat and clean.The property is good.

title: “I would stay again”
text: This hotel was clean and in a great location. Pretty standard Courtyard Marriott, but it seems to be fully living up to the expectation. The room was spacious and the decor was nice. The front desk staff was friendly and their is complementary internet in the rooms and free parking. I did find that the water from the sink and tub were yellow when you initially turned it on (maybe that's a Houston issue, I don't know). Overall, it was a pretty good place to stay and I would stay again.

title: “Very pleasant experience”
text:
My wife and I spent three nights at the Westin over the past weekend on a business/pleasure trip. As a Starwood Preferred guest got a deal on a suite.
Couldn't have been more pleased. Suite was huge. Hotel was quiet, even though NBA playoffs were beginning (the Lakers were in the hotel!). On the quiet side of the Riverwalk, a short, pleasant stroll to all the action. Heavenly bed is a bit overrated, but the bathroom more than compensates. Instead of room service ($$$), go to the small snack stand on the lower level. Large sandwich, pastry, and two soft drinks were only $10. Unlike previous raters, had no problem with valet parking. We will be back in San Antonio next year, and will go to the Westin.

title: “Room with a view; almost!”
text:
Location of the Hudson is great. The grounds are fantastic. Rooms are no larger than a postage stamp. In my entire life of travel I've never stayed in a room so small; however ingeniously designed to appear larger at first glance.
The small bathroom was not very clean. For such a tiny space one would think the chamber maids could manage to do a better job. They do a great job at banging around the hall and door areas early morning.
The garden bar area is beautiful but the service is below standard. Brilliant restaurant concept but wouldn't burn a meal there. NYC has far better choices.
For the most part the staff are helpful. They don't seem to care or like their jobs. More like a transit stop to a bigger and better place.

title: “Best value close to San Jose airport”
text: This hotel is a great deal for the following reasons: Location: close to the airport and walking distance to several large hotels that host conferences and conventions. However it is not noisy as it is not under the flight path. Very close to the Airport station of the light rail. There are also several restaurants within walking distance (including a Denny's right by the motel). The neighborhood seemed safe. Room: Somewhat larger than the typical motel room. The bathroom was also nice with floor to ceiling tiles. Everything was clean when I checked in. Wireless internet is free and of good quality. The room had a microwave and fridge. There is free breakfast but it is just juice and danish.

title: “Upscale affordable accommodations”
text: The Ritz is one block off of Michigan Avenue and easily accessible to up scale shopping. Also it is connected to the 8 story Water Tower Place which is a fabulous shopping mall. The concierge had numerous suggestions for quant, intimate restaurants close by. There was a spectacular view of Navy Pier and the lakes from the room.

title: “Stay away”
text: bed buds,drug addicts, rudeness,false advertising,over charging,dirty, nothing works, faulty wiring. Just stay away from here. The rates are WRONG, they have no posted rates so they charge what they want.

title: “Will Stay Again, Definitely!”
text:
Spent a Saturday night at the resort. One bedroom condominium on 2nd floor was excellent. We overlooked the 18th fairway. Had coyotes at night but staff reacted to get them to move along. Concerns about thin walls came to pass in the morning when the couple next to us started yelling - but in any hotel you would have heard these idiots.
Tremendous GOLF COURSE and STAFF! Highly recommend the course!

title: “It's the Good Stuff”
text:
The anticipated visit to this 4-star hotel for its panoramic views, spacious rooms and fine dinning was to be expected. What wasn't, was the extra mile Guest Services Representative Michelle Bennet and her collogue call - "The Good Stuff". This was an added bonus!
A birthday celebration was briefly mentioned by our party during the check in process, when we returned to our room from dinner, there was a complimentary bottle of chilled champagne, accompanying flutes and a tray of chocolate delights with a "Happy Birthday" greeting written in chocolate. YUM!
Spotting Michelle in the grand lobby, I thanked her and she smiled and replied, it's what we do here...Its "The Good Stuff"!
The gesture was unexpected...but welcoming and enriching to the soul... Thank you Michelle for going the extra mile.

title: “A good choice close to the airport.”
text: We checked in for one night before flying to NY. It was a very busy hotel, with people everywhere, and a couple of conference going on. We chose this hotel for it's close proximity to LA Airport and free shuttle. The shuttle was frequent and easy to find the stop out the front of the airport. We booked the night prior so as could get into our room at 8am, which was a good idea because they were full. At first we were given a room key to an occupied room, which was a bit annoying. Then we went back down to the front desk, and the computers crashed, so the whole check-in process was not great, but had I not been so tired after flying from Australia with 2 little kids, it wouldn't have worried me. Our room overlooked the runway, and the windows were exceptionally soundproofed. Very comfortable beds. The other puzzling thing was the shuttle back to the airport pick up point was moved from out the fron, to the side of the building, but there were no signs to indicate the change which was confusing. I found the buffet breakfast to be expensive. $80 for 2 adults and 2 children incl tax and tip.

title: “Nice, Large Sized Rooms”
text: In the heart of all the action. Rooms are oversized..some with 2 seperate bathrooms.

title: “Location, Value”
text:
We recently returned from a trip through California, with a three night stay in the Columbus Motor Inn. I chose this Inn based on the reviews I read here. The reviews are on point--this Inn is located within walking distance to most attractions, centrally located, has knowledgeable desk people, has extremely clean rooms, and the price value is fantastic. I only wish they were able to provide a continental breakfast, but, due to the small size of the lobby and its set-up, that really isn't doable. However, there is a cafe of sorts (my husband walked there one morning) about half a block away where he picked up some mighty tasty muffins. The garage parking was a big plus, and we didn't need to take the car out during the time we stayed there. In fact, we were also booked for a Muir Woods/Wine Tasting Tour, and were able to picked up right in front of the hotel.
I'd say my top reasons for staying here again are the value and the cleanliness of the rooms. It's not the Ritz Carlton, but it's absolutely worth the price and within walking distance to the Wharf.

title: “Good location at a reasonable price”
text:
Excellent location for the theatre-going crowd. The first room we got had a bummed out airconditioner so we changed room the next day and the rest of the stay was comfortable. You don;t want to be in NYC in July without an air conditioned room. 
Front desk service was very good and efficient.

title: “Loved it! Had a 2BR Apt to Ourselves!”
text: My wife and I stayed for the always stressful week of visiting family. We rented the apartment around the corner from the B&B (1837 Branard) and had our meals in the B&B itself. We live in a stressful crowded city with tiny apartments the SPACE in the apartment was like a cool salve on our frayed nerves. There was a couch for each of us to fall asleep on before retiring to the King sized bed. Proper TV with proper cable, full kitchen (but I think pots and pans are upon request -- we didn't cook) and what's better than ordering a pizza and a sixpack and watching Scifi on teh couch after a long flight? It was literally like having our own apartment in Houston. Only place I want to stay now.

title: “much improved”
text: rooms, hallways and conference facilities have all seen upgrades since last year when parts of hotel were looking tired. Pub bistro in basement serves good food but they don't know how to serve continental beer.

title: “Pay the extra $'s and stay somewhere else!!”
text:
We booked this hotel through hotels...(and thank the lord for that...cause after our experience they were wonderful). We arrived at the Pennsylvania at 2 pm tired after driving for 8 hours to hopefully get an early check in, which we did and we were quite pleased UNTIL THE ELEVATOR DOORS OPENED...on the 7th FLOOR...and the nightmare began....the paint was peeling off the walls the carpet looked as though it had been there for a century...we entered what they called a hotel room (more like a dump!).....no headboard instead a stained stood on the wall above our two neatly stacked mattresses. The sheets looked worst that something in prison movie and oh yes there were no towels to be found. 
When we called down to reception to switch room, they stated that "this was one of the best rooms they had"...we were mortified after explaining to the lady that we refused to sleep in a bed with a rather sizable stain suspended above our heads...she switched us to a room on the 10th floor which was slightly less appalling. The staff overall were not nice, I actually feared the housekeeping on our floor and was rather cautious in asking for a set of clean towels (since there were none). 
We stayed at the Pennsylvania Hotel ONE NIGHT (because every other hotel in NYC seem to be sold out) and switched the next day to the Millenium hotel on Broadway, which was only $20.00 dollars more a night and was absolutely breathtaking!
PLEASE THINK TWICE ABOUT STAYING AT THE PENNSYLVANIA NO AMOUT OF SAVINGS IS WORTH THIS!!

title: “WONDERFUL!”
text: This is a great hotel. We recently stayed there while we moved our daughter to Houston. The room was fabulous. The floor to ceiling windows gave us a nice city view. The room was updated and clean. After traveling for 2 days, it was nice to sleep in the very comfortable bed. We also loved the pool. It was 93 degrees. The pool is a good size and one can order beer, snacks , etc. chairs...towels..sunshine! The only drawback was the parking. It's an underground garage and somewhat a pain to drive to. On the plus side, our car stayed cool. I will stay here every time I visit my daughter!!

title: “truly the best city hotel in the US”
text:
We've been loyal Peninsula visitors for years and returned this year for another weekend retreat. It is truly the best of the best for its level of personal and dedicated service.
In Chicago, the location is outstanding and the restaurants are of the highest quality anywhere. My wife is a passionate advocate of the Spa and the pool space - again the best in Chicago. We'll be back for certain.

title: “Man entered our room in the middle of the night”
text:
I stayed in this hotel for two nights as part a vacation. While for the most part it was an enjoyable stay on our first night a man used a key to enter our room at about 2am. I was fast asleep (ko'ed from Jetlag) but my girlfriend said he knocked at first and then entered. He may have had a legitimate reason for needing to access the room but at that time of night it was a little creepy.
Apart from this the hotel is well located in the Wall St area right by the 9/11 memorial. We were there at the weekend so it was a little quieter than usual. The room was very small (but its NYC) it was very clean with all modern appliances.
There is a nice concierge lounge near the lobby with complimentary coffee and wifi etc.
If I had been staying in the hotel longer i might have raised the issue of the man in our room. Other than this it was a positive stay.

title: “Great location for families and those with a rental car”
text:
Things I liked the most:
Easy to access the interstate**, front desk was friendly, within walking distance to universal, always something going on, pretty views of the hills, beds were comfy and bathroom was roomy, also the walls weren't paperthin like some hotels
Things I didn't like:
Maid service, down pillows (it was hard to get replacements-i'm allergic), parking was ridiculous, layout was confusing, air conditioner was either really hot or cold and never at the temp it said it was, definitely for families with kids, it was expensive for what you got (but what isn't in LA)
The only problems we ran into was that the maid would change our towels everyday even if we hung back up (we were trying to be ecofriendly since there was a drought going on); they kept replacing the one non-down pillow i had with down pillows; and they would never replace the coffee stuff for the coffee maker (i guess b/c they wanted you to hit up starbucks in the lobby but still...)
The layout was confusing because there several elevators in the parking garages (BTW-the parking spots were apparently made out of gold lol) that led to various places around the hotel.
Internet was $10 a day, but we needed it to plan out our days. Printing was also expensive so print everything out before you come.

title: “Amazing Marquis”
text:
When we checked into this hotel we were given a room with a
times square view even though we didn't request it! We stayed on the 28th floor and the room was nice. It was agreat stay.

title: “Excellent Value for Convenience and Good Service”
text:
My wife and I stayed at this hotel because of its proximity to the conference she was attending. We were so pleased by our experience that we will certainly want to stay there during future trips
to Indiana. We particularly wanted a quiet room, and this is exactly what we received. The staff was uniformly freindly and helpful. We enjoyed the compimentary reception each evening and the complimentary breakfast each morning. Lassandra was the chef who prepared our breakfasts to order during each morning of our stay. It was amazing to watch her prepare the orders of many guests one after another to perfection. Access to coin-operated laundromat on the premises was a beneficlal convenience.

title: “Friendly Sophistication”
text:
Once past the "interesting" bunker-like exterior, you'll find a staff that is sincerely grateful to serve, and a hotel interior that is equal parts soho gallery and cozy lounge. The lobby is as inviting as any other, and the rooms convey lots of light and warmth (hardwood floors and floor to ceiling windows make all the difference), materials are first rate and overall design is comfortably understated. Did I mention it was one of the most comfortable hotel beds I’ve ever slept in? 
Negatives? Almost too small to mention: reservations process was not without its trouble, and although the staff is extra friendly, there seems to be no dedicated concierge. Given that the hotel has an art curator and focused on local artists (loved QWERTY 5, an art piece at ground floor), we found it curious that no one on staff we spoke to had heard of MoMA PS1 (a must for art lovers) or could help with directions.
But, trust me, if you’re looking for a fabulous location, soul-comforting design, and a staff that charms from the onset, you’d be hard-pressed to do better than the James.

title: “Outstanding hotel”
text: Our new favorite! The rooms are large (for NYC), well appointed, and kept spotlessly clean. The staff are all wonderful - professional, helpful and friendly. The location is excellent - subway at the door (and 2 other subway lines within a few blocks), and a short walk to lots of restaurants and other attractions. Highly recommended.

title: “Best Bargain In Mid-Town”
text: If your accustomed to staying at five star hotels and have no objection to paying five star rates than the Travel Inn is not for you. However, if you are a thrifty traveler who is looking for a sizable clean room in a good location with amenities exceeding other hotels in this class then the Travel Inn is the best bargain in New York City. Hotel provided iron, ironing board, hair dryer, brand new refrigerator and microwave, two double beds with good mattresses, desk and easy chair. My cost was $175 per night and that included FREE parking (an additional $40 to $50 per day charge at most mid-town hotels) . This hotel provided the best rate for the accommodations of a any hotel I have stayed in the NYC in the past 10 years and I have stayed in virtually every level of hotel in mid-town. Maybe a bit more of a walk to the theatre district but the area seemed safe and clean even when returning near mid-night. Next trip to NYC I won't even bother to check for availability at any other mid-town hotel - I'll simply book direct with Travel Inn. And to those complaining about the size of the bathroom - admittedly the bathroom is small for most hotels but it was adequate for individual use and the water pressure was good and the water was always hot for morning showers.

title: “"Pleasantly Surprised..."”
text: Although I have stayed at other Thompson Hotel locations I must say the Smyth has, by far, exceeded my expectations! It was cute and trendy...and a little bit quirky. Describes me to a tee which is probably why I adored it! Popping into the city for a quick 'Girls Nite Out' stay, the staff was extremely accommodating (to include upgrading our room) and more than helpful (fetching a few buckets of ice), the room was nice, perfect size. I was completely satisfied by the end of our too short trip. My friend and I have now dubbed this our go to spot. Kudos to everyone for making us feel more than welcomed and right at home.

title: “I LOVE this hotel!!!!!”
text: I am finally writing a review after SEVERAL stays at the Aloft. I love this hotel. I can not say enough about it. The hotel is gorgeous inside. It is very well kept and is the cleanest hotel I have ever been to. I live about 2 hours away from Philadelphia and my husband and I visit often for sporting events and family functions. We always choose to stay at the Aloft because it is a great value and it close to all the major spots in the city. As a runner, I appreciate the fitness room at the Aloft. The machines are new and in good condition. There are several pieces of equipment, plenty of towels, and free water. This is a service many other hotels simply do not have. There is a snack bar (it is a little expensive) but it is great for midnight snacks. The parking lot is gated and safe. The indoor pool is very nice - I highly recommend taking a dip. There is also free internet access, a pool table with free pool, and a lounge area.The best part of this hotel is the rooms. The rooms are nicely decorated and the showers are absolutely amazing. Another great feature of this hotel is that they allow animals. I would highly recommend this hotel if you are staying in the Philadelphia area. It is much nicer than the others!!!!

title: “Nice Hotel, Would stay again!”
text: This was a nice suprise in Manhattan... The hotel is truly up to Westin quality standards throughout (unlike other hotel chains in Manhattan). The smell of white tea when you arrive is quite calming. The room was much larger than I expected. Usually, I stay at the New York Hilton on the Hhonors Diamond Floor (most renovated) and I have to say that the room here on the regular floor was much nicer and larger. The Westin Heavenly Bed is the best (in my opinion) of any hotel chain and the Heavenly Bath Towels are awesome after a shower. The shower was okay, but water pressure was a bit low. The location is very good with lots of restaurants in walking distance. I generally prefer the central location of midtown, but this was an acceptable location and would be a gret location if you wanted to see shows. The bar area was nice, though busy, and service was good. The hotel has a Shulas Steakhouse in the lobby level which is consistantly good. All in all, I would recommend this hotel and will stay here again!

title: “a classy gem”
text: The Chancellor is a classy and reasonably priced gem: superb location; friendly, helpful staff; comfortable room (others have commented that the rooms are small -- ours was most adequate and larger than several in which we've stayed in Europe). The Pillow Library is great, especially since I prefer a down pillow, and they are rarely standard issue. Other nice touches: complimentary coffee, cookies, apples, newspapers (including The New York Times).

title: “From worse to better”
text: We are visiting with family in Denver and by chance found this Marriott right where we needed to be. Front desk young man very polite and helpful. Great rate, very quiet, very private with nice courtyard. Wish the offered free breakfast but glad we stayed.

title: “Great weekend in Chicago”
text:
We stayed at the Fairfield Inn July 8-10, to celebrate my husband's birthday with a Red Sox/White Sox game (the 19-inning marathon, actually......we stayed through 14 and are glad we didn't stay longer to see Boston lose!). Anyway, the Fairfield Inn was a perfect choice for our weekend. Definitely plusher than other Fairfield Inns (and most Courtyard Inns). The location was unbeatable - right in the middle of the action - restaurants, shopping, 5-minute walk to the subway, the beach, or Navy Pier. The room was larger than we expected. Decor was clearly recent. We could have done with more toiletries and a larger breakfast room, but otherwise, it was a good deal.
On Saturday nights in the summer, the Navy Pier has fireworks. They were quite good, and it wa sa fun way to experience Navy Pier. We also enjoyed Millenium Park and the CAS river cruise. For meals, we recommend Harry Carey's - I feared it would be too touristy, but actually a lot of Chicagoans were eating there (at lunchtime) and the food was excellent.

title: “Best stay ever”
text: It was a deliteful stay hospitality was great it's like being at home Thx. Vickie the prices were great.:)

title: “Bad experience all around at Penn's View”
text:
After having read the reviews for this hotel on TripAdvisor, I felt that $230.00/night for one of their suites was going to be a good deal. I was expecting European charm and elegance, and a high standard of upkeep and cleanliness that I have always experienced in the numerous Italian hotels where I have stayed.
Instead, it's almost like the room we stayed in was in a completely different hotel from the one described in the reviews on this site! Our room was undoubtedly quirky and it had plenty of "character." There were a couple of pieces of furniture that gave it a quaint old fashioned feel, but they were combined with some decidedly cheap pieces that I almost recognized from my college days of scrounging for cheap furniture. There was a huge oval table in the sitting room that might have been nice; I couldn't tell because all I could see was the plastic padded table cover that was ripped in a few places and had certainly seen better days. Looking down to the floor, I did love the look of hardwood floors. Too bad that the floors were marred by the very old and dirty oriental rugs. It looked like they had not had a good cleaning in quite awhile. Not only that, but there were crumbs all over the carpets. 
Our room did overlook the freeway. However, the traffic noise was minimal, and there was no noise of guests in other rooms, or any hallway noises that I could detect. So, I cannot blame noise on a bad night's sleep. The bed was a bit of a problem. While the king-sized bed in the bedroom wasn't horrible to sleep on, it wasn't a comfortable bed. Too close the the edge, and the edge would just droop. I spent the night making sure that my two-year old stayed far from the edges.
There was a pull-out sofa in the living room. We had to spend considerable effort pulling it out. When we did, we noticed that there was one thin, stained sheet to cover oneself, and once positioned in the center of the mattress, it became "a cave" (my husband's words). I have never seen a person literally engulfed by a mattress. The mattress was only usable once placed on the floor.
The details in the room were similarly lacking. We had only one clean glass. After looking around, we found another glass on top of the wardrobe filled with possible petrified goldfish (the kind that you eat). The bathtub had dirt and hair accumulated by the drain. The white bedspread on the king bed had multiple stains. It was disgusting. We would have left as soon as we arrived, but we had arrived at the hotel late in the evening after a long plane ride, and our son needed to sleep. We asked to check out the next day, though we were scheduled for three nights. We were not notified that we would be reimbursed for the additional two nights until 15 minutes before we needed to check out. I forgot a new jacket that I had just purchased (worth $200.00) in the closet in my haste to leave. When I went back the next day to get it, they informed me that it had not been found. No one else had checked into the room since we left.

title: “Very pleased”
text: I read the previous reviews but for the price and location it was hard to pass up. We stayed in a mid-size room and it was clean with a standard set up. The location is hard to beat as is the hot breakfast served every morning. Renovations are in the cosmetic stage so there are no more power tools being used. We were very happy and would stay there again.

title: “clean hotel”
text: Very clean hotel with comfortable beds. The kids liked the biscuits and gravy for breakfast.

title: “Great 'Babymoon'!”
text:
Firstly, we had checked into an old establishment hotel close to Grand Central only for me to realize that I could see no 'view' of the City and for me the view of the City was very important. So, I convinced hubby to let me check this affordable hotel with views that I had read about called Bentley. The reservation agent told me that she could not promise me a room with view but would put us on a higher floor. At this point it was chance that I'll move to this unknown hotel and get crap views and hubby was not too thrilled with the location (it is off-center).... In the end what saved the day (and my vacation) was this gentleman named Brett. I called the hotel front desk and explained my situation to Brett who promised to upgrade me to a superior room with a view. And he delivered, we got a corner room on the 14th floor with bridge and river views! And hubby was happy cos I was happy - I literally stayed up till 2 am looking out of the window. 
Also, the front desk staff were always friendly and we had a good stay, will come here again. Thanks again Brett!

title: “Great downtown hotel”
text: Our first time here, and we will return! Located in the hub of downtown. Many restaurants and bars in the area. You must have a Martini in Oliver's!

title: “5 star... I don't think so.”
text:
If your a true user of 5 star Luxury Resorts such as Four Seasons and Ritz Carltons, then you'll be disappointed in this one. 
Just got back from this resort (Nov. 2004) and booked it because of the reviews on line, but very disappointed all around.
Rooms are average and the bathroom after reading the reviews was very disappointing. Only one sink and not very large at that. Eventhough there is a sperate shower stall, it was so on top of the toilet that when you opened the shower door you just miss the toilet by about 2 inches. 
One day I had the call front desk to get my room cleaned. This was after 2:00 pm the day after I checked in. I was told they were busy because a lot of guest checked out and new ones were arriving and they needed to turn over the rooms. So I quess that means I was put on the back burner since I was already checked in. Staff were ok, but not 5 star helpful or even 5 star friendly. 
Beware major conventioneers at this hotel. In fact the week I was there the hotel was 95% booked and probably 80% of quest were there on conventions. They litterly take over the hotel. One night the only lobby lounge in the hotel was taken over by these conventioneers and there was no place to sit and have a quite drink. Also a hugh TV screen was brought in so all the "men" could watch Monday night football, for which they proceeded to behave as typical male's would during a football game. I think you know what I mean. Another evening most of the pool area and hot tub section was closed off for a private convention dinner party.
This type of service would not happen in a true 5 star resort. The Marriott is trying to match the Ritz Carltons and Four Seasons, but are falling short. Remimber conventioneers do not pay out of their pockets for these trips, their corporations do. They could care less about your hard earned vacation.
All in all not worty of a 5 star rating. Spend a couple of dollars more and stay at the Phoenician or Four Seasons. Much more worth your hard earn dollar.

title: “Clean rooms, amazing location for price”
text:
If you are looking for a place for a conference or a place to unload your things while you spend your days exploring the city, this hotel is great. If you are going to San Francisco expecting any version of a luxury vacation... look elsewhere. The key to this hotel is value and location. No frills, but very clean and within the heart of the fishermans wharf. A wonderful neighborhood to use as your home base. It is somewhat of a tourist trap, but if you're not from San Francisco it is fun to see and you will not have a hard time finding souvenirs and postcards for anyone back home.
Some general San Francisco advice: I bought a pass for the subway the week I was there (for a work conference) and saw almost every part of the city. My favorite neighborhoods were Chinatown and Japantown. If you have any experience using public transit, I would recommend this. It might be a bit daunting for a novice, though. Overall, San Francisco has one of the best organized public transit systems of large american cities. While no subway like NYC, the busses, cable cars and rail make for a plentiful combination of options. If you're dressing up for a nice dinner, an occasional taxi is also reasonable. If you've never done public transit, I'd recommend checking out the websites for the busses before going anywhere. If you type in where you are and where you want to go it will find a route (or 10) that fits your time schedule.

title: “A Fav Place to Stay in LA”
text:
This is an updated Hyatt property and centrally located to everything on the Westside/BH. Love the access to the Century City mall for dining/ent/shopping. Great on site spa. Rooms are tastefully done, not over the top but very nice. 4 star plus hotel from my perspective. Service is good, rarely eat in the hotel but when I have its very good.
Location-clean-safe-easy access-whats not to like? 
Parking is easier than the W
Safer than sketchy hotels on Sunset
Easy to get on the freeway

title: “The Magnolia is the Best!”
text: I have stayed at The Magnolia in Dallas at least 3 times now while on business and it is THE BEST for the price! The complimentary breakfast hands down makes it worth it, and the cookies and milk at night! Great location to convention center and very helpful concierge! Close to other very good restaurants, too!

title: “A gem in the heart of NYC”
text:
Already for more than 15 years I have made the Edison my preferred middle class hotel in NYC. The location is just perfect in mid town, the art deco lobby is a great time piece, the rooms are all you need for a good night sleep and it is remarkable
quiet for the noisy Times Square location. Don't expect a big luxury bathroom but the one you get has all you need including always plenty of warm water. The bed in our last room was bit old but my wife and I anyhow slept well. We love the fully original 20th/30th busy breakfast/lunch room with it large choice, however we never had dinner in the restaurant because there is to much choice in the area. 
We will be back!
Ben Gall, Malvern, PA

title: “Great price, great location....small room”
text: My 16 year old daughter and I stayed at the Pod March 24-28 2007. We stayed in a bunk with a shared bath. I was a little worried about that but it wasn't bad at all. There never was a time that I had to wait to use the restroom or shower. Not to mention it was right outside my door. I must say that if you are expecting a 5 star go somewhere else. This is not a 5 star hotel nor does it claim to be. I was looking for something decent, cheap and just somewhere to lay my head at night. I got exactly that. My daughter and I were a little cramped since the bunk rooms are about 7 X10 ft. If you plan ahead so that both of you dont need the mirror and sink at the same time, it will be fine. The room and shared baths were kept very neat and clean. I also enjoyed the roof top deck. If you are a smoker the rooftop is a great place to go since you cant smoke in your room. This hotel is only 2 blocks from the subway. 2 French and Japanese restaurants right next door. You have to check out PAX foods on the corner of Lexington and 3rd. It's on the way to the subway. Great food at good prices. I would definitely stay here again without a doubt!

title: “Great to have somewhere safe clean and friendly when you're travelling alone”
text: I stayed here after looking it up on this site and believe I made a good decision. The people are friendly and helpful and the hotel is so central that it makes a wonderful place to come and go from during the day.My room was clean and compact with a bathroom with bath as well as shower . The coffee and muffin for breakfast were a lovely touch. The only suggestion I would make as an improvement would be a kettle in the room for making your own tea or coffee - but this is minor and the place was certainly good value for money when I looked at what else was available in this category. On arrival I was given the option of an upgrade for a few extra dollars and I took it so I could have my own bathroom. I would certainly recommend the Mosser.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: This is a great looking hotel. Overall there are a lot of positives e.g. room quality good, the location is ideal, the hotel is quite opulent etc. the negative is the total cost can be a little on the high side. All-in-all, probably the best place to enjoy Memphis.

title: “Very nice but a few quirks”
text:
I was a little concerned about the hotel after reading some of the negative reviews, but for the most part they were overblown.
The hotel is in an historic Art Deco building in a fabulous location right on Michigan Ave. The room is very nice with a very comfortable bed, a large flat screen tv with excellent audio and a clean modern bathroom. The only negative about the room is that it's too dark. We had to call housekeeping to ask for an additional lamp, which they said they couldn't bring until the next day, but managed to find and bring to us quickly.
The high speed Internet is wired and wireless in the room and free. That's a biggie for me and quite nice.
The fitness room in the basement is fairly well equipped with some nice conveniences like headphones with disposable foam covers, but guess what? It's too dark in there too. What's with this darkness in the hotel? Is it supposed to be romantic? I don't need my room or the fitness center to be romantic.
The China Grill is a top notch restaurant that's attached to the hotel through the lobby -- great if you want a fine meal without having to put on a coat or find an umbrella.
The only other annoying thing I can think of is that there was no notification to my room that packages had arrived for me. They should have put a paper notice or had the light blink on my phone. I had to call and ask if any packages had arrived for me. What if I didn't know? Just an annoying little lapse in service.
Overall, I would definitely recommend the hotel. I give it a 9, but not a 10.

title: “About average but ok”
text: I stood at the Marriott for 4 night in September 2007 for a conference. The hotel is very nicely located directly at the water in the inner city of Baltimore. Very close to the Baseball Stadium which I realized at check in (many baseball visitors were just returning from the game). If you step outside there is a lot to see and you can immediatly start walking. Bringing your own car is an expensive thing, since parking garages charge you a lot of money in this nice area . The rooms are nice and big - at least my one was. But the bath is small, even though it has a seperate shower what I really love (this is so much better than a bath tub, I will never understand why most hotels have a tub). My room had a bid panel TV set and was quite clean. Why I do not give a better ranking are two items: everything looks like it is heavily used and nobody is maintaining it. I can name the bath, but also the wardrobe or the desk. The walls have dirty stripes on it etc. These small an little things where you see nobody pays attention and they are just behind to make the best money out of it as long as it lasts. In my room the internet was not working and even after four days, there was nobody called to fix it. I had to go to the 31st floor where they have a business lounge with internet access - very inconviniet. By the way: this lounge you should visit - what a great view over the bay! Then the hotel has at least one restaurant with excellent food, I really liked that. Reception is very nice and over all you can only complain about the price ... I would go there again if there yould be another conference one day.

title: “The Very BEST!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text:
We came to Chicago for a few days after a family reunion. We never expected the beautiful and comfortable room we had. The decor was definitely "High End" and the beds could not have been more comfortable. The room was very large and the4 bathroom spacious. BUT.....Maybe the best part was the staff, from the guys who greeted us at the door to the wonderful people at the desk. Specifically, Andrew, Keesha, and Denise. Everyone else was great too, but I don't know their names. The breakfast was great and the breakfast area very attractive and comfortable. I rate this place "AAA+"
Bruce from Mandeville, La.

title: “A nice 3 Star Hotel for a 4 Star price on Hotliar”
text:
Firstly thank you all other reviews as I was able to get a quiet room but had to have the shower head replaced in my bathroom which was only a shower stall no bathtub. I booked on Hotwire (or Hotliar) where they promise a main brand hotel. The room was clean and adequate but I could have gotten a much nicer 3 star hotel for a cheaper price. The room was small, dark and no dresser. The staff was very courteous and helpful and location is great, as long as you have a room facing the back. 
Thank god for may tethering to my droid phone to avoid their internet charges

title: “Look forward to returning to the Alexis, Seattle”
text:
I stayed at the Alexis for three nights. Loved the walking proximity to all points of interest, including museum, pikes market, peer, shopping, bookstore, cafe's, restaurants. the hotel staff, front desk, concierge and restaurants were absolutely friendly, grecious and genuinly interested in accomodating me/guests. I enojyed my stay in Seattle immensly as a result and look forward to returning soon.
Paulette

title: “Second time here...still like it!”
text: We returned to this hotel again this year. Everything was just as nice and easy as last year. Love the location. Easy walk to everything. We were very happy! Breakfast (complimentary) is an especially good deal!

title: “I'll Stay There Again!”
text: I stayed in the Edison Hotel about 18 years ago. It was Ok. My friend and I were taking our young granddaughters to New York this Christmas. I made our reservation at the Edison, but was a little apprehensive. I had read a review that said to stay above 5th floor because of street noise. We were on 6th floor and there was street noise. Ask at check-in for the best floor to stay on to not have street noise. Hotel Edison has a decent price (for New York), and the location is the best. The room was very adequate, compact, but clean. Bathroom was adequate (not large) and very clean. I am picky about hotel pillows and mattresses and I have no complaints about the Edison. Theirs were better than most hotels. Elevators were very convenient just walk in front door and elevators are very close. Housekeeping gave us more than enough linens after we were short one set of towels the first morning. They also repaired a floor lamp. Concierge was helpful. I will definitely stay at the Hotel Edison again.

title: “room/bathroom way too small”
text: I stayed at the Palmer House on business. I was so disapointed in the size of the room and bathroom. I had a small cosmetic bag and there was litterally no counter space in the bathroom, only a small ledge above the toilet where my things kept falling into. I was not too impressed by the check-in service although a particular bell hop was especially helpful. The concierge was medicore. I am going back on business in May and I am going to try staying somewhere else.

title: “Luxury in a Great Location”
text: We stayed here with our two kids (ages 7 and 11). We requested a room with two beds. The room was very spacious (especially by NY standards). We'd stayed here before (before the remodel) and, although we liked it before, we liked it even more this time around! The location is excellent. The minute you walk into the hotel, you just feel good being there. We took the red-eye from SF and were allowed to check in immediately upon arrival at 8am. For the latter part of our vacation, we switched to a hotel near Wall Street. My kids were "shocked" by the tiny size of the WS hotel. We will definitely be staying here again.

title: “I was pleasantly surprised!”
text: I was so nervous after reading so many reviews but we were satisfied with hotel and would stay again. I had a king room, 1226 and we had continental breakfast included which was right down the hall. Bath was small but great water pressure in shower and clean. We were told no A/ C yet until summer so we opened window and slept like rocks..don't believe everything you read about this place. We thought it was a great value!

title: “I've never seen this before”
text: I had to spend the night at this Wingate due to an American Airlines mistake. The room seemed quite alright for the most part. What I didn't expect was that the lights next to the bed were directly linked with the light switch as you came into the door. You can turn off your light next to the bed, but that would not turn off the entrance light. So I could not read in bed until I fell asleep unless I got up to turn off the lights. I tried turning off the main switch and turn on the bedside lamp, but no go. I've never seen this before. Scratching head.

title: “I SO wanted to fall in love with this hotel...”
text:
but the prince sadly turned into a frog. I erred on the side of generosity but 3.5 stars would have been more accurate. 
This hotel has a lot going for it as far as the hardwiring is concerned- to start the location is perfection - around the corner from Fifth Avenue and right across from Central Park. You have the best of New York laid at your feet. The rooms are timelessly elegant and generous in size. The bed among the best I have ever experienced... BUT to quote Gertrude Stein "There is no there there". 
The staff and service, the soul of any great hotel, are wildly disparate and range from truly excellent to borderline disgruntled. Several times there was no one at the door including when I first arrived with luggage in the middle of the afternoon and after arriving back after the theatre late at night. Check in was somewhat perfunctory and it was the first time I was not upgraded as an Amex Plat card holder which is fair enough if they have no rooms available however upon check-in the guaranteed late checkout of 4pm was confirmed by the clerk at her initiative which I did appreciate. On my final day, at a little after the regular check out time I received a call thanking me for the stay and well, in short asking me to leave! Taken aback but thinking this was a misunderstanding, I assured the clerk that the guaranteed check out at 4pm was confirmed by one of his colleagues but instead of apologizing he just asked me when I would leave and said that my keycard (which is used for both the room and elevator and was faulty the entire time of my 3 night stay) would no long work and if I intended on staying I would have to come to the front desk. I was so disgusted I packed up and left with a very bitter taste in my mouth and astonished at the rudest treatment I have ever experienced at any hotel. I am the type of person who always checks out 5 minutes before the time and If they were pressured for rooms they could have handled this a lot better. To add insult to injury the bill contained several mischarges in the favor of the hotel including all three breakfasts (which were included in my rate) charged as lunch. It was quickly remedied but still this shouldn't happen at a hotel of this caliber. 
While I rather like this hotel doesn’t have a large impersonal lobby it is missing a great bar like Bemelmans at the Carlyle or the King Cole Bar at the St. Regis. 
Most importantly and sadly, however, I found the Ritz-Carlton Central Park lacking in any sort of graciousness or charm.

title: “Dated, in need of a re-model”
text:
There is nothing wrong with this hotel if you had arrived here 20 years ago when it was new. However, now, the carpet is old, the paint is old, the dining options limited and the prices are expensive. It needs a refresh with so many better more affordable alternatives nearby (i.e. the Hampton Inn and Sheraton that are just north of the airport are both nice and more affordable in general). 
On the plus side - good shuttle to the airport, the fitness room is in good shape with new equipment, and the staff is generally helpful if not friendly. Full TV selection including showtime and "suite" style rooms. 
On the negative side, very dated, looks and appears worn, they charge for wifi unless you work a deal in advance, and the food in the restaurant and bar is at best ok - but nothing special - and is over-priced. 
Personally, I would rather stay at the Hampton which lacks the amenities but it is very clean and comfortable and has a great staff. If you want full amenties I would recommend the Sheraton.

title: “Great stay!”
text: We recently stayed firv3 nights and everything was wonderful exceptvforthe view from our room. We actually were staring at thebrick wall of the next building. It didn't seem that busy so I wish we were given a room with a better view. Other than that, the stay was excellent. The staff was extremely helpful. The room was new and modern. I would not hesitate to stay again.

title: “Decent hotel, very good location!”
text:
Despite some of the negative reviews here, we had no problems with this hotel. We checked in on July 2nd for 1 night. Check in was quick and we were upgraded to a corner deluxe king room, (comes with being a starwoods preferred guest), and that was a nice treat without having to ask for it. The room was pretty decent ie; nice comfortable king bed, fairly decorated, small but adequate bathroom (no tub), and air-condiitoning was great, especially with it being in the high 80's that day. We did spend some time at the pool, nothing fancy, but very spacious and plenty of lounge chairs. The parking is a bit expensive, but that was to be expected and they added the parking fee to our bill, which was a plus, so for $137.00 including parking for the night, not bad. Staying on the harbor would have easily been about $75 - $100 more.
The location was perfect for us ie; 3 blocks from the harbor, within walking distance to convenience stores, and a nice little diner and bar across the street name "Tony's!!! The bartender Rob will make you some killer drinks, and we ate breakfast their the next morning. The meal was pretty good for $4.99, that included, 2 eggs, home fries, toast and your choice of meat. My hubby had Begian waffle, home fries, and meat for about $2.00 more. 
Some people complained about the downtown location, but it was typical of any urban downtown location. Locals and tourists were walking about. We are from a big city, and I work in the city, and for it to have been a Saturday, night, it was actually pretty quiet, until you got to the Harbor. We never thought twice about anything bad happenening, and their were cops walking the beat.
For a quick overnight getaway, this hotel fit the bill. Most of our time was spent at the harbor, with under two hours spent at the hotel pool.
Overall, we enjoyed our overnight stay, I rated the service 3 stars only because we really did not have to use it for anything, except to check in and out... We are looking forward to returning before the summer is over.

title: “outstanding service”
text:
Employees of this Hotel were very nice. Especially ALYSSA and SARAH. They go above and beyond to help me. They were constantly calling the shuttle, asking other hotel to see if they found my lost phone or maybe someone turned in one. They finally found it after 2 hours. 
i have stayed in this hotel for business many times, and not once i was disappointed. Love this hotel and will be back. Especially Emplyees like Alyssa and Sarah. Thank you gals. 
kunal

title: “Nice place!”
text: I pretty much only slept here and didn't use the pool, restaurant or convention services but I can say it was the best night's sleep I have EVER had in a hotel. The sheets were crisp and clean, the bed was soft, the temperature of the room was perfect. The room was clean and recently remodeled and every employee I encountered was very friendly and helpful. I would definitely return to this hotel.

title: “Really good, then minor annoyances”
text:
Stayed on a Thursday nite. Very pleased, clean and very nice breakfast. Then, 3 nites later we stayed again. Very different last time. Got to the room to find the tissue box completely empty. So, i went to office for a new box. Then, i noticed in the bathroom there was a dirty wash cloth hanging over the shower railing which was missed by housekeeper. So, we were very tired, both took showers right away and i got into bed. Then, the noises began. Our room was right over the office and for a few hours every time someone went in or out of office, the sliding door would open/shut & make a "pounding" sound. I woke up several times overnite, heard the door a few times even then. 
The next morning my husband did tell the manager about the door noise & he said we should've notified him & they would've moved us. Well, after we've both taken showers & in bed clothes and me in bed already, thought we'd put up with noise. But, guess we should've asked for a different room. Manager was very pleasant about the situation. Didn't mention the dirty linen or empty tissue box to him.
Overall, satisfied and a very nice clean property. Would stay here again. Very nice hot breakfast.

title: “they were so gracious”
text:
After my room was given away by the Lenox Hotel at 12:30 AM., the Marriot Courtyard graciously accept me at 1:30 AM. I was also given a complimentary breakfast. Of course the Lenox Hotel paid the bill, since they gave my pre- paid room away to another guest. 
 The Courtyard Hotel was very clean and the beds were very comfortable. I was given a suite. They boasted that their hotel was small, about 80 rooms, and very quiet. They were totally correct. "The Hotel tone was that of a comfortable home where you were welcomed. My room was more suited for a businessman. It was decorated in sailboats, which I do own one, but had a more masculine and/or business tone to this suite. 
 Again, The staff was wonderful, keeping my bags for me the next day so I could run the city. They went out of their way to make sure that the rest of my stay was not tainted by what the Lenox Hotel had done. I want to thank them very much for their gracious hospitality. I highly recommend this hotel. Oh by the way, the location is great.

title: “Amazing!”
text: We had an amazing 4 nights at Hotel Metro! The location was amazing (right near a subway station, walking distance to many attractions including Time Square). The decor of the hotel is lovely! Our room had been recently renovated and had an extremely nice bathroom, comfy bed and linens, a nice big TV, couldn't have asked for more. The free breakfast every morning was also great (lots of bagels, muffins, cereal and yogurt), it definitely saved us a lot of time and money! The only negative thing I can say is that they forgot to clean our room one day, but to be fair we slept in pretty late and they had knocked on our door and we told them to come back later. it wasn't a big deal and I asked for some fresh towels and they brought them up promptly. If i ever went back to NYC I would want to stay at this hotel again!

title: “Our preferred "downtown" hotel.”
text: We always have a very good experience when we stay at the Magnolia. It is our preferred "downtown" hotel. We like to stay here when we visit our son who lives downtown. It is convenient to his apt. and hotel offers nice amenities like the wine reception, cookies and milk, and the breakfast buffet. Employees are happy, helpful, and interested in making guests comfortable. We have recommended this hotel to friends many times.

title: “I knew something was wrong when we walked in and were overpowered by the smell of carpet deodorizer”
text:
This hotel must pipe deodorizer that is used to cover up the odor in a smoking room through the entire ventilation system b/c it was so strong upon entering the establishment that it made me want to gag. The room was, at best, just a place to sleep, didn't feel clean, and even though the website said it was recently renovated, that must have been the part of the hotel we didn't see - no wait a minute, the sign outside was actually quite nice and looked new. Maybe that's what they meant. 
Anyway, we arrived late at night anticipating a quiet meal in the restaurant or bar and relaxing before bed only to find that the restaurant was closed (which was fine) and the bar only served pizza (okay, we'll have pizza) but on that particular night, they were out of pizza and had nothing to serve us. The staff then strongly recommended and sent us to a local bar that turned out to be a smoky hole-in-the-wall with the music so loud we couldn't hear ourselves think, let alone talk, and a waitress was seen bringing out a bottle of beer squashed into her sweaty armpit since her hands were full of other drinks. 
I'm just of the mind that if you don't have a lot to work with (an older building) and maybe the area you are located isn't in the best neighborhood, that you make up for it in service and amenities and at this particular hotel those things were just non-existent!

title: “Great location, small rooms”
text:
The Grand Hyatt, NYC is located by Grand Central terminal, which I found convenient because my meetings were scattered north and south. The hotel lobby is currently undergoing a renovation, though the bar area was not affected. An indoor shopping area attached to Grand Central terminal sits under the hotel. My room was clean and comfortable, though was as small as any room in a major NYC hotel in which I have stayed.
The staff was courteous and the lobby market place offered a selection of food and beverages. It was priced typically for bigger brand names in NYC, and given the location it
was a decent value. I would probably stay here again given my company's travel policies, but otherwise am likely to look for a place with a bit more space.

title: “Nice Accommodations, Convenient Location”
text: This 4 star hotel served us perfectly for a recent weekend getaway to Philadelphia. The hotel's location was close and convenient to public transit as the Market Street East station is just 1 block away - great if you're arriving via train! There is a lot within a reasonable walking distance of the hotel. The hotel itself is nice, nothing wowed us but nothing really disappointed us either. I will mention a few things - WiFi is not included for free with your stay, however the Starbucks has AT&T wifi, so if you have an AT&T phone you should be able to pick that signal up from the lobby. Our room faced Market Street, so while we had a nice view, we heard the sirens and other loud street sounds through our 9th floor window. You must have your room card to make the elevator go to your floor, this is clearly stated, but as a weary traveler I didn't notice sign until the elevator went up to the 7th floor, stopped and then started going back down again. The staff that I interacted with were friendly and accommodating.

title: “Great hotel & fantastic customer service”
text:
This is a very delayed review as it was 6 months ago this week that we stayed at the Pearl Hotel. I’ve never felt the urge to write a review of a hotel before, but I really wanted to for this hotel as I was so pleased we found this little gem & wanted to share our experience with others thinking of staying here. 
7 of us Brits (age ranges between 30 & 62) arrived at the Pearl late on a Sunday night in November 2010 after driving from Las Vegas. The service we received at check in was great, we were advised on where to park our car (if you park on the street round the corner, its free as opposed to paying for parking outside) & were shown to our rooms. It was nearly midnight when we got our luggage out of the car & into our room when we discovered a (very minor) issue with our room. We weren’t going to mention it to reception but thought we would bring it to their attention. Without going into lots of detail (as it would be boring!), we received the best service over our 4 day stay we have ever had on our many trips to the US from this hotel. The reception staff were fantastic in helping to resolve our problem & they went out of their way to make sure we enjoyed our stay at the Pearl. 
You can tell this isn’t a chain restaurant & is a family run hotel as the little touches made a big difference to our stay. For example, they leave a note after cleaning your room each day telling you what the next day’s weather will be & the menu for that evening’s dinner at the restaurant. We were very fortunate to be offered a free meal at the hotel, to be totally honest we were hesitant at eating in the restaurant as we like to explore the local area rather than eat at our hotel for dinner. We were very pleasantly pleased at how yummy the food was, both my husband & I had the burger & loved it – they aren’t lying when they claim it to be the best burger in the area! We were only disappointed that we left it till our last night to eat there as we would have had more food there had we ate there earlier. We ate in the outside little garden terrace & although it was a chilly November night, it has several garden heaters that made it a nice cosy area to eat & drink in. Before we headed out for the evenings, we had a few drinks in the bar – the beer drinkers in our party were impressed at the wide array of lagers & ales on offer. I had a lavender cocktail that I remember being very tasty indeed. There is a good seating area around the pool / cinema screen to enjoy drinks from the bar.
With regards to the room, each one has its own fish tank on the wall which is something I’d never seen before in a hotel & I loved this detail. Between us we had 4 rooms so I got to see all rooms & all were of good standard.
The location is pretty good, we drove to SeaWorld, San Diego Zoo & Old Town – none of which took that long to get to. For the evenings that we went out into San Diego, the hotel rang up for a taxi & it didn’t take long to reach our destination. 
Overall, I would rate this hotel very highly & if you are thinking about booking this hotel – I recommend that you do as you won’t regret it. 6 months on, all 7 of us who went on the trip adored this hotel & we still talk about our stay there – it was a real highlight of our 2 week stay to Las Vegas, San Diego, Anaheim & LA. If we ever go back to San Diego, I will make sure we stay at this hotel & if anyone who works at the hotel is reading this – thank you very much for the fabulous service!

title: “Worse than Motel 6”
text: The rooms are terrible -- small, noisy, dirty... and all for the average price for $520 per night! I stayed here by myself on a business trip and my $600 room was so small that I couldn't get by without knocking something off... My other 5 colleagues have similar complaints... Wouldn't stay here again!

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
What a fabulous hotel this is! We had a wonderful stay; amazing location, superb city!
The staff of the hotel are excellent - they are attentive, efficient and work incredibly hard to ensure that your stay is first rate.
The room we stayed in was really lovely - art deco style, recently refurbished and classy.
I would certainly stay here again and highly recommend it to anyone contemplating a stay in this great city. Hotel situated on Michigan Avenue - central to EVERYTHING! we coiuld not have asked for a better location or hotel.

title: “Not at all near Union Station”
text: I booked this room after calling them directly to question the location. Although they are named Union Station they are 15-20 minutes away by car. However they assured me that the hotel shuttle whould take us to Union Station any time we wanted. NOT TRUE! The shutlle runs once every 30 minutes from 7am to 11am and once an hour from 5pm to 11pm. That is certainly not all day or on demand! The driver did give us his cell number in case we were going to be late for any reason, which I thought was nice. There is no charge for parking, which is a big plus. The room was relatively clean and the bed was comfortable. Breakfast was included and consisted of waffles you could make, bagels, toast and pre-peeled boiled eggs, which kind of gave me the willies, but I ate one as there was no other source of protein. The coffee was good. There is a rail line right out back, with quite a number of trains rumbling by but I was so tired from all the walking I did downtown that they did not keep me up. There is wireless internet.

title: “Clean rooms but noisy”
text:
We stayed here twice in may, and stayed in two different rooms. The first one was the biggest and less noisiest (you are nearly IN the Manhattan bridge), the other one was smaller (still OK and clean), but very noisy. We heard and felt every train going by.
I liked the neighbourhood, it was funny to have our first steps into NYC in Chinatown. The location in Manhattan was OK too, near nice neighbourhoods and restaurants/bars in Lower east side.
In short: good location and nice rooms, but noisy. They charge for storing your bags, $ 2 a piece.

title: “I like the design,it is fantastic”
text: I like it because the services are good,the people on the reception are helpful and the breakfast it is also good.it was quiet in the room even if it was a club in the hotel.

title: “needs re-decoration and updating”
text:
2 night stay.
room very hot - 
hotel is noise with thin walls - 
safe needs you to carry a key (not electronic) - 
no wifi in the room (only chargeable) but free in lobby - 
room needs updating (mould in bathroom) - 
somethings not working (bathroom door doesn't lock) - 
good location +

title: “Mixed feelings”
text:
Let me break up this review into sections as there are different opinions around different parameters.
Location:
Conveniently located close to the freeways and the mall.However right now (Aug 2012) this is in a royal mess due to construction around the 465. Hopefully when the construction is complete this would be more convenient. But till then purely avoidable unless you like sitting in traffic for hours!
Room:
The suites are nice. They are designed well and the bed is comfortable. The downsides were spiders in the bathroom and lack of attention to the appliances in the room. The phone had a broken jack so you had to hold it in place if you wanted to use the phone
The dishwasher did not work.
The television was not connected to the DVD player and staff on reception said they could not do anything till next morning when the technician came in. Well we would have checked out by then... still could not offer a solution. 
The manager on duty was much more helpful. She came and tried to fix the DVD (apparently needed a connector that was missing). She actually got it from another room and helped us get the DVD player to work. That was good customer service.
Breakfast:
Major let down. Hardly any variety. Most Hampton Inns have more spread. For the same price have seen other hotels run an omelet bar. 
Saving grace was the helpful lady at the breakfast area.
Front desk:
This is where you get the first impression of the property. The staff here could be a bit more courteous and forthcoming to help. The two guys there would probably do better in a non customer facing role.
With a few pluses and minuses, this property manages to tide by my expectations but unless they pick up their act and tighten the loose ends, they will end up loosing a lot of business.

title: “Great boutique property and location”
text: Found this property on Tablet Hotels and got good value for a Times Square 4-star. The pictures are very representative so was very satisfied with the stay. It's quite dark and moody which isn't to everyone's taste but was great for us and the dark rooms helped us sleep and get over jetlag! The room had every amenity we needed for the 4-night stay and though the New York rooms are renowned for being small it was more than adequate. The staff were very helpful and charming and helped make our celebratory stay very comfortable.

title: “Recommend for business travelers”
text: I stayed in a fair share of Marriotts as a Gold status member and this one was impressive. I was very happy with the service at the front desk and location of the hotel. Despite its location, I could not hear a thing once I was in the room. It is a great spot to be able to walk out of the front door and get to a number of theaters. If you can stay on the concierge level, it is definitely worth it. The views from the lounge are lovely, and the breakfast was wonderful.

title: “Loved the Suites”
text: I stayed at the Marriott Suites a few months back. I found the staff and hotel quite pleasant. Every thing was very tidy. The staff was very efficient and friendly.
