I look forward to my next stay at the Dallas Marriott Suite hotel. I always recommend this location to my friends and family!! THANKS SO MUCH FOR MAKING MY STAY SO WONDERFUL!

title: “Incredible. I could live there.”
text: Have done most of my trip planning based on TripAdvisor searches as well as overall reviews from folks. Based on what my needs were for this PA trip I turned to the aka hotel in Rittenhouse Square. From the second we arrived we were hooked by the accomodations and charmed by the staff...... and it never stopped. We stayed in an amazing 'room' that had over 1,000 square feet - more than most condos! We really lucked out since this room also had a full kitchen! Was a blessing since this was the weekend that Philadelphia received 23 inches of snow ! We ran to a local market, got provisions and hunkered down for the blizzard. Wound up having a great adventure, at a wonderful hotel. This is really a hotel for extended stay corporate travelers so there is no restaurant, etc. However, I would, without any hesitation, recommend this hotel to anyone travelling- for any reason. You can always find a restaurant closeby or bring/buy groceries while you are there.

title: “Wonderful hotel”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights at start of holiday to Boston, Plymouth and Cape Cod. Hotel was amazing. Beautiful lobby, large room with 2 queen sized beds and very clean. Staff were on the ball with service. My 5 year old son was greeted with a toy lobster when we arrived. 5 minutes later he received a bag to colour in and felt tips. He was very happy! 
We were greeted every time we entered the hotel and staff really wanted to be of assistance at all times. There was coffee in the lobby but only in the mornings. It would be nice if it was all day.
Boston is a beautiful city and the hotel is so close to Newbury street and Boston common. We were able to walk to most places even Quincy market. Although we got a taxi back as my little boy was tired. Lots of great restaurants near to hotel. Ate at the Irish bar one night. Food was great but beware huge portions. We completely over ordered!!!!
Would I return? In an instant. Cannot believe negative reviews were from the same hotel I stayed in.

title: “Nice surprise at The New Yorker”
text:
Went as a gift from my family for my 60th birthday. When we checked in Ana noticed it mentioned my birthday on the reservation and gave my daughter and I free full breakfast every morning, beautiful chocolates and we had a nice big room with two beds and two closets. We were so surprised and Ana made our day. The hotel is in a great location with all the subway lines within a block and Times Square about 15 minutes away by foot. 
We walked from Times Square at midnight every night and felt totally safe. Macy's is right around the corner and there is lots of great shopping within a block or two of the hotel. The Empire State Building is only 3 blocks away. Overall great stay. I would definitely return to the New Yorker!

title: “What a cool spot!”
text:
We had a wonderful time at this magnificent hotel. My wife and I spent our one year wedding anniversary there! It was magical and we had a blast!
HIghly recommend staying at Hotel Drisco. Thanks for everything!

title: “Nice and clean hotel, great location”
text:
Great location, minutes walk to Union Station and the Capitol. Close proximity to the Mall made it easier to spend more time in all the great museums, and the monuments. 
We booked "allergy friendly" room. Room was very clean. But small. 
Bathroom was clean, but again small. And not enough racks/shelves for towels for family of 4.
Parking was very expensive, at $40 a day. They did inform us that we could park at the Union Station for $20 a day, which we did after the 2nd day. 
Service was good, they delivered the extra towels promptly when asked. We stored our laptop with them everyday when going out, and had no problem at all.

title: “Great service And location”
text: Great week at a a beautiful hotel along Lady bird trail. This is definitely a place to book. Amazing staff w great service...close to everything? The staff from the first to the last day were incredible

title: “Exactly what we were looking for”
text:
We ended up at Hotel 71 after a Hotels .com search for downtown Chicago hotels close to the magnificent mile.
The price was right and were were surprised with an unexpected upgrade to an Executive Deluxe. The newly renovated room was lovely, the view spectacular, and the ease of walking around to where we wanted to go was exactly what we were hoping for and more. Michael and Kareem were wonderfully welcoming and the only thing I would change is to forego the valet parking and just park the car for the weekend. We never drove anywhere!
Walked the mile and then over a few blocks to Fado's Irish Pub.. authentically fun atmosphere, cold beer and excellent appetizers while we watched the football games.
That night we walked- literally- one block over the bridge to eat dinner at Smith and Wollensky . We had a river view window table, excellent service and the best Steak Oscar I have ever tasted.
We'll definitely be back to Hotel 71

title: “A fantastic hotel in an ideal location!”
text:
We stayed at the Argonaut for the first four days of our honeymoon in San Fran, and it was utterly perfect.
The location was amazing, right on Fisherman's Wharf. There were loads of bars, restaurants and shops within walking distance, most notably Pier 39.
The hotel staff were great too - so welcoming and attentive. We even got a little welcome gift in our room to celebrate our honeymoon!
Our room was a great size, with everything you could want - including free wifi and a view of the Golden Gate bridge! We loved the nautical theme running throughout the decor as well.
To top it all, the hotel runs a free wine tasting evening every night - what's not to like?!
A fantastic hotel - highly recommended, we'll be back!!

title: “Bah Hum Bug!!”
text: When I was at The Belnord it seemed adequate, even though we had no storage space. However, I got home a few days ago and am covered in bed bug bites from head to toe. Do not stay here unless you like bed bugs!!

title: “Great location, sleek and sexy”
text:
If you are looking for a wonderful location in the heart of Times Square... this is it. We were perhaps not the typical clientele for this cool, very modern and sleek hotel, as we were here on a family celebration. Two grandparents and mom and 16 year old. The rooms at first seem on the small side but are extremely well laid out. Ample space for luggage and the beds are unbelievably comfortable! We slept like logs. 
As you arrive there is music playing outside the hotel and as you enter it is like going into a nightclub. Very cool atmosphere, sleek furniture, and the offer of salsa lessons, but everyting was handled extremely efficiently. We arrived at the hotel and were in our room in under 10 minutes. There is only one elevator so there can sometimes be a delay, but it is a small boutique hotel so there are not many rooms. The continental breakfast is included and was very nice- fresh fruit, tea, coffee, bagels and cream cheese, croissants, danishes and a selection of muffins anad cereal as well as bacon and eggs for those who prefer a hot breakfast - a good way to start the day without having to go out a look for a place to have breakfast.. All in all would highly recomend this hotel.

title: “Home away from home”
text: Since Sept 2009, my son and I have stayed at the Ramada Hollywood each month for 7-14 days while he filmed a tv show. My son uses a wheelchair and the hotel is so very accommodating to his and my needs. The hotel is immaculate and the staff makes you feel welcome and safe. The location is minutes from the studio and all sightseeing. We now feel we have a 2nd home in CA!

title: “Good central hotel”
text:
Stayed at the hotel for three nights as part of a Califonian tour.
I looked long and hard for a hotel in San Francisco as good hotels are expensive. Settled on the Nikko for the ok cost ($300 a night) and the location.
Room was on 18th floor, was a bit small but clean and it had everything you would want. Had a great shower over the bath and a smart fridge which was in two parts. One for the mini bar and the second for you to put your own water, etc in.
The hotel is a great location, near the shops and transport, etc. As other have said you have to pay for the Internet which is a bit much considering the cost of the room but we just went to the starbucks in the hotel. The local Westfield shopping mall also offers free Internet.

title: “Personalized attention in a remarkable setting.”
text: The Hotel Indigo exceeds the expectations of travel goers. A fun and captivating modern atmosphere exists throughout the hotel. From a heavenly bed to a chic bar overlooking Petco Park, this hotel is sure to please all, including guests' four legged friends. My fiancé and I couldn't imagine staying anywhere else! One particular individual, a bartender named William, who works there made our trip especially memorable by providing individualized attention combined with a friendly attitude to everyone in our group. After the experience he provided us with, we look forward to returning to the Hotel Indigo!

title: “Excellent one night stop”
text: We stayed here on 7th May having arrived from UK at 6pm. We wanted an efficient free shuttle service and a restaurant on site and got both here courtesy of a booking through Hotwire. I think the previous two postings must have been very unlucky. We found everything satisfactory. We had a meal in the bar. The salmon salad was very good and enormous - enough for two. Morning shuttle was also very good - we were going to the Car Rental Facility and the hotel driver dropped us at a terminal where we just walked across the pavement to a waiting airport shuttle bus (free).

title: “Won't be staying here again.”
text:
We chose this hotel for a family vacation largely as a result of favorable Trip Advisor reviews, but won't be returning. It seemed promising at first. The room was ample but I question the "newly redecorated" part. Everything felt (and looked) very late-90s to me. The staff were friendly and responsive, but we had a bunch of minor problems that sort of added up. Our thermostat didn't work, the pbs station on the tv didn't work (and that's all our kids watch!), the dvd player didn't work, and our room was missing a trash can. Very responsive fixes to most of these problems but the pbs never got fixed---we were told it was a LodgeNet issue).
The location is a little odd....there appeared to be a mobile soup kitchen a couple of evenings right outside our window which drew a colorful crowd. I never felt my safety was threatened, but it was not exactly a neighborhood feel. Skip the breakfast...many local places were very good but the whole "Carribean Room/pool" scene was pretty unpleasant. The pool is very small, not particularly clean, and not somewhere we felt comfortable lingering.
The worst part of our experience was the cigarette smoke. We did have a non-smoking room, but even with the patio door shut, smoke from the neighbors must have been seeping through the walls. Our poor little asthmatic three-year-old ended up on oral sterroids she flared so badly (handy CVS pharmacy a few blocks away). If we hadn't brought a portable nebulizer with us "just in case," we likely would have ended up in the ER. Most good hotels are entirely non-smoking these days, and I no longer even think to ask about cigarette smoke. Big mistake!
I would not give this hotel four stars. Maybe three without all the other issues. At best, 2 1/2. The bill for six nights, with parking and only 1 breakfast, was $2,800. I think we would have been much happier at a Westin or similar business-class hotel. The beach location doesn't add THAT much. We still had a nice vacation, but it was more in spite of the hotel than because of it.

title: “Not bad but not wonderful”
text:
Got shared van from SFO to hotel was very painless.
Checking in went ok but card machine was playing up so couldn't get room keys so they took us to the room and told us to come back for the keys later. We were given a choice of 2 rooms one on the 7th floor that was subject to a lot of lift noise or one on the 5th that was quieter but had a smaller window. We took the one on the 5th (506). We were informed that there was a little function happening in the lobby later with free wine and entertainment provided by the bloke that checked us in, it turned out it was just him with an electric keyboard plonking away. 
room was a very nice size compared to rooms we have had in american citys before. decent sized walk in closet with a safe. Bathroom was al right size wise but bath looked very grubby. bed was large but not very comfortable (we do have an exceptional mattress at home though) but we slept well.
location wise the hotel isnt too bad but we did see a number of drug deals in close proximity within 2 blocks. nice bar next door and a few markets nearby as well. Lots of students though. 
There are buses that go past the hotel from just above union square but to get to union square you need to take a left from the hotel then turn left at the corner walk down the block then wait outside a dry cleaners.
San Francisco seems to have a huge homeless/drug/drunk problem they are every where staggering round asking for money quite clearly doped up or drunk. as said before we did see quite a few drug deals while we were there for a week possibly 10+ and quite often when walking around the city you could get very strong smells of weed yet the police dont seem to do anything.

title: “You REALLY care and follow through”
text:
I recently returned to Hotel Angeleno for the fourth time mainly for the location and
the overall satisfaction. This time, I really got it. They REALLY care. And they
DO read their questionaires. I managed to leave behind an expensive article of
apparel and they secured it for my friend to pick up. They would have mailed it
but were kind enough to send me a personal note to acknowledge that all would
be well. Gracie, Merci, Shokran, Danka, Arigato, Muchas Gracias. Won't stay anywhere else when I am in the City of Angels.

title: “Mold infested and horrible, rude service”
text: If this site would let me, I'd post a picture of the black mold on the ceiling and the hole in the wall. The carpet was ripped and rumpled. Check-in tool 50 minutes and he front desk workers were rude and incompetent.

title: “Fantastic Stay!!!!”
text:
Myself and a friend of mine stayed at this hotel for 3 nights at the end of March for a girlie shopping trip. 
I have been all over america and have to say the free breakfast was one of the best I have had there is such a good range of food to suit everyones taste. 
The check in was good and smooth. We got given a rom right at the end of the corridor on the 9th floor, which was quite, good size and clean. the maid service was brilliant even laid out our products for us, as we left them in a pile.
The staff were great, reccommending some resturants for us to try, I have to say concierge Robert was lovely - he was funny and really helpful. 
The situation of the hotel is fantasic - one block from michigan avenue and is literally 2 min walk with subway next door and 7- eleven just down the side road. 
I would have to say our overall stay was great and we had a fantastic time especially as my friend had never been before. 
I would deffinately reccommend to friends and family and have done so already and when I go back to Chicago with my other half, We will deffinately be staying here as the price is right for the great service you get. 
Thank you to the staff at Fairfield who made our holiday an even better one.
TIPS:
Got to go to signiture room at top of John hancock centre as sun is setting amazing view. 
Warburtons (I think thats what it is called) steak house 16 oz new york strip best steakl i've ever had and huge portions - i swear they think they were feeding a family of 5 not 2 people.

title: “Enjoyed our stay - great location”
text:
Our family of 4 stayed at the Vintage Park for 6 nights as we toured around the great city of Seattle and area. We booked the Queen Queen Deluxe Room with 2 Queen Beds; the room also had a sofa, chair and coffee table which was great additional space. We requested a quiet room on an upper floor and that's exactly what we got. Beds were extremely comfortable. Before our arrival, we were contacted by the concierge, who helped arrange for transport from the airport as we were arriving later at night. They also booked the Mt Rainier Tour for us - they agreed that the one we saw on TripAdvisor was the best one for us!
The location of this hotel is great; it is near the library (tip: you can access free internet daily at the library if you need a computer - the hotel does offer complimentary WIFI, but charges to access the computer iin the business centre) and restaurants; easy 10 minute walk to the Pike Market as well as the more crowded shopping district - the hotel's area seemed much quieter and safer than others - we walked back from both a preseason football game and a Seattle Mariners Baseball game. We also got a free minibar item for being Kimpton members - remember to sign up for this free program. We really enjoyed our trip to Seattle and to this hotel.

title: “The Best”
text: We had a pre-paid week-end rate, which made this one of the best values we've had at a major chain hotel in a mjor city. But it wasn't the price value that made our stay so special... nor was it the great location. It was the absolute friendliness of the professional staff. They acted liked they really, really were happy that you were staying with them. And it was everyone... from the doormen, the desk staff, the concierge, the cleaning staff... everyone. The rooms are large, the beds extra comfy and the bathroom well supplied.

title: “No frills, but great location - parking across the street for $28/day”
text:
Stayed on the 8th floor, view faced a wall next door, and was located right next to the ice machine on our floor. Didn't matter - we didn't hear any outside noise at all, and we only heard the ice machine a few times during our three-day stay. Beds were comfortable, and we slept really well.
Good light in the bathroom, not much light in the main room, dingy but decent decor. 
You can't beat the location - it was a 15-20 min walk to the corner of Michigan and Wacker, and we made the trek a number of times over the weekend. We parked our car in the ramp across the street and let it sit for three days at $28/day - definitely worth the peace of mind, and the lot was locked each night and perfectly safe. 
Would recommend to anyone who cares more about location then decor, and who plans to spend most of their time on or around Michigan Ave.

title: “clean”
text: we stayed for one night in july,we booked a one room suite.the rooms were spacious and clean.I slept on the pull out sofa bed which was uncomfortable,my friend took the bedroom and said the bed was good.The location is excellent,right off of N st., short walk (5min.) to harbor which is cool.we paid altogether w/tax $165.00 for the night,very reasonable.

title: “A beautiful place”
text:
I read the reviews on Trip Advisor for this property which had it ranked as #1 in Chicago. I got a king room overlooking Michigan Ave. The view was beautiful. The room was also impeccable. Nice and bright, very fresh and modern. I find it very hard to fault any Sofitel's. The service, attentiveness of staff, cleanliness and luxury are always top notch. 
Location was great, head left from the lobby and you reach a bunch of european style cafe's and restaurants. Straight ahead of the hotel on Michigan Ave is a shoppers paradise. A great place to stay, and much better value than Park Hyatt. I do find some of the charges in luxury hotels to be a bit crazy, such as for the internet. When you are paying top dollar, a few inclusions would be nice.

title: “Awesome location, great service, and spacious rooms”
text:
I hope to vacation again in Washington DC, and when it happens, the Palomar is where I will stay again. Its DuPont Circle location offers plenty of restaurants and shops within casual strolling distance. The Metro is a couple blocks away, giving one easy access to all the other sights of the city. 
It was an extremely busy weekend in DC, and the hotel was at capacity. This did not stop the staff from offering as much time as needed to answer questions about anything. They also greet you with a warm smile whenever you pass through the lobby. It makes it feel like a home away from home. Highly recommended.

title: “Trying too hard”
text:
What can I say, this hotel came at the end of a wonderful Highway 1 road trip for my wife and I. We got a great deal on price, but having stayed in hotels of this (apparent) standard before, we had certain expectations. Many of these were not met, so here's a summary of them.
Location: a hotel of this standard would be expected to be in a nice location. Don't be misled, the W is not in the cleaner, nicer West Hollywood area, but in the run down area of Hollywood Blvd, about a mile from the main Hollywood bustle. If you're into smoke shops, 'adult' shops and tattoo parlors, this is for you. If not, you may not (like us) enjoy the area so much. Surprising therefore that a 'designer' hotel would be located in this part of the city...in fact, we did not like the atmosphere outside of the hotel complex after dark.
The hotel complex: nice restaurants and bar areas (if you're happy to pay $15 upwards for a drink) but full of wannabe types and those who reckon it looks good to be seen in this place. We were unimpressed by this. Compared to hotels such as the Gamercy Park in New York this one seemed to try too hard to be something it wasn't. 
Rooms: nice room, not massive, but had a nice look and feel, retro-futuristic design. We really liked the room. We had a courtyard view, which was nicer than the view onto a parking lot or the rather run down hollywood and vine area. Also this aspect meant it was quiet at night,so we got good sleep.
Cleanliness: we couldn't honestly say whether our room was actually serviced or not. If it was, it was certainly a rushed job!
Overall, nice rooms, wrong location, a hotel which attracts wanabe A-listers, but tries too hard to be something the location won't allow it to be. A good 3-star hotel at best, with some good price deals at the moment. Just don't expect the same feel as Sunset Blvd or West hollywood here!

title: “Do yourself a favor... don't stay here!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text:
Oh my gosh...where do I start....
We arrived early ... no room available. They said to retun in an hour.
We returned every hour on the hour...no room. This started at 10:00 am only at 9:00 pm did we get a room. The lobby smelled of sewer gas or mold or something terrible. We got to our room and it was disgusting. There was food debris on the countertops and kitchen floor. The bathroom had hair on the floor and in the tub. There were dead crickets in the hallways... and roaches in the room. The first day it was warm, but the AC did not work. We tried to get another room and were told there was nothing else available. 
Next morning we went down for breakfast only to be told that they had stopped doing breakfast because they had a new manager. We tried again to get a new room for the second night and we were told that the hotel was sold out and there were no rooms available. The person at the desk was very unfriendly. Later in the afternoon, we came back to try again, and we were moved with no problem. When we told the desk clerk what we were told in the morning, he laughed and said they had plenty of rooms. When we told them what had happened, we were told that the morning person just didn't want to bother with us. The second room was just as filthy as the first.
This used to be a great hotel. It has really gone downhill. The company must be in financial trouble or something. The hallway carpets were filthy. The furniture was beat up. The desk was leaning against the wall because one of the legs had come off - I reattached it, but was affraid it would fall on my daughter and wouldn't let her play near it.. 
It's a nice location, but spend the extra 30 bucks and stay at a better hotel!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Stuck in Denver, Days Inn at the Airport was a welcomed sight”
text: Great hotel option if you need one at the Denver airport. It's clean, US Military friendly and reasonably priced.

title: “a great find”
text: spent time twice over 2 weeks here. the first time was its birthday so guests were invited to the food and desert truck outside and drinks inside-all free. What fun.Service was amazing, so personal-how's your day -every one speaks to you without being intrusive. It 's a lovely building in a not so hot area -well near the parole board and Port authority bus terminal-2 other family type hotel in area so lots of people around. i always felt safe as did my daughter.The rooms are spacious and beautifully done\ even coffee and tea making facilities. The staff must be particularly handpicked.

title: “Beautiful hotel in a great location”
text: We were in town for a soccer game and spent two nights. Our room was a great size with a king bed. Service was wonderful and everyone was very helpful. We had drinks and brunch in the restaurant. The food and staff were great.

title: “Lovely small hotel in great location.”
text:
Arrived to find I had mistakenly booked another Marriott hotel and also didn't have my cocnfirmation number with me, but had my Marriott Rewards card. The desk manager was wonderful. He tracked down my reservation, cancelled it and provided a lovely room at the same price of my original reservation. He was pleasant, smiling and welcoming the whole time.
It's a great location for walking and shopping. My sister and I attended the Boston Ballet before checking in and took in the Chihully Exhibit at the Museum of Fine Arts the next day. The breakfast buffet at the hotel was convenient and a good value for the selections offered. 
Overnight parking is pricey at $42.00 and the vallet informed me of the cost on arrival. Convenience is worth the price. Other oprions might be less but not by much. It is Boston!

title: “Pleased”
text: I stayed at this hotel from Sept 8n through the 12th during my son's graduation from Basic Training. I was very pleasantly surprised. Our rooms were clean and kept clean the entire stay. All of the employees were friendly and very helpful. The food at the restaurant was good and the children eat free. I would recommend this hotel to the families of airmen.

title: “Best hotel I've stayed at in a long time! Newly remodeled and very nice!”
text: This is an extremely nice hotel. The rooms are large and very comfortable with a great view of the city and local mountains. The Westin Workout facility has very nice equipment and they always have complimentary bottled waters and towels available. If you forget your headphones, they have complimentary sets for you to use. Nice big bathrooms with walk in showers. I definitely recommend. Who knows, maybe I'll become a Starwood guy.

title: “Caught in a 1960's Polynesian Time Warp”
text: The lobby tells you what you're in store for: an indoor waterfall, a dark koi-filled pond, lots of palms and tropical plants. Inside the complex you'll find a maze of pathways lined with lots of overgrown tropical plants/trees, streams filled with some huge koi, and a multitude of ducks (and lots of duck crap...so watch where you walk and don't go barefoot!) Our first impression inside the room wasn't much better: we had two stained comforters on the beds, carpet that was in need of replacement, bathroom tile that needed some serious re-grouting. We were unable to get a king bed (hotel was booked solid they said) so they gave us what they called 'two queens', which in reality was two full-sized beds. The place needed a fairly significant face lift and freshening up--and perhaps a good hosing down as well. It did look like the hotel was replacing carpet in the rooms across the courtyard from us, so perhaps they're underway with the cleanup. On the plus side, the pool was very nice, there is a large hot tub, and the hotel is in a convenient location, within walking distance to many restaurants, bars, etc. and Mission/Pacific beaches. We did not use the restaurant or spa services; however, we would not stay here again.

title: “Lovely outdoor pool garden in middle of city”
text: This hotel is not only a bargain for the expensive Galleria area, but it has a lovely outdoor space amidst a busy urban area. We had a large room with a refrigerator and microwave, and bought food supplies at the nearby Target (a short walk) and relaxed after a busy day. The staff is friendly and helpful. We didn't have a car, but noticed that there is a large parking lot. Breakfast and internet are included in the modest price. My husband had a business meeting in the garden by the pool.

title: “Excellent shuttle service , room allocation issues”
text:
I stayed here for a night as I knew I was arriving very late- plane was delayed at JFK and I ended up calling the shuttle around 1.30am from the courtesy phone in the Jetblue terminal- it came within a few minutes. The shuttle is regular and will drop you at the airport T station (blue line) if needed- I used it several times that day and found it really convenient. 
Due to the late hour of arrival I basically took the room key from the desk and fell into bed without taking too much notice of the room- I was allocated a room on the 9th floor (9 and 10 are the honors levels). For plane spotters the view from upper floors towards the airport is great -with the bonus of effective soundproofing. There are free computers in the lobby.
As it was the weekend the honors lounge is actually closed so I was given as voucher to the restaurant for a hot breakfast. Breakfast was good- plenty of choice-all very nice.
Before checking out I looked at my reservation and realised the room type allocated to me was really a downgrade from the larger corner room I had actually booked . I queried this at checkout and had my bill reduced accordingly ,although the argumentative clerk insisted that the rooms were "nearly" the same despite the room descriptions on the website- I find this hard to believe-it all seems rather deceitful. 
This is part of a problem I have encountered on numerous occasions as an honors member where the "upgrade" is really a worse room ( smaller than the category booked) but on an honors floor. Honors members it pays to asked a lot of questions before accepting a room so you know what you are getting.

title: “Terrible Visit, room was like an oven, front desk personnel terrible!!”
text: The main reason for my review is the room was about 85-90 degrees in temperature, I went to the front desk to tell them and they told me it was because the seasons were changing. So, what I have to roast because the seasons are changing? Front desk personnel, were totally unresponsive. I asked for a fan, which I got 3 hours later. The second night same temperature and then there was a gas smell in the hotel, I reported it and got no response. I left, didn't even stay the second night, wasted alot of money and the front desk personnel, worthless.

title: “Pleasant - excellent value”
text:
The Microtel Inn (off I-77 - Sunset Rd) says that it is the newest hotel at the interchange. I mistakenly assumed it was a year or two old, its apparently been around much longer. This being said, the age of the hotel is / was not an issue.
The hotel has free hard wire high speed internet (which is what I was looking for) and it really works well. 
When it comes to what matters, the hotel was perfect.
I would not have known that the hotel wasn't only a year or two old had I not asked.
There isn't a great deal of dining, shopping, entertainment, etc. at this interchange however there is plenty a few interchanges up on I-77 (where there are much newer - much more expensive places to stay).
If you're looking for an economical place to stay that is clean and has free high speed internet, this isn't a bad choice.

title: “Great location and great service!!”
text: Stayed here for Marine Corps Marathon. Located across street from Metro and within walking distance of great restaurants, sites, etc. Two Starbucks within 2 blocks in either direction. Staff was super friendly and attentive. Shannon in restaurant/lounge was awesome! Definitely would stay here on next visit to DC.

title: “La Quinta Inn Indianapolis East”
text:
The room was very clean and I was very happy with the service. 
The only thing I was unhappy about was that there was no hair conditioner. The one time I forgot it, but if you take your own, it's no big deal.

title: “An awesome hotel in every aspect”
text: I can not say enough good things about our stay here. First, the location was amazing; 1 block from central park and a 10 min walk to times square/rockefeller center. The staff was so friendly and helpful and the hotel is gorgeous! Spend the extra money and get a room other than the standard. That room is way too small so we upgraded and was well worth it. Seriously, this was my first trip to NYC and the folks at the Hudson helped make it the best trip. If you want to save money on food there is a whole foods across the street that has great prepared foods

title: “Overall very nice”
text:
We just arrived home after a week stay at the Clift in San Francisco. The following is a brief summary of our stay. Overall I would have to say that the hotel gives a very nice "boutique" experience at a reasonable San Francisco price.
Location: I have to agree with other reviews that the location is overall very good. The cable car is just two blocks east of the hotel on Powell Street. Also, its a few blocks from the upscale shops of Union square. The location's only down side is that West and South of the hotel the neighborhood makes a considerable turn. A large number of very aggressive panhandlers take any opportunity they have to ask for money. Having visited many other large metropolitan areas over the years I have to say that San Francisco is the one with the largest number of people asking for money. 
Hotel staff was very helpful. Whether it be arranging dinner plans at a local resturant or assisting with transporation to the airport they were very accommodating. 
Rooms: we were upgraded to a corner suite as part of the Amex fine hotels and resort. The size of the room was great! However, the bathroom was way too small for a room of that size. The furnishings were very simple. No dresser at all and a fairly small closet so I would pack on the light side! 
Dining and Entertainment: our daily breakfast in the Velvet room was great at first. However, it was amazing to mee that there was absolutely NO change to the market buffet during the ENTIRE week we stayed at the hotel. The coffee was excellent but it was offset by the lack of other variety in the breakfast offerings. Management could at the very least TRY to offer up some variety!! The downstairs Bar was excellent. Drinks were pricey but well done. The bar food was great. 
The Clift delivers on nearly all its promises. I would recommend it for sure...

title: “Not a pleasant experience”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Artisan at about the midway point in a Southeast US Road trip. We had been staying in friends' guest rooms and pull out couches and we were looking forward to having our own space and not encroaching on anybody's house. This was the wrong place to attempt such an idea. The hotel is in disrepair. we tried to nap during the day, but someone was shampooing the carpet in the hallway for at least 5 hours. the smell of the cleaner mixed poorly with the funky scent that had greeted us when we checked in. The hotel is quite a ways from Beale St. It's not situated in the greatest of neighborhoods and we worried about the safety of our car in a poorly lit, non secure parking lot. All in all, our stop in Memphis was nice, but with a better hotel, it would have been great.

title: “Being Renovated.”
text:
October 1st is what they expected as the completion date for the renovation. This was a Four Points by Sheraton until recently. The location is near I-465 and not far from Clay Terrace that has a lot of great restaurants and shops.
When you walk in the lobby looks nice and right around the corner is a small bar and past check in is a small snack shop and a couple of computers for the public.
We stayed in a room that we think was renovated, but not finished. It was a nice room with great linens and choice of pillows but there were paint splatters that had not been touched up, the plumbing access in the shower was bent down from the ceiling and some other imperfections. 
One gripe is that there is only a bed side light next to one side of the bed, so if one of you is a reader, better chose sides of the bed wisely.
There is an indoor pool and hot tub, a gym I never saw, and meeting rooms.
Kudos to the staff for being so friendly when they are also dealing with the chaos of a hotel full of kids for a baseball (I think) tournament.
I really feel that by November this hotel will really be nice place. I would come back and try it again (after the renovation of course.

title: “Everything you need is there, and would go again!”
text: Laid out very nicely with complete kitchen. Clean and secure. Staff was very helpful and courteous. Great little vacation.

title: “Magic @ the Murray Hill”
text:
We booked our short stay after reading about a hotel price special via travelzoo.com. 
Arrival was smooth with a map, directions from the hotel web site, and low-traffic @ arrival time, around 3PM. 
Parking (valet only) costs $32-42/day, with no in/ou, which we'd read about on the hotel website. OUCH! But, hey, it's NYC.
The front desk staff were friendly and welcoming, and check-in took less than five minutes. 
Our room on the 7th floor was lovely, with lots of attention paid to decor and cleanliness. Lighting options were unique and plentiful: artful swirly blue glass lamps, circular lighted mirrors (small and large) in the bath, individual reading lights - - modern and very cool! 
Top-notch cleanliness and comfort, particularly with mattresses, pillows, and bedding. Loved the homey-touches of afgans spread across the foot of each bed corner. The sleeper sofa was not made up, as per our request at booking, but one call to the front desk and that was taken care of right away.
We'd read on hotel reviews here at TripAdvisor that the top floor offered great rooftop views - - and that was right on! There is a clear view of both the Empire State Building and the Crysler Building, as well as a beautiful nighttime NYC skyline from the 16th floor. Signs indicating that the rooftop was only for use by 16th floor guests though put us off momentarily. Maybe we weren't supposed to go up/out, but we did, and I'm glad. Very, very nice view.
The hotel is located within easy walking distance of the Empire State Building, Grand Central Station, St. Barts, and more. A bit further to 30 Rock, but completely do-able. 
We've paid far more for far less in other NYC hotels!

title: “Not ideal for couples”
text:
My fiance and I spent our first vacation of the year at the Hyatt regency hill Country Resort and Spa. The property looked beautiful and the reviews were mostly positive. If you have a family, this place seems wonderful - but if you are a couple looking for a romantic escape, definitely look elsewhere.
We arrived EARLY - around 10am on a Sunday - although the room wasn't ready yet, Tess said they could probably have one ready for us in an hour or less which was pretty impressive as we didn't expect to be in a room until at least 1pm. If you are planning on arriving early, there is a chance a room could be ready much earlier than the '4pm' check in listed. Tess was very friendly and even remembered our name from a telephone conversation earlier that morning. 
We opted out of waiting since we were heading out to Seaworld - a quick less-than-10 minute drive from the resort - it would be nice if they offered shuttles to Seaworld (saw a Marriott resort shuttle there and parking is $15 so it would have been a nice to have that available) Either way, they carted all our luggage away and let us know it would be delivered to us when we were ready to be checked in.
Check in is very easy, Phillip at the front desk was very informative and enthusiastic - the luggage was delivered to our room in less than 10 minutes by a bellboy. 
We stayed in a King room on the 2nd floor in the 800 wing. (which is actually the same floor as the lobby which is nice though our 'balcony' was more like a walk out patio) The room itself is spacious and I love the separate vanity and sink though the toilet and shower room were quite snug. You can tell the rooms are dated (there were chips and cracks in the paint of our door and in the tub itself - also there was no fan in the bathroom?) but overall comfortable.
My fiance had a headache that night - NOT helped out by the fact that the hall noise is incredibly pronounced - there must have been at least 3 screaming kids that woke him up on separate occasions throughout the evening. 
The amenities are average with the exception of the lazy river. The lazy river is nestled in a lovely natural setting - it feels like you are floating down a real river minus the critters, dirt and sharp rocks! There are plenty of tubes and they keep the grounds immaculate. (Props to Fred the friendly groundskeeper)
Bikes can be rented for 30 minutes at a time and it takes around 10 minutes to do an entire loop. 
It being a resort, everything is at a premium. There are hidden surcharges and fees added to everything (18% extra for the food at the poolside grill and $6 extra if you want to split a meal at Springhouse) - the portions are generous at the Springhouse cafe but the food is truly subpar and not worth the hefty price tag. For breakfast or a quick lunch, you are better off going to the general store for made-to-order burgers and generously sized breakfast tacos! All the ladies working the General Store are truly fantastic and very sweet.
Service was exceptional with the exception of Mike at the Springhouse Cafe (we waited forever for the bill and he had to be hunted down by both the waitress and busboy on two separate occasions just to receive service!) and the fact that 'hotel policy' forbids you from checking out a luggage dolly. I understand that they want to make your life easier at the resort by handling your luggage for you BUT if you are a do-it-yourself type of person than it seems awfully strange to be denied the freedom of choice. We ended up making several trips to our car to load up since they forbade us to use one of 25+ luggage dollies in the front as I didn't want to use the bellboy for checkout. 
Overall
*Pros*
-Lovely natural setting and well-kept grounds
-LAZY RIVER and free shuttle service/access to the slides at Wild Oak ranch
-Friendly service and smiles wherever you go
-Family friendly - lots of activities for the kids
-Close proximity to Seaworld
*Cons*
-Smaller resort compared to La Cantera or the new Marriott resort
-Noisy halls and crying kids 
-Older resort 
-They would rather you lug 3 loads of luggage out to your car than allow you to use a luggage dolly
-High prices for average food (Food was much better at La Cantera IMO)
All in all it was a nice resort but nothing phenomenal. I have stayed at both the La Cantera resort and the Hyatt - if you are looking for romance, I would definitely opt for the La Cantera - save the Hill country Hyatt for the kids!

title: “Love The Drake!”
text:
I stayed at The Drake for almost a week for a conference being held there. The room overlooking Michigan Ave was bigger than I expected for such an historic hotel. Very large bathroom, closet w/personal coded safe, desk w/chair as well as a sitting chair and side table, large credenza w/TV, and of course the comfy queen bed. Yet there was still plenty of room to walk around.
The food inside the hotel is too expensive. I had to leave the hotel for meals that weren't provided at the conference because I refuse to pay those prices - or have my company pay them.
I used the concerige several times and was able to find my way around easily with her guidance. All the staff I encountered were great. Especially the housekeeper and I wish I had gotten her name because she's the best I've ever had and deserves to be recognized. When I do the hotel survey I'll be sure to provide my room # so they'll know what they have in her.
My only complaint about The Drake - and the reason I couldn't give it an excellent rating - was because it is the NOISIEST hotel I've ever stayed in. Doors slamming (or some kind of booming) constantly! In addition, on the last two days I was there Navy fighter jets were practicing for the weekend air show over the lake which is just behind the hotel. That's not the hotel's fault but you can imagine how that was and with the room rates so high - it's too much noise and they should compensate for the inconvenience and provide ear plugs to all their guests staying in their rooms.

title: “Definately a Business Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Hyatt Regency for 3 nights and, although it is still a nice hotel, it is not (as Priceline and other sites demonstrate) a "4-star hotel". In its prime, this hotel was probably the place to be; however, today, it seems to really cater to the business travelers. 
It is located in what appears to be the business district and during our stay, we noticed MANY business travelers. Furthermore, they had a business reception in the pool area during prime swimming time, which made for an awkward setup between the families and the business travelers.
Overall, the room was decent, but it is showing its age. The valet was wonderful (very easy), but somewhat pricey. All in all, we had a nice time, but would have rather stayed somewhere more family friendly.

title: “4 night stay in Warwick New York Hotel”
text: A buddy and I just returned from 4 night baseball trip to New York, staying in the Warwick New York Hotel. The location is absolutely fantastic - close to all of the major sites - Central Park, Times Square, 5th Avenue, Rockefeller Center, Broadway theaters, and more. We bid on Priceline and got a room for $175 per night. The staff could not have been friendlier or more helpful. The room was clean, comfortable and quiet even though we were close to the elevator. The only problem, and it was a small one, was that we did not get hand towels or wash cloths regularly. We usually had to call to request them, but we received them quickly after calling. We did not use the restaurant or bar facilities, so I can't comment on them. We had no problem with our bill upon checking out. As a matter of fact, everything went very well with no surprises.

title: “Wonderful stay!”
text: We found ourselves stranded by yet another airline so we started calling around Baltimore for a place to stay. We took a gamble on this hotel. It was an excellent choice. Spacious rooms, wonderful bathrooms, robes and comfortable beds. They even offered us a nice glass of wine as we checked in. The building is beautiful and historic. The restaurant located in the hotel was a welcome sight considering it was pouring down rain. Excellent service and the food was very filling. I highly recommend this hotel in Baltimore.

title: “Lost sleep!”
text: We stayed here because of a reputable name of Jw Marriott. We had a horrible night. This is our first time in Houston so the entire family was so excited and booked the hotel for two nights. First , our room was small and so the two beds. The room was just behind the elevator but didn't notice the sound until ready to fall asleep. Every time the elevator goes up and down so with the noise. We didn't call for change of room since the kids were so sound asleep. We didn't sleep that night. To make it worst the pillows are so uncomfortable. That morning we checked the pool and the sauna. The pool was okay. When I went to the sauna, the sauna room was warm not hot. I think it was 80 degrees not 105-110, the right temperature for a sauna should be. Called the front desk that the temperature of sauna was not hot but nobody came to fix it. We checked out that day and found another hotel. I would not recommend this hotel to my friends and family.

title: “Luxury hotel with down-home service”
text: After conducting extensive web research, I chose the Palomar for my stay in San Francisco last week on vacation. I found a wonderful deal for the room, but I was concerned my husband and I would be stuck in the broom closet. Thankfully, my fears were unfounded. Staying at the Palomar was overall a lovely experience, during which we were treated as first class guests. I will say, though, that I missed having a "real" lobby area, and the concierge service was spotty, since the concierge also doubles as a front-desk worker (believe me, the desk can be quite busy at all times of the day). However, all the staff were quite friendly and tried to be helpful in any way. The room was well-decorated, the beds were comfortable, and the towels/bath fixtures were sumptuous. Be sure to take advantage of the Fifth Floor restaurant -- the hotel holds a few tables for hotel guests, so there's no need to try for an impossible-to-get reservation before you go. While pricey, the dining experience is worth it!! The location is prime, close to all public transportation, yet somehow the interior of the hotel managed to be completely sound-proof to the extremely noisy street. Very relaxing environment. Check around on the major travel websites for deals on this hotel, and you won't be disappointed.

title: “Great service and value, slow internet”
text:
I stayed in a room on the 8th floor that faced 6th street. I did not have a problem with road noise nor a problem with graffiti or dumpsters out my window like some other reviewers did. 
Overall, I thought the hotel staff was really friendly and the room in top condition. I must agree with the other reviewers who commented that this Hampton Inn is a notch above the others. In the room, the attention to detail is very apparent. There is a dish to put the soap near the sink (often missing from many hotels I stay at), they put stickers on toilet paper rolls, and the housekeeper leaves their name on a little card should you have any concerns. 
The breakfast, in my opinion, was more than generous. The day I had breakfast, they had fresh fruit, waffles, muffins, danishes, toast, cereal, oatmeal, scrambled eggs with ham, biscuits and gravy, and french toast strips.
The only negative aspect of my stay was the horribly slow internet (both wired and wireless). I did a speed test and the download speed came to 0.5 Mbps which meant lots of waiting for pages to load and abandoning any hope of streaming any videos.

title: “Very Good, but soft beds”
text: Overall, a very nice hotel with wonderful service. The only issue I had was with the soft beds, which are much softer than I am used to. Specifically, it was soft not because of the pillow top covering that they place on top of the mattress, but because of the underlying soft mattress, which gave minimal support.

title: “Loved it, hotel very nice, needs work in room service area”
text: Just got back from our 2 night stay, we would stay there again. We had arrived 3 hours before check in, had no problem getting our connecting rooms. My husband had called and said we were coming up to celebrate our 36th anniversary and also our grand daughter's birthday. When we returned to our rooms, there were cupcakes in the girl's room and champagne in ours. (thanks Mark, you are amazing) The only issue I had was with the room service. No cart (to eat on), we had asked for waters with lemon to go with the food (just got 2 glasses, no lemon) and when they brought the food 1 order was missing. 45 minutes and 3 phone calls got it. (the gentleman that brought it up said something about he had to go to Jewel to get the ham for the sandwich, in all honesty, the sandwich didn't come with ham and we told him when we ordered it, if they didn't have it leave it off) Like I said, we would stay there again & again. Keep up the good work!!

title: “Not a great vacation/relaxation spot”
text: I stayed here for a two-day business meeting. I spend 70 plus nights a year in hotels for business and pleasure.This property is fairly run down. The room I had was clean, but needed major updating. Smelled old and the carpet and furniture had seen better days. Price was reasonable and included a very basic breakfast. There is nothing around this property. No restaurants, stores, places to walk or relax outside. There is an indoor pool. This property is geared toward those leaving on cruises from the nearby port or for those that need to be near Johns Hopkins. The hotel does have a complimentary shuttle for getting to the Inner Harbor and other attractions, but it must be on their schedule and the last one leaves Baltimore at 10:30 pm. And strangely, no airport service. There is free parking. I am 60, and was one of the youngest guests staying at the property.

title: “Good location, average hotel”
text: me and another chaperone took 5 17 year old student to NYC for a week in June for Journalism workshops on Columbia. We chose this location because of it's access to the subways lines to go to Columbia or downtown to the sites. We LOVED the location of the hotel. We were 2 blocks from central park, 2 blocks from the subway and 1 block from an amazing grocery store. The area felt less touristy and more like a home to people who actually live in the city. We walked by schools and daycares, grocery stores and dr offices. This is the first time in 3 years (and 4 trips to NYC) that I have seen an area this "laid back" and residential. We were within 10 minutes from Columbia and 10 minutes from Times Square. We chose this hotel also because we could get a room that fit 5 people. One of our rooms (that I was in with the 4 girls) had 2 queen beds in the room, and a pull out sofa. My students said the beds were comfortable, but the sofa may have been some of the worst sleep I've ever had. The room wasn't cleaned thoroughly. The tub got a little grungier every day. We constantly had to call down for towels. Front desk staff wasn't overly helpful. It was nice that there was a breakfast buffet - definitly saved us money. And the price was great. Considering how little time we spent in the hotel, I wasn't too picky. If I had been able to sleep as well as my students, I have rated it higher. For the price, this hotel is worth while. But it's just an average hotel.

title: “Clean hotel with a Great Free Breakfast!”
text: This hotel is in a great location! Close to fantastic shopping at the Shops at La Cantera and The Rim shopping areas. Also about 2 minutes from Fiesta Texas, and not too far from Sea World. The breakfast served every morning at the hotel is huge and filling. And the staff was great!

title: “Wow! Fantastic, amazingly historic hotel.”
text:
The Willard is known as the "residence of Presidents" because every president since Franklin Pierce has either slept in or attended an event at the hotel at least once. The term "lobbying" was coined due to those waiting in the lobby to ask favors of presidents and others in power. Julia Ward Howe formalized the patriotic "Battle Hymn of the Republic" at the Willard. Martin Luther King, Jr. wrote his 1963 "I Have a Dream" speech here (which means they allowed African-American guests in 1963)!
None of that would mean much if the Willard wasn't a great hotel. It is. My upgraded King was large with a small wing for the bath rather than a teeny cut-out of part of the room. All the furniture and linens were in excellent condition. At the end of the small wing was a connecting door to the adjacent room with bay windows. From a corner 7th floor room the only street noises which penetrated were sirens, which weren't very loud. It would have been easy to oversleep with the quiet (despite the location next to a secondary elevator) and the comfortable bed.
It wasn't the purpose of my visit, but sight-seeing would be easy from the hotel. Right across from the White House, the hotel provides easy access to the typical tourist sites, and as previously mentioned the double-decker tour busses stop at the hotel. Valet parking ($35) was easy and speedy. The Elizabeth Arden Spa looked excellent, but I did not take advantage of its services, despite the temptation of the deep tissue massage
My experience with room service was excellent. The tri-color ravioli in pesto sauce was delivered in just a few minutes at 2 am, much faster than experiences at other hotels. I didn't like it that 10 oz. bottles of soda were $4, but that is typical of hotels of this class, and the $7 bottle of Fiji water made my trip home easier. If you remove a mini-bar item from it's place for more than 20 seconds it is electronically billed to your room, but I had no problem with that even with picking up items to check their size vs. price. A few had a tempting ratio. There are many shops for food across F St. along Pennsylvania Ave. if you do not wish to indulge in room service or the hotel's restaurant and bar.
Because of the limited unloading area and crowd of cars being dropped off at the hotel, I rushed and left my navigation unit in the car. I called about it at 1 am, and the staff was exceptionally speedy in locating and delivering it to my room.
Staying at the Willard was a reward night for me, and I have no regrets about using it here!

title: “Great location, nice hotel”
text: We really enjoyed this hotel. The suites are very nice and it was great to have the extra space during our 4-night stay. The hotel is in a great location and you can walk to so many things. They had a really great promotional rate for the room and I would stay there again. The one big annoyance that we had was with the elevators in this hotel. You have to take one elevator up to the lobby and then go to another bank of elevators to take a different one up to your room. It just felt like we spent quite a bit of time waiting around for elevators due to this and there was no way around it. Other than that this hotel is really great and I highly recommend it.

title: “Way Exceeded Expectations”
text: I figured this was just going to be a run of the mill conference center style hotel. It is, but it's so much more. My room looked like it was built the day before I got there. It was immaculate and the amenities were great. This is a very eco friendly hotel, but nothing is lost because of it. The staff was amazing. Friendly and helpful from the parking garage ticket taker to the room service delivery guy. Speaking of room service, I got back to my room late one night and got room service. It was one of the most amazing meals I've ever had. I can't say enough about this place. Friendly service, great location, great rooms and amazing food. Loved it.

title: “Clean. Convenient. Cheap.”
text: We just spent 4 nights at the Best Western River North in Chicago and had a GREAT stay. The room is clean and well kept. Pretty basic, but really good. Great mattress, and we got great sleep. The location is fantastic, the rooms are comfortable and the parking is FREE. The hotel is an easy walk to State Street and to Michigan Avenue. Will definitely stay there again.

title: “Hide your wallet!”
text: What a surprise I got when I checked in to this so called resort. First of all, how can you call yourself a reort when you sit next to Interstate 10? There are no good amenities available in the area. I was disappointed at the mandatory $40 a day resort fee that was revealed to me upon check-in. For that you get valet parking, usa today, internet and admission to their athletic club and water park. The water park was dirty, the room leaked water in the bathroom and the staff in the gift/concession were rude. They will not see any money from me again.

title: “sad view from the window for that price!”
text:
I came to this hotel to relax after a long week of conference. I just wanted to chill out and enjoy a nice weekend of shopping and meeting friends before back home.
 From the photos, I was expecting a bright spacious room, or at least some view of Boroadway... nope. And I paid LOTS for it.
My room was a small double, indeed clean and with a very comfy bed, and the plus side of no nasty carpet, but so so tiny. Not even a small desk, a part from the bedside table. I had to place everything on the small fridge, located on the floor. I didn't think the fridge location was really hygienic, however I must say the inside was clean and shiny.
No storage space at all: the so call wardorbe was too tiny to fit my luggage into, and the few hangers were not enough for my clothes. the upper shelf was filled with covers so I could not place anything on it, therefore I had to leave all my clothes on the open luggage on the floor, totally feeling like a temporary passenger, not feeling at home or even close to it. 
The bathroom was very clean even if basic, and fresh towels were provided for me even if I went out quite late in the morning. 
The worst thing ever was the view from the window: a brick wall. Next to it, another brick wall. If I really really stretched my neck, I could see a 10x10 cm of sky, very high above the building. It felt like a prison. Plus I didn't want to leave the window open, since it was very dusty and dirty with pigeons feathers on the outside. 
On the good side, the staff was really friendly and the location is unbeatable, and there are lots of nice places to eat around. 
however, since I wanted to chill out after a buzzing day in the city, this did not work at all. I just felt kind of claustrophobic in that room (I think it was room 629, but not sure) and for what I paid, I'm not sure I'd like to go back to this hotel.

title: “Great time!”
text:
We had a great time at the Catamaran. My mother, son and I went for 5 days/4 nights. Everything went smoothly. We were upgraded to an bay front suite which was beautiful. We could walk right out the door to the beach. My son loved playing in the sand, and the bay side was much more relaxed than the Pacific side. We did eat at a restaurant on Pacific Beach a few times called World Famous...the shrimp tacos were amazing! We had breakfast every morning at the hotel, and the portion was large enough for my mom and I to split it making it a very reasonable price for breakfast. 
The hot tub was large enough for my son to swim in, so he spent most of his time in there rather than the large pool (chilly at night). He also loved the free arcade room. This was a great resort for a family vacation!

title: “Great!”
text: Great! Excellent! The best hotel i've been to so far! excellent facilities and very accessible!

title: “Everything costs extra!!”
text: Internet was between $14 and $17 depending on what type of service you wanted. Gym was extra $17. Parking was extra $20. There were barely any channels on the TV for all those who like to vege out. You had to cab it to everything if you don't have a car. Horrible ATT service (although I guess that can happen everywhere)! Restaurant service was sub par at best - we had to re-order multiple times in order to get what we wanted, it was slow to come out of the kitchen. It took house keeping over 24 hours to clean up the room service tray outside our room. Took them 48 hours to remove the wine glasses.

title: “WORST MOTEL EVER”
text: Worst Motel I have ever stayed in. Closet size rooms, Dirty, Threadbare Towels, Walls so thin I could listen to conversations in next room . 1980'S TV

title: “very nice and comfortable”
text: I dont usually write reviews on places ive stayed while on holiday,But after seeing some of the very poor reviews i felt compelled to balance it up a little.First things first,the lobby was something special with the darkness highlighting the cosy fireplace.The room whilst not massive, was a fine size for my partner and i,Loved the Ipad ,the comfy bed and the best shower ever.Great location for Times square ,Broadway ,Central park etc etc .We were in new York for my partners 40th ,And on returning to our room after a hard days exploring We found a bottle of champagne in an ice bucket ,plate of cookies and a nice handwritten card ,Very nice touch thanks again.My only gripe about the hotel was the prices of the food and drink ,10 dollars for a beer was a bit too expensive for me ,but there are loads of other places nearby to whet your appetite (not much cheaper by the way).Overall very nice place to stay would recommend to anyone .

title: “HOagy's Heroes thank Vagabond Inn”
text:
The
Vagabond is a great place to stay. I stayed at the Vagabond as one of a group
of charity riders ... Hoagy's Heroes who were riding from San Diego to
Jacksonville to benefit the children of veterans. The rooms were excellent and
very clean with comfortable beds. The swimming pools (Two) were both very clean
and very well maintained. Even the hot tub was super clean which is different
from most public hot tubs I have seen. The 'make-your-own' waffle breakfast was
a very welcome change from the bland continental breakfast served by so many
less welcoming hotels. All in all I had a great stay and want to thank Vicki
and her staff for making us welcome.

title: “My stay at the Wyndham El Paso Airport was superb”
text: The Wyndham El Paso Airport is a great hotel to lodge in. It is within walking distance from the airport. It has many close restarunts to dine at if you prefer not to dine in. The conference rooms are very spacious. The bottom line of this report is that the Wyndham El Paso Airport is the hotel you must lodge in if visiting El Paso.

title: “Will not be back”
text: I travel a lot for business and have stayed at other Hilton Garden Inns numerous times with no complaints. This one was by far the worst ever. I stayed in room #302 for four days. Complaints: there is no bathtub (only a shower), the sink area in the bathroom is very, very small (hardly enough room for a flat iron and makeup), no full size ironing board, the clothes bar in the closet is very, very low, so when I hung my clothes up in the closet, they would drag on the floor, the gentleman that checked me in seemed unhappy to be there and did not tell me about the $10/per day parking charge. I did like the huge desk in the room and the free internet service. I will pick another hotel the next time that I am in Houston.

title: “Running Stairs with Luggage - 9 Flights!”
text: We stayed 2 nights at Homewood Riverwalk and will not return, despite the fact that we go to San Antonio several times a year. It was not apparent when we checked in on Friday night with our 3 teens that we would have such a terrible frustrating experience. On arrival, the room was clean and orderly, nicely appointed though nothing special. A flat screen TV in the sitting room but an antique in the bedroom. The check-in clerk could not have been more gracious. However, the nightmare began on Saturday morning. Breakfast is served until 10 AM - or at least it is so advertised. We left our room at 9:00 and after waiting nearly 15 minutes for the elevator to arrive on the 9th floor where our room was located, we got to the Breakfast Buffet at 9:15. It was standing room only... completely inadequate seating area for a 10 story hotel. Dirty dishes were stacked on every surface and no bus boy in site. The "buffet" was cleaned out. No items were re-filled in the 20 minutes we walked around trying to find a place to sit and something to eat. The only stocked stations was the make-ur-own waffle area which had a line 15+ deep at all times with 2 griddles. U do the math! We had coffee and cold cereal while standing up! We then waited another 15 minutes for the elevator back to the 9th flloor. After we readied ourselves to leave for the day, we called for our car from our room and then again waited nearly 20 min for the elevator to arrive. By now, a sign was hanging on the second elevator car stating that it was out of order. So a capacity crowd in a 10 floor hotel was being serviced by 1 elevator. After we finally got to the lobby, despite the 20 minute lead time we still had to wait an additional 10 min for our car. We left for the day and when we arrived back at the hotel Saturday night, it appeared the elevator situation had been sorted. We were fooled. Sunday morning it was the exact same scenario... waiting forever for a single operational elevator car that was packed wall to wall with people. Breakfast was somewhat better stocked and we did find a place to sit...expect that many people chose to leave early rather than eat there again and deal with the single elevator car! We waited another 15 min for a lift back to our room so we could gather our bags for check-out. Our teens got frustrated and took the 9 flights of stairs! It was such a hastle that we decided against trying to use the pool or other amenities as planned before leaving. When we called valet for our car, we were told they were not taking any calls for cars... it was first come first served to the valet podium. We left our room and waited another 30 min to get back to the lobby via the single elevator . The lobby was running over with people and baggage as most of us were trying to escape the insanity and while others were just beginning it by checking in to this ill-equipped facility. We waited another nearly 45 min for our car to arrive! I used 80,000 club points to stay here and spend my weekend annoyed, hungry and frustrated! Never Again - Do Not Stay At This Hotel unless You Want to Run the Stairs with your Luggage.

title: “Great hotel, excellent service”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for 4 nights and were both really happy with everything. 
The rooms werent the largest but they were clean and well appointed and we had a nice comfy bed. we got a great deal online and compared to some other prices that were quoted for similar hotels in and around the same location we did really well.
The staff were extremley helpful and just couldnt do enough for you, the are a real credit to the hotel. LIke others have mentioned the walls are quite thin, but the noise was no greater than I have experienced in other much larger, much more expensive hotels and we were never bothered by it.
Some have mentioned the unsafe location, however we felt very safe, but San Fran is like any other major city in the world, you just need to keep your wits about you and you should be OK. We walked everywhere and came back relatively late most nights and had no issues at all. 
I enjoyed this hotel very much, the wine tasting in the evening was a nice touch and much enjoyed after a days sightseeing. I would recommend this hotel and a cheaper alternative to those on a budget but still looking for quality and some style.

title: “Fantastic”
text: Great hotel, location & srevice. Staff was unbelievable!!

title: “Don't Stay Here”
text:
Hotel was awful. 
1.      Check-in process was disorganized and confusing (seemed to be a bunch of students at the desk who were new or lacking the appropriate training). Our keys were not programmed correctly, and we had to make a special trip back to the lobby to correct the problem. Another colleague could no open her door because the lock stuck from inside. At 10:00 p.m., this was not what any of us wanted to experience.
2.      We asked for a bar where we might get a nightcap. We were sent to a local bar that was very inappropriate for professionals. It was loud, people were drunk, service was horrible and slow—it was more of a rowdy college scene than a professional setting.
3.      We asked the night auditor for directions to the Adler Planetarium. She had never heard of it, and wasn’t able to help us using Google Maps, although she did try.
4.      The restaurant was understaffed and extremely slow. I helped myself to coffee from the wait station since no one came back to check on us. We chose not to eat there on the second morning because we didn’t have time and felt the food was mediocre.
5.      The concierge desk was not very well informed. We asked for directions on a few occasions and no one seemed to agree on distances, times to allow to get from place to place, etc. They had no more gym passes although I was told when the reservation was made that in addition to the fitness center on location, there were passes for a nearby gym. They didn’t know how to help me find an outdoor running area—said the good concierge was on vacation? When we asked how long it would take go get from the hotel to Rosemont for an 11:00 a.m. appointment, they told us to leave no later than 9:15. We were at the appointment location in Rosemont before 10:00 a.m.
6.      The fitness center on location was small and too busy—had to wait 25 minutes for a treadmill. There were no wet wipes in the fitness center for both days I was there. It was dirty.
7.      I was charged for water in my room, and I didn’t use any water.
8.      The housekeeper walked into my room without knocking on Tuesday morning at about 9:00 a.m. I was ironing a dress shirt and wearing nothing but underwear. She didn’t even apologize, but backed out and said “Oh I’ll come back later.” I would expect this at a cheap motel, but not a Marriott.
9.      Overall, this was the worst Marriott I’ve stayed in, other than the one at Houston Airport.

title: “So bad it is almost funny...if I hadn't had to stay there”
text:
I've liked Extended Stay hotels in other states because I like to cook my own food when I travel on business. Not this one though! I booked this through the hotel website and requested a "very quiet top floor non-smoking room". When I arrived I was told that the hotels do not receive any "special" requests made on the website, and that the staff had been given the holiday (Thanksgiving) off and only one room in the entire hotel was cleaned to be available--a first floor room near the lobby. It was actually quiet enough, except when the desk clerk was having spirited conversations with friends in the lobby.
The real problems were:
A continually running toilet. It could sometimes be coerced into stopping, but would run so hard it also flushed itself!
Food (pasta sauce?) on the kitchen floor.
A sticky toilet seat (eewww...)
The iron was encrusted in black sticky stuff, which I ruined pants with (my fault--I should have checked it before using).
The trash disposal room across the hall was not attended to and smelled like, well, garbage.
PUKE IN THE BED (no I'm not kidding--see photos)
The last, of course, was the intolerable problem. I took the stained pillow and case to the desk to demonstrate the problem and was rather grudgingly supplied with clean linen. I asked for a clean mattress pad and pillow, as these were also soiled. I was told they were not available and I could check out if I was not happy with the room.
As I had already moved in with all my stuff and was cooking dinner (on Thanksgiving Day) I went ahead and stripped the bed, gave the soiled items to the desk clerk, and used my own sleeping bag and pillow I had in the car (I had planned to camp the next week at a state park, not in the hotel!) Because I was there on business and had very early and late hours over the holiday weekend (and I had cleaned up the worst of the room) I put up with this for the 3 nights I had booked. There was no apology, no comment from the manager (perhaps also on vacation?), no service for the room, no discount for cleaning the room myself, and no response to the e-mail I sent to the Extended Stay Corporation after my stay.
Obviously I won't choose Extended Stay again!

title: “Great for one or two night layover.”
text:
Arriving at SeaTac at around 10.30pm we were pleased to find the shuttle area relatively quickly and within 5 minutes the shuttle turned up. A couple of minutes to the hotel and the driver helped us to unload.
We had 2 rooms booked and check in was quick and easy. One room was fine but the other was simply too hot, sauna like, the control on the wall did nothing to reduce the heat coming out of the vent. We approached reception and were told, confusingly, that there is no individual aircon in the rooms, it was all centrally controlled. I later took this to mean that the rooms could be individually heated but not cooled. Anyway they offered another room without a problem and that was that.
The rooms were quite large, the beds comfortable and we got a good night’s sleep, there was no noticeable noise. Breakfast was available for around $7 next door, and whilst nothing to get excited about was acceptable (especially for $7) and the waitress in there was really pleasant and helpful.
We had a 2 night layover due to the Icelandair schedules and decided to spend the first day in Seattle. Asking at the desk they pointed us in the right direction for the train, and it was about a 10 minute stroll along the road. The second day we decided to go to the local mall before our late afternoon flight and, after storing our luggage for us, the receptionist arranged for a taxi to take us there and pick us up later for about $20 each way, which for 3 of us and the convenience was fine by us.
Overall a great place to stay for a layover. A good price, comfortable rooms and convenient for shops, trains, planes and food. Next time I’m passing through Seattle I’ll be sure to bear this hotel in mind.

title: “Clean and Comfy”
text:
Pros: Hotel is very clean and Staff is very helpful. Rooms are very new, Rooftop Terrace restaurant has a super view on 9/11 Memorial. Price is very low for NYC standards. South Seaport TKTS locations is within walking distance. Several Subway stations are within a few blocks.
Cons: Hotel is so close to 9/11 Memorial/Ground Zero that the construction noise (24/7) can be very annoying (I have the idea that once the construction ends, prices per room will skyrocket...). Location is far from everything of interest in NYC, but as stated above subway stations are very close by...

title: “A lovely hotel, everything you could hope for.”
text:
This is a lovely hotel for a relaxing break, it is quiet and have everything you could hope for.
i had a room without any outside space, on reflection I think getting a room with outside space would have been better. The room was large, separate TV / lounge, big bath, a lovely big and comfortable bed. The gym is very well equipped, particularly for cardio machines, I think there are 6 treadmills plus stepper and i think there was a bike as well, but it is all new kit with ipod connectivity. There is a cable machine and some free weights up to 50 kg. The pool is small (ish), a cooling off pool, not for swimming, but the service there is excellent, it was notable that the staff remembered that I preferred no ice in my water, there is also food available by the pool.
On my arrival it was a very nice touch to have some water sent to the room, plus a fruit platter.
The bar whilst I was there was quite quiet, but they do have a happy hour and "special" nights to liven it up a little, but in truth, this is a hotel for mature adults, not for the hedonists.
I thought the main restaurant was good, but not great, maybe it was my choices or my mood.
