I went to the Fashion mall one night (it was a $15 towncar ride), it is very lively up there, lots of bars and restaurants, I went to Wildfish, which was good.
Royal Palms is a little isolated, so you probably need a car, unless you are like me and happy to stay on site.
I used the Spa on the last day, it is in keeping with the rest of the resort, quiet and stylish.
Overall, I had a lovely stay at Royal Palms, it is a classy place, quiet and perfect for relaxing and recharging your batteries.

title: “Did not stay, still charged $150!!”
text:
DO NOT EVEN THINK ABOUT IT! Horrible experience with the manager, Beth, over the phone before we even got there. Tried to cancel reservations because it was our 10th anniversary and my husband booked the room before he knew I had made other plans to surprise him. The manager would NOT let us cancel the reservation and we were going to be charged $150 for the room whether we stayed or not. Tried 3 times to reason with her and explain that we did not want to stay there on our ANNIVERSARY, but could not afford to lose our money. Totally rude, unreasonable, and condescending to me. 
So, since we were going to have to pay $150, I cancelled my special plans, and we went to the hotel. It was dingy, musty, and smelled of too much cleaning solution! The decor was 70's log cabin- complete with a picture of a deer on the wall. NOT a quaint, romantic place like my husband had thought (from the website). NO VIEW due to overgrown trees and shrubs. Other guests had taken over the small pool and lobby. We decided we could not ruin our anniversary by staying in this place. I wish my husband had read these other reviews first. 
I am so glad we did not ruin our anniversary by staying...even if we are out $150...it was worth it NOT TO STAY! This place needs new management, tree trimming, and re-decorating. Then it might be ok.

title: “Excellent accommodations, great service.”
text:
We selected Hotel Andra as one of our hotels for our out of town guests for our wedding weekend, hosted our rehearsal dinner in their banquet space, and stayed in one of their suites on our wedding night.
The facility is very modern and clean. All of our guests who stayed there were very complimentary of our choice of hotels. The location is great and within walking distance to many great restaurants and downtown Seattle attractions). The restaurant in the hotel, Lola, is wonderful. The catering for our rehearsal dinner was excellent (in house Tom Douglas catering) and everyone was extremely impressed with the quality of food for a 60+ person dinner.
Finally, the service was wonderful, particularly by Kelsey H., Hotel Andra's Sales & Marketing Manager, who coordinated the whole weekend, made sure the weekend went flawlessly, and helped make sure our wedding night was extra special with flowers, champagne, etc in our room that evening.

title: “Trip to Capitol Hill”
text: The hotel was very nice. I would appreciate if there was an elliptical machine in the fitness room so I wouldn't have to pay for the Health /Club around the block.

title: “Be careful”
text:
I paid an enormous amount to stay at the Quincy BUT---the room I booked (king)was not available so they gave me a different room (queen) which was next to the heating/airconditioning plant. you can imagine after a journey of 36 hours how badly i needed to sleep but the constant noise had my ears buzzing long after I checked out . When I tried to check out the next day, the manager was not available and I spent a lot of money calling up just to figure out if I could get a refund..which I did not. The next day my room was changed, but the entire experience was already ruined. The hotel staff at the front desk is unfriendly if not downright rude. The only positives were the two doormen -Larry and a guy of mediium height, thin who wore spectacles. I think this hotel and its staff could actually learn a lesson or two from these two men who were courteous, helpful and polite. 
I have traveled all over the world and stayed in both top hotels and average ones. The Quincy is below average - the over size room stuff works only if you get it, else you are wasting money and time. btw, the internet sucks.

title: “We just loved it!!!”
text: Perfectly situated in New York (which matters much given how you walk in the city), this hotel far exceeded our expectations : very comfortable and vast rooms (with a view of the Empire state in our room), excellent service, splendid restaurant etc ... Let's hope this new hotel will not raise its prices too much in the years to come

title: “Great value and location”
text:
This hotel is older, but well kept-up and very clean. The beds were comfortable, and our room had a HUGE closet! Free Wi-fi, too.
It's attached to the Virginia Mason hospital, so is perfect for family of patients, but I stayed there while attending a convention at the Convention Center. It's about 6 blocks from there (pretty steep hills coming back) so was very convenient.
The food at the restaurant was quite good, and reasonably priced. There are also several restaurants within 2 blocks, as well.
I was worried about the noise, being so close to the hospital, but I didn't find it overly noisy, at all.
The rates were very good! Much lower-priced than other nearby places, downtown. Ask for the AAA rate, if you're a member.
The only downside was the parking - there is a surface lot a half-block away for $20/day, and the hospital parking, 2 blocks away, also $20/day.

title: “DONT GO THERE”
text:
My experience with the hotel is not the worst ever, but I tell u its not worth your money. 
I just moved to Intercontinental, I am paying here 100 dollars less believe it or not :S
and moreover, the hotel beds were very bad I wasnt able to sleep for 3 nights from back ache, bathroom had broken tiles , rooms very small :(
called for technitian to solve a problem I was having with water took him 30 minutes to arrive (which made me late to where I wanted to go) also the area where the hotel in is not secure :(
Also surrounding area is not really safe.
on the other hand the stuff were nice, but very slow it takes me 15 min each time I want to reach to front desk which is really so long

title: “Good Clean Affordable Accomodation”
text:
We stayed here in May 2008 based on the reviews on here! We weren't dissapointed. Just to be clear upfront - this is not a luxury hotel by any means, but for the price and location you couldn't ask for much more. The rooms were clean and had fridge and microwave which was a bonus. The shower was hot and the pressure good. 
What really set this apart though was the customer service we received from Varsa at the front desk. She couldn't have been more helpful, whipping out a map of the city of San Fran as soon as we checked in, circling all the best places to go, and highlighting the areas to avoid. We parked the car in their free car park (which we didn't find too tight or small contrary to other reviews on here, though we could understand how some may have found it a little tight in places). The car wasn't needed for our stay though as the hotel is just a few yards from a main bus route so we got a 3 day MUNI pass and used the frequent buses and trams during our stay. 
Breakfast is literally some baskets of pre-packaged Danishes Pastries and Nutrigrain bars, with Coffee and Orange Juice available. Nothing glamorous but adequate if you just want to grab a bite on your way out! There are also many eateries within a stones throw of the hotel (we recommend 'Polkers').
The hotel is not going to be for everyone, particularly those who want or need to maybe spend a lot of time in their hotel room, but if you are looking for affordable, clean and safe accomodation in San Francisco, then this would be a good choice to make.

title: “Ok hotel for the money”
text:
I bid for this hotel on Priceline and paid 80 bucks per night for Thursday and Friday evening. Given the asking price on the hotel site, it's not a bad deal. It is pretty close to downtown 6th street so we can walk out to the restaurant and bars without worrying about drink and drive. 
The overall service is good, except that when we asked for a king bed instead of two double beds, we were told it's no longer available, which I don't believe, I think they give less nice rooms to people who got a godd deal on third party. 
The hotel is still kind of old in our opinion and the pool on the roof top is a huge dissapointment, we were so excited and prepared to hang out in the pool but only stayed there for 10 mins. It was tiny (much smaller than the one we have in the house), water is not clear and the whole roof top is just .....how do I put it? big turn off ....
They also charge everything additionally: Parking, Internet.....Since I didn't pay much for the room so I was not that upset with it. 
I wouldn't not stay here again for the kind of money they ask for, but if i come again with friends to hang out in downtown area, I might still do my online bidding and stay there for the location.
Supprisingly, we didn't find this hotel that noisy as many of the viewers here said, maybe because we stayed on Thursday and Friday. Who knows, maybe the Saturday is the night!

title: “Incredible value. Very helpful staff. Beautiful room.”
text:
Staff was extremely helpful. The rooms were large, comfortable, very clean, and attractive. 
Amenities-including fitness room, pool, and sauna were very well-maintained.
The inclusive breakfast had a wide variety of choices.
I would definitely stay here again.

title: “great!”
text: Family rooms were large & had adequate privacy. The queen rooms were so tiny that at a few points 2 people could not pass. Inner rooms are nice and quiet. Definately the best location in town across from beautiful Union Square, and an unbelievable price. I am a 4th generation San Francisco who lives on the "other" side of the bridge now, but I come back to Villa Florence at Christmastime frequently.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
I've stayed in dozens and dozens of Manhatten hotels over the years and for the life of me I can't understand how others can rate the Distrikt so highly. I found it hugely disappointing.We reserved and paid extra for a larger room with two beds and a city view on an upper floor.Upon our arrival the room had not been cleaned so we told the front desk person we would return at 4:00pm. When we returned at 4:30 the room still had not been cleaned and there appeared to be much confusion and whispering behind the desk. Ultimately, we were told that the hotel would "try" to find someone to make up the room but they could not be certain when this would occur.Becoming suspicious, I asked the person to confirm the larger, upper room details etc. This only caused more confusion, whispering,and panicked looks. Finally someone whispered to another authorization to change our room. We ended up in a small room on the 19th floor (out of 32) with a view of the parking lot atop the bus terminal.The room had almost no place to hang anything up, two small draws and no shelves or counter space in the tiny bathroom. So, most of our clothing stayed in the suitcase for 3 days and all of the toiletries etc ended up on the desk in the bedroom.No sooner had we arrived in the room but housekeeping was at the door wanting to turn down the bed! This was not unique-the next day we returned to the room at 4:00pm only to find it unmade. After complaining, someone arrived to remedy the situation and less than 15 minutes later a knock on the door announced the bed turndown crew once again.The hotel is not very good at cleaning but they're great at turning down!
On the brighter side, the room was quiet, the beds were good and firm, the air conditioner worked and the staff generally was friendly. However, for the same money you can do much better in nicer neighborhoods and get what you actually pay for.

title: “Other than location, don't expect a lot.”
text: Was there for 3 nights the last weekend in July 2009. Booked through Hotwire for $100 a night. Would have been VERY upset if we had paid more than $100 a night. First, the location is right on Michagan Avenue, right in the middle of shopping and dining and near the major touristy spots (literally a 4 minute walk to the Chicago Architecture Boat Tour which should NEVER be missed when in Chicago). Just could not get over the location - it was perfect. The rest of the hotel, eh. Some sites were giving it 4 1/2 stars, some 5, but it is AT MOST a 4 Star Hotel. When we checked in we were told the hotel was completely booked. We were assigned 2 double beds. I asked if we could get a king and the front desk said no, not unless we wanted to pay $75 a night for an upgrade. But if the hotel was full, how was I going to pay for an upgrade? Day 2, with a completely different staff, was much more accomodating and they moved us to a different room. They only misplaced our luggage for about an hour, but it was found so no worries. The rooms are smallish, gym nice, the pool is very historic looking and neat. We never could get the internet to work in our room (and yes, we're decently technology savy people) - when we talked to the front desk about issues, they simply gave us a briefcase size box of cords and modems and connectors. Even after all that, never could get the internet to work. Not a bad hotel, but not a great hotel either. If you're looking for luxury, stay someplace else. But if you're looking for location, stay here. But don't pay over $100 a night to do so!

title: “Not the Best Best Western”
text:
We spent 6 days here visiting our daughter. During the entire visit, our toilet did not function adequately despite repeated complaints by us. While we were given the option to move rooms, it was not extended until late in a morning when we had already left the area to sight see, making returning/packing/unpacking prior to 3 pm impossible. Upon arrival the hot tub was not HOT. After inquiring about this, we were told it is on a timer and can't be changed. The hotel rooms are dated and the bathrooms are minuscule making putting your toiletries in there next to impossible!
We have spent many nights in Best Westerns, but won't stay here again.

title: “They just don't seem to care”
text:
The Blake is severely mismanaged. It's renovated many of it's rooms and is "trying" to be a nice, hip hotel, but it simply isn't b/c it seems no one in management cares.
Examples:
- The renovated rooms look nice, but they choose to buy cheap hard mattresses.
- The bathrooms look hip, but then your realize not having a shower curtain floods the floor.. Yes, the showers have a half glass door as a curtain... nothing really blocks the water. My floor was flooded after every shower.
- The receptionists made it a point to check us in late b/c "we booked through Expedia". She mentioned this 5 times making it clear we would not get good service b/c we used Expedia (ridiculous).
- They have a pool table in the hotel lobby/bar, but only offer broken pool sticks.. Seriously, every pool stick was broken. How hard is it to buy two new sticks... even one new stick.. so people can play?
I will say the location is great if you have business downtown and everyone (minus the receptionists) are very nice.

title: “Convenient location, friendly staff”
text: I stayed at the Jolly Madison Towers with my husband and 10 year old daughter March 20-24. Our room was on the 6th floor looking into the air shaft between the buildings. What we lacked in view was made up for by the lack of noise - we never heard any street noise at all. We were in a standard room with two double beds, and the room was quite adequate for our needs. I would estimate the size of the room at 14 ft. by 20 ft., with the TV atop a cabinet containing the minibar. The room also had two small chairs with a small table between them, and a fairly large desk. The closet also had a small chest of drawers for storage. The bathroom, while small, was pretty marble. Our room was always clean and there were plenty of towels, but you must ask for washcloths. We should remember that Jolly is an Italian chain, and is pretty much the Italian equivalent of a Holiday Inn. The staff was always courteous and friendly. Manny, one of the doormen, was extremely kind to our daughter and very helpful with suggestions and recommendations. Most of the guests seemed to be Italian business people, not many tourists. The rate we paid for the room included continental breakfast daily, served in restaurant on the mezzanine. It was typical European continental including breads, meats, cheeses, tomatoes, fruit and sweetrolls. Being on the corner of 38th and Madison was very convenient, 4 blocks from Grand Central, 8 blocks from Times Square, 4 blocks from the Empire State Building. All in all, our stay here was very good and we would not hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Love San Diego”
text:
Westin Gaslamp Quarter was a last minute booking and it was definitely a good choice! Only stayed for one night but it was great all arond. Service was very good from the check in to the concierge and valet was also very smooth. The location was superb and many restaurants and bars are close by. We also saw a San Diego Padres game and that was a great experience for just relaxing and taking in the city. 
The hotel is modern and rooms were great - had a nice view of the city and looked as though it was newly renovated. Parking was not cheap but for valet service it is pretty much the going rate these days. You pay for what you get and the Westin is in my opinion a quality brand and paying a bit more doesnt bother me if the experience is worth it.
All in all a smooth and positibe stay at the Westin Gaslamp Quarter in San Diego, cant wait to come back - love the city.

title: “Our best stay in NYC yet!”
text: Great service. Great perks. Friendly and helpful staff. Even the sheets were superb! The location is convenient with easy access to subway, close for a run in the park, overall great location. We will return to the Library Hotel!

title: “Really liked the hotel - but be aware of major construction next door”
text: The hotel itself was great for business or family trip. In fact, I even extended my stay after the first night (rather than move to a previously reserved hotel). The location was good with fairly easy walk to some tourist sites or to the Metro. The lobby, breakfast, and manager's reception areas were nice with very good selection at breakfast particularly. The staff members were mostly friendly, helpful, and responsive, but not hovering. The restaurant (including room service) was fine - not exceptional for the price, but adequate. The fitness room and pool looked nice. Room was clean, and as with all Embassy Suites, the in-room microwave and fridge were a nice addition. The room itself was quiet even though I know neighbors were present on both sides. However, at least for even-numbered rooms, on weekdays there is CONSIDERABLE construction noise from the building behind the hotel. This seemed to begin around 7am and was really loud later in the morning - probably depends on what they are working on at the time. The milder early noise was eliminated by some readily available earplugs and a pillow over my head, so it didn't end up disrupting my sleep. For light sleepers or those wishing to sleep in, I would strongly advise either taking earplugs, requesting a room on the "front" (odd numbered) of the building, or both.

title: “The Best Philadelphia Hotel”
text: We always stay at The Rittenhouse when staying overnight in Philly. The rooms are large and luxurious, the hospitality is second to none, the park view is beautiful, and so many places in walking distance. Stay here and you'll never stay anywhere else.

title: “nice and quiiet but not perfect”
text: My wife and I recently stayed and Wyndham Blake, and we found it to be a very decent hotel. The staff was extremely friendly (especially Showtime) but the room itself was below average. The vents in the room had lots of dust, and the bathroom shower had mold in it. The location is great and is in walking distance to Michigan Ave and that famous Garrets popcorn. If travelling by car, self park for 25.00, as opposed to valet parking for 44.00. I would probably stay here again if the shower were cleaner.

title: “Wedding splendour”
text: Spent a week at the W Hotel Union Square in New York City, for our son's wedding, although we were delayed by 2 days due to Hurricane Irene. The staff at the W are exceptional, nothing is too much trouble and the hotel itself is lovely. The beds are the best, so comfy. The only negative thing I will say is that we thought the rooms were a little dark due to the fact that we had trouble opening the curtains, which were huge. Other than that everything else is terrific, nice bar area, great breakfast in the restaurant (no dodgy buffets here) and the door ambassadors were fabulous. The gents on shift while we were there were Jose and David and did they make our stay memorable. Having such great guys on the front line really gets your vacation off to a terrific start. The location is perfect, with the subway right there in Union Square and plenty of restaurants to choose from.

title: “I highly recommend this hotel!”
text: The Affinia 50 is my first choice for NYC hotel accommodations! I have stayed there during my annual NY vacation for the past three years and have not been dissatisfied. The rooms are clean, well-appointed, and comfortable, the staff is friendly and welcoming, and the location can't be beat!! The rooms are also a good value for the price paid. I highly recommend the Affinia 50 to anyone traveling to NYC.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text: I was really impressed with the genuine hospitality of the staff. I don't like it when I am made to feel as if I am intruding or making someone's job difficult. The San Carlos staff was so accomadating I really felt like a guest and not some customer. There was discounted parking nearby, which is important for NYC. I was also very pleased with the location. We were within walking distance of Rockefeller Center, Grand Central Station, Times Square, and a number of really good restuarants. This hotel is definitely what I paid and more.

title: “Location, location, location”
text:
What a great location! We were delighted to find that the Moore Hotel was perfectly situated for our Seattle adventure. We were less than 2 blocks from the Pike Place Market, 2 blocks from the shopping mall and a few blocks from the monorail (and hence a quick ride to the Pacific Center). 
Our room was actually more like a suite. We had 2 queen beds in separate rooms along with a bathroom and a small efficiency kitchen. Our room was on the front side of the hotel along the street (3rd floor). Windows opened to the street and provided a nice breeze. We had been forewarned that the traffic noise could be loud at times so we brought earplugs with us but we did not need them.
The staff was wonderful. This is a european style hotel. No frills kind of a place but very clean and again, location, location, location.

title: “Will definately stay again!”
text:
Was extremely surprised by how awesome this hotel was!! OK fine so it is not right downtown, but it is merely 2-3 blocks from a whole bunch of restaurants, starbucks, etc.. so people who i have noticed that are complaining that it is so far from everything - try going outside and walking - there are lots of options around! INCLUDING a safeway right down the street so for people who want to bring back food to cook!
Firstly check in was quick, parking was easy (although for future, i would recommend just parking on the street, i think it is cheaper than the $15/nt the hotel charges) - we parked in the parkade because it was rainy outside, and didnt know how safe the area was.. but now we know, likelynext time we will do the street. 
Once we got to the room - we thought we were at home! OK we are used to metropolitan Vancouver urban lifestyle with 700-900sq. ft. living being the norm.. and this room must have been 600-700 sq. ft.! TV room, kitchen, bathroom, and bedroom - what else do you need! Plus with free wifi, and an AMAZING breakfast (different each morning!) - next time i am back in town i will for sure stay here. 
We booked from Hotwire, $85ish/nt.

title: “inner harbor hotel”
text: Stayed 2 nights,enjoyed both. Desk people were wonderful especially Richard. If we decide to return to area will defiantly stay there again. Thank you

title: “Thought it was a good place to stay in Seattle”
text: Great views and nice hotel, all the big hotel amenities and friendly staff too. Room was nice with spectacular view. Concierge floor is worth the extra dollars, better views/rooms and good food available, etc. Recommended...!

title: “Bad price/quality ratio.”
text:
Stayed two days in March for a corporate event. The room was OK but didn't reflect the price they charge, the halls could use a revamp as well as the carpeting on the room itself.
Be careful with the tempting water bottle they leave by the big screen LCD TV, it has a nice paper tag that says "Refreshing" and you may miss the $5 price tag written in a considerably smaller type below it.
On the other hand the front desk people were the most helpful i've ever seen, the halls and the lobby architecture is quite impressive.
The hotel is at walking distance of Gaslamp District and USS Midway. I recommend visiting the bar at the 40th just for the awesome city views that its windows give you, be warned that drinks up there can be quite expensive...

title: “Very good!”
text: We stayed about a week. The hotel is very good. The suite was roomy and comfortable. The location is very good. The staff was always helpful. The prices were quite reasonable. I would highly recommend this hotel and I will return there if the occassion arises.

title: “Fantastic hotel in Outstanding location!!”
text:
It was the 1st time to NY and the states for me and the missus and the beacon hotel was exactly what we were looking for,to keep it short there's nothing bad at all to say about it, the staff are great the rooms are well kept and very spacious we had two double beds in our standard room along with a kitchenette.
Downstairs right next-door is a brilliant restaurant/diner serving fantastic food till late, wherever you want a quick snack or a full meal we ate in there daily!
Right across the street opposite is a mini-market if you wish to take any food/drink back to the rooms.
The subway is just 2 blocks south (literally 2 mins walk) and central park is only a 10 min walk away and you have the theatres down Broadway if you fancy it, I can honestly say that we will definitely be returning to the hotel beacon in the near future as we wished we could've stayed longer. Fantastic hotel in Outstanding location,you will not be disappointed!!!!

title: “Amaizing hotel!”
text:
The hotelroom was extremely clean. Great service and the staff was very friendly.
We had nice view over Columbus park.
We Highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Not Bad”
text: Recently stayed at the Denver WEstin. Great location but the hotel looks a bit worn. Staff were uniformly pleasant and helpful.

title: “Birthday weekend from NYC & Long Island”
text: The hotel was in a perfect location...right on the beach. We had really no problems with our stay what so ever. We are returning very soon!!!

title: “Nice place. Very Touristy area.”
text:
We stayed here a few days ago. The hotel staff were pleasant and the room was nice, but overall, I prefer the Fairmont or the Vitale. The hotel could definitely use a little updating (especially the bathroom). The business center was $10 for 20 minutes of internet access. Really? $300+/night and you're charging for internet access. 
Our room was next to the elevator, so if you're a light sleeper, I would suggest requesting another room if you're assigned a room next to one. Plus the walls are very thin - I could hear kids running in the halls and crying etc. The highlight was listening to the conversation of the occupants in the room upstairs while I was shaving! I sure hope Martin and Deb had a nice flight home!
The hotel is in the heart of Union Square, so if thats where you want to be, then it's a perfect choice. Having lived in SF until last year, I can tell you that the only place more touristy is Fisherman's Wharf.
It's about a $50 cab ride from SFO or you can take BART to Powell for $8.10 each way and then walk about 3 blocks to the hotel. It's actually quicker to take BART!
Overall, it's a nice, clean hotel and if the rooms were $200/night, it may be worth staying here if you're coming to SF for the first time.
There are some great restaurants within walking distance (Canteen, Fifth Floor and a little spot for breakfast called Farm:Table).

title: “Fab hotel let down by the unwelcoming/unhelpful staff.”
text:
Fab hotel. Located in excellent position. 
Rooms of very high standard. Comfortable and well equiped, including free WIFI, i pod docking station and a coffee maker with lovely complimentary coffee. Very modern bathroom with lovely large shower. 
Wonderful amenities located on the 3rd floor, large outdoor and indoor pools, hot tubs and running track. 
However this is all a little spolit by the unfriendly and unwelcoming staff, offering little or no information on the hotel. 
At one point the fire doors on the third floor were all locked. 
Another time we found the main hotel door blocked off. No signage on how you leave the hotel or assitance was forecoming. 
For two days we had to put up with someone doing maintenace around the outdoor pool area, with a machine making a noise I could only compare with a pneumatic drill. 
The outside bar area was closed for two days as the sidewalk was being dug up.
The swimming pool towels is the hotels best kept secret . 
Staff need a lot of customer care training. It is my thoughts that they do not care about the individual guess and prefer to concentrate on large parties and groups. 
Would I use the hotel again? Doubtful.

title: “NO RETURN VISIT FOR US”
text:
Hotel was just ok .. we booked 4 rooms and asked for 1 room to be in a quiet part of the hotel as we are very light sleepers. the quiet room they gave us turned out to be the noisiest it was next to the restaurants kitchen and staff work stations, needless to say we could only sleep between 2am and 5am . Although close to the marina and restaurants there are lots of beggars on the streets. so when walking around we never felt safe at any time Other than that the staff was very friendly and helpfull this will not keep us from visiting San Fransisco again .I think i have said enough.
Cape Town 
South Africa

title: “Excellent front desk; avoid restaurant”
text:
The front desk and concierge staff were quite friendly, and were also very helpful with locating nearby restaurants.
We arrived around 10pm, and were told that the restaurant (Bistro 300) was open until midnight. That was quite a nice surprise - until we went there. We arrived at the restaurant at roughly 10:30. The service was unbelievably slow. After quite some time a waiter took our order. Fifteen minutes later, we managed to get a bus-girl to give us some water. Drinks took almost a half-hour from time-of-arrival. The sandwiches took at least 45 minutes.
Breakfast at Bistro 300 was a little better, but nothing to write home about.
The room was reasonable, but below traditional Hyatt standards. There were hairs on the counter, and a couple in the shower. The bedding was not great.
There is a coffee shop in the lobby, but it closes at noon! Also, the elevators advertise a top-floor restaurant with great views. We went up there on a Thursday night, but the place was apparently abandoned - strange.
Lastly, my partner slipped on some greasy patch by the pool, and got some nasty scrapes.

title: “Good and Dependable”
text: We travel regularly to Seattle and stay overnight at the Best Western Loyal Inn. Over the years, we have found this hotel to be the best deal if you want walkable access to the Seattle downtown and the Seattle Center. Getting to the hotel is a bit nutty because the city is messing about with the streets, but once you are there, it is nice to park and walk downtown--and much cheaper. The room is clean, the mattresses are firm, the free breakfast and wifi meets our needs, computers are available for email checks, and the staff is great. Plus, this is a no-smoking hotel. It is not fancy, but a good deal for family trips and business travel.

title: “Good But Not Great”
text:
Having stayed at Hotel ZaZa, Dallas many times I was very excited to check out the Houston location.
While the ZaZa style and vibe are here in full force it is lacking the same energy as the Dallas location. 
The service was very good, especially the Bellmen and Valet's. 
The guests in the room next to me had a raging party that went all they way into the morning. Not a huge disturbance to me noise wise, but it gave off a cheesy spring break feel.

title: “Always enjoy this hotel”
text: This is a nice out of the way place, not many rooms and each room is different, some very small, some with jacuzzi tubs, or claw tubs etc., very old hotel., nothing fancy., its in a residentual area with a grocery store next door and Yak-Zees restaurant pub across the street, starbucks, a drug store etc......... walking distance to lake Michigan and a few miles walk to down town !

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: What a great hotel, It is a new hotel (approx 2 years old), I found it to be clean and welcoming. The staff was so friendly and helpful. The rooms were large and the bed was so comfortable. My room had a sofa and a comfortable desk chair, the wireless internet and TV was really good. Breakfast was one of the best I've seen in a long time, hot items, 2 kind of waffles, cereal and too many other items to list, it was very clean and well stocked. Everyone was friendly and made me feel right at home. If you are going to Houston, I recommend that you try this hotel, you will have a good visit.

title: “Dissatisfied with service”
text: The hotel is in a great location for the price i paid. Arround $150 per night. The rooms are terribly small. There is no silverware, cofee maker, microwave or a table. I am from the west coast and this is my first visit to NY. I am not sure if this is how all manhattan hotels are. The main entrance to the hotel is horrendous as well. Would not recomend this hotel.

title: “Nice”
text: I like the location, very accessable and good locations to eat. However, I did not like the fact that it is not user friendly for handicap, wheel-chair bound guests. When we stayed there we were at the very bottom meeting room and one of the guests had to use the freight elevator. Also the dining area had stairs, how can a person who uses a wheelchair get thru there. Other than that it was great.

title: “Not recommended”
text: My company booked us a business stay at The Roosevelt earlier this month. I would not recommend it. Both the bedroom and bathrooms had not been cleaned, there was a large cigarette burn in the sheets and other stains, the tv didn't work and there was a load of mould growing around the shower and bathtub. The staff were incredibly rude, barely even speaking to us let alone being polite. They seem more interested in chatting to each other than helping at the check in desk. However the concierge that came to fix a problem with the heating in my room was very helpful. Bellboys try to procure money out of you by using threatening and abusive language, and actually count their tips in front of you as you wait in the lift! All in all it was a horrible stay and I will never go back their again.

title: “Love Palmer House, not Hilton”
text:
I love the Palmer House. It is a great old hotel. Yes the rooms are a bit small. The bathroom too. Yup a view of a brick wall. But it is grand and historic and right in the middle of everything. It has history and a vibe that you can only get from being around a long time. The lobby is exquisite. The staff are amazing. It is incredible. Well worth it. We checked in with a woman I think named Maria - and she remembered us later in the day and then again two days later. She has a four year old and we talked kids. She was really great. 
My one gripe? WiFi! It is $15 per day per device! Per device! We are a modern family and travel with: an IPad, a laptop, two IPods and a Kindle. And there are three of us. If all were able to get onto wifi, it would be $75 a day. As is, we had to lurk in the lounge to get work done, send emails and catch up on some of the entertainment that we keep up with. And the TV wasn't particularly good - three channels in Chinese and no Food Channel or HBO. So it was sort of a media blackout for us. Come on Hilton - reach the 21st century and have free wifi! It is the way of the world! 
Other than that, absolutely love the place.

title: “Decent enough hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed at this hotel last weekend for 2 nights. The room was fairly spacious by NYC standards with a large and comfortable bed and of sized bathroom. The place was very clean. The TV came with HBO on demand (free) so I watched a couple of movies at night (no, not the pornos). The location was way down at the bottom of Manhattan 4 blocks from the Staten island Ferry station. A huge plus was there were multiple subway stops within 3 blocks of the hotel which I used to go up the West side (1,2,3) and the east side (4,5,6), plus the R line (to union square and penn station). I attempted to use the J line on Saturday near Wall Street to go to the LES but it is closed on the weekends, so I took a cab instead. I had several issues with the hotel in terms of service. The key card machine was broken when I came to check in but they called security who let me into my room with minimal wait. I was hoping to check in early but no such luck. There were plenty of bags in storage with the Concierge so I assume I wasn't the only one who couldn't check in. The biggest fault I had with the hotel was the exceptionally slow elevators and so I docked the place to a 3 instead of a 4.

title: “Great location, clean hotel.”
text: We stayed for 2 nights in the renovated King Premier room facing the pool. Staff are polite, room was clean. Internet reliable. The valet brings the car to us pretty quick. If you are parking to check in with your heavy luggage, use the disabled elevator to go down to the lobby. Either that or the stairs. I saw lots of other guests with luggages who weren't sure if they could use that elevator and then lugged their luggages up or down the stairs. After checking in, we had to carry our luggages up that stairs again to go to the other elevator to our floor in the premier section. That's the only quirk in our stay.

title: “Awesome Views”
text:
Great location overlooking the ocean. We saw dolphins passing by from our balcony. We have been staying here for the last 4 years, unfortunately others have identified this great place to stay. The prices have increased and availability is getting slightly tougher to obtain rooms based on the popularity. 
Beach front location is good for those wanting to take in all that San diego has to offer.

title: “Club Quarters was terrific with one exception...”
text: I booked the best internet rate deal in the South Loop through Expedia (?) - where you can't see the where until it's paid for. My initial regret came from reading reviews that spoke of tiny rooms and little beds. With a 6'5" spouse who possesses a cranky case of hotel room claustrophobia, it sounded like a recipe for disaster. I called ahead to request a king-size bed, only to find that there are very few in the hotel and no guarantee of getting one. So I prepared my husband for spending 99% of his time outside and hoped for the best. End result? He LOVED the room because of the business-friendly set up ---- great desk, ample room to work, phone, lamp, wireless Internet ready- perfect for his work-on-the-road needs. And the shower was amazingly roomy. The hotel has a really comfortable lounge area just off the lobby with several computers w/ wireless Internet, fireplace, TV, newspapers, coffee etc. So - the exception to our instant satisfaction was a ongoing failure of the wireless Internet system (because I had work product to finish and e-mail) until the very last day. All in all, a minor challenge to overcome and the hotel is one we look forward to enjoying in the future. By the way, there are several street parking spaces in front of the hotel available for free overnight parking (7 pm - 6 am) if you're willing to get up and out early enough to avoid being towed. That was an great convenience and a big money-saver ($24 overnight parking, three blocks away).

title: “Great second stay at the Westin”
text: Stayed here two years ago. It was so good we didn't think it could happen again, but it did! Fabulous high floor corner view room with windows that open a little. Location is great. Right next to Times Square, but adjacent to residential and local businesses. A friend lives a few blocks from the hotel in what seems to be a totally different part of town. Easy walk (20 mins) to Central Park and midtown shopping and sights. The staff is very helpful and friendly, especially considering what a large hotel this is. Our son and his girlfriend had a room on a lower floor. Not the great view, but a good value and very comfortable room.

title: “Helpful and hard working staff”
text: I stayed here with my wife and son and was due to leave the day after Hurricane Sandy hit, but due to flight cancellations ended up staying until Friday 2nd Nov. The Hotel was still without power at this point and we had already arranged to move to another Hotel until our delayed flight home on 5th November. If we had known that power would be restored on the Friday night we would gladly have stayed as the room in Hotel we moved too, which was in the same price range, was nowhere near as spacious or as comfortable as at the Dumont. Also the staff at the Dumont where much friendlier, helpful and always had a smile on their faces, even during the testing times before and after the Hurricane hit. The manager and staff went out of their way to make our stay as comfortable as possible and keeping us informed of what was happening, which was difficult without power, phone lines, internet. etc. We were particularly grateful for moving us to a lower floor just in case the generator gave up the ghost. We were originally on the 37th floor with fantastic views of the East River and Downtown Manhatten, but dont think we could have coped with having to walk up to 37th floor without a lift. On the Monday afternoon (29th oct) Mr Spector and his staff opened up a room on the 3rd floor with an X Box and Table tennis table for the kids and coffee/tea for the adults (which was replaced by wine and beers later on). This was very much appreciated and kept the young ones amused and gave the adults chance to relax a bit. All the time during our stay we could not fault any of the staff, from the chambermaids, maintenance staff, doormen, concierge,front desk staff to the management, they all worked extremely hard in what must have been testing times for them all, making sure we the guests were put first. All the staff are a credit to the manager and hotel. We would not hesitate staying at this hotel on any further trips to New York.

title: “The worst of the WORST!!”
text: I would not stay here even if they pay me. The WORST hotel at which I've ever stayed. It's 10 times worse than what you can possibly imagine of a bad hotel. It's so very nasty. I couldn't stand it even with my eyes closed.

title: “Response to Email Query - Excellent”
text:
I've yet to make this trip but have been booked for July. I had a query with regard to the travel from LA to San Francisco and sent them an email and the response received was fantastic detailing all options of travel. Thanks to Jeff Zarrinnam, Hotel Director - Looking forward to my stay at this hotel and hoping for excellent service.
Letty from Western Australia

title: “Staff's attention to detail and personal touch made all the difference!”
text:
Stayed there for just one night on a saturday and it was an absolute treat. We actually live in VA at a distance of hardly 40 minutes drive but decided to stay in DC that Saturday for multiple reasons. First, wanted to get away from home to relax, reconnect and get romantic; second, one of our friends was throwing a graduation party at a club in DC, and last, I had a 5K run early on Sunday morning. :-)
We had heard a lot of good things about this hotel so we decided to try it and all I can say is WOW! Even though it is rated at 3&1/2 stars it is almost 5 star quality. The whole experience was great ... as soon as we walked in we were awestuck with the atrium area, absolutely gorgeous. The check-in staff was extremely friendly and courteous. Right at the check-in they gave us a late checkout since I mentioned that I was going to run the 5K the next morning (extremely nice of them). We got a room on the 8th floor with a street view (in retrospect we should've ask for the atrium view, next time). Rooms were quite big for DC standards (compared to the other hotels that we have stayed at in DC) and very comfortable.
The best part was that we were given a complementary bottle of champagne which I think was because I mentioned that this was a romantic outing for me and my wife. Such small details do make a particular hotel special. Most certainly this is going to be our hotel of choice in DC.

title: “Convenient location”
text:
Great location, you can walk to shopping, restaurants, easy access to public transportation, the staff was fantastic! Lobby area was good, restaurant is inventive, small bar area, convenient continental breakfast. As far as the rooms go, this place is old, and you can feel it in the rooms.
Small area, very small bath, enough room but not an updated feel. Kinda like staying at your grandmothers. Can not beat the price and location. Everywhere we went there were homeless people and beggars, kind of sad but I guess you get that with big city.

title: “There are other options at DIA. Use one of them.”
text:
This particular Hampton has lost my business. At best it is an average property. With a ton of other options literally right next door, why settle? Some nice features (plenty of delivery menus at the desk for one), some things needing attention (e.g. stained carpets). Little things they have scrimped on. A terribly meager number of television stations comes to mind. 
But here is the killer. The front desk. I arrived late in the evening. Admittedly I was tired and hungry and not in the best of moods. After standing out in the a brisk Denver February night and watching Holiday Inn, Comfort and DoubleTree vans come and go I called the desk to see where there the van was. Oh, they don’t send it till you call. Maybe my mistake, but I don’t think so. Fast forward, it was promised in 15 minutes. It came in 25. I tried calling back (3X). No answer (huh??). When it finally arrived he said the desk sent him to the wrong side of the terminal. Then, I had to wait for a while cause he had a few more arriving passengers. So, total time to hotel was nearly an hour. Totally unacceptable. The desk seemed like they could not care less. One point of redemption was the van driver. This guy was a customer service ace. I suspect he has had to deal with guests who encountered the front desk people in the past. Bottom line is this place is certainly OK, but with so many other choices, why settle?

title: “Redbury is ace”
text: We stopped here on our honeymoon in May and although we got off to a slow start (they couldn't find our reservation made months before and weren't overly helpful or friendly) the redbury was amazing! The rooms were quirky and cool and we had a brilliant view. The location was good for Hollywood but didn't get a chance to see more of LA in our short stay. The club below the hotel is totally not out scene (we are less hip more grungy!!) but the staff were polite and we couldn't hear it from our room even though we were only a few floors above it. The decor in the room and the hallways was amazing. One of the best hotels on our whole trip.

title: “Cozy hideaway in the heart of San Fran and a super great value!”
text: Our family of 2 parents and our 13-yr old stayed at this 7-story hotel for a few nights in early March 2008. A wonderful location, just steps away from everything including Union Square, theaters, the best restaurants, the trolley, and all the fun shops and stores. The hotel is early 1900's but has been renovated from top to bottom and is very charming and very clean. We were going on a driving trip, so we got our car at the airport and self-parked it a block away from the Inn during the time we were there and used the trolley everywhere. The parking lot is cheaper than the hotel's valet service by $20- they can tell you the exact location. If you use the valet service, it's about $41 or so with in and out service, but you have to wait. The rooms are very clean, our master bed was pretty good, not great (the rollaway our child slept on was lumpy and thin unfortunately). The linens were very good quality. Bathrooms small but what you'd expect for a downtown hotel. I really liked the complimentary toiletries - a rosemary and mint fragrance that is so San Francisco! The rooms are smallish for 3 but we made do without a problem - for 2 it would be perfect. The view is non-existent - looks out on another building nearby, but here's the nice part: sheers cover the window so you don't see the building and light comes in, and because it does not face the street, the room is extremely quiet and great for a good night's sleep. We opened the window, which I like more than those sealed up skyscraper hotels, and kept the ceiling fan on. We did not use the heat because we were comfortable with a cool room. There is no A/C so not sure what it would be like in the summer. If you want a bigger room that looks out on Post street below, get a suite. They have a pull-out sofa bed with queen bed and cost a little more. In the mornings, an elaborate continental breakfast is set out in the fireplace keeping room at the end of each floor's lobby. Everything from freshly boiled eggs to sourdough toast, cheeses, bagels & cream cheese, sweet rolls, fruit, fresh juices, fresh coffee and tea and more. In the evening, a lovely assortment of cheeses, crackers and wines await you after a day of sightseeing. It's all self-serve, very private and so much better quality than one would expect. The hotel reception was very friendly, although the lobby is small. We liked that about it and felt it was quaint. During our stay we needed a few things and the young men in reception took care of it promptly. We will definitely stay there again. This place is a little jewel!

title: “gym traveler”
text:
Indianapolis, Indiana Quality Inn & Suites.
4345 Southport Crossing Way
We stayed at the Quality Inn & Suites the night of February 8th 2008. We stayed there because it was one of the host hotels for the gymnastic meet being held on the 8,9 and 10 of February 2008. 
When we arrived there around 8pm we checked in and we were assigned a room, room103. The room was to be a non smoking King suite. When we entered the room the smell from old cigarette smoke could knock you over and the suite had one bed and two chairs. We complained to the front desk and the person behind the desk stated that " I forgot we took one of the beds out". 
We were then sent to a different suite, room 303. When we entered the room everything appeared to be ok. The carpet was a little dirty, but it got worst. The bath tub had two live spiders with spider webs in it. I killed the spiders, so we could use the shower. I then went to turn on the television, and it did not work. I called down to the desk and talked to a male employee and asked if the television could be fixed? He replied "he could not fix or replace the television but we could check out and stay at a different hotel." He then said "I can put you in another room" which would have been our third room. I asked to speak to a manager he replied there is not one on duty. We booked this room in November 2007, because the other hotels in the area were booked up due to the gymnastic meet. We had little choice but to stay. 
I am so glad we traveled with our own blankets an pillows because four of the six pillows in the room were to dirty to use. One of the pillows had a big orange red stain on it along with a long black hair. The other dirty pillows had black spots all over them, it looked like dried black mold. I then pulled out the sofa sleeper. There were no sheets or blankets for the mattress anywhere in the room, and the mattress was filthy. So the sleeper could not be used. Due to the filth we were afraid to use the rooms blankets and pillows so we used our own. 
At that point we called the corporate office and spoke with a very nice friendly person that went out or her way to make us feel happy. The person from the corporate office advised that the corporate office would be contacting us by February 12, 2008. Corporate has not contacted us as of the 14th. On the 14th of February we received a letter from the Indianapolis Quality Inn & Suites. The letter stated I apoligize for the problems you experienced and appreciate the comments so that immediate changes can be made. 
After our experience at this hotel I would not recomend this hotel.

title: “Classy hotel in a superb location”
text: I spent two nights at the Conrad during a recent business trip. My overall stay was excellent from check in to check out. I was able to check in early and was given a room on the same floor as the lobby, which was very convenient, yet quiet since it was well removed from the common areas. The room was not huge, but it was larger than standard hotel rooms, and well laid out and decorated, including a nice bathroom and a large flat screen TV. The room was very quiet during my entire stay. While the hotel itself is quite nice and recommended, it's location is fantastic. It's connected to a mall anchored by large Nordstrom's, and it is in the heart of the Miracle Mile, steps to State and Michigan.

title: “Not too bad”
text: Our room was small and smelled like cigarette smoke (though we had asked for a non-smoking room) but overall it was pretty clean and in good condition, except for a couple of cigarette burn marks on the comforter. The staff seemed to be indifferent and listless. We were also woken up at 7:30 am by construction workers outside of our window. But we got a great deal on the room and the location was good so overall my girlfriend and I were satisfied with this place.

title: “Great location, friendly staff and pet friendly!!”
text: My husband and I spent one night at this hotel on July 21st and had a great time. We were in town celebrating our 25th anniversary. The staff is wonderful and everyone we came in contact with had a smile on their face. We travel with our dog and were happy to find a pet friendly hotel within walking distance to downtown Charlotte. Several dining options were minutes away from the hotel. Hopefully, we will be able to visit again very soon and stay for more than one night. We had a great time thanks to the staff at the Crowne Plaza Charlotte!

title: “Disappointing”
text:
The pictures they show you on their website and the room you get are two very different things. I had a very tiny cramped room (even for NYC) and I had a lovely view of a brick wall. The bathroom was its only redeeming feature. The bed was literally wall to wall. The location was not bad but I would never stay here again. It was over $750 for the two nights. I could have found better elsewhere for equal or less money.
One last thing to point out, CHECK YOUR CREDIT CARD STATEMENT! A week or so after my stay there, two charges showed up. One was for 84 cents and the other was for $9.50. I had prepaid for my room and I did not use anything from the mini bar. I disputed this charge with my CC company did a chargeback. Shortly after the chargeback became final I received an "updated" folio from Hotel Chandler showing they had credited my account for a $9.50 bottle of large water! I never touched anything in their mini bar and I am a seasoned enough traveling to know to never drink the water!

title: “Great Staff/Shabby Rooms”
text:
Overall a good Hotel due to it's perfect location, comfortable beds and attentive staff.
However...
Bathrooms are so small that the toilet takes up all the space infront of the sink
Showers are dingy and not updated
Our room had very bad smell (although staff did there best to try to correct it)
I felt that It was overpriced considering the condition of the rooms
I found the best rate by using my Marriott Rewards number.
You may also want to check Travelzoo

title: “Thanksgiving day stay in HELL !!!”
text:
Arrived at hotel after parade, room had two towels and no toilet paper (we were dropping off our stuff after the Chicago parade. Upon leaving to go back out , I asked for add'l towels and Toilet paper, was told that it would be taken care of. 
Returned four hours late neither was done called down and was told I could pick up my toilet paper in the lobby, had to go to lobby to get toilet paper and towels .
TV in kids room didn't work maint. came about an hoour after calling and told me htere was nothing they could do.
Then the head board attached to the wall by the kids bed fell on my daughters hand, called and maint came about 8:30 p and decided to fix it, took about an hour and half. 
Service personnel were terrible and acted like idiots, would rather sleep in parkinglot across the street than sleep at this hotel again.

title: “disappointed.....”
text:
We booked this hotel thinking it would be a great locale for our needs. The street noise never ended and we only were able to sleep when I called front desk at 3:00 a.m. to have them get us another room. Rooms were adequate. Very expensive for what you receive.
No wireless..(unless pay for)....50.00 for parking your car...We definately overpaid for what was given.

title: “Not Too Bad”
text: The floor in the bathroom was sticky, the shower curtain had weird spots on it and the top of the TV looked liked someone had left a caramel apple on it and the service never cleaned it. Otherwise the roomrate for this room was higher than expected, they did not have any king beds available so I had to take a quenn at the same price.

title: “Beautiful Hotel but not so beautiful experience”
text: We checked into the Villa Florence and loved the curb appeal. It's located right in the heart of Union Square and has a beautiful lobby. It's an older hotel which color schemes that make it unique. We actually enjoyed our room and it was pretty spacious for downtown hotel. Unfortunately though, I woke up in the middle of the night covered with bites from my knees down. It was unfortunate that this happened because I had some cute shorts and dresses I wanted to wear but couldn't! If I go back to San Francisco I will definitely stay at a more "chain-like" hotel such as the Hilton.

title: “Their goal is a "10" and they delivered”
text:
Last year we stayed here twice for our trips to see the Mariners play. In my review I said I could see the potential but it had not yet "arrived"
So, now it has. From check in on I could tell that things had changed. It is now a DoubleTree property and it is easy to see that they know how to get it done! We were given a room on the Hilton Honors floor but it looked much the same as the other rooms we have had there, all very well appointed and stocked with STARBUCK'S....yeah! We dined downstairs at JUNO's and surprise, surprise!!!...the prices had gone down yet the food was fabulous as usual. Our waiter was wearing a button "10". I asked what it meant and she told me that their goal was nothing less than 10 in service and quality. She was great...giving our friends directions and taking time to show them on a map. Later she saw us upstairs in the lobby lounge and stopped to joke with us about finding our way to the bar with no difficulty.
The beds are just the best. I slept so soundly and because of the blackout drapes we slept in later than we thought we would. Again....STARBUCK's in a french press....does it get any better?
The breakfast options in the neighborhood are plentiful but we decided to go back to Juno. The waiter was quite a character and we enjoyed the entertainment with our breakfast. My smoked salmon benedict was to die for and the chef made us a smoked salmon and shrimp omelette that was the best ever. He delivered it personally then checked back to see if we liked it.
We returned to The Arctic club this year because it is a close walk to the stadium. We were delighted that they have it down now and they certainly delivered the "10" they were striving for.
By the way....Mariners won in the 11th inning.

title: “Great location, Friendly Staff and a Decent Value”
text:
We recently stayed three nights at the St. Gregory Hotel & Suites. The property is in a great location within a ten minute walk from three different Metro stations. The staff was very friendly and quick to assist when needed. The room was one of the cleanest and well maintained rooms I have stayed in. I have seen complaints on some reviews that the hotel was dated and run down. This is far from the truth. The only thing that seemed old in this hotel was the TV, but we don't travel to watch TV. It worked, so who cares! If you stay through a weekend, parking is $29 all together, not per night which is a big plus considering some of the other rates I've seen. 
Something to be aware of is noise spilling over from the neighboring room. We were next to the Presidential Suite, and if people were in there talking next to the doors that connected the rooms, it sounded like they were in the room. This may or may not be an issue depending on what time everyone settles in. But if you're next to someone who gets in late, it could be. Otherwise, it was quiet. We would stay again.

title: “Good”
text: Rooms were great. But we all had problems with the keys not working and had issues with the air conditioner

title: “Excellent location, rooms lack style”
text: 1 block from two major subway lines, red and yellow. Close for transit lines, Penn station and all the buses. On a quieter side street. Windows open. Room decor was fine. Boring. 17$ onsite breakfast. Though plenty of places to eat breakfast at so shouldn't be eating at hotel. Lots of hotels on the side streets, two others were here. So plenty of options. Comfy bed, can adjust firmness of mattress. And mix of feather and non pillows. the front street views weren't bad, even on the 6th floor

title: “Great Service with”
text: I just returned from a 5 night stay at the Clift. I had my reservations of staying at The Clift after reading some negative feedback on this site. After the first night I knew I was staying in a hotel that values their customers.I would not recommend this hotel for families. On the weekend it is very similar to staying at a night club. The long lines outside to get into the Redwood Room identifies the popularity of this night club. Yet you would never know there is a night club below you with very well insulated room.The room was clean and very posh. The beds have silky sheets and very romantic lighting. This is an older hotel but everything is nicely updated.The staff is very friendly and approachable. Anywhere you see a staff member they always smile and say hello. I would highly recommend consulting with the Concierge to help with transportation and advice on restaurants.I highly recommend Clift for couples wanting a romantic stay in San Francisco. I would also recommend room service. Expensive but great food.

title: “Could be great but is not”
text:
We stayed 3 nights at this hotel last week, and will give it a very average review. First, if you end up with someone above you, you will hear them walk. I am guessing there is a wood (not slab) structure between floors, so can be noisy. This also mean your downstairs neighbours will hear you...
Rooms are good and clean. Bathrooms small. Tub small. Beds are great. You have to like marine themed hotels. Wireless internet is a total rip off and we did not use. 
Valet parking is expensive, but valets are courteous and prices are clear when you check in. The parking ramp across the street is 30 a day but without in or out privileges.
We did not eat at the hotel except for one comp breakfast. Very good but for 25 bucks a piece, just go to starbucks on bay (2 blocks). There also is a traders joe on mason and bay (1 block) which has a much more affordable selection of wine than this hotel. No fridge in rooms.
Overall, for 130 a night, it is a decent choice for the proximity of the attractions but really, this is subpar due to the paper thin floors......
The staff at front desk and valet was great. Some of the other staff was not.

title: “A hostel is better than this place!!”
text:
Carpets Dirty with a layer of dust
Bathrooms old and moldy
A/c : a truly antique, never seen anything like that!!
smells old and dusty.
The location is great, but I prefer to take the metro and stay out if can not afford DC prices.
Cut my stay short because of the hotels condition

title: “I think I can find a better place with this price”
text: The room was too small even for a single person. The only space you can have in the room is setting on the bed. The blanket was dirty and I could find some human's hairs on it. There is no way you can adjust the air-conditioning. The hotel staff was polite and helpful, but one thing made me feel uncomfortable was: The housekeeper complained I made the bed sheet very dirty. I think it was so ridiculous saying that in front of the customer. As I was just overnight alone for one day and out for most of the day, I think the bed sheet was probably dirty before I checked in and I didn't notice. By the way, I think you hardly can find a cheaper hotel in downtown, but you definitely can find a nice hotel like Travelodge with this price or less near the airport area. The transit is excellent as well. The bus stop is just in front of the hotel.

title: “Paradise Point the good and the bad”
text: My family stayed at the Paradise Point on October 4th, 5th and checked out on the 6th. (Family of 5 Dad, Mom, Kids 15, 11 and 6) Upon arriving the grounds look great - you feel like you are arriving at a resort in Hawaii. The Lobby is very attractive. We had booked a Lanai Garden Room, but upon arrival my husband decided to upgrade to a bayside suite. The checkin attendant was quick and friendly. The Bellman that drove us to our room by golf cart was very friendly. Upon arriving my husband told me that the room was not as nice as he expected, but not terrible. The kids slept out in the living room on the pull out couch. We had a king size bed in a separate bedroom. A single bathroom is shared by all. The toiled is in with the shower so one person at a time had the whole bathroom. The room definitely showed it's age. The Bay outside was ok, but there were signs about the water not being safe after a rain (runoff). We did not feel that the bay water was swimmable and was cold. The room had a kitchenette, but no utensils, etc... That night we were cold (being from Phoenix) and turned on the heater. Our room filled with smoke and the fire alarm went off. No one called or noticed from the front desk. We fanned the room out till the alarm stopped. It was late and we did not want to change rooms so we went to bed with the smell of smoke in the room. The next morning we called the front desk. They did not seem to care about it - said they would send a repairman while we were at Seaworld. No apology, etc... We decided to see how the repair went. Seaworld was great. Our daughter got splashed by Shamu so when we got back to the room she layed her wet sweatshirt out on our deck chair. The sweatshirt was from Paris and had sentimental value for her. Well in the morning it was gone. She was crying and called the front desk to see if anyone had turned it in. They did not seem interested - did not act like they cared - and did not have it. I know it should not have been left outside, but they could have been like - oh no! We will definitelykeep our eyes open and watch for it (ie at least feign fake concern). The heater did work the second night so we did not pursue that issue. The last morning we called to see if we could get a late check out (a Weds in the middle of October) and they said no. There hotel book says to ask about late check out, but I guess they were busy?! We did check out then go to the pool for awhile. The pool is very nice. In summary the good points are the beautiful grounds, great pool - nice and heated, the barefoot cafe - where the staff was actually very nice! The bad points are substandard accomodations for the price, mostly uncaring staff. I would only stay here at a discounted rate - definitely not for full price!

title: “Elegant Decor”
text:
I have been staying at the Waldorf for over 50 years and have always considered it "home" in NYC. However, my wife and I have never stayed in The Waldorf Towers and decided that staying there would be nice upon our return from Europe on the QM2 in July 2010. I had arranged through the concierge for a car to meet us at the ship and had requested an early check-in. We had a little difficulty locating the car at the pier because the driver was late and did not hold up a sign with our name but this was really not a big problem and we had a nice ride to the hotel. The Reception clerk seemed very nice and said they had a wonderful upgraded suite for us but it was not ready and we could wait in the Astoria Lounge which we did - waited and waited and waited. I finally went back down to the lobby to enquire about the room. Surprise! It was ready! It was also completely unsatisfactory - far smaller and in poorer repair than any accommodation we have ever had at the Waldorf. Another surprise - another much nicer suite was suddenly available which we took - Suite 38R2. The decor was elegant and the suite very comfortable but many little annoyances such as the TV not working, a plumbing problem, and the third day sandblasting the building immediately outside our windows! We could not hear a word anyone said in person or on the phone because of the incredibly loud sandblasting noise. I could not believe that at a hotel of this service-oriented calibre we had not been advised of this scheduled sandblasting prior to check-in! The Towers operations manager did come to our suite to apologize which was appreciated (also necessary because we could not hear each other on the phone) and did comp us for two of our five nights.
In summary, the Waldorf Towers is lovely and could have been a great experience. We will probably return some day but not with the enthusiasm we had originally had this time.

title: “Decent Hotel - But DoubleTree wins on Breakfast and space”
text: Stayed at the Hilton Times sq for a night because the DoubleTree Times Sq was sold-out. The Hilton is much more of a business hotel and the rooms were recently re-done. Had we not just stayed at the DoubleTree - it would have been a fantastic experience... but... the Hilton times square doesnt compare on breakfast and the beds were not as good. If given the choice - go with the DoubleTree

title: “Excellent Business Hotel”
text: I stayed at this Hotel as part of a very large conference. The rooms were very large and elegantly appointed. The food was good (for the US) and excellent value. The Reception and concierge staff could not have been more helpful.

title: “absolute nightmare! NOT worth the money saved!”
text: I am usually not very picky about hotels, which is why I originally chose the Sun Bright (mainly for its low cost in such an expensive city). I have stayed in hostels all over Central America and Asia and Europe. This, in comparison, has got to be the worst I have ever stayed in. The sheets were dirty and stained when I got to my room. The showers were infested with roaches. The dorm is literally a chicken coup, with chicken wire separating room from room. A word from experience, pay a little more and get a better hotel. This is not a place to take children or family.

title: “Very classy, very elegant”
text:
This is an upmarket classy stylish hotel in San Francisco on Geary Street (a short walk away from Union Square). Owned or at least managed by the same people that own the St Martins Lane Hotel in London and it has the same feel about it (i thought it immediately reminded me of St Martins Lane when I walked in without knowing the ownership).
It is very chic and cool and stylish in layout and decor. The rooms are a decent size considering they have king size beds in them. The shower was fantastic. Mini bar was available if you wanted to use it.
Only downside was that there was no free wi-fi as standard and you had to pay US$14.95 to use for 24 hours. 
The hotel will valet park your car for US$50 (which includes the parking fee and the taking and delivery of your car) which is the going rate for hotels in the area. 
The bar looked pretty swish and chic but I didn't use it nor did I try the restaurant. 
A very enjoyable experience!

title: “Never again”
text: Booked our room through Hotwire and got a good deal. It said the hotel was a 3 and a half star but definitely felt like I was staying in a two star. I asked for a room with a king bed but the front desk guy said there were none available even though the lot was half empty. Didnt feel like arguing so then he gave us a room on the second floor. The room was so small, I felt claustrophobic right when i walked it. Also felt like i walked into a western movie but i guess all the rooms were western themed so there was nothing i could do about that. Then when I opened the window I saw NOTHING but cement! I called the front desk and asked for a bigger room anything was better than this! He asked if I had booked through Hotwire or the hotel. Why does it matter?! I shouldn't get a crappy room just because I got a good deal. Then the next room we were put in was on the 5th floor with a somewhat view onto Greenville ave. overall the whole room is a 2. The bed was okay. Bathroom was decent. But the floors were stained and I found a baby bottle under the bed. They should probably clean the rooms a little better. Anyways I don't plan on staying again.

title: “Fabulous hotel, great staff, great location, highly recommend!”
text: This hotel was brilliant, only a few minutes walk from Times Square the location couldn't have been better. The hotel itself was fabulous, with lovely modern rooms of ample size, friendly helpful staff and the facilities were great especially the free wi-fi this saved us a fortune on communicating home. During my stay I needed to go to A&E and the hotel were so helpful both on the night in question and also afterwards when I had to send faxes & emails etc. to deal with my travel insurance company. I have been to NY several times and this was my first time at this hotel but for the future I will never want to stay anywhere else!

title: “Great location”
text: Nice hotel. Very conveniently located. Huge room and bed, although the mattress was very soft. Excellent value for money. Starbucks in the lobby was great!

title: “Fantastic Stay”
text: Tremendous hotel experience. Was there for a single night of business and needed a room, as well as 2-day conference room. They set our team up great. Attentive to details. Awesome rooms (was in a suite). Great dinner recommendations. The car service works fantastically. In a great spot. The gym is a little small -- I'd suggest getting some better cardio stuff (how about a non-recumbent) bike? I'd like to call out "Trevor" from the front desk/concierge staff as AWESOME. He made life very easy for us. I wouldn't stay anywhere else. Ate three meals at the Monarch and the food was excellent, fresh and varied.

title: “Great find in Harlem”
text: This hotel is a great value for NYC. I spent 2 nights here recently and it was comfortable, convenient and safe. The subway, shopping and restaurants are a short walk away. Freindly and helpful at the front desk. I will definitely return.

title: “Great Package and Location”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Mark Hopkins for two nights taking advantage of the "San Francisco City Tour" package which included parking (usually $45/day), a three day cable car pass ($10/person per day) and the full buffet breakfast at the Top of the Mark. The buffet was outstanding and featured American choices, European fare and even dim sum. We really enjoyed it. Our room was lovely, clean, quiet and comfortable. We requested a high floor and were given a room on the 12th. We were away from the elevators and did not hear any noise during the night. Our car was quickly retrieved any time we needed it, and we took advantage of the cable cars right outside the hotel. There is even a small grocery a block away we used to purchase our own wine. The hotel is older, however very classy.

title: “Best Place to Stay in New York City!!”
text:
As a native New Yorker, I can pretty much pick out a winner amongst restaurants and hotels...and I have never experienced hospitality as I did at the City Club.
My husband and I decided to stay at a hotel for a relative's wedding, just to get away from home and join the rest of the wedding party at the City Club. I'm SO glad we stayed here.
The City Club is unlike any other hotel in New York - the staff is genuinely friendly, SUPER accomodating, and very gracious. 
The front desk treated us like royalty, and the manager (Hugo) was spectacular. He made us feel like family and treated us with such courtesy and consideration.
Not to mention the location! Right in the heart of Midtown, we were able to hang out a few blocks away at Rockefeller Center & Times Square! 
I've stayed at other 5-star hotels, but The City Club really went above and beyond. It was clean, the decor was gorgeous, and the shower in the bathroom was amazing!! 
Best stay I've had in a very long time!
Thank you City Club Staff!!
I will continue to recommend you to all my friends & family!
Becca M.
Brooklyn, NY

title: “dissappointment”
text: we stayed for five days. there was never ice on any floor. We didn't rent a car and the only transport service was a cab. or walk the lengh of the Island to get to food. The hotel shuttle went to the airport and wildlife park. The wild life park got us there by 11 and picked us up by 4. that wasn't enough time to see anything for the price of the enterance fee. ON our last day we learned that there was an island bus that stopped by am and pm. Lot of good that did us then. Room service took over an hour for a pot of coffee. In the end I could have stayed in town walked to starbucks. The room was fine but it was just like a quality inn room only add on was you got to look at the yachets. But I bet every room there had view since it was an island.

title: “Nice warm and welcoming hotel in NY”
text:
Stayed at the Aloft Harlem from April 23rd to 27th, and the rate was 249 USD (busy week in NY - all hotels where fully booked). 
The hotel lobby has a vibrant, yet cozy feel to it. The furnishing is modern with an internet cafe for printing, a nice piano and a snack area.
