There is nice music playing in the evenings and friends hanging out in the bar that opens out to the lobby which encourages even lone travelers to hang out in the lobby. The staff are nice and very helpful - everyone was so willing to help! Located very closely to the 125th Street train station and the precinct. The staff willingly gave directions and a map to facilitate navigating the city subway.
Internet was free with good connectivity.
The rooms are nicely done and soundproof - I had to stay in two different rooms during my stay, and one was right by the main street, yet, i didn't hear any noise.
Was a bit nervous walking too far away from the hotel, as there were groups of young men that seemed to be loitering around at street corners. We never experienced any incident or what may have seemed to be one. Turned out great!

title: “Simply amazing!”
text: Best value for money in Phoenix area. We were so impressed with this hotel, we would absolutely love to go back. Rooms are huge, elegant and impeccably clean. Staff are kind, helpful and most courteous. Breakfast in the hotel restaurant was delicious. Don't even consider another property; just stay here and see for yourself!

title: “WOW waht a great lcoation and value”
text:
Recently I had the pleasure to book nights at the South Loop Hotel in Chicago, Illinois
Upon arrival the agent Leo and care staff Patrick were personable, stellar and helpfull.
The hotel has great open parking and accessibility. The rooms are spacious and basic, what you need for sleeping. I would without question stay here again. It is just a few blocks south of McCormick place and easy, brand new and a value. 
Greg Pierceall Landscape Architect and Professor

title: “The staff top the many positives about this facility”
text: We stayed for one night on our way from Madera Canyon Az. to San Antonio and then for 2 nights on our way from San Antonio to Santa Fe. We selected this motel because of it's proximity to the freeway and indeed, access was quite easy. While not impressed with the general layout (kind of reminded me of a maze) the rooms themselves were very clean and quite adequate , the beds were quite comfortable and at no time did we feel insecure (we never leave valuables in the car). Freeway noise was not a problem (the dog barking next door could have been but was not) and we had no problem keeping the drapes closed. As mentioned in other reviews, we found a problem with the shower taps but this was quickly resolved. Access to a bar was greatly appreciated after a long drive and there are some great restaurants on the other side of the freeway (Barrigas on Sunland Park Drive is one). I have to agree with other reviewers that having internet access in the bar area is rather distracting. We did appreciate the Managers Happy Hour Thursday evening. The staff, from Liz on were fantastic. The only negative comment I can make is about the grounds. Someone needs to walk around once in a while and make sure that the odd bits of garbage are picked up.

title: “First time great, Second time, not worth the price.”
text:
My first stay at this hotel was in December 2011. When I entered the hotel I was amazed by the lobby. Very impressive. I was greeted at the Hilton Honors desk by an extremely nice person who welcomed me as a member, offered me free internet and a free upgrade to a higher floor. I was surprised by the size of the room, small, but the bath was lovely. Enjoyed my stay and vowed to return.
November 2012. This time, my family joined me and I was excited to show them this hotel. It was a special visit, as it was a birthday celebration, and we were attending a show in the area that evening. Upon our arrival, around 1:00pm, we were told our room wasn't ready, but the registration person took our phone number and promised to call when it was available. No problem, went to Art Institute around the corner. At around 5pm, we just went back, having never received a call.
We had booked a room on the executive floor as this was a special day/evening. Upon seeing our room, my family was happy that we had booked this "large" room, as anything smaller would not have been good for 3 people. It was a standard room at any other hotel. The room was located between the cleaning staffs supply closet and what must have been the common wall to the elevator's machine workings. Bothersome at night, but especially irritating starting at around 6am.
On the executive floor, a continental breakfast is served, that is if you can find a seat. It was completely crazy with people roaming with plates of food, some taking it back to their rooms. If you did find a table, you may have had to clean it. Internet service was available for 12 dollars, but don't bother. It worked for about 10 minutes in the evening and than 10 minutes in the morning.
Generally, I had a better time in my little room last year than on the executive floor this year. The beds, pillows and bath accessories are very nice and pretty much the same on the executive floor as in the smaller rooms. The concierge was very helpful and the bellman nice. Another plus, the Chicago Art Institute is only a block away, State St. is just outside the hotel's door and the lobby of the Palmer House is impressive, but you can visit without being a guest.
I only get to visit Chicago once a year, and if I do get another chance, I will consider a different hotel. For the price, there are better deals in the area.

title: “great vacation”
text: all of bad reviews about the hotel i can say that they were all wrong.... the hotel was great...... room was great, no noise at all, all attractions were in walking distance of cable car distance..... definately will say there again

title: “Great hotel tucked away on 55th St... Great value!”
text:
Having been a NYC resident for over 10 years, I am picky when it comes to finding the right place to stay on my visits, now that I don't live there any longer. The Blakely turned out to be a pleasant surprise. It was truly a home away from home! My previous stays in places like the Ritz on CPS was nice, but a little too touristy for me. I thought I found a place to go back to when I stayed at the Shoreham, but the Blakely beats it by far. The rooms are nice and spacious, even with 2 huge suitcases sprawled on the corner. The beds are comfortable, bathroom feels brand new, and the kitchenette really helps for week-long stays. The hotel accomodated my request for a room facing 55th St on as high floor as possible. While the 7th floor room they got me didn't clear the theater right in front, it was bright enough during the day. If you're looking for an in-between of the grand, world-wide chain hotels and the stylish but cramped, tiny rooms of new designer hotels, the Blakely is your solution. While I checked out of this hotel completely content, there are some negative points I should point out for your references. (1) The staff seems to be inexperienced, in general. Especially the bell boys. (2) I'm surprised no one has commented on the elevators... They forgot to renovate the SLOW, OLD elevators. I don't know how many times I had to wait forever downstairs to catch one. (3) The space under the door to the rooms is quite big... You can see if the lights are on inside the room from the hallway... also hear people talking in the hallway. (4) The lobby was completely unattended a lot of the times... even late at night. It made me wonder about security. (5) There was one male staff (most likely a bus boy from the restaurant), who made me feel extremely uncomfortable while stuck in the elevator with him. Not something you'd expect from a hotel staff... maybe out on the streets of NY!
.... Overrall, a place to go back to!!

title: “just nice!”
text: very clean and stylish rooms. free wifi and free coffee/tea/muffins in the morning. pc at lobby is also available for free. perfect location at times square, market, subway and bus station in the near. friendly hotel stuff and service.

title: “A wonderful hotel and phenomenal location!”
text: Just a lovely hotel - beautiful rooms, outstanding location in relation to Pike Market and the waterfront, and a gracious and responsive staff. Outstaning hotel!

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Stephen F Austin for the event of my daughter's wedding.
I cannot begin to cover how wonderful the experience was on so many levels - from Liz Young who took care of the room arrangements - to Elicia Maroda who as concierge was wonderfully helpful not just to me , but to many of our guests who traveled far distances to come to Austin - many for the first time.
Any good hotel knows the concierge must be excellent - She was!
 HOPE BUDNER BROWN

title: “Tired...”
text:
The location of this hotel is "off the highway" which after driving two hours from Anaheim, made me a little nervous. But on the plus side of its location, it is very close (10 mins. or less) to Historic San Diego (not the Gaslamp Dist.) and of course highway access is a breeze. It is set pretty far back from road and noise or activity level were never an issue. 
Okay - we were put in a Handicap room (seemingly because we arrived in the late afternoon). The room seemed to be smaller than other Res. Inns. The interior is dated and a little worn. The shower is NOT one of those wall-less handicap showers that lets water go everywhere though. There is no closed closet - no bigg-y. And the volume on the dated TV's is picky. 
The breakfast is a free-for-all. It was so busy but they have a sign that indicates that they restock btwn. 9:15 - 9:30. And they do. It has what you would expect - powder eggs, fruit, oatmeal, breads, drinks, etc. 
We paid more for this hotel for two nights that we did for four nights at a Marriott Suites in Anaheim. (We got a screamin' deal there). Admittedly we were not there for its ammenities and again the location (convenience wise) couldn't be beat. But it's too bad they can't put a little money towards making it a slightly nicer retreat for travel, park weary families.

title: “Weekend in Boston!”
text:
Meeting up with a group of friends and families to take in a red sox game and do some sight seeing. Hotel was recomended by a friend. It was exacly what we we were looking for. GREAT location -- We walked to ballpark, and all the shopping the wifes could handle, Great Value- This is not a super fancy 5star but it delivers what we needed. CLEAN, Big Rooms, Reasonable rates. We had 5 rooms in total and everyone was pleased. We almost booked down the street for $150 more per room,,,would have been a big mistake. Staff was great as well and helped with recomendations and directions. 
Free parking with Sox ticket...
Two people in our party have already rebooked a July trip to stay again

title: “Lovely location with adequate room for short stay”
text:
won hotel through priceline for $100 a night. fabulous location for sea world. beautiful stunning 'island'. Resort grounds are lovely, although not clearly signposted.
Gift shop adequate as is the barefoot bar and grill, although service lousy.
Reception and porter staff are great, Ring 0 for a courtesy buggy to collect you from your room,
The cove/beach is pretty too. Lovely resort for couples or families. Very quiet and i wouldnt wanna stay there on my own.
i agree with a previous review - it is like butlins on a paradise resort. shalet bungalows and little lanes.
nice and relaxing... i would recommend it for a week or less

title: “Good for long stay or need for extra room.”
text:
The hotel was okay overall; the front desk staff was friendly and helpful. I felt safe in the neighborhood. The location was a little odd, but was not that inconvenient. It was about 7 miles from downtown. The hotel is fenced, with raising gates in front (which were always raised when we came thru). Initially pulling into the hotel, we saw Memphis police drive thru the parking lot (I allowed myself to think it was just as a security measure and should make me feel more safe).
The hotel does have internet connection thru an Ethernet cable (which is in a plastic Ziploc baggie hanging in the closet). The only wireless is in the lobby. I confirmed with the front desk and there was no fee for the internet. 
I shared this room with 4 other family members. It was perfect for us b/c this was more of a family reunion of the sorts and spent a lot of time just talking. So having the living area will was beneficial to us. The two beds were in a separate room from the living area, which had a couch (makes into a bed), chair, table and chairs, sink, microwave, tv and frig. It was nice to have the seating for us to all set and talk. A lot more enjoyable than all of us cramming into a normal hotel room with only beds to set on. There were also 2 flat panel tvs, one in each room. I had a few minor issues with the room, which I should have mentioned to staff but didn’t. The plastic toilet handle was chipped and broken, the shower curtain eyelet had ripped and there was a nasty yellow stain on the living room chair. My husband went down to get extra towels and was told would have to wait for them to be brought to the room. I had to call 20 minutes later to see where the towels were. A little frustrating but nothing to ruin my stay.
I didn’t use the exercise facilities, but did walk by it and it looked nice. There is not a pool. This looks more of a hotel for business. 
We did eat breakfast at the Medallion restaurant. Unless you don’t want to leave the hotel, I would suggest eating somewhere else. We ordered off the menu on day 1, presentation was nice but the food just wasn’t that good. Day 2 we ate the buffet. It was $8.95 and the food on the buffet probably would not pass a state inspection if someone was to drop by. Food was room temperature at best. We really shouldn’t have paid for this meal. It was the worst breakfast I’ve ever had. I didn’t think the staff was very nice in here either. They definitely move at their own pace doing other things and you literally have to ask for service. 
I would stay here again if I needed the living area space again. But if I was just needing a place to sleep, I would not pay the extra price for this hotel. I don’t intend to stray people away from staying here, b/c I would stay again, but my hope is maybe my issues will be fixed and improved upon.

title: “Great hotel”
text: I was a little apprehensive having read many of the reviews about the Hudson Hotel but could not fault the Hudson. Yes the rooms are small and the bathroom even smaller, but the room was clean and after all I was only there to sleep so personally the size of the room was not an issue. Great location for shopping, central park etc. staff very helpful, and great breakfast at Route 66' just a few blocks away. Good price compared to other hotels near by. I hope to return again in the future.

title: “Great Place in the Heart of San Diego”
text: I wasn't sure about booking here because of some of the reviews, but I am SO glad I did. We went to a concert at Symphony Hall and it was SO amazing to park the car, walk to dinner, and never leave the building to go back to our room. It was clean, quiet, and great service. Like many hotels, they charged $23 a night to park the car, room service tacked on several charges including a 20% gratuity. Restaurant was great for breakfast, but be sure and ask for an Omlette if the made to order isn't offered. Our waiter didn't tell us, and we already had food before we heard another waitress offering omlettes. Join their Starwood Preferred Guest program and you get to stay on the 25th or 26th Floor. BIG rooms, nice living rooms, tub PLUS shower. Good times!

title: “Will come back!”
text:
Fantastic Hotel!
I read other reviews and was a little concerned about booking, but once I arrived I saw that this was a fantastic hotel! Clean, large with amazing views of the city. This location is perfect for any type of trip to NYC! Staff is friendly and extremely accommodating! I was even able to check in several hours early.

title: “Great Location”
text:
Me and my husband stayed at the hotel a week ago and were very pleased. One word describes the hotel....location, location, location. You can’tget any better than this….you get a new trendy hotel right at the beginning of the Gaslamp District!!! We had a car, but chose not to use it unless we were going out of the area. It was not baseball season but when it is I imagine that place is packed to the brim. There is an entrance from the lobby right into Petco Park, not to mention you can see half the field from certain windows in the hotel. If you have some $$$ stay their and catch a game (I imagine during the season the rates go up quite a bit).
A few things that we were particularly happy with were the QUICK check-in and out....we even were able to check in 4 hours before check-in time, wireless internet, the pool, and last but CERTAINLY not LEAST....the bell staff and doorman. EVERYONE of these individuals was SO nice. I especially fell in love with the doorman, he was so helpful.
A few things that we weren't happy with was the room service...we tried a few different things and NOTHING was good, the jacuzzi was broken throughout our entire 5 night stay...we were VERY bummed about that....and the bar was VERY small....which I suppose is normal for a hotel bar:)
Overall the hotel was a great place. The service was FANTASTIC, never came across a person that wasn't genuinely helpful, everyone went out of their way to accommodate ALL needs. It is a bit pricey and I wouldn’t mind trying a few other places I saw in San Diego but this will definitely be a place I suggest to others.

title: “Intimacy in New York”
text: Beginning with a perfect arrival with a smiling doorman followed by a friendly greeting at the front desk, our five-day stay at the Affinia Dumont didn't disappoint. The intimate lobby ensured contact with staff, whether simply a greeting or a questioned asked, but the interaction wasn't intrusive nor faked. The large guestroom was a bonus. Cleanliness throughout the hotel was impressive.

title: “Trying to get their act together”
text:
I've stayed at this property numerous times over the past few years due to its convenient access to IAH. Each time I stay there...I want it to be better. On this trip, I had two separate one-night stays, one evening apart. Both times, I was on the Club Level floor, but the two different rooms in which I stayed were miles apart in comfort. The first room, 1017, had an old, clunky air conditioning system that really didn't work, and a toilet that worked too well (it was in a state of continual flushing). Since I arrived late and left early, I didn't bring these to the attention of the management until check-out--I hope they've taken measures to correct these flaws. The second room, 1044, was quite nice and everything worked. On my previous visits, the Club Lounge was not open on weekends--it is now. The food is plentiful and good and "discounted" wine and cocktails are available, although still overpriced. (Just go across the street to a liquor store if you want wine--it'll save you $$$.) Too, the service from the Club Lounge attendants was excellent. My one recommendation would be to switch TV stations from Fox News to something less inflammatory. I don't need biased commentators screeching at me at 7:00 a.m. The Today Show, perhaps??? 
Overall, I will stay at this Sheraton again as the staff is friendly and helpful--it's not their fault that the upkeep of some of the sleeping rooms isn't great and that food (at Basil's) and drinks are over-the-top in cost.

title: “wrong type of room, hotel refused to resolve the issue, and I did not get what I paid for”
text: My girlfriend and I booked an executive suite through Sniqueaway. The room description on Sniqueaway's website indicated that an executive suite would be from 700-750 square feet. The room we received, #1909, while beautiful, was only 12.5 feet by 35 feet. In other words, less than 450 square feet. I expect to receive what I pay for, and if I pay for a 700-750 square foot suite, it is reasonable to expect to receive such. The Adolphus own website even indicates that a deluxe room would be approximately 500 square feet in it's room description, and the executive suite is an upgrade over that! I contacted the front desk and spoke to a front desk manager named Chris who insisted that I was booked in an executive suite and would not resolve the issue. Chris claimed to not be aware of the general size of an executive suite, and would not send someone to investigate the size of the room, nor did he appear willing to do anything to resolve this issue. Chris acknowledged that deluxe rooms are up to 500 square feet, and that executive suites are an upgrade but the upgrade is based on appointments, not size. Chris was the hotel manager on duty last night, and was therefore the primary decision maker for customer service at the hotel. Unfortunately, he did not appear to be inclined to utilize any customer service skills to resolve this issue. This is not the first time I have stayed in a luxury hotel, more than likely it will not be the last. My girlfriend and I have been repeat patrons at other hotels that we enjoy, and we always spend a large amount of money on incidentals. Despite the flap with the room, we proceeded to spend a large amount of money on room service, dinner, the bar, the honor bar, and the valet parking. The hotel received a large amount of money from us through incidentals, but this did not seem to matter to Chris at the front desk. Unfortunately at this time, I do not believe that I will be inclined to return to the Adolphus.

title: “Incredible trip from the time the cab stopped, til we checked out.”
text: We had such a wonderful time here on our Anniversary trip. We arrived extremely early - and while we couldnt check in right away, they called me on my cell before noon to allow us to check in. The service was so wonderful - it was always like "Welcome Back". The rooms were great, spacious with amazing shower heads. It was very clean for us. The concierge made us reservations at a great steak house - after being sent away by Ditka's (that's a different review) . All of the staff was courteous and prompt. Our iron did not work originally, so we called for a new one which they brought up quickly. They made our trip to Chicago amazing - and one we won't soon forget.

title: “Highly disappointed in this hotel”
text:
During my last trip in New York, I reserved a Grand Luxe room at the Peninsula.
I wanted to test the only NYC 5 stars hotel I never knew
I must admit I was quite disappointed in this hotel for many reasons :
- The lobby was very small and didn't invite guests to stay in there
- My room was big but the furnishing was old fashioned
- The global decoration of this hotel is old fashioned in every place and really needs to be renovated
Service was perfect but the global impression is that Peninsula is an old institution that has not adapted its environment to customers expectations in the 21st century.
Given the astronomic room rates, Peninsula is definitely not a good value for money.
When signing the check out invoice, my wife and me had the impression we had been crooked...
Next time I travel to NYC, I'll have little choice but to stay at the Four Seasons which is with no doubt the best hotel in New York...

title: “SF Trip”
text: I recently traveled to SF for business. The cons for this hotel would be the noise. The noise from the street is so loud that it was hard to sleep and I am usually a pretty sound sleeper. The hotel itself is nice and located in the financial district of SF so it is close to a lot of businesses. On Saturday there is a great farmer's market right outside the hotel's doors which make it great. The hotel is not inexpensive and I am sure there are less expensive options out there, but Hyatt is a good name with a good reputation so it's usually the safer choice.

title: “Exceptional property”
text:
The Amalfi Chicago is an exciting property in a perfect location. The attention to detail with design makes this a very unique luxury boutique hotel. Rooms are well appointed with additional amenities. The continental breakfast served on each floor by the elevators is a brilliant twist on the typical continental breakfast. The most exciting was of course the Ravello Lounge. This was a great place to meet with co-workers before our evening dinner.
What really sets this hotel apart was the service. The sense of arrival was extraordinary. The Experience Designers were fantastic and provided excellent recommendations. The interactions were personal. I wasn't just another business traveler staying in the hotel. Rather, I felt welcomed and at home.
I look forward to staying at this property again! (Hopefully next time for leisure travel.)

title: “Lovely clean hotel, great loacation!”
text:
Just returned from staying at the Chandler and we enjoyed our stay there very much. 
Hotel was very clean, the staff were very friendly and helpful and the free Tea and Coffee they supplied in the Lobby was great too.
Would definitely stay at this hotel again, walking distance to all the main attractions.
Only fault I would say the hotel had was the mini bar in the room was very noisy and I like silence when I sleep :D

title: “Great Service”
text:
The best thing about Nine Zero is the service. From the bell service to room service to the front desk, every experience was excellent. Also the location is great for a business trip.
The rooms are very clean and stocked with Mario Badescu beauty products (shampoo, etc). Also the robe is a nice touch.
The only thing I didn't care for was the decor. To me, it looked like a tacky, garish modern interpretation of the Art Deco style. The bed cover was black and tan wide stripes...ugh. The chair in the room looked like it belonged in a clowns room, with its ridiculously high back. Way too much laminated black furniture! Also, in the areas outside the elevators there is tacky shimmery bronze lamae curtains covering the walls. This is just not my preference, as I prefer a more understated atmosphere. Others I was traveling with, loved the decor. The bathroom was nice, in all white tile and marble, very different in style from the rest of the room.
I enjoyed the service, but since ambiance is important to me, I will look for a different hotel next time I am in Boston.

title: “Bad”
text: No ice machine. Hair drier is down. No breakfast on weekend. Many wired ppl with wired tattoos.

title: “Don't Judge a Hotel by its cover”
text: I was excited for my accepted price of $75 dollars on priceline for a four start hotel. When I got there the building from the oustide as well as inside the lobby was gorgeous. Much like a four star quality hotel, but as far as the room goes, some updating could possibly be done here. It was obvious that the room had aged. The walls, the bathtub, closet, the t.v. seem to be the ones that could use some help into modernizing the room up to a four star quality. I expected a nice flat screen t.v for a 4 star hotel. Luckily there was a beautiful view in place. The room is not ugly, nor dirty, it just is not the standards of a 4 star hotel. I thought a 3.5 star at the Hilton was much nicer. Overall, nothing to complain about, the stay was pleasant, but again, the Westin Bonadventure looks only like a four star outside and inside its lobby but inside its hotel room it has yet to reach its 4 star standards.

title: “A Perfect Stay”
text: I have wanted to stay at this hotel since it opened about 4-5 years ago. Everything is brand new. The staff was top-notch. We were greeted outside when we got to the hotel and were offered help with our bags. Check in was easy and friendly. Our room was the best! We needed a 2-bedroom suite because I was travelling with my elderly mother who likes her privacy -- but we wanted to be within earshot in case she needed anything. There was plenty of room and the view -- oh, the view was the best. We overlooked Bryant Park and everything was in Christmas mode - the ice rink was open and the decorations were beautiful. Breakfast was the best I've ever seen at any Residence Inn. Lots of variety and, because they serve a lot of people, the food is fresh and hot. Fresh NY style bagels, good coffee cake, and plenty of eggs, bacon, sausage, pancakes, waffles, hot coffee ... and lots of people to make sure that the dining room was clean and presentable. Very impressive operation and the staff is professional and courteous. The major complaint that I've seen on this site is that the elevators are slow. Well, there are at least 4 elevators but the hotel is 39 floors so it takes a minute or two to get an elevator. If you haven't scheduled enough time to get where you need to go, then it would seem like the wait for the elevator is long. We used the elevator at the "peak" times and never had to wait longer than 2 minutes. Most of the time, we did not have to wait at all. The room was hospital clean and the bathrooms were spotless. It was dead quiet in the room at night -- something for which we were very grateful. Overall, this is one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in -- and I travel 42 weeks out of the year. Great accommodations, superb and professional staff, and a dynomite location - right in the heart of Times Square. Oh, and there are a number of spots to go for supper or a snack right nearby. In fact, there is a great pizza place right across the street that had slices for $1.00!! Christmas in the city -- it was the best.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: Very friendly staff even showed us up to the room. Very pristine rooms. Some of the rooms had shared balconey which was nice. The hotel was in walking distance from the Rivercenter Mall and close to the Hard Rock Cafe.

title: “This place should be condemned”
text: Where do I start? I'm NOT a picky traveler - really. Mold in the bathroom. Disgusting rug that I wouldn't DARE walk on barefoot. A SHOWER I wouldn't dare shower in without protection.The cable didn't work. old coffee machine with No coffee cups. Housekeeping never came even though they called at 8:45 am to find what time you were leaving. The walls were paper thin, thus, I unfortunately heard the people next door having sex every 2 hours till 4am. GROSS. They switched my room secondary to my asking, because of the broken cable, paper thin walls, moldy tiny shower, ammonia ridden sheets and dirty bathroom. Second room was cleaner, thank God- but it was a pain in the neck to move all my things from one room to another with the old school elevator for which you need 2 hands to pull BOTH doors open. I paid $150 a night for this?? First thing I want to do is take a bath with those jacuzzi jets - GUESS WHAT? It didn't work!! Oh and did I mention the people on my new floor smoking pot, thus, the strong smell in the hallway? How about the intermittent running toilet that annoyed me and woke me up several times...A dump.

title: “Perfect”
text: I stayed at this hotel over Christmas 2007 and it was perfect. The rooms and hotel were very peaceful and made our trip a very relaxing stress free vacation. It was a perfect location to walk to the shows and dinner. We couldn’t have asked for a better hotel or location in NYC. Keep up the good work!

title: “Room too small and air conditioning too noisy”
text: The hotel looked really nice but the room with two beds felt like a closet with no room to move around, not even enough room to put your luggage down comfortably. The closet was tiny and not practical. The TV was so close to the bed that it hurt the eyes. The air conditioning was so close to one of the beds, it was very disturbing during the night. The view of the court was dark and dingy. The overall value for this hotel was poor, perhaps the suites are worth while. I would not recommend staying in this hotel if you are travelling with older kids and require a bigger room.

title: “Swanky Hotel, Standard 4-star”
text: We stayed here during Christmas, and was as expected. The rooms are on-par with this level of hotel, but seems like its trying to be something its not. It was the first time I've stayed in the Upper West Side, but I prefer its counterpart, The Upper East side as there is much more to do. It is in a great location, however, if you are going to Lincoln Center.

title: “Walking distance of almost everything”
text: I've only been there for 3 days and 2 nights but had the time to visit almost everything as the hotel is walking distance of almost everything. The 5th avenue is 1 minutes of walk, Time square is 5 minutes and Center Park is no more than 10. If you'd like to go in China Town, Soho or to the Statue .. then just take the subway .. grand central is about 5 minutes of walk too.

title: “Magnolia is Really Nice”
text: Stayed 4 nights and loved the place. Close to all restaurants, shopping is one block away. Starbucks in building. Went to Rockies game and walked to Coors field. Attended concert at Red Rocks and the drive was super easy. Staff is very good. Check in went smooth. Get the valet parking for the $24.00 a night. Bell/Valet staff was very friendly and helpful. Night time cookies and milk were a hit with my family. It was also nice to sit in the leather reading chairs while eating cookies and reading the denver paper to unwind in the evening. Breakfast was minimal but very good with fruit, yogurt, granola, danish, cereal and juices. Not a full breakfast, but better than any other upscale hotels in downtown for free. It would be $5-10 a person for this breakfast at a hotel cafe. Rooms were large and clean. Bathroom is on the small side and could use more shelves for cosmetics and towel storage. Tub/shower is very large and had a great shower head. 2 queen beds in our room were very comfy. good tv channels. Excellent workout room, but bring your own headphones to listen to tv on workout equipment. 2 computers with internet connections were available for free use. Will be staying there again on next trip to Denver. Hotel had free wi-fi and a cool on site bar if you want an adult beverage.

title: “Great Location, Nice Room”
text: This was the 2nd time I stayed here. I was here for a conference 2 years ago, I went to the same conference this year. My room was a king, the bed, sofa and desk were nicer than I had two years ago, and it was fairly spacious. The bathroom was also upgraded, it seems the hotel may have done some improvements. Conference was at Moscone Center, it's close enough to walk- maybe 4 to 5 blocks. The Parc55 is right on top of Union Square; if you want to shop, it's literally 1 to 2 blocks from major boutiques and Macy's/Neiman Marcus/Nordstrom's. There's a Bart and Muni station 1 block away, the cable car turnaround is 1/2 block, and the trolley stop is 1 block. Wireless Internet is $15/day or $49/week, kind of steep even for a hotel. Join their loyalty program and I believe they give you free WiFi at all their locations (Wyndham). I would say this is an upper-midrange hotel, with amenities and prices to match. They know their competition, and you get what you pay for. I've stayed at nicer, but it was more expensive. San Francisco is not a city for cheap hotels, at least not ones you'd want to stay at. I would stay here again. P.S.- they have a 'Grab and Go' breakfast bar, you can get muffins/bagels/yogurt and coffee. 2 pastries and a coffee for $5- that's a steal in this town.

title: “Nice little hotel”
text:
My wife and I stayed at this Inn for two nights during the month of June, during a record heatwave.
Good Points about the hotel:
-Wine and Appetizer selection in the evening is very enjoyable. It 's a nice way to relax after busy days of traveling and sight seeing.
-Breakfast are very convient and quick. Fresh fruit is really good, otherwise standard buffet breakfast.
-Hotel has complimentry beverages in the refigerator
-Very large rooms, Their is a seperate closet and sink area, meaning two people can using sinks at the same time
-Hotel Front desk and all staff are very nice and made great reccomendations and reservations for dinner places. You get very individualized attention, something you will not get at a larger hotel
Bad points
-Bathrooms are a little dated.
-Very old elevator, some may feel it adds to the charm.
-We stayed during a record heat wave, and very poor ventalation no AC, Ceiling fans, or window screens. The fans or screens would of really helped and probably would have been more comfortable. Most places in SF did not have proper colling facilites. More a risk of traveling during the summer
No Opinion
In room Fire Place
Overall.
Very charming hotel, I would stay there again and reccomend it to others as well. The staff is very friendly, and one of the hotel's assets.

title: “Perfect place and excellent service.”
text: Excellent hotel. Beautiful accomodations great location, wonderful staff. Couldn't have been better.

title: “Nice stay”
text:
We stayed at the Loews for a wedding. We had stayed here many years ago and was not impressed, so I was very skeptical, but since this was where the wedding was being held we opted to take a room here. This stay was very nice and changed my opinion of this hotel. Parking in the garage was easy and quick. Because of the location, you really dont need to move it once you park. Check-in was easy and we were on our way to our room. We had a high floor (23) and a nice view of the city. The room was a nice size and so was the bathroom. The room was very clean! The bed was soft and comfortable. There wasnt many down sides to Our stay, just a few: the windows were so dirty (outside) that it was difficult to see out, the water pressure could have been better and the in room water was $5.50 a bottle!
Overall this is a really nice hotel in a very good location in the city.

title: “Greatest place to stay in NYC”
text: From checking in and having our bags held until room ready to checking out and having our bags held until our airline departure our stay was excellent. Laura, manager, Eugene, bell man were fabulous as well as every other employee we came into contact with. The breakfast was wonderful, and complimentary with the option of 'to go' breakfasts. You know what they say.....location, location, location. Well this location was better than we hoped. One block from subway, one block from the lights and excitement of Times Square. Don't miss Wicked and be sure to take a tour with On Board Tours.....so much better than the double deckers on and offs. Just politely say 'no thank you' to the hundreds of people who offer you those....you can't go wrong with On Board Tours. Highly recommend this hotel and would stay again for sure!

title: “A Chicago Gem !!!”
text: I travel to Chicago for both business and pleasure about 10 times a year and always make it a point to stay at the Majestic. It is the perfect big city combination of hotel and B&B for a great price. The location is great, the staff always attentive, the cookies and coffee plentiful, reasonable parking and decent breakfast. The small upgrade to a Sunroom suite is worth the extra since the standard rooms are a bit on the small size and the suites are very large. Mona is a wonderful as are all the staff. Ask for a free day pass to the local fitness club. To sum it up... A great place to stay !

title: “Like a Place that Features the Comforts of an Outhouse?”
text: The place sucks. The staff is unfriendly, it's shocking to see naked people wrapped in towels walking to the "public baths" , the rooms are sorry as can be, etc. The only good feature is it is in midtown and the location is good. Let me relate a quick story: My wife is wheelchair bound. As we prepared to leave I was securing her wheelchair in the van that we drove to N.Y. and the doorman came and told us to "move on". Explained that we had been guests and were just preparing to leave and he threatened us with calling a cop if we didn't move on. He left us alone after I threatened him with violence but the impression of the staff was fixed. If you have VERY low standards, by all means stay at the Pickwick Arms. And good luck. Watch out for the roaches.

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: This hotel has it all!! From the time we arrived until the time we left, it was a wonderful experience. The staff is very friendly and quick to meet any of your needs. The rooms are outstanding as far as the size goes. We had a junior suite for three of us, which included a full kitchen area, a couch and chairs for relaxing. The beds were so luxurious, with a special pillow menu, which we indulged in. The location was great, easy walking distance to most attractions. We felt very safe in this area at night(3 women). It is also right by the subway line, which is very convenient(direct line to Canal Street) if cabs are not readily available. The only downfall is getting a cab if it's raining, because the two hotels down the street get the cabs first (one way street). We had to walk across to the Waldorf for a cab which still took some time. We would definitely stay here again. It's a lot quieter than Times Square.

title: “Looking for a disaster? STAY HERE!”
text: I checked in, the first room I had, had a a view of a BRICK WALL.! Upon expressing my dislike to the (behind-the-bullet-proof window guy) I got moved to room 210.The reason I chose this shanty was bc I was there visiting my son, who lives in Hollywood in a VERY small studio apartment, and I felt his place would be TOO small (haha, yea, if I only knew). Room 210..stinky,dirty windows,tv minimal reception,certain outlets did/didnt work) oh what i would of paid for a ultra violet light at this point)'.. we didn't take our sandals off!!!!. After we ordered a pizza and discovered the plates/napkins we had asked for didn't arrive, I decided to venture down to the front desk to ask if they had any. (dumb question now I know) I went out of my room and down the steps. The front desk rude (woman I am sure here on a Visa) said "No". I kindly walked away and went up the stairs nearest the front desk to my room . BAM, GURRLL down, literally, what the heck!! I am finding myself on the floor wondering what the hell!! NO WARNING, no RED TAPE...nothing! Long story short...I end up at Cedars Sinai, severe sprain, hairline fracture...VACATION RUINED! My son packed up our things while I was at the ER, and when we demanded our $ refunded bc we had only stayed ONE night and paid for 4, they made a stink about it!! LOOK IF YOU WANT A DISASTER STAY COMPLETE W/ BED BUGS,STINKY ROOM AND A POSSIBLE VISIT TO A HOSPITAL bc this CRAP HOTEL DOESN'T KNOW WHAT A ELEVATOR IS......this is your lucky day. PS..make sure u ring the hidden doorbell up front for service) Tank U

title: “Very happy with my stay”
text: Although the hotel was not my choice because I traveled for business, the hotel was very nice and in a convenient location. The metro was in walking distance and there were many, many local restaurants to choose from in the area. We particularly enjoyed Ruth's Chris and went there for two nights out of our 3 day stay. The hotel pub is also nice. I dined there for lunch and had the chef salad. The hotel room was very comfortable and very quiet. The hotel is very large in size but I was located in the center tower which was not far from the lobby area. I would certainly stay at the hotel again if I am ever in the area again.

title: “Great Location”
text: We got into LA late and decided to stay here for just the night. We got a room for under $100 so that was nice. The room was very small, but since there was only 2 of us for one night we had no complaints. I would stay again.

title: “Amigo Spot Cantina and resturant”
text:
Very friendly and curtious staff. Kile should win bartender of the year award.
And Rosa, the hostiss. Makes you feel very comfortable and relaxed.
Very close to The San Diego Zoo. Balboa Park. And Sea World.
Only 10 minuites to the beach. And 30 minuites to an adventurous
day in Mexico. I recomend the Kings Inn to all my friends. Wayne L.

title: “Management needs to do something about large number of guests' off-leash dogs.”
text: The percentage of guests with dogs suggests this is one of the few hotels in the area that allows them. I have stayed at dozens of Staybridges across the US, and have never encountered such a concentration of dogs - especially off-leash dogs. They are even welcome in the breakfast area: on the last morning of my stay, I ate next to an off-leash german shepherd while his owner was getting his food - directly in sight of the front desk staff. On the evening I arrived, the hallway to my room was blocked by a large off-leash dog until his human finally wandered out to leash him for a walk, giving me a "What are YOU looking at?" sneer. Management cannot be there to police every infraction, but some effort needs to be made: this hotel is unfit for anyone who does not want to share the public spaces with large off-leash dogs. That's a shame, because the front desk and breakfast/dinner staff were friendly and efficient, and the property overall is satisfactory in appearance and location. But I will not return.

title: “Good value, great location but paper thin walls and really basic facilities.”
text: Pleasantly surprised by this Orel in a really good location. A short walk through Manhattan to Times Square, 5/6/7th Avenues for shopping. There is also plenty to do in and around the hotel with good eateries and pubs a stones throw away.

title: “Very Clean, Poor Reservations Service”
text:
We stayed at the hotel for one night for a family gathering. We made reservations through the hotel website. A day prior to checkin, I called the hotel to confirm our reservation. I was told that I have TWO reservations under my name, for TWO nights each. I asked the person I was speaking with to fix it to be ONE reservation for ONE night, and he said that he did it. At check-in, we were told that we've got two reservations, which means that the person I spoke to on the phone did not fix the reservation to correspond to what we booked on the hotel website. So, at check-in, they fixed it to ONE reservation, but told us that a king room, non-smoking is unavailable, only king smoking and double non-smoking are available. Time being 6:30 (checkin time is published to be 3:00), I got irritated and the front desk rep IMMEDIATELY found one more non-smoking king room that we initially reserved. But he did not see in the system that our promotional rate had free breakfast vouchers included in the rate. He took another 15 minutes to verify that and we got our vouchers (needless to say that the folio under our door the next morning prior to checkout had charges for those breakfast vouchers that were supposed to come free with our promotional rate. They fixed that when we came down to complain). 
On to the good part -- the room was the cleanest room i've ever been to. Not a stain was anywhere -- which is great in my book, and redeems the poor front desk service. The hallways are spacious and clean; as are the common areas. The buffet breakfast is excellent, and there is a piano bar upstairs, as well a a really delicious and suprisingly cheap Thai restaurant on the second floor. All in all, I LOVED the hotel, and would recommend it to anyone who appreciates a nice, clean room and spotless linens more than a seamless check-in experience.

title: “Would Never Recommend This Hotel!”
text: Our stay was a prepaid gift, but the desk people required a credit card from us on arrival, "for incidentals." Of course, our credit card was billed for the entire amount -- a discounted rate that, in our fairly sophisticated opinion, was too high anyway. We and our benefactor had to make many calls and provide several copies of the prepaid booking, to try and straighten the situation out, and after a week, we think we may be making progress. Unlike some reviewers, we found only some of the staff to be rude. Most of the people we have dealt with have just been clueless. No one seems empowered to make a customer-oriented decision. After an average room, average service, and a very substandard billing experience, we would advise other travelers to go elsewhere.

title: “Good location, nice rooms”
text: I was in town this past weekend for the Great American Beer Festival. I've stayed here several years when in town for the fest. Staff is great. Breakfast bar is stocked with a good variety of options. Rooms are comfortable. My one peeve would be the clock by the bed. Setting the alarm was easy, but I could not determine what buttons to press to correct the time.

title: “Efficient, Good location”
text:
Hilton Garden Inn is always business efficient. Our plane was delayed but checking in at the hotel took only 5 minutes. Take the Blue line subway from O'Hare airport to Clark/Lake station, walk to the LaSalle exit to street. Cross over the Chicago River and 2 or 3 blocks you will be there. From the Hotel, you can walk to most of the attractions.
The restaurant Weber Grill in the lobby was very good. Its related to the Weber Charcoal Grill people.
My husband got a call from work at 11pm. He was able to take care of it at the business center. The use of printer, fax etc without any service charge.
The indoor pool is small but nicely decorated, and with no one around, is really enjoyable.

title: “Great Location”
text:
Stayed at the Petite Auberge in April for 3 Nights. Was looking mainly for a great location and wasn't disappointed. A short walk to Union Square and trollies which can take you all the way to Fishermans Warf. 
The Room was small but nice and clean - only problem was the noise from the lift shaft could be heard through the paper thin walls.
Staff were friendly and helpful and made us feel welcome and comfortable.

title: “Love The Indigo Great Service Large Rooms”
text: What a terrific location and property. Was upgraded to a larger suite for a 5 night stay. View of Lake Michigan from room. Easy walking distance to Michigan Ave., went on daily walks on the beach every morning when we stayed at the Indigo last summer- it's just a few blocks and easy walk. Bathrooms are small, note this is a historic property and not a modern high rise.

title: “Perfect basecamp for your San Diego visit.”
text:
I used to work in Sorrento Valley and faintly remember the area. We stayed at a Holiday Inn Express in the Monterey, CA area and had a good experience and thought we'd give the chain another try for a couple of days.
We flew in on a red-eye and after driving a couple hours from LAX, I was a bit tired and hoping for an early check in. I was nicely greeted by the staff and told that since I was a preferred hotel member, that we would be able to check in. Great! We could off load the luggage and freshen up before our big day at Legoland.
The hotel was very clean and surprisingly, quiet. We had a room overlooking the pool, and the kids were excited to test it out. The room had a refrigerator (a necessity with kids) and a microwave. The beds were very comfortable, with two different levels of comfort pillows.
The best thing is that it is right off the freeway, for easy access to North/South driving. There are plenty of stores/restaurants if you go a little inland on Mira Mesa Blvd. Don't make the mistake of driving this during rush hour, though. Slow!
The next morning, we went down for the breakfast and it was not too bad; scrambled eggs/bacon/yogurt/hard boiled eggs/juices/coffee/pancakes/pastries/assorted flavored oatmeal. Definately, enough to get you started for the day.
Another great experience at a Holiday Inn Express.

title: “Lovely hotel, perfect location, excellent experience.”
text: My two night stay was great. Had higher floor room so it was fairly quiet. Check-in was quick & easy. Housekeeping had everything well stocked & spotless. Reservation through hotel’s website: unbeatable price. LOCATION is perfect. Just steps from Bart station, cable cars, F bus. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND Parc 55!

title: “Nice hotel, great location”
text:
The only thing this hotel is lacking is white noise in the rooms, and next time i'll bring my own. My room was very quiet (no a/c or fan noise), but when there was street or hallway noise it seemed louder because of that. 
If you are a workout fanatic, there is a nice health club across the street that allows the Hyatt guests to workout for a small fee. 
This is a nice hotel in a great location, and I recommend it.

title: “Well, the cockroach was friendly”
text: Looking at its website you would be forgiven for mistaking The Shoreham for a decently priced, good quality boutique hotel. We should all send congratulatory notes to the web designers. I imagine it was the same team that faked the Apollo 11 lunar landing, such was the level of deception. Look, it is a conveniently placed hotel and is not a hell-hole, but by the same token neither is it presenting itself (or charging itself) as an economy option. Rooms are tiny, dark and either very hot or freezing cold. I have yet to find any natural light and emerge blinking into the daylight upon exit from the place each time. The staff are clearly not happy, motivated souls who live for customer service, perhaps they just need a hug, but perhaps they also need to move on and find a career that fulfils them more. The place is tired and rather poor. It wouldnt take a lot to fix it, a little bit of sympathetic refurbishment from a designer that actually cared for humans rather than purely aesthetic, clever light management, a menu over-haul, comfortable beds and a staff change and you would be back in business. The cockroaches were pleasant however and the wifi was free. Whoop whoop.

title: “Horrifying Hole”
text: My flight was canceled, I needed an emergency hotel, but none was to be had. I wandered through Manhattan hearing "All booked, sorry." Then I found the Carter. I hit 43rd Street and saw the huge “Hotel” sign. In the lobby I’m so tired I don't really absorb the crowd. It's a dive but I'm not thinking straight. I go up to the desk and the guy behind the window tells me he has a room. "I'll take it." "OK. It's $116 plus one dollar nonrefundable room key deposit." "Fine," I say, and pull out my credit card. "No. Cash only." He sees me look at the Mastercard and Visa signs. "You can pay by credit card only if you have a reservation." "Well, give me a reservation." "It's too late for a reservation today. Cash only." I pull out my money. He passes me a plastic room card with 1031 written in bleeding red marker across the front. I get in the elevator with some teenagers reeking of alcohol. The elevator door creeks opens on ten and I know I'm in trouble right away. The exterior room doors are all badly painted a vomit-teal-bluish hue. I put in my key and open the door. It gets worse. The bathroom. The tub has rust stains. There is no shower head, just a pipe sticking out of the wall. I turn the heavy silver metallic cold water knob and immediately the hot water knob falls off and clatters into the tub. The toilet has no tank so the opened toilet seat falls backwards and looks like a pitiful gaping mouth, jaws wide. I close it then feel like I should wash my hands. But I see no soap. And no shampoo. There is no stopper in the drain in the sink. Later, the cap of my toothpaste falls into the sink and disappears. Across the bathroom is a closet. When you open the door you see the emergency exit plan. For the Dixie Hotel. Which I can only hope was the name of the Carter Hotel some lifetime ago and they simply didn't bother to change the sign. Above this was scrawled a profanity laced poem I cannot repeat here, but it alluded to bed bugs and unclean toilets. An unmarked phone sat on a rickety table. No alarm clock. The king sized bed was the most sanitary seeming thing about the place. A large mirror with a piece of broken frame sharply protruding hung on the wall. A functioning air conditioner mercifully sat in the window behind a receptionless television. A metal coat hanger sat in the corner. I intuited why I had been made to pay cash: no refunds, no refuted credit card bill. I went back downstairs to ask for another room. The earlier guy was gone, and the night shift guy had taken over, an older man. I asked him if he had a better room. He gave me a pitiful look, innocently shrugged and said, "They're all the same." He handed me three tiny bars of soap. I walked outside. As near as it is to Times Square this section of 43rd is pretty desolate. Across the street is the entrance to a huge parking garage. Across from that is the Cheetah Club where I saw a “dancer” screaming at the guys in the parking garage. Before going upstairs I asked the front desk for a wakeup call. "Does the phone ring pretty loudly?" I asked. "I don't know." I went to the room and took a shower. Or rather, it took me. Because the pipe sticking out of the wall was bent toward the back shower wall I had to sort of push myself against the tile wall to get wet. Then the drain immediately clogged and the water got to ankle level. I then took the metal hanger and put it's hook on the frame of the door on the inside so that in the event some criminal broke open the door (the secondary lock was long gone) at least the hanger would clatter to the ground to alert me a second or two. After the shower I got fully clothed and laid on the bed on top of the covers and tried to sleep. I got up with my 4:00 a.m. wakeup call and escaped in a cab to airport. I emailed some of this adventure to my friend, a long time New Yorker who emailed me back: "I should have told you, whatever you do don't ever stay at the Carter Hotel."

title: “Fantastic Service - Perfect Location”
text: Beautiful hotel, and the staff provides incredible service!

title: “GOOD HOTEL NEAR TIMES SQUARE”
text:
*Major renovations taking place when we were there
*Staff very helpfull, nothing too much trouble
*Rooms quite spacious and well appointed

title: “Great Stay!”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Revere Boston Common while in Boston for a week-long vacation. The hotel, as I understand, was previously a Radisson, so the outside looks a bit older, but the interior has been completely redone and is lovely. Our king room was very clean and inviting. The bed was comfortable and linens were very nice...fluffy pillows and comforter and nice, thick towels! The bathroom had Skoah skin products which I loved. Richard and Sargent, the two concierges with whom we worked, were extremely helpful and accomodating. Location is great...within walking distance of most everything. We will definitely stay again!

title: “Great stay! Made my business travel less stressful”
text:
I experienced greaty service at this hotel.
The staff was very professional and also honest.
I lost my cell phone on the hotel shuttle and the driver returned it to me.

title: “Comfy and clean!”
text: We just spent the weekend in New York, and stayed one night at the Americana. Our room was small (we had a double bed) but spotlessly clean and comfortable. The shared bathrooms were also very clean, the staff was friendly and helpful -- even letting us leave our bags in the office after we checked out, so we could get lunch without having to haul luggage around -- and the hotel was very quiet. We definitely plan to go back -- it wasn't luxurious, but it made for a very pleasant and restful overnight stay!

title: “The friendliest atmosphere and great bar”
text: The front desk was extremely friendly and helpful, and the restaurant was the best you could hope for. The management was great and the Bar was immaculate. Peter was a great help in our stay and the bartender Lisa was the warmest and friendliest person we met. It was nice to not have to ask for something to drink, it was always there. She really knew how to make you feel at home, we will always remember her warm smile. Thank you nios and the Muse, we will be back for another round.

title: “Poor value for money... and so noisy”
text:
Welcome rather good
Concierge advices excellent and very friendly;
Rooms are small, Take 1 luggage because you will not find space to place your second one...
Elevators (2) are slow and you be ready to wait long minutes before you'll enter it.
Be prepare to dance in your bed. A nighclub is located at the groud floor; DJ is probably not aware that people are in their hotel room also to sleep...
Be prepared also to welcome some young unexpected drunk guests as neighboors coming at the middle and shout, dance, ...
Positive point: location near Time square.

title: “Inn at the Opera is a charming, convient hotel.”
text: We chose to stay in the smallest room available and it was a marvel for all it contained. I think I might opt for a larger space next time, but the hotel is a great place to stay. The Opera House and Symphony Hall are just a block away. The hotel is charming. The room very well appointed, valet parking very good and continental breakfast first rate. The staff was super. Couldn't have asked for better service.

title: “Decent hotel in a great location”
text: Was pleasantly surprised by the Hyatt after securing a room through hotwire. It's a very comfortable hotel, though the lobby and entrance area left much to be desired. Strange layout, with a parking garage basically the first thing you see of the hotel. Great location if you're interested in the theater district or the down-town crossing shopping district - it's actually in the same complex that also houses the big Macy's store in boston. The park is also very close by. Very quiet while we were there. Nice pool, though a hot tub is sorely missed! Small but decent work-out room is attached to the pool. Didn't try the restaurant - decided there were much more reasonably priced places to eat near-by. All in all, a great stay.

title: “Crisp, clean, friendly, comfortable. Will always stay here when in NYC.”
text: This is a gem of a hotel, tucked in a very accessible location. It is my second time staying at the Hilton Garden Inn on West 35th Street and it will always be my hotel of choice when visiting New York. Perfect if you are in town for meetings and out of the hotel for most of the day ONLY because the rooms are compact BUT provide every amenity/service you could need including in-room refrigerator. Very comfortable bed and linens, wonderful shower and bathroom supplied, clean, crisp, neat, and tidy. The staff is incredibly friendly and generous with their time and knowledge. I agree with the hotel motto, "Everything right where you need it!"

title: “A bargain in NYC”
text: We stayed here for 5 nights in mid-July and were very pleased. It is an older building, of course, but very nicely appointed. Rooms were small-ish, as is typical of New York, but we had plenty of room to open suitcases, get around beds, etc. so no complaint. The bathroom was small and could use some re-grouting but I think small bathrooms and rooms are part of the NYC experience! The hotel has a Starbucks, a nice bar, a good restaurant, business center, and all you might need. Staff very helpful: I have a broken foot and therefore preferred 2 beds (so my husband didn't inadvertantly kick me!) and they let us change rooms with no extra charge. We had used Priceline so they could've said "Sorry, no changes" but they didn't. The rate was excellent, and LOCATION perfect. The hotel is about 5 easy blocks from Grand Central Terminal, & several other subway stops are right up Lexington so getting anywhere is a breeze. It's easy to walk to Times Square, Central Park, Rockefeller Center, St. Patrick's Cathedral. Lots of restaurants/bars are located a short walk away on 2nd and 3rd Avenues, and we enjoyed breakfast at the little deli across the street every morning. This hotel is fine and we had no complaints. Would stay there again.

title: “Great employees, location and value....”
text: I was wondering what I would find here after reading a few reviews about how tired and dated this Sheraton is. Must be that there have been some recent renovations - I found it to be perfectly clean and very comfortable. Above all, the staff was top-notch, especially the bell-hops - they were all professional, friendly and helpful. We are planning another stay within the next month because we loved this hotel so much!!

title: “Stunning Views”
text: I have stayed here a number of times and although it is a bit if a walk to the shops of Mich Ave, I cannot fault it! Absolutely amazing views especially if you get a corner room! The staff are friendly however I would admit that the breakfast buffet is really not up to much and is shamefully in the bowels of the hotel with no exterior views which is such a shame. Also the lobby can get very congested! But otherwise a very relaxing experience!

title: “Daniel-Front Dest Agent”
text: This is our sixth year staying at the Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square. I was the first one to get there on Thursday January 21, 2010 awaiting for the remaining 14 guests to arrive that same day. Daniel was professional, courteous and helped me get all the rooms set in advance with the rooming list. The accomodations and professionalism displayed by Daniel was exceptional. I highly recommend this hotel and working directly with Daniel.

title: “A WONDERFUL EXPERIENCE”
text:
I know this is a bit of a late review, but i had to write about the fantastic time i had staying at the New Yorker. I was over in New York with the N.ireland team for the World Fire and Police games. We arrived around 2.30 pm and after a bit of confusion at the desk we finally got to our room. The view down 8th avenue, and towards the empire state building was fantastic. could not fault the decor or beds. Bathrom was a bit small but served its purpose. stayed a total of 9 nights. on my last night my wife joined me so i needed another room. when i went to pick up the keys i was informed i had been given an upgrade for the one night. once again the room was fantastic and had great views overlooking the hudson, and had a balcony. We where leaving for a cruise the next day but had nothing planned for the few days after the cruise. I had origionaly planned on booking another hotel in New York for the remaining part of our holiday, but went to reception and booked with them for the remaining few nights in New York. 
I have to mention also mention Legends Bar beside the Empire State Building. My friends and i have never had a warmer welcome

title: “Reminds me of a European hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Warwick New York for two nights over a long weekend with my fiance. I got a great rate of $170/night using Priceline's Name Your Own Price option. I think it normally goes for about $230/night. The first person we encountered at the Warwick was the person behind the check-in counter, and he was extremely friendly, and funny! Our room wasn't ready but they took our bags and held them in back so we could go sightseeing.
When we went back a few hours later, we got our bags and went upstairs. We got a room on the 16th floor; it was a corner room - plus! However, beware of the elevators: if you are claustrophic, take the stairs! They are very small and probably can only fit about 4 or 5 people comfortably.
The room was a good size and the bed was so comfy! We both slept amazingly well. The only thing that wasn't so great was the bathroom size - I felt like I was back in Europe, it was so small - and there was no full-length mirror.
We went to the hotel bar one night for a couple drinks, and yes, they are pricey. My fiance got a specialty cocktail for $15 and all the beers were $10. The chick next to us was drinking a Budweiser (for $10?!) while I got a Blue Moon for the same price. Not sure who would pick a Bud! Regardless, it has a very loungy feel and the servers were attentive.
I would absolutely stay here next time, and in fact, it was such a great stay that if I didn't have a Priceline/Hotwire option, I would actually pay full price through the hotel. Oh - and you can't beat the location. A few blocks south of Central Park; a few blocks north of Times Square.

title: “This is where you want to be....”
text:
After researching several sites for a hotel in San Diego, I settled on the La Pensione. No regrets. I wanted a reasonably priced,clean place located near Zoo, beach and other hotspots. Being in the heart of Little Italy was a bonus. On Saturdays, the street in front of the hotel turns in to a marketplace with music and vendors selling anything from art, coffee to fresh sea urchin (?) ! 
Regarding the rooms, they are smaller but comfy..Our room faced the ocean, which is about 3 blocks away.
I stayed here with my partner Sept 18-19, which i figured would be cooler in the hotel. It was on the warm side in the room during the day but cooled off enough during the night.
Not sure if summer stay here would be ideal, but I'm not a meteorologist so dont know if SD weather varies much in the summer.
Restaurants galore. 
These are among the friendliest people I ever met, until you trek out onto the freeways...Yikes
We will be back to San Diego and the La Pensione as soon as we can.
If your looking for something a little different with charm., give this place try

title: “Made my Seattle experience even greater than it was”
text: Great stay at decent price close to anything you need and transportation. Very friendly staff, bikes can be rented and almost all major central objectives are within walking distance or few bus stations away. I'd happily stay there again if I end up in Seattle in the future

title: “Great Location”
text: Very convient location...right off Michigan Avenue. Small, no frills rooms/small beds ..... no problem for us since we did not spend much time in our room. We had to wait quite awhile for the slow elevators since the "Plant Show" was on and many exhibitors/guests filled the two slow elevators with their plants...no biggie. The BEST surprise was the roof top garden where you could byob (on a weekday) and enjoy the beautiful chicago views. Hopefully the hotel has caught on to the non-hotel stayers enjoying this rooftop and bringing and cranking their own music also:-(! We got this hotel for a good deal through a "name your own price" site!

title: “Great hotel, but staff is unhelpful and the odor in lobby is awful.”
text:
We did not see valet parking availability on the website; however, when we arrived, we opted not to utilize the valet parking because there were garages in close proximity. We were not told, nor were there signs that indicated the connected garage that we chose was NOT affiliated with the Magnolia. This caused an issue upon leaving Sunday morning. The front desk was little help, but more due to lack of information; although she was aware the problem we had, occurred regularly. She was friendly and directed us to the Bellman/Valet, whom was absolutely no help and acted as though my wife was intruding on his time. It made sense that there the bellman/valet might have a number to the garage next door for this repeated issue. (we could not get out of the garage Sunday morning because there was no attendant available) The bellman/valet appeared uninterested in helping us find a solution, but rather more interested in standing behind the desk. He asked if we tried calling the number posted. There was no number posted and we had already tried the number on the ticket. My concern if we had been made aware of our parking options prior to booking we may have had a smoother time or even if the Magnolia staff cannot help, pretend to be empathize with the customers plight. If feels more human and caring. Our initial set of keys did not work and we were asked by an employee that happen to be walking the floors (I believe to check the rooms and housemaids progress)if we were in the correct room. Strange question. The second set of keys only had one working keys. There was also a wedding reception the evening and no communication was happening, because when we checked in we were told happy hour and the evening snack was on level two when it had been changed to level three for the evening. We found this out because we entered the 2nd floor as the setup was going on for the wedding. Also, for such a nice hotel with great rooms and beds that offer a great nights sleep, walking distance to many things in downtown Houston, the ODOR was unbearable in the lobby. Surely there are air purifiers or odor eliminators that can be used repeatedly. Your traffic would definitely increase with a more welcoming aroma.
On Saturday evening we walked out the front door and asked the bellman/valet if he knew of any quick eateries and he said no, only the hotel room service. I get that making money for the hotel is important, but if more knowledge of the area would be appreciated. It appears the employees do not care if the guests enjoy their stay.
 Overall detail are important. I would stay at the Magnolia again because it is a beautiful hotel, but I would like to know that some of these issues are addressed.

title: “A Well Kept Secret!”
text:
It was such a pleasant surprise to come upon this hotel! I travel 30-45% of the year and have seen some doozies! This hotel was so nice to come home to after a hard tradeshow day. The decor is awesome and the hotel is VERY clean! My bathroom was always sparkling. Location is most important and being in the heart of Union Square cannot be beat. 
There are several wonderful little restaurants walking distance (5 minutes away). You won't be disappointed with this one!

title: “Just Wonderful”
text:
Stayed 4 nights end of September into October. All requests were honored - no smoking, room in rear, and adjacent room next to other family members. Very efficient and courteous staff.
Rooms were very large with small efficiency kitchen - refrigertor, microwave, sink, toaster, & coffee. Very clean and nicely furnished. Free Wi-fi connections and access to computer and printer in lobby. Location was perfect - only a couple of blocks to Union Square and near all transportation. Nice little walk into China town also.
Hotel served a continental breakfast with bagels, croissants, and pastries and some fruit each morning in the roof top lounge which was plenty to get us started for the day of touring. Hotel also had a gym with sauna but unfortunately we never had time to use it. Hotel also has a nice restaurant and bar area which offers half-priced apertizers during "Happy Hour". Great hotel at a great price. I would highy recommend this hotel.

title: “A DUMP!!”
text:
I arrived at the hotel at 3 p.m., was sent to my room and found it had not yet been cleaned. The beds were stripped, no towels, old food in the little fridge, etc. How does a hotel not make sure a room is ready at check-in time?? After we brought it to the manager's attention, we went back to the room. We opened the screen door to the "garden area" (a little plot of dirt with weeds), whereupon the screen door fell off the track and I noticed the army of ants crawling up the side and into the room. When we complained to the manager, she said she'd send someone in with a can of Raid!! My partner had to point out that we did not care to breathe in bug spray for the next 5 days.
She told me to go look at one of the "suites" on the second floor. I did and said it was much better. She said, "Yes, it's very beautiful." HA! It was definitely better--large bedroom, a living room, a kitchen with fridge and oven, and kitchen table--but far from beautiful. It was old and needed updating. We had to clean the a.c. filter ourselves! The bathroom service was inconsistent (only 2 bath towels and soap one day, then suddenly they decided to give us hand towels, and we finally got another bar of soap on the last day).
The pool was DISGUSTING. It looked like it hadn't been cleaned in weeks. There was a ring of rust/dirt around the water line (ewww!) and dirt and leaves on the bottom, which stayed there for the entire 5 days we were there.
But what galls me the most was that she told me she would only charge me an extra $20/night for the suite just to make me happy! Any other hotel would have upgraded me for free after that. AND she charged me a $50 deposit, even though the room had been pre-paid in full (except for the extra $20). I've never heard of such a thing and I was apalled with this place.
The sad thing is that it has a lot of potential. It IS nestled in the Hollywood hills and is 2 blocks from Hollywood BLVD. It could really be a nice place, but the owners are too cheap to renovate and don't know how to treat their guests. Never again.

title: “Good hotel”
text: This hotel is very good. Stay for a week. Forgot my money bag which I left under pillow. Call security and they put it away for me straight away. So very happy or else it would be no money.

title: “"Great Service, Location, Comfort."”
text: This was our first stay at a Sofitel hotel. The location and service were terrific. The restaurant was very good, and our room was clean, comfortable, and quiet. The only reason I did not rate the Sofitel 5 stars was due to the dimly lit lobby and public areas--rather depressing, after visiting other hotels with light-filled lobbies. Some of the public areas for relaxing and reading had such low lighting that it was a strain to read the books and magazines. The Sofitel's attributes outweigh this relatively minor criticism, but it was enough to dissuade me from staying here again. That being said, it is clearly a very popular hotel, and was crowded the entire time.

title: “Fun and funky”
text: We loved the funkiness and the history of the Hotel Chelsea....the location was perfect for our lower Manhattan touring. The staff was awesome...gave us great tips and arranged a wonderful car service to the airport. We will definitely stay here again!

title: “Outstanding Service!”
text: The Bladensburg Road Holiday Inn provided service that went above and beyond my expectations. Great price for the area too! Will definately stay there again when I visit the Washington DC area.

title: “Excellent family stay”
text: My family and I arrived very late (3am). Our room was terrific. Recommendation: Try to get an upper room on southeast side to get views of Empire State Building and Bryant Park.

title: “Excellent!”
text: Very very nice hotel. Closed to Time square (just a couple of blocks!). We walked around for 3 days and took the subway only twice to go downtown. It's not true the street is not safe...It's also very close to the bus station, therefore very convenient if you have to go to any other city by bus (Grayhound). Room: modern and clean. Service: super! They were very friendly, give nice suggestions for restaurants and diners. I forgot a dress in the hotel and they were very kind and help me to have it back. I appreciate the chocolates, newspaper and weather forecast left every day in the room...Absolutely we will stay there again and suggest to any friend.

title: “Great staff”
text: The loaction of the hotel was excellent for my purposes. Very pleasant room and well equipped exercise facility. But what I liked most was the extremely pleasant and professional staff. From the initial contact at the front desk, to the concierge, to the bar tenders everyone was polite, helpful, and made my stay there very comfortable. When the transportation to the airport van did not show up right on time the hotel staff immediately took me and another guest to the airport in a hotel van with no questions asked. Very well run facility.

title: “Another Hilton Homer”
text:
I chose this property because of its proximity to Universal Studios, which we were visiting. It is right on the property and an easy walk to and from the park, even though a shuttle is available.
