I stay nearly exclusively at Hilton Properties and enjoy Diamond status as a result, although my stays are usually at Hampton inns or Hilton Garden Inns.
I am also very critical of small details.
This hotel is outstanding. The staff is attentive and each request was followed with a prompt and polite "my pleasure." The Starbucks on site also serves gelato and the barista was very kind to our 9 year old, offering her sample tastes of whatever she wanted. (He was rewarded with a generous tip).
We had room service the first night (delivered within 40 minutes, very hot and exquisitely presented by a very personal server who, upon entering the room, wished me a "happy father's day.") Each day we availed ourselves of the breakfast buffet that rivals that found on any cruise ship, with American, European and Asian fare. We also had dinner in the restaurant one evening, with all our expectations being met, then exceeded. There really was no reason to eat anywhere else.
Self-parking in an exceptionally clean parking garage with in and out privileges was convenient and billed to our room, although valet is available.
We also spent some time in the lounge and were treated to Melody Federer, whose entertaining style made us laugh. You can check out Melody here:://www.melodyfederer.com/#!__home.
I expect a lot from a Hilton. This particular property delivered service, food and amenities "above and beyond" what I had expected. Definitely will return to this hotel whenever I can.

title: “Excellent”
text:
My first visit to an Omni property.....this was a TA induced stay based on reviews as I am a Marriott die hard usually.
Location is pretty peaceful also.
I have to say from start to finish our stay was excellent.
Great service from the staff.....car valet gave me all the parking options when we pulled up.....John gave us a great run through of our room facilities while bringing in our luggage.....Eddie looked after us at breakfast.....just very very good.
The hotel has obviously had some updating recently as.....decoration...floor coverings etc and all nicely done.
Room was a good size..really nice size bathroom also.....beds were great....slept like a log.
Pool area is nice also.
There is a hotel car that will take to Galleria shopping etc if required.
If this hotel is in the vicinity of where your looking to stay....would recommend consideration.

title: “Perfect airport hotel”
text: We stay here often and I can't say enough about this hotel. They are lovely, child friendly and perfect for early morning departure from the airport. I love that you can wok over to the airport if you don't feel like waiting for the shuttle and the walk is covered so you don't have to worry about the shuttle. We often order pizza and have it delivered to the hotel. The rooms are big and have anise view of the city (and sometimes the harbor). While nothing is perfect this comes close to making travel out of Logan in the morning stress free. It can be a bit expensive but is worth it. The staff will go out of their way to accommodate your every(and sometimes random) wish.

title: “Good Hotel”
text: We enjoyed our stay in this Hotel, the stuff was kind and helpful, the Room Service very punctual and our room was clean. Just a few minutes walk to the Rodeo Drive and Wilshire B. and near the Hotel is a bus stop, you can reach other places like Hollywood B. or Santa Monica Pier. There is also a Limousine service, we have benefited to reach the airport. We will recomand this Hotel.

title: “birthday getaway”
text: The hotel is very nice and we chose a Sunday night stay because of the price of the rooms. Although the rooms and service a very nice the prices for a night stay are seemingly high especially in a casino hotel where you are not spending all that much time in your room.

title: “Never Again”
text:
My stay here was for 4 nights, 4-8 January '05. I was staying with family and I have to say it was one of the worst hotel experiences I have ever had. 
Upon check in, the reception staff was rude and very distant. When I noted that I had requested a high floor room. I was told that I would be on the 4th floor and that was that. Once in our room which to give it credit was a decent size, we realised that the closet was tiny and the room smelled old. I understand that this is an historic hotel, but not having the ability to open windows and allow fresh air in, is ridiculous! 
On the first time using the shower, I opened the shower curtain to find the bathroom had flooded! I called down to report it to the main desk. They sent an engineer, who had no idea what I was talking about. Not sure what was done to stop the problem, it looked liked they re-grouted the bath. But the bathroom flooded again everytime it was used! In the end it seemed as though the double layer shower curtain was leaking! 
There was a fridge in our room which we didn't have to pay for. Good thing too! Considering when I went to use it I found old food from the previous guests inside! Who knows how long it had been there!
 I know they have housekeeping, but somehow they seemed to have forgotten our room! Only when I dropped a piece of clothing on the floor, I found it covered in dust! That was when I realised that they only vacuumed the areas on show! 
Continuing with the service received in this hotel. Upon check out, they did not disappoint, I was ignored for around 10 minutes, until I approached the desk and announced my wish to leave. The lack of attention and eye contact from staff made my exit from this hotel something that could not have come too soon!

title: “Excellent hotel , very centrally located”
text: Stayed here during a stop over in New York. Was presently surprised with the hotel, excellect service and location. Walking distance to time square and the other attractions. Very clean and nice, excellent in-room internet for free. Very good breakfast and excellent coffee : -). Will definately stay here again as it is an well priced hotel in New york

title: “Disappointing for a Holiday Inn”
text:
We probably made a mistake at check in. We had booked a non smoking room. We were given a choice – a non smoking room in a separate Annex block, or an upgrade room in the hotel itself – albeit a smoking room. After an 11 hour flight and no sleep for nearly 24 hours I cannot always think too clearly; I picked the upgrade. The word ‘Annex’ conveys the impression of something tacked on and ‘upgrade’ of unexpected benefits and luxury. When we got to the room, I couldn’t help but think “if this is the upgrade, then I wonder what the standard rooms are like”. I wouldn’t go as far as to say it was awful, but it was certainly very tired and in desperate need of refurbishment. It also had a hint of that nasty odour caused by stale cigarette smoke which I suppose was not unexpected. In short, it was disappointing. If it wasn’t for the fact we were cross eyed with tiredness coupled with the knowledge we were only there for one night, I would probably have requested a different room. On the cleanliness front, I would describe it as reasonably clean but not spotlessly clean. With regard to the heating/air conditioning arrangements, there did not seem to be much variance between hot and cold on the rather ancient unit. Fortunately, neither was really necessary; we had excellent weather for January. 
On the positive side, there was complimentary internet access on the floor (part of the ‘upgrade’ package), as well as a decent sized fridge in the room. 
We found the staff to be helpful and pleasant, particularly the concierge. 
We didn’t eat in the hotel; breakfast seemed expensive for what it was, but there were a number of places just a few minutes walk away from the hotel that did breakfasts for just a few dollars. 
For dinner, I had done a little bit of research before we arrived. Seemed to me that while there were indeed loads of restaurants in the vicinity, none seemed to stand out as being particularly remarkable. So we picked out one in the Russian Hill district called Antica Trattoria on Polk Street (at Union). It is a ‘neighbourhood’ restaurant (ie frequented by locals) – always a good sign in my experience. It was excellent (you can look it up by tapping the name into Google). About a 10-12 minute walk from the hotel, up a steep hill – but it’s downhill on the way back! Cost us approx £30 a head with all drinks including a very pleasant bottle of Napa Valley Pinot Noir – a good meal for a fair price. After we got back to the hotel, we had a quick night cap in the bar. We found the barman to be helpful and knowledgeable.
Noting some of the previous comments over the ‘tackiness’ of the area – it certainly was in places. It would be unfair to label the whole area in that way though. ‘Touristy’ it certainly is – and we knew that when we booked. Overall though we found the area to be quite pleasant with a relaxed atmosphere; the nearby Cannery certainly falls into that category. From that perspective, the hotel is very well located. 
I would only stay at this hotel again if I knew that the rooms had been refurbished. As it was, it was singularly unremarkable.

title: “Great Choice for Downtown Dallas”
text: We recently went to Dallas for the first time and did not know what to expect and we chose to stay at the Adolphus based on TA reviews and we were not disappointed. Very nice place to stay downtown. A beautiful and impressive classic hotel. Everyone on staff was friendly and helpful and they made our stay a good one. For an old historic hotel, the rooms were quite large and nicely appointed. Recently renovated and there is no "old hotel smell." We got a great rate and were pleased to also receive free breakfast coupons for the Bistro - which was a nice surprise. The hotel room was spacious, modern, new comfy king bed, nice bath & bath amenities, in-room coffee, mini-bar, good wireless connection, large walk-in closet, great views of the city, close to many things including the JFK memorial site, the Dart train station (2 blocks away) which made getting to and from the State Fair a breeze. The hotel is also close to several great places to dine in case their French Room is not your cup of tea. Everyone on staff was nice and helpful. Valet pakring was also easy. We would stay here again and we can also recommend it.

title: “Awesome Hotel”
text: Beautiful hotel, decent size rooms, very clean, nice, friendly, helpful staff. Emailed me ahead of time for any requests and requests were granted. Arrived early and was allowed to check into room early. Was greeted by person who emailed me and given a welcome bag of goodies. Was able to store luggage on the last day after checking out. Close to Times Square and tour buses. Everything in walking distance.

title: “Good value, great location and fun staff”
text:
Highest points here go to the staff. Always friendly and helpful even with a large group of teenagers. The breakfast is just enough but nothing special. A few hot choices and a plenty of fruit, yogurt, etc. The river view is pretty cool and you can see the Ben Franklin Bridge and Penn's Landing. The district behind the hotel seemed safe and was OK for walking and jogging in the evening. 
The hotel loses points on the touchless key system they were trying. You just have to swipe your keycard in front of the door for it to unlock but our keycards had to be reset every night. Ended up being quite a hassle.

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: I have stayed at the Conrad, before and after the Meridian. I travel extensively on business throughout the country and always look forward to the Conrad in Chicago at least twice a year. Wonderful staff, the best doormen, great rooms and service. Especially in the winter, when you can shop without going out to Michigan Avenue! I am a single woman and have always been treated beautifully by the staff! Highly recommend and I am picky!

title: “Hilton Times Square, Splendid Views, Staff and Service”
text: I recently spent time in the Big Apple. I am a die-hard Marriott guest but this time decided to check out this hotel based on reviews from this site. I was pleasantly surprised. The hotel sits in an excellent location for just about anything that one wants to do in New York. The rooms are spacious, clean and inviting. The restaurant and bar area is classy and staff are ultimate professionals. My room overlooked Times Square but I was never bothered with any noise. I will stay at this hotel again.

title: “Good - could be great.”
text:
I stayed at this well located hotel on the upper west side close to Central park and right next to the museum of natural history for three nights. I had a semi private single room, which means you share toilet/bath located in the corridor. The room was very nice compared to others in the same price range ($ 100) I´ve stayed in in NY, spotless and not too small. Bathrooms were very nice if you managed to find a vacant one, and that was the major drawback. Only two bathrooms per floor and constantly occupied from 7-11 am. My room had a sink so you could at least wash your face.. 
The staff was friendly but didn´t go out of their way to help you. I needed to get tickets to a Rangers game and asked if I could go online for two minutes to buy and print tickets at the hotel lobby (internet cafes nearby had no printing capacity) but that was a no-go.
All in all a good hotel that could be great with abetter bathroom access, if I had stayed in a room with private bath I would rat this hotel a 4+.

title: “Great Happy Hour”
text: The most exotic happy hour foods in Seattle - rabbit pate, fried smelt, lamb meatballs, etc goes beyond most happy hour fare. The lobby area is one of the best hide-outs in Seattle, especially on a rainy day.

title: “The worst place I´ve ever been!”
text:
The minute I walked at the door I knew I have made a big mistake: there were no elevator, so we had to carry our big luggage trough the stairs. The manager told us to pick the room we like, so we made a horrifying tour through this place, to find out that the rooms were one worse than the other. We had a reservation for 4 days, but we stayed only that first night. The next day we run away...
There were mushrooms growing in the carpets, and the smell of the room was disgusting.
Please, do not go to this "inn"

title: “Amazing”
text: Stayed overnight at this new Hilton Garden Inn just minutes from Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport. It's an amazing property. Rooms are large and bright and great views of the airport one side and mountains on the other!! Staff are very friendly and the amenities are first class. Can't be beat for the price .... PLUS, it's only a block from the 38th Street Light Rail station that takes you right into downtown or Tempe in just minutes for only $2.50/day unlimited rides! Would highly recommend!

title: “The Best Vacation with Family ever”
text:
Our Family stayed at Humphreys June 27 through July 1. My husband and I along with our two children and their friends stayed at this wonderful hotel. We had previously stayed at a new hotel downtown attending a conference June 25 and 26. While the new hotel was beautiful it was extremely expensive and ultimately not as kid friendly as Humphreys was. The staff at Humphreys went above and beyond to make our stay comfortable. I visited Humphreys a day ahead of our check in to make sure we were getting a room that would work well for our family - we had reserved a suite and a regular room and wanted to make sure the kids were fairly close to us for safety purposes. I called the next day and the reservationist was able to share with me the rooms that had been assigned to us and really put my anxiety to rest. She did her best to put the kids close to us and gave us a room we were thrilled with - the view was great and we were more than satisfied. 
We checked in that afternoon and the kids were thrilled with the tropical atmosphere of the entire hotel. Being able to check our emails in the lobby was super, the pool was great and the service around the pool superior as well. In fact our last day we stayed at the hotel and lounged around the pool, ate room service and drinks by the pool. The service staff was always friendly and efficient.
Our vehicle was hit in the parking lot and the security personnel was right on it because the driver drove away. He was able to secure a license plate from a hotel guest and went above and beyond to make sure harbor police was called and followed up to make sure our needs were met. Wow what a great experience given the circumstance.
I highly recommend this hotel to anyone. They are in the process of modernizing all the rooms and that will prove to be great. One of our rooms was completed and the flat screen tvs, bed linens and all was superior. While our suite was older it still was very nice and we were very pleased. The toaster, pots and pans were older and some didn't work well but when I brought it to the attention of staff they indicated all I had to do was ask and they would be replaced. The TV in our bedroom didn't work at 10 p.m. one night - a staff period replaced the tv and made sure our needs were met - everything we asked was met with incredible service. Someone is training and motivating staff they right way. The only downside was I felt the cleaning staff were not as friendly and was rushing us so they could clean the rooms and be done. 
Kudos to Humprheys staff and all that made our stay great.

title: “Perfect, perfect, perfect”
text: This hotel was perfect! The location couldn't have been better . . . . walking distance to Central Park, theaters, Rockefeller Center, St. Patrick's Cathedral, shopping, shopping shopping! . . . and convenient subway stations. The rooms were nice size, bed was very very comfortable, nice bathroom and amenities. But most of all, the staff (front desk, concierge, security, door man, bell hop, cleaning crew) were the most friendly and courteous I've ever encountered. My daughter and I had dreamed about this trip for just the two of us for years . . . and The Manhattan at Times Square helped make it the perfect vacation. I will definitely stay here again and recommend it wholeheartedly.

title: “Beautiful Bay Views, fantastic Hotel, great restaurant on site = stellar location”
text:
Its hard to decide what was better; the spacious nice rooms, the helpful and friendly staff, the stellar location close to the bay (as well as the beach and Downtown), the awesome pools, the fantastic food at the Firefly restaurant on site. I consider myself a foodie and was really pleasantly surprised that the food there was above par. Honestly the number one reason I chose this hotel is that it felt more quaint, more boutique than many of the other choices around the bay. With its tropical feel and buildings not higher than two stories, it was perfect. 
I just had my wedding there last month and I couldn't be happier with how the hotel handled my event and my family and friends coming in from all over the world. Everyone was thrilled with the hotel and some have even told me they plan on staying there again when they come to visit us. The location was great for us to be able to plan a full "wedding weekend" of events. We went to Old Town for dinner one night and Saturday during the day we rented bikes from the Dana (very reasonable) and took a bike ride around the Bay. That was one of the best moments of the whole weekend. Forced relaxation! 
Keith Robinson, Director of Catering at the Dana, along with his wonderful staff really made it so easy to have an amazing event there. I really love the giant ballroom they have for events and the serene ceremony site set up along the bay. I'm sure my husband and I will be back for our anniversary. Or perhaps a weekend staycation if I'm lucky! Cheers to the Dana - its nice to have great hotels so close by.

title: “Hurricane Sandy - Plan B”
text:
After 3rd day with no power at home, we bailed and stayed at Embassy Suites near the Phila Airport. Took 2 rooms for family of 5, and were very happy with the rooms, staff, rate and breakfast included in the price.
Great respite in the middle of a bad 2 weeks.

title: “Great Hotel! Very friendly staff!”
text: Both the staff and amenities were beyond my expectations. I very much enjoyed my stay and would certainly return in the future!

title: “Very nice stay”
text: We booked this hotel after the wonderful reviews here on TripAdvisor. The only problem is that with amazing reviews come the potential to be let down! Overall, our stay was great and I would suggest this hotel to anyone. My only hesitation would be to compare this at all to a Ritz or Four Season standard. It does not come close to that, but in this price category it is way above others at this rate. The lobby was confusing and I wasn't even sure who worked there and who didn't, but i had read reviews so I knew to be patient and someone with an iPad on her hand came and helped me. She was very nice (Jessica) and started my weekend off just right with being so kind. I did ask for an upgrade as I've read they are generous with them but was told there wasn't anything available unless I wanted to pay an additional 189.00 which I did not want to do. The room was stunning upon first look. Really big and comfy and totally cool and hip. Upon deeper look, the black tiles were quite dirty and the pillows and bed were not of high standard. The view was of the building across the street so we saw nothing, but thank goodness for the windows as the room was so hot. Our toilet wouldn't stop flushing but my husband fixed it. I don't mean this to sound bad, as I guess it is going that way, but it is just to be honest and frank and again, I would still suggest this hotel to friends, but not to friends or business people who are looking for Ritz quality. We had called the Ritz and could get a similar room there for the same price, but I'm a Hyatt Gold Passport member and between that and the reviews on Trip Advisor we went for it. I don't regret the decision, but I do wish there were a few things that made our stay even more special, as we were looking to be blown away. We did spa treatments which were okay, but expensive including a tip which I was asked to provide--yikes!! Hope that helps and makes sense!

title: “Charming and affordable.”
text: Hotel Rex is one of those great finds--a charming, comfortable hotel in downtown San Francisco. Rhenna at the Front Desk had an amazing memory regarding the guests. And she never seemed to tire of answering their questions. She's a great asset to the hotel.

title: “Great hotel, on beach, centrally located, nice staff”
text:
We spent spring break here in April w/our 2 teenage daughters. Right on the boardwalk with the beach literally 50 feet away. The hotel was freshly painted, clean & included breafast, which is big for us...we then just eat a light lunch & don't waste time looking for places to eat in the morning. I have to say that every hotel staff person we encountered were very friendly and helpful--totally personable & accommodating. The hotel has an outdoor pool, hot tub & lounge chairs, but the kids prefered the beach. The hotel had some beach chairs that other guests had left behind, so they just borrow them out to other guests, which was perfect. We don't have any complaints about the hotel. 
We parked in a private parking garage under the hotel for around $10 a day, which was convenient and no worries about the vehicle, and no hassle looking for parking & hauling things to a beach if you stay off-beach. This was handy since my husband just had foot surgery, so he had to use a knee cart or crutches to get around. Being right on the Boardwalk was handy since we had plenty of restaurants and shops nearby, and he could navigate easily--even go sit on the beach easily. There were surfboard lessons, board/bike rentals available, and even though the surf did come up certain times of the day, plenty of people enjoyed swimming. I also appreciated that the city does not allow smoking and alcohol on the beach, so the beach was clean. 
We weren't familiar witih San Diego and I was worried about traffic, location,safety, etc. No worries once we arrived. The hotel is close to the airport---we had no traffic issues any time all week long. We could zip over to the zoo, Safari Park, airport, Old Town, Gaslamp District in about 15 minutes. We also spent one day touring the Midway Aircraft in the morning, then visiting Coronado Island early afternoon, then up the highway maybe 15 miles to LaJolla to see the baby seals and shop, enjoying great ocean views on the way back to Pacific Beach & our hotel--very easy to navigate and fun to see the nice homes. It's also close to Mission Beach and the pier where kids can ride rides & a golf course. 
I'd highly recommend this centrally located spot for any family. We usually go check out different towns/beaches, usually in Florida or the Caribbean; however I wouldn't mind going back here again and taking and spending a day in LA to take in Universal/Disney/Hollywood, then retreating back to the quiet beach. Even though it's a metro, it didn't feel like it here, and the hotel staff, especially at the front desk, made the trip all the better.

title: “Perfect location”
text:
We -2 adults and a kid- stayed 10 days at the Belleclaire in October and, quite frankly, did not experience any of the troubles other reviewers mentioned. The elevators were working properly and there was tea/coffee when there was supposed to be. The staff was always friendly and helpful.
The room -deluxe double- was big, nicely renovated with very comfortable beds and we did not find the bathroom was that small -in need of some little upgrading maybe. Noise can be a problem, even on 7th floor, but you can't expect quadruple glazing in a historical building. Watching the sun rise over Broadway was enough to make us want to stay in that room.
The hotel is conveniently located close to the subway (79th & 72nd), a crosstown bus to the Upper East (79th) and Central Park. There are a lot a fantastic places to eat -from breakfast to dinner- in the surroundings.
All in all, a very nice hotel in a very nice and friendly neighborhood. 
As with most hotels in big cities like Paris or London, it is still a tad overpriced, but I suppose it is unavoidable.

title: “Excellent location but room was old and needed updating”
text: We stayed here from 3rd to 6th of Feb. Checkin was quick which was great. The room on the other had was a dissapointment and needs an urgent update, the walls need a lick of paint as they had put some filler in to cover some damage but it looked unsightly also in this day and age to be still using shower curtains is unbelievable. For 3 adults it was very small and when we enquired we were told that the room we were in was the biggest they had!!!! On a more positive note the location is spot on right in the thick of it, just what you want when visiting New York. Went to see a couple of shows and would definitely recommend Jeresy Boys excellent entertainment.

title: “Pretty damn good!”
text: Very friendly service. Great atmosphere at the hotel.

title: “Good value, reasonable motel but nothing more”
text: It is probably the cheapest accommodation that is really close to OSU, so the value is good but In overall it's not a very comfortable place to stay. Stil, for limited budget is probably the best solution in the area.

title: “Holiday Inn Charlotte City Center”
text: The hotel was very nice. The suite was spacious and quiet. The only drawback is that the sink area has little to no room to lay any items whist getting ready in the morning/evening.

title: “Loved it.”
text: My husband and I just got back from our stay at the Lakeway Resort and Spa. We had a fabulous time. The staff was nice, the food was pretty good, and the location is awesome. We really enjoyed our stay. The bathrooms could use some updating, but that's really being nit picky. We had a great time.

title: “Excellent Hotel in every way, everyone should stay here.”
text: I had a trip that had been cancelled at the last minute due to flight problems, I was not within the time frame to cancel for a refund at the hotel. The manager, Mike Owen advised that he would honor my reservation at another time. He did not forget me when I needed to reschedule MONTHS later. He went well above and beyond to make my stay pleasant and confortable. He even upgraded my room to a suite. I would strongly recommend this hotel to anyone that is staying in Dallas. Everything about this hotel was top of the line.

title: “Best customer service... best local hotel!”
text:
After learning about a special rate celebrating the 40th birthday of Ben, the hotel owner, I booked two nights at The Clarendon, the first in July the second in November. I had visited the property once before, a few years back when the restaurant on the premises was under different management; I was left with the impression that the hotel looked really cool and fun and I made a mental note to check it out sometime. With the special deal I found, I decided now was the time.
I booked a Jr. Suite for both nights, and my first stay was last night. I checked in early before my boyfriend arrived. Rachel helped me check in and was really friendly and helpful. I took in all the details as I walked to the elevator and then to my room. Really fun, local tilt-shift photography was hung on the walls leading to my room (#221). I wish I had snapped a few photos of my room, because it was really fun - a great king-size bed with a funky, upholstered headboard, dark-wood heavy furniture, a plush occasional chair by a lamp, a long desk/dresser, a 42" (if not bigger) TV anchored to the wall, and awesome blue walls made up the room. Unfortunately, I noticed the room hadn't been cleaned properly. By the Keurig coffee maker, I found a mess of opened sugar packets, creamer, and used swizzle sticks, and no cups or coffee. I called down to the front desk and Rachel answered. I told her what I found, and she came up to check it out. She seemed sincerely disgusted at what she saw and she was very apologetic. She left the room and came back with some cups and went down once again and this time returned with coffee, tea, and a wet rag to wipe down the counter. She also brought a few bags of chips, some candy bars, and four bottles of chilled water. She asked me what else she could do to make up for the mess, but I told her she'd done enough - more than was her responsibility, actually.
Later that evening, after a pretty dismal experience at the Gallo Blanco Cafe, in the hotel lobby, I stopped at the front desk to request some extra towels and some sugar for the coffee. Ben, the owner, happened to be at the desk at the time and told me he heard we'd had a bad experience at the restaurant and asked how our stay had been otherwise. I told him about what happened before in the room and complimented him on having Rachel on his staff. Like Rachel, he was very apologetic and asked what he could do to make up for it. He also told me it had been Rachel's first day, and I couldn't have been more surprised - what an asset to his team! Before we went back upstairs, Ben gave me his card and asked me to let him know when we'd be staying over again so he could upgrade us to a full suite. He then came by the room with a huge stack of freshly laundered towels (they were still warm!) and apologized again and thanked us for our patience. Talk about customer service!
When we checked out, Rachel was back at the front and asked about how our night went. I recapped for her the rest of the events and she again thanked me for our patience and good nature. This is why I support local businesses, especially when they hire amazing people who know how to treat their patrons and guests. For the wonderful customer service we were given, I'm rating this hotel five stars.
Ben and Rachel, THANK YOU for being great. I look forward to our next stay, though I wish I didn't have to wait until November!
P.S. - The amazing AC in the room? What a delight!

title: “Great Hotel love to go back”
text: My husband and I went to NY at the end of July coming from TO. We were celebrating our anniversary and wanted it to be a special long weekend. Based on reviews online we decided to try Bryant Park Hotel. We loved this hotel! Nicole was so pleasant checking us in (and out). Felix considerately upgraded us making things all the more special. Thank you! Thanks also Darren Sumner for the complimentary wine sent to our room. All the staff were gracious and accomodating. The room and bathroom was immaculate. Excellent turn down service and perfect view of the park! Thanks for making our stay so special!

title: “Nice but not great”
text:
This is a hard review to write, there are a lot of things to like about the hotel and some things that make it unlikely for me to stay again when I come to San Diego. the first impressions are very good, nice airy lobby and friendly staff. I was here for a conference and the staff knew where they were setting up. Check in staff was friendly and remembered my name when I came back to the lobby to check out where the restaurant was. The rooms are clean and the bed is comfortable. The desk is decently equipped for working. Wireless Internet is has a good signal on my floor or at least in my room. The bed is comfortable. The pool area is pleasant and there are plenty of clean towels. There are some nice touches in the room like toothpaste in the bathroom. There was an air conditioning problem with my room that was fixed quickly when I reported it. There are several modestly priced decent restaurants in the area
Now for the less then desirable, valet parking is $25 a day and self park only a little less. This isn't downtown its in the middle of a bunch of apartment complexes. The bathrooms are nice but there is no ventilation in them and the doors close automatically so it smells damp all the time, not bad but I wouldn't be surprised if they have mildew problems. The restaurant is really expensive. No free Internet, again what I expect from a non downtown hotel. The final nit is there is not a comfortable chair/footstool in the room, the two armchairs were functional at best but not meant for relaxing.
So all in all not a bad place with a very courteous staff, but unlikely to win my business from the downtown Sheraton Suites at symphony hall which has the problem with valet parking but none of the other issues.

title: “Loved it, would stay again”
text: good area where the inn was. So many restaurnats and other places next door, friendly staff, nice room, cheap.

title: “Great location & price but needs a real makeover”
text:
When i booked this hotell for my NY trip i actually had to send an email just to ensure that the price was right, and it was! 
When u pay 218$ for 3 nights total for 2 adults for a manhattan hotel it must be a bargain. The location was just perfect with the park across the street, and not that many tourists around. Local breakfast at some of the nearby cafès is recommended. The metro is just around the corner to take you quickly downtown.
Our room was situated on the 7th floor and had a "park view". The elevator was a trip of its own but safely took us up and down, but we had to walk a couple of times downstairs because of staff used it when cleaning the rooms and it took ages.
The room itself was nothing to cheer about. Small, clean and out of date is three good words to discribe it.
The main problem was the combination of heat and the loudness of the aircondition.
Outside it was below freezing but our room was a sauna, and when the aircon was on it was like living in a construction site.
There was a pipe in our room that was so hot, we were actually a bit worried that it could lite the room on fire.
My conclusion is that i actually enjoyed my stay despite the sauna and noise from the aircon, we got "used" to it and we didnt go to NY to stay in our room.
Location and price was why we booked this hotell and i would do it again!

title: “Great hotel, fresh design”
text:
Spent a couple of nights there on a Rocky Mountain trip - what a great hotel! Its location is perfect, in a great area for wandering around. The bathrooms were very modern - glass sinks lit from behind made for a cool glowing effect and the rock wall behind the tub really fit the local style. I'm now hooked on TVs built into mirrors too. The pool was great and the hot tub nice and toasty. Housekeeping added the little touches.
The Edge bar is an extremely happening place on Friday nights - was great to sit and watch some games, eat some great food with excellent drinks among an upscale crowd. The bar tenders were top notch too.

title: “Disappointed!!”
text: Our family of recently stayed at this "resort" hilton hotel for the first time. Expecting it to be like other Hilton resorts, we planned to enjoy the pool and other featured amenities of this hotel. Therefore, we only went to Legoland on this trip, with the plan of coming back to enjoy the hotel with our 6 and 7 year old girls. The room was nice and clean when we arrived. However, on the second day, when we returned in the evening, we were surprised to find our room had not been cleaned and a message was left from housekeeping. They said we had a sign on our door, and if we wanted our room cleaned to call them. Well, it was 9:00 p.m. and we were checking out before 6 the next moring. So, we just called for fresh towels and for our trash to be emptied. The beds were still in disarray. Lastly, as we were checking out on Oct. 8, we called for assistance with our luggage to the front desk at 5:00 a.m.. At that time we were asked if we had our ticket number for our car validation, so that they could get the car. We waited for 20 minutes and no one showed up to assist with our luggage. So, my husband made two trips to bring our luggage to the front desk area, while I stayed in the room with our two girls. When we finally all got to the valet area, we were surprised again... no car!! It had been 30 minutes, with no one else checking out, they could not find our car!! I expressed my disappointment to the front desk, who were very apologetic. I would definitely not be staying there again. Our friends were planning to stay there next summer, I will convince them to stay elsewhere.

title: “NYC luxury that wont break bank”
text: Everything about the London is terrific with the exception of the unprofessional and icy cold front desk staff. The rooms,location,food doormen and bell staff are wondeful. If they could just teach the front desk staff how to treat guests it would be a gem. Unfortunately they greet you as if they are doind you a big favor by checking you in.

title: “Great location for tourists, tired rooms in Annex”
text: If the rating was solely based on location, I'd give this hotel a 5. Parking is hard to find and costs $40/night even for hotel guests. If you can get having a car out of your mind, this is a great location. You can walk to Fisherman's Wharf and many other tourist spots. One end of the streetcar line is behind the hotel and cable car lines are an easy walk. It was a bit further to North Beach, but easily doable. Numerous dining/entertainment options are also near by. The rooms in the Beach Street annex, where we were, are tired and need updating. Internet access is so slow I wonder if the whole annex connects over a dial-up line. If you want to use the hotel pool, it's a block walk down the street to the main hotel. Still, if you are out and about all day, this would be a great place to stay.

title: “Cute hotel for a great price, walking distance to major attractions/metro”
text:
Stayed at this hotel on a whim for $89! We went over Labor Day weekend and I couldn't believe how convenient their website is and how easy it was to get a reservation with less than a week before booking. 
My friend and I expected a small, ok... very small, city hotel room with maybe a few amenities. Boy was I surprised when we were upgraded (for free, no fee) to a California King size room with a small kitchenette and very large bathroom! The room included access to a wonderful pool! It was across the street from a park, within a few blocks of a major metro station, and in a nice neighborhood overall. The only complaint we had was that the staff members were a little pushy trying to sell the trolley tours, but that's part of their job. Hotel rooms are stocked with Bath and Body Works, which is always fun when it's a group of gals traveling together. 
Lots of conventions and big groups stay here and I see why! Overall, a great time! I highly recommend you save some money staying here to use it on the attractions! Will return when I'm in DC again.

title: “We Were There for Hurricane Sandy”
text:
The Kitano is a great hotel in a superb location. Close to Grand Central Station and The Empire State Building. Rooms are very nice and clean, with comfy beds and a good bathroom. Our room had a great view of ESB. The Restaurant is great quality, if a little pricey, but you're obviously free to eat at lower cost restaurants close by.
We arrived the day before the storm hit, and unfortunately lost power and consequently hot water, at about 8pm on Monday. Hotel management briefed guests, and provided glow lamps to help, relying on emergency generator power for essential services only. 
The hotel provided complimentary cold buffet breakfasts, and did all they could to help the guests, in spite, I'm sure of significant personal problems as a result of the storm. They were really 1st class.
We left before things returned to normal, as power had not been reconnected.
Would we return under normal circumstances?......yes, with no hesitation.

title: “Great hotel amd location”
text:
Very good hotel in walking distance to most attractions. Hotel staff were very helpful.
Spent a few nights here at start of holiday - one question - why does it now seem to be the 'normal' thing to have a window looking into the shower /toilet from the bedroom...this is not the first one i have found, and its wrong!!
Nice rooftop bar, bar downstairs with live music, very plush overall - would return...

title: “Amazingly good!”
text: We recently stayed at the newly renovated Milford Plaza over the holidays and were a little skeptical before arriving -- after all, who gets a quality hotel room in New York City for $99.00? Answer -- WE did! We were there for a long weekend and were amazed at the quiet, clean and well-appointed room with a large-screen TV, safe, iron and board, hair dryer, personal amenities in the bathroom, wonderful shower with great water pressure, and more than adequate lighting. The staff was very accommodating, anything requested of housekeeping appeared immediately, the doorman unfailingly delivered cabs upon a minute's request, and the lobby featured free boaring pass print-outs and a very helpful concierge desk. The bed was extremely comfortable and afforded a wonderful night's sleep. Express check-out featured a copy of our paid bill delivered under the door the night before and a key drop near the front desk. All in all, a fantastic experience! We'll stay there again!

title: “Best Hotel in NYC”
text: I have stayed at Gild Hall many, many times in the past 6 months. I felt I needed to share what a wonderful Hotel this is. The staff is wonderful, professional, informative and most important - polite!! The rooms are large by NYC standards, beds are extremely comfortable and my room has always been clean and NEVER had a bed bug problem...something you need to be very careful of in NYC. There is a very quaint bar which is always welcoming as well as the dining area. This hotel is located very close to the subway, and cabs are easy to get as well. I highly recommend this hotel for business or personal travel to the City. I have stayed here for 6+ months and will continue to book only this hotel no matter where I am visiting in the city!

title: “May 2008, $195 per night..”
text:
I booked this room last minute, three days before depature, Rm 503. Great location. This room directly overlooked 23rd street. It was noisey and you constantly heard traffic, shouting ; ect. I'd highly recommend call the hotel directly for reservations. I filled out the online reservation form twice and got no reply. dont even think about checking in early. From what I understand, check out is late and the maid staff also comes in late. My room wasnt ready until 2pm and this was on a friday check in. The breakfast: I read many comments like.."great coffee" , "mmm coffee out of this world" ect ... but it tasted like standard generic coffee to me. Dont execpt eggs, pancakes... its all bread items , sweet and non sweet. Hotel had a hard time keeping bread and coffee stocked!
Room 503 is double bed , with TV , air con and a private bathroom. Right across from the elevator. The room was clean and smelled nice. My bathroom light didnt work when I finally checked in and it was changed in under 10 minutes. 
This is a nice location between the subway #1 and C,E train lines. I'd highly recommend the bake shop on the corner of 8th & 23rd. There are plenty of places to eat around the hotel (boston market, cuban resturant; ect) but I liked the mango/papaya spot that was diagonal across (23 & 7th).

title: “The Best Hotel in Hell's Kitchen.”
text: This is a great hotel all the way around. I have stayed at both Ink48 and Kimpton's other new property, Eventi, and found both to be amazing properties, but The rooftop bar and larger rooms at Ink48 win me over. This is an ideal hotel for other New Yorkers like myself, who are currently living away but like to come back home and visit. It's private, away from all the tourists and in one of the coolest neighborhoods in the city. I thought the staff was very nice, but respected your privacy while being attentive to your needs, everything is high-end but not stuffy and the bathrooms are amazing, with a shower and a garden tub, double sinks and ultra comfortable beds. I can't say enough good things.

title: “Great facility, terrible service”
text:
The good: The facility is great. The rooms are nice, the bars are wonderful, the food is great. 
The bad: First, I booked with the American Express platinum service AND I am a Hilton a diamond level. That is just so you know if anything, you will be treated worse that we were. 
Arrived at noon for the "early check in if available" benefit. Was told that our room was not quite Ready but they would call my cell phone as soon as it was available. They called me at 3:40. I do not believe for a minute that there was no way for them to prioritize the room for somebody already checked in. I also do not believe that they really monitor anything, they just simply call in a batch at 3:30 or so. 
The food/beverage service at the pool was awful. The server was working very hard, but they were clearly understaffed on this spring break weekend. Also, there were chairs around us with used towels for 3 hours and nobody came to clean up during that entire time. 
At one of the restaraunts we waited for 20 minutes at our table with no server. I had to go to the bar myself twice to get drinks, and the bartender said he would send somebody to our table. 20 minutes later the server arrived. The food was OK. 
Finally for anybody planning to use he American Express amenities, this is the only place I have stayed where the resort credit benefit has to be used in one shot. So, if I have $50 of drinks at the pool and spend $80 at dinner, I can ony apply the $100 voucher to the dinner and loose the $20 from the voucher.

title: “Very Nice Stay”
text:
I recently stayed at this hotel for a conference and can honestly say it is one if the nicer hotels I have visited in a long time. The staff was outstanding. The night I arrived, I asked for a room with a view of the city, but the hotel was full, so we had a view of a roof. The next day, the front desk called to let me know that a room would be available by 3 PM. The second room was exactly like the first except that it had a nice view. Both rooms were clean and comfortable. . .and quiet. The beds were confortable, too. The lobby is nice and there is a Starbucks there that is convenient for grabbing a coffee between conference sessions. Also on the same level as the lobby is a bar. The food is ok, but the service is pretty slow and the food is expensive. There is also a restaurant on the second floor, which I didn't eat at because it was expensive ($20 for breakfast). Just outside of the hotel (actually connected) there is a mall with several restaurants and a food court. The Italian restaurant and the pub are very good and the prices are reasonable. There is an IHOP express in the food court that is great for breakfast. .. .$11 for two of us - we shared the pancake breakfast (4 pancakes). The Riverwalk is lovely and be sure to take the boat tour. Up the steps from the Riverwalk is Alamo Plaza where you will find, of course, the Alamo. Across the street from the Alamo is a group of fun things like a wax museum, Ripley's Believe it or not, etc. A pass for all 6 attractions is about $50, but it's $20 each if you don't buy the pass. The pass is good for a year. There is also a little candy shop with a mirror maze and a lazer game which are pretty fun, especially for kids. If you walk further down (or take a cab) you can also go to Market Square where you can buy all sorts of souvenirs, and have really good Mexican food. The Tower of the Americas is the opposite direction, and you can go up and see the whole city. Frankly, if you flew into San Antonio, you saw it anyway . .I wouldn't do that again.
If you rented a car or have transportation, the zoo isn't too far and there is a botanical graden near the zoo that is free, and amazing. Another great attraction was the Natural Bridge Caverns which is well worth your time.

title: “Good Business Hotel”
text:
Stayed here for a 5-day business trip to Boston. All in all a decent venue.
Positive: Nice clean and spacious rooms, comfortable beds, big bathrooms, great service, good location (not far from Fenway park, about a 15 minute bus ride to downtown), shuttle service from the airport.
Negative: Very loud (you hear the traffic from the 2 crossing streets and ambulances that go in and out of the nearby hospital), pricy (about 1100$ for 5 nights), not the best breakfast buffet, had a stain on my bed sheets one day after they were changed in the morning.
Not the best 3-star hotel I have stayed at, but ok for a short trip.

title: “Disappointed traveler”
text: I rented a room at this hotel through Hotwire.com, and although I got a good price in general, the hotel did not come close to living up to its 3.5-star rating on that site. The location is excellent (right at the airport), but the rooms and corridors are shabby. We had a king-sized bed, which was comfy, and a sofabed, which was tattered, poor in quality, and very uncomfortable. The blanket had a hole in it the size of a plum, the wallpaper was old and out-of-date and tattered, the toilet seat was discolored, and the general quality of the room was more like that of a 1.5 or 2-star hotel. However, the staff was great and very responsive. Next time, though, I will choose a different airport hotel. Don't plan on staying at this one again.

title: “Great location, good hotel”
text:
We picked the Catamaran based mainly on location. And its location is perfect - right on Mission Blvd and a block from the boardwalk and beach.
It took us only 10 minutes to get to Sea World by car, and we walked everywhere else. Parking was an extra $12/day (for non-valet), and the parking garage offered convenient access to the tower and other buildings.
We stayed in the tower (third floor). The room was clean, and we had no problems. The room could have used updating, but we felt it was a pretty decent value considering the hotel's location and the price we paid (approx $250/night). The walls seemed thin, as we could hear a lot of noise; however, once we turned the wall a/c unit on, we couldn't hear any external noise.
We did not use any of the hotel's amenities, so I can't comment on that. The spa and restaurant looked nice from the outside. The hotel staff was always courteous, but we didn't have a whole lot of interaction with them, as we were out and about most of the weekend.
If you stay here and want a great breakfast, head about 1/2 mile south on Mission Blvd to "The Mission". We had a spectacular meal there, and will definitely return next time we're in San Diego.

title: “Immaculate - Friendly and Helpful Staff”
text:
Earlier this summer, I wanted to book an overnight local getaway because there was work being done on my house in Phoenix. I found a great price at this location and booked it.
Having checked prior Tripadvisor reviews, I was aware of the possibility of highway noise. So, I asked for a room facing away from the highway and that made all the difference! 
The room was immaculate and very comfortable! At this location, the rooms really do look like the photos on the Website. (That isn't always the case.) The bed was so comfortable that I didn't want to leave. Actually, I was quite content to hang out in the room to finish up a work assignment. Breakfast was, as another reviewer had commented, healthy - with a varied selection.
I gather, from the location - near a suburban North Phoenix office park, that this hotel caters mostly to a business clientele. I was there on a weekend and it was moderately busy. All the staff were most friendly and helpful - providing the feeling of a smaller boutique hotel.
This is a terrific place to stay. (Just remember to book a room facing away from the highway.) You won't regret your decision!

title: “NOSSR CONFERENCE”
text: This is a decent hotel, you definatly do not get what you would expect to get paying the prices that they ask. Also make sure if you drive you are prepared to pay $41 a night!!! that was a shock to the system during a 5 night stay. the restaruant had alright food pricey but all in all ok. the morning staff for the restaruant was sort of rude! My friend was in the middle of ordering and as she was still talking he turned to me and wanted my order. Also he came to refill the water glass splashed ice and water on the table didnt say sorry excuse me or anything. then when the order was brought to the table it was totally wrong. so I would probably steer clear of the morning staff in the Coldwater bar and grill within the restaruant.

title: “Exceptional value. Great location!”
text:
Stayed here on a quick trip into the city December 2011.
The price was amazing, for what you get. The rooms are comfortable, modern, with that "design" feel. The rooms are very clean, and the bath amenities nice. The hotel opened in 2007, so things still work. And the location is great, close to Soho, and with the F train subway at the door.
Plus, the free continental breakfast is nice (but the yogurt was expired... likely just an oversight).
My only complaint was the free WiFi. It didn't work, and despite asking 4 different employees about it, and them resetting it, it never worked! I was left having to steal WiFi from an unsecured network in the area, which was spotty at best.

title: “The Good, the Bad not much Ugly...”
text:
In town for conference. First, great facilities for having meetings, well laid out and easy to get to. No complaints there.
The Room: You have to pay extra for the City View but it was worth it! Saw the Navy Pier and the fireworks, watched the Bears Game at Soldier Field on the stadium Jumbo-tron, great night views of the skyline.!No frig in room and I cannot believe they charge for Internet access! $10.00 per day! The beds were soft and very comfortable and the rooms are "surface clean" ( just don't drop anything behind the bed YIKES!). Quiet and relaxing otherwise.
The Food: Bring Fort Knox reserves with you if you eat here. Very pricey and not so great. My steak was tough and charred on one side and the other menu items I ordered were mediocre at best. The front desk will give the menus of restaurants that deliver and they are worth the $2.85 delivery charge. Guidanno's (sp?) and a Chinese place nearby are very tasty and the delivery was fast. There is a Starbuck's there and a small bag of Chex mix is $4.50.
Transportation: The hotel has a shuttle that will take you to the Navy Pier, the Watertower Area and downtown but won't bring you back. Cabs ranged from $10.00 to $15.00. Too far away to walk anywhere. Next time I will stay downtown.
Recreation: Went to Shedd Aquarium. Buy your tickets online and avoid the HUGE lines of people w/o tickets. Very nice and well worth the price. So was the Field Musuem. The Navy Pier was fun and be sure to take a spin in the Ferris Wheel. 
All in all, a good hotel just hindered by its unfortunate location,
overpriced, unfortunate food. Great for conferences though.

title: “Beautiful View from my room...”
text: The hotel is in a central location. It's very beautiful and I had a great room overlooking the Betsy Ross Bridge. The only problem with the hotel is that the highway runs right below the hotel. I was on the 22nd floor and I could hear the traffic from below.

title: “Well used average hotel.”
text:
A nice hotel but showing signs of wear and tear in the rooms . Bathroom in particular could do with a refurb. A bit old fashioned .
I had travelled from LA to Chicago on a route 66 motorcycle trip and stayed in hotels and motels coxing from $45 to $140, all of which supplied free wi fi and the majority had a free breakfast. I paid over $200 per night for this hotel with no free breakfast and charged $12 per 24 hrs for use of the hotel wi fi system. A bit mean when you consider I could walk 200 yards down the road to a nickel and dime burger joint where the wi fi is free.. !

title: “Fabulous! Modern, sophisticated and comfortable”
text: Our company just used this site for a conference. The hotel itself was beautiful - smaller, with a modern, sleek look and comfortable feel. The staff was friendly, helpful and always available. We really enjoyed our stay and felt we received exceptional treatment by every member of the hotel team. We've already booked another workshop there for the fall. Highly recommend!

title: “Great location and service”
text:
Spent a weekend with my sister and daughter at the Warwick. Lovely spacious room and excellent service. Nothing is too much trouble for the hotel staff from cashing traveller's cheques to advising on all aspects of exploring the city.
The Warwick is in a great location - 5 minute walk to Times Square, 5th Avenue with all the fabulous shops, 10 mins to Grand Central Station, Chrysler Building. 20 mins to Empire State Building and Macys.
Cocktails in the Randolph Hearst Bar a must!
Great value and central location.

title: “Brilliant stay”
text: My girlfriend and I stayed here in April for our anniversary. Hotel reception were extremely helpful and friendly, excellent location for hotel and was a very reasonable price. We have recommended this hotel to friends and will definately stay again, next time we're in New York

title: “Careless stuff and cheating with prices”
text: I would not recommend this hotel at all. Firstly, I reserved a room through internet for $65, but several hours later when I checked in I was told that the only room they have left in the hotel cost 144 and they are willing to give it to me for 99. Well, that was pretty late at night and eventually I paid $113 instead of planned $65 for one night. Pretty unexpected for a budget hotel. Secondly, the lady at the front desk was incredibly rude with me all time. It was first time ever in the US I felt that the hotel stuff did not care about their guests. Thirdly, when I got into my room and wanted to call to front desk and ask for a wireless password I found out that the phone in my room did not work. I came downstairs to ask for a password and she was rude again when I told her about the phone. She said I was not the first person who told her about the problem and they are working on it. Well, it was not a reason to raise a voice when speaking to me. Finally, on my way back to fourth floor I saw that the door - access to the roof was open and anyone (a child, for example) can easily get there and there was no wall in between next building and a hotel. It was an absolutely dangerous place and open access to it, and nobody seemed to care about that. Overall, even a pretty big hole on the curtains in my room and lack of available parking did not discourage me more about the hotel than its careless stuff, cheating with prices and rude with customers.

title: “Nice property”
text: After reading the reviews, I was expecting the Capital Hilton to be pretty bad. On the contrary, it was quite nice. The room was spacious and clean and had all the usual comforts including Crabtree & Evelyn products. The property is older, which can be seen in the details. I agree it doesn't quite seem to be a 4-star property. However, the public spaces are beautiful and every employee was exceptionally friendly and helpful. I will stay here again.

title: “Great hotel - Beware of the honor bar”
text: Very nice hotel. Very friendly staff. If you so much as pick something up from the honor bar and place it back within seconds it shows up on the bill. Staff is nice to fix it but its a bit embarrassing. All in all great location and a Very nice hotel. Bar 10 staff is not the friendliest and the service I poor. Again the staff that really matters is great !

title: “Weekend at the Fairmont in San Francisco”
text: Vermont Bike Tours placed my group at the Fairmont for the weekend before a week of cycling in the Sonoma area. The elegant, impressive hotel makes a striking first impression with the gorgeous marble and stone interiors and beautiful, spacious public rooms. Then comes the unpleasant, constant dinging for maximum profits from hotel services. Coffee service is a sore point as the Fairmont forces patrons into an inconveniently located venue for pricy coffee, beverages and pickup breakfast items beginning at 7 a.m. More understandable are the $15 glasses of wine in the main gathering area but no less abrasive. Our shuttle for transport to Sonoma was not until 1:30 p.m. on Sunday, and I was told by the front desk that the 12 o' clock check out was in cement. I understood that, but not the agressive, obnoxious cleaning attendant who knocked on my door 3 times Sunday morning to come in and clean the room. There are a range of very nice hotels in the Nob Hill area. I will certainly be looking at another place to stay next time out.

title: “First Class, Fair Price, Very Accommodating”
text:
My wife is a finickity traveler, so I booked this room near the GORGEOUS railroad station with a feeling of mild apprehension. We were en route to State College where my youngest daughter was being awarded a PhD and this was our first stop after a weather-troubled and delayed flight from Seattle. I am in my 80th year and she's 15 years younger.
Arriving late, we moved into our room (compact, tidy, well appointed) and the young desk clerk directed us to a nearby restaurant ($5 by taxi) for an abbreviated dinner. The neighborhood was fairly busy with young college students still out. Returning near midnight, we crashed into one of the nicest, warmest beds we've enjoyed in years. 
The fried potatoes at breakfast could have been cooked a little longer, but the service was very good and warranted a nice tip. 
Next time I'm in Philly, THIS is where I'll stay! My wife was a happy camper; what more could you ask for?

title: “Perfect hotel in Detroit”
text: This hotel is located in the heart of Greektown, downtown Detroit. A very safe area. Greektown is filled with wonderful restaurants and bars and plenty of nearby attractions. The casino is adjoining the hotel and easily accessible. My room was on the 29th floor with a splendid view of Detroit river and city. I love the room decor and had a great snooze during my stay. Great for couples or families.

title: “Good Location, Good Service, A bit pricey”
text: Ok for the not so good news-- the price was $200/night during the week, when there was no major conference in town. Now for the good news -- the hotel was clean, staff was pleasant and accomodating, Philadelphia's downtown is very walkable and despite troubling crime rates...I felt safe walking from my meetings after 10pm nightly. I didn't eat in the hotel (I seldom do in a city the size of Phily) so I can't comment on that. However, several coffee shops and chain restaurants were closeby in the Market Street area. If I stay again, I will shoot for a much better price. It shouldn't be over $149/night.

title: “Great Value for money”
text:
Stayed at the Arlington from Feb. 7-9, 2004.
Start with a caveat. If you want an awesome hotel, with a spa and a doorman and that looks after your every whim. Look elsewhere. The Arlington is for the person on a budget that wants good value for money.
My two nights at the Arlington cost $85 each, which is a great price for a double bed and a private bathroom and really great maid service in mid-town Manhattan. No complaints about the bed - it was nice and firm. No complaints about smells, bugs, or poor furniture. The place was nice and clean and smelled fresh.
The location is almost perfect. Within a longish walk to central park and a longish walk to the tip of Manhattan. If you're in good shape, you can walk to almost all of the major sites in New York without ever taking a taxi or a subway. The neighbourhood that the hotel is in itself is nothing to write home about, but it's a five minute subway ride to the Village, Soho, Chinatown... well, basically every cool neighbourhood in town.
The place isn't perfect - no onsite parking, no tub, slightly worn look to the walls and carpets, ever so slightly dodgy street (nothing I'd worry about, though), slight wait for hot water, and thin walls. These deficiencies are more than made up for with the price, solid value, and fabulous location.

title: “Ugly & unhygienic plus a rude manager”
text: I never had a proper sleep during my 3 days of my stay here. The room was awful. The room service doesn't happen on time and sometime they do forget to do it. It happened to me on the first day, I went to the manager and complained about it. He was so rude and told me I could vacate the room if I wanted to. This is the first time any hotel manager has every talked to me like this. I would definitely NOT recommend anyone to stay at this hotel. Even if it means you need to spend few more bucks, its wise to stay at the near by Marriott or Hilton.

title: “This is a Sheraton and that it?”
text: I was there for one night! This is a good hotel, well located but really crowded when I was there (people for christmas), so all employees were really busy and stressed! the room was ok and the pillow really good! I slept well but the "fire detector" or whatever lnked to security on the wall in the room was really noisy!!! the wall between rooms are so bad isolated that you can hear all the noise from others! I recommend this hotel for the location and the global service quality, but if you need to have a rest be careful when you choose your room!!!

title: “Past and Future”
text: We stayed at the St. Regis last year with our toddler son and had absolutely phenomenal service from point of entry to exit. Everyone was most accommodating and as one might guess, traveling with a toddler is not always easy. The front desk was quite kind and the restaurant helpful in allowing us to eat while our room was readied (we arrived early). The room itself (Astor suite) was fabulous and quite spacious. Extremely clean which is most important to our family. We can't wait to stay here again - during the month of December. Thus far the staff has once again been enormously accommodating and helpful as we arrange our upcoming stay. Can't say enough great things about the quality and service of this establishment.

title: “Nice hotel but have too work on somethings”
text:
I think this is a very cool and trendy hotel. I choosed this hotel beacause the pool and the rooptoopbar. I liked our rom is was nice and a nice bed. Its was quiet at nights.
Our first day the pool was closed beacause they had been a party the day before and the pool was still dirty. 
But i think that your staff have to work on your communications. I really wanted to go too se the rooftoop bar. Wee stayed here for tree nightds and every night it was closed early in the evning for private parties. Its was no letter in our rooms that told us u couldnt go there i hade really looking forward for it. Later after around 22 it opens again but then u had to be on the list beacause we are tourist we arent. I asked the front desk two times for help to go there but they sad the have outsourced it and couldnt help us. We got no information that u can go to marquee from the front desk. One night when I tried to go too the rooptop bar one of the guard sad the it was a private party but in a couple of minutes we could go up. We wanted for 40 minutes and then we were tolf no you cant u most be on the list.. I think its rude too waste our time like that i talked to the front desk and they just sad that they are sorry. I have lived on a lots of lyxiors hotel and it have never been a problem to go too their bar o club in other cities. If u go here don´t except too se the rooptopbar.

title: “Excellent location and structure”
text: I stayes at the Hilton Times Square for 7 nights as part of a business trip to NY. The king room was big, comfortable bed, good working desk, and the amenities you would expect from a Hilton. Breakfast was not included in rate, as well as wifi internet at the room. I paid for both. Must say that I would expect a larger buffet for the value paid and at a Hilton. There was for example no space for a toaster, and I just noticed at the second day a sign informing that you should request for the waiter to have your bagel warmed. Other than that, a great hotel, adequate to the rate billed. Fast and realible wifi internet, try to get a rate that includes it.

title: “I don't know what some people want!!!”
text: We have just returned from our 5th visit to New York and our 3rd time staying at the Wellington. Once again we had a great stay. On our first visit we were given a room on the 23rd floor and subsequently always asked for a room on this floor since and our request has always been granted. The hotel is certainly the best value and in the best location of the ones I have tried, the staff are always friendly and helpful in particular the bellboys (men). I am not sure what some of the people reviewing on here want, not being able to fit 2 people side by side in a corridor is in my opinion a ridiculous comment and not one that has any relevance to a hotels ability's or amenities!!! I would have no problem recommending this hotel to anyone and have done so on many occasions. We personally took friends with us on this trip who had not been before and they also enjoyed it. We will certainly be visiting again soon and are already looking forward to it, the only reason I rate everything bar the location as very good is there is always room for improvement, even in the best hotels!

title: “lovely”
text: Fitzgerald Hotel Union Square is a very lovely hotel with an excellent location. We enjoyed staying there. Nice design, high standard facilities, not expensive.

title: “I was very impressed at the efficiency and greeting which I had by your deskclerk Louise Rechlis.”
text:
I had the occassion to stay at this hotel and when I checked in I was greeted by the staff at check in. The person who checked me in was very fast and efficient and handled my check in in a very effiicient way. I was in my room alot faster than I expected. She was polite and friendly and I asked her name. She told me her name was Louise Rechlis. She seems to know her business and is an asset to this hotel. It is a pleasure to see someone with a smile and disposition as Louise. I had a good stay and would recommend this hotel as a very comfortable place to stay in NY. It even had a lap swimming pool.
BOB, Vergennes, Vermont

title: “Will keep going back”
text:
My husband and I have now stayed at the Inn at El Gaucho twice and each time has been extremely pleasant. We originally booked a room for after our wedding and the staff was incredible (although a bit slow for off-hours food requests). The rooms are warmly lit, the beds are extremely comfortable, the robes are very nice, and the sitting area great for your morning cup of coffee or just an afternoon nap. It isn't a scene, which is quite nice after a disappointing stay at the W in Seattle. The Inn is private, small and discrete - perfect for our mini-honeymoon.
Our second trip just concluded as we needed a quick stop over in the city. The staff remembered us by name and upgraded our room upon arrival. We had drinks downstairs and the waitstaff brought them up for us when we were ready to retire. We needed to leave earlier than the first breakfast delivery time, so they brought us our coffee and breakfast early without us asking for it. It is now the only hotel (aside from the Willow's Lodge) in the Seattle area that we will stay.

title: “Not for me”
text:
I know all the rooms in NYC are small, but this bed has to turn into a futon for you to walk in the room. Therefore the bed isn't comfortable at all, which to me is the most important thing. 
Also, the music is extremely loud on the fourth floor. You couldn't even talk to the person next to you. 
For what it is, it's pretty good. However, this hotel is super nichey. I don't fall in their target market so I was left wanting. If you want an ultra trendy nightclub hotel, it will be your go to. If you want a good nights sleep and to relax after a hard day, try elsewhere.

title: “Perfect Location, Great Amenities, Lush Landscaping”
text: Staying at the Red Lion was a pleasant surprise. The room was cozy and I enjoyed having a microwave and fridge for restaurant leftovers since we stayed for 1 week and for drinks. My family and I took advantage of the shuttle services to the mall and trolley station in Old Town. If you want to go to the North Coast, you can hop on the Coaster for $5 one way and beat traffic...that is a beautiful ride especially when you see Torrey Pines beach. The main restaurant downstairs had good Kona coffee and desserts. They just renovated the sushi bar and outdoor lighting and exterior paint. You can see they are trying to make the effort to maintain the establishment. Someone was having a fun wedding in the middle courtyard one night. My 3-year-old loved the koi ponds and waterfalls..they are gorgeous. There is a laundry room which came in handy at the end of the trip. The Bath and Body Works toiletries were very nice..better than the generic stuff you normally get. Most of the staff were very friendly and accommodating..all but the front desk staff. I'm thinking that since it's such a big hotel, they are tired of their jobs so it is difficult for them to be jovial. However, being as that the front desk personnel are the first impressions one would have of the hotel, it would be a definite plus for many of them to work on their hospitality. A lot of people work hard to make it to San Diego and take a vacation, so it's nice when you are greeted in a classy manner rather than just a number. I would give it 5 dots, but I've seen impeccable hotels so I save my 5 dots for those. The Red Lion has a lot to offer, and as a mother, I think it's wonderful for kids.

title: “Convenient aiport stay”
text: This is a very convenient airport hotel, not a destination hotel by any means, but a perfectly good place if you need to remain close to the airport. The shuttle bus arrived promptly, and it takes under 5 min journey time to get to the hotel. I stayed in a double-roomed suite - very comfortable bed, good large bathroom, separate seating area. The views are typical airport humdrum, but then again, you aren't exactly here for the view. Wireless internet connection is slow and erratic. Short walk across the park to the Airport T stop. Breakfast area looks a bit tired and could do with a revamp, but food quality is acceptable and staff are friendly and helpful. I have stayed here twice in the last 3 years (both business trips), and will definitely be staying here again - A+ for airport convenience!

title: “Great city, terrible motel”
text:
Booked this place for 10 days. Rude staff, filthy room. Had a amazing time in LA so i wasn't too bothered about staying here. Even went to stay with some friends for a few days. I come from a dodgy part of London so the area the motel is in didn't bother me too much, and walking is good for you, so that was ok. Got around by bus & metro really well by calling the MTA helpline and they plan your journey for you. 
The staff at the motel were very unhelpful & rude. And as for the room..had it ever been cleaned? As for a fridge in the room..
Didn't bother with the 'coffee and doughnuts' as there's a pretty cool cafe down just a few minutes away.
Do yourself a favour and pay a few extra bucks and stay somewhere decent.
The liquor store across the street was convinient though!

title: “An unfortunate experience”
text: I thought the hotel was exceptionally friendly and courteous and I enjoyed my stay overall. The service provided by the concierge, desk staff, and overall staff were great. But, unfortunately I had one problem that was not dealt with well and it has made me unlikely to return to the hotel in the future. On Tuesday, 11/13, I returned to my room shortly after 4 pm to find that my room had not been serviced! I was upset (to say the least) especially since I had been at a conference where I had to leave about 6 a.m. and finding my room in its state was the least of things I wanted to deal with. I called the service line and was told casually that the staff had until 4:30 to finish rooms and that there was little that could be done. I did not get her name, but I was not pleased to get her message. I am supposedly a starwood preferred guest, and this did not seem like preferential treatment. I called the desk again at 4:30, this time talked with Bogdan who told me someone would be there to address the problem within 10 minutes. I called back at 4:40 and was told that he would talk with the housekeeping supervisor and would get back to me. At 5:00 as I was on my way out the door, Julie, the supervisor called my room, told me a crew was finally on the way, and that she could offer me a cocktail or an appetizer for my inconvenience. I told her that would not resolve the situation, but since I had to leave the room for it to be cleaned, I would accept this, but still wanted some kind of explanation (since she claimed she did not know why my room had been overlooked). I then went down to the front desk and spoke to the supervisor there (I did not write down her name). She was on the line with Julie when I came to the desk, she then spoke to me, I told her my concerns and that I wanted some explanation. I was assured that someone would contact me the next day with an explanation. She also offered me a cocktail or appetizer, and I went to Grant's Grill and had a glass of wine. When I returned the room had been serviced. On Wednesday my room was serviced before noon, but no one contacted me with any further information or explanations. My room had also been serviced late on Saturday, 11/10, but when the person giving out water came by, and I asked when my room would be serviced, he had a crew sent right away.
