With rates of $249 + a day, this is absolutely not acceptable. In my experience I pay for comfort, courteous service, and cleanliness. Having to wait until after 5 pm and having to make multiple calls to get my room serviced is not preferential treatment and is not appreciated.

title: “Great service - great staff - great location”
text: I recently planned a week-long conference at the Curtis. All arrangements were made long-distance and by phone and with no prior personal experience with the Curtis. I found their operations to be spot on, and very accommodating with lots of last-minutes changes from our end. Food & service - good, staff very friendly, best conference event experience I've ever had; recommended them for several more events with my company.

title: “Good hotel with a good location.”
text: My wife and I stayed one-night with an annual free certificate. Centrally located to what we were doing (Statue Park; Art Museum; Larimer Square; 16th Street). Valet parking is steep, so be ready. This was the first time I'd driven in from the airport, usually opting for the bus when travelling on my own. The hotel was clean, room was nice size, though I hate it when bathroom do not have an exhaust fan system. Bed was comfortable, watch your toes on the solid platform though. We had the Denver Post (Sunday edition) delivered to the room. 3 or 4 PCs available to print boarding passes. They have interior facing rooms, we'd always opt for windows overlooking the 16th street mall or Curtis St. We'll be back.

title: “One of the best stays ever!”
text: Out of all the travelling recently, this stay went off without one glitch. The only change would be a better mattress. My back is hyper sensitive so it could just be me. Totally impressed w/ staff and service!

title: “DC for the Phillies game!”
text: Overall hotel was great, they could not check us in at 3pm, so they gave us free drink cards for the rooftop bar. Our Starwood card should've gotten us an upgrade or more drink tickets, but we didn't feel like waiting. So we took the first available rooms that were ready. Nice coffee and tea in the lobby in the mornings with all the important newspapers. Drinks on their rooftop are great with a lovely view of the Washington Monument and the White House.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
Just wanted to stay that 70 Park Ave was a great great hotel. After researching possibly every single hotel in NYC, I settled on this one, partly because of the great reviews and great price from their own website. The room was very spacious (though no view) and an awesome flat screen tv, big bathroom, etc etc. I had read so many reviews about how rooms are tiny in NYC but this one was very big (2 full beds) and comparable to most hotels we've stayed at around the country, but nicer, very stylishly decorated.
The location was very central- very close to most tourist attractions, many by walking, all by subway or a quick cab ride. The staff was very helpful, even checking us into a room after we arrived from a red eye flight around 7am in the morning- did not expect that at all but pleasantly surprised since we were all very tired and just wanted to crash.
So, all in all, I recommend this hotel to those visiting NYC- it had a nice mix of tourists, business people, hipsters, etc.

title: “Waste of money”
text: The only decent thing about this hotel was the people working there.

title: “FILTHY AND POOR SERVICE”
text: I recently stayed at Tremont Plaza for 3 nights with nursing colleagues for a conference. the room was terribly filthy, with hair and mildew in bathroom and shower. The very small and unaccomodating shelf above the sink was held in place by wedged pieces of cardboard. The carpet had large stains and linens smelled of mustiness. The kitchen was small and poorly stocked. we had 4 guests in our room and there was utensils only for two. The hotel is in walking distance to the inner harbor, but don't walk alone, as you walk through some very seedy areas to get there. The front desk personnel were not very welcoming, (not rude, just there). We were not offered bell service to our room, in fact, after bringing our own luggage down for departure, were "scolded" by the head doorman for requesting that the hotel store our bags, as our ride was not scheduled until 6pm and we had conferences scheduled until that evening. Even after agreeing to store our bags, he continued to inform us that there is limited space and if "everyone" wants to leave their bag at the hotel, they run out of room. The only person that provided any type of customer service was one of the drivers "Nate", he was helpful and recommended a great restaurant and offered to drive us there and gave his number for a pick up when we were ready to return. I definatly would not stay at the Tremont Grand again. The only food onsite was a small deli/store with bruised fruit and stale bread.

title: “Wonderful Time in Boston At The Omni Parker House”
text:
Grand historic hotel perfectly located on the Freedom Trail and across the street from the Granary Burial Ground. Three different Subway stops very close. Hotel dining room has great food (scrod, Boston Cream Pie and Parker House Rolls invented there) and is elegant. About a block away is Beantown Pub, which is a locals place good for lobster roll and burgers, etc.
The coincierge service at the hotel was very helpful recommending places to eat and directions. A nice surprise for my birthday: The Hotel sent up champange and chocolate strawberries!
 In the North end be sure to go to Pizzeria Regina (get there right at lunchtime opening to avoid the crowd). Modern Pastry makes great cannolis and other delights.
A walk around Beacon Hill is a delight. The Art Museum is excellent and is free on Wed's after 4 p.m. (open to 9:45 in a safe neighborhood.)
Cambrige is terrific to wander around. Visit Harvard and don't miss the Havard Coop and Harvard Bookstore.
Disappointed by Salem: Hoakey Witch Museum. House of 7 Gables good, but not worth the trip up to Salem.
Rooms are a little smaller at the Parker House, so ask for a King Room with a King Bed. Clean room with a very comfy king bed. Some noise from adjoining room(s), but otherwise very nice.

title: “Nice Location, Shame Thats The Only Positive Part!”
text:
I stayed in this hotel with my course for a weeks trip to NYC. After arriving at the hotel at 1am after a long travel all we wanted to do was to sleep as we had an early start. to our avail half of us found people staying in the rooms we had been assigned! To make it worse it took about 2 hours to get everyone into new rooms for us to find that there were 3 of us sharing a room that had 2 double beds! Bit awkward when you've only spend a term in class with the person you now have to sleep in a bed with. This was sorted when we complained the next day and got a fold out bed placed upstairs.
The state of the rooms wasn't amazing. the mirror in the bathroom looked like it would drop if you placed anything on it. there was debris all over the bath and only 2 of the 8 plug sockets in our room worked (bit difficult when you have so many electrical items and one of the plugs is for the heater) the heater made a sound so horrible it sounded like an elephant screaming.
Would have been nice if we were all notified of the arrival of dogs. Much to my displeasure i'm allergic to the things so spent half the week sneezing and looking as though someone had punched me in the face. (and that was me staying as far away from them as i could!)
I did feel that the majority of the money did get spent on making the lobby look good. if they had dome that to the rest of the place it would have been impressive!
one thing i cant fault however is the location. if you put aside all the problems within the hotel you see that its opposite an amazing stadium (madison sq gdns) and times square was only a 15 minute walk away (everything a girl could want!)

title: “Friendly staff and clean, comfortable rooms in a great location.”
text: Our room was spacious (by San Francisco standards) and very clean and comfortable. The staff at the front desk, the bar and the dining room were exceptionally courteous, friendly and helpful. We stopped for a before-dinner drink late one afternoon and the bar wasn't serving yet because they were cleaning up from a wine tasting event they had. Instead of just turning us away, they told us to sit down and even gave us glasses to drink some of the wine that was left over from the wine tasting. We ended up with a full bottle of wine "on the house" plus servers and the staff stopped by to talk to us in spite of being busy trying to get the room back in order for dinner. My only complaint was their was no business center. They had a computer at the front desk, but you had to stand up in a corner to use it. Overall it was a great place to stay.

title: “Always clean, pleasant, and quiet”
text:
I always stay at this Candlewood Suites whenever I'm visiting my family in Memphis. It is always clean and everyone there is extremely friendly and knows me by name. I love the comfy beds and the free laundry room.
This hotel was always one of my favorites, but what made it stand out was how accommodating the manager was during a time of crisis. One of my loved ones was going through a nasty divorce and needed somewhere safe and affordable to stay immediately for a month until they were able to find a new place to live. The manager worked with me for an affordable rate and took great care of her while she was there. She commented on how caring the staff was to her during this sensitive time. This hotel and staff will forever be my favorites!!
For location: It is surrounded by many restaurants, close to the FedEx world HQ, and right off the interstate.
In response to the previous posts about the area being a war zone and littered with prostitutes and drug dealers, that couldn't be further from the truth. Just go to google maps and look at the street view for yourself. Hardly what I would call "The Ghetto".

title: “Very good stay @ newton”
text: Just arrive back from 6 nights. We had a larger room (4 persons - 2 double beds) than we had reserve (1 double). So we had more than enough space. I think they really have a good cleaning staff, because the rooms are really clean. The location is super it is a small 10 min. walk to the park or the hudson. We went to see Times Square and i think it is crazy to stay there! The neighbourhood of the hotel is i think quit expensive. It is thank god not full with hotels. Broadway is busy but if you take a side street than you are in a quite people living neighbourhood. With metro (2 and 3 are really fast) you are so in a other place of the city.

title: “Not as Grand as I had hoped...”
text:
For brevity, I'll just list the pros and cons, and briefly comment on each as needed....
Pros:
-Fairly new hotel
-Large (many rooms)
-Very nice common areas, banquet, and meeting rooms
-Exercise room - huge, and well-equipped - it was basically a full-blown gym like you might find at Bally's, President's, World, or Gold's Gym.
-Services was accomodating with special needs, requests, and circumstances
-Comfortable (but small) beds, pillows
-Large tub/shower
-Large bathtowels
-Clean (with caveat below)
Cons: 
-Rooms are small - two full sized beds are not comfortable for two adults sharing one bed, and even with the smaller beds, the rooms are fairly cramped.
-Rooms did not cool well - my home A/C set at 78F was cooler than the room set at 66F with the fan on high. Do not bother opening your shade, as it will heat your room to the point of being unable to cool it. Because of this, I was unable to sleep well.
-Room hallways and elevators are either have the A/C off, or are unairconditioned. Being in South Texas in August, I would work up a sweat from leaving my room to arriving at the lobby or meeting areas.
-Better signs indicating room direction: some areas came to a "t" hallway, and you have to look around a corner to read the directional sign.
-Pool area - cramped and crowded, disgarded cups and limes were found strewn about the area, and beer bottles, cups, and a warning pylon (cone) was tossed off the balcony across an alley to the roof of a Municipal Performing-Arts Theater.
-Parking is woefully inadequate. Five levels are available, but parking spaces are limited and tight - some areas were closed for construction. Self-parking is $15/day, valet parking is $45/day. Our parking (self) was paid by the conference, but none was available. As such, I did not budget for valet parking for the whole weekend. Thankfully, enough complaints were made that the hotel provided the valet parking at no additional charge.
-Couch/bed and business chair in the room were stained.
-Bathroom needs an exhaust vent.
-Room decor can best be described as retro '60's or retro '70's, or modern and spartan - taste is subjective, but I just don't care for that decor. I was expecting something more...opulent
-Formica veneer on the center nightstand was chipped, and my two young children were scratched horribly on it trying to access the bed from there.
-No free high-speed internet. Come on! Even the mom-and-pop hotels provide free internet these days!
I would not recommend this hotel, but only marginally so.

title: “Great Hotel with Excellent Service”
text: We had a delightful experience here and it was totally unexpected for an airport hotel, but the service was wonderful and the rooms were bright, spotless and delightful. They have black out shades and shears and the noise never bothered us. The rooftop pool is great and the fitness center is very complete and well kept. The hotel gives you a pass to pay for parking inside of DFW.

title: “Mediocre hotel.”
text: I stayed here for one night. The lobby was nice, and the staff was friendly. The room was cute, had a retro feel. I was told that my room would have 2 queen sized beds, they were the smallest queen beds I've ever seen. The shower didn't close in the bathroom which was incredibly inconvenient and made the entire bathroom very wet! Also, there was no heater in the bathroom so it was pretty cold getting out! The view of the river and the bridges were very nice. The giant water stain on the top of the curtain however was not. Also had some trouble operating the television, we could only seem to get one channel! I did not get a chance to see the rooftop bar, the breakfast seemed a bit over priced, and we found a delicious diner just one block away. It served its purpose if your looking for a cheap place to sleep, but did not do anything to achieve above and beyond in my mind. I booked through a discounted site, so I am satisfied and feel I got my moneys worth. However, I wouldn't recommend staying there for full price, I feel there are better options in the city to get your moneys worth.

title: “a bit dated but everything was fine”
text:
Stayed 2 nights at the Marines Club in late July 2012. Everything was fine but the basic room was quite small and needs some updates.
They offered complimentary breakfast which was excellent and free cocktail hour each day from 4 - 6pm. These were very nice offerings that would bring me back.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
This hotel was perfect for our first trip to New York .The rooms were very clean .The bed was very comfy ,especially after a long day sightseeing and shopping.All the staff were very friendly and helpful.The location was about a 5 min walk from Times Square.We found the free use of the Macs in reception very useful.As there are only four rooms on each floor it was avery quiet hotel.
Location was great for sightseeing and shopping,we felt it was very central.

title: “great budget choice”
text:
Just turned up and booked a room. Great service for the cost. Staff very friendly and rooms very clean. Breakfast served in restaurant/bar next door - very nice! Good selection and staff very helpfull and full of knowledge.
Overall a great budget choice!

title: “fine business hotel”
text:
I am home from my 4th trip to the San Diego area and third stay at the Hyatt in La Jolla. My reason for choosing this hotel is primarily one of convenience. I was visiting family in the "Golden Triangle" and the hotel is just 3 blocks away. 
Overall, the hotel is clean and modern. It's public areas are clean and well maintained. The reception staff is pleasant and accommodating. The small fitness centre well ventilated and reasonably well equipped at far as hotel gym's go. For those looking for a more elaborate fitness facility or spa, there is one next door for an additional fee. Patrons of the Hyatt have free use of the large heated outdoor pool. The dining room Barcino's serves up a great breakfast with all the basics of a cold and hot buffet. On the recent stay over the Thanksgiving weekend, I was fortunate to take advantage of the "Bed and Breakfast" deal which included breakfast for two including taxes and gratuities as well as valet parking. As mentioned by another reviewer, the parking at the hotel is quite steep although there is parking a block away along Nobel Drive.
If there is any area for improvement, I would suggest more frequent dusting of the air vents and steam cleaning of the carpets in some of the rooms. I did not request a "hypo-allergenic" room on either one of my three stays but did not have trouble until the last one. There was a generous layer of dust on the vents this time and a few small sticky patches on the carpet probably from the previous occupants.
Finally, there is a charge for wifi. I didn't spend much time in the room so I didn't bother to sign up. The industry standards are interesting though. It would appear that the cheaper the hotel, the likelier that free wifi is included.

title: “Great place to stay in NYC”
text: The room was very nice. The workspace was excellent. The bathroom was nice, but there was a mildew odor. I would stay here again. Great location near central park, shopping and restaurants and away from the craziness of times square.

title: “Nice central location”
text: Rooms aren't very big, the pool is tiny, but it's central location was pretty good. Enough to explore in walking distance (Walk of fame e.g.) Plenty of breakfasts to be found (Ihop next door more or less)

title: “Decent and affordable accomodations in Midtown Manhattan”
text: My girlfriends and I were looking for an affordable, centrally located place to stay in NYC to attend a concert at the Manhattan Center and the Comfort Inn Midtown West was just that! Hundreds of dollars cheaper then some of the other commercial names like Marriott and Hilton and still within walking distance of all the major sights. It wasnt luxurious and it was rather small..but...it was cheap, clean, decent and for the money, hands down the best value in the area. I wouldnt reccomend it for a romantic weekend, but for a weekend of partying, where your not really spending much time in the room it'll meet the basic hotel requirements.

title: “Hotel made our stay in New York perfect.”
text: We stayed 5 nights in the hotel paid for with reward points and had two rooms. As a gold card member our rooms were upgraded and were amazing. They were both on 30th floor and were newly refurbished, one was an enormous corner room which looked down onto Broadway and the lights between the two sides of the street. The other room was a regular sized room which was large enough for two double beds and a sofa. The view was stunning it looked towards the clock and police dept and because of its position you could see time square with nothing blocking the view and no.other tall buildings nearby it really was awesome (room 3035). We had free breakfast in the concieege lounge which included a good selection but was only available Mon - fri. We also ate breakfast in the hotel restaurant (expensive as you would expect but good food) and juniors (across the road) which was also good. We did not go to the view restaurant but the newly refurbed bar overlooking time sq was nice. Overall the stay was excellent the rooms were stunning and the hotel was big but nicely done. We stayed over the same weekend as hurricane Irene so the hotel was full and people had to stay in more than usual due to no subway and most shops restaurants and bars were closed. The hotel coped with this well and it did not feel overly busy especially considering its size. We had a fantastic time I would love to return.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Area”
text: My husband and I stayed at Hotel Boheme from 10/27-11/01. I loved the charm of our hotel and room. My husband felt the room was much too small. It was small but I didn't mind, as we didn't spend a lot of time at the hotel or in our room. North Beach is a very hip, busy area and I think in the perfect spot. We were within walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf and Pier 39 Easy access to public transportation and great restaurants and things to do steps outside our door. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Burnham - great experience”
text: My friend recommended this hotel and I didn't know what to expect other than that I would have a good time. Not only did I enjoy myself, I felt right at home. The staff made sure we had everything we needed. When we needed extra towels, they brought them to our room right away. The room was very stately and had high ceilings with a great view of State St, even though our room was on the Washington St half of the building. The hotel is perfect for a few days in town as it is perfectly located in the heart of city, literally a few blocks away from Millennium Park.

title: “OK hotel but really lacking some necessities and customer service.”
text:
I stayed here for one night with a friend who was visiting from Ireland. I was really pleased and excited when we first got there because the room was lovely and spacious, and because we got surprise free parking for having a red car! The problems developed later when we came in for the evening, exhausted and wanted to get in bed to watch a movie. First I found a millipede in our bathtub that had crawled out of the drain. EW! Then our bed had no fitted sheet, it was just a flat sheet laying on the mattress and it wasn't even tucked in, so the mattress was exposed. I called down and a man came up with more sheets. He left them with us and left. He didn't even fix the sheet. When we went to do it ourselves we saw both of them were flat sheets again. This hotel doesn't have fitted sheets? The sheet came undone multiple times throughout the night and was uncomfortable. Then we settled in to order a movie. It would not let us order a movie. We called down to the front desk and the woman had "no idea" what the problem was. She said she'd try to figure it out and call back. She never called back. That's REALLY unacceptable. So then we decided to watch TV and the menu didn't match any of the channels. So our night was somewhat ruined. No one apologized for this and when we did late check out the next day the guy at the front, I think his name was Jerry, acted as if we were doing him a huge inconvenience despite the fact that we received nothing for our negative experience the night before. He asked me to do a review before I left and I said sure, he said he'd e-mail it to me and then asked if I was going to write anything negative. I told him about the TV and sheets. He never sent the link to do the review...I don't find that particularly classy.
So the rooms are nice and that's about it. I was really excited and was planning on coming back with my boyfriend but I think we will try somewhere else next time, not even because of the inconveniences, but because of the indifference of the staff to make up for them.

title: “Lovely, lovely, lovely.”
text: We booked this hotel on the recommendations from trip advisor and we we're not disappointed. We were there for three nights. The staff were lovely, friendly and professional. The room was lovely, beautifully decorated and very comfortable, especially after a long day sight seeing. The bathroom is lovely with plenty of nice bath products. The restaurant food was great and my husband said the Caesar salad he had was the best he'd had all holiday. The valet parking was very efficient but very expensive at $47.00 a day with tax. I too would recommend this hotel.

title: “Super expensive but good quality and service”
text:
I attended a conference at the Marriott Marquis and decided to stay there for the sake of convenience. Through the conference I got a rate of USD 439 for 4 nights and USD 479 for the 5th night. It is extremely expensive, but understandable due to the location: right on Times Square.
The room was clean and comfortable; we even had a side view of Times Square. The conference facilities and lunch provided was excellent.
I definitely recommend this hotel if you want to be in the middle of it all.

title: “Excellent hotel in midtown”
text: In midtown area, this is probably one of the best hotel in this price range. Very good location if you want to be close to Central Park and all the destination shops of the 5th Avenue. Welcome at check-in was very nice and professional. Rooms are spacious (I stayed in a London suite), not noisy (in NY, this is hard to find...!) and offers all basic amenities in room. Rooms are simply but nicely decorated and bathroom are quite spacious as well, displaying separate shower and bathtub. Very nice dressing room allowing easy storage of the suitcase. Good breakfast with good variety of products is available even if, like in all hotels, very expensive.

title: “Great value hotel”
text:
We were delighted with the Chancellor. The location is absolutely perfect for first time visitors to SF, right beside Union Square and the main shopping district. The cable car runs outside the hotel on Powell St. The second stop is across the road and you can skip the queue at the bottom by just hopping on there. 
The room was small, but nicely furnished and clean. There was no AC, but it wasn't needed. It was the first stop on our honeymoon and there was wine, champagne, sweets and a photo frame in the room for us - very nice touch. Also the free wifi is rare for a hotel in the USA.
You could go for a more expensive place with more space, but in a city like SF you don't spend much time in your room and you're better off saving your money for the fantastic restaurants and shops.

title: “Third Time and Still Good”
text:
This is our 3rd time to stay at Hilton New York. Our first stay was in 2009 and every year thereafter. As we expected, the experience once again have been wonderful. We booked from the 24th of Sept until 20 Oct, if this is any indication of how much time we have spent in this hotel to really get to know hotel service, we believe our stays are good tests to see the consistency of service. 
We specially enjoyed the Executive Lounge but this time, with Amy Moreno at the helm of things, the lounge experience became warmer. She was very helpful and and was always checking on what else we needed. We noticed that she was doing this to all the guests, We look forward to seeing this in our next visit.
We hope that we will see fresher rooms in our next visit. While our room was clean and properly maintained, it would be good to see some freshing up. (i.e new paint, wall paper, or carpet?)

title: “The Town & Country is the best”
text:
Our reunion group convened at the Town & Country for the third time on the weekend of April 27-29, 2012. As we always say to each other, why even consider any other place? I could go on and on, raving about everything, because all facets of their organazation are at the highest level.
But, I'd like to say a few words about their staff. To a person, starting with the sales manager, they cover their responsibilities perfectly. Because we are a group, we are assigned a Convention Services Representative, who worked flawlessly with us during our stay, assisting us with every need we had. We had two group meals, involving the catering department, and each and every person was right there for us, without being in the way. And the food was 5 Star comparible. All of this plus the beauty of the property, with the roses in full bloom, made for the perfect weekend. thanks T&C, we'll be back. Ken Walton

title: “Nothing Fancy, but good value for the price”
text: While nothing fancy, I decided to give this place a try based on the price so I wouldn't have to drive close to 3 hours after a concert. Was a little leery after reading some reviews, but I must say, I am glad I stayed here. The location was fine, the room was clean. The heating system could use some updating, it was tough to adjust it for an overnight sleep and had to get up to turn it off after a couple of hours. The TV remote didn't work, but since I was just there to sleep I didn't bother reporting it to the front desk. All in all a positive experience for the price, and would stay there again.

title: “Beautiful, but wouldn't stay again”
text: We stayed at the Mansion a week, scouting Austin for retirement. It was beautiful, our room was comfortable and nicely furnished, the food was good, the staff was courteous and for the most part helpful. Our room on the second floor was right next to the ice machine...the door was 12" away...When we were constantly disturbed at night from people getting ice we asked them to put up a sign and they were very reluctant to do so. At that time we found out that for some reason people from the first floor were directed to the second floor's ice machine....The door to our room allowed light in all the way around it, and noise. The heat, or air con blew high only, and right at the bed. The view was trash bins and a filthy alley and noisy parties until 3am, so no opening the windows for fresh air. Beautiful, but never again.

title: “Excellent Hotel in the upcoming Hells Kitchen area or Midtown”
text:
Funky, midtown, well priced, easy to get around, walking distance to all of Mid-Town attractions and offices, taxi to Downtown direct on 11th Ave, Access to NJ through the Lincoln Tunnel.
The rooms in the hotel are big for NYC, the drinks prices are level with those found in all of NYC hotels, the staff are friendlier, and the roof top bar is excellent in summer (in winter, it's freeeeeezing).

title: “Best choice”
text:
Very comfortable place and very friendly stuff.The rooms were very clean and quiet! 
Everything we wanted to see was in a walking distance. The neighborhood was great as well for breakfast as for lunch and dinner. 
We will definitely come back!

title: “A Most Enjoyable Hotel in San Fran”
text: I have stayed at the Galleria Park Hotel many times and find it consistently good - an excellent place to stay. It is only 2 blocks from the Montgomery BART station and as many to the Streetcars. About 4 blocks to Union Square and heart of shopping. A short walk to the Ferry Building and all that it offers. Chinatown is only 4 blocks away. If you're a runner and prefer flat ground to hills, this is the place to stay. The staff has been there a long time, a good sign and are always accommodating. I always sleep soundly at this hotel. The beds are comfortable. All of the rooms I've stayed in have a nice cushion chair to sit in besides a desk chair. I will stay here again.

title: “Nice, Moderate Hotel”
text: Stayed here in December, 2004 for the Ravens - Colts game. Nice location with easy access to RCA Dome (across street) and downtown (5 min walk). Room was OK, not flashy. The room supposed to be a "double suite" but did not have more room than an average double hotel room. Better off at an Embassy for more room, but it was clean, new, and the staff was very friendly.

title: “Boutique Chic @DreamDowntown”
text:
Throughout the years, my love affair with NYC has been somewhat bittersweet. Some of my fondest memories stem from my time there - my 21st birthday, the day (technically early morning) I first stumbled across Pop Burger, the numerous MPD bars and clubs, the ridiculous queue for a Kati Roll, the infamous brunch parties, Brooklyn Bridge at night, Black Cod at Koi, and the many a random night out with some of New York's finest. 
On the other hand, however, you also have the not so fond memories - my 25th birthday, the "random" airport inspections and numerous hours spent in NY Customs and Immigration for yet another "random" interrogation - if that's what the Americans call "random", I should really play their lottery more often. So when we rocked up to the Big Apple for yet another birthday celebration, I was somewhat apprehensive as to which side of the fence this holiday would fall. "Mentally Scarred" or "Happy Hols".
The hotel choice was largely down to our sketchy travel agent, I wasn't sure what to expect, and although I was ill, I had to endure a 50 minute taxi ride with the windows open in an NYC winter as my brother would otherwise get travel sick sat in the back of a cab and 'Abdul' wouldn't let him ride shotgun and alleviate the problem. It wasn't looking good. "Mentally Scarred" was racking up points.
But this all changed when we finally arrived at the hotel. It's difficult not to be impressed when you see this place for the first time. The world's largest (and best looking) cheese-grater! After a quick Google images search on the place, I was reassured to see that I wasn't the only one who made such a connection! The looks certainly do not fade when you walk in. The lobby is split between a mood-lit hotel reception and a very cool looking restaurant and bar with even cooler hanging globe lights. We arrived at approx 7pm and there was certainly a buzz around the place. Check-in was quick and effortless and we even received an unexpected welcome/introduction from the Guests Services Manager on duty that night which I thought was a nice touch.
There was a little confusion as to which elevator we needed, but soon after we found ourselves in our adjoining rooms on the third floor where the distinguishing signs of good service continued - the door between the two rooms had been unlocked for us, for example, and we were welcomed to the hotel with a hand-written note left in each room. 
The rooms themselves were of a good size, not what you would call extravagant but certainly more than adequate given the location. You have all the usual trimmings you would expect to see, a well stocked (and pricey) mini-bar, flat screen tv/monitor, complimentary wi-fi etc. but if we really were pushed to make complaints, I would say that the wardrobe could be a little bigger and they could provide you with more hangers and hanging space but this really is clutching at straws and nothing a quick call to house-keeping couldn't fix. A quick warning to the uninitiated – beware of removing items from the mini-bar for longer than 30 seconds as they are automatically charged to your bill (just laugh at the “intimacy pack” from inside the drawer)!
The location is exceptional. Around the corner from my regular haunts, Pop Burger, Chelsea Market and the iconic MPD and literally a stone’s throw away from some of the best restaurants NYC has to offer. 
Concierge were extremely helpful to get us to all the right places on an otherwise relatively quiet weekend in New York (Thanks-Giving) and Guests Services more so – especially in braving the winds and rain when my friend called through requesting boxer- shorts for himself after he had realised he had brought too few with him for the trip!
If you can, certainly try PHD for the views of the NY skyline, music and lethal caipiroskas. I’ve been told Electric Rooms downstairs is also worth a shot, but it was (unsurprisingly) quiet when we tried it on a Sunday night. 
Things you’ll remember if staying here: 
the glass-floored swimming pool on the first floor which you can see from the hotel lobby
the view of NYC skyline from PHD
great service
the location
the most comfortable hotel beds in NYC
All in all, aside from all of the alcohol-related stories I could share with you here, it was certainly a ‘Happy Hol’ and largely down to the fantastic hotel and its staff. Look forward to my return trip very soon!

title: “Small and friendly”
text: Just spent 6 nights at this hotel and it was great. Small yes, looking a bit tired okay, but very friendly, approachable staff and a fair price for such a knockout location. For people like me who just want a room and a bed in a clean, safe & well located hotel, you could do a lot worse in NYC.

title: “Just OK”
text: I booked this hotel through hotels.com as a friend and I were coming for the Final Four. For what I paid (approx. $130 / night) it was a decent hotel in a good downtown location. That said, the room was really small with a small TV and a small bed which was really inconvenient as they didn't have any rooms with two doubles. And the hotel didn't have any cots, extra blankets or extra pillows as they were at capacity. Also the entire hotel smelled like smoke including our room which was a non-smoking room. They did have free high speed internet which is a huge plus and a drinking water station with fillable water bottles which was a nice touch.

title: “Review from diamond member. Great place to stay”
text: I cannot say enough about this hotel. The manager Britt has gone above and beyond for all my stays there. The staff goes out of there way to make sure I am happy. The rooms are clean and the beds are great. I get a good nights sleep everytime I have been there. I travel alot and love all the TV channels they have. Good breakast as well. If you need a great place to stay this is it.

title: “Exceptional”
text: Hampton Inn is usually my first choice when I’m looking for a hotel. I’ve stayed at quite a few in various cities, and have never been disappointed. However this particular Hampton Inn, located in the beautiful South Park shopping area of Charlotte, is on another level, quite a bit more upscale than most and in some ways more comparable to what you expect to find with the more high-end Hiltons. I had the pleasure of staying there recently (October 2010), and as always, I found the front desk staff to be friendly and efficient, and had an extremely pleasant, clean, and quiet room, a very comfortable bed (and pillows), good TV, and free wifi. But beyond that, I would add that the entire building, recently renovated, is unusually attractive and impressive both inside and out. And I would also call attention to the business center, situated in a quiet enclosed space, and with not only the 2 computers and printers (on opposite ends of the room for a bit of privacy) but also plenty of neatly organized desk supplies. The complimentary breakfast buffet is similar to the usual Hampton Inn fare, but does include a few extra items. And if you want something more gourmet, there is a wonderful market just about a block and a half away. Finally, this review would not be complete without my mentioning a very ‘cool’ feature in the bathroom that was quite an unexpected surprise to me—a TV embedded in the mirror!

title: “Acceptable NY: old building, reasonable service”
text:
This hotel is just fine, and from my (somewhat limited experience) one of the better ones in this area of the West Side (it's at 79th & Amsterdam, within steps of Natural History Museum, Central Park, tons of NYC transportation options). I was in a "quiet room towards the back" with no view - I don't know how the rooms on the "front" are but when I'm in NYC I do enjoy a street view. 
It's an older building, with the issues that older buildings (esp in NYC) have including small elevators, small funky closets, steps into the lobby (no ramp - fine if you have small bags or doorman is on it). In fall/winter the air tends to dry out (true pretty much any older NY hotel without integrated climate control). Pillows are decent, medium soft. Sounds of other guests are audible, including any crying babies (not super loud, but quite audible). 
The service is pleasant and attentive, although a bit spotty (little things e.g. they deliver NY Times to your door in theory but not always in practice, semi-broken hairdryer in room). All in all I'd stay there again but wouldn't go out of my way to do so.

title: “Horrible Hotel”
text:
The room that we stayed in for one night was $475 per night. Disgusting, horrible, full of stains and made me sick to my stomach imagining what more I could have done with my money.
We ended up dishing out $100.00 more at the All Suite Omni Hotel for the next two nights. Beware of the Tremont!

title: “Perfect hotel for a family”
text: We stayed at the Belevedere Hotel in January 2005. The rooms were a bargain for NYC standards (really for any town!). It was one of the few hotels that offered a breakfast deal. In addition, the rooms all have a refrigerator and microwave, which came in handy for weary kids needing a drink (parents too!) after a long day of sightseeing. The buffett breakfast was good, and kids 5 and under eat free! I read a lot of reviews complaining of slow elevators, but we didn't notice any worse than other hotels we've stayed in. We would definitely stay here again; the rooms were bigger than we expected and much cleaner than many chains we've stayed in. The hotel is just a few blocks from times square.

title: “Wonderful hotel”
text:
This hotel was excellent. We dined in their restaurant and found it to be wonderful. 
The hotel rooms were clean, the location great and the staff very courteous. We will be staying at this property again and again.

title: “The Inn is Awesome”
text:
We stayed at the Mediterranean Inn for three nights in October and were very pleased with this hotel. Beautiful views, excellent location, clean room - with a nicely equiped kitchenette - and a Starbucks in the lobby. 
Best buy in the Seattle area if you are looking for a comfortable place to stay and don't need a pool, restaurants, or conveniance store on location - it's all within a block of the place anyway. 
We did get a corner room - better views, but the stairway cut into the size of our room considerably. We still had plenty of room and with a view, but if it is more than two people or with kids it would be a tight fit. 
Able to walk to everything - Space Needle, mono-rail, water front, etc.

title: “An Extraordinary Experience in New York City”
text: We were greeted by the wonderful staff, quickly checked in and wisked up to our room which looked out over Park Avenue. Everything was perfect. The room was comfortable and in excellent condition. We stayed at the hotel for three days while visiting family on the upper east side. The location is perfect, close to subways and Grand Central Station. Like most Kimpton hotels, the resturant is very good. In summary, facilities well above average and a staff second to none. I intend to return both on business and with my family for personal trips.

title: “They aim to please.”
text:
Just returned from our 11/16/08 - 11/19/08 stay. At check in we rec'd #710 - a very large room for NY - with one lovely full wall of windows. Great during the day, but Sunday night street noise is outrageous. We had snatches of about 45 mins. of sleep all night due to construction, deliveries, cab horns, and squeeling brakes. 
Asked the front desk for help the next AM and rec'd upgrade (no cost) to #1410 - corner digs at the back of the building. This is the size of a typical NYC apartment with foyer, full kitchen, dining / living area and separate bedroom. 
Rooms are clean enough - although worn edges / scuffy baseboards / stained carpets beg for attention. Edge dust build up also in hallways - although again quite typical of NYC hotels.
Beyond a bit of a 'down in the heel' feel, overall a good time and their beds are the very BEST we've ever slept in! 
.

title: “Easy come easy go”
text: No hassle - services all worked smoothly - centrally located - top floor pool nice but could be so much nicer - bar and lounge area feels just a little neglected - breakfast whilst relaxing help yourself is a little bland.

title: “Nice”
text: My husband and I stayed here the night before we went on our honeymoon cruise and found it a very nice place. Everything was clean and well-made and the night staff was very helpful. I would certainly reccommend this place to anyone who is cruising. It is definitely the best value. We will be staying again for our next cruise!

title: “An Amazing Stay”
text:
My wife and I celebrated our ten year wedding anniversary with a stay at The Inn at The Black Olive, and we could not be happier with our decision.
The staff was incredibly helpful.
The Suite was decorated simply and tastefully. Previous reviewers have said it, but it bears repeating, walking into your suite you really get the impression that you have traveled to a completely different locale. For us, we felt transported to a Caribbean location, similar to where we spent our Honeymoon.
The proximity to Inner Harbor AND Fells Point is another plus!

title: “Get shower room”
text: Stayed here in January 2012 for 4 nights, saw from reviews that the rooms were small so I upgraded to a bigger room before I got to New York, but even still found the queen size room to be very very small, loved the shower room it was almost as big as the bed room which does not say much for the size of the room. But found it to be very clean, and loved the decor. Great location. Had a great time and the staff were very helpful.

title: “Nice but not very clean”
text: After reading the reviews for this hotel, I expected an immaculate room; however, I was disappointed. The room we were in had a shower in its own room, separate from the bathroom. The tiles in the shower were mildewed. It's not surprising, considering the door to the "shower room" did not stay open, so all the moisture was trapped in it. I ended up using a garbage can to hold the door open to let the room dry out after a shower. I accidentally spilled some water on the wood floor in the bedroom, and when I wiped it up, the cloth was filthy, as if the floors hadn't been cleaned in quite some time. On the plus side, the staff was extremely friendly and helpful, the valets had the car available quickly, and the location is perfect--right across the street from the Alamo and within easy walking distance to the Riverwalk. I would consider staying here again; however, I would request a larger room and an inspection.

title: “Take advantage of everything New York has to offer!”
text: This was my second trip to New York so I knew my way around and had decided to get away from the tourist traps around Times Square and found Hotel Giraffe. It's close enough to be a short walk, subway trip (on the No 6 line) or cab ride to just about everything. Greenwich Village, Chelsea, Soho, and other areas. While I think I'm a pretty low maintenance guest, there wasn't enough that the staff there could do for me. The room I had was facing E26th Street, but I don't think that there would be a 'bad' room - unless you were on the second floor as this would mean you couldn't sleep with the window/balcony doors open if you wanted to. The area it's in has some great restaurants - try Bread and Tulip next door. Overall, an amazing place to base yourself in New York. I'll be back again!

title: “Quaint but interesting..”
text: This hotel is strictly for people who are looking for an antique Victorian feel to their stay. The elevator for instance took forever to take us to our floor and back down. The upholstery looked rather old but thankfully wasn't smelly or dirty. The bathroom was rather modern compared to the rest of the room which was also quite small. However, all said and done, it was an interesting stay in one of the oldest hotels in the city.

title: “Great hotel staff”
text: We stayed here twice for 2 nights each time and found the place to be perfect the hotel staff were the best we found in california The rooms were large and very clean and they offered a light breakfast in the mornings. There is also free internet access in the front lobby. The hotel also has a small workout room with sauna. The hotels location is excellent we were a 2 minute walk to all of the walk of fame attractions and the metro which is 1 stop from Universal city. A good place to eat is the Pig and Whistle look around for the 15% discount vouchers. We did all 4 city pass attractions the stars homes tour is very average you see more homes where people used to live than where they are living now, its really just a tour of the district. the Entertainment museum was good and also the Kodak theatre was worth seeing. The best one was the Redline walking tour which was very good and worth doing when you very first get there. We went to the Guiness book of records which was good but the wax museum is terrible don't waste your money on this place. I highly recommend staying at the Hollywood Celebrity hotel

title: “It could be so much better with little effort.”
text: I was pleased to be allowed an early check in with my early flight. I was a female solo traveler placed on the bottom level in room 102. This room had an exit next to my room, and unfortunately the door slamming late at night was annoying and unsafe in my opinion. The room appeared to be clean at first, but the shower had mold, and maid service was not available each day. The AC worked most of the time, but seemed to create moisture issues and the carpet was always damp. The location itself is a dump. Buildings are boarded up and there are no close by restaurants. There are other similar looking hotels. The breakfast buffet was mediocre at best, the coffee was good. I asked for a wake up call for an early flight that never came. The next morning as I checked out I asked what happened to my wake up call and the gentleman looked at a piece of paper for my name and said it was never written down. Seems like an outdated system that didn't work anyway. The price was ok, but for a little more you can get a much better hotel nearby with more options. I did like the wireless internet in my room.

title: “Clean hotel, great location in town, fairly priced”
text: Although not a fancy hotel, we found the staff friendly, the room clean, the kitchenette small but adequate, the wifi usable, and the pool small but good enough for a quick swim. The location was great for being in the city, near Balboa park, with many good restaurants nearby and walkable. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Exceeded Expectations - Excellent Stay in LA”
text:
We reviewed this hotel against the expectation set by price. It is in Westwood in a very convenient location for places such as Hollywood, Beverly Hills, etc... Clearly parking is at a premium so despite the tightness of parking it was great to have no charge.
Our reception was very warm and the gentleman could not have been more helpful; we received and upgrade to a room with a large sitting area. A great help as this was the last night of a fourteen night holiday so lots of clearing out was needed.
Although the open areas of the hotel looked a little tired, the room was great.
Breakfast was weak being served in a dingy room with no windows. Again space is at a premium so not far off expectations.
Being close to the university meant there were lots of places to eat.
Overall a good stay and very good location to get in West and N LA.

title: “A great mid town pick”
text:
The good bits
It all looks fabulous. The lobby/bar is great, very cosy for the winter. We stayed for New Year and it was a great atmosphere and we had loads of fun.
Some of the staff were amazing (eg the girl who arranged New Year - long blonde hair -if anyone from the Royalton is reading this) was fabulous - completely understood customer service and the lobby waitresses were very good but a couple of the staff just couldn't be bothered (there was a big guy on reception and a very thin girl on reception who just couldn't be bothered).
Location is great for midtown you can walk to most places. We got an excellent recommendation from reception about the brasserie across the road (DB Brasserie) which was great and they didn't try and convince us to eat in the hotel which was refreshing.
The bad bits
You can tell a man designed this hotel because some of the design isn't practical. The lighting is so low in the rooms that you can't see what you're doing half the time! Also, there is a lack of mirrors and storage space. It's difficult if you are staying for any more than a few nights. There was no room round the sink to put things and no hooks to hang towels on, no wardrobe space etc.
The rooms aren't huge (there were three of us) - if you stay in Flatotel (midtown) or Hotel on Rivington (downtown) you get bigger rooms but it was perfectly ok.
Also, check your bill they completely overcharged us but sorted it quickly.
The restaurant wasn't very appealing - looked like a canteen.

title: “Great hotel great location”
text: My wife and i are travelling the west coast of the US and our first stop was San Fran a place i did not want to leave, our hotel for 4 nights was the Orchard Hotel which was perfect in every way, the staff were very friendly and helpful and with a 2min walk to union square and a cable car outside the door what else could you ask for ? the rooms are very spacious and clean but the most important thing when your staying anywhere is its very quiet at night . The rooms are cleaned daily and if and when i return i will be staying in the same place, the location has everything shopping, restaurants, tour buses all a few min walk ,, hope this helps guys

title: “Clean and quiet”
text:
Stayed here on a Priceline win 5/10/09 - 5/13/09. The room was clean, and although the furnitures seemed updated, bathroom marble top was cracked and showed its age. Double shower heads were awesome with good water pressure. I was on the 20th floor across from the ice machine, but did not have any major noise issues. Great to have a sofa bed in the room (not for the bed, but for the seating). 
They had minor construction going on in the lobby area, but overall, a very comfortable stay.

title: “Centrally located hotel geared for the Korean traveller”
text:
I stayed here for a week while attending a conference on Korean culture and history at the Korean Cultural Center, located a bit further along down Wilshire. This hotel is Korean owned and obviously caters to Korean travelers. While I am all about multiculturalism, it was a bit bothersome when signs in the elevators and in the room were only in Korean. My experience at the front desk was that their knowledge of English was limited. The staff there very friendly, though, and professional.
The room I was in was incredibly small and spartan. With the king-sized bed in the room, there was only a small border around the room in which to move. There was no ironing board or iron in the room, which for a cross-country traveller was a bit disappointing. However, there wasn't room to open one up anyway! There was a small writing desk wedged into the corner, but there was barely room to pull out the chair. I do really appreciate the complementary wi-fi access in the room. (You do need an access code from the front desk.) I also appreciated the mini-fridge in the room. My room looked across to the other wing of the hotel, so I didn't really feel a sense of privacy with the curtains opened, so I kept them closed most of the time I was in the room.
The room was always thoroughly cleaned each day by the cleaning staff, something that I truly appreciate. The carpet in the hallway was very worn and needs to be replaced. 
Overall, if you're staying in Koreatown, this hotel is in a very central location, conveniently located next to the Wilshire/Western Metro Stop. Drawbacks include the lack of amenities in the room (I almost forgot there was no coffee maker in the room), no fitness centre or pool and the lack of English signage. Would I stay here again? Maybe. I do not know how much it costs per night, as this was paid by someone else.

title: “Favorite Hotel in SF!”
text: I absolutely love this hotel. Have stayed there many times in the last three years and am always heartbroken when I can't get in. They have great rooms - but what I love most is the amazing staff. Ask for David and Isaac at the bar. Katherine is one of the managers at the desk is gracious and helpful. One tip - ask for a high floor as the garage is open 24 hrs and makes a loud noise when cars are exiting (to warn pedestrians) so that can get a little annoying if you are sensitive to noise like I am.

title: “Smart and modern”
text: We stayed for one night only and had a favorable impression. Arriving rather late (and that was no problem), it was good to be able to eat here despite the hour. The bed was so very comfortable and the room quiet and large. I suspect this may be a hotel used mainly by businesspeople rather than us vacationers, so perhaps it was not surprising that the hotel building did seem somewhat impersonal. Certainly it was all smart, clean and modern. The staff were most friendly, all of them, and nothing was too much trouble, whether at the front desk or at the front door or in the restaurant. The cooked breakfast was excellent. The location is good- within walking distance of the downtown area, light rail, Amtrak and so on.

title: “Fantastic hotel in NYC! We will be back!”
text:
The Library Hotel was everything I hoped for and more. The staff was very friendly and accomodating. Our flight got in earlier than expected and we went right to the hotel. Although our room was not ready they told us we could help ourselves to their fantastic free breakfast! One of the BEST reasons to stay at this hotel is the free breakfast and evening wine & cheese. You're already going to spend a ton in NYC so why pay more for breakfast! Fresh bagels, fruit, danish, yogurt, cereal, juice, coffee ... what more could you want! You're going to eat at some amazing restaurants in NYC so there is no need to fill up at breakfast anyway! Ok, enough about the breakfast! 
We went with their largest suite and it was well worth it. The bed and linens are amazing ... many afternoons I wanted to take a nap because it was so comfy! Our room was on the 7th floor overlooking Madison Avenue and I thought we might hear some street noise but it was very quite. In the evenings they offered wine, cheese, nuts and crackers. Yum! They have a great selection of books in your room and throughout the hotel too. 
The location was fantastic! A very short walk to Grand Central Station, Times Square, Fifth Avenue and the Empire State Building. We took cabs everywhere else we needed to go which is so convenient. Our cab ride to lower Manhattan was only $10.
A few things I would recommend in NYC include the Top of the Rock tour, Empire State Building, a sail boat cruise with [--] and Curtains on Broadway. Some of the best restaurants we visited included Brio Restaurant [--], Osteria Doge [--] and Katz's Deli [--]. If you're from Chicago like us don't bother with pizza at Lombardi's. It's said to be NYC's best pizza but we really didn't care for it. The adventure and fun was walking to the place which took us through Washington Park, Soho, etc. We came home wanting some Uno's Pizza! 
Enjoy your trip to NYC! Again, stop driving yourself crazy searching for a great hotel and make your reservation at the Library Hotel!
Sorry no hotel pictures. Who has time to take those anyway! It looks just like the website.

title: “Nice property, good location, friendly staff”
text: This was a nice property, right on the Riverwalk. Everyone was helpful and friendly. Ask about discounts when checking rates.

title: “Great Hotel--Stupid Charge”
text: This is an awesome hotel. The room is very good and the location right on the UT campus is perfect. The people working there were all very kind but the 14 day a day charge for parking is the dumbest thing I have heard of. In this kind of economy to charge 14 dollars a day is just plain wrong. I was there only one night but multiple nights would have been over the top. Hotels need to think of thier consumers instead of making cheap money off their good paying customers.

title: “Nice hotel next to UVillage”
text:
I needed to find a hotel near UW on very short notice (2 days). My usual "go to" hotels were fully booked, so I chose the Silver Cloud University District based on its location right next to the UVillage mall and close to campus. I found the hotel to be very clean, very quiet, and comparably priced to the other hotels I have stayed at in the area.
Parking is included in the hotel rate, and there were always plenty of open spaces. A nice breakfast is also included in the rate, which included scrambled eggs and sausage, make-your-own waffles, assorted muffins and cereals, juices, coffee, yogurt and fresh fruit. There is a good-sized eating area with comfy seats, fireplace, and library nook. It felt very "homey". Wifi is also included.
The room was quiet, clean and comfortable. Maybe the carpet and bedding could have been a bit newer and the towels could have been a bit fluffier, but it was a nice room. The wall heater/air conditioner unit was the quietest I have ever used in a hotel room. I did not hear any plumbing noise in the walls nor people above us or in adjacent rooms.
I used the fitness room one morning. There are free weights, two treadmills, three ellipticals, and a multi-purpose machine. Everything was clean and well-maintained. The Burke-Gilman trail is right next to the hotel, so it is easy to access for a hike, jog, or bike ride when the weather permits.
UVillage is walking distance from the Silver Cloud Inn with its numerous shops, restaurants, a market and a drugstore. All-in-all I highly recommend this hotel for visitors to UW.

title: “EXCELLENT in EVERY WAY”
text: Its nice when you go to a Hotel with High Expectations and then have all of them exceeded! Just spent the Weekend (2 nights) at the Four Seasons and had a fabulous time. The hotel property is beautiful in an excellent location overlooking the lake. We had a lake view room on the 6th Floor which provided a spectacular view. The hotel is very clean (as you would expect) and nicely appointed. What sets the hotel above and beyond however is the Service we received. Everyone from Check in, to the Bar Staff, pool staff restaurant wait staff, housekeeping and parking attendants were exceptional. Everyone greeted you with a smile, took care of your request timely and asked if there was anything else they could do for you. Also would highly recommend the restaurant TRIO which is in the hotel. Ate there Once for breakfast and once for a nice Dinner to celebrate an anniversary with a group of family members. They truly made it a memorable occasion. The food there was exceptional as was the staff. Looking forward to returning to the Four Seasons in the future!

title: “beautiful grounds”
text: My husband and I stayed for a weekend stay-cation. The staff was incredibly friendly, tending to every need. The rooms are spacious and very clean. We got a room with a single king bed, so comfortable. I slept better than I do at home. I love that the rooms all look over a courtyard with large trees, water fountain and pool/jacuzzi, made it feel very private. We had breakfast in the lobby restaurant, everything was cooked to perfection. We took some time to sit on the terrace overlooking the 1st tee of the golf course. Very comforable seats w/ a fire pit. The resort was so peaceful and offers a nice bit of romance.

title: “Old feels old”
text:
I stayed at the historic Menger Hotel for 3 nights. The room I had was old, very small, dated (old analog TV), walls spotted, carpet in disrepair, slow running drain in the tub (never fixed as requested). The bed was adequate, the room was quiet, AC worked OK, and excellent water pressure. 
The location of the Menger is very good, next door to the Alamo and across the street from the Riverwalk. Only Valet parking for $25 a night and still had to wait 5-10 minutes each time when my vehicle was requested before I left my room. The lobby was quaint but smelled Old. All in all, glad to say I've stayed there, but would not stay again nor recommend.

title: “Cozy Quaint hotel”
text: Nice size room. Staff very friendly. Love the wine at 5pm in the lobby and the cookies late at night. Close to subway and the circle. Nice neighborhood.

title: “La Quinta Inn”
text: When I checked into the hotel I found trash in the hallway, but I was willing to overlook that since it seemed very quiet and otherwise clean. However, the cleaning person threw away my sister's belongings that she had in the dresser. I was really embarassed and felt bad for her. I will never book this hotel again.

title: “Great Deal for good price”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for one day and night during my first ever trip to NYC, being a resident of Connecticut this seems a bit odd, but nonetheless... I arrived via bus and found that the hotel is a nice 2 minute jaunt from the main bus depot near Times Square, the hotel itself was alittle hard to find with all of the scaffolding - but if you look for the signature spiral starecase going down the front of it - youll find it easy. I checked in an hour later than planned, and found to my happy suprise - that i had been upgraded from a Standard room to the largest penthouse suite in the hotel. For Free! This along with the great advice about asian cuisine in the area, broadway shows playing, and free bottled water made a great first impression.
 The staff were very courteous, and after spending my first night wandering around the city ( including an hour or so at the MET and another hour or so figuring out why the bloody S train kept changing tracks on me ), i came back and had a nice frosty glass of Guiness in the great little bar on site. The next morning, i went down and enjoyed a great breakfast ( free ) with huge bagels, coffee, and complimentary NY Times. The staff was very polite on checking out, wishing me a happy trip home and hopes that i had a good stay. They even watched my luggage for me in a secured room for no additional charge. All in all i have to say that this is a very good hotel and is in the center of everything.
Some advice: There is a brand new restaurant up on 44th street ( the restaurant zone ), it is a BBQ shack that has been open a little over a month at this point. Unfortunately the name escapes me, but it should be easy to find. They have some of the best microbrewery beer on tap ive had in the US.

title: “Comfortable place to stay”
text: I stayed here with my family of five from august 23rd to 27th. My son attends UT and we have stayed at many hotels in the area. This hotel is convenient to everything. The view we had was of the lake and it faced the skyline. You don't get this view from other city hotels. We had a 2 room executive suite with an adjoining bedroom for $590 a night. Much better value then the single room at the Four Seasons that we recently stayed in. The staff was friendly and accommodating. One night we woke up to loud noises at 2:30 am. When we realized the people were not going to calm down, we called the front desk. Spoke to Josh who sent someone up immediately. I will stay here again.

title: “We loved it and we'll be back!”
text: The suggested title captions it well. For a 3-1/2 star, this meet/beat my expectations. Charming hotel with a novel "shared" balcony-style door that provides a view overlooking the pool. Helpful, courteous front desk. Nicely laid out. Comfortable (albeit slightly clinical) bedding. Super convenient location. Parking garage is an extra charge, but allows you to park at your room level for added convenience. The only noticeable shortcoming was an old-style television (not an LCD), but the room was enjoyable and relaxing and we felt no need to turn on a tv. Also, please note the available Wi-Fi is not free.

title: “Not brilliant”
text:
Hotel - room comfortable. Room service slow and didn't always get order right. Reception very helpful. Free airport transfer. Biggest problem - it is right next to the train tracks which go past all the time. Worst one in the middle of the night and they have to sound their hooter as the tracks cross the road - so don't expect a quiet stay!
Not convenient for Downtown Denver! When I booked (through Trailfinders) it stated on the website that there was a downtown shuttle - asked about it to be told they had just stopped it! They really push you towards taking taxis downtown - only $20 but still inconvenience!
Wouldn't stay there again! Only convenient for airport and if you aren't planning on staying in Denver as hire car rental next door.

title: “A gem.”
text: The Kimberly is well-located--walking distance to great restaurants and attractions as well as to Grand Central terminal. A discount coupon available at check-in gets you almost half off parking (directly across the street--can't be more convenient). The staff is extremely helpful and pleasant. Not a sour note in the bunch. We were upgraded to a suite on check in and as a veteran of a score of Manhattan hotels, I would have to say this was the most pleasant, spacious, spotless accommodation I've had. A wonderful buffet breakfast is available on the penthouse level. Very pricey, but in the pouring rain it fit the bill. Will surely stay there again.

title: “choose a different hotel if you can”
text:
We stayed at the Hilton hotel in Chicago for 2 nights for a meeting. We usually choose a different hotel such as the Fairmont or the Swiss but we ended up staying at the hilton. In the voice mail in the room, the manger welcomed us and indicated that the hotel is celebrating its 85 anniversary. It seems that the hotel and specifically the rooms remained the same for the past 85 years. The room size was OK but the carpets and the furniture have seen better days. The bathroom was small with old design. The service of the room was adequate. Other buildings blocked the view from the window.
One of the most disturbing policy of the hotel is the charge extra fee for every service they provided, they charges for the internet, exercise room and even $2 per bag for storage. When we asked for late check out, they requested $50 for 2 hours. These charges usually not present in other hotels. We will recommend that you choose a different hotel next time you are in Chicago RSTMN 4/10

title: “Very modern, in the heart of the city”
text: I travel for business and have seen my fair share of hotels and this one was great!! We were upgraded to a junior suite upon arrival for our weekend stay. I had never been to SD and this was the perfect place to stay. In the heart of the gaslamp district and close to the marina. Endless food, bars and entertainment. We loved Mary Jane's and Pinkberry! Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Excellent”
text:
The last hotel on my trip of route 66 and waht a hotel to finish on,great bedrooms ,toiletries of quality nice large bed,very friendy staff (except for the barman)lovely but small swimming pool.
Drinks very expensive but it is the Hilton but you can go out and buy cheaper .
I recommend this hotel and it is close to all the atractions as the hollywood walk of fame

title: “Fabulous!”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights in October 2012 and had a fantastic time. Our room was No 501, it was gorgeous, a 2 bedroom apartment really with a lovely balcony where we enjoyed our breakfast which was included in our stay.
We were greeted by John who is just lovely and he recommended a great Italian restaurant just across the road called Beccos, it was fab & we couldn't believe how busy it was on a Monday night, great food and service.
We met the manager of the hotel, Colin and he was lovely too, he even called round a couple of bars to see if anyone was showing the Scotland football match for us.
The hotel is in a great location for exploring NYC and a lot of the attractions are in walking distance, it is a fantastic, friendly hotel which we would be definitely stay in again on our next visit.
Checking out was so easy and the lovely receptionist even checked us in online and printed our boarding passes and then organised a car for us to the airport. They really couldn't do enough for us and the personal touches just made our stay even more special.
We'll be back!

title: “Our stay at the Chicago South Loop Hotel was a wonderful experience.”
text: I recently spent a long weekend in Chicago with my two young adult children, and I was more than satified with our accommodations at the Chicago South Loop Hotel. Our room was very large and clean, and the beds were extremely comfortable. The bathroom was remarkable, with one of the largest hotel bathtubs I have ever seen! The hotel has an amazing jazz feel, mostly due to the beautiful artwork displayed on the main level. It also boasts a resteraunt, lounge, deli, salon, fitness room, business center, and a small gift shop. Parking was plentiful and free - an unusual combination among Chicago hotels. The staff was friendly and helpful, and made us feel very much at home. The only downside was a lack of rerigerator in the room. It would also be nice if the gift shop had "set " hours instead of the sporadic hours it was open. All in all, though, we had a wonderful visit, and I would not hesitate to stay here again in the future.

title: “Hot Tub Suites”
text: Highly recommend the Hot Tub suite, room 1103 with the view of Baltimore skyline, worth the extra money. Even the normal room for our daughter and kids, room 1120 was spacious. The heated (85 degrees) indoor pool was a hit with me and the grand kid. There was a Life guard on duty until 10PM. The gym was great and just off the swimming pool. The free breakfast was better than Embassy Suites. The kids loved making their own waffles. The dinner theater in the hotel was an awesome treat. The only suite room complaint is the couch was old and needed replacing. The in house restaurant was average but the lady restaurant manager Theresa was great. The level of all hotel management and staff was outstanding.

title: “Very nice”
text: Stayed here recently for two nights on a business trip. The hotel was great - good location and modern rooms. The hallways on each floor are relatively short, so you don't ever feel like you're walking a mile to your room. The rooms on ends of each hall are really strangely shaped, but offer a little alcove with a coffee maker that's good for storing suitcases or placing a room service tray out of the way. The cookie at check-in is always a nice touch and there is a Starbucks in the Hyatt just across the street. Overall, really nice but nothing crazy spectacular.

title: “Great Hotel and Great Location”
text: We stayed at the IC Times Square for three nights. We were given a room on the 5th floor, but awoke earlier than desired due to noise from the elevator cable (our room must have been nearby). The front desk graciously moved us to a room on the 14th floor and all was well. This hotel is brand new and in a perfect location. Our children, 11 and 7, absolutely loved it. It is two blocks from Times Square (the lights) and nearby everything. The subway is literally right next door too. Checkout was a breeze and we will stay there again next time in New York.

title: “Basic, clean, great location”
text: This is the first hotel I've stayed in that did not have a clock radio in the rooms. Also no ice maker. The room keys are old fashion brass tags that are turned in at the desk when leaving. My room was large with large dresser, desk and night stand. Large closet with removeable hangers. Bath had been re-modeled with new fixtures and the windows were new. Carpet and bedding were basic and relatively new. Cable TV was also basic and was knocked out totally one morning by a storm. Two deli's next door. The luggage storage were $5 lockers in the back room. I didn't use phone system, so can't comment. Bottom line it's good value for the dollar given it's NYC. I've stayed in worse for more money.

title: “Dated, but clean and friendly staff”
text: When i first arrived, i got lost because the place is huge! Staff was friendly and pointed me in the right direction many times. The food was good, and i particularly enjoyed charlie's and the great service by aaron and sarah. Overall, i would stay again

title: “All that we hoped”
text:
I know this review is a little late in coming. We stayed at La Mansion between Christmas and New Year's for our 30th anniversary. I like historic hotels and we wanted to see the lights on the River Walk. Everything was perfect. I had read some of the reviews that stated River Walk rooms had trees that blocked their view so when I made the reservation I requested that it be an unobstructed view and let them know it was our anniversary. We got exactly what we wanted. We also booked a package that included valet parking, breakfast, and a river tour. 
It is right on the River Walk and we were there during a holiday so we expected it to be noisey but it wasn't so noisey that is bothered us. We checked-out the day of the Alamo bowl so during our stay at any moment one of the college bands or Pep squads could break out in a song or cheer right across or under our balcony. All of this actually enhanced our experience and while I know the hotel didn't put this on just for us if you want a exceptionally quiet place this is not for you. We however loved it all!
Because it rained one day of our stay we decided to try out the restaurant/bar for lunch. We enjoyed it and would definitely eat there again. 
Service everywhere was excellent.
Thank you La Mansion del Rio

title: “Fun for Families”
text: This resort has activities to keep the kids and parents busy all day long. The lazy river, water slide and miniture golf course are all within a short walk of your room. This is a popular resort, even during the hot summertime, so this is not the place for people who don't like crowds or children. A car is a must since dining options here are very limited.

title: “Comfortable, great value and location”
text:
We've gone to this hotel to spend weekends and visit different Chicago attractions. We find it to be clean, comfortable, in a great spot (very close to subway station and the "Magnificent Mile"), not too expensive, and with free breakfast!
We've made reservations on-line, and even though we have gone earlier than the official check-in hour, the room has always been ready for us. Breakfast is not some sort of "amazing experience", but it is free, you serve yourself the quantities you want/need and there is a lot to choose from: eggs, waffles, fruit, juices, breads, yoghurts, coffee, cereals, etcetera.
There is a fire station just a block away, so you will hear sirens often. Some might find this annoying, but for us it hasn't been a big deal. For us it is a highly recommendable hotel.

title: “Not great, but not bad either”
text:
Had to spend 5 nights in Jacksonville for business. I like Omni's very much. I did have a few small gripes which may seem petty, but not to me.
I prefer a firm mattress, this one was one of those pillow-top types, nice enough but just not firm enough for my liking.
The real issue I had was with the shower. The water was warm, but I couldn't get it hot. Who doesn't want a hot shower? And more importantly, the shower liner was really mildewy and smelled terrible. Not quite the optimal shower experience.
On the positive side, front desk people were incredibly helpful and friendly, the rooms were clean and spacious, and the internet free if you are an Omni member.
Not bad, but not great.

title: “/my Stay!”
text:
Initial appearance of hotel could be improved as you can not see it from the road. 
Great Value - Room needs updating furniture, tub, mattress, TV etc.
