Breakfast was limited and could offer a little more variety. Would I stay again.? Yes, if I was spending a week for training like I did this time. Would I bring my family? Probably NO. .

title: “It's just a place to sleep...”
text: My husband and I check into this hotel every year for the holidays, there are nicer places to stay but for the an overnight stay and parking (up to 2 weeks) for the price, you really can't complain. This time we took an unexpected vacation in August and them it another try, this time we stay on the 1st floor. We have stayed on every floor and by far it is much quieter on the first, the staff is very friendly and helpful, another add bonus is they will take or pick you up at the airport.

title: “Mediocre at best”
text:
This hotel was average at best, and once your factor in price its totally not worth it! 
Overall this is a really small hotel with an extremely awkward layout. Once you get off the elevator you feel like you are walking through a maze to find your room. Like many reviewers have said, the rooms are really small, but I am used to staying in NYC so that didnt bother me so much, what I disliked most about the room was lack of privacy and noise control. I could clearly hear conversations of guests in neigboring rooms spoken at normal volume - which means they could hear everything I said too, and if street noise bothers you, you should know you can hear everything happening outside too. It is in an older building that lacks any insulation/noise control, rather than considering guest comfort and privacy and doing work to fix this, they have tried to make it look like a modern hotel by covering it up with cheesey decor that tries too hard to be swanky and cool . The bathrooms were poorly designed, and in an attempt to be sleek and hip they chose to use an immoble glass plate as a partial screen instead of a shower door or curtain. The bathroom was laid out in a way that it required you to literally climb over the toilet to get around this glass partition and into the shower. Then this partial glass wall didnt even block the water, so when you climbed back out over the toilet you had to be careful not to slip on the now wet tile floor. 
In a nutshell this hotel seemed to be trying too hard to be hip with its design and lacked real quality. For the price they ask you can do better, not sure how they got a 4 star rating.

title: “WOW - What a great hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Tuscan Inn for four nights in mid May 2009. We were in town for the Bay to Breakers.
What a wonderful spot.
We had a car, so we started with the valet. He was very friendly, and explained just what we had to do to retrieve our car – when they were available (24/7), how long to expect to wait to retrieve the car ( about 7 minutes), etc. He also helped us with our bags to the front desk.
The front desk staff were very friendly and efficient. Our room rate was all in order – we’d booked a TravelZoo special, and the front desk had the right rate, and the right parking discount.
We asked for a high room, and off the street. We got exactly that. 
We went down for the free wine reception, and had a great time. We met a number of other travellers, and the wine pour-ers and hostess were very friendly and efficient. The wine reception each night became an event we looked forward to (for more than just the wine!). The wine is Charles Shaw (two buck Chuck) so you wine afficianados should not get too excited, but it was fine for our standards. 
The room itself was a little small - pretty normal for the wharf area. But it was immaculate and nicely decorated. The bed was big and very comfortable. One interesting thing – the room doors open out to the hallway, rather than in to the room. This makes the room seem slightly bigger, as the door does not swing into the room, taking up space. I’m surprised more hotels don’t do this. The bathroom door does the same thing, making the bathroom seem slightly larger.
The room was very quiet. We'd seen some reviews saying the rooms that face the street are noisy, so by asking for a room off the street, we got a very quiet room.
The air conditioning worked perfectly. Yes – we needed air conditioning in San Francisco. It was unseasonably warm when we were there.
We ate in the hotel restaurant – an Italian theme – and it was very good. Good food and service.
The concierge was very helpful and extremely friendly. We did find the concierge was very busy in the mornings, trying to arrange tours for people. 
We didn’t use the workout facility.
The hotel has one computer (with printer) available with free internet. And free wi-fi throughout the hotel which worked flawlessly.
This is a Best Western, but it is operated by Kimpton - so it is pet friendly. They advertised that with a picture of the manager's dog on the check in desk. 
All in all it was a wonderful stay and I’d highly recommend it – we did get an amazing rate, so that made it seem even better.
The location is excellent if you want to be near the wharf. It was a two block walk to Pier 39. And the street it was on (North Point), was busy enough to always feel safe walking, but not so busy that you felt crowded.
The only downside, is not a fault of the hotel – rather, my personal preference. We usually stay in the Marina District, but we wanted a hotel near the wharf so we could walk to the Bay to Breakers (we didn’t want to stay near Union Square, even though it would have been more convenient).
I like visiting the Wharf, but personally, I’d rather stay in the Marina District, and visit the wharf. To be honest, I was pretty sick and tired of the wharf after four days. But again, that was my choice, not a hotel problem.
All in all, if you want to stay near the wharf, I’d highly recommend the Tuscan Inn. Though I’d try to get a discounted rate.

title: “We WILL be back!”
text: We can't begin to describe our stay at Tower 23. From the moment that we walked in to the lobby to check in, to the moment that we checked out, we had a wonderful experience. We stayed in a "Surf Pad" room with a 2nd floor balcony that looked out over the ocean. It was a birthday celebration that the hotel recognized with a complimentary room service appetizer and dessert tray. A perfect location to be able to walk to good restaurants, and short drive to La Jolla restaurants, and Gaslamp restaurants.

title: “Solid”
text: Overall, no complaints. Cheap, clean, professional, easily accessible. Best Target ever right by there too! Only nitpicking comments are that a free continental breakfast would be nice, as would a refrigerator and box of tissues in the room. In any case, at the low Priceline rate, I was very pleased with what I had. The nearby Target provided a good and inexpensive breakfast.

title: “Stressful Hilton Weekend”
text:
We stayed here at the Hilton for a long, Easter weekend. The Hilton Club actually invited my husband and I to check out their new 57th Street property - and we tacked on an additional day to enjoy the city sites - - a good idea, you would think? Well, we were probably better off going home.
The hotel is like Grand Central Station - especially the entire lobby area which was loaded with people, noise and NO security! Anyone could get into the hotel off the street and onto your floor without showing ID. We were never asked for a room key.
The elevators were horrible. We were consistently waiting going up and going down for an available elevator. By the end of our stay, it was growing pretty old.
The glorfied "cafeteria-style restaurant" was SO overpriced - - breakfast for our family of 3 was $76.00!! It was just breakfast!
There was no free internet, I think the charge was something like $12 or 14 per day. Ugh.
And let's not forget the $42/day we paid for parking. I needed a serious trip to the cash machine to take care of all the expenses on this little NYC getaway. (and i'm from NJ!!!)
The finale of the stress was upon checkout. Before we decided to tack on an additional day, the gentleman at the front desk quoted us a $225 corporate rate. We get our bill and it says $299!!! It took about 20 minutes to settle this dispute that wasn't even our fault. The manager at the front desk was rude and completely didn't take our word for this rate. (Like we made it up??). Oh, and I even forgot about how we were locked out of our room because they had us checked out. We then had to go to the front desk and get new keys!
Finally, everything's settled with the front desk, they finally honored our $225. We were going to finish up the rest of our double decker bus tour. We decide to check our luggage at the hotel. Would you believe the Hilton wanted to charge us $3.50 PER bag to store our luggage? Just what I needed to spend, another $14.
At that point, I was like -- let's just go home. We all had enough of this Hilton hotel. I'll never stay at that hotel and ..and forget about even thinking of buying their time share property - the reason we came to the hotel in the first place. They were very rude and unaccomodating at the front desk. 
If you're looking to spend some time in NYC, do yourself a favor, stay somewhere else where you can be treated like a human being. Ugh!

title: “Exceptional Value”
text: Spent four days in DC this past week and stayed at this hotel. The staff was very friendly and very helpful. Our rooms were clean, and the beds comfortable. They have a shuttle to take you into the mall, and the Metro is not far. We actually walked to the mall one day which only took a half hour pushing a stroller! The building is older and in need of updates, but not run down by any means. One thing to keep in mind is that they do have the pool parties on the weekend. They did not bother us, but they are NOT for kids by anymeans. All in all considering price, location, and staff, I would recommend this place to most everyone.

title: “GREAT bed!! WONDERFULbreakfast. VERY clean!! Would recommend any day.”
text:
We stayed one night at this Columbus Airport East location. The bed was very nice and comfortable (I always look for a good bed), isn't that what you go for to sleep??
The room was VERY clean. That is the 2nd thing I look for. The continental breakfast was the best that we have had anywhere. There were eggs, bacon, sausage, waffles, fresh fruit, whipped cream for the fruit and waffles. Also was cereal, bagels, toast, biscuits, gravy. Many times, we just skip the cont. breakfasts and go to Cracker Barrel, but not in this case. It was very good. GREAT PLACE to stay. Would absolutely come back.

title: “Highly recommend”
text:
I had a corner room with an amazing view of the city. Hotel bar was well stocked. Staff were very welcoming. I had no problems sleeping, however I've been told the street noise can keep you awake if you're a light sleeper. The concierge was extremely knowledgeable, helpful, and hands down the best concierge I've ever seen. 
Starlight Room on the 21st floor offers spectacular views, interesting cocktails, and turns into a club later in the evening.
Location is great, Tenderloin and China Town are within walking distance. If you don't mind a little longer walk (with a lot of hills) you can reach Fisherman's Wharf, Ghirardelli Square, and Lombard Street. Starbucks is next door and one of those trolley things stops right outside the hotel.
Make sure to join the Kimpton In Touch rewards program, it's free and the perks include free wireless internet and 2 drink tickets (at least in San Francisco).
Will definitely stay here again.

title: “It may have just been the day.”
text:
My family and I just returned from a stay at Doubletree, August 9th one night, 99% of the reviews give this property an A+. Yes, the property is clean and the rooms quiet, but the front desk staff were not accomodating, I think mainly because of a conference in the hotel of a law school, this group seem to have priority. Rooms were not ready on time, not just my family, but other families as well, now this could happen anywhere, the attitude is what bothered me the most, "take it or leave it". The bell hop's were over worked, no room to store luggage. I think the main point of my review, is guest beware, if Hilton can make money off a conference, then regular guests suffer, I guess that is what business all about these days, the all mighty dollar.
 If you are looking for location, cannot beat it, security is amazing at the hotel, hats off to the doorman/ladies.
If you do not require a suite, I would recommend Hilton Times Square on 42nd.

title: “IPO restauraunt at the W chicago”
text:
Ate dinner at IPO, which is new restaurant at the W. Great food. ordered the grape salad, and the seared ahi tuna. The grape salad was light and tasted great. Great salad for upcoming tuna. The tuna dish was very good. Also ordered their carrots (side dish). It is not like your typical carrot side dish. It was incredible. 
For Dessert, had the gelato trio. Service was great. Waiter was James. Very helpful and pleasant staff. I highly recommend this restaurant.

title: “NICE PROPERTY & GOOD EXPERIENCE”
text:
We are looooong time Marriott timeshare owners now re-evaluating Marriott properties within the Marriott system, and this is the third such property evaluated since June 2011. Please see my other reviews; one was good and one dismal.
This property is very well run, and staffed by people who seem to be actually happy that we came to stay.
The good:
Front desk STAFF: Very friendly, efficient and informative. We avoided the check in madness that characterizes Marriott by arriving one day late. We had asked for and recieved a room in a quiet area,
Concierge: solid C+, no better, no worse.
Housekeeping: Exceptional in their execution of duty. Our room was CLEAN!!!
Windows were washed, mirrors were streak free, carpets, countertops, etc were CLEAN. Silverware and utensils were spotless. Glassware was sparkling clean. Patio area was clean and usable.
This is very much different than the last Marriott we stayed at.
Maintainence staff: Very efficient and very tuned in to guest needs and quite willing to go out of their way to offer the random act of kindness.
One maintainence fellow saw us parked in the handicapped parking (I'm handicapped) and struggling with luggage. He stopped what he was doing and came over to offer help. That's a first for us in a Marriott property. 
We encountered a scorpion in the room on night 4. Not a big deal but we called to report the incident as they request. We had a maintainence staff member at our door in 10-15 minutes, just to offer help, even though we did not request it.
GROUNDS: are the usual Marriott spectacular. Well groomed, litter free, and carefully covered each night to ward off any chance of frost. Yes, it gets cold in the desert at night.
BBQ grills were spotless and cleaned by staff daily. We did use them one morning.
Childrens play areas were well thought out and mixed fun with education for the kids.
POOLS looked very inviting, but it was too cold even think about outdoor swimming.
LOCATION is in a residential neighborhood but once in the grounds, you would never know it. Good shopping is very close and freeway access is very convenient.
The BAD:
MEETING ROOM / COMMON AREA is small, and a bit crowded during a function. We just walked away from one such function because of the crowding.
Kitchen Hood fan was non-operational. Housekeeping should have caught that before we got there.
The in-sink trash disposal was taken out. Not an issue for us, but for others this might be important.
OVERALL: Very clean and well managed property. We will go back.
Thanks to the management and staff at this facility for a job well done.

title: “Best Boutique Hotel in NYC!!!”
text:
The Iroquois Hotel is a wonderful boutique hotel, with a perfect location in midtown. 
From the time we arrived we were warmly welcomed and greeted by their friendly staff, from the doorman, to the front desk staff and housekeeping. Every person we came in contact with at this hotel was genuinely kind and made us feel so very welcomed. The concierge staff went above and beyond to find us theater tickets, and a wonderful pre-theater , 3 course dinner at Le Cirque, and many other activities to enjoy during our stay. 
We cannot say enough good about this wonderful hotel! 
I have already shared our experience with many friends and work colleagues and will continue to share your praises.

title: “Fantastic hotel. Great customer service.”
text:
Fantastic hotel. 
Short walk to the underground station and from there it’s a short train ride to the heart of Washington DC. 
The customer service was EXCELLENT. Our travel agent had made an error and our booking for our stay here couldn’t be found by hotel staff (we later worked out it was not the fault of the hotel). But while they sought to rectify it with the travel company, they gave us a room instead of making us wait - and that was the last we heard of the booking issue.
The rooms themselves, and indeed the entire hotel, is very well presented, comfortable, clean and have tea & coffee making facilities. It seems like a hotel where its main clients are corporates, hence the presentation. In fact Obama gave speech in one of the function rooms while we were there.
Breakfast at the hotel’s restaurant was a bit pricey for a continental breakfast. You can go a slightly more expensive option and get the buffet though.
Would definitely stay there again. Great accommodation.

title: “For A Change of Pace.....”
text: Watertown advertises itself as "a unique urban hotel" and it is, offering such amenities as wine tasting in the afternoon, bike rental, and a variety of fun "carts" that one can reserve free of charge! I chose the spa cart which contained everything I needed to have a relaxing retreat in the bath, right down to music choices (and the best part was no extra charge). The continental breakfast was way above average, the decor very modern and sleek, and not typical of standard hotel room configuration (plus, everything was immaculate). There was a well-stocked little area in the lobby for snack purchases, as well as a nice workout room and conference rooms. The staff was very pleasant and competent, and obviously cared about doing a good job; rates were very reasonable. Contributing to its hip, urban feel was the close proximity of the University of Washington--we enjoyed walking around the area and even found a wonderful little farmer's market several blocks north which offered local specialties in seasonal produce and baked goods. We will definitely make the Watertown our hotel of choice during our next opportunity to visit Seattle!

title: “Disappointing From Start to Finish”
text:
My wife and I stayed 2 nights at the Loews in late July while attending a professional conference in the city.
Our problems with the hotel began with check-in. We had received an e-mail telling us that check-in commenced at 3pm, so when we arrived at the hotel shortly before 3pm we weren't too surprised to find that our room wouldn't be ready for a little while. When we checked back about 30 minutes later they told us it would still be a while and that they would call us when it was ready (in fairness the desk person did provide us with a couple of drinks coupons for the bar). An hour or two later we still hadn't been contacted and so we checked back with the desk only to be told that it would still be a while and to await their phone call. Finally, approximately 4hrs after first arriving at the hotel and desperately needing a room so that we could get ready for a 7pm reception we checked back with the desk and were told that our room was ready - no phone call, no nothing. We later found out that people who had arrived at the hotel an hour or two after us had no problems getting a room even though we were still waiting! During this 4hr wait we looked around the hotel to try to find somewhere comfortable to pass the time, however the only space appeared to be in the restaurant/bar and once we finished our drinks we felt obliged to move on. After wandering around other parts of the building it became evident that there just aren't any good social areas in the hotel, even the lobby area doesn't really lend itself to hanging out. 
When we were finally given key cards to the room they were incorrectly coded so we had to rush downstairs to take care of that. Our room (822), once we did get into it, was also a little disappointing. While the view was nice enough, a glance around the room revealed that it needed some freshening-up (rust stains in the sink, scuff marks on the ceiling, etc). It just gave the impression of a room that had seen slightly better days. Coupled with this there were at least two occasions during our stay when the wait for elevators was very long. Additionally, it appears that wifi is not available for free and parking is very expensive (NOTE: a very short 2 blocks south at 12th & Sansom is a Central Parking facility - they usually have a coupon online which means that parking there costs 1/2 the price of the hotel parking). 
Overall, our short stay did not give us a good impression of this hotel. While I think this is an interesting, historic building I'm not convinced that it makes for a great hotel space. The mismanagement of our check-in process definitely didn't get us off to a good start, but the hotel and its services did little to help win us back.

title: “Hotel Amazing!”
text: I can't comment on how great and respectful everyone was at hotel Adagio. My gf and I went and stayed through the busiest time, New Years Eve, the staff were great, the hotel clean, the bar was great and friendly. Our trip was nothing short of extraordinary! Great management, great service. Highly recommended!

title: “Only stayed a night - very comfy bed!”
text: Only stayed one night, but it was very nice. Large comfortable bed. room was a little dingy, and the view wasn't amazing 0 but then its right next to an airport so what can one expect!?

title: “A Dream of A Hotel”
text: Beautiful location, clean, relaxing, quiet hotel, I heartily recommend it as a luxurious, reasonably priced get away. The only slight hesitation I have is that internet service was spotty in the room I was in.

title: “a non serious place to stay”
text:
if you can avoid this place, do it! The building is old, the rooms are big but not very conservated. The housekeeping does not touch in your bed if something lies on it. The breakfest is not good similar to a harbour restaurant. 
To complete the disguisting experience the hotel charge me twice for the stays and simply ignored my request to backcharge, even with de CC statment attached showing his errors!

title: “Fabulous customer service and attention to detail”
text: I travel weekly for business and always enjoy staying at westin properties because the quality and service is consistently good. However I have to commend the staff at the westin San Diego for really going above and beyond the call of duty. I had a challenging situation when I arrived and I have to say that the front office manager Luke profancik was solutions- oriented and took time to make sure that everything was resolved exceeding my expectations. It is always nice to stay at locations where the staff make you feel like family. Daniel Lucas couldn't have been more pleasant and helpful - And always had a smile no matter how busy he was. If you stay there you will be greeted with a warm welcome and the quality experience we expect at westin properties.

title: “Wonderful stay at the Gansevoort”
text: This hotel has it all: location, views, great rooms, super comfortable beds, a fabulous bar, a great roof top pool and amazing service. We were treated with 5 star service from the moment we arrived to our departure. I highly recommend the Gansevoort as THE place to stay in NYC. I work in the hospitality industry and have stayed in NYC many times. The Gansevoort will always be my first pick from now on.

title: “Great location, below standard service and rooms”
text:
The Dupont Hotel has everything going for it--great architecture, great location, even a great restaurant (with an excellent brunch menu). Unfortunately, it's lacking in a few areas that you come to expect from a 4-star: 1) quality, attentive service; 2) working TVs; and, 3) bathroom doors.
The check-in experience is nice enough, the staff were very courteous and helpful. However, that's about the best service you'll interact with the rest of your visit. The majority of bellhops are worthless--only one (a younger guy who worked evenings) was helpful. On the day of our departure, we had a lot of luggage and the other two barely lifted a finger to help us get our luggage into our taxi. We even had a tip in our hand, ready to pay for the service but they just wheeled our luggage out the front door and quickly disappeared. Quite disappointing. Also, it rained while we were in DC and we didn't come with umbrellas. Normally, a 4-star would have loaners to help unprepared guests but not at the Dupont Hotel. When I asked I was told to cross the Circle and by one at CVS. Thanks for the help.
Also, we ordered room service for dessert on night. The person who delivered it was very nice but why should it take 40 minutes to deliver a smoothie and slice of cake? They did follow-up with a call to see how we enjoyed our meal but if they spent that time instead actually getting the food out the door in a reasonable amount of time, then I would be more impressed.
Second, the hotel uses a satellite dish for TV, meaning that when it rains or is windy you have no TV. Not usually a problem but when you're tired and it's raining outside and all you want to do it watch TV, it's kind of annoying for a 4-star to have figured out a way to get the TV signal back up and running several hours after the last storm cloud has passed. If they can't figure it our, just breakdown and get cable like the rest of us.
And finally, I love modern hotels but I also like bathroom doors. I mean, is a bathroom door that anti-modern? Be forewarned that if you're traveling with someone you'll need to turn the TV way up to give yourself some privacy in the bathroom.
In the end, great location but substandard on many of the little things that distinguish a 4-star from the rest.

title: “Roosevelt Hotel New York”
text: Absolutely beautiful hotel, the service is excellent, the rooms are sensational, the most comfortable bed, easy to get around New York walking distance to Times Square, and other attactractions, we would recommend staying there for everyone ,

title: “Vintage chic on a budget”
text: I stayed at the Jane for a week in July 2011, and loved every minute of it. The hotel has a great location, and i mostly walked everywhere I wanted to get to. Sure the rooms are tiny, but they are cute as a button. The bathrooms are shared, but they are spacious and spotless. The whole hotel is beautifully decorated in vintage style. The bar was fun, the restaurant served delicious food, and all of the staff were wonderful. I am certainly coming back in 2012.

title: “great spot quick NYC trip”
text: Stayed here with family age range 17 to 77, and everybody thought it was great. New hotel with nice facilities, and very comfortable beds. Small rooms, but that's to be expected. Dan the bellman will take care of you.

title: “CHARGED TWICE FOR ROOM -- WHERE'S MY CREDIT?”
text: I would have given this hotel higher marks, but I pre-purchased a voucher from Otel. com for TWO HOTEL ROOMS and I told the front desk staff. They assured me that yes the rooms were prepaid and they took a credit card for the deposit for any room incidentals. Well, guess what? Our guests woke up to find a bill under their door, yes I was charged twice for this room. Otel says that I need to wait 5 to 20 days. Sir Francis Drake had an original credit pending and now it is now my bank cannot find it. I'm out $122.50 and I'm very mad. And, the price that I paid was $300.60 for two rooms $150.30 per room and I was charged even less directly from Sir Francis Drake @ $122.50. Sorry to rant, but maybe I'll get a response for the Sir Francis Drake or Otel.com. This is very disturbing.

title: “Chic But Comfortable”
text: This was my second stay at the Hotel Valencia in San Antonio. Each was a business trip to a downtown client. The location is terrific -- adjacent to the Riverwalk with beautiful views of the river, and within relatively easy walking distance of most of the downtown sites, including the Alamo. The interior is dark and quiet (almost somber), because they are trying for an upscale chic look. Rooms are comfortable, but a bit eclectic in decor because of the overall look the hotel is going for. The hotel restaurant (Citrus) is a great choice for breakfast. This is a nice alternative to the large convention hotels that tend to predominate on the Riverwalk.

title: “Great Family Place”
text: Because we didn't get much of a family vacation, I told my boys that their first 3 day holiday we would book a trip where ever American had a netsaver. Well, last weekend the Netsaver from Dallas to Chicago was $139. We booked the Lakeshore Embassy suites ($279 a night). First, Chicago is a great place to take the family. There were tons to do. The hotel's location is so-so. It is great if you are interested in the Navy Pier and things on that side of town. You can walk to Navy Pier in 5 minutes. We did that on Saturday. It is quite a ways (about 2.5 miles) from the Museums. We bought a CTA pass that will take you on any train or bus in town. It was $9 a piece for a 2 day pass, but it sure saved on cab fares. The only problem is that the main line (the red line) is about 5 blocks from the hotel. That would not be a big deal unless the weather is bad, which it was on Sunday and Monday. So, if you want a hotel closer to the line, you might look somewhere else. Anyway, we did the Bears game on Sunday...a great way to experience true Chicago. We ate at the typical pizza joints (Gino's East and Giadarnos sp?). The hotel itself is really nice. Getting into it is a little cumbersome. You go into a small lobby on the street level where the bellmen are then take an elevator to the Sky Lobby located on the 6th floor. Then check in. The main lobby is huge and very open with lots of windows. In the main lobby you have the manager's reception at night (mixed drinks, beer, wine, sodas, snacks) and breakfast in the a.m. Breakfast was quite good (omlette station, pancakes, egss, bacon, sausage, hash browns, and assorted pastries and breads). There was a pool and hot tub, but according to my boys (who are like polar bears) the pool was too cold and the hot tub too hot. The rooms are typical Embassy Suite rooms. We booked a corner suite, which was great. We had a view of the lake, which was really nice. My only criticism is the walls are very thin. We could hear our neighbor's radio as well as other entertaining sounds at different points during the night and I am sure they could hear our boys early in the morning. The first night the hotel was packed, but with the Sox playing in the World Series I expected it. So the lines at the happy hour and breakfast were long. The next night and morning were much better. Let me know if you have any questions, but overall a great trip and good hotel.

title: “clean & friendly!”
text:
We originally had a room booked at the Courtyard Fisherman's Wharf. They oversold the hotel and sent us to the Courtyard Downtown. 
The staff at the Courtyard Downtown was professional and processed our reservation quickly. The front desk gave us a good recommendation for a pizza delivery and upgraded us to a King Suite for our troubles at the Courtyard Fisherman's Wharf. We were very appreciative of his efforts. The King Suite was very large and clean. There is free internet access in the lobby. Prompt Valet service.

title: “Birthday Party”
text:
The hotel was pretty good. We got some use out of the gym before going out. The bed was super comfortable. If possible ask for an extra fridge because the one that comes with the room is filled with small bottles and beverages sitting on pressure sensitive pads. 
I had gotten the room as a place to pregame before going out for my birthday. The London Suite fit at least 30 people, at least that's how many I counted at one point. We got a smoking room on the 18th floor. My friend had gotten a non smoking on the 10th floor. Possibly something to keep in mind. 
The ice machine is located in a room with a 'small sign' that says ice machine. Should be 2 doors down from the elevator. Sounds dumb but it'll make sense when your trying to look for it.

title: “A lovely stay! Can think of few things”
text:
Spent three nights at the Argonaut Hotel, booked online directly with the hotel for two standard rooms. The Argonaut is situated in a great location, offers a very good room, is attached to a great restaurant and offers excellent service. Overall, we were very pleased with our three nights here and would gladly return in the future. 
Hotel location is directly outside and just a few minutes walk to the Fisherman’s Wharf, making it ideally located for exploring this area of San Francisco. The famous Cable Car stations just around the corner and the Hyde Street Pier and very good Maritime museum ship attractions are directly across the street.
Room is decorated in a sailor theme but avoids falling into the tacky category. The color scheme was not to our preference but it wasn’t offensive either. The bed was soft thus falling asleep at night was no problem. The pillows were a bit too soft but not enough of a problem to have asked for another, which I'm sure they would have gladly given. Water pressure in shower was very good and cleaning staff made the room up very very tidy each day. 
Safe in room is large enough to hold laptop, one standard size camera body, another digital camera and all paperwork. Coffee machine in the bathroom was not the best in the world but fresh Starbucks coffee filters was a nice touch! WiFi was free if you registered for Kimberly membership. Or you can pay US$10 per day. 
There is also a very good restaurant attached to the hotel called Blue Mermaid Chowder House with tasty breakfast and excellent clam chowder for lunch. Return restaurant visits is a rarity for us. We ate there three times. 
The doormen, valet parkers, desk staff, concierge and room service staff were all very friendly and helped make the stay very pleasant. 
As a real touch of class, the Argonaut provided free wine sampling in the lobby each afternoon. This was easily beyond expectations we had for the Argonaut and helped seal the deal for an Excellent grade. 
Overall, our stay was excellent and we have no touble offering full recommendation for the Argonaut Hotel for holidays in San Francisco.

title: “Good but not great”
text:
Maybe I get out a little more often than the people who wrote the previous reviews. The hotel is not all that much of a big deal. The hotel lobby is in need of a renovation.
Location is good, 3 blocks from Michigan Avenue, but it is very close to House of Blues, Hard Rock Cafe and a few decent resturaunts.
If you like a large lobby, a lounge, and flowered carpet, this is your place.
The room was very nice and seemed new with good furniture and the view over the river was nice. The room was standard size
The staff was excellent, which is very important.
I believe I was on the 17 floor and you still could hear noise from the street.
The A/C system is set to go off if there is no motion in the room, this is ok if you are in Motel 6 but not a 4 star.
The valet was very helpfull.
If you like totally new hotels, try the Sofitel, the rooms are a bit smaller, but the hotel is new and hip and very close to the Rush street scene. Rooms stay very cold.

title: “A Perfect Stay - Home away from Home”
text: I live in Temecula area and I had to attend a conference in San Diego and was looking for hotels to stay at when I came across the Town and Country Resort. I spoke to Margaret Kennedy from the Sales Department and she was so pleasant and wonderful to talk to that I trusted everything that she said and was very convinced that this is the hotel to stay at. Well, she was right. The feeling as you walk in the hotel is like walking to your living room. The Front Desk and Bell Staff greeted you with a smile. Everyone was just so nice. I have stayed at hotels in San Diego and this just tops them all. I knew I was far from home but still got that feeling of HOME. It was a perfect stay for me. Unfortunately, it was a short one but I am convinced that I will let my collegues and friends know on how great I was treated at this hotel. Kudos to Margaret for such a warm first impression. She was the reason that I stayed at this property and I was very happy about my choice. Thanks, Margaret...you are truly a gem at your resort. I will definitely be back...SOON.

title: “historic but contemporary”
text:
The Liberty Hotel is a renovated jail- surprisingly, it was in use until relatively recently (70s-80s) before it was shut down (in the 90s?). Mass Gen Hospital next door bought it and it has been renovated into a hip, happening place to stay. The atrium is pretty cool to gawk at- there's a bar at which to have a drink, during which time you can gawk some more. Clink, the restaurant, has tables behind bars, literally. I can't comment on the food since I didn't eat there but the menu looked good.
I had a corner room in the Jail Tower- there is one other tower which my friend told me has similar accomodations. My room was on the corner, overlooking the hotel entrance. Nicely appointed and comfortable. I did not like the ventilation system which was very noisy (and I'm a pretty deep sleeper). I also did not like the soundproofing: because the walls are exposed brick, sounds reverberate throughout the halls- I could hear every conversation in the hallway while sitting in my room.
The location is fine, next door to MGH and across the street from the T- we went to Fenway and it was a very easy 15 min trip on the T. The hotel overlooks the Charles River, at the base of Bunker Hill.
The business center is joke. To print out my boarding pass would have cost $7. You're better off asking the concierge nicely- he can save you $7. Wireless access is NOT free, which irritates me to no end.
Front desk staff and concierge were friendly and helpful. The rooms are nicely appointed separate showers and tubs. The rooms are spacious and comfortable. TV is a little annoying since it is on a satellite, hence changing channels is slow and cumbersome.
All in all, a very nice, comfortable, hip hotel. I would definitely come back for a weekend with the wife, especially if I could get a room rate under $300.

title: “Modern, cealn and great location!”
text: Great hotel in the middle of it all. The staff was very polite and professional. The amenities were good: hair dryer, iron, etc... The room was extremely clean and very modern with it's decor. The bed was comfy and the view (facing south from the 30th floor) was incredible. I paid $200/night on Priceline. Definitely worth the price.

title: “Very nice place.”
text: We had a great stay at this hotel. Staff was friendly and courteous. Would stay here again.

title: “Great room; easy walk to restaurants, subway, grocery.”
text: The room was large, comfortable and clean. The hotel is right next door to the subway entrance and a taxi stand is out front. Doorman was great and very knowlegeable about what was close by. Easy walk to lots of restaurants, a small grocery and very safe neighborhood. Bus terminal is across the street. Fenway Park is right behind the hotel as is the House of Blues. Despite this, not noisy at night. Would definitely stay again. Parking is steep ($42 per day.)

title: “Elegant and refined”
text: We are a family of four. We spent Christmas in San Francisco and stayed at this beautiful property. We had a suite that had everything we needed to feel right at home. Having a Bose Ipod dock in the room was a welcome detail. Great staff, tasteful decor, excellent service throughout. Ritz-Carlton has always resulted in an excellent experience but this hotel in particular sets itself in a higher category.

title: “Even Better Than Expected!”
text:
We spent a week at the Hotel 1000 in Seattle, WA prior to going on an Alaskan cruise. Hotel 1000 far exceeded our expectations following extensive online research. 
You were thoroughly pampered and the words, "no" or "we can't" are not in the staff's vocabulary. They will literally jump through hoops to accomodate you and your needs, no matter what requests you may have. From the doormen to the front desk staff, we were quite impressed. The rooms (we had 7 of them) were just lovely and extremely clean and comfortable. We did not experience any service problems which have been written in previous reviews, i.e., housekeeping problems, lack of clean towels, etc. The French pressed in room coffee was a plus! The location was perfect, centrally located in downtown Seattle. There was rarely a need to use the rental car we had other than for sightseeing trips. There is great shopping and dining within walking distance. I just love and appreciate a hotel with the personal touches such as referring to you by name at all times. 
Our son lives in Seattle and we have stayed at many other fine hotels. The Hotel 1000 will now definitely be our hotel of choice!

title: “Nice Hotel in a Great Location”
text: We always enjoy staying in this Marriott property. The location can't be beat and the recent renovations have added to the attractiveness of the hotel. The only drawback is that it is pricey.

title: “Great Great Great”
text:
What can I say about the Belvedere:
It is an unassuming hotel on a side street off 8th avenue. It is very central for anything you might want to see or do in central or upper manhattan.
There were 4 of us and we booked two rooms. We were very pleased to have a Queen size bed each ( my sister had a single bed in the Radisson on Lexington sharing and they paid $30 for the room more than us).
Checking in was very quick-less than 5 mins -and our rooms were ready even though we arrived at 3 instead of 4.
The lifts were never a problem. I am sure if the hotel was very busy, maybe there would be a delay but we never waited long. Most of the time we got a lift straight away!!
We went to the diner across the road on 8th-In the Days Inn-but realised that breakfast in the Belvedere was better value-and ate in our hotel after that.
if you are looking for breakfast in the area-the Westside diner on 44th and 9th is very reasonable and very clean too!
I have to say that we were all very happy with our Belvedere experience. 
I booked the hotel for the four of us on the back of the advice given here and I was a bit nervous about my friends reactions.
Well I didnt need to worry as they have all said that they will stay in the Belvedere next time they are in NY. 
What more can I say?!

title: “Great hotel in a great location”
text: I stayed here for 3 nights in May on business. It's right on the Riverwalk and connected to the Rivercenter Mall. Very convenient to walk to the Convention Center. Rooms are clean and housekeeping does a good job. They have a work out room that has sufficient cardio equipment but the weight machines are better. They have an indoor and outdoor pool that is connected. Overall a great stay.

title: “Not bad, not great”
text: I was first annoyed by valet parking only. We like to come and go as we please and don't want strangers in our vehicle. The hotel was being renovated. Sheraton bought the Adam's Mark. The location is central and convenient. The pool area was nice and clean and on a roof. I was bothered by $11 a day internet access. Free WiFi in the lobby only. I would not pay full price for the room we stayed in.

title: “Perfect Location, 5-15 minutes from all major parts of Diego”
text:
This hotel is unbelievable. We travel around a ton and just got engaged and choose San Diego for the first time trip. We also pricelined our hotel. We were only 10 minutes walking from most major parts of San Diego's hot spots - 5th Ave! Also, the trolley is a 1/2 block walk and can take to anywhere for a couple bucks all over San Diego. Behind the hotel is Sea Village, a great place to grab lunch or take a walk on the Ocean. You will not find a better location and a solid hotel with good ameneties.
My fiancee and I will return to San Diego and will hope to stay here again.

title: “Room o.k., Check your bill , restaruant overpriced”
text:
Our stay was comfortable. The new bathroom was a pleasant surprise. tile and shower clean with good water pressure.
Beds were clean and comfortable but rug was a little dirty and not vacuumed well. I had conflicting info on how rooms were billed. When I called to make reservations the 800 number said that the rooms were billed by day with cost additions per number of people per room. At the hotel he said that the rental varied because of the fluctating market rate on rooms in the area. I figure a $20.00 difference. So have your price quote and reservation info available.
Parking is tight but available and getting in and out a challenge but the advantage of being close to Hollywood is a plus. Not very friendly staff . 2 out of 6 were nice.

title: “Spacious room Great views Affordable prices”
text: After travelling in Europe,Republic of Ireland and UK we could not believe that we left the best till last before we flew home to Australia. Fridges in these expensive hotels have extra costs. This fridge and small freezer was empty no extra costs. The amenities were easily accessible. Very comfortable bed. Coffee and tea making facilities and TV to watch at no extra cost. From Bell boys, Concierge (excursions) to reception desk staff everyone so helpful. Just ask ! Access to Internet. Restaurant in hotel has buffet breakfast and other meals. We felt like we were one of the family. The only complaint we had we did not stay longer.

title: “Very big and very nice!”
text: Impressions after staying at this hotel for one night - it is big, it is high standard throughout, hotel is clean and fresh, staff professional but not very personal. This hotel is a safe bet if predictable and very good is good enough, and cosy, romantic and personal is not on your wish list.Extra bonus was the amazing view offered in the breakfast area on one of the very high floors. It was absolutely beautiful, overlooking the Bay Bridge, Angel Island, and parts of the this interesting and vibrant city.

title: “Really Bad”
text: Really worst customer service, lousy front desk staffs, slow performance, can't even greet customers, noisy environment, worst wireless service...and so on...

title: “Home Away From Home”
text: I actually have been in Jacksonville, for work for the past few months. I tried the Quality Inn and the Microtel before I came to Value Place on Merrill rd. The rooms were bigger than both pricier hotels, for less money a month. The place is kept extremely clean, they have a large laundry facility, and are located in a quiet area, yet the local grocery store is less than a half of a mile away. The service at the front desk is the best part because I have been here two months and have seen people stay for one week and they treat us all with the same hospitable compassion. The other plus is that they run a sex offender background check on their guest and when my sister in law who is 14 came for a 2 week visit for the summer it was a relief to know that she was in a place that actually made an effort to help keep her protected. I would recommend Value Place on Merrill rd. to everyone who is looking for a relaxing stress free place to stay. Buffie, from Norfolk, Va.

title: “Anniversary”
text: Had a very wonderful evening. We enjoyed the pool view. Quiet location.

title: “Terrible experience”
text: Came in with 5 people 4 rooms after long flight from overseas tour. Exhausted. Counter staff are upset and lecture me on not having correct names on rooms (all in my name). After ten minutes of lecture. I asked for different counter person. The young man said he would just cancel my rooms right now. Had it not been after 6 pm and my Amex already billed $144 each room for 4 rooms I would have agreed and gone elsewhere. This is an old quality inn or ramada with a little facelift. Warnings in parking lot about theft. (rough area it appears). No hot water in morning barely warm. When I asked about was told maintenance not available. No more Wyndham garden for me

title: “Outstanding experience!”
text: From the moment we checked into the Hotel Vitale, we felt like pampered VIPs. The hotel is beautifully situated overlooking the Embarcadero and the historic Ferry Building. Upon arrival, we were greeted by friendly and professional staff who offered us a warm towel, infused with rosemary- a welcome surprise after a long flight. We were promptly shown to our room. The guest suites are beautifully appointed with organic materials that give every room a Zen like elegance. Rustic woods, muted colors and rich linens create a serene retreat from the hustle and bustle of the city below. Before heading out to dinner, we stopped into the hotel bar for a cocktail. Far from your typical sleepy hotel hangout, this was a chic, energetic meeting hangout for SF's young executives. I highly recommend the Hotel Vitale and look forward to my next stay!

title: “Perfect for our needs”
text: Stayed there for 4th of July weekend. Brought my (big) dog and had ample room in the top floor suite which had a nice size balcony. Am so grateful that the Kimpton Hotels are hospitable to dogs (of any size), which is so helpful to those of us that like to travel with our 4-legged family members. The front staff was friendly but not over imposing. The location is key if you know anything about Dallas. It is across the street from SMU and in the heart of University Park such that access to most parts of town is extremely easy. Did have one snafu with housekeeping missing my room but when asked to come and service the room, they did. Liked the quaintness of the hotel...not too big with easy in and out access. Overall it was perfect for our needs with our faithful friend. Plan to return in near future.

title: “Nice, tidy and good priced.”
text:
Clean and tidy low budget hotel.
Good service. Minutes away from downtown Detroit.

title: “Much Better Than I Thought It Would Be”
text: I was booked here not by choice but by the organizers of a national meeting. As such I was suspecting one of those Grand Old Dames of Washington Hotelery: Elegant once; now a little frayed. I was pleasantly surprised. First the common areas such as the meeting rooms and lobby are quite nice and clean and bright. The paint appears fresh; the carpets are plush and spotless. Actually the lobby is quite welcoming and very attractive if not downright elegant. The hotel personnel are attentive, friendly and efficient. The health club is very up scale and unbelieveably well equipped; much, much more than what one would normally expect at a hotel health club. Our breakfasts and lunches were catered thru the hotel (I am not sure who did the actual meal preparation - the hotel staff or an outside caterer). The food was top notch; bordering of the spectacular! I had one room service dinner which though not anything special was decent. My room was extra large. Talking to my fellow meeting attendees I found out that room sizes vary tremendously from the very large room in which I stayed (#519) to much smaller ones. Also, it just so happened that the heat was not working in my room (it was a very nasty five chilly April days; and I could have used some heat); whereas the opposite was true in some of the other rooms were my colleagues were staying: they wanted airconditioning - their rooms were hot as hell and they could not cool them off!! (This was the major complaint to our meeting organizers). My wife and I did spend some time walking around the immediate vicinity of the hotel. This also is a major plus as the hotel is very close to the White House (for those interested in such things) and some very nice restaurants (McCormick and Schmidts - seafood - and Jimmy's Steak House) as well as a Metro Station. Overall, and aside from the heating issue, I was very pleasantly surprised: I really enjoyed this hotel. It is a great or near great city hotel. I recommend it (hopefully management will get their heating/cooling problems resolved before summer arrives).

title: “Historical”
text: Great location, JFK stayed here the night before he was assassinated. Beautiful property, rooms were quite small and cramped bathrooms. Very clean and pleasant staff.

title: “Excellent! Recommend to eveyone”
text:
Stayed in the comfort inn midtown, with my boyfriend. Being students we didn't have a great deal to spend on a hotel so we thought that the Comfort Inn sounded reasonable. I wasn't sure what to expect, but as we entered our room we were really pleased with what we saw. The room was sparkling and was cleaned everyday. The staff were really friendly and couldn't do enough to help. The situation of the hotel couldn't be better. Just a stones throw from Times Square, Empire State Building, Macy's and 5th Avenue all within short walking distance. 
Once we left I realised I had left my wash bag at the hotel, full of brand new and unused Clinique products and MAC makeup, which I never thought I would see again. The next day my cousin went to the hotel on my behalf to enquire about my bag, to our surprise had been handed in by the maid, containing the full contents. This alone is a reason to stay at the Comfort Inn Midtown. It really put the icing on the cake for my boyfriend and I and made our trip to the city a happy memory.

title: “Favorite New York hotel experience in 20 years.”
text: Hotel is new and sleek and efficient. Amazingly comfortable bed, nice size bath, by New York standards. I think it would be considered a 5 star in Europe...including beautiful breakfast and a rooftop bar that is a great escape. Location was good for going in any direction. Staff warm and sincerely helpful; concierge a blessing. Best French food I have ever had just 2 blocks down on Madison.

title: “Great Family trip to the big apple!!”
text:
Having stayed at this hotel in February 2008, I was suprised to find that it was as good as I had remembered. Like the reviewer below states, the rooms are becoming slightly tired, bathrooms in particular, though are still large and comfortable.
Sleep quality was only troubled by the street noise on 8th Ave, but in New York it's to be expected. The beds and duvets are supremely comfortable, I wish I could have brought them home with me!!!
Breakfast was busy, mainly because we went down at 8.30 each morning so again, to be expected. Waffles are my new obsession!!!
The location of the hotel is ideal for people who want to be within easy walking distance of central park, bloomingdales, times square and rockerfeller. The subway is only a block or so away so getting around Brooklyn and Manhattan is a doddle.
Having stayed here twice, I wouldn't hestitate to book again, comfortable rooms, good breakfast, location fab and sleep quality superb!!
Colleen

title: “Tired of being nickeled and dimed.”
text:
Pay $13 a day for internet access, $13 a day for fitness room access, extra charge to unlock the fridge that is already in the room, $6 for the bottled water in your room if you don't want to go back to the shop in the lobby to buy the $2 soda because there are no vending machines in the building. I had just spent 11 days on the road earlier in the month and had stayed at motels that cost half the price and threw in all the extras. 
 Yes, the location is right downtown, but the rooms are a little tired, the carpeting is worn, and the cleaning leaves a little to be desired( there was an old used towel hanging in the bathroom at check in.) If you can get a room here for less than $120 go for it, otherwise I would look elsewhere.

title: “our experience”
text: room was so so. Breakfast was reasonable. Free courtsey shttle for 5 mile radius is a pure marketing gimmick in my unbiased opinion as traveller from florida for six nights stay at this hotel.The shuttle ride is subject to "availability" or" should be scheduled" according the convenience of the hotel staff or may not be available on Sunday through tuesday after 5 p.m. due to "slow business season". In other words all sort of excuses to avoid the courtsey shuttle facility to the customers. Hotel is located in a odd area without reasonable restaurants nearby or transportation facility for the customers other than cab service. Better to find another decent hotel for the money of average rate of $150 per night! I will not recommend this hotel to my relatives or friends.

title: “A great find if you need to be near the Galleria”
text:
We wound up at the Hilton thanks to Priceline and it was a great experience. This is what I have come to expect from the better part of the Hilton Hotel family of properties. It would be perfect for business travelers but also has the comfort and convenience (to the mall) that made it great for our personal getaway. 
Like the other "nicer" Hiltons I've stayed at the design of this one is decidedly modern, some would say austere if you go by the lobby. I think that's why it does not immediately strike you as a 4-star hotel as others have noted. It lacks the warmth and/or classic feel of other luxdury hotels, but it has all the services and ammenities. Go to the Fairmont or Ritz for your romantic weekend (but expect to pay more). 
The rooms are well appointed, in great condition and are very comfortable. The free bottles of water are always welcome (as opposed to those with the $6.00 neck tag) as were the chocolates and turn down service. We also had a chance to visit the 14th floor lounge. And while the breakfast was very short on protein (i.e it would kill an Atkins person!) it was fine for getting your day going, clean, well layed out, and well managed. 
Having stayed at the nearby JW Mariott and Omni hotels I would put this on a par with those (though again the JW probably is a warmer feelling hotel). And if you need to be in the Galleria area, it's a great choice.

title: “best breakfast in town”
text:
I hadn't stayed at the Harbor Court in years. Now that I work for myself I am a bit more price-sensitive. However, I recalled their excellent breakfast so I walked over from my other hotel and for about the same price got unlimited fresh orange juice and a delicious vegetable omelette.
I would recommend eating here at least once if you are staying in the downtown area.

title: “Unremarkable...”
text:
but not in a bad way. They did what they were supposed to and what was expected. A good value for the money. And pet friendly!!!
Above average full breakfast.

title: “Great Older Hotel”
text: The downtown location is great, especially to QWest field, for a Seahawks game. Staff friendly and helpful. The room ARE small, however very clean and well appointed. Recommend for quick overnights.

title: “Amazing Hotel in the Heart of the Action!”
text:
We arrived to find a HUGE (1900+ rooms!!) hotel with a HUGE, 20+ story tall atrium in the middle. We were very impressed with the design of the place, the elevator bank with 20 elevators, many of which are glass and the location! But then when we saw the view from the lounge of Time's Square we were AMAZED! WOW! What a view!
Definitely a must see property!!
The food in the restaurant was very nice... ate breakfast a couple mornings and also had drinks and munchies and everything was prepared very well.
Housekeeping has it's issues though... a little slow... We were gone all day, got back around 5PM to find our room was never touched. Also, we requested a cot on our first night only to get it the next day around 6PM.
The room are very nice, but parking is HEFTY! $80 for a truck/SUV, so we parked around the corner for $62/nt (including taxes) at Central Garage.
The ability to walk right out of the hotel and into Time's Square is priceless though!

title: “Good but i have had better experiences”
text:
The location is great, near by the theaters. The rooms are edgy, pretty modern. I must say that the bathroom lock did not work. The area where you could sit and take the breakfast does not match the style of the rest of the hotel, in fact look a little deteriorated.
The construction in front f the hotel was not as noisy as i thought was going to be.

title: “Great hotel in the ideal location”
text: The Hyatt is located on E 42nd St, right next door to Grand Central Station - you really don't have a chance to get wet in the rain when arriving by train. The rooms and lobby have all been recently renovated with a very modern yet functional theme. Web check-in was a breeze and the room was available 4 hrs early (1/2 hr ahead of my request on the train). Hotel is 8 blocks from 30 Rock & Radio City Music Hall, St Patrick's, Empire State Bldg, and theater district. 2 blocks from the Chrysler Bldg & just a few blocks west of the UN. It's located right next to the Lexington Ave line (4, 5, 6 trains) making access to Uptown & Downtown (City Hall, WTC, 9-11 Memorial, Greenwich Village, Statue of Liberty, Ellis Island) accessible within 15 min of leaving your hotel. We left our room at 11:45, did the express checkout at the "no brainier" kiosk, walked next door to Grand Central, bought our Metro North tix (yes, there was a line), found our departing track and boarded the 12:07 to New Haven with 7 min to spare - no joke. A great experience in a VERY convenient location.

title: “Well maintained but expensive for the room”
text: why would a room have a step up in it soon after you enter the door? Not sure but it reminded me of a room I once stayed in Vegas with a sunken living room. It has to be a safety hazard which is why it's lit at night so you don't stumble down the two steps if you head to the bathroom. The internet connection worked well. The room was clean. The night staff were very knowledgeable about the area. However, the morning person was uninformed about the free pass I could get for working out at the nearby MetroFitness training facility which is just two short blocks away from the hotel. Skip the valet parking and park one block away for $6 at the public lot. And skip the buffet breakfast while you're at it - it's not worth the $8.95 for the eggs and bacon. My main beef with the hotel is the price - it just is not a lot of value for the price.

title: “One memorable stay”
text: My wife and I just celebrated our fifth year wedding anniversary. As part of this celebration we spent a night at the Marriott Baltimore Waterfront Hotel. The hotel staff was very courteous and our room had an excellent view of the harbor. I say thanks to all who made our anniversary a memorable one. I plan to be back some time and certainly recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Cool, hip and chic”
text:
I was there with a friend visiting for 3 nights in one of the most beautiful cities. I am glad I stayed at this hotel. Its convenient to Union Square and public transit as well as hopping on BART to head to the airport.
The rooms are modern, classy and roomy. The bathroom is quite big and the lighting is good. The only downside to this hotel is the water pressure. It literally took 30 seconds to fill a small glass of water from the tap and taking a shower is a bit of a pain. The bathroom also lacked a bath tub which would have been nicer considering that they bathroom is quite big. Some hooks in the bathroom would be nice too.
I will be back for sure.

title: “They lost our reservation”
text:
We made a reservation over the hotel's website. We received a confirmation via e-mail, with a confirmation number. We received an e-mail prior to arriving, saying that 'they' were looking forward to our visit.
When we arrived (4:00 p.m. on the scheduled day), we were told that they had no record of our reservation, could not locate the reservation number, and had no rooms available. The receptionist did offer us one night free in a sister property (in Santa Monica, not at all near the area of the city where we had wanted to stay). We checked on-line and the reviews were extremely poor. We declined the offer, and made our own arrangements for another hotel elsewhere in the city.
The receptionist then offered us three Best Western 'gift cards', each for $50 off a stay at a Best Western. Upon examining the cards, however, they each expired in 1/08. (This was March 2008.) Two of the cards, the receptionist (or someone) had used a black marker to cross out the expiration date. I can really see using one of these cards at some Best Western, and explaining that I was not the person who crossed out the expiration date; that the cards should actually still be accepted!
I told the receptionist that I wanted a statement, on the Inn's letterhead, indicating that we had arrived on schedule but there was no reserved room for us, and that we would not later be charged for not showing up at the Inn as per our reservation. The receptionist at first refused, saying that he could not do this. He said that of course we would not be charged. I noted that I had no reason, based on my current experience, to believe him. He offered to call his general manager. I said that was fine; that he could explain to the manager that there were two women there who would not leave without this letter. He then apparently decided that he could provide this letter without calling the general manager. However, the first letter was not on letterhead. The next two times my name was spelled wrong (despite clearly printing my name in two-inch-high letters after the first time). I finally was given the requested letter. 
While we were trying to make reservations elsewhere, a man came in to check in; from what I overheard, he had booked a room with two double beds. He was being given a room with one king. He was traveling with a friend, not a bed companion. When the man questioned this arrangement, he was told that they could provide a "roll-away" (i.e., a cot). He eventually agreed, but asked if they could transfer him to the requested double room the next night. Good luck to him.
I can't tell you anything about the rooms, the ambiance, etc. The lobby looked clean. 
Oh, and after I arrived home, there was another e-mail from the Carlyle Inn, saying that they appreciate our business and hoped that we enjoyed our stay. 
If you want to try staying here, good luck. I would recommend that you call in person to double-check any reservations that you make.

title: “Very Impressive”
text: Stayed here for the chicago marathon. Very beautiful and friendly staff. Willl definitely return .

title: “Nice Stay”
text:
Stayed recently for a buisness trip/meeting which included a Cubs game. Had a nice corner room. Certainly an hotel in an old building but the rooms were updated and clean. Overall a quaint little place to stay especially if you can appreciate the old building for it's charm. 
The staff was very friendly & helpful when I needed help finding a place to eat or info about getting back to the airport.

title: “Accomodations and staff are excellent.”
text:
The entire staff is professional and very accommodating. 
We arrived a day early for a family vacation and were greeted with warm smiles. Luke at the Front desk was able to help with special requests. 
We ate breakfast at the hotel everyday where Zulema Lopez made us feel like we were at home. Service was excellent from everyone in the restraunt including Kelly Norton and Lindsey Hoeho, they responded delightlyfully to any request.

title: “First time in Chicago. Terrific hotel.”
text:
I stayed two nights at the Blackstone and really enjoyed it. Check-in with Brett was very welcoming. So glad I booked a lake/park view room - $119/nt. Loved the decor/furnishings. Found it spacious. Did not dine at the hotel, but got coffee at the Starbucks which closes earlier than usual. (7/8pm, I think.) Convenient location. The Michigan Ave public bus stops are one block north and one block south. 
Quirks:
-- The mattress (pillow-top) was a little too soft for my liking.
-- The noise of my neighbors' doors clicking/slamming shut was startling.

title: “Felt permanently like night”
text:
I could see from the hotels website the style of decor they have went for and fully expected the dull reception area. I agree with a previous reviewer that they really could do with at least a sign pointing to the reception desk - it takes a few minutes standing in the lobby with your suitcases to work out where it is. 
Firstly the good points about the room. I was pleased with the size, it wasn't huge by any description, but for NYC standards, we were fairly happy. Well appointed and furnished. Comfortable bed, plenty of pillows and spotlessly clean.
The negatives? Well one main one really - our room was pretty much as dark as the lobby due to facing directly on to a wall and literally no daylight. I certainly wasn't expecting any kind of view from the window in the middle of NYC, but we had to permanently have the lights on and it was so dark we slept in every morning with zero daylight to waken us naturally. 
Whilst the bathroom was well appointed, I felt some of the luxuries were just wasteful. For example, the soap is packaged in a small plastic box with a paper insert and 2 plastic inserts - is this really necessary for the amount of bars of soap they must go through? Can someone please reassure me that you have a good recycling policy? There is no point having a sign telling you about reusing towels when you are wasting such a silly amount of paper and plastic on a bar of soap.
The hotel is very well located with Time Sq a few mins walk in one direction and Fifth Avenue in the other. There are a multitude of restaurants and deli's in the area, therefore we did not eat or drink in the hotel at all. 
This hotel really does tick the main boxes, clean, good standard, comfortable and well located. But stepping inside was like going into a cave - I guess if you like that sort of trendy style then you will love this hotel. There's nothing really wrong with this hotel, it's just not to my taste, I will choose to stay elsewhere in New York in future.

title: “Good hotel for a family who like to shop.”
text: Rooms were good. Separate bedroom was comfortable and quiet- we upgraded to a Queen sized bed and our two daughters slept on the pull out. The upgrade also gave us a view of the lake but you could only see it over a bunch of roofs. Bell men were not the happiest group of employees but front desk, concierge and bar and restaurant staff were friendly. Hotel is located around the corner from Watertower Place as well as other shopping and within walking distance of some good restaurants. We had breakfast in the hotel both mornings we were there- food was acceptable. It was very busy both mornings but they fit us in with minimal wait.

title: “Great place to stay - everyone is so courteous”
text: A very good value for the price. From arrival to checkout, a pleasant experience. Rooms very nice and employees even better.

title: “Never again.”
text: Over priced small room. Took FOREVER for room service and when we finally got the food we had to send it back because it was COLD! You have to pay for parking or vellet any which way you go. LOTS of hidden fees! Beautiful views of SD though.

title: “Pleasant Surprise!”
text: We purchased the Groupon special and were glad to get it for our trip to San Antonio w/our daughter & 2 kids-just the right price and just in time. This hotel has just been renovated and the rooms were comfortable, newly decorated and the a/c was great. But the big thing is the service-everyone was so accomodating-bell men, desk personnel, wait staff in the restaurant-and when in the excruciating heat the ice machines ran out they brought us a whole bag of ice. It is at the end of the old Riverwalk area but water taxiis will take you north from there if you wish-up the new extension. The lovliest of rooms are probably on the Riverwalk side but our daughter's had a balcony and overlooked the pool. Our room in the tower had a beautiful nighttime skyline view. Plan to go back in Aug w/ another daughter and 2 kids.

title: “Believe the reviews- this place is great!”
text:
I'm always a little wary of hotels that have all excellent reviews on tripadvisor, but the Chancellor Hotel deserves all the best reviews and more. 
I just got back from a week long stay at the Chancellor and it was great. My husband and I met my parents in San Francisco to celebrate my mom's 60th birthday. Before we arrived, I was contacted by Monica, the events coordinator. She arranged flowers and champagne and chocolates to be delivered to my mom's room for her birthday. It was great service.
The hotel admenities are great as well. The rooms are big enough. Very clean. Great bathrooms, comfortable beds, etc. The staff is at your service for whatever question/request you have. The breakfast we had in the hotel was great...very good eggs benedict! 
All in all...this hotel made our trip to san francisco perfect. We had the best time in such a great city and I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a great deal.

title: “Great NY hotel”
text: This is a great hotel. People are correct that the lobby is tiny and unimpressive however how much time do you really spend in a hotel lobby? I'd rather have a bigger room than a huge lobby. My room was a great size and very clean and comfortable. I could control the temperature of the room and make it as cold as I want when I slept. Granted most hotels have thermostats you can control in the rooms but in my experience they only work about 50% of the time. The staff is very friendly and helpful. My one complaint is I set out the door hanger for breakfast delivery before I went to bed, and when I got up in the morning and went to get my paper it was still there. No one picked it up that night so no breakfast for me. I mentioned it to the staff when I checked out and they were very apologetic. Also the temperature in the cardio room seems inconsistent. I went down one evening to work out and it was freezing in the room and I went down another day and the room was like a sauna. The location of the hotel was perfect for me, away from the Times Square madness but within walking distance of a lot. Overall this is a great hotel and I would definitely stay here again. I travel to NY quite a bit for work and this could easily become my preferred hotel.

title: “Walking distance to Universal Studios”
text: My husband, 14yr, 6yr & I stayed here for a trip to Universal Studios. The hotel room was fine, no complaints. We needed extra towels & they were promptly delivered within minutes of calling front desk. There is a shuttle to Universal Studios but we did not use it as the park is extremely close. If you are not completely out of shape or elderly, the walk should not be a problem for u. It's probably 5 minutes away.... We'll probably not return to Universal Studios again but if we did, we would definitely stay here. Btw, I was lucky enough to get this hotel using Priceline's "Name Your Own Price" feature :)

title: “Faded gem, in need of refurbishing”
text:
This "classic" property was likely once a happening spot located right in the center of Seattle. Alas, it's small European hotel-sized rooms are showing their age. Despite a few modern conveniences like rain shower heads and older model flat screen TVs the rooms feel tired and worn. The bathroom in my room, 804, was tiny with a sink the same size as an airplane bathroom and the toliet is so close to the wall it is almost unusable.
We paid $200 which is a bit much given the age of the place and size of the room.
On the positive side the girl at the front desk was happy and helpful as was the doorman.

title: “Great Location, very comfortable hotel”
text:
My college-age son and I visited Seattle, where we lived for 13 years, before we moved East three years ago. It was a trip to visit our old favorite places. Since it was the weekend of the annual Bumbershoot music festival and Labor Day weekend as well, hotel rooms were extremely scarce, and I had planned the trip only a couple of weeks beforehand. The Alexis was one of the only hotels that offered a separate bed for my son with enough room to get around, at a reasonable (less than $300 per night) price for that time period. We ended up in an "Executive suite", which has a living room, fully separate bedroom, and dining/conference area. We put a rollaway bed in the living room (it supposedly had a sofabed, but did not, a glitch.) The arrangement was extremely comfortable for our four-night stay. The staff was friendly. There was coffee and tea in the lobby in the AM, and, for a change from most hotels, plenty of copies of the NY Times, Seattle Times, and Wall St Journal -- there were usually some left to take even in the afternoon! There was a guest PC with internet access at the front desk so you can print out boarding passes and quickly check email or find info online. 
The only real glitch was that the shower head did not work -- I took baths -- but there was plenty of hot water and high water pressure. (To be fair, I did not notify anyone about the shower head.) I had requested a room on a higher floor, but all they turned out to have was one on the second floor, so they took about ten percent off my nightly hotel rate. Great location -- walking distance to Pike Place Market, the waterfront, Elliott Bay Books in Pioneer Square and the good restaurants in Belltown. We even walked to Seattle Center, although that is about a half-hour walk even at a fast pace. You could also walk to the International District. Parking is a bit pricey - $36 per night for overnight guests - but the valet service was friendly and very efficient. 
I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Place to Stay!”
text:
This was my first time staying at a Hilton Garden Inn - the whole experiences was wonderful! The entire staff offered excellent customer service, the food was good, the rooms nice. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to the Denver Cherry Creek area. I actually joined the Honors program based on this stay. 
There is construction of a new shopping/dining and lodging complex next to the hotel that will only add to the value of this facility when construction is complete but does create a little bit of chaos near the entrance.

title: “Our Boston stay 23-27 July and 6th August Perfect”
text:
This was our first visit to Boston in July and the management could have not been more helpful. On the morning of departure from the UK an employee from another Marriott hotel in Boston had unfortunately cancelled our booking! Upon cantacting Marriott Customer Services we were allocated 4 nights at Long Wharf who luckily had free rooms! I need not have worried as we had a personnal message from the Manager (John Collette) on our way to Heathrow. Upon check in we were given a room on the 7th Floor overlooking the harbour which included the Concierge Lounge! A superb breakfast was included as well as early evening delicious canapes and snacks including all soft drinks which saved us a fortune. We were also particularly well looked after by Ryan Tavares the Senior Manager who spent time and effort into making this a most memorable stay and to prove this we even squeezed another night in before our return to the UK on Thursday 9th August!
