To sum this hotel up:- Great location - Aquarium just outside, Freedom Trail outside, Water Taxi to Airport outside as well as great shopping and restaurants within walking distance! What more could a traveller want 
Thanks Ryan and John we will be back X

title: “Great value, great location”
text: We are not able to book non refundable rooms when we travel so we aren't able to score the best deals but this hotel was a wonderful find. The hotel appeared to be brand new. We had a king sized room which was much more spacious than I anticipated. There was a large bathroom as well which can be unusual in NYC hotel rooms. The room came equipped with a refrigerator and microwave. The hotel was spotlessly clean as well. The location was excellent, close to both Herald Square, Times Square and Fifth Avenue as well as any number of restaurants of all prices. We saw some shows while we were there and we were able to get there easily from here. There was a Hampton Inn adjacent which may have been a little less in cost, I'm not sure. I would definitely stay at this property again.

title: “great location, but no, I'd probably would not stay there again”
text: I stayed at a four star expecting 4 star experience in a big city. Well, not so much. Not once could we ring directly through to the concierge desk ALWAYS VOICEMAIL, although they did call us back later....we could not hear them over the traffic. Thank God I wasn't counting on them for tickets to a show! So no Spa Days for us! We couldn't get through! Also, we were told by the booking agent at Westin to again request hypoallergenic pillows upon arrival. We did. We did NOT receive them, was informed THEY WERE OUT. We are all highy allergic to Down so we got stuck sleeping on our clothes and clean towels for the duration of our stay. Heavenly bed? Not so much!! They were very accommodating to our doggies, in fact were quite sweet. When they made a mistake on my bill and overcharge me over $300 it only took a quick trip to the front desk to have it fixed. Food was quite good.

title: “Mostly happy with the Hard Rock”
text: My girlfriend and I just spent 4 nights at the Hard Rock in Chicago. I love the Hard Rock in Vegas, but not surprisingly, the one in Chicago didn’t quite have the same excitement. The location (on Michigan Ave just south of the river and the Magnificent Mile but near Millennium Park, LSD, and the Loop) worked very well for us. The hotel seems to have been converted from an office building which created some oddities like having to switch elevators to reach the fitness center (which is very respectable with TVs on many of the machines.) The lobby and bar connect in one large area and, though both are spacious and clean, they lack the atmosphere of other modern hotels like the W. The room had a great king size bed and a modern feel. The bathroom felt spacious, clean, and well designed though the shower curtain was flimsy and grabbed onto to my body like a giant wet sock no matter how much I tried to dodge it. Our only complaints related to the service. We encountered two small problems – the drain in the shower had a partial clog and the stereo didn’t work. We had to ask the front desk twice to have the drain fixed and three times to fix the stereo (which never ended up working.) Overall, we enjoyed the Hard Rock and we received a great price from Hotwire.

title: “A Hotel that really spoils you”
text:
We live in the bay area and decided to go into the city for the night and stayed at the Argonaut.
Upon arriving, a lively, happy doorman greeted us , attentive and motivated to make sure we are happy and well taken care of. 
Checking in , Front desk was no different, genuinely elated, yes elated to check us in! Gave our Daughter a toy, offered us some wine in front of the fire.
The setting was a crispy , clean but, charming and authentic nautical theme. It felt like we were on an elegant turn of the century cruise liner. 
Even the bellman was gracious. This was like bizarro world where everything is opposite from how reality is. Most hotels are not like this and if they are, you pay through the teeth for a smile or an act of kindness. Which feels more like they are your servants.
At the Argonaut, we felt like we were greeted by Family and Friends, not forced smiling employees.
Later after checking into our impeccably clean, tidy and nautically designed room ( view of Alcatraz in the bay ) We strolled to the lobby where the staff was serving hot Toddies with whipped cream and hot cider for the children. The Following day served, build your own hot chocolate.. shaved chocolate and other add ons. Amazing!
We did not want to leave the hotel, it was so welcoming and generous.
Checking out the front desk and so impressed with our first Kimpton experience, the front desk gave me a brochure of all the Kimptons in the United States.
So when we booked our trip to Cambridge, Massachusetts,, I booked in advanced 5 nights , non refundable .... big mistake!( Door man , texting all the time ( you'll be lucky if he opened the door for you) More importantly , The Beds sank! energy low, some of the front desk people are nice) wine hour you are lucky to get a few of the tiny pieces of food they put out, then it is gone. 
warning... NOT ALL KIMPTONS ARE LIKE THE ARGONAUT , KIMPTON. Do not book non-refundable rooms unless you have stayed, slept in the bed at least on night!

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location, but not worth the "rack rate"”
text:
We stayed here over the valentine's weekend. 
THE GOOD:
-It is a beautiful hotel
-Great service from every employee we encountered
-Location near ferry building, cable cars, bart, etc can't be beat. Walgreens, Starbucks, Subway all are accross the street.
-Lobby computers could be used to check in online for flight (free).
THE BAD:
-Price: we got a great price of $99/night on Priceline, but the rack rate seems to be about $300. OUCH. Not worth $300.
-They nickel and dime you to death...parking per day: $57, fridge in room $15/day, etc.
-Street noise was loud. We were on the 4th floor and could here the traffic all night. Also, the piano player in the lobby will play until 10pm, good luck going to sleep before that.
Overall, a great hotel, if you can get it for the right price.

title: “Decent for a short stay”
text:
The location is GREAT if you enjoy the nightlife that the meat packing district has to offer. Lobby decor is super trendy and cool. Staff was OK; nothing special. The room was enough to sleep and shower, but I definitely wouldn't have kept sane if I spent more than 2 nights there! The bed was comfortable, but practically on the floor. The TV was right in front of the bed. I would not recommend it for older people with ailments, anyone who is tall, or if you have back problems. Also, this hotel is NOT for families or shy couples. The shower has 1/2 a pane of glass separating it from the sink/vanity. Yes, the floor will get wet. The separate toilet room is definitely not for anyone who is overweight! It is a bit claustrophobic in there.
The floor to ceiling windows made for an awesome view, though. This hotel is not for everyone, but decent for a short stay in the city.

title: “Good value, good location, very friendly staff”
text:
We stayed at the w on our first 3 nights in san diego. We arrived quite late on the first night and were welcomed very cheerfull and warm. 
We got a room on the 9th floor. The rooms are ok size. The decor is great!
The beds are really comfy and the bathroom we had was huge.
One downside is that the waterpressure of the shower is really low. So no nice hot shower.
Wifi is good, fast and free in the lobby.
Location is good. Just around the corner of little italy, the trolleystop and the ferry to coronado. 
Forcpartying you should find a hotel more to the gaslamp quarter.

title: “The personal touch in a big city”
text: An excellent room, tastefully decorated, outstanding service, wine reception every night and coffee in the morning. What else do you need? Oh, interesting magazines to read, check, an outstanding restaurant, check, valet service, check, doorman who can get you a cab in les than one minute, check. Hotel Monaco in San Francisco: warmly recommended.

title: “Great value for money”
text:
Was pleasantly surprised after reading some reviews. Couldn't have been more convenient for everything including all public transport.
Fantastic value for money given its location.
Probably more like a good hostel than a hotel - no problems with staff, lift, cleanliness, noise etc. 
Room was basic with no frills (but it did have tv and phone)
Breakfast was toast, jam, bagels, cream cheese, enormous muffins, OJ, coffee and tea and you could have as much as you like - I thought it was fair enough that you couldn't load up with food to take to your room - its only meant to be your breakfast not food for all day - I was pleased to get breakfast at all for the price - in France, Italy etc you're lucky to just get one croissant and a cup of coffee.

title: “Beautiful, great location”
text:
We drove here from San Antonio for weekend getaway. First time in Austin and we couldn't have picked better location. Hotel was right in downtown few blocks away from State Capitol and 2 min walk from the 6th street with all the restaurants and clubs. 
All the staff, starting with front desk and ending with valet, was super nice. Our room was much bigger than one would expect from junior suite. Style was very elegant, not too old fashioned but also not too crazy modern. Just perfect and very comfortable. The pillow top on bed was heaven. Bathroom was very spacious. I liked to have my own area with large mirror to do my make up and hair.
Definitely stay here. Price is good for what you get. Plus you can walk everywhere, including University of Austin and LBJ library (20 min).

title: “Great trip!”
text: I had a fantastic experience at the Mayflower! I couldn't ask for a better location.

title: “Standard rooms are small, but rest is Okay”
text:
Stayed here, as we were attending a concert at WaMu Theatre at Qwest Field. Several previous reviews noted that the standard rooms were small, so no real surprise when we checked into ours for the night. 
The room itself was clean, nice bathroom, flat screen TV, etc. The bed was extremely comfie.
The front desk service was above par, and they answered all our questions without hesitation and provided maps etc to make our stay more comfortable.
We did not eat or drink at any of the bars/restaurants, so no comment.
Our room safe had a glitch, but a call to the front desk, and the problem was rectified within minutes.
Found it close to everything, and not much trouble walking to Qwest field, Pioneer Square and Pikes Place Market. Yes Seattle is hilly, but we found walking down Cherry St, right next to the hotel, down to 1st Ave, was the lesser of the steeper hills.
Recommended for a Seattle visit.

title: “Nice Hotel, Great Location”
text: This hotel was nice. We were on the 7th Floor and lift was very slow, so 7 flights of stairs were tiring but hotel was nice. Breakfast is poor but we didnt expect much more. Location is fantastic, just off union square and next to Cable car stop, which takes you direct to Fishermans Wharfe for $6 each. Its a bit noisy at night, but i think that ay have been due to our room having a view over the road, which was lovely dispite the noise. Definatley Reccommend

title: “Largest rooms in Times Square”
text: This hotel is great if you want to be in Times Square, close to everything! The rooms are the largest I've stayed in in NYC (normal size for anywhere else)I usually stay here on business trips and the staff are always courteous and friendly - and usually upgrade my room too! The beds are comfortable and overall its a great stay. The hotel is very clean and there is a wonderful, distinct vanilla smell when entering the hotel that I absolutely love!

title: “Built in 1931 and unhampered by the signs of progress”
text: Original bath tub, doors, paint and I think carpet, The AC would not get the room below 80, there was mold in the tub and the staff did nothing, even though I reported the conditions every day for three days. Internet was $27 a day and did no always work. There are only two AC outlets in the room.

title: “ok hotel”
text: The room was nice and clean, and the staff was nice and helpful (if you didn't get one of the teenagers - they didn't know where anything was). However, the beds were like marshmallows they were so soft. And I had to stuff newspaper SECTIONS (not sheets) into the door to block the light coming in from the hall. The worst thing about this room was the tissue and toilet paper. It was about par with sand paper. I went to blow my nose, and thought I had scratched my face!

title: “Not worth the cheap price.”
text: This place was the most affordable option in the area, but it wasn't worth it in the slightest. The room was filthy, it's right off of a busy road, the bed had to be atleast 25 years old. Avoid at all costs!

title: “What a great place to stay!”
text:
We were having a girls weekend in Houston and needed a room that would fit all 5 of us. We picked the new Embassy Suites and loved it. The staff is so friendly and the accommodations were fabulous. We will definitely stay there again for our next girls weekend.
Melissa McCown

title: “Large Rooms-Nice People-Shame about the Smoke!”
text: The pool area is great at this hotel, it was warm even in the cool spring. There is plenty of grass available and they are the most pet friendly hotel I have ever been to. The staff actually smiled at us when we had our dog out and about and asked about her and petted her, instead of giving us dirty looks like a lot of places do. Thanks Sheraton for being so welcoming! They don't charge a fee either, which is nice. The rooms are very large and yes, the decor is a little outdated, but I'd rather deal with outdated decor and have a large, clean room instead of a cramped trendy place. The only complaint I have is the smoke in our room that came through the vent in the bathroom. Our floor did not smell smoky, but we had to keep the bathroom door closed because smoke was coming from this vent. I stuffed a wet washcloth in it and it seemed to help a little, but smoky hotels are a big issue for us. So, this is the one dark spot on an otherwise good hotel. The jacuzzi jets didn't work and we called someone to come check it out and they said they'd be right there. We waited an hour and no one ever showed. Like others have experienced, we didn't think the front desk staff was very knowledgable about the area and when we asked for directions, we were just given a printed sheet with directions on it that wasn't very helpful or personable. All in all, I'd stay again, since the price was right and they allowed our dog. Very convenient to downtown. My husband drove in every day and it took him less than 10 minutes to get there and back, during rush hours. Not really any places to eat close by. We ate at Dave and Busters a few exits away and it was good. Try the Lacy's Chicken. They have a security guard who patrols the parking lots at night and he was very nice. I felt safe walking my dog at night because he was there.

title: “Friendly staff - free breakfast - scary neighbourhood”
text: Spent four nights here with my wife and overall was a very pleasant stay. Hotel decor is very old fashioned and rooms are small and dark but clean. Good base for midtown area of Manhattan but be warned you will have to walk through a few 'project' like streets adorned with homeless people which can be a bit intimidating but we werent bothered once. Staff in hotel were very friendly and the free bagels/doughnuts and coffee for breakfast is a bonus for New York. We were in New York just for the sightseeing/shopping and just wanted somewhere decent to lay our heads. This place delivered.

title: “Charming little European style hotel”
text:
I stayed here on my last visit to NYC for a gathering of the Oscar Wilde Society of America. I was on my own in New York and this place was ideal. The hotel is charming and the staff is friendly and helpful. It's located in a very quiet location near Gramercy Park and the walk to Union Square to catch a subway was fairly close and convenient. 
I was worried about having to share a bathroom, but I never had any trouble or wait and the bathrooms were very clean.
Yes, it's small and funky, but it was perfect for me and the price was right.

title: “Nice for the price”
text: The staff was very friendly. The room was small but very clean. The furnishings were contemporary and free wifi was a nice extra. The bathroom was VERY small, but clean and functional. The free breakfast was good and the breakfast room was comfortable. Overall, it was super convenient and a good value for the price.

title: “"Not Trustworthy"”
text:
My husband and I traveled to Baltimore to attend a wedding. When we arrived, we were first surprised by the cost of the parking, valet and in and out fees were outrageous. They said nothing about this on their web site. Secondly, they requested an additional $50.00 on your credit card if you were paying by debit. Then once we checked in the room, it was extremely small. The ice machine was broken on our floor and we had to constantly go to another floor for ice. The room service was okay but the food was not that good. After we checked out, we realized about 1 hour later that my husband forgot his shoes in the room. We had not been out of the room since we returned from the wedding except when we checked out. He took the shoes off in the room and left them and the foot of the bed. We called back to the hotel 3 times and everyone seemed very unconcerned about the shoes and just continuously told us that there were no shoes found in the room. We know they were there. I think it is awful to uphold your staff in stealing guest property and showing no concern. These were very expensive shoes and yes, he should not have forgotten them, but the hotel could have shown a little more courtesy to their guests.
One last thing, when we checked in the first day, there was a line for checking in. I have never in 51 years checked into a hotel and had to stand in line with your luggage to check in. It was extremely noisy at night. Siruns and car horns, etc We will never stay there again!!

title: “Noisy & not very clean. Poorly maintained.”
text: We booked a Kid's suite for 3 nights but only stayed 1 night! This hotel is right beside the freeway & is terribly noisy as a result. On top of that, there is a loud air-conditioner in the room & thin walls, making it easy to hear the conversations of your neighbor. We were told ALL of the Kid's suites face the freeway. The rooms could be cleaner. There was a used tissue in the kids' sleeping area, a pop can on the balcony from the previous guest, & hair on the bathroom floor! The carpets & kid's duvet were also stained!! The kids' bunk beds were not properly made. The duvet was just sandwiched between the duvet cover & a flat sheet, instead of being INSIDE the duvet cover. When we arrived, the phone & wall clock were not working. I had to ask twice for the phone to be fixed. The mattress is terribly soft. I wonder if it is from Ikea, like the rest of the kid's furnishing. The staff were great but unfortunately it is not enough to make us leave as soon as we can.

title: “Good experience”
text: Overall, our stay here was a good experience. There was some remodeling happening, but we never heard it from our room. The staff was always cheerful, courteous and helpful. We have stayed at other Embassy Suites and found the breakfast here to be quite good. Even if we came down late or at a busy time, they did not run out of certain things. Didn't care for the plastic plates. For most of our stay styrafoam cups were offered -- awful! The valet parking was expensive and if it was a busy time, we had to wait a few minutes to get our car. We've visited San Diego several times and this is our first time staying downtown. It was very convenient to lots of things.

title: “nice hotel, good location”
text: The hotel itself is on a street wich is not that busy with noisy trafic. We arrived very early in the morning and they provided us with a room anyway. As this was next to the airco installations, we asked for a new one, wich they had ready for us at 13.00. The staff was very friendly and helpfull, the rooms clean and comfortable. The subway is close, the MOMA and Central Park are at walking distance.

title: “Exceeded my expectations and then some.”
text:
This was my first time staying at the Andaz on 5th Avenue, and I have to say that my wife and I had a wonderful time there. The room and decor was relaxing and modern. The service was warm and accommodating. Kelly at the front desk always addressed us by our names and always inquired if we needed anything, and greeted us with her great smile. Joe was also very helpful. New York is a fast and busy city, but every time I stepped into the Andaz, We felt at ease. Their gym is accessible 24 hours a day, which is great for guests traveling from a different time zone. 
Coffee is ready in the lobby every morning, and wine is offered every evening. It was raining during our trip, so umbrellas were offered at the door for guests. Staff members flagged down cabs when it was pouring outside. I'm very appreciative of all the hard work the staff puts in. Kudos to them. We thank you for your service.

title: “THE BEST IN CHARLOTTE METRO AREA”
text:
Once again randi and her staff have gone above and beyond the call of duty. Again this year the state games region 5 team stayed at townplace suites and had the best stay ever. The word must have got out about last year, because 3 other regions stayed int h e hotel as well. As always jason and the rest of the desk staff left no detail undone. The parents from region 5 as well as the other regions had nothing but A+'s for the condition of the property and the friendliness of the staff. The even had run off maps to the different venues the teams were playing at. When the state games returns to the charlotte area, this is the place to stay. Its location is close to concord mills and shopping and yet far enough away for quite and rest each night. Thanks for 2 great years at Townplace suites.
Michael Langone
Head Softball/ Volleyball Coach
Chatham Central High School
Region 5 Assistant Coach
West Senior Games Assistant Coach

title: “Luxury Hotel-moderate price- a Must-Stay”
text:
We attended a local sporting event with our teenage daughter. We booked the King Suite room and were suprised that there was not a pull-out bed in the room. We had to belatedly order a roll away. That issue aside, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The King bed was HEAVEN! --the roll away wasn't terrible either. The bedding was plush and high quality. Our daily schedule did not permit us to take advantange of the complimentary cocktail hour; however, on a separate couples get away, we would have. We did get to enjoy the cookies and milk each evening, and the breakfast--a tremendous value-add. It included eggs, sausage or bacon and either grits or oatmeal, in addition to the typical carb, fruit, yogurt options. Overall, we would give the stay a 9 out of 10, reducing the score only because of the roll away bed--and perhaps a marginal ding for being skimpy on the towels in the bathroom. (although, to be fair, there were microfiber robes in the closet, which was a nice touch.)
Families: make sure you are aware of the room configuration so you can accommodate the sleeping needs for your children. The roll away had to be put in the entry hallway because the other furniture was very heavy and not easily moved to position the bed in the "living room." Also, in case you are bothered by city noise, be aware that room 1210 had a lot of street sounds (i.e. light rail bell, and sirens). The hotel is refurbished beautifully, just not with sound-reducing windows. Once you climb into the comfy bed, you may forget about the other stuff!

title: “Not Happy!”
text: Front desk ruined our stay. Charged me $500 without letting me know 4 days after I checked out and after I had already payed for my hotel stay upfront and they had already held $300 for incidentals. I was refunded my $500 nine days later after i had checked out with no explanation and I was just told it was a mistake only after I called and complained to accounting. The hotel never contacted me to apologize for the inconvenience they caused me for holding my money for 9 days with no explanation or authorization from me. Also rooms were dusty and food was very expensive.

title: “Beautiful views and location. Parking is expensive”
text:
I stayed at the Omni on business. I had a very spacious room on a corner. I had beautiful ocean views. 
The parking is quite expensive at $32 per day. I had my husband stop by to join me for dinner...so our parking total for the trip was $96 for an overnight trip!
Service was good and had no problems holding my bags after checkout when I was attending a meeting. 
The room was quite noisy. I was woken up many times with the nearby trolley noise. The bed was of good quality and quite comfortable.

title: “Excellent**”
text:
We stayed at this hotel in September and must say it was excellent. We arrived in early by train from Vancouver and the reception staff kindly found us a room that was ready. The room was spacious & very comfortable. The hotel is in a great location (next to the shops & a couple of blocks from Pike Place Market). 
The staff were very friendly (especially the gentleman on concierge each morning).
Would definitely stay at this hotel again if we return to Seattle - Thank you

title: “ok hotel”
text:
stayed here for a few days and must say that overall it was a nice hotel. A few downsides though...
plus:
-large rooms
-pretty good location (foggy bottom metro nearby, a few blocks from georgetown (with shops and restaurants) and the circulator bus one block away)
downsides:
-shower head is crap
-noisey room
-no smoking anywhere in the hotel
-charge for the pool
-pricey
-no service in the garden (and no smoking either)
I had a feeling that there must be better places to stay in Washington.

title: “Staff not as good as other reports say”
text: I took my now fiance to New York and after looking at various hotels I chose the Morgans, as it had wonderful reviews. The trip was in aid of her 30th birthday and I planned to propose and yes she said yes!! Thanks for the many congratulations. I had planned to have a bottle fizz in the room after the proposal, something which I discussed over email with the hotel prior to arrival. Due to the fact that they wanted me to fax my credit card details over to them, I chose to sort out the fizz on my arrival. I spoke to Todd on the reception desk, he remembered who I was and informed me that a half bottle of champagne would be placed in my room on my return from the theatre and that this bottle would be complementary. On our return I found ONE chocolate looking dessert and no champagne!!!!!! Which was a dampener to the celebration. This could be forgiven after all Todd did reccommend a romantic restaurant close to the theatre but the lack of interest from the three other members of staff I spoke to about my disappointment (we never saw Todd again to speak to him) was boardering on rude, impersonal and uncaring. P.s the chocolate thingy was left (uneaten) in our room for three days and only removed when we left a note for the cleaners. The hotel itself was good, great location and size of room but as a tip, if you can request a back room. Madison avenue is busy and windows were only single glazed. Breakfast was good, although Sunday seemed a bit lacking, especially in fresh fruit! All in all a fantastic trip (clearly as I am now engaged) but could and would have been better if hotel staff had lived up to their expectations! This does exclude the doorman (with dark hair) He was extremely friendly and imformative!

title: “Absolutely loved the Adolphus”
text: I booked the Adolphus with high expectations after reading several reviews, and was not disappointed. The staff were extremely friendly and gracious, and they were a perfect accompaniment to the grand lobby areas. Our room was enormous with a separate living area and represented excellent value for money, with the very comfortable bed & pillows affording superb sleep. The bathroom was spacious, although the water pressure in the shower not so fantastic - a problem I have enountered at several hotels throughout the US. Other than that I couldn't fault the hotel, and its ideal location to downtown attractions allowed short walks to all there was to see.

title: “Great location and price”
text: You get what you pay for. It's a great location, 3 or 4 minute walk to times square. Subway is across the street and down the street. It's an old hotel so don't expect anything fancy. Small rooms and bathrooms but clean. We had our room cleaned every day. Staff were very nice and helpful. Accommodating. Very busy hotel. We had a great time. The bed and pillow was comfy for me but may not be for everyone. Even got us a cab.

title: “Location on River Front”
text:
The service was outstanding A+, easy to get around town and it was very clean and comfortable.
On site parking, internet access, the cleaning ladies were allways helpful and the service was very fast.

title: “The best all around Chicago hotel”
text: Wonderful hotel with a great location. Rooms are as shown in photos. It was very clean, exceptionally quiet and comfortable. Service was impeccable. Everyone on staff that we encountered from the doormen, to the cleaning lady, restaurant staff and front desk staff were genuinely polite and very professional. They do a great job at making you feel welcome. Further more, having the check in area on the 3rd floor made it feel even cozier. Food and service at 676 on the 4th floor was terrific with a wonderful view of Michigan Avenue below. After staying at other hotels in Chicago, I have to say - this is by the best! You will not be disappointed. We already have reservations to stay there at the end of this month. Make a point to join their Select Guest program, it's worth it. (Free beverages delivered to your room in the morning and a discounted rate on breakfast breads.)

title: “Comfort Suites Pflugerville Provide real comfort at reasonable price”
text: The Hotel was Extremely clean, The Management second to none. The beds are not your ordinary cheap mattress. They provide the comfort and feel like being in your own bed. We were pleasantly surprised and higly recommend this hotel over others in the area. If you want to feel like like a king at reasonable cost then stay at the Comfort Suits in Pflugerville when visiting in Austin Texas.

title: “Must be the best value hotel in the city”
text:
We just had two separate stays here on our recent west coast trip. Both visits were great. This is just the kind of hotel I like. If you want a glitzy bathroom with all the other big hotel trappings this is not for you. It's a little dated but clean and that's always the main thing for me. It's individual and the people were really friendly and helpful. There's free wifi throughout the hotel, although the signal was a bit patchy in our first room, and free use of the computers on the first floor with a printer for boarding passes etc.
The room itself had an ok rooftop view towards the downtown area and had flat screen tv with a comfy chair. Table and chairs for eating at and a desk for laptop use etc. Mini kitchen area with sink, fridge and microwave and cupboards with cutlery, wine glasses and crockery supplied if you want to eat in. Nice market next door for most food stuffs and plenty of local take out places within a block or so. Comfy queen bed - slept very well with no street noise even with the window open(room was on the 6th floor on the side of the hotel facing East I think).
Breakfast is help yourself buffet style and quite basic but really all you need. Cereal, juice, coffee and toast though no hot stuff. There was a microwave for heating oatmeal etc.
It's about a 10 min walk down the hill to Union Sq and a block from the cable car on Mason St.
We had a great stay at this charming hotel and will definitely stay here when back in San Francisco. It doesn't have a lot of the flash stuff of larger more modern places but it's just the job for a cheap and clean base from which to explore the city.
I would recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “great hotel”
text:
I have just got back from this hotel and cant understand the complaints some folk put in their reviews,i went with my sister to see graceland and we were delighted with our stay.
The courtesy bus saved us a fortune,took us everywhere,even back to the airport free of charge. A few small gripes, the girl in the bar was dour,we were watching a film one nite in the bar and she was banging things about,saying she should have got off 20min before, also the tv in reception was running films all week,my sister and i have hearing aids and the lovely receptionist turned it up for us,no one could hear it so it wasnt just us, crabbit older white lady receptionist turned it back down,why run films in reception if the sound is constantly down,the chairs n beds at the pool are the most uncomfortable i have ever sat on, should be cushions on them.
Can i say jo the receptionist was fab, so friendly and helpfull, nothing was too much bother, and anyone going to tupelo, ask reception to book claudine, she was great, but i think the $130 each should include your ticked,we had to pay $12 each when we got there, all in all we had a fab stay and would def go back.

title: “Nice location, average hotel”
text:
Location is great-3 blocks from Michgan Avenue, check-in was very fast. There is a nice new Starbucks in the lobby along with a Sandwich type restaurant. Room was small and it looked as though the ceiling was falling down, however the bed was comfortable. Looked like they had purchased new towels, and was clean. We would stay here
again if the rate was good.

title: “No Worries here”
text: Rooms a little run down and in need of a bit of TLC, but that is where the criticisim ends. Cannot fault the staff, all extremely accommodating and friendly. Free Breakfast much appreciated by our family of 7. Free wireless on ground floor and a friendly small bar and lounge area. Room prices a bargain when you use discount coupons found in accommodation guides. Well recommended for those not looking for a Westin!

title: “Beautiful location and scenary”
text:
This resort is located in a stunning part of Mission Bay. The grounds are beautiful and well kept. We also liked the location which was convienent to the airport, downtown and the beaches.
The rooms are located in 3 - 4 unit clusters scattered around the resort. They has some updated features like flat tv's, granite bathrooms and nice beds and bedding. The basic structure, however, was pretty dated. It appeared to be a '60s vintage and the couch felt like it had been there 50 years. The room also had a rather moldy smell - we couldn't tell if it had just been not used in a while or actually had a problem. The a/c was also ancient although you probably don't need to use it much with the beautiful weather.
We ate several times at the casual restaurant overlooking the bay. THe food was actually much better than I expected from a place that really had a capative audience. 
Al in all, we had a very nice time and the hotel staff was great. With a major room refurbishment, this could be a world class resort. As it is, Paradise Point is a very nice place with a few things you must overlook.

title: “Good Place to Stay”
text: I was in town on business, and the location was great for visiting a federal agency. The room was very clean and spacious, and the staff was friendly and helpful. I have seen some reviews criticizing the continental breakfast, but I thought it was good--coffiee, juice, fruit, muffins, croissants, and toast. I would definitely stay here again without hesitation

title: “Clean, comfortable, and good value for money”
text: This hotel was perfect for our overnight stay in Memphis. The rooms were clean and comfortable. A night light and toothpaste were provided very quickly when we asked for them. The pool is on the small side, but fine for a cooling dip. Breakfast not very exciting, but the children liked making their own waffles! All in all, very good value for money and I would stay there again.

title: “Elegant Charm”
text:
Initially, we were hesitant to visit the Warwick Regis because it looked like it may be a little too formal or stuffy, especially for our two young girls.
We were delightfully surprised, however, with the charming elegance of the hotel. Most of the rooms are appropriate for two adults only, but we upgraded to the Junior Suite (for a reasonable amount) and the four of us were quite comfortable.
It made for a very special birthday trip for my daughter as we stayed in a place that was not a cookie-cutter hotel, no matter how modern.
To add, we found that everyone on the staff with whom we came in contact were extremely helpful and friendly. They certainly added to our pleasant stay.
We would certainly go back again!

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: I had occassion to visit this hotel during the holiday season and the decorations and entertainment were Fabulous. It was conveniently located to food, shopping and entertainment. What a lovely hotel!

title: “Value for money if you're a member”
text: I checked into the club quarters when I couldn't get a room at the Hyatt Regency for a conference I was attending. Club Quarters admits both regular visitors and also members of its club, who get a discounted rate. Overall, I think the place provides pretty good value for your money, especially if you are a member. It is well located in the heart of the business district and very close to china town and the embarcadero. I loved the free internet; it always amazes me that the more expensive joints (yes Hyatt, that's you!) always stick on these little ticky-tack extra charges; at Club quarters, it is clear their goal is to provide clean, efficient hotel rooms at a good price. The room was pleasant in a mod sort of way, and it seemed designed in a practical way, with a nice desk for work, and a shower-only instead of a space-consuming tub. The other reviewers are right about the noise although - you can easily hear people in the hall outside, though I didn't notice much noise from my neighbors. I think they get a pretty considerate bunch of guests, who seem to be pretty quiet. I will consider joining the "club" to try out other branches of the hotel.

title: “If only all business trips were like this!”
text: I've been travelling a lot for business and there are details which make the experience wonderful...let me tell you how the W Dallas Victory ...victoriously did that! I arrived after flying for 9.5 hours. I was exhausted and quite chilly. Before I knew it I had a down comforter on my bed which was much more comfortable for me because that's what I have at HOME! I wanted to pick up a couple items and the front desk first called to see if they could book the Acura Experience for me (unavail). That would have been fun but I actually wanted to walk! I ordered a sandwhich in the Living Room and it was far too greasy for my taste. I think I just generally expected a Turkey sandwhich to be a healthy option. I was probably too jet-lagged to read the description properly - there was cheese and bacon too. LOL The Living Room took care of me when I woke up groggy on the hunt for coffee and breakfast and later on I found the cobb salad was pretty delicious. They were also fantastic while we spent time socializing inside and on the terrace with business partners. I slept like a baby and felt pretty well rested even having displaced myself by 6 time zones for just a few days complete with a hectic schedule. The beds are wonderful! The Bliss spa products are great. Next time I stay at a W I know I can pack a bit less! There are lots of different snacks and drinks available which is quite convenient. The internet connection in the room was 5 star. And I personally really got to experience the WONDERFUL of the W. Room service arrived with two bottles of bubbly and fruits dipped in chocolate...and I knew it had to be a mistake...I insisted it was a mistake which it was. A little while later the guy came back with one bottle and plat for fruits dipped in chocolate and a note from the W saying this time it WASN'T a mistake. The gesture made me smile from ear-to-ear. When you're a woman travelling on business you feel like your life is in the hands of others in many ways. The W made me feel like I was in a super safe, comfortable and welcoming place. Thanks W. xox

title: “Fine stay in Hillcrest, San Diego: Restaurant Row!”
text: I won a sweeps and this is where they put us and it was great- a nice big suite with a cute little balcony (parking lot view!)!, & a pool/hot tub downstairs & a computer w/internet access- what more do you need?! We added on 2 days, and the staff was Very nice and helpful. The best part is Hillcrest has a million GREAT restaurants and wie bars all within a block of the hotel! Sushi, Vietnamese, Indian... you name it, and all excellent.

title: “1920s grand hotel”
text:
The hotel was fine; elegant, sophistocated, smart and clean. Room was averaged sized and bath was large, marble and very modern. The toilet has the most vociferous flush I have ever encountered...it would seemingly take off one's arm!. However, the shower head and sink faucet have SEVERE water restrictors with VERY poor water pressure/velocity....so, one must wash and rinse twice or thrice as long as normal...completely defeating the purpose of saving water. I do not know if this is a hotel thing, or a San Francisco ordinance, but either way it is very poorly designed and executed. View from my 12 floor room was specacular. 
My main concern with this hotel is the location. It is atop Nob Hill, and every street leading to it is VERY steep. Even going down is no picnic! Cable car is not close, and few, if any, busses trek up the hill. So, it is our two (sore) legs, or a cab. This alone is enough reason for me to not stay here again, but the hotel was really very nice and enjoyable.

title: “The cleanest hotel I have ever stayed at.”
text:
The room smelt great and on closer inspection there was NOT a trace of dirt or grime insight. The staff were extremely helpfull in letting us borrow screwdrivers to assemble products that we bought to helping us with our travel, Which was much needed as we had never been to San Diego before. 
I was expecting to stay in a dump as we have stayed in many low budget hotels across the states and was pleasently surprised the onsight diner is a must especially the belgium waffles. Mission valley mall is a short walk which was great for me proberly not so great for my husband though.

title: “Great Location”
text:
The MMC was a great downtown DC hotel experience. The bed was comfortable, the staff accommodating, Starbucks in the lobby, great restaurant and all around solid Marriott hotel.
The location can't be beat - practically on top of the Metro, short stroll to the White House and National Mall.
Restaurant choices during the weekend in downtown DC are few, but we always enjoy the Old Ebbit Grill. They have wonderful food, ambiance and convenience to the MMC hotel.
Definitely will stay again!

title: “Great staff, keeps me coming back”
text: One need only point to the attentiveness of the guest services staff, especially Raquel, to understand why it's easy to keep coming back time and time again. As much as I travel and as many travelers as a hotel staff see during the course of a day/month/year, having someone that gives that personal touch always is refreshing. This hotel is consistent.

title: “Nice location...kinda trendy...a bit above average”
text: Just completed a two night stint here. Paid for the larger broadway king (260sq ft room) and it was cool but cool in a way where you are trying to make something old look new. Floors were dirty. Windows filthy and a misty water smell was masked by a awesome bed, great bathroom and nice decor. Location was great as two subway stops were a block away on either direction and your on madison ave!

title: “Great Place to Stay if you are Flying Out”
text: My wife and I arrived early on a Sunday morning after five nights in Sedona, the staff was gracious and welcoming and had a room ready for us. the staff was attentive and great, especially Camille who was at the front desk, the food in the restaurant and room service was very good and the breakfastt buffet was only $14.50, unlike the high of $26.00 I paid at an East Coast big city property. I would rec this place to anyone who is flying out of Phoenix and does not want to add two hours to the trip by driving from say Sedona to Sky Harbor.

title: “Great "little Jewel" in NYC”
text: This was indeed "a little jewel". Best hotel I've stayed in NYC.Great location....minutes from Time Square Theater District and very close to central park.Clean room.Small but very efficiently designed.Booked online with the hotel and received excellent rate.Great service.Would highly recommend.

title: “Beautiful hotel near the riverwalk”
text:
I accompanied my husband for a conference at this hotel. I really enjoyed this hotel.
The staff was very helpful and the location was great.

title: “Sofitel is superb!”
text: We have just returned from a five night stay at the Sofitel and can honestly say that we cannot find fault with the hotel. It really is as good as all the reviews claim. We particularly appreciated the free internet access in the lobby, the cleanliness of the rooms and the great location, not to mention the free drink/late check out and upgraded room afforded by the Sofitel Privilege Card (see their website). When we return to NYC we will be staying at the Sofitel.

title: “Blackstone Renaissance Hotel - Mercat a la Planxa Restaurant”
text:
Hotel: Loved the place, but used a Groupon deal and as a result of this deal, ONLY paid $303/night and no view. $55/night parking ridiculous! 
Restaurant: What we did love is the little restaurant upstairs from the lobby called Mercat a la Planxa - it was wonderful. Had 6 tapas and enjoyed the complexity and flavor explosion of each one. The only problem is we arrived late afer sailing and the server was very hurried. Our fault.

title: “Frequent traveler to LA and I always return to this centrally located hotel. .”
text: The staff and management are completely accommodating, friendly, and attentive. The hotel's central location is amazing. Minutes from Hollywood, WEHO, Beverly Hills shopping and restaurants. Just off 405 and 10 can get you quickly to Santa Monica, the Valley, LAX, and all of LA. Shops, restaurants, pharmacies, markets and gyms are walking distance. Hollywood site seeing is nearby as well as great hiking at Runyon Canyon Park. Just off Pico Blvd offers quick shortcuts to most of LA. The rooms are clean and family friendly with kitchenettes. As a frequent LA traveler, I always return to this Marriott because of the staff, the location, and it's amenities. The daily breakfast and happy hour are a big plus.

title: “First Class Service”
text: The Pierre is in a perfect position on 61st and Fifth beside the bottom of Central Park. Our room was excellent with an ultra modern bathroom, small bath but very large separate shower. The bed's are extremely comfortable and the room was spotlessly clean.

title: “Great location”
text: Great hotel. Check-in was easy and the room was as expected. Room was comfy and cleaning staff extremely nice with the customer as their #1 priority. Located very close to subways, Broadway, Central Park, the LOVE sculpture on Avenue of the Americas, Rockefeller Center, and more.

title: “downtown DC hotel”
text:
Hotel is centrally located in downtown Washington DC. It is only about 10 blocks from AmTrak Union Station. You can catch the subway for two stops and get off at Gallery Chinatown. You can get a Subway farecard for $10 for multiple uses. Amtrak tickets are flexible. If you find yourself finish your meeting early, you can ask for an exchange of your ticket for an earlier train without penalty. You just have to ask for a new ticket at the Amtrack ticket counter.
The hotel is situated in center of town within walking distance from, Spy museum, Dupont Circle, Treasury Dept, National Mall and Chinatown. Chinatown is no longer the traditional Chinatown. You'll find a lot of different cuisines in Chinatown. There is a trendy fusion Asian restaurant called Ping Pong around the corner from Renaissance. It is a London based chain with only two stores in US both is in DC area.

title: “Well recommended by Trip Advisor Member”
text: This very convenient Motel-type Hotel was recommended to us by another Trip Advisor member for my twin Grandsons' Graduation and we could not have been more pleased.Large room with king bed, full bath/shower, full fridge and microwave Good breakfast, excellent pool[part in shade] and Launderette Several restaurants on site. Might be bit near the main road for some, but we did not find this a great problem because of the convenience of being only a couple of miles from my son's" full house" in Copperlakes. Plannning return visit here in 2 years time for my Grand-daughter's Graduation.

title: “Decent Hotel”
text:
Pros: large rooms; comfortable bed; large meeting spaces, lobby, and bar; free outside parking; six elevators and one was always available; close to galleria and good food.
Cons: hotel showing a little age; expensive internet; free parking sometimes limited; location a little difficult to get in and out of.
Overall, this is a fine hotel but nothing outstanding. We would stay here again without complaint, but I wouldn't pay top dollar for it.

title: “great time , nice room and freindly people”
text: The Hotel Blake is a great place to stay and go to a Bears game. Clean and nice place to stay.

title: “Memorable stay to say the least...”
text:
We arrived on a Friday and were checked-in. We eagerly made our way up to our fifth floor room and entered our suite. We both entered and were admiring the sitting area when we noticed an older couple napping in their beds. We quickly backed up and went back downstairs to the front desk. We let the front desk staff and manager know that we were given a room where there were two people sleeping in their beds. She said she was going to find out what they were doing in there. In the meantime, we were given keys to another suite on the fourth floor. We were not offered any complimentary upgrades or comps in general, which would have been appropriate considering the major security issue and awkward situation that just occurred. Thank goodness my boyfriend and I are both decent human beings!
It was so loud outside of the hotel at night that we barely got any sleep. There were fights and dogs barking. It was such a major disruption that continued until about 5 a.m. Check-out was at noon. Between 11 a.m. and noon housekeeping came in too our room four times to see when we would be leaving so that they could clean. I told them each time that we were checking out at noon. We did not have a door handle notice or anything available to use to hang on the knob to let them know but it was the same two women. They were literally camped outside our door for the hour.
The front desk staff were not particularly friendly or warm. However, the valet were very kind and courteous. The breakfast was very basic but the room overall clean. I wouldn't recommend this Marriott to any of our friends or family. We were greatly disappointed with our stay.

title: “good hotel, but watch out for parking charges!”
text:
This HI Express is a very good deal, ideally located a few blocks from Seattle Center (Space Needle, etc.). The breakfast is plentiful, but be forwarned, they don't have the cinnamon buns so heavily advertised in HI Express commercials! They also have a nice, albeit small, indoor pool,usually filled with kids. We stayed on the top floor facing the back side (not the Aurora Ave. side), which turned out to be very quiet and had a decent view of the city, although not the Space Needle. It was worth the quiet to stay on the back side of the hotel. 
My biggest complaint was that, although they advertise (on Travelocity, for example) that they have free parking, lo and behold at checkout there was the 4.50 per day charge. Not exorbitant, but when I pointed it out to the manager he feigned ignorance. He did refund my money, but it all made me feel like they were a little sneaky. Most people probably wouldn't even notice, much less challenge the charge...so print out the web page where it states this and make sure you have it at checkout!!

title: “GREAT”
text: Found this Hotel on Expedia.....it was really nice and clean hotel, the people who worked here are very friendly they would really assist you if you need anything. Had a great time with my husband staying at this hotel. We will surely stay here again next time we come back to Phoenix. Very nice......

title: “Compact room!”
text: Nice hotel very modern look. East Houston is a busy road and directly opposite the subway. Our room was very compact which is common for NYC but the bathroom was oversized, its not necessary - extra room in the bedroom would have been a better design. Fortunately as we only stayed one night I didn't unpack, that was a blessing since the cupboard isn't really adequate for many hangers. The rooftop terrace has brilliant views both up and downtown, breakfast can be taken up there and guests can take their own food and drink up there too - spent an hour early evening with the the terrace to ourselves. Great location for nightlife too around ludlow, rivington, and over on avenues a and b towards tompkins square park which is only 5 mins walk.

title: “The Pearl is a Gem”
text: My wife and I spent 3 nights at the Pearl in May of 2012. The location is perfect for theatre goers and for touring New York with subway stops very nearby. The concierge desk was very helpful and knowledgable. We were delighted to have our room upgraded to a very spacious suite. Complimentary breakfast is good and the hotel bar and restaurant is quiet and friendly. If you are looking for a hotel that is central to Times Square, theaters, restaurants and convenient subway entrances this is the place.

title: “Sheraton Gateway”
text: Very good hotel,in a perfect location to reach LAX. Rooms are comfortable, clean and large, with an high quality of beds. The service is punctual, even in in-room dining and the hotel brasserie is very good. Good service of shuttle bus every 20 minutes to/from LAX. The perfect choice to stay near the airport.

title: “Great time in DC”
text:
Just got back from 3 nights in DC and had a fantastic time at the Embassy Suites DC Convention Center. The staff were excellent and the value outstanding (hot breakfast and 2 hour free drinks each night) while the quality of the accommodations was excellent. We were only a few blocks from the Circulator bus but really it was only a few blocks to walk to the Mall and we did this with our three kids (10,8 and 5) a few times with no complaints. 
The pool is small but clean and safe and the kids enjoyed it a lot. There are lots of windows in the pool area making it feel pretty open and some sun makes it's way in later in the day. I went down to the bar and was happily given some drinks in plastic cups that we could drink in the pool area while we watched the kids play, a great way to wind down after a busy day on the Mall. I would highly recommend this hotel on all counts except perhaps the room service food which wasn't that great, but it wasn't too expensive either. Anyway plenty of restaurant options close by. Breakfast is included in the room rate and pretty decent.
We would go back tomorrow.

title: “Great for families. Not so much for business”
text:
October 2012
This hotel had the best reviews. It seems primarily geared toward families with kids though. At least this appeared to be the the demographic when I stayed there. In other words I'm saying it was kind of noisy. Other than that the room was clean, spacious and comfortable. Breakfast, not so hot. Wi-fi signal spotty and weak. All in all though this is a great value if you are in the area for a while and want a cheap, decent place to cook your own food and set up camp. That is if you don't mind little kids being little kids next door. If you're a business traveler, like me, maybe it's not the best choice. I'm going to keep looking for the "perfect" Choice Hotel in this area.

title: “Smooth flowing conference”
text: The DoubleTree conference staff was helpful and fun to work with. They timing was speedy and the staff provided good service. The hotel's event coordinator was beyond helpful. She is very good at her job and she provided beneficial information which lead to a successful conference. Overall, the participants enjoyed the foods and their rooms.

title: “Great Place to Stay in the City”
text: We wanted a place near our daughter's apartment and took a chance on Park South-- it was $199 on Quikbooks, when we arrived they had my price at $209 but instantly adjusted it when I asked about it. The room was smallish but comfortable, shower was great, free breakfast was excellent, NYTimes delivered to door each day (except Sunday), getting ice delivered to the room took awhile but the fridge kept it frozen so we only had to do this twice. Rooms were clean and staff was excellent-- lots of little restaurants near by...and easy access to the 6 Subway...plus lots of cabs... Grand Central within a few blocks, Madison Park and the Shake Shack within in a couple of blocks...we had a terrific stay-- will go there again!!

title: “Can't beat it!”
text: This was the 3rd time we have stayed a night at the Harbor Court while attending a Friday night and Saturday Giant's game. The hotel has friendly, helpful staff and a fabulous location: easy walking distance to AT & T Park. Breakfast across the street at the Farmer's Market. Parking is only $20 if you have a hybrid!

title: “Good for one night, very nice furnishings, next to Lucas Oil.”
text:
We booked a room through hotwire for $57. It was downtown and I was willing to gamble given that it was one night and 90% of people from hotwire liked it. 
It is right next to Lucas Oil Stadium. If you take a left out of the complex and then two rights at 10am you can purchase tickets for a Lucas Oil tour at 11am. They will tell you where to park, it is down the road a little and to the right. $5 to park. You enter through the pro shop for your tour.
The hotel I knew was updated having been a previous hotel at some point, you could tell that from the hot tub. The rooms look new, the furnishings are very nice and nice artwork on the walls. The king room with pull out sofa was next to the street and you could see the stadium. We had to keep the air on low all night to cover some of the street noise, it was fine for a night. The room had a fridge, mini sink and microwave. The shower was very easy to work. Everything was clean except for one stray hair on the bed, again, for one night and the price I paid, I wasn't complaining. 
When I checked in the lady was not as friendly as some other hotels I have stayed at and reviewed on here, but she checked me in and told me the hot tub itself wouldn't be open until 5pm because they were refilling it. Great, it is nice to know they clean the area. I have kids, the highlight of a stay in a hotel is getting to swim after a long day of sight seeing. At 515 we go downstairs and see an out of service sign on the the whole pool area. No! ( for my sanity ). I go to the front desk and a new lady had come in at 3 pm after I checked in. I asked her when the pool would be open and she asked maintenance and came back with an 8 pm reply. No smile, no sorry, no I apologize but we had to do this and I'm sure you understand. She didn't know I wasn't paying a full rate, and it shouldn't have mattered. Because I do understand things happen, it was the lack of friendliness overall on this trip that leads me to only recommend it for a night. We went to the pool at 640 to check and see perhaps was it open? And it was, we got in our swim before bedtime. We had a great time, it was clean and nice. 
They have a "SuiteShop". If you forget anything, or want ice cream or soda, they have it there. No milk though. I heard no sounds on a Monday night from any other rooms. We ordered pizza from a local Mancino's pizza place featured in the room directory and they delivered.
I would recommend this for a one night stay, with family or otherwise. I think in general a lot of hotels don't seem to have the "welcome to HIE thank you for staying with us, how was your stay etc? " Just general friendliness I guess I want to stay, and since I'm trying to relax and make some memories with my family those are the sorts of places I just won't stay in more than once.

title: “Quick stop - wished I could have stayed longer”
text: First, let me say I am a FAN of the KIMPTON brand. Again, I was very pleased. For this trip, I was collecting my daughter from a cruise trip down at the pier on Sat morning and wanted a reliable hotel to place our heads after a long workweek. My college age son accompanied me and we convinced an aunt to also book a room at this property for the night. Just walking into this historic building is a treat in itself. Marble from floor to three stories up, WOW! I cannot tell you how beautiful it was, you have to see it in person. Any train buffs out there? This is your hotel! It is the former home of the B&O RR Headquarters; apparently, they did QUITE well back in the day... Our room was a double queen, smartly decorated and very clean (I am particular). It was also very quiet. The mini-bar was fun to puruse, for our stay they had a wine promotion - 2 tickets for wine at the bar in addtion to the wine hour in the lobby, we met for din at the hotel B&O Brasserie that night for convenience and the food was outstanding. For Kimpton Loyal rewards members, they had a special "raid the mini-bar" promotion too; we had $15 in complimentary mini-bar credit, fun! I truly did not want to leave the hotel at 7am in the morning, and plan to return when we can enjoy for a weekend getaway. If you are traveling by rail or bus, it is a very convenient location downtown. Not far up the hill is the lovely Mount Vernon neighborhood. Looking forward to exploring this stately area on our next stay.

title: “A great boutique hotel, but service makes this a 4-Star property and not a St. Regis.”
text: Positives: Beautiful historic building in a great location; Beds are extremely comfortable. Food in the hotel's restaurant is very good as expected; Great place to have a small reception. Negatives: Bathrooms are extremely small and awkward; The in-mirror TV in the bathroom is hard to see and the channels don't correspond to the main TV or the channel guide provided; The Hotel "Athletic Club" is small and poorly equipped, so the hotel directs you to a has-been club 2.5 blocks away at $15 per day; Service is inconsistent--most times the staff presence and attentiveness is as expected and at other times the staff presence and attitude rivals that of a motel; Concierge was present less than half the time I walked up to the counter and the one time I called, I received a message; Nightly turndown service can occur early in the evening before dinner or at an expected time after 8pm. One night, staff forgot to draw the curtains, once accidentally unplugged the Bose radio (should be turned on at turndown) and left, and twice failed to removed room service plates and food left on the table; Some bathroom accessories need to be replaced or polished--the plastic toilet seat cover was well scuffed and unattractive. Again, this is a beautiful property in a perfect location. The rates at the property have dropped since I last visited, but even at $400, when you book at a St. Regis, you expect St. Regis attention and service. In their own words, St. Regis is supposed to be an experience "beyond expectation," yet this property failed to meet my expectations. To be fair, this is a historic property, so little can be done about the size and layout of the bathrooms, but most of the inconveniences are a result of poor training, poor coordination and poor supervision. Based on the number of similar reviews, perhaps its time for a new GM.

title: “nice place, but found bed bug”
text:
nice hotel and room was ok, good location. but on the last day, when i was packing up i found a bed bug on my pillow. the little [--] was alive and walking around. i squashed him and called the front desk. at first i don't think they understood that it was a bedbug that i was talking about, but they came to check. 
when one of the employees saw it and realized what it was, they took it seriously, apologized, moved me into another room (even though it was my last day, i kept my stuff there in the new room until i was ready to fully check out) and when i went back to my old room, they had an exterminator there already.

title: “Beat expectations”
text: I needed two nights stay in west LA. When I checked the hotel prices, it turned out that I would need to spend at least $400-500 for my stay, which did not make me happy. So I booked a two-star hotel from hotwire for less then $100 per night. That hotel turned out to be Azul Inn. Looking at the photos and reviews, I thought that I would have two nights of hell there, but everything went above my expectations. The room was good in size, clean, the bed was comfortable, all personnel were friendly, and there was not too much noise. Besides, there is free parking (I had no trouble finding an available spot during my stay), free breakfast (though very basic), free safe box, and free internet (not the fastest I've seen, but does the job). I don't know what else to expect from a 2* hotel in the heart of West LA. Probably the only down side is how the hotel looks from outside: Next to a busy road with a cheap motel feeling, but I could not be happier in the end, especially considering what I paid for it.

title: “Nice hotel, helpful staff, great location!”
text: I stayed at this hotel during a conference. The room was clean and nice. The staff was very nice and helpful. And the location was great -- access to the trolley, around the corner from the convention center, and lots of shops and restaurants all around! I'd definitely stay there again.

title: “Incredible NYC Property”
text:
This was the second time I’ve stayed at this property. I liked it even more this time around. The location is top-notch. It’s literally a stone’s throw away from Penn Station, so if you’re arriving by train, you couldn’t be in a more convenient location. Unlike many of the hotels a little farther to the north, the Affinia isn’t stuck in the middle of the most egregious tourist traps that New York has to offer, but it isn’t unreasonably far from them if that sort of thing interests you. It is close to Chelsea, Hell’s Kitchen, and a number of subway lines which make it incredibly easy to get downtown.
Most of the bad reviews for this property are from people with completely unrealistic expectations. If you have realistic expectations about what a New York City hotel is, the Affinia Manhattan will not disappoint. If you’re expecting a room like something you’d find in Las Vegas or a suburban hotel next to the interstate, you’re probably going to be disappointed here and everywhere else in New York City.

title: “Parking a hassle”
text:
Guests must use valet parking, a pain.
The pool supposedly closes at 10 p.m., but staff seems relucant to enforce that curfew.
Staff was clueless when it came to deleting a message on our phone saying we needed to report to the front desk.
The free breakfasts were excellent.

title: “Loved the Worthington”
text: Had a wonderful stay. Very comfortable beds, nice decor, great room service, perfect location. The only things I didn't like bathtbub was very small. Also pool was small and indoor.

title: “Nice Hotel Good Location attentive staff”
text: Nice place, great breakfast buffet, near Metro station, near Dupont Circle affordable weekend rates

title: “Hell in Hell's Kitchen”
text: I have stayed at better hotels in the third world, no kidding. The NYPD was always in the lobby writing police reports about thefts that happened in the hotel. I discovered that my room key opened every door on the fifth floor. Stay away, I was lucky and did not get ripped off, but I heard and saw horrible stories and situations.

title: “Great Courtyard close to the Airport”
text:
This is a newer Courtyard close to DEN. It has the new lobby, and nice new rooms. the front desk was very nice and helpful. the room was great with all the amenities a business traveler would expect.
One exception. I called the front desk from the airport and it took 2 tries to speak to a human

title: “My 1.5 year stay - Excellent!!”
text:
Due to my current job position in Houston I need a long term place to stay. Extended Stay, Energy Corridor, met my needs in both location and rate. Since I have been here, the entire staff have done all possible to make my stay pleasant.
Haris, the Mgr., has done so much to improve my stay. When the hotel remodeled, and I had to relocate, I was told I would get my room back, and Haris was true to his word, I did. When I see him, he asks if I need anything or have problems, if I do, he does what is needed.
The Reception Staff, Kenny, Atriana, Jaber are always available and ready to assist.
Housekeeping, Maria, Yolanda, Alaba keep an immaculate room, and as scheduled.
After many plces worldwide, this the BEST I have been!!

title: “An original -- both pros and cons.”
text:
I'm torn so I'm going to write this review as objectively as possible. The Palace is just grand downstairs. The dining room is amazing, it's all old school glitz and glamour. The rooms upstairs are charming, if you were in a country house in England. It's just a little out of place, since you know there are 270 rooms or whatever there.
The bed was very comfortable, but the walls are paper thin. I could hear someone blowing their nose (I'm not kidding) and also the pipes of the shower the next morning. I probably wouldn't stay there again.
But the Palace is an original and may deserve some of your time if you love the turn of the century style. It's also in a great location!

title: “Great Value”
text: My wife and I spent two nights at the Argonaut and were blown away by the service, room decor, location and amenities. This hotel is the total package. It is a real bargain comapred with other hotels in an otherwise very expensive area. You can walk to almost all the top tourist spots and great shopping. We will definately stay at the Aronaut again and again.

title: “Great Conference Hotel”
text: During our conference I was very pleased to find Revolution Tea offered with the coffee service. As a tea drinker I often bring my own tea due to the lack of tea offerings. Thank You. Also the service staff providing our meals during the conference were very helpful with my questions and were able to get me desserts from the kitchen that were not sitting in the decorative raspberry sauce that was served as I am severly allergic to raspberries. This accomidation by them was much appreciated! And the concierge and bell staff were very helpful during my stay, and were able to answer questions about food options nearby.

title: “Let down by service staff”
text: The hotel is well serviced by a number of Metro stations (Foggy Bottom, Farragut North & Farragut West) which makes it easy to get around. THe hotel is slightly on I (eye) St NW which is a good thing as Penn Ave can be noisy with ambulance sirens. Reception was friendly and good with maps and info. Despite comments in previous reviews, the elevators (2) were modern and quick (although very small). We had one of the Parkview Suites which was a decent enough size although sparsely furnished. The main bedroom has a king size bed which was very comfortable. The lounge area has a pull-out sofa which was OK for our 11yo. The bathroom is VERY small. We didn't eat at the hotel as there are many good restaurants close by (try Founding Farmers and El Chalan Peruvian). Now I get to the service staff. Firstly the door guys mostly stood out the front chatting to each other and talking on their mobile phones. The door was not opened for us and they seemed more busy on their own business. They were not professional at all and I have to say a very motley crew. Secondly the housekeeping. Our room was clean enough but housekeeping has a strange racket going on with the bottled water. We were given 2 bottles of water each day but these aren't just left in the room for you. No, the housekeeper waits each evening until they know you are in and then they'll deliver the 2 bottles personally. This was obviously just so you gave them a tip. Otherwise why don't they just leave them in the room? As I said, this is a racket and I don't even know if this is endorsed by the hotel or a money making scheme by housekeeping.

title: “Excellent”
text:
Staying here for a NYC vacation Dec 2010. Got a suite with a separate bedroom which is working out great with two small kids. Great location - very close to Grand Central.
Lobby is a bit cramped and seems like it's always busy.
Great staff - very helpful and nice - highly recommend. We will be staying here for all our future trips!

title: “Value for the money!”
text: Got a room with absolutely no view, but it was perfectly clean, and so was the shared bathrooms and the rest of the hotel. Perfect location and great value for the money. We would stay there again..

title: “Worth it.”
text: This hotel is clean,centrally located,and has small Starbucks kiosk.it is great for business meetings as well.

title: “Service that Makes the ritz taste like a partially hydrogenated cracker wrapped in yellow wax paper”
text: Some of the best service I have ever experienced. They would literally drop whatever they were doing to help you. They have an courtesy Escalade that I used instead of taxi's and I tipped the kids driving- they would pick me up anywhere downtown as well. The rooms were spotless (mine was on the tight side but well appointed). Every time you sat in the lobby they would ask if you wanted something to drink, etc... coffee, water, etc.. the doormen would run to open them for you and the bartenders encouraged samples of all the local micro brews. the housekeeprs were fantastic as well.

title: “Because the price of the room was due to being part of a...”
text: Because the price of the room was due to being part of a conference, it was more than reasonable. I understand for the location, the price of the rooms are usually much more, but I would not pay the $300 + as the rooms are very worn and the carpeting was very dirty. There was also a musty smell when I returned to my room at the end of the day. The TV picture and sound were also poor quality due to age. The hotel provides earplugs because of the street noise, weekends are very noisy. The location is very convenient though; close to the Bart. I could easily walk to museums, parks, Union Square. If you are there to shop, the location is fantastic. The maid service was very good and there was followup by the supervisor to make sure all rooms had been cleaned. Although I did not use the hotel restaurant, the food service provided for the conference was very good; the wait staff very attentive. And most of the meals provided through out the conference were good, with a few exceptions. I would possibly return if the rates were reasonable - but not at the current posted rates for the current condition of the rooms.

title: “Customer Service is Incredible”
text: The staff at the Hotel Palomar are super friendly, professional and just downright wonderful! They made my stay so nice while I was there all week. I didn't realize it was a pet friendly hotel and wish I had brought my dog with me while I was on my business trip. The parking is expensive, but there's really no where else to park in Westwood. The fitness center was small, but usable. The rooms are really comfortable, very clean and it's within walking distance to a lot of good eateries too since it's close to UCLA. Easy access to the freeway as well.

title: “Good Value "Green" Hotel On Bush Street”
text: Have enjoyed several stays at The Orchard Hotel which enjoys a good location on Bush Street two blocks above Union Square. The rooms are comfortable, attractive and moderately priced. They use hypoallergenic cleaning products, forbid smoking and meet the standards of chemically sensitive guests like ourselves. While the healthy choice restaurant on the ground floor has never appealed to us, Roxanne's Cafe fourty steps away on the corner at Powell is one of our favorite local places for breakfast, lunch and dinner. The cable car also runs on Powell which provides convenient transportation up and down the big hills when needed. We also like The Orchard's proximity to the Grand Hyatt on Sutter which has a top floor restaurant and bar area providing commanding views of the city and Bay in addition to a good menu. We have many breakfasts there and don't mind the two block walk downhill for a convenient meal in a congenial setting. The Orchard fulfills all the basic comfort requirements admirably (hair dryers, robes and nice marble bathrooms) and the staff is polite and friendly. The suites have TVs in both the bedroom and sitting area which provide nice viewing alternatives. We also make use of the DVD player in the room by bringing a collection of our favorite movies from home since we find the local cable selection a little thin. The Orchard is a competently managed mid-tier hotel and an enjoyable place to stay. In the only incident where we had cause for complaint, the management addressed the problem expeditiously and completely satisfied us with their response. We will undoubtedly stay there again. It should be noted that the same company also owns a property called "The Orchard Garden Hotel" a coupe of blocks further down Bush Street. This review is not about that property and guests should be careful to direct their cab drivers to the correct address (665 Bush Street) lest they find themselves unrecognized at check-in (as happened to my son at Christmas).

title: “Although a bit pricy, it's a great place to stay”
text: The location is wonderful and allows you to walk to the mall. The rooms are large and well appointed. The beds are very comfortable. Ask for a room that does not face the back of the hotel.......you will view the air conditioning units and another building. The rooms are on this side are also dark. Opt for a room that faces the front of the hotel or the side (away from the White House). The lobby of the hotel is beautiful and a pleasure to sit with friends and relax a bit. The service was excellent and I would love to stay here again.

title: “Another Excellent Stay With Some reservations”
text:
Recently spent two nights at a discounted <$250/night rate. Corner larger than average room with an unobstructed view of the Hudson. Usual excellent housekeeping, large flat screen TV, comfortable king bed, and furnishings in good repair.
Room was ready upon arrival at 12:15 PM on a Friday afternoon.
