Only reservations: the breakfast buffet which is pricey (we already knew that) didn't seem to have very tasty food. No waffles or pancakes..just kinda tired French toast; OK omelet. Good, fast service however. Buffet at the nearby Crowne Plaza is better IMO.
Always stay here since we normally travel to NYC to see shows and the location for Broadway theatres cannot be beat. Nearby Westin and Hilton Garden Inn would be possible alternatives as would the Renaissance across Times Square.
Overall will almost undoubtedly stay again since we know what to expect.

title: “With Sincere Thanks”
text: Can't say enough about how friendly and help full the people of Jerry's Motel are. On the night we arrived the reception lady drove us down to LA live so we could get a meal. That meant so much to us as we were hungry tired and a little unsure re safety haveing never been to L/A before. Do agree with others a car is the way to go and as we were keen to walk every where the location is not suited to this.Thank You !!!!

title: “Incredibly pleased by an affordable airport hotel”
text:
This hotel gives you almost everything you need for a comfortable business visit near the airport: Clean, quiet rooms; fast room service; a surprisingly good restaurant and bar; and a free shuttle to and from LAX. Plus the price can't be beat.
My room was clean, quiet and up to date. I could see plans landing at LAX, but I'm a New Yorker, and so I barely noticed the noise. The hotel is far enough from the runways that you shouldn't be bothered. I was a little concerned when I hear a barking dog in the early afternoon and was told that there's a kennel nearby, but the faint barking did subside by the evening. And I'm particularly sensitive to sound, so I would definitely have been bothered if it had continued.
Room service was exceptionally fast and the restaurant offers more than the usual fare. The fish tacos are especially good. It's a bit pricey, though.
My only complaint: More and more of the hotels I stay at for business offer free Wi-Fi, and this Westin should follow suit.

title: “DC on a budget”
text: My teen son and I stayed at the Grand Hyatt for 5 nights the week after Christmas 2011. I got a good rate from Southwest.com and it was a good location for us since we had no vehicle. Good thing too since the hotel charges $40 a day for parking with NO in/out priveldges! Ouch! Most attractions are within 10-15 minutes walking distance. The hotel has underground access to a nearby Metro (subway) connection which is actually the hub for all the trains...makes getting around very easy. Using a subway was new to us so there was a learning curve...look at the metro website for info before you go. Be sure to have lots of singles too...you can get change for a five but its all in coin and the machine wont accept it back. The room was very comfortable...feather bedding and pillows, thick soft towels, large flat screen. huge bath. Coffee maker but no tea or micro. The fridge was nice and cold for drinks. The atrium in this hotel is beautiful! The buffet breakfast is pricey..$22 pp. We opted to eat in the Zephir deli next tot he Starbucks on the ground floor...you can get a hot egg sammie and juice for around $7. There is a Mc'ds a block away if you walk outside and to your left 2 blocks then go up a block. Other than that there is Lincolns Waffle House a few blocks away....across from Ford's Theater. Capitol City Brew Co is across the street...very good food, great fast service...reasonable prices considering its in DC. Tues. is $2 beer night! ChinaTown is a few blocks away and there are a myriad of restaurants....not all Chinese...to choose from. Be careful at night..its a tad sketchy there. Go early and watch out for panhandlers. Ask for a map of attractions at the front desk to find restaurants and attractions. The concierge is also helpful. Room service was very pricey so we did not use it...wifi is $15 a day and the gym is not free so we did not partake. In room movies will set you back $18...we found enuf to watch on the channels they offered for free. The staff were helpful and maid service was good altho the staff woke is several times talking to each other in the hall. You could hear every word they said to each other. There is a construction project going on across the street so ask for a room away form the front. There are no safes in rooms but you can get a free safe box at the front desk. My only true complaint: the remote was missing and it took 2 calls and a full hour to get one after checking in. Overall a very nice stay!

title: “Clean, convenient motel in SF with free parking”
text: We stayed for 2 nights here at the end of our holiday and it was just great. The free car parking gave my husband a break from driving and the room was clean and much larger than I expected for a city centre motel. It was within easy walking distance of Fisherman's Wharf and Chinatown etc and the reception staff were very friendly.

title: “Exceeds all expectations”
text:
The Hotel Union Square is a truly a gem right in the heart of Union Square. You absolutely can not beat the location, at the bottom of Powell, just a few steps from BART and the trolley car. 
The staff is exceedingly gracious and helpful. There is a complimentary wine tasting each evening from 5:00-6:00 pm, and the staff encourages guests to participate generously, even allowing you to take multiple glasses back to your room to enjoy in privacy. 
There is wireless access, but if you don't feel like toting your laptop, there is a computer in the lobby and a 24-hour business center downstairs where you can print boarding passes at no additional charge.
The decor is newly renovated, with very modern, decent-sized rooms. The best part is the price, very reasonable (less than $125) for this city.

title: “Amazing location, service, staff, room (Towers room) but beware of construction noise and validate room rate”
text:
Incredible hotel right in the heart of New York City. An incredibly friendly staff, always smiling, going out of there away to be helpful. Stayed in Towers part of building which has big rooms, well furnished and plenty of light. A few things to be aware of though. 1. Best rooms are on the west side because you have unobstruced view, but you cannot reserve these in advance and all the suites and connecting rooms are on that side of hotel, so close to impossible to get them. Views on east side are ok, but you need to be on the 48th floor or above to have a great view (we were on 43rd). 2. There is massive construction site just to the SE side of the buiding and no mattere what floor you are on it is extremely loud all the time. Only break is between midnight and 4am. Bring earplugs, you will need them. 3. If you are staying in thw towers part of the hotel, which is definite worth it, despite what the web site says, access to the towers club lounge is not always included. Ask them twice and make them send it to you in writing ... When we checked in we were told we did not have access, then showed them in writing from the reservation agent and they gave us access, but the lady said normally would have doubled the price of the room! That being said, while it is certainly not worth double the room price it is AMAZING! Fantastic food and drinks basically all day long. So you could actually eat breakfast lunch and dinner in there, it is on the 39th floor so you get a great view on top of it all. 
So overall a great hotel in a great location with a super friendly staff. Take the towers rooms, validate your rates and bring earplugs (or wait til construction is finished) and you will have a great stay.

title: “Best in Manhatten”
text: Great location;wonderful staff;beds to die for;showers that thrilled my 17 year old;turndowns my 8 year loved,and finally views that are amazing

title: “Nice, clean, cheap rooms in Manhattan”
text: We stayed there 3 nights, in a bunk-bed room with no bathroom. We were pleasantly surprised by the cleanliness of the room, and cleanliness of the shared showers and bathroom. A bit of a wee walk (but subway stations are close) from Times Square, but overall, for the price, cleanliness, and location, this is a great place to stay.

title: “Good for just a bed and desk”
text:
I stayed here for 2 days for business. The room was SO small. It was fine with me for my limited stay in the actual room, but you had to move the desk chair to open the bathroom door! The room was clean, but there is no way you could have more than 1 person in there. The 2nd floor has a “living room” and I am sure that is for the claustrophobic people who had to get out of their small room. The living room has a lot of book and magazines. The lobby is also very inviting and relaxing.
Nearby is EVERYTHING you would want – shopping, restaurants, you name it. Very easy to get a taxi or get to busses, etc. 
Great for business traveler – definitely not for families!

title: “A great place to do business!”
text: I had an extended court case in downtown San Diego and was fortunate to find the W. The rooms were large. clean. quiet and comfortable. The best part of the stay by far was the staff. Everyone from Dion at the bell desk, Kelly and Patrick at the bar and Samar at room service was amazing. The front desk was excellent as well. I would (and do) book the W anytime I am in San Diego now.

title: “Great Location Good Price”
text: Even though the rooms are small, the hotel's location is amazing. The hotel itself is very elegant, clean and the staff is nice.

title: “The Best Yet In NYC”
text:
I arrived with a large group of 29 as part of a charity event and from the minute we arrived to the minute we departed we were so well looked after it was a service hard to beat. On arrival the manager came onto our bus to welcome us all and to give us some basic information about the hotel, the locality and the services they offered. He gave us each a card with his number on it if we needed anything. We were all checked in super fast and there was plenty of helping hands to assist with our luggage.
The Room was amazing exactly like on the website. The room was very big by New York standards it way exceeded expectations. The bed was fantastic I really didnt want to get out of it. The breakfast was continental and plenty of it. Fresh coffee, tea, bagels, toast, croissants, muffins, cereals, fruit, yougarts and fresh fruit juice.
The location was perfect for our trip it was literally 2 mins walk to times square but on a busy street with plenty of bars and restaratunts to choose from hence the name of the street restaraunt row. The hotel bar had some great food and drinks offers too and was lively every night.
On departure we had a late night flight but checkout time was 11am. The staff kindly told us to just leave our luggage in the rooms and they would look after it for us which they did. I must also compliment the reception staff as wether it be 7am 7pm or 3am they were always bright, cheerful and welcoming. I will definitely be back on my next visit....

title: “Amazing”
text: From the service to the uniqueness of decor and rooms, Aveda toiletries, and the friendliness and helpfulness of the staff made our stay very enjoyable will return there whenever we are in Seattle.

title: “Best bang for your buck”
text: This past December me and my two daughter's stayed at Morningside Inn on the upper west side of Manhattan. This made the 6th or 7th time we have stayed here. It is a great place if you are watching your pennies. It is a hostel, so no mints on your pillow, but it is very clean, safe and Patrick and his staff are wonderful. The neighborhood is very safe, and it has a lot of great restaurants within walking distance and is very close to Columbia University. Also it is only a couple of blocks from the Subway and less than a block from the bus. Would highly recommend it to anyone!!

title: “Excellent hotel and rooms.”
text:
We stayed 1 night here so we could visit Hollywood on our road trip between Las Vegas and Huntington Beach. It was a good choice for us. After reading some of the other reviews, it's clear that not all of the rooms have been renovated. We had the kids suite, which was very new and modern and the kids loved having their own area with bunk beds. The location is convenient to the highway and Universal, which we did not visit. The hotel shuttle can drop you off at the Metro station and goes out every hour (we walked about 20 minutes there) and you can take the Metro for 1 stop and you're in Hollywood. So no need to drive. We saw everything in Hollywood Boulevard and then returned on the Metro. We walked back to the hotel and on the way, stopped at a nearby shopping center which has a nice Ralph's grocery store, Jamba Juice, etc. so we loaded up on snacks and drinks. Very convenient. The next morning, we drove to see the nearby Hollywood signs and take pictures and then headed out to the coast with a drive through Rodeo Drive and Beverly Hills. So the location worked perfectly for us. 
We did not eat at the restaurant (but kids eat free) but we did use the pool and hot tub, which were great after our long drive. It was also very convenient that they had a very nice and clean laundry room (with free detergent!) right next to the pool. So I took care of doing a load of laundry while hanging out at the pool.
Yes, you pay for parking and it's $15 for a safe lot. Although I think maybe people pay different rates for parking? You probably could park on the street though. There were local cars parked there.
The hotel is not inexpensive, but it's probably the nicest Holiday Inn I've seen and the room we had was very nice and updated and the courtyard area and pool and hot tub were very nice and made it worth it. 
I would stay here again.

title: “Ok, but you can probably do better.”
text:
The hotel is faily clean with a good location. That's about all that can be said for it. The desk staff ranges from friendly and inept to rude an inept. The standard room (which Hotels books) is hardly big enough for the bed to go into. Upon viewing this room, I asked about an upgrade. They told me that since I'd booked through Hotels, there could be no upgrade. When I was ready to leave, they said they could upgrade me to a "Jr. Suite" for an additional $75 a night. Add this to the $100 a night I'd already paid, and I'm only $25 away from staying at a really nice hotel, like the Hilton across the street. So, this place is really no bargain.
Best part: Location
Worst parts: Front desk staff who really doesn't know ANYTHING. I asked for a spoon one night to eat some hard-packed ice cream, and the front desk clerk REFUSED to give me a spoon. I've never seen a hotel that would refuse a guest such a simple, basic, reasonable request. The elevator is tiny and very slow. If you try to take the stairs, be careful. The stairs are not even big enough to put your whole foot on--a real safety hazard.

title: “Great first visit to the Dana”
text:
We were attending the wedding of a friend's daughter at the Dana, and stayed a total of four nights. The rooms were clean. comfortable, and appealing in our building (one of the older ones). The beds are a delight, with comforters and plenty of fluffy pillows. Our room was also very quiet, despite being in the middle of the building.
Although we didn't have a great view, we found the room's central location very convenient in meeting and keeping up with friends staying in the other buildings. All the rooms have a small fridge and microwave, a nod to the lack of breakfast restaurants (besides the Blue Pearl) nearby. 
The location of the hotel itself is convenient to lots of local attractions. There are rentals for bikes for the bay trail and all kinds of watercraft. The hotel's lush landscaping and low profile (no higher than 3 stories) gives it a more deluxe, private feel than I was expecting. The Blue Pearl is a good casual restaurant, and the food and drinks at the Firefly were delicious. 
The hotel staff were marvelously helpful and friendly at all times, whether it was talking to a housekeeper about our room, arranging for a late check-out, or dealing with some detail of the wedding reception in the ballroom. I was very impressed with the hotel on that basis alone.
I am trying to figure out when I can go the Dana for another delightful stay!

title: “The Metro station under the hotel was great”
text:
I'm really happy I picked this hotel simply for its location. We planned to spend the majority of our time at the different Smithsonian museums and if you walk outside the main door of the hotel, make a right, and walk about 2 blocks you arrive at the Smithsonian castle. Although the hotel is in an area that doesn't have much to offer at night, having a metro stop right under the hotel was just perfect, we used it to get everywhere. Myself and my girlfriend felt safe at night having an elevator that came right up into the hotel. 
The room was very clean, although it could use updating. The wall paper in our room was peeling, the furniture was badly scratched, the phones were at least 20 years old, and the art on the walls was beginning to wrinkle and turn yellow. If you want any sort of air circulating in the room you can hear it run constantly. None of that stuff about the room bothered me or my girlfriend. We wanted a hotel in a good location, safe, and clean; the L'Enfant Plaza Hotel fulfilled all of those wants. We didn't plan to spend much time in our room just to sleep and take an occasional break from sightseeing.
If you don't feel comfortable using the metro to get around the city I wouldn't book a room here. It's vital because if you don't choose to have dinner in the hotel there is really no other choices within reasonable walking distance. We used the metro to get everywhere including breakfast, lunch, and dinner (the hotel's dinning options were ridiculously over priced). Getting a taxi in that area is not a reasonable option. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who plans to visit the Smithsonian museums or explore the national mall.

title: “What a dump!”
text: Bathroom sink partially clogged, cold shower, paper thin walls and the rattling noisy, stop and start heating unit.

title: “Worst Hotel we ever stayed at!”
text:
First night came into bustling hotel checking in at 11:15 p.m. DJ and about 11 Bouncers in the lobby..even a bouncer for the elevator. Checked in, ordered room service and went to sleep. Was awakened at 2:00 a.m. when the party started next door. Finally called security at 3:30 then at 4:30. Everytime they came up, the party got louder. They all finally left at 6:30 in the morning.
Next day, they offered to move our room. When they moved us, they forgot a dresser of clothes. I called the "Whenever Whatever" service line and told them we were missing the items in the dresser. The called back, said security checked the room and there was nothing there. Called again later to say I had confirmed I did not have the items and could they please let me check the room. They never called me back. I was hoping I had an extra key and went to try to get in the room myself. Some worker saw me and I told them the story. They let me in and of course my clothes were there.
Next night at the bar having the free complementary glass of champange that they gave us for the horrible night we had before, my husband went to the restroom and this man called me a horrible name I won't repeat because I didn't like Obama. Told my husband what he said and my husband ran up to him and called him a coward...and many other choice works for talking to a woman like that and the guy called security and turned my husband in for assault. My husband spent the night in jail because of this guy. Now we had to hire and attorney and go back there. Security should have just kicked the guy out! 
To top it off, the night my husband was in jail I got to hear the next door gay gentleman having a sexual relationship starting at 3:00 a.m. 
It ruined our whole trip and month. I recommend that everyone boycott this hotel. We are in our early 50's and just wanted to have a good time and see out country now that our kids are grown and gone.

title: “best hotel in NYC”
text: Loved this hotel. The location can't be beat. We like to stay in midtown area and this hotel has the largest rooms by far. Huge bathroom and tub and well lit (a rarity for hotel rooms it seems). Smaller hotel so you get better personal service than the other chains in the area. Staff were very friendly and accomodating. Parking is available at a reduced rate for hotel guests in nearby garage. Highly recommend. Book early for the best rates. Ask for upgrade when checking in.

title: “Excellent experience”
text: We stayed here for a night out in the city. We loved the hotel. The rooms are a little small, but you are staying in NYC right on times square. The hotel is nicely decorated. Each floor has a different wall paper. The pool area was great. The hotel bar has a service window that opens up to the pool. You can order your drinks without leaving the water. The sauna and steam-room were a nice touch as well. They are well kept and a nice relaxing touch. The front office staff was very nice and helpful. The beds were comfortable. Our room was very quite. We didn't hear any of the city noise. The late checkout was a nice touch as well. The room blackout curtains really helped us sleep in too. We did not eat the breakfast buffet so I do not know how it is. There were too many excellent food choices surrounding the hotel to stay in for breakfast. We will definitely stay here again for our next trip into the city.

title: “Needs to be shut down”
text: Cant believe the front desk has the nerve to accept money for this dump. I would rather sleep under a bridge. Checked in for a week and stayed 12 hours. Filthy dump

title: “Great place to stay when visiting OSU.”
text:
I booked a room for my brother and sister-in-law who were in town for a OSU football game. 
This is a recently converted Cross Country Inn and thus, all the rooms and common area have been updated. It appears the new owners are taking great strides to make sure it is a good lodging experience. The staff was friendly and the room was well appointed and clean. The outdoor pool area, although not big, is very clean with plenty of towels. Currently, there is no in-room internet, but the Wi-Fi in the lobby is good and strong and if you have a room near the lobby you can pick up a signal.
The location is also a very big plus. The campus/stadium are within walking distance and a Bob Evens and the very nice Buckeye Cafe are next door. 
I will continue to recommend this hotel to anyone I know who is coming to Columbus for any OSU event.

title: “African Vacation”
text:
We found the hotel to adequate. The breakfast was lacking as the staff were heating pre made food in the same microwave as the guests were using. The variety was less than we've been offered at other nearby hotels. 
We utilized the park and fly option. Upon our return to Denver after a 22 hour flight, we had to wait an hour and half for the hotel shuttle to come by and pick us up. During that time all of the other Tower area hotels cme by 3 - 4 times. We had to wait in line to check in so that it was 2 hours from the time we initially called for a ride and when we actually got a room. The front desk staff were nice, but seemed restricted by rules in trying to be really helpful. As we waited in line we heard "that's not our policy" rather than helping customers to find a solution. 
The rooms were very nice, but other area hotels are a little more enticing for a return visit.

title: “Loved the Waermark”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Watermark Hotel in San Antonio for a Valentine's Day long weekend. We had a WONDERFUL time.
The Watermark is right on the Riverwalk and is truly an outstanding hotel. We found the service to be excellent, from the concierge to the Room service to the hotel maids. Every night the room was freshened with a turndown service and chocolates were placed on the pillows. Our room was on a high floor overlooking the Riverwalk. A LARGE room with a balcony where we ate breakfast every morning.
We had a SPA day and the services at the SPA were good, but not great. Still it was a fun experience. (Try the Cocoa scrub).
The restaurants on the walk are fine, but not truly 5 star. We ate at Pesca at the Watermark (decent seafood), Las Canarias across the street. (Nice atmosphere especially when sitting outside and watching the world go by) and at Boudro's for some excellent guacamole and Margueritas.
We took a day trip to Fredrickburg (about 75 miles away.) It was something to do, but don't expect to be wowed, not even by the Admiral Nimitz museum.
The Alamo is a 5 minute walk away and can be covered in about an hour or so.
Overall, we had a very pleasant time in San Antonio and would recommend it for a relaxing long weekend

title: “Consistently beautiful and comfortable with top service”
text: I had yet another wonderful stay at The Greenwich this weekend utilizing the restaurant, library room and spa and all did not disappoint. A wonderful enjoyable visit. One minor note is my very large room had one of the smallest bathrooms I have experienced there...too small for women so be sure to ask for a bigger bathroom as the rooms are all different. Also if you have a platinum amex, definitely book through them as the benefits are great.

title: “Don't be put off”
text:
Like everyone else that read reviews off this hotel I was very worried about our stay. The worries were unnecessary. Yes it is a little old fashioned, and maybe needs a lick of paint here and there. But it is clean, with the rooms cleaned every day with fresh towels etc.
If there is a critism then the reception desk could be a little bigger or just more staff, the wait could sometimes be a little longer than necessary.
But don't worry it's OK to stay here, if you need anything just ask and they will do their best to help and Location just couldn't be better.

title: “No longer a great place.”
text: First the positives. The St. Francis USED to be the place to stay. It's a historic building, centrally located and has a gorgeous lobby. Now for the bad. We have been at this hotel several times and it will probably be our last. Each time we have been here, the wait to check in has been around 20-30 minutes, even in the SPG preferred line. As a gold members we have never been offered an upgrade. The excuse has always been there are no upgraded rooms available, however there are plenty of them available should you go on to their website to try and book one. There are two buildings at this hotel, the historic building and the tower. Although we did not get to stay in the historic building we visited the floors and they were well taken care of, rooms were nice although a bit smaller than the tower rooms. As far as the tower goes, ICK. It has not been renovated in YEARS, the carpet in the hallway was worn and filthy, the wallpaper old and the lighting awful. Once you get into the room you can expect cleaner carpet a nice bathroom and the typical heavenly bed. However the furniture is dated and worn and the wallpaper was peeling off in several locations. The windows open slightly which is nice. All in all it's an OK place to stay. Do not expect the usual level of comfort, beauty or service as in other Westin properties. The historic building should be branded a Sheraton and the tower should be branded a Holiday Inn. On this trip, for about $50.00 more, we could have stayed at The Palace (luxury collection) which is beautiful, better and a bit quieter location, service is wonderful, amenities are much better and as gold members we have always been upgraded. We were only in SF for one night on this trip so we didn't really care much, but for longer stays we would not stay here again.

title: “Why bother going to Italy when The Grand is right in your own backyard?”
text:
The purpose of my visit was to check out the spa and 5 Star restaurant for a possible
reunion site next year and the experience truly amazed me. From the friendly greetings at valet and Front Desk to the superlative service at both restaurants I was hard pressed 
to find any enduring flaws. The pool service was the only area that needed improvement as it did take quite a while to get a waitperson and she was not versed in the menu. It was just as well as I ended up having lunch at their 'casual restaurant' which had the best $14 hamburger I've ever had. The waiter was great. Served hot bread (rolls and breadsticks freshly baked) and fresh butter. His suggestion of the grilled garlic lime shrimp salad was wonderful. They use freshly ground angus beef (sirloin) and it came rare as desired and the bun was homemade. The dinner at Addison was also wonderful - the highlight being an incredible cheese gougere served as one of three amuse bouches. An explosion of cheese was like a mouth orgasm. Loved it. The lamb however - supposedly a 'signature dish' was oddly sweet and bland and lacked juice. 
Not recommended. The sweet pea ravioli was lovely - almost as good as Spago. All the vegetarian options were very creative and highly recommended. Excellent King Crab first course.
The rooms were well designed, beds extremely comfortable - outfitted with Pratesi sheets. Great bathroom. There was an annoying green light above the bed (smoke alarm?) that was poorly positioned for people who like a dark environment. I would suggest that housekeeping provide eye masks on request. The feel of the place was like a wonderful Italian palace - lavish and opulent and yet warm and inviting. Perfect place to feel pampered and less than 2 hours from Los Angeles. A real gem of a place that I hope is around for a long, long time.

title: “$20 PARKING FEE Automatic Added/ 72 hour Hold on Debit Card”
text: Hotel automatically adds ANTICIPATED Fees and the hotel room charge to your DEBIT BANK CARD and wont release the unused portion for 72 hours AFTER your stay. $20 PARKING FEE is automatically added to your room. They also didn't have the creamer w/coffee in the room they are supposed to have, called guest services TWO times to get the creamer and they never SHOWED. They gave us two rooms we booked together on two DIFFERENT floors, and its a very big hotel. But they have a survey card to make sure you were given their warm chocolate chip cookie, which I found ridiculous, TWO people staying in the room give you ONE cookie. I'd rather they just not give one. Check in person was not very friendly or knowledgeable. I HAVE no plans to their again or the slightest idea how they are rated 4 stars. I will say the room was nice and the bed comfortable.

title: “Great hotel...clean rooms and friendly staff”
text:
I live in Columbus, and my parents came to town from Florida to visit for Christmas. They were there on Christmas night along with a few nights before and after. Everytime I came to pick them up to bring them over to our house they always said it was a great hotel. And each time I came into the lobby the front desk agent (blonde-haired girl i think) always said hi and asked how I was doing. 
It looked really clean and my parents' room was rather large. I'm not sure if it was a standard room or a suite. It wasnt divided by a wall or door, but it had a living room-type sitting area. 
Great place I would really recommend.

title: “Loved it but rooms are very small.”
text: Extremely friendly staff and immaculate rooms. Continental breakfast was above average and lounge area was very well maintained. Wine tasting was very refreshing. Suggestions from staff were very helpful. The main limitation was the size of the room. If you are uncomfortable with small spaces (the room was approximately 11' by 16") this is not the place for you. On the other hand the location was excellent and I am told that most NY hotels have very small rooms. The restaurant next door, Tony's, was very good. One portion for two is more than enough.

title: “Best Staff in San Diego”
text: This was the greatest Holiday Inn i have ever stayed at. Granted it isn't a five star hotel so my expectations werent very high but i was completely astonished with everything in the hotel. The simple touches such as the FREE water in the room all the way to the FREE BEER at their Happy Hour i could not have asked for more. The rooms were larger than expected certainly for Holiday Inn standards. Next door was an excellent Chinese restaurant which we ate at every night. All of this was excellent but the best thing at the hotel by far was the staff. These have got to be the nicest and most accomadating people i have ever met in my life. We stayed Thursday night through Sunday morning and the "PM Boyz" working at the front desk were the most helpful young men in the hotel. They informed us of everything possible to do in San Diego and gave excellent directions. Other than there extensive knowledge of the area they were just fun to talk to and hang out for a couple of minutes at the end of each day. The one with the beard seemed more knowledgeable of the immediate area thus making local travel very easy. The only problem i had was that one of the sunday morning front desk ladies was very rude but the boys the night before made up for it by far. If i come down to San Diego again i will definetly stay here again and recomend it to all of our friends.

title: “Poor service for a Hilton”
text: The hotel is located strategically in times square and close to central park. Lots of eating places around the hotel. Check in was fast and the reception staff courteous. That is where the 'good'ends. On entering the room we found that it was not vacuumed properly, there was even a baby,s pacifier found left from the last guests. Although we were out of the room for most of the day sightseeing the room was sometimes found to be not made up on returning. Even when done it was a sloppy job. Buffet breakfast was OK although the menu was never changed . However what was irksome was the some the staff attending the tables almost demanded a gratuity for a self service buffet, we definitely had planned on giving a tip but such arrogance made us think otherwise.Having stayed at Hilton properties in the far and middle east the house keeping and breakfast services was surely a let down

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: I think this hotel is a great value, right in the heart of Chicago. I would have given it 5 stars if my hotel room window had a better view than the opposite wall of the building and if the beds were actually queen like they claim to be and not doubles. On a more positive note, there is a free pool and hot tub to use and the hotel foyer (if you can even call it that, maybe atrium) is amazing. This place definitely makes a statement from the moment you walk in and see the 3 story high ceilings, painted Sistine Chapel-esque. There is a bar in the foyer as well as bars and restaurants off the sides. One thing to note is that this hotel is HUGE which could be a pro or con depending on your purpose. I think ideally this place is just perfect for a convention which I was not a part of, but still enjoyed myself.

title: “Very large, comfortable room”
text:
The rooms are the reason to stay here. My room was very large - much larger than expected - and had a big TV, a big desk, and its own air con that was fairly quiet. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom was large with a hot, high pressure shower. 
Top marks for giving me what I asked for, i.e. a room on a top floor with a view (unimpeded) of the Empire State Building. Go for a top floor room if you're a light sleeper - there's very little noise. 
The staff are professional and efficient. The service is not personal, but then you wouldn't expect that in this kind of hotel. 
The area is not pretty or pleasant - you wouldn't go for a nice after dinner stroll here - but you're only a minute from the metro so it doesn't matter at all. And it's perfectly safe - the reason it feels a bit dodgy is because most of the shops seem to be selling cheap clothes and second hand watches or offering to unlock SIM cards. (If you're from London, think Tottenham Court Road - a bit of a dump, but basically safe). 
The big slap on the wrist for this hotel is the breakfast. The "breakfast room" was tiny - half the size of the bedroom and not nearly adequate for a hotel of this size. It has no natural light and is dimly lit and basically felt horrible and dingy. There was no air conditioning so it was stiflingly hot. The muffins and doughnuts were actually melting - they looked disgusting. Needless to say, I didn't eat anything.
I made this complaint to the hotel management in response to an email asking for feedback. To his credit, the manager left a message on my voicemail with an apology. I think he sounded very sincere. He said the breakfast room as it is now is a large step up from what it used to be and that it's all the hotel can accommodate for now. He also said it should be air conditioned - so maybe it was just broken when I went. However, I don't think he should have made the point that the breakfast is complimentary. Most hotel breakfasts are, but that's not an excuse for them being bad to the point where I don't want to eat them or even stay in the room a second longer. As for the room size, he said trays are provided in each room so guests can bring breakfast back to their rooms - that's fair enough, I suppose.
Breakfast aside, though, this is a very good hotel to use as a sightseeing base. And, I suppose, who cares about the hotel's breakfast when there are so many eating options on the streets of New York....? It just seemed like a quality let-down, that was all.

title: “Great Location, Clean and Quiet”
text: This hotel is 5 blocks from the White House, and 7 blocks to the Washington Monumrnt, Metro is across the street. Checkin is fast and informative. Rooms are clean and quiet. Food is good. Did not park a car. Used the metro. Taxi fare from DCA to hotel was $15 and too 10 minutes.

title: “Terrible Everything”
text: As many other reviews pointed out, the expectation before arrival is a nice cheap hotel in a decent area. We arrived on a sketchy small street with an out of place hotel right across from a run down warehouse. DO NOT GO TO THIS HOTEL. The relative (It really isn't ) cheaper hotel cost really isn't worth it. The clerk is rude and always make excuses about not giving you the service you ask for, and is overall an unhelpful person. The hotel has nice pictures in their websites, but be warned, those clearly doesn't accurately reflect what the rooms are and the quality of it.

title: “Run down,musky rooms. Very outdated”
text: We booked this hotel because it was located in the Historic district of Philly. The hotel is in a convenient location, but the rooms and staff are awful. From the moment we checked in the frontdesk lady was very rude, unfriendly and b@#chy. At first, we thought maybe she was just having a bad day, but she was the same all three days of pur stay.The rooms were very musky, outdated and dark. I would never waste my money on this hotel again. Holiday Inn is really going downhill and this hotel is a prime example why.

title: “My new NYC favorite”
text:
The Ace won't be for everyone, but I found it OUTSTANDING. I am neither young nor hip, but I loved the scene, the vibe, the funkiness, a VERY comfortable bed and a spacious bathroom with a luxuriously large shower.
I travel lots for work and sometimes wake up unable to remember quite where I am. This does not happen with The Ace--I mean, how many rooms feature a guitar and an old refrigerator? The Breslin restaurant is really delicious--breakfast was awesome--and I think Stumptown coffee it, quite simply, the best. 
When I checked in, I jokingly asked if they had a special floor for "old people" and the young attractive people at the front desk laughed (with me, not at me) and put me on the top floor with a killer view of the Empire State Building. Two TV stations weren't working so a friendly maintenance guy came right up and rebooted the TV for me--all fixed. The subway stop is right there and it's an easy walk to Penn Station. Definitely will return.

title: “Enjoyed my stay except for the lack of internet”
text:
I had a lovely time at the Morgans Hotel -- the rooms are nicely furnished and well-appointed. The free breakfast at Asia de Cuba in the morning was a huge plus; it was really nice to be able to take a coffee and croissant (which were very good!) to go. 
My only complaint is the wireless situation -- it's $10 a day and would BARELY work for us. The wireless signal was weak at best, and most of the time didn't work at all. Having internet access is fairly important to us when we're away from home, so I'm still undecided if I would stay here again. 
I've stayed at some of the other boutique hotels in the area -- 70 Park, the Roger Williams, and they're all pretty comparable. I would stay at Morgans over the other two if the wireless situation was better.

title: “I had no idea...”
text: Perfect location. Comfortable beds, awesome linens, quiet rooms. This is why I love Priceline. I never would have found (or selected) this hotel without Priceline. Wow! What a gem! Secret is to park at the Embarcadero Shopping Center across the way if you don't plan to come and go often and you don't plan to leave after 1 a.m. Personally, I like to park the car and leave it. You are within a 10-minute walk of the Ferry Building. Very few panhandlers and zombies. Clean. Peaceful. Awesome views from our room. Loved it!!!

title: “Very noisy and rooms are tiny”
text:
This is our fifth trip to NYC and we booked this hotel to be near to Soho and West Broadway. Unfortunately when we arrived we were offered room 402 which was probably about 9 foot square. We were moved to 403 which was larger. The rooms were clean and the beds were large, but the rooms were very noisy, it almost sounded as if our bed was in amongst the traffic on Lafayette Street!
The hotel is situated on a corner in Chinatown where you can't walk out of the hotel without being asked if you want to buy a fake handbag. I would say it is about 3 or 4 blocks south of where you would want to be (if wanting to come for Soho), particularly for single women.
I agree that the staff are very friendly, but that unfortunately didn't make up for the size of room or the noise from the road.
To sum it up for those UK travellers I would say that the hotel is a glorified Travelodge, cheep and cheerful in construction but with larger beds.

title: “Great Location Friendly Staff”
text: We stayed at the Barclay over Thanksgiving weekend. The hotel is located in midtown and close to everything, very convenient. We upgraded to a Suite which made our family stay more comfortable and is large for NYC standards. We were celebrating my daughter's 16th Birthday and one particular staff member Marie-Emilie Dagot went out of her way to make the stay special for her having a special gift for her upon arrival. Thanks Marie-Emilie! She was very thoughtful and it was a extra special touch. The hotel was quite and clean and all and all a nice hotel for the price. I would defiantly stay there again for a future trip.

title: “Incredible bargain in a fabulous location.”
text:
A friend and I stayed at the Belnord the first weekend in April. The room was $89/nt plus tax on Hotels.com- room 514. The place has been undergoing renovations and we got a renovated room with twin beds. Everything was brand new and spotless and I cannot say enough good things about the experience. The decor was fashionable. The beds were comfy, the linens were fresh and clean. The towels were thick and fluffy. The bathroom was brand new with beautiful tile, a pedestal sink and a good sized shower. The toiletries were basic- no name soap and no name shampoo. A flat screen television is mounted to the wall. WiFi is free with a code from the front desk.
The building is located on a quiet side street in a very safe area with tons of shops and restaurants within walking distance. We could have easily spent the weekend hanging out in the neighborhood. It's a short walk to Central Park on one side, and Riverside Park on the other. The subway ( 1 2 3) is a block away. It was an easy walk to the Museum of Natural History.
The rooms are small - there was not much room for anything besides the beds, a nightstand and a little alcove with a closet. There was no chair, and not really room for one. There is no tub in the bathroom, only a shower. But we did not find the room cramped. I have stayed in more expensive NY hotels that were about the same size but not nearly as nice.
We were originally in Rm 501, right across from the elevator with a very loud bell. I asked to be moved because of the noise, the pleasant staff immediately changed the room. Room 501 did not have a closet, only a small dresser. It did have a writing desk, but seemed smaller than the room we ended up in (514). Although I read of complaints of noise from the renovations we did not have that problem, no jack hammers, no noisy neighbors. 
We were completely stunned by how nice the room was, the cheap price, and the amazing location. I've stayed in a lot of hotels in NY, but from now on I will stay at the Belnord.

title: “We loved the Handlery - Staffordshire, England”
text: We stayed at the Handlery August 14th to 19th and thought it was great. We had booked a club room and asked for a high floor if we faced the street (to keep the noise down). We arrived at 12.30am and the receptionist was very helpful and had our bags sent up to our room. The room was large, clean quiet and on the 6th floor. All of the staff were very pleasant and always said hi when they met you. The female concierge was very helpful and gave some great restaurant recommendations - particularly the Mexican across the road. I cannot praise the hotel enough. I thought it was great value and the location is ideal. The negative reviews on this site do not reflect the hotel that we stayed in and should we travel to San Francisco again I would not hesitate to stay at this hotel. The bar next door in the Grill Room was good (the best Cosmopolitan in San Francisco!)

title: “A great place to stay”
text:
This hotel was selected for me to stay at during a business trip. This hotel is rather large with a huge lobby/retail area and guest rooms situated in different towers. My room/bathroom were great--clean and well kept. The bed and pillows were comfortable and the shower had excellent water pressure. The biggest drawback was the walls--I don't know if they were "thin" or if my "neighbors" were just loud (they were morning people raring to go at 5 A.M.).
I also ate breakfast at the hotel, twice, which is unusual for me. I chose the "ultimate" breakfast buffet which included the buffet, coffee, what tasted like fresh squeezed o.j., and an omelette with 3 fillings. The buffet items (sausage, bacon, egg whites, etc) were fresh and constantly stocked. The omelette I had was perfect--fluffy eggs and fresh vegetables. I also need to note that my server was very pleasant and attentive.
While I am referring to staff, everyone from receptionists to concierge to housekeepers seemed sincerely happy to help. 
The biggest drawback to this hotel is the area in which it is located--Downtown LA. It is conveniently near the Staples Center and LA Convention Center, but other than businesses, restaurants, and hotels, this area has nothing to do. However, the Metro subway is very close to the hotel and is easy to use--and I felt safe the one evening I travelled on it.

title: “Sheraton LAX in June”
text:
We enjoyed our stay at this hotel. We stayed for two weeks and paid $109/night through Hotwire.com. At the time of booking, other comparable hotels were charging closer to $150/night.
The amenities provided at the hotel meet the criteria of a 4-star hotel. There is an airport shuttle that runs 24 hours a day (there are multiple shuttles and the wait time is about 5-10 minutes). There are two restaurants in the hotel: The Brasserie serves breakfast and lunch (on the expensive side-simple breakfast will run about $12-$14, $16 for the breakfast buffet), and Shula's (steaks will run about $40). In addition, there is a Starbucks which opens at 5:30am. There is a Subway within 1 block which serves from 6:00am to 9PM. If you are renting a car, there are a number of restaurants within 2 miles. For a simple, inexpensive dining place (where the locals go), try Dinah's on Sepulveda Blvd.
Tips:
Free coffee is stationed at the bar in the lounge. Free TAZO tea bags can be taken at the Business Office Center on the 2nd floor. Lemonade is served at 3:30pm in the lobby.
If you have a car, parking is provided by an independent company towards the back of the hotel. Cost is about $13/day. Otherwise, the hotel offers valet parking.
There is air traffic noise but this can be remedied by purchasing inexpensive ear plugs before you start your trip.
The primary clientele of this hotel is conferences and airline pilots/stewardesses, and probably those of us who used Hotline.com to book. There are relatively few children in the hotel.
We contacted guest services twice during our stay, once for additional towels and once for A/C noise. Both issues were handled immediately.
All the staff we came in contact with were very courteous, friendly, and efficient. We would definitely stay here again.
Cons:
No free parking
No free continental breakfast
No free internet
Limited storage space for clothing
Room noise was only occassionally a problem
Air traffic noise can last through the night since this is an International Airport.
If you are not turned off by any of these issues, then you'll enjoy your stay here, as we did.

title: “What a great hotel!”
text:
We have just stayed at this hotel for our 4th visit in 2 years. We have stayed in a variety of rooms; King room, King room Deluxe and Hudson room. Obviously you get more space the more you pay, but even the ordinary king room is very comfortable, clean and well decorated. If you join the Kimpton In-Touch program, which is free, you get free of charge Wi-Fi. This means you can use Skype for international phone calls at minimal cost and can stay in touch with your emails. It is a chique boutique hotel that does not do New York City brusqueness. The staff are extremely friendly and well trained. Everyone seems to take a pride in the hotel. They have a guy who touches up any chips on the paint work. We have stayed there with friends and recommended it to friends who were equally impressed. There is complimentary coffee in the morning, in the foyer, which we take back to the room while we wake up properly. There is complimentary wine is the late afternoon form I think 4:30 - 6 pm. This is Australian Oxford Landing Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. It is worth taking the continental breakfast package (coffee/tea, scone or muffin, fruit salad, orange/ grapefruit juice). For evening dining, their Print Restaurant is not the cheapest, but the food and service are quality. 
The reception staff are always happy to help with theatre and restaurant reservations. 
Cocktail on the roof terrace give you stunning views over New York. 
I will stay there again.
If you need flights, it is worth looking at some of the consolidators, e.g. Expedia, Netflights, Continental Airlines etc. who do feature this hotel as an inclusive option along with flights.

title: “A happy stay”
text: I was so glad that I chose the Renaissance Boston Waterfront, after indecision concerning another hotel. I found a very good senior rate on the Marriott.com they do drop their prices once in awhile, it was probably a Labor Day special or something. My view was beautiful, the staff were very gracious and accomodating, and the hotel is very airy and fresh. I did not know that the silver line is so close to the hotel, and this was extremely nice since it comes right out of the bus or train station and your there in no time. I also liked the fact that the convention center area is more quiet and open. I am a fuss budget when it comes to clean rooms, so my complaints would not be fair, I cleaned my own window so I could see that sunset without a smudge. Will stay there again, Thank you Marriot for a happy stay.

title: “No 4 star hotel!”
text: I stayed in this hotel in 2007 and didn't like it then. The rooms were small, the bathrooms, tiny and the walls were thin. I decided to try it again in hopes that Kimton had made improvements. Though the rooms are stylish, the bones of this hotel remain the same. The worst is the tiny bathroom with no counter for makeup. The bathtub above our room overflowed and came through the bathroom overhead vent. The hotel simply changed our rrom to a handicap room with a lowe, tiny sink. Never again! This should not be a 4 star hotel!

title: “Needs an redo”
text: We booked their large two bedroom suite which also had a living room and dining room. While the view was lovely, this room needs to be spruced up...it is old and shabby. There was turn down in only one of the bedrooms..and the coffee maker in the little kitchen had no milk provided for a morning pick me up! there is a skimpie supply of towels in the bathroom as well! While the lobby staff is tremendously attentive, the spa also needs to be modernized..it reflects the 80's and is poorly stocked..there is no steam room and no attendant visible.

title: “A wonderful, elegant experience!”
text: The staff was friendly, the service was excellent! The hotel has so much charm and history. I would and want to stay there again!

title: “Close to Seaport”
text: Overall it was not bad. The room was clean, however smelled bad. Good price for us, but was more expensive for the people behind us. Close to airport and walking distance from all the sites. Free breakfast, great hot waffles. Free wireless internet. Good place to stay for a few nights.

title: “Amazing hotel, right on Times Square”
text: When we arrived we were expecting the rooms may be quite small, but ours was very generous in size! Great amount of space, nice clean room and AMAZING location. Would highly recommend.

title: “Elegant accommodations”
text: Very clean, modern, and elegant. Great location with good food close to the hotel.

title: “Very charming with lovely staff.”
text: This is a great little find in a super location. The room was clean, the bed and bed linen good quality and the bathroom nicely appointed. The staff was very friendly and helpful.

title: “Great service at reception, room very comfortable and excellent value”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights and as soon as we arrived the staff were very helpful
Their local knowledge helped us decide where to go shopping and the hotel free courtesy bus to anywhere local is a great idea

title: “Do not be fooled by the rating!”
text: This hotel is the worst hotel i have used. The place is old, smelly and roach infested. We got a deal from priceline; this hotel had a 3 star rating--- that is deceiving. This hotel should be rated 1 or below. We had a huge stow away roach in our luggage.

title: “Great stay in SF”
text: I planned a suprise trip to San Fran and then Pheonix for my boyfriend. I chose Chancellor for price, location, reviews and the fact that the manager responds to negative reviews himself on this site. I figured that would reflect on the hotel staff. We loved the Chancellor! The room size was slightly small, but its SF and was fine for us. The bed was VERY comfy. The location was great because although we had a rental car, in the city it is just convienient to walk everywhere. We did valet for only a few dollars more a day, HIGHLY RECOMENDED. We didnt have to worry about getting our car in that crazy city! We would just call about 20 min early (when we were at breakfast) and our car would be waiting right out front. We went north to the Muir Woods, absolutely beutiful, highly recomended. And also traveled south to pebble beach for a round of golf. Bathroom amneties were nice, and we stole the rubber ducky from our room for a little souvenier. The only reason Im giving it four stars was because of the service our last day before leaving for the airport. Our car was brought to the front.. but the bell boy who had been very helpful when we arrived just watched as I dragged all our luggage (inluding a large golf bag carrier) to the rental car. I was expecting some help as a female! Unfortunate, but overall the hotel was a great place and I would stay again.

title: “Wowzers! What an incredible place to stay on the weekends!”
text:
3 friends and I stayed here over Halloween weekend in 2008 and had an absolute blast. (NYC is a hoot over Halloween, btw!) Staying in the financial district on the weekends is very cheap, and this hotel is just a block or two from countless subway stops. You're also walking distance to Battery Park if you're playing tourist and plan on visiting the Statue of Liberty. 
The rooms are absolutely gorgeous and staying on the 29th floor had incredible views of the river and the World Trade Center site (the hotel goes well above 50 or 60 floors). The pullout sofa and bed were incredibly comfortable, the housekeeping staff was very attentive, and the flat screen tvs in each room were a great perk. For less than $300 each night, you can't beat this in NYC!

title: “Good stay at san antonio”
text:
Was here during my week's training. Chose this location as its close to the training centre. 
It is a budget accommodation. Have no complaints. The break fast was average. 
It is a good place just for sleeping in. 
Worth for the less money you are paying.

title: “Would TOTALLY stay at this hotel again!!!!!”
text:
Things feel apart the day before my trip and i booked my room through Expedia unpublished deals and got this hotel. At first I was disappointed because of the reviews. I was TOTALLY shocked when I arrived at the hotel. I thought to myself WTF??? The hotel was clean, well lit and the employees were very helpful. The pictures does not do the hotel any justice. BEWARE of the reviews!!!!! 
The first person I met was KIERRA and she was AMAZING!!! All the employees were all AMAZING, especially KIERRA, EVELYN, MONIQUE, TARON, YVONNE, REGINA, JACKIE, DAVID. 
I stayed at the Chicago South Loop Hotel for a week (7/11-7/17) and had a great experience. The hotel had free parking and free wi-fi. Parking is not cheap in this city. I would totally stay at this hotel again.

title: “Great hotel, great staff!!”
text: Checked in to spend one night, room was small which we expected but clean and crisp. The amenities were up to date and clean. I would stay there again, the staff were very helpful. Close to everything restaurants, Times Square and theatre.

title: “Jewel that needs a little polish”
text: This is one of great hotels of American maybe the world. However, she seems a bit tired these days. We had a suite in which we checked in around 1 pm. The front desk said they would call us. Appreciate the idea. As of 5:30 we still did not receive a call. Back to the front desk, room was still not ready. Staff said room would be ready in 20 to 30 mins. Gave us free tickets to the bar. One adult and two kids.....one of us was happy with that. 45 Minutes later ....back at the front desk room no ready....One adult really not happy as we had dinner reservations at 8 pm in Little Italy. That got us breakfast buffet...eh....appreciated the effort. The suite living room was a very nice size...put a very comfortable cot in that room (for one adult) Bathrooms are not what I expected for such a upscale hotel. Pluses are comfty beds, large closet, nice size rooms for NYC, Starbucks down stairs, but best of all is location, location, location. A couple of blocks from subway, Grand Central, Grey Line bus tour, 30 Rock, Times Square and Broadway. Love that

title: “Sadly not as good as it used to be!”
text:
Having previously stayed here in 2005, when the hotel was a great deal newer, my second visit left me feeling a bit sad.
My two biggest moans are that the rooms (we stayed in a corner king both times) have not been touched in those six years. Cracked tiles in the bathroom, even a cracked window pain, and the tv and iPod dock now just seem old. On one of the 4 nights our bathroom wasn't cleaned.
Perhaps more sad is that the bar and restaurant are now almost completely estranged from the hotel. At the prices charged, it feels more like you are staying in a serviced apartment rather than a hotel, which the old Hotel didn't feel like. The new Co-op restaurant is a blatant attempt to entice the local population in, to the detriment of the hotel guests. I think this is a big mistake by the hotel, especially when the rooms are now so tired.
You cannot fault the location, the views and the surrounding bars and restaurants - but Hotel on Rivington have really dropped the ball here, and with hungrier and hipper places springing up nearby, you have to worry for the hotel in it's current guise.
Still good, but need some big investment and to recapture some of the original attention to detail. Overall a bit sad.

title: “Great hotel, bend-over backwards staff”
text:
Stayed here for a conference a few weeks ago for one night. This is a very nice property, quietly tucked off Michigan Avenue. 
Pros:
It was nice to escape from the chaos of the city to a very calm, relaxing place. I liked that the Conrad didn't seem like a gigantic conference hotel like some of its neighbors with conventioneers all over. Not much of a scene like the Peninsula, but the bar area was busy enough.
The room: nice, though if you looked closely you could see a few shortcuts taken in putting it together. The tub was super and the water pressure amazing. A deep soaking tub that actually filled rapidly! Good Molton Brown toiletries. But the best was the staff. Everyone was super professional, extra friendly and went out of their way to help. 
Cons:
As I said there were a few shortcuts in the room (no convenient outlets to the bed; when you soaked in the tub you looked at the raw underside of the sink area, etc. No view, but that wasn't so important. 
I'm definitely recommending the Conrad to friends who want to be near Michigan Ave but away from the crowds around Oak St.

title: “It's okay”
text: Stayed one night. Called to request a room in a quiet part of the hotel but was told that because it was booked through Priceline, we pretty much don't have a right to make any requests. Sure enough our room was on the second floor by the ice machine. Spotty wifi. Restaurant was overpriced. Nice enough property but wouldn't pay published rates for a room here. (Stayed at the Osaka Hilton the next night...they do it differently there, don't they? Excellent 2 nights there!)

title: “Unsafe, filthy - worst place I've ever stayed”
text: My manager booked this motel because it was close to our client site. The rooms were filthy and the area is unsafe. There were too choices for the heat ... full blast and off. Since it was cold outside, I opted for full blast, which resulted in a room temperature of about 92 degrees. There are dozens of cats roaming the exterior of the property, along with food dishes, etc. -- presumably to address a rodent problem (I did not see any rodents). The front desk is safely behind bulletproof glass and, depending on the time of night, a retractable steel curtain. That will give you an idea of how safe you are in your room with large plate glass window and flimsy door lock. I slept maybe 2-3 hours per night -- maybe -- with lights on the whole time. We did not return, needless to say. If it had not been for the fact that I was a brand new employee, I would have refused to stay there. I regret I allowed someone to put me in danger for three nights.

title: “Loved it!”
text: I stayed in this hotel while attending a conference and I found it to be excellent. The room was large with a sitting area. The bed truly was "heavenly", and the bathroom was above average. The best part, however was the view. Through the large window I could see the space needle and the sound and it was breathtaking at sunset. I did not find the lobby to be particularly smokey as other reviewers have mentioned. Overall I thoroughly enjoyed my experience.

title: “Comfortable stay.”
text: Stayed for 3 day weekend. Very convenient to attend concert at Key Arena, quick 10 minute walk. Shuttle to Seahawks game was very convenient and economical. Hotel is older but updated, comfortable, clean. service was friendly and competent. Woul;d be happy to stay here again.

title: “Nice people, older property”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights to attend a graduation at Lackland AFB. The desk clerks were great, and Mary Ann really went out of her way to accommodate us. Also, we were given good advice to eat at Bill Miller BBQ just next door. The property is dated, but very clean and pleasant. The price was right when I booked through a third party online. Not a place I would take my wife, but it was fine for 2 old guys. There seemed to be a lot of activity (noise) the first night. As far as a bad neighborhood, we didn't see any evidence of that. We walked to the restaurant next door and had no issues. We didn't notice a smell either, except that terrific BBQ smell from next door!

title: “Beautiful Lobby, lots of history, better options for the price”
text:
We were in town for a friends wedding. We frequently travel to Austin, usually staying at the Hilton, Hilton Garden Inn, Courtyard, or Residence Inn. Since the wedding was being held at the Driskill we decided it would be neat to stay here. While the hotel is beautiful, the service and offerings do not live up to the high prices for the hotel. You can not live on the history of your hotel alone. To be honest, the best part of the hotel is the lobby. Nothing was particularly bad, but nothing was particularly outstanding either. For the price of the Driskill compared to the other hotels nearby, I expect outstanding. 
The location was easy to find and the hotel smack in the middle of the 6th street entertainment and a very easy walk (5 minutes) to the convention center and warehouse district as well. You only have the choice of valet and pay a premium for that. The lobby of this historic hotel is beautiful with with front desk and nicely appointed common area. 
There is no free Wi-Fi available in the lobby or rooms. It seems like most hotels in the 4-5 star category are at least offering complimentary access in the lobby. There is a bakery and café in the lobby. We tried to eat here twice, but the wait was in excess of an hour and there are many other good options in the area. They really should give priority to hotel guests! We never took the time to check out their gym, and I am unsure if they have a pool. Check in was quick and efficient, thought they made no attempt to accommodated our request for a quiet room, but quiet may not really be possible where they are located. When we asked for foam pillows and extra towels they brought them promptly. Though we were there for the wedding and the nightlife of Austin, once you went inside the hotel at night you do experience a respite from crazy 6th. 
The rooms are nicely decorated, but as expected in a historic hotel they are somewhat small. The bathrooms are relatively big for a historic hotel, with a sink both inside and outside the bath area. We had no noise from adjoining rooms but experienced a lot of outside city noise. Bathrooms are well equipped with plenty of storage space. There is a tub with shower We could hear doors slamming in the morning from time to time. Many small items in the room were tattered or dirty and could use a refresh. 
The area has every type of dining and entertainment option you could ask for all within easy walking distance. We did not partake of any of the hotels dining venues other than trying to eat breakfast there.....other than the banquet food at the wedding. (though the food was good, some of it was cold) 
We would not likely stay here again if we were in the area for a personal trip. Room rate seemed too appropriate for what you get. The Intercontinental (which we3 also have stayed at) is just as nice and less expensive.
They were agreeable to late check-out when we asked which was nice. 
I love historic hotels, but unfortunately in this case, the price - payoff is not there. But, more power to them if they can continue to get those rates without providing anything stellar. That seems to work for them.

title: “Wonderful Weekend in Downtown San Antonio”
text:
My husband and I enjoyed our stay at the Holiday Inn Market Square for 4 nights from Thursday, October 20th through Monday, October 24th. We celebrated our first wedding anniversary with a short road trip from Houston and our stay was great! We had originally only booked for three nights, but stayed a fourth. Thanks for honoring the discount a fourth night!!
Service was excellent. We checked in about 6-6:30ish on Thursday evening. The young man at the desk (I can’t remember his name) was on the phone very patiently explaining to a seemingly confused lady directions to the hotel, answering some of our own questions at the same time. When he finished the phone call he apologized for the delay, and promptly helped us check-in. 
We were put in a first floor room with a king bed and sliding glass doors that led to the parking lot. My husband was really excited about the fact that we could park right in front of our room, load/unload with ease, and keep an eye on the car. I had read in several reviews that if your room does not have a mini-fridge or microwave you could request one and, if available, it would be brought to you. This is very true, about five minutes after requesting a mini-fridge, one was in our room ready to use (the microwave as well, even though we didn’t request it). The room was clean and the bed was comfortable. It is true that the TV was not of the flat screen variety, but considering we weren’t paying good money to stare at the boob tube all weekend (we could have done that at home), that was not a priority for us. The bathroom was clean, and I really liked the updated tile and countertop. It felt less hotely and more homey. 
After unloading the car, we headed to the bar for a beverage to wet our parched throats and met Mari. She is awesome. This young lady is super friendly. She made several suggestions on things to do and places to go downtown. The $2.50 Pacifico/ Heineken special wasn’t bad either. We also stopped back by when she was bartending Sunday evening after a long day walking the river walk and checking out the Tower of the Americas. While we were enjoying our adult beverages, she brought out a complimentary piece of cheesecake with strawberries, blueberries, raspberry sauce and whipped cream. That was a great touch, I couldn’t believe she remembered what we had told her on Thursday. We were very impressed. 
I had to knock a star off the rating though, for just a couple of issues, and all of them stem around the restaurant/bar . The first is that on Sunday there was a not so great smell in the bar area. It almost smelled like there was a drainage issue behind the bar. The smell was not there Thursday, but Sunday night it was pretty bad. It was still there Monday morning as well. The second is that, according to the hotel’s information channel, the bar was supposed to be open until 12am Saturday night (Sunday morning). My husband and I decided to return to the hotel after dinner Saturday night and have a couple of drinks at the bar there before retiring for the evening. We got to the hotel just after 11pm and the bar was already closed. That disappointed my husband quite a bit. Had we known the hotel bar was going to close early, we would have just found one downtown to stop at before catching the bus back. The last blemish to an otherwise wonderful stay was the food at the restaurant. We decided to have breakfast there Monday morning before heading home. While it was fairly inexpensive, it was not good at all. We both got the eggery burrito. It was bland, and the tortilla had an odd flavor and texture. Based on my experience with the food, I could not recommend eating there.
The best things about this stay, and the reason I give it four stars, are the service, the free parking, and the comfy room. Oh, and did I mention the service.
A few FYIs- Durango St. has been renamed Cesar Chavez, so while your GPS will give you the correct directions, the street names will be different. (That was a little confusing exiting the freeway. I would have missed the exit had there not been an exit number as I was looking for Durango and not Cesar Chavez.)
The river walk is six blocks east and two blocks north of the hotel. While it is within walking distance, there is a trolley route right across the street and parking is expensive downtown. If you plan on staying a few days and enjoying the sights I recommend getting a VIA day pass for the trolley lines. There are three different routes that stop at all the major attractions downtown. Individual rides are $1.10 per person, and the day pass is $4.00. We were really glad we did this, it was a huge help as we didn’t have carry around a bunch of singles and dimes all weekend.
Also, there is construction going on across Cesar Chavez (Durango St). It got a little annoying a couple of mornings. That is no fault of Holiday Inn’s, and I did not base any portion of my rating on it.

title: “perfect.”
text: The Beacon passed expectations which made our stay the best of five NYC visits. Suite was perfect, and we enjoyed preparing light meals and relaxing before heading out again to enjoy not only the neighbourhood, which included fairway for food, but easy access to the subway and the delights of NY. The bed was the most comfortable we were to find in two months of travelling and the standard of the linen was the best. Staff were friendly and helpful and we will go back there again, and again!

title: “It was a wonderful stay.”
text: The staff was very nice and courteous. Everything needed was in the room and convenient. Location was great for me only had to drive about a mile away from my conference.

title: “Perfect location and great accommodations”
text: My wife and I spent 4 days in Washington and chose the Hilton Garden Inn Downtown due to its proximity to the Metro which is right across the street and the location which is within easy walking distance of both the Mall and its museums. The price is reasonable considering its great downtown location and we also got the breakfast buffet which I would highly recommend. The staff is very helpful and very professional, the room was very clean with adequate room for us both. Everyone who works there is courteous and helpful. We had a great stay and I would highly recommend this Hilton for a Washington D.C vacation trip.

title: “Not what we thought”
text:
We stayed here for a week in October 2008. My husband booked it and I must admit to not having read TripAdvisor reviews beforehand, so maybe our disappointment was our own fault.....
The hotel website shows lovely rooms, so I was quite surprised when we drove in to what appeared to be a fairly ramshackle site. Our room was in one of the older buildings, admittedly facing the marina, but opening on to a public walkway (which we had assumed would be divided into private balconies). The whole room shook every time anyone walked by and noise was a constant problem, especially at the weekend. You make a choice between privacy and natural light - if you want the latter you must have the wooden shutters open but the world and his wife can look in as they walk past. Also the walls are very thin and we could hear conversations in the next room.
The bed was comfortable enough but facing it was a huge cupboard, half TV cabinet and half wardrobe; with the doors open for either function, it was impossible to walk past the bed.
Off the bedroom was a space containing a double sink unit but there was no door for privacy - do I want to watch my other half brushing his teeth, or vice versa? Then off this space was the bathroom with toilet and bath, thankfully with a door.
The air conditioning was incredibly noisy. It would start up like a rocket motor, clatter away and then stop altogether till the next time - like Chinese water torture if you let it bother you.
We asked to move to the new block with private balconies, but they could only offer us one overlooking 'parkland' i.e. a strip of green separating the hotel from the road and for 4 nights only, so we stayed where we were.
Our breakfasts were included to the tune of $15 each at the Blue Pearl, and not once could we reach this total. Hearty is the word that comes to mind! On our first night we ate at the more upmarket on-site Firefly restaurant and had a disastrous encounter with a waitress which left us feeling like we'd been part of street theatre or a 'happening' by the end of the meal. This put us off till our last night when we ventured back and to our relief were served by a very nice young man - and the meal was good as well.
We were glad we kept our rental car for the duration of our stay, as it would have been hard to get around by public transport. However, we didn't like being presented with the parking charge when we checked out - not mentioned on any previous occasion.
There was free computer access in the lobby, which was a bonus, and people were very good about keeping to the requested 10 minute limit if there was a queue.
If we return to San Diego, I would not stay here again. The marina location is very pleasant, but there are no shops or cafes close by, and we were not interested in Sea World, which seems to be the main attraction for families. I would prefer to be somewhere with better facilities and nicer rooms.

title: “Better places to stay in DC.”
text:
My husband and I and 3 other couples go to Washngton every year for a political function. We normally stay at hotels we know(the Willard is our favorite), however, after the functions activities it is hard to find cabs/transportation back to our rooms so we decided to stay at the hotel that was hosting some events. I had read about Kimpton hotels and even checked some rooms out at the one in San Francisco, so I assumed it would be alright. They seemed to be in the category of the Embassy Suites, which we had also stayed one year. However, not even close. But they are priced the same or higher.
The outside is beautiful and the lobby fine. Very historical. We checked in in the 2nd floor and
they told us rooms were on the first floor. We jokingly said basement and they said yes actually. Should have stopped there and left, but they insisted they were sold out for the 
function and the luncheon we were attending was there and we only had about 30 min. to
register and get a table, so we stayed.
When we got off the elevator in the basement, we ran into a man wheeling an eight tier cart of
 raw meats and salads into the employee elevator to take up to kitchen. Some not covered. As
 we walked down hall, parts literally looked like old stone basement walls, peeling paint, some 
kind of equipment thrown at bottom of beautiful spiral staircase, like they just quit working and left. The decor reminded me of circus tents and jesters. Very odd. Room decor same. When 
you looked out the two windows you looked up into the window wells and saw people walking 
on the sidewalk above. Could hear traffic all day and night.
No closet in room, armoire had about 12 inches of hanging space with drawers beside it. No in room coffee maker.
