Very small bath with one small sink and a tub with walls so low you had to barely step in. Great water pressure.(guess 'cause we were in basement). Bed and bedding were great too. Slept well. After lunch we took nap and then showered and when we came back to room that night, bed was still messed up, which didn't realty matter, however, we had a stack of about 6 clean towels, bundled with string, literally thrown across our bed. The towels we had used earlier were still in the tub where I left them. Not your normal turn down service.
The weather was nice and we sat out in a middle courtyard for drinks after lunch, which was 
very nice, but we could not get waited on because they quit service at 2:30 until dinner. Other people were there also and they probably would have sold some drinks and snacks if they would have had a server. However, that night at about 10:00, we went back for drinks and waited forever to get waited on, and then forever for our drinks, and there were 3+ people working at the bar. We did not find service to be a priority anywhere at this hotel. 
One of friends missed lunch and ordered a shrimp cocktail and Cobb salad in the afternoon at the restaurant, and could squeeze the water out of the shrimp in the cocktail. And the shrimp was not cooked on the salad. They sent both back and said the server wasnt overly concerned. Breakfast was good though, but took a while and cost $20+ each.
We were only there one night, but this experience will probably steer us away from ever booking rooms at this hotel chain again.

title: “Classy and full of style and elegance”
text: The Inn is a great place to stay for business and romance. It will now be the place for me to stay whenever I'm Detroit. I have told all my family and friends in MI and AZ that the Inn is the place to be. I just loved the music library.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Club Quarters Hotel for 4 nights from the 27th November with my partner. We both thought the hotel was great, it was in the perfect position, just a 10 minute walk from Central Park and a 5 minute walk to Times Square. The receptionists were very helpfull, always suggesting somehwere new to go and they also made restaurant reservations for us.
I'd read some of the other reviews about the rooms but I have to say ours was spacious with plently of cupboard space, the bathroom was clean and had everything that we needed (could of done with a dust though!!).
If we were to visit New York again we'd definately stay here, compared to some of the other places i'd stayed in the city this was 100 times better!
If you see reception they will also provide you with discount ickets to some of the major attractions.

title: “Excellent water view value”
text: I haven`t been to San Diego for 10 years, but for my last visit I stayed at this property when it was the flagship hotel for Travelodge. Back then you could get a beautiful room with a spectacular water view for $79. I fell in love with the place and said then that if I ever returned to San Diego, I would stay nowhere else. Of course, since Hilton took over, the prices have gone up considerably, but was still able to get a room for $139 through Expedia. It`s still a bargain 10 years later. The location on Harbor Island (actually a peninsula) is stunning, with the marina on one side and the bay on the other. You`ll feel as if you`re in a private resort area with limited traffic, beautiful landscaping, jogging path, and those beautiful water views. Our spacious room was bright, impeccably maintained, and immaculately clean. Our private balcony offered a panoramic view of the San Diego skyline and the bay. The staff was genial and helpful and the bountiful buffet breakfast was reasonably priced and well prepared and presented. You will not hear any noise from the adjacent airport as there is only one east/west runway and the hotel is a fair distance south of the airport. If you`re in need of a convenient San Diego location, beautiful water views, and a lovely room at a fair price, this is where you need to be!

title: “Nice & clean, just lacking in the "bells and whistles" area”
text:
My wife and I just came back from a week here.
I must admit to have been worried beforehand reading some of the reviews and noting the location (next to the freeway). Upon checking I requested a quiet room and got one in the SW corner (1222).
I was quite impressed with the hotel and room decor. It looked like the hotel had been updated in the last couple of years - it wasn't "day 1" fresh, but it was very clean and comfortable. In fact the mattress was a memory foam type, so quite modern. The room also had a fridge, which came in handy (as they don't have a bar).
The suitability of the hotel location depends on how long you are staying. If you're there for 1 or 2 nights and just want to see 6th Street and a little bit of downtown, it's ideal. For our week-long stay it got a bit tiring (literally). The hotel is at the far east end of 5th avenue - a good 7 blocks away from Congress. It's always on that borderline of just about a mile away from most places (University, Capital building, South Congress). We joked that we must have walked 4-5 miles each day and got to know downtown pretty well!
The primary downside of the hotel is lack of facilities. The pool area is extremely small - 2 tables, a very small pool and a hot-tub. It's also stuck between 2 towering buildings meaning it gets very little sun. As I said about there's also no bar - or at least one that I could find.
The hotel staff area all nice and try really hard - there's chilled water and cookies in reception, they let you use the reception computers when the business center one is in use........small things like that.
We didn't see any of the gripes that other people had. We liked the hotel. If you decide that the price is worth the lack of a real pool then it's a good deal.

title: “Must stay in Seattle”
text: We travel a lot and have stayed in so many hotels, but Alexis Hotel was by far the best! We stayed in President Suite and it was just gorgeous! Extremely spacious with lovely furniture and super comfy bedding! They also prepared us a nice playpen so that our 8months old son could sleep safe. The location was excellent as well. I had made some special arrangement for my spouse birthday and it went really well. It sure was a memorable stay and we WILL come back to this hotel!!

title: “Nice accomodations in Downtown Austin!”
text:
Not sure I would call this place 4 stars but it is a very nice hotel in downtown Austin, near the Bat bridge. Got an unbelievably good price on Priceline and it was worth every penny. The staff are very friendly and professional. There appear to have been some recent renovations and the lobby is looking very nice. One of the crown jewels is the workout facility, one of the nicest hotel facilities I have ever been to. Looks like it was just facelifted and the results are excellent! The pool is small but very nice. 
The rooms are a bit small but decent. This is definitely an older hotel and it shows. The beds are very comfortable and the LCD flatscreen TV is a nice upgrade. The bathroom is small but nice. One thing that really perplexed me was the bathroom door looked like it was taken out of an abandoned hotel from the '70s. It was an old dark wood and had definitely seen better days. Why spend a lot on renovations and leave old junky doors? Shower water pressure/nozzle was adequate at best. The Portico products smell great. 
Austin is a great city and you can walk to a lot of downtown places from this hotel. It was 105 degrees when I stayed so I kept the walking to a minimum. 
Overall, a great experience!

title: “Great Overnight Spot”
text: Great location, extremely helpful staff, beautiful and clean rooms! Totally recommend this one!

title: “Posh & upscale in the heart of Chi!”
text: Went here for a bachelorette party after staying here once before. Love it....love the location! It's right next to the House of Blues, walking distance to Top Shop, BHLDN, and a TON of delicious restaurants and fun bars. The decor is so upscale and posh, kind of twilight-esque. Super friendly staff. You feel like you're really living the life when you stay here!

title: “Great Concierge”
text: The hotel is located just a mile or maybe less from Union Square. However, the area is nice, with restaurants and spa. I was impressed from the concierge, the service was great, always someone available to give informations, directions, with maps and addresses. Also, they have parking. The rooms are clean and comfortable. But do not chose the side on the tram road...it is not quite. I had a cocktail at bar, probably the best Manhattan I ever had. Great stay.

title: “worst hotel I've stayed in”
text: I stayed in their basic room during December 2011. Rude staff at front desk. Rooms were too hot (in winter). Only one lift in the entire hotel, so you have to wait over 5 mins for it. Overpriced. Only gave 1 star based on its amazing location - close to Macys, 5th Avenue and Penn station. Lot's of restaurants nearby, located in Korean Way.

title: “Great Place All Around”
text: The staff is absolutely great, they are extremely friendly. They have shuttles to the airport and to the medical district. The pool is nice but there's no hot tub. You have to walk a little ways to the elevator. The rooms are also very nice as well. It's only downfall is it's location. If you are there for medical reasons it's a five minute drive. Also it's right on a busy street which is sometimes hard to pull out into. We've stayed there twice now. I would go again but it's easier to stay at hotels that are in walking distance of MD Anderson. Oh, also the zoo, bass pro and the galleria aren't all to far away either. Also great movie and game selection, with no rental charges.

title: “Great rate, great hotel”
text: Booked a run-of-house room at this hotel, received a two-room suite. I am led to believe that this is an all-suite hotel. Beautiful pool and amenities, and for the rate I paid it is one of my best bargains of the year. Would return in a heartbeat, am disappointed I didn't stay longer.

title: “lovely rooms and staff”
text: the suite was beautiful ,clean well laid out and very comfortable . there was alot of outside noise due to the location (hospitals and fire station plus the industrial area to the rear )but the unusual shape of the building cleanliness and friendliness of the staff plus the courtisy shuttle bus made up for the noise .i would stay here again and recomend it to friends .

title: “Decent, clean, and gets the job done”
text:
The hotel is clean, but you have to request a fridge; and food prices are pretty steep. $45/day for breakfast buffet for 2 (including 20% tip). Buffet is not extensive, however, the make-to-order omelettes, and included beverages are what kept us coming back. Due to time constraints, the buffet was the best option. One night we paid nearly $25 for a room-service burger, and a can of soda. The burger & fries was $14; 12 oz. soda was $3; plus the 21% gratuity, and $3.50 service charge. I think the hotel could make lots more money on their food service if the prices were more reasonable.
Other than that, the staff was very friendly, professional, and accommodating. The rooms were average (for what I expected of a Sheraton), and in need of modernization. There was a flat screen in the living room, but an older model box tv in the bedroom. As far as location, it was just a block or so from the tip of the Gaslamp Quarter. My husband and I aren't the athletic type, but with comfortable shoes, and much excitement, managed to walk the entire area.
So, I would give this hotel 5 stars for cleanliness, professionalism, and convenience. But their prices definitely forced us outside of the hotel for meals (other than breakfast). If you're looking for luxury, this is NOT the hotel for you. But for a clean, comfortable place to stay (with no frills), you've come to the right place.

title: “Impressive exterior, not so great interior”
text:
Recently stayed here for work. I was disappointed in the hotel in general and felt it was not up to the standard of other Omni properties. Even though I had a suite, I found the property in general needs an update. The location is great however and the mall area under the hotel is very convenient, offering a Starbucks, meals, a convenience store, etc. 
The staff is very friendly and helpful - I will say that. However, My first impression of the hotel was not so great. After a pleasant check in, I headed to my room. Upon exiting the elevator to get to my room, there was a strong mildew odor permeating the floor - my guess is the ice machine failed and over flowed, as that area was being reconstructed while I was there. When I got to my room, the door handle was covered in a white substance. Upon entering the room, I was impressed with the size and the corner layout, but my eyes were drawn to a tear on the side of a chair. Later, when I attempted to watch TV, the battery in the remote died. I'm not making this up. 
The bed was comfortable enough, and the view of the plaza was great. Parking was a hassle and cost $12 per day but that's to be expected in any downtown hotel. 
My 3 biggies when I travel are - internet speed, cleanliness, and exercise facilities. Internet speed fluctuated, at times speedy, other times incredibly slow. The hotel was very clean overall aside from the substance on my door - public areas were clean. The exercise facilities were very poor, possibly because there is a pay gym on the premisis - available for $15 a day. From my perspective, passes to this gym should be included in the room rate, or a decent exercise room should be available. 
In general, there's a feeling that the hotel is dated - from a hard couch in the suite to an older TV in the room where many hotels have started upgrading to plasma or lcd tv's. I expected to be wow'ed I guess, and I wasn't at all.

title: “Wedding/Reception Location”
text: The Hilton at University Place was the perfect place for my wedding. The ceremony and reception location were absolutely gorgeous! The location of the hotel was very convenient for family traveling from all directions. Wedding specialist Jenna Yates did and excellent job making sure that our wedding day was everything we could have dreamed of and more! Hotel accomodations were top of the line. I would definitely recommend this location for any special event or even for accomodations only.

title: “Horrid....”
text: I took my wife there in the summer of 2003 for a conference. I was so embarrassed! Bad smells, wornout, used furniture from Days Inn, one of our towels was actually from a local gym with the logo on it. We got the run around about the room as well. We booked a queen and got a double. Opened the window to get fresh air and got the room filled with smoke from the bar and grill downstairs. Homeless all over, some looking at porn on the open sidewalk. Got back one night in time to catch someone peeing on the wall by the entrance. The room above us must have been rented by the hour if you know what I mean. We got suckered by the internet on this one. There is more, but why go on? I agree with the other review about the nice young lady that did her best and was very nice to us. Sad thing is, I think she was embarrassed also.

title: “loved Shelter Pointe Hotel”
text: My family - 2 adults & 3 kids spent a week here. We had a Jr. Suite overlooking the beautiful marina for a very reasonable price. The room was large enough for all of us - 2 double beds & 1 cot. There was an eating area with a fridge, sink, counter & microwave & a large round table. The resort & our room was clean. We had a semi private pool & jacuzzi. The health club was great & the restaurant had a terrific selection of food for all of us. We would stay there again in a heartbeat.

title: “Probably a fine place but my stay had it's share of problems”
text: I really want to rate this hotel well as I think it has potential of being above average, however I am being generous at rating it average solely based on the experiences I had during my stay. After a long day getting there, I arrived late in the evening only to be told there was not a room available for me. The lady behind the counter was very apologetic (which I appreciated) and stated a large group of people had not checked out that day as scheduled and consequently they did not have a room available for me. She noted that I was a Choice Priviledge member and said they made arrangements to put me up next door for the night. She said they would comp my room for that night and that the rest of my 6 night stay would indeed be back here where I originally booked. I was exhausted and not knowing the condition of the establishment next door, I agreed. Without writing more of a novel than I already am, let me just say the place next door was unacceptable. It was a complete dump, filthy and disgusting. I was NOT happy. If I had wanted to stay in a dump, I would have booked a room there. They could have at least put me in a comparable quality establishment, of which there were several in the area. The next day I was indeed given a room here for the remainder of my stay. Upon entering my assigned room, it initially appeared fine and of the quality I had expected. However after setting my laptop up on the desk and was preparing to sit down and do some work, I discovered there was no desk chair. I called down to inquire and was tld someone would bring me a chair. A short time later, a young man did indeed show up with a brand new chair he stated he just assembled for me. Ok, that was impressive. Problem solved. The next morning, when I opened the closet to get the iron, I discovered the ironing board was missing. Once again, I called down and was promptly delivered an ironing board. Ok so kudos for problem solving. I also discovered there were no hand towels or wash cloths in the bathroom. Ok so now I'm wondering if this had been a room they were just using to rob Peter to pay Paul with items they needed for other guests. I might also just mention, in case they are reading this review, please invest the additional $0.15 a roll for something other than bargain brand toilet paper. The shower pressure was anemic and the temperature was very hard to control. Other than these complaints, the room was fine, very clean and the beds were moderately comfortable. Oh speaking of clean, upon arrival back to my room on the second night at 5:15pm, I discovered my room had not been cleaned yet. "Really"? After calling housekeeping, I was advised the cleaning staff was still working on my floor and would be there momentarily. Apparantly not an expeditious crew. Fortunately, I was leaving again to go out for dinner, so it worked out. This happenned once again on the last night of my stay and finally at 5pm I stepped out into the hallway and advised the cleaning staff (who coincidentally was just standing in the hallway chatting) that I would not need my room cleaned tonight at this late in the day as I was not going to leave while they did their work. The breakfast selections were plentiful however the eggs were unedible, rubbery and with a slight chemical taste. The ice machines on 2 of the 3 floors were out of order. One vending machine ate my money. The cigarette receptacles outside had not been emptied during my entire stay and wer overflowing. The coffee pot in my room was not used for two of the days during my stay as no cream/sugar packets had been left during the cleaning process. I could easily rate this hotel much lower based on my experiences during my stay, however my gut tells me there is potential here for an above average establishment. The staff was always very friendly and most of my problems were dealt with swiftly. I will chalk off my issues to the exception and hopefully not the rule with this place.

title: “Rooms clean and spacious, staff great, food good, beds a bit hard”
text:
I stayed here a couple of weeks ago for the first time. It's a new property and very nicely appointed. The staff is extremely attentive and friendly, not quite bordering on cloying. I had dinner in the restaurant on two evenings: a burger and a chicken special; both were excellent. Breakfast is worth trying, but go for the B&B special for best value for money. It includes made-to-order eggs, cereals, pastries and fruits. The chef even stopped by to make sure everything was to my satisfaction.
One small beef is that the beds are a little hard for my liking, as I am not exactly well padded around the hips. I had forgotten that Hilton hotel beds are rather firm. Another minor qualm is that the location is pretty far from downtown Fort Worth, and I rather like the idea of walking to my client's office which is just off Sundance Square.

title: “Great location, friendly”
text: Second visit to this Hampton. Love the location easy to get on either blue or red subway lines. The problem was I used my Hilton Honor points so the room was free, so they ignored all of my preferences and gave us a room right in front of the ice machine. I called downstairs and of course they were sold out and couldn't do anything for us. Think they should consider their loyal customers and their requests. The other problem was on the first night our tub had water and black debris in it. We called the guest services the next morning and got an answering machine. We stopped by the front desk and told them we needed the problem fixed with in an hour and thank goodness it was. The only other thing is during the holiday season they should consider extending the breakfast hours. When the hotel is sold out it is very hard to get in the room for breakfast. The staff is very friendly and we will stay here again even with these issues.

title: “Location Is The Best Aspect”
text:
If this hotel wasn't across the street from the Convention Center, I would not have booked it to spend one night going to the Philadelphia Flower Show and have dinner with friends. We stayed here once before a few years ago and it was fine. This time it was a little less than fine.
As others have mentioned, parking is a bit of a project. You park in a commercial parking lot next door to the hotel, and for events like the flower show, it can be packed. My biggest issue with the lot is that it's quite confusing. For example, we noted our section of the lot and what floor our car was on, but when we went to retrieve our car and got off on the correct floor, we were in the red section instead of the blue section, but couldn't figure out how to get to the blue section! We walked around and ended up walking to a different elevator to find it.
The hotel itself is a bit dated in decor and in the condition of some of the furnishings, but it's comfortable enough. The staff is always friendly, the room comes with a mini-fridge, and the location is perfect for Convention Center stuff. We didn't have very much time for this trip, so we basically dropped our bags off in the room and headed out for the night. Upon returning we discovered that a bedside lamp wouldn't turn on for 10 minutes, the duvet cover had black lint on it, and, most importantly, once we crawled into bed the strong, sickening odor of cigarette smoke wafted in. This is a non-smoking hotel. We called the front desk and they said that even though it's non-smoking "people do what they want to do," but said they'd send security to roam the halls and try and discover the source of the smoke. I mentioned that this is quite a problem as my husband has asthma. In the meantime they suggested we close our bathroom door. I have to say, it has been a very long time since cigarette smoke was an issue in a hotel room.
The next morning we found an apology note with some breakfast coupons and a promise of awarding us a small amount of Hilton Hhonors points (1000, I believe). The gesture was appreciated, but we didn't feel great. Upon checkout we mentioned the lamp and the duvet and also the cigarette smoke, and one of the attendants who was nearby took it upon herself to credit our bill by $50 -- we really were happy that she was listening as the young man who was checking us out was just noting our complaints but didn't offer anything. I have to note here that although we were given some points and a bit off our bill, we've had hotels (including Hilton family hotels) offer more in compensation for lesser problems, but we did not ask for more.
Once home we got an email from the manager, asking about our experience. I basically wrote him a version of this review, and he thanked me and said the comments would be discussed with his staff and he was glad we were compensated. 
This hotel is next door to Reading Terminal Market, across from the convention center, and walkable to many Center City restaurants, so its location is its best feature. However, I think next time we'll go with a better hotel that isn't as conveniently located.

title: “Steps from Union Station”
text: Easy checkin, great lobby with bar, restaurant and expansive sitting area for work or play.The food from restaurant was surprisingly good and fresh as well as reasonable! Conveniently located and well priced. Plan to revisit.

title: “Great Stay!”
text: Went with the family (wife and 2 kids) for a trip to Sea World and San Diego Zoo November 4-6. Booked the standard "Garden View" room and were upgraded to a an ocean view Family Suite on the first floor. The staff was wonderful, and my only possible gripe would be that the ocean view from the patio was obstructed by a clear partition that separated the patio from the public areas. Kids had a blast running on the beach and playing in the water, would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Older building, thinner walls”
text:
The room was nice, charming, and large. Unfortunately, there was a family with child a few doors down. The young boy got up early and took advantage of the spacious rooms, running back and forth. From a few doors down we could hear the steps clearly.
The only off street parking is by valet for which you pay. We parked on the street in front of the hotel, free over night. However, we had to feed the meter at 8:00a.
All in all, we enjoyed the hotel and will probably return.

title: “Good - but a couple of things to watch out for....”
text:
My wife and I stayed in a Junior Suite. The size of the room was good, they had ensured that the room was feather free as requested, but the room was inward facing and had no view at all! For a junior suite I would have expected an outward facing room - or at least given the option as they claimed the inward facing rooms were quieter.
Also, we booked a car with the hotel to take us to the airport. Had a number of large bags so had specifically requested a large SUV or estate car. What we got was one of the hotel workers in a normal old taxi which was his second job.Really struggled to get all our bags in the car and ended up with laptop bags on our laps etc for the long drive out to Dulles. Did not have time to argue the point and wait for another vehicle as we had a flight to catch, but this was not acceptable and not what had been requested! 
other than that, room service was good and prompt, staff were polite and helpful, umbrellas were available - and when they ran out they went and purchased more for guests. 
I would stay here again.....but there are a couple of things to watch out for, and these issues are reflected in marks off for the service and room ratings.

title: “Wonderful trip!”
text:
I have stayed many times at this Days Inn and have always had a wonderful experience.
The location is very convenient to public transportation, restaurants and shopping.(There is a Trader Joe's just across the street.)
The front desk staff is courteous, knowledgeable of the surrounding area and always ready to be of assistance. I had a quite interior facing room , which was great for a good night sleep. Breakfast is good bonus. Will stay again here in my next visit to Chicago.

title: “Super location”
text:
Spent one night in September before our cruise. Old property but clean. Location makes up for lack of extras. There was no towel bar in the bathroom and no hairdryer, but it was a great place to get a night's sleep as we did a quick tour. The price was fantastic and I couldn't believe how close we were to Times Square. I would definitely stay there again.
The deli next door had great breakfasts at a very reasonable price.

title: “Parking during Cruise”
text: We utilized the Park n Cruise option at the Vagabond Inn during our 14 day Panama Canal cruise. Hotel staff was polite with the reservation process, and provided efficient transport to the cruise ship. Cost was very reasonable.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: We stayed 4 nights at at this hotel while visiting our son stationed at Ft. Sam Houston. The room was great; the staff was great. We had to return a rental car to Enterprise near the airport and the shuttle picked us up there. That was a nice suprise. The breakfast is good; the evening drinks and food was even better. We actually made a meal of the snacks twice. Once was chili dogs, salad, baked potatoes, and nachos, the other was mac and cheese and meatballs. We received three complimentary drinks each evening. The staff went out of its way to make our stay more comfortable. I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

title: “Nice hotel in centralized location”
text: After reading some poor reviews on Trip Advisor for this hotel, I was dreading staying here; however, I was pleasantly surprised upon arrival. I was able to check in much earlier than anticipated, the hotel staff was hospitable and helpful! My room was clean, and I felt safe. Which are my two top priorities when traveling alone. The lobby at times can be a bit hectic, but any lobby is when you have a convention going on in town. I was on the 16th floor with an interior room facing the pool. Even with people partaking in the pool my room was not that noisy. At times the hallways seemed a little maze like, but I quickly found the short cuts. My only complaint was that if people were talking in the hallway you could definitely hear them in your room; however, that only happened every now and then. Not a big deal.

title: “cant go wrong”
text:
My friend and I did a girly weekend and enjoyed the Houston science and history museum. Our hotel was wonderful we got an awesome rate of 48 a night. The room was clean, flat screen tv, fridge, microwave, granite bathroom, nice comfy bed, free internet. There really wasnt anything else I could ask for. 
great place to stay and we will be coming back
melissa

title: “Nice hotel but not as good as Grand Hyatt, DFW”
text:
This is the first time staying Hyatt Regency, DFW.
I stayed in the other Hyatt last year, I didn't know there are two Hyatt hotels in the same airport.
Grand Haytt is newer and nicer.
Internet was not free even I had to pay $200 plus for room.
I would stay in Grand Hyatt, not Hyatt Rengency if I come to Dallas again.

title: “Good downtown hotel”
text:
Depending on the paid price, I would rate this hotel with 4 or 5. If you get a discounted price, it deserves 5. If you pay the full price, it deserves only 4.
The hotel is new and modern. The room's equipment is very good with an iPod deck and a large flat TV. The bed is very comfortable and the linen very pleasant.
The swimming pool is enjoyable with a view on the other buildings and on the stadium.
The location is ideal in downtown although it is a little deserted on week-ends.
The self parking is free (gate open) if you exit early in the morning or outside the regular business hours.

title: “Going Downhill”
text: My "Ok, but problems" rating is generous based on their decent staff and low price. I felt uncomfortable here because it had a low occupancy rate and I had the feeling there were security issues. I was given a decent room on the top floor. It appeared to be basically clean and ok; the linen was clean and fresh. However, I happened to look behind the end table next to the bed - and there was lots of trash there - empty soda cans, food wrappers, etc. I called the front desk and they offered to change my room, but it was late, I had unpacked some, and the rest of the room seemed ok, so I remained there. I had reservations for 3 nights, but I was uncomfortable enough (not just because of the trash) that I felt it was better to check out than ask for another room. The desk cleck was nice about it. Overall, this place appears to be going downhill - not recommended unless you really need the low price and are comfortable in a place that might have security problems.

title: “Small ain't that bad!”
text:
I checked into the Comfort in with my 2 daughters. As expected, we had double 2 beds. What wasn't expected was the room size. It was surprisingly small - to the extent that we wondered how we would manage. We had no more than 2 feet at the foot of the bed, 2 feet between the bed and the bathroom and 1 foot between the beds, My daughter joked that we could not have 2 suitcases open at the same time. Sadly. it was true. 
However, sleep is sleep and the room was completely quiet and the beds very comfortable.The location, though on the lower East Side, was a gateway to the trendy neighborhoods, and a subway 2 blocks away. Cleanliness could use a bit of attention but that would not preclude a future stay. The free breakfast was hot and enjoyable but had a "fast food" air about it (except for the waffle maker which was a hit for all).
The staff were friendly and welcoming - particularly Jasmine who's personality and charm made it hard to complain about minor inconveniences. Though she certainly attended to any concern we may have had. She was the definitely the face of this property - to the extent that we had pictures with her before we left.
After 3 nights, I can say that, despite the room size (not uncommon in Manhattan), we had a great stay. Thank you Comfort Inn and THANK YOU Jasmine !!

title: “In the heart of the Financial District”
text:
I've stayed at this hote many times since it's only a block away from the Transamerica building. On my walk to the office I have a choice of 3 difference Starbucks and 2 Pete's so everything is right here.
Lately when coming to town I have been staying at the Omni, which is just as close. My last stay at Le Meridien several years ago was unpleasant because the staff was on strike and picketing out front. But it's been a few years so I decided to give them another try.
I would say I was pleased with my stay. The bar in the lobby is convenient for meeting up with other colleagues who are also staying in the hotel. The concierge was deadon in suggesting a sushi restaurant in North Beach. The room was modern contemporary in design but comfortable.
My favorite part of my stay was all of the movie choices on the television. If only I had the time to watch one but I've never seen so many good choices. 
My tips:
Request a room on the upper floors with a bay view. The way the windows are designed, everyone has a corner window view and sunrise is breathtaking.
If you can't find a good rate online, call the local number. They will work with you.

title: “fabulous hospitality and comfort”
text:
I traveled alone for the first time and couldn't have had a better time or selected a better hotel for me. The staff was exceptionally receptive and helpful and the hotel was nicely appointed and located in the center of the activity. I had a corner room with extra windows and a side view of the Mississippi River.....all of the appliances in the kitchen appeared new and everything worked. Although the staff offered to shop for me, I would have preferred easy access to a supermarket. Without a car, it was a long walk to carry groceries back to the hotel.
The breakfasts served at the Residence were really wonderul.....hot and cold buffet tables and everything was fresh including the fruit. Complimentary buffets were served in the evening as well and one could easily take dinner there at no cost.
I would return to this hotel and to Memphis in a New York minute.

title: “Awesome and great location”
text:
We went there to celebrate my husband's 40th and it was fantastic. The location simply cannot be beat. One block to the subway, within walking distance to central park and tons of fabulous restaurants and museums, Zabar's, Filene's, etc, etc.
The room was great (we stayed in the penthouse loft on the 16th floor), check-in/out was a breeze, there was a very handy business centre with free internet, and the concierge was very helpful too. Oh, and the beds were SUPER soft and fluffy and awesome :) My only disappointment was the terrace, as we ended up getting the very smallest one that could barely fit 2 chairs, while others were much bigger. But, we didn't spend any time out there anyway so it didn't end up bothering us too much.
If we return to NYC I would definitely consider coming back here!

title: “OMG Awesome”
text:
i booked this hotel b/c i had stayed at the grand hyatt nearby last time i was in town and wanted to try another hotel (not that i didn't love the grand hyatt :)) we arrived at the hotel friday afternoon around four o'clock from seatac (we were an hour late) and our dinner guests had just arrived. the staff of the hotel were so helpful and understanding (thanks ashly). i was able to check-in easily and we were taken upstairs by todd, the bellhop (thanks to you too). the room was awesome (double beds, seating area, tv, work desk with four outlets). the sliding doors for the closet and bathroom were a plus (though the bathroom one would open on its own if you didn't shut it completely). i did experience the loud closing doors and the loud people in the hall discussed earlier (also it was always 3 in the morning and i woke up). another suggestion would be to put an extra hook or bench in the bathroom (some place else to put clothes when hook in use) and another luggage rack (i had to use the bench beside the bed and the bed to get items out of two pieces of luggage) there was a blank area on the wall between the tv and the closet that could be used for artwork and the other luggage rack. 
i used the pool saturday and it was great (sat in the sun and read for a few hours) 
checkout was a breeze and was able to print out my boarding passes from the conceirge's laptop.

title: “Nice, functional hotel”
text: I stayed here one night in June when traveling to DC for work. The room, as is the case in in Club Quarters hotels, was on the small side, but the furnishings were pleasant. My one significant complaint about the hotel is that the room service food was of poor quality (especially for the price). DC was inundated with a massive storm the night that I stayed at the Club Quarters so I decided to rely on room service for my dinner. The portions were small and, amazingly, the Caesar salad was salty. Stay at the hotel if you are primarily concerned with function, but look elsewhere for dinner.

title: “loved the bed”
text: Very nice Westin. I loved that there was a real comforter and not a gross bedspread. There was a Christian Teenagers Conference going on at the hotel the weekend I was there but they were pretty well behaved and quiet. Conceirge was really helpful and staff were very nice. It is about a 30 minute drive from the airport.

title: “A great Birthday visit”
text: My wife was having a birthday and I was looking for very nice location for dinner. The French Room is one of the highest rated restaurants in the area and we decided to go there. The Adolphus was also running a room special, so we also decided to stay there. It was a very good choice. The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful. We were provided a very nice room upgrade. The French Room was excellent. Our wait staff was very helpful and professional. It was one of the best meals we have ever had. I will return there again.

title: “Awesome hotel!”
text:
Stayed in Yotel over the past weekend and had a great time! The rooms are very small but with the openness of the bathroom (its all glass inclosed) it didn't really feel too small at all. Check in is very quick and easy because its done on a computer instead of having to wait in line to have someone check you in. Unfortunately after we checked in and went to our room there was someone else's stuff in there! We went right to the "mission control" where they very quickly assigned us a new room. It actually worked out in our favor because we were given a room on the 26th floor instead of the 9th which had a much better view! 
The hotel overall was very modern and new. It was also extremely clean and all of the staff was very helpful. We didn't eat here or get to make it onto the terrace but I would be back to check it out for sure.
I like that Yotel was located close enough to Times Square and Penn Station but far enough out of the way that you weren't stuck in the over crowded area, especially at this time of year! We easily walked from the train station and to see the tree at Rockerfeller.
I think it's a great place for young couples as the room was very sexy... especially with the glass wall between the shower and the bed.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
Great location and spotlessly clean. Our room was quite small, but in-line with the price that we paid. The decor was nice and the bed was very comfortable. 
With the exception of the check-in staff, all staff were very friendly and helpful. Alison at the concierge desk deserves special recognition for making our stay such a memorable one - flowers in our room, restaurant recommendations and reservations, show recommendations and tickets, baseball tickets, she arranged it all. 
Great club sandwich from the room service menu!!

title: “book it AWAY from here!”
text: This hotel was dirty and unfriendly. From untimely room service and housekeeping to pubic hair on the bathroom ceiling. From the front desk staff that has zero clue about customer service to bartenders that don't know how to make a standard drink. From showers and sinks that looked like they'd never been cleaned since installation to putting a couple in a room with two queens instead of a king. From never getting that wake-up call to dusty curtains. From taking 40 minutes to get my car from valet to the cabinet knobs hanging off. From housekeeping not even coming one day to the safe being already locked. This place was miserable and I would not wish this sort of expensive dirt-bomb on anyone.

title: “Terribly Disappointing”
text:
I had stayed previously at this hotel and enjoyed it very much. My most recent stay was terrible. The room was smaller than usual, but was still nice. Thankfully we opened the minibar and noticed it looked like it was missing some things - we compared inventory against the card and noticed a number of things missing. Someone had to come up and check and restock - glad we checked as I'm sure we would have been charged for missing items! Next day, received e-mail with our bill - gave it a cursory check as I knew we had pre-paid for room and hadn't incurred additional charges. Much to our surprise, there was a charge for over $150 to the 24 bar/restaurant on-site. Upon investigating, we were told there was NOTHING the hotel could do and we would have to talk to either 24 or the spa, as the charge could be from either. They thought they were open then (10:00), but they weren't; we assumed 11:00 so sat around and waited until then. Still not open at 11:00 - checked again at front desk and learned that Sundays they don't actually open until 4:00!! The front desk would do nothing to remove the charge, and we weren't going to wait around until 4:00. We left, and resolved the issue over the phone, but it got our day off to a terrible start, and wasted hours of our time. SO disappointed in the lack of satisfaction we were given by the "manager"; not a single apology for any of our problems we encountered. Definitely NOT returning; thought this would be one of our favorite hotels, but now see that is not in the cards! 
As an aside - we were on "executive" floor, but it was LOUD throughout the night and definitely not a good nights sleep.

title: “A nice stay: Basic accommodations, friendly staff”
text:
Location:
-Great for families & friends visiting OSU 
-Next to an Applebee’s, McDonalds, convenience stores and gas stations.
-5 minutes from Lennox Shopping Center (Target, Barnes and Noble, restaurants)
-10-minute drive or $10-13 cab ride to Short North; 15-20 minute drive or $15-$18 cab ride downtown (upon check-in, ask for the card of the taxi service the hotel recommends)
Rooms:
- Clean, comfortable rooms, but very basic accommodations.
- Motel-style, with hotel room doors facing the outside
- Room came with 1-cup coffee-maker; other items, like iron and hair dryer available on request only
My take:
When in Columbus, I prefer to stay at hotels located on East Nationwide in the Arena District, right between Downtown and the Short North. However, as it was OSU’s Move-In weekend, most hotels near the action were booked, so I landed here. I don’t regret it, but I missed being able to walk to nice bars and restaurants. However, this hotel isn’t that far away from all of that, and if you are there to see an OSU student, it’s probably perfect for you.

title: “Not perfect but would return!”
text: We got a great rate from Expedia and were concerned when we read the other reviews. It is true that there were no indoor pools, hot tubs,gift shops,microwaves, or fridges in rooms. One elevator was not working. However, the rooms were big and clean and we had no problems with our stay. We ate/drank at the bar and there were other restaurants on site. It looks like they are working to fix up the hotel. The online pictures really need updating because the hotel is nicer than what is shown. If you are passing thru Indy and get a great rate, don't hesitate to stay for a few nights!

title: “Worst hotel ever!!!!!”
text: Hotel was a nightmare booked a room that was suppose to have 2 queen beds, got a room that had a twin and double, requested a new room after seeing cockroaches. The next room wasn't much better it had friggin bunkbeds and barely had room to move. Forget the fact that we couldn't even check in until after 6pm because the room wasn't ready after I even called at 3pm and was assured the room was ready. Front desk help was from mars. Oh and after we were told the room was cleaned and ready we found a bunch of empty beer cans on the ledge. We requested towels because the only left 2 got more towels that were like sandpaper and no wash cloths. The front desk guy reminded me this was a budget hotel but I think that paying over $300,00 for a nights stay constitutes a little better quality.

title: “Nice hotel as base for exploring San Diego”
text:
We stayed here for two nights recently. Check-in was smooth and friendly, and my room was quite nice with a harbour view. The bathroom was small but clean and functional.
I arrived at the airport and at the last moment I was able to arrange a free pickup by the hotel shuttle service. Great service. 
We used the hotel bar twice and loved the ambiance with the marina views-and the fireplace. A great place to have a nightcap and unwind on a cool SD evening. The restaurant breakfast and dinner selection was also good and reasonsably priced for a Hilton Hotel.
The hotel is only about 5-10 mins cab drive ($12) from the main tourist sites in San Diego. It's very close (almost walking distance) to the airport, and being directly on the harbour and marina, there's some nice views and walking/jogging tracks along the waterfront. 
The hotel has a small pool, not suitable for a lap swimmer, but ok for a splash with the kids.
So, overall, no complaints, and was just what we were looking for. It's a nice hotel in a nice location. We booked online and had a very reasonable rate (under $130pn) for what is a 4 + star hotel.
We would recommend this hotel for a quick stay for business or pleasure. 
If you prefer to walk to the major attractions of the Gaslight District and the maritime museum/Midway, perhaps check the rates at the other the downtown Hilton and compare first.

title: “Nice place. Good location”
text: The staff was fantastic! The rooms were a little small but for the price you can't complain. Everything was very clean. The beds were comfortable and we could see the Empire State building from our window. The breakfast for kids was free and our breakfast was delicious and cheap. We went on the weekend and got in around midnight. One of the people at the restaurant said there might be street parking and went out to look with us. He found us a spot but it was back a bit and the hotel is on a one way street. He stood in the spot and saved it for us and we were able to keep our car there all weekend for free thanks to him! We will definitely be back!

title: “What a Great Stay !!!!!”
text:
I stayed at this Sheraton last Saturday. What a great time. I visit Charlotte at least 6 times a year. I've stayed at many hotels, and my experience here was the best. I was greeted by the very friendly front desk staff, and had a personal greeting by Lupita Gasga, the Front office Supevisor. Lupita quickly offered to personally take our luggage to our room. While in front at the car, she instantly started to tell us about all of the amenities at the hotel and offered us a great upgrade, that we couldn't refuse. 
We had Lunch and Breakfast the next morning in the restaurant. The food was great and Patricia (our server) was fantastic. 
Both Women were awesome, personable and great representatives of the Sheraton. They really made our stay memorable and I will never stay any where else, when in the area. I will also recommend the property to my friends and Family for our next Southern Family Reunion!!!
Thanks Lupita and Patricia.

title: “Comfortable and quiet”
text:
This is a very nice hotel located in the heart of all the fun and at the conference center.
The hotel has great comfortable rooms, and it is very quiet at night.
Limited dining on site, but again very close to bars and restaurants. 
THere is a small pool and workout facility, but I recommend neither as it is in the basement, pretty musty, little ventilation and looks pretty warn down.

title: “Not Worth The Money”
text: My husband and I just returned from an overnight at the Park Plaza Hotel. I had read many of the reviews and was a little concerned about the hotel but thought how bad can it be, well it can really be that bad. We arrived around five in the evening and upon check in were told immediately that the hotel was over sold. The manager said that because we booked with Priceline we were going to be moved to one of their "sister" hotels around the corner the Sheraton 4 points. I knew based on my research that there was no Sheratons just around the corner and discovered that we were being moved to a hotel out by Logan. After telling them that this was not going to happen and that we were on our way to the Red Soxs they found us a room (an economy room) to stay in. We didn't known that this would mean we were being put in a closet somewhere. The room was smaller than my sons room at home with the bed just barely fitting in the room. The bathroom was smaller than a closet and the shower may have measured if I am being generous 18 inches across. My husband had to keep on foot out to actually shower. We also were right by the elevator which ran up and down our wall all night and sounded like a very loud thunder storm. Our view was of a very ugly alley and they dragged the dumsters out a five in the morning waking us up once again. I had asked before heading to bed if another room had opened up and the girl at the desk who spoke very broken english told me to check back on Saturday. This was a little confusing because it was Wed. and we were there for one night. Overall not worth the money at all. Stay at the Hotel Commonwealth, Wyndham,Weston or anywhere else but don't waste your money here. Even if you can get it on Priceline it is not worth it and they treat priceline customers very poorly!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! JillMurf

title: “A Great Place to Say In the middle of Everything”
text: My Sisters and I just Stayed at this Hotel, I have to say first that I had read the reviews before I left about the staff not being to friendly ect, My experence was Great, they were Very Helpful and Very Friendly, I can not complain at all, The Hotel its self was always Clean, The lobby was always being mopped and cleaned, Our Room was Clean, and with 4 of us with suitcases ect were very comfortable, Its Not Fancy But clean and comfortable and the location was Perfect, you are walking distance to just about everything, and also the Subways and Buses, There was only one elevator but the wait wasnt to long, overall, If you want a clean, comfortable, Not Fancy, great rate Hotel in the middle of Manhatten this is the place, I would Stay again for sure, we Enjoyed our first trip To NY:)

title: “SATISFACTORY HOTEL”
text: I stayed here for a couple of nights recently. I was just reading some of the bad reviews and felt it necessary to give a favorable one. It's certainly not a luxury hotel but for the price (I paid $40 a night,) I thought it was a good deal. The room was clean enough (didn't leave with bug bites!) and everything worked properly. The front desk staff was friendly enough and my room was fairly quiet.

title: “AWSOME!!! Hotel to stay at!!!!!!!!!!”
text:
This is a hotel with outstanding service and incredible comfort (the bed sheets are soo comfortable) and well designed! It has a modern yet personal touch and you will enjoy the incredible food form the restuarant. I had room service (in LA on business) and it was FAST and well prepared.
Overall a real class hotel in the BEST location local to all of LA!
Thanks Angeleno!

title: “Take your chances.”
text:
I could see how this could go either way but our room was not good.
Good: 
-The rooms are a good size.
- The wifi seemed fast.
The Bad: 
- The rooms smell real bad! Out of the four rooms our family got, two smelled real awful. 
- My wife and I had a normal smelling room until we turned on the heat (because when we walked in the room was freezing). The heater made funny noises and then spat out an awful smell.
- The AC didn't work. Obviously I didn't want to use the heat so I tried different temps on the "cool" setting and it was all freezing.
- The "blankets" are more like an extra sheet. There is no comforter but that wouldn't be a real problem if the room weren't freezing.
- The staff was unfriendly. I mean, I guess I wouldn't know since they barely talked to me and were mostly watching the TV in the lobby.
I booked four rooms for my family. My elderly grandma was with us and they put us on the second floor with no lift! She's handicapped! We walked all the way to the end of the hallway where she stopped at the bottom of the stairs. I should have walked back to check in and asked for a first floor but we instead we assisted her up the stairs. My mother wanted me to complain and said that it was against the law to have no handicap accessible ramp. I'm not sure if that's true but my complaint is that the staff is oblivious. Like couldn't they see that I was with an elderly woman.
Oh yea, and I called ahead and asked for the room to be together. And requested at least one of the king rooms be connected to the double room so someone could be connect to my grandma. Our rooms were on the same floor but was it so full that none could be connected even after calling? Didn't look it.
I should have spent like $20 more for a nicer hotel or $50 less for an equal quality hotel. Also there was no recognition of elite status and no upgrade. Not that it matters.
All that being said and one of the rooms we had didn't stink... well two before I turned on the heat! I give you 50/50. The experience makes me weary of Park Inns now.

title: “Why go to Hawaii when you can stay at the Dana in San Diego?”
text:
I have never written a review for a hotel based on my experiences whether good or bad but I feel impelled to share the wonderful stay at The Dana Hotel in San Diego.
The service, room, restaurant and view are all 5 star. I don't know what The Dana is rated
but if I were giving it a rating, it would be at least 5 star. A real "10" on my scale.
I really didn't want to come home after my stay at The Dana and with SeaWorld right next door and a shuttle, we never had to use our vehicle during our stay. If you are like us, the last thing you want to do is drive after commuting everyday for work. Everything nearby including renting a bike - biking riding (which we did) and a 28 mile ride around the bay (we didn't do the whole ride but we did 14 miles) and riding around the beauty of the bay/beach is magical. I really didn't know how much there was to do in the area as well as right at the hotel. We sat in the hot tub in the evening watching a movie on the big screen outdoors next to the pool. That along with a cocktail, it just doesn't get any better.
Although we don't have children, they seemed to be having a blast as well! It's a great place whether you are a family with children, or if you are at The Dana for a romatic birthday weekend as we were. My partner said it was the best vacation ever and she felt like a queen for the weekend. Go and enjoy, pamper yourself.....we will do it again.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text:
Loved this hotel! Our room was super clean and comfortable and after a long day of touring we enjoyed a great night's sleep. The staff was wonderful and professional, they were 
friendly and informative. They also, offered us an upgrade to a junior suite, which gave
us more room for a great price. The rooms and the lobby are beautifully appointed and the internet was free. As, I will be retuning to San Francisco in the future I will be staying at the
Villa Florence!

title: “Great Price, Great Quality, No Complaints for a 1 Night Stay”
text: Used it as a crash pad after a night out with my best friend. Good quality, room was on the small side, but I paid a very competitive price, it was like new, very clean, very easy check-in and check-out, so I was pleasantly surprised.

title: “Good place for cubs fans”
text:
We stayed for 2 nights starting Sept. 9th at this Days Inn. This is a 100 year old building in the Lincoln Park area of Chicago.
We pulled up to the curb and the valet came out and asked if we wanted to have our car parked - $20.00 a day. Since parking is so hard to find in Chicago we decided to do this and we really did not intend to use our car during our stay. The $20.00 a day includes in and out privleges. Check in was a breeze - very fast and efficient. We had a room on the 2nd floor. There is a small elevator or stairs.
 Our room was a double room which consisted of 2 double beds with a chair on each side of the bed and a night stand in between the beds along with a low long 2 drawer dresser that held the TV, coffeemaker and ice bucket. There was also a "walk in closet" that consisted of a low, long 2 drawer dresser, a clothes rack and safe. (there is a $1.75 fee per day for the safe) Just off the room was a small area that had a desk with mirror over it. This was next to the small bathroom. The bathroom consisted of a toilet, tub/shower combination and a sink. Unlike most hotels the sink did not have an expansive counter. It was simply a small sink. It did have a glass shelf above the sink. The large window sill also could be utilized for storage. The bed weren't the most comfortable but okay. And the room was clean. 
 The hotel has a free contenental breakfast which was included in the rate. It consisted of 4 types of ceral, apples, oranges, 3 types of fruit juice, bagels, sweet rolls and waffles. Of course coffee, tea, milk and water were also available.
 There are several restaurants that are within walking distance (1-6 blocks) along with a Walgreens, and 2 bookstores. The hotel is about 1 mile from the Wrigley Field. There is a bus stop right around the corner on Clark that will take you right up to the stadium for a $2.00 fare. We chose to take the bus to the game and walked back - the walk back took about 10 minutes. There is also a bus stop right in front of the hotel.
 All in all this is a nice hotel in a good location for Cubs games. I would stay here again if attending a game.

title: “Hotel was nice but we were treated poorly due to booking on Priceline”
text: We booked this hotel through Priceline and have used Pricelines many times in the past with no problems. I had called the hotel at least 2 weeks before our arrival to make sure we would be able to get a room with 2 beds and they said depending on availabilty and she put it down on my reservation. Well knowing that we would be arriving around 2pm I decided not to worry and did not pack a sleeping bag for my son. We were able to get our room with two beds for an $30/night plus additional fees this is unacceptable! I was never told there would be an extra fee just that it was based on availability otherwise I would have packed a sleeping bag for my son. I checked into the DoubleTree in MN 2 nights later again using Priceline and had no problem getting 2 beds and no extra fees. Other than this issue the hotel was nice and clean. Bathroom door as others have mentioned is not a big deal you can other see the other person if they go right up to the door. Also we did have a room with a tub but no TV in the mirror not that I needed either.

title: “The best hotel in the city, you haven't heard of.”
text:
I wanted to stay in Union Square when celebrating our anniversary, but can't stand staying at a large hotel that treats people like just a number. A friend recommended this place since its next to the park, on the cable car line, next to a city jewel pancake house and just finished a renovation. 
The staff is hysterical, the rooms have all new furniture, the location is perfect and to top it off your not going to break the bank on the cost of a room.
Stay here. You won't regret it. 
TIP: Name the rubber ducky.

title: “Wouldn't consider anywhere else”
text: We are in our early fities, and this was our first trip to SF. I did a tremendous amount of research to prepare our itinerary. Our number 1 priority was to stay "on the water, with a view from our room," so we chose the Radisson after looking at the pictures on various websites of the "waterfront" hotels. We stayed in room 4117, and I can't even begin to tell you what a tremendous view we had ( Alcatraz , Golden Gate Bridge, Fisherman's Wharf people watching spot, and the magnificent Pacific sunsets.) Yes --- it's not the latest and greatest hotel in SF, but that doesn't matter to us. We're willing to sacrifice to get what we want. Our room was as clean as most of the places we've stayed in, and every employee we met throughout our stay went out of their way to say "hello" and asked us if we needed any help. I originally had a reservation at the Argonaut (very highly rated, on the water.) However, I changed it to the Radisson because it was 1/2 the cost, and I just couldn't see the "waterfront" on the Argonaut pictures. We walked down to the Argonaut one day to check it out, and we just didn't see how any of their rooms' views could possibly compare to ours. I wouldn't even consider staying anywhere else if we ever go back to San Francisco (an incredibly fun/educational/scenic vacation, by the way!)

title: “Excellent hotel,far from city center”
text:
The hotel is great,clean,comfortable,good value for money.
The only downside is the location - about 20 minute drive on the highway to most city attractions. It is located in a living neighborhood, nothing much to do in the area. However there is a nice kiosk in the hotel w
here you can buy drinks,food etc and a nice restaursnt in the hotel- breakfast is big and inexpensive.
The staff is very nice and helping and there is a business center,pool, fitness room and free parking and wifi.
If you are visiting san diego witha car,great place to stay.

title: “OK Stay”
text:
I stayed here for 3 nights last week for a conference. The hotel itself is very clean and modern in decor. The staff overall was very friendly. The room was comfortable. The exercise room was great but hard to find; it took quite a bit of exploring on my part to find it. The single restaurant in the hotel is very overpriced and not worth the money. The small gift shop is also very overpriced, as is the bar. Make sure you don't open the bottles of water in the room; you will be charged $5 per bottle. 
The location of the hotel is only good for those attending conferences in the hotel itself or the convention center next door. It is not within walking distance of anything (other than a couple of restaurants); the T stop is about 3/4 of a block away (not across the street as advertised).

title: “Like coming home to a retreat”
text: Our family just completed our second stay at the Hotel Drisco and it was every bit as wonderful as we remembered it from a year ago. At the end of a long day in the city, I felt as if I was coming home to a luxurious yet relaxed retreat. The rooms are spacious, beautifully decorated and appointed, clean and comfortable. The staff was friendly and helpful, often times giving us directions, calling a taxi for us, or recommending restaurants. And the complimentary breakfast is not only fresh and healthy, it is presented in a very relaxing setting. I plan to return to the Hotel Drisco whenever I'm in San Francisco and wouldn't hesitate recommending it as a place for others to stay.

title: “One night was enough”
text:
Booked this hotel ahead of time and, upon arrival, found the parking to be a nightmare, the lack of a/c unbearable, the noise almost impossible to sleep through, the vagrants outside our door and along the boardwalk hard to ignore and the threat of a fight breaking out at any moment constantly in the forefront of our thoughts.
Not good value for the money although the staff were wonderful - they must own the property!!!
We promptly left the CAdillac AND Venice Beach the next day. 
Would not recommend Venice OR the Caddy Hotel to ANYONE!!!!

title: “Very clean and modern; no Internet”
text: Modern and clean interior spaces, although the lobby was a little cozy. The room was very spacious, almost suite-like. There was a large sofa with ottoman and two full-sized beds. Crisp sheets & bedding and a comfy mattress made for an excellent night's sleep. If you like watching TV, the room has a 60 inch screen; perfect for watching a presidential debate. The best thing about this hotel was the excellent free breakfast. There were breakfast sandwiches, French toast, yogurt parfait, oatmeal, granola, fresh fruit, pastries, and strong Starbucks coffee. All well-presented with generous offerings. There's also a sports bar next door if you like to have a beer. I also like the hotel's close proximity to the airport and they have a free shuttle too! Only negative: no free Internet in my room.

title: “Major Renovations in Progress”
text: Stayed one night on the 8th March. The room was nice and big although not the nicest decor (walls very scratched and marked). Beds were comfey and clean, with no bed bugs. The location is good, with the space needle only 10 minutes walk away, and Pike Market about 20 minutes walk. Neighbourhood is ok for walking in with a group, but would not recommend it on your own (but that applied to the whole of Downtown Seatle). Me aware though that their are major renovations in the loby (jackhammer starts at about 9am), so expect a lot of noise. Also the pool is shut during the renovation. Breakfast was good for a freebe (Bagels, Waffles, Muffins, Toast, Yougut, Fruit, Orange and Apple Juice).

title: “Great Hotel for 1st timer to NY”
text:
Where to start .This was the 1st time to NY for my wife & I .The Hotel is New York ,being right in the middle of it .On arrival we went to the check in desk on the 1st floor I mentioned to them it was a special occasion & we were upgraded to a room on the 21st floor & were sent the biggest chocolate covered strawberrys I have seen .The bed ,,,where do i start,,, i remember my head hitting the pillow & waking up some 8 hrs later .We had room service (the Burger was great ) & i thought was reasonably priced 
All the staff made you feel welcome & went the extra mile all the time just to help & NOTHING was ever to much trouble.
The free use of computers & wi fi in the lobby was great also.
Would I recomend it YES
Will I stay again YES
Well done to this Hotel ive stayed at some very expensve Hotels in Paris & London the this stay tops them all

title: “Good choice”
text: The hotel has a very good position for visiting New York. The room was cosy, we asked for a family roon and it was appropriate. The kitchen was well equiped, the bathroom also. We had nothing to complain. Maybe the furniture a little worn out, but it does not make a difference. The hotel has no restaurant, no breakfast included. It is some expensive hotel, but I think that these are the prices in New York.

title: “Very good choice, minus a few amenities.”
text: I was a guest in Chicago at this hotel for a buisness week in August. My stay was plesant and the service was excellent. It was clean and friendly. The bars and restaurants were great and the prices are a little high but fair for the area. My only complaints were a lack of dvd/blueray player in the room, no Jacuzzi (its the north I would think that was mandatory lol), lack of convenient access to the vast city train system, and only 2 bars within reasonable walking distance besides the hotels. So you may save money on the room but its spent on extra transportation. Everything else was great.

title: “Classic hotel, historical and updated, still needs more...”
text: Stayed at the Palmer House for business for 10 days. Very good experience at check-in as I told the clerk that I had heard (and read) that "some" of the rooms were on the small side -since I was going to be there for an extended time could they find me a larger room, which they did (although 2 queens instead of a king bed). As you can read elsewhere, the lobby is quite nice, and the entire hotel is living history well-preserved. The lobby bar is a fun place to hang out and the lobby in general is full of activity at night. The hotel is huge with banks of elevators serving groupings of floors - expect longer than reasonable delays at peak hours (old hotel, old elevators). The hotel is very big, the walk to the room can be far... the room was fine, nothing special - although it was pretty large based on my request :) No flat screen LCD/LED TV here, just a cheap old 27" tube TV, no coffee maker in room, no mini-bar, and NO WIRELESS INTERNET IN ROOM. One of my co-workers told me that the front desk provided him with a wireless router for his room upon request, I stuck with the in-room wired connection during my stay. Again ,the rooms are older, have been updated (although mine still had the very old AC/HEAT controls), clean, beds were comfortable, but nothing really that special. I guess people aren't staying here for the "great" rooms but you can't sleep in the lobby :) Ordered room service a few times - no need to order more than that as there are only about 10 items on the menu, VERY limited selection for such a "large and prestigious hotel" - or for any hotel for that matter. Careful if you order the "bottled water" as they will bring you the $5 glass bottle - the front desk gave me free bottled water whenever I stopped by and asked, although only once was it cold. There is no coffee service in the lobby either and unless you pre-order coffee the night before be prepared to wait (i was told 45 minutes or longer for room service, weekdays and weekend) - your only on-site options are the hotel restaurant or the Starbucks on ground floor (the street level "S"). If you arrive at the Starbucks between 7:30 and 9:30 be prepared to wait as the line got very long - I would suggest one of the many places on the block as an alternative if you are looking for a quick breakfast at a reasonable price (or the Starbucks across the street). Regarding the rating, I would give it a 3.5 out of 5 but that's not an option.

title: “LOVED the Distrikt!”
text:
We arrive at 7:30 am so no room available of course, but they took our bags and our cell phone number so we could start exploring. The location of the hotel is an excellent base for exploring this huge city. It is located at 40th Street and 9th Avenue, and 9th is where you can find countless restaurants! Every evening we would just walk up 9th and find somewhere to eat! (We LOVED Arriba Arriba for Mexican, and L'Allegria for Italian!)
We had a queen room (the smallest) but it was plenty big for a 5 night stay in NYC, who spends time in the room anyway? The bathroom was gorgeous and the rooms were spotless! Every single staff member we met, from the front desk, to housekeeping, to bartenders we super nice and always helpful!
The hotel is really close to the 42nd street subway station which we used quite frequently, as well it's only about 2 blocks from Times Square so you can take in the lights when you want to, but not feel like part of the crazy tourist pack!
All in all we LOVED the hotel and would go back in a heartbeat, that is if we can afford it! We got an excellent deal on Expedia when it first opened, now the nightly rate listed on the door of our room said $629 (a bit steep if you ask me). Go to the Distrikt while it's still affordable.. you won't be sorry!! :)

title: “Very Impressive”
text: While my stay was short, I wanted to make it longer. Great front desk and concierge staff. Large oversixed guest rroms with huge bathrooms (and great lighting). Tv's could have a few additional channels but then a casino hotel would prefer I spend my waking hours downstairs.

title: “nice family resort”
text: We visited when San Antonio was experiencing 105 degree temps. We were impressed how the staff, even in the outdoor heat, was energetic, friendly and fun. All the service staff were friendly, helpful and polite. The rooms were not huge and a 2 bedroom room did not allow for much room for a family to spread out, but you will want to spend time out of your room at this resort. It would be difficult to find room for a pack-n-play. This resort will nickel and dime you. If you can, we suggest bringing your own waters, drinks and even breakfast, lunch and snack foods. There is a fridge in the room, and there is ice available for filling a cooler.

title: “Over priced”
text: Too many hidden costs. The resort charged $25. a day to park car outside. My clean car was returned covered in dust and bird droppings. A charge of $59. per day for housekeeping. Numerous charges, you are unaware of until check-out. I was not the only one complaining at check-out. My package deal turned out to be more expensive, than a regular booking.

title: “Amazing team! Exceptional service!”
text: I stayed at the W Los Angeles - Westwood with 12 members of my family. The property is beautiful. Clean and well maintained. What set this hotel apart for me was the wonderful service offered by the associates. Everyone form the front desk, housekeeping to valet were friendly and welcoming. A couple of note worthy experiences. The restaurant, Ninethirty was terrific. The manager was present and actively engaged with guests. We had several meals there and the service and food quality exceeded our expectations. The Eggs Benedict were great. Also, on the dinner menu-the Scallops, Rack of Lamb and Hanger Steak were excellent! The team at the Backyard were also wonderful and attentive. When we were leaving the Hotel, the valet (manager) was assiting us. He asked if we would like any water for the road. We said sure. And asked for two bottles. He asked where we were driving to and after I told him, he offered us a case of water! Very nice touch and what a surprise. Congratulations to the entire team...amazing job!

title: “Weekend Getaway”
text: Went to the Hyatt Regency in Boston last weekend with my wife and another couple. We had beautiful suites that were ready as soon as we arrived. The rooms were immaculate. The staff had arranged tickets for Blue Man Group at a lower cost than we could find anywhere else and had the tickets waiting for us. The staff was very pleasant to deal with and extremely helpful. Brunch on Sunday morning was outstanding. Again, the staff was very attentive to our needs. The overall experience was probably the best example of customer service from top to bottom than we have had in any of our travels.

title: “Good for Purpose”
text: Room was OK but amenities were great. Free hot breakfast, free drinks and snack, and 10 minutes to airport. Room had a smoker in it the night before so the bathroom smelled awful. Bed was just alright with terrible pillows with no support (but I bring my own when traveling).

title: “Very pleasant, standard Sofitel”
text: We stayed one night and were upgraded to a realitively spacious junior suite. The hotel and its rooms have a couple of years on them, but our room was very clean, pleasantly decorated, and everything worked just as it should have for a Sofitel. Staff was friendly, said hello, and was willing to please. The restaurant staff for breakfast the next morning was expert and very attentive--a nice detail in these more casual days, and a great finish to a very relaxing stay. This is not the sexiest or most post hotel in town, but it is a solid hotel up to Sofitel standards.

title: “Excellent!”
text: We spent a night at the Ritz Carlton in Denver. The service was great, and the rooms were awesome. The restaurant has the best steaks I've ever had. We had a great time! We even had room service breakfast from the restaurant. I had biscuits and gravy and it was delicious. We bought a movie on the tv too and I fell asleep halfway through the bed was so comfortable. We can't wait to visit Denver again!

title: “I really liked this place.”
text: I have rated this place a 4 because my husband wasn't so keen.. I think he would have preferred a place closer to Fisherman's Wharf, but he doesn't understand the cost/benefit ratios of the area like I do after all of me research! This place was in an excellent location - very safe, right next to the best restaurant street - and the BEST "Rice Pudding Shop" which we ate at every night after dinner.. We were walking distance to Fishermans Wharf too. Just a tip if heading to Alcatraz (prebook!!). For our family of 4 this was a good choice, and the service staff were very friendly and helpful - don't expect too much from the breakfast though!

title: “For a good nights sleep”
text: I read the reviews about the noise from Ground Zero but thought it can't be that bad. IT WAS, we tried to sleep in 1402. We could see the work being done from our room. It didn't seem bad during the morning as the traffic covered the noise, but at night even the loud air conditioning unit couldn't cover the noise. Our last night there Sept 28th was the worse, I got about 3 hours sleep.Other than that it is near to the subway, we had a lovely time on the Staten Island Ferry and will go back to New York but not to this hotel.

title: “Great Stay!”
text:
Me and 3 friends stayed at the Belvedere for 5 nights. We had 2 double beds, a tv unit, mini fridge and microwave - the rooms were very spacious and very clean.
