The mini fridge came in handy for water, juice etc. The staff at the Belvedere were extremely helpful and even made quick last minute arrangements for us to get a town car to the airport when we had forgotten to do so in advance (very appreciated!).
The elevators were not a problem at all - they are typical elevators.
The hotel is in a great, safe location ~ literally a 2 minute walk from Times Square (and walking distance to most areas).
Coming in from 90 degree weather it was nice to have the a/c (the unit was a bit noisy, so for light sleepers I would recommend ear plugs - that goes for any hotel with a window a/c unit)
I would definitely return to the Belvedere and recommend it to anyone staying in NYC.

title: “okay.”
text: My family and I just returned from our delayed vacation in DC. We were impressed by the quick check-in process and the friendly front desk staff. They answered all of our questions and were more than willing to give suggestions on how to get our stay started off right. As the week went on, we had to call down and have the maid service come back up and clean our room frequently (at least twice), and request towels and washcloths. It was almost like they started cleaning the room and replenishing everything, then left to get something and never returned. We also had requested on the my affinia website to have a floral bouquet and a fruit plate set up at 2pm on our arrival date, this did not happen. Much later that night, I called down to the front desk and asked them why the request had not been completed. They spent 10 minutes questioning me on if I had a confirmation, which I did via email, when I know that they had the request from the beginning. The woman who checked us in verified the request, which at the time I took to mean it was either in the process of being done or had already been taken care of. Again, a small detail but very frustrating. We were surprised that the hotel was on the hop-hop off bus route, after a day of sightseeing it was nice not to have to walk back a couple of blocks. The rooms themselves are comfortable, and fairly quiet. During most of our stay the conference center was being used, and I have to say that in the mornings the different groups took over the lobby and it's staff. Unless you are a late riser, don't anticipate using the lobby to meet up with the rest of your party- there will be no seating available and there really isn't any place to stand either. For our itinerary, this hotel was in a perfect location. We walked to the capitol visitor center in about 10 minutes, and the Russel building in about 5. Overall, this hotel has some wonderful qualities, but they also have a couple of issues that need to be ironed out before calling themselves a boutique hotel.

title: “Perfect location, great service, will definitely return”
text:
We loved our stay of one night and will definitely return. We have stayed at many
downtown hotels in Denver and this was one of our best stays ever, The restaurant food was excellent, great chef, Jason. The staff was extremely friendly, the room was exceptionally clean and location is the best in downtown Denver. We have a lodging business in Colorado so we always look for the best. We were totally/completely satisfied and will be back. We only wish hotel rates in downtown Denver were a little more affordable but this was worth the money.

title: “Excellent choice!”
text:
The rooms are excellent, except maybe for the bed, which I prefere to be equiped with an orthopedic mattress, more firm.
Very clean, very spacious, very well luminated, very good furniture, very good accesories... Only a single minus: the lack of any digestive drink in the minibar.
I had an excellent picnic basket, even the weather was ugly in the picnic day, so I ate it in bed :)
The service was great, the staff very nice.
One tip: the continental breakfast is more than enough for 2 people, so you don't need to pay for 2... Just order for 1 guest in the room!

title: “It was ok.”
text: I like the location. The view is nice. I love Grandys resteraunt which is close by. Quiet hotel. Bathrooms could be bigger.

title: “Nice Hotel, convenient location”
text: The Hamilton is a nice hotel with a beautiful lobby. We enjoyed our stay here but found the rooms to be small. We are a family of 4 with 2 older teens and we all stayed in one room 2 double beds the first night and found it to be quite crowded. We split into two rooms and were much more comfortable. This hotel has reasonable prices on the weekend, due to the fact that it is in the business district. Unfortunately, since it is in the business district many of the small restaurants are not open after about 5pm. We were ready to go out to dinner at about 9:30pm and the restaurant selection nearby was limited. We did enjoy the hotel restaurant for dinner and Priorty Club members recieve 50% off of the breakfast buffet. We loved the breakfast buffet and highly recommend it. The hotel is not sound proof and there is a little bag in your room with ear plug to block out the street noise. On the lower level there is a computer room where you can print out you boarding pass for free. Great hotel with comforable beds but the rooms are not spacious.

title: “Excellent service; very clean”
text:
The Homewood Suites Washington, D.C. is an excellent find. Service is excellent (far better than you expect to find in an extended stay hotel). Rooms were spacious and comfortable. This was the perfect place to relax after a long day of work.
More on my trip to Washington, D.C.:
http://justanothertravelblog.blogspot.com/2011/01/winds-of-change-in-washington-dc.html

title: “Great "times" at "Times Square".....”
text:
My husband and I stayed for 2 nights, after a Carnival cruise, out of Manhattan Pier.
Check-in was a breeze, though it was a very busy weekend.
All staff we encountered, from bell-boys, desk clerks, concierge desk, housekeepers...were very cordial & professional.
The property is immaculate, especially considering the huge traffic.
The room was spotless : a very spacious suite. There were plenty of towels, a robe, nice bath toiletries, safe, coffe maker, LARGE flat screen TV, and the MOST plush, comfortable bed & bedding, ever, in a hotel stay...including a DUVET, instead of a blanket.
Food & convenience store items on the 8th floor lobby are rather costly...you're better off walking to the very near-by WALGREEN's, to get over the counter-type items, and soft drinks, or yogurt.
The best thing about this property is LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION!!!
You're literally on TIMES SQUARE..just step out of the hotel, and you're right smack in the middle of great N.Y. action....plus right in the middle of the theater district. There's even a half-price TIX booth, right in front of the hotel. You also have the play "EVITA" (starring Ricky Martin) right at the hotel's 3rd floor MARQUIS theater. It is also within walking distance of hundreds of eateries, 5th Avenue, Midtown, Empire State bldg; Rockefeller Center, Bryant Park. Also, double-decker tour buses have stops right in front of the hotel.
As for the elevator system.....once you get the "hang of it", it makes a lot of sense...and it expedites the huge elevator traffic.
All in all, we had a GREAT time! I would highly reommend this property!!

title: “Overbooked the hotel and cancelled my reservation!”
text: Made a reservation 4 months ago for the Philadelphia Marathon weekend in Novemeber. I got an email yesterday stating they had a computer error and they had to cancel my reservation! At this point all of the other hotels are booked! They said to call the Marathon booking group (which was passing the blame since they were the ones to overbook!) I would like to thank the Sheraton for ruining my marathon plans that I thought I had figured out a long time ago! Will be less likely to book at any Sheraton hotels now!!!

title: “Perfect hotel in a great location”
text: What a really nice hotel. The beds were very comfortable and the staff was great. JP at the pool bar was terrific and Cory who runs the Valet service couldn't have been more helpful. I was really impressed and would stay here again. The hotel is very clean and right in the middle of the gas lamp district with all the action. Perfect.

title: “Great hotel, perfect location.”
text: Our first visit to New York and we could not have chosen a better hotel or location. Nothing was too much trouble for any member of staff we spoke to, the front desk is very efficient, housekeeping was excellent, but the real bonus for us was the concierge desk, their knowledge and friendly attitude really helped make our holiday. The only downer for the hotel is the over priced bar and restaurant. We would have spent a lot more money in the hotel if the prices had been a little more reasonable. Great choices for food and drinks on the doorstep and no one at the hotel complained when guests took food into their rooms. No doubt we will return in the future.

title: “Wonderful place to stay”
text: We stayed 5 nights at the Ink48 in July. We enjoyed the place very much. The personal is very friendly and professional . Good quality restaurant. Approx. 20 minutes walk to Time Square. I recommend it .

title: “Great location for getaway with kids!”
text: We stayed here with our children (5 and 1) last weekend and it was great. We were upgraded to a larger room on a higher floor and the crib we requested was waiting in the room for us. The location was perfect as it was close to all of the things we wanted to do in NYC as a family. We heard that the hotel had the best burgers in town (there was a line up for the restaurant every time we passed the lobby) and were delighted to find out that we could place the order from our room and easily pick it up without lining up (which we did). We had a smooth check in and check out. The staff was friendly. I don't have anything negative to say about our stay or the hotel .. just wish we got to stay longer! I wasn't aware that there were any kids activities other than the little booklet and crayons they give when you check in which is why I gave it an average rating.

title: “Pricey, but thats Chicago”
text: The hotel is located within a short walk of the river, the Magnificent Mile, and a train stop. Like any other big city hotel, the House of Blues is a bit steep. A happy hour for two people ran $62...probably $30 more than expected. Hotel is unique, and the workout area is an independent gym ($16 per day), but it is a full size, full service club. Parking is $34 a day and it can take 15 to 20 minutes for them to retrieve your vehicle. Overall it is a decent hotel, clean and centrally located, but at the price I would look to other options first.

title: “Thanks, Tony Bennett!”
text: We had a great time staying at the Fairmont for Texas/OU weekend. Tony Bennett provided awesome service with a smile! He kept us laughing and helped us with everything we needed! We're planning to stay here next year, too!

title: “Clean, nice but not posh”
text:
Clean, nice but not posh
Pros
Location, nice staff, valet, clean rooms, good bath products.
Cons
Loud elevator, overlooked goodwill donation and taco bell.
Full Review
The Elan Modern is a nice hotel, not as posh as the photos may make it seem. It is a good deal for the location 2 blocks from the Beverly Center. No swimming pool, bar or restaurant, although you can order from diner across the street. We drove to the Farmers Market for meals a few times. Bfast buffet not too exciting, cereal, bagels, juice.
The staff was nice, the valet service very fast. We did have to move our room - it got very hot on 2 afternoons so they moved us. There are only 2 floors so it is nice to get in and out to your room. The elevator made a lot of noise.
We drove to several studios, up Mullholland, to Hollywood Blvd, and for our four days everything was pretty close.
If you want a very high end LA experience, this isn't your hotel. But a good value, clean room and nice staff makes me recommend it.

title: “Good for the price, 5 min drive from downtown”
text: Very conveniently located near freeway. Just 5 min drive from San Antonio downtown and riverwalk. Good service - the manager at the front desk welcomed us with bottled mineral water.

title: “Very clean & comfortable; excellent value”
text:
I recently spent 5 nights at the Jameson.
I pretty much hibernated in my room recovering from surgery and didn't want room service. I left garbage bags & wrapped up used towels outside my room around maid service time. 
Without my having to ask, they left a daily privacy bag with soap, fresh towels, shampoo & coffee outside my door. 
My room was clean & equipped with a coffee pot, mini-refrigerator and microwave all of which were very clean. There were no visible carpet, wall or comforter stains that are quite common in most hotels for that price level. 
All in all, a nice place to stay for a very reasonable price.

title: “Good business”
text:
I like this hotel, the beds are very comfortable, its quiet and mostly clean. The staff is very friendly and attentive to problems. The casual food however leaves alot to be desired, its expensive for what you get. There really isn't any other restaurants in the near vicinity to go to as well. 
My room had had some type of animal staying in it, a cat or a dog, there was alot of animal hair in the carpeting and I'm quit allergic to it and had a bit of a problem, I would have liked to have been forwarned about it, I usually choose to stay at non pet hotels. The convention facilities are nice and they are easy to navigate. Food again is marginal.

title: “Fine for business travel”
text: It is a bit tired. Cracks in the tile bathroom floor. Rust on the door base. Caulking needing to be done. Excursive room was nice. Up to date with treadmills and elliptical machines. I think room service and front staff were above average. Very nice group working there. It maintained Marriott standards with their bedding and pillows.

title: “Good value in the best location”
text:
We spent four days in a suite in Time Hotel and had an overall good stay. Rooms are pleasant, it is modern, well kept, clean and the staff is extremely friendly from the doorman over the receptionists to the cleaning staff. Thanx guys.
The hotel is located on 49th with about 100 meters to all the action on Times Square and everythings works to our liking unless for two minor things:; The beds are only 180 centimeters and the wifi (not free but try to get that in your deal. it is possible) is too slow. The staff is aware of problem 1 and promises that number two was being solved ad we spoke.
But apart from those minor problems (we're not long and we didn't go to New York to surf the net) our stay was pleasant and all went well.

title: “Great staff. Nice rooms. Good price.”
text: The hotel was great. The staff were helpful and friendly. The decor was nice and the room was quiet and comfortable. I plan to stay there again when business brings me to Jacksonville. I have stayed at a handful of these hotels and Haven't had a bad experience yet.

title: “Nice hotel, nice people, good food”
text:
We stayed at this hotel to attend a large ball in the ballroom. We found the place nice, clean, comfortable. During our stay, there was an Anime convention next door but other than the lobby, we heard no one at night. 
Good: Bed is comfortable, place is clean, people are nice. View was wonderful. Restaurant breakfast was delish. Next to all the major shopping, restaurants and WA Convention Center
Bad: No on-site parking and the place they sent us was two blocks away and $30 extra by the time we checked out the next day; no vending on any floor, only in room and the prices were very high ($3.50 for a can of soda); no free breakfast and the pancakes at the Daily Grill were $11 for a plate you can get at Denny's for $4; Wireless internet was $10.95 per day in room.

title: “Make sure you bring the exact credit card”
text:
Our stay here was okay- but it didn't start off well. We arrived late, ready to just crawl into bed... after a long day of travelling. I paid for the rooms in full before getting there on my MC(and paid off the bill prior to), and unfortunately forgot that credit card at home!
So when we got there, i gave him my visa for incidentals etc... They wouldn't accept it. He kept asking me for the other card, and I kept telling him I dont have it. He just shrugged and said "I cant give you your room then". He tried to give me some bull that they wouldn't get paid if he doesn't "swipe" the actual card"... Come on! Its 2012!
 Luckily, after hours of phone calls, I was able to get a friend to transfer some $$... The hotel would not refund me immediately-- and so by the first night, we had paid for our rooms twice ($600x2)
It's been two weeks since the incident, and I still have yet to receive a full refund to my MC. 
Besides that- the room was okay. The was a very noticeable stain on our comforter the first night, but I was too tired to care. It's evident that their cleaning staff don't have a "keen attention to detail", as I noticed little hairs on the sheets too. 
On a positive note, the breakfast was great. We slept well, and the bathrooms were great. The view of the Manhattan Bridge was stunning as well. Hotel was close to the metro, making it easy to move around. (Honestly, if you can grasp the metro in NYC, you can stay anywhere in the city... don't pay extras for Times Square if you don't have to! Taxis are super cheap as well. about 8$ from Brooklyn Bridge to Midtown.)

title: “Close to Airport BUT...”
text:
We stayed at the Amerisuites to be near the airport for a very early flight. And it was very close to the airport...5 minutes from hotel to departures. We have stayed in quite a few Amerisuites around the country and this one just didn't live up to what we've come to expect from their brand. 
The hotel was clean which is our top priority. However, this particular Amerisuites was a bit run-down. On arrival, one elevator was out so there was only 1 elevator left for the entire hotel. The room was a little tired looking with some of the furniture scraped and nicked. The bathroom had a bit of mildew around the corners of the floor and surround of the tub. The toilet and bathtub were pretty clean. The mattresses were a bit tired and the pull-out sofa bed was so lumpy and bumpy that my daughter had to sleep crossways on the very end to have an even surface!
The hotel was pretty noisy but I think there was a group of high school girl soccer players staying on our floor. Also...the hotel is located next to a major highway (281) and a train track. We heard traffic and train whistles all night.
The breakfast bar is usually my favorite part of Amerisuites but this one was unbelievably BAD. There were no fresh waffles and fruit as touted in their ad. There were only 2 slots working in the toaster. The orange juice was pure water. The danishes were moldy tasting. Generally, the breakfast area looked like a disaster area with chairs and filthy tables and no one at the hotel seemed to care! Quite a disappointment.
In summary, we'd stay there again if we needed quick access to the airport and a clean room. However, I think for the $90 we paid we could find something better in the same location and will try to do so next time.

title: “Perfect Management”
text:
I have stayed again in this hotel for six nights and every time is a perfect experience thanks to the General Manager, Mrs. Pollack, and her professional staff, especially at the front desk and the door men who are always smilig, giving to Clients a warm welcome. I wish all the best to this property and I will certanly go back again.
I will honestly recommend the Alex to all my friends.

title: “Beautiful Hotel. Wish I could've stayed longer!”
text: We stayed in the King Suite, which was gorgeous, modern & had plenty of room to relax & have friends stop by before we went out. The beds were very comfortable and the room was perfect.

title: “Great Location but Horrible Service & Fraudulent Charge on Card- Awaiting Full Resolution as promised”
text:
I will update this review once I receive the resolution I was promised by the GM. I had the misfortune of staying here from 09/05 to 09/07/2012. This hotel was the only bad thing about my first visit to San Francisco, but I thought that it would be the BEST aspect during my check-in with Edwin and Hugo. However, things went downhill quickly. 
I found that my room could have been cleaner. i really disliked finding condom wrappers in the trash can, an OB tampon wrapper on the floor, and a filthy rag on top of the AC unit. However, I would have let everything slide if housekeeping would not have been rude. I had called to request forgotten toiletries, and was given a stern lecture by Rimel once he arrived an hour later. I was chided for asking for too many items, but he would hear no reasoning from me. So if you stay here, be aware that they give TUBES of toothpaste, not packets. This may save you from beiing treated like you are that poor that you have to rely on the Holiday Inn to supply your toothpaste.
The preceding was the beginning of a downhill spiral for me & my family at this hotel. I spent hours dealing with management about the lack of respect that I was shown, but things kept getting worse. The slow internet was an afterthought for me when compared to the my dealings at this hotel, including my little one hearing restaurant employee Hector (who I never even dealt with) call me a derogatory name. Management (not the GM) told me "at least the meal was free" when I spoke of this issue. Itwas evident that management thought that gradual discounts would pacify me, but all I wanted was respect. I felt like I was purchasing a car when dealing with this hotel, but the product that we were negotiating was to be treated right. I did get the respect that I am used to from traveling 100+ nights per year once I checked in somewhere else. 
Three days after checking out of the hotel, I was stunned to learned that the night that was supposed to be free was mysteriously charged to the card. They went back on their word! I immediately called my bank to close the card. I finally did get GM Sheila Martin on the phone, and she was sympathetic and understanding, but also unaware that I had any issues. She did agree to refund my entire stay, and called back to confirm. However, the card they issued the credit on is closed (due to the unauthorized charge for one night from them). My bank said that it will not go through, and I have to give them my new card number. At this point, I only feel comfortable talking to the GM. I'm hoping that I can get this resolved soon, and will update my review once this is resolved. 
In closing, the only thing this hotel has going for it is the location. Any good experiences were mostly marred by the bad. As a professional who stays in hotels over 100 nights per year, I was deeply disappointed with my experience here.

title: “A few disapointments”
text: My family stayed at this hotel September 14 and 15. Kings Inn was a little on the small side but we made it work. The hotel was great about working with my family we had 5 rooms with 17 people. It was clean and well kept. The only disapointment was that there were no coffee pots in the rooms. We ate at the waffle spot one morning. The food was good, but the service was extremely slow. The prices were a little on the high side so we got fast food after that. The front desk was awesome the night we checked in, they were friendly and made sure we were comfortable in our rooms. The girl that was at the front desk the morning we checked out really acted as if she had better places to be than helping us and she was not really friendly. We will stay here again if it is available the next time we make it to San Diego.

title: “A must!”
text: You must visit Austin and you must stay here.Pay the extra and stay in one of the three pool rooms ,make sure to visit the Continental club!

title: “Beautiful roof top access”
text: Every time my boyfriend and I stay in seattle we always stay here. Its a great location for us with starbucks in the same building and a wonderful rooftop to see the seattle skyline. They also offer free bike rental so cruise around town. Queen anne is a very cool area with lots of restraunts and shops. My only problem with this place is that you would think they would keep track of frequent stayers. But i feel like our business isnt important to them. They have never allowed us to have a late check out or when we werent happy with our room we werent not given a different one. We keep staying here because its perfect for us and a great price i just wish the service was a little better.

title: “A Home Away From Home”
text:
I NEVER give a 5 out of 5 to anything, but after this experience, a 4 out of 5 just didn't seem to be enough. I had never stayed at a Residence Inn before, but this one in particular will be my choice for long-term stays going forward. 
The location is perfect: 5 minutes to Century City, 10 minutes to Westwood, 15-20 minutes to Santa Monica or Venice, and 20 minutes to Downtown. 
For those who like shopping (not a personal favorite), you are steps from the heart of the Beverly Hills Shopping District. 
There is not a great variety of food in the immediate area, but Factor's Famous Deli is a block East on Pico and it is fabulous, especially if you love authentic Jewish deli food. The rooms feature full kitchens (my room had a refrigerator/freezer with icemaker, a 2 burner electric stove, a microwave, a dishwasher, a sink, and plenty of plates, dishes, cups, glasses, cutlery, and other cooking accessories), so I took advantage of the quaint Jewish market (Pico Glatt Market) directly across the street from Factor's. (Skip the adjacent convenience stores and experience the culture of this neighborhood by checking out this full service, reasonably priced market.)
I've read complaints about the parking fees, but perhaps these folks have not paid to park elsewhere in Los Angeles. At $18 per day, plus tax, the convenience and expedience of the garage and its staff were well worth it. I gladly paid the parking fee and tipped the courteous, friendly valets each time. There is street parking very close to the hotel and the neighborhood appears very safe, so that's an alternative when available.
My room was immaculate. That is very important to me when I travel, so I was not disappointed. Housekeeping was thorough, effective, and almost stealth in their cleaning. Instead of just a "Do Not Disturb" and/or "Please Service" sign, the rooms offer magnets (the doors are metal) that read "Later, Please," "Day Sleeper," and "No Service" to indicate to Housekeeping when, if at all, they should service the room. On several of the days of my stay, I left the room for barely an hour (at different times of day) and returned to find my room serviced in an almost clandestine manner. I was very pleased.
The bed was almost too comfortable (if that is possible). There were plenty of SOFT pillows (I'm a stomach sleeper) and the down comforter was both cozy and light. The bed linens were nice and the towels were soft and plentiful.
The front desk staff was friendly and very helpful. I didn't call upon them much, but when I did, they could not have been more attentive.
I did not indulge in any of the weekday hospitality hours, but I enjoyed the complimentary FULL (not just "continental") breakfast all but one morning. In addition to the typical continental breakfast items one might expect, the breakfast also featured an omelet bar, scrambled eggs, potatoes, french toast, and a wafflemaker with ample pre-poured cups of waffle batter. There was so much to choose from that I could not bring myself to have breakfast anywhere else.
Overall, I was impressed, maybe even shocked, by the Residence Inn Beverly Hills and how much I enjoyed my stay. Friends in Santa Monica and Westwood invite me to crash with them whenever I'm in LA, but this was a much better choice for me. I have, without a doubt, found my home away from home in Los Angeles.

title: “Great Location”
text: Great location, walking distance to many places. Rooms were larger than I expected and nicer. There is a nice sitting area about 10 feet from bed. Only complaint was the sink wasn't inside the bathroom (So when one of us was up early, so was the other). Average Pool. Great breakfast included with the room.

title: “Service Prior to Arrival”
text:
Kudos's to Michael the electric engineer at Andaz. Prior to my stay I had call the hotel to ask if I would be able to connect my xbox system to the awesome tv's furnished in the rooms there. To my surprise I was connected to the engineer who was pleasant in answering my questions as I had just purchased the new Black ops game for my son who was traveling with me and in fear of his boredom wanted him to be able to enjoy his new game during our stay. Upon arrival my second visit I was greeted by a wonderful staff and once getting into my room I connected the xbox as Michael had suggested and it was a treat for my son to be able to play his game. 
That afternoon I had received a phone call from Michael asking how I was enjoying my stay and to see if I had any problems with hooking up the system and if so would come to my room to install it and answer any questions. How wonderful to be remembered and my request days before my stay for a follow up.
Kudo's to engineering......
Happy Holidays

title: “Hudson Hotel NY”
text: Worst hotel stay in NY ever! Room was the size of my closet at home. Did not get room until 6pm and wasnt the one we wanted.Bed was very comfortable. See through shower to bedroom. A/C unstable - too hot or too cold..Beautiful patio but closed in the evening. Why? Dark lobby didn't even look like a hotel when we got there. Strange lobby entrance, Not very practical layout. would never stay there again.

title: “Beat bed ever!”
text: The room was clean, and the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in! Quiet, no noisy neighbors.. Front desk was nice too! We reserved our room, and got in as soon as we got there... We thourghly enjoyed our night away! I highly recommend the marten house hotel! Awesome stay!

title: “Not so bad after all”
text:
We are staying here for 8 nights in a one bed room suite (upstairs). After all the reviews here, we were a bit worried and had double booked the last 4 nights, just in case. After one night here we cancelled the other hotel.
The pool does have a grimey line just above the water, but the water itself is refreshing, and we've seen the staff clean the filter and pour chlorine in. There are some dry leaves in the garden, but hey, this is California in July. There are squirrels and humming birds.
The room is clean enough - you get black feet if barefoot on the balcony. The sheets and towels are crisp and clean. We get service every day - they change the towels even if we don't put them on the floor.
The utensils, plates, glasses etc in the kitchen were clean, and the fridge+freezer seem rather new. The suite has a high ceiling and feels spaceous. TV works fine. We had a clogged sink in the kitchen, which they came and fixed right away.
With Graumann's Chinese 1 block away, free parking and cooking possibilities, I'd say this place is well worth the money. There may be other rooms with poorer quality, but ours is very OK.

title: “Best sleep I have ever had in a Hotel”
text: We loved this hotel, not for the amenities, but for the sleep! We stayed here 3 nights and slept until almost 10 am each day. I don't know how the room was so quiet, dark and comfortable in the worlds busiest city, but it was. As for the other amenities/service at this hotel? I really cant say--we slept the whole time!

title: “Lovely hotel, great staff, serious noise problem”
text: I loved the hotel, which is a really nice building, quite centrally located. It isn't in the world's greatest area, but that wasn't a problem at all for us. The staff were really helpful and knowledgeable, with great advice on the area. However, the noise in the evenings from their bar/restaurant is massive. With all the rooms opening onto a shared courtyard, which is used by guests from the bar too, it was like trying to sleep in a nightclub until at least midnight, with the bass from the bar's sound system going onto at least 2am. It is a lovely hotel, but I fear I value my sleep too much to stay again.

title: “Medium hotel a bit disappointing concerning services”
text:
Positive Points
- Perfect location (if attending to visit the National Mall and all related museums, memorials, etc.), also close to Union Station
Negative Points
- Location at night: unsecure walking at night + lake of night life and nice/reasonable restaurants (i.e. no fast food restaurant).
- Front entrance: noisy cars (radio), Valet staff should be trained on the how to present and be polite
- Cleanliness: Dust everywhere (in the room, in common places), dirty towels.
- Room: very old, cleanliness concern, old fashioned AC, blocked bath-tub, mirror up the WC.
- Noise everywhere: in the room, inside the main entrance (breakfast, bar, restaurant). Especially in the room: AC noise, door slams noise, corridor noise, etc.
- Old menu in the room (for room service ordering)
- No refrigerators, but an ice machine available 24h (which is not usefull when you want to store medicines that must be conserved under 28 deg centigrade)
Negative points linked to the boutique/us hotel :
- we must always tip everybody, even when service was from a poor quality
- Untrained waiters always refill your cup of coffee and glass of juice every minute: they do not leave you drink in peace and there is a real waste of food as you cannot drink all the quantity they are continuoustly refilling. They take back your plate even if your spouse hasn't finished, and bring you the check before the end of the dinner (giving the impression that they just want you to pay and leave quickly, and if you want a desert...it is no more possible)
- We figured out that room services can be ordered & eated at the bar for less tax that in the room..
- The Restaurant is really not quite: situated in the main entrance at the breakfast place (dust everywhere), the place is cold, noisy (during the week-end there are permanent in & out), waiter take people for idiot by recommanding beef when salmon was asked (see the logic). Food was not bad, but it's not worth the money regarding the place.

title: “The perfect place to stay”
text: I flew in town for a reunion with some of my girls from college and had the best stay at Jet. I was able to get ready in my hotel room and party the night away in the Lobby! This awesome little hotel is funky/chic! With super comfy beds! Right in the heart of Lodo, it was convenient to walk everywhere. I don't know what these other users are complaining about...The Jet Hotel is a fun place to stay and party! Thanks Jet!

title: “Columbus Favorite”
text: This was our first stay at a Homewood Suites Hotel and we were very much impressed by the small things that made a big difference. It started from the time of our arrival and continued to checkout. While checking in the clerk noticed my military ID card and immediately checked to see if the military rate was better it was and he changed to the military rate. The room was as expected and the bed was comfortable. The small kitchen area was nice but the fact that there was real glass dishes including coffee cups was most pleasant. Breakfast was also served on real china instead of paper plates which was delightful to say the least. All staff members contacted during our visit were pleasant and eager to help. At check out I reported a small problem in the room and was assured it would be repaired. We often stay in Columbus and we have several hotels that are our favorites. We now have a new favorite. One last note about a week after our visit I was surprised by an e-mail from the Manager thanking me for my visit. We will definately be guest at this hotel when traveling through Columbus.

title: “Very friendly, great staff, very unusual for New york, David concierge deserves particular mention .”
text:
Had a great experience in this hotel. Arrived early evening ,great welcome, were given all sorts of info and local magazines without request which was very helpful. Admittedly, they got our booking wrong as we had requested a suite and they had us booked in a regular room. they offered a room move the following day which we declined. Just as well, the room was very large, really comfy bed, slightly strange decor, but all the essentials for a really great stay, plus an amazing view of the Chrysler building.Also kitchen attached, very handy if only for enormous fridge.
Requested a few things for the room which arrived more promptly than lots of 5* hotels I could mention.
David, the concierge, deserves special mention . He really knows his stuff, has a great delivery, obviously loves his city and imparts his info with great enthusiasm and humour.
Took all of his advice and he didn't send us wrong.
Donald , the doorman, was also a gent. In general our experience was all positive, in a city where hotels generally offer an indifferent service. It was a pleasure to come home in the evening to a friendly welcome.
An entusiastic member of our party tried the gym and declared it to be the best he had used in an hotel.
Murray Hill diner around corner great spot for breakfast.

title: “Excellent location . . . . shame about the thefts”
text:
We recently stayed at the Times Square holiday inn express hotel for 8 nights. 
Th hotel is in a great location - 5mins from Times Square and close to the bus terminal and subway connections. Room was comfortable and we appreciated the free use of the ice machine on the floor above. Our room was on the 25th floor and you need to be patient as there are only 2 lifts for the entire hotel - even though there are 6 rooms per floor and over 30 floors.
Breakfast was included and is pretty basic e.g. rolls, cereals, toast machine and variety of drinks. Be warned to get there early or avoid. We had breakfast there on the first day only - it a bit of bun fight! The room breakfast is in is tiny and getting a seat - let alone a table is nigh impossible. We had breakfast out on the remaining days. Can recommend Balthazar in Soho - amazing breakfasts and we went twice.
My wife & I were extremely annoyed that whilst staying at the hotel we had items from our room stolen by staff. We informed reception on the first occasion when a brand new aftersun lotion was taken. Bought only days before our visit was £9.00. Reception said that they were unable to give us money to repurchase an aftersun but would add 10,000 priority club points to my account along with my points from our stay. We were told house keeping would be spoken to. 
A day later we returned to our room to find more items had been stolen by staff: a nail polish & sweets which were unopened. Again we indicated this to reception & were told the house keeping manager would be informed, yet because of the previous days theft they had added 10,000 they were unable to do anything more. 
We were offered to have the nail polish replaced but only when checking out & when we had transport waiting to take us to the airport. 
I am extremely annoyed that having returned home to the UK on Saturday 25th I am still waiting for these '10,000' points to be added to my account. 
Our stay was blighted by these thefts. 
From this experience we will hesitate to use Holiday Inn Express and it's co-hotels again.

title: “Best Ever”
text:
Three friends and I stayed at the Iroquois while in New York for a delightful week end this summer. It could not have been a better experience. The staff was so friendly and helpful. They made us feel special and at ease from the beginning of our visit.We also found the restaurant superb. The location was a plus for us because we planned to see several 
broadway plays.

title: “Did not clean room”
text:
Jun 11 thru 15-07
Reserved room on phone. 1st person was very nice, called back for additional info, that lady was openly hostile. Clerk behind counter at check-in was very nice. Hotel grounds and rooms were nice, but they did not make up or clean rooms each day. Had to clean the bathroom before we could use it. They made the bed one day. We had to take out our own trash. Breakfast was gone before 8:00. Hotel is switching over to time share, so maybe since we weren't potential buyers we were overlooked.

title: “Great family place!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights on our vacation in June 2012. It was perfect for our family of 5. Our room had 2 double beds and a pull out sofa bed. They provide a buffet type breakfast each morning and a snack dinner every evening with free pop, free popcorn, and even free alcoholic drinks (I think it was a limit of 2 each night). With a family, we are always trying to save a few dollars, and this place was perfect for that. Although the breakfast was essentially the same each morning, it sure helped us out. We even at the snack dinner most nights! The snack dinner changed a little each night. There were several restaurants with in walking distance, so we supplemented the snack dinner with tacos and hamburgers a couple of nights. Still, very inexpensive! The food they provided allowed us to enjoy very nice lunches out! 
The room was perfect for us. The employees were wonderful - very friendly all the time. Check out the secret lounge area on the top floor at the front. Floor to Ceiling windows and a seating area made for a very relaxing evening:) We would definitely stay here again!

title: “Convenient and reasonably priced for my purpose.”
text: The room could have been a little larger (I was running out of space to put stuff) but the price was right. Although the sign stating that one of the elevators was being serviced that week seemed to have taken on a semi-permanence and thus the elevator waits were long, this hotel was clean, desk service was fast and courteous, my reservation and pre-payment were found immediately and the place was close to my conference and the Airtrain station.

title: “So Happy no one like this place but ME!”
text: YOU have got to be kidding me........... The price is awesome. The rooms are CLEAN and amenties are all over the place!!! So close to the airport...........restaurant (24hr) next door...Great CT breakfast ... POOL.... HISTORIC... READ THE HISTORY...... free WIFI.. Boarding pass..... o.k. desk staff, but had less from the CROWN PLAZA..... Had an issue with the remote and it was fixed in less than an hour..... I hope you all stay away as the price will go up and I would come back and stay a week in a heart beat!

title: “1a located, friendly staff, but definitely (no more) 4*”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for 5 nights for visiting NYC. The pros are the excellent location in the heart of Midtown Manhatten, just 4 min walk on foot from Grand Central (and the airport transfer busses around- if you don't decide to take an expensive taxi to/from the airports JFK/ La Guardia/ or Newark. You can not only reach the Manhattan sights and shopping areas on foot, but are also well connected to other destinations by the mentioned Grand Central Station. The staff was very friendly and helpful on arrival and depart, the roommaids were excellent as well.
Now for the cons: you don't have to be in a hurry when trying to leave the hotel with the elevator. The 6 of them seem always to be very busy, so we often decided to take the staircase (luckily we had a room on the 3rd floor). Don't buy your morning coffee in the bar at the lobby- too expensive though good (did that on the first day), but rather in the small cafè on the right hand side when leaving the hotel at the exit/entrance 46th street! Be aware that this (rear) entrance will let you out all times, but not in before 9 a.m. and somewhat in the evening.

title: “Huge rooms, Great value”
text:
My company stayed at Hawthorn Suites last week. The rooms were huge and it was really nice to have a kitchen and living area so we could all hangout in each other's rooms. The hotel staff was very nice and helpful. They were the most accommodating hotel staff I have ever worked with. 
Besides being a 15 minute ride to down town, this hotel is a great option for a comfortable, affordable trip to Dallas!

title: “Loved the contintenal breakfast”
text: We recently stayed at this hotel for 3 nights and found the hotel to be great value for money. While the rooms were a little small, the great service and the delicious continental breakfast made our stay hassle free. The hotel is located in a nice area and is fairly central. The staff were very friendly and helpful.

title: “And a wedding too!”
text:
From LA and found the hotel on this site. It was FABULOUS!!!! The location, the staff, the room, the ambiance all perfect. We came to NYC on vacation and planned to get married at the City Clerks in Manhatten. It was a perfect trip and the wedding turned out great.
We are coming back every year for our aniversary and staying at the Belvedere. Had a corner, sky line view room which is a must. For a boutique hotel the room was the perfect size and the decor was great. A real gem in the city.
Within close distance to restaurant row and some great local places without the horrible crowds; BECCO and Amarone should be on your list.

title: “Best Hotel at the Airport!”
text:
I have now stayed 4 nights at this hotel and every stay has been top notch. The rooms are clean and comfortable and the staff is so friendly and helpful. The breakfast offerings are quite good as well.
They are not pet-friendly, otherwise I would have stayed there more often.

title: “This is a GREAT PLACE”
text: I will promise you that you won't regret one minute or dollar you spent at this resort. We went during a weekend that they were having a Junior Golf Tournament and it was packed with players and family but the resort did an incredible job keeping everything running right and timely. There was 1 or 2 slip ups with our tee times but they fixed them and we were not delayed in anyway. The food at the resort is really, really good. You honestly don't need to go anywhere to eat but there. From breakfast to dinner and room service, every meal we ate was very good. I have to say that we were shocked at how good every meal was because a lot of times the food at a hotel/resort isn’t much to talk about. The grounds are beautiful and the golf courses are gorgeous. Just make sure you have a lot of extra golf balls because you will lose site of them if they go towards the trees. And there are a lot of trees on their courses. We played 3 of the 4 courses and I think that one course that we didn't get time to play isn't as full of trees. Seriously, this is a great place to stay whether you are there to play golf or not. The staff makes you feel so welcome from the time you pull up to the doors until you walk out those doors.

title: “Good value with free parking”
text: With a web coupon, we got upgraded to a suite--large and roomy. All plumbing worked great and had hot water. WiFi not great. Room temp hard to get right, but had no noise from neighbors or the street. Skip the pizza and walk 3 blocks to Gino's East for great Chicago deep-dish. Large swimming pool--big enough to really swim. Helpful front desk, and free parking a big plus. We got a great car rental, so had the options of walking, driving, or a CTA pass--and we did all three.

title: “Great location, great facilities”
text: Booked a 1-bedroom suite: had 1 bedroom with 2 x queens, and a fold-out queen in lounge. 2 bathrooms and self contained kitchen --- fabulous for a family stay. Clean, functional, fun. Opposite Madison Squre garden, Penn station -- can walk to Times Square. Great value. Activities Centre staff could have showed a little more enthusiasm or entreprenurial skill: we would have booked whatever they recommended, but maybe they weren't used to our Kiwi reticence. Would love to go again. It was a haven during the 1-in-100 year blizzard!

title: “Great Chicago Experience!”
text:
My husband and I chose The Palomar for a long weekend (February 17-20). I made reservations online and made a note that we would be celebrating our Anniversary and coming from out of town (We live in Denver). Upon arrival the staff member who checked us in wished us "Happy Anniversary" and was very polite and helpful. When we arrived at our room there was a nice note from the manager of the hotel along with a bottle of champagne to celebrate our special occasion. What a wonderful touch!!
I can't think of one negative thing about this hotel or the hotel staff. Staff members went out of their way to help us and were always smiling!! The room was great - ask for a high floor - the city view is wonderful!! The location is great - perfect walking distance to shopping, restaurants, and more! We didn't eat at Sable, but we did stop in for a cocktail - AMAZING!
Thank you Hotel Palomar for a wonderful trip, we'll be back soon!!

title: “Great location, Great Price, Clean too”
text:
We just returned from a 5 night stay. The purpose of our visit to Baltimore was to attend a family reunion. Originally we planned to stay in D.C. for a couple of days and then stay at the Mt. Vernon for the night of the reunion. But, since the hotel prices were exorbitant in D.C., we stayed in Baltimore and went in to D.C. for the day. Our room was in a corner on the 2nd floor...very clean and quiet and a decent size. Check in was a breeze and the front desk people were cheerful and helpful. Yes, it is also a dorm for students attending the Baltimore International College; but their rooms seem to be on the top floors (6 upward). The students were courteous and created no problem for us during the 5 nights we were guests. The only negative was the cafeteria for breakfast (which was included). It was more like a soup kitchen, plastic utentils, etc. But, we found a great breakfast cafe, David and Dad's, just one block down on Charles Street. 
Teo Pepe's is a super resturant, 1/2 block away. It was so good that we had dinner there twice. It is Spanish cuisine. The chef has been there for 28 years, so you can imagine how great that is, knowning how chefs come and go on a regular basis in most resturants. We also enjoyed a local Irish pub, Mike O'Shea's, 1 block down Charles Street (next door to David and Dad's). Not only a friendly local pub, but the food was really good. We had both lunch and dinner, and except for the enormous portions, the food was very good.
Next time we go back to Baltimore, we would definitely stay at the Mt. Vernon again.

title: “Indifferent to poor customer service”
text:
Hotel front desk was not helpful and did not seem to care. Requested early check-in, and was confirmed we could. We had the most expensive room at the hotel and all they could say was the room was large and it took a while to clean. Three hours, I don't think so. We did not get what they promised and they offered nothing as an apology. Finally we got to the room and was assured the luggage would be 'right up'. Thirty minutes later I returned to the front desk looking for our luggage. No one had a clue about the status of the luggage. I found it in a side room--with no sign of delivery anytime soon. I had to drag it upstairs myself. The only save was the conceirge who assisted. 
The hotel was too far from the Riverwalk excitment, I would recommend staying somewhere else, NOT as the Hotel Contessa.

title: “Home Sweet Home”
text: As usual ,our stay has been very pleasant and satifying.Management and staff were and have always been courtious and professional.Thank you Ernie and staff.We will be back and continue to refer family and friends.Again we love the location.Restaurants and shopping are covienient.See you guy's when we get back.

title: “as expected”
text:
Check-in was smooth though early check-in was not possible this Saturday morning. Room was available promptly at 3 pm.
Had a wonderful lunch at the rooftop bar; service a little slow but food tasty, if a little ill presented for the windy rooftop conditions (salad lettuce blowing everywhere.) couch-like loungers very cozy for two or more, loved the Astroturf, outdoor fireplace a nice touch as well. Nice to be able to eat outside in December but this is a place beckoning for summer evening drinks.
We got a gigantic room (corner) on the 9th floor. (staff told us that the floor right beneath the rooftop pool can be rather loud at night and suggested that if we minded that to stay on a lower floor) room was decorated nicely, appropriate to the rest of the hotel’s aesthetic (white, yellow, grey). While it was indeed gigantic for a city hotel, the room’s walls felt rather stark for the size. Linens were clean and adequate the bed was mediocre. Everything appeared clean but the interior side of the shower curtain had 3 different types of hair on it before either of us got in and a remnant of unused soap remained on the sunken tub’s ledge. Shower pressure stunk. Entire hotel smells like smoke – even our “non-smoking” room and hallways – but this is a party hotel the place smells like beer, sex and cigarettes because that’s what a lot of their customers are there for. We were there on the day of the UCLA/USC game and a few rooms down from us was some kind of afternoon party that was loud and drunk. Who cares - they were just having a good time. Lots of mid-twenties guests this day.
We ate dinner at the restaurant. Food was alright, described better than it turned out to be. Bread was tasty and warmed as was the calamari. Vibe was very upscale, hipster diner-ish; though cheekily designed and low-light. Menu was different than what is online. Service was indifferent; pushy and hurried though only was at half capacity. I asked for two items from the lunch menu (I’m pregnant and had my heart set on the onion soup and onion/goat cheese tart!) and was told by the waiter, who didn't even bother to check with the chefs, that the request couldn’t be accommodated even though those items were available for dinner through room service. (Is this is a shared kitchen?) Waiter seemed to feel his only job was to deliver food not a decent experience. As we were leaving, we said something about the ridiculous amount of coffee grains in our coffee, even showing the guy and as he walked away he said “well, that’s what happens when it’s made fresh.” (?)
We pre-ordered our breakfast the night before; it was delivered exactly on time, hot and served with a smile. The prices on the breakfast struck us as unusually low for a hotel, ditto the meager service charge of $1.50. (e.g. – French toast at $7 and 3 Eggs, home fries or salad, 4 pieces of bacon (of ham, sausage), toast of your choosing, juice, and a pot of coffee/tea filled with 3 full cups all for $12!) They forgo the maple syrup and remedied it within 2 minutes of our calling to request it.
We requested a late check-out an hour before we were supposed to depart with no problem. (They moved it to 1 pm.) 
Check-out went smooth and valet was quick to get our car.
By and large, it was exactly what we expected. Great front desk service, sexy and thoughtfully designed room, mixed bag of food, and downtown LA. (Agreeably, much less pretension than the Standard on Sunset.)

title: “Super Hotel”
text: We were inclined to stay in a B+B but our daughter who lives in Seattle got us to come here. What a GREAT hotel! The location is excellent. We took the light rail in from Seatac (VERY inexpensive and comfortable) and walked 2-3 blocks to the hotel. It is what you would expect from a Kimpton. High style and personal, pleasant staff. The goldfish on the reception desk - Pickel - is already a sign this is a quirky hotel - in a good way. Our room is smallish but the size is made up for by very thoughtful use of space. We have 2 flat screen TV's and - A FIREPLACE! Not just for show. There is a duraflame log and box of matches, ready to go. The room is quiet and beautifully appointed. We'd be happy to own most of the furniture. (OK, my wife might not agree.) We enjoy free Starbucks coffee, wifi and the New York Times. The bathroom is smallish, but again very stylish. It has a walk-in shower - no clingy plastic shower curtain. Shampoo and conditioner are in large dispensers. I prefer the little bottles, but this is a small complaint. The hotel offers free bicycles, a lively (but not too loud) bar and a yoga studio is slated to come. AMAZING. The neighborhood is terrific - about half way between Pike Market and Pioneer Square. Oh yes, the room was quiet, even though it looks out on 1st Street. It's close to the elevator bank, but no swoosh through the walls. Incidentally, this is a side benefit of a smallish 4-5 story hotel. The elevator is always there. No long waits. So we're real fans.

title: “Fabulous”
text:
We stayed in the St Regis for 2 nights during a weekend. The reception in the hotel was as expected from a hotel of this class; the doorman asked our name upon arrival and we were greeted by our name whenever we left or came in. The check-in was pleasant, we received an upgrade to a suite and, surprisingly, we were brought to our room by the person who checked us in. Shortly thereafter the butler arrived to explain the mechanics in the room and she immedialty checked whether we needed dinner reservations (which she obtained at Adour, in the hotel for that evening). Throughout our stay the service was excellent. The room was classicaly decorated, very comfortable and spacious. Coffee and tea service was complimentary and apeeared shortly after calling the butler.
We didn't have breakfast in the hotel but had dinner in Adour (Alain Ducasse) which was excellent, both service and food, but what else do you expect when the chef has several Michelin star restaurants.
On our second day we asked the doorman for a taxi to the restaurant we had a reservation for, but instead of hailing a cab he called the St Regis Bentley for us; a very pleasant surprise.
The hotel is very conveniently located between 5th Avenue (corner) and Madison Avenua and 3 blocks from Central Park.
We have stayed in several other hotels in NYC, and althougfh there are many other cheaper and great alterantives, this was by far our best experience and highly recommended for a special event.

title: “Brand new!”
text: Beautifully designed hotel. Swarovski lobby chandelier, winding hall to living rm with fireplace and multi sitting areas with comfortable inviting vibe. Don't miss the complementary wine nightly. The room is beautifully furnished. Nice bar choices and cute rocky robe. Red owl tavern quaint and so is rooftop bar. Love this new boutique hotel overlooking independence park! Shout outs to bell staff... especially James and Shawn...really nice accommodating guys! It's the real deal here! Will be back!

title: “Cool hotel in Great Location-Fabulous Deal”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Distrikt for a long weekend. We loved the hotel. The room was a good size and we found the furnishings super comfortable. The staff at front desk was very helpful and we loved the apple cider they made each night (it was cold when we went). I would definitely stay there again.

title: “The Good and The Bad”
text:
This hotel is not a 4 star but still nice. It is probably more of a low 3 star. The hotel is in an amazing location and the staff is great. The staff makes this place, not the rooms or amenities. They try very hard to ensure that their guests are happy and will go out of their way to help you. This makes some of the problems with the hotel easier to overlook.
When we first arrived, our room was so small we literally could not get our suitcases in past the doorway. The bathroom was also very small. My shoulders actually brushed each wall as I walked in, it was so narrow. We explained to the concierge that our room was far too small for our needs and they put us a suite which had more space. 
The room decor in both rooms and the hotel was nice but run down. The wall paper was peeling off, the bathrooms needed some refurbishment, the carpet in our room had burn holes in it, paint was chipping off and the beds were very poor quality. Additionally some of the public areas needs to be cleaned up.
The hotel offers nothing in the way of amenities. They only provide soap and shampoo, no lotion, no toothpaste or other things you might need but forgot to bring. There are also no vending machines and no gift shop. The bar and restaurant are only open limited hours (soft drinks and water are $4 in both the hotel and the bar). There are places nearby that you can go to for necessities but be aware that they are not available in the hotel.
The Allerton, while it did not meet our expectations comfort-wise, is staffed by people ready and willing to do whatever they can to make your visit a good one. The location is prime, it is right in the middle of the magnificent mile and only blocks to some of the most famous Chicago attractions. 
The only thing we could not overlook were the beds. They were miserable. They were old, hard, and the mattresses were in disrepair. The springs had worn through most of the inner lining and they can be felt when you lay down. If the beds had been more comfortable, the other things probably wouldn't have mattered so much. 
Overall, this is a decent historic hotel in a very good location. If you are not too concerned with the appearance being a little shabby or the beds being uncomfortable this is good hotel. It is close to lots of attractions and historic sights.

title: “CHECK YOUR BILL & WATCH YOUR ACCOUNT !!!!!!!”
text: We booked this hotel for a 5 night stay thru a travel agent and paid the travel agent IN FULL 1 month before the trip via our debit card. The day we checked out we received a statement from the hotel for a zero balance. Three (3) days latter this hotel billed our checking account for the full amount ($712.40). We saw the error, called the travel agent, she attempted to rectify the situation, and this hotel charged our checking account AGAIN, for the same amount, $712.40. The Sheraton Hotel Corp. owes our account $1,424.80 and I don't want a "credit" for hotel rooms. Each manager keeps passing it off to another manager. Eleven (11) days after their inexcusable error 2 x's, we're still waiting for this to be resolved. The hotel management/accounting department is horrific!

title: “Housekeeping Needs Better Management”
text: We came back to an unclean room on our last night there. Beds weren't made, used bath towels on the bathroom floor...it was not something you want to come back to late at night on a hot summer day with 2 small children. A post-it note was on our door stating the time (10:30 am). When I took it to the front desk, he said there wasn't anything they could do since housekeeping was gone for the day. The manager never contacted us and NOBODY offered their apologies for the inconvenience. It was upsetting since this is a service you pay for. Besides this, we had a pleasant stay but it ended on such a sour note and it spoke of the level of management here. Not sure we'd stay again.

title: “Very nice stay”
text: I stayed here in a large, corner suite. The room had a large balcony with incredible views of the city and included a mini-fridge. The front desk clerk Onelea Green was great. Her and all employees were very friendly and professional. I had not visited NYC in 10 years and the stay here at the New Yorker made it a memeorable one. I will be staying here on my next visit to the city.

title: “Fantastic hotel - will def return!!”
text: It's all been said before but this hotel cannot be faulted. From location to room size, staff to cleanliness, everything just great. Although I have to say, we weren't in the room very much over the 4 nights we stayed, there's just so much to see out there! A lovely touch was the gift bag left in our rooms, this followed email correspondence by myself & Jennifer (Director of Guest Experiences) as to the reason for our trip to NY - very much appreciated! Bed extremely comfortable and slept well, quiet in the room but the odd siren screaming outside added to the whole NY experience. Location fantastic, we did so much walking but then started to use the subway just round the corner, day pass fantastic value. The female concierge (can't rememember her name) very friendly & helpful, booked us an airlink cab back to the airport, driver a real character! We didn't use the restaurant attached to the hotel but can recommend the bar directly across the road (Social I think) and also the Cosmic Diner ( 3 blocks up 8th Ave), real American diner with good service and fab omelettes! The Irish bar Hurleys (round the corner from hotel) also great, say hi to Mickey the barman. All in all a fabulous holiday & hotel and will recommend this hotel to all family & friends & hope to be back in the not too distant future! Well done Hilton Garden.

title: “Looked nice but the wrong crowd for a family place”
text:
Nicely redone and clean hotel but that is the extent of the positive comments 
Young family for an early flight Sunday morning and found out the quiet time started at midnight. Rowdy drunk 20-30 year old crowd having a good time but at others expense, not a good idea for an airpot hotel .
Had a large room at the back of the hotel ground floor by the main a/c unit and could not sleep all night as I could hear it start up through the single pane windows about every 20 minutes
Seemed like there was a gang element at the hotel (ie clean shaven , muscle bound tatoo'd young men driving tinted out sports car in and out of the hotel all night) Police showed up at about midnight on force to deal with some problem.

title: “Awesome”
text: Since the time we walked in we knew we made a great choice I looked for a hotel for hours online and this place was the best of them all.... the staff here are so friendly and helpful.... I would highly recomend this place to anyone that trying to save a lil money by cooking they have everything you need at this place....get choice so happy we got to stay....

title: “clean, inexpensive but ultra small beds!”
text: I requested a queen bed and got a full. After switching rooms I was assured the second room was a queen. Not sure where these folks got their beds but someone was fooled and it wasn't me! Staff was helpful, facility was clean, modern, compact and convenient but the bed thing ruined our stay.

title: “Great stop-over near the airport”
text: My husband and I had an overnight stop-over at Houston, and after reading the reviews here we chose La Quinta. It was a great choice in terms of price, convenience, cleanliness, etc. The staff is unhelpful, but you get what you pay for. (The first room they sent us to had other people's stuff in it. Oops.) The shuttle bus was full in the morning when we needed to get to the airport, but 15 minutes later it was back for another pickup. We still made it to the airport in plenty of time. The most convenient part of our stay here was the shuttle that took us to any local restaurant of our choosing for dinner, and then picked us up again afterwards. This was a helpful perk. We went to Pappasito's (www.pappasitos.com) and had terrific fajitos.

title: “Embassy hotel”
text: Stayed at hotel early December ,,was hard to find hotel in the city as there was conference on..looking at the reviews was not encouraging but at that stage had no choice,, paid 129 dollars pn for a 3 night stay,,location was fine as like most cities you have to taxi anyway,, I stayed on the 6 th floor ,, room was large and a king size bed,, very clean overall,,large plasma tv,, bathroom old fashioned but very good shower,, after visiting most of the sights in the city by day were in bed by 10ish,, slept well,,considering the price ,,overall happy and would stay again,, there is parking there but a small charge,, there is no restaurant,/ bar ,,price wise great,, location fair,,Liam Germany

title: “My new go-to in Chicago!”
text:
I've lived in Chicago and now travel there often for work and this is hands down my go-to hotel that I also recommend to friends and family. It's extremely convenient to all of the tourist hot-spots, clean, comfortable, very affordable, and with all of that comes free breakfast, free wifi, and free happy hour that includes appetizers. Need I say more? 
The breakfast isn't huge. Don't expect the big vat of eggs in the lobby. It's served near the elevators on every floor and includes juices, coffee, fruit, cereals, donuts, bagels etc. The basic continental service that does the trick for me! Happy hour was also a very nice surprise. When I read about it, I expected a tiny glass of wine in a plastic cup as well as some chex mix. That couldn't have been farther from the truth. They have set up a big room with some tall tables, comfy chairs and a big screen TV to make it more of a lounge feel. (This means that there isn't a hotel lobby bar. But really? People are complaining about that? There are fantastic bars/restaurants literally RIGHT next door.) The hotel then offer an open bar as well as a big spread of Italian appetizers - breads, meats, cheeses, olives, etc etc. You could easily make a meal out of it. I've found this alternative to be a great way to cap off my work day by kicking back with a free glass of wine (or 5), chatting with other guests and relaxing while not having to be holed up in my room alone. 
My rooms have always been very comfortable as well as quiet. I've never run into loud AC issues like another reviewer noted. It's true - you're not right on the river so you most likely won't have a fantastic view. But for around $100 less per night and amenities galore, they can keep their view and I'll walk the one block to see the river in the morning. :)

title: “Perfect place for convention guests!”
text:
If you are coming to San Diego to attend an event at the San Diego Convention Center, this is THE place to stay!!
PROs: It is just across the street from the San Diego Convention Center- you can't get any closer. It's bounded on one side by a small park and on the other sides by the famous Gaslamp quarter, complete with dozens of restaurants, shops, and other attractions. Room service is prompt, housekeeping keeps the rooms immaculate, and any in-room assistance is done well and attended to by friendly individuals. The rooms are comfortable, although the beds gave one other person in my group and me a little trouble (softer than what we like) - but the others in our group were quite pleased and comfortable. There is a good selection of TV channels, the bathroom toiletries are nice, and there is always hot water and good water pressure. Overall, we were very pleased. My travel companions also noted that the fitness center and, especially, the outdoor hot tub were great. On top of that, the front desk folks are helpful - best yet, the bell hops go out of there way to help in any way possible (truly, these fellows are very nice).
CONS: The concierge is not that helpful - everytime we needed a taxi, a private driving service was called (because no taxis were available?.?), costing us 2-3 times more than what it should have for every trip we made. That got annoying - although the driving services were impeccable. The foyer stinks - it is so malodorous (smells like a combo of feces and dead things) that one is quick to leave the sitting area if meeting someone there. No one ever answers the internal Guest services line via the button on one's phone (I let it ring over 40 times on numerous occasions), and it can be equally difficult getting anyone to answer at the front desk. Remedy (learned this after 3 days there): call the hotel's phone number, as if you are an outside caller. Someone, ironically, will answer immediately - then have the charges for local calls taken off your bill at the end (as you cannot be charged for using the local call line when no one answers the internal lines after calling many times and letting it ring dozens of times). Other than that, though, when you do reach someone, they are ALWAYS helpful, and pleasant, and ready to ensure that your stay is good. The food is overpriced, and not the best (adequate would be a good way to describe it - although the steak I ordered one night was good); with the gaslamp quarter there, you would be cheating yourself eating "in" anyway - go out and try the myriad of wonderful eateries just outside the door of the hotel. 
CONCLUSION: I would highly recommend this hotel if coming for a convention - they are perfectly located, and are very reasonably priced - and will ensure that your stay is good, comfortable, and pleasurable.

title: “Great Location in TIme Square!”
text: This was my first trip to NYC with my 2 children, who wanted to stay in Time Square. This hotel was great as far as location goes! Price was under $200 which was also great for the location. We had arrived early (1pm) and was told -after not being acknowledged for 5 minutes at the fron desk - that our room was not ready and that we could leave our luggage with the doorman. Apparently there were several people in the same situation because the hallway was packed with guest luggage! I thought the day front desk staff were average-not overly nice or helpful. The evening staff were much better! The room -we had a junior suite- had a queen bed and pull out sofa, was small but nice. Took forever for the shower to get hot water. The decor was modern, but could tell the place was old. The bed was very comfortable and the room had 2 flat screen TV's. Hallways and elevators quite small. I would probably stay agin if in the area.

title: “Good value for your money”
text: The Embassy Suites San Diego-La Jolla gives you good value for your money. It is right across the street from a mall, and there is a P.F. Changs right next to the hotel itself. Parking, though, is $20 a day, which I thought was steep. It has the typical Embassy Suites setup, with a living room, bathroom and a bedroom. Breakfast is free, and it was OK. I expected a long line for breakfast because we came down late, but the line wasn't too bad. I also expected the food to be almost gone, but there was still plenty left (We always go late for breakfast). We stayed when it was Orientation week for incoming freshmen at the nearby UC San Diego, but the hotel wasn't crowded - I had expected it to be full of students with their parents. Our room had floor-to-ceiling windows and the bed was a little high, but comfortable. The fridge and the microwave were very convenient since we had a lot of dinner leftovers, which we ended up eating the next day. There was no concierge but the front desk could answer questions. There is also a daily afternoon reception with free snacks and drinks available. It was also OK. Overall I would stay here again the next time I'm in the San Diego area.

title: “Great deal! We'll go back!”
text: I was nervous because of some bad reviews, but decided to give it a try because of the price, parking arrangements, and location! SO glad we did! Air conditioning worked (thankfully, since it was over 100 degrees when we visited). Our room was clean, huge (two queens and a single for me, my husband, and two teenagers). We were on the sixth floor and it was very quiet. Our view wasanother building, but this made our room extrememly quiet, no street noise. Room has an electric kettle for tea and coffee, fridge, iron, and hair dryer. Front desk staff were friendly and helpful. There are three restaurants and a gift shop in the building. Convenient to many other restaurants, sights, and stores. You just cannot beat the location and price! Parking was 15$ a day, as opposed to 45$ at another hotel we looked into. As other reviews mention, it is an older hotel (white and black tile bathrroom, slightly dated patterns on the bedspreads and rugs) but perfectly fine and CLEAN! I recommend this hotel for anyone!

title: “Awesome”
text: I was somewhat worried after reading reviews on here but wanted the full Elvis experience and thats what I got. Our room was very comfortable. It was double beds and also had a loveseat and a little eating area with a sink, micro, fridge and pantry. Very clean and no odor like some of the older hotels do. The complimetary breakfast was nice with gravy, biscuits, boiled eggs, cereals, Krispy kreme donuts, etc. I was very pleased. Staff was very friendly as well.

title: “Great hotel, great location, clean and friendly.”
text: We just returned from our second visit there. We always love the place. The location is perfect, central but not busy, a simple but adequate breakfast included, parking included, and of course a pool for those rare days the weather is warm enough to swim. If you like a firm bed, this isn't the place, but everything else is top notch.

title: “Difficulty @ check-in but otherwise very good hotel”
text:
We arrived at 2:45pm & I realize check-in time is 3:00. However, there were around 50 people waiting to be checked-in, milling around the lobby. When I spoke to the front desk clerk, he said there WERE rooms available but that they would not start checking anyone in until 3:00. Made no sense to me. We travel extensively & have NEVER had this happen, even when a flight has arrived around noon - nice hotels are always ready to accommodate if they can. In fact, last week in New Orleans, the Marriott didn't have room available when our flight arrived around 11:00 but the front desk clerk took my cell phone number & called me once they had a room ready around 1:30 - you can bet I'll be back & have already recommended this hotel to others. Back to Crowne Plaza SA Airport: He said they were instructed not to check anyone in early because they were at capacity & wanted to make sure everyone got a room. But wait, if everyone has a reservation - how would they not get a room?? I stood @ counter & my phone said 3:00 so I asked if I could check in. No, their time showed 2:58 - give me a break - you've got to be kidding. You've got families with small children, & tens of other people waiting & you won't begin the process?!! At just that time, another employee came on duty. He saw the lobby full of people waiting & asked the clerk what was going on. He was told same as I was told & the new clerk said, "wait, we've got rooms available & you've got all these people waiting - let's get them checked in". Everyone around front desk agreed that he was a smart man willing to take the initiative to provide top quality service. The others were just following someone's orders without regard to the negative lasting impression they were creating. From the time we arrived until the time they began checking people in, they stood behind the counter talking among themselves, doing nothing while everyone waited for them to begin their job. 
Other than this terrible first impression (& remember, you can never change a 1st impression!), the rooms were very comfortable & it is a good location - easy to get downtown to river walk & other attractions. However, if this is how they treat customers, I'll find another hotel when I go to SA next time.

title: “One of my best stays in my 4 week USA trip”
text: I enjoyed a lot my stay at this LA motel. It had a very nice room with enough space. It was very clean. Loved the disposition of the motel with a quiet garden and a swimming pool. Breakfast would have been nice but there's a Starbucks 2 min away from the motel. Even if we didn't use it it also has a washer which can be very convenient and a computer. Wifi is free.
