It is less than 5 min away from a metro station and if you're ready to walk a little you're 20 min away from the walk of fame.

title: “The Mayflower is fabulous!”
text:
I stayed at the Renaissance Mayflower Hotel (part of the Marriott chain) for three nights at the end of May 2008. It was fabulous!
Even though my room (624) was a little small, it was clean, comfortable and had that fabulous Marriott bed. This room was at the end of a hallway, with two windows overlooking 17th street where it was surprisingly very quiet.
Room service comes within 25 minutes and the staff were extremely friendly and professional, as were the bell and front desk staff.
The Mayflower feels like a much smaller hotel than it is. It is a beautiful historical site and if you stay there, take about 5-10 minutes to view the electronic slide show of the hotel and the events and history that has occurred there. It's located in the main hall way, down from the lobby on the right side wall before all the conference rooms.
The Mayflower is within walking distance to great shoppoing and dining. I recommend walking about two blocks west to Famous Luigi's for a great italian dinner or pizza. I have been there twice and I loved it both times.
When venturing further out from the hotel, the the Red line metro is a few steps to the left of the hotel and the Orange/Blue line is about 3-4 blocks south. The metro-rail in DC is a great way to get around. It is affordable ($1.35 to $1.65 to most locations one-way), clean, has frequent trains, the colored system is easy to understand and I have always felt safe on it - no matter the location or time of day I am travelling. 
On your next trip to DC, check out the Mayflower. It is my new favorite hotel in Washington.

title: “I Love this Hotel!”
text:
Sure it is old. Don't look for glitz or glitter. My room was extremely clean and comfortable. For an unexplained reason, the room became hot and stuffy on my last night"s stay.
Otherwise, staff was friendly and helpful. The restrauants are good but a little overpriced.
I give this hotel an excellent rating and would definitely stay there again. Thanks, Wellington!

title: “Watch out for Extra Person Charge”
text:
We stayed here for two nights this weekend using the NYU preferential rate for families of NYU students. The quoted price of $194/night (before taxes) was good for a New York hotel, and the room, although by no means luxurious, was absolutely satisfactory and included free internet. I requested a room with two beds since I was going with my teenage son. We were given a room with two twins -- apparently there are no rooms with two queens. Again, not luxurious but very satisfactory. 
We did the express checkout thing where you run your credit card through and the printer spits out your bill. I did a quick run-through before we left the hotel and noticed that we had been charged a $15/night extra person charge. I took the bill over to the front desk and asked what this was for. The guy said that it was because there had been an extra person in my room, ie., two people instead of one. To me, two people in one room is not a crowd and should not justify a surcharge. I told him I had been quoted $194 and that no one had mentioned a surcharge, as he claimed they had. This must happen a lot, because he immediately took my bill and credited me the $30 (two nights' worth of surcharge). The experience left a bad taste in my mouth, because it felt like they'd just tried to see if they could get away with tacking on an extra charge -- if I didn't notice, great, and if I did notice, they'd just remove it. 
Other than that, Club Quarters seemed great -- a good price for a decent room in New York City.

title: “magonlia hotel in downtown houston was a great hotel, girls night or couple night.”
text: roof top great!!!! the bed was omg sofe and luxury,night life fun and social, nice view I lOVED IT. i will be back

title: “Loved it!”
text:
We had three rooms at this hotel between Christmas and New Year and really enjoyed our time there! We had one suite and two standard rooms - though I wouldn't call them standard, they were very luxurious!!
Our view was facing the strip of stores and was gorgeous at night. there is a great Dean & Deluca wine bar, A PF Changs which we had dinner at, and a Dean & Deluca market (separate and across the road from the wine bar) which had fabulous coffees and cheeses.
the upscale stores were really nice, as was the movie theater at the end of the road.
The staff at the hotel were awesome and could not have gone more out of their way to make our stay enjoyable.
The breakfast room was undergoing construction when we were there, so it was served in a conference room, and it was just ok i thought.
Overall, though, we would return in an instant.

title: “Central location 1 block from river and Millenium Park”
text: I was a little concerned that our room would be noisy since it was across from the elevator and on the second floor. We were not disturbed by noisy guests using the elevator, nor did we hear street noises, aside from an occasional ambulance. There are lots of restaurants within walking distance - Smith & Wollensky, Mc Cormick & Schmuck's, Catch 35. It is an easy walk to Millenium Park and all the activities there. You can walk to Navy Pier, but it is quite a distance. The room was compact, but there was enough space between the bed and the walls and other furniture to easily walk around. Having a refrigerator in the room is a nice extra touch. The housekeeper noticed the empty bottle of Cherry Diet Pepsi and provided us with another one, which showed she was aware of her guest's preferences. The front desk staff was very helpful in pointing out local sights and restaurants.

title: “Very dreamy bed!”
text: I stayed here two years ago and a nice time. Dream is true to it's name, it is meant for sweet dreams... the bedding is the key feature here. The down comforters and Molton Brown products, including an awesome scented "sleep spray," were so nice. The room has black out shades so it was very easy to oversleep. Plasma screen in-room was nice. The bathroom was very small and overall, there was not much space in the room. We liked the lobby bar and the cool paintings on every floor. It felt pretty hip. Since you are really not in the room that much in NYC, it was OK to have a small room. The bed was worth it. Just request a room away from the elevator, which is loud, and you can hear it at night.

title: “Good group site”
text: Attending a conference with about 1000 other people. This is host hotel. Plenty of rooms, good meeting rooms. Some good dining nearby. Did not eat at hotel. Supurb room service. Room excellent value for price....and it stayed cooool.....Houston is hot and humid. Only time I left hotel was to go with group across freeway for dining. Really did not want to challenge Houston traffic. Would stay here again, but really prefer to be further away from congested places like Houston. Parking is secured with fencing around entire permiter, with only one entry in front.

title: “FIND ANOTHER HOTEL”
text: Most horrible disgusting place I have ever stayed in my life. For $90 I can't believe it. I've stayed in $40 a night places 15x nicer. Half the lights in the room didn't work. Mold in shower. Someone's left over food was in the fridge. So much dust. Absolutely terrible. Most horrible smell in the room. And they had a condom machine next to the lobby. Real classy. Hate this entire city. Can't wait to be back in Stephenville.

title: “Fantastic hotel!”
text:
This is the only place to stay if you're visiting Universal City and Hollywood and make sure you get the Executive rooms as the lounge with breakfast and afternoon snacks is great. Everything about this hotel is good - food/room/pool/bar/parking etc.
We ate at the bar on two nights and it was great and very reasonable with excellent service.
Buses to Universal are regular and convenient and we did a hollywood tour by bus from the hotel as well.
This really is 5 star with value for money. Oh except for the phone calls - don't use the room phones as international cell phones are cheaper!!

title: “Perfect!”
text: We started our 3-week USA trip with 3 nights in Hollywood at this hotel and I couldn't be happier! It was the perfect choice- the location was unbeatable, barely a 30second walk to the Kodak Theatre entrance, the room was spacious, the included breakfast had such a huge variety, use of the internet and printer were complimentary, the staff were so friendly... I will insist that everyone I know who goes to LA should stay here! :-)

title: “Better Than The Reviews”
text:
I was concerned about our stay after reading the reviews. My husband and 2 boys (ages 5 & 9) stayed here for 2 nights on June 7th & 8th. I was pleasantly surprised with the service from the staff. The room was as to be expected and the beds were not that comfortable, especially after staying at the West Inn and Suites the night before. On Thursday, there was a great happy hour because the Padres were playing the Dodgers. They had a hot dog and hamburger bar, nacho bar and salad bar. They also were giving out little soft baseballs to my sons and a Padres glass to my husband. The next morning at breakfast, they gave our son's a cute take home cup with animals on it (the kind you get with the kid's meal at the zoo or seaworld). That afternoon we were at the pool and the hostess walked around giving away ice cream sandwiches to the people enjoying the pool and blow up beach balls to the kids at the pool. I think they have gone above and beyond any hotel that we stayed at during our trip.
We didn't experience any loud noise. We were on the 2nd floor facing the pool. I would stay here again and I would recommend it to my friends. The location is convenient to Sea World, the Malls and the airport, however you do need a car.

title: “my stay 12-18th November 2011”
text:
This is our first visit to NYC and it was for my husband's birthday.
When arrived the hotel's computer system was down so we had to wait for a room to check into which staff was checking for manually. We were upgraded at no extra charge . when we got to our upgraded room it was no different to what we had originally booked! and we were put on the 37th floor.
the location is very good for all the major sight seeing attrations - 10-15 mins walk to places like empire state building, macy's, times square, rockfellars centre, 5th ave. 
The maid service is very good. the room was cleaned every day and if u wanted clean towels they were changed every day as well.
staff were helpful to an extent - we wanted to use their internet which was 6 dollars for 20 mins put they had no cards to buy if you wanted to use it you had to pay by credit card which i thought wasn't a very good service.
The convience service - mini bar, room service & spa was very expensive don't use it unless you are willing to pay over the odds!!
The rooms aren't sounds proof so my advise is to take ear plugs we did put you can still hear noise.
the beds are huge & comfy.
We booked through booking.com which were the best price compared to other websites even the hotel's own. the only thing we found was when we tried to contact the hotel via e-mail for an invoice for the money we paid we never got a reply from them.

title: “Attitude”
text: Some very hip and happening hotels are so hip and happening they forget that they are in fact there for the benifit of Guests. Excellent Room, great decor thoughout the hotel just too many staff with a bad attitude. I dont know what the man management style is but all the staff seemed pretty miserable. Everything else about the hotel is fine the rooftop bar is spectacular but again the staff attitude was bad.

title: “You get what you pay for! AKA "Rat Hotel"”
text: I would not write a bad review unless I felt it was absolutely necessary. So to avoid others from making the same mistake as I did I definitely wanted to publish something for everyone to read. Upon checking in, the room's tub had spaghetti in the bath tub, however that was not the reason we had to abruptly leave. While in our room, we saw a "rat" run by the curtain. Upon calling the front desk, they sent a man with a flashlight who informed us this was the 4th time however the rat(s) usually hide by the time they get there. The front desk did not do anything to accomodate us. Their answer was the Mgr. was gone till Monday they were overbooked by 6 rooms and had no vacancies. Whereas my reply was so you are expecting us to sleep with the "rats". Needless to say, I and my 78 yr. old mother checked out immediately. Staff was very unprofessional at all times. Rooms accomodations were not met as originally requested and even though you have a reservation you are not guaranteed a room (six were without rooms at 10pm in a city awaiting the DNC)! However, I think their add should include "Hotel Pets aka rats as a hotel ammenity!

title: “Best Staff at a hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Hampton Inn at White Marsh for 17 days on business. I have never been treated so well by the staff at any hotel and I stay at a lot of them. The front desk staff was great, the morning breakfast girls were great. That would be Miss May, Tammy and Cathy. Just tell them what you like and they will have it waiting for you. If you miss the managers reception on Wed. nights tell the front desk staff and they will save something for you. That is every Wed. night, free food, beer, soda.
Also if you need to do laundry they have a washer and dryer there for guests to use at NO CHARGE and they even give you the soap and bounce to use FREE.
The place is clean and very home friendly. They have an office space set up for you to use also.
I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great location!”
text:
This hotel was at 49th and Lex, you can see just about everything from there.. walking distance. And yes, I know everything in the City is pretty much walking distance... but you could get to TONS of places no sneakers needed... if you know what I mean. 
Grand Central is like 10 short-blocks away, Central Park, Time Square, Rock Center "Today Show", shopping and restaurants.. Cheesecake at Juniors! 
A bit pricey for those that want to save moola for nights out... but if it's just location you are looking for then you save on taxi fare in the end. Both "huge" Tour Bus lines stop right infront.. Downtown Loop , Uptown Loop, Brooklyn Loop... etc. So you can get just about anywhere all day (every 15 minutes) Even the Ferry (Free Statue Ferry) drop off too. And the cost is about $50 for 48 hours.... so good deal. The guide is nice too... lets you know all about everything and you can stop all along the way. Concierge at the hotel can give you maps and they were really informative with all things local. You can order tickets and everything right there in the lobby. 
The service was a bit blah... very clean, but I found it odd that I ordered things that never came (not charged) but in the end... I wanted it!! lol
The hotel does have great weekend packages so check those out before booking. We visited American Girl Doll store and they have a package for that (kids get a bed for their doll as part of the package - very nice).
Concierge/Business center access isn't really worth it... unless you want to just snack. ($70 a day per person for Fruit Bars in the AM, Small Sandwichs in the evening and various cookies in the PM)... better off popping by CVS down the street (2 blocks) for $10 to buy the same thing... And rooms have frig!! 
The only thing that was the pitts in the end was the Elevators... run so slow... small too! Floors 16 and above are the greatest... but you might end up waiting 15 minutes for a ride on the lift.... Not sure why (maybe one was out of service or something).. the place holds functions as well so they are busy.. I wouldn't call the lobby quite but the floor our room was on was very peaceful.

title: “Very nice”
text: The villas are beautiful, and the grounds are well kept. There are several pools with lots and lots to do. A dream come true for families with kids of any age. The location is central to all Scottsdale, Tempe, Pheonix attractions. The only reaso that I didn't give 5 stars is because we had some trouble with housekeeping. Still, this property is highly recommended.

title: “Quaint hotel, safe neighborhood”
text: We were looking for an affordable weeknight room while checking out the Nationals new stadium. The front desk staff was very courteous and helped us find parking, as well as recommending an area within walking distance where we could find a variety of restaurants, shops, and bars. The bed was comfortable, the breakfast room was like eating in someone's dining room, and we enjoyed the patio set in the semi-private front courtyard. Lovely walk through Embassy Row to get to Dupont Circle Metro Station.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
Fantastic location for visiting Graceland, but that's about it. Very little surrounding shops for decent food, soda, water etc We were told there was a Walgreens a five minute walk up the road which was more like a 20 minute walk..... and at night the area doesn't seem all that safe for walking. Front desk staff very unhelpful and unfriendly. We booked a shuttle to pick us up from the airport which never arrived and we had to catch a cab. The shuttle we booked to return us to the airport was 30 minutes late as they had accidentally booked it for the day before.... you think they'd let us know after we didn't check out and get on the shuttle when they had booked it for us! The vending machines were all but empty...we tried every vending machine on every floor (we couldn't even get a bottle of water.....even from the bar!) and the food in the restaurant was just plain awful. The hotel is far from boutique as advertised. If I ever visit again I will stay in the city and commute to Graceland.
If you do decide to stay there make sure and join "Elvis Insiders" as you will get a discount room rate. I just signed up in one of the gift shops and they honored the discount when we checked out.

title: “A good choice for DC”
text:
We originally booked into the Hilton in Arlington (way overpriced) and moved to this location on the advice of a colleague. Great advice. I've stayed at Residence Inns e;sewhere and they are pretty consistent. Nothing posh but very comfortable and that sense of being in an apartment instead of a hotel is great when you are staying multiple nights. This one was clean, the service was timely and the staff were great. The hot and substantial breakfast, if not gourmet, was well laid out and served and way beyond the usual continental breakfast. Btw, we paid way less than the posted rates and only booked 48 hours in advance.
Not many restaurants in the vicinity but the metro station is close by and we were impressed by the convenience, cleanliness and cost (great alliteration or what?) of DC's metro system - but easy walking distance of the Capitol and the Smithsonians. We were really pleased with this hotel for the price. A great value, and great staff.

title: “This hotel needs a facelift”
text: First of all, our check in was at 3:00 pm and our room was not ready. In this world of electronics, we could not find an outlet that worked to charge our cell phones and digital camera. The lamp in the room worked intermittently. The TV had a bad picture that needs to be switched out for a flat screen TV. We would not stay here again.

title: “Good Stay in Jacksonville”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this property June 2 -4, 2012. We were in town for an anniversary party and this location was closest to the house of our friends. The hotel was clean and well appointed with microwaves, mini fridges, and coffee pots in each room. The bathrooms were very spacious. Best feature has to be the full cook-to-order buffet breakfast they offer for $8.95. It is right off of I-95, one exit up from International Golf Parkway. There is a Starbucks and Applebee's right next door (walking distance) and a Khols and small shopping center right across the highway.
My only complaint would be that the front desk people were not always visible. There was a "Be Back in 5 Minutes" sign that seemed to be up a lot. However, if you would call, they always answered right away.

title: “The best hotel in Seattle”
text:
Having stayed at nearly all of the major hotels in downtown Seattle I was thrilled to come upon the Alexis. It has many of the unique and quirky touches of a Kimpton Hotel and more.
The hotel itself has a comfortable (yet professional) feel from the moment one enters the lobby. Rooms are all different but beautifully appointed and spacious The staff is first rate, and everyone I encountered went out of their way to be helpful. Food at both restaurants is outstanding and worth a trip even if you are not a hotel guest. And if you travel with a pet I cannot imagine a nicer experience. Front desk staff volunteered to babysit my lab last year while I ran quick errands!
The neighborhood is so interesting, a welcome relief from the big chains and convention center area. Yet there is so much within easy walking distance (including Pike's Market, museums, dining and great shopping). A great way to experience Seattle.

title: “Great free shuttle”
text: This hotel was very recently opened when we visited. The public areas are modern and nice. Our room had two beds, a desk, sink outside the bathroom and a big sectional and big tv. It was very comfortable and provided a lot for the space it had. The free breakfast was ok, but is all carbs. Hot options would be nice. The best feature of this hotel was the free shuttle. It will take you anywhere within a mile, which includes PIke Place Market. One night the driver took us outside the 1 mile range because he had no other passengers and we appreciated that very much. The hotel is walking distance to the Space Needle and Experience Music project. There doesn't seem to be much in the neighborhood though, so you can't walk to much else. The pool was too cold to use in our opinion, although it was a good size.

title: “Clean and friendly.”
text: It's hard to argue with 3 free drinks at happy hour, along with substantial snacks that you can make a meal of. On top of that there is free breakfast, free internet, friendly staff, and a feel-good atmosphere. At this location, it does cost $12/night for parking, but that makes sense given the downtown setting. Otherwise, affordable and genuinely all-inclusive.

title: “it was nice”
text: it was very good i licked it a lot i thought it could be nicer

title: “Great value, great location, great service”
text: We spent six days at this hotel near Times Square and could not have been happier. The location is excellent, although 40th Street still needs some work. The staff was friendly, courteous and knowledgeable. The breakfast was adequate and the 5 p.m. wine and beer on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday was quite enjoyable when we could make it. This is the best value I have found in NYC in a long time.

title: “excellent hotel”
text: i recently stayed at the sutton place hotel for my birthday. what a great hotel! the room was small but brightly decorated and artfully designed. the bathroom was awesome. the staff was helpful and courteous. the location is amazing i would stay here again and again.

title: “Hands down THE best hotel in LA!”
text: I was completely blown away by this hotel! From the moment we walked in I was in absolute awe! The hotel itself is gorgeous and modern, incredible attention to detail everywhere you look! It's not just the aesthetics though, the service was extraordinary! They went above and beyond when it came to service. The bellmen brought us whatever we asked whether it be an additional lamp for more lighting, extra vanity mirrors or an iPod player! The pool is another huge selling point! They had a gorgeous rooftop pool with a dj on Sundays. We ordered these gigantic pitchers of watermelon mojitos that were amazing, $85 a pitcher but worth every penny! Unfortunately we didn't get a chance to try out their restaurants but we heard The Bazaar is one of the best in all of LA. I will definitely make it a point to dine there next trip! As we were checking out, one of my fave rappers Rick Ross was checking in- now you know that's the trendy, hip hotel to be when you see your fave artists there! Now that I've stayed at SLS in Bev Hills, there's nowhere else I'd like to stay when visiting LA!

title: “Sheraton a Family Hit”
text:
Thanks to previous reviewers for guiding me to this hotel. It was a perfect choice for our one-night stay in Seattle before heading to destinations beyond the city. I took the advice of other travelers and requested a room in the new tower. My family of three agreed we were very happy with our choice.
The location was excellent, close to shopping and lots of restaurant choices. Close walking distance to Pike's Place and major national retail chains and restaurants. The rooms were modern, well appointed and impeccably maintained. Beds made for a great night’s sleep. Front desk was very accommodating about our request for a room in the new tower. The concierge was helpful in selecting family friendly restaurants
Our teenager was disappointed the pool was closed (but we knew that going in); the cost of valet parking was very steep and there was no self park option. The bellmen were a bit unhelpful and borderline rude. This was definitely a tourist-dominated area and not for those wanting something more authentic. Overall a real winner with our family.

title: “Great Option In Downtown Chicago”
text:
This hotel is the best option for a family visit to downtown Chicago. I have stayed in Chicago for business and pleasure, and this is my favorite place to stay for both.
The staff here are great, from the front desk to the housekeepers, they are all wonderful. The rooms are clean, standard Embassy rooms. The breakfast is great, and I've never had to wait an extraordinary amount of time.
The best of this hotel is it's location. You are a block from the Red Line CTA train and three to four blocks from Michigan Avenue. There is a Rainforest Cafe a block away which is one of the stops for the Double Decker trolley. For a nominal fee, this will take you on a tour of the entire downtown, including the museum campus, Millenium Park, Sears Tower, Navy Pier, etc.
Stay here and you won't be disappointed.

title: “Great hotel”
text: We stayed one night at the Arctic Club and had a great time. Ate dinner at Juno and had drinks at the Polar Bar. Atmosphere in both was great. Food at Juno was pretty good but we can be discriminating - really nothing wrong with it. The hotel atmosphere is what really makes it - think old gentlemens club - scotch and cigars. The staff was friendly and eager to provide help and advice on local attractions. Highly recommend.

title: “excellen Marriott Experience””
text: My husband and I have stayed at the Marriott Hotel a number of times, and once we discovered this amazing hotel we have never stayed anywhere else when vacationing in NYC. The rooms are clean and comfortable, staff is attentive and friendly and accommodating i really loved.

title: “Basic but Excellent: Aug 2012”
text:
I love the price, and the location. From previous reviews I worried about the A/C, but
it was fine. The windows would even open. A bit noisy when nearby doors opened,
but not a problem. It was very clean. Hot water took minutes to warm up, but I got used to that.

title: “Best service of any hotel I have stayed in.”
text:
On the Ave Hotel has selected the very best people to work for them. All areas of the hotel have bright, thoughtful, employees. Our family has been coming to this hotel since 2005, making 3 to 4 visits a year and there has never been a time when the quality of service was not of the highest caliber. 
It is located on the Upper West Side with easy access to Central Park, subways, and Riverside Park.

title: “Promising”
text: I stayed here a little after they originally opened. Booking was easy and smooth. Upon arival they told me they had lost the reservation. In the most polite way possible they explained the situation and gave me a comp upgrade for the troubles. The room was comfortable and well furnished. The price was fair and seemed fitting for the amenities and location. I would stay there again.

title: “Be careful!”
text:
We booked this hotel online through a third party website and had it paid for before we arrived. When we checked out it appeared that everything was ok. A month later when the credit card bill arrived, the hotel had charged us for the room, so essentially we were charged twice! I had to call Best Western and have the charge removed. Needless to say it was not an easy process. It may have been a one time mistake on the hotel's behalf, but I remember it almost a year later!
The hotel itself was decent - the breakfast was good, the room was clean, but the room view at the back looked out onto a construction site. I guess for the value and proximity to the airport it was not bad, but just make sure to check your charges when you check out!

title: “The Arizona Grande is comfortable, beautiful, and has wonderful staff!”
text: The grounds of the Arizona Grande are breathtaking and made me feel as if I was on a tropical vacation. I love all of the fountains, palm trees, flowers, fire pits, and well-manicured trees and shrubs. Our room in the Villas was to die for and with the water fall right outside our window, I thought I may never leave. The spa was such a relaxing, wonderful experience, and I love all of the different pools. Each staff member that we met was friendly and helpful, especially Ryan at the front desk. He was amazingly accomodating! I can't wait to go back next year for the fourth year in a row!

title: “Awesome hotel”
text: Not only is the hotel in a really cool building (an old bank building with the vault downstairs still in use as a conference room), but the room was great. The service was great, super fast, very friendly, and informative. The room was ideal for a couple with a child. We had enough privacy to be able to watch TV after kids went to bed. NICE!

title: “Good Place to Stay in Lower Manhatten”
text:
Reservations: easy using Hotels.com
Check-in: friendly, efficient, and flawless.
Room: clean, well-furnished, and quiet! Spacious bathroom. Very comfortable bed. Top notch linens and towels. Excellent bath products. No closet but nice armoire. Superb flat screen TV. Free high speed internet.
Check-out: friendly, efficient, and accurate.
Drawback: two elevators for a very tall hotel.

title: “romantic getaway in dallas”
text:
NO complaints about this older hotel: our suite was larger than one of our properties in Cali. The staff were attentive and the amenities were just right to make this a very romantic get away.
Although some of the facilities were dated, it added to the charm of the venue. We used the gym, hung out in the library bar, and enjoyed the food from room service. Can NOT believe that people complain about the location -- it is one of the jewels of Dallas.
This is one you will want to book -- especially if you have to be in Dallas. LOL.

title: “Good Value for the Dollar”
text:
Good choice if you're trying to keep room rate under $200 per night. I was in Tower B for 3 nights in early January for about $120 [er night. 
As mentioned by everyone, rooms are large and comfortable. Furnishings were nice and clean. Bathrooms are nothing special, but not dirty either. Maid service was dependable and friendly. Nearest subway stop is 2 blocks away. Walking to Times Square takes anywhere from 15 to 20 minutes. Central Park is nearby. Many sites within walking distance if walking is your thing. Otherwise buses and subway are close by. Good choice for the cost conscience such as myself.

title: “Nice little hotel with great location”
text:
Stayed here four night with my family around christmas.
We liked the Magic Castle Hotel very much. Everything worked very smoothly and we didn't face any problems.
We had asked for a quiet room in order to be able to rest out our jetlag and that was also what we got. The room was quiet, clean and functioning.
The best things about this hotel are location which couldn't be better and the nice staff. Our kids also enjoyed the possibility to use an outdoor swimming pool at this time of the year very much.
Their concept of complimentary snacks and DVD's was also very nice. At check in we received a list of snacks, beverages and DVD's available and you could ask for what you wanted whenever you felt like it. Quite a nice difference compared to other hotels whose minibar prices could be classed as robbery.
I warmly recommend this hotel.

title: “Average but GOOD value for money and near Union Square”
text: We reached the hotel via a shuttle we picked up at the airport. The shuttle guy invented his own tip but I guess he didnt get paid much so who's complaining? You can pre-book if you want but you tip for everything in the USA. The hotel was at the edge of what you could describe as a seedy area. If you walk up the hill on leaving the hotel you will be fine. Turn right at the first road junction and walk a couple of blocks and you will be in Union Square. 5 min walk. Great location. The hotel warned us that it was not the done thing to turn left and walk down the hill. That would be asking for trouble as the homeless frequent from there onwards. Go almost anywhere in the world and you will find the same. We certainly did in lovely Vancouver for example so dont over-egg this point. We would stay there again. It is less expensive than a lot of the other hotels in the area. The hotel is slightly shabby and there is only one lift. The free lemonade fountain in the lobby issued pretty watered down drinks. You had a coffee machine in the room with sachets of real coffee and could ask for more anytime - free of charge. There were ice-making machines on several floors which you could also help yourself to. The staff were courteous and helpful. There was an internet connection for guests to use in the lobby and free WiFi internet access too in the rooms. TV had very limited channels but do you go to San Francisco to sit in the room and watch TV? Hopefully not. The room was a bit on the warm side but the ceiling fan helped. All in all, for the price, you got what you paid for and it was fine. We would stay there again if we wanted to be near Union Square.

title: “good value, good place to stay”
text: Very good hotel - clean, fancy, best of all great value! We stayed 3 nights for $88/night. King sized bed, flat screen TV, free coffee/tea/water, free wifi, free social hour w/ drinks/snacks, free hot breakfast. We had a jacuzzi tub. I love the option of choosing what kind of services you want (ie: just replace towels or take out trash, full cleaning, or no service, etc). It saves them time and resources. All the staff members were very nice and friendly. Close to various highways for our day trips. Lots of places to eat nearby.

title: “Still a Classic!”
text: The Palmer House continue to be a classic stay in Chicago. The history has been well preserved but the modern touches are noticed. This isn't a budget hotel by any means, but the cost is well worth the luxury treat.

title: “adorable hotel, great location”
text:
what a lovely charming hotel! 
we had a big beautiful room, two queen sized beds placed at opposite ends of the room. the room was very bright and full of natural light. i loved the decor of the room. 
the bathroom, shower, closet (separate rooms) were also really lovely.
the hotel was in a really good location, close enough to walk to the attractions we wanted to to go to. 
the staff were also really helpful, and helped us after we had lost a credit card and needed to get a money transfer. really enjoyed staying here.

title: “What a nice getaway”
text:
My husband and I stayed her for 5 mights in May 2011. The staff were so courteous and helpful. We had originally booked for 4 nights and were having such a relaxing and nice time that we extended our stay by one night. 
I am handicapped. Our room was two doors down from the self-serve laundry room and only a few steps from the front desk. We were never bothered by any noise.
This is one classy place. The lobby is very inviting. There was food available 7/24. You ordered it from a computer kiosk and it was billed to your room.
I would definitely go here again.
Ice machines are located on the 3rd and 5th floors.
Nice little restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. A Goodwill store with a nice attached bookstore was in the strip center next door to the hotel.

title: “Beware of ratings”
text:
I'm not actually sure this is the correct forum since I didn't actually stay in this hotel because it was unacceptable from the get-go. 
This is advertised to be convenient to the downtown area, and that is the reason we chose it. I guess convenient had different meanings; it was at least two miles from any real central attractions and definitely not a place I would want to walk, even in a crowd.
The first clue was the general odor of the place. We decided to check the room before getting our luggage out of the car...good choice. We were directed to an elevator near the back of the property; the elevator had plywood walls, the call button was a screw in the switch and the carpet was dirty and matted. Upon opening the room we observed: dirty windows, marginal bathroom facilities, grungy carpet (I told my wife I would not walk in the room without my shoes on), the pervasive smell of mildew mixed with smoke (non-smoking room), and a general aura of not really being safe.
We returned to the desk and told them we wouldn't be checking in. They didn't really argue; it was sort of "Who cares?"
We chose this place based upon a AAA rating of 3-diamonds; I have since informed AAA of the situation with no response. 
My point is: ratings don't always tell the story. Maybe this will save someone some anxiety.

title: “Nice hotel, good breakfast, excellent pre-arrangement made for bus parking”
text: This hotel was nice, clean, and had a nice buffet breakfast. As a motorcoach operator, I see lots of hotels and motels on tour and charter trips. My The experience here was very good, for one they made a very convenient arrangement for the parking of 5 large motor coaches. They get 4 our of 5 stars from me.

title: “Well worth its TA rating”
text: I stayed here for one night while attending the RUSH concert in Boston Garden. On arrival at reception, I was delighted to be offered an immediate upgrade. There's not much more I can really add to all the previous contributions, all I can do is endorse all the posative ones. All the staff could'nt have been more helpful. We had stayed in the Back Bay Hotel back in April, but the better location of the Lennox was a factor this time. This will be our choice of hotel next time we visit Boston.

title: “Great for People and Pets”
text: We recently stayed in a one bedroom suite at The Benjamin and thoroughly enjoyed our visit. The staff were helpful and friendly, the room was the quietest we've ever had in NYC, the location was great--easy walking distance to Radio City, Central Park, 5th Avenue. Even the room service was excellent--I ordered spring rolls and they were actually crispy! We chose this hotel because we wanted to bring our two small dogs to the city--and the hotel was welcoming with 2 dog beds, listings of dog-friendly restaurants and stores, dog parks, and dog bowls. And, unlike some "pet friendly" hotels, everything was first class--so much so that we will stay at The Benjamin again--even without the dogs!

title: “Good experience,bad service at the bar and from housekeeping”
text: I have stayed at the Setai for over a month. We chose a deluxe apartment that was spacious and clean. We also liked the facts that the windows were openable allowing us to refresh the suite with fresh air every day. The bathroom has very large windows with a beautiful view. The only two negative experiences I had at the hotel were with the Bar at the lobby and the housekeeping service. It took the waitress almost 15 min to bring one soda and orange juice amid a very empty bar. We paid immediately and did not even take a sip from the beverages. To our surprise, the waitress did not seem to care and brought the check to us as soon as we asked for it. Regarding the housekeeping, their service is not consistent, with some ladies performing remarkably better than the others. Also, when I ask for the service, the ladies do not show up soon after my call. To the hotel management, please improve on these two points.

title: “Breathtaking Views with grumpy teens”
text:
My family just came back from a 5 days trip to Boston. We have been staying at this hotel once a year for over 10 years. We are a family of 5..Mom, Dad, 2 teens and a younger child. There is plenty of room for all of us. Each suite (all rooms are suites) has a mini fridge, microwave, sink, blender, coffee maker, utensils, glasses/plates/bowls. The bathrooms are very spacious with hairdryers and the living rooms have a large sofabed, 2 chairs, a dining table with 4 chairs. Cots and High chairs are available upon request. There Plasmas in both the living area and bedrooms.
There is no denying the hotel is gorgeous with the most breathtaking views of the harbor and city of Boston. The location can not be beat, as its literally 10 steps away from Quincy Market/Fanueil Hall and about a 45 second walk to the docks and Aquarium. There are many many restaurants and shopping locations in every direction within seconds of the hotel. there is also a convenience store located across the parking area (25 ft away from front door of hotel)
The staff is fantastic. The best Concierge staff in the city. Hotel front desk staff are very informative too. Housekeeping (I think the same woman has been there since they opened their doors), valet/bellhop (again, we see the same friendly faces year after year after year) are fast and friendly.
The one draw back is that the hotel has a small lounge and some entertainment at night, they do not have a restaurant (there are a million within steps outside of the hotel) and does not have a pool (you have full privledges a block away at the Marriot Longwarf Hotel). The game room is good for young kids, but my teens were a bit bored with it. There is a weight room and laundry room, both did not appeal to the teens. My teens spent more time down the street at the Mariott Longwarf than they did at the Custom House. My younger child had fun at the Custom House and got to play and do some craft at the Maze, their daily activity center.
I recommend this hotel to everyone. Its a must do at least once in a lifetime place!

title: “Great locations, tiny/awkward bathroom!”
text:
We only stayed here for one night but it was a great location. It is only a two block walk to the Riverwalk and about a 5 minute walk to the Alamo. The room was very clean and quiet - it felt like we were the only ones on the floor! The staff was also very friendly and helpful. The breakfast buffet is delicious - especially the omelet station!
The only complaint I have is the bathroom. The shelf for the towels was a few inches too long so they had to put it above the tile for the shower. I had to stand on the toilet just to reach a towel! Also, the light switch controlled the shower room as well as the area where the sink is (outside the shower room.) This made it impossible to go to the bathroom in the middle of the night without illuminating the entire room and waking everyone up!

title: “Nice, but...”
text: I stayed her for four nights in October, and was overall pleased with the hotel. It was in an excellent location, just across the way from Boston Common. Like other hotels in the area there was a charge to park a vehicle, so that was expected. I felt welcomed on my arrival, but was rarely spoken to otherwise. In the restaurant, I felt very unwelcome, which is a shame considering the price of the food there. I will say that I was disappointed in the free continental breakfast. With just some fruit and a few stale, quartered pastries it paled in comparison to free breakfasts and other chain hotels. Overall the room was nice and there was never a problem with cleanliness. I just feel that for the price I paid, the service would have been better. I will probably stay further out of the city in a more reasonably priced hotel next time I am in the city.

title: “Sleek, Modern & Worth It”
text: The rate was a it pricey ($160) for one night. we live in the area, just wanted to have an all girl slumber party. atmosphere was perfect! modern style, beautiful lobby, great furniture AWESOME BATHROOM! they didnt have 2 queen size beds available as promised and didnt accomodate us much either. only offered a rollaway. I complained when I checked out and the manager offere me a free night stay which I was happy about. but it was difficult accomodating the girls sleep when i expected an extra comfortable bed. it all worked out and the room/hotel was very clean. great location!

title: “Nice quiet place”
text:
Go down early for breakfast, near the time it opens, as it will get crowded!! There is seating outside that is much quieter to enjoy your breakfast. Nothing out of the ordinary for breakfast.
Good quiet rooms
The pool needed maintenance when I was there so I did not use it.
Parking spaces are small unless you park around the back of the building on the south side.

title: “A comfortable, quiet hotel in a terrific location.”
text: This was my third visit to the Milburn, and it was better than ever. An express subway ride away from Times Square and Penn Station, it's in a neighborhood with an incredible array of typical New York shops (Zabar's, Citarella, Harry's Shoes, The Town Shop) that offer much more than the more touristy areas. Check in and out are fast and simple, and the room was beyond expectations as I was upgraded to a suite. Free internet, a mini-kitchen, a working radio, two TVs, intelligently configured lighting. A rudimentary (free) continental breakfast could have used some fresh fruit and more healthy options, but it was a nice surprise to have it on offer at all, as was the hot apple cider discreetly available in the lobby in the late afternoon. It's a 10 minute walk to Lincoln Center, 15 to Columbus Circle, a real find for anyone who likes small hotels with big rooms.

title: “Overated-Never again”
text:
#1 rated family hotel? How? Terrible service, rude employees, serivce, small room, slow drain, non working windows, not enough coffee (amenities in general), charges for EVERYTHING, nothing was free but the internet. Slow check in, slow check out, terrible bell hop service, bags in a dissaray, could have all been easily stolen, very unorganized. 
Terrible experience, would not reccommend nor would I ever stay there again. Not even a bagel, coffee or fruit offerred for breakfast, and you'd think a family hotel might have a pool?
Never again.

title: “Really? People call about the shower EVERY TIME?”
text:
Be aware - if you book on a reduced price web site, you might not get the room you want. We were a party of 6 - requested 2 rooms with 2 double beds each. Got 2 rooms with king beds. Oops. Our bad? We did get roll-aways... eventually.
The room is fine - beds are fine...but we did have a little problem with the bathrooms.
One room - the toilet was blocked and would not flush.
Second room - the shower was impossible to turn off. Got stuck on super hot during the kid's shower - I could not make the handle budge. Finally called housekeeping who sent up a maint. man - he fixed it quickly, but said and I QUOTE - "Not the first time, not the last time." SO, I guess that means the hotel is aware of problem and doesn't FIX IT. Thanks to this incident, we were late.
The ice machines are not on every floor, and not all of them work.
Skip breakfast - the food is okay, but the staff is rude and has no sense of urgency - you'll see them texting in the corner - and when they do bring the food, they almost throw it at you... instead, walk over to the Europa Cafe on the next block [8th Ave] for a good breakfast and great service.
The walls are T H I N. We heard all people going in and out of the doors [they slam] and the man next door was having a great time with a "rental" - they were extremely loud...or maybe it was the walls.
Now the good part - the location is fabulous. Close to the subway. 57th Street is a 2 way street, so you can hail a cab in either direction. Walk to museums, the park, etc. 
The computers in the lobby aren't free, but you can print your boarding passes pretty cheap. The concierge can book anything for you. There is a parking lot at the hotel. The staff was helpful, except in the cafe. 
The thing about being in NYC is you don't want to be in your hotel room. I guess if you can sleep and shower, you're good - too bad that wasn't so easy on this trip!

title: “Rooms are inferior quality and poor value for $$”
text:
As former NYC dwellers and current, regular visitors, we really appreciate the small size of the typical NYC hotel room; however, the Hudson Hotel rooms are well below the bar on this scale. From a trendy design perspective, the lower levels of the Hudson Hotel (i.e., bars, lounges, etc.) are well designed and executed. I have always liked people watching in the Hudson Hotel Bar and I love grabbing a drink at the library bar. I'm sad to say that the hotel rooms don't live up to the standards of the rest of the hotel. We stayed in a Deluxe King room, which was uber small and poorly conceptualized from a functional design perspective. The combination of these design flaws made the room feel cheap and gimmicky in my opinion.
Pros:
- Hudson Hotel Bar & Library Bar
- Location, location, location 
Cons:
- Ridiculously small rooms (i.e., the upgraded room fits a King Size bed with just enough space to walk around the bed on either side 1.5 ft, I'm guessing). There also is a small writing desk placed immediately at the foot of the bed, and a privacy curtain because the hotel door literally opens directly to the hotel bed.
- Thin walls - because the rooms are small and there are thin walls you can hear people in the hallway walking and casually talking as if they were in your room. Not to mention what happens after hours with the inebriated guests return to their rooms between 2-5 am blissfully unaware they are waking other guests on the floor (and lets hope they don't after party in the room next to you...). Of course, this unlucky situation has occurred on two of my three of my trips to this hotel.
- Tiny bathroom (i.e., an estimated 4' x 4' partition of the room). From a design concept, the open glass wall in the shower stall looking into the bedroom could have been really sexy, but the shower is so small that the curtains from either side of the shower (i.e., shower entrance and 'viewing window' curtain if open or closed) literally stick to your legs on either side while you're trying to shower, so you feel like you're trapped in wet blankets during your shower. Secondly, the shower curtains are so light and flimsy that loads of water escape on the bathroom floor during your shower, and extra towels are not provided (two per room). Third, you literally have to hurdle over the toilet in order to get to the shower. Fourth, there is no space for your legs between the toilet and the wall. I probably sound like a massive person to you by now, but keep in mind that as a 5'7'', size 4 female, I don't think at my size that I should have to sit on a toilet sideways to fit!
- Bag service is a bit slow, but that is minor.
Things to consider:
- If you want a nice hotel in a good location, there are much better and more comfortable rooms in Midtown (even the Doubletree, Hilton, and Courtyard Marriott in midtown have nicer, larger rooms) or, if you want to keep the caliber of a nice, trendy hotel, there are other locations downtown that keep with the trendy vibe (i.e., Gramercy Park Hotel, SoHo Grand). 
- All trendiness considered, I actually prefer comfortable and functional rooms. So, from a quality of sleep perspective, the rooms at the above mentioned hotels are superior values for money, despite their mundane brand names.
- This hotel may be good for you if you stay in NYC one night and plan to do nothing more than pass out in the bed and check out in the morning. With the lights out, the Hudson Hotel feels more like a trendy college dormitory hall than a trendy NYC hotel.

title: “Perfect in every way”
text:
WOW, Great product, awesome staff. Clean rooms with nice furnishings. Very close to freeway and a quick jump to the airport. The best staff I have encountered in quite some time.
Highly recommended!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: Just like most other clients who wrote rave reviews here, this hotel did not disappoint me either. It was a very pleasant experience. I loved its location, decoration and kindness of staff. Upon check in, I was upgraded to a beautiful, large suit. Room had everything I could ask for and more. I particularly loved the location of this hotel. It is close to parks, main shopping and entertainement area of the city. Due to my jet lag, I woke up at an odd hour and wanted to print out some reservation documents. There is a free printer to use by the hotel customers. Staff was very helpful and nice about answering my printer related questions at 4am in the morning. I recommend this hotel for everyone. It is a great place to stay.

title: “Nice, with some minor problems”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights over new years. Paid $55/nite thru priceline. 
Missed the entrance to self park, and had a ton of bags, so used valet. Valet is $22/nite, self park is $19, so not a huge difference. But was disappointed to find out other hotels within a block or 2 of the hilton only charge between $10-12 for self park- Radisson was $12 for self park, $18 for valet. Valet parking attendant was okay, bell man very prompt and attentive to helping unload car and bringing us to desk to check in. We switched to self park for the last 2 nights.
Upon check in, we were given a room with 2 queens. We asked if we could have a king with a queen sofa. basically we were told we had the cheap rooms, and it would be an additional $51 a nite to upgrade to a king with sleeper. so we took our 2 queen bed room, and the bellman helped us upstairs to our room on the 19th floor (pool floor). 
upon the elevator doors opening onto the 19th floor, we were greeted by the most horrendous screaming I have ever heard. We walk over to the pool door and looked in. A large family had taken over the entire pool area, and were carrying on like it was their backyard pool party. Flips, dives, marco polo, screaming and yelling like maniacs. A small baby was floating on an inner tube in the whirlpool! Just a mess, unsafe for all involved- and no one else could possibly use the pool.
I asked the bellman if there was security to deal with this. he informed me that if there was an adult present, there was nothing they could do about it. He led us to our room down the hall from the pool, where we could still clearly hear the screaming from the pool. No soundproofing at all. Were seranaded by the pool revelers until almost 11pm.
Initial impression was that the room was nice, but nothing special. Basic hotel room. There was only 1 trash can in the room, and it was one of those narrow, art deco small cans that hold like 3 tissues, so most of our trash (our kids had juice boxes, toy boxes from gifts for the kids, etc) had to put placed next to the can. Room had a coffee/tea maker in the bathroom, and we used the tea bags, sugar packets, napkins, paper cups, and stirrer the first night.
2nd day, housekeeping came through, but left all the trash boxes next to the garbage can, did not replace tea packets, sugar, cups or stirrer, and left a sheled sunflower seed on the floor where there had not been one before.
When I complained about the pool and bellman the morning after we arrived, the manager gave us breakfast coupons for the buffet. The food was so horrible, if I had paid I'd have demanded my money back. Eggs were undercooked, oatmeal overcooked and one large lump in the pot, poor selection of breads, and poor food presentation. Even my kids who usually love breakfast wouldn't eat any of it.
Location is excellent. We could easily walk to all downtown attractions, but had to drive to zoo, speedway, and children's museum. Be aware, parking fills up quickly on game nights. We ended up taking a cab on game night, since we were afraid of moving our car and not finding a spot when we returned back.
We did order room service for lunch on new yr's eve- all of which was very tasty and large portions. We ordered 2 kids' pizzas (which were large and very good), hamburgers (which were also good, and the sides with it were huge), and the homemade chips with dip (large portion and very good). 
The third day, the trash was still not picked up, and the tea/sugar/cups were still not replaced, so I called down asking for more tea. Someone brought up 2 tea bags, and nothing else. I've had more generous supplies at a travelodge.
So as I was checking out I did mention my concerns regarding housekeeping, garbage pickup, and replenishment of supplies. Gentleman behind the counter (Jonathan) was very helpful, and took off my bill the room service and first night valet parking.
So our stay was nice, just okay. I would not rate this hotel exceptional in anyway. It's about even with a hyatt. Three stars is appropriate.

title: “Extraordinary service at Hotel Drisco!”
text: I had been looking at small, upscale boutique hotels located in a quiet section of San Francisco. I had read some of the previous reviews and decided to try Hotel Drisco. It is worthy of all of the excellent reviews. The staff was more than helpful in every way. As I am a female traveling alone, I am very conscious of safety and security. The area is very safe and I felt secure at all times. The staff greeted me by name and always asked how I was doing. The amenities were also first rate. But the most impressive aspect of the hotel was the personalized service. All requests were met with a smile and without question from making restaurant reservations to small room repairs. One of the faucets in the bathroom was not functioning properly and I informed the front desk. I expected to have a washer replaced, but instead received a completely new faucet set. The breakfast that is provided was quite enough to satisfy my needs and very tasty. The only thing that people should be aware of is the only parking is on the street and is restricted during the day. I had no problem finding a space in the evening though. The Hotel Drisco was a great place and a great alternative to the large, somewhat impersonal hotels and I would stay there again without hesitation.

title: “Walking Distance to Freedom Trail”
text: We drove from VA and went up to see the NCAA Lacrosse Championships at Gillette Stadium. Got the Hotwire room on the 4th Fl, across the street from the fire station, so sometimes you'll hear the sirens in the middle of the night. Room was clean, fine for us since we were never in the hotel except to sleep. Valet parking was $40 for 24 hours so be prepared to pay. Gillette was about 25 miles away and you have to go on a main thoroughfare so if it's rush hour, make time to go there. Freedom Trail is within waling distance, be prepared to walk alot, or take a taxi back from Bunker Hill back to hotel. It's also down the street from the Children's Museum. Hotel is pricey but clean and modern so if you just want a posh stay at a cheap price go to Hotwire or Priceline.

title: “Absolutely fabulous in every way possible”
text:
We stayed at the Four Seasons after our trip to NYC was derailed by Hurricane Irene. From the moment we arrived, we were made to feel welcome. The staff were friendly and engaging. No snobbishness here!
On our last night, we asked about a late checkout and were given until 4pm. That allowed us to explore for the day and freshen up before our flight home.
The concierge team were full of great advice and information. Loved the extra discount at Bloomingdales!
We look forward to visiting again!

title: “Very nice rooms”
text: Stayed here during the Christmas-New Years hiatus (only 20 rooms filled?), but also means I got a killer rate ($67/night). Rooms were very clean & nicely decorated. Flat screen w/HD. Only one regular & one decaf cup/room, but full service Starbucks is available in the lobby. Unfortunately Starbucks & other food is a la carte, but I'd rather pay for good coffee & pass on a lousy free breakfast. Nice lobby & family enjoyed the small fitness center & pool. Friendly staff. Could be noisy so ask for a room away from freeway.

title: “They Still Have BedBugs And They Don't Care!!!”
text: 1/22/12 we stayed there so we could attend a concert where one of our best friends was being honored on stage as a marine. He booked this hotel for us thinking it would be a blast for our children. Bless his heart, he could only have known what a D U M P this place is if he had read the reviews. We brough two babysitters with us to stay with our children so we could attend this very important event. We got text messages from them around midnight that they had bed bugs all over their bed. They went downstairs and they switched their rooms and offered to do nothing else. Once we got back to the hotel we were too tired to deal with the managers so we figured we'd take care of it in the morning. First of all...Beverly...who everyone is saying so so rude...is still there. Run Fast if you ever have to deal with her. And when you find bedbugs. Take pictures of them because they will "send someone up" to "take everything down" and look for them and "call you the next day" Our babysitters killed one of the bed bugs and left it on a note in the room so they would see it. What happened? "Oh, we didn't find anything." They didn't find the note or the several bed bugs!?! REALLY? And the towel situation in the water park? I had a freezing cold 11 month old baby who desperately needed a towel and I was told there would be none for 20 Freaking minutes! If they gave a crap about anything...someone would be running to a room to grab a towel for my poor baby. The water was freezing and tubes should be treated like Gold because there are definetely not even close to enough to go around. Even the bartender there complained to us about what a dump it was and compared it to a crappy Holiday Inn. The trash in the waterpark was very accurate as well. And by trash I mean more than just garbage. So what happened after complaining about all of this stuff? Absolutely nothing. No refund. Nothing. They basically told us we lied about the bed bugs. As plenty of others have said - Do not go there even if someone offered it to you for free!!! They do not care about anything! How are they still in business?! I wish I would've read these reviews before we went!!! The only decent employee is the bartender! And he hates it just as much as you will!!

title: “Excellent Hotel Close To Washington Convention Center”
text:
The Renaissance is just across the street from the Washington Convention Center and surrounded by great restaurants and just a few blocks to the Capitol, Monuments and White House. I stayed here for a convention, the check-in process was smooth and the front desk staff were very welcoming and friendly. The hotel has lots of great restaurants and a full service Starbucks with breakfast sandwiches (important to those who love Starbucks). The hotel is just finishing up some room remodeling on the 2nd and 3rd floor. I had one of the new rooms and they are beautiful. It was a good mix of modern design and good desk space for working. As a Marriott Gold, I had access to the concierge lounge which was very nice, well decorated and had lots of seats and table areas. It's a large lounge. The food was average to meet what most in the U.S. expect. The disappointment were the little touches, like the coffee wasn't all that tasty, the eggs had an odd powder taste and the cold cereals were all from mass dispensers like those found at a Fairfield Inn. Where are the little individual boxes of cereal? It would also be good for the hotel to provide a little more training for the ladies working in the lounge. The atmosphere should be one of high service and professionalism. Instead, the wait staff slammed dishes into grey dirty dish bins which sounded more like a Denny's restaurant. The waitress at breakfast had a massive set of keys on a key ring that sounded like a team of Clydesdales walking through the lounge. Lose the keys and gently place the dirty dishes in the bin. 
You will love the service in the rest of the hotel. The front desk, the bar, restaurants and even the Starbucks are all very professional. The hotel is beautiful and I liked all the seating areas in the lobby. 
I highly recommend this hotel and will be back.

title: “My Favorite Hotel in Westwood”
text: I have stayed at the Hotel Palomar many times on business and can say that they go above and beyond to make you feel welcome. Everyone on the staff from the valets to the front desk is always very attentive and treats you like a valued guest. I love their daily wine hour, a great way to relax after work. The restaurant, Blvd. 16 serves excellent food, as good or better than most others in Westwood. The rooms are a little on the small side, but the decor is hip. The double rooms on the south side have great views over the city and the coast. The location is convenient to both Westwood and Century City. Only one negative, valet parking is expensive, and there is no street parking.

title: “Great spot”
text:
My family stayed here 10 nights over the Christmas New Year holiday period and wanted some space and quiet if possible. After various discussions with Nadia in reservations we took two rooms being a studio with kitchenette and a deluxe Queen.
Both rooms were exactly as described. My husband and I had a corner deluxe queen which was a great size with study alcove and room for a sofa. The bathroom though, was extremely small and tight. If you are a large person you may have some difficulty. We still loved the room and it was probably as quiet as you can get for midtown New York.
My two adult children had the studio with kitchenette which was small but serviceable. Their bathroom was slightly larger than ours.
I believe since the renovations that some rooms can be different, as in some studios with kitchenettes are larger and have dishwashers. 
The staff were terrific in providing the extra services such as pillow choice, DVD player etc., 
though it was a bit of a pain not having free wi-fi you just have to go across the road to use Starbucks wi-fi.
The hotel concierge does have a dedicated computer for flight bookings confirmation and printing which has no charges.
We wanted a hotel that was close to everything and that's what we got. We were able to catch a train from Newark and JFK to Penn Station and just walk across the road to the hotel.
 It is noisy in this area but that is to be expected and you do get used to it. 
We walked everywhere and felt safe at all times even with all the spruikers outside Madison Square Gardens selling tickets. 
If you want quintessential New York this is it.

title: “Union Square Gem”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Orchard for four days on vacation. It's clean, quiet and modern. Our room faced Bush St., which is very busy; however, we were on the top (10th) floor and traffic noise was minimal.
The location can't be beat. It's near Union Square and Chinatown, at the intersection of Bush and Powell Streets. It's six blocks uphill from the Powell St. cable car turnaround and two blocks from the Chinatown Gate on Bush and Grant.
My only negative comments about the hotel are that there was no microwave oven in our room, and that the mini-bar (fridge) was packed with way-overpriced drinks and snacks. There are no guest vending machines in the hotel, but there is a 24-hour Walgreens one block away on Powell and Sutter. Resist the urge to pop open a $2.50 can of Diet Pepsi and walk two minutes to Walgreens where you can buy one for less than a dollar. And it's California, so you can buy beer, wine and hard booze there too if that's your thing.
There is a restaurant in the hotel. It's called the Daffodil, and we ate breakfast there one morning. One word: Overpriced. $34 for mediocre fare that we could have gotten for less than half that price at Denny's, and it would have been far better. I mean, $3 for a (small) cup of tea? Gimme a break. 
For dinner, cross the street and go to Uncle Vito's Pizzeria. I'm Italian, so trust me on this - that was some wicked good pizza. We had enough left over for breakfast the next morning and it cost only $25.

title: “Great stay”
text:
This is beautiful, luxurious hotel and property. I had a room overlooking the 18th green, which provided beautiful scenery. The room was very plush - plenty of pillows, comfy mattress and nice linens. Big executive desk to work at, and a comfy chair with blanket to get cozy and watch TV. Bathroom is huge, and included a stall shower and soaking tub. Turn down service with chocolates were a plus.
We were at a conference, so buffets were the meals, but everything was cooked well and at the appropriate temperature. There are 2 different bars - one right in the lobby, and one at the far end of the hotel in "The Gallery" restaurant. Service in all areas of the hotel was terrific. The fitness center was one of the better ones I have seen. At least 3 treadmills, 4 elliptical machines and a few bikes for cardio. Weight machines, and then plenty of space and yoga mats if you wanted to do your own stretching. Hotel also has a spa but I didn't have a chance to use any of these services.
The only weirdness about the hotel is it's location. It's about 20 minutes away from the airport, but it is in the middle of a corporate business park area, surrounded by office buildings. There is a small shopping center nearby but from what I could tell it had just a few stores like a drug store and a Five Guys. 
Otherwise, it was a great stay at the Ballantyne.

title: “This is definitely not a "Skid Row" hotel!!!”
text:
This is a very old and colorful area. Yesler Way where this hotel is location is on the original skid row. This was orginally a muddy road that logs were dragged (skidded) up to get to Yesler's mill. Thus, the term skid row was was given to this area. Loggers and millworkers being lonely at times liked to frequent the business that sprung up around this area. They also got a bit thirsty!!! 
I previously lived in Seattle for about 15 years. I rode or walked by the hotel several times and never gave it a thought. Was looking for a hotel close to the train station, by the bus stop, and close to the waterfront. You step out the door of the hotel and turn left walk about a block and your at the ferry terminal on the waterfront. You walk out the hotel door and practically next door is the bus stop for FREE bus service within the Downtown core. 
The Klondike Gold Rush museum is also in the area. They sometimes offer free walking tours that include a trip to the top of the Smith Tower (originally the tallest building on the West Coast). If you walk north up 1st Ave about 6-7 blocks & at the Seattle Art Museum (SAM) and the Pike Place Market. 
The rooms were small, but the hotel was built in the early 1900. The room was immaculate, and because of something we were given an upgrade to a deluxe room with city view. We got in about 9pm and walked to the waterfront. Ivars is open until late. We found a really good deal. They extend their Happy Hour on Fridays til closing. Well drinks, wine are $3.00. Limited menu but I got fried oysters for $4.95, can get Fish & chips also for 4.95 with view table looking out as the ferry terminal. 
We will definely recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to Seattle. The most beautiful city on the planet!!!!!

title: “The New York City Experience”
text: If you cannot climb stairs, look elsewhere. If you must have a closet, ironing board, desk and easy chair in the room, look elsewhere. But if you want to feel like you are staying in a friend's apartment in NYC, with windows that open to the street sounds and fresh air; if you want a friendly, helpful, professional staff; if you want to be right at a subway stop for easy access to everything the city has to offer...try the Marrakech. The rooms are clean and the bed is comfortable. The price is right. The staff will lock up your luggage for safety on your last day of exploring the city, tote the heavy stuff downstairs for you, and they will hail you a cab when it's time to depart. The only negative was the hot water...it disappeared. But if you wait until the adjacent room isn't running the shower, the hot is plentiful again. Altogether an enjoyable stay.

title: “Horrible service!!!!!!!!!!”
text:
For starters I would never stay at this hotel ever again. We went to check in Friday afternoon at 1PM and didn't end up getting a room until 10PM that night. They kept giving a handful of customers the excuse that the rooms aren't ready yet and needed to be cleaned and the cleaning staff went home for the night. This is after 7PM at night!!!! What have these people been doing all day????????? We were suppose to get 2 rooms with 2 doubles beds in each but they only gave us 2 rooms with 1 king bed in each. We had to sleep three people to a bed....tons of fun let me tell you! The bathroom was the size of a small closet and the toliet seat had dried paint and glue stains all over it, not to mention the mold in the shower. A receptionist by the name of Kathy was probably the rudest women I have ever met. She looks like a sweet grandma but don't let that fool you. She turned her back and walked into the back office area three times while I was talking to her trying to get our rooms straightened out. The 2 dozen or so people waiting in the lobby were all irrate at the horrible service and [--] these people were trying to feed us. I have honestly never seen something like this in my life! I can understand your 1 disgrunted customer, but not 2 dozen all at the same time. I was waiting for a fight to break out there was so much yelling and frustration in that place.
I wish I would have read previous reviews before staying here. These people are right about the rude service.

title: “Great spot in Seatac”
text: We stayed here for several nights, partly on business. It is incredibly conveniently located close to Seatac Airport: five minutes away from the airport, and you would hardly know it. It is a sprawling, spacious lodge/resort, with good rooms, comfortable beds, and a quiet environment. The breakfast included in our stay was outstanding – continental but much more than adequate. The fitness centre was one of the best I have used. The natural wood everywhere – panelling, posts and beams – really adds warmth to the décor. If you have to stay in Seatac, then it is hard to imagine a better location.

title: “Could've been okay, but turned out terribly.”
text:
I'll start with the good things: The bed was very comfortable. The room was very clean. The bathtub was outdated, but large. The lobby was beautiful, and the bar was good.
And now the bad: The room was a shoebox, and based on the floorplan stuck to the bathroom wall (fire routes), it was easy to see we had the smallest room on the floor. We asked for 1 King bed, and got 1 Queen bed. The bed had only a fitted sheet and a duvet - no top sheet, no blanket. Fortunately, we managed to find a bag in the closet containing the missing sheet and blanket. Unfortunately, we really didn't need it, as the thermostat seemed to be broken and the room was sweltering all night. After supposedly having it fixed for our second night, I once again woke up in the middle of the night and had to go sit in the hallway to cool down. 
We also requested early check-in if available, and while I didn't mind the $25 fee for this, it would have been nice to know in advanced when I requested it instead of being notified upon check-in.

title: “Great room in wonderful location”
text: This is the Manhattan version of the Courtyard concept.....few frills, but very comfortable. The room was very spacious, and comfortable. Great bed, and accommodated three with a pull out sofa bed, which was a relief from the dreaded rollaway. The hotel is in midtown, but on the East side, and away from the Times Square craziness, although I would warn visitors that if they plan on spending a lot of time in the Times Square area, they may wish to stay there or on the West Side, as a long walk or a cab is the only practical way to get there. My one criticism is of the lobby....it is narrow, and the check in is a counter, not a desk (you will see what I mean) and does not give a really welcoming feeling. I would definitely go back.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
My husband and I were looking forward to staying at a different hotel - especially this one. We expected a lot - and were so terribly disappointed.
At this price point, the details you would expect are non existent. Requests went disregarded - newspapers, extra pillows. Water view that was promised didn't happen. Housekeeping slow and managed to "lose" a shirt (later returned), and bed linens came complete with holes throughout (were changed upon request). Our room was ok, but in desparate need of a paint job and carpet cleaning. The valet staff however was great - nice, friendly and helpful.
We won't be back. The Inn's location is great, but nothing else was memorable. We'll go back to the Edgewater in the future.

title: “Better bedding would make this hotel a winner”
text:
On the plus side my room on the 49th floor was spacious by New York standards and the bathroom was a very nice size. Check in was quick, the room was quiet, there is a very large flat screen TV and a mini-bar. 
Personally, I hate being anywhere near Times Square, but the location of this hotel is near my firm's New York office, so it's convenient.
To me, what takes a hotel from good to great is the quality of their bedding and towels. I'm especially picky about the bed spreads, which often gross me out. Unfortunately, in pulling back the bedspread there was a 3 inch round stain on the underside. I quickly put the bedspread on the floor and got out the extra blanket from the closet. This blanket should have been thrown away long ago -- I can't even describe the fabric, it was rough and felt like a thin sheet of foam rubber that had perhaps been baked in a oven (or a too-hot dryer). Plus it had fuzz and a small wad of hair stuck on it. Anyway, it makes it hard for me to sleep when the bedding is even a little cruddy.
If the Millennium would just improve the bedding, I would give this hotel a great rating, but until then, I'll just give it a good rating.

title: “Nice place”
text: My wife and I stayed here to visit w/ friends and go to a UT football game. It was close to 183 and 360 without being noisy. The staff was friendly and the breakfast was good. I really liked that there was a fridge and microwave. We would stay here again.

title: “STAY AWAY....STAY VERY FAR AWAY!!!”
text:
On my first night, I called, in person alerted, and begged the phone operator to send someone to fix the heat.
