At 1:00 AM when I alerted them for the sixth time they sent someone up who turned a lot of valves and fixed it. On my third night, another worker came and told me I it was leaking and I had to move rooms because the heat was broken. By then I was so disgusted with them I just bundled up. 
It took at least 20 minutes to get through the lobby and elevators at the beginning and ending of the day. I got very familiar with the service elevators as a survival tactic. That was what this place was like -- you figured "work arounds" in order to survive. 
The staff seemed nice, for the most part, but they seemed as frustrated as you were, but this is NO WAY to see NY, either for personal time or business.

title: “Best place ever!!!!”
text:
Of Course I read the reviews so we where a little nervous about the Paradise Point...But what a great vacation we thought we where in Hawaii. (for half the price and no long flight)
We had a wonderful room. We did request a room by the adult pool since this trip was without kids. Not only got by the pool but close to the ocean also. Staff was very helpful and nice! (Mary)
 My boyfriend lost his jacket and they stayed on it until it was found. Had a great waitress (Lauren) and the food at the pool restaurant Tropics is great. We ate at all 3 restaurants and loved the food. Take your family or just your other and enjoy we sure did!

title: “Great value!”
text: I stayed at the Edison from Dec. 29 - Jan. 3 2004. The Edison was a terrific value! Our room was very clean and spacious (room 1819). It is an older hotel, but it has been well maintained. I never had to wait long for an elevator, the staff was wonderful, and the Cafe Edison on site offered good food and a good price. I will choose this hotel again when in NYC!

title: “Nothing special”
text: We stayed here three nights in August. We found the staff quite unfriendly, often we were ignored when entering the hotel. I would expect a hello from reception staff when guests are returning to their rooms. Rooms are ok, our room had a leaky tap. They seem a bit grey and sad, they need a little brightenning I think. Breakfast was satisfactory, nothing special. Internet access, wireless and free. Thats's it. I wouldn't return, its was just too bland for me.

title: “Great location, great hotel, nice rooms, highly recommend”
text: Stayed at this hotel on a recent trip to DC. Proximity to Dupont Square is excellent - only a couple of blocks from the Metro and a bunch of restaurants. Room was very spacious and very nice. Staff was friendly and helpful. Highly recommend!

title: “Other reviews don't lie...this is a wonderful place to stay!”
text: Other reviews don't lie...this is a wonderful place to stay! Extremely clean and outstanding value with updated rooms, no polyester comforters here! Helpful front desk staff, quiet even though near the airport, although currently road construction happening out front at all hours...don't let it stop you from staying here. We discovered, since the restaurant next door is also a bar and therefore allows smoking, children are not allowed entry (the law in Indiana?), which was absolutely fine with us as the hotel front desk took our order and our food was delivered from the restaurant to the hotel...be warned...portions are large, our salads were more than enough for two! Our room included coffee maker, dorm sized fridge and microwave.

title: “Last time we'll stay here!”
text:
We have been staying at this Hotel for the last five years. We normally use this hotel for our twice a year business trips and have always been impressed with everything one could want from a boutique hotel experience.
This last experience will keep us from ever returning or suggesting it to our friends and business associates. From the very moment we arrived till the time we checked out, we encompassed an incompetent staff that could not make decissions because there was no management on duty.
Because we stayed there so often we began to know the rooms and always requested something on the same exposure. We always got what we requested and it was confirmed at the time of my booking that we would be getting our request. There was never a question about this service because of our repeated business and referrals. Not only did we not recieve our request but were put in a room that faced the alleyway and of matchbox size. I objected to the selection and was told to pay over $100.00 more to get what I wanted in an upgrade. It was 11:30 at night and we just retired to this awful, dirty room to discuss it in the morning.
This hotel is tired and could use a face lift. We had no lights in our bathroom which were eventually fixed and the floors seem to never get vacuumed. On our third day, housekeeping never came to clean the room until we called to do so at 5:30. When I finally had a chance to speak to a manager, she had very little empathy for our experience and commented that they were experiencing problems that they were working on. I would have thought for sure that she would have tried to make me happy by offering something but nothing came forth. 
Beware all travelers to this hotel. It is not what it was and should be reduced to one star if that. Also be prepared to carry your own bags from the curb, bellman not present.

title: “Great Choice near the airport!!”
text: We arrived late - nearly midnight but still received friendly and helpful service. Room was clean and comfortable. Breakfast had nice variety.

title: “Excellent care for guests”
text: My wife and I had a wonderful one night stay at the Madera for a quick anniversary getaway. The staff was very professional, and we were very well cared for on our special day. The location is rather unbeatable as well, as we took a great long walk to the White House and another around the Dupont Circle area. Furthermore, the food and service at Firefly (downstairs) was sensational, and we have already begun recommending to our D.C.-area friends that they dine there soon. Danny is an amazing executive chef, and Justin was a spectacular server. We will definitely be staying at Kimpton hotels in the future!

title: “Very unhappy with policies”
text: We have a business in San Jose, and the hotel has a very negative policy on cancellations. It is a 24 hour notice, but one of my colleagues met their deadline and still had the charges put to the card. They refuse to remove the charge. Our company will be taking our business to another hotel.

title: “Rude reservationist, loud rooms, minimal breakfast buffet. Just average.”
text:
We were really excited about this place. Right on the water at Shelter Island, it seemed like a fun place to stay in San Diego. It ended up being below average for us.
RESERVATIONS:
We booked the room directly, and days before called because the rate had dropped on their website. The Reservations Manager was rude, told me that he was going to "Fire the Web Guy, I Guarantee That" (although the lower rate is STILL on the website weeks later, so he's a jerk and a liar), and that if I wanted the lower rate, I'd have to book the new rate online, and then call to cancel the first reservation, because he wasn't going to do it for me over the phone. He said "Do what you have to do". What a jerk.
ROOM:
We had two rooms, and I'll tell you this. STAY ON THE SECOND FLOOR. It's much nicer and much newer refurbishment. The first floor was so loud that we LITERALLY didn't sleep the first night. We could hear EVERY STEP ABOVE US. The room also was old and dirty. 
The second floor was much quiter, much cleaner, and seemed newer. The HVAC unit was all digital and very cool, compared with the 80's version downstairs.
BREAKFAST:
They bill it as a full breakfast buffet, but it's a continental breakfast plus tubs of potatoes and eggs. And the waiters expect tips.
All in all, we won't be coming back. It was overpriced and not as nice as we expected.

title: “Great hotel on Times Square”
text: I really love this hotel. It's on a great spot on Times Square. We had a renovated room. Excellent breakfast. Would go back there.

title: “Cheap and cheerful”
text:
The location of the hotel Is the main attraction to choosing this Hotel. I mean it is in an ideal location a stones throw away from times square in one direction and Central park in the opposite.
First thing was Reporting to the receptionists who were rude but the porters were very helpful. The hotel itself is in reasonable condition we were on the 25th Floor and getting down in the mornings was a nightmare, The lifts were terrible sometimes they wouldnt stop on your level and go straight past you on many occasion we were stuck for around 15 mins trying to go down to the bottom of the hotel.
The room Was of a good size Bathroom was a bit cramped but clean and tidy. There was no safe in the room which was a downer but we left things out and had no problem. 
The one problem we did have was the noise of the Air Conditioning unit it was LOUD to say the least. But it done the job so its a catch 22! 
All in all We would recommend the hotel to friends and family as its location is Bang on and the hotel Does the job so to speak.

title: “Very good in many ways.”
text: Just did a mini-vacation with our adult kids staying at Springhill Suites. We had 3 rooms in our reservation, we requested (and received) the rooms near one another on a high floor. Rooms are very adequate for a downtown location. The staff was friendly, the breakfasts are what you'd expect (a variety of cold cereals, a waffle maker, muffins, etc.). The only thing I had an issue with was the elevators. The hotel was booked full (at least it appeared that way) as there was always a wait for the elevator. Other than that, great location, friendly staff, etc. I would have no qualms about staying there again.

title: “Stay somewhere else”
text:
I recommend staying at another hotel as there are many options near this one. The hotel was way overpriced. I used the laundry service and asked for pressing. Wringles were ironed into both my pants and blouse.
The room was not very clean the base boards were dirty and there was stains on the carpet and furniture. I was there for work and other people with our party observed the same thing. Expect to wait for check in and out. It's often busy in the lobby and there are not enough seats.
There was also a union protest outside the hotel which started very early in the morning and was loud. For what the hotel charges per night they could pay and provide benifits for employees.
If you want a clean hotel with better service look into other hotels that may even cost less like Hotel Lombardy that has clean rooms and wonderful service.

title: “BREAKFAST WITH A VIEW OF LAKE UNION!”
text: This hotel was voted by our family of four as the best one that we stayed at in our month long tour of the West Coast of the US. The rooms were more upmarket and comfortable than other hotels on our trip and the gym was outstanding. The yummy breakfast overlooking stunning Lake Union was a fabulous way to start the day before taking the free shuttle into the city. With free parking and free wi-fi the Silver Cloud was a bargain.

title: “Boutique Renaissance”
text:
I stayed two weekday nights at the Renaissance M Street in late October and enjoyed my stay very much. The public spaces convey a sense of intimacy along the lines of a boutique hotel, and everything is crisp, clean, and modern in design. My king-bedded room was very spacious, though the bathroom was small, and the design similarly modern. The bathroom amenities were provided by Lather, Inc., a Pasadena-based producer of luxurious aromatherapy soaps, lotions and shampoos. The desk was odd in that one edge was attached and the other swiveled on wheels. At first I thought it was broken, but after getting used to it's mobility, the desk was perfectly functional. Wired and wireless connections were available for the usual additional charge.
The fitness room on the lower level was nicely equipped with Lifefitness treadmills and cycles, each with a monitor to which you could attach your own headsets. Just for the fun of it one morning i walked to the nearby Washington Marriott to try their indoor pool (access was arranged for Renaissance guests). The Marriott fitness room and pool were primitive and tiny in comparison to the Renaissance, and after looking around a couple of minutes I retreated back to the Renaissance.
The real surprise for me was the quality of the M Brasserie. I enjoyed two dinners and a lunch and found the quality of food and service to be exceptional. The prices were also quite reasonable for Washington, DC dining. 
Overall, I would stay at the Renaissance M Street again, either for business or pleasure.

title: “Great hotel in a perfect location. !!”
text:
When we stayed at the hotel it's lobby was under renovation. So there is little on can say about that. But the rooms have been renovated and are nice and clean. 
The staff is really courteous and helpful. 
The roof top restaurant and bar is a great place. 
China town is just walking distance. 
The only thing that I thought needed improvement was the TV quality and the quality of programming. 
I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Good spot downtown”
text:
Pros
- great location, couple of blocks from Hancock building
- 2 bedroom suite was rather large and big enough for family of six
-front desk staff was very helpful and courteous
Cons
- housekeeping did not replenish supplies (shampoo, TP, kleenex, etc)
- breakfast was set up in temporary location, while work being done.
Would stay there again.

title: “Absolutely Terrible”
text: Just dreadful experience. Room was dirty, the front desk gave me in correct info about parking, and i had to pay money to get my car back!! never again!!

title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text:
When booking this hotel there weren't many reviews or pictures around so I didn't know what to expect, but from the moment I stepped into the hotel, I knew i'd chosen the right place for me.
The hotel is very clean, check in was fast and prompt, and the staff were friendly. It can take a little while remembering how to use the elevator, but it was a nice little security feature that made me feel that little bit safer. I was on my own and the room was just the right size for that, but it may have felt a little crowded if there were two of us. The room was always clean.
The location was spot on for where I wanted to be, which was near the theatre district. There is a convenience store a couple of doors down, which I found very helpful, and plenty of places to eat nearby.
There is no doubt in my mind that I would search this hotel first next time i'm visiting New York.

title: “excellent 8 night stay”
text:
Stayed in the Sofitel for 8 nights in May. 
The Pluses:
The rooms were beautiful (see pics). Beds have a down mattress pad that is very soft but not to soft, baths have full shower and tub. Bathroom products are standard Sofitel which means Roger et Gallet which is excellent. Beautiful heavy curtains that blocked out the light well. Staff was outstanding. The concierge was very helpful and helped us with restaurant ideas and reservations on more than one occassion. We had eaten at Old Ebbitts near the hotel on our own and had to wait 1h20 mins for a table. latter in the trip we wanted to eat there again and the concierge was able to secure a reservation for the same evening only 2 hours in advance. Saved us the wait and we were given a very nice table. Room service breakfast was a fair value at 14 dollars for a continental with fresh squeezed juice, croissants, raisin danish and coffee. The bar was a hopping place and seemed well liked amoung locals. its a short walk to the White House and a quick metro ride to the Mall.
The Minuses:
Housekeeping is usually outstanding in Sofitels however, I felt it was only good in this hotel. The rooms were always clean and the beds well made but they did not do the little extras like straighten up the room when clothes,book, shoes, belts etc. were about. They never changed the fresh flowers in the 8 nights we were there so they were quite dead. They often forgot to leave the room service breakfast order form.
With the exception of breakfast the room service menu was over priced and uninteresting. The hotel restaurant was also uninspiring and pricey.
Although close to the sites, it is a business area so it clears out at 6 pm and is very dead on the weekend. There are very few restaurants within walking distance of the hotel that are open for dinner. 
Terrible view from the window. Check it out in my photos. We had two rooms, both with the same view. From looking at the floor map it looked like several rooms on each floor had this type of view. Be sure to ask for a room facing the street if you like to look out the window.

title: “Nice hotel, but few problems”
text: This hotel is very cute, they have a kids movie playing outside every night and firepits for roasting marshmallows for making s'mores, they also provide complimentary popcorn to have while watching the movie. However, there were a few things that went wrong during our stay, i understand things can happen but what is annoying is when the problems arent resolved in a timely manner. For the three days we were there none of the ice machines on any of the floors were working, the pool was dirty each time we went down and the water in our bathtub wasnt working for hours.

title: “Love the room and the gang at the Newton”
text:
This was my husband's and my fourth stay at the Hotel Newton since 2002. My sister Gayleen and her husband came again, her third trip, they love it here also! Emilio booked our room and we always get the room that we ask for, never a problem. He and my husband love to talk baseball. All of the staff at the Newton are just the best. Very friendly, helpful with any questions. Alex, John and Emilio are the ones we know the most behind the desk, the others just as great, sorry forget your names. That Humburto (sp) at the front door is just a pleasure. Always a smile on his face when we come and go. They all sure makes us feel welcome.
The hotel rooms are spacious, affordable, and always cleaned spick and span. (Tip your maids, they do a great job!) Plasma TV, coffee maker, great shower area, sitting room with another TV, AC works just great. We always get a suite as one or two of my sisters will come along. In 2004, my husband Toc and I had 3 of my sisters, Joleen, Colleen and Gayleen with her husband an Greg in two rooms on the 9th floor. It was my oldest sisters 50th birthday and they all loved the rooms and the staff. Still need to get Dorleen and Arleen out there...
The location is upper west side, a quaint neighborhood to stroll around, go just a few blocks west to the river or east to central park. Plenty of shops for this and that and restaurants galour! Then head to the action by taking the subway right down the street to south street seaport, times square, the trade center etc,.
Thanks again Newton ya did a fine job once again!
See ya next year! Kathleen!

title: “Friendly staff, nice location”
text: I initially stayed at this Marriott Courtyard because it was almost next door to an on-site project I was commuting to from Orange County. As with all the Rancho Bernardo area hotels, it's pricier than nearby Escondido and Poway, but I stayed at the Marriott at least one night a week for the next three months for its convenience, comfort and friendly staff. A large shopping center with plenty of restaurants and a Vons supermarket is across the street, a really nice park with waterfowl acts as a backyard for the hotel (and there's some more food on the other side of the park, including dim sum and a Denny's), and the staff is always cheery. I stayed there often enough to get upgraded to a Silver membership, and sometimes the staff comped me one of my regular midnight Dove ice cream bars from the "pantry". The rooms are large and clean and new-looking (there is in fact one room located at the elbow of the building which is oddly shaped but extra large, so some people ask for that one), with a nice flat screen TV and fairly good channel selection and no problems with the wifi (well, except for early one day and that's when you find out how many people depend on their Internet access..) The only thing it lacks in comparison to other area hotels is a free breakfast (the Hilton is the other one that doesn't), but hey, there's Denny's...

title: “Good price, bad location”
text:
If you're going to DC to see the sites, stay closer to the Mall or Dupont Circle. The Hyatt Regency is in the Capitol Hill area and a loooong walk to good restaurants and shopping. The hotel restaurant is grossly over-priced, but there aren't many choices in the area so you have to eat there. The food itself wasn't even that good.
The hotel is like most Hyatts - very nice and comfortable. The staff was very accommodating. We requested a king bed and were given 2 queens. The front desk moved us immediately. The housekeeping staff was really nice, as was our waitress in the restaurant - her name is Do.
We'll definitely be returning to DC but definitely not staying at the Hyatt Regency - Capitol Hill, and this is based solely on it's location.

title: “Good choice if need to be by the Hynes Convention Center”
text:
The hotel is located in the “back bay” area of Boston … towards the south side. It is not in the immediate downtown area but is right across the street from the Hynes convention center and a large mall. There are plenty of restaurants in the area, as well as other major hotels like Sheraton, Marriott, Westin and others.
The Hotel – the interior of the hotel is nice but nothing fancy. No extravagant lobby or sitting area. The elevators appear to be designed to have at least one unused elevator at the lobby. Check-in was quick and staff was courteous. There is a bellman at the entrance most of the time. The hotel is kept in good shape and the hallways are clean. Did not use the pool or workout facility. 
The Rooms – nice, and fairly large for a big-city hotel. As usual, the Hilton beds are among the most comfortable. Bathroom is small but efficient. Room was generally clean but found a few stray hairs in the bathroom. TV was not HD. Good views from the upper floors.
The Restaurant – had breakfast at their restaurant Boodles. The buffet was decent and the dining room quaint. There is really not a good bar at this hotel but you can walk across to the Sheraton and find a nice lobby lounge or at one of the area restaurants. 
If you are spending time by the Hynes convention center, this is good choice of hotels but there are others with better lounge & restaurant areas. 
NOTE: make sure you tell the cab driver the “Back Bay Hilton by the Hynes center on Dalton”. Just said the “Back Bay Hilton” and got dropped off at the Boston Hilton … which is more downtown.

title: “Great Service, Clean, Free Breakfast, and Good Price.”
text: I stayed at the Ramada Chatsworth last week for 3 days when I went on vacation to California. We had a great experience at the hotel and I really recommend this hotel. I was assisted by Bibian Medina at the front desk. She was so kind, took care of our reservation and called for assistance to take our stuff to our suite. I needed more towels and shampoo and she sent it to me right away. My internet was a bit slow and when I called she sent me a wifi cable to make the internet faster. I really recommend for families to get a suite. The beautiful suite has a living room with a sofa bed, TV, refrigerator, coffee maker with coffee,sink, and microwave. There is plenty of space for the kids to play. In the room there was a soft king size bed with another TV for me to watch my programs while the kids watched TV in the living room. We went swimming and the swimming pool was heated, very clean and the Jacuzzi was so relaxing. They gave me more clean towels at the front desk after I left the pool. I loved it that hotel is so close to restaurants, and places to go visit in CA. I took my kids to the zoo, Universal Studios, Six Flags, Malibu beach, and Santa Monica beach withing 20-30 minute drive. Every time I came back from our trips to the hotel, our rooms was so clean and neat. The staff is very friendly and they give you more things if you need. Every morning they offer free breakfast. I love it that they have a waffle makers and you just pour the mix already made and you get fresh delicious waffles. I had plenty to choose for breakfast. They had fruit, cereal and hard boil eggs, pastries, bagels, english muffins, toast, cream cheese, coffee, tea, chocolate and different juices. I can't wait to go back to California and stay at the Ramada Chatsworth for a great vacation with my family.

title: “Worst Hotel experience of my life!”
text:
I made reservations on the Hotels site to stay at the LaQuinta Inn Charlotte Airport.
When we arrived in Charlotte from Massachusetts we called for directions to the hotel and the young lady at the desk said "85, exit 33" and hung up. We found the exit after going on the highway and going north and then south only to find we needed only cross over 85 (not get on it!). We found the corner of Queen City Drive and went left to the end, turned around and went right to the end and then called the hotel again. The same young lady said "we're right next to Cracker Barrel". I asked if there weren't another hotel in that location. She said "yeh, Quality Inn, that's us". So, after an hour of driving around in the rental car we found the hotel. It has changed names, ownership and management. It is dirty, and moldy, and stinks of cigarette smoke and other things. When I mentioned the wild goose chase that the young woman sent me on she shyly said "I know" and proceeded with our booking. We did not have time to look for another hotel. We quickly prepared and left for the Statesville High School graduation ceremonies and barely made it to Statesville in time to get seats. This was my worst experience with Hotels. I hope never to repeat this one. Oh, and someone should tell La Quinta that their name is being used to draw customers to a flea bag. 
Tina Johnson

title: “This is a lovely antique 5-star...”
text:
This is a lovely antique 5-star hotel
that is one block from the White House. The rooms have been redone and are very comfortable... Every thing you would expect with a five star hotel, except for one thing. The hotel does not provide bathroom slipers, so bring your own. The cold bathroom tile is so cold, you will wish you did!

title: “Unbelievable Service and Location !!!!!”
text:
What a fantastic hotel, location, and staff ! 
I've never been treated better at a hotel than during our long weekend for a Texas football game. The staff was more than accommodating for my complicated check-in and worked through all the nuisances of my group reservation. Matt (Front Desk Manager), Becky (Front Desk), and Rob (Guest Services Manager) were so great, and made us feel right at home. The concierge spent over 15 minutes telling me about the must see sights and restaurants. We were greeted each time we stepped off the elevator and walked into the hotel, many of them remembering my name. We left feeling like we made new friends, and I'm really struggling to find a downside to the hotel.
The location is literally one block from the heart of 6th Street (an easy 1-2 minute walk to 6th and San Jacinto), but back far enough where you can get a good night’s sleep and aren’t constantly in the action. If you are in Austin and don’t have much time, this is the hotel for you. We walked back and forth to 6th street at least 3 times each day because it was so easy. If you want to get away and see the State Capitol, UT Campus, West 6th Street, Warehouse District….the walk is a little longer, but very manageable. Cab service is also good if venturing out to SOCO, Lake Travis, Hill Country or some of the more outlying areas. We had a rental car, but really didn’t need it. 
The recently renovated rooms and bathrooms show very well along with the larger suite my friend had on one of the executive floors. The openness of the lobby and bar really make for a nice gathering/meeting spot. Fitness center is fresh and vibrant with more than enough machines/equipment. 
I travel frequently for work/pleasure and the staff at this hotel is really SECOND TO NONE. We will be recommending this hotel to all of our friends !!!

title: “Service beyond”
text:
This hotel has service down pat. There is no detail left untended. Check-in was easy. We were upgraded to a partial ocean view. The room was nice, if a bit small, and the bathroom was luxurious.
Housekeeping was great (please tip them). THe food in the restaurant was excellent. THe workout room was very nice with gatorade supplied. The spa area has a steam room and nice showers with all the amenities. I did notice, as did another reviewer, that the lower floor rooms facing the street are a bit noisey.
When you leave they give you a bottle of water and directions.. I would definitely stay here again. It is pricey but worth every cent.

title: “Great Modern Hotel..Very few concerns, would def. return”
text: I'm extremely critical in all my reviews as trip advisor has served me abounds over the past 10 years so I try to pay it forward. I really enjoyed my stay in chicago, I would like to add though it was sunny and nearly 80 each day in october which was apparently nearly unheard of weather so I might be overly excited about the trip in its entirety. I stayed a long weekend with my girl and really enjoyed the hotel overall. I paid a little extra for a corner room, had a great decent size bathroom with seperate shower/tub and the view down state st. was priceless especially the chicago theater sign.. I enjoyed being able to open the window and hear the elevated trains/sounds of the city and close it to complete calm. Bed was super comfy, TV was great and hotel could not have been in a better location, always easy to catch the train or a cab. One morning I had the pleasure of seeing 40,000 people run by for the chicago marathon and it was always easy to find breakfast in walking distance. Had a drink at the rooftop but couldnt stay long as we ventured to different restaurants and clubs every night. Concerns: Only a few first of course being the $12 for internet for 24hrs, its 2011 lets go with the charging for internet it just makes your hotel look stingy alot of us need web access for business. I travel alot and so many higher end hotels do this its just not right, especially in the US. Second I left a neck pillow in the room I used for the plane, had my girl run in literally an hour after we checkout and they were unable to find the pillow or the maid who might have taken it as the room had been cleaned, my girl seemed to feel they were genuinely unconcerned with it at the front desk. Not a big deal but enough to say something about. Finally the door opening issue. I travel alot and have stayed in decent hotels to top rated hotels all over the world. Wit has literally 2-3 "doormen" at all times (at least during my stay) and all weekend they hadn't opened a door more than once and we were in and out all day/night. If you are paying people to stand outside in a shirt with your hotel name on it, make them open the cab door, and the hotel entrance door, its simple enough and I tip when they do so!! Easy to make a great first impression... Overall staff seemed genuinely nice, with the exception of an extremely sarcastic valet who checked my baggage on the last day, and after I somehow misplaced my ticket for it an hour later proceeded to poke fun at the situation and then had trouble "locating the bags" even though it was an hour duration inbetween. Just nitpicking at this point though, I would definetely return in a minute!!!

title: “Ministry Presenter”
text:
I stayed at the Marriott East for three days and two nights due to the fact that I co-conducted a workshop on financial stewardship for a statewide church organization. Having been reared not far from here, I was reticent about staying at this hotel. (I remembered this Marriott as not being very nice.) However, much to my pleasant surprise, I found the hotel to be well-appointed after extensive renovations. It also has an excellent staff. In particular, I would like to commend Khylee, who is efficient, attentive, and pleasant. Having stayed at many hotels due to the nature of my work, I can verify that her service is atypical. I look forward to staying here again!
Larry Smith

title: “OUTSTANDING FACILITY AND STAFF”
text:
I have stayed in San Diego several times in the past. The Town and Country, in every way, has been exceptional, beyond the ordinary, with beautiful grounds, good sized, clean and modern rooms, excellent restaurants (from Kelly's Steak House to breakfast and lunch venues as well) and a staff that is outstanding. 
Not only is the staff helpful, they are professional, know their hotel, and facilities and have a genuine interest in caring for their customers. In particular, Sherida Green, the shift manager answered every question, provided helpful suggestions, knew her property and her staff. Johanna Nunez, the booking agent was prompt, courteous, thoughtful and helpful and offered to show us rooms before we checked in. 
Every detail was considered. Aaron Zuniga, went out of his way to show us various rooms and the advantages and disadvantages of various rooms and locations on the sprawling property.
Waitresses in the restaurants, including Pati Mukzevicti, went out of their way to suggest menu items and provide excellent service.
The price, for all the services and the outstanding facility was reasonable and the facility is certainly family friendly.
The Best That San Diego Has To Offer.

title: “Loved it. I will return.”
text: I was late arriving so had only a short time to see the sights. Concierge called ahead to my destinations and made up a map so I could walk down Main Street from the hotel and get to visit the fabulous Sid Richardson Gallery and eat delicious ice cream. My check in was quick, the room on the 14th floor was elegantly appointed, and the view over the convention centre was stupendous. Clean bathroom, fabulous bed. Good location for Stockyards and Sundance Square, a bit far for the Cultural Centre. Amazing breakfast buffet! Lots of free newspapers provided. All in all a good hotel.

title: “Not Worth 4 Diamonds”
text:
This large hotel, conveniently located in Union Square, wasn’t deserving of the AAA 4 diamond rating in my opinion. At least our room was not. It is located on the edge of the Tenderloin district—San Francisco’s adult entertainment section, so I felt as if I had to be somewhat careful at night. The area has a seedy feel—lots of homeless people sleeping on sidewalks and urinating in the street. Conversely, it is in a good spot for shopping, with Macy’s, the Gap and many other chains within five minutes walking distance. It’s also a half a block from the cable turnaround and several bus lines.
The attractive lobby is spacious with lots of seating areas. The front desk clerk was very friendly when we checked in. We asked for a smoking room, as high up as possible and she put us on the 15th floor –the highest in the smoking section, so we had a good view of the city. 
The rooms themselves were not that big, but you find that a lot in large cities. We had two double beds, an armoire with 27-inch TV, and two comfortable overstuffed chairs, and an iron and ironing board. The bathrooms were small and nondescript, but they did have hair dryers, and provided shampoo, conditioner, moisturizer, a shower cap and shoe shine mitt (but no sewing kit). The conditioner and moisturizer, both from Bath and Body Works, looked identical and one morning I put the moisturizer in my hair instead of conditioner. I wish they would distinguish the bottles in some way or make their products in different colors!
The bath mat looked as if it could use a good bleaching, with a brown something or other on it that made me uncomfortable enough that I never put it in the tub. Sometimes there were hairs on the bathroom floor that they never cleaned up when the housekeeping staff made up the room. The towels were fairly thick but not soft. The bed linens were nice but the beds were not triple sheeted. The comforters were thick and done in beautiful rust tones which matched the fabric on the chairs, and the windows were expansive offering a great view and pretty window treatments. 
The hotel is supposed to be known for outstanding service, but one morning when we asked the concierge to try to get us a reservation at Boulevard, a popular San Francisco restaurant, she laughed at us. She ended up getting the reservation, and called us on our cell phone to let us know, but we felt that was somewhat demeaning to have her laugh. She could have said, "Well, Boulevard is a very trendy restaurant, but I'll try my best to get you in." It was in the middle of the week after all. Another time, a different concierge seemed less than enthusiastic when we asked for directions to a sports bar so we could watch Sunday morning football. There was a pad of area maps on his desk, but he merely motioned with his head when describing where this bar was. "It's over on 4th Street" he grumbled. And when we asked, "Well, where is that?" he hastily said, (nodding his head toward the map which we were trying to read) "Where that grey area is." as if he was annoyed at us for not knowing the streets! A good concierge would have highlighted the area on the map for us and told us how to get there. 
The hotel does provide complimentary coffee and tea on the second floor, each morning. They also offer cereals, yogurts, fruit, and breakfast pastries for an additional charge.

title: “Handlery Stay December 2012”
text: Very friendly and helpful staff. Rooms are clean and everything is replenished in the room daily. Nice stay for the money. Close to shopping. Food choices are not as great, but we ate at Cafe Bellini and Cheesecake Factory (located in Macy's), the food was good.

title: “Great hotel great access”
text: This hotel is a nice place to stay. We stayed in the 2 bedroom suite with family. They have two bathrooms which is so helpful. The little kitchenette is great. The kids enjoyed the pool and they had a really nice breakfast. The breakfast had waffles, eggs, a meat (bacon or sausage depending on the day), oatmeal (not in pouches), cereals, fresh fruit, yogurts, and breakfast pastries and bagels. Really a large selection and nice eating area. The staff was so friendly and just very pleasant. It is easy to get up on the highways and get to anything in Denver.

title: “Acceptable Convention Hotel Near Shopping/Dining/Transit.”
text:
This is a large, dated convention hotel facility. The rooms are a curious mixture of upper end --"Sweet Sleeper" beds, flat screen TVs, free Starbucks coffee with real half and half -- and older, beat-up furniture and a low level of bathroom amenities. Wi-fi is free in the lobby, but $10 a day for internet (non-wi-fi) in the room. 
Location is a big plus for this hotel. It is just off Copley Square and Newberry Street in the Back Bay, so there is plenty of dining, shopping, and people watching to be had. This is important because food and beverage prices in the hotel were prohibitive, but could be alleviated by a quick walk to much less expensive, high quality, alternatives either within the attached Prudential Center Mall, or out in the nearby neighborhoods. 
The Hotel is close to either the Hynes Convention Center or the Prudential stops on the Green Line (so the airport is only a $2 away on the T, if you're traveling light). Likewise, Amtrak can be accessed via Back Bay Station, which is a ten-minute walk through the connecting malls and pedestrian bridges. You only need go outside to cross Dartmouth street from the Westin to the station.
For excellent, inexpensive breakfast just up the block, go to the "Pour House" on Boyleston. Really hit the spot for us and for well under half the price of the Sheraton's overpriced breakfast buffet.

title: “Noisy rooms and thieving valet atendants.”
text:
We spent a weekend at this hotel (Feb 19-22), to explore downtown. Hotel location is excellent for this activity. Rooms were old but clean and EXTREMELY NOISY! I have never stayed at a motel or hotel that supplies EARPLUGS WITH THE ROOM!!! Most expensive valet parking ($37/D) I have experienced even compared with NYC prices!
DO NOT LEAVE ANY VALUABLES IN YOUR CAR WHEN VALET PARKING! After leaving hotel I discovered that all my "parking" change had disappeared from the center console. Dollar bills as well as quarters, nickles and dimes (~$15). The only people that had access to my vehicle in Seattle were the valet attendants. VALET ATTENDANTS STOLE IT ALL!

title: “Great Location”
text: Came here for a concert at The Music Factory which was about 2 miles from this hotel. Their shuttle service made it completely worth it (make sure to check when the shuttle ends) and there was a lot to do within a closer proximity to the hotel as well. Great customer service at the front desk and everything was as promised. Overall, a wonderful experience!

title: “Look forward to the next stay”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel several times and continue to recommend it. The service is always great and the location is ideal. 
During our most recent stay, we had a breakfast and dinner at Trio and both meals were great. We especially enjoyed sitting on the back patio for those meals and relaxing on the back lawn. The lake view room was nice and comfortable and a huge plus goes to the shower's water pressure.
Hope to be back soon!

title: “Perfect place for first timers”
text: Arrived in Chicago for the first time ever about 8 hours before the rest of my party. The Sutton was the perfect starting location to get the most out of my first day. The staff was friendly and helpful with an early check-in. Then, after checking out some of the materials in the room for maps and highlights, was able to walk around to find an abundance of dining, drinking and shopping options right around the hotel, and at the end of the block, the famed Michigan Avenue with all of the city's best shopping -- right there! We never went further than walking distance of the hotel the entire trip because we didn't have too. There was so much do to within just a few city blocks and every place we ate near the hotel was absolutely amazing especially the small pancake house across the street. Even with all of the bars on Rush Street just a couple blocks away, our favorite night spot was the Whiskey Bar located inside the hotel. On Saturday nights it was the perfect little lounge with good music, cozy seating and a good crowd. This place is located in the best part of the city and i would recommend for any kind of trip.

title: “Great old dame!”
text: After being disspointed by our booked hotel (see 70 Park Ave. hotel review "Checked in then out") we booked a luxury suite here not knowing what to expect, only that we would have lots of room & luxury as promised. Well, after doing the tourist thing all day we finally checked in at 9pm & when questioned our rooms lower floor status, the 7th, decided to trust the front desk when they told us "We will be really surprised if you arent happy with this room." Well, for once they were right & we were pretty shocked to see what $600. a night at the Waldorf buys. We had; 1 large living room, (the kind you see in much older homes, a very large bedroom (LARGE!), a dressing room, a marble bathroom with 2 seperate sinks, a large tub & a seperate tiled in shower all surrounded by black marble & of course 2 comfy terry robes waiting in our large, formal, mirrored closets, just off the bathroom. We also had a full size kitchen (yes, a bit old & funky, but a kitchen!) with a small fridge & even a stove if you decide to whip up some omlettes or something. This is all off the wood floored foyer & thick, wooden (no cheapy things these) double doors. Now if you like comtemporary, this will not suit you at all as you will have to put up with a few portraits of presidents, antiques, & some sour looking others who I would have rather not watch me sleep, but then could always be retired to a drawer. The Audubon print above the bed made me feel right at home here & the room service was impeccable. We ordered a cheese plate for 2 (not on the menu) & got what looked like something out of Dean & Delucca's cheese department in double quick time...WOW!

title: “Really comfortable, central location, nice staff.”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights. The room was really spacious, the bed was soooo comfortable, the bathroom was nice, we didn't want to leave. The closet is big enough to store your suitcases, propped up on the stands. The desk was the perfect place to sit on your laptop and work. I had problems getting my computer to connect to the wireless connection, so they brought me something called a "bridge" and that helped. The room is big enough to spread out and make yourself comfortable. No street noise. No noise from rooms next door, so it was very easy to sleep at night. It was a joy to come back to the room after a day of walking around the city. It's located on a steep hill, so if you're walking with suitcases, be prepared. The Powell St. street car line is right on the corner. We had breakfast right next door at Roxanne's every day, not cheap but lots of options and good caffe latte. I would definitely stay here again if the price remains reasonable. I got the best deal through their website, I assume the economy is the reason for the reduced rates.

title: “Just o.k. for the price.”
text:
Stayed here 2nd week of February 2012. Room was on the 3rd floor. First the positives: Price was only about $70/night. Not noisy at least on the side away from the highway. Convenient to get on interstate hwy 17. Bell road has a lot of shopping, eating, etc. not too far away from the hotel. The shower drained well, the TV worked and the bed was comfortable. Didn't have to test the air conditioner or heater very much.
 Now the negatives. Cleanliness was o.k. in the shower, the stool, the bed linens, etc. but, the room wasn't clean in general. The rug was worn, the furniture and linens were old and thread bare. Dirt smudges on the wall and dirt in the corners and just generally felt dirty. Hallway rugs were worn and the facility in general is a little run down. Bring your Lysol wiper. Its o.k. for a single adult traveler if your trying to save money but I wouldn't recommend it to a family that is trying to relax for a couple of days.

title: “Old and Dusty”
text: I ended up at this hotel property because nothing else was available in the city. The hotel is old and caters to a crowd that does not have much class (hence the low daily rate). The property is in desperate need of renovations and the club lounge is a complete joke (same size as my hotel room). Stay out of Phillips Seafood restaurant in the hotel lobby as it is a rip off with mediocre service.

title: “Easy stay”
text: Of course there are probably nicer hotels in nyc for a lot more money! The Westin is so easy. It's near Times Square which can turn a lot of people off. You can't hear the traffic. The room is clean. The beds are amazing. There's nothing better than the heavenly bed at the Westin. The subway station at Times Square is the hub for every line in the subway system, so it's easy to use. The staff at the Westin is very nice and helpful. My only complaint was that I couldn't get anyone to answer the phone at the front desk when I called a couple of times. I'll definitely be back.

title: “Just average”
text: This hotel is located pretty far from all the good stuff in San Diego, so beware. Actually, there isn't much around except for other hotels. There are a couple restaurants around, but you definitely need to drive there. They charge you $10 a day for parking here, which seems ridiculous since you're already paying over $200 a night. The actual rooms are nice and clean, but fairly small. The rooms have their kitchenettes with microwave, fridge, stove, and dishwasher. The free breakfast isn't all that it's cracked up to be, either. The only real "hot" food item was the waffles that you make yourself. I think they had some scrambled eggs, but by the time I got there... nothing was left. Overall, I wasn't very impressed with this place considering it's pretty expensive. I would have been just as happy staying at a nice Motel 6 or something that was closer to all the cool stuff in San Diego.

title: “Parking Stinks”
text: I have always enjoyed staying at the sheraton even when it was the Wyndham. This past weekend we were in town for the Yankees game. I gave my valet ticket to the person running the desk and he very rudely told me I had to wait 40 minutes for my vehicle. After enquring about the guy I was shocked to learn that he was the parking manager. I do not think I will ever stay at this hotel again.

title: “Wonderful stay at the Inn at Venice Beach”
text: Our stay of 2 nights was so enjoyable - the canals of Venice Beach are located right by the hotel. The Inn was very comfortable as we stayed in the bigger rooms (2 queens), very quiet. Breakfast which is included, was one of the best we have ever been too. Hospitality was excellent and we would definitely stay there again!

title: “Great Downtown location”
text: Lovely room, quiet, great location just off the Circle. I enjoyed the stark architecture, but my husband felt the hotel lacked personality & would have preferred more greenery for a "Garden Inn". Also, there is another Hilton 3 blocks away on Market, so be sure that you are at the right Hilton before going into the parking garage! Front desk & parking staff friendly & competent. I had no complaints except $22 for parking (valet) seemed high. This is a great location for nightlife & shopping and of course for touring the Soldiers & Sailors Monument in the Circle.

title: “Noisy, noisy, noisy”
text:
We booked this hotel since my spouse had a business obligation in Baltimore and we were also on our way back from a long weekend in Washington, DC. I liked the location near Camden Yards since the Orioles would be home during our stay, and it was a short walk to the Inner Harbor as well. Expedia had good rates for this hotel compared with its neighbors.
We arrived late in the evening, as we were visiting with family outside of DC. The security guard was very nice and assisted us with our luggage and check-in. The clerk at the desk was also friendly, however gave me unclear directions as to how to get on the parking garage at that time of night, which was very stressful for me since I had enough trouble finding the entrance to the hotel in the first place. I was pleased to see my bags and my souse in our room upon my return.
I did not sleep very well the first night as the wall-unit air conditioner was very loud (even though there was a "sleep" mode) and the room would get too hot if it was not on. Being given a first floor room in a city, we did not get the chance to sleep late with trucks and morning traffic whizzing by.
There was a cafe and a full service restaurant in the hotel, but I went to the nearby Starbucks for coffee and we used the in room fridge and microwave to heat up breakfast we bought in DC. The restaurant was kind enough to provide us with plates and utensils both mronings since there were none in the room. There was also a lack of information regarding the hotel and its policies in the room, which I found quite odd.
The second night we slept a little better, but overall we did not have a relaxing stay. Although the room was nicely furnished and clean, it was very stuffy and the shower provided poor water pressure. Another annoying thing was that although we paid for 48 hours of parking, we really only got 36 hours as we arrived late in the evening and had to leave the garage by noon.

title: “Very Good”
text: I loved the location and the facilities at this hotel. It was very clean and the service was very good.

title: “good location, but no beach hotel”
text:
The Manchester Grand Hyatt is probably the biggest hotel in San Diego. It consists of two interconnected towers. Due to the huge size of the hotel, the atmosphere is a little bit anonymous.
I had room with a very beautiful view of the harbour bridge and the bay. My room had a decent size and the bed was very comfortable.
The lobby area is quite impressive due to ultra-high ceilings (which is not unusual for Hyatt hotels). There is a bar on one of the upper floors that offers a great view of San Diego and the Bay/Harbour. There is also a pool area which has a decent size.

title: “A Refreshing Night”
text: Having stayed at several San Diego area properties, I would definitely choose to return to this one. It is a newer, well-managed and conveniently located HGI which was a very welcome stop after all day on the road. Amenities we liked were the free wireless, the stay fit kit (everything you need for a pilates or yoga workout plus a medicine ball!), the professional and most helpful front desk staff, the readily offered printouts of running paths and local directions. Deserving special mention is Bistro 39, which offered a very nice, very good value 4 course prix fixe dinner-with a wine list. We did not have to drive any further to find dinner and were very pleased with the choices, including for us, cioppino, fresh salads, hearty appetizers (calamari with different dipping sauces and chicken on a skewer) and a great chocolate dessert! Also of note was the "garden sleep system." On each side of the mattress, tucked into a velcro-closed flap is a dial that allows the sleeper to choose the firmness of the mattress. It really worked! We also liked the ergonomic Herman Miller desk chair. After our overnight stay at this HGI, we actually felt refreshed and ready to get back into the car for another day on the road!

title: “All about the location”
text: I chose this hotel because of the price and location. It is a little further walk to places downtown, but at half the price. The desk staff was helpful and quite nice, and there was a friendly security guard there at night. Most of the staff was great at offering information and suggestions. They had a computer you can use in the check in area, and they told me I could print the info I needed for my traveling. I was able to leave my luggage with them when I arrived three hours before check in. My room was okay, mostly clean and a bit run down, but it did have microwave and a fridge, which was great. The beds were not too bad, but the pillows were super flat, I used three of them to sleep on. The bathroom area was alright. The no-slip adhesive mat in the tub was losing the adhesive, so it was coming loose which was kind of gross (stuff getting trapped under there) and made me watch my step so I would not trip on it. The shower head was fantastic for a budget motel. Breakfast was a bit better than most budget motels, with the waffle maker and yogurts. The pool looked clean and refreshing, but it was only in the 50's while I was there so did not get to check it out. This hotel is just off the expressway but it did not get much road noise. I only saw a few questionable characters during my stay. It seems the hotel was quick to remove them from the property. Overall the area was pretty good. There is a CVS across the street and it was really easy to get there and I did not feel at all uncomfortable walking around the area. One of the best BBQ food trucks is just a block or so from the hotel. This hotel was not the best, but between the staff and location I could stay here again.

title: “Clean hotel, great location”
text: I just stayed at the Amsterdam Court for 3 nights. Overall, a good hotel with a great location in the Theater District. The rooms are small, yes, but it's NYC--that's pretty standard. The room was clean, which was great, and the staff was helpful. I got a great rate at hotels.com (<$180/night). In almost any other city, the small room size and lack of cable TV would not earn an "above average" rating, but for NYC, the concerns should be cleanliness, location, and price, which this hotel had. I would stay there again!

title: “Best Honeymoon experience ever!”
text:
You must stay at this hotel if you are in NYC!
We stayed at St Giles – The Court for 10 nights from 19 October to 29 October 2010 on the first leg of our honeymoon.
We are from Melbourne, Australia and it was our absolute dream to honeymoon in NYC! A couple of months before our wedding, our 3-month old pug puppy had to undergo expensive eye surgery to save her left eye. As a result, all of our honeymoon savings were wiped out. Luckily, our beautiful pug’s eye is now almost fully recovered. 
Given that October is a peak time in NYC, we could not find any remotely affordable accommodation. We were just about to resort to staying at a youth hostel on our honeymoon (something no bride would look forward to). 
Given the amazing reviews on Trip Advisor, my dream was always to stay at St Giles – The Court. I emailed them, explaining our predicament but still thinking that there would be no way that they could help us given our limited budget. My desperation turned to pure joy when I received an email back from Clayton Channing from St Giles saying that, given our circumstances and the fact that we were honeymooners, they could offer us a rate within our budget. Prior to our stay we also received emails from David Lopez, General Manager of the hotel saying that he looked forward to meeting us. We even exchanged photos of our doggies (he has a French bulldog called DC). 
We arrived at the Hotel at about 6:30pm on 19 October after a 23 hour flight from Australia. We were greeted by the most friendly reception staff and when we said our names, they said “oh the honeymooners. We have been expecting you”. We were escorted to our room to find that we had been upgraded to a massive 1-bedroom suite (larger than our apartment in Melbourne) with an enormous balcony overlooking the Chrysler Building. There was also chocolate covered strawberries and chilled champagne waiting for us in our room. I cannot tell you the feeling of absolute elation at that moment, especially that just a few months earlier we thought we would have to cancel the honeymoon.
The buffet breakfast at the hotel is amazing. I had a tropical fruit salad every morning followed by a to-die-for omelet cooked by a chef at the “egg station”. Harold in the breakfast room is the most wonderful, kind and thoughtful man. He was always ready with a NYC recommendation or a laugh. He introduced me to the best citrus-mint tea I have ever had. 
I have nothing but praise for the wonderful José at the concierge desk. We went to him daily for NYC attractions or restaurant recommendations, every time his recommendations were spot-on. He has a brilliant sense of humor and had us giggling along with him. We showed him our wedding dance on You Tube and he kindly praised us on our dance moves (despite them being terrible).
My husband used the gym every morning (I stayed in bed) and said it was state of the art. We had a drink in the hotel bar, which was very cool and funky not at all like the stale, lifeless hotel bars at most hotels. We had one day where the jet lag was getting us so we stayed in the room watching the cable TV and ordered room service. 
This hotel literally glows with the kindness, style and sense of honor of its staff. The hotel itself is sharp, cool and funky. The room was extremely spacious and comfortable which was a very pleasant surprise as we were told about the small sized rooms in NYC. The hot water was plentiful so showers were a joy. 
In terms of location, it was perfect for us. The hotel is 1 block from Grand Central Station and a 10 minute stroll to Times Square. We were initially told to stay in Times Square but I am so happy that we didn’t. The area around the hotel is lovely with tree-lined streets and Lexington, Park and 5th Avenue extremely close. You are close to the bustle of NYC but the area around the hotel is peaceful and not overwhelming with activity like some NYC streets. 
I’m sorry to write such a long review. It is just very rare in this day and age to come across pure kindness and hospitality like the kind we experienced at this hotel. I therefore thought it might assist fellow travelers to read all about our experience at this hotel. We left feeling like we were leaving good friends. I will never forget the kindness of David Lopez, Clayton Channing, Harold and José and all they did to make our honeymoon experience in NYC something that we will never forget. 
Every time we return to NYC, we will definitely be staying at this hotel (which we hope will be many times). 
Juliet and Ryan, from St Kilda in Melbourne, Australia

title: “Caribbean feel here in the US!”
text: I absolutely loved this resort! I went with a group of friends and stayed for 3 days. I now wish that we would have stayed a little longer. The rooms are nice with large bathrooms and plush robes! The spa was the best I have ever experienced! The spa has its own pool, sauna, steam room, hot tub and restaurant. The breakfast buffet was a little pricey but they do have a nice selection of foods! If you are at the pool and want a drink be prepared to go to the bar and get it yourself. The drinks were also a little pricey but very good. This resort is located across the street from a huge shopping complex that has a lot of restaurants if you prefer not to eat at the resort. The staff and locals are very friendly! I highly recommend this resort!

title: “Best location in town”
text:
We only spent 5 nights at this wonderful small hotel but it felt like we were leaving old friends when we had to go. Well equipped, comfortabe room, superb location and some of the best concierge/reception service we have ever received. 
Each room is themed on a section from a library and we found ourselves in the Ancient History room complete with books on Ancient Rome, Greece etc. They also have the delightful 'Reading Room' with floor to ceiling shelves of books of all kinds where breakfast, all day tea and coffee and evening cheese and wine is available..
Although quite expensive we would definitely stay here again.

title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text: I had a great experience at this hotel! From the start, we arrived a few hours early and Sheraton Gateway was able to accommodate early check-in for us witlhout any delay. The concierge service was exceptional as well. As far as Guest Services is concerned, everyone was great! Two individuals stand out to me in particular. One is a lady named Diane who made sure we received our requests in a timely manner. Another is a lady named Merlie(?) who went above and beyond to assist me with a special request. She even came out and met me at the front desk to assist me. Everyone I dealt with during this visit displayed the highest level of customer service and I would highly recomnmend this hotel to anyone visiting the Los Angeles area.

title: “Great short stay!”
text: The Hotel Carlton is a great place to stay in SF. The service was the best I have seen in a long time. Very friendly staff who was willing to help with any request. The hotel is in a perfect location, situated just a few blocks from Union Square, Chinatown and a fun walk to the Fisherman's Wharf. The only thing I would advise people of is the fact that this hotel is very old and has been remodeled to feel cozy, but there is no air conditioning in the building. Maybe we are just too used to A/C, since we are from Arizona. The walls are also very thin, but the noise from the hall was not bad. I would recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to SF. Another recommendation is to book the hotel on their website with the valet parking package. Not only do you not need a car in SF, but there are no parking spaces either. The parking we did see was at least $25 a day. The Hotel Carlton is a great value, and they make up for lack of luxury with a great rate and excellent service.

title: “Excellent staff, best Wifi, amazing customer service & warm, I love it!”
text: I stay at this hotel almost once a week not because I don't have a choice but due to the wonderful, polite, patient & very efficient employees there from the front desk to the kind GM who is available most of the time, to the drivers of the shuttle, the brkfst room attendant to the cleaners! they all go out of their ways to help no matter how busy they are. The area is safe but far away from night life & shopping but the clean rooms, comfortable beds, excellent upgraded internet system, testy brfkst & a free shuttle service will make it up to you. I highly recommend this hotel to solo travelers like me or to families as you get more than you really ask for or think of. Will always be back, thank you Fairfield Inn Marriott, NE.

title: “Nice location, nice hotel”
text:
Close to all of the action in downtown. Clean hotel. Right next to parking garage (a little pricey) but convenient. Garage adjoins directly to Peabody Place.....nice for coffee, movies, etc. One short block to the action on Beale Street.
Lots of panhandlers at night....everywhere. But to be expected for area.

title: “Sweet Dreams”
text: Extremely pleasant personnel. Room was clean and enjoyed the gym and pool but didn't use the spa. Massage available. A little on the heavy side when it came to buying a tube of pretzels in the room. $9.00 for pretzels and $8.00 for a bottle of water. Easier to go across the street to the local deli and order a sandwich and coffee. Go to Mel's diner around the corner for breakfast. Location is near the cable car off Market Street. Tremendous restaurants in Little Italy. Avoid Chinatown as it is filthy.

title: “Stay away if you don't want your holiday spoiled”
text: Staff is rude, room are not clean. Someone was complaining in the lobby regarding bed bugs. Not recommended at all. If you don't want to bring little criters home reconsider booking somewere else.

title: “Close to uptown and very clean.”
text: Two things would give this hotel an excellent rating. 1: Front desk 2: Parking The front desk person (a young man) was nice enough, friendly, chatty, but not extremely thorough. As a HH Gold Member, you can opt for extra points or free breakfast. After a long day of working, didn't think about getting the breakfast coupon and had to go back down after settling in to ask about it. He had automatically given me the points instead of offering breakfast. Small detail I know. The parking is something they can't really do anything about. It is in a deck that is connected to both hotels-Hampton and Hilton Garden Inn. It has a very closed in feeling and just seems a little creepy coming back in at night. There is a sign when you enter the deck that offers Valet Parking but I never saw an attendant. Everything else about this hotel is excellent. Rooms are nice, very clean, attractive. Beds are extremely comfortable. I probably would not walk uptown by myself at night from here, but would with friends. It is only a few blocks away.

title: “Impressive”
text: The newly renovated hotel is not only a great deal but impressive as well. The rooms are larger than the usual standard big city hotel room for a very reasonable rate. Hotel is clean, staff is friendly and is located in the entertainment area of the city. Not difficult to get anywhere from here either walking, cab, bus or getting to the "L". Nice restaurant/bar located in hotel with variety of dishes to choose from. Staff there very friendly as well. Hotel has a pool, very clean. This was our second stay at this hotel and once again we were very pleased. Give it a try!

title: “My husband and I enjoyed the stay at this location.”
text: The young lady at the desk was very pleasant. The room was clean especially the bathroom. The good part was that the room did not smell like smoke this has been our experience at other hotels.

title: “The Talbott: Above and Beyond!"”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Talbott Aug. 1st as the beginning of my husband's 50th birthday celebration (we flew to Cozumel the next day and stayed at the amazing Cozumel Palace Resort--see my review). This was our 3rd year of staying at the Talbott, and because I'm a hopeless romantic, I asked for the same room we'd had the previous 2 years. The Asst. Mgr., James, said that unfortunately, the room was occupied, but that he had one he thought we'd like. He surprised us by upgrading us to a 1 bdrm. suite for no extra charge and graciously, wouldn't even allow us to tip him!
The suite was magnificent--we couldn't have asked for a lovelier room. Like the entire hotel, it was elegant without being ostentatious. That is the Talbott in a nutshell--understated elegance. The incredible service, immaculate and beautifully appointed rooms, location, and overall feel ensure that we will always continue to return to the Talbott--our favorite hotel in Chicago:-)

title: “Great Service and Staff”
text: I have stayed at a few other hotels in El Paso; however, I chose this hotel because it was close to my son and daughter in law. From the moment I walked in on Thanksgiving evening, the ladies greeted us with a smile. The first room we had was next to several families who had small children and those children were running up and down, screaming and yelling at 6:30 in the morning and not one of the parents quieted their children. I told the front desk and they offered to move us to another room and they apologized for my inconvenience, which I told them that I did not blame them at all. When I was checking out, the lady that checked us out was the lady that I booked my room with and she remembered me and that my daughter in law was about to give birth and asked me if the baby arrived (yes, safe and sound). There is also a Denny's right next to this hotel which provided excellent service. Also, they offer a 20% discount if you show them your room key from La Quinta. Will definitely be back in El Paso within the next few months and will be staying at La Quinta, Lomaland.

title: “I adored this hotel.”
text: The setting was attractive and spaciolus, all staff couteous and attentive, the Sunday high teas was sumptious, Sou'Wester hotel restaurant had delicious food, close to Smithsonians and Mall. Fabulous!!!!

title: “Excellent location, well-executed”
text:
This hotel is very convenient. Easy access to/from US75 (North Central Expressway), North Park Center, and SMU. I went to downtown museums, bars in Deep Ellum and Cedar Springs, the Galleria, Richardson, etc are all were within a 15 minute drive.
My room (338) is a smaller "studio" suite, I think. Not huge but certainly adequate with a great flat-screen TV which turns to face either the bedroom OR living area, a small-but-complete kitchen and a nice bath with marble vanity. Nice-sized walk-in closet, too.
Parking is free. Breakfast is free. Evening cocktail reception is free. Local calls are free. And the hotel is very clean.
Excellent overall!

title: “Hotel is average for under $100. Horrible parking!!”
text:
Pros: 
Friendly and helpful front staff. 
Good downtown location. 
Nice lobby / fountain with average restaurants. 
Beds are nice. 
We have stayed here a few times and each time was $100 or under. So it is priced pretty competitively. 
Cons:
The parking situation is horrible. First the nightly fee is $23 and you have to valet. We stayed for 3 days and our average wait time for our vehicle was 45-1hr in the rain and cold. Doing this with an infant compunded the situation. They even lost our keys one day. Completely disorganized parking system and when the hotel is busy the guest suffers. Make sure you check if there is an event at the hotel. If so, I would recommend not staying for this reason alone. 
Rooms are showing thier age. The bathroom had mildew on the ceiling and mold around the bath. Pretty unclean for the property type. Doors, walls, carpet and furniture were all pretty beat up. 
Overall, I like Hyatt and will continue to stay at their properties. However, I will probably not stay at this one due to the parking and that there are better kept properties for the same price in the area.

title: “Great service, nice room but no atmosphere”
text:
Yes, the four seasons provides excellent service, from bell hop to room service... No doubt about that. But if "ambiance" is what you're looking for, this hotel is not going to meet the mark. The entrance and lobby are on different floors, both are unwelcoming, dark and gloomy, devoid of any distinguishing features or plant life. 
My room was big and very comfortable, relatively well sound-proofed, great bed. The bathroom was also large, well appointed with a marvellous shower. One slight negative aspect was the drain smell from the wash basin. The other bigger downside was the wifi. I needed to connect to a number of conference calls at odd times. It was impossible to stay connected for more than 5 minutes before the signal dropped, even with their high speed option. Very annoying.
For business, I would probably go back, although the lousy wifi was a huge handicap. But frankly, for the price, I would rather find somewhere with more character.

title: “Modern, Relaxed Hotel - great for families”
text: Stayed two nights with my husband and two children in a room with two double beds. The staff were very friendly. We were offered an early check-in which was efficiently handled. The area map we were given was handy and useful. Our room had three sections: a seating area, a bathroom area, and the two double beds were located towards the rear of the room. Each section could be closed off by an opaque screen, This was handy when privacy was needed for changing, and when we sent the kids to bed for the night, my husband and I were able to watch TV in the front seating area without disturbing the kids. There is a nice park across the hotel and a pedestrian area that leads towards Battery Park. The West Side Highway is just around the corner which makes catching a cab easy. There is also a food court in the World Financial Center, an office building located across the street from the hotel. Very clean hotel with great amenities. We will certainly stay here again the next time we visit NYC.

title: “Make sure to get a renovated room!”
text:
The only reason to stay in this hotel is for its' proximity to USC.
The room I was in had a Motel 8 feel to it - peeling wallpaper, scratchy sheets, old & tired air conditioner, musty hallways. I understand they are currently renovating though, and I have high hopes that this hotel will someday be a better place to stay. 
The elevators need some work - One of them would come to the floor, open the doors 2 inches and then close quickly. I would then have to wait for the elevator to be called to a different floor before I could push the down button again. During one elevator ride, it stopped on a different floor and the people got in and it started to close the doors but then stopped. One of the men inside physically pushed the doors closed and we continued on our way.
On the morning I was leaving town, my bathroom sink started convulsing-literally, a cable came down and started spewing out brown liquid while making a machine gun like noise. I called to the front desk and they weren't overly concerned, just said they would send someone up. Ten minutes later, the sink started gushing water. I called back and they didn't answer. So I gathered my stuff and left - wet hair and all (hard to dry your hair when you can't get in the bathroom).
I did check out and let them know about the sink and that the carpet was now getting wet and she again wasn't concerned. 
I only ever stay here if I have to be close to USC. For the price, you can stay at a much nicer hotel in LA. Long Beach even - way better hotels for the same price.

title: “Excellent Value”
text: We stayed one night (January 2) and I wished we could have spent a week. I wasn't expecting much for $129 a night but was VERY pleasantly surprised. This reminds of me of small,reasonably upscale hotels in Europe. It is cozy and well-maintained with polite, helpful staff. Our room,#812, was adeuate in size, and very pretty. It had a well stocked mini fridge, wine and snack selection. For our $129 we received: complimentary valet parking, a generous continental breakfast for two, turn-down service complete with a chocolate on the pillow AND The Washington Post delivered at our door. Ours may have been off-season rates, but even for somewhat more $$$ this hotel would still represent an excellent value. I have paid far more for far less. The Henley Park has a romantic little restaurant, bar and an attractive lobby with fireplace. Ours was a "deluxe" category room. I understand some of the rooms are newly refurbished with four poster beds. The "standard" rooms are much smaller, maybe too small, if you travel with much luggage. Since there is quite a variety of rooms and furnishings, I suggest you talk with reservations about what you would like and need and have them describe what's available. It is a brisk 1/2 hour walk to the National Gallery and the Mall and we felt safe taking that route during the day.

title: “What Happened”
text: Stayed here in August 2011 and it was great, what happened? This trip was made for a family member having surgery at one of the downtown hospitals, as were the three previous stays. Stayed here before, and was pleased, this last trip, not so good. The beds were good, but room not the cleanest....TV was so dark, hard to see. No linen in room, had to ask for linen. For two people we received, two towel, two wash clothes for showering, no hand towel to dry hands. Could not use chain to secure door from inside, only chain hanging there, no latch hook. Curtain did not close over windows, Breakfast not good either, waffle batter out sitting on counter and sour tasting, before it was kept refrigerated. Although staff nice, had to wait over 50 min for shuttle pick up at Medical facility. And to top it all off, access to room blocked before check out time, entry key card did not work, we were told room had already been cleaned. Will not return here.

title: “loved the Elan”
text: My daughters and I stayed at the Elan for a week in April. My son-in-law booked it for us, so We had no idea what we would get. We loved it and would stay again any time we are in LA. The room was extremely clean and and pleasant. The staff were very helpful and friendly. The breakfast was more than enough for anyone. The location was great for shopping or sight seeing. We always felt very safe there, and that is important for women traveling alone. The bedding was so comfortable, it felt like home. I would recommend it to anyone.

title: “Overall A Good Value”
text:
For $110 a night near the Capitol, it was a great buy. First the negatives. A liitle dark and danky, and neighborhood a little scary at night. Not much to do for kids.
Now the Positives. Great staff, and an awesome location. A block from Union Station so the Metro is very handy. Also, only about a 10 minute walk to the Capitol. Would be a 2 star if I had to pay the 300 + asking price, but through priceline it was a great stay!

title: “All round good hotel”
text: Hi, The hotel staff are friendly and efficient. Collected my car quickly. I found it quiet and clean.

title: “We always enjoy our weekends at the Omni!”
text: Great hotel - great service! Comfortable rooms and helpful staff.

title: “Great Location”
