text: This hotel provides a perfect location with perfect service except for on one occasion this past weekend. On the Saturday before Easter our room wasn't made up until our complaint at 3 pm. Everyone is otherwise is very friendly and takes care of your every need. The bed is comfortable, room quiet and best of all a small hotel gets you away from the frenetic style of a large city when you need quiet.

title: “Convenient, clean and cheap”
text: We chose this hotel for its location, only 10 mins drive from Phoenix Sky Harbor airport and because it was very cheap! Our room was nice & clean room (fairly small but perfectly OK for a night). Check-in & check-out were both efficient and friendly. Breakfast was fine - fruit, patisserie, breads, cooked items - but coffee was awful & the juice very sickly & sweet. We left very early the next morning so didn’t try the pool but it looked fine. Recommended if you need somewhere to crash before / after a flight.

title: “Exemplifies the luxury of Four Seasons!”
text: A return, and too short, visit to the Four Seasons on E. Delaware Place at N. Michigan Ave. What a great neighborhood! What a great hotel! It's pricey, but so worth it. There is no "warm & fuzzy" feeling here, but staff are consummately professional and efficient. I took a city-view room this time, on the 33rd floor, just to have a different experience from looking out the other side of the hotel. It was just fine. The beds are so comfortable, the closet is large, the bathroom is top of the line. Had a little problem with dropped internet connections one morning, so the front desk person volunteered to remove all internet charges for my whole stay - unexpected but kind. This hotel makes you feel as comfortable as at home, even when you're far from home.

title: “Frienly staff, nice hotel, great location”
text:
The hotel is really nice and clean. The rooms are good but the bathroom is rather small, the bath itself slippery and has no place for putting the shampoo and staff.
Regular rooms has no fridge. We also stayed in a junior suit that wasuchmore comfotable and had a fridge, though bathroom was thw same.
The hotel staff is really nice and friendly.
Nice buffet breakfast, offering quite a big veriaty.
Above all, the great location next to the galleria is Really great, its just a short walk, and you can take the hotel's shuttle for free.
Dont let the proximity to the highway scare you, you can not hear it and if you wish they'll give you a room in the other side.

title: “No Sleep”
text:
The Radisson Austin is in a great downtown location on the lake. Although efforts have been made to upgrade and improve this facility, they haven't been completely successful.
Check-in was easy and efficient. The room was large, but the decor was a mix of fabrics and colors that didn't quite match. Sleep number beds are a nice touch, but they didn't help our sleep, because of the poor soundproofing and noise from other guests at 3 am.
We awoke at 3 in the morning to a loud group of young people coming home after a night on the town. Unfortunately, some or all of these people were in the room across the hall from us. We hoped they would quiet down and go to sleep. After almost 30 minutes we called the front desk. The woman working was very apologetic and immediately responded to our complaint by going (or sending somebody) to the room. The noise stopped for a short time, but began again. To make a long story short, the hotel employees weren't able to maintain quiet until sometime after 5 am. 
I appreciated the efforts made by the hotel staff to respond to my complaints. They tried to control the people. Unfortunately there is nothing they could have done to control the lack of soundproofing. 
We checked out the next morning (two days earlier than planned) and the clerk asked us if everything was ok. When I explained that it wasn't and why it wasn't, the response was nothing more than a two word, "I'm sorry." I don't know what I expected in response to this complaint, but I know it was more than what I received. 
Despite the great location, I cannot recommend this hotel.

title: “Pretty good, great location”
text: This hotel was very clean, comfortable and well appointed. The location was especially good for accessing Central Park and all it has to offer. I was disappointed with the lack of a safe in our room and the small safety deposit boxes provided at reception (although they were free of charge), and the showerhead in our room leaked pretty badly. Having said that, on the whole I enjoyed staying here and wouldn't object to staying again.

title: “Excellent Location & Very Nice Hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Fitzpatrick for our 9th anniversary and we could not have been more pleased with the location and the hotel itself. It was nice being so close to Grand Central; we were able to travel throughout the city easily using the subway. Our room was clean, big and quiet. As a lot of the reviewers have stated; the bed was fantastic. Everyone we met on staff was very pleasant and helpful, especially Mike the doorman. We always felt welcomed on our return from long days of site seeing. We truly love New York and it’s especially nice when you stay at a hotel that makes you feel relaxed. Keep in mind this is a boutique hotel, with a small lobby; but has a warm feel to it. We would not hesitate to stay here again on our next trip to the Big Apple.

title: “Excellent - Front Desk Staff Great”
text:
I checked in today and was very surprised as to how nice this particular InterContiental was. I have stayed at several other locations primarily in Toronto but this is one of the nicer properties. 
Additionally, Ed at the front desk was great upon checking in. He was very knowledgeable about the area and also followed up with me after I was in my room to ensure that I was satisfied. 
Definitely would recommend this hotel and you will enjoy the location and friendly staff.

title: “Perfect and great service”
text:
Stayed with freinds in September and we were all very pleased with the service and the room witch was big clean and very nice. We stayed four nights in a one bedroom luxery apartment, and one night i the penthouse wich was absolutely briliant, you sould try one night there the views and size of the room and terrace was much more than expected.
We also recieved graet service from the front desk through out our stay.
We Will stay at the Marmara Suites when we come to NY next time.
John From Denmark

title: “An amazing oasis”
text:
I absolutely adore this hotel. The rooms are wonderful, the beds dreamy, and the staff delightful. There are a variety of pools to choose from, all of which are excellent.
A stay at this hotel is a must-do. I'll keep coming back.

title: “Very poor service/amenities-huge disappointment”
text:
We had a reservation for 3 nights, 2 people each. We requested 2 rooms next to each other, away from the elevator, 2 beds each room. Made reservation via booking.com and confirmed with hotel. After we were told we didn't ask for 2 beds. (despite showing the booking confirmation) Did not get the rooms we wanted, different floors and close to the elevators, which was not what we requested. Our room was dark and small, and most of the outlets in the room didn't work. Called 4-5 times to reception to switch rooms, was lied to, blown off, etc...by sheer persistence we were moved to a better room but still not next to/on the same floor as our other party. Didn't seem to be a manager around or if there was one, he/she not helping or calling back.
No ice machine or refrigerator, had to request ice from front desk. No wine opener in room. Rooftop "bar" was a bar on the top floor, but totally enclosed. There was a terrace with a nice view but no wait service available, had to get your own drinks, food, etc..No in room coffee, coffee bar downstairs not open 24 hours as indicated. Our remote for the tv didn't work, had to request a new one more than twice. Our ac unit was loud and didn't seem to adjust to any set temperature. In our first room there wasn't even a readout to adjust the temperature. My sisters room had no working phone and when she requested extra towels they brought only 2, and was told there weren't any more available(!)-she had requested (4).
THE ELEVATOR IS SO SLOW YOU COULD PUSH THE BUTTON, GO BACK TO YOUR ROOM, FIX YOUR HAIR, BRUSH YOUR TEETH, COME BACK OUT AND IT STILL WOULDN'T BE THERE. We used the stairs many times. 
Would never go back.

title: “Lucky to find Ace Hotel”
text:
I was planning my trip to New York since summer, having read a lot of information and reviews. Finally, I booked for Ace Hotel the last week before my trip (ten days' wedding trip with my husband), as then they offered a lower rate than earlier. However, I was rather sceptical, as there is a lot of complaints about expensive and small hotel rooms in nyc.
Fortunatelly, the place is exactly what i wished to find: great disigned and decorated to the last detail, young crowd, fabulous enormous lobby and bar, with an indepedent - no hotel - atmosfere. Our room was like a small studio, with a leather sofa and other minimal - retro furniture, very clean and comfortable. Moreover, they satisfied my request for a city view, giving us a 10th floor room with faboulous view to the Empire State building, which was just opposite the hotel!! (5 blocks north) 
What was also important to me, is that it gave me a feeling of an independent residence, because of its studio effect and the hotel's discrit, but effective staff. 
But, beware: if you look for a more traditional hotel, you may not be satisfied.
Just to mention a disadvantage: the air condition heating system is not efficient enough for chilling winter days..
Therfore, I highly recomend this hotel, if your wishes are like mine!

title: “What a great hotel!”
text: Based on reviews here at TripAdvisor, I booked this hotel initially for a week's stay, and ended up extending my lodging there for three weeks. The cleanliness, the friendly and professional staff, the good food, and the sound sleep every night was tremendously welcome. The exercise room is great, with lots of machines, and neat as a pin. The hotel is located just far enough from I-10 that road noise is not an issue. This will be my preferred place to stay for business on the west side of Houston, for certain!

title: “Little gem in Chinatown”
text: Honestly, I can't fault this hotel. It's clean, modern, in a great location (couple of blocks from Canal Street subway). The staff were friendly and helpful, the room was big (much bigger than I expected!) and clean. Free wifi and a great breakfast at a local cafe (Mama). I would definitely recommend this hotel and it will be the first place I look for a room if I go to New York again.

title: “Classic New York Hotel”
text: A beautiful hotel, loved the lobby, ballroom, atmosphere and breakfast.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
We stay here for just one night on April 7th. Short and quick here. Hotel was clean, check-in was easy. We had a room on the top floor(28th) right next to the elevator. Never heard it and didnt have any issue with noise with the exception of some street noise. Had a few sirens and car horns that woke us up. Both were expected and not a huge issue to us.
Was disappointed that the restaurant was closed.Were told they had a gas leak if some sort. Not only closed the restaurant but i guess there was no food prep aloud in the entire hotel. Strange that next door pizza place was open and serving. 
We went to have a drink at there rooftop bar which was small but nice. We asked if we could have food delivered to the bar and were told we couldnt. Understandable but with no option for food in the hotel we hoped they would make an exception. 
I will say the female bartender(shawn) wrote down a few options for a late night bite that will deliver to our room and that was appreciated. 
This was the only hiccup the rest of the stay was nice and we would choose the Affinia again in a heart beat.

title: “Pure, unexpected bliss!”
text:
What a pleasant surprise! We were recommended this Hotel as the splendid Sherry Netherland where we were staying was to be full later into our stay.
Our arrival was , initially a little drab as from the 11th Ave entrance one has no idea of the splendour within. A swift , efficient check in to an enormous 7th floor room with a stunning city view. Our room is exceptional in so many ways; spacious , huge walk in shower, seperate loo, giant bathtub , twin sinks , great lighting , more than adequate electric sockets, iron and board, fine ameninities. Housekeeping , linen , cleanliness and attention to detail of the highest standards.
Our meals , including breakfast were excellent , well served by efficient , friendly and warm staff.
the Wine hour served excellent , complimentary Chardonnay each evening and , indeed our every need was catered for.
The Highlight is sunset on the roof at the superb Roof , Press Club....honestly there can be no finer venue in the city with stunning views of the city , Time Square llights flashing and the sun settimg over the Hudson with Inrepid , cruise liners and the water life displayed before you.
We will recommend this hotel to all our friends visiting NY and , should the opportunity arise there can be no doubt where we will stay should we return to this fabulous , vibrant , friendly city.

title: “New York”
text: fantastic location, in the heart of manhattan with everything you need around you & more. very comfortable, clean, tidy & all staff were very helpful at all times, would definately go back again.

title: “*much* better than expected!!!”
text: After reading all the negative reviews online, I was almost afraid to try this place, but ended up getting a room here anyway because it was last minute and everything else was booked up. As noted in previous reviews by others, the lobby does have wood paneling in it, but it's more of an upscale interior decorating sort of look with nice art sculpture. The desk clerk was friendly and helpful, and we had no issues with service at all. The room was clean and did not have any bad odors. I did smell air freshener when we walked in in initially, but it was not unpleasant. The room was very clean, the bed was *very* comfortable and all in all it was surprisingly quiet considering that area of town. I put the 'do not disturb' sign on the door and no one bothered us at all. The pool and hot tub were clean and everyone there were friendly. I noticed that they appear to have a uniformed on-site security staff as well. Parking was a bit tight, but I was able to find a space each time I left and came back to the room. This is not a bad place to stay at all, and probably one of the nicer rooms you could stay in that area of town and for a price that low.

title: “Pleasant surprise”
text: You don't have to be an Eagles fan but that made it fun. Older building, well restored. Room was surprisingly comfortable, nice decor and the bathroom restored and well functioning. Safe neighborhood.

title: “It worked for what we needed”
text:
Got this on a Priceline bid. I was initially disappointed because I was hoping for a grand hotel stay. This is rated 4* and I'm not sure it met those starndards for me. But, this worked for us because they upgraded us to a 1 bedroom. 
The kitchen area was somewhat odd--there were some dishes in the dishwasher, but no silverware. We weren't planning on actually using the kitchen, so it wasn't a big deal, but don't expect forks, knives, etc if you plan on using the kitchen.
The bed in the bedroom was very comfortable. However, the foldout bed of the couch was really bad.
The neighborhood is mostly office buildings. There was a Au Bon Pan, McDonalds within walking distance, but most everything else was a cab ride away. I don't think I'd feel safe walking in the area at night, there were many homeless and beggars when we returned from dinner at Daily Grill. After reading other reviews, did not try the restaurant in the hotel.
Staff was very friendly.

title: “Excellence in the city”
text: From check-in to checkout, everything was superb. The location is perfect, the hotel is swank, and the staff is very personable. You will be staying in a luxury hotel without the stuffiness. I love Kimptons, but this one was topnotch.

title: “Nice!”
text:
We combined business with pleasure for a weekend in the Big Apple and decided on the Royalton based on Tripadvisor reviews.
The first thing that hit us was the dim lighting and trendy atmosphere. After a while the dimness becomes annoying but that may have to do with our advancing years (we're both 47). The corridors to the rooms are even darker. 
The room was superb (904) with working fireplace but best of all; a Bose iDock for my iPod. Superb! 904 is a large room and has a pleasant decor with a few very nice pieces of furniture. Again, the lighting was just about adequate. Nice flatscreen which we didn't use.
The bed linen is superb and the duvet of good quality. Light switches are a tad confusing. Wardrobe space is too small and awkward to get to. There's also a flat screen in the bedroom we did use.
The bath is great. It is a five foot round tub. Excellent! Water pressure supeb. The sink arrangement is less than practical. Lighting again is an issue here.
The staff at the hotel are young, good looking and very friendly.
The location is great too and we managed to walk to most places we wanted to visit.
Overall, we loved our trip and liked the hotel. Would we stay there again? Possibly but we are likely to try somewhere else next time.

title: “A perfect gem in the heart of the Upper West Side...”
text:
Just a perfect place well situated in the Upper West Side. Good location...
close to Central Park, Restaurants, Museums and transportation. Immaculately
clean, pleasant staff, comfortable bed. Rooms are not huge but are certainly ample.
Reminds me of hotels in Europe. This is my new 'go to' place!!!

title: “Great Family Hotel!”
text: We were pleasantly surprised by how great this hotel was. The rooms were very clean, the front desk staff was very prompt, accommodating and attentive to our needs. The location was ideal. Having a kitchen and separate seating area so we did not all have to go to bed at the same time was ideal with young children.

title: “Very Disappointing.”
text:
We stayed only one night at the Solita, and unfortunately, it was very disappointing. 
Our room had a foul odor, and the front desk was slow in responding to our requests for air freshener. In fact, our other requests pretty much were neglected, and we had to repeatedly call the front desk for a confirmation of our request for a car service for early the next morning. When contacting the hotel about these complaints, we were met with denial of said complaints.

title: “One night stay”
text: Stayed here for a quick business trip. Arrived about 7:30 in the evening and was starving. Ordered some wings and pizza and it hit the spot. Order arrived promptly in 30 min as room service person quoted. Prices were reasonable and taste was good. Hit the concierge lounge for a bit of desert and it was great pecan pie and the biggest chocolate chip cookie I've ever seen. I believe this hotel was once a Embassy Suites so all of the rooms were suites. The decor was fine and the room was clean and comfortable for my one night stay. Hopefully my next trip will allow me to stay longer and enjoy more of this hotel.

title: “not very irish service a let down”
text: stayed here recently call sitself an irish hotel.. didnt make proper tea didnt meet any irish staff...? no irish atmosphere half the bar was closed for the majority of our stay.. didnt recieve any complimentary drink as i believe is standard after every 2 or 3 drinks despite being hit for 18 percent 'gratuity' with every order of food or drink...food very overpriced. rooms were nice but felt like the place was a rip-off.. concierge wouldn order taxi for us was trying to pressure us to hire some private car for minimum of 200+ dollars (obviously on commision) when room service breakfast card wasnt collected and brought it to receptions attention they didnt seem too bothered and said they would look into it and i heard no more about it.. is handy place to stay as is well located but found service and staff to be wanting..

title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text: The hotel itself was not that amazing, but the service I recieved was AMAZING! They was one bell hop, Derrick Little, that was the friendliest, move helpful person I have ever met. He always greeted me and my friends with a smile and was always eager to help us and hold the door. He gave great directions to where ever we went and informed us about the shuttle that would take us anywhere we wanted to go. He really made my stay enjoyable.

title: “True vacation in the city”
text: We have stayed at the Magnolia before and loved it, so jumped at the chance to stay there again. The location can't be beat: it's close to restaurants, shopping, and entertainment. The staff members treat each guest like a valued customer. We love the wine/beer reception, cookies and milk in the evening, and breakfast in the morning. It's a true vacation in the city.

title: “Cadillac Hotel hygine issues”
text: My friend and I contracted bed bugs/scabies from this hotel. We could see the bugs on our bunk bed clearly the entire time we were there. I've spent a fortune on treatment and doctors visits, not to mention that I'm scarred from head to toe. I would not reccomend this hotel to ANYONE.

title: “Excellent Choice”
text:
This was one of the absolute best hotels I've ever stayed at. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful with whatever questions I had. We were checked into a smoking room the first night, and by the next afternoon, while we were out, they had our things moved to a nonsmoking room right next to the pool. 
Most of all, they served complimentary breakfast every morning with an abundance of wonderful food to choose from. My friends and I never eat breakfast, but every morning there we were up at 7:30 to eat. 
Everything we wanted to do, the Zoo, Old Town, the beaches, Balboa Park, etc were only a short 5 minute, at the most, ride on the very driver friendly interstates.
The hotel is geered more towards families, but my friends and I, who are in our 20s, enjoyed every minute of it. I would definitely recommend staying here if you seek excellent service, great breakfast, and easy access to the attractions of San Diego.

title: “Westin Philly”
text: Excellente localisation. Bel hôtel. Only drawback,...internet access free only in lobby. For a business trip, with that location and the cost of the room,...we should have free internet access int the room

title: “Impressed with the Red Roof Inn”
text: Very well located, clean and pleasant rooms - I would stay here again in Chicago!

title: “LEFT out in the cold!”
text: We stayed on opening night really wanting to give this a try since we are Seahawks Season Ticket holders and Mariners fans. Unfortunately the fire alarm went off when we were just about asleep for the night. We grabbed a blanket for the baby and ran outside down several flights of stair in our jammies. The fire department came and we continued staying outside...NO ONE from the hotel EVER came out to say it was safe to go outside. My husband being angry went in to the desk and asked what the deal was and was told they didn't have TIME to tell their guests they could come back in as they were answering THE PHONE!!! I was out in the cold in just a nightgown and our two month old baby had on nothing but a diaper and fortunately we grabbed a thing blanket on the way out. There was never any apology from the staff...it was a horrid way to treat paying guests. The rooms were very average and the noise level with the trains make it hard to get any rest. We asked for extra towels and never got any.

title: “Very tight quarters - needs some up-keep”
text:
I realize that New York City has a different set of expectations when it comes to hotels - most are small, feature tiny elevators and aging facades, but a little up-keep can go a long way. The Doubletree on 36th suffers from the same afflictions of most aging buildings in Manhattan - tiny rooms, decades of layers paint, noisy elevators and narrow hallways. 
I am not saying this was a "bad" hotel - I mean the location is very central to all the happenings of Times Square, Madison Square Garden and the rest of Midtown, but I feel like for the money, the management could spend a little more money on the small things, like updating the bathrooms and brightening up the paint to give the hotel a little more visual appeal that is expected with a mid-level hotel. 
Staff was very friendly and helpful, but next time I think I'll spend the extra $30/might for the full-service Hilton.

title: “Top notch service...”
text: I guess you expect great service from any Fairmont Hotel, but the staff here exceeded my expectations. From the front desk staff, to the valet, the bell staff, the housekeeping staff, every need was not only met, but anticipated. I hosted a small group here and highly recommend the Fairmont Olympic for its location, quality of rooms and furnishings, and friendly, efficient staff.

title: “Outstanding in every respect”
text:
We arrived at the palomar as part of our honeymoon touring the west coast of California. As such we have experienced a lot of different hotels in a short amount of time. The palomar was exceptional in every regard (apart from some pretty steep parking charges!)
Upon arriving we were congratulated on our marriage and told we were upgraded to a suite on the sixteenth floor. The suite wasn't quite ready when we arrived but we were invited to have a complimentary glass of wine in the lobby with the other guests for their wine hour - it was a lovely way to relax after our journey. The room was ready quickly and upon entering we were very impressed. The living space was lovely; modern decor, comfortable and a great tv! The bed was huge and comfortable and the bathroom was excellent. Some other reviews have criticised elements of the bathroom but we found it to be excellent. 
The balcony overlooked the pool area so we ventured down for happy hour. Contrary to other reports we found the staff to be very helpful and we had two $5 cocktails which were both delicious and strong! Indeed one was a little too strong and the staff immediately brought fresh lemonade and an extra glass to help dilute the drink at no extra charge. The pool, loungers and general ambience were lovely and we spent quite a lot of time there as it was the perfect place to relax. 
The front desk also couldn't have been more helpful. They not only provided maps and directions but also recommended a few bars - which we tried out and indeed had an excellent night out. 
The only issue as mentioned was the price of parking - $35 per night, however it did mean that they car was safe so really must grumble. 
Perhaps the greatest demonstration of what the Palomar is really about came at check-out. Having asked how our stay was, the assistant front office manager, Johnson Menezes asked where we were going next. When we told him (the Bellagio in Vegas) he said that he knew somebody who worked there so would let them know we were coming. True to his word, by the time we arrived in Vegas that evening, we had a message waiting for us from the team at the Bellagio who said they knew we were valued guests of the Palomar and as such they wanted to help us in any way that they could. You simply cannot buy that level of personal touch and as such, we would now only stay at the Palomar when staying in San Diego - something which I really happens again soon.

title: “Great easy nice place to stay! Clean and Professional!!! Wonderful Staff.”
text: Great easy nice place to stay! Clean and Professional!!! Wonderful Staff.

title: “Lovely stay at the Benjamin”
text: We returned today from a weekend stay in New York City. My husband booked our stay at the Benjamin on Orbitz as part of a package with our flight, which was a great deal. We loved our stay there...the location was great and the hotel itself was lovely. We were fortunate to receive a complimentary upgrade to a one-bedroom suite for our anniversary which was a real treat. The room size was very generous and it was tastefully decorated. The king-size bed was so, so comfortable and the pillow menu was fun to choose from! It was noisy outside our window but to us that was part of the ambience of the city, we loved it! Sadly the restaurant was closed for refurbishing, so I can't comment on that. The staff was very genuine and helpful...thanks to the manager William for the champagne he sent to our room, and also to the concierge Sara for her great dining advice. It was such a great first time trip to New York, largely thanks to the Benjamin!

title: “Great stay at a great hotel!!!”
text:
Just returned from our weekend in San Francisco.
After reviewing most of the hotels we decided to stay at the Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf.
We booked 2 connecting rooms. One for my son and the other for my wife and I.
The rooms were nicely upgraded and had excellent lighting which many hotels these days do not. The personnel were all very cordial and proficient.
The location of the hotel was just a block from all the activities the area has to offer.
We did not dine in the hotel due to our friends
making reservations at various restaurants in town.
Yes, the bathrooms are on the small side but very functional and adequate.
This hotel made for a very comfortable weekend escape.
We plan to stay at this hotel again on our next S.F. visit.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: We recently visited California and stayed at four hotels while we were there, the Marriott Courtyard San Diego Airport was by far the best location. It was clean, comfortable, great location, great service and the breakfast was very good with many options. I would highly recommend this hotel for any travelers business or family vacation.

title: “Great for Groups”
text: The service team at the Residence Inn Gaslamp has proven to be a truly service oriented group at a great property location. We have brought three separate groups of 15 or more international travelers to the property and received world class service every time. The service team has met us at check-in and expedited the process for the groups and gotten us out quickly to enjoy the Gaslamp District and the waterfront instead of standing in line. The rooms are all well-appointed with comfortable furniture, flat screen tv’s, and kitchenette. Not that you need any of that because the property is located in the middle of the Gaslamp District’s restaurants, pubs, Petco stadium and the waterfront. The complimentary breakfast has included a wide variety of items including fresh fruit and even fresh homemade banana bread. Every guest in our groups has walked away loving San Diego and that is due in large part to our accommodations at this property. Without a doubt we will continue to host our groups at the Residence Inn Gaslamp District because we always get first class treatment at a great location.

title: “Clean, peaceful and great stay!”
text: Rooms were clean,air conditioner worked well,the maid service very good,location perfect for our needs. The staff was very helpful, and professional. Again, staff was really helpful. Has a great location. Look forward to another stay soon.

title: “Hate to stay anywhere else!!!”
text: This is my favorite hotel in Manhattan. Perfect location, rooms are exceptionally nice and free tea (Mighty Leaf) in the morning. Again, good customer service is imperative and the Eventi provides it. Free internet service if you are a Kimpton member, which is easy to do. Also, love Kimpton's raid the mini-bar for members, saves on a couple of snack purchases.

title: “A nice, inexpensive place to stay in downtown close to many sights.”
text: A block off Wacker, the La Quinta is located near the Willis Tower, water taxis, a few CTA lines and Union Station. There are many restaurants in the area, but most close at 5 or 6, due to being in the financial district. Room service/delivery from Italian Village is available. A short walk will get you to a few bars and late night restaurants though. There is a small pool and hottub, that wasn't ever busy. The hotels breakfast is very good, with an extensive offering. Fruits, yogurt, cereals, waffles, muffins, pasteries, bacon, sausage, eggs and biscuits and gravy and coffee, teas and juices. Definately get up for the breakfast!

title: “Mold and Hairs in the Rooms!”
text: My family and I recently had a weekend getaway in Jacksonville. Florida using a Groupon deal with this hotel. I travel a good bit for work and see many hotels across the United States every year. I have NEVER stayed in a hotel this deplorable in all of my travels. The hotel room smelled of mold, and rightly so when you entered the bathroom and found all of the mold growing on the walls and around the base of the tub and toilet. There were also hairs from previous guests in one of the beds and lining the sink. To top off the disgraceful conditions of the rooms and the overall outdated feel of the hotel they were having some kind of convention the night we arrived that lasted until after 11:30 with loud music that could be heard all of the way up to the 4th floor. After the convention was over and I thought we might actually get some sleep we had a group of children running up and down the hall outside of our room until 2:15 in the morning and pulling the fire alarm for the hotel TWICE! Needless to say we did not use the second night of our stay with this hotel and immediately left the next morning to check in the wonderful Hyatt hotel across the river.

title: “Perfect Rooms and Staff made all the difference”
text: Been to NYC many times but this time was looking forward to stay at the trump. We arrived earlier then the check in time and had to wait however they upgraded us from a park view one bedroom suit to a 2 bedroom suite with incredible view of the park. They also gave us complimentary drinks when they really didn't need to. The room was perfect, beds so comfortable. What i really liked about the room is it didn't feel like a hotel and i felt that could be ''my own apartment'', the decor was so nice that is beyond the ''another hotel room''. Staff incredibly nice, helpful and attentive. When i went for Dinner it was bit difficult to find a taxi and they offer straight away a complimentary driver to take us to our restaurant. Worth the experience.

title: “Don't let the reviews fool you!!!”
text:
This is a TERRIBLE part of town, signs all over the parking lot warn you about the loss of any belongings. The hotel is beyond old, and in terrible shape. The rooms are NOT suites....they merely have a "curtain" that you separate your bed from your TV area!!
This is not a place for children (the pool is empty, with dirt in it...obviously it has been a long time with no care). The signs in the parking lot scared us from the moment we got here....."take your belongings, take your keys,".......wow, serious warnings!!
This is not a place to stay and feel any sense of relaxation!

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: Stayed recently for 5 nights at the Colonnade hotel and loved it. The staff were very attentive and friendly, the dining room Brasserie Jo was superb and the location couldn't be better. Right across from the Prudential Centre mall, a few blocks from Copley Square, Boylston St and Newbury St and a 20 minute walk to Fenway park for a Red Sox game. Very modern room with all the amenities, would definitely want to stay here again.

title: “close to lots of shopping”
text:
After spending 2 nights in midtown to see the New Years Eve festivities, we were happy to retreat to SOHO.
The hotel staff was exceptionally friendly and efficient. We have no complaints - this is a basic, clean, comfortable and well designed hotel. It is very close to the subway station (train 1 - Houston St).
The location is 2 blocks away from tons of shopping - from upscale designers to the Canal St craziness. We walked from the hotel through SOHO, Little Italy and the West Village in FREEZING temps. 
We would stay there again - in fact - we would like to have more time in this area to really explore it.

title: “Wonderful stay at the Artic Club”
text: We found the customer service during our Dec 2011 vacation at the Artic Club to be top notch. They were very accomodating about our needs and the front desk set us up in the same room when we returned from an overnight in Vancouver since we loved the room. The Artic northern light dome room is breathtaking with stained lights and carved wood shaped into a dome .....the room was being set up for a wedding and it was a sight to see. Great old bones to this hotel with charm, clean and outstanding food in hotel restaurant and room service. We will stay here again, do not be concerned with booking at this hotel!

title: “Spectacular location, and service”
text:
The hotel staff isn't kidding when they say the hotel is on Riverwalk. In my humble opinion, the location of this little boutique hotel is as good as it can get. Main entrance of the hotel opens to a busy street intersection, and plenty of hotel guest doors open directly on the Riverwalk (accessible via a set of stairs). 
We were travelling with a few friends who had young kids. The reservation staff was extremely accommodating especially with respect to needs of young children e.g. cribs, microwave and freezer in the room etc. 
Upon arrival, starting from the bellman to front-desk the staff was extremely friendly, and very helpful. 
The rooms (other than riverview ambassador) are relatively smaller in size (compared to other Omni hotels). The rooms are also a tad-bit noisy i.e. rooms don't do a good job at isolating external sounds -- perhaps this was intentional, but an inconvenience to us nonetheless.
One neat feature is that a set of (three or five or more) rooms share a common balcony. This is something unique amongst full-service hotels -- atleast i've yet to encounter it before. Adds to the 'cool-factor'.
Only valet parking is available, and can be a tad-bit expensive ($32 for overnight parking). If you don't need to get in-and-out of a garage, and simply want a parking place for the night, I would recommend parking at the public garage opposite to the hotel ($8 for overnight parking). 
All-in-all, a wonderful experience.

title: “Best Hotel in D.C.”
text: My wife and I stay in hotels all over the world. We are extremely picky. Each year we come to D.C. for 4 or 5 days of play, then I leave and she heads out to Arlington for 4 days of work. We have stayed in a number of hotels in D.C., most recently the J.W. Marriott. We decided to try the Shoreham since we love the Omni Royal Orleans. Without a doubt our experience, from the minute we walked in at 7am after a red eye flight and were immediately given a beautiful room, to staff throughout the day and the stay making sure all of our Select Guest preferences were met, it was one outstanding experience after another. Every aspect of the hotel is impeccably maintained, staff are all incredibly friendly and go out of their way to assist, every amenity is covered perfectly and even the late night dining was superior. My only complaint is that I have to wait until September to go back. Oh and by the way, the neighborhood restaurants are terrific, especially Mama Ayesha's.

title: “Wonderful Service”
text: I came to S.F. with my boyfriend- check in staff was attentive and friendly with advice. Got up to our room and was surprised to hear a knock at the door. A hotel staffer came in and gave us a bottle of wine and two photo albums, compliments of the manager! Apparently my boyfriend e-mailed the hotel explaining our vacation, and asked for a room on a high floor if possible. The attention and care we received far exceeded my expectations for such a low price for a hotel downtown in San Francisco. Would definitely recommend to anyone visiting! The elevator was slow, but its an old building so its to be expected, the service more than makes up for it!!

title: “The Best I've stayed at !”
text:
In April 2003 my friend's dad suprprised us with a trip to Chicago for her birthday. Upon our arrival, we got off the plane at O'Hare airport and boarded a taxi. While we were riding, my friend's dad called the Drake to see if there were any openings. There were. As we pulled up to the Drake my friend and I's jaws dropped. We were very "Wowed". The bellman took our bags, gave a ticket stub and took our bags up. We walked into the hotel, again being "Wowed". We went up the stairs to be greeted by a huge vase full of flowers! ( I stood next to it and it was taller than me, and I'm 5 feet! ) We turned and walked to the check-in/out counter. Check-in was quick. We were told we would be staying one the 1st floor ( one story up from Lobby (L) level ) and that our room number would be room 115. We walked to the elevators where another bellman took us up. The hallways were so quiet. We walked to our room, slid the key in and the door wouldn't take the card. After about 10 times we went and got someone. The housekeeping came with the master card. The door opened. They said they were very sorry and then left. We went to see our view: A view of Michigan Ave.! Our beds were great, and we had two beautiful marble bathrooms with beautiful soaps and shampoos. A mending kit and a shower cap. Even more. The bathrooms had a hairdryer ( I would pack a hair dryer, I have short thin hair and it took me about 45 minutes for me to dry my hair and when we had to go eat it still wasn't dry! )and an extending magnifiying mirror. We had a safe, an excellent closet, walk-in. When we opened the door to the minibar, our jaws dropped again. A stocked fridge, a trow-away camara, gummies, snacks, crackers, candy, etc..... The mini-bar came with a price list , whooow. $16.50 for a trow-away camara. We had to buy it because there wasn't a store that sold camaras until 15 minutes away! 
We only bought the camara. The tv was huge. We had wireless internet on the tv like the new Msn-Tv. You could access your e-mail for a fee. 
There is a neat book in the room about the Drake's history. Queen Elizabeth II stayed there! We had free postcards and stationary in our room. We went shopping. Our bags were taken up to our rooms by the bellman, we returned to a broken door lock again. Housekeeping came and fixed it again.Around 5:00 we went to dinner at the Rosebud Steakhouse, just a short miniute walk down the street. The food was great. Our waiter was Teddy. At the end of the meal I said my compliments to the Chef. As we were about to leave, Teddy brought out the chef, so I cound meet him and tell him personally. (I want to be a cook when I grow up. 
) Later on we left to see the Lion King on Broadway around 7:00 We came back around 11:00. Our door was finally fixed. We ordered a sunday and a coke from room-service. The sunday was $3.00 and the $2.00! $! Five dollars total for a snack. Room-service promptly delivered it. We set the tray outside our room to find we we woke up and left the hotel to go home the tray was still there. We did have a free complimentary newspaper outside our door, through. I would love to come back to the Drake again, and you will love it, too.

title: “Convenient Property”
text: Returned to this property as it is convenient to airport and downtown Denver. It was around fifteen minutes from Coors Field so we took in a game. Nice rooms, comfortable pillows. I did get the room for free by cashing in some Hhonors points

title: “Wonderful surprise in the heart of New York”
text:
We were lucky enough to find the Hilton and enjoyed the stay there immensely . 
Staff was amazing, hotel was extremely clean, and the rooms were huge. We have had a few previous bad experiences with rooms that would qualify more as closets than anything else, but this was a very very very nice hotel. We will definitely recommend and stay there when we visit new York:)

title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text: I recently completed a series of weekend stays at the Mission Valley Travelodge. I was impressed with the friendliness and courtesy of housekeeping and the front desk staff. The rates were affordable, the rooms were clean and the facility was excellent. They even were thoughtful enough to ship my cell phone charger to me after I inadvertently left it after my departure. I would not hesitate to recommend this facility to a friend. Dr. DM

title: “One word: Excellent”
text: We love staying at Courtyard when we visit Jacksonville. It is situated within a short driving distance of attractions, it is safe and secure with good car parking facilities. The rooms are well equipped and clean with very friendly and helpful staff. The beds are extremely comfortable. We enjoy the pool, gym, and fire pit. We even felt safe as tropical storm Beryl hit the area. The room was well equipped with a fridge and microwave so we were able to have a sensible breakfast and night time snacks which saved a lot of money. Staff were helpful and knowledgeable. The room had a large desk and space to work so equally suited to leisure tourist or business traveler. The Bistro was good for food, drink, and Starbucks coffee. No hesitation in recommending this to others to stay.

title: “Be aware”
text: This hotel is surrounded by homeless. People kept asking for money as we entered the hotel. The lobby was really nice, but we were disappointed because of the bad attitude of the front desk clerk. Our room did not have A/C, which I thought was odd. Anyway, I'll try another hotel next time.

title: “I will definately stay here again!”
text: I booked a room last minute for a place to sleep after a long drive. I read the reviews and some were great and some were bad but decided to give it a try since it was just off the highway. Well..... the check in process was quick and the guy at the reception desk was very friendly. After a long drive, all we wanted to do was to get a good night sleep and boy! their beds are so comfortable we slept like a baby. We were going to leave to go grab breakfast somewhere until I took a peek at their breakfast buffet. They had scrambled eggs, bacon and sausage etc. everything you can get at an IHOP but better!. We saved 30 bucks! The room was clean and smelled fresh. I will definately stay here again!

title: “Great hotel, a little bit away from the madding crowd!”
text: This is a lovely, contemporary hotel about 10 mins walk from Times Square. It has a fantastic view back up to central Manhattan. We stayed as a family of 4, and had a room with 2 double beds which was spacious enough. Lovely and clean. Complementary wine served 5-6pm was a nice touch, and our kids absolutely loved the 'pet-friendly' policy that allowed dogs into the hotel. The food at the restaurant was fabulous, and the views from the rooftop terrace superb, though we couldn't have a drink there as our children were too young. All in all we would return - we had a great stay. Right beside 'Intrepid'.

title: “Solid Friendly Staff”
text: Very good service, great staff though small no less efeective. Always enjoy my stay.

title: “What a lovely place to stay”
text:
We went to San Francisco for a wedding and many of the people attending the wedding were at the Donatello. The rooms are quite spacious - I can't say that about many hotels. The hotel was bright, very clean and had comfortable beds and chairs. Everyone we met who worked in the hotel had a kind word and a big smile. The people at the front desk and the bellmen were extremely helpful.
Getting a cab in San Francisco was a problem but the bellman went outside to help flag one down for us. It's centrally located - near Union Square. The only problem is that there's lots of noise from the street (even though we were on the 8th floor). We'd go again.

title: “A Wonderfully cosy, luxury room”
text: Couldn't be happier with the room the bedding was devine.lots of extra pillows, pillow tip mattress was sooooo comfy! Perfect Location to hop on the subway, restaurans nearby, gorgeous, safe naighborhood. The hotel was near perfect, my only 2 reservations are that we could usually smell whatever was cooking in the restaurant downstairs (not unpleasant, but not all the time!) and that we learned of a substantial parking charge upon checkout, no mention was made of it during booking or chjeck-in. Would be nice to know in advance. Otherwise, Perfect Hotel, great pleasant and courteous staff. A wonderful quiet spot close to everything!

title: “what happened to the A game?”
text:
We have spent at least one week a year for the last 4years at this hotel.As many reviewers mention,the location is excellent and the building unique.Unfortunately,the service during our most recent visit had deteriorated significantly;
-our room was serviced anytime between 11AM and 4PM even though we were out by 9 AM at the latest and had the service tag hanging outside the door.
-We specifically ask for a room with a tub-we got one but unfortunately the stopper didn't work rendering it useless.
-On a couple of occasions when our room was serviced ,used towels were removed but no fresh towels were provided.
-Hotel staff only greet guests if greeted first-otherwise they stare into the distance or chat among themselves.
It is unfortunate that at a time when competition amongst luxury hotels in Down town Austin is intensifying,the Driskill is drifting in the wrong direction.

title: “Solid for the Price”
text: This is an smallish (maybe 10 stories), older hotel that appears to have been redone and rebranded as a Comfort Inn. We had a room on front of the building with a view of the top of Empire State building. Of course room was small, but clean and well stocked. We were shopping, eating and sightseeing hard all weekend, so didn't spend much time in the room. Perfect for our purposes. Got a good AAA rate for 1 king size bed during expensive holiday season ($242). Ate breakfast out - too many awesome options to waste time with cold cereal and a dry mini muffin. Really had no interaction with staff other than quick check in and checking baggage with concierge after check out while we did a little extra sightseeing before leaving town. But those were both pleasant. Subway is nearby and many lines stop at 23rd St. Eataly (italian market/food court/coffee bar) is close and a must stop, as is the Shake Shack in nearby Madison Square Park. We usually try to book a moderately priced hotel through applecorehotels.com (Hotel @ Times Square being our favorite of those) but they were all full and this hotel is similar and almost as good.

title: “Adequate for Business Travel”
text:
It is unfair to say that the Tudor is bad- the staff is competent, the location is near public transport, and the rooms are not unclean. For someone needing just a bed, this hotel suffices. 
It is the little things- lingering, stale smells from breakfast or past guests, bad lighting in the awkwardly dark rooms looking out to the sides of other buildings- that make this hotel joyless to stay at. WIth prices and services similar to a Club Quarters or a nicer Holiday Inn, I would suggest staying elsewhere.

title: “Trendy hotel with party atmosphere”
text:
I was traveling with my friend so it was a girls trip for fun outings, trendy restaurants, good food, tennis and night life. We found this hotel fit our life style very well. The staff is amazing, very friendly and welcoming. The lobby is inviting, with silver couches, interesting interior design and amazing scent in the air. 
The rooms were a bit too small, even for two people. They did not provide an iron or an ironing board, once brought to our room, it seemed to take a huge chunk of our small real estate. The bathroom was "party-like" with silver toilets, faucets, sinks etc. And if you don't cleaning staff to disturb you in the morning, you can just push a button on the control box.
I definitely like the location of the hotel, close to all the entertainment. I liked the customer service and interior design.
I did not like the fact that I forgot to turn the "do not disturb" button off and we never had our room cleaned :(( which was extremely disappointing. Apparently, we were also supposed to have a room orientation, which never happened.
Other than that, 5 stars and will be back!!

title: “Never stay again nor recommend to anyone”
text:
Summary of my stay:
Price range: upper $200 with business discount excluding tax on weekday
Check-in Time: after 1am (no lines at the time, of course) yet it took 15 min to complete checking in. This was very irritating to me after a long night at work. 
Room location: I was disappointed by the fact that the hotel, upon seeing I was clearly tired and it was 1am, did not assign me a quiet room and instead assigned me one in front of the construction site. I was able to sleep less than 4 hours.
Room condition: some drainage issues-I was not so surprised by the level of this hotel's maintenance after seeing how the check-in was handled.
Amenities: min level-some missing standard items such as shower cap, lotion. No bathrobe-hotels in this price range ($300s) should provide bathrobes.
Customer service: terrible -I called & left a message with complaints to the hotel manager but I was never contacted back.

title: “Great stay for a conference”
text:
I stayed at Humphreys for four nights in early March for a 4-day conference that was also held on-site (meeting rooms were great). I had a wonderful view of the San Diego bay from my room and enjoyed watching the sunrise and sunset each day. I did have a maintenance issue that was handled promptly and professionally. The in-room safe was a great addition and I enjoyed the 42" LCD TV in my room. The property is absolutely beautiful, complete with lush, tropical gardens, which surround the pool and hot tub.
My only constructive comment has to do with the breakfast. A "continental" breakfast was provided in the Humphreys Restaurant and consisted of choice of a bread item, four cubes of fruit, and a small cup of juice -- not really enough for me. For the price I paid, I would have liked to see some additional options -- the same breakfast choices for four mornings just didn't cut it. While I understand that the San Diego market is more expensive, I drove 3 minutes each morning to the local McDonalds and got oatmeal for $1.99. 
I would definitely stay here again as the location is great -- close to the airport and easy access to the freeways.

title: “Great Location!!”
text: It was two blocks away from Time Square! I stayed with my Aunt so we had two double beds and a small washroom. The breakfast wasn't anything fancy, but for a great location in the center of New York AND a pretty cheap price, it was perfectly acceptable.

title: “Great Value, Amazing Location and Wonderful Service”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Monticello for 3 nights during my daughter's March Break. We had an absolutley great stay. The valet service was very helpful (thank-you Cruz) and the location perfect. Although just steps to the main stretch of Georgetown, I found that the road that Hotel Monticello is on was very quiet and peaceful. The decor is a little outdated but we learned that in a few months it will go under renovation. There is no restaurant but they do have breakfst which was very good (great assotment of fruit, yogurt, passteries and bread). The rates at this hotel are also amazing in comparison to other hotels in Georgetown. Also even if you want to see the sites in Downtown Washington the subway is only about a 10 min walk away.

title: “Better than Reviews Would Lead you to believe”
text:
This is an excellent place for the price. Do not expect a top of the line Hyatt/Wyndahm/Marriott, but then you are not paying for that. We got the package with 2 breakfasts and they were vouchers for the Du Par's across the parking lot. GREAT breakfasts. 
The location is very close to the beaches or Sea World or Old Town. We were going to stay on the water at a mid range resort (Bahia) but this was bout 1/3 the cost and was just fine. Especially for a family.
Only complaint would be the internet could have been stronger.

title: “Nice hotel, one mile from Independence Hall”
text:
This is a fairly well-maintained upscale hotel in the midst of the "Arts District," 3 blocks directly south of City Hall. It is within walking distance but not that close to Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell if you ar in Philadelphia to see those sights.We did not ride the subway but saw a station across the street from the hotel.
We had a corner room on the 14th floor. Our large, spacious room had a queen bed, flat-panel TV, sofa, desk and an arm chair with ottoman. The bed was very comfortable.
The bathroom was in good condition and had plenty of hot water.
The plumbing was noisy for a modern high rise hotel. We could hear our neighbor's pipes when he/she took a shower in the morning, which prompted us to get out of bed.
We did not eat in the hotel.

title: “Great location and great value”
text:
Just spent 5 nights with my family of 5 in a garden suite. it was our first time to SD and chose this based on other reviews and was not disappointed. It is not a glitzy 5 star resort, instead it is a very clean and comfortable 'polynesian' property with a marina at the back with the front of the property having views of SD skyline. It was good to stay over this side of SD because I dont think the Gaslamp quarter or Old Town are as kid friendly and we had a car to get around so being out of the centre was fine. only complaint is the parking charge, overnight street parking is not allowed in the area.
Staff were friendly and the tour desk girl was very helpful.

title: “Nice Place, Crap hospitality Staff”
text: We had a beautiful room, the location is great and the property is beautiful. However housekeeping didn't clean our rooms until about 3 - 4 pm. We realized this on the first day after coming back from Brunch (1pm) to dirty rooms so we asked the next day for them to come earlier since we were getting ready for a wedding the next afternoon. Byt 3pm they didn't come! As we were borrowing towels from the neighbors they showed up annoyed we were in the room and demanding a time frame for them to come back. We suggested an hour and were told that wouldn't work. UNACCEPTABLE. Called front desk to discuss situation and was directed to housekeeping to a line that didn't answer. Not pleased with this service at all!

title: “The stay was wonderful!”
text: We had a great time. The hotel took great care of us. We missed the breakfast brunch, but the chef served us anyway. When we checked in they informed us that the buffet was at ten, when we came down we learned it was at nine. The chef insisted on taking care of us. The shuttle was very useful! They drove us to dinner and the theater so we did not have to drive all over downtown. The only concern was we put cake in the mini fridge and the sensor in it read like we took something out. Just don't use the mini fridge for personal use. I will most definitely stay here again! The bed was VERY comfortable!

title: “A Quiet Retreat From Times Square Madness”
text:
My wife and I just returned home from our stay in the French Quarters. What a great place to stay, if plans require you to stay in or around Times Square! Neither one of us cares a bit for the glow, the roar, and the fervent pace of tourist-centric frenzy in the Square. A conference at the nearby Marriott Marquis required us to stay nearby, however. TripAdvisor came through yet again with an excellent recommendation.
Located on W 46th Street, between 8th and 9th Ave, the hotel is only a 3 - 5 minute walk to Times Square, yet is far enough removed from it that it is entirely possible to escape the crowds. 
Our room (#204) was well-appointed, with beautiful, comfortable linens and a nice bathroom. A lot of thought obviously went into the decoration of the room. The room was a bit on the narrow side, however. This was solved by storing the luggage racks behind one of the chairs in the room. 
Nights were very quiet, even with the lively Bourbon Street Bar two floors below us. Never once did bar nor street noise disturb us during the night. We did frequent the bar during our stay, taking two meals there. The food was well-prepared and reasonably-priced. There are many restaurants near the hotel, as well. We did not have the opportunity to try them, but appreciated the convenience of having them there.
The service was excellent, save for one small error. Room service forgot to replace our used coffee cups one day. Other than that, however, they serviced the rooms well. The front desk was helpful and friendly, too, both with check-in / check-out and in providing directions around the city.
We'll likely look to return to this hotel if we need to return to the Times Square area.

title: “Lovely and Luxurious”
text: We've been doing winter getaways at the Sofitel Water Tower for three years. We recommend the Prestige Suite. Beautiful marble bath with a bedroom and a large living room. Wow! This chain is French and modern in decor. You are walking distance from Michigan Avenue.

title: “Comfortable, great safe location”
text: We spent 2 nights in the Cow Hollow Motor Inn in October. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was very comfortable and quiet. It's wise to ask for a room away from the street. The location is great, within a short walk to many good restaurants and shopping. We took the bus to the civic center and returned to the marina area for a delicious dinner at ISA and a evening stroll. We would definitely stay in Cow Hollow again.

title: “old hotel”
text: The thing that best characterizes hotel de anza is that it's old. The age of the hotel shows everywhere. The exterior and the interior of the hotel loos old, there is no wifi - instead you have to use network cable, there is nothing really good or bad to say about it other then the age shows on it

title: “Great for early flight out”
text:
Good hotel - comfortable and updated rooms. Had 530am flight out - shuttle from hotel runs at 4am but was taken out earlier by driver as it was only a quick 5min trip to terminal.
Excellent service.

title: “Loved this place!!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for one night before boarding a cruise ship for the Caribbean. I had never been to NY before so I wanted to stay in the heart of everything. I picked the perfect place!! It was near the corner of W 49th & Broadway and as soon as I turned the corner, there were all the lights of Broadway!!! So the room wasnt huge, it was enough for me. It has a very nice European feel and several of the guests stayed up and in the lobby drinking and talking, very comfortable atmosphere. I did notice a $3 charge on my credit card bill after, not sure what that was for, but it was worth it!!! We will def be back to stay there again.

title: “Treated First Class”
text: Get what you pay for at the US Grant in San Diego. Vintage hotel in great location near the end of the gaslamp and horton plaza shopping center. The rooms were spacious and had a vintage decor to it. The most impressive aspect to me was being treated first class. Valet and front desk always spoke to me as "Mr" and always thanked me for staying at the hotel. I scored a great internet rate and it was well worth the weekend away with my wife...

title: “Astoundingly clean, fantastic staff”
text:
For those less familiar with Manhattan, the lodging options are overwhelming. With so many choices, it should be easy to find a myriad of properties that suit any number of requirements. But for me, it was a struggle to find the perfect location, level of amenities, and acceptable price point for a recent 4-day trip w/ my hubby. 
I ruled out the overpriced hipster boutiques, the stuffy landmarks, the dinosaur properties, the tourist-laden chains, and the too-good-to-be true rates in less desirable parts of town. After that, I wasn't left with nearly as many options as you'd think.
Then I found the listing for the San Carlos. I loved that they're one of the very last independently owned hotels in NYC, catered to a European clientele (which usually means non-fussy rooms, immaculately clean spaces, and competent staff), and the Manhattan East location; the area was convenient to RCMH where we were seeing 2 nights of concerts. The fact the rooms looked large vs the price and came w/ mini fridges and microwaves (somewhat unusual for Manhattan) sealed the deal. But looking good on paper doesn't mean in reality it will pan out.
I'd made my reservation months in advance, over the phone, for a certain room type that the young lady I spoke to had 100% guaranteed. When I called week-of to confirm my reservation, I was told there was a possibility I might not be able to get the room type I'd been promised. Irked, I referenced the original reservation but they explained sometimes these things happen. True, but I hung up the phone and considered rebooking elsewhere; the phone rang back moments later and the young lady I originally spoke to apologized, said they would upgrade me at no fee and get me what I needed no matter what, and really acted as if she valued my business. I'd expect this from a 5 star property, but at a under $300 a night spot, it was refreshing. Customer service is a dying art. The staff at the San Carlos is old school, in the best possible, most refreshing way. 
Upon arrival, an easy cab ride from Penn Station, the lobby was sparkling, the bellman exceptional, and the check-in flawless. It's not the fanciest place, more suited for the upscale business traveler (though I spied many families too) but the cleanliness, a huge factor for me, absolutely perfect. And my room, a King, was HUGE. Not huge just by NYC standards, huge by any hotel standard. 
The view from our particular room wasn't much to see, but windows that actually open in both the room and bathroom were a bonus. The amenities were lovely, towels and robe divinely soft, the bed linens super comfy, and a pant press a blast from the past. The room was modern, simple, understated, private, quiet, and cozy. Everything worked too. Which should go without saying but unfortunately is often not the case in any class of hotel. The real silverware, plates, and glasses provided were a great compliment to the microwave and fridge.
 Did I mention that housekeeping is outstanding? In my years of travel, I've never seen more competent housecleaning. 
My interaction with the staff was easy peasy. Items I needed were sent up immediately, dinner spots/phone numbers provided, and I was always greeted with a smile. I dreaded check out because it meant our experience was over. I literally had zero complaints during my entire stay except that the Indian restaurant next door (that serves as the San Carlos' complimentary breakfast serving area and then offers their own menu for limited room service too), is simply not up to par with the rest of the hotel.  If 24 hour American cuisine room service is a make it or break it deal for you, that's about the only reason I'd consider finding a different hotel. Seeing as Manhattan has every food conceivable, most of it deliverable, I easily overlook this.
Quiet rooms, pleasant interiors/halls, a great business center/overflow lobby, elevators that were kept constantly cleaned (check the Ritz for smudges, lol), and staff that valued my business means that next I'm in NYC I'm making a beeline right back here. Sure, there's more glamorous or hip spots, but for the level of service vs price and comfort, there's a reason this is a hidden gem amongst your hundreds of NYC hotels. Part of me doesn't want the secret to get out.

title: “Do not recommend”
text: The water park and hotel were dirty and outdated. Way OVER PRICED for what we received. Will not stay at this hotel again.

title: “Wonderful”
text: We found everything to be clean and tidy. All the personnel were friendly and attentive. We found the price to be very reasonable.

title: “Boutique Hotel Wanna Be”
text: I was antsy about my 5 day stay at this hotel after reading the reviews so kept my receipt of on-line payment but didn't have any problem at check in. I did however encounter 3 drunk middle aged adults on the elevator trying to get to my room one of which tried to pick me up. I quickly made it to my room and wanted to bolt the door being a female traveling alone. However their was no interior deadbolt. The room was very small since it is a circular structure located right on the freeway. It is convenient but somewhat noisy. I was dying to open the balcony door to let the gorgeous breezes blow in but it was way too noisy. The shower only gave a steady stream of warm water for about 7 minutes then I would get long stretches of cold water then warm again then cold. It almost seemed like there was a timer and you only got 7 minutes before they said "times up' and started sending cold water. The bed was a pillow top and very compfy, there was a nice plasma TV but the lighting in the entire room was very poor. The worst part of the entire stay was the $18/day valet parking + tips. There is no self-parking at all. So when you add a minimum of $20/day to the cost of the room, I don't think it substantiates the over all value of the room. The maid service, newspaper delivery etc. was very unpredictable. I spent 5 days there, my bill was $900 and only received 2 newspapers and 1 turn-down service at night. It is however very convenient to the UCLA campus and freeway.

title: “Radison Fishermans warf San francisco”
text: Great location and the courtyard with the fire pit was nice, I noticed that people seemed to like gathering there. The staff was very helpful to me. I chose this hotel becasue I called first and asked about transportation and sightseeing and they were so helpful. I would definetely stay there again.

title: “Hotel was convenient for shopping but service was subpar”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for one night.
While it is very convenient for shopping and the room was spacious, we find the service to be below expectations for a hotel which is supposedly 4-star.
First, we found one of the bellman totally unfriendly although I also saw some who were very helpful. Second, we find that employees do not have a "can-do" attitude. For example, I asked if they could look up another hotel's phone number. When they couldn't find it in their internal database, they just told me they couldn't find it. In other hotels, they would have offered to look it up on the internet for me or doing something else instead of giving up right away. When I suggested that concierge help me with the phone number, I was transferred to concierge but was put on hold for so long that I eventually hung up.
The room was adequate although again for a 4-star, it didn't have basic items like a pad of paper or pen to write on ( I was trying to take down notes from a phone call and couldn't locate one).
In all, location was great, room was satisfactory, but service was extremely disappointing.

title: “I stayed for one night, they charged for 22 nights”
text: The title says it all. So far, I've spent 45 minutes with my credit card company trying to fix their mess. When I called, they didn't even apologize -- they just told me to call back later and speak to accounting. I guess overcharging by $6,000 doesn't merit an apology.

title: “Close to the historic district and the Seahawks”
text: Wonderful place to stay to visit the historic district (Pioneer Square) in Seattle or go to a ball game. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The moment you drive up the valets are right there to assist. There is only valet parking at $28 per night. The historic district and the Mariners and Seahawks stadiums are well within walking distance. The rooms are well appointed and large. A gem in the middle of town.

title: “Not family friendly, Not a resort”
text:
When we checked into our hotel (Mission Valley Resort) we were given keys to a standard room and upon entry were horrified to see how small it was. It comprised of 2 double beds and some furniture which left no room for a crib and no room for luggage. The bathroom was small and the overall condition of the room was dingy.
We returned to the hotel clerk and expressed that the room was unacceptable and how could they expect a family of 4 including a crib to stay in such cramped quarters. They advised that was the room which was booked and they had no record of a requested crib. (it was listed on the Hotel Voucher with Queen Beds)!
The end result was an offer to upgrade to a larger room for an additional $45.00 US per night for 6 nights plus taxes $300.00 . It felt like a complete scam

title: “Boutique Hotel, handy for walking...”
text:
Having read the reviews and received a personal recommendation, we booked the 'On the Ave' hotel with high expectations.
It's probably fair to say that they've done quite well with what they have, the hotel is clean and comfortable, the staff are first class!, (very helpful, attentive, very good humoured) and the location is probably it's best asset, lots of reasonably priced and good restaurants close by, handy for Central Park and a pleasant neighbourhood to walk around.
Downsides...no restaurant in the hotel, so no breakfasts, just a portable coffee pot with Starbucks coffee and tea brought in, (although there is an adjoining public restaurant, but on our visit it was packed out, had to wait for a table, pizzas were 'average' and wines expensive).
Old rooms, quite dark and two sets of two lifts / elevators, meant long waiting times to go anywhere, or use the stairs!
Having said all that, I would go back and I would stay again, it's kind of a good place to stay in spite of itself!

title: “Home away from Home”
text:
Staff service was friendly and helpful. The room was clean, the grounds beautiful, with a sparkling clean pool, and pretty trees and foliage. Parking was convenient to rooms, and
smokers were accomodated. The breakfast bar was very sufficient for most any taste. Delightful experience!

title: “Great hotel”
text: I stayed at this hotel twice for business, once in April 2008 and again in May 2008. The hotel is located in Harbor East, which is the new, up and coming area of Baltimore's Inner Harbor. Location-wise, it's great. There are many excellent, high-end chain restaurants, like Roy's, Oceanaire Seafood Room, Flemings, Lebanese Taverna, as well as local restaurants, such as Pazo and Charleston, all within walking distance of the hotel. Whole Foods is nearby and there are some cheaper restaurants, too, like Chiu's sushi and a Mexican place. There are also little boutiques to go shopping. Just a few blocks away, is the Inner Harbor itself, which has many great restaurants. The hotel itself is lovely. Its location on the water allows great views of the harbor. At night, it is lively, and if there's a concert, it is a bit loud until the concert is over, usually 11pm. Rooms are spacious, and the bathroom is standard. There aren't that many towel hooks, so towels are folded and stacked on shelves. Bath and Body Works products are great. Hotel staff is friendly and willing to help out. The concierge is great! The hotel breakfast is standard hotel fare, but good. There is also a Starbucks located within the hotel. Parking is expensive, $21 per day, but you're in a city. This is also a good business hotel, but you do have to pay for an internet connection. Overall, you will be paying for the great view.

title: “what a view”
text:
Booked a room for two nights in a conference-oriented suite. The room itself had this very great look to it, and the murphy bed was perfect for removing from view when it came time for business. It was a legitimate office.
But what made this room special was the view. You overlook the Chicago River and many of the city's architectural landmarks. What fun.

title: “Great Location”
text: Stayed here one night while attending a baseball game. Location is great, never heard the noise other reviewers talk about. Room was large and comfortable. I would not hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Great room to eat.”
text: Nice hidden restaurant near the Common - beautiful room, with fireplace and small bar. Lunch is best deal - also great Monday night wine themed events. Loved going here for years.

title: “Fantastic location”
text:
After reading the reviews we were a little concerened but found we had no reason to be. Yes it's an old hotel but that added to its charm. We found all staff without exception pleasant and helpful. The room was very good . A good size, well decorated, spotlessly clean. The bathroom was indeed small but this did not hinder our stay ; the shower , toiletries etc were fine. We were using Reward points but were still upgraded as I noted on my booking it was our Anniversary. 
The location in particular was perfect, right in the heart of Manhattan, with easy access to all main tourist attractions. As for New York, first time visitors and we fell in love with it.

title: “Great for it's price”
text: I stayed there for a couple of nights and the staff was very, very, very friendly. Romos were in a good shape and I didn't have to worry about things not working in the room. Internet was really fast; surprisingly for hotels. Overall I would stay there again.

title: “Great location, terrible accomodation”
text:
I requested a queen or king size bed because my wife and I are tall. We were given a double bed in a 9" x 10" room fitted with old and unconfortable furniture, with a wet carpet from the noisy AC. I complained to the desk, and they said that all rooms are the same and can not offer a bigger bed. I told them that the pic on the internet show more confortable rooms. She said they were not available. The lobby sofas were smelly and old too.. One day we had no water for 10 hours, whne we had water there was no pressure. It was a horrible stay of 5 days.
The staff was nice but could not help. Will never go back.

title: “Great quality and price”
text: The hotel is well located to Ponte Vedra Beach, where we were visiting family. The staff was exceptional and the rooms were clean and the price was great.

title: “warning”
text: We drove to D.C. from Massachusetts. Long drive but got there fine. When we arrived we were told that there were no parking spots left. I asked if this was unusual or common. I was told it happens "every day." Mind you we got there at 4:00 in the afternoon and I would never expected them to have no available parking. My husband had to drive around and look for a public lot. Eventually he found one but we were not happy not to have at least been warned that this was a common problem. The public lot was expensive and inconvenient. Just be sure you have parking plan B if you are driving to this Hyatt.

title: “Great location”
text:
My husband and I stayed for six nights over Thanksgiving. The good: We had booked a deluxe room and were upgraded to a deluxe corner room upon arrival that had lovely views. Room clean and staff helpful. Windows thickly paned so we did not hear much street noise or hallway noise. Subway right next door was a great perk and it was a central location for Hell's Kitchen, Broadway and Times Square. The not so good: I was disappointed that the standard rooms and suites had turn down service but those who paid in the middle did not. Seems very odd.
