The restaurant that is attached to the hotel, Ca Va, had VERY poor service and was quite expensive for rather so-so food. We were not told our first night that the kitchen would be closing in the bar area until it already had but were then told that we could go into the main dining area and eat. Just like the turn down service, things just seemed to be a bit backward. 
I would stay again and simply avoid the restaurant.

title: “Good Hotel”
text: This hotel is pretty much just as pictured, very clean. Bathrooms are decent size for SF. Felt very comfortable, very safe. Close to public transportation in business district. Restaurant on first floor is not really very good at all, very overpriced. Would stay again :o)

title: “Awesome view, but...”
text:
Just back from an epic motorcycle trip to MotoGP in Monterey, CA. My husband and I stayed at the SF Regency our second night out. We were upgraded to a suite due to being members of their Gold Passport loyalty program. This is my first review and I'm pretty good at being objective so here goes... We rolled in around 8:00 pm.
The first thing I heard as we walked in was a door man (? - top hat and long overcoat) complaining to his coworker that there was a group who was returning to their rooms last night, and when he asked how their evening was they said it was the best night of their lives, and then "Can you even believe it, they didn't give me a quarter or nothing!!" which made me think about my tipping technique. I didn't know you were supposed to tip the door man for addressing you. Really bad form... Complain about the patrons on your break where the rest of the patrons can't hear you.
The front desk wasn't feeling cheery, and they were not welcoming. Then again, we were road weary and probably didn't smile much either. 
We were put on the 8th floor, and if you went out on the balcony, you could see the pier and bridge. FANTASTIC view! The room you entered into was very cold both in decor and temperature. It wasn't a neo-modern look either... there was just nothing there. 400 SF with a TV, a chair and a couch. There absolutely nothing decorative, except for a stainless vase it looked like they found in a storage closet and placed in on top of a seriously scratched vanity that held the TV. The carpet had a cool design, but was F I L T H Y: multiple coffee (?) stains and something wet, sticky and smelly by the sliding glass doors. The furniture was old and well-used.The rooms were freezing; the AC had been blasting for quite awhile, and the temp in San Fran was no more that 60 F. We couldn't seem to get the place to warm up. And yes, we tried to rally the heater. 
Just a heads up for those on a pleasure trip thinking about staying at this Hyatt... It's in the Financial District, and because it's a business oriented area, nothing nearby is really open past 8pm. Fisherman's Wharf or Union area would have been better choices.
Where I'm sure it's probably rare, on another note if anyone else finds themselves riding their motorcycle to this location, there was nowhere on site for us to park our bikes. We were directed to the Embarcadero Parking where we paid a greater price than if we had been able to park at the Hotel (they wouldn't let us park in the same space, therefore we had to pay double). As you're probably aware, the Regency is a steep $57/night to park.
We'll find elsewhere to stay next time we're in San Francisco.

title: “Anniversary Weekend”
text:
We live in a suburb of Memphis and since our Anniversary was coming up we decided a night downtown might be fun. So we booked a club room at the Peabody and dinner at a restaurant close by that we had wanted to try. Upon arrival we were notified that the Club Level was closed for renovation, but they had upgraded us to a mini-suite. We weren't sure if we would be happy but the suite turned out to be very nice and spacious. In addition, the 'extras' that would have been included with a club level room were still included as best as was possible. When we arrived back to the room that evening, lovely desserts were waiting in the suite along with a nice handwritten note congratulating us. 
 The bed and high-quality linens were very comfortable. The next morning we ordered our continental breakfast which was included. The pastries were delicious, fresh and warm and everything was beautifully served. Overall we felt that the accomodations, service, and experience exceeded our expectations...even for a 1-night stay.
 The Peabody is a legend in Memphis and the location cannot be beat in terms of walking to Beale Street and other nearby areas. We found it to be just as wonderful as we expected.

title: “Full of character”
text: The Omni stood out at the Riverwalk due to its charm, historical appeal and sheer personality. The place is supposedly built upon an old school. It had the lots of old spanish architectural touches, muted lights in corridors and lovely little touches. The beds were a tad smaller and the bathroom was small also. But the finishes were lovely. It was all marble and the shower was refreshing. Pool was also a bit small. But overall, given that you were in the prime part of the river walk where all the action was, it was a fabulous place. Parking is extra. But we found space int he garage right across the street for 9 bucks per day. And we did not need the car for everything was walking distance. Will definitely recommend the property!

title: “Great Location”
text: The location was great. The hotel is a large convention type hotel. It is walking distance to Pikes market and all downtown. It provides easy access to highways. Room was, comfortable. Be cautious about ordering drinks in the Lobby. Quite pricey!

title: “Certainly different”
text:
We grew up in New York City and to even want to stay at the Blue Moon, you'd have to be curious about what has happened to the Lower East Side. The neighborhood is not for everyone. It is old and farily dirty, but a moment away from both Chinatown and Little Italy. Greenwich Village is about a 15-20 minute walk.
The hotel itself is clean and immediately appears out of place in the neighborhood.
There is one thing however that I cannot forget. The day we arrived it was 95 degrees outside. When we checked in, I asked the desk clerk where I could get some ice. He told me without apology or hesitation, that I could go to a store and buy some. No embarrasment or reluctance was apparent. For almost $300 per night, ice should be available. We stayed three nights; but I knew not to ask for anything again. Another response like that, and we would have a serious confrontation.
This place is offbeat; but if you are used to the Ritz Carlton, stay away.

title: “Standard hotel, great location”
text: Really nothing wrong with this hotel, however in this day and age I think that Internet should be free ($13 a day). The hotel is clean, rooms have a bar fridge, staff were very friendly, location is great and there's a gym and pool. Rooms feel slightly dated and one can't shake the feel that it's just a stock standard hotel: nothing wrong, but nothing great.

title: “Perfect”
text:
Found this by accident.
Traveling CA and went to San Diego as a drive thru
Motel was an old Spanish fort that overlooks a row of restaurants and shops in Old Town
Great welcome cocktail hour, and full breakfast buffet
Room was generous and clean
Perfect way to end the day

title: “Pretty good but with flaws”
text:
I stayed at the Public around Jan/Fev of 2012. The hotel had been recently renovated and it was spotless. The lobby is very nice and had character, service was absolutely impeccable. We booked two rooms, one for us and the other one for my in-laws. Both rooms were very nice, modern and bright. They did a very good job on renovating to a modern style but without losing the character. There was a gourmet café next to the lobby that was pretty damn good.
On the bad side, in the evenings the hotel would become a big party. There is some sort of night club that is connected to the lobby, that whole lobby, café, restaurant becomes a night club with tons of people and loud music. That did not bother me directly, since I’d get back to the hotel and squeeze my way to the elevator, but it can be bothersome. The other problem I had was because my room was connected to the next room by a door. If was closed, of course, but it was not sound proofed at all. On the first night there were no guests on that room but on the second night I could hear everything that they said and also other types of sound if you know what I mean. That was quite annoying. Other than that, a solid 4 start hotel in a decent localization.

title: “Old and new world combined”
text: Such a lovely hotel! Rooms are comfortable and clean. The staff is a model that other hotels can only dream of. Great location on the River Walk. Will be one of my first choices when traveling to San Antonio,

title: “Definately would stay again!”
text:
This hotel was great FOR THE PRICE, remember this is a 2 star hotel. We got a great deal on it. The rooms were spacious and the bathroom was almost as big as the room. Traffic was loud but if you put on the fan it drowned everything out. This hotel seems to get a lot of bad reviews, I'm not sure if they are old or not but I don't have any major complaints about it. Also alot of the bad reviews seem to come from out of state/country. As a frequent visitor to SF I will be staying here again! 
Staff wasn't overly exuberant, but definitely friendly.
It is walking distance to the Warf, and a nice neighborhood. I wasn't asked for change once! Even at night there were women walking around by themselves (the seemed to be locals). 
I have 2 downsides to this place and they are minor. They didn't have fitted sheets so they kept curling up when I was sleeping, and also I didn't see any continental breakfast. We were there during the week so I'm not sure if that effected it at all.
Oh and the parking is free which is AWESOME! Even if the spots are tight free parking in SF is always great. 
Also its newly renovated, not the most modern décor but it seems to be better than what the other reviews say.

title: “The perfect location”
text:
For us, this is the perfect DC hotel. It was very reasonably priced (we paid $120 a night which we got through their website). The rooms were fine, I would think they would be very good for business travelers as they had a large desk and 2 phones (with 2 lines each). The lobby was quite pleasant and a nice place to sit and read the paper in the morning. The restaurant (Smithson's) is nothing to rave about - I'd eat elsewhere, but there is a Starbucks off the lobby - we grabbed breakfast there. The main selling point is the location. It is a 5 minute walk to the Air and Space Museum. Anything on the mall would be easily walkable. And it is about a 3 minute walk to the L'Enfant Plaza Metro station. 
We will definitely stay there again!!

title: “Perfect Hotel!”
text: We just stayed here for a week with our two children. We had a beautiful suite. It was set up perfectly. We had a large bedroom with a TV and double doors that led into a small room/hallway. Then there was another set of double doors that led into the living room with a pull out couch, desk and TV. There was plenty of room and privacy for the four of us to live and sleep. We requested a small refrigerator that was happily provided for no cost. There was a small but perfect indoor pool with an adjacent sitting area outside. We saw many people having their breakfast outside while their kids swam. The gym was spacious and well equipped. Of course the coffee in the am and happy hour in the afternoon were great, as were the 4 different free newspapers. The concierge arranged for a limo from the airport. He also hooked us up with discounted tickets to the aquarium which allowed us to skip the line. The neighborhood was perfect. We walked to the Willis Tower, Miracle Mile, Navy Pier and many other sights. Also walked to many great restaurants (Wildfire, Chicago Q). The red line is steps from the front door. Everything you need is right in the neighborhood. Great and friendly service. Wish every hotel stay was like this.

title: “Hotel was ok, but will definitely try others before coming back”
text:
I booked my reservation through priceline's bid feature and thought I got a decent deal until I realized this four star hotel is ala carte pricing.
First, the positive. My room was very clean and comfortable. There was a big event in the conference area. I had to walk by as the parking lot was quite full and I had to park on the other side of the hotel. The music was very loud, but when I went to my room I couldn't hear anything. Had a good night sleep. The air conditioner is a bit louder than I expected even though I only had it on Fan 1 which was annoying. The staff was overall quite friendly. And yes, the cookies are good. 
But instead of free cookies, I'd rather have free parking. Or free internet. Or how about both? It's shocking to me that a hotel of this caliber charges for in room internet AND parking. These were not charges I could see prior to booking through priceline. Had I known, I NEVER would have stayed at this hotel. I'm not sure I understand how you can provide free shuttle service to the hotel, but charge for parking? I'd rather pay a little for my room and have everything included than to make it feel like I'm being nickeled and dimed. 
There are plenty of hotels in the same area that have similar per night fees that have: free high speed wireless internet, free parking AND free complimentary breakfast which I would gladly exchange for the 1 cookie they give you at check in. Even Motel 6 has free internet!
The wait for the elevators was also a little trying. There were four elevators but it only seemed like two were working. Even late at night, trying to get up to my room I had to wait quite a while to get an elevator. 
Overall, it's a decent hotel, but I will definitely not stay here again when I'm back in San Jose.

title: “Terrific value, great location for a short business trip”
text:
A few weeks ago I was in Washington for four days on business and frequently stay at Club Quarters hotels when I'm traveling for work. So the CQ Washington was a no-brainer.
But I should note that I've only stayed at the CQ hotels that have been renovated, and this one hadn't been. It was a bit of a shock: a little old-school, I have to say, between the 1980s-looking sofa, the dark wood-paneled furniture and a TV sort of weirdly perched on a coffee table. What a sharp contrast to the Chicago property, which had a comfortable, well-upholstered modern sofa, a desk that rotated 90 degrees to turn into a table for dining, enough drawer space and hanging space for a two-week trip and a flat-screen TV built into the wall with a port to hook up a laptop or DVD player.
So some of the other reviewers have commented on these things, plus the size of the rooms (very small, even by CQ standards) and the lack of full service amenities.
Frankly I think it depends on what you're looking for in a hotel. If you're a business traveler who spends almost all your time at work or out to dinner/drinks with clients or colleagues, you'll like a hotel that doesn't waste your money on frills you don't need. If you're a vacationer you may not like the location or the small, relatively under-appointed bedrooms.
(And if you're just in town for an afternoon meeting and can spend the rest of your trip having fun, can we trade jobs?)
When I'm traveling on business I'm frequently at the hotel just a few hours in the morning to work out and get ready and an hour or two at the end of the night watching SportsCenter. I don't want or need a large room, a concierge, a continental breakfast, a bellhop, or a front desk with four people. To me, safety, comfort, cleanliness and location are much more important than, say, a concierge, a pool or a bellhop. My colleagues or clients always have more dinner and bar recommendations than I ever have time to try out, and that's one more thing to drive up the cost of your room.
Here's some of the things you can have at a Club Quarters that are negative/indifferent for vacationers that are big pros for a business traveler:
* Convenient business district location (in Washington that is *also* convenient for tourists, but that's unusual)
* Location is also usually convenient to public transit -- my company won't generally pay for a rental or livery service in big cities
* Self-service check-in and check-out -- walk in, check in, walk up to your room
* Inexpensive valet laundry service, sometimes a free laundry room (not in Washington)
* Free (small) workout facility
* 24-hour lobby, required key card in elevator for security late at night
* Restaurant/bar open late
No, Club Quarters doesn't have a concierge, a pool, locations that are convenient to museum districts or other tourist/nightlife hotspots, big, well-appointed rooms for families, etc. That's not their thing.
I'll gladly stay there again the next time I'm in Washington on business.

title: “If you just want a clean basic room, with a great location this is the one!”
text:
I booked this accomadation online via travelrepublic.co.uk. Arrived at the hotel during late afternoon and recieved a easy and quick check in. I was in room 1130, this was a fair sized room, but clean. What else do you need when you are out all day and night? Although my room view was of a brick wall!! 
The location of the hotel cannot be faulted, it is right on Broadway and just off Times Sq! Within 30 secs and you are in the middle of times square!

title: “Stay well at Staybridge SA Sea World!”
text:
We couldn't have been happier with this place and our stay there. We were here in October 2011 for my son's graduation from Lackland Air Force Base. It provided a very nice, homelike atmosphere, which he greatly appreciated after being away from home so long for the first time. There was an actual kitchen, a bar to sit/eat at, a "living room" with a TV, and a separate bedroom with TV and bathroom that could be closed off from the rest of the suite. He couldn't sleep over with us per Lackland rules, but he really enjoyed just hanging out with us there and having meals together again, etc.
Everything was new and clean and comfortable. Parking was ample and free. Staff were very welcoming and also helpful, upon check-in and each time we'd come and go. The eating area was large and comfortable and offered lots of choices. We were never bothered by outside noise and always slept comfortably.
The location was great because it wasn't too far from the base yet wasn't too far from downtown. Also, it's right next to Sea World, although we didn't go there. There's a Cracker Barrel not too far away; also a Barnes & Noble.
I enjoyed this place so much that I always enter "Staybridge Suites" in the search box when I book a trip somewhere. Sadly, I haven't been able to find it again where my trips have taken me, but I'll keep trying.

title: “Great Stay, but Food/Beverage Biz Model Must Change”
text:
We recently stayed at the hotel and were booked for three days. It boasts a fantastic location; 1 block from Union Square and 2 blocks from Powell St for the cable car. The hotel is not too big and not too small, and has clean and comfortable rooms.
Our check-in was fine. Every guest gets a letter from the GM welcoming them to the property. The room was a decent size and the bathroom was fairly large. It has Molton Brown products (great!) although I was hoping to see Taj-branded products (amazing!).The bed was heavenly - I dont think I have ever slept so well. The turn down service was also a great perk.
But here is my only complaint. Campton Place needs to ditch the U.S. business model of ripping off customers with a 20% gratuity and $4 delivery charge when it comes to food. Taj Hotels (Taj "Mansingh") in India are very well known for their food and beverage service. We would have eaten at the hotel for breakfast, but the prices were crazy. We found a Starbucks right next door. Moreover, there is a french cafe two blocks away called La Boulange (good). There's also a Cheesecake Factory (good) above Macys (two blocks away). I also suggest the hotel makes the snacks and soft drinks free for guests in the rooms. Finally, putting together a really nice buffet for guests for 25 bucks or offering complimentary pastries in the morning would be a way to change. That's how Taj Campton will get five stars from me.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: We stayed in this hotel for three nights during the summer because we got a deal on the price. Initially we were put in a room that was located across the hall from the elevator. You could hear entire conversations coming from the people getting on and off the elevator and every time the doors closed you could hear the little "ding sound" the elevator made. The noise was outrageous and I knew I wouldn't be able to sleep so we went downstairs and asked if we could be put in another room. They put us on a different floor far away from the elevator. Service was good, the rooms were clean, and the location of the hotel was great and within walking distance of a lot of different places we wanted to see. The parking garage was pricey, maybe $20 per night if I remember correctly, but this seemed the norm in Philadelphia so it wasn't a problem. I would stay here again and recommend it, just don't get a room next to an elevator!

title: “What a dump”
text: I visit Boston between 5-10 times a year and have never stayed in a hotel as bad as Hotel 140. Do not be fooled by their use of the word "boutique." I can deal with small rooms and actually prefer boutique hotels but just because you have small rooms does not make you a boutique hotel. If you are looking for a true boutique hotel in Back Bay, I'd recommend the Charlesmark. I paid over $200 for 1 night at Hotel 140 and was expecting much better. My room felt more like a college dorm room than a hotel room. The furniture was cheap and ugly and the carpet was ragged and stained. It didn't appear to have been vacuumed before my arrival. If you're just looking for a place to crash, I suppose it'll do. Just don't expect to have a romantic weekend here. Check out the pictures I took and decide for yourself.

title: “Good location - no problems”
text:
Stayed for 7 nights from 19th Nov - pretty much as advertised.
If like us you like to do a show (or 5) and eat late this is a perfect location as main resturants (Resturant row / Hells Kitchen) are on your route back from Broadway. Mostly an easy walk (10min max) even in the rain. NB for a 24hr city most places still shut around 11pm... 12 at weekends.... and all day on Thanksgiving!
If your room is near the service lift shaft it can be noisy during the day but no problem during hours that are important. Our room was good size with microwave and full size fridge so you can DIY breakfast although eating (Breakfast is good value - try 'Village' south on 8th) in NY is a major part of the fun. Keep an eye on the 20% automatically added service charge? and still space for the tip on the bill! in most resturants.
Our room kept very clean and all staff were great... helpful efficient and friendly.
Slightly negative points to bear in mind...
Lifts are slow and very busy at peak times (8:30 - 9:30?)
and NY is a very noisy city so a high room is good on both counts (at least you get in the lift - even if it does stop a lot).
Good hotel, great location... not cheap and there are alternatives but it's location could save you any extra you pay?
Have fun - NY is a magic city.

title: “Great Value and Service”
text: I was visiting philadelphia to take in some history and discover america's roots when i came across this quaint style hotel with charm and character. I was very impressed by affordable it was compared to the other hotels in the area. If you are looking for a nice clean room at an affordable rate then this is the place!

title: “What a find”
text:
Just returned from a 4 night stay at the Affina 50. Location excellent. Service outstanding. Clean , comfortable, just brilliant.
Subway one block up from the hotel. Great places to eat nearby.Eat at the New York dinner a couple of doors up from the affina. Breakfast is a must we paid no more than $25 for a family of 4.If in the city on a sight seeing trip I'd suggest the Gray line hopper bus tour. Well worth the money.We were in the city with our 2 children aged 10 and 14 who fell in love with New York. Well done affina on making our visit a happy relaxed chilled out one. We will be back .
The Bentley Family.
BARNSLEY

title: “GREAT location...otherwise OK”
text:
The location of the hotel is unbeatable. Pier 39 and the Embarcadero are within walking distance so we did not need to rent a car during our San Francisco stay. One very convenient thing about this hotel is that there is a Dollar rental car annexed to the building. We left SF for a few days in wine country and it was really nice to be able to pick up our rental car right next door.
The concierge desk was also very helpful to us in suggesting restaurants (they have some discount coupons if you ask) and helping with directions. Very pleasant!
The hotel itself was otherwise average -- which was fine with us because we spent such little time there. We came to SF to see the city and needed an affordable, comfortable hotel to spend a few nights -- and the Sheraton provided just that. I wouldn't recommend if you are looking for a luxurious accommodation with a lot of amenities, but if you need a convenient, comfortable place to stay, this is it.
PROS: Great location, VERY comfortable beds, rental car availability 
CONS: Our room had quite a bit of street noise -- but on both nights we were so tired from a full day exploring the city that it didn't bother our sleep.

title: “Great location”
text: If you're looking for an amazing location, close to the T, the bay, and food - this is an awesome place to stay. Minimal hotel amenities but Quincy Market is across the street for great food. Old Town Trolley Tours next door were very helpful in planning our trip - we did 2 days of trolley tours (you can get on & off at your leisure) and then a Salem tour the third day. Loved all of it! Northend is in walking distance to great Italian food & Mike's Pastry (amazing). The staff at the hotel were not friendly and did not go above & beyond so keep that in mind if that's what makes you happy. The location made up for it :)

title: “A one-hour wait for the hotel shuttle!! But they made up for it.”
text:
I landed at SeaTac Airport, called the hotel immediately and was told that the shuttlebus circulated every 15 minutes. As I was crossing the pedestrian bridge to the garage, I saw the shuttle standing by -- it didn't even stop or slow down. Despite repeated phone calls, it took another 52 minutes before the next shuttle showed up.
When the bus pulled to the hotel, I realize I could've simply walked faster, and I wish I had! It was like waiting for the cable guy to arrive -- they kept telling me the bus was on the way, right around the corner, etc., and either they were lying to me or the shuttle bus driver was lying to the front desk staff.
However, to their benefit, the front desk manager was extremely, extremely apologetic, upgraded me to a tower room and give me $15 coupon for breakfast. Also, you can't beat the price -- I only paid $40 on Priceline.
Despite the issues with the shuttle, I would definitely stay at this hotel again, but I would just walk from the airport... it's maybe a 10 minute walk at most.
PS the tower elevators are absolutely freezing!!

title: “Small, clean rooms, friendly & accommodating staff, great location!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here for the latter part of his visit up from Florida. We booked through a third-party site using the "Name Your Own Price" feature (you don't see what you book until you pay). When the hotel name was revealed we were surprised because we'd never heard of it. Understandably, we were a little apprehensive.
Our experience:
We called in the day before to request a late check-in (we planned on checking in late Saturday after my mom's wedding & reception). Joe was more than happy to assist with that. He even offered us an early check-in, but we figured so much would be going on that day that arriving early would be highly unlikely so we politely declined.
We were in the area Friday night and decided to see if we could find the hotel. We were successful. & May I say.. GREAT LOCATION!
We enter, it's cute. Definitely a boutique hotel. (Not a chain).
The receptionist, Althena, greets us and quickly asks to assist. I say "Oh, we're just taking a peek around before our check-in tomorrow night." She offers to take us up to see a room and shows us three!
Althena was awesome, just really genuinely nice. The final room she showed us was a standard queen (we were curious of the sizes of the other rooms). It was cozy, appealing, and definitely clean. It wasn't much larger than the standard rooms, just the setup made more sense to us and although this particular view didn't offer the same scenery as the others, we preferred it.
We were then given a complimentary upgrade. (Thanks Althena!) We explained that on our account there would be a note from Joe about a late check-in and Althena says that she can reserve the Queen room we viewed for us and that since it was technically Saturday and there were multiple vacancies, we could check-in right then. Although we declined, we did end up coming back checking in around 2:40AM. She assured us that it wasn't a problem.
Not a single hassle. The next morning while my boyfriend was in the shower, he cut himself on a damaged wire-frame shower caddy. I call the front desk and request a first aid kit, the woman says they don't have one, but asks about the nature of the incident. When I told her what happened, she sent housekeeping with an ascetic spray solution, alcohol pads, bandages, and a newer, upgraded caddy.
The housekeeper was an older woman with a beautiful European accent. She was concerned about my boyfriends well-being and the following day when we passed her in the hall she asked how his hand was and apologized again.
Now, I'm not giving this a 4/5 star because it's huge hotel where you get lost in the shuffle and there's a grand pool because there isn't any of that.
I'm giving a 4 star because i anticipated 2.5 based on online reviews and if these people stayed at the same hotel I stayed at and had the same or similar staff, there's just no way they didn't enjoy there stay.
Realize that you pay for what you get and in this case, it was a steal.
The location was GREAT! Walking distance to Boylston Street (shopping, dinning, pharmacy, supplement shop, library, etc) and Newbury (infamous for more shopping and dinning). Bus stops and T stations are located at every other corner. Very easy to maneuver.
My boyfriend and I are athletic so we didn't mind walking a semi-lengthy distance... If you're at all like us, you can even walk down to Mass Ave too for more dining. & If that's not you're thing, cabs are easy to come by.
Regardless, this place was awesome.
Clean rooms, friendly and accommodating staff, great location.
Hotel 140 serves it's purpose... A place to rest your head.

title: “loved the window seats!”
text: Great location and helpful, professional staff. Elegant lobby and fun comfortable rooms. Ours had a view of the river. My only complaint was that the rooms both had a bit of an odor. My sister described it as "leisure suit".

title: “Loved it!”
text: Had a mother/daughter weekend and stayed one night at this lovely hotel based on the numerous excellent reviews found on this website. This hotel has the elegance and quaintness of many smaller, older European hotels. The staff was courteous and helpful; the rate ($139/night) was very reasonable; and the room itself was a good size and tastefully decorated. Wrought-iron gates surrounded each floor of elevators...very art deco! The only tiny drawbacks are the $31 parking fee for guests and the expensive (for what you get) menu at the Atwood Cafe. All in all, this was a wonderful experience and I will definitely go there again.

title: “Nice...but not cheap”
text: This boutique hotel is small, but clean and well maintained. It's not cheap and the rooms are qutie small, like most other NYC accommodations. I've stayed at this hotel 4-5 times....

title: “Great Service...and Patience”
text:
We were only here overnight for a business meeting. The staff took excellent care of us and catered to every need. The rooms were outstanding and spotless. I love the clean feeling of a nice room. 
The staff really impressed me. Our company has some "blue collar" type workers so towards the end of a long night of drinking, our crew became a bit obnoxious and loud. The staff courteously reminded us of other guests but still took care of us like we were VIPS.

title: “A Great Night!”
text: We had a great stay at the Rancho Bernardo Inn! We're locals and went for a night out after our friends in the area told us about it. We had drinks at Veranda Fireside and Dinner at El Bizcocho. The service and food were excellent at both and we love the grounds! The Suite had an awesome outdoor fireplace too! A great night! - Jorge K.

title: “Nice Rooms but Shady Managment”
text:
May 2010. We had the opportunity to spend several nights at this property when we were in the area. The hotel off of a side road off of the toll way. Be careful about driving on the toll way or you could get fined $25.00 each way. I recommend staying off of it. This property is near Rice University, the Galleria is not too far by car and it is near the River Oaks area of Hourston. There is plenty of free parking in the parking lot. 
Check-in was very fast but I knew something was wrong when the front desk person take my Marriott Bonus Bucks coupon. 
Our room was comfortable and your standard Big Box Residence Inns. The bed was comfortable. Lighting in the room was good. , The work desk was moderate and the office-style chair okay.. My The room had a sleeper sofa and a comfortable arm chair.
 The bathroom was clean.. Lighting was good, the towels were plentiful, and the shower worked well – immediate hot water with plenty of pressure. Bath amenities include shampoo, conditioner, lotion/
The breakfast buffet featured scrambled eggs, hot oatmeal, and all the other things you would expect on a breakfast buffet.
The hotel public areas were clean and well-kept, but could use an updating to the style of the rooms. 
When checking out and settling my bill, the front desk management processed Marriott Travel cards first before the Residence Inn Bonus Bucks. This left with a difficult choice because if I used the Bonus Bucks I would not able to use the face value. This is awful strange since on this trip the Residence Inn at Alamo Square in San Antonio had no problem accepting the full amount of the Bonus Buck. Also after this trip I used a Marriot property bonus buck at the Renaissance Madison in Seattle and they had no problem accepting it. I had used a Bonus Buck at the J.W. Marriott Union Square in San Francisco and they had no problem accepting it. This property and it's managment was sneaky in what it did just to make a few bucks!
I have a future trip scheduled for Houston and it is fair to stay I won't be staying at this property again!

title: “Awesome Experience”
text:
My wife and I stayed here on our honeymoon this summer. Overall the Waldorf Astoria was awesome! We booked our room on Priceline, doing the negotiator thing, and got a room for $150 a night, for five nights. We figured since we did one of these deal things we'd get the smallest, least expensive room they had. Instead when we were checking in the person working there asked why we were in New York. We told him it was our honeymoon and he responded by saying that he would make sure we got a nice room to make our stay even more memorable. He got us a suite with king size bed, large sitting area, and two bathrooms. The room was huge and very nice! We couldn't believe it.
Everything else about our stay was also wonderful. All the staff people we dealt with were great. The room was clean and very comfortable. I will agree with some other people who have left reviews that in some places it is showing its age but this in no way took away from our experience. It was such a cool place to stay. My wife and I debated about which hotel to stay at in New York and we were both so happy we went with this one. It was incredible!

title: “wouldn't go anywhere else”
text: When i arrived at the hotel i was greeted with great customer service from the front desk clerk and GM. They quickly got me a room at a great rate. The room was very clean and they even provided me with an advil for my headache and a razor since i forgot mine. The swimming pool was in a comfortable area and very clean as well. My family enjoyed the continental breakfast (great waffles and OJ) and housekeeping constantly did their job. I always stay there when i visit my family in El Paso. They also provide a shuttle to the airport, and the location is near great restaurants and across the street from a mall with a movie theater.

title: “LOVED it! A Gem of a place!”
text:
My friend, who lives in LA, scouted out this hotel for my first trip there with a friendand recommended it because it's located in a safe neighbourhood, at a very convenient location (5mins to the freeway, 10mins to Hollywood & Sunset Boulevard by car) and offers free parking which is amazing because that is partically non-existent in hotels anywhere in the world! 
While the hotel is definitely no Hilton, it is a standalone gem because of it's architecture and interior design. The hotel staff are really nice, friendly & understanding too which is a huge plus! Our return flight was a past midnight flight so it didn't make sense to check out at 12pm because we had the whole day to go. So we asked the front desk if we could extend and were told that if we wanted to extend till 6pm (the norm maximum), we had to pay an additional $20 which was very reasonable, so we did and they gave us the room till 7pm instead! 
Of course, there are some downsides too, as with all places. No elevator, small bathroom and thin walls but these are all honestly very bearable & after a day, you won't even think about it. I quite like the fact that there's no elevators - suits the hotel and it gives you a good daily workout! 
All in all, it's a great hotel to stay in LA for $50/night - I've stayed in a hostel in Korea for the same price because I wanted an ensuite room, it didn't have elevators either & i even had to pay to get my room made up each morning over there!
Great location, great staff and across the road, there's a great little mexican cafe that serves the most amazing freshly made guacamole! 
2 thumbs up!

title: “Perfection!”
text: 1st trip to Boston. Loved the Liberty Hotel! It's all in the details, really. Fantastic service, interesting and beautiful accomodations, great rooms...and quiet, never heard any neighbors! Try Clink, great brunch. Drinks in the lobby are delish. This hotel has a lot of character, I was sad to have to leave it!

title: “Decent hotel for the price and in a GREAT location!!!”
text:
A co-worker and I were in San Fran for an interpreter convention that was held at the San Francisco Marriott (55 4th st). Rooms were way more than we could afford for the week long trip. After much on line looking, I ran across the Taylor web site. I was not impressed w/ the looks but LOVED the price (it was less than $60 a night for two double beds, a private bathroom, and a simple continental breakfast). I was worried about the Taylor due to all the negative reviews but felt " we will be in workshops all day, all we need is a bed and a shower...we should be fine." Much to our surprise, the Taylor was BETTER than we expected! The hotel manager was fantastic! He was able to answer every question we had and recommended some great places for eating and drinking. (There is a great place called the Cellar just around the corner w/ cheap drinks before 9:00...like $1 coronas). The hotel is w/in walking distance of everything needed (laundry, walgreens, union square...even grocery stores IF you are up to walking a little over a mile...one way). And what's great the rooms have a small microwave and fridge in every room so IF you walk to Trader Joe's you have a place to keep your groceries AND heat up food (another bonus to staying at the Taylor).
I will admit there are MUCH nicer hotels in the area but the Taylor has everything you need if you are on a budget! THe rooms are clean, but are old. The bathroom was clean but has thick paint on the walls. It is true that the hotel smells like indian food...often, but it was never bothersome. We never had to wait more than 30 seconds to be buzzed in...even at 2:00 in the morning (the doors are always locked and you have to ring a buzzer to be let in). Yes, the elevator is old and hard to use...we only used it when we were lugging our luggage up to our room and down when it was time to leave. (There is a sign on the front of the elevator about being charged $25 if you leave the gate open...we were very good about closing the gate behind us)! 
I would stay at the Taylor again w/out hesitation!! If you are looking for a budget hotel w/ decent accommdations, the Taylor is for you. If you don't plan on spending much time in your hotel room...the Taylor is for you. I would not recommend this hotel for a family w/ young children and If you want a classy hotel, stay away and shop around the corner. But bottom line, the Taylor is a decent hotel and I plan on returning! (I took pictures and will add at a later time).

title: “Great Location, Construction noise....”
text: Overall we had a pleasant stay at the Hotel Metro. The room we had was great, hot tub and flat screen TV in the bathroom. The elevators were very slow and old but to my understanding they are being updated judging by the signs around the hotel. Some minor problems were that the room service wasnt available for much time, but the restaurant was open pretty late so that made up for it. the restaurant in the hotel was fantastic. the staff were plesant and very quick and the food was outstanding. the main problem i had with the stay was the noise from the consruction in the next building. It started extremely early and felt like they were drilling a hole in my head. Other than that it was a good stay. Im sure i will visit again.

title: “Good stay in Baltimore - old hotel with character”
text:
After reading some of the reviews on here prior to going to Baltimore from the UK I wasn't sure what to expect. Having stayed there while attending a business conference in the Bay Sheriton in July (17-22nd) I need not have worried.The hotel is an old art deco style hotel but the interior is clean and well serviced, my bedroom was large and well appointed. The staff were very helpful and friendly and I have no complaints in that respect. Some hotel areas could do with a slight lick of paint and brightening up but nothing too bad, if the hotel was closer to the bay then I'm sure the owners would spend the money to make it the top hotel in Baltimore as it does have a day gone by character lacking in many modern hotels
When I first arrived I came via shuttle through the less glamorous part of town and wasn't sure what to expect. The Bay is just a 5 or 10 minute walk down hill in a straight line, shops are about 5 or 10 mins walk also so no worries there.

title: “Average Hotel Below Average Service Restaurant”
text: As others have said, be warned the rooms are very small. If you have traveled a lot you will be surprised at the size considering the location, price and that it's a Sheraton. The suites are bigger, book one of those if you don't want to feel cramped. The rooms look very average. Most hotels have ramped up their decor, comfort and luxury details to stay competitive, not this one. Now to the restaurant, yikes where to begin. We are traveling with kids, so when we arrived in the evening they were starving. It took almost an hour to get our food, our appetizer came at the end of our meal. At some point we asked for bread explaining the kids were really hungry, the waitress curtly told us they didn't have any. My husband decided to ask at the more formal restaurant next door and they gave him some and informed him the two restaurants share a kitchen so they should have been able to help us. When the food finally arrived our sandwich was dry, no mayonnaise etc, the chicken nuggets were small and dry, and the spinach dip had to be the worst I've ever eaten served with burnt pita chips. I rarely take the time to write reviews but this experience has been so disappointing that I am writing this during our stay!

title: “Good but could use some help in minor ways”
text:
Firstly, the location is VERY good if going to visit the 9/11 Memorial or have business in lower Manhattan as it is across the street from Ground Zero and around the corner from Fulton St. subway. Beautiful St. Paul Chapel is next door also. 
Rooms - As a Diamond member I inquired about an upgraded and was happily obliged to a junior suite. Perhaps one of the smallest jnr suites I've seen but was happy anyhow. My biggest complaints, the noise from the A/C system or some central unit with a constant loud hum. You can't fault the hotel for the construction noise during the day, just don't expect to sleep much after 6am when the noise starts. I'm actually in DC now in a quiet hotel and very glad for it! --- My other complaint: the carpet. It could use replacing. The carpet felt sticky on the bottom of my bare feet. This could be from residue from carpet cleaners, but either way, gross and you could still see many stains. -- Last complaint: the food. I ordered several items and they were all average or sub-par and the prices were INSANE. I get it that it's Manhattan, but a $6 6oz diet coke. Seriously? You'll be fine if you avoid the hotel food and over-inflated pricing. 
The staff were always smiling and kind and helpful so no fault there. I did not like one wait staff member that was there every Tue-Thursday for breakfast. He was a bit gruff and hurried and never once offered a high-chair or seconds on drinks. 
I will probably stay elsewhere next time, but I'd def stay here again if it were a reward night.

title: “Clean and beautiful”
text: We arrived at The Orchard and loved the location and style of the building. The lobby is well appointed and the staff was incredible. We (and our friends) were upgraded to suites and they were spacious and clean, clean, clean! There's a great pizza place on the corner and the cable cars are closeby. A great hotel at any price and a suite bargain with the free upgrade for around $200 per night. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Atmosphere”
text: I stayed at the Marriott for a conference. The hotel was beautiful. The grounds were wonderful and it was so close to the shops, right next to the convention center and a short walking distance from the Gas Lamp district. The rooms were very clean. The hotel bar had a great sports bar type atmosphere. Very relaxed. Hey, it is San Diego! The pool was a sight, waterfalls and caves and there was a coy pond along the sidewalk coming out of the hotel toward the pool. Each room in the South tower, if I remember correctly, had a balcony and I was one of the lucky ones. If you look to the left you can see sail boats galore in the Marina when you have a city view. The hotel restaurant offered a wonder buffet style breakfast with pastries, omlettes and a lot more. One of the other neat features of the hotel is that it had a computer in the lobby for guests to print their boarding passes. Saves a lot of time when it comes to check in at the airport.

title: “Extremely overly expensive”
text: I'm staying here now. This has been my experience so far: day one... I ordered room service pancakes and they showed up black (burned). We were told by a lady that my next day breakfast would be free (although the hotel keeps arguing it). It was smoked salmon and I had awful food poisoning from it (I've only eaten at the hotel, nothing else would have caused it). The hotel doesn't have a wash/dryer so I had to get my baby's clothes cleaned. For a tiny (and I mean tiny) bag of baby clothes, they charged us 81 bucks-the same as adults and refused to reduce it. I think that's insane.

title: “Amazing trip to San Antonio”
text: This hotel just topped off a great trip. Perfect location and great amenities!

title: “Expect me back!”
text: Such great experience!, the price, the location, the view, the amenities,the staff, all worth it. Expect me back very soon. I have to admit I was surpriced overall, and was not expecting to be treated nicely considering everything I here about NY culture and ambience, but I have to say I loved it! New york, New York is like no other place in the world.

title: “Great Hotel Experience”
text:
My wife and I are newlyweds and this past Christmas we decided to take a Christmas trip to New York City instead of giving each other gifts. 
This was our first time visiting NYC. We researched almost every website for reviews on hotels, as we are very picky about staying at hotels. We finally decided on the Michelangelo. What a wonderful place. 
The staff was excellent and extremely friendly and knowlegable about the places to visit. Bell-Hop Henry is the Man. The hotel is very clean with comfortable beds and lovely bathrooms. I was very impressed on the size of the room. We reserved our hotel based on a internet special for $195. Well worth it. The Hotel is smack in the middle of New York City. 
Only one block from Radio City Music Hall and about 2 blocks to Time Square. The hotel is very quiet, as it sits off the main road. The continental breakfast is another plus. One tip, park your car yourself in the Michelangelo Parking Deck. Parking deck is about 2 blocks from hotel and is very secure and inexpensive. This hotel made our vacation a wonderful Holiday memory. NYC during Christmas is magnificant. We visited the Empire State Building, Statue of Liberty, saw the Radio City Christmas Spectacular, visited Ground Zero, shopped 5th Avenue, strolled Time Square, rode a carraige ride through Cental Park, and saw the Broadway play Urinetown (hilarious) in a three day visit. I highly recommend staying at The Michelangelo. Good Bless America
John and Courtney

title: “Excellent location and style”
text: Great location close to Sundance Square. Very comfortable rooms. Staff was very courteous and attentive and the valets were top notch. This will be my new place to stay when visiting Fort Worth.

title: “Eclectic and professional--and home to a wonderful cat.”
text: My room was large and quaint and equipped with desk, rocking chair, refrigerator, along with a nice bed with a down comforter. The host cat, Mona, is humble and polite, as are all the staff people. The breakfast room includes freshly boiled eggs along with the regular continental fare. The walk to the U Street Metro was quick and always interesting.

title: “Perfect location, comfortable beds and bedding”
text: We stayed at Nine Zero for four nights. The location is ideal as it is in the centre of the city next to Boston common. Happy hour every evening. Always iced water with lemon or orange sometimes iced tea in reception. Pillow menu useful as we needed one firm pillow and another not so firm. Restaurant good but pricey as with most hotels though lots of places to eat or get takeaways nearby.

title: “Lovely friendly hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed for 6 nights in April. I had read several poor reviews so was nervous about what the hotel would be like. We had a city view room which although not a great view, it was nice to have a view of the city.
The room was nice, it was a little old fashioned but kind of quaint. It had a king bed and plenty of room, and outside of the bathroom was a little make up area with huge lights above the mirror. The wake up beverages were great, they were always there on time and enough for two cups each, it was a nice touch.
Room service was great, the lemon souffle pancakes are the best, we had to have them twice!!
The concierge was very helpfull, and arranged restaurants and trips for us.
The Town car took us to the airport at the end of the stay, I would reccommend it rather than taking a taxi, it costs the same as a taxi but is a nicer car and the driver was friendly.
We didn't really drink in the bar, it didn't have a very good cocktail list and was lacking in atmosphere.
We really felt that the staff were very friendly and helpfull, and we couldn't fault the service that we had.
All in all we really enjoyed our stay at this hotel, I would recommend it.

title: “Wonderful Stay.”
text: Room was nice albeit slightly outdated. Beds were great, breakfast was fantastic, all in all a wonderful stay. Staff was friendly and efficient, check-in was extremely fast. I would definitely stay here again. Also worth it to note that the desk chair was the most comfortable of any hotel I have ever stayed in.

title: “Brand new, spacious rooms, incredible views, Times Square and Theatre”
text: Really a great room for New York. The high floor, corner room was awesome with great Hudson river and city-scape views. We also enjoyed the location. Although Times Square was not the big attraction for us, it was fun to end each evening by walking through, just to get that last dose of NYC energy.

title: “We won't stay any where else!”
text: The Dolphin is our place to stay while in SanDiego. We love Point Loma and all the marinas. Even if we rent a car, public transit is so great in town and the motel is conveniently located for that. Restaurants and eateries are very nearby and really close is a TraderJoe's. Best of all is how extremely nice the owners are. We love the retro feel and the cleanliness as well. Can't go wrong with the Dolphin.

title: “Tragically hip”
text: I stayed there last week (2nd week in Oct. 2002). I have to say though it was quite neat looking in decor, it was a little overly trendy. From the lobby to the rooms, the halls and common areas are all dimly lite. I'm sure this is to create an atmosphere, but it was a little too dark for my taste. The rooms also have TERRIBLE noise isolation from room to room. There was about 12 of us that all had their own rooms and no one had anything good to say about that. You could hear everything from casual conversation to typical TV noise, etc... . For the price of the rooms I don't think that I've ever stayed at a place with that bad of "noise isolation". It does look quite cool, though.

title: “Much better and newly remodeled!”
text:
I have stayed at this property before, and this time around, the hotel stay exceeded my expectations!! I stay in San Deigo often for work and have stayed at many locations in the Hotel Circle area. When making the reservation, I spoke with Sherri, who was incredibly helpful and kind. She informed me that this hotel has been going through a renovation, and gave me a great rate to come and check it out. Once I got to the hotel, the front desk staff was equally kind and helpful. Merideth, who checked me in, made sure that I had a room that was catered to my needs, and also informed me of various places in the area that may be of interest to me. She went far beyond what is expected to make me feel comfortable about my stay. My newly remodeled room had a brand new fridge in it, as well as a brand new microwave and coffee maker. The carpet was new and so was the bed and bedding. I also received free wireless and a good selection of television channels.
All and all, the stay was perfect, at a perfect price. If you are looking to travel to the area, and consider this hotel, just be sure to ask for one of the newly remodeled rooms and you will not be disappointed.

title: “Great location by City Hall, good for business travelers”
text: I stay at this property often when on business at City Hall. The location can't be beat, and the staff are accommodating and friendly. The hotel restaurant is above-average in terms of quality for a hotel, I think, and the prices are not bad. I prefer it to the Residence Inn next door. While the Residence Inn has larger rooms, I think the rooms in the Courtyard are a bit nicer and more updated. The Executive Suite with the separate desk and sofa area are great for spreading out when you have work to do. My only complaint would be that the gym is small, (a few treadmills, 2 bikes, and 3 ellipticals and some weight equipment) and sometimes you have to wait for a machine in the morning. I have not visited the pool and can't comment on that.

title: “Clean, modern hotel in a great location with friendly/helpful staff”
text:
This was a very clean, modern hotel in a great location. The staff were very friendly and helpful and had good recommendations for places to eat. They really seem to care about your experience and do everything they can to make it a good one. 
If coming from LaGaurdia Airport don't take shuttle! It took 1.5 hours and cost almost the same as it would for a cab ($25), and the cab taken at the same time would have taken .5 hours. For coffee lovers, empire coffee is right around the corner on 7th avenue and offers great selection.
We were very happy with our experience at this hotel. Don't forget to visit them on FB before your trip!

title: “Great Location and rooms”
text: We loved the location it was reasonably quiet and it had the best supermarket across the street "Fairway Markets", 72nd street subway close by. We would stay there again.

title: “Imagine my unpleasant surprise when I arrived at this Hotel!”
text: I got bumped from the Hilton, Inner Harbor, and instead they offered me.... the Home 2 Suites. Same price, but a world of difference. It just looked like a local, seedy joint where undesirables might hang out. The Front Desk staff were ok, not overly friendly, but not bad. Nasty, small elevator and really ugly rooms. The bedspread and linens were so wrinkled I was afraid to sleep on them. I put things over it, so that I wouldn't have to let it touch my skin. To add insult to injury, they wanted to charge $25 a day for parking. I was already paying almost $170 a night for the dump! Be very careful! Just because it has Hilton attached to it doesn't mean it meets the standards of most Hiltons.

title: “good old hotel”
text:
we liked the hotel but was little mislead by website room photos which shows a much newer hotel than it really is
rooms are ok but ailes and reception are in need of an urgent renovation
rate wasnt cheap so i was expecting something better
rooms are on the small size
pros:location at union square,parking just one block away (they deal the price for you paying directly to the hotel),coffee apples and cookies for free
just a place to stay no long last memories here

title: “Smelly sheets, disappointing hotel”
text: My husband and I are not picky when it comes to hotels, but we felt we really picked a bad one with the Stratford. We have stayed in several hotels in the Union Square area and this one was definitely the worst. Upon arriving, we found the front desk staff not very inviting, and the garage that was supposedly available to park our car was nonexistant. That is not something that typically bothers us, but when we got to our room we were dissapointed some more. The room was tiny, which again, no problem. BUT, the sheets STUNK! It smelled like mold had been growing on them for weeks. We were hoping they would be changed for our second night, but the smell was on the second night's sheets too. It was gross. The bed was not very comfortable either. We're 26 and 27 years old and we had neck problems after waking up there two days in a row. Another annoying thing is that the remote was nailed down into the bedside table as well as the alarm clock. The problem with this was that the glowing red neon lights of the alarm clock were glaring in my face when I was trying to sleep, and you can't turn the stupid thing around because it is nailed down! Our bathroom had the dingiest flourescent bulb which shed harldy any light as well. On the plus side, it is in a great location, but we have stayed in several other hotels in that area for the same price that blow this one away. This was the first hotel I've ever felt I needed to write a review about.

title: “Awesome place to stay”
text: Simply amazing place. Loved the large, double twin size beds that were in our room. Had a comfortable night's sleep. Definitely would return for another stay.

title: “Stay Here!”
text:
This was a great place, I could check in earlier than 3pm, and as I had requested a quiet room at the back of property I would not have thought I was downtown, it was so quiet.
The staff were all fantastic, nothing was too much trouble and any questions were answered with a smile.
The room had everything I needed, comfy bed and pillows,coffee maker, fridge and new flat screen tv. The bathroom had a bath/shower and the water was always hot,with lots of toiletries available.
Hotel is close to Union Square, Ferry Plaza and most attractions,and Public transport is close by.
Umbrellas are available to borrow too in case you strike a wet day!!! In the mornings coffee is available for guests and there is an afternoon wine reception as well. I had the best stay here and when I next visit San Francisco I won't hesitate in booking a room at The Galleria Park again. Thank you for a marvelous stay.

title: “Nice accomodations, convenient.”
text:
I just got back from a 3 night stay at this hotel. I had a nice experience. The staff was very helpful and made us feel welcome. The free shuttle is very convenient. My boyfriend and I used it twice to go downtown- about a 15/20 minute ride. We called when we wanted to be picked up (usually they circulate every hour and a half but you do have to let them know in advance). The breakfast was decent. There is a pool but we didn't have time to use it. The room was spacious and the fridge is larger than most hotel fridges. 
I would definitely recommend staying here.

title: “A well located convenient Hotel”
text: The hotel is situated near the city centre and is conveniently located. The rooms are spacious and provided with all necessities.However ,what is lacking is good arrangement for complementary breakfast,, which to say the least, is miserly.

title: “WEEK OF HORROR!”
text: I would definitely not recommend this hotel, (if that's what you want to call it), for anyone to stay. I would have rather stayed under a bridge under the freeway. The staff was unprofessional and down right ghetto (but I'm sure that's what they are used to). The manager/owner is a serious joke. He was the leader of that nasty rat pack of a hotel. No microwaves in room, outlets had shortages and some not working, iron not working, smoke alarm hanging from wall, toilets soiled, And this was just the first day. So you can imagine the rest. Take a word from the wise, if anyone suggests that you stay at Americas Best Value Inn at 6510 Frankford Avenue, Baltimore, Maryland please do yourself a favor and run in another direction.

title: “very good and recommended”
text:
We staying at the Inn for a total of 6 nights between in Late july and early august 2011. I can keep this review short and sweet:and all this is given the 200 USD average price we paid for the family room with extra bed.
Nice rooms, good service and kind staff.
great location as its close to the subway and easy to get taxis,
internet working well, shops nearby and the restaurant both for breakfast and dinner good.
 FEDEX packages waiting for which we had send to the hotel,
luggage left for a few days taken care of,
always helpful when we required directions or cabs,
good attitude while it was pretty busy.
I will certainly stay here again and recommend you to the same if you require a decent, clean room at a good, quiet and safe location in DC.

title: “The hotel was nice, but didn't have the amenities that a typical Embassy or Hilton Hotel would have.”
text: The Service was Excellent and the staff was very friendly. But the amenities weren't up to par with other Embassys or Hilton Hotels I have stayed in. There was Never any Ice in the Ice machine or soft drinks in the coke machine on the 4th Floor, the entire time I was here. I paid over $400 dollars a Nite, and expect to have things like that for that room rate. The excuse was that the Hotel was Full, but they knew it was going to be full, and should have made preparations for their guest!! I even told the night clerk, and he said he would pass it on to the Management, but Nothing was ever done about it? Why? The TV's weren't set up for pay per view Movies, and several of the channels were scrambled & couldn't be viewed in the bedroom of Room 426. The channels were also diferent on the 2 TV's in my Room. The TV's were very nice, but need to be Updated to the standard of other Embassy's & Hiltons.

title: “A good cheap place to stay”
text:
I booked in to Chelsea Star after reading reviews of budget NYC hotels here on Tripadvisor. Good central location, clean rooms and friendly staff. Even though they were really busy, they still had time to answer my queries, and stored my huge monstrosity of a bag - at a very small cost, for a few days while I was visiting another state. 
They were helpful with giving me directions and making suggestions of things to see and do in the area, and where to go for decent cheap meals. 
They do have complementary coffee downstairs there too, just take your own creamer or milk. 
I found their outside door security to be very good - while I was waiting for my airport shuttle which was running a bit late, they came down twice to make sure everything was ok. 
I'll stay here again.

title: “Nice with a few oddities”
text:
This hotel is exactly what I would expect for a higher end chain in terms of cleanliness, service, decor, etc. A few negatives and positives stood out though.
POSTITIVES
The conierge was great. I really liked the email ahead option to help us plan our trip. They found us tix for a Yankees vs Red Sox game at Fenway. They booked us a car for a day. They provided us with tickets for sightseeing tours.
The Rumba bar was a hip and happening place, unusual for a hotel bar. Lots of locals as well as hotel guests. A fun place to start of end a night.
The food in Miel was great, especially the Sunday brunch. Being open 24hrs was a bonus too.
Bed was comfortable. Linens awere nice enough.
COULD HAVE BEEN NEGATIVE, BUT HAD HAPPY ENDING
We were unhappy with our first room and a request to move was accommodated. We started in a room that was facing a wall of plastic covering a construction project. We were worried about the noise in the early morning and asked to be moved. We got some push back from the front desk initially, but they relented and moved us in the end. We ended up in a room on the 11th floor facing the city (the fire hall). This was fine. It was a corner room so lots of windows and natural light and neighbours only on one side. 
We were able to check in at 10am. Although, I would not have expected anything less because we had actually paid for the previous night and were unable to use it due to a missed flight connection. When we asked to move rooms we were told we would not be able to check in until 3pm and that there would be no guarantee. It took some time to explain that we should be able to stay in our current room and move later because we had technically already paid for the night, even if we didn't arrive until the morning. All I wanted was to freshen up after more than 24hrs of travel then head out sightseeing. In the end this was accommodated. However, the process to get there was a bit painful.
NEGATIVES
The service in Miel, the restaurant, was TERRIBLE. At brunch we were greeted by a waiter who explained the brunch menu to us and then actually said he wasn't our waiter and walked away. As he did this I was in the middle of asking for a drink and he turned and said he supposed he could do that for us even though he wasn't our waiter. Then somehow he became our waiter, but basically ignored us. I eventually got up and asked the hostess to either get us a waiter who wished to wait on us or to move us to another waiter's section. We got the same waiter, but he was obviously told to smarten up. The service improved, but still wasn't great. However, it should be noted that the crepes (both sweet and savoury) were fantastic.
We ate at Miel late at night (just past midnight) one evening. Again, the food was fantastic. The service was slow and frankly painful to watch. The restuarant had about 5 occupied tables and two servers. Between then they couldn't determine who was doing what and as a result we waited for bread, for drinks, for everything really. The food preparation was slow for such an empty restuarant. Surely they would realize that what people want at that time of night is a quick bite, not a lingering meal.
During both instances in Miel we noted that the wait staff dragged their feet (literally shuffled around), spoke at a barely audible level, and seemed annoyed to be asked to do anything for you.
The business centre is a corner of the convenience store and the hours are not clearly marked. The computers face out so all the customers can see what you are doing.
The room didn't have a hotel information book so it was hard to determine what the amenities were and what the various hours and costs for certain amenities were. When I asked the front desk told me that they don't put these books in rooms. This was frustrating as I had to look everything up on the TV and it was slow.
The bell hops and door staff were great until check out day when we actually had to step onto the road and hail our own cab.
The sliding frosted glass windows that link the bathroom to the bedroom were a terrible design flaw. Fine if you are in the room alone, but with a partner to meant that all activity in the bathroom was easily heard by the person in the bedroom. There is a gaping hole at the bottom of the sliding windows so any bathroom odour leaks into the bedroom. Also, when you get up in the night (or are the first to wake in the morning) and turn the bathroom light on it completely illuminates the bedroom and disturbs your partner.
FINAL THOUGHTS
All in all we enjoyed our stay. There were a few elements that could have been imporved.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Unable to stay in it's sister hotel the Casablanca we chose the Giraffe and so glad we did.
Located in an excellent location (26th and Madison) close to subway stops this is a top hotel. The staff are so friendly and helpful. Rooms are large and airy which is a godsend in New York. Bed was very large and comfortable. All the amenities in the room were good, TV showing ESPN (great for Euro 2012), the ipod docking station and even the toiletries. 
A very good breakfast comprising of all types of bagels, breads, pastries, eggs and a fresh fruit salad is included in the price as is a cheese and wine evening every night apart from Sunday from 5 to 8.
Would recommend this hotel for any type of stay and when returning to New York we will stay here again.
As a side note I have read some reviews complaining about hearing the road noise. We had no problem even when they were resurfacing 26th Street during the night!

title: “All right”
text:
Friendly and helpful staff, free breakfast in the morning, but I'd say the hotel needs some remodeling.
Rooms were OK, not too small, but not too big either (for NYC standards), bathroom OK, room was a little dark and somewhat outdated. 
Location is a little south, I'd rather go further north next time (for business or tourism).
However, I've stayed in better hotels in NYC. I was expecting a little more from a Hampton Inn hotel, i don't know exactly what, but something more. And the price is not so good value for money either.
I don't think I'll come back.

title: “Great location”
text:
We stayed here for 9 nights on our recent trip to Boston. For the first 6 nights we had the accessible studio suite on the first floor, then after a few nights in Provincetown we returned to the Inn and had a smaller studio suite on the second floor. Both rooms were spacious and lovely. The accessible suite has a jetted tub which I made use of and enjoyed. The other room had a shower stall which was fine. We loved the look of this hotel and decor in the rooms. We also loved the kitchenette as we were able to make some of our own meals and refrigerate milk for coffee, wine, snacks etc. The continental breakfast was fairly basic but did the trick (yogurt, juice, English muffins). 
Location is perfect - just around the corner from the T, shopping, restaurants and a 24 hour grocery store. It is also walking distance to Fenway park where we spent much of our trip.
One thing that did annoy us was the lack of maid service. You have to request housekeeping for short stays. I understand that this is an effort to be more environmentally friendly and I don't need my sheets and towels changed every day but it would be nice to have the garbage changed, especially since we did some cooking ourselves so we did produce some mess in the kitchen. We requested housekeeping one night around 10 pm and they didn't come clean our room until about 6 pm the next day, so when we returned to the room after our days's activities we had to wait for the room to be cleaned. It would have been nice if it had been done while we were out during the day.
We would return to this hotel.

title: “Good for families, but just okay for couples.”
text:
We stayed at the Town and Country this last weekend, which was a very busy summer weekend and the hotel was full. Several conventions were going on and the hotel was full up with families. The first night we stayed in the Palm Court Tower, which was very noisy and we could hear what the people next door were saying because of the adjoining door. 
The room itself was on the shabby side, with stained wallpaper and the bed was very hard. My husband and I both had trouble sleeping and were awakened early by the family in the next room. We could also hear the elevator, which was next to our room. I called the front desk and asked for a change of rooms. They were very helpful and polite. The next night we stayed in a much smaller, but much more comfortable, remodeled room. I have to say that all of the staff in the hotel, restaurants and the concierge desk, were very helpful and polite. Also, the Trolley is located just behind the hotel, which was very convenient. I would advise you to stay in the Palm Court Tower if you have a family, which awakens early, and you want extra room. Those rooms are large, with a small fridge, extra sink, table and couch. For couples who want privacy and comfort, you would be better off in the courtyard rooms. I would stay here again, but only in the off season, but my husband said he would not, because the price was too high for a below average room.

title: “Feels like home”
text: My family booked a king with sleeper room for a week. As you walk into the room, there is a large closet to one side and your kitchen amenties to your other: sink, cabinets, dishwasher, fridge and stovetop. Straight ahead is your table with 2 chairs tucked against that same kitchen wall and the sofa sleeper is just beyond that facing you. Our room bumped out to the left...so there sits your king bed facing the table and your roomy bath on the other side of the wall of the closet. I share all this info...because I could not find a decent picture on their website when we booked. I must say you can tell it is a new hotel. I love the decor and the finishings feel more expensive. Hall noise was not an issue except for maybe my family when I tried to sneak out in the morning to workout. The doors to the room were incredibly loud. The workout room was great..complete with weights. I enjoyed the patio area outside the lobby complete with tables and sofa, fireplace and TV. There is even a grill for your use by the pool which we did take advantage of one night. There is a decent reception Mon. - Wed. evenings. When we were there, they served Chicken Alfredo, Chicken Fajitas, and Hamburgers. Overall, the staff was EXCELLENT! They were all so polite and friendly and hard-working. The common areas were usually very clean. David, a manager, wished us safe travels our last day. We had stayed at a Holiday Inn Express in Fort Worth prior to attend the same convention and was disappointed by their shuttle service. BUT not here! They were so fast and efficient. I would highly recommend the Towneplace if you are visiting Fort Worth. It has a lot of nice touches that make it feel like home...for a value price. You are just a heartbeat way from everything. Also, FREE PARKING!! You will not be disappointed!

title: “Unparalleled SF Hotel”
text: The St. Regis is the best hotel in San Francisco, no question. The lobby is outstanding, with comfortable sofas and chairs, a unique fireplace, and welcoming bar. The rooms are beautiful, well designed, and classy. I stayed in a Metropolitan Suite with a view of the Park; the living room, dining room, secluded separate bedroom and expansive bathroom with deep soaking tub, is a home away from home. The Remede spa is clean, spacious and comfortable, with separate men's and women's jacuzzi, steam room, dry sauna, showers, and then a short trip up to the treatment rooms (with complimentary champagne before a massage). What makes the hotel superior is the quality and friendliness of the staff - thoroughly professional and caring. Superb location and value. Stay here.

title: “Just OK.”
text:
The hotel is a nice bargain for the location and room amenities. Located in the middle of Hollywood, is a 3 start property with a 4 start service. Front desk is extremely helpful, and provide you with many attractions information as soon as you check in. Room is what you expect in a studio apartment. However, don’t expect a fancy room. Just a nice place to relax. Pool is small, but great. Many dinner options within walking distance. Metro is just 3 minute walk. My only complaint is the noise during the morning due to the trucks loading/unloading process at the mall. Ask for an inside room, not one that face the street.
If you are looking for great location and a nice place to relax after a long day, this hotel is a strong option.

title: “Would gladly be locked up here anytime”
text:
The Liberty Hotel, located on the site of the former Suffolk County prison next to Mass General Hospital in Boston's Beacon Hill neighborhood, is the rare hotel that correctly plays a theme just right. It is apparent from the moment you pull up that this is no normal property and the hotel did a good job of preserving some parts of the old jail. However once you get up to the rooms, lets just say no prisoner ever had it this good. They are very nice and the bathrooms in particular are an exercise in getting the most of the available space. The views towards the Back Bay from our room were spectacular, we could see all the way to Fenway Park.
One of the nicest things about this property is that they don't try and nickel and dime you for things that many hotels often do. Wireless internet access is complimentary and the business center allows you to print as much as you need at no additional cost.
