The food service in the hotel is also very nice, we ate one meal in the Clink and had drinks in the Alibi bar. Try to "Jailbait Mojito" at Alibi, you'll thank me later. 
The location is excellent at well, a close walk to downtown Boston but, perhaps even better, literally across the street from the Charles/MGH red line stop.
We would gladly stay here anytime.

title: “Been there, done that”
text: I'm a bit late writing this as we stayed at the Waldorf in December 2010 but I doubt much has changed ;) This is undoubtedly an iconic location and at Christmas when we were there the public areas were beautiful and made for a fantastically atmospheric entrance. The room we had however was really very basic, pretty small and the bathroom very outdated. We were travelling with children (8,11) who found the hotel stuffy and old fashioned and we left with the feeling that we've had in other high end hotels that the constant stream of 'extras ' such as wifi and tv channels are designed for those that don't have to think about running up a big bill. I felt that the Waldorf was a bit too complacent, relying on it's fantastic heritage. When poor weather cancelled flights and extended our stay we were unable to extend our room and moved to the Pearl which was without doubt a much better option for our family. Glad we did it as it feels great to jump in a cab and say 'Take me to the Waldorf' but we've done it now and wouldn't stay there again.

title: “Service is everything”
text: In this case, the service outweighed anything that wasn't perfect about my stay here. From the moment you enter the building until you leave, your interaction with the staff is very professional and positive. The workout facility, steam room, spa, etc.was an unexpected perk compared to the nearby Marriott and Hilton. Can't wait to stay there again.

title: “Cheap rooms, but poorly equipped & bad service”
text:
The private room was very very cold and the blankets was very thin- no duvets were availiable. 
The service was poor- the receptionist had no clue what so ever and was not serviceminded.
We had made a reservation for 7 days and we had booked a private room. The first thing they told us was that after three days we had to change room because the was a mix up with the booking. No problem was the word they used but sure that's a problem. The hot water was turned off twice, without any notice. And the second room we had to move to during our stay was if possible even colder than the other, was smelling indian food and was a missing a heating element, a nightlamp, a coat hanger, a chair and the tv remote!

title: “"Cozy and Inviting Five Star Hotel"”
text:
My first ever Four Seasons Experience was the Four Seasons Philadelphia. We were warmly welcomed by the friendly and informative front desk staff. When the concierge was busy helping another guest, the Front Desk agent was able to give me outstanding restaurant recommondations that completely fit our needs.
The rooms were spacious and the views of the fountains were spectacular. I really felt like we were able to see the best of Philadelphia from our room. You can never go wrong with a hotel that offers Turn Down Service! 
Do not forget to enjoy a night cap in the Swann Lounge. Definitely a place to see and be seen. Amazing!

title: “Very reasonably priced, awesome views, friendly staff, small bathrooms”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here for 4 nights in December. It is hands down the most reasonably priced hotel on The Magnificent Mile! Parking fees are reasonable as well. I spent a very long time researching many hotels in the area so am confident in saying the fees are reasonable! After debating on whether to reserve the King Deluxe or Standard, we decided on the King Deluxe and were very happy we did. The views of the lake, Grant Park, and Museum Campus are amazing, the king size bed was very comfortable, and the room was very clean!! Lucky for us, Chicago was experiencing some mild temperature winter days during our stay, so walking to Museum Campus and back to the hotel on multiple days was enjoyable, and well worth not paying a taxi or paying to park our car at one of the museums! The staff at Essex Inn are also extremely friendly and helpful!
 The biggest downside was the small bathroom, but we managed just fine. The sink is literally not much bigger than your hand, and I imagine it would be difficult for a bigger person to move around comfortably in it. Some people might also consider the lack of a restaurant in the hotel to be a downside, but there are plenty of restaurants within walking distance, so we didn't consider this a big deal at all. The water temperature of the pool was luke warm, but again not so much of a big deal to us. The only other minor negatives that I can think of would be hearing other hotel room doors slam, and a slow elevator at times.
 Overall, highly recommended if your budget conscious and want to stay on The Magnificent Mile! Pay the extra money and stay in the King Deluxe, walk as much as possible to your destination to save on transportation or parking fees, and enjoy your experience in The Windy City!

title: “Cheap place to stay in Philly, but expect what you pay for.”
text:
I am a very frequent business traveler. I almost always stay at Starwood properties, however, this was my first experience at Four Points. The Philly Four Points was a very good bargain for Philly, however, this is a expect what you pay for experience. 
The hotel is located a few blacks away from the main areas of Philly, however , a 10 minutes walk will be all you need to find yourself in the main restaurant and vibrant center of downtown Philly. The lobby is small, however the bar and restaurant is what you would expect from a hotel of this variety. 
The rooms are extremely small, the bed taking the majority of the room. So much so that you can barely sit at the desk. The rooms are also a bit noisy. Rooms were of questionable cleanliness. 
All in all, a value based experience.

title: “Great location, feels small. Breakfast needs help.”
text: Within walking distance to great shopping, Rockefeller Center and the theater district, this well-run hotel is perfectly situated. Unlike the 1000-guest impersonal behemoths, this hotel has the feel of a bed and breakfast. Unfortunately, breakfast is a weak point. The restaurant shares a footprint with the evening bar, and music from the previous evening permeates, albeit at a lesser volume, at 7 o'clock in the morning. Coffee is refreshed infrequently.

title: “Definately, Home away from Home!!”
text: Everything about this hotel was excellent. The rooms were very clean, offered everything i could have possibly needed. The location was nice. The employees were awesome!! It was truthfully 'HOME AWAY FROM HOME!!"

title: “Nice location in SF”
text: The Tuscan Inn provided us with a nice location close to many of the traditional tourist sites in SF. The accomodations were comfortable and the staff was very helpful in guiding us to resources for bike rentals, places to eat, etc. The in house concierge service was nice to have at our disposal.

title: “excellent views with very helpful staff”
text: We arrived at the hotel feeling pretty tired due to the flight, but once we got into our room we woke up.The view was second to none, a staff member named frank helped us with our luggage and gave us a map and pointed out some landmarks and gave us a detailed but quick brief on where to go how to get there ect... We was on the 38th floor, the very top, the lift took no time at all to reach the top. The only thing i can think of that could improe the hotel is to place Tea/Coffee making facilities into the rooms.

title: “Just average for a Hyatt”
text: This hotel is mostly lobby (beautiful) as the rooms are only slightly better than a new Hampton Inn. The room was clean and well maintained and the carpet/furniture had no obvious stains, tears, etc. The best point was the volume of water from the shower head. Very impressive and the best I have ever seen at a hotel anywhere. The most suprising disappoiment was the quality of the towels - thin and cheap and not at all what I expected from this Hyatt. Overall my stay was fine and I have no real complaints.

title: “Comfortable "No frills" hotel with free parking”
text:
This is in a small chain of hotels in San Francisco that we love. It is located in the Marina District and within close walking distance to many good restaurants.
The parking garage has room for one car per family and you can come and go as you please with no charge. The rooms are comfortable, clean and quiet--accessed by an elevator from the garage. No breakfast but the room has a coffeemaker which is fine with us. We simply walk or drive to a cozy little breakfast diner on Chestnut street next to the movie theater. Sorry, can't remember the name but a real gem.
Great area for walking to Giardelli Square, the Marina, Union Street, etc.
Prices are quite reasonable for San Francisco.
Recommend to anyone who enjoys a good night's sleep with free parking and walking distance to good eateries.

title: “Would definitely return”
text: I thought it was an excellent value for San Francisco. While touted as in the Financial District, it is really in Chinatown. The service was good and the hotel offers complimentary wi-fi. The wine bar and restaurant in the hotel were excellent. The bedding was comfortable but it was a little noisy due to the construction and we were located on the 16th floor.

title: “57 minute wait to check in”
text: In addition to the long wait to check in, the air conditioner sounded like a waterfall and leaked water all over the carpet which had also stained the bed skirting. Black mold was growing up the wallpaper in the corner by the air conditioner!! Seriously!! I only discovered this problem when we returned to our room around midnight. Since the person at check in told me the reason for the delay at check in was that the hotel was overbooked, I didn't bother asking for a different room. When I checked out, I related all of the above to the person at the desk and they simply shrugged and told me they would notify maintenance!! I'm sure the hotel manager will respond to this review by saying he is sorry for the inconvenience. This type of stuff is not what I expect to find at a Sheraton Hotel. I hope they get these problems fixed before they rent the room to someone else.

title: “This great hotel facility and staff that made the stay exceptional”
text: My wife and I enjoyed a great anniversary weekend. The hotel staff was great and obviously concerned with making sure we had everything we needed. The breakfast was great, the breakfast room was clean and the staff was very attentive.

title: “Room was clean service was good, just a few problems that will keep me from going back”
text: Rooms were clean, but we stayed on 10th floor and it took 4-5 minutes for hot water to get to tub, toilet wouldn't flush contents. Air conditioner was old style mounted in window. Took me a few minutes to find the light switch that powered the ac

title: “We had only one complaint!”
text:
It was our first trip to NYC. My wife, two daughters and I stayed at the Crowne Plaza and we really enjoyed our stay. The only complaint that we had was that because of the large amount of people staying there on occasion there was a long wait for the elevators. We were on the 41st floor and the view was great! If you want to be in the middle of everything this is the place to stay. The rooms were very comfortable. Don't listen to the negative comments, you won't be disappointed.
Ottinger Family,
Greeneville Tennessee

title: “Great Stay and convenient and Great Staff”
text: Went for a Large Conference AIHce from Sunday 6/17/12 to Wednesday 6/20/12 1. Hotel was really close from the convention Center 2. Great view of the Museum of Indiana 3. Restaurant Staff extremely friendly 4. Room Clean. 5. Great Response from Reception when asking for info or suplies 6. Good Gym.

title: “value for money and great location”
text: clean room, central location (hop on /off bus stop right around the corner) and polite staff, with a complimentary continental style breakfast. what more do you need in NYC. would definitely stay there again, and would recommend to others.

title: “The best hotel in NY, discrete heaven yet full of celebrities”
text:
We again went to the NY4S which we simply love to go everytime. The rooms, the service and everything about this hotel is just perfect. It lacks a swimming pool if you need one, we do not in NY. But its Ty lounge is fabulous, the staff is just great and its restaurant Joel Robuchon offers an exquisite world class food experience in the utmost relaxed service atmosphere so to us it is simply perfect.
Our daughters loved the fact that the hotel had Jennifer Aniston and Justin Bieber in the hotel. Last year the Boston Celtics where hanging out in the lobby, never felt so small! Guests there are all discrete and all enjoy the peaceful atmosphere commanded by its magnificent entrance hall. So that is probably why all celebrities feel good staying there, enjoying themselves and not being disturbed. One of these celebrities is actually my wife which also enjoys the peaceful and distinguished atmosphere.
The 4SNY is always a wonderful experience so we keep returning to it everytime.

title: “8 simple reasons why you'll love this place...”
text:
The best staff you could ask for - friendly and helpful with lots of knowledge
Nice and clean rooms
The bagels at breakfast
Beautiful, quiet garden
Wireless internet access all over the place!
Coffee 24/7
Located right between Chelsea and Village
Last but not least, the overall ambiance - once you've set your foot at this friendly and easygoing place you'll keep coming back, year after year.
Anders Thorssell

title: “Great location, clean and affordable.”
text: We stayed at the LA airport Marriott at the end of a road trip from San Francisco down Highway 1 and ended here. The hotel is extremely clean and modern. Prices are relatively affordable for the area (LA can be expensive). It is a great location to get to various points throughout the city, assuming you have a car which is a necessity in LA. Overall I would recommend this hotel and definitely stay here again.

title: “Amazing stay in Chicago”
text: Being a brand new hotel you might expect some start up glitches. Not so, this hotel was perfect. We were able to walk to the hotel from Union Station, the El and was at the corner near the hotel. The staff could not do enough for us. The room was so comfortable and new and clean. The bathroom was to die for. The soaking tub was unbelievable. Under mount lighting at the vanity, large stand alone shower and small separate toilet room. Thick doors and virtually sound proof. How great was our stay!

title: “Internet”
text: Literally the slowest internet I've experienced in years. I felt as if I was using dial up when I tried to use my laptop in my room. It wouldn't connect all day and when it finally did not a single page would open. Everything else was okay, but not great.

title: “Nice hotel in North Houston”
text:
The furnishings and decor of this hotel are top-notch. The rooms are very comfortable, quiet, and functional, with a great office chair, desk, sofa, and comfortable bed. The Bathroom is nice and clean, great shower and bath amenities. The internet service is excellent, but expensive (though included on executive floor). Breakfast buffet in the lobby is also very good, but expensive - stay on the executive floor for included continental breakfast and snacks. There is a Starbucks open in the lobby open mornings. The restaurant/bar just seems like it isn't really trying - I only ate there once in 10 days.
The self service laundry for this large hotel consisted of only one pair of machines on the 3rd floor. This is really disappointing for a hotel of this caliber. I guess they expect you to have it laundered. Another disappointment was a lack of power outlets on the nightstands - I really dislike moving furniture to access an outlet on the wall to charge my phone.
The neighborhood the hotel is located in isn't that great, although the grounds are well kept and security is ever-present. The mall across the street is mostly defunct, and although there's fast food nearby I found myself driving more than 5 miles for decent restaurants. However it was very convenient for my work location with great access to the highways.

title: “Pleasing”
text: My company put me here for three weeks, and I really had no issues with anything the hotel had to offer. True, the beds were hard, but, if you looked on the side of the mattress you could dial the desired softness you required. Reception was friendly, the gym and pool were nice, and the attached restaurants were a treat.

title: “Heat Issues”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights in February, the room itself was fine, however our room had heating issues. First of all the windows were poorly sealed and there was a draft causing the heating unit not to operate, while the hotel did provide a portable heater this did not help in the marble, tiled bathroom which was freezing. We were forced to run the shower to heat the bathroom. I am still trying to figure out why there was no heat in the bathroom, not even a heat lamp. Honestly we were just disappointed , which was unfortunate because the location is great.

title: “Well placed, spacious and great service”
text: The Westin is large but retains a personal level of service which is admirable. Placed conveniently for shopping at the Domain mall, the hotel has a cavernous reception which is sleek and modern with plenty of sofas and seating. Check in was effortless and rooms were spacious and well equipped. Breakfast was not cheap and not included in my rate, but the choice, freshness and quality was excellent, including some local dishes which was a nice touch. Overall, I'd recommend the Westin whole heartedly as it's a quality hotel where over a week's stay I was always greeted with a genuine smile and will to help out guests.

title: “Great location”
text: The location was great, the bed was comfortable, and the service was excellent. Would definitelt stay here again!

title: “Great location and clean hotel”
text: Went to SF to celebrate our 1 year anniversary. The hotel is in an excellent location. I prefer the Embarcadero to Union Square. We walked to the hotel from the subway station. Very easy to get to. The rooms are a good size and very clean. The bathrooms are also a good size. We had partial view of the ocean and bridge - very pretty. Love San Francisco. So much to do and see. We did a tour of Alcatraz which was great. Got lucky with the weather. It was sunny and warm (in February). Also did a tour of the city that we enjoyed. Overall it was a nice hotel and we would stay here again.

title: “not happy”
text:
At a rate of $135 a night, I expect better service and cleaner, fresher looking rooms from a hotel. The furniture is worn out, shabby (not in a chic way). The duvet cover I did not feel like touching at all. 
Cleaning staff refolded used towels and put them back on the rack. I found hair on the sink after the place had been cleaned (apparently). Bath towels felt like sand paper on skin. The heater rattled and hummed all night. 
Coffee makers are not provided but wake-up service provides complimentary coffee/tea/hot beverage if requested. 
The front desk attendants rarely smiled. The bellhops and concierge did a far better job in seeming friendly and pleasant. 
I had a great view of the puget sound from my 11th floor window. 
Location - Pike Place market is walking distance (15 minutes) and so is west lake center from where one can take the monorail to the space needle. Then again, nearest Macdonald's is also a 15-minute walk. That to me is a big disadvantage if you are craving junk food (as I am wont to do when I am traveling) at midnight.

title: “A Pleasant Stay”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Monaco one night. Because I booked through Hotwire, I had some concerns. However, the Hotel Monaco staff was wonderful and we never felt like we were treated differently because of booking with Hotwire. We checked in quickly and they gave us a room on the top floor. I ordered a goldfish and it arrived within minutes. The room was not overly large, but it suited our needs. We were able to hear other hotel guests outside of our door at night, but that is why we bring earplus when we travel. We did not park at the Hotel, as there is a parking structure (the Olympic Parking Garage) exactly one block away that charged $29 (the hotel charged $40). The 5:00 p.m. free wine hour was a nice touch and we thought the wine was rather good. Restaurants were within walking distance with a Starbucks two doors down. We did drive over to Pike's Place Market as it would have been quite a walk.

title: “Love the Hilton”
text: Conference held at this hotel, rooms always comfortable and clean, bathrooms have plenty of towels, staff very helpful and friendly, love Starbucks coffee! Should put it in the rooms as well, and real coffee cream not powdered. Very comfortable bed

title: “Nice, Relaxing Stay at The Tremont”
text:
Stayed at the Tremont Suites Hotel for one evening. We arrived at the hotel at 11:30 and checked into our studio suite room (3107) within 10 minutes. Staff at the front desk was very nice and friendly.
Room was very spacious and included two queen beds, though I would have preferred one queen bed. Rooms are slighly dated, but this was not a big deal for us. Beds were very comfortable. Two issues with the room: Room was very, very hot (without even turning the air on). A/C function wasn't working (prob. because it was winter, but it would have been nice to have). I've never been so hot in a room. If we had stayed another night, I would have requested out of this room. The other issue with the room is that, when turned on with the remote, the TV would shut itself off seconds later. TV was also very staticky. Again, not a huge issue as we spent the bulk of our time siteseeing. 
Overall, the hotel was very nice, but wouldn't pay hotel rate for room. I paid $50 before taxes via Priceline.com and got what I paid for, which was fine. Also, checkout was very quick and had our car (which we had to valet) in just a few minutes.
 I did not use or see any of the hotels ammenities (sauna, restaurants...).

title: “Great Place to Stay to catch a flight out of LAX!”
text: I stayed here in March on my way to St Thomas, USVI. The shuttle has you go to like 4 other hotels before getting here, but on the outbound it is the last stop! Staff was very friendly and helpful. Room was as promised, clean and comfortable. FREE wifi worked great. Breakfast was ok, some pancakes and the rest of the hotel fare. Good value if staying a night to catch a flight. BONUS - Taco Bell and McDonalds next door, got beer for my room at the gas station next door. Stopped at Subway and got a $5 footlong for my flight the next day and kept in my fridge.

title: “Great Place to Stay in Venice”
text: Great place to stay in Venice. 2 minutes to the beach, very clean and comfortable rooms. The decor is very funky and very Venice. The hotel is short walk (5-10 mins) to Abbott Kinney (the main drag in Venice with lots of cute shops and restaurants). The hotel is also about a 2 mile walk to the Santa Monica Pier (very doable- just wear sneakers!). The staff was great, very easy going, but attentive. They have parking available (valet only- $28 a day) which is very nice. If you don't mind walking a few minutes away, you can park your car on the street for free, just go down Market St. or any street near Abbott Kinney and check the parking signs, it is not tough to find! The hotel roof bar is amazing, the views are literally breathtaking! Try and stop up early evening, it gets a little trendy, so dress accordingly! Overall I would wholeheartedly recommend this hotel to anyone looking to stay in the Santa Monica/Venice area.

title: “Excellent Location”
text:
I just spent three nights at the Galleria Park attending a conference at the Ritz. During those three days I did not have to take a cab one.
Galleria Park is centrally located. It is only a block away from the Montgomery BART station, which you can take to and from both SFO and OAK airports. I was able to walk to the conference every day and the hotel is within a block distance to restaurants ans shops. 
The rooms are newly remodeled, with brand new furnishings and the staff and service was just terrific.
If you're looking for all the amenities at a great price, Galleria Park is a great choice.

title: “Excellent family Hotel”
text: Excellent facilty, easy access to transport, shops , wonderful staff that go out of their way to help in anyway possible. Very clean. Excellent ***** breakfast provided. Shuttle service provided by Jeff on application. Generally fantastic place to stay.

title: “Beautiful small hotel near union square - a little bit of old England!”
text: Great location - have to get the cable up (& down) to Fishermans Wharf but that was half the fun! Near the shops. Hotel had some good recommendations for restaurants. Wine and nibbles very nice we made sure we got back early a few days to do that. Room was lovely - very OTT on the decour but again was half the fun! Staff couldn't have been more accommodating. Only areas for improvement would be the breakfast - was billed as full English - no way. Quiche and small sausages do not equal full English. That was a disappointment but on last day did have scrambled eggs. Also the bed - when we arrived there was a lovely arrangement of cushions. For the rest of our stay they were piled in the corner - that let the quality down. But, overall, lovely and would recommend. Street outside noisy but didn't bother us.

title: “Absolute perfection!”
text:
This is simply the most amazing place to stay. 
The hotel has no sign outside, so it is incredibly discreet, and a little like walking into your own house in NY. As you step into the house it gives you a good impression of what to expect during your stay - classical music, antiques and sweets for you to help yourself to when arriving or leaving (which became a tradition!). Ruth was a fantastic host - there just when you wanted her but gave the right amount of privacy. 
We stayed in the Opera suite which was on the ground floor. It is around 30 metres long, with a grand piano complete with music books and scores, a living area, a kitchen, bathroom with jacuzzi bath, bedroom and private terrace at the back. Absolute luxury!! Every need was catered for and we did not have to ask for anything additional during our stay.
The kitchen was fully stocked with breakfast items, including bagels, jams, croissants, fresh fruit and orange juice, but there was also a whole host of other items including freshly baked cake (a new one every day!), wine, bottled water, sweets... I could go on and on! 
The hotel itself is situated on a quiet street on the Upper West Side, with the subway situated one block away about a 3 minute walk. The subway is four stops away from Times Square on the local line, or one on the express line, and from Times Square you can get a connection to pretty much any line to take you anywhere you want to go. The hotel itself is also only about a 15 minute walk from Central Park - the walk is really pretty and takes you past all of the brownstone buildings in the area.
I could go on and on about how wonderful this place is for hours but needless to say it is absolutely highly recommended. We would go back in an instant.

title: “Excellent service. Stylish hotel. Thermostat needs work.”
text:
My husband and our two young children stayed at the Moorepark Hotel in August for one night after visiting the Monterey Bay Aquarium. As I was walking up to the front desk, the manager had already told me that the crib was set up in our room and they were ready for us to check-in. Top-notch and truly a dream after our night before experience at another hotel where we had to check 4-5 times for a roll-away and a crib.
The room was very clean and large enough for 4 of us to comfortably fit in it (even the bathroom!). The couch had a hide-a-bed which was perfect for our daughter to sleep on. There weren't any sheets for the hide-a-bed; no sooner had I called down when I was whisked a fresh set within 8 minutes. Truly stunning service. The pool and the hot tub were fantastic: clean, fresh towels and working furniture!
My only complaint about the Moorepark was our in-room thermostat. It never seemed to accurately register the temperature of the room when the AC was off or on and when we clicked it on, an arctic blast cooled the room down within 1 minute but it never turned off. As a result my husband and I didn't get much sleep as we were up 3-4 times a night turning it on and off. We would have opened the window but our room faced a very busy street and the hotel is located next to a major freeway. 
Aside from the temperature, everything was fantastic and the staff was great. We hope to be back again!

title: “Enjoyed Our Stay”
text: I normally stay at Tribeca but i booked this with the location in mind for my 18 year old son. We arrived at the hotel at 12.30pm after a short walk from 42nd St Port Authority Newark Airport Bus. After reading some of the reviews i wasn't hopeful that we would be able to check in at this time. The staff were really helpful and was able to check us straight in giving us a room away from the ice machine and lifts on the 20th floor. They were very informative on checking in explaining the costs of breakfasts and drinks and also gave us alternative options outside the hotel. The room was spacious and very clean, we had no traffic sound. We didnt pay for the internet option as we didnt really need it and Starbucks was just across the road which offered free access which pleased my son. The hotel has 3 Apple Macs in the lobby it was just a matter of picking the right time to use them for printing boarding passes out for our next flight. For Breakfast we used Cranberry Deli west 45th street (Between 6th & Broadway) which is approximately 15 mins walk from the hotel and just off Times Square. You can get a filling breakfast and a drink from here for around $4 and they offer something for everyone. We also had dinner a couple of doors up at perfect pint Irish bar which offered good food and was good value. There is a DuaneReade drugs store below the hotel where we purchased beer/drinks rather than pay the hotel prices. All in all we had a good stay, liked the location and would stay again.

title: “My stay was excellent”
text: I absolutely loved the Paramount Hotel. The staff was exceptionally friendly and the service prompt. The hotel is beautiful and the room is comfortable. The location was absolutely perfect. .

title: “Need recent reviewing”
text: I have stayed in the Da Vinci many times over the past five years. I am hesitant to do so now because of postings regarding bedbugs. Has anyone who stayed there recently encountered this problem at the Da Vinci? I always found the hotel itself adequate at best, but the location is great. Can anyone who has stayed there recently enlighten me on the bedbug situation at the Da Vinci?

title: “Too big and too noisy”
text: I stayed at he Sheraton,53rd Streer recently for a business trip. The hotel is in a good location in midtown Manhattan, surrounded by restaurants and other hotels.The hotel was exteremly crowded, there were wall to wall people in the lobby and getting to the check in desk was difficult. I was on line for over 20 minutes (4th on line) due to the fact that the hotel had one person working the front desk. There were two other hotel staff just standing at the desk but did not assist any of the guests in front of me. This struck me as odd since it was 3PM which is the hotels check in time. My room was clean and I found the staff to be friendly when I had to speak with them. I did not spend any tme at the hotel due to the fact that there were a constant stream of people in and out of the hotel. The hotel bar is small and crowded.This would not be my first choice for a hotel in Manhattan. The hotel is overpriced and too crowed to enjoy any of the amenities that the hotel may offer. There are better alternatives in the city.

title: “Another great stay at the Hyatt”
text: My family and I have been staying at the Hyatt for 2 years now when we travel to Chicago and will not stay at any other hotel. We are always greeted with a smile and a welcome back. We are Hyatt Gold Passport members and use the Passport desk for checking in and for any questions we have during our stay. The desk staff is top notch and always ready to help. The concierge desk is right near the front desk and is well staffed and helpfull. We usually have a Jr Suite and enjoy having the extra room and being able to watch traffic on the river. The location is just right to reach the shopping on Michigan Ave and close enough to the Art Institute and Grant park so that we can walk instead of taking cabs. The Big bar is a fun place to have a drink and yes you need to get the "BIG" glass one time. Overall we are always pleased with our stay and remembe to friend them on FB so that you can get the word of the week and get discounts on parking.

title: “Mediocre customer service, great location”
text:
The hotel is in a fantastic location in Boston, at the South West cornert of Boston Commons, and walking distance to Chinatown and even places like Fenway Park. Boston's a small city, so walking almost anywhere is possible.
The building also houses a couple of restaurants. We tried Finale, which is an incredible dessert place. At first, the prices seemed a little high for dessert, but they were worth every cent. I wanted to go back every night.
Apart from that, the hotel was a bit of a disappointment. We had problems with check-in, parking, room service and the lobby restaurant. At check-in, they said no rooms despite a reservation, and the manager had to be called. With parking, no valets were available, so we had to find a garage on our own near the hotel. For room service, they forgot a few items and delivered well past the promised time, and the lobby restaurant service was bad - a lack of waiters, and drinks took half an hour to arrive.
The room was small and very subdued looking. Very clean and tidy, though. I've seen better furnishings in comfort inns. The in-room internet service didn't work and we were still charged for it. The view was into other people's hotel rooms, a few feet away.

title: “great for the money”
text:
My son and I stayed at the Chinatown hotel for 3 nites recently-he's still in college and wanted to go to Chicago to do some sightseeing. My wife did not go-only he and I went. I don't need 5 star hotels myself and neither did my son. We have gone to other cities over the past 5 years. We spend little time in the room except to sleep and take a shower. We cover a lot of territory and see as many tourist attractions as possible.
Chinatown hotel is basic, clean and has an excellent location for the money. It's only two blocks to the tram ($5 for an all day pass is great). We try to cover the most distance and see all we can in a short time period. It was great for our purpose. The staff was very nice (all spoke english except one older gentleman). Our room was very clean and the bathroom was quite large. We did not see any bugs while we were there. Although there was no elevator, climbing to the second floor was no problem for us. Parking is available two blocks away if needed. Although we had a rental car, we found a parking space on the street in front of the hotel every nite.
I love Chinese food and so does he. There are many fine restaurants very near. We ate at a different one each nite. They gave so much food, we just ordered one plate with an extra order of rice. That was plenty for both of us. The prices were very reasonable for dinner.
Each afternoon or early evening when we returned to our room, the bed was made, bathroom was cleaned up, and everything straightened up very nicely. 
In summary I found the hotel great for our needs. No, it's not a four or five star hotel. But it was clean, very cheap and had a great location and we really liked it for the money. I would certainly go back in the future if I needed to go to Chicago.
If anyone has any questions, I would be glad to answer them by email if you want.

title: “over priced”
text:
We've stayed at 2 Embassy Suites in 2 different cities. I think both have been over-priced for the level of quality.
The location of this hotel is excellent and very convenient for tourists and business travelers.
The complimentary breakfast was simply satisfactory. The free cocktail hour was nice. However, neither are enough to make up for the over-priced rates. There are nicer hotels available in Embassy's price range.
One thing I've noticed at both Embassy Suites is that their electronic door locks are complete pieces of s. We've had tons of trouble with them at both Embassy Suite Hotels that we visited. We've never had any such trouble at any other hotel ever. It's a bit frustrating to have to put your key in 10-20 times just to get your door to open, every time you come or go...
Probably won't stay at Embassy Suites ever again.

title: “Wonderful Unit, Close Proximity to Airport”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Legacy for two nights in a one-bedroom, upstairs corner unit which overlooked the golf course. After reading the reviews I requested an upstairs unit, quiet location, nice view. I was very pleased and surprised when my requests were met. The furnishings are very nice, the unit was spotlessly clean, and the view from our balcony was lovely. The people at the front desk were pleasant and efficient. I particularly liked the gym which afforded a pleasant view of the golf course. We got take-out food from the restaurant there which was reasonably priced and tasty enough. The swimming pool looked to be nice too, but we're not swimmers, so we never ventured into it. Now, that first night we hardly slept. We kept hearing what sounded like the front door opening and footsteps coming down the hall. I was a bit scared, and even got up to investigate more than once. Big brave me. If I had been staying on my own, I'd have called the front desk to enquire what was going on. By the way, we heard the same noises during the day, in addition to other odd noises. We never did figure out what the noises were, and in the end, surmised that perhaps the place is haunted?! Or, it could be the building settling? However, all in all, we'd stay at the Legacy again. Its close proximity to the airport is an added attraction.

title: “Personal get-away”
text: Fantastic Place! Staff was extremely friendly and helpful, Rooms were clean and quiet. We stayed here 2 nights on the front and back of our trip as we flew into the Phoenix airport, then moved on to Vegas and Tucson. Would definitely stay here again. The free evening kick-back and morning breakfast were very good also.

title: “The worst in NYC”
text:
incredibly small narrow rooms; noisy, stunning air conditioning ( - impossibile to sleep if on); no chairs, No hangers; internet for 10 dollars a day! Small bottle of water (no complimentary) 5 dollars; no bar in the room; french size bed (that means no space if you are two !!) black an white kitsch furniture (just two "design" boxes not useful) . The bathroom is not a room but a loculus: 1x1 square meter, no window, no hanger, you can sit on the wc and have shower at the same time...
What else? Even the address is fake: the Gramercy Park is far away form this hotel.....

title: “Hotel penn”
text: Its a standerd hotel with a great location, in the middle of every thing. We were a bit dissapointed because when we got out of the lift the carpet was old & then we got to our room & it was clean, carpet & furniture was old. seeing what the lobby looked like lovly & posh u get upstairs & see what its like a bit dissapointing. thay cleaned our room every day towls changed, bed made & staff were very friendly. You cant really complain for the price & the location, its just a room for sleeping as long as its clean.

title: “Won't stay here again.”
text: The staff was pleasant enough. They advertise 'deluxe' breakfast.- it was in no way deluxe. Situated next door to strip club, didn't feel very safe. Room was just ok. Unless you can sleep like a rock, you won't want to stay here. Airplanes were flying directly overhead all night- very loud. If you can sleep through that, this hotel would be ok for one night of sleep. I wouldn't stay here again.

title: “Close to all shopping, and Powell/Hyde cable car line”
text:
Hotel Nikko is convenient to the shopping mecca of Union Square, including Barney's, Macy's, Juicy, Neiman's to name a few. 
Waking is safe with the occasional person approaching you for handouts. 
There is a full Starbucks in the street level as well as Enterprise rental car. Caution if you prefer to return car at airport, there is a$175 up charge which they negotiated down to $75 for corporate customer. The hotel has a nice gym with weights, treadmills, stair masters, pool , sauna, separate locker rooms for men & women. Added bonus is the dry and steam saunas inside each locker room, with showers, digital programmable lockers, with plenty of towels and shower products. Shiatsu massage is available in appt but $125 an hour seemed high. Food order in room service was fast, okay quality, but they automatucally charge a 19% service charge, plus $3.75 for each order. The sushi restaurant in the lobby was mimimal selection but what they had was fresh.

title: “Fabulous Trip”
text: Rooms were clean and nice. The beds were VERY comfortable. Really liked having a kitchen available. The staff was extremely helpful. The hotel was in a great location - within walking distance, short cab ride, or subway station of whereever we wanted to go. Would definitely recommend!

title: “Would stay again”
text: The room was clean - beds are small only doubles. Air conditioner very loud but it worked to keep room comfortable and ventilated. The bathroom was clean and fully stocked. Remote did not work for TV, but we are perfectly capable of getting up and walking to TV, and some channels did not have volume. The staff at front desk that I encountered was WONDERFUL... the staff in the free breakfast area, except for Sunday ,was not very polite and when you asked for items that should have been out they were rude and seemed to try to avoid getting it for you, they actually would walk away remove dishes from a table (which they never wiped off any table just removed used dishes) and sometimes I had to actually ask several times. I am sure many people waste food as I saw happening, but this ruined this experience for the rest of us who just really wanted a yogurt... I would stay here again as the location was good for uptown and downtown ventures.

title: “Extremely Satisfied”
text:
I just had to write about how great this hotel is! Having read a couple negative comments, I have no idea at what hotel they stayed because it's not where I am.
Chose the hotel because it's close to the courthouse where I am doing business. Recently stayed at Ritz Carlton, pentagon city. Loved that hotel, but not conducive to business stay on a budget. ES has coffee makers, cooked brkfst & great rooms.
Check in a breeze. Room too hot. A/C not very effective. Engineer shows ASAP & he is unsatisifed, so HE takes care of getting moved a few rooms down. (I like it cold in my room) New room is as promised, nice & cold :)
I don't know what the poster is talking about as far as the breakfast or the manager's reception. The breakfast is great. There's an "express" where there's only a few things you cannot get. The 'cooked to order" area is ample & quick.
Manager's reception, *plenty of room* both upstairs & down, quick line & no complaints about multiple orders. This, during a Painters Union Convention! 
The rooms are huge -- what I love about all ES, or maybe I've spent too much time in Europe.
Decor, pleasing, great amenities -- Bath & Body Works toiletries, *five* pillows on King bed - unusual.
They do have strangely place vents in the bedroom area which allows noise from next room in -- could hear kids laughing & TV -- but earplugs I religiously travel with came in handy. 
No noise from room above. Hate you can hear doors slamming, but this too, at the Ritz. BUT with ES, you're asleep a room away if you close the bedroom door. Must be some hotel thing to make sure doors shut.
Oh, and disappointed no weight equipment in fitness center BUT LOVE 24 hour access. Ritz opened at 5:30. Huh? who can workout & get to business matters that late?
A 3 block walk to Chinatown/Penn Quarter, lots of restaurants, Metro stop. Up 10th street is Ford Theater & gorgeous St. Pat's. very good spot & I felt very safe, even walking alone as a woman when it was dark, albeit only 9:00 p.m.

title: “BED BUGS!”
text:
We stayed one night in room 307 and upon arriving we inspected the room and mattress thouroughly but didnt see anything. The next morning I woke up and felt something in the bed. When I flipped up the sheets I discovered a bug. I immediately placed it under a glass on the counter and called management. When I told them I had saved it, the disregard made it evident that they knew there was a problem and decided to put me and my family at risk anyway.
Apologies and comping a room will not help me if my house becomes infested and I have to spend thousands of dollars and a countless amount of time to exterminate them. I have stayed in Homewood Suites before and LOVED it. This hotel was no comparison to the others I have stayed at.

title: “Nightmare”
text:
Our travel agent booked us here in 2005 for an overnight on the way to Cancun. The hot tub was not working, the hallway smelled musty, the tv was fuzzy and there were dirty clothes in the bathroom. The breakfast was dismal--fruit loops and watery juice and not much more. Upon our return from Mexico, the hot tub was still out of order but at least the tv worked.
A year later, while vacationing in the Bahamas, our agent booked us there again. At the time, our memories had faded and we figured it couldn't be so bad the second time around. We were wrong. It was worse, much worse.
Upon check in, we were informed that "our travel agent" had not booked us with the "park and fly" feature--not true--and we were not allowed to park our car at the hotel. Instead my husband was instructed to take it to a lot 4 miles away, then had to hitchike back as there was no shuttle. The front desk was very indifferent to this. Again, the hot tub was not working, again, the hallway had a bad odor, there were wet towels in the room and the tv didn't work. The breakfast was terrible, the spoons and forks were cheap plastic and broke easily and the food was lousy.
Upon our return 7 days later the hot tub was still not working. My husband asked the shuttle driver if he could drop him off at the parking lot and he refused to do so. Another guest overheard his plight and gave him a ride. 
We were traveling with my parents and had connecting rooms. My youngest daughter who was 5 at the time has Autism and has a tendancy to wander. We had chained to door to the room she was in to contain her but had the door between the rooms propped open with a trash can. Somehow in the confusion of unpacking she managed to lock herself in the room with both of our keys inside. We figured it was no big deal, that the front desk would have a key for the connecting rooms, but they were unable to find one. The girl at the desk actually told me if I hadn't been so stupid it would have never happened. She did call in the owner who showed up an hour later to inform me that the maintenance man came to work in two hours and he had the key. At that point I told her I was calling a locksmith, the police, the fire department ANYBODY but that I would have that door opened. I asked her what would they do if they had a suicidal guest or a hostage situation and she said "It's never happened." She called the maintenance man to ask him to come in early and he informed her the key was hanging in the office in plain sight. She finally didi get the door opened and my daughter was laying there fast asleep.
She never offered an apology of any kind and calls to customer service were futile. I will NEVER stay there again and have told everyone I know about this experience

title: “What a Gem of an Inn!”
text:
Having read many of the previous reviews about the Inn, I reserved a room there when I recently stayed in Baltimore and can agree with almost all of the previous reviews. The room was spotlessly clean, the decor was very plush and inviting and the staff were outstanding, particularly Kelly, who was unfailingly cheerful and helpful.
The breakfast buffet wasn't quite as large as I had expected and the lack of a dining room caught me by surprise, but the foyer has enough chairs and tables to cope with the guests that don't want to eat in their rooms. The buffet itself was, however, more than adequate and enabled me to eat a good healthy breakfast each morning - probably doing me some good over what I might have eaten had a more extensive cooked buffet been available!
My only negative observation was that I had not realised before checking in that the Inn rooms were all on the ground floor, with residences on the upper floors. This meant that I had a room with windows next to the front door and looking out at the marina. Whilst this was a nice view, I felt a little uncomfortable that people could look into my room whilst walking past on the pavement and therefore kept my shutters closed whenever I was in the room. Fell St is quiet enough that I didn't feel unsafe at any time, but I would probably try to book a courtyard view room in future.
Overall I had an extremely enjoyable stay and wouldn't hesitate to book there again if I was back in Baltimore. I would also recommend it to anyone who wants to stay somewhere with a bit more character than the normal bland hotel chains.

title: “A Hidden" Gem”
text:
I have stayed at other hotels in Times Square over the years,but this one is the best!
The suites are spacious and clean, the hotel is in a fabulous location, and the staff has always been welcoming and professional. Security is great. (You'll need to show your room key to get beyond the street level lobby.) You can easily walk to theaters, restaurants, Fifth Avenue, Rockefeller Center.
This hotel does not have the curb appeal of some nearby hotels, but the size of the suites and the wonderful amenities more than make up for any negative first impression made from the street.
The only hesitation I have in recommending this hotel is that it will become more popular and it will be tougher to get reservations!

title: “Not worth it.”
text: We have stayed at tis hotel twice. The first time we were on th back side of the hotel and everthin seemed fine. We stayed may 2012 for our second trip and it was horrible. There were roaches, carpet turned feet/socks black, bathrom was not cleaned upon arrival. Our first night was not bad, we did notice alot of traffic in and out. The second night the hotel rep on duty was kicking hookers (yes hookers) out of the hotel. As we walked to the car we were approached by a man who was from the Econo lodge in the same parking lot. It turns out he was the pimp of thehookers and was tryingto get my husband to go use them! He them asked alot of questions like if we were going out for the night, what kind of radio was in our car etc. We did not feel safe. Will not stay here again even if price is lower.

title: “Ideal Location”
text:
Stopped here for 3 nights whilst touring West Coast and found the hotel to be ideally placed for the majority of attractions.
 This hotel is a 2 minute walk to the sea front where there are lots of places to eat, the cable car stop is about 5 minute walk to take you into the city centre. The hotel was very clean and tidy with tea and coffee making facilities. There is a 24 hour eating place near the main door where you can get a decent breakfast.
Would definately use the place again if we ever visit San Fransisco again.

title: “Charm, comfort, location, easy on the budget”
text: Four of us stayed here between Dec 24 and 29th, two in a "triple", two in a "double" room. The triple had 2 beds, one a queen, the other a twin. Both had sinks. The double room had a double bed, so if you are two people used to a king or queen sized bed, you might find it small. But the beds were very comfortable, the rooms quiet (we were on the 8th floor in the B wing), with nice views. True, the wallpaper looks tired, the radiator knocks and pings a bit, the one elevator is tiny and slow, the lobby at bit dark, the rooms smallish - but this bothered us not one bit. The bathrooms are extremely clean and sharing them was no problem. Check in was prompt and friendly and the one issue we had with the TV was looked after right away. There's an ice machine on the 1st floor, but no restaurant, bar or even food machines. Plenty of stores and restaurants within a block though. Great location.

title: “Great Value, Great Location, Great Price”
text: this hotel was great! it is in a great location, directly across from a large grocery store. it has a large pool, and parking (free), also free wifi service. while the staff may not be overly friendly, they certainly are ok, they did whatever was asked of them, and answered any questions that we had, i was a little leery about the possibility of there being bugs (judging from other reviews), but I am happy to report that there was NOT 1 single bug seen in my room, and i was looking (just in case). for less than $100 a night, this hotel is exactly what one should expect at this price, it was a great deal, and good experience, luckily my room was in the back so the noise of sunset was not a problem, i did however hear people coming and going late, but it was not overly noisy. I WOULD RECOMMEND THIS HOTEL HIGHLY if you want a basic, comfortable, clean place to say.

title: “A little quirky, but great fun and great value”
text:
This hotel was apparently quite the spot in its day....but that day was a while ago. It's not, however, without its charms. It's a touch threadbare here and there - but for the money, I thought it was great. The rooms are fine - plain but pleasant - mine was as clean as a whistle - the bed was plenty comfy and the bathroom was nice and clean. The sliding door to the balcony was a little old and beat up...but this ain't the Ritz.
 It wasn't swimming weather for me so I didn't experience the pool but it looked lovely. I did experience the Patio Cafe and absolutely loved it. I have no idea if the food is any good because I only had toast and coffee - but the feel of the place is wonderful....all warm and cozy. Some hotel cafes feel good, most don't - this one felt fantastic.....the people working the cafe seem genuinely friendly and it feels real nice just being there.
The lobby is pretty funky and pretty famous (I think)....with it's northern ski lodge (?) motif...the round fireplace, white banquettes and plaid carpet....you can feel the days when the movie people from the nearby studios hung out there....it's definitely in the air....
 .....and the crowd at the hotel was perfect....very LA....from the young and painfully hip Asian rockers to the older folks with long gray hair and strange hats to the gorgeous young woman across the hall with legs that make grown men cry....and the cute families on their way to Universal Studios just down the road.....the guests seemed to perfectly fit the somewhat offbeat charm of the place.
The location is great too....up or down Ventura Blvd is just about anything you might need...and it's a quick shot over the hills into town.
This is clearly not a place for people who want upscale and elegant.....it's a place for people who will enjoy a one-of-a-kind hotel full of charm and character....and don't mind that the elevator might be showing a touch of wear. And, at the rate I paid, it was an incredible deal.

title: “Exceeded our expecations”
text: We booked a room at the Hilton recently on a trip to visit family in the area. We didn't expect much from it but were really impressed with the hotel when we arrived- it far exceeded our expectations. I travel very frequently for work and rarely have my expectations for a hotel met, much less feel as feel as impressed as I did on our stay at the Hilton. The staff was great, the hotel itself was beautiful and we will be staying there on all future trips to the Memphis area.

title: “Uniquely Fairmont”
text:
Not the nicest Fairmont you'll encounter, but a comfortable retreat in a great location, with awesome views. I'm not a big fan of the "contemporary-modern-meets-Austin-Powers" lobby thing they have going on, but that's just me. Many reviewers here seem to like it just fine, so take my monkey chatter for what it's worth.
The location is hard to beat and in a city the size of Chi-Town, location matters. It's right next to Millennium Park, The Miracle Mile and The Navy Pier, so you can't get much more central than that. It's worth it to get an elevated floor if views matter to you - the views are stunning in every direction. As in many hotels in major cities, day rates for valet is not cheap and the Fairmont is no exception - $50 per day, self-parking is less. 
The rooms, while not in the most elegant Fairmont tradition are very comfortable, but the usual Fairmont amenities apply - Robe, slippers, safe, iPad in the breakfast dining room for reading the paper ...

title: “My second home. Staff is like family!”
text:
Unexpected stay. We were in Charlotte for the Coca Cola 600 but never made it. My wife had to have emergency surgery. The staff here helped me with a room for the week. They even upgraded the room to the Hhonors level which was amazing. The staff treated me and my two small children like family making an unexpected stay feel like we had never left our home. They are truly amazing so helpful. They ask each day how my wife is doing and if I need anything for her. They have gone as far as to give me additional toiletries to bring to her to make her hospital stay more comfortable. Special thanks to the following staff members,
Thomas
Lexsa 
Elena
Kim
Carlos
Fanny
Krysta
Mr. Afriyie 
Kaitlyn
Marretta

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
This is a very nice hotel with great service. I stayed here with my family for a weekend getaway. Every staff member we encountered was friendly and helpful. They were very customer service oriented. 
We had a room with a view of the Water Tower and Lake Michigan. Terrific view. The room was clean and comfortable. The bathroom was large and the separate walk-in shower was a nice feature.
The gym/workout room was as good as any I've seen in a hotel. It also included free weights which I rarely encounter in hotels. The pool was large and kept at a comfortable temperature. The steam room was also nice.
The location of the hotel can't be beat. It is at the far north end of Michigan Ave. close to Water Tower. It is convenient to shopping and lots of great restaurants.
Finally, my family loved the hot chocolate in the lobby on a cold January day. A nice touch.
I would not hesitate to stay at this hotel again.

title: “Excellent stay but beware of the bed”
text: We stayed here for a few nights and had a terrific time. The staff is outstanding - friendly, quick and efficient. They allowed us to store our bags before we were able to check in and provided us with a room with a gorgeous bathroom and well furnished room. The concierge was helpful and a request to the front desk for more pillows was fulfilled within two minutes. The only two downsides are that parking is exceptionally expensive ($48 a day) and the beds are not very comfortable, particularly for this kind of otherwise great hotel. We were planning on parking in one of the cheaper lots near the hotel but when we arrived we found out that they're all closed on the weekend were left with no other option. (The bellhop told us that other hotels nearby charge even more and that they were "reasonable".) The other disappointment was the uncomfortable bed - you literally feel and hear the springs moving underneath you (and I'm not even overweight!). Otherwise it was a great stay. I'd strongly suggest joining their membership program for free beverages each morning along with complimentary water when you arrive. Also, in the lobby upon arrival, were the largest lillies I'd ever seen and refreshing tea and fruit.

title: “Good value”
text: I paid less than $70 per night and was expecting the worst. I was quite surprised with the Howard Johnson. Clean, quite pleasant and helpful front desk. The conditions of the could be better maintained, but everything was clean and worked perfectly (from air conditioning to how water). My bedroom was actually big.

title: “My aching back”
text:
The Sheraton sweet sleeper is anything but! My back is aching. My wife's back is aching! My 14 year olds back is aching! The hotel is clean. The majority of the staff is friendly but the service is lacking! It started at check-in. I was fourth in line to check in (in the standard line). There were three employees at the desk at first taking care of the regular line. There were two employees taking care of the VIP high SPG POINT member line. As I approached the front of my line (10 minutes later) a third line started with the regular airline customer line..This is when one of the employees walked away from the standard line to take care of the airline employees. Now there are two employees assisting the standard line. I make it to the front of my line (10 people behind me and line is growing) and one of the employees assisting my line who just finished helping the man that was In front of me sees a friend in the VIP lane (just a hunch since the employee ran over and they started hugging each other). The VIP LINE must have been getting too long (3people) so another employee came out to help that line and the hugging employee decided to leave the care of my line from now take care of her friends accommodations personally. The way he was smiling at the end he must have gotten one heck of an upgrade from his friend. He walks away very happy and as I walk towards her she quickly turns and disappears in the back, must have been break time! I wait another ten minutes at least when another employee appears out of another door and YES, I finally checked in. I glanced at the line and I couldn't see the end of the standard line. 
The beds are horrible! The wait for an elevator could take anywhere from 5 to 10 minutes. People would be so tired of waiting they wouldn't wait for people to exit elevator to get on. They would push their way on making an already full elevator dangerously full. My wife and daughter were stuck in the back of the elevator when this happened one time. Thank god one of the security men finally stepped in to end a pushing war between people trying to get out and people trying to get on.
I usually stay at a different hotel chain but thought I would try Sheraton. Never again!!!!

title: “Loved the Hyatt”
text:
Based on reviews on tis site, we stayed at the Hyatt 11/30-12/2. It is a great property in downtown Seattle. Barney's, Nordstrom's and lots of other shopping is within two blocks. It is a short walk to Pike Market.
The staff was incredible. When we got back to the hotel Saturday afternoon, the room still wasn't made up. We called downstairs and let housekeeping know we were going to the gym, and needed the room made up right away. No problem! 
Our requests for ice, towels, etc were handled promptly and courteously.
We had a corner room, which was big. However, I'm not sure I'd book another room like this, since you have to keep the curtains closed to block out light from the street (not to mention for privacy).
My husband and I both worked out at the gym. They have everything you can imagine there -- freeweights, weight machines, ellipticals, bikes, treadmills, etc. They even have exercise balls and body bars. They had more equipment in the gym than any other hotel I've stayed at, including a Four Seasons.
We will definitely stay at the Hyatt again the next time we're in Seattle.

title: “Nice Hotel, ok location”
text: This hotel is steps from the Powell Street (@ Market) Muni stop so it is convenient. The surrounding neighborhood varies between ritzy and dodgy. The hotel itself is nice, boutiquish, but I could see how anyone could easily get in. Having siad that I did feel safe. The hotel actually has rooms for one! With single twin beds. In small rooms. But for me it was just enough. There was a small fridge, that was somewhat stocked but left enough room for my things. The bed was comfortable. There was a large closet and nice bathroom. I had two rooms here. The first was on the 2nd floor (room 217) and the window opened onto a landing shared by other rooms. It was also across from the ice machine so the staff gladly changed it for me. My second room was on the top floor (510) and had an inside courtyard window and felt more spacious because of the design. Most of the staff are very friendly and great. The breakfast is on the 5th floor and is "grab and Go" so there's nowhere to eat except your room. They had a nice selection of danish that was in stock until the breakfast hours finished (7-9am). The neighborhood leaves a LOT to be desired if you walk two blocks in the wrong direction. I would stay here again.

title: “A very good hotel in the heart of Manhattan”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for a week, and we had everything we need.
It is noy so luxury, but clean, and the staff was friendly.
Ther is free internet only in the lobby. 
Our room had no good view, but we were all day out, so doesnt matter !!
Breakfast is excellent and the price for the room very good.
I will definitelly be back !!

title: “Excellent stay and great location.”
text: My wife and I had a wonderful time in Seattle and chose the Edgewater for its location on the water and its proximity to downtown and Pike Place Market. We weren't disappointed. We read all the bad reviews prior to booking and just wanted to experience it for ourselves. I'm not quite sure what the bad reviews were all about as the whole staff from the valet to the front desk attendants to the wait staff to the maids were all very courteous and greeted you upon arrival and throughout our stay. We did have a partial waterfront view room and was great, very cozy and the fireplace kept the room nice and warm. The next time I am in Seattle, I would stay here again, can't wait unitl our next trip.

title: “Good hotel, good value, great location.”
text: Just got back from a weekend in Seattle at the Warwick. Took the grayline airport shuttle and it dropped us off right in front of the hotel. Also picked us up for our return to seatac. Our room had an incredible view of the city skyline, was a fairly good size, with a nice size closet and plenty of drawers for your clothes. Also had a good size desk to work, but the wireless internet was not free and the signal was very weak. The location of this hotel is very convenient, within walking distance of nearly all the sites; pioneer, safeco, and qwest being exceptions. Ralph's grocery across the street was a great added feature, as was dahlia's bakery. It looked like the hotel was on the edge of a transitioning neighborhood, but we never felt unsafe. Walking north of the hotel after dark made me a little uncomfortable, but walking south towards the main shopping district was great with plenty of others out walking. This hotel seemed more European than American. Overall, a great experience. I can definitely recommend the Warwick when travelling to Seattle.

title: “Average”
text: Very average property. Nothing special. Great location. Dated, so dated. The Club floor - only the name. So on)

title: “Close to Darrel Royal Stadium: Avoid the Drive”
text:
We chose this motel because of price, location and availability. We prepaid for two nights and showed up very late to check in. Check in was quite painless and the staff member was pleasant. Free WiFi. Room 101 was our spot, right below the roaring partiers from Texas Tech. The fact that we could not hear them in our room says a lot about the structure of the motel. It must be made of real concrete. This motel is located about 50 feet from Interstate 35. We couldn't hear that either. So, pick room 101 if you stay here. The room itself was a good size with pretty beat up furniture, victims of too many football fans. However, it was clean, neat and the bathroom was much cleaner than I was expecting. The king bed was actually comfortable and there were five adequate pillows. Towels are really really small, but clean and did absorb water. AC worked well. No bugs seen. Minimal mildew. Did not make it to the free breakfast. Coffee maker was missing a lid, so it was a no go. Fortunately, the Star Seeds cafe is literally 30 feet from room 101. We got a beer there and some breakfast. 
Best reasons to stay here for a UT game: 1) free parking 2) walk to stadium in about 15 minutes 3) avoid that annoyance of having to drive in the Austin traffic which just stinks on a good day and more than stinks on a game day 4) while everyone is sitting in their cars trying to go somewhere you can be back at the Days Inn drinking a cold one from your in-room refrigerator 5) you can freshen up and head back out once the traffic clears. Win win. 
Tip: bring ear plugs. 
Challenge: Dare you to swim in the pool. It was clean but it is right on the street and smaller than a lot of hot tubs. It is just odd.

title: “Convenient and overall great value”
text:
We used this hotel as a base for our girlfriends' weekend trip to SF and Napa. 
The location was great and was down the street from the Westfield Mall. There were a variety of stores around the area which was a big hit during a girls trip. There were also plenty of restaurants nearby including a Buca di Beppo across the street. It was within a few blocks from the Powell BART station and the Powell and Market street cable cars. 
The rooms were pretty spacious and beautifully decorated and were very clean. We all slept comfortably on the beds. We thought we had 2 queen beds during reservation but it turned out to be double beds. The bathroom had a sliding glass door with no lock. There was no bathtub but a pretty spacious shower. There was plenty of storage in the room and bathroom considering there were four ladies staying inside with a lot of accessories. 
Service was absolutely wonderful from the concierge staff who helped us out with free tastings in Napa to recommending places to eat around the neighborhood. The front desk were all courteous and helpful accomodating us by placing our other friends across the room from us. The bellmen always greeted us with smiles and were more than willing to help us out. We would absolutely stay here again for its convenient location and great overall value.

title: “Beautiful, elegant hotel.”
text: This elegant hotel is in a very good area. It is an easy walk to Buckingham Fountain, the Riverwalk area, and Michigan Avenue shopping. And there is a Starbucks in the lobby of the hotel. It appeared as though most of the guests got the package we had which included the Breakfast Buffet. Be warned - a long line may be experienced to get a table for the buffet. Also, you can order fresh omelets. Our first morning the waiter did not tell us this but the 2nd morning we had a great waiter and he said we could order omelets or waffles with the Breakfast Buffet.

title: “luxury”
text:
my wife and i stayed here in june for 5 days as part of trails of tennesee tour, and it was brilliant the hotel is fabulous the staff are very friendly and it is ideally situated,you can jump on a trolley for $1 and go to beale st, which was only 3 stops,then the tour bus would collect us from the hotel to take us to gracelands etc,so if you ever have the choice of hotels of which to stay i would definitely recommend then marriott!!
 fabulous!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “No towel racks in the bathroom”
text: I hope the Marriott people read this and address the problem because it is an easy and inexpensive fix. Our room had a bathroom with one small (maybe 18 inch) towel rack inside the glassed in shower stall. No towel racks in the bathroom proper. And when we took showers in the afternoon the rack wasn't big enough to spread out even one of our towels. And because it was enclosed in a damp space, the towel didn't dry by morning anyway. There is one hook on the back of the door that we used for our robes, but the only place for the towels was to hang them over the shower and they were never completely dry in the AM. There was plenty of wall space where towel racks would easily fit. It seems a really stupid oversight but we would not book there again. If it sounds petty, I'm sorry but when you wake in the morning, you need to take a shower and have a dry towel to use.

title: “Excellent hotel in downtown houston”
text: I stayed for 10 nights in early October for business reason (which is very stressful). The hotel makes me feel good and relax after long working days. The room is well appointed and clean. The two complimentary drinks during the happy hours (5-7 pm) at the Magnolia club (2nd level) did help me wind-down. Free cookies and milk during 9-10 pm also help your bedtime more pleasant especially for traveller far away from home like me. They also serve free basic breakfast on the 2nd level in the morning. A very short walk from the Houston Astro's baseball stadium and some nice restaurants. In short, I recommend this hotel for your down-town stay in Houston.

title: “Beautiful view of the Harbor”
text: Four days with an awesome view of the Harbor including night time fireworks shows from Seaworld which were visible from my room and the top floor lounge. I was in one of the rooms they said they hadn't renovated and it neat and clean with beds in good condition so no issues. The renovated ones are nice but lower floors. Great location for Old Town and loved the restaurants are truly trying innovation on their menus. Only issue with the entire stay was slow internet speeds so bring your own if you can.

title: “perfect”
text: Great central location within easy walk of Fifth Avenue for shops and Central Station for the metro. Plenty of good, reasonable restaruants within walking distance. Staff very helpful and friendly - informal atmosphere and like a home-from-home with tea and coffee available in the reading room 24/7. Rooms full of nice touches like iPod/radio player, slippers etc. Would certainly stay there again and the best hotel I have stayed at in NY, having been there 7 times.

title: “An excellent hotel and good value”
text: I stayed here for the first time in June; I picked the hotel for its proximity to my business meetings. It was just what I wanted: quiet, comfortable and close to my meetings in NW Washington. It has a wonderful, free coffee service in the lobby. I couldn't pass up the opportunity for a coffee every time I passed. I tried the Nage restaurant in the lobby three times; it didn't open before 7 am so I walked across the street to the next hotel one morning, but on two mornings I had time to eat in the restaurant. The breakfast food was excellent quality; but service was slow one of my two mornings. The guest rooms were well lit, comfortable and clean. The staff was very pleasant. I used the business center only once, to print a boarding pass; it had two work stations there and another in the lobby. Overall, this was a great value. I loved that coffee service. Thanks.

title: “Amazing location...”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights. The location is awesome, literally a 2 minute walk to Times Square. It's a safe place to stay at (we are two females). The hotel is gorgeous, the decor and vibe is great. Free wifi was a great touch as well. The rooms were really quite hot, which considering it was freezing outside was a bit strange, so we used the fan a lot, only downside of that was that the fan was SO loud. But we managed with it. The ensuite was great, had everything you needed and extra toiletries etc. 
There was a safe in the room which was really great to keep everything protected. Our room only got serviced once, not sure why this is, but we were not too bothered. 
Only downside was the size of the bed. When I booked it said a full size bed, but it was nowhere near big enough for two adults, so beware of this when booking and if you can opt for a bigger sized bed if available - we managed though as it was just a base for our NYC adventures so we were often so tired we just slept through.

title: “loved it.”
text: This was my first time in New York and we were finding it really hard to find an affordable hotel that was close to Times Square. We stayed in the POD for 5 days and loved it. The rooms are small but you have everything you need in it and they're very clean. All the staff were very helpful and friendly and check in and out was quick. It's only about a ten minute walk to Times Square and I felt perfectly comfortable walking back to the hotel at night. The area seems to be mainly residential with a few smaller businesses along the street. We had a bathroom in our room but we saw the shared bathrooms and they were really clean too. Hope to visit New York again and would definetley stay here.

title: “Great value, but...”
text: Nice room, new furniture, good breakfast. The location is also great for exploring the financial district, Battery Park, South Street Seaport and historic Stone Street. The only real downside is the extreemly slow elevator service. There just aren't enough elevators for the number of floors, so you might be waiting a while to get up or down at busy times of the day or night. Otherwise, we were very happy with the hotel. Great, quick service too.

title: “Large, clean rooms. Modern Finishings”
text:
Stayed 3 nights for a conference at the hotel. Very clean. Rooms were well appointed, quiet and comfortable. There is a digital combo safe in the room to secure your valuables.
My room was on a lower floor, offering a city view, lots of concrete, but still felt open and airy with the huge floor to ceiling windows.
The fitness centre is above average compared to similar hotels. Plenty of treadmills, but could use some extra stationary bikes. Each piece of equipment has its own TV. A good mix of weight machines a solid road workout session to shake off all the conference sitting.
Hotel is very centrally located in the central business district. Not much going on in the immediate area, but it is just a short trip to most of the attractions and night life.
Self-parking was convenient.

title: “hotel in good location”
text:
The motel is located in a good location. We arrived in San Diego via Amtrak and walked for around twenty minutes before reaching. It's near the seaport area (where the USS midway aircraft museum is) & Horton plaza (shopping district). Parking is free too if you drive. The staff gave us a map of places to go and was helpful when addressing our queries. 
The room is pretty basic but clean. We did laundry there too and washing powder was provided at $1. My only complain is that we couldn't get the Wifi up and the guy who was in charge of looking into this failed to turn up in our room as promised.
