Not too sure if this was due to our room being located at the far end of the motel.

title: “More than acceptable for the price and location”
text: This was my very first trip to New York City and I was shocked at the hotel prices when I started investigating. I can usually find great deals through Travelocity and other online sites for around $100, even in places like San Francisco, but the ones I was finding in NYC had horrible customer reviews attached to them. I finally settled on the Buckingham for $159 on the nights in October that I was staying, and was more than pleased. Aside from the fact that I was NEVER in my room, when I was there, it was roomy and clean and a fine place to spread out and rest up from the day's adventures. Granted, it wasn't the Plaza, but who needs that unless it's your honeymoon and your sole purpose in renting a room is to pull the shades and never leave? NYC is to be experienced OUTSIDE the walls of a hotel, and this little place allowed me a clean and friendly home base a block from Central Park and 5th Avenue. I was more than happy - I'm going back next week en route to London and will likely stay there again!

title: “Loved this hotel”
text:
I was put up at the Clift for one night on a business trip and had Room 602, a junior suite. It was a very large, clean and oh so trendy room (yet extremely comfortable). The mattresses and down pillows were wonderful and the bedding was fresh, crisp and comfortable. I had two nice sized Sony flat screen TV's (one in the bedroom and one in the living area) and a nicely tiled bathroom with plenty of hot water, a robe and a ton of fluffy towels. My room had a Bose iPod dock in the living room (always appreciated) and a CD player in the bedroom.
Despite its busy location, I had no outside noise issues from the street or other rooms. The in room wireless WI-FI was hit or miss with my computer and a couple other business associates, also staying at the hotel. I cannot comment on the value as my company fortunately paid for the room.
My few dealings with the staff were excellent - the front desk folks were terrific and a manager from the gorgeous art deco lobby bar (which was hopping at 1 a.m. on a Thursday) couldn't have been nicer when she told us we couldn't have our cocktails in the lobby. Not a problem as we retired back to my suite where the music wasn't so loud and we could talk (the busy bar had pretty loud music). The crowd at the lobby bar was populated with an extremely diverse (ages, nationalities and income brackets) crowd which was quite refreshing and everybody seemed to be having a good time.
I cannot attest to the food but was told by co-workers it was wonderful. The lobby fireplace is fabulous on a chilly San Francisco night and I had some nice conversation with others who were waiting to go out for dinner.
Of course the neighborhood is right where you want to be in San Francisco - steps to Union Square, tons of theatre and a quick cab ride (or public transportation) to anywhere else you want to go.
I'm sorry I was only there for one night on business as this was a really fun hotel.

title: “Great staff, free wireless, close to things”
text:
The hotel is proximate to a lot of interesting things -- it's at the terminus of the cable car line to Chinatown, there's a BART stop right out the door, the Moscone and MoMA are three blocks away. The disadvantage of this location is the location: that part of the city is very noisy. 
The staff were top notch in helpfulness and enthusiasm. The room was small, but comfortable with a lot of pillows on the bed and a ceiling fan for cooling. For amenities, there was a flat screen TV (basic channels), free wireless, coffee maker, and hair dryer.
As for minuses: the bathroom had mini-blinds whose louvers weren't adjustable, but pointed down. The problem was the hotel across the street would have a [bad] into the activities in the bathroom.

title: “Huge Room”
text: After spending hours reviewing other opinions on LAX Airport hotels I chose the Marriott & wasn't disappointed! The free shuttle took about 5 minutes to get there, the hotel was spacious, friendly and very clean. There's a Starbucks in the huge foyer, a massive restaurant and sports bar there too.. Big pool area (although warning, as it's in the centre of the hotel, it is quite shaded when sun isn't directly overhead). The hotel (like most in the area) looks older from the outside than it does inside. I had a kingsize bed - huge.. sooo comfortable. Room service was quick, food was good. Checkout was 1pm - very convenient if you are using the hotel as a quick stop before going to another hotel. Also had a Hertz downstairs - so we could hire a car onsite.. we also chose to return it to the hotel & used the hotel shuttle to the airport ( just convenient because we knew where to go etc.).. I picked up my mother the next morning off an early flight, went back to the hotel - where we had bfast, which you can choose a la carte, or buffet.. Good quality food, proper freshly squeezed juice, very attentive waiters. Overall a great experience.

title: “Chic and cozy, great service... FANTASTIC location!”
text:
Came up for a house hunting trip, wanted to try something different. Greeted by friendly, extremely bright staff. Checked in in record time. Parking is not free but it's reasonable at $15/day (I think) for being right in the middle of the city. Room was a little small and door was very thin (I could hear a hair dryer running in another room down the hall), but beds were comfy and could see enough of the streets from the window to get a feel for the neighborhood.
Easy 10 minute walk to Pike place market. Had an awesome meal at a corner seafood restaurant. Continued about 20 more minutes to Pioneer Square. DO the Underground tour!! Soooo cool!! Nice walk back to hotel thru city. Stuff is open late (not like Portland) and every single restaurant is awesome. We true all the restaurants near the hotel. Recommend Lola's as well as Bell Thai. Fabulous! Also there are bicycles for loan, great idea to ride over to the Space Needle and City Center (10 min walk opposite direction of Pike market).
Parking on the upper level was extremely tight, but doable. Not a lot of kids in this somewhat chic hotel, so our stay was rather quiet. Would 100% stay here again! 
Over 4.999 stars because of the thin doors.

title: “simply amazing!!”
text:
Our family stayed in the hotel. The second I arrived I knew it was going to be a great stay. We had no trouble getting into the room and a very nice guy parked the car in their specialized garage. The swimming pool was humungous and led to almost an hour of swimming. They recommended an italian restaurant called Buca de Bepo. Moi delesioso!
It was a 3 minute walk to the needle and 1 LRT ride away from the market with the original starbucks. In general this is an amazing hotel. Not mentioning the amazing breakfast. The regular continental breakfast with hot food as well. The T.v's were kind of small but way better than some of the others we saw on our trip. I would stay there again and a small stuffed animal was left behind. no matter, they saw to it asap and when we got home there was the animal, all packed up.

title: “1st Rate Hotel With Convenient Location”
text:
We have always stayed at this exit and at a competitor up the street for years to break up our trip from Sarasota to the Charlotte, NC area to visit family. Our last visit to the hotel we usually stayed at was a disappointment in cleaniness and in the breakfast offered. Hyatt Place was a few $$ more, but more than worth it.
The rooms are large, clean, tv is awesome and modern decor a treat throughout the facility. The beds were awesome too; we were on the 6th floor and not a sound heard; best night's sleep in ages!
The breakfast had a nice variety of offerings from various juices, hot oatmeal, cold cereals, yogurt, fresh fruit, french toast and two breakfast sandwiches with meat. My favorite was one that had spinach, cheese and mushrooms added. 
An added plus is that it is a short distance across I 95 to a huge Shopping Center with chain restaurants, Wal-Mart and other stores.
We definitely will make Hyatt Place our choice, each way, when we visit family in the future!

title: “Excellent Hotel in Great Location”
text: We were extremely impressed with the Westin Georgetown. We switched from another hotel at the last minute to stay somewhere with an outdoor pool, and we are glad we did! The pool/fitness area is very nice, and our entire experience at the hotel was great. The front desk personnel were some of the best I have ever encountered. The hotel gave us both early check-in and late check-out to accommodate our flight times (such a plus when traveling with a baby). The room itself was nice and clean. The bathroom had a soaking tub and nice shower. My only complaint is that the crib they provided was very small, poor quality (looked more like a small metal cage), and a little worn. If I stayed here again, I'd bring my daughters travel crib. We'd stayed across the street at the Park Hyatt less than a month before, and their crib/baby ammenities were much nicer.

title: “Good staff on a bad day”
text:
Although the hotel was very nice and the staff extremely personable, they did not have it together. Checking in on a July Saturday afternoon involved a 45-minute wait. At least 20 guests got up there and were told it would take a while because they were waiting for rooms. The only explanation I got was that "we were full last night." Gee, that's a shock, full hotel on a Friday night.
I stayed there to go to a Nationals game (about a five-block walk) and noticed there was still a line to check in at 11 pm. It is very convenient for baseball and the rooms were nice. Just hope they get their staffing figured out.

title: “Outstanding Service and Location - Above Average Rooms”
text:
We traveled to Seattle for a fun weekend and stayed at the Inn at the Market. We booked our room via an Alaska Airlines Vacation Package. The package deal provided a free night (equating to a nearly $300 savings). The key elements of this hotel are the location and staff. The rooms are fine (not remarkable) but they are plenty clean and comfortable. We highly recommend staying here via a package deal to save some money. 
LOCATION:
The hotel's location is tough to beat. It is literally right across the street from Pike Place Market and the original Starbucks. It is within a short walk to key Seattle downtown sites (Space Needle, Pioneer Square) and in our case we didn't have a car. Valet parking at the hotel runs about $30 a day. 
ROOMS:
Our room had a partial view of the water (which really added a lot to the experience and reduced noise compared to the city-only view rooms). They were pretty new and felt clean but did not exude luxury. The bed utilized a foam-based mattress (but was comfortable) and the sitting area was small but nice. Overall the room was the least memorable aspect of the stay but clearly not a reason to not book at this hotel. 
SERVICES:
This hotel has an exceptionally friendly and helpful staff. From the moment we arrived (they set us up with an early check-in), to great food suggestions and a kind valet service we felt like service was king here. They provide a free choice of newspapers delivered to your room (Seattle Times, NY Times or WSJ), the hotel has a free shoe-shine service and they provided taxis and other needs without hesitation. The restaurant (which is connected but not affiliated) was good for breakfast but a bit expensive - it ran $40/couple. If you are willing to walk a little there are bagel shops and other food opportunities at reduced rates in the area. The wireless Internet was reliable and fast/free. 
OVERALL:
Overall we would stay here again. We found rates to be a bit high through their website but would attempt to stay via a package deal. We would highly suggest attempting to obtain a view room (water view) and possibly eating at non-affiliated restaurants to save money. If you want a weekend location where you can walk to everything, have a clean and comfortable room with outstanding service this hotel will work well.

title: “mixed”
text: the rates were good, the staff is nice but there were stains on the bedcloths and the bathroom floor and shower had way too much visible hairs on them. i will pay more next time to stay at a cleaner place

title: “Absolutely filthy, worn and unsanitary!!”
text: I am so upset after reading the reviews from some senior reviewers who gave this hotel great ratings. This hotel is absolutely disgusting! The floors, the shower, the sinks were like a truck rest stop. The only saving grace was the bed and the location. This hotel is right across the street from Central Park and a perfect area to stay in while visiting the City. But trust me, steer clear of this run down, just down right filthy hotel. Cleanliness is not on the priority list at all. Such a disappointment..... I am now cautious in trusting some of these do called senior reviewers as the integrity is not present in reviewing this hotel. Ugh!!

title: “Good hotel for the price and location”
text:
I have traveled to NYC more than two dozen times and have stayed in 4 and 5 star hotels every time. This was my first experience with a Holiday Inn property in Manhattan.
I was not disappointed at all. 
Parking: parked around the corner for 30.00 a day with hotel stamping the parking ticket.
Location: Great location if you want to be in Lower Manhattan. Walking distance to Wall Street, South Street Seaport, Ground Zero/Freedom Tower site, Brooklyn Bridge". Short walk to Chinatown and Little Italy. 
The hotel was very clean with a nice, smallish, lobby area. The staff was friendly. 
The room was large enough and comfortable for two people (my 16 yr old daughter and myself). The beds were comfortable and there was really no street noise. The only noise complaint I would have is that when people left their rooms, the doors slammed very loudly. Other than that, no complaints. The bathroom was clean and had ample amenities.
There was a small business center with free internet service, which was nice as I forgot my laptop.
The breakfast buffet was decent. Someone mentioned the watery eggs, which I'm sure were just powdered eggs, but they were kind of blah. The small omelettes were decent. Selection of bacon, breads, danishes, muffins, etc....My only complaint is that it was PACKED every morning. The poor guy trying to clean and restock the food really had his work cut out for him....
All in all, this was a nice hotel in a good, safe location and I would recommend if you want to make Lower Manhattan your hub of activity. I did miss being in Midtown, but it was a short subway ride away.

title: “Moved to the Fairmont”
text:
So I stayed at the Palace because of meetings and invited my wife to join me for the trip. We had intended to stay for two more nights. However, after awakening at 4 am to the sounds of Market Street, we had to move. I had upgraded to some special level and honestly thought they made a mistake--surely this is not the upgrade room. It felt dark, small and a tiny bath--not by European standards but by American standards. The clerk said the upgrade was due to this room being 100sf largers---I'd hate to stay in the smaller room.
Lobby, fitness center, meeting rooms and halls were all great, just not the room. 
We checked out the Fairmont, found they had availability and moved. Boy are we glad we did. Same elegance, but for the same price, we have a much better room overlooking the bay.

title: “Terrible staff”
text: We stayed at the Edison for 5 nights in June, FANTASTIC Location, Hotel was just average, which is what we expected based on the price we paid, we booked it for the location. The staff really need quality training in the customer service industry. Particularly Reception and some of the bell boys, one in particular was so rude and unhelpful. I don't know whether the Reception staff are unhappy with their lives or jobs, but boy are they a miserable bunch. Would be nice if they cracked a smile or at least appeared to be pleasant. We were reluctant to even disturb them as they were just not plesant to approach and ask any questions. FYI to the Edison staff - all it takes is a smile to make your customers stay abit more enjoyable. If you don't like working in the tourism industry - find another job please......

title: “Great place to stay”
text: Hotel was clean, close to Fishermans Wharf and the front desk was so friendly , especially Brandy.

title: “Awesome bed!! Staff was helpful and friendly.”
text: A group of us stayed here during Comic-Con... a crazy time for hotels in San Diego. The staff was professional and super helpful. There was a minor problem with our bedside lamp and someone came up immediately to fix it. I needed info on local churches and the front desk not only gave me the info on the phone but printed out mass schedules and driving directions and then delivered these to our room. The best part of this hotel though are the amazing beds and pillows straight from heaven. I am seriously going to find a place to but some of those pillows for myself!

title: “Changed rooms 3 times...”
text: This was a frustrating experience. First we were sent to a room where the door was wedged open. As we peered in we noticed part of a wooden bathroom cabinet on the bed. After traveling back to the front desk we were given the adjacent room. It was fine until the morning when we had no hot water. The front desk individual said we just needed to let it run (it had been for 15 minutes) and then sent a repairman. He said they should have known that these rooms were being worked on. They sent us keys to yet another room after 45 minutes, which made us about 2 hours late for an event on the 4th. When we returned our keys didn't work. No compensation was ever mentioned.

title: “Great location and atmosphere!”
text: Everyone was pleasant and professional. Decor was chic and clean with cool New Age music pumped in. Library bar was classy, yet comfy. Food and drink delicious and reasonable. Fantastic, yet simple buffet breakfast. In the heart of the theatre district right by Times Square. Restaurant row down the block. Bring comfortable walking shoes and enjoy!

title: “Good location close to Union Square”
text:
We stayed here recently for a family event. Got a good rate through Hotwire and used our Wyndham Rewards card to get the free internet (otherwise it is $14.95 a night). The hotel is around the corner from the BART Powell St Station which makes it easy to get back and forth from SFO airport. Lobby was spacious and modern. Rooms were spacious and quiet.
Close to Union Square shopping, public transit, walking distance to Chinatown and Nob Hill (if you don't mind walking uphill).
Plenty of nearby restaurants both affordable and high end
Staff was friendly and attentive

title: “Great location”
text: Great neighborhood. Lots of nice restaurants and bars down the street. Close to the Convention Center and train station. Neat old building. Room was small but very comfortable.

title: “HORRIBLE PLACE”
text: This is easily the WORST motel I've ever stayed at...the Indian management (especially the female that works in the afternoon) is rude and doesn't care about their customers. My "non-smoking" room smelled of cigarettes, the lock on the door was broken, I saw rats in the parking lot, roaches in the room, numerous holes in the walls, stains all over the sheets, pillowcases, and towels, the toilet wasn't flushing properly, and the tv only gets about 10 stations, with most of them in spanish. When I called the front desk to report any problems, they basically told me that it's not their problem, and refused to move me to another room. There is a sign when you check in that states NO REFUNDS, so the owner does give a s--t about you after taking your money. Although the property is within walking distance to the convention center, the area is very sketchy at night. There seemed to be plenty of budget accomodations in the area, so my recommendation is to AVOID THIS MOTEL!

title: “So so”
text: On the beach, great location, great view. Some rif-raft hanging around on the board walk late at night. Rooms very small. Square foot price is on the high side. Score C+ Parking was good and secure. Supply and demand. Maybe a little on the pricey side for what you get. This is an older property in need of updating.

title: “Will stay here any time we are in San Francisco”
text: We spent one weeknight in Marina Motel in early November. Both my partner and I were very impressed with the property, staff, and accommodations. The free, individual stall garage parking was a unique perk compared to many other hotels in the city that only had $30-$40 per night parking lots or no private parking at all. Although we had read reviews that recommended not leaving your spot later in the evening, we saw plenty of open garages when we returned from dinner. This may be different on weekends. The room we were in was very small, but as a couple traveling light for an extended weekend, it was just the right size. If you tend to be a traveler that packs more than a couple of small carry-ons, I recommend requesting a larger room. We loved the more personal and homey feel of the room with pretty brocade bedding and windows that opened up for some fresh air. Both the room and the bathroom were charming with a retro feel. The only problem with the bathroom is that the shower stall was very dark. There was only one light in the bathroom and the stall style shower's curtain blocked most of that light, even during the day. I did see some other guests checking in to rooms next to us but surprisingly, I never heard any of them. I'm not sure what prevented the sound from traveling, but I didn't hear anyone walking to or from rooms, watching TV, or talking in other rooms. The staff was welcoming, warm, and helpful. I went straight to the front desk to ask how to get to Chinatown on mass transit. The person on duty had an immediate answer and drew the directions on a map of the city. I was really happy to find out that one of the main bus lines runs just one block away from the hotel and took us directly to Chinatown. You can easily walk to the Palace of Fine Arts and there are plenty of eateries within walking distance. The grounds were very pretty, with lots of bougainvillea hanging from the buildings. Once you come in off of the street, it feels like a different world. We stayed in a room right in the middle of the property and it was really quiet. I did notice that any rooms on the Lombard St. side would probably be pretty noisy. Overall we have no real complaints about the stay and we really enjoyed it. We're already talking about our next trip to the area and would love to stay at Marina Motel again.

title: “My favourite hotel in New York”
text: This was my fourth time at Chelsea Pines and, once again, it was a fantastic experience. The location is perfect, the staff attentive and friendly, and the rooms (I have stayed in four different ones) are charming. Most importantly, I always sleep well as it's is extremely quiet and peaceful. Also, there is free WiFi and a business centre. Also, movie-lovers will get a real kick out of the star-themed rooms.

title: “Sheek romantic boutique hotel with breathtaking loft rooms”
text: The best part of this hotel is the room. You walk in and you are immediately met with floor to ceiling window's for all exterior walls - looking out over the city. The room itself is all dark hardwood floors, the shower is fantastic, and the flatscreens are nice too. The rest of the hotel is nice and not too pretentious... there is a steakhouse/sushi-bar in the main level and a club at the top floor with a rooftop deck. My wife loved the spa too.

title: “False alarms”
text: I am a business traveler and log over 120 nights per year in hotels. I've stayed here 5 times. In the past 10 years, I have experienced 3 false fire alarms in the middle of the night. Two of the three were at this property. Unless you don't mind a 3:00 am loud wake up call in a panic and descend 7 flights of stairs, I would not stay here.

title: “Best Hotel in San Francisco”
text:
The past year I have stayed at the Parc 55 at least once a month for over 4-5 days at a time. Each visit here is remarkable. These folks treat you as if you are home, the rooms are outstanding, great views,and very clean. You have access to all the shopping and food you could imagine or simply eat in the dinning area there. 
I cannot say enough good things about this hotel.
Remarkable stays

title: “just ok”
text: When we arrived at the hotel, we asked for a non smoking room. We opened the door, and it looks like somebody was smoking there just 10 minutes before, and all the beds were undone. We went back to the front desk, and they were waiting for us, because they must have realize that they did something wrong. The hotel is overall ok for the price you pay, but nothing special.

title: “An amazing historic hotel”
text: We stayed 3 nights and it was great. The room was a great size; bed was very comfortable

title: “The worst in denver”
text: Crack heads, bed bugs, drug dealers, prostitute, DANGEROUS, pool filled with trash, this place should be shut down as a public menace, Run for your life the worst motel in denver, donna the crackhead clerk is rude nasty and just a terrible person, rooms are nasty I found used rubbers, used tampons and needles in the room hallways covered in urine and vomit, if you value your families safety then pass this place up

title: “Fantastic holiday over the Christmas period.”
text: A friendly hotel in a great location. Good breakfast, best to go earlier to avoid queuing, great value for money and would definitely book again.

title: “Great”
text: I think the hotel is Great! We booked the room in advance and a cheap rate. We got there, talked to bartender for a while, found out that they had a low occupancy rate for the weekend and asked if we could get an upgraded room. The gave us exactly what we asked for, never made us wait and it was wonderful. I agree with other review, the rooms are a bit small but definitely luxury. The views are beautiful, ALL the staff was very accomodating and would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Location is Awesome 1 block from Carnegie Hall & Central park South”
text: Can you imagine paying less that $200 a nigh in Mahattan? If you are a looking for good hotel and great price AWESOME location, this is the place. It is on block between Carnagie Hall and Central Park South. This is NOT a luxury hotel. There is no bell hop or turn down service. There is small & unobtrusive staff. Our room had a Queen bed, a writing desk with chair & a dresser with a TV on it. The TV was old & only had local stations but who cares you are in Manhattan. I was not there to watch TV. There is maid service. The room was made up after a long day out like clockwork. They had a breakfast that consist of of a coffee, juice, or tea with either a muffin or a bagel. I think the breakfast service was on the 6th floor small room with an attendant that ask for your room nbr. The breakfast service is only there for about two hours. It is good way to get started for walking your way around Manhattan.

title: “I've found the best place to stay in NYC while on business!”
text:
We had such a lovely stay at the Lucerne! Everything about it for our three-night stay was a joy. First, the staff was so accommodating in checking us in earlier after I pleaded because I had to make an important engagement at Columbia University. Not only did they give us an early check-in, but also they upgraded us to a beautiful suite! The doormen were all really warm and just pleasant folks, always greeting us with a smile. I'd been traveling for a week, and at the Lucerne I slept like a baby in the firm king-sized bed. The room is tastefully decorated, and the rotating showerhead in the bathroom feels great on the skin.
I've stayed in numerous NYC hotels, and I've rarely felt this comfortable. This is the best hotel stay I've had so far. It's location is superb, near dozens of really delicious eateries, and only an avenue away from Central Park and a main subway line (#1 train). I've already made up my mind that I'll come back here 
again and again.

title: “Decent”
text: This hotel was decent. Parking is free, but if you want to go out at night, take public transportation. If you come back late, all the spaces will be full. I found it odd, that when leaving we left the "do not disturb" sign out, but the maid still came in, I thought that was the purpose of leaving the sign out. Had trouble with the cable going out one night. Also, the internet didn't work a couple times, but at least it was free. The elevator was a little loud/scary, but it worked. If I were to make the trip again, I would consider staying at this hotel again, if the price were still good.

title: “TA is right - #1 Hotel in San Jose”
text: Now called the Hyatt Place- this hotel is so new, the addy was not even on my dated GPS! Hip, cool decor in the rooms and the common areas - very very clean and had a very nice smell! Beds were nice, water pressure excellent, breakfast buffet w/ omelette bar great, free wi-fi great reception, free parking that's actually close to the building, but the most important thing is that the staff was very accomodating& courteous! Special mention to Kristina & Kimmy! I have stayed in a LOT of hotels; certainly, while this is not 5*, this was truly truly exceptional! Thank you!!! Love it! Will certainly come back!

title: “Ask for a higher floor”
text: Initially when we checked in they were going to put us in the queen rooms which was on the lower floors. I hear these rooms have sinks inside the room and not the bathroom. When I asked the lady at the desk to put us in a king room, she said they were booked (we were there for a conference) however after playing around she was able to put us in one. Overall the room was nice with a big window overlooking chicago. My main complaint would be the funny smell in the lobby (smelled like mildew). Otherwise the room we were in was nice and very comfortable.

title: “Stay on a GOLD Floor”
text:
Having read some previous reviews, we stayed on a newly remodeled Gold floor. Our rate was $139 and we also belong to the Fairmont President's Club. The rooms are well appointed and updated in a neutral tones. We had a corner king room with excellent views in two directions. The food presentations in the club lounge are excellent and second only to the Ritz in quality. The club rooms at other hotels nearby are nowhere near the quality of the Fairmont. 
The restaurant Pyramid is very well reviewed in the Dallas Press and currently running a four course $40 prix fixe menu to celebrate the Fairmont 40th Anniversary. It's a wonderful offer. 
The Fairmont has an excellent and quite large gym along with a large outdoor pool. Given their normal rates, it pays to do a little shopping online for specials which are easily had in this economy. 
We enjoyed the rooms, our incredible bath robes, free internet, soft down pillows etc. It's all a lovely experience. There is twice daily maid service and with one phone call we had anything we requested without waiting any longer than 5 minutes. Very impressive.
We were surprised by how quickly the valets had the car each time we called, even with the hotel being quite full and handling three weddings that we counted. 
Don't worry about the previous people who seemed to have numerous complaints for one wrong or the other, we did not experience anything close to these experiences and again, I would do a little a shopping online and definitely book a Gold level floor it is well worth the extra amount you'll pay.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Nice hotel if you need to be close to the aiport. Its a short drive from a nice mall and many local places to eat. If you want to stay IN San Antonio, I'd suggest you look elsewhere. As this is a trek to the riverwalk. But a very clean nice room!

title: “Waterpark ok but rooms dirty”
text:
We stayed one night to be close to the airport after a weeklong stay in other parts of Arizona. Kids loves the waterpark. Clean and plenty of seats and lifeguards.
Room was a nice size but outdated and sheets and towels were dirty. We didn't like being in the room at all.
Price included the 100 resort credit which was nice. Dinner at lobby grill was good.
If you are paying a 30 resort fee wifi should be included!

title: “Worth Every Cent!!!!”
text:
We Stayed At Le Meridien San Francisco During A Holiday To California September 2008. From The Moment We Stepped Out Of The Taxi Cab We Were Treated Amazingly By All The Staff At The Hotel. The Concierges Were Helpful in Giving Directions And Suggestions For Restaurants. Check-In Was Simple And The Hotel Was Able To Accomodate Our Early Check-In Request With No Problems. While High-Speed Wireless Internet Is Available At The Hotel, There Is A Fee Charged Per Day. However, The Hotel Does Have A Business Centre With 3 Computers With Highspeed Internet Available To All Guests. The Room Was Quite Spacious & The Bed Was Extremely Comfortable. There Was A Large LCD Television, But No DVD Player. However After A Day Of Sightseeing, We Found No Need For A DVD Player Anyways. 
Overall, Our Stay At Le Meridien Was Amazing And Worth Every Penny!!!! Would Definitely Stay Here Again.

title: “Service with a Smile”
text: The staff are most certainly what would make me return to this hotel...from the doormen & bellhops to the housekeepers & concierge, everybody was exceptionally eager to please. The rooms were clean and comfortable, although dated in there furnishings and somewhat small, but the free breakfast and free tea/coffee station in the lobby was a godsend.

title: “Excellent Property, Great Service”
text: Have stayed here a number of times over the past couple of months for business trips. Nice older property, conveniently located across the street from LAX. Despite having a view of the runway from my window, I never hear any noise from the planes. This is by all means a full service hotel- nice pool, nice gym, good room service and lively bar. Just to show you how great the employees are here, I left my credit card in the room when I checked out once. Called when I realized I left it a few hours later and was able to go back and pick it up before my flight back out of town that night. I was going to cancel it and have another card issued but decided to wait. This was about a month ago and I havent had any issues with the card. In this day and age, that's almost unheard of. Because of their honesty and integrity, this property has me as a customer for life! Highly recommend and of course I'll stay here again.

title: “The PERFECT Hotel”
text: Great location, within walking distance to Little Italy, China Town and SOHO. Particularly close to the Subway as well, making it very easy to get anywhere in New York. The service was exceptional. I reserved a twin bed room, and they gave us two double bed rooms instead with no extra charge. The front desk staffs were friendly and more than helpful to help us with the direction. However, like many hotels in the USA, they will charge you for the bottled water.

title: “A place to stay”
text: We are staying at Residence Inn, Downtown San Diego. The hotel and staff have been nice enough with our limited exposure to them. The breakfast is typical for this kind of hotel. It is only open until 9:00 a.m. so if you are late sleeper, don't expect to see it because they clear it out on the minute. We did not use the pool but it looked clean and there were people out there. Our room faced the town and right behind our hotel is the railroad train which goes by all night long. We can hear it as well as the planes flying over head landing and taking off from the airport.. The entire hotel needs refurbishing including the Marriott promise of upgrading all of their mattresses. This one was certainly not an upgrade. We had our 10 year old with us and he is sleeping on the hide a bed which also needs to be upgraded. Generally they leave it open and made up but tonight it was closed with no sheets on it so we had to make the bed ourselves for him. It must be weekend staffing. There is a good wifi in the room which is free. The bedroom has queen sizes beds. I don't think they have king sized beds at this hotel property. The bathroom is okay with a tub shower. All in all, it is a place to stay, but not that exciting with all of the choices in San Diego. We are only here because we are using points.

title: “Honestly, its not good”
text: Im not really one to complain but this is THE WORST hotel we stayed in our whole trip! The bed smelt faintly of urine and our TV only picked up 2 channels and this was never fixed dispite calling the front desk a few times about it. But the worst thing is the location... its in this really scary area where there were so many weirdos harrasing you as you walked down the street. We really didnt wanna go out after dark. My advice is to stay near Union Square if you wanna be in the city. its cheap but not really worth it!

title: “Worth it for location”
text:
We recently stayed at the Ritz for my birthday weekend. Every employee we interacted with was unfailingly polite and pleasant. The hotel is clean, well kept, and the service is very good. All of which you expect at this level of hotel.
 Lobby and exterior are impressive; standard rooms are very nice but not anything special. Lacking simple conveniences such as an iphone/mp3 docking station, easily accessible outlets to charge electronic devices, blackout curtains that truly blackout, etc. 
We were on the 20th floor with a view of City Hall and there was definitely street noise. Also, there was a wedding here our 2nd night, and we could hear the revelers in the hall until around 2am. That's not entirely the hotels fault, but better soundproofing and a closer eye on the noise levels would've helped.
We enjoyed drinks at the bar one night (Saturday), and I wouldn't say that the service was exceptional, although the atmosphere and drinks were very nice. Had room service breakfast both days and it was quite good.
Overall, the greatest selling point of this hotel is a phenomenal location. You are near the theaters, nightlife, amazing restaurants and across the street from public transportation that will take you anywhere in the city. For just a luxury experience, at this pricetag, I would probably give somewhere else a try next time.

author.location: Traveling every week from VA to VT !

title: “Overall, an enjoyable stay.”
text: We were back in town for two nights and gave GP a try. Check in was fast and the room was comfy. Sheets and towels were comfortable and the bed was a good nights rest. Room was a little cramped for two but if you're not in the room that much it works. They have a wine tasting in the afternoon but it's a little too popular so we steered clear. Room service was pretty dismal, they were out of everything we asked for and we gave up and went out for breakfast. The coffee maker in the room was very odd. A Keurig, which we have at home, so we knew how to use it. Thing is they give you these tiny cups that will overflow if you follow the directions as listed on the device. I suggest only filling it with the cup provided to avoid the flood we had. My biggest complaint would have to be the valet. We dropped the car off on arrival and took it out the second night to meet old friends for dinner. It took a good 30 minutes to get our car because the valet was MIA after taking someone else's car. When we returned from dinner I waited another 30 minutes for the valet before going to the front desk to ask them to locate the guy. He walked up like nothing was wrong so needless to say a tip was not offered. Great location for getting around town whether by cab, public transit or car.

title: “A failed trip to the spa”
text:
When booking the appointment the staff was fantastic, so I discounted the review above. 
Unfortunately, my appointment was also lost. The explanation I received upon arrival was that several therapists were out sick, and so the appointment couldn't take place at the scheduled time. 
To be fair, they did reschedule it for a later time that day, but no one called to tell me this, and the new time conflicted with the meeting I'm in town for. 
The final straw though was when the receptionist told me she may have to charge me for half of the appointment for 'cancelling' that later time they had chosen.
Too bad - it's beautiful inside and I was really looking forward to it!

title: “You get what you pay for”
text: You really are getting what you pay for when you stay at any four seasons resort. In Seattle, the location really is fantastic; mere minutes walking to pikes place and the original Starbucks. As always, the staff will bend over backwards to help. I got lucky with my room, it was a corner room so it had views of the city and if you walk close to the window you can also see the water. It was quite large, and had a fantastic bathroom and tub. My parents stayed a couple rooms down (same price) but our room was far superior since it was a corner room.

title: “Great Uptown Charlotte location”
text: We stayed at the Charlotte Marriott City Center for 3 nights for our son's wedding. The employees at the reception desk are unbelievably helpful, the bellhops can't do enough for you and our room was spacious, impeccably clean and comfortable. The hotel is huge and includes 2 bars, a restaurant, and a Starbucks. The business center has 3 computers and a printer that are free to use. The only thing missing is an airport shuttle. Although there are always taxis in front of the hotel, it is $25 to get to the airport. The location in uptown Charlotte is really convenient to a lot of attractions, restaurants and bars. Not sure what the hotel costs per night but we got a great rate in the wedding block. I would definitely stay again at the Marriott if I ever return to Charlotte.

title: “Great ammenities, but couldn't use”
text:
We checked in and were a little surprised that we needed to take our own bags to the room. Room was very clean, large and comfortable. The matresses were very comfortable.
They had turn-down service and free newspaper and had many options for eating in your room.
The Langham has an award winning dining room and wonderful spa services. We were there for a wedding and, unfortunately for us, did not have the time to utilize them.
The conciege was excellent. When I needed something, the gift shop was closed, so the congierge opened it for me so I could make my purchase. (I did not realize there was a CVS close by, or I would never have taken him up on his offer to open the shop)

title: “Neighborhood folks give this hotel high marks.”
text:
I had stayed at this hotel some years ago while attending a professional conference, so I knew of its reputation. Nevertheless, I imagine the best review a hotel can get is that the people who live locally like the place so much that they have their out-of-town family and guests stay there. This is what my airport shuttle companions told me while driving from La Guardia to Columbus Circle. 
When I commented on the amount of construction taking place on 57th Street and its environs, the desk clerk suggested a room in their "B" wing which faced an interior courtyard rather than the street, adding "Besides, there are two conventions in town and the house is full." Because I agreed to accept a smoking room rather than the non-smoking room I reserved, I was given a certificate good for a free drink at the bar and another certificate good for a free continental breakfast. So far, so good.
The room turned out to be in an older wing of the building, and the smell of smoke permeating the corrider carpeting led me believe that the room itself would probably have cigarette burns on the furniture and carpeting. Nothing could have been further from the truth. The room itself was smell-free and had recently been scrubbed and vacuumed within in inch of its life. 
I can see why the locals like this place for their guests--the rooms are squeaky clean.
Room service was good too. I ordered a salad plate and a bowl of minestrone at 10pm, after I had finished unpacking. It arrived in 38 minutes, brought by one of the most cheerful servers I've ever met. Have hearty, simple food well-prepared, and you can't go wrong.

title: “LOVE IT!”
text:
This hotel is perfect for couples looking for a weekend getaway or anyone travelling for business!!! The hotel is used for businesses during the week and is open to the public on weekends. We got our room for $159 a night and let me tell you it was worth a lot more!
The room was contemporary and designed well. There was a flat screen tv (loved it!!!) that looked to be about 26inches. The bathroom was immaculate! There wasn't a tub, instead a shower stall, which was perfect for New York because you don't really need to take a bath while you're in the city. We also stayed on the top floor so our ceilings were about 13 feet high!! It made the room feel huge! (I can't say whether the other floors had ceilings that high.) They did a great job designing the rooms and made the best of the space they had. 
You need a room key to use the elevator, which may seem annoying, but it was actually comforting and I felt safe knowing that you had to be a guest to get around. One of the best features is that each floor has a closet on it with extra blankets, pillows, irons, ironing boards, coffee, etc. It's perfect because you don't have to annoy housekeeping and wait forever, instead you can just get it yourself. Another great feature is that the hotel will deliver food to you from any restaurants near the hotel. We didn't take advantage of this because we were out in the city most of the time. 
The location of the hotel is perfect for anyone who likes to get away from the tourist areas of NYC. We usually go every year so it's nice to stay in downtown. The subway is right around the corner, both the red line and green line. The hotel parking offers a discount at a garage two short blocks away for $25 a day which is great for Manhattan!!! If you're interested in seeing a broadway show, there is a ticket discount booth a few blocks away [---]
The ticket booth is actually on the backside of the building to make note. This ticket booth is A LOT less crowded. My boyfriend and I walked up and waited behind only one person. We got 50% off Chicago tickets for the next day and we were in row G in the orchestra!!
Overall this was a wonderful hotel, with a wonderful location, and a wonderful staff!

title: “Great visit”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Apolphus for two nights. We went to a concert a few miles away and celebrated our anniversary with a dinner at Tthe French Room on-site. We were greeted very warmly. While the hotel is a glimpse back at old-money opulence, the staff is not stuffy at all. Everyone was friendly. The rooms are quite large for a downtown property and very comfortable.
The French Room provided us with a memorable, though expectedly pricey, anniversary splurge meal. The food was and service were both just spot-on and the wine was perfect. Overall, a great little getaway.

title: “Good secret location!!”
text:
Here we go
1 valet $23 a day( or park your own Car- good luck)
2 very nice valet workers
3 Tracy at checkin is a super worker( tell ya why later)
4 queen queen suite is decent for 2 people not 4 
5 bathroom small (bathroom could have been cleaner- I'm really picky)
6 small small pool ( one family at time type) not really indoor but the pool is surrounded by the height of hotel and heated
7 breafast is decent for free( don't expect too much) hard to get a seat 
So it gets really crowded
8 Tracy was working the breafast too after checking us in the previous night.. Wow go girl!!!
9 one block from Alamo

The top for a no room service hotel!! Calm down and relax David 
13 now someone said beware of Bryan... But I had no issues with him.. He was polite and very down to earth!!! 
14 very nice hotel for price.. Nice presentation of decor.. But it's per friendly and not sure if house keeping can keep up later in years...
15 so for now.. It's a perfect location and clean hotel!!
Iheart travel

title: “Liquor galore”
text: We stayed at the hotel for 2 nights in August, 2012. The hotel was very nice, spotless, and a welcoming staff. The only complaint that i have is they place so much liquor, sweets, etc in your room for sale. You can't even use the fridge in your room because they have it stuffed with beer. For the price they charge you would think they would at least have a coffee maker in your room and an empty fridge for you to use. Will look at other options next time i stay in Boston.

title: “Really enjoyed my stay!!!!”
text: I really enjoyed my stay at this hotel. The service was great. My suite was beautiful. The staff is very attentive and very helpful. I would highly reccommend this hotel to anyone staying in the midtown area. Also reccommend their other hotel in Manhattan. Their location is a great one for the business or the leisure traveler.

title: “A bargain motel, take your ear plugs.”
text:
Its a bit old and i guess that's what gives it character. The rooms are clean and the bathroom works as it should. Nice shower. 
The staff are very helpful and we always had a parking space in the three days we were there. Its a noisy motel though. Sounds from the car park area seemed to be amplified and sent through the half inch gap under the door or though the single glazed window (room 214) but really our first two nights were OK, just a few door slammers and the occasional loud conversation at 11 o'clock at night. Then the 36 school kids plus teachers arrived. I must say that we didn't hear much of them after 10pm apart from the odd door slam (i can shut doors without slamming them) but the morning ( 6.45am ) was a different story. Why did these people think its OK to make so much noise outside peoples rooms. They knew we were in there. Perhaps they are just naturally inconsiderate. I was brought up to have have more respect for others.

title: “Great Location...Nice Place”
text: I recently stayed here after our tour company booked us four rooms for a high school senior trip. I did not research the cost of the hotel as it was part of our package. We were extremely busy while there so did not get to take advantage of the pool or courtyard area, however, they looked to be quite nice. I felt the rooms were adequate size with a room safe, frig, coffee maker, blow dryer and I think microwave but can't 100% recall. The bathroom was clean..the rooms were clean. We were right outside of the elevator bank and I didn't notice any extra noise. We weren't arriving to our rooms until 9:00 ish each night so maybe it was quieter then. I see someone commented on the beds..they are sleepnumber beds and none of our group could completely figure out the way to operate them...we either had them too firm or not enough. I did notice that whenever anyone moved, rolled over,anything, that they made noise. This would have been an issue for me had I not had earplugs :-) The pillow were comfortable and the bedding was nice. We had one person with allergies and needed to have the down comforter and pillows switched out...the help did that right away. There isn't a restaurant at this place, however, there was an IHOP (International House of Pancakes) right next door. There are many restaurants within a block or two radius. I did see a morning area in the lobby where they served coffee and cold drinks and I think muffins and such. The location of this hotel was awesome. It's within almost all of the major tourist spots and within walking distance really. If I go back for a non-student vacation, I'd probably stay at this place again or for sure in this area as reviews that I weed through and cost are a factor for me. The hustle and bustle and fun of the wharf, pier 39, cable cars, was all great.

title: “Peaceful stay in lovely hotel”
text: We were in town for the SF Nike Womens Marathon. The concierge was very helpful and showed us how to walk from the hotel to MLK Park a few blocks away where we found a relaxing tea room and outdoor patio. We enjoyed the pool and hot tub and the gym has brand new fitness equipment. The bed was unbelievably comfortable, especially after the marathon! We were able to extend our stay with late check out at 2 PM. The restaurant has delicious food, 'tho quite expensive.

title: “Not up to Embassy Suites standards!”
text: We recently booked a stay at this hotel for five nights - we only stayed one night. The air conditioner did not work. They sent someone up pretty quickly to fix it. The bathroom door was broken and the ceiling was molding with parts of it falling down. I was afraid to put the kids down on the floor because it was dirty. The nice cheese plate that was advertised when I booked the room online was obviously on the fridge too long - the nuts were mushy!! This experience is not what I have come to expect from embassy suites!

title: “Without Hesitation - Five out of Five”
text:
I had read a lot of bad reviews in advance, and was pleasantly surprised as the hotel exceeded my expectations! 
It is true that there is quite a lot of commotion going on on the weekends (not my kind of crowd I must admit) and it can get loud in the lobby, however, our room was on the fifth floor and we had no noise problem whatsoever. If you want to make absolutely sure that you are not bothered by the noise from below, I suggest you ask for a room above the fourth floor.
I must admit, we never used the pool as it was, I think it's primary purpose is not for people to swim in but is rather used on the weekends for the previously mentioned parties as it is adjacent to the hotel bar. 
We had one minor hiccup which we sorted out very quickly. When we entered the room there was no safe. We phoned the reception desk and fifteen minutes later a janitor knocked on our door to replace it. That was that :)
The staff was very nice and to our surprise ordered us a limousine to the airport on our departure for the price of a normal cab :) that was a great experience! 
Maybe we are not very demanding travelers, but we had an amazing stay at the Room Mate Grace!
Oh, and the beds are super comfy!

title: “Clean & Efficient in a Perfect Location”
text: If you are looking for a basic hotel that is clean and located within walking distance to Union Square and public transportation, this is it. We had a King Suite on the top floor for a week and the entire bill with taxes and fees was less than $500. The staff was friendly, the suite was cleaned everyday (regardless of what time we left the room) and there was a safe to keep valuables secure. When we had problems with the cable in the bedroom and with one of our room keys not working upon check-in, the issues were resolved promptly and professionally. We will definitely stay here again and will recommend it. It is an easy subway ride to the Castro and close to the Powell cable car for your trip to the wharf. It is also close to BART for the sad day that you have to leave this remarkable city.

title: “Hotel Mela was wonderful!”
text: We went into NYC for a show and booked through Hotwire, for the first time. We were skeptical because the rate was so reasonable, but the reviews were so good we just had to go for it. We are so happy we did. The hotel is intimate, squeaky clean, and the staff could not have been friendlier or more helpful. We love going to New York on special occasions and seeing the Broadway shows, and are so happy we have found such a great new place to stay.

title: “Its an older hotel but its roomy and spacious at a good price.”
text:
The staff was very polite and helpful. We took advantage of the late check out at 2pm. We got this deal for a Saturday night stay for $88. It included a breakfast for two in the morning that would have been $30. The chef for the breakfast was really cool and made me a customized waffle and omelet. 
 Didnt really have too many complaints but it is an older hotel so the bathroom faucet wasn't in the best shape.
 Overall the value for what you pay is great and for that i would definitely come back.

title: “Very Disappointed in service of an airport hotel”
text: I recently stayed at the hotel as I had a one night layover before heading back to Atlanta. I asked if the hotel had a shuttle to and from the airport and the concierge said yes prior to me booking. Since I was literally just staying at the hotel for the use of a bed and shower with a quick layover, price and comfort was important.. I arrived into Dallas, TX at around 11:20pm to find out that the hotel stopped shuttle service at 11pm and to pay a $24 cab ride to go 2 miles to the hotel. To make matters worse, when I checked in, I found out that the shuttle to the airport only runs once every hour at the top of the hour. Well since my flight was at 8:55am I had to catch the 7am shuttle along with miss the free continental breakfast which started at 7am - What kind of service is this for an airport hotel when there are tons of hotels to choose from? Unhappy guest...

title: “Very expensive, but charming!”
text: I extended my business travel and my husband joined me for a long weekend. The staff are very professional and helpful. Like others said, location is everything. We returned the rental car as it wasn't needed at all - and parking was $46 per day. We did the hop-on/hop-off trolley and saw the sites over 3 days' time. It really wasn't enough to absorb this beautiful and historical city! Access to the concierge lounge was so worth it! We asked for a small refrigerator in our room so we could store water and some food -- we had just come from a Residence Inn so we had quite a bit that we didn't want to throw out. They brought up the crudiest looking thing and stuck it right in the middle of our entrance/foyer - LOL. (We moved it.) There is a "cooler" in each room (not really a fridge) which is a nice touch. Our bed was a bit lumpy, but the linens were luxurious. We were in room 165 and had a front-row seat to the busy sidewalks (fun people-watching) and the beautiful skyline! Our housekeeper was the best! We tipped her well and she gave us extra chocolates and towels! Breakfast on Saturday was $50 for 2 for the buffet - very good food but a bit expensive.

title: “Great place!”
text:
Stayed at The Lucerne in September for 4 nights. Quiet hotel, but excellent location, Just out of the bussle and noise of the city, but right next door to a subway station, and a short walk to anything you could possibly need. Cannot recommend this hotel enough, the staff were helpful but did not interfere unless you needed them. 
The rooms were of a decent size, not bad for NYC, nice decor, and free wireless, and flat screen TV. Stayed in a Queen room and found it to be big enough for two people. Very clean, and maids did a good job every day. Free news paper every morning too. 
Great place, nice location, clean, friendly, and a definite recommendation! Will be going again, and have recommended to all my friends and family.

title: “Orlando Hotel, LA's "in-the-know" secret boutique hotel.”
text:
I have stayed here and my parents have stayed here. It is in a great location. It is a chic, understated boutique hotel. It is LA's "in-the-know" secret boutique hotel.
Service was excellent. Nicole at the front desk was very friendly. I like the design and the restaurant has 1/2 orders of pasta. It is down the street from Joan's on Third (which is a paparazzi-looking-to-snap-a-celebrity photo), which is one of LA's best cafes. It is also close to Robertson Blvd, Beverly Hills, Beverly Center Shopping Mall and other chic destinations. 
I wish I could have a permanent room here.

title: “don't do it”
text: location is nice but goes from bad to worse once you walk through the door. staff very surly and unhelpful. tried to charge me $100 more per night than confirmed in writing. room and hallway had a very strange smell. rooms very run down. so bad that i checked out immediately and went to another hotel. intercontinental chain should be ashamed.

title: “Game was awful, hotel was okay”
text:
Drove to Charlotte with a friend to see the Colts/Panthers game last fall and stayed overnight at the Hilton when Priceline picked it for us.
It was pretty good. There was a pool and a decent workout gym. Everything was clean and the people were friendly. When we checked in they told us to sign up for the Honors rewards program. I just got my statement that's what made me think to post.
That night we walked to Tryon Street and found lots to do. And we had a decent breakfast in the hotel the next morning.
A good nights stay. I don't know if I'd pay full price to stay there again, but only because I don't need anything that fancy.

title: “Overall positive experience”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 1 night while passing through Baltimore. As some other reviewers stated, the hotel is not new. While I wouldn't call it "old," I would say that a renovation should be in it's near future. 
We had a room with a king-sized bed and fantastic view of the inner harbor, the window was huge and we could see the whole harbor/waterfront. 
PROS: quick check-in, clean room, nice linens, flat panel TV
CONS: expensive valet parking, older hotel - could use a renovation 
SIDE NOTE: We booked through our american express card and dinner & breakfast was included. For dinner - by the time we paid for tax, tip and drinks we felt that we should have just eaten where we wanted because the hotel restaurant is totally dead and awkwardly quiet. The food was ok, but we could have spent a few more bucks and eaten at a place of our choice in the harbor. The breakfast worked out well because they allow you to order room service and the room had a nice dining table and we were able to enjoy our view of the harbor.

title: “Fabulous location, stunning hotel”
text:
Excellent location, right off Times Square. Staff friendly and helpful. They upgraded us to a bigger room which was fantastic except it was a smoker's room. There's an ATM on the second floor and a mini gym, but let's be honest - who's going to the gym when there's the whole of the city to see!
Decor was modern and the king bed extremely comfortable.
Definitely make time to go to Magnolia bakery on Bleecker Str for their cupcakes and The Plaza for a glass of bubbly on a rainy day

title: “Stay at Affinia !!!”
text:
Just back with my girlfriend from a 3 night stay at the Affinia Manhattan. This Hotel is the place to be! Trust me! We stayed on the 24th floor our view was to the rear of the building which wasnt great but still provided views over the city. We booked a studio room, large bedroom area, small kitchen and small bathroom! room was clean, spacious, and serviced every day. Ironing board and iron are provided as well as a safety deposit box. We were worried about location, but this was ideal. You will be almost central for everything. Times Square 8-10 minute walk. Broadway 5mins, Macy's 2mins, empire state 5mins, central park 20mins, madison square garden - you look at it! We walked to ground zero taking in the sights right down 7th avenue, went to statue of liberty, then walked back up broadway towards the hotel, you see all you need to see, and it keeps you fit. Penn station is also facing you, this is great if you arrive at newark airport as you can grab a train which transfers you in 20 mins.
Never took a taxi or used the subway once!!!!
Friendly staff add to this classy hotel, in midtown new york.

title: “Good Location; Rooms Ordinary”
text: The JW Marriott has a good location and a friendly, knowlegeable and helpful staff. The rooms are ordinary and not as well appointed as one would have expected for the price class. Everything worked but it was starting to get a little bit shappy and worn around the edges. The room was quiet and I could get a good night's sleep for the three night's I was there to attend a convention. I think better values could be had in DC.

title: “Great Location”
text:
My first time staying at this Towne Place Suites Hotel Gahanna was for four nights. I was in the Columbus area for a show at Ohio Expo Center/Fair Grounds. Driving time was about ten minutes between the Fair Grounds and the Hotel. I liked the location of this property in Gahanna. It is close to a Krogers Supermarket, Gas Station. and numerous Plazas and Restaurants on nearby North Hamilton Road. Easy access to Downtown Columbus, Easton Town Center Mall, and Columbus International Airport,
I stayed in a 2 bedroom Suite with my family. The room was Good space wise. This is a traditional room/building layout in which You would find at most Towneplace Suites. Two Bedroom suites are at both ends of a hallway on each floor. Hotel has two buildings separated by a parking lot. There is an outdoor pool near the lobby.
The Front Desk Staff was very friendly and helpful with directions, information, and reccomendations of restaurants and nearby Columbus attractions ie: Columbus Zoo-Fantastic!!! Housekeeping also turned out to be a positive. Housekeepers were very nice and accomodating while providing extra towels, pots and pans, paper towels, and coffee filters when we needed them, we did ask for extra. Our Housekeeper made it a point, personally to see if we were content or needed more of anything during our four night stay. She even offered to help assist us with our luggage/cart at check out. 
Good stay Overall. I would definitely stay here again. Family Friendly and Attentive.

title: “Will stay again & again!!”
text: This hotel was wonderful. It was clean, safe & in a great location. My husband said he had the best breakfast in his life at the Serafina. Staff was freindle except the girl when we checked in. Will stay again.

title: “Outstanding!!!”
text: Without a doubt the friendliest and best hotel I have stayed in within the US!! Welcome was warm and helpful and the room was fantastic. Breakfasts were very good and we especially enjoyed the complimentary coffee, pastries, and fruit throuhout the day. All the staff were absolutely fantastic and were super polite and helpful at all times. I couldn't recommend this hotel more and we will definitely be coming back soon with my children in tow!!! Stayed here Feb 2012

title: “Great bargain - good location - little noisy”
text: Stayed at the Baldwin first week of Nov '09 for two short visits. Rooms were spacious meticulously clean and good beds (we had two queens). Only problem was the temporary construction going on next door and the mid-night garbage pickups. After a tour of Big Sur we returned for a night prior to our departure back home. Very good for a bargain stay.

title: “Great for the price”
text: For 50$ a night (from priceline.com), this was a real bargain. Yes, we got a small lousy room near the ice machine. Yes, the air conditioning made the noise of an idling truck. However, it was not hot, so we turned it off. The bathroom is very small, with little counter space, but everything was very clean and in working order (even the kind-of-hard-to-figure-out coffee machine). The hotel has a pool and an adequate fitness center. Even next to the ice machine the hotel itself was quiet. Overall, for the price, quite a bargain. For the standard rate of 134$ a night, I would have been quite unhappy. Self-parking was extra, but at 14$ a day it wasn't too bad. The hotel has access to one of the extremes of the Riverwalk (which is currently being expanded), so if you are tired of walking and don't mind waiting forever, you can get there by watertaxi.

title: “Did not live up to agreement”
text: Offered airport shuttle, but none was available to take me to the airport, Promised they'd be there to pick me up, Did not show up, finally told me to take a shuttle. The room reeked of smoke so much that when I got to my destination, friends could smell smoke on my clothes.. When I complained the manager just said sorry.

title: “Embarrassing”
text: I have never been more embarrassed on a trip with my fiancé. I unfortunately choose this hotel because in the past Holiday Inn has offered a consistent product. This hotel is clean and crisp. No complaints for housekeeping. Great job. The breakfast staff was also very friendly. The front desk employees are miserable, have attitudes and blatantly made a comment about me and laughed one night as I rode down the escalator. I guess no one ever told them that they are the first and last encounter with their guests. My key card did not work three times and I had to go back to the desk to get another. Saturday night after getting back late from a night out so ready to get into the room the key wasnt working. The lady at the desk was polite, so thank you to the lady with the awesome nails! You turned a frown upside down. The third time it happened the women sent up a man to check my ID in the room. 0 privacy at this hotel. This morning the front desk was the rudest I have ever came across. Do you even want to be working here? My fiance is currently in the shower and I am laying in this bed. Annoyed I was offered nothing in return. I have worked and lived in a hotel for the last three years and I have never seen a guest have to come reset their key three times in a 2 night stay. I would not stay at this hotel if you are service oriented.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: Stayed for five days in August and couldnt have been happier. Requested a top floor and was given the 29th floor with a great view. staff at check in was very friendly. room was small, but isn't that what is expected in new york? best thing of all: location location location! in the middle of the best shopping, down the street from the empire state building and a 2 avenue blocks from times square. Would stay here again.

title: “Good price, good location....”
text:
Good value for the money and an excellent location.
Above the 7th Ave subway (23rd st) for the 1,2,3 & 9 lines. One block either way to the V & F or A,C & E lines.
Quiet neighbourhood.

title: “SUPRISINGLY PLEASANT :)”
text:
Stayed here with my wife and 1year old son, along with my sister-in-law this past January. I've been meaning to write a review but it just dawned on me two weeks ago when I stay in SF again but this time my sister-in-law book a different hotel which will remain nameless but I can tell u that it had more stars then the Inn on Broadway. For that very reason, I leave a positive review for The Inn on Broadway because for the price, the courtesy, the cleanliness, location and surprisingly the parking was beyond exceptionally accommodating. 
To be honest with you, this is the first place from now on that I’ll look for an availability….I’m from San Diego, CA and just writing this review makes me wish I could visit again.

title: “Great service!”
text: The best part of the Warwick is the service! Very helpful and quick with absolutely anything you need.

title: “Great hotel but lots of large groups of school children”
text: We really enjoyed our stay at the Hampton Inn. It's a great location and a good price. There was a large hot/cold breakfast that changed daily. We walked everywhere! There were also many restaurants nearby for lunch and dinner. The National Mall and other attractions are all nearby. The only draw backs for us were that this hotel seems to cater to large groups of school children so the pool area, lobby area and breakfast area were over-run at times and very busy! That being said there was never a shortage of anything at breakfast and the breakfast staff are very friendly. Next time we would stay on a floor away from the pool. Short taxi to Reagan Airport but Dulles International was over $80 by taxi. For the subway either get off in Chinatown or Convention Center.

title: “Nice hotel in good location”
text: We stayed here twice in September '08 with a couple of weeks inbetween. Both rooms were pleasant and had views of the Empire State Building. The first had a nice new flatscreen TV. The location of this hotel is one of its strongpoints. We were able to walk to Time Square and the theatre district and the nearest subway was only a few blocks away. One downside, though, was that we had to pay for use of the Internet PC.

title: “Huge hotel with service of à 'hotel de charme'”
text:
Perfect service (Thanks Amanda for all hour help)
Friendly staff
Nice and clean rooms
Great fitness and pool
Good location
Great lounge
We will come back!

title: “Was surprised how good it was.”
text:
I had to be in Chicago for a conference. Most of the hotels were sold out and we ended up at the Hard Rock hotel. I am a member of the Starwood/Hilton program, I didnt expect much as I have no 'status' here. I was happy to receive good service from the front desk staff. The room was clean and modern and bed was comfortable. I liked the location, close to a Walgreen (or was it RiteAid) and Starbucks. I did eat at the Restaurant once for Breakfast but would rather eat at Starbucks which I did the rest of the time. 
In the end, I would stay here again.

title: “Tired, tiny and smelly pillows”
text:
This may be the straw that breaks my SPG habit, or at least, it will be the last of my Sheraton stays in the US. 
Have enjoyed great stays in S America and other places, but this tired and somewhat dumpy hotel doesn't deserve to be a category 3 much less a category 4. 
Have a tiny room, the pillows smell like they've been stuck up someone's armpit, and a view overlooks the parking lot. No wireless in the room (Club room). But, at least, I'm not getting calls and voicemails every couple of hours to buy into a timeshare, so this is an improvement over my end of the year Orlando stay.

title: “great hotel for conference attendees”
text: It's a very large hotel & gets really busy during conferences. The guest rooms are well appointed and conference halls are very good. The lobby is grand and warm. It's very close to the convention center. The only disappointment is getting restaurants in nearby area. Sally's is not sufficient as you need prior reservation.

title: “MASSIVE room, great location, cheap price”
text:
First of all, the room was absolutely massive. It had a kitchen, dining area, study desk, sofa and 40" tv in one room, leading through into a really decent sized bedroom with two double beds. Each room had separate, albeit somewhat noisy, air con. The street noise was noticeable but nothing that stopped us from having a good night's sleep. The room was spotless and was cleaned everyday.
The location of the hotel is great for the main sites - about 15min walk to Times Sq and a stones throw from central park and Trump Tower on 5th Avenue. We walked to the Empire State and Macy's aswell. Tube station at the end of the street so real easy to get to downtown Manhatten.
A lot of shops, cafes and eateries near by - we didn't struggle for food! 
Overall a great break

title: “Great place, great location”
text:
Stayed here because this hotel was much cheaper than the Sheraton where the conference
was I was attending. Turned out to be a great decision. The rooms are as nice as in any four star hotel and you have free internet, free breakfast and free wine reception at night. Check out time is too early though, 11 am and gym was not airconditioned enough, but other than that, this place was fantastic.

title: “Elegant and spacious grand hotel”
text: Loved the location and elegant foyer which has been used in a few movies! Even with the least expensive room had lots of space in room, 2 windows and big bathroom. Had in room monitor and key board--little pricey to use but better thatn hauling a computer when leisure travelling. Ate in hotel's Pub friendly group and staff. Did not use their parking found cheaper choices nearby. Little restaurants and cafes in the area are safe easy walk.

title: “Solid, Great Location, Very Good Service”
text: The Hilton Suites on the Magnificent Mile is a solid, very good hotel. There is nothing flashy or “boutique-like” here. The hotel is outfitted with your standard, run-of-the-mill Hilton hotel interiors, business center, and pool / gym. However, what makes this hotel desirable is its ideal location, room size, and being an all “suite” hotel, the bedroom is separate, and closed off by solid doors from the rest of the room. You can count on a quiet, good night’s sleep here. The service is also very good here. The staff are pleasant and responsive. Worth mentioning also are the pool and gym, which are located at the top of the property with commanding views of Lake Michigan and downtown Chicago. Also, the hotel seems to fill up with families and children on the weekends … fortunately, we didn’t have to deal with early morning, residual hallway noise since the bedroom was separate and an ample distance from the hotel door.

title: “Great Hotel with Superior Service”
text: Superior customer service started from the minute we walked in the door. Michael brought us a drink and checked us in. The lobby is beautiful and there was a good vibe about the hotel. The rooms were modern and the rain shower was fantastic. As other reviewers have mentioned - the free (non-alcoholic) drinks in the bar fridge were a great touch as well as the breakfast bar/coffee bar which was available all day. In fact - I quickly became addicted to the lattes which were served. I would highly recommend this hotel to almost anyone looking to stay south of midtown. The only reason its not a 5 star is the location (for me anyway) - we found it a bit difficult to get cabs during the week around rush hour.

title: “Exceeded all expectations”
text: I have stayed in other Fairfield Inn hotels and are just good, not great, so I didn't expect much from this one. Since my arrival was pleasantly surprised! Lobby looks good, rooms are bigger than many more expensive hotels in New York, brand new rooms, good furniture, very comfortable bed, great bathroom. I got city view room and it was very nice, looking at the Empire State building. Breakfast is very basic, neighborhood is very quiet, located in a flower shop street, there is a subway station at the corner. And the price (at least the one I got) was amazing. Strongly recommend the hotel!

title: “By far the best”
text:
I stayed in the Smyth Tribeca in April 2012, The hotel itself is fantastic: Very Clean, spacious and Trendy! It is also in a great spot, right beside ground Zero, and a short bus ride to Times Sq. The staff were what really stood out, they were exceptional some of the best I have ever seen, without being overpowering. ( A shout out to Ella the concierge you were fab!) The management team of this hotel are obviously doing a great job. Having stayed in various NY Hotels in the past, including the Waldorf Astoria, If I was to return I would definetly book the Smyth Tribeca!
Thanks to All the staff, Keep doing what your doing!
Justine & Family

title: “Perfect!”
text: Let me just say, I love this Hilton location. It is located directly across from Camden Stadium and is surrounded by lots of food and entertainment venues. The location couldn't be better. I've only stayed at the Hilton Baltimore for business, but I would stay with my family as well. The rooms are beautiful and clean. Service is impeccable. I will continue to stay at this hotel during my visits to Baltimore.

title: “Perfect!”
