text: Our room was great. We booked the double deluxe for a mother/daughter trip for two teenage girls and their moms and it was quite spacious. So go for the deluxe, skip the cozy, no brainer!!!!. After reading the reviews we were nervous about the room being too small and not clean. No need to worry at all. It was fabulous. The lobby is breathtaking. The rooms do need some updating but ours was fine. We even had a large walk in closet to use as a changing room. I have no complaints at all with the bathroom or the beautiful comfortable bed. The staff, especially the concierge origianlly from FallRiver and the doorman Bernard were super helpful!! !We even got a late check out with no issue at all. Location is great, not on top of Times Square or the shows but close, although after walking all day it can seem far! We really got a great deal for this room and it was perfect. Don't believe the bad reviews. We were concerned and I would return tomorrow and recommend to friends!

title: “Great Accomodation”
text:
Stayed at the Sommerset Suites for 5 nights and experienced a pleasant stay. It wasn't anything fancy or memorable but good for what they offer. Here are the highlights:
Pros:
- Early Check in Available if you ask kindly at the front desdk ;)
- Free continental breakfast (includes waffles and hard boiled eggs which usually are not found in places with continental breakfasts)*
- Free Wifi*
- Free local calling*
- Patio or balcony in room with patio furniture
- Very comfortable beds
- Walking distance to restuarants, shops and bus stops
- Very helpful and cheerful staff
- Free Pool, computer in the lobby
- Complete kitchen with utensils, dishwasher, appliances (but no soap to wash anything with)
Cons
- Can get noisy as the hotel is close to many hospitals in the area
- breakfast lady always hovering around in the breakfast room waiting for tips (most of the time she just stood there doing nothing but reading a newspaper)
- Can be tricky to find the hotel entrance, especially when driving in for the first time
- Water pressure can be an issue and the water in general coming from the pipes have a foul odour and taste bad (use bottled water for drinking).
- $6 for parking per night, hoever this is cheaper than most hotels.*
That's it in a nutshell. The con's are not all that bad except for maybe the water issue, but I am not very picky as I'm sure it is safe to use the water in San Diego regardless of smell and taste. 
Any ones I marked with a "*" indicate that this hotel is one of only a few in the city that offer this amenity (in the same price range) as I looked all around specifically for these amenities in the city. All other hotels in the same price range charge for these amenities or are more expensive (specifically price of parking).

title: “Nice hotel... a little impersonal”
text: Having come from Casablanca Hotel we were a little disappointed in Hotel Giraffe. The staff are not as friendly, had more of a corporate feel than a friendly welcoming one. The room – a one bedroom suite – was nice... but the bathroom was small and with the sofa bed down for the 3rd guest - there was little room to move in the ‘lounge area’. The wine and cheese is a nice touch but as we had a beer drinker amongst us we went instead to the bar where prices were on the expensive side, and the staff were indifferent. We could see the appeal of this place and it suited our needs but our view of it was affected by our stay at the far superior Casablanca.

title: “Disappointing”
text: We arrived on a rainy sunday afternoon. We expected the bellman to help with bags but with the rain everyone was inside, so my boyfriend had to bring all of the bags in on his own. We did opt for an early check-in. They gave us a room that wasnt ready. We walk in covers were tossed, towels on the floor, and the tv was still on. The hotel staff didnt even apologize, just gave us another room and sent us on our way. Through-out our stay if felt like we were doing everything on our own, opening our own doors, hailing our own cabs. We expected five star treatment because we seen other couples and guest receiving that kind of treatment. We were just disappointed with the hotel staff.

title: “Beyond Luxury, People!”
text:
The Joule is touted as a luxury property. I would say for us, it was beyond luxury! I've stayed in numerous properties of this caliber over the last 25 years on business so I know what I'm talking about. On this occasion however, I went for pleasure. We were greeted at the curb by 3 very friendly bell staff. In less than 30 seconds we were unloaded, vehicle whisked away for parking. We walked to the front desk and were promptly greeted by name, wished a happy anniversary complete with a champagne toast and our room keys. Dinner at Charlie Palmer's was terrific and it finished with an anniversary card of sorts with a message spelled in chocolate at the top of our unbelievably rich Peanut Butter Bar - which btw, was practically a religious experience!
The concierge drove us herself to the symphony when it was apparent that there was a traffic snafu that could render us late. Upon our return our suite was adorned with rose petals, chilled champagne and a basket of fruit. 
Loved. the. shower. 
All of the staff appeared to really like their jobs. It was more than your usual hotel staff friendliness, it was an attitude of liking what they did.
The only down-side for us (because we're not as young as we used to be) was the night life (we were there on a Friday night) on the street kicks in at about midnight and continues with great enthusiasm until about 4am. Had we been paying attention though, we could have asked for a room on the back side of the hotel when we made our reservation.
Would I recommend the Joule to others? Well the fact that 3 days later I was wishing I was there again should answer the question. YES! Great property in a downtown location.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Very nice hotel. Everyone was friendly and helpful. Right off the subway so that was convenient. The carpet was a little dated but the comfortable bed made it very enjoyable.

title: “Great Hotel in a Great Location with Great Vibe”
text: Two friends and I chose to stay at The Maxwell Hotel last weekend, in large part to the excellent reviews, and we were not disappointed. The staff was friendly and courteous, and even upgraded our room upon arrival. Our room, as well as the rest of the hotel, was clean and nicely decorated. Although, not in the center of downtown, we loved the location. The hotel is located on a fairly quiet street just north of Seattle Center. We were able to walk everywhere we wanted to go and we were able to take public transportation to and from the airport (with about a half of a mile or so walk from the Seattle Center Monorail). I don't think any of our destinations was further than 2 miles (most were under 1.5). This hotel just has a great vibe and was the perfect place to begin and end our sightseeing days.

title: “Fabulous-ity”
text: After reading all the negative reviews on the Waldorf, I was really expecting a bad experience. Much to my pleasant surpise, it was fabulous. The location cannot be beaten, our room was very well proportioned, bathroom was upgraded, check-in was quick and easy. Fresh flowers abound. When one walks through the tiled lobby the scent of lilacs permeates the air. I must say that every single person we dealt with, from check-in to concierge to customer service reps, (who are roaming the floor offering help and guidance) was 5 star. I would add that I got a special price after perusing the internet which made all the difference. For the price, fabulous! Did I mention it was fabulous?

title: “Great Hotel A+”
text: Beautiful Hotel at five minutes of Time Square and a very good and friendly staff ! Room very clean with air conditionner (maybe little but ok for 2 persons who visiting the city) ! The only bad thing is the price for eating and drinking there but we find a very good little restaurant (named The Red Flame) beside of the hotel (Breakfast , Dinner and Supper) for a very good price !

title: “Fantastic Stay!”
text: We just returned from a four day stay at the DoubleTree. Front desk staff were great. Breakfast was good and comped as Diamonds, Mo took care of every morning. The rooms were spacious and quiet except for traffic noise. All the staff was very personable!

title: “Nice sheets, shame about everything else !!!”
text:
I've stayed in some hotels around the world and never have I felt compelled to leave a negative review !!!
When paying this kid of money (ok we are not talking mega bucks, but budget it is not) you expect certain things, Politeness and courtesy being one of them. (some of the front desk staff, may be your buff disinterested, and cold manner has been developed by too many complaining unhappy guests)
1. No safe in room (can't remember the last time that happened)
2. No offer of bags being taken to room.
3. Appalling in room refreshments etc.
4. General lack of amenities at hotel 
5. Drinks vending machine on 12th floor the only way of getting a drink other than water or coffee from the room.
This is basically a hotel to catch the unaware, promises of sumptuous rooms, plasma TV etc, to catch their trade. Upon arrival you will realise these things are very superficial, and the true nature of this hotel is revealed.
We had to stay an extra night in New York very unexpectedly, and booked into a budget hotel at the last minute out of necessity, then wished we had been there all week !!!
Do your self a favour, and pass this one by !!!

title: “Good location in midtown but needs some renovation”
text:
The hotel was well located near Central Park and had good access to Times Square and Midtown. Its right next to Radio City, MOMA and the 6th Avenue Financial District. The room had a nice big flat screen TV but because the hotel is very popular there is some wear and tear visible all over the hotel. 
When I checked out I was shocked that for $3.50 per item they would keep luggage in a separate area of the lobby. I had a 30 minute wait between checking out at midday and my car to the airport and they charged me for keeping my case. I have never been to a hotel where they charge for keeping luggage and I was very disappointed they did.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: We could only enjoy this unique hotel for 1 night, before flying home after a 2 week vacation around the Pacific Northwest. Very clean, comfortable rooms, with the best bed we've ever slept in at any hotel. Upgrade to a premier room, if available. You won't regret it!

title: “Great Location and Very Good Value”
text: We very much enjoyed our stay. The location is perfect, the rooms were clean as well as the entire hotel. I highly recommend this property. It's a great value too! Vivvian at the front desk was exceptional. Check out the "burger place" down teh hallway behind the front desk. We'll definitly book again.

title: “Best place to stay in NYC”
text:
I stay at the Sanctuary Hotel every time I visit mid-town NYC.
I have not found a better mid-town hotel in a convenient yet quiet location, great design, well appointed rooms, recently refurbished, very clean, and staff who are very friendly and helpful from the front door, to the hotel desk, concierge, bar keeper, and management team.
The rates are very competitive and the standard rooms are of a very reasonable size by NYC standards; after all you won't be spending much time in your room anyway. The Deluxe Queen and King Rooms have even more floor space.

title: “Excellent hotel in good location!”
text: New York is far from a cheap place to stay, but the Salisbury offered a reasonably priced suite of rooms bang in the middle of Manhattan. For about £175 per night, the suite was a good size - one large double bedroom and a similarly large lounge area - the sofa converting into a pull out double bed which provided ample sleeping space for the kids. The bathroom comes off the bedroom and there is a small kitchen area (pretty basic - microwave, fridge and coffee maker and no pots and pans) so we could grab a quick coffee and bite to eat without hitting the streets. The staff were very friendly and professional all round. The hotel was clean and largely in good order - the bathroom was a bit dated but lounge and bed room came with flat screen TVs. A few scuffs on the paintwork but nothing major. You can get a hearty continental breakfast in the morning for only $4 which is great value - eggs, breads and pastries, cereal, coffee and juice - and the staff aren't overly military if you leave the dining area with an extra muffin. Location was great - not far from the subway and a 20 minute walk from Times Square. All in all, a great find.

title: “recommended”
text:
well placed on the 16th, roomy and spacy. quiet room. staff friendly and professional. closed from restaurant on the 17th and 14th. 
needs 7 minutes walking to a subway station or bus line to Georgestown.

title: “Nice rooms, friendly staff"”
text:
Location was pretty good, especially if you want to go to Old Town. It is, however, on the side of a major highway, which is odd... but worked out for me because it was easy access to the highway so we could go to the zoo and such. 
 The staff is incredibly friendly and helpful. If you are planing on going to the zoo or other attractions, you can buy your tickets at the check in desk for a discounted price!!!
 Upon check-in, I got a very nice up-grade for a good deal.. and they were willing to haggle a bit :) Free breakfast was so-so, but hey.. it was free.
 The rooms were nice and clean... highly recommended!

title: “Speechless!”
text: Wow, what can I say about this place?! Well first, the architecture of the building is absolutely breathtaking. My husband and I arrived on a Sunday, at 12:30 pm hoping to check into our room early. Once we were at reception, I thought I might ask if they could upgrade us to a corner balcony room. Jaime was assisting us and he was able to get us the exact room we wanted. I absolutely loved his eagerness to help make our stay fantastic. Once in our room, we danced around like giddy kids with the beautiful view of the park below and Navy Pier. We spent a good hour admiring the views from our balcony. We went down to Fillini to have a few cocktails and some appetizers. Our waitress was attentive to our needs. My husband was immediately impressed when he ordered his first drink, a bloody Mary, and removed the olives because he doesn't like them. When she brought him a second, there were no olives in his drink for him to remove. We were immensely impressed with this hotel and are looking to come back in November for my birthday. We could not have been more pleased. I will recommend this hotel and restaurant to everyone I meet!!!

title: “Loved the Hilton Los Angeles”
text:
I spent just one day in July at the Hilton Los Angeles on my way back to the east coast. I have stayed there before, and the service was just as excellent as always. Check-in is quick, they arrange for your parking lot ticket, and then I am off to a great room. 
It is close to LAX and the rental car locations, so I can drop off my car the night before and take the hotel shuttle. The staff is friendly and helpful from the doorman to the check in to the shuttle diver. 
They have several choices off the lobby to eat and drink. The Hilton has the best variety of all the hotels near LAX. 
I use the shuttle to go to the airport. I do not remember a driver that was a pleasant and worked to help everyone with their luggage and make sure they got off at the right stop. I know it is hard to stand out as a shuttle driver, but this person did. The attitude of all the staff is just great.
In my travels I stay at a lot of hotels, and I look forward to my stay at the Hilton. The staff is great, the rooms are always clean and comfortable, there a lots of choices to eat and drink, and the internet access works every time.
I highly recommend the Hilton when you are in Los Angeles.

title: “Beware of staff”
text:
Worst hotel yet that i have stayed when in San Diego. Locks on door always broken, maintenance never got around to fixing. Horrible maintenance service.
 Someone came in room when we were gone & also at night when we were asleep since the door would not overlock. Riffled through our things steeling money out of our pants pockets. Overcharged on room & never deducted the full amount overcharged.

title: “Nice hotel”
text:
I parked in front of the hotel and I noticed that they had valet parking, which price was quite steep. The valet parking was almost 20 dollar more expensive than all the other places that I had used before but I decided to use it anyway as I just wanted to get in and relax. The price was 47 dollar a night, so you can say that it was paid.
I was quite surprised when I saw the hotel from the outside as the hotel looked really huge and it not something that I had expected. The valet guys were all over me when I arrived at the hotel and I took out my stuff and gave them the car keys and went to the reception inside.
The lounge area in front of the reception was quite full of people but it was also quite small compared to the huge hotel. The reception was two small desks with a girl sitting behind in an office chair. My receptionist found my booking quite fast and I was given a room on second floor, which I was okay with. 
My room was quite nice and I especially liked my bed. It was large and pretty high, which is a fact that I like because beds in European hotels are usually quite low. The room was really bright and the Wi-Fi worked quite well. The bathroom was nice and I liked my room a lot.

title: “Good location, service and price”
text: We stayed here while vising San Diago. This hotel fits our budget and it was a decent place to stay. The staff was friendly, helpful. Room was clean and comfortable. Good location if you want to see Seaworld, town or beaches.

title: “Location, location, location - and friendliness”
text:
New York is notorious for expensive hotels, so it`s a joy to find one that meets most criteria, at an affordable price. And in a great spot, on the corner of the lively Washington Square, with chess players, dogs, elegant bag ladies and everything else. Easy access to the metro, and lots of interesting sights within walking distance. 
One of the things that made us fall in love with the hotel, was the extreme friendliness of all the staff. Big smiles, real interest in us and willingness to help is something that is definitely not found everywhere, especially not in big city hotels.
The restaurant serves lovely food at night, and the breakfast is good and copious.
The rooms are on the smallish side, but it works for couples and good friends. Nicely outfitted, and kept clean and tidy.
There are quite a few good restaurants in the area, a big plus point for the hotel is the Italian restaurant Babbo just across the street. A great place to eat, reservations necessary, but we actually got a table for the same evening on a Sunday...
We would very much like to come back to this hotel.

title: “Credit for the concierge”
text:
On new year's eve BA flight to London was cancelled due to fog. We stayed the night and most of next day in the WESTIN. I wish to give credit to THI NGUYEN, the concierge who handled us, a group of stranded passengers, for the whole time there, with patience and grace
And did not leave us with unanswered questions. She really did a very good job !!

title: “Best location in Boston!”
text:
Recenlty stayed at the Marriott Long Wharf. Great location for sure. Close to everything. Easily walk to Freedom trail, norh side, Fanuil hall, etc. Duck boat tour also departs across the street. Many ferries arrive and depart so there is a lot of action in the area. 
As far as the hotel goes, it is nice and clean. Rooms are a bit cramped especially when there is a rollaway in the room. Never waited long for elevator. Pool is very nice. The restaurant bar is also very nice. Many local beers on tap and strong pours for mixed drinks. 
Would be first choice when staying in Boston again.

title: “Our stay at the James”
text: We stayed at the James last month while visiting NY. and we experienced the total package. Our room was upgraded, the service was wonderful, and the location perfect! The staff was devoted to making our stay memorable and the room was exceptional in size and comfort. We almost stayed at the Mondrian, but I am glad I went with my gut and chose the James...a little oasis in Soho. I am looking forward to our next trip at our home away from home.

title: “Hotel pennsylvania is not as bad as people are saying it is”
text: We have just returned from a 6 day stay in New York. We were a group of 8 people and after reading the reviews we were somewhat apprehensive about the hotel. The location is great, convenient to everything you will want to see.The room we had was huge O K it could do with a bit of a makeover but on the whole it wasent that bad.One of the joys of the hotel it is smack next door to a wonderful coffee and doughnut kiosk so we were able to have a wonderful coffee and fresh doughnut every morning before we went on our way to do some sightseeing. [ and only for 2 dollars ] My daughter is planning to go to New York next year and I have told her to go to Hotel Pennsylvania as a rule you only spend the night there. By the way the young man in the luggage hold dept is a pure joy...helpful..happy.. We couldnt ask for more Give Hotel Penn a try and judge for yourself.

title: “Highly Recommend”
text: We booked this through ClubCorp recently, had never stayed at this hotel. It is in a perfect location for the River Walk, close to Dick's Last Resort, Landry's. Hard Rock, County Line, etc. We were not disappointed, it was a very nice hotel....clean and quite. I saw someone made a negative post about the parking, the parking is going to be pretty much the same at any hotel you stay at on the River Walk.

title: “Great Hotel; Great Location”
text: Rooms are spacious. Staff is very friendly and works really hard to make you comfortable. Location is terrific - restaurants, bakery, shopping and sight seeing all within walking distance.

title: “Excellent Choice”
text:
I should have posted my review on this hotel a long time ago. I have stayed here on a number of occasions and will definately be returning again. I have recommended many times and friends have stayed there on my recommendation and felt the same as I did.
Location is perfect. Staff excellent - we had a very slight problem one evening (nothing that I would worry much about) with the heating in our room and it was fixed without any delay at all once we brought it to the attention of the front desk. 
Very comfortable rooms with plenty of space. Little kitchen great to have (although we did not really use it).

title: “Great location, reasonable price for Boston”
text: Needed a place in the heart of Boston at a reasonable price. Both were found at the Marriott Courtyard. Staff was friendly and very helpful. Location was perfect. Our room was clean and comfortable.

title: “A reason to visit the Emerald City”
text:
Being just four states shy of seeing the entire United States, I can honestly say I have been putting off visiting Washington. I am not a fan of water and believe me between rain, snow, sleet and blowing winds this state has an abundance of everything connecting hydrogen to oxygen. We stumbled on the Pan Pacific by accident and I wish we stumbled a little more in this direction when we travel. The staff are wonderful and are happy to help a guest no matter the weather. Check-in was effortless from the valet to the front desk staff. The staff knew the area well and were prepared for any questions and had local maps readily available.
The room was beautiful with a hint of the orient. I would have thought the room perfect if there had been some bath salts to accompany the deep garden soaking tub. There were thick terry robes for guests and my husband just reveled in the fact there was even a shoe horn available.
(It was as if a butler had appraised the room and said now a guest would be comfortable.)
The neighborhood surronding the Pan Pacific was very quiet and not typical of a city experience. We felt quite comfortable walking and were given great directions by the staff. I am glad we visited Seattle but was even happier to have found the Pan Pacific.

title: “Very nice - but noisy air conditioner on the next building at the side”
text: Good value for money and included breakfast - great location !

title: “Tries hard to be boho and chic but it's stiff, tired, tiny and way overpriced.”
text: It's not stunning. It's average. And although it is on the waterfront, of course, the majority of the matchbox sized rooms look onto "views" a lot less pleasing on the eye, like neighboring buildings or air con units. Staff are courteous. They're just doing their job. No more than that. It's redeeming feature is it's convenient location. Would I stay there again? Probably not. Shame!

title: “Excellent Property”
text: I just love staying at this hotel, it is absolutley my first choice when traveling to Manhattan from Colorado. I have managed a hotel for over 15 years and believe me I know something really fantastic when it comes to the "best" service. Your services go above and beyond my expectations each time I stay there!

title: “Uniquely elegant with a professional leisure party client; located in the heart of the San Francisco shopping district.”
text:
The Clift Hotel is the consummate SF Hotel. Upon check in the customer service was impeccable. Valet, front desk and bartenders made every attempt to cater to hotel guest first. The hotel manager made routine visits in the lobby and bar to ensured guests were assisted in a timely fashion.
I highly recommend this gem in the big city. The hotel furniture only enhanced the ambiance. The mature mid 20’s to mid 30’s crowd will enjoy the business casual setting. 
This will be a frequently visited hotel for my family/friends and I.

title: “A great DC hotel for tourists on a budget”
text:
One of the main problems with review sites like this is that anywhere you search for will have good reviews and bad reviews, it's inevitable. I booked 5 nights at the State Plaza after getting an incredibly cheap deal on Expedia, then looked at TripAdvisor to see if it was any good. As you can see if you've read through them, a lot of people had a pretty awful time there, so that made me wonder what it was going to be like.
As it turned out, the State Plaza is a brilliant hotel, and a great base for the Mall sights in DC. The room was clean and enormous, and having the kitchen was an extra bonus. Sure, the paint on the kitchen cupboards was a bit cracked - but if you have a hard time with that, or complain about faded bedspreads or worn carpet, then pay $100 a night more and go somewhere else. This is a budget hotel, and a very good one.
The staff are incredibly friendly and helpful, and personally showed me round when I was confused by the two-building layout (happened a lot!). The breakfast is in a small room as the restaurant is still under decoration, but you can grab stuff and take it back to your room. The location is perfect, two blocks from the Vietnam/Lincoln Memorials with the other Mall sights beyond. To the person who couldn't find anywhere to eat nearby, if you walk 5mins north to I Street then there's a mini-mall at 2000 Pennsylvania Avenue (2000penn---) with restaurants, bars, food shops and a newsagents.
I'm a frequent traveller, having stayed everywhere from insect-infested hostels in the remote part of New Zealand, to the Tokyo Hilton - believe me, I was very impressed with the State Plaza in that location for that price. If you want to spend several hundred dollars a night, then good for you. There are some excellent top-range hotels in DC. If you want to spend a more reasonable amount on a clean, safe hotel with friendly staff, then I can't recommend the State Plaza enough. I would have given it 5/5 if they hadn't charged me $18 for using a minibar, when my room didn't actually have a minibar (Expedia are looking into it). Even that hasn't put me off going back, if I return to DC.

title: “It was perfect.”
text: I went to NYC for a few nights to visit some friends, and decided to stay at the Off Soho Suites. It was perfect and I appreciate that it was well located and still has some of the feel of the village in the old days.

title: “hmmm, Form over Function”
text:
Well, After the mixed reviews on here I was unsure what to expect.
Definitely this hotel suffers from form over function, and I'd say pretentious without good cause. It's really trying hard to be something it's not.
The room like most have said on here is small. We had a 'Wonderful' room which was the smallest hotel room I've ever stayed in - smaller even than one in Paris I stayed in. The room was incredibly dark with poor lighting.
There was no WiFi in the room at all, only paid for 'Wired' internet connection which was $7 for 30 minutes or $15 for 24 hours. Also there was no free WiFi in the lobby. The lobby is nice but like a cave - quite dimly lit. 
The guest information booklet resembles a brick that fans out with information on cards. It really is form over function - quite difficult to read. Room service was really expensive. A cup of tea from room service is $6 plus $4.50 delivery charge + Tax (8 odd %) + mandatory gratuity of 17% ! I didn't bother with room service in the end there's a Starbucks one block down and a few good deli style places handy to eat at.
The inroom toiletries are quite nice - all in the Bliss range. They are restocked everyday.
The bed + pillows were very comfortable.
The desk was a bit shabby, much of the varnish has come off. The shower was OK, although water would go over the floor - mopped up however by the plentiful supply of towels which were changed everyday - around 6 towels a day.
On the whole the staff were quite friendly, I got a later checkout (+1 hour) for free, and the concierge helped me to check if the show I'd booked had been cancelled due to the strike or not.
I paid $300 per night and my room was on floor 6.
The hotel is just OK, or acceptable. I won't stay here again. Not because they hotel did anything to upset me, but more because I think there are nicer places to stay.

title: “Rennovated Recently”
text: I stayed at this hotel for one night while on business in Houston. I was pleasantly surprised to see that the hotel had recently been through an upgrade of sorts. The bed linens were brand new (nice white duvet) and the room had high speed internet. It was very clean and quiet. It's literally right around the corner from all of the car rental facilities and the airport. I've stayed at some dumpy Hampton Inns so I was a bit concerned but this exceeded my expectations.

title: “OK value wise, good location, clean rooms, little noisy at night”
text:
This hotel is a pretty basic motel, but has good clean rooms and fridge/microwave in the room etc. Lombard street is very busy all night, so the rooms are pretty loud. We ventured out onto the street behin,m chesnut st and were pleasantly surprised to find lots of cue little restaurants and bars there, which were nice and lively.
value wise, its might seem like a lot for what it is, but its right in the centre of a big city, so expect to pay more.
Receptionist was incredibly helpful. Overall nota bad place to stay for a flying visit.

title: “Central for restaurants, sites & shopping”
text: A great hotel, particularly if you get a river view (I only had to ask). The room was spotless, the bed fantastic, the shower even better. The bar was spacious and relaxing. The staff did everything to please. And do try Bin 36 over the road, an amazing restaurant with a cheese bar and a novel opportunity to try numerous wines in one sitting. Highly recommended hotel whether for business or pleasure.

title: “Great Place to Stay on Business Near Central Park”
text:
This was my first time at Essex House, and it was a winner. I liked being near the Park for running in the morning, and I liked the bar in the hotel for meeting up with colleagues (I was in NY for a media tour). Mid-town is also nice for running around to meetings, centrally located. There's a Pain Quotidien around the corner for casual breakfast, and a pub on the next block for a pint. 
My room was clean and well-appointed, with a comfortable workspace, good bed and bedding, and nice shower pressure. The lighting system is a little odd, and takes some getting used to, but other than that it was all good. I liked the ability to plug iPod into TV speakers. 
No complaints at all. I would stay here again.

title: “Wedding Anniversary Weekend”
text: We stayed here to celebrate our first anniversary weekend. The hotel is gorgeous and immaculate. The service was exceptional, from the moment we pulled our car in until we checked out the following day. The woman at the front desk asked us if we were celebrating anything special and we informed her it was our first anniversary. Later that evening, when we returned from dinner, there was a complimentary chocolate dessert in our room with a lovely card from her. Truly a weekend to remember.

title: “Basic Hotel with nice bathroom”
text:
What we liked: The Bathroom was nearly luxurious and very clean, shower was good, the bed was ok and clean, the room was clean, the manager was very friendly and courteous
Not so good: It had an old carpet and the (wooden?) floor was sqeaking when you walked over it. My friend said the room smelled bad but I did not smell it....

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Great little hotel 2 blocks from Union Square and really close to the Cable car on Powell Street. Rooms are small but very clean and well serviced. (Everthing is small in SFO). We felt very safe in this hotel. 
It was convenient to everything and very reasonably priced in a somewhat expensive city. Beds are really comfortable.
The Afternoon Manager 'Oscar' was truly very helpful and knowledgable. 
He made our stay entertaining, easy and fun - always there with a smile for us a the end of a very busy day, ready to hear of our adventures.
Definately stay there again if I get to SFO again.

title: “Convenient rooms and location, staff unfriendly”
text:
I travel to New York City one or two times a month with my family and it is very nice to have two rooms for the 4 of us. The hotel is convenient to many attractions in New York City and does have a restaurant on site. However, the breakfast buffet is not very good, but edible. The people at the front desk are not friendly bordering on downright nasty sometimes. One women at the front desk was downright rude. When I contacted double tree about it they did nothing, so my husband and I stay elsewhere when possible.
Except for the staff and the breakfast, the rest is fine. However, when you pay $400 + a night I would like something better than fine.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: My husband and I recently stayed at this hotel for 2 nights while we visited Indianapolis Speedway. We booked through hotwire and got a really good price which suprised me as other hotels in the area had put their prices up during Moto GP weekend. When we got to the hotel the receptionist was very friendly and gave us a tour of all the hotel amenities. The room was clean and spacious and the bed was one of the most comfortable and biggest I have ever slept in. The location was good, it wasn't too far to drive to the Speedway and it was right beside a decent mall. I would definately stay at this hotel again.

title: “Staff Is Very Rude”
text: The rooms were clean. The air conditioning didn't work well. We had to buy a fan to keep the room tolerable. Almost all staff members were rude. Check in was posted as 3:00. After an 18 hour drive we arrived at 3:20. The receptionist yelled at me that we needed to come back in an hour because they were completely booked up and had a lobby full of people waiting for rooms that weren't ready. Our ball team had 11 team members that went down for the free breakfast. We had 11 kids that couldn't have milk with their breakfast because the attendant said she couldn't find any. She was rude to our kids who politely asked for anything that wasn't stocked. The internet connection did not work well. We're a non-profit organization, the front desk wouldn't accept our tax exempt certificate. We called the desk to ask for a couple extra towels and the rude woman said we just sent some to you why do you need more? We had never requested anything. We spent over $6000 for the week and everyone is our group was treated poorly. Find somewhere else to spend your money!

title: “Girls Weekend Perfection!”
text: We enjoyed a phenomenal Girls Weekend to celebrate a friends' 50th. This place is so comfortable and welcoming in the heart of the city. We all used the spa & it is truly worthy of Four Seasons. We only regretted we hadn't booked for 2 days of treatments! Our rooms were just lovely with nice finishes. The beds...oh the beds! We never wanted to leave! The staff was fantastic & very helpful. We had 2 delish meals at The Edge & were pleased to discover they are truly a wonderful restaurant, not just leaning on the hotel for patrons. Fun menu & quality ingredients done well. Four Seasons Denver would be perfect for a romantic getaway weekend. Larimer Square is so close & the 16th Street Mall...lots of fun walking & sites. I will not stay anywhere else when in town.

title: “Not a good location for elderly or families with young children”
text: A very good hotel but is away from most activities in DC. Bring your walking shoes or plan on using a cab.

title: “Beware - They May Not Give You the Room You Request”
text: They gave us a smoking room. We requested no smoking. The room reeked. They could not give us a no smoking room; they were booked full. We were prepaid, and we had to pull teeth to get our money back. Their "continental breakfast" wasn't good at all; go to McDonalds. They have a lot of cockroaches. Their vending machines don't have much selection - try liquor store across street. They didn't seem to care if you were satisfied or not.

title: “POOR customer service & hot rooms”
text: New a/c system..........a/c does not even turn on until you enter the room. Certainly not the type of a/c system you want in Texas in the hot, humid days of summer. Room never cooled down; had to change rooms after midnight. A/C "engineer" was extremely rude and very unprofessional. They charge for internet on top of the outrageous prices they charge for the rooms.......funny how you can stay in a "cheap" hotel like Holiday Inn or Marriott Residence Inn and not be charged for internet, yet at an "expensive" hotel you have to pay for that service; seems like the higher room charges would cover the expense of the internet. Check in was slow; restaurant prices are extremely expensive. I will not stay at this location again after I was treated so rudely by the a/c staff member. I do not pay these rates to be spoken to disrespectfully.

title: “Nice hotel, good locatoin”
text:
Next to Chinatown, the hotel is in a good location. Hotel rates are also pretty good, compared to similar hotels in other SF areas.
The hotel itself is good. It is a 'normal' business hotel, but still a nice place to stay. The rooms must have been recently refurbished: they looked very good and seemed newer then what you would exepect from the outside of the hotel :-)
The room was nicely decorated and was very comfortable. Bathroom was clean, although not too big. Which was ok for me since I stayed alone (business trip).
Bar is a great area, lobby is almost non-existing. Breakfast is average, restaurant as well.
The location is excellent: just walk outside and you're in Chinatown. DId I mention I really like chinese food... :-)
All in all a good place to stay for a few days.

title: “Disgusting”
text:
This hotel was filthy, falling apart and just downright horrible.
We checked in having paid for a twin room for 8 nights - they gave us a double and told us we only had 5 nights booked and had to pay for the others - even after showing our receipt they refused to accept this. Next morning we finally got a manager to move our room and agree wee had 8 nights paid already.
The first room was tiny - one small double bed with only a few feet from the wall on one side, with the other side jammed up on the other wall - and aout 1 foot to the window. The next room was bigger but still cramped,.
The hallways walls were filthy and stained, the whole place needs demolished and re built.
Good location but I stayed in the Marquis a few months earlier and had I know I would have paid the extra to go back.

title: “Nice hotel in a convenient location”
text: The Crowne Plaza Hamilton was an enjoyable place to stay while in D.C. It is conveniently located one block from a Metro stop making travel to area attractions a piece of cake. Our room was clean, and the bed was comfortable. The room was very quiet despite the street below being very busy due to a popular establishment. There is a Starbucks attached to the lobby for that morning cup of coffee. There is a nice restaurant and lounge in the lobby as well. We would not hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Well maintained, beautiful grounds”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for 3 days and couldn't be happier. The grounds were beautifully maintained and the service was courteous and very prompt. Daniel, the manager, stopped by our table while we were eating sushi at the restaurant there called the Islands. He wanted to make sure everything was going well. He was very nice, too. The sushi at the Islands was awesome! No wonder it's rated number 1 in San Diego.
This hotel is great for people of all ages. We saw elderly people, young families, business men and women, and people like us with older children. It's conveniently located on Hotel Circle right next to the freeway, but it's quiet with a secluded feel. It's a nice, clean hotel and even though it's old it's not showing its age.

title: “Wonderful experience!”
text:
We, my two daughters, my mom and I, spent a Saturday night at the Regency, and could not have enjoyed our experience more!!! From the very first phone call to the Regency, to when we left the hotel, we had impeccable service, and an unforgettable experience in NY!
Our trip had been planned for my Mom's birthday, and was a surprise to her. We had an executive suite which allowed all of us to stay together, which was ideal. The living room area of the suite allowed all the family to gather for birthday cake after dinner, which was very relaxing and allowed all of us to be comfortable together. Brunch in the Library the next morning was quite a treat, and our waiter, everyone at the front desk, concierge desk, and the doormen were wonderfully solicitous, and provided excellent service. We would love to make a stay at the Regency an annual treat after this incredible experience.

title: “nice property and that's about it...”
text: First, we stayed on points, and this was a good value for the amount of points required. Our room was large and clean and new. Now for the bad: the staff was impersonal--my husband checked us in, and as our family walked in, no one at the desk acknowledged us (the desk and lobby were empty). The kids wanted to swim in the indoor pool, and it was trashed--dirty towels everywhere, trash left out and no clean towels. When we asked at the desk for pool towels, she replied "there are some in there". We told her there were not, and she insisted on coming to look for herself then stormed off to bring more. While in the pool area, she did not clean up a thing. There is no breakfast offered, so we headed up to the local HEB grocery every morning. On our last night, there was a auto break-in on a car parked right in front of the hotel. Definitely will not be back.

title: “Hit and miss”
text:
This is a good quality hotel that I stay in regularly on business trips to NYC. The location is very convenient for my workplace. 
It is a large and busy hotel. Decor is rather gaudy for my taste but is generally clean. I have always found the staff to be courteous and friendly. 
The rooms are hit and miss. If you get one of the newly-refurbished rooms there is nothing to complain about. I recently stayed in a couple of the older rooms however and I wasn't impressed. The carpet in one was damp due to faulty a/c...not nice 
The restaurant is pleasant enough. Breakfasts are better than the evening meals. 
There is no minibar in the rooms so even for basics like a bottle of water you have to purchase from a small shop in the foyer. They have a good selection but this is not convenient given the room rates. 
Final point to make is on the gym. It's on the top floor. Clean and I've always found there to be plenty of room. I find the selection of equipment rather odd. There are several running machines and cross trainers but only 1 bike and no rowing machines. 
In summary, there are a few frustrations with this hotel. But for business trips in mid town it's hard to beat for convenience and service

title: “Best price in town, but expect some discomfort”
text:
I stayed at the hotel together with my girlfriend during a weekend trip to Chicago. The hotel is probably the cheapest accomendation in downtown Chicago but you have to expect some discomfort when you go there. The room and bed where okay but the windows where pretty thin (compared to the typical situation in Germany) so you hear pretty much everything what's going on outside. Our window was towards the back side of a huge department store and there where noisy fans running all night long. Besides that you hear a lot from the big crossing next to the hotel, and people in Chicago really like to use their horn. On the other side you have free parking and other hotels in downtown are 200 bucks up...
Enjoy your stay,
Markus

title: “Excellent Choice!!!”
text:
WOW! What a wonderful hotel! We stayed here for two nights at the end of a cross country trip that involved nine different hotels.
The location is excellent. You are on the waterfront (there are only two waterfront properties in Seattle) about one block from the aquarium and across the street from one of the cruise ship docks. From this location we walked everywhere - Space Needle. REI, Pike's Market, etc.
Because my husband is a platinum member, we had access to concierge lounge. Free breakfast items, afternoon snacks, evening appetizers and desserts. It was a very nice touch. 
Our room had a beautiful view of the bay and the skyline. Gorgeous at night. 
Lovely lobby, very friendly and extremely helpful staff. We truly felt welcomed and at home here.
Only negatives were the hot tub at the pool area was not functioning properly and parking is $25/night but that is average for area. Minor issues compared to all of the great things about this hotel.
We would definitely stay here again!

title: “best location with great service”
text: I love staying at this hotel. very convenient to penn station, shops and food. Staff is great, fitness center is good. My last stays have had great views. Loved the apple cider! nice touch!

title: “The best hotel in Seattle”
text:
I was really stunned by the Hotel 1000. I needed to make a fast trip to Seattle to renew my passport, and found this hotel right across the streed from the federal building.
If you like an elegant, quiet, nice hotel with outstanding staff, this is the place for you.
The lobby is really quite beautiful, with subdued lighting, no musack, quiet elegance, and a staff whose response to every one of my queries was "no problem."
The room was a knock out with original art and sculpture, large screen plasma tv, outstanding free internet, fand ree long distance calls.The bed was superb, with goose down quilts and wonderful designer lighting. I had a deluxe room on the 10th floor, and the writing desk for work was one of the best I have ever seen in a hotel.
The bathroom had top designer fixtures, a nice view over Seattle, and a tub which fills from the ceiling! The only bathroom I have seen that compares in the Okura in Tokyo or perhaps the Amangani,
The breakfast buffet is really nice- thick linen table cloths, a small fire in the center of the room surrounded by Japanese river rocks. They served muffins, , proscuttiio, vanilla and banana pancakes with real maple syrup, parfaits with fresh berries, freshly squozen orange juice, hot oatmeal and all of this on a small two meter long table. The breakfast area is quiet with earth muted tones in design. The waiter even let me see the container of 100% maple syrup (I have an allergy to artifical maple flavor) so didn't have to worry..
They gave me a free extended checkout, stored my luggage for ne, sent a staff member into the street to flag down a cab to the airport, and did whatever they could to make my visit as pleasant as possible.
I log about 150k air miles a year and stay at a lot of hotels around the world, particularly in Asia. Hotel 1000 is one of the nicest I have stayed at any price,. I have stayed at the Seattle Four Seasons and I think Hotel 1000 is nicer. In fact, I want to take my famly back there just to see the quiet elegant design of the Hotel 1000. The staff and the property deserve an A+ for excellence.
This will definitely be my headquarters in Seattle from now on.

title: “Only for dogs”
text:
We stayed here for one night, having originally booked in for 5 nights. The location is its best feature being in Ocean Beach, right next to the Dog Beach.
It is designed for dogs and maybe their owners. Note that we have dogs but they had to stafy in the UK. The only reason we stayed here was that it was literally the only place with vacancies in the San Diego area on a Saturday night in summer. Overall the property looked as if it has suffered with time and is in dire need of a renovation.
The rooms are simply tiled and the walls are a little grubby (but it is a glorified dog kennel in which the owners also sleep). We had to change rooms because the toilet blocked up. Although the reception staff were friendly, maintenance consisted of me being handed a toilet plunger to sort it out myself. The patio and patio furniture were very dirty and off-putting.
Great if we had had our dogs with us but they should keep a few non-doggy rooms for other guests.

title: “View of Elliott Bay”
text:
This was a stay for business. I am a rewards member so was able to upgrade to a view room at no charge. The front dest staff were wonderful at helping pick a room for me that would meet all my requests.
The rooms was just as nicely appointed as you would expect at this level of hotel.
The location was wonderful for us. There were a few restaurants in short walking distance. The hotel restaurant left a lot to be desired though. I had stayed here before so did not eat here again.

title: “Location is Everything”
text: It is hard to complain about this hotel. It was clean, friendly, and the location was AWESOME! Located just one block away from Time Square, with many great restaurants within walking distance. A cab ride to Chelsea area will cost about $7, and to Central Park is about $4. This was a big plus since I sprang my ankle the day before we got o NYC. The downside to this place is that the cost is a little too much and the rooms are a little too small. The restaurant located in the lobby was not that great, I would recommend venturing out to find something to eat. But if it is all about Broadway & Time Square for your travels then this is a great choice.

title: “A Great Bargain & A Great Hotel”
text:
Spent 3 nights with a family of 2 adults and 3 kids in one double bedded room. Paid $179.00/night thru the Holiday Inn Express website. Fantastic rate for this hotel and location. 2 blocks from Rockefeller Center, St. Patricks Cathedral, Times Square. Much shopping and many dining choices all around. 
Super service. Everyone at the hotel were friendly and very helpful. CLEAN - CLEAN - CLEAN. Hotel is brand new so nothing to complain about at all. Felt very safe and very comfortable.
If there is a negative it is the size of the rooms. Cramped, but average for NYC. Front desk reception aisle is literally an aisle way, seperated from the breakfast area by the buffet bar. Sometimes difficult to maneuver in or out of hotel on either side as it's so narrow. 5-10 peoople in the lobby area and it's a crowd! Forget it though -- go and enjoy!

title: “If you don't need a car stay here...”
text:
Hotel is extremely nice, very convient to most stuff but parking is like $50 a day. Yikes. I think some other folks mentioned the lofty parking prices but they are probably the highest I'd seen in the city. I was there for 4 days and left the car parked the entire time and just decided to walk everywhere. Everything was reasonably close. The longest walk was the Prime Rib restaraunt which it was late so I took a cab back. My office was about 10 blocks and the warf probably another 5 blocks or so. The room was a good size, the bed was comfortable, clean and very hip. The restaraunt was reasonably priced for a swanky hotel. The bus boy kept reminding us when the they closed. Guess he didn't want us holding him up... Our waiter was great and the food was pretty good. 
I'd definately stay again but I would just take a cab from the airport and walk everywhere or take a cab. Less hassle and cheaper in the long run.

title: “Reasonably priced, quality hotel in a good location”
text: We are a family of 4 from the UK (2 adults, 2 boys - 10 & 12) and stayed at the Carlton in late August. All the good things you read about this hotel are true! I booked direct with the hotel and had a great email correspondence with the Reservation Manager about the right room for us. We settled on a corner room on the 3rd floor for all 4 of us. When we arrived, the Reception staff were genuinely friendly and helpful. The room was quite large enough and tastefully decorated. We had no noise problems from outside though we could hear the person next door occasionally. We did not eat at the hotel but preferred to eat at local cafe's. It is within easy walking distance of Union Square and we encountered no issues with homeless people, though there are a fair few people in this situation and they do beg.

title: “Friendly, laid back, on the beautiful Riverwalk, and a GREAT value”
text: Very friendly, accommodating staff. Informal lobby & front-desk set-up. The hotel is right on the Riverwalk but a tiny bit away from the "busy," lively section of the Walk. However, I am not a walker (arthritis) but if I could walk to the Alamo, and return to the hotel via the Riverwalk then ANYONE can. The walk is handicapped accessible also. The hotel is very low-key yet has all the amenities one could want. Parking is free and the included Continental breakfast was very generous in offerings and hours. It is not a large lobby/restaurant area so it could get crowded if lots of people show up at one time. The front desk staff is terrific - friendly, warm, helpful, and very accommodating. The room was a nice size and had plenty room for a family of sleepers. The bathroom is a bit small with the toilet and bathtub/shower in one small room and the sink outside this room - but it does the job! Nice sink and fridge in the room with a coffee maker. Our room' s balcony overlooked the Riverwalk and because we were not that near to the downtown nightlife, it was beautifully quiet and serene with lots of trees, flowers, and water birds swimming past. This hotel was a great choice for us, location-wise, for the excellent value, amenities offered and we are very happy we found it. We would definitely return to it when we come back to San Antonio (so much we did not have time to see).

title: “Great hotel, great service!”
text:
My family and I have never had a bad experience at a Hyatt property. We are pretty loyal to the brand and stay at a Hyatt whenever possible, whether for business or leisure (anywhere from 5-10 times per year.) Having said that, the staff at the Hyatt at Olive 8 treated us absolutely amazing and made us feel extremely welcome...maybe even the best out of any other Hyatt we've stayed at!
After getting the best possible room available at check-in, we checked out the gym and pool on the second floor (both are great!) The spa looked really nice, but it's not really our thing, so I can't comment on that. Urbane, the onsite restaurant, was the perfect spot for dinner. The service was great, the food was tasty, the portions were good, and the prices were very reasonable. They even had a good kids menu!
The hotel is new and has a nice modern look, the location is perfect for walking down to Pike Place Market, or for a nice evening walk (which we took after dinner.) It'll be a no-brainer when deciding where to stay next time we're in Seattle. I'd recommend this hotel to anyone!

title: “A gem still exists in LA Land”
text:
On my travels and always staying at Hyatt I have stayed at this property several times over the years. I always feel like royalty driving up to valet. Great location.
The rooms are spacious and great for business travelers like myself. High speed Internet is excellent and business center available as well. Excellent location with a large mall around the corner and just centralized enough if most meetings are on the west side of town.
I can't say enough about the wonderful staff. From arrival to departure and everywhere in between attention to details and courteous friendly attentive staff makes this a great hotel.

title: “Would definitely return”
text: We held our inaugural convention at the Hilton Anatole and I can't imagine another facility meeting our needs as well as the Anatole. The staff were so courteous and helpful. The chef literally hovered to ensure our special dietary needs were met. Beautiful workout facilities, art and rooms.

title: “The service is great!”
text: The air conditioner in the original room we got seemed have some problem. After changed to another room, it is very nice! But, there is a problem: the signal of WiFi is too weak, you have to go to the office to use internet.

title: “nice hotel for Silicon Valley”
text: I hear that this was a Crown Plaza Hotel previously. Usually, I see Hyatt Places in suburbs, that pretty much look the same. This HP looks different, of course. But, the room was clean and comfortable. I loved the continental breakfast, as always. It was very close to San Jose International Airport, as well as St. Joseph's Cathedral (walking distance). I would consider staying here again if I come back to visit San Jose.

title: “Truly Luxury, Naturally.”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel Vitale on Saturday, April 2, in one of the panoramic suites. I've never stayed in such a room... the attention to detail and design were amazing... great bathroom products (a great break from Aveda), healthy snacks/bar, automatic window shutters, sound machine, long working desk with office chair, very comfortable bed/pillows, iPod speaker system, dvd player, flat screen tv, interesting magazines, unique services and amenities offered, regular and rain drop shower heads in glass faced walk-in shower with wooden stool, two sinks in separate toilet/shower rooms, mini bar, Bose alarm clock, sofa and chair, bath tub by the window, 270 degree views, circular room design, etc. You must experience this room.
As far as customer service went, it was excellent... everyone is super helpful/friendly (and presentable) and although the hotel has a stylish, hip feel, you feel comfortable and not pressed to "be cool". And when you check out, you really do feel like you had a relaxing stay. The spa/wellness, natural theme should appeal to all types of travelers. The Americano (Italian) restaurant complements the hotel well, too. In my opinion, it is a great date place because of its reasonable prices, classy/stylish feel and opportunity for pre and after dinner drinks in either the long bar area or circular lounge. 
Lastly, you can't really beat this location. It is along the Embarcadero/water and across from the Ferry Building/Farmer's Market... a great place to hang out during the day, for food, exercise, sights, etc.
Hotel Vitale should be THE place to stay from here on out. Definitely, luxury, naturally.

title: “Fantastic Time at the Westin”
text:
I had a blast at the Westin Grand. I was there from 12/29-1/4 with my boyfriend. We checked in a little early at around 12:00pm. The man working at front desk was extremly helpful and he even looked in the computer to find my starwood number when I didn't have my card. We ended up in a fabulous room on the 6th floor. The starwood floor? There was a plaque by the elevator that said starwood preferred that the other floors didn't have (I checked...lol.). There was fruit by the elevator which was nice. The room was huge! The bathroom was definitly "heavenly" with a huge shower with 2 shower heads and the toilet in a seperate little room. The maid service was also great. They came everyday and did a good job. Westin has cool conserve cards that you have to put out if you want them to change the bed linens, and they tell you to put the dirty towels on the floor if you want them to be changed because anything on the towel racks will just be refolded. There was a mini bar in the room which was very well stocked but very expensive...gatorade was like $5. There's a CVS a block up the street, and a Trader Joe's around the corner. There's also Starbucks coffee in the room which they replenished, there's also a mini Starbucks in the lobby but thier prices are a bit more expensive. I would just walk to the regular Starbucks which is less than a block up the street. The hotel is very close to Georgetown, it was nice out so I walked there in less than 10 minutes straight up M street. We drove and just found parking on the street. Be careful to read the signs and feed the meters on weekdays. I had a wonderful time at this hotel and don't understand all the negative reviews.
FYI: They charge $50 to your credi card when you get there for incidental's and don't return it until after you leave.

title: “Location Location Location”
text: I appreciate the history of the facility and the wonderfully supportive staff. The rooms are updated quite nicely and the view can be wonderful if you're facing Sundance Square. The one thing that I dislike about this hotel is they charge for Internet access, which seems insulting, given how much the room rate is.

title: “Excellent stay at a great boutique hotel!!”
text:
This was my first experience with a Kimpton property but it certainly won't be the last. We stayed at the Alexis for 6 days in April 2009, partly for business (a conference for me) and leisure (wife and daughter catching up with sister-in-law). Since my conference hotel had no rooms big enough for us (my daughter is handicapped and wheelchair bound) I searched for a hotel with a large suite at a good value. While I looked at the Hotel Monaco, the Alexis caught my eye. We setttled on the Fireplace suite, an 850 sq. foot room with fireplace, expansive dining table for 6, sofabed, separate bedroom with King bed, and a nicely set up bathroom/bath. With the Kimpton promotion of 30% off for stays over 3 days, the cost was minimally more than I would have paid for a standard hotel room at the conference hotel. Also, I was only 4 blocks awar from the conference and closer still to the water and piers. 
Although we arrived late on day 1 after gathering all our gear and a minivan at SEA-TAC, the hotel had a valet to greet us and help us shuttle our stuff to the room on the second floor. The flowers I requested were there (great choice, very fragrant) + the rollaway for our daughter. Lots of space to work in as there was a long counter with sink, honor bar fridge which we emptied onto the opposite counter, and put my daughters medications and formulas into. My wife marvelled at the room's size, decor (great paintings on entry with nice accent lighting), and layout. (won some points with this choice). It did face the western alley looking directly back to another office building but it was relatively quiet and very comfortable. Beds were very comfortable, 37" LCD TV's with remotes, bathroom was great except for small amount of counter space around sink. shower was great, nice and hot with good pressure at all hours of the day.
Had a great recommendation from the front desk for a late take out snack from McCormick and Schmick's on the next corner. The front Desk check in was great, the valets were ALWAYS ready with our car when we called and helped us with our wheelchair stowage or packages, and were very friendly, calling us by name each day. Note that there are two drop off areas - in front facing east, and to the south side. The front is used during most of the day but there is no stopping during some parts of the rush hours so they take you in from the south if needed. However, the main entrance is the only one handicap accessible, the south side has stairs that lead to the Library Bistro. Not a problem for us once we learned the layout.
My sister-in-law also enjoyed visiting with us and felt the room was a hit and a great value. The food at the Library and Bookstore (same kitchen) was excellent day and night. The art all around the hotel added a nice sophisticated touch. The concierge was quite helpful and even came out to our car to deliver a specific map we had requested.
The hotel's housekeeping staff was very good, cleaning each day when we requested it and provided a turn down service too. They were respectful of all our stuff (we do spread out in a room!!) yet tidied up quickly and efficiently. They certainly earned their gratuity at the end of our stay. Both the wired and wireless internet worked quite well, nice to have two ways to hook up since we brought 2 laptops with us. The only glitch was one faulty network cable which was easily exchanged at the front desk.
I travel reasonably often and stay at a lot of different chains and properties. This was one of my best stays and my wife, daughter, and sister-in-law enjoyed having the Alexis as our Seattle base - we looked forward to returning back to our "second" home each eveing and relaxing by the fire. We had no problems with internal noise, and only 1 day was there outside noise - a compressor or jackhammer run by either a city crew or one of the crew workinig on the hotel/building facade starting at 7am!!. The manager apologized profusely and their schedule was delayed to after 8am.
When we visit Seattle again, we'll stay at the Alexis! I can't see any reason to look for anything else!
Regards,
The Yee's
PS - Loved seeing Lily, the resident dog/pet relations agent in the lobby. She's nicely mannered and comfortable around people. Adds a nice homey touch.

title: “Very nice place!”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights while traveling to Detroit. The staff are great. This is a pet friendly place. The breakfast is out of this world, didn't use the pool, so I can't comment on that. They do have a "kick back" time starting at 5:30pm and you can get finger foods and three adult beverages...a nice touch....you can make a meal on this! This hotel is within walking distance of the downtown hot spots from restaurants to bars to coffee houses...very near the arts district. We will definitely come back.

title: “Very cool retro feel - reminded me of set from A Clockwork Orange”
text: Besides the super friendly and accommodating staff, the atmosphere is really the selling point here. There were still minor renovations being made while we were there, but I like that they are preserving the unique Kubrick-esque vibe.

title: “Very deceiving from the beginning.”
text: Just to mirror some of the other reviews we also found the Hotel dirty and dark. To begin we tried to check in early but to no avail wanted to leave luggage with bell services but had to bring luggage to the "dungeon" aptly named ,cold dark and filthy area on bootom floor where they hold your luggage. There was a station next to the check in area labeled Bell Services but I guess that doesn`t apply to luggage holding for guests. Told to come back after 1 there should be something then,came back about 2 and the other 75 people in line must have been told same thing,anyway got room 697 in back of hotel down two dark smelly corridors noticing all the large areas on walls with paint literally hanging off the walls(wondering if it`s lead paint) opening the door to the smallest room for price I have ever seen.. Opened up the curtains and viewed a brick wall 30 feet away with no view of anything The curtains were riddled with holes and tears not that any sun was going to find it`s way to the room..Smoke dectector hanging from the ceilingopened no battery(but you can rent a dectector at front desk at check in. There was no receptacle to plug in clock or light on night stand inbetween beds(I later found plug behind mattress of bed ,doesn`t sound to safe to me. No fitted sheets on bed tossing and turning during sleep is not optioned or you will be wrapped up in ill fitting bedding. I am just 6ft tall and feet hung iff end by ankles meust be a special size New York bed. The bathroom was horrendous paint chipped everywhere took 5 minutes to get hot water for shower shelf above sink and toilet only 5 inches wide everything falls off etc.

title: “Good enough for a short business trip”
text:
Pros:
1. Big room - the bedroom was separate from the living room. 
2. Great breakfast with eggs, sausages, hotcake, made to order omelette and they had Manager's cocktails but I never had the chance to try it though.
3. Helpful Front desk 
Cons:
1. They ran out of toothpaste on my 2nd day and was advised just to buy from the gift shop.
2. There is a gap in the curtains beside the door so people walking the corridors can see you from outside. i think this is the case for all the rooms because I could see the inside of the other rooms when I walk to my room from the elevator. 
3. The fire alarm went off at 4AM because according to the manager the water pressure went down. The manager did send out a letter apologizing.
4. I saw a cockroach walking on the floor going into the plants while having breakfast. 
5. The bed may have bed bugs because I had little bites on my arms towards the end of my stay. 
I will probably look for another hotel when I come visit.

title: “Contemporary Hotel, in a great location”
text:
I stayed in this hotel back in November 2008 whilst on a business trip to New York. The hotel is close to Times Square, but not too close, so the hotel doesn't feel as if it's in the middle of the hustle, bustle and noise of Times Square.
The rooms are quite small, though this isn't unusual in NY, the rooms are decorated mainly in white and black - like the rest of the hotel, and maybe a little too modern for those used to traditional hotels.
The restaurant has a small lounge bar (which is used for breakfast in the morning), but no restaurant though this isn't too much of a problem as you are in the centre of New York, and there are numerous restaurants within a couple of minutes walk - though the hotel does offer room service in the evenings.
On the whole a good hotel, in a great location, though rooms are a little on the small side - though you don't go to New York to spend absolutely all of your time in the room! 
A good hotel, one which I would recommend, but with photographs of topless women in the lobby and around the hotel, as well as the Karma Sutra in the bedside drawer, perhaps a hotel to avoid if you're travelling with those who aren't broad minded!

title: “Clean, fun, perfect, relaxing and close to everything.”
text: The Magnolia was everything we could hope for. We'll be staying there form now on and will be highly recommending to everyone.

title: “What a wonderful experience!! We can't wait to go back.”
text: This hotel is just perfect in every way. The staff fabulous and so were the rooms. We had a one bedroom suite on the 12th floor. The room was huge with a separate bedroom and lovely patio. The view of the city was breathtaking. We loved the rooftop pool and hot tub. The location was perfect for an evening on the river walk. The happy hour was ok. We will always stay here when visiting San Antonio.

title: “Front desk mgr William Mathews made the stay”
text: I read Trip Advisor regularly when researching hotels, but this is the first time the service was so outstanding that I am taking the time to write a review. We recently completed our first stay at the hotel after Christmas with our 4 young daughters, booking 2 rooms. When we checked in I noticed that William Mathews at the front desk was the person checking us in. I remembered his name being favorably mentioned several times in reviews, so I was curious, although I didn't mention anything. To make it short, these good reviews didnt do him justice. He couldn't have been nicer or more helpful. He went out of his way to put us in great connecting rooms, gave us all the tips and in's and out's of the property, gave us one of those free tourist books with Sea World discount coupons when we mentioned we were going to Sea World, etc. He set the tone for a great stay at the property. Whatever they are paying him isn't enough. Our kids loved the property, rooms were great, as was the service. We will absolutely be back.

title: “Could have gone bad but management made the difference”
text: Stayed here for a quick weekend to visit son who is in Tenleytown. Metro'd everywhere, had such fun! Injured my leg due to hotel problem. They were extremely helpful and kind considering I had to walk a lot. They made up for my injury with professionalism and customer service. The front desk was harried, but it was a weekend. Easy, clean, cheap. Not the 4 seasons but great for the price.

title: “Business trip”
text: Worst hotel I've stayed at in over 5 years. Common areas were unkept, chipped paint, stained carpet, and dirty. My room had dirty walls and chipped paint. The sliding closet door was falling off.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text: Great service, amazing hot breakfast, clean rooms, full kitchen, granite countertops, nice pool and spa, enjoyed our stay there, very close to the galleria and shopping.

title: “Disappoined”
text: My selection of this hotel was based on the positive reviews I had read on Trip Advisor. My stay was not as positive. We were not given the room that we had reserved until a day later. We had to wait several hours (past 4:30 p.m.) to check in. The room, when we finally got it, was nice, clean and comfortable. When we requested extra towels from the maid, only 2 sets of towels were left. There were four of us in the room. We called the front desk for more towels and the stack they delivered included a greasy stained towel, 2 bathmats. The attitude of the front desk staff and the manager were very arrogant. I think they could have cared less if you stayed in their establishment. I would not stay there again. The location was very convenient, however.

title: “I could get used to this”
text:
My 'complimentary' one-night stay was arranged by the airline after my international flight had been abruptly rescheduled, resulting in my having to stay an extra night in Houston. Check-in was rapid and efficient, and staff were professional. I was given a spacious room on the executive floor which came with a very comfy bed, a small balcony with a sweeping view of the area, and free Wi-Fi. However, I was a little disappointed in the layout of the bathroom - somehow, the bath and WC had been tucked in a tiny corner next to the closet; the lighting was also somewhat too dim. I was also given free use of the executive lounge/business centre which was also the venue for the daily self-service continental breakfast.
I'm glad I had chosen to stay in The Galleria district because the hotel was only 5-10 mins walk from good eating and retail establishments, making it convenient for me to do some last-minute shopping before heading for the airport. I decided to call for room service before checking out - this was fairly fast and friendly, a delight. Overall, I was very pleased with my experience and wouldn't mind returning.

title: “Made our stay in New York memorable”
text:
I used Hilton.points to book this hotel so expected the lowest room however this was not to be we arrived and were upgraded to a conference room suite right on timessquare with views of the Hudson river
The service was brilliant our room amazing clean very spacious and looked after really well by housekeeping
Our complimentary breakfast was better than most paid for breakfasts and Eugene the short order cook could not do enough for us Thank you Eugene your service was greatly appreciate
I highly reccomend this hotel for location.room sizes service and attention to detail
After speaking to friends who stayed in a trendy new York hotel and paid a fortune for their room we know we had the best experience and would definetly stay here again

title: “Very nice all around”
text:
Got the reservation on price-line. First off, we were worried that we won't have space for our two kids. No guarantees on that were given 24hrs ahead over the phone, but at the time of check in the double room was found with two beds and, nicely, early check-in was allowed 2 hrs ahead of time. A couple of things in the room didn't work, but we didn't make a big deal of it (like the TV in the bathroom?!). The shower fixture is a little weird - but there is a phone in the bathroom as well to get quick help in operating the shower. :) The furniture is pretty interesting - many clever ways of using small space in multifunctional way. We were in the room 710 - not the greatest view perhaps, but very quiet at night, and I would rather take that, if the view would have to come with the noise. Personnel was very helpful and polite at every single interaction in the hotel. (Advised on places to eat, etc.) Also we got offered extra hour before the check out. All together, at the price we paid, it was a pretty nice experience. 
Things to keep in mind: 15$ for WiFi connection and 43$ for parking (both per day).

title: “I love this Hotel!”
text: The Brookshire suites was a fabulous find. The rooms were very CLEAN and comfortable. The location is great, easy walking distance to the inner habor attractions and Camden Yards. The breakfast in the cloud room was one of the best breakfast offerings I have ever seen. I can not say enough good things about Brookshire Suites. We will stay there again!

title: “Grand Dame of Chicago”
text: Have high tea at the Palmer House. The lobby is a spectacular Art Deco masterpiece. You can walk to the Art Institute and the Miracle Mile. Some of the older rooms have been joined to create super large rooms.

title: “the nightmare before christmas”
text:
My husband and I wanted to start a special tradition with our son of staying in a luxury hotel Christmas Eve. The experience we had at the Sorrento was so bad we will not continue this tradition.
To summarize: 1) not given hypoallergenic room even though it was requested and then reluctance on part of front desk to remedy problem; 2) dinner at the Hunt Club (hotel's restaurant) was moved twice by hotel.
