We weren't seated until 9:15pm and not given booster seat for our two year old despite being told we would; 3) foreign hair found in bathtub as well as strong Comet smell; 4) bathroom window never closed and room became very cold; 5) no assistance from staff, anything we needed was begrudgingly executed by staff or not done at all; 6) food in Hunt Club was mediocre with a baby beet salad swimming in vinegar and subpar scallops; 7) if you eat in Hunt Club order the salmon; 8) extremely warm temperature in restaurant and Not Family-Friendly; 9) went most of the meal without water and no one would remedy this despite asking two restaurant staff to remedy problem; 10) promised complimentary breakfast in room that required countless phone calls to optain; 11) used child's bandage in bedsheets not belonging to our son!; 12) no refrigerator in room; 13) no newspaper; 14) promised discounts not honored; 15) valet parking did nice job of loading and unloading car; 16) only one staff member showed concern for our enjoyment.
Overall, we will Never return!

title: “Great hotel and location”
text: I was a little sceptical booking this hotel after reading other reviews, but was pleasantly surprised after my stay at the Sheraton. The construction is over and the hotel is lovely. The room we had was in the newly refurbished tower and the rooms were large and immaculate. The beds were also very comfortable. My brother booked a suite and their room was incredible with a view of the water. The staff was extremely helpful as well. Definitely worth considering for your next visit to Seattle.

title: “They could have cared less...”
text:
From start to finish, they could have cared less about customer service or us simply as a guest. When checking in they did not have the room type we had reserved yet did nothing to compensate or even apologize. We were simply told nope, not available and then smiled at us like we were idiots standing in front of them at the desk.
We then went to the concierge after reluctantly accepting our unacceptable room to ask where we might find some suitable dining, to be snapped at by a rude, extremely disrespectful woman with a french accent, who again made us feel like we were bothering her and how dare we do so. I was so put off by her rudeness that I was about to call a manager over when my traveling companion simply pulled me away and reminded me that the management and front desk really wouldn't care.
As in the other reviews we had the noisiest night I have ever had in any hotel and in addition, it got extremely cold that evening and the hotel was absolutely freezing and no heat on anywhere.
The following morning we go to the restaurant for our "free breakfast" to find out its really not free, even though the room was booked that way, its simply a $10 voucher off the price of your breakfast check!!!
We would have run from this hotel screaming at the first encounter with the front desk if we were not exhausted from traveling all day and were not boarding a cruise ship across the street early the next morning.
If you care anything about service, comfort or your own well being, steer clear of this hotel!

title: “Cute and affordable”
text:
Love the decore! We stayed for 9 nights and had a great time checkin out the city.
The location is great, bed was comfortable, rooms were small but we didn't mind As we were only sleeping there anyway, rooms cleaned daily.
Bad: tv reception was poor and no safe or phone in the rooms.
I would happily stay here again though.

title: “Mediocre property-not retro as advertised.”
text:
Recently stayed here a couple of nights with family to attend some Mariners' games. The potential is here for a retro "boutique" style property; but at the moment it is far from retro, unless the definition of retro is tired and worn with slaps of 60's style colors. It resembles a motor inn and not a hotel style at all. The rooms are very basic: with a crowded sink/microwave/mini-fridge area, old style TV's, very spotty WiFi connections and the old fashioned heater/ac units under the window.The bathroom is small and when we checked into our room, towels and hand soaps were missing. I do have to give kudos to the staff for getting our missing amenities to the room very quickly. While we were there, a group of teens were there for a conference and over two nights, it was ridiculously noisy with running on the outdoor hallways late into the night and van alarms going off at 7am. My sister was a few doors down and was up til 3am listening to a ruckus on the floor above them; she finally went down to the front desk after repeated calls to the desk didn't address the problem. We did use the shuttle to get to Safeco Field and it was great getting there. Coming home, there seemed to be some confusion as to how many were going back, with not enough vans or seats available to porter us back. We stood around while the hotel staff tried to figure it out and finally after about 20 minutes all were accommodated. This shuttle confusion continued the next day when we tried to use the shuttle to get to Pike Place Market. I had put our name in at the front desk about an hour prior to the scheduled departure and when the time came, again the staff seemed confused as to where they would put the people in the couple vans that were going to various places. Had they kept us all updated of what they were trying to do instead of running in and out of the hotel lobby and looking confused, it would have been a lot less aggravating standing in the driveway awaiting some kind of direction. When they asked where we were going and what our room number was, the driver couldn't find it on his clipboard and this seemed to confuse them even more. We finally gave up after waiting 30 minutes and took a cab into Pike Place Market. They really need a more organized method for their shuttles so they could run more efficiently. 
 We decided to cut our stay short by a day and checked out the third morning; the front desk staff did seem slightly apologetic but basically said that the noise they had with the teen group had cost them some business and remarked to me "I guess we won't be seeing you at this hotel again." No, I don't think you will.

title: “Pricey but good facility”
text: Stayed one night at this hotel for $269, which seems high to me. Front desk service was wonderful. Room was fine -- including light-stopping shades that actually stopped every lumen of light from the outside. Bed was comfortable. In other words, it had everything the business traveler needed, but at that price....

title: “Okay convention hotel--nicer choices nearby”
text:
This is a decent, but fairly sterile hotel. The rooms are up to par with good beds and decent furnishings. The bath rooms have been "granitized, but the tubs are small (5ft) so it doesn't really feel luxurious. Room service has a limited selection, but it is decent and quick (and the staff is quick to point out that the 20% "delivery charge" was not "gratuity.")
The big disappointment was the slow check-in and limited service offered by staff to the guest. I was in a line of five guests waiting to check in through one desk staffer. Two other desk men stood just back from the desk engaged in conversation. This was typical whenever I went to the desk with a problem of question. They seemed to enjoy making guests wait. The hotel was not busy at the time either, being between conventions.
There was very little information in the room about hotel services, which was disappointing. No pens or paper to write with either. Very limited amenities (conditioner, soap and shampoo were about it.) No-one at the desk offered any information. 
Staff going through the hallways were often very loud--you could hear them in the rooms. 
There was a "Guest Services" desk but it was not manned during my stay for even an instant. I stood in front of it several times and was just ignored by passing staff.
The restaurant (there is only one) looked okay, but uninteresting. The hotel entrance is bady designed and crowded. When you leave you have to walk among the cars coming into the hotel in order to reach the street. Good thing they are all jammed up so none of them can be moving very fast.
This could be a nice hotel if staff cared a bit more about the guests. Instead you get the feeling that everyone is just going through the motions.
The location is next to (attached to) the convention center, so if you are attending a convention there , it is probably an okay choice (better than the scruffy Hilton on the other side of the center). Otherwise I would stay at the Fairmont or the historic hotel just across the street were I to go back to San Jose.

title: “Took Some Getting Used To But I Adjusted And Enjoyed It”
text:
Just spent two consecutive weeks , each week a 4 night stay here. On my first arrival I walked into the lobby and was very skeptical. It has the look and feel of a club and everyone in there seemed under 35 ( I'm much older). Check-in was nice and polite and once I got in my room, although it is pretty minimalist I admit it was clean and comfortable. 
The gym on property was nice enough for me and I hear they have rights at another nearby gym with more extensive facilities. Breakfast is OK- self service with free coffee in the lobby. 
During the first week one night there was live music in the lobby and many of the guests ended up outside in a courtyard where it was pretty noisy until past mid-night. Other than that though the lobby bar scene didn't bother me.In fact the bar tender Matt was a really nice guy who remembered my name and what I drank when I returned the second week.
One night a co-worker dropped me off after dinner and I then realized I'd left my cell phone at the restaurant. The hotel van ran me over immediately and my phone was recovered. I really appreciated that.
I left my bag there for the weekend and they secured it and returned it promptly when I re-arrived the following week. The front desk staff is great, friendly young people who seemed very eager to help. My second week was even better. I was addressed by name by many staff members and felt very much at home. 
Overall I was very impressed and this will be my place when I'm in CLT which will be quite often.

title: “Layne Rules!”
text: The hotel is magnificent, and the service is incredible. It is conveniently located three blocks away from Union Square. The front desk people is extremely helpful.

title: “Weekend getaway”
text: Just got back from a stay at this hotel. Room was fabulous - bed linens luxurious, bathroom was incredible with walk in shower with double shower heads. We had a CD/DVD player in our room (unlike previous from another reviewer). Flat screen in bathroom as well! Hotel was spotless throughout and the casino staff were constantly tidying up. The staff throughout the hotel were amazing. Every staff member we passed smiled and said hello and wished us a nice stay. The concierge service was great, free valet parking with no waiting for our car upon checkout. Had a great dinner at the Saltwater. Check in and out was very quick. Only complaint was my husband thought the luxurious king bed was too soft! It was like sleeping on a cloud to me! We will definitely go back again.

title: “Fantastic !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text:
Stayed here from 6th to 13th June 2007. I booked through expedia and after spending a few weeks searching lots of hotes in san fran. I chose this based on the reviews given on trip advisor and was not dissapointed!!! I am a bit OCD with hygiene however this hotel ticked all the boxes. The room was immaculate and cleaned every day. The staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful and the location of the hotel was perfect. Its a 10 min walk to union square which was lovely to do and in a very safe neighbourhood. The sahara restaurant within the hotel was the best ive had in a very long time especially the shitake raviolli !!! very resonable, quaint and friendly. If you want a cheap yet decent hotel within walking distance to union square and in a safe neighbourhood this is the one for you. I seriously would not consider other hotels as this really was a lovely one to stay in.
Alison, Essex

title: “Home Away From Home”
text: If you want a wonderful accommodation while visiting San Francisco, I suggest you stay at Petite Auberge. The room we occupied with the fireplace was charmingly decorated and very comfortable. Each day began with a wholesome hardy breakfast with a nice variety of selections, a great start for each day. Each evening, we were welcomed back with a delicious assortment of appetizers and choice of wines while enjoying interesting & fun conversations with other guests. The staff at Petite Auberge was fantastic with their genuine friendliness and helpfulness. Petite Auberge is located in the heart of downtown San Francisco close to Cable Cars, Chinatown and wonderful restaurants. Petite Auberge was our perfect "home away from home"on our visit to San Francisco.

title: “Great for a staycation.”
text: We (me, my wife and 3 yr old son) went to enjoy the last weekend of the Oasis water park as it closes for the year at the end of October; yet the weather is still fantastic We are locals and our pool gets to be too cold to use around mid September. We could not have been more pleased. The water park is a blast and when it closed at 4:30 the pool and hot tub near our room were still available. The water temp in the water park was heated to low 80's, about perfect when the air temp is around 90. We plan to return as soon as the Oasis re-opens in February.

title: “Fantastic hotel, wonderful staff!”
text: We recently spent three nights at the Palomar and had a fantastic stay. From the moment we arrived we were made to feel welcome. Nothing was too much trouble for the staff, from the doormen, receptionists and restaurant staff etc., to the brilliant concierge Philip, who was more than helpful and went the extra mile to offer excellent customer service. The hotel was in a superbly convenient location for access to what Washington DC has to offer. There with plenty of good restaurants in the immediate area. We had executive king rooms which were large, well furnished and stylish, with an extremely comfortable bed. The hotel had wine, fruit and a selection of meats and crackers sent to our room as we were celebrating our 25th wedding anniversary. The wine reception each evening was great, it was good to mingle with other guests and pick up tips on what to do in Washington. Overall a most enjoyable experience, I would definitely recommend the hotel and would book a Kimpton hotel for future holidays.

title: “just booked for best friends wedding night!”
text: customer service was great since i was purchasing this for my best friend getting married mid june. i have had problems with other hotels and sending me an authorization form, the rep was super helpful explaining the suites to me. only con i have is that there is no romance or honeymoon or wedding night packages!!??!?!? i really expected with how lovely this place seems for wedding and celebrations and the fact they had their own beautiful spa that there would be an enhancement package of some sort available to make their night amazing :( Im having to book on such short notice within nearly 2 weeks of wedding because of a super bad experience the couple had with another hotel and their reservations :( its hard having to purchase separate add-ons now and using an authorization form for each :( and my husband and i will now have to beat the bride and groom to their own room to fill it with candles and strawberries and champage. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE ZAZA its summertime and wedding season please make a romance package and offer maybe a bath butler and breakfast in bed and a late check out and a spa couples package!!! its such a hassle doing this all separate, but as far as i can tell the hotel is beautiful and hopefully the suite "splendito" is equally as beautiful :)

title: “A different type of hotel”
text: This is a 'different but very enjoyable hotel in LA. It is convenient for many attractions. The rooms were themed and absolutely fantastic. Dining was informal Californian, but food was very acceptable. The staff were pleasant and very helpful.

title: “Little gem in the middle of the loop”
text: Don't let the outside of this hotel fool you. It's a small hotel with comfortable quiet rooms. While the view out of our windows was the rooftop of a smaller building, the room made up for it. And yes, because of the decor and the direction our room faced - the room was somewhat dark, but it was ok. Unless you're spending all day in the room, it shouldn't be an issue. The bed was super comfy and the room was clean. Staff was friendly, including the valet downstairs. It's located in the middle of the loop within walking distance to everything.

title: “Great location, Unprofessional Management!”
text: Fortunate enough that I am in NY for work. I have been in 3 hotels, and I like this one the best. However; due to my experience with the unprofessionalism of the front office management, I would not recommend this particular location to anyone working or vacationing.

title: “Outstanding”
text: We received wonderful service from everyone especially Kevin who provided us with daily taxi's, wonderful directions, info, etc. Breakfast and happy hour was great everyday. Our Granddaugter loved it. Yolanda the person who cleaned our room was really great.

title: “Small but Enjoyable”
text:
This Kimpton hotel is in a great location, blocks from Dupont Circle without being in the middle of it all. It is a small property, with rooms on the smaller side but very comfortable. The balcony rooms they tend to charge a little extra for, but we've found that the ones on lower floors actually let a lot of traffic noise in from the road in front of the hotel. 
The restaurant in the hotel, Firefly, is quite good and is a favorite of locals and visitors alike. 
Each time we've stayed here we've had an enjoyable stay and any issues during are stay were immediately addressed and resolved.

title: “Superb!”
text:
We stayed at the Distrikt Hotel from September 23rd – 30th. This place is superb and deserves its fabulous reputation! Few highlights for us:
• The staff are fantastic, really friendly and happy to help you out, whatever you need.
• The rooms are really well appointed – loads of space, flat screen TV, top quality coffee/tea machine, WiFi, superb towels and the beds are SO comfy! Just what you need after a hard days sightseeing.
• There’s loads of extra little touches like a welcome brownie in the room on arrival, a special delivery of cheesecake as we were there to celebrate our birthdays, chocolates and a weather card waiting on your bed every evening and a New York Times outside your door every morning.
• The location is just perfect – a 5 minute walk from Times Square and there’s a subway station at the end of the street. We weren’t troubled at all by the parole office or sex shop – to be honest I don’t think we would have noticed them at all had we not read about them on here. 
All in all a fabulous hotel, we’ll definitely stay here again when we come back and I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it to anyone. Thanks DIstrikt for a fab stay!

title: “Nice hotel!”
text:
We only needed a hotel for a one night stop and chose this hotel based on other reviews. We were very happy with the hotel. We were greeted by very friendly and helpful desk staff workers who gave us a list of nearby restaurants. The room was clean and fresh with a very comfortable bed. The free breakfast was great and was kept well stocked despite several groups who hit the breakfast area all at the same time. Every employee we came into contact with was friendly.
I feel this hotel is an excellent value and would not hesitate to recommend it to anyone staying in the area.

title: “Not sure where all the good reviews are coming from!”
text:
We stayed here when we were in Austin for 2 nights because it was so highly rated on trip advisor. To give the management their due the service was faultless, to compensate for a mix up in our booking (their fault) they put us in the Longhorn suite for no extra cost (i have no idea if it should have cost extra or if the room rates are all the same!)
Beyond the courteous staff the hotel has very little to offer. The corridor outside our room smelt horribly of very strong food. The inside of the room was musty and didn't seem particularly clean, especially the longhorn memorabilia.
Of course this is a cheap motel and as such can't provide luxury, but we wouldn't stay here again no matter how good a deal it was.

title: “Pretty Good!!!”
text:
I recently stayed in the hotel for 4 days. The staff are really friendly and the hotel is clean. Its not the diggest in the world, but thats a nice change for NY. The rooms, ok, are a bit worn out, but they are clean, and the daily room service is fantastic. Fresh clean towels every day, and you can more or less get anything you ask for. Walls are a bit thin so be warned! 
If you are looking for action near to Times Square this is fantastic location, but i went out around Chelsea and in Lower Manhatten and it was a bit of a pain getting a cab back etc. The nearest subway in 2 1/2 blocks away at 50th. Overall though, i couldn't complain, I have stayed in a lot worse.

title: “hidden gem”
text:
Booked this for a conference in the seaport district. The location is walkable to everything downtown. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The staff was great- Matt W. was a favorite for my whole team staying there. And the water bottles were a nice touch and very convenient!
Because of the staff and location I will be booking a room here for my next conference!

title: “They were great, we would stay there again”
text: We were there for our first anniversary, for 4 nights. We were very pleased with it all. We were very impressed with our housekeeper, Karen...her personality, her attitude, the encouraging notes she left for us, her attention to detail, etc.

title: “dissappointed”
text: beds not very comfortable. too noisy during the evening(sirens) They charge your credit card as soon as you arrive for your full stay and then hold an extra $200.00 per day, of your stay. so go with plenty of money in your account. All this, they do not tell you when you arrive. When we complained we were offered a free breakfast as the best they could do.

title: “Very Kid Friendly”
text:
Just stayed there last weekend with my wife, 4 year old and 1 year old and the stay was excellent. We stayed there 2 years ago as well.
I really like the pool set up. There are great areas for all ages from toddlers to an adult only pool. We spent to majority of the time in the kiddie pool but also went into some of the other pools and the slide is very popular with the kids. Service around the pool area was very attentive.
Not sure if they do it every night but both nights(fri and sat) we were there they had smores at 8pm and an outdoor movie at 9pm. 
The staff was very courteous from check in to check out. Our room was 4304 which was convenient to the pool, had a balcony and an ok view.
Kids 5 and under eat free and they have a breakfast and dinner buffet that is $15.95 for the adults. The breakfast buffet is really nice with pretty much everything you would want. The dinner buffet could use some improvement but very convenient when you have kids. Self parking is free and I think the valet is about $15/day.
Fiesta Texas is right next door as well a very nice upscale shopping center. Seaworld is about a 15-20 minute drive.
The pool water was a litte colder than expected. When we called they said it was heated to 85 but it definitely wasn't. It should warm up naturally though soon.
I would definitely reccommend and will probably go again this summer.

title: “Great overnight stay in Seattle”
text: We live an hour away from Seattle, and stayed here on a Saturday night to meet friends in town for the weekend. Great location, great price and the room was fine. While I would not choose this hotel if I planned to spend a lot of time in the room (the bathroom is particularly tiny...), it was the perfect choice for an overnight visit that included a visit to the nearby Seattle Art Museum, dinner near Pioneer Square and shopping. Friendly staff and Seattle's Best Coffee connected to the lobbymade it extra nice. Will stay here again!

title: “Terrific!”
text:
This hotel is not in the heart of downtown or the "cool" shopping areas, but it's within walking distance of the Experience Music Project, the Family Fun center, and several restaurants. AND the parking is free! Being slightly off the beaten track means it's a little quieter, too.
We drove up from Portland to attend a Mariners game, spending one night here. Our room was spotless and smelled fresh (something we never take for granted when traveling!), the beds were comfortable, the breakfast was bountiful, and the staff were SO polite and helpful! My husband wandered out to the front desk at 9:30 p.m. and requested a down pillow. Bam! There it was, cheerfully procured. 
We walked 7 blocks to a Mexican restaurant called Peso's. YUMMMM! High-end Mexican food, plus a colorful decor, and attractive wait staff. Not especially appropriate for our 7-year-old - no kids' menu - but he was happy with a cheese quesadilla.
We will stay at the Hampton from now on!

title: “Great location, but the valet service and facility left me shaking my head”
text: I was booked for one night at the Ritz-Carlton, Los Angeles, on November 16 for business. When I drove into the valet driveway (3:30 PM), there was nobody in sight. I proceeded to unload my three bags from my SUV myself... until someone finally asked about my car (that wasn't until I was in the lobby waiting in line for the front desk). Strike one. My room was on the 25th floor, requiring a transfer to a second elevator each time I went up and down (the lift from the lobby only goes to the 24th floor). Strike two. While the room was beautiful and well appointed, there was no electrical outlet near the desk and the WiFi was intermittent (both critical for business travelers). Strike three. Lastly, it took several very long minutes to get hot water to the shower in the morning. Strike... um, four. On a positive note, all staff that I actually interacted with were very friendly and nice... and the rooms were very comfortable... but I expected more from a modern Ritz-Carlton property.

title: “Good modern compact hotel...”
text: First time at a Yotel.... At first it's interesting intriguing and a tad confusing. But once oriented it's a great concept. The cabins are an efficient and thoroughly cool design but they are compact. For one person it's perfect but for two you better really like each other! The best surprise was dinner one night at Doh Yo the restaurant..... Alll small plates and wonderful! Still dreaming of the dessert..... Churrahs! Oh my!:-)

title: “Old & Out Dated”
text:
We stayed here because this hotel was close to family and old friends. The room was in need of deep cleaning, new bedding, new carpet, decor & paint. We had a king room, but no king pillows on the bed. the wall paper border, bed spread, curtins and pics in the room were all mix matched. There were several maint issues that needed to be tended to, such as the bathroom light shorting out. When we got into bed the smell of mildew was so strong we had to stuff the pillows between the matress and wall to keep from smelling it and be able to sleep. The coffee maker would not stay on and you could see where they tried to fix it with tape. 
This place needs to be closed down by the bord of health!
ONE MORE THING...Don't bother askin for a late check out!

title: “Loved The London and will definitely return!”
text: Our stay was for eight days. The rooms are very large for NYC and very clean. Beds are extremely comfortable and great sound proofing. We could not hear any noise from the street. Service is impeccable as well. The staff did an outstanding job making us feel welcome. Maid service and room service was top notch. We have stayed at many five star hotels in the city and I would rate this one number one for room size, amenities and excellent staff. We will definitely stay at The London on future visits.

title: “Really Enjoyed Hotel 1000”
text:
My wife and I escaped down to Seattle for a 2 day getaway and booked a superior room at the Hotel 1000. The room was wonderfully spacious with all the modern amenities you could expect. I loved the funky tub that filled from the ceiling and thought the free VOIP calls were a bonus (although why not free to Vancouver BC?) My only gripe, and it goes for all Seattles downtown hotels is the scandalous parking charges - why is it $35 to park when the lot across the street is $18?
Would we return - absolutely!

title: “Great Place to Stay!!!!”
text:
This is one of the best kept secret's in San Antonio! Tucked out of the way, about 2-3 blocks from the Riverwalk. The staff is amazing! They are very friendly and helpful! We have been staying there for the past 3 yrs and same staff each year so that says a lot to me about the management! Very very clean hotel, minutes from the AT&T Center, downtown, anywhere a person would want to go! Super easy access to IH 10 or IH 35. Has shuttle that will take you downtown and pick you up! Breakfast is very good and good varity! Parking lot is gated after dark on the street side and security guard at the entrance felt totally safe and felt my vehicle was safe! 
Wouldn't even consider staying anywhere else!

title: “Beautiful hotel and perfect location for touristy things”
text: I stayed here when I ran the Marine Corp marathon. The location is perfect for anyone wanting to take part in touristy things in DC. Just blocks from the capitol and blocks from Union Station, accessing the subway is incredibly easy. It was nice that the race organizers had a bus for us to take to the expo. If you want some serious excercise, you can walk the national mall, smithsonian, and monuments, but I suggest taking the subway to get there. The only downside is that right across the street is a fire station so we heard fire sirens often. Ask for a room away from the fire station and you will be fine. We did not dine in the restaurants. Gorgeous room, great service.

title: “cozy and near the beach!”
text:
My family and I took up five rooms, and were very happy with the rates, service, and pool-spa.
The staff was kind, accomadating, and friendly. Sure, it's not the Ritz, but you get a kitchen with a fridge, stove,pots and pans, and don't pay 200 a night.

title: “Kind of strange location, but very convenient, spotless, great breakfast and the pool was heated enough to swim in March”
text:
Stayed here for 2 nights with my family in March. It is very close to everything, but the location is a little different, not a bunch of hotels but sort of semi warehouses. You can walk to old town in about five minutes. The staff was so organized, we asked for directions to the nearest grocery store and were given a printed sheet with directions to pretty much everything you might need. Also suggested some great restaurants. 
 Room was clean, breakfast was nice (bagels/muffins/make own waffles/juice/hardboiled eggs/cereal/ toast, fruit and so on)
 I was very pleased that the pool was heated enough for my kids to swim in March, it was a great way to wind down after a long day at Midway and the zoo.

title: “Breakfast was how much??”
text:
We were able to utilized their “romance” package, which including an upgrade to a balcony room, valet parking, breakfast (room service), champagne, late check out (3 pm) and Hershey’s kisses. The hotel is located in a pretty residential area with tons of interesting shops, like the Red Onion, a second hand music and book store. The room was large, we had a comfortable king sized bed, sofa, ottoman, desk, 2 chairs and an HD TV. Bathroom was really tiny but clean. We were on the 3rd floor, so we heard noise from people entering & leaving the restaurant but the hallways & floor above us
 were very quiet. My husband is an exterminator and since there has been an outbreak of bed bugs, he checked every surface. I’m happy to report, he didn’t see any bug evidence. The lobby is tiny but everyone was attentive and we always had help when needed. You have to call for your car 10/15 minutes ahead of time I liked the wine served at cocktail hour. Oreo cookies and milk are available in the lobby after 10 pm and was a sweet way to end the night.
 A few things that prevent us from giving the hotel an A are:
1 – We ordered room service for breakfast, 2 orders of eggs with bacon, homefries and coffee. That’s all we received, no butter/jelly for toast, no milk/cream for coffee or salt & pepper. We received the “extra “ items within 8 minutes of calling the lobby. Breakfast was included in our package but we were given a bill for $44.00 (FOR BREAKFAST), which was not worth it, extremely overpriced. 
2 – We received a bill in the morning that had one price, when we checked out the bill was different. Of course, we were charged for the overpriced breakfast TWICE. Not a big deal once the error was explained but it took 10 minutes and two people to credit the $ back. 
3 – The hallway on the 3rd floor has a slight sour smell, like a pipe connected to the bathroom had a leak. 
4 - Our car was left in the front of the hotel for about an hour, again not a big deal but since you have to pay over $ 30.00 for parking it should be taken care of fairly quickly. 
Overall, we had a relaxing, comfortable stay and we would return but would not order room service. We’ll go back to Five Guys for awesome burgers about a 5-minute walk away.

title: “Parker House : good location, tiny rooms, noisy”
text: The room was tiny, and everything from next door was audible. So I didn't think it was 5 star. And I didn't think it was worth the hefty charge, for that I thought breakfast should be provided. But the history of the hotel was interesting, and the neighbourhood was fascinating.

title: “Terrible Customer Service!”
text: I was really disappointed with how rude the front desk staff was. I expected a much better experience with the Ramada name. My hotel key didn't work the first time (not a big deal, that's happened at other hotels too) so I lugged two suitcases in the tiny elevator back down to the front desk. Then my second set of keys didn't work either. I found a phone in the 5th floor hallway and asked if a bellboy or someone could bring a third set of keys up so I didn't have to make the trip with the suitcases again. I was told no, I would have to return to the lobby. Luckily, my third set of keys worked, but there was no apology given. In fact, it was almost the opposite, like I was inconveniencing THEM!! The room was TINY, not like the picture showed on their website. The shower dripped all night and there was a really strange smell in the hallway. We did like the bar/restaurant attached to the hotel. That was a perk. But we didn't like it enough to ever stay there again! We will not be returning to this hotel.

title: “Great Service but rooms need urgent update”
text: The staff at this hotel are exceptional. Unfortunately the room we stayed in had an offensive smell. I believe the carpet in both the hallway and room needs replacing.

title: “Comfortably beds, nice views, convenient location, but charge for internet”
text:
Comfortably beds, nice views above the 22nd floor, convenient location, but annoying daily charge for internet usage. This hotel seems to cater primarily to corporate conference attendees. Close to good restaurants and shops. Pleasant walking area.
We came in late and wanted to check email for 10 minutes before going to bed. That would have cost us $14 a day, but the day was almost over. We went to the lobby where the wifi connection was so-so. First a message came up that said, usage is full, then after twenty minutes we were able to get on, with sometimes slow speeds.

title: “SPEECHLESS...MOMENT FOR LIFE”
text: I really don't know where to start or end, from the time i spoke with guess services I felt so relaxed and at ease. When I pulled up at the hotel and enter the lobby I was really impressed and was greeted within seconds. I went past the lounge for a second and the ambiance was very nice but couldn't wait to get to the room. The suite was a wow!!!, minutes later i recieve a knock at the door from the manager himself with a bottle of champayne for my anniversary.OVERALL THE STAFF WAS SCARY NICE (LOL), and our stay was a night to remember. You have to experience it for yourself, I can't wait to go back . ENJOY YOUR STAY....ENJOY THE STAFF...

title: “Warm, Friendly and Elegant”
text: I love this property!! It is very historic, elegant and the service is great and it is in by far the BEST location in the city.

title: “room nice, service?”
text: My husband and I had a good sized room on the 9th floor facing the Peabody. I was disappointed with the service. I came to surprise my sister who had traveled from MN. She did not know that we had driven down and checked into the same hotel. When I arrived I called the front desk and asked them to call my room when she checked in. They could not give me her room number for privacy reasons and I understood this. After waiting and calling down to the front desk twice and being told that she had not arrived yet my husband and I decided to go ahead down to Beale as we only had 2 nights there. As an after thought when we got down to the lobby, I again asked the front desk if she had checked in. They said "oh, yes she did about 15 minutes ago, we told her to call your room." They immediately rang her room and when I went to greet her she told me they had checked in 45 minutes before! In fact she said the people at the front desk mumbled something about calling room 954 but she did not understand what they were trying to tell her! As an after thought I guess if I had slipped them some money at the front desk I might have gotten better service. I didn't think I should have to do that for a simple common courtesy. Also the pop machine on the 9th floor was sold out the entire 3 days we were there!

title: “Expected more!!”
text: Apart from lack of services within d hotel ex. Bar or restaurant or drinks in the room your member of staff has been more than accommodating so far he has been d friendliest face on our trip and has gone out of his way to meet our needs the best he can you should consider Robert for a nice big pay rise due to him I'd recommend the hotel to friends thank you Robert(reception) :)

title: “Great in-city place to experience Seattle's unitque waterfront”
text: Staff were very professional and eager to be of service. Went out of way to make sure we had what we needed. Lounge and dining room had great serrvice and food. Our room was stuffy and had limited air circulation. Finally able to get window open for fresh air but would have liked stop lock for security. Shower was fantastic! Fitness room had nice equipment but was small for the amount of use it was getting when we were there.Parking was quite pricey but in-out was available.

title: “A Fantastic Seattle Boutique Hotel Experience @ A Great Rate”
text: Three cheers for the staff @ the Hotel Andra. At all points of contact I felt welcomed & assisted in a professional but warm manner. We were provided a complimentary upgrade on our room type (without our asking) when the front desk noted that they had room to do so. Room service was fantastic (gourmet larger than life BLT sandwiches and delicious kebabs & dips). Big comfy robes, cool ambiance, and a blissful sleep. The hotel is a bit older (like most in Seattle) but extremely clean and decor has been upgraded with a modern contemporary look/feel. I'm confident that we couldn't have found a better boutique hotel for a better price. A great experience - we will stay here again next time we travel down to Seattle for a getaway weekend!

title: “Dallas Fairmont nice with few elevators for manyh floors”
text: After reading reviews was concerned about the hotel. However, it was acceptable, clean and bed comfortable. Walls a little thin. Great location and walking distance of excellent reatuarants. Would stay here again.

title: “Beware of this place!”
text:
Upfront - we canceled our reservation after having to contact the Sheriton Headquarters. The hotel did not disclose the $43.00 (Almost $50 with tax) nightly rate for parking. I spoke with numerous people about it including the General Manager who hung up on me when I asked for the name and number of his supervisor in Sheraton.
In my opinion, they tease you with a good rate, then hit you with the parking fees to make up for it. Other nearby hotels charge from $20-30 per night so be sure to facter in parking with the 15% tax rate on it when you are determining your cost.
When I called the Sheraton in New York, they offered to reduce the parking rate slightly, but by then I was so upset about what seemed like a bait and switch practice, I canceled the reservation and stayed at another nearby hotel - who only charged $20 per night!
Just a word of warning - you'll get little or no sympathy or accomodation if you complain about anything at this place.

title: “Just what we wanted”
text: Off the beaten path, clean suite, free parking, complimentary breakfast. The suite was perfect for this family of 2 parents and a teenager. Board games need to be replaced, but front desk loaned us a deck of cards. Front desk and housekeeping very professional and helpful. After very busy days, it was nice to return to our quiet "home". This is the first hotel (ever!) that we did not hear slamming doors and loud guests in the hallways.

title: “Average Hilton hotel”
text:
Stayed here for business for a couple of days and the hotel had everything you could expect from a Hilton hotel. The service was very good and I got a friendly greeting at the front desk.
Got a room at the 20'th floor with a nice view of the waterfront. The room was pretty old but it was clean. The doors at the hotel was a bit noisy and every time someone slammed the door shut in the corridor I woke up.
The breakfast was served at the top floor and you could enjoy your breakfast with a stunning view of Seattle.

title: “Enjoyed the Hilton Garden Inn”
text: I stayed in Late April Early May for a Seminar and this hotel was just fine. The room was sufficient and was less money then the Seminar sponsored hotels and it is only three blocks from Michigan Avenue and all the action. There is a subway/metro entrance directly in front of the property if you need public transport, but not to be confused with EL or the Elevated Train, which could be loud in the evening. Great Stay and Drama Free..

title: “Hard Beds”
text: Convient location, you are able to walk to the T. Bakery on the corner, Starbucks across the street, and Whole Foods behind the Hotel. Valet parking attendants are lazy, and don't forget to budget an extra $40 to park for the night, bell boy bums ciggs. Do not do the breakfast for $16.95, go to Whole Foods, better food, service and price. Beds are hard. The rooms were well sized for Boston, and clean. Once the renavations are complete this hotel may have more going for it than location. I probably will not give it another chance though.

title: “Lovely, clean rooms, friendly staff”
text:
We enjoyed the most was simple, fresh design of the room. It was spacious and included a kitchenette. A lot of windows and light. The staff is most hospitable.
We were disappointed that there is a fee for Wi Fi..

title: “Convenient hotel”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 4 nights. I am from DC so I am not sure if this is normal for LA but the restaurant and gift shop prices were VERY high. The only problems I experienced was with the parking gate, my card kept not registering and causing me to have to park and go inside. I would suggest a better way of coming and going especially when you are staying multiple days. Also, my room was next to the laundry room, I suggest making that for staff or something. Caused A LOT of noise in my room. My bed was huge and comfortable. All and all I had a wonderful experience.

title: “Almost perfect”
text: I stayed at the Westin, as I was taking the train from Union Station. Check-in took minutes. They up graded me to a suite on the 14th floor. Room was spot less, bed was great. Had dinner in my room, it arrived in about 20 minutes. Had breakfast in room, it came in about 15 minutes. Check out was a breeze. Hotel was maybe 10-15 minutes to the train station, so worked out great. I have stayed at this hotel numorous times and have never encounted a problem.

title: “WWWonderful Stay!”
text: Beautiful hotel with very friendly and energetic staff. And my dog was treated to the same excellent service as I was.

title: “Enjoyed!”
text:
I have mostly good things to say about the hotel. Great location in the University District. Fashionable, updated hotel in the Art-Deco style. Clean rooms and bathrooms with super comfortable beds and (even more important) pillows. I always bring my own toiletries on my trips, but this time I liked the ones provided by the hotel so much, I did not use mine. Both shampoo and conditioner were of great quality. As a matter of fact, nothing about his hotel seemed cheep to me. Everything was done with a good taste and a comfort in mind.
One drawback was the service. We had waited for 3 hours for the empty cups so we could drink some tea in our room. I had to call the front desk 3 times.

title: “Quality Was Somewhere Between Poor and Average”
text: I booked this hotel for $59 online for a Friday night knowing that it was not in the best area, although there were some very nice hotels in the same area at a much higher price. I'm white, and I was among a very low minority of the hotel guests. I did, however, feel quite safe. I could tell that hotel was trying to improve its appearance. Some areas were much better than others. For example, the hall carpeting on the second floor looked new; on the first floor it looked dirty and worn. In the elevators, it was downright despicable. There was no apparent AC in the hallways and a sign on the ice machine on the second floor referred me to the third floor. The one on the third floor didn't work and didn't have a sign. The first impression of the room was good, although all the lamp shades were askew and there were only three pillows on the king-size bed. The carpeting in the room looked new but was in need of being shampooed. Neither of the bedsize table lights seemed to work. A staff person brought up bulbs, but that didn't help. Finally, he brought another lamp and plugged it into the lamp on the desk. With some effort, I pulled the bed away from the wall and discovered the two non-working lamps had cords that were dangling from the outlet behind the bed. I reseated the plugs, and one of the two lamps began to work. As the switch on the non-working lamp was broken, I really couldn't be sure it I had turned it on. I did not reposition the bed as it would have knocked the plugs free of the outlet once again.

title: “Well, you get what you pay for ...”
text:
Good points about the Francisco Bay Inn:
- Hotel situated on relatively safe part of town, walkable to Fisherman's Wharf, Crookedest Street, a laundromat
- Elevator for those of us who aren't light travellers
- Microwave and refrigerator in room
- Free parking
- Free breakfast
Bad points:
- Very open corridors but we were given a Fourth Floor "inset" room (Room 436) with an outer door (in addition to our room door) so that made us feel just a little safer
- Severely limited parking spaces (you are allowed to double parking in the parking lot if you leave your car keys with the Front Desk so they can play musical chairs with the double-parked cars in the AM)
- Rather surly on-site managers/receptionists/owners (?) -- they are the same two persons with matching attitude problem
- Breakfast consists of only coffee, hot chocolate, muffins, Danish, croissants
Personal experience at the hotel that may or may not happen to you:
Had to unclog bathtub drain-hole of wads of hair by myself using, of course, feet of toilet paper in order for us to take a shower that first night. That didn't do much so, the next morning, had to ask Front Desk to send for a plumber. Clogged drain problem only somewhat fixed for the rest of our stay.
Advice:
Forget the high-fat, all-processed sugars breakfast provided by the hotel. Buy cereal and milk from the convenience store across the street or another store just three blocks away for your breakfast.

title: “great place to enjoy SF”
text: Had a chance to stay at the Clift recently, hotel was amazing with a great view of downtown SF. The staff was great, everyone from the valet to the front-desk were extremely helpful and made me feel very much at home.

title: “Great getaway and very dog friendly”
text: My husband and I stayed at Pier 5 along with our dog and had a wonderful time. The staff were quite friendly and helpful. Although we were overcharged by $100, this was easily resolved at check-out. The room was very comfortable and spacious. The room also had a nice large bathroom and a sweet balcony to sit and sip our free bloody marys on Sunday morning. We look forward to going back for another weekend escape...so does our dog.

title: “Wonderful stay”
text:
I went to the Hotel Metro one week in January with a friend, it was my second time there and it was even better than the first time.
We arrived earlier than the check-in so we were upgraded because we had to wait for the room. So we had a bigger room with a view on the Empire State Building. It was excellent!
The breakfast included is a real pleasure, big muffins, bagels, bread, cereals, juice, coffee... all that in a great atmosphere.
The room service was excellent too, the bed was huge and the mattress perfect!
The hotel is extremely well located near the Macy's and the Empire State Building, you can't ask for a better location.
The hotel has also a terrace on the roof and it's wonderful! You go there and you see the Empire State Building right in front of you!!! EXCEPTIONAL!
I won't hesitate if I go to New-York another time!

title: “Very enjoyable...recommended”
text: What can you say...intimacy kit and oxygen provided in the room, seems they thought of everything! Bar excellent, service could be better, overall recommended

title: “2nd visit not as good as the 1st”
text:
I reviewed this hotel in Feb 08 and gave it a great review. However we experienced a number of problems this time which detracted from their previous service.
We made a booking for a room with 2 beds, one for us and one for our teenager. They turned out to be very small double beds, (almost incapable of holding two grown adults), not queens which are the usual size in most upscale hotels of this category. Unfortunately they were also very uncomfortable which is strange as we have found Hyatt beds so comfortable previously we even considered buying one! 
Secondly our room had a connecting door to the next room. There was a lock for safety, unfortunately it didn't stop any noise which meant that we could hear every conversation, cough and pin drop next door. 
Thirdly when we tried to fill the bath the plug would not work and the bath drained quicker than it was filling. Unfortunately we only found this out at 11pm on our first night. After reporting it next morning it was mended before 6pm. It meant that we only had a chance to use the bath on one of our two nights stay, which was a bit of a let down.
Fourthly, when we tried to arrange a later checkout they could not accommodate us. Odd as we didn't have a problem the previous time we stayed, even though we booked the room on points on both occasions.
Lastly, when we went down to catch a taxi to the airport there was no porter to be seen anywhere. We were jumped on by two taxi drivers parked in the loop who ended up heatedly arguing over us in the middle of the Grand Hyatt driveway/lobby door area. Not exactly the behavior expected in a hotel of this class. A porter should be there at all times to organise transport, baggage, etc and to assist guests of the hotel We ended up walking onto the street to hail another taxi to avoid the argument.
Our experience this time means we will reconsider our accommodation options during our next visit to Seattle.

title: “Superb Location”
text:
Picked this Hotel based on cost and previous reviews. We was not disappointed. The location is ideal being only 2 blocks from Grand Central Station and in easy walking distance of many of main attractions.
Clean throughout, towels changed daily, staff helpful, good size room but bathroom dated and in need of decoartion - but hey it was clean and acceptable. Didn't have a view but what do you want for your money - we were out most of the day & night. Nice to be able to open windows and get some fresh air. 
Summary - a good well positioned hotel at attractive rates.

title: “Good value, very nice people”
text:
Everyone I came in contact with was really nice and flexible. It was comfortable, clean, and affordable. I've read some of the other reviews and would say they must have made some changes more recently. I stayed here in mid May (traveling through on my way back home and needed a place to rest), and I didn't have any problems.
I would recommend it.

title: “Manager has bad manners”
text: I recently stayed at the Fitzpatrick Grand Central Hotel in Manhattan. I was there with my sixteen-year-old daughter. My husband had recently passed on and this vacation was meant to hopefully cheer up her spirits. A friend of mine had suggested I go to New York, as the shops there are more reasonable then here in Ireland. I knew of the Fitzpatrick Castle in Killiney and was pleasantly surprised to find out there was one in New York. I must say that my stay at the hotel was not pleasant at all. Although the clerks and bellman where especially nice and attentive to my needs the hotel manager George Chavitz was rude and disrespectful to my daughter. One day while we were eating at the hotel restaurant she went to the bathroom, but before entering was stopped by the hotel manager who asked her in a threatening manner if she was a guest at the hotel. He remained at the door until she came out and followed her back to our table! She was very upset, as was I, but we didn’t want to start trouble. Whenever we entered the hotel the bellman greeted us with a warm welcome, but when we past Mr. Chavitz’s desk he looked at us as if we didn’t belong there. When we were checking out the clerk suggested that we can obtain boarding passes from the hotel, but when they directed us to Mr. Chavitz he became irritated, telling me that he was busy and I would have to come back later. This man made our stay extremely uncomfortable and he could care less. It amazes me how a well respected man like Mr. Fitzpatrick can choose a manger like Mr. Chavitz to represent his hotel. I found out that there was another Fitzpatrick in Manhattan and I highly recommend that anyone thinking about the Grand Central Fitzpatrick should try the other hotel to avoid this very rude man.

title: “great place to stay”
text:
My daughter and I stayed here during our first trip to New York . It was a great location, spotlessly clean, and the staff were very helpful. The rooms are small but adequate. The beds were very comfortable. Our room had views of the Empire State Building from both the bedroom and bathroom...what more could you ask? Loads of places to eat in the area, and if you are vegetarian there is a great Korean vegan restaurant a few blocks down on E32nd st called Hangawi, which serves fantastic food in great surroundings.
Only slight downside, and no fault of the hotel at all was that it is quite noisy....but it is New York. I would definitely stay here again on my next visit.

title: “Very good”
text:
We stayed at this allocated accommodation for one night at the beginning and for another night at end, of our 11 day fly drive tour of US Rockies in early and mid June.
On a our first visit, we had problems, in that the travel documentation had not been left at the front desk as indicated by our UK travel company and Kevin on front desk, was very helpful in trying to track down the literature via the US travel Company, even though it was out of working hours. He said the management would deal with it overnight. After a long transatlantic flight, this was the last thing we wanted. It so happened a rep from the US travel company turned up the next morning and gave us all our documentation. On the second check in, the front desk clerk Sato, was not as efficient and seemed to think we were paying for the room ourselves rather than through a voucher from the travel company. It took a bit of explaining to her!
Our first room was in the Plaza block on the second floor and did face the inner square, so it didn’t have much of a view. However on the second stay, we were again in the Plaza block but on the 5th floor overlooking 16th Street mall and the main entrance.
We used the restaurant once for breakfast buffet, which was fairly good, although the hot dishes were slightly cool. We also had an evening meal in The Yard House, which was buzzing and lively, and the food was very good and we thought reasonably priced. Service was also very good considering how many people were in there.
The rooms are a good size and the beds very comfortable. The staff, on the whole, were friendly and helpful.
The only slight criticisms are that valet parking is expensive, $28 on the first visit and then increased to $29, 10 days later. Our first room on the second floor had a long walk from the Lift (elevator) and there are no clear instructions in the room (or on the TV) of all the hotel facilities and where they are. It is a huge complex, on both sides of Court Place!

title: “In this time it was perfect”
text:
I was in Lombardy from April 13 to April 22.
In this time the hotel was perfect.
All the staff is very friendly, helpful and I didnt have any trouble like the stay in September that I described here.

title: “Just off MI Ave and on the Lake”
text:
Swissotel Chicago is on the corner of the river and lake, just about 2 blocks off Michigan Ave. Be prepared for slightly uphill walk if you are shopping MI Ave. That is the only downside to the location, but you may enjoy the access south to Millenium Park. The Chicago bus does come in front and along with El (rail) very easy to use. 
Rooms were good, nothing spectacular about them except the views. The building is tirangular shaped, and we could see Millenium Park. Bath is roomy with separate shower. Single sink and tub were nice also. Room included desk & chair along with casual chair & ottoman. 
Overall good but not great 4* hotel. The rate we received on travelzoo special $159/nt for labor day weekend was ok. If you want to be in the middle on MI ave shopping, this is not the best location, but a nicer hotel at decent rate (less than $200) this is a good choice.

title: “Park Plaza-Boston”
text: The Park Plaza was just as good as it looked online. What a great location too; it's easy to walk the whole Freedom Trail and explore the city. It's in a convenient location with tons of great restaurants. We had a wonderful brunch every morning. We will definitely stay here again when in Boston.

title: “Great Stay for Quick Getaway!”
text: Very helpful and polite front desk clerks. Great valet service. The non suite rooms are small but very clean. Great downtown location, close to the ballpark!

title: “Enjoyable Stay in the Windy City”
text:
I found this hotel on Priceline booking about a week in advance. Everything ran smoothly at check-in and the hotel staff was friendly, helpful and courteous. The concierge gave some really good advice on restaurants and transportation. 
While this is a historic hotel, the room had a comfortably modern feel, a snazzy bathroom and cozy bed. 
The location is right on Michigan Avenue in the South Loop, so if you're venturing out into Grant Park, you merely need to cross the street. While this is a good location, you'll still need to get on the subway or walk quite a ways to the River North area. The subway is not very far from the hotel at all and the neighborhood typically has a lot of foot traffic so it feels pretty safe. 
The hotel has a very trendy restaurant and a smaller bodega for food options; however, I highly recommend exploring the neighborhood. 
Overall, with the price I paid, this hotel was a great value and highly recommended.

title: “What A Shame”
text: Great location for Boston. Run downed. Needs refreshed. Stayed 2 different times in a 30 day period. 1st stay, had respiratory problems in room. Refused to switch my room. 2nd stay, room reeked of cigarettes. Said smoking not allowed in motel. Sprayed so much freshner, had to open window. Smell returned. Staff refused to switch room. They couldn't smell a thing. Stayed 3 nights with acute headache. Head mechanical person has a very bad anger issue. Seen him "scream" at bus load of customers who were unloading. Made statement "he didn't care WHO they were, he wanted bus to move away, so a single car could move. Should have waited in my opinion. Manager was apologetic, but did nothing. Needs some money invested in it.

title: “Great deal”
text: Clean , safe and friendly. This is a great budget hotel. the building and our room was very clean. The staff are very friendly and helpful. The location is safe and close to downtown. My wife and I had a great stay, there are two very nice places to eat two blocks from the hotel. This is an excellent budget motel not a full service hotel.

title: “Great Times Square location”
text:
We stayed for 6 nights at this hotel. From check-in to check-out we were made to feel welcome. The proximity to Times Square, Theaters, the subway and shopping was excellent. The complimentary breakfast and evening wine and cheese were of a very high standard with friendly and congenial staff. 
When a hotel promotes a restaurant for lunch or dinner, always be wary. In this case both recommendations, Tony Di Napoli's and the Brooklyn Diner were excellent. 
Full marks to all the staff. They were friendly, courteous and helpful. The public areas maintained the consistent theme of "Casablanca". Our room was adequate in size, but not spacious. the amenities in the room were of excellent quality. 
Although New York never sleeps, we did get tired after a full day. Therefore, one drawback was the lack of sound proofing from street noise through the windows. This was a problem especially at night. Having said this, we would readily stay there again, only this time we would ask for a quiet room not facing the street. Live and learn.
We would rate this as one of the top three hotels that we have stayed at

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: I think most of the crappy reviews were written before this hotel was given a complete renovation in December 2007. First, the hotel staff was nothing but wonderful and friendly, and helpful. The place looks new, with all the renovations done. The room was great with granite countertop in bathroom, wall in shower, and counter in walkway (coffee pot area). Flat screen tv, mp3 player plug in on the alarm clock, and very quick valet service. I would suggest valet instead of self park due to the fact that with valet it is one price per day ($24) no matter how many times you go in and out. There was a nice outdoor garden area with tables and chairs set up. We ordered in and ate out there. We have 2 children under the age of 3, so going out to dinner can be a hassle. We really enjoyed our stay, and would come back here on our next visit to Baltimore without question.

title: “Awesome Staff”
text: I always stay at this Hotel. Last time I cam to this Hotel I had lost my credit Card and no cash on me. The staff made exception (FD Agent Nichole) and let me stay for the night on a promise to pay in the morning. Next morning I went to the Bank and paid it to the Hotel

title: “Location, location, style?”
text: The position of this hotel can't be faulted. In the heart of the Gaslamp quarter within easy reach of the harbour front with all it's shops and restaurants the hotel couldn't be better placed if it had been moved there... which it has, brick by brick and apparantly, ghost by ghost. Modern it ain't, but it doesn't pretend to be. The rooms are all individually furnished in a Victorian style to match the exterior and if that appeals you will be ok. It was clean and comfortable, if a little dark in the courtyard rooms, and when we visited, quiet, but I can imagine when full the noise levels may prove bothersome. If you like modern give it a miss, if you want a hotel with character, the location should be a big bonus.

title: “A Wonderful Experience”
text: Having traveled to Baltimore numerous times and staying in the large hotels in the Inner Harbor area, I was looking for a different experience-- something more along the lines of a bed and breakfast. Fortunately, during an internet search, I came across Henderson's Wharf and what a wonderful discovery it was. The weather could not have been more perfect during my all-too-brief three day stay. The staff was friendly and accomodating, the Gardenview room clean, warm and inviting. Should you drive, parking is offered free-of-charge in a secure and convenient parking lot next to the hotel. A wonderful complimentary breakfast awaits you each morning. In addition, complimentary coffee and tea are available 24 hours a day. Should you decide to venture downtown for sightseeing, shopping, dining or to see a ballgame, the downtown area is accessible by Water Taxi, or if you like to walk, by foot. But you will miss nothing by staying in Fells Point, a quaint and picturesque area, to enjoy the many fine restaurants and drinking establishments located within a short walking distance from the hotel. I look forward to my return.

title: “Amazing service, Fantastic Hotel”
text:
I have had to stay at this hotel a couple of times for work. Each time I have been happy with the great service and comfort of the hotel. If you can get a lake view even better. The staff is always willing to go above and beyond. They have arranged delivery and shipping of packages for me without any trouble. 
The last time I stayed I got snowed in and had a high fever and it was the nicest place in the world to get sick. When I called for tea, they brought me my own hot water electric tea kettle to use for my stay so I could make tea whenever I needed it. The bed is luxurious. The bathroom is well laid out. The toiletries were L'Occitane. Wonderfully thick robe and slippers were provided.
I have eaten in the hotel restaurant which has been fine, but not spectacular. Our real favorite is the hot cocoa in the lobby/bar/cafe. It is delightful on cold winter nights. 
If you need to buy some items at the Water Tower Mall the elevators to the hotel give you direct access. Again helpful during the winter when you don't want to take a stroll outside. 
There is a small business center with computer terminals and printers. 
The only negative is taxi drivers seem to not understand there are two different Four Seasons properties and even if you tell them the Water Tower they drive to the wrong one!
A wonderful luxury hotel and I would return again and again, as long as someone else is paying for it!

title: “Loved it!”
text:
I was here for a meeting two weeks ago. Between the location (2 blocks away from the Gallery Place stop on the Metro), the room itself, and the free 24-hour coffee, tea, and hot chocolate in the lobby, I was a happy camper. Most importantly, the employees there were beyond kind and gracious. From the woman who checked me in to the guy that offered me bottled water when I was coming in from an afternoon session, to the folks that thanked me on my way out, these Marriott employees were the best. If the manager is reading this, you need to give them all raises. :)
PS- I love the screen in the lobby with the weather and random news bits, as well as the lounge in the basement. I sneaked down there to watch one of the WCF games because my roommate was asleep. I'm crossing my fingers the fellowship program I'm currently participating in lets us stay there again the next time we have to come to DC!

title: “Convenient location”
text: The hotel is a business class hotel, room was comfortable though may need a little upgrading especially the carpet, the size of the room more than make up the lack of space in the bathroom. Though its a very busy hotel, check-in & check-out is a breeze, concierge is very helpful. Grand Central Station is connected to the hotel with a fantastic food hall where you can get great gourmet food. It is within easy walking distance to all the major tourist haunts.

title: “Very handy to everything”
text: We had an unscheduled layover for one night in SFO on account of the weather, so had to find a good hotel. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom was fine, the view was great. Did not try any of the facilities, so the main impression is its handy location to Market St, the cable car, Moscone and the Union Square shops.

title: “The price is for the location, not the resort itself.”
text: The location was great! Just steps from the bay and one block from the ocean! We spent a lot of time at the ocean so I was pleasantly suprised to see that the ocean was just a very very short walk away. There were plenty of restaurants around as well. It was close to the airport and I felt it was rather centrally located to most attractions we visited. It was just a short drive to: La Jolla, Torrey Pines, The Zoo, Old Town and the city. We stayed in the Tower where if you don't request a view, you will probably get stuck with looking at a parking lot on your balcony. Fortunately, we were high enough up to see the ocean and the bay view as well as the beautiful hills in the background. The area was filled with college aged kids (it was still summer) which was fine for us but some may not like that. The staff was OK. We never told about the free night cruise upon checking in but Kristi (the awesome bartender) told us about the cruise as well as some "must do" things in the area. Most of the front desk staff was pleasant but the young girl who checked us in wasn't exactly warm and welcoming. The hotel grounds were decent and nice and I enjoyed the birds and other decor. You pay for parking which is kind of crazy but you don't really have a choice. The rooms were decent. The bathroom tile looked to be dirty but was probably just scratched up and old. The tub did not drain well at all which was a pain. The bed was comfortable but the walls were pretty thin as we could hear our neighbors. The balcony furniture was pretty gross but I was just hapy we had a balcony with somewhat of a view. Over all, not a bad place to stay but not exactly a 5 star location either. I would put it at average. Not awful but not spectacular.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: This hotel is the perfect place to stay while in Phoenix. Central to most everything with plenty of places nearby to eat. Great meeting spaces with the best catered food I have ever had at a meeting or convention.

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text:
This hotel is very clean with unique decor (it was formerly the old Alamo Bank building).
The free breakfast was delicious. Loved the uncarpeted hallways (much cleaner). My kids loved the rooftop pool and the view of the city from there was amazing. Very nice place to stay

title: “Thanks Wyndham!!!!”
text: Josie Zimmerman was very helpful. I would recommend this location to others because of her southern hospitality

title: “Gem in a perfect location!”
text: My husband and I along with another couple stayed here recently for a couple nights and just loved the location along with the fabulous service! It is a boutique Inn in a great location for food and fun. Located near Pike's Market, you can enjoy all the varied shopping and foods that are available around it. We even sat up on the roof where they have comfortable seating to enjoy our wine and cheese (bought locally) and the lovely view one late afternoon. Charming and worth the reasonable price!

title: “Next time we'll choose another hotel”
text:
We stayed in this hotel 3 nights in May 2010.
The location of the hotel is great - everything in Midtown & Central Park is in short walk. 
The hotel seems to be very old and definatly needs a renovation. 
Rooms are spacious but furniture is old and shabby. The bed is also old and not comfortable. The bathroom was at the same level. The view from the window was to the inner yard - means the view of the wall in front. . 
The breakfast was only available by room service. 
The advantage was the price we paid - was much less than other hotels nearby. 
Also we'd like to pay tribute to the staff - they tried to thier best in those circumstances. We changed room twice before find an acceptable one and received a complimentary drink. 
Next time we'll choose another hotel.

title: “LOVE LOVE LOVE”
text: This hotel really had all the charm of a home away from home. Staff was great, friendly and very accommodating. The rooms were modern, new with large flat screen tvs and the most comfortable bedding. Location was perfect, I was within walking distance to the best shopping mall and great restaurants. This boutique hotel is truly a MUST, exceptional overall experience...can't wait to go back.

title: “Exceptional service and a nice hotel”
text:
We stayed here recently and, having checked out, my son was taken ill and needed a doctor before flying that evening. The hotel allowed us to call the UK to contact our insurance helpline, arranged for us to visit a local doctor and then provided some toast for my son when we returned to pick up our luggage. 
Bearing in mind that we had already checked out this was exceptional service. Our room was a junior suite and very pleasant. The hotel is "pleasantly dated" but lovingly looked after and with very good staff it made a great place to stay in Boston. There's a "T" station half a block away with access to the Downtown and some good restaurants a block away on Newbury. Thoroughly recommended.

title: “Pleasant Stay & Good Value – Recommend!”
text:
Moved here from another hotel in the area that was less than adequate. It was recommended by fellow colleagues staying there also. The minute I opened the door I felt relief. The room was newly updated, spacious, clean and well appointed. I had a room towards the back and it was very quiet. The exercise room was also well equipped but smaller size weights (5 & 8lbs) were missing. The hotel especially caters to business travelers and offers to put aside a snack it you are not able to make the nightly social. I asked for that one evening since I had to work very late. I was surprised by the amount and quality of the food they put aside for me. Breakfast had a good selection, something for all. One suggeston, they may want to add an additional office workstation – the one they have can get tied up frequently.
The staff was very pleasant and efficient – always willing to assist. Great loc, close to the University, Speedway, Outlet malls, restaurants, and major highways. I would definitely recommend and would stay here again if in the area

title: “great room bad check out time !!!”
text: nice friendly early check in very super clean and quiet room , very nice place until the next day ....while i Tried To Check Out At 10:30 AM Busy Time to catch my metra train I Waited And Waited While The One Person Behind The Counter Kept Giving People Tourist Direction And They Kept Asking Question About Visting Chicago So I Finally Got Mad At The Check Out Service And Threw The Key At Her And Said Do Whatever....!!! Never Again !!! The Tourist Should Have Used The Computer !!!

title: “Clean, new, fresh, affordable”
text: This property looks like it has just been renovated. It is accessible and squeaky clean. I mean it! The rooms are big. It has all the perks. Courtesy internet, parking, airport shuttle. It is limited service but the price is unbeatable. Attitude is nice. It has a pool, fitness center, coffee shop. Everything that pricier properties have plus it is all new. Not what you would expect from an airport "motel". Strongly recommended.

title: “San Francisco Vacation”
text:
We absolutely loved the Hotel Nikko. Charleyne checked us in; she was very pleasant and attentive to my requests, providing us a wonderful room. Attention to detail is important to me, and Hotel Nikko excels at this. The room had a very comfortable king size pillow top bed, wonderful bedding including pillows and a nice cotton blanket at the foot of the bed, not one of those heavy comforters you wonder if they are ever laundered. You can request robes, which were great; they are very soft and not heavy. The room had a desk, comfortable chair and foot stool and the lights in the room have dimmers. The closet also has a room safe, which I always use. The water closet is separate from the deep soaking tub and walk in shower. The bathroom has ample counter space and closet space. There was a large window, with nice drapery and sheers. There is a coffee pot in the room, something we always use. Our room was 1807.
Hotel Nikko generally had two concierges on duty most of the time. A special thank you to Christopher Wang, who personally delivered some salt to my room. I found all of the staff at Hotel Nikko to be outstanding, helpful, and pleasant. Housekeeping did a great job as well. You won’t wait for an elevator either; I think the longest we waited was ten seconds. 
The hotel is located in Union Square, a very convenient location. I have traveled to San Francisco many times for more than twenty years and I would highly recommend Hotel Nikko and certainly intend to stay again, many times I hope. A note for those new to the city, San Francisco is a fairly large city, and there is city noise, you have to expect that. Also, unfortunately there is a considerable population of homeless people and panhandlers. This is in no way a reflection on Hotel Nikko, and you will simply see this in all parts of the Union Square area. 
I personally value reviews on Trip Advisor, and I am so pleased to be able to provide such a positive review of Hotel Nikko.

title: “Good Vaule”
text: Basic but clean. Location suited us well with the proximity to the Johnson Space Center and many natural sites along waterways. Good breakfast and helpful staff. The one way street on which the hotel is situated caused a few dilemmas as we always seemed to be coming or going from the wrong direction and needed to go a way to get turned around!

title: “Great room, great location, great hotel!”
text: This is my second stay at the Millenium Hotel in NY. My family and I loved our first stay a few years ago, so we decided to try the Millenium again for our quick one night stay this past weekend. After booking the hotel, I came accross some negative reviews, which I must say concerned me a little. We decided to keep our reservation since we were only staying for one night. From the moment that we stepped into the hotel, the staff was wonderful. The counter staff at check in, the concierge, bellman and the bartender at the hotel restaurant were all outstanding. We had room #5111 which was a corner room located on the 51st floor. The room was large with expansive windows overlooking time square.
