Since I was traveling with my 22 year old son, the hotel suggested this particular room as it featured 2 oversized twin beds. I originally would have preferred 2 double or queen bed's, however to my surprise, these beds were much larger than twin's. The beds and bedding were extremely comfortable, the air conditioning was consistant and quiet, the bathroom was large and the room was newly renovated and extremely clean. It was the best night's sleep that I had in a long time! I would highly recommend this hotel, especially for the price.

title: “Great Value”
text:
I chose to stay at Eastgate towers because they were one of a few hotels I could get under $200 a night. How well my money was spent!
We were luckily given an early check in after arriving from a red eye flight. Our room was clean, spacious and quiet.
The hotel is situated in a quiet area, only 10 minute walk from Grand Central station. A good station to be near as it is easy to connect to most lines. 
There are plenty of restaurants nearby and also some supermarkets for self catering.
As first time visitors to NY, we were out til late every night and felt totally safe walking back each night.
Yes the room was a little outdated but as soon as they refurbish the price goes up and ultimately I care little about the colour of the walls when I'm asleep!
Definitely recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Very nice, but some disappointments”
text: Although we usually stay in small luxury boutique hotels, we were excited to experience the history of the Brown Palace. The hotel is very beautiful and the staff was quite professional. However, being seasoned travelers, there were a few things that we found disappointing and surprising for a luxury hotel. We could not remember when we had last stayed in a hotel that had no amenities as far as the typical "mini bar" products that are normally provided in rooms. Not only was nothing available in the rooms, there was nowhere in the hotel to so much as get a soda! When we called to ask we were told that it was necessary to call for room service if you wanted something to drink. We thought that the $26 per day valet charge was high (especially once you add tips) as we were coming and going all day and night. Our room had only one robe hanging in the closet and the safe was much too small to fit a laptop computer. We also felt like a hotel such as the Brown Palace should have offered free internet (not $9.95 per day). Our desk didn't have a phone on it and if someone was sitting at the desk, the other person couldn't watch the TV. This was a somewhat awkward set up for travelers if one person needs to do business while the other one wants to relax. Our first morning we were surprised to not have a newspaper delivered to our room. I realize that many of these points seem trivial, but when all added together, it began to become frustrating. These are the kinds of details that one assumes someone at the Brown would care about.

title: “Excellent hotel .”
text:
Great location loved the nightly wine and cheese perfect after a long day of sightseeing 
And shopping. Very calming at the end of the night to walkminto your room and experience the
Turn down service the hotel gave. Great staff and would definitely come back. Just a little hint try and get a higher floor........less road no ice

title: “Previous ratings are spot on!”
text: Stayed at this hotel after reading reviews. This was a really great place to stay! Rooms were immaculate and common areas were beautiful. The staff was great and we really enjoyed the breakfast and all other amenities.

title: “Inn-stantly likeable”
text: Rooms for five adults aren't the norm, but the Residence Inn had accommodation that suited us perfectly. The bedrooms and washrooms were a good size, the small sitting room and dining area meant we didn't need to stay in our bedrooms, and we made good use of the kitchen. Beds were comfortable, and I liked that we could choose the type of pillows we wanted at the time of booking. Breakfast was tasty with plenty of choice, but the dining area can be crowded at times. Staff at Reception were friendly and helpful, giving us good advice about where to go for a quick meal near the hotel. One of my friends liked the hotel so much she's booked it for a stay later this year; I would certainly stay there again.

title: “Very good experience”
text:
We stayed at Distrikt for 7 days in a queen room on 9th floor facing the backyard. The room was on a small side and with no view (however there was some distance to the wall of the other hotel facing the backyard) but we did expect that and chose delibarately deciding on it for a more budget price. 
The room was very clean and modern. Bathroom excellent. Beds very comfy.Chair super comfortable. Fast and free wifi in the room. Very nice tea, coffe maikng facilities in the room. Hot coffe in the morning and ice tea in the afternoon and night in the lobby. Very nice and cooperative stuff. Nice and well designed common areas. Two fast and large lifts - so no waiting even though there are 32 floors. 
Location - very central - however the street itself is quite dodgy (nexts to state parole and on the opposit of NYC main bus station) - but we felt very safe even late at night. 
I'd recommend the hotel - but try to book early and find good promotion - we booked it well in advance throgh tripadvisor code - so for us the price / value ratio was best in NYC.

title: “Great Location”
text: Friendly, helpful, attentive staff. Clean, comfortable rooms. Within easy walking distance to Seatte Center and I found longer hikes to Pike Market, downtown, Pioneer Square, international district no problem for me but there are plenty of convenient bus stops for those who don't care for longer treks. Why is there no Hi def TV? And too often no Wi Fi connection for IPad.

title: “Absolutely fantastic!!”
text:
We called to book our room at the Holiday Inn Express after we'd had enough of killing cockroaches at our cheaper 'boutique' hotel. When we arrived the next morning and explained the situation (including the fact that our luggage had been missing for three days), Michael at the front desk found us a room right away.
The room was excellent - great bed and linens, new bathroom fixtures and amenities, flat-screen TV and tons of channels. There are two computers with free internet in the basement, and a great continental breakfast in the mornings. An absolute winner at a great price, just two blocks from Times Square...we will not hesitate to stay there again!!

title: “Perfect location, renovation under way.......”
text: I stayed for 2 nights. Very nice staff at the reception. Had a fairly "cheap" room on lower floors with no view of Central Park. The room was one of those due for renovation & refurbishing. Nothing to say about that considering the low rate. The Hotel has great potential when the renovation is completed considering the top notch location of the hotel.

title: “WONDERFULL”
text:
the location was exelent, just in downtown.
it was very clin and very good service.

title: “Hotel Commonwealth”
text: My daughter became ill unexpectedly and we needed to find a good place for her to rest and recover. Their staff was wonderful and assisted us very well.

title: “Outstanding location and value.”
text: An excellent choice for location and value. A bit dated but very clean and well maintained, this hotel provides a quieter and more intimate alternative to the larger Sheraton New York across the street. The staff is friendly, helpful and attentive to your needs. The restaurant is now only open for breakfast, which is a shame given its interesting sidewalk level location. This hotel also has a well maintained pool that while fully enclosed and also dated, provides a relaxing excercise alternative and seems very popular with the kids. Free wi-fi and terminals in the lobby. Times Square, Broadway theatre's and Central Park are all short walks from this hotel.

title: “ABSOLUTELY THE BEST!!!”
text: I have stayed at many 5-Star hotels and resorts around the United States and Canada, and whenever I need accommodations in the Los Angeles area, I check availability at Villa Delle Stelle first! I can't tell you how wonderful it is to not deal with parking issues and constantly reaching in my wallet for tips, but knowing that it feels like a "home away from home". I have stayed in the Parisian and Art Deco suites and the Bungalow...all are fabulous...but I really enjoyed the Parisian the most. I love feeling like I'm in my own apartment and can bring in take-out, sit down at the dining table, read my book and relax after a long day running around the hectic city. I have stayed just a few nights and up to two weeks at a time. Samantha is lovely, helpful and always responds quickly to anything you need! If you want people waiting on you hand and foot, this isn't the place for you...but if you want something wonderfully quiet, private, beautiful and comfortable, you should consider this location. Remember...it's not a hotel and you don't have maid service daily, but you also have the relaxed privacy you don't get anywhere else!

title: “Best Hotel Ever”
text:
Our family had been planning this vacation to Chicago for a long time and it was well worth the wait. We had to cancel our plans last summer due to a sudden medical emergency but the General Manager, Nabil, was kind enough to hold our reservation for another year at the same rate. The service at this hotel cannot be beat. I communicated with Mark, the Head Concierge, through email and telephone many times before our visit. He was always very professional, responsive, and thorough in answering my many questions. He made excellent recommendations and was very efficient at making all our reservations. By the time our family got to Chicago, I was very anxious to finally meet Mark because he felt like an old friend! He was even nicer in person and greeted us with enthusiasm and a huge smile. The Palomar is very fortunate to have him. My husband feels that Mark defines the word "concierge". After our early check-in, Mark sent cookies and wine to the room - a very nice surprise! All of the staff - from the front desk to the housekeepers and doormen - were pleasant and accommodating. It is obvious this hotel is extremely customer-service oriented.
The location of this hotel is fantastic. You can walk to the Magnificant Mile, there is a free trolley to Navy Pier just around the corner, several restaurants & stores are within walking distance, and it is close to the train station and bus stops. 
The beds were very comfortable and the room was immaculate. My one and only complaint (and it is very minor) is that the towels have an odd smell (not unpleasant, just odd). Perhaps this is because the Palomar is a "green" hotel and they use detergent that is eco-friendly. 
This is the only hotel you should ever consider when making a visit to Chicago. Be sure to join the Kimpton In-Touch program and get the evening turndown service (with chocolates placed on your pillows), free wi-fi, and newspapers at your door every morning. The free morning coffee/tea and afternoon wine reception is a nice extra.
All in all, we had a fantastic stay at this hotel and cannot thank management enough for all they did to make our stay so memorable. My two teenagers had a great time in Chicago and that means the world to us. The Chicago Palomar is the best hotel ever!

title: “DO NOT STAY AT THIS HOTEL”
text: If you wish to be ripped off, then stay in this hotel. I used my card to guarantee a room for my daughter. She paid for the room on her card upon arrival. Total for 2 nights stay was 350.00. Her card was authorized 450.00 upon arrival in case of incidental charges. I understand and agree with this policy. However, 225.00 was also authorized out of my account and the front desk said it would take 3-5 days to unlock. So, this hotel held 675.00 for A 350.00 room. I travel 10-12 times a year and I am very disappointed with this hotel. I have never had a hotel hold almost double amount in case of incidentals. I have stayed at Hilton many times in the past but will not again due to this incident. The hotel is most certainly not worth the aggravation

title: “Godd Stay with bad parking fee”
text:
We arrived late, so there was no more parking places left (at least there not enough boxes for the guests) - so the front desk woman told us to park just in front of the hotel.
But didn't tell us to remove the car from the space next day - otherwise we got a ticket.
So we stayed there 2 nights - we got 2 tickets for the parking outside the hotel (139$)
I took my choice of booking this hotel because of free parking at the hotel (normaly parking fee in SF is about 25-40$ a night) - so we paid that with our tickets !!!!!!!!

title: “It was great for us and other family members”
text: Reviews of the Holiday Inn Arboretum saying it's old or run down are, at best, way out of date. We stayed there over the first weekend in May 2009, and it was great -- clean, in good shape, excellent service from the staff. The hotel no doubt has been updated not long back. We had several family groups there for a reunion, and everyone was pleased. The hotel even accommodated us needing meeting space when their usual meeting rooms all were booked. They let us use part of the restaurant, then a meeting room that had been vacated. We couldn't have asked for better service. It's sort of hard to get to, but maybe that's good -- keeps away the riffraff that write bad reviews. No, I am not an employee of Holiday Inns nor have I ever been. I'm writing as a traveler who found a good hotel..

title: “Giant Inflatable Rat Says It All!”
text: When we arrived, the hotel staff had all been fired and they were all protesting outside with a giant inflatable rat. The scene was very uncomfortable and I cancelled my reservation. The staff were all very impatient and didn't understand why we wouldn't want to stay. They were not accomodating in the least. The hotel is not in a good location, not very close to anything,and directly across the street from an auto garage and next to the horse stables for central park. Needless to say, we didn't stay there because of the horrible conditions and I don't recommend it to anyone.

title: “Cool property,great location, fair prices incredible staff!”
text: My house had a leak and I had to be relocated. My Insurance company suggested Hotel Solamar. I said why not. I was a liitle worried it would be too fancy. After dealing with the mess at home I came in late on a friday night. It was busy loud and really intimadating. I instantly was greeted with one of the warmest and friendliest smiles from the front desk manager Kelsey. I informed her I was checked in and she was already aware of my problem. She even gave me and girlfriend a bottle of wine to show that they understood it wasnt easy just getting up and leaving my house for a few days. This kind gesture made all the difference in the world. After the brief but calming interaction I promise my girlfriend we had to write a review based soley on that interaction. We got to our room which was really nice, a little small but suitable. During our stay we enjoyed being able to venture out and eat and have a bevarage or two and not have to worry about driving home since everything was so close. This was a great stay and everyone was very pleasant. Solamar should be proud of their staff and property. I have repeated this story to many of my friends who plan on visiting us. The only problem was how noisey it is on the weekends and the unsavory characters who hang out near by.

title: “Clean and nice”
text:
Just arrived back after our pleasant 4 day stay in Manhattan at the Chelsea Indigo. The hotel was located on a pretty quiet 28th street. The street itself isn't anything grand - sort of a Chinatown feel with cheap little shops and florists between 7th avenue and 6th avenue...but quiet and safe feel even late at night. It is also locates seconds to the 1 line subway and within a 10 minute walk of Penn Station and other subway lines along 28th avenue. There are numerous Star bucks and little places to eat all around and you’re a quick 10 minute walk to Macy's and other shops. You are also about a 15-20 minute walk Time square and other 
The hotel lobby is small but quaint and friendly staff great you. We arrived at 1 pm and were checked in within minutes and in our 12th floor room moments later. The room had 1 King bed which was very comfy to sleep on, nice clean bedding and no carpet in the room which is exactly what I like (1 bonus star from me). Although there isn't a whole lot of room to move around, I have stayed in smaller rooms so no issues with space from us. The little extra width in the entrance was just right. There was a little sitting chair and desk (with chair) and an LCD TV in the room. There was free wireless Internet, but it was very slow. Negatives were there is no view and the shower is messy - no door and only a half glass wall so water can/will get all over the bathroom floor if you’re not paying attention. There was also a humming noise each time the heat or air flow went on - no an issue for me as I wear ear plugs and don't know if it is better or worse when the air conditioning is running.

title: “Decent rooms, Questionable Customer service”
text:
I brought a group of College Students on a business trip and we stayed at the Wingate. While the hotel itself is in pretty good condition, there were numerous problems with housekeeping and the front desk staff. Our first night there, the rooms were not cleaned by housekeeping. When I approached the young lady at the front desk about the situation that evening, she seemed rather frustrated because housekeeping had left for the day. She even seemed bothered with us asking for towels, too busy on talking the phone I suppose. I could tell that it wasn't hotel business because she was speaking in Spanish and I'm somewhat fluent in the language. The next morning when I explained the situation to the lady who had checked us in the previous night, she stated the problem may have occurred because of our very late arrival. However, I called the hotel twice to notify them of this situation and we were in our rooms well before housekeeping started knocking on doors. Sounds to me as if someone may have neglected indicating that our rooms were occupied in the system. 
When housekeeping was eventually called to service my room, all the housekeeper did was make the bed and left - nothing else. A student complained the next night that a lipstick stain on her pillow which she requested be changed was simply flipped over onto the other side. That is simply beyond ridiculous. The pillowcase should've been changed.
Besides this, other problems noticed by students were the front desk staff having continuous personal conversations on the phone, staff always on the computer in the business center, and the staff was eating much of the breakfast that is supposed to be for guests. While I didn't witness this personally, I have never known students to exaggerate about something like that. I emailed the hotel manager to contact me about 'issues' we were having but she never responded or called me. While some of the hotel staff were friendly, as a Management Professor, I strongly believe that more professionalism and customer service training is needed.
That being said, given the problems with housekeeping, I'm not so sure I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is particular about cleanliness. As for service and professionalism, I've seen better at a Days Inn and I don't even stay at those anymore! I expected better at a Wyndam property.

title: “Is this Disneyworld?”
text:
This place is huge - felt like I was in Disneyworld!! This is an older hotel that has gone through a recent renovation. Overall I was quite pleased as we paid only $50 through Priceline.
Unfortunately there was no wifi and the parking was $16 per night - expensive for the area.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
I am a businessman from Hong Kong and I do a lot of travel in my work.
In March, I had to make a trip to New York and I wanted to bring my family with me. My colleague recommended the Buckingham Hotel. They took time to understand my needs and offer me a reasonable rate. 
This is an outstanding hotel in the best location. We had a 2 bedroom 2 bath suite and it was more spacious than most apartments in Hong Kong. We loved it. And the staff was sooo helpful and recommended restaurants 
for us that were quite delicious. 
I would definitely recommend this hotel to everyone and I will stay here again on my next trip !

title: “Great weekend stay”
text: We stayed over Memorial Day weekend and were pleasantly surprised by how excellent the service was. We expected it to be a zoo because of the holiday, but found a calming oasis. The room was amazing - don't let the comments about shutters between the bath and bed throw you off. the shutters close and we liked opening them to talk while I was doing hair and makeup. We had plenty of space to rest and relax. The bed was as great as I remembered. My boyfriend, who never sleeps in, slept until 9! The staff was fantastic, accommodating and kind. The minute we needed anything or had any questions, they were there. The only reason I didn't rate higher was the motion-sensored cooling system in the room. It was HOT over the weekend and I woke up 3 or 4 times in the night because I was just too hot to sleep. I understand why the system is in place, but I was still uncomfortable. Maybe the time frame should be set longer. Sure, it is not brand new. The halls are dated, the carpets aren't new, but everything is clean and very nice. We got great service and that is much more important than cosmetic issues.

title: “Accomadating, clean and great location!!”
text:
We stayed here while getting treatment at the Mayo Clinic. It is very close and you can't beat the location. It is only a 10-15 minute ride. We had two dogs with us. The management took extra time, effort, and was very accommodating approving our pets. 
We did not meet their requirements, oversized and two dogs. We actually got a call directly from the general manager making sure our needs were met. The breakfast was adequate. The normal continental breakfast. The dining room was very clean and the girl working it was very attentive. Our room was also clean, and had newer bedding.
Overall, you can't beat it for the price and location.

title: “Nice hotel, great location!”
text: The Best Western Bowery Hanbee Hotel is right on the border of Chinatown and Little Italy. The neighborhood was fun with lots of character. Our room was clean, unusually spacious for NYC, and the staff was friendly. Will definitely stay here again.

title: “no good”
text: Attendant totally lazy and provided false info in order not to move or do anything. Rooms have moss which is unhealthy. only good thing about it is location. noisy outside due to construction but they promised a quiet room.

title: “Not a top rated hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel so he could attend a conference downtown. We were there from 9/12-9/16/12. We arrived and initially all seemed fine. After about an hour I was about ready to check out. We had an outside king suite on the 4th floor and could hear a lot of noise. I requested a different room and was given a smaller room on the same floor, so still noise. It also took an hour for housekeeping to bring up more hangers and towels. It was a good location. Construction next door didn't help with the noise. The best part about this hotel was the valet parking. Best I have ever had.

title: “great doubletree and fantastic location”
text: I was just going up to Chicago for two nights to have a girls trip with my friend. Hotels in Chicago are pretty pricey, even during the week. Since I am Hitlon gold member I used the option of paying partial points and money. Even though we got there early, we were not able to check in early. That was fine, we checked our bags with the concierge and went out to sightsee. When we did check in the room was very nice. You can tell it is an older building but whenever they did the last renovation, they did a very nice job. Beds are very comfortable and love the bench seat along the window. The comp breakfast for being a gold member was great. A million times better than the comp breakfast at the Doubletree in Oahu. If I come back to Chicago I would consider this hotel again, but would use points and pay option again since the price is high.

title: “Worth the money”
text: I treated myself to a lovely stay at the JW in February! The word lovely describes everything and everyone at the hotel! The staff was so gracious and delighted to assist you in any way! My personal fave was the fabulous flavored water in the Lobby-kudos to the person who created citrus peach!!!! I cannot wait to visit again!

title: “Just fine”
text:
I had to make a last minute trip to Seattle while two conventions were going on and this was the closest hotel to the downtown area I could. When you arrive the dingy 70's exterior doesn't do a lot to ease your mind, nor does the location but once you get into your room things improve. It seems to be newly renovated and everything was clean. Bed was quite comfortable and the room was quiet, despite facing a rather busy street. The rooms are quite small but I live in NYC and I'm used to tight quarters so it didn't really bother me. The breakfast room makes your high school cafeteria feel like the Ritz and is a rather depressing start to the day, I'd skip it and talk a walk over to Belltown for a proper cup of coffee and any kind of breakfast you'd want.
Totally acceptable for what it is, a motel on the edge of town.

title: “Disappointing for the price paid”
text:
I was disappointed with the quality of the rooms, especially the beds which did not have duvets but instead had thin foam blankets sandwiched between cheap white sheets (the sheets on my bed had holes in them!). As it was quite cold while we were in San Fran, we were forced to keep the outdated and noisy heating on overnight as the beds were not warm enough. 
Location is ok (3 blocks to union sq) and all other services and facilities are same as any other hotel of this standard but I would expect better overall quality for the price.

title: “Stay away!”
text: I have to wholeheartedly agree with most of the other reviews of The Riverside Tower. I stayed there on my last visit to New York in March, and it was a disgusting dump. At under $100 a night, I didn't expect the room to be large, but I did expect it to be resasonably clean. The carpet was so stained I wouldn't walk on it with bare feet. The walls were filthy and there was dust all over. The bathroom looked like it should have been in a welfare hotel--it was in terrible shape. Thank heaven I brought flip-flops because I wouldn't have trusted the shower floor enough to place my feet on it. The top ledge of the tile on the bathroom wall was so caked with dust that I was afraid to breathe. When I sat down on one of the sofas in the downstairs lounge, I practically fell through--the cushioning must have been worn down to nothing. I could write a lot more about this place, but rather than go on, I will just say: Don't stay here!! Some things are more important than money.

title: “Nice Bedroom pity about the Disgusting Bathroom in Room 143”
text:
Flew in from UK and needed an hotel for first night before travelling on. Have regularly used various La Quinta hotels in the past so chose this hotel for its convenience for our onward journey.
The bedroom and bed were excellent and up to La Quinta's usual high standards as was breakfast but ...
The bathroom was disgusting. The tiles around the bath were black with mould. The cleaning had not been carried out properly as the previous occupants hairs were still to be found all around the bathroom.
The manager was polite when we complained and said he 'would look into it' and gave us a $30 discount. However at no point did he apologise or express concern,

title: “Nice and clean room”
text: I was quite impressed with the cleanliness of the bedroom and bathrooms. The bedroom was very small but it was clean and not too bad for the price. Initially I was worried about having to queue up for the bathrooms but my concern proved unfounded since they were seldom occupied. The location was great too. The 72nd Street Subway station was around 5 mins walk. The express train to Times Square at 42nd took less than 10 mins. The area was pretty safe even at night. The downside was the steep staircase. However, you could get the staff to help you carry your luggage, which I did. The staff might not be extremely friendly but at least they were helpful and efficient. Overall, it was a good experience and I would recommend this to others who want to travel on a budget.

title: “Best choice I could have made!”
text: Celebrating my birthday I had done my research and the Porto Vista Hotel not only had a great price, but a unique atmosphere. Upon arrival, the staff exceeded all my expectations! They upgraded our room, were extremely friendly, and recommended an exquisite restaurant that turned into a fabulous club. They even went so far to hook us up with reservations just 30 min before we headed out. Had a GREAT experience! Would definitely go back again!!!

title: “would go back!”
text: Stayed here to go to a show which was close by. The location for sightseeing and theater is great. The hotel was clean, quiet, and the morning brunch was plentiful and tasty. The concierge was very helpful, and the bellman was superb. Would definitely stay again.

title: “Great place, friendly staff!”
text:
Our family of five stayed in a two bedroom suite at this hotel for one night. Each bedroom had a queen-sized bed and there was also a pull-out sofa. 
There were three very helpful and friendly gentlemen behind the desk when we checked in. They immediately got us the additional rollaway we requested for no extra charge. 
The room was clean and comfortable. Breakfast the next morning (included in the price) was not so hot...some greasy eggs and sausage, and the rest was cold foods....but we aren't big breakfast eaters so that was okay. There was free internet access in the lobby.
I would definitely recommend this place!

title: “Nice place to stay”
text:
We recently spent 3 nights at the Travel Inn and we were very pleased with our stay. Our room as clean, the beds were comfortable and the room was big enought that we did not feell crowded...our son stayed with us and there was plenty of room for three...There was a little noise from 42nd street but we always travel with ear plugs so we had no problems..you will have noise no matter where you are in New York City
The only thing that happend was the fire alarm went off at 6am the one morning when a guest thought it would be funny to pull the alarm...
The room was always cleaned as soon as we left each morning. We left one morning for only an hour and when we came back the room was already cleaned, I have stayed at the "Big name hotels" and have had to waite hours to get the room cleaned.
The "free" parking was a huge plus...they even let us leave our car there the day we checked out since we still had things to do past our check out time.. I would stay here again.

title: “a great experience for good holyday”
text: The Hard Rock Hotel made my first trip to San Diego very memorable. I recommend this for couples or groups. The staff was attentive and cheerful. The room was kept cleaned every day. The room service was fantastic and prompt. The shower and all other amenencies was the best that I have ever experienced in a hotel. No noise within the hotel rooms. The location is great with the convention center, shops, restaurants, markets and several attractions within walking distance or any public transportation easy. We went to Ocean beach by bus (no. 30) for about 35 min. The restaurant Mary Jane's food was very good. The shop is famous. The access to the pool and the bar area need reservations and the drinks are expensives. The Hard Rock Hotel is an experience, and it was a fantastic one.

title: “Close to airport, clean”
text: Clean hotel, close to airport, fine for our flight next day. Shallow bath, small bathroom. Comfortable bed. Used HHonours to get free wifi, sign up before arrive. Can walk through walkway straight to airport, undercover.

title: “Definately stay again!”
text: From Madeline(sp) who answered all my pre visit questions to Ron the bellman who held our luggage, the visit was great. Never saw or heard housekeeping, but our room looked and felt great. Nice comfy bed and soft sheets. Clean pleasant bathroom. We had views of both the Empire State Bldg and the Statue of Liberty. All staff members were friendly and knowledgable. But the best of all was the location. Across the street from Penn Station and MSG. Blocks from Time Square, who could ask for more? I will definately return!

title: “I love the Sheraton Gateway”
text: OK, so I'm biased. I'm a loyal SPG customer and try to stay at the Sheraton Gateway for my LA travel. I'm fussy about hotels. On first inspection some people might be turned off by a hotel near a large airport. Many flight crews stay here and the hotel is often booked for conventions. The management and staff of the Sheraton Gateway really get super customer service. I've never experienced this level of service at an airport hotel. I was upgraded to an executive suite - nice surprise. During past stays at this hotel, I have always ventured to the beach towns for dinner. Last week I decided to stay put and eat in the hotel restaurant, Paparazzi. I'm glad I did. The food was incredible!

title: “Not bad overall”
text:
I would give the hotel 3 and a half stars. The staff were wonderful and very helpful, the hotel is in a prime location but be aware that the website is quite misleading as when I arrived the 'cosmopolitan hotel' banner hanging on the scaffolding wasn't exactly what I was expecting when I booked it. Still it's good value for New York City especially if you book in advance; there's really good (free WiFi) and two Macs for use in lobby with free printouts.
The hotel is extremely dated (still use conventional keys) and a fresh lick of paint wouldn't go amiss. My room was quite small, and was noisy given I had a room facing the street.
Overall I would recommend it mainly because of the staff, and because the room was clean, safe and in a great location. 
Being in the Tribeca area I could walk to Soho and towards the World Trade the other way. A great buzzing area with Chambers Street station right outside the doorstep. There's also a wonderful diner/cafe called Kitchenette on Chambers Street where I'd go most mornings for breakfast.

title: “Great place to sleep & even got some work done!”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel three previous times over the last 2 years and wouldn't stay anywhere else in NYC (unless I had an unlimited budget). It's close to the subway (6) and has food just around the corner (PAX and a grocery). It's easy to get a cab (often there is one right outside the front door) too.
I have stayed in the bunkbed room w/a friend and in the single while traveling alone. Both rooms were the same size and offered room enough to move around and to store my stuff.
The hotel also offers wifi which I am using to write this review right now! I took advantage of the free wifi and got some work done today as well.
The only complaint I have is that some people slam their doors and you can hear it in your room. Not sure what the slamming was about but they did quit after 5 mins or so so that's not too big a complaint.
The other thing I have noticed over the last couple of visits is that the hotel is showing some signs of use--cracked grout in the bathrooms, dirt in the corners, etc. Nothing too big (believe me I have seen worse in NYC) but things that I hope the hotel mgmt will take care of as soon as possible as this is a very hip looking hotel in a great location and I would hate for it to go down hill.

title: “Hawey/front desk”
text:
It's a shame the way "Hawey" front desk staff treats customers, rude, disrespectful.
This guy, treated us very disrespectful and rude when I was trying to get a second room key. The way he was asking us what we needed was very rude. 
I had to asked him to stop talking to us that way.
Tipically, his answer was "sir.. I'm trying to help you" to which I answered, yes but you don't have to talked to us in that sarcastic and rudely tone. 
He finally gave us an extra key. Without activating it.
When we came back to the lobby. Another front desk staff helped us. This guy Hawey came back to the lobby asking the other employee with a sarcastic smile." what happened? It didnt work? Walking away without apologizing. 
Obviously They don't know what the term "Customer Service Mean"

title: “Close to the Gardens!”
text: The hotel was once a police station, and it could use some touching up, but the location is great if your business is in the West End. The round-the-city tour bus leaves from the Gardens, and the walk to the Navy Ship Yard is just across the bridge, if you start in the right direction. Some of the staff was outstanding; some of the staff seemed bored with their jobs. Dinner at their new tapas restaurant was good with excellent service by staff. The wine was quite good, but I hate that the serving size seems to be getting smaller and smaller - or is the glass getting larger and larger? Good value for the money, but the closest Boston Globe was about a block away, and the nearest Start\buck's was a few blocks away on Cambridge Ave. God choice of nearvy eats due to the location near the Gardens.

title: “Words aren't enough..”
text:
This stay was our first getaway together as a couple and the stay at Comfort Suites topped the entire trip. Upon arrival we got a complimentary upgrade from a king room to a king suite. The view from the 25th floor was magnificent! We spent the first 15 minutes acting like little kids in a candy store, taking pictures, laughing, and enjoying a much needed sense of relaxation and peace. This relaxation was continued with an unexpected solid nights sleep on a mattress that I want to get for our home! Most hotels I stay in do not have great mattresses, but this one I will say has been the best in my experience. And I cannot leave the staff out of course.. each one was very attentive and friendly. We will be returning in April to take my boys to the Skydeck and there is no question we will be staying here. We've already discussed how easy and convenient it will be to keep a 4 and 6 year old occupied because of the nearby sites and restaurants to Comfort Suites. We thank you for an awesome getaway & look forward to staying with you again soon!!
Kendra & Austin

title: “Romantic Getaway just after the Wedding...”
text: We stayed here on our wedding night. It was nice and romantic, but the service was subpar. We had the "Romance Package" added to our doom, but we never received the 'breakfast in bed' that was part of the package.

title: “Cool Manhattan Hotel”
text: I was treated to a stay at this hotel and it was so nice. Its a boutique hotel. Had a lot of cool displays. Glass chandeliers in unique shapes. A really interesting glass tube fireplace. The lounge Opia attached to the hotel had delicious appetizers and drinks. The room though small was very nicely decorated and the staff was ever so helpful when asked about restaurants to visit late night in the city.

title: “Charming Place”
text:
Room was clean and remodeled (decor a bit tacky though), staff seemed attentive, pool area was great for the kids, charming atmosphere in the evening with the fire on the restaurant's balcony, all-in-all very relaxing. Only minor downside was the charge for parking which seemed a bit excessive. 
Would definitely go there again.

title: “summer vacation”
text:
hello i stayed at this hotel for 4 nights and it was very nice the rooms are updated .We Were able to use the bbq grill and just enjoy the evening i felt like it was home away from home..and not to mention the staff there were amazing especially Ana,and Richard i will definetly stay here again thank you for taking care of us soooo good!!!!
Thanks vanessa,

title: “Disappointing”
text:
I most always try to see a silver lining but so far our stay here has not been good
1. I'd phoned ahead by a week, confirmed our stay and mentioned that our flight would arrive close to midnight -- so our check-in would be very late. We had prepaid via Priceline. Lo and behold our purchased nonsmoking king was no longer available when we arrived; we were put into an old nonsmoking full bed room and I spent most of the night praying for no bedbugs. The carpet was filthy and pulled away from the tack board where the walls met the floor.
2. We were told to leave that room in the morning, check our bags with the bell captain and return after noon to get our king room. We did so, and then returned at 2:45 pm. Checked in and couldn't get into our new room -- housekeeping was still in there. We were told to come back in half an hour. This after 3 hours of sleep and then walking around NYC half the day. I am not amused. I told the front desk nicely and at least they apologized, but am holding my breath to see the room.
UPDATE: We did get a slightly better room on the fifth floor, but continued having troubles with the key card throughout our stay. At least the carpet was cleaner. I can't say enough about the one bell captain -- can't recall his name, but he was a wonderful, charming man -- a Manhattan native who is a real asset to the property. 
The good: Location, location, location. Great upper West Side locale near the park and subway. 10 minutes to midtown. Scads of nice eateries abound plus shops on Broadway and Amsterdam Ave.
Bottom line: I'm a NYC native, but this was my first foray to the Upper West and I loved it. I felt completely safe at all times. The vibe is still very much New York, but not as crazed as midtown/Times Square. I loved the little shops and restaurants everywhere and the convenient location. That said, I wouldn't return to this particular hotel in a hurry. Having to go down to the lobby to use wifi is a real drag, too. And, these are probably the slowest elevators in NYC.

title: “Fleeced like a sardine”
text:
Besides paying too much for a closet-sized room, I called the morning before I checked in and inquired as to what the car storage fee would be. I was told that this was included in my room rate and parking would be FREE for my stay. So I actually drove into the city for a change. Only to find upon checkout that the garage they instructed me to used wanted $20 (discount rate for the Amsterdam). I returned to the counter to inquire why this was happening, and was assured that NO ONE at the Amsterdam Court Hotel could have possibly told me that there was FREE PARKING. I tried to get them to decide whether I was a liar or an idiot for 10 minutes and then left.
No way to run a hotel - they made no attempt to fix the situation.
Don't fall victim to these misrepresenting grifters. Better off to pay more and go somewhere else!!
TH
Columbus, OH

title: “Something close to the job”
text: One of my Chicago favorites, when I need to be close to work and feel like I'm at home this is the perfect spot. The rooms are cozy and just right. The food is to die for, a Chicago gem.

title: “Typical excellent Marriott, but two annoying cons give it 4 stars”
text:
I stayed here recently for a trade show and for the most part was very pleased.
Pros:
1. Excellent location for the convention center. You can get there without going outside since the Marriott is connected via the second floor of Reading Terminal Market. This made the location perfect for getting to and from the show without having to worry about weather or traffic and crowds of people outside.
2. The rooms were well appointed and if you are lucky, some of the views are pretty nice.
3. The staff was typical Marriott, very courteous and helpful. The housekeeping staff did a stellar job.
4. The lobby has a nice lounge area and useful shops. There is a gift shop in case you need to buy a local item for family members but do not have time to go anywhere, a Starbucks and a FedEx Kinkos. Even though I did not go to them, there are restaurants too, but Reading Terminal Market is across the street.
5. If you were having a meeting at the Marriott, the number of conference rooms is amazing, in all shapes and sizes.
6. The room keys are RFID so you could just hold up your wallet to your door and it will open.
7. Security personal are abundant. Also, there is an easy to use safe in the room if you need it.
Neutral:
1. The elevators required a room key to get to a specific floor. This is great for security, but not good if you want to visit someone on another floor. If you are staying with family, and they are on another floor, make sure you get another key get access to their floors.
2. There is a small lap pool with splash area for kids, but no hot tub, which I was really wanting after working the trade show. I am surprised there was no hot tub in a hotel like this, but not enough to warrant a con.
3. The closet space was fine for me, but may be small for others, especially if staying for more than a few nights.
Cons:
1. No Free Wifi! This continues to irk me. Wifi should be free for hotel guests; we are spending enough money on the room that this service should be included, like in the much less expensive Hamptons and Holiday Inns. I understand that Marriott has you trapped, especially if your conference is in the hotel, but seriously, $14 a day for wifi? Are you kidding? Luckily, I have Sprint so I just had to turn on my 4G Wifi Hotspot (Android phones have this) which costs $0.67 a day and I was able to work around the issue. But this continues to annoy me at these premium hotels. The more you pay the less you get.
2. Parking cost $45.60 per night for guests! I completely understand that cost for non-guests considering it is downtown Philly, but I think that is a bit outrageous for guests. I am not expecting free parking, but maybe some sort of discount would be nice.
If I was in the area again for a convention, I would definitely consider staying here again.

title: “This is NOT a Valid Starwood Property”
text: When you stay at a Starwood hotel, you have certain expectations. Those expectations were not met. We are told that this hotel is 'going to be improved.' But Starwood should not put it in inventory until it is ready. There is no A/C because the system is on 'heating' and they haven't switched over - despite an unusually hot fall - so it was impossible to sleep - even with the windows open. The TV has few channels (they say they have 72 channels on order) and is as big as my computer screen. The carpet in the room has giant stains (on the SPG floor). The elevator shakes and bangs against the shaft as it travels - and there is only one elevator for many rooms and 16 floors! Starwood clearly wants to fill rooms and put this in their reservation system despite the fact that it makes you think less of the brand. I have no idea what their plan is - to make this a Four Points or something else...but what they have is a disaster and I am very disappointed. Do not choose this hotel!

title: “Excellent date night!”
text:
Got a killer mid week price plus free parking, on a whirlpool mini suite via Travelocity/American Express. We regularly stay downtown for events and have stayed at many of the finer hotels in Seattle. Loved the Roosevelt, early check in, friendly front desk. Lovely lobby area, great for watching people walk by on the street or just reading a book. The room was sensational and a great value! Full sized couch with ottoman, desk area with lamp, free wi fi, tons of light, great views of the hustle and bustle of Westlake. Plenty of space if you wanted to have another couple come up to visit before a dinner or show. The bathroom set up was neat, one room had a giant whirlpool and shower, separate room for toilet, sink, vanity, lots of shelf space for products etc. The room was very clean, bed was super comfortable, big flatscreen t.v. you could move and adjust to see from the bed or couch, all the good cable channels, no porn or PPV, no mini bar, but glassware was provided. Also pleasantly surprised to find a very large refrigerator with mini freezer in the bathroom. Kept our bubbly nice and cold!
Have a restaurant and bar attached (Von's) we went for a cocktail and food after a soccer match, disappointed to find the kitchen closed for maintenance. Went up the street to The Taproom.
Easy walk to all Seattle highlights, Pioneer Square, Pike Place, shopping etc. We bused to CenturyLink Field for free and walked back.
My only (minor) complaint was the valet service was very overwhelmed and not very friendly.
We will be back to this hotel soon. Very happy with our visit. Especially for the amazing price!

title: “Best deal in NY by far”
text:
I've stayed in 5 different places in NY and this is the best you can get for $140 (via Priceline), which would be the price for a double room in a hostel. Room is TINY - not only small by really tiny. Since space in not a driver at a hotel for me, this place is amazing due to:
- Great location: west side, very close to the park and one block from subway and Lincoln Center
- Altough tiny, room is very well decorated (not fancy but truly modern) and has everyone you need: good tv with complete cable service, nice shower, bad and linen, iPhone docket and USB charger (never saw it in W, for instance), good air conditioner
- the library where you can have breakfast + internal garden is unbelievable pleasant
- free wifi at room (again, not commum in US, even in 4 stars and up)
- very clean and everything looks new
- nice staff so far
I hope they keep it like this and I'll never stay in another hotel in NY.

title: “Relaxing atmosphere for the weary traveler”
text: The Residence Inn was great. The room was spacious and they aren't kidding when they say piles of pillows on the bed. The staff was courteous and accomodating and you certainly can't beat a complimentary hot breakfast every day...certainly beats the traditional continental breakfast. One draw back...the key card maker wasn't working when we checked in and it took a while (longer than necessary) to get in a room. But, that didn't take away from the stay. Location is great...central to everything and if you can't walk to it they will get you a car.

title: “The Hotel Stay Exceeded my Expectations”
text:
I was concerned due to the previous reviews but the hotel stay exceeded my expectations. My boyfriend and I wanted a weekend get-away. We stayed in the newly remodeled Signature Suite; extremely clean with a full kitchen & new appliances. I loved the separate sleeping, living and working areas. 
We could hear the faint sound of children playing and automobiles whizzing by on the expressway but this did not bother us. The hotel staff was extremely friendly and helpful with directions and information concerning restaurants in the area. We would definitely comeback.

title: “Not the usual Comfort Suites quality-will do but that's all!”
text: This is a hotel that with a bit of work would be much better. Stayed for 3 days but had a dollar store plastic garden chair instead of a handicap shower chair, had no soap dish in the shower, no method of securing the shower head, and the floor flooded with use of the shower. All of these conditions require quite easy and inexpensive fixes but it appears they don't care. Many instances of deferred maintenance including old construction materials standing beside one entrance door-just looks bad and allows bugs to accumulate. My husband killed 2 small bugs in our bed the first night, they moved us to another room but I found a bug there and in the dining room. Just poorly kept!

title: “Wonderful place except for plumbing problem...”
text: We stayed for 3 nights recently in Room 101. First impressions were great: large clean suite, nicely decorated, great kitchen and bath, king bed with excellent bedding and pillows, flat screen TV, balcony off suite and bonus rooftop deck with panoramic views of the city below and Alcatraz. The location, as noted previously in reviews, is excellent. Front desk staff were welcoming and helpful with information. Although there is no on-premise restaurant, we had decent breakfasts at a couple of little places right around the corner, and good food and fun at the Irish pub at night right down the street. On our second morning, however, though we had not used the kitchen at all, the sink was suddenly filled with soapy water. We reported the problem to the desk clerk on our way out for the day, and she said she would send maintenance up to fix it. The next morning, quite awhile after my husband had showered, I heard a gurgling noise from the tub and entered the bathroom to see the tub filled with a black substance looking like sewage. We were checking out so thought we'd report the problem to the front desk, but when we went down, the whole front desk area was covered with buckets, lights out, and the front desk clerk distressfully apologized. It looked as if our suite was directly above the wet area, so apparently there was a bigger plumbing issue than just the one that had occurred in our suite. Nevertheless, realizing that emergencies do happen and considering all the other pluses of the hotel, I would give it another try on my next visit to San Francisco.

title: “Joe Beer Can can afford a Resort Stay and Feel Special”
text: I wanted to book a special day for my Wife's birthday. I have a limited budget, and since we live in Phoenix, generally speaking the hotels here are reasonable during the summer time. Working with the conciege, she helped me with my limited expenses and made it work. She made sure that our room had "birthday amenities" that made my wife feel very special. The property feels as if you are on an island away from Arizona as the grounds were filled with beautiful blooming flowers. The service exceeded our expectations. The staff was continually opening doors, smiling, and wanting to be of service.

title: “Excellent Hotel...Great Location & Customer Service”
text: Very Historical and Nice Hotel. Pleasant Customer Service. A plus is that there is a Metro Station right below the hotel...very convenient.

title: “Our favorite getaway year-round!”
text: We have been coming here for short visits for 10 years, and have never failed to enjoy the incomparable views, rooms and wonderful amenities at the resort. Perfect place to enjoy the best of San Diego- the weather, the numerous bay activities just steps from your room, Sea World, the San Diego Zoo, downtown, etc. The pool area is perfect for families with clean restrooms and delicious food easily accesible from the deck area. We have always found the service to be excellent as well; on our visit last weekend, we were greeted warmly and helped to our room by Jeffrey. He was genuine, professional and most of all, helpful with everything we needed! Thanks for a great visit!

title: “Pleasant Experience”
text: We were very pleased with our October 8-10 stay at the Omni. Early check-in was no problem. All service was pleasant and efficient. Price was a bit steep ($319) for a fairly small but nice room with 2 double beds. The complimentary room service beverages in the morning were much appreciated. Nice bathroom and ammenities. Because of the convenient location, we would definately consider staying there again.

title: “Surprisingly clean, friendly, affordable airport hotel”
text: Our flight out of Indy was canceled and so we searched tripadvisor for a reasonably-priced airport hotel. This was the first we called, and we're glad we didn't call any others. We were cheerfully greeted on the phone, quoted an unbelievably low rate (lower than the usual rate on this property) and told where the free shuttle would meet us. Fifteen minutes later, we were given a clean, amply-sized room, free internet and cable TV and a cheerful staff. The swimming pool, which we did not use, was clean and well-maintained. No complaints, only praise for this hotel. Be aware: there are two Extended Stay properties near the airport: this is the one called "deluxe"

title: “Decent but dated”
text:
I wasn't sure what to expect as Sheraton's can be bad or great. It was about in the middle. I didn't get upgraded even though I'm gold due to E3 making it so packed which was fine. The lobby was very nice and fresh with free internet in their special computer zone.
Getting to the room was a bit of a mess. You have to go down a long hallway and then take what looks like a service elevator and go down a floor to get to some rooms. I don't necessarily mind being on a lower floor but the hallways here really made me feel like I was in a basement. Dark, grungy.
The room was not bad. Not too big but about what I would expect. It had a balcony but since I was on the 2nd floor it made it worse, not better as someone could easily climb up into the room if they wanted to break in. Again, very dated.
The location is great if you want to go to Universal or their citywalk but it took me an hour to drive to the convention center and the free shuttle to E3 took even longer. I had asked beforehand how long it would take and they said 30 min. I allowed for 45 but was still late.
Parking is a bit steep at $18 a night but there's no choice.
Check in staff was nice. He was a gamer too so we had a nice chat about that.
If they upgrade the rooms and hallways to be as nice as the lobby then the rating would go up in a hurry. Adding directions to the elevator would be nice too.

title: “Discusseed”
text:
I have nothing really good to say about the manager of this motel! 
 This is what happen to me on this trip. I found out that my " Travel Agent " Had booked the wrong motel for me. 
 So we had to CANCEL the reservation for this motel because it was in the wrong location that I needed to be in, Though the Milatary Sato Office They booked the right Motel for me. The problem came to my attenation when I arrived at home " Founding Out!" This Motel That I canceled Charged My Credit Card for a night stay. The Manage On Duty told me over the phone the reservation was never cancel, I stated to him that he was dead wrong on this. He wounld not recredit My Credit Card for this charge, All He Would do was COMP me a night stay the next time I was in Seattle. I Stated to him this was "unacceptable" to me. I all so stated to him I would Never again stay at another Ramada Inn ever again so they could keep my money Beacuse They must needed it more than myself.

title: “Nice Hotel, Nice Location”
text: A beautiful hotel in a charming part of DC. The hotel has a rich history, with posters around the lobby chronicling the large number of famous folks who frequented the hotel in years past. The room was well-appointed, though the bed wasn't the most comfortable I've seen. In contrast to what most hotel chains offer, there we only two pillows for a king bed. Wrth the stay.

title: “Budget”
text:
So, when I arrived at the District, I did wonder what the heck we had let ourselves in for. On first impressions, it's pretty shabby, very tired and in desperate need of renovation. Later, I found out that they were actually renovating. Check in took a long time, I have no idea why as we had already paid online. The room that I had was tiny. I had a chest of drawers, very little floor space and my wardrobe was actually a nail with a couple of coathangers on it in the bathroom. The decor was awful - paper coming off the walls, various cables were running up and down the walls, an air con unit was wedged into the window with carrier bags keeping a seal. Some of the other rooms were apparently bigger, and some even had wardrobes. Some rooms didn't have doors but were filled with various tools, etc. There was also a very old, very noisy ice making machine on my floor which we had to unplug so we could sleep. Each floor also had a lounge area, so overall it was a bit like grotty halls of residence. No coffee machine in rooms either. The room doors don't fit well, and when someone opens their door, yours bangs, which isn't great when a bunch of people come in at 3 a.m. 
The good bit? There is a good bit - the beds are comfortable, sheets and towels were good and clean - the cleaner makes a good job of it considering what she's up against, the breakfast isn't so bad, there is coffee whenever you want it in the lobby, the staff are nice, the hotel is probably one of the cheapest you'll find in DC.
This would be an excellent hotel for someone on a strict budget - no so good if you are in DC on business.

title: “far from a 5 star experience”
text: Myself and my sister have stayed in the barclay before and were very impressed with it however this year we thought that the whole experience was definitely not worth the money. The room was big but the decor was very dated, the wall paper was coming off the bathroom walls. There was no turn down service and no robes, which I would expect from a 5 star hotel. The food and drink was way over priced. Some of the staff were very unfriendly and openly showed that they were not happy with the tips given...Sorry Barclay will definitely not be returning again.

title: “Wonderful stay!”
text: Our first stay at the Adolphus far exceeded our expectations so it will be the first of many stays to come. This hotel is beautifully maintained where every staff member makes you feel appreciated as a guest. We enjoyed hearing about and experiencing the historical background of the hotel-be sure and ask about the background of the Steinway piano. The staff was knowledgable about other locations in Dallas and the hotel courtesy car was a real plus for ease of getting around. Afternoon tea provided an enjoyable glimpse into elegance of the past. This was one of the most relaxing and enjoyable stays I have experienced. If you are visiting Dallas, reward yourself with a different hotel experience offered by the graciousness of the Adolphus.

title: “Terrific hotel - fantastic location”
text: I stayed here during a business trip and it was a terrific hotel! I had a large room with wireless internet in the room and I had access to the Concierge Lounge which included free breakfast, appetizers, and dessert bar at night. The fitness facility is huge with free weights and plenty of cardio equipment. The View Lounge on the 39th floor offers a breathtaking view of the city. The location is close to great shopping and restaurants. The staff was friendly and helpful - an overall great hotel.

title: “Clean & Convenient!”
text:
Just returned from staying at the Candlewood - and wanted to reiterate comments already made. If you do your research on this properly (TripAdvisor!) then I guess you won't be disappointed - as this is not a hotel in the traditional sense. There is no daily housekeeping - though clean towels are provided on request. Yes - the rooms are small - but probably in line with other similarly priced NYC hotels - and isn't a problem if you're not planning to spend time in the hotel room, which we weren't. That said, the rooms are clean and the kitchette is handy for preparing breakfast and light meals if you're not planning to eat out all the time.
In terms of location - it was ideally suited for TImes Square (and associated,eatieres) and getting around Manhattan with a subway station nearby to get to sites such as the State of Liberty (direct line for the 1 line). We walked all the way to Central Park from here to the north of the city in about an hour. You're also a few minutes walk away from the Empire State Building. Some reviews have stated that the Candlewood located in a "seedy" side street. We certainly didn't feel this - though that said we probaly wouldn't opt to stay further south or west from here. 
There are some nice touches such as free cookies at about tea time on some days and a free welcome back of microwaveable popcorn. They also provide washing up liquid and dishwasher tablets which is helpful. I understand there was a free laundry and gym facilities though we never used these. There is also a complimentary DVD library at reception.
Only slight quibbles - one of the elevators wasn't working for the duration of our stay - which meant waiting ages for the lift. Also, the front desk staff could be more informative when providing travel and sightseeing information.
Overall, a clean and convenient stay and would stay here again!

title: “There were bugs in my room... Concord California”
text: At first glance I was excited about staying here. I booked this hotel for 4 days and all seemed well until I was actually in the room for most of the day. I initially had a problem with a backed up sink and the shower or tub leaked like crazy after taking a shower. I spent so much time trying to correct this issue myself without any prevail. I was spending more time trying to figure out what was wrong with it that finally I just gave up! I asked the housekeeper if she could at least unclog the sink and she did. Thanks! Hei She was great and very efficient with her room cleaning skills! I also noticed on the 2nd day these big ant looking bugs dropping from the ceiling onto the bed which made it very hard to fall asleep at night. The last 2 nights were the worst. I had these things popping up from who knows where. I didn't have any food or sweet drinks in the room (I only drink water) so I don't know what the deal was there. I took pictures because I never seen anything like it before. Not what one would expect from a 3.5 star hotel. I wish I would have had the opportunity to at least try one of these famous cookies that everyone talks about but I wasn't even offered one at check in. I was in buliding 4 and the elevator wouldn't let me out on 2 occasions ( I thought I was going to have to use that red button) then 3 different times I had hit the button to take me to the 3rd floor only to be sent back to the first floor. A fellow guest told me to hold the button down until the doors opened in order to avoid being sent back to another floor. My room (4328) was the very last room to the right of the elevator on the 3rd floor and overlooked a small lake which actually looked more like a swamp and the balcony had so many spiders, webs, and bugs it was hard to stand out there. I spent as little time in that room as possible. I was dissatisfied with the quality of the hotel after alll of the issues I had. The bugs really grossed me out and I believe I was bitten by one as I slept as I had the biggest knot on my foot on the 2nd morning of my stay. These were not bed bugs just some kind of huge ant I mean huge for an ant. Also this hotel charges 21.00 for parking per day. At the end of my stay I had a 88 dollar bill JUST FOR PARKING! That doesn't seem fair considering that I was a paid guest. Guests should not be charged extra for parking or internet! I didn't pay for internet as I just tetthered my phone connection to my laptop for my normal monthly fee. I would have given this hotel a higher rating if it wern't for the bugs, clogged sink, elevator and parking oh and my cookie that I never received. It's a shame because I was all excited about staying here, bragging to my friend about my 3.5 star hotel. Who had a better experience at the cheaper hotel down the street with free parking. Gee Thanks Doubletree!

title: “I Will Stay Here Again”
text:
Very pleasant, convenient, safe, with a great staff! Good location for visiting SF: Only about a block to the F Trolley that goes down to fisherman's wharf. The Gray Line tours have a pickup point here, which was helpful.
The internet worked perfectly.

title: “Great Location”
text: My husband and I stayed in this hotel for 7 night on a 2 week trip to New York. The room was clean and tidy albeit small but we had expectatioins that this was the case based on other reviews. On 2 occassions we had cold water showers, there seemed to be no reason for this according to the hotel but unfortunately it tainted our stay. To the hotels credit they did refund our internet connection fee for the inconvenience. Also found that you could not regulate the heating - it was way too hot in the room and then all of a sudden the heating would go off. During our stay my room card became defective and would not open the room door, apparently the hotels reservation system was down so for an entire day each time we went back to our room they had to send security up to let me in, and security were not quick. The hotel is in a great location if you want to be really touristy, all the restaurants cater for tourists and it is very close to Times Square and Central Park. For out second week we stayed at Murry Hill at the Affinia Dumont which was much better, very centrally located and a much better class of restaurant district.

title: “My stay at the Good Nite Inn”
text: My stay at the Good Nite Inn was comforting! I was here to see my grandson graduate from the Marine Corp. bootcamp! The stay in the hotel was pleasant, quiet and nondisturbing from other roomers! The desk clerk was very helpful with all my concerns and questions. He even helped with finding me the right map to get to Coronado Island. Very prompt service! Was checked in and out very quickly! Would recommend this hotel to others!

title: “Excellent experience!”
text: This was the cutest hotel! My husband and I stayed there for a weekend get away for our anniversary. I loved the literary theme, and the decor was nice. The rooms are a little small, but this is common in SF. They were very clean and I loved the two jazz cd's they provided in the room. The restaurant is magnificent -- I highly recommend the portobello mushroom eggs benedict thing.

title: “Great Times Square Location”
text:
The location for this hotel cannot be beat if you are looking for Times Square (although if you don't like crowds, Times Square is not the right location for you!). This hotel is literally steps from the corner of Toys R Us and ABC (Good Morning America). We were able to walk out of our hotel in the morning and watch GMA taping and see the hosts and guests - it was great! A 10 minute walk in the other direction and we were enjoying a Today Show Friday morning concert. A 15 minute walk to Central Park. Subway is around the corner. Fabulous location.
The hotel itself is decent. It is clean and the room size fine for New York. Our room on the 39th floor had a fabulous Times Square view. The room shows the wear and tear and it is evident that a renovation is needed soon. Having said this, it was clean and comfortable just not up to a four star standard. As for the staff I found them generally helpful and pleasant. The concierge, while she tried to be helpful I found some of the information she provided not very accurate and so preferred to figure things out (re directions) on my own or ask someone on the street. This was probably the only diappointing thing about the hotel as we have previously relied heavily on our concierge's for tips, directions etc. Overall I would stay here again if going to New York with my kids because they loved Times Square and at $200 / night the price was great for the location. I wouldn't pay much more than this and if travelling on our own, my husband and I preferred our previous location off Lexington (Waldorf Astoria/Hotel Benjamin location).
There are numerous restaurants in the area. Carmines (also on 44th street) was great family style Italian food at a reasonable price.
If the price is okay, this is not a bad choice especially if you are not spending a lot of time in the hotel itself.

title: “Excellent value”
text: I stayed in May with my wife and 5 year old daughter. Wow. What a deal. Location is excellent and room was just enough to make the trip a great one. In room 508, we were in the back of the hotel and it was very quiet. My daughter even caught a mid day nap between the Statue of Liberty and the Lion King. Staff was friendly and breakfast was perfect. Cable tv seemed not to work but we didn't use the tv at all. If you're on vacation and want to get around NYC, this is a great option. I'll stay again for sure before I even look elsewhere.

title: “Mother daughter dream come true weekend”
text: Every minute of our stay was a dream come true, especially for my daughter who came with me for a special mother daughter weekend in NYC to include a visit to the American Girl store. I had arranged for the American Girl package. I cannot describe her delight when at check in she was handed an american girl bag filled with goodies including a special doll bed, blanket and pillow for her doll. Also a great surprise was in the morning when we went to the 2nd floor, there was a display set up with complimentary to-go snacks, water bottles and fruit for us to take with us on our NY adventures. The room was spotless and comfortable, and the location terrific, close to Rockefeller Center skating rink (another of our destinations) but also a little bit away from the crowds and traffic, to afford us a quiet nights sleep. We loved the Affinia 50 and can't wait to return.

title: “Ok hotel, a bit outdated. Slow internet connection. Great Service.”
text: I stayed here for a Convention. Service is quite good, they have a free shuttle service that can take you to close distrance places. The hotel is far from downtown, close to Cherry Creek Mall; nothing good close.

title: “Wonderful experience and we will be back.”
text: After hours and hours of on line research we selected the Affinia Dumont as our hotel for our first visit ever to NYC (7 full days). We are very fortunate we did. It had everything we were looking for in a hotel. The location is excellent, a subway station within 2 blocks, numerous restaurants and grocery stores near by, and a beautiful neighborhood for leisurly strolls. The online photos of the hotel do not do it justice. It is immaculate and modern, and the rooms are VERY spacious,comfortable, QUIET, and have a kitchenette. The bed was one of the finest we have ever slept in. The staff was perfect for our needs, we never saw a house keeper, yet our room was always immaculate. The lobby personnel are friendly and professional. For the budget conscious, I challenge anyone to find a hotel of this quality at the same or lower rate! It is a truly remarkable hotel!!!

title: “Basic Hotel, Great Location”
text: Stayed here over the 4th of July with the family. We were on the 20th floor with a great view of the harbor. We had a great view of the fireworks from the hallway windows. Within walking distance to the Boston Commons. The Duck tour picked you up across the street from the hotel. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Valet parking was expensive (46/night) but the only other option was a public lot that wasn't much cheaper (35/night). There is a mall across the street with some inexpensive food choices and a supermarket as well so I didn't have to spend an arm and a leg at the Ben & Jerry shop for the kids. Just got the ice cream at the supermarket and ate it in the room. My only complaint was that the beds were too soft.

title: “Good for what you pay!!!”
text: We stayed at this hotel from 9/1 thru 9/3 and so far we thought it was a good deal for what we paid. The room although old fashion-like, was clean and quiet and the staff was very friendly. On the sad note I would like to add that priceline.com shows continental breakfast as one of the amenities and that isn't true. Also the shower head is located so low you could easily hit your head with it. I guess they were made for midgets. Boston China Town like all the China Towns I've seen are always too congested and awfully dirty so that doesn't add beauty to the hotel sorroundings and it doesn't compare to the rest of Boston which is neat. Anyway I'm satisfied with this hotel and will stay here again.

title: “Loved the Waldorf Astoria!!”
text: We stayed for 4 nights at the Waldorf Astoria!! Great location -you can walk to alot of different sites ! Comfortable bed and very friendly staff! Highly recommend it!

title: “Convenient to Amtrak Station”
text:
Wanted a hotel near amtrak station, this hotel is about 5 or 6 blocks, cab fare was $5. Convenient to San Diego Pier we
sailed on cruise the following day. Staff is very pleasant and accomodating.

title: “great location, small clean room”
text: my husband and I stayed here for an overnight trip to do some shopping. This hotel is located right on the Mile. We took a chance on one of the petite rooms for a great price and were not disappointed. It was small but it was clean and appeared to be updated. We would definitely stay here again if we had another opportunity for a great rate.

title: “A lovely hotel with friendly staff.”
text: Our first visit to the Morgans hotel in New York, we arrived late evening for check in and found the staff to be very friendly and efficient. The hallways to our room were narrow and dark with dimmed lighting but we were pleasantly surprised with our room,it was large,very clean and contemporary with a very comfortable bed. The buffett breakfast was a great way to start the day, everything you needed. The living room on the fourth floor was a very comfortable area to relax with free tea and coffee. The hotel was in a great location 5 mins walk to Empire State Building and Macys, 10 mins to Times Square and Grand Central Station. Would stay at the Morgans again we had a great holiday in New York, Alan and Angela England.

title: “Awesome!”
text: I expected the Gansevoort to be fancy, but it went farther than I had even anticipated. The rooms were big enough to fit 4 - 2 rooms were perfect for my 6 girlfriends and I. The bathrooms were beautiful and inviting as were the beds. Dinner at Ono was superb as was the waitstaff. But my favorite part of the entire experience was the roofdeck pool. It was much bigger than I expected and not overly crowded. We were all able to get lounge chairs (a must for this crew) and were able to relax completely. I would ABSOLUTELY stay here again!

title: “Located close to heart of union square and public transport”
text: Family rooms here are great, seperate parents room which is nice for privacy with a connecting bathroom....has a safe...2 tvs...and was surprised to find a lovely welcome gifts....bar and grill resturaunt downstairs has yummy food but a little pricey for what you get....especially with a family....service was great from all hotel staff....parking is dear but really where else is there to park?? Room was very dated but elegant for its years....very clean...shower was average not much pressure...bed not that comfortable....would stay again though as liked the location...lots of great shopping in walking distance....

title: “Great meeting and stay at Radisson LAX”
text:
The staff at this hotel was very inventive in all area. Arrival was warm and friendly. The beds are incredible.
As a meeting planner, I could not have asked for more attention to detail. Feed back from my attendees gave this hotel an A+. This hotel ensured the success of my meeting. I could not have asked for more.
We will return!

title: “Great value - Terrific Reno”
text:
