Stayed at Sheraton BH as part of business in the area. Although there's not much to do within walking distance (however I do recommend the Mexican restaurant for takeout -- Juanita's), the hotel itelf is terrific. After hurricane damage in 2008, it appears they completely renovated the hotel. 
Lobby is very nice with a new business center / internet cafe; in-house gift shop for any last-minute items/snacks; restaurant with a solid breakfast buffet (including custom-made omelettes); and room with nice large flatscreen and comfortable beds.
If you're renting a car, I would highly recommend this hotel as you can easily jump on the 610 and head to the Galleria for shopping or downtown (you must brave Houston traffic volumes though!). It's basically halfway between the airport and downtown. 
Staff are friendly and helpful, the rooms well appointed and the rate was very reasonable! I will always stay here whenever I'm in the area.

title: “Wonderful resort”
text: My husband and I and our two small children stayed in a one room condo and loved it!! The condo was spacious and clean. The bathroom was wonderful with a huge shower and a large jacuzzi tub. The employee's at the resort were just wonderful, when we would call for anything we needed they would be at the door injust a few minutes. They have alot of activities for the kids which they enjoyed. The pool is large and not crowded the only thing with the pool is from most of the buildings you have to drive to it but we got used to it. We would definatley come back, we enjoyed every minute :)

title: “It was worth the price”
text: It's not the best hotel I've been to but there was nothing terrible about it. Clean, safe, easy to get to and priced right. I'd stay again for sure.

title: “Fantastic Place”
text: Stay here! Great customer service, very nice rooms, great views, top of the line hotel. This place is huge! Lots of things to do.

title: “Nice spot”
text: Didn't know what to expect and was pleasantly surprised. The hotel is tucked in the hills & offers great views. I stayed in a suite which was very nice. The convention center had an easy layout and the banquet food was surprisingly very good. I travel a lot and usually after food has sat on a buffet for a few hours its not at all appetizing, but here it was excellent. We went to the lounge at 'different point of view' which is on property and has an amazing view of Phoenix. They have marshmallows soaked in different liquors that you can roast over open fire pits! This was very cool! There are 4 pools and it seems to be a great place to bring families, have a family reunion, or even a small wedding. I would stay here again.

title: “Wonderful Hotel!”
text:
My husband and I recently got married at the Back Bay Hotel. It is a beautiful hotel that has a great location in the back bay- a short walk to both the Green and Orange T lines. The hotel staff was amazing and they went out of their way to make our stay unforgettable. While we were there for our wedding we were treated like honored guests. From big things like having our room upgraded to the presidential suite to smaller things like hot cocoa waiting for us at check in and champagne and hand made truffles waiting for us in our room after our wedding. 
You certainly don't have to be getting married to receive great service at this hotel. All of our friends and family raved about the friendliness of the staff, the cleanliness of the hotel and its amazing decor. Several of our guest even got upgrades of their own. I recommend this hotel to business travelers and pleasure travelers alike. Also, if you are looking to plan an event go here for the most amazing service in town!

title: “Varsity Inn revisited”
text: We returned to the Varsity Inn after a great experience and the second time it was still pretty good but not as clean. I asked the desk to have someone clean the faint ring in the sink and I noticed the caulking around the tub had started to yellow which can make it look dirty even though it wasn't. The overall experience was still that it is a great value. I will try it again

title: “Location Location Location”
text: My family enjoyed our stay at the Salisbury. The rooms were a bit old and in need of some renovations but the location could not have been more perfect. We were in town for the Macy's Parade and could not have lucked out for the location and price. We got a fabulous deal on Expedia and had a fabulous vacation with the Salisbury serving as a more than suitable home base.

title: “Nice clean hotel with hospitable staff”
text:
You can only rate a venue on what it is trying to achieve. I don't believe the mark twain hotel is trying to achieve much more than what it is. 
It is clean and the staff are hospitable.
One gripe would be that the valet parking was quiet expensive and it did need 20 mins notice to get your car.
The. Neighbourhood at the bottom of the hill isn't great and would advise to walk up and away from that area, but as soon as you do you are perfectly safe.
Free wifi is a big plus

title: “Just a place to sleep”
text: Was in town for the Nascar race on Sunday and of course spent very little time in the room so for the cost it was well worth it. If your looking for a place where you will be spending sdome time in the room and in the pool, look elsewhere. If your looking for a place to just crash and catch some Z's and not spend a lot of money then this is your place.

title: “Not bad, but just average. Definitely not worth a No. 1 slot.”
text:
OK, so let me start by saying we got a room at a rate of $200 because we got a special hospital rate. Whether this influenced the quality of the room we were given and the service we got, I'm not sure. I hope not.
We entered with the assistance of a doorman named Jeff. He was really pleasant and helpful - I'd rate him highly. My husband and son went straight to the room and I followed them a little later. On entering our room (a Fenway room), I noticed immediately a dusty smell with an odor of old smoke (or even a pet). You know, when a place cleans a room but cannot really get the smell out? Which seemed weird, as I specifically asked for a room that had not seen a pet or allergens because I have bad asthma and allergies. Within a minute or so my eyes were itching and my nose was starting to play up. There was a thick line of dust on the window sill, plus a lovely note from a previous occupant about the jogging trail info saying 'that was the vacation ruiner for me'. Not great cleaning attention to detail!
So I returned to reception to ask if we could swap to a different room? I handed over the note discretely. The receptionist really wasn't interested. She didn't acknowledge the note, simply put it to the side and didn't offer any apology for the room, but took her time clicking away until she found another room. Same style, same layout, same side. That was fine by me (I wasn't looking for a free upgrade - that's not my style), just so long as it was fresher but an 'oops, sorry' would have been nice. The receptionist just seemed almost bored by the request as though it was a chore. Moving into the second room, it was obvious that this was a lot cleaner than the first - no itchy eyes or dust or smell. However, there was no waste bin in the bathroom and some of the room decor was missing. Not worth mentioning to them, but something a No.1 hotel should notice.
The rooms are tired - I suspect the Fenway rooms are all the same decor. They are definitely not up to date. The furniture (armoire, table) is very much like old Floridian pastels decor of the 90's. The beds did not have proper bed covers...simply sheets covered with...blankets. There's something not quite right when the bed looks half dressed and that's the impression it gave. The bed itself was very comfortable - kudos for that. Someone in a previous review mentioned the awful pillows - so soft that when you lay down your head you basically touch the mattress. I didn't know you could ask for firmer pillows otherwise I would have done. The decor felt very much to me like being in an older Marriott - a decent sized room but with striped wallpaper and dark green carpeting. Maybe we were just in the older side of the building?
The bathroom was light and very clean with heaps of towels...a definite plus...but with a tiny bath - nothing to relax in. The shower was very powerful, also a plus. Unfortunately there were not enough toiletries for the three of us, so I had to request more. Again, whoever on Reception answered the call didn't seem particularly energised or bothered about the request but we did eventually get the toiletries from a very nice housekeeping guy. 
My husband was working from the room and one of us had to be in the room at all times due to our child on meds, but there was no coffee or tea facility in the room and he was desperate for a coffee whilst working! This is bizarre because if he wanted a coffee, he'd have to order room service coffee. I'm not sure why anyone would bother with room service just for a cup of coffee.
We took turns going to the Eastern Standard restaurant for dinner and sat at the bar to eat. The bar staff were very good as was the food. I had fish which was the best I have eaten. The bar is very well stocked and I noticed that a couple of people were raving about a beer on the reserve list - so if you are a beer drinker, that will be worth checking out. Food-wise, if you are a vegetarian - it's not the place for you as it had an over-reliance on offal dishes - bone marrow, offal, beef cheeks, etc and I found it difficult to find something on the menu that would work. That being said, the cod dish was fantastic.
I was going to give the hotel a 2 rating. The only reason I knocked it up to a 3 rating is the quality of the food in the restaurant and the nice doorman. Otherwise the hotel deserved a 2. It really needs to step it up in terms of attention to detail in order to maintain a top 10 rating (never mind the Number 1). The let-downs were the quality of the room and the quality of the staff. I'm sorry but rooms should be clean and stocked properly and with modern decor. If a room isn't clean - then a staff member should really acknowledge that appropriately and work to sort it out. Simple things like the ability to have a coffee in one's room and attention to detail seemed to be lacking. It almost felt like the staff interest at reception was just not there - I felt like I needed to turn their guest-centric dial up a few notches. It's just not worthy of a No.1 hotel slot. I'm amazed that other reviewers have called it a luxury hotel. The dining and in-room bar prices are 'luxurious', but nothing else.
Having stayed in other places in Boston over the years, I really can't recommend it. There are places with more facilities and updated rooms and more engaged staff for an equivalent price in the city. It's just not somewhere we'd bother with in future.

title: “Location, view, and service”
text: This is a fabulous hotel and location is next to convention center. The Roy's restaurant is on the marina. The weather was windy and cold so the gorgeous pool was empty. The service is top notch too. You can walk from hotel to shopping very close by or take a cab to great restaurants near by.

title: “How is this a Doubletree!?!”
text: This hotel is so out of date and doesn't know how to treat their guests. This is a ridiculous representation of the Doubletree/Hilton brands. I hear it's being renovated, yet I haven't seen anything happen yet. I hope the service will change with the renovations.

title: “W Hotel - The Court”
text: We arrived late for check in and the room STILL wasn't ready! The customer service at this hotel was NOT worth the money paid, but the hotel itself was pretty nice. On another night we called room service for extra pillows, and the guy who answered said "are you serious?" (it was late) and the pillows never came. YES, when I call room service for extra pillows I am serious, even if it is 2am. One day the elevator was serviced ALL day, so we were forced to take the stairs or service elevator. The service elevator took FOREVER, so taking the stairs provided some un-needed exercise. The room was nice, the bathroom could have been nicer but the bed was ULTRA comfy and the room had all the basic necessities. GREAT hotel location, right next to Grand Central and walking distance to Times Square and the Empire State Building. I like that the hotel was still close enough to everything but far enough from the Times Square bustle.

title: “New Yrs 30th Birthday Surprise Bust!!!”
text: If your looking for something special, a pampered feeling, or something that isn't your run of the mill hotel do not stay here. The hotel is very poorly staffed so be prepared to wait, not have your needs met, or feel like your in for a treat. My sister usually stays here when she works on call @ Hopkins but had to cancel at last minute due to my sickly nephew..so I hoped on this deal.My BF and I "went away" for the weekend for my b-day (New Yrs) 2011. and he said he had called ahead for some basic suprises in the room(rose pedals, cake, and balloons) to be there for our arrival. They were not able to do as promised. We noticed during check in a rather large amount of young people racing through the lobby at that point I assumed they were having a hotel party. At check in it was the worst. They had me sign some smoking policy paper with a $$deductable, boy oh boy and at that point we were able to find the a/c broke, I need air a little air circulating because of allergy problems That took about another 1/2 hour to fix. No apologies or deductions for their error on the b-day suprise or a/c issue. The bed was sooo uncomfortable, the plumbing noise in the bathroom unbearable. Check out was even a bigger hassle, they actually sent housekeeping to "sniff" the room before I could get my cash back, what the hell, she literally inhaled for a scent check. TOTALLY UNBELIEVEABLE!! I see from some reviews they have some done some updating and renovations, but with the experience I had I'm way too scared to try this place again. What a way to bring in a landmark 30th Birthday & New Years-very disappoining!!!

title: “They live the term 'quality'”
text: We had the opportunity to attend a Indianapolis Colts Football Game (daughter is a cheerleader) and stayed overnite at the JW Marriott. It was an outstandstanding experience. Not only did the room have a great view but the room was amazing clean and comfortable. If JW Marriott, has a mission statement or core values, the employees live it...you feel the special treatment as soon as you get out of your car and it continues through the desk and into the restaurants. Because of the game ending late, we showed up for dinner late but the staff did not hesitate to serve us and with a smile. The atmosphere and the park setting that this hotel is in, makes it more attractive. Then with the fact that it is attached to the convention center which is right across the street from the football field makes it even more convenient for the inside walk to the stadium.

title: “Very grand, good location”
text:
I just got back from staying at the Palace with my wife this past weekend. I knew going it was an older hotel with smaller rooms, and I wasn't sure about the location, so I was skeptical whether I would like the hotel. But I must say I was pleasantly surprised. 
The hotel was very grand. The lobby was much prettier than I expected. There was a big crowd checking in when we arrived but the front desk handled it smoothly and efficiently. 
Our room was larger than I anticipated. We had a king size bed, flat screen tv. , lounge chair and a desk that was sufficient for me to work from. The bathroom was small, but since I knew that going in, it wasn't a problem. But there was definitely no way more than one person at a time could be in the bathroom. 
The bed was comfortable and room quiet so I had no complaints. 
The only meals we had in the hotel were the breakfast buffet. The buffet was nothing spectacular but it was good. In addition to the usual scrambeled eggs, bacon and sausages, there were blintzes, waffles, pancakes etc. Nothing to complain about. 
The restaurant in which the buffet was served however was spectacular. The room reminded me very much of where they served the buffett at the Alvear Palace in Buenos Aires. For that matter the common areas of the hotel (not the guest rooms) reminded me of the Alvear. 
The location of the hotel worked out very nicely for us. It is in close walking distance to the convention center, china town, and good shopping. 
All in all a positive experience. The only negative comment either I or my wife had was that when she gave the concierge two packages already sealed with fed ex forms filled out and ready to go, the concierge charged her 5 dollars to out in the hotel's fed ex pickup. I thought a formal charge to basically put a package in the mail was kind of chintzy but nothing worth complaining about. I would stay there again.

title: “Older property loaded with character and excellent service”
text:
I attended the same 3200-person convention someone else mentioned below. While a lot of our people stayed at nearby hotels, most of us were here and everyone attended sessions and meals at the T&C. With one exception, every interaction I had with staff was excellent - the service was generally what I would expect at a much more luxurious (and expensive) place.
It's an older property, made up of many one and two storey buildings sprawling around a large campus, filled with pools, gardens and courtyards, plus a couple newer towers at the back. The usual amenities in the rooms, several restaurants, gift shops, day spa etc. A nice big convention center unobtrusively on one side.
Pros: 
- The afore-mentioned service. Every staff member was friendly and pro-actively helpful, whether I was in the coffee shop or taking a short cut and getting myself lost in the bowels of the laundry. :-) 
- Everything was spotlessly clean, everything worked, and everything looked nice (no mean feat in an older property). No broken blinds, crumbling sills, spotty showers or threadbare linens to be found - full marks to housekeeping & maintenance.
- We ate all our meals in the convention center, and for having to feed 3200 in about an hour per meal (plated meals each time), I was extremely impressed. (Except for breakfast. Oh well.) Fast, quick, friendly and even tasty, too!
- Well-located and easy to find. And just a 5minute walk across a footbridge over the river to a mall, should you want more dining options etc.
- A lot of space, if you're booking for a group. Nice convention center, and a host of smaller ballrooms and meeting rooms, as well. Many of them have nice views to gardens, pools, etc.
- Staff will drive you around in a golf cart if you need it.
- Character! Peace and quiet. I took some free time one afternoon and just wandered around the gardens and courtyards. I'd much rather stay somewhere like this than a high-rise block that could be anywhere.
Cons:
- Well, for those who don't appreciate that character...It is older, which in many areas means "smaller". I think I was in the "Traditional Accommodations" - very small room. (We referred to it as the "European section".) If you need your space, or have more than two in a room, ask for one of the towers. (That said, I found the room charming.)
- Some people might not like the size of the resort - it's very spread out, and can be hard to find your way around.
- No free wifi (per my roommate).
- Parking was $10/day
Issues:
- Any 3200-person group will have them. One of our rooms was given away - we were told the previous guests had decided to extend their stay. Our couple was offered a "parlor" (the sitting/dining area of a suite - it's a separate connecting room, and wasn't in use) and rollaway beds. While it worked out for them, I was shocked the hotel allowed the previous guests to stay on like that, knowing the property was fully booked out.
That issue aside, I was really impressed. I'm keeping it on my list for my next San Diego trip.

title: “Elegant but with Problems”
text:
We stayed at the Hay Adams for 2 nights recently on a weekend visit to DC. It was a nice experience, but not quite up to what I expect from a hotel of this reputation and at this price. 
Our room was nice, but not substantially nicer than many other hotels I have stayed in. The hotel could use some sprucing up. The hallways were dingy and the carpet needs replacing. 
The bathroom was spacious, immaculately clean, and very nice, though the shower situation was not great. As one reviewer noted, the water pressure isn't very good, and there is an awkward shower mechanism which we could not adjust to keep it from shooting water in such a way that it drenched the bathroom floor.
The room itself had scuffed and chipped floor mouldings and standard-issue furniture. There was no proper closet, only a very small wardrobe that scarcely held our clothes for the weekend. However, the bed was lovely and very comfortable with crisp linens and plentiful pillows. One thing I particularly liked was that, in contrast to many hotels that are now providing only a duvet on the bed (which in most cases is WAY too warm for the room), this bed had a sheet and a light blanket, with a duvet folded at the end of the bed. The sheet and blanket were plenty of cover, and I appreciated not having to swelter under a duvet. In the end the bed is what matters most to me in a hotel, as I'm mostly there to sleep, so this was a positive. 
Another positive is that housekeeping is very attentive--the bed was beautifully turned down in the evening and after we showered in the afternoon the towels were all always replaced when we came back after dinner. 
My gripe is that there were several special events in the hotel that weekend and these caused some inconveniences which were not acknowledged by the hotel. There was a roof party on Saturday night and the guests was constant, noisy traffic in the hall from the time we got home from dinner until after 11pm (we were on the 8th floor where the stair to the roof is located). A few of the drunk partygoers were also staying in rooms near ours, and we could hear quite a bit through the walls. As other reviewers have noted, you hear EVERYTHING in this hotel--your neighbors, the housekeeping staff in the hall, etc. 
Additionally, another special event took over the restaurant, which is a lovely space for breakfast, and instead breakfast was pushed to a small, noisy, windowless room where the staff are clearly not accustomed to serving. No compensation is made for being pushed out of the main dining room. I think a true luxury hotel that wants people to come back should make some kind of concession when the expected amenities are not available because of special events.
So in the end, If you are going to Washington to see the monuments, the Smithsonian museums, the National Mall, the White House, this is a great location, and the rooms are nice and service is good. But don't expect a really memorable and special experience. As for me, next time I want to stay in a luxury hotel in Washington I will probably try the Willard.

title: “Fabulous Location and Newly Renovated”
text:
i stayed in this Hilton hotel 3 nights while my husband was having surgery at the University of Penn Hospital. It is only a four block walk through the campus to reach the hospital which I made many times, cutting through the campus each time. It was a safe walk at any hour. My room was on the 4th floor overlooking the campus and I did not hear any street noise. The King room was lovely, with one lounge to sit in by day to read as the sun gleamed in the window. There was an ipad in the room to use, which was very convenient since I only had my smart phone to e mail. 
Pros
~The service was fantastic and the maids were very understanding of my situation letting me sleep in one morning while skipping service, they hung a bag of extras like water and coffee on my door. 
~The rooms were spotless, roomy the bed and pillows were comfy, the shower was great.
~ I loved their lighted mirror in the bathroom. It is the only time I have every looked good by a hotel bathroom light. I want one for my home.
~ The Penne restaurant attached had a nice lunch special which I enjoyed three days in a row. The arugula salad and a chose of entree for $17 was a good deal and served as my main meal. There is a breakfast buffet also, but I did not partake. 
~Front desk staff very helpful and there is a large living room area with fireplace area which was a nice touch.
Very quiet. I never heard anyone above or next to me or any street noise. 
~Coffee available in room, but also there is a starbucks in the college bookstore next door, and one down the street. There is a cafe called Cosi right out the back door entrance which served wonderful breakfast sandwiches and lunch salads/sandwiches which I purchased and put in the refridge in my room for a late dinner. There roasted veggie sandwich was my favorite.
Cons
Parking is 39.00 a day, a bit steep, but it is the city. I parked my car at the hospital since my husband was a patient and rolled my luggage over...short walk.. You might want to check out other near by self park lots.

title: “Lots of glitz but not so much substance”
text: A beautiful property for sure, but not all rooms have bathtubs, the bar cuisine and room service mens are somewhat limited (for those of us arriving late from the other coast). I

title: “My husband had to pry me out of the Ritz bathrobe!!”
text:
Over the top...every aspect of this beautiful hotel was over the top.
Every staff member was lovely, the place is impeccably clean and the hotel is beautifully decorated.
It was a huge treat to stay somewhere so special. I just wish that we had more time to relax and enjoy it. We were in Chicago on business which left little time to use all the facilities. On our next visit, we will be sure to add another day to our stay so that we can enjoy the pool, steam room sauna and whirlpool. I will also book a massage and/or a facial.
The Ritz couldn't have been nicer.

title: “Loud and Busy”
text:
We stayed in room 606 which faces Light St. The street noise on a weekend is very loud until late at night. Also, the noise coming up from the bar, which was 2 floors below, and people walking and talking (drunkenly) in the hallways persisted until 2 am. Now granted there were several conference groups in the hotel, including comic-con, but that is the nature of this hotel.
Room was clean. Bathroom is very industrial looking with little counter space. No bath tub, just a shower.
Bed was comfortable. A/C was easy to adjust and not terribly loud. Mini-bar refrigerator, but not enough room to really put your own items inside.
Staff is very courteous. We got in at 11:30 pm and room service was gracious enough to make me an entree even though the cut off time for anything but appetizers was 10pm.
Location is right across from the harbor and you can walk there in about 5 minutes from any room in the hotel.

title: “Recommend”
text: Comfortable, Great Location. Problem Arose with Safe, which was dealt with above and beyond what was expected, to our benefit. Would certainly stay there again.

title: “Excellent value in NYC”
text: I almost hate to post a good review here, because I think the word is getting out and I couldn't get a room here on a recent visit. That being said, this is not the nicest hotel I've ever stayed in, but for what you get per dollar spent, it's my top choice when visiting New York. The hotel is spot-on for the most important things--cleanliness, quality bedding, and quiet--and although the rooms aren't fancy, it's New York, and if you're spending all that time in the hotel, why even bother visiting? And the staff are the nicest and friendliest in the city. It seems like the front desk staff changes a lot, but no one is ever anything less than warm, genuine, and helpful. The kitchens in the rooms are an added bonus, especially if you have kids, and can save you some money for breakfast, snacks and cocktails. Bathrooms are a little dark, but clean and large and there's no issue with hot water or pressure. Gym likewise is dark and dated but is free. Maybe Affinia will upgrade to free wifi for our next visit, since the computers in the lobby are usually taken during normal hours. If you want a big name or a fancy location or a lot of bells and whistles, this is not the hotel for you. But if you prefer to spend your travel dollars outside of your hotel, you can make a visit to New York less of a budget breaker by staying here without worries.

title: “Train and Train Crossing makes it IMPOSSIBLE to sleep!”
text:
I'm a Hilton Diamond member and the experience at this hotel has made me consider changing to another chain completely! I have lost all confidence in Hilton. My party and I (4 rooms rented) specifically asked about the train noise and we were lied to by the front desk person. She told us that the trains stopped at 11pm and didn't begin again until 6am. She neglected to tell us that the trains run until nearly midnight AND a HUGE freight train comes through at 4:15AM!!! Then, the trains started again at 5:15AM.
I showered and departed the hotel 2.5 hours before I needed to because I couldn't stand the train and bell noise! Horrible experience and I caution all except the totally deaf to stay away from this property. As a train station it's fine, but as a place you're supposed to sleep it's a joke.
Shame on you Hilton!

title: “amazing hotel”
text:
We stayed during the busy final four weekend and although we paid a ridiculous price per night, we couldnt have been happier with our stay.
The rooms are fabulous, bed was large and comfortable, modern lights, large flat screen tv in bedroom, and the bathroom was awesome with its large dual head shower, seperate toilet and flat screen tv in the mirror and bose sound system.
The highlight of the room was their turn service that went above and beyond all expectations.
The piano lounge had a lively atmosphere and reseasonable drink prices. We did not eat in their signiture restaurants but the food court provided a good place to grab a quick bite, with a lot of variety, decent food, and not too expensive.
If you are looking for a romantic getaway in Detroit, look no further.

title: “Terrific”
text: I travel quite a bit, and this is one of the most phenomenal places I've ever stayed. The hotel and rooms are absolutely gorgeous, the location is literally blocks away from a great park, restaurants and retail, and is very convenient to the local convention center. There are several cool small hotels in Indy, but nothing beats this place. Definitely check it out.

title: “Good Pre-Flight Place to Stay”
text: I stayed here one night before a flight out of Phoenix. The hotel was right off of I10 minutes from the Airport. The hotel was clean, updated and a good value for the money. The breakfast had good offerings, but in my opinion could have been better quality. I took the shuttle in the morning and it was ontime and the driver was courteous. Overall I would stay at this hotel again for a pre-flight but not as a Phoenix vacation extended stay. The swimming pool was very small.

title: “Real New York”
text:
My visit to the W New York was for only one night. I have read the reviews on the positives and negatives and felt that the W (49th St.) deserved my business. 
Here is my experience. I arrived to be greeted by an easygoing hotel staff. I was upgraded to a Spectacular Room on the 15th floor at no charge; however, this upgrade was for a room that is located in front of the 15th floor elevator hall. Because of this set-up, expections were to be hit with a barrage of noise from the comings and goings from the elevator, but to my surprise there was little noise. The room was clean with exception of toilet. There was a stain in the toilet bowel. The sheets were clean and the room was free of any litter. The overall size of the room was compact. My companion and I were fine with the size, but other folks may have trouble maneuvering around the bed. The bed was very soft and falling asleep was not a problem. I would say this room reminded me of a studio apartment in Midtown so staying here would be a realistic New York experience. 
Overall, I would urge people to seek out other review sites before dropping money on a place. I did not take in the bar scene within the lobby so if the W (49th St.) selling point is the bar/restaurant then I missed out. The location for the hotel is one block from the Green 6 line so if you want to get in late after a long night in the city then this place is for your consideration. 
Later

title: “Disappointed with the Hotel Drisco”
text:
My husband and I recently booked a "standard room" at this hotel through Expedia. In booking a standard room, we assumed, mistakenly, that our room would include an attached bathroom. It turned out that our so-called "standard room" had what the hotel referred to as a "detached bathroom," meaning a bathroom across the hall. For some reason, Expedia didn't mention this feature in its list of room amenities. When I asked the hotel for a room with an "attached" bathroom, the hotel clerk advised that I would need to upgrade. The hotel clerk pointed out that the hall was "private" even though the hotel cleaning staff and guests in one other room made use of the hall. 
Private or not, we still had to put on a robe, and take a key every time we wanted to use the bathroom. After looking at the hotel brochure, we figured out that the hotel had actually split up a two bedroom suite located in the so-called private hall. If you are booking through Expedia, opt for the suite or stay elsewhere if you want to be able to stumble to the bathroom in the middle of the night. Other than this problem, the hotel was very nice and the breakfast was quite good.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: I had a very good experience with this hotel. Staff was very friendly. In case you are traveling with a baby, they have cribs available.

title: “Don't believe any of those negative comments!”
text: I booked this hotel in mid April to stay May 27 to May 31 and a week before we arrived, I noticed on their website that the price had dropped . I immediatly emailed the hotel and was emailed back within 5 minutes to tell me that of course I would get the lower price. Then, that evening I found out that I could also upgrade my room at no extra charge! We had breakfast included at the Cafe Edison and I just wanted to say that the food was good and the staff was extremely friendly and efficient. Check in and out was a breeze and we had no problem getting our room at noon and storing our luggage when leaving for a mere fifty cents a bag! The whole experience was extremely pleasant and we would not think twice about staying there again if we have the good fortune to visit NYC again! Mom Tina and daughter Amy-Brampton,Ontario

title: “Just What We Were Looking For”
text:
I got a sweetheart deal for this hotel on Expedia and was glad that I did. The hotel is so convenient, right next to Market Street and near MOMA also and the Moscone Center. It is one block away from major transportation routes on the bus and BART. The front desk personnel were friendly and efficient, all business. I like that. The hotel lobby was busy and uncluttered, as was the front area where taxis pulled in and out. If you drive to the hotel, don't park there and pay fifty dollars plus tips, you should instead turn left on Stevenson Street right after the front of the hotel, and drive down the alley and take the first left into that parking garage where you will only pay twenty five dollars for 24 hour parking. It's clean and very cheap for the area. We loved it. 
The room was very clean, and she upgraded us to a Starwoods Preferred Room, on the corner of the building. It was very quiet, and so modern and attractive. We had a fabulous view and the bed was very comfortable. The amenities were great! I would recommend this hotel to anyone travelling to SF. The only problem with this hotel is that it is close to Market Street, and there is a lot of questionable activity on that street, so just try to avoid that and you'll be fine. It close to Union Square and all the shopping too. For the price this hotel can't be beat!

title: “Pity they didn't tell us about the renovations!”
text: We stayed here 11 yrs ago and enjoyed our stay. However, on returning we found the hotel in a state of upheaval with only a small lobby, always packed with people, Dean and Delucas is gone and only a small lounge always packed with people because the wifi is free there only. The rooms are tired though clean. Wouldn't stay here again.

title: “Great hotel in a very convenient location”
text: We stayed for 8 nights in May 09. I researched a large number of hotels before deciding on the Sofitel. The overall experience was superb. A lovely quiet room on the 29th floor. The midtown location is great, on a nice street, and only few minutes walk to Times Square and many other attractions. Hotel staff are very good.

title: “okay hotel”
text:
It is a typical business oriented hotel: shiny large lobby, conference rooms, posh restaurants, and rather small but okay and clean rooms. Never mind, I enjoyed staying with the family for a couple of nights. The kids loved the spaceous pool. Breakfast buffet was superb. Though I had a bit of a run-in with the waiter when he pointed out that we as a family of four had only two b'fast vouchers. I asked him whether my kids were supposed to starve, or whether two people had to watch the other two eating. I don't know why we had only two vouchers and I wasn't in the mood to make much fuzz about it. Don't get the wrong impression: I was immediately offered the deal that only one extra breakfast was charged and the restaurant staff was very friendly and competent.
Overall, I was very satisfied with the hotel.

title: “Clean and Basic”
text:
I needed an economical hotel for one night that was located near the convention center. I checked every hotel in downtown and was surprised to see moderately rated properties were well over $150 a night.
So I weaved my way through the Trip Advisor lists until I found the Rodeway Inn for under $100. I had the same concerns as everyone else on the board, particularly the safety issue. 
I have to say, this hotel is a pretty decent value for downtown LA. The parking is free, the wireless is free, and the convention center is only a quick drive away. The bus lines are also plentiful, as another person mentioned. The food situation is bit dicey. El Pollo Loco, MickD, and a smattering of mom and pop places are nearby. There is a 7-11 next door. The area is okay, not quite the place for an evening stroll, but then neither is anywhere in downtown LA.
The check inn was friendly and smooth, and the room was clean. For those of you not familiar with downtown LA, you should know that parking is practically non-existent. Most hotels will run you over $150, charge for parking, wireless, and the food prices will be astronomical. A one night stay can turn into a pricey nightmare. 
The Rodeway is en excellent choice for business travelers or tourists who need a central base.

title: “Not bad, free for all at breakfast time.”
text:
A great position, near subway, Maceys etc - ideal for nipping back to whilst you are out and about. There is even coffee available 24 hours in the lobby area.
The rooms were ok. Our's was on the 12th floor and a little pokey and 1980's but lets face it you're hardly in the room at all. The staff were ok, cannot say much about them as had little contact. . My only warning to you is watch out at breakfast time. Peak breakfast time was about 8-9am and there were not enough chairs, people were standing to eat their crunchy nuts - bizzare! We were there at peak time - Easter, but still. In fairness though, a clean and well run hotel. All in all pretty much what you would expect for your money. The city itself however! Fantastic.... Book Up!! Happy Holidays.

title: “Mold”
text: We were looking forward to staying here because it is a new hotel. We were shocked and disappointed to see a moldy shower curtain. The front desk staff were unfriendly and the snacks that were offered for sale were very limited and not anything we could eat. The best thing about this hotel is that it is totally pet free and totally non-smoking.

title: “Very good property”
text: Just returned from a four night stay. The hotel is perfectly located and has very professional staff. The rooms are very nice and the bathrooms are beautiful. The hotel itself is relatively small so it has something of a boutique feel to it...which is good. I would certainly recommend this hotel and would be happy to stay here again.

title: “Great location. Free Room upgrade, nice. Three annoyances, though.”
text: Second trip to NYC. Hotel is in Central location which is fantastic. Staff are great. Concierge was fantastic for infomation on babysitter, subway access, etc. Three Annoyances: ONE: We were touted in the lobby to join the NY hilton club - or a timeshare club. Actually I had no idea what it was for. It was not appreciated. Came for a holiday. Did not want to go through 90 minutes of incentives about club 57.We didn't participate. TWO: I had to screw back on the shower head before we could use it. Figured it was quicker to do this than asking for it to be done. Why was it so un-screwed off in the first place I don't know. Also, the steel caddy for soap etc, was barely recognisable as there was metal prongs sticking out from it - or missing. A bit dangerous and not what I expected to find in the Hilton! The room was a recently rennovated room. But it still was tired in places. Given the room rates there is no excuse for tiredness in furniture? THREE: Internet access $10 for 10 minutes - rediculously dear. Go to "smilies" (I think that's its name) near times square and you can go upstairs and get internet access for about $5 for 20 mins. San Fran Hotel - Americania had the internet for free. Which is a great idea! I won't come back to the NY Hilton. I think I would like to make my $ work harder for me by either going for a cheaper (but no-less tired) hotel, or a newer (same price bracket) boutique hotel.

title: “Perfect location for a Thanksgiving Break”
text:
It was our first visit to New York so we timed it to cover both the Thanksgiving Day Parade and the lighting of the tree at Rockefeller Center. The Michelangelo was our choice of a nice affordable(ish) hotel on the new route of the parade down 7th Avenue. As we were staying for 11 nights it was important for us to be comfortable as well as ideally situated for touring Manhattan. The Michelangelo did not disappoint even before we arrived, thanks to the excellent service provided by James, the Concierge, and his colleagues. The hotel is clean, smart and comfortable. We had nothing to compare it with as far as NYC hotels go, but our room was very nice and a reasonable size compared with hotels in most major cities.
We decided not to pay $900+ per night for the privilege of facing the parade - a wise choice as we really enjoyed the atmosphere of the crowd outside.
For Thanksgiving Day Parade the hotel had an area cordoned off for guests, so we had a great view and didn't have to wait there from 6am! The location of the hotel was great and the complementary coffee and pastries in the morning were a perfect way to start our day.
We walked almost everywhere and on a couple of mornings took the complementary limo downtown to the Wall Street area.
The hotel has an excellent restaurant attached to it but it's not cheap, so the hotel staff can recommend loads of good restaurants all over the city. If you like New York Delis then two of the best are just a couple of blocks away - Carnegie's and The Stage Deli. We preferred The Stage for its atmosphere, the fantastic cheese cakes and the shorter queues! 
It would have been nice to have got a better deal for the length of time we stayed, but overall we can highly recommend it to travellers. If we go back to NYC we'll definitely stay at the Michelangelo again.

title: “Helped me sharpen my tongue”
text:
Staying at the Algonquin was a dream realized! I felt I was breathing literary history every second of my stay (I am a great fan of Dorothy Parker). Since this was my first stay at the Algonquin I cannot compare the facilities prior to the recent renovation, but my room was gorgeous. As a solo female traveler I felt very safe and the staff ensured I had a great time whether I was in the Blue Bar or the lobby. They were very obliging to take photos of me around the hotel and with Matilda.
Yes, the rooms are small, but don't you expect that? I stayed in room 1200 and would book again in a heartbeat for solo travel. I can't imagine two people being comfortable there. The view wasn't so great, but I could see the tip top of the Chrysler building which is my favorite NYC landmark. Comfortable bed and pillows and good lighting. There was a fantastic historical photo above the bed that was backlight. I probably had that on whenever I was in the room.
My only peeve is the motion sensor in the bathroom. There was no manual override for the switch, so when I was in the shower the light would switch off. The sensor did not pick up movement through the glass shower wall no matter how non-steamy they were. Also, using the bathroom in the middle of the night would trigger the motion sensor and a flood of light.
I highly recommend the Algonquin because of its history, warmth, and location. I enjoyed pretending to be a local and a literati.

title: “Plagued with noisy children, rooms with paper-thin walls.”
text:
It shouldn't be any surprise a "suites" type hotel will attract families. That said, it doesn't give them the right to let their bratty kids spin out of control as if they've gone through a case of Red Bull to the point of bouncing off the walls (which happen to be next to my room). If I wanted to hear all this banging and screaming, I'd fly out east to visit my nephews, not shell out $200+ a night while on "vacation".
Contacting the front desk didn't help much either. They said they'd send someone up (which they did) and it got quiet, until that person left, and then the noise started up again. The hotel manager did, however, offer to move us to a different room, but not until the next day, since it was Saturday and they were sold out.
The hotel offers free breakfast and a Mon-Thurs "happy hour", neither of which were all too appealing (free is free). There were, thankfully, many other choices within walking distances. On that note, we were also thankful for Mediterranean Inn being 3 blocks away. No screaming kids, better location and security. Sure, the rooms were smaller (same features for the most part), but who really) spends all their time in the room anyway?
And for all you parents out there, please show some respect to others and control your children (not only in hotels, but on airplanes as well).

title: “Great Stay”
text:
My daughter and I stayed here for the night and were very pleased with our stay. Our room was very clean, the bed and linens were comfy and breakfast was very good for a continental breakfast. We enjoyed the homemade waffles. Check-in/check-out was speedy and efficient. The front desk staff were very courteous and helpful. 
Our visit in Charlotte was for a concert at the Verizon Wireless Amphitheatre. The proximity of the hotel to the amphitheatre was not very convenient. I think we will pick the Concord Mills area for our stay if we return for another concert. 
The only real problem I had was the inability to connect to Wi-Fi. I called the front desk and was told that yes they did have free Wi-Fi, but no solution was offered when I relayed that I was unable to get an appropriate signal to connect. This was not a huge problem because we were in the room only a short ammount of time prior to going back out for the evening, but I would have been upset had I spend very much time in the room.
Overall our stay was very satisfactory and I would recommend it to others.

title: “Location location location.”
text: My husband and I stayed here while in NYC the end of September 2011. We absolutely loved it. Small but charming. Great service. Awesome location.

title: “Quite Nice time had - again!”
text:
Have stayed now at the Allegro Chicago twice now. The entire property is a mix of old world elegant and funky modern, it works! The staff was uniformly friendly and efficient from the front door, to check-in to room service. It seemed natural and genuine vs the forced smiles some establishments require of their staff.
The rooms are spotless and ok sized. If you upgrade they are quite a bit larger and not a ton more $$. The Wine Hour each evening is a nice touch in the lobby.
Encore bar on site, again service was great. Place was not exactly hopping either visit, but then again I am not quite the late night owl I used to be. Room service was amazingly quick!
Will be back soon!
Only two negatives of a small sort:
The bathroom is super small. You can turn on the shower and the sink faucet while sitting on the toilet with out stretching at all.
The closet is super small as well, to be expected with an older property. Neither issue was a big deal and for only one or two people for a night or two should not be a big issue.

title: “Classy and Relaxing Experience”
text:
My mother and I traveled to Denver for a long weekend as vacation. We didn't stay at the Brown Palace (though I would have loved to) but we did hit up the spa one morning to relax. 
I typically go to Elizabeth Arden back home and thought the prices were comparable, but the experience much more unique in that the Brown is older, more historic, and so more memorable. The relaxation room allows you to use the sauna -- all the products you would need are available after your services -- from hair products to curling irons to paper products. It was quiet and relaxing.
I had a facial done and my mother had her hair done. Both girls were incredibly friendly and clearly enjoyed their jobs, which is always refreshing.
I would encourage you to double check your booking time and service before going as we had some confusion with that initially...but the experience was a unique one and I was glad I took a girlfriend's recommendation to check it out.

title: “Not Bad, but some incompetent personnel”
text:
I like this hotel. It is very clean and convent to the area I needed to be in. The breakfast is good and the service is not bad. They did have an employee that was out of his mind. He called at 00:20 the last night I was staying here. He claimed to be the audit manager and said there was a problem with their computer system and wanted me to either go to the front desk to swipe my credit card again or give him the information over the phone. I told him that it could wait until I checked out in the morning and hung up. He called back about 10 minutes later and threatened to have me removed from the hotel. I told him to have the property manager call me and he then claimed to be the property manager. I went to the front desk and told the clerk to have this employee come out and see me. He then informed me that the employee was not located at that property. I was unable to sleep again that night.
When I reported the incident to the hotel manager the next morning they did credit me for that night and they were very good with the way they handled the situation.

title: “Pretty cool”
text: Hubby had a meeting in NYC so the kids and I went along for the ride. I'm not usually big on crowds, but it was time to introduce the kids to the city, and the view of times square from our room was breathtaking. The front desk people were friendly and helpful, as were the valet and bellmen. Our room was clean, huge, and very nice. The bathroom was big with tons of counter space. I don't especially like the energy of this hotel as it feels pretty frenetic. That said, it's in Times Square, and if you're staying in Times Square, you're probably looking for that energy. If you have kids, they'll love the elevators. We rode them for fun. The room was an oasis. I ate breakfast at the hotel twice. The first waiter was less than friendly, and less than attentive. He also charged me for a meal that should have been free. That, I learned from the waitress on the second day, who was lovely and attentive and took it upon herself to bring the matter to the attention of the manager. The manager, also friendly and helpful, took care of the overage. Everything here is super expensive (except the elevators!). It's tourist central in NYC. It's to be expected. If you're looking to be in the middle of the action, this is your place.

title: “pretty much as everyone says”
text:
stayed here for a trade show for 5 nights. As most have said it's a average downtown hotel, nothing really bad about it , just nothing really special about it either.
check in was smooth, friendly and effecient. We got a room on the 9th floor and had a spetacluar view of the roof.......and a bit of the skyline and hills surrounding the area......
room was typical , beds comfy, bathroom the usual.......on it goes.
I ate at the terrace for breakfast buffet..........it was decent for 18.00 bucks
We had dessert in the compass room, it was sort of fun rotating around with a rumble with a nice view of the city and surrounding area............hotel must've been built in the late 70's
If was very convenient for the trade show which was directly across the street and a short walk from our hotel to our booth.......
the area has decent restaurants within walking distance. The downtown is not to exciting accept for the ball park and arena..........
again nothing special, but not really bad either........
pool area is quite small

title: “Perfect location, small rooms, great service”
text: Right off Union Square 1 block from Bart's Powell Station. Great front desk service. Small, but nicely appointed rooms (w/bathrobes) Sink was an alcove in the bedroom, separate from the toilet and tub. No sink counter space -just a SMALL shelf. Ask for a room away from the nightclub on weekends. We bearly heard it from the 3rd fl.-didnt bother us. Small continental breakfast room for take away only. Considering the lack of hotel space on an extremely busy weekend, this was overall a great value. Im glad I booked early.

title: “Horrifying experience.”
text: I am traveling with my family relocating to L.A. and lost my credit card. I prepaid two nights on hot wire before losing card. The hotel would not check me in told me I needed a $250 deposit for the room forcing me and my wife and child to sleep in the car.

title: “Amazing location but a bit grubby and staff not that helpful”
text: Amazing location but a bit grubby and staff not that helpful. right in Times Square near Planet Hollywood, great for Broadway shows and everything is 10 to 20 minutes walk in this amazing city. Breakfast was really nice (Great coffee!) but the room was a bit grubby and dark even though it was pretty big! If you get a good price the location is worth it. More of a sleeper hotel than a amenities one.

title: “Great hotel for the price”
text: It's not central but not in the outskirts either. Perfect to visit National Cathedral or Embassy Row. We had no trouble getting around. the rooms are great value, comfortable and spacious. Service friendly and efficient. Parking is free!

title: “Restaurant staff let it down!”
text:
Just come back from a trip to New England, after travelling around for 2 weeks we thought we would give our children a treat by staying at the Hilton 
Logan airport before flying home, most of the hotel is okay but it lets it's self down in it's catering departments the staff at breakfast made it clear that as we were on a bed and breakfast deal we were only entitled to the buffet which was average at best and so the staff were inattentive we had to clear our dishes ourselves I think they were only interested in the business customers as they probably tip better! It's a shame as our children were really excited about it.
Also the coffee shop closes at lunch time so you could not get a hot drink unless you made it in your room.
On the possitive side the spa staff were great with the kids and the shuttle bus to the T was hassle free.

title: “Nice, but not great, hotel with great location”
text:
Stayed just one night as I was hoping hotels, but was impressed. This is a nice, bordering great, hotel. Check-in was smooth. Junior suite was sweeeet. It had a Mad Men retro feel that was deliberate and not a consequence of aging. The bed was comfy and the location fantastic. Was given a late check-out, which made siteseeing easier.
NB: Enter from 56th street, the 57th street enterance is through a bar/restaurant.

title: “Great location, great price, great staff!”
text: Our first trip to San Diego and did not know area. Could not have picked a better location. Across the hwy from Old Town, 2-3 block walk to transportation center that will take you everywhere and convenient to shopping (you need a car) and a drive up to LaJolla. Very good breakfast, clean and comfortable room and free parking and internet. The only drawback I could see would be that it's located on a main highway by the airport. Would highly recommend and will definitely return.

title: “Good rooms - but no food!”
text:
I stayed here for two nights recently with colleagues whilst on a business trip to Washington DC.
The hotel itself is in quite a good location and easy to find and if you want to explore the city it offers a free shuttle bus to certain locations every half an hour.
The room I had was comfortable and clean with everything you need for a short stay.
However, the hotel was let down by two things;
Firstly, the food. Or lack of it. We were there in January and the restaurant wasn't open! We were told it was because we were visiting during the winter months but, come on, if you aim to be a decent hotel surely you don't suspend your restaurant facilities whatever time of year. Not even any room service. There was the option to order in pizza's from an outside supplier and have them delivered to your room but this just wasn't good enough. Breakfast was served but this was a poorly stocked buffet consisting of juices, teas & coffees, boxes of cereals and some muffins & pastries. Very disappointing.
Secondly, car parking. The hotel has an ample underground car park but you pay for it and we weren't told we were paying for it until we checked out - an extra $25 per night! What made it even worse is that we were slapped with a warning ticket for not displaying our parking confirmation but nobody ever gave us this or suggested e needed it upon check-in. I really don't mind paying for parking but I want to be told about it upon checking-in.
A reasonable stay which was let-down by the parking fiasco and the lack of a restaurant.

title: “Pleasant From Check-In to Check-Out”
text: I've stayed at this hotel several times while in Chicago for ongoing programs. Each time, from parking valets and front desk to housekeeping and room service, service has been exemplary. Requests are handled immediately and with little fanfare. Service in the restaurant is expedient and yet not rushed. The rooms are clean, and vacation could mean just a wonderful night's sleep. Room temps can be managed and all at a reasonable price. We were within walking distance of great restaurants, Green Tavern Door and Melting Pot to name two. Navy Pier is a wonderful walk, and there's a Whole Foods Market just about 3 or 4 blocks away!

title: “Needs a little freshening, but a fantastic value & great service.”
text:
We visited DC for an extended Memorial Day weekend. The Topaz fit the bill for us in terms of location (a couple of blocks from the Dupont Circle metro), size (not too big and impersonal, but not creepy small, either), style (nothing generic here), and value (got a great "stay-two-nights-get-the-third-free" deal as one of their Kimpton InTouch members...very much worth it to sign up for that!).
Service was great. Our room wasn't ready when we arrived early afternoon, so they held our bags for us while we headed out for lunch. The folks at the front desk greeted us coming and going each time, and they made a special effort to do things like hit the "automatic door" button when they saw us coming, as my husband was on crutches with a broken leg. They host a nice wine reception each evening (sangria in the summer!) and have free coffee service (including iced coffee) each morning, great on those 90+ degree city days.
We had continental breakfast at the hotel one morning, and we would not do that again. The food, while not bad, wasn't anything special, and the restaurant is horribly dark. I want sunshine at breakfast time.
Our room was certainly spacious and, in general, above average quality. The decor was eclectic and funky, which we enjoyed, but things in the Topaz are definitely starting to show some wear. Nicked furniture, torn/replaced wallpaper, a few snags in the rug, and a strange bleached spot on the ottoman. Everything was very clean, though, and the bed was comfy. We enjoyed the view onto N Street and felt like we were right in the middle of everything.
The elevators are desparately slow and stuffy. I think the overnight valet charge was pretty stiff, but we did not have a car w/us, so don't know for sure.
Overall, we feel like we got a great value for our money. Clean, comfy, stylish (if worn), and great service, to boot. With a little freshening/polishing/paint, the Topaz would definitely be a place we'd stay again if in DC.

title: “Decent a bit more like an EconoLodge than Comfort Inn but Won't Stay Again”
text:
We travel for business and stay in hotels 5 months of the year, and so have a lot of points of comparison. This hotel was basically lean and well kept but an older property. If you were to just put me in the room and ask me to guess the brand, I would have said it was an Econolodge. That brand tends to be older, fewer frills and its quality can vary from quite good to very bad. (If this were an Econolodge I would have said it was a good one. As a Confort Inn I would rate it as a bit less than I expect.) 
The price was good and the check in staff was friendly and helpful. We had a rare day off and asked about a shuttle to Graceland, which they do offer-- Graceland is a couple of blocks away. The shuttle is the same price as parking at the attraction, so it is not much of a benefit. I do not know if they charge to take the shuttle to and from the airport as well.
I have one particular pet peeve that will keep me from visiting this hotel again. We have a routine when traveling. We often check in late and work late. In order for my partner to preserve his energy for our tour, I get up early and get breakfast for him and we eat in the room. I also dislike having all the noise of all the people around in the morning. Occasionally we run into a hotel where there is a sign that says "breakfast is to be eaten only in the breakfast room." Usually it is in an Econolodge, not a more upscale brand. In this hotel, as I was pouring coffee, a worker in the breakfast area noticed my tray and said "breakfast is not for your room." When I pay for a room that includes breakfast, I like to be able to eat it. So I make a note never to stay in these properties a second time. This may not be a problem for every traveler, but it is my pet peeve and we have a lot of options.

title: “No Frills Hotel”
text:
Upon arrival, having a truck to park in their parking spaces felt a little bit iffy. Their parking spaces are a tad on the smaller side, but we adapted by just parking in one of the designated parking spaces on the side of one bottom floor walls - not in an actual parking stall. Parking was free, albeit, limited. (& made us a bit scared to come back late and not have a spot). Checking in was a breeze, the front desk young male was very pleasant and cheerful. We walked to our room to find that the room door was already propped open & the heater was on full blast with the window open (other rooms around it were the same). They were cleaning the carpets to the rooms, which was a plus, but our carpet was still a bit damp when we arrived. 
The room was comfortable and had a fridge, a microwave, and a coffee maker. I was happy to see that the light in the bathroom was bright and not dim at first (like some other hotels I've stayed at). The hotel was in close proximity to a lot of things you could do, so that was a plus. Free wireless internet in the room - but our connection was really in and out so it was kind of hard to watch something on the laptop.
The cons of this hotel would probably be that it was designed more like a motel, so the hallways are not closed, they are open and you can hear the traffic and everybody who walks by, especially if they just came back from going out all day/night. The air conditioner/heater was particularly loud when it was bringing the temp. back up/down, but quiet when it was in-between those cycles. Also, the TV was a bit weird, it was a flat screen Samsung but it had lines that would run across it while you were watching - it reminded me of those old TVs. I already mentioned the parking spaces, so beware if you have a large car, if you can't get one of the more easily to back out of spots in the back. The parking area could probably maybe fit 20-30 cars at most.

title: “Not a 4 star hotel”
text: While this hotel is located close to the Magnifient Mile, Museums, and shopping, I don't think that it warrants 4 stars. The lobby is in badly needed renovation: as you look up at the huge atrium, the windows are cloudy, and need to be replaced, the water feature reeks of chlorine, and the furniture is stained and dirty. The rooms (we had a deluxe, with a view,) was very clean and comfortable, but the towels were thin and grey. We paid 35.00 extra per night for access to the Regency Club, for that we had a breakfast much like any express motel, fresh fruit thoughout the day, tea, coffee, soft drinks, bottled water, and wonderful cookies. While the rooms were clean and comfortable, the atmosphere of the hotel leaves a lot to be desired...Stetson's restaurant, on the other hand, was very upscale, and the food was and service was wonderful.

title: “Good location but really small room!”
text:
This hotel is in a very good location. Walking distance to most attractions. Cheaper parking at the Boston Common Garden underground parking.
Our first room was supposed to be with just 1 a FULL -not a Queen bed. I requested to be transferred the next day when they have at least 2 full beds in the room.
Will recommend if only of the location.

title: “Great Location, Huge Rooms”
text:
I stayed at the Affinia 50 on two seperate occassions during Dec 2004. 
Great location. The staff are extremely helpful and courteous. The first time I stayed I was given a studio room on the 3rd floor, which was clean, modern and nice however it was slightly noisy. Checked in again a couple of days later and was given a 1Bd Suite on the 9th floor. What a surprize this room was HUGE !!! 
Definately reccommend this hotel, but ask to be put on a high floor, the lower rooms are noisy.

title: “Location, Location, Location!”
text: My family and I stayed at the Soho Grand Hotel over President's Day Weekend. If you want Soho, steps from art galleries, great boutique shopping while staying at a very safe and very accommodating hotel that's very chic and cool? Stay at the Soho Grand. Your kids will love the goldfish and you will love the complimentary glass of champagne at check-in. Now that's how everyone should start a holiday weekend!

title: “Convenient, clean, comfortable hotel”
text: The Hilton New York is clean, comfortable, well-located and offers excellent service and amenties. Although it seems a bit old, the lobby and certain floors have been recently renovated. Our 30th floor room came complete with mini-bar and large flat-screen TV. Although we didn't have much time, we were able to use the check-in kiosk, the taxi service, baggage hold service, and visited the hotel bar. I'd highly recommend this hotel for tourists and business travelers alike.

title: “European without the smokers”
text: I've stayed here several times on business. The locaton can't be beat, the price is usually very reasonable. Look--if you want a big room, then get ready to spend big bucks, this is New York. With that said--the Mansifeld's rooms are small. Great for one, great for two--who travel well together. These are really rooms for sleeping and watching TV, if youw ant to lounge around the room--go to the HIlton or spend $600 a night. The service is generally good, the bar is a scene (which I'm not in to). Its a little rough aounrd the edges at times--but then again, for the neighborhood and the price, a bargain. REquest rooms that are not across from the elevator. IF you don't like the breakfast, go to Starbucks (two within one block) or the coffee shop at the corner. Rooms have all new HD flat screens, new window ACs for summer. Come, enjoy and for all you whiners...clearly you don't know what costs what in NYC.

title: “Romantic Birthday Getaway”
text:
We had the most amazing view of the lake. The hotel staff was very professional and even upgraded our room, for free, because it was my husbands birthday. 
The room was absolutely beautiful. The decor was very contemporary and fresh. 
We will definitely go back again when we return to Austin.
Thanks!

title: “Excellent service, charming personnel.”
text:
I chose the Hampton Inn based on comments from TripAdvisor. I even had reservations for another hotel, which I cancelled, and I am completely satisfied with my choice.
The rooms and lobbies are nice and recently decorated. The morning breakfast is very abundant and with different choices every morning. The breakfast and the 24/7 free coffee, chocolate and tea service in the lobby help you save some money that you can invest in treating yourself with one of the many shopping options NYC offers (if you are a lady, don't miss Sephora and Century 21).
In addition to checking me in three hours before the expected time, they provided a minifridge to the room one one hour after I requested it.
I would recommend this hotel to any friend and it will definitely be my choice for my next trip to NYC.

title: “Walking distance to mayor sights - Great location”
text: Crowne Plaza Washington, located at 14th / K street is just a short walk away from the White House, the Mall and the Capitol. Metro's just a block away and the bus to exciting Georgetown is in front of the door. As a Starbucks store is in the house and even provides room charge, the infrastructure could not be better. The hotel itself is located in a historic buildung. The lobby is restored nicely while the rooms are refurbished and comfortable. As upgraded due Platinum status in Priority Club we got a suite for an unbeatable rate, which was an outstanding value. The suite was modern and nicely furnished. Most of the staff were helpful and nice. The staff in the restaurant 14k, where we had complimentary breakfast was not as professional as extected. Large groups and plenty of guest led to slow service. That might be improved by the management. Parking is 34 $ for valet and the charges for internet are 12,95 $. In my eyes internet charges in the US are not state of the art and should be removed. All in all, nice stay

title: “Very nice experience”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights with wife and two children. I know this is a business hotel, but, figured it would be very quiet. Noise was non-existant. Very close to the freeway, north or south. Only about a 15-20 minute drive to the Zoo, Sea World and Legoland.
We've had two great experiences at Woodfin Suites (Emeryville & San Diego). The mini kitchen is convenient with two small children. Plenty of fast food/sit down dining or grocery stores, Von's and Ralph's, are about a 7 minute drive east on Mira Mesa Blvd. 
Staff was pleasant and helpful as we came in early off a red-eye flight and they made early accomodations for us.

title: “Cool Room”
text: Loved the platform bed and the shower in the bathroom. It was very small, but thats to be expected in NYC. I would stay here again. the only problem that I had with the hotel is that they did not have a microwave anywhere in the hotel. We had gone out and spent a ton eating, brought back our left overs, and had to throw them away. I find it strange that the rooms have refrigerators, but there are no microwaves. Not even a public usage one. :(

title: “Pros & Cons”
text:
My husband and I have stayed here for business and pleasure multiple times over the past several months. While I would go back again, I do agree with some of the other user's comments. The location of the hotel and size of the rooms are what keeps us coming back. You don't feel shoved into a small hotel room like so many any other places. We stayed at The Ritz in December and while the rooms & bathrooms were much nicer, the room was also much smaller. At any rate, YES, the Rittenhouse rooms & hallways are in desperate need of an overhaul. I'm sure the decor rocked in the late 80's a la Tony Montana (Scarface). However the bathroom's black ceilings & doors coupled w/ black and gold wallpaper doesn't exactly speak to 2008. Also, the beds are sooo dated. Even the Marriott has down comforters! I can't believe the Rittenhouse is still using shiny polyester bedspreads. Where could you even buy one today? I find their choice in decor very disappointing. I understand they want to maintain a traditional style, however that can be acheived in a much fresher, current way. 
On the positive side, I appreciated the daily complimentary newspaper(s) (We opted for NYTimes and the Phila Inq). Also, the afternoon champagne, cookies and strawberries are a welcome treat. We also enjoyed our breakfasts in Lacroix. It's such a pretty room. So as you can see, my biggest gripe is w/ the decor. We secured very reasonable rates during our last several stays and we did not have any issues w/ the staff or cleanliness. I love the Park views and staying in such a great location. BTW - if you want a casual meal in a neighborhoody place, try Smith's around the corner. We had a great, casual night there one evening. If you're not a design snob, you'll probably be very happy here.

title: “What more do you want from a Hotel !!”
text:
I had to write a review due to the fact that having read up before we stayed I was under no illusion that they had all the amenities available being a newly opened establishment, unlike others that seem to have not done their homework (see below!)
Location, spot on, could not have asked for a better place right in the heart of Theatre Land and 2 minute walk at a slow pace from Times Square.
Hotel staff were not over friendly which suited us but very polite and it appeared that everyone was still getting to know the place and each other so no real negatives there. I did ask where the ice machine was one evening and struggled with the receptionist over who was going to get the ice, personally I have no problem jumping in the lift and filling up a bucket of ice. Others may want for more but I managed to convince her it was no problem although she did say it was a hotel and that is what they done.
As stated by many no restaurant or bar on site although these are being finished at present. A wine hour is available to all and there are menus in the rooms from local establishments if you want room service but you are in New York FFS, who wants to sit in a hotel room and eat?
Due to the fact there was no bar we had to endure six different establishments for late night drinks. What a chore it was trawling round one of the liveliest cities I have ever been to and trying out a different bar every night, three of which were within less than a minutes walk away and highly recommended. Even when hotels have onsite bars, which most do these days, its much more fun to get out and about don’t you think?
The rooms are great, very new and modern and extremely comfortable. Showers are more than up to the job and fresh towels are plentiful, if you want your bed changed which we did half way through our stay this was also done without fuss.
Breakfast was perfect, yes they had paper plates and the seating arrangements are not the best but coupled with the superb coffee machine in the rooms to make a fresh brew no more is needed.
Did I mention the superb coffee machine, lovely coffee. We had a fridge in our room that we stocked with water, soft drinks and chocolate to satisfy the odd craving after a hard night out enjoying ourselves.
As a footnote, I stay in many hotels for business and would rate this as one of the best.

title: “Great hotel great location.”
text: Great hotel, great location. Nice wine happy hour.

title: “Great location, clean and comfortable”
text: A great little hotel situated right in the middle of everywhere you need to be! Very clean and comfortable and staff welcoming and friendly..........one word of caution is to avoid Sam's Grill restaurant which is just down the road - we were forced to leave an 18% tip by a very aggressive and demanding waiter - not a nice experience!

title: “NIce and simple. Good location”
text:
I read the reviews here and decided I'd give the Fitzgerald a try - despite some rather bad reviews there seemed to be some good ones too. When in SF on business I generally stay down on Geary or O'Farrell but all the places I generally stay were full. It turns out I'm glad they were as I enjoyed my stay at the Fitzgerald.
Location: It's close to Union Square and Market Street, but being up on Post Street is far enough away, by a block uphill, to avoid the real touristy traffic. It's also nice because you stand on the sidewalk on Post and not be bothered every few minutes by the panhandlers. The street also has kind of nice feel to it. Little restaurants, lots of young people, a couple hostels in the immediate vicinity.
Room: My room was great for just me. I booked one of the largest rooms available so it was big enough but I could tell that some of the rooms in the hotel are extremely small so keep that in mind. It was clean. Nice old heavy wood furniture. Comfortable bed. 
Staff: Staff was friendly, very pleasant and helpful.
Other guests: A mixed bag. Lots of younger folks, many from Europe. No big noisy partying or anything though. 
I really liked the little wine bar in the lobby. Very nice place, excellent selection of wines and little plates of food like cheese and charcuterie. 
So - it's not fancy but it's nice. Most of the rooms are tiny but for the price it's doable. Great location. Great for younger or budget travelers. It ain't the Ritz, but that's not what I was looking for. If you fell the same way you'll enjoy your stay here.

title: “Good, central hotel with friendly staff”
text:
I stayed in this hotel during a business trip, and enjoyed it. The staff was very friedly and helpful throughout; in particular the concierge, whose restaurant recommendations were spot on. The hotel is located within walking distance of the conference centre, which was the main reason I picked it, and which was very convenient indeed. The room was nice and had all amenities you would expect from a hotel like this.
