My room on teh 9th floor was extremely quiet, which was great; although I am not sure, whether it is because the hotel is well build/designed, or whether I was just lucky with my neighbours...
The only drawback was the charge of $12.95 per day for internet access in the room (there is free WiFi access in the lobby); however, it clearly says so on the hotel's webpage, so I was aware of this before booking it.

title: “Great location, rooms almost worth the price”
text: You can't argue with the location. The staff was very friendly and the service was very good. We needed more towels and they were there within minutes. The room was very clean as was the rest of the hotel. It seems like they are updating the rooms in such a was as to compete with the other "modern" hotels. The decor was very nice but the bothroom had no tub (didn't bother us but may have been a problem for someone else). The bothroom door was translucent and thus when you are trying to sleep, the light from the bathroom was very bright in the room. The door also did not have a lock on it (pocket door). The TV was about a 19" that was not a flat screen. We did not pay for the ocean view so our view was of the city. I am guessing the ocean view would have been great but that was our decision. We had breakfast there and it was pretty good. Kids eat free so that was nice but the prices for the adults made up for it. That being said, it was still nice not to pay for the kids. Lastly, the price was $139 for a Saturday night. We also had to pay $22 a day for parking. I know we were staying downtown but I think for this economy I could have found a better deal for this time of year.

title: “Had an early appointment in DC so decided to come the night before”
text: Friends had stayed there before and they said it was the best value for the area. The place is ok for a sleepover, but would not recommend it for any lengthy stay. Stuff broken in the room, dark narrow halls, small elevators. If I were a woman, I probably would not feel safe. The web site said there was a restaurant, but I did not see one. They also said it was newly renovated in 2009, but they must have missed my room. 1 block from the metro.

title: “Great Experience with Hyatt”
text: The room was spectacular, the staff always friendly, full service at everything. Exactly what you'd expect from a Hyatt Regency. My two nights were exceptional and without any problem. Location was superb for visiting Beverly Hills, West Hollywood, etc.

title: “Top Marks for Top of the Mark”
text: Superb Hotel on Knob Hill. Stunning view over the City and Bay especially from the 19th floor 'Top of the Mark'. Breakfast is a bit on the expensive side (maybe not for this class of Hotel)but worth it for the view. Bay views a little obsructed due to other tall buildings. If you plan to go to the Top of the Mark in the evening - go early as they fill up quickly and you have to wait for others to leave. Internet access no free and expensive!

title: “It's "okay" so long as you don't spend a lot of time in your (tiny) room”
text: Wife and I went to NYC for 4 days of shopping, eating, etc. W was the only "4 star" in the 300-400 range. Would have been very unhappy if I spent more. I read the reviews before arriving and was expecting a small room. But this was ridiculous - and we were "upgraded" from the "cozy" room (which I assume means the former broom closet), otherwise I don't think our bags would have fit. Staff was incredibly polite (a misguided effort to make up for the tiny rooms?), lobby is nice in that chic modernistic W Hotel way, but overall the place is really just a 3 star hotel that is coated with a thin veneer of hipness. Too big flat panel TV for the room, an incredibly noisy AC system that could not make up its mind, and an electronic minibar that kept charging us if we even just bumped the items on the shelf added up to a no return experience. I'm usually pretty easy going on hotels, but I seriously cannot recommend the W New York. Sorry, but it's not worth the coin, even at half the price I paid.

title: “Very pleased with our stay”
text: My sister and I stayed for a couple days 5/24, 5/25. We were a bit skeptical after reading some of the reviews. From the time we arrived to the time we left we could not figure out why some of the reviews were poor. The grounds are beautiful, the customer service was great. We were given free drinks (2) because our server forgot about us. No big deal, we were there during dinner just sitting outside the Balene enjoying the fire. We weren't there for dinner, only a cocktail. I call that good customer service, they made up for their mistake. We did not have kids with us but noticed how family oriented the place is. We thought it would be wonderful for families with children. There is so much to do. Bring your bikes and beach toys. In conclusion, it's a wonderful place. You get what you put out there. Go.... with the plan to have fun and you will. Oh, we called the front desk twice. Once to turn off the porch light (can't be done from inside) and another to fix the water faucet. Both times they arrived VERY QUICKLY, did the job then later called to make sure it was done and we were satisfied.

title: “Fantastic!! Fantastic!! Fantastic!!”
text: Not a lot to say other than this is a top of the line hotel. Everything you would expect in a 5 star resort. Great staff, great rooms, beautiful!

title: “Excellent hotel - but charged for wi-fi”
text:
Excellent location.
We had a family stay of 4 nights and really could not fault the hotel except that despite the room rate, they still charged for wi-fi. Given that hot-spots are available all over the place, would have thought that this would have been included.

title: “Awesome”
text: I can't possibly say enough great things about our stay at this hotel. Location was awesome - we had access to any part of Boston we wanted to see - most within walking and the rest with the "T" right nearby. Room was awesome - very spacious, comfortable bed and pillows, and very quite - never heard any neighbors. Service was awesome - smiles everywhere, offers of help were unending, and food recommendations were right on. If I ever visit Boston again, we wouldn't stay anywhere else!

title: “how to be dissatisfied in NY”
text: This is a hotel focused in their bars ,restaurants and not on their guests,is better come here for the roof top bar than be a guest ,at night a crowd arrive here and as a guest you dont have any privilege otherwise you gonna be check all the time by security guys if you are a gest or not .For me they have to decide if they want to be a hotel or a party place , or advise that they are a party hotel.

title: “Missing items not returned”
text: I stayed at this hotel a few weeks back for a week and unfortunately left by mistake in the shower some personal items, such as expensive shampoo and conditioner, ladies Gillette razor and some facial scrub. Approximate replacement value estimated at £40. I also left (intending to throw in the rubbish) a name tag and a plastic pen. Upon contacting the hotel the morning I checked out, they advised they had the later unwanted items but not the former. That week I wrote to them via their website explaining my dis-satisfaction and could they give me an explanation as to why cheap, clearly unwanted items were handed in and NOT clearly wanted relatively expensive items were not???? I don't normally write things like this, choosing to favour the benefit of the doubt, but three weeks later they have not even bothered to reply to my email, which is now just shocking customer service. So be warned, light fingered chamber maids and poor customer service and to top it all off, the TVs in the rooms do not have television guides so it's anyones guess as to what's showing on which channel at which time. When I enquired about this, they responded to me as if I had just landed from the moon! Unbelievable. Shame on you Hyatt. I stayed her as I had a great experience at the Hyatt in Bellevue six months earlier.

title: “Excellent place to stay”
text:
I booked this hotel in advance for my final night in San Francisco. I ended up staying prior to this as I was stranded in San Francisco unexpectedly due to a missed flight. The staff were brilliant, gave me a great room and offered really helpful advice.
The lobby was lovely, I spent a fair bit of time there as there was free wi-fi, a fireplace and free wine in the early evening. Could have not asked for more.
The location seemed absolutely fie - I felt perfectly safe and did not encounter any shady characters referred to in other reviews! Convenient to everything.
The staff really make this place. Wonderful. Will definitely stay here again and recommend it to anyone.

title: “Okay hotel, not great with kids”
text: We booked this hotel with Marriott destination points and basically only stayed here because it was free and the points expire if we don't use them. The room was nicely updated and was a typical Marriott room and did have a nice view. We usually stay at the Hyatt or in that area of the Riverwalk and I prefer that area to the location of this hotel as most of the restaurants with nice patios on the Riverwalk are much farther down. I don't mind walking, but with 4 kids in tow and in the July heat it is not as enjoyable. I noticed hookers were hanging out in the bar / lobby area one night when we returned to the hotel. This hotel gets a lot of business travelers and I'm sure this is why they are hanging around, but they need to crack down on this!

title: “Dark, small room and v noisy ac but close to Times Sq if that's what you need”
text:
My office books the best priced hotels close to the office so it is a bit of a lucky dip - previous trips have included the Hilton, Sofitel, Mercure, Morgans, Marriot, Milenium and Bryant Park. I should state that I am not a fan of midtown generally but it is where I work so convenience wins over vibe. 
Having stayed in Morgans' before I knew what to expect - cool (aka dark), tiny, and pricey food and drinks. What I wasn't expecting was the world's noisiest aircon unit - think old diesel bus engine on start-up and then settling to a steady 747 takeoff roar. Not relaxing.
Staff were mostly great (a big step-up from Morgans where I was simply too uncool to serve, or that is how it felt.....The breakfast team especially were great, really friendly and helpful.
Overall, if I could get a room marginally bigger, less dark and without the bellowing whitenoise from the ac then I would be ok to stay again but thus far the Bryant Park and Sofitel are still vying for #1 status.

title: “Great Location”
text: We stayed here in March and can honestly say it was a great choice. We couldn't have asked for a better location. It is right on the bay, directly opposite the cruise terminal and the maritime museum. It's within walking distance to Horton Plaza shopping mall. The old town trolley stops virtually opposite the hotel and the train station is just around the corner. The hotel has parking at a reduced rate for residents. The hotel compises several different buildings, all surrounded by nice gardens. We ate in the hotel's restaurant every day for breakfast and 2 evenings and the food was great and at a reasonable cost, children were well catered for. We can higly reccomend the Chris Steakhouse also (although a bit pricey). There is a small shop in the lobby selling the essentials and souveniers. The rooms were a good size and very clean. Our only complaint was that we had a noisy air conditioner, however when we reported it to reception they fixed it the same day which was good. Service at reception was friendly. Safes are available free of charge in reception. The hotel has a small outside pool. All in all good value for money but with a good level of quality.

title: “Great Place to stay”
text: My friends and I loved this hotel. It was in the perfect location, the staff were great, especially the guys at the door. They were friendly and very helpful. The beds were VERY comfortable. I would reccomend this hotel, and I would stay there again...

title: “Fabulous Except for the Staff”
text:
I stayed in the New Tower section, which I was told from others is newer and bigger. My room was very clean, large, and comfortable. The beds were among the most comfortable I have ever slept in at a hotel. The bathroom was large with a shower tub combo and two shower heads. I have allergies and the air was cleaner than most hotels which made for nicer mornings. 
If you book in the tower ask for a room on one of the higher floors. I stayed on the 8th floor, which had a view of other hotel rooms across the top of a rooftop. The higher floors had a fabulous view of the city.
The service was awful. The concierge dept. was the worst of any hotel where I have stayed. They don't answer their phones, so you need to go all the way down to the lobby to ask a question. They carry on personal phone conversations while you are waiting for them to acknowledge you. They provide incorrect information (outdated and incorrect phone numbers), and will not book reservations; when I asked them to, they said that I needed to go back up to my room and book them myself (which using the hotel phone costs at least $2/call to begin). 
When I asked if there was any live entertainment nearby on a Saturday night, they said; "not really, there is an Irish bar around the corner, but that's about it". This was my 9th trip to San Francisco and I could have named a dozen places to go, but I always ask for suggestions, to see there is someplace new, or that I haven't been. We ended up going across the street to the Starlight Room and danced to a live band and then for last call went right next door to the Golden Nugget where there is always an entertaining band playing 7 nights a week.
I tried to book an airport shuttle at night, for the next morning, and the person at the reception desk said that they couldn't do that at night and I would need to speak to the concierge in the morning, who of course didn't answer the phone when I tried calling down in the morning. The year before I stayed two doors down at the Villa Florence and the fabulous staff there, not only took my reservation for the next morning at 2 AM, but they allowed me to prepay and provided me with a reduced rate voucher.

title: “Cab drivers were not familiar with Hotel”
text: Nice NYC hotel with reasonable amenities. Staff was welcoming and courteous. Room comfortable although the small sink with strong water pressure led to much laughter in our room. Wi-Fi worked well. Great breakfast. Sole concern with the hotel is that the cab drivers did not recognize the hotel name and location. Through 4 different cab drivers, we found it necessary to repeat the name and address, and give them side streets to enable the drivers to find the hotel.

title: “Beautiful rooms, lobby and pool and very accomodating employees.”
text: We have been traveling across the country for 2 months and this hotel is by far the best we've seen. The employees are friendly and helpful. The restaurant is great and the amenities are plentiful.

title: “Great small hotel, location,staff!”
text: We stayed for 4 nights in April. Had a great experience. Only disappointment was the lack of lobby. There is no where to "hang out" with others in the hotel. The lobby is the smallest lobby I have ever seen, almost like a youth hostel. The rooms are very small, but clean, well appointed. Bathrooms are very small, but again, well appointed, full length mirror in the room, very small closet, desk. Location is incredible. Make it down to Eataly to eat, great food, neat experience. Nice park at the end of the street. Can walk to everywhere. Staff always smiling. Housekeeping staff was there immediately for anything you need, towels, pillows, etc. Would stay again.

title: “i love the location of this hotel”
text:
i was travelling with my son and we were here for five nights - feb 11th to 16th.
we have stayed here before several times so knew what to expect.
the rooms are clean and comfortable - no view worth mentioning, with small bathrooms.
the concierge staff are excellent - they always are and took care of our bookings to wrentham village and reconfirmed our flights back to england.
the breakfast buffet is fine - with a continental and full option - be aware that the price varies - it is sometimes $17.95 and sometimes $20 - depending on which menu they give you to order from!
you can upgrade to a business plan which includes breakfast for two, internet access etc we declined as we didn't have a laptop with us - now if they had inroom computers it would have been worth it!
we like it here - we like the fact that it so close to shopping.
if in boston again we will probably stay here - especially if we can get a good deal with priceline or hotwire - we paid $66 + taxes and were happy with that.

title: “oh my god!!!!!!!!”
text:
That the expression I used when I got to the room of the hotel!!!!!!!!!!!
Already the check in was not the best impression I got from the hotel: I called to day before the hotel to make sure that reservation and special requests were taken care but when I checked in they did not anything about it. I booked a room with king size and asked to put a rollaway. I was given a room with 2 twins and a rollaway on the way.....really????There were no space to put the rollaway and the room I got on the 17th floor was disgusting moldy and a/c filter was full of dust and God knows what else!!!!!!!I returned to Front desk and asked to be moved. They got me in a room with 2 full beds. The room was bigger but always moldy and falling apart...We had to stay in there as apparently they were sold out and there was no other option. And of course they made me pay for the extra person and for the luggage storage at check out.....
The location is the only positive thing the hotel has...just in front for the Madison Square Garden and the Penn Station...but really the price does not worth the "non-quality" of the hotel...

title: “This is THE place to stay in Memphis”
text: We arrived late and were tired from our long drive, but were immediately perked up by the friendly staff at the Residence Inn, Memphis. The front desk clerk was very kind to our kids and joked with them even though they started out a bit cranky (it WAS a long drive). The valet parking and service helping us with our bags to the room were quick, efficient and pleasant. The room is very clean and the location can't be beat. The next morning, one of the workers helped me carry plates of delicious breakfast as I herded the kids to a table. Such hospitality!!

title: “Centrally placed hotel in Washington for good value”
text: The hotel was best priced I could find and very centrally located for visiting Washington's business center, capitol hill and monuments. Metro to shopping centers is near. The little apartment had more scape than I could use.

title: “No sleep”
text: Newer hotel, friendly front desk person at check-in, free weekly happy hour and daily breakfast buffet. Good deal, right? I thought so until I tried to sleep. The hotel is pretty much directly next to train tracks that that are very active all night and trains must sound their horns at each intersection, of which there are about 3 surrounding the hotel. The hotel must receive many complaints on this because there are ear plugs (ear plugs!) and an informational card about the train in the room. Unfortunately, I can't sleep with earplugs in my ears, so my stay, while pleasant during the daylight hours, was miserable when I tried to actually sleep in the room. (Interesting that the card in the room stated that the train station was over 100 years old; the hotel must be no more than 7 years old. Either Staybridge doesn't do good market/area research prior to building hotels or they don't care about their guests.)

title: “San Francisco Quick Hit”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Marriott San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf for one day. I enjoyed the access the location provided; however, we mistakenly thought the hotel was a little closer than three (or so) blocks to the water. Despite this short-lived let down, we found the location centrally located with easy access to Ghirardelli Square and the Warf. We ended up with this hotel as a result of a Priceline bid; thus our room had a to-be-desired view. Expect this when using Priceline; we typically only use Priceline when we do not plan on spending much time in the room.
Marriott is somewhat inconsistent when it comes to customer service. Some Marriott facilities have the absolute best services…others truly treat you like another piece of profit coming through the door. Fortunately, the front desk associate that serves us was wonderfully helpful. In fact I called him from the room he responded promptly, friendly, and accurately. On the other hand…the bar tender…wow…maybe we asked him the wrong question at the wrong time.
Regardless, I would rate out stay as above average. I adore the Marriott beds and cleanliness. We would stay there again although I would most likely not strike up a conversation with the same bar tender :-).

title: “Great for quick trips out of DIA”
text: This hotel has simple rooms, but it is still comfortable for a one night's stay. For those early morning flights, I usually drive up there the night before, and I pay to leave my car there. The shuttle runs every 30 minutes. If you get back to the airport at an odd hour (such as 1 AM), you can call and they'll pick you up within 15 minutes. For the price, the convenience is great.

title: “Nice Airport Hotel”
text: Nice airport hotel. Front desk staff is (almost always) friendly & helpful. Tower rooms are great - spring for a corner king with huge wrap-around deck. Rooms are very comfy with nice amenities. HBO is free. Typical for Seattle Airport, they charge for parking if you have a car. Want a drink? You may want to bring your own -- service can be spotty in the lounge. Long waits appear to be the norm even when not that busy. Good sized outdoor pool & hot tub. Suites are very nice & have oversized showers & deep soaking tubs (no jetted tubs though). If you're HiltonHonors Gold internet is free; otherwise they charge except in the public lobby area.

title: “Hidden but awesome!”
text: We've stayed at this hotel a half dozen times or so when we go to Boston. We frequently travel to Boston to watch hockey games and ran across this place and fell in love. It's walking distance from the aquarium and Quincy market, with plenty of great places to get food in the area. Also on the weekend there's a public market just a few blocks away and also about a miles walk from the North End. All in all, especially for the price, you cannot beat this hotel. The parking is the only issue as you have to walk 2 blocks to get to the garage but it's well worth the walk.

title: “Quality hotel at a fair price.”
text: We enjoyed a clean and comfortable room. We were happy with our stay after flying in to the airport. As we were returning home we also stopped at the same hotel for the night before flying out the next morning.

title: “Boring”
text: Went there to celebrate our 36th wedding anniversary. There was absolutely nothing to do if you did not want to hang out at a pool or play golf. The balcony faced the balconies of other residents so there was no scenery - we drove to Sedona. Parallel parking on an incline was the highlight of the day. Not our cup of tea.

title: “Perfect for our gettaway”
text:
My wife and I had a wonderful experience at this hotel. We arrived at 10:45 and were immediately checked in. Our room was clean and comfortable. We spent the whole afternoon walking and shopping from Macy's to Times Square to Grand Central Station and back by way of Rockefeller Center. A short cab ride took us to the Van Gogh exhibit at the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Right around the corner was a great little catering business that served a first rate breakfast for very reasonable prices.
All in all, a perfect base for a quick trip around Midtown Manhattan!

title: “Good location, value and staff”
text: We stayed 5 nights at this hotel in one of the suites. It was in a good location in downtown Chicago within walking distance of most attractions. There were lots of restaurants and bars in the area around the hotel. The room was clean and well kept with free WiFi and a good buffet style breakfast included in the price of the room. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Although there was a fire hall across the street and sirens were very frequent ( all over Chicago I might add), the 4 of us were not bothered too much by them and the hotel offers free earplugs which helps for sleeping. Other than that we heard no noise from within the hotel from other rooms. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Night Hotel Review”
text:
My 2nd stay at this hotel at Thanksgiving weekend time, and good to see regular faces-simon (at the door) great welcome back, you were as helpful as ever...
Perfect location, great styling and good sized rooms for NYC
Very well maintained and welcoming and their service was fantastic, they could'nt help enough
I've recommended this hotel to friends whom have stayed and loved as much as me
Boutique, ambient, attractive and enticing everything i look for (interior designer/ and letting agent owner) so room sizes, ammenties, service, cost and style all catch my eye and they meet all expectations
Disappointing to read people moan re room service-really in a town full of amazing delis (cafe manhatten 1 block down for the most amazing breakfast) to dos caminos, bills burger bar & Buddakan i could go on-
The whole point of visiting NYC is to get out and about-if your not sure where to go then ask Simon or the desk they'll happly point you in the right direction
See you next year guys

title: “Best place to stay in New York!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel in April 2006 after lots of researching on the internet and we are soooo glad we did!!
Location;
A few minutes walk from Times Square, right in the middle of everywhere. Couldn't have been more central. Near a bus stop for the Grey-Line tours which meant everywhere was within walking distance or bus-ride distance.
Room;
Absolutely excellent! Massive room on the 27th floor. The biggest bed you have ever seen! Clean and comfortable with great views of the city. The toilet got blocked one night so we phoned reception and someone came up to fix it within minutes.
Food;
We never actually ate at the hotel. The food looked to expensive and too fancy for us. Food is so varied and cheap everywhere in New York that its better to eat out. There is a lovely little cafe just underneath the hotel where we ate breakfast every morning. Other than that we ate out in the city wherever we happened to be when we got hungry.
Staff;
Other than checking in and checking out we didn't have much contact with the staff, we didn't need to, but they always seemed friendly.
Price;
We booked directly on the Novotel website, which is the cheapest place we found it on the internet despite hours of searching. We booked a deluxe room for approx £470 for 4 nights. The room should have been about £1600 for those 4 nights but we got a "no change, no cancellation" deal which we were very happy with as we knew we'd definitely be going!
Interesting places to go / things to do;
Greyline tour bus
Horse and carriage around central park
Maceys
Bloomingdales
Disney store
Empire state building
Statue of liberty
Ground zero
Madame Tussauds
Next time I go to New York (there WILL be a next time!) I will definitely stay in the Novotel, no doubt about it!!

title: “Nice Stay”
text: Stayed at the Westin Grand for the 4th of July. The hotel is nice, although don't expect any kind of view! The beds are comfty and there's starbucks coffee in the room which is nice. Parking is $35 per day for valet service BUT you can choose self parking even though it does not state that on their website. Self parking is $28 per day, but there is also a lot behind the hotel on 23rd Street which is about half the cost, it's not covered, but it's a cheaper option. We stayed with our pup and had no issues. Check in went fine, but the agent at the check in desk was not particularly helpful and didn't leave a lasting impression of difference that the Westin is supposed to be known for. Overall, it was pretty cheap for DC, however I would choose another hotel a little closer to most sites as this one is a bit further.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: My friend and I stayed in the Nine Zero while visiting Boston and prior to a cruise. We selected the hotel because of its great location on the Freedom Trail and near Fanneul Hall, and that was really great. Even more so was the fantastic staff and great room. Everyone was helpful and extremely friendly. Tom, the concierge, helped us immensely and made us feel welcome. The wine event in the pre-dinner hour was very friendly and we met many people....they even set up a Weii game for us to play. Personal service in a great location and a wonderful room.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location, Comfortable room”
text:
I stayed at Westin Seattle from July 29th to July 31st. 
I checked in late. The airport is about 25 mins from Seattle airport. Check in was smooth. I requested a room with a view and they were accomodating. I got to stay in south tower on 27th floor. Room had a good view
I called in room service. Room service took about 25 mins to get the dinner.
Bed was comfortable. Room had a desk facing the window which was nice.
I saw many folks from cruise staying there
Hotel is nearby to Westlake shopping center and other attractions. You can walk to Pike Public market. Very nice place

title: “OK with some issues”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel a few times over the last few years and it has lots of positives: the staff is friendly and helpful, the property is convenient to many areas of DC including China Town, it's close to two Metro stops (McPherson Square and Metro Center), and is pretty reasonably priced for Washington. The hotel has free Internet access (at a lobby kiosk and in the rooms), a fitness center, and an on-site bar and restaurant. I did find the bar was a bit pricey, though. A glass of Robert Mondavi wine (not exactly premium stuff) was $9.
Rooms have safes big enough for laptops (a great feature), free internet access, the usual amenities including hair dryer and coffee maker, and a comfy bed.
There were a couple of glitches during my most recent stay. The wall unit air conditioner was fairly loud and, despite a sticker saying, "The controls for this unit are located on the wall", they weren't. They were underneath the panel on the unit with the sticker on it. 
A far more egregious issue was the water temperature. When I got to my room (#829) after dinner, the shower had plenty of piping hot water. However, at 7:30 the next morning, the water was barely lukewarm. Not ice-cold, but not exactly the pleasant experience I'd hoped for. When I told them about this at checkout, the desk personnel were very apologetic and promised to have maintenance look into it.
Given that enough hot water in the morning is pretty basic, I'd definitely talk to someone at the hotel and make 100% sure the water issue had been addressed before staying here again. Otherwise, it's a solid three to four on the T/A scale.

title: “Great business stay”
text:
I spent three days at this location and the worst thing was the occasional train passing. Aside from that this was a great experience.
The room was clean on arrival, and kept that way by housekeeping. My particular room was complete with a kitchenette, with stove top and small (not micro) refrigerator. 
I give this an excellent stay.

title: “So so...”
text:
We had three nights here as the end to our four week adventure, and it was a tad disappointing. We had a Bay Room - enough said really. While it was tired and old, I could cope with that. What I couldnt cope with was the fact it was an adjoining room - and there is absolutley no sound proofing between the rooms. 
Noise, light, movement - you name it, it comes from one room to another. That might be fine if you are using both rooms, but when you are not it's unbearable. After two nights we requested a change and we shifted to another Bay room, this time a non-adjoining one. I wished I had asked for a tower room, but I didn't have time to muck around. The new room was definitely quieter. I left two items of clothing behind in the first room and they weren't found by housekeeping (to my knowledge)...
I can highly recommend conceige services however. Joseph did wonderful things to help us with our tickets to Seaworld and Adrian did what he could to get us tickets to the football. That made for some happy kids in our group, so thank you again for your service.
The kids liked the waterslides in the pool but they shut at 6pm, which after a day at Seaworld is a little too early.
The Bagel place wasn't too bad for breakfast snacks - didn't try anywhere else.

title: “Seattle”
text: We enjoyed the location of this hotel. Right on the sound and easy walking to restaurants, the aquarium and shopping. Easy walk (take the public elevator outside the hotel, or else you will climb many stairs) to Pike Place. Nice room, restaurant/bar in hotel. The only draw back I saw was that the free WiFi was only in the lobby. You could connect in your room, but there was a charge. Odd, to me, in this day and age.

title: “Great location plus rooftop pool is a plus”
text:
I would definitely stay here again. This hotel has an outdoor pool on the fifth floor which makes it really nice to stay here during the summer. They have a server walking around offering drinks (about $7 for a mixed drink). Although I brought a thermos with my own iced tea and that was fine. Only problem I had with the hotel was the parking is $41 for only 24 hours. I parked for 26 hours and was charged $67. Make sure you read the fine print. Also, twice my bedroom key did not work, so I had to go down to the front desk and have it reactivated. Otherwise it was a pleasant stay. We arrived really early and they allowed us to swim for a few hours while they got our room ready, (we left our bags at the desk). Although check in is 3 pm they had our room ready at 1:30 pm. 
The hotel is in a great location, very close to Michigan Ave and many other sites. We went to a spa called Renew spa located on Michigan Ave, they had a great deal $99 for 1 hour massage, manicure, pedicure if you visit during the week.

title: “Great location, great hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Hyatt from 16th - 21st Dec 2010 and were extremely happy with the hotel. We'd stayed with a Hyatt before in Maui so having had a good experience last time, and seeing a competitive price, we went for it this time.
Upon arrival, we checked in instantaneously and were told that because we were staying for a while, they would upgrade us for free, from a Double to what I'm guessing was a Deluxe King - a huge bed, very spacious, sofa, desk, etc. And to top it off, right outside our window was the Chrysler building - couldn't have asked for better. As with the other Hyatt we stayed in, the room was nicely decorated, helpfully had some iPod speakers next to the bed and was generally very comfortable. And after a long day of sightseeing / shopping, it was just perfect to return to it. The only noise we heard, apart from the traffic which wasn't a problem, was a noisy neighbour. Down at reception, some renovation work was underway but disruption was kept to a minimum and it didn't distract from the attractive lobby, filled with Xmas trees. 
Location wise, you can't go too wrong with here. You have the Grand Central Station subway virtually below the hotel, that can take you anywhere you need and back again. On foot, you are 10-15 minutes south of the Rockefeller Center, 10-15 minutes north of the Empire State and 10-15 minutes east of Times Square. Fifth Avenue, Chrysler and Grand Central a lot less than that! 
We would most definitely stay here again next time we visit NYC!

title: “Amazing!”
text: My husband and my 9 and 11 year old children stayed here for a week to celebrate my birthday. WOW! Great views, comfy beds, nice kitchen, and reasonable price. I would HIGHLY recommend!!!

title: “Brilliant hotel brilliant location !!”
text: I had read negative reviews on this hoter so wasn't looking forward to it but after a long long flight we were met by helpfully staff !! And our room was ace a view of time square and all the hussel and sounds of new York and we could see the empire state building from it too loved this hotel will be staying there again !!!

title: “Frugal and fitting”
text: In town for a conference on my dime. Room was $68 ($78 with all taxes). No complaints, room was clean, fine, quiet. There's a shuttle to downtown, or buses if you're an accomplished PTU (public transit user). I walked in one day (2+miles), but got a little lost. You need to find the crossover bridge not far from hotel to get to the other side. Hotel is essentially in the parking lot of Mile High Stadium. No breakfast, small but usable pool. I recommend if money is a factor. Conference hotel was $200 a night before taxes.

title: “Step back to the glory days of hotels”
text: Beautiful, elegant hotel. If you want to feel pampered this is the place. Great breakfast. Lovely pools. Surprisingly reasonable summer prices.It really is stepping back into the glory days of hotels.

title: “I Love This Place”
text: I stay here every time I visit San Francisco and so far spent 3 New Years Eve's holidays there. I've been staying there for many years. Excellent location, great deal for the price, free parking - where are you going to find that in San Francisco ? Great dim sum place right next door and close to many other restaurants and North Beach adjacent, family owned for decades, friendly, helpful staff, clean rooms, recently renovated so the beds are firm and new. Of coursr you could stay at more expensive places, you can spend whatever the hell you want, man...it's San Francisco... but I never spend much time in my room when I visit San Francisco anyway and feel it's a rip off to spend cash for a room I'm not going to be in. . I mean if your not spending all day in your room and you're not an uptight snob, this is the place. Of course if money is no object...good for you... go and spend five hundred a night at a fancy joint...and can you send me a few bucks ?

title: “Exceeded my expectations!”
text: I was pleasantly surprised on our stay. This hotel is an excellent value for the price. Front desk staff were very friendly. The room was larger than average and had a refrigerator that I didn't expect but appreciated. I'm a light sleeper but the room was quiet and I slept very well. A request for extra pillows was attended to immediately. Parking is free and secure which is unheard of in a Chicago hotel. When we lived in Chicago 20 years ago this would have been a dicey area but it is gentrifying and I felt very safe. Public transit access is excellent and the interstate is easy to get to as well. I can't comment on the other facilities as we didn't use them - too busy!! All in all I was very pleased and would definitely stay here again.

title: “Average Hotel”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for a conference, which was being held in the same hotel. Thought I would be smart by staying here...
...wireless is awful. Had to call tech support to told me to do something completely opposite of the instructions received at the front desk. The wireless connection drops frequently. Then you can't get back onto the connection you were just connected to. I moved a nightstand to find and outlet and found a DSL wireless router bolted to the back of the nightstand. So, it's just DSL, but worse than DSL. While all this may not be important to the vacationer, for the busiess traveler it's is pretty much unacceptable.
Room was clean. Furniture, while basic, is new. Bed is very comfortable. Pillows are abundant and comfortable. Towels are thick and abundant. Front desk staff were very friendly and helpful. The conference rooms were comfortable with thickly padded chairs (a plus to those who attend a lot of conferences). The breakfast and lunch provided (paid for by the conference sponsor) was fresh and tasty, which you can't always say about hotel-catered food.
The bathroom only has two hooks on the back of the door to hang your towels on. The sink is one of those "sink on a table" setups, so there's no counterspace to put anything. Even being a simple guy with some bathroom basics, it was difficult getting ready in the morning.
The room service and restaurant are outrageous prices. e.g., $14 + 20% gratuity for a plain caesar salad. $10.38 for a smoothie. OUCH! Jamba Juice is just a few blaocks away - go there!
So, the wireless is my complaint. Got to have a connection!!!

title: “Don't waste your luxury dollars on this hotel”
text: My husband and I get very few chances to spend time alone away from our children. We scheduled a weekend in Dallas beginning June 26, 2009. First, our keys kept stop working. They had to be replaced twice. On Saturday, we arrived at our room at 4 pm to find that it had not been cleaned. We had no towels to get dressed for our evening event. I called and the cleaning woman arrived at 4:30. My husband and I left to get out of the way. Arriving back at the room at 5 PM we were shocked to find our sheets half way pulled off the bed, cleaning supplies laying in the room and of course, no towels. I called the front desk and again the woman came back saying that their laundry is very slow on weekends. I asked her to just fix the bed and leave towels so we can get dressed. She said she had no towels but left the room for about 2 minutes and returned with towels. I stepped in the shower to find that she had taken all of the soaps and shampoo and did not replace the items. When paying for a luxury hotel, you expect luxury service. This is not what happened on our trip. My husband and I deserved much better treatment than we received at the Joule in Dallas, Texas.

title: “Great Price, location and staff!! :)”
text:
You staff was amazing. We have stayed in San Antonio plenty of times and I think we have found the one hotel we will come back to. The price, location, and customer service was amazing. A special thanks to Eric at the front desk for the rate.
Thank you again for letting us check in really early (noon). It helped out tremendously.
Hope to see you all again really soon.
Sandra

title: “Nice stay, very convenient for travel without a car”
text:
We were just staying a couple of days before our cruise. This motel is very convenient to everything and very nice to return to. It felt very clean and comfortable. The in motel restaurant is good but every other kind of food is within walking distance, so you have a lot of choices. We used room service for breakfast and the food and service were very convenient. We walked to the Westlake Center and rode the rail back. We were lucky the entire vacation with the weather, so we really had a great time.
I left our jackets in the closet, called when we got to the ship and they had them for us when we returned.

title: “Great location, wonderful staff, very good breakfast”
text: I went with my daughter in law and my granddaughters grandmothers, aunt and great aunt for my granddaughters 16th birthday and we were very pleased with this hotel. The beds are extremely comfortable, the breakfast has something for everyone and the conciege was so helpful. This hotel is centrally located to everything and we mostly walked where we wanted to go. Would definately stay here again.

title: “Mixed feelings”
text:
That's our second stay at the Algonquin in three months. The first one we stayed in a classic room and this time we booked a suite. Classic rooms are small with tiny bathroom but well decorated. Suites are more spacious (and more expensive) with beautiful furnitures. There is a special atmosphere in this hotel thanks to its historical backgrounds, the bar is a lovely place with great services
 BUT yes the sound of the street is very annoying, we were wakened up at six in the morning by a big compressor.
 The staff at the desk is rude
So would I recommend a friend to stay in this hotel. Yes, in a suite and with a big warning about noises

title: “great location”
text:
great location 2 mins central park 5 mins times square yes the hotel is a bit worn here and there but found it very clean room was a decent size two double beds in two rooms with two bathrooms .hotel was busy and there was always a wait for lifts and reception staff but would stay there again as it was good value hotel 
used the hotels town cars to jfk home not much $ than a yellow cab but worth it

title: “Nice Airport Hotel”
text:
As an airport hotel this is great - not sure I would want an extended stay though
Rooms large and clean with great bathrooms
Bar area is well decorated and staff are great
Breakfast was very good (especially as it was included in our rate)
Definitely one of the better LAX hotels we have stayed in

title: “Great place to stay”
text: Clean large rooms.Happy hour -Free. Very nice breakfast -FREE. I dont know how they do it. Staff friendly. Great location for us. Wifi slow. But other than that it was just great. A very good value for the money.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text:
We spent one night in early Oct. prior to departure to Victoria. This is a stunning hotel - beautiful Asian-contemporary decor with flat screen TV and whirlpool bath that opens to bedroom area. Service was excellent - we had a luggage problem that staff was very helpful with, and we enjoyed sushi and drinks at Marazul.
We weren't thrilled with the location. It was a 10-15 minute walk downtown and although there is a lot of construction in the area, it was pretty deserted after dark. This looks like an area that will be full of hotels, condos, restaurants, and people in a few years, but it isn't there yet.

title: “Nice Room, Staff and Location”
text: Stayed at the Le Meridien for three nights. It was a very nice stay. The lobby is a 12 story atrium with an ok bar. Modern and nicely furnished rooms. Pleasant staff. Great location thats across the street from the Galleria, close to a few good restaurants and good shopping.

title: “Lost money”
text: I lost some money during my stay at this hotel even though I put my money in my luggage and the room was locked all the time when I was not there. I am upset about it. The condition of the hotel room and the food was good though. After this bad experience, I will never trust any hotel and will lock my luggage all the time even when you think it will be safe leaving it inside your room.

title: “Quick Overnight stay”
text: Booked a room last minute for a one night stay in Baltimore over Memorial Weekend. My overall impression was very good. The rooms are clean and well appointed. The staff was very pleasant and friendly. I feel like i cannot give too detailed a review since i did not get to take advantage of many amenities due to my short stay. The hotel location is pretty good, i would say 2nd best to the Little Italy/Fell's Point Entrance area which seems to cater to more foot traffic. There are less food options in the immediate vicinity but it is a short 5-8 min walk to the waterfront where the harbor tours are and the chain restaurants. However, take caution when walking, the area surrounding the hotel is a little rough and i would definitely not walk alone at night. All in all, I would try the Monaco again, for another stay.

title: “Awesome Concierge-Georgia Healy”
text:
Our concierge, Georgia Healy, went above and beyond to make my stay exceptional. I was unfamiliar with the area, so Georgia directed me to the architectural boat tour and the top of the Hancock building for my last night in the city. She also made a reservation for our group at Sunda, which held its value and got us in promptly at 830 (after a previous attempt on our own which failed miserably)!
Thank you Georgia, you made the W-- WorthWhile!

title: “Fab”
text:
This is my first review and I felt that it was appropriate to write about the most amazing time I had in NY.
Having spent three nights with family in Huntington on Long Island we were dropped off in the city at the Staybridge. Despite being dropped off 6 hrs before check in they went through the full process for us, took our bags into their storage and even offered us the breakfast even though we hadn't paid for that morning.
We returned to the hotel at 4:00pm and checked in. The room was excellent very spacious and clean, could honestly not find a fault. Everything we requested had been adhered to even the views!!
We used the reservations desk several times which was brilliant and nothing was ever a problem. Even the doormen were quick to help when ever they could
Breakfast was ok not my cup of tea but to be fair when you spend that much time eating its good to have a yoghurt, although I do have to say the scrambled egg was amazing :). On the Tuesday evening the held a drinks reception which I believe is actually on Tues/Wed and Thurs, this was excellent, pour your own pint, wine at the ready and some lovely nibbles, I am sure if we hadn't booked a table for dinner we would have filled up there.
Location was great for us; I absolutely could not fault this hotel and have recommended it to several members of my family who will be going over there, not to mention I will be staying again when I return.
Thanks to the Staybridge foe helping us have amazing holiday!!!

title: “BED BUG NIGHTMARE!!!”
text: After 2 nights of stay at hotel, right after checking out in the morning I noticed small red bumps on my face, arms and legs. After a couple of hours they exploded into swollen, itchy puss-filled bed bug bites. I immediately called the hotel and they admitted they had had problems with bed bugs. Manager was 'out of town', said I would be called first thing on Monday morning - was NEVER called back. I had to visit the EMERGENCY ROOM the next day because bed bug bites got infected - over $1,000 in medical bills, not to mention missed meetings, etc. I was not even refunded for the 2-night stay!! NEVER stay at HAWTHORN SUITES BY WYNDHAM COLUMBUS NORTH!!!!! They are irresponsible for renting out infested rooms and their lack of response to my nightmare was REPREHENSIBLE and SHAMEFUL!!!!

title: “Good Value”
text: We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights. The location is great - very central. The hotel is unique and we found it to be good value. I was a bit surprised at how small our room and bathroom were, but it wasn't a problem since we were hardly there. The front desk people were very helpful. We would probably stay there again.

title: “good for the price”
text: My husband and I stayed at The Pod for a one night getaway. The room was small as we expected, but the bathroom was a different story. We stayed in room 929, and there really is not a door to give you privacy in the bathroom. There is a loose sliding door that you can slide directly in front of the toilet or the stall shower, but it really does not conceal your "personal business". If you are looking for luxury, this is not the place, but it was clean and in a great location. We ate at Pescadore, a wonderful fish restaurant around the corner on second avenue. We paid $99 for the night at this hotel, and it was worth it for the location.

title: “Not recommended for kids”
text: The hotel itself was beautiful, but it is definitely not a place for kids. I had my two teenage sons with me, so they were ok with it, but they were not really all that excited for the place. Not much for them to do. The location was ideal. You walk out the door and see all the stars in the sidewalk. The staff was exceptional and treated everyone with equal respect. Even the valet parkers had class. They worked hard - running to get people their cars in a timely manner. I asked for help several times and the staff were always courteous and helpful. The rooms were on the smaller side, but it was nicely decorated in a contemporary theme. Clean. The only thing I really didn't like was the pool. It was small with not many chairs around it. There were cabanas, but they're pricey to rent. Starting at something like $200 and up to in the $1000s. Definitely not kid friendly. Keep in mind in the summer months, the weekends are reserved for adult only parties at the pool, so the kids are definitely not allowed in then. The restaurant attached to the pool was very cool looking and trendy, but again, after a certain time, there is a hefty cover charge and the kids are not allowed in. If I stayed there again, I would either go only with my husband or go with friends. Definitely not the kids.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: The shower was the best part. Water pressure was wonderful and it kept the correct temperature for an extra long shower. The room had a box air vent and the options were only high or low, no off. It was a little loud but it certainly prevented any hallway noise from coming in the room. Had an inside room so the view wasn't very good but I was only there one night for work so I wasn't very concerned.

title: “Tiny suite, lumpy pull-out sofa bed”
text:
When my adult son and I travel together we get suites. This one was the tiniest I have ever been in. I tried to get a 2-bedroom suite but was told none were available so we took a king 1-bedroom with a kitchen since we needed to be close to a conference. The moment I saw the layout I was not happy since you had to go through the bedroom to get to the bathroom - so I went down to the front desk and once again asked for a different room without success. 
The rooms were so tiny we had a difficult time trying to find a place to put our suitcases. It almost looked like they had taken a king sized room and put a wall up to make it into a suite. When my son went to make the sofa into the bed he discovered the most uncomfortable pull-out sofa bed, the springs poked through the thin mattress. I immediately called another hotel and got a reservation for the rest of our stay. Then I called the front desk and explained our situation, saying we were leaving the next day. Since Hamptons have 100% satisfaction guarantee and they were well aware from the moment I had checked in that I was unhappy they gave me the room for free after a little prompting. 
On the upside the actual bedroom was comfortable, and very quiet. The breakfast was well stocked and a little better than most. Lots of nearby restaurants.

title: “Great Location, Great New York Experience”
text: I've had the pleasure of staying at the Gansevoort several times for business. The service is friendly and helpful. The rooms, while they can be small, are well equipped. If you're able to get an upgrade (or pay for a bigger/better room) you could be treated to beautiful views of the Hudson. The location is great, just steps away from Pastis, Chelsea Market and the Highline. I have not recently taken advantage of the nightlife, but the hotel's top-floor lounge also has sweeping views. The room service is good and prompt as well.

title: “Will be back again!”
text: I am much more in agreement with the three most recent reviews! As a traveler on a budget, I was shocked at the rates I was quoted in NYC for four nights over Easter weekend! I wanted to be in walking distance of the theater district. Finally, out of frustration, I tried Priceline.com and landed the Hudson for only $110 per night!! At this rate who cares about small rooms! The hotel's public areas and staff were supurb. My advise is if you can't get a room here for under $200, then look elsewhere!!

title: “Hotel Bliss!!!”
text:
This place is wonderful - such an amazing and beautiful property from lobby to rooms, to the impeccable service. 
I have stayed here twice and have received nice upgrades as an SPG-Gold member. 
Everything about this place is 5-Star - service, decor, cleanliness, and cost...lol ... yep, it is not cheap - but it's worth it for a splurge weekend! Just go!

title: “Great Find”
text:
I stayed at the Hampton Inn Times Square South from 10/1/09-10/4/09 and I had a very enjoyable stay. The area is not "bad" as other posters have stated. It's a city street no different than many other city streets. If you've never been on a street in a city such as New York it might seem daunting. But it's as safe as you make it safe. Be aware of your surroundings and know where you're going. People who look clueless or lost are targets. So even if you don't know where you're going - fake it. Attitude is everything. Remember, any place can be "dangerous" from the cleanest suburban neighborhood to the dirtiest city street. The hotel is situated between 8th and 9th Avenues (though is closer to 9th) and both avenues are fairly busy. 
You're only a few blocks from the theatre district which made the hotel perfect for me. While in town I took in a production of "Bye Bye Birdie" at the Henry Miller Theatre (on 43rd Street between Broadway & 6th Avenue). A very quick walk from my hotel. The staff was helpful and courteous and I have no complaints about them. Whenever I stay in a hotel I put the "do not disturb" sign on my door to keep out the hotel staff. I don't need my bed made every day and don't accumulate much trash during a short stay. While the Hilton Family of hotels is quite reputable I'm not sure the temptation to go through someone's belongings or swipe something would never occur to one of their employees. Temptation is always around. Especially when there's a laptop and an ipod in the room. So, I just have them stay out of my room. They can clean it once I'm gone.
I highly recommend this hotel. Only six blocks up from Penn Station and a few blocks down from the theatre district. Not many taxis come down 39th Street but one can be easily hailed at either 8th or 9th Avenues (though if you're going uptown it's better to hail one on 8th). If you're uncomfortable with the thought of hailing a cab just ask the front desk for help. I never had to do this but I don't see why it would be a problem. The only time I used a cab was when I went to the Lincoln Center (in the 60's). I walked everywhere else. Walking can be a real treat because you never know who you'll see. During my stay I saw four Broadway actors just walking down the street - one of whom was Dustin Hoffman.

title: “It was the perfect place to end long holiday trip, fab time!”
text: After reading the Trip Advisor reviews, I decided to book the hotel based on the roominess, value and service people consistently commented on. We were visiting family in the area and my in-laws said to stay here too as they eat here once a week and love the place. My husband and two kids shared a room and were not disappointed at all - the rooms are spacious, a huge plus for us! The crew was amazing and gracious. This is our new favorite local place to stay next time we visit our inlaws. Thank you for a pleasent stay.

title: “Feared for our safety!”
text: The hotel itself was okay (and I really mean just okay)...not at all what you would expect from a name like Marriott. The room was in need of updating. But we could have lived with that. What we could not live with was the "elements" in the hotel. When we first arrived, my husband told my teenage son and me not to go outside to walk the dog or for any other reason because the appearance and the conversation of the people hanging out in the parking lot made him feel uncomfortable. In fact, he would remove his jewelry whenever he had to go out. No big deal...we were there only for one night and would simply stay inside. But at about 5:00 in the morning we were awakened to the sound of two men in the room next to ours arguing and fighting each other. (The walls in the hotel room were extremely thin!) The arguing was so intense that I literally got down on the floor for fear that bullets might start flying next door. And that was before they actually starting physically fighting! After about 45 minutes of listening to this and fearing for our family's safety, my husband and I just collected our kids and checked out. My husband had barely slept and he had a 4 hour drive ahead of him, but we sim ply could not stay there another minute. Before we left, my husband called the front desk to report the fighting next door, no manager was available and the front desk clerk did not seem inclined to do anything about the problem. When we checked out early my husband told the desk clerk our reason for doing so. The clerk said that the manager would contact us, but no one ever did. I would never ever ever stay at this hotel again.

title: “Boston weekend”
text: great location, very clean room and bathroom, very friendly staff, hotel doesnt have much to offer inside of it, no real extras, but since spent most of time outside didnt need them, run by ywca, helps support y progams, so profit goes to a good cause

title: “Very good location and decor but too mcuh contruction noise.”
text:
We stayed at this hotel during our July 4th long weekend trip and it was great.The location is perfect , very close to the mall area and right across the US capitol.
But there is too much construction going on in the vicinty, though i should admit the inside of the hotel was very nice.
The hotel staff is very friendly and accomodating.

title: “Huge Nice Room....Low Price!”
text: Staff was very welcoming. The rooms were nice and comfortable which included a fire place and full size kitchen. A free hot breakfast every morning, which is something you do not find at other hotels. It is a little hard to find at night, but I would recommend this to anyone wanting a hotel near the airport.

title: “Excellent choice for a special anniversary!”
text: We spent our wedding night at the Sorrento 25 years ago and decided to go back for our silver anniversary. So glad we did! We were upgraded to a large, lovely suite with a super comfortable bed and windows looking out at the city. The room was deluxe but the service at the hotel was even better. We were greeted as if we are valued guests and treated wonderfully throughout our stay. The staff even left an anniversary greeting in our room! I don't know that this hotel would meet the needs of every traveler, but for a local couple looking for a special way to celebrate, the Sorrento was just perfect. We don't plan to wait another 25 years to return.

title: “You could not ask for a nicer staff!”
text: We love staying at the Hotel Angeleno because of its proximity to UCLA, free parking, first rate restaurant with a spectacular view, but most importantly for the outstanding staff. They bend over backwards to accommodate your every need. No one could make you feel more welcome than Joseph at the front desk! We will continue to come back every time we are in LA!

title: “Exceptional Hotel!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for three nights after having finished a cruise in Quebec and driven down through Vermont and New Hampshire for ten days, having stayed in several country inns.
What a wonderful hotel! Great location in the Back Bay area of Boston. Right on the corner of Boylston and Exeter, very close to the subway and within walking distance of downtown. Very close to Newbury Street with lots of shopping and restaurants. One block from the Prudential Center.
Our room (819) was spacious, impeccably clean with large bathroom and a walk-in cloakroom with safe and a large flatscreen TV which was welcome in the evenings to see the latest financial and election news!!
The check-in and concierge staff could not have been more helpful as was the rest of the service. Every evening a maid came round with an optional turn-down service, complimentary water and cookies.
The hotel also has complimentary internet facilities and Wi-fi and a state of the art gymnasium for those with the energy to spare.
We didn’t use the hotel restaurant but we did use the adjoining Irish Pub which belongs to the hotel. Great food and atmosphere at very reasonable prices. 
We did eat one evening at the Atlantic Fish Co. opposite the hotel which was very good and well worth it for the experience but it was fairly pricey.
All-in-all, a really nice finish to our month-long stay in the USA. 
Will most definitely book again, well worth the money

title: “Great place to stay, just seal all open food”
text: From the time we arrived until we left, the service was great. We did not want to drive downtown,it was great that SEPTA transportation was right outside. I love the idea, there were always fresh coffee and newspaper available daily. They also provided a microwave oven for our leftovers. My only downfall I noticed, that several ants were on the counter near the bathroom.

title: “Not worth the price”
text: This was an expensive hotel compared to others in the area, therefore I assumed it would be nice. The carpet needs replaced, the bathrooms are small, the ac/heating unit did not work properly, the cleaning staff did a poor job. I would not go back.

title: “Awful gym - nasty pools - needs another facelift - nice bartender”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for a week while attending a conference downtown.
While the hotel was clean you could tell that they were on a budget when they remodeled the place. The bathroom's had old bathtubs and the new paint didn't come all the way down to the floors. On the website it clearly states that all rooms have upgraded beds, but mine was old, dingy and not very comfortable (I should have asked to switch when I checked in.) Speaking of checking in, when I was checking in (after waiting for the one guy on duty to get off the phone for a good three minutes - which is a lot if you are the only one in the lobby with the only employee in the place - the guy on the phone was offered a lower rate than I was paying - can't you do this from the back office?) I was given little info and sent to my room. If I was paying for this I would have renegotiated or even walked away.
I also selected this place due to it's gym (which is an absolute joke - if you are looking for a small room with three antiquated machines that don't even work, this is your place) and the pools are dirty and not very inviting.
The only great thing about this hotel is that it's close to the tram (a four minute walk and then a 20 minute ride to downtown) and the bartender. The free breakfast also isn't that bad (although I did just stick with the fruit and toast.)
Suggestions for management: upgrade the gym so someone can actually work out there or be truthful on your website about the gym, pool, check-in folks and state of the rooms.
While walking to the tram I did see the Extended Stay Deluxe Midtown which looked brand new from the outside, so you may want to check out that place (but again I haven't been or stayed there).

title: “An Experience...”
text:
While I was very concerned after reading previous reviews by people who purchased their room through a third party, such as Priceline, our room was perfect. Matter of fact, after staying there one night my husband and I decided to extend our stay and pay full price for the same room. Sure, it was smaller than modern hotel rooms, but it's far from the size some people seemed to describe. It had very high ceilings and I believe it didn't feel small at all really, even though it was by no means "large" by contemporary standards.
The bed was very comfortable, the bathroom quaint and very functional, and internet access and cable were first rate. I honestly can't think of one thing I didn't like. Actually, besides The Shelbourne, in Dublin, Ireland I believe this is one of my absolute favorite hotels. Perhaps it's the grand and historic atmosphere? Although, the delicious room service menu probably didn't hurt either. My husband and I ordered the Boston Cream Pie, which originated at this hotel, three times! 
As far as the staff are concerned, I haven't been more impressed. I'm sure there could be exceptions, and it could be that I was just lucky, but the people I spoke with were very polite, warm and understanding. At one point my husband and I locked ourselves out of our room and I had to go to the front desk to get a new key. The man I addressed was reassuring and even managed to make me laugh at the rather annoying situation we were in. Our servers were extremely well mannered, and the concierge was pleasant and efficient. 
I would easily stay at this hotel again and would recommend it to others. Omni Parker House is not for people who are accustomed to the large, and in my opinion often generic and cold, hotel rooms of most modern establishments. However, if you appreciate old world charm, cozy luxury and elegance this hotel will delight you.

title: “Just ok”
text:
Hotel is very historic and depending on which room you get--might be very small and cramped, cracked paint, dingy bathtub and poor lighting. For the rate that I paid, I expect a lot better. Waited 30 min. for front desk to move me to another room. I have to say the next room was a lot nicer. Twice as big, bigger window, larger bathroom-very nice. Staff is friendly enough. 
Was in the city for a convention and the location of the hotel is excellent. Plenty of bars and restaurants to walk to so there was no need to rent a car. All in all, not a bad stay.

title: “Don't do it!”
text: Booked a twin-bedded room - very specific as it was for my son and I. Politely told one was not available but they would upgrade us to a deluxe room and WE would have to pay an additional fee for a roll-up bed. Not happy, so asked for the Manager, who could only be described as obnoxious. Room was NOT upgraded and was small and dingy. No roll-up bed was provided although I literally pestered them for hours for one (although when we checked out they tried to charge us 50 odd dollars for it!). Lock on the door didn't work and the safety chain was literally falling off the door. The fact that anyone could walk in to our room and help themselves, together with the noise from the bar area meant two sleepless nights and the spoiling of our stay in New York. I wouldn't give it a single star!

title: “Had a room next to the staff room....”
text:
Which meant we were woken up by very loud television watching at 230am, it's one thing to be woken up by guests but for it to be the staff themselves is something else. We got moved the next day which was a pain but at least we could sleep.
The rooms are average, pay a bit more and go somewhere else.

title: “Our favorite place to stay in San Diego”
text:
We just completed our 5th stay at this property over the Thanksgiving Holiday. We are never disappointed. I can't say enough good things about this hotel but I'll share a few: CLEAN and 
updated, great FULL breakfasts (eggs, potatoes, bacon, sausage, pancakes or waffles, and fresh fruit, juice and coffee); convenient restaurant (great menu and quality food too) on site for those evenings you just want to stay in; unlike Hotel Circle, this area provides miles of walking trails along the Bay in Shelter Island Park; great location within the City, close to downtown and other attractions; coastal location with great views of the City or the Marina; great value for the $$; and we love the staff many of whom have been with them for several years. Our daughter and her 8 month old baby joined us on this last trip and it worked out perfectly. The room was large enough for 3 adults and the accessories a baby requires.

title: “Blew Me Away”
text:
Best hotel I've ever stayed at:
Staff was over-the-top helpful from reservation to car service to check out. The bed was the best bed I've ever slept in. The ambiance from the courtyard to the lobby to my room, made a boring business trip something to smile about. (Really - I literally did smile!) I'll never stay at another hotel in Seattle.

title: “Great Hotel and Staff”
text: Even though the hotel could use a "update", the rooms, service staff and location are unbeatable. It is highly recommended when compared to other dozens of hotels in Chicago.

title: “Great location...some problems with housekeeping.”
text: We stayed here June 17-21. Check-in was great and easy with wonderful cookies!! We had no shampoo in our room upon check-in and the maid outside did not have any in her cart either and asked me to phone the front desk. We also did not have towels replaced when we asked. Our shower drain was broken and we had to rig it when we wanted to shower, not bathe. There was no vent in the bathroom and no hair dryer. Older T.V's too. Also, no safe in the room. The room and overall look of the hotel is great, very modern. Bathroom is very roomy. Concierge was very helpful, as were the porters. We got a great deal on the room, and in all honesty that's all we use it for on vacation, a bed to sleep in! Which was VERY comfy! Plus, the alarm was one I could actually figure out how to set. We were on the 8th floor and had no noise from the hall. If you don't expect street noise, go on vacation in the country-side. The pool was awesome, very clean and tended to.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
Got this hotel via a Priceline bid. Absolutely wonderful hotel. Got upgraded to an Exexutive Suite which obviously helped, but everything made the stay perfect. Check-in staff at Reception, the concierge, the valet guys out front, the housekeeping staff - they were all wonderful - always ready to help and never looking for a tip. Rooms were really well appointed and looked worthy of the star class rating the hotel has.
People keep refering to the homeless shelter and the fire station nearby, but really, to me - that is being really picky. Yes, one did hear sirens, but you could just as easily avoid the homeless shelter area if it really bothers you. Parking is expensive, but keep in mind that parking is free on the streets over the weekend, and that is exactly what I did - it's $38 a night at the hotel!!
Some might say that it may not be safe to park on the streets at night, but it isn't like that at all. I was there over the Memorial Day weekend, and parked on the street 3 nights - no problem finding a spot, and atleast I felt absolutely safe where I parked.
I'm not one for eating-in via room service or even in the hotel, so I couldn't really comment on the food, but the first night we got in really late, and got some food in from room service, and it really was quite good - admittedly only soups and pasta, but good nevertheless.
All in all it was a great experience, and if you really pushed me for a negative, I'd come up with the pool. The access to the pool/fitness area was free over memorial day weekend, but they always seemed in a hurry to get people out by closing time - almost overanxious. Strange considering that on 2 of the 3 nights I later saw from my room window people in the pool again!!
BUT bottom line - great hotel, wonderful rooms, polite staff, and a good deal.

title: “Decent Hotel for the price...not four stars though.”
text: I was in town for a football game and some sightseeing with my husband and son. We needed a last minute reservation and the Sheraton was available at a much better value than other 3+ star hotels we had looked into. It was in a good location, only a few blocks from the Wharf with lots of restaurants and shops you can easily walk to. Public transportation was also nearby, so this hotel was a perfect location for our 5 day trip. From the outside of the hotel, it doesn't look like anything special, but once inside, the lobby was clean and modern and the check-in staff and concierge were friendly and helpful. The room itself was old (popcorn ceiling) and on the smaller side, but we made do. The beds were comfortable and that is what matters. The bathroom was small, but I've had smaller. The only complaint I really had was that the sink was separate from the shower area, so if someone got up in the middle of the night and turned the bathroom light on, it woke everyone up. There was barely any room to change in the doored area of the shower, so you felt like you had no privacy in the sink area. They really need to put another door there. If noise is a concern for you, ask for a courtyard facing room. All in all, it was a decent hotel and I would stay here again for the price.

title: “Simply the best”
text: I made the reservation and requested any upgrade they could offer. We were settled into a mini suite with a partial park view. The staff was warm, accomodating and incredibly pleasant. Not one instance of New York snobbery. A delightful experience.

title: “Very Nice Room, dificult to locate if driving alone.”
text: Despite the remote location my wife and I thought this hotel was very nice. Specifically the room was excellent and the bed quite comfortable. The door key did not work and it took 15 minutes to get that resolved. I find it hard to believe that the staff did not know about this key pass malfunction for this specific room. Other than that it was pleasant stay. The cab- which was small with no AC and the fare to the ballpark was $25 each way and given the $50 extra it might have been nice to stay in a Philly proper hotel and not have to worry about getting a cab. However it was convenient to the airport notwithstanding it's very confusing locale especially when the visitor is alone or travelling at night in a rental car. Staff at the desk was very friendly...

title: “Clean Elegant Friendly Place in center of Manhattan”
text: First, I am very particular with choosing a place to stay, and read most reviews about any hotel in whichever manner possible [i.e ratings from least to most rated, from most recent to oldest, etc]. My experience of Sofitel started right here on Tripadvisor, and it was great. Our room was clean, classy, marvelous marble bathroom, and with dawn bed. Service was very good, staff very helpful. Location excellent. Clientelle mostly european. Only issue was Parking, which the staff told us would give discount, which turned out to be false, but not a major issue as Parking in this part of city is very expensive regardless. Never ate at their restaurant since the breakfast prices were very expensive, and you can get the same thing for much lower few doors down in a nice diner.

title: “10/10 would do again”
text:
Got a great price on a room since they are renovating the lobby. The renovations were no bother whatsoever - I only noticed the work in progress because of the scaffolding outside and the masking plastic in the employee stairwell.
The room was fashionably lovely, clean, quiet, and I couldn't have asked for a better location. Employees were friendly and helpful.
This hotel is a great way to introduce yourself to the joys of a NYC vacation, as the location also lets you stumble upon neat unexpected lesser-known things such as the flea market, the farmers' market and the boat basin cafe, while also being within decent walking distance of Central Park, the Museum of Natural History and a palette of culinary options.

title: “Would stay here agian!”
text:
My husband & I stayed here for one night while we were in town to see a concert. We prefer to stay at small hotels rather than the big chains so I was quite happy to find this place. The staff were nice and they let us check in early. The room was a little small but comfortable enough. The continental breakfast was similar to any other place. 
I would definitely stay here again, nice neighborhood and within walking distance to many many attractions.

title: “Outstanding service”
