text: My husband and I spent a long weekend in D.C. I had read mixed reviews on this hotel, but the customer service and rooms were outstanding! The staff went out of their way to make our stay perfect! I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Great Downtown Denver hotel”
text:
Great smaller downtown Denver hotel.
Very professional and friendly staff. The extra amenities - full breakfast, cookies and milk at night - are a nice touch. Great suite with fireplace, comfortable furniture. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great family time”
text: We have frequented this location for the second time and we have decided that we will return. This resort is a great place for families with every age child. We thoroughly enjoyed the Oasis waterpark and the grounds. The room is great and hosts one of the most comfortable beds I've slept in in a while. The golf course offers a very serene atmosphere and views. The Oasis was great, with water slides, lazy river, wave pool, and kiddie pool. There are plenty of lounge chairs, swim-up movies and a great wait staff. Trees surround the lazy river, for those who want to find some shade and the resort offers plenty of age appropriate events, during the holidays, for the kids. There was dancing, hula hoop contests, and arts and crafts. Kids are certainly entertained here. Overall, it was a great trip for our family and we look forward to our next trip there.

title: “Perfect For everyone”
text: From the lobby to the rooms, this is a great place to call home in San Diego. The food is excellent, the rooms are clean and the bed is comfortable.

title: “We loved this hotel - but it isn't for everyone”
text:
Before you book this hotel, check out their website. In doing so, you will know there is no free parking, that there is internet for a fee, no free breakfast, expensive mini bar items, no amenities for children, and it overlooks Beale St.
My impression, before booking, was Westin Beale Street caters to a high-end business person and I believe after staying there that that is their target customer. My family is a middle class, blue collar family, so we stuck out like a sore thumb a bit, but were treated just as well as the other guests. Most of the guests are middle aged and well dressed and can more than likely afford the perks of a place like the Westin.
The room was comfortable. We had a double queen room that overlooked Beale St. The bedding appeared clean, and the rest of the room was well maintained. The bathroom was gorgeous (not your typical hotel bathroom) with a large soaking tub and a separate glass shower. There were plenty of towels and toiletry items for the three of us. While we did hear some music coming into the room, most of it was quieted by 10pm or so; at least enough that I was able to get to sleep. Unlike most hotels, we did not hear any hallway noise; perhaps because there were not many children at the hotel. The valets and bellhops were courteous and extremely knowledgeable about the area.
Because this hotel caters to a different type of person, you really need to do your 
homework. We got a room for 139 a night, but it is typically a lot more expensive; this should be an indicator on what to expect. They advertise that there is a cash minibar so this should not be a surprise. They advertise that parking fees are separate; this is typical of many downtown hotels across the country. If you have children, they might be very bored without a pool or free internet. If you are bothered by panhandlers, Westin is one block away from Beale St. where they tend to congregate due to the tourist money available; some will stand on the edges of the property to get you on the way to Beale St. Be polite and keep walking. Most of all, keep in mind you are paying to be centrally located and paying to be a Westin Beale St. guest. When we come back to Memphis, we WILL be staying at Westin Beale St.

title: “Treated us well...”
text: We stayed at this hotel while spending the weekend in Charlotte on a family trip (3 nights). They gave us a very nice corner room on the top floor when they found out we were visiting and really trying to enjoy ourselves (being a Hilton diamond member probably helped a little as well...). Breakfasts were good and the room was clean. Nice walking area including a small lake with some good restaurants in the area.

title: “NEVER AGAIN”
text:
We booked the room for 2 nights because of the heat. We wanted to get a nice room with
A/C but no such luck. We were on the 12th floor with no A/C. They gave us 2 very small fans that did not help at all. Then they refused to give us a discount for our inconvenience.
We paid well over $600.00 for 2 nights. They are enitrely too exspensive, the pool is extremely small and to top it off they make you pay for parking. $20.00 per day. The Best Western and Motel 6 is better than the Custom. I will never return

title: “Your typical airport sleeping factory”
text:
I pass through Seatte, either for business or vacation, several times per year and I use Priceline if I need a room close to Sea-Tac Airport. A $35 bid for a 3-star room in the Sea-Tac hotel zone will often get you into the Doubletree. By the time Priceline adds on taxes and fees, the cost goes up to $47. Because of my flight schedules, I merely use the Doubletree for sleeping. I arrive at night and then catch an early flight the next morning. Therefore I can't comment on the hotel's public amenities; I never use them. 
This Hilton-managed, chain hotel is almost certainly the largest in Sea-Tac. It has hundreds of rooms, some of which can be quite a hike from the lobby. Be aware of that if you have a lot of luggage. Once you get to your room, however, it will probably be reasonably clean and reasonably quiet (except when school groups or conventioneers have filled the place). The matresses are reasonably comfortable and the linens are of reasonable quality. The free shuttles to and from the airport operate with reasonable efficiency. The warm cookie the desk clerk gives you at check-in is a nice touch. Nevertheless, there is nothng remarkable about this hotel. It could be on any airport strip in any mid-size city in North America. 
Across the street from the Doubletree is one of the locally-owned "Roasters" bar and grill restaurants. It is a good place for a beer (lots of drafts on tap) and some roast chicken or a burger and fries. For more upscale dining, check out the 13 Coins. That restaurant is on the same side of the street as the Doubletree and about two blocks north. The food there is good, but a dinner for two will probably cost you more than the room at the Doubletree.

title: “Great location”
text: Just came back for a 4 nights stay at the Wellington. It is so well situated, 5 minutes to Central Park , 10-15 minutes to Time Square and close to lots of attractions and restaurant, The hotel room was small but it is very clean and the bed was comfortable, I would certainly stay there again!

title: “If you have to stay at the airport... try this”
text: Nice hotel for the location, right next to LAX (really about as close as you can get). Free shuttle makes it easy. Customer service is good - Diane at front desk very helpful. The food in the italian restaurant here is tasty, but overpriced. The decor is worn and everything is kind of dark.. dark furniture, low lighting...not my favorite. But it has all you would expect in hotel services and friendly staff, so give it a shot if you have to stay at the airport.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
We were at the end of a visit to Colorado from England.
We stayed for a single night in a Regency Club room on the 35th floor. Great views from the room, the breakfast room on the same floor and from the superb bar on the 27th floor, facing the Rockies.
Staff very courteous and helpful.
Room was spacious and modern with flat screen TV.
We will definitely consider a return to here.

title: “Ripped a new one on parking - and more!”
text:
We arrived in May, 2011 for our two day stay with a car for which we had committed to pay a daily parking fee of $37.00. Check-in was courteous. Bell service fine. 
The room was tiny, but that was as expected. The beds were worn out and hard, which wasn't really a surprise, either. Bathroom was similarly small, with a puzzling sheet of glass across half of the tub in lieu of a shower curtain. It worked exactly as you'd expect. Lone ice machine located on the fourth floor. Not much of an inconvenience, really. 
We got a good laugh perusing the room service prices. We knew it was New York, but we were still able to laugh at their obviously grandiose opinion of the value of their offerings. Luckily, there is a small grocery store around the corner in the same building for food, drinks, etc. and a really nice diner with reasonable (for New York City) prices right across the street. We wouldn't be eating their overpriced room’s service items or using their similarly overpriced breakfast buffet. 
Didn't try the bar. Can't say whether it is overpriced or not. We can, however use our imaginations. Air conditioner on one of the coolest Mays in record could barely keep the room comfortable. We felt sticky and uncomfortable most of the time that we were in the room. Fortunately, the instinct to flee the room at every opportunity kept us out of it for a good part of our stay. 
The hotel description mentions "city or courtyard views." Well we knew we didn't have a city view but "courtyard?" "Courtyard" must be Italian for "three dark walls and a rank of industrial air conditioners." A darker, more depressing scene would be hard to imagine. The complimentary shampoo and shower gel was colorful and effective. (The fruitiness of the flavors made me feel just like a lollipop after showering!) The bottles that I managed to cram into my suitcase are going to make great stocking-stuffers for Xmas, I'm sure. 
The big surprise came on check-out when they charged us not two, but FOUR DAYS of parking charges! The desk clerk said, “But you used your car.” Admittedly, I had for one day, in order to move my daughter’s things from her apartment to a storage facility. He explained that every time you use your car, you incur a NEW 24 hours of parking charges. (Indeed, buried in their web site is the language, “There are no in/out privileges. If you take your car out, the 24 hours starts over when you return.”) I accepted that policy, yet he couldn’t explain how the fourth parking charge was added to the bill. The more I inquired, the heavier his accent got until we simply couldn’t communicate. I paid the entire bill with my credit card and left, vowing never to return.
To add further injury, when my credit card bill arrived, they had added another $49.00 in unexplained charges, which American Express had removed after disputing them.
I’m used to small, dark, hot, uncomfortable accommodations in New York, but to have a series of continual charges added to your bill is more than even an out-of-towner ought to have to bear.
Never again!!

title: “Not What We Expected”
text:
No Tea/Coffee facilities in room. You have to go down to the breakfast room for that.
Poor quality TV. Excessive noise from building work outside - even after 12:00 midnight.
Staff not very friendly. Continental breakfast very unimaginative. Toast, Yoghurt, Fruit. (same every day). Tea and Coffee not very good. Fridge in room tiny. WC. flush sometimes continued to fill indefinitely. Shower cramped and impossible to control water temperature. Safe in room did not lock. Noisy air conditioner/heater operates continuously and woke us up during the night.
The whole hotel is very 'dated'. Probably would have been excellent in 1960s.
The one good thing is the location. Just a few yards from Herald Square. Aparently the Hotel is being updated. It certainly needs it. We have ppreviously stayed at the Hamton Inn in Chelsea which was much better.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
The Palomar Chicago is a nice boutique hotel in downtown Chicago, near to the river and ideally located for exploring the city. The rooms are big and well cleaned, everything you need is available. When you register with their loyalty program, you get free WiFi and 10$ credit for the mini bar. In the evening, there is a hosted wine tasting hour in the living room. 
The hotel's design is great, warm and modern. The staff is caring. There was no problem to print some rail tickets for us - just send them per mail to the receptionist. In one of the highest floors, you find the pool with stunning views on the architecture near to the river.

title: “Excellent!”
text:
I had high expectations for this hotel and the hotel lived up to them and even outperformed them. The location is great with BART, Muni and Union Square within easy walking distance. If you need a rental car for a trip out of town there are several options just around the corner. The rooms are as people mention, quite small, but are very nice decorated and our room had a nice stereo and even a cd with some cool music as well as an IHome for Ipod-docking. Combine that with free Internet (for InTouch-members) and that the hotel threw in complimentary continental breakfast in the Grand Café and a small welcome gift in our room along with the welcome note at arrival and you have a very nice package. We had a room on the 6th floor (requested a high floor room at the time of booking, a request they honored) On top of that you have friendly staff and of course the "wine reception" every afternooen with wine, some snacks, Nintendo Wii and a quick massage.
People tend to talk about "a home away from home". Hotel Monaco is the hotel that I've visited that has been closest to that saying. I highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Excellent location and gorgeous beds, shame about the customer service”
text:
Stayed 4 nights in April. I had booked over 3 months in advance and despite requesting a room with a view 'up Manhattan' I was not allocated one. I had paid the supplement for a corner room and that is worth the money but do your best to get one with a better view. We arrived late due to it taking 3 hours to clear passport control at JFK. No assistance with bags when we arrived (around 11pm). Rooms very clean and had everything we needed. The next morning at 7.50 I enquired about breakfast and was quite rudely told that it is not available until 8am! Pardon me for my jet lag switch being 10 mins out. We left the hotel having received a coffee and juice and didn't trouble them for breakfast again.
It is a great location and would definitely recommend on that basis alone if you don't need information from staff. Also, the best beds outside of the Grosvenor in London will be found here - a very big positive.
The bar is great, quite a limited selection but a great atmosphere from customers, staff were a bit better in the bar area but the service overall was poor and such a shame as the building and location are a real surprise and worth the money

title: “Nice stay in San Diego”
text: We stayed in this hotel several years ago. We found that the common areas were still very nicely kept. We somehow stayed in the exact room we stayed in 4 years ago. Seems as the room hasn't had much of a face lift though, but they were clean. The views are beautiful with floor to ceiling windows -- stayed in a corner king room with 1 view of the city, 1 view of the harbor. Beds are comfortable. Ordered room service 1 night, food was really good, with quick service.The Top of the Hyatt (40th floor) has a nice bar with sweeping views of the city. Only "complaints" would be that we had a "sticky" lock on our door that took SEVERAL passes with the key before it would unlock and on the last day our drain stopped up in the sink. (however, we didn't complain because we were just leaving in the morning). Overall a great say with a PERFECT location.

title: “Nice Lobby, Tiny Rooms!”
text:
The service at the hotel is first rate, location is superb. But if you are a businessman or family looking for comfort and space.... this is not for you.
The lobby is massive, lush, and well appointed. This image begins to deteriorate when one walks into the cramped elevator, and dips further as musty odours waft you towards your tiny room. 
I'm sure you can pay for a sitting room and all, but I didn't and the room is so small that you almost have to squeeze by the foot of you bed to get to the bathroom. If you want to watch TV, there is no 'sitting room' style chair even. You either sit on edge of your bed, or lay down and watch it at an angle. 
Like most 'old lady' hotels (with apologies to any elderly women), the money has been spent in the lobby for those touring it's historical significance vice business style amenities for those staying there. A final kicker - 7$ for a bottle of water in the room - come on!.
As with many who travel constantly, please.... book me at the Courtyard Marriot or equivalent next time! Likely cheaper for the company, and more practical!

title: “Very cool hotel”
text: Very nice staff. Building is amazing... like stepping back to a century ago. Only downside is the Wifi is kind of lame... Kimpton requires you to sign up into their rewards system before accessing, and performance was not great.

title: “Good Hotel”
text: I selected this hotel after many, many, many hours of research, mainly because of the free parking and the good reviews on trip advisor. It also appealed because it meant that we didn't have to drive into the main part of the city. We stayed one night at the end of our 16 day road trip round Washington, and were very happy with the choice. We arrived a bit early, frazzled because of the traffic on a Saturday afternoon, (having been in the mountains for days it was a shock to the system!) and they checked us in straight away, which was great. The room was spacious and very clean, overlooking Lake Union. We enjoyed watching the sea planes and boats coming and going. Later we walked down the road and had a meal at Dukes Chowder House, which we enjoyed very much. The free breakfast was very good.

title: “So disapointed”
text:
My husband and I choose the Sheridan hotel on the Inner Harbour in Baltimore Maryland to celebrate our anniversary. I called the hotel to inform them that we would be arriving late and I was told that reservations would be held until 2am. When we arrived to the hotel we were told that the only room available was a handicap accessible room. Although not what I expected to hear, we were tired and planned to stay only the one night. At worst, I expected the room to have bars in the bathroom to assist with bathing and larger space for wheel chairs or walkers.
To my surprise, the room dirty and the furniture looked like it was retrieved from a yard sale. The carpet was discolored, the bathroom floor had circles of dried dirty water stains, the bathtub was visually dirty and the tub was scraped and worn. The bathroom doors were scuffed and the walls were peeling. The sleeping area had what appear to be mold on the wall. The furniture was missing drawer handles and was terribly scratched. And even better, we received a note under the door from management that there would be no hot water for bathing.
I reported all of this in writing to the front desk clerk and although she was very polite, I doubt if any of my complaints were forwarded on to management. 
This property needs a complete overhaul. The Baltimore inner Harbour has so much to offer it's a shame that this hotel put a damper on our visit. Dont look for ambiance at this hotel.

title: “Wow, what an amazing trip!”
text: The W San Francisco really went above and beyond the Starwood standards. My husband and I stayed for 3 nights for my birthday celebration. The service was outstanding and the room was marvelous. The staff was very caring and pleased our every need. We loved everything about it! Will be staying here every time we visit San Francisco, without a doubt.

title: “Enjoyed my stay in this value-for-money hotel (near PAHO)”
text:
This is a good hotel! We stayed here during a convention and it was a really short walk down to the PAHO building so the location was ideal. We were given mini suites with a small kitchenette - rather useful if you are in meetings all day, sometimes till as late at 7-8pm. It was comforting to come back and know that you could eat in (stock up the fridge) or go downstairs to the rather nice restaurant near the lobby area. Breakfasts were also very nice though a bit expensive if you're on a budget. There's a Trader Joe's at five minutes' walking distance and is very close to Georgetown if you want to go out in the evenings.
About the rooms: they were clean, the bed was very comfortable, the bathroom was standard, amenities were pleasing and never lacking (Neutrogena products for toiletries). I had a flat screen TV in the room, a desk and a table to eat from. There was also a sofa in case you were entertaining guests. 
The staff was friendly too! I would have given it 5 out of 5 if it weren't for small inconveniences we had with the prices. Many guests during that week were all attending the same meeting. Some got better deals than others (inexplicably). When we explained that we all wanted the same rate, the manager said this was not possible and that was disappointing. Some of us had to go back to the same organization with different bills for reimbursement, which was embarrassing to explain. Nonetheless, the manager did offer those paying more money breakfast coupons, which was at least a gesture.
All in all it was a good stay. I would recommend this hotel for those who have a budget of 100-140 dollars per night.

title: “Great for price”
text:
Very clean hotel, rooms are comfortable, double rooms are huge! Although it is an "express", but there was a fridge, coffe machine, iron in rooms and vending machines in all floors and tea, coffe 24 hrs in the lobby. Breakfast was very simple,very few options, but everything was very tasty, I don't think I could need more.
This small hotel is located outside downtown centre, first, I thought this is a disadvantage, but after that I knew it's a very good location, being on the highway, makes everythig close without stucking in traffic everyday. also, the hotel offers free shuttle every 30 min to the underground station, which is 3 stops only from downtown crossing. It is 45 min by taxi to "wrentham premium outlets" , a must for shopping in massachussetes, also 30 min from"south shore mall" which has got all the famous departemental stores in USA (sears, nordstrom, target, macy's, lord& tailor). Also, just behind the hotel, there is south bay plaza, with many bargain departemenral shops and few restaurants such as Applebees.
Two computers with internet and printer free to use in the lobby.
The only bad thing in fact, I had a box delivred to the hotel, and it stayed in the recption for 3 days and they didnt tell me except when I asked if it arrived or not.

title: “Great location, room and breakfast.”
text: Right in downtown with views of Minute Maid Park. Houston Pavilion and restaurants nearby. Clean, modern, trendy hotel.

title: “Nice location”
text:
My 9 year-old son and I stayed two nights at The Doubletree last weekend.
We had been scheduled to fly in on Thursday evening, but our flight was cancelled and we had to take an early morning Friday flight. I called the front desk and was able to get my reservations changed around. I was staying on Hilton Honors points and had to make a few extra calls, but everyone was helpful and things worked out.
I had asked for a room on a high floor, away from the elevators. Our request was granted as we were given a room on the 33rd floor of the 43 story hotel and we were as far from the elevator as possible. The only downside of our room location was that we were as far from Times Square as we could be. Our room looked out over 49th Street.
The rooms that face out over Times Square would appear to be rooms 01, 02 and 03 on each floor. Room 01 is right next to the elevators (all 7 of them) and 02 and 03 also each appear to face Seventh Avenue. I don't know how quiet they are, but if you want a great view, you will likely be near the elevator.
As others have noted you need to show your room key or have your name checked against the reservations list to gain admission into the small ground floor lobby and to take one of the three elevators to the third floor registration area. These elevators were always quick to arrive. I do not think we ever waited longer than 15 seconds for an elevator, coming or going. The main entrance is at the corner of 49th and 7th, right in Times Square, so the security is nice.
I had asked for a room away from the elevator to ensure it was quiet, and we did have a quiet room. 
To be honest, we were not in the room that much. I did not come to New York to sit around my hotel. I was looking for a room with a comfortable sleeping quarters, clean, safe, convenient to the subway and close to the New Amsterdam Theater where we had tickets to see Lion King. The Doubletree met those requirements. Other than late night and early morning, we did not spend more than 30 minutes at a time in the room.
The king size bed was very comfortable. 7 pillows on the bed, great mattress. Had probably my best nights sleep in a hotel in a long time. I usually don't sleep well in strange beds, but had no troubles here.
The bathroom had entrances into both the bedroom and "living room." There was only one sink in the bathroom. The shower had good water pressure and decent heighth. I did not have to worry about the shower head being below my head (I am 6-2).
The living room area had a sleeper sofa, chair, desk in front of the window (with extra power outlets and phone jacks) and a dresser with the TV on it. It also had a small sink (wet bar type) and a refrigerator. There was an honor bar in the dresser area that we did not even look at.
Our room had a king size bed. There really was not much extra room in the bedroom. The bed, two night stands and Armoire (with TV) pretty much took up all of the room.
While the rooms are of ample size, the overall size of the suite I found comparable to a typical room in the Hamptons, Courtyards, etc that you find along the Interstate highways. Maybe a touch bigger, with the bathroom definitely bigger. But I don't know that I would want to try more than 4 people in one of these suites.
We did not eat at the hotel. The Kids area was closed when we left.
The conceirges were helpful. Gave us subway directions that we needed and other advice. 
I would stay again at The Doubletree, but I don't know what I would pay for a room (as noted above, I stayed for free using Hilton points). Given how little time I spent in the room, I might be tempted to try somewhere else if the price were right. But if the Doubletree price was competitive, I would stay here and take the known quantity.

title: “The Perfect Hotel Experience”
text:
We just returned from four nights at the Fairmont and all I can say is it was perfect, from the bellman when we arrived to the woman who checked us in to the housekeeper who checked on us 10 minutes after we arrived in our room to see if there was anything she could do for us. We stayed in the old building and our room was spacious. The bathroom was quite large with wonderful toiletries. There was a nice size closet with hanging space, shelving and an ironing board and iron. The service is impeccable, all the staff we came in contact with could not have been nicer or more helpful. I can't find one negative thing to say. 
While there, you have to go down to the Tonga Room. Great drinks, great food and a great band. Just a lot of fun. Also, if you are in the mood for a nice french restaurant, try Rue Lepic. It's one block down Mason from the hotel. Only bad thing, you have to walk back up the hill!

title: “Had no choice but to stay here”
text: We had to stay here because it was near to the location where we needed to go.it was our first experienced to stay there but not very good because of the cleanliness standard specially of carpets and the towels....not enough pillows too....drainage problem also...

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: I was recently at this Westin for a meeting and came away very impressed with this hotel. I stay in hotels on a regular basis, and this hotel really stood out. I liked its layout and design, and the staff was excellent. The rooms were clean, quiet, with a nice design. If I am back in San Diego, I would definitely stay here.

title: “Love it here!”
text:
Hi. Just finished a trip to NYC with some friends. I have personally stayed at the Kimberly several times. I have stayed with my husband, my kids, and with friends. It accommodates all. This is a suite type hotel. They were originally condominiums that did not sell, so they converted it to an all-suite hotel. The rooms are elegantly appointed and with antique furniture. The rooms are laid out as follows: One bedroom, one bathroom and a separate living room with a pull-out sofa. There is a full kitchen that is in the format of a bar with granite counters, sink, and all appliances and serve-ware and bar-ware. Tons of closet space with a safe. The sofa-bed is NOT your traditional spring pull-out. It is a tempurepedic with no springs and frankly extremely comfortable. King size pull-out that easily sleeps 2. The rooms also have a balcony with chairs and a table. 
The hotel has a roof-top restaurant that is OUTSTANDING for breakfast which is an extra charge of $22 for the full buffet or their is a menu to order from. In the evening it is a club called UPSTAIRS. Fantastic view of the Chrysler building and the NY skyline. It gets a bit loud with the DJ. I wouldn't recommend staying on an upper floor if you want peace and quiet in the evening. They still need to work out the sound-proofing. 
Great staff.
The location is excellent if you want to walk madison, park, 5th Ave. and shopping. You can walk to Central Park and Times Square also.

title: “Close to Seattle”
text: This was our first visit to Seattle and it was less expensive to stay outside of the city. This hotel was clean and well kept and the staff was friendly. We were very tired the first night, so we decided to order room service. The service was fast and the food was good, although overpriced (as expected with room service). We did visit the pool, which was nice. Because of this hotel's location near the airport, you can obviously hear the airplanes, but it was not bothersome at all.

title: “Great Business Hotel”
text: This hotel is sparkling clean! the staff were super attentive. I think they really cater to the business traveler. It is close to the convention center, world trade center and plenty of restaurants. Short walk to the rest of the city.

title: “Good hotel, good price.”
text: Spent one night here and it was a good deal for the money. The room was clean, though a little worn around the edges it was worth the money. Walls are a little thin so could hear neighbors (bring ear plugs) but not bad. The staff was friendly and helpful. Great location for my needs...

title: “Very good choice on Market St near the Financial district”
text:
Stayed for one night on a quick business trip to San Fran. The property is more than adequate - good location between two Bart stops, a block away from Market St., with a Starbucks and Calif. Pizza Kitchen across the street. 
 Decent bar with a surprisingly good wine-by-the-glass selection; only problem is the bar seemed to close early despite a conference on the property, and the kitchen closed at 10pm, about 5 minutes before I got there. The only other option was room service. 
 My room was large however oddly shaped. Small bathroom and tiny closet but perfectly comfortable for my purposes. 
 I have no problem recommending it - but of course if you're looking for something more hip and trendy, or for something more evocative of local San Fran culture, I guess there are better options. This is just a solid business choice, and if you can score something below $200 a night, definitely go for it.

title: “Euro 'concept' hotel trying desperately to be hip...”
text:
Here's a novel idea - build a faux-futuristic hotel in Midtown Manhattan, put a robotic luggage storage system in the lobby and have Tumi sponsor it - no need for bell hops! Put airport-style automated check-in counters in the entrance lobby - no need for a reception desk or clerks, but wait! There's plenty of staff in the lobby to help you check in anyway.
Get a Premium 'cabin' (cruise-ship style) and have an adjustable bed so it looks like the room is bigger than it is! Throw in an 'entertainment wall' - essentially a HDTV with an iPod connector and back lighting - and a stand-up shower with a rainfall shower head (I know! We'll call it a Monsoon Shower!) and you've got the latest in trend-chic.
The Yotel is walking distance to the Javits Center (I was there for a convention), which is great because the NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission doesn't communicate with the Javits Center to coordinate cabs for the start and end times of any conventions in town. Easy in/easy out of Manhattan via the Lincoln Tunnel with a parking lot right there at 41st and 10th make it perfect for travelers coming in from New Jersey or Newark Airport.
Breakfast at the DohYo restaurant was very nice - the omelets were tasty and the yogurt/granola combos were a nice healthy option. Night-time brings local NY DJs spinning tunes till the wee hours in the 4th floor lobby lounge, with the requisite crowds of hipsters drinking and dancing. Fortunately, the noise doesn't filter up to the rooms if you stay in the upper floors.
Since the bed is adjustable, it employs a futon-type mattress, which is not very comfortable to sleep on. In an era where most chain hotels are promoting their new dream beds with ultra-comfortable mattresses, this is a let-down. Overall, for a Midtown hotel in this price range the Yotel is a good value - it is clean and well run and the staff is friendly and helpful. There are great bars and restaurants nearby (I recommend the Lansdowne Road bar for scotch drinkers, and the 44 and X and its sister restaurant, 44 and 1/2 for dinner) and plenty of shopping, plus it's only a block from Port Authority and a few blocks from Times Square proper.
Younger travelers will likely be impressed with the Yotel, as it is geared toward their generation. Older travelers - especially business and world-weary ones - will see this hotel for what it is. It's not that it's a bad place to stay, it's just that it's trying too hard to be trendy.

title: “Marten House is the place to stay in Indianapolis”
text:
Just a quick note to tell you that many of my 36 Guests continue to Thank me for staying at this fine hotel. Everyone raves about how neat and clean everything is, how good the service is and how well everyone is treated. Thank you to everyone at The Marten House for running such a great establishment. See you again next year.
Andy Granatelli

title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text:
I recently stayed at the Westin Copley Place while on business in Boston. I work out regularly and their fitness center was under renovation. I woke up at 5:30 AM to go to the fitness center that they told us to use. Unfortunately, the doors were locked and I could not get to the other hotel from inside the hotel. I told the night manager about my problem.
He proceeded to get me a taxi ... he took me to the concierge desk, spoke to the taxi driver and made sure that I was able to get back to the Westin Coply. I was surprised and gratified that he took the extra time to make sure that I had access to the other fitness center. He went above and beyond what I expected.
The door man that meets and greets guests as they drop their cars is great ... he remembered me from previous stays and really made me feel welcome.
I travel a lot on business and usually stay at another major hotel chain ... however I have never seen the great custormer service that I received at the Westin Copley Place. They really do a super job.
I would recommend this hotel to anyone ... they are the best!!!

title: “Decent place to stay for access and price downtown”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Crowne Plaza for four days mid-October and found the acomodations reasonable and location good for the price. The parking valet upon arival was very attentive and helpful and ended up also being the staff member to bring the bags to our room.
The hotel is older but has been renovated in the common areas as well as the rooms at some point in recent years. The hotel was 100% booked with two conventions and therefore we were assigned an ADA room which we did not need and provided no closet (shelves and a rack) and no counter space in the bathroom (to make room for wheelchair access). We didn't make a fuss but after 4 days I was really tired of balancing things in the bathroom and not being able to have our luggage actually put away for the trip.
The trolly to downtown was only a short walk across to the Marriott (appeared to be a nice hotel) at the convention center. We found walking to many areas of interest easy and the city to be clean and friendly. We enjoyed some wonderful meals also within walking and trolly distance and only used the car for day trips away from downtown.
We had breakfast two mornings at the hotel but unless you have a discount I would go elsewhere. The staff is pleasant however service was slow and both mornings all tables were dirty to choose from with only a couple of persons eating. Hard to say about staffing but I would not pay $13.95pp for a cold buffet with very limited choices there again.
Overall the staff is very pleasant and we were satisfied with our stay but nothing special. Would consider staying again if the price was right compared to other options.

title: “Excellent Clean hotel”
text: Excellent service and a very clean hotel! Will stay again!

title: “Beautiful!”
text: Gorgeous hotel! Beautiful building, lovely location. Nice, comfortable rooms, with a very comfortable bed. Was decorated very festively for Christmas when I was there, which made the place feel very cozy and warm.

title: “Room for improvement”
text:
■ Not the best experience ever. For one night only, well... acceptable.
■ The room: as soon as I lay on the bed my legs started itching...
■ Location in the middle of nowhere; breakfast was less than satisfactory

title: “Disappointment”
text: I was at the Hyatt for a large conference and was disappointed. There were some very nice and helpful persons on the staff, however the hotel services for a conference were poor. The food was totally overpriced (($60 for 2 salmon salads and one coke delivered during lunch in the conference room), the free wireless service (specifically ordered for this conference) did not function for any of the 3 days of the conference and some colleagues who out of sheer desperation had bought a paid internet connection from the hotel also could not get online.

title: “Doesn't feel like San Diego”
text:
When in San Diego, if you're renting a car I suggest staying outside of downtown. I've stayed in several W Hotels in other cities, this one feels cleaner but like many I felt like I was in a hotel trying to have boutique hotel touches but really is a massive hotel. There's no warmth in their service and I was just one out of hundreds of guests staying there. The pool looked nice in their pictures but it was a tiny little puddle. Gym was not impressive given the size of the hotel. Am I the only person who gets irritated with the "whateva wheneva" line?
I hate how hotel rooms are increasingly becoming a convenience store where they sell amenities with ridiculous mark up. I understand the mini-bar cost, managing the inventory and overhead that comes with it. But I don't need to see so many tent cards that show the cost of everything that takes up valuable counter space. See wine rack on wall image.

title: “Wonderful Room, Wonderful Service”
text: I stayed here for a week while travelling on business. The room was wonderful - particularly the luxurious bed and expansive bathroom. Service was also great - from check-in to check-out. Lastly, I appreciated the building's LEED NC certification and the opportunities that they have taken toward incorporating green practices into their building operations.

title: “Great deal....Will go back with Family Again.”
text: We just returned from a long weekend in NYC. We have stayed at The Novetel and DoubleTree in Times Square in the past, this time we wanted to spend our money on better things like Broadway shows and shopping. And we did. This is a great Family hotel, the rooms were clean, and the decor was nice. The staff was helpful and very resourceful. The hotel is only a two blocks from Broadway / Times Square. We paid $150. per night not including all taxes, this is an excellent NYC Deal. We will book at the Belvedere again without any hesitation.

title: “Charming with great location”
text: We stumbled upon this wonderful hotel through an Internet deal. The hotel has a fabulous location, right in the heart of the Mag Mile. Also, the service was excellent- we had some challenges with an error that I made with the reservation (accidently selecting the wrong month), and they were very helpful in assisting us in working it out. I would certainly stay there again, and recommend it to others. The location alone, not to mention the charming atmosphere, makes it a great choice for a downtown Chicago experience.

title: “Fab place for a quiet weekend away”
text:
We arrived here for one night and we fell in love with it straight away we got upgraded to the laurel suite which was fantastic with a huge huge huge tub in it. it had a bit of a musty smell but hey its an old mansion. we got to stay in the main mansion but the regular rooms are in a building next to it. 
The pool was warm and quiet with very few hanging about. only complaint is that the sun loungers are few and far between.
THe gardens are fantastic. the hotel extremely quiet and the staff very friendly we even got a late check out for $0
We will definately be back again this summer

title: “Loved everything except the STREET NOISE”
text: I loved this hotel, staff, location, food, ect. My only complaint is the street noise. The windows are old and need to be upgraded to doubled pane glass; if not triple. So if you are easily bothered by outside noise or are a light sleeper this is not the hotel for you.

title: “Nice Rooms, Nicer people, great location”
text: The hotel is very clean and nice, although it's showing it's age. The Hanalei has been a San Diego fixture for many decades. The location is excellent as you can get to all the major San Diego freeways in no time at all. Best of all, it is a hop, skip and a jump from Old Town. (See review of La Pinata Restaurant here on Tripadvisor.) The hotel has wonderful staff who are quite helpful (typical of Crowne Plaza). There is plenty of free parking and the rooms facing north have a great view of the Mission Valley Golf Course. The rooms are clean. At night, if you are on the north side of the hotel and on the higher floors, you can watch the nighttime fireworks show at Sea World, a nice treat.

title: “Very nice long stay hotel”
text:
I was here over the weekend for a convention that was held at the nearby Westin hotel. I had a nice studio unit that came with a kitchen (no oven though so be aware of that). Check in was easy with friendly front desk staff. There is a marketplace around the corner from the front desk that has assorted frozen meals, snacks and drinks, and ice creme novelties, along with some toiletry items. 
The room has a microwave and burners, with a full size refridge. You can order grocery delivery or room service from a local meal delivery service. You get coffee, tea and popcorn in the hospitality packet. 
Breakfast is included with hot and cold items. Items are changed daily so you may find sausage one day with ham another. 
There is an outdoor pool, fitness center and computer room for printing boarding passes.
Road construction is in force, but if you pass the property and take the next road up, go around to the road where the taxi drivers are waiting to get to the back of the property. 
I enjoyed my stay here. You will too.

title: “Very sheek hotel”
text: Great hotel! I have been staying at this hotel over the past six months. The staff is great! Very friendly and accomodating. The rooms are of an average size and offer many amenities...one of my favorites, the luxurious bath robes. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Fabulous Place to Stay”
text: We spent two weeks in California and stayed in a couple of first class hotels - but this hotel was the favourite by far. We were only able to stay two days because it was booked up. Next time we will plan ahead!! Hollywood Boulevard with the Walk of Fame, Kodak Theatre, Madame Tussaud's etc. etc. is literally a block away and is a nice residential area so very safe to walk. The pool area is lovely, with lots of towels to use and staff circulate with popsicles. We hit the tourist areas early in the morning when it wasn't crowded and spent the afternoon by the pool. The kids loved the unlimited snacks and drinks at the front desk. Our room was like a little apartment. The decor is dated, but we still loved it and would definitely love to return and recommend it highly!!

title: “Great Place!”
text: A beautiful cool hideaway in a baking 105 degree Dallas! The room was clean, nice and cool, well presented with a very confoartable bed!! Loved having a fridge and microwave in the room and the coffe shop opposite the car park was very handy! The staff were lovely and helpful, I'd come back here in a flash!

title: “Customer Service excellent”
text: My second time staying here. Great location. Macys a hop skip & jump away. plenty of great restaurants nearby. Empire state just behind. Staff friendly & helpful. Room spacious & clean. Bar area comfy and staff excellent! Female bartender friendly & entertaining. Food yum. Will be back.

title: “Stop over in LA”
text: Stayed here but for only one night en route to Hawaii. Probably too far away from the airport for that but in a nice neighbourhood in LA. Hotel was really nice with a modern sllightly quirky feel but we enjoyed it more for that. Staff were all very helpful and the check in and out process was very efficient.

title: “Fabulous Location”
text:
- Small attractive hotel, but what really makes this hotel is the location. The location is excellent!! A short walk takes you to Union Square or Chinatown or to the financial district. 
- The rooms are small but adequate. We upgraded to a King size bed for an extra $10 per night. The bed is very comfortable, although we didn't like the pillows but no biggie. The bathrooms could use an upgrade and we could sometimes hear the neighbors when they are busy in the bathroom next door. We also opted for a courtyard room so as not to hear any street noise/traffic and we slept very well.
- The reception staff and concierge are extremely helpful. 
- The wine tasting in the evenings is a nice touch. 
All in all, we would stay here again.

title: “great family vacation”
text: We travel with our grandchildren, but this is the best kid's hotel we have been to. The children loved the waterpark. Their parents loved it too. The rooms were excellent, extra pillows, wonderful mattresses, everything new. The water park is running over with life guards. They even have wrist bands for the children so parents can track them within the park. Grandparents, take your grandchildren!

title: “One of the Best in Chicago”
text:
I spent three days at Peninsula. The district is perfect, Everything is AROUND THE HOTEL.
It was my first time in a Peninsula hotel and I must say I would go again.
The decoration is old but nice, the bathroom is huge bathtub and shower. The view from my room was not amazing but once in the gym one can work out with a view all over the city and the lake which is very pleasant.
The Asian restaurant is good, service perfect but the atmosphere quite boring.
The bar is really nice at night better to reserve on friday night because it is very crowed.
Note: If you order breakfast in your room it always take more time than promised 40 mns sometimes. They always call to apologize but...the water used for the tea tastes really bad by the way.

title: “Very noisy, busy location”
text: This hotel is tightly placed between a nightclub hotel spot, another hotel, a packed marina, and the Bay. While the rooms are clean and adequate, the carpeting and sofas in the lobby/halls need to be replaced. The steady noise from the activity of helicopters and military ships in the Bay, along with the airport traffic and the adjacent nightclub's outside concerts makes sleeping and rest a bit challenging. The balconies are teeny, the air-conditioning units noisy.

title: “Great if you are trendy and really really good looking. Zoolander's perfect hotel! :)”
text:
I love the meatpacking district in NY and have stayed in numerous hotels around the area. From the very best to the average. I chose the Dream when my first choice The Standard was full. I have liked the look of the sister hotel the Maritime for some time but fancied the Dream more when it came to booking.
You know what to expect when the doormen look like models. This is a hotel full of pretty people, both staff and guests. Not a bad thing, but I got the impression the better looking you were the better your service was. On a couple of occasions I observed some less than stellar service given to people who just looked like normal folk.
The room I paid for was one with a view of the Empire State. Nice view and the portholes aren't too small so light does get in, but it's not the lightest of rooms. 
The bed was excellent. Very comfy. The bathroom was ok, shower very nice but a too hip for any use sink annoyed me. Brushing your teeth was not easy! Most of the stuff I spat out I had to clean up myself afterwards!!
Room service was ok. Expensive and based upon the expensive steak house in the hotel. My medium sirloin came to me like a piece of leather. Not what I expect for $80+ dollars. 
These trendy hotels lack some of the simpler things I come to expect in hotels. Ice machines in the property or a coffee machine in the room. The fridge was the usual mini bar crammed full of expensive stuff that you end up eating and drinking when you are slightly drunk. Dangerous! 
I barely got a smile out of anyone the entire time I was and for $400+ a night it's not a lot to ask for. 
The property itself is really attractive, albeit on the very dim side lighting wise. A lot of thought has gone into it and some of the design of the hotel was breathtaking.

title: “For a budget hotel.....Better than I ever expected!”
text: I did a lot of research before booking a hotel for our trip to New York City. I was concerned about bedbugs, price(we stayed over New Years), location, and cleanliness. We were pleasantly surprised by nyma. We had no bedbugs, the price was reasonable for the time of year, the location was excellent, and the hotel was very clean. The receptionist and concierge were friendly and helpful. We were a day late due to weather complications and plane cancellations, but a simple phone call let them know our plans. When we checked in, I asked for and was given a room on the 15th floor looking out to the Empire State Building. As first-timers to NYC, we were very pleased! The room was small but comfortable, with the fridge and microwave we had requested. Housekeeping was attentive and friendly. We only had our room cleaned once during our one week stay(a personal choice), but they were always willing to give us clean towels and extra soaps. We left our garbage bagged outside our door, and it was always taken care of. The location of this hotel is prime. One street block to the Empire State Building, three avenue blocks to Penn Station and Madison Square Garden, two street and two avenue blocks to Macy's and Herald Square. Relatively close to major subway lines( I would recommend the subway for Manhattan travel if you are cost conscious.....one week use for $27, the price of one taxi ride!) All in all, we had a wonderful time in Manhattan, and this hotel was an excellent base of operations for our adventures! Thankyou nyma!

title: “Great Stay!”
text:
We stayed one night at the Holiday Inn Manhattan 6th Avenue. As with all hotel rooms in NYC they are a bit on the small side, fitting the king bed, a desk and a small bathroom. The suggested occupancy of the rooms should be heeded...do not try and fit a larger group into these modest size rooms. No roll aways available...they wouldn't fit in our king room anyway! That being said it was nicely appointed with comfortable beds and a big flat screen tv. Free wi-fi was a plus.
We did not use the workout facility at the hotel, but it had one treadmill, one exercie bike and an elliptical. All brand new. It is located in the basement of the hotel.
Only two elevators for the 25 floors so your wait can be long (around 4 minutes). We had no problems waiting though!
The front desk staff was very helpful and friendly. Always willing to help with any question or request. They are very knowledgeable about area restaurants etc.
A convenient location with multiple subway stops within 3 blocks. The neighborhood, Chelsea, felt very safe at all times of the day and night.
We would stay again if we were in the area. A good price/value ratio! Overall a great stay!

title: “A Great Place to Wait Out the Storm”
text: The Library hotel was a fabulous place to wait out Hurricane Sandy. What was originally a 3 night business trip quickly became a week's mandatory holiday. The staff at the Library Hotel are professional, friendly and helpful. Due to the storm and flight cancellations, we extended my stay twice. Nothing was too much trouble for those at the desk, especially Jessica and Billy, to assist us. We cannot recommend this hotel highly enough. It was a quiet refuge and we felt lucky to be so well looked after.

title: “All Good”
text:
The hotel was easy to find and very close to the subway making it easy to get about. The room was a good size, clean and the bathroom had a lovely warm shower. The breakfast was ample and a good start to the morning. The staff are very friendly there 24/7 and happy to give me directions to anywhere I wanted to go. The housekeeping are also very efficient.
Some of the hotel is looking a little tired but there was some work going on while I was there so I'm sure it will be looking its best in time for the summer season.

title: “Friendly helpful staff, wonderful catered food!”
text: I found the staff at the Baltimore Hilton to be some of the friendliest, most helpful and professional I've encountered anywhere. The catered meal I had during the course of my business there was also without a doubt the best hotel food I've ever eaten! Truly outstanding. While the hotel is overall very clean, the carpet in my room is showing signs of needing to be replaced. The one thing I don't like about this hotel is the charge for internet usage. Not only is there a charge, but it is outrageously high!

title: “outstanding customer service in a clean and modern hotel in convenient location”
text: Our ten-day stay at the San Antonio Hampton Inn (Airport Location) was very positive, exactly as we expected after our many overnights with this hotel chain and the excellent reviews on TripAdvisor. The staff was 100% welcoming, professional, friendly, and dedicated to making our time there a pleasant one. Letty at the Reception was quick to find us a room more suitable than the first one we’d reserved, and when we left or entered the hotel, we always received a warm smile and greeting. The 24 hour tea/coffee bar was appreciated, and not only daily cookies were provided, but Halloween was celebrated with decorations, as well as cookies, cupcakes, and candy. The hotel seems well-maintained and tidy, and the rooms are in good order, too. The daily breakfast is typical: daily warm dish/eggs, cereals, juices/tea/coffee, pastries and bread items to toast, waffle maker, etc, but after a few days, we found ourselves going out to cafes or diners for a change of scene and some variety. I would highly recommend this Hampton Inn for their service, the level of professionalism, good condition of the facilities, and there is plenty of free parking. We look forward to staying here again.

title: “Disaster with No Sleep”
text:
This past week I spent three nights at this hotel and to put it briefly, it was the worst hotel I've stayed in during my adult life. Most of the time I usually stay in Fairmonts, Marriotts, and Hyatts for both business and leisure travel because for one thing, I like their loyalty programs. After a while a person can begin to take certain things for granted by staying in the usual quality those three companies put forward in their properties, even though there are good things and bad things in any particular property. Stay in a hotel like this though and you'll be shocked back in to an appreciation for the better hotels in the world. 
The staff was nice and seemed to want to work very hard to be friendly and please the guests--and my room was very clean. However, what good does any of that do you if you can't sleep??!! My room was in what I now know is the infamous South Tower. The traffic noise from Baltimore Street below was crazy. It's a main city bus line street so starting at 5am, every 60 seconds there was a bus roaring by. It was horrible. Not even turning the clock radio to static could drown out the noise. It wouldn't get quiet on the street until 2am. That allows a guest three hours of sleep. There's a bed. You won't be sleeping in it much though. I can't warn people enough about the noise from outside. You will not sleep. This led me to think about the couple of other times I've stayed in loud hotels that prevented me from sleeping, the Hyatt Regency Miami's loud drawbridge and the Aruba Marriott's slamming doors at 7am and I must ask--what good is a hotel that you can't sleep in? As the buses roared by for three straight nights at this hotel, I once again had to ask that question but in this case, I decided to write a review about my experience to at least try to warn others of the street noise at this property. Ear plugs might help but it's such a deep noise that comes from the bus engines as they accelerate through the intersection below the tower that I don't think they would help--and then how do you hear the alarm clock in the morning if you've got to use ear plugs?
The room itself was also very odd in the lighting. There were three light sources for the entire room. The bathroom light and two dim lamps on either side of the bed. No desk lamp. No overhead light by the door or closet. To look at clothing, I had to use the bathroom light. I have never stayed in such a darkly lit room. They need to buy those cheap round white lights that you can stick up and push to turn on like they advertise on TV and put one of those in each closet area. 
The elevators to the tower went out the morning I was checking out. I had to climb up the stairs to get to my room to finish getting my stuff and then climb down again. Other people were also forced to use the stairs. Later in the day when I was going to my car in the self-park garage, those elevators in the North Tower were out and I had to go down by stairs in to the garage.
The garage was flooding due to rains and there was water streaming from overhead as well as ponding all over the place.
Finally, the public areas of the hotel have a dated and tacky look to them. Think royal blue and bright white with bright red accents and you'll get the picture. 
I have never in all my life been so happy to get out of a hotel and come home to peace, quiet, and lights!! 
Downtown Baltimore is such a great place to stay and have fun in. It's full of hotel choices. Stay at another hotel other than this. Even with an ongoing renovation, without an entirely new set of buildings on the sight that have been built with soundproofing, it's beyond help and you should seek out another place where you've got a better chance of getting sleep in your bed and a better chance of seeing things in your room with lights.

title: “Excellent value, great staff!”
text: We stayed here specifically because of the price and because of the pet-friendly quality. It was our first time traveling with this particular small dog, and we are very impressed. Staff loved him, and even offered to babysit him while we attended our concert, if he was too lonely while we were gone. The room was spacious and while the view was of the building next door, there was a small balcony, and we could see to the cross street. Noise control was pretty good--we were on the 6th floor, and so that helped. The king-size bed was so comfortable, with plenty of pillows; there were plenty of towels, and a roomy dressing area just outside the bathroom/shower/tub. We will definitely stay here again. We loved how close this (as far as walking distance) was to everything we wanted to see.

title: “Very Nice Hotel - Guest Services Lacking”
text: This is a lovely hotel located right on the Inner Harbor. Our room was very comfortable although we had to change rooms because the first one was too small for us. It did require an upgrade but was worth the money because the second room was much more spacious for our family of four. My only issue with the hotel was the lack of a concierge or anybody at the hotel who could help us out with recommendations for restaurants or provide us with any suggestions for sightseeing etc. I did speak with the concierge at the hotel prior to our visit and was told he would put together a listing of sights and restaurants for us to visit during our 3 day stay. When we arrived no one had any idea about this and for the three days of our visit there was no concierge on duty. The front desk folks although pleasant were not very helpful in this regard. I was surprised that a hotel that one would consider high end did not have anyone who could provide this level of service. Overall, staffing seemed to be lacking not so much in quality but in quantity.

title: “Good value, but not on the metro.”
text:
I stayed here with a friend who was in town for a conference at the university. The hotel is nicely appointed. The room was on the smallish side, but clean, crisp and new feeling/looking. The cafe seemed to have kind of strange hours, couldn't seem to catch a meal there, so can't speak to it. Also didn't have a car, but I bet there's free parking. That would be a major bonus. The internet was high speed and free. The grounds of the university are beautiful. It's a nice short walk to H Street with some great places to eat. We really like Ethiopian so that was a plus to be able to walk there. Capital Hill neighborhood is also a nice walk.
The negatives: the shuttle (maybe b/c it's summertime) was nearly always late and unreliable. The walk to the metro is through a depressed area and maybe dicey at night. The service is not like a regular hotel. There is one person who staffs the desk and it's a kid! They looked like maybe early 20's. The guy had no clue about anything, including what building the pool was in and wasn't about to try to find out. There was a young woman on staff later who had her act much more together, was professional and helpful.

title: “What a great place”
text: I stayed at the Omni back in October with a couple of girlfriends for a fun weekend. I had just come in from Phoenix and was exhausted, but we had a great time. The Omni is the classiest hotel downtown and I felt proud each time we were walking down the street coming back to our hotel to walk in the door. Service was friendly and great all around...and they say people in Philly are mean! Whenever we needed a cab, the guys in the front were great and the room was outstanding. Breakfast was awesome also. Great service there too. Not to mention my cousin is one of the chefs. Had a great time!

title: “Met expectations”
text:
Stayed here over an August weekend and I would confirm most of what has been said in previous reviews. Booked room through discount website for $105/night, which is very cheap for a San Diego weekend stay in the busy season. Assigned a large room facing marina in West tower on lower level. I would recommend this hotel assuming you are not paying rack rate ($229/night), because there are much nicer truly 4* hotels available downtown at that price.
Pros:
-View of marina
-Clean room, no service problems or complaints
-Close drive to downtown, beaches, Coronado, zoo, etc.
Cons:
-If you don't have a car the hotel is not within walking distance of downtown, beaches, or anything else.
-Definitely not a 4*--furnishings and hallways are a little worn and dated, especially in west Tower.
-Lanai rooms looked dark and motel-like.

title: “Beautiful hotel with excellent service”
text: The hotel is lovely, well appointed, and the staff is friendly and helpful. When we first got to our room, the TV remote wasn't working a maintenance person came right up and fixed it. The front desk staff was very helpful in use of the safe deposit box as well as sending up extra towels. There were two weddings going on while we were there, so the place was really hopping. The valets were very helpful when we checked out. All-around nice place.

title: “Great hotel.”
text: I only stayed for a night, but it was a very nice and clean hotel. The beds were very comfortable and the guest services were very helpful. The only issue was the AC did not cool very much, but we were lucky that the days and night were pleasant. Overall this was a perfect place to stay and I would highly recommend it to anyone.

title: “Amazing wedding weekend!”
text: Family and friends from all over the country stayed at the Mayflower for our daughters wedding in the city. Every level of service was excellent. Booking a group of rooms, the concierge desk answering many questions and helping find services, a whimsical bridal Tea Party! From the moment we pulled up to the hotel to the moment we left I always felt that there was not one need that could not be handled. A beautiful, historical hotel with many wonderful personal touches. And the location is perfect!!

title: “Location and nothing more”
text: The hotel is extremely well located at La Salle street , walking distance from the Michigan Avenue and other Chicago attractions. It's really a Motel and almost everything is outdated: lobby, facade, doors, hallway carpets and so on The rooms are clean, furniture and TV a bit outdated and the bathrooms look they have been renovated recently and are clean, the carpet inside rooms is not as old as the hallway one and is clean . The price is reasonable and has free parking. So you've got to weight if location is really an important thing for your stay. I may return if location is important.

title: “Great Place for a Great time!!”
text: I recently stayed here over the Labor Day weekend along with 24 other friends for a Bachelor party. I am a big Starwoods guy and used points for my stay. Its a great property and close to everything. The pool is great as well. I had so much fun and a way too early fight the next morning that i forgot a number of items in my room and didn't realize it till i got home. The W security personnel were very helpful and were able to find all my things and get them FedExed to me within days. I would definitely stay there again if i was in the Austin area and would recommend it for anybody traveling there.

title: “Amazing hotel with amazing staff!”
text:
We stopped at this hotel for my 30th birthday and 3rd anniversary celebrations! It was also when hurricane Sandy hit! The hotel could not have been more helpful and accommodating given this situation we were all faced with. On arrival we had an upgrade to a lovely suite room which was great. The restaurant and bar areas are very nice and the food is also lovely!
When we return to NYC we don't have to worry about looking for a hotel as I would always stop at the Andaz!

title: “location, amenities, staff, food”
text:
we stayed at the Capitol Skyline for four days and our stay was great. Helpful staff, good food,
great pool area and work out room. Our room was very comfortable and cool and quiet.. The front desk was very helpful helping us to locate sites and very helpful with a problem we had with our car locating where to buy the part we needed also where to have it fixed.

title: “Good Location, Older "Historic" Hotel”
text:
We decided upon the Congress as we had a problem with a previous reservation at another hotel and had to make a last minute selection on a very busy convention weekend. We chose the Congress based upon location and comments that the hotel was clean, which it was and knew it was going to be older.
We used the bellman to check our bags prior to check-in and all the staff was quite friendly. After our return later that afternoon they were able to put us into a King room which was not available when we originally made our reservation. The room was large enough and had the traditional high ceilings with a building of this age. The rooms are dated however clean and again, not bad considering almost the entire downtown was sold out. If I had paid the $220+ any other time I would not have been pleased. 
We did not dine at the hotel but did visit the cocktail lounge on Saturday evening and the one bartender on staff was overwhelmed with the amount of guests trying to get service. I continued to expect help to arrive but it didn't happen and we eventually left and dined and enjoyed cocktails elsewhere. Checked back into the lounge Sunday afternoon and same thing/same gal, lots of guests waiting and slow service. We again opted to dine and drink elsewhere. 
Yes, the hotel is aged and shows it, but the location is great (across from the park and lake) and there is something to be said for that historic feel at times. Would probably make another choice next trip but in a pinch this worked.

title: “In Need of a Facelift”
text:
The Sheraton Suites San Diego is, in the words of my wife, "a fine hotel that just needs a major remodel." I think that sums it up perfectly. The hotel is really a "fine" place - with a convenient location and nice views of the harbor, but the decor and the general public spaces of the hotel are really wanting for a little TLC.
The room was very clean (we stayed on the "Club Floor" - originally floor 27, but because we had been given a room with two queen beds, we switched to the 26th floor where we had a king bed). The amenities in the room are standard Sheraton - from the Starbucks coffee to the shampoo. The Internet is fast and reliable. And, finally, by report from my wife - the food in the hotel restaurant was decent enough.
The hotel is, however, older and the decor in the rooms really shows the age. Don't get me wrong - it is not a threadbare situation by any means. It is just that I have come to expect a little more from Starwood properties. Would we stay here again - probably not, as there are a number of really nice Starwood hotel properties in the San Diego area that have been updated and remodeled.
In closing - this is a "fine" hotel; but, there are better places to stay in San Diego that still allow you to take advantage of your SPG status and points.

title: “Typical large airport hotel”
text:
Typical large busy airport hotel.
Good well appointed room, with very comfortable bed.
Own room had cleanliness problem, that may conceivably not have been typical (bathroom surfaces grimey, sink seriously crazed, room carpet stained.)
Heavily stained carpets in corridors rather let down the overall ambiance and are clearly due for thorough cleaning or general replacement. 
Overall not up to the standard expected of the Hilton brand name.

title: “Loved the location”
text:
The location is great...just 3-4 mins walk to Times square. The floors are not clean but I aksed to clean and one guy has cleaned to a better position. Beds are good.
I stayed for 3 days and this is the only time the room was cleaned and bed sheets are not changed in these days. If you are in budget and want to stay in central NY with $120/night, this will be the only one option for you. But if you want luxary, you won;t get here. This place is only to sleep in the night and who wants to be in hotel in NY?
This is not that bad what ever told in above reviews. I stayed in room# 427 and there were no mice or something. Bathrooms are also clean.

title: “Awesome Concierge”
text: Roy the concierge/driver was great. He was so friendly and helpful. He drove the courtesy van for our group several times and always had helpful tips, knew the shortcuts to avoid traffic jams, had cool stories about celebrities and was super nice. Ask for Roy, he's the best!

title: “Great hotel, great location.”
text: Stayed three nights here on a business trip. The hotel met all the high standards that I have come to expect from the Marriott chain of hotels. Front desk staff were attentive. I experienced a problem accessing the wireless internet from my room, called the front desk, and help arrived at my room within ten minutes. The hotel has a great location right in the heart of downtown Charlotte. Lots of very good restaurants and pubs within walking distance. The NASCAR Hall of Fame and Time Warner Cable Arena (home of NBA's Charlotte Bobcats) are also within walking distance. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Beautiful rooms”
text: From check-in to check-out, the service is exceptional. Beautiful lobby, nice lounge. A real treat was to see glass work by Dale Chihuly going down the Grand Staircase to the Ballroom. A great venue for a special event! I would've like a small coffee maker in the room (there was coffee available in the lobby and juice or milk and cookies in the afternoon) , and also find it baffling that a hotel of this caliber would only offer complimentary internet access in the lobby, but in the guest rooms. Overall, a very nice hotel.

title: “Warning Stay Away”
text: My daughter and I were booked to stay at this location for two nights. We checked in about 10:00 the first night and walked into the room the first thing you notice is that they had put a towel down on the seat of the recliner in the room to hide all the stains. If you look were your head would normally be in the recliner it was filthy. As I walked across the room I find dog food laying on the floor and find the carpet full of dog hair. We stayed the first night and when we woke up the next morning my daughter said she felt sick, her nose was running and her eyes were all puffy. We spent the day away from the hotel and all of her symptoms cleared right up. Later that afternoon we went back to the room grabbed out belongings and went next door to te Jameson Inn. After checking in at the Jameson Inn we got our stuff and we walked by some of the staff talking and they said those people were at the Ramada last night and could complete their stay this happens several times a week. We woke up the next morning at the Jameson and my daughter had none of the symptoms she had experienced the day before. Listen to the reviews here stay away from this place.

title: “We had such a good time and the place added to the special feel.”
text: I was here for a girl's trip and we had such a good time. It was nice to have a car with a driver to take us where we needed to go in Downtown.

title: “Good Boutique Hotel,Somewhat Odd Location, Small Adequate Rooms”
text: I completed a one night stay at the Onyx on January 12, 2011 to attend a business meeting. At first I was concerned about the location. It is near the Boston Garden so handy for sports events but somewhat out of the way for other purposes. As it turned out, the location was not a problem since the T at North Station is only 1 1/2 blocks away. Hotel is generally nice; boutique hotel of 112 rooms. Basically not much of a lobby and the rooms are certainly on the small side (think closer to NY size than Boston 4*size). It was a little odd that the bathroom was so small that the towel rack was inside the shower area of the tub (on back wall) but the room size was certainly adequate for my short visit; longer visits may make the room size an issue since there is not much of a lobby either. But the rooms are comfortable, bedding is of high quality and the staff is very helpful and upbeat. Many good restaurants nearby including Boston's North End relatively close by. You can purchase the continental breakfast available in the lobby for $16 or full breakfast for $20. I did not elect either option but it would be convenient for some. Coffee in lobby in morning is free. Valet parking is $42 but you can find nearby overnight garage parking on for $25. Free WiFi in rooms but I did not use it so I do not know how good the signal is. Overall a good value for the amount charged for my Priceline stay ($89) and I would not be disappointed to get it on a future bid.

title: “Expected more from a Wyndham”
text: The hotel is pretty old - the rooms have that aged smell. The rooms' air conditioning is bad. My room had no electrical outlets. So I had to unplug some of my lights to plug my laptop and other chargers. They also had a water outage one day and in the evening when the water was restored, only muddy water came through the faucets. The American breakfast served in the restaurant was okay. The plus sides in this hotel are the free Internet and has free airport shuttle.

title: “Perfect Stay”
text: I enjoyed this very comfortable hotel. Stayed 3 nights in January 2006. Wonderful bed, wonderful view, friendly and professional staff. You can't beat the location and at any price it's a deal. I travel a lot and this was a perfect experience. Hope to stay again in April.

title: “Excellent Service and Very Friendly”
text: Some people recommended this hotel and we're glad they did. They had excellent service, the staff was very friendly, and it was very comfortable. It was very close to Union Square, which put us in the middle of where we wanted to be.

title: “Great location and service. But small rooms and no pool”
text:
The location is really nice. Walking distance to most of the attractions. Art museum is just across the street.
Service is really nice too. I worked in the lobby one night pretty late for a presentation ppt. The service person sent me ice water, peanuts and cookies to the sofa and table for free.
Room is pretty small. I traveled with my wife and my daughter (2.5 years) and my son (7 months). The room is too small. And there is no pool in this hotel.

title: “Super place to stay in San Antonio”
text: I was looking for the perfect hotel for a couple of days in San Antonio for a group of 11 people which included 6 adults and 5 children. I found it. Thanks to the reviews here(which were amazingly accurate) we had a great stay. The kids loved the roof top pool, the location was fabulous, the breakfast was great, all employees were polite and helpful. We used it as a base to explore downtown SA and did one day a Sea World. Could not have picked a better place. Reasonable rates for this quality of hotel at peak tourist season and the $18 per day for parking was well worth it. Valet service was quick and easy. Highly recommended.

title: “Smiling, helpful staff”
text: Each and every staff person, from the cleaning crew to the front desk, were exceedingly pleasant and helpful, offering to go the extra mile.
