I expected to find at least one who was rude or at least unhelpful, but that was not the case. BTW, my room was clean and beautiful, with a view of the outdoor courtyard. I would highly recommend staying at this Hilton.

title: “Amazing Viewes”
text:
Every time I visit Universal I stay at this Hilton, the staff has always been incredible and the same can be said for their rooms.
I had booked this room rather late, a week in advance. We had decided to see a concert at the Gibson Amphitheater. There is a free shuttle service the operates between the Hilton and Universal Studios/Citywalk and even if you have to walk it is not that far at all.
Even though we arrived a little after hotel check-in time, our room was not ready. So they gave us vouchers for the Lounge to get appetizers. The room was well worth waiting for, had a spectacular view from the 19th. floor.
Internet if offered for a small fee unless you are a gold or higher Honors card holder.

title: “Convenient location”
text:
We had a late flight into Seattle, so I picked the Radisson Hotel at the airport based on it's location. When we first arrived, we called the courtesy pick up service. The shuttle came after 10 min or so, and it wasn't a long wait. I didn't realized how close the hotel was. It's literally right outside of the airport, and you can walked there if you don't have too much luggage to carry. (To walk there, exit the airport on baggage claim level. Do not use the sky walk to get to the parking lot side. Once outside the airport, make a right, and walk out to International Blvd. The hotel is right across the street.)
We also rented a car. Parking is free, and we didn't have issue with finding a spot at night. 
The room is clean and decent size, standard hotel amenities. The shower head was new and water pressure was good. We actually used the pool and the hot tub. Both are clean, and the pool is big enough for lap swim.
The hotel bar/kitchen/room service closes at 11pm. If you are looking for food late at night (as we landed around midnight), 13 Coins, which is a 24 hour restaurant, is right next door that you can walk to. Food is actually pretty good there!
Overall, we had a pleasant stay at the Radisson. I'll definitely consider this hotel again.

title: “This is where you want to stay.”
text: The rooms were absolutely beautiful! The staff upgrades you whenever possible. The restaurant was fantastic. The staff was beyond terrific. Say hello to Steve at the front desk or Christopher. They will go out of thier way to make your stay great. I went with my son as a tiny vacation alone before he leaves for college. The staff (above) went out of thier way to make it comfortable for us by making sure we had two beds and even a balcony so we could hang out and talk. (priceless) I truely have never been happier with a hotel and I travel pretty often.

title: “Great bargain near Times Square”
text: While this isn't your typical Residence Inn (a converted apartment building, I suspect), it's clean, convenient and a bargain. The rooms are spacious by New York standards; ours had a sofabed, kitchenette, and a great view of lower Manhattan. The free breakfast was outstanding (but don't be late -- they close at exactly the advertised time). We did have an issue with our room not being cleaned until we called at 5 p.m. -- not sure what the problem was, but the maids were there within a minute of our call. There is sometimes a short wait for an elevator (all four never seemed to be in service at the same time). The front desk staff was friendly and efficient. There's a small grocery store a block away if you plan to make use of the kitchenette.

title: “Perfect location! Nice rooms!”
text: Great hotel!!! Awesome location!!! The suite is perfect for a family, we have 3 children and plenty of room! Drum bar is nice on the top level! The elevators were not as much of an issue as we had read. Clean rooms! Nice staff! Yummy donut/coffee bar in lobby!! Would stay here again for sure!!!!

title: “The people made it a great stay for my family”
text:
Beginning with the first class welcome from Monique until we departed 5 days letter it was a first class experience. Located a half a block from Union Station when you walk outside and see the Capitol 4 blocks up the street. The rooms are cozy, a little small but more than adequate for our family of 4, quite comfortable and tastefully decorated.
What really separated the hotel was the friendly professionalism of the staff. They were most supportive( you need all the help you can when you travel with twin 10 yr olds) and accomodating. We will definitely stay there again!!

title: “Highlight of our America Trip”
text: My Husband and I arrived at 10pm on Thanksgiving from a long flight from Australia. Check in was a breeze and arrived to our room to champagne and strawberrys. Thinking my husband was being thoughtful but it was from the girls at the front desk as they saw my birthday was approaching a really lovely gesture. We also managed to get a beautiful thanksgiving dinner on room service after we had a beautiful shower under the heavenly rain head. Room service meals were huge could have just shared one between us. I know other people had mentioned the rooms were small but they were not bad at all considering we were out sightseeing all the time. The rooms were warm and the beds super comfortable. Great bar downstairs to have a cocktail with a DJ to rest those weary bones after a long day. We can't wait to go back!

title: “GREAT”
text:
Tree at front desk was up on her customer service and made stay a pleasure. I ask for unusual information and she called me within 5 minutes with answer 
Breakfast was great, the gentleman attending it made sure one got whatever they wanted. 
When in Austin this will be where I stay

title: “Elegant hotel!!”
text: I stayed at the Majestic hotel in Chicago and I enjoyed it! The hotel lobby is very cozy and elegant. The staff is very friendly and helpful! I would higly reccommend this hotel to everyone who visits Chicago!!

title: “Great Location, Hotel not so much.!!!!”
text: Before leaving I read all the reviews before heading out on my trip and i have to admit that i went in expecting the worst. I prepared myself with my own sheets and a bottle of fabreeze. We check in a little early about 3:30 and our room was still not ready. We had to wait until 4pm to actually get the room. Finally alittle after 4pm our room was ready. We were put in room number 116. The sheets were clean and i was pleased to see the bathroom clean as well. Although it did smell in there, the carpet probably hasnt been changed in about 10 years and the curtains as well. The room was very little, i could of book a motel 6 for as little as the room was. The first night we got their they gave us complimentry passes to get on the boat cruise. We went on friday night at the 730 boarding and all it was is a cruise it had no music and no live entertainment as it stated. When i asked about the music. the attendent notified me that the music and live entertainment wouldnt start until 9pm which childern were not allowed on at that time. So i asked the attendent for 2 pens and some paper, she came back about 15 min later with one pen and a little piece of paper. So the kids were bored and i wouldnt reccommend the boat cruise for small childern although it was nice for adults. The first 2 night i got to sleep well but at the third night i think we got neighbors and it got very noisy, we could have been in the same room because that how close they sounded. The location is nice and i loved the heated pool and jucuzzi, although when traveling to seaworld again i wouldnt stay at this hotel, there are better hotels in the area for better prices. Bahia is not a resort and should be remodeled soon to have the resort in its name. I rate this hotel a 3 star hotel.

title: “Better than expected!!”
text: My husband and I celebrated our 40th wedding anniversary in NYC. We booked a concierge king room on the 25th floor overlooking 7th Ave. with a little view of Time Square. When we went inside our room, there was a surprise of juicy huge chocolate dipped strawberries. They were delicious!!!! The room was very clean, light and roomy. The bed was very comfy. The bathroom was a little small but very clean and well equipped with supplies and a hair dryer. The lobby is sort of art deco design. ALL the staff were exceptional. Anytime we asked for anything, our requests were immediately taken care of. Naomi & Drita were great. The bell hops could be more friendlier and attentive but we didn't have to deal much with them. You can't beat the location. Walking distance to so may attractions and I'm not even a big walker. Naomi even printed up our boarding passes for our flights the next day.. The only negative is that we were promised a refrigerator and never got one (they need to buy more) and the bar could use some nice music (maybe some jazz) in the evenings. Other than these small things, our trip couldn't be better. Some family members will be visiting NYC soon and I will surly make sure they stay here. Thank you Park Central for making our anniversary trip so special. We would return in a heartbeat.

title: “Convenient access to a wide variety of food.”
text: This no smoking hotel offers clean rooms with free wifi access. I stayed here for three nights on business in a King bed suite. My room had a microwave and mini-fridge. The A/C got my room ice cold. This room was a great value for the money spent. The "free" breakfast included cheese omelets with a meat rotated each day that included thick sliced ham or breakfast sausage during my stay. If you are a coffee gourmet the coffee here won't satisfy. I would stay here again because of the price I paid. I had no problem accessing area restaurants and didn't have to drive far to find great food values.

title: “No complaints...no raves...”
text:
This was an "average" hotel. it wasn't great, but it wasn't horrible either, and the location worked out well for what we were in town to do. Being next to an Outback was nice, too. There was another restaurant next door as well but we never went there.
The property seemed a little dated, but the room was fine and the staff was very nice (above average). We enjoyed impressive, fast, and speedy service at breakfast most mornings, too. The fitness center was empty every time I went there, and there was plenty of parking. I had a hard time sleeping there --- not sure if it was adjusting to the time change from the East Coast, or the horrible pillows they had!?
If I was headed back to town for another trip, I might end up back here again, but I'd take a look around and compare prices/options as well before I booked.

title: “Very nice!!”
text: We were very happy with this hotel. They upgraded us to a suite for some reason and it was very comfortable. There was quite a bit of noise with the bar/restaurant being in the center area, but it didn't bother us too much. The service was excellent, the staff was very helpful. Free parking was a big bonus. The location is great because it's really close to San Diego but it's also very nice to be close to Oceanside as well. We didn't find any problems while we stayed here. We'll be back!

title: “Lovely little hotel”
text:
A friend and I stayed here for 5 nights (20th April - 26th April) and were very pleased.
We stayed in room 601 which was a twin with private bathroom. Very clean and tidy. Fresh towels every day and bedroom was tidied and cleaned every day. Beds were very comfortable, a great place to get your head down after a tiring day of sight seeing and shopping! The lift was an experience and added to the character of the hotel. Staff were always very friendly and helpful.
One tiny little thing, I left a packet of chocolate covered doughnuts on the bedside table and the following day I noticed that "something" had been nibbling them! I can only guess it was a mouse! 
Location of hotel was fab, 2 blocks away from the Empire State and not far from Macey's or Times Square. I am defintelty going to visit NYC again and I would definitely stay at Hotel 31 again - I will just make sure I eat all the doughnuts next time!!!!!!!

title: “Good value and comfort”
text: The Hotel Tomo is a great value in a city that has a tendency toward great hotel expense. The rooms are large and comfortable. The location is within walking distance of some of the great up and coming restaurant and shop locales and BART is a short bus ride away. Staff is excellent -- our assigned room had a small problem, and when I brought it to staff's attention, we were immediately reassigned. The room was large, clean, and well-furnished with excellent wi-fi connections.

title: “Okay”
text: Despite the clean rooms and friendly staff, I wouldn't recommend anybody to stay here. I have no complaints of the hotel itself. It's a no frills hotel that suits its purpose. There were four guys in our party staying in 2 rooms for one night as part of a golf trip. Many reviews said people felt unsafe staying here. While we didn't feel unsafe, this definitely is not the nicest part of town. Here's what we saw just to give you an idea. Many of the houses in the surrounding neighborhoods have all of the windows and doors barred. The grocery store across the street had all of their hard alcohol locked up in a cage and we had to have a clerk get it for us. There were quite a few sketchy looking citizens walking around after dark. On the morning we left, there was a cop driving around the parking lot dressed in a bullet proof vest. We watched him stop a kid who appeared to be breaking into a truck in the parking lot. During the night, there is a security guard on site who ventures around the hotel so we did feel okay about leaving our vehicle and golf clubs in the parking lot. If you need to visit this area for any reason, I would recommend staying either closer to the airport, further west of Phoenix, or further north of this area. The extra 15 minutes of drive time is well worth it.

title: “Great Value and Location in Pricey Boston”
text:
The Holiday Inn Select Boston - Government Center is a large, boutique-style hotel that offers good accommodations within reasonable walking distance of many sights in central Boston. The standard rooms are standard fare, with no surprises either on the upside or the downside. There are executive levels on the 12th and 14th floors. Views toward the front of the hotel are superior than those to the rear, which face a part of the medical complex that is under construction. That said, the immediate area offers nothing particularly spectacular. The hotel's restaurant offers a breakfast buffet at $12.95 that is decent. We found housekeeping to be adequate and the hotel staff cooperative, though unrushed. 
The hotel's best attributes include its location, which places visitors within walking distance of much of historic Boston. We found our most common routings to be through the city hall plaza and also up Joy Street to the Boston Common. Charming Charles Street is also a nice walk in the neigborhood. Best neighborhood restaurant: Antonio's, an Italian place that you'll see less than two blocks down toward the overhead T track on the other side of the main drag. It's a small, 23-table dandy and you'll see the people lined up outside. 
The hotel is an outlet for Red Trolley tour tickets, one of several hop-on, hop-off trolley operations in the city. The tour provides a good orientation to the city, but we found ourselves more than happy to walk after getting our bearings. 
Noteworthy is that we were able to book the Holiday Inn Select using Priority Club points at 15K/night, which is an exceptional deal when you consider the avoided cost involved. (It is difficult to book decent hotel rooms outside of Priceline in Boston at less than $150/night, plus a stiff room tax.) 
We would definitely be willing to book this hotel again, but it's important for people to understand that hotels in Boston are just plain pricey. Comparing a $150-$250/night room here against what might be expected in a less costly destination leaves some people feeling that they should have been getting more. The Holiday Inn Select Boston - Government Center is a solid choice and a decent value, but it is not an exceptional property in any particular respect.

title: “Dated but decent, middle of the road hotel.”
text:
I stayed here a couple nights on business. when i checked in, very late due to a delayed flight, they only had one smoking room left YUK!! I was very disapointed though they did all they could to make it smell ok. The fan from the heat/ac unit was very loud! I had to shut the door to the bedroom for some quiet. I was moved the next day to a non-smoking room but not offered any sort of amenity for my inconveience.
Pros: large rooms. Nice hot and free breakfast. Room service was really good, fast, friendly. Pizza looked good as well. The swans were a nice feature and not something you see often. Good in room coffee - better than most other hotels. Gym was ok. Cardio equip/treadmills are super old and clunky.
Cons: Noisy hotel. Lots of kids in the hallways late. One elevator broken. No stairway alternative. Internet was not free but was a decent speed. So-so in room bathroom amenities. Bathroom was very tight, and i'm a small person!

title: “Nothing special here...”
text: We needed to stay near the airport and driving back from Spokane, we looked for a couple of rooms using internet booking sites. This place did have 2 rooms available, a 3-star rating and an indoor pool, so we booked. The staff was most unhelpful. The TV in the lobby was blaring cartoons - I asked the person at the desk if we could turn the TV down as no one was watching and he said he was watching... my mistake, I thought he was supposed to be helping me! The stay was okay, the rooms so-so, and I just don't see how this place gets a 3-star rating.

title: “Wonderful experience at the Flatotel!”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Flatotel over the July 4th weekend. We had a wonderful experience! We were greeted by the doorman the second we stepped out of our taxi. The outstanding front desk attendant checked us in with a warm hospitable welcome and was extremely helpful. Our hotel room was very well appointed and the bed was lush, plush and super comfortable – pure heaven! Our room was exceptionally clean and updated. The housekeeping staff was very friendly and paid close attention to detail. The Midtown location was perfect to check out the city scene and in walking distance to many NYC favorites. The service in the restaurant was very good and the lounge area was relaxing with a great vibe! I would highly recommend staying at the Flatotel if you are planning a trip to the Big Apple! We can’t wait to return one day soon!

title: “Always a Pleasure!”
text:
The St. Anthony Hotel has the friendliest and most accomodating staff I've ever experienced in a hotel. From the comfortable bed to the amazing room service food - no joke - I had the best stuffed Quail on the planet. The last day we wanted to leave the hotel for brunch and the concierge was kind enough to recommend a restaurant in another hotel and it was fantastic. 
Superb service and well worth every penny spent on the room - which was incredibly reasonable for location, even though it is not on the riverwalk, it really doesn't matter becuase you are a short block away. My favorite place to stay in San Antonio!

title: “Pet stays for free!”
text:
We live in San Diego and decided to do a short staycation on a whim. My husband decided to book a hotel last minute through hotwire and we got lucky with Hotel Indigo for about $130 for a Saturday night. We didn't have any intentions to take our 4 1/2 year old puggle with us, but once we saw that she could stay for FREE (NO additional pet fee like most other hotels) she convinced us that she should come along for her first hotel stay. From the moment we arrived to the moment we left, the staff, especially SERGIO, was very friendly and made Gigi's first hotel stay so much fun. 
As far as the room, you can't beat the size for being in downtown. 
RATINGS: Cleanliness was 4 only because of a bit of dust. We informed the front desk, but decided it didn't bother us to the point that it needed to be taken care of. Sleep Quality got a 4 only because a loud car drove by late at night that could be heard even on 11th floor, beds were extremely comfortable so that made up for it.
FLOOR: Laminate wood with an area rug.
BED: Very comfortable, inbetween firm and soft. Pillows are very soft and fluffy. Gigi liked to hide under the bed so make sure you check under the beds for lost items.
BATHROOM: Spacious with a Large shower (no tub). 1 sink with plenty of counter space. Aveda bath products are provided.
VIEW: Floor to ceiling windows to admire the city view.
ETC: Nice LG tv, but no mini fridge. iHome dock in room too.
SUPER pet friendly! Gigi was able to go to the 9th floor and see the bar/lounge, grass patch, eat breakfast with us in their restaurant, and she got to run through the hallway. Petco Park's Park at the Park is only a 3 minute walk from the hotel which was open for her to take care of business and socialize with other dogs too. 
This hotel has APPLE products in the lobby :)
REGRETS: Didn't get to try any happy hour specials...maybe next time!
Starbucks, Basic (for pizza and they deliver to the hotel too), 7-11, Quizno's are all on the same block as the hotel. Lotus Thai, Tavern & Bowl (drink and bowl), The Corner (burgers) all "just across the sreet" from the hotel. 5 minute walk will get you to Heavenly cupcakes (but the run late at night, so go early) where you can get cupcakes for yourself and your dog.

title: “Loved the Valencia”
text: I had a great stay with my husband. We had a romantic getaway. The staff, service and food was excellent. I would reccommend to anyone wanting to stay on the quieter end of the Riverwalk!

title: “Great hotel!”
text: This hotel was in the best location, the best value for the money and I would highly recommend it. Within steps of all the monuments and museums and if we didn't feel like walking there was always a cab there for us. Room was clean, bed was comfortable and we got the view of the Patomic which was a nice bonus. Hotel was going through some remodeling but we didn't have any issues with noise or dust. Staff was very nice and the restaurants in the hotel were good. I would stay in this hotel again!

title: “Very Good for the price.”
text: Good inexpensive hotel. If you are in Austin for business, you'll find anything you need at a good price: free wifi, free business center, laundry, microwave oven in room and free coffee.

title: “Great stay!”
text: This is the ideal place if your planning a trip to Sea World! It's just down the street, and even better, a free shuttle to take you to and from for FREE! Parking alone is $40 at Sea World. And the restaurant next to the Holiday Inn was great, perfect stay!

title: “What a pleasant surprise!”
text: We recently stayed two nights at the Doubletree Del Mar booked through Expedia. When we arrived we were promptly greeted. Without asking, we were upgraded to the Horton Suite, in the southwest corner of the building, top floor. (5th floor) (IMO the nicest suite in the Hotel) For $145 a night, this suite was the size of two standard rooms with two large flat screen tv's, two phones, and a king size bed that was excellent to sleep on with extra pillows. The room was bright with great views to the south and west (ocean), a great view of the pool area, quiet, and more than spacious. The HVAC had two separate controls that promptly heated and cooled the space while not being too loud. Our stay included the breakfast buffet for two which was great . . . . It had all the things I would expect for a hearty breakfast as well as low fat and/or vegetarian options, if preferred. We may not get the same room again, but I would definately consider staying at the Doubletree Del Mar again if in the area. What a great value for the money.

title: “Good deal”
text:
Checked in on July 26th, the front desk staff were always helpful, easy to deal with. The free buffet breakfast is always a plus for any overnight stay for us. Hotel was easy to find, parking was always available & free for guests. You have everything you will need, hairdryer, microwave & mini ref. 
I chose the place because it was centrally located to where we were going, 30 minutes from Lego in Grapevine and 30 minutes from Rockwall & the airport. Just one thing, the fire alarm went off on the 26th from 12midnight to 1am, they said there was a technical problem. It was not the front desk's fault, I hope that has been resolved. 
All in all, we had a good deal for a 4 night stay in Dallas.

title: “Value for money”
text:
My wife and I always enjoy big city vacations and we are not that much in the hotel. This hotel was perfect for a big city trip.
3-4 blocks on 5th street from marketstreet.
If you are very sensitive to street noise there was a little at times, but we do not mind and can sleep from anything.
Again for the amount we paid, I think this was truly worth the money.
Extra plus was the very nice guy in the reception, who helps with everything!
NB. free internet and PARKING

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: Sopped over here for a few nights and it was an excellent experience. Sam the Manager was amazing and treated us like royalty, (something other hotel I have stayed in could take heed of!) When the shuttle was not available this guy took time out to run us into town in his own car. That's service! Will definatly recommend to others and also hope to return on a personal trip next time. Thanks to George the barman, Maria and Cindy on reception who was so helpful with check in, printing etc. Rooms were perfect and had everything needed for both buisness and personal stop over. Thanks again

title: “Fun Hotel and Great Meeting”
text: I stayed at the W for four days last week. I was hosting a medical advisory board. The hotel is beautiful and very modern. All of my participants got great rooms. We were conducting a training session with several demands for special items. The hotel staff helped us on every occasion. Everyone who worked at the hotel was very friendly. Even the maintenance workers that I encountered said hello and seemed to be happy to be there. The hotel is definitely well run and cares about its guests. My meeting participants were impressed. I would definitely have another business meeting here. I have seen some of the comments about the Hollywood scene, but that is actually what makes it fun. Nice difference from stuff business hotels where I stay way too often.

title: “Good experience”
text:
Though the hotel is not located in downtown LA, there is a large shopping mall nearby (within 5-minutes walking distance) and with many high-quality restaurants and food court. 
Good swimming pool and fitness center and good in-room dining service. I also like the Starbucks here and if you are a Hyatt Diamond/Platinum member, you have free Starbucks coupons as well!

title: “I'll come back again!r”
text: The localization is perfect, the rates are inexpensive. I'll come back! The only thing that is awful is the elevator system. It takes a long time to arrive, along time to close the doors , but it's ok...

title: “Best kept secret”
text: Stayed with two adult sons and absolutely adored this hotel. The room was excellent- well equipped and very spacious. The small kitchenette has everything you need for a longer stay. The location is fantastic. Fairly close to everything we needed. We were very impressed with this hotel and I don't think the website does it justice. I recommend this hotel. It definitely exceeded our expectations.

title: “New York was fabulous ,hotel was not”
text: Rooms are big but very dark and dingy and being on a lower floor made it even worse.The window blind got stuck halfway when we 1st opened it stayed like that for 2 days till i left a note to ask if it could be fixed.The ironing board went up but couldnt get it down again for fear of chopping my fingers off.The kitchen was useless ,no kettle to make a cuppa ,you have to either boil a pan on the stove which takes ages or risk being scalded by putting full cups in the microwave which was high up . No toaster , No where to eat with a knife and fork as there is only one chair at the oversized desk and one heavy armchair on the other side of the room.Oversized fridge which has a mini bar in ,but dont touch anything as it is grossly over priced We were there for 6 days for a family wedding so needed to style my hair on the day only to find the hairdryer completely useless as it only had a 10" flex ,i ended up on my knees on the bathroom floor with no mirror so i wasnt best pleased .4 lifts available but only ever one in use so took ages to get up and down .Far too expensive per night did not enjoy our stay there at all .we booked 10 months in advance and all our requests in emails were ignored .Expected far more basics and luxury from the USA, but were very disappointed, certainly would not stay there again.

title: “Close to marina, airport, short ride to downtown”
text: Very nice hotel almost walking distance from the airport with a surprisingly beautiful setting near the marina. Service was typical/good for a well run large hotel.

title: “Great location!”
text: This hotel is in the perfect location in the middle of times square with the subway literally just steps by the front door. Our experience was great! Check in took less than 5 min. The concierge (sp) was wonderful in planning things to do (show tickets, dinner reservations, etc). I highly recommend!!

title: “Nice place”
text: Everything I am writing here have to be taken in the context of New York. Having said that, this is an awesome place. The rooms are very large (by NY standards), clean, with nice furniture and great view. The Internet is $15 for 24 hours and if you are not a HHonors member the Bfast is $28, a little high but again considering that this is NY and the food is pretty good, not a bad deal. If you are on the budget or not sure about spending $30 for food early in morning, there is an Applebee's in the lobby at street level and a McDonald's next door. The location is great for site seeings, theater district and restaurants. Also, there are 2 Subway stations near by, on 42nd and 8th Ave and 42nd with 7th Ave. The staff is pretty friendly and helpful. The TVs are nice with HDTV. The only complaint I have is the channel selection; if you are a news junkie and like me and like MSNBC, you will be disappointed because they do not have that channel. I really miss the Countdown with Keith Olbermann....

title: “Worst Experience Ever”
text: I had the most worse experience one can have. I was traveling with a large number of colleagues and we selected Extended Stay America, Fort Worth as the manager agreed to give us special rates. However, as it turned out, their manager (Miss Trish) hooked us up on a much higher rate than the hotel's normal rate and had kept her personal commission. When i learned about the Fraud, she tried to shut me up by calling my boss and threatened to file a harassment case against me. Thank God we some how got rid of her. So, my advise to u is 'rooms r smelly and small + the manager is corrupt, so beware...!'

title: “Fantastic experience”
text: Fantastic hotel with great staff and perfect location.. We just cant wait to return

title: “Perfect for our family”
text: Just returned from Affinia Shelburne. Spent two nights with husband and three children. Great location, great space in the rooms, and excellent staff. Upon arrival we were greeted warmly by the doorman and the front desk staff (Andy) was wonderfully welcoming and warm. We arrived on a Thursday evening and enjoyed the managers reception. The next day we recieved the same warm and helpful service from the rest of the staff, housekeeping to front desk. Have traveled often with our children and this was the most comfortable and welcoming hotel and staff we have experienced.

title: “Great location, average rooms, strange Fairmont Gold building”
text:
The location is great - 10 minute walk from either blue or orange lines, adjacent to the North End, and right on the water. I was oddly "upgraded" to the strange Fairmont Gold outbuilding of sorts. Supposedly, this equals a higher standard of service or something. First, the private entrance with no doorperson made me feel less than safe. Yes, the complimentary snacks and breakfast were pretty awesome, but my room was not. It was small, there was no bathtub, the bedspread was pilly and worn, and a lot of things in the room were dusty - particularly the platform the bed was sitting on. The mattress was smaller than the platform - and the platform had lint, dust, leaves etc. very visible around right at the foot of the bed.
The service in the restaurant was great, but the food itself, aside from the awesome bread, was disappointing. Maybe I ordered the wrong thing... but I really suspect this to be a Boston thing. It looks like a lot of restaurants in Boston are throwing ahi tuna, burrata and truffle oil on random dishes these days, and it doesn't always work.

title: “Very Good Location for D.C.”
text:
I stayed at this hotel from 6/13-6/17 and the location was excellent. It was close to everything. I easily walked to the White House and all of the Smithsonian Museums. Chinatown was only 5 blocks away. The Convention Center was a mere 15 minute walk.
The hotel staff were nice, although I found that the cleaning staff was MORE nice if you gave them a tip. After I did that, they gave me 6 bottles of shampoo and 6 bags of tea in my room. 
The noise level was ok. I was on the 11th floor, but the street noise in the mornings were loud. I didn't have many neighbors, so it was mostly quiet. I did wear earplugs, as usual, so my opinion may be flawed. 
I was on a conference rate at $295 per night, so it was steep. But, the location was definitely the best. Safe neighborhood too. Rooms were nice and clean. Bed were excellent and soft with down comforters and pillows. Bathrooms were a good size. No refrigerator though. Rooms included: flat-screen TV, 2 queen beds, 1 dresser, 1 desk, and 1 sofa chair. Bathrooms had regular amenities (Bath and Body Works), hair dryer, coffee maker, etc. No shower caps though.

title: “Sophisticated, Friendly & Fun”
text: Staying at The Bowery Hotel was a treat. It was pricey, but I enjoyed my visit immensely and recommend this hotel wholeheartedly. The room was immaculate: clean, bright and welcoming, with lovely views of the East Village. The hotel remains faithful to its period architecture and design, without sacrificing any modern amenities. It was so quiet in the mornings, but in the evenings the absolutely gorgeous main areas were bustling with activity. Every member of the staff I encountered was attentive and very friendly. The location is ideal for exploring the East & West Villages, NoHo, SoHo, etc. The only complaint I had was less than perfect service at adjoining restaurant Gemma: while the food and atmosphere was delightful, I felt rushed to order (brunch). Our waitress hovered, as if waiting for us to finish, but ignored our empty coffee cups. With so many wonderful eateries within a short walk, The Bowery should work a little harder to make Gemma their hotel guests’ dining destination.

title: “Nice location”
text: This hotel really was in a perfect location. We were very close to the Blue Line to and from the airport which saved us $30 per way getting to and from the airport. The Blue Line is only $2.50 each way. The views were spectacular from our room on the 22nd floor. The rooms were nice and clean. The staff was very friendly and very eager to help in any way. The bar had great night views of the river and downtown. Take in the views at night with a cocktail, just wonderful!! There were a few cons though. The free wifi was terrible. Out of the 3 of us staying in our room, no one was able to access the wifi for more then a few seconds at a time ANYWHERE in the hotel. It's a min of $5 to use the hotel computers which is only for the first few minutes, then you pay per minute after that, not to mention if you need to print anything, that's an additional $.50 per page to print. The elevator was broke the entire time on our floor. We would have to first go up a few floors just to get back down to the lobby which for some reason confused every person who were in the elevator with. The restaurant was a bit pricy for what you got. Overall, it was a nice stay!

title: “Reasonable stay but off the mark for me”
text:
We stayed 4 nights in The Carlyle Suites, booked mainly for the kitchenette - a useful feature to have when travelling with 2 small children. We had a pretty good rate for our room from Expedia. The room was roomy, 2 comfortable double beds, HDTV, a 2 seater sofa & 2 chairs, short coffee table, free wifi. Kitchenette had microwave, stove, toaster, coffee maker, full set of cooking set, cutlery and utensils. Washer/dryer was $1 per cycle each. Safeway supermarket was a block away. The front desk has restaurant menus to order with delivery to the hotel. 
But it was just off the mark for us: 
Maybe it was the black/white 70s art decor theme that i thought was dated or the thin carpeting in the room or that there was no bathtub in the room. 
Perhaps it was the officious "welcome" i received. I felt like I met with an immigration official instead of a hotel front desk. She asked me several questions: "how many in your party, you need a crib? how old is your baby?" weren't these already in the reservation and what's with the tone? do i owe you something?
It was more likely because i was being charged $20 for the baby crib. I'd earlier called to request for a crib and received a no problem. now the official at the front desk told me, "if you want the crib it is $20." i asked, "$20 for the stay?" she said, "per night, ma'am. so do you want the crib? at least i told you first." that's it. i totally regretted my choice of hotel even with the kitchenette. i didn't need the attitude - now i know i owed her $80. I would've left but there wouldn't be anywhere for me to go at this last minute at a cheaper rate. 
So that added $80 to our stay, which no longer made the rate 'pretty good'. This was really the frist time being charged for a baby crib. Shouldn't the crib be part of the service? Where would the baby sleep - on the bed and roll off? i can understand charging for a roll-away - extra linens, extra service to make the bed, extra towels for extra person etc. but a crib? I felt robbed. And it wasn't even a crib. It was a Graco playpen which takes 2 min to snap together, came with a blanket but no pillow (good thing we brought our own). it also came with an insect glue trap (maybe a good gesture so the insects get trapped before getting to the crib) that already had 2 dead insects trapped on it!! it was disgusting! i threw the insect trap away immediately. 
I have to say that the rest of the staff that i met in the evening were much nicer and very helpful. Despite a reasonably comfortable stay, I will not go back to the hotel. I would've traded off the kitchenette for another hotel with a better welcoming attitude and would not charge for a crib. 
At check-out while paying for the miscellaneous crib charge, I registered my surprise at being charged for a crib when other hotels don't normally charge for one. I received a shrug - amazing, they don't have an answer for the charge? The hotel should reconsider its $20/night policy for a crib or indicate $20 for the crib in the website and maybe inform the hotel staff a reason to give as an answer. Any answer is better than a shrug.

title: “Disastrous Service”
text: Well, this is one hotel I won't be staying at again. I was woken at 0200 one night by revellers in the hotel pool (closes at 2200) and had to go down to the front desk to complain. The following morning I talked to the acting manager - who sympathised and said that measures would be taken. However, the next night it happened again! This time the night manager was not so cooperative and it took 30 mins to clear the pool - and the noise. There are so many similarly priced options here, this is one to miss.

title: “Good hotel, pricey parking”
text:
We stayed three nights at Homewood Suites (DC) last summer, and we're going to stay three nights there this summer. As you can guess, we really like the hotel. First, of course, every room is a suite, which is important for us--our kids have special diets and we have to cook for them ourselves. A kitchen (or kitchenette) is almost mandatory for us. Ours was very clean and well-maintained. The rooms weren't big or anything, acceptably sized. The strong points for us were the following:
0) Easy access to The Mall, both by subway and by cab.
1) Friendly staff: Two things stick out; First, I'd left two of my bags (heavy-ish) in our car; the parking attendant helped my wife carry them to my room. Of course, the fact the we'd generously tipped him a few minutes before for parking of our car certainly helped ;-) Second, after we returned home we discovered that I'd dropped the keys to my other car at the hotel. The front desk people promptly Fedexed it back to us (at our charge, of course).
10) Easy access to Whole Foods; we walked the couple of blocks everyday for kitchen needs & dinner for the adults.
11) Generally decent neighborhood, although the route we took to get to the hotel went through some seedy neighborhoods. We saw police offers stop and frisk some young men on the street; this was rush hour on a weekday, about 4 miles from the hotel.
100) Coin-op washers and dryers.
Negatives:
101) Expensive parking! About $35 a night. That's the price you pay for convenience.
110) Bed's were OK, not great--I hate hotel pillows in general

title: “a delight!”
text: The Chelsea Pines Inn was an excellent place to stay in every way. Perhaps the most notable aspect of this charming hotel is the delightful staff. Everyone we met was friendly and very willing to go the extra mile to be helpful. Moreover, the hotel was sparkling clean and tastefully decorated, the location can't be beat and the breakfasts were excellent. This place is much more personable than your average hotel; but more casual and enjoyable than staying in a prissy bed and breakfast. I would highly recommend this place to anyone visiting New York for any purpose.

title: “Absolutely beautiful! Can't wait to go back!”
text: We booked this hotel via Hotels.com and chose the std no view room. After staying one night we decided to ask how much it would be to upgrade to a bay front room. We were quoted an extra $45 per night for the same room we had but on the bay. We loved it and thought it was a great deal! So nice to walk out your door onto the sand. There was a fire pit right in front of our room and after a quick trip to the grocery store to get smores making supplies and wood we enjoyed the evening on the beach in front of a fire. Our kids had the time of their lives swimming in the gorgeous pool, doing the mini putt golf course and building sand castles on the beach. The $25 parking fee stinks but oh well, all San Diego hotels charge exhorborant parking fees. We also brought our own small coffeepot and took our coffee out to walk on the beach in the mornings. No need to even leave this resort. We came to relax and take advantage of the resort offerings and activities. Newly renovated rooms are gorgeous! Super clean, freshly painted with wonderful tile floors and beautiful furniture. We can't wait to go back- we miss our ocean paradise already!

title: “Nice Nice and Nice!”
text: On Union Square, amazing location, good service, great room, wonderful view from the restaurant. I don't have anything else to say but RECOMMENDED! Much better than Westin St Francis. ;)

title: “Good Value”
text: Stayed two nights. Our room was a little small but really you're only there to sleep so don't need a lot of space. The property and room was incredibly clean and appeared to be fairly recently renovated. We appreciated being close to the subway line and relatively close to the main sights. There are plenty of restaurants nearby, but only tried the gourmet pizza place across the street. Very good. Breakfast was a nice bonus as well. I would definitely stay again or try one of the other Apple Core properties.

title: “Incomparable service at Four Seasons Denver”
text: We loved this hotel from the moment we arrived. The hotel itself is sleek and beautiful, centrally located in downtown Denver. We were upgraded to a corner room and had tons of natural light streaming in with great views of all the action downtown. THE BED! Wow, it's unbelievably comfortable, I never wanted to get out of it! All the amenities that one would expect from an upscale hotel ( especially loved the freestanding huge tub that sat underneath a huge window) The workout area and spa are top notch and a pleasure to visit every day. The rooftop pool was gorgeous and had it not been raining we definitely would have been hanging out there. All that said, the best thing about Denver Four Seasons was the service!!!!They did not miss a thing. They were spot on throughout our 4 day stay....front desk, valet and courtesy service ( loved all those guys!) room service, housekeeping. All just impeccable. We will stay again and again.

title: “NO SECURITY IN THE PARKING LOT”
text: I stayed a night great room..!VERY NOISY NEIGHBORS!.WATCH out if you park your car right next to the front entrance, my truck was broken into and no one was around not even security on the premises. Management is absurd! Supposedly they have security?? Well he must have been the one(s) that broke into my vehicle... DON'T LEAVE ANYTHING IN YOUR CAR!

title: “Fabulous City, Great Hotel”
text:
My fiance and I went to Chicago for some Christmas shopping and sightseeing in November 2011. It was the most wonderful City with fabulous people, so friendly.
I will keep this short, but all in all it's a great hotel, brilliant location close to everything you need. If you are after good pizza then come out of the hotel and turn left, keep walking until you get to Pizano's, you won't be disappointed. 
T.J (doorman) is a credit to the hotel, so helpful and he excels at his job. We found all of the staff to be great. 
Be sure to do the John hancock observatory and eat at the Cheesecake Factory (both a 5/10 min walk away) Also make sure you visit Navy Pier and go up the Willis Tower.
The only reason I didn't rate the hotel as excellent is because I didn't try the food. 
Book it and have fun, we certainly did. Can't wait to return.

title: “I hate to post this - but, pls beware of bedbugs”
text: I enjoyed my stay. Cannot say anything negative about the hotel. However - I feel compelled to share that shortly after I returned home, I had bedbugs in my apartment. I have contacted Holiday Inn Priority Club mgmnt to let them know. I recommend thoroughly searching your room for bugs if you stay here. Bugs can be caught anywhere. I cannot 100% state that the bugs were picked up in this hotel. But I feel as though it is the most obvious place for me to have encountered them. I stayed here and 1 other Holiday Inn hotel (Long Island City) during Sept./Oct. No other trips. Therefore, I probably picked up bugs here or @ Long Island City. Both hotels NEED to conduct a bedbug inspection and then post the results of their findings on TripAdvisor. Having bedbugs in your home is been mentally, physically, and monetarily exhausting.

title: “Not much more than average here...”
text: Hotel staff were extremely friendly and helpful - room was clean and adequately furnished with the standards - this is an "old style" hotel (1 story, external entrance, park at your door) that my wife and I almost drove right by in order to stay at the much "nicer from the outside" Holiday Inn right next door - however, we were relieved after our stay that we didn't let our first impression of the facility turn us away from it - the property is well-maintained - landscaping is well-groomed - breakfast was the standard "continental" (danishes, cereal, waffle iron) - pool was small, but clean - internet connection (not wireless) from port in room was fantastic speed - hotel is an easy 5 minute drive from the San Antonio Missions ballpark

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
My friend and I spent March 26-29 at the Belvedere. The room was excellent, very clean and plenty of room. The staff was outstanding, every member we encountered was friendly and went out of their way to help you. I would definitely recommend the Belvedere to anyone visiting NYC. I have stayed at several other places and there was no comparison. 
Also, within walking distance of bus lines, time square and many other places to visit. They also let us store our luggage since our departure time was after checkout for no charge. Great place! Will stay with them on my next visit.

title: “Excellent location”
text:
Good place to stay with excellent location. I found the staff to be very helpful and friendly I wanted to purchase some ugg boots but didn't know where to get them from, the staff went on Internet for me and wrote the shops and addresses down in closest order.
The room was quite basic but there's that much to do in NY you only want to shower and sleep
Overall good place to stay

title: “All Around Enjoyable”
text:
I stayed at Gild Hall in NYC this past weekend. The experience was excellent and the service was fantastic. Will definitely stay there again! I will list the pros and cons of this fabulous hotel:
Pros:
- Excellent front desk service and response to requests from my room
- Gorgeous decor 
- The most comfortable bed and sheets I have slept in at a hotel ... ever.
- Fantastic water pressure and excellent lighting in the bathroom for make-up
- Quiet location
Cons
- $15/day for internet service and $20+ cab fares to go uptown
- Doors to bathroom are clear/blurred, so if sharing a room, make sure you know them well
- Rate went up $100 / night from Friday night to Saturday night

title: “Convenience with character!”
text:
We just got back home after staying at Kings Inn from 3/7/05 to 3/10/05 and enjoyed our time there. The price we found was great ($60/night) and the location was right in the middle of San Diego and close to everything. 
The hotel staff were courteous and polite and saw to our needs and our room faced the pool, so there was no audible highway noise. There was, however, a loud water noise whenever the neighbors took a shower. There is plenty of parking here and easy access to your rooms. 
However, security is not the best & that can't be avoided for this kind of hotel. Each night expect to get pizza ad slipped under your door by unscrupulous people that the hotel recommends you avoid...these pizza places have no address & up to a $7 delivery charge.
They have 2 restaurants on-site. One mexican, and one breakfast place (The Waffle Spot). We had breakfast there on our first morning in San Diego and it was ok...nothing to write home about. The decor was interesting at best, and the waffles were about average. The service was poor.
They have a unique pool surrounded by all the rooms and a jacuzzi. The pool hours end early at 10pm and for some reason the heated-pool was on the cold side. Stay in the jacuzzi. 
If you enjoy a retro look and value your money, this is the hotel for you. When considering the price, they rate 5/5 stars.

title: “Perfect in every way”
text: My adult daughter and I spent 3 nights at this hotel. It was perfect in every way. Location - great to be so close to Union Station, Postal Museum and Capitol Building within eyesight. Rooms were delightful and beds were fit for a princess. Bathroom great - I was happy to be able to use the small sewing repair kit! We only ate at the restaurant once and that was fine, but nothing exceptional. It is a pub restaurant so delivered what we expected.There is a really nice place to have breakfast or lunch just around the corner, (turn left as you exit the hotel) and plenty of eating places in the station complex. Safe deposit box in the room was a huge bonus as was the free internet/wireless access. Close to circulator bus stop which was great for our trip to Georgetown. I would recommend this hotel and I would look forward to staying there again if I ever travel to DC again. I got a good rate by using Hotwire secret deals.

title: “The Twilight Zone”
text: After the first 15 minutes, we knew we had made a big mistake. We asked (via phone during booking) if we were close enough to walk to the Riverwalk, and were told that we were " just 5 minutes away." Yeah, 5 minutes away....by car! Nothing and I repeat nothing looked like the pictures on the website. No microwaves, no refrigerators, no Internet, broken phone, I could go on and on. We attempted to address these issues with management, and were told (quite rudely) that nothing could/would be done. After about 45 minutes of this, we were ready to checkout. When we attempted to do so, we were told of a 72 hr group cancellation policy (which was not previously discussed nor posted anywhere), and that we would still be charged for the entire 3-day stay. That's when the fireworks truly began! They called the police. The police agreed with US!! Need I say more? I would not recommend this location to anyone....friend or foe.

title: “Decent Hotel for a heavy sleeper”
text:
We stayed three nights at the hotel, and while the hotel was, on average, good, there are a few things that bring it down.
First off, it's the rooms. They older, but seemed to be remodeled recently, and are in good shape. But you'll hear anything in other rooms around you, including the hallway.
I'm a light sleeper, and had a hard time getting to sleep without taking a sleeping pill. Even then, the windows are only single-pane overlooking the parking areas, so you'll hear anyone walking by or cars. 
The other problem was with the concierge. A concierge is supposed to be the one taking care of reservations for you. That's the whole point. We wanted to book a sightseeing trip in the bay, and he was at a loss on details. "I think this one is pretty nice", he says about the SECOND company he calls. (The first one he gave up on after they didn't answer the phone.)
I also asked him about tickets to Balboa park attractions, and he proceeded to Google it, while on hold. Then promptly forgot. Never got back to us, or mentioned it again. 
The breakfast included in some stays is pretty limited. Cubed pineapple? Really?
All in all, it's a great location and lots of parking, so it just comes down to if you're a light sleeper or expect more than a place to stay at night.

title: “Absolute luxury”
text: The hotel was perfect for our wedding night. The rooms were unbelievable and the area was quiet. I would recommend to anyone I know.

title: “Great place to stay in Boston”
text: Perfection! We really enjoyed the location with our rooms overlooking the public gardens. And all the usual four seasons wonders are definitely present at this hotel.

title: “AMAZING”
text:
OK so we pulled up to this hotel and all we saw were..... 40+ yr old men playing golf. my friend and I (both 21) came for vacation and weren't feeling it. we were so wrong! i would not have wanted it any other way. yes, it was far (30 mins) away from Downtown and all the 'happening' areas,but that was fine. the resort has such a big property we found so much to do on it and meet new ppl (when we did bump into anyone younger than 40 we would get so excited and both us and them would get all excited like "omg! someone under 40!") we had a good laugh but as the weekend went on, younger ppl came there. (for weddings etc). theyre rly friendly here, and its super relaxing with adult pools (no kids) family pool and then a special pool just for those who are at the spa. oh, and a HUGE golf course.
overall, my experience was wonderful - if youre looking to party every night in DT , this might not be the place for you (we went there once - cab ONE way is about 80$... )
if youre here to relax and maybe drop down to DT one during your visit, this place is perfect.
enjoy!

title: “Fabulous Experience”
text: The hotel is perfect from beginning to end! I've stayed here several times during visits with my daughter who attends school in DC, and I'm always amazed and pleased with the friendliness of the staff, the high level of service and the 5 star accomodations. This trip we stayed in room 1039, and when I walked in the door all I could say was WOW! I recall commenting to my husband, "I'm not easy to impress, but this is really nice." My trips to DC have included stays at the W, the Ritz and the Hilton. The Palomar is by far the best of any of them. And if that wasn't enough, you couldn't possibly ask for a better location! Close to Starbucks, restaurants (Scion is my fav), nightlife, entertainment and the metro. I'm anxiously awaiting my next trip to the DC area.

title: “4 Stars”
text:
I've stayed at the Millenium for both business and leisure. The hotel is comfortable with clean, comfortable rooms that provide a nice rest from a busy day in the city. The ongoing construction was a slight annoyance for me on my most recent visit, as we were in an 8th floor room directly facing construction that continued late into a Saturday evening. I was so exhausted though, I quickly fell asleep through it. On another visit a few years ago, I was in a 23rd floor room where the noise was not at all audible.
This is a nice hotel that I will continue to frequent at prices of 200/night. It can feel a bit isolated down in the financial district, but one can quickly access the train and get anywhere they want to go. It's particularly convenient to Brooklyn.

title: “Good Location”
text: Clean room and a good staff. I'd stay again. Baltimore is a great city.

title: “Clean, spacious, WiFi, great staff, suited my needs perfectly”
text: I was in town for a conference at the Omni Hotel in downtown Fort Worth and felt it would be worth the drive to save on the trip and it certainly was. It was a 12 minute drive each day and self parked at Conference Center.

title: “Sophisticated and modern stay in mid-town Manhattan”
text: We had a great time staying here for 7 nights in late July. The place is ultra clean and the service and the staff our great. We booked on expedia and got an upgrade to a room with a great view of the Empire State building and surrounding mid-town Manhattan (2109). Free internet if you sign up (for free) with the Kimpton hotel website (no problem). They hotel had a great happy hour between 5-7 pm every day with free sangria and wine and lemonade for my pregnant wife. Other little touches were nice as well such as the strawberry infused water that was always available in the lobby after a hot day in the sun. There was also a quasi-fast food place called FoodParc right next door (I think affiliated with the hotel) that was fantastic for breakfast (great quality food at a reasonable price) and always got things started for us everyday. Only down side was the lack of a pool (which is understandable I guess) but there was no sauna/steam room or anything like that which would have been great after a long day at the museums! The fitness center was small but pretty good (enough free weights and cardio to get a good workout if you were so inclined). The bar of the hotel is on the second floor (Bar Basque) which is a pretty pumping club on the weekends. It is not the kind of old-school bar in the lobby that some people might be used to. This is a modern hotel with a modern vibe and although it might not be for all tastes it definitely fit the bill for my wife and I. It's close to everything and only a $10 cab ride to everything. Good times.

title: “great staff!!”
text: the only problem is the breakfast value, it's too expensive. But that wasn't a real problem, there are a lot of options in the neighbourhood.

title: “Boutique-like Hotel despite the name”
text: The name Trump conjures up images of big: big hair, big buildings, etc. The Trump Hotel in Chicago is in a very big building but the hotel itself beginning with the intimate lobby does not feel very big. The service was excellent and we were upgraded to a large room with stunning river views. The restaurant, 16, is also very good.

title: “Very decent hotel stay!”
text:
This hotel stay was decent.
Pros: 
Room large enough to accommodate 5 people. 
Full breakfast available complete with sausage and eggs.
Good water pressure.
Clean, Clean, Clean, but it is new. Only open for about 2 weeks at the time of our visit.
Beds were very comfortable.
Check-in time was listed as 3:00 pm, however we arrived at 2:00 pm and were checked-in without additional charges.
Convenient location to local attractions.
Cons:
This hotel only has valet parking available, which was not listed on the reservation page. 
You must actually search the Marriott page to find that you that parking is an additional $21.00 per night. (Thankfully, we only stayed 1 night.)
Although the room has a pull-out sofa, there is no bedding readily available in the room for the sofa bed. You must request these from the front desk.
We encountered on issue with check-out. We were billed for valet parking twice. The front desk staff handled the issue quickly without hassle.

title: “The Godd, The Bad & The Ugly”
text:
Stayed for almost a week in April. If you have small kids-DO NOT STAY
AT THIS PROPERTY! Page down to the Bad & Ugly for more details.
The Good: beautiful landcape scenery, outdoor speakers w/ soothing music playing everywhere, tranquil water features, attractively designed rooms/suites, complimentary laundry facility. Tuscany Restaurant and great live music( 2 guys in their 40's)Complimentary mountain bikes. Allison at Tennis Center is a gem! Fitzroy, and red hair German waitress at Blue Sage are super nice as well. Lots of pools.
The Bad: Black mold & mildew in every corner and grout line of the adjoining room's shower. Filthy bathroom floor covered in hairs upon checkin. Housekeeping overall was lax for such a $$$resort. 
Stopped into the "Revive Spa" the 1st day to make an appt. for a $125.00 skin scrub for next morning. Made the mistake of taking one of my kids w/ me to make the appt. All of a sudden a man was standing
over my child and I, motioning for us to leave. We had been in the spa reception area for all of 5 minutes!!! We were in the process of walking toward the door anyway. I wound up cancelling b/c I knew after being treated so rudely, I would not be able to "revive" there.
Finally, the UGLY-and I mean UGLY:
Beside shelling out a $$$$ money for the suite and joining room, we also decided to shell out even more for a passcard to the "CLOUD ROOM". They offered snacks, lite meals, drinks, web access, open bar.
However, they just instituted a no kids allowed rule. That meant either parent having to go solo to the "CLOUD " while 8 yr old sat outside to help w/the carry out food; the other parent stayed in room
w/other 2 kids. Never got to enjoy the view, or ambiance as advertised. Despite this, we understood and used our divide and conquer plan as mentioned above and were fine with it.
Then there was the issue of me trying to take my totally asleep 2 yr old into the "CLOUD" room b/c my spouse w/other 2 kids were at the pool. I figured it would be ok since I was doing a quick snack run. I didn't think it was safe to leave her alone outside in the hall. Asleep toddler and I were 6 feet into the "Cloud" Room when "on duty " Cloud concierge person stopped me and tried to shoo me out b/c
according to her, kids aren't allowed (though it is a family resort) and it's not fair to the other guests who can't bring their kids in. She spoke rather loudly, repeating herself and embarrassing me in front of the other 6-8 guests who were in there. Naturally I reacted and told her that it was ridiculous that I paid extra $$$ for the CLOUD Room, and that I couldn't stop in for 2 minutes to grab a few things to bring back to our rooms. Not once did she offer to stand outside the Cloud room and watch my baby for the 2 minutes it would have taken. As I was leaving she got infront of me pushing the Cloud Room door wide open, for all the guests to see-more humiliation for me, and said "I'm a momma too". I turned to her w/ baby in stroller and said " That's not the point " but I didnt get to finish what I was saying to her, b/c one of the male guests came charging to the door and told me I was making a scene. Of course all he could see was
upsetment on my face responding to her, and not the continued snipping she was doing to me. I am 5'7", and the Cloud Concierge person was easily 5' 9" , and the guy who charged at me was atleast 6'5" tall. It was intimidating and scary to have these taller people standing over me in such an aggressive manner. And they did this to me w/ my toddler by my side. I wound up in tears at the front desk as my 8 yr & 6 yr old children walked up w/ their dad. It was awful. I didn't want to leave our suite and room after that, it ruined the last day & half of my trip. It also upset my kids to see me crying. 
In conclusion: If you have children younger than teen years, you are not welcome at this resort, no matter how much money you spend. P.S. The on duty manager Mr. Donough? comped us for dinner that night.

title: “How one concierge went the extra mile to make my trip a success!”
text: Eden at the Chicago City Center did everything she possibly could to get our reservations and turn our stressful business trip into a fabulous vacation. I have never had so much dedication in the 30 years I have been operating my business. Eden you are the best!

title: “Old and run down”
text: I’ve never written a hotel review before, but after staying here I just had to warn others. I was here for a conference, and apparently the conference rate entitles you to a room the size of a closet. I could hardly use the desk in the room for my computer because there wasn’t enough room to move the chair back to get in and out (I’m not a huge guy). I had a tiny walkway at the foot of the bed that I could scoot past to get to the bathroom, but couldn’t open the 1/2 width door all the way because it would hit the tv mounted on the wall. The bathroom countertop was hardly bigger than the sink, so there was barely room for my toothbrush, deodorant, etc. There was room in the bathroom for a bigger countertop, but they apparently purchased the smallest, cheapest drop-in unit they could. The shower was falling apart and had screw holes everywhere from where things apparently used to be attached, and pieces were loose and missing screws. My view looked across a space the width of a hallway (literally) at a brick wall on the other side, but a little sun was able to filter down the hole from above. Avoid the restaurant in the hotel at all costs, there are far better places within walking distance, and you’ll get more professional service at a McDonalds. For positives, the bed was great, the same as you find in all Westins. The maids would all smile and say hello as you walked by. And the food at the conference, provided by the hotel, was fantastic, many of the items were obviously made on site and were delicious. But overall, for a Westin, it was incredibly disappointing and I will never stay there again. I’m also fighting a charge that showed up after I left and isn’t on my receipt. It doesn’t show on the new copy I had them send either, and they quite rudely insist that it doesn’t exist. My credit card company says otherwise so I’m having to dispute it through them instead.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
We booked this hotel at the last minute. The staff was helpful through each step; very pleased to have a fridge! Note: the crowd at the entrance was for the bus.
We were horrified with the room. We were initially distracted by the colorful background lighting above the bed, until we realized the room was freezing COLD. The heater was not on. It was 55 degrees. The heater was loud and took a long time to heat; it finally peaked at 71 degrees, perhaps because of the draft coming from the window. It intermittently came on all night. (My husband and I kept bickering about who should call the front desk about extra blankets. Neither of us would give in, so we resorted to snuggling to get through the night.) 
This wouldn't have been too big an issue if there had not been hair all around the sink area. At 1100pm at night, with poor lighting, it was still very visible. The final straw was the urine on the rim of the toilet and the floor in front of it. There were other minor things, like un-wiped bedside tables and greasy fingerprints on the clock, and 12x12 square for night pillows.
If not for the late hour and our long travels, rationale would have made us call the front desk for another room. Fatigue definitely played a part of our dissatisfaction but I am sure that is common for many guests. We should not have to do quality checks on cleanliness of hotel rooms.

title: “Perfect on a budget”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights and we were really happy because we weren't sure what to expect on our budget. I really struggled to find a hotel within our price range and was delighted when i found this one. 
Good things about hotel were price, spotlessly clean room and bathroom, good shower and very comfortable beds. The location is also good - it is on the west side of the city, which isn't quite as nice as the East side, but still fine. The hotel is a short walk from Times Square. There is a deli right next door to the hotel that did a good breakfast and then nice food throughout the day.
The only small gripe i have is that there were no tea making facilities in the room - a bit of a pain when you like your cup of tea. However, if you are thinking of staying at this hotel and you like a hot drink, just buy a small travel kettle.
Really recommend and would stay there again.

title: “Nice Hotel, Great Location”
text: Great location close and/or easily accessible to fun activities in San Franciso. Directly across the street from the cable cars with easy access to downtown and Chinatown. Within walking distance to Ghiradelli Square, Fisherman's Wharf and Pier 39. Much safer than hotels located in Union Square area. Hotel decor was beautiful, similar to being on a cruise ship, with great wine gathering each evening at 5 p.m. Rooms were small and narrow. Rooms on the interior face other rooms, with no view. Rooms on the exterior face bay, cannery or park. Cannery side is noisy during the day and evening, even on the higher levels. Fourth floor rooms do not have old wood decor like other levels. Most of the staff is very friendly, however, some have an attitude that borders on arrogance. Overall a nice hotel, but I would hesitate to pay the higher price for the Cannery or Park View rooms versus the interior rooms.

title: “very close to Lackland Air Force Base”
text: We were a little disappointed when we got there. The room had a musty smell to it. I feel like they only made the bed and changed the towels. I don't think the sheets were even changed because they didn't appear to be. The bathroom was not cleaned up each day. They didn't even bother to give us a new bar of soap each day, instead they just left the little pieces laying on the side of the tub. There was food left in the refrigerator from the previous guest, that I had to throw out. I had to go track down an iron. I have seen much better pools also. The best thing about the stay was it is very close to the Base. That was the whole reason for us even being there. If you don't plan on staying at the hotel to rest it's not really that bad. The conntinetal breakfast was nothing more than a couple of pasteries, juice and coffee. They didn't even have milk for the small children. I don't plan on staying there again, but I don't plan on taking another vacation to San Antonio. I really hated the town all together.

title: “One Star for Room Windows - Fours Stars for the rest.”
text:
I lodged there for the entire Presidential Election Day week on the 7th floor facing 16th street, about three blocks from the north entrance of the White House. On Tuesday night it was very difficult to sleep from 11:00 p.m. to about 2:00 a.m. because of the cacophony of noise emanated from the hordes of over zealous crowds marching down 16th street to the White House screaming, yelping, colorfully cursing the loosing candidate while praising the winning candidate with equally expressive words of passion as happy horn blowing and not-so-happy police sirens added background music to the scene. Sure it was an historical week in America and human expression is to be expected, welcomed, and perhaps embraced. I agree BUT I did learn something about the Capital Hilton that I found less than adequate for a prestigious hotel located in a populated city – BAD WINDOWS! More than 90% of all the exterior noise comes in through windows and doors. So when windows face a noisy city street, then installing soundproof windows can reduce noise levels by 75-95%.
Other than the poorly acoustically engineered windows, the Capital Hilton was a delightful place to lodge in all categories – But do know that it is never a good choice to get any sleep during a local celebration or even a political demonstration on the streets of Washington.

title: “Not a 4 star hotel...its actually 3 star”
text:
Front desk Service is rude....doorman and valet are kool... restaurant service was good..restaurant food was excellent....
This hotel claims to be a 4 star, but it is not, it is a 3 star pretending to be a four star, lobby is nice..fitness center is good....elevator is crowded and small....room is small and crappy for a 4 star....they have double beds only unless you get a suite. I paid 600 dollar for 5 nights for business and they put me in a studio room with one double bed...what the hell..the room are so tiny, and the front desk service is horrible....the hotel s own by the nearby doubletree , so it sucks! never gonna stay at the allerton again!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Great location, Lovely lobby etc but small old rooms”
text:
Hotel is in great location, at bottom edge of CDB - this means it is accessible not only to City but also chinatown and backbay areas. 
The lobby, lift wells and hallways all have lovely, old-word carpets etc - quite presentable. However, the rooms themselves are fairly small and in need of some renovation (ie. stained paint, loose tiles, flaking ceiling). Personally, I didn't mind these consessions since it did have good location.
There is a restaurant next to the hotel that specialises in Desserts!! A girlfriend and I shared a sampling platter for dinner - fabulous! Also recommend a visit to the Back Bay area (10-15min walk, lovely treelined neighbourhood with boutique shops - try Malborough Street) and Beacon Hill (10 min walk, old english-style village with lovely small streets and street lamps).
I did the Freedom Trail tour using a headset which was hired from the main Boston Common information Center. Whilst it offered a lot more information and covered a much greater distance than the mini group tours that most people go on, I found that unless you are really intereseted in the dates and details it is a little boring/long. 
Lovely city. Well-located hotel which would benefit from renovations in the rooms themselves.

title: “Smells Terrible like a smokey bar room”
text: When I checked in to this hotel, the smell of smoke was so overwhelming, I should have turned around and gone home. I had pre paid, unfortuneately. I love marriotts, normally, and this was equal to a motel 6, except for the cost! No coffee offered in the lobby on a Sunday morning, no extra's at all. The view out of our window was apartments, the shabby low rent type. I was extremely disappointed as you can surely tell! Oh, did I mention that I am a smoker and even though, the stink was nauseating. BTW this was a Marriotts Courtyard Hotel, but there was NO courtyard. The residence inn across the lake looks like a courtyard but is actually a Residence Inn. My Bad for sure!

title: “You get what you pay for - great location”
text:
The room was small and the bathroom admittedly run down looking but the hotel is in a super location, was great value, and you'll only be in it to sleep. peopel on here slating it are massiveyl over-reacting. For the price they paid did they expect the Hilton? 
ps when I visited in June 2008 there wasnt a urine smell so maybe that's a new developent. pps as an aside, make sure you visit Dotty's True Blue Cafe in the Tenderloin for breakfast!!

title: “Tribeca”
text: Very pleasant. I've never stayed in Tribeca before and loved the area. Wonderful restaurants. Room very pleasant as well. Hotel has edgy design.

title: “A Marriott Port in the Storm of a Convention-Full City of Washington DC”
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. MARRIOTT NW, 
George Washington University
One of the best values of being a Marriott frequent guest is the dedicated telephone reservation service. In these days when everyone in business wants you to go online and spend your time looking for and booking a hotel room, it is a small blessing be able to call a special phone number and have a live, intelligent human being offer to assist you.
I always seem to end up using this service when all of my normal efforts to get a hotel room have failed, and this time I was in Washington, D.C. for a meeting and had not been able to get a hotel room, assuming that some sort of concierge or hospitality desk at the meeting could help. Well, they didn’t and so I sat in the convention center and started using my cell phone, looking for a room.
Marriott to the rescue, I ended up at the Washington DC Marriott NW at George Washington University, which is a bit of a misnomer, because it’s a few blocks from the school and hospital and a short 15 minute walk from the Foggy Bottom Metro station. 
As much as I hate to spend an entire day’s fiscal allocation on a hotel room, I was happy with the hotel. Check in was easy and quick. They could not accommodate me on floor seven, which is the concierge floor, but my fourth floor room with king bed was fine. 
There are always those little Marriott touches that, as a weary traveler, I find as unnecessary annoyances: A bottle of FIJI water, (does it really come all the way from Fiji?), is priced at $5.95. Given the room price, it should be free. WiFi costs $9.95 a day, ending at midnight, so it’s not a good idea to stay hooked up unless you want to pay for an extra day. The house computer system was down while I was there anyway. An independent internet access system is available in the lobby and it can be used even if the hotel’s computer isn’t working. the view from the room was of another building being built, so no reason to open the curtains. (see photo).
Typical of D.C., this is an old building and shows it in some places. For example, the connecting door to the next room was mis-aligned and had about ¾ inch of space at the top on the handle side and was very tight at the hinge side. A nice breeze whistled through this opening. Could the building be settling or listing that much, I wondered?
Flat screen TV and the usual Marriott special bedding and amenities were all part of the justification for the price, which was, as usual for D.C., high enough to bring tears to the eyes of any corporate expense account reviewer in the accounting department.
