The hotel is just a block away from the spiffy, newer Ritz Carlton and I swear that some of the RC charm has rubbed off on this Marriott. The staff members, every single one of them who I met, were charming, courteous and friendly beyond any I have seen in recent years. 
When I checked with reception about a nearby pizza place, instead of sending me to the concierge, they not only told me about a secret little spot up the street, but offered to loan me an umbrella for the walk. 
The floor maid not only greeted me, but inquired about my health and my travels. 
The phone operators were incredibly courteous and helpful and even the engineer, who happened to be in the elevator during one of my trips, was outgoing and cheerful. These are little RC–type courtesies and it was nice to see them at Marriott.
Underground parking was $26 a night and the garage was stifling, probably because the day I was there saw record high temperatures in DC and the rest of the Northeast. 
Any complaints? No, not really. The fitted bed sheet was not fully fitted to the bed and there was hair in the bath tub. The shower curtain needed to be really cleaned and the toilet tissue dispenser looked like someone had reclaimed it from a Baghdad bomb site, but in general, this is a good place to stay in DC if you don’t have to be in the middle of Capital Hill or shopping areas. Like so many major city properties that are running at very high occupancy levels, the Marriott’s rooms could use some TLC. 
Globally, I am convinced that housekeeping quality has decreased as hotel rates have increased. Certainly, housekeeping and maintenance have been at the center of most of the problems which I have seen in middle to high level hotels in the last few years. It is hard for me to buy the hotels’ position that they cannot get good help when you seldom see a non-alien working on hotel floors, which means that the pay rates are terribly low and the jobs are not attractive to many people. When you consider that you are usually paying several hundred dollars for a room for less than 24 hours, it seems odd that the help is making so little or at least not being trained and supervised more carefully.
10.16.07

title: “Six Columbus delivered in spades”
text: I enjoyed the stay here in NYC. I was in Manhattan for a friends wedding, and the retro style and incredibly polite staff were very courteous, and helpful, particularly getting dinner reservations for a VERY last minute bachelor party, and getting around a very busy city.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
I bid on this room through Hotwire, not knowing that O'Hare actually had a hotel in the airport. I was a bit disappointed to find out we'd have to stay "at the airport" and contend with the parking and traffic, but it turned out to be a wonderful experience!! When I called to inquire about the parking, I was told they only had valet parking and that it would cost $47.00 a day. I found an online company <www.aboutairportparking.com> and we paid $17.00 a day. It was wonderful. It provided the same exact service.
 When we checked into the hotel the staff was wonderful and helpful and it remained that way throughout our stay. The room was great--quiet and clean--and the "L" was accessible from the lower level of the hotel, so access to downtown was a breeze!!

title: “Great value”
text:
The Bedford was great – I stayed for two nights on a recent business trip and it was one of the smoothest trips to New York I’ve had, largely because of the Bedford. In general a midtown location is fairly convenient, but much of the convenience came from its being on 40th street, just one block from the buses that stop just south of Grand Central and run to all three major airports. Being able to walk one block and catch a bus to Newark for $16 was a revelation.
The room was surprisingly spacious – I had paid for a small room, but was upgraded to a “Tower Suite” which was essentially a one-bedroom apartment. The bed was a bit hard, but other than that the room was great. Street noise was a bit audible (room was on the fourth floor) but this was not a problem for me. Finally, the hotel staff was especially friendly, which made each walk through the lobby an unexpected treat. Highly recommended, especially if an airport bus is in your plans.

title: “Wonderful!!”
text: I went here in October for a mommy getaway alone and it was wonderful! The Staff was amazing, I stayed in a Valencia Casita which was great, right next to the pool where I spent all of my time. The guys at the pool were constantly filling my glass with yummy citrus water, and brought me a menu at lunch time for great poolside meals. The food was amazing, I didn't eat at the restaurant but enjoyed appetizers and drinks outside in the beautiful courtyard in the evenings. had great roomservice meals out on my patio for breakfast!!!. I can't wait to bring my husband and celebrate our Anniversary!! wonderful staff and wonderful service

title: “Where everybody knows your name.....”
text:
Okay, not everybody. But I have stayed here several times in the past year, and after just one time, have come to know a few of the staff on a first name basis. It is nice to return to a hotel to be greeted by the same people over time, who actually remember your name and your grandkids. Makes it feel like home.
The suites are roomy and comfortable, the atrium style feels safe and friendly, the complimentary breakfasts and evening receptions are bonus, and the location offers tons of dining, shopping and entertainment options.
Keep rockin' it!

title: “The staff was very helpful and accomodating!”
text: For starters, my friend and I were checking in at different times and had a special request for how to handle the charges between us and they agreed to accommodate us. Then we needed help finding our way around town and they were very specific in their directions which gave us a lot of confidence in an unfamiliar area. And I've never seen THIS before... but they have a library of really cool movies that you can borrow to watch in your room on a DVD player at no charge! A computer to check emails...again no charge. And then breakfast is included from 6-10am also at no charge! Breakfast can easily cost an additional $10-$20 when you're traveling and it was GOOD breakfast. All around, we were really pleased with the room and the staff and all the goodies that were included with the price of a one-night stay. Thanks Old Town Inn!

title: “Great City Hotel, also ideal for families”
text:
The Hotel is an ideal base for exploring the city, particularly for families. If you are looking for a francy, stylish and luxury hotel, this is not your place. If you require a central base which gives you good value for the money, this is it. The hotel is located near Grand Central station, so Downtown and Uptown is in good reach via subway and a lot of attractions are in footwalking distance. The bus M42 on 42 second street gives you a ride to the West, particularly Pier 83 & Time Square.
Dining & breakfast locations and a nice beer bar (Perfect Pint) are around the corner.
The staff of the hotel is very friendly and helpful. The rooms are clean and well equipped. We shared a double king-size room with 4 persons (2 adults + 2 childred) which fitted our requirements. Only downside is that there is no free wifi neither on the rooms nor in the lobby/bar.
I would not hesitate to recommend to friends.

title: “Elegant & Civilised”
text: What a fantastic hotel! Gorgeous rooms, polite, friendly staff, and the location cannot be beaten. This was our first time in New York and the Michelangelo made sure it won't be our last. It is a lovely serene place to relax after the hustle and bustle of the city. The price ($189 per night) dollars is definately competitive and even more so considering the current strength of the dollar! Highly recommended.

title: “Noisy & crowded, but great location”
text:
I stayed here for the location, but I wasn't expecting the chaos of times square to follow me into the hotel. There was a huge convention in the hotel the same weekend I was there. This caused massive problems, like not being able to get an elevator for over 30 minutes on several occasions and hearing noise/music from a conference room 6 floors down until 2 am.
The staff was very professional, the location was great, the rooms were a bit small ( but that's to be expected in NYC) but their inability to handle the crowds in the hotel was what ruined the experience for me.

title: “Nice hotel, clean and friendly!”
text:
Title says all. Rooms were spacious, quiet and clean. Hotel staff were very friendly and most helpful. Breakfast was a little basic, but in NYC who has breakfast at the hotel?!
Two subway stations closeby making anywhere in NYC easy to get to. 
Situated in chinatown, a fascinating place to stay with plenty of Chinese restaurants to sample.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Just returned 5/16 from a family "girl trip" to New York. We had to 2 suites at the Doubletree and the accomodations were great. Had read reviews about the unfriendly desk staff, but found them most friendly and helpful. Rooms were clean and bathrooms large. Our rooms faced 47th St. and were very quiet. Security is the best I've seen. Location is perfect if you're a theatre buff. Have stayed in many other hotels in New York but this is my "new found favorite!" Plan to stay there next trip.

title: “Shockingly bad hotel-waste of money!”
text:
I CANNOT believe that I just spent $400 for a room that barely even fit the "queen" sized bed we requested (it felt more like a full-sized). My husband and I could barely be in the room together at the same time with our luggage - there was nowhere to put it! There weren't enough towels for one person, let alone two, and there was no fan or exhaust system in the bathroom - so when you took a shower, the hotel room was also steamy. To make things worse, there is no coffee maker in the room - and it took me 5 calls to room service to even order my $8 "pot" (about 2 cups worth) of coffee. If we were going to be in town for more than one night, I would have left - TOO SMALL!
On the plus side, it was clean, and everything in the room (furniture, bedding) seemed new. Good location if you like noisy Times Square and the theatre area, but I feel like I got ripped off big time!

title: “Enjoyable stay”
text: The Washington Plaza was a convenient 5 block walk from the convention centre where we attended the International AIDS Conference. Our 9th floor room was clean and comfortable, if a bit small for two. The basement gym and business centre provided all that was needed. Staff were consistently friendly and the breakfast buffet allowed for a good start to the day. Free internet and a good range of television channels add to overall good value.

title: “Great location!”
text:
This hotel is an ideal location in midtown. The front desk staff is extremely helpful! I was very pleased and impressed with Reina and how informative she was when she checked us in. However, twice during our stay we were interrupted by other staff members in unusual ways. First, a man came to our door, rang the bell and asked us if we needed mini-bar service even though we hadn't touched anything in the mini-bar. Second, on the morning before we checked out around 8:00 a.m. (check out is at noon) a member of the housekeeping staff rang the bell and woke us. 
Overall, it was a nice place and we are still sad we didn't have a chance to try to burger place that everyone raves about, but the line fills up fast and the hotel was packed the weekend we were there so there were long waits at both the restaurant and at the bell station so we opted to not check out luggage and catch an earlier train. There was also no ATM in the hotel and the burger place only takes cash, which again, is somewhat inconvenient.

title: “It is worth staying here because of the view!”
text: I was nervous about booking this hotel after reading the reviews. I am so glad that I did. I had a fabulous view of the space needle (that has chirstmas lights on top for the holidays), and puget sound. It is also easy to find street parking around the hotel. It is within walking distance for all the sites and the indoor pool was great to keep the kids happy.

title: “Great place and I will be back”
text:
Excellent rooms , large and very clean, huge excersise room with top of the line equipment, if you stay in the 400 block you have to walk a lot to get to your room .
breakfst is oke , but pricey 
very close to the Reliant Center, you can walk there. The hotel shuttle will drive you to reataurants in the area and pick you up again.

title: “Efficient Well-Located Hotel”
text: Had a pleasant stay at this hotel. It was well-located--close to the Art Institute and a block away from the blue line and two blocks from the red line. I left my car at home since I had intended to get around the city by public transportation, so the proximity to the "el" line was a bonus. The staff were friendly and helpful and quickly attended to any concerns. The room was small but the bed was comfortable and the furniture and appointments up-to-date. I would have preferred more closet and drawer space, however. There was a shower but no bath tub--which for me was not a concern as I prefer taking showers anyway. I liked the fact that there was real milk/cream for coffee in the room. Nothing is worse in my view than powdered "creamer". I had a couple of meals at the adjacent English pub. I thought it was well-priced and had good food. Breakfast is not included in the hotel price, but you can have breakfast at the pub for around $10. There is also a Starbucks next door. There were some nice touches--water coolers from which you can fill bottles for personal use (they provide throwaway plastic bottles, which in my view is somewhat ecologically wasteful) and self-serve laundry and laundry supplies at no charge. I needed to store my luggage at the hotel after I checked out and the process was very efficient and convenient. I would definitely consider this hotel the next time I visit this wonderful city.

title: “Beautiful hotel- Horrendous service.”
text:
The good: very chic hotel. great location within walking distance to restaurants & bars. good onsite restaurant and bar. Rooms are spacious.
The bad: The pool, bar & restaurant area turns into a club at night, It is definitely a party hotel and it is VERY loud. If you're looking for a party hotel, Za Za will work for you, but if you're a light sleeper or want a more relaxing time, I'd be wary.
The ugly: The service was simply awful. We had reserved 2 rooms- 1 for 3 nights and the 2nd for 2 nights. They couldn't find the 2nd reservation. Even with my printed confirmation from Jetsetter, it was still a hassle. OK, these sorts of things happen, but the people at the front desk were so unbelievably rude about it. Apparently, I was causing them a tremendous inconvenience to give us our 2nd (and PREPAID) room. They also have a complimentary shuttle- in theory. We called down to the valet stand to ask if they would take us to a specific area. They said yes, and recommended a time to leave to avoid rush hour traffic. When we went downstairs, they told us the destination was too far (I got 3 different mileage requirements over the course if our stay) and we would have to take a taxi. When I explained that we had been told differently on the phone, the valet was extremely rude (again) and kept questioning me with the implication that we were lying! Lastly, we had some questionable charges on our bill at check out. There were charges showing up as "room service charges" when we had never ordered room service. It turned out that they were bar charges that were classified incorrectly, but I felt justified in questioning it since the descriptions were unclear. Furthermore, our waitress at the bar the previous evening had simply disappeared and I couldn't find her to sign my bill. So I wanted to be sure we were not overcharged. Again, the woman at the desk was beyond rude. It was pretty much the last straw. The whole thing really put a damper on our girls weekend. And I was pretty appalled that a hotel billed as 4 star would have such terrible service. I know we'll never go back nor would I recommend Za Za to anyone visiting Dallas.

title: “convenient location, comfortable stay”
text: My husband and i enjoyed 3 nights here and found the location convenient, did not have any trouble with noise. nice little kitchenette with microwave , sink and mini fridge. no complaints - except we had some trouble with the internet dropping in and out, and no main light in the bedroom - just lamps galore.

title: “Great hotel, lived up to the expetations”
text:
Our last hotel on our 3 week trip. A friendly welcome in a hotel with all conveniences. The room was large, the beds excellent. All very clean and very well looked after. 
The hotel is one block away from LAX, but we didn't here any airplane.
One mishap, the trainee forgot to book our wake-up call. However, our complaint was acknowledged and we got a full compensation !.
Crowne Plaza is a hotel to remember for a next stay in the US.

title: “Not the best hotel”
text: I was visiting Philadelphia and I booked the Microtel because it was the least expensive. I've stayed in hotels for this price even less, but the condition of this one was the least desirable. It was ok for one night, but anymore I would've gone to the Marriott or the other surrounding hotels. Once you enter the hallway where the rooms are, it reeks terribly of pot. The room itself smelled like stale cigarettes. Burn marks everywhere. I would come here again just for an over night stay just because of it's convenience. If you're looking for a great atmosphere or ambiance this is not the place.

title: “Bargain Deal !”
text:
We were a party of 3 adults, in a two double bed room. Price was great 212$ per night including tax. (relative to other hotels from same class). 
Room was nice, with all the amnities you need. 
The hotel is located an walking distance from Union Sq, adn othe SOMA attractions!

title: “Good Value”
text: Stayed here at the end of Oct '08. Only complaint is that for someone not accustomed to San Antonio's Freeway System it is a confusing place to find,enter and exit. When exiting the hotel you MUST turn left onto the feeder road. This is not signed at all on the way out and there's only a small one way traffic sign across the road which isn't even directly in front of the exit. To go to the downtown you need to exit through Applebee's parking lot and turn right. We stayed in the north wing which was super quiet. The hotel is getting a bit old but we had no complaints with anything. Considering we paid $90 plus taxes, it was good value with free secured covered parking, breakfast, evening drinks, substantial snacks, computers and free long distance calls.

title: “Not what it used to be”
text:
I visit Boston fairly regularly and have stayed at the InterCon a few times. It opened a few times and was then THE place to stay in Boston. I have noticed that quality has slipped somewhat over the past few years.
Rooms are OK. I was there a week and the turn service only took place once.
A colleague of mine requested a kettle and this was supplied but she wasnt given any tea bags and shown she asked for some she was told she would have to pay for them even though coffee was provided free of charge. 
La Miele is pretty consistent for food quality and service. I ordered duck one night and parts of it were terribly undercooked. I was offered a replacement but I had by then finished my meal and didn't want to eat mire and no adjustment was made to my bill. The service is good there though.
This hotel is busy through the summer season and has a lot of summer events organized so it is constantly very busy, which can result in frustration if the lobby is full of people drinking and you are trying to push your way through to get to the lifts.
The instant service button on the phone in my room was not working.
No free wi fi.

title: “A Staycation”
text: I am a resident of Baltimore City but sometimes you just need to get away from it all. My Husband and I booked a stay at this location for some R and R. We were pleased with the room and the comfort of the bed. The shower was a bit tricky, as it seemed to be extra slippery but everything was clean and fresh. We opted for the Club Lounge this time and we are so happy we did. Lar Rhonda took excellent care of us during our stay in the lounge. The space was organized, clean and well stocked with snacks, beverages, and a variety of food choices for the evening rush. She was funny and very helpful. Looking forward to our next staycation.

title: “Fantastic Hotel & Location”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights and we found it perfect. We had a superior king room and this was very spacious and well equipped. It was based at the back of the hotel and on the 11th floor. This meant it was a nice quiet room...just perfect. 
The location is just up from Union Square so great for transportation and shopping. 
Starbucks over the road with free wifi for an early morning coffee and a 24hr diner on the corner and a Walgreens, so perfect! 
Staff and service were excellent. 
Would definitely stay here again, can't wait to go back!

title: “Loved”
text: I loved it in this hotel it was brilliant. Everyone was so nice and kind and it was very relaxing and sunny. And the service was just excellent the food tasted really nice and yummy. I think more people would come here. Every day that I was in there I always looked outside. The view was amazing and super clear if I had a favourite hotel so far

title: “Great hotel in a fantastic location!”
text: We just returned from a weekend stay at Hotel Cass Holiday Inn Express and had an enjoyable visit. We arrived on an early flight and went straight to the hotel to drop our bags. By the time we strolled down the street and had breakfast our room was ready. That was great news since we were tired from the early flight. The rooms were small but we had a corner room and from the reviews here on TA I guess those are bigger. The only downside was the walls were paper thin and the outside noise was awful (parking garage across the street buzzed constantly) so I would bring a fan or something to drown out the noise. The location was excellent, breakfast was tasty and the service was outstanding. We would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting downtown Chicago.

title: “Couldn't have been better”
text: We spent five wonderful nights at Hollywood Orchid Suites, after being told by our daughter, who had stayed previously, that there was no place better as a base for exploring LA, and she was not wrong. Only a couple of minutes walk from the action of Hollywood Ave, the free parking made it easy to get to other LA and District attractions and sights. Staff were excellent, with a special mention of the lovely lady who looked after the breakfast area - they couldn't do enough and always had a cheery smile when we were coming and going. Although the rooms were a little dated, they were very quiet,clean and roomy, with good self catering facilities, and thus very reasonable for the rates being charged. Whilst we were there they were in the process of refurbishing a couple of the rooms. We won't bother looking anywhere else for our next stay in LA.

title: “not what i expected, but not bad”
text:
I stayed at aloft Charlotte for one night for business. This hotel was not BAD by any means, but was not what I expected. As a SPG gold member, I have had the opportunity to stay at many Starwood properties, and this was not up to par with all of the other properties I have stayed at. Being a "vision of W (hotels)", I expected much more of this property. The staff were friendly, the hotel was nice, but I simply expected more for my money at this property. The rooms were cheap and decor was not nearly up to par. The decor of the room reminded me of cheap Ikea furniture, not something that a W hotel would provide. Although the rooms were not amazing, the location was perfect. 
I did not have a problem with this hotel, and if you find a good deal <$150 or so then I say give it a shot. I had never stayed at a Starwood aLoft or Element property, so I decided to give it a shot. f I were to travel to Charlotte again, I would stay at the W down the road though.

title: “Superb value. Will stay again!”
text:
My wife and I plus our four small children stayed in an "oversized" suite of this hotel on a recent weekend. It was a very good experience for us, and we will very likely return for a longer stay.
The PROS: It was very clean and comfortable. The staff was very helpful and friendly. It is, apparently, a very popular hotel and tends to stay full, so book early. Parking is free. The downtown shuttle (currently $4/day for a pass) has a pickup point behind the hotel that will get you anywhere downtown you want to go very easily. That's a lot cheaper than paying for downtown parking.
The CONS: It is located right next to a major street and a highway, so expect some street noise, especially if you have a ground floor room facing the street. We were on the fourth floor on the side opposite the street, and the noise didn't bother us at all. Also, the thermostat in our room was off by a few degrees, but once we figured that out, we had no trouble adjusting it.
OTHER: It is not ON the Riverwalk, but it is only a few blocks walk to the Riverwalk and the Riverwalk shopping mall. It is about a half mile walk to the Alamo. The beds are soft and the pillows are VERY thick and fluffy. Room service is contracted to an outside service, so selection is great, but delivery takes about 30-45 minutes. The gift shop sells "healthy" frozen dinners in case you get tired of eating out. Breakfast is continental plus eggs, bacon, sausage, pancakes, etc. Kids get to eat breakfast for free, adults and older children are about $3.50.

title: “Good value, nice water park”
text: Upon arrival we were upgraded to a Casita. The room was spacious and clean with a frig and microwave. We came here b/c of the mini water park and it did not disappoint. The pool was grea, as was the lazy river, and water slide. The also had mini-golf as an option as well. The workout area was well equiped and spacious. The staff was very professional and attentive throughout the resort . Our $89 package came with breakfast, which was average at best. The only thing I would warn anyone on is the prices by the pool for food and drink, but than again that's to be expected. This hotel was a great value during the hot summer and we will be back as my children loved the water park.

title: “Hidden charges ruined our stay”
text:
This is a nice hotel in a good location of Chicago but there were some problems we had which have turned us off ever staying there again. On the plus side, the staff are friendly and helpful; the rooms are comfortable and clean (even though the plumbing system in the bathroom really needs to be updated-showering in water up to my ankles is not fun); the food in the restaurant is terrific, and the fact that it actually had a bar was a real plus for us.
The problems with check-in and check-out are ridiculous. The bottle neck created by the queue of people trying to move around make it very awkward to speak to the receptionists. 
We also needed to send a fax from the hotel (something I have had no trouble doing in other hotels) but we were charged $5 just to send it, I personally thought this was a little extreme.
We asked if we could store our bags for an hour while we went to eat breakfast in the hotel restaurant and we were charged 50c per bag to store them. I have never had to pay for a luggage room before, and I heard others around us complaining about the same thing.
The dinner we had in the hotel restaurant was delicious, but it was when we paid our bill that we got ticked off. Though the waitress and the service were excellent, she placed our bill on the table before we finished eating, leaving out much chance of having a drink or dessert after dinner. What really annoyed us was that she had already added a gratuity of 18% onto the bill before we got it. I can understand this being automatically added to a bill when its a large party, but I've never seen it done when it's a party of 2. The other thing that annoyed me was, as far as Im concerned, is tipping not something that's supposed to be at the discretion of the customer? Since when did the waiters and waitresses start deciding how good they are at their jobs? We had fully intended in leaving her an excellent tip that suitably reflected the service but what if our service had been terrible-were we just expected to tip her regardless?
All in all the hidden charged we incurred during our stay really put us off staying here again.

title: “A+ Hotel, A+ Location, A+ View, A+ Value”
text:
Arrived via Amtrak from Phiadelphia at 1PM Sept. 9 for a 3 night stay.
Despite being early check-in, they had a room on the 45th floor ready and awaiting my arrival. 
First, realize this hotel is downtown, near Wall St. and immediately across the street from Ground Zero. Built in the early 1990's, the hotel was damaged by the scumbags, closed for nearly 2 years, and completely re-vamped. I stayed in the regular 1King bed room. This is the most basic room at the hotel. For more $ you can get a junior suite, which offers some more room, and a view that looks more uptown rather than downtown. Some consider this a plus. For me, ground zero, the buildings around ground zero, the Hudson River with its traffic, and NJ and the sunsets made my view the best in the hotel. All rooms offer the large plasma TV, nice work table with convenient internet and electrical plugs, floor to ceiling windows and in-room safe. No in-room wireless internet (wireless in lobby/lounge/restaurant only). They charge $5.95 per 24 hours, or $9.95 if you must log on to your own internet provider. They will give you the T1 cord for a $10 deposit.
Rooms very comfortable. Bed nice and well appointed with sheets and comforter. Closet small-enough room for 1 person but would be stretching it for 2 people. The dresser is dominated by mini-bar, mini-refer which doesn't leave a lot of drawer space. Bathrooms very nice w/marble and a good shower up high so someone 6'2" or so doesn't have to bend over to wash hair. Towels and bathroom amenities servicable. Note only one sink-may be 2 in the junior suite - if that's an issue, check.
Not only is the room comfortable and new, the view is stunning. I was there for the 911 aniversary/memorial. To look out and see the crowds and the firetrucks and police cars and mourners and everyone else paying their respects was staggering. To be able to walk out the door and across the street and be Right There was amazing. 
A lot of people suggest staying up towards ( or in) Times Square so you can really be a part of the party. I disagree and am more than happy I stayed at the M. Hilton. 15 minute walk to L.Italy/Chinatown. 15 to Wall St. 15 to ferry boats to NJ. Anything further, there is a subway stop a block away, or just catch a cab. It is quieter and less congested down here than up at Times Sq. It is convenient to go up in the evening, see Times, see the lights and masses of people and hawkers, and for me; cool to leave it behind and come back to the hotel. 
Also, restaurant and room service both very good - if you do get room service, realize you are paying $4 plus 15% on top of the price of food. This is the tip. Don't leave more money after you are already forced to tip (unless you are just really generous - if so, give me a call). I had no time for pool and no need for work-out after all the hiking I did each day, so I can not comment on either of those facilities. My minor complaint: while room was clean, there were a couple strands of hair in tub. I seem to see this almost everywhere I stay, yet I don't like it and find it disquieting - once I see that I question the cleanliness of the rest of the room and am on the lookout for something else to complain about. Other very minor incident - on 9/11 I removed DND sign from door and went to GZ. Returned 2 hrs. later and room not yet cleaned. Called housekeeping then took computer down to lounge, had a drink, sent a couple emails, returned 50 minutes later, and room was completed. No big deal.
I will certainly stay at the Millenium Hilton again. In fact, I am already planning my next trip in 2006 to NYC, and have no cause to stay anywhere else. Last advice, if you do stay at a Hilton property, become a member of their frequent guest club. 500 miles per stay or a couple other options. If you like to fly first class you can't beat incentive bonuses.

title: “Cozy rooms, loungable restaurant/bar”
text: At first glance, the Tryp Hotel is immediately inviting. It's colorful, welcoming interior, viewable from the street, offers a golden respite from the hustle and bustle of New York City. The look is modern, fashionable, and modest. Having just dropped in from out of town, I was in dire need of a leisurely meal. I recommend one of the homemade "green" Martinis, a couple orders of the shrimp shooters - the shrimp sauce is perhaps one of the most succulent liquids to ever slide down my gullet - and get yourself an entree - they're all hearty and good. The rooms are cozy, colorful and evoke a Mediterranean feel. You feel like you're in your own private pocket of New York City. It's just a shame we had to leave.

title: “Have your DC meeting here”
text: Our group has always been downtown at the JW Marriott and we moved to this location. It was a great move. This place is set up for meetings and handles them well. The staff was always nice and helpful. I liked that I didn't have to wait for elevators and the options for dining and access to the city were great. My room was spacious and had nice amenities.

title: “Have a great time”
text:
I was stay one night and 2days at Dupont circle hotel! got help from hotel respection staff the way 
to IAD and nice bar!
I was stay one night and 2days at Dupont circle hotel! got help from hotel respection staff the way to IAD and nice bar!

title: “Book you Washington DC stay here!!!!!!!”
text:
I was looking for a unique hotel for a 2 day trip to Washington, DC and actually "Googled" "Cool Washington DC hotels" and Hotel Helix poped up in my search. The lobby, lounge and room photos indeed looked very cool so I decided to give it a try. From the moment we drove up to the door we know we were in for a unique experience.
From the Bellman/front desk personnel and managment each person was nicer than the next. Everything (hotel decor, rooms, service) exceeded my already high expectations. There was a terrific happy hour with food and even the other guests were wonderful. Everything in this hotel has a unique attitude.
Hotel Helix is not just lodging; it's a total experience! I strongly recommend it.

title: “Fine Hotel--Very hectic atmosphere”
text: I've stayed at all the hilton properties in Mid-town from the waldorf to the hampton inn. The hilton is fine and in a great spot if you are a tourist, but was too hectic for me. For example even as a Diamond member it took 20 minutes to check in, the elevators were so full that I usually had to wait for 2 full before getting on and the concierge lounge had a line with a "bouncer" at the door was so busy. The room was standard for hilton. Probablly a fun stop if you're visiting as a tourist, but if you're an experienced NYC traveler or business traveler I'd skip...

title: “Want a simple cheap hotel in NYC? This is it.”
text: I had my reservations about hotels such as the Larchmont, mostly due to the shared bathrooms, however, after looking at reviews on Tripadvisor, I decided to reserve it and hope for the best and I am so glad I did. The hotel staff (with the exception of the lady downstairs during breakfast who had her moments) was very polite and helpful. My room was cleaned everyday. There are two showers on each side of the hallway (with only a handful of rooms) so I never had to wait to use the shower or restroom. I saw them being cleaned each morning and never felt they were "dirty" or gross. The hotel provides a robe and slippers for privacy. The beds are a little hard but not uncomfortable. The hotel is located in a quaint Greenwich village neighborhood; you'll see more families walking their dogs than tourists. It's a very safe hotel and are; I was young, female solo traveler and never felt unsafe. The continental breakfast is less than what you're probably used to at major hotel chains, but it has the essentials (coffee, juice, breads, and muffins). All in all, I loved this hotel. It was just what I needed at a super affordable price in a great location. I've found my NYC hotel!

title: “Nice rooms, nice location”
text:
Stayed 2 nights on business related to the attached Memorial Hermann hospital. My room was a nice surprise, being extremely clean and organized. I liked the technology in the room, especially the iPhone/iPod clock-radio in the room since I lost my iPhone charging cord during travel, and thought I was going to have to buy another one. The shower appeared newly remodeled, was clean, and the double shower head was awesome. The room was also very quiet even though I was placed next to the elevators.
There is a sky bridge crossing the street to a moderately size mall with shopping and restaurants.

title: “Great Value, Central Location”
text: We had 5 nights at The Magnolia Dallas which is in a central downtown location and fabulous value. We booked a double Queen room and were upgraded to a one bedroom suite which was much appreciated as we were travelling with our teenage son. We had stayed in Magnolia Denver the year before (which we loved) and Magnolia Dallas certainly lived up to expectations. Great service, clean room, helpful concierge, 'value' breakfast....highly recommended!

title: “Worth what you pay”
text: Having been consistently disappointed with 4-star hotels recently, which really should be ranked 3-stars, this hotel deserves a 4+ star rating. The rooms were impeccable, modern furnishings -- not the bare minimum that seems to be becoming the standard these days; the staff was polite, efficient, and helpful; it's location is perfect; it has a great bar/night scene; and although I did not have a chance to try the restaurant, it looks nice and is well situated. One thing I did notice about our room was the soundproofing. I rarely heard any activity outside our door, even though we were fairly close to the elevator. When I walked out of my room, I was surprised to hear music playing in the hallways at a noticeable level, however did not hear it at all in our room. Great attention to detail when putting this hotel together. I would definitely stay here again, without even looking at any other options. Thank you Hotel Valencia for being a standout and keeping the standard high!

title: “Very comfortable place to stay!”
text: Perfect place to stay if you don't mind the small rooms. When you only need a comfortable place to sleep this is perfect. Within walking distance of Grand Central Station, and many NYC attractions. Will go again if I go back to NYC!

title: “Fabulous place, especially for the cost!”
text: I've stayed here twice now, and it has become my favorite Chicago hotel over The W and even The Peninsula. Now, if you're looking for true 5-star accomodations like The Peninsula or The Ritz, then don't stay here; it's not that kind of place. It's totally unpretentious, hip, minimalist, modern and definitely a 4-star establishment. The Staff are equally unpretentious and friendly. For Chicago, the room rates, spa prices, and the room's "mini-bar/wines/snacks" prices cannot be beat! If you want the best experience, get a corner room; do not get a Cozy King or any standard room with the balcony.

title: “Not Impressed”
text: This hotel has a $99. a night room room rate right it is one block from Times Square. Price is very reasonable however you get what you pay for. You don't receive washcloths you must ask for them and then you are told they don't have anymore. It is an old hotel which needs a lot of work done to it. TV only gets a few stations and they don't have remote control. Our stay there was just awful.

title: “I am at a loss as to exactly how I feel about my stay here.”
text:
The hotel itself is a value deal for NYC, with it's free parking and it's very large pool, which I did not get to try as it was too chilly, it adds a real zing factor to it, but with it's outdated decor, tvs, and only one lift available, that was unGodly slow it detracts from the whole experience, not to mention that the WiFi never worked.....
I am truly trying not to judge it too harshly as I am quite honestly used to a much higher level of hotel..... 
It definitely is NOT a 3 star hotel, except maybe for it's pool area and the added factor of free parking.... the diner/deli/restaurant that is attached to the hotel does not bring it's star rating up either, and probably actually helps detract from it, as the food is bland and without taste, there are signs posted up that you are not allowed to use your laptops or iPads, and it has more of a feeling of a truck stop somewhere along a lonely highway except that there is more than one or two patrons.
As I said, I am torn on this.... Free parking, bonus, large pool, excellent, other than that the rooms and the areas beyond the small lobby made me feel as though I was back in the Brady Bunch era and that did not appeal to me on any level. Would I stay again? Probably not, unless it was summer time and I was able to swim in the pool. *Note* The staff was friendly and did put forth an effort to make it as pleasant as possible.

title: “Horrifying”
text: We booked this hotel for a weekend. The website made it appear charming. Wrong. SCARY!! Photos are completely deceptive. One of the attractions for us was the pet friendly aspect. My dogs would not stay here. NO NO NO. I stayed 30 minutes and paid for one night just to get out of there.

title: “Excellent Location, Very Clean, Reasonable, and Comfortable”
text: We were staying only for a night in NTC and found the Travel In Hotel a perfect spot. Nearby restaurants, very close to the Javits Center, the riverfront for cruises, and not over-the-top expensive. Fabulous, very inexpensive breakfast/lunch restaurant right next door. A big pool with lounge chairs, and... free parking! Someone was always cleaning and sprucing things up! This does not pretend to be the Plaza, but for a quiet, comfortable, and reasonable night or more in the city, this is wonderful!

title: “Great option in D.C.”
text:
I stayed at this hotel in my first trip to Washington D.C. I choose it because of it's price (which was an amazing deal) and because of it's location.
It's an old hotel, however it's well preserved.
The rooms are nice, the bathroom was recently upgrade. Beads where really comfortable, and had all the room we need for our stay.
The front desk staff where specially nice and helpful, they really tried to fix any situation we might have while we stayed there.
They have a restaurant on side, that offers you a buffet option or the menu. We never got the buffet, because in breakfast time, it was mainly fruit, cereal, egg and sausage, and you could get that same stuff from the menu at half the price of the buffet. All the waitresses where really nice and helpful.
It also had a souvenir shop, where they sell also tickets for many attractions in the D.C. and snacks also. One thing that we really appreciate is that they sell you tickets for the trolley tour, and the trolley pick you up at the hotel. This is something really nice, because you don't have to be walking around to find the nearest stop.
Talking about location, this place is only 5 blocks from the White House, north lawn. This 5 blocks are really safe, it is a great neighborhood. You'll find a lot of up class hotel in this area and a lot of people, so you will feel safe walking around. You'll be walking for around 10 minutes from the hotel to the north lawn of the White House.
The nearest metro stop is in Dupont Circle, so it is not much of an option, because is like 6 blocks away.
They also offer you private parking, however for $50 per night. And you have to ask for this on the moment you place your reservation, because the parking lot is 3 levels, however it is full most of the time with employees, and there isn't any other parking lots nearby.
One tip you should consider is that they will print your boarding pass for free at the front desk, no need to pay for the computers and the printers.
This is a great option in the D.C., great price, great location and great staff.

title: “No frills”
text: I received a great deal on priceline and was given a corner handicapped room. The room was large, but the beds were uncomfortable and the facility was shaggy at best. I just used it to sleep so no big deal. If I were to stay longer, I would certiainly not have considered this property.

title: “Most Memorable Stay”
text:
The Driskill is an architectural wonderland, and the minute you walk through the door you become part of its grandeur. And yet, the people who work there are friendly, helpful and down-to-earth. We were made to feel comfortable in every way. (Thank you, Antoinette, you made me feel like a queen.) Everyone was great--the servers at the bar, room service attendants, valets, and a helpful concierge who understands not everyone owns a GPS and printed out directions to the Ladybird Johnson Wildflower Center for me. 
We had a tower room on the 10th floor, and it was a good, quiet choice given there were two weddings at the hotel over the busy Memorial Day weekend. Very comfortable beds, bathrobes and nice room layout. 
Tips: take advantage of the great amenities this hotel has to offer: have a 'Batini' or "Orange Blossom" at the bar--there is live music there most nights, enjoy the excellent location close to the Capitol and Sixth, eat at their restaurant serving some of the best Southern food you can get anywhere (try the fried chicken, mashed potatoes and pecan pie or banana pudding---go ahead, it's your vacation.) If you are disappointed that there is no coffee-maker in your room, do not be too down. There is free coffee in the lobby in a hutch across from the stairs.
This was one of the most memorable hotel stays I can ever remember. Thank you, Driskill Hotel.

title: “Perfect location”
text: This hotel is ideal for sightseeing in Manhatten, a short walk to cental park, 5th ave, Times Square, we went in winter so walking was warming and you get to see more. our room had a king bed in the bed room and a large comfortable pull out in the living area, our kettle didn't work on arrival and this was replaced in 25 mins, breakfast was buffet continental style, good value. Staff were pleasant, great place to stay

title: “Don't stay there ever!”
text:
My sister and I just came back from a two day trip to Boston. We booked the Hilton Financial District through Priceline for $100 a night. We got to the hotel around 1:30pm, after a 4 hour trip from New York, and was politely told by the front desk, that no room was available yet, because they were booked last night. So we had to come back at 3pm, which was to be expected, if it wasn't for the fact that when we did make it back to the hotel at around 3:15pm, there was a 30 min. wait in line to check in! And they had four staff working at the desk. I am not quite sure what kind of issues people were having because our check in literally took less than five minute. 
Once we got the key cards, and get into the room, we could not believe how tiny the room was! We arranged for a room with two double beds. There was barely enough room to leave the luggage on the floor. Nevermind that there was no desk, or a couch. We brought lunch back to the hotel, and had to eat at the wide sill, since that was the only solution without having to eat on the bathroom vanity.
The same evening, we discovered that there was no hot water in the building, and when we called the front desk, we were told that they had no idea when it might come back on. Eventually later that night, the hot water came back on, but it was off again the next morning. 
Also if I had known better I wouldn't have bidded on the Downtown Boston area, because during the weekend, it's a ghost town, luckily it's walkable to Quincy Market. 
I usually wouldn't complain about Priceline hotels, since they are such good deal, but the Hilton Fiancial District definitely does not deserve a four star rating. Our stay was barely a two!

title: “Nice place - very helpful staff”
text: This is a nice place in a great location, but the main reason I recommend it is for the friendly and helpful staff. In miserable weather - an unseasonable heavy wet snow - Raul stood out on 3rd Avenue flagging down off-duty taxis until he found me one. Earlier in the day and the day before, he was helpful and very friendly. Juan at the front desk was very nice as well...everyone was, really. I ate dinner at the inoteca restaurant next door, which was great. I recommend the kale salad. (And don't forget to check-in on Foursquare for a free cocktail with a Newbie Badge.) I would definitely stay at The Marcel again.

title: “Good hotel, bad location”
text:
I stayed at the Sheraton Franklin Plaza for a three-day conference in May. This is a nice hotel but it has just switched from Wyndham to Sheraton and it showed in the housekeeping. The room was cleaned nicely but was missing the usual amenities (when did you ever run out of toilet paper in a hotel?). Still, my calls for new supplies where met promptly. Also, I received a call to make sure that I got the item. The room was comfortable. I wish they had more than a dozen cable channels (note to those with kids: no Nick, Disney or Cartoon Network).
There is a nice looking lobby with a conveniently located bar. Breakfast is very expensive so you'll have to look elsewhere (such as Yannees (sp) which is two blocks away). 
The biggest downside with this hotel is the location. It's not near any sites or shopping. As a result, you're three or four blocks from any activity. This made it impossible to get back and forth to Redding Market during a lunch break. As a result, I suggest being closer to Rittenhouse Square or Independence Hall.

title: “Won a trip”
text: We won a trip for two couples. We REALLY had a good time here. The desk personnel and concierge went beyond customer service. They were knowledgeable, eager to help, and always smiled. Even the room staff were beyond friendly. We didn't pay for our rooms this time, but next time, we'll stay here. Right in the middle of all that is New York. Barely a 20 minute walk to Times Square and it took that long due to traffic lights and window shopping.

title: “Great downtown hotel”
text: This is a terrific place to stay in downtown Denver. The hotel is beautiful with great contemporary decor and a wonderful, friendly and helpful staff. The location is wonderful, convenient to everything in the downtown area--the convention center, the Denver Center for Performing Arts, the Pavillions, the capitol, and the 16th Street Mall. The room was clean and nicely furnished with a very comfortable bed, lots of pillows, and a flat screen TV. The bathroom was nice although I would have preferred to have the vanity outside. Good water pressure and nice clean modern sink and fixtures. It did not, however, have any towel racks! The amenities--soap, shampoo, conditioner, lotion--were first rate. It was very quiet although the hotel appeared to be quite full and the lobby area was teaming with people even late at night. The Peaks bar on the 27th floor has a fabulous view of the mountains and is beautifully furnished. The restaurant on the main floor was very attractive with high ceilings, very modern china, lots of windows, and good food and service (only had breakfast there). The workout facility is very impressive--lots of state of the art equipment, a lap pool and a very nice outdoor hot tub. Way nicer than the usual hotel fitness center, more like a real gym. Lots of large, thick towels. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “OUR LITTLE GEM.”
text: Stayed there for 3 nights. Service was great and lots of restaurants around. Parking is expensive but worth it,found my car upfront after i called down . Bags were handled by the bellman and the valet ,very friendly and efficient. Special thanks to the smiling african valet guy for directions i did not get lost. Looking forward for the boston marathon!

title: “Good for a short stay, but...”
text: Stayed here one night while we were in town for a hockey game at the Garden. If the Garden is your destination, you can't beat this hotel for its location alone. It only took us a couple of minutes to walk door to door. The place is in great condition (it's new, so this is to be expected), and SPOTLESSLY clean (and I'm a fanatic when it comes to cleanliness in a hotel room). The bathrooms are very nice. On the downside, the rooms are TINY-- not "on the small side" but TINY. We had a room with two double beds, so perhaps the single-bed rooms have more elbow room. However, our room didn't even have enough space to open up a suitcase without putting it on the bed (no room for a valet here!) --definitely not a room I would want to stay in for several days. I thought the room was very expensive ($232 incl. taxes -- AAA rate), considering its size and the lack of amenities offered by this hotel. There is a decent steakhouse next door, but again, VERY expensive (it wasn't the food, but the bar bill that was a shocker!) There are, however, lots a restaurant options in the area. All in all, this hotel is very good, but overpriced. If you don't require a double room, and if you can get a good price on a room, grab it...I don't think you'll be disappointed. (A quick response to some other reviews: this is NOT a bad area of the city. I lived and worked in Boston for several years, and this area was always a little "grittier" than Back Bay or Beacon Hill, but it has undergone a gentrification of sorts in the past few years. The removal of the elevated train tracks in front of the Garden has also done a lot for this area. When (and if) the Big Dig is finished, this area will definitely be the better for it.)

title: “Very nice hotel, great location”
text:
First of all, the hotel is very nice. The staff were very professional & polite from the front desk, bell boy, valet, security & engineering. The rooms are amazingly beautiful & clean, their beds are comfortable. They have wooden/tiles floors which is great for a pet friendly hotel. 
However, they have some small kinks that they need to fix before I can give them 5 stars. They only have 3 elevators. So, if you come late at night (fri-sat) expect for a wait since the pool party is on the 4th floor. We waited close to 15min for an elevator. I would also avoid staying on the fourth floor if you want to rest. The tv & iron in our room didn't work so we had to call engineering to fix it. Besides that, our overall stay was pleasant. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “A quick getaway”
text: My husband and I had our first getaway without the kids and decided to do it Chicago style. We were very impressed with the Knickerbocker. Great location and friendly service. I liked how they were able to renovate the hotel to make it comfortable and up to date, but keep some of the old world charm and architecture. As for parking -- it's Chicago. We tried to go cheaper (valet at the hotel is $50) by parking across the street in the parking garage. We missed the 24 hour mark by 11 minutes and ended up paying $8 more than if we had valeted it and with non of the convenience. If your going to drive, just valet it and pay the $50.

title: “Not what I expected”
text:
This hotel was chosen because it was near the Metro and only one stop from Union Station. Also it was a new hotel and was a green hotel.
First very hard to find as it is in a redeveloping area.
Second no coffee at the food area in the am only starbucks speciality coffees .
Food cooked by Micro wave and served on paper products.. Not appetizing and I do not use a micro wave or eat micro waved foods.
The room was weird as it was very small and only a small portable closet that only had rooms for one guest.
Towels and linens in bath were of a poor quality
Mattress was not the usual Marriott Slee[ , in fact did not sleep well.
Right on top of the rail and hear trains early in the am.
No restaurants of quality near by for dinner .
So would i stay again NO 
I prefer to stay in a hotel that has the expectations fulfilled and this one did not

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
We got lost!! It was on the hard side to find. The parking sucks, and that is all that is not good about this hotel.
The front desk staff are very nice and helpful. We got our room very fast, and we did call the front desk for directions to get there. 
The room itself was very nice. A lot of room, and nice and quiet.
The bed was very nice and we both got a great nice sleep. We were a little worried when we were going up the elevator, and another guest said that the street side of the hotel was very noisey. Well we were on the street side and we did not hear the noise. Breakfast was nice and tastey. A lot of restaurants to choose from, so that is nice. It was all within walking distance, which was good, because again the parking was not fun. The traffic is terrible, and very hard to get around, but not the hotel's fault, and once inside you can walk to get around.

title: “Wonderful hotel with a lot of terrific perks!”
text:
Beautiful bay side location, complimentary coffee in the morning, wine reception in the evening, and milk and cookies at 9PM. Need I say more? Our queen room on the 8th floor was surprisingly much more spacious than I was expecting from some of the reviews. Although we didn't splurge on a bay view, we had a terrific view of downtown. Both the room size and view were superior to the one we had at Monaco (another Kimpton property at Union Square) a few years back. The Harbor Court is my new favorite hotel in San Francisco. We loved coming back each day to the crackling fireplace in their wonderful lobby/living room - and the treats! 
Staff is professional and friendly, although a little reserved which may be why some reviewers seem to indicate they seem aloof or uncaring. But the fact that the coffee, wine, and cookies are served on time each day, rooms are spotless, and we got all of our questions answered at the front desk easily and promptly, shows that the staff is truly top notch. We met some wonderful staff members, including Brad at the front desk and Michael at wine hour, who clearly work hard to ensure the comfort of guests.
Our stay was not without glitches, but the hotel handled these issues very well. Due to high winds and pouring rain, we returned our first night to find a power outage in the hotel. The staff more than made up for this issue by passing out glow sticks which was a lot of fun, and pouring more complimentary wine! In fact, the power outage turned out to be one of the highlights of our trip. The atmosphere was very romantic sitting in the dark lobby in front of the fireplace, and as we made our way up the staircase to our room, we found that staff had lit the entire 8 floors with glow sticks which was very clever and pretty. In the AM we had lukewarm water to shower in, but PG&E did not get the power turned back on until 6:30 AM which was not the hotels fault. We also had a lamp that quit working during our stay, but a maintenance worker came immediately (at 10 PM none the less), assessed the problem and had it fixed for us - all in a span of about 20 minutes.
If we have one complaint at all about the Harbor Court, it is that it is somewhat removed from the hustle and bustle of Union Square. BUT, we knew this before booking, and we chose the serene Embarcadero location instead as we wanted to be on the water. Union Square, Fisherman's Wharf and the other San Francisco attractions are all within walking distance, and/or less than 10 minutes away by either the F Line streetcars or BART. It is also right next to the Ferry Building which has a number of places to eat, Peet's Coffee and a farmers market on 3 days of the week. The quiet location also made for a wonderful nights rest.
One tip on San Francisco in general. If you plan to do a cable car trip during the day, take the F Line to Fisherman's Wharf and catch it there. The lines at Powell/Market were close to 2 hours when we went at 11 AM. No wait at all at Taylor Street at Fisherman's Wharf. The California Street cable car (which starts a few blocks from the hotel) is currently not running due to work being done.
To summarize, the Harbor Court is a wonderful hotel, with terrific "extras," a great staff, and a peaceful location on the bay. I would highly recommend it to anyone.

title: “Beautiful boutique hotel at great location with friendly staff - and a fabulous roof-top lounge”
text: Very nice design-hotel. rooms are quite small but location is great for restaurants, bars, museums, galleries, shopping.. even breakfast is included - a small but good and healthy breakfast buffet. very friendly and helpful staff. the only thing I did not like: the dirty breakfast tables. I recommend this hotel!

title: “Just OK!!”
text:
We just got back from a long weekend in Memphis!! The front desk staff is not the friendliest. They do give the impression of being bothered when we asked them questions. 
The biggest problem I had with the hotel is that they charge you $5/day for each car you park in the garage. I didn't even know until I checked out. So if you can park on the street on the weekends. Had we known we would have because they direct you to park in the garage and tell you nothing about the charges!!
The bonus was the location to Beale. If it had been summer we would've walked, but we had below freezing temps so we drove. The room was great except there are no fridges or microwaves. 
The workout room is small and only has a treadmill, bike, stepper, and 50-yr old universal!!
The Greek restaurant, O'kypos, was good, especially the Gyros! Not the cleanest but we'd go back. 
So check out a Memphis Grizzlies game and Beale St. We also went to the Civil Rights Museum which was very enlightening and I believe most would enjoy it.
All in all we would stay somewhere else if we went back and wanted to stay downtown.

title: “great hotel with every ammenity I needed and some I didn't know I needed”
text: Great free breakfast, Great staff ,Good fitness center ,Free Laundry, ice maker in room, conveinent to highway system, runners path near hotel, Stayed with 4 women and adequate room for us all to get ready. Staff cares about comfort, Nice lounge area with huge flat screen TV if your roomates get on your nerves. Highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a nice place at a great value

title: “Large rooms in an out of date hotel that definitely needs redecoration”
text:
The lobby looks impressive buth as soon as you get in the elevator you'll find out that the hotel is really out of date. Although the rooms are large the carpet is old, the paint flakes off and the room doesn't feel clean. The bathroom is very tiny, especially the shower. In our room with kitchen wasn't even a kettle to make some tea, only a frying pan. The noise outside especially at night keeps you awake. But at least one of our rooms had a window with a view. The other studio that we've booked looked out on a shaft with no daylight and no window that could be opened. Terrible. Light bulbs were broken, the painting light above the bed couldn't be switched off completely so there was a light shining in your eyes all night. 
It's a long walk to get to Times Square. The hotel is conveniently located if you'll have to visit Madison Square Garden.
Unfortunately we will not recommend this hotel to others.

title: “Great rooms, but very noisy on weekends!”
text: This is a very cool, interesting Hotel. The staff were friendly and helpful. The only problem (and it was a big one) is that the Gaslamp Plaza Suites is located right smack in the middle of most of the clubs in the gaslamp district. We stayed here on a Saturday night and the noise from the street kept us up until about 2:30 AM. This was pounding music from the clubs and cars, as well as the sounds of people out on the street. It may be better on weeknights or on higher floors (we were on the 4th floor.) After this, I wouldn't stay here again.

title: “Good location...”
text: stayed here 4th - 7th October 2011. Great spot for access pretty much anywhere downtown/midtown right up to Central Park. Hotel seems fairly new and facilities are good and all is clean. Staff are friendly and helpful. Recommended.

title: “Horrible place to stay, but rather nice staff”
text: Beeing foreigners we arrived in San Diego unprepared for the labour day weekend meaning that there was no reasonable prices to be had in this town. The staff at the frontdesk was nice and helpful but that's probably the only good thing to say here. The room was small, outdated and not too clean. There was a smell of urine/chloride from the bathroom that was horrible. And due to the busy weekend it was quite expensive too. Have stayed at other Motel 6 in the U.S. but this is the worst one by far. There's plenty of other places to stay in San Diego, so my advice is go find them instead of staying here.

title: “Great value for money”
text: This is the most convenient hotel in the area of the Bush Convention and Toyota Centers. The suites are very comfortable and have all amenities. Breakfast is typical American style, but sufficient. The staff and management are very friendly and helpful. Wi-Fi is available all over the place and free of charge! Within 10-15 min. walking distance there are plenty of restaurants and shopping centers available.

title: “Nice hotel in a nice neighbourhood”
text: Stayed here two nights in october 2011. Very friendly staff. All tips and answers to our questions were found very usefull. Ideal location within walking distance of metro so only a few minutes away from the tourist highlights. The bar at the hotel was rather expensive however there are restaurants and bars very close by.

title: “First time stay @ this Hotel”
text:
This was my first stay at Marriott East in Indy, Henry was a highlight of my stay. He is fantastic! On my arrival, I was the last of my party to arrive. I was standing in the lobby waiting for a friend to meet me. He asked if I was arriving or departing. When I reply just arriving, he says "welcome and if there is anything I can help you with while you are staying with us just ask and I will be happy to help. He must work around the clock because it seemed that everytime I turned around he was there asking others and myself if we needed anything. As I was leaving he thanked me for coming and said please come visit us again. Now I realize this hotel has plenty of employees but I must say Henry is the only one that stood out. He always had a smile on his face!! Many places I stay are not as pleasant as this stay was do to this man.....Henry. I can only hope he is treated well and with respect. 
Renee

title: “Okay hotel, horrible location”
text:
I feel bad for this hotel and its management. They've taken care of all of the basics that guests typically gripe about: comfortable rooms, nice hotel and easy parking.
But the location is just horrible. It's just off I-70 in an industrial area. Why they ever built a hotel here is beyond me. There is nowhere to go, nothing to do and you're trapped at the hotel unless you're driving 10 or 15 minutes somewhere else.
We booked this hotel blind on a stay to the Denver area. We wanted a non-downtown location. But the Aurora neighbhorhood is certainly not the place you want to be spending 3 nights.
I have no other complaints about the hotel. Checkin staff were wonderful and hotel workers were really above average. The location is just depressing and one to avoid if you're a tourist on vacation. It's always tough trying to locate a hotel when you're far away trying to get the lay of the land. But this was definitely the wrong hotel for our family vacation!

title: “Out for comedy show weekend”
text: Hotel was clean and nice for the money. Located 5 miles south of downtown. On a busy street. Hard to get out if u want to make a left turn getting back on interstate. Me and my wife was there to see Kevin Hart Comedy Show.. Only complaint 'was we in the non smoking section and smell like smoke "WEED" in the hallways

title: “Do not stay here!”
text:
We were in town with teen-age girls for a softball tournament and did not have a say in the pick of this hotel. It is in a questionable part of town. 
When we arrived their were two families traveling together. We asked for rooms next to each other but were told this was not possible. When we escorted our friends to their room, we found a box cutter and broken glass all over one bed. We went back to the office. There was a couple in there without a reservation asking for a room. They were told they had plenty available. Yet they could not give us rooms next to each other? 
Due to the clientel, we would not allow our girls to go to each others rooms unless in a group. Appareny they let truckers use the parking lot as there were always several trucks parked with loud engines running the while 3 days we were there. 
Breakfast consists of the bare minimum. So if you are looking for staples like cereal or toast, don't look here. Danishes are all you get! And don't expect the free WiFi to work. No connection available. 
We are going back to Houston on late July and will avoid this place like the plague!!!

title: “Great Deal For A Trendy Hotel if you don't mind the noise”
text: We went to San Diego to celebrate our 1st wedding anniversary and watch the Chargers vs Eagles game. My frugal husband insisted we stay somewhere cheap but I was determined to bypass the standard price conscious accommodations such as holiday inn, etc. I found a great package for flights and accommodations at the Pearl. Overall we had a pretty good stay with a few minor complaints. The accommodations are very clean & trendy. You can see they pride they have in maintaining the hotel with the cute little additions (pet fish, daily quote sheet with menu specials, adopt a towel). It is true that the washrooms have minimal renos (faucets & lights) but they are clean. The staff is friendly. The food is delicious (we found a coupon on their website that gave us 2 for 1 dinner entrees if we purchased 2 drinks) however we had more than two since we were crawling distance to our room and our waitress let us know that they had some wines on special for $5/glass. And the location is fantastic. Biggest downfall is parking. We paid an additionally $10/day (which we figured would guarantee us a spot) however on Saturday night we didn't finding parking and were told they'd deduct the cost from our bill (but forgot to) and told to park across the street in the Medical clinic as they don't check on weekends. The only time we benefited from the parking pass was the first day when we wanted to offload our suitcases. I believe parking in the front is free (4-5 tiny stalls) but hotel parking on the side (4-5 stalls) is charged. You should be able to find street parking during the day or during the week. Parking Friday & Sat night is the biggest issues. The other issue we had was the paper thin walls. You can hear everything. I had issues sleeping one day because someone was chatting outside. I could hear them clear as day and when I commented (in a normal voice) to my husband they quieted down. Closing the windows helped a little. We live in the heart of downtown at home so the street traffic & airplane noise didn’t bother us too much. Aside for these two issues we had a great stay and would likely come back.

title: “I definetly recommend the hotel,clean room,good breakfast and friendly pesonal.”
text: We were only 4 days in New York even thought the hotel was very good,the weather was very cold.New York is expensive city,if u want to eat or do shopping not on main streets as they are expensive.The hotel is next blok to Empire State Building,easy to walk all main attraction places.I do definetly recommend the hotel.

title: “Great hotel, just a little out of the way”
text: Classic Kimpton. Friendly, cool, luxurious. The staff were terrific, esp. the woman at the front desk with the crazy hair. We had some very slight complications with amenities, and the food from room service wasn't top notch, but the room itself (a junior suite) was really nice. Huge tub, fantastic linens, very sleek and attractive design. My only real complaint is that it's not really near anything, even a Starbucks or other coffee shop. If you're willing to walk over to 9th Ave and the heart of Hell's Kitchen, it is of course lousy with great places, but those are just a little far, especially in less than perfect weather. But the location is, I suppose, why you can stay at a genuinely luxurious hotel in NYC for the prices they're charging.

title: “Excellent choice for a city break!”
text:
My husband and I stayed for a week at Staybridge during Christmas 2011 and we could not have chosen better! 
The hotel is just as is described/shown on its site http://www.staytimessquare.com/.
The location is perfect, just a few minutes’ walk from Times Square. In fact, it is in front of the Port Authority bus station so it’s ideal if you’re looking to visit the outlets. The road the hotel is on is not so great but you don't feel unsafe. 
The rooms are spacious, clean and comfortable as is the bathroom (cleaned daily with plenty of fresh towels). The kitchenette is fully equipped and great if you don’t intend on eating out all the time. The mattress is extremely comfortable and sleep quality is excellent. Don’t expect items such as dimmer switches and fancy lighting however. The rooms are all the same (except the bed type), modern, have all the basic comforts but nothing over-the-top. (The only downside is the very limited wardrobe space).
There is no room service but you can order in from any take-away in the.
Even though we visited the hotel during the Christmas holidays and the hotel was full, we never had any trouble with slow lifts even with our room being on one of the very top floors.
It is good to have breakfast included. This is not a buffet with very many options but has a small choice of everything and very much to go around. This is a self-service breakfast so don’t expect to be seated and served. You may also take breakfast up to the room.
This is the perfect hotel for a city break and we would definitely stay here again!

title: “Very Nice, Clean Place”
text:
I travel quite a bit for work and I have stayed at this chain twice. I have enjoyed my stay each time. I have stayed in Houston near the Galaria and this one here in Dallas. This used to be a Bradford Suites. They have been remodeled and are very nice to stay in. The main difference is the one here in Dallas charges a little extra for parking and the one I have stayed at in Houston did not. 
The bedding was nice in both places. I don't like cheap bedding, by that I mean I don't like linens that look and feel like they are from 1980. These were clean and fresh. I really enjoy the TV that swivels aournd through the bookcase. Nice touch. 
The breakfast isn't anything special, but hey it's breakfast and it's hot. 
The down side to this Dallas location was that getting to it was a little challenging, but not a deal breaker. Parking in the garage was extra. 
Overall I like the hotel. I would stay there again. Especially a longer stay because it has a kitchenette.

title: “Great experience in NYC”
text: I stayed here for 2 nights in April 2012, very nice reception friendly staff, I was in room 201 which is across the courtyard up to the left. The first night the neighbor had some kind of attitude problem but when he stopped yelling I went straight to sleep. The breakfast was great, everything tasty and adequate for the price in NY. Second night was better, great night sleep and again good breakfast. I will stay here in a couple of months again since I will travel for business to NYC frequently.

title: “Avoid Staying Here If At All Possible!”
text: My mother booked this hotel for us for one night in advance when we knew we would be coming in on a late flight and wanted something close to the airport. The next day we were headed to another destination, and thank goodness for that! The shuttle service to the Days Inn was very touch and go from the airport. Although the driver himself was friendly, the hotel staff did not notify him of our pickup in a timely manner which left us waiting at the airport much longer than expected after a late flight. Once we arrived at the hotel, the service was incredibly cold and upon entering the room we were shocked at its condition. At first it was difficult to tell if the room had even been cleaned as pillows seemed to have just been thrown on the bed. Thankfully, the room at least smelled clean even though the air conditioner didn't work well and there were cracks running from one wall to the other. The next morning while checking out, a woman and her two young children entered the lobby after having just seen their room. The woman said "This place is disgusting- there is no way we are staying in that room." She proceeded to ask reception for a cab to take her to another hotel. That pretty much sums up our experience. As for the cost, I don't consider $90 cheap for a room in this condition, surrounded by what seemed to be a very seedy neighborhood. I have never written a hotel review before, but this experience needed to be shared. Due to this hotel, I will not be staying at another Days Inn again.

title: “5 Minute WALK to Union Square!”
text:
As a small motel owner myself, I check out hotel areas and reviews - especially on Trip Advisor. That is how I found the Mosser - and what a find! From my first contact, to their last detail, everything was perfect. 
I know the reviews are generally positive, but they don't say half of the story...
The staff is professional and friendly, and go out of their way to make life easy for you. The entire hotel is steeped in history, but clean and modern in decor. The doorman and valet remove your vehicle from your list of concerns - delivering it back to you with only 20 min. notice. (I LOVE that because my main reason to shy away from SF is the question of what to do with my car!) The biggest surprise, though, is that the hotel is so well located, it was a mere ten minute walk (with a child in tow) along safe, well lit and highly foot-traveled streets to UNION SQUARE, and all it holds. Of course, from that location, one can pick up Muni, BART, etc. and go just about anywhere in the entire Bay Area!
The front desk handed us keys and protein bars for the morning, in case muffins and coffee weren't enough for us before a scheduled meeting. As we entered the room, which was small - BUT - had plenty of room for two of us and seemed the "right" size for the Victorian heritage of the hotel, we were greeted with a large flat panel TV, a modern and well appointed room, and an array of gifts on our bed! From local area brochures and information - to a box of chocolates - we were treated like valued friends from the outset.
