Only about 1/3 of the rooms have a shared bath situation, which, from what I noticed was just the bath tub/shower. That leads me to believe that is the ONLY portion of the bathroom one shares -- the remainder being privately held in each room. Check with the reservationist on that one. WE had a private bath, as do the remaining 110+ rooms. Our room also looked out on 4th and we kept the window open all night without issues from traffic noise. 
Price-wise, I felt I got a SCREAMING deal. I paid $105 INCLUDING PARKING ($30 itself), tax, etc. To be so close to the hub of activity at that price was just ridiculously positive. We will be back!!

title: “We're headed back!!!!”
text: This is actually my first review ever on Trip Advisor...And I travel constantly. Had to do it because i'm just that excited and had such a pleasant experience. My best friend and I stayed here for a random girls wknd in Feb 2011. She came from Dallas and I came from Atlanta. First time in Memphis for both of us. We had such an AMAZING time. We fell in love with the city and this wonderful hotel. The staff was the absolute BEST. Wonderful room, good breakfast, great service, perfect location. We had absolutely no complaints...and we are picky ladies. Anyway, we decided we needed to do it again. We'll be there in 10 days! Room is booked and we cant wait to see you all again!!!!

title: “Tucked Away, Trendy, Tiny”
text: This would be my 2nd time to stay in the Hudson New York. I picked it again because of it's location, trendiness and at the time of my stay, the price. My room for my 1 night stay was $279, which included 2 beds and a larger bathroom. It's lounge/club downstairs on the lobby level was a ton of fun on a Friday night, great crowd and super music mix. Oh, and the breakfast room service was out of this world! We ordered 4 different things between the 4 of us and it was a superb!

title: “Loved this place...amazing!”
text:
This place is huge! I would definitely stay here again. I am not sure I would stay here if I was there for sight seeing as it is quite a ways from the main attractions in the city, but for business travel, you can't find a better hotel.
Fitness center: Amazing! Had everything anyone could need! 5 Stars for sure!
Restaurants: Very, very good! Great service and wonderful food!
Rooms: Not very big, but perfectly appointed and very clean.
Meeting rooms: This place had it all!
Service: The housekeeping staff was very friendly and did a great job. Every staff member said hello when I passed.
Location: Kind of out of the way for the sights, but not too far from the Metro or you could definitely find a taxi there. It was about a $20 cab ride to the Capitol Building.
This is a business travellers dream. Everything you could possibly need under one roof, even a UPS/FedEx shipping center. Shops, restaurants, fitness center, shoe shine, and more!

title: “Frustrating Experience”
text: I would like to start by saying I have never written a hotel review before; however, I felt like I would be doing other travelers a disservice by not sharing my experience. My initial room was so small I had to go beg the front desk for a room with double beds, their only solution was upgrading me to a single bed suite with a pull out couch (which they charged me an additional 30/night fee for a 4 night stay) and told me to try again the next day to see if I could get into a double room. I tried the following day and then the following day but failed. I was stuck on the 6th floor facing air conditining units out one window and a brick wall out the other. Cell phone service was almost nonexistent due to this. The sink in the bathroom had cracks, the carpet smelt and the bed didnt sleep much better than the couch. I booked this hotel thru Priceline's name your own price which had this hotel classified as a 4 star, I'd say it's more closer to a 2.5 after staying 4 nights.

title: “Good Value”
text:
Spent a few days here last week for a short vacation visit to DC. I just wanted to echo the reviews of others – 1) great location, close walk to the National Mall, within the George Washington University complex and almost next door to the White House. 2) Good value choice providing a clean suite with a small kitchenette, comfortable bed, and even a small sitting area though only basic in quality. Convenient CVS store next door. Recommend BTS a few blocks away for great burgers – skip the shakes for a shaketail! ) 
The staff was friendly though unable to extend a requested late checkout. Note you can get a return ride to airport from hotel for a reasonable price (Reagan @ $20). The dual entrances and elevators are a bit unusual but were not a problem for us. Only negative was room location on ground floor by parking ramp. Would certainly stay here again.

title: “Great Location”
text:
This was our first trip to Seattle and we wanted to stay in a convenient location.
The Inn at the Market was perfect. The staff was very nice and helpful and the beds were soooo comfortable. Lots of restaurants and shopping close by. The only negative was the bathroom. There was a lot of room but no separate shower and not much of a vanity. Wasted space and needed update.

title: “Good location and nice staff!”
text:
This was my second stay in this hotel. 
The staff is helpfull ! 
You have free wireless.
Very nice breakfast (delicious muffins)
Nice view!Close to times square and city center.
Good quality/price ratio for NY!
I would go back, and reccomend it from every point of view!

title: “Thin walls”
text: Stayed one night on our way to Maui.  Room was average the staff very helpful and friendly.  The only problem was we could hear the couple in the next room.  Compared to where we stayed on our return trip it really wasn't that bad.

title: “Modern, clean hotel in a great location offering great value in NYC! Excellent hotel!”
text:
Great location, very easy to find, easy access to times square and rest of Manhattan.
Check in process is very quick and simple on the computers in the lobby, the guys there will help and show you to your room, giving you some useful info about the hotel on the way.
The room is small compared to other US rooms but has everything you need and the bed slides up to create more space and it has everything you need - big tv, iron, hair dryer, large shower etc. 
The galley is a great idea - free water, ice, coffee and fridge on every floor which is very convenient.
Concierge on level 4 are very helpful. The free wifi in the rooms and computers in reception come in handy for researching attractions or checking flight details.
We booked on last minute .com and saved 25% with the advance purchase offer which made it even better value.
All in all a fantastic hotel!

title: “Absolutely Perfect”
text:
My husband and I celebrated his birthday by staying at the Hotel George this past weekend (1/6/07) and the hotel was perfect. Upon arrival, we easily checked in, were given a room facing the main street with plenty of natural sunlight. There was a night turndown service, which was unexpected, and the room was outstanding. Flat screen TV's, marble bath, separate tub and shower, comfortable bed, complimentary bathrooms, stocked mini-bar...I could go on and on. The pictures don't do it justice - the fitness room has individual flat screen tv's at each cardio machine, and provides headphones for your listening pleasure. AWESOME! A short walk to Union Station - very nice. Upon check out, the hotel manager remembered that I had stated when checking in that it was my husband's birthday. The hotel gave us a complimentary bottle of wine to celebrate - which they would have left in our room, but we had the "Do no disturb" sign out. That was going above and beyond anything I expected!
For those comments made by others about the noise, please keep this one piece of advice in mind - you are staying at a hotel in the heart of a downtown area - there is going to be noise!! To me, anyone who was awaken from there sleep must be naturally light sleepers. As for safety - again, you are in a downtown area. Yes, there are homeless people, but they are not intrusive or hostile. I did not use the valet service because there was no need, there was ample street parking, which was extremely safe. 
I will definitely be returning to this hotel for years to come!

title: “An Amazing Evening in Fells Point, MD”
text:
Recently I took up the opportunity to stay at the newest addition to my favorite part of Baltimore - The Inn at the Black Olive in beautiful Fells Point. I am a Baltimore native and was so happy to be warmly greeted in this super clean, open, and aroma rich building that had a very Mediterranean feel permeating from the moment we walked in. The cafe allowed for a quick browsing of wines, a sample of hummus, and a nice place to get adjusted before heading to our room. 
The room was very large. The open spaces, the art on the wall, the music that was playing when we entered were all chosen with taste and our comfort in mind. The bedroom was private, quiet, and had a bed that trumps all other beds! The bathroom was equally spacious with a tub that resembled a small pool and a shower that (as a guy I take shorter showers) was hard to get out of because it was so luxurious.
I have stayed in many of my hometown hotels and B&Bs, and without a doubt I will no longer be needing any of those places because I'm nominating the Inn at the Black Olive as my dream home away from home.

title: “Good Location in the Times Square Storm”
text:
My wife and I stayed here in June of 2012. We had tickets to see a show and were only in town for two days; we wanted to stay near to the theater and enjoy the Midtown area. They have recently remodeled the lobby and lounge areas and did a great job. The decor is sleek and hip, maybe a little too hip for our tastes. 
The R Lounge, looking over Times Square, seemed like a great place to sit for a drink or two prior to an evening on the town. We asked for a table for two in a lounge that was only a third full and found ourselves placed in the center of the room (away from the windows/views) and at a table right next to a larger, and louder, party. The techno music thumping in the lounge added to the stress levels until my wife and I made eye contact and both stood up and left. We are not old folks, we enjoy a party and dancing as much as most folks, but I find this strange trend toward thumping computer beats very annoying (I have stopped shopping at some clothing stores because of this same issue). I'm not bad-mouthing it, just letting the reader know what to expect and how we felt about it. Some folks, like the louder hipsters next to us, seem to enjoy it. 
The hotel itself is in a great location for tourists (first time NYC tourists). We have been to NYC before and quickly discovered that perhaps the Renaissance was not in the ideal location for us. We spent time in Chinatown, Chelsea, and Hell's Kitchen for the food and sights and found ourselves a bit sad to have to return to the throngs of tourists in order to get back to the hotel. 
The rooms were very large for NYC, the housekeeping was fantastic. The desk clerks and folks working downstairs were very friendly and made great recommendations for food in the area. Not a bad place, it was a good two day trip, but I believe next time we'll pick something a little further from the crowds.

title: “What happened to our beloved Kimpton chain? The Helix is in NEED of repair”
text:
This is the worst Kimpton I've ever checked into. I'm apart of the Kimpton loyalty program, and Kimpton prides itself on clean, well maintained rooms. The Helix did not meet those standards at all.
After check in, I asked to be moved to a second room because the first room had stains on the curtains. The second room I was given had rust around the bathtub drain, wall paper coming off at the seams and peeling paint. It was so disappointing. My room wasn't dirty though, it was just an issue of the hotel not maintaining their property.
On the positive side, the location and service was great! The Helix is near Dupont Circle and it's in a safe neighborhood. As a woman traveling alone, I felt safe walking back to the hotel at 1am after having drinks with friends. The staff is very friendly, most of them are Washington natives so they are great resource on how to navigate the city. 
I also really enjoyed the free champagne during the Hotel's daily wine reception/happy hour.

title: “Depressing grotty hotel”
text: The only good thing about this hotel is the location. We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights before our cruise to Alaska (room only thank goodness). The hotel decor was depressing the sheets were threadbare and the bathroom the pits. They messed up our booking due to the fact that someone there booked us in the previous weekend so when we arrived on the Friday evening at 10.00pm US time (very tired) after a 10 hour flight they said there was no reservation for us. We had no option but to use our credit card to cover a one nights stay until it was sorted. We then had to wake up at 3.00am to phone the travel agent (due to the time difference) to try and sort it. This did not get sorted properly until the Sunday morning when we were due to leave for the cruise. This spoilt our stay in Seattle.

title: “Great place to Stay.”
text:
I stayed 2 nights for a business seminar. This hotel is very clean and quiet. Breakfast was good but would be better with scrambled eggs. What I like is that it has full breakfast they were out of scrambled eggs when I stayed. 
Great big screen TV. Just a great stay. The Manager and Staff make you feel special when you check in. I will be back many more times and will refer everyone.

title: “Great location and wonderful customer service”
text: A good time was had by all. Thats what my husband and I had to say about our last trip to SF. We stay in the Donatello - which is so pefectly located to everything. The rooms are comfortable, quiet and have everything you need already there. The bed deserves its own sentence: COMFORTABLE!! We'll stay there everytime.

title: “Amazing hotel! Will be back again!”
text: Stayed here for two nights... Excellent location just a few blocks from Union Square, and just a half hour walk over to AT&T Park... Excellent sized rooms with some of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in. Top notch staff and a very comfortable stay. I will be back again for certain next time I am in San Francisco!

title: “Great boutique hotel in the heart of Pike's Market”
text: This little hotel may be a bit on the expensive side but it's well worth the price for its location, just steps from Pike's Market. It's staff were, without exception, friendly and helpful. The hotel has a large viewing balcony on the fifth floor overlooking the market and Puget Sound. You can bring your own food and drink onto the balcony so even if you opt for a city view room, you can still enjoy the evening sunset view of the bay. Because the hotel in on a hill side, the city rooms do not provide much in the way of a view, as you're mostly just looking at the building across the street, but we didn't mind as the city view rooms were less expensive and we were so tired from walking all day that we basically crashed when we got back to our room each night.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
We had booked the Westin Philadelphia and despite confirming the reservation, when we arrived we were informed they were overbooked. They "walked" us to the Sofitel.
We arrived at the Sofitel and were greated by a very friendly gentleman at the desk. He was in the process of checking us in and the manager had overheard what happened with the Westin and instructed him to upgrade us to a suite. Very cool! I think it was probably some kind of Julior Suite as it wasn't a huge room, but it was a good size and very nice. It had a sitting area with a couch and desk seperate from the bedroom. The decor was contemporary and comfortable. The bed was very nice, soft. Nice sized bathroom.
We ordered room service and it was pretty good. It was around 12am when we ordered, available until 2am I believe. I had the Philly cheesesteak and it would have been great but the overcooked the beef and dried it out a little. My girlfriend had the turkey sandwich and said it was very good.
We were there just the one night checked in after 11pm and out around 10am, so we didn't really get to enjoy the facility. It looked like it had a very nice bar and restaurant, but again we didn't get to take advantage.
The room does have a mini bar stocked with a nice variety of items. Pricing is what you would expect. Except for Jack Daniels $12 for a mini bottle?

title: “OK for one night”
text:
We stayed in San Francisco during the Bay to Breakers foot race and had great difficulties in getting a hotel for that night at a decent price. If those hadn't been the circumstances, we wouldn't have stayed in Marriott SF Fisherman's Wharf. 
The lobby is possibly the best feature of the hotel, it's quite stylish and actually raised our expectations of the rest of the premises. The rooms, however, were a bitter disappointment. The hotel has only three floors, and at first we were given a room from the second floor. A horrible cigarette stench faced us on opening the door and we turned on our heels and went to demand for a new room. The next room we got was facing a very busy intersection (Columbus Ave & Bay St), and the traffic noise was overwhelming. I couldn't have gotten any sleep there, not even with earplugs. Again, we went back for a new room - care to guess, what we got? Yes, the stinking room, which we were offered at first. They had brought there some kind of an air purifying device, which helped a bit, but still some of the stench was left behind. Actually later that night we found a cigarette stub from the room, so the housekeeping hadn't been that careful either. 
If we ignore the problems mentioned above, the hotel itself is ok for a one night stay. The rooms seem nice and are of average size. There's a fridge, a safe and coffee making facilities. During the day there were coffee and pastries offered outside the hotel front entrance, which was a nice touch. The location of the hotel is convenient for the wharf area and other attractions in the northern part of the city, but those you are able to cover in one day. If you want anywhere else, you would have to do that by some other transportation means than foot.

title: “Such a pleasant staff!”
text: I was originally checked into a different downtown hotel that my sister booked at a ridiculous rate. I was able to book here at an over 65% savings. The common areas of the hotel were not as tidy as I would have liked them to be but there were cheerleaders there on competition and who cares?! My room was clean, the bedding was comfortable and the staff was so polite and friendly! Specifically, when I got there the room I reserved on a travel site moments earlier was ready but the desk concierge (forgot her name) noticed I booked 3 adults. Without prompting, she found me a more accommodating room and though it wasn't ready at the moment, Jimy (valet) was more than helpful in storing my family's luggage until we returned later (and being patient as we rifled through our bags for last minute items)! When we finally returned and picked up our luggage, it was nearly midnight and the night desk concierge (forgot his name but if I say "biker braid" they will know!) was happy to offer his assistance and humor. Upon checkout the next morning, Terence & Samad were absolutely delightful as they got us checked out swiftly and sent well wishes for our trip! :o)

title: “What a steal of a deal!!”
text: We were not expecting much given some of the reviews, but I found a great deal on this property on Priceline. Hotel was amazing. We asked for a room away from the crowds because the other reviews said the walls were paper thin. We had a great night's rest and never heard a peep all night. The bed was so comfortable. Room was very spacious. We loved it! Also convenient to a few places downtown to grab a quick dinner.

title: “Pretty good, but ask for a courtyard room.”
text:
Overall, I had a fairly good experience here, but I think it could have been improved with a better choice of a room (more below).
The first impression of the hotel was positive; it has very attractive landscaping and the lobby is clean and bright. The person at the front desk was friendly and efficient. The room was something of a disappointment, however. The previous evening I had stayed at a new Courtyard by Marriot in Casper, Wyoming, and this one simply didn't measure up to the one in Casper. This hotel is obviously a renovation of a hotel from the 1970's era, so the rooms are slightly small and the bathrooms are not up to the standards of newly-built hotels. Having said that, however, there was nothing wrong with the room; it was clean, well-decorated and comfortable. 
I did have one or two complaints, however. I wanted to do some ironing, and could not find any place to plug the iron in. Finally I had to move the couch to plug the iron in - all of the plug-ins are blocked by furniture or the (large) television. In addition, the room was quite dark and a bit noisy. The noise was a function of the hotel's location, since the west side faces busy Quebec Street . If you can, ask for a room facing either into the courtyard or facing east; they should be much quieter. In addition, if I were to stay here again I would ask for a room on the second or third floor, since those rooms should be brighter. Also, the first floor rooms have patio doors to the outside, and I didn't feel entirely comfortable with that despite the good security bars on the doors. Rooms on the second or third floor wouldn't have that problem.
The hot buffet breakfast (extra cost) was very good and extensive, with the normal scrambled eggs and potatoes, cereal, bread and bagels for toast, danishes and coffee. In addition, this one had a good selection of cut-up fresh fruit, yogurt and juices. If you are hungry, it's well worth the money, in my opinion.
Overall, I would certainly stay here again, but only if I could get a courtyard room or a room facing east.

title: “Not awful, but needs work on a few fronts”
text: I recently stayed 3 nights at the Marriott Tech Center for a business meeting in Denver (which was not conducted at the hotel). It wasn't terrible, but I wouldn't pick it for a return visit to the area. Although front desk staff was friendly and the shuttle staff were super helpful, I had a few discouraging interactions with staff answering the guest services line regarding the difficulty I had getting wireless internet. The information I got was contradictory, they sounded put-out with my questions, and it took 20 minutes to find out that I was supposed to ask the front desk to "connect" me to wireless (why anyone should have to do this, I can't imagine; and there was zero information in the room about this). Overall, the hotel seemed kind of shabby to me. Some of the towels in my room had bare spots worn through and the furnishings were sort of run-down. A colleague who stayed at the same time as I did broke out in a rash and thought she had bed-bugs. But she had been to the hot tub the night before, and I just saw in a previous review that another guest got a rash from the hot tub. It seems that this hotel has some issues it needs to address before it will attract repeat customers.

title: “NEVER STAY HERE”
text: My family and I stayed at the Sky View Plaza hotel on June 13th 2012, when we got there the room was disgusting, the lock didn’t work, the sheets were stained, the phone nor tv didn’t work, there were holes in the wall and ceiling, we didn’t want to complain because it was one night and we didn’t want to be “those people.” We got back from vacation and the driver picked us up almost killing us, speeding, texting and driving, slamming on his breaks, as well as talking on his phone. We got back to the hotel and our tire was slit in their parking lot. I was fed up and went in to talk to a manager, no one was there. I tried calling as well as emailing the next day to talk to the manager. After a week he finally decided to answer my call and told me it was too late to refund my money. Well if he didn’t ignore me for a week it wouldn’t have been too late. The workers there are unprofessional, and I do not advise anyone to stay there.

title: “great airport location”
text:
Our studio suite was very spacious with a sofa and armchair. As with all Residence Inn's, there was a full kitchen. Large closet and plenty of drawer space. Our bathroom vanity drawers had seen better days, but were clean. 2 huge windows in the room, one with a window that you could open. Had some problems with the internet. We faced a parking lot--not much of a view. They had a recyclable basket in the kitchen...great idea! Mangers reception offered chili and pirogies (odd combo). Breakfast was as always, very plentiful--something for everyone.
All rooms offer exterior entry. This is a 2 story hotel with no elevators. Reminds me more of an apartment complex then a hotel. Nice meandering walkways. Outdoor pool and basketball court located near the main building (building 1) which also houses an small exercise room. Business center was a computer and printer in the lobby on a stand, no desk. 
There was always a security guard walking around, not sure why....?? The area is next to an airport--not many things to do. Convenient to highway. Center of Philly was about 20 minutes away--found driving around Philly to be confusing, thank goodness for Garmin!
Within walking distance to the hotel was the Hilton. There are plenty of hotels in the area. Our surroundings were nothing to speak about--
We were in town for a hockey game in Aston, Pa...we were 20 minutes away and that worked fine for us--easy drive. Average room rate was $200/night for a studio, we got ours for less than $90 thanks to Priceline. I'm not 100% certain, but I think the hotel only offers Studio and 2 bedroom Suites.

title: “Amazing and Outstanding Staff”
text: The hotel is in a great location, the staff goes out of the way to make you feel part of the Hilton Family. Since I travel to the Hilton frequently they know me on a first name basis and always welcome be back.

title: “Incredible Boutique Hotel”
text: This hotel allowed us to have an incredible experience while we visited NYC. The staff was very accommodating-fun-professional. Being from the south we were somewhat dismayed by the the demeanor of other staff at nationally branded hotels. The hotel Mela had such a warm and inviting feel, very clean, lovely decor and the staff could not do enough for us! This hotel stands way above the rest!

title: “Free cookie on arrival and the nice touches keep on coming!”
text:
Lovely hotel, posh enough to feel luxurious, but not pretentious enough to be annoying (no overbearing bell hops for instance). The room was spacious and spotless, the beds sooo comfortable with luxurious bedding. Neutrogenia toiletries are a nice touch too. Breakfast and room service VERY expensive, but there is a starbucks in the lobby. 
One bad point, they advertise highspeed wifi access in all rooms, but they don't tell you it is $12.95!

title: “Great Motel close to LA.”
text:
I stayed with my wife at the Rodeway Inn en Route to SFO. We can strongly recommend this nice Motel on the Pacific Coast Highway. The manager is a very nice & honest person.
Rooms are clean & well equipped. Most importantly: A very service-oriented location. TOP!

title: “A very good airport hotel”
text:
If you're a gold member in the Hilton loyalty program, you get free breakfast when you stay at a Hilton Garden Inn. This generally makes these properties a good value choice, and this Phoenix Airport location is no exception.
The hotel is conveniently located to the airport, and particularly convenient to the off-site car rental center. Rooms are a little unusual for the chain, in that they all have kitchenettes and a separate 1-bed bedroom -- kind of like an extended stay hotel. This makes the property a little better for solo travellers and couples instead of families, as the only other bed is a fold out couch in the living room.
Furnishings in the hotel are attractive, the rooms each have 2 flat screen TVs, and the pool area is above-average for an airport hotel. I wasn't crazy about the beds (there's a knob to adjust their firmness), but I didn't find them terrible, either. 
Breakfast was very good, with cooked-to-order omelettes, eggs, pancakes, etc., and also a buffet bar with bacon, fruit, potatoes, etc. A restaurant-quality meal.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text: We spent 5 nights here in October 10-15. Down town Charlotte is a wonderful city to visit and everything is walking distance from here as well as Charlotte Motor Speedway only 25 minutes away. Front desk and service were great as was the bar and breakfast. Our only minor issue was the valet parking. The guys were great and super fast. It was expensive but if you're going to worry about $100 over 5 days then maybe you should re-think vacation. It was more that if we forgot or wanted something out of the car we felt bad about having it brought down - not that valet complained. Without doubt we would return to this hotel.

title: “don~t forget anything in your room”
text: Room was small . I could hear people talking at 3:00 am could not sleep . I FORGOT MY 200 DOLLAR SUN GLASSES IN THE ROOM , We are 100% positive they were in the room . when i called at 9:15 am they went to my room and they said there is no glasses THEY KEPT MY GLASSES .... To them its no big deal......

title: “Best hotel I have stayed at!”
text: The staff is so accommodating and nice. The rooms are beautiful and very comfortable and modern. Beautiful view and easy walking to many restaurants and attractions, close to the Logan airport. Cannot wait to stay here again!

title: “Great location at a great price”
text: A short weekend trip. Amazing location close to shopping, commons, and nightlife. Interiors seemed to be updated recently. Chic boutique feel with great spa quality products. If I return to Boston I would easily choose to stay here again.

title: “The hotel is okay”
text: The hotel is located just outside of the downtown area but a block or two from the monorail. It is appropriately rated a 2-star hotel. I stayed at the hotel for two nights because I was attending a conference at the convention center. Checking in and checking out was speedy and pleasant. The hotel room was okay, it was a nice size, clean (although I did find a hair on one of the towels). If you need an inexpensive place to stay with basic amenities, this place is fine.

title: “Hidden gem in a great location”
text:
The main thing about this hotel is it is in a fantastic spot right opposite Grand Central on Lexington Av, and you can walk to most of the main attractions and Times Square is only a 5-10 min walk.
The hotel has an Irish theme and the bar is great, they serve a wide range of good food and drinks. The staff are friendly and accommodating and the service is quick - the concierge desk staff are especially helpful and they all have a good knowledge of the local area, which is what you want when you get to NY!
The rooms are small but I gather that this is normal for NY, but they are so cosy and comfy and I'm not the sort of person to be bothered about the size! The beds are so soft and the bathroom is lovely and quite spacious. The hotel is also quite quiet considering you are in the middle of the city! Not too much noise comes from outside and I usually find it quite hard to get to sleep in hotels! Not here though. 
Have stayed here many times and the hotel has always been spotless and never had a problem with any room or service issues at all.

title: “Comfortable. Great location”
text: We had a wonderful stay at this hotel. Staff were all very friendly. Usually I do not get a good night sleep at hotels, bu here the bed was comfortable and room was very clean. I always enjoy my stay at Kimpton Hotels and this was no different. I would stay here agian!

title: “Clean, convenient, and big”
text:
This hotel is what every Hilton should be. Clean large room with good TV, desk, and couch. Comfortable bed. Close to 6th street, the convention center, and lots of restaurants. It's an easy walk to anywhere and there are always cabs outside if you need one. 
The fitness center is beautiful, clean, and up to date. However, if you aren't Hilton Honors Silver or higher it will cost you 10 bucks. I think every hotel's fitness center should be free.That said, it is also has complimentary coffee and is a great place to fill up your water bottle. 
Internet is totally reliable, but comes at a steep price $13.99/day! 
Put the do not disturb sign on your door or housekeeping will knock early.

title: “Primarily for Military staff”
text:
It feels like an upscale YMCA with some of the three star Hotel features and yet the infrastructure of a Youth Hostel.
I was looking for a decent price during the Columbus week-end. An hotel under 175 US during pick season is a steal! 
Located about 2 miles from the closest subway (North Station), there is the Hopital shuttle that provides free transportation every half hour to the subway on week-end from 9 AM to 6 PM, extended hours during the week and no service at all on legal Holiday. If you do not own a car, a cab would be the alternative to get to the closest subway ($6 each way) or walk if you're fit and the weather is working with you.
The staff is helpful and reasonnably friendly. It takes pride to display the Mission of the Hotel is to provide a safe accommodation to the Military organization (who gets the preferred rate) and the general public and it does, in the Army style.
No thrills in that place. Rooms are not sound proof. Although it is on a cul-de-sac, you cannot avoid hearing the noise of cars passing by or neighbor taking a shower. The room is quite large which takes more time to heat it. My large room came with a kichenette and all rooms have an Iron board, Iron and Hairdryer. A fitness center free of charge to Guests is available during regular working hours.
Apart from the Constitution and the amazing Constitution Museum, this place is somewhat inconvenient if you are hoping to spend your time by foot or subway.

title: “Amazing Algonquin Landmark”
text: I love NYC & I love History....put these two together and you get The Algonquin! The Algonquin is rich in history, Style & class. The location is great. Close to Broadway. The only NYC Location I know of where you can enjoy a 5 star dinner and take in a fabulous show at the same time! The decor is classic and some of the rooms hardware & bath styles are classic which make the stay nastalgic. If you go ou must try the signature "Algonquin" Cocktail made famous by the the round table in 1920's . If you find the review helpful let us know!

title: “Not up to Country Inn standards”
text:
I prefer to stay in Country Inns when I travel because they have always been clean and comfortable. I booked one night at this hotel, and was really disappointed. 
The room had a stale smell when we walked in. The drapes were stained, the duvets on the beds were stained, and the shower was dirty. I was afraid to touch anything.
The breakfast was alright, but the trash in both trash cans was overflowing. 
The service at the front desk was slow. I had to wait about 5 minutes for the clerk to even appear when I went to check out. 
The only good thing was the price through AAA. And that it was easy access to I-71 to get out of there the next morning.

title: “BAD customer Service!!!”
text: My fiance and I stayed at the Beacon Hotel this past weekend in Jan., and had one of the worst experiences ever. We're avid travelers and we have never been treated so carelessly by a hospitality venue in our travels. First, upon checking in, everything went pretty smooth. We got the Corporate King Suite and it was pretty small, not at all what the virtual tour depicted. Aside from that, the customer service was the WORST ever! my fiance came to the hotel 2 hours after I checked us in. I told the receptionist to give me ONE key to the room and leave the other key for my fiance at the DESK! I was suffering from Strep throat and a cold during that time and just didn't want to be bothered with the phones ringing or going all the way down to the desk to get him (the elevators only operate with the room keys). Low and behold, I get a call from my fiance (who is standing in the lobby) that only are they giving him a hard time but they didn't have his key at the desk or name on the room! I call the front desk to get some middle eastern guy who told me in a rude manner that they will take care of it and let him up! 10 mins later my fiance calls me AGAIN! I call down to the front desk ONCE AGAIN and ask them why they have him standing in the lobby! I get an African guy that yells something rude at me and just HANGS UP THE PHONE IN MY FACE! At that point, I get angry, have to put on all my clothes and go down stairs to get my fiance. I ask them where is the other key to my room and they act as if they could careless and are SO VERY VERY rude to us. I say forget it and my fiance and I go up to the room. All night long we're getting calls from the front desk asking us if we ordered room service! We tell them no over and over! They come banging on the door twice throughout the night about room service, disturbing our sleep! The staff seemed extremely disorganized and frustrated (not sure why because not many people were checking in!) I can't get over the one representative hanging the phone up on me after yelling at me as if I was NOTHING and my service to the hotel meant nothing! I have never been treated so badly, ever! I was so exhausted from being sick that we didn't have the time or energy to move to another hotel so we just stayed for ONE NIGHT and left. I would never recommend this hotel for anyone.

title: “Don't Judge by the Outside”
text:
During my last trip to Seattle, several cruise ships were in town as was a convention so I booked my hotel stay on Hotwire and ended up with this hotel. When I first approached it, near the Space Needle, it looked stuck in the early 80's and looks like it's ready for demolition. However, once I reached the lobby I was surprised; it was updated, comfortable with a huge fireplace and the desk staff were nice. Although this hotel still has a dark inside appearance and low ceilings in the hallways, the rooms have been freshened and are actually large! Flat screen TV, free wireless internet that reached full strength, refrigerator, fantastic comfortable bed and beautiful views of Capitol Hill from the 4th floor. The bathroom, however, is ridiculously small but the water pressure was good and everything worked. 
All in all it was a good stay. You can't always judge by what you see on the exterior. This is also close to Gateway where there are several restaurant choices and a Whole Foods. 15 minute walk to downtown.

title: “Location location location!”
text:
It was considered as a last minute booking (if you call 3 weeks as last minute!) and as expected, most of the Times Square hotels were very expensive and this is one of the affordable hotels, at almost 350usd/night (not cheap!) and of course, carefully considered the reviews in Trip Advisor. Since I am staying for only 2 days and a night, I might as well get a hotel in Times Square to maximize the short span of time spent in NY in which I made the right decision.
Check in was ok and front desk staff and concierge were helpful. Lobby had a good lighting vibe, rooms were clean and comfortable. The room had the usual amenities like dryer and a small safe to keep your important belongings (no tootbrush and toothpaste but no big deal anyway). The room had an ipod dock in which Im happy about, free wifi, and had comfy beds too and was not noisy at night inspite of being in Times Square so I had an undisturbed good nights rest. 
It's a walkable distance form the hotel to Macy's and Central Park (if you like walking!). Times Square is just 5 minutes by walking. Starbucks is all over the place. There are a lot of food choices around too. It is just a few minutes walk from where the happening is. Very good location I should say. 
But I somehow feel the amount I paid is too pricey for a 3 star hotel. Judging the hotel's appearance, services it offers and location, they should've charged my stay at at least 200usd inclusive of taxes and surcharges. Anyway, that is what you get if you want it to be in the middle of all the "chaos". A pricey 3 star hotel. 
The asian guy who was in the bar (near the front desk) was nice BUT when I asked him if they are still serving food just before midnight, he showed me a plate of noodles that seemed to be prepared earlier (or whatever reason he might have!) and offered it to me since their kitchen is already closed. It was nice of him but its just not proper for him to be serving something that was disliked by any guests or maybe by him or even precooked earlier to another guest and then now being offered to me. Its just night proper. 
So word of advice, enjoy NY food while walking in Times Square. Book your hotels way early or better yet, once in a while check travel websites (way ahead) for better deals. Enjoy NY!
Not sure with the pools. I accidentally clicked it as average but I haven't really seen or even know if they have a pool.

title: “The best located”
text: Definitely the hotel carter isn't the cleanest and welcoming , but it is the best located, it is near the bus station and the subway, you can find everything that you need near here. Also when you are in New York you don't think about going to bed and staying in the hotel, what you want is to go out and visit many places. I stayed in this hotel and the employees and the receptionist were very friendly . It is an excellent option to stay in New York.

title: “Clean and Nice breakfast not as good as other La Quintas”
text: Stayed over 1 night on our way to an antique weekend with the girls. Convenient location, and good check in experience. Flat screen TV, with sofa and king bed updated. basics all taken care of . only disappointment was the breakfast did not have a lot of selection as other La Quintas - no hard boiled eggs, only 2 cereals and no friut.

title: “Good value, Great Location”
text: We stayed at the Chelsea Star Hotel for 6 nights for a shopping/sightseeing holiday. As New York is a pretty pricey place to stay, I did loads of research and came across this hotel because of its competitive rates and good location. I would certainly recommend it - its located in the heart of the city. The room was made daily, with a small kitchenette (microwave/fridge/coffee machine) and fresh sheets and towels provided. After reading some reviews on this website I asked for a room facing away from the road - we were put up in room 4R (3 queen sized beds on the 4th floor facing the courtyard). My only reservations would be that it was a bit of a hike up to the 4th floor (especially after a hard days shopping!!) and the nearest subway station is about 2 blocks away. otherwise no complaints - would definitely consider returning on my next trip to the Big Apple...

title: “Great location on the Riverwalk”
text: We typically stay in Courtyard hotels and there wasn't anything unique about this one. The best part about this one was the city view from a high floor at night and the location on the riverwalk. It was far enough away not to hear noise, but close enough to walk to everything no problem. I do like when they have a Bistro, but unfortunately the person making the Starbucks drinks didn't know what she was doing - I threw one away and the next morning she asked a coworker so that one was OK. Parking was valet and expensive but worth it. Nice hotel and very nice staff.

title: “Clean rooms, hearty breakfast”
text:
On our way to Nashville we stopped in Memphis and stayed at the Best Western. The rooms were clean and there was free internet. The staff was nice and welcoming. 
Two tips that I can give about this hotel are:
1. the GPS doesn't always get the hotel's address. If so it's better to print the directions from Google Maps ahead of time. 
2. If you need directions to Graceland or a map of Memphis you need to ask for them specifically, for some reason the person checking us in didn't ask us if we need this information though he gladly handed it to us once we asked.

title: “Great View”
text: We stayed Aug. 16-Aug. 19. We flew in to Chicago to celebrate my birthday at my mom's favorite restaurant and catch a game at Wrigley field. Location was perfect. We were only there two and a half days but saw everything. Sears Tower, John Hancock, Michigan Ave, The Navy Pier (ate at Bubba Gump's), watched the Cubs beat the Cards in the rain, took a water taxi down the river and a horse drawn carriage at night. The Hotel has spectacular views. We did not request specific rooms, as we did not plan to be in the hotel much but had a perfect view of Sears Tower. The atrium lobby was nice to sit and have a cocktail before going to bed. Darryl at the bar was awesome. We had dinner at the restaurant the last night and the food was good and reasonably priced. The hotel was clean and the service was great. Don't let the elevators intimidate you, they were no problem. It was a nice stay and without a doubt will always stay at this hotel. If you like fondue, the best fondue around is at Geha’s Café in Chicago. It was worth the trip alone.

title: “Brilliant hotel”
text:
I really don't know why everyone is putting this hotel down. My partner and I have just got back from a week stay at this hotel and thought everything about it was fantastic. We arrived and checked in with no major hiccups, we were not able to check into our room as we were several hours early but they kindly put our bags in a waiting room which allowed us to get out and start exploring straight away.
We were both not sure what to expect after reading so many bad reports, of rooms being small, dirty etc, but we were pleasantly surprised. We didn't choose the size of our room on booking and im not sure what size you would have called the room, it wasnt big but its wasn't too small either. There was enough room for the two of us to move around comfortably with a couple of foot either side of the bed, we had a very large suit case and this stayed on the floor with no problems. We were only requiring the room to sleep in so what more do you want. The bathroom was small but enough room to bath,shower and use a bathroom for what you need to do. Stop whinging everyone! make the most of what you have and be thankful your even in New york!
The location was fantastic about a 1 minute walk to times square. We didn't use the restaurant facility's so cant comment on these. The internet is not free at the hotel but the rest of times square provides free internet access.
New york itself is a wonderful place with so much to see and do. My best advice is take some comfortable shoes as you will be walking a long way! we both ended up buying trainers as our normal shoes were not comfy enough.
So many places to eat, we found Applebees the best place to eat for breakfast.

title: “Great Stay in a wonderful little hotel on the Upper West Side”
text: We came to NYC to attend a function at Columbia University, which is just two subway stops away from The Hotel Newton. What a wonderful staff, from the moment we checked in until we left Monday morning. Twice I called the hotel prior to our arrival with a question. Each time I spoke with the manager, Emilio. He could not have been nicer or more helpful. Upon our arrival, we were greeted with the happy news that we had been upgraded to a suite with a roomy bathroom and 2 queen beds. Service was very prompt when we needed more towels, and helpful and polite with directions and suggestions. Overall, we were quite pleased and will most certainly stay here again when we return to NYC.

title: “Excellent staff, Need to Upgrade Amenities to Reflect Standard Set By Staff”
text:
First of all, do not use a GPS if you are arriving by car. It took us an hour hitting closed streets, not known by GPS. I called the hotel, and I think Bobby the Concierge Mamger talked us in. Being very frazzled, he very kindly offered to comp our parking which was a classy move. The hotel is gorgeous. The lobby is spacious and quite inviting considering how large it was. I liked the there is a lovely restaurant adjacent to the lobby, which had delicious Food and a stunning view of Boston Harbor, overlooking the downtown skyline.
The elevator had surrounding windows, so you can see the lovely view as you ascend to you room. We were on the 11th floor, the rooms were on the small side for a hotel of this stature. I did enjoy this hotel enough that Even with the things wrong with it I will list below, I think I'd stay there again and take the water taxi or Subway into the heart of Boston.
Some things need fixing. There is NO need for a hotel with this many rooms, catering to many business customers to charge $12.95 PER unit for Internet. Definitely take my advice!! This hotel competes with much higher end hotels for the same type of costomer. Free Internet could make the difference to budget minded companies choose this Hyatt! Also, the heating systems are terrible. We had to turn ours off, but then the people next door had theirs on and it sounded like a freight train was coming through our room. We can't be the only ones mentioning this! We Changed rooms but it's evidently a flaw hotel-wide. This is the first 4-star hotel I've stayed in with this heating issue. This is a 1-2 star hotel issue!! The parking is over priced for the area and they should think about lowering those rates a bit (although our's was comped, I am just passing along information. 
I'm going to nitpick here: more glasses, hand towels, washclothes, and towels should be in each room. It felt like the barest minimum was given for our use. A bottle of Aquafina Water went for $5.00. REALLY!!! I've stayed in some very pricey hotels, and they might charge $5.00 for bottled water in the room, but it's Evian or comperable water. One more nitpick. I'd called for extra pillows, but it took them an hour and a half to get to us. They SHOULD have free bathrobes in every room at that level!
Two big things to rave about: the bed certainly was heavenly, I slept better than at home. And Bobby, the Manager Concierge, was truly exemplary at helping us overcome several problems. A really terrific young guy, named Devon helped get us a 4:00 checkout the next day, as we were picking someone up coming from Seattle and the plane wasn't scheduled to arrive until 5:30 that afternoon. It allowed my husband to nap comfortably as we were driving 250 miles after we picked them up to go home. As I said before, dinner was very, very good in the restaurant, which looked over at the Boston skyline and was quite spectacular as all the building across the river were lighted up. Very lovely! A very nice gentleman named Denice waited on us. While we were waiting in the lobby for the plane to arrive the next afternoon, we were well taken care of. Jorje came over, introduced himself to us and asked if we needed or wanted ANYthing at all. Several waiters did the same thing followed by a big smile and even offered us a glass of water (free, I assume) while we waited. I guess I want to say that the level of amazing pampering appears slightly out of sync with the level of amenities and I think corporate needs to offer the whole package if they want to upgrade their image as a whole. You have amazing people who go out of their way to help out and/or make things more comfortable. You do them a disservice by not offering a classy, unique room to go with it! I want to thank Bobby, Devon, Jorje and Denice and every single other person on staff at Hilton Harborside for helping to make this trip a fun trip in the end and let them know I'll be back next time if for nothing else, but for the top-notch way they all helped us out under all circumstances. Come here for the vacation, or shopping, or just to wait for a flight. Stay and enjoy pretty much the best staff I've met at any hotel ever!!!

title: “Good location, older but nice property!”
text: Stayed one night on the ending of an Alaskan cruise. Everyone nice, has washers and dryers which were used to avoid having to do it all when we got home. Close to the Pike market. Breakfast was good. Staff was pleasant and we were allowed to check in early.

title: “Good hotel in the heart of SF”
text:
Stayed at the Carlton for 3 days mid-October on our way back thru SF from Napa. Since my beautiful (and new) wife and I were not experienced with the first hotel we stayed when we first came to SF (Hotel Drisco), I thought it would be fun to stay downtown for a change. And since the Carlton is a JDV hotel like the Drisco along with postive reviews found on Tripadvisor, I thought we couldn't go wrong.
Staff was great, always with your best interest in mind. Rooms were small but how much time do you really want to stay in a room when all of SF is out there asking to be explored? Location was great and convenient to Union Square -- within a 10 minute walk if that. 
I would recommend the Carlton if you're looking for a good hotel in downtown with a staff that is customer focused.

title: “Gracious, elegant, historic former private home tucked away in Washington Square.”
text: I am almost reluctant to share this find, as there are only 15 rooms here. With the original wide plank hardwood floors and beautiful original fireplaces, it feels like the 1700's, but with modern amenities. My husband surprised me with a two night stay here to celebrate our anniversary. The staff were congenial and accommodated us at every turn. Our beautifully furnished room had large windows overlooking a courtyard below. We were just steps from Walnut Street, convenient to great shopping, restaurants etc. It was an absolutely romantic, lovely getaway.

title: “Great hotel, excellent price!”
text: I stayed at this hotel for three nights. The service was great and the rooms were very clean and spacious. The hotel also offers a complimentary shuttle that goes out every hour to some of the most popular tourist attractions in the area. Overall, this is a great place to stay for such an affordable price.

title: “Our Favorite NYC Hotel”
text: The Hilton Garden Inn Times Square is our favorite choice for annual trips to NYC. Its mid town location makes it ideal for Theatre (you're there)..shopping (Macy's is only twenty minutes away), Central Park (10 minutes). Subway stop is just across the street and you're steps away from a great array of restaurants and cafes. The hotel staff is helpful, professional and courteous and the rooms are spacious, clean and comfortable. Couldn't ask for more.

title: “I can't find anything negative to say.”
text:
I don't have a bad thing to say about this hotel. 
Great location? Check. Right near Madison Square Park and the flatiron district.
Finely appointed rooms? Check. Great decor, granite surfaces, comfy beds.
Free breakfast? Check. Delicious, and graciously served by smiling hotel employees.
Lack of street noise? Check. Even on the 3rd floor, I never heard a thing.
Free wi-fi? Check.
Attentive and polite staff? Check.
I could go on and on, but you get the point. I'm loathe to write this positive review--I don't want the hotel to become too popular and ruin my future fun!

title: “Wish my company was paying...”
text:
Great business hotel, lots of seminars going on during the 3 days we stayed. Pretty pricey...and it killed me to pay $33 plus tax daily for parking! Lots of tips...the valet, the porter to the elevator, then another porter brings the bags to the room! Business travelers may be used to this... fee for fitness center, fee for wireless in room...
 The room was smallish but very clean. Nice linens, small bathroom. No fridge though there was a cabinet for it. They brought one up when I requested it. Lengthy trek to the elevator-seriously, the hall looked as long as the one in" The Shining"( REDRUM!)
 Close to Woodley metro stop and the Zoo. I would recommend this hotel to others ... but they should do the homework that I didn't to make sure it is what they signed up for.

title: “June tour visits Serrano”
text:
We stopped here on 13th June 05. It was a lovely hotel, beautifully decorated and well thought out. 
We had a standard room which was reasonably sized and well furnished. It was very clean and in an excellent location only 5 minutes walk from Union Square. It really was no problem walking into town, it felt safe and in a popular area.
The hotel offered free coffee on a morning and free wine tasting in the evening if you can tear yourself away from the shops for 5pm! The staff were helpful and friendly and there was free use of a business room for internet access if required. 
Parking was next to the hotel at $22 a day. Turning right out of the hotel entrance and opposite the Hilton is the 'Taylor street' coffee shop that was independently highly rated for its breakfasts. If you like Indian food, we found the Merla next door is also a good place to eat. 
We would definitely stop here again and would definitely recommend it. 
To put our review into context, this was part of our June tour of California and New York that included the following hotels, also reviewed on tripadvisor.
Sofitel - Los Angeles, Best Western O'cairns - Lompoc, Travel Lodge Monterey Bay, Serrano - San Francisco, Wuksachi Lodge - Sequoia Nat park, Yosemite View Lodge - Yosemite Nat park, Furnace Creek Ranch - Deach Valley, Aladdin - Las Vegas, UN Millennium Plaza - New York

title: “Great Value!”
text: Stayed for 7 nights in a two room king suite at this new La Quinta location. Clean & nicely decorated. Only disappointment was that the door separating the living area/bedroom is glass -- light will disturb anyone trying to sleep in either room (covering with a sheet will help). Well pleased with breakfast selection & business center as well as the availability of the guest laundry.

title: “Best NYC hotel experience ever”
text: I lived in New York for 9 years and travel back once a month for work. I've stayed in all sorts of hotels over the years but this was by far the best experience I've ever had. The service was outstanding, and the suite I was in was larger than most NYC apartments! I've paid more money and stayed in rooms not even 1/4 the size. The people were lovely and really went the extra mile. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this hotel to anyone, and l plan to book future trips based on when this hotel has availability.

title: “Great Location - Great Staff - Clean!”
text: We stayed at Hyatt Fisherman's Wharf for 3 nights just recently and found the hotel to be nicely located and with a great staff. We got a great deal through Priceline so we can't complain. We were given a 2 doubles bedroom near the elevator and facing the entry parking. The elevator actually didn't bother us but we can hear the people from the parking valet area in the morning. That didn't really bother us much either since we were out sightseeing most of the day. The only drawback for this place is the parking fee. Hyatt charges $45 a night (with in-out access). The closest parking lot charges $32 a night with no in-out access. On the night of arrival, we paid for the $32 a night parking since it was late but every night after that, we were able to find off-street parking for free. You just need to make sure you read the signs since some streets have street cleaning and no parking is allowed at certain times. You also will need to get up by 7 to take the car or else you will need to feed the meter. The room itself was great: roomy, clean and recently renovated. We didn't try the restaurant since there are too many options in San Fran. They do have a heated pool but we didn't have time to try that out since it drizzled while we were there. Overall, we enjoyed our stay and for the price we paid, we loved it.

title: “Great Pre-cruise Hotel Near Seatac”
text: We stayed here the night before our flight left for Vancouver BC to begin our Alaska cruise. The hotel has a Stay & Park program so we had a place to leave our car for the week we were gone. The hotel is well located, clean and up to date. Our room was very large and comfortable. We had to leave too early to take advantage of the free breakfast but from the pictures it looked yummy. They also provide free 24 hour airport shuttle. Very reasonably priced.

title: “Great for business travelers”
text: The hotel is very accommodating with setting up rooms. Our clients were impressed and appreciated the surroundings.

title: “AVERAGE, NOTHING SPECTACULAR!!!!”
text: The location to everything was very ideal. I like that security is perched on top of the building with a 360 view. I did see a few bugs here & there but nothing to call the front desk about. The staff was friendly. I did not like the cleaning technique of stripping all the rooms at the same time because I returned to my room for a nap & my bed was undone & by the time it was done I had to return to my convention. The last day I paid for late check out at 200pm instead of noon and the desk did not communicate this with the housekeeping staff. My door was banged on every 15minutes up until 0200pm when I left by different employees. I still was charged the fee despite the ongoing interruptions. Overall, it was alright. There isn't anything spectacular about it.

title: “Great location, informative staff and a very clean hotel”
text:
A great location with many fabulous restaurants within walking distance. Lots of shopping, cable cars close. We walked to Fisherman's Wharf three times. The Moscone Convention Center is a nice walking distance away. Felt very safe walking everywhere.
The service at the hotel was superb, right from check - in, to the maid. All personnel were friendly and willing to help out in anyway possible. The restaurant was pricey, particularly for breakfast. Lots of machines available in the fitness center.

title: “great long weekend”
text: Loved it. staff all so friendly. rooms clean. great rooftop bar. near many popular places to visit. best night's sleep ever.

title: “Very good but not quite as good as I expected”
text:
I've stayed in a lot of 5 star hotels and was just a little disappointed with the Lenox. Nothing was wrong with it all all, but compared to some of the places in other countries it seemed to be lacking somethings for one to the top hotels in Boston. They were just small things really - for example there was no newspaper provided in the morning. That seemed odd. Another oddity was that the desk was positioned so that it partially blocked the bathroom door unless it was pushed all the way under the desk. The bed was comfortable but not as nice as a Westin bed. 
On the other hand, the location, the free wifi all over the hotel, the free coffee in the lobby each morning were all great. 
I was happy but not dazzled at the Lenox.

title: “Impressed”
text:
Visted Inn since I had been interested in staying at the Inn but was turned off by some of the prior reviews. I was at the Japenese American Museum and decided to walk over to the Inn (1/2 blocks away) to check out the Inn. Glad I did!!
Lobby: Very impressive. Clean, friendly, elegant and modern. In the Lobby there is a sitting area, a coffee bar, a nice resturant and a small shop. Very hip.
Parking: There is parking for the hotel. The hotel has its own parking structure, not a "parking lot". The parking is $8.80 a day for its guests.
Neighborhood: Very nice, seems very safe, clean and right next door to "Little Tokyo." Very impressed with location and how nice the surrounding area seemed to be.
I am going to stay at this hotel next time I am in town.

title: “Quirky but a great place to stay”
text:
If you're looking for the Holiday Inn or the typical large chain hotel experience, do not stay at Balboa Park Inn. However, if you appreciate (or at least aren't bothered by) quirky touches like plastic flowers, this off-the-beaten-path B&B has a lot going for it. 
We stayed here with our preteen son in one of the suites, which was perfect for us. The kitchen was nice to have -- we got dinner from the local Whole Foods in Hillcrest a couple of nights we were there, and the kitchen has all the basics you need (including a corkscrew!). The service was great, the beds were comfy, the rooms were clean, there wasn't much noise from the street, and you can't beat the location. Oh, and there's free wireless broadband.
After reading other reviews, we skipped the breakfast and either ate in or visited the fabulous Bread & Cie in Hillscrest. Some people here have complained about parking, but we had no problems finding a parking space on the street. Most nights we got a spot right in front of our building's door; two other times we had to park a short walk around the corner, but this didn't bother us.
We would happily stay at Balboa Park Inn again.

title: “Good for parking only, not a great hotel.”
text: Hotel was not clean, and we could hear noise from all sides of room, and above us. When we treied to open the window it was completely broken. The front staff were helpful and let us park overnite and next day so we saved on parking.

title: “Relocation to Jacksonville, FL”
text:
We chose to stay at the Days Inn a couple different times... however, the second time, the room could have used some maintenance. The carpet trim on the wall was lying loose on the floor, the bathtub faucet dripped, the paint had been touched up with another shade, or the original color had faded....
Also, in 5 days, we could never get the wifi to work in either of our rooms. The hotel desk staff had offered to come down to the room to check it out, but never did. Disappointing as we were in need of the wifi to continue our search for permanent housing during our relocation to the Jacksonville area.
However, the beds were VERY comfortable and the extra pillow was very much appreciated. And that is the main reason for us to return to the Days Inn was the comfort of the beds and the quality of rest we received.

title: “Great Location, OK Service”
text:
All in all, an OK place to stay.
Room was nicely appointed and the location is very good, one block from the Metro, a few blocks from the White House and Capitol Mall. 
Now for the not so good. I was traveling on business. Now, I know my reservation clearly stated check-in time is 4 p.m. However, in my travels, I often have no problem checking in early. Not here. I arrived at 3 p.m. and was told my room was not ready and to check back in 30 minutes. Still not ready at 3:30. Somehow, all 700 rooms were magically ready by 4 p.m. During that entire time, I maybe only saw 10 people approach the check-in desk. I'm not gullible enough to believe all the rooms magically became ready at 4 O'Clock. Also, I'm a silver Marriott member. They need better communication with their housekeeping staff and more concern for early check ins. The Crystal Gateway Marriott has been much better for this and I will stay there in preference to this hotel in the future.
Secondly, after a few mile run, I thought it would be nice to soak in the whirlpool "hot" tub. When I got to the pool area, the hot tub was crawling with kids splashing around and swimming under water. Now I love kids but typically, "hot" tubs are at least 100 degrees. I saw the pool attendant's log and it was consistently 90 degrees all day. For an upscale hotel, you'd think this would be better or they would put up a sign stating the hot tub isn't...
All in all, a decent place to stay. Great location. Average customer service. Oh, the chocolates for the turn-down service were a nice touch.
Happy travels.

title: “Nice Value”
text:
Converted apartments, the Buckingham was a decent value, but with a few flaws. I rented a suite and got pretty much what the pictures indicated. There are some remnants of the conversion, such as too few electrical outlets, windy hallways, and older elevators. 
The staff certainly was responsive, but they weren't exactly warm or friendly, either. Hotel is slim on some amenities, but the lounge on the second floor offers free - but slow - wireless if you're willing to listen to the TV blare CNN. 
Hotel is not big on extra towels or washcloths. Neither the shower nor the furniture are very comfortable, either. But for a suite with a kitchen in midtown, it's a decent price and a good location.

title: “convenient location, but another disappointing W”
text:
Just like the other W Hotels I've stayed at, the W UNion Quare offers a gorgeous lobby, cool lounge, inept service and staff totally unprepared for work at a so called luxury hotel. 
Personally I would have preferred to stay at the Soho Grand or Tribeca Grand for NY downtown luxury, but I was travelling with my mother and she has limited mobility. For those of you who don't know NY, Union Square is downtown and more or less centrally located between the east and west sides of NY, so it doesn't take too long to get anywhere in the city. ALso, there's Union Square park with its great farmer's market and you're in something of a neighborhood, as opposed to awful, touristy Times Square , or Mom-unfriendly Tribeca. (Too hip, and tough for someone who doesn't know the city to take a walk.) So credit where credit is due....the place is conveniently located.
Other than that, the rooms were nicely designed but very worn and not all that clean. (Think used Holiday Inn.) The staff was very willing to help, but nothing seemed to get done. For example, we arrived back at the hotel from a day trip too late to return the rental car at the Hertz 3 blocks away. I had until 10am the next morning to return the car without being charged for an extra day. I called down for the car at 9, jumped in the shower and got down at 9:40 to find no car waiting. Door guy said it's on it's way. It wasn't until I asked him to check on it 10 minutes later that he found out it hadn't been called for. (I called, but the call wasn't relayed to the lot where the car was parked.) Finally the car arrived at 10:15. I finally got hold of an assistant manager, informed her of the situation and told her that I would expect credit on my bill for the cost of the extra day's car rental. ($100 cause it's NYC.) She called ahead and got Hertz to waive the second day's charge even though I was almost an hour past the dealine. I appreciated her making the call, but could have done without the hour delay. She also waived the $40 parking fee for the previous night. That's the good news. The bad news is that when I checked out I had 6 other $40 parking fees added. After a few minutes atthe desk the clerk removed the charges (I only had a car for 1night) and handed the bill back to me. A closer look showed that all of the charges had not been removed. I pointed this out and was told with attitude that they had been removed. I pointed to the charges that still remained and with a big sigh she reluctantly removed the charges, but still left the one night's charge. I told her the manager had comped the original one night's parking fee because of the problem and then with another sigh she headed off to talk to the manager and confirm my claim. All of this while I was trying to leave the hotel and fight NYC rush hour traffic on the way to JFK.
All in all, every complaint was resolved, but every complaint was more than avoidable, and I got attitude while they were being resolved. I'm a New Yorker and I'm used to attitude, but not when I'm paying over $400 a night. 
Had a very similar experience at the downtown Chicago W. I stay at nice hotels several times a month for work, and have had very few negative experiences. The negatives happen too consistently at this chain for me to recommend it or choose it in the future. It's all downhill after the lobby. Find a Loews.

title: “Great upgrades”
text: This is my 2nd visit to this hotel. The hotel has gone under a lot of renovations. I would say that I loved everything, except the brown hallways. It makes it a bit dark. The rooms are now phenomenal. Great service from concierge, drivers, and employees.

title: “Wonderful service”
text: We stayed here for our first anniversary trip to NYC. The staff knew their way around the city and were extremely helpful with recommendations. If you don't know the city, don't bring a city guide, just let them know what you want to do! The hotel is small and very cute, and its location can't be better. The only con was the size of the bed (a little bit small).

title: “Big name little impression”
text: I stayed at this hotel to attend a conference that was being held there. The hotel was booked solid and they obviously had no way to handle that, they seemed understaffed. The high-speed internet that was supposed to cost $14 a day but was free for conference attendees did not work. The parking costs were OUTRAGEOUS! I thought the food was good that the hotel provided for the conference events. Very good actually. The other complaint I have is that half of the hotel was sweaty hot and the other half was freezing cold. We had to turn the heat on in our room. In July.

title: “Great Hotel!!”
text: Stayed here for two nights, and was very impressed with our stay. Nice clean rooms, great resturants. The desk help was very helpful, anything we needed was taken care of. Staff was extremely helpful. Would stay again.

title: “Great experience”
text:
I arrived at Hotel Adagio on the evening of February 29 and was immediately taken care of by the front desk staff. The young man asked if I needed the double-double that was reserved in my name, as they had a nice, large King they could put me into instead. I took the King and did not regret my decision. I was in room 511. It was huge, clean and well-appointed. There was no view to speak of, which was fine with me, as I prefer quiet over scenery.
My 3 night stay was a great experience. My room was well taken care of by the housekeeping staff and the rest of the staff did everything they could to make my stay a pleasant one.
I had a great rate that I booked on their site that was much cheaper than comparable hotels in the Union Square area.
I would recommend this hotel to friends, family and colleagues.

title: “Free Wine! A great base to explore San Francisco”
text:
You will get a bit of a workout when walking from the hotel and Union Square and back, but just think of the amazing legs you're going to get out of it! And hey, this is San Fran, if walking up steep hills is not your thing, try Amsterdam.
We stayed here in San Fran for three nights in King room 801 and our package included Wine Reception. Seriously, wine reception should be part of all hotels, a genius idea if you want your guests to mingle with each other. But I couldn't really be bothered mingling and who says no to free wine at 5pm? So I took two glasses to our room upstairs and was pleased as punch.
The room probably doesn't look as small because of the floor to ceiling mirror wall but for all intensive purposes this room was big enough for the two of us. Nice big clean king bed, TV could be slightly bigger (first world problem), Free Wifi (although annoying that you have to login each time, again first world problem), and after staying in a hostel the first two nights it's a comfort to know that when you come back to the hotel in the afternoon the bed has been made, the bathroom isn't in the same state of mess you left it and there is still time to go downstairs and get a free glass of wine!
It's close to everything Union Square and the neighbouring BART, there is a great bar nearby called Cantina that makes a great ginger cocktail called the Flying Buddha, if you want a free hot dog with your beer visit the White Horse on Sutter, and for terrible and overpriced Japanese food you're welcome to visit Maru Sushi on Powell St.

title: “Good service for such a busy hotel.”
text: We stayed at the HIlton Chicago for the weekend of the Chicago Triathlon and were quite pleased with the services despite the fact that the hotel was fully booked with nervous triathletes AND wedding participants. Staff and front desk were VERY accomodating. Our rooms, with a view of the lake were just what we wanted. We've stayed at the Hilton for several years and enjoy the proximity to the race and local attrations.

title: “A warm and welcoming place.”
text: I stay at the Sofitel every week. The staff knows me by name and does everything they can to make my stay pleasant, which it always is. The rooms are always clean, and Gaby's restaurant is a solid and easy choice for any meal. Of course, the location is superb. This is a truly precious hotel in New York.

title: “Great Place”
text:
One Great hotel. Spent NYE here.
Location is great. The area is very accommadating as we had dinner at Nick and Sam's which is right across the street. Parking is easy and done on site. It is about $20 a car and the only issue was that in the morning around 11 when we left it took 25 minutes to get the vehicles.
The renovation has been great. The bathrooms are top notch and huge. We booked our room via hotels.com and got a much better rate. Without asking we got a corner room that was great. One issue is that they are building a building near buy and you look into that but no big deal. 
Upon arrival, the butler took our bags up and told us the real deal and was great. We spent some time at the bar in the hotel and it was great...they had a band and it was crowded but the service was good without too high of prices.
The overall quality of the hotel and room was top notch. You could tell it was an old bldg. but the renovations are perfect. Stay here! 
Also, they have a free shuttle as well.

title: “Loved the Bliss Spa, but hotel could loose the "too cool for you attitude"”
text: The bed was comfortable, but one of the lamps didn't work and the room service was beyond bad. The room appeared to have been renovated, poorly, from a hotel that was clearly NOT 4 star, as W rates itself. Too bad, because it's in a a nice location, good view. But the crux of it all is the "too cool for you" attitude. It's the antithesis of the other Starwood brands such as Westin and Sheraton. There are better options in Chicago.

title: “EXCELLENT STAY and CLOSE TO EVERYTHING DOWNTOWN”
text: I have to say the room was super clean and comfortable. They had DVD's to take back to your room if you wanted to check one out from the many offered in the office. The breakfast that is served by the hotel is awsome! not just your average donuts and coffee they have everything even a make your own waffle station! A cute pool and area to kick back with your friends and family and even a gas BBQ grill in the pool area for the guest to use. They also had a laundry for the guest to wash if needed, ( dont go home with diry clothes!) i was so impressed with this cute little gem of a hotel. Not to mention it has a nice convience store very close by to purchase your drinking needs ( of the Adult kind.) And here is the best part they are a Gay Friendly hotel for all you family out there.

title: “Great place, beautiful grounds”
text:
Had a great stay at this resort. I had read some bad reviews, so i was actually on guard. But our room was great. Freshly painted, great carpeting. Everything one could expect.
