We did joke that the paint was peeling off the furniture, but it was "antiqued" and in perfect condition.
The only negative is that they chrge you 25.00 per day for parking, even though there is a multitude of spaces on their fabulous grounds. I wish they would just include tha in the room price to be more accurate. Oh well. It seems like this is a trend.
Didn't try the restaurant, but our friends had. They said it was expensive, but really well worth it.
i wouldn't hesitate booking tthis fabulous property.

title: “Great Location”
text:
The Omni is a beautiful, historic hotel right by the Freedom Trail, just two or three blocks from Boston Common, and just one or two from the Government Center station, which takes you to and from the airport.
Walking in we were helped to the front desk right away. They were very helpful, and since I had called earlier about early check-in, we were given a room right away (noon-ish). The room was very nice; we had a king deluxe. I thought the size of the room was pretty average and found it very comfortable. The bathroom was small but comfortable. The bed was very comfy. The only minor problem was that there wasn't enough drawer or closet space.
All in all, our stay at the Omni was great. The staff was always helpful and our room was always clean when we came back in the evening. We stopped in at their bar, The Last Hurrah, on our last night and also liked it very much; all mahogany and leather.
I did get a deal on Travelocity, so considering their regular rates I'm not sure when I'll stay next, but I hope to.

title: “Very nice!”
text: Very nice hotel, near the water, surrounded by restaurants. This hotel is getting older but still clean and well managed.

title: “Great location”
text: Stayed here for an overnight stop and woke up to the best views of Venice beach. Hotel is pretty basic but a nice room and bathroom. Everything was good about our stay however we were not advised about the charge for wireless until we checked out! If I had known I would have made use of it!! Anyway we didn't let this affect a nice stay in a good hotel in a great location.

title: “Not At All What I Expected”
text:
I had the misfortune of staying at the hotel during the air conditioning fiasco as well but that is indicative of a bigger problem at the Plaza Athenee -- unevenness in staffing. 
I arrived at the hotel for check-in at about 5 pm and was told that my room wasn't ready. When I asked about the large fans I was assured that the problem would be resolved by 6pm. I left the hotel looking for a cool spot to relax (and a little shopping). I returned to the hotel about 7pm to find that the a/c was still broken but my room was available. I asked to be put on the wait list for the soon to arrive portable a/c units and went to my room. Not a word apologizing for the heat or asking if they could help with the luggage. They did offer me a warm bottle of water. 
I let myself into my room (the bellman were busy running around delivering water so they were at least trying to help) to find average accommodations and melted cookies. The closet held a fluffy robe and slippers. At least someone was trying to make it pleasant. The furnishing are dated and a little worn but the room itself was spacious. The bed and linens were lovely. The bathroom was not quite spotless which is a big negative against the Housekeeping staff. 
I had an evening engagement downtown and left for the evening with assurances that I would have a/c upon my return. Guess not as I returned to a room that was almost 84 degrees -- at 12:30 am. When I called the front desk she told me that there were no a/c units available. What happened to earlier promises of a/c or the portable unit? She couldn't say. I did ask her to prepare my bill as I would be leaving directly to go to another hotel. Yes at 1am....it was that bad. Low and behold 5minutes later a portable unit arrived. The gentlemen installing the unit were as kind as they could be particularly after what must have been a long day. They even smiled!
After a fair night's sleep I awoke to find that room service would not be available as the electric was off to fix the a/c Hmm. And when I got to the front door I too had to schlep down the block to Madison to hail a cab in the rain while the doorman watched from under the awning.
To recap the grades: Check-In staff a C, Housekeeping staff a D for dirty, Doorman rate a C as they did open the door for me on the way in and Room Service is a question mark as they were not functioning.
Overall a very uneven stay in terms of the service provided. And I paid rack rate for the pleasure. In NYC there are just to many great hotels to risk a stay here. Try The Lowell and you'll never need wonder if the staff is well trained to deal with a set-back. Hotel Plaza Athenee just isn't worth the risk or the $$$. 
I know that many of you ready this is say that a hotel can't really be responsible for the air conditioning failure however they are responsible for the way in which they dealt with it and this hotel got a failing grade in that department.

title: “Great room, but that's it”
text:
The rooms are nice, but for the price, I am sure you can find another hotel with a nice room and have a better experience.
First I will start with the pros. Apparently it's a brand new building, per every cab driver who didn't believe there was a Hyatt at 48 and Lex. The room was great. Clean and very comfortable. The room size was average for NY, but we also had a suite, so I can't imagine how small the regular rooms would be. Also, we traveled with our 10 month old, so having the dishwasher was a major plus for us. 
So, the cons. Basically all have to do with everything other then the room. Let me preface this by saying that my husband talked to another guest during our trip and they were comparing check in horror stories. This guest said he complained to the manager who said that they hire for personality not by experience. Once we learned that, it all made perfect sense! First check in was ridiculous. We checked-in the morning, no room available, totally fine. When we came back later in the afternoon to get into our room, we had to re-do the entire check in process, which took another 30 minutes. The lobby is very awkward and small, and based on our experience constantly crowded. The front desk is basically in the middle of the room. So when the lady checking us in had to go to the office to get help (multiple times) she had to squeeze through us and all our stuff to make it to the office. The desk needs to be right in front of the door so they can go back and forth without a scene. Also, during check in, we requested a crib. I had to make 3 more phone calls to finally get the crib. The next problem, the 2nd floor where there is supposed to food and drinks? For the two days we stayed we would pop in and out of the floor and there was never anything available. Even first thing in the morning, no coffee, no fruit, nothing. 
Our biggest problem of all, there is no service elevator. So we were constantly being held up by the staff. One time we got on the elevator and it took us down to where the kitchen is, then a staff member held the door while they were putting food on a tray to take someone room service. We asked 3 times if we could please go and they said no! I mean really? Then we were on the elevator with the maid and her trash bags. I feel sorry for the staff that I am sure it takes them forever to do their job, but it just seems to me that the guests should have the top priority. There are not very many rooms, so they could have just one elevator for the guests and use the other one for staff.
Like I stated in the beginning, the biggest deal here is that it is a brand new hotel. The rooms are clean. But, it is expensive and you can find another hotel of equal quality with much better service.

title: “Little Low rent”
text: Cheap and clean enough, but nothing fabulous. People walking through lobby and golf course in swim suits with no cover ups, tacky. Service at both lobby grill and market very poor. Kids had fun at waterpark, but have to get there very early to get a decent seat.

title: “Sophisticated lady”
text: Contrary to other reviewers, we found this a really great hotel, full of history & Art Deco/nouveau class. Staff are efficient, helpful & not over-efficious, just good at their jobs & friendly. Try for a "superior" room overlooking Park Ave or Lexington Ave it's worth the extra for the comfort & quiet.

title: “Great location and fabulous room”
text: We stayed at the Palace this weekend. We had a beautiful, quiet room overlooking the Cathedral on the 36th floor. The rooms were very large (by NYC standards) - we had two double beds and there was plenty of room. The concierge recommendations were perfect for what we were looking for as far as restaurants and things to see. The location cannot be beat and it is a beautiful hotel.

title: “Really nice..”
text:
I found this hotel on Trip Advisor and there's a reason it is #1. Staff were very friendly, capable and repsonsive. There was no remote for the tv in my room and 5 minutes after I called the room service, a technician was at my door with a replacement. I didn't eat in the restaurant but I did order in and the food and service was excellent. 
Bottom line, I will stay again.

title: “Not kind to the Hyatt name”
text:
I stayed here as part of a conference. I arrived early in Chicago because I had other things to do, but made a special trip into the city to check into the Hyatt. I was assigned a room, they took my credit card, they got me all setup but couldn't give me the keys because the room wasn't cleaned yet. Fine, I'll come back later. 
I arrive later that night to find out they gave my room away! Apparently checking in is of no actual value unless they give you the keys. Something that could have been brought to my attention WHEN I CHECKED IN! I got the distinct impression that because I was on a conference rate they weren't willing to give me a nicer room, so they stuck me in a rancid smoking room. 
After a night smelling nicotine and tobacco I insisted they give me a new room the next day (something they had promised) which they did. Props to them for keeping their word, this time.
The rooms are nice, no question there. But nickeled and dimed to death isn't the half of it. They offer "deluxe" rooms for an extra $15 per night, and those have things that a Hyatt hotel should have as part of every room. As for my room, the fridge threatens me with a $25 fine if I put something in it. Nice. Paying $10 per night for internet seems absurd at this price point as well. At least with the Westin if you belong to their frequent traveller program it is free... but not here.
I went to the "Big Bar" something they are very proud of. The service was glacially slow. I asked about premium liqours and the waitress said they had everything. I named a few bourbons that I would like, and they didn't have them. So I settled for a glass of Maker's Mark and some wings. When my bill finally came I paid over $30 for a single glass of bourbon and some chicken wings!
Needless to say I was not even remotely impressed. This hotel has a nice plant, but it seems to have an identity crisis. When I stay at a cheap hotel/motel I expect them to charge me for small things. When I stay at a hotel in this price range, I don't expect to be threatened with a $25 fine for using the fridge in my room.
I would not stay here again unless I attended another conference that was physically in this hotel.

title: “NYC trip”
text: The location is good for visiting Times Square. You can take public transportation to other areas of the city. Location was also good for the fireworks on July 4th. Breakfast is good but you need to be early because it does run out and they are very slow to replenish. Breakfast is over at 10 am and the food starts to be put away at 9:55 am. They want you out of the breakfast area by 10. The breakfast area needs to be cleaned and mopped daily not just swept. The fresh linens by waffle area are NOT changed daily and should be. Syrup and stuff spills and really needs cleaned.

title: “Might be the best Seattle has to offer”
text: Having not stayed @ the Four Seasons (yet), Hotel 1000 in Seattle is an all around perfect experience. From the modern, well appointed room to the knowledgeable staff, this hotel is top of the line. From the valet to the front desk hosts, to the bartender, everyone and everything impresses. They really make an effort to personalize your stay.

title: “"Wonderful staff and terrific room"”
text: Wonderful hotel in a midtown location. Very convenient to Central Park. The design and appointments to the room were fabulous. Loved the ability to open the large windows. The staff was friendly, helpful, and gave wonderful suggestions. Enjoyed our stay.

title: “5 Star stay the first time, this time very different”
text:
I feel terrible writing a bad review over a hotel that I love so much. My first visit to the property was December 2010 and Mr. Wonderful and I fell in love with the hotel. We had a great room and great customer service. Even when the sink sprung a leak they sent someone right away to fix the problem. 
I signed up for email notifications for the hotel and received a promotional email that we decided to take advantage of. The package included a great rate, free parking, bike rental and 2 for 1 dining vocher. When we arrived to the hotel to check in, it was a different story. In short, we argued with the front desk staff who stated this was not the package we booked and refused to honor their advertised rate/package. The staff was terribly rude. It was my own fault for not printing out the confirmation confirming these added perks (I did not think it would be an issue at check-in). Now I am sitting here typing looking at the print out which I didn't have with me at the time that states the free things we should receive but never did. I checked my bank statement today to show that I had been charged for parking when I shouldn't have. I called the hotel once again to get the refund which they still refused.
The hotel would rather argue over $20 and lose a customer for life. We visit San Diego 4 times a year and would have brought great business.
Aside from that, the hotel is beautiful, and the grounds are well kept. Just please learn from my mistake and if you book a package deal where you are supposed to get stuff included, bring the proof!

title: “A real budget hotel downtown San Francisco”
text:
We had room 310 as per request away from the street. Room is sparsely furnished, bathroom has been upgraded, everything is simple and clean. Breakfast is included , not a very plentiful breakfast although there is orange juice, milk and real butter for sliced bread or bagels. Wifi is available in a large and quiet room on the 2nd floor. Television had no remote and if you want a hair-dryer you just ask for it. Hotel is on Bush street and Geary, the main gate to Chinatown is next door, you can walk to every where downtown (not the Golden gate bridge ).There are lots of budget and more uspcale restaurants nearby. The after-noon desk staff is very pleasant and remembers your room number, the other staff is more distant. For the price of $65 per night, this is a true budget hotel and Europeans have discovered it. It makes for very interesting conversation in the Wifi room.
I would recommend this hotel if you do not expect more than what you paid ...
Seattle98103

title: “Excellent Service - Diamond Member”
text:
I am a Hilton Diamond member and travel on a regular basis. Each year around the holidays I travel with my family and this year we chose Washington DC to see some family. I spoke with a front desk manager (Rachel) a few weeks before arrival and reviewed everything I needed re: rooms, cribs, receiving shipments, etc. Rachel handled everything from start to finish. I arrived and everything was setup, crib was put together, etc. Rooms (2) were perfect and exactly what Rachel had promised. I had a stroller like item delivered to the hotel and James in Maintenance took the time to assist in putting it together and getting me on my way.
There was an issue with running out of food during breakfast with all of the people that showed up. The restaurant manager told the truth and did whatever she could to take care of my party including sending a fruit basket to my room once she had fruit again to ensure my party had fruit for the remaining days of our trip.
Thank you to everyone at Embassy Suites DC. Your service was very much appreciated! A special thank you to Rachel and James for their personal services!

title: “Tea at the Brown Palace”
text: A few weeks ago I was fortunate enough to experience high tea at the brown palace. Everything was wonderful. The service was extraordinary and the finger foods were delightful. The tea was delicious as was the complimentary champagne. Even though it was a bit expensive, it was worth every penny and most certainly a value. I will not hesitate to recommend this to all of my friends.

title: “Great location but limited signage frustrating”
text:
We stayed here for two nights. THe room was clean but small. Not that we spent much time in the room. THe location was great. Very convenient to Central Park and subway. The staff on our floor always smiled and said morning which was refreshing. 
Negatives: It is extremely frustrating that there is zero labelling on the hotel. There is no sign on the hotel. Not sure if that is attempt to come off as "hipster" but for people lugging suitcases it is VERY frustrating. Walked up and down the street and took awhile to find the hotel. Found someone to ask and they directed us. We waited in line to check in for at least 20 minutes. WAY too long. Probably exacerbated by the fact that it took us awhile to find the place! And check in seemed to take a long time.

title: “Great Location”
text:
We stayed 7 nights during the hurricane. The hotel staff was very professional
yet friendly & helpful. The standard suite was comfortable, however, the 
bathroom was on the small side. No hand/body lotion included in sundries.
The buffet breakfast was always fresh and well presented. A good choice of
foods. Shopping for any item is available in the area with reasonable prices.
We enjoyed the delis that had a good selection of salads, sandwiches & desserts.
Would definitely stay again at the RI.

title: “Friendly and professional staff”
text:
My husband and I recently celebrated our tenth wedding anniversary. Although we live in the District, our weekend "getaway" was at the Fairfax. It was a lovely experience; the room, staff, and restaurant were all top notch. 
The doorman and bellhop were very friendly. The front desk clerk, Josh, was kind enough to send us a complimentary bottle of wine and handwritten note. Housekeepers were always smiling in the hallways and the turndown service was a nice surprise. Breakfast in the Jockey Club was delicious.
We're looking forward to returning next year.

title: “Very Hip, Great Location”
text:
The Ace has a very hip vibe and I may be too old to stay here but it is nice, clean, comfortable, great location. Really good beds and I'm a stickler for that. I don't know if they have a rule about being younger than 30 to work there but whatever they are doing it is working! The front desk staff is charming, energetic and very very helpful. Reed Smith, in particular, was a great help in advising on food, cabs, the little ins and outs of NYC. He is a delight, seems to work constantly and never fails to have a smile on his face. Room service was prompt and friendly, food is delicious. 
The only drawback as far as I'm concerned is the attitude of the hostesses at both hotel restaurants. They were officious, short and kind of snotty. I really didn't appreciate it at all. 
I think the hotel is geared more toward younger people but it's still a great place to stay. AND it is one solid structure, we couldn't hear a thing from any other room, the elevator, above, below, nothin'. And we had a great view of the Empire State Building. 
Thanks Ace!

title: “Very pleasant stay”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at the Doubletree Metropolitian from for 1 week in July. I have no real complaints about the hotel. The staff was nice and willing to help out; they acknowledged you everytime you passed by them. The hotel is clean, the lobby is clean and inviting and the rooms are clean. The bathroom was quite small (could only fit one person) but, this is New York and what would you expect from an already crowded city???? The hotel is within walking distance of many attractions and considering my boyfriend and I are athletic, we chose to foot it and use the subway system for most of our stay. For those who do not like to walk, there are 2 subway stations right outside the door of the hotel and plenty of taxis pass by on the street. We enjoyed our stay and would use this hotel again if when we revisit the city!

title: “Hiltons, always a pleasure”
text: I am a frequent Hilton guest and nothing about this particular Hilton was any different. Service was great and the hotel was clean as always. The bell man who greeted me was especially nice and helpful. The back bay area is a great location. I really liked the Starbucks and business center located right in the lobby, it's super convenient. I hate that they charge for the internet being that the room was almost $400 but again, that's to be expected. I do want to point out their restaurant 40 Dalton, mmm mmm good. I'm from Las Vegas so I wanted to taste something different and the room service lady suggested the Lobster grilled cheese sandwich and clam chowder, omg delicious! So much so that when I checked out, I made a special trip back to the restaurant to order that same dish. I have stayed here once before and will stay here again.

title: “This is more a home than a hotel”
text:
I love this place. They call it the cinematographer's hotel, because they use(d) to stay here when they where working in LA for several months. This is one of the best places when in Hollywood, especially when you look at the price.
Rooms have fantastic size and it's quiet. Like I said in the title, this feels more like an apartment than a place to crash for the night.
Again: I love this place!

title: “Relax and fly...”
text:
The only choice when traveling from the Detroit airport. Park and fly... and sleep in the world's most comfortable bed!
A beautiful hotel with a relaxing atmosphere. You can even have a room that looks overlooks the planes at the gates (a huge hit with the children!).
Staff is extremely helpful, polite and genuinely nice.
We highly recommend the Westin Airport hotel.

title: “Great location”
text: Just a block from the Air and Space Museum and very near l'Effant Plaza Metro stop. The bed was comfy and the shower hot. The TV did't work, the telephone had a short, and the published Wifi password was wrong. On the up side, the food was above average and the staff friendly.

title: “No better hotel in Boston!”
text: Great location and greater service at this Hyatt in Boston. No more convient place to stay. Came in by train and never needed to have a car. You are right in the middle of everything! The hotel & service is top notch and this isn't my first stay in Boston!

title: “Great stay!”
text: Really nice place to stay. Clean, great service, and fun pub! Hard to believe this is a hotel by an airport, even with the reminders of the planes overhead - easy to overlook with the smallish but very clean rooms and again, great bar with friendly staff throughout the hotel. Will stay here again.

title: “Very basic, but very clean, tidy and spacious”
text: After reading the some of the reviews about this hotel, our group of 11 coming to Washington DC for 5 days were very concerned about what it would be like. Upon arrival, I can definitely say we were pleasantly surprised. The staff were very friendly, and although there was a very old fashioned smell in the reception area, it was clean and in a perfect location. As a group of 11, we had four rooms; one for each group leader and one for a group of 5 boys and another for the 4 girls on the trip. The rooms were spacious with a bed for each person and very clean providing towels, television and very comfy mattresses. If you're looking for a quaint hotel, cheap and bang in the centre of Washington DC, then you should definitely choose the Harrington. The Steak and Chips on the breakfast menu was very delicious and I can honestly say it is one of the best I have had. Some of the other reviews are very unfair as it is obvious the Harrington do their upmost best to ensure customer satisfaction. The man in the gift shop in the lobby was very polite and embarked on numerous conversations about our trip which was lovely to see. Would definitely stay here again and would recommend to everyone who wants a hotel close to all of the tourist attractions.

title: “Great Hotel on the North Side of San Antonio”
text: This is a great hotel on the north side of San Antonio. If you want to go to the River Walk.... you will have to take a car... its not close... but if you want a nice hotel on the outside of the downtown area its a great hotel. I stayed here in Dec of 2011 and the hotel was in full Christmas swing. It had a nice outdoor skating ring... the lobby looked great... it was nice. The room was on the end of a small standard room size. The bathroom was huge, but the room itself was on the smaller side of a standard size room. The gym was nice... pools were great.... this hotel was great. Would love to stay at this hotel again. Its a great place to escape with the family or friends.

title: “Great location, weird room, less than stellar overall”
text: This really is just a cleaner than average 2 star hotel. Room was taller than it was wide - the ceiling had to be 20 feet up. Felt like living in a fish bowl. Room was sparsely appointed (as are all CQ hotels), bathroom was cramped, furnishings were old. Room was clean. Location is great, though - right off Wall Street. You can walk to anywhere downtown from here.

title: “Great Family Hotel”
text:
This is an excellent hotel!!!
the rooms are large & updated, the pool is heated, the staff is friendly, the continental breakfast is FABULOUS and the price is reasonable!!!! you couldn't ask for more.
i'm definetely staying there again.

title: “One of the best options @ LA”
text:
Great service, clean room, a nice bed and a wonderful shower in a great location near to Downtown and all the other LA attractions. Very easy check in/check out process. Great TV channel selection and we also received a very sweet welcome bag on arrival.
Highly recommended!!!

title: “Helpful Staff”
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights with a 6 month old. The staff provided a crib/cot, baby bath and travel pack of Johnson and Johnsons. All of the staff were friendly. The location was excellent for us (only a short walk to the hop on/hop off trolleys, Boston Common, subway etc). We had excellent views from our 20th floor room of Back Bay. Only downside was not having a mini fridge in the room. 
As for the attached restaurant we did not enjoy that was much. We had lunch there one day and the meals were below par (mine had over-ripe advocado on it - so ripe it was brown). The buffet breakfast we also thought was below par for the standard of the hotel.

title: “WOW, This place Rocks, PLEASE READ!”
text:
I stayed here to celebrate with my boyfriend, we stayed for 4 nights, 5 days, and we could not have been happier. We told them we were celebrating our honeymoon initially, but ended up celebrating an engagement instead as things were postponed. However, when we arrived they were so friendly and helpful, that we just left things as were. 
We arrived at the hotel just after 9am, trendy and really fun lobby however, naturally the room was not was available being so early. We requested a West Side View facing room on a higher level, so we didn't mind waiting to see if they would accomodate us. We checked our bags and began our travels around the City, which was EASY as this hotel is PERFECTLY located for Times Square and Theatres & tons of shopping & places to eat, and REALLY close to subways. Just after 3pm, they called to let us know our room was ready so we made our way back. Henry helped with our luggage as we made our way up to the room. They had given us a bottle of wine, complimentary to help us celebrate, along with a very nice welcome/congrats letter. We were surprised they took the time to do so. We had a room on the 25th floor with an awesome view right into Times Square from the bathroom, and awesome view from the living area as well. The room was not very large, but it was perfect for the two of us! The bed was exremeley comfortable, clean, and faced a large flat screen tv that made for great relaxing time after walking all over the city. The bathroom was clean & bright and had fresh flowers daily it seemed! Had a rain shower head along with a hand help, which was really nice! My first trip to NYC, I didn't know what to expect, but for a 4 star Hotel, I felt like we had 5 star service. 
Our favorite employee was Armando! We actually stayed a good 45 min outside with him one night just chatting, and he gave us some good tips on places to go, and places not to after dark, lol. He always greeted us with a smile, and even hailed us a cab at 4:30am to get us to Penn Station! He was great, and we enjoyed our nightly chats with him! We were sad when it was his days off, and we had to leave the following day. Henry was also great, as he brought our bags, answered some questions for us etc. 
The entire staff was great. The place was nice, the continental breakfast was REALLY great also, in a cute little room they called the 1945. We were impressed! 
When I visit again, I will definitely stay here! 
If I had any complaints at all, I will just say that we wish there an ice machine there, and a fridge that worked. Also, being that the rooms were on high levels directly facing other windows, it felt uncomfortable at night in the shower as I could see directly into the offices that had lights on, and in viewing from the street, that meant that they could see directly into the shower as well, which was odd and uncomfortable, so much so that we ended up hanging a towel when we saw people working across the way. Aside from that, we were thrilled.
I do agree that having just the one operating elevator was frustrating at times, however, we also understood that they JUST opened and are still working out the kinks! The longest we waited was just a few minutes, so I think the people who said they waited 10 were fabricating a bit! Have some patience people, this place is outstanding! 
Overall, I think this is a GREAT hotel, awesome location, friendly and helpful staff, and very clean. I can't wait tio visit NYC again, and next time, I will surely stay here again, I just may have found my second home. Thank you Cassa for making my first trip to NYC even better than I could have imagined! And a special thank you to Armando for making us laugh and making our stay even better!

title: “Very classy....”
text: We have stayed in dozens of hotels in NYC, and this one ranks right at the top. Classic. And, classy. Large room. Wonderful service. Excellent location. The "King Cole" bar is...unique. Pricey, but, actually, we had a wonderful deal which made it very reasonable. Highly recommend it....

title: “Horrible staff-Not What I reserved”
text: I have to say; i have stayed in many places and this was by the far the worse. I have been to the houston medical center quite a few times and I have never had this bad of a stay. This is a hotel near the hospitals, there should be friendly service and no problems with reservations. My husband is having surgery at the Michael E Debakey VA Hospital and we stayed here for his pre-op for surgery. When I arrived at the hotel a little earlier than check in time, the front desk was very rude and said that i could not check in until 3pm. I came back at 3pm and she at first could not find my reservation. I had called several times over the phone to make a reservation at this location and they kept telling me they were busy , they would call me back (that should have been a sign), they told me to call the 800 number. I made reservations for a queen bed and a sleeper sofa. When the found my reservation or at least said they did the guy had to go check the room to make sure it was a queen bed. He came down and said it was and it was not. It was a double bed and a chair that folded out into a cot. No towels, pillows or sheets. The staff at the front desk was too busy chatting to take care of customers and not friendly at all..I cancelled my reservation for his surgery and made it somewhere else.

title: “Great place”
text:
Nice looking motel that's way above average! Clean room and great pool at the back. I can't remember what the breakfast was like but overall it truly was a great stay. 
Will definatley come back if I'm in the neighbourhood.

title: “Can't wait to come back!”
text: My mom and I took my 9 yr old daughter to Chicago for our "first annual girls weekend" and trip to the American Girl store (of course). We couldn't have picked a better hotel to stay in. As soon we arrived and our luggage was on the cart "Big Ben" (one of the bellman) took my daughter on a luggage cart ride to the elevator. I can't explain the impression made except that she couldn't leave or come in the rest of the weekend without saying hi to Ben. She even got a pic with him that I know she will treasure. The entire staff was friendly and helpful. Our room had a great view and was so comfortable. Loved how modern everything was. The beds were super comfy and the bathroom was very clean. Everything was easy to walk to from that location and I know this is where we will stay when the second annual trip comes around!!!

title: “Boo”
text: Embassy Suites, You Should Do Better Than This! Cloudy pool, dirty room, dirty sheets, glasses had hairs in them, a booger was smeared on the bathroom door, ants were walking around the bathroom, dead bug on bathroom floor, air conditioner not working correctly, smelly room. Nice breakfast, good sized room, but OVERPRICED.

title: “very nice !”
text: Really nice room - clean and comfortable very nice staff

title: “First Class Experience at the Erwin”
text: I was very favorably impressed with the experience at the Hotel Erwin this past weekend. From the moment of checking in, the staff were pleasant, helpful, and energetic. My room wasn't ready, so they put me in one of their suites, which was as large as an apartment. I loved the clean-but-funky aesthetic of the decor (not the bland, antiseptic feel of the other high end LA beach hotels). When the internet was down on Sunday morning for a short time, front desk manager Chip called me as soon as it was back up, and offered me a late check out to compensate for the trouble. They also kept my car in their parking after check out until I was ready to leave the area. The roof top bar is a very cool way to experience the frenetic energy of the Venice boardwalk. All in, I can't imagine a better place to stay in Venice or Santa Monica.

title: “***** Star Service”
text:
SO much has been said about this property already, but I am happy to report The Hotel Vitale is my new found fave in San Francisco. I'm usually a creature of habit, but decided to give Hotel Vitale a try. I always love walking along the water, visiting the Ferry Building and Farmers Market, Dining, Shopping, Exploring-and this property makes a great base to experience the best of San Francisco. 
The service was incredible from the moment I arrived. I felt genuinely welcomed by the Valet & Bell staff, Front Desk etc. The Concierges are !!outstanding!! and every recommendation was spot on. 
The Vitale attracts a nice diverse all ages mix of people (singles, families, couples) and is such a comfortable place to stay and relax. I was truly surprised at the quality of staff, quality of food, and water view/s at reasonable prices. 
The Vitale has a cozy Lounge and stylish Restaurant offering some truly delectable food and delightful service, and let us not forget about the simple comfortable rooms complete with every amenity.

title: “Nice hotel - Standard excellent W service”
text: Stayed at the W for 2 nights. Have stayed at several W properties around the country. As usual - EXCELLENT service and as always - funky decor (make sure you turn off the glowing budha in your room before turning in for the night). I would recommend asking for a room on a higher floor (which I had). The street noise can be loud at times (there is a fire station next door). It is close to the Mascone center and the financial district. Not a lot of local charm in the area (it is the business district after all) but it is a quick cab ride to anywhere you need to go in the city.

title: “great boutique hotel in the loop/chicago”
text: This is a smaller boutique hotel in the loop/Chicago. Located on Jeweler's row next to the train tracks. Great location, near many great restaurants, the lake, museums etc. Easy to walk to many locations. Parking is $46/day plus tax so I took another traveler's advise and parked in the Millenium garage several blocks away as it was "only" $23/day. Not a bad walk really. The rooms were roomy and rather plain but served the purpose. It was built in 1897 and has historical information all over. Would highly recommend this hotel. Check in is on the second floor.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location, Great Value”
text: My partner and I stayed here with our two friends at the start of December 2010 and found it to be everything we had hoped for. It is just a short walk from Grand Central Station which means getting around to see all the sights is very easy. We were upgraded for free (both rooms) as there was space, without even having to ask. The room was very large, the beds were very comfortable and the room was always kept very clean. Despite the busy location it was very quiet at night and the staff always seemed very helpful, from getting us take away menu's to lending us scissors! Broadband was a little slow (and quite expensive) but nevertheless it was sufficient for all we needed. Yes the decor is slightly dated but it was perfectly adequate and for the price we paid you could not expect 5 star decor! There was plenty of draw and wardrobe space, and all the little extras that you don't always get (hairdryer, iron and ironing board, coffee maker). It was really everything that we needed for our short trip (4 days) and I would reccommend this hotel to everyone, and would definately stay again.

title: “Loved the Mayflower rooms and services”
text: Plush bedding, great views, sitting room, and great service!

title: “great location but....”
text: This hotel is in a fantastic location but has not much else going for it. It is tired and needs a revamp badly and the staff are apathetic at best. That said, it was ok for a few days and there is so much to do in Washington you don't spend anytime in the room anyway. Such a waste of a great spot,right in the centre of Georgetown.

title: “Great location, staff mixed.”
text: Hilton Baltimore is located right in the heart of downtown and is connected by bridge to the Baltimore Convention Center. Front desk staff was a little less enthusiastic about my visit and not very helpful in terms of explaining Hilton Gold lounge access. Concierge was excellent, though.

title: “Excellent small hotel in Midtown”
text:
Traveling with family, we needed a room with three beds. We found a clean, comfortable, affordable and spacious (for New York) little suite at the Blakely. Two queens and a flat screen T.V. in the main bedroom, a full-size day bed and second flat screen in the extra room.
This is not luxury, but neither does it feel like a budget hotel. Continental breakfast is included and is not bad (if low on protein-rich options) and there is a computer and printer available for use in the lobby that works well.
The staff were all helpful, especially the bellmen. I was impressed by how attentive and friendly they all were. They seem to double as concierge, happy to give advice about subway stops and restaurants, and if they don't know the answer, they find out and get back to you.
Would absolutely stay here again.

title: “Great Location and Price”
text: To start, it was veryeasy to make reservations. I just called the 800 number and got to talk to a lovely woman who was very helpful. Then I decided to add an extra night to our stay and that was easy too. We showed up early(1 pm), and they let us go ahead and check in. I was with my daughter, and she wanted a vew, and the man at the desk was very accomadating. He put us on the 12th floor not facing the Hilton. The rooms were lovely. The decor was tasteful. Each floor has a theme, the 12th is The Art Institute. There is free wifi access from your room and a minifridge and coffee pot.. The pool is very large, but not as warm as I'd hoped for it to be called a heated pool. The kids enjoyed it nonetheless. The sauna is nice, but I think it needs a hot tub. There are pool towels available also, which is nice. They are larger ones too, not the usual small ones like at most hotels. The location is great, right across from Grant Park, and within walking distance to most other stuff. There is also a shuttle that will drop you off lots of places. The in-hotel resturant is very pricy, but she let me order off the kids menu, and that was enough food for me. I will definetly be staying here again when I go to Chicago.

title: “Great Location, Excellent Service”
text: In town for a conference and got a great rate. Hotel location was excellent, right next to Millenium Park. Walk to Michigan Ave, Lake, North Pier and Navy Pier. Close to restaurants, Art Institute, Cultural Center and architectural boat tours. Hotel staff outstanding! The hotel has a first come/first serve complimentary Bentley! Lucky enough to ride in it on a Saturday night - we felt very cool! The hotel asked what we wanted and we got it - local paper in the morning rather than NY paper, regular coffee maker instead of a capp. maker, etc. Restaurant food delicious and service super friendly.

title: “Highly Recommended the Affinia Dumont”
text:
We decided to book the Affinia Dumont, after reading MANY hotel reviews for NYC. We spent 5 nights there with our 7-year old son. My husband took the train each morning to work-related meetings in NJ. My son & I spent our days exploring NYC. This was our 1st time in the city and we had no problem figuring out the subway/transportation system and had an absolute blast! I am a very picky traveler - I must say the Affinia Dumont was one of the best hotels, overall, that we have ever stayed in. We had been warned about the size of hotel rooms in NYC, but our room at the Affinia Dumont was by no means small. There was ample storage space, which enabled us to unpack for the entire week. The full kitchen in our room was over-the-top!! We did some grocery shopping a few steps away, which enabled us to eat in for several meals. It was relaxing to wake up and not have to worry about getting dressed to go out 1st thing in the morning. If we wanted to grab a quick lunch or snack...it was at our fingertips! Our 1st day in NYC brought rain. My husband took the complimentary umbrella in our room, for his morning commute. The Bell Hop was quick to offer my son & I umbrellas for our day out. Which brings me to my next comments - kudos to the absolutely WONDERFUL Bell Hop and front desk attendants. They were exceptionally friendly and very, very helpful. We brought along a portable DVD player, but forgot cables to connect it into the TV in our room. My husband went to the front desk to see if we could get cables; the front desk attendant sent a technician up to our room within minutes with a DVD player. He connected it and made certain it worked before he left. I also made use of the fitness center, which was also very well-equipped. There is also a self-service laundry, which came in handy, on the basement floor. 
We would most definitely stay again at the Affinia Dumont!! The rooms were fantastic and the staff was outstanding!!

title: “Decent Freeway budget massively understaffed”
text:
Waited 15 minutes to check in beacause no one was at the front desk busy fixing a room
for another guest could use a bit better staffing.Rooms were ok renovated basic not great.Breakfast was sparse mostly packaged boiled eggs but free.Paid $59/tax.
Worth maybe half of that.OK for a one night stand off I-10 in West Houston though.

title: “Great location/Clean rooms”
text: Hotel location was perfect for downtown shopping. Rooms were very clean and updated. Tenth floor pool and workout facilities were enjoyable. Easy parking (structure attached for $28/day).

title: “Great hotel, great location & great staff”
text:
Booked this hotel after reading reviews on Trip Advisor and am so glad I did. From the moment we arrived it felt right. The welcome from reception staff (particularly Jake) was wonderful and nothing was too much trouble. The doormen were always so polite and always smiling and unlike many places in San Francisco, I didn't feel they were only being nice just to get a tip out of you.
We stayed here for 3 nights initially on floor 5 and had a great view of California Street and the cable cars. The cable cars never disturbed us at all as they stop at a reasonable hour in the evenings and pass by the hotel quickly. 
Our room was fantastic, large, clean and comfortable and the bathroom had that wow factor with lots of marble and complimentary toiletries & lots of fluffy towels. 
In the wardrobe (closet), there were luxurious bathrobes to use during your stay, an iron and ironing board (useful as the airport luggage handlers squash your cases so much your clothes have creases where you didn't think they could have creases), plus a safe to keep your valuables in.
The beds were soooo comfortable I wanted to take one back home with me - clean crisp sheets, clean crisp duvets and covers and lots of comfy pillows.
After spending a few days out of town travelling other states we returned to the same hotel for the last few nights of our stay in San Francisco. This time we were on the top floor (floor 17) where the room was exactly the same layout but being so high you only had little windows and this slightly lost the fun of being on California Street as we couldn't see the street - only the buildings opposite.
Being in the financial district had its pros and cons. Cons being there weren't that many places to eat around the hotel however there is a lovely new Irish bar just opened on Sacramento Street (about 2 minutes walk away) plus another restaurant next to it (can't remember the name but recommended by hotel staff). Also, as someone else mentioned, I felt a little out of place in casual wear when most other people were in business suits but this was mostly apparant during the day rather than at night. 
The pros of this hotel's location is that it's only 3 short blocks from the Montgommery Street BART stop and took us only 10 minutes to walk from the BART to the hotel. Another good point about the hotel being in the financial district is that (unlike every other part we went to - particularly the tourist parts) you didn't get any 'down-and-outs' hassling you for money as the businesses and hotels in the area don't take kindly to the down-and-outs hassling their clients. It all felt very safe around the area.
I don't know if it's a sign of the financial downturn at the moment, but be warned if you are out and about in general San Fran - there are a LOT of beggers / down-and-outs / homeless / drunks constantly trying to get money out of you and it gets a bit tiring after a while.
If you are going to San Fran, stay here - it's fantastic.

title: “Nice hotel; I hope the area catches up with it”
text:
This hotel's best service is undoubtedly its valet parking. The service is amazing. I never waited more than a minute or two for my car. In fact, there are some rates that include unlimited valet parking in it; however, be careful. I paid the higher rate to include this amenity and was charged for the parking anyway. The readily amended it when I brought it to their attention. (Maybe they're accustomed to having to do so.) 
The area surrounding the hotel is very dicey. So, the hotel offers a free service in which they will take you or pick you up from any location within a three-mile radius until 11:00 p.m. This can be especially helpful since the streets are quite confusing with lots of one-way streets. 
They offer free Starbucks coffee all day, which is especially nice if you have travelled and are now in a different time zone. The staff at the Grand Cafe was very friendly and accommodating.
The room was cleaned early in the day, which is somehting that I just haven't seen happen in most other hotels.
We requested early check-in for two rooms and, although they weren't ready when we arrived, they were available to us within the hour.
Prior to this trip, I stayed at the Hollywood Renaissance Hotel - and I cannot begin to list all of the problems that I encountered with them. It was so bad that they offered me a free room on my next trip. Oddly, I haven't been able to get the Manager who offered this compensation to return my call. 
Try the Omni Los Angeles. It's a part of the city that many people visiting L.A. don't see - but should.

title: “Always Come Back”
text:
I'v stayed here over over 25 times the past 3 years for business. It's very conviently located whether i fly into Burbank or LAX. walking distance to several restaraunts and shopping centers
Service is always extremely good, Front Desk and houskeeping are always accomodating of my needs.
The Executive lounge breakfast has really improved over last year or 2. Laura who works the lounge most mornings is always helpful and freindly. She gets my tea ready as soon as i walk in and gets day off to great start with friendly conversation.

title: “Needs updating and attention to detail.”
text: We stayed here one night when attending an event in the Marriott next door. Check in was smooth. However, the rooms are very worn and the carpets in the hallway were dirty. The hot water in the shower was not that hot. The bathroom sink was clogged and when I called for someone to address it, noone ever showed up. We had to leave to our evening event so I never called again. Lastly, the room was not equipped with the sheets/blanket for the sofa bed. I had to call for that also. All in all, this hotel is not up to the usual Residence Inn standards. There are better options in the city at this price point.

title: “Worst Experience Ever”
text: We arrived on a Wednesday with our two and four year old. We checked into our room to find that it was dirty. The bathroom was not clean and there was a sticky matter still on the desk/table. We decided to go downstairs and eat at one of the few restaurants that the resort offered. The only choice available was the lounge area. We went to the front desk and asked if any of the restaurtants would be opening later in the evening, we were told no due to the lack of customers in the resort. We were told to go to the bar/lounge area and eat. We chose not to do this due to the ages of our children. We then mentioned that our room was dirty. No other room was offered and the supervisor on duty was very rude. She did apologize for the room being dirty and that was it. She did not care if we stayed there or not. We checked out and went to another hotel in a better part of town. After only being at this resort for no more than 3 hours, they still charged us for the room. Staff was very rude and unaccomodating and the rooms were dirty. I WOULD NOT recommend this resort to anyone!!

title: “You get just what you expect”
text:
This is a nice building in a nice location with nice, clean rooms. Don't expect super-personalized service, just expect nice facilities and you'll be satisfied.
We spent a week in the Grand Hyatt while puttering around Seattle. It was a nice base of operations, though in hindsight I would have chosen something a couple blocks closer to the water. We didn't eat or drink in the hotel, except Starbucks from the lobby and bottles of wine we carried in. The fridge did a FINE job chilling lots of wine.
We came to Seattle to eat, and that doesn't mean at the hotel. Get out and experience the city, and use the hotel as your basecamp.
Of particular pleasure (in May 2007) was Union. Amazing food, great service. The Seattle Art Museum was an excellent afternoon excursion. Salumi, a casual cured-meat joint run by Armandino Batali, was spectacular. And hop a ferry to Bainbridge Island (or Victoria if you want a longer excursion), it's a nice change of pace in good weather.

title: “great value in Waldorf suite”
text: We were in NYC for college visit, needed sleeping arrangement for three in three separate beds. For about $500 got a 1BR suite with two doubles in the BR and a pullout sofa in the LR. Beautiful furnishings, fireplace, comfy seating in living area, nice bathroom if smallish for a suite. Sofa bed was ridiculously uncomfortable, we folded it back up and made up the sofa into a bed, which was fine for my teen son. Love the public areas and bar, loved the room. Do wish they would give you a break on a slightly early checkin, we arrived about an hour early absolutely drained from a long drive in really bad weather, they would not budge on the time. All in all a good experience and the suite was cheaper than two standard rooms in another hotel,which would have been our other option.

title: “Very Nice Business Hotel”
text: I have stayed here twice in the past three weeks and will return again mid-August. The hotel is conveniently located to the airport and has free shuttle service. The people are vey accomodating making your stay enjoyable. They will recommend local places to eat with restaurants in many price ranges. The restaurant on site serves an excellent hot breakfast buffet. Complimentary wifi is available if you belone to Sheraton's Club. They have an indoor-outdoor pool that wanders back into part of the main lobby; nice effect. There is a convenient store right next store for snacks and gasoline. Nice location; nice people. There is also an area in lobby to print boarding passes.

title: “Perfect Location, Very Nice Hotel”
text:
We stayed here on 2 separate occasions on a trip to the Bay Area several weeks ago. The first 3-night stay we stayed in the new tower and the second 3-nights were spent in the old tower. Rooms have been renovated in both towers, personally I liked the 'old' rooms better as they were more classic San Francisco, more character, while still having been updated.
I don't think anyone could say something negative about the hotel's central location. Literally the only hotel located on Union Square, everything is right outside. As a San Francisco local, and someone who is very familiar with SF hotels, I knew this was a good choice and we got a great deal. We had stayed at Le Meridien SF in the past, which is a great hotel, although the location isn't quite as central. This hotel offers everything from Starbucks in the lobby to resturants, bars, a full spa, etc. 
My husband worked out several times and the workout room was fine. We both got massages which were fine, but not anything extraordinary. The lights were only slightly dimmed which I don't prefer - not that I want it pitch-black, but more dimmed would have been better. They have a nice changing area with all the essentials, plus showers and a steam room.
The first room we stayed in, in the new tower, was a classic, nice room. Nothing particularly noteworthy and no unique decor or style, but had everything you need and was definitely well-done. Only one sink which I wan't terribly thrilled with, but there was a large counter.
The old tower had a lot more personality and felt more like old SF. The room was large and the TV was at a weird angle on the side table though. The bathroom was smaller than the 'new' room.
One complaint, we had the 'do not disturb' sign on the door and were actually sleeping in on the day of our anniversary. They kept knocking and knocking despite the sign. They were delivering Champagne a friend had called to order for us and yes, it was 10am, but being woken up for it wasn't the most pleasant thing.
Oh and parking is ridiculously expensive. We left our car for 2.5 hrs and paid $30!
Overall, we had a very nice stay and b/c of the location we would definitely stay again, but it would really depend on getting a good deal. I think there are hotel rooms in the city that are a bit more stylish but I definitely am not complaining with what we got. Just a bit more basic, style-wise.

title: “A Good Room at a More Than Fair Price.”
text: I stayed in Room 714 and it was big, clean, and comfortable. The staff was friendly and accommodating. I also got a great deal through Orbitz for multiple nights. I only have two complaints about the room. The TV won't swivel so you can watch TV in bed and while the hotel accommodates several hundred people, the dining room only has about 25 seats, so go early. On the plus side, they serve a hot breakfast, which for the price was quite impressive. The hotel has a great location for commuting to OSU, Worthington, and Dublin. I had a nice time there.

title: “Great hotel and Location”
text: Overall it was a great experience, room was very nice and view wasn't that bad even though it was a city view and on a floor that wasn't very high. Location is perfect for shopping, it is a 2 minute walk away from the mall and all the boutiques. Lots of options for food nearby, try the burger joint around the corner, i think it was called juicy burger, amazing burgers. The tram is right outside the hotel and it takes you straight to the wharf and the pier.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
It is a quiet escape from the city streets . Clean ,friendly and they have the best beds we slept in during our vacation.
Free breakfast is definitely a big plus.
The 32 street Korea Town is packed with restaurants serving ethnic food and is an interesting experience. Didn't like them putting out their garbage on the street tough .
As you make your first step trough the hotel entrance you leave all that behind and can enjoy a nice relaxing atmosphere in a 2 level lobby well equipped with wide screen TVs and hot drinks.
Enjoyed our stay and i would warmly recommend this hotel.

title: “It was Good... for free”
text: My husband and I are originally from Boston and were up visting family. We stayed the last two nights of our trip. The hotel is an average $300+ a night hotel, I didn't think it was a five star as advertised. But we had two nights free. As for the room, the bed is comfortable, small pillows standard size, the bathroom was great, very big with good lighting. The main lobby is very big, I didn't like it..has a very cold feeling to it. We decided to have dinner one night at Rumba's the bar located in the lobby...we were very disappointed when we got there. It was packed with people just off of work...drinking. It was upsetting as guest of the hotel we could not get a seat, and had to wait in the lobby until people started to leave. Don't go between 5-7pm. The food was great though, staff not very friendly at all. As for the location, for anyone visiting Boston, it's good. You are in walking distance to everything. Good location for family vacation.... very close to Children's museum, Aquarium and Faneuil Hall. Would I stay there again..no prefer Newbury St area for shopping and dining...better hotels...Oh the other thing I'd like to mention...even though they advertise walk-in service for a chair massage...not true..you better call ahead. I was looking forward to a little massage...but it didn't happen they were booked...not enough help...didn't like that.

title: “Nice staff, comfortable, spacious rooms, and closest to airport. Very reasonable rates!”
text: Our rate to stay and park was much cheaper that airport parking alone. Nothing special except for nice staff and shuttle. Breakfast could've been a little better, but OK for what it was.Highly recommended.

title: “Wonderful Sights, Wonderful Room, Wonderful Vaction”
text: My family and I just loved it there. Our room (107) was perfect. It was right near the patio, close proximity to the beach. We were treated very well. The entire hotel experience was a delight. A very highly recomended hotel for everyone.

title: “Beyond Budget”
text:
Booked this hotel for a weekend in November upon recommendation as "clean, Spartan room" from a travel book, so we were not expecting much... I was seriously under whelmed. 
The room was old, tired and felt very dirty. I slept fully clothed and wore socks at all times. The shower was gross, but sink and toilet seemed new and clean. Pillows felt filled with cotton balls, bed creaked and squeaked with the slightest movement (as did everyone else's around us too), walls and carpet were stained, did not feel the lock on the door would work. We faced a lovely strip club. 
The noise outside the hotel was expected due to the downtown location, but the noise from inside the hotel was obscene! People banging on our door at 3 in the morning, a party in the room above us (not to mention the 'lovemaking' we felt as if we were right in the bed with them!) Walls in general were paper thin could hear all of our neighbours conversations and whatever show they were watching on TV.
Some of the staff was very friendly, others not the sharpest... 
The location was great and we could walk everywhere. 
Would not reccomend and am embarresed to say I stayed here!

title: “Top Notch”
text: Stayed at this hotel in mid October and EVERYTHING was first class, from valet to check in to the quality and comfort of the room! I'm in the hospitality industry and this is the way to treat guests. We stayed in a suite which was huge with nice views and very chic. The location can't be beat. Definitely one of the best hotels I've stayed in and we'll definitely return.

title: “Honeymoon”
text:
My Wife and I stayed here for one week on our Honeymoon in August 2011. We had booked in January, prior to the hotel becoming part of the Hilton Group.
A few months prior to our trip, I contacted the Guest Services Manager, Elle Lee, to arrange flowers and champagne for my wife as a surprise. From first contact, I felt there was nothing that they wouldn’t do for us, and this was carried through by every member of staff we encountered throughout our stay. I’d arranged for roses, rose petals and champagne to be in the room for our check-in, and my wife really liked them.
From the guys who helped us unload and then load our luggage in and out of the cars, the staff on reception, the concierge and the bar staff were all friendly and helpful. We used the concierge to book into a couple of restaurants – I knew the name of them and they did the rest. 
It took us a few days to realise that there were a couple of computers that we could use for free (along with a printer), and once we did we started to use them to find restaurants and information on Broadway shows.
Most nights we had a drink or two in Rare Bar before we went out. Again the staff were really friendly and one bartender had remembered what beers I’d already tried from their selection of draft beers. The hostess pointed us in the right direction for the Subway.
The room was nicely decorated and we weren’t short of space for our bags, clothes and even when we bought stuff, it didn’t clog the room up. The bed was massive and so comfy. The air-con made it easy to keep the room cool enough for us and the black-out blinds meant that the sun wasn’t waking us up. Our room was directly outside the elevators, and we were never woken by noise from either the elevators or the rooftop bar, and we were on the 19th floor. The bathroom was a good size and the walk-in shower was great.
The rooftop bar was nice, but was a bit too trendy for us. There were a lot of New Yorkers in when we went up. I was surprised how loud the music was as we hadn’t heard any noise from anywhere else in the hotel. The view was great; absolutely worth going up and having a drink or two.
Overall it is a really great hotel for the price, and the staff helped in making it a little bit more special.

title: “Good hotel but not outstanding”
text: I had a pleasant four night stay at the Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan SoHo Village; the bed was comfortable, the view was good, the staff were friendly, but there just wasn't anything special about it that would make it any better than a nice Premier Inn. It wasn't like it was cheap either. Don't get me wrong - if you're looking for somewhere to rest your head for a few nights and want it to be in a great West Village location then go for it. Other than how tiny the room and pretty noisy air-con was there's really nothing to complain about, but I just wouldn't rave about it.

title: “neat hotel!”
text:
I was not expecting this to be as good as it was! Price & location were my reasons for staying here, but it was great! Very funky nautical theme throughout (rooms have round windows like portholes) with a really pleasant & good patio restaurant off the lobby and a very good oriental restaurant down below. The location is wonderful: near Highline; meatpacking district; Hudson; Chelsea market. Only drawback is every room has just 1 queen bed which is very limiting but if it works for you, definately stay here.
Nancy C., Cincinnati

title: “Very Nice”
text:
I was here once before, maybe 5 years ago, and thought it was good. This time, i'm thinking it's fab. The bed was super comfortable. The room was HUGELY quiet. No LAX noise at all, WOW. The LAX shuttle service was VERY good, the driver helped with my oversized bag, very good service. The restaurant needs more light (could barely read menu) but the service was GREAT and the food was REALLY GOOD.
i'm actually a picky person when it comes to hotels, but this one was quite good and i'll be back when in LA. Really happy with this one.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: This hotel is right off I-74 in south Indianapolis. It looks slightly dated from the outside but the inside is very up to date and inviting. The front desk person was very friendly and the lobby is clean and attractive. They do have an elevator. The hallways are wide and well-lit. Standard fare for breakfast.

title: “A wonderful affordable downtown hotel”
text: This hotel is well kept, beautiful inside, some rooms are small but beautifully appointed. Right on Market street near transporation and the Orpheum theater. The hotel staff is unfailingly helpful and courteous. A great place to stay with more reasonable prices than most downtown hotels.

title: “Fabulous place to stay in NYC”
text: The Hotel Giraffe staff makes this the perfect place, along with coffee in the AM, drinks & snacks at happy hour, the lobby is a great place to meet up or work. Nice sized really comfortable rooms, good location, subways close by. Really great place, many places nearby to eat reasonably, don't miss Eataly - I visit NYC alot for business and this is one of my favorite places to stay!

title: “Wonderful room & location!”
text: Our family of three recently stayed for four nights at the Comfort Suites and could not have made a better choice. Our room was spacious and spotless and the location afforded us easy access to all of Chicago's top attractions. The in-room kitchen was very much used and appreciated. We would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for top-notch, yet affordable, accommodations.

title: “Comfortable and clean”
text: This is a great hotel with a great price. My room was nice and big, everything was clean, and the desk staff were friendly and helpful. My only complaint was that housekeeping didn't get to my room until fairly late in the day -- past the 3:00pm check-in time. Other than that, I was thrilled with my experience.

title: “Terrific hotel; great bed, great service”
text:
My wife and I stayed on a Friday night in December and had a great time. 
The room was very nice, on the cozy side, but not unexpected for a city hotel. The in-room amenities were great; tv, very comfortable bed and linens, couch. The hotel is very clean. We were wondering if it would be loud in our hotel room because the lobby area/bar areas are very active (lots of hotel guests and locals/other tourists and music) during the weekend nights - but there was no spillover. We actually liked the way we could grab a drink and snack in the main area and have fun and then retire to our room without having to go far away. The complimentary car service was terrific too. No waiting for a cab!
The location is nice, right on the Charles and next to the T stop and Beacon Hill, so easy and quick (<15 min) to get to Downtown Boston or Cambridge without having to be inside either

title: “We loved it!!”
text:
We stayed here for 2 weeks in October and there is absolutely no complaint whatsoever! The rooms were cleaned promptly and properly, new towels each day, bathroom and toilet was bleached every morning and the cleaners were so friendly! The pool was clean and tested regularly!
Reception staff were accommodating and understanding and had more patience with my daughter who has ADHD and special needs than I expected! The restaurant staff were great especially Louis. My daughter loved his cheese grills every morning!
We had such a great time we are going again next year for a month!
I would recommend this place to singletons, couples and families! Basically I would recommend this hotel to anyone!!

title: “I would not recommend”
text: I chose this hotel because of its location, close to the West End, aquarium. and reunion tower. Be aware you can not go up into the tower without dinner reservations and you can't take the kids into the bar area just to look around. This hotel might be fine for business travelers, but not for families. There was a dance workshop going on and the hotel was full of tween girls and the valet parking took almost an hour. Nothing special about the rooms, and don't call for extra blankets, they will take almost an hour to get to you...

title: “Another World of Luxury!”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for my birthday and let me tell you, it truly is a different world of luxury. Upon check in we were upgraded to an Executive Suite (without asking) that had a living room, HUGE bathroom and a king sized bed overlooking the Water Tower. Also had some dried & fresh fruits as well as a box of Vosges Chocolate Truffles waiting in the room for us. Oh, the bathroom had a jacuzzi tub with a TV in the wall! While we didn't eat at the hotel (we went to Gibson's), we did grab some pastries & coffee from the French bistro on the 1st floor for breakfast that were perfect. Obscenely expensive, but an experience we'll remember forever. Well worth it!
p.s. The shampoo/lotion they provide is from Molton Brown which you should try your hardest to use all of, it's fantastic stuff!

title: “Friendly Staff, Great location”
text:
The staff at this hotel were friendly and helpful. The room decor was outdated but by no means shabby. We had a corner room which was a very nice size and quiet. We also had a wood burning fireplace and enjoyed a nice fire made by the staff. All calls made to the staff were promptly responded to. The location is wonderful and many attractions, dining and great shopping are all within walking distance.
Also has free wireless! Very nice amenity.

title: “We loved the Watertown”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Watertown and loved it. The room was clean & the bed comfortable. We loved the Aveda bath products. Parking was free and the buffet breakfast was good. The desk help were friendly and extremely helpful. The area was interesting with lots of coffee shops, vegetarian restaurants, several movie theaters and funky shops within walking distance (3-8 blocks).

title: “Great location”
text: Could not be in a better location, staff very helpful, room clean not particually big, hotel would possibly benefit from brighting up with a refit but generally ok

title: “Fabulous, charming and traditional”
text: This hotel lived up to every bit of expectation me and my partner had about it. Spacious, pefectly spotless rooms, attentive and friendly staff, situated on the top of the quietly delightfull Nob Hill, totally central to some of the most interesting areas in SF. The traditonal cable cars just steps from the hotel entrance is sure a plus, we used it all the time for the sheer fun of it. The overall feelling is of elegance in that delicious old-fashioned way, to the point that you even don´t care about the dated tv sets, the furniture is old, yes, and perfectly kept , I would be sorely desappointed to find anything other than that. And on top of it all (literally) the Top of the Mark, for a drink / dinner with a (great) view. I would definitly go back, since it made our SF experience a way better one.

title: “Average Motel”
text:
We stayed at the La Quinta Thomas road for three nights after flying into Phoenix Airport for the start of a 3 week trip through California. In general the hotel was ok and reasonably clean. It does however get noisy at nights with trucks manouevring on the lot quite frequently. The neighborhood is probably not the best, we did however not feel unsafe while we were there.
The staff were quite friendly as well, particularily in organizing us a room despite our booking beeing cancelled by La Quinte because we did not arrive before 18:00 even though we had indicated late arrival when booking and had it guaranteed with a credit card.
The location of the motel is convenient, if you are travelling by car. Using public transportation (busses) from downtown Phoenix and particularily Scottsdale takes forever, so i recommend to use a cab to get around.

title: “Not worth the money they charge”
text: The public areas are nice to look at. The staff at reception were helpful and check-in was met with a warm greeting. The staff in other areas were mostly courteous and professional but the bar staff was wooden and unhelpful. The room itself was a decent size but not big. Furnishing were comfortable enough. The internet was unbelievably slow and had to call the hotel's IT department 3 times to troubleshoot problems. Not acceptable as they charge $15 a day for internet service. If you use the valet service, expect to wait upwards of 30 minutes whenever you want your car. Returning in the evening after dinner, waited about 15 minutes to be acknowledged by a member of the valet team. The staff seemed to smile alot but lacked any substantive abilities when dealing with any issues. Had a minor problem with my booking that took far longer than necessary to resolve as the staff were dense and difficult to talk to, as though it were their first day on the job. This hotel seems a magnet for conferences but I couldn't recommend this place for business or leisure purposes. There are much better choices for the money they charge.

title: “Great reception staff; shame about the rooms.”
text: The staff on reception staff are all excellent- polite, helpful and quick. Unfortunately, the rest of the hotel doesn't live up to the welcome. The hotel corridors are dark, dingy and dirty. Most of the grey doors are covered in scuff marks. The standard of cleanliness is poor. In my room I found hairs and bodily fluids belonging to other people, the shower curtain was the mouldiest and smelliest one I've come across in years. Finally, the carpets are not properly cleaned. There was an inch of dirt around the edge of the room where the vacuum didn't reach. I will not stay here again.

title: “OK Hotel - don't trust them with your reservations”
text: I booked a room at the Hotel Indigo - Chelsea because my husband I stayed at the Hotel Indigo in London and had a great visit. I booked a room at the Hotel Indigo in Chelsea about a month before the stay and booked a room to stay with a coworker - so booked a room with two beds. When we arrived we learned that our reservation had been changed to a single king room. The hotel staff who was working at the time was extremely disrespectful (not an ounce of customer service) and blamed us for the mistake - they blamed my credit card - although my card had been charged - they said it was my fault. They said we could call the manager or settle with a roll away bed brought in from another hotel. We did not have any options and ended up staying. When we were checking out a few days later we overheard someone else having the same experience. I will not stay here again.

title: “great spot for st patricks day...fab view of the green river”
text:
i booked this hotel with a tip on deals from the trip advisor forum and got a good deal...after reading the reviews (and seeing and hearing the house of blues as I arrived) I asked for a high floor and a quiet area of the hotel....i was on the 16th floor in a great room with a view of the river, the marina towers and 35 wacker drive one of my fav buildings in chicago...very convienient for my evening at the oriental seeing hair...and for viewing the green river on st patricks day!! I had a problem...my toilet overflowed...and the response was quick and clean up promt and thorough....i think this is where you find out if you're in a good hotel with good service!
loved this hotel!!i

title: “Westin is top notch”
text: This place is great. Top notch from the time we pulled up to the time we left. The place is awesome through and through. Two things though......1) they will hit you with 40 bucks for the valet. You really have no other choice and don't want to deal with finding a spot. 2) They charged me for the mini bar. I questioned it at checkout and the guy just took it off. Very politely and never asked a question. Probably standard procedure. Who knows. Place is great.

title: “You MUST stay here!”
text:
I had SUCH an amazing experience at Cedarbrook. My fiance' (at the time) and I booked it for the Friday night prior to and the night of our wedding. We booked about 6 months in advance. The staff was friendly, took us around, showed us the rooms, failities and grounds. We booked it then. When we came back 2 weeks prior, they remembered our NAMES! Not only that, but there was a small glitch in the booking and they fixed it - no problem. 
I stayed in a suite and adjoining room with my bridesmaids the night before. It was perfect for hanging out, and we loved the "living room" and snacks :)
The wedding day was perfect. Spacious enough for lots of getting-ready and we used the adjoining room (closed off by then of course) for the groomsmen. The grounds were beautiful for photos.
I highly, HIGHLY recommend staying here. It was a wonderful experience . . . one I will never forget :)

title: “One of the better options in Boson”
text:
The location of the Ritz places it as one of the better choices in the vicinity of the theater district and Boston Commons. Although not necessarily the prettiest of locations, it is quite convenient. 
I had a suite on the 10th floor, and found it to be very good for an upscale hotel like the Ritz-Carlton. Although housed in a modern building, the room itself seemed in keeping with the more traditional Ritz style. 
Like some other Ritz hotels, I found the climate control to be marginal.
