There are traditional home-style thermostats, but they only seem able to work across a limited temperature range...no more than maybe +/-5 degrees from what the hotel sets. To most people this probably isn't an issue, but I tend to like it just above meat locker temperature, and so I found the room a bit too warm for my liking. 
Otherwise, no complaints whatsoever about the room or the furnishings. The shower was wonderful, as was the plush, inviting bed and all the rest. Very "Ritzy". 
One of the things I liked best about the Ritz was the quiet. Even though the hotel seemed full, inside our room was dead quiet. I'm the type who doesn't usually sleep well away from home due to all the little noises, but I slept like a baby at the Ritz.
I found the staff to be very friendly and accommodating. Although we were only there for a few days, they catered to our every need, and always made you feel welcome and appreciated. 
Like all top hotels, everything was pricey. Breakfast for two ran us about $75, and even things like on-demand movies were fairly expensive. Still, it wasn't *so* expensive that you felt ripped off. 
The parking is all valet, which I sometimes find troubling as I drive an exotic car that I always prefer to park myself. Still, there were no issues, and the valet service was prompt and efficient. I suppose this is the norm for big-city hotels - just a pet-peeve of mine.

title: “Eduardo is fantastic”
text: I often stay at the Hilton Woodland Hills. The Hotel is nice and the service overall is good. Eduardo at the front desk is fantastic. He makes every stay a pleasant "homelike" experience.

title: “Two thumbs up!”
text:
We spent a week in December at the W.S.H. and loved every minute of our stay. The location has been way mentioned in other reviews, in a word just great.
The hotel is well maintained with a charming lobby and our room was indeed a big surprise: we feared a phone booth sized one but ours was more than adequate for two persons, I'd say even largish for NY's standards and very clean. It was also pretty quiet, we didn't need to use earplugs (absolutely essential for a good sleep in other parts of the city, e.g. Theater District). The continental breakfast included was rich and tasty and we could choose to have it buffet-style or served at the table. A very big plus are the desk and lobby staff: very professional and always genuinely nice. We'd definitely recommend this hotel, it's one of the biggest bang for the buck and overall nicest stays we've ever had.

title: “Brilliant hotel and location”
text:
My son and I travelled to San Francisco at the end of June for a 16 night tour of the West Coast of America starting in SF.
Following our arrival by the BART $5.30 each from SF airport we came out of the station and walked across the road to the Renainssance Parc 55.
Checked in by Robert who was lovely, very nice room on the 10 floor good view of the city and bay in the distance.
No complaints what so ever. 
Our only disapointment in SF was not pre-booking tickets to Alcatraz via the internet, and as our stay was only for 2 nights we missed out! It may cost a few more $ but not as much as another trip from the UK!!!! 
We would travel back to SF but only to see Alcatraz, everything else was very nice and just like on TV but we've seen it now!
Oh.....do remember a coat YES IT IS COLD IN SUMMER!!!! about 62 degrees and very windy!

title: “Great Location But Some Problems”
text:
This hotel is in a wonderful location on the Upper West Side. The UPW is a quiet reprieve from the hectic pace of downtown Manhattan. And the best thing? You're a half block from the underground metro, which means you can be downtown in ten minutes! What could be better? Well, there's more. Also half a block away is Central Park. You're across the street from the Natural History Museum. A Starbucks is two minutes away. And lots of shopping and restaurants nearby. So location is definitely a 'plus'. 
Other plus's:
- comfy beds
- nice breakfast (but pricy)
- lovely tile in the bathroom
On the negative side:
- some VERY bad front desk staff... practically the worst I've ever seen... I notice other reviewers have commented on this so I won't say more
- found a cockroach in the room one day. Apparently this is almost unavoidable in NYC, and even the best hotels have 'em. But still, it wasn't pleasant.
- elevators extremely slow
Overall, I'd return to this hotel for the location. It's not for everyone, because it's out of the 'main action', but we loved it!

title: “Good location, OK rooms”
text:
Pricelined for a good deal around the holidays. Place was sold out too. Asked for a king, all they had was 2 twins non smoking. Went for the king smoking. Acutally not bad at all. I guess not too many people smoke anymore. No discounts/extras/general acknowledgement for the inconvinience though. 
Location is right off of Times Square, so good for touristy stuff. The whole place looks fairly dated. Would have been edgy and trendy...in the mid 1980's. Room was OK. Large enough and quite good by NYC standards. Bed was nothing special, nor was bathroom. Adequate, clean, but not stunning or new. Definately needed a makeover decoration wise. I have stayed at the other Millenium property by the UN and that is MUCH nicer. More updated rooms, they have a pool, and quieter neighborhood. 
For a priceline deal I was happy. If I had paid rack rates, I would have been disappointed. For the price, I would expect a Westin type experience. Good decor, outstanding bed, good service. Note this is not a Fairmont experience, but neither is the price. This is really more of a Marriot/Radisson type of place. Very adequate. Clean. But not stunning.

title: “Maintained Older facility”
text:
While an older facility it has been fairly well kept up. The hair dryer in my room was broken an smoked when turned on, clearly a fire hazard if a child were to try and use it.
I reported this to the desk upon check-out and noted to them that a replacement was 
needed not a fix.
I was charged for the safe in the room without ever using it. I noted upon check out and
the charge, I think, was removed. Although they could not give me corrected statement.
But it should never have been on the bill in the first place.

title: “Fun and Exotic!!!!!”
text: Me and my wife just compleated a four night stay..and the longer we stayed the more we enjoyed this Grand Old Hotel..the Decor and Ambiance of this Hotel just Grew on us!! The Location is perfect, just a block or two from the LA subway...we rented a car also and the 12 dollar per day parking rate is the best in the area..we needed an iron..and were astounded by how fast they delivered...meals downstairs were tasty and reasonably priced...our room was over the Beautiful Pool/Cabana area..and the sound of party people treated us every nite..maybe a bit much for some..but we thought it gave our room an exciting feel...overall we would stay again in a heartbeat...Hats Off To "The Fig"!!!

title: “Don't go to this hotel!”
text:
After numerous delays in our cross-country flight, we finally arrived at the hotel at 4am. Despite having a guaranteed reservation with late check-in confirmed, the hotel gave away our room! Because they were fully booked, it took over an hour for them to find a room for us. During this hour, both the front desk manager and the manager on duty were extremely rude to us and blamed us for them giving away our room (because we didn't call them from the plane). And, yes, they charged us a "no show" fee for the night.
The cleanliness of this hotel was not up to Hyatt standards (including lots of hair left in the bathroom/bathtub). 
We stay at many hotels in many different cities, and I would NOT recommend this hotel.

title: “Outstanding Value and Location”
text: We always stay at River North. Great location and value compared with anyother lodging in The Loop or North River. A dated fascility but well worth it. If you like the Tavistock in London or other modest hotels in Europe and around the world, this is the place for you. We would rather spend more money on seeing the sights than spending more on a hotel where all we want is a place to sleep. The staff is very professional and friendly. Free parking is a great deal and the hotel is walking distance to most major sites. On balance, excellent.

title: “Great, quiet hotel - perfect for teens”
text:
My daughter, son and my daughter's friend are at the Conrad as we speak. I booked two rooms through Expedia, and with a non-refundable package, we got an extraordinary rate.
The hotel is very clean and very serene. The room service has been wonderful, and the concierge services have been excellent. I can barely get my son out of the shower in the morning, they are so big and nice.
Our view is dismal, but our rate was wonderful. I'm sure that there are some great views from more expensive rooms. But we're in Chicago. There's a lot to do OUTSIDE of the room.
We are two blocks from Michigan Ave. and have several nice restaurants in walking distance.
The attached NorthBridge mall is nice for my daughter. I can allow her a little big city freedom with safety.
We saw Wicked and have been to the Art Museum and the Museum of Science and Industry. Awesome.
Great city, great place to enjoy it from.

title: “A home run....”
text: Spouse and I were in Boston to watch Boston Red Sox play. They hit several home runs that night; however, the staff at the Back Bay Hilton managed to hit their own hospitality home runs. From arrival to checkout they could not have been more friendly or helpful. Mario at concierge desk, was indeed a heavy hitter and a star player. Restaurant and lounge staff added to the high score of this two night stay with their good food and quality service. Twelfth floor room cleran and marble bathroom sparkeled. Room A/C controls were a bit confusing to operate but we figured out. Bell staff did their jobs with high degree of personal attention and friendliness. Without question, we would return whether Sox are playing or not.

title: “Great time at the Villas”
text:
We just got back from a weekend at the Villas and everything was fantastic. Great service, beautiful rooms (we had two two-bedroom condos), beautiful grounds. The beds were extremely comfortable and the kitchen was well-stocked for cooking. We also used the gas grills to BBQ. 
We were really impressed with the staff both at the Villas and at the rest of the resort (which includes the Marriott Desert Ridge) across the street. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful, even in the 105 summer temperatures. For pool time we preferred the Marriott/hotel side of the resort (the Villas office will provide you with a wristband to get pool access there). The main hotel has two pools and a lazy river. There are two pools at the Villas but the area is smaller and it feels more crowded. The hotel also has a few restaurants, including a Roy's with patio seating and happy hour from 4 to 6pm. Although we spent a lot of time on the hotel side of this resort, I always prefer the condos for kicking back, relaxing and for eating in when we want to.
We'll definitely go back.

title: “excellent hotel”
text: My wife and I and 3 friends stayed for 4 nights prior to picking up a cruise to Alaska. We journeyed from the UK so we had a long flight. We were extremely satisfied with all aspects of our visit and just wished that we could have stayed longer at the Hilton. The hotel is very central for Union Square which had entertainment at the weekend. The rooms were spotless and all of the staff were courteous including the security staff who were visible but who also gave reasurance as sometimes in San Francisco the beggars can make you feel uneasy. We will be back as we received excellent value for money.

title: “New York Minute!”
text: Super Chic!...This is NYC!...All courteous & helpful...Very trendy bar...WOW rooms a bit on the small side but, very comfortable with everything that you would need...Aveda products used...Economical rates...Walking distance to EVERYTHING!

title: “Awesome”
text: We stayed there for A three day weekend Of hot in the sun all day playing at the Ohio stingray softball college showcase tourney,,,, the staff was awesome very nice , room was clean and had an awesome set up,,, oh and the bed was so comfy, & wide, if I could have packed it up I would have!! The free washer was so nice :)) for our uniforms'!!

title: “Good Value”
text: The building it self is old and the furniture is showing it's age but it appears to be clean and maintained. Staff was friendly and they do offer a great shuttle service to old town, sea world and airport. If you are planning to hang around at the hotel, this isn't the place for you. This is not a destination resort hotel. If you are using this as a home base for your SD vacation, this clean comfortable quiet motel can be had at very reasonable rate. Lot's of places to eat near by and good location for all activities. I recommend this place for value oriented travelers. (not cheap travelers, there is a difference)

title: “San Francisco's Best”
text: With it's close proximity to Union Square (less than a block), the Hotel Rex is the perfect spot for a San Francisco shopping trip. The staff is superb and service couldn't be better. Free wine is served each evening in the Library which includes a full-service bar. The best part is sipping a beverage on Friday nights in the Library, while listening to live music and having a bite to eat from Cafe Andree, the restaurant adjoining the Hotel Rex. It's San Francisco's best.

title: “Great location”
text:
I stayed here with a friend while she attended a work conference. The lobby has free internet access, but if you want it in your room, you'll have to shell out some dollars. Fortunately, the lobby has a comfortable seating area, a bar, and a restaurant.
The location is excellent since it's within a short walking distance of the Lake Shore Path, Navy Pier, shopping on the Magnificent Mile, and lots of restaurants.
The room itself was clean and comfortable with lots of extra pillows on each of the beds. I would have liked some extra shampoo and conditioner in the room, but overall, everything was to our liking.

title: “Quick Trip but Great Service”
text:
I had a one night stay in Detroit and enjoyed my short time at the Westin Book Cadillac. I was greeted with excellent professional customer service at the front door, the front desk and with the housekeeping staff. The room was great and bed was awesome. 
As I was waiting for directions, a disabled man approached the bellman (wish I had gotten his name). He was extremely polite, kind and courteous to this man who I am sure others have mistreated. The man was asking about a job at the hotel. He was treated with dignity as we all should be. It was so good to see this happen. KUDOS to the staff and this particular employee who knows that is good to respect others -- never know who is watching and will be writing.

title: “I HEART HUDSON”
text:
Me and my boyfriend's (20-somethings) first time in NYC and we decided to do it in style and stay at the Hudon Hotel on West 58th. 
Its a great location, right beside Columbus Circle and just on the South West corner of Central Park (where all the buggies line up to offer you a ride). 
The Hotel is essentially a nightclub. There were people standing outside (smokers) as we rocked up in our cab on the first evening and as we went up the illuminated yellow escalotors into the lobby, house music pumped throughout. Very fun atmosphere and fabulous music!. 
The lobby is a glorified conservatory - there is ivy covering the ceiling and the reception desk runs along the back wall. The staff were very friendly (although had to wait about 40 mins for our luggage to be brought up to our room once we had checked in). 
Be warned! Everything is very dim-lit in this place! (a common theme in NY it seems). Our room was on the top floor. We had a deluxe room (basically 2 double beds and a bathroom), Do not expect to have much space, we paid top dollar to have this room as we had heard that the other rooms in this hotel (and everywhere else in NYC are teeny tiny). It was definately worth spending that bit extra. Lovely soft linen, comfortable beds, lots of mirrors but so so so dark. The bathroom was basic. It was jazzed up by the modern sink but the shower was aged and needed a re-vamp. But the water pressure was good and it was clean and thats what counts. 
We could hear quite alot of noise from the room next door at night. People who had obviously spent their evening in the bar downstairs and had come up to carry on their drinking. Not great but it was ok. 
We did wonder why everyhting (even in the corridors) was so dark and we concluded that it was a good mask for the peeling paintwork and pretty drab corridor decor. But the rest of the hotel and the City make up for the couple of bad points this palce has.
We didnt drink grab a drink at the bar as there were so many other places we wanted to hit in Manhattan, but it looked great and was heaving on Friday and Saturday night. Great music also!
The terrace bar looked very lovely but was just thatt little bit too cold to sit out while we were there. 
The Hudson was a great place to stay. It is very cool and had alot to offer. Very New York. We would definately stay there again.

title: “Truly amazing!”
text:
I took my 13 year old daughter to San Diego for the weekend to celebrate her birthday, and spent 2 wonderful nights here.
I had read previous good reviews, but my main motivation in staying here was the closeness to the zoo...NOT the good reviews.
From the moment we stepped into the lobby, I was in awe...it looked like someone's living room...not a cold, hotel front desk. We were welcomed by Bobby, who made us feel like relatives. He took us to our room, "Victoria's Secret", and it was like spending the night at grama's house. It was cozy and comfortable, and did NOT in any way, shape or form look ANYTHING like a hotel room. I have never before slept soundly in a hotel, but I tell ya...I slept like a baby here.
In the morning, the newspaper was slid under our door. We called down for breakfast, and it was delivered to our room within 10 minutes. There was so much food that we put some away in the fridge to snack on later. We were given melon, apples, oranges, warm cinnamon rolls, mini muffins, croissants with butter and jam, cereal and orange juice.
The zoo and Balboa Park were a mere 5 minute walk away. We grabbed a burger at the zoo at closing and brought it back to the Inn where we sat in the courtyard and ate. Other guests were there, and again it was like hanging out with family...sipping wine and talking about our adventures. The staff is so friendly and helpful and accommodating, that you really hate to leave.
I may have chosen the Balboa Park Inn because of the zoo, but I will stay there again because we love it.

title: “good service hit and miss”
text: We went there for our fist anniversary, and had a huge mixup with a bottle of champagne I ordered ahead of time for my husband. After waiting for 2 hours, and calling the concierge several times, the champagne arrived. They said it was on the house, and sorry for the trouble, but still charged us for it (on our credit card). Otherwise, it was fun to lounge with the beautiful people, but you got sick of it after awhile because you needed a whole face of makeup on just to go to the lobby. LOVED the room. LOVED the bed. Very feng shui oriented, very comfotable and comforting. GREAT location too!

title: “Nice Hotel, Close to Transit”
text: My husband and I recently spent three nights at the Renaissance Chicago O'Hare Suites Hotel due to our daughter marching with the band in the St. Patrick's Day parade. We booked our package which included the room through the school. We were picked up at the airport by the complimentary shuttle and taken back to the hotel. Check in was very easy and the staff were super nice. One of the best features of this hotel is it's close proximity to the train station, which makes traveling to the city very convenient. The cons of this hotel was the fact that the cleaning was a little lacking. It was not vacuum very well before our arrival or during our stay. The bathroom could use updating, as the tub's grout was black in some places. Overall a decent stay.

title: “Security Problem, No help from staff”
text: My room door was left wide open and curtains were also pulled open where anyone could see into the room. I came in after working all day to a door that was propped open and curtains were wide open. Hotel staff said they did not have a manager on duty and also did not have any security on duty until midnight. Being an elderly woman, this was very disturbing. I had left a medicine bag with my daily pills in the room and that bag had been gone though. This I know because it was not in the same manner in which I had left it when I left for the day. I did call the Columbus police and discussed the problem. They informed me that I was in an area where they had alot of drug problems including cars being broke into and cars being stole. Due to the situation, I left the next morning. I was scheduled to stay one more day.

title: “How suite it is!”
text:
No complaints about this hotel. Since I used this website to chose my hotel in NY, I felt like I should leave some advise for others also. We found this hotel to perfect for us. We had a 2 room suite, one room had 2 double beds and the other was a living room/kitchenette area, the sofa pulled out into a bed so this was idea for us traveling with 2 teenagers. The suite was clean but a little drab in color. The hotel staff was very friendly and helpful and Alex the bartender was fun to chat with. Drinks and food are very pricey here but it is that way all over NY. The location is right in the middle of Times Square and easy to get anywhere. There is a discount ticket shop right across the street for Broadway tickets. There is also a McDonalds next door and good breakfast buffet just across the street ($5.00 all you can eat)! 
Shopping is everywhere and the NY deli's are a great place to eat. The hotel security made you feel very safe. You had to show your room key to get into the elevator that took you up 3 floors to the lobby.I know that we would not hesitate to stay here again. And oh yeah, the hotel gives you a welcome cookie at check in that is warm and to die for!!

title: “Good for a budget...”
text: I booked this hotel mainly because of the price and location. It was VERY cheap and I found it to be within reasonable walking distance of everything I wanted to do (Cloud Gate, Magnificent Mile, etc.) You certainly get what you pay for. It's an extremely outdated place. The room was small...there were maybe 3 inches of space between the wall and the bed on all sides of the room except the small area in front of the bathroom. Everything in the room was clearly very old..the carpet, the bedding, the heater....easily from the 60s or 70s. But I didn't go to Chicago to stay in a hotel...I just needed somewhere to sleep and it served that purpose. It was at least clean. If you're someone who is claustrophobic, needs amenities, or cannot handle walking several miles, I would suggest an upgrade. Otherwise, it's decent for the price.

title: “Would definitely stay here again!”
text: Stanley, the doorman at the Executive, was awesome & gave us the best recommendations for a great trip! The rooms were small & cozy & the hotel as a whole had tons of character. It took ten minutes or less to walk anywhere!

title: “Fantastic Elvis Experience”
text: Spent a week here earlier this month and could not have had a better experience. As Elvis fans it was perfect, everything we were looking for. The hotel is dated and the bar/restaurant facilities basic but this is more than made up for in the brilliant friendly, intimate atmosphere, which we hope they don't lose in the planned renovation/refurbishment of the hotel and area. The rooms were spacious and clean, the staff all friendly and helpful, the foyer really cute and Elvis just permeates the building. It is a must for all fans. The best thing was the location just 2 minutes walk from the Graceland plaza so we could walk up to the meditation garden each morning, free from 7.30 to 8.30. It's so beautiful and tranquil up there at that time with the sun just coming up behind the house. We went on 2 tours with Mike Freeman (former owner of 1034 Audobon Drive) which were brilliant - ask for his leaflet at the front desk. There were only 4 of us on the first one to Tupelo ($75) and he took us to places we could never have found on our own, he is a wealth of information and we found it very moving and interesting. Also did a half day tour of Memphis with him which again was a fascinating insight into the private Elvis in his home town, only 3 of us on this one. I cannot recommend him highly enough. He will adapt your tour to see whatever you ask. There is a shuttle bus to all the main attractions in Memphis so you don't need to spend anything on public transport, which is good as you could go bankrupt on the unbelievable selection of Elvis souvenirs! We especially loved the 6' screen in the restaurant of the hotel which shows Elvis movies from 3pm to 11pm but wished they showed more variety, after all there's plenty to choose from. If Elvis is your main reason for being here then Heartbreak Hotel is a must!

title: “Good hotel with Great Staff but in a less than desirable location”
text: A suitable hotel in a poor part of town. There are three times as many rooms as there are parking spaces so arrive early!. Parking is $12 per night and if you miss out one of the 20-odd spots, you're on the street. The view out our window was of the lovely Juvenile Justice Center which provided some good people watching (in conjunction with the "takeout" shop across the street.) There was also a lot of street noise at night (from both trucks and sirens which seems like a common occurrence in Baltimore.) The hotel itself is in an old bank, leading to an impressive lobby area. The staff was friendly and very helpful and the room was spacious and clean. The pillows were really nice as well, a mix of firm and soft, which is hard to find in this type hotel. So all in all, its a good hotel, affordable, less than 10 minutes from Johns Hopkins, with a shuttle that runs to and from, but I wouldn't stay here again unless I were visiting the hospital again (which hopefully doesn't happen.)

title: “The Best Experience”
text:
After traveling to Mary Kay Seminar for 25 years this was the most relaxing trip. I hestiated booking at the hotel because of going back and forth to the convention center. The shuttle service was so convient for us. We didn't have long lines to wait. Also, the drivers were so professional and couteous. We loved all the extra amenties the hotel provided for us that actually helped us to reduce our expenses.
We definitely plan to stay mnext year.

title: “great little hotel!”
text: This is a great hotel overall, and at the rate I got on the internet ($159), quite a bargain. Great service, convenient location, good restaurant on site, and helpful staff. My room was a good size, with a huge bathroom and very comfortable bed. The free wireless internet throughout the hotel was a nice perk. I was able to walk almost everywhere I went, though it's also convenient to buses, which are free in the downtown business area. I'd recommend this place without hesitation.

title: “FANTASTIC!! Highly Recommended!”
text:
This was my 8th time staying in manhattan in the last 4 years.
We had booked a twin room but when we arrived we were told it was very small and would we like a bigger room - AT NO EXTRA COST!!!!
We were given a huge double room.
I had read reviews about dirty bathrooms, rude staff etc and was very nervous about this hotel.
But I can categorically say it is without doubt the best hotel I have stayed in in NY.
This includes, The Howard johnson, the Penn, The Skyline, Milford Plaza - none of them come close.
The place is spotless, staff are excellent, rates are superb, the Cafe edison does a mean milkshake and burger! The location is perfect - one side is Times Square, the othe side is Restaurant Row.
I can't think of anything bad to say!!!! Give it a try - you'll be amazed!

title: “Little gem in the Chelsea area”
text:
We stayed at Chelsea Lodge back in Oct/Nov 2009. We had a brilliant stay, staff made us feel welcome and lend us some essential stuff like iron and hairdryer. 
Even though the rooms are small there is just enough room for 2 people, the shared toilets were not a problem either. 
One tip we ate a few times at Le Grainne cafe which is on 9th Avenue 21st. Lovely little gem and we never had a bad meal. 
Overall i would recommend Chelsea Lodge to people on a budget.

title: “Business trip”
text:
Stayed hear for three nights for a business trip/convention. The hotel is conveniently located in downtown Phoenix and is walking distance to the conference cent and many restaurants. The Sheraton is also one of the tallest buildings so it is easy to see when you are walking around making it difficult to get lost. There is a large restaurant with decent food and a large bar both places were well used by the patrons of the convention. This facility also has a number or meeting rooms.
The actual room was okay. Nothing special. My room had two doubles although I was traveling alone. The room felt a little small. I was in an end room and I think it was designed to be a family suite so that the other room across the corridor would be mom and dads room and mine was the kids room. The window was very small. The very small tv was wall mounted and next 
to the window so you had to close the drapes to watch tv during the day. There was a small wardrobe no closet. There was little storage anywhere a total of two tiny drawers. There was no place to store more than one small roller board. 
Generally this hotel is fine and better than average for a business trip. I spent very little time in the room. But I would not stay in this hotel for family trip. Partly because this place seems to be geared for convention center events.

title: “Great location, walking distance to everything!”
text: My first trip to NYC from April 26 to May 3. Super location within walking distance to almost everything. 2 blocks from Central Park, next door to Carnegie, the Subway, and eating establishments. Clean, safe area. Staff very courteous and accomodating. Our room could have used a bit of refurbish but for the price & just to sleep/shower you can't beat it!

title: “Good central location”
text: This was our first stay at the Sheraton, actually a very convenient location, right off the interstate and near the Galleria. All in all, it's a fine place, ideal for business travelers. They have a business center right in the lobby with free high-speed internet and printers. Rooms are nice but a bit on the small side, so suggest paying no more than $139/night tops. I would strongly recommend asking for a room facing the back side of the hotel as there is considerable freeway noise on the front side.

title: “Great area and value but avoid the extras”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed at the Hilton for 9 nights while staying in New York.
We were really impressed with the room itself, service, and the Chelsea location is within walking distance to plenty of nice restaurants within Chelsea and The Meat Packing District. Considering the hotel was the one of the cheapest when we were searching, overall we were very happy with it and would definitely recommend it. The Rooftop bar also offers great views of the skyline.
The only slight gripes I had was that paying extra for a high floor was probably not really worth it as the view was nothing special (although for $150 in total I guess it only works out to $20 a night or so), and the wifi at $15 dollars a day is pretty extortionate.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Very nice hotel. Minutes from downtown. Very clean and very nice staff. Breakfast staffed very friendly and used first names to talk with us. Would stay again, definitely.

title: “Good location, good Hotel”
text: The only down side was the fire engine siren every night, we were on the 17th floor but could still hear it. The rooms were very clean and spacious. The location was for us excellent, right across the road from Madison Square Garden. If you want to go to church while you are there you must visit St. Francis Church just along the road about 2 blocks away.

title: “Only Praise”
text:
My husband, myself and our 2 children aged 14 and 19 stayed here for five days over the New Year and were delighted with the hotel.As previous reviewers have said the location is superb and apart from using the Sightseeing bus to view the outlying areas we were able to walk everywhere else.eg 15 mins to the Rockerfeller centre 25 mins to central park.The lifts were slow and crowded but we only used them th efirst and last day with our luggage so it was no problem. We were there New Years eve and they had employed a bouncer to ensure that only hotel residents entered.I think he was the biggest guy I have ever seen!!
 The staff at the hotel were very helpful and the room was clean and quite spacious.Impressed that the sheets were changed daily.
As suggested we had breakfast at both The Olympic and the French restaurant Pigalle.The latter was more expensive but we loved the food and the ambience and ate there most mornings. Recommend that you arrive before 9.30 as otherwise there is a queue~ although this week is the busiest in the year so it may 
be less crowded from now on.
 Would definately come back and would stay at this hotel again.

title: “Never again.”
text:
Where to start..... Rather than a long story, I'll give you some facts.
Sheets feel like burlap. Unwashed burlap.
Walls so thin I cold hear our neighbors entire conversation.
Airconditioner that made the room either freezing or hot - but not cool.
No extra blankets. (see above comment)
Towels so thin you can almost see through them.
Breakfast VERY limited and limited quantity.
No iron and ironing board. Had to go the front desk for one. The iron was broken.

title: “Oasis in Manhattan”
text: My teenage daughter and I stayed here for 4 nights. We loved every minute of our trip and can't wait until we visit again. The Library Hotel was a perfect place for us to stay. Great location, wonderful staff, delicious breakfasts and relaxing cheese & wine receptions to tide us over between sightseeing and dinner reservations. Our room and bathroom were sparkling clean. The turn-down service was a very nice touch along with the chocolates and weather forecast for the next day. We really enjoyed the ambiance of the Library and even managed to find time to get some reading in. We will return.

title: “A quiet, elegant retreat just steps away from the energy and excitement of times square.”
text:
We haven't been to Midtown Manhatten in ten years so I was hesitant to book a room until my well-traveled daughter suggested Tripadvisor.I zeroed in on the Sofitel quickly because of it's: proximity to the theater district yet not directly on Broadway and number of rooms in the hotel. If a hotel is too large you wait 10 minutes for a crowded elevator ride with conventioneers. If too small like a bed and breakfast the staff almost becomes a member of your family. We were given a room next to the elevator which is almost always a disaster. Not this time.This was the most quiet room my wife and I have ever stayed in. We could tell everywhere in the hotel there was a premium on cleanliness.The staff was extremely well-schooled and helpful at every turn including complimentary umbrellas to shopping tips for my wife. If you are not aware yet, Times Square is pedestrian friendly.We enjoyed the theaters, restaurants and shops until 1:00am each night and then walked less then ten minutes back to cozy room at the Sofitel.
One last thing, the French Toast coated with cornflakes and drizzed with caramel and maple syrup are out this world! Dr. M. in Naples, FL

title: “quite satisfied”
text: We stayed here based on other's reviews from Expedia and TripAdvisor. The overall stay was a very pleasant one. The room was neat and clean with the small exception of a corner in the shower that was a little moldy and needed some bleach. The rest of the room was great. I would definately tell others to go out for coffee or try the coffee with their breakfast in the lobby. The in room coffee maker took FOREVER and the coffee its self wasn't very good. It's quite a drive from Down Town San Antonio. As for Six Flags and Sea World, we didn't go. The positive is, you can get places pretty quickly with the interstate. There are lots of fast food places just down the road from the hotel, including Subway, Wendy's, Taco Bell, KFC, and Denny's. There's also a really nice gas station called Tiger Mart. They have lots of beverage and breakfast choices. Overall, I would definately recommend this place to anyone.

title: “I was disappointed...didn't feel like a JW”
text:
Stayed at the JW Marriott for 3 nights on a business trip...this hotel was higly rated so I was really disappointed on the whole, including lobby (very unimpressive) quality of the room furnishings, bath, you name it, other than the bed which was very comfortable with good sheets and the flat screen TV which was a good touch. 
It took several tries to get a room with a decent view (I was offered two on a lower level looking out at a roof) and I must say 'Lee' could not have been more helpful in this effort, but I was later told by room service that the hotel was slow and only at 50% capacity, so I'm not sure why this should have been so difficult! I requested an upgrade (more than willing to pay for it) but was told that none were available for my 3 night stay. Asked for a refrigerator for the refrigerator space and was told there weren't any available....you get the idea.
The room itself was adequate, but the furnishings were tired, small and beat looking, and the air conditioning / heater clanked and rattled, if you banged it a few times it stopped. The bath is teeny tiny postage size and cheap, but the towels were good. I'm not certain why but I could hear the elevators all night, my room was no where near this area but they are either pretty loud or there is no insulation in the building as you could hear them move through the shaft and stop at floors. 
Went to the health club which was a nice surprise, large with a good deal of well maintained equipment but the outside pool was a disgrace, tattered louge covers, dirty small pool, no attendents to be found in either pool or exercise area.
The location is about the best thing this hotel has going for it, across from a mega-mall and as a big shopper I can appreciate it's presence, also a lot of good restaurants in the mall and surrounding area.
All in all I'm sorry to say it wasn't much of a JW experience, and I've stayed at Marriotts (minus the JW) that have been nicer....think it's time to adjust the rating system...

title: “Loved it! ”
text: We just got back form a weekend trip to SF and stayed at the Four Seasons Hotel on Market Street. We loved everything about it. Our two bedroom suite was spacious, very clean, and comfortable. What a treat it was to sleep in the heavenly beds after a full days sight seeing and shopping. The gym is amazing if you like to work out. The staff was VERY kind and smiling all the time. The location is perfect for shipping and a block away form Union Square. A big THANK YOU to Jane our concierge for making great suggestions and reservations for dinner and a fabulous show. Don't miss seeing "Beach Blanket Babylon" if you ever go to SF.

title: “High quality historic hotel”
text:
I stayed here for a conference in September 2012. Because of the conference rate, I was able to get a historic train car room. This was a really fun experience. Although the room is narrow and maybe not as spacious as some people are used to, I thought it was still well-designed and made good use of space. The decor was in keeping with the 1920s period, but the room had all the expected amenities. It might be a little difficult to get in and out if you have limited mobility, since you have to climb the train car stairs, but most people will be fine. Trains still run under the building, so it was sort of a strange experience to be awoken at night by a shaking/rumbling. It wasn't scary, though, and when I realized what was going on, it actually added to the experience. The train cars are in a corridor that people walk through frequently, but I didn't find that to be loud or disturbing. Unfortunately, I don't think I would have sprung for the train car if not for the special discounted rate. I think it may be a little expensive otherwise. 
I am an architectural historian, so I loved the reuse of an historic building and just being able to explore the different gorgeous areas of the hotel. The hotel restaurant was fine, basically your standard American fare. The hotel is conveniently located 3-4 blocks from the main downtown area full of restaurants. The staff was friendly and the room and hotel were kept neat and clean.
I give the Crowne Plaza 4 out of 5 stars because it is a well-run, clean, unique mid- to higher end hotel.

title: “Exceeded Expectations”
text: We stayed in a double room which had a fantastic view of the bay! The room was very clean, with down pillows and comforters. We stayed four nights and each day housekeeping did a marvelous job. There were never any problems with noise, faulty elevators, climate control, or any other problems travelers often encounter. There was a coffee maker, iron and ironing board, and blowdryer in the room. The only thing we could have wished for was a small fridge, as there were several places on-site where we could buy beverages and keep them in our room. The staff were very courteous, and helpful if you asked them directly for help or information. There are three convenient places on-site where you can get simple food, or have a nice meal. We did not enjoy the deli as much as we had hoped,(but you could buy any beverage you wanted - like a small convenience store) but the pub and restuarant in the main building was outstanding.

title: “Great hotel in a convenient area of Chicago”
text: I was a little nervous about booking this hotel based on other reviews and because I used credit card points to redeem, but was very pleased with this hotel! Great location opposite Grant Park, beautiful and clean lobby, the room was fine - nothing flash but very clean and comfortable, and just a short number 3 bus ride to the Magnificent Mile. Was very easy to get around with this as our base, we actually booked a hop-on hop-off tour and the pickup point was right outside our hotel...couldn't have been more perfect! I'm a very light sleeper and was a little concerned that it would be noisy but requested a quiet room (was given 10th floor) and with some ear plugs I slept like a baby. Really enjoyed our stay at the Essex Inn and if I ever return to Chicago I will absolutely stay here again!

title: “Nice hotel,Great location. Pity about the small details”
text:
This hotel is ideally situated for Times Square, Broadway and many other iconic NY sights. The rooms are excellent and the beds are very comfortable. However, I would take issue with certain things. 
1. Basic services such as replenishing shower gel and shampoo were random. Often not done
2. Same applied to the coffee sachets. There were two people in my room (my wife and I) so providing one sachet is insufficient.
3. Supposed to provide fresh drinking water daily. Usually didn't happen.
4. Our room was supposed to have free mac internet access, When I complained that it wasn't working, I was put through to a help desk and an assistant who didn't have good English. She was unable to help me, and in any event, I don't think I should be sorting out the hotel's IT problems. Next morning when I asked again about this problem, I was told to contact the help desk!!! I demanded that the hotel sort the problem out and eventually all was well. 
All these things are minor in themselves, but add up to constant irritation. It's all very well ringing reception to send up a coffee sachet or a bottle of water, but one shouldn't have to in a well run hotel. I will stay here again, but I will be very alert to the faults.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: My husband and myself stayed at the Tuscan Inn 12/8-10. We absolutly loved the hotel and would stay again. Comfortable bed, staff was excellent....great get a way!!!

title: “Wow! All the best of everything!”
text: This was one of the nicest hotels I have stayed in! Everything is brand new and clean. Helpful staff and every amenity you could ever want in a hotel. Very cool bathroom and super comfortable beds. Windows are like 12 feet and take up the whole wall for excellent views! The only negative for me was the $28 self-parking fee.

title: “Lovely room, great location.”
text:
Firstly I was supposed to stay at the Dakota, 2 doors along! - I had booked through HostelWorld.com. When I arrived I was informed that I had been moved to the Fitzgerald.
The guy on reception was incredibly laid back - but that wasn't a problem. It helped actually. To be fair I think I came off better, as the building was lovely, it had a slightly 'old fashioned' feel to it and had a great welcoming and warm feel to it. The Dakota looked far less welcoming!
The room wasn't massive, but it had a great large double bed, that dominated the room. It was very comfy as well.
Bathroom [en suite] was lovely and clean with very hot water!
the hotel is located a few blocks up from Union Square, so there aren't any complaints with the location!
I would absolutely stay there again and have already recommended the Fitzgerald!!!!

title: “The 5 Star Red Roof”
text: If you want to stay downtown by the convention center in Columbus Ohio and you value price for accomondation this is where you want to stay. The manager Ken Schraudner is focused on making your stay enjoyable and trouble free in nice well maintained rooms. During my stay I interacted with the following desk staff: Haley, James, JJ, Madalyn, Alecs and Tom who with a smile and positive attitude made my check-in and check-out seamless and provided suggestions with coupons for taking advantage of the local entertainment and restaurants in the immediate area. Tom shuttled me to and from the airport. Comment cards are left in the room to help evaluate the service performed and Heather and Tarah kept the room spotless when I returned. Whenever I go to Columbus and work downtown this is the place of choice; a 2-3 minute walk to Nationwide or the Convention Center. Only issue is the Wi-Fi is not fabulous in all rooms.

title: “Fantastic Hotel...boring city”
text: The Hyatt property was in a new renovated area of town. Loved the location. FREE parking. The hotel staff was very nice. Property was the BEST place to view the RED WHITE AND BOOM fireworks. We were on the 6th floor and our room faced the fireworks display. We were able to watch from the comfy bed. It was great! Breakfast is a bit "stuffy". Don't expect a waffle or pancake bar...more like egg mcmuffin..and no bacon or sausage. Those of us from the south felt a bit cheated in the breakfast area. The rooms are huge. This place was perfect for our family of 3 for a long stay during a volleyball tournament. Too bad Columbus is such a dud of a place to visit. UGHHHH! Ohio State was only OK. And the football stadium didn't produce an ahhhh's. Oh well. The mascot is a buckeye. Probably won't ever go back to Columbus but I would recommend this hotel for long stays.

title: “Very comfortable, marvelous location”
text:
I occupied a room at the Berkshire Place from April 24 thru May 3. The room was very nice, any problem was quickly solved. The location is absolutely remarkable and the staff, as well, most friendly.
Nevertheless, the hotel should not advertise everyday turndown, as it only provides it if you call downstairs and ask for it, or else to some guests (there was a list with the turndown maid), maybe the ones who belong to the Omni Select Guest or whatever.
I will possibly stay there again, but hope other guests continue to comment on it, to find out whether the renovations are being kept up.

title: “Excellent Stay”
text: Got in on the Travelzoo promotion for this hotel. We are Chicagoans’ and thought it would be fun to play tourist for the weekend; I could not have picked a better hotel. I agree with other reviews that once this hotel completes it renovation it will be the little gem off of the Mag Mile. I have never met a friendlier staff at a hotel. I noticed they ask each patron the purpose of their stay upon check in and then make suggestions accordingly. Our only request, was to get a room on an upper floor with a "view". We arrived before the scheduled check in so Annie (reception) took my cell phone number and called me within and hour with availability. Boy did she deliver! We were upgraded to a Jr. Suite, at no additional charge, on the 25th floor facing south. FYI this building only has windows facing north and south as they are in the middle of an east/west street. Thus your best views will be "in the front" facing south. No restaurant or bar in the building yet, but hardly something to complain about; so many choices within a block. Those who complain about this hotel, even while under construction, are crazy! Good job Affinia and welcome to Chicago.

title: “Our valued goods are stolen from Carter Hotel”
text:
The rooms are dirty and old. The pictures we saw on internet, don't correspondate with the reality.
Despite the information we already got from the forums, we were very disapointed.
Besite this, our goods have been stolen out of our room. With us, two Swedish couples had a break in. The manager, mister Abdullah was really rude to us. He wouldn't talk with us and tried to empty the computer with keyinformation. It was clear that somebody of his staf was responsible for this all. 
When we arrived at the police voor a report, they were laughing when we told them we stayed in Carter Hotel. They asked us how we could pick the worst hotel in New York. They confirmed that it happened frequently that hotel Carter causes trouble.
A warning to all: spend some more money for a more safe hotel. 
If you don't listen to this advice: Take all your valuable goods with you and always lock your suitcases. From the Swedisch people they took clothes!!!! 
Good luck

title: “Awesome Stay”
text:
Great hotel. Service was outstanding. Hotel was at capacity, but the staff handles the number of guests very well. 
The suites are very large and great for those traveling with family. Two TVs in each room. So everyone gets to watch what they want. The rooms are also very quiet. Easy to go to sleep early or sleep in late. Cleaning service is also very good.
Hotel breakfast and manager's reception in the evening (complementary drinks and snacks) where a big hit for kids and adults alike. 
We took the Metro from Regan airport to/from the hotel and used the Metro to tour the city. No need to rent a car. Hotel is 4 blocks from either the Dupont Circle or Foggy Bottom stops. 
Great restaurants within walking distance in the Dupont Circle area. All in all you really couldn't ask for more. You can't go wrong staying at this hotel.

title: “Incredibly tired of starting hotel experiences on a good note and them ending on sour notes.”
text:
I travel ALOT. Meaning I am in hotels a minimum of 9 - 10 days a month, sometimes 20 days a month. I probably spend more a month on hotel cost than I do on my mortgage. So with this in mind, I am a consumer who understands the workings of a good hotel. I know the industry standards so to speak and what to expect.
I knew that the room would be small. It's a "boutique" style hotel, small is ""standard" in NYC. The room was a little bigger than I had expected, but still small. The bathroom was larger than I expected, I've been in ones that you actually had to out your knees into the shower stall to use it, so this one was pleasantly accommodating for the price.
The bed and pillows were actually incredibly comfortable and very comfortable to sleep in. 
I was disappointed that there was no desk, no chair, and no outlets to be used near the bed. In this day of cell phones an outlet near the bed is a mandatory item.
The was no outlet near the sink, making doing hair an obstacle, as it was several feet away from the mirror. There was no bathmat, so when you got out you had to be very careful to not slip on the floor with wet feet.
No washcloths. No mini bat. No ice bucket. And the IPods dock alarm clock could not be set.
All of these things I could deal with for the price point.
BUT, I have been aching to try this hotel, as I fell in love with the online photos of a beautiful lobby, and bar/ lounge area.
The lobby is under construction and has no appeal what so ever, although I will give them points for the lemon ice water available. 
The lounge area was ok. I loved the bar area. It was what I had hoped for and my server was gracious and knowledgeable not only of drinks but in suggestions.
Everything was acceptable enough for me that I extended my stay one night. To do so they had me check out and check back in, although this was odd as I had to do it online. Originally I made my reservations online with a debit card, when I checked out I paid with cash and was told the room charges and incidental charges - which I am clueless as to why they do this since they have no mini bar, no hotel robes.... I was told over the phone the incidental hold would be 50 dollars, when I got there they put a 75 dollar hold on my card.
So I have paid cash for my first nights stay so I have been told specifically that the hold on my credit card of 238 dollars would be immediately released. Great.
So I check in for my second night stay and pay for the stay upfront with cash, including the incidental charge, which will be returned to me upon check out. No big deal.
This hotel is not really convenient to my business in the city as I have an industry function to attend down on Varrick Street, which is quite a hike, even by cab or subway, but at the price point, it is acceptable, even though the lobby is under construction, which they do not tell you prior to booking, and seems a little deceiving....
In other words, the only reason I booked here was because this was a hotel I wanted to check out because of it's lobby and the library bar, and with the price, I thought now was the time to do so. It hasn't been a wonderful or notable venture, but nothing so far that would make me avoid it in the future. Hotel management, take note to that, as of that point, you could have been assured of possible repeat business with a very frequent traveler, that is mire valuable in any business than anything else.... as to constantly try to get new customers through advertising dollars becomes very expensive, when all you have to do is maintain a certain standard once you have a guest to get them to come back.....
Before I check out I get onto my IPad and log in to my bank account and notice that my funds have not yet been released???? Hmmmm..... 
When I get to the front desk to check out I inquire as to why the hold is still on my bank account, and am told, that the hold was immediately taken off the moment I originally checked out, 24 hours prior, and that it must be my bank..... which I know is untrue. I travel too much and always use the same debit card for my travels, and have seen in nearly 98% of the hotels that I have stayed at, that the moment I check out, the hold is released, and the money back available for my use within an hour. 
Once I leave, I call my bank to get the REAL facts, I have been dealing with them for years, I have a good relationship with them, while this is my first dealings with this hotel, and my bank, which is the one I use for all of my travel bookings, informs me that the hotel has never contacted them AT ALL TO RELEASE MY FUNDS, AND THAT THEY HAVE ACTUALLY PUT A HOLD ON MY MONEY FOR 5, YES, FIVE DAYS!
I had specifically inquired when I checked out the first day and opted to pay them with cash if the release would be done immediately, I was assured that the minute they checked me out from my original reservation that it would be done that moment. When I checked out the second day I again inquired and was again assured that it happened immediately when I had checked out the day before.
They never released the hold, my bank was NEVER contacted at all, except to put a hold for 5 business days. This is unacceptable on every level. If they had been honest with me from the start I would have simply left the room on my debit card and not paid them in cash, so now I am out 238 dollars until they decide to honor their contractually legal obligation, which was to release the hold immediately upon my check out from my original reservation.
They falsely advertise their hotel in the depiction of the hotels photos, if it's under construction this should be made aware to the guest, as it is the ONLY reason I wanted at stay at this hotel, as there are hundreds of other hotels in this city to try, and they have in an essence stolen my money. 
And they can try to state that this is industry standard, but I travel enough to know better. They can try to blame my bank, but I have been using my bank for years, and have never had any issues with them releasing my funds, EVER, and the fact remains, I was told specifically that they released the hold and my bank has been very clear to me that they were NEVER contacted by the hotel to release my funds, only to hold them and this has caused me great inconvenience, and if I had been told the truth from the start, I would have opted to have kept the charge on my debit card and not paid them with cash..... thank God that I had enough money on me to be able to afford to pay for my travel arrangements to get home. God forbid another traveler goes through this and then finds themselves stuck on the streets of NYC trying to get home.

title: “Very Dissappointed!”
text: We flew in from out of town and got to the hotel right at check in. We got to our room and put all our stuff away and left to make a wedding on time. We got back late that night to find that bathroom door makes a super loud screaching noise while trying to close it. This wasn't very convenient for our guests that came to our room. We tried using their audio block that goes through the tv to entertain our friends and found it wasn't working. Even the remote control for the TV wasn't even working! I had to physically get up and turn the tv channels myself. I decided I wasn't going to complain since this was our first vacation away from our 5 month old son. That came to a complete halt when early in the morning we heard dogs barking. The dogs barked every half hour. Just enough to fall back asleep and to be woken up again by high pitched dog barks. We complained to the front desk but they said that we were put on the dog floor. We didn't have a dog! I asked the man, why didn't you let us know you were putting us on the dog floor? Who in their right mind puts a wedding party on the dog floor??? The man said it depended on when we checked in. I told him we checked in right at check in. He just starred at me. With all the complaints we had about the room the guy did nothing to remedy the issue. I will never go to this hotel again. I might as well have just flushed my money down the toliet.

title: “Great location for a great price!”
text: My husband, 11 yr old son and I stayed here May 3-7 2011. We had the Deluxe Suite that slept up to five. It was three individual rooms connected by accordian doors. All rooms had their own bathrooms (hot water was touchy, beware, but there was no lack of it!), small closets with irons/ironing board, dresser, tvs, clocks, windows. Room one had a single twin bed, hot pot with tea/coffee, mini-fridge. Room two had a double bed, table/chairs, vanity w/ chair. Room three had two twin beds. The hotel is old and dated but pretty clean, bathrooms spotless. Price was awesome, can't beat $800 for four nights this close to everything. Why spend big bucks on a hotel you are never in? We got up early each day, walked around, came back, took a nap then went out at night to see it all again. D.C. downtown/around the mall/whitehouse/capitol is super safe at night, we saw only maybe 5 homelss/bums the whole time. Cops everywhere in this district/area. We walked everywhere day/night. (You have to go to the memorials at night, totally different experience and a lot fewer tourists!) White house within 4 blocks, the mall within 6. Two Metro stations within three blocks (awesome metro system, once you learn how to read the pillars you can go anywhere fast - we rode from Metro Station to Ronald Reagan Airport on the Blue line for 1.65 each, sure beats a $30 - 30 minute minimum taxi ride!! - by a farecard and add as you need) We didn't waste money on the tour busses, you can see everything by foot and catch Metro if you're wore out. Bathrooms are everywhere on the mall. For eats, Ollies Trolley is AWESOME!! Looking for Chinese? Head to Chinatown's Szechuan House on corner of 6th and H- best Chinese I've ever had, and I've had alot! Ben's Chili Bowl just out side U-Street metro station on the Yellow line is a trip, worth checking out for lunch. Don't bother eating at the Old Post Office Pavilion, food sucks and is over priced! Union Station wasn't all that everyone makes it out to be, overpriced shops, quite a few fast food places, but we saved our $ and ate at local fares like Ollies & Bens would rather use that time to see the monuments anyway. We had a ton of maps, but found that the free one the hotel gives you is the easiest to use. Once you find your bearings, you can go anywhere. (It is tough sometimes when you come out of a metro station, you don't know which way is which, the locals were all nice and willing to help you find your bearings when needed.) The Smith-museums were sort of a bust, tons of screaming kids- I've seen most of it on History Channel or Discovery anyway. Deffinately go to the Holocaust Museum. Get there early, lines are really long, but it is something everyone should experience. I would totally stay at the Hotel Harrington again!!! You wont regret saving that money for other things - like Ollies or the Szechuan House!

title: “Absolute dump”
text:
Stayed at the radisson with four nights, going with high expectations which were soon shattered. Our welcome at the reception was cold. We asked for a smoking room and were given one on the 5th floor. The lift doors opened to what can only be described as walking into a brick wall of ashtray and must smell. My boyfriend (who smokes) was even disgusted by the smell.
Things only seemed to go down hill, our room was tiny, so much so we had no space to even unzip our suitcases, the desk took up most of the room and still contained the previous occupiers confidential paper work! There was no ashtray in the room, I was told one would be sent up straight away but had to ask for one a second time and from house keeping.
The bed was small, the main sheet appeared to be old and was very lumpy, I wouldnt even allow my dog to sleep on such a worn dirty blanket. Our room overlooked a large air con system which was extremely noisy. My boyfriend (who smokes out of open windows only) had to shout over the noise to speak to me when the window was open.
We didn't step foot in the bath tub the full time we were there as it was so disgusting, the bath was peeling with chips and dirt, the shower head was mostly made of rust. We washed out of the sink, which wasn't much better, having an old hair slide stuck and sticking out of the hole amongst the many cracks and marks. The bathroom light would flicker repeatly before coming on, although this was an improvement on the main bedroom light as we didn't have one! Only two dimly lit bedside lamps. 
Flicks of paint decorated every item in the room, have the radisson never heard of dust sheets when decorating?
The decor was old, worn and peeling away.
I called the front desk on arrival to complain and asked for another room to which I was told the hotel was full, despite been asked moments earlier if I would like a smoking or non smoking room.
We were woken up at 5.30am on out first morning to the alarm clock which the the previous occupier had set! We were then woken by the maid banging and knocking in surrounding doors. We had the privilege of hearing the surrounding rooms flush their toilets throughout the night.
Housekeeping was inconsistant throughout our stay, our bedding was never changed only made.
This was my third visit to NYC and worst hotel experience, we will never be staying at the radisson again and will be advising others not to also.
Don't waste your money the Wellington is a much better hotel stay there instead.

title: “Like living in a well furnished apartment!”
text: Great place to stay while visiting a beautiful city. From check-in till the complimentary shuttle dropped us off at the airport, we sincerely enjoyed our stay. Great food for breakfast and dinner with complimentary wine and beer thrown in add to the great value!

title: “Not Worth The Money.”
text:
First off let me say the Hotel is in a woderful spot in the city.There is a subway entrance right out side the door.China town is 3 or 4 blocks south.There isnt much after dark around the Hotel so plan ahead.There is a deli 2 blocks away and a Starbucks that closes early for a starbucks.
-----The Hotel charges $150 a day for incidentals.Plan ahead. I didnt and was shocked when told I had to pay that. I also had all the junk removed from my room so that I couldnt be charged for it..
-----If you use the phone even for local calls you will be charged $1.50.You can talk all you want I guess but you still get charged the intial $1.50..
-----When I stayed weekend of April 22. The Hotel is only Half open.Floor 27th is the highest that availble....Pool not done. Spa not open. SoHI not open.
----- If you goto the Trump site there isnt a picture of the rooms.You would think they would be able to take up to date photos and put them on the site.Theres a reason there isnt actual photos on the Site.
-----Also if you want to use the internet its $14.95 a day.For unsecured wired/wireless connection. This is 2010 everyone uses the internet these days.
----- I feel I was nickled and dimed.
It seems as though if you stay here you are helping train the staff. I know that currently it is availble for a discounted rate. There is a reason..
I had a Supuerior Room. It is small.Had I brought my wife we wouldnt have had any room in the closet for clothes.There were like 6 hangers. I was disapointed and was up graded to a Deluxe. Which ment it was a little bit bigger but still small. In both rooms the Bathroom was the only bright spot. It had a large deep tub next to the window.The shower was a nice.You have 2 choices. There is a wand where the water shoots out and a non adjustable rain head over head.I have stayed in NYC.The room was small. Its only a 5-star hotel if you care about the Taschen books and bench thats worth $1500.
I dont care about any of that.
You dont go to NYC to pend all day in the Room.
+++ The maid service was beyond belif.They come by 2 times a day.They folded my clothes.
++++ Door men were outstanding as well.Always nice,polite and friendly.
++++ The view while looking out the window was nice.I could see Empire State building ,the Brooklin bridge,Another bridge and central park..I will say if you had a room at the top there isnt a better view in the city from a hotel.
++++ The bed was really soft.I slept well on it.
In closing I dont feel right now its a 5-star hotel.It will be in the future.There is no way I would pay the prices that the hotel will ask for in the future.I didnt want to pay the $300 a night even if it was fully open. The rooms are to small. I guess I can say I stayed there when the Celebity Apprentice Final shows.
For the price go stay else where..

title: “Hassle Free for Red Eye Flights”
text: Staying here for one night (actually a morning) was the best decision I made for a non-stop red eye flight from San Francisco to Chicago! All I did was get my luggage and walk, completely within the airport, and I arrived at the hotel's front desk. I checked in, went to my room and flopped! Then refreshed after a few hours of sleep, (and it is very quiet) I checked out and took the El train right into the city. So convenient - you will be glad you did this.

title: “A little disappointed”
text: My husband booked 2 nights here based on the website and the pictures. He was disappointed. The pictures make it look a lot better than it actually is. (he wanted tacky, but fun) I am the big Elvis fan in the family. The room was basic with the only thing worth noting were the Elvis prints on the walls. Breakfast in the am, was nothing to write home about. Flavored creamers for my coffee made my day! None of the staff were cleaning the tables, so many were covered with leftover food. My biggest complaint was the 24 hour Elvis movies. They were fuzzy. I called and asked about this. They sent someone up within 10 mins. He was friendly and came with extra cable. In the end, he said that there wasn't anything he could do. They had everyone wired together and until the hotel fixed it with a better plan, it was going to stay that way. He said that female Elvis fans were gtting fed up with it. LOL! The front desk staff at check-in were very friendly and nice! Check out staff was annoyed, but not rude. If you are coming to Memphis, just to see Graceland (like we did), the hotel was ok. Walking over to see the Meditation Gardens at 7:30 (ended at 8:30 for us, be sure to check) was a plus. There were only 2 other small groups and we managed to work around each other to take pictures without getting in each others' way. Later on the tour, there was no way to take pictures without other people being in them. Finally, I was a bit spooked about the reviews on security. I never felt anything concerns. We went out for dinner by our car, but felt the property was secure. (there is a guard house)

title: “good stay”
text: My family and I stayed at the Hyatt Place near the mall about two weeks ago. The room was nicely decorated and the flat screen tv was great. There were only a few minor things that needed to be fixed such as the mini fridge was not very cold and the bathroom is really small. We stayed two days and received pretty good room service (we ordered pizza which was tasty) and our room was cleaned by hotel staff. The hotel staff were friendly and greeted us by name. My family did go to the pool and found that it was not very sanitary. There were leaves everywhere and there was a group of basketball teams that were staying in the hotel. They sort of crowded the pool area and were a bit noisy--they had won their tournament game so it was understandable. The location of the hotel is great, near restaurants, shopping, fast food places, and pretty much anything that you need. There was a walmart nearby and a walgreens too. I would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to stay near memphis but not in memphis. The area was nicer and better than staying in downtown memphis.

title: “Really nice place!”
text: First off, I must mention this is the only Westin or "W" hotel I have stayed in. I have stayed here twice now, and had great experiences each time. My first stay was in a Deluxe room. It was nice. Everything is very comfortable. I really like the designs of everything in the hotel. You can not go wrong with the Heavenly bed, and even though the "Heavenly Bath" is just a curved shower rod, and two shower heads, it is still really nice. The towels and robes are also really nice. Not what you would find at a competing hotel. This hotel is fairly new, and well taken care of. Second stay was in a "Club Floor Room" and had access to the club lounge. Complimentary drinks and hors devours were nothing to write home about, but still good. Westin Times Sq. is in a great location at 43st./8th Ave. Times sq. subway stop is less than a block away for transportation, and near many many attractions. Overall: Great Location, not too busy at all, reasonable prices, very "comfy", excellent choice. My next reservation will be next month in a Club room. Highly Reccomended!

title: “Night to remember!”
text: My wife and I returned to Manhattan where we were initially engaged, to celebrate our 10th Anniversary. After emailing several locations with no response, Tom and Jhoanna both contacted me and were very helpful. Staying at the Night was an excellent decision. The service and the room decor was amazing. Even though our reservation was short notice and there were no Suites available, the room was just enough for our stay. The two ladies who handled our reservations were extremely helpful, particularily one to mention ( and I can't recall her name) shared some tips about the area and her marriage. I also want to thank the Doorman for his help. Although our stay was short with respect to timeframe, the Night's location made our ability to manuever around the city on foot so much easier. From our first Broadway show, to walking Central Park, Ice skating at Rockefeller Center, and even a trip to the Statue of Liberty, the location was key. Even Ona, the bartender took care of us after our Show on Saturday and we appreciate her time with us. We look forward to visiting again soon and have even discussed starting an Anniversary tradition of seeing a new Broadway show every year.

title: “Wow...”
text: Great customer service! Had a small snafu with my work credit card and they handled it very well. Rooms were amazing, beautiful views of city ( Could see the baseball game!) Love the pool on the upper deck. Was just a great hotel. One of the best I have ever stayed at and I am a HUGE hotel snob.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
For the price tag don't expect anything more than the average Hampton Inn... but LOCATION... that's what makes the difference... walking distance to the heart of Manhattan... Times Square, Rockefeller Center (and its Top of the Rock attraction), Radio City Hall (now showing wonderful, spectacular Cirque du Soleil Zarkana.. highly recommended), 5th Ave and its wonderful shops (window shopping or not...), Broadway... and many more!!! 
There are restaurants, cafes, diners... all prices, all cuisines... Convenience stores, specialty stores... You name it!
What you overpay in the hotel rate you will save on transportation, that's for sure... and valuable time, of course... BUT, for the price you may expect a little more than a Concierge desk in the lobby... The included breakfast is surely a PLUS ....BUT ...will it kill Hampton Inn to extend the breakfast until 11:00am... at least here ... ?? Breakfast was the average Hampton Inn's hot breakfast...nothing out of the ordinary. 
BEDS ARE GREAT... very comfy, so are the pillows. Bathroom shower is very good...massage type, our bathroom sink cabinet was in the need of a renovation...but it served its purpose. Overall, I would certainly recommend this hotel to families with children and teenagers. 
We stayed in NYC for 3 nights and Hampton Inn TSQ North was a good choice overall.

title: “Great Location, Friendly Caring Staff”
text: We stayed here prior to a cruise. We travel extensively and only stay at Hampton Inns, which we find are consistently good. I have to say that this Hampton Inn was the best one we have stayed in with regard to the staff and quality of service. From the moment we stepped in their door we were greeted with warmth and they could not do enough to make your stay a good one. We were also impressed with the breakfast, which was the standard for this chain, but stood out from any of the other Hampton Inns we have used because it was so clean and well supplied. The manager was going from table to table asking if all was okay and then the lady who was taking care of the breakfast area, came and took away our plates etc for us. The location is wonderful, right near the Space Needle and close to transit. We are walkers, so we found it convenient to even walk down to the waterfront and Pikes Market. If you are going on a cruise, they also offer a shuttle service to the port for a nominal fee. We couldn't be more pleased with this hotel. They exemplify what good customer service is all about.

title: “Nice hotel - if you're in the Tower rooms.”
text: Stayed here during our last 2 nights of our Disney/So. Cal trip. Were disappointingly booked in a room in the gross 'motel' looking section - not disclosed anywhere on website; paid a sizable fee to upgrade to a real room in the tower (Regency King corner room), which was worth the $$ for better view etc. Great room service (convenient for late arrival) / bellhop Ryan was so nice/helpful! Employees were all great overall. Buffet breakfast in Red Marlin was good (healthy options). Didn't spend much time in hotel, but pools looked nice w/ waterslides for kids (closed before 6 though - letdown for my kids on one and only night we tried). Room was nice overall (comfy bed, but small bathroom), but I think next time I'd try to stay closer to Coronado in a different type of hotel. Didn't love this format - strange mix of buildings/'motel' rooms with exterior access - (spoiled by Huntington Beach Hyatt - top notch in every manner).

title: “Where's the doorman?”
text:
The Mayfair website shows a picture of a smiling door man greeting you. Ha! No one smiles there and there's no door man.
First the good, extremely comfortable kingsize bed and an a/c unit that worked, our room was actually cold. Both are definite pluses. The room was small and really there was not enough room to open up two suitcases. The bathroom mirror had a huge crack from end to end. It looked like the whole thing was ready to fall off the wall. The shower(no tub) door would only open at one end and that was a struggle. The shower tile looked like it hadn't been cleaned in ages. I put down a towel on the shower floor and left it there the duration of our stay. Almost forgot, the elevator, only one light working and it's filthy. How much effort is it to clean the elevator doors. While waiting for the elevator on the7th floor, we happened to look up the stairs and noticed a tremendous hole in the ceiling. 
It's a good location, good bed, good a/c. The staff seemed to not care if we were staying there or not, they weren't vey friendly.

title: “Overpriced for what we got”
text:
A friend and myself visited San Fran and needed a decent place to stay with good public transport options. The Handlery was perfectly located within easy walking distance of Amtrack, Bart, and cablecar with a very friendly staff. So far so good... BUT; we just booked the first room that popped up on Hotels.com, (Petite) and for $163 we were put in the tinest of rooms imaginable, with only a dbl bed and so little room that the TV was at right angles to the bed. How are you supposed to watch? We are two single, energetic guys, and being stuck in a tiny room completely piled with our belongings wasn't very cool. So to the front desk we go. Very polite, but the pool and excercise room both close at 10pm. What is a guy supposed to do???
