 On the positive side, very clean facilities, great staff and perfect location. Only take my advice and buy a queen room at minimum and get in your excercise early. Cheers!

title: “Great Location near Union Station and the Capitol”
text: Beautiful, quiet small hotel. Great restaurant and bar on site. Much nicer than the local big chain hotels.

title: “Very nice, dependable Dallas hotel.”
text:
As a former Dallas resident, I've had many opportunities to attend functions at the Fairmont and to stay at the hotel. My most recent visit was for a short weekend in the Dallas area. As usual, I was not disappointed. The room was in a quiet corner of the hotel, large, well appointed, and with a very nice bed and bathroom. The staff is pleasant and "on top of things". 
The only thing that keeps this review from being a "5" is the chronic valet parking issue at the hotel. 15 minutes before my departure, I attempted to call the valet desk, but there was no answer. When I arrived at the valet area, I had another 20 minute wait. The lady at the window was very pleasant and apologetic and appeared really hassled; there appeared to be only 3 valets attempting to serve many departing guests - a lot of whom were headed to "Jerry's World" for the Cowboy-Bills noon kickoff. I hope they made it...I arrived at my scheduled stop barely in time.
In spite of that inconvenience, the Fairmont is a really nice hotel and often will have nicely discounted rates. Its downtown location and convenience to Uptown and the AAC are definite pluses. We'd be more that happy to return.

title: “Adequate”
text:
Good, but frantic service by concierge and reception (they were very busy, MJ had just died!).
I had requested a twin room but was shown to a single. They couldn't help, so I had to share a kingsize bed with my 17-yr old daughter, which was OK, but not ideal. Room was fine and quiet. I had also asked for B&B, but there was only a la carte. They did say they would exclude the cost of breakfast from my bill. Overall, not great value-for-money, but it is LA!
The irritating thing about Hilton is you have to pay for everything, e.g. internet access was $10 per day, why?!!! Valet parking was $40 and is essential.
This hotel is well-located for concerts, etc, but not for visiting Hollywood and car travel in LA is awful.
If I was forced to visit LA again, I would consider this hotel, but I really don't want to visit LA again! Go to Santa Barbara instead.

title: “Had a decent stay here”
text:
Stayed here recently. Room was comfortable. They gave us a high floor since the mezzanine level was torn apart and under construction. Good location downtown. 
Only problem we encountered was they have a computer by the front desk with a sign stating it is only to be used for printing airline boarding passes and to use the business center for internet use. (Business center is on mezzanine level which is torn apart) We asked at the front desk where we could find a computer for internet use, and the front desk agent rolled his eyes and said in a VERY snotty tone, " maybe you should have read the sign!" We told him that we did read it - we went and got the sign , brought it back to him and pointed out that the business center was torn apart. We got a " oh - sorry"
Other than a front desk guy having a bad day, it was alright.

title: “Funky hotel in great location, but a touch noisy”
text: We spent 4 nights here on a short vacation. The location was perfect - walking distance to food, drinks, cinemas and shopping. Cool light fixtures and wallpaper, and great quirky furnishings in the lobby. Rather than coffee in the room, they set up a good "help yourself" selection in the lobby every morning. Wi-fi was fast and reliable. Air conditioning was window mounted and pretty noisy when turned on. The room was comfortable, but we didn't sleep very well due to the amount of street noise that came in, whether windows were opened or closed. Now, I'm not a delicate petal - I know cities are noisy, and have stayed in my fair share. Maybe because this was facing a hill, and the second floor was effectively at street level, it was worse? We just put up with it, rather than asking for a different room. In retrospect, I should have been more proactive, but we kept forgetting until the early hour wake-up rolled around again!

title: “Perfect!! Incredibly better than expected!”
text:
My husband and I spent 12 amazing nights at the Distrikt. Since the very first moment you get to the door you feel welcome. Everything is perfect! The room and the bathroom are really clean and smell good. The staff is amazingly friendly: always helpfull, polite and professional. We arrived at the hotel at 10 am and left at 2 pm and we didn't have to pay any extra penny for that. I would definitely come back there and recommend this awesome hotel. If you are still looking for a place to stay in NYC, stop it and make your reservation now!
Martinha - Brazil

title: “quality and originality”
text:
I view it as a good sign when a hotel seems to be popular with international flight attendants, as the Carlyle Suites are. But of course, their likes and dislikes are not mainstream American. So the suites rooms might be small by American standards, which I didn't mind, but perhaps some might. In general, this hotel has class and comfort in a great location. They have renovated an Art Deco period building in Art Deco style; it isn't opulent but it is well done. The suite had everything one might need in the kitchen, including plates and silverware. I had a great night's sleep on the Tempur-pedic mattress. The free wireless worked great. The staff were efficient and friendly. Fast elevator, always available. My room was high enough to have a lovely view from the windows looking west over the Dupont Circle neighborhood.
On the down side, the lobby is small, just two chairs, always filled. Also, be aware that the hotel is a 10-15 minute walk from Dupont Circle station. A pleasant walk on a quiet street past embassies and consulates but still a walk. It seems to be a safe neighborhood.

title: “Celebration of our 38th Anniversary!”
text: The overall ambiance and decor was great, reminding us somewhat of an European hotel. The staff and service was impeccable. They helped make our anniversary a memorable one. I had just returned from a five week business trip to West Africa and it was a great place to re-enter the States and celebrate with my wife.

title: “Great value, great location, no pretense”
text: Just returned from a 5-day stay in New York City, and had a great stay at the Hilton Garden Times Square. First of all, the "pros" of the hotel --- and there are many. The price was outstanding for New York City ($140.00/night can't be beat). The location was outstanding - literally one block west of Broadway along 49th - steps away from Times Square. The room was spacious enough for New York - even a family of four survived in the same room for 5 days! The staff of the hotel was extremely friendly and helpful. We requested extra pillows - no problem at all. We needed help with airline checkin prior to departure - no problem. They willingly gave directions as required and the concierge was very helpful to find restaurants on Christmas Day. The "cons" of the hotel are relatively minor in nature - the heating vent clicked at night so we had to turn it off (OK since the weather was perfect for a December visit). The toilet ran one night and the windows didn't tend to keep the sound out, even though we were on the 6th floor of the hotel. In general, the hotel needs a little bit of a "facelift" - a can of paint, new carpet in the hallway - just a little bit of elbow grease will bring this back to a wonderful place to stay. No need to overstate these negative points though - in general this was a great hotel, a great value and a superb find for Manhattan. I would recommend it to friends who will travel to New York in the future.

title: “Great Location, Terrific Staff, Creative Amenities”
text: My husband and I were quite sick and it was our last night in New York City, looking for a place that was more comfortable than our tiny, only slightly cheaper hotel room right around the corner. It was a significant upgrade, and I was very impressed with everything--the staff was helpful and friendly and even sent up a complimentary bottle of spring water because we had asked about where to buy water. They have fun amenities, like a wide variety of dvds to watch for free, bicycles to use. I think it'd be a great place to stay for families to the young crowd who want a central location. I'd been to the bar here last year and it is really gorgeous as well.The room wasn't huge but they all seem to have great views, very comfortable, nice free toiletries, even fancy toothpaste. A visually stunning place, overall quite welcoming, I would spend the small amount more to stay here.

title: “Hidden Gem in SF, you need to check it out”
text: SF has great places to stay, but normally it is good location, expensive, but it is SF. Well, we found an alternative. The Hotel Monaco is a Kimpton property and one of probably six in SF and truly a European boutique hotel, close to Union Square and very inexpensive, try a junior suite for $230/night. Wonderful staff, they honestly got to know you and made you feel so welcome. Oh, their food is excellent as well. Our friends who stayed at the Four Seasons were jealous and came to our hotel for everything.

title: “Great hotel and location”
text: We are really glad that we stayed at Sutton Place in July 2012. Great location! Our deluxe king room on the 21st floor had beautiful views of the lake and city! The bellmen were very friendly. If you want a hotel with a fast elevator, this is it! We are planning on staying at this hotel the next time we are in Chicago.

title: “A New York Experience”
text:
I think that the people who are most disappointed by this hotel are not familiar with the "Manhattan experience". There are numerous hotels of the same genre in Manhattan all built in the early 1900's, room sizes like closets, bathrooms with old style fixtures and tile, peeling paint, stained walls and carpeting, and other general maintenance issues. Well welcome to NYC! Oh sure you can find hotels that are newer, more updated, and better maintained, but at 3-4 times the price. You just have to assess your own personal sense of value. Yes, the Waldorf Astoria has larger rooms, but old style furnishings and fixtures, and most of what you pay for is the elitism of the property.
I was pleasantly surprised at my recent stay at Hotel Pennsylvania. Despite the tumult and mobs of people in the lobby, for after all the Hotel has over a thousand rooms, when it was my turn to check in I was treated with the utmost attention, respect, and courtesy by Maria at the front desk. I had reserved a Club 5000 Double and was trying for an early check in. Since there were no non smoking doubles available at this time I was upgraded to a King and checked in. The room was clean with a comfortable bed in a very quiet interior (no view) location on floor 12. Yes there were some dings in the furniture and peeling paint issues, but it hardly affected my sensibilities when I knew I had a nice quiet room for sleeping with a very fair rate in a great city location. 
I found that the staff I encountered were all helpful and courteous. The Club 5000 Club Room was small and breakfast was nothing special-a true Continental Breakfast with Bagels, Rolls, Danish, Croissants, Juice, and Coffee. it may not be worth the extra cost, but it does provide a convenience and perhaps a little clout if you have issues for the management. I would readily stay at this property again especially when there is a large disparity among other hotel rates.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
Ez check in, check out...friendly staff, good room service...Rooms have nice appointments, beds are very comfortable. Nice fitness room. Lobby bar is good, restaurant good. 
Very nice facility...ez to get work done, and ez to relax...
There is a train track nearby and the trains blow their horns. 
Blue fin is down the street with great sushi. or go up the street to nice Northfield mall- Ling and louie for great asian fusion. Bass Pro Shop for great entertainment.

title: “Never Again”
text: The convenience of staying near our kids has been a major appeal of the Hilton Dallas Park Cities, as was the gracious service. Never again! We ckecked-in for a two night stay and were disappointed with the inconvenience of the remodeling work underway. But that's a temporary thing. However, upon returning to our room on Friday evening, we encountered the strong and familar scent of cigarette smoke on our floor. This was reported to the management, but went unchecked ... as Saturday produced the same result when we returned from dinner. Worse than that smelling smoke in an allegedly smkoe-free hotel, we encountered soggy carpeting in our room. The source could not be identified. The next morning, the adversely impacted area had expanded, ruining a pair of shoes and a piece of luggage. Upon checking-out, we reported the water problem to the Front Desk. The on-duty person was appalled, said she wanted to make things right and called the hotel manager ... who dismissed the incident, overrode the Front Desk and wanted to know how else he could help us. We left. Never to return.

title: “the location and the room was great”
text:
the location is great it's next to "beleive it or not" Museum and just in the corner there is the Times Squaer.
the room is great the size of the room was enough for tow adults and teenager.
the staff was friendly but the staff on the breakfast was not that much, they are kinda off rude and the service was so so not good "for Hilton Hotel".

title: “Great trendy boutique hotel, inconsistant service”
text:
Just so you know my perspective, I am a single business traveller in my late 20's and stayed for 3 nights for a business trip. For business travelling I know what top notch Ritz/Four Seasons service is like but when I travel on my own I stay at much more economical places and am not super fussy. Overall I thought The Dream was a great boutique hotel and I would definitely stay there again.
For the price which was high 200's/mid 300's depending on the night, I thought it was a great value compared to most things you could book in NY for that cost.
The overall look is very trendy and hip! The lobby & rooftop bar and restaurant are VERY cool and eclectic. You can tell the $$ went here as the rooms are more spare. The pictures on this website are very true to what you get. Not luxurious but cute and worked great for me. The airconditioner is LOUD. The windows open to let in fresh air which was great. Toiletries very nice and are from the Deepak Chopra center which is actually attached to the property so looked like some great though very pricey spa options ($185 & up for a massage)
A big pro for the property is the fact that there are multiple restaurant/lounge options. The on-site restaurant has a great variety of delicious cuisine but bad service (see below). The bar upstairs has a penthouse view and a rooftop open air level that is great in the spring. Think there is also a bar on the lobby level. The location is unbeatable. 2 blocks south of Central Park, 3-4 blocks north of Times Square, 3-4 blocks west of 5th Ave shopping.
The service is inconsistent! The hotel feels upscale because of the decor but the front desk does NOT give upscale service. They are friendly but untrained, too casual and lack the service standards that a hotel managed by a major brand like starwood, etc would have. Restaurant servers lack training. They are not rude, just spacey. I ate in the restaurant many times and it was fine for me & a colleague as the food was great but I would never bring a client as it would be embarassing. The concierges are great and very knowledeable about restaurants, give detailed directions & really took their time with us. Bellman were also super friendly and responsive. Housekeeping keeps things clean & in order but again service inconsistant. Sometimes for turndown I'd have fruit in my room, sometimes not, sometimes a weather report for the next day, sometimes not.
Cons for the business traveller are that room service doesn't start in the morning until 7am and there is no business center altough lots of nearby kinko's. No wireless internet but high speed ineternet access is in the rooms.
I would stay here again due to the hip atmosphere, great food options & location and would just know I'd have to put up with the inconsistent service. Have also stayed at The Alex but prefer The Dream now because it is superior in these respects and less expensive.

title: “Very Comfortable, Nice Decor”
text: This was a very nice hotel. Having never been to NY before, we weren't sure what to expect. This hotel is in a great location, close to theatres & Times Square, Central Park, 5th Ave, etc. The decor was very nice. It was great to stay in a place that didn't have a cheesy floral bedspread.

title: “Not a single printer worked.....”
text:
Stayed at the Ren Cen for a conference in late September. Overall, typical Marriott property, somewhat dated rooms, the lobby bar was nice and Coach Insignia was great. 
However, being there for business, and hosting a major conference, you would think they would have their business center up to par. Two computers in the business center - one would not accept any of the 4 credit cards I tried. The other (after paying $5 to simply use it) would not print the documents I need for a meeting in 5 minutes.
Informed the front desk of the issues, and they apologized and invited me to use the computers they had set up in the Volt bar to print the documents.
Wrangled with the touch screen (no mouses) for over 5 minutes to get into my email and open the document - only to look down to see an "out of order" sign on the printer. Informed the front desk of this and got nothing in reply. Guess I really didn't need those documents.
Also - be aware that when you book a meeting room at this hotel and they tell you it will be $300 for the day, be ready for the hefty 24% "set up charge." For a simple meeting room with one table and 6 chairs - isn't that what I am paying the $300 for?

title: “Hotel great but read the small print”
text: Stayed here with toddler granddaughter and her parents. The hotel was lovely, rooms comfortable and our booking had said breakfast included. This turned out to be a continental breakfast for one person in a room - crazy idea and feels like misrepresentation although it does say that when you read the small print. It was sorted out but detracted from the overall good impression. Good location for downtown Dallas. Valet parking efficient and convenient but not cheap.

title: “Friendly staff, great location, excellent service.”
text:
I found out about the Chelsea Pines Inn through TripAdvisor and I'm happy to say that all previous reports are right.
The staff always available and helpful, the relaxed environment, close to the subway and to all trendy places like Chelsea Market, the High Line, Union Square and more.
Will totally recommend this hotel and return when I have the chance.

title: “Quirky and fun; worlds away from the hustle of DC, a short walk away from everything.”
text:
Red and I checked into Topaz for a 3 night end of summer vacation. Just looking through their website is what got me hooked on the Kimpton brand five years ago - a quirky little boutique hotel with a focus on zen, tranquility, and self actualization. Seriously! 
The staff are amazing - professional but not at all stuffy. I was challenged to a hula-hoop off by their general manager for an upgrade and even though I lost (due to a technical foul!), they still gave me an *amazing* room. I could probably fit three regular sized cookie cutter hotel's rooms in it. Everything was AMAZINGLY clean with attention to detail.
During wine hour the staff was friendly and engaging - helping us with dinner and brunch recommendations. This is quite on par with the Kimpton brand but leaps and bounds what you would find anywhere else considering the star rating and price.
Red and I felt like super celebrities in a little known boutique hotel around the corner from everything. Between two metro stops - the location was perfect.
I began to wonder how they do it all so well. But a look at their Facebook pages and a look into their job culture shows a company who values ALL their employees and treats each client (down to the littlest puppy) like the most important one they have. Clean, convenient, friendly, attention to detail, and a defined personality. I'll definitely be back.

title: “LOVE THE COPLEY MARRIOTT, ALWAYS HAVE GREAT SERVICE!!!!!”
text: We always come to the Copley Marriott when visiting Boston, whether it is with the kids or just adults, we always stay here, it is centrally located, clean and the staff rocks... oh and so does the chowder.. we've been coming here for years and have never had a bad experience... love copley!!!!

title: “Nice place to stay”
text: This is a nice hotel. Quite rooms, with nice furnishings. You will need to pay for parking/valet, but the wait usually wasn't long.

title: “Very comfortable quiet night.”
text: We just stayed one night because we were passing through but will definitely stay again when we come back to Charlotte for a visit. The staff was very helpful and were prepared with a bed for our toddler grandson. We agree with other reviewers that our suite was amazingly quiet for being so close to the airport.

title: “Best Hotel in Chicago”
text:
This is absolutely the best place to stay when you visit Chicago for pleasure or business. The rooms are excellent. The staff treats everyone like family and handles all requests with a very professional manner. The location can't be beat...walking distance to great shopping and eating!
The bathrooms are spacious and the rooms quite nice! This is a superb 2nd home!!!

title: “Charming hotel in a great neighborhood”
text:
I can't say enough good things about the location of this hotel. It's on a quiet, beautiful residential street, but close to shopping and interesting restaurants (what'll it be: Persian? Turkish? Japanese? Mexican? locavore?) and an easy walk to the El. Much more restful than staying downtown, but much more convenient than staying out by O'Hare or in Evanston (my usual non-downtown choices when visiting the city). 
The lobby is charming, and my small room was spotlessly clean and comfortable. I admired the quirky mini-bar: it held not just the usual snacks, but also a rubber ducky ($6) and teddy bears. The bathroom fixtures were stylish, and even though the shower wheezed and complained a bit, there was ample hot water. The free breakfast was the usual bad coffee and limp pastries, but who cares -- there are plenty of other options in the neighborhood.
If you're a runner or walker, the Willows is just a few blocks from Lincoln Park (the actual park, not the neighborhood) and the lakeshore bike/running path. I was in town to go to a concert at the Vic Theater, which turned out to be an easy, pleasant walk away.

title: “Great location and staff - a good find”
text:
We spent 4 nights at the Casablanca in early March 2010. The staff and the location are outstanding (very pleasant helpful people, and maybe 40m from Times Square). Our room (a larger one with 2 double beds for a couple and adolescent) was fine but fairly small - double beds are doubles, not queens. The hotel building is itself small - 6 floors I think - and is surrounded by higher buildings, so unless you face the street (abit noisier) the rooms tend to be dark. Decorations are not overdone - not real kitchy, except for the two tiger statues in the 2nd floor cafe. The breakfast buffet, coffee/tea and cookies/fruit all day long, and the cheese and wine/bubbly all were good (the bubbly is a better quality than the wine). We got a very good price by paying all up front with no possibility of reimbursement, and given the location and the amenities, this was a very good option for us. All worked fine and we'd happily return, although at full price I'd probably check out the other good options nearby.
Food: Tony's downstairs was fun - a noisy Italian restaurant with enormous portions (the strawberry shortcake at the end was excellent and while listed for 2-3 people could have fed 4). Haru's Japanese restaurant just on the other side of Broadway was also quite good for the price. And for vegetarians, Blossoms restaurant (a 25 minute walk or 2 subway stops south - around 21st street and 9th as I recall) was outstanding - the best food we had in New York.

title: “We loved the hotel and the front office manager took great care of us.”
text: We had booked a room with 2 beds and they didn't have it when we arrived and Stephen Kelly stepped in and made our stay perfect with an upgrade and a roll away bed. I highly recommend this hotel. It was really clean and in a great area. The staff was awsome and handled our situation the way a hotel of this caliber should.

title: “Clean, central and friendly”
text: I stayed at the New Yorker Hotel on 8th Avenue (35th street) for a girly weekend. The first thing that hits you as you walk in is the air conditioning - very essential during an August heatwave. The rooms were standard - two double beds for three of us girls. very - comfy . the hotel has a diner attached to it "tick tock diner" which gives 24 hour service for takeaway coffee or sit down food. very reasonable and tasty food, with regular refills of coffee and iced water. the maid service was excellent - clean towels, rooms tidied and the beds made daily. A slight problem with a blocked toilet was resolved within ten mins of it being reported. I would highly recommend staying here - the location was fab - didnt use underground at all although it was located on the side of the hotel if it was needed. everything you need for an enjoyable holiday in the city that never sleeps.

title: “Good Location. Clean place to sleep in.”
text: We went to Boston on a last minute trip for Stanley Cup Playoff. Everything else in the city was booked and I found 1 room here popped up less than 24 hours before the plane took off. We didn't expect much but it turned out better than we thought. We got to Boston around 10.30 am and they let us check in early as we have a 2 years old who was very tired. (Luckily they had a room ready for us and even give us a discount for going us a queen size bed instead of 2 doubles.) The location was very conveniently close to subway stops and Chinatown & Theatre districts. The room albeit being old it is relatively clean. Good enough a place to sleep in. You can hear some noise from the street at night but it was not bad. All in all if you can find somewhere better that's great but if you don't, this hotel will do just find.

title: “Aussie family review”
text:
We stayed here for two nights from Sept 14th after finding a great price online. Location was AMAZING, so close to The White House( 1 1/2 blocks away) and metro station within 1 block.
Very clean, very quiet. Our family of five (2A and 3C aged 14yrs and two 11yr olds) had a room with 2 double beds and a lounge that folded out. For the amount of time we spent in our room(we slept here that was it!) it was fine but if your family needs to be in the room for longer than minimal time then this room type/ hotel may not be for you.
Would definitely stay here again if the price is right

title: “The Place To Stay !!”
text: Had a very good lodging experience ! Staff wonderful, Rooms very nice very clean !! We were on a cross country motorcycle event and the manager even looked us up, and gave us towels to clean our bikes. Very good Motorcycle Stop !! Overall just a very good establishment and Motel !!!!!!!!!

title: “Elegant and beautiful.”
text: Very romantic. The hotel is in a central downtown locaiton, very convenient to restaurants.

title: “OK place to stay - nothing fancy, but worked for us”
text:
Just got back from a 4 night stay at the La Quinta Mission Valley. Were there with husband and 3 kids (8, 3 & 4 months). We originally booked a standard room - check in was smooth, but when we got to the room, we realized that it was going to be way too small for a pack-n-play + all our stuff. So, we asked the front desk and they had a 2 room suite available for $10 more/night. We went ahead and took the suite and were so glad that we did.
The 2 room suite was perfect for our family with plenty of room for the 2 kids on the pull-out sofa and room for the baby's pack-n-play. There were also 2 TV's (one in each room) which was nice so that we didn't have to watch Cartoon Network the entire time :). The king bed in the 2nd room was very, very comfortable. In fact, both my husband and I were shocked when we woke up after sleeping on the bed the first night and we weren't sore. We've stayed at lots of hotels (cheap & expensive ones) and this was one of the most comfortable beds we've slept on. Big bonus points with us!!!
Noise wasn't an issue for us. For the most part, we kept the air units on "FAN" the entire time and so we didn't hear much of anything. Occasionally we would hear rolling luggage upstairs (we were on the 1st floor), but we didn't hear traffic noise or any of the rooms next to us.
The cleanliness of the room was OK - our feet still got a little black from the carpet, but everything else was pretty clean. Our only complaint with housekeeping is that they would only leave us 2 washcloths each day so we always had to call and get more. They brought them quickly, but you'd think that if there were 5 people in a room, that they would leave more than 2.
We only ate the free breakfast once - at 7:30 in the morning. We tried the other 3 days later (around 8 & 8:30) and the line was out the door. It just wasn't worth it for us to wait that long for toast, bagels, cereal & juice. Also, the breakfast room was very small and was extremely HOT - there was no air flow in there at all, so it was very uncomfortable. Don't know if they did that to keep people from staying very long or what. Anyway, breakfast totally not worth it at this La Quinta. We've stayed at other La Quinta's before and breakfast has been much nicer. Oh well, we weren't there for the food!
All in all, a good place for our family to stay. Location was good - Sea World was about 10 minutes away. It's also near a shopping center with lots of places to eat. 
I booked through La Quinta's website and kept checking back every day - was able to reduce my rate by about $35/night by checking and canceling/redoing the reservation. Got the suite for less than $100/night, so a pretty good deal for San Diego, especially since parking was free.

title: “80th TC”
text: Rooms are nice. However, some times it smelled moldy. Also, the internet was not at all desirable. Often times I could not even connect from my room.

title: “Location, location, location (and the bar is great too!)”
text: Fantastic location, incredibly nice staff, quiet rooms (even though we had a view of the city buildings), comfortable bed, and good shower. Love the wine reception, free wireless and the little touches of this hotel. The bar is good, great food and friendly staff.

title: “Great Hotel For Us”
text:
I've read a lot of the negative reviews and must say none of that applied to our trip.
We were greeted nicely by the front desk staff, they even gave us a fridge at no additional charge for our room when I asked. 
Rooms were clean. The two times we used the pool it was clean as well. Great location near a blue, green and red line station.
Whole Foods and CVS right behind the hotel.
Our room had a great view of the Charles River, Prudential Building and the John Hancock Tower.
Not a lot of good restaurants right there, but with a short walk or T ride you can get to anyplace.

title: “pretty good place”
text:
You can read what everybody else says about this place. One nice feature is ease of entrance. The building is a square doughnut so the center is open. The entrance is not on the street but inside the "doughnut" so you don't have to deal with street traffic.
The staff was good and the view from the outside from rooms facing California was excellent. But what I will always remember about this place is not the good stuff but the fact that they charge $15 daily for Internet usage. We've stayed at places costing only a third as much as this place and they all offered free internet access. Why not Stanford Court?
And many of those lower-priced places also had a free refrigerator (the one in Stanford Court was free but was fully stocked with beer, wine, juice, etc, so you couldn't really put anything of yours into it).

title: “location, location, location”
text:
1/2 a block away from times square..
friendly doormen (brian)
close to EVERYTHING

title: “Love this hotel!”
text: This hotel has such great style! That was a bonus to other more important features of an affordable price through Travelocity, great location, free parking, and helpful staff. We were just in Seattle for one night of our month-long road trip, so we wanted to make the most of it and the Maxwell Hotel certainly helped make that easy with its close location to the Seattle center and walking distance to downtown sights. We parked the car (which was full of camping gear) in the secure feeling free lot below the hotel (very convenient) and then walked or took public transportation/taxi everywhere to get around. Loved the bright, bold decorating of the hotel and rooms!

title: “Good deal”
text: My wife & I and friends stayed at the Crowne Plaza, S. F., over the Xmas holidays. For the location the room rates were great. One blk from Union Square, 1/2 - 5 blks from good restaurants, and I smiled when I got the bill when we checked out. The room was large enough for the two of us, the bathroom was good, everything was clean. Rate was $104 per night.Now the weird stuff. We ate at the hotel restaurant one night, huge steak cooked to perfection. Paid the bill and was told by the waiter that the tip wasn't big enough!And: we arrived at 1:00 AM and checked in with no problems. However, we were told by the clerk "there's the luggage cart, help yourself" and then he disappears.And: our friends reserved their room till January 1st, but due to a clerical error the hotel had them as leaving on Dec. 31st. So at 3:00 PM the hotel tells them they must leave or pay a new rate of $149.00 per night. A fist fight practically broke out with the assistant manger, but to no avail.But: on Dec. 31st we called down to room service for 6 champagne glasses and were told there would be a $3.50 service charge. No problem and, of course, we would tip the waiter. The catering asst. mgr. arrives with the glasses, waives the service charge and declines a tip!Summary: good with some glitches.

title: “Avoid this inept, uncaring hotel”
text: My husband booked a room for a business trip that fell through. When we called to cancel, we were told the hotel had the discretion to issue a refund if the hotel could rebook the room. I was told by the reservation department that the hotel had sold out, yet the general manager refused to issue a refund. He said his "hourly clerks" in the reservation department typically give out misinformation. The GM repeatedly said things like, "why should i deal with you?" and belittled the significance of the amount of money we had lost - not a business expense since the business had fallen through. He said he certainly had the power to issue the refund but would not. It seems the management at Hotel Windsor is inept and uncaring about its guests or generating return business and certainly has no confidence in its own staff. This reflects poorly on this hotel.

title: “Good hotel apart from the strikers”
text: This is a great hotel and I would recommend it to anyone however on our first day on our way to check in we were accosted by labour strikers. These people continued to strike from 7am very loudly and we were on the 9th floor! A lie in was on of question!

title: “A good choice as a base”
text:
OK, Manhattan hotels are going to cost you. This was still one of the better prices I found for a good-sized two-doubles room in a hotel that's convenient to two sets of subway lines and some of the sights. 
The entrance is pretty much a counter, and most of the space is for the two front desk staffers, the bell captain, concierge and security guard. The 12th floor adds the breakfast room and a business center. 
Our room was completely satisfactory. As spacious as we could reasonably expect, with comfortable beds. Very clean, and everything in the bathroom was as it should be. There's a small fridge. 
Breakfast isn't included. You can buy it on the 12th floor, but it's the usual hotel pricing with very few options for a light breakfast. Do your homework on what's around (use google maps, yelp.com, etc) and you'll find Au Bon Pain, Ess-A-Bagel, Toasties on Lex, and many more good options very close by. 
The E and M subways are right there, and the 4/5/6 are a block away. The E in particular takes you to a lot of useful places, including Penn Station and the WTC. The 4/5/6 goes to Grand Central and other useful places. Get a map and study the routes well to understand how well located this hotel is. 
The staff were always cheerful and helpful during our four-night visit. I'd stay there again.

title: “Excellent hotel!”
text: We stayed there on our honeymoon and the staff went out of their way to help us. Even gave us free upgrade & wine & strawberries! The concierge were extremely helpful also and even got us a table at a near by restaurant that we wanted to try. Hotel was clean, tidy & in excellent location. Would def recommend it and stay there again in a minute!

title: “honeymoon perfection”
text: what a great location and beautiful setting....obviously once in a lifetime but I would absolutely recommend this place to everyone traveling to Chicago. The rooftop balcony was cozy with little fire pits and a great view. Our service was excellent as well, the valets, concierge and other staff all very helpful in finding great places and making the best of our trip.

title: “Lovely hotel with friendly staff”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights last week. I stayed in a room with
2 queen beds. The room was really roomy with plenty of light. 
The location is great at the top of Nob Hill (California and Powell).
The intersection of 3 cable car lines it takes you to Fishermans Wharf
in 15 mins or union Square in 4 mins. Walkable down to Union St but would recommend getting car back up. The third cable line takes you to
China Town.
The hotel is very nice indeed with a nice courtyard. The door staff/
bell persons are super friendly and courteous. Free complimentary town car in the mornings to the financial district. use of the car for
the same price as a cab if availble.
The reception staff and concierge are helpful and make the hotel. Even
the gift shop staff are lovely.
i would recommend this hotel for a good base to see San Francisco.

title: “Just what I expected.”
text: The Mark is a very old hotel. I last stayed there 20 years ago and little has changed. The rooms, as expected, where small. The upper floor views can be sensational -- mine looked out on part of the bay and Alcatraz. The Top of the Mark is a great spot for a drink or dinner ($$$$$). Valet took forever --- 30 minutes to get my car.

title: “Good value in Union Square”
text: Stayed here because of the proximity to Moscone Center. The staff was friendly and the room was clean; although it seems like the hotel in general could use some updating. The seating in the lobby was very worn out! I didn't use the pool but it looked clean. The room itself had a comfortable bed and new TV. For what I needed it for, it was fine but if you're looking for a luxurious room this probably isn't the best spot.

title: “Great Breakfast!”
text: The omelet cooks were a great start to each day. Many ingredients and cooked to order. Those guys deserve a raise. This hotel was of course like the other embassy suites in many ways. It was louder than some with our room being next to the elevator.

title: “Great value for travelers with dogs”
text: We stayed here while traveling across the country with two kids & two dachshunds. The price for a double room was much less per night than we paid on this trip for other similarly rated accommodations along the interstates - a really good value. The room was clean & quiet, and the continental breakfast was fine. You can't beat LaQuinta's free pet policy. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: I would recommend the Castle Inn to anyone looking for an inexpensive place with lots of ammenities. The location is great. Each room has a refrigerator, microwave, freezer, ironing board, iron, free wireless internet, and a comfortable bed. Clean. Friendly and helpful manager. Free parking. Small free continental breakfast of muffins, bagels, breakfast bars, coffee.

title: “Great Location”
text: What good timing to get room and breakfast for 3 nights at a great rate online. (AAA rate) Although their breakfast buffet was nothing to write home about, service was good and it removed one decision for our short stay. The room was very comfortable, small, but nicely furnished with a comfortable bed and great t.v. Check-in was not easy, and we stored our luggage until 3 in the afternoon. A second wait for keys was annoying, but we endured, and the comfortable room and great location made up for that annoyance. We walked in all directions during our visit - Central Park, Times Square, and all the Midtown points of interest we could fit in during the 3 days. Our visit just wasn't long enough.

title: “Below average and overpriced”
text: This is a big old hotel with nothing going for it really. My room was large, but everything in it was old, the room smelled old. The windows didn't shut, out the cold air, heating didn't work (it was below freezing the week while I was there) and it was really noisy from the street noise. The bathroom was tiny and the kitchen was dirty and disgusting. Finally the WiFi was unreliable, slow and still about $14 per night from memory. I would never stay here again and could not recommend it to anyone. Maybe if you got it on a really cheap deal it would be ok. I was paying over $350 per night.

title: “Ink48 THE Spot to stay in NY”
text:
Wonderfully decorated rooms, with lots of space and so nicely appointed. Very hip design.
Extraordinarily accommodating staff with nice restaurant in house and a terrific bar on the top floor. 
They love pets here as do so many of the other guests. Out dog gives this place a paws up. 
Will definitely recommend to others and stay here again on our next trip to NY.

title: “They Lack Simple Human Decency”
text:
Here is my emaiil to the hotel:
My daughter brought her son there for a hockey tournament this past weekend. They reserved a room for Friday & Saturday night.
On Friday night my daughter became severely ill. Saturday morning she went to a critical care nurse who recommended she go the hospital. My daughter did not want to go to the hospital in Columbus because if they told her she had to stay she would be staying in a hospital far from home. So, naturally, my daughter opted to return to Michigan to seek emergency care there.
When she asked if she could cancel her room for Saturday night she was told that you had a 'policy' requiring 72 hours notice so you could not refund her second night.
My daughter is a single mother who really stretched her budget for that trip.
I think that your action indicates that you lack a certain fundamental human decency. The 'We have a policy' excuse could have been used by any inhumane despot in the history of the world.
I want to assure you that I will make it my life's mission to publicize your lack of simple human decency on every publication/internet avenue available.
Let me know if you have anything to say about this.

title: “Quiet location, accessible to shops/restaurants, clean, highly recommended”
text: My first time to stay in this hotel and will recommend to anybody. Location is accessible to Mayo Clinic, shops and restaurants. Easily accesible to the highway. I stayed here for 6 days and everyday, I came back with cleaned room. Room was immaculately clean, with plenty of drawer space, with full kitchen, chaise lounge, with ottoman where I can raise my feet while watching TV. TV can be rotated such that I can watch from the living area or while in bed. Airconditioning temperature can be adjusted. Soft clean white sheets and pillows. Good shower pressure with hot water. Welcome basket consisting of coffee and tea for the first day. Breakfast was available from 6am - with fruits, yogurt, scrambled eggs, potato, sausage, oatmeal, pancake, juice and cereals. What a treat! In the afernoons, there are snacks provided (chips, salsa, cheese and crackers, etc). Shutle is provided complimentary within a 2-mile radius. I rented a car and didn't have to use the shuttle. Service was great, staff was friendly. Recommended good restaurants close by (Kona Grill had delicious sushi and grilled salmon). Only few miles to J W Marriott where I had my conference. Gym is clean and has TV for each treadmill. Bring your headset to plug into the equipment otherwise you will not hear anything. There is a TV where you can use the remote and hear without a headphone, but if you want your exclusive show, use the equipment TV. There is also a mini store for snacks, medicine, and drinks. Fridays have special music or drink events. This is an enjoyable hotel to stay. I will stay again whenever I am in the area.

title: “GREAT LOCATION, GREAT SLEEP, GREAT STAFF, GREAT VALUE = GREAT HOTEL!”
text:
My family stayed here for a week. We had three rooms. Everyone in our group had great things to say about their trip. The location is perfect. The rooms were very clean, every day. The staff are very accommodating and efficient - especially John, the doorman. The internet worked well. The beds were great and the a/c worked perfectly. The rooms were quiet for an older, downtown property.
I have stayed at Kimpton hotels for years. Last year, I stayed at the Hotel Vintage Park in Seattle. I had a miserable stay. The heating cooling-system didn't work at all. The staff there were terrible and had no desire or ability to rectify my problem. Needless to say, I was reluctant to stay in another Kimpton property. But, the stay at the Serrano has changed my mind about Kimpton hotels again. I'll definately choose this group again (except the Vintage Park in Seattle).
I can't say enough for the wonderful week and would definitley recommend the SERRANO HOTEL.

title: “Excellent transport links. Don't need a car!”
text:
I stayed here for 3 nights, booked through a third party site and got a very good rate. I was pleased overall with the hotel. I had a ground floor, king size room, which was large, clean and comfortable. The fridge and microwave are a bonus if you are on a budget as there are restaurants and supermarkets, drugstores, all in close proximity to the hotel. I felt that the area was reasonably safe, as most of the people you encounter are workers in the area or other tourists/travelllers. Yes there are homeless people, just like any other major city in the world. 
The public transport is very accessible and cheap! I didn't have a car, but was able to easily reach all of the tourist areas, downtown and airport. To get from the airport to the hotel will cost $8.50 and could take up to an hour and a half in peak time, but its much cheaper than a taxi or shuttle! From the airport take the Flyaway bus (under the green sign) to Union station. Make sure the bus is going to Union because there are a few different buses that leave from here. From Union station take the redline metro to Hollywood/Western station - North Hollywood - and from there it is a very short walk to the hotel. To go to Hollywood major tourist areas, take the red metro train 2 stops to Hollywood/Highland station, less than 10 minutes, which will take you directly to the Highland Shopping complex, Chinese theatre, etc.

title: “The best deal on the Magnificent Mile!”
text:
The location was the best part of this hotel. Right across from the Water Tower and within walking distance to the subway and many attractions. The rooms were clean and comfortable. It was easy to find a good rate (I think we got ours from TravelZoo). We avoided the “extras” like the mini fridge, internet, and parking as they were extremely overpriced. 
Traveled with my wife and toddler, and we were all accommodated nicely.

title: “a quick great getaway”
text: This is our first time staying at The Kimberly and as we have heard so many great reviews of it. The Kimberly Hotel is located in mid-town which is a great location for theatre, Rockafeller Center, The Rock and the more tourist driven area. The Upstairs at the hotel has a fantastic brunch which we had on Saturday. This is not to be missed! My husband who knows his burgers puts it up there with the best of them! I had a great dish called the egg milanese. It was excellent and along with it we had complimentary mimosa's. Our suite was definitely extra large, clean but did need to be updated. It had a balacony which was great and views were fabulous. The bathroom was quite small for the size of the suite as we are a custom to larger and more luxurious bathroom, but it was clean! Our bed was so comfortable which we both had amazing sleep which sometimes we find that the bedding can be a break it or make it!. Overall, we would stay here, again, when we want to be located in this area. We would, however, like to stay the next time in a more updated suite as they do have them. The staff were very accommodating and friendly. The Doorman went out of his way to walk up the block to flag down a cab for us! The Sunday buffett was disappointing, though., we wished we could have stayed longer and waited for the brunch instead! I would give this hotel a 4 star for the only reason as our suite was quite in need of an update and larger bathroom! The furniture in the living room was broken and dreary as well as the curtains were torn with holes and runs in it.

title: “Great- just as website says”
text:
After searching many websites we finally chose the hudson. I am glad we did, it is in a great location, a two minute walk from 2 coffee bars, subway, and columbus circle. Cental park is within a 5 minute walk. 
The hotel is just as on its website very stylish. There is great music playing throughout and all of the public rooms are different in style. The main bar we found to be loud and busy in the evening which if you want to drink and dance is great. The outside bar area which is a smoking area is lovely. Waitress service somewhat of a limited pricy drinks menu but you're paying for the experience. 
The hallways are dark but it was not a problem for us. The bedrooms are small but we found them to be all that was needed for our four night stay in this fabulous city!! The bathrooms were so small they just made us laugh as yes your knees do touch the wall while sitting on the toilet but the shower and sink are fine and both the bathroom and the bedroom were spotless all through our stay. Towels are changed daily and bed linen as often as you request by putting card they provide on pillow. This is a modern new york hotel that provides style, modern surroundings and a good base for a stay in New York. I would recommend to anyone. Plus my partner proposed while we were there so will always be part of a special memory for me. Book Now New York is Fantastic!!!!!!!!!

title: “Great value, great location”
text: If you are expecting a five-star hotel, book a room at the ritz. But for what I paid, this place is value central. I booked for 170/night on hotels.com--practically the price of a hostel! Yes, the room is small, but with everything the city has to offer, what the heck are you doing hanging out in your hotel room? If you're looking for good value and good location, look no further. If you're looking for luxury, be prepared to spend a lot more.

title: “Great value, great location,great view!”
text: Hotel is nice and clean. Staff is friendly. Room has the basics and is nicely decorated. Shower is nice, no bath tub. Bed is firm. A little too firm for my liking, but still comfy. I will be staying here again.

title: “Second Stay - Just as good”
text:
This was a our second time staying here in the last year - this time was again for a single night.
Spent more time at the bar area. The wings were great - sauce was on the side - very spicy and excellent. Drinks were perfect. Ate at Bistro 555 - it was good. Empty the night we were there - but good.
Room is very clean. Pretty quiet - though some sirens came up. Had a great view of the capital at night. Stayed in a single room this time, instead of the suite.
One complaint was the shower. Very nice design with dual shower heads on opposite sides. very spacious. However the water temperature was all but impossible to control. Could not get hot water, just wamr at best - and that was with a lot of playing around.
Still - this is a great hotel. Staff is very attentive. Stay here and enjoy!

title: “Great location”
text:
We enjoyed our stay at The Lenox, very nice and clean hotel with good service.
We had a quick breakfast at their restaurant Azure every morning and it was OK. The place did not "invite" us to come back for dinner.

title: “Great View”
text: The hotel lobby was beautiful. The rooms were pretty average. The view from the 23rd floor facing the bay was wonderful. We really enjoyed watching the ships sail in and out. The kids enjoyed the heated outdoor pool and hot tub. My complaint was that our hotel safe did not work reliably. We had to have security to our room 3 times to open our safe. They kept telling me that I was probably putting too much in the safe. I only had an envelope with money in it. All in all though. It was a nice hotel.

title: “You could not find a better hotel in Chicago for the price!”
text: We booked the Talbot, based on Trip Advisor reviews and the price. We got a great deal on Orbitz for $116 a night in August. You will not be disappointed with this hotel. Excellent customer service...turn down service, like at a 5 star...super comfy king size bed, excellent (absolutely in the center of all you want to do) location, spacious room. I cannot say enough about how wonderful this place is. We LOVE to find a 5 star experience at a 3 star price. In this case, we found a 5 star experience at a 2 star price. I cannot find a single flaw with the Talbot. Excellent Consierge, also. Don't waste your money spending double at the high end chains. All you need is at the Talbot. You will love this hotel!!

title: “The Pearl is a Pearl!”
text: What can I say? I stayed once again at the Pearl and they again proved they really do have the talent to deliver amazing customer experiences! You are treated not so much as a hotel guest, but rather as a friend staying over - but with legit hotel perks! The restaurant is amazing - you have to check out their draft beer list which is authentically local and fits the Pearl's personality! I only wish I had more time to stay (and eat + drink).

title: “Location?”
text: Very nice hotel but I was not happy with the busy street location. Not close to the wharf or cable cars. We moved to their sister inn-Columbus Inn where we could walk to the wharf and hop on a cable car.

title: “Good across the board, especially location near theaters”
text:
Visited NYC during July 2010 for the first time. Wanted to spend money on NY experience rather than hotel and was happy with our choice. Consistent experience with other Hampton 
Inn properties. 
Good.....
Great location theaters (1 min. Walk to Wicked, Jersey Boyes, Harry Connick Jr., etc)
pharmacy 1 block south and north
Room was decent size and air conditioning was working nicely during a hot week
Subway very close
Easily walkable to Time Square & Central Park
Ok Proximity to restaurants and Hells kitchen
WIFI - decent connection both wired and wireless.
Bad......
Bathrooms are small, one person at a time
Elevators a little slow
Breakfast - became a cattle call in the mornings, but would recommend to go out for 
breakfast (better experience and food anyway)
TV - typical setup. Turn it off and go outside and walk around.
Wish List.......
Little better bellhop service - didn't have a taxi easy after a call to the front desk
Beds - beds were a little harder than typical great beds at Hamptons
Paid around $260 AAA rate for 5 day stay which was pretty good for the area.
Overall solid stay. Would stay here again if I needed a solid bet in the theater district.

title: “Great for the Business Traveler”
text: This recently renovated Sheraton was beautiful and very conveniently located. The rooms were great- only complaint is that the walls are thin (my neighbor was in the shower at 4:30 am so that is when I was forced to wake up.) Beds were comfy, love the down comforter. Staff was incredibly friends- greeting me with a smile on my way out to my meetings and on my way back. Again, only complaint is that I had pre-ordered room service for breakfast, woke up early and requested an hour earlier delivery and they forgot about me (had to call back 30 minutes later). Outdoor space is beautiful with fun fire pits where we had a welcome reception. Would definately return.

title: “Great location, large rooms, friendly service”
text: We had spent way too long deciding on where to stay for our "girls week" in New York. I am happy we finally decided on the Blakely. It is a cozy, boutique hotel in a great location only a few blocks from Central Park and subway around the corner. The suite with separate lounge area gave us plenty of room to handle all our shopping bags we came back with each day. The construction noise outside kept us awake the first two nights so we asked to change rooms and they were happy to do so. Unfortunately our new room was even noisier so we moved back ! Staff were helpful and understanding. I would recommend a room at the back of the hotel and as high as possible to escape street noise. Lifts were slow as others have commented but if you are on holidays you should be able to spare the extra few minutes to wait. Continental breakfast and free wifi are excellent inclusions and although the breakfast was the same each day we were happy not to have a decision about where to eat each morning and just go downstairs to the small restaurant connected to the hotel. Overall we were very comfortable at the Blakely and would recommend it as a boutique style hotel experience.

title: “Not Bad but could have been much nicer with a few simple upgrades”
text:
My wife and I stayed at this hotel for one night. We used Hotwire and got booked here. The hotel appears to be a clean hotel with no obvious issues. Our room was in good shape and ready on time. Hotwire had booked us a smoking room with two beds and the hotel gladly let us change to a non smoking king bed. 
Here are the things that kept me from giving this hotel a better rating. Most delt with the bathroom.
For a king bed there were three almost airline size pillows...
The towels were those cheap, thin towels that don't dry off anything
The toilet paper said soft on the name..I think they were referring to the paper it was wrapped in
The toilet was the loudest thing I've ever heard.....if you have been on a cruise, you know how loud those things are...this beat them. 
The pillow, towel and toilet paper issues could easily be resolved and would have made a nice difference. I'm writing this from our next stay which is in a Hampton Inn in Harlingen, TX. We payed $10 more for this room and it doesn't have any of these issues...it makes all of the difference in the world. 
Overall, not a bad hotel..but could have been much better

title: “Unique hotel experience”
text: Really enjoyed our stay at this property near the Charles River in Boston. Beautifully renovated former jail house with lots of history. The check -in was swift & friendly (champagne as well) Lobby area was comfortable and fun,a good area to sit and chat or listen to jazz trio that was playing the evening we stayed. We received a free room upgrade, which was unexpected due to the low room rate we payed. Room was spacious and clean. Would love to stay there again.

title: “The BEST HOTEL in Chicago!”
text: We had the most FABULOUS time at the Conrad. Both my husband and I have never had such an amazing experience at a hotel as we had there. What a way to celebrate our first anniversary! Every member of the staff, from the front desk (especially Carol for recommending two great restaurants for dinner), restaurant staff, bar staff (especially Sergio) and even the housekeeping staff were always friendly and smiling. I travel to Chicago twice a year for different trade shows, and now I will only stay at the Conrad. They truly go above and beyond in every aspect of their hotel. Our room was beautifully appointed, and most of all clean and comfortable. I would recommend the Conrad to anyone looking for a special hotel experience! It's truly a home away from home!

title: “Great job by Marriott's Residence Inn”
text:
Spent five days at the Residence Inn Downtown in Houston at the end of September for a work related trip. Like most Residence Inn's, the hotel was immaculately clean and the staff unbelievably friendly. The front desk staff started greeting me by name after one day, and the woman who took care of the breakfast service made the morning much brighter. The hotel provided free Wall Street Journals.
There is a lot of construction in Downtown Houston and that was very annoying. Some of it is adjacent to the hotel. Can't hold the hotel responsible for that, but if that would bother you, be careful. Note though that the same situation exists all over downtown and affects other downtown hotels.
I will definately stay here again. The price, cleanliness, friendliness, and convenience of having a full kitchen are great.

title: “Proof is in the pictures”
text:
No, I would not recommend this hotel. No, I would not stay at this hotel again.
Me and my wife stayed at the Doubletree Hotel in downtown D.C. on a recent trip to the nations capitol.
 Positives: Location, close to downtown D.C.; nice neighborhood; can walk to the White House; restaurants close by.
Negatives: 
-Flies and gnats in the room. When I complained to staff at the hotel about the insects, I was told that the D.C. area use to be a swamp, therefore I should expect a few flies and gnats.
-Toilet broke in my room and when I asked for a different room, I was told that the only room available was a handicap room. Toilet was eventually fixed, but this was a huge inconvenience. 
-Staff was often times rude and uninterested
-Bathroom and hotel overall is a bit dated and in need of upgrades.
 1. The tub in my hotel room has chipped and peeling paint in the tub (pics attached)
 2. The floor and tiles are dirty (pics attached)
-Too expensive
 1. One domestic drink cost me $15
 2. Valet Parking is $35, not including tip
 3. Restaurant prices in the hotel are insane
-Rooms are small and loud (buzzing from a/c, phone room, etc)
-AND THEY WERE ALWAYS OUT OF COOKIES.
I have come to expect more from the DoubleTree brand. This DoubleTree really disappointed me and my wife. I was comped 2 nights of valet parking and the G.M wrote me a handwritten letter apologizing...but the guy did not even have the courtesy to call me while I stayed in the hotel.

title: “Good Hotel”
text: Hotel was nice, room clean. The hotel is atop a large hill in San Francisco - not too far from China Town or Fisherman's warf. When you go to these tourist stops, you have a big hill to go down and climb back up to the hotel. They offer apples in at the front desk (a nice snack and touch). They have a decent health club (a few treadmills, a few cross trainers, etc). It was a bit crowded in the morning and the gym could have used better air conditioning. I was on the 2nd floor and it was a bit noisy from outside traffic - I would have been better off on a higher floor. A friend on a higher floor said the elevators were a bit slow and he thought the 2nd floor was better (since I could easily use the stairs).

title: “Very cute and chic”
text: I stayed at this hotel in July 11 for a business trip. The room was very small but the bed was ultra comfortable. The location was absolutely perfect! Close to shopping, tons of taxis, walking distance to Navy Pier and of course great restraunts. The concierge was knowlegable and friendly. The bar was small but very chic. Some of my coworkers likenned the hotel to one seen in a mob movie, I likenned it to a super cute, chic, modern hotel.

title: “Retro Gem in the Heart of Downtown San Antonio”
text: I had a last minute trip to San Antonio and needed to find a hotel at 9:30pm on a Friday evening. This newest brand of Hilton seemed to fit the bill so I booked it sight unseen from my vehicle. What a surprise- clean, friendly staff and the room was adorable and well-thought out. I don't need a full suite when traveling by myself and the little kitchen area perfectly complemented the *studio* feel of the room. A perfect location on Houston and Navarro, just a block from the river and in the middle of everything. If the rest of this new brand continues along these lines it will become my *go-to* choice - for either business or pleasure. Absolutely no complaints whatsoever and the entire crew was friendly and efficient- I was especially impressed by a young lady named *Alex* who worked the front desk-she was above and beyond with me and everybody else I saw her attending to.

title: “Needs renovation, Bellman had bad attitude”
text: Won this by bid on priceline for $262/night. Big disappointment. The only good thing about it is it is next door to Starbucks. It looks like it has not been remodeled since the 80s when black marble was popular. It is dark, out-of-date and the service was lacking. Would not stay again.

title: “Really Fantastic!”
text:
We stayed at the Residence Inn on our first trip to New York in '07 & it really was the cherry on top! The service was great, along with the location & breakfast is just perfect.
We stayed in a corner suite. The rooms have everything you need (including a full kitchen) and are a good size. I would recommend this place to anyone, it's amazing just like NYC!

title: “Terrific Location.”
text: Recently stayed here on business, really enjoyed the stay. Terrific location, within walking distance to the GW university campus, Georgetown, and only 15 minutes from Reagan National. The staff is very friendly and helpful, the on-site restaurant is terrific (try the salmon on mashed potatoes with spinach!), and overall it was a very pleasant stay. Would highly recommend it to the business traveler as well as families.

title: “Dismal turned into an above-par experience.”
text:
Initial room assignment was terrible. Admittedly, I checked in WAY too early (before 10:00am), but I was given a room in the tower building that was smaller than any I have ever been assigned - including in New York and Europe!!! There was NO room to walk on one side of the bed, there was only a small light bar above the sink in the bathroom, which cast zero light into the tub area, plus (not the fault of the room) the phone didn't work and the WiFi couldn't connect in that room. Why? Because the room is located in the elevator lobby. What??? Yes. There are nine "doors" in the elevator lobbies. Seven are elevators. One is the vending/ice room. And the other is a guest room. Really? As a Starwood Preferred Guest, I'm appalled. Beyond appalled. I was STUNNED to find I'd been given a room with a double bed (not even a queen!) in the elevator lobby! These rooms should only be assigned as a last resort!!!!
After checking in and quelling my shock at the room, a knock at the door and the announcement of "engineering!" surprised me. I answered the door, and the two ladies from engineering were surprised that the room was occupied??? They apologized, saying they thought the room was empty and they wanted to make "some repairs." They asked if I had any requests, and I asked for an iron. They assured me they'd have one delivered.
Fast forward two hours. I returned to the room to find no iron. I picked up the phone to call the front desk and was inundated with static, squealing, and a simply horrible connection. Within five minutes Linda (one of the two engineering ladies from earlier) stopped in to "fix" the phone. She looked around, noted the iron had not been delivered, that the Internet wasn't working and that the phone was crap... She called the front desk and had me re-assigned to a king room. OMG -what a difference!
She helped me move to the new room, pointed out the landmarks visible from my window, and showed me where the HVAC controls, etc., were located. She salvaged the ENTIRE stay for me. 
The bed? The bed was AWESOME! Very comfortable, and I slept like a ROCK!
I only stayed at this hotel because of a conference on-site, and have to say that wayfinding is difficult, at best. I only thought the Chicago Marriott Magnificent Mile was awful. This convention center is terrible! The concierge, when asked how to get from her desk to the exhibit hall, said something to the effect of: "Go past this door, take the elevator to 2, take the bridge to the tower building, go down a floor (or up??) and then go around two left-hand corners to another escalator, then left, then right, then up an elevator, to..."
Seriously. Even the three-d maps at all the elevator banks are confusing... No easy-to-read signage at all. This needs to be rectified.
Conference services were OK. The foodservice staff was short-tempered and somewhat surly...

title: “Central and very comfortable”
text:
Sophisticated, central location. Good service. Modern and clean room styling making the rooms feel light and spacious. Very comfortable beds. Powerful overhead shower.
Very good indoor pool for the family. Well equipped gym.

title: “Hip hotel with a businessy vibe”
text: Very hip hotel with trendy afterwork crowd filling up the bar monday to friday. room was nice but dark. Great location.

title: “Old, out-dated, and smelly.”
text:
Some of these old big-city hotels can be diamonds in the rough, but this one was just rough. The lobby and common areas were nice - typical marble and brass accents you would expect in a hotel from the early 1900's. Unfortunately, the accomodations were far from charming. The hallway was filled with scuff marks to the walls, old carpet that hadn't been vacuumed in some time, and holes in the ceiling. And then, there was the smell...kind of like what you experience in grandma's basement. It was musty and unpleasant. Our room smelled the same way. It was coverfed in VERY outdated wallpaper. We found other people's garbage under our beds (old soda can, wrapper, and a champagne cork.) As an added challenge, the walls were very thin. We were able to hear our amorous and boistrous neighbors each night - not fun with a six-year-old in tow.
The positive notes were that the sheets and bathroom were clean. Also, the hotel is ideally located, directly across from Buckingham fountain and within blocks of both the "L" and the redline subway. Because it was cheap and we didn't spend much time there, it was fine. But I would NEVER stay here again.

title: “You Get What You Pay For”
text:
My wife, son and I went to Boston to visit our daughter in Boston, and stayed at the Copley House for one night. It's actually not a house but a collection of apartments in several row houses all within a few blocks of each other. We had reserved a suite room on the 3rd floor of one of the 2 Newton Street buildings. When we arrived (after driving 7 hours) we were told the room had already been "assigned" but we were given another in a building on St Stephen St. Well, the room was nothing like the website prictures. It was 1970s decor, worn by 30 years or so. Light bulbs were dead, tiles loose in the bathroom, the toilet seat coming off, etc. It reminded me of my edge of Brooklyn Heights apartment, circa 1975. That's not a compliment. I only wish I thought to take a few pictures.
Don't be fooled about the parking. It is not included, unless you know the owner or the place is empty. The Manager did take the parking fee I paid for a garage a few blocks off the tab after I complained.
I commented about the condition of the apartment when checking out and the bait and switch routine. I was told I'd get an email regarding my issues. I'm still waiting.
The 1 plus was the location, in Back Bay. But unless you're on a recent college grad budget, spring the extra cash for a real hotel room.

title: “good sized rooms but welcome tray needs attention”
text: The staff were very helpful. While we were there, my husband became ill, and the conciege arranged for a doctor to phone up to give us advise. The doormen were also very helpful, recommending places to eat. However, our room was at the front of the hotel and the lack of double glazing made it difficult to sleep due to the street noise-bin men collecting rubbish at 4am!! Had to buy ear plugs to get a good nights sleep. It was disappointing that we couldn't make a hot cup of coffee with the coffee maker supplied. What is wrong with a kettle? Had to heat the water up in the microwave and use the coffee like a tea bag! Also, the tea bags weren't replaced when the room was serviced and as a 4 star hotel, I would except biscuits on the welcome tray as standard and china cups not cardboard ones!

title: “Great Hotel”
text: I read over the reviews and I'm surprised about the negatives that were posted. I absolutely loved Morgan’s. The staff was so nice and accommodating. I called down with a question and they answered the phone how can we help you Mrs F. Always a smiling face in the lobby between the door man and the desk clerks. The breakfast was lovely: fruit, bagels, cereal, juice, yogurt, muffins, croissants, coffee. The location was the best. 37th and Madison. Perfect mid town location in a very nice quiet neighborhood called Murray Hill. It's decorated modern in black, white and grays; the bed was cozy, pillows amazing, great down comforter. Yes the room was small, but it's Manhattan. We were in a room right beside the elevators, I didn't hear anything and I sleep very lightly. I can't wait to go back to Morgan’s; it's my new favorite place to stay in Manhattan.

title: “Excellent value, comfortable, clean, nice staff”
text: Stayed here two days in late March. Staff was very friendly and helpful (sent someone up within three minutes to fix a sticky door lock). Room was very clean with no musty smell and no carpet deodorizer to cover up. Bathroom was fine, spotless. Enormous amount of closet space. Was great to have the fridge, microwave, and stove. We were on the tenth floor, so there was virtually no noise. It's in a quiet, safe area, with anything you need on either 2nd or 3rd Aves. We paid $138 on the Web, and for that price, it's pretty much unbeatable. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great place for the cost”
text: Good place to stay when traveling to airport! Quick and easy! Parking was quick and service was great! The price was great compared to others in area! Would stay again for sure!

title: “In a great shopping area”
text:
Stayed at this hotel as we are spg members and collect the points. We stayed in a suite on the 15th floor and, facing the freeway. Other comments had mentioned traffic noise, but with the curtains being closed and the AC on, you couldnt hear the road. Room was spacious and clean, seperate living area with a fridge and sink. The decor in the room was nothing super-fancy, but the bed was comfy and me and my partner had two very relaxing nights.
We ate at the Omaha steak house on our first night, pricey as most sheraton eateries are, but the steaks were done too perfection. Hubby enjoyed a well done sirloin, while i had a very tender filet. i wasnt too keen on the mash, thought it was a bit gummy, but hubby loved it, so, personal preference i guess. If you order extras, such as sides or dessert, the portions are HUGE! i had a side of broccoli, which was practically a tree, and a piece of chocolate cake to go. The piece of cake weighed atleast 2 lbs and took me 3 days to eat it! thankgod for the fridge in the room!!
The area is nice and feels safe. The galleria is well worth a visit, and is right on the doorstep. Wear comfy shoes!!
Also FYI, we flew into Hobby and took a taxi to the hotel, they charge an extra $6 ontop of the meter price, because its in a "downtown area", it came to about $45. Avoid yellow cabs if possible.
This hotel may not look the fanciest from the outside, but did not disappoint. Clean, modern, comfy, convenient.

title: “Most enjoyable stay at the Willows”
text: We just returned from a short break in Chicago where we enjoyed summer weather in March! The Willows is a great choice to be away from downtown while able to get into within 15 minutes on the bus. Old style smallish hotel with very comfortable rooms and modern bathrooms. Fridge in the room with very affordable drinks and snacks. Absolutely fantastic staff, so friendly and always happy to help. Great neighbourhood. Only downside for us was the fact that the very decent continental style breakfast was served in the lobby which is not properly set up for that but you can take your tray to your room if you prefer. Will definitely use again and highly recommend!

title: “the Wit”
text: Great hotel, a little pricey - but would stay here again

title: “Clean, restful hotel”
text: This hotel was located across the street from a workshop I attended and was the perfect place to rest, eat, work, and network with others. I stayed in a waterside room and the sights and sounds of the bay were delightful. The staff was helpful, friendly, and professional. Overall, it was a delightful experience that I will look forward to repeating.

title: “RIDICULOUS NOISE”
text: Here for a week's stay...after one night starting to crack up already. The noise in the hotel is awful. The rooms have adjoining doors so you can hear everything in your neighbours rooms, the balcony glass is so thin you can hear the traffic and the cruise ships horns all night. The worst part is the noise from the pool, the filters have been buzzing and banging all night. Rooms and entire hotel dated. Noise from air con is dreadful too.

title: “Big Brother is watching you.”
text:
On checking out, they accused myself and my wife (who's never smoked a cigarette in her life) that we smoked in the room, and charged us a $200 fine.
They wouldn't furnish us with a reason for the accusation, only saying that "They have extensive proof".
When asked to forward our case to upper management, the lobby manager forwarded our complaint to housekeeping instead - to the very person who accused us.
3 days later, at the threat of legal action, they finally dropped the charges.
Worst hotel staff ever. Rude and dismissive. Spoiled our stay.

title: “Great location and good service”
text: From the perspective of someone that used to live in NY, the location is fabulous. The staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful. The room was lovely. The bed was super comfortable.
