To be picky, they could use new carpeting and new bathtubs to take it up a knotch. But I was very happy with the room overall. My only real complaint is about the room keys. Almost every time we left the room, they stopped working and we had to ask for new ones (they were not next to our phones or anything magnetic). This seems to be a known problem that the corporate company should probably prioritize on its repairs list!

title: “WONDERFUL stay!”
text: We actually live in Chicago but having our parents in town decided we would give up our condo and cozy bed to stay in a hotel while they took over our condo! Just a few blocks from home we checked in to the Sutton Place, what a nice welcome, quick and easy check in. Our room was great, spacious with all the amenities and the bed was unbelievably comfortable! The bathroom, my favorite room, was large, great lighting and exceptionally clean! We were hesitant to give up our own condo for a night down the street but would do it again in a heartbeat at the Sutton Place!

title: “loved it, great service, great breakfast!”
text:
We stayed here for 8 nights. 
After much research of where in NYC we would stay for our first visit, with the help of TA members through forums, we came up with this. 
I had previously read that some taxi drivers had difficulty finding this - we experienced this problem a couple of times. 
We had 1 great taxi driver who got us to the intersection and we said, that's fine we'll just get out here, and he said let me know where it is, im interested to know - to which we showed him. 
however there was another night where (because of TA warnings) I was pedantic about giving correct directions, the cab driver stopped the car, our surroundings didn't look familiar, I said is this it? And he just mumbled "yeah I don't know where it is", so silly me not only paid him, I tipped him too. Only to realise how far north we were - somewhere up in Greenwich village, walking in the cold and dark, decided to hail another cab. 
So just be aware of this, its a bit of a hidden gem! 
as for the hotel itself - great breakfast buffet, cosy but nice, fantastic waffles! Not only coffee available all day, but a selection of juice too. 
Hotel staff were extremely friendly. (Except one who would mutter "mm-hmm" when we bothered her with a small question!) 
room itself - we had street view, quite noise proof considering the traffic that goes down there. nice modern bathroom - its so good to have a shower glass and not curtain. 
surprised to see so many french guests - I had to ask staff about that, the owner is french so it must be advertised a bit over there. 
short walk to a few different subway stations - take your pick.
short walk to canal st too - which we ended up at every single day so I did get sick of that. 
for the experience, next time its possible I would stay close to Times Square, though for the price and still a good location (besides the annoying canal st every day) Hampton Inn is a great place.

title: “Great in concept, bad in execution”
text:
Great concept for a hotel, but certain things were lacking. 
The Bad: Upon check in we were greeted (use that term loosely) with a staff member that was less than helpful and frankly just seemed disgruntled every time we attempted to speak with her. Our shower would not drain properly which resulted in us standing in 4-6 inches of water after only a few minutes. After asking for the fourth time that it be fixed we gave up. It also appeared that the maids gave the room only a once over - as there were stains on the wall and the furniture. 
The Good: Great location. Good atmosphere, and comfortable room for the price.
I give the Night a very reluctant recommendation based mainly on its location and hope we just caught them at a bad time.

title: “could'nt have asked for more”
text:
went with my wife for 5 nights at end of august 2005 and to say we enjoyed our stay would be a understatement, it is rare to go away and not have any complaints about a hotel stay, well this was one of those, each and everything about the hotel and their excellant staff could not be faulted. the highest compliment we could give is we will be back, any request, query was no trouble, the room size for new york was big 
thank you hotel shelbourne for making our stay in new york even more enjoyable

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
If you are just flying in and out and need a bed to stay or wanting to see Dallas this is a great place to stay, the staff are friendly and helpful and the food it fantastic well worth a visit.
The total package starts when you are picked up by the free shuttle bus to take you to the hotel ( our driver was Bill) so helpful talking about the hotel and happy to help with any questions that we asked also remember our names when we came down stair later in the day a great asset to the hotel.
As we were staying in a quiet time of the year we also were luck enough to be able to have ala carte breakfast at no added cost very nice.
We had dinner at Aces lobby bar both night we stayed it was great we were served by Ron another good employee for the hotel. The food was fantastic.
The hotel also has a Starbucks coffee available. 
So all round we had a great stay, why do you give it a go next time you visit you will no be disappointed.

title: “Nice stay, clean rooms.”
text: Great location, loved the spot for business or play. Rooms typical New York and the service was great from one man in particular. I wish I got his name. Small India/Asian man with classes. Very nice man. I recommend this hotel.

title: “Huge rooms, great views”
text: This is a stunning hotel, and I really won't say too much more about it. The name sort of speaks for itself, but overall, our suite was humongous, beautifully appointed, and the views from our floor were breathtaking, to say the least. The tower is centrally located in Chicago, and it's easy to travel anywhere you'd like to go in the city. Recommended.

title: “Average Stay”
text: Stay here 3 nights and really had no major issues. It is located in a business area and car is needed if you don't plan on eating at the hotel restaurant. If you are accustom nice contemporary this is not the place for you. This hotel was formally an office building and you can tell that remodeling expenses were kept to a minimum. The rooms are located in an atrium theme that looks just like an office building. So much more could have been done to jazz the place up!!! If you are not going to spend alot of time in your room then this is an ok hotel at tops. We stayed gone from 11a-8p so it was really just a place to shower and rest overnight as we took the kids to LegoLand about 35minutes away and Mission Bay Beach about 20mins. Mission Bay Beach was nice and has a small amusement park for kids and free parking. All in all for under $110 a day it was an ok stay, but being accustom nicer hotels I wound not stay again. Hotel did allow for a early checkin and a late check out that was appreciated. Save on $$$ here and miss out on all the nice finer amenities at hotels priced $160 above. My recommendations stay near Hotel Circle or Carlsbad.

title: “Service above and beyond expectations”
text: Per my request, Ms. Judy Teague, Assistant Manager went out of her way to gather my personal items left over in my room that saved me time and allowed me to reach the airport in time for my flight.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: Got a great rate at Hotwire. This hotel is close to everything downtown. The room was spacious, well-appointed and comfortable. The desk clerk was helpful and friendly. I wish that I would have had time to explore the facilities more extensively. I can honestly say that I've never had a bad experience at any Crowne Plaza. The only issue that I have about staying in any hotel downtown is the expense of parking.

title: “Nice lobby, shame about the rest”
text:
We just stayed five nights at The Roosevelt (and picked the hotel based on the reviews here). Certainly has a big lobby that's very 1920s grand. But of course you don't stay in the lobby.
Our room was on the 17th floor. The basics were OK - large good quality bed, little street noise, walls solid enough to give you privacy, only one blood stain on the bed linen, etc. The rest was poor. Not enough hanging space for clothes, large and noisy heating units, cracked and flaking paintwork, dirty nets, old heavy brown furniture with plenty of marks and dents, nylon carpet that needed a good clean, big black cheap Phillips television with poor reception, florid decor all mismatched and gone drab.
The bathroom was small to middling, the bath very small and getting grubby, the shower good, but with no extractor everything got misted and damp very quickly. A very basic and functional beige tiled bathroom. As with the bedroom, everything was approaching worn out (the hairdryer looked like a museum piece).
Room service was adequate. You get through to an answerphone and they call you back a few minutes later. The staff hit you with the same patter every morning (gets tedious) and shamelessly dig for tips regardless of how long they kept you waiting. Service generally followed the same model. Plenty of syrup and mock concern, sure, but delivered with blatant unconcern for anything except the dollars in your wallet (tip low, or not at all, if you want to hear a sincere remark).
The restaurant should be avoided. Food comes heavily salted and overcooked, my salad was memorably disgusting, the place anyway looks like Hell's anteroom, and prices are optimistic. For the same money, you'll get a great meal at The Oyster Bar just over the way at Grand Central Station. We wouldn't recommend Eammon's Bar (up the street) unless you just want convenience - the food there was warmed up and ordinary.
Final score: Worst hotels exist and service was OK (apart from being mindlessly insincere). Room quality was poor (we were in a group of 12, everyone got a more or less shabby room). Location is good (bear in mind that Manhattan isn't half as big as you'd think, so being in midtown is only a modest bonus). Would we stay at The Roosevelt again? Unlikely. Lobby apart, this was a poor place to stay for the price.

title: “Definitely would return”
text:
We booked this hotel at a very last minute, so none of the 2 double bed room was available (we traveled with a 2 yo and 8 yo). So we decided to book the corner king thinking the corner room would be and is usually bigger with big windows so it would be decent when we add an extra rollaway bed, i was wrong. Btw the website didnt say much about the room size and description, now i know why. That first night we arrived, we were so suprised of how small the room was, and the view from our big corner windows were back alleys and rear sides of buldings. It was the smallest room ive ever stayed in for all these years ive travelled to all over the world. More bearable if only 2 people, but still very tiny and sad looking in my opinion. So we survived that first night although we could hardly walk inside the room, no kidding!
The next day, i insisted to change to a 2 double bed room although they said none was available for that day either. After further conversation, the manager finally let us move to the 2 double bed room considering that we were there for 6 nights. They said this 2 double bed room was only 10-20% bigger than the corner king room, but when we actually moved it was much bigger, at least thats how we felt.
This 2 double bed room was actually a downgrade from our original tiny corner king room which i thought was a joke but i guess it was because it was on the lower level, but definitely was much better. So we tried to get some credit since it was a downgrade but they said we could not since we booked it through Expedia, lame! So i asked for some compensation, after all we styed there for 6 nights, and they were able to give us a one time use of $40 breakfast credit which we ended spending more for 4 of us.
The 2 double bed room actually was a very nice size and well appointed. It only had one single window with a horizontal wooden blind but we ddnt feel caustrphobic at all inside the room. Comfortable, nice bathroom, nice shower and water pressure. The room provides the Keurig single serving tea/coffee maker along with nice selections of regular and decaf tea and coffee etc. Cant really use the fridge, its one of those thats packed with all kinds with sensors. It has a PC too which was nice but we didnt use it since we brought our own.
Location is very good, next to subway and Shake Shack! One of the best burgers ive ever had. Went there on the first night we arrived around 11 pm, and only 5 mnute line, the next day the line was around the corner :) speaking of being lucky! 2 blocks from Times Square, restaurants, shops, convenience stores were everywhere. Hells Kitchen was 1 block away.
Very nice hotel in a very good location, nice and helpful staff, very good value for the $. Despite of the rough arrival we experienced, we still enjoyed the rest of our stay very much. Definitely would return and recommend!

title: “Great Hotel...”
text:
I didnt like the location of the hotel. The hospitality was great and food within the area was perfect but a little expensive. I took Boston tour on a trolly. The trolly tour was great and like it alot. I wished I had more time to explore the city. This is historical city. The hotel has a conceige where they sell USD30.00 ticket for all city tour for 2 days. 
The hotel room was ok but the first room they assigned, the next door neighbor was smoking in the room. Then, I told the front desk about the it and they gave me a suite room. The bed was very comfortable and awesome view of the Boston. This hotel has a small indoor pool. Everything within the hotel was clean and neat. There are couple restaurants and a Starbucks in the hotel. This make it convenient for Starbuck fans!

title: “Great location but would not stay at this hotel again on return”
text: Hotel is very central which is a major positive however this really was the only upside. Our room was tiny & at first I thought our window might have been broken as there was a cold draft that was coming in that would give you the chills & the noise levels from outside was like the window was actually open. We purchased their "high speed Internet" for $15 which kept disconnecting but we brought this to their attention & we were not charged. Great location but will book elsewhere if returning to New York

title: “Don't Leave Anything In Your Room!!!”
text: My room was acceptable though slightly overpriced. My problems started after I checked out. I left a pair of boots behind and they "disappeared". I called the next day and every day after that for five days. I was given the run around by the staff, and was promised return calls which never happened. The first day I was told they only had one housekeeper and she was still cleaning rooms, but they would talk to her and call me back. They never called. The second day I was told they needed to talk to the head housekeeper but that she was off that day so they would call me back the next day. The third day I still hadn't heard anything by late afternoon so I called again! This time I was told the housekeepers had gone for the day. I was told there was no record of my previous calls, however, when this employee began to take my contact information he "found" a record of my call from the first day. I was promised by him that he would personally go talk to the housekeeper, check the storage area., and call me back the same day. He never called. I called the next day and was told he hadn't "had a chance" to check for me yet but would that day and call me back. Of course, he never called. I called again today and was told the housekeeper never saw my boots and they were not in the storage area. So I called Best Western Customer Service. They were very nice and polite, but there is little they can do as each Best Western is independently owned and operateed. Customer Service said they would e-mail the hotel with my complaint and the hotel had seven days to respond. Basically hotels are not responsible for items left behind. This is understandable. The horrible customer service I received, though, is NOT understandable. I was planning a return trip to this hotel, but after the awful customer service I received I will definitely NOT be staying there again.

title: “Beware”
text: Worst possible management: after the valet scrapped and scratched our car and the assistant manager told us to expect the problem would be taken care of later that day, it tooks ten months--47 phone calls, registered letter and emails--before being resolved; complaining to company's customer service got the same silent treatment. Even their insurance rep wanted advice on how to get Embassy Suites to return a call. Hard to believe the hotel belongs to Hilton.

title: “Fabulous stay - couldn't be better!”
text: Our stay at the Hudson was fantastic. From the moment we entered, we felt like we were in an oasis away from the frenetic pace of the city. The front desk staff were friendly and helpful and the room was serene and comfortable. The location can't be beat as it is very close to 2 subway lines at Columbus Circle, near Whole Foods (great for breakfast on the go) and is walking distance to Carnegie Hall. We've stayed at a few different hotels in the city, but the Hudson will be our "go to" place from now on. It has a beautiful and trendy bar (which is full of life especially on weekends), but the room was really quiet and we were made to feel very comfortable every step of the way.

title: “Excellent stay”
text:
We stayed here on a family summer road trip. Kids Loved it. Central Location. At one time, way way back when, this hotel used to be a Howard Johnson. Most recently it was a Radisson 
(I believe) until it was bought out and converted to a Revere Hotel. 
Its been updated to an upscale hotel. Some of the touch are borderline and not "solid" renovations BUT overall this is a very nice hotel.
The rooms were very modern, having the desk in the room was nice.
The shampoo/conditon selection in the shower was very nice. A local producer makes the products. They are for sale if you like them; we sampled quite a few and they were indeed 
worth buying.
Overall this is a nice hotel, and worth staying in. 
Not to mention its location, location, location.

title: “Great location, great people”
text:
Have to say was a little worried about some of the reviews. But there was no need to worry. Our stay here was great. It was an easy trip on the light rail and then monorail from the airport. We only had to walk a couple blocks to get to our room. Our room was comfortable- nice and big, comfortable king size bed with nice bedding. We had a fridge and micro-wave in the room. There was a bar and restaurant. The bartender, Cheryl was great!!! Everyone was helpful at the hotel and the room was always cleaned well. 
They have a couple of washer and dryers in the fitness room area - which is great when you travel light. 
We had a view of the Space Needle which was great, too! There is a lot of talk about the noise. We slept great. One night there was emergency sirens from an ambulance or fire truck, but you are in a city after all and things happen. There were a couple of homeless people in the area- but again you are in a city. I never felt unsafe. 
The monorail is right there and bus stops are all nearby. You can walk to the waterfront in 10 minutes even with your luggage. It was a great stay. I would recommend it to anyone.

title: “Very classy hotel with helpful, friendly staff.”
text:
I took my 71 yr-old Mom and 12 & 8 yr-old kids to this hotel on the weekend when NYC was hit with driving wind and torrential rain storm. I chose this hotel as a treat to my family. I was afraid the weather would put a damper in the whole experience. I was pleasantly surprise when the friendly staff greeted us warmly as soon as we enter the revolving door. After a brief checkin, we went to the room. My kids fell in love with the room right away. They love the luxurious marble bathroom, mood lighting, electronic darkening shade, large flat screen TV, iPod-ready radio and best of all, a mini-bar where everything except the alcohol is free. My mom giggled at the soft terry slippers. I was impressed by the high ceiling loft design. This hotel has the biggest rooms I've seen in NYC.
In the evening, I decided to take the family to Chinatown for dinner. Since it's raining hard, I figure we would take a taxi. Well, Wall Street is a prestigious address but on a weekend evening, taxi is hard to come by, especially in a maddening rainstorm. One of the hotel staff (the hosts) volunteered to flag down a taxi for us. He was out in the rain and the wind for 10 minutes before he successfully stopped a taxi. We felt so bad because he was all wet. But he was all smile when he held the door for us to the taxi. That's the best customer service I've seen in my many years of travel. I really appreciated the help given I had young kids and an elder with me.
All in all, the hotel is as luxurious as it advertises on the website. The staff is wonderful. The free mini-bar is a refreshing idea. This is one hotel I feel like I could stay for a while and not miss home.

title: “Do not stay here!”
text: My children and I (mom) arrived late at night and regretted once I saw the homeless/foot traffic in the area. If your activities bring you back to the hotel after dark, stay somewhere else. The room was decent but the traffice/train noise was intolerable without the t.v. being on all night. My car was broken into the second night and hotel staff didn't notify me. I found out after I checked out and started to load my vehicle at 11:20 am! It was obvious my car was broken into as customers were loading up as well. Very disappointed and will save money to stay in a pricier hotel with onsight security.

title: “Waht a mess....terrible customer care”
text: No cleaning nor fresh towels nor linens even though the housekeeping master log showed that this was accomplished.

title: “Great location with fantastic service and a great gym view”
text: The four seasons Seattle is absolutely one of my favorite hotels anywhere in the world. There service is fantastic, down to the little details like towels and water bottles in the foyer in the morning for those of us who like to go for a run. Speaking of runs, there is a great running path down along the water, which is just down the steps from the hotel. If you prefer to work out in the gym, the view across the infinity pool out to the water is amazing. Location is a short walk to a lot of restaurants and the Pike market. Clean modern rooms.

title: “Great for Business Travelers!”
text: I started staying at this hotel because it's the hotel my company used, but now I stay there any time I come to Charlotte. The hotel is beautiful and the personnel is very friendly. It's right in the middle of the downtown area, so it's really close to a lot of fun stuff.

title: “Motel from Hell”
text: This was the motel from hell! On the night of 12-29-07 hotel management lost control. A party with loud thumping music and a bunch of drunks flowed into the hallway and went late into the night. At 3 AM drunks set off the fire alarm. In the morning broken beer bottles were all over the hotel entrance and the parking lot and at least one vehicle lost a window. Management never called police. Guests were first annoyed, then mad, and then scared!

title: “The Best British Import in New York”
text: Having loyally stayed at Firmdale properties in London, we were thrilled that their only NYC property exceeded our expectations. Backed by an outstanding location in the shopping/nightlife mecca of Soho, Crosby Street is the definition of a luxury boutique hotel - sophisticated design, smart rooms, special amenities, lively bar/restaurant, and consistent service. Plus, the bathrooms have the best showers around. Of course, you pay for the experience, but Crosby Street is worth it!

title: “Lower Case W”
text:
This is not your older brothers W! I was disappointed with the quality of my stay at this W hotel. the room was mot 4 star, nor we're the facilities. I walked into my room directly into a spider web. Turned on the lights and met my freeloading neighbor with 8 legs. The room was small. I could hear the sounds of running water from the rooms above and to the side of me. Parking is $35/day and Internet $14.99.
 It is about 10 blocks from the Gaslamp and situated close to the courthouse? At night you must walk the gauntlet past the many homeles that call this part of downtown San Diego home. 
For my money there are at least 10 superior hotels in a similar price range that are closer to the Gaslamp, convention center, Petco Field, or water front. I would not reccomend unless you get a great rate or are desperate for a room in this area. I give it 2.5 - 3 stars

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text: The Hotel Burnham is the place to stay in downtown Chicago. The hotel is carefully refurbished to accent its historical significance but also has the modern conveniences of free WiFi throughout, lighting, and window coverings. Our room on the 14th floor was very comfortable and quiet. The staff is friendly and courteous from the front desk to the housekeepers. The location is perfect for sightseeing, shopping, and connecting with public transit. It's easy and inexpensive to reach the Kimpton via the Orange Line from Midway or the Blue Line from O'Hare.

title: “Great NY Hotel”
text:
We checked in late after an eleven hour train journey from Niagara. we had been upgraded to a suite which was nice, lovely to have the extra space. Air conditioning units in both rooms.Room was clean, bathroom sparkling. Bath slow to fill and shower pressure not the best.
No sign of bed bugs - (call me cynical but I am always suspicious when people only make one post).Staff very helpful - booked us a car to take us to Brooklyn cruise terminal, good price, nice driver and beautiful car.
did not have breakfast in the hotel.
Used the gym which was excellent

title: “Small, dark room and awful view compensated by location and good bed”
text: The location of the Empire Hotel is fantastic - right by Lincoln Center, easy to get everywhere, and as we have friends on the UWS, even better, so that was one of the main reasons we selected it. Another reason we chose the hotel was because it had a rooftop pool, and as my husband was going to be in meetings for the three days we were there, at the end of May, I figured I'd be using it a lot. Sadly not. Even though it should have been opened by the end of May, the bad spring weather had delayed the pool opening. It opened the day we left. That was a big disappointment. The room we got was small (common in NY), dark, and with the worst view ever - we were in the 'well' directly overlooking and just above all the AC units and piping. The noise level from the ventilation equipment is so loud that you would never open the window even if you wanted to. However, we were at the end of a long hallway, and we never heard a peep from anyone. As a result of that, the darkness of the room, and the 'white noise' from the hotel's equipment, we overslept every morning! The bed was very comfortable, the bathroom was big, although rather outdated. The decor was fine. The TV worked. We paid less than $200 a night through one of the online deals that popped up, and for this location it was fine. I am sure if you were paying rack rate you would get a lovely light room overlooking LIncoln Center. Another bonus to this hotel was going across the road to eat at Cafe Boulud for breakfast. One last comment about the hotel - my husband and I used to live in NY so we know about some of the long term residents that still exist in these old buildings. If you're walking down a hallway in this hotel and you see a little old lady sitting in her unfashionable room staring out at you, it's because she still lives in the hotel and has probably lived in it all her life - long before it became a hotel. She probably doesn't have AC, so leaving the door open means she gets to cool off from the AC in the hallway.

title: “Great Location & Friendly Staff”
text:
I wanted to base our trip out of the West Village/Greenwich Village area, and at half the price of most other NY hotels in mid-September, this one fit the bill. 
Pros: The lobby is beautiful and felt luxurious, the staff always greeted us with a smile, and the free breakfast was perfect for our appetites, with cereal, yogurt, fresh fruit, bagels, and even chocolate croissants available along with coffee, tea and orange juice. The room was always clean and the free wifi was reliable and fast. 
Cons: We were prepared for a small room, but our Double Superior room was really tiny! We made it work with some creative storage solutions. The bigger issue for us was the lack of natural light due to not having an outside facing window. It did allow us to sleep in well, but it was a little disconcerting to not see the sun until we walked outside the hotel. 
The location was incredibly convenient for access to great restaurants and shops. We had a wonderful romantic dinner at Le Gigot, a french bistro on Cornelia St., and I was glad to be near my longtime favorite bookstore Three Lives & Company and favorite coffee shop Joe, both down the street on Waverly Place. A wide array of subway lines were all very close, so we could get anywhere pretty quickly. Being away from the Times Square tourists and feeling like a part of the neighborhood were both major benefits of staying at this hotel.

title: “In a word exquisite”
text:
From the moment you pull into the courtyard, you feel as if you are arriving somewhere in Europe. Beauty can be subjective, but this is truly lovely. The artwork, chandeliers, flowers, textiles, and textures, and are true candy for your senses. The guest representative that greets you is yours from check-in, to escorting you and your luggage to your room. The rooms are luxuriously oversized, with features that will surprise you. A sophisticated lighting system, stunning lamps and sconces, beveled mirrors, an unbelievable mini-bar with, upscale treats, and a microwave discreetly hidden from view, a marble bathroom retreat with two sinks, soaking tub, separate shower, in mirror TV, IPOD dock, Juliet balconies, all rooms with gas fireplaces, luxurious bedding, textures and colors, from champagne, and platinum, to crown molding and Chanel style furniture…did I say artwork and a sparkling chandelier in the sleeping rooms, too. My husband and I were celebrating his birthday this weekend in anticipation of the official opening on Wednesday, December 9th. We did see the lovely spa, yes, more stunning sights for the senses, with twelve treatment rooms, a lap pool, men’s and women’s Jacuzzi’s, steam, and dry sauna, classroom, and a large and very impressive selection of equipment. We did experience room service, which was quite reasonably priced. The two restaurants Balsam (European bistro), and Ria (upscale dining, “where land meets sea”), and bar named Bernard’s were lovely. 
In Greek mythology, the Elysian Fields in Elysian were the final resting place of the souls of the heroic and the virtuous.
I could tell you more, but there are some things you will just have to find out for yourself.
Unconditionally recommended for all guests, both coming into town and celebrating a special occasion. I hope you get to see, hear, touch, smell, and taste for yourself soon.

title: “Great Priceline Win!”
text:
Won this hotel at the very last minute on Priceline and didn't have a
chance to find out anything about it. I was pleasantly surprised by a
gorgeous new hotel well located in the Finacial District. The lobby
was modern, beautiful, clean and busy in a good way, making you feel like a part of something exciting. The bar in the lobby and the restaurant were very good.
The room was spacious and well appointed. The beds were okay, not ultra comfortable. Also, the pillows were disappointing - not enough of them and too soft. The bathroom was great - huge with a big tub and separate shower. There was a plasma screen tv in the room, but the cheap kind with only a mediocre picture. There was not free internet in the room; in fact it was $15/day. In a brand new hotel, this in inexcusable. Also, parking is a steep $39/day, but the valets were helpful and always available. 
Room service was prompt, polite and tasty. My favorite part of the hotel, however, was the spa and fitness area. The fitness area featured brand new equiptment with individual television screens. The
weight machines were very smooth and easy to use. The pool was serene
and clean. The spa was small but lovely. My sister and I had truly great facials there. We would stay at this hotel again, any time, even at three times the price.

title: “Everything is Relative”
text:
Hyatt hotels are a safe choice as long as you behave like a smart traveler. The Grand Hyatt is in mid-town and obviously convenient to attractions in the area. It is a bustling site on top of Grand Central Station so expect to walk out of the hotel into the midst of clamoring crowds and noisy street scenes. Negotiate for a room on a high floor and emphasize your desire for a pleasant room but do not expect more than a partial view of anything since the hotel is surrounding by high-rises. The exercise room on the top floor is accessible with a room card and nicer than most hotel gyms
The bathrooms are small but the rooms are Hyatt-quality and
the hotel deserves its high rating. You can't go wrong with this facility especially if you are paying discount rates.

title: “a great stay!”
text: we stayed at the candlewood suites for 2 days and were very pleased with our choice. we found the location very ideal and the hotel itself was clean and the rooms were spacious. they offered complimentary coffee and were very helpful in booking us a taxi to take us to our cruise. its a great hotel and would highly recommend it.

title: “Not what we thought....”
text: We came to the hotel and knew it was on the marina...and the way the website looked and description read, it sounded like it was close to the beach- like walking distance. Not so much. We did drive there and it was not too far- maybe 15 minutes? The hotel has a nice tropical feel with lush gardens all over and green grass. The pool was okay, and it had a bar next to the Jacuzzi, but it closed at 9pm. What I did not like was that the room smelled like mold. I guess being located on the water it is hard to get out the dampness. The door opened to our own patio, only semi-private, for two reasons....we had to share it with the local resident ducks who begged for food and the vegetation did not cover the entire perimeter. If you stay on Shelter Island, the sidewalks roll up at 10, leaving us to drive to forage for food. (Or a nearby restaurant that was open.) We had to venture off the island to find some nightlife as well. Gas lamp quarter is very pretty, but was teeming with college students as it was Labor Day weekend. Overall, I would not be back to this location, as secluded and tropical as it is- unless I docked my own boat to it.

title: “Ideal for short solo trip”
text: I hadn't stayed here since the mid 90's. But, I had heard that it had been remodeled with new beds and bath tubs. No longer was the mattress on the floor. The service was excellent, the staff very helpful and I had a great night sleep each of my three nights. Now, the rooms are very tiny. You can barely get around the bed. But as a solo traveler it was fine. Plus the location is great and much quieter than right in the center of Times Square. What a difference a block makes. I got a rate of $169 which is an excellent value in NYC.

title: “Loved it”
text: The area was not the best but the hotel and staff were very nice and accommodated all of my tour and hotel needs.

title: “Very Hip Place to say with Positive attitudes!”
text:
I wanted to give a review since I almost canceled our stay due to the many negative ones listed on this site.
We were here to celebrate a 40th birthday. In total we had 5 rooms. We requested to stay in the same vicinity and we were all on the same floor. Requested the 2 complimentary Acura car rides which were prompt and pleasant. Requested coffee make and brought up in a timely manner. In other words, "the anything" requests were granted and we were very pleased with our experience.
The rooms were very contemporary. A bit worn but clean and comfortable (Love the bed!) I am a "Westin" girl and prefer the more traditional but I loved the "hip vibe" of the hotel lobby and atmoshere. My husband and I had a Marvelous suite with a great view of Lake Michigan and Navy Pier. It was also excellent to entertain the group before going out. Michigan Ave four blocks away so the location was pretty convenient.
Don't be frightened to give this place a try. We will certainly go back sometime!

title: “Love the Sanctuary”
text: The Sanctuary is a rather new hotel right next to Times Square. I only stay at small hotels while in NYC and the Sanctuary did not dissapoint. Highlights include a large room by Manhattan standards. The bed was very comfortable and the room was stylish without having annoying design details such as confusing bathrooms. The only thing I was not crazy about is the need to put the room key in a slot so that the lights and such work. This was a minor inconvenience.

title: “Excellent choice”
text:
Spent a great time at this hotel. In the heart of the Gaslamp Quarter, near Petco park, and Convention Center, and walking distance from nearly everything. It is a bit small property, but space is well distributed. We booked a small room, so I don't know how the bigger ones look, anyway, it was, actually, quite comfortable and roomy. Just a little noise from the street, but not a great deal (anyway, if you're looking for a peaceful relax-and-meditation-inner-peace realm, you just don't stay at a Hotel in the Downtown) 
Clean and neat bedrooms, bathroom and kitchen, specially carpets and beds, as we are both the allergic kind. Staff was great, always with a smile. My wife isn't very fluent in english, and they don't speak spanish, but really managed to help her in absolutely anything she needed. There's free internet at the lobby, and an ATM, there's also another ATM across the street. Only had valet parking, which seemed to me a little expensive, but was in fact on the average prize range for the area. Breakfast was included, served 6 to 9 on weekdays (7-9 on weekends) and there were a lot of options in the menu. I agree pool is small, in a shadowy area of the building, but we weren't gonna use it anyway. Bar at the lobby looked really good. There's a nice, familiar environment all around that makes you feel comfortable, as if you weren't staying at a Hotel at all. 150% reccomended.

title: “Be careful of credit card theft”
text: I stayed at the Kimpton on an all expense paid business trip provided by my client. The only time my credit card left my wallet while staying in NY was when I checked into the hotel,and the card was swiped for any incidentals. After I checked out and returned home to Boston, someone went on spending spree in NY utilizing my credit card number, until the fraud department of my credit card co.detected the unusal acativity and shut it down. Someone who worked at the hotel lifted the number. Travelers beware.

title: “Way Too Expensive”
text: At $249 + tax per night I would have expected a hotel where Wi-Fi and access to the gym were complimentary. But they are not, over $15 dollars for 24 hrs internet access in the room and $15 for a pass to the gym. These are unacceptable. The room was clean and comfortable but the A/C made tremendous noises every time it went on and during normal operation; this noise made sleeping a challenge. Street noise insulation is also poor. Housekeeping did not do a very good job and did not replenish the coffee and water in the room, and I had to call the front desk to request such items.

title: “Clean, comfortable, quite, but ....”
text: My room was clean, the bed was comfortable, and the hotel's area was quiet. However, I cannot recommend this Inn based on the one night I was there for two reasons. First, the Inn would not honor the reservation of my colleague who traveled with me. Apparently another guest overstayed his reservation and, with no other rooms available, the Inn would not kick out that guest so my colleague could have a room. The Inn sent my colleague to another hotel five blocks away. Second, the Inn had entirely insufficient parking. I had to park in a metered space on a busy street b/c the Inn was resurfacing its parking lot. I wish I had known about this before reserving...I would have considered other hotels.

title: “2 nights stay...very enjoyable”
text: We were here for a concert at American Airlines Center. This is very convenient and the hotel shuttle provided a ride to the arena. However, it only runs until 7 pm but we walked back, which was a very easy walk. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The hotel was clean and we enjoyed having two sinks, one in the bathroom and the other in the bedroom. This was great for two females getting ready at the same time. The continental breakfast was better than your average one. I especially liked the fact that the parking garage was attached to the hotel and you could park on the same level as your room. We enjoyed our stay and would recommend this hotel.

title: “Great boutique hotel”
text: Just 1/2 block from Times Square - this is a terrific intimate little hotel in the heart of everything! An indoor pool too. Loved this place and will stay there again on my next trip. Great staff too.

title: “Great Labor Day Weekend!”
text: My stay here was just wonderful!! This hotel is so new and fresh and my bed was very comfortable. The staff is just fantastic! Mike and Ali were so helpful with in providing transportation to the galleria. George the bartender is just great! Caroline at the front desk is so friendly and cooperative as were all the agents with whom I came into contact with this past weekend.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: The Omni Hotel in Charlotte is a great place to stay the entire staff was friendly and helpful. My husband and I were treated with honesty and respect. We have traveled to Charlotte for the Coca Cola 600 weekend for the past 4 years and never stayed in a place where we were treated like someone. I would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in the Charlotte area.

title: “Better than expected!!”
text:
We had excellent support from the whole staff. Reception, parking watch, concierge etc etc.
The Spa was excellent. The park felt like a tropical island.
Only the morning travel to the convention centre took a little long. Not enough restaurant choices near the Hotel.
Still plenty reasons to return.
Our breakfast girls Pati Muklevic and Angelica Stephens were very warm and helpfull.
Yesss good value for money and absolute candidate for a revisit.

title: “Good property at a great location”
text: This hotel is in a great location near restaurants, public transit and Michigan Avenue. Property is very clean and well maintained; staff is very courteous and rooms are comfortable. These rooms are designed with a fully-contained bathroom, as compared to many Courtyards and equivalent brands that have the sink outside the bathroom. I find the Garden Inn layout preferable, especially if you are sharing the room with others.

title: “Location is great; cleanliness is lacking.”
text:
I had read the previous reviews before booking this hotel. I was able to get a steal on the room, so I planned ahead and brought antibacterial wipes. The staff was wonderful, the location cannot be beat. My son and I were able to walk everywhere, we were so close to it all.
Other reviews were right, the hotel is dated, but who cares, we weren't in the room that much. The bathroom needed a cleaning... what is with all the hair??? It was everywhere in the bathroom! Plus had to clean some urine off the toilet seat... ick. Also, the blanket on the bed had obvious dirty areas. Had not been changed/cleaned?
My son found items on the floor of the room... old maps of NYC, candy wrappers, and worse of all, a previous guest's medication. Yes, he found capsules on the floor.
Our room was actually spacious, two double beds with two bathrooms. Wonderful. But it was facing the building next door on a low floor. There was no sunlight. The room was pitch dark at 10 am.
I'm not sure if it was the location of the room, but there was constant noise all hours of the night, almost sounded like banging of pipes??? Maybe from the alley below? Unsure. Didn't get much rest.
I put that I would recommend this hotel to a friend, but with reservations: be prepared to clean, and PLEASE check the floors for items, especially if with small children.
And as I said... you CANNOT beat the location. It's a toss up for me if I would go back.

title: “Wanted to love it - but inconsistent.”
text:
We stayed here for four nights and while some things were positively brilliant, other things really disappointed. The art and photography makes this place different than most, and we had a look at the photos on a few different floors just to appreciate it. We did have to laugh as the content of much of the work is quite adult -- no problem with us, but we seen details of a 'children stay free' promotion and thought it might have been a bit of a challenge in that instance. I am sure the artwork in various rooms makes this just fine, however.
Other positives for us: we ate in the restaurant twice - once for dinner and once for breakfast - and had an excellent experience both times. (And if you don't fancy their breakfast, Top Pot Donuts & Coffee is a nice little walk away and far nicer than the gazillion chain shops you'll pass on the way.) Very nice beds & bedding. Elevator seemed to be set to never stop on the way, which provided it isn't busy, is cool. Not once did I have to feel guilty because there wasn't room for someone else due to my luggage.Some days, very attentive and friendly staff on the door. 
The disappointments: when we checked in, we were sent to a room that was still occupied. It wasn't as awkward as it could have been, and we were quickly given a new room, but the experience was a bit worrying. Parking is a general problem in downtown Seattle -- the hotel has secure, valet-only parking for $25 a day, or there is a pay lot directly across the street that could be a little cheaper if you wanted to feed meters and pay each time you move the car. Some days, the staff on the door didn't acknowledge our presence, whether we needed help or not.
I totally dig what they want to be...I guess I just thought for the price we paid that it would actually live up to it. Some days yes, other days not at all.

title: “Perfect location, great hotel”
text: Stayed for 3 nights with family over Easter weekend. Really couldn't have asked for more. The location is perfect for a tourism trip with the White House, Lincoln Memorial, Washington Monument and many museums a short to medium length walk away. The Capitol took a cab ride but I suppose we could ahve walked. The hotel itself was very nice and was a good value at around $200 per night. The indoor pool is as good as you could expect from a city hotel and my 7 year old seemed very happy with it. The JW Marriot also has a good gym. Highly receommend this hotel to leisure travels especially those with kids and looking to hit a lot of the tourist spots in a few days.

title: “Practically perfect in most every way”
text: I am reluctant to submit by review of Hotel Newton for fear that it will become so popular that it’s reasonable room rates will skyrocket and rooms will be difficult to secure. But, that would be selfish. We spent Christmas week as Hotel Newton and it was one of the most pleasurable hotel experiences we’ve had. First, the pros: Immaculate, spacious rooms (we had two adjoining suites); great beds, prompt attention by the staff to any and all requests; excellent location (safe neighborhood, 1/2 block to subway, great bus service (96 Crosstown gets you to east side in minutes and 104 will get you both south and north), drug store and wonderful café next door); friendly staff (Charles & Eduardo are singled out). We never had any problem with the elevator as some have mentioned. Now the cons: Nothing…not a single thing. The only thing I missed was having a robe, and I can certainly live without that! I have spent 4x as much for hotels in NYC and consider some of them inferior to Hotel Newton. I look forward to coming back.

title: “Great place”
text: My stay here was AWESOME! I loved staying here. I had never stayed here before and wasn't familiar with the surroundings, but I am glad i stayed here and no where else. The front desk clerk, Mie, really made me feel welcomed and was very helpful. I love her personality.

title: “The Westin service always exceeds my expectations.”
text:
I asked for a city/mountain view - - i got it. In a weekend that had wedding people, U2 people, and conventioneers.... the Westin accommodated me.
The heavenly bed in every Westin gives me a sense of comfort and stillness the minute I jump on....
Staff went above and beyond to help a distressed bride find important items the morning after. No request was ignored or silly. Very professional people are found here!

title: “Worst. Service. Ever. Stay at your own risk!”
text:
We recently stayed at The Bristol for a high school reunion being held in their ball room. Not only was it my reunion, but also the first night away from our precious newborn son, we were looking forward to a night away and sleeping in for the first time in four months! :) Both the ball room and our hotel room were nice enough, but the customer service was appalling. As it was our 20th reunion and we were seeing friends we had not seen in years we were told about the hotels "no party policy", but told we would be able to socialize as late as we like in the hotel lobby as it was two floors below the nearest hotel room. And just to clarify "socialize", I was giggling with old girlfriends while sitting on a couch in the lobby, not yelling, screaming and running up and down the halls. After following these guidelines, and catching up with friends in the lobby as requested, I returned to my hotel room (where my husband was sound asleep) to a party being broken up by security across the hall. I entered my room only to receive a knock on the door moments later by a security guard saying we were being evicted. When I asked why, she said she had received complaints about a party in our room. When I invited her in to see that my husband was sleeping and had been for hours and that I was just returning from the lobby, she said it didn't matter and left. Within an hour two police were knocking on our door to evict us!!! When we asked for an explanation we were told they could evict whomever they chose for any reason and they did not need to give an explanation. Really?!?!?! When we asked for their names, they refused to give them, which to me is an automatic admission of fault. The worst part is that the group having the party across the hall, also alumni, had received multiple visits from security and we later found out they were not evicted.
We chose to wait a day to contact administration to cool off a bit, as we were understandably upset. The way the situation was handled by the management was equally, if not more appalling. We were hung up upon by management on our first call, the administrative assistant at the main office refused to give us the email of the president, as the one online was no longer valid, and when we finally received a response by those in upper management, we were threatened not to post a review in travel blogs. So....I am taking a risk by writing this review, but advise potential guests to stay at their own risk.....you, too may receive a knock on your door to be evicted for no reason.

title: “Great place to stay, highly recommend”
text:
This was a nice, newly remodeled Holiday Inn Express that was elegant and clean.
The staff was friendly. They recognized me as a Priority Rewards Gold Member, and we got some freebies for that.
The pool and the hot tub were great.
One minor tweak: No towels at the pool. We had to go back to the room and get our towels.
The complimentary hot breakfast was delicious and plentiful.
This is a great place to stay if you're passing through San Antonio, headed west. It's on the northwest side of town, and staying there frees you from the downtown crowds.

title: “Didn't meet my expectations”
text:
I stayed here for valentines day with my girlfriend. We opted to get the Concierge Lounge Access.
The room: Clean and roomy, but it had a musky smell that bothered me. I turned up the A/C so the smell disappeared. The room was missing it's robes and toothbrushes. I noticed that at the Hilton toothbrushes are available upon request and it was nice they had it in the room. Called the front desk and it took them 15-20 min to bring upstairs, which was much longer than expected.
Bathroom: One bathtub and one shower, which I thought was very cool. The tissue box had some sort of nice setup of tissues on top, but once I took those off there was two tissues left on inside the box. This wasn't an issue until I needed them to blow my nose later in the evening. The bathroom is very clean and bright. 
Pool: The pool was pretty small and I think it was 3' 6" deep. After seeing the pool I walked away in my swimming trunks back to the room. It's understandable that hotels in downtown LA don't have the space for large pools. 
Lounge/concierge access: Well worth the extra cost! At 5-9 there are wines, beers, and spirits available. It's open bar so you can drink to your hearts content while relaxing in a large clean room with a nice view outside. The wine tasted okay, there was whiskey, vodka, and congac. Those basically cover my three favorite spirits. They had Heineken, Sapporo, and Corona. There was plenty of munchies to go along with all the alcohol. If you like to drink and relax then opt for this package.
Service: For some reason I didn't like the front desk service. I wasn't greeted properly when checking in or checking out. Sort of felt robotic to me and I was almost offended that I didn't get the same greeting as the gentleman in front of me. It was almost as if my age or race had something to do with the level of service I would receive. On the other hand the valet staff and doorman was very friendly. 
I stayed here instead of at the Kimpton because I chatted with their online rep. She managed to convince me to give Omni a try, which I did and was a bit disappointed at their level of service. I understand that it was valentines day and it might be busy, but I stayed at the Hilton Huntington beach last Valentines day and the service was as good as any other day. Will I stay here again? It's hard to say no because the value was very good, but what turns me off was service, which I less than what I expected from the number one rated hotel in Downtown Los Angeles.

title: “Loved the Heartbreak!”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights at the Heartbreak hotel, and really enjoyed our stay! If you are an Elvis fan you must stay at the Heartbreak!
The room I had was very large, comfortable and clean. They have an airport shuttle and also a shuttle going to Beale street in downtown Memphis at night, during the day we used the Sun studio shuttle to visit the other attractions in Memphis. These were always on time and are very convenient for those that do not rent a car!
The Front Desk/Staff were helpful and the heart-shaped pool is very nice!! They also offer continental breakfast, which was good.
Not to mention Graceland, that is right next to the hotel!

title: “Worst Ever!”
text: I booked this hotel on the internet and I was skeptical from the beginning. I wanted something on the beachfront but all others were booked so I called the Blue Sea and felt better about booking it after speaking to the reservations manager. I should have gone with my first instinct. From the moment we stepped into the elevator from the underground parking garage, I knew we were in trouble. The elevator was dirty and smelly. As we got out on the third floor the carpet was dingy and the halls had an awful smell. Then when We walked into our "queen" oceanfront room, WHAT A DISAPPOINTMENT! Small is an understatement. Tiny is more like it and for the price I had to pay, it wasn't worth a third of that. There was only two of us and we were constantly in each other's way. No room to move and the bed was only a double, not queen. It was smelly, dingy and overall, disgusting. If this is considered a three-diamond property I'd hate to see their one-diamond. It was a total waste of money. The ONLY good thing was the view, which is a given anyway. Afterall, it was facing the ocean. We walked up the beach and found a "great" place that had a vacancy and it was $30 a night cheaper and the room was HUGE. It was beautiful! We went back to the Blue Sea and reluctantly stayed one night and moved over to this other place, that was UNBELIEVABLE! The Blue Sea is terrible. If you're considering beachfront and don't care about the room or the money, book it. But take this advice, don't waste your time, you'll be COMPLETELY disappointed and ripped off.

title: “bissystrax”
text: stayed at this hotel for 6 nites, absolute fab, staff were very helpful and friendly, where else would you get the heating in your room switched on for you and your bed turned down after a hectic day sight seeing or in my case shopping, just fantastic, will deffo be back :-)

title: “Great experience”
text:
I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again. My last trip I stayed across the street at the JW Marriot.
Location is great for getting around Union Square. The only complaint I have was the gas line in front of the Hotel broke and I couldn't get back into my room for a couple of hours(the whole block was closed down) but I can't blame the Hotel for it.

title: “It has potential, but they have a long way to go”
text:
Pros: Great Location, lush beautiful landscaping.
 The kids had a great time in the heated pool.
Cons: 
1.Understaffed; we called several times before anyone answered. We didn't even get an answering service, the phone rang and rang.
2. We got there late and had dinner at the Barefoot cafe 25 minutes before closing, one of the restaurants on their property. We were urged to be quick by the hostess and server they were eager to leave on time. THe server was impatient taking our order and kept clicking his pen and sighing. THe seat cushions,( without any cushion whatsoever) were absolutely filthy! My tomato bisque soup tasted like pasta sauce and we paid $78.00 for two kids mac and cheese a bowl of soup and an fish entree. 
3. The shower still had hair from whomever used it before us and the showerhead had very low water preasure.
4. The entrance door to the room is glass with a very thin white curtain that you can see through, so you will be wakened every morning by the blazing light.
5. The walls are not sound proof! We could hear our honeymooner neighbors getting busy every night! His coughing kept him up all night and us too!!

title: “Can't wait to go again”
text: After reading some of the negative comments on trip advisor about the Hyatt Islandia we were a little hesitant about staying there. We even considered cancelling our reseration. We're so glad we went. When we called to make reservations, we were told that the hotel was undergoing some extensive renovations: there was only one restaurant open and the pool area was closed. However, the hotel did make arrangements for pool use at two other locations. When we arrived, we were very pleased. Yes, there is construction but it didn't affect our stay at all. We had a BEAUTIFUL room on the 9th floor of the tower. It had just been redone. All new carpeting, furniture, bathroom, towels etc. The view of the water was gorgeous from our patio. The entire staff was pleasant and helpful. If we had one complaint, it would be that you must valet park your car. At $15.00 per day plus tip we think that's too pricey. Hopefully, when the renovations are complete, the hotel will have free self-parking available. We'd stay at the Hyatt Regency Islandia in San Diego in a heartbeat!!

title: “Simply Fantastic”
text: We found this place somewhat by accident and initially chose it based solely on its location (proximity to where we needed to be) and price range. We simply could not have been happier with our choice and can't wait for a reason to go back! This hotel has an updated "metropolitan" style and our room was a corner room, making it extra spacious. The bedding was to-die-for comfortable and I wished we had more time to just hang around in the room. Normally, I don't want to sit around in hotel rooms, but this place was just so enjoyable. The staff was outstanding from the valets, to the bell staff, desk staff, and bar staff . (There is a martini bar in the hotel, just off the main lobby which was absolutely delightful and has a great happy hour!)

title: “Best trained staff I have ever met!”
text: We stayed for a weekend at Hotel 1000, chosen from the internet and chosen based on reviews. We couldn't have been happier. For me, a manager with 30 years experience, the stand out for me was the quality of the staff. From our check it with Alyssa, it was clear that staff training is a high priority for Hotel 1000. Alyssa gave us maps and advice, as well as a glass of sparkling wine to welcome us. The staff in the restaurant were similarly helpful, knowledgeable and friendly. Sandra was particularly helpful. The Hotel itself is lovely and perfectly located. And, when leaving, the valet brought our car around and he'd taken out our empty coffee cups and diet Coke bottles and replaced them with fresh bottled water. Professional in every way.

title: “Lots of kinks, lots of potential”
text:
I planned a girl’s long weekend with 5 friends who flew in from around the country. We had a terrific time, but there were some serious hiccups along the way that marred the experience. I made our reservation several months in advance, and was told that Travaasa would charge one night for each of the 3 rooms I booked at the time of booking. When I checked my credit card a few weeks later, I found that they charged me for the total experience, instead of the just the lodging and classes I had booked...which was three times the amount they were supposed to charge me. Once I called, they apologized and refunded the overcharge to my card. I told the representative that this error made me nervous, since sight unseen I had convinced my friends to fly to Texas for this trip, and I didn't want things to go wrong. I was assured this was an isolated incident, and they would work to make sure everything would be wonderful.
When we arrived the resort was very attractive, and the pool was lovely. Our rooms were not in the building I had reserved because we were told it was being remodeled. It would have been nice to have been contacted about this. There was a big variance in the size of the rooms, despite all being the same price, and some people were not happy to have such a small space. 
We enjoyed the setting, the classes, the pool, and spa. The spa treatments were outstanding and facilities were lovely. The food and service were above average at the restaurant, but the hours were very limited and even the bar closed by 9:00 or 10:00 pm. Because the resort is so far out and roads are windy and dark, it's not optimal to go to an outside restaurant or bar late at night. The housekeeping service was spotty. Twice rooms were not cleaned, and we had to request for housekeeping to come. They left cookies in one room but not in the other two on one occasion, and on two other occasions they left one cookie in rooms with two guests...were we supposed to share the cookie? The topper was our last evening, when the single cookie left in our room appeared to have a bite taken out of it. We thought it was so ridiculous that we took a picture of the half-eaten cookie wrapped in a pretty bag with ribbon.
The real problem started our last evening, when we tried to do an early checkout, since several members of our party had crack of dawn flights and we were leaving very early the next morning. To call the night front desk staff incompetent would be an vast understatement. All six bills were incorrect, and they didn’t seem to be able fix them, even after 45 minutes of explaining. They asked that we come back in the morning, when the day staff was there. So we woke up extra early to try and fix the errors, but they still couldn’t figure out the problems. We had to leave to make flights, but we were assured that the accounting staff that came in at 9:00 am would be able to rectify all the issues and they promised to email us the corrected bills. Only one person received a bill. Two others had their credit cards charged the wrong amount. It took several phone calls and emails over a couple week period to get it all straightened out. Three of the emails I sent to Travaasa staff went unanswered. I was really embarrassed that the trip I planned had these kinks my friends had to suffer through.

title: “Awesome!”
text: The baymont inn & suites is overall one of the best I have been to. The entire hotel was awesome! The only problem I had was the location. I came for the bears vs cowboys game, I thought I was close to arlington texas.

title: “Belleclaire bargain”
text: The Belleclaire is a gem and a great New York bargain. We stayed for four nights in a fifth floor family suite. Yes, they're not the largest and the heating is a trifle antiquated, but the rooms are clean, the linen fresh,and were well maintained. The staff are very friendly and helpful; though the hotel was always busy, they were never other than obliging. The situation is great: Central and Riverside parks nearby yet only fifteen minutes to Times Square, and the subway close by. Lots of shops and supermarkets nearby and I can only echo the reccomendations for the Manhattan Diner for breakfast and Nick's (round the corner on Broadway) for everything else - try the White Pizza!! You get whay you pay for - the Belleclaire is not 5* luxury but for a value place to stay in NY it measures up.

title: “No frills”
text: This hotel is clean and comfortable. The staff is helpful. It is no frills, but the price is right. It is located within walking distance to the Van Ness Metro. Parking on-site is reasonable, as well. I have stayed here many times and would do so again. The only cons is that the walls are "thin" and so at times it can be noisy.

title: “What a great find!”
text:
We were a family of 4 -2 adults & 2 kids. We booked directly with the hotel and got a better rate with them than lastminute.com! It also meant we could get all our questions answered by a human being. It makes all the difference. They were great.
We had a room on 21st floor but with the King bed it wasn't really suitable. Reception staff were most helpful and agreed to move us to a higher room which had a fantastic view of the Chrysler Building. The facilities are great - great Queen beds and a large sofabed in the sittingroom with a TV directly facing it. My son thought he was in heaven and we sometimes had to chase him out of bed and away from the TV! We used the kitchen for breakfast nearly every morning. All the staff were helpful and cheerful. 
When you first arrive the outside appearance of the hotel is initially disappointing as it is low key. However once you meet the staff and enter the lobby that disappears and it is great from start to finish.
We thought it was great value and the location is superb. A word of advice- Don't do what we did for the first few days. We always turned left on exiting the hotel...heading for Empire State and Macys direction. Make sure you also turn right..there are great restaurants on Third Avenue. 
We would definitely stay here on future trips to New York. Thank you to the staff in Affinia Dumont.

title: “Great place to stay when going to see the Indy 500”
text: This is a beautiful Courtyard prpoerty with a stunning lobby. This hotel is located rather close to the airport and was a terrific place to stay when attending the Indy 500. The rooms were standard for a Courtyard, which is to say that they are comfortable, clean and attractive. Downtown Indianapolis was only about a 10 minute drive.

title: “Great location but a bit lacking”
text: Nice hotel, you can't beat the location. So close to transport and Newbury Street etc for shopping. Also the trolley bus picks you up right at the front door. Bit disappointed that there wasnt a safe in the room or a bar fridge. The room is nice and spacious but our view was over the top of another building so not very inspiring. Would stay there again only because of the location.

title: “Essentially a Hostel at Hotel Prices”
text:
Very disappointing experience. Walls are paper thin. You can hear people cough or watch TV in rooms next door. Bed was not very comfortable. Room was musty and humid despite turning on the Air/Fan unit. AC/Heat unit was not temperature controlled. No incoming calls or messages; nor was there a clock in the room, or hairdrier, or safe. Linens and towels seemed slightly unclean. Breakfast was sugar with a side of sugar with some sugar on top: some bagels and jam, but mainly danishes and cakes. cream cheese and milk was on the table but was left out without refrigeration or ice. tables aren't cleaned by the staff, so they stay dirty after they were eaten at. 
On the plus side, it is in a great location. Room had fridge and two sinks, which was nice. Wifi and parking are included. Front desk staff are helpful.
In sum: would not recommend and would certainly not go back. You can probably find a hostel for half the price and same quality. we are not sure why this is so high on tripadvisor....(currently #11)

title: “AWESOME STAY!”
text: I would recommend this hotel to anyone with a family. This was our first time at a staybridge and definitely wont be our last. Everything about our stay was wonderful!

title: “value & comfort in san diego”
text: we stayed at the dolphin motel for 5 nights. The room was a good size, with a good bathroom, very comfortable bed, a/c and cable TV. The room was spotless and was cleaned every day. A breakfast of muffins, fruit, coffee, juice & yogurt was included. Staff were really friendly & helpful, in fact one day we were at the bus stop and the owner came out and insisted driving us to the beach and he stopped to show us a few places of interest on the way! A good location with bars & restaurants within 5 minutes walk, and if you don't have a car, like us the bus stop is 2 minutes away and links with the trolley to downtown etc. Cant imagine you will find a better place to stay for the money in San Diego

title: “Great place to stay”
text: What a joy to stay where the staff are great and extremely helpful. Rooms are very good and the location is right where you can access everything new York has to offer. Thankyou for making my first trip to NY so great. C

title: “Disappointed!!”
text: I went to New York and took my 15 year old daughter with her two cousins and my sister in law. My daughter and I stayed at Hotel Mela. Two of the nights when we returnned to our room to sleep after a wonderful day of shopping and dinner we could not stay in our room because the marijuana smell coming from another room down the hall was overpowering! We notified the desk and they said they could do nothing but move us for the night. But I am hear to say if I was at the Ritz or any other upscale hotel they would do something to take care of the people causing the problem! They would not inconvience me by having me sleep in a different room for two nights. We had to take our pajamas and toiletries and sleep in another room on another floor because the smell was unbearable. I was not excited about experiecing something like this especially on a mother/daughter trip. No compensation just inconvience for us by having us move. They made us be inconvience for the two nights that these people were staying at the hotel and smoking marijuana. No apology upon checkout, no offer to compensate for the two nights we were inconvienced. Nothing. I would say that is not good customer service or good management at all.

title: “terrible place to stay”
text: hotel breakfast was bad and made me very sick, the hotel does not look nice at all, poor view from the balcony(unless you want to see what old apartment looks like), very old and unsafe balcony, poor drainage system in both sink and shower tub, free shuttle van service is nice but waiting time is too long.

title: “Great location and good value”
text: You can't beat the location for visiting Manhattan. It's close to the subway and Penn Station, and you can walk to a lot of attractions. I needed a convenient, reasonably priced hotel for visiting the city with my 5 month old baby. Our room was small and the window looked directly into the windows of the building next door - but that also describes my first apartment in New York. The A/C wasn't working well, but a very pleasant man showed up minutes after I called and fixed it. The cafe in the lobby is great for grabbing some coffee or pastries in the morning. All in all, I was completely satisfied and would stay there again. It's not a luxury hotel. It's a clean, centrally located, relatively cheap place to sleep in Manhattan.

title: “Great for a young couple”
text: Although we were at first scared by reviews, my boyfriend and I went ahead and booked a room in this hotel anyway because of the price. We found it just fine for our needs, and the staff was actually very helpful. The room reminded me of a dorm room, which is about what we expected for what we paid. The sheets were clean and the floor was vacuumed, although perhaps prior complaints were because some little details were missed (walls were a bit dirty, dust in corners in closet etc.). Location is a huge plus. It's worth noting that the walls are a bit thin, and if you are a very light sleeper this could be a problem if you have noisy neighbors. Although the accommodations were fine for me (a young woman just out of college), I can see how people used to a higher standard might be upset by this hotel.

title: “Hospitality!”
text: We stayed in the Springhill Marriott in Indianapolis a couple of weeks ago and were AMAZED! If you need a location near downtown Indy, any of the connected Marriotts will be a prime choice. The guest services went above and beyond! We decided to "tour" the various locations since the new JW had be opened for about 6 weeks. It is beautiful, I can't wait to stay there next month for work! Each staff member smiled, and it was not a forced/fake-I am here to work and they make me smile. Guest services were fluid-you pass between brands and still are treated with respect and amazing service. My favorite person was young mother working at the front desk of the Springhill. She was there the evening and the next morning, both days with a welcoming smile and extending her assistance for EVERYTHING! The lobby, with her kind conversation and the games provided for children, and the breakfast area were our favorite hang-outs! Kudos to each employee who goes above and beyond to make our family feel genuinely welcomed and comfortable! Please hold on to the sincerity that so many other hotels seem to have lost!

title: “Perfect location”
text:
i stayed for a night at the Chancellor hotel with my parents while visiting San Francisco and was pleased with the petite accommodation. 
i will be staying there again this December which goes to show that I am happy with my previous stay. The bathrooms are good enough, and what's really amazing is that they have allotted a small room for the luggage so it does not clutter the walking space of the room.
i am looking forward to my next stay there.

title: “Hidden gem in a perfect location”
text: We stayed for 3 nights and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The location is perfect, the nearest T stop is only a couple blocks away and there is an abundance of restaurants and shopping in the area. If you're interested in taking the trolley tour, the nearest stop is only a 5-minute walk from the inn. Even though they don't provide housekeeping for stays less than 7 days, you can request one if you want it. All in all a very good experience and we'll definitely return there the next time we visit Boston!

title: “The Hotel Drisco topped all our expectations!”
text:
Bolton, England
We have just returned from our first trip to California, which incorporated two visits to the Hotel Drisco. Having seen all the fantastic reviews we felt quite secure with our booking and were pleasantly surprised to find that the Hotel and Staff exceeded all expectations!
We received a very warm welcome on arrival and had a beautiful room. Bob was extremely helpful with providing us with a map and highlighting various useful items, which was a nice touch when in a new city.
The furnishings were all beautiful and we couldn't fault anything, from the lovely oak floorboards throughout the hotel, to the lovely crisp bedding.
Every evening the Hotel holds a complimentary wine reception which was a lovely start to the evening and gave a chance to meet other guests. This is hosted by Julio, who has a fantastic knowledge of San Francisco and was able to help us with many of our arrangements. 
We spent a week touring the area then returned to the Hotel Drisco for the final few days of our holiday. It was lovely to return and we were given such a warm welcome it really felt like coming home! (We had also been upgraded to a Junior Suite which was an added bonus!) The front of house staff were all excellent and very professional, in particular Michael who helped us with a missing bag at the beginning of our stay and for whom nothing was ever too much trouble.
The position of the Hotel is great - probably the best in the City, surrounded by fantastic houses and very peaceful. It is a lovely walk down into the City and very easy to get around / back up the hills using either taxis or the local bus system, which we found to be excellent.
We wouldn't hesitate to recommend the Hotel Drisco to anyone looking for a classic, beautiful place to experience San Francisco.

title: “Very enjoyable!”
text: Ok, I read the reviews before I stayed and was actually a little aprehensive. But, I didn't find any issues at all with this hotel. I will say that I stayed on a Monday night so it may not have been as busy at the EpiCenter as it would be on a weekend but there were no noise issues at all. I found the room to be clean, quiet, and comfortable. I appreciated the complimentary bottled water in the guestroom. All the amenitites I needed were there and the staff was pleasant. I enjoyed having so many restaurant options within walking distance of the hotel. I used the fitness center and was pleasantly suprised that they offered complimentary disposable headsets to use with either your iPod or the TV system. I've never seen that at any other hotel and that seems to be the item I forget most often! The valet team was efficient and courteous. Overall, it was a great stay.
