Just keep your expectations at a reasonable level, know what the brand offers, and I don't think you'll be disappointed.

title: “The Spa and outdoor casitas were heavenly!”
text:
My husband and I decided to get away for a little staycation after a long week at work and snuck away for one night to the Rancho Bernardo Inn. Our room was absolutely beautiful overlooking the golf course so clean and very big!
We decided to use the spa and get some of the made fresh daily massage packages - the one I got was the Latin and it was absolutely heavenly! My massage therapist Jill had a very skilled hand and I left the massage revived and relaxed (oh and smelly spicy from the signature oils they blended for the custom massage.
After our spa we decided to hit up El Bizcocho and try the tasting menu, we had heard there was a new chef. The food was very creative we did a five course tasting that included the chefs using some of the most ingredients that took us back to our childhood including pop rocks and a fruit rollup that complimented the yummiest salmon!
We had a chance to enjoy the adult pool after our stay in the comfy beds and had breakfast overlooking the golf course. Service at the property was fantastic we will absolutely be back to the Inn!

title: “You can sleep here!”
text:
I stayed for 10 days in a room in the second floor. The location is not far from freeway driveway wich was an advantage for me.The hotel is obviously ageing, but the room appeared to be clean. Breakfast was simple but ok. Regular coffee was very weak, could be much stronger because they also offer caffeine free coffee.
Regarding the pool: Do not expect big sunny area around the pool. The pool is cooped up between the two wings of building and often in shade. There is not much space for sunbathing left. 
The stuff was very friendly and helpful. 
Resume: A hotel where you can go for shower and sleep without worrying about hygiene problems. For relaxing on the pool its defenetly not the right place.

title: “Never again”
text: this place was way overpriced and too dirty, there are other places that are nicer and accept pets, the bed was very uncomfortable and felt like i was sleeping on a worn out box spring without a matress, the heater is a combined wall air conditioner unit so you cannot sleep if it is on, people were fighting and cussing each other. the sliding glass door had a broken security latch. I felt like i was in the Ghetto.

title: “roadway was disgusting”
text:
Although this was awhile ago, I was prompted to write this after again searching for another stay in Philadelphia and saw Roadway reviews. This place was a living nightmare. The front door had glass missing and it was taped together. The stairway was so small, we had to wait until someone came down to go up. No elevator service, broken. The rooms were very small and there was no fire escape accessible to us. We could not sleep for fear of getting out safely. Stuffy.
The advertisement shows great location, which it is, but I would never stay here again. Above us were thirteen girls staying for a bachorlette party. This building is an old three story fire trap. Do not stay here. The price invites you in, but you may never get out.

title: “San Francisco Hyatt Regency”
text:
Recently joined Hyatt from Hilton. Checked into Hyatt Regency in San Francisco's Embarcadero area this past weekend. Wasn't sure what to expect since some of the reviews here haven't been that great. Thought I would give a quick review:
Used valet overnight @ $57 (yes I know about Embarcadero 4)
Valet and bell man were nice (didn't tip because I didn't have money at the time and no one complained, I usually make it up to them on the return anyway)
Hotel is impressive, check-in was a breeze, asked about a upgrade to suite (as Hyatt Diamond Member), Andy checked offered Embarcadero suite but he said the room they had for me was better, took his recommendation and was checked into room 1621.
Room was clean and even checked the carpets based on what other people have said, can say for sure that they are clean as is the room. View was awesome. Can see the Ferry Building, bay, etc...Happy that we took it.
Regency Club - amazing...(the reason I choose this vs Grand...where I will be staying soon)... great selection of food, view is unbeatable, 360 degree view.
Location...can't be beat this hotel is across the street from the Ferry Building, near muni and bart...and of course all 4 embarcadero buildings. Check out the Farmer's market in the Ferry building on Sat morning for a great experience. Directly across the hotel is some cheap restaurants, small drug store, fast food. Also occupy wall street stuff by the fed building was not noticeable at all.
Liked this Hyatt.
Will be staying at the Hyatt Scottsdale next...hopefully they are as good

title: “JANETTE”
text:
Although I am still at the Ramada Inn Lake Shore, I just wanted to acknowledge the quality customer service I received from a young woman named Janette when my wife and I checked in yesterday. In a world where good customer service is the exception, not the rule, it was a refreshing break to encounter a person who was courteous, friendly, knowledgeable of her position and thoroughly willing to insure that the person of the other side of the counter from her received the best possible experience at her particular that could possibly be had. Hat's off to Janette.
On the other side of the fence, this is the second time I've tried to submit this review because the internet service is not good. The signal fails constantly and it is extremely slow. I guess its an electronics thing with this hotel because the television reception is not good either...especially for cable. Many of the channels have a lot of "snow". 
But, overall, thus far, the stay has been good. Janette's service overshadowed the problems I'm having with the electronics in the room. I'll comment more at the end of my stay.

title: “Above and BAYond Location / Service”
text:
Located just off Union Sq, this boutique hotel has all the amenities needed
to be comfortable in San Francisco (internet, laundry, local phone)
PLUS the knowing and gracious mgmt of Rodel.
Whatever u need, wherever u want to go, he is an excellent source
and sets the tone for a wonderful stay in the city.

title: “Good, solid hotel choice”
text:
Very happy with hotel choice - just a 10 minute walk from Union Station if you turned right/right exiting the lobby; turning left took you past a Hilton and Holiday Inn directly over to the Capitol.
Oh and there's a Starbucks just across the street.
Front desk staff were very welcoming and helpful; hotel is a little dated and the marble lobby reminded me of Trump Towers! 
Room was fine; again a little dated but very comfortable beds; TV reception wasn't the best and beware if your room is an 'adjoining' type, as you can hear your neighbours TV and all else. Even a row of pillows along the gap at the bottom of the door couldn't muffle the neighbours TV and conversation.
Staff, from the front desk, doormen and chambermaids, were very friendly; no problem getting a taxi as the doorman would instantly magic one up. 
As the hotel was only 10 minutes walk from Union Station; used the excellent Metro service to get around DC and walked to/from hotel in daylight hours. However, I preferred to take a taxi at night - yes, there are homeless people around the Union Station/Postal Museum area and just thought it wiser to use door-to door transport at nightime.
Had absolutely no problems though, if I got a good deal would definitely stay at the Washington Court again.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
Room was nice, looks like it was recently updated, very clean. Breakfast was great with a large selection to choose from.
Gym was clean with mostly everything you would need. 
The entire staff was very friendly, and the door man was great!

title: “Fabulous Stylish Hotel, Great location. Would stay again.”
text:
I can not speak highly enough of the Hotel Affinia Shelburne, Lexington Ave. LIke everyone, after hours and hours of trawling the internet, reading review after review I was struggling to find a hotel to book, there are soo many to choose from. We came across the Affinia reveiws and I have to say they were by far the best. We took the plunge and booked hoping for the best. The best it turned out to be!. The hotel, the staff, the cleanliness, amenities were all top knotch. It was my birthday and I emailed in advance to politely ask for a room with a view and to our surprise we were given room 1120 with the most amazing view of the Empire State. The rooms are a fantastic size for New York. There is a fantastic view also from the Rooftop bar (closed winter) but we went up anyway, great pics.
Reception were fantastic, concerige helped us with places to Eat. We ate at Serge, a little romantic, well priced french restaraunt just up the road and had amazing steak. We also highly recommend PIPA Tapas Bar, stunning place just a short hop on a taxi in Gramercy. Very popular place. That was the highlight of our trip! Breakfast we ate just right out of the hotel at Bloomers diner, amazing food! 
The hotel is very well located, Lexington and 3rd have loads of places to eat and bars, supermarkets are dotted round too. Times Sq was 10 mins walk, empire 5 mins. We spent alot of time in Bryant Park on 42nd, nice place to chill with a coffee and watch the world go by.
We are booking for next year, same time, same place. Thanks Affinia Shelburne.

title: “Well taken care of”
text: It's very close to Southern Methodist University and Northpark Mall. I was hesitant to stay reading some reviews but needed to be close to ferry my daughter to and from the university and the clinic for her injured knee for 5 days. Agree the hotel corridors are a little shabby and I did find a mouldy water bottle under the desk when I checked into the room. Yes, we are diamond members etc used to staying in amazing hotels but I gave this hotel 4 stars for accomodating all our requests. I had asked for an accessible room but needed 2 beds so was moved to the 7th floor. Not great views but except for the mouldy bottle, the room was clean and the beds very comfortable. Housekeeping brought up the small fridge I requested very quickly. The room was cleaned nicely every day. A bright light in this hotel was the breakfast room - plentiful and varied food and the staff was extremely helpful to my daughter on crutches.(BTW, the waffle was in the shape and the size of Texas - like a double portion - they make it for you when you request it and it was delicious!). The staff was friendly and attentive every morning we had breakfast there. On day 2, I saw the reception desk had a large bowl with delicious red apples but that was gone by the following evening and disappointingly not filled again. Its these little touches that will help to make this a really good hotel. Free parking was a bonus (compared to $24 p day valet at Hilton Park Cities).

title: “Convenient, Relaxing and Friendly”
text: I visit DC regularly but this was my first stay at the Madera. Overall, I would give this hotel high marks. The staff was extremely friendly and the location right off of Dupont Circle was very convenient. The room showed a little bit of age but was nicely appointed and beautifully decorated in a very upscale fashion. Many of the rooms have balconies overlooking the street below. There is a restaurant (Firefly) in the hotel and although I didn't eat there, it seemed to be rather popular. Also, this is a pet friendly hotel, which I always consider to be a plus. The price I paid was OK, but if you can find good internet deals I would probably pick Hotel Palomar or Jury"s Washington first. If nothing was available for a reasonable price at either of those, then Hotel Madera would definitely be my next choice.

title: “Improvements needed for this class of a hotel”
text: The only reason I gave this hotel a 3 was the service. I found it to be very good, especially the bell hops and valets. The cons are numerous, including the confusing layout of 5 towers and trying to navigate to the food court area where the elevators do not stop. The room space was wasted due to the circular walls. The room carpet was stained, the beds were excessively bouncy, and were short. I am 6'2" and my feet hung over the end. The availability of the food court (clearly mentioned in the hotel's guide found on room's desk) was nice. However, I was not impressed with the hotel and would not recommend it to Los Angeles travelers.

title: “Well worth it”
text: The Hotel is a very nice place to stay if you have buissness on the Uppewr East side... If not it is a bit out of the way. The rooms are nice and large. Very comfortable. The decor is OK but not fancy. Beds are comfortable, clean and well maintained.

title: “Great location - Best value for money”
text:
This hotel is just awesome. The modern European design and the young dedicated multi-cultural staff make the stay most comfortable. The rooms are well decorated and offer any amenities. The food is great starting with breakfast, thru Lunch up to the happy hour (nice bar and fancy drinks) and dinner. 
Then of course the location. Nice shops and restaurants around in a walking distance and of course the Metro Station offers you easy and fast access to any point of interest.
Finally: Internet access is free!

title: “Excellent location and staff; tidy rooms”
text: Helpful staff. Small but very tidy and quiet room. Great location right near the subway, Central Park, and Museum of Natural History.

title: “GREAT hotel!”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights. I have no complaints. The room was clean. Beds were super comfortable. Housekeeping came whenever needed. And with it being right near the airport, it was surprisingly not loud AT ALL. It was actually pretty cool to be able to see the planes landing. Bonus... there is a McDonald's right in front of the hotel (much better than paying for the expensive breakfast in the hotel). Overall, I'd recommend staying at Holiday Inn LAX. Although, I would NOT recommend eating the hotel food. Way overpriced and not very tastey at all.

title: “Above expectations”
text:
Was a bit cautious when I reserved a room, both because I'm wary of motels and didn't like the photos of the neighborhood on Street view. 
Turns out, the location is great. It's not the best neighbourhood in LA, but it seems safe and there's both a hypermarket and various shops ±50 meters. Plus, lots of great Thai restaurants nearby. But most importantly, LA metro's red line is ±100 meters away. So, for example, if you're coming to LA for a tradeshow downtown, this location is perfect unless you want to pay the exorbitant prices they charge at downtown hotels.
As for the property itself - it was clean and quiet, no sanitary problems except a very noisy and somewhat inconvenient shower, but there was plenty of hot water. The room isn't the largest I've been at, but it's not uncomfortably small either, there's a pool and a jacuzzi outside (Haven't used), and the hotel managers are both friendly and helpful. 
Overall, would warmly recommend to business travelers.

title: “Don't believe all you read, I almost did”
text:
I booked the room for 2 nights, then started reading reviews and i was horrified by them. But i still kept my reservation and I am glad that I did. The staff is friendly and helpful. Upon entering the room, I noticed no coffee maker, and i live and breath coffee. I called the front desk and with in 15 minutes, one was brought to my room. It is not a 5 star resort, but for a 3 star it is great. The room was clean and bug free (including bed bugs). I took precautions by buying travel space bags and trash bags to put everything personal in. I kind of feel stupid that I did, but protective measures are never stupid. 5 star hotels in New York have bed bug problems. The room I had did not have a problem at all.
The package deals you get on the internet are great. I got the splash, bed and dinner package for 2 nights. It included dinner for every night for all 4 of us, at either restaurant. You have a grill or bar type restaurant. The grill had a buffet or a menu. A 9.95 limit on the dinner, per person, but the restaurants are not expensive and we all ate for the 9.95 or under. The package also included a breakfast buffet for the 2 morning, for all 4. And we brought our own snacks and soda.
Yes, the water is cold in the water park, but alot of outdoor waterparks in the summer have cold water. Heck, that goes for swimming pools and my pond at home. The air temperature is pleasant in the waterpark and if your not into the slides but the kids are, bring a book, park yourself in a chair and the kids will have a blast. They also have activities through out the day at the resort that are not water related, so there is plenty to do.
So, don't always judge a place by reviews. If you noticed most of the reviews are from people who had bad experiences. People usually dont write reviews when they have a pleasant experience, the just pass it along by word of mouth. But a bad experience and they want the whole world to know and feel sorry for them.

title: “A bit cramped but a nice hotel at a good location”
text: My wife and two kids stayed one night on the 22nd of December, 2011 in room 903. We booked through hotels.com. I had read that there were some poor reviews regarding cleanliness, but did not find that to be consistent with our room or lobby area. The lobby offered free coffee. The suite had a full sized fridge with microwave, plates, utensils, etc. -- all the stuff you'd normally expect in a suite. There was a pull out sofa bed, and a flat screen tv in the bedroom as well as the sitting room. The thermostat was a bit antiquated as there was no digital setting or any kind of gauge - you just had to set it and decide it it was warm or cool enough and modify your settings based on that measurement. The beds were soft - a bit too soft for my taste but possibly suitable for others. The whole suite (especially the bedroom and bathroom) felt as if it was built for smaller furniture but felt cramped with the furniture in it. The doors always seemed to be in the way, but otherwise everything else was fine. The hotel is just a few minutes walk to the Foggy bottom metro stop. There is also several (almost fast food type ) restaurants ( we ate at the mediterranean restaurant - Rito (I think) and it was quite good) and a whole Foods store and cafe two blocks away. The neighborhood seemed to be quiet and safe. We left our electronics in the room and there were no incidents. The sheets were soft and clean (and white) and the towels were very soft and fluffy.

title: “Great hotel! great location!”
text: This is a great place to stay in LA. Very good location. Hotel is clean, hip and quiet. The staff are excellent. Friendly. Helpful. The restaurant is great. Had a really good stay and will be back again for sure. I highly recommend this as a place to stay when in LA.

title: “Good Location, Nice Hotel”
text: Very pleasant and polite staff, hotel is a little worn but clean and comfortable. Breakfast buffet is great with hot and cold offerings including eggs and waffles. Hotel is very close to the Longwood area with Boston's important hospitals including Brigham & Womens, Childrens, and Dana Farber. A free shuttle service is offered to hospitals and to the airport. If you need a place to stay during a loved one's hospitalization or are coming to Boston for treatment, this hotel is a good choice.

title: “Cozy elegant place in the perfect location”
text:
We spent 6 days at St Botolph's, enjoying it very much. My husband attended a conference at Copley Place, which was 3 minutes from the hotel, and there was also plenty to do for me and our 1-year old daughter. Playgrounds and parks, shopping malls, restaurants, Boston's landmarks - all within a walking distance. We loved the accommodation, it was very convenient to have your own kitchenette, a separate living room, a big TV - especially if you are with a little one and have to cook for her and entertain her ;) Breakfast lounge - also a big plus, with great coffee, bagels, muffins and whatnot. The guys in the office were super friendly and eager to help.
Even on a cold and rainy day we were glad because we could quickly get to Copley Place with all shops and restaurants to keep us busy. 
All in all, this hotel was a wonderful alternative to regular huge chain hotels, both in terms of convenience and price. And it was so much better to spend these days in Boston in an apartment in a nice old house instead of characterless hotel room.

title: “Just Perfect !”
text:
Spent a week here with my cousin, on a leisure trip, between 20-26 May. 
First place, excellent location: just between 5th & Broadway, 10 minutes walking distance from Times Square, Penn Station. There´s a subway station just off the hotel !
All the crew is very helpful, from the front desk to the belhops...they helped a lot explaining routes, calling cabs, storing luggage, etc. 
Rooms: Fine - two medium size beds, lcd tv, carpet, regular bathroom. Not big..but enough. 
There´s a restaurant you can acessa through the front lobby, where you can have breakfast (USD 16/person), grab somthin´quick to eat.
There´s also a shop in the lobby, where one can get everything from souvenirs, water, soda, snacks, to simple medicine (like aspirin), and even set a car to the airports ! Really helpful !
This hotel is perfect for tourists - especially if in large groups - and families not expecting luxury !
Would definitely recommend !

title: “They treated me well.”
text:
I was traveling for business, and staying for 2 months. The staff treated me very well during my extended stay. The hotel offers a great shuttle service. They were able to get me to my training, local shopping and food. 
The front desk staff of Melissa, Shemekia and Mike were a great help to me. They gave me a few great options for food and entertainment. Mike even was able to get me signed up for the Hilton Honors program.
All in all this was a great place. If I am every back to the Seattle area, I will choose to stay here again.

title: “Charming hotel, great location”
text:
We stayed here for 10 days in the summer. We chose the hotel mainly because it seemed to offer a great central location, got good reviews and wasn't too expensive... a good quality mid range hotel.
And it lived up to expectations.
The location was the best aspect, on 6th avenue, just a few blocks from Times Square, a couple of blocks from the Rockerfeller Centre and a few blocks from Central Park. It was near subway and bus connections too. Perfect for us as we wanted to get out and about in New York.
The lobby was relatively small with only a small lounge area. But there was a good restaurant and bar. We didn't really use these though as we preferred to head out to the many eating/drinking places nearby.
The staff were friendly and helpful.
The accommodation wasn't the best but it was perfectly clean and adequate. That suited us as we didn't want to spend a lot of money on hotel accommodation that we weren't going to spend a lot of time using.
Anyway it suited us just fine. Perfect for exploring New York without costing a fortune.

title: “Better Than Expected!”
text: From the outside, because of the neighborhood and the older, worn appearance of the building, the property might look less than appealing. But staying here was actually a good experience and the hotel had many great features. The room was very clean, attractive, and well kept. The view from our balcony, 5th floor back side, was beautiful - the city with bay and bridge in the distance. (I paid twice as much for a room at the Hilton Union Square and my room looked out on a wall.) The location was excellent - 1/2 block from the Broadway entrance to Chinatown, which meant great entertainment and food right outside your door, and within 1-2 miles of the Fisherman's Wharf area and the downtown higher end shopping & business district. The free parking was fantastic and the room had the basics such as a coffee pot, hair dryer and Wi Fi. I came to this hotel after staying at the Hilton all week at a conference and although it's not fancy, it met our needs nicely and for those on a budget, we would give it a thumbs up.

title: “Quiet relaxing hotel in the big apple!”
text:
This hotel is in a great location only 5 minutes walk from Penn station and 15 mins from Times Square.
The room was large by New York standards and tastefully decorated with a king bed, fridge and microwave. The best thing for us was how quiet our room was, we had a front facing room on the 19th floor.
We also loved being on a quiet street, as New York is frenetic!
We did not eat at the hotel, so can't comment on the restaurant.
I would definitely stay here again and would like to thank the hotel staff , who were friendly and helpful at all times.

title: “Great location for a Chicago Getaway”
text: My wife and I stayed at theWit the Sunday before Christmas to enjoy downtown Chicago before the holiday and finish up some shopping. The location is pretty central to everything... Michigan Ave, Millennium Park, Marshall Field's (I know it's now Macy's but wish it wasn't) on State St., theater district, etc. The corner room was a little narrow between the bed and the dresser / desk, but it was comfortable, quiet and had a nice view of the Chicago River. They have a terrific bar on the top of the hotel with outdoor decks that would be great in warm weather, and good fitness center. Had breakfast in the restaurant off of the lobby - great service and good food! The only downside is the hotel does not have a lot of room out front to handle cars. We have already recommend theWit to several friends, and will definitely stay again!

title: “Great hotel, great location!”
text:
This is a small, modern boutique hotel located just one block from Chicago's magnificent mile. I couldn't have picked a better location for a quick overnight stay in Chicago. We were upgraded to a suite and it was just perfect.
The staff were wonderful--gracious and courteous. I usually don't consider my experiences with staff when giving a rating but everyone was so exceptional that I feel they deserve some accolades. I will definitely stay here again the next time I'm in Chicago.

title: “Past reviews unnecessarily scared me!”
text:
I booked at the Melrose and then read the reviews on tripadvisor and wanted to change our reservations to another hotel. My husband told me that we should stick with it since it was a great deal. I had my doubts....I'm happy to say we had a great 5 day/4 night stay. Breakfast was included in our rate which was a bonus. There was something everyone in the family liked to eat. Even my 6 year old was happy with her breakfast choices. Elisio, our server, was an added bonus as he catered to all of my daughter's breakfast whims.
We had a one bedroom suite which worked out perfectly for a couple with a child on the fold out couch. When the bedroom door was closed she couldn't hear the tv or us talking in the next room. Everyone was helpful and enjoyable. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Caught scabies, tinnea pedis”
text:
We have stayed at this very inexpensive motel several times. During the holiday, December 2007, we booked a week. A couple days after we went home, my friend and I began developing lesions beginning with our feet and progressing throughout our bodies. We went to the hospital where they diagnosed the parasites as scabies (contagious itch or mange especially with exudative crusts that is caused by parasitic mites), together with tinnea pedius (athletes foot). We returned to the manager of the motel to notify her that the room had parasites, and to request a refund to defray medical costs. She refused, saying that we had no proof that the documented parasites were contracted there. (Coincidentally, however, staff at the motel did acknowledge that the room we had was now closed for “repairs”).
The parasites are extremely annoying, not to mention embarrassing. I wonder how many others were infected before they closed the room. If denial was not management’s first response, I wonder if my friend and I might have been spared this pain and embarrassment. Management must have received other complaints before ours to prompt the room closure. 
Fortunately my friend and I have no spouses to have to explain this to. I wonder how many others who have been infected have been as fortunate.

title: “great stay !”
text: I am a native New Yorker, who lived on the upper West Side for many years. During a solo trip to NYC this month, I stayed at On the Avenue. I got an upgrade to a huge room through facebook, but the construction noise was too much, so they graciously moved me to another fabulous room in the back. Also way too big for one person, but what a great pleasure. The bed ( there were 2 queen-size ! ) was amazing and I slept like a baby. I can also recommend Fatty Crab restaurant in the building. The next time we stay in NYC, Seraphina should be open, too. The front desk personnel, especially Jessie, were extremely helpful, as were the rest of the staff. I can definately recommend OTA to anyone visiting NY !

title: “Great Room for the Price”
text: I got a $120 room rate from Pricelines name your own price. I was planning on staying at the Millenium Nickerbocker for $195 a night so I was not sure what to expect from the Intercontinental. Let me just say I was pleasently surprized! This hotel is BEAUTIFUL! The lobby and location are great. You are directly across from Nordstroms on Michigan Ave. The door men were very pleasant and helpful. The room was a large for Chicago. I just had to call and request a two double beds non-smoking after I made the reservation. I do agree that the price for parking, internet and roomservice is high. Vending machines would have been nice. The Starbucks was a nice treat in the morning located to the left of the lobby. My only big complaint was the water temp. in the showers. It got way to hot and then you couldn't get it any cooler. But all in all I would stay at this hotel for the normal room rate which is twice what I paid.

title: “Not so Bad!”
text:
I was absolutly dreading staying in this hotel after reading the reviews on here! I contacted my agent and asked that they request that I get a decent room to stay in as I did not want my trip to New York ruined. I got to the Hotel and althought there was a queue I found that it moved quite quickly, I was in at the front desk in no time. They gave me a room on the 5th floor and it was tidy and clean with no bed bugs or any of the other nasties that have been described on this website. The cleaners on our floor were very good and I was so impressed with the who ever cleaned our room that I left them a tip when I checked out. The Bathroom was clean and the shower was powerfull although I did spot a little rust under our sink and I could hear my neighbour singing in the shower quite clearly!! I got a good price on this hotel and for the money I paid I was quite prepared to put up with a little shabbyness however It just wasn't that bad. My advise is to get in touch with your agent and advise them of this site and request that you get a good room (maybe on the 5th floor).
P.s One review on here mentioned Homeless people sleeping rough in the corridors however I found that there were no homeless people sleeping in our corridor when I stayed as they have a man who checks guests for room keys when entering the lifts in the lobby.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text: We were just here for an overnight stay after completing the Bicycle Tour of Colorado - I had to drop my son off at the airport the next morning so he could return home to start his summer job (I continued on a side trip by car). Everything was fine except that the front desk guy called us at 4:40 AM, wondering if we were expecting to be on the 4:40 AM airport shuttle. I had told the staff at check-in that I would want to take the 6:40 AM shuttle and they somehow got it wrong. Just an honest mistake, and the guy was very apologetic. The shuttle, BTW, was quite convenient, making this an excellent choice near the airport.

title: “great place just to crash after a party night”
text: we travel from central tx on amtrak to party in the fort worth dallas area, its close to the rail station short walk,last trip it was clean and staff helpful,party all night so we join in at the bar and band on our why back from town, then way to drunk to even care what the room looks like and the smell changes during the night that depends what we eat!!! its a no thrills place we know it and its just right for our need and the price, works out great for a group

title: “Downtown Detriot and safe”
text:
My friend and I stayed in the Holiday Inn Express Downtown Detroit, in August 2011. We found the hotel to be beautiful, newly renovated, clean, and we felt very safe.
Our car, we parked in the valet parking. When we were ready to leave, they brought it to the door for us, and everything was perfect.
We had read bad reviews on this hotel, before we went. Are we ever glad, that we did not believe them. We had a great stay. Did not have an opportunity to check out the pool. But I am sure, it was as clean, and beautiful as the rest of the place.

title: “Highly recommend staying at this cozy hotel!”
text: Attended conference for Alpha Kappa Alpha Soroity Inc. My stay at this hotel was wonderful. One it was in walking distance to the Mosone Center where I attended conference. The staff was wonderful, customer service was excellent. The space in the was tiny but I found out that I can manage living in a small space. The space actually helps you connect to your inner. The hotel I found out is a 100 yrs. old. So I fiqure it survive the equakequake so that made me happy. Nice place to stay.

title: “Loved the atmosphere & coziness!”
text: My daughter lives in Venice. While I was there we stayed in the Venice On The Beach Hotel...I figured if I were going there, I wanted to be 'on the water' and we just about were. One could not get any closer. Out the private patio (cute, clean, well furnished) and there we were! The price of $200 a night was fantastice compared to other availability. The room was very clean...although small (especially the bathroom (nice water pressure too!) it was tastefully decorated. Gotta tell you though the bed (king) & the pillows were extremely comfortable. Left the lovely shuttered windows open & nothing better to sleep by than the sound of the busting surf and breeze. The mgr. Greg, was very nice. The place felt like a little home away...very relaxing atmosphere. Would definitely recommend it. Parking is at premium but we did not have any real problems. Would I stay there again? Yes!

title: “Very Group Friendly”
text:
Excellent breakfast ( a lot more substantial than others we've had)
Friendly staff.
Clean rooms.
Very accommadating-- kept our group together, which is nice for the group and for others!
Great location-- easy highway access-- 10 minutes to everywhere.
I would strongly recommend this place to anyone bringing a team or other group to San Diego.

title: “Needs to revamp their 'room-with-breakfast' policy”
text: Loved the hotel: the service and its location are wonderful (second time staying here). However, I hope they change their 'breakfast included' policy. They really only give a dollar amount -- which does not match any of the listed breakfast groupings on the menu. So, you end up paying extra or ordering a limited selection from the a la carte listing,

title: “Great Location, solid hotel”
text:
I was here for a convention for two days. This is a solid Hilton property, with friendly staff and a great location. My room was in excellent condition, as were the common areas.
My only complaint were the prices in the restaurant downstairs along the riverwalk. At lunch, $7 for a small cup of what they referred to as "Watermelon Gazpacho." To me it looked like watermelon juice with some diced celery and onion. Come on!

title: “Second Time's a Charm”
text:
A few things have been said in previous reviews about some unfortunate circumstances and I must say that I had experienced some of them during my first stay at the W Dallas. But the place was so suited to my taste that I decided to give them another try and it was well worth the second trip. 
 As an SPG Platinum member, I was placed both times in a “marvelous suite” and this room has got to be among the best of all the W's I've stayed at (and I've stayed at practically every one in the US). In contrast to the stark and cramped early incarnations of W rooms, this suite was extraordinarily spacious, bright, and airy. The gargantuan two-rooms were furnished with ultra comfy velvety sectionals, funky office chairs, and the usual inviting W signature bed. The living room was so huge that it housed a dining room table large enough to accommodate a wedding banquet. Floor to ceiling windows with sweeping city views and streaming sunshine added to the “WoW” factor. Gadgets are the usual for a swanky ultramodern room including extra large plasma TVs and space-age phones. I found the glass-abundant bath room motif chic and stylish but would have to agree with previous reviewers that the layout leaves little privacy for the occupant and even less to the imagination of roommates and service staff. Best extra-room amenity is the very well kept fitness center with, unlike most hotel gyms, actually enough room, weights, and cardio equipment to support a real exercise routine.
 A noticeable improvement the second go-around was the service. Door staff were in abundance but minus the attitude and more forth coming with service. Front desk check-in and out was considerably warmer and more efficient. A couple of minor glitches (phone not working, bottle opener missing) were expeditiously addressed and all the while, a Whatever/Whenever agent kept track of the fixes until issues were resolved. Room service was particularly pleasant and the meal scrumptious.
 All in all a fabulous stay at the W-Dallas that I hope I can experience again in the near future.

title: “Rooms could use a makeover, lobby is nice.”
text: Stayed here this week (10/29). Have stayed many times here but like the W NYC, the rooms could use some updating. The lobby is very cozy, staff are relatively friendly and notice you when you walk through the lobby. The rooms have the nasty brown duvets that I cannot imagine get washed each and every time a guest leaves. The walls are paper thin and I heard a couple getting it on next door. They went out partying and I woke up at 3 am to hear their ridiculous radio thumping and I assume more getting it on. I called the front desk but nothing was done. I might return, but Seattle seems to be getting some cool boutique hotels that will give this place a run for its money unless they step up their game.

title: “I'll definitely be back”
text: Great service and convenient downtown location. You do pay for parking, but it's valet with unlimited in/out service.

title: “Don't Stay Here! It is a Pig Sty.”
text: We are not picky in anyway. This hotel is the most horrible thing we have ever seen. Homeless shelters are fancier and cleaner. Do not be fooled by the lobby or the exterior. The front desk hates working there and it is apparent in their customer service. It was so bad, that we thought we were on some Candid Camera type show. We were waiting for the host of the TV show to surprise it with "We got you!"

title: “Great location!!”
text:
You can't beat this location for proximity to the BART station! You literally come upon the hotel when you get off at the Montgomery street exit. 
There is a Ghiradelli store right in this building. 
It was a short walk to the ocean to the market in the morning and not too far of a cab ride to Lombardi area (to see the crooked street)
We also walked back from Grant Street (China Town) and later a shopping district. Union Square was an easy walk from here, and pretty much anything you need to see. (It was less than a 10 min cab ride to the Pier where we boarded the Alcatraz cruise)
The room was clean, and pretty much quiet.

title: “Friendly and Pleasant”
text: The staff is incredibly friendly and helpful. The rooms are clean and inviting, though a tad run-down and with rather thin walls. A great value for a family vacation!

title: “Nice but not spectacular.”
text: A family of 4 stayed on one of the suites for 3 nights over a long October weekend. The hotel was a short ride from the airport. We stayed in a suite that we found to be very nice. It was bigger than a suite at something like the Embassy Suites, a little nicer too. The bathroom was nice but nothing too elaborate. The only concerns I had about the hotel itself was that the walls were thin so that if someone was watching TV with much volume next to you, you may be able to tell what they are watching. Also, if you are on a low floor, you may hear noise from the streets. We were on the 4th floor and could hear the Red Sox celebrations coming from the local watering holes. But not enough to keep me from staying here. We did wish they had a resonable, or even better, free breakfast. But, there are several spots to stop close by for a quick breakfast. Note that since this hotel is in the business district, some places are not open on weekends. It was less than a 10 minute walk to the "T". Would be nice if a little closer, but nothing too bad. We would consider staying here again but might prefer the Copley area is you can find a reasonable price for a hotel, especially one with a suite.

title: “Super small room”
text: Room was the smallest I have ever seen, it is the cheap version of the other w hotels, definitely below the w standards. location is ok but spending the extra $ to be on union square is worthy

title: “Good Hotel in a quiet neighborhood in SF”
text: We stayed here over a weekend during our 3 week holiday in the US and it was a nice place. We loved the neighborhood. Japantown is much quieter than Union Square or Fishermans's Wharf but still easily accessible and we always felt safe, also when returning at night. The rooms are large and clean with coffee/tea making facilities and an Ipod docking station. Hallway noise does seep into the room, though, but we always slept well. We had no problem with noise coming from other rooms. The parking was full when we arrived, but we parked in Japan Center, which is only a block away and cheaper than the hotel (16USD per 24H as opposed to 25), a bargain for SF. Breakfast in the restaurant on the 1st floor is overpriced and not included in the room, but there are a few possibilities in the vicinity (Japantown shopping center). Good value for SF.

title: “Location, location, location! Great staff and kitchen facilities greatly appreciated.”
text: This hotel is truly a hidden gem. Doesn't look like much from the outside but the rooms are large and comfortable. Full kitchen a great bonus. Breakfast was included and fantastic - muffins/bagels/croissants/cereal/toast/fruit. Staff extremely friendly and helpful. Free wifi and free computer in the breakfast area. Best thing is the location. Literally walk out the door and down an alley and you are at the Kodak theatre and hollywood walk of fame/madame tussauds/graumanns chinese theatre. Close to shops and grocery store.

title: “Location, service, cleanliness!”
text: The Casablanca Hotel is literally a stone's throw from Times Square and Broadway. The Hotel is art deco and has a wonderful ambience. All staff are polite, courteous and eager to assist with anything to do with your stay in New York City. The lounge/dining room on the second floor (Risk's Cafe) is a real bonus as you can take a break there anytime to to have a snack, read or just chill out. We really enjoyed the central location of the Casablanca Hotel as everything is within walking distance.

title: “Great service, quiet street, updated rooms”
text: We (3) stayed in the Executive Suite for three nights in June. The staff here is among the most friendly and professional I have encountered anywhere- and I am a seasoned traveler. The Chandler is also in an ideal location on a quiet street. It has been uodated in lovely modern decor and by New York standards our spotless bathroom was huge! No restaurant- but they are in the process of adding one now. There is wifi, a small bar, and continental breakfast is available daily in a room off the lobby. There are many good places to eat nearby and the concierge was more than helpful in suggesting those we may like and even printed out menus and directions in additon to making dinner reservations for us, I have stayed in many hotels in NYC - uptown and midtown. The Hotel Chandler is by far my favorite. Can't wait to return. .

title: “Ideal for business travel”
text: I have stayed at the Stoneleigh four times in the last three months. The first time I stayed here, I assumed that the rooms, and especially the bathrooms, would be small since the hotel is in an old historic building. However, the bathrooms are quite large, with giant bathtubs, and each room I have had has included a giant walk-in closet. The hotel is very comfortable and stylish. I have not eaten dinner at the restaurant, but several times I have ordered a salad at the bar (delicious) and the breakfast is also very good. The fitness center has all the basic equipment (it's been empty every time I have used it). The Katy Trail is a short walk from the hotel, so that is a nice option for walking / running nearby. I have no complaints about the hotel at all, so I am surprised at some of the negative reviews. I will continue to stay at the Stoneleigh when I am in Dallas on business.

title: “Great Hotel: Clean, spacious and professional”
text:
I stayed at the Affinia Manhattan for four nights in June 2009. First of all, the hotel is only steps from Penn Station, which made it very convenient to get to from JFK airport via the Long Island Railroad. Its location is close enough to Times Square that you could walk, or take the subway (which is only one block from the hotel). 
My room was the largest NYC hotel room I've ever stayed in. The room had three closets! Strangely, it had a tiny bathroom. The size of the bathroom is the only reason I give the hotel 4 stars instead of 5. The shower stall had barely enough room to turn around in! I wish they had enlarged the bathroom by taking away one of the closets. However, the room was very clean and comfortable. I had a corner room on the 23rd floor, so I had windows on two sides. I could open the windows a bit and let some fresh air in, which was very nice. 
The staff was extremely friendly and professional. I would definitely recommend the Affinia.

title: “Great location and great staff”
text: This was my first time to Chicago. I had heard it was a beautiful city. I chose the Palmer House because it looked like a beautiful hotel - I was not disappointed. Executive level complimentary snacks/breakfast/drinks were a lovely bonus. The female bartender went out of her way to make my sister and i feel like VIP's. She was the BEST part of our experience. The front desk staff were a bit uptight and would be the only complaint about staff in the hotel. Every other staff person at this hotel was 10/10 on service/customer care. The concierges Tracy and Philippe were outstanding as well. Great suggestions on where to go. Our beds (2 doubles) were not comfortable and the pillows too small. The location of the hotel is excellent and I would recommend staying here.

title: “Luxury with a Few Minor Flaws”
text:
Wow. Huge beautiful rooms and many luxurious touches. Unbelievably friendly and helpful staff. Spectacular views. Nespresso coffee makers.
BUT, there is room for improvement to satisfy the female business travel. They need a great makeup mirror with adequate light for working. Also, there are wonderful umbrellas, shoe horns and lint brushes in the room, but while a lint brush works for suits, they are useless for many items in a women's wardrobe. Also there's a rain shower which is fantastic unless you're worried about getting your hair wet. And the little shower cap in the box is the same one that you find in any hotel room -- useless in a normal shower, hopeless in this rain shower. (Although there's an Aveda Institute across the street where you can get a new blow out for $15 if you are lucky enough to get an appointment).
The products are great, but where's the bubble bath to go with that amazing tub?
Finally, the bathrobes are fantastic but the towels -- though abundant and huge -- aren't particularly soft.
These lacks aside, this is a wonderful hotel and if you get a chance to stay here, grab it.

title: “A two hour stay”
text:
We chose Paradise Point because it looked amazing in the Virgin brochure and decided that this would be a great place to spend 10 nights on our honeymoon. How wrong could we be! Granted the location is gorgeous and the staff (with whom we dealings) were very friendly but the room we had assigned to us was appalling. As soon as the bell boy opened the door the stench of damp hit us full on. We then clocked the grubby, worn furnishings and thick cobwebs on the lampshades and the mould all round the bathroom was a sight to see. To top it all we then met our room buddies - the ants!! It was so bad (standard room) that we decided we weren't going to stay whatever the cost and checked out within an hour (no upgrades available). We then enjoyed a great holiday at another hotel further round the bay. To sum it up - great surroundings, friendly staff but extremely poor standard accommodation. 
If you enjoy comfort avoid!!!

title: “Good deal for what you pay”
text:
Since this was one of the cheapest hotels I could find in NYC I was wary about staying here. However, other traveler’s had good experiences so I decided to check it out. 
Overall, the experience was great. The hotel had a lot of “character” but in a good way. I found the rooms and bathrooms clean. It was also nice being able to leave luggage before and after check-in. The hotel is in a great part of town. There are a lot of restaurants and shops nearby. There is also a major subway stop a few blocks away. I would recommend this hotel to the budget traveler who is looking for an unique, quirky yet affordable NYC experience.

title: “Was there for Operative Gynecology Course- felt like my wallet got biopsied!”
text:
While this has a nice location, the inside of the room reminded me of a bad Motel 8 in Appalachia. The room was grimey, the bathroom was moldy and the walls thin. I was overwhelmed with the smell of curry everytime I walked onto my floor. The elevators are inadequate to service the volume of guests. One of the hotels representatives berated one of the conference directors as I was waiting to ask a question. The conference was in December but the ballroom was HOT- and the "AC cannot keep up.."
There are better hotels nearby. There are great delis nearby. The Greek Restaraunt , Molyvos, is across the street and is heavenly- I do reccommend it. Also the famous Carnegie Deli is just down the street. Not a bad walk to Broadway plays.

title: “A little slice of heaven...............”
text:
I traveled to Austin for a girlfriend's getaway recently and this resort was superb, as usual!! This was my fifth visit. Each visit has been just as lovely and memorable. The ambiance, impeccable grounds, view of the lake, nicely appointed rooms, amazing variety of fitness and wellness classes and great staff make this one place that should be on your bucket list. Seriously. Having traveled to high-end spa resorts all over the world, this one is still one of my all-time favorites. I recommend arriving on Sunday to avoid the busy weekends at the Lakehouse Spa, which is part of the resort. Plan to stay several days to fully avail yourself of the ammenities. I recommend two or three days to enjoy the plethora of fitness classes, cooking demo and other such offerings; one day at the spa and two days to just lounge around (including a nap in one of the hammocks by the lack, which is a must!!!) I have visited Miraval, which is also a great destination spa with great offerings including the Equine Experience. However, the lake view, attention to detail and exceptional staff give Lake Austin the leg up.
My favorite instructors are: Sandy (cardio/hiking/fitness), Katherine (foam rolling, yoga, etc.), Anne Irving-Likes (Yoga, "Train your Brain"), Paul (yoga, meditation, five tibetan rites, ayurveda), Annie (stability ball, spin).

title: “A few hiccups, but still top notch.”
text:
I will stay here again.
The grounds, service, and restaurant are basically what you would expect from a top notch resort. Why not five stars?
- elevators did not work properly. One stopped on every floor every time, even though no buttons were pushed on the elevator or on the floors where it stopped. Once it went up instead of down, though the only button pushed was down, the corridor light indicated it was going down, and I was the only one trying to get it to go down. Every time I went by the elevators and someone was coming off, they were complaining abut the elevators malfunctioning.
- Nice big television in the room, but very poor picture quality.
- i was not given or offered a key to the mini-bar. Front desk informed me that this should have been done at check-in, and that all I needed to do was call down and they would have immediately run it up.
It think that was all. Overall beautiful grounds, good service, nice restaurant - just a few things to work on before earning an "excellent" rating.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
I paid $132/night--a good rate for the Union Square area. Hotel was very nice and rooms were clean. 
Pros: Hotel staff very friendly and helpful, room was nicely decorated and spotlessley clean, location was convenient to BART and lots of shopping.
Cons: No in-room movies (as advertised on the hotel's website), continental breakfast was the cheapest I've every seen. A staff member did tell me they plan to upgrade it in the next few weeks, air conditioning did not work, location is noisy (any hotel in this area is probably noisy).
Overall, I liked it and would stay again. I don't think you can beat it for the price!

title: “All About the Decor & Restaurant!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at this hotel after it was recommended by my parents. It’s appears to be an old apartment building that was converted into a super trendy hotel. We stayed in the jewel room. The room was large, well decorated, had a semi-private patio and even had a little beta fish. All the little touches (like the fish) made this hotel so unique and neat to stay in.
The common areas (restaurant seating, “entry lounge” and pool) were very well kept and very welcoming but it didn’t seem to be the place to hang out in the daytime. Though the hotel is very mellow during the day (workers on their laptops in the restaurant and an empty pool), the whole hotel comes alive at night.
Between happy hour, amazing cocktails, beer on tap, appetizers, main courses and delicious desert this restaurant is a hit and fills up to capacity every night! Both nights we made sure be back to the hotel early so we could get good seats and hang out all night to eat, drink and watch whatever was showing on the huge projector screen over the pool. I was adventurous and tried a lot of their specialty cocktails. They varied from great to weird to umm.. no BUT it all depends on your taste! Everything we tried was delicious.
I highly recommend this hotel, especially for the restaurant.

title: “Amazing in every way!!”
text:
We stayed in a one bedroom suite for six nights. This hotel was amazing in every way. Clean rooms, curtious staff that really went out of their way to welcome you, remembering you from one day to the next. The gym is one of the best you'll see in any hotel, along with the complimentry wine hour in the evening.
We would recommend this hotel to anyone. Even those who have pets.

title: “Nice Hotel with Great Location, but not worth current rates.”
text: I have stayed in the Palomar hotel several times in the past 4 years, and enjoyed the stay, primarily due to the excellent location of the hotel. The wine reception is a nice way to end the day in the city. The rooms are clean and the furnishings are nice. My major complaint about this hotel at this point is the outrageous prices that are being charged. This is a 4 star hotel, and the current prices are what one would expect to pay for a 5 star property. I have had nice rooms there in the past for less than $150 per night, and now I am seeing rates of $450-$500. It's a nice hotel, but not nice enough to warrant such an extravagant rate increase.

title: “Didn't live up to promises”
text:
This hotel was picked for its airport and area shuttle. Upon arrival we asked if our wedding party could reserve the shuttle for our wedding party and we were told no but it should be available. Hours later when we requested the shuttle we were told another wedding group had reserved the shuttle and it would be unavailable, so we had to pay for cabs. This issue was discussed well in advance of our stay and again early in the day of the wedding. 
I requested a room on the Hwy side of the hotel, didn't get it. Our welcome baskets for our out of town guests were not all delivered until I saw them at the front desk the day of the wedding, Guests were all checked in the day before. The hotel did deliver a "romance package of champagne and strawberries" to some of our guests, at 10:30pm at night! 
This hotel has good intentions but the follow through is terrible.
I called the manager the day following check out thinking she needs to know what needs to be addressed in her hotel..... I was ignored!
The room was nice!

title: “awesome location for the price”
text: this was as close as you could get to the alamo and riverwalk without taking the car. Staff was more than accommodating with any of our requests

title: “A NYC Gem!”
text: My husband just did a quick overnight in the city to visit friends and didn't want to pay a fortune for a nice hotel. We booked a standard room at The Iroquois and hoped for the best. When we got there, they let us check in early and even upgraded our room for free! From moment one the staff were courteous, friendly and very helpful. Our room was small but very clean and with a great bathroom. Even our friends in the city were impressed (they met us there to start our day) - they will reccomend The Iroquis from now on for out of town guests. Everyone from the concierge to the desk staff to the doorman were friendly and great to talk to! the only consideration is that the place isn't super 'cheap' and our room had a view of a fire escape - but this is pretty standard for a downtown hotel - in the end a good value. I'll be staying there whenever we go back to NYC in the future!

title: “The "W" Really Should Be "Club W" Pick Another Hotel”
text: If you are looking for a nice girls trip in Chicago during the winter, by all means skip this hotel. Our flight had us arrive about 8:00pm at the hotel on the Friday. We entered the hotel and the lobby was covered in people smoking and drinking and for a second we were so taken aback we couldnt find the check-in area. The people were sooo rude, we couldnt understand it. WE got to our incrrrrrrrrrrrredibly small room (with a nice view of the lake, I might add) but there was no where to put toiletries. The rooms have these awkward plantation [--] that close off the bathroom from the bedroom and unless u r with your husband that is a bit awkward from a privacy perspective. The "Whiskey Sky Bar" is on the top level of the hotel (which is pretty forgettable, is this really what people consider fun?) and guests of the hotel have to share the elevator with all of the patrons coming to the hotel to "get their drink on". Yuck, my girlfriend unfortunately was the recipient of someones cocktail when he misstepped and lost his balance in the elevator. The spa was forgettable expect for the showers in the spa -AWESOME!!! but they serve you no brownies like they said in the add and there is NO COFFEE in that dang blab place- AWEFULLLLLLLLLLL!!!! I complained and wrote a detailed letter, do you know what I got back, an invitation to try them again- on my dime. ARE YOU KIDDING......apologize, give me a partial refund or even invite me back for a reduced rate, but just ask to come back again. DO NOT GO THERE EVER!!! Unless you really need a drink and can't afford one. Then step on the elevator, I am sure you will taste someone's alcohol!!!

title: “Just OK”
text:
I was there this weekend. I couldn't not sleep very well as I found the bed and pillows to be too soft for me. I had to use one my daughter's stuffed animals under my head for more support. While we had the AC on, it was like hearing a coffee maker perculating all night long. We had an OK view,...the location however is great. The staff were all very friendly.
So, I would only come back due to the location and staff. I will make sure to bring more head support next time.

title: “Great location”
text: Great view of Times Square. The staff was helpfull and friendly. The room was large, clean and the bed, king size, was very comfortable. My dayghter and I went to Washington for 2 days by train, so we left some luggage at the hotel, since we were coming back to NY and they only charged $1 per day.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
Great hotel Staff was friendly.
Room was very clean and the hotel is located with easy access to subway and central park. I would stay there again and recommend to friends.

title: “There are better choices”
text:
When we couldn't get the Rivercenter we decided to stay at the Menger. 
Musty but not so much run down. Everyone was nice. We did the necessary valet parking and the bellman told us he'd have the bags up in 5 minutes. After 10-15 minutes (we wanted our bags) we called the desk and the manager acted like we were just then ordering our luggage--he took our number. After 10 more minutes I went down to get our bags. 
They were over in the corner and I think would have been for quite a while longer. He refused to let me take them but agreed to bring them up with me. The hotel system clock on the tv was 15 minutes early and the bedside clock was 15 minutes late. There were four messages (in Spanish) for a previous guest (?) on my telephone. Didn't try the restaurant or room service.

title: “You Can Do Better”
text:
Purchased a 2 night Aquarium Package including parking - harborview room - tickets to aquarium & breakfast. King room with a rollaway. 
Upon arrival- hotel didn't know if parking was valet or self parking but told us to remove all valuables from view since the adjoining parking garage is not owned by the hotel. Decided to self park and had ticket validated. Never told us to validate each day. Somehow our ticket expired at 3am on the morning of our checkout?? Wouldn't let us out of the garage unless we paid another $25 to the attendant. Tried to explain the package - they were uninterested. I finally got out of the car and marched up the garage ramp to the hotel. (Other than one front desk person and the security guard)the staff and management could have cared less too. Finally had security settle the issue without incident. 
Friendly check in. Told that the requested refrigerator was in our room. (?) They must have thought that rollaway meant refrigerator! Took a couple of attempts to get the rollaway. Got it, but no linens! Got them, but they were for a crib! 
Other than the parking and rollaway issues...the hotel does have adequately comfortable rooms with a lovely view of the harbor. However, the harborview rooms are extremely noisy in the early morning hours with the many deliveries to the shops and restaurants that surround the waterfront. Sirens day and night too. Just not our cup of tea when you want to sleep in until - oh I don't know - 8am!! 
I will say that room service breakfast was on time and delicious...albeit the wrong order. Close, but not up to par for a Renaissance property.
Also, housekeeping will call your room to see if you are in fact checking out - especially if you hang a Do Not Disturb sign on your door. They can't knock, so they call. Let's see...they called us at 10:15 for an 11:00am checkout. Not a good idea. 
All in all - attention to detail was lacking and anything that needed to be resolved was eventually resolved, but not without an unbelievabe an almost shocking abundance of attitude. I can honestly say that they were...yes...RUDE. You can do better elsewhere.

title: “Modern budget minimalism that works”
text:
This is what a hotel would look like if Ikea built one, inexpensive but modern minimalism design employed well. Do print out your reservation to get the rate you booked. Parking is $25 a day on the next street with a coupon from the hotel.
When you walk in the check-in counter and gift shop are smartly condensed together on your left. The hotel lobby is a play on levels, the glass enclosed pool is a few feet above floor level and the bar is a few feet below. There's stadium seating next to the pool and on the Friday night we were there, it was spilling over with twenty-somethings bouyed on cocktails from the pass through window to the bar.
Although the web site gives the impression that each bed has a flat panel, there is only one and it's could be bigger, keeping budgets in mind it's fine. The DVD player is underneath the bench seating. The closet has nice thick steel hangars, no drawers in the room but plenty of space to store stuff under the bed. The layout of the bathroom for the king w/bunk is spacious enough to move around easily.
The bathroom has a long counter, more spacious than a many expensive hotels with an additional outlet. The lighting fixture is near the sink, moving it to the middle or adding another one would be a nice improvement. There is a sliding panel to cover the shower or the toilet. Didn't care for the above your head shower, yeah it looks cool but it isn't and it would be nice to have a towel hook nearby. The refrigerator with glass door is well chosen.
We stayed in 1207. Though I could hear the garbage collection down below, I fell asleep within minutes and didn't wake until the alarm went off in the morning. Good bed and great bedding. Be a little careful with the bunk bed, it's big enough for adults but a little closer to the ceiling than an adult might be comfortable with.
It could use a few tweaks, but is such an improvement over the traditional hotel that it will be on my short list again.

title: “Very glad we found this hotel”
text:
We chose this hotel after reading the TripAdvisor reviews and are so pleased with our choice. 
The front desk staff were exceptionally friendly and very helpful in providing information on sights and events. The owner himself made us feel very welcome.
The hotel is less than 1 block from a subway stop, for easy access to anywhere we wanted to visit in NYC.
We found the room size and quality to be one of the best values in NYC, including a flat-screen TV and granite counters. 
They have a business center with free computer access, and an easygoing cat who hangs out in the hallways. 
Breakfast is included , with a nice selection of food and juices. 
We will definitely stay here again next time we are in NYC.

title: “Magnolia was a convient site for me to stay downtown while transitioning my family to Houston.”
text: Nice hotel for business travel. Needs a restuarant on site and a small gift shop.

title: “Fabulous hotel!”
text:
An amazing hotel! Very clean, comfortable rooms with ample room for a hotel in New York. 
The room was more like a small apartment and contained two double beds, a bathroom and fully equipped kitchen. Given current exchange rates, should you wish to limit your budget whilst on holiday, the kitchen enables you to cook your own meals if you chose to. 
Hotel staff were very welcoming and friendly and were always on hand to offer advice on exploring New York. A selection of different novelty pillows were available and fun to try.
The hotel is excellently located within a short walking distance from the Empire State Building, some bars, restaurants and shops. Public transport links are close by so the hotel is in a perfect location for exploring other areas of New York.
If we have the chance to return to New York, we would return to this hotel as it really made our holiday a great one.

title: “just love fitzpatricks”
text: i stay here at least once a year on annual shopping trips. it always feels like a home from home. service is excellant, rooms lovely with the most comfortable beds in the world! very convenient for bloomingdales and 5th avenue shoppong. good irish breakfast every morning.

title: “Great airport location”
text: We stayed recently at the Jacksonville Plaza Hotel & Suites and the overall experience was great. The location is only minutes from the Jacksonville Airport and we chose this facility based on exceptional price, free parking for up to 14 days and free airport shuttle available on a 24 hour basis. The room we stayed in was comfortable with both a fridge and microwave in the room. We will definitely stay there again!

title: “Excellent choice!”
text: We found the online positive reviews of this hotel to be accurate. The hotel was very clean, very well maintained, Bed was comfortable and there was little noise from the street/outside. The front desk staff were very friendly at all hours (late night and early morning). While the hotel is compact, it did not feel too small for 2 adults to stay in the room. Great location.

title: “Beautiful setting, clean, convenient”
text: The setting is lovely. My room was on the second floor facing the pool and had a balcony with a chair and table. From my balcony I had a view of the mountains. Room was very nice, standard for what I expect from Marriott. Housekeeping was especially early (rather than tardy like some hotels) and cheerful. Location is fantastic...I walked to do my shopping and dining. My only complaint had to do not with the hotel, but with the thoughtless guests above me who carried on a boisterous conversation at 2:30 a.m. I finally called the front desk; the staff shut them down within 5 minutes.

title: “Great place to stay in San Francisco”
text: If your visiting San Francisco, this is a great place to stay. Close to Market Street, Chinatown and Union Square area, not overly touristy like the Warf area. We stayed in a one bedroom suit that was clean, well maintained and comfortable.. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Great value and good location.

title: “Clean,Comfortable and Convenient!”
text: Got to stay at this hotel through Groupon! Great deal 2 nights, 2 breakfasts and 2 Museum Tickets. Was a great deal and would do it again. This hotel has a secret gem with the roof garden and lounge! Free coffee and tea 24 hours, free wifi and friendly staff. Very Nice!

title: “Looking for Old and Rundown? This is your place”
text:
Not impressed at all. This hotel looks like it has not been updated since about 1980. From the decorations, to the cracks in the parking area, to the extremely old fashioned lay out and waste of space in my room. 
My room was large and odd--the doors into the suite led in from an indoor courtyard set up. The doors were french doors, with the glass and had curtains behind them. They made me feel less protected somehow-- lilke it would be very easy for someone to use a credit card to get into my room, or pry off one the old glass panes. Once inside, you are now in a very large sitting area, with full couch, table and chairs, a wet bar, and an old TV. This was the size of a regular room! But the carpet looked old in the burnt orange colors in the room made it feel musty and old. Further back in the room was the separate bedroom. This was the size of a small regular hotel room. This area was a bit more modern. My number one concern was how unsafe I felt. I knew that since the front entrance door to my room was so far away, I would not be able to hear someone trying to enter my room. Maybe I am paranoid, but as a woman traveling alone, this resulting in a less than comforting night of sleep.
The breakfast in the morning was impressive. They had a omelet station, which is not a normal site at most hotels. And it was included with the room rate. 
As I travel to El Paso frequently for work, I have decided to not stay at this location again. I will stick with the Holiday Inn Downtown.

title: “Icing on the cake - FANTASTIC HOTEL!”
text:
Absolutley fantastic hotel - BEST IN NEW YORK:
- Great Room (Massive)
- Friendly staff
- Great location
- 24hr convinient store next door
- Pillow menu
- Widescreen TV with cable
- Very clean
- Great Chinese takeaway 1 block away
- Excellent facilities
- Very nice restaurant
Need we say anymore......
Wouldn't think to look anywhere else If we were to go back - This is definately the place to stay in NEW YORK!
An absolutley fantastic hotel, which truly did put the icing on our stay!

title: “Great place to stay for the entire family”
text: Wonderful staff, friendly, pleasant. Beautiful courtyard, lobby area, breakfast area nice, rooms clean and very roomy. Very nice place for the whole family.

title: “Lived Up to High Expectations”
text:
We were here for a 4 day weekend (President's Day) and had a great time! The rooms are large and the bathrooms spacious with nice amenities. The hotel offers a variety of recreational activites-spa, golf, tennis, pool, variety of restaurants. If that's not enough, a very large shopping center is across the road and free hotel shuttle transportation is provided. 
We used the golf and spa facilites as well as the pool area and found all to be great. There are 4 restaurants. The 3 we ate in were all excellent. All the staff members we came in contact with were polite and attentive. 
After reading some other reviews, our main concern prior to our visit was whether the hotel is relaxing or a "convention hotel" with a rude and noisy "expense account crowd" dominating. During our visit several groups had meetings but none seemed to interfer with the guests who were just there to relax. 
Although it's a short outside walk outside to get to the health club and self parking is a 3-5 minute walk from the hotel, Phoenix weather is good most of the time so neither should be a serious issue.
Overall, our visit was an experience we look forward to having again in the future!
[A large, separate exibition/convention hall is under construction and looks like it will be ready in summer or fall 2008. We trust that Marriott will ensure that convention business doesn't overwhelm the hotel and interfer with the guests paying their own way who expect to have access to the facilities at their convenience without being subjected to noise and overcrowding (if you think it might be a problem it might be wise to call and see what they have booked at the time you plan to be there ).]

title: “TERRIFIC HIP HOTEL”
text:
The Ames is a hip (but not snotty) boutique hotel. Small, nicely appointed rooms, friendly staff and a great location. The hotel bar/cafe is quite good, too.
My only complaint is that the pillows are all over-sized and I found them a bit uncomfortable - i prefer something smaller or a mix. But the bed was comfy.
All in all, a nice place to rest your noggin.

title: “Loved the Location”
text: I was at the Park Plaza from Sept. 23-28, 2004 and thought the hotel and location excellent. I did find that the bathroom was tiny and the carpet needed replacing. The rooms were rather pricey, however, the staff was very helpful and courteous.

title: “Service was special!”
text:
Super special service from the moment we walked in the door...our daughter was under the weather, front deskman David Tortora (totally rocks!) sent up milk and cookies stat. Dinner at Noe was great, traffic was so slow that night (probably due to bad weather) that we felt like we had the whole restaurant to ourselves.
Room was upscale nice, would do well for either business or pleasure travel, with large sitting/desk area, gorgeous view of pool and lush grounds. Love the swans.
Only downers: valet charge for the car was a bit steep at $26, and room service bill was loaded with all number of charges (2 types of delivery charge??), just watch it.

title: “Top hotel”
text: Only had 1 night,was on a stop off en-route to Memphis.Great hotel,in a tremendous location,no complaints whatsoever,friendly helpful staff,nice food,clean and comfortable,couldn't ask for much more,altogether good value for money,would definitely use again.

title: “A Classic Hotel in a Great Neighborhood”
text:
My wife and I stayed at Park Manor Suites during a recent week-long vacation. We were more than pleased with the hotel, the staff, and especially the location.
A few specifics (and responses to some of the negative reviews I read):
The Hotel Itself:
A beautifully restored 1920s-era building. The suites are really apartments with lots of space. The building definitely has character--high ceilings, Murphy beds, built-in cabinetry. Our suite even had a grand piano! I felt like we'd walked into Bertie Wooster or Hercule Poirot's apartment. Everything was sparkling clean and well maintained. The only negative for us was noise from the street and the rooftop bar when we had the windows open (and the windows didn't completely block the noise). I'm not sure I would stay here in the summer when it's too warm to keep the windows shut.
Food:
The continental breakfast was good, although perhaps nothing to write home about. The menu included cereal, English muffins, pastries or banana bread, fruit, coffee, juice, milk, and yogurt. It's definitely fun eating on the rooftop patio overlooking downtown, the bay, and the park. We didn't eat in either of the restaurants, so I can't comment there. (However, one couple we ran into said they'd eaten at Inn at the Park several times during their stay.) Inn at the Park was running a $19.95 early-bird prix fixe menu when we were there.
Location:
Park Manor is literally across the street from Balboa Park. An easy (and safe) walk to the Zoo and other park attractions--1.5 miles tops. The hotel is also right on the edge of Hillcrest, so there's lots of dining within easy (and, again, safe) walking distance. (Among our favorites: Extraordinary Desserts, Chocolat, and Bread and Cie.) Several days we didn't even use our rental car.
Other destinations are a bit farther away and would require a car or the bus, including downtown, the Embarcadero, the beaches, etc. The #120 bus stops a block from the hotel and provides easy access to the Fashion Valley Transit Center, where you can take the green line trolley. That bus or another one will get you downtown.
Parking:
The parking lot is small, but we never had a problem getting a space, even when we got back late in the evening. The hotel seems to work hard to keep people out who are just there for meals or special events. (Registered guests get a hang tag that forestalls towing.) Also, there is ample unmetered parking nearby.
LGBT Issues:
Park Manor Suites is proudly gay-friendly, as indicated by the rainbow flag above the entrance. Also, Hillcrest is the center of gay culture in San Diego. If you're easily offended, stay at a different hotel in a different part of town.
