Having said that, I think you would have to be very easily offended to encounter problems at the hotel and in the neighborhood. We found everyone, gay and straight alike, to be warm and welcoming.

title: “delightfully different”
text: My family of four (children ages 8 & 10 and their parents) spent three nights her in February 2005. Every one of us loved this hotel. The lobby and all the common spaces were so comfortably cozy. Kids especially liked the library. Our room was quite spacious but I suspect it's because it was designed to accomodate a wheelchair (bars in shower and handheld showerhead). I really liked the hardwood floors with rugs as opposed to the ubiquitous hotel carpeting found in many hotels. Staff were all friendly and approachable. Concierge sent us to some good restaurants. The Hudson was a great place to return to after playing tourists all day in the February chill.

title: “The best value in Manhattan”
text: The Milburn is an incredible value -- we paid just under $200/night after taxes. It's a quiet, impeccably clean, well-run place. Our room was perhaps twice the size of a typical, tiny NYC hotel room, nicely furnished but nothing trendy. The service was flawless. The location offers the opportunity to experience a New York residential neighborhood, and a lively but quiet one, at that. It's an easy walk from the 72nd Street subway stop. Lincoln Center, Central Park and other places of interest are walkable. The Beacon Theatre and Museum of Natural History are right in the neighborhood. Close enough to Times Square and anywhere else you might want to go, but just far enough away to be a very pleasant area. Some people might find it a little out of the way, but that's one of the best things about it.

title: “Been Before and Will Again, BUT...”
text:
Like the hotel, like the location, (when the price is right) but had a disturbing experience this last visit. When checking in, my room was not ready. Perfectly fine since it was about 10AM. I had an important meeting the next morning and I needed a suit cleaned. I asked the receptionist if I could drop my suit off to send out for cleaning and was told no problem. I made sure to ask if it would be OK since I did not yet have a room assignment and again I was told no problem. I put it on the sheet that I did not have a room assignment yet. 
I got back to check in at about 4PM. I asked about the suit, and they said they would check and get back to me. The room was great as usual. I did not hear back for a few hours and called the front desk. They still knew nothing and did not seem to care. I started getting concerned. I told them it was a personally tailored $1,500 suit I had made while in Hong Kong and more importantly, I had this important meeting first thing in the morning. I called the front desk back at 7:00PM and they said the head of housekeeping went home already but would contact me first thing in the morning. I woke at 7AM and waited then called at 7:30AM and they STILL did not know the status of the suit. They said they would check and call back. Then about 8:00AM there was a knock at the door and they handed my suit in through the door. No explanation, no apology, no sense of concern that I was a little freaked out.
BTW, the cleaning for a 2pc suit was $23!!!

title: “Grand Hotel....Excellent Location”
text: I used the TripAdvisor to make my decision to stay at the Michelangelo. I mainly made my decision based off of the rating that it is #22 out of 431 rooms reviewed in New York. It was everthing I expected and more. The room was wonderful. I stayed in a Jr. King Suite which was beautiful and very large! The location of the hotel is the best. I walked to everywhere that I went. The only cab that I took was to meet a tour bus at 6:30am and did not want to walk in the dark and rain. My best word to describe my stay is "grand". I had a great time.

title: “Hyatt was awful!!”
text:
Had made my reservations through Expedia. When I arrived, was told by the folks at the Hyatt that I had cancelled my ressies! I showed them my paperwork that I indid had a reservation and that it was also paid in full. Was told by the front desk, "It's not our problem, call Expedia". Which I did. Was put on hold, then the folks from Expedia came back on and said my room was there. I then had to endure listening to two of the front desk staff tell me how they hate deal with Expedia. At that point, told them that they needed to take it up with administration and NOT the customers, that so far Expedia had far exceeded their customer relations than the Hyatt. The room was a typical room, could of been staying in any one star hotel. There was mold on the tile in the bathroom, and I don't mean a little! The topper to my stay was that I actually took the time to write out my entire experience on one of those "How'd we do" cards that goes to the general manager. Not a word of response! Great location on the Riverwalk, but find another hotel!
-debbie in Seattle

title: “Good Property-Would Stay Again”
text:
Wife and I were at this hotel for the marathon this past weekend. Rates were a little more elevated for Chicago than normal given that, a Notre Dame football game, as well as a conference I believe. Overall wasn't bad though.
Our train got in at 11 am, so we cabbed it over, and were able to drop our bags, as our room wasn't ready yet. Got back around 3 and we were given our room keys. The lobby is nice, with attentive bell staff. Elevators have a bit of a bounce to them, but not too bad. Got to our room, and it was as advertised, with good space for a Chicago hotel room. 
Turned on the TV, as Friday was the first day of the baseball playoffs. TBS was carrying the games, and showed up as channel 8 on the TV, but there was no signal. Called and complained about it, someone would call me or stop by. No word. Checked again later that night, nothing. Went down to the front desk to ask. While I wanted to see Friday's games, Saturday was the real important day. As of that morning there was nothing, so I went down again. The girl at the front desk said they needed to call the cable company. My wife and I were heading out for a bit at that point, and when we got back, it had finally been resolved. I had also made mention of problems with ESPN News and Classic,(although I wasn't really interested there), and those seemed to have been resolved as well.
The only other negative we had was the temperature control. It seemed no matter how high we tried to put the temperature, it would always blow cold air. Finally we simply turned it off.
Overall I would certainly stay there again, although it does make for a long walk to Grant Park :-) But anywhere north of the river is definitely in walking distance. The room was nice and big. The shower had tremendous water pressure, and the staff were very helpful. Given some Chicago attitudes I had seen before I wasn't sure what I would get, but it turned out great. We had a bit of a lake view from the 15th floor. Between two other buildings, but they never made a fuss about room being lake view, so that wasn't a concern.
Definitely worth staying at.

title: “Good Option for the Price”
text: This hotel is a good option if you're able to get a good deal. We ended up getting a Standard King room at $89 a night through Hotwire which was unbeatable considering the location. It's located right in Fisherman's Wharf, across from Pier 39. There is access to a huge variety of restaurants and attractions. The F line street car picks up right in front of the hotel and can take you to several other areas including Pier 33 which is the location to buy tickets or board the on-site Alcatraz tour (it's the only tour which takes you ON alcatraz, not just around it). The hotel itself was outdated, but I would still consider it a 3 star considering the ammentities, options and location. All staff was helpful and considerate. Overall, we were happy with the hotel considering the great price! If we would have paid more, I might have been a bit disappointed.

title: “DON'T STAY HERE!!!”
text: Worst radisson I ever stayed at! Upon arrival, the parking garage which is normally free to park in was under construction and they wanted to charge me $22 to valet my car 5 feet from the door. I could have parked the car myself. The front desk girl ignored my concerns completely and would not transfer me to the buena park radisson where I preferred to stay because radissons are all franchises. I called radisson customer service who told me it was my obligation to check the parking tab before booking my reservation. Even they had an attitude instead of helping me! Customer Service is dead in this country. I will never stay in radissons dirty filthy rooms again. I used to frequent these hotels but will never stay there again. If they don't care about their customers then they don't deserve my hard earned cash. Don't stay here!

title: “We loved The Beacon”
text: As a family of four we were very impressed with The Hotel Beacon. The room was very spacious and exceptionally clean.The kitchenette was a god send,with fresh tea and coffee every day.The location was perfect,with a good selection of shops and restaraunts just moments from the hotel,and the Fairways supermarket had a wide variety of food and drink,all available 24hours a day.Times Square is only 20 minutes walk or 5 minutes on the subway for all that New York has to offer.Also with Central Park only 5 minutes walk away it was great for the kids after a hard days shopping.All in all I would reccomend it for a romantic weekend for 2 or like us a 7 nite stay doing all the touristy things as a family.We will definately be staying here again and will be recomending it to all our friends and family.

title: “Great location, friendly staff.”
text: We stayed here for my daughters graduation at University of Washington and it was a perfect location for all the fun downtown and a quick drive to the University district. There were steep hills all around so if this is a problem for some people a cab is readily available to take you wherever. Rooms were clean and very comfortable. Beds were great and view from our bedroom was really nice. We would stay here again!

title: “Great service & location!”
text: The Amalfi was the perfect hotel for our 4 nights spent in Chicago. The staff were very helpful and friendly. The hotel is in the perfect location for exploring Millenium Park, the Loop, the Mag Mile, etc. The room was nice and clean and had a mini-fridge, the only thing I wish it had was a full-length mirror. It was nice having coffee and a quick breakfast just down the hall from our room in the mornings. We went up to the cocktail hour on the 6th floor one evening, it was busy and had good atmosphere. We would definitely stay here again next time we're in Chicago!

title: “Great location”
text: Big, comfortable rooms, well-appointed, good service.

title: “Should not be allowed to market itself under 'Marriott' banner”
text: This Residence Inn is grim all round, the local area is really down at heal and the kerb appeal is seriously lacking. It was obviously busy with what I can only assume were mainly 'long term' residents, I had booked a bi-level suite at a cost of $179 plus tax, the receptionist was fine and the area looked clean, the room we were given was really poor though, plaster on the floor around the fireplace, sticky marks scattered around the kitchen surfaces, the decor was tired and discoloured with cigarette burn marks on the work surfaces. There was rubbish in some cupboards and the linens smelt stale. It was so bad that we decided not to stay (despite an 8 hour drive from SD) and went to a Fairfield nearby instead. I have never felt the urge to write a report before but this hotel was a disgrace to the Marriott brand.

title: “Good Location”
text: Good location for most of the main attractions - subway adjacent but we used yellow cabs or walked most places.Hotel room adequate (king size) and clean although next to the lift and a request to move was not well received - the alternative offered was even less attractive. Not too many friendly faces amongst the staff and the general New York attitude of "take it or leave it" dominates. Breakfast was included in our deal and had a good buffet selection but plenty of options for this locally at a cheaper price. Don't bother with the concierge service unless you wish to pay a premium for theatre tickets or the airport taxi service. We got a room extension till 3pm on the day of our departure at no extra cost - anything later is charged at full day rate.

title: “Totally Impressed from Start to Finish!”
text: I have to say from start to finish, this has been one of the better stays I have experienced at a hotel. The staff at the hotel was probably the most polite and attentive people I have come accross. Whenever we needed something, they were all very engaged and very helpful. The room itself was better than I expected. With two very clean and nicely done bedrooms, each with their own separate bathroom, and a separate living room and rather big kitchen area - complete with most everything you would need to have/cook a meal. Not that you would have to cook breakfast - the free breakfast buffet each morning was awesome and was changed up daily. I can't say enough how impressed I was with everything. Even the private whirpool room that sat umpteen people. Very Cool. All in All... this is the place to stay when going to L.A.

title: “Perfect spot for families”
text: I went with my sister and our children to Baltimore for a "road trip" and stayed one night at the Brookshire. It was really great. We parked our car and were able to walk everywhere. Prices for parking are on par with any other dowtown city area you visit. Every staff member we came into contact with was fantastic, from endulging our children with the "coin collection" (great idea for kids) to suggesting restaurants. "Mr. Dave" was great at the cloud lounge evening reception. The drinks were very nice and a wide range of snacks were offered (salad, cheese platter, crackers, chips, dips, veggie and fruit platters). We said you could easily make a light dinner out of the snacks. Breakfast also was very good and plentiful (waffles, eggs, potatoes, sausage, cereals, breads and sweets). The rooms do differ in layout and there are some spots where the ceilings are low but we were very comfortable. I will definitely return to the Brookshire for our next road trip to Baltimore.

title: “Some people don't know they're born ....”
text:
You can't complain about this hotel. For location, cost, quality and service it was a great hotel (no hotel deserves excellent).
Location - 2 minutes walk from McPherson Square Metro, National Airport is 20 minutes away. The White House is 5 minutes walk, Washington Monument a brisk 15 minutes. Ok - the area is not flush with restaurants but the Metro makes any only 30 minutes away.
Cost - we got charged a flat $175 for 5 nights in a superior double (2 queens) when the 3rd, 4th and 5th should have been racked upto $275. Bar food is reasonably priced as is bar food - but who eats in Hotel restaurants ??
Quality - Great room, great beds - no view (in our room) but who cares you don't stay in your room to look at the view from your room ?!?. Boutique-style but not pretentious.
Service - couldn't fault what we used of it. Front desk were efficient and courteous, Concierge knowledgable and quick to help out reserving restaurants and making suggestions for lunch on Thanksgiving), Door-men very friendly.
Tips - walk to places (Capitol is a great 40 minute stroll) get the Metro back - it's all very safe. Ebbit Grill is great value for money. Don't bother with Georgia Brown's - way over-priced unless your going to eat all Sunday and not do anything else. We found Georgetown over-rated - Just like Marlow, Bucks. (England) and Manchester (England) rolled into one (probably a novelty for U.S. citizens. The Deli round the corner (Loeb's ???) is good for breakfast. Brunch at the Market Lunch (Eastern Market) is a must). Anyway find out yourself but don't go complaining.

title: “Ironman 70.3”
text:
We stayed at this hotel because it was very close to the Ironman Austin 70.3 race we were doing. The room was great....it was big, lots of pillows and breakfast was decent. 
The location is good if you are doing something on this side of town or at the Travis County Fair/Expo center. But other than that there really is not much around it in the way of dining and entertainmnet. That wasn't our reason for the visit so it was perfect for us. Very nice hotel overall though.

title: “Excellent location, great room, no noise.”
text: Stayed 4 nights. Loved being so handy to Hop On Hop Off bus routes and many activities easy walking distance. Room was compact but quite sufficient. Very clean, and though less than 300 meters from Times Square no noise problems. Staff very helpful. Would definitely recommend Hotel Mela.

title: “Great place to stay - good value & family friendly”
text: We have an 18 mo old baby and my husband and I stayed there with my parents & sisters family with their 3 kids ages 11-17yrs after our cruise to Alaska. The rooms were clean and spacious but there was no minibar/refrigerator in the room so I couldn't keep food in there for my son. We were in adjoining rooms 286 & 284 facing the atrium/pool. It was noisy due to the echo of kids playing in the pool all day & night and we could hear music from a ballroom event. My parents were in room 275 facing the airport and their room was very quiet but a bit far from the lobby. The enclosed pool was awesome and our kids had a great time swimming. The room service was ridiculously slow so we drove 5 min up International Boulevard to Subway. The hotel is minutes from the airport and the free hotel shuttle runs every 15 min, they are super courteous and helped my parents who have a wheelchair with all our bags. There is a kiosk in the lobby that allows you to check in online and print your boarding pass for free, plus a display on the wall showing the current departure times for all flights. There is a Hertz rental car kiosk in the lobby and we rented a car for 2 days at a good rate. All very convenient. There is a train stop a short walk from the hotel which might take you into Downtown. Free internet access in the lobby but my computer got the signal in my room. I'd recommend this hotel to anyone with kids or without. If you want quiet, I'd recommend a non-atrium facing room.

title: “Fantastic - Worth Every Penny!”
text:
I stayed here with my mum back in July and we had a fantastic time.The sheets were spanking new, and the pillows were so comfy and had that delicous wiff of duck feathers. We absolutley loved the exciting bold decoration everywhere and enjoyed chilling after a day out in the lounge. This had a constant supply of freezing cold water, usually flavoured with floating fruits (lovely touch), and teas, coffees and hot chocolate.
Every staff member we saw would always greet us with a friendly smile, and the petite girl with dark hair (sorry I forget her name!) was particulary helpful. She even went out her way to find the nearest place where we could by a kindle and other shops we wanted to peruse. They were also happy for me to use the lounge after I'd checked out for the day, with their speedy wifi.
The hotel itself is in a great location - close to subway stops, and wasn't far from Central Park either. We also were happy to find that Carnegie's Delhi (think man v's food) was round the corner.
I'd definatley stay here again in a heart beat...if only to sleep in that bed again!

title: “Business in Fort Worth”
text:
While conducting business in Fort Worth, I opted to stay downtown. I chose the Hilton because of the location. It is easy to get to the different highways and there are plenty of restaurants within walking distance.
Checking in was easy. Everyone from the front desk to the car valets were very nice. The quality of the room was nice. Furniture clean, room spacious, bed comfortable. The room was clean but there was the same hair in the tub the 4 nights I was there.
Valet parking was the only option and gets expensive after 4 days having to tip. Also, this hotel is in the business district, right next to the convention center. Everyone I saw at the hotel were business people yet the only premium TV channel was HBO Family. It would have been nice to be able to watch a real movie while working at night. There is no pay movies either. There were a couple of nights I would have paid for a movie but didn't have the option.
Over all the visit was comfortable and convenient. I would stay there again.

title: “"It's the most wonderful time of the year"”
text: this hotel i remeber staying at way but when i was in 4th grade. These rooms are beautiful and the views are amazing. Of course it's pretty expensive but it's all worth it. Here's exactly what you should do in New York (I live there) Check into this hotel (the people are so nice your gonna want to be bestfriends! Then go straight up into your room and get organized! Then around 12 head over to a resturant called Jekyll and Hyde! It's supposed to be a "scary" themed resturant but it's awesome and really fun! Not scary to me but it gets crowded really quickly! Then go over and check out some sights! My favorites are Ellis Island (statue of liberty), top of the rock, empire state building and broadway! take a boat tour that takes you to ellis island. there you will stop and now that the statue of liberty is opened, go check that out! (Take lots of pictures!) Then go to the top of the rock! It's very historical and the view from the top is spectacular! If you're afraid of heights this is not for you. You take an elevator like 2,290 feet or something crazy into the air and then walk through all the floors, look out the balcony, take pictures, it's amazing! By that time, you may want to go get some dinner. I would suggest an Italian Resturant there are really amazing ones! oooo and also check out toys r us and go on the ferris wheel...INSIDE IT! (and do LOTS of shopping at all the stores.) Then go back to the london and get some rest..you're gonna need it! In the morning, the london has free breakfast which is lovely as well. it's ok but there aren't many choices of food to eat. Next, go to broadway and see a musicial or go to radio city music hall and see whats going on there! The empire state building isn't all that fascinating from the inside i dont believe but go see it! and if you're there in the winter, go to times square and go ice skating! BEAUTIFUL! you'll love it there!

title: “Mediocre”
text: Nice hotel with fantastic fitness center. That's all that can be said. The duck march was crowded and lame. The service was typical. Truthfully I'd rather had stayed across the street at the Holiday Inn.

title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text: This was a nice stay. The hotel is located close to a lot of DC sights, right by the IRS building and close to China town. The rooms are large and clean and the free breakfast is great !

title: “Fantastic Service”
text: I took my husband for a night in New York City and was very impressed with this Hotel. From the moment I arrived to the end of my stay, I was always looked after. I got a welcome call and even a evening check out call the evening prior. I was nervous about staying in New York, with all the fuss of bed bugs, but the room was immaculate and my husband and I were very pleased. I would stay at this Hotel again and would recommend it to anyone.

title: “Elegant home away from home for the business traveler”
text: Wonderful service and attention. The Hotel itself is a design lover's dream with well appointed rooms, plush sleeping set-ups, and very clean as a whistle. Situated a stone's throw from Times Square on 6th on one side and Bryant Park on the other (Ave of the Americas)-you are perfectly positioned for a great time. Don't forget to try the chow at Sagu downstairs-delicious French Vietnamese, ask for Phillipe!

title: “Kids 1st Trip to NY”
text: I "researched" this hotel till my fingers were numb. Was reluctant at first based on other NY hotel stays based on price/night. We reserved a Jr. Suite (had 5 traveling) with a balcony. I can definatly say that price does NOT reflect quality! I can say that we will be back later this year to view Xmas and stay at the Affinia 50

title: “The clift management and staff provided the most extraordinary experience, well beyond my expectations”
text: The hotel management and staff provided a stay that the most discerning traveler would be hard pressed to beat. From the food staff to the housekeepers, the hotel has a clear agenda to make every guests stay a memorable experience.

title: “No better location or venue in the LA area for your events”
text: Our organization has been hosting almost monthly community events for the last 4 years. While we occasionally use other venues, our organization as well as our guests overwhelmingly prefer the Luxe Hotel Sunset. From the first contact to arrange the event, to driving up to the valet and the staff helping with your event, everything is perfection. After our first event, the staff almost intuits your needs. The venue is gorgeous. The acoustics is excellent - whatever you need they can make happen. From small events of 50 to 450, the service is great. Guests can have dinner or drinks before or after. When we have speakers come in from out of town, we always put them up at the Luxe and they love it. It is centrally located and easy to get to. We have never been disappointed and enthusiastically recommend the Luxe Hotel Sunset.

title: “Lap of Luxury”
text:
This resort was way up there in luxury and service - the second best we've ever stayed at - very opulent. In the words of the in-room guest book: "...inspired by the rich, decorative arts of Spain, Portugal, Italy and Morroco"; "colorful palette, graceful arched doorways, rotundas, vibrant tile, wood-beamed ceilings, ornate stone and wrought-iron accents, decorative columns, parquet flooring and gracious verandas.". More simply put, you walk in and say "Wow!" - several times.
First impressions were exceptional, from the eucalyptus-scented hand towels presented at the front desk during check-in, to the fresh lemonade, iced tea, and cookies and huge, aromatic, floral arrangement in the lobby. The concierge desk was very nice and helpful, especially Gabrielle and Lynette. We asked their advice every day.
We requested and got a room with a fairway (golf course) view - the one downside is there's only a standing balcony, with insufficient room for chairs to sit and enjoy the view. We found the room to be very luxurious - all the amenities you could possibly want and more. The room (389) had a great layout, including a bathroom with a huge tub, two sinks, separate shower and toilet, and a folding window above the tub that opens into the main bedroom. There are lots of subtle, sometimes hidden extras, like a vanity with a top that opens up to reveal a large mirror and provide a compartment for your wife's things. The bedroom offered plenty of drawer space, slide-out table tops, a beautiful corner couch, cushions, and ottoman for relaxing, and a large flat screen TV on the wall. Two newspapers were delivered to the room each day, and we were asked if we wanted any others.
Valet parking is the only available option, and they charge quite a bit for it ($30 plus tips). I complained because I didn't see this spelled out up front until my reservation was confirmed - the resort very kindly said they would waive the fee. Each time you leave the premises, the valet offers bottles of cold water for the road. Nice.
A plus for us was that we rarely heard or saw any other people in the adjacent rooms - either the walls are nice and thick or no one was in them.
A couple of relatively minor downsides:
We only got turndown service on the first night of our four night stay. Not sure why. We loved it when we got it.
We were offered and accepted an in-room coffee maker, but housekeeping just didn't seem to know how to handle this extra. They consistently failed to clean and provision it, even bringing coffee bags without filters on the last day. On a similar note, we requested extra towels (to their credit, the hotel asks before you arrive), but housekeeping had to be reminded to keep replacing them.
We used in-room dining several times, but got tired of it. Would have liked some simpler, less "frou frou" options to choose from. We switched to muffins from the coffee shop (Cent'Anni) for the last couple of mornings.
Speaking of dining, we opted not to eat at their highly touted restaurant, Addison - settling instead for "second best", Amaya. It was fine - great decor, nice waiters, good food, very classy - frankly it was hard for us to believe Amaya wasn't the best!
I can't emphasize enough how pleasant and accommodating the staff was. We had the feeling they would do anything within their power to make our stay a nice one (and they succeeded). Also, the resort is absolutely beautiful. Be forewarned, though - it's about a half hour drive north of San Diego just off I-5, so it's not right in the heart of the city if that's what you're looking for.
We loved it!

title: “Weekend in San Francisco”
text:
We chose this hotel based on a friend's recommendation and location.
We found the hotel to exceed our expectations. It is very well located - across street from train station, street cars and near Union Sq
Staff and concierge were pleasant and very helpful. The rooms were nice - linens, bed and bath were great! it is a city hotel, so there was some outside noise, but not enough to be disturbing - and for those who are lighter sleepers, earplugs are provided.
We had breakfast each morning in the hotel restaurant and did not find it to be overpriced, as many city hotel restaurants can be

title: “Beautiful hotel with spacious rooms and friendly staff. Looking forward to my next stay!”
text: Upon my arrival I was greeted by a helpful bellman who assisted me with my luggage and boxes. The Guest Services staff were friendly and accommodating during the check-in/out process. My guestroom was well appointed and spacious with very comfortable beds. The restaurant staff were very attentive and the food was absolutely delicious! The Sales staff was professional and very helpful in assisting me with my event. Overall, the Orchard Hotel staff made me feel like a part of their family - I was spoiled and look forward to my next visit! Thank you, Orchard Hotel!

title: “Great staff”
text: We recently used their facility for a four day regional sales training/sales meeting location. The entire staff was extremely friendly, helpful, pro-active and competent. The meals were very good by hotel standards and the guest rooms were clean, comfortable and quiet. We would definitely come back to this hotel for future meetings in the Phoenix vicinity. Some improvables are that the facility probably should be renovated in the next few years and some meeting rooms are relatively small with air walls that do not isolate sound very well. Overall, we were pleased.

title: “Nice relaxing location, very friendly and helpful front-desk staff”
text:
If you're looking for good value on a medium budget in a great location , this is deffinitely the place to stay. With the marina on one side and bay on the other the whole island has such a relaxed up-market feel. If you enjoy an early morning or evening walk or jog along the waterfront you will love this. The pool is nice and clean, and relaxing in the spa overlooking the marina at night is a real treat. The front-desk staff were very friendly; no request is too much. Once we had checked into our room - the manager called personally to introduce himself and say that we could contact him if there were any problems or if we needed anything during our stay - we have never had that sort of service in any hotel before - and many of those cost much more than the Island Palms.
The room was a little on the small side for the four of us, but the bathroom was big with quality fittings. The room lacked the ubiquitous 'big chain' feel -which was nice.
One complaint we had was the service in the restauarant - this was slow, disorganised and not too friendly - so we ate elsewhere after that (there are good restaurants in easy walking distance). Maybe it was just a bad day.
The rate was $109 - why pay more? We would deffinitely stay here again.

title: “Decent place”
text: I have stayed at this hotel several times while on business trips. What you get is a decent room for a decent price. The rooms are acceptably clean and everything works, including the free wireless internet. The rooms are quiet and quite comfortable. The staff is friendly but sometimes seems a bit overwhelmed when more than one guest is at the front desk.

title: “NYC is about the people”
text:
In past trips overseas we have stayed in all levels of accomodation (incl Sofitel Washington/ Bellagio Vegas on this trip also). NYC accomodation is very expensive, and we were under no illusions we would be getting what we paid for, though were really happy that our expectation was exceeded. 
We knew before we arrived that the NYC experience would be about cramming as much into our day as we could - and crashing when we got to bed - to us, the room was somewhere to put our head down. The trade off, is the money we could save in accommodaiton we could put into expereinces in the City.
The Rivington streetscape is a bit edgy, though once through the door, we were greeted with the friendliest desk manager we have ever encountered - Gabe is a deadset legend - one of the lovliest blokes we have encountered, and every night gave us the opportunity to shoot the breeze with a hard working family man.
Location wise, the place is brilliant - a short walk to the Bowery, where the only decent cup of espresso coffee in NY seems to be made (head to Think Coffee). Close to Chinatown/ Little Italty/ Soho/ East Village - in short, a walk in any direction gets you to an interesting part of the city. The 2nd Ave subway uptown is a short walk around the block, and Prince St on the Yellow Line (a bit further west of Broadway) opens up a heap of other options. Try Cup and Saucer for a US diner brekkie experience and Prosperity Dumplings for authentic Chinese at a ridiculously low price. (both on Eldridge St) 
If you are after glitz, and are willing to pay for the honour, head mid/ uptown. If you want a really central location that allows you the opportunity to spend the extra $'s saved from an uptown chain hotel, this is the digs.

title: “Great New Rooms But...”
text:
Stayed here one night, Thursday, 9/20/2012 to try out the hotel. Booked a King Executive Club Level room. I am Priority Club Platinum Elite and all my paperwork was ready, waiting for me, room pre-assigned (impressed). Now, we liked the room a lot. The bed was wonderful. The room size was surprisingly large. We liked the selection of cable tv channels (although the on-screen and laminated list of channels in many cases do not match the actual channels). Very quiet. We did not hear any noise from any other room or even from the hallway. 
Now, my question is why is there are picture of a club level lounge, posted June 2012 by the property, and there is none? I asked at check-in about the times it was open and was told there was NO club level lounge. I booked this type of room specifically because of this. I also asked if there was a washer and dryer on the property and was told no (although the in-room hotel guide says there is by the pool) that there was only a dry cleaning service. Also, everytime I stay on a Club Level at any other hotel, it is keyed access but not at this property.
In our room, upon arrival at about 4 pm, there was a what I thought a nice cheese and fruit tray as a welcome amenity (beyond the water that we were given at the front desk). When we opened it, the crackers were soaked, the strawberries were moldy and I later found a live single ant under the plastic wrap. 
I really want to like this hotel, and am looking for a hotel in San Jose as I come frequently, but I am not sure if this is the place or not.

title: “Fantastic Hotel!”
text: Very nice hotel we were in a renovated room which was very nice had a little refrigerator and microwave which is a plus in NYC. Within walking distance to all theater district and Time Square and close to subway. Could only stay one night here due to obligations elsewhere would stay here again definitely! Very nice service and bellman were wonderful! Not a great view from our room but room was so nice it didn't matter highly recommend!

title: “Brilliant service and facilities”
text:
If you are wanting to stay in a clean, friendly and well equipped hotel then this one is for you. The staff are exceptionally friendly and helpful. The hotel has a lovely bar, restaurant, gym, pool and even a convenience store. The hotel itself is extremely clean and comfortable. The rooms are of a standard size, bit very comfortable and the house keepers do an amazing job. 
The best part of this hotel is Jeff. I have never encountered in all my travels a more sincere, helpful and thoughtful concierge/shuttle driver. Jeff took us to old town and recommended where to go and where to eat. As we were staying a lot later than the shuttle service he showed us where to get a cab home from etc. A few days later we needed to send home to Australia some parcels. Jeff took us to the post office, took our parcels in, waited in line with us and organized all of our things to be sent. We were in the post office for half an hour. Jeff just wanted to make sure that we had the correct forms and to make sure our things were sent off safely. 
This hotel is close to everything and especially the great shopping at the fashion mall.
Highly recommend!!!!!

title: “Fabulous hotel, but check your phone charges”
text: Loved everything about this hotel - truly a lovely place to stay. Our room was enormous and the breakfast buffet was the most impressive I've seen. I rated the service low as we were charged for long distance and local calls that we did not make - we surmise that a staff member accessed our room, while we were at the zoo and used our phone, so beware. The charges were made, while we were gone and security was supposed to check the door to see which key was used, but they didn't show by the time we needed to check out. The charges were refunded.

title: “Great choice!”
text:
You cannot beat this hotel for the location, price, cleanliness and great bar restaurant to boot! We booked our room for $220/night which was a very fair price. Our room was clean (the most important factor for me), spacious, great bath products & very quiet. I asked for a quiet room b/c I have insomnia so our room was in back of hotel so not much of a view but that was fine with me. 
This location is perfect b/c if you want to walk uptown or downtown, it's an easy walk with lots to see on the way. I only hope that I can stay here again and get the same price!

title: “Fairly average all round...”
text:
We stayed in a deluxe king room... it was very a reasonable size for a NY hotel, which was good considering that we had 4 suitcases and were able to spread out a bit. The bed was comfy but pillows were terrible. The bathroom was fairly small but certainly not the smallest we've seen! Overall the room was clean and the hotel staff were very attentive with making it up and providing us with whatever we needed. Also, patience is needed with the lift when going down to the lobby as continually skipped our floor and were often left waiting for 10-15 minutes to get downstairs!
We arrived in NYC the day before Thanksgiving and were in a PRIME location to watch the parade, plus we were able to walk to heaps of restaurants, shops, the subway and even Central Park - given this, I would stay at the Paramount again if need be.
Disappointments included having some spare change taken from our room (not a BIG deal but still, glad it was only a few dollars), having a truck stop-point RIGHT outside our window which added to the NYC noise factor and made a good nights sleep virtually impossible... and booking a shared accomodation van to the airport through the concierge desk, which never turned up and the hotel just passed the buck and wouldn't do anything about it - FYI, in NYC cabs to JFK airport are FIXED, so don't bother with the shared vans, the hotels only recommend them because they get a kick-back from it!

title: “The best surprise of our trip”
text:
What a nifty hotel. It's convenient to Central Park and Times Square, next to the Seinfeld "soup man's" counter, and posh. The room was extraordinary comfortable (shower only, though) and spacious. The modern, artistic feel is everywhere.
The Central Parking Systems elevator-driven garage is next to the entrance and reasonably priced.
The staff is what made it really great - each employee seemed well-trained and suited to the job. I can't say enough about how great the stay was because of them. A real gem!

title: “Perfect Location!”
text: My 8 yr old daughter and I stayed for New's Year and we both loved it! The location can't be beat-we were able to walk to the Space Needle, Pike's Place and downtown for shopping. One of the reasons I like small hotels is that they take the time to help. The staff was very helpful securing dinner reserv. for NY Eve at the last minute. Stayed at the Westin previously, but it's too generic.

title: “Amazing location, hotel iteself was OK”
text:
I have just returned from a 4 night stay in New York where we stayed at the Crowne Plaza - first thing to say is you can not fault the location in any way. You are in the middle of Time Square and pretty much everything is within walking distance. You could not be more convieniently located for Broadway shows or even sporting events at MSG. It is of course very busy, but this is of course to be expected!
The hotel itself was OK- at check-in the staff were pleasant enough, but they forgot to tell us where our breakfast would be served which was included with our concierge room. Check-in was though quick and we made our way to our room. Room itself was OK- nice view of the Hudson river and no real noise from the traffic below which was good. Very small considering the cost, but decent enough compared to some of the rooms I have seen mentioned on here.
Only real issue with the room was the temperature, which was too warm to sleep comfortably (fine for during the day, but needed to be a few degrees cooler at night) and there was no way to change this (air-con was there but made absolutely no difference).
Breakfast was again ok- 3 days out of 4 we went to the designated breakfast area only to be told that it was full and given a voucher for the main restaurant- again this was OK but it did add an extra 20 mins to the waiting time as the main restaurant was always packed. The food itself was nice and the service in the restaurant was good.
The bar area was pleasant and you could have a nice relaxing drink whilst watching the hustle and bustle of time square below- very relaxing.
Overall I would probably rate this hotel at 3.5 if that were possible- a couple of things were very nice, and the rest OK- I don't think I'd stay here again- there are plenty of alternatives and paying a premium for this hotel (especially a concierge room) was not good value in my opinion.

title: “Good location, beautiful view of the Space Needle”
text:
I had to stay in this hotel due to business. I had a conference on the W so it was very convenient walk there. I didn't rent a car since Westlake Plaza and other places in downtown is walking distance. Pike Peak's and the Needle are walking distance but not as close as you think! I gave up walking back and took a cab. 
I had a beautiful view of the Space Needle. The room was spacious with a king size room and a desk area. The closet fit my 2 suitcases. The bathroom was roomy as well. The hotel could use some updates or make it a little bit brighter, I felt it was dark at times. I prefer natural lights and kept the windows open most of the time.
It would have nice if they offered free breakfast. I did ordered room service and the food was pretty good, but I did not have any other meals there.

title: “GREAT STAY! GREAT STAFF! GREAT HOTEL!”
text:
We are on our 2nd of 3 nights and we LOVE this hotel.
The rooms are great, the staff is incredibly accommodating and the stay at this Hotel is beyond our expectations. We are traveling with 2 teenage girls and you could not find a better location for them. Attached to the Galleria Mall!
We have stayed at many "5 Star" properties including Four Seasons, Ritz Carltons and Hyatts, and the Westin Galleria Dallas meets or exceeds all expectations. 
Best most attentive staff we have ever encountered and the cleanliness and upkeep of the hotel is second to none.
To all of the staff thank you for your help and especially to Munya, you are the best!

title: “Worth It!”
text: My friends and I went April 2-4, 2010 to ATX and needed an affordable place to stay! We found a 1 King, City View, Smoking Bedroom at this hotel and decided to book it. Most of the hotels usually have a small king bed and since we were 3, we thought 1 would have to sleep on the floor but to our surprise we all fit (and we arent that skinny!). It said the distance to downtown was about 15 minutes, yet we did less so I think the location was pretty convient. Also, next to the hotel there are many restaurants, however you receive 15% off in Bikinis and 20% off in Dennys, which is a pretty good deal. My friends and I went for some drinks @Bikinis, they were cheap and good, my friend ordered a salad and it was good too! The bedroom was good, I think it was gonna be ugly but it turned out to be GREAT for the price we payed. The people were friendly and the place was secure. I would definitely stay here next time I am @ATX. If you're on a budget, North Austin Plaza Hotel & Suites is a really good place!

title: “Don't Bother!”
text: It continually went downhill. The room we got was dated, small & smelled from all the air freshener for smokers. (we had asked for non-smoking) Afer leaving the door open, it was still so bad I insisted they change our room. That one wasn't much better but didn't smell. When we took showers, it was intermittent Hot then Cold - never just right. We found nothing we read on the internet that said it had all these features, amenities, & more - they must have stayed elsewhere. It is a great location for touring Fishherman's Wharf (insist on a room away from the street if noise bothers you). For 1 night maybe but our advice is spend a little more & stay somewhere else - you'll be much happier!

title: “Very Chic”
text:
We booked this hotel after reading these reviews and having had a positive experience of Sofitel Cairo!
When we arrived we were disappionted to find that some gifts which had been sent for us prior to our arrival had not managed to reach us...and an urgent email which had been sent was not made avaiable until we enquired after it. 
We mentioned that we thought this was a little bit poor, and the Sofitel management could not have been more apologetic. We came in one afternnon to find they had placed chocolates and fruit in our room along with a letter of apology!
On our last day the Customer Relations Manager made a point of finding us and asking us about our stay! She even offered us a late check out which meant we really enjoyed our last day in New York.
The room was spacious and comfortable! The beds were amazing! Air con that works! Great bathrooms. The carpet in the inner lobby feels like sand under your feet at the end of a long day of walking in New York City.
Very chic, understated hotel, amazingly central but quiet location! FAB breakfasts
I'd recommend a stay! (Would not recommend the mini bar....BIG prices for small items, which are available in shops just around the corner. e.g mini bottle of evian over $4 in the mini bar, only 99c in Duane Reed's)

title: “Service and Friedliness that you can count on”
text: I travel to this hotel for vacation and a convention 3 times a year. The staff Including Estelle Estrada, go out of their way to make me and my friends feel welcome and at home during out stay here. Highly recommend this hotel to anyone who has to stay in the area.

title: “Good stay”
text: If you are looking for a clean hotel with a good location, this is the place for you. Our family of 5 stayed there for 2 nights and cold walk to all the major locations and attractions such as the cable car, Alcatraz, Fishermans Wharf. Parking is right next store. We would stay here again.

title: “One of the best Kimptons”
text: I stayed here three nights during Thanksgiving weekend 2012. The Palomar is conveniently located downtown San Diego. You can pretty much walk to most attractions and restaurants within minutes. It was my first time to San Diego so I was surprised how close everything was. The Palomar has an incredible pool/bar area where you can kick it with friends. Free happy hour wine! I've stayed at many Kimptons around the US and this is one of the best and definitely top notch. The staff was very friendly. The beds are pillow top and I swear I was sleeping on a cloud. I fell asleep so fast I went down while I was adjusting the brightness of the lamp! It was hard to get up in the morning because it was so comfortable - thats a good thing. The only thing I didn't like about the hotel was that the doors shut very loud, to the point of disturbingly loud. I strongly recommend you bring ear plugs. The cleaning staff needs to do a better job dusting areas in the room you don't normally think about.

title: “Great Service and Experience”
text:
Our daughter spent several weeks in Chicago for inpatient rehabilitation. Rather than commuting every day, my wife and I spent several nights each week at the Drake. The entire staff at the Drake made us feel at home from the very first day. As the weeks went by and more and more of the staff learned of our daughter's recovery, they were sure to ask how she was doing and did everything they could to make us feel more comfortable without neglecting other guests. 
As a Hilton Diamond member, I have had many great hotel experiences, but none better than our stays at the Drake.

title: “Excellent Hotel with good location”
text: I stayed in this hotel for 2 nights in January 2010. The Check In was the best we have ever had in a HGI. The people were very friendly and helpful. Great Staff!!! Our room was very clean and the beds were very comfortable. We had a LCD Flatscreen with over 200 channels. Unbelievable! The breakfast near the Lobby was very fresh and tasteful. The Hotel is located only 4 streets away from the NY Penn Station. The only negative thing was, that we booked a room with Empire State View. But we couldn't see anything from this building. We had Room Number 2108. So, if you are looking for a very nice and clean Hotel with a great staff at the Front Desk, Restaurant and Housekeeping you should book this hotel!

title: “For the price totally worth it”
text:
Older hotel remodeled. Everything brand new in my room. Walking distance to Toyota centre and minute maid park plus convention centre. 
Free town car to take you anywhere you wanna go at night

title: “Good Hotel”
text: This was the second time I stayed at this location. Very nice hotel, staff was pleasant. This location puts you closer to the airport than any Denver hotel but it is still a decent drive. The location is ok, you can't walk to any restaurants but there are a few choices within a couple of miles. Overall I would say if being relatively close to the airport but still near civilization is what you are looking for this hotel should exceed your needs.

title: “Lacking”
text: For a Hilton I expected a little cleaner room. I checked in and found mold in the bathtub and hair in the sink. The internet connection also kept going in and out. The location was pretty good but the staff could have been better. All in all, it was ok.

title: “Great hotel; lousy guests”
text:
Stayed at this Hyatt Thanksgiving weekend. The staff is extremely pleasant and helpful, even during busy periods - I arrived Thanksgiving day and the restaurant was completely booked but I was able to enjoy the same dinner in the lounge and the staff was very attentive. The rooms are great; the bed is so comfortable you may not want to get out of it. I liked the T-Mobile Wireless Internet - it's $9.95 for a 24-hour period. I'm not a fan of the dispenser in the shower for shampoo, conditioner and shower gel but I suppose it does help keep expenses low. The neighborhood can be scary at night but there are safe pockets for you to walk if you want.
The only problem I had was with the two different parties who were in the adjoining room. On Friday night, the first group decided to stay up and talk all night and I finally had to call the front desk after 3:00 a.m. to see if they could do something about it. Saturday night was fine, but on Sunday morning the second party decided to get up extremely early and carry on a loud conversation where one member kept laughing loudly every few seconds. Since I couldn't sleep any more, I just checked out early. The front desk suggested that next time I ask for a room that does not have an adjoining room.
All in all, a great hotel.

title: “Perfect Location”
text:
This is a perfect location to stay in NYC.
Walking distance to Times Square, Grand Central Station, Central Park & Empire State Building.
Located at 5th Ave. & Bryant Park so you can turn the corner and shop until your hearts content.
The rooms were very clean and we stayed in 2501 and this is a king room with a desk and sofa and a very large bathroom.
Very large room for NYC standards.
The view wasn't great at all and this Courtyard doesn't serve breakfast but all in all I would highly recommend and would stay there again.
Maybe their are some small rooms there but not ours.
Are rate was great too! Worth every penny.
It is not the frills and thrills of staying at Times Square but not the price either.

title: “Awesome Stay”
text: There were 13 of us: three women and 10 girls. Upon check in we were greeted by a friendly staff. There were staff outside ( I remember Ben) that was ready to help us out in getting taxis and giving information to wherever we needed to go. The hotel was close to everything including a 15 min walk to Navy Pier. The warm chocolate chip cookies were delicious. They didn't have the rooms (double queens) that we wanted initially, but once available they accomodated us with adjoining rooms and the double queen beds. The beds were extremely comfortable, we didn't want to leave! The kids loved the indoor swimmimg pool. There was a charge but they waived that for us. Any request we had was accomodated right away. So all in all we had a great time staying at the Doubletree and would stay again anytime!

title: “Value per square foot?”
text: Originally, I had booked another, less expensive, downtown Chicago hotel for our quick trip in and out, but all my pals had elected to stay at the Hotel Felix. It seemed a little too rich for my blood, but this was a wedding, these were my friends, and well...it's only money. So I changed my booking and went with the Hotel Felix. So how to write this review? The room was attractive and expensive looking, very high-end finishes; the bed was fabulous, so very comfortable; the shower was terrific with its rainfall showerhead; the room was...small. Tiny. Almost miniscule. I bumped my shin on the box frame of the bed *every single time* I came out of the bathroom. There was no chair save the desk chair, and I -- thrashing and sleepless for a time -- needed one. Of course, there was no space, so I suppose there is no point in lamenting the lack of a lounge chair. So how do I ultimately judge the value of the room...was it comfortable? Yes, the bed was amazing. Was the staff helpful? Yes, you know at a hotel like this you're going to get actually information from the staff. Was the hotel attractive? Yes, in a modern and tasteful way. So was the room worth the exorbitant price I paid???? In the end, that was a lot of money for the amount of useable square footage, so I have to judge no...I've had better value at a good Hampton Inn. I don't think we could have spent more than one night in that room. However, if you get a deal, and a bigger room, I have no doubt the stay will be lovely.

title: “Amazing Value”
text: I very much enjoyed my stay. My room was clean and the kitchen was ready for use with utensils, plates, glasses and cooking supplies already there. Although they said there was no maid service during the weekend, my room was cleaned. I was on the first floor right next to the lobby and the room was still very quiet. The air conditioner was so noisy though that I did need to turn it off to be able to sleep. I was plenty cool with it off, so it was not an issue. The separate sitting area was great for visiting with my friends. My only complaint is that although I had reserved a crib, I did not have one when I arrived. There are only 2 cribs for this very large hotel so, be sure you reconfirm your crib before you arrive.

title: “Nice, but needs a bigger breakfast area”
text: We (family of four, kids aged 10 and 12) stayed here for one night when travelling from Florida to Virginia. We stayed in a room with two double beds. The room itself was clean and nicely furnished, but both my wife and I found it a little damp. The air conditioning was on so I couldn't understand why that would be the case. The beds and bedding were of good quality, as it typical of the Marriott chain. The hotel also had a nice outdoor pool area and was attractively landscaped. It was very convenient to I-77 for the car traveller. The hotel features a complimentary continental breakfast buffet that includes cereal, toast, muffins, bagels, waffles, juice, coffee, yogurt, etc. The buffet was good but the breakfast area was too small for the number of people. We initially had to wait to find a table to sit at. There was another long wait for the waffle iron. I filled out a comment card suggesting to management they needed a larger breakfast area and perhaps a second waffle iron.

title: “3rd rooms a charm”
text:
I travel for business and recently spent 4 nights at the Lancaster. The first room they gave me was on the second floor, right above the valet parkers - it was too noisy. Next, they have me this teeny little room on the 14th floor that was smaller than my walk in closet at home, I stayed on night, but was back at the front desk the next morning. Then they moved me to a beautiful deluxe room on the 11th floor, nice and quiet and tastefully decorated. The king size bed was extremely comfortable, the bathroon was nice, the tv was old and hard to watch. Room Service was horrible, don't order it, way over priced and then no taste. I ordered a BLT and throught brought it without any mayo... I ordered another sandwich that came with avacado, but never got the sandwich - it was all pretty hit and miss. The room was great, the temperatr conrols worked great. One night one of the valets drove me to the supermarket in his limo, I felt great about that. The best part of the Lancaster are the people who work there, always trying to make you feel at home. 
I can't wait to go back, next time I know what room to ask for. This is an older hotels, with history and very slow elavators, but its really nice.

title: “The W on Lexington is a great hotel to get away from the noise.”
text: Staying in NY for business can be quite hectic, and most of the hotels, especially those in times square, can be noisy and crouded. Walking into the W on Lexington is refreshing and morever, the hotel employees are kind and friendly. I have stayed here several times and Gloria Morales, who works at the front desk has always gone out of her way to make me feel welcome and help me when I have mixed up my reservations. The hotel is great, the service is friendly, and the gym is much larger than the one at many other NY hotels. The food at the bar could be better, but overall a great NY hotel.

title: “WOW!”
text: Wow, what a positive experience I had at the Madison Hotel! The new décor is great. The quality of the food is fantastic. The customer care from the wonderful staff at The Madison Hotel is top notch. If you are looking for a Hotel in Washington, DC go to the Madison Hotel. You will not go wrong!

title: “THE HEATED POOL MADE THE STAY A DREAM!!!”
text: My husband took me out for my birthday and I got this room on line. I noticed it had good rates and a pool and hot tub. We got there and there and the staff was nice, the hotel seemed clean, and the room was clean. The best part was the heated pool. We stayed there most of the time. The hot tub was great too!!

title: “Love Yotel.....quirky, cool and different”
text:
i just stayed at Yotel for the second time this year, the first time was on Business, so i stayed in a basic cabin....it was great they're compact but perfectly formed and completely teched up, plenty of sockets for charging, great TV's lots of nik nak space built in, great contemporary shower/wet area with incredible views over NY...perfect for 1 or 2 people on a whirlwind trip with lesser luggage as there isn't oodles of space for cases ( just 1 really ).
However on the second visit which i've just returned from i stayed in a VIP suite on the 26th floor and it was Incredible they are very trendily kitted out, large living area, spare sofa/bedroom with ensuite, large bedroom with moving circular bed that looks out over the hudson and the empire state building, quite an incredible view to wake up to ( though austin powers does spring to mind with the bed) :) there was a pool table in there, small side kitchen, coffee machine and large tv's, fire and 3 zeppelin Airs dotted around to stream music and there is apple TV fitted...it really is something pretty special, and i was even able to have 5 friends up to join me for dinner one evening, all 7 adults and 1 child could sit comfortably with so much space, and there are full length windows all around, so it doesn't matter where you are in the suite, there was always a spectacular view to look at.
The breakfast there if you do A la Carte is fantastic...my boyfriend is quite a food snob and even he said it is one of the best breakfasts he's ever had, also Dohyo do some of the finest, tastiest cuisine around, if you like sushi and chinese especially you HAVE to eat here it awakens the taste buds....it is still some of the tastiest food i have eaten.
The gym is great for short stays, though there are bike and run trails next to the hudson just a couple of blocks away.
There is also a really vibrant night scene there on a couple nights during the week, if i was one for having a good night out i would wonder downstairs to the club, but i'm more a chilled out in my room type person and surprisingly it is very insulated so the noise doesn't carry to the rooms.
the terrace is one of the largest outdoor terraces in NY and again its very trendy and a great hang out......
What else can i say i love this place, it epitomises, modern, fun, vibrant, quirky ...all in one.
only downside is where its situated could do with being maybe a few blocks east, but besides that the little walks to things are worth it.
enjoy if you stay there.

title: “LondonJoseph1”
text:
never has a hotel been borne a more inappropriate name. I was in the Grand Hyatt on business. I dont normally review, but I thought I would this time. Dreadful. NOT the staff - they were helpful and polite. It was the state of the rooms that amazed me. Put your hand in your pocket please, Mr Hyatt and invest in some decent rooms becase, at the prices you charge, it is nothing short of despicable. Thank goodness my company was paying and I didnt stop the weekend as I initially thought I might because, if prices were the same as my employer paid, Id be $1000 down
To say a Travel Lodge would have been a huge improvement is an understatement. The room was small and pokey, the shower was cold when I first used it and the bathroom was so minuscule that I worried about my glasses falling off the sink and disappearing down the loo. 
In comparison to some other people's stories, my irritations are, of course, minor. But for the price they charge, the deal could not have been worse, in my view. Hotels in the USA are normally a delight. This one was (ahem) disappointing.

title: “Wonderful Staff”
text:
Great location. The property is clean and well maintained. We liked the restaurant but food prices are a bit high for the current market.
We can't say enough good things about the helpfulness and friendliness of the staff. My partner had a medical emergency (all is well now) and we very much appreciated the assistance provided in contacting medical help (on-call Dr), arranging a wheelchair and transportation to hospital. After the incident we were approached by many staff who we had not been in contact with before expressing concern and asking if anything else was needed. They hotel very kindly offered an excellent rate for our unexpected extension. This should not detract from the friendly service in the restaurant etc whose staff were not involved in our emergency. I would come back just bescause of the service.
The no-charge internet access, under the circumstances, was a Godsend as we worked through all sorts of insurance and transportation issues.
Thank you VERY much.

title: “Safe location, close to metro, quick comute, reasonable price.”
text:
Safe LOCATION, a quick 5-10 minute walk straight down the street to the red line Van ness station, a 15-20 minute metro ride to Metro Center. There is a McDonald's next door for breakfast. We ate at the Chinese restaurant down the street and the Pizza place diagonally across the street. Both restaurants were decent. There is a CVS, a market and liqour store within walking distance. Super Shuttle took us to the airport. 
 The ROOM'S were small but comfortable. There was a big flat screen TV. The rugs could have used a good vacuuming in the corners and the heater needed dusting. The bathroom was newly tiled and very clean. The matresses were brand new (no sign of bed bugs). We had a good nite's sleep in a quite room. There was an Avis rent a car behind us. For $90 this was a DC bargin. I was dissapointed that I was unable to print my boarding passes on their internet(3 terminals in lobby), and the front desk could not help me. 
 The STAFF was very nice. They let us leave our luggage there as we went sight seeing. Lost and Found mailed us our left behind cell phone charger. A great experience.

title: “Amazing place to stay!”
text: We stayed at the Affinia Gardens from November 9-12th and just loved it. The rooms are huge. We had a group of 6 girl-friends staying there and it was plenty of room. We used the kitchen to brush teeth and the makeup mirror to get ready, so others could shower in the bathroom. It was really nice. We were not too crowded. The location was great. We felt very safe at all times. Kris even helped us with a ride to the airport and it was even cheaper than Super Shuttle. They were very nice and helpful. The rooms were clean and our requests (extra towels, etc) were met in a very efficient amount of time. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Mildly surprise at the overall service and the staff was complimentary and helpful”
text: Plan to return if the circumstances present itself again. Manager " Connie " was a very accomodating and cheerful personality.

title: “Great location for a night out”
text:
We had a perfect night in this great hotel. It's surrounded by a lot of good restaurants and shopping. The rooms our very well done and the bathrooms are big with a great shower.
From our room we can see the whole city skyline so it's got great views from the upper floors.

title: “What a place!”
text: Just went back to the fairmont..after 20 years!!! It was as wonderful as it was then! The rooms as beautiful , checkin was done by the dearest young man and I was up graded to a wonderful room.Very pleased with my entire stay!

title: “Very Average Marriott with Below than Average Service”
text: I stayed here one night in November 2009. The last time I was at this hotel was July of 2004. The hotel has not changed much since 2004. The service was really bad. I stood in line to check in for about 20 minutes. There was only one person working the front desk. I had been told, via email, there would be a guest ambassador for quick check in.... this person was MIA. I saw the counter the ambassador would use, but it was tucked away and not in service. The room was dark and a bit on the small side. I do not like when I am working at the desk and I can reach to my side and touch the bed. The room is way too small when that happens. The gym was nice and was the highlight of the short stay. I checked into the Hilton on the other side of the convention center from this hotel and it is a much better value than the Marriott. I would stay here again if I could not get into the Hilton. It has a great location to the convention center, but thats really the only thing that would bring me back to the hotel.

title: “Safe, Clean and Convenient!!”
text: My 9 year old daughter and I stayed here for 4 days last week. I was a little concerned about safety, but my mind was put at ease by the other reviews. The staff was so nice to us and really went out of their way to make us feel welcome. We were even given a "goody bag" upon arrival, which was the coolest thing for my daughter! Our room was on the small side, but was large enough for 2 twin beds, a desk, entertainment center and our luggage. The bathroom was clean and even had a hair dryer, coffee maker and window shelf for all of things. The BEST thing about this hotel is the location. You are literally steps away from Times Square! We walked everywhere (Today Show, shopping on Fifth Ave. and all Broadway shows). For the price, you can not go wrong here. If you are going to New York to sit in a big expensive hotel room, then you are going for the wrong reasons!! We will stay at this location on all of our future trips and will highly recommend it to our family and friends.

title: “It does what it needs to do”
text:
My stay was quick, less than 24 hours. But in that time, I found the front desk and bell staff to be friendly, the rooms to be comfortable (but "cozy and dark"), and the location to be convenient for walking to my meetings and dinner. In addition, the fitness center was open 24 hours, which is always a plus when you have to be someplace early in the morning. 
If I was traveling with another person, I'd definitely look for a hotel with larger rooms and bathrooms. But for a single traveler, this did the trick.

title: “Not my favorite HIE”
text: We got a great deal at the HIE, Fisherman’s Wharf, so I can’t complain. The room was clean and comfortable and that’s most important. One of the features at the Holiday Inn Express is the free breakfast. It’s a light buffet, usually with cold cereals, breads, juice, fruit, and yogurt. Plus, they have some hot items – usually scrambled eggs and bacon or sausage, biscuits and gravy, and sometimes a pancake maker. We usually take advantage of these free breakfasts and we did again at HIE, Fisherman’s Wharf. However, this was the most chaotic breakfast at any HIE I have ever stayed in. I presume that it is because it’s the biggest HIE I’ve ever stayed in. We finally managed to make a couple of plates of food, but then had to take it back to our room to eat because there was nowhere to sit due to the breakfast area being completely inadequate for the number of guests the hotel can accommodate. The elevators were also an issue – just because of the volume of people trying to use them. We tried to find the stairs, but had no luck. Worth it for what we paid, but not my favorite HIE.

title: “Yes!”
text: The room was very clean and the decor is just like the picture if not better. The staff is friendly and EXTREMELY helpful. The beds were big and comfortable. Cab fare around town from the hotel is nominal. This is the place to be if you want to get what you pay for plus more. I will be back!

title: “Will definitely be staying again!”
text: We stayed at the Cresent for 4 nights and absolutely loved it. It is a cool, boutique hotel in a great location, and the Burritt Room bar on the 2nd floor was one of our favorite spots in San Fran. The rooms are a little on the small side but they are clean and well designed and we weren't in our room that much anyways. The beds are incredibly comfortable, I slept better there than in my own bed at home! My only negative review would be that the people at the front desk were not very friendly. I recommend requesting a room on one of the top floors facing Union Square, if not you may end up with a window facing a brick wall. Overall, great experience and we will definitely stay there again on our next trip to the city.

title: “Nice clean rooms for the price. Very quiet. Would recommend to others”
text: My stay at the comfort lodge was pleasant and nice. Decent rooms for the price. Better than the other motels down the road.

title: “Great hotel right in the middle of everything you can walk to!”
text: We used hotwire to get a good deal for a very special 1st Anniversary evening. And we got a great deal and the hotel I really wanted, Omni Chicago. The hotel was a 4 star hotel with all of the perks. Check in was fast and we were greeted with a glass of champaign. I told them it was our anniversary ahead of time and they gave us a corner suite with an unbelievable view of Michigan Ave and the Hancock building. The room was spacious and the bed was comfortable. We signed up with Omni's Select Guest program - a great extra perk. They provide a turn down service, and your choice of complimentary beverages in the morning. After coming back from dinner there was a wonderful piece of chocolate cake in our room with Happy Anniversary written on the plate in chocolate. A VERY nice added touch! We used the workout facility in the morning (had everything that one would need) but did not use the pool, the only thing that did not impress us. It was very small and the space needs a little more TLC. Check out was a breeze and we were given a bottle water upon check out. The only other negative would be how much valet costs ($46). Crazy expensive. I would suggest to use the over night parking garage near the Peninusula Hotel ($29) for the night. But overall I give the hotel, service and ammenties an A+. Thank you for a wonderful Anniversary!

title: “Ask for an upgrade”
text: We booked our stay the the Peabody through Hotwire and got what we thought was a pretty good deal $159 before taxes, and that included all of the "added extra's" other's have described except for self parking. When we arrived at 4:00pm Hotwire had still not sent our reservation to the hotel. My wife was a little stress out by the desk staff, Joanna, was fantastic. When we gave her our Hotwire reservation sheet she assured us that we would have a room. After reading a review that recommended to ask for a room upgrade I figured this would be the perfect time to ask for an upgrade... When she returned we we upgraded from a second to the bottom tier room to a second from the top tier room. The room itself was beautiful and the bed was fantastic. We did go down to the lobby to see the duck's walk from their pond to the elevator. 2 drinks at the lobby bar as we waited was $20, overpriced but about what was expected at this type of hotel. The lobby is a zoo during the duck march, it would be nice if they had a preferred place for guests of the hotel to watch the ducks over the general public, but no such luck. The restaurants at the hotel are nice, but also very overpriced. Not a good option when there are so many other very good places to eat within a 5 minute walk of the hotel. Room service breakfast was also declined by us as a basic 2 eggs, meat, juice, toast, and coffee for 2 was over $50. Coffee service, that $10 fee people are writing about, stops at 7am so get up early if you want a free coffee as there are no coffee makers in the room. We went for a dip in the pool, very nice Roman Bath theme with a pool and hot tub. The fitness center looked very nice, but we did not use it. Overall a nice place, it was well worth seeing once, and for what we paid compared to other hotels in Memphis it was well worth it. The hotel's restaurants are very poor value and I would not pay what they ask for a meal with all of the other great places to eat nearby.

title: “casual clean and friendly in the beach”
text: Bright new rooms in a vintage building, friendly young desk staff and the ocean side. Top it off with the weird, the Hot and the Pitiful in the boardwalk and you won't need the big plasma TV in the rooms. Not cheap but good value. Thanks, Cadillac

title: “Affordable luxury”
text: Found a great rate by searching on line for this beautiful hotel on Nob Hill. Small lobby. Upgraded to larger room which had small kitchenette, plenty of closet space. Cable car stops in front. Friendly staff. Clean. Dated but charming.

title: “Convenient for the convention centre”
text:
Stayed here for a few days attending a conference at the convention centre. It is extremely convenient for the convention centre - just across the street. The hotel itself looks better on the web-site than in reality. All in all, it is pretty comfortable. A few specifics:
Location - marvellous for the convention centre, being right across the street. It is in downtown, but Phoenix downtown is not particularly exciting - there isnt really very much there. But arguable, this is a problem with Phoenix, not the hotel.
Lobby - definitely looks better in teh web-site than in reality.
Breakfast - Food not good and the waiters/waitresses I find a bit blunt, even a bit rude. Smile please, and be a bit more sincere.
Room - clean, tidy, well maintained, spacious, well decorated. But there isnt a comfy chair or a coffee table - the only chair in my room was the chair at the work table. Checking the picture on the website, these arent there either.
Wifi-wired - apparent, only the lower floors has wired access.
Restaurant - the restaurant at the top of the hotel seems very popular - every time I wanted to go there, it is full, so havent managed to eat there. Had dinner once in the sports bar instead. Food OK.
Coffee shop - it has a starbuck style coffee shop on the ground floor which is very good, and convenient.

title: “Great expectations met!”
text: My teens love it! We are locals but stay when girls have volleyball at convention center. Tried another hotel attached to convention area but convenience didn't compare to comfort, amenities and staff. We are back to the Magnolia to stay. Beautiful skyline view from rooftop pool. Breakfast was fantabulous. Something for everyone. The garden bathtubs are wonderful. The valet staff is great, one gentlemen remembered us from last year, pretty amazing considering there is one of him and thousands of guests. Shuttle service to and from convention was quick and easy. My hat's off to those guys!

title: “Perfect End to a Perfect Road Trip Around Washington/Oregon”
text:
Stay here the last two nights of our Road Trip and it was a wise choice. Had room 2215 on the 22nd floor a corner room with great views.
