Everything was fantastic. Felt right at home as we had the Everton Football Team staying at the same time.
The hotel position was great within walking distance of everywhere. We even walked 1 block to the train to get to the airport at a cost of $2.50 each.
Would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Terrible terrible”
text:
I give the hotel one start because I cannot give it any less.
My colleague and I stayed at the Howard Johnson Express Inn - Washington for slightly less than a week while attending a conference in Washington DC. 
The hotel is not in a neighborhood where you would feel safe walking outside alone. Also, the cab took a very long time (around 20-45min) to arrive each time we call for one.
The hotel is old and run down. The magnetic card locks were all broken down. Every time we wanted to return to our room (be it after getting some snacks from the vending machine or after breakfast or after a day trip out), we need to get the male receptionist to open the door for us with the master key card. And, what's even more horrendous, he would just open any door for us without first verifying if we are the registered occupant of the room we wanted to open! This made us worry a lot about the security of the belongings we have in our room. (I'm not sure if this has improved since our return and I really hope it had!)
Halfway through our stay, after returning to the hotel after the day's meeting, my colleague was shocked to realized that the hotel had changed his room for him in his absence and without his consent. The hotel also acknowledged having moved my colleague's belongings from his previous room to his next one. I'm not sure if this violated the privacy of my colleague. Fortunately, he did not find anything missing. The hotel's excuse was that the daytime repair going on at the hotel had caused his room to leak. Instead of apologizing for the inconveniences caused to my colleague, the hotel receptionist challenged my colleague if he would rather stay in a wet room or a dry one. 
In addition, I witness the roaming of a couple of mice running around the hotel, both inside the hotel lobby cum breakfast area as well as inside my hotel room. I had to pack all my belonging and lock my luggage each day in the hope of preventing any accidental entrance of any of these mice into my luggage. It also made me wonder just how safe and hygienic the breakfast served by the hotel was.
This had indeed been an eye-opener for both my colleague and I. For those planning a trip to the area, do think twice.

title: “Great, Intimate Hotel”
text:
There are about four hotels in my regular NYC rotation, The Pierre, The Plaza Athenee, the Mandarin Oriental and the Lowell. The Mayfair Regent was also a fave, but it succummed a few years back.
In general I like smaller, older and more intimate hotels that have great locations. The Lowell is all that and more. The rooms can be small, but if all I wanted was a bigger room, I'd stay at the Courtyard by Marriott.
The Lowell drips charm and the staff is well trained and very attentive to your needs. This last trip was no exception. Everything was perfect in the bathroom, you get a nightly turndown service and a concierge who knows his business.

title: “Would go back!”
text: I stayed here in February with my teenage daugher and her friend. The hotel is very clean, beds are comfy and the room was spacious enough for us (we didn't spend much time there). The concierege could have been a little more friendly, but I guess that's all part of the "NYC charm"! The location is PERFECT for everything, yet a bit out of the way so you can escape a little. The heart of Times Square, and many theaters are just a short walk. Also, the parking is so convienent, additional money, but well worth it IMO.

title: “Girl's weekend in Chicago”
text:
We had a roll away bed in our room and there was barely enough room to turn around. The mini bar was locked as well and they didn't give us the key until day 2 of a 3 day stay. Mind you it was the Marathon weekend and everyone was pretty overwhelmed.
The staff was very friendly and they did try hard to make our stay comfortable. The room was just too small for 3 women to stay.

title: “Great hotel with very recent renovation...”
text:
Loved the modern decor & the hotel overall! The only reasons I didn't rate "excellent" across the board. 1) not enough drawer space in the room 2) even though we were on a "quiet floor" you can hear the people in the next room (literally when they flush their toilet). The room rate was pretty high but that's the going rate for a nice hotel in Union Square. I found the most reasonable rate through the hotel's website (pre-pay, non-refundable). 
With that said, everything else was wonderful! They let us check-in early & beds/pillows were amazingly comfortable.

title: “Beautiful Luxurious Historic Hotel /Wonderful Location”
text:
We stayed with the kids and went to see the Lion King show and enjoyed our dinner along with a Wonderful Suite.
Thanks to Omni for a Great Stay!

title: “Location location location”
text: I have stayed in quite a few hotels in NYC and even though this is a little run down and there is no restaurant or breakfast like they advertise on their website, the location, room size and service makes up for it. I had my 16 month old son with me and we were able to walk to everything I wanted to see. The location is amazing, to me it's in the heart of the city. The rooms are massive which I've never seen in NYC unless your paying 400 a night somewhere and the service is great. They did get rid of the bfast, but you can call for a coffee maker and honestly in NYC you can find breakfast anywhere. I would stay there again.

title: “Great Choice Near SAT If You Have a Car”
text:
My wife and I stayed at this property for two nights earlier this month. The property was initially an Amerisuites that was converted into a HGI. This is the reason it does not look like most HGI properties.
We were in San Antonio for a family gathering halfway between SAT and downtown. We had a rental car at our disposal which would be optimal to choose this property. 
We were impressed with all aspects of our stay.
There was ample free parking.
Check in was easy and quick.
Our room was modern, quiet and clean. The room had a flat screen TV with multiple channel selections and comfortable beds. The bathroom was well maintained with a tub/shower in good working order.
The business center was well maintained and in good working order.
The full breakfast had a great variety, was in a pleasant open setting and the wait staff was friendly and helpful.
Check out was easy and all charges were appropriate and correct.
In short, I had only positive experiences at this property.

title: “Always a safe bet, but...”
text:
This is my third time there as I love the location (a lot of walking-distance options for shopping spree, such as Macy's, Victoria's Secret, GAP, Sephora, etc), free wifi and breakfast. Also, wonderful cookies every afternoon. Half block from Penn Station.
We had a 2 double bed room, very clean, and nice shower. But...I just don't understand why they do not have safety box in the rooms!
There are only 2 elevators, so expect some wait during rush hours (breakfasts and check out times).
One important note: I amended my reservation during my stay ( added an extra night) and the staffer forgot to update my account. After a lot of complaining ( they said hotel was sold-out), and because it was their fault, manager got me another room. But it was an inexcusable mistake, fortunately they've got it right.

title: “Blah”
text:
I stay at lots of Marriotts for business...not sure why I picked this one. First off, Courtyards don't make sense for gold/platinum members as they are the only Marriott property where you don't get free breakfast...and here they wanted almost 15 bucks for some eggs and pancakes.
As for this particular hotel...its OK if you need to walk to the Navy Yard, but the parking garage stinks...they even told me at the front desk it is "first come first served"...I guess if you get in to town late you are in trouble because there is NO other parking around.
Rooms were on the smallish side, but clean. TV service was spotty, internet connection was typical (i.e. mediocre at best). Staff was friendly overall.
I'd stay again if I had to...i.e. if I was in town, with no car, had a meeting at the Navy Yard, etc...and I suppose it would have been nice if there was a Nats game!

title: “Warm welcome for weary wanderer...”
text: Last minute trip and arrived late. Nearby hotels already booked (and pricey). Made a call to HIE on Spencer and they delivered in a big way! The little things made the best impression - such as bottled water and a newspaper at no extra charge. I so appreciated being treated as a welcome friend and not as a victim of highway robbery!

title: “Terrific Family Hotel”
text: We have stayed here twice and love it. We plan on staying again this March. Rooms are very comfortable, plenty of room for kids and adults. But the complex with the waterpark area is awesome for kids. They have a lazy river, a water slide, basketball court, etc. Kids can swim, play with friends, etc while parents hang out with them or lounge by the pool.

title: “Disappointed”
text: It really takes a lot for me to complain, and I know this is an airport hotel, but although it is a Hilton ... it is NO Hilton. First of all, I will give credit where it is due. The staff at the front desk and concierge were polite and helpful. The breakfast was good. We didn't experience the noise issue (i.e., hearing others through the walls) as other people have mentioned. The rooms were clean. But, like others have stated, the hotel is mediocre at best. First of all, the rooms, while updated in some areas, were also lacking in others. We found the lighting to be poor, there was no fan in the bathroom, the sofa was old and dirty, the fridge smelt like "feet" when we opened it, and the air conditioner was incredibly loud and went on and off every minute all night long. Exercise room and pool were nothing special. I think the worst part was the valet service though. I couldn't believe how unprofessional the service was. I SO agree with setter1vb who stated that the staff have NO sense of urgency and stand around talking - that is, when they aren't taking "breaks" and can't be found. The complimentary shuttle will get you to the airport once the driver can be located - you just may miss your flight in the meantime, though. There was also no attention to detail, as we found out when we retrieved our luggage from the storage room and were given the wrong bag because the tag wasn't even checked. And then there was the taxi ride from hell. We had them call us a cab as we were going out for dinner, and we don't know where this driver came from (suspect connection to valet staff), but he arrived in a beat-up black vehicle, told us we "didn't need" to put on our seatbelts, drove like a maniac and ran several red lights, took about 5 personal phone calls during all this, and then ... brought us to the wrong restaurant! And then did it for a second time! He had no idea where he was going, and we ended up being 30 minutes late for our reservation. This Embassy Suites hotel cannot compare with the Embassy Suites that we stayed in last year in Chicago. It was like staying at a completely different hotel. What a disappointment.

title: “Terrific hotel”
text: European feel, fabulous restaurant/bar and thoughtful service. I spent 5 nights there. The hotel is beautiful and staff is extraordinary. Perfectly situated, right at the north end of the Magnificent Mile, but not right on a main street.

title: “Outstanding Customer Focus”
text: My brother was getting married in Baltimore and I arranged for much of my extended family to fly in from all corners of the country and we used the Sheraton Inner Harbor as our base hotel. My family members were of all ages, a number of them with special needs, and all the normal chaos and dysfunction that goes along with a big family event like a wedding! While the event wasn't at the Sheraton, you wouldn't have known that based on how they supported everyone. From the valet to the front desk to Rena the outstanding concierge, they greeted us all by name, kept us moving in the right directions, and always did it with a great attitude and a friendly smile. Getting even two people in my family to agree on a place to eat is a small miracle, and from restaurant reservations to transportation support to special needs in the room, they handled everything without missing a beat. From my perspective, any hotel can have a great staff member. This hotel has a great staff. Everyone is clearly enabled to not just respond to your needs, but to anticipate them. I felt so fortunate I had chosen this hotel because their service was so good, I didn't have to worry about my elderly parents or my young cousins or my aunt that can't make up her mind. My family is like herding cats, and the staff at the Sheraton Inner Harbor were like the cat whisperers! Beyond the service, the rooms were fine, location is great, lots of places to eat and visit nearby, and great access to the Metro (in and out from the airport) and Camden Yards. I wish I had the staff at this hotel organizing my life at home.

title: “Perfect place for our family vacation”
text: Our family of five stayed here 3 nites, monday thru wednesday, and we couldn't have been happier. We had a two bedroom, two bath suite and a pull-out sofa in the living room. We choose the Homewood Suites based on its ability to sleep all five of us in one room. The beds were very comfortable as was the bedding. Having two bathrooms with sinks separate the shower/toilet area was great for us getting ready in the mornings and also for getting the kids ready for bed after swimming at night. The breakfasts in the morning were better and larger than expected. The light dinners were more like a full meal to us. We ate dinner on two of the nights, spaghetti, meatballs, garlic bread, and salad bar one night and chicken fajitas, rice, beans and salad bar the next. My wife and I especially liked the wine and beer they offered. A nice way to end a long day of "touristy" adventures. The hotel was centerally located for all of our planned activities, seaworld, zoo, beaches, midway, etc. We would definately recommend this place to all our family and friends. We will seek out other Homewood Suites whenever we travel based on our stay here.

title: “Unexpected Gem”
text: Was expecting a new, but budget hotel in a less desirable area with few facilities and tiny rooms - however, I was pleasantly surprised. Hotel was chic and up to date, room was clean and spacious and very well appointed, staff were knowledgable, helpful and friendly and the location was great. The location in Harlem is in a great neighborhood with excellent restaurants, bars and quick access to Central Park and Columbia University.

title: “Not bad, but tried to rip us off”
text: We reserved this hotel for a last minute one night stay through the westin web site. According to the web site, we reserved a king, non-smoking. However, when we go to the hotel, they claimed to not have any kings on a non-smoking floor. They offered a queen. We went to look at it, and it was a double! The same double I could have booked for $30 less on the web site. We called down to reception, and asked to see the king, smoking. It didn't smell bad, so we took it. However, the hotel was far less than accomodating! The bed and shower were "heavenly," but the service was far from it.

title: “Good place to stay in Manhattan”
text: Excellent point, great room and friendly staff. Next time in New York we will stay there again for sure. It has all nearby. Restaurants, supermarket, subway, good shops...

title: “Great value”
text: Excellent hotel and friendly staff. The hotel is in a convenient location. The rooms are clean and attractive.

title: “good location, reasonable hotel”
text:
The location is excellent. Worried about some other reviews here I asked for a quiet room and was given one on a higher floor at the back. I didn't have any noise problem.
I agree with others that the staff are friendly and helpful. The rooms are reasonable, a little on the small side for my liking. The bathroom was about as small as it could be. The bed was large and very comfortable. 
The room had no coffee/tea making facility which I missed. 
Aspects of the hotel seem a little faded but it was a good choice, although not my first one, for a few days in DC.

title: “Can't seem to understand why it only gets 3,5 stars”
text:
OK, it's a bit noisy in the neighbourhood, but if you close the windows and book it as an overnight stay before or after your flight, it's a perfect stay!
Close to the airport and car rental companies (for picking up or returning your car), great service (they even suggested picking us up at the rental car company), friendly staff, clean and spacious rooms, very good bed, 24h shuttle, fresh fruit at breakfast (even at 5.30am!), ...
Don't expect it to be the best stay for visiting LA, but as a perfect stay before or after your flight.
Parking lot is a bit small for the number of rooms they provide though.

title: “Wonderful hotel, wonderful location!”
text: We just came back from a four day get away in San Francisco. We stayed at the Chancellor Hotel. The hotel is in a perfect location with the cable car stop just outside the front door. The room was quiet, clean, airy, and very comfortable. We took advantage of trying out their pillow choices during our stay. The staff was friendly and helpful. If you want a home away from home in San Francisco I would definitely suggest the Chancellor!

title: “Solid Choice”
text: As other reviewers have stated, the staff at this hotel is exceptional. The rooms are nice - sort of bland and corporate but spacious with comfortable beds and crisp linens. The location isn't scenic or charming, but it's a quick walk to Union Square, Moscone and lots of transportation options. When you leave the hotel, just make sure you're properly oriented and walking in the right direction as it is quite close to some seedy areas.

title: “Nice Place to Stay”
text:
This motel is tight next to Baptist Medical Center, there are three places to eat within walking distance ( two fast food and one sit down). The hotel was having problems with one of the two elevators while I was there, this slow down access to the ground floor for some guests, 
The room was what you would expect for a this type of hotel. 
Getting out into traffic in the morning can be hard, unitl you learn to go thru Baptist Medical Center and get to the light there.

title: “A tiny, cozy, wonderful experience.”
text:
To celebrate my 21st birthday my Mum and I decided to take a trip to New York. I began researching early on and heard about this little place called "The Pod Hotel". After reading some reviews on here (thank you!) we decided that this was the place for us. We didn't want to spend money on a fancy place to be unconscious because we knew we'd spend most of our week out exploring. But the time spent at the Pod was always great. From stepping into the colourful lobby where we were checked in quickly and efficiently to checking out the tiny room. 
I've read some negative stuff about the staff but I feel like I need to come to their defense. Just as an example, one night we brought a bottle of wine back to the hotel and realized we didn't have a corkscrew - the front desk clerk went running around trying to find one for us and delivered! I wish I had his name...
I could go on about the room itself the but all the pictures and other reviews would make that redundant. Needless to say we enjoyed all the amenities.
The location worked out for us and we managed to walk to most places. Central Park, Times Square, Rockefeller Plaza, the list goes on. As for places to eat you basically walk to 2nd Ave, close your eyes, and point and you'll be headed in the direction of some place wonderful. We tired not to repeat places but found ourselves at the Morningstar Cafe twice.
If you're claustrophobic or a germaphobe this place may not be for you with its tight quarters and shared facilities. But I like the economy of it all and it definitely made my trip a lot easier and cheaper.

title: “Great location, ghetto room!”
text: Walking distance to Times Square, across the street from Penn Station. Nice lobby. It goes downhill from there. The rooms are filthy, with paint peeling from the walls and ceiling. You don't want to walk on the carpets with bare feet. It is a real scuzzy place!

title: “First Time in New York”
text: Le Parker Meridien was delightful... We checked in at 1030am and the room was amazing with a beautiful view of Central Park. The Burgers were fabulous and the pool was refreshing after our long days of sightseeing. The staff was always very friendly and the location was ideal. When we return to New York City we will be returning to this amazing hotel!

title: “Great price and convenient!”
text:
Club Quarters Wall Street is located in a great location in downtown New York. It is conveniently located right near the corner of William and Wall Streets. The Wall Street station is just a few steps from the doors and it is a short 5 minute walk to the 9/11 Memorial site. Only about a 10 minute walk to Battery Park and the Statue of Liberty/Ellis Island Ferry. Plenty of great restaurants in the area. 
The hotel itself is simple and nothing to fancy. We have stayed here twice (both times less than $145.00) per night over weekends. In New York that is unheard of. The rooms are a decent size and very clean. The showers are a little small but were sufficient for our needs. For NY hotels rooms, the size of the room was decent. There is a nice desk area and closet in the room as well. 
On each floor there is a guest closet with extra pillows, blankets, toiletries, etc. This is very convenient and you don;t have to wait for these items to be delivered. There are also irons, and ironing boards available in this closet as well. The hotel also offers free, purified bottled water on each floor. 
The majority of the staff are very friendly, however, we did encounter several that couldn't even say hello. 
Check-in/check-out is very simple and is done through a kiosk. We were able to check in over 3 hours early both times we have stayed here. The front desk is located right next to the two kiosks in case you need help. 
Overall, pleasant stay both times at a price you can't beat.

title: “not realy suites,but excellant value”
text: my family and i stayed for four nights on our vacation.the room was pretty small but we managed to make it work.the landscaping was perfect, rooms were very clean.kids liked the pool.no noise complaints.overall excellant value for the price

title: “A very nice luxury hotel”
text:
This is a beautiful hotel with very nice rooms. The bed was soo comfortable. The furniture was very classy and there was always about 5 people standing at the front door ready to open the door for you. The valet guy was very helpful even though we did not valet. We parked at the lot across the street which was much cheaper than the valet, but not as convienient. The room was absolutely gorgeous. the bathroom was nice and there were complimentary bath robes for you to use. 
This is a great hotel for baseball fans. There is a bridge connecting the hotel to Petco Park. There is also tons of baseball memorabilia scattered throughout the hotel. There are things such as Babe Ruth's baseball bat (I think) or someone else's shoes, etc. Very nice. 
My only complaint is that it is near a port (or something) and there was a lot of noise in the morning. I looked out the window to find out that there were giant machines moving things that were either contruction material or containers to be put on a ship. I"m not sure because I couldn't really get a good look at what they were doing. but there was a lot of noise. It seemed to be a GIANT crane that was making all the noise. 
Other than that... this was an excellent hotel and I would recommend it to anyone!

title: “It's not that bad. Read my review!”
text: It really is'nt that bad remember. That you are paying for what you get the location is perfect.The hotel is in a prime location, 5mins walk from anything of interest and 2secs from penn station to take you anywhere further, for the price you pay for this hotel you cant ask for any better, i come to new york every year and always try and stay in this hotel the years i have been unable to stay in this hotel i have been extremely dissapointed if you think this is bad go and stay in the new yorker then you will be able to Complain!!! just go to new york and enjoy your self just remember while your there shopping and site seeing how long will you actually be spending in the hotel?

title: “Location is nearly everything”
text: Ideally located just two short blocks from Union Square, this hotel has a lot of character and friendly staff. We were in a room in the back so no street noise although when there is garbage pick-up, that changes but fortunately, it's quickly over with. Will definitely stay again when in San Francisco.

title: “YUCK......Never again”
text:
This place is terrible. They totally deceive you on-line, so please make sure to do research prior to staying here. The room was not clean, half of the few tv channels did not work, and the staff is really rude. The price is not that great to endure all of these headaches. Also, one of the cab drivers told me that they found a dead body in one of the rooms. Although, it is in a really good location (minus the gentlemen's club right next door) and the subway it really close.....that's really the only nice thing I have to say about it.
I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND THIS PLACE TO MY WORSE ENEMY!!!!!!

title: “Best Beds Ever”
text: Arrived at the hotel on a Friday night which is the best time to go to Washington as you can park on the street. The receptionist was extremely helpful and showed us on a map all the places of interest. The best bit was when we went up to the room we found the biggest most comfortable bed we have ever slept in. I would stay in that hotel again purely for the bed! The room was large, clean and comfortable with a fridge, ironing board, alarm clock. Hotel also has a business centre and you can use the internet for free. Hotel is only a very short walk from the White House and surrounding area.

title: “Christmas and an engagement...”
text:
Looking for a great way to capture some of the Christmas season spirit and a way to surprise my girlfriend, I took advantage of low cost shuttle tickets from DCA-LGA to hit the City for some shopping and Nutcracker tickets. From TripAdvisor- I selected Hotel Giraffe.
Location: 27th and Park is a great location. Not on the main path, but really is a good walking location for the major attractions. Cabs were always available when we looked for them, and if you needed the staff- the doorman easily tracks a cab down for one.
First impression: Newer construction. Extremely nice art decco look when you walk in. No major signs of wear and tear. Doorman was more than eager to assist. Front desk was able to check us in early due to room availability. Staff was very friendly and consistent. 
Room: Having worked in the city previously- and staying in the boutique or unique hotels, the room (minisuite) was very spacious, superb high ceilings- and over all way bigger than most NYC properties. The bed was comfortable. Pillows--if you don't like the down pillows and need a bit more substance to a pillow...ask to see what they have. We did not know until too late. Linens were great. Towels- nice! I personally like the small architectural details in the rooms- hospital track for the shower curtain, the wave glass pocket doors...It is fair to say- our room looked like the website and met all of our expectations.
Staff: Cleaning/Maintenance people were super efficient and omnipresent. Never in the forefront- they were none the less out and about performing. Front Desk-super friendly. Concierge like questions handled efficiently without too many recommendations that were really tied into marketing relations! That is a nice thing. The staff does read their email if you have a special need or comment. Use that- for they are really responsive. They took note of my comment about the pending engagement and made sure to ask how all went that night. Thank you!
Club: The club had a long line of patrons after 11:00 pm- looked like it was just starting to crank when we returned. Did not use, but looked like a nice dressed crowd.
Breakfast: Couple of comments from others I agree with- we were running late, had about 15-20 minutes before hours were done. I came down to grab a bite for us to take up. The morning crew was busy already beginning their break-down so pickings were slim, and it was a bit of an inquisition to get some silverware and cream cheese to take upstairs to everyone getting ready for check-out and the Nutcracker. 
Concierge Service recommendation for dinner: Many thanks to the crew for recommending Primehouse. Part of the BRGuest chain, the steakhouse is located on 26th...it was one of the best steaks that we've had in some time.
And yes- Hotel Giraffe was part of our engagement...after shopping all day, we came back cleaned up (and I slipped the ring into my coat). We took a leisurely 5 minute walk over to the Empire State Building- shot up to the 102d floor...and with just my son, my "fiancee" and the guard- I used the sights and night to propose.
Lasting impressions: Hotel Giraffe- great place. Will always think back fondly- and shall return. Look for the right price and your value far exceeds the nightly fee. It is a welcome change to the usual big chains that us corporate road warriors have to stay in.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: This hotel was beautifully decorated and super chic! The lounge was stunning with a huge gas fireplace, lots of couches and floor-to-ceiling windows. There was also free wine tasting in the lounge every evening from 5-6, but we were never back at the hotel in time. The rooms were also stunning. We had a very nice view of the surrounding city. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful. The only complaint I could make was service at the attached hotel bar was very slow on our first visit and the cocktail server seemed annoyed by our presence. However, on the second evening, we ordered a bottle of wine from a very friendly bartender and were able to take it back to the hotel lounge to enjoy it in quiet. The bar gets quite packed on the weekends. I have read other reviews that it is noisy, so I might suggest that you request a room on a higher floor. Our room on the 14th floor was very quiet.

title: “A great stay!”
text:
We really enjoyed our 9 night stay in The Westin, Gaslamp Quarter. The room was stylishly decorated with a huge bed and everything we needed including toiletries, an iron and ironing-board and safe. The room also had a kettle/coffee perculator but our only complaint would be that tea-bags were limited for those who don't drink coffee. We also paid over $11 to have a pot of tea brought to our room by room service late one evening.
The views over the harbour were fantastic and the pool area and jacuzzi were great for lazy days and evenings.
On the whole, we really enjoyed our stay at the Westin and would recommend it to others.

title: “Clean and comfy”
text:
We stayed at the Hampton Inn and Suites in Downtown Seattle for two nights prior to a cruise to Alaska.
Our taxi from the airport cost us $40
The hotel was well situated close the the Space Needle and within easy walking distance of Pike Street Market and the main shopping area. (warning - it is quite hilly) A monorail runs from the Needle to the edge of the retail district and you can hop on and off metro buses within a free zone in the centre if you feel you cannot walk.
 There was a large 24hr supermarket I block away which was very well stocked. And across the road up the hill was a nice little bar that was buzzing.
The beds were large and very comfortable and the rooms were at a nice temperature. The bathrooms were clean and the shower was good with the usual complimentary toiletries.
The breakfast buffet was good with fruit, cereals, a small selection of hot items and toast with jams, marmalade etc.
Coffee was always available in reception and there was free internet access. The folks on reception were very friendly.
All in all a place I could recommend.

title: “Cute decor, friendly staff”
text:
Kimpton hotels aim for a quirky, boutique feel. The decor is whimsical, all in red hues. Little perks from the friendly staff make a difference, like their wine tasting in the lobby. Join their loyalty program for free goodies from the mini-bar. 
The location was walkable to the subway for an easy ride to the museums. Otherwise the location was great for the Saturday farmer's market and other areas.

title: “Convenient, Quiet and Relaxing”
text:
We stayed in an Waterfront Suite K - definitely worth the extra $$ for this room. It was very spacious and had a fabulous view of the marina. It was relatively quiet, clean and comfortable. It is located near Sea World, so I was concerned that it might be noisy with families and was pleasantly surprised to find it was not.
The location is close to downtown, La Jolla, the malls and sporting venues. 
We stayed here several years ago and it needed a remodel then. I'm pleased to say that it has been remodeled and the rooms have all the latest amenities: high speed internet, flat screen TV, refrigerator and desk with lots of outlets.

title: “I Loved It, But Not for Everyone”
text:
I really loved my stay at the Hotel Kabuki, but it’s not a hotel for everyone. I’ll elaborate below.
The Room: I spent the extra for a corner king room, and I was glad that I did. The room was on the 14th floor, and the view was spectacular! The sliding glass doors on 2 walls were covered with sliding shoji screens and stepped out onto a narrow balcony which ran around the whole corner of the room. The room had a small entry hallway with one closet. Half the closet, though, was filled by a large bookcase which held the minibar, the coffee maker, the coffee service, the safe, and a tray of minibar snacks. Tucked into the open side of the closet were two folded luggage stands. The room itself was large and contained a chaise, a glass-top desk with a TV, a desk chair, a low glass table, and a second chair. The bed was unfortunately one of those almost-a-king beds and my husband’s feet stuck off the end. The bed itself was very comfy with a warm duvet and fluffy pillows. On either side of the bed were endtables. You’ll note I never said “dresser.” The room only has half a closet and the two small drawers in each endtable. If you come for a week, or like to unpack fully, you’ll find yourself living out of your suitcase. The TV was a very low-end flat screen, and we had to wiggle the cables to get a good picture. Because of the arrangement of the room, we also had to pull the desk into the middle of the room to see the TV from the bed. On one of the endtables is a clock/radio that is also an iPod dock, so you can have your favorite music and leave your charger at home. The heat/AC were very old controls, and was strangely noisy on the middle fan setting, but not on low or high. The room was in pretty good shape, although the wallpaper was peeled back where one of the shoji screens rubbed on it.
The Bathroom: The bathroom was in 3 sections, the toilet closet with a solid door, the sink area, and the shower/tub separated by a glass door. The room comes with a Japanese bath. If you’ve never seen one, imagine two tubs side-by-side. Now take out one tub, but leave the faucet and handles and then tile the floor. Make the 2nd tub narrower and pull the sides up to knee height. Where the 1st tub was there is a low wooden stool and small bucket that you use to soap and rinse, then you get into the 2nd tub which is just for soaking. It was also been fitted with a showerhead, for us Americans, but if you’re taller than 5’2” you’ll need to bend over to rinse your hair. The water pressure was great and the water was always nice and hot. The bathroom comes with an exfoliating soap for your scrub, bath salts for your soak, as well as the usual shampoo, conditioner, lotion, and hairdryer. The toilet closet was quite spacious, so even the largest guy wouldn’t feel cramped.
Service: Check-in & check-out were quick and pleasant. After you settle into your room, you can call down for complimentary hot tea service. It was served in a great iron teapot. Our doorman – a happy Buddha-shaped guy – recommended a Chinese restaurant across the street that was some of the best Chinese I’ve ever had (San Wang Restaurant). The room was always very clean. We called down for extra towels the one night that we took a Japanese bath, and although they took a long time to come, we got a huge stack of towels, two extra bath salts, a roll of TP, and a box of tissues. They had us covered! Every night from 5-6:00 there is free wine and sake in the lobby. We also got a free breakfast and 2-for-1 drank coupon for the hotel’s restaurant. The breakfast was the usual American buffet, but service was fast and attentive. We also could have gone for free to the Kabuki Springs & Spa which is about a block away, but we didn’t have time. The room should have had free wifi, but we could never get a signal – not even in the lobby. There is cab stand right outside the hotel, and a bus stop ½ block away. The 3-day Passport is a great deal for $18, considering it’s $5 to ride the cable car just once. Bus service is fast, efficient and runs 24-hours.
Overall: This was great, fun hotel. My husband and I loved the Japanese theme. The location right next to the Japan Center gave us tons to eat and tons to shop. The downsides were the short bed, the lack of wifi, the poor TV, the lack of a dresser, and very short shower.

title: “Amazing Hotel”
text: Wow what an exceptionally good hotel. We arrived by taxi at 11.30pm to be greeted by 4 porters. Then check in also was a breeze. We had booked a suite which couldn't have been nicer with a beautiful large bathroom. The service was top class. Every single staff member was a credit to this wonderful place. Also great location across the road from the Beverley Centre.

title: “Great location, comfortable hotel”
text: we have found that most American city hotels have small rooms. This wasn't big but not too snug either. The room was comfortable and clean.Hotel in a great location for walking anywhere or catching public transport. Complimentary coffee and water available in reception on tap.

title: “TOP REVIEW: Great Customer Service, but a few major flaws...”
text:
Let me be clear: The customer service at this hotel is second to none. The hotel is beautiful, great decor... but I know you are not reading my review for the good stuff... You want to know the "flaws." With that in mind...
The room was very clean upon our arrival. Then, we opened the beside drawers to find not one, not two, but THREE open condom wrappers. Now we all know what goes on in hotel beds, but we don't need a reminder. The hotel promptly removed them and offered to change rooms. 
Second was the bed. This was the most uncomfortable bed I've ever slept in. I didn't complain, because I thought I had a UTI (which causes back pain). That's how bad it was... I honestly thought I was ill because of the bed. (I wasn't.) Otherwise, I would have discussed with the staff. What I DID discuss, though, was that the feathers on the feather top were poking me throughout the night, to the point that I had to pick them out of the bed. I did mention this and they removed some fees for us, not that that was my intention at all. 
I hope you can tell from my other reviews that I'm not a complainer... 
I would love to give this hotel the review I thought I would be giving before we went; however, I will probably not stay here again just based on the bed alone.

title: “4star???? Paper Thin Walls”
text:
Upon arrival I was shocked at how small the lobby was. I also was disppointed because on the web-site of the hotel it stated that there was a restaurant in the hotel. When we arrived I found no such thing. 
We booked a double double and from the pictures it looked as though it was a decent size. When we got to the room it was smaller than expected. The toliet didn't work and the sink drain did not drain properly (the toliet was fixed in a timely manner). 
The staff was nice (except the front desk person upon arrival). 
We went to Cafe Med across the street for our spirits, the staff was extremely nice!
In a nut shell I would not stay at this hotel again, was not pleased with the rooms or hotel itself, the renovation I think makes it a 4 star but I would have to rate it a 3 star.
NOT TO MENTION THE PAPER THIN WALLS!
We "spoken" to for complaints when we were talking in our room at 4am (not at a loud or partying tone at all, normal, indoor voices)

title: “Pleaseant surprise”
text: Came here with colleagues on a business trip. I'm from Memphis but had never stayed here and was impressed with the stay. It was a bit busy when we checked in and our helper was somewhat overwhelmed. However, the other two workers helped us out and were very pleasant, engaging, and professional. The room was nice, bigger than expected. I have NO COMPLAINTS about this hotel. Great location downtown too. I definitely recommend staying here.

title: “Paradise Bowl”
text: We were invited to stay at the Paradise Resort when playing Pop Warner football the first week in December. We were amazed with the beauty of the resort and the GREAT group rate they offered all who called and booked early with them. We were very happy with the over all experience. Friendly staff, nice rooms. everything was Excellent.

title: “Okay, but major issues”
text:
I stayed at the Embassy Suites Philadelphia Airport May 15 - May 17 for a business conference. The hotel lobby is spectacular with an Atrium and Koi pond. The rooms are bigger than Manhattan studio apts. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful (until our last day)
Major issues: My traveling partner and I went to the bar (Embassy Grille) upon arrival on the 15th and a security guard was training a rookie "first night on the job" he said. At breakfast the next morning, there was alot of chatter about cars being broken into. Come to find out that several cars in the parking lot had their windows busted out including one of my collegues. There was no kind of reaction by the hotel staff to notify the guests or rectify the problem, as I went out to check my car during lunch at 1pm. My car was fine but the row behind mine was littered with glass and there was a SUV still parked with its window busted out and the glass on the floor so obviously no one had bothered to come to the lot to check on guets cars and they have the nerve to have a sign denouncing any responsibility for your car (I have two lawyers who will dispute that claim successfully). 
 There seems to be alot of water damage in the bathrooms as I saw the wallpaper bubbling up whenever the water came on in the room above me (I stayed on the second floor) and it was apparent in Room 112 which was turned into the mens room during our last day to accomodate the amount of women that arrived for a conference for another company. When this company arrived, all other guests became second class citizens. My company actually had to go get our own food and bring it to our meeting room to eat and then clean up after ourselves. All other amenities that we enjoyed prior were taken away.
 Overall this would not have been a hotel that I would stay for a vacation or otherwise but since I have no chose for business trips, I guess its okay for 2 days. I will however recommend that my company utilize the Marriott (as they actually dropped off some collegues that flew, from the airport when Embassy would not) if we come to Philly again.

title: “something to love,something to hate”
text:
I'll never forget "La Pensione". My ex-fiancee a couple of years ago surprised me with a trip to San Diego. Well,when we got to "La Pensione" she was in a foul mood due to the heat. When we walked into the small,but cozy room, she dropped her bags, went to the wall looking for the A/C controls and was flabbergasted when she realized there was no air conditioning. When she called the front desk and was told that no room at the hotel had any airconditioning, she immediately started calling hotels in the area. 
We found a room with airconditioning not too far away, but they were no rooms for that night. So we stayed at "La Pensione" that night. THe area is fabulous and we had a nice dinner in German style restaurant nearby. However, at night, we had to leave the window open for ventilation. The noise was attrocious, with a jack-hammer going until 7:00 (no Sh_t) and needless to say, we got little sleep. The next day, we had a very nice breakfast in the coffee shop. My fiancee's humor had not improved and that morning she told me that she thought we needed to split up because we weren't "right"for each other.She was correct, just took some years to convince me. :-)

title: “Loved the Mt. Vernon”
text:
We thought this hotel was a little hard to find and didn't realize it had an underground parking garage until we'd already arrived and had tried to find a parking place while checking in. 
The hotel was in a great location with lots of restaurants and a mall not far and within walking distance. The Harbor and National Acquarium were within walking distance as well. We loved our time in Baltimore and the Mt. Vernon Hotel was a great addition to our visit.
The room was clean and the staff was outstanding. The free breakfast wasn't great, but it was okay. But give me a clean room over a great breakfast anytime!

title: “Loved The Ritz”
text: I recently stayed at the Ritz Carlton for work related business two different times in July. I was really impressed by the entire staff. They made me feel as if I was the most important guest. From arrival to check out it was an amazing experience. Loved the toiletries and the in room coffee bar. The room was beautiful and the bed was comfy. Would I come back ..yes I would. The staff was amazing. Thanks Ritz Carlton for such a great experience

title: “Great place to stay”
text: Every year for the last ten years I take my family to PB we always stay at the mission bay motel it's a great value and rooms are always very clean there is no ac but it has never been a problem , as it is a stones throw from the beach ,I will continue to stay here for years to come as long as rates stay competive.....

title: “Convenient locale with old-world style”
text: Stayed at this Spanish-styled boutique for a few days in May at a discounted price. It’s conveniently downtown, diagonally located from the Hilton. Walking distance to the Powell St BART station and cable car turntable near Hallidie Plaza. Simple & inexpensive to take the BART from SFO airport to the Powell station. Then just walk 2-blocks west on Eddy and another 2-blocks north on Taylor until you see the hotel on the NW-corner of O’Farrell & Taylor. An easy walk to downtown locations, like the theater district around Union Square (3-blocks away), Chinatown, or you can hop on the cable cars to reach touristy stuff down on the wharf. Grab a day- or multi-day pass if using the cable cars more than 2 times a day. Large open, lobby with old-world styling. Coffee & tea provided all day in the lobby. Nicely appointed rooms and bathrooms, but not much of a view with our window overlooking an opposite building. You can let your inner-beast loose with the Serrano’s leopard-print bathrobes! Renovation work was taking place on the outside of the hotel, but it was hardly noticed since it was limited to day-time hours when away touring/seeing the city & hopefully the work is done by now!

title: “Econo lodge is Econo-fabulous!!”
text: I stayed at the Econo Lodge Times Square from March 13-18, 2006. I took my 2 high-school aged sisters and their their 2 friends for a "Senior Trip" to NYC. The hotel had barely been open a month. Check in was very smooth, and the front desk was exceptionally kind and quick. My husband was meeting us in NYC late the next night, and when I checked in I asked if it was possible to get a room close to ours for him even though he wasn't there yet. They went out of their way to reserve the room right next to ours for him and were so nice about it. Above and beyond is the way to describe the front desk. Breakfast is good, as well as free (!) and has a wide variety of choices. We also enjoyed the 24 hour hot tea, coffee, and hot chocolate. Our keys got re-programmed every day in case they were lost. The rooms were small (as are all NYC rooms), but bright and sunny feeling with comfy beds and nicely done bathrooms. Much more elegant than you think of when you hear "Econo Lodge". It was top notch and even included a flat screen TV and high-speed internet (they provide the cable if you don't have one). They even gave us the front-most room with a great view straight into times square. The workers constantly asked how we were enjoying our stay. Overall I would stay here again in a heartbeat! It was only a block from the middle of times square, in a very safe area, convenient to all of the Broadway shows too. When I go back I will definitely stay here again!

title: “All it is supposed to be”
text:
Got to spend a night here for a business conference. Very good service, everything impeccably clean and new. You know you're somewhere a bit different when the bellman offers to "show you the features of your room". Little command center next to the bed, large TV that swivels out from the wall, windows that actually open a few inches, an fax machine in the room, built in phone and TV with the tub, nice separate shower. All requests were addressed quickly and efficiently. No, you won't find a microwave or ironing board here, though the minifridge is big enough to hold a few items. Unpack the suit and get a quick freshening, $35. Basic no frills bacon and egg breakfast, $30. But if you are staying here, you know this is just the way it works. The bed was excellent.
Note there are some very nice views from the outdoor patio on the 4th floor, a walk down from the lobby on the 5th. Lots of quality deck furniture, large plantings, shade if desired.
I did try out the gym, very nicely equipped, including a large room all mirrored up for your yoga or martial art needs. Vast collection of weight and cardio equipment. Floor to ceiling glass, 20th floor, so nice views. I ordered a personal trainer to work with, and that went wonderfully. Selma charged me for an hour, but worked with me for more like 90 minutes, and was great. Very professional, very knowledgeable, and a nice person as well. Talked details of techniques, as well as nutrition, etc.
And surprisingly, no nickel and diming on every little item. Wifi was free and throughout the hotel. Around 4PM they brought up a loaded up fruit plate, just cause.
As I was a bit early arriving, I ventured across the street to Rosebud, a little corner Italian restaurant. Sat outside, sipped a glass of wine, had some good food, very nice way to relax.
Overall, loved it, and would gladly stay there again.

title: “dump with a capital D”
text: First trip to San Francisco, great city too bad about the accom. Rooms were not ready when we arrived at 4pm given other rooms , dirty broken window in bathroom and we were on the ground floor , had to stuff a towel in the window to have some privicy. If we had known our way around the city would have moved . Time this place was taken off the list.

title: “You won't be disappointed!”
text: We stayed at the Palomar Hotel in Phili. A cute boutique hotel. Had 2 queen size beds. Very modern hotel, more chique than the traditional model hotel. Staff are very accommodating and friendly- very helpful. They have wine hour from 5-6pm and in the morning they have coffee, multiple tea selections and canoli's in the lobby. Have healthclub. Nice roaring fire blazing in the lobby.There is a questionaire that patrons can fill out prior to arrival, to better meet your needs. Consequently, there were feather pillows waiting in our room and a NY Times delivered Sunday morning. There is a nice restaurant/bar adjacent to the lobby. All the little touches were appreciated. If you become a member of their rewards club, you get a $10 voucher for things in the in-room fridge, which is nice. Location is great- 2 blocks from Rittenhouse Square- lots of good upscale shopping and great restaurants. a 30 minute walk to South Street. We loved the hotel and wished we could have stayed longer. One suggestion- wish there was a lock on the slidding door to the bathroom. Would highly recommend!!!!!!!!

title: “Unusually nice”
text: Other than the somewhat smallish size of our bedroom, I can't find fault with anything else at the Washington Plaza Hotel. It was a pleasure to interact with all the very nice and helpful staff I met (front desk, gift shop, restaurant, bar, doormen, maids). This does not seem to be like a place where people hate their jobs! The decor in the lobby and bar is understated and calm. There are a good breakfast buffet, and efficiently designed bedrooms and bathrooms. For the relatively low weekend price we paid, it was a nice surprise to get evening turndown service. The hotel is just a few blocks from the Metro, with plenty of restaurants and several theaters within walking distance.

title: “Good Location & Clean”
text:
Small newer hotel in a great location, parking right next door for $36/day...Very clean rooms and breakfast area...Inexpensive for the City ($250/night)...Very short walk to Madison Square Garden area/Penn Station for subway...Nice employees...Very comfortable bed and pillows...
Our only "issues": Small rooms (but who cares, you aren't going to be in your room much anyways), and garbage truck pickup in the wee hours of the morning woke us up each night (our room faced the front-29th. St.)

title: “Great Front Desk & Staff”
text:
Stayed here June 10, 2008 and June 21-24, 2008 with wife, 4 year old, and mother-in-law in a suite (separate bedroom). Very nice room, large and comfortable for at least 4 adults - sofa sleeper in living area, 2 T.V.'s, king bed in bedroom, bathroom had double entry through door foyer and bedroom. Furnishings are very nice and everything looks very new, and very pleasant and well kept grounds.
The hotel is caddy-corner to San Antonio airport, and the hotel provides free shuttle service to airport, and to malls, restaurants, etc. within a 2-mile radius (Quarry Market, etc.). So you will hear jets roar by the hotel around 6 a.m. - 7 a.m.
Melissa at the front desk was always cheerful and friendly. Answered all my questions, and helped me get a low rate for extra days due to car trouble and had to stay put in San Antonio for 2 more days.
Standard continental breakfast - large dining area w/ 3 waffle irons. Never felt too crowded during the breakfast hours. Pool on the small size, but should be adequate for most, unless you want to do laps.
Hotel has business center with a computer and free internet access - very convenient to use, but have to ask for the key to the room.
P.S. Hotel allows you to park your vehicle for - FREE - in the hotel parking lot if you are leaving from the airport up to 30 days. You have to sign the usual waivers for loss and damage, but it saved me over $100 of parking fees for a 10 day trip.

title: “Unexpected Guests in Room”
text: We checked into the Indianapolis Airport Fairfield Inn. The desk clerk was pleasant as was the entire staff during our one night (we did the Park and Fly Package). Our first room had ants- both live and dead ones. The dead ones were all along the wall- the live ones we killed were by the air coditioner. I went to the desk and we were promptly moved to a second room (next door to the first...at this point they took 40% off my bill and apologized several times). The second room still had ants...dead and alive. Back to the desk...another apology and new room...this one 3 floors up. There were still a few ants, but after moving 3 times in 30 minutes with 2 children we stayed in our room with the ants. Other than ants the rooms were spotless. I understand ants can be anywhere, but you could see the edge where housekeeping had missed them in the cleaning. After talking to the manager after our return I was credited the full amount back to my account. The location was great, staff was nice but be careful of uninvited guests!

title: “Great Hotel! Great Location!”
text:
We stayed at the Hollywood Inn Express from Sep 23 to 30. We couldn't be happier! The check-in was quick, and we got our room with two queen beds, as booked; the room was pretty comfortable, it had a convenient safe and a cool massage shower, besides a complimentary coffee machine and coffee. The free WI-FI, nice addition. If you need to book a tour, you can use the room phone, since all local calls are free! (for my surprise!)
The complimentary breakfast was pretty good, including the USA Today every morning. 
Please note since it is an Express hotel, they use plastic tableware, which for us was not a problem at all! besides, the breakfast was just delicious! specially the coffee!
The staff was really pleasant and helpful! and most of them speak Spanish. 
Also, the hotel is walking distance from the Hollywood Blvd (3-5 minutes approx.), where all the main attractions are located: the Kodak Theatre, The Chinese theatre, the Walk of Fame, Madame tussauds´s museum, Ripley´s, and so much more. Also, most tours depart just from the Chinese theatre, which is very convenient. Since we preferred to use the public transportation to move around, I must say the Metro station is exactly in the Hollywood Blvd. and Highland Avenue. The bus stop is also there. it was really easy to move around.
I would definitely go back to this hotel.

title: “Lovely”
text: Visited on business for a meeting. My room was large, comfortable, nice bathroom. The food served at the meeting was excellent as far as meeting foods go. The grounds were pretty. Good choice for a meeting.

title: “Our favorite in San Diego”
text:
Friend in San Diego got us a great rate. We stayed there last year and enjoyed it so we decided to stay for the Fourth of July weekend. 
The Room is the best we have stayed in San Diego. Corner room with a balcony overlooking the pool and Petco park. The other windows gave us a bay front view over the convention center. We watched the fireworks from the room at the same time as the Olympic Swim trials. The Concierge, Connie, hit is great three times. Oceanaire for seafood three blocks away, Filipi's in little Italy, and Dusinni's bar for Happy Hour. July 4, we are at the Omni Bar for Happy hour. Hamburgers $1.95, Sushi $1.95, and Three sliders with blue cheese for $4.95. Go for a Padres game if you can.

title: “Great Location”
text: Great location for sight seeing in the Back Bay of Boston. The rooms are very simple so don't expect much even though the price is what close to what you might pay for a more posh hotel.

title: “The Muse is inspired!”
text:
Recently spent two nights at The Muse while attending NY Comic Con. Our room was lovely and well-appointed as was the bathroom. L'Occitaine amenities were a delightful addition to the latter as was the upgraded amenity bag containing toothpaste, hairgel, etc (I may have gotten this because I am a Kimpton In-Touch member). This was definitely one of the most spacious rooms in which I've stayed in NY and was a welcome respite after a long drive from Boston (night 1) and an even longer day at the convention (night 2). 
District, the restaurant in the hotel, has delicious food but the service leaves something to be desired, to be honest. While the individual servers were pleasant enough while waiting on us, when we were seated near the kitchen we were privvy to a variety of loud arguments amongst staff members. Additionally, apparently District doesn't serve mixed drinks in spite of the fact that the hotel bar is a stone's throw away and you *can* have restaurant food in the bar! Very odd...
The front desk staff and concierges Barbara and Stephen deserve additional kudos for their wonderfully personalized service and attention to detail. I will definitely stay at The Muse again, and I would encourage anyone looking for a little oasis of calm and class in the middle of Times Square to do the same!

title: “Enjoyed every minute!”
text: My 10 year old daughter and I stayed there for our first trip to NYC. The location of the hotel was excellent. We were able to walk almost everywhere. The staff was super friendly and helpful (especially in helping us with directions). The room was beautiful and superclean. The food was excellent. The breakfast that was delivered to our room each morning was excellent. The lobby and main public areas were beautifully decorated and the security was topnotch because we always felt safe there. If I ever go back to NYC, I would 100% stay there again and would recommend anyone I know to as well.

title: “Birthday Trip”
text: Had a very nice clean room for a one night visit to our grand children. Arrived before actual stated check in time but was given a room anyway. Very nice receptionist. Very nice, clean, spacious rooms. Free coffee 24/7.

title: “Great service”
text:
We ended up in this hotel because of problems about getting a rental car.
It would have been hard to find a better place to stay at such short notice. Great room, roomy, well furnished and clean. Friendly and capable service at the front desk. 
The hot breakfast, included in the already nice price, was very good as well.
As the name suggests, in close proximity to the airport, with a free courtesy bus available on request.
I can heartily recommend this hotel.

title: “Great family vacation hotel.”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights with wife, Grandpa and 4 kids 12 and under. Great location to see all the sights in DC. Easy walk to Air & Space and tourist buses. Attached parking below was very convenient to head out to NW for dinner. Passable pool on roof which was full of kids... all mine needed but not exactly for a relaxing evening by the water.
Pros: Location, location, location. 
Cons: not the quietest place I've stayed, beds are double (small), lots of families and groups, very few food options nearby.
Ate in the hotel once, highly mediocre and very expensive. BUT we found Cosmos Cafe across the street which was a buffet breakfast that was fine and very cheap so we ate there every day. La Vie en France (same building) was also very good and a bit more expensive but also a bit nicer.
All-in-all a fine place for a family trip due to the convenience. If you're not sight-seeing then I'd advise you to stay somewhere else. Kids had a ball.

title: “Great Location but Pool Closed despite 70'F Temp”
text: Nice hotel in a good location. Not only is the hotel right opposite the Prudential ‘T’ Station but it is walking distance to Fenway Park (15mins) and Boston Centre (20/25mins). A few good chain restaurants in the vicinity Cheese Cake Factory, 5 Napkin Burger, Californian Pizza Kitchen. Bed was very large and comfortable and room hard a large tv with an excellent selection of channels. The bathroom, whilst fine, was on the small side compared to other quality hotels. We were disappointed that the Pool was closed when we arrived. Apparently it closed on Labour day which was a shame given the excellent weather we enjoyed at the end of September (70’F). No mention on the hotel website of this as the pool was one of the reasons we chose the hotel over others in the city. Staff were friendly and breakfast was enjoyable in the brassiere next door which offered cereal, omelettes, pancakes etc. which was a great start to the day.. I would recommend this hotel if you are sightseeing in Boston but without the pool in operation you could easily stay in the Hilton or Sheraton in the area. On a final note the staff were very helpful.

title: “Hotel is just okay”
text: The location is good, but we weren't exactly impressed with the hotel room. The living area is dated and bland, and the bathroom was small. We were surprised to see a huge crowd at breakfast...a little bit of a turnoff, and the breakfast wasn't even that good.

title: “Good deal for the area”
text: This is a typical Comfort Inn, nothing special. It is a great deal for the location in San Francisco. We used the parking garage, which again wasn't a bad price for the city, at $26 per night with in/out priv. If you arrive before check-in time or need to leave your car up till 4pm on day of check out you can at no extra charge. Be warned, though, that it is a very tight garage. We could barely get in and out. Our room was clean and we had a view of the Golden Gate Bridge. There is the typical breakfast, with english muffins, cereal, waffles, oranges and apples. It was very convenient to the bus stop and was within walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf and Ghiradelli Square, if you don't mind walking 5 or 6 blocks. I felt safe, even walking at night.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: I loved staying in this hotel. Not only was it a great deal for being smack-dab in the middle of downtown, the rooms were clean, the staff friendly and extremely helpful. My boyfriend and I had one of the shared-bath rooms. It was small, but the bed was extremely comfortable and the room clean. Lots of nice little amenities were provided, like (nice) razors and a bathrobe. There was a sink in the room, which was really convenient. The TV was pretty tiny, but there was so much to do that we only spent an hour our last night watching it. I never had to wait for the lavatory or the showers. The front desk attendant who checked us in was continuously helpful; we asked a few times for restaurant recommendations and were quite pleased each time. I have stayed in similar "historic budget" hotels that weren't half as nice as The Mosser. If I go to San Francisco again, that is definitely where I will stay.

title: “near ground zero ...”
text:
- near ground zero 
- sometimes too near !
- rooms facing ground zero suffer from building noise
 (hotel offers free earplugs) 
- breakfast buffet: small but fresh food
- friendly staff
- different underground / subway stations nearby
- near huge shopping center (Century21)

title: “good”
text: staff members where very accomodating. However, the continenal breakfast did not stay replenished during its open hours, having alot run out as it got closer its end time.

title: “Excellent choice”
text:
We stayed at The Dana from September 18th thru the 21st. I'd already checked pictures here in TripAdvisor, and knew before hand the parking fee ($18 usd per day, but they only charge 2 days), so no surprises for us. Check-in was excellent, and the upgraded us to a bay-room in the new remodelated area. I did send an email asking to be place there, and were lucky enough to get it! 
The room was very spacious for a family of four, it had a microwave, a small fridge in a kitchenette that we didn't use but to wash our mugs. It had a balcony with a partial view of the bay (we had to be in the balcony to see the bay). We could hear the seagulls very early in the morning!! I hardly hear noise even thought we were almost near the stairs (we were on a 2nd room). The bathroom was big and very nice, I like it even better than the bathroom at the Grand Californian in Anaheim. Lots of towels, bathrobes for the adults and pool towels as well. Amenities very nice, I usually don't like to use shampoos in the hotel, but these ones had a great smell and leave my hair so nice that I was glad to use them. Overall, we loved the room, great value indeed.
What we didn't like was the carpet outside, it was old and stained in some places, it didn't match up with the rooms at all, I suppose they will change that as well.
We did stroll to the other area of the hotel, where the older rooms are, and from the outside we liked them better than our area, it had a tropical feeling to it and the pool seemed nice enought. 
We used the shuttle to Sea World, it arrive promptly, but when waiting for it at our return, never came and we have to take a cab, which we regret when we noticed how near we where from the hotel, and after the treatment of the cabby who was very mad to take us so near.
The pool are is nice, right in front of the Bay and The Firefly, We needed our key to enter, which was a good thing. Hot tub was great too after a long day at SeaWorld.
Blue Pearl was closed the night we wanted to dine there, so we went to the Firefly, using our restaurant.com certificate. We liked the place and the food was good, I think is nice to dine there if you are staying at the hotel.
Overall, a great place to stay in San Diego. We did have a car so the distance for us was no problem at all, so easy to drive in San Diego!

title: “Nice 2 night stay at the four points”
text: We stayed at the Four Points midtown- times square for 2 nights. It is located across from the Port Authority bus station. Yes, you do pass by some questionable businesses on the half block walk to eighth avenue but it really isn't a big deal. We felt perfectly safe here. The hotel itself if new and in excellent condition. Room was clean but typically small as is usual in NY. The concierge was fairly helpful. The only problem that we encountered was the key cards were deactivated at noon even though we were given a 4 pm checkout. I would stay here again.

title: “When Non-Smoking Room Isn't”
text:
Reserved a NON-SMOKING room for Sept. 30 and when we arrived it had the non-smoking logo and no ashtrays, but smelled of cigarettes. We inquired about the smell at the front desk and they assured us it was a non-smoking room. Since both myself and my wife are allergic to cigarette smoke we tried to get another room but were told they would all be "the same". We went for a walk in the fresh air and came back to the room for the night and could barely sleep because of the stench. 
This might have been a non-smoking room, but someone had been smoking prior to our arrival. We won't be back.

title: “Great hotel and location”
text:
My wife and I stayed at The Belvedere for 8 nights. We had one of the renovated rooms facing toward 49th street. The room was a great size for two people. It has a king size bed, flat screen TV and a microwave and fridge. For me those last two things are great. I didn't want to spend all our money eating out for breakfast so we bought food to eat for breakfast. Very nice not having to worry about that. The elevators in the hotel are a little slow but then again it seems like a lot of people stay there. Oh, watch out for the sprayer in the shower. If it's facing toward you and you turn the shower on wrong, yourself and the entire bathroom will be wet, lol!
The hotel is in a great location, located between 8th and 9th on 48th. Just a short walk to 9th and you are in Hell's Kitchen. Great food there and not the hustle and bustle of Times Square. If you keep walking on 48th past 9th toward the shore, you will find the Intrepid and Circle Line tours. Walk toward 8th out of the hotel you will be pretty much in Times Square. I implore you.. take an hour and walk around Times Square at most... then get out!!! There is so much more to NYC than Times Square, but this review is about The Belevedere so I won't go there. There are subway entrances a few blocks away.
I would highly recommend this hotel for it's service, location and the renovated rooms. I would stay here again.

title: “Grand historic...but awful rooms”
text:
Stayed at The Biltmore for 2 nights.From the outside it really doesnt look very impressive but once you enter the lobby like alot of the previous reviews have stated the decor and architecture inside was beautiful reminicient of the early 1900s.Very big lobby area with ample seating...reception was generally efficient and businesslike but like all american hotels service was pretty minimal.Lifts to rooms were across a long hallway and also to the restaurant downstairs where they serve a pretty good buffet breakfast.The small lobby area just outside the restaurant is a very popular place for filming of movies and there was some shooting going on during my stay.
The rooms were big and spacious but really needed a major overhaul.No doubt the bed was big and comfortable the room was just not cosy or had that homely feeling.It just felt cold dark and depressing.Windows had no curtains at all...instead they had really old dusty wooden blinds...so early in the morning one would be woken up by the daylight coming in but being surrounded by tall buildings the room doesnt get much sunlight.Lighting was pretty minimal.In contrast the size of the bathroom was really tiny and had hardly any counter top to put my toiletries.Awful rusty taps and bathtub with yellowish ring stains.Some how or rather the room decor reminded me of the inside of Norman Bates` famous house up ontop of the hill in the movie Pyscho.
Location wise not to my liking as i was there during the weekend so being right in the middle of the business district the whole place was dead.I suppose good in a sense as it wasnt crowded or with alot of traffic because my room faced the road so would it have been a weekday i am sure it would have been very noisy.Nothing much in the way of shopping around the area except 2 blocks away there was an area selling cheap electronics clothing and the usual other shops you find anywhere.The people hanging around this area tend to be more of the South American/Mexican races.Few usual eateries like subway Panda express and other fast food joints.
On the other side of the hotel behind...a totally different scenario.Tall office blocks and just down the road about 10mins walk away was a small shopping mall with a Macy`s and the usual foodcourt below the Hyatt i think it was.
Would i recommend or stay at this hotel again?Definately not.Even if i had to stay around that area again there are far better hotels like The Westin Bonaventure or the other major chains.
I would have taken a few photos of the room and bathroom but it was just to depressing i didnt bother.

title: “Great Hotel!!!”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights during our spring break. I was somewhat leary on staying here after reading some of the bad reviews. This hotel was VERY nice! The rooms were VERY clean. We stayed in a double room which was a little small but nice. Nice flat screen tvs on the walls, nice beds and furniture. Even had a walk in closet in the room. The towels and washclothes were VERY nice. I was very impressed with the rooms. The breakfast area was small but we just went down for coffee and thats it. The parking lot was a little tight but we didn't have any problems with that. We didn't use the pool because it wasn't warm enough outside at this time of year. Overall, I was very impressed! The hotel staff was extremely friendly too!!

title: “Country manor charm + big chain amenities”
text:
Normally I do an obsessive amount of research before choosing a hotel, but when I learned that other Earthquakes soccer fans were staying at the Country Inn for the playoff game, I booked a room.
I could not have been happier.
I've stayed in my share of chain hotels -- who hasn't? -- and my expectations were not exceptionally high. So I was surprised to walk into a reception area that felt more like a cozy living room than an impersonal hotel lobby. The clerk at the desk -- in fact, everyone I encountered at the CI&S -- hit the right note of service, pleasant and friendly without being obsequious or unctuous. 
Our room, a non-smoking double queen, was generously sized and included a refrigerator and microwave. The bathroom was equally spacious. I was a little concerned about noise as our window looked out on the entrance, but it was quiet and the beds comfortable. 
Breakfast is included, and the choices were impressive compared to the options in most U.S. hotels. There were quite a few kids lined up to use the make-your-own-waffle iron, and it's a testament to the high quality of service that the serving and dining areas remained immaculate. 
The staff cares about making your stay a positive experience, and I think that's what makes the difference. They could not have been nicer.
My only knock against the CI&S is that it's kind of in the middle of nowhere. It's reasonably close to the airport and to the soccer stadium, but a 20 minute drive into downtown Denver. There are a number of restaurants within walking distance, but the location itself feels kind of sterile. For our purposes, that didn't matter, but if we'd gone to Denver to explore the downtown area, it wouldn't have worked for us.

title: “Great hotel.”
text:
I have traveled a lot and this was one of the best hotel experiences I have ever had. Friendly, helpful staff. Recycling in rooms. Sunrise from room.....great housekeeping.... great locations.....easy to catch a cab only one block away and lots of bars and food within walking. Fly bar next door had great food and drinks. Everything was perfect and staff was most helpful. First time in city and they advised where to avoid walking.... helped with bus tour from hotel....
Did not participate in wine reception however it looked like other guests loved it.

title: “Great Location, nice hotel and friendly staff.”
text:
We stayed here for three nights in May 2010. This hotel was selected due to it's location near Fishermans Wharf and the fact that in a city with VERY expensive hotels this was reasonably priced for a chain we recognised.
The check in was quick and painless with very helpful staff, the room was clean, large and had free wi-fi.
We ate the first night at the onsite Dennys which was ok for two very tired people, I would advise staying in the main building as it seems better staffed and maintained. We requested this the week before arival and no problems getting it on check in.
The hotel has a pool and small gym available free for guests, parking is expensive (but this is the case all over San Francisco).
Location is perfect within walking distance off all major San Francisco tourist attractions.
Overall recomended.

title: “Wonderful Hotel, accommodating staff”
text: I had the pleasure to stay at this hotel for a friend's wedding weekend. I was able to see many different rooms and interact with the staff on multiple occasions. Our 6th floor room was great, large, comfortable, and a leak in the bathroom was fixed immediately. I also got to experience a few of the top floor suites as I helped the groom check in. The first room was a huge living area suite attached to a bedroom with a queen bed. As my friend is very tall and it was his wedding night, he asked for a king and was given a different suite with the king bed in the attached room. Both Suites were great. The staff was also helpful getting the tuxes back to the tux shop and hadling lots of in and out at the valet and other last minute wedding needs.

title: “not so great stay”
text: We booked a junior suite with a connecting double bed room. Room connected only through an outside hallway door and not directly. With one child sleeping in the other room and my husband leaving early for business, it wasn't safe to leave her there so four of us slept in one room. Double bed room had a complete view of pipes.
