Location is great for Central Park and we walked daily to Rockefeller Center, 5th Avenue shops. The service is great, but I didn't like their lobby setting in which there's no where to just relax. For breakfast we were supposed to receive breakfast vouchers for everyday for all of us due to our Silver Sirius card holder status. But the vouchers were for continental breakfast and a hot breakfast was $15 more/person. Sometimes the server would charge us for 2 people only since the other 3 where children and other times for 5 people. And every time we brought the vouchers they had to go ask someone because they hadn't seen them before. A real hassle. There's no coffee making facilities in the room and we had a tough time finding glasses to drink water from. It was never hard to get a taxi anywhere because the doormen were very efficient. Always greeted with a smile everywhere you go. Sofa bed in junior suite was not comfortable because of the springs and we ended up putting in on the floor. I guess for almost $1000/night it just wasn't worth all the problems. Their price is reasonable for Manhattan, however, and if you have the money to spend on room service and extras, then stay here.

title: “Very Nice”
text: Very nice hotel. Kind of a retro modern feel in the rooms. The front desk was busy and we had to wait. Close to Chinatown and Union Square. It's windy and cool on Nob Hill. The rate was reasonable ($140) but it cost $50 with tax to park the car.

title: “Great price, friendly staff, clean and modern room”
text: Did I mention amazingly convenient location? It's literally a fifteen minute walk or less to Times Square, another five to get to Central Park. I was feeling pretty bad during my trip, I was trying to catch a football game but I missed the train to get there on time(the next one was in another hour!). But upon arrival I instantly felt better, from the friendly and professional approach of the staff to the very nice room I had!! The gym is very tiny, but this is understandable given real estate in the area. I got some free drinks for my stay, wi-fi, a very comfortable bed, alas, aside from the gym, everything else was amazing. I wish I had purchased the breakfast, it looked so good!

title: “Bad! Bad!”
text: I have to say that this hotel is terrible!!!!!! the bathroom is dirty, old, awful.

title: “Not bad at all”
text: Unlike some found, we found that the service was excellent, the lobby area very modern and comfortable and the rooms modern and clean. Not a bad place to stay IF you can get a good price through Hotwire or Priceline for example as we did. 216.00 inc. taxes for two nights. The downside is (self) parking which costs 17.00 bucks per day; it's an airport hotel and I guess that's part of the deal.

title: “Terrific Mid-Century Hotel with Good Spa”
text:
My wife and I stayed here with a great rate we got on Hotwire. When I paid with a Starwood American Express, we were upgraded to a beautiful room on the concierge level -- we even received Starwood points for our stay, although stays booked through Hotwire are not supposed to be eligible.
The property is a classic mid-century cosmopolitan hotel. Though it has been remodeled, it retains all of the distinctive 1960s design elements and charm of the original hotel. Our room was on the small side, but well-appointed with nice furniture, a balcony with a great view, and the Westin Heavenly Bed. The bathroom was the best remodel I've ever seen in a hotel of this age, with custom fixtures and great lighting.
Attached to the hotel is a complete spa, added fairly recently. My wife and I got a couples massage and used all the spa facilities -- on par with some of the beautiful resort spas in our home town of Phoenix.
The location is great, and the staff is friendly and helpful. Be sure to use the valet to park your car, as it's actually less expensive than the self-park garage -- and the self-park garage is a good ten-minute walk and several sets of stairs away from the front desk and guest elevators.
Very nice hotel oozing with 1960s charm; good location, nice staff, comfortable rooms. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Sleepless in New York”
text:
If you have a little bit more money, take a real hotel. 
This "hotel" offers: no service, no help with the bags, no advice on restaurants, no good working air conditioning, no decent pillows and a very tiny room.

title: “Great hotel at a great price!!”
text: My wife, 2 year old daughter and myself stayed at this hotel over Labor Day Weekend and we could not have asked for a better place to stay! We got the suite and it was nice and spacious and clean and more than what we expected. It was nice to have a family room area with a pull out sleeper sofa and an actual bedroom. The full size fridge and kitchen come in very handy (although we didn't make any meals) if you don't feel like spending money on food, although the free breakfast every morning and dinner Monday-Thursday help you cut down on quite a bit of that! The staff was very friendly and accomodating, so much so that our first night when our two year old woke up at 3 in the morning asking for some milk, the young lady at the front desk went to the kitchen and brought out 2 milk cartons and a box of cereal for us! We will definitely be staying here next time we are staying in the Galleria are of Houston!

title: “last time for me”
text: We stayed two nights at the Renaissance last week. We had stayed here several years ago and had security issues at that time. This time, on the morning of check-out, I happened to notice a small corner of a piece of paper that was 7/8ths outside in the hall. It was our bill, not in an envelope, with our name, address, charges and credit card used all out there for any passer-by to see. The room itself was okay though the toilet was rather sluggish. The bathrobe provided looked like it was ready for the rag bag. There were plenty of clean towels provided and the bed was comfortable. Next time we'll stick to the Swiss or the Talbot.

title: “Exceptional”
text: From the check-in, we were greeted by a friendly staff. The room was large and the bed was very comfortable. Free bottled water and free wifi were bonus. Close to a lot of restaurants and shopping. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Wow, what outstanding service!”
text: I could not have been more impressed with my stay at this hotel in Denver. It was right downtown and near everything you could want to do which made going to and from the hotel very convenient. I will be staying here whenever I come back. JM

title: “Pleasant but slightly bland”
text:
Stayed here on a weekend in April on a very reasonable discount rate. The location is OK--good neighborhood and convenient for 5th Avenue shopping; less convenient for Broadway theatres.
The lobby is compact but comfortable; had to wait for bell staff to appear both when leaving and picking up luggage. The rooms are smallish (welcome to NYC) but comfortable, though distressingly beige. The bathroom was well-designed, with some drawer space, good water pressure and a towel-warmer. The windows actually open, but as there was jackhammering on the street below, it didn't do me any good. When closed, though, the windows entirely shut out the sound.
There are no ice machines--room service will deliver ice for free. Breakfast was fine, presented with fresh tulips and right on time. Bar staff very friendly. I still prefer the Sofitel, but when it's full or too expensive, this is a good backup.

title: “Needs revamping”
text:
Okayish hotel. Do not go with great expectations. 
Pros: Best part is close proximity to Seattle airport, okay service, free shuttle from airport to hotel and back, free parking, free wifi internet.
Cons: Otherwise, old run-down look, definitely needs a new carpet, no complimentary breakfast. Again, hotel can improve its look if they invest in buying a new carpet for corridors and rooms.

title: “Wedding Cocktail Party”
text: We hosted our wedding cocktail party at Potter's Lounge in the Palmer House Hotel after our destination wedding. The hotel was absolutely perfect from the service to the food to the ambiance of Potter's Lounge to the room accomondations for our guests. We had many people come in from out of town and even Chicagoans who decided to stay for the weekend to enjoy the hotel and it's surrounds. Everyone was very happy with their rooms and had nothing but great things to say about Potters-- it honestly is an ideal spot in the city to host a party, it is the perfect bar/lounge set up that comes with everything, compared to all the other rooms to rent in the city for such an event it is a steal and huge bonus to be part of the beautiful Palmer House Hotel.

title: “Great Value, Great Location”
text: I'm an Embassy Suites lover and this one is no exception. You cannot beat the value of the 2-room suite with made-to-order breakfast. The staff was wonderfully nice, and even helpful with directions around town. The rooms are spacious, clean and simple. Beds are SUPER comfortable. The atrium is beautiful. For the first time, we visited the hotel's restaurant and the food was superb there as well. We paid $129 per night and that's absolutely phenomenal for downtown DC. This hotel is a little off the beaten path, but just a few blocks walk to a Metro station, it's worth it to save the money and just have to travel an extra stop or two.

title: “hassle”
text:
I booked our son's soccer team there for one night for a soccer tournament. I also was working with someone and arranged for a buffet dinner on Saturday night of our stay. She arranged for all our rooms to be blocked on the same floor of the banquet room. Between our 1st and 2nd games I called to see if any of the rooms were ready and was told they were not yet - which was acceptable because it was only noon, but when we went back at 4:00pm after our 2nd game, we were told only some of the rooms were ready. When I questioned this I was told that they had been sold out the privious night and that was causing the delay in getting the rooms turned around. We had a family with newborn twins who was stuck sitting in their car until their room was ready. Then I found out that some of out team was put on the 9th floor and some on the 2nd. 
Needless to say we were not pleased. If you know all your rooms are going to need to be cleaned in a timely manner then schedule the proper amount of staff to get the rooms cleaned on time. And if you tell people check in is at 3:00 and they cannot get in till after 4:00pm then you better be able to offer something more then justy 2 breakfast vouchers to people traveling with families of at least 4. Finally - if you say you are going to put us on the same floor then do it!!! NONE of this is acceptable and I encourage you to be cautious when traveling here as a group.

title: “Left Early”
text: We found the front desk staff to be very friendy and helpful but will not stay here again. We stayed in room 207 which is a handicapped room, not sure how it passes as that, there was barely enough room to squeeze through walking at the end of the beds. My husband had to repair the TV cable to get tv to work, you could see the hallway lights shining through all four sides of the door jam at night. The toilet is a handicapped version but it slanted upward in the front, so being 5'5' my feet dangled 2 inches off the ground. The cleanliness of the room was questionable with hair laying on the bathroom floor when we arrived, burn marks in comforters. We were also told that a roll away would fit easily in the room, there was hardly any room to walk without the roll away. The location is great if you're going just to the beach, we did not feel this was a safe area to stroll around the streets with children. We found this to be more of a college party beach, which was ok, but we did have adults screaming and chasing each other through the halls at 1:30am which is not acceptable to me, of course this is not the hotels fault, but that is the kind of people this location attracts. We will not stay here again. A couple positive notes to leave on, the front desk staff was very nice and helpful, there was plenty of parking. There is an awesome surf shop within walking distance that was so friendly and accommodating, Pacific Beach Surf Shop 858-373-1138, they did an excellent surf lesson for beginning teenagers. The view from the room was very nice.

title: “Just Like Downtown!”
text: Enjoyed our stay here over Thanksgiving, using points and cash option with SPG. A very nice room and amazing view of the city and Lake Michigan with a good value. Parking is $45 a night, like anywhere in the neighborhood, but you can park nearby for less, or on the street overnight if you are quick!

title: “Ask for a room toward front - you'll be fine”
text:
Wife and I stayed there before/after a cruise. Before the cruise we were toward the back and the big trains like Amtrak do come in loud and clear especially when they blow the whistle whilst crossing streets. On Sunday night after cruise we were in the front on the street and the noise was barely noticeable.
The value and location of the hotel far outweigh the noise factor - unless you are in the very back right next to the train tracks. Plus you are right at the "trolley" (actually light rail) stop and about 4 blocks from the cruise ship terminals, Midway museum, etc.
Two Tips: (1) Cabs are cheap in SD. The rail trolley is $5. A cab ride from Gas Lamp district to hotel is about $5 for two people. (2) Go over to Coronado Island either via ferry or other means (we took the Old Town Trolley tour which was nice) and eat at the little Greek place called "Spiro's Gyros" at the Ferry Landing Marketplace. Great food, good beer, an excellent view of downtown SD, and nice price. Outdoor seating is available.

title: “Excellent Choice for Madison Sq Garden/Times Sq Area”
text: This is a new to the area hotel with recent renovations, It is an excellent choice to stay near MSG, Times Sq or Javits Center. I am a New Yorker who has stayed overnight in NYC for business many times (as well as lived in Manhattan for 2 years) and this hotel is an excellent value.

title: “Charming but old throughout”
text: Very cool old (1886) building right on 6th St in heart of the grunge and cheese of Austin. Guest room off the mezzanine level couldn't have been in a more bazaar location. The room was taller than it was wide and quite loud at times. Room felt tired. Service was very good throughout though.

title: “exceptional service especially at breakfast”
text: Our waiter, Thomas Burns, was the most curteous and considerate waiter my colleague and I had waiting on us. He went above and beyond and exceeded our expectations.I truly belive that Thomas should be the example and the perfect ideal in these issues that all perspective wokers shoul strive to emulate.He is a valuable asset to this Hotel and obviously should go very far in his carreer because of his humble inteligence and people skills....respectively submitted....Rene St.Laurent rph/dnm/ccn Tiverton, R.I.

title: “Excellent value, Prime Location”
text: Our purpose in visiting NYC was to locate an apartment for our daughter. This was a perfect location to scout Manhattan from. The staff was helpful, the rooms clean and the outdoor patios provided a nice place to chat with visitors.

title: “Good hotel”
text:
We stayed in a suite corner and we had a plenty of space. The room was very clean like the lobby and the swimming pool.
We like this sort of hotel/motel wich have only 2 floors and with windows that we can open!!!
Everybody , at reception, at restaurant housekeeping ,etc....was kind. 
This hotel is a good choice to stay near the airport and/or to go to visit Amélia island , Fernandina beach and the coast of Jacksonville.

title: “Not what I expected”
text:
Pros: 
Rooms were nice - very comfortable beds.
Just a few blocks from Metro.
Cons:
Concierge is helpful but there was only 1 person most of the time, so we, and others, had to wait. There is a security guard at the Pennslyvania avenue entrance who is supposed to check for room keys. One night we walked right past him. Another night he was on his cell phone and I don't even think he saw us. The pool attendant spent over 20 minutes sitting outside speaking to a women. Meanwhile, people were coming in and out of the pool without showing room cards and young kids were in the hottub.
Room service was a mess. First morning took no less than 10 minutes to order 3 meals - I was out on hold a number of times. Second morning, received 2 extra meals than ordered and drinks we did not order. Third morning was best but they did not bring ketchup when there were threee order os eggs. Our package included free breakfast. We were given a piece of paper "stated the free breakfasts" with begin and end dates of our stay. We were told, on check-in, not to give the paper to room service or the restaurant. 
Each morning the I had to explain, and then read the paper with them, to show that I was supposed to keep the paper. Two of the three mornings there was a problem with the receipt and they had to go have it adjusted. On check-out a charge appeared for one of the days for breakfast. After explaining, the clerk acted like they were doing me a favor by removing the charges.
I'm not sure if I would stay there again.

title: “Excellent location!”
text:
We stayed for two nights & pleased with the location; within walking distance of all attractions near Fisherman's Wharf. Room was clean & staff friendly. We weren't able to check in early & they were very helpful directing us to the nearest restaurant for a bite to eat while we waited.
Only drawback would be the fee for parking; $40 for each night!! A bit ridiculous!! But it seems anywhere you stayed it was the same.

title: “Love the Perks!”
text:
I empathize with those who gave this hotel a so-so review.
However, I am giving this a positive rating because my experience is just way different from their. Being an HHilton member, they gave me a (large) king room (not suite) on the 18th floor (executive level) with free breakfast and hors d'vour. Nothing exceptional about the breakfast, but the hors d'vour was really good, and if I didn't stop eating, it would have been my dinner. 
I was able to peek at one of the king rooms and its significantly smaller than my room. Don't ask me why, I didn't request for a large room. The channels were OK, I was able to watch the shows I wanted to watch (mostly sports and detective shows). My robe was very clean and even had a plastic cover. Bed is very comfortable, and so are the pillows.
Internet is ... expensive. If you're in the executive floor, you should give that for free! Although there were computers available on the executive lounge. I was able to print for free, which is also nice.
Parking is $12 overnight or $20 for overnight valet. 
The hotel connects to 3 buildings which is very convenient. Didn't have to go out to walk to the office.
I wanted to use the pool but the weather was uncooperative. It was too cold outside and the pool isn't heated. For a big Hilton hotel, that's a huge surprise.
They have a shuttle that brings you anywhere around the area. I had a rental car so I just drove 5-10 minutes and there were tons of dining places. Target was across the street, but as if you can cross the highway.
The lobby is always packed in the evening, which I think is good because you feel the vibe.

title: “Perfect location”
text: This is the best place to stay if you're on a holiday as it's bang in the middle of the tourist area and is walking distance from a number of tourist hot spots. It's right next to the M&M store and has lots of restaurants and supermarkets nearby. The rooms are a bit small (which is not surprising in New York) but clean and renovated. The service is very good with all the staff being quite friendly and helpful. I would definitely pick this place again...

title: “Clean and Friendly - but BYO Breakfast!”
text:
The hotel is well located, and economical - however we found the room to be hot and stuffy - and without air-conditioning would have been unpleasant.
The biggest gripe, however, was the "light breakfast", which basically was a choice between pastries, danishes or cake, and tea/coffee/juice and a small selection of fruit (granny apples or oranges). We ended up buying breakfast elsewhere every day after the first because the choices were too unhealthy unless you wanted instant oats. (i.e. no toast/yoghurt/muesli, etc). Thankfully, our room had a fridge.
We found staff to be friendly and helpful, and the rate was very affordable (particularly as our visit coincided with a big conference in San Fran), and our room was kept very clean. They also allowed a late checkout at short notice.

title: “Inexpensive, comfortable, but incovenient”
text:
I attended a conference in San Antonio recently and elected to stay at the Best Western Alamo Suites. The price was relatively inexpensive compared to the hotels closer to the convention center. It's about a 15-20 min cab ride off peak hours to and from the airport and costs you about $30. It's about a 20-30 min walk to downtown where the Alamo, Riverwalk, and the convention center are. 
Unbeknownst to me, the hotel is apparently situated in a part of town that is not considered very safe. It's located by a major highway, in an area with very little street lighting and as a result very dark at night. The hotel is locked down by 10 pm and you need your keycard to get in. On my way leaving San Antonio, the cabbie was incredulous to hear that I was walking outside in the area as late as 10 pm, saying he was shocked that I wasn't robbed or worse. If you are driving in and out of the area I suspect it will be fine. Walking in the evening, in hindsight, was probably not a great idea. 
That said, the hotel itself was very good. The staff were always friendly and the room was functional and very clean. Upon first entering the room there was a musty smell but otherwise I didn't have any complaints. The bed was comfortable. The entire washroom was very clean, although the towels felt like they have seen better days. The flat screen cable TV was good enough quality. There was free wifi but the signal quality was not great and every so often the signal was dropped. Complimentary breakfast was served 6-10 am but I didn't try it. Overall, it made for a comfortable, inexpensive stay, at the cost of some inconvenience and possible safety concerns.

title: “Perfect location”
text:
Hotel is clean, comfortable and very well located for all the attactions and transport links. Our room was very large, not much of a view but more than adequate we thought. Bed was vast!! and VERY comfy too. If you're lucky you'll get a sea view with views accross the Bay and its most notorious attaction, Alcatraz which is directly opposite the hotel.
Whilst the hotel doesn't have its own resaurant, it has two ajoining diners. The iTop on the roadside and Jonny Rockets on the waterfront. Both are ok, but we preferred Rockets which is a 50's style diner with oldie music being played 7 till 11.
The hotel has an outdoor pool so if its warm enough you can chill out there, but if beaches are your thing, you'll need a car but there are plenty not too far from thr city.

title: “Can't wait to go again”
text: The room was gorgeous. The walking paths were so nice to get some exercise in. The spa was so tranquil. The food was superb. I loved that it had an adult only pool. I liked being away from downtown in the country. So convenient to Sea World. Staff was professinal. Can't think of one negative - and I'm picky!!!

title: “great facilities, variable staff, slight-scary location”
text:
Good stuff - the beds (my teenage son declared it the most comfortable bed he'd ever slept in!), the pool/gym, the buffet breakfast, business centre (for internet access/computer use). 
Not so good,one quite surly male reception staff person, females great. 
and the hotel itself was a little more out-of-the-way than i realised, and the walk back from the metro stop, while short, was a little scary in early evening once all the businesses had closed and streets deserted.

title: “BIGGEST SCAM IN THE WORLD, BEWARE OF THIS HOTEL”
text:
Upon arrival we were told the room we had reserved was unavaiable. We were given a very small room which we quickly discovered had no heat. There were noisy parties going on the floor we had been given. Instead of upgrading us we were kept in that room.
The scamms started immediately; We purchased items from the store inside the hotel and the person at the counter did not give the proper change for a 20 dollar bill. She shorted us 10 dollars and then acted as is she did not understand when this was brought to her atention. She finally gave the correct change after we had to insist she shorted us-nice try...
The maid did not clean the room one day and she just happened to show up when we were in the room and gave us a story about having to leave for a family emergency. The entire story seems to look as if she was looking for a tip. She made it a point to tell us she would not be back the next day to make sure we left the tip. We had snacks missing and that also seemed odd. 
My wife got food poisining and had to go to the hospital. Unk if it was a result of the food from this hotel, however, it happened shortly after we arrived. 
The most scary was the last day. We made arraingements with the Washington Flier Taxi Service for pickup to the airport. When we went to the lobby the Bell Hop ask if we were waiting for a taxi. When we told him the company we were waiting for he told us they were outside and the driver was in the bathroom. When the driver came out we were assisted to his unmarked taxi and the Bell Hop assisted us with the bags. (We made it very clear we were waiting for a specific company-he insisted the cab we were getting in was the correct one). Once inside we noticed there was no meeter and no markings on the taxi. We told the driver to stop and he got angry with us asking if we had already paid for the other company. We luckly insisted upon getting out because who knows where we would have ended up or what amount we would have had to pay. The cab driver and the Bell Hop clearly knew each other and this was clearly a scam. We should have read the other Trip Advisor reviiew listed in September section. 
The hotel is clearly lacking ethical management. We would never stay there again. This hotel was outright scarry to stay at. Poor customer service, and extremely disappointing for an Embassy Suites....

title: “Beautiful hotel close to Georgetown.”
text: Beautifully decorated hotel in lovely neighborhood. Taxis were easily available. Easy to acces Foggy Bottom metro or Georgetown, both are a 4 minute walk from the hotel. The king suite is spacious and very comfortable with a separate tub and shower. We had booked a standard room and upgraded for a small fee to a king suite, and were glad we had. The room had a small refrigerator and the hotel will provide a small coffee maker for the room, if you like.

title: “Away from home but treated like family”
text: From the minute we were met at the door to departure, the staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome. My daughter just loved interacting with the staff. The rooms were immaculate, the service was impeccable and the location was perfect,. The restaurant Urbana on site is not to be missed. We will be returning very soon.

title: “Very Satisfied”
text: Everything was fresh and new. The front desk was very accomidating as I took over the business center printing things for a training session the next day. Very convenient location. Couldn't ask for more.

title: “Fun place to dwell overnight!”
text:
I celebrated my 25th birthday in NYC. Instead of staying up all night and catching the LIRR home, me and my friends chose to stay at the Marriott. The building itself is gorgeous and a good location. Now I recommend if you get any discounts from gov or whatever use them. 
Even if you reserved certain types of rooms you can always upgrade when you are about to check in or finagle your way. They are very helpful with they want you to stay. We also brought in pizza from the outside to our rooms when we got back from partying. We were able to use the gym and other goods that came with our package. 
The only annoying moment was the cleaning lady trying to kick us out early in the morning to do our job. Other than that it was all good.

title: “Top Notch Hotel”
text: This hotel was close to absolutely everything we could have wanted in downtown Denver. The beds were very comfortable and the decor is very trendy/crazy designs ......... I liked it!

title: “Good value for the price!”
text: My husband and I stayed here prior to an early flight going back home to Detroit. We had been in Houston for about a week. We had a king suite, which was very spacious.This is a better than average hotel, very clean, excellent staff, good airport location. With that being said, keep in mind that in is very close to the airport, in a somewhat industrial location, and not near any good sit down restaurants. There is only a gas station, Taco Bell, and Jack in the Box close by. We had to drive several miles to find a decent restaurant. But, the hotel is less than one mile to the Houston car rental return, and airport. They offer a Manager's happy hour and full hot breakfast, which was appreciated as we had an early flight. There was some noise from the planes, but that is to be expected. I would plan to stay here again, due to the proximity to the airport.

title: “The Vibe is AMAZING!”
text: I loved the Vibe. The atmosphere was amazing, and the staf was even better. Prior to my stay, I had read some negative things about the staff and the area, but I experienced NONE of those things when i stayed there. The staff is undergoing some employee changes and its certainly a great thing! The people there made my stay comfortable and accomodated me when there was a problem. I felt just like family and loved it. The security guard has made the area super safe and I never felt a bit worried. The rooms were cleaned every day and everything was on point. The location was SUPERB and I will definately visit again in the very near future! A+++!!

title: “Don't stay here”
text: The location of the hotel is why I choose it, its great. Unfortunately that’s where my good points end. I paid more to be around the pool, huge mistake. The first room I was given had a very small window, which was completely frosted and you couldn’t see out of it. Once I opened it, I realized why, the room was directly on the side street next to the hotel. I went into the bathroom, the sink clogged and there were dead bugs on the floor. I went to the front desk and asked to be moved. They moved me to a room that was directly across from the back of the outside bar. Apparently something there was a large alcohol spill and the entire hallway was wet and there was a large dryer on the ground trying to dry up the mess. The entire hallway spelled like old beer. It was completely nauseating to stand in front of our door. I asked to be moved again and they told me that was the last room left in my category and I would have to pay for an upgrade. It was completely shocking to me that they would even let guests go into either room given the circumstances and you would think they would have put me into a different room without having to pay. I was only there one night so decided not to ruin the time I had by arguing with people who don’t know anything about customer service. Instead, I’ll try to let everyone know to not pay extra for a room by the pool and also that if you do happen to have an issue, you can either pay to make it go away or you’ll regret not staying somewhere else and wasting $287/night on a room. The room also had extremely poor lighting, to the point where you can't put makeup on or read anything. You're forced to go into the bathroom which felt like a prison cell, the entire thing is dirty concrete (showers, sink, etc). I stayed almost a year ago but while about to plan my upcoming trip to LA for this summer, I was reminded of this stay and where not to book a room this year.

title: “Style with service in SF”
text: Had heard of this hotel and always a fan of the style of Morgans hotels so decided to give it a go this stay. Location is perfect for access to shopping, restaurants and the cities attractions. The bar is a destination In itself and service from all staff was exceptional. Room was very spacious and great personal touches throughout. Big tick from us.

title: “Great stay at the W City Center”
text: This hotel is a great place to stay all the staff were wonderful. It was our first time visiting Chicago and all the concierge staff were very willing to do what it took to answer our questions and then immediately book us what we decided we were going to do that day. We were a little concerned reading reviews that the Wonderful room may be a little small but it was just right. It's not the largest room we've ever stayed in but just the right size for the two of us. And the beds were really comfy! Highly recommended!

title: “QT was great! But...”
text: In light of the rates, the QT is a rare find in Manhattan. For under 200 dollars a night you get a clean, cool hotel with an excellent location just seconds from Times Square. The room me and my girlfriend had was quite big - only two things though: telephone didn't work and there were no place to hang towels. The lobby pool and bar was great after a day of shopping. More of a "spa feeling" than an acutal pool - but who likes swimming anyway? The sauna and steam room looked beautiful, but I never tried them so who knows... During the weekend, the bar scene was really good - but a bit pricey considering you get served cocktails in plastic glasses. The front desk looked cool and was pretty well stacked - BUT, and this is my main problem with this hotel - the staff (except for one guy) knew less about New York than I do - and this was my first visit to the city! 1) The didn't know how far it was to Shea Stadium and they were not able to find out (which resulted in a 45 dollar cab ride, where a 2 dollar subway ride would have been easier and just as quick) 2) The wouldn't help me reserve a dinner table at a restaurant 3) When asked for a place to get a really good breakfast, they recommended Howard Johnson on Times Square, which is one of the most disgusting places I have ever been to. 4) When I asked for a nice sky bar, they directed me to Dream Hotel where the bar was on the 12th floor with NO "sky bar" feeling what so ever 5) They googled everything, since they acutally didn't know s**t about the city... So, all in all - a great place for a party/shopping vacation but be sure to get your inside information on whats going on in the city from other sources than the hotel...

title: “Staff ok, hotel needs updating, not to Westin standards”
text:
The staff was fine, though the waiters in the restaurant were just ok; not rude, but not particularly responsive. I asked for hot sauce when my food was delivered, and got it 5 minutes later after the waiter sat more people, took 2 more orders, talked to another waiter, then grabbed the bottle from another table. I could have done that while my eggs were still warm. Food was also not to the level I expect from a Westin. It wasn't bad, just not as good as I think Westin can be (this was more mid level hotel food.)
The shuttle service is horrible. While the drivers are nice & helpful, the route is so long that you are waiting a long time. It took me 30 minutes to get from the airport to the Hotel (it's only about 2 miles) You need to plan at least 30 minutes to get back as well since the shuttle also stops as the Holiday Inn & LaQuinta. Not a good first impression to the hotel.
The best part of the room was the bed. It looked great. Sheets were a little scratchy, not as soft as I've had in other Westins. Carpeting was badly stained, one closet door was not fully on its track, the in-room safe was closed/locked, the veneer edge of the dresser was broken in a section, the carafe for the coffee was missing its lid, the lights on the alarm clock indicating that the alarm has been set weren't working so I didn't know if it would go off, was getting a lot of noise from the airport...not major problems, (except the carpet which really was disgusting, and the alarm clock which could cause you to miss a flight), but lots of little things that added up to an experience that is not to Westin standards.
Good things--the bed looked great, great bath robe, nice towels, soap, Starbucks coffee in room to be brewed, real cream for the coffee (this makes up for the carpet.) Besides the carpet, the place was clean. Loved their treadmills in the exercise room--Lifefitness with attached tvs, much sturdier than I've seen elsewhere.
Parking is $15 night/$20 valet. There is a Thrifty car rental right next door, which is convenient, but very busy (30 minutes in line to get a car but that's a different review.) The ARCO gas station at the corner of Century & La Cienega doesn't take credit cards, does seem to sell a lot of booze.
Overall, the place is ok, the staff was fine, but if they don't start repairing the rooms, I wouldn't go back.

title: “Location good for travellers on a budget”
text:
The Opal is well located for travelling around SF. The room was a little on the small side and a little dated; but they kept it clean and well serviced. I missed not have coffee making facilities in the room, but there was coffee 24/7 in the lobby. There is a great continental breakfast; just help yourself. The staff are friendly and helpful - happy to spend time telling you where to go and how to get there. 
I found having access to a laundry useful.
Would I stay at the Opal again? Yes I would. SF is an expensive city, and The Opal met my needs at the price I could afford.
One word of caution; if you use the airport shuttle that Opal recommends; do not be late for your pick-up. The driver was as grumpy as hell and was not prepared to wait for someone who was not out on the side walk when he arrived. While it made o difference to me (I was on the shuttle), I did feel for the person who had been left behind.

title: “Perfect price on Newbury street”
text: I stayed here for 2 nights on November 26-28th. I was in a deluxe bedroom on the top floor and our room was facing the alleyway. The hotel does have an elevator as well as stairs. It was very quiet at night and only used the hotel for sleep. Our room had a desk with chair, a sofa chair, queen bed, flat screen tv, shower, small mini fridge in the closet, along with a safe in closet, and there were a few coat hangers to hang clothes. The room wasn't small but medium size so you can lay your suitcases in an area and still have walking area. I had the breakfast that was included with our stay. It is down in their restaurant and there was cereal, juices, English muffins, scrambled eggs, bacon, sausage, and fruit. I would say my only complaint is I wish they offered more than just English muffins as a carb, would have like either bread or bagel as an option as well. This hotel is centrally located on Newbury street and is walking distance from everything. If you want to go to Faneuil Hall, its only a 20 minute walk and not a bad distance. As for the receptionist staff, they were friendly but they didn't have much to do or no one really went to them for help or suggestions.

title: “Escape to tranquility in LA”
text: A quite and pleasant hotel snugly nested in a residential neighborhood. The pool garden is a nice and relaxing outlet for a light snack and some celebrity looking. I recommend the Apple Pizza (yes pizza!) with vanilla ice cream. Another plus is the assignment of an entire floor (the 9th) for smokers, including the corridors! Also there is a slim and sleek veranda surrounded by exotic trees for smoking overlooking the quite street entrance.

title: “Relocation stay”
text: I was happy with the hotel and the service I received the first time I check into the Wingate. When I came back after a big Convention that was in town I thought this a great hotel, but then I saw some little friends (roaches) and my phone didn't work in the room. The next morning I told the person at the front desk he said he will move my room and have the phone fix, needless to say they didn't move my room and the phone didn't get fixed. I went to the front desk the next day to remind the guy and I was moved that same morning to a new room. I like the Wingate, the location was great not far to get to down town Indy, the bed was great and I enjoyed the beer and wine each night and I really liked having FREE dinner on Tuesday night (great touch).

title: “Great Hotel and Friendly Staff”
text:
I recently stayed here while attending the Marine Aquarium Conference of North America and had a wonderful time. The executive suites in the North Tower 5 were spacious and comfortable. Tip: If you pre-pay you can get a much better rate.
Food in their Draft Sports Lounge was tasty and reasonably priced but drinks were a bit expensive.

title: “Im surprised the health dept. lets them operate”
text: This hotel is the health departments worst nightmare!! I had to stay there for a week so I could get back and forth to work while my car was in the shop. It was a nightmare to say the least. The pool is empty except for dirty rain water, frogs, tadpoles and water bugs( the large cockroaches), The rooms are very unsanitary and by that I mean, sheets and comforters not being changed in between guests, no mattress pads on the beds. In fact, the lady in the room next to me was so large that she was in a wheelchair and could not make it to the bathroom in time during the night and she had an accident on the mattress. This caused the odor to be so overwhelming that we could not take it and management finally moved them to another room. The worst part though is when they cleaned the room they didnt change out the urine soaked mattress and tried to re rent the room! That was the last straw for me and I left after telling them that I planned on calling the health dept, better business bureau, and code enforcement.

title: “Comfortable, clean and new but a bit out of the way.”
text: The staff are great, really enjoyed the bartender. The rooms still look brand new and I love the sleep comfort mattresses. However, didn't see any restaurants within walking distance. A must for me after having a few drinks at the bar.

title: “Good location”
text: I have stayed at this property several times while in DC for business, great location, close to the metro, short walk to the waterfront. Clean rooms, courteous staff and a good breakfast. This hotel is close to several of the government office buildings, there are not many restaurants close by so you will have to walk or cab it .

title: “Great place to stay in LA”
text: We stayed at this hotel in the heart of Beverly Hills two weekends ago. The location is great...so many places nearby to walk to. The service was great and the staff so friendly and helpful. The beds were so comfortable....and no outside noise at night. This is a wonderful value for your money.

title: “Home away from home”
text:
I love this hotel and use it as my primary for all business trips to SF. I'm in SF about three times a year and am disappointed if it is sold out. The location is great for views and its very close to my favorite restaurant, Nob Hill Cafe. Word of caution though. This hotel is at the top of a steep hill and sits above Union Square and the wharfs so be prepared to get some exercise or use a cab. The Powell St. cable car stops right by it as well. You can take BART into Union Square and then walk to Powell St. and catch the cable car. Get off at California St, which is exactly the corner where the hotel sits. 
As for the hotel itself, it has a very nice gym complete with free weights and several cardio units. The lounge for Marriott Rewards members is top notch with a killer view. I find the rooms comfortable and decorated with style. Price is about average for SF. I used to stay in the financial district and that's nice as well, but this feels more residential and a little more quiet. The wharf seems more family friendly to me.

title: “Wonderful Experience”
text: We arrived at the Sofitel ready to check-in, and possiblly receive an upgrade. We were greeted and later informed that they did not have a double room ready for us (this was at about 5:00pm). We were offered two complimentary drinks and some snacks while we were waiting for our room or to accpet a king room with no wait. No problem for us, we had the drinks (which would have been $12 each for a martini) and then made our way upto the room. I loved the decor of the hotel, very modern and relaxing. I'm not sure what the room rate was, as we were not paying and traveling on business. We were placed in room #602, which was on the lower floors and really didn't have a view. I asked to be assigned another room and we were told they were full. Complimentary comuters are located on the 2nd and 3rd floors, therefore don't purchase an in-room Wifi or ehternet connection unless you would like the added privacy. The bathroom was very spacious and had a walk-in shower, seperate soaking tub and large vanity with high quality towels and bath products. The Beds were super comfortable (I'll tell you now that I am a very picky prerson for when it comes to beds in hotels and this hotel exceeded my expectations. The fitness center could have been nicer, I found it very dark and stuffy, however it contained a large collection of stregth and weight equipment along with cardio machines equiped with personal viewing monitors, wery nice. Check-out was efficent and quick. I highly reccomend that Sofitel Chicago.

title: “The Stunning, Wonderful Pierre”
text:
There are not enough superlatives to describe the Pierre. Just spent 4 nights at the Pierre with wife for special occasion, in a very attractive (if subdued) room with stunning views overlooking Central Park and 5th Avenue. City looked great also with all the Christmas decorations on display, and the tree-lighting at Rockefeller during our visit. The woman who checked us in personally took us to our room, then sent a complementary bottle of champagne (Tattinger!) up. 
This hotel transports you to a time when such places were elegant and gracious, not just fancy. You can't believe this place exists in 2012 - formal without being stuffy, absolutely beautiful, calm but not dull, and a staff that is genuinely nice but with appropriate distance. The 2E bar is a gorgeous room off the lobby - perfect place to have a pre or post theatre drink. The newly opened Sirio is a sleek, really cool on-site restaurant, with a long marble bar. Great place - you could see a famous person or two there - we did. The vibe throughout is class and elegance, and just phenomenal (and polite) service. If you ever saw The Shining and recall the (hallucinated) Jack Nicholson scene where he's at the party in the radiant hotel bar, with all the beautiful people dressed up, having coctails and dancing - this place evoked that kind of feeling. The Pierre is a Stanley Kubrick movie without the scary.
Compared to the 3 other grand dame NYC properties in the touristy / 5th avenue stores area (Plaza, St. Regis and Penninsula), the Pierre is no more or less "fancy" than those, but is definitely "nicer." They are pleased to have you. By contrast, the vibe from staff at the Plaza (where we went for a drink before deciding to walk out) is obnoxious, even threatening. What is up with that? Like the others, the Pierre is expensive. Get over that - this is a special occasion / splurge kind of place. It's worth it, and while you're at it, might as well upgrade to a room with a view of the park - it's the icing on the cake. If there is anything negative to say, and it's not really negative, I'm not sure this is the place for travelers coming with young children. Others might disagree. Either way, the Pierre is truly a wonderful, 5-Star hotel. Enjoy!

title: “Very nice stay, would stay again”
text: My sister and I stayed here the weekend of March 24. We were in town to sightsee and go to the Springsteen concert at TD Garden. I was concerned after reading so many negative reviews, but we had a very nice stay. Our room was clean and comfortable and by no means tiny. Although, it is our understanding they also have "petite" rooms. The hot water and shower pressure were both excellent. The location is beyond fantastic. In addition to being just a block from the Public Garden, there are also many excellent restaurants within a couple minute walk. The "T" is 50 yards away from the front door and goes straight to TD Garden. The bathrooms size is what one should expect in a hotel built in the 1920's. My only complaint would be that on Sundays at check out time, the wait for the elevators was painfully long. I would definitely stay again when in town.

title: “This is the place to stay in DC”
text: I booked a suite at the St. Gregory for the weekend. I have stayed at many hotels in my life and none of them can compare to the wonderful, friendly service of this one. The staff were amazing and extremely attentive. The suite was was large and well appointed. The price of the suite were very reasonable. The location was in walking distance to Georgetown and Dupont Circle. This is the best overall hotel I have ever stayed at and I would recommend it anyone. It is also GLBT friendly. This will always be the hotel I use on my trips to DC.

title: “Never again!”
text: The best that can be said is that I left without any bedbug sightings. This is the most dilapidated place i have ever stayed in in NYC, and was a fully depressing experience. it is being renovated, but the lack of care given to the most rudimentary things like hanging the drapes correctly and making sure an electrical box was IN the wall and not projecting out, as well as a mirror on the floor behind its dresser, were just a sign that management did not care. To be fair, a fellow at the front desk switched me from my original room assignment (which I would not have stayed in on a dare - blood under the bottom sheet) to another room that at least had soap and towels and appeared to have been cleaned. Had to ask for hangers. Couldn't get a wake up call (phone would not connect me to the wake up service). TV with about 5 channels. Bare bulbs. I felt like I should go stand out in front, grease my hair back and smoke a cigarette (and I am bald and don't smoke). The cheap price was no bargain; I might have paid that to leave had I not been so tired and under pressure. It is not a matter of getting what you pay for -- it was a rip-off at any price.

title: “Close to Sea World”
text:
Hampton Inn Sea World is a nice place to stay.
This hotel is conveiniently located close to Sea World and Belmont Park/Mission Beach. The hotel staff was excellent and friendly and the hot breakfast great. They have a nice pool too. The rooms aren't brand new but, are clean and comfortable. The only complaint is that the parking is very tight with limited spaces available. They do offer overflow parking directly across the street in the Denny's parking lot.
If you are visiting Sea World or the surrounding area, this is a good place to stay.

title: “Wonderful experience!”
text:
Booked with a nearby convention. Beautiful lobby and grounds, large beautiful room (3rd floor corner room), great restaurants and bars, quiet despite large crowds, plentiful staff who were helpful and friendly, cab service available, easy access to tollroad to Galleria, convenient parking.
Not perfect - couldn't get king bed, a/c in room didn't cool very well (a friend on the 7th floor said she froze), expensive food, no maid service (did immediately bring up clean towels when requested).
Overall a great experience - I've never stayed at a perfect hotel.

title: “Awesome hotel with great Views”
text:
Awesome hotel & staff. I booked our room in advance and joined the Loyalty club online great perks. We are a family of 4 with two kids 17 & 7 so I always get a King suite with a sofa bed. The room (#802) was just amazing with wonderful views of Independence Park and all the historical buildings. Very clean with plenty of room and the bed was really comfortable. We had a mini fridge with snacks & drinks but you take you pay so to my kids it was off limits. With the loyalty program you get bottled water service & morning beverages delivered to your room. Express check in & out was very convenient also. Check in was a breeze & we opted for the valet parking for a few extra dollars $34 a night no hassle there. This hotel does have a pool but it closes early, we found this out after our 7 yr old asked all day to go swimming & we told her if she was good we would swim after dinner and hang out in the hot tub. After walking all day and seeing the sites we went back to the hotel got cleaned up went to dinner & headed back to the hotel around 8:12PM. I called to ask when the pool closes and I was told they closed at 8:00PM.
We were very confused most hotel pools close at 10PM or 11PM, our little 7 yr old was so disappointed so the hotel apologized and sent her up complementary milk & cookies. The phone rang an hour later and the manager was sending up complimentary coupons for breakfast in the morning. This is a hotel that will go above and beyond to make sure you are happy. Thank you Glen we just love the Omni at Independence Park. You are in walking distance to great restaurants and night clubs with history all around you. Great city! Thank you Philly for a great vacation 

title: “Look Elsewhere”
text: Hotel is a dump. Beds were extremely thin, especially sofa bed. I slept width wise becaise length wise was impossible. Overall the room was quite dirty, especially the bathrooms. Other than the desk manager, all other staff members were completely clueless. Location is good, but otherwise, this hotel is a waste.

title: “A couple of negatives”
text: Overall a nice downtown hotel - nothing special - but a good location for walking around. But there were two big negatives for me. First of all, my room had some kind of frosted cover on the window. Now, I'm sure it was put on the window to conceal the terrible view if a rooftop and building. But I could not see outside at all - not even to see what the weather was. I would have preferred the bad view. Secondly, and more important to me, is that they do not put clean glasses and cups in the rooms. After seeing a news story that some hotels do not put clean glasses and cups in the rooms to replace the dirty, used ones - and being a little grossed out by this- I marked the bottom of my cup and glass to see if they would be replaced. Much to my dismay, when I returned to the room after housekeeping had cleaned it, the same cup and glass, with the marks still on the bottom, were there - rinsed but not replaced. I went to the next room where housekeeping was cleaning the room, to ask if I could get clean ones, and I saw on the housekeeping cart that there were NO clean cups or glasses!! And I could see the housekeeper in that bathroom, rinsing the glasses out and drying them with the bathroom towel, and putting them right back on the counter! Bad enough when a cup that I used is not washed properly and replaced, but being there were no clean ones on the cart, I can only assume that they are not replaced even when the room changes guests! This was not acceptable to me at all!!

title: “Excellent, excellent, excellent!”
text: My best friends and I stayed at the New Yorker Hotel for my birthday. Everything was great -- the room was extremely comfortable and spacious for NYC. The amenities were modern. The staff was wonderful and very helpful! Upon arrival we were given a free upgrade to a penthouse room (4008) which was one room with two double beds, and an adjoining living room with a pull-out bed. Our 40th floor room had amazing views of midtown. We were also given coupons for free breakfast the next morning at the hotel's diner. The food and service at the diner were fabulous. I would definitely stay here again! Everything was great.

title: “Great Hotel for a Convention”
text: The Sheraton Boston is a great hotel if you are attending a convention. The Hotel room was large enough, so that a person would not feel cramped: two double beds, Desk and chair, addition upholstered chair and ottoman, multiple door bureau with large flat screen TV. The bathroom was more compact, with sink set in large marble counter, a toilet, and tub with shower--adequate for a convention crowd. What I didn't like about the room was there were not enough electrical outlets! I use a CPAP machine, we have a computer, we like to have space to recharge our cellphones and it would be nice not to have to hunt for an outlet to do these things. I wanted a refrigerator in the room for my insulin, and it was provided free of charge, but that took up outlet space. The shower was really bad--not enough pressure so I had to fill the tub and take a bath each morning. I prefer a hand held spray shower head, so for me this was a problem. Would have liked to have had free Internet access (The room was expensive, why not just charge a bit more and give free Internet?). Breakfast at the hotel was a bit pricey, but very good! I recommend the small panini sandwiches served at the breakfast buffet--excellent! Staff at the hotel was great, but there were certain times that it was hard to get through to them from the telephone in the room. Beautiful Lobby with computer areas and easy access to 2 indoor malls and the convention center.

title: “excellent hotel”
text:
From February 2-5, 06 we stayed at the Riverwalk San Antonio. Everyone from checkin desk to maintenance we encountered on the elevator was friendly and made eye contact. 
We requested info on the Rodeo and what the concierge did not know, he checked on and got back with us. Directions to attractions were given in a friendly yet professional manner. Our room was made up promptly. Restaurant staff was pleasant and efficient. We were there for a small convention and the banquet meal was adequate and served professionally. Perhaps based on other opinions we read, the hotel has done some customer service training. If so, it has surely paid off because we had absolutely no complaints and the location is great. One does not need a car for many of the local attractions. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Luxury and splendid service!”
text: Our only disappointment was that the Bohemian Suite was not quite what was featured in pictures on the website. But it was very, very good! Looking back now, it was only one piece of furniture and a few different pillows in the photo. We stopped in at the lounge late Saturday night after the restaurant had closed. The hostess went beyond herself to prepare a desert and fresh coffee for us! After departure, my wife discovered she had left her cell phone charger in the room. The hotel operator put us in contact with the head housekeeper who had the charger and promised to keep it at her desk until we had a chance to stop back by and retrieve it. Everyone was gracious, attentive, and met our expectations for luxury-level service. Every square foot of the property treats the visitor to a sensory experience!

title: “Very happy”
text: I had a last minute business trip to Boston planned, with a certain dollar budget I needed to stay within. The "name brand" hotels I would usually stay in were either sold out or prices were outside the budget. When I started to extend my search I found the Charlesmark. It was within a mile of my meeting and it seemed like a good alternative. I checked their website for parking choices as well. Overall I was very happy with the hotel. It was only me so the size of the room wasn't an issue. It was clean, well appointed and had a nice modern feel. The small wardrobe as others have mentioned is a drawback, but they had two hooks on the wall where you can place hangers/clothing, so not really a problem. The lounge has an arrangement with the Thai restaurant next door, so I ordered a dinner and the bartender brought it to me within about 10 minutes. That and a glass of wine was perfect. The breakfast was coffee, fruit, bagels and donuts in the upper lounge area, starting at 7am. That was fine with me. I had room 106, which is the first floor in the back, with a view of the alley. I really didn't care until about 5:30 the next morning when a trash truck woke me up! Avoid that room if you can... The only other issue I would report is parking. The website said for quickest walk, pass the hotel, take left on Dartmouth, left on Newbury, left on Exeter, and the garage is on the right. I pulled into the garage that ended up being valet only, which I don't really like.. It also closes at midnight and reopens at 7am. That worked for me, so I decided to stay. They quoted me a price and when I cam back at 7:12am the next morning they quoted me 5 dollars more because I wasn't there at 7am.... Now, in the room in their hotel book on the night stand they also had parking information - but on that page it said turn left on Exeter, CROSS OVER BOYLESTON, and the garage will be on your right. A detail that they should fix so guests know EXACTLY where they are recommending... Now that I have been there once, I wouldn't hesitate to return.

title: “Love this Hotel !”
text: This is a must stay at Hotel, from the time I pulled into the garage the valet gentleman were very helpful and always greeted us with a smile. Checking in was very easy and the rooms are like being in a studio, everything was very clean, the beds were like sleeping on a cloud, The kitchen had all the basics that I needed, loved relaxing in the large whirlpool sauna after a long day. the location was a huge plus I was walking distance to nice restaurants and grocery stores and even a short driving distance to every place I wanted to see. I will definitely being staying here again!

title: “Excellent staff and acomodation, but location...”
text:
I´ve just got back from 4 days at the COVA Hotel in san francisco, if you are planning to stay in here and get to the hotel by public transport never walk in any other street beside HYDE STREET, all the other ones of the zone are full of homeless people and prostitutes because of several shelters located near the area. 
Ever since we got to the lobby, we felt more secure, the assitance given by Victor at front desk was wonderful, he was willing to help us at all time, kind, patient and great attitude,also samantha was really kind and helpful.
The room was pretty clean and confortable, the bed was amazing ( set an alarm otherwise you wont be able to wake up next morning).
An extraordinary detail is by ifar the free shuttle transportation and pick up offered to Union Square/ Moscone Center and FIsherman´s wharf, with this service you avoid walking and getting into the homeless concentration areas, adn you can even save up money on cabs.
The breakfast was really complete, it included fruit, cereals, waffles,cheese, ham, bread, coffee milk and juices, good enough to start the day,
I would definitely come back to Cova Hotel.

title: “Great location and staff”
text: I stayed here for a work conference for a week. The hotel was very clean and the staff were very nice, helpful, and accommodating. I loved the wine reception every evening that featured wines from the area. Close to a great shopping district.

title: “Get a room”
text: If you find yourself stuck at LAX overnight or just looking for a conveniently located hotel on the westside, consider the Crowne Plaza. Recently renovated rooms are very comfortable, staff is very accommodating and the in house restaurants are better than average.

title: “If You Love Street Noise You Will Love the Duane Street Hotel”
text: This hotel is an unmitigated disaster, a perfect example of the boutique hotel gone wrong. The unfriendly, unhelpful desk clerk was the highlight of my one night stay. The biggest problem at the Duane Street Hotel is that every room faces Church Street, which is a busy thoroughfare in lower Manhattan. There is no escape from the traffic noise associated with it. Despite assurances from the hotel that the rooms had double glazed windows, it made absolutely no difference. All day, all night long all you could hear was cars, trucks, buses, motorcycles, sirens, etc. It was impossible to sleep and there was nowhere to escape. So if you like street noise, this is your place. If you are a light sleeper, best to look elsewhere. The room was cramped, closet tiny. The bed however was comfortable and the free wireless worked well. No chance I would return for any price.

title: “Dreadful start but got better”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for four nights. We were greeted after a long flight by a very sullen receptionist having been ignored by others for several minutes. We checked in to our room on the 31st floor having prepaid a premium rate for a room with a city view, our view was a brick wall so don't bother paying extra for the higher floor as you're view won't be as promised. We waited at least 30 minutes for our luggage to be sent up before ringing reception to ask where it was, they said it was on the way up, it wasn't and we rang again 30 minutes later & they couldn't find it. My husband ended up going down for it and it was still sitting at reception! 
Thankfully things improved after such a bad start. The room was lovely & spacious & very comfortable. The bed was really comfortable also. The hotel is beautiful, we ate in the Gilt bar one night & the service was very good & the surroundings stunning. The hotel lobby has free wifi so is always busy, you have to pay for it in the room. My husband used the gym which was very good. The location of this hotel is fantastic & overall we really enjoyed our stay. It seems it's just the reception staff are not welcoming as every other staff member we encountered was really helpful & friendly.

title: “great hotel great location”
text: fabulous hotel in NYC. On Amsterdam Ave, walking distance from wonderful restaurants and bars ( Amsterdam Inn for a lively place). I stay at hotels all over the world and this is a reasonably priced very nice hotel in a quiet location. The service is excellent . The upper west side - walk to Central Park and the Museum of Nat History.

title: “Great hotel for shopping, Galleria + best stores in Houston nearby”
text: Very comfortable hotel, great location, great breakfasts - even the (free) early suppers the hotel lays on were more than edible. However, one star is lost because this hotel has the slowest internet access this side of Outer Mongolia... It took me ONE HOUR to book our seats on our return flight. Grrr.

title: “Great Service!”
text: I reserved two adjacent junior studio suites for a bachelorette party/girls weekend and the rooms were very spacious, clean and decorated very nicely. One of the rooms had a large bathroom and the other had two smaller bathrooms (all had showers). We had 7 girls spend the night and we had plenty of room to spread out. The rooms were very spacious. The customer service was amazing! We had cupcakes to store, so they let us put them in the fridge downstairs, needed a pitcher and they brought that up right away. I think we called them 5 or so different times for things and in 5 minutes, we had it. Fantastic! (And no hidden charges). The staff was very professional and very friendly. The location is amazing. We walked to the Green City Market in the morning to get breakfast and it was a 5 minute cab ride to get everywhere else we needed to go (Old Town, Downtown). Most of us all live in Chicago and we agreed that we would stay there again vs staying at a hotel downtown any day! Hotel Lincoln is a great addition to the neighborhood.

title: “False Advertising”
text:
I stayed at the Westin Park Central on the night of June 1, 2011. Their in-house television advertisement projected that in-room movies start at $5. They did not give a range for how high the cost could be. I ordered an old classic to watch. They charged me $16 for it. I went to their business center to use the internet. The cost of 15 minutes of internet was an exhorbitant $6. Even motels offer free internet. A small bottle of common mineral water in the room was labelled at $3. 
The hotel is located in a complex of buildings. The easier access to parking was closed, to find an alternate required several rounds around the complex. The charge for one night of parking was $12.
It seems that this hotel's mission is to skin the guest for whatever they can.

title: “Fantastic Stay at the Night Hotel NYC”
text:
I could not recommend this hotel enough, perfect location 10 seconds from the centre of Times Square. The hotel itself has fantastic decor and a great atmosphere, the rooms are a decent size for NYC and presented really well. Nice touches like a small box of chocolates in the room for arrival, nightly turn down service with chocolates on the pillow and a weather report for the next day, makes you feel very special. The maid service was fantastic. Staff unbeleivably helpful and welcoming. I would definatley stay at this hotel again, it makes me want to try the sister hotels in New York, Stay and Dream.
Also across the road from the hotel is a deli called Cranberry Cafe, the food is wonderful and reasonably priced, ideal for breakfast and lunch.

title: “Disappointed”
text: Last weekend a friend and I decided to go to the W to experience the inside/outside bar. When we got there about 9:00 the line was about 50 people long. We finally entered the downstairs bar at 1030!!! Totall Unsat.. To make matters worse, the downstairs bar is not conducive to large crowds. In fact, a majority of the people (about 80%) were packed like sardines waiting to get to the upstairs bar. Finally we were upstairs at 12:25! Now we spent a total of 3 hours in two separate lines. I think the W could profit more by people buying drinks not waiting in lines. Too add insult to injury, the barstaff and doormen were very rude. This is not a customer service oriented bar and I can assure that I will not be back.

title: “Great Hotel & Great location”
text: This hotel is perfectly located in Boston for all tourist activities. We recently had a weeks stay and thoroughly enjoyed. Our room over looked Faneuil Hall and Quincey Market (beautiful view of all the lighting trees and Christmas Trees at this time of year) it was of a generous size in comparison to most city hotels. Room was spotless and had daily cleaning service. amenities included mini bar, huge flat screen tv, very comfortable armchair, dressing room and decent hairdryer. We requested feather free bedding prior to our arrival and was all organised as requested. The staff were very pleasant and very helpful. Breakfast was of a very high quality and provided a great choice.

title: “Boutique???”
text: We wondered what boutique meant - well if pokey rooms, antique carpets, paintwork that was laughable, a lift that limits to 3 people and takes an age to travel 2 floors, rounded off by a 'breakfast' we had to balance on our knees due to insufficient seating, then this is it!!

title: “fantastic is all i can say!”
text: What a fantastic hotel, the location was great, the lobby was beautiful and the room crisp and clean! The staff were fantastic and helped my fiance and I celebrate our engagement while on this vacation. Would stay at again!

title: “Thanks For Your Hospitality.”
text:
The services were excellent.Room was good.Location was near the airport so you won't miss your flights.Shuttle service was excellent,the driver was perfect always on time and explained all the important sites for us to visit and was careful not to lose us and he came back and again explained to us where and how to get around he treated us like a family. Thanks he was the best.The bar manager Mr John and his two bartenders Miss Donna and Miss Candy keep up with all the guest drinks during the happy hours and everybody was happy they even remembered our drinks.Thanks to you all.The breakfast guy was concern as he was not sure if we took ham and bacon so he made sure he asked us again if we could consume it he was so sure not to go against our religion.Thanks for the concern he was so taught full.and last and not least the front desk ladies were so efficient as we accidentally locked our keys in the car they quickly called the mechanics to hep us get our keys out of the car and attend our meeting in time.Thank you we have been to many Embassy Suites hotels but this is the best. 
Thank you all again.

title: “Loud rooms”
text:
Very dissapointed - my first room was the loudest I have ever stayed at - the railroad kept me up all night even though I was on the 14th floor
Moved to a very slightly quieter room (there do not appear to be any rooms where the railroad isn't very loud) but had to sacrifice a lot of space and the comfortable chair that was in the first room and was told that if I wanted a bigger more comfortable room would have to be on the street side that would prevent a good nights sleep
Glass pained door into my rainforest shower was actually a plastic shower curtain with cheap shower head
They also tried to charge me 359$ / night when I had a guaranteed group rate of $254
Wanted to leave but city booked for convention
My advice - stay away!

title: “Liked this Hotel”
text: I stayed at this hotel with my husband in Oct 2005. Located on Times Square, it was like living in two worlds - outside it was like being in a madhouse, inside it was peaceful and clean. I am returning to the same hotel in November 2008 with my Mother as I know my way around from that point and know exactly how to find things without too much stress....it IS completely mad outside, but inside its like breathing a sigh of relief. Not the absolute best hotel I have ever stayed in, but very good for the money.

title: “Fabulous Hotel!”
text: We have been staying at the Harbor Court Hotel for many years now and continue to love it! The former manager, Jason, and present manager, Melinda, go above and beyond for their guests. This is also the case for each and every staff member regardless of their duties. The rooms are exceptionally clean and comfortable as is the entire hotel. The views are an added bonus. You can walk to everything and are close to public transportation. We can't wait for our next visit!

title: “On the Avenue - A Great Experience!”
text: My family chose On the Avenue as our hotel choice while moving our son to Columbia University. The entire staff were extremely friendly and helpful. We truly felt at home inside the hotel. The beds are very comfortable, and the atmosphere is calm and quiet once inside the hotel. The ice machine was out of order, so an employee sent a container of ice to the room. Although construction is occurring just outside the hotel across the street, our room was quiet. We loved the location also. On the Avenue is on Broadway and 77th so subway access was two short blocks. Also, the location provides quick access to many restaurants, markets, and shops. Finally, our room was clean, and the maid was very nice.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
My mum & I stayed at the Travel Inn for one week at the beginning of December 2004. While the hotel is basic, it really is all that is required.
The staff (manager, front desk, clerks) were all absolutely lovely and extremely helpful. Our room was also kept spotlessly clean. When I go back to NY, which I hope to do as soon as funds allow (!!!), I would most definitely go back to the Travel Inn. The Deli downstairs is amazing for the price. Few blocks down from Times Square, tubes easy to use. All in all, the Travel Inn made our trip all the better. Also, look out for Aveline, the lady who runs the gift shop in the hotel. She is an absolute star and can help you get any tickets to any shows you want. We got fantastic tickets to see 42nd Street for $44 each!

title: “Hip, different, not your father's Warwick”
text: Stayed here because of the proximity to the medical center. Better than the Medical Center Marriott by far! The hospital booked this place which I had never heard of, even though I lived in Houston 5 year ago. Low and behold it is the old Warwick, but completely different. I like boutiquey hotels with a modern flare, and Zaza didn't disappoint. A nice chill to the place given the Houston heat and humidity. Perhaps too many valet attendants (there were 4-5 waiting for one car to arrive at any given time). Service was great. Ambience also just my style. It was a bit pricey, and the shower design (no lip to keep the water in the shower stall vs the floor of the bathroom) resulted in many waterlogged towels. And as was noted, there really is little else near by, although one can quickly hop on the light rail to go to downtown. I would stay here again.

title: “excellant”
text: Fantastic service. Immaculately clean room, all be it a bit small, with crisp clean bedding and very comfortable beds. The bathrooms again were a bit on the small side, however, they were lovely and modern and very clean. In a great location too!! Complimentary bottles of water a nice touch. We were on the 29th floor so the views were amazing. Just a shame we didn't stay longer to make use of the facilities and enjoy the comfort!! The perfect end to our tour of the north east corner of the US!!

title: “Excellant Service”
text: While attending a conference at the Hyatt in the middle of a weight loss program, I brought fat fighters with me to help fight off the expected high fat saucey foods we were sure to be served. NOT NEEDED except for one breakfast with lots of eggs, sausage and bacon and one dinner with new york strip served on top of grits. (that was a new experience all together as I am not a grits kind of girl) The remaining five meals were well balanced and healthy! Service was great and access to 16th Street shopping was awesome!

title: “Ok if you can get a good rate”
text:
I stayed there in june during the week for 4 nights. I chose the Ramada because on weekdays most hotels with 3 or 4 stars were 400-600$ a night this period. The room (king bed) was clean, so was the bathroom. A friend of mine stayed in a room with queen bed, the room was very small and I wouldn't recommend it for two persons.
The room was simple but ok, the mattress was very good. Complimentary internet (although I think that's only for king-rooms) was very convenient, so was the complimentary breakfast (fruit, yoghourt, donuts, bread, juices, coffee, ...).
I'm giving the ramada inn eastside only a two out of five because I think the room certainly wasn't worth the 214$ a night I paid. If you can get a rate around 100$ or a bit more I would recommend it.

title: “Nice, clean, convenient, affortable. A keeper...”
text: We stayed at this hotel 1 night on the way to Washington DC. It was very clean, confortable, nice sleeping conditions. the studio room had a full kitchen and a separate bedroom with confortable king bed. The room was modern and nicely decorated. No complaints! Would stay there again. There was complementary breakfast which was very nice and with lots of variety including self made waffles, yogurt, cereal, pastries, coffee etc but there was a bit of a crowd.
